11101020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101020.value: The lives of many severely deaf individuals have been improved enormously with the advent of cochlear implants (CIs). These implantable prosthetic devices restore enough auditory sensation to allow patients to understand speech and hold conversations. However, the auditory performance afforded by these devices falls short of natural hearing, particularly in the areas of pitch discrimination and spatial hearing. Some researchers have blamed an inevitable period of deafness in early childhood for the insensitivity of CI users to so called interaural time difference (ITD) cues for sound source location, positing that the brain’s binaural processing system fails to develop properly in the absence of appropriate, early stimulation. However, another, to our mind more likely, explanation is that contemporary CIs do not faithfully encode ITD information present in the “fine structure” of auditory inputs. The sound processing devices used for CIs translate incoming sound waves into series of electrical pulses which are sent through electrode arrays to the auditory nerves of the patients. CIs vary the amplitude of these electrical pulses in a manner that encodes the so-called “sound envelope”, that is, the manner in which sound intensity varies over time, but the timing of the electrical pulses does not reflect the timing of peaks or troughs of the sound waves. In other words, in contemporary CIs, the “temporal fine structure of the electrical stimulation” is independent of the temporal fine structure of the incoming sounds, and any ITD information contained in the temporal fine structure of the sounds is not encoded by the timing of the electrical pulses. In normal hearing, both fine structure and envelope ITDs have been shown to be audible and to contribute to our ability to localise sound sources, but electric hearing with current prosthetic devices is sufficiently different from natural hearing that the hope that CI users might be able to make adequate use of envelope ITDs encoded by current processing strategies is probably ill founded. In this project we plan to use behavioural and physiological studies on bilaterally cochlear implanted animals in order to determine how sensitive the hearing inexperienced auditory system can be to envelope and pulse timing ITDs respectively. This will provide valuable data, guiding the development of improved sound processing strategies for future generations of binaural auditory prostheses. 隨著人工耳蝸的出現，許多嚴重失聰者的生活得到了極大的改善。這些植入式設備可恢復足夠的聽覺，使患者能夠理解語音並進行對話。然而，這些設備提供的聽覺不足以替代自然聽覺，尤其是在音調辨別和空間聽覺的領域。一些研究人員將人工耳蝸使用者對所謂的雙耳間時差（ITD）線索對聲源定位的不敏感性歸咎於失聰兒童早期不可避免的聽覺空白時期。原因是在缺乏適當的早期刺激下，大腦的雙耳處理系統無法正常發育。但是，在我們看來，另一種可能的解釋是，當代的人工耳蝸不能忠實地編碼聽覺輸入的「精細結構」中存在的ITD信息。用於人工耳蝸的聲音處理器將傳入的聲波轉換成一系列電脈衝，然後這些電脈衝會通過電極發送到患者的聽覺神經。 人工耳蝸以編碼所謂的「聲音包絡」的方式（即聲音強度隨時間變化的方式）改變這些電脈衝的幅度，但電脈衝的時序並不反映聲波的峰值、低谷或峰值的時序。換句話說，在當代人工耳蝸中，「電刺激的時間精細結構」與傳入聲音的時間精細結構無關，而聲音的時間精細結構中包含的任何ITD信息都不會被編碼成電脈衝。在正常的聽力中，精細結構的和包絡式ITD都被證明是可以被聽見的，並且有助於我們定位聲源，但是目前的人工耳蝸提供的電聽力與自然聽力有顯著的分別，因此人工耳蝸用戶能夠充分利用當前處理器編碼的包絡式ITD的假設可能有誤。

11101020.label: Realisation of objectives
11101020.value: Except for some slight, Covid related delays, the project was carried out as planned, and all project objectives have been achieved. A paper detailing our results for objective 1 (Use behavioural experiments on neonatally deafened (ND) rats to test their psychoacoustic sensitivity to envelope or fine structure interaural time difference cues delivered through binaural cochlear implants) is currently under review, as is an opinion paper that positions our research in the wider context (see the details in our manuscript). Cochlear implants (CIs) have restored enough of a sense of hearing to around one million severely hearing impaired patients to enable speech understanding in quiet. However, several aspects of hearing with CIs remain very poor. This includes a severely limited ability of CI patients to make use of interaural time difference (ITD) cues for spatial hearing and noise reduction. A major cause for this poor ITD sensitivity could be that current clinical devices fail to deliver ITD information in a manner that is accessible to the auditory pathway. CI processors measure the envelopes of incoming sounds and then stimulate the auditory nerve with electrical pulse trains which are amplitude modulated to reflect incoming sound envelopes. The timing of the pulses generated by the devices is largely or entirely independent of the incoming sounds. Consequently, bilateral CIs (biCIs) provide veridical envelope (ENV) ITDs but largely or entirely replace the “fine structure” ITDs that naturally occur in sounds with completely arbitrary electrical pulse timing (PT) ITDs. To assess the extent to which this matters, we devised experiments that measured the sensitivity of deafened rats to precisely and independently controlled PT and ENV ITDs for a variety of different CI pulse rates and envelope shapes. We observed that PT ITDs completely dominate ITD perception, while the sensitivity to ENV ITDs was almost negligible in comparison. This strongly suggests that the confusing yet powerful PT ITDs that contemporary clinical devices deliver to biCI patients may be a major cause of poor binaural hearing outcomes with biCIs. A second paper describing our results for objective 2 is currently in preparation. To investigate the sensitivity of CI-implanted rats to envelope and pulse timing ITD, we designed a stimulus comprising a 900pps pulse train modulated by a 20 Hz sine envelope in which pulse timing ITD (PT_ITD) and envelope ITD (ENV_ITD) could vary independently from the values {-0.1, 0, 0.1 ms}. We recorded neural activity from the inferior colliculus (IC) of anesthetized neonatal deafened rats using a multi-channel silicon probe. For each multi-unit, we first applied a Wiener filter method to remove electrical artifacts, and then computed the analog multi-unit activity (AMUA) over the onset response window (0-50 ms) and the baseline window (150-200 ms). Any multi-unit with a peak amplitude in the onset window AMUA larger than the average plus 5 times the standard deviation of the baseline window AMUA was identified as responsive to the CI stimulation. For every responsive multi-unit, the proportion of variance explained by PT_ITD and ENV_ITD was computed to reveal the effect of envelope and pulse timing ITD on AMUA intensity. Our study recorded a total of 332 responsive multi-units, with 83% of them being sensitive to PT_ITD, while only one multi-unit was found to be sensitive to ENV_ITD. This indicates that CI-implanted rats exhibit far greater sensitivity to pulse timing ITD than envelope ITD. These findings suggest that the current CI stimulus strategy is not providing effective ITD information that CI users are sensitive to, and that CI users have the potential for better sound localization ability.These results provide little evidence to support encoding ITD in the carrier of current bilateral processors.

11101020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101020.value: We performed an extensive set of both behavioural (objective 1) and physiological (objective 2) studies on neonatally deafened rats, which both demonstrated beyond doubt that the auditory pathway is natively highly sensitive to the pulse timing ITDs of pulse train stimuli delivered via cochlear implants, but is an order of magnitude less sensitive to the envelopes of such pulse trains. This holds true over a wide range of pulse rates and envelope shapes. For further details, please see the attached outputs.

11101020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101020.value: The results of our project have significant implications for clinical practice. Specifically, they indicate that the algorithms used for converting sounds to electrical stimulation patterns in cochlear implants are not well adapted to the needs of the auditory pathways. Consequently, at least some of the deficiencies observed in cochlear implant users are likely due to the auditory system adapting to inappropriate stimulation, and losing sensitivity to what could be valuable sensory information. This prediction is in principle testable in follow-up experiments, both in animals and on human patient volunteers. We are working actively with international collaborators as well as with clinicians at CUHK to build on these results with the long term aim of developing significantly better patient outcomes through improved technology.

11101020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101020.value: Over 1 million patients who are severely deaf currently benefit from the use of cochlear implants (CIs), which use electronics to convert incoming sounds into patterns of electric pulses. While these devices often allow sufficient auditory perception to make it possible for patients to understand speech in silence, the auditory experience they provide is far from perfect. Significant deficits are observed, notably in the ability of such patients to localize sounds in space. We suspect that part of the problem is that the algorithms used in the devices do not normally cater to the brain's ability to process temporal features of auditory input with sub-millisecond precision. Testing this hypothesis in patients is difficult given that they are adapted to their standard input. We resorted to experiments in rats to show that very precise processing of sub-millisecond temporal cues is easily possible, provided these cues are encoded in the timing of individual electric pulses, not just in the timing of bursts of pulses, as is commonly done in current clinical practice. Our findings should provoke a rethink of CI processor design strategies, which in the longer term ought to give deaf patients who rely on CIs a much richer auditory experience.

11102120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102120.value: 耳鳴是不間斷的鈴聲持續在耳里響起從而造成日常生活許多不便的主要因素。聽力受損引發的耳鳴多數伴有許多可嚴重影響生活素質的并合癥如注意力不集中，失眠甚至壓力等。這些并合癥不但嚴重影響了生活素質甚至還能導致自殺的傾向。至今，可以有效的治療耳鳴的方法是有限甚至還不明朗。為此，我們之前通過皮層圖重組（或擴張）從而導致聽覺皮層損失區的感覺輸入增強能夠有效緩解耳鳴。可是這一初步的成果還未通過活體進行測試。在此，我們瞄準通過皮層刺激以增強突觸驅動以直接測試連接感覺神經元網絡的可行性從而減輕聽力受損引起的耳鳴。我們通過此前的經驗成功研發了混合將薄而靈活的電子設備集成到皮層（ECoG）陣列中的多管道電擊基于石墨烯。這一個科技能夠不但達到我們診斷目的既是同時檢測多個皮層部位的活動甚至并提供電脈康復的治療作用。我們的初步成果顯示基于石墨烯的表面陣列能夠更省時和省勞力於探測皮層圖。此外，當感覺刺激與皮層表面電擊配對時，長期的皮層重組能夠明顯的被觀察。我們藉此斷定通過我們研發的基于石墨烯以重組腦皮層圖是一個有效緩解耳鳴的治療方案。不但如此，成功把這項科技實施將有效的既用在其他與腦電圖有關的疾病如精神分裂癥，癲癇，憂鬱症甚至帕金森病等。

11102120.label: Realisation of objectives
11102120.value: Objective 1: To achieve time-efficient cortical mapping with graphene-based electronics. Our prior research demonstrated that a graphene-based electrode array is capable of capturing neural activity at multiple sites on the cortical surface. This success opens a possibility that our graphene-based electronics can be utilized as a time- and cost-efficient brain mapping tool. Conventional brain mapping tools such as penetrating electrodes and optical imaging methods are invasive, laborious, and have low spatiotemporal resolution and are thus limited in their ability to precisely and promptly assess cortical activity at multiple sites simultaneously. In contrast, our graphene-based electrode array allows simultaneous detection of large-scale neural activity, offering a novel approach to brain mapping. We have completed this objective, demonstrating the effectiveness of our graphene-based electrode array with one publication, Lee et al, 2021, NPG Asia materials. Objective 2: To investigate macroscale map reorganization by graphene-based cortical stimulation. This objective is designed to study the feasibility of our graphene-based electronics to assess cortical map reorganization. The occurrence and severity of noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) is tightly correlated with the degree of cortical map reorganization. NIHL results in the alteration of the threshold and tonotopic maps in A1. We aim to show that our graphene-based electrode array can record the hearing loss-induced changes of the auditory cortical map over time. We predict that animals with high frequency hearing loss will display an expanded low (or middle) frequency map with high frequency map disrupted. It is previously shown that high frequency stimulation (HFS), including theta burst stimulation (TBS), is effective in inducing neuroplasticity and has therapeutic applications. Here, we directly tested whether graphene-based electrical stimulation at the cortical surface can induce sensory map reorganization (Fig. 1). Furthermore, our result would demonstrated that the graphene-based electrode array can be a viable option for investigating brain map plasticity and diseases. This objective was published in our recent two publications, Lee et al., 2021, NPG Asia materials, and Pak et al., 2022 iScience. Objective 3: To alleviate hearing loss-induced tinnitus by graphene-based cortical stimulation. We propose that our graphene-based electrode array is capable of producing a therapeutic effect in animals with noise-induced tinnitus. To test this hypothesis, we used a hearing loss-induced tinnitus model which shows the destruction of the auditory map by hearing lesion. NIHL resulted in reduced sensory inputs to neurons in the sensory-deprived cortex. It has been hypothesized that electrical rehabilitation of neurons residing in the normal hearing frequency area can rewire or unmask neuronal connections across various frequency areas, thereby restoring synaptic inputs to the sensory-deprived neurons. Enhancing synaptic drive is likely to rescue neural networks, potentially alleviating noise-induced tinnitus. This hypothesis was directly tested with cortical surface stimulation applied through a subset of the channels of the graphene-based multielectrode array. Electrical stimulation to the areas representing normal hearing frequencies restored the topographical frequency and threshold maps in hearing loss areas and thereby lead to the alleviation of tinnitus. Success would not merely confirm our hypothesis but also provide an opportunity to develop a systematic, effective treatment for noise-induced tinnitus. Three publications (Pak et al., 2022, J cellular physiology; Pak et al., 2023, Prog. Neurobiol; Zhao et al., 2023, Front. Comput. Neurosci) were made under this grant support.

11102120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102120.value: Electrotherapy is integral to patient-centric clinics from diagnosis to treatment. This industry is growing fast globally. According to an industry outlook report for 2024, growth in the electrotherapy market will continue. The global electrotherapy market is predicted to grow from USD 815.2 million in 2023 to USD 938.8 million by 2029. However, there are no commercially available electrotherapy devices produced in Hong Kong or globally for deaf individuals. Our current results may promote an advanced neural encoding implant in Hong Kong, with the ultimate aim of providing a cost-efficient and minimally invasive treatment for patients with hearing and speech disorders. The establishment of our approach will further promote the booming electrotherapy industry and will improve the outlook and quality of health care. After the successful development of our product, it will enter the next phase of testing in clinical trials, potentially offering tremendous benefits for public health in Hong Kong and globally. Our newly designed neural implant is now in the proof-of-concept (POC) stage. Once our pre-clinical product is developed, it can immediately move to the next stage of an investigational new drug (IND) application. In the POC stage, patent applications are expected for ‘cortical hearing’ and ‘cortical language model’ tools. After applying for hearing loss patents, we will seek to identify a potential industry partner or establish a start-up company for technology transfer/manufacturing/sales in the later phase of development. Further development for an IND-enabling study will continue under China National Medical Products Administration-/USA Food and Drug Administration-/ European Medicines Agency-compliant GLP facilities.

11102120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102120.value: Tinnitus induced by hearing loss is caused primarily by irreversible damage to the peripheral auditory system, which results in abnormal neural responses and frequency map disruption in the central auditory system. It remains unclear whether and how electrical rehabilitation of the auditory cortex can alleviate tinnitus. We hypothesize that stimulation of the cortical surface can alleviate tinnitus by enhancing neural responses and promoting frequency map reorganization. To test this hypothesis, we assessed and activated cortical maps using our newly designed graphene-based electrode array with a noise-induced tinnitus animal model. We found that cortical surface stimulation increased cortical activity, reshaped sensory maps, and alleviated hearing loss-induced tinnitus behavior in adult mice. These effects were likely due to retained long-term synaptic potentiation capabilities, as shown in cortical slices from the mouse model. Our findings suggest that cortical surface activation can be used to facilitate practical functional recovery from phantom percepts induced by sensory deprivation. They also provide a working principle for various treatment methods that involve electrical rehabilitation of the cortex.

11102720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102720.value: Pseudomonas syringae, the leading cause of crop diseases world-wide, uses the type III secretion system (T3SS) to invade host plants. The T3SS of plant pathogenic bacteria is induced in both plant and minimal media (MM) growth conditions. Although a number of components that regulate the T3SS gene expression cascade have been identified, how bacteria sense the environmental conditions and further transduce the signal(s) to the known regulatory components remains largely unknown. We recently found a novel two-component system (TCS) called TsiRS that is a major regulator of the T3SS in P. syringae. In our previous studies, we found that TsiS negatively regulated a group of T3SS genes, including hrpR, which encodes a key regulator of the T3SS. We also identified that succinate regulates the expression of tsiS and its downstream gene argF. We propose a novel signalling pathway of succinate-TsiRS-hrpR-T3SS, the verification of which is the focus of the proposal. Genetic and biochemical characterisation of the TsiRS pathway is the first step toward identifying signals to which the T3SS responds, and toward the development of new strategies for disease control based on T3SS manipulation. Our long-term goal is to leverage the outcomes of the studies proposed herein to develop improved therapies against P. syringae infection in agricultural crops. 丁香假單胞菌是全世界農作物的主要病原菌之一，其致病性主要由III型分泌系統介導。雖然目前已經鑒定了一些調節的組份，但是細菌如何感應環境信號並作出相應的反應還知之甚少。我們在丁香假單胞菌中發現了第一套負調控III型分泌系統的雙組分系統TsiRS，並且初步分析了它的信號通路和調控機理。根據初步實驗結果推測：1. 琥珀酸是TsiS識別的信號分子； 2. TsiR通過直接抑制hrpR啟動子和從而抑制T3SS；3. TsiRS直接調控很多代謝基因。本課題旨在圍繞“探索TsiRS調控T3SS的信號通路”這一關鍵問題，鑒定TsiS的信號分子，解析TsiRS在T3SS信號通路中的關鍵作用和分子機理，為丁香假單胞菌的防控提供新策略。

11102720.label: Realisation of objectives
11102720.value: Objective 1: Based on the suggestion of reviewers of our publication, TsiRS is renamed to CbrAB2 because of its similarity to CbrAB in other bacteria. To determine whether CbrAB2 directly regulates hrpR and other virulence-associated genes, we first detected the expression of T3SS genes in the wild-type (WT) strain and the ∆CbrA2 strain using RT-qPCR. We found that the expression of many T3SS genes, including hrpR, hrpL, hrpK1, hrpZ2 and hrpA2, were increased in ∆CbrA2 and were restored in the complementary strain in KB. The expression of hrpR, hrpL and hrpZ1 of ∆CbrA2 were also promoted in MM compared with WT which was consistent with RNA-seq results. As our previous ChIP-seq datasets and EMSA results have shown that CbrB2 directly binds to the hrpR promoter, we hypothesized that CbrB2 directly repressed the expression of hrpR. We found a CbrB2-binding motif (TGTTAC-Nx-GTAACG) in the hrpR promoter, which resembles the CbrB consensus sequence described in P. aeruginosa (TGTTAC-Nx-GTAACA). To determine whether the regulation of hrpR by CbrB2 is phosphorylation-dependent, we constructed CbrA2 (H794A) plasmid which lost the ability to autophosphorylation, and CbrB2 (D52A) plasmid which was unable to obtain phosphoryl groups. We then transferred these two plasmids into ∆CbrA2 and ∆CbrB2 strain, respectively. RT-qPCR result showed that the expression of hrpA2 was significantly increased in ∆CbrA2 strain, while was not restored in ∆CbrA2/CbrA2 (H794A) strain. These results indicated that the regulation of CbrA2 on T3SS pathway depended on the ability of autophosphorylation. We also purified CbrB2 and CbrB2(D52A) protein to detect the influence of CbrB2 phosphorylation on the direct interaction with hrpR promoter. EMSA result indicated a lower binding affinity of CbrB2 (D52A) with the hrpR promoter. These results demonstrated that CbrAB2 directly inhibited the T3SS pathway in a phosphorylation-dependent manner. To further explore the influence of CbrAB2 on other important physiological processes, we detected the direct interactions of CbrB2 with other virulence-associated gene (fleQ encoding flagellar regulator) and metabolic-associated gene (PSPPH_3576 encoding dihydroxy-acid dehydratase). EMSA results showed that CbrB2 bound to the promoters of fleQ and PSPPH_3576. We also constructed the fleQ-lux reporter and detected the expression of fleQ in WT and ∆CbrA2 strains. We found that the fleQ-lux reporter activity was observably promoted in ∆CbrA2 strain. RT-qPCR result also showed the higher expression level of fleQ and the lower expression level of PSPPH_3576 in ∆CbrA2 strain compared to WT. Therefore, our results demonstrated that CbrAB2 played important roles on not only virulence pathway but also metabolic pathway in a phosphorylation-dependent manner in P. syringae. Objective 2: To identify whether CbrAB2 repressed T3SS pathway in P. syringae by sensing the carbon sources, we added a series of carbon sources to minimal medium (MM) to detect the expression of T3SS genes between WT and ∆CbrB2 strains after 6h culture, including arginine, histidine, proline, and sodium succinate. We found that the expressions of T3SS-associated genes (hrpR, hrpL, hrpA2 and argF) were significantly increased in ∆CbrB2 compared to WT strain under the sodium succinate condition. To determine whether CbrAB2 regulates T3SS pathway through directly sensing sodium succinate, we performed thermal shift assay (TSA) to detect the interaction between CbrA2 protein and sodium succinate. We constructed two recombinant plasmids containing the full-length CbrA2 sequence and periplasmic CbrA2 sequence, respectively. Full-length CbrA2 protein and periplasmic domain of CbrA2 were purified and used for TSA. Our results indicated that CbrAB2 senses succinate to regulate T3SS. Objective 3: We screened 800 conditions for crystallization of CbrA2 and CbrB2, but obtained no crystal. We then relied on AlphaFold2, which shows that CbrA2 is a complex protein which contains 982 amino acids. Based on InterPro annotation, amino acids from 628-746 formed a classic PAS domain that functioned as a signal sensor. The amino acids from 761-975 were the His_Kis domain, functioning for autophosphorylation and high-energy phosphoryl group creation. The phosphoryl group will be transferred to CbrB2 and induce in a conformational change. We purified full-length CbrA2 protein and periplasmic domain of CbrA2, both of which showed activity of autophophorylation with the conserved histidine residue at H764. The first half of the protein is defined as sodium/solute symporter, which means that the protein may be involved in the transport process of substances on the cell membrane. Sodium/solute symporter is a membrane protein that can transport sodium ions (sodium) and other solutes (solute) from the outside of the cell to the inside of the cell. This type of protein plays an important role in cells and participates in physiological processes such as maintaining ion balance, regulating cell volume, and absorbing nutrients. To identify the functional domains of CbrB2, we searched through the protein database UniProt and InterPro, and we found two possible regions of CbrB2 to function as a response regulator which have the DNA binding domains. We then relied on AlphaFold2 that shows a clear and high confidence structure at 3-113aa region, where β-sheets and α-helixes appear alternatively and were linked by random coils in CbrB2. And β-sheets and α-helixes were confirmed as most possible secondary structure to interact with DNA. The 149-378aa were annotated as “RNA polymerase sigma factor 54 interaction domain”. RNA polymerase sigma factor 54 (RpoN) is regarded to regulate bacterial transcription which plays a role in guiding RNA polymerase to bind to specific promoter regions in bacteria. Structural domains or functional regions that interact with RNA polymerase can help regulate the transcription process, including promoter recognition and regulation of transcription initiation. This means that this region of CbrB2 can bind to RpoN, participate in regulating the transcription process, and may affect the function and selectivity of RNA polymerase. Our pull-down assay verified that the direct interaction between CbrB2 and RpoN. We purified the N-terminal of CbrB2 (1-194aa) protein that did not bind to the hrpR promoter, suggesting that its DNA-binding domain (DBD) is located in 195-378aa region.

11102720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11102720.value: Type III secretion system (T3SS) is the key determinant of P. syringae virulence in plants. In our previous studies, we identified a novel two component system (TCS) CbrAB2 that negatively regulates T3SS genes. However, the regulatory mechanism of CbrAB2 remains unknown. Here, we find that CbrAB2 negatively regulates the expressions of hrpR and other T3SS genes both in KB and MM through directly binding their promoters. A binding motif of CbrB2 in the hrpR promoter (TGTTAC-Nx-GTAACG) is found. We also confirm that CbrB2 binds to the promoters of virulence-related gene fleQ and metabolic-related gene PSPPH_3576. Furthermore, we find that CbrAB2 binds to the promoter of hrpR and suppresses its expression in a phosphorylation-dependent manner. We also determine that CbrAB2 inhibits T3SS pathway in a succinate-independent manner by TSA. In addition, we obtain the structures and functional domains of CbrA2 and CbrB2 by AlphaFold2. Two regions of CbrB2 are identified as response domain and DNA-binding domain. Among them, 149-378aa region are identified to bind with RNA polymerase sigma factor 54 which regulates the bacterial transcription process in P. syringae. We also identified a PAS domain (628-746aa) of CbrA2 as a signal sensor and a His_Kis domain (761-975aa) of CbrA2 for autophosphorylation and transference of phosphoryl groups, which suggests that CbrA2 plays an important role in transportation, absorption of nutrients and other physiological processes.

11102720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102720.value: Since CbrAB2 is important in regulating T3SS, its signaling pathway is key to fully understand the CbrAB2-mediated regulation of T3SS. We plan to continue to test all potential direct target genes (containing the CbrB2-binding motif in the promoters) of CbrB2, and verify their functions in the CbrAB2 mutant. We will continue to search for inducer of CbrAB2 by screening chemical libraries of natural compounds. We will also perform pull-down assay to test whether CbrAB2 can regulate T3SS by binding with other regulators. Since CbrAB2 is potent negative regulator of T3SS, its inducer can be an ideal inhibitor for P. syringae infection, which will be tested in field study in the future. Based on all the results, we can further understand the molecular mechanism of CbrAB2-mediated signaling pathway of T3SS in P. syringae.

11102720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102720.value: Pseudomonas syringae, as a model organism for plant pathogenic bacteria, is widely considered the most destructive plant bacterial pathogen, causing deadly diseases and huge economic losses in agriculture worldwide. Pseudomonas species use T3SS to deliver effector proteins into plant cells. In this study, we found a novel TCS CbrAB2 that directly not only inhibited the expression of virulence-associated genes, but also promoted the expression of metabolic-related gene. We also identified a binding motif of CbrB2 in its target genes. In addition, we obtained the structures of CbrA2 and CbrB2 and identified the functional domains. Our research not only revealed a new and key regulatory mechanism of T3SS, but also provided new insights to develop better therapies against P. syringae infection.

11102820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102820.value: Using well established visceral hypersensitive (VH) rat model of colonic anaphylaxis, our previous electrophysiological studies using multiple-electrode array recordings have demonstrated that functional disturbances in basolateral amygdala (BLA)-anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) neural circuitry in chronic pain. However, the biological mechanism has not been investigated. Myelin is a modifiable structure regulating neural network synchrony and information transmission. Defects in myelin biosynthesis and structure would affect the precise interactions and synchronization between brain regions. Oligodendroglia are particularly susceptible to excitotoxicity induced by inflammation. In the current proposal we will show an increase in the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the ACC. Performing studies of immunohistochemistry, confocal and TEM microscopy we will determine decrease of myelin basic protein, oligodendrocyte precursor cells, mature oligodendrocytes, and ACC myelin thickness in VH. Consistent with our previous reports, the decision-making deficits in VH will be confirmed. To ensure that myelination is necessary for the synchronization of ACC circuitry and cognitive function lysolecithin-induced demyelination will be performed to mimicking the impairments observed in chronic visceral pain. Clemastine is a leading drug candidate for myelin formation approved by Food and Drug Administration. Next, we plan to expand recent report that the dysregulation of interactions between BLA and ACC associated with impaired decision making in VH rats were repairs by administration of clemastine. Astrocytes function as cellular mediators of myelination and remyelination of oligodendrocytes by releasing various factors (PDGF, FGF2, CNTF, LIF, etc). In astrocytes, glycogen is catabolized to lactate. Notice, myelinating oligodendrocytes also release lactate through the monocarboxylate transporter MCT1. Oligodendrocytes utilize lactate as a metabolite. Finally, we will focus on using optogenetic activation of astrocytes to test our hypotheses that astrocyte -lactate-oligodendrocyte supply promotes oligodendrogenesis and adaptive myelination. We expect to show that local infusion of lactate and optogenetic stimulation of astrocytes could release lactate, which is able to repair the dysfunction of ACC network and rescue impaired decision making under pain state suggesting astrocytic lactates supply plays a critical role in modulating spike timing accuracy of ACC neuronal network and cognition. The HMRF Reviewer’s concern on our model regarding the causes or consequence of pain–desynchrony–demyelination vs. pain ̶̶ demyelination ̶̶ desynchrony has clearly addressed. Understanding the mechanism of hypomyelination leads to desynchronization in ACC circuitry and impairs cognition in chronic visceral pain state could facilitate the identification of potential therapeutic targets in the brain cortex for cognitive deficits for human chronic visceral pain.

11102820.label: Realisation of objectives
11102820.value: 1. Characterize the chronic visceral pain affects oligodendrocyte functions and myelination in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) associated with decision making deficits. The objective has been fully achieved. We demonstrated that there is impaired decision-making performance, an executive function, during the Rat Gambling Task (RGT) in rats with chronic visceral pain. To assess decision-making behavior in VH rats, we performed RGT. In the VH group, there was a smaller proportion of good decision-makers compared to the controls. The difference in proportions of the three behavioral subgroups and total food consumption between the control and VH groups were significant, suggesting that chronic visceral hypersensitivity impaired decision-making ability (Hasan, et al., 2023, iScience, Figure 4). Similar decision-making deficits were also shown in rats with trigeminal neuropathic pain (Murugappan, et al., 2021, Journal of Neuroscience Research, Figure 2). We showed higher expression of inflammatory cytokines like IL-1b and IL6 in the ACC of rats with trigeminal neuropathy and the VH rats compared to that of control rats. Increases in the number of reactive microglia were also observed in the ACC of VH rats compared to control, which is the possible cause of neuroinflammation. We also demonstrate that chronic visceral pain state causes a decrease in myelin basic protein, as observed by a lower intensity of MBP+ fibers in the VH rats than in the controls. A reduction of MBP expression was identified in VH rats (Hasan, et al., 2023, iScience, Figure 1B), as well as a reduction in the density of unmyelinated axons in the ACC of VH rats. Myelin sheath thickness was compromised in VH rats compared to the control. Next, we characterized the effects of chronic visceral hypersensitivity and chronic neuropathic pain on oligodendrocyte progenitor cell (OPC) proliferation and oligodendrocyte (OL) population. We observed that total number of OPCs (NG2+) cells was increased in VH rats. Conversely, there were a decreased number of matured oligodendrocytes (OLs, CCI+) in the ACC of VH rats suggesting that the shortage of mature OLs could account for the hypomyelination in VH rats. We also showed decreased cells co-labeling of EdU+ and CC1+, suggesting impairment of OPCs differentiation and a substantial decrease in the generation of mature Ols in the ACC. Moreover, ultrastructural analysis using electron microscopy revealed that the myelin sheath thickness had been compromised in VH rats, indicating that inhibition of OPC differentiation and impairment of mature myelinating OLs formation result in hypomyelination. We demonstrate that MyRF protein, a transcriptional protein critical for OPCs differentiation into pre-myelinating and myelinating oligodendrocytes, and mature myelinating Ols, is downregulated in VH rats compare to control. These results are consistent with the findings in a model of chronic neuropathic pain, where OPCs and mature Ols were found to be decreased in the ACC (Murugappan, et al., 2021, Journal of Neuroscience Research, Figure 10) 2. Demonstrate that focal demyelination of the brain impairs decision making and disrupts BLA-ACC synchronization mimicking the impairments observed in visceral pain The objective has been fully achieved. To identify the physiological role of myelination in ACC in the VH model, we performed a study of de novo focal demyelination (DM) by injecting 1% LPC31 into the rat’s ACC region. The level of LPC-induced focal demyelination is greater than that of VH induced hypomyelination (Hasan, et al., 2023, iScience, Figures S1A and S1B). The proportion of poor decision-makers was increased, and the proportion of good decision-makers and total food consumption was significantly decreased in the demyelinated rats (Hasan, et al., 2023, iScience, Figures S1E and S1F), mimicking the impairment found in the chronic pain state, further supporting the idea that myelin plasticity is necessary for cognitive performance in normal and pathophysiological conditions. Our study showed that trigeminal neuropathy caused ACC hypomyelination and impaired ACC-BLA spike field phase synchrony was demonstrated in the late stages (Journal of Neuroscience Research, Figure 7-8). The functional disturbance in BLA-ACC neural circuitry is pathologically associated with the myelin defects in the ACC region which may be relevant causes for the deficits in decision-making in chronic neuropathic pain rats. 3. Demonstrate that promoting myelination through lactate and optogenetic activation of astrocytes can facilitate recovery of decision-making performance and modulate ACC neuronal network in chronic pain The objective has been fully achieved. In our study using a chronic visceral pain model, we showed that astrocytic Gq activation promotes OPC proliferation, differentiation, and generation of new oligodendrocytes in the ACC of VH and normal rats. Ultrastructural analysis further clarified the significant increases in the density of myelinated axons in CNO-treated VH and normal rats. These findings support recent reports concerning the ability of glial cells to promote OPCs to stimulate remyelination after the loss or damage of myelin. Additionally, chemogenetic activation of astrocytic Gq pathway was shown to restore spike-field coherence and phase-locking between ACC and BLA in VH rats (Hasan, et al., 2023, iScience). In a separate study, we show that ACC astrocytic Gq pathway activation improves decision-making in a subset of rats who are not consistently good decision-makers Furthermore, we show that astrocytic Gq activation is associated with an increase in the L-lactate level in the extracellular fluid of the ACC (Akter, et al., 2024, Oxford Open Neuroscience).

11102820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11102820.value: Using a well-established chronic visceral hypersensitivity (VH) rat model and chronic trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) model, we characterized the decrease of myelin basic protein, reduced number of mature oligodendrocytes (OLs), and hypomyelination in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). In both chronic pain models, the results of rat gambling test showed impaired decision-making, and the results of electrophysiology studies showed desynchronization in the ACC to basolateral amygdala (BLA) neural circuitry. Our findings strongly suggest that hypomyelination in the ACC neuronal circuitry may have a significant impact on neural network functioning. Demyelination is the important mechanism underlying impaired decision making in chronic pain state (Murugappan, et al., 2021; Hasan, et al., 2023). Myelination is critical for information flow between brain regions, and myelin plasticity is an important feature for learning. Neural activity in the cortical regions impacts myelination by regulating oligodendrocyte (OL) proliferation, differentiation, and myelin formation. In the VH and TNP model, we characterized newly formed oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, and mature OLs are reduced and are associated with reduced myelin strength in the ACC region. The functional disturbances in the BLA-ACC neural circuitry is pathologically associated with the myelin defects in the ACC region which may be relevant causes for the deficits in decision-making in the chronic pain state (Murugappan, et al., 2021; Hasan, et al., 2023). Astrocytes release various factors that modulate oligodendrocyte progenitor cell proliferation and myelination. Astrocytic Gq-modulation through expression of hM3Dq facilitated oligodendrocyte progenitor cell proliferation and OL differentiation, and enhanced ACC myelination in VH rats. Activating astrocytic Gq rescued impaired decision-making and desynchronization in ACC-BLA. These data indicate that ACC hypomyelination is an important component of impaired decision-making and network desynchronization in VH. Astrocytic Gq activity plays a significant role in oligodendrocyte myelination and decision-making behavior in VH (Hasan, et al., 2023). Furthermore, in a separate study, astrocytic Gq pathway activation of the ACC improves decision-making in a subset of rats who are not consistently good decision-makers. In the same study, we show that astrocytic Gq activation is associated with an increase in the L-lactate level in the extracellular fluid of the ACC (Akter et al., 2024). Together, these results expand our knowledge of the role of astrocytic GPCR signaling in modulating cognitive functions. Insights from these studies have potential for interventions in myelin-related diseases such as chronic pain-associated cognitive disorders.

11102820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102820.value: Astrocytic Gq-modulation through expression of hM3Dq facilitated OPC proliferation and OL differentiation, enhanced ACC myelination in VH rats, rescued impaired decision-making and desynchronization in ACC-BLA. In a separate study, astrocytic Gq pathway activation of the ACC was found to improve decision-making in a subset of rats who are not consistently good decision-makers. In the same study, we show that astrocytic Gq activation is associated with an increase in the L-lactate level in the extracellular fluid of the ACC. The findings of this project point to myelination, facilitated by astrocytic L-lactate, may mediate cognitive enhancement in decision-making behaviour. Further studies could be aimed at confirming whether L-lactate’s beneficial effect on decision-making is mediated by L-lactate-induced enhancement of myelination. Given our findings, it is reasonable to hypothesize that the astrocytic Gq activation-mediated enhancement of myelination and decision-making observed in the studies was mediated by the increased L-lactate level in the ACC. Evidence suggesting astrocytic L-lactate role in facilitating myelination to enhance cognitive functions is emerging. Robust studies are needed to broaden our understanding of this yet-poorly-understood niche, as this might unravel novel therapeutic strategies for promoting myelination and ameliorating deficits associated with the loss of myelin.

11102820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102820.value: The study explores how activating certain brain cells, called astrocytes, can help repair damaged nerve fibers and improve cognitive function in rats with visceral hypersensitivity, a condition linked to chronic pain. Researchers found that stimulating astrocytes led to better myelination (the process of insulating nerve fibers), which in turn improved decision-making and brain network synchronization. These findings suggest that targeting astrocytes could be a potential approach for treating myelin-related diseases, including cognitive disorders associated with chronic pain.

11103220.label: Project Objectives
11103220.value: We will develop a brain-slice model for patch-clamp recording to examine the enhancement of inhibitory GABAergic inputs or iLTP, after high-frequency laser stimulation (HFLS) of the GABAergic CCK neurons. We will inject Cre-dependent, GABA-specific AAV-virus to the neocortex of the CCK-Cre mouse and prepare the brain slices three weeks after. We will use PV-Cre, SST-Cre and NPY-Cre mice as controls to examine whether this iLTP is CCK-dependent or universal by HFLS of other inhibitory inputs. We will examine whether iLTP can be produced after local application of CCK agonists on CCK-KO and CCKAR/BR-/- (CCKAB-KO for short) mice, and whether HFLS of inhibitory neurons after virus injection can induce iLTP on CCK-KO and CCKAB-KO mice. We will adopt the bioinformatics method to check the similarity to the known CCK receptors, AR and BR of the existing GPCR library based on their protein structure. We will use immunohistochemistry to examine the co-localization the GABAergic CCK terminal and GABA ARs with each of 10 shortlisted receptors. We will produce a high differentiation cell line to "flag" the anatomically-identified candidate receptor and then confirm whether it is a CCK receptor. We will finally produce an AAV virus that can induce overexpression of the candidate receptor and their shame control without overexpression. We will examine whether overexpression of the candidate receptor can enhance iLTP.

11103220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103220.value: Activities of glutamatergic cholecystokinin positive (CCK+) neurons in the entorhinal cortex induce long-term potentiation (LTP) and promote neuroplasticity in the auditory cortex [1-3] and the hippocampus [4]. Thalamocortical and corticothalamic neurons can also release CCK that enables LTP in thalamocortical and corticothalamic projections when they are activated by high-frequency stimulation (HFS) [5]. However a prominent population of CCK+ neurons in the cortex have been identified as GABAergic. We recently discovered that, in stark contrast to the conventional view, these GABAergic CCK+ neurons seem to be capable of activating a novel type of CCK candidate receptors (e.g. not A or B type) to induce inhibitory long-term potentiation (iLTP, Fig. 1,2). Thus, the objectives of the present study are to confirm this preliminary finding and further explore the iLTP hypothesis by examining: 1) the enhancement of inhibitory GABAergic inputs or iLTP, after HFS of the GABAergic CCK neurons; 2) whether iLTP can be produced after local application of CCK on CCKAR/BR-/- (CCKAB-KO for short) mice, and whether HFS of inhibitory neurons after virus injection and functional rescue can induce iLTP on CCK-KO and CCKAB-KO mice; 3) the similarity to the known CCK receptors, AR and BR of all existing GPCRs based on their protein structure and the co-localization the GABAergic CCK terminal and GABAARs with each of 10 shortlisted receptors; 4) whether the anatomically-identified, final candidate receptor is a CCK receptor; 5) whether overexpression of the candidate receptor can enhance iLTP. To our knowledge, unlike excitatory LTP, the general phenomenon of long term inhibitory synaptic modulation in the mammalian CNS has never been clearly elucidate. Our hypothesis, for the first time, describes an original and robust molecular mechanism on how the inhibitory circuit participates in the formation of long-term synaptic plasticity. The most impactful aspect of this research, however, resides with our ability in determining the nature of a third CCK candidate receptor subtype, which may has far reaching implication in future drug development and disease therapies. 內嗅皮質中的谷氨酸能膽囊收縮素（CCK）陽性神經元的活動誘導長期增强（LTP），並促進聽覺皮層[和海馬的神經可塑性。丘腦皮層和皮層丘腦神經元也可以釋放CCK，當它們被高頻刺激啟動時，可使丘腦皮層和皮層丘腦投影中的LTP啟動。但是，皮質中CCK能神經元的最大群體是GABA能的CCK神經元。我們最近的研究表明，這些CCK-GABA神經元可能具有增强其抑制作用的能力，換句話說，具有抑制性的長期增强作用。增强作用可能是通過一種新型的CCK受體，而不是已知的CCKAR和CCKBR。囙此，本研究的目的是通過檢測以下內容來探索這一假設：1）在CCK-GABA神經元發生HFS後，抑制性GABA能的輸入或iLTP的增强；2）在CCKAR /BR-/-（簡稱CCKAB受體敲除）小鼠局部應用CCK後是否能產生iLTP，病毒注射後抑制性神經元的高頻刺激是否能在CCK敲除和CCKAB受體敲除的小鼠上誘導iLTP；3）與所有現有GPCR的已知CCK的受體，AR和BR相似，基於它們的蛋白質結構以及GABA-CCK末端和GABAAR與每個<10個入圍受體的共定位；4）在解剖學上確定的最終候選受體是否為CCK受體；5）候選受體的過表達是否可以增强iLTP。本研究致力於闡明抑制電路如何參與iLTP的形成。特別是，CCK-GABA神經元如何促進iLTP的形成並促進我們現時對iLTP潜在機制的理解，尤其是CCK-GABA神經元的作用。我們希望我們可以識別第三個CCK受體並命名其孤兒GPCR。它將推動我們對抑制性回路的神經可塑性的理解，這暗示著有可能通過調節抑制性-興奮性平衡來治療癲癇等腦部疾病。

11103220.label: Realisation of objectives
11103220.value: Objective 1: The HFLS of CCK-INs, but not PV-INs, enhances sIPSCs in glutamatergic neurons. To determine whether the enhanced GABAergic input inhibition was specific to CCK-INs, we used patch-clamp recordings of the pyramidal neurons. CCK-INs were targeted, with PV-INs as controls, given their significant presence in the cortex and hippocampus and role in perisomatic inhibition. Using a Cre recombinase-based genetic approach with the Dlx5/6 regulatory sequence, we specifically labeled CCK-INs and PV-INs in PV-Cre and CCK-Cre transgenic mice. Cre-dependent AAV virus was injected into the AC of PV-Cre or CCK-Cre mice to target PV-INs or CCK-INs comparably. We designed an AAV expressing Channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2) and mCherry under the control of the mDlx enhancer (rAAV9-mDlx-DIO-ChR2-mCherry-WPRE-pA, or mDlx-DIO-ChR2-mCherry). The virus predominantly labeled CCK-INs or PV-INs in CCK-Cre or PV-Cre mice, respectively (96.3% of mCherry-labeled neurons were GAD67+, 95.4 ± 1.6% were CCK+, 96.7 ± 1.2% were ChR2+ in CCK-Cre mice; 97.5 ± 1.0% of mCherry-labeled neurons were PV+, 98.2 ± 1.0% were ChR2+ in PV-Cre mice). Brain slices from CCK-Cre and PV-Cre mice were subjected to in vitro patch-clamp recordings. Pyramidal neurons identified by their morphology and regular spike trains were patched. Responses to step currents confirmed physiological properties, with IPSCs (latency of 4.53 ± 0.28 ms, n = 10 cells) recorded upon laser stimulation. HFLS potentiated IPSCs in CCK-Cre mice, but not in PV-Cre mice. Normalized IPSCs before and after HFLS showed no significant potentiation in PV-Cre mice (100.00 ± 2.43% vs 103.67 ± 7.00%, n = 7 neurons, two-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, p = 0.26, N.S.), whereas significant potentiation was observed in CCK-Cre mice (101.56 ± 5.73% vs 183.70 ± 6.25%, n = 9 neurons, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, ****p < 0.0001). Thus, HFLS of CCK-INs significantly potentiated IPSCs, indicating iLTP (183.70 ± 6.25% vs 103.67 ± 7.00%, two-way RM ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, ####p < 0.0001). Objective 2: Next, we aimed to determine which CCK receptor mediates iLTP in CCK-INs. We used CCK1R/2R-KO and CCK-KO mice to examine which CCK receptor mediates the contribution of CCK signaling to the iLTP of CCK-INs in brain slice experiments. We performed genotyping confirmation of CCK1R/2R-KO and CCK-KO mouse lines before virus injection and in vitro recording. We combined two viruses (mDlx-DIO-ChR2-mCherry and mDlx-Cre-helper rAAV9) that both contain mDlx and are expressed only in interneurons. The viruses were injected into the AC of CCK1R/2R-KO and CCK-KO mice. Immunohistochemical experiments examined whether the combined viruses were expressed in the target GABAergic neurons effectively and precisely. Confocal images showed that almost all infected neurons were GABAergic neurons in both mouse lines (one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, N.S.). In the following experiments, pyramidal neurons were selected for recording using in vitro patch clamping. HFLS of GABAergic neurons induced iLTP in recorded pyramidal neurons in CCK1R/2R-KO mice but not in CCK-KO mice (CCK1R/2R-KO mice, baseline vs 20–25 min after HFLS, 100.36 ± 2.91% vs 150.34 ± 5.32%, n = 9 neurons, two-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, ****p < 0.0001; CCK-KO mice, baseline vs 20–25 min after HFLS, 99.93 ± 2.22% vs 97.71 ± 2.98%, n = 9 neurons, two-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, p = 0.82, N.S.). These results indicate that CCK-enabled iLTP is likely mediated by a novel receptor other than CCK1R or CCK2R. Objective 3: Bioinformatics and binding assay search for potential CCK receptors. We speculated that a new CCK receptor mediates CCK8s-induced iLTP in the mouse AC, which is probably a GPCR similar to CCK1R/2R. The binding sites of all GPCR secondary structures (extramembrane) were selected based on the CCK binding domains of CCK1R and CCK2R, and the GPCRs were compared with the two CCK receptors based on hamming distance. We listed the GPCRs with the highest scores as probable candidates for CCK receptors. We hypothesis that if the novel CCK receptor mediates CCK signalling of CCK-GABA neurons on their postsynaptic neurons, the novel receptor should localize near the CCK-GABA synapses. To test the above hypothesis, we injected the mDlx-DIO-ChR2-mCherry in the AC of the CCK-Cre mouse. We examined the possible colocalization between GPCRs and CCK-GABA synapses, adopting triple-labelling of mCherry, synaptophysin, and the 7 orphan receptors with the highest correlation scores. We found that GPR173 has the highest colocalization density with CCK-GABA synapses compared with other 15 GPCRs including GPR85, CCK1R, CCK2R, GPR15, BRS3, GPR17, GPR135, GPR132, TAAR9, GPR19, GPR34, GPR83, GPR45, TAAR5, and GPR20 (3 independent experiments, GPR173 vs GPR85, the highest among others, 948.90 ± 35.36 vs 53.46 ± 17.68 numbers/mm2, one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, ***P < 0.0001), indicating that GPR173 is the most likely GPCR mediating CCK-GABA signalling. Objective 4: To evaluate which GPCR candidates were novel CCK receptors, we established a cell surface binding assay based on previous reports. We cloned the CDS of candidate GPCRs and CCK2R with an N-terminal Flag tag into pCDNA3.1(+) cells to transfect HEK293T cells. We synthesized HA-(ε-Ahx)2-CCK variant probes, including CCK4, CCK8s, non-sulfated CCK8 (CCK8ns), and the control HA-(ε-Ahx)2, which are known for their specificity for CCK1R/2R. As CCK8s are the main form of CCK in the brain, we used HA-tagged CCK8s for the initial screening of high-scoring GPCR candidates, including Flag-tagged GPR173, HTR2C, HTR1F, HTR2B, HTR1E, HTR1B, and NPY5R. We found that HA-tagged CCK4, CCK8ns, and CCK8s colocalized with Flag-tagged CCK2R, showing a significantly higher HA-tag to Flag signal ratio than that of the control group, validating our assay. CCK-2R and GPR173 bound to CCK8s, while other GPCR candidates did not. Detailed ligand specificity analysis using HA-tagged CCK4/CCK8ns/CCK8s probes, with HTR1B-expressing cells as a negative control, showed that FLAG-tagged GPR173 binds exclusively to HA-tagged CCK8s. No binding was detected for FLAG-tagged HTR1B. Thus, we conclude that GPR173 is a novel CCK receptor and CCK8s is its specific ligand. Objective 5: The upregulation of GPR173 in the cortex enhances iLTP through high-frequency laser stimulation (HFLS). We used a blood-brain barrier-penetrating AAV to infect the entire brain, producing AAV-PHP. eB carrying AAV-CMV-GPR173-eGFP-PHP.eB (CMV-GPR173-eGFP) or its control AAV-CMV-Sham-eGFP-PHP.eB (CMV-Sham-eGFP). To verify whether GPR173 upregulation enhances iLTP, we used brain slices from CCK-Cre mice for in vitro patch-clamp recordings two weeks post-virus injection. We patched pyramidal neurons in the virus-injected area of the AC and recorded inhibitory post-synaptic currents (IPSC) evoked by the laser stimulation of nearby inhibitory neurons. HFLS induced more significant IPSC potentiation in CMV-GPR173-eGFP-injected CCK-Cre mice compared to CMV-Sham-eGFP-injected CCK-Cre mice (baseline vs. 25-30 min post-HFLS of CMV-GPR173-eGFP: 100.01 ± 1.54% vs. 271.69 ± 18.43%, n = 12 neurons; HFLS of CMV-Sham-eGFP: 100.45 ± 1.45% vs. 158.15 ± 8.01%, n = 12 neurons; two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, ****P＜0.0001). No significant IPSC potentiation was observed after low-frequency laser stimulation (LFLS) in CMV-GPR173-eGFP-injected mice (baseline vs. 25-30 min post-LFLS: 100.17 ± 0.66% vs. 100.06 ± 1.66%, n = 13 neurons, two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, N.S.). Thus, the HFLS of CMV-GPR173-eGFP-injected CCK-GABA neurons significantly enhanced IPSC potentiation compared to CMV-Sham-eGFP (271.69 ± 18.43% vs. 158.15 ± 8.01%, two-way RM ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, ####P＜0.0001). These results indicate that exogenous GPR173 expression in CCK-GABA synapses increases the iLTP.

11103220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103220.value: We performed a patch-clamp recording of pyramidal neurons to examine whether the potentiated inhibition of GABAergic inputs was CCK-IN specific. HFLS of CCK-INs induced significant potentiation of IPSCs during the recording period, or iLTP (He et al., 2023). Next, we applied CCK followed by LFLS. iLTP in CCK-INs was induced by the application of CCK8s followed by LFLS but not in the aCSF control group (He et al., 2023). We then used CCK1R/2R-KO and CCK-KO mice to examine which CCK receptor mediates the contribution of CCK signaling to the iLTP of CCK-INs in brain slice experiments. HFLS of GABAergic neurons induced iLTP in recorded pyramidal neurons in CCK1R/2R-KO mice but not in CCK-KO mice. The same results were also repeated in in vivo recording experiments, indicating that a novel CCK receptor other than CCK1R or CCK2R is likely involved in mediating the signaling of CCK from CCK-Ins (He et al., 2023). We speculated that a new CCK receptor mediates CCK8s-induced iLTP in the mouse AC, which is probably a GPCR similar to CCK1R/2R. The binding sites of all GPCR secondary structures (extramembrane) were selected based on the CCK binding domains of CCK1R and CCK2R, and the GPCRs were compared with the two CCK receptors based on hamming distance. We listed the GPCRs with the highest scores as probable candidates for CCK receptors (He et al., 2023). We also established a cell surface binding assay, to further evaluate which of these GPCR candidates is a novel CCK receptor, and we conclude that GPR173 is a novel CCK receptor, and CCK8s is a ligand of GPR173(He et al., 2023). Our previous studies have shown that GPR173 mediates CCK signaling of the CCK-GABA synapse and the potentiation of inhibition. Therefore, we sought to restore the E/I balance in epilepsy by exogenously upregulating GPR173. We first examined whether CMV-GPR173-eGFP successfully upregulated GPR173 expression in the CCK-GABA synapses. The results showed that the GPR173 group had significantly higher counts and area of triple colocalizations than the sham group (He et al., Under Preparation). Next, we verified whether upregulation of GPR173 enhances iLTP. The HFLS of CMV-GPR173-eGFP-injected CCK-GABA neurons enhanced the potentiation of IPSC during the recording period, or iLTP, compared to the HFLS of CMV-Sham-eGFP. Our results demonstrated that exogenously increasing GPR173 expression within CCK-GABA synapses contributes to increased iLTP (He et al., Under Preparation).

11103220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103220.value: Our study focused on CCK-GABAergic output to pyramidal neurons. As CCK is colocalized in some VIP neurons, some VIP-INs preferentially inhibit SOM-INs, increasing their activity during whisking and leading to disinhibitory control in the cortex by inhibiting SOM-INs or PV-INs. Whether and how iLTP occurs among CCK-INs and other GABAergic neurons remains to be investigated. The anxiolytic effect of CCK-INs in the ventral hippocampus of rats and the observation that CCK-IN activity inversely scales with pyramidal cell activity suggests that CCK-INs also play a functional role in the hippocampus. How CCK-INs switch inhibitory plasticity in other brain areas and how they interact with other GABAergic neurons in inhibitory plasticity remain to be explored. In the current study, we could not exclude the possibility that CCK-IN–induced iLTP is restricted to the CCK postsynaptic area without affecting neighboring PV-IN synapses or other synapses. Whether this GPR173-mediated iLTP is homosynaptic or heterosynaptic remains to be investigated in the future.

11103220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103220.value: Cholecystokinin (CCK) facilitates excitatory circuit long-term potentiation (LTP). In this study, we investigated its role in enhancing inhibitory synapses. Activation of GABA neurons suppresses neuronal responses in the neocortex to a subsequent auditory stimulus in mice of both sexes. High-frequency laser stimulation (HFLS) of GABAergic neurons potentiated this suppression. HFLS of CCK interneurons induced LTP in their inhibition of pyramidal neurons. This potentiation was abolished in CCK knockout mice, but remained intact in mice with both CCK1R and 2R knockout in both sexes. Subsequently, a combination of bioinformatic analysis, multiple unbiased cell-based assays, and histological examinations identified a novel CCK receptor, GPR173. We propose GPR173 as a CCK3R, which is localized in the CCK-GABA synapses and mediates the enhancement of the GABA inhibition effect through cortical CCK interneuron signaling and inhibitory LTP in mice. Consequently, GPR173 may represent a promising therapeutic target for brain disorders related to excitation and inhibition imbalances in the cortex.

11103320.value: To develop a high pulse-repetition-rate, multi-wavelength laser. Stimulated Raman scattering, frequency encoding, and fiber-based delay techniques will be used to build a new OR-PAM laser source. The laser will have up to 1 MHz pulse repetition rate at each wavelength, a broad spectrum including 532nm~712nm, a sub-microsecond wavelength switching time, and several hundreds of nJ pulse energy. To develop fast-scanning OR-PAM based on a polygon scanner. A water-immersible polygon scanner will be developed to scan the aligned acoustic and optical beams at high speed. A voice-coil stage will be used as the slow-scanning axis. The OR-PAM will acquire cross-sectional (B-scan) images at ~3 kHz. The volumetric (C-scan) imaging speed will be up to ~20 Hz. To develop an algorithm for simultaneous quantification of multiple contrasts, including hemoglobin concentration, blood flow, oxygen saturation, the metabolic rate of oxygen, and tumor cells. Simultaneous imaging of melanoma tumor cells and multiple functional parameters will be demonstrated in vivo.

11103320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103320.value: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells to new areas of the body via blood or lymphatic circulations. Majority of cancer deaths are related to metastasis. Study of tumor metastasis mechanism can provide guidance and useful information to cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment, and drug development. Previous research has shown that local functional parameters play important roles in tumor growth and metastasis. In vivo high-resolution imaging of the dynamic process of tumor cell spreading into or extravasating from blood or lymphatic vessels, as well as quantification of the local functional parameters, may offer comprehensive information to the study of tumor metastasis. For example, such new imaging capability may uncover the relationship between the local oxygen supply and the tumor cell shedding rate, or may be used to test new cancer drugs. Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy (OR-PAM) is an emerging high-resolution functional imaging technique. In the past decade, OR-PAM has demonstrated in vivo imaging of total hemoglobin concentration, blood flow, oxygen saturation, metabolic rate of oxygen, and imaging labeled or non-labeled tumor cells in both shallow and deep tissues. However, due to slow imaging speed, OR-PAM imaging of the dynamic process of tumor metastasis have not been reported. In addition, OR-PAM has not demonstrated simultaneously imaging of the anatomical, functional, metabolic parameters with both high speed and large field of view. Most existing OR-PAM techniques require multiple times of scanning to measure different parameters, making it challenging to record multiple contrasts in real time. This proposal aims at developing high-speed multi-contrast OR-PAM based on a frequency-encoded broad-spectrum laser and a fast polygon scanner, to meet the need in realtime imaging of tumor metastasis in its microenvirment. To achieve this goal, two major technical challenges, slow imaging speed and narrow optical spectrum, will be addressed. A fast multi-wavelength pulsed laser and a fast polygon scanning technique will be developed for OR-PAM. To simultaneously image multiple contrasts, the proposed OR-PAM system will sequentially acquire multiple photoacoustic signals over a broad optical spectrum at each scanning spot. Fast water-immersible polygon scanner will offer up to 3 kHz cross-sectional imaging speed. The new OR-PAM system will be demonstrated in visualizing and quantifying the melanoma tumor metastasis process in vivo. The proposed research provide a new tool in the study of tumor metastasis mechanism, as well as other applications such as high-speed multi-contrast hemodynamic imaging in the brain. 癌細胞通過血液或淋巴循環會轉移擴散到身體的其它組織。大多數癌癥造成的死亡與轉移有關。對腫瘤轉移機制的研究可以為腫瘤的診斷、分期、治療和藥物開發提供指導和有用的信息。已有的研究表明微環境功能參數在腫瘤生長和轉移中起重要作用。對腫瘤細胞向血管或淋巴管擴散或滲出的動態過程進行活體高分辨率成像，並對微環境功能參數進行定量分析，可為研究腫瘤轉移機制提供全面的信息。例如，這種新的成像能力可以揭示局部供氧和腫瘤細胞脫落率之間的關系，或者可以用來測試新的抗癌藥物。光學分辨光聲顯微鏡（OR-PAM）是壹種新興的高分辨率功能成像技術。在過去的十年裏，OR-PAM已經被用於對血紅蛋白濃度，血流，血氧飽和度，氧代謝率，和腫瘤細胞進行活體成像。然而，由於成像速度慢，OR-PAM成像對腫瘤轉移的動態過程還未見報道。另外，OR-PAM還沒有同時顯示高速和大視場的解剖、功能、代謝參數成像。大多數現有的OR-PAM技術需要多次掃描來測量不同的參數，這使得實時記錄多個對比度變得困難。本項目旨在研製壹種基於寬譜激光與快速掃描的高速、多對比度OR-PAM，以滿足腫瘤轉移微環境實時成像的需要。為了實現這壹目標，項目將研制快速多波長脈沖激光和快速多邊形掃描技術，並且在每個掃描點連續獲取多個寬光譜光聲信號。通過快速水浸式多邊形掃描，系統將實現高達3千赫的二維成像速度。新的OR-PAM系統將在活體內顯示和量化黑色素瘤腫瘤轉移過程。本研究為腫瘤轉移機制的研究提供了壹個新的工具，也為腦內高速多對比度血流動力學成像等應用提供了新的工具。

11103320.label: Realisation of objectives
11103320.value: The three objectives were fully achieved. We developed a high pulse-repetition-rate, multi-wavelength laser. Stimulated Raman scattering, frequency encoding, and fiber-based delay techniques were used to build the laser source. The laser will have up to 1 MHz pulse repetition rate at each wavelength, a broad spectrum including 532nm~712nm, a sub-microsecond wavelength switching time, and several hundreds of nJ pulse energy. Based on the advanced laser, we further developed fast-scanning OR-PAM based on a polygon scanner. A water-immersible polygon scanner was developed to scan the aligned acoustic and optical beams at high speed. A voice-coil stage was also used for scanning. The OR-PAM can acquire volumetric imaging up to 4~20 Hz, depending on different field of view. We develop software for simultaneous quantification of multiple contrasts, including hemoglobin concentration, blood flow, oxygen saturation, the metabolic rate of oxygen, and tumor cells. Simultaneous imaging of tumor growth and multiple functional parameters were demonstrated in vivo.

11103320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103320.value: We show that a high pulse-repetition-rate, multi-wavelength laser in the visible range can be developed for advaned photoacoustic imaging. The laser will have up to 1 MHz pulse repetition rate at each wavelength, a broad spectrum including 532nm~712nm, a sub-microsecond wavelength switching time, and several hundreds of nJ pulse energy. We validate the fast-scanning OR-PAM with a polygon scanner or a voice-coil stage can achieve multipe-wavelength imaging at high speed, and can simultaneously quantify multiple contrasts, including hemoglobin concentration, blood flow, oxygen saturation, the metabolic rate of oxygen, and tumor growth.

11103620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103620.value: 腫瘤轉移是當今世界癌症高死亡率的根本原因。不到10％的癌症患者死於原發性腫瘤，而高達90％的癌症患者死於腫瘤轉移。內體運輸是一個進化上保守的細胞過程，在腫瘤轉移中起重要作用。然而，調控內體運輸的分子機制還很不清楚。先前我們證明了一種小分子化合物Vacuolin-1（V1）通過激活RAB5阻止早期內體到晚期內體的轉變，並導致形成大的早期內體。我們還證明，V1顯著抑制異種移植和轉基因小鼠模型中各種癌細胞的轉移，這表明V1是一種潛在的抗腫瘤轉移藥物。在當前的研究中，我們發現用CRISPR/Cas9敲除封蓋蛋白Z beta（CapZβ）能消除了V1誘導細胞中形成大的早期內體的能力。我們還發現CapZβ能定位在早期內體上，並且用V1處理細胞會導致CapZβ在漲大的早期內體表面積聚。但是，CapZβ敲除顯著抑制了早期內體的成熟和細胞遷移，而表達抗sgRNA的CapZβ能挽救這些缺陷。我們也證明了RAB5在CapZβ敲除細胞中的活性較低。此外，在原位轉移小鼠模型中，CapZβ敲除顯著抑制了乳腺癌細胞的轉移。我們假設CapZβ通過調節RAB5來控制早期內體的成熟。因此，在本課題中，我們將：（1）進一步確定CapZβ在早期內體成熟中的功能；（2）剖析CapZβ介導的早期內體成熟的分子機制。鑑於功能失常的內體運輸與包括癌症在內的許多人類疾病有關，該項目的成功不僅將闡明內體運輸的分子機制，並且將揭示癌症治療的其他藥物靶標。

11103620.label: Realisation of objectives
11103620.value: Realisation of the objectives 1. To Further Determine the Function of CapZ in Early Endosome Maturation CapZ, a heterodimeric protein complex composed of α and β subunits, plays a pivotal role in early endosome maturation. Our studies revealed that CapZ regulates the actin dynamics required for vesicle fusion by capping actin filaments, ensuring controlled polymerization and depolymerization around early endosomes (EEs). Specifically, CapZ docks to EEs via its C-terminal actin-binding motif, where it facilitates RAB5 activation by recruiting key RAB5 effectors such as Rabaptin-5 and Rabex-5. These interactions are critical for the progression of early endosomes to late endosomes (LEs). In CapZ knockout cells, we observed an increased density of F-actin surrounding immature early endosomes, leading to impaired vesicle fusion and an accumulation of small vesicles. Vacuolin-1 (V1), a triazine analog, stabilizes CapZ on early endosomes, effectively blocking their maturation into LEs. This disruption impairs critical trafficking processes such as integrin recycling and focal adhesion turnover, which are essential for cancer cell motility and invasion. Consequently, in vitro experiments showed significant reductions in cancer cell migration, invasion, and colony formation following V1 treatment. In vivo, we demonstrated that these effects translate to reduced metastasis and tumor growth in breast cancer and melanoma mouse models, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting CapZ-mediated endosome maturation (DOI: 10.1186/s12915-024-01819-y; DOI: 10.7554/eLife.65910). Beyond cancer, CapZ also regulates the trafficking processes exploited by viruses during infection. Stabilizing CapZ at early endosomes with V1 or using a rapamycin-induced artificial tethering system prevented the maturation of early endosomes, thereby blocking the escape of viral RNA from endocytic vesicles. This mechanism significantly inhibited infections by flaviviruses (e.g., Zika virus and dengue virus) and beta-coronaviruses (e.g., murine hepatitis virus). These findings suggest that CapZ-mediated actin regulation and RAB5 activation are crucial for endosomal dynamics in both physiological and pathological contexts (DOI: 10.1186/s12915-024-01819-y; DOI: 10.7554/eLife.65910). 2. To Dissect the Molecular Mechanisms Underlying CapZ-Mediated Early Endosome Maturation We further dissected the molecular mechanisms by which CapZ orchestrates early endosome maturation. CapZ transiently associates with early endosomes and is released upon vesicle fusion, a process driven by the phosphoinositide switch from phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P) to phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate (PI(3,5)P2). Stabilizing CapZ at early endosomes with V1 or artificially tethering CapZ to EEs using a rapamycin-induced system blocked this phosphoinositide-driven transition, effectively halting early-to-late endosome progression (DOI: 10.7554/eLife.65910). We explored the implications of this mechanism in immune evasion by focusing on PD-L1, a key immune checkpoint protein. Our studies demonstrated that PD-L1 undergoes continuous endocytosis and trafficking through early endosomes, late endosomes, lysosomes, and extracellular vesicles (EVs). This process, dependent on Rab5, CapZ, and clathrin, is disrupted by the triazine analog 6J1, which activates CapZ-Rab5 signaling and leads to PD-L1 accumulation in early endosomes. Additionally, 6J1 promotes exosomal secretion of PD-L1 via Rab27 activation, reducing PD-L1 levels on the tumor cell surface and enhancing tumor cell susceptibility to T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In vivo, 6J1 treatment increased tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells and enhanced chemokine secretion in the tumor microenvironment. These effects were reversed by Rab27 knockdown, demonstrating the critical role of PD-L1 secretion in immune modulation. Notably, combining 6J1 with anti-PD-1 antibody therapy significantly amplified the anti-cancer immune response, emphasizing the therapeutic potential of targeting endosomal trafficking pathways (DOI: 10.1002/advs.202206411; DOI: 10.7554/eLife.65910). CapZ’s role in actin regulation and RAB5 activation emerged as central to its function in early endosome maturation. By capping actin filaments and coordinating the recruitment of RAB5 effectors, CapZ ensures precise vesicle dynamics. These findings not only advance our understanding of endosomal trafficking but also provide a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies targeting CapZ-mediated pathways. For example, stabilizing CapZ with V1 or modulating its interactions with RAB5 effectors can be leveraged to inhibit cancer metastasis, enhance immune responses, and prevent viral infections (DOI: 10.1186/s12915-024-01819-y; DOI: 10.7554/eLife.65910). Conclusion Our research highlights CapZ as a critical regulator of early endosome maturation and elucidates its molecular mechanisms in trafficking dynamics. Composed of α and β subunits, CapZ caps actin filaments and facilitates RAB5 activation, ensuring efficient vesicle fusion and cargo sorting. Triazine analogs such as V1 and 6J1 disrupt these pathways, providing therapeutic avenues to inhibit metastasis, enhance immune modulation, and combat viral infections. These findings underscore the broad implications of CapZ-mediated endosomal trafficking in diverse pathological processes.

11103620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103620.value: For therapeutic applications, the optimization of triazine analogs like V1 and 6J1 is a critical next step. Developing derivatives with improved pharmacokinetics and reduced off-target effects could enhance their efficacy and safety profiles. Combining these compounds with existing treatments, such as immune checkpoint inhibitors or standard chemotherapies, in preclinical and clinical studies, would help evaluate their potential in enhancing anti-cancer immunity and reducing metastasis. Another promising direction is the exploration of CapZ’s role in viral infections. Investigating its function in other viruses, particularly those utilizing endosomal trafficking for entry or replication, could identify CapZ as a universal therapeutic target. Furthermore, studying the interplay between CapZ-mediated trafficking and immune responses could reveal novel strategies to combat viral evasion mechanisms. We propose a systematic course of action, beginning with detailed mechanistic studies of CapZ's interactions and functions using advanced imaging and proteomics. Parallel development of next-generation triazine compounds will focus on optimizing their efficacy. Preclinical trials in relevant cancer and viral infection models will validate these findings, paving the way for eventual clinical translation. Collaborations with pharmaceutical and immunology experts will ensure robust development of these promising therapeutic strategies.

11103620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103620.value: Triazine compounds, like V1 and 6J1, are potent compounds that inhibit endosomal trafficking and show promise in combating metastasis and enhancing anti-cancer immunity. We demonstrated that V1 or 6J1 inhibits autophagosome-lysosome fusion and general endosomal-lysosomal degradation, suppressing cancer cell migration, invasion, and colony formation, while disrupting focal adhesion dynamics by preventing integrin recycling and degradation. In vivo, V1 or 6J1 significantly reduces metastasis and tumor growth in breast cancer and melanoma models. V1 or 6J1 targets capping protein Z (CapZ), a protein essential for regulating endosomal trafficking, by stabilizing it at early endosomes (EEs), which blocks the transition of EEs to late endosomes (LEs). We also explore the role of 6J1, which inhibits PD-L1 endosomal trafficking via activating CapZ-Rab5 signaling, accumulating PD-L1 in early endosomes and promoting exosomal PD-L1 secretion by activating Rab27. This reduces PD-L1 membrane levels in tumor cells, making them more susceptible to T cell-mediated killing. In vivo, 6J1 increases tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells and chemokine secretion, and combining 6J1 with anti-PD-1 antibody enhances the anticancer immune response. Together, these findings highlight the potential of V1 and 6J1 as therapeutic agents targeting endosomal trafficking to treat both cancer metastasis and viral diseases.

11104020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104020.value: hnRNP A1, a member of the large RNA-binding protein family (hnRNPs), exhibits important roles in transcription, RNA splicing and stability, translation, as well as viral activities. The dysregulation of hnRNP A1 contributes to a number of diseases, including human cancers and neurodegenerative diseases (such as spinal muscular atrophy, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, HTLV-1 associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis, fronto-temporal lobar degeneration, etc.). Many neural diseases are associated with viral infections, in particular, infection by picornaviruses. hnRNP A1 is well known in its redistribution in the cytosol and its binding with internal ribosome entry site (IRES) to enhance IRES-mediated translation after infection by positive-sense (+) single-stranded RNA virus. However, little is known on the molecular mechanism of hnRNP A1 relocalization. In our previous GRF-funded project, we investigated how Hsp27 responds to enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) infection and contributes to its life cycle [Ref. 21]. Results from our and others’ studies reveal an important mechanism: viral infection largely induces hnRNP A1 protein relocalization in the cytosol to enhance IRES-mediated viral protein translation. Importantly, we showed that hnRNP A1 is almost completely blocked in the nucleus without affecting the cytosol distribution of FBP1 [21], hnRNP L, and AUF1upon EV-A71 infection when Hsp27 is knocked out by CRISPR-Cas9 mediated gene editing [21]. Our recent study showed that hnRNP A1 relocalization in the cytosol is reversely correlated with Hsp27 nuclear localization. Furthermore, the nuclear relocalization of Hsp27 is positively correlated with Hsp27 phosphorylation during viral replication. For the first time, we showed that besides nuclear pore components, the well-known host factor Hsp27 can also play a function in regulating hnRNP A1 relocalization. This provides us with a precious opportunity and platform in demonstrating the molecular mechanism of RNA binding proteins’ relocalization between the nucleus and cytosol. We hypothesize that Hsp27 nuclear translocation, induced by EV-A71 or its viral components, is essential for hnRNP A1 relocalization, and that the process of Hsp27 nuclear translocation is determined by the phosphorylation status of Hsp27. In this following study, our objectives are to investigate the structural basis of Hsp27 essential for (1) the nuclear relocalization of Hsp27 and (2) the cytosol relocalization of hnRNP A1, and (3) viral components that cooperate with Hsp27 in regulating hnRNP A1 relocalization. Our study will not only shed light on the regulation of hnRNPs relocalization, but also provide a solid basis for developing drugs used to treat multiple human diseases. hnRNP A1是一个RNA结合蛋白家族（hnRNPs）的成员，在基因转录、RNA剪接、RNA稳定性、蛋白质翻译以及病毒活性中发挥重要作用。 hnRNP A1失调导致许多疾病，包括人类癌症和神经退行性疾病（例如脊髓性肌萎缩、肌萎缩性侧索硬化、老年痴呆、神经多发性硬化等）。许多神经疾病与病毒感染有关，特别是与小核糖核酸病毒感染有关。 hnRNP A1重新分布在胞质与病毒IRES的结合，增强正链RNA病毒蛋白质翻译。但是，目前我们对hnRNP A1重新定位的分子机制知之甚少。 在前一个GRF资助项目中，我们研究了Hsp27如何响应肠道病毒A71（EV-A71）感染对病毒生活史的重要影响。病毒感染导致hnRNP A1蛋白在细胞质中重新定位，从而增强了IRES介导的病毒蛋白翻译。通过CRISPR-Cas9介导的基因编辑敲除Hsp27，hnRNP A1在核中几乎完全被封闭，而不会影响FBP1，hnRNP L和AUF1在胞浆分布。hnRNP A1在细胞质中的重新定位与Hsp27核定位副相关。此外，在病毒复制过程中，Hsp27的核再定位与Hsp27磷酸化呈正相关。我们首次表明，除了核孔成分外，Hsp27可以在调节hnRNP A1重新定位中作用。这为我们展示RNA结合蛋白在细胞核与细胞质之间重新定位的分子机制提供了宝贵的机会和平台。在此研究中，我们将研究（1）Hsp27的核定位和（2）hnRNP A1的胞质重新定位的结构基础，以及（3）病毒的分子成分如何协同Hsp27调节hnRNP A1重新定位的结构基础。这项研究不仅将阐明hnRNPs重新定位的分子机制，还将为开发用于治疗多种人类疾病的药物提供坚实的基础。
