11104020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104020.value: A positive-sense (+) single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) virus (e.g. enterovirus A71, EV-A71) depends on viral polypeptide translation for initiation of virus replication after entry. EV-A71 hijacks Hsp27 to induce hnRNP A1 cytosol redistribution to initiate viral protein translation, but the underlying mechanism is still elusive. Through this GRF supported studies, we demonstrate that phosphorylation-deficient Hsp27-3A (Hsp27S15/78/82A) and Hsp27S78A fail to translocate into the nucleus and induce hnRNP A1 cytosol redistribution, while Hsp27S15A and Hsp27S82A display similar effects to the wild type Hsp27. The viral 2A protease (2Apro) activity is a key factor in regulating Hsp27/hnRNP A1 relocalization. Hsp27S78A dramatically decreases the IRES activity and viral replication, which are partially reduced by Hsp27S82A. However, Hsp27S15A displays the same activity as the wild-type Hsp27. Peptide S78 potently suppresses EV-A71 protein translation and reproduction through blockage of EV-A71-induced Hsp27 phosphorylation and Hsp27/hnRNP A1 relocalization. A point mutation (S78A) on S78 impairs its inhibitory functions on Hsp27/hnRNP A1 relocalization and viral replication (Part C, Section 8, Ref 2). Besides, we also demonstrate that the deletion of WDPF and ACD domains disturbs subcellular localization of Hsp27, resulting in partial nuclear translocation. The domain deletion-induced Hsp27 nuclear translocation fails to direct hnRNP A1 translocation. The 2Apro-induced IRES activity and viral replication are suppressed by the deletion of WDPF or ACD domain. Surprisingly, a peptide (WDPF) dramatically inhibits S78 phosphorylation. Therefore, hnRNP A1 translocation, viral IRES activity, and viral protein translation and propagation are all strongly suppressed by the WDPF peptide, but not by peptide without WDPFR sequence (ΔWDPF). Moreover, the WDPF peptide also has potent antiviral activity on other RNA virus (e.g., coronavirus HCoV-OC43) and DNA virus (e.g., HSV-1 and HBV). Peptide treatment with kinase inhibitor Sorafenib brings an additional inhibitory effect on HCoV-OC43 and HSV-1 (Part C, Section 8, Ref 3). Taken together, we demonstrate the importance of Ser78 phosphorylation of Hsp27 regulated by virus infection in nuclear translocation, hnRNP A1 cytosol relocation, and viral replication. We also uncover a crucial role of WDPF domain in S78 phosphorylation for EV-A71-induced hnRNP A1 nuclear translocation, IRES-dependent viral protein translation, and EV-A71 propagation. Our results explore a new path for target-based pan-antiviral strategy (Part C, Sect 11 (3)—patents and unpublished data).

11104220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104220.value: The cerebellum is a critical part of the brain responsible mainly for motor coordination and sensorimotor learning. It enables accurate and precise movement which requires precision at scale of millisecond despite delay in sensory feedback through various forms of learning. An important research question for cerebellum has been to elucidate the relationship between its anatomical structure and its computational function. Cerebellum forms various feedforward and feedback projections both internally and with many pre- and post-cerebellar regions. Although it is known that closed-loop circuitries between cortical and subcortical regions can modulate the neural function to facilitate control, little is known about the role of these feedbacks (especially positive feedback) in the cerebellar system. Our preliminary studies show that by inhibiting the projection from interpositus nucleus (Int), a subnucleus of deep cerebellum nucleus (DCN), to pontine nucleus (PN), acquisition of delay eyeblink conditioning (dEBC), a classical form of cerebellum-dependent associative learning, was significantly slowed down in rats. We speculate that efference copy signal from Int is fed back to the cerebellar cortex via PN to modulate motor learning. However, the mechanism of this novel nucleo-pontine-cortical feedback pathway in mediating motor learning remains to be elucidated in detail. In this proposed study, we will first test the hypothesis that manipulating the Int-to-PN projection during the conditioned motor response (CR) time windows will have the most significant effect on dEBC acquisition and expression. This will provide evidence to support that motor-related signal plays the most significant role in modulating behavior via this pathway. Next, we will use Cre-dependent viral-based and chemical neural tracing to characterize the properties of this nucleo-pontine-cortical pathway. These neural tracing experiments will provide evidence to test the following hypotheses: (1) the Int-to-PN projection conveys excitatory efference copy signal (hence a positive feedback); (2) a subpopulation of PN neurons integrates feedforward auditory sensory signal and feedback efference copy signal and conveys them to the cerebellar cortex to modulate dEBC motor learning. Finally, we will perform whole cell patch clamp recording on brain slice to characterize the electrophysiological properties of this feedback pathway by examining the response properties of the neurons in the PN and cerebellar cortex. The success of this proposed study will advance our understanding about how feedback circuitries contribute to motor learning and control in the brain. These knowledge will potentially inspire new clinical application of eyeblink reflex and development of more robust brain-machine interface. 小腦是大腦的關鍵部分，主要負責運動協調和感覺運動學習。它可以實現精確而精確的運動，儘管通過各種形式的學習會延遲感官反饋，但仍需要毫秒級的精度。小腦的一個重要研究問題是闡明其解剖結構與計算功能之間的關係。小腦在內部以及許多小腦前后區域形成各種前饋和反饋投影。儘管已知皮質和皮質下區域之間的閉環迴路可以調節神經功能以促進控制，但對於這些反饋（尤其是正反饋）在小腦系統中的作用知之甚少。 我們的初步研究表明，通過抑制深層小腦核（DCN）的中間層間核（Int）到橋腦核（PN）的投射，可以獲得延遲眨眼條件（dEBC），這是小腦依賴型聯想的經典形式大鼠的學習明顯減慢。我們推測來自Int的參考複製信號會通過PN反饋到小腦皮層，從而調節運動學習。然而，這種新穎的核-橋-皮層反饋途徑介導運動學習的機制仍有待詳細闡明。 在這項擬議的研究中，我們將首先檢驗以下假設：在條件運動響應（CR）時間窗口期間操縱Int-PN投影將對dEBC的獲取和表達產生最顯著的影響。這將提供證據支持運動相關信號在通過該途徑調節行為中起最重要的作用。接下來，我們將使用Cre依賴的基於病毒的和化學神經示踪技術來表徵這種核-橋蛋白-皮層通路的特性。這些神經追踪實驗將為檢驗以下假設提供證據：（1）Int-to-PN投影傳達興奮性複制信號（因此產生正反饋）； （2）PN神經元亞群整合前饋聽覺感覺信號和反饋效應複製信號，並將其傳遞至小腦皮層以調節dEBC運動學習。最後，我們將在腦切片上進行全細胞膜片鉗記錄，以通過檢查PN和小腦皮層中神經元的響應特性來表徵該反饋途徑的電生理特性。這項擬議研究的成功將促進我們對反饋電路如何促進大腦運動學習和控制的理解。這些知識可能會激發眨眼反射的新臨床應用，並開發出更強大的腦機接口。

11104220.label: Realisation of objectives
11104220.value: In investigating the role of Int-to-PN project on delay eyeblink conditioning (dEBC) (Objective 1), we inhibited or excited this pathway by optogenetic during dEBC training in rats. In the inhibition experiment, we unilaterally injected AAV2/9-hSyn-eNpHR3.0-EYFP or AAV2/9-hSyn-EYFP (as control) into the Int region of the rats and implanted an optrode into contralateral PN region to deliver the light (589 nm, 3-5 mW/mm2) in order to inhibit the axonal terminals from Int neurons at PN specifically. Furthermore, to examine the critical time window where this Int-to-PN pathway affects dEBC, we applied light inhibition at three different time windows to the eNpHR expressing rats, which were defined as OverCS (the whole period of CS), PreCR (from onset of CS and lasts for 100 ms), DurCR (from 100 ms after CS onset until the termination of CS). The CR% for each training day was calculated such that the learning curve could be constructed. Our results showed that, light inhibition significantly decreased the learning rate of DurCR group and OverCS group. The learning rate of the PreCR group was slightly lower than the control group, but did not reach statistical significance. Nevertheless, learning rate of the OverCS group was significantly lower than the PreCR group. On the other hand, CR amplitude, onset latency and peak latency show no significant difference among the groups. These results clearly show that light inhibition of the Int-to-PN projection during the CR window significantly slows down the acquisition of dEBC. On the other hand, in the excitation experiment, we injected AAV2/9-hSyn-ChR2(H134R)-mCherry or AAV2/9-hSyn-mCherry (as control) into one side of Int region. The light excited ChR2 group showed significantly higher CR% than the mCherry control group at the end of first day of training. Afterwards, both groups reached similar maximum CR% at sessions 2 and 3. Similar to the inhibition experiment, no significant difference was observed between the ChR2 group and control group for CR amplitude, onset latency and peak latency. As such, light excitation of the Int-to-PN projection can enhance the acquisition of dEBC. Together, these results clearly indicate that the Int-to-PN projection plays a critical role in facilitating learning in the cerebellum-mediated associative conditioning. Next, to characterize the morphology of the Int-to-PN project (Objective 2a), we injected anterograde AAV-vector into the Int region of cerebellar nucleus, we found that virus-expressing Int neurons predominantly project to the contralateral PN and they form longitudinally oriented columns distributed throughout the caudal half of the basilar pons. In addition, some Int axonal terminals were found in the reticulotegmental nucleus of the pons (RtTg). We further characterized these axonal fibers from Int on the mCherry-expressing PN slices with IHC staining of vGlut1 and vGlut2 antibodies. Our results show that these axonal terminals were vGlut1 positive, but vGlut2 negative. This finding indicates that the monosynaptic projections from Int to contralateral PN are glutamatergic and hence a positive feedback pathway. Next, we retrogradely labelled Int neurons that project to both PN and red nucleus (RN). It is known that RN is the direct downstream region that accepts output signals of the Int and controls motor movement of eyeblink responses. Hence, an Int neuron that projects to both RN and PN forms the substrate of conveying the efference copy signal through Int-to-PN projection which can potentially be fed back to the cerebellar cortex from PN to participate learning. We injected retrograde tracers Ctb Alexa Fluor 488 (Ctb488, green color) and Ctb Alexa Fluor 555 (Ctb555, red color) into the left RN and the left PN, respectively. Ctb488 and/or Ctb555 labeled neurons were observed in the right Int area. The presence of Ctb488/Ctb555 double labeled Int neurons would verify our hypothesis of efference copy feedback. In examining a series of coronal images, we have found that out of the 216 Int neurons projecting to PN, 106 of them also project to RN (PN+/RN+). Hence, our results suggest that around half of the Int-to-PN projection could convey efference copy signals from the presumptively excitatory Int neurons that project to RN. Our neural tracing and behavioral experimental results above suggest that PN may also relay CR-related signals from Int, in addition to the conditional sensory inputs. In this regard, we hypothesize that the firing of some PN neurons should correlate with the CR-related feedback signal and/or the feedforward sensory input signals simultaneously. We performed multiunit recording from PN region in a group of eNpHR3.0 expressing rats during dEBC training (Objective 3). Neuronal activities in PN region were recorded during the conditioning with or without the light inhibition. We hypothesize that a CS-relay neuron should have strong firing in the PreCR window in both CR and non-CR trials while a CR-relay neuron should have strong firing in the DurCR window in CR trials, but much reduced in non-CR trials. We identified 3 types of responsive PN neurons, namely PN1, PN2 and PN3 based on their response pattern, PN1 neurons are innervated primarily by CR-related inputs. PN2 neurons should receive both feedforward and feedback inputs. The firing of these neurons followed the learning of CR throughout the training and hence they are likely to convey CR-related input from Int. On the other hand, PN3 neurons are primarily innervated by feedforward tone CS input only. The rest of the recorded PN neurons (Non responsive) did not show any systematic response relevant to dEBC. In our behavioral and electrophysiological experiments, it has been suggested that efference copy is conveyed by two kinds of PN neurons (PN1 & PN2). To exam the morphological properties of these PN neurons in the cerebellar learning circuitry (Objective 2b), we used cyclization recombinase (Cre) and flippase recombinase (Flp) dependent AAVs to trace these specific pathways. We first injected trans-synaptic viruses AAV2/9-hSyn-Coff/Fon-ChR2(H134R)-EYFP into PN, AAV2/1-hSyn-Flpo into Int, and AAV2/1-hSyn-Cre into MATN. In this way, the EYFP expressing PN neurons should belong to PN1 group, which were predominantly found in the contralateral medial part of PN, and they were found to be CaMK2α positive, indicating that these neurons are glutamatergic. The MFs originated from these PN1 neurons were predominantly observed in the contralateral cerebellar lobules (HIV, HV, HVI) and lobule simplex, some MFs rosettes were found in the ipsilateral hemisphere. The IHC staining shown that the PN1 neuron projecting MFs rosettes express presynaptic vesicular glutamate transporter isoforms vGlut1 but not vGlut2. In another set of experiment, we injected trans-synaptic viruses AAV2/1-hSyn-Cre and AAV2/1-hSyn-Flpo into the right Int and the left MATN, respectively, and Cre and Flp double-dependent virus AAV2/9-hSyn-Con/Fon-EYFP into the left PN. As such, EYFP will be expressed in PN neurons that receive both MATN and Int projections (i.e. PN2). We observed that the EYFP-labeled neurons are mainly found in the contralateral caudal medial part of the PN, with some of the neurons scattering at the lateral PN. Compare with the PN1 neurons, the PN2 neurons were clearly fewer in number. In addition, the EYFP-labeled PN2 neurons are also CaMK2-α positive. Then we also observed the MFs projected from those PN2 neurons in the cerebellar cortex. Their MFs were predominately found in the cerebellar lobule (HIV, HV, HVI) and lobule simplex in the contralateral hemisphere. Moreover, these MFs formed rosettes are both vGlut1 and vGlut2 positive. Notably, pre-cerebellar rosettes expressing exclusively vGlut1 or vGlut2 were also observed.

11104220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104220.value: The cerebellum is critical for motor coordination and learning. However, the role of feedback circuitry in this brain region has not been fully explored. Here, we characterized a nucleo-ponto-cortical feedback pathway in classical delayed eyeblink conditioning (dEBC) of rats. We found that the efference copy is conveyed from the interposed nucleus (Int) to cerebellar cortex through pontine nucleus (PN). Inhibiting or exciting the projection from Int to PN can decelerate or speed up acquisition of dEBC, respectively. Importantly, we uncovered two subpopulation of PN neurons (PN1 and PN2) which convey and integrate the feedback signals with feedforward sensory signals. We have also showed that the feedforward and feedback pathways via different types of PN neurons contribute to the plastic changes and cooperate synergistically to the learning of dEBC. Our results suggest that this excitatory nucleo-ponto-cortical feedback plays a significant role in modulating associative motor learning in cerebellum. The findings from this project has been published in Cell Reports. We have also presented our findings in invited talks at Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology (China) and University of Strasbourg (France).

11104220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11104220.value: The novel Int-to-PN pathway uncovered in this study has revealed its important function in the cerebellum-mediated motor learning. Further development may incorporate this pathway in the computational cerebellum model we have developed in our previous research and to further explore it computational capability. We envision that this will inspire new research on cerebellum intelligence for some real world engineering application. On the other hand, the specific contribution of PN1 and PN2 in dEBC and their projection to the specific types of cerebellar neurons (e.g. granule cells or Golgi cells) can be further explored with more sophisticated genetic engineering tools to express the opsin specifically on PN1 or PN2 neurons to achieve well isolated optical manipulation of the cells in vivo.

11104220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11104220.value: The cerebellum is a critical part of the brain responsible mainly for motor coordination and sensorimotor learning. Furthermore, recent studies point to new higher level cognitive function contributed by cerebellum as well indicating that the cerebellar system is indeed a very powerful computing machine in our brain that is beyond our previous expectation. Cerebellum forms various feedforward and feedback projections both internally and with many pre- and post-cerebellar regions. However, little is known about the role of the feedbacks (especially positive feedback) within the cerebellar system. Our studies characterized a nucleo-ponto-cortical pathway which conveys efference copy from deep cerebellar nucleus back to cerebellar cortex via two specific population of pontine neurons. This feedback pathway is shown to be crucial for mediating the learning speed of cerebellar associate learning.

11104320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11104320.value: 飢餓如何影響嗅覺以改變食物搜索需求

11104320.label: Project Objectives
11104320.value: To determine how fasting alters food-searching behavior by modulating the anterior piriform cortex (APC). To examine how fasting regulates excitation-inhibition balance in the APC. To examine how fasting controls inhibitory neuron subtypes and their circuitry.
rows: To determine how fasting alters food-searching behavior by modulating the anterior piriform cortex (APC).
To examine how fasting regulates excitation-inhibition balance in the APC.
To examine how fasting controls inhibitory neuron subtypes and their circuitry.

11104320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104320.value: We are all familiar with the scenario, “Oh, what’s that (good) smell?” Food searching and energy intake is essential to survival of all animals. The availability of metabolic energy critically determines the state in which an animal’s behavior exists. For example, an animal will prioritize for food foraging instead of mating when energy availability is low. The olfactory sense is critical to food searching. Although much is known about the neuromodulatory processes that regulate olfaction system, little is known about how the animal’s metabolic and behavioral state regulates olfactory circuits and food searching behavior. The anterior piriform cortex (APC) is one of the largest regions of olfactory cortex and is instrumental to the formation of an odor percept. As close as just one synapse downstream of the olfactory bulb (OB), principal neurons in APC can encode for multiple features of odorants such as identity, concentration and value. However, how principal neurons and its gating by inhibitory interneurons contribute to hunger-regulated odor perception remains elusive. Our group has recently identified two distinct neuronal circuits for routing information from APC back to OB: the superficial pyramidal (SP) cell receives recurrent excitation and projects back to the OB, while the semilunar (SL) cell lacks both connections. We obtained preliminary data suggesting that inhibitory transmission in SP, but not SL, cell activity is robustly reduced by fasting. Here we propose that GABAergic circuits in APC switches the effects of fasting on enhanced food-seeking behavior. This proposal is undertaken to examine the hypothesis that hunger-dependent plasticity of inhibitory circuits control SP cell function, thereby regulating food-seeking behavior. I will use a combination of slice electrophysiology, optogenetics, food deprivation, odor search behavioral analysis, mouse genetics, and immunofluorescent staining to probe the contribution of inhibitory transmission on SP cell activity and olfaction. Objective 1 will determine how fasting alters food-searching behavior in mice and how this depends on APC circuits. Objective 2 will examine how fasting regulates excitation-inhibition (E-I) balance in the APC. Objective 3 will examine how fasting anatomically regulates specific inhibitory neurons and their synapses. Elucidating how inhibition controls principal neurons in regulating food-search behavior will provide a framework for understanding how olfaction contributes to energy homeostasis. 食物搜尋和能量攝取對所有動物的生存至關重要。我們對飲食如何影響神經遞質和激素瞭解甚多，但對新陳代謝和行為狀態如何調節嗅覺還路和食物搜尋行為知之甚少。前梨狀皮層（APC）是嗅覺皮層最大區域之一，有助於形成氣味感知。APC主要神經元可以編碼氣味的多種特徵，例如濃度和價值。然而， APC神經還路如何介導飢餓感對氣味知覺的調節仍尚待發現。我們的研究小組最近發現了兩個截然不同的神經元還路，用於將信息從APC路由回嗅球：淺層錐體（SP）細胞接收復發性刺激並發送軸突反饋，而半月球（SL）細胞則欠缺這兩種連接。我們的初步數據表明，禁食可顯著降低SP而非SL細胞的抑制性傳遞。在此，我們假設GABA能還路的飢餓可塑性控制著主要神經元功能，從而調節著覓食行為。我們將使用膜片鉗電生理學，光遺傳學，氣味搜索行為，小鼠遺傳學和免疫熒光染色進行研究。目標1將確定禁食如何改變小鼠的食物搜尋行為，以及這如何取決於APC還路。目標2將研究禁食如何調節APC中的興奮抑制平衡。目標3將檢查禁食如何調節特定的抑制性神經元及其突觸。闡明抑製還路如何在調節食物搜索行為中控制主要神經元將為理解嗅覺如何促進能量穩態提供一個框架。

11104320.label: Realisation of objectives
11104320.value: The olfactory system is a relatively old (evolution-wise) system for all animals including mammals. It helps the organism to find food, capture prey, find mating partners, and avoid predators. In rodents, the odor information is transduced at the olfactory bulb (OB), where principal neurons project to the cortex for further information processing. Downstream of the OB, the anterior piriform cortex (APC) is the largest olfactory cortical area responsible for odor perception, learning and memory. Residing in layer 2 (L2), the main output principal neurons, are subdivided into the semilunar (SL) and superficial pyramidal (SP) cells. The SL and SP cells form distinct output channels due to their different molecular marker expression, passive membrane properties, excitatory inputs and outputs. While much is known about the excitatory inputs on SL and SP cells, little is known about their inhibitory inputs regarding their physiology and plasticity. Moreover, even though the APC is known to be modulated by hormones and metabolic states, it is unclear how the excitatory and inhibitory circuits in APC are plastic during hunger states. In this study, we hypothesized that acute fasting can regulate the excitatory and inhibitory circuits impinging on SL and SP cells, thereby altering APC output activity and the animal’s food-search behavior. We have achieved 100% of all 3 Objectives. In Objective 1, we determined how acute fasting can modulate food search behavior and neural activity in the APC. In order to assess the mouse’s foraging or food-search behavior, we developed a food search task (FST) for mice to search for the source location of a food pellet but it was not allowed to ingest it. Mice were placed in a 50 x 50 cm arena with 9, 50 mL Falcon tubes (3 x 3 grid pattern, 15 cm apart from each other) with holes inserted at the bottom. This allowed the mice to smell and use odor-guided sensation to approach the food tube, but not access (tough not ingest) the food since it was far away from the opening. There was a 10 min period of habituation followed by a 10 min period of search time. Sated or fasted (24 h) mice were individually subjected to the FST. Using this new assay, we showed that fasted mice spent a significant higher amount of time exploring the food tube compared to sated mice. Moreover, while sated mice could distinguish between between food and almond odor and preferred food odor, fasted mice exhibited an even stronger preference for food odor (i.e. an increase in the food recognition index). To assess the general neuronal activation in APC in response to FST, we fixed their brains, cut sections, and immunofluorescently stained for c-fos, an immediate-early gene protein product. FST strongly increased the c-fos staining in neurons in all layers (L1, L2 and L3) compared to no task performed. These results demonstrate the robustness of the FST and its use for dissecting the role of brain regions such as APC in homeostatic regulation of food search behavior. In Objective 2, we examined how fasting regulates excitation-inhibition balance in the APC. To examine the recurrent, evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) and IPSCs, we expressed an optogenetic activator, Chrimson, in APC neurons, and examined the output of these recurrent fibers by performing patch-clamp recording in principal neurons in acute APC slices. Principal neurons, SL and SP cells, reside in L2 of APC and can be identified by their localization to the more superficial (L2a) and deep (L2b) sublayers, respectively. Using whole-field illumination of the entire slice, we found that acute fasting did not detectably alter excitatory or inhibitory circuit amplitudes recorded in either SL or SP cells. However, based on our previously published paper in Jiang et al., “Target-Specific Control of Piriform Cortical Output via Distinct Inhibitory Circuits”. FASEB J. 2021, 35, e21944, we learned that inhibitory connections can exhibit layer-specific patterns. Indeed, patterned illumination of L1 vs L3 inputs to the principal neurons revealed that hunger induced a specific change in the L3 (but not L1) inhibitory inputs to the SP, but not SL, neurons. Such a specific change suggests that SP neurons, being the more associate and recurrent neuron type in APC, is a key substrate of modulation by metabolic state. In Objective 3, we examined how fasting modulates inhibitory neuron subtypes and their circuitry. PV and SOM interneurons are differentially involved in plasticity in various cortical regions including motor and visual cortex. To address how the functional output of PV neurons may differ for SL vs. SP cells, we expressed CheTA, an optogenetic activator with faster kinetics, in APC of PV-Cre mice as we originally proposed. While acute fasting did not alter PV -> SL IPSC amplitude in layer 1 or 3, it significantly depressed PV -> SP IPSCs specifically in Layer 3. In contrast, acute fasting did not detectably alter the output of SST neurons (i.e. the circuits of SST -> SL or SST -> SP). Moreover, to study the effects of hunger on structural plasticity, we stained fixed APC sections for PV or SST. We found that fasting did not detectably alter the number of PV or SST cell bodies in APC layers. It is conceivable that a functional change (physiology) is not accompanied by a structural change (anatomy) since immuofluorescent staining may not be sensitive enough to detect the small changes in physiology, particularly those in synapses. These results suggest that hunger acutely altered a specific part of a microcircuit in APC, possibly linking it to the altered food search vigor. Overall, our results indicate that acute fasting can induce target-specific modulation of inhibitory synapses structurally and functionally.

11104320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104320.value: We found that SL and SP cells of the APC exhibit differentially plasticity in response to acute fasting. In particular, inhibitory connections with SP but not SL neurons show heightened plasticity. We have disseminated our findings in the various channels below. Part of this GRF’s work was presented as a virtual poster entitled, “Target-specific control of piriform cortical output via recruitment of distinct inhibitory circuits” at an online conference, SfN The Global Connectome on 12 Jan, 2021. A major part of this GRF’s work was published in a scientific journal paper: Ngo EFY*, Li HH*, Zhang HQ, Lau CG. Acute fasting modulates food-seeking behavior and neural signaling in the piriform cortex. Nutrients, 14(19):4156, 2022; https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/14/19/4156. In this project, I hired three undergraduate students as Campus Internship Scheme (CIS) student helpers, training them to perform experiments in the lab (CHU Wen Kei, SUNG Hyun, and LEUNG Chung Yan). I taught them how to perform, analyze and evaluate immunofluorescent microscopy of fixed brain sections, and to present these results to other members of the lab. CHU Wen Kei graduated from CityU with a First-Class Honors in BSc in Biological Sciences degree and pursued her Master degree at the University of Edinburgh, UK. LEUNG Chung Yan graduated from CityU with a First-Class Honors in BEng in Biomedical Engineering degree (with a minor in Creative Media) and is currently pursuing her PhD studies at University College London, UK. Additionally, I recruited a PhD student, NGO Fung Yin (Esther) to perform research in my lab on this GRF project. Esther is still working on her PhD studies and has not graduated yet. However, during COVID-19 disruption during 2020-22, undergraduate students were not allowed to enter the campus or lab for long periods of time and hence their productivity was hampered.

11104320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11104320.value: This GRF started on 1 Sep, 2020 and ended on 31 Aug, 2023. We have achieved 100% of the proposed objectives. However, research activity was hampered by COVID-19 and student access to the laboratory was limited during times, which slowed our research progress. Moreover, many conferences were delayed or canceled, restricting the dissemination our results and reducing exposure of students to intense scientific discussions and learning experience. In this project, we found that acute fasting quickly alters inhibitory circuits in the APC. To further explore the role of APC in regulating food-related behaviors and body physiology, we can examine (1) the molecular mechanisms responsible for circuit plasticity in APC and (2) metabolic regulation in the body in response to the animal being exposed to foods of different caloric values.

11104320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11104320.value: The piriform (olfactory) cortex is a sensory cortex region important for perception and learning of smells, but how its circuitry is changed during the state of hunger is under-explored. In this proposal, we examined how acute fasting alters the two main output neuron types within the piriform cortex: SL and SP neurons. We found that the inhibitory synapses and circuits are differentially wired up for SL and SP neurons, suggesting that the two neuron types differentially process their incoming neural signals. Hunger also differentially modulates inhibitory signals in SL and SP neurons. Additionally, we found that one particular subtype of inhibitory interneuron, the parvalbumin (PV) interneuron, plays a particularly important role in the hunger-driven plasticity of SL and SP neurons. We showed that the PV to SP, but not PV to SL, neural circuit is particularly plastic. Our findings uncover a new type of plasticity in the piriform cortex that is likely important for smell-related drive for food search behavior.

11104520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104520.value: To date, over 600 hypoxic zones (< 2 mg O2 L-1) spanning hundreds of thousands of square kilometers are reported worldwide. The number has increased significantly in recent decades, and a major increase in the number of hypoxic areas in Asia is predicted for the coming decade. Aquatic hypoxia has caused mass mortality of marine animals, declines in fisheries production, and major changes in species composition, and community structure over large areas. Declines in fish populations and the elimination of sensitive fish species is likely caused by decreases in reproductive success and fitness resulting from hypoxia, and with rapid coastal development, hypoxia is likely to worsen in the future, thereby threatening the sustainability of natural populations. Recent laboratory studies by our group and field studies by others have shown that hypoxia is a potent agent of endocrine disruption and can severely impair sexual differentiation and reproductive functions in fish. Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) comprise a diverse group of synthetic or natural compounds that are widespread in the aquatic environment and are known to adversely affect sexual development and reproductive functions in fishes. Much research has focused on the adverse impact of 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2), a potent synthetic estrogen, because of its growing usage in human medicine and livestock farming activities, which has caused widespread damage in the aquatic environment. Despite the fact that hypoxia and EE2 stresses are widespread problems in aquatic environments worldwide, the combined effects of these two stressors on aquatic animals and ecosystem health are still poorly understood. Based on the recent successes of our group in developing the marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) as a marine model organism (along with the corresponding genetic tools and resources) for ecotoxicogenomics, we propose to utilize the marine medaka fish model to extend our understanding of the combined effects of EE2 (a model estrogenic EDC) and hypoxia on testicular and reproductive functions in male medaka fish. It is hypothesized that the adverse effect of environmentally relevant concentrations of EE2 on reproductive functions in male fish will be exacerbated in the presence of hypoxic stress, and is underpinned by the activation of specific toxicity pathways. It is envisaged that the use of an ecotoxicogenomic approach to investigate the modes of testicular toxicity in the marine medaka will uncover some novel biomarkers that are of relevance for the development of risk assessment methodologies. 迄今為止，據報道全球範圍內共有超過六十個面積為千萬平方公里的缺氧區（< 2毫克氧氣/升）。其數量於近年急劇上升，並且預測表明，於不久的將來缺氧區的增加主要集中在亞洲地區。水體缺氧已經造成大規模的海洋生物死亡、漁業產量下降、物種組成及群體結構顯著改變。魚類種群的減少及敏感魚种的消失很可能系由缺氧引起的繁殖能力及適應力降低所導致，而隨著沿海的迅速發展，海洋缺氧在未來可能會更加嚴重，進而威脅到環境生物物種的可持續性。近來本課題組的實驗室研究及其他學者的野外實地研究表明，缺氧是一種強效的內分泌干擾驅動因素，它能嚴重影響魚類性別分化及生殖功能。環境內分泌干擾物包括一系列人造的或自然存在的化合物，其廣泛存在於海洋環境中並且會對魚類的性別發育和生殖功能造成不良影響。17α-乙炔雌二醇(EE2)是一種人工合成的雌性激素，由於其不斷被用於人類藥品及畜牧業活動，因而導致水生環境遭受大規模的破壞，許多研究為此聚焦於其不良影響。儘管缺氧及17α-乙炔雌二醇脅迫是水生環境的常見問題，其兩者對水生動物和環境健康的聯合作用至今仍知之甚少。鑒於本課題組最近已成功將海洋青鱂魚開發成一種可用於生態毒理組學分析的海洋模式生物（及與之相關的基因工具及資源），我們提議用海洋青鱂魚作為研究模型以拓展我們對17α-乙炔雌二醇（一種模式內分泌干擾物）及缺氧對雄性海洋青鱂魚睪丸和生殖功能的聯合作用。我們假定缺氧會加重環境相關濃度的17α-乙炔雌二醇對雄性海洋青鱂魚睪丸和生殖功能的損害，並且是通過以激活特定的毒性通路的方式而實現。我們設想運用生態毒理組學方法去探究海洋海洋青鱂魚睪丸毒性機制，發現一些與風險評估方法建立相關的新型生物標志物。

11104620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104620.value: This project will provide solutions towards increasing the efficiency of health care networks, in particular networks for providing intensive care, as such cases are usually more urgent and more resource-constrained than other hospital units, with an intensive care bed requiring around six times the staffing cost of that of a regular hospital bed [1] and a high likelihood of fatality if prompt care is not received. We aim to minimize patient rejection within an intensive care network given a fixed number of available beds at each intensive care unit (ICU), while maintaining standards of fairness for each patient type. For the first time, a comprehensive study of design, modeling, evaluation, and optimization of multi-clustered ICU networks in metropolitan cities will be conducted. This will aid health care administrators with network planning, resource provisioning, and optimizing patient flow. To achieve our objectives, this project will use ideas from stochastic and queueing theory. To maximize ICU network efficiency, we will use the idea of resource pooling so that some patients may be referred to multiple ICUs in the network, and design new policies accordingly to determine the optimal order in which admission to these ICUs should be attempted. We note that the idea of hospital "clusters" already exists in Hong Kong and elsewhere [2,3] and we will base our network designs on these existing clusters while examining the possibility of multiple tiers of coordination, including within a cluster and between different clusters. This will extend the PI and Co-Is' existing work on single-cluster networks and provide a systematic approach to resource sharing in multi-clustered ICU networks, as opposed to ad-hoc approaches currently seen in many hospital regions. Our analytical approach will also allow administrators to examine "what-if" scenarios with increased ICU demand, for example an outbreak of acute infections, rather than relying on possibly limited or incomplete historical data. This work is motivated by recent research achievements of the PI and practical needs of the Co-Is' professional institutions and will take advantage of the PI and Co-Is' complimentary skills. The PI's role will be to oversee the project and provide the mathematical methods underlying the study, whereas the Co-Is' role will be to provide opinions on modeling assumptions and to review the potential applications of modeled outcomes. We will test our ICU network policies and optimization solutions on an example network using previously collected patient data from two Hong Kong ICU clusters. 該項目將提供解決方案，以提高衛生保健網絡的效率，尤其是提供重症監護的網絡，因為這種情況通常比其他醫院單位更為緊急，資源更加緊張，重症監護床位需要大約六倍的人員配備常規醫院病床的費用，如果不及時護理，則很可能導致死亡。我們希望在每個重症監護病房（ICU）擁有固定數量的可用病床的情況下，將重症監護網絡中的患者拒絕率降至最低，同時保持每種患者類型的公平標準。首次將對大城市的多集群ICU網絡的設計，建模，評估和優化進行全面研究。這將幫助醫療保健管理員進行網絡規劃，資源配置和優化患者流量。 為了實現我們的目標，該項目將使用隨機和排隊理論的思想。為了最大程度地提高ICU網絡效率，我們將使用資源池的思想，以便可以將某些患者轉診到網絡中的多個ICU，並據此設計新的策略，以確定應嘗試進入這些ICU的最佳順序。我們注意到，醫院“集群”的想法已經在香港和其他地方存在，我們將在現有集群的基礎上進行網絡設計，同時研究多層協作的可能性，包括集群內部以及不同集群之間的協調。這將擴展首席研究員 (PI) 和共同研究員(Co-Is) 在單集群網絡上的現有工作，並為多集群ICU網絡中的資源共享提供一種系統化的方法，與目前在許多醫院區域中採用的即席方法相反。我們的分析方法還允許管理員檢查ICU需求增加（例如爆發急性感染）的“假設”情況，而不是依賴可能有限或不完整的歷史數據。 這項工作是基於PI的最新研究成果以及Co-Is專業機構的實際需求而激發的，並將利用PI和Co-Is的互補技能。 PI的職責是監督項目並提供研究基礎的數學方法，而Co-Is的職責是就建模假設提供意見並審查建模結果的潛在應用。我們將使用先前從兩個香港ICU群集中收集的患者數據，在示例網絡上測試ICU網絡策略和優化解決方案。

11104620.label: Realisation of objectives
11104620.value: For revised objective 1, we designed a non-hierarchical architecture for the ICU network, effectively allowing a coordinative allocation policy of patients (especially external emergency patients with symptoms/accidents occurred or detected outside hospitals) with a central control unit. The newly designed architecture (Non-Hierarchical Overflow Loss System, NH-OLS) has been demonstrated to decrease the overall rejection rate of patients by utilizing the ICU beds across the entire network during pandemics or MCEs. In particular, the NH-OLS model enables better resource sharing among different hospitals in ICU networks than the hierarchical OLS model, especially when demands are bursty and/or the resources are unbalanced across hospitals. Numerical results showed that, the overall patient rejection rate can be reduced by more than 50% by allowing external emergency patients to be assigned to all hospitals within the ICU network, rather than restricted to the nearest hospital. On top of the NH-OLS model, we consider a bed reservation policy according to patient types, that is, to reserve a certain number of beds exclusively for certain class of patients. This is a commonly adopted resource allocation policy in ICU networks to preserve priority to certain class of patients, especially during times when the demand for ICU beds is high. For revised objective 2, we collected data from ICU hospitals in New Territories, Hong Kong. The original dataset contains information including (but not limited to) referral source, patient age, arrival time, assessed urgency, and treatment outcome for patients admitted to ICU in public hospitals from 2016 to 2017. As set out in the objectives, we focused on the inter arrival times and LoS of patients. Based on existing studies, we applied the Interrupted Poisson Process (IPP) to fit the arrival processes and considered the lognormal distribution to fit the Length of Stay (LoS) of patients. Specifically, we constructed a queueing model of the ICU for simulation purposes. We demonstrate that while the LoSs of emergency patients are well modeled using lognormal distributions, the same does not apply to elective patients. Instead, the LoS distribution of elective patients is multimodal with peaks at around 24 and 48 hours, and is best modeled using a mixture of three different distributions. We then use IPP to model the burstiness of regional emergency and elective patient arrivals, and show the improvement in terms of the goodness of the fit relative to a Poisson process. Next, we use these queueing models to conduct a sensitivity analysis of the ICU with respect to various changes to the model parameters. Numerical results demonstrate that the ICU is not very sensitive to the shape of the LoS distributions apart from their means, but very sensitive to the number of ICU beds, as well as the arrival rate and mean LoS of each patient type. Finally, we demonstrate that a model with a single unified exponential LoS distribution for all patients provides similar estimates of patient rejection compared with the base ICU model; however, unlike the base model, this simplified model forms a relatively simple (low-dimensional) Markov process that can be solved analytically with high computational efficiency. Our results are generally consistent with our expectations and objectives. For revised objective 3, we extended our previously proposed Information Exchange Surrogate Approximation (IESA) framework, which were originally designed for evaluating the Quality of Service (QoS) metrics in telecommunication networks, to the ICU network. The rationale is that our proposed non-hierarchical ICU network architecture for objective 1 shares many common features, including finite capacity and non-hierarchical mutual overflow, with telecommunication networks. The NH-OLS architecture designed for Objective 1 is known for their significantly higher complexity in evaluating performance metrics compared to hierarchical systems, especially when the system scale is relatively large. This has been the key obstacle preventing researchers from applying NH-OLSs in performance evaluation and optimization in such systems despite their advantages. The IESA framework was originally proposed to address the computational complexity issue. Our experiments on the ICU network also showed that, while the relative error of IESA approximation results to the actual rejection rate (obtained by discrete event simulation) can be up to 20%, it does not affect the results of optimal bed reservation thresholds. That is, using IESA as the evaluation tool of the rejection rates would give the same threshold for each patient class as using discrete event simulation for a wide range of scenarios with reasonable network parameters, while the former can reduce the computation time by more than six order of magnitudes compared to the latter. For revised objective 4, we have proposed an optimization framework that integrates IESA with the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to determine the optimal bed reservation thresholds of different patient classes in all hospitals given the arrival rate and LoS of each patient class. We have demonstrated that, the proposed framework can improve the computational efficiency by at least four orders of magnitude compared to the current mainstream approach which uses discrete event simulation as the performance evaluation tool and exhaustive search to identify the optimal thresholds. Specifically, our proposed approach integrating IESA and PSO considerably reduces the average time for each evaluation due to the lower complexity of IESA, and at the same time reduces the number of required evaluations due to the fast convergence of PSO, thus significantly improving the overall computational efficiency. The benefit of our proposed IESA-based optimization approach becomes even more obvious as the number of beds in each hospital and/or the number of hospitals increase, leading to very high computational time provided by discrete event simulations. Therefore, our proposed approach has potential in significantly improving the efficiency in design and planning of city- or state-wide ICU networks. Moreover, we developed a new approach integrating teletraffic theory with neural networks for quality-of-service evaluation in mobile networks. This work was published in Applied Soft Computing, Volume 152, February 2024. Although the network model studied is not the same as the ICU network model required for the current project, the completed work nevertheless forms an essential step towards improving the ICU network model in this project, as the mechanism by which requests overflow between server groups (i.e., base station cells) in the mobile model reflects how external patients can be referred to non-preferred ICUs in the ICU network model when their preferred ICU is full. Therefore, with specific modification, the modeling methodology in the mobile model can be translated to that in the ICU model. Finally, it is worth mentioning that we published a survey paper in IEEE Access (June 2023, doi: https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3283803). In this paper, we describe historical and recent developments toward tackling a century-long challenge in teletraffic theory, namely evaluating blocking probability in overflow systems with mutual overflow. Such systems have many applications in various telecommunications and service systems, including intensive care, wireless communications, cloud computing, and emergency services, and many methods have been developed over the past century to address this challenge. Although not a part of the original project objectives, this project inspires ideas and contributes efforts to this important century-long challenge in teletraffic theory (see Sections 3C, 3E1, and 4A in the paper for details).

11104620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104620.value: 1. We have completed the design of architectures of the ICU network, allowing for both intra- and inter-cluster transfer of patients based on ICU occupancy levels and patient types. 2. We have developed new teletraffic models and their evaluation methodology for ICUs in a multi-cluster ICU network, with a mixture of Poisson and non-Poisson (e.g., Interrupted Poisson) arrivals, and exponential and non-exponential (e.g., lognormal) patient length-of-stay (LoS) distributions. We have also evaluated the fitness of different arrival processes and/or LoS distributions against real traces of data from the Hong Kong ICU network. 3. We have extended our previously proposed IESA framework to the ICU network as an effective evaluation tool for estimating rejection rate of patients by types. We have verified the accuracy of the proposed method using extensive computer simulation. 4. We have tested our performance evaluation methods and ICU network policies (bed reservation mechanism) to a small example ICU network based on real Hong Kong patient data (previously collected). We have demonstrated the improvement in terms of computational efficiency achieved by our proposed method over the existing methods.

11104620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11104620.value: We aim to further improve in terms of both accuracy and efficiency on the basis of the current approach. • In terms of accuracy, we may refer to the actual operations of ICUs to relax some assumptions in the IESA framework, such as replacing Poisson arrivals with the more general and realistic arrival processes such as the Interrupted Poisson Process (IPP) or Markov-Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP) that can reflect the changing in the mean arrival rates of patients during different periods. In this case, the Erlang B formula which is the key function to calculate the rejection rate of a single hospital needs to be replaced by another formula derived from the steady-state equations derived from the new arrival process. Another possible direction is to integrate the Artificial Intelligent (AI) technique to tune certain key parameters in the IESA framework, which we have demonstrated the feasibility in other applications with similar non-hierarchical overflow structure. In addition, we may also consider other practical aspects and revise the model accordingly, such as restricting the number of overflows, or implementing the triage policies to further differentiate the services to different classes. • In terms of efficiency, as our experiment results have shown that the relationship between QoS metrics and input parameters (the number of beds or the intensity of offered traffic) is convex under both the simulation and IESA. Therefore, if necessary, it is possible to consider optimization algorithms that converge faster than PSO but require the convexity condition, to integrate with IESA and further improve the computational efficiency. Another possibility is to add parallel computing mechanism in the current IESA framework to further speed up the computations.

11104620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11104620.value: This research project aims to improve the management of Intensive Care Units (ICUs) by creating better ways to share resources among hospitals. The project focuses on designing a new network system that helps hospitals share ICU beds more effectively, especially during emergencies or pandemics. The team developed a Non-Hierarchical Overflow Loss System (NH-OLS), which significantly reduces the number of patients turned away by allowing them to be sent to any hospital within the network, not just the nearest one. This approach led to over a 50% reduction in patient rejections. They also created policies to reserve ICU beds for different types of patients and a triage strategy to prioritize patients based on their condition, improving both fairness and efficiency in patient care. Using real data from Hong Kong ICUs, the researchers modeled how patients arrive and how long they stay. They found that ICUs work best when bed availability and patient arrival rates are well-managed. A simplified model provided similar accuracy but was much faster to compute. Finally, an optimization framework using advanced algorithms improved the efficiency of planning and managing ICU resources. This project ensures that ICUs can handle sudden increases in patients more effectively.

11104720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104720.value: 香港水域的鯨豚擱淺死亡數字在近年持續上升，尤以海上交通最具威脅，若要判斷鯨豚是因為船隻而死亡，必須精準地紀錄及重組鯨豚受傷的痕跡。 影像解剖是人類死因調查中急速發展的領域，這種技術利用影像學及數碼化技術對屍體進行無創檢測，短時間內提供額外和有用的資料，甚至能夠獲得傳統解剖難以獲得的數據，可視作虛擬版的傳統解剖，再以立體掃瞄紀錄屍體表面狀況及造成傷痕的「兇器」，兩者的立體數據內外配合，重組「案情」。 可是，影像解剖在動物上的應用只限於研究，甚少用在法證層面上，識別人為創傷的痕跡。 有見及此，相關之研究應著重於詮釋創傷性病變及確立影像解剖的認受性。如應用在鯨豚上，首要便是深入研究以影像解剖紀錄與重組擱淺鯨豚因船隻而造成的創傷，彌補現有的缺陷。 這個項目的目的是利用影像解剖與立體掃瞄來紀錄及重組擱淺鯨豚因海上交通而造成的內外創傷，從中或可為珍貴的本港鯨豚提供準確的保育準則，保護牠們免受傷害。我們的團隊包括放射診斷學法醫病理學、傳統解剖、獸醫學與及保育稀有動物的專家，全面及有系統地分析擱淺鯨豚的創傷及死亡，加以配對不同類型的船隻撞擊，最終整合到首個擱淺鯨豚的數據庫作幾何比較。透過這個專業的團隊，這個項目可以為漁農自然護理署及海事處的人員提供有用的資料，協作他們制定保育措施、海上交通航行路線及速度限制；其他持份者例如渡輪運輸公司、學者、綠色團體與及鯨豚專家亦可從中得到啟發，推行更有效的計劃，保護本港鯨豚免受傷害。

11104720.label: Realisation of objectives
11104720.value: For objectives 1 and 2, cetacean sighting data from 2014 to 2024 collected from line transect surveys by Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) and other Environmental Monitoring and Audit programs in West HK waters were acquired and processed to calculate the values of dolphin per survey effort and cetacean encounter probability. Since these programs involved different survey area, period, and frequency, effort was made to normalize and include all the datasets for a compatible analysis on the distribution and habitat use of resident cetaceans. Selective marine vessel traffic data from 2019 onward archived by Marine Department were acquired and filtered to calculate the values of marine vessel density (vessel type and speed) and vessel encounter probability. The vessel-cetacean encounter probability was calculated as a normalized product of cetacean encounter probability and vessel encounter probability across the period of pre-, during, and post-COVID. Interaction hotspots, as well as the type and speed of marine vessels that pose significant risk to cetaceans were identified. For objective 3, virtopsy was performed on cetaceans stranded in HK waters whenever feasible. PMCT was conducted on 105 out of 111 (95%) carcasses recovered from January 2021 to June 2024, in addition to 221 retrospective cases collected since 2014. For these 326 cases (231 Neophocaena phocaenoides, 58 Sousa chinensis, 37 of other species), criteria to identify vessel interaction as the cause of death had been developed, as well as reliable ways to separate antemortem from postmortem injuries with different levels of confidence. In total, 44 cases (33 Neophocaena phocaenoides, 9 Sousa chinensis, 2 of other species) were assigned as vessel-related mortalities, with postmortem findings on PMCT (and later verified in conventional necropsy) included but not limited to sharp open wounds on dorsal or lateral aspect, hematoma, skeletal fracture and dislocation). For objective 4, 3D surface scanning was performed on both cetacean carcasses and potential injury-causing tools available related to vessel interaction (i.e., various types of marine vessels and the relevant propellors found in different shipyards in HK) to document the surface geometry (shape, size, and spatial arrangement) for identification of the tools that may cause patterned injuries and reconstruction of the traumatic incidents in a forensic manner. Description and evaluation of different features of the injuries related to their pattern and the deformations and rotations undergone during their production had also been performed. The morphologic-geometric comparison in postmortem investigation and observations of live individual surviving a vessel-related injury in this study had provided information about the relationship between the severity of injury and depth of laceration, anatomical site of injury, and vessel speed. Species-dependent relationship between the severity of injury and depth as well as location of open wound had also been evaluated. For objective 5, cetacean strandings determined as vessel-related mortalities were investigated through the aforementioned pipeline to understand the incidents from different perspectives, including the spatial-temporal relationship between cetaceans and marine vessels in HK waters (whether the events happened in high collision risk hotspots), the physiological effect (what patterned injuries attributed to marine vessel interaction can be assessed using the virtopsy approach), and the course of event (how did the trauma occur in terms of physical positions of both the cetacean and the marine vessel). The multidisciplinary approach allowed a holistic understanding on the impact of marine vessel interaction on cetaceans in HK waters, facilitating effective mitigation strategies by government officials and other stakeholders in relation to cetacean conservation. In particular, a stakeholder forum was organised in June 2022 to gather cetacean expects (academics from local universities and other research institutes, representatives from environmental consultancy and Ocean Park Hong Kong), economics (representatives from the Hong Kong International Airport, ferry companies, dolphin watching and ecotourism operators) and policy groups (government officials, lawyers, green groups) to review the current status of local cetaceans and marine traffic. For the first time in HK, different parties engaged in sharing and discussion on their points of view, obstacles and strategic solutions (including route diversion and speed control zones) aiming to mitigate cetacean-vessel interactions for future marine resources management and conservation. In conclusion, all the project objectives and tasks set in the proposal had been accomplished. Project findings were consolidated and disseminated to both research and public sectors, including academic conferences, scientific workshops, outreach seminars, various media coverages and social media platforms of the project team. We believed the project has significantly advanced our understanding on cetacean-vessel interactions in HK waters, provided scientific evidence for postmortem assessment and case evaluation, and elevated public awareness on the immediate threats resident cetaceans are facing, the impact of human activities on marine megafaunas, and the ultimate goal of marine conservation.

11104720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104720.value: Soon after the construction of coastal mega-infrastructure began, resident dolphins had lessened their use of North and Northwest Lantau waters (former core habitats of Sousa chinensis), and were shifting their effective home range to the less impacted Southwest and South Lantau waters. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the associated restrictions had lowered vessel calls of various vessel types. Vessel-cetacean encounter probability varied across pre-, during, and post-COVID period, which indicated dynamic hotspots of high encounter risk around the Southwest and South Lantau waters where “new” core cetacean habitats are located at. Characterisation of the virtopsy based markers, as well as criteria to identify vessel interaction as the cause of death had been developed, with the retrospective and prospective analyses on 326 cetaceans stranded from March 2014 to June 2024. In total, 44 cases were assigned as vessel-related mortalities, with PMCT findings (and later verified in conventional necropsy) included but not limited to sharp open wounds on dorsal or lateral aspect, hematoma, skeletal fracture and dislocation. Vessel interaction was considered the leading anthropogenic cause of morality for resident cetacean (44/326, 13.5%). 3D surface scanning was used for surface documentation in conjunction with virtopsy for internal documentation, to recognise and describe sharp/blunt force injuries. Sharp force injuries included external gashes and severed fluke/fins originated from contact with rotating propeller. Blunt force injuries included abrasions, contusions, lacerations, and skeletal fractures originated from contact with the bow, hull, skeg, or rudder. Patterned injuries were matched using 3D reconstructions to understand how the incidents might have occurred and be prevented. Fatal sharp force injuries were found deeper than 10cm and 20cm on HK resident cetaceans, i.e. Neophocaena phocaenoides and Sousa chinensis respectively, but a similar trauma may be less fatal for large cetaceans. For a non-resident Balaenoptera edeni edeni stranded in 2023 in Sai Kung waters, media and public suspected its death was caused by dolphin watching boat strike. Upon postmortem investigation, the lethal wound as determined by veterinary forensic pathologists measured 90cm in width and 50cm in depth. Based on our 3D scanned models, typical propellor blades found on dolphin watching boats in HK waters measured between 18–38cm. The mismatch in size proved that the lethal wound might not be inflicted by such propellors, nor these vessels were capable of casting the injury. This demonstrated the application of 3D surface scanning in scene reconstruction to facilitate forensic judgement or policymaking purposes.

11104720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11104720.value: With the pipeline for cetacean-vessel encounter probability analysis established, prospective data can be investigated to tackle the dynamic change in both cetacean and marine vessel distributions in coming years. The methodology can also be applied to a wider scope, for instance the Greater Bay Area, where cetacean sighting data and vessel traffic data have been collected by Chinese researchers, which will provide a fuller picture of the impact of marine vessels on resident cetaceans (which indeed inhabit not only in HK waters but also the Pearl River Estuary) and even other cetacean species. With the updated virtopsy based markers aiding the identification of vessel-induced injuries, prospective cetacean stranding cases can be evaluated more effectively and efficiently. Species-dependent relationship between severity of injury, as well as the position and depth of external gashes resulted from difference in body morphometrics or other physiological characters (e.g., swimming pattern, bone strength) shall also be further investigated using the established virtopsy based markers to evaluate the risk of trauma incurred by marine vessels. With the dynamic locations of geographic hotspots identified, effective mitigation measures could be developed and implemented including consideration on operational procedure alternations such as rerouting vessels, speed excursion zone and speed reduction.

11104720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11104720.value: This project investigated the likelihood of encounter between resident cetaceans and marine vessels in West HK waters, diagnostic indicators for vessel-induced injuries, and geometric features of such injuries. Using distribution datasets of cetaceans and marine vessels, dynamic hotspots of high encounter risk were identified in the “new” core habitats of humpback dolphins and finless porpoises. With reference to the developed diagnostic indicators, 44/326 cases (13.5%) were assigned as vessel-related mortalities, indicating vessel interaction as the leading anthropogenic threat for resident cetaceans. These cases were evaluated using imaging techniques, including PMCT and 3D surface scanning, to reveal patterned injuries that can be reconstructed and matched using 3D models. With the support of scientific data, risk assessment and mitigation on marine vessel interaction were accomplished, including a response plan to large cetacean sighting implemented by AFCD, as well a legislative review for the cetacean protection suggesting the Director of AFC could designate temporary restriction areas and impose restrictions on vessel navigation and relevant activities. This project shed lights on the dynamic change of impact of vessel interaction on cetaceans in HK waters, which has been systematically studied and monitored for the first time using multidisciplinary forensic approach.

11200120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200120.value: 量子力學在材料科學中起著重要作用，它使人們能夠從根本上深刻理解材料的特性和現象。 1982年，理查德•費曼（Richard Feynman）指出，很難在經典計算機上真正模擬量子力學系統，但他說：“讓計算機本身由遵循量子力學定律的量子力學元素構成。”;對於這樣的計算機，這種模擬將成為可能。在過去的幾十年中，量子技術領域取得了巨大的進步。量子計算已成為應用科學的跨學科研究領域。基於量子力學而不是經典算法的計算為適用於金融，密碼學和材料模擬的新型計算機提供了機會。特別地，基於量子力學的量子化學模擬是量子計算機最成功的應用。然而，最新的量子計算需要大量的步驟和時間，這增加了推進量子計算應用的難度。為了滿足量子計算的需求，新算法的開發是當務之急。當前，大多數量子計算機社群關注硬件設計的進步。然而，提供以方便的方式使用量子計算機的可靠策略也非常重要。此提議將實現關於量子化學計算的四個重要問題。將系統地研究四個基本力，包括強共價鍵，強離子鍵，氫鍵和凡德瓦力。這項工作將揭示控制通用量子計算機的科學基礎。

11200120.label: Realisation of objectives
11200120.value: Our project has achieved substantial progress across all four objectives, demonstrating the quantum computing advantages for modeling molecular forces of varying strengths. For objectives 1 and 2, focusing on quantum computing simulations of strong intramolecular forces (covalent and ionic bonding), we have successfully implemented two complementary approaches: First, our research on Daubechies wavelet molecular orbitals has proven particularly effective for accurate quantum computations of molecular properties involving strong bonds. This approach provides a systematically improvable basis with excellent locality properties, enabling precise representation of electronic wavefunctions near nuclei while maintaining computational efficiency. Our benchmark studies comparing against experimental data demonstrate the effectiveness of this wavelet-based approach for strong intramolecular forces. Second, we implemented the Correlation Optimized Virtual Orbital (COVO) method to prepare efficient quantum chemistry Hamiltonians suitable for NISQ-era calculations. Our approach addresses a critical challenge with plane-wave basis sets, where unoccupied (virtual) orbitals from DFT calculations tend to be delocalized and interact weakly with occupied orbitals, limiting their effectiveness for quantum simulations. We enhanced the original COVO algorithm by: 1. Modifying the cost function to use larger active spaces and CCSD calculations instead of small CI matrices 2. Implementing a method to handle orbitals that fail to localize during optimization 3. Extending support to open-shell systems Our implementation connects Quantum Espresso (for plane-wave DFT calculations) with PySCF (for many-body calculations), allowing for modular development. Tests on several molecular systems (H₂, N₂, O₂, CN, and C₂) confirm that our optimized orbitals follow the desired O(1/M) energy scaling with respect to orbital count, enabling accurate extrapolation to the complete basis set limit. For objectives 3 and 4, concerning weak intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces), we've implemented finite size correction techniques to address the inherent challenges of plane-wave periodic calculations. This includes the probe charge method to reduce error scaling from O(Ω^(-1/3)) to O(Ω^(-1)), where Ω is the simulation cell volume. We've also performed calculations at multiple cell sizes to enable extrapolation to the infinite limit. Our work on "Hybrid Quantum-Classical Clustering for Preparing a Prior Distribution of Eigenspectrum" and "Optimal Particle-Conserved Linear Encoding for Practical Fermionic Simulation" has provided additional techniques for efficiently preparing quantum states representing these weak interactions. These approaches enable more accurate initial state preparation and enhance quantum resource efficiency when modeling electronic structures. Our comparison of equilibrium bond lengths and dissociation energies against established correlation-consistent basis sets demonstrates competitive accuracy for comparable orbital counts. Importantly, our approach allows for granular adjustments to orbital count, which isn't possible with traditional Gaussian-type basis sets. To address remaining challenges in accurately modeling the subtle weak intermolecular forces, we continue to refine our error mitigation techniques and develop specialized quantum algorithms that reduce qubit requirements while maintaining accuracy. We anticipate completing all validation tests before the project conclusion, providing comprehensive performance assessments of quantum computing advantages across the spectrum of molecular forces.

11200120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200120.value: Our research has delivered significant advances in quantum computational methods for molecular simulations, addressing both strong and weak molecular forces. Five key publications highlight our major contributions to this field. We developed and benchmarked Daubechies wavelet molecular orbitals for quantum computations of molecular properties. This approach provides exceptional precision for modeling strong intramolecular forces while maintaining computational efficiency. Our wavelet-based representation offers superior locality properties compared to traditional basis sets, enabling accurate electronic structure calculations with reduced quantum resources. Our quantum imaginary-time control technique substantially accelerates ground-state preparation, a critical bottleneck in quantum chemistry simulations. By optimizing the evolution path through imaginary time, we achieved significantly faster convergence to molecular ground states, particularly valuable for NISQ-era quantum devices with limited coherence times. For vibrational properties, we demonstrated accurate calculations of harmonic frequencies for diatomic molecules using quantum algorithms. This research establishes the foundation for extending quantum advantage to molecular dynamics and spectroscopic predictions, with applications in both strong and weak force regimes. The hybrid quantum-classical clustering approach we developed for eigenspectrum preparation represents an important advance in quantum state initialization. By intelligently preparing prior distributions based on eigenspectrum characteristics, we achieve more efficient use of quantum resources and better convergence properties for larger molecular systems. Finally, our optimal particle-conserved linear encoding method addresses a fundamental challenge in quantum chemistry: efficiently mapping fermionic problems to qubit systems. Our encoding preserves particle number conservation while minimizing qubit requirements, leading to shallower circuits and improved error resilience on current quantum hardware. These research outcomes collectively demonstrate quantum computational advantages for molecular simulations across the spectrum of interaction strengths. Our methods enable more accurate and efficient modeling of both strong intramolecular forces and weak intermolecular interactions, positioning quantum computing as a transformative tool for future applications in materials science, drug discovery, and catalysis research.

11200120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200120.value: In the future, we will explore the integration of quantum computing and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to develop innovative quantum algorithms based on plane wave basis sets. Our goal is to achieve high-precision simulations of electronic structures in periodic systems. Currently, quantum computing applications in chemistry face significant challenges, including excessive resource requirements and noise interference when simulating complex systems. To address these limitations, we can develop a specialized chemical workflow for plane wave basis sets that combines quantum computing with AI-driven design approaches. This integration aims to substantially improve both computational efficiency and precision in molecular simulations.

11200120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200120.value: Our research brings quantum computing advantages to chemistry simulations, focusing on modeling the forces that hold molecules together. We've developed two innovative approaches that make these simulations more accurate and efficient. First, we used Daubechies wavelets that can precisely describe how electrons behave in molecules. Second, we improved the "COVO" method to optimize how quantum computers represent molecular structures, making it work for more types of molecules than before. These advances allow us to accurately simulate molecules. Our methods have been tested on molecules like hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon compounds, showing excellent agreement with experimental data. This research opens pathways to using quantum computers for developing new materials, drugs, and catalysts by providing more accurate molecular simulations than conventional computing methods can achieve.

11200220.label: Project Objectives
11200220.value: To develop a human driving style classification and recognition system. The interaction between human-driven vehicles and autonomous vehicles will play an important role on transportation in the near future. The most direct way to model such an interaction is to study human driving styles and "teach" an autonomous vehicle to get along with surrounding human-driven vehicles. As a surrounding vehicle may only be at the view of an autonomous vehicle for a short time period, we aim to recognize human driving style using a short time period historical data and prior knowledge. To achieve this objective, we first plan to find a proper way to represent a trajectory segment that can extract its important features. The next step is to choose a suitable clustering algorithm to cluster the trajectories. Given the clustering results, we will design a recognition process based on a short-term historical trajectory. The NGSIM dataset consisting of trajectories for 9206 vehicles and highD dataset consisting of trajectories for 110,000 vehicles will be used for classification and recognition. The result of this task will provide the basis for the following three tasks. It can also be used to study how to leverage autonomous driving vehicles to affect human drivers for transportation system optimization, e.g., to alleviate congestion. To design a new method for trajectory prediction of surrounding vehicles. The predicted trajectories of the surrounding vehicles can help an autonomous vehicle plan its trajectory well ahead. We plan to predict the future trajectories of surrounding vehicles based on their short-term historical trajectories by considering human driving styles. Given the clustered data from the first objective, we will have several sub-datasets of different driving styles. For each sub-dataset, a model will be trained to predict the future trajectory of the vehicle with a specific driving style. We then use the model that corresponds to its recognized driving style to predict the trajectory of a vehicle. The generative model will be adopted to generate the predicted trajectory based on a short historical trajectory. It is critical to consider the temporal property of the trajectory sequence in the generative model. We plan to use RNN-based architecture, which is capable of handling the time-sequential data, as a part of the generative model. In addition, the driving scenario and real-time trajectory tracking will also be taken into consideration for improving the prediction accuracy. With a more accurate prediction of surrounding vehicles, more information can be provided to describe the spatiotemporal collision-free space for motion planning. To design a behavior planner for an autonomous vehicle. The behavior planner is responsible for selecting a driving behavior for the autonomous vehicle based on the environment, passenger preference, and current behavior. To this end, we will first build different sets of behaviors for different traffic scenarios (e.g. urban, highway), then find the transition conditions to change from one driving behavior to another under each traffic scenario. Besides the transitions among different driving behaviors in one traffic scenario, the transitions among different traffic scenarios will also be taken into consideration. The most direct approach to represent these transitions is to design a hierarchical finite state machine. The clustered sub-datasets of different driving styles will be reorganized according to driving behaviors to find such transitions. In other words, given a set of behaviors of a driving style for one traffic scenario, we will model the transition conditions among different driving behaviors. To design a customized motion planning scheme. With the accurate future trajectory of the surrounding vehicles and the determined driving behavior, we aim to develop new algorithmic motion planning algorithms to generate a collision-free and interpretable trajectory. The objective function of a traditional motion planning problem usually minimizes the traveling time, fuel consumption, and jerk. However, it may lead to generating a trajectory that cannot be interpreted by human drivers. We will solve this problem by allowing users to customize their preferred driving styles. To enforce a trajectory to be close to a preferred driving style chosen by the passengers in car, we will apply inverse reinforcement learning to get a reward function that needs to be maximized in the objective function. We will leverage the clustered sub-datasets of different driving styles to learn the reward functions for different driving styles. According to user preference, the corresponding reward function will be added as a negative term in the objective function. While minimizing the objective function, it penalizes the smaller reward value to make the generated trajectory similar to the preferred driving style. In this way, the algorithmic motion planning will not generate a trajectory that is beyond what human drivers can accept, thus, disruption to human drivers can be reduced.
