11200220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200220.value: In recent years, autonomous driving has demonstrated its feasibility but there are still many issues to be solved before the large-scale adoption of self-driving vehicles. One of the key issues is how to address the co-existence of human driven vehicles and self-driving vehicles, which will be the norm in the coming decades. Such a co-existence brings challenges and opportunities to motion planning in autonomous driving. On the one hand, a human driver usually maintains a consistent driving style, which offers the opportunity for an autonomous vehicle to recognize the driving style of a surrounding vehicle and then predict its trajectory. Thus, an autonomous vehicle can have a better environment perception and take safer driving behaviors. On the other hand, the driving behaviors of an autonomous vehicle shall make both passengers in the car and other nearby drivers feel comfortable, which can be accommodated by training an autonomous vehicle to have a human-like driving style. To address the above issue, this proposal will thoroughly consider the impact of human driving style on the motion planning of an autonomous vehicle. Specifically, this proposal aims to develop a novel motion-planning framework that organically integrates two types of motion planning, namely, algorithmic motion planning, which can generate collision-free and energy-efficient trajectory, and imitation learning-based motion planning, which emulates the human driving style and generates more interpretable trajectory. In the proposed motion-planning framework, state-of-the-art learning techniques will be adopted to provide more accurate inputs for algorithmic motion planning. In particular, we will first cluster trajectories in available datasets according to different driving styles and driving behaviors. For each given driving behavior and driving style pair, a prediction model is trained. The trained models will help an autonomous vehicle predict the future trajectory of a surrounding vehicle, which will provide better environment perception for motion planning. To incorporate the comfort of passengers in the autonomous vehicle, preferred human driving style will be utilized to select the driving behavior, e.g., car-following or lane-changing, which determines the goal point for motion planning. At last, algorithmic motion planning algorithms will be developed to generate a collision-free and human-decided trajectory, where a penalty is introduced to minimize the deviation from the preferred human-decided trajectory. The project will enhance the safety in autonomous driving, build the trust bond between passengers and the autonomous vehicle, and reduce the disruption of autonomous vehicle’s driving behavior to other human driven vehicles. 近年來，無人駕駛已經證明了其可行性，但是在大規模採用自動駕駛汽車之前，還有許多問題需要解決。關鍵問題之一是如何解決人類駕駛汽車和自動駕駛汽車的共存問題。這種共存為自動駕駛中的運動規劃帶來了挑戰和機遇。一方面，駕駛員通常保持一致的駕駛風格，這為自動駕駛汽車提供了識別周圍車輛的駕駛風格並預測其軌跡的機會。因此，自動駕駛車輛可以具有更好的環境感知並採取更安全的駕駛行為。另一方面，無人駕駛汽車的駕駛行為應使乘車人和附近的其他駕駛員都感到舒適，這可以通過訓練無人駕駛汽車使其具有類似於人的駕駛風格來解決。為解決上述問題，本項目將全面考慮人類駕駛方式對自動駕駛汽車運動規劃的影響。具體來說，本項目旨在開發一種新穎的運動規劃框架，該框架將兩種類型的運動規劃有機地集成在一起，即算法運動規劃（可產生無碰撞且節能的軌跡）和基於模仿學習的運動規劃（模仿學習運動規劃）。在擬研究的運動規劃框架中，將採用最先進的學習技術為算法運動規劃提供更準確的輸入。在特定情況下，我們將首先根據不同的駕駛方式和駕駛行為在數據集中對軌跡進行聚類。對於每對給定的駕駛行為和駕駛方式，都會產生一個預測模型。訓練有素的模型將幫助自動駕駛車輛預測周圍車輛的未來軌跡，這將為運動規劃提供更好的環境感知。為了將乘客的舒適感融入到自動駕駛汽車中，將採用人類駕駛方式來指導運動規劃目標點的選擇。最後，將開發運動規划算法以生成無碰撞且類似於人的駕駛的軌跡，並引入懲罰以最大程度地減少與人的駕駛軌跡的偏離。該項目將增強自動駕駛的安全性，通過規劃符合乘客偏好的運動軌跡，建立汽車中乘客對自動駕駛汽車的信任，並減少自動駕駛汽車的駕駛行為對其他人類駕駛汽車的干擾。

11200220.label: Realisation of objectives
11200220.value: To address objective 1, we first study Driver Behavior modelling (DBM). Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) is a prevailing DBM technique with the goal of modeling the driving policy by recovering an unknown internal reward function from human driver demonstrations. However, the latest IRL-based design is inefficient due to the laborious manual feature engineering processes. Besides, the reward function usually experiences increased prediction errors when deployed for unseen vehicles. We propose a novel deep learning-based reward function for IRL-based DBM with efficient model personalization via machine unlearning. We evaluate our approach on a highway simulation constructed using the realistic human driving dataset NGSIM. We deploy our approach on both a server GPU and an embedded GPU. The evaluation results show that our approach achieves a higher prediction accuracy compared with the latest IRL-based DBM approach that uses a weighted sum of trajectory features as the reward function. Our model personalization method obtains the highest accuracy and lowest latency compared with the baselines. The work is published in Part C 9(1). We studied a novel generative hybrid car-following (CF) model, which achieves high accuracy in characterizing dynamic human CF behaviors and is able to generate realistic human CF behaviors for any given observed or even unobserved driving style. Specifically, the ability of accurately capturing human CF behaviors is ensured by designing and calibrating an Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) with time-varying parameters. The reason behind is that such time-varying parameters can express both the inter-driver heterogeneity, i.e., diverse driving styles of different drivers, and the intra-driver heterogeneity, i.e., changing driving styles of the same driver. The ability of generating realistic human CF behaviors of any given observed driving style is achieved by applying a neural process (NP) based model. The ability of inferring CF behaviors of unobserved driving styles is supported by exploring the relationship between the calibrated time-varying IDM parameters and an intermediate variable of NP. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed models, we conduct extensive experiments and comparisons, including CF model parameter calibration, CF behavior prediction, and trajectory simulation for different driving styles. This work is published in Part C 8(4). To address objective 2, we proposed QCNet, a modeling framework toward pushing the boundaries of trajectory prediction. First, we identify that the agent-centric modeling scheme used by existing approaches requires re-normalizing and re-encoding the input whenever the observation window slides forward, leading to redundant computations during online prediction. To overcome this limitation and achieve faster inference, we introduce a query-centric paradigm for scene encoding, which enables the reuse of past computations by learning representations independent of the global spacetime coordinate system. Sharing the invariant scene features among all target agents further allows the parallelism of multi-agent trajectory decoding. Second, even given rich encodings of the scene, existing decoding strategies struggle to capture the multimodality inherent in agents’ future behavior, especially when the prediction horizon is long. To tackle this challenge, we first employ anchor-free queries to generate trajectory proposals in a recurrent fashion, which allows the model to utilize different scene contexts when decoding waypoints at different horizons. A refinement module then takes the trajectory proposals as anchors and leverages anchor-based queries to refine the trajectories further. By supplying adaptive and high-quality anchors to the refinement module, our query-based decoder can better deal with the multimodality in the output of trajectory prediction. Our approach ranks 1st on Argoverse 1 and Argoverse 2 motion forecasting benchmarks, outperforming all methods on all main metrics by a large margin. Meanwhile, our model can achieve streaming scene encoding and parallel multi-agent decoding thanks to the query-centric design ethos. The work is published in Part C 9(2). To address objectives 3 and 4, we integrate the human factors that are represented by driving styles to design a new discrete lane changing (DLC) decision-making model. Specifically, our proposed model takes not only the contextual traffic information but also the driving styles of surrounding vehicles into consideration and makes lane-change/keep decisions. Moreover, the model can imitate human drivers’ decision-making maneuvers by learning the driving style of the ego vehicle. Our evaluation results show that the proposed model captures the human decision-making strategies and imitates human drivers’ lane-change maneuvers, which can achieve 98.66% prediction accuracy. Moreover, we also analyze the lane-change impact of our model compared with human drivers in terms of improving the safety and speed of traffic. The work is published in Part C 8( 3). We integrate algorithmic motion planning with learning models to improve sampling-based motion planning (BMP) in highway traffic scenarios from the following two perspectives. First, given the number of points to be sampled, we develop a new model to sample “important” points for SBMP by predicting the intention of surrounding vehicles and learning the distribution of human drivers’ trajectory. Second, we empirically study the relationship between the number of sample points and the environment, which is largely ignored in conventional SBMP. Then, we provide a guideline to select the appropriate number of points to be sampled under different scenarios to guarantee efficiency. The simulation experiments are conducted based on the vehicle trajectory dataset NGSIM. The results show that the proposed sampling strategy outperforms existing sampling strategies in terms of the computing time, traveling time, and smoothness of the trajectory. The work is published in Part C 8(1). Besides the above objectives, we also studied how to better utilize map information and model the interactions of vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-lane. Specifically, due to the heterogeneity of the map data and trajectory data, many learning based models extract vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to lane interactions in a separate and sequential manner, which may capture biased interpretations of interactions, causing lower prediction and planning accuracy. As for the mathematical models, the environment information is mainly used to characterize the collision-free space, while the interactions are largely ignored. To address the above issues, we propose an environment representation, called Temporal Occupancy Flow Graph (TOFG). Specifically, TOFG unifies the map information and vehicle trajectories into a homogeneous data format and enables a consistent prediction. We incorporate TOFG with a graph attention (GAT) based neural network and propose TOFG-GAT to demonstrate the benefit of TOFG to learning-based trajectory prediction and motion planning. Moreover, we design and implement an interaction-aware sampling strategy based on TOFG to improve the mathematical sampling-based motion planning algorithms. Extensive experiment results show that our proposed TOFG can contribute to the trajectory prediction and motion planning tasks by improving the quality of the generated trajectory and computation efficiency for both the learning-based and mathematical models. The work is published in Part C 8(5).

Given the clustering results, we will design a recognition process based on a short-term historical trajectory.

To design a new method for trajectory prediction of surrounding vehicles. The predicted trajectories of the surrounding vehicles can help an autonomous vehicle plan its trajectory well ahead. We plan to predict the future trajectories of surrounding vehicles based on their short-term historical trajectories by considering human driving styles. Given the clustered data from the first objective, we will have several sub-datasets of different driving styles. For each sub-dataset, a model will be trained to predict the future trajectory of the vehicle with a specific driving style. We then use the model that corresponds to its recognized driving style to predict the trajectory of a vehicle. The generative model will be adopted to generate the predicted trajectory based on a short historical trajectory.

To design a behavior planner for an autonomous vehicle. The behavior planner is responsible for selecting a driving behavior for the autonomous vehicle based on the environment, passenger preference, and current behavior. To this end, we will first build different sets of behaviors for different traffic scenarios (e.g. urban, highway), then find the transition conditions to change from one driving behavior to another under each traffic scenario. Besides the transitions among different driving behaviors in one traffic scenario, the transitions among different traffic scenarios will also be taken into consideration. The most direct approach to represent these transitions is to design a hierarchical finite state machine. The clustered sub-datasets of different driving styles will be reorganized according to driving behaviors to find such transitions. In other words, given a set of behaviors of a driving style for one traffic scenario, we will model the transition conditions among different driving behaviors.

To design a customized motion planning scheme. With the accurate future trajectory of the surrounding vehicles and the determined driving behavior, we aim to develop new algorithmic motion planning algorithms to generate a collision free and interpretable trajectory. The objective function of a traditional motion planning problem usually minimizes the traveling time, fuel consumption, and jerk. However, it may lead to generating a trajectory that cannot be interpreted by human drivers. We will solve this problem by allowing users to customize their preferred driving styles. To enforce a trajectory to be close to a preferred driving style chosen by the passengers in car, we will apply inverse reinforcement learning to get a reward function that needs to be maximized in the objective function. We will leverage the clustered sub-datasets of different driving styles to learn the reward functions for different driving styles.

11200220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200220.value: In this project, we have thoroughly studied how to characterize driven styles, how to generate different driving styles, how to integrate driven styles into the consideration of trajectory prediction and motion planning including lane keep and lane changing decisions. The research has been published in top conferences and journals. In particular, the work on trajectory prediction has won a few championships in International challenges. The major findings can be summarized as follows: 1) Driver behaviours can be modelled, and modelling driver behaviour can help model personalization which is important for imitation learning. We proposed a deep neural network (DNN)-based reward function for inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) based driver behaviour modelling (DBM) with efficient model personalization via machine unlearning. The evaluation results show that our approach achieves a higher prediction accuracy compared with the latest IRL-based DBM approach that uses a weighted sum of trajectory features as the reward function. Our model personalization method obtains the highest accuracy and lowest latency compared with the baselines. 2) We studied a novel generative hybrid car-following (CF) model, which achieves high accuracy in characterizing dynamic human CF behaviors and is able to generate realistic human CF behaviors for any given observed or even unobserved driving style. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed models, we conduct extensive experiments and comparisons, including CF model parameter calibration, CF behavior prediction, and trajectory simulation for different driving styles. 3) We proposed QCNet, a modeling framework toward pushing the boundaries of trajectory prediction. We introduce a query-centric paradigm for scene encoding, which enables the reuse of past computations by learning representations independent of the global spacetime coordinate system. Our approach ranks 1st on Argoverse 1 and Argoverse 2 motion forecasting benchmarks, outperforming all methods on all main metrics by a large margin. Meanwhile, our model can achieve streaming scene encoding and parallel multi-agent decoding thanks to the query-centric design ethos. 4)We integrate the human factors that are represented by driving styles to design a new discrete lane changing (DLC) decision-making model, part of motion planning. We integrate algorithmic motion planning with learning models to improve sampling-based motion planning (BMP) in highway traffic. The simulation experiments are conducted based on the vehicle trajectory dataset NGSIM. The results show that the proposed sampling strategy outperforms existing sampling strategies in terms of the computing time, traveling time, and smoothness of the trajectory.

11200820.label: Project Objectives
11200820.value: Screening of crosslinking methodologies for hyaluronic acid (HA) to optimize its swelling properties and mechanical properties. The hydrogel microneedles (MNs) will be based on crosslinked HA. We will focus on the chemical crossing with chemicals like glutaraldehyde, acrylate, maleimide etc. HA hydrogels derived from these methods will be compared for their swelling ratio, mechanical strength in dry status, and cytotoxicity. Evaluation of the universality of HA MNs for extraction of different types of biomarkers. There are different types of biomarkers in skin ISF, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, small (<500 Da) and big (>500 Da). Therefore, it is critical to fully understand the capability and limitations of this HA MN system. We will screen a few representative biomarkers that are present in skin ISF and had been successfully sampled using the conventional methods. Development of the flexible base for MN patches through templated assembly. A flexible base is critical to conform the curved human skin and to accommodate body movements. But a rigid MN tip is required to penetrate into the skin. Thus a combination of flexible substrate and rigid needle tip could assemble both advantages. Instead of fabricating one continuous array of MNs, we will modify the mold design to segment or discretize the individual MN tip. Then, the segmented MN will undergo re-articulation on a flexible substrate made of flexible materials like silicone. Integration with electrochemical electrodes for timely analysis of biomarkers. Taking glucose as a model biomarker, we will print the enzymatic electrodes for glucose on the flexible base of the MN patch. Segmented MNs can be identified as a unit of electronic signal. We will use the unitized electronic signal as monitoring the concentration of glucose in extracted fluid. In vitro and in vivo experiments will be performed.

11200820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200820.value: Personal health-monitoring devices have been commercialized in the form of eyeglasses, watches, bands, and clothes to detect the physical vital signs such as heart rate, blood pressure, and body temperature. The next generation is expected to monitor analytes in the skin compartment that contain more accurate and complete biological information. One key challenge is the accurate acquisition of the bio-signals in real time. Skin interstitial fluid (ISF) exhibits a dynamic exchange of molecules with capillary blood thereby offering continuous access to analytes with minimal trauma. This next generation of personal health-monitoring devices is built on microneedles that penetrate into the skin and extract ISF for the timely analysis of health-related analytes. It involves the synthesis and characterization of biomaterials, microneedle device fabrication and integration with electrochemical sensors. The platform technology will be tested in vitro and in vivo by taking glucose as the model biomarker. 智能可穿戴设备可以提供血压、血糖系列健康信息，并将这些信息进行有效收集和分析，从而使我们实现对自身健康状况的即时跟踪检测。在开发这类设备过程中，一个关键的技术难题是于实时准确地采集生物生理信号。皮肤间质液具有与毛细血管间存在动态分子交换的特性，因此可以持续地提供生物生理信号。本项目致力于开发一种基于微针的皮肤贴，以微创方式来提取皮肤间质液、并实现生物生理信号的实时采集和分析。它涉及到生物材料的合成和表征，微针设备的制造，以及与电化学传感器的集成等过程。该平台将以葡萄糖为生物标志物模型进行体外和体内测试。

11200820.label: Realisation of objectives
11200820.value: Objective 1: Screening of Crosslinking Methodologies for Hyaluronic Acid (HA) to Optimize Swelling and Mechanical Properties Achievements: We successfully synthesized hyaluronic methacrylate (MeHA) by modifying HA with methacrylic anhydride, combining HA's superior water affinity with enhanced stability through crosslinking. This allowed the development of hydrogels capable of significant swelling without dissolving in aqueous environments. MeHA microneedles, when inserted into the skin, demonstrated rapid swelling and effective fluid exchange with subcutaneous tissues, enabling continuous collection of interstitial fluid. We systematically investigated the relationship between crosslinking degree and water absorption. By varying UV exposure times (3, 5, 10, 15 minutes), we controlled the crosslinking degree of MeHA patches. Swelling studies revealed that patches exposed to 3 minutes of UV (MeHA-MN-CL3) exhibited the best profile, absorbing up to four times their weight in water within five minutes. However, insufficient crosslinking at less than 3 minutes led to partial dissolution during swelling. Mechanical testing showed that the patches achieved a force load of ~30 N, sufficient to penetrate skin under minimal pressure (~1.5 N) without deformation. Publications: 1. Seeni R., et al., Advanced Functional Materials, 2021, 31, 2105686 2. Zheng M., et al., Bioengineering & Translational Medicine, 2023, 8(5): e10413 Objective 2: Evaluating the Universality of HA Microneedles for Biomarker Extraction Achievements: We demonstrated the feasibility of MeHA microneedles in extracting large biomarkers, using FITC-Dextran (20 kDa) as a model. The successful extraction of FITC-Dextran confirmed the capability of MeHA microneedles to handle macromolecules. We further investigated the effect of internal mesh size on the extraction of S100A1 (10 kDa), a melanoma biomarker. MeHA derived from HA with varying molecular weights (10-100, 200-400, 900 kDa) was tested on an agarose-based skin model. Microneedles from 10-100 kDa HA showed superior performance, especially at higher concentrations. In vivo experiments using melanoma mouse models validated the ability of these microneedles to extract S100A1. Results indicated significantly higher S100A1 concentrations in interstitial fluid from melanoma sites compared to normal skin, highlighting the potential for non-invasive melanoma screening. Publications: Wang G., et al., Advanced Science, 2024, 11, 2306188 Objective 3: Developing Flexible Bases for Microneedle Patches via Templated Assembly Achievements: We engineered a stretchable electrode array integrated with MeHA microneedles. Flexible substrates were designed to maintain stability under deformation, while serpentine electrode patterns simplified circuit design. Each microneedle was secured to electrode units via in-situ photocuring, with additional carbon paste layers preventing oxidation of the copper substrate. This design ensured the mechanical stability of the microneedles, even in swollen states or under strain. Publication: He J., et al., BME Frontiers, 2024, 5:0044 Objective 4: Integration of Electrochemical Sensors for Biomarker Analysis Achievements: We developed electrochemical biosensors using screen-printed three-electrode strips with linear responses to biomarkers such as glucose and alcohol. These were integrated with MeHA microneedles to create biosensors for non-invasive glucose and alcohol monitoring. The challenge of combining water-swellable MeHA with non-swellable electrochemical strips was resolved using an adhesive chitosan layer. The biosensors, validated in mice models, showed strong correlations between electrical signals and blood glucose levels, demonstrating their efficacy for real-time, non-invasive monitoring. 11200820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200820.value: Through this project, we developed a highly swellable, mechanically robust, and biocompatible microneedle material, optimized for minimally invasive sampling and biomarker detection. This platform successfully monitored glucose, alcohol, and S100A1 protein from interstitial fluid, offering a transformative approach to non-invasive diagnostics. The project resulted in 20 peer-reviewed publications, including high-impact journals such as Nature Reviews Bioengineering and Nature Biomedical Engineering. The PI delivered five keynote talks at international conferences, including Microneedle 2023 in Seattle. Additionally, six undergraduate and two PhD students were trained under this grant, contributing to innovation competitions and securing further funding. The PI's achievements also led to the prestigious National Natural Science Foundation of China's Distinguished Young Scholars award.

11200820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200820.value: Future research will focus on expanding the biomarker range to include inflammatory cytokines, hormones, and metabolites. Addressing sensitivity and specificity challenges, particularly for low-abundance biomarkers, will be a priority. Efforts will also explore multifunctional microneedle systems that combine diagnostics and therapeutics, leveraging stimuli-responsive materials for precision medicine. To advance clinical translation, we aim to improve the scalability of microneedle fabrication and integrate wireless signal transmission for real-time data monitoring.

11200820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200820.value: This grant has supported the development of an innovative wearable microneedle device for minimally invasive sampling of skin interstitial fluid and in situ detection of biomarkers such as glucose, alcohol, and the melanoma biomarker S100A1 protein. The device consists of three key components: highly swellable microneedle tips, a flexible backing, and integrated electrochemical sensors. The microneedle tips penetrate the skin to extract interstitial fluid, the electrochemical sensors convert biomarker concentrations into digital signals, and the flexible backing houses the sensors and signal processing components while ensuring user comfort. The device's functionality was successfully demonstrated in mice models, accurately monitoring biomarker concentrations. This research is significant as it has the potential to transform healthcare by simplifying diagnostics and treatment. By providing a fast, affordable, and less invasive solution, this technology could greatly enhance early disease detection, personalized medicine, and overall patient care, ultimately improving quality of life on a global scale.

11201020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201020.value: Artificial intelligence is transforming human society at a phenomenal speed. Its profound impact is attributable to the application of machine learning, the core technology of artificial intelligence, to many areas of scientific and engineering research. However, there have to date been few machine learning-based investigations of the micromechanics of granular materials. Accordingly, the aim of this proposed research is to develop machine-learning methodology for investigating the macro-micro-mechanics of granular soils. The microcomputed tomography data of inter-particle contact and particle morphology within a sheared sand specimen will be combined with discrete element simulation data of inter-particle contact force to form a comprehensive database for the training of two artificial neural networks. The first artificial neural network will use microcomputed tomography data to predict the inter-particle contact forces between sand particles, and the second artificial neural network will use these predicted inter-particle contact forces and microcomputed tomography data to predict the macroscopic mechanical properties of a sheared sand specimen. There is currently no optimal experimental technique to measure inter-particle contact forces within an assembly of real sand particles, and thus this proposed methodology is highly innovative and will yield new tools for understanding and solving the long-standing and complex macro-micro granular mechanics problem. This project will have high impacts on basic and applied research in a variety of fields such as geomechanics, granular materials, powder technology, geophysics, geotechnical engineering, engineering geology and petroleum and mining engineering, concomitant with great economic and societal impacts. The research impacts will primarily derive from the newly established machine-learning tool, which will enable accurate, efficient and robust predictions of the multiscale mechanical properties of granular soils to be made. These predictions will lead to new scientific discoveries and inventions. The economic and societal impacts will derive from the use of the machine learning tool to generate data for geotechnical engineering activities such as site investigation, design, construction and maintenance of infrastructures, risk monitoring and hazard mitigation, or manufacturing, handling and processing of granular materials in relevant industries. This will catalyze the development of optimized engineering activities and processes, subsequently leading to improvements in civil infrastructure, construction management, hazard warning and mitigation systems, and to novel and inexpensive granular materials. 人工智能正以現象級的速度改變著人類社會。其核心技術機器學習對於許多科學和工程研究領域有著深遠的影響。然而，關於顆粒土體微觀力學領域的機器學習研究至今仍顯不足。有鑑於此，本項目致力於發展和運用機器學習方法以研究顆粒土的宏微觀力學行為。基於微觀X射線斷層掃描所得的顆粒土試樣在剪切過程中的顆粒間接觸和顆粒形貌數據，以及基於離散元模擬得到的顆粒間接觸力數據，共同組成一個綜合數據庫，用於神經網絡的訓練和預測。由於目前尚不存在完美的試驗技術用於測量真實土體內顆粒間的接觸力，所以本項目提出的方法具有高度創新型，，並會生成新的工具，用於進一步理解和解決複雜的、長期存在的顆粒力學問題。 本項目的成功開展將對諸如地質力學、顆粒材料、粉末技術、地球物理、岩土工程、工程地質以及石油和採礦工程等領域的基礎和應用研究方面有著深遠的影響，伴隨著可觀的經濟和社會效應。研究影響主要來源於新建立的機器學習工具，該工具將對顆粒土的多尺度力學性能進行準確、高效和穩健的預測，從而得到新的科學發現和發明。經濟和社會影響來源於運用所得機器學習工具為岩土工程中的諸如基礎設施的實地勘測、設計、建造和維護，以及風險監測、防災減災，或者在相關工業領域製造、處理、加工顆粒材料提供必要數據。從而促進工業活動和進程的最優化發展，進一步引領民用基礎設施、施工管理、防災減災系統以及新穎、造價低的顆粒材料的迅猛發展。

11201020.label: Realisation of objectives
11201020.value: Objective 1: This objective has been fully achieved. In-situ X-ray micro-tomography (CT) studies on silica sands, completely decomposed granite (CDG), carbonate sands and rubber balls using a miniature triaxial loading apparatus were carried out at the BL13HB beamline of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility. Specifically, the silica sand studied is Fujian sand (FJS), which contains more than 98% of SiO2, was created by the region’s dynamic geological history, involving mountain formation, erosion, river transportation, and deposition. The CDG is composed primarily of quartz, feldspar, biotite, mica, and other minerals, where the weak minerals such as feldspar and biotite have weathered and decomposed over time to form a clay matrix. A thorough investigation into the particle-scale behavior, processes and mechanisms of all the above tested materials has been made using advanced image processing, analysis and particle tracking techniques. Objective 2: This objective has been fully achieved. Sophisticated Discrete Element Method (DEM) modeling of the mini-triaxial test based on one-to-one mapping of sand particles has been conducted for two kinds of quartz sand, namely, Leighton Buzzard sand (LBS) and Fujian sand (FJS). The study compares the DEM simulation results with physical experiments at multiple length scales including the macroscopic sample length scale and the particle scale. A series of image processing techniques were utilized to binarize, segment and label the raw data in CT images obtained from the mini-triaxial test. A spherical harmonic analysis was used to filter the image data and to reconstruct the natural particle morphology. This study demonstrates that the proposed modeling approach is capable of reproducing macroscopic (e.g., stiffness, deviatoric stress response and volumetric response) and particle level (e.g., displacement, rotation and branch vector orientation) behaviors that are very similar to what occurs within the physical experiments, validating the effectiveness of the proposed one-to-one mapping technique. Objective 3: This objective has been fully achieved. Based on DEM simulation data, an artificial neural network (ANN) is developed and applied to predict the anisotropy of the contact force chains (CFC) in two types of idealized granular materials with different initial relative densities undergoing triaxial shearing. Five features including particle size, coordination number and particle displacement (i.e., x-, y- and z-components of the particle displacement) at the particle-scale and the meso-scale each are used to train and test the established ANN model. The results of ANN model prediction show that the 3D orientational distributions of the CFCs from the ANN predictions match very well the DEM simulation results during the whole shearing progress. It is found that for both dense and loose samples, the combined set of particle-scale and meso-scale features have a dominating influence on the CFC evolutions but the ANN model performs better in the CFCs estimation at the strain increment of 0–7% than at the strain increment of 7%–14%. The outcome of this study shows that machine learning is a promising tool for studying the complex mechanical behavior of granular materials. Objective 4: This objective has been fully achieved. A machine learning-based strategy was developed to estimate the CFCs of uniformly sized spherical granular materials under triaxial compression, using particle kinematics and inter-particle contact evolution data measured by μCT. A graph neural network (GNN) was introduced to predict the contact force chains of granular materials at the end of a shear increment based on the evolution of contact network and grain displacement during that shear increment. Meanwhile, DEM modelling is performed for a glass bead (GB) specimen under triaxial compression with the use of in-situ μCT scanning. The DEM model has the same initial conditions as the GB specimen and is validated by comparing the calculated stress–strain curves, particle kinematics and inter-particle contact fabric evolution of the numerical specimen with the experimental results. The DEM model is used to generate sufficient virtual data to train the GNN model, which is applied to the GB specimen to predict the evolution of contact force chains. The model-predicted results yield a power-law relationship between the above mean normalized particle maximum normal contact forces and the probability density function, which is consistent with the findings reported in previous numerical studies. Objective 5: This objective has been fully achieved. A machine learning-based strategy has been developed to experimentally estimate the CFCs of granular materials under triaxial compression. The study shows that the CFCs of a granular system at the end of a shear increment can be estimated based on the particle kinematics and the inter-particle contact evolution of the system that occur during the shear increment. The method is applied to a GB specimen under triaxial compression with in-situ X-ray μCT scanning. To this end, a GNN model is developed to model the complex nonlinear relationship among the PMNCFs, the particle kinematics and the inter-particle contact evolution of the specimen. The model is trained using virtual data provided by DEM simulating the GB specimen under triaxial compression. The DEM model has the same initial macroscale properties as the GB specimen, including initial porosity, specimen size, sample grading and confining stress. Both the macro-scale and micro-scale mechanical behaviour of the numerical specimen, including the stress–strain behaviour and the particle kinematical and contact fabric behaviour, are essentially consistent with that of the experimental specimen. Therefore, the numerical model is considered to accurately capture the force transmission mechanism of the GB specimen under triaxial compression. Objective 6: This objective has been fully achieved. A paradigm-shifting methodology for the constitutive modelling of granular soils subject to triaxial shearing which integrates the techniques of X-ray micro computed tomography, three-dimensional discrete element modelling and deep learning has been developed. Firstly, the triaxial testing on a mini-sample of a quartz sand with in-situ micro computed tomography is performed to acquire the complete set of macro- and micro-scale mechanical properties of the sample. Secondly, the tomography data of a series of representative sand particles is used to construct the three-dimensional discrete element model of the sand sample which is then used to generate the numerical datasets for the subsequent deep learning task. Thirdly, a deep learning model called the long short-term memory network is developed to capture the combined effects of particle shape, confining pressure, and initial sample density on the constitutive behaviour of sands. Lastly, the effectiveness of the deep learning model is shown by comparing the model prediction on the testing datasets with the numerical simulation results. Furthermore, the capability of the model on predicting the real sand behaviour is demonstrated by an excellent agreement between the model prediction based on the input of tomography data and the soil response measured from the triaxial test.

11201020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201020.value: Major findings of this project include: 1) particle-scale behavior, processes and mechanisms of a series of granular materials including silica sands, completely decomposed granite (CDG), carbonate sands and rubber balls elucidated by In-situ X-ray micro-tomography (CT) studies; 2) sophisticated DEM modeling tools of granular materials incorporating one-to-one mapping of sand particles and morphological gene mutation and decay of sand particles; 3) artificial neural networks (ANN) that are capable of predicting the contact force chains (CFC) within idealized granular materials; 4) a graph neural network (GNN) that is capable of predicting the contact force chains (CFC) within a real granular media such as glass beads; and 5) A paradigm-shifting methodology for the constitutive modelling of granular soils subject to triaxial shearing which integrates the techniques of X-ray micro computed tomography, three-dimensional discrete element modelling and deep learning. The project has generated very abundant research outcomes including 28 journal articles, 13 conference papers, 2 PhD graduates and a number of national and international research awards.

11201020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201020.value: Great potential exists in extending the methodologies developed in this project to the characterization, quantification and prediction of contact force chains within real granular medias that are composed of irregularly shaped grains and crushable materials. The constitutive modelling of granular soils using deep learning methods is also a promising line of research worthy of further investigation. Future grant applications will be made in these areas to advance the frontier of fundamental research in granular materials and mechanics.

11201020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201020.value: This proposed project has pioneered the development and application of machine learning methods to the study of the micromechanics of granular materials based on a large database of granular soils established from the X-ray micro-tomography (CT) and Discrete Element Method (DEM) simulation studies. The significance and value of this research mainly stems from the newly established machine-learning tools that have enabled accurate, efficient and robust predictions of the multiscale mechanical properties of granular materials. In particular, a paradigm-shifting methodology for the constitutive modelling of granular soils which can take into account the effects of discrete particle shape on the macroscopic soil behavior has been developed. These research outcomes may open a new avenue towards the exploration into the multi-scale morphology, structure, and mechanics of granular materials.

11201120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201120.value: Cooperative control of networked multiple dynamical systems has become a topic of focus in the control community in recent years. This is mainly due to its broad applications in many areas including multiple spacecraft vehicles, biological systems, networked multiple mobile robots, teams of unmanned aerial vehicles, sensor networks and so on. Networked multiple dynamical systems are often referred to as multi-agent systems. The problems commonly addressed for networked multiple dynamical systems or multi-agent systems include consensus, cooperative output regulation, rendezvous, formation and so on. On the other hand, practical systems are often subject to variety of time delays, which can be typically classified as bounded or unbounded, and they are often the main cause of poor performance or even instability of the concerned systems. Multi-agent systems are no exception and often subject to various time delays, in particular, transmission delays between agents during their communication. Cooperative control of multi-agent systems with time delays has received considerable attention and many results have been reported in the past years. However, most of those results focus on only bounded delays, while unbounded delays are considered only for very simple agent dynamics such as integrators or homogeneous linear systems with some very restrictive assumptions, and for fixed transmission topologies. The recent literature review reveals that cooperative control of multi-agent systems with unbounded time delays is in its very early stage of development and many critical issues remain to be addressed. The issues include (i) how to deal with more general heterogeneous agent dynamics, (ii) how to deal with system uncertainties, and (iii) how to tackle more general time-varying transmission topologies. The successful addressing of these issues would greatly expand the range of applications of relevant theories and methodologies developed for cooperative control of multi-agent systems subject to unbounded delays as practical multi-agent systems are often heterogeneous, often of various uncertainties, and often subject to switching transmission topologies. This project will investigate and develop novel theories and methodologies for cooperative control of more general multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays, and in particular with heterogeneous agent dynamics, system uncertainties, and/or switching topologies. The outcomes of this project are expected to enrich the theoretical foundation and to provide more solid analysis and synthesis tools in cooperative control of networked multiple dynamical systems with unbounded transmission delays. 近年来網絡化多動態系統的协同控制已经成为控制界關注的熱門話題。這主要是由於其在多航天器系统、生物系統、網絡化多機器人系統、無人機、傳感器網絡等方面的廣泛應用。網絡化多動態系統通常代指多智能體系統。其常見的研究課題包括一致性、協同輸出調節、會合、編隊等。另一方面，實際系統常常受到時滯的影響，從而讓系統性能變差甚至不穩定。典型的時滯可以分為有界時滯和無界時滯。多智能體系統同樣會受到時滯的影響，尤其是，智能體間的通信會導致傳輸時滯。因而具有時滯的多智能體系統的協同控制也在最近幾年被廣泛關注並且有大量相關的結果發表。然而，絕大多數已經發表的結果僅考慮有界時滯，只有少量的工作考慮了無界時滯。這些已知的相關工作討論的系統動態比較簡單，例如單積分器系統或者具有較嚴格假設的同構線性系統，並且也只考慮了固定的通信拓撲。近期的文獻綜述顯示，具有無界時滯的多智能體系統的協同控制方面的研究尚處於早期，有許多關鍵的問題亟待解決。這些問題包括（一）如何處理更具一般性的異構多智能體系統，（二）如何處理系統不確定性，（三）如何處理更具一般性的時變拓撲。考慮到實際應用中的多智能體系統通常是異構的，且往往具有不確定性和切換拓撲，以上關於具有無界時滯的多智能體系統的協調控制的問題如得以解決，將極大地拓展相關理論和方法的應用範圍。基於以上原因，此項目將研究和發展新的理論和方法，以解決具有無界传输時滯的多智能體系統的協調控制的更一般化問題，尤其是與異構智能體動態、系統不確定性和切換拓撲相關的問題。項目的最終結果有望充實現有理論基礎並且提供更加堅實的可綜合分析具有無界传输時滯的網絡化多動態系統的協調控制的工具。

11201120.label: Realisation of objectives
11201120.value: All of the project objectives have been achieved. More specifically, we have investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays. We have also investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays and agent/system uncertainties. In addition, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approaches and methodologies by extensive simulations.

11201120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201120.value: We have investigated cooperative control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays. Stability analysis and control of even single systems with unbounded delays have been a challenge in the control community. To address the cooperative control problem of heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays, we have developed fundamental theories and methodologies for stability analysis and control of single systems with unbounded delays first. We then have investigated and developed novel distributed controllers for the concerned multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays. It is shown that the controlled heterogeneous multi-agent systems can achieve consensus or cooperative output regulation under some mild conditions. We have further investigated and developed novel distributed controllers for the concerned multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays and agent/system uncertainties. We have found that both fixed and switching directed graphs can be handled. A key feature of the proposed approaches is that the knowledge of the unbounded transmission delays is not required a priori. We have also found that our results include many existing results for cooperative control of multi-agent systems with bounded transmission delays as special cases. In the process of achieving the objectives of this project, in addition to those results on stability analysis and control of single systems with unbounded delays, some other results on cooperative control of multi-agent systems have also been obtained. Extensive simulations via various multi-agent systems including networked mobile robots have been conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. As a result of our research effort, more than 10 journal papers have been either published or accepted.

11201120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201120.value: This project has investigated cooperative control problems of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays. However, communication channels are also often subject to other constraints such as packet dropouts and quantization. It would be interesting to investigate cooperative control problems of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems under simultaneous existence of unbounded transmission delays and other communication constraints such as packet dropouts and quantization. In addition, our results on cooperative control of multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays and switching graphs require that the switching graphs are always connected which is conservative. Further studies to remove this restrictive assumption would be interesting and desirable.

11201120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201120.value: Cooperative control of networked multi-agent systems have attracted considerable interest in recent years. The recent literature review reveals that most existing works on cooperative control of networked multi-agent systems with transmission delays focus on bounded transmission delays. This project has thus investigated cooperative control of networked multi-agent systems with more general unbounded transmission delays which include bounded transmission delays as special cases. To address cooperative control problems of multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays, we have developed fundamental theories and methodologies for stability analysis and control of single systems with unbounded delays first. We then have developed novel distributed controllers for the concerned multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays under both fixed and switching directed graphs. It is shown that the controlled heterogeneous multi-agent systems can achieve consensus or cooperative output regulation under some mild conditions. We have further investigated and developed novel distributed controllers for the concerned multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays and agent/system uncertainties. We have also carried out extensive simulations to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. The outcomes of this project are expected to consolidate theoretical foundation and also enhance application potential of cooperative control for networked multi-agent systems with unbounded transmission delays.

11201220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201220.value: The major challenge impeding the progress of machine learning is the lack of sufficient labeled data. Effectively addressing this problem is particularly critical for applications in which human lives are at stake, as in the development of an intelligent traffic management system through training a deep neural network. If the trained network is expected to have the capability of detecting pedestrians and oncoming vehicles, and issuing warning when they are too close to each other, the inadequacy of labeled training examples may lead to tragic consequences if the system fails to detect pedestrians in the path of approaching vehicles. To address this challenge, a possible approach is to adapt a trained model from a source domain, with plenty of labeled data, to a related target domain in which few labeled instances are available. However, the main problem of this transfer learning approach is the mismatch between the source and target data distribution, as in the case of adapting a model trained with synthetic images to analyze real images. If the mismatch is severe, no amount of adaptation based on re-training a single model can bridge this domain gap. Adopting the Bayesian interpretation of a model as an instance sampled from a posterior probability distribution of model parameters, given a training dataset, we introduce a new transfer learning framework in this project. Specifically, we re-formulate transfer learning as the transformation of a complete source domain model distribution to a target domain distribution, such that knowledge can be effectively transferred across the domains without extensive iterative training. The importance of this framework is in its capability of bridging significant domain discrepancy through generating and combining a diverse class of models, which cannot possibly be achieved through training a single model. To model this distribution-to-distribution transformation, the generative adversarial network (GAN) model will be applied. The generator and discriminator of the GAN model will compete with each other, such that the transformed source model parameter distribution can generate a target model indistinguishable from the actual one. The proposed framework will question the necessity of requiring a data-rich environment and extensive iterative training for effective machine learning, and introduce the new approach of creating a hypothesis-rich learning environment, with the sparse dataset serving as constraints for the hypothesis generation process. This will result in a significant impact to the entire field of machine learning and many of its related applications, including object detection, scene understanding, and face analysis/verification.

11201220.label: Realisation of objectives
11201220.value: Identification of the performance limit of current transfer learning frameworks: To address Objective 1 of the project, we have conducted a systematic evaluation of standard transfer learning methods across source/target domains in settings characterized by sparse supervision and wide domain discrepancies. These settings include mismatched input distributions, non-overlapping label spaces, and multi-task configurations where the feature relevance varies across domains. Through controlled experiments, we observe that applying fine-tuning to a single deep network model often leads to performance degradation due to overfitting and lack of alignment with the target task. In addition, existing techniques lack the flexibility to account for uncertainties in task- or domain-specific variations, and these limitations motivate us to explore a more expressive and flexible framework that could accommodate distributional shifts at the model parameter level, guided by higher-level task specifications. Transforming a source model parameter distribution to a target model parameter distribution: To address Objective 2 of the project, we formulate a novel transfer learning framework based on distributional transformation in the deep network model parameter space for mitigating the problem of significant domain discrepancy. Rather than transferring knowledge via a fixed source model, we construct a hypothesis-rich representation by modeling the source parameter space as a distribution, and learning how to adapt this distribution to a new domain using minimal supervision. The key innovation lies in integrating domain knowledge with model adaptation. To achieve this objective, we develop a multi-modal adaptation module that maps both input features and task-specific knowledge into a joint latent space. This space captures not only low-level feature similarities but also high-level task alignment, enabling effective matching between source and target domains. We further introduce a mechanism for learning the posterior probability distribution of target model parameters conditioned on sparse samples or task embeddings. This posterior distribution is represented implicitly in the latent space and sampled during inference to generate diverse, yet structurally aligned, candidate models. The resulting diversity ensures robustness across various target scenarios, while domain knowledge conditioning guarantees relevance. This approach effectively resolves the issue of domain overfitting and allows the system to generalize to unseen or low-data tasks with improved fidelity. Representation and transformation of model parameter distributions: To address Objective 3 of the project, we have successfully developed a domain knowledge–driven transfer learning framework by modeling both the source and target models as distributions over model parameters, rather than single deterministic representations. Based on this formulation, the source model parameters are first embedded into a structured latent representation space that encapsulates the underlying domain knowledge. This facilitates the learning of a more accurate transformation from the source domain to the target domain, especially when only sparse data is available in the target setting. To learn this transformation, we represent each deep network model using a modular parameter encoding scheme, in which each network layer is associated with a compact embedding. The distance between domains is then modeled as the alignment between these embedded parameter components. A set of encoding and decoding modules are jointly trained to capture this distribution-level correspondence. Importantly, we propose an iterative refinement mechanism to progressively improve the generated target model parameters. After the initial transformation, the sampled target models are evaluated on held-out validation data, and the feedback is used to adjust the embedding and generation modules. This closed-loop correction process ensures consistency between the learned domain representation and the actual target domain performance. To synthesize models that generalize well in the target domain, we employ a conditional generative model architecture. Specifically, we train a generator module to synthesise layer-wise parameters conditioned on both source model embeddings and task-level domain descriptors. We use a discriminator to ensure that the generated model parameters are statistically indistinguishable from those obtained by training on real target data. By sampling from the learned target model distribution, we generate an ensemble of candidate models, each tailored to a slightly different interpretation of the target task. This ensemble allows us to approximate the hypothesis space even with limited labeled examples. To enhance knowledge transfer effectiveness, we develop a model selection procedure that identifies the most appropriate generated models using unsupervised criteria such as intra-model consistency, task confidence scores, and compatibility with the target domain’s knowledge embedding. The selected models are further fine-tuned using a lightweight adaptation strategy that maintains alignment with the original posterior distribution of parameter values. By completing the above tasks, we have successfully achieved Objective 3 of the project to effectively learn the transformation between the source model parameter distribution and target model parameter distribution. In addition, the incorporation of domain knowledge to guide the learning of this distribution-to-distribution transformation also plays a central role in downstream model refinement and selection. Evaluation across diverse application domains: To address Objective 4 of the project, we have extensively evaluated our framework on a wide range of real-world applications, including pedestrian detection under occluded conditions, face analysis/verification, and high-fidelity image synthesis with limited data. These tasks reflect both visual and structural domain differences that necessitate the incorporation of robust adaptation strategies. Extensive evaluation was conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in various computer vision tasks: it is observed that the proposed framework achieves an improvement of 44.3% over representative pedestrian detection approaches in terms of average precision on KITTI, which is one of the largest datasets for autonomous driving research, an improvement of 15.8% over competing low-resolution face verification methods in terms of accuracy on the well-established face image dataset CelebA, and an improvement of 78.4% over leading class-conditional semi-supervised image generation methods, in terms of the Frechet Inception Distance, on the most widely-used fine-grained image dataset CUB. In all tasks, our framework outperforms conventional domain-adversarial methods and distribution matching baselines. Results of multiple ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each component of the proposed framework, in particular the iterative refinement mechanism and the conditional generator module based on domain knowledge. We also demonstrate that even without target labels, the framework maintains strong generalization capabilities, highlighting its effectiveness in real-world application scenarios where annotated data is scarce or unavailable.

11201220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201220.value: In this project, we address the challenge of transfer learning under large domain discrepancies by shifting the perspective from single-model adaptation to modeling at the parameter distribution level. In this formulation, the source model is no longer treated as a fixed entity, but instead as a probabilistic representation from which multiple model instances can be sampled. These parameter samples act as auxiliary candidates that, once conditionally transformed based on target-specific domain knowledge, can adapt to diverse downstream tasks. To enable this transformation, we have developed a generative model adaptation framework in which domain knowledge, encoded through task-specific conditioning information or structured descriptors, is used to guide the generation of target model parameters. Specifically, a generator learns the mapping between the source and target parameter distributions, while a discriminator evaluates the plausibility of generated parameters within the target domain. This adversarial modeling process ensures that the generated models are both structurally coherent and functionally aligned with the target task. A key feature of our framework is the introduction of an iterative refinement mechanism, wherein the generated model candidates are progressively updated using feedback derived from downstream validation performance. This bidirectional adaptation process enhances the alignment between the generated parameters and the actual task structure, leading to significantly improved target models. Through extensive experiments across tasks such as pedestrian detection, face analysis/verification, and image enhancement, the following main findings were observed: - The use of domain knowledge–guided generative modeling enables the framework to outperform conventional fine-tuning and domain adaptation methods, particularly under sparse supervision. - Compared to standard domain adaptation, the proposed approach maintains stable performance even as the domain gap increases, due to its ability to synthesise diverse and flexible model candidates. - While increasing the complexity of the generator module initially improves performance, the resulting improvement tapers off when the number of parameters increase beyond a certain value, thus highlighting the importance of controlling the model size. - The ensemble of generated parameter sets allows for more robust generalization across domains, surpassing single-model baselines in both accuracy and robustness to unseen data. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the effectiveness of reformulating transfer learning as a model parameter distribution transformation problem driven by domain knowledge, and validate the potential of our framework for a wide range of real-world applications.

11201220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201220.value: To further enhance the adaptability of the proposed framework, we shall investigate the possibility of integrating large language models (LLMs) for encoding domain knowledge into the model adaptation process. Specifically, we aim to represent task-level descriptors such as metadata and domain tags by encoding them into embeddings generated by LLMs. We will compare several LLM integration strategies. First, a LLM will be used to extract domain representations for conditioning the generative parameter transformation process. Next, the LLM will be fine-tuned on a set of task adaptation examples to improve its alignment with the target model objectives. Finally, adapter-based conditioning will be examined, where lightweight plug-in modules are attached to LLM layers to enable task-specific modulation of the auxiliary parameters associated wtih these modules, without altering core parameters. These LLM-derived embeddings will be fused with the source model representations to condition the generator for synthesising target model parameters. We will also analyse how different conditioning information and embedding granularities affect the quality, diversity, and fidelity of generated target models. Through these investigations, we aim to establish a systematic understanding of how to achieve effective domain knowledge–aware model generation across tasks.

11201220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201220.value: One of the key challenges in machine learning is the lack of sufficient labeled data, especially in critical applications such as pedestrian detection, scene understanding, and face analysis/verification. Training reliable models under such constraints is difficult, and failures due to data scarcity can have serious consequences. To address this challenge, this project proposes a new machine learning framework to transfer knowledge from a source domain to a target domain. Instead of re-training a single model, we treat models as samples drawn from a probability distribution, and focus on transforming a source model distribution, trained on a data-rich domain, into one suitable for the target domain with minimal labeled data. The new framework facilitates more effective and flexible cross-domain knowledge transfer, even when the source and target domains differ significantly. We achieve this objective using a generative model adaptation framework that learns to synthesise diverse and target-relevant models through a domain knowledge–guided transformation process. This framework reduces reliance on an intensive training process and creates a hypothesis-rich learning environment, where limited target data is used only to constrain the model generation process. The proposed framework has broad applications in different areas, including image modeling, scene understanding, and object recognition.

11202320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202320.value: Three-dimensional point clouds (3DPCs), which consist of a set of 3D coordinates indicating the spatial locations of points to represent the geometric structures of real objects/scenes explicitly, are becoming popular in various emerging applications owing to their flexibility and computational-efficiency. Additionally, the recent advancements of 3D sensing technology make 3D acquisition relatively easy. In spite of its popularity, some fundamental issues still exist, diminishing the use of such data modality. First, it is still costly and time-consuming to acquire high-fidelity dynamic 3DPCs, i.e., a sequence of 3DPCs densely-sampled in both spatial and temporal domains for simultaneously capturing geometric details of objects/scenes and their temporal changes. Instead of relying on better hardware configurations, we will investigate a novel learning-based framework, which is capable of reconstructing such high-fidelity geometry data from a hybrid input, including a static dense 3DPC and a dynamic sparse one. Being aware of the essential difference between 2D image and 3D geometry data as well as the challenges posed by the irregular structure of 3DPCs, we will develop a deep learning framework with novel modules from the perspective of discrete differential geometry to explore and leverage the advantages of the hybrid input in complementary and parallel manners. Second, the associated algorithms for processing such emerging data modality have not been well established. Particularly, as a fundamental theory, sparse representation has been popular and proven to be advantageous in 2D image processing. Unfortunately, the irregular structure of 3DPCs challenges the straightforward extension of existing techniques. In this project, by making full use of the unique permutation-invariant characteristic of such data, we will study novel learning-based permutation-driven approaches for sparsely representing 3DPCs. Besides 3DPCs, the proposed methods are applicable to general high-dimensional, unstructured signals. With our solid backgrounds and promising preliminary verifications achieved, it is highly expected that our investigations will provide effective solutions for rapid and affordable acquisition of high-fidelity dynamic 3DPCs as well as elegant algorithms for processing 3DPCs, which will significantly advance the 3D acquisition field and be beneficial to 3DPC-based applications, included but not limited to effective data transmission for immersive 3D telepresence, accurate object recognition for autonomous driving, visually pleasing perception for virtual/augmented reality, and efficient documentation of culture heritage sites. We believe that beyond the three-year period envisioned for this work, the scientific findings of this project will continuously motivate the research on irregular high-dimensional signal modeling and be applied to real-world applications. 三維點雲是由一系列點在三維空間中的坐標所構成，能夠表示真實物體/場景的幾何結構。三維點雲的數據結構具有靈活性與高計算效率的特性，並且隨著三維傳感技術的提升，三維點雲數據的採集越來越容易。儘管三維點雲很受歡迎並在很多新興應用中嶄露頭角，但仍然存在一些基本問題亟待解決，來加快該數據的廣泛應用。 首先，獲得高精度的動態三維點雲仍然是高成本且耗時的。動態三維點雲是同時記錄了空間與時間信息的點雲序列，能夠表示物體/場景的幾何特性及其時間變化。不同於依賴更高精度的硬件傳感設備，我們計劃研究全新的深度學習方法，該方法能從稠密的靜態點雲與稀疏的動態點雲的混合輸入重構高精度的動態三維點雲。由於非規則排列的三維幾何數據與二維圖像數據有著本質區別，我們將從離散微分幾何的角度出發以開發深度學習方法，我們將提出新穎的模塊以互補和並行的方式以充分利用混合輸入。 其次，針對此新興數據的處理算法並不完善。由於三維點雲的非規則性，在二維圖像上已經成熟並應用頗廣的稀疏表示並不能直接拓展到點雲數據上。在此項目中，我們將充分利用點雲的排序不變性來研究新穎的基於深度學習的排序驅動以實現三維點雲的稀疏表示。我們提出的算法也可適用於三維點雲之外的其他非結構性高維信號。 通過初步的驗證分析以及紮實的專業知識背景，我們的工作有很大可能獲得有效的解決方案，即快速且低廉的三維高精度點雲序列生成算法與三維點雲處理算法。這些算法能夠幫助點雲採集，更能應用於一系列基於三維點雲的實際應用，如沉浸式三維成像中高效點雲數據傳輸，自動駕駛中更精確的物體識別，虛擬現實/增強現實中的高質量視覺體驗,高效的遺跡檔案管理等。該項目成果也將啟發其他關於非規則高維度信號的研究工作。

11202320.label: Realisation of objectives
11202320.value: Objective 1: Motivated by the intuition that one can transform two aligned point clouds to each other more easily and meaningfully than a misaligned pair, we proposed to learn the correspondence between 3D shapes by means of deformation-like reconstruction to overcome the need for annotated data. Then, we designed an end-to-end learning pipeline consisting of a deep feature embedding module and two novel modules called correspondence indicator and symmetric deformer. Feeding a pair of raw point clouds, we first learned the pointwise features and passed them into the indicator to generate a learnable correspondence matrix used to permute the input pair. The symmetric deformer, with an additional regularized loss, transformed the two permuted point clouds to each other to drive the unsupervised learning of the correspondence. Objective 2: To reconstruct dense 3D point clouds with more geometric details from 3D sparse point clouds, we incorporated discrete differential geometry into deep learning elegantly by learning the first and second fundamental forms that are able to represent the local geometry unique up to rigid motion fully. Based on the linear approximation theorem, we first formulated the problem as the determination of the interpolation weights and high-order approximation errors. In addition, we adopted the generative adversarial network that can make the upsampled points evenly distributed on the underlying surface and efficiently generate clean high-frequency regions. Finally, we incorporated normalizing flows and weight prediction techniques to produce dense points uniformly distributed on the underlying surface. Objective 3: We formulated the problem of temporally interpolating dynamic 3D point cloud sequences with large non-rigid deformation as an estimation of pointwise trajectories (i.e., smooth curves) and further reasoned that temporal irregularity and under-sampling are two major challenges. Then, we proposed a temporal consistency learning module to align two consecutive point cloud frames point-wisely, based on which we can employ linear interpolation to obtain coarse trajectories/in-between frames. To compensate for the high-order nonlinear components of trajectories, we applied aligned feature embeddings that encode local geometry properties to regress pointwise increments, which are combined with the coarse estimations. Objective 4: Considering that the quality of the reconstructed 3D point cloud depends on both the geometry and color distortions, we explored the optimal allocation of the total bitrate between the geometry coder and the color coder to optimize point cloud data compression. We also explored the construction of perceptual quality assessment metrics for 3D point cloud data, which can be further used to guide the compression process. In addition, we explored new sparse transformation techniques to improve compression performance. Objective 5: We explored the task-oriented sparse representation of 3D point clouds (i.e., the performance of subsequent applications applied to resulting sparse point clouds should be maintained as much as possible) from the perspective of matrix optimization. To tackle the challenges posed by the discrete and combinatorial nature of the sampling matrix, we relaxed the binary constraint of the sampling matrix and formulated a constrained and differentiable optimization problem. We then designed a deep neural network to mimic the matrix optimization by exploring both the local and global structures of the input data. We also formulated the problem as a Top-k operation and designed a contribution-based sampling network, where we used a differentiable approximation to the Top-k operation via entropy regularization of an optimal transport problem to ensure that the network can be trained in an end-to-end way using gradient descent algorithms. Objective 6: We first explored only utilizing 2D images of the complete objects as supervision, which are easier to capture than complete and clean 3D point clouds. To take advantage of the complementary information from 2D images, we used a single-view RGB image to extract 2D features and designed a fusion module to fuse the 2D and 3D features extracted from the partial point cloud. To guide the shape of predicted point clouds, we projected the predicted points of the object to the 2D plane and used the foreground pixels of its silhouette maps to constrain the position of the projected points. Then, we explored the 3D point cloud completion method that can be well generalized to unseen categories. Specifically, we constructed a prior bank consisting of representative shapes from the seen categories and then designed a multi-scale pattern correlation module to learn. In addition, we explored the 3D point cloud completion problem by leveraging both region-level and category-specific geometric similarities to complete missing structures. In addition to the six objectives listed in the proposal, we also explored the generation of 3D point clouds using GAN and the long-standing and challenging problem of continuous surface reconstruction from sparse 3D point clouds by learning the unsigned distance field.

11202320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202320.value: Objective 1: We proposed CorrNet3D [Zeng et al. CVPR’21], the first unsupervised and end-to-end deep learning-based framework to learn the dense correspondence between 3D shapes. Objective 2: We proposed a series of 3D point cloud upsampling algorithms, including PUGeo-Net [Qian et al, ECCV’20], MFU-Net [Qian et al., TIP’21], PUFA-GAN [Liu et al. TIP’22], and PU-Flow [Mao et al., TVCG’23]. Objective 3: We proposed IDEANet [Zeng et al. CVPR’22], an end-to-end deep learning framework, to reconstruct temporally dense dynamic 3D point cloud sequences from temporally sparse ones with large non-rigid deformation. Objective 4: We proposed a series of algorithms for 3D point cloud compression, including a compression framework for color information [Liu et al., TCSVT’21], a bit allocation algorithm between geometry and color information [Liu et al, TMM’21], a rate control algorithm guided by a reduced reference perceptual quality model [Liu et al., TIP’21], no reference quality assessment metric [Liu et al. TCSVT’21], a regular representation-based compression paradigm [Zhang et al. IJCV’2022], and a rendering-oriented compression framework [TCSVT, under review]. Objective 5: We proposed task-oriented point cloud downsampling/simplification methods, namely MOPS-Net [Qian et al., TCSVT’23] and CS-Net [TVCG, under review]. Objective 6: We proposed a series of learning-based 3D point cloud completion methods, including [Wu et al. TMM’23], [Wu et al., TVCG’24], and [TVCG, under review]. Beyond the four objectives listed in the proposal, we proposed WarpingGAN [Tang et al. CVPR’22], an effective and efficient 3D point cloud generation network from latent codes. We also proposed a learning-based surface reconstruction method from sparse 3D point clouds, namely GeoUDF [Ren et al. ICCV’23].

11202320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202320.value: The research and proposed course of action can be significantly advanced by exploring the following three promising directions: 1. Leveraging the extraordinary capabilities of pre-trained large foundation models to elevate the quality of low-fidelity 3D geometry data. 2. Exploring efficient yet effective learning mechanisms to manage the irregular and unstructured nature of 3D geometric data. 3. Exploring robust diffusion-based generative frameworks to create high-fidelity 3D geometric data from textual inputs, images, or other modalities.

11202320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202320.value: In this project, we have created advanced techniques to improve low-quality 3D point clouds. These methods enhance details by adding more points, fill in missing parts, and smoothly connect different frames in dynamic sequences. We have also devised ways to compress and simplify point clouds for more efficient storage and transmission. These innovations promise faster, easier, and cost-effective ways to capture, store, and transmit 3D data, benefiting applications like immersive 3D telepresence, autonomous driving, and heritage preservation. Our work also inspires further research in modeling irregular high-dimensional signals.
