11203120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203120.value: The goal of this project is to develop basic theory of networked control aiming at its practical application. Networked control, with today’s omnipresent and ever-expanding IT technology and infrastructure, is widely believed to be a key enabling and transformative technology for the next-generation engineering systems. Notable applications include, e.g., industrial control systems, manufacturing systems, intelligent transportation, distributed sensor networks, and more broadly, cyber physical systems and Internet of Things. Networked control systems differ from conventional feedback systems, in which communication noises and transmission losses usher in new challenges. This project targets a fundamental limitation with the current model and theory of networked control, that is, the communication channel noises must be independent or uncorrelated. This restriction limits severely its applicability; indeed, it poses a central obstacle for real-world applications, to, e.g., industrial control systems. We aim to develop a theoretical as well as a computational framework that focuses on networked systems with communication channels subject to correlated noises and transmission losses, which encompass a wide range of channel models and will be tackled as correlated stochastic multiplicative uncertainties. Central to our investigation are a set of synergistic objectives unified under this framework, including (1) developing a generalized mean-square small gain theorem capable of coping with correlated stochastic uncertainties; (2) developing mean-square stabilization conditions and optimal control methods under the generalized mean-square framework; (3) developing mean-square stability and stabilization conditions for systems containing random communication delays, and computational algorithms and analytical bounds for random jitter control. Throughout the execution of this project, the benchmark Tennessee Eastman process will be employed to guide and validate the theoretical development. A coherent technical approach has been carved out to achieve the objectives, which is centered at the generalized mean-square small gain framework built on the correlated stochastic multiplicative uncertainty formulation. The framework attempts to overcome some of the existing limitations and restrictions, by presenting a considerably more realistic-in fact a generic-networked control model, and by developing theoretical results and computational algorithms to facilitate the practical applications of the networked control theory. The project is motivated by real-world industrial control systems, and it seeks to provide answers and solutions to the challenges for realistic applications to such systems. We hold the viewpoint that the understanding generated from this project will contribute significantly to the advance and application of the networked control theory, and more broadly, shed light into related fields such as cyber physical systems. 本項目旨在對網絡控制的實際應用开展基础理論研究。基于当今无所不在且日益扩展的信息技术和基礎架構，網絡控制被广泛认为是下一代工程系統的關鍵使能和變革性技術，其應用包括工業控制系統，製造系統，智能交通，分佈式傳感器網絡，以及更廣泛意义上的網絡物理系統和物聯網。網絡控制系統不同於傳統的反饋系統，乃在于其中的通信噪聲和傳輸損耗帶來了新的挑戰。本項目針對通信通道噪聲必須獨立或不相關这一當前網絡控制模型和理論的基本局限展开研究。該局限嚴重限制了网络控制的適用性，也是實際应用中--例如工業系統的控制—面临的主要障礙。本项目针对具有相關噪聲和傳輸損耗的廣泛的信道模型，通过相關的隨機乘性不確定因子描述，试图发展相应的網絡控制理論和計算框架。我們的研究重點是在此框架下紧密相关且有机統一的一組目標，包括：（1）建立能夠應對相關隨機不確定性的廣義均方小增益定理； （2）在廣義均方框架下建立均方穩定條件和最優控制方法； （3）為包含隨機通讯延遲的系統发展均方穩定和镇定條件，及为含有jitter的系统发展計算算法和解析邊界。項目執行過程中，將使用田納西伊士曼这一规范流程來指導和驗證理論發展。為實現這些目標，我们提出基於相關隨機乘性不確定因子的廣義均方小增益框架为中心的统一技術路线，以此跨越现有工作的局限和约束，发展更具现實意义的理论结果和计算算法，从而促進網絡控制理論的實際應用。項目受現實世界中工業控制系統的启发，旨在為应用于此類系統的实际问题提供解答。我們認為，通过研究該項目，我们獲得的理解將大大有助於網絡控制理論的發展和應用，並且对更廣泛的諸如網絡物理系統之類的相關領域有启发之效。

11203120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203120.value: This project is rather successful. All three objectives are completed, and in fact, are much further beyond. The project has resulted in the publication of 9 journal papers (with 6 in the top archive journals IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Automatica, SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization). In accomplishing the proposed objectives, we conducted research activities in a number of synergistic areas, with the following selected highlights exemplifying our results. Strictly adhering to the objectives, we have developed a general mean-square stability analysis framework to address correlated structured stochastic uncertainties, which may arise from multiple sources or from multiple communication channels. This consists in the development of a new mean-square robust stability measure termed the mean-square stability radius, and a general mean-square small gain theorem. Along with the developments we obtained fundamental necessary and sufficient conditions of mean-square stability, which ensure that a system can maintain stability under the mean-square criterion. With the mean-square small gain theorem developed, we studied the mean-square stabilization and performance problems within the aforementioned framework. We discovered the fundamental variance bounds on the structured stochastic uncertainties required to stabilize a system. Furthermore, we established an intrinsic connection between optimal mean-square performance problems and mean-square stabilization problems, thus providing a systematic tool in tackling mean-square performance problems. We also studied stability properties of linear systems subject to random delays. We addressed several typical classes of random delays, and for each class, we obtained small-gain type mean-square stability conditions. The results allow us to ascertain whether a system’s state variance matrix converges asymptotically to the zero matrix under the effect of random delays. The works alluded to above are reported in Research Output [3,7,8,9]. Equally worth noting, the project has led to the expansion and outgrowth into the investigation of networked multi-agent systems, an area of close relevance to the core objectives. The research endeavor concerns the consensus attainment of networked agents under the effect of communication delays. We examined first- and second-order agents, and developed estimates on the largest range of time delays allowable in order to achieve consensus, known as the delay consensus margin, which are considered significant advances in the research areas. Together with this effort, we placed emphasis on PID controllers, which, as widely known, are the most popular control strategies used in industrial systems and networks, accounting for over 90% industrial control applications. These results are reported in Research Output [1,2,4,5,6].

11203120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203120.value: The project has also shown the potential for extension to estimation problems under the influence of networked noises and uncertainties, with our preliminary success reported in Research Output [8], where we investigated an optimal estimation problem over lossy communication networks subject to multi-channel packet losses. The problem is to employ a modified Kalman filter to estimate the system’s states, and the primary issue under study is the convergence of the state estimate under a mean-square criterion. This convergence is shown to be equivalent to the existence of a stabilizing solution to a modified algebraic Riccati equation. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition to characterize the existence of the stabilizing solution, and show that the solution can be computed by solving a set of linear matrix inequalities. From a robust convergence perspective, however, it would be of significant interest to consider communication losses whose probabilities are unknown and uncertain. The well-known denial of service (DoS) attacks belong to this category, which have been found prevalent in cyber-physical systems. The current work can be employed as a launching pad toward the investigation of such cyber attacks.

11203120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203120.value: Networked control has been widely regarded as a key enabling and transformative technology for the next-generation engineering systems. Notable applications of the networked control theory include, e.g., industrial control systems, manufacturing systems, intelligent transportation, distributed sensor networks, and more broadly, cyber physical systems and Internet of Things (IoT). For a wide range of networked control systems and applications, communication constraints and transmission losses can be modeled by stochastic multiplicative uncertainties. This project targets a fundamental limitation with the current model and theory of networked control, and it seeks to develop a theoretical as well as a computational framework that focuses on networked systems with communication channels subject to correlated noises and transmission losses. The project developed a general mean-square stability analysis framework consisting of a mean-square robust stability measure called the mean-square stability radius, and a general mean-square small gain theorem. We also obtained fundamental necessary and sufficient conditions of mean-square stability, and algorithms for optimal estimation over lossy communication networks. The results obtained will lend insights to the theoretical and applied research of networked control, and have the promise to provide tools for practical applications to real-world industrial networked control systems.

11203220.label: Project Objectives
11203220.value: Propose a highly conceptual and extremely compact representation scheme for visual sensor data by leveraging the front-end intelligent analysis and inference in IoVTs. The scheme is essentially built upon the distinguished characteristics of visual sensor data, which provide us abundant opportunities to further improve the representation capability. Within this scheme, the visual data can be naturally traced, identified, inferred and reconstructed through four embedded analytics modules deployed at the front-end. As such, the proposed scheme is expected to significantly improve the representation capability of visual sensor data from IoVTs by tracing the origin, identifying the data utility, removing the intrinsic redundancies and improving the ultimate user experience. Develop a representation-in-loop visual data tracing scheme against the uncontrolled physical acquisition environment. In this research, we plan to adopt the adverse weather (e.g., fog and rain) as a concrete instance due to the all-weather data collected from sensors. Through the theoretical analysis, the haze and rain which typically influence the representation capability are highly correlated with not only the quality but also the representation data rate. As such, the representation-in-loop tracing scheme with data-driven optimization has great potentials to explore the path towards the optimal representation element in the generalized rate-distortion space. Develop the utility-oriented resource allocation scheme to optimize the whole IoVT networking and storage infrastructure. The utility is modeled with the non-linear combination of intrinsic scene statistics as well as allocated resources, which could be further organized to drive the optimal resource allocation at multiple granularities (e.g., sensor, video, frame), such that the overall representation capability can be significantly boosted by unlocking the data value. Develop an efficient compact representation method that naturally incorporates the data-driven based inference into the signal-level compression. The background is inferred by leveraging the reinforcement learning to automatically learn the behaviors in the optimal representation sense. The foreground is inferred by imposing the deterministic and statistical constraints to ensure the representation fidelity as well as naturalness. The proposed method is expected to greatly improve rate-distortion performance by removing intrinsic redundancies. Propose an unsupervised deep reconstruction scheme that is specifically designed based on the characteristics of IoVT data, as in this scenario it is difficult to acquire strictly paired source/ground truth for fully supervised model training. Such observations promote us to explore the utilization of unpaired data for intelligent reconstruction in an unsupervised manner. The attention mechanism including the spatial self-attention module and statistic-based channel attention module are incorporated, in an effort to improve the quality at different granularities.

11203220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203220.value: Recent years have witnessed a tremendous amount of visual sensors deployed in ambient environments, which have greatly powered the internet-of-things with the advent of powerful 5G wireless networks. The astronomical amount of internet of video things (IoVT) pose great challenges to the storage, transmission, and utilization of visual sensor data around the internet. Despite demonstrated success in video coding and processing, in this project, we demonstrate that the representation capability of IoVT sensor data can be largely extended by exploiting the front-end intelligent sensing with enhanced embedded video analytics capabilities, and more importantly, the subsequent video data utilization pipeline can greatly benefit from such representation paradigm. Generally speaking, there are three distinguished properties of IoVT sensor data 1) the data are acquired in an uncontrolled physical environment without sophisticated equipment and elaborate acquisition preparations; 2) the data are featured with high volume and low-value density, instead of being entirely valuable with high utility; 3) the data possess underlying regularities, as they are generated without human intervention instead of being carefully processed and edited. As such, we propose a new scheme based on intelligent sensing at the front-end, in an effort to provide highly conceptual and extremely compact representation with the consideration of these characteristics. The pipeline is composed of four modules, including visual data tracing with representation-in-loop, utility-oriented resource allocation and data-driven based inference at the encoder side, as well as unsupervised deep reconstruction in an effort to better reform the visual data at the decoder side. The application scope of the proposed research is much broader than data compression. The distribution of analytics and inference modules at the front-end can greatly shrink the data volume such that only the valuable data are concentrated on, which could optimize the whole sensing and networking infrastructures in terms of data volume, transmission latency, energy efficiency, etc. Moreover, the proposed scheme can also benefit video storage and transmission by exploiting external redundancies across different sensors. With the design of algorithms based on multidisciplinary approaches and promising preliminary verifications, we are confident that the proposed scheme can achieve a very compact representation of the all-weather, all-time, all-coverage mega-scale visual sensor data. More importantly, beyond data representation, the proposed scheme can also contribute to the technology innovations of front-end smart visual sensing, which will play more and more critical roles in numerous personal-scale and industrial-scale applications. 近年來，大量的視覺傳感器部署在周圍環境中。隨著5G網絡的商用，視覺傳感數據極大地推動了物聯網的發展。大規模視頻物聯網傳感器對互聯網中視覺數據的存儲，傳輸和利用提出了巨大的挑戰。在本項目中，我們旨在通過利用智能前端大幅度地提高視頻物聯網傳感器數據的表示能力，更重要的是，後續的視頻數據的應用可以從這種表示範例中受益匪淺。一般而言，視頻物聯網的傳感器數據有三個顯著的特徵：1)數據采集於不受控制的物理環境中，無法利用複雜的設備及提供精心的採集準備；2)數據具有高容量和低值密度的特點，并非完全具有實用價值；3)數據具有潜在的規律性，源於它們是在沒有人工干預的情況下生成的，并未經過仔細地處理和編輯。因此，我們提出了一種基於前端智能傳感的新方案，旨在通過考慮這些特徵來提供高度概念化和極其緊湊的表示。該方案由四個模塊組成，包括具有環內表示能力的可視數據復原，面向可用度的資源分配，基於數據驅動的編碼端推理，以及無監督的深度重構，從而更好地在解碼器端重塑可視數據。本研究的應用範圍較之數據壓縮要廣泛得多。分佈于前端的分析和推理模塊能夠極大地縮小數據量，僅集中有價值的數據，從而在數據量、傳輸延遲、能源效率等方面優化整個傳感和網絡基礎架構。此外，所提出的方案還可利用不同傳感器之間的外部冗餘來實現視頻存儲和傳輸。通過基於跨領域的算法設計和初步驗證，我們相信所提出的方案能夠實現對全天候，全時，全覆蓋的大規模視覺傳感器數據的非常緊湊的表示。更重要的是，除了數據表示之外，所提出的方案還可促進前端智能視覺傳感的技術創新，這將在眾多個人和工業規模的應用中扮演著舉足輕重的角色。

11203820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203820.value: Along with the development of display technique, high dynamic range (HDR) has become a “must-have” TV feature, which can provide a user experience clearly distinguishable from existing HDTV. HDR video represents scenes by increasing the bit depth to show pictures into a wider range of tones, which make HDR videos more vibrant and provide users immersive experience. According to HIS Markit report, shipments in the USA of consumer TV sets supporting HDR picture enhancements are more than 4 million units in 2016, and this number will increase to 30 million units by 2020. On the other hand, there are very few HDR content and most of existing video content are still compressed SDR videos. To provide more HDR content, signal processing technique for HDR creation is demanded to convert SDR video to HDR version by expanding their tone. Different from the popular HDR imaging by fusing multiple exposures, there are mainly three challenges in HDR video creation from SDR video. First, there are not multiple exposures, since existing videos have been captured without considering HDR problem at that time. Second, the SDR videos have been compressed for transmission and storage, which have been contaminated by compression artifacts. These artifacts are easily enhanced during SDR to HDR conversion. Finally, it is also a difficult problem to evaluate the quality of HDR video. In this project, we aim to solve the above challenges from the fundamental quality assessment problem. In general, there are two factors in evaluating the quality of converted HDR video, i.e., HVS preference and style preservation. In the first stage, we plan to construct two HDR VQA datasets to explore these two factors via subjective experiments. Second, we will utilize a multi-model network framework to improve quality assessment by leveraging adaptive perceptual uniform transform and unsupervised HDR classification network. For style preservation, we will design a tone mapping network and a style translation network as feature extractors to measure the cross-domain similarity. Finally, a weakly supervised method for SDR-to-HDR conversion task to avoid the requirement of strict SDR-HDR video pairs during training stage, and also explore the conversion by utilizing a generative adversarial network (GAN) to enhance the contrast of input video and suppress compression artifacts jointly. Moreover, a coarse-to-fine framework is used to enhance video contrast by utilizing the proposed HDR VQA model. 最近，對超高清（UHD）視頻服務的需求不斷增長。 UHD視頻提供大量數據的逼真的觀看體驗，正在徹底改變視頻生態系統並推動信息產業的升級。在這種背景下，超高清視頻大數據的指數增長與有限的存儲空間以及傳輸帶寬之間的矛盾日益突出。面對這些挑戰，來自ITU-T和MPEG的視頻專家聯合團隊已經啟動了下一代視頻編碼標準多功能視頻編碼（VVC）項目。在VVC中，採用了新的編碼結構和一組編碼工具，與以前的HEVC標準相比，它們大大提高了編碼性能。隨著標準化進程的發展，研究編碼器優化算法顯得尤為重要和迫切，這不僅有利於將來VVC標準的實施和部署，而且為標準化進程提供了有益的信息和指導。 在這個項目中，我們將利用人工智能技術，從高效速率控制和低複雜度編碼的角度系統地研究VVC編碼器的優化。特別是，我們首先研究VVC中UHD視頻的速率失真特性，以規範編碼比特率。更具體地，利用結合了四叉樹-二叉樹和三叉樹劃分的新編碼結構來研究速率量化和失真量化關係，並且基於增強學習的最新發展實現了智能速率控制。這樣，優化了每個幀和CTU的編碼位數，以實現高效率速率控制。此外，我們將速率失真模型擴展到VVC編解碼器的聯合速率失真複雜度（RDC）優化，目的是在低失真編碼的速率失真性能和編碼複雜度之間取得良好的平衡。特別是，通過使用高級機器學習技術對它們之間的關係進行建模，可以在復雜性受限的情況下確定編碼器結構。此外，可以通過複雜度分配策略進一步優化編碼模式的決策。通過對本地RDC關係進行智能建模，可以為每個編碼單元優化複雜度分配，以實現整體最佳編碼性能。預計該研究結果將被基於UHD視頻的各種應用所採用，包括視頻監視，數字電視廣播，IPTV，視頻通信和Internet視頻。

11203820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203820.value: In recent years, High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) images have gained widespread popularity across various domains such as security, multimedia, and biomedical fields due to their ability to deliver an authentic visual experience. However, the extensive dynamic range and rich detail in HDR images present challenges in assessing their quality. Consequently, current efforts focus on constructing subjective databases and proposing objective quality assessment metrics to achieve efficient HDR Image Quality Assessment (IQA). This paper addresses the lack of a systematic overview of these approaches by providing a comprehensive survey of both subjective and objective HDR IQA methods. Specifically, it reviews seven subjective HDR IQA databases and twelve objective HDR IQA metrics, and conducts a statistical analysis of nine IQA algorithms, incorporating three perceptual mapping functions. The findings highlight two main areas for improvement: the size and diversity of HDR IQA subjective databases need significant expansion to encompass a broader range of distortion types, and objective quality assessment algorithms must identify more generalizable perceptual mapping approaches and feature extraction methods to enhance robustness and applicability. This paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers by discussing the limitations of current methodologies and potential future research directions. Additionally, this study aims to develop advanced and training-free full-reference image quality assessment (FR-IQA) models based on deep neural networks. It investigates measures that allow perceptual comparison of deep network features and reveals their underlying factors. The study finds that distribution measures exhibit advanced perceptual awareness and tests the Wasserstein distance (WSD), Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), and symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence (SKLD) measures when comparing deep features acquired from various pretrained deep networks, including the Visual Geometry Group (VGG) network, SqueezeNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet. The proposed FR-IQA models demonstrate superior alignment with subjective human evaluations across diverse IQA datasets without requiring training, showcasing the advanced perceptual relevance of distribution measures when comparing deep network features. Additionally, the study explores the applicability of deep distribution measures in image super-resolution enhancement tasks, highlighting their potential for guiding perceptual enhancements.

11203920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203920.value: Increasing life expectancy and reduced mortality are leading to significant growth of the aging population in Hong Kong (HK). The proportion of elderly residents is projected to rise further from 17.7% in 2019 to 26.5% in 2031. To tackle this problem of rapid aging, the HK government re-confirm to enact the ‘aging in place’ policy in 2011 and ‘long-term care’ policy in 2012 (HK Housing Society 2019). Care and Attention (C&A) homes, therefore, accommodate the elderly in the same place even if their health deteriorates. However, most people have experienced change in their vision by the age of 50. 174,800 persons have difficulty seeing resulting from age-related impairment and eye diseases (Census & Statistics Dept 2015), which significantly affects their independence in daily life. Although the government provided additional subsidies to non-governmental organizations for the special needs of elderly, the funding was mainly used to improve manpower rather than the facilities in homes. Indeed, inappropriate luminous environment reduces elderly vision-relevant Quality of Life (vQoL), leading to health and safety problems. Physical living environment is a recognized dimension of vQoL (World Health Organization QoL Assessment [WHOQOL] Group 1998), and is likely to be particularly important for persons living in residential care. Due to visual impairment, many older people spend most of their time at home and rely on luminous facilities management (LFM) to compensate for their physiological health problems and also to maintain their psychological well-being. However, the latest official Code of Practice Residential Care Homes (Elderly Persons) in HK (2013) still only mentions ‘adequate’ artificial lighting required in homes without providing any specific lighting guideline. There is extensive literature on lighting, FM, caring environmental design, post-occupancy evaluation (POE), visual issues, and QoL for adults in general and elders in particular, but little research integrates all these aspects in C&A homes for the elderly. The purpose of this study is to enhance the vQoL of elders in C&A homes through LFM. Its objectives are: (1) to factorize LFM components in C&A homes and vQoL indicators for elders; (2) to establish LFM–vQoL relationships; (3) to develop an integrated LFM–vQoL model; (4) to verify the model using longitudinal data; and (5) to propose LFM guidelines for enhancing vQoL for elderly residents in C&A homes. The findings will promote the development of a proactive holistic assessment of LFM in C&A homes, and enhance the vQoL of elderly residents in C&A homes. 11203920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203920.value: Three main topics have been revealed in this study. 1. Luminous Environment (LE) - Quality of Life (QoL) of Older People Model We objectively assessed the situation of the LE in C&A homes, as well as recorded the subjective LE and satisfaction of QoL of older people. The analysis found that lighting control is associated with physical health while lighting that renders color and the lack of ELC is positively associated with independence. The spatial luminance distribution, natural light and navigation lighting impacts psychological health, and basic activities of daily living is positively related to navigation in the room, light level for work and natural light, and negatively impacted by no ELC. 2. Indoor Visual Environment (IVE) - Visual-related Physical Health Model for Older People Older people with declined visual ability have high requirements of the IVE (i.e., opening design, interior design, and lighting conditions) to maintain their visual-related physical health (i.e., general vision, func­tional vision, visual acuity, physical discomfort, and injuries). An integrated IVE-physical health model for older people living in RCHs was established. The model indicated that the view out, window, corridor, furniture locations, curtain or louver, handrail, and light level signifi­cantly impacted the visual-related physical health of older people. 3. Indoor Visual Environment (IVE) - Emotional & Behavioral Symptoms (EBS) Model for Older People with Dementia The EBS in older people with dementia (e.g., emotion disorders, environmental adaption problems, sleep disorders, limited mobility, etc.) can cause difficulties in their daily life in C&A homes. The IVE could relieve or aggravate the EBS, thus influencing their life in C&A homes. The research has explored the impact of the IVE on the EBS in older people with mild to moderate dementia to improve the IVE in C&A homes and satisfy the special requirements of older persons with dementia. An IVE–EBS model was established using various statistical analysis methods. The model uncovered that the space, view out, window, furniture, door, and color significantly impact the EBS in older persons with dementia. The scripts from the staff members were used to further explain the interactions between the IVE and the EBS in people with dementia.

11203920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203920.value: This research focused on older persons residing in C&A homes. The IVE in their own home varies greatly from the C&A homes. In future research, the effects of IVE in Public or Private residential buildings on older people could also be studied. The participants in this study involve with and without dementia (mild or moderate). Older people with different stages of dementia manifested different EBS. In the future study, older people with mild, moderate, or severe dementia could be studied separately. The age, gender, degree of blindness, and eye diseases of older people may also influence relationships between the IVE and their visual-related physical health as moderators. Hence, the moderating effects of those characteristics of older people could be studies in the future. The specific impact of lighting control and the impact of ELC on the quality of life of older people could also be further investigated by qualitative data measurement on site. Other indoor environments, such as acoustic environment, thermal environment, and air environment, may also influence the EBS of older people. This study specifically concentrated on how the visual space, interior design, and lighting conditions affect the older people. Hence, the potential effects of other environmental factors, such as sounds, temperature, and air quality, could also be investigated in the future

11203920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203920.value: The luminous environment (LE) impacts significantly on the Quality of Life (QoL) of residents of Care and Attention (C&A) homes through multiple channels. Data was collected through on-site observations, questionnaire survey and interview in purposively-selected C&A homes. The observed C&A homes performed well in the spatial luminance distribution in the dining rooms and the corridors and natural light in the bedrooms, but performed poorly in lighting control. The results show that psychological health can be positively predicted by spatial luminance distribution, lighting for navigation and natural light, that independence is impacted by color and no extreme luminance contrasts, that navigation lighting, natural light, and that light level for work positively influences basic activities of daily living. The somewhat more surprising positive correlation between physical health and lighting control, and negative correlation between basic activities of daily living with the lack of extreme luminance contrasts are explored, and reveal further insights regarding methodological refinements. On the other hand, the study also uncovered that the space, view out, window, furniture, door, and color significantly impact the emotional & behavioral symptoms in older persons with dementia. Further study in other topics such as acoustic, environment, & air environment are strongly recommended.

11204020.label: Project Objectives
11204020.value: Observational Studies of Offshore Wind Characteristics and Wind Energy Potential. Most observational studies of wind energy potential have been based on surface wind measurements, which are inevitably influenced by the nearby topography. Wind characteristics at the turbine hub heights have typically been generated by extrapolating the surface measurements using existing wind profile models, and yet the reliability of these models is questionable. The HKO has established a dense monitoring network across the territory, which comprises over 50 meteorological stations and 8 buoys. A large variety of measurement devices have been employed, including GPS dropsondes, radiosonde balloons, Light Detection and Ranging systems, Sonic Detection and Ranging systems, Doppler radar wind profilers and weather radars as well as anemometers, thermometers and barometers installed on meteorological masts and buoys, etc. These instruments can provide a full range of observations of various climate variables. Based on long-term (~30-year) observational records, a structured database with topographic effects removed will be established. The performance of several algorithms in calculating Weibull parameters and various statistical distribution models will be examined. Wind energy related parameters such as the operating probability, the wind power density, the annual energy production, and the capacity factor will be determined. Moreover, a comprehensive study of offshore wind characteristics and energy potential at heights up to 200 m will be conducted. The vertical variations of parameters such as wind speed and direction, turbulence intensity, and air density will be investigated, and the performance of different roughness estimation methods will be examined. 3-D Analysis of Offshore Wind Fields and Wind Energy Resources Using a NWP Model. Offshore wind characteristics and energy potential can only be investigated over small-scale areas based on observational records from sparsely distributed meteorological stations and buoys. However, offshore wind farm siting requires wind resource assessments over extensive offshore regions. Thus, 3-D high-resolution wind fields will be generated by a Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) model with data assimilation, which incorporates a wide variety of observations to improve the model accuracy. An extensive assessment of offshore wind energy resources will be conducted based on the 3-D wind fields. Spatiotemporal variations of wind energy related parameters will be examined, and the influences of special weather events and upwind topographic conditions will be investigated. Moreover, semi-empirical models to describe how the wind characteristics and energy potential vary with the distance to the coast will be developed. A multi-criteria wind farm siting procedure will be proposed, which will enable optimal wind farm locations to be recommended. Projection of Future Offshore Wind Energy Resources with Consideration of Climate Change Uncertainties. It is unclear how the offshore wind field patterns and wind energy resources in Hong Kong will change in response to climate change, nor the magnitude of the associated uncertainty. To investigate this, a statistical downscaling model to reproduce local wind fields based on large-scale climate variables from Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 5 General Circulation Models (CMIP5 GCMs) will be developed and validated, and then both historical and future wind speeds under climate change will be generated by downscaling CMIP5 GCMs. Moreover, the associated uncertainties, such as GCM physics, greenhouse gas emission trajectories, wind speed statistical distributions, statistical distribution parameters, air density, and wind speed profiles, will be identified, and uncertainty in future wind energy resources in a warming world will be quantified using the Monte Carlo method. Estimation of Typhoon Design Loads of Wind Turbines under Climate Change. To enable the safe design of wind turbines, it is essential to have knowledge of typhoon wind characteristics at turbine hub heights (80–200 m). However, it is unclear how climate change may affect typhoon extreme wind speeds. To explore this key issue, observational records during typhoons will be used to establish typhoon wind and turbulence profile models that span heights up to 200 m and incorporate wind speed and direction profiles, turbulence intensity profiles, gust factor and peak factor profiles, turbulence integral length scale profiles, and turbulence power spectra at various heights. Monte Carlo simulations will be conducted in conjunction with a synthetic typhoon model that combines the genesis, track, intensity and 3-D wind field model to simulate thousands of typhoons situated in the western North Pacific. In this manner, typhoon wind speeds corresponding to different return periods under climate change will be estimated in conjunction with GCM projections. The wind-wave joint distribution will also be investigated based on long-term observational wind and wave records. The results will enable the determination of the design loads of offshore wind turbines under typhoon conditions.

11204020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204020.value: Based on long-term (over 30-year) observational records, a structured wind speed and resource database has been established. The performance of different algorithms in calculating statistical distribution parameters for various distribution models, such as Weibull distribution, Kappa distribution, and Wakeby distribution, has been examined. Wind energy-related parameters, such as operating probability, wind power density, annual energy production, and capacity factor, have been determined. Furthermore, a comprehensive study of offshore wind characteristics and energy potential at heights up to 200 m has been conducted. The vertical variations of parameters such as wind speed and direction, turbulence intensity, and air density have been investigated, and the performance of different roughness estimation methods has been assessed. 3D high-resolution offshore wind fields have been generated using a numerical weather prediction (NWP) model with data assimilation, which has incorporated a wide variety of observations to improve model accuracy. An extensive assessment of offshore wind energy resources has been conducted based on the generated 3D wind fields. Spatiotemporal variations of wind energy-related parameters have been examined, and the influences of specific weather events and upwind topographic conditions have been investigated. A multi-criteria wind farm siting procedure has been proposed to recommend optimal locations for wind farms. A statistical downscaling model has been developed and validated to reproduce local wind fields based on large-scale climate variables from global climate models (GCMs). Both historical and future wind speeds under climate change have been generated by downscaling GCMs. Moreover, the associated uncertainties, such as those related to future climate scenarios, GCM choices, and wind speed statistical distributions, have been identified, and the uncertainty in future wind energy resources in a warming world has been quantified. Observational records during typhoons have been utilized to establish typhoon wind and turbulence profile models that span heights up to 200 m, including wind speed and direction profiles, turbulence intensity profiles, gust factor profiles, turbulence integral length scale profiles, and turbulence power spectra at various heights. Monte Carlo simulations have been conducted in conjunction with a full-track typhoon model that combines genesis, track, intensity, and 3D wind field models to simulate thousands of typhoons situated in the western North Pacific. Based on the full-track typhoon model and GCM projections, design wind speeds corresponding to different return periods under climate change have been estimated. The results have enabled the determination of design loads for offshore wind turbines under typhoon conditions.

11204020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204020.value: In the future, new field measurement instruments such as unmanned drones can be utilized. Unmanned drones are particularly effective for measuring winds in remote offshore regions and typhoon eyewalls, where conventional observations are rare or even impossible. In addition, machine learning-based methods can be developed to downscale the global climate models and improve their spatial and temporal resolutions. This will enable a higher-resolution assessment of wind resources under climate change.

11204020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204020.value: This project thoroughly investigated the wind characteristics and energy potential across the entire offshore region of Hong Kong considering climate change impacts. Offshore wind characteristics and wind energy potential have been comprehensively analyzed based on long-term, multi-platform observations from the Hong Kong Observatory. Three-dimensional maps of offshore wind fields and wind energy resources have been generated using numerical weather prediction models. Future offshore wind energy resources under climate change have been projected using global climate models and statistical downscaling approaches. Typhoon design wind speeds for offshore wind turbines under climate change have been estimated using a full-track typhoon model in conjunction with global climate models. The outcome of this project is expected to provide valuable data and guidelines for offshore wind farm development in Hong Kong, ultimately contributing to a low-carbon and sustainable future.

11204820.value: 太赫茲波指頻率在0.3-10THz範圍內的電磁波。該頻段由於包含眾多可用於識別不同分子的“指紋”吸收譜線，而在化學檢測和非接觸式成像上具有重要應用。據預測，全球太赫茲技術市場總量將以每年25%的速度增長，並在2024年達10億美元。 然而，太赫茲波段因恰處於電子技術和光子技術的常用頻率之間，難以使用這些成熟技術實現高效發生，因而常常被稱為“太赫茲鴻溝”。缺少高效和低成本的太赫茲源已經成為太赫茲技術走進我們日常生活的主要瓶頸。 本項目將研發一種基於納米光學耦合波導的高效和小型化太赫茲源，以解決這一瓶頸問題。該系統通過將兩束激光在光學非線性結構中高效混頻產生連續譜太赫茲波。由於光波與太赫茲波的波長相差一百倍，該方案的最大挑戰在於如何同時實現光波和太赫茲波的強束縛，同時最大化二者的模場重疊。該器件採用新型混合集成方案，由微米尺度的週期極化鈮酸鋰（PPLN）光波導和硅基的太赫茲波導組成。其中PPLN波導提供強光學束縛和准相位匹配的非線性相互作用，而硅波導給產生的太赫茲波提供低損耗的持續傳導通道。 項目負責人致力於集成鈮酸鋰光子學研究，此前已經研發了一系列薄膜鈮酸鋰非線性光學器件，包括超高轉換效率的PPLN二次諧波產生器件。為高效產生比光學頻率低兩個數量級的太赫茲波，本項目將在同一個光-太赫茲芯片上同時設計集成光學和太赫茲器件。器件的加工和測試將依靠城市大學先進的毫米波、光子學與微納加工基礎設施，以實現項目目標。 本項目的成功實施將實現一種芯片級、連續譜、可調頻和高效率的太赫茲源，可望應用於痕量化學物質檢測、醫學成像、安全監測和後5G通信系統，並推動香港和世界範圍內的學術研究和產業發展。

11204820.label: Realisation of objectives
11204820.value: Objective 1: Optimization of the coupled-waveguide structure for efficient THz generation (100%) We have successfully completed Objective 1 in the mid-term progress report by performing a systematic theoretical investigation of the proposed THz generator. The results were summarized as a journal paper and published in Optics Express [1] (Item 1 in Part C, Section 8). Our numerical simulation results show theoretical continuous-wave THz generation efficiencies as high as 3.5×10−4 W-1 at 3 THz with high tolerance to device fabrication variations, three orders of magnitude higher than current lithium-niobate-based devices. The results were later further expanded to include investigation of a coplanar-waveguide-based approach, and published as a conference paper in OSA Nonlinear Optics 2021 (Item 1 in Part C, Section 9). This approach was later used for the experimental realization of THz generation to be discussed next. The proposed coupled-waveguide THz generation scheme has been granted a US patent [11] (Item 1 in Part C, Section 11). Objective 2: Fabrication and characterization of high-quality thin-film PPLN waveguides (100%) We have developed a robust wafer-scale thin-film PPLN fabrication process for large-scale nonlinear photonic circuits. Specifically, we developed an ultraviolet stepper lithography process that can directly pattern the poling finger electrodes and photonic waveguides on 4-inch thin-film lithium niobate wafers. We have also built a customized poling setup that can perform automated poling process for more than 20 devices on each die, significantly improving the throughput and repeatability of wafer-scale poling. To address the inhomogeneous broadening of the quasi-phase matching (QPM) spectrum induced by film thickness variations across the wafer, we propose and demonstrate segmented thermal optic tuning modules that can precisely adjust and align the QPM peak wavelengths in each section. Using the segmented micro-heaters, we show the successful realignment of inhomogeneously broadened multi-peak QPM spectra with up to 57% enhancement of conversion efficiency. We achieve a high normalized conversion efficiency of 3800%/W-cm2 in a 6 mm long PPLN waveguide. The results were summarized as two published journal papers in APL Photonics [2-3] (Item 3&10 in Part C, Section 8). Objective 3: Integration of thin-film PPLN waveguides with Si THz waveguides (100%) & Objective 4: Characterization of the efficiency and noise performance of the THz source (100%) Through our theoretical investigations described in Objective 1 and initial device fabrication tests in the first half of this project, we have determined that the most feasible coupled optical-THz waveguide structure is to use a coplanar THz waveguide integrated with TFLN photonic waveguides on top of quartz substrate. Based on this optimal architecture, we have fabricated a THz photonic device that can perform both efficient THz generation and THz-optic modulation. The measured continuous-wave THz generation efficiency is 4.8*10-6 /W at 500 GHz, marking a tenfold improvement over existing tunable THz generation devices based on lithium niobate. Importantly, this coherent optical THz generation process allows us to naturally achieve high-speed electro-THz modulation using mature optical modulation techniques. We demonstrate high-speed modulation of THz signals at frequencies up to 35 GHz, promising for future THz communications, remote sensing, and spectroscopy applications. This result was summarized as a journal paper currently in revision at Nature Communications [4] (Item 7 in Part C, Section 8, initial decision letter attached in the PDF). Apart from THz generation, the TFLN nonlinear photonic platform developed in this project also shows promise for other extreme nonlinear optical processes such as high-harmonic generation. We demonstrated high-harmonic generation up to the 7th order with the shortest generated wavelength down to 226 nm. This result was published as a journal paper in Nanoscale [5] (Item 5 in Part C, Section 8). Objective 5: Investigation and optimization of the frequency tuning range of the THz source (100%) We have performed systematic theoretical and experimental investigations of the frequency tuning range of the proposed THz source, as summarized in Items 1&7 in Part C, Section 8. In particular, the measured THz generation signals can be continuously tuned from 0.22 to 0.5 THz, with consistent conversion efficiency and noise performance over this broad tuning range. The excellent single-wavelength emission ability and broadband tunability are direct results of our proposed continuous-wave THz generation scheme, which significantly differs from traditional THz generation schemes based on nonlinear crystals that often require pulsed lasers with high instantaneous powers. It also allows high-speed electro-THz modulation by simply modulating one of the two input lasers using mature optical modulation techniques. In addition, the platform developed in this project that features strong bidirectional THz-photonic interactions has become a crucial infrastructure for the development of various high-performance millimeter-wave and THz photonic devices. These demonstrations include an integrated lithium niobate microwave photonic processing engine that can perform multi-functional analog signal processing tasks at ultrahigh speed (67 GHz analog bandwidth, Nature) [6], the first integrated photonic radar that can operate in the millimeter-wave band (Nature Photonics) [7], ultrabroadband and high-linearity electro-optic modulators [8-9], as well as broadband waveguide-integrated two-dimensional material photodetectors in TFLN platform [10]. 11204820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204820.value: 1. We have proposed a novel device architecture for efficient THz wave generation in the continuous-wave regime with significantly improved efficiency over past demonstrations. (Item 1 in Part C, Section 8). 2. We have developed reliable wafer-scale fabrication process of thin-film periodically poled lithium niobate devices, all based on in-house facilities at CityU. Based on a novel segmented micro-heater design, we have achieved nonlinear photonic circuits with excellent conversion efficiencies and robustness against film thickness inhomogeneity. (Item 3&10 in Part C, Section 8). 3. We have achieved the first observation of continuous-wave THz generation in the TFLN platform, with ultrabroad tuning range from 0.22 to 0.5 THz, and the ability to perform high-speed electro-THz modulation. (Item 7 in Part C, Section 8). 4. We have developed ultrahigh-performance millimeter-wave photonic devices and systems, including an integrated lithium niobate microwave photonic processing engine that can perform multi-functional analog signal processing tasks at 67 GHz (Item 6 in Part C, Section 8) and the first integrated photonic radar that can operate in the millimeter-wave band (Item 8 in Part C, Section 8).

11204820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204820.value: The wafer-scale device fabrication process, theoretical and experimental investigation of photonic devices at THz frequencies, as well as the design and engineering of thin-film PPLN devices developed in this project, have laid important foundation for the continuous development of TFLN photonics in PI’s team. The device design and experimental knowhow have been adopted in the development of novel photonic devices and circuits in microwave photonics (e.g. in-situ optical vector analyzers, Advanced Photonics 2308840, 2024; programmable multifunctional integrated microwave photonic circuit, accepted at Nature Communications) and nonlinear photonics (Brillouin photonics in TFLN, under review at Science Advances; cryogenic nonlinear wavelength conversion, Laser & Photonics Reviews, 2401491, 2024). The further development of the research toward the realization of scalable and efficient nonlinear photonic circuits for phase-sensitive amplification application is currently underway with the support of another GRF fund (CityU 11215024)

11204820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204820.value: Terahertz frequencies ranging from 0.3 to 10 THz are of particular interest for chemical identification and non-destructive imaging, since a wide variety of molecules have their “fingerprint” absorption lines lying in this band. The terahertz range, however, is often referred to as the “terahertz gap”, since it lies just between the frequencies of mature electronic and optical technologies. As a result, terahertz waves cannot be efficiently produced using either electronic or optical methods. The lack of efficient and low-cost terahertz sources has become a major bottleneck for terahertz technologies to further into our daily life. In this project, we have developed an efficient and compact terahertz source based on an integrated photonic coupled-waveguide system. The system generates continuous-wave THz emission by mixing two optical lasers via nonlinear optical interactions. We engineered the coupled-waveguide system to achieve strong optical and terahertz confinement and large mode overlap simultaneously. We achieve continuous-wave terahertz generation with a broad frequency tuning range from 0.22 to 0.5 terahertz and a tenfold efficiency improvement over existing solutions. The compact, efficient and tunable terahertz source developed in this project could provide cost-effective solutions for a range of future applications including communications, remote sensing, and spectroscopy.

11205420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205420.value: 視覺顯著性的概念或眾人常看的地方是 很有趣的，因為我們所有人都会不斷在視覺 上 關注著我們所生活的世界。在計算機圖形學中，三維形狀的視覺顯著性考慮眾人在三維形狀表面上常看的位置。以前的研究已探索二維圖像的顯著性，并考虑觀看者的任务是否影响人们在图像中常看的位置。但是，現時的研究中沒有任務感知的三維形狀的視覺顯著性的工作。在這研究項目中，我們將會建立關於任務感知的三維形狀的視覺顯著性的計算理解。我們的主要推測是觀看者的任务是会影响人们在三維形狀中常看的位置。這種研究工作是很重要的，因為這種研究工作可應用於廣告，遊戲，和電影中。這研究項目是以首席研究員(PI)的以前的三維形狀感知研究工作為基礎。 我們將會收集任務感知的三維形狀顯著性的數據。數據的收集會考慮不同的觀看者任务，三維形狀代表模式及顯著性收集方法。我們將會對數據進行定性和定量分析，并了解為什麼觀看者對每種三維形狀的注意力在不同的任務中可能會有所不同。然後，收集的數據將用於學習任務感知的三維形狀顯著性的函數。與以前的研究相比，我們會創造新的神經網絡架構，並會考慮三維形狀的任務感知方面及視覺數據的時間方面。最後，我們將會探索一些任務感知的三維形狀顯著性的應用。

11205520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205520.value: The general objective of this project is to implement and study postnatal osteogenesis by natural hypertrophic chondrocytes (HCCs) associated with osteogenic progenitor cells (OPCs) in a tissue-engineered cartilaginous template for rudimentary bone formation. The ultimate goal is to develop viable and vascularized bone grafts for regenerative purpose. As the functional cells, HCCs are hypothesized and attempted to play a central role executing osteogenesis with or without involving OPCs. As an artificial osteogenic niche, a novel decellularized, tissue-engineered cartilaginous template that is made of pure hyaline cartilaginous extracellular matrices (ECMs), named dLhCG, will be produced and recellularized with the functional cells to implement postnatal osteogenesis via a pathway similar to endochondral ossification during the primary development. Accordingly, the Specific Objectives are listed as follows. The Objective 1 is to achieve relatively pure and natural population of HCCs from primary chondrocytes via a microfluidic approach. Rather than inducing or producing HCCs from chondrocytes or OPCs via deliberate biochemical treatments such as exposure to particular cytokines or hormones, which result in unnatural and/or already apoptotic HCC-like cells, relatively pure and natural population of HCCs will be sourced from primary chondrocytes harvested from native articular cartilage. The primary chondrocytes will be settled into Passage 0 without further subculture, from which smaller-sized regular (non-hypertrophic) chondrocytes (PCCs) and greater-sized HCCs are critically isolated from each other via a size exclusion cell sorting through an inertial spiral microfluidic approach. The Objective 2 is to achieve rudimentary osteogenesis from the tissue-engineered osteogenic niche made of functional cell-laden cartilaginous template in vitro. The functional cell populations that will be employed to re-cellularize dLhCG template are, respectively: HCCs, marrow derived stromal cells (MSCs) as the OPC, and co-culture of HCCs and MSCs; the Controls are, respectively: PCCs and co-culture of PCCs and MSCs. The Objective 3 is to achieve vascularized rudimentary bone formation from the re-cellularized dLhCG Samples using the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) of fertilized chicken eggs as a natural bioreactor. To fulfil this Objective and reveal the mechanism, as hypothesized and proposed, the central roles played by HCCs will be investigated with emphasis, including execution of direct osteogenic trans-differentiation, initiation of the co-cultured OPCs’ osteogenesis, induction of vascularization via angiogenesis in situ, and successive degradation of the cartilaginous template – the dLhCG scaffold. In summary, the study in this project can fulfil dual missions of understanding osteogenic biology and developing live bone grafts for regenerative applications. 本項目之總體目標即為于組織工程化軟骨模板中，透过成骨祖細胞（OPCs）與天然肥大軟骨細胞（HCCs）之共同作用，研究與實現其成骨作用，并用以初期骨組織生成。該項目之最終目標系開發一種可應用并可血管化之骨移植物。作為功能細胞，無論有無成骨祖細胞參與，肥大軟骨細胞皆被認為于成骨過程中發揮關鍵性作用。本項目應用dLhCG作為模板，將功能細胞透过再細胞化植入其中并發揮其成骨作用，實現類似軟骨內成骨之過程。該模板由透明軟骨細胞外基質（ECMs）組成，系一種新型脫細胞組織工程化軟骨。在此，現將本項目之具體目標列舉如下。目標一，透過微流控之方法于原代軟骨細胞中獲取相對純淨及天然之肥大軟骨細胞。先前研究中肥大軟骨細胞通常經由特定生化方式（例如將其暴露于特定細胞因子或激素）自軟骨細胞抑或相关类型祖細胞誘導而來，以獲得非天然或已趋于凋亡之肥大軟骨細胞樣細胞。本項目相對純淨之天然肥大軟骨細胞將來源于由天然關節軟骨中獲取之原代軟骨細胞。原代軟骨細胞將作為第〇代細胞，無需進行進一步傳代培養，透過慣性螺旋微流控方法，對不同大小之細胞進行分選，將體積較小之正常軟骨細胞（PCCs）與體積較大之肥大軟骨細胞嚴格分離。目標二：于由負載有功能細胞軟骨模板組成之組織工程成骨模板實現初步成骨過程。用於dLhCG再細胞化之細胞包括：肥大軟骨細胞，骨髓源性間充質幹細胞作為成骨祖細胞以及上述二者之共培養。實驗對照組分別為：軟骨細胞及軟骨細胞與間充質幹細胞之共培養。目標三：利用受精雞胚絨毛尿囊膜作為天然生物反應器，于再細胞化dLhCG中實現血管化初步骨生成。為實現此目標并揭示其作用機理，如假設所述，本項目將著重探究肥大軟骨細胞之主要作用，包括執行直接成骨轉分化，啟動與之共培養成骨祖細胞之成骨作用，誘導原位血管生成以及軟骨模板——dLhCG支架之連續退化。綜上所述，本項目可既可探究骨生物學，亦可開發可應用於再生之骨組織。

11205520.label: Realisation of objectives
11205520.value: To fulfil Objective 1, we used two microfluidic technologies to sort hypertrophic chondrocytes. We initially used polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as the material and employed a soft lithography fabrication strategy to create a spiral microfluidic chip device with one inlet and five outlets. However, due to the soft nature of chondrocytes, they undergo shape changes in the fluid. Chondrocytes deform under stress or fluid shear, causing changes in their trajectory and position as they pass through the device, thereby affecting the accuracy and efficiency of sorting. Therefore, we utilized forward scatter laser scattering signals to determine the relative size of cells and employed flow sorting for the separation of hypertrophic chondrocytes from cartilage cells. After sorting, there was a significant difference in cell size between the two populations, indicating successful separation. Subsequently, gene expression analysis revealed significant differences in Type X collagen, a prominent phenotype of hypertrophic chondrocytes, between the two subgroups. This indicated that we successfully isolated a subgroup of hypertrophic chondrocytes through the physical means of microfluidics. To fulfil Objective 2, regarding the implementation strategy of Task 2, we adopted the in vitro endochondral ossification (ECO) scheme and developed the osteogenic niche of engineered cells through the living hyaline-like cartilage graft (LhCG) created by our research group. By further decellularizing LhCG, we obtained dLhCG. This is an ideal template for studying the mechanism of ECO, because compared with the two-dimensional cell model, dLhCG can well simulate the biophysical conditions of the cartilage microenvironment, and this scheme does not require the sacrifice of additional experimental animal models. In this task, we used bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) as engineered cells. We hypothesize that the MSCs within dLhCG will undergo chondrogenic differentiation, hypertrophy, and subsequent trans-differentiation into osteoblasts, ultimately leading to ossification. To validate this hypothesis, we seeded MSCs into dLhCG to create mrLhCG. The mrLhCG constructs were cultured in chondrogenic medium containing TGF-β3, followed by high-serum chondrogenic medium (CGCC group). As a control, the mrLhCG constructs were differentiated towards osteogenesis in osteoinductive medium containing dexamethasone (OI group). The ossified mrLhCG structures are referred to as OsLhCG. Gene expression analysis results showed that the CGCC group expressed higher levels of articular cartilage ECM (COL2A1, SOX9) and endochondral ossification (COL10A1, RUNX1) markers compared to the OI group. RNA-seq data further confirmed that both groups of MSCs successfully ossified in the dLhCG constructs, but through different differentiation pathways. The CGCC group followed a process similar to endochondral ossification, transitioning from a chondrogenic state to a hypertrophic state before ossification. In contrast, the OI group achieved osteogenesis through a more direct MSC-to-osteoblast differentiation. Calcium deposition within the dLhCG gradually increased, as evidenced by an increasing trend in total calcium content. This calcium deposition was visually observed by Alizarin Red S and von Kossa staining, especially in the OI group. In contrast, the mrLhCG constructs in the CGCC group exhibited minimal calcium deposition, as evidenced by the lack of staining. However, the OsLhCG constructs in the CGCC group did show some degree of calcium deposition, as indicated by positive von Kossa staining. These quantitative calcium and histochemical staining results further support the notion that the OI group and its direct osteoinductive cues were more effective in promoting robust mineralization and osteogenesis of MSCs within the dLhCG. In contrast, the more modest calcium deposition in the OsLhCG-CGCC constructs suggests that the endochondral ossification pathway induced by the CGCC group was less efficient in driving complete bone formation compared to direct osteogenic differentiation in the OI group. Osteopontin (OPN) expression was not detected in mrLhCG constructs from both the CGCC and OI groups. But OPN concentrations were significantly higher in OsLhCG constructs from the CGCC group compared to the OsLhCG-OI group. To further investigate the extent of ossification at the protein level, IHC staining was performed to detect key bone-related markers, including osteocalcin, osteopontin, osteonectin, and type I collagen. We found that mrLhCG constructs had relatively low deposition of these bone matrix proteins compared to OsLhCG constructs, regardless of culture conditions. In contrast, OsLhCG samples, especially those from the CGCC group, stained more intensely for these osteogenic markers. Notably, OsLhCG constructs from both the CGCC and OI groups exhibited positive Alizarin Red S and von Kossa staining, indicating calcium deposition in the mineralized matrix. Compared with the mrLhCG construct, the culture conditions and differentiation induction process used by the OsLhCG construct were more effective in promoting MSC ossification and bone-related protein deposition. The enhanced bone matrix formation in the OsLhCG samples (especially the CGCC group) further supported the successful induction of osteogenesis in dLhCG. To fulfil Objective 3, our investigation into vascularization began with the use of the fertilized chicken egg chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model. Specific pathogen-free chicken eggs were purchased from a local distributor and incubated at 37°C for 11 days. The eggshells were then carefully peeled, creating a window to access the CAM. Sterilized dLhCG samples were placed directly onto the surface of the CAM. The window was sealed with parafilm, and the eggs were returned to the incubator for an additional 9 days. Then the eggs were sacrificed by exposure to 90% CO2 for a minimum of 20 minutes. The dLhCG constructs were then carefully removed from the CAM for further characterization. On a macroscopic scale, the CAM model appeared to be a suitable in vivo system for evaluating the vascularization potential of the dLhCG and rLhCG materials. This initial result suggests the possibility of using the rLhCG construct as a viable artificial bone graft for future implantation. We then implanted the OsLhCG-CGCC and OsLhCG-OI constructs into the omentum of nude mice. After 14 days, we conducted IHC staining on the retrieved samples, now designated as OsLhCGang-CGCC and OsLhCGang-OI. The vascular markers assessed included VEGFA, HIF1-α, VWF, and CD31, while the osteogenic markers included OCN, OPN, and ON. Positive staining for these markers indicated the successful vascularization of the OsLhCG. Interestingly, the deposition of osteogenic markers was significantly higher compared to the in vitro results. We further established a critical-sized bone defect model using rats. The decellularized OsLhCG constructs were then implanted and after 30 days, the rats were euthanized, and the samples were collected for micro-CT scanning and histological evaluation. Macroscopic observation revealed that the surface of the bone defects had been largely restored. In contrast, the control group exhibited significant residual defects, highlighting the reparative ability of the decellularized OsLhCG constructs. Microscopic evaluation through H&E staining and IHC analysis confirmed the occurrence of bone regeneration. The control group demonstrated noticeable persistent defects, while the OsLhCG-CGCC and OsLhCG-OI groups exhibited less pronounced defects. Positive staining for osteogenic markers, such as type II collagen, indicated the successful integration of newly deposited bone tissue with the original host bone and the decellularized OsLhCG scaffolds. This suggests that the decellularized OsLhCG constructs were able to promote bone repair and regeneration, with the implanted scaffolds being dispersed and replaced by newly formed bone over the 30-day in vivo implantation period. The micro-CT imaging data further corroborated these findings. Overall, decellularized OsLhCG samples, modified with different osteogenic induction methods, have been transformed into artificial bone grafts that can be implanted, achieving successful bone repair and regeneration with excellent osteogenic effects.

11205520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205520.value: a. Hypertrophic chondrocytes (HCCs) were successfully harvested: HCCs were isolated from cartilage tissue through physical means of microfluidics, as evidenced by their large cell size and significant gene expression of Type X collagen. b. The successful establishment and in vitro osteogenesis effect of the tissue-engineered bone graft: A tissue-engineered bone graft was developed via endochondral ossification (ECO) strategy. MSCs-laden dLhCG (mrLhCG) culturing in chondrogenic medium was named CGCC group (resembling ECO). The mrLhCG construct in osteogenesis-inducing medium acted as the control, OI group (direct MSC osteogenesis differentiation). The ossified mrLhCG construct was called OsLhCG. Gene expression analysis revealed higher levels of chondrogenesis-related (COL2A1, SOX9) and ossification-related (COL10A1, RUNX1) genes in the CGCC group compared to the OI group, indicating successful induction of the ECO pathway. Similarly, RNA-seq analysis demonstrated successful induction of MSC ossification in both groups. Through calcium quantification, Alizarin Red S and Von Kossa staining, elevated calcium deposition was observed in scaffold after 49 days of in vitro culturing. Osteopontin could be detected in OsLhCG-CGCC group and OsLhCG-OI group with higher concentration of OPN in OsLhCG-CGCC group. Both OsLhCG-CGCC group and OsLhCG-OI group exhibited high depositions of bone formation related proteins including osteocalcin, osteopontin, osteonectin, and type I collagen, indicating the successful osteogenesis induction at the protein level in vitro. c. The rudimentary ossification and vascularization of bone grafts using the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay and the in vivo greater omentum implantation trials: The CAM assay results suggested the potential of utilizing mrLhCG as an artificial bone graft for implantation. These scaffolds were further implanted into the greater omentum of nude mice for 14 days, ultimately demonstrating positive staining of vascular markers (VEGFA, HIF1-α, VWF, and CD31) and strong positive staining for osteogenic markers (osteocalcin, osteopontin, and osteonectin). d. The ability of the developed bone grafts for the repair of critical-sized bone defects in rats: The defects showed considerable restoration in OsLhCG groups. Positive staining for osteogenic markers confirmed successful integration of newly formed and existing bone tissue with OsLhCG. OsLhCG promoted bone repair and regeneration, with gradual replacement of the blocks by newly formed bone within 30 days of in vivo implantation. CT results demonstrated significant bone repair in both OsLhCG-CGCC and OsLhCG-OI groups, with slightly greater bone repair observed in the OsLhCG-CGCC group compared to the OsLhCG-OI group. e. This project result in 7 publications. 2 international conferences were attended. 2 PhD students graduated.

11205520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205520.value: This research proved the capability of the functional cell-laden dLhCG via in vitro differentiation of MSC and endochondral ossification strategy for bone repair. Further development may focus on in-situ recruitment of MSCs for in vivo differentiation. The precise modulation of MSC differentiation towards chondrogenic lineages and followed osteogenic differentiation through endochondral ossification, enables simultaneous repair of both cartilage and bone tissues. The recruitment of MSCs from the surrounding tissue or systemic circulation to the injury site can be facilitated through the release of chemoattractant factors in drug-releasing scaffolds, creating a microenvironment conducive to MSC migration. Besides, the differentiation of MSCs towards chondrogenic and osteogenic lineages can be precisely controlled using various strategies, including the use of growth factors, such as transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) and bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which promote chondrogenesis and osteogenesis, respectively. Additionally, mechanical cues, such as scaffold stiffness or dynamic loading, can influence MSC fate determination. Importantly, we can further investigate the mechanisms regarding the temporal sequence of MSC differentiation during endochondral ossification, the transitions in cell fate determination, and the dynamic changes in cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions. To achieve this, scaffolds preparation, animal models, and spatiotemporal transcriptomics may be unutilized.

11205520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205520.value: This research project developed an engineered bone graft as a promising alternative to autologous bone grafts for treating bone defects, which are common in the elderly population. The engineered graft exhibited excellent biocompatibility and the ability to support angiogenesis, promote osteogenesis, and successfully regenerate critical-sized bone defects. The significance of this work lies in its contributions to tissue engineering and its potential clinical applications. Unlike autologous bone grafts, which are limited by graft availability and donor-site morbidity, the engineered graft utilizes the patient's own stem cells to create a biomimetic autograft. This approach allows for patient-specific customization to ensure optimal fit and functionality, while avoiding the need for a second surgical procedure required for traditional autografts. Moreover, this project provided an invaluable model to investigate the underlying mechanisms of mesenchymal stem cell differentiation, chondrocyte hypertrophy, and trans-differentiation. These investigations can deepen our understanding of the role of hypertrophic chondrocytes in bone formation, which is crucial for advancing bone regenerative strategies in tissue engineering. Overall, this research has made significant contributions to the development of innovative bone graft substitutes and the advancement of fundamental knowledge in the field of bone biology and regeneration.

11205620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205620.value: 場景上下文主要描述物體周圍環境與某些感興趣的物體之間產生的關聯。基於最近在使用深度學習模型從圖像中提取場景上下文信息方面取得的成功，現有工作在如何將場景上下文信息應用於各種計算機視覺任務（包括物體檢測，識別和分割）上進行了大量研究。研究表明在考慮場景上下文時，模型通常獲得最優異的性能。然而，所有這些現有技術都利用從現有圖像中收集的上下文信息來推斷圖像中某些感興趣物體的屬性。在本文工作中，我們提出研究這些現有工作的反問題：給定多個物體的屬性，我們期望模型可以預測未知的場景上下文。能夠預測場景上下文的模型有許多應用，包括圖像合成，視頻合成以及場景類型分類等。 本文所提出的研究的主要目的是回答一個重要的問題：模型是否可以僅通過幾個輸入物體的屬性以生成有意義的場景上下文。我們在CVPR 2019論文中進行了初步探索：證明了當僅給出一個或兩個前景物體（以語義分割圖的形式），模型可以學習生成周圍的物體以及圖像的背景。由於這項工作旨在作為概念驗證，因此該工作只研究了這個開放問題的一部分。特別地，該工作並沒有考慮輸入物體的屬性將如何影響模型所推斷的場景上下文這個基本問題。在本文所提出的工作中，我們將沿著這個方向探索三個主要問題： 1. 我們觀察到，當給定多個物體時，不僅可以使用這些物體的存在來推斷周圍的場景上下文，而且這些物體彼此之間的交互關係對於確定場景上下文也同樣重要。例如，兩個人慢跑的場景上下文信息通常與兩個人互相搏鬥的場景上下文大不相同。這是一個非常高維度的學習問題，涉及到學習多個物體的類別，大小，形狀，位置等信息的交互情況。在這個項目中，我們將探索基於圖表示方法針對物體對像多維交互問題建模的不同方法。 2. 我們的初步探索工作並沒有考慮小物體作為輸入的情況。這是因為從小物體中通過卷積運算學習到的信息通常非常薄弱。為了處理不同大小的輸入物體，在本項目中，我們將探索金字塔學習，以豐富不同大小的輸入物體的表示形式。 3. 在我們的初步工作中，用戶以語義圖的形式指定輸入對象，該語義圖指定了每個物體的類別，大小，形狀和位置。然而，現實應用中用戶可能並不總是關心每個物體的所有這些屬性。我們在SIGGRAPH 2019上發表的最新工作中探索了以文本編碼進行圖形設計佈局的方式。在本項目中，我們將探索基於文本編碼思想以允許用戶通過文本指定部分輸入物體屬性的方式。 我們將對研究的模型進行全面評估，並通過圖像生成應用以證明該想法的有效性。

11205620.label: Realisation of objectives
11205620.value: In this project, we have conducted four main tasks w.r.t. to the four project objectives. First, we investigated how objects in a scene might interact with each other to determine the inferred scene contexts. Second, we investigated techniques to handle objects of different sizes in the input images. Third, we investigated the use of text input to specify object properties. Fourth, we have conducted thorough evaluations on the above methods. For the first objective, we first explore the idea of scene semantic interaction via two applications, saliency detection and mirror detection. In saliency detection, we investigate the relationship between salient objects and the semantics of their surrounding objects. Although existing salient object detection (SOD) methods have already considered contextual features, they often fail in real-world complex scenarios, due to two main issues: (1) most existing datasets consist of simple foregrounds and backgrounds that hardly represent real-life scenarios, and (2) the learned contextual features are too coarse for saliency reasoning in complex scenes. To address these problems, we construct a new large-scale dataset with complex scenes for SOD, and propose a context-aware learning approach to explicitly exploit the semantic scene contexts, with a novel Transformer-based pipeline. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that this proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art SOD methods in complex scenarios. We published this work in ICCV’21 (Conferences[3]). Mirror detection is a new research problem. It is important, as the presence of mirrors can be hazardous to automatic machines, such as robots and drones. If these machines are not aware of the presence of mirrors, they can easily crash into the mirrors. The difficulty of detecting mirrors is that mirrors generally lack a consistent visual appearance, making mirror detection very challenging. Existing works [Yang19,Lin20] are typically based on exploiting contextual contrasts and correspondences. They tend to fail in complex real-world scenes, where some objects, e.g., doorways, may have similar features as mirrors. We observe that humans tend to place mirrors in relation to certain objects for specific functional purposes, e.g., placing a mirror above the sink. Based on this observation, we propose a novel model to exploit semantic associations between a mirror and its surrounding objects for reliable mirror localization, via a Quadruple-Graph module to facilitate the diffusion/aggregation of semantic association knowledge using graph convolutions. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the mirror detection task. We published this work in CVPR’22 (Conferences[4]). To take the idea of semantic scene context learning further, we apply it to video-based novel view synthesis. Given a single scene layout and the camera transformation as inputs, our goal is to generate a novel view scene layout for a specified viewpoint. To tackle this challenging problem, we propose a model to capture contextualized object representation by explicitly modeling the object context transformation of the scene in the time domain. The contextualized object representation is essential in generating geometrically and semantically consistent scene layouts of different views. Experiments show that this model outperforms several strong baselines on indoor and outdoor scenes. We published this work in CVPR’22 (Conferences[1]). We also apply the idea of semantic scene context learning to urban layout regeneration. Urban regeneration is a crucial process to revitalize decaying or underused regions in cities, and regenerating urban layout is an essential step. In this work, we propose a model to regenerate the urban layout of a target region, given the textual descriptions of the surrounding context (surrounding regions). In other words, the proposed model learns the correlation between the target region and its surrounding context to infer the layout of the target region. Evaluations show that our method outperforms the baseline methods in regenerating desirable urban layouts that meet the textual descriptions. We published this work in AAAI’24 (Conferences[5]). For the second objective, we note that if the user inputs a very small object, the encoder tends to extract a meaningless object representation from it. Such an object representation cannot be used to reliably predict a potential scene context. Inspired by the zoom-out and zoom-in architecture in [Pang19] for detecting tiny objects, we re-scale the input object layout to enlarge the spatial resolution of small objects. We take an object layout as input. As the feature maps of an object layout contain much less information than those of a complete scene image, we cannot directly enlarge the feature maps as in [Pang19]. Hence, we first divide the input object layout into 9X9 grid cells. Based on the cells overlapped by the object, we select a minimum region containing the object. We then re-scale the region into the same size as that of the input layout, and pass it through the same encoder to obtain the zoomed object representation. Finally, we concatenate the zoomed object representation and the original object representation to obtain the final object representation. Our experimental results show that this idea can help improve the overall performance of the scene context prediction framework. This idea was discussed/presented in our TPAMI papers (Peer-reviewed Publications[2]). For the third objective, we first investigated the application of text prompts in specifying photo color adjustment in graphic designs. Given a graphic design containing a photo that needs to be recolored, our model can identify the source colors and the target regions from the user-provided language-based instruction, and then recolor the target regions in the photo with the source colors obtained from the graphic design. We evaluate the proposed model via extensive experiments and user studies. We published this work in TOG (SIGGRAPH’23) (Peer-reviewed Publications[6]). We then investigated the urban regeneration project that we mentioned above (Conferences [5]). In this work, we design a module to help convert input text descriptions into region attributes, specifying the properties of a given region. We further investigated the use of text prompt for image generation. Given an input text prompt and a layout map of the key objects in the image, we propose a model to generate the image as specified by the text prompt, with the objects and the corresponding visibility order following the specification of the layout map. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other baseline methods. This work has been accepted for publication in CVPR’25 (Conferences[7]). For the fourth objective, apart from the thorough evaluations on individual techniques as mentioned above, we also combined these techniques on two applications, map layout synthesis and image synthesis, to evaluate how these techniques worked together. In map layout synthesis (Conferences[5]), we aim to synthesize the layout of a region given the text descriptions of its surrounding regions, through surrounding context learning. In image synthesis (Conferences[7]), we aim to synthesize an image with contents specified by the input text descriptions and the visibility of the objects specified by a layout map. With these two applications, we could evaluate the developed techniques together under the two frameworks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of semantic context learning, handling of large and small objects, and using text prompts to specify object properties. References: [Lin20] Progressive Mirror Detection, CVPR’20. [Pang19] R2-CNN: Fast Tiny Object Detection in Large-scale Remote Sensing Images, GRSS’19. [Yang19] Where is My Mirror? ICCV’019.
