11205620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205620.value: In this project, we have studied how objects in a scene interact with each other and how their interactions may affect the scene context as well as the image (or design) as a whole. We have also studied how to compensate for small objects and how to apply text prompts as input to describe the relevant objects. While the detailed research outcome is presented in Section 5.3 of this report, our key research outcome can be summarized as follows: 1. We have thoroughly studied how objects can determine the scene contexts, and how scene contexts may then be used to infer the rest of the scene. We have also studied how the extracted scene contexts can be used to predict some object properties or the presence of certain objects. (Research Output: Conferences [1, 3, 4, 5] and Peer-reviewed Publications [2, 6].) 2. We have investigated techniques for handling objects of different sizes. In particular, we have developed a technique for rescaling the input object layout in order to enlarge the spatial resolution of small objects. This has proven to help improve the overall performance of scene context prediction. (Research Output: Peer-reviewed Publications [2].) 3. We have investigated different approaches to describe object properties using text prompts. We have applied in three very different applications. First, in graphic designs, we introduce text prompts for users to specify how to carry out photo recoloring. Second, in urban regeneration, we introduce descriptions to describe the properties of adjacent regions in order to predict the properties of the region to be regenerated. Third, in image generation, we apply text prompts, together with a layout map, to specify the properties of the objects to be synthesized. (Research Output: Conferences [5, 7] and Peer-reviewed Publications [6].) 4. Based on the developed techniques, we have explored some applications, including may layout synthesis (Research Output: Conferences [5]), image synthesis (Research Output: Conferences [7]), and layout-based video synthesis (Research Output: Peer-reviewed Publications [6]).

11205620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205620.value: Learning object correlations and how they form semantic contexts to infer the surrounding objects/scene is a very interesting research problem. During this research, we have found that it can lead to many different applications. Apart from the applications that we have explored/discussed in Section 6.1, we would like to apply it for video generation applications. In recent years, video generation has become a very hot research topic, due to its impact/usefulness in our daily life. It would be interesting to learn the changing semantic context over a video, under different scenarios. The learned contexts can then be used to infer new video contents. As a future work, we are currently exploring this direction of research.

11205620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205620.value: A scene context refers to the correlation of some background objects in the scene to the main objects of interest. In recent years, there is a lot of research on how to apply scene context information in various computer vision tasks, including object detection, recognition and segmentation. However, all these prior works utilize the context information gathered from existing images to infer the properties of the main objects of interest in an image. In this research project, we have investigated an inverse problem of these existing works – given the properties of multiple objects, we attempt to predict the unknown scene context. Being able to predict the scene context has many applications, including a new approach to image synthesis and video synthesis, as well as scene type classification. Through this project, we have studied three key issues. First, we have studied how objects in the scene interact with each other to determine the final scene. Second, we have studied techniques for handling objects of different sizes. Third, we have studied different approaches to describe object properties based on text prompts. Further, we have also developed a number of applications based on the developed techniques, including may layout synthesis, image synthesis, and layout-based video synthesis. As a future work, we are currently investigating the application of scene context to video synthesis.

11206120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206120.value: We propose to use error correction alignment for mass spectra search. The new concept can avoid the problem of error accumulation and lead to better performance. We propose a faster algorithm for the error correction alignment of spectrum mass graph and proteoform mass graph problem and produce a program package TopMGFast. The newly designed algorithms require less space and running time so that we are able to compute global optimal alignments for the two input mass graphs in a reasonable time. For the local alignment version, experiments show that the run-ning time of the new algorithm is reduced by 2.5 times. For the global alignment version, experiments show that the maximum mass errors be-tween any pair of matched nodes in the alignments obtained by our method are within a small range as designed, while the alignments pro-duced by the state-of-the-art method, TopMG, have very large maximum mass errors for many cases. The obtained alignment sizes are roughly the same for both TopMG and TopMGFast. Of course, TopMGFast needs more running time than TopMG. Therefore, our new algorithm can ob-tain more reliable global alignments within a reasonable time. This is the first time that global optimal error correction alignments can be obtained using real datasets.

11206320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206320.value: Network controllability is a fundamental issue that must be determined and guaranteed before one can consider how to control a complex dynamical network in engineering applications. When the network is subject to random or intentional attacks, its controllability needs resilience by means of supplying backup control inputs, which presents the robustness to the network: the less new control inputs are needed, the more robust the network controllability is. The present proposal aims to address this theoretically fundamental and technically challenging question for some specific complex networks, for which controllability and its robustness can be precisely defined and characterized, paving the way to studying more general and advanced configurations of complex networks. Specifically, a measure of robustness is defined for the network controllability as the effort to withstand failures due to malicious attacks, so as to recover the network controllability from the destruction, by the percentage of new control inputs versus the size of the network. Both node-removal and edge-removal attacks in random and intentional fashions will be investigated. Some optimal network building blocks, namely basic motif structures, for best controllability robustness will be identified and characterized. Typical directed networks, such as directed Henneberg networks, Random Triangular Networks (RTN), and Random Rectangular Networks (RRN), will be simulated and analyzed using machine learning-based optimization techniques for their best robustness of controllability. To that end, a general directed complex network with many loops will be studied to confirm the essential role of loops in the network controllability robustness. Then, for theoretical analysis and robust network design, controllability robustness bounds will be estimated. Both lower bound and upper bound for the network robustness of directed Henneberg networks, as well as directed 3-motif RTN and directed 4-motif RRN, will be established. In many engineering applications, it is key to determine, before a design, whether or not a network is controllable and how robust it would be against malicious and destructive attacks. This project will address this important issue, hence will have significant impact in the interdisciplinary scientific fields of complex networks and control theory, as well as network design optimization, which has rapidly evolved in the past decade towards real applications in industrial assembly automation and biological systems such as brain science and biological neuronal systems. 在許多工程應用中，在設計之前確定網絡是否可控以及抵禦惡意和破壞性攻擊的魯棒性至關重要。 網絡可控性的魯棒性定義爲承受惡意攻擊而導致的故障的能力，用新控制輸入與網絡規模的百分比來衡量。隨機和敵意攻擊分爲節點刪除和連邊刪除兩種攻擊。本項目研究最佳的網絡結構，將獲得最佳的可控性的魯棒性。將使用基于機器學習的優化技術對典型的有向網絡（例如有向Henneberg網絡，隨機三角網絡（RTN）和隨機矩形網絡（RRN））進行仿真和分析，以實現最佳的可控性。爲此，將研究具有多個回路的連通有向複雜網絡，以確認回路在網絡可控性魯棒性中的重要作用。然後，進行理論分析和魯棒網絡設計，並將估計可控性魯棒性的界限。將建立有定Henneberg網絡以及有向3-motif RTN和4-motif RRN的網絡魯棒性的下限和上限。 本項目將解決上述重要問題，期望將對複雜網絡和控制理論之間跨學科的研究以及網絡設計優化産生重要影響。 目標： （1）識別並表征一些最佳網絡構結構模塊，以實現最佳的可控性魯棒性。將通過基于機器學習的優化方法對典型的有向網絡結構（例如有向Henneberg網絡，隨機三角網絡（RTN）和隨機矩形網絡（RRN））進行仿真和分析，以了解其可控性的魯棒性。爲此，將研究具有許多回路的一般有向複雜網絡，以確認回路在網絡可控性魯棒性中的重要作用。 （2）建立可控性魯棒性的界限。將建立有向Henneberg網絡以及有向3-motif RTN和4-motif RRN抵禦邊緣刪除攻擊的網絡魯棒性的下限和上限。

11206320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206320.value: It is important and often necessary to determine the controllability of a dynamical network before one can consider how to control it for practical applications, since if a network is uncontrollable then it is impossible to design a controller or a control strategy to drive the network to accomplish a desired objective. This important theoretical issue of controllability of complex dynamical networks has been studied, leading to good understanding with practical criteria for network controllability, as well as controllers design and implementation. On the other hand, the real world today is full of risks and threats existing in many well-designed and well-functioning technological networks, such as the Internet, wireless communication networks, transportation networks, power grids, and above all, the Internet of Things. Consequently, there is an urgent need for the resilience and robustness of the network controllability against malicious attacks. This proposed project addresses both the network controllability and its robustness against malicious attacks. The funded research has been completed according to the original proposal with fruitful results obtained and a large number of journal papers published. It also laid a foundation for future research on the same subject but in higher-order complex networks, which could be more useful for real applications.

11206520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206520.value: 用於廣範pH生產氫氣的MoS2電催化劑的合理設計及其機制，動力學和優化

11206520.label: Project Objectives
11206520.value: To gain knowledge on the adsorption state of the active intermediates, related adsorption energy and reaction kinetics on the catalyst active sites to derive the catalytic reaction mechanisms in a specific medium environment; To establish the intrinsic connection between the catalyst microstructure and electrocatalytic behavior; To devise synthesis method to fabricate MoS2 based catalysts with properly designed heterostructure; To optimize MoS2 catalyst design for maximum pH-universal HER catalytic performance.

11206520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206520.value: 對於解決生產氫氣以實現氫氣經濟的瓶頸問題，開發有效，低成本的氫氣分解反應（HER）電催化劑是至關重要。 根據我們最近的研究，基於二硫化鉬（MoS2）的催化劑在酸性環境中可以作為具前景的非貴金屬HER電催化劑。 然而，MoS2電催化劑通常在鹼性條件下表現差，並且在廣範試劑活性方面顯示不佳。 當前的挑戰在於設計能在酸性和鹼性條件下均具有高氫釋放催化性能的MoS 2催化劑。 在這個項目中，我們將進行計算建模和實驗研究。 正如先前的研究指出，材料的微觀結構可以控制電催化作用，我們的研究的第一步旨在獲得有關MoS2微觀結構與電催化行為之間固有聯繫的HER動力學的知識。 我們將進行第一原理電子結構計算和動力學模擬，以完成基於MoS2的催化劑的合理設計，以進行有效的HER催化。 在實驗部分，我們將通過生長過程的調控，開發出具有可控的生長方向，活性位點分佈和特定的異質結構的MoS2基催化劑的合成方法。 我們將製造MoS2催化劑並對其微觀結構和電催化行為進行表徵測試。 並透過進行HER雙路徑動力學模擬，原位同步輻射X射線吸收光譜和密度泛函理論計算，研究MoS2微觀結構對HER過程的影響機理。 最後，我們將進行MoS2催化劑設計的參數優化，以實現最大的廣範試劑HER性能。 此項目將使我們更理解電催化氫的產成機理，從而提供一種新的策略，以開發有效的微結構化電催化劑，實現高HER動力學。

11206520.label: Realisation of objectives
11206520.value: Developing effective, low-cost electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is crucial to solving the bottleneck problem in hydrogen production for the implementation of hydrogen economy. Based on our recent research, molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) based catalysts can perform as promising non-precious-metal HER electrocatalysts in acidic environment. However, the MoS2 electrocatalysts generally exhibit poor performance under alkaline condition and show inferiority in pH-universal activity. The challenge in the present development is to design MoS2 catalysts with high hydrogen evolution catalytic performance under both acidic and alkaline conditions. In this project, we will conduct both computational modeling and experimental studies. As previous research has shown that the material microstructure can manipulate the electrocatalytic effect, the first step of our study aims to gain insightful knowledge on the HER kinetics of the intrinsic connection between the microstructure and electrocatalytic behaviors of MoS2. First-principle electronic structure calculation and kinetics simulation will be conducted to accomplish rational design of MoS2 based catalysts for efficient HER catalysis. In the experimental part, we developed the synthesis method of MoS2 based catalysts with controllable growth direction, distribution of active sites and specific heterostructure through the regulation of growth process. MoS2 based catalysts were fabricated and characterized for the microstructure and electrocatalytic behaviors. The mechanisms of the effect of MoS2 microstructure on the HER process were investigated by conducting HER dual-path kinetic simulation, in situ synchrotron radiation X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculation. Finally, we conducted parametric optimization of MoS2 catalyst design for maximum pH-universal HER performance. This project has enableed better understanding of the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution mechanisms and subsequently provided a new strategy to develop effective microstructured electrocatalysts with controllable synthesis method for high HER kinetics. In this project, a dual-photoelectrode PFC system was constructed using an excellent SnO2/BiOBr/MoS2 as a photoanode and copper oxide/copper as a photocathode for the first time. The appropriate interfacial contact and outstanding photoelectrochemical activity of the photoanode can be attributed to SnO2 hole-blocking layer. It is not only employed as a conductive scaffold for BiOBr/MoS2 but also provided less tendency for charge transport loss. In addition, the by-product Bi2S3 acts as a sensitizer due to its broad absorption spectrum (~800 nm) to increase light harvesting. The resulting SnO2/BiOBr/MoS2 photoanode yields the highest photocurrent density at all bias voltages and achieves 4.0 mA cm− 2 , which is around eight times higher in comparison with bare BiOBr while it is twice as much as that of the BiOBr/MoS2 photoanode without SnO2 hole reflection layer. This study demonstrates that recombination is significantly inhibited by adding methylene blue (MB) as the hole scavenger, resulting in a high power output efficiency in the dual-photoelectrode PFC system. An ultrahigh power density of 0.045 mW cm− 2 and improved photodegradation efficiency to reach ~ 91 % after 180 min. The excellent power density can therefore be assumed that the enriched strong oxidizing photoexcited holes were used to participate in directly decomposing MB. The reaction kinetics of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is largely determined by balancing the Volmer step in alkaline media. Bifunctionality as a proposed strategy can divide the work of water dissociation and intermediates (OH* and H*) adsorption/desorption. However, sluggish OH* desorption plagues water re-adsorption, which leads to poisoning effects of active sites. Some active sites may even directly act as spectators and do not participate in the reaction. Furthermore, the activity comparison under approximate nanostructure between bifunctional effect and single-exposed active sites is not fully understood. Here, a facile three-step strategy is adopted to successfully grow molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) on cobalt-containing nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (Co-NCNTs), forming obvious dual active domains. The active sites on domains of Co-NCNTs and MoS2 and the tuned electronic structure at the heterointerface trigger the bifunctional effect to balance the Volmer step and improve the catalytic activity. The HER driven by the bifunctional effect can significantly optimize the Gibbs free energy of water dissociation and hydrogen adsorption, resulting in fast reaction kinetics and superior catalytic performance. As a result, the Co-NCNTs/MoS2 catalyst outperforms other HER electrocatalysts with low overpotential (58 and 84 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in alkaline and neutral conditions, respectively), exceptional stability, and negligible degradation. Designing low-cost, high-performing electrocatalysts is key to green energy development, yet relying solely on the "synthesis-characterization" catalyst screening model is time-consuming and costly. There are two main applications for Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in electrochemical reactions: explaining mechanisms and predicting performance, which play important roles in fabricating robust electrocatalysts. MD simulations of electrocatalysis include the adsorption and desorption of reactants, intermediates, and products in this review. The structural changes in active centers under various electric field states, the effects of alkali metal cations, common anions, and pH effects in the electrolyte on the electrocatalytic process are also discussed to reveal the reaction mechanism. Then the prediction of the catalysts performance in specific reaction using MD simulations are introduced. Finally, the optimization and challenges of MD techniques are discussed. Developing high-performance hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts working at a high current density is essential because of the increasing demand for clean and renewable hydrogen energy. Herein, we have developed Ir nanocluster-decorated macroporous NiCo foam (Ir-nc@m-NiCo) to overcome the sluggish HER kinetics for enhanced hydrogen production. Ir-nc@m-NiCo can be fabricated by a corrosion engineering method. In the mechanism of electron transfer from Ni and Co to Ir at the interface between the NiCo foam and Ir cluster, the electrons accumulated on Ir favor optimal adsorption of H* for the HER. Therefore, Ir-nc@m-NiCo exhibits excellent HER activity, reaching current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm−2 at low overpotentials of 101 and 146 mV, respectively, in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte. Moreover, Ir-nc@m-NiCo possesses remarkable HER activity in simulated alkaline seawater electrolytes with 1000 mA cm−2 at 178 mV and demonstrates long-term durability with a slight potential increase after 10 hours testing under 500 mA cm−2.

11206520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206520.value: Iron-based nanostructures represent an emerging class of catalysts with high electroactivity for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in energy storage and conversion technologies. However, current practical applications have been limited by insufficient durability in both alkaline and acidic environments. In particular, limited attention has been paid to stabilizing iron-based catalysts by introducing additional metal by the alloying effect. Herein, we reported bimetallic Fe2Mo nanoparticles on N-doped carbon (Fe2Mo/NC) as an efficient and ultra-stable ORR electrocatalyst for the first time. The Fe2Mo/NC catalyst showed high selectivity for a four-electron pathway of ORR and remarkable electrocatalytic activity with high kinetics current density and half-wave potential as well as low Tafel slope in both acidic and alkaline medias. It demonstrated excellent pH-universal ORR and long-term durability with no activity loss even after 10,000 potential cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed the modulated electronic structure of formed Fe2Mo, which supported the electron-rich structure for the ORR process. Meanwhile, the mutual protection between Fe and Mo sites guarantees efficient electron transfer and long-term stability, especially under the alkaline environment. This work has supplied an effective strategy to solve the dilemma between high electroactivity and long-term durability for the Fe-based electrocatalysts, which opens a new direction of developing novel electrocatalyst systems for future research.

11206520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206520.value: We describe a promising Fe2Mo catalyst having high activity and high durability for the ORR electrocatalysis derived from the ZIF-8 precursor. HRTEM and XPS analyses proved the distinct microstructure of Fe2Mo/NC catalyst with FeMo nanoparticles as the core, nitrogen doped carbon as the shell. The as-prepared Fe2Mo/NC catalyst possessed more effective hydrogenation of OHad on its Fe2Mo surface than and commercial Pt/C single metallic Fe/NC catalysts with lower Tafel slopes and higher half-wave potentials in both alkaline and acidic environment. The Fe2Mo/NC catalyst exhibits high kinetic current densities of 82.28 mA/cm2 at 0.85V in 0.1M KOH solution and 37.62 mA/cm2 at 0.75V in 0.5M H2SO4 solution, which are 21-fold and 4-fold greater than those of the commercial Pt/C, respectively. Furthermore, the Fe2Mo/NC catalyst can largely retain the ORR activity after 10,000 potential cycles demonstrating its excellent long-term durability. DFT calculations have revealed that the formed Fe2Mo alloy shows a high electroactivity towards the ORR process in both acidic and alkaline environments. The superior ORR originates from the d-d orbital coupling between Fe and Mo, which forms electroactive catalysts with strong stability for long-term applications.

11206520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206520.value: Iron-based nanostructures are a new type of catalyst that are very effective for reactions needed in energy storage and conversion, like in batteries and fuel cells. However, they haven't been widely used yet because they don't last long enough in harsh environments, like acidic or alkaline conditions. To tackle this, scientists have started experimenting with adding other metals to make them more stable. In this study, we introduce a new catalyst made from a combination of iron and molybdenum nanoparticles on nitrogen-doped carbon, called Fe2Mo/NC. This catalyst is particularly good at efficiently driving the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), which is crucial for energy technologies. It works well in both acidic and alkaline conditions, showing high activity and stability. Even after 10,000 cycles of use, it doesn't lose its effectiveness. Using advanced calculations, we found that the combination of iron and molybdenum changes the electronic structure in a way that supports the reaction. The two metals protect each other, allowing for efficient electron transfer and long-term stability, especially in alkaline environments. This research offers a promising approach to overcoming the challenge of creating iron-based catalysts that are both highly active and durable, paving the way for future advancements in catalyst development.

11206620.label: Realisation of objectives
11206620.value: With regards to Objective 1, we have successfully designed, fabricated and tested a novel in-plane sensitive magnetometer based on a higher order free-free wide beam or what could be otherwise referred to a flexural plate wave (FPW). We have verified that the measured resonances match the finite element simulation prediction of the mode of interest. By this novel design, we were able to scale up the frequency from 160 kHz (based on a low frequency fundamental mode resonator described in a previous work prior to this project) to 5.3 MHz. This allowed us to scale the bandwidth up by 30 times (due to similar Q and therefore the widest bandwidth reported to date, 10 kHz bandwidth) while still maintaining a sensitivity that is state of art (4 ppm/mT vs Microsystems & Nanoengineering 10, 58 (2024). With regards to Objective 2, we have successfully designed, fabricated and tested a novel out-of-plane sensitive magnetometer based on a laterally vibrating resonator with a resonant frequency of 71 MHz. This represents upscaling the bandwidth of about 4 times (due to similar Q), delivering the widest bandwidths demonstrated to date (7 kHz). Going from a lower frequency fundamental mode up to a higher order mode (15th order to be specific) required a complex routing design within the constraints of a single metal layer allowed by the foundry process that was used. In our design phase, we had increased the mode order to maximum possible with a discernable strain pattern from extensive simulation iterations. We compared two designs that differed only in the routing layout: one with the current loop running between the sensing piezoelectric transducer electrodes while the other separated the current loop and sensing piezoelectric transducer electrodes into separate non-overlapping halves. We had found through our tests in the first half of the project that feedthrough is particularly critical going to higher frequencies (as in the case of higher order modes). We successfully lowered feedthrough by 10 times (20 dB) through the novel split actuation-sensing design. With regards to Objective 3, we have successfully demonstrated how wide acoustic bandgap phononic crystals could be applied to BOTH the <110> crystal orientation and <100> crystal orientation to reach the targeted Qs of 10,000, without any noticeable tradeoff. The Young’s modulus of silicon along the <100> crystal orientation is lower than along the <110> crystal orientation, which allows us to realise magnetometer designs with higher sensitivity resulting from a lower stiffness while maintaining the record high Qs that have only be observed for <110> direction to date. Preliminary results were presented in Transducers 2021, with more extensive results incorporating contrasting phononic crystal designs reported in [J2].

11206620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206620.value: Upon the departure of Prof. Lee, who was the original PI of this project, from CityU in 2021, the current PI took over some of his projects and collaborated with Prof. Lee. The PhD student who worked on some of the devices for this project also withdrew his candidacy before the devices could be tested. Before his departure, Prof. Lee had fabricated several samples, which the current PI and his team subsequently evaluated for performance. Prof. Lee’s ex-PhD student, now a research professor at UESTC, was engaged to help with the testing of the devices to leverage his experience in the field. We have found that while the various higher order modes could be modeled and actuated efficiently by piezoelectric transducers, having to be constrained by a single metal layer in the fabrication process that was available for the project made routing of the current loop unexpectedly challenging. This was a unique challenge that we found when moving from simple and low frequency fundamental modes to more complex and higher frequency higher order modes, be it for in plane resonance modes or out of plane resonance modes for different magnetic field sensitive axes. Another major finding was the uniqueness of the solid-disk phononic crystal that provided a wide acoustic bandgap, which is desirable for boosting Q towards increasing sensitivity. The solid-disk phononic crystal could boost Q to 10,000, the limit we have reached by various methods, on both the <110> and <100> crystal orientations. While we had thought that other phononic crystal design would afford the same gains, we were surprised to find that was not the case. This finding is also significant in the context of other considerations relevant to magnetometers that were outside the scope of this project. One example is that of temperature sensitivity. Temperature sensitivity of frequency has been shown to be lower for the <100> crystal orientation of degenerately-doped silicon. And thus being able to apply phononic crystals to deliver record high Qs in this less researched orientation for sensing allows both a boost in sensitivity (by lower stiffness) as well as reduced temperature sensitivity. The results have been reported in [C1] and [J2]. As outlined in the progress report, the research team explored the utilization of magnetic field sensors in high-sensitivity, wide-bandwidth sensing for power electronic applications. The team focuses on employing nonlinear inductors to regulate converter operation in DC distribution networks. The use of nonlinear inductors in power converters is disseminated in [J1], [C2]. In the realm of addressing impedance mismatches in DC microgrids, there is a rising interest in model predictive control (MPC) over traditional passive and active damping methods. The preliminary result is given in [J3], [C3].

11206620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206620.value: We were limited to Aluminum Nitride (AlN) for the piezoelectric layer and by the thicker membranes available. These were the only options available for foundry processes. This limited the achievable sensitivity based on the concepts explored in this project. Simulations show that further significant improvements could be made if the stack design could be optimized more favorably to increase sensitivity. For example, a lower silicon to piezoelectric film thickness ratio would reduce the stiffness of the structure at a faster rate than frequency, thus leading to higher sensitivity by scaling down the film thickness. Another very promising optimization route would be the use of highly doped Scandium AlN or even Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT), materials not available from foundries yet. These piezoelectric films have substantially higher piezoelectric constants as well as lower Young’s modulus. The former provides higher mechanical strain to charge ratio, while the latter lowers the net stiffness of the structure. This provides a double or compounded effect in raising the sensitivity. In short, the concepts from this project could be reapplied to more advanced materials to further boost performance. Application of the developed magnetometer as a current sensor for high-frequency-switched power electronic systems has a huge potential for further development.

11206620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206620.value: This project aims to develop chip-size magnetic field sensors (i.e., magnetometers). Magnetometers now found in every smartphone comprise materials in-compatible with semiconductor manufacturing; the other sensors are fabricated in semiconducting fabs. The magnetometers developed in this project aim for both high sensitivity and bandwidth based on Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS). The tradeoff between sensitivity and bandwidth is intrinsic to existing MEMS magnetometers. Bandwidth limits the response time of the sensor and its range of operable frequencies. This project has investigated a novel approach using piezoelectric devices, intrinsically more sensitive to forces to increase sensitivity. To increase bandwidth simultaneously, this project investigated complex higher order mechanical resonance modes to scale up the oscillation frequency. While conventional MEMS magnetometers typically work up to 10 kHz and bandwidths limited to a few Hz, the magnetometers developed in this project oscillate up to 70 MHz with a bandwidth of 7 kHz. And while conventional MEMS magnetometers need to operate in vacuum, the novel devices we have developed surpass these in performance without requiring vacuum. The outcomes from this research could enable high performance chip-based magnetometers benefitting a diverse range of applications in the biomedical, power systems, consumer electronics fields.

11206820.label: Project Objectives
11206820.value: Use of highly efficient modulation formats need good linearity which then requires power amplifiers to operate at output power back-off. Operating at output power back-off severely degrades efficiency resulting in higher usage of energy. The first objective is to increase the linearity of RF power amplifiers by using innovative Harmonic-Modulated Impedance Inverters to realize a Doherty-Like Power Amplifier. Bandwidth of the Doherty power amplifier topology is limited mainly by two components, one of them being the impedance transformer. The second objective here is to increase bandwidth of the Doherty power amplifier using novel impedance transformers. The second component that limits the bandwidth of the Doherty power amplifier is the phase compensation network. The third objective is to implement an innovative coupled phase compensation network with specific optimal impedance to increase the bandwidth of the Doherty power amplifier. The last objective is to combine the previous three innovative and novel ideas to realize a wideband/dual-band Doherty like power amplifier for use in 5G wireless communication systems.

11206820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206820.value: The efficiency and linearity of radio frequency power amplifiers has been one of the limiting factors in the use of modulating schemes used in wireless communication systems. In first generation cellular radio, FM was used because of the need to use high efficiency amplifiers operating in class C. This has undergone numerous transformations and has now been made more challenging with the advent of 5G cellular radio. 5G usage scenarios can be divided into three spectrums, below 2GHz, 2-6GHz and above 6GHz. Each spectrum have their own usage scenarios and this proposal intends to address the sub-6GHz band. The base station power amplifier (PA) is the main consumer of electrical power which becomes even more of a problem as they will proliferate even more in 5G cellular radio. They are also the main contributor of distortion and interference within wireless communication systems. RF power amplifiers used in 5G, will be required to operate at the output back-off region, because of the use of the more spectrally efficient modulated signal. These more efficient modulated signals have a high peak to average power ratio (PAPR) which require operation at back-off in order to mitigate adjacent channel interference problems. Carrier aggregation techniques are also used for high data speed but requires each component within the wireless system to operate over a broad bandwidth. The Doherty power amplifier (Doherty PA) has become the amplifier of choice in base station PA design in past decades due to its additional efficiency peak at back-off. This allows higher efficiency operation at lower power levels. However, most existing Doherty PA works cannot satisfy the strict requirements of 5G wireless systems, without a dramatic increase in costs due to the need to combine numerous amplifiers at a high loss in power. In this proposal, the design of power amplifiers for use in 5G base stations based on innovative circuit techniques are investigated for the sub-6 GHz. The main challenge in designing power amplifiers, will be to achieve high performances (including efficiency, linearity and ultra-wide bandwidth) using innovative circuit techniques. The works proposed in this project will include a number of solutions for different application scenarios in 5G wireless communication systems. 功率放大器的效率和線性度已經成為調製信號在無線通信系統中使用的主要限制因素。在第一代蜂窩通信中，因為高效率C類放大器的使用，FM信號被使用。現在隨著5G移動通信的出現，這經歷了無數的轉變並變得更有挑戰性。5G的使用場景可以被分為三個頻譜，2GH以下，2GHz - 6GHz，和6GHz以上。每一個頻譜有他們自己的使用場景，此專案旨在解決6GHz一下的問題。 基站功率放大器是電力的主要消耗器件，這將成為一個更大的問題，因為它們將在5G蜂窩無線電中激增。它們也是無線通信系統中造成失真和干擾的主要因素。在5G系統中，更高效的調製信號被使用，這些調製信號具有較高的峰均功率比（PAPR），這需要功率放大器工作在輸出回退區以減輕鄰近的通道干擾問題。載波聚合技術也被用於高速數據的傳輸，但需要無線系統中的每個組件在寬頻帶上操作。Doherty功率放大器已經在過去幾十年間成為基站功率放大器的首選，由於其在回退區間額外的效率高峰。這允許更高的效率可以在低功率區實現。然而，大多數存在的Doherty功率放大器工作不能滿足5G系統苛刻的要求。 在此專案中，面向Sub-6GHz，基於創新電路技術的5G基站功率放大器設計被研究。功率放大器的主要挑戰將會被克服以實現高性能，這包括高效率，高線性度和超寬頻寬。本項目所呈現的工作將包括一系列面向5G無線通信不同應用場景的解決方案。

11206820.label: Realisation of objectives
11206820.value: After starting the research project objective 3 was completed first, followed by objectives 1, 2 and 4. As mentioned in the objectives, one of the bandwidth limitations of the Doherty Power Amplifier is the phase compensation network mentioned in objective 3. The challenge here was how to realize the phase compensation network. It was known previously that the peaking branch has a larger effect on the bandwidth due to the larger impedance ratio compared to the carrier branch. Therefore, if the peaking branch bandwidth could be increased, then the overall bandwidth could be increased. A coupled line structure was investigated and it was found that it was able to reduce the external Q-factor. With a reduced Q-factor, the bandwidth would therefore be increased. Thus, if the coupled line structure is placed in the peaking branch, a bandwidth improvement should be possible. This had to be implemented in conjunction with the frequency variation. This was proposed and implemented [1] and gave a significant improvement in bandwidth. Since this is quite complex a design procedure is also provided in [1]. The high efficiency range of a Doherty Power Amplifier is the reason why it is found in almost all Mobile Radio Base Station transmitters. This high efficiency must also have an acceptable linearity as mentioned in objective 1. The reason for this with the use of more efficient modulation formats using Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM). With even higher data rates that require larger QAM levels, the Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR) will increase. Their disadvantage is that amplifiers operating with large PAPR will suffer from lower efficiency. Doherty structures can handle higher PAPR but with the drawback of using larger number of sections and therefore larger number of transistors. This will invariably increase cost and size. The increase in the number of transistors and its associated size increase will also result in higher losses and therefore lower efficiency. One way to improve efficiency, is to consider the use of harmonics. This is a problem because harmonics gets lower as power level reduces. Harmonic Injection is normally considered as a one port or at most a two-port methodology for improving efficiency. Since the combining port at the output of the Doherty Power Amplifier is comprised of three-ports, a three-port Harmonic Injection Network (HIN) was investigated to see if efficiency could be improved. It was found that the optimal drain fundamental frequency termination for the carrier device at back-off and saturation could be realized simultaneously. This was found to increase the efficiency at back-off. Not only that it was found that due to the effect of the second harmonic, the saturated power was found to be increased. This was a good and unintended consequence [2]. In objective 2, the other bandwidth limitations of the Doherty Power Amplifier is the impedance transformer. If this limitation could be reduced, then the bandwidth could be improved. The use of an impedance transformer that operates in different modes was investigated and it was found that with careful design, realizing a complex to real transformation was possible at two frequencies. If these two frequencies can be spaced far apart, then its bandwidth will be increased. However, the larger frequency separation will result in poorer in-band performance. A dual mode impedance transformer was proposed and implemented [2] and it was discovered that this method could also be used to eliminate the post-matching network. With the post-matching network eliminated, again the unintended consequences were an additional improvement in the bandwidth. Since the post-matching network was now not necessary, the circuit size was also reduced. For objective 4, the wideband performance was already addressed in the previous objectives so the dual-band operation was investigated more. A power amplifier usually has performances that degrade with increase in bandwidth. An alternative solution would be to operate with two bands rather than with one broad bandwidth, which will give better in-band performance. The difficulty with dual-band operation is the realization of the possible networks that would not only give a dual-band filter response but also satisfy the Doherty effect. After several attempts it was found that stub-loaded stepped-impedance transformers could satisfy this problem. It is well known that the use of stub-loading could realize multiple transmission zeros. However, having multiple transmission zeros does not satisfy the Doherty requirements. It was found later that not only can these stub-loading realize multiple transmission zeros, but they can also realize impedance transformation. These two characteristics when used properly can satisfy the Doherty requirements. These characteristics were studied and it was found that a dual-passband Doherty Power Amplifier could be realized [4]. This is not entirely what was in objective 4 because only some of the novel ideas in objectives 1-3 was used. In particular [3] is used to aid in the realization of a dual-band Doherty Power Amplifier.

11206820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206820.value: The operation of a Microwave Power Amplifier is complex as they have many interacting characteristics. When you change one parameter it affects the other parameter and vice versa. This bilateral operation is compounded by the fact that we are using semiconductors that can have large variations which makes accurate verification of measurements with simulation difficult. This is again further compounded by the fact that the Doherty topology is comprised of two interacting bilateral transistors. With these challenges the bandwidth was increased with the use of a coupled line structure [1]. This was achieved by targeting the part that affected the bandwidth the most which was the peaking branch. To improve the efficiency, harmonic injection was proposed and not only was the efficiency improved, but an unintended boost in performance was noticed. In the past, harmonic injection was performed mainly as a two-port network, here a three-port network was considered. The good and unintended outcome was an increase in saturated output power [2] in addition to the increased efficiency. Another problem that limits the bandwidth is the impedance transformer, it was found that the impedance transformer could by design be operated in a dual-mode. Operation in a dual-mode eliminated the need for a post matching network, thereby increasing the bandwidth and reducing circuit size [3]. An alternative to increasing the bandwidth of the Doherty Power Amplifier is to operate it over multiple bands rather than over a broad band. Broadband operation usually suffers from a reduced performance because you are not able to match the transistors over a broad band but only at certain frequencies [3]. A dual-band Doherty Power Amplifier [4] was proposed and implemented using the stub-loaded impedance transformer. With the dual function of matching and impedance transformation, a compact circuit was achieved.

11206820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206820.value: With existing 5G and upcoming 6G (2030), there is a need for ever increasing efficiency, linearity and bandwidth. The reason for this is the ever-increasing need for higher data rates, equating to either broader bandwidth or more efficiency signal modulation formats. Although more frequencies have been allocated for 5G and the soon to be 6G, there is always a need for more. In parallel more efficient signal formats such as M-QAM with ever increasing M, there requires an ever-increasing linearity requirement. This linearity requirement results in lower efficiency due to a large Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR). An alternative to the Doherty Topology is the Out-phasing power amplifier which was also investigated when looking into the two input Doherty topology [5]. The two-input Doherty topology was considered in this research work to reduce the effects of bandwidth due to the input. However, while looking at the two-input Doherty, it was fund that there was a lot of research work that could be done for the out-phasing topology as they share very similar characteristics. Not much work has been done on the out-phasing topology and is worth investigating due to their highly efficiency operation, albeit over a narrow band.

11206820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206820.value: The research work carried out here aims to improve the ever-increasing requirements for a given amplifier output power. These requirements include efficiency, linearity and low costs. In a mobile radio base station, the major consumer of power is the transmitter RF power amplifier. Higher efficiency equates to lower power consumption which is better for the environment and lowers operating costs. Linearity also affects efficiency, because if amplitude varying, but more efficient signal formats are used, a highly linear amplifier must be used. The problem is that the more linear an amplifier is, the less efficient it will be. For higher efficiency, a larger number of stages can be used but this results in increasing costs and the improved efficiency can sometimes be counter acted the increase in circuit loss due to the increase in size. Increase in size can also increase costs as well. Outcomes of the research work carried out here will increase linearity, efficiency and bandwidth for modern and future mobile radio base stations. This will make them more cost effective and because of the lower power consumption will help to improve the environment by reducing greenhouse gasses.

11207320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207320.value: Effective communication through text is critical for an information society. Written materials intended for the general public are supposed to be easily understood by the average reader, but that is often not the case. In principle, automatic readability assessment should be helpful in promoting the use of clear and plain language, but current readability models do not give sufficient feedback for this purpose. Their feedback typically consists of a single score, expressing the school grade or proficiency level needed for the reader to understand the document. This document-level score provides no guidance as to which sentences, and what aspects in these sentences, are difficult to understand. To address this need, this project aims to build a readability assessment system that works at the sentence level. Document-level readability models cannot be directly applied on sentences because they rely mostly on surface cues, such as lexical and syntactic features. While these features can provide reliable aggregate statistics on a document, they work less well on single sentences, which offer fewer cues for readability prediction. Accurate readability assessment on a sentence likely requires deeper semantic analysis to model its meaning and cohesion with the context. We propose a sentence-level readability assessment system that incorporates semantic features, and evaluate its performance on Chinese documents. We exploit a state-of-the-art Chinese semantic parser and database of semantic verb frames to build this system. This project will answer two research questions: (1) whether semantic modeling improves accuracy in readability prediction at the sentence level, and (2) whether it facilitates more efficient and effective text revision. Our findings will have implications on future design of readability models, as well as computer-assisted text revision and simplification systems. 閱讀並理解以自然語言文本為主要表達方式的資訊，對於知識社會來說尤為重要，可是不少文本過於複雜，令普通民眾難以理解。文本可讀性自動測評系統理應有助改善文本的易讀性，但由於現存系統提供的反饋，一般只以一個分數來評估文本的整體質素，所以不能具體指出文本裡哪一部分需要以更簡單和清晰的方法表達。 本項目旨在構建一個句子級的可讀性測評系統以解決上述問題。現存的文檔級可讀性模型綜合整編文本裡的語言模式來進行可讀性分析，在文檔層面上可達到甚高的準確度，但是由於單句中的詞彙和句法特徵比較少，模型不能直接應用於句子層面。為了提高句子級可讀性測評的準確度，系統須更深入地分析其語意複雜度和與上下文的銜接。 我們將運用一個高質量的中文語意解析系統，以及中文動詞詞彙語意網，建立一個能分析語意複雜度的句子級可讀性測評系統。本項目將探討語意分析能否在句子層面上提高可讀性分析的準確度，及能否幫助作者更快和更有效地修訂文本。本項目的研究成果將對可讀性模型、智慧文本編輯和文本簡化系統的設計作出貢獻。

11207320.label: Realisation of objectives
11207320.value: Objective (1): Improve readability assessment at the sentence level by incorporating semantic features to the readability model An Automatic Readability Assessment (ARA) model predicts how difficult it is for the reader to understand a text, by classifying the text at a grade level (Grade 1, 2, …, etc.). This project focuses on the use of ARA to predict the grade level of a sentence, with the goal of raising prediction accuracy by incorporating semantic features. We have achieved this goal with an innovative hybrid model that combines the strengths of linguistic features used in traditional ARA classifiers, and semantic information encoded in transformers, based on neural networks that have led to recent breakthroughs in natural langauge processing. This model achieved state-of-the-art accuracy on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) dataset. It also set the first sentence-level benchmark result on the OneStopEnglish (OSE) dataset and two newly created Chinese datasets. Our approach is summarized below, with details on the English experiments reported in Liu and Lee (2023) and Chinese experiments in Liu, Lee and Jin (under review) (both attached). Our study compared the performance of three ARA models: linguistic model, neural model and hybrid model. The linguistic model makes no use of semantic features. It is trained on XGBoost using 255 surface features, such as sentence length and part-of-speech frequencies, extracted from the input sentence with the LingFeat library. In contrast, the neural ARA model encodes semantic information of the input sentence through word embeddings from the transformer BART (Lewis et al., 2019). BART was selected because it yielded better performance on the development dataset than BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet and ELECTRA. Our implementation used the BART-large version provided by HuggingFace. The hybrid model takes advantage of both models by wrapping the linguistic features and neural model predictions in a statistical classifier. Our experiments evaluated the performance of these three models on the WSJ dataset (1,200 graded sentences) and OSE (19,904 graded sentences) datasets. The neural model improved over the linguistic model in all metrics (67.9% vs. 61.8% accuracy on WSJ; 57.1% vs. 45.1% on OSE). The hybrid model obtained the best accuracy of all models (72.9% on WSJ; 58.1% on OSE). For WSJ, the previous best result was 60.0%, obtained with an SVM model (Brunato et al., 2018). Notably, our hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 72.9%, surpasses the previous best result by almost 13%, demonstrating the impact of the semantic features. To facilitate evaluation in Chinese, we created two new sentence-level ARA datasets from Chinese pedagogical materials. The Chinese L1 Corpus consists of 9,700 sentences, taken from textbooks used in Mainland China and annotated by assessors with a background in linguistics. The Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages (TCSOL) corpus consists of 69,424 sentences, taken from teaching materials released by the Confucius Institute, and annotated by teaching assistants who are experienced TCSOL instructors. Evaluation on these two Chinese datasets also showed that the hybrid model outperformed the linguistic and neural models, with 49.3% accuracy on the Chinese L1 Corpus and 48.9% accuracy on the TCSOL corpus. In summary, experimental results in this project have shown that semantic features can raise the accuracy of readability assessment at the sentence level. Objective (2): Demonstrate that text revision is more efficient and effective when assisted by a sentence-level readability model with semantic features Text revision is necessary when the difficulty level of the text must be adjusted to accommodate the linguistic proficiency of the intended reader. Since our Automatic Readability Assessment (ARA) model can assess the difficulty of a sentence, it can potentially assist human editors in the text revision task. We have achieved this goal by leveraging our ARA model, which encodes semantic information from sentences using the BART transformer (see above), to predict which segments in the input text require modification. We summarize below the approach and results of our text revision experiment, with the details reported in Liu, Lim and Lee (under review) (attached). To facilitate quantitative evaluation, we created a text revision dataset by aligning the elementary, intermediate and advanced versions of the texts in the benchmark OneStopEnglish (OSE) dataset. The word alignments between two versions thus indicate the words that must be inserted, deleted or substituted to revise the text from one level to the other. We built a computer-assisted text revision system that takes an English text and the target difficulty level (elementary, intermediate or advanced) as input. The system first applies the ARA model, developed in Objective (1), to determine the gap between the current level of difficulty and the target level of difficulty. It then predicts the words or text spans that should be revised based on neural attention scores in the ARA model. Experimental results show that this approach yields an F1 score of 0.457, outperforming MICE (Minimal Contrastive Editing), a competitive model that predicts word changes that are needed to flip the model prediction to the target grade (0.380 F1 score). Further gains can be obtained with a pipeline that combines our ARA model with Large Language Models (LLMs) such as Llama-2 (Touvron et al., 2023), a leading open-source LLM. When fine-tuned on the OSE training set, Llama-2 achieves the best text revision result with an F1 score of 0.572.

11207320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207320.value: (1) Semantic features improve performance in Automatic Readability Assessment (ARA) models: Semantic features, such as those encoded in verb frames and transformers, can improve ARA accuracy (Cai, Lim, Lee & Liu, 2022; Liu and Lee, 2023; both attached). entence-level neural ARA models, which encode semantic information from the BART transformer, are shown to outperform models trained only on linguistic features. Hybrid models, which combine neural models and linguistic models, achieve additional gains in ARA performance. Further details on the hybrid model can be found in Section 5.3. (2) Ordinal classification improves performance in ARA models: ARA is an ordinal classification task since the predicted grade levels (Grade 1, 2, 3, …) follow an underlying order, from easy to difficult. However, most ARA models ignore the distance between the gold grade and predicted grade, treating all grades as independent labels. Our experiments show that ARA performance can be improved with ordinal regression and distance-sensitive loss functions. On both English and Chinese datasets, the soft labels proposed by Diaz and Marathe (2019) outperform the standard cross-entropy loss (Zeng, Xie, Yu, Lee and Zhou, 2022; attached). The ordinal log-loss function, proposed by Castagnos et al. (2022), leads to further improvement in adjacency accuracy (Lim and Lee, 2024; attached). (3) ARA facilitates text revision: Text revision is necessary when the text must be rewritten and simplified for less advanced readers. Computer-assisted text revision aims to predict the text segments that require modification. An ARA model can facilitate this goal by determining the gap between the current and target levels of difficulty. Experimental results on the benchmark OneStopEnglish dataset shows that ARA can improve upon competitive baselines by using neural attention scores to identify the most important words, and by leveraging the Llama-2 Large Language Model to perform revision (Liu, Lim and Lee, under review; attached). Further, a user study shows that participants are able to perform text revision effectively with our ARA model through a browser-based interface (Lim, Lee and Liu, 2024; attached).

11207320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207320.value: This research project could be extended in several directions. First, the effectiveness of semantic features can be confirmed using other datasets with a wider range of languages beyond English and Chinese. Experiments on low-resource languages might yield especially insightful results, as the ARA models would need to rely on less training data. Second, the recent advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened up new avenues for text difficulty assessment. While they can already lead to improvements in text revision in our experiments (Liu, Lim and Lee, under review), preliminary evaluations on GPT-4 suggest that they do not yet perform as well as our neural ARA model (Liu, Lee, and Jin, under review). Further research on prompt engineering and fine-tuning algorithms would be worthwhile to fully exploit LLMs in text difficulty assessment. Third, further opportunities for knowledge transfer and commercialization of ARA, especially in the education sector, should be explored. Given sufficient computing power, a software product offering efficient and robust ARA and text revision could be developed to assist language teachers in the preparation of pedagogical material and review of high-stakes assessment materials, and to support general users in text editing tasks.

11207320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207320.value: Automatic readability assessment (ARA) aims to determine how difficulty it is for readers to comprehend a text. Many applications in natural language processing, such as text revision and language exercise generation, require assessment of the difficulty of individual sentences. Even so, ARA has traditionally been performed at the passage level, with less attention paid to ARA at the sentence level. This project has investigated ARA models that leverage semantic features, and in particular neural models that encode semantic information of a sentence in word embeddings. Experimental results have shown that hybrid models, which combines the strengths of semantic and linguistic features, yield the best performance on both English and Chinese sentences, and can assist humans in performing text revision. Notably, the best hybrid model achieved state-of-the-art results on a dataset of sentences from the Wall Street Journal, surpassing the previous best result by almost 13%. These new insights into sentence-level ARA have set new benchmarks for the research community, and can help inform future design of readability assessment models.

11207620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207620.value: 大腦受傷或退化可以導致終身殘疾。在美國，每年大約有17,00人患上脊髓損傷(SCI)，而全球大約有2700萬盛行的SCI病例。對於創傷性的腦損傷，全世界有超過200萬宗病例嚴重到需要住院甚至造成死亡。無法再生受損的神經軸突和重建中樞神經系統內的神經連接，是創傷或疾病後導致永久性殘疾的主要原因。因此，目前有迫切需要開發一種可以完全逆轉對神經系統損害的治療方法。數百萬人可以從新穎，創新的治療方法中受益，並減輕腦損傷的痛苦。 我們建議開發具有已設計地形和可以精確控制導向信號的二維和三維平台，以通過它們與圖案化表面的相互作用來促進神經生長。可以期望神經元不僅在水平面，還會在垂直方向被引導作單向生長。這將是第一個在工程化二維和三維平台中通過精確控制物理地形和圖案化學塗層來控制單向神經生長的論證。 我們將開發具有不同尺寸和佈局的導向圖案，以促進海馬神經元的生長。為了提供有效的導向，尺寸將圍繞細胞，軸突和樹突的大小來設計。較小的尺寸和密集的圖案有望促進更好的神經突排列和生長，但它們可能會限制神經突分支或形成完整的神經突網絡。神經導向信號的有效性將在物理地形，化學圖案和微通道三方面之間比較，以測試物理步驟，化學吸引劑和軸突限制的重要性。我們將研究導向圖案以不同彎曲角度和曲率的影響，以了解表面接觸面積和急劇彎曲時神經突生長的競爭因素。 已設計的圖案將通過三個原理用於促進單向神經突的生長：導向圖案的不對稱性，不連續的圖案和密度變化的圖案。我們還將研究如何利用導向信號促進功能性神經聯繫的形成。通過將神經導向圖案放置在關鍵位置，可以預期將增強神經連接性，及可以控制神經元在三維平台中沿垂直方向生長。這不僅在水平面還能在垂直方向上控制神經生長方向的獨特功能，可以為神經連接和再生提供重要的見解。

11208220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208220.value: 热舒适性是室内健康的一个重要方面，对使用者的健康和生产率有着重要的影响。空调系统被广泛用于提供舒适的室内环境，但在建筑中能耗最高（约50%）。为了减少能消，人们提出了数种垂直不均匀送风方式（置换通风、分层通风和层式通风）。垂直非均匀送风方式注重工作区的热舒适性，节省用于调节上部无人区的能耗。然而，有两个问题限制了它们在共享房间中的热舒适性和节能：（1）热状况的水平不均匀性；（2）居住者的不同热偏好。 传统上认为工作区的热环境在水平方向上是均匀的，为了保证热舒适，工作区的平均热状况必须控制在一定范围内。然而，热状况不可避免地是不均匀的。传统的方法忽略了水平方向的不均匀性，这在很大程度上导致了热不舒适投诉和低能效。 另一个问题是，虽然使用者的热偏好天生是不同的，但使用者通常被当作典型人，他们的热偏好被设定为相同的。由于典型人的热偏好并不能代表实际使用者的热偏好，传统的方法无法有效地反映对热舒适性的实际需求。 考虑到热环境的水平不均匀性和使用者不同的热偏好，提出了将热环境状态与热偏好耦合以提高热舒适性的新思路。耦合运行的策略为：（1）将占用区域水平划分为多个子区域，（2）指示偏好凉环境的居住者坐在凉的子区域中，（3）控制子区域的热状况以最大程度地满足热偏好。根据热适应理论，使用者在热舒适性管理中起着积极的作用。当被告知房间的热状况概况（即，从凉到暖分区的热状况排序），居住者倾向于本能地选择热条件与他们的热偏好一致的分区，以得到热舒适。因此，该耦合运行策略创新性地利用了热环境的水平不均匀性和使用者在热舒适管理中的积极作用来提高热舒适性。通过改善热舒适性，还可以减少不必要的冷却以提高能效。 开发耦合运行策略的核心任务有三个：（1）开发一个耦合热状态和热偏好的控制算法；（2）描述不同运行条件下的鲁棒热状态；（3）优化分区，考虑热状况与居住者热偏好的匹配程度。耦合操作策略将在我们独特的环境舱中进行验证，该环境舱可方便地实现办公室和教室的不同气流组织（例如，层式通风和置换通风）的实验。并将编制一套指南，以应用热舒适和节能的耦合运行策略。

11208220.label: Realisation of objectives
11208220.value: The project was completed in six phases within three and a half years as follows: 1. Supplemental literature search. 2. Data collection and model development. Objective data and CFD simulations were used to establish the models of the horizontal non-uniform thermal conditions in the occupied zone as a function of supply and exit air parameters using the method developed in our preliminary studies. Individuals’ thermal preferences were investigated to develop the models of occupants’ thermal preferences and derive the statistical distribution of the occupants’ thermal preferences using the existing methods. 3. Development and verification of a control algorithm for the coupled operation strategy. 4. Development and verification of a method for robustly characterizing air distribution. 5. Development and verification of a method for optimizing the division of subzones. 6. Reporting of research outcomes. The deliverables include, but are not limited to, high-quality publications.

11208220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208220.value: This project innovatively proposes and verifies a coupled operation strategy to utilize the horizontal non-uniformity of the thermal condition and the active role of occupants in thermal comfort management to cater for differentiated thermal preferences. With the improved satisfaction of thermal preferences, the overcooling is minimized, and the energy efficiency is improved. Specifically, this project has: 1. developed a control algorithm coupling the thermal condition profile and thermal preferences to maximize the satisfaction of thermal preferences; 2. developed a method for characterizing thermal conditions robustly under different operation conditions; 3. optimized the division of subzones considering the coupling level between the thermal condition profile and occupants’ thermal preferences; 4. produced nine high-quality SCI journal publications.

11208220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208220.value: High airborne contaminant concentration in inhaled air may occur because of the non-uniformity of air distribution. In contrast, this proposal attempts to take advantage of the non-uniformity in air distribution to reduce airborne infection risk effectively by developing a proper operation strategy. Therefore, the new air distribution delivers clean air to the breathing zone, particularly to the critical area, to reduce the amount of airborne contaminants inhaled by susceptibles to minimize airborne infection risk. To develop such an operation, three challenges have to be overcome. Firstly, how to evaluate the airborne infection risk with a spatial resolution? A dilution-based method can be developed. Secondly, how to obtain the contaminant concentration produced by infectors in the breathing zone of susceptibles? A method will be developed to infer the quantity of airborne contaminant exhaled by infectors. Thirdly, how to determine the operation of air distribution robustly? In a shared room, the numbers and positions of asymptomatic infectors are uncertain. To solve this problem, a simulation-based method will be developed. The health crisis has ended because newly developed vaccines prove effective. Nevertheless, a lesson taught by COVID-19 is that engineering solutions must always be in place for unknown enemies.

11208220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208220.value: Thermal conditions are inevitably non-uniform. Conventional methods overlook horizontal non-uniformity, which largely contributes to thermal discomfort complaints and low energy efficiency in practice. Another issue is that the thermal preference of a typical person cannot represent the actual occupants; conventional methods fail to effectively track the actual demand for thermal comfort. The novel idea of coupling room thermal condition profiles and occupants’ thermal preferences to improve thermal comfort originated. The proposed coupled operation strategy (1) divides an occupied zone into subzones horizontally, (2) instructs occupants preferring cool/warm conditions to sit in cool/warm subzones, and (3) controls the thermal conditions of the subzones to maximize the satisfaction of thermal preferences. Therefore, the coupled operation strategy innovatively takes advantage of both the horizontal thermal non-uniformity and the occupants’ active role to improve thermal comfort. With improved thermal comfort, energy efficiency can also be improved by reducing unnecessary cooling. There were three core tasks in developing the coupled operation strategy: (1) developing a control algorithm that couples thermal condition profiles and thermal preferences; (2) characterizing robustly thermal conditions under different operation conditions; and (3) optimizing the division of subzones considering how well the thermal condition profile matches occupants’ thermal preferences.

11209520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209520.value: The wide area network (WAN) is a crucial infrastructure for many cloud service provides as it carries traffic for numerous online applications and services at a global scale. These WANs are typically software defined with a logically centralized controller taking charge. Traffic engineering (TE) is a critical and difficult problem in these SD-WANs that involves assigning traffic with various requirements to paths with different constraints. Recently, deep learning (DL) algorithms are applied to TE, yet they all assume that the network is a black box, limiting them to model-free reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms with many issues. We therefore ask, why are we stuck with RL for TE? Can we find a way to enable the rapid advance in many other DL models to be adopted for TE? This project presents a holistic effort to address this fundamental question. We show that the SD-WAN network environment can be sufficiently modeled for TE, and design a fully- differentiable network environment, ∂NE, that can be directly integrated into any DL models. With ∂NE, we can differentiate with respect to control parameters, and directly evaluate gradients between actions and states to facilitate gradient descent based training. We show with a proof-of-concept prototype that ∂NE accelerates DL training for TE by 228× and achieves higher scalability compared to existing network simulators. Based on ∂NE, we also propose to develop novel DL-based TE algorithms beyond RL. As a concrete example, we examine a new TE scheme based on LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory), and preliminary experiments on our ∂NE prototype show that it achieves 7.0% higher throughput and 89.9% lower congestion loss than state-of-the-art RL-based TE. Finally, we plan to investigate the explainability of DL-based TE, and better understand how DL helps TE in a principled way. TE in SD-WANs is an important research area with eminent practical value, and DL promises huge potential for online control problems like TE. Our project opens up the possibility to apply arbitrary DL models to TE beyond RL. To maximize the impact, we plan to implement ∂NE and our DL-based TE algorithms in popular machine learning frameworks like PyTorch and Tensorflow and open source them. We are working with Tencent to experiment ∂NE using their production network and traffic information, and we plan to collaborate with other cloud operators in order to propel the transfer of our research results to production systems. 广域网（WAN）是许多云服务当中的关键基础架构，承载着全球范围内众多在线应用程序和服务的流量。这些WAN通常是由软件定义的，通过一个逻辑上的集中控制器进行控制。在这些SD-WAN中，流量工程（TE）是一个关键且困难的问题，涉及将具有各种需求的流量分配给具有不同约束的路径。近年来，深度学习（DL）算法已开始应用于TE，但它们都假定网络是黑匣子，因此被限制在无模型的强化学习（RL）算法，但这存在许多问题。 我们问，为什么坚持使用RL for TE？我们是否可以找到一种方法来使其他DL模型和他们的众多成果能够被应用到TE上？ 该项目提出了解决这一基本问题的整体方案。我们发现，可以针对SD-WAN网络对TE进行充分建模，并设计一个完全可微分的网络环境∂NE，该环境可以直接集成到任何DL模型中。利用∂NE，我们可以区分控制参数，并直接评估TE动作和网络状态之间的梯度，以促进基于梯度下降的训练。我们的实验原型证明，与现有的网络模拟器相比，∂NE可以将TE的DL训练速度提高228倍，并具有更高的可扩展性。基于∂NE，我们还建议开发新颖的基于DL的RL以外的TE算法。作为一个具体的例子，我们研究了一种基于LSTM的新TE方案，并且在我们的∂NE原型上进行的初步实验表明，与基于RL的TE相比，它的吞吐量提高了7.0％，拥塞损失降低了89.9％。最后，我们计划研究基于DL的TE的可解释性，并更好地理解DL如何以有原则的方式帮助TE。 SD-WAN中的TE是具有重要实用价值的研究领域，而DL有望为TE等在线控制问题提供巨大潜力。我们的项目为在TE上应用RL以外的任意DL模型提供了可能性。为了扩大影响力，我们计划在流行的机器学习框架（如PyTorch和Tensorflow）中实现∂NE和基于DL的TE算法，并将其开源。我们正在与腾讯合作，利用他们的生产网络和交通信息进行试验，并且我们计划与其他云运营商合作，以推动我们的研究成果向生产系统的转移。

11209620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209620.value: The construction industry is a labor-intensive industry that recruits the majority of manual workers in Hong Kong. Owing to its large employee population and reliance on manual operation, nearly one fourth of all workplace injuries and fatalities occur in the construction industry. Many studies reported that more than 70% of these accidents are related to human activities. However, it is extremely difficult to improve on-site safety due to the dynamic nature of the construction working environment and the unpredictable behavior of workers. Previously, researchers developed various technologies that focus on identifying site hazards and providing protective equipment such as radio-frequency identification for labor positioning, RGB-D cameras for labor activity detection, and biological sensors for labor monitoring. However, many studies reported that the major source of on-site accidents is the subjective unsafe behavior due to workers’ lack of sense of danger. Conventionally, the most widespread approach to raising workers’ sense of danger has been conducting safety training programs. Although researchers proposed the concept of safety culture to enforce on-site regulations and safety codes, the efficacy and validity of different safety programs are seldom examined and unsafe behavior has been constantly observed, as there is no objective and convincing approach to evaluate the performance of these safety programs. This proposed research aims to develop a novel Perceived Risks Extended (PRE) safety program development framework to utilize quantitative perceived risks to assess safety programs and improve the efficiency of program modules. According to findings of previous research, the mismatch between the actual site risks and workers’ perceived risks is the main cause of unsafe behavior. Therefore, this research intends to (1) develop quantitative methods to assess the perceived risks using the Hybrid Kinematic-Electroencephalography (EEG) sensing method, (2) investigate and reveal the inter-relationship between perceived risks and unsafe behavior, (3) propose a PRE safety assessment to evaluate the efficacy and efficiency of safety programs. This proposed research will reveal the mechanism of on-site unsafe behavior and provide an effective tool to evaluate current safety programs. Using the proposed framework, construction and safety managers will able to develop effective and responsive safety programs or supplement existing programs to further improve project safety. In turn, this will secure the safety and health of construction workers, avoid losses due to injuries and fatalities, and reduce the costs of ineffective safety training or regulation. 11209620.label: Realisation of objectives
11209620.value: Our research has successfully achieved the three objectives addressed above. Based on the research outcomes, our research team has published four journal papers. In recent decades, the complexity of construction tasks has posed significant concerns and challenges to worker behavior and safety performance. These tasks involve intensive physical movements, uncertainty, and unorganized manual judgments. While researchers have made efforts to study efficient worker management, decipher safety causes, and employ emerging technologies, recognizing worker actions and implementing automatic action recognition algorithms remain essential for minimizing safety risks and improving outcomes. Traditional research approaches are no longer adequate for monitoring worker actions due to their time-consuming nature. However, advancements in computer vision technology, vision-based cameras, and wearable devices have made it possible to automate tasks that were previously challenging for the workforce. This development has the potential to enhance worker safety management and production efficiency. This research focuses on developing an automated monitoring and identification framework for on-site construction workers based on deep learning algorithms. The main research areas are as follows: 1) Developing an enormous and heterogeneous dataset for generic motion and artificially intelligent models is necessary. As we know, many researchers have developed public three-dimension (3D) human skeletons for automated postures and activity recognition. However, the construction-related motion dataset and labels should be specifically designed, as construction workers are often exposed to awkward postures and intensive physical tasks. Therefore, this study first developed a small construction-related activity dataset with an in-lab experiment and implemented some alignment strategies to unify the public datasets and manually label a large-scale construction motion data library (CML) for activity recognition. The developed CML dataset contains 225 types of activities and 146,480 samples; among them, 60 types of activities and 61,275 samples are highly related to construction activities. To verify the dataset, five widely applied deep learning algorithms were adopted to examine the dataset, and usability, quality, and sufficiency were reported. 2) In recent years, the skeleton-based ergonomics model has been widely studied and implemented. Most of these models rely on the 3D coordinates of body joints. To supplement these studies and extract more comprehensive features, this study examined seven high-level geometric features based on joints, lines, and planes to find an effective geometric feature for action recognition. To accommodate these features, this study also proposed a spatial-temporal soft attention mechanism based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model and the spatial-temporal attention mechanism with residual units enhanced LSTM (STA-Res-LSTM) for more flexible action recognition based on the second chapter proposed CML dataset. 3) Recently, graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have been used to recognize skeleton-based human actions and achieved remarkable performance. However, for most existing GCN-based models, the graph is fixed and constructed relying on the human body’s physical connections. It is unsuitable for recognizing complex construction tasks because construction tasks usually rely heavily on hands, and it could be completed by moving a specific part of the human body. Thus, this study divided the human body into different parts and designed different level topology graphs based on body-segment strategies. Meanwhile, a multiple-input streams attention (MISA) network is proposed to improve existing algorithms and extend the body-structure topology graph of GCNs with richer input graphs. Two-modality motion data and three attention blocks are introduced to capture more discriminative characteristics. 4) Introducing a lightweight activity recognition framework that focuses on simplified key joints of the skeleton and utilizes the stacked Temporal Convolution Network (TCN) model is worth studying. This framework aims to improve the effectiveness of workforce action assessment while reducing computational resources. Performance evaluations are conducted using different feature combinations and low sample frequency situations. Overall, recognizing construction workers' activities is crucial for improving project task allocation and enhancing workers' career health. Exploring the impact of deep learning frameworks on skeleton-based automatic recognition techniques is essential for ensuring the safety and productivity of the human workforce. As human skeleton information extraction and processing tools spread in the construction field, automatic recognition techniques hold great potential and desirability for construction sites in the future.

11209620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209620.value: Construction Motion Data Library: Further development could involve expanding the dataset to include more diverse activities and environmental contexts, enhancing its applicability across different construction scenarios. Multi-Stream Fusion Network: Future work might explore incorporating additional data streams (e.g., environmental or contextual data) and optimizing the model for real-time, on-site use. Handling complex interactions, such as multiple workers or occlusions, could also be a key area for improvement. MISA Network: Enhancements could focus on refining the attention mechanisms to better capture subtle movements and adapting the model to various construction tasks. Integrating the model with wearable tech or edge computing devices could improve real-world applicability. Lightweight Deep Learning Framework: Further development could aim at optimizing the framework for low-power devices and expanding its capabilities to recognize a broader range of activities. Developing adaptive algorithms that can quickly learn from new data would increase the system's flexibility in dynamic construction environments.

11209620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209620.value: This research tackles the challenge of keeping construction workers safe on the job, especially as tasks become more complex. Traditionally, monitoring worker actions was slow and inefficient. However, new technologies like computer vision, cameras, and wearable devices can now automate this process. The study focuses on creating a system that uses deep learning (a type of artificial intelligence) to automatically monitor and recognize what construction workers are doing. The researchers built a large dataset of construction-related movements, including 225 types of activities, to train AI models. They tested these models to ensure they could accurately recognize and assess worker actions. To make these models even better, the study looked at new ways to analyze body movements and developed advanced algorithms to recognize specific actions based on how different parts of the body move. They also introduced a simpler, more efficient system that uses fewer data points to reduce the need for powerful computers. Overall, this research aims to make construction sites safer and more efficient by automatically monitoring workers' activities using cutting-edge AI technologies.
