11210020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210020.value: Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials recently have shown great promise for applications in stress visualization, lighting, and optical signaling. However, current trigger modes of ML need either destructive action (fracture) or high mechanic load (up to order of 10^3 N). The rising demands for flexible device with stress sensing and colour display characteristics have brought up attentions on ML materials which are capable of emitting light in an elastomeric framework, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The existing elastomer-based ML composites mainly employ transition metal doped sulfides as luminescent component, which limits the range of available ML colors. Here, we propose to develop a series of elastomer composites containing lanthanide ions (Ln3+) doped semiconductor compounds for performing mechanically activated multicolor light emission. The diverse 4f-4f electronic transitions of Ln3+ endow a library of emitting spectra spanning ultraviolet to near infrared. Al2O3 layer will be coated on the microcrystal surface to assist effective stress transfer from matrix to the doped crystal by virtue of intimate adhesion between Al2O3 and siloxane matrix. Moreover, we intend to investigate the detailed physical origins of ML through experimental investigation and theoretical prediction. These crystals with carefully designed composition and microstructure may inspire new research interests in ML field and fascinate researchers from different application areas. 力致发光材料能够在外力作用下，不需要借助电、光等额外激发产生肉眼可见的发光。这类独特的光学性质在照明、显示、以及光学传感等方向具有巨大的应用潜力。现有力致发光材料的常见问题是激发阈值高、发光颜色有限、可处理性差等，这些问题在一定程度上阻碍了力致发光的实际应用。本项目拟通过合理选择材料组分、并优化合成方法以期制备一类稀土掺杂的CaZnOS微晶颗粒，以期在较低外力作用下产生多色的明亮力致发光。我们的目标是控制较小的晶粒尺寸，并在表面包覆Al2O3涂层以提高其对外力的响应，同时利用Al2O3与高分子材料的较好亲和力来实现高性能复合应力发光薄膜材料的构建。基于这些材料体系，我们亦计划仔细研究力致发光过程中的一些机理问题。

11210020.label: Realisation of objectives
11210020.value: This project aims to expand the toolbox of mechanoluminescence (ML) materials by developing novel lanthanide-doped ML phosphors and elastomer composites. Based on the newly developed ML materials, we want to gain insights into the ML mechanism and expand the range of applications for ML. We have achieved these objectives through the following deliverables. 1. We have established a doping strategy, which allows precise control over nanocrystal size and promotes the formation of pure-phase crystals in chemical synthesis. We also develop a two-step synthetic procedure for preparing small-sized ML crystals while maintaining high ML performance. Our investigation may raise vast possibilities for constructing high-quality luminescent materials for advanced photonic applications. At the same time, our insights into the chemical reactions are expected to facilitate the future synthesis of complex inorganic crystals. 2. We have achieved uniform coating of Al2O3 on ML phosphors by sol-gel processing and atomic layer deposition (ALD) technique. We also have developed methods to coat inorganic and organic silicon layers on phosphors. These achievements allow us to control the interfacing between ML phosphor and polymer substrates, thus enabling systematic study of the luminescence mechanism and maximizing ML performance in practical applications. 3. We have devised a homemade instrument to quantify the ML performance, which utilizes a linear motor and a pressure gauge to provide quantitative mechanical excitation to the system. The instrument allows us to characterize the ML properties comparatively at prescribed conditions (e.g., different magnitudes of force, in the presence of light and heat stimulations) with high repeatability. Accordingly, we have confirmed the self-reproducible nature of lanthanide- and Cr-doped ML materials. 4. We have constructed several types of ML composites by integrating ML phosphors into capillary tubes, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrates, polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films, and mouthguards. These ML composites can emit visible and near-infrared light by diverse mechanical excitations, including stirring, scratching, rubbing, and biting. 5. We have integrated SrZnOSe:Nd crystals developed in this project into a mouthguard for light generation by the bite force of teeth. We show that the transmission of complex information could be achieved by biting in prescribed patterns. For example, the NIR signals generated by the molars and incisors in the human oral cavity could be resolved to encode different photonic information,

11210020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210020.value: We have identified the important role of ionic doping in controlling crystal formation and growth. Specifically, we find that Ce doping can lead to precise size control in CaS nanocrystals synthesized at otherwise identical conditions. In addition, we find that Ca doping in the Sr-Zn-O-Se system can promote the formation of pure-phase SrZnOSe by eliminating the SrSe and ZnO byproducts. These results, published in Chemistry of Materials (2022, 34, 7799) and Advanced Materials (2024, doi: 10.1002/adma.202406899), significantly enhance our ability to prepare novel luminescent materials for advanced photonic applications. In addition to altering crystal growth habits, we find that lanthanide doping can be used to fine-tune the ML spectra of Cr ions in Ga2O3 host by local crystal structure modification. In particular, Yb dopants can simultaneously tune Cr emissions and introduce additional emission band, giving rise to a record large full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 267 nm. Using the ML phosphors as light sources, we establish a self-powered technique for nondestructive detection and stress visualization. These findings are published in Matter (2023, 6, 1393). We find that the ML phosphors can be encapsulated in transparent polymer films to generate emissions under sliding force, which allows us to quantitively characterize the ML property and reveal the luminescence mechanism. Particularly, we confirm the self-recovery nature of ML through elastic deformation in these ML phosphors. In addition, we find that the ML phosphors can be integrated into capillary tubes and mouthguards for light generation by magnetic fields and bite forth of teeth (Advanced Functional Materials 2021, 31, 2006357). These findings are expected to expand the range of applications for ML materials. Due to our innovative and systematical works in this field, we have been invited to summarize our findings and provide perspectives in a number of review papers, which include 1) Expanding the Toolbox of Inorganic Mechanoluminescence Materials (Acc. Mater. Res. 2021, 2, 364); 2) Controlling X-Ray Activated Persistent Luminescence for Emerging Applications (Trends Chem. 2022, 4, 726.); 3) Recent advances in cellular optogenetics for photomedicine (Adv. Drug Deliv. Rev. 2022, 188, 114457); 4) Emerging Halide Perovskite Ferroelectrics (Adv. Mater. 2023, 35, 2205410).

11210020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210020.value: The doping-mediated synthetic methodology developed in this project can be extended to prepare complex inorganic crystals that are difficult to form under normal reaction conditions. Besides, the newly developed material systems can be used to explore other optical properties, such as persistent luminescence and electroluminescence.

11210020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210020.value: Mechanoluminescence (ML) is characterized by photon emission in response to mechanical stimulus. As mechanical stimuli are ubiquitous, ML materials have recently shown great promise for applications in stress visualization, lighting, and optical signaling. Nevertheless, the lack of efficient ML materials has constrained the progress of utilizing the fantastic ML process. In this regard, we have developed several new ML materials and explored the relevant ML mechanism and their potential applications in absorption spectroscopy, information technology, and biomedicine. During the course of our investigation, we have established advanced synthetic protocols for preparing complex inorganic crystals with extended control over the crystal size. Based on these new crystal systems, we have achieved tunable ML spanning the visible and near-infrared spectrum with enhanced emission intensity. Overall, our findings provide both the theoretical basis and practical guidance to construct ML phosphors for applications in nondestructive detection, information security, optogenetics, and beyond.

11210920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210920.value: Nucleate boiling is one of most effective methods for transferring large amounts of heat by liquid-vapor phase change process. It has widespread applications in high heat flux dissipation and thermal management devices. Therefore, to improve overall heat transfer performance, the increase in both critical heat flux (CHF) and heat transfer coefficient (HTC) is required. The aim of this work is to devise a control mechanism in which CHF and HTC can be enhanced and tuned on demand and independently of surface modifications, and therefore the same boiling system could be used for the high heat flux dissipation and the thermal management applications. A great deal of work has been done showing the enhancement in HTC when surfactants are added into working fluids. This enhancement is often associated with two mechanisms; change in surface tension due to surfactant adsorption to liquid-vapor interface and change in surface wettability due to surfactant adsorption to liquid-solid interface (heater surface). Recently, a significant enhancement in boiling heat transfer performance of an order of magnitude was observed when a small electric potential (~1V) was used in addition to surfactant. However, only few studies have considered the surface roughness effects for surfactant solutions and those were limited to just random roughness and without electric field. As for the CHF, many studies have proved a significant enhancement when micro/nano textured surfaces are used. This enhancement is often attributed to parameters such as roughness, wettability and wicking behavior but is still not completely understood. Therefore, it is encouraging to combine the nucleate boiling on micro/nano textured surfaces with the surfactants and the electric field in order to further enhance and control the boiling heat transfer performance. First, nucleate boiling without electric field on micro/nano textured surfaces for different roughness values and surfactants types will be investigated. Secondly, a small electric field in combination with surfactant will be introduced to control the surface wettability, and thus the heat transfer enhancement. The usage of electric field and surfactants will allow changing surface wettability without affecting surface tension of the bulk fluid and independently of surface roughness, which will also help understanding the basic mechanism of CHF enhancement. Besides, to check the long-term working of boiling process, boiling system robustness and durability over long time-periods will be investigated also. Finally, to get deep insight of surfactant effects on bubble dynamics, numerical simulations using lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) method will be conducted. 核態沸騰是通過液-汽相變過程傳遞大量熱量的最有效方法之一。它在高熱流密度散熱和熱管理設備中具有廣泛的應用。因此，為了提高整體的傳熱性能，需要增加臨界熱流密度（CHF）和傳熱係數（HTC）。 這項工作的目的是設計一種控制機制，其中CHF和HTC可以根據需要進行增強和調整，而與表面特性無關，因此可以將同一沸騰系統用於高熱流消散和熱管理應用中。大量的工作表明當將表面活性劑添加到工作液中時，HTC可以顯著增強。這種增強通常與兩種機制相關聯：由於表面活性劑吸附到液-氣界面而引起的表面張力的變化和由於表面活性劑吸附於液-固界面（加熱器表面）而引起的表面潤濕性的變化。近來，當除了表面活性劑之外還疊加低的電場（〜1V）時，觀察到沸騰傳熱性能顯著提高了一個數量級。但是，只有很少的研究考慮了表面粗糙度對表面活性劑溶液的影響，而這些影響僅限於隨機粗糙度而沒有電場。至於CHF，許多研究已證明，使用微/納米紋理表面可以顯著提高CHF。這種增強通常歸因於諸如粗糙度，潤濕性和芯吸行為之類的參數，但仍未完全理解。 因此，本研究將把微/納米織構表面上的核態沸騰與表面活性劑和電場結合，以進一步增強和控制沸騰傳熱性能。首先，將研究不同粗糙度值和表面活性劑類型在微米/納米紋理表面上沒有電場的核沸騰。其次，將引入與表面活性劑結合的小電場以控製表面潤濕性，從而增強傳熱。電場和表面活性劑的使用將使表面潤濕性發生變化，而不會影響主體流體的表面張力，並且與表面粗糙度無關，這也將有助於理解CHF增強的基本機理。此外，為了檢驗沸騰過程的長期工作情況，還將研究沸騰系統在長時間內的堅固性和耐用性。最後，為了深入了解表面活性劑對氣泡動力學的影響，將進行使用格子Boltzmann方法（LBM）的數值模擬。

11210920.label: Realisation of objectives
11210920.value: Experiments and numerical simulations are extensively conducted on the research objectives. All the three research objectives are fully achieved. 1. The research activities to achieve objectives 1 are summarized as below: Extensive experimental studies have been carried out to investigate the boiling performance of surfactant aqueous solutions on micro/nano surfaces. Firstly, the separate effect of surfactant aqueous solution on the critical heat flux (CHF) was studied. The possible mechanisms of surfactant effects proposed in the literature were revisited. Combined with the experimental study, it was found that when the surfactant concentration is low, its influence on the physical properties of the solution, including equilibrium surface tension, dynamic surface tension, and viscosity, is very limited. But the boiling performance has changed significantly. The change of physical properties of the solution by surfactant is not sufficient to fully explain the change in boiling performance at low concentrations. Surfactant molecules are adsorbed on the vapor-water surface, making it immobile and difficult to deform, changing the local hydrodynamic characteristics. This is the underlying reason why it is difficult for bubbles to coalesce in surfactant aqueous solutions. This influence can be effective even though the surfactant concentration is very low. At low heat flux and low concentration, the boiling heat transfer coefficient (HTC) gain of surfactant aqueous solution is mainly related to the inability of bubbles to coalesce on the wall. There will be a far-wall hydrodynamics effect that surfactants can have on CHF. Even if the concentration is very low, it can have an influence that cannot be ignored. This mainly includes two reasons: First, the difficulty of coalescence of bubbles causes the formation of wet foam at a high heat flux, which blocks the wetting of the heating surface by the bulk water. The decrease of CHF caused by the formation of wet foam is also consistent with the predicted results of the percolation CHF model. Second, the immobility of the surface increases the flow resistance of the vapor as it leaves the surface, reducing the vapor removal velocity. Then the combined effect of micro/nano textured surface and surfactants was studied experimentally. The findings underscored that while utilizing a micro-pillared surface can markedly amplify the CHF by the wicking effect. The micro-pillar allows the liquid to spread rapidly across the surface, which in turn inhibits the expansion of dry spots on the surface during boiling crises. Even though most of the surface is covered by vapor, a small portion of the surface exposed to water is still able to provide wetting for the entire surface. In comparison to the smooth surface, the pool boiling experiments conducted in deionized water with a micro-pillared surface demonstrated a maximum enhancement in CHF of 119% and a maximum enhancement in HTC of 59%. However, introducing a surfactant diminishes this enhancement. On separate effect studies on surfactant, it has been found that wet foam produced by surfactant can reduce CHF near boiling crisis. When surfactants are added, the wickability benefits of the pillared surface for CHF enhancement are masked because wicking flow is completely blocked by the wet foam on the outside. At the same vapor content, the volume of wet foam is larger than that of large vapor slug, and it is easier to cover the whole surface without leaving a channel for wetting flow. 2. The research activities to achieve objectives 2 are summarized as below: Experiments were carried out to study the combined effect of surfactants and electric field. The results show that when the electric field is applied, the surfactant molecules move directionally and adsorb to the boiling surface, which reduces the energy required for the bubble nucleation, and thus makes the onset of nucleate boiling occur at a much lower wall superheat degree. This greatly improves the boiling heat transfer coefficient at low wall temperature. By controlling the electric field, the adsorption of surfactants on the wall can be controlled and the wettability of the wall can be regulated. However, near the boiling crisis, there is a large amount of steam on the wall. Since the insulation of the vapor is much better than that of the surfactant aqueous solution, the electric field is largely shielded, and its effect is greatly weakened. Moreover, the wall wettability is not the only factor that determines the CHF. Because an aqueous surfactant solution is used, the bubbles produced by boiling are difficult to merge and form a wet foam covering the wall. This wet foam does not leave as quickly as a large vapor slug formed by a merge of bubbles. It prevents the outside water from flowing in and wetting the walls, causing the boiling crisis to arrive earlier. The CHF deterioration caused by the surfactants covers up the CHF enhancement caused by wall wettability, so the overall CHF still shows a decreasing trend. Since boiling is accompanied by rapid evaporation of water, the solubility of surfactants in water is limited and they are inevitably deposited on the surface during the boiling process. This deposition transformed initially smooth surfaces into roughened surfaces. Post-experiment analysis using the optical surface profiler and digital microscope revealed that a substantial portion of the micro-pillars became unobservable due to the deposition effects. Similar to the deposition of surfactants, oxidative corrosion caused by electrolysis can also destroy the artificial micro structure on the surface. Both the deposition of surfactants and the corrosion caused by electrolysis can destroy the original artificial microstructures, which poses a challenge for long-term applications. 3. The research activities to achieve objectives 3 are summarized as below: Significant numerical simulations have been conducted for the research objectives 3 listed above. In this work, the effects of surface wettability change with time alternately between the hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity, inspired from electric field and surfactants-based surface wettability tuning, are investigated over a rough surface using lattice Boltzmann method. The results show that rough surface with alternating wettability (wettability changes with time alternately between the hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity) significantly improves boiling heat transfer performance. The contact line dynamics show that bubble expands rapidly during the hydrophobic time and when wettability switches from the hydrophobic to hydrophilic, it induces a much faster contact line retraction even higher than uniformly hydrophobic surface and uniformly hydrophilic surface. This faster contact retraction process helps to disintegrate the vapor film and rewets the surface at higher wall superheats and as a result higher critical heat flux (CHF) is observed for the surface with alternating wettability than uniformly hydrophobic and uniformly hydrophilic surfaces. The effects of time-period of alternating wettability shows that CHF increases with time-period until a certain value and then decreases with further increase of time-period. Then, the effects of wettability contrast are investigated by changing the hydrophobic contact angle while hydrophilic contact angle is kept fixed. It is found that CHF increases with contact angle until a specific value (θ=107°) and beyond it decreases due to fact the surfaces with higher hydrophobic contact angles tend to quickly form the vapor layer on entire surface. Furthermore, it is found that changing surface tension affects greatly the heat flux at larger wall superheats and CHF is observed to be increased with increasing surface tension.

11210920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210920.value: After carrying out a large number of experiments, numerical simulation and theoretical analysis, the following main conclusions can be drawn: 1. The micro-structured surface with pillar has a strong wickability to help liquids wet the surface quickly, also providing an additional nucleation site, significantly boosting the boiling critical heat flux (CHF) and heat transfer coefficient (HTC). The addition of surfactants can prevent bubbles from merging, maintain the microlayer of bubbles growing on the wall, and enhance HTC. However, near boiling crisis, the formed wet foam covers the whole surface, causing a decrease in CHF. When the two factors are present at the same time, the effect of surfactants covers up the effect of microstructure, and the CHF decreases. Because the wet foam blocks the wetting flow, the wetting acceleration effect brought about by the microstructure cannot work. 2. The coordinated action of electric field and surfactants can change the wettability of the surface. This can significantly reduce the temperature required for the onset of nucleate boiling at the initial stage and greatly improve HTC. However, near the boiling crisis, the effect of the electric field is greatly weakened by the insulation effect of large amounts of vapor generated. At this time, the action of surfactants dominates and becomes the determining factor of CHF. 3. During the boiling process, surfactants are deposited on the boiling surface. At the same time, electrolysis caused by electric field will also cause oxidation corrosion on the boiling surface. Both of these two factors make the previously smooth surface rough and porous, but also causes the original artificial microstructures to be covered and destroyed. This phenomenon poses a serious challenge for the long-term use of artificial microstructures. 4. The separate effects of wettability and surface tension were studied by numerical simulation using lattice Boltzmann method. Surface with alternating wettability (wettability changes with time alternately between the hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity) significantly improves boiling heat transfer performance. Bubble expands rapidly during the hydrophobic time and when wettability switches to hydrophilic, it induces a much faster contact line retraction. The faster retraction process helps to disintegrate the vapor film and rewets the surface and as a result higher CHF is observed. It is also found that changing surface tension affects greatly the heat flux at larger wall superheats and CHF is observed to be increased with increasing surface tension.

11210920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210920.value: After completing the research of this project, there are three enlightenments for future research: 1) The effect of addition of surfactants on boiling heat transfer cannot be simply reduced to surface tension change. The resulting special bubble dynamics feature has other effects that cannot be ignored. 2) The influence factors of CHF are hierarchical, and the strong factors will cover up the weak factors. 3) When the heat flux is large, the effect of electric field is greatly reduced because of the insulating effect of vapor. Based on this, future studies should focus on the effect of the addition of surfactants on bubble dynamics and establish theories to correlate this with heat transfer parameters such as HTC and CHF. These bubble dynamics factors may also mask other CHF influencing factors, such as roughness, surface material, and so on. This needs to be explored by future research.

11210920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210920.value: This research project explores how to improve boiling heat transfer, which is crucial for many industrial processes, by using specially designed microstructured surfaces and surfactants (substances that reduce surface tension). The main goal was to understand how these factors can enhance boiling performance, which can be described by parameters such as critical heat flux (CHF) and heat transfer coefficient (HTC), and then to see how combining surfactants with an electric field could further improve these effects. The findings revealed that surfaces with tiny micro-scale pillars can help liquids spread quickly, significantly boosting heat transfer. However, when surfactants are added, they can create a wet foam that blocks the surface, reducing the benefits of the textured surfaces. Additionally, applying an electric field helps surfactants move to the boiling surface, making boiling more efficient at lower temperatures. Yet, as boiling intensifies, the insulating vapor reduces the effectiveness of the electric field. Overall, this research provides valuable insights into optimizing boiling processes, which could lead to more efficient industrial applications and better energy management in heating systems.

11211720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211720.value: Helical microstructure is regarded as one of the most fundamental geometries in laboratory and industry (e.g., mechanical manufacture, electronics, and biomedical engineering) for sensing, heating, actuating, and the like. As a key specification, the precision of helical structure highly regulates its working performance, e.g., the resolution of the force sensor, the signal of the antenna, etc. At current stage, although several kinds of methods have been proposed for high-precision helical structure fabrication at small scales, such as vapor phase deposition, glancing angle deposition, electro-spinning, 3D printing, etc, they are usually restricted to few types of materials and the fabrication of micro helical structure from metal remains a big challenge. This project aims at developing a microrobotic system with multiple units to realize the high-precise, flexible and automatic micro helical structure fabrication made of metal. To achieve that goal, this project will be implemented as below: 1) To develop a multi microrobotic system under microscope. We will develop the microrobotic system with four independent units to meet the manipulation requirement for helical structure fabrication at small scale. These units are with mm size and will be integrated with various microscopes (e.g., optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM)) based on requirements. 2) To study the cooperation strategy of multi microrobots. We will establish the model of the multi-robots, design the proper cooperation strategy and conduct the trajectory planning to realize the flexible manufacturing of the helical structure. Here, the system initialization, calibration and shaft alignment will be addressed as well. 3) To design the control strategy. We will develop a force and vision based hybrid sensing system and a dual feedback control method to realize the high-precise, flexible and automatic operation at microscopy environment. 4) We will manufacture the helical structures with controllable shape and promote them in the field of hybrid micro sensing, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy by cooperating with company. Compared with existing manufacture techniques, our proposed method is laconic, precise, flexible, and controllable. Moreover, it allows to manufacture the helical structure precisely from various metal for the first time. Besides the helical fabrication, the successful implementation of this project will have long-term impact on many aspects: it will pave a new path for the high-precise manufacture at small scale; it will deliver a series of micro structure with complex structure for various applications; and it will promote the fundamental material research and practical industry output. 螺旋微結構是實驗室和工業界(如機械製造、電子和生物醫學工程)中最基本的幾何結構之一,在感測、感測、驅動等方面有著廣泛的應用。 螺旋結構的加工精度對其工作性能,如力感測器的解析度、天線的信號強度等有很大的影響。 儘管目前已經存在幾種小規模高精度螺旋結構製造的方法,如氣相沉積法、電紡、3D列印等,但基於金屬的微螺旋結構製備仍面臨很大挑戰。 本專案旨在研發一種具有多個模組的微機器人系統,以實現金屬微螺旋結構的高精度、柔性及自動化加工。 為了實現改目標,我們將研發具有四個獨立單元的微機器人系統,並將其與各種顯微鏡(例如光學顯微鏡、掃描電子顯微鏡)集成。 研究多模塊機器人的協作策略,進行軌跡規劃,實現螺旋結構的柔性製造。 此外,我們將研發基於力和視覺反饋的感測系統和基於雙反饋的機器人控制方法,以實現顯微鏡環境下的高精度、柔性和自動化操作。 最終,我們將製造形狀可控的螺旋結構,並驗證其在微傳感、表面增強拉曼光譜等領域的應用。 與現有的螺旋結構製造技術相比,本專案提出的方法簡單、精確、靈活、可控。 除螺旋加工外,該專案的成功實施將對許多方面產生潛在影響:為小規模的高精度製造提供一種新的技術方案;為前沿應用提供一系列複雜的微結構;促進材料基礎研究和推動工業應用。

11211720.label: Realisation of objectives
11211720.value: 1. To develop the microrobotic system with multiple independent units to achieve adequate manipulation DOFs in a narrow space. We have developed a microrobotic manipulation system with 6-DOFs, including one rotational manipulator and one linear manipulator. There are three motion DOFs (xr−yr−θz) for the rotational manipulator that functions as the active actuation of the rotating mandrel. The linear manipulator with three translational DOFs (xl−yl−zl) here is applied to deploy the wire. The linear manipulator is constructed by three linear piezo actuators (ECS3030, Attocube Inc.). The selected linear piezo actuators have 90 N maximum load and 1N maximum dynamic force along axis. Thus, it is sufficient enough to hold and drive wire winding stage for vision feedback manufacture and adjustment. Besides, each linear piezo actuator has maximum size with 30 ×51.6 ×9.5 mm and made of stainless steel, so that it can fit the narrow space and ultrahigh vacuum in an SEM. When it comes to the coarse positioning mode, the typical minimum step size of the linear piezo actuator is 0.05μm, the travel range is 20 mm, and the maximum drive velocity is 4.5 mm/s. While under fine positioning mode, the fine positioning range can be controlled from 0 to 1.6μm and the fine positioning resolution can be controlled down to half nanometer. The resolution and repeatability of the linear positioners are 1 and 50 nm, respectively. The rotational manipulator is constructed by two linear piezo actuators (ECS3030, Attocube Inc.) and one rotary actuator (ECR3030, Attocube Inc.). The rotary piezo actuator has 20 N maximum load and 2Ncm maximum dynamic torque along axis, which is sufficient enough to hold the mandrel during the manipulation. Besides, the rotary piezo actuator has maximum size with 30 ×30×13.5 mm and made of stainless steel. When it comes to the coarse positioning mode, the typical minimum step size of the rotary piezo actuator is 0.4 m◦, the travel range is 360◦ endless, and the maximum drive velocity is 10◦/s. While under fine positioning mode, the fine positioning range can be controlled from 0 to12m◦ and the fine positioning resolution is controlled down to micro degree. 2. To realize the flexible manipulation under microscope by multi-robot cooperation. We integrated a microscope on the top to provide vision feedback for the motion of the robotic system. Before manufacturing, we first established the transformational matrix between the microrobot coordinate and the microscope coordinate and employed the vision to eliminate assembly error of the manipulator stage. Next, we developed the triple-image alignment (TIA) strategy to eliminate the eccentricity error of the rotary actuator so that the mandrel can obtain an exact coaxial rotation. Later, according to the calibrated coordinate system, we generated the theoretical trajectory for both the two robotic manipulators to achieve cooperation by implementing the task of mandrel rotating and wire deployment, respectively. Finally, based on the online recording feedback, we developed the closed-loop control framework to achieve real-time adjustment in the manufacturing process. 3. To implement the high precise and efficient helical structure fabrication by establishing the dynamic model and developing the dual feedback system. We developed the feedforward and double feedback control system to realize the microscale manufacture. For the rotation module on the left robot, the accuracy of the rotational speed is controlled by the controller-embedded PID method with the angle feedback from the internal robotic system. For the right robot, the X-,Y-,and Z-modules feed wire to ensure the uniformity of the helical microstructure. However, only tracking the designed trajectory is not sufficient, since the displacement between the mandrel and the center of the rotation axis will cause the position fluctuation of the mandrel, which highly decreases the manufacture precision. Therefore, we developed the feedforward compensator to correct this sample installation error. Furthermore, the feeding wire may not locate on the proper position and result in irregularity of the pitch. So, we further developed a dual feedback system based on the vision servo and the internal position/pose feedback to adjust the real-time lead angle to improve the manufacturing accuracy. 4. To verify the fabricated micro helical structure and promote its applications in research and industry. We introduced the robotic manipulation system and the closed-loop control algorithm to achieve the manufacture of micro helical structures with high precision. To demonstrate the working ability, we employed several mandrels with different diameters e.g., ranging from 300 μm to 1000 μm, as the rotating samples and fabricated many helical structures with customized pitch sizes from 100 μm to 530 μm. The results suggest that the 3-D micro helical structures can be manufactured with high precision and repeatability, i.e., pitch error down to 2 μm (STD 1.06). Compared with the existing work, this system can realize the 3-D high precision manufacture without the limitation of specific materials, which is more concise. We also demonstrated some applications of the fabricated micro helical structures in research and industry. Due to the inherent helical geometry, the fabricated structures can be directly applied as the micro springs. By calibrating the corresponding spring constant of the structures with different geometrical parameters, we demonstrated the application of force sensors by single/combining multiple springs together. With the fabricated high precision micro helixs, we further employed them to achieve modulus measurement of lab-made hemostatic sponges. By recognizing the difference between the hemostatic sponge with different materials composition, we can help the researchers find a better application scenario. Except for the research field, we also found the industrial applications for the fabricated micro helical structures. By employing metal materials as the winding wire, we demonstrated that the fabricated helical structure could also be applied to connect electrical components and perform as the resistance.

11211720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211720.value: This project proposed a microrobotic manipulation system and fabrication algorithm to improve the manufacturing precision of micro helical structures. The major findings and research outcomes from this project can be summarized as: (1) A microrobotic system with 6-DOFs was designed and developed and the precise rotation/translation of the mandrel/winding wire was realized based on this system. (2) A real-time visual servo system based on a microscope was integrated and developed the multi-robot cooperation strategy by establishing the coordinate system transformational matrix and eliminating assembly error. (3) A dynamic model of the fabrication process and the position/vision dual feedback control framework was established to achieve dynamic adjustment for the micro helix fabrication process. (4) With our system and algorithms, the manufacture of micro helical structures with varied customized geometrical parameters was accomplished with the pitch precision reaching up to 2μm. Moreover, we also demonstrated corresponding applications of the fabricated micro helical structures in both research and industry fields. Relevant achievements have delivered 5 SCI journal papers and 2 US patents. See Part C for details.

11211720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211720.value: In this research, we proposed a high precision fabrication strategy for micro helical structures based on multiple robotic systems, developed the prototype consisted of two microrobotic manipulators, established the dual feedback closed-loop control framework, and verified the effectiveness of the fabrication precision up to 2 μm. As the future work, we will try to accomplish the 3-D high precision manufacture of micro helical structures with more types of materials, with variable gradient pitch or conical contour, so that we can promote our system to more practical application fields, such as electronics, photonics, biomedical engineering, MEMS, and so on.

11211720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211720.value: The helical microstructure has been widely applied to various fields, such as mechatronics, photonics, microelectromechanical systems, and biomedical engineering, but their fabrication with high precision remains a challenge. With the support of this project, we proposed a high precision fabrication strategy and system for micro helical structures. Firstly, we developed a microrobotic system with 6-DOFs for controlling the mandrel rotation and wire deployment. Then, we integrated a microscope as the real-time vision and developed the multi-robot cooperation strategy. Later, we established a dynamic model of the fabrication process and the position/vision dual feedback control framework to achieve dynamic adjustment. The results suggest that our system and algorithms can achieve the high precision (up to 2μm) manufacture of micro helical structures with varied customized geometrical parameters. With the fabricated micro helical structures, we demonstrated that they can be applied as force sensors or electrical resistance. We believe that this project pave an effective solution for the high-precise 3-D helical structure fabrication, which would prompt their applications in engineering and inspire other microstructure manufacturing as well.

11212620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212620.value: 建築暖通空調系統的技術進步是緩解全球變暖、構建可持續社會的關鍵之一。能源消耗是暖通空調領域溫室氣體排放的主要來源，其為產熱和發電所需化石燃料的燃燒產物。建築能耗通常占地區總能耗的20-40%，其中暖通空調佔據最大比例。暖通空調領域另一個重要的溫室氣體排放源是全球變暖型製冷劑的洩漏。因此，提高能源效率和發展環境友好型製冷劑對於解決全球變暖問題都非常重要。吸收式熱泵是減少這兩類排放源的有效技術方案。吸收式熱泵能利用可再生能源和廢熱，進行供冷、供熱、除濕和蓄能，以減少化石燃料消耗。此外，吸收式熱泵通常採用水/溴化鋰和氨/水等環境友好型製冷劑，符合蒙特利爾協定吉佳利修正案的要求。 然而，目前存在兩大問題限制著水/溴化鋰吸收式熱泵的推廣應用：(1) 大尺寸和高成本；(2) 結晶和堵塞風險。因此，很有必要研發佔用空間小、成本低、無結晶風險的緊湊型吸收式熱泵。為解決這些問題，本項目提出採用離子液體的微通道膜式吸收器，其具有較大的比表面積，能顯著提高系統的緊湊性。因離子液體具有較低的熔點，是很有潛力的無結晶吸收劑。本項目還將採用表面活性劑進一步強化傳熱傳質，以降低離子液體的高粘度劣勢。本項目的研究目標包括：(1) 建立微通道膜式換熱器的分佈參數模型以研究傳熱傳質特性；(2) 研發實驗樣機用於模型驗證和實驗測試；(3) 開發吸收器傳熱、傳質、壓降的精確關聯式；(4) 優化膜參數和吸收器結構以實現容積製冷量最大；(5) 遴選並測試離子液體/表面活性劑以進一步提升吸收式熱泵效率。 所提研究對於小型化、低成本、無結晶吸收式熱泵的研究和開發具有重要意義，能夠促進高效、經濟、低碳的能源技術在香港及全球的推廣。

11212620.label: Realisation of objectives
11212620.value: We set five project objectives and carried out a lot of activities focused on these objectives. These activities can contribute to (1) model establishment of the microchannel membrane-based absorber; (2) prototype development for model validation and experimental investigation; (3) accurate correlations development for heat/mass transfer and pressure drop; (4) membrane geometry and absorber configuration optimization; and (5) working fluids screening to further enhance the cooling efficiencies. All the project objectives have been successfully achieved as planned, with details summarized as follows. 1. Establish distributed and dynamic models of the heat/mass transfer processes in the microchannel membrane-based absorber using advanced working liquids. In a typical membrane-based microchannel absorber, water vapor diffuses into the solution through the membrane-solution interface, driven by the pressure potential. The water vapor is absorbed by absorption working fluids, with both heat and mass transfer through the membrane. To guide the optimization of the absorber structural design as well as the screening of novel working fluids, we established a model of the membrane-based absorber using novel H2O/ILs. It can be used to investigate the heat and mass transfer processes along the channel length, including the dynamic distribution of the temperature, velocity, and concentration in the solution channel. The property model of a wide range of novel working fluids have been established with proven high accuracy. The continuity, momentum, energy, and species transport equations are employed in the model. The partial pressure difference is a driving force, based on which the mass transfer flux across the membrane can be calculated. The simulation results were compared with the reference data. The temperatures predicted by the CFD model are in good agreement with the reference, and the maximum relative error is only approximately 0.1%. As for the pressure potential along the flow direction, the relative error is less than 1%. 2. Develop a prototype of the microchannel membrane-based absorber using advanced working liquids, for model validation and experimental investigation. A microchannel membrane-based module consists of four plates. The membrane is glued on the membrane support plate using the method from the reference. The four plates are assembled by screws and gaskets between plates. Based on the designed experimental loop, the developed experimental setup of a microchannel membrane-based absorber is further developed for performance measurement. This experimental setup is also suitable for the microchannel membrane-based desorber if it is replaced by a microchannel membrane-based desorber. For the absorber experiment, it requires stable inlet parameters, so three PID controllers are applied to regulate the entering solution/refrigerant/cooling water inlet temperatures. The solution feed tank supplies the solution with pre-mixed concentration while the solution recovery tank recovers the solution leaving the absorber. Temperature sensors, pressure transducers, flow meters, absorbent concentration meter are used to measure different streams. With these measurements, the heat transfer rate, absorption rate, and pressure drop can be obtained. Uncertainty analysis has been conducted for these derived performance indexes. These experimental studies have been used to validate the models and demonstrate the merits of the novel absorber including: enhanced performance, compactness, and crystallization-free operation. 3. Develop correlations for heat/mass transfer and pressure drop of the microchannel membrane-based absorber using advanced working liquids. This project has developed correlations for heat/mass transfer and pressure drop behaviors with respect to absorber configurations, fluid properties, and operating conditions. These correlations are essential for the design, analysis, and optimization of compact absorbers and absorption heat pumps. The influences of different factors on the heat transfer rate, mass transfer rate, and pressure drop have been measured and analyzed. The influential factors include the vapor pressure, solution temperature, solution concentration, solution flow velocity, cooling water temperature, and cooling water flow velocity. We find that increasing the solution flow rate, vapor pressure, and solution concentration or lowering the cooling water temperature can improve the heat and mass transfer processes significantly. Through comprehensive analysis of the experimental data, new correlations of the Nusselt number (Nu), Sherwood number (Sh), and friction factor (f) are developed for the first time for heat and mass transfer and solution pressure drop, respectively. It is verified that these newly developed correlations significantly enhance the prediction accuracy of the overall heat transfer coefficient (U), absorption rate (J), and pressure drop (DP) by 72.39%, 78.55%, and 64.56% as compared to existing correlations. The exceptional accuracy achieved by these correlations contributes significantly to the design, evaluation, and optimization of efficient and compact absorbers. 4. Optimize the membrane geometry and absorber configuration to maximize the volumetric cooling capacity, with an objective target of minimized absorber. The plate-and-frame membrane-based absorber has been optimized assisted by ML methods. To investigate the effects of different design parameters on the pressure drop and absorption rate with limited CFD simulations, the orthogonal experimental design is used. The CFD simulation data are randomly divided into two groups, 80% utilized for training and the remaining for testing. The results from ANN model yield the most satisfactory accuracy, so ANN is selected for performance prediction. Based on multi-objective optimization, we obtained the Pareto front to reveal the trade-off between absorption rate and pressure drop. The optimum design schemes could be chosen depending on actual preferences. Compared to the scenario with the maximum absorption rate, the optimal structure generated from the TOPSIS method presents a 47.75% reduction in DP with a 17.12% decrease in J. As for the LINMAP method, these changes are 55.92% and 28.32% respectively. Compared to the scenario with the minimum pressure drop, the optimal structures generated from the LINMAP and TOPSIS methods both improve the absorption rate whilst significantly increasing the pressure drop. The volumetric cooling capacity of the LINMAP-optimized case is 1.41 times higher than that of the base case, while the pressure drop is lower by 1.30 times. For the TOPSIS-optimized structure, the volumetric cooling capacity is increased by a factor of 1.47 (reaching 575.48 kW/m3), while the pressure drop is lower by 1.26 times. 5. Screen advanced working fluids to enhance the heat/mass transfer in the absorber and therefore increase the cooling efficiencies of absorption heat pumps. The cooling efficiency will be evaluated for absorption heat pumps using novel absorbers and fluids. A multi-scale computational screening method assisted by computer-aid molecular design is established. To accelerate molecular design in various operating conditions, eight ML algorithms are integrated to predict the cycle performance based on molecular descriptors with less computation cost. The agreement between experiment and simulation illustrates high accuracy of this screening method. The multi-scale approach achieves the high-throughput computational screening of optimum ILs for high-efficiency absorption systems. Furthermore, we have investigated the feasibility of microchannel membrane-based absorption heat pumps using different H2O/ILs under various working conditions, with H2O/LiBr as the baseline. The results show that under a desired cooling capacity of 0.5 kW, [EMIM][OAc] and [EMIM][OMs] can yield higher COPs. The necessary smallest system volume of each working pair increases with the targeted COP to satisfy the requirement of membrane liquid entry pressure. Comparing the Pareto frontiers that show the trade-off between the COP and compactness, LiBr is the best choice with the targeted COPs below 0.778, while [EMIM][OAc], [EMIM][OMs], and [BMIM][BF4] perform better with the targeted COPs above 0.778. The novel system outperforms the conventional falling-film systems in efficiency and compactness when the targeted COP is below 0.80.

11212620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212620.value: This project is mainly focused on novel heat/mass components and novel working fluids towards energy-efficient, crystallization-free, and high-compactness absorption heat pumps. For novel heat/mass components, we systematically compared the heat/mass transfer performance of various advanced absorbers/desorber. Results showed that the proposed novel membrane-based microchannel structure achieved the largest absorption rate of 0.015 kg/(m2·s), desorption rate of 0.0225 kg/(m2·s), volumetric cooling capacity of 1147 kW/m3, and coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.855. Based on these results, I designed and fabricated microchannel membrane-based absorbers/desorbers to increase the compactness of small-capacity absorption heat pumps. I further developed a prototype of a microchannel membrane-based absorption heat pump with a cooling capacity of 0.5 kW. We then measured this 0.5 kW microchannel absorption heat pump on the testing platform established in the lab. Heat/mass transfer and pressure drop were measured and correlated for the microchannel membrane-based absorbers and desorbers. We further built enhanced channel structures and artificial-intelligence-assisted CFD optimization methods for geometry optimization, maldistribution minimization, and performance improvement. Based the proposed new methods in this project, the pressure drop of the microchannel membrane-based absorber can be significantly reduced by 6.3 times and the mass flux can be increased by 55%. As for novel working fluids, we aim to overcome the shortcomings of conventional H2O/salt absorption working fluids, for which the crystallization is always a big concern. To realize crystallization-free absorption cycles, novel H2O/ionic liquid mixtures were screened using high-accuracy models. We developed a machine-learning-based multi-scale molecular design to look for high-performance H2O/ionic liquids. The quantitative relationship between the molecular structure, H2O/ionic liquid mixture, and heat pump performance was established. From 26360 candidates, the best-performing ionic liquids were identified under 18 operating conditions. Furthermore, we developed a multi-criteria approach to rationally screen a wide variety of refrigerants (H2O, NH3, methanol, acetone, DME) paired with 44 ionic liquids, considering cycle performance, heat transfer, hydraulic resistance, and applicable range. H2O/[OMIM][OAc] and NH3/[DBIM][Tf2N] were found to have excellent performance comprehensively. Furthermore, we investigated the performance of microchannel membrane-based absorption heat pumps using different H2O/ionic liquids under various working conditions. Results show that under a desired cooling capacity of 0.5 kW, [EMIM][OAc] and [EMIM][OMs] can yield higher COPs. LiBr is the best choice with the targeted COPs below 0.778, while [EMIM][OAc], [EMIM][OMs], and [BMIM][BF4] perform better with the targeted COPs above 0.778. The outcomes are significant for developing novel absorption heat pumps towards efficient and affordable low-carbon building technologies.

11212620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212620.value: The proposed novel microchannel membrane-based absorber using ionic liquids is significant for the development of small-size, low-cost and crystallization-free absorption heat pumps, facilitating efficient and affordable low-carbon HVAC technologies in the future. The results and findings of this project will motivate further research on novel heat pump components and systems. Wide commercialization and applications of this technology will greatly cut the fossil fuel consumption and GHG emissions. It can help the Hong Kong Government realize the target to reduce the carbon intensity by 65-70% from the 2005 level by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The success of this project will contribute towards sustainable buildings and societies in Hong Kong and all over the world. In 1-5 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant institutes and manufacturers to deepen the research and promote the development. In 5-10 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant enterprises and building users to promote better applications and further improve the energy saving effects. Over 10 years. our research team will collaborate with relevant governmental departments and NGOs to promote wider applications of this technology to maximize long-term energy saving and emission mitigation.

11212620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212620.value: Absorption heat pumps are promising for building decarbonization. Absorption heat pumps can utilize renewable energy/waste energy for cooling, heating, dehumidification, and energy storage. Additionally, absorption heat pumps usually use environmentally-friendly working fluids with very low global warming potential. However, there are two major problems preventing wider applications: (1) large size and thus high cost, and (2) crystallization risk and thus system blockage. This project seeks to address these problems by developing a novel microchannel membrane-based absorber using ionic liquids. The microchannel membrane-based absorber offers a very high compactness, while ionic liquids can eliminate the crystallization risk. The project objectives include: (1) establish distributed and dynamic models of the microchannel membrane-based absorber to characterize the heat/mass transfer behaviors; (2) develop a prototype for model validation and experimental investigation; (3) develop accurate correlations for heat/mass transfer and pressure drop within the absorber; (4) optimize the membrane geometry and absorber configuration to maximize the cooling capacity per volume; and (5) screen and test potential working fluids to further enhance the cooling efficiencies of absorption heat pumps. The project is significant for the development of novel absorption heat pumps towards efficient and affordable low-carbon building technologies.

11212920.label: Project Objectives
11212920.value: To explore transition-metal-based layered double hydroxides (LDHs) that have favorable structures for use as cathode materials that can host Zn2+ ions. These LDHs should show intrinsically good electrochemical activity with good reversibility. To optimize LDHs for enhanced electrochemical performances. Full cells based on these LDH cathodes are expected to show high specific capacity (> 250 mAh g−1) with superb capacity retention over 80% after 2000 charge/discharge cycles. The target maximum energy density and power density is 200 Wh kg−1 and 5000 W kg−1, respectively (based on the mass of cathode material). To analyze the dynamic process of zinc ion intercalation and LDH structural evolution during charge/discharge via in-situ characterization techniques, including X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, providing solid evidence for verifying the electrochemical mechanism as well as effective guidance for development of electrode materials.

11212920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212920.value: 自從1866年在Leclanché電池中首次出現以來，金屬鋅因其固有的高容量，低氧化還原電勢，高自然豐度，低毒性和絕對安全性而被認爲是水性儲能系統的理想電極材料。這些有利特征導致可再充電鋅電池（ZBs）的開發近年來複興。然而，將鋅金屬暴露于傳統的堿性電解質中會導致鋅中嚴重的不可逆的電化學過程，這是由于其剝離/電鍍的庫倫效率不足，在充電/放電時形成枝晶，副産物的不可逆産生以及持續的水消耗造成的。因此，使用堿性電解質的ZB表現出較差的循環穩定性。 近年來，通過使用中性或弱酸性電解質和具有隧道結構的二氧化錳陰極，ZB已成功進入了一個新的發展時代。這些電池已大大改善了循環穩定性，並保留了高比容量和安全性的優點。盡管具有適度的循環穩定性，但二氧化錳在循環過程中作爲鋅離子嵌入/脫嵌的主體時，仍會遭受不可忽略的結構轉變，並且所産生的大體積變化往往會導致累積容量衰減。此外，庫侖效率低仍然是一個問題，因此需要高的充電和放電速率以減輕電化學過程中不良的可逆性的影響。 已經開發出多種可用于ZB的新型陰極材料。研究人員從其他電池系統中借用了釩氧化物和釩酸鹽作爲配對鋅陽極的陰極，並取得了很大的進展。基于這些材料，ZB表現出了大大改善的性能，包括增加的比容量和更好的循環穩定性。但是，大多數釩氧化物和釩酸鹽的鋅離子嵌入/脫嵌電勢相對較低，這導致放電平穩期降低，降低了其能量密度。此外，還研究了普魯士藍類似物作爲新型陰極。盡管具有較高的潛力，但這些材料仍存在比容量低和循環穩定性差的問題，這極大地限制了它們的進一步應用。 在這個項目中，我們建議開發新型的過渡金屬基層狀雙氫氧化物（LDH）作爲ZBs的陰極。可以合成和優化具有結構的LDH化合物，這些化合物有望實現離子吸收，快速嵌入/脫嵌和穩定的循環。它們的工作機理，結構演變和電化學動力學將通過原位X射線衍射，拉曼光譜和基于中子的技術進行深入研究。根據我們的初步結果，我們堅信所提議的LDH將作爲高性能陰極工作，填補ZB高效陰極的空白。

11212920.label: Realisation of objectives
11212920.value: Supported by this project, we designed high-performance nickel cobalt-based layered double hydroxides (LDH) materials with modified electrodeposition method, which was investigated as cathode materials for constructing the aqueous zinc batteries. Preparation of LDH electrode and the corresponding morphologies and structural characterizations We adopted traditional electrodeposition method to prepare the NiCo LDH on the nickel foam (NF) to from the free-standing LDH electrode. The NiCo LDH generated near the electrode substrate is readily loaded on the NF skeletons, denoted as LDH@NF. Theoretically, this deposition process contributes to the formation of the composite hydroxide ultrathin sheets with a porous structure, which is beneficial for fast ion transportation during cycling. However, with prolonging electrodeposition time, the electrodeposited NiCo LDH is prone to form stacked nanospheres, which can be attributed to the change in crystallization kinetic of NiCo LDH due to the inferior electrical conductivity of the LDH nanosheets and the increased OH- concentration around the electrode surface. To prepare high-performance LDH materials with favorable structures, we then developed two strategies to optimize the electrodeposition preparation. First, to enhance the contact between LDH and NF substrate, MXene is selected to support the fabrication of the NiCo LDH electrode. Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets are successfully prepared and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image confirms the successful fabrication of a few-layer Ti3C2Tx MXene. Owing to the electronegative characteristics, the MXene nanosheets easily covered the 3D frameworks of NF (denoted as MXene/NF), leading to improved interfacial contact between NF and the platting solution. Then, we also added the MXene component into the platting solution to assist the electrodeposition of LDH based on the improved electrical conductivity of LDH, and the resulting sample is denoted as M-LDH@MXene/NF. During the electrodeposition process of LDH, the dispersed MXenes in the plating solution were adsorbed and incorporated into the LDH structure, enhancing the electrical conductivity and structural stability of the LDH and promoting a highly efficient electrodeposition process. Ultrahigh loading mass of LDH can be achieved in the M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode, reaching ~65 mg cm-2, which is much higher than LDH@NF (24 mg cm-2) and LDH@MXene/NF (36 mg cm-2). Subsequently, we thoroughly investigated the morphologies of the electrodeposited LDH. The irregular LDH nanoparticles can be detected in the LDH /NF and LDH@MXene/NF electrodes, and no LDH nanosheets can be detected even in the enlarged SEM image of the two electrodes. However, for the M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode, the LDH nanosheets can be observed clearly even after 1-hour long electrodeposition. The 3D open architecture is obtained by forming the interlaced structure with large amount of honeycomb-like pores, which will provide channels for ion transportation and increase the area of interface between active sites and solution. In addition, high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) examination was carried out to confirm the LDH nanosheets with ultra-thin feature and a polycrystalline structure with a well-organized orthohexagnal lattice fringe. In addition, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was also conducted to reveal further the chemical compositions and states of the as-prepared electrodes, verifying the co-existence of Co, Ni, Ti, C and O elements in the above electrodes. In a word, MXene could reinforce the overall structure of LDH, making it more resistant to mechanical stress and deformation. In addition, due to the 2D feature of MXenes, they can provide additional support and prevent the layers of LDH from collapsing or delaminating. In addition, the incorporated MXene effectively facilitates ion and electron transfer on the electrode surface, which is beneficial for large-loading electrodeposition of LDH. Electrochemical performance of the optimized NiCo LDH We employed the NiCo LDH as electrode materials in alkaline zinc batteries. The battery based on the M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode owns long discharge plateaus located at ~ 1.61 V with up to 20.2 mAh cm-2 areal capacity. In addition, the specific capacity of the battery is up to 311.7 mAh g-1. The superior capacity of M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode can be attributed to the low bulk resistance and charge-transfer resistance. The areal capacity and specific capacity of M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode surpass most other electrode materials in zinc batteries. Subsequently, the rate performance of the M-LDH@MXene/NF-based battery was assessed and the same reaction plateau at around 1.6 V can be observed at all curves, meanwhile, the battery exhibits a remarkable rate capability of 311, 289, 272, 261, 245, 202 and 148 mAh g-1 at 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 90 and 120 mA cm-2, respectively. In addition, in our developed zinc battery, due to the ultrahigh loading density and excellent electrochemical activity of the LDH cathode, ultrahigh areal energies and power densities (31.2 mWh cm-2 at 7.9 mW cm-2, 13.5 mWh cm-2 at 180 mW cm-2) were achieved, which means both high energy and power densities (465 Wh kg-1 and up to 7500 W kg-1) can be achieved in our battery. Furthermore, the M-LDH@MXene/NF battery exhibits excellent cycling performance, with a high capacity retention of 88.6% after 10000 cycles at 2 A g-1 and high Coulombic efficiency. Reaction mechanism of the NiCo LDH electrode To reveal the reaction mechanism of the LDH electrode in zinc battery, we investigated the chemical structure transition behavior by ex-situ Raman analysis. When the LDH-based electrode was charged to 1.6 V, two new peaks emerged at ~482 and 584 cm-1, which can be ascribed to the characteristic peaks of MIII-O (M: Ni, Co). With the charge process proceeding, the characteristic peaks of MIII-O show slightly enhancement in strength, and when the LDH-based electrode was discharged to 1.1 V, the characteristic peaks of MIII-O totally disappear, which reveals a clear transition between Ni2+ to Ni3+. In addition, as shown in Figure 5c, during the charging process, the characteristic peak of MOO- (M: Ni, Co) located at 1089 cm-1 gradually appears, and during the subsequent discharging process, the peak gradually disappears, which further confirms the transition between Ni2+ to Ni3+. In addition, X-ray diffraction (XRD) was adopted to disclose the crystal structure of the resultant electrode during cycling, which confirms the stable electrode structure of the M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode during cycling. Furthermore, we investigated the reaction kinetics of the developed LDH-based alkaline zinc battery. The electrochemical polarization of the battery is weak during cycling, demonstrating the fast redox kinetics of LDH-based cathode during the electrochemical process. In addition, the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) test was employed to evaluate the ion diffusion coefficient, and up to 4.8 × 10-8 cm2 s-1 ion diffusion coefficient is achieved in M-LDH@MXene/NF electrode. The high ion diffusion coefficient of the MXene-supported LDH-based electrode further confirms the superiority of the optimized electrodeposition method in the preparation of high-performance NiCo LDH electrode.

11212920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212920.value: The main challenges faced by aqueous rechargeable nickel-zinc batteries are their comparatively low energy density and poor cycling stability, mainly due to the limited capacity and reversibility of existing Ni-based cathodes. LDH-based electrode is highly promising for constructing the high-performance aqueous zinc batteries. However, the preparation procedures of these LDH materials are complex and not easily scalable, which makes them less promising for large-scale energy storage. For the above issues, we innovatively utilized MXene as a functional additive to effectively improve the electrodeposition preparation of NiCo layered double hydroxides (LDH). Benefiting from the improved interfacial contact between nickel foam (NF) and platting solution and the enhanced ionic conductivity of platting product based on MXene additives, the resulting binder-free NiCo LDH electrode can achieve ultrahigh areal loading (~65 mg cm-2) with abundant active surface for redox reactions and maintained short transport pathway for ion diffusion and charge transfer. Furthermore, the as-fabricated alkaline NiCo LDH-based battery delivers high discharge capacity, up to 20.2 mAh cm-2 (311 mAh g-1), accompanied by remarkable rate performance (9.6 mAh cm-2 or 148 mAh g-1 at 120 mA cm-2). Due to the high structural and chemical stability of MXenes/LDH-based electrode, excellent cycling life can also be achieved with 88.6% capacity retention after 10000 cycles. In addition, ultrahigh areal energy density (31.2 mWh cm-2) and gravimetric energy density (465 Wh kg-1) can be simultaneously achieved. Our findings has inspired the design of advanced LDH-based cathode materials to develop high-performance zinc batteries.

11212920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212920.value: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) show great promise in constructing high-performance battery due to their tunable properties, high specific capacity, and good cycling stability. To further develop LDHs for battery applications, the following course of action can be considered: 1. Optimization of Synthesis Methods: Explore different methods to synthesize LDHs with controlled morphology, surface area, and crystal structure to enhance their electrochemical performance. 2. Doping and Surface Modification: Investigate dopants and surface modifications to improve the conductivity, cyclability, and overall electrochemical properties of LDHs for better battery performance. 3. Scale-Up: Scale up the synthesis processes of LDHs for mass production while considering cost-effectiveness and sustainability. Collaborate with industry partners for practical applications. 4. Advanced Battery Architectures: Explore novel battery architectures such as solid-state batteries, hybrid organic-inorganic systems, or flexible/wearable devices integrating LDHs to cater to specific application needs. 5. Safety and Environmental Impact: Conduct thorough studies on the safety aspects and environmental impact of using LDHs in batteries to ensure compliance with regulations and promote sustainable energy storage solutions. By following these steps and continually exploring new avenues in LDH research for batteries, there is significant potential for advancements in energy storage technology with improved performance, longevity, and sustainability.

11212920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212920.value: Zinc batteries currently have limitations like low energy capacity and stability issues because of limited cathode materials. LDH-based electrodes have shown promise for making better zinc batteries, but they are hard to make in good quality and large quantities. This project found a new way to make these LDH materials by adding another material MXene. This addition helps in making the battery electrodes more efficient by improving the contact between nickel foam and the plating solution, making it easier for ions to move around and for the battery to charge and discharge effectively. The batteries made using this new method showed impressive results. They have higher discharging capacity due to the optimized electrode structures and increased areal loading, a long lifespan with very little loss in capacity even after 10000 cycles, and they could deliver higher energy density. This innovation could lead to the development of better zinc batteries that are more efficient and can store more energy, which is essential for advanced energy storage systems.

11213320.label: Project Objectives
11213320.value: Design, fabrication and characterization of transistor-like energy generator. The electrical output performances of the as-proposed device under continuous droplet impinging will be systematically investigated and compared with control samples. We will also design a platform consisting of collector and capillary tuning-based dispenser for generation of droplets in an on-demand manner to address the random distribution in the spatial distribution and size of water droplets. Exploring the feasibility of high durability under harsh environments. The effects of ionic concentrations, relative humidity, and ambient temperature on the performances of the transistor-like energy generator will be explored. Revealing underlying mechanisms of the transistor-like energy generator. The effects of intrinsic water droplet charges, electrochemical storage due to the different electrochemical potential (ITO and Al) on the electricity generation will be first investigated. The synchronization of droplet dynamics and current response will be studied to reveal the source for the enhanced electricity generation. An equivalent electrical circuit model will be developed and molecular simulation (MD) will be conducted to probe the basic mechanisms underlying the enhanced output performances. Demonstration of practical applications. For the first demonstration, we will develop flexible devices that can collect mechanical energy from body motion for power supply in wearable electronics. In the second application, we will extend the droplet-based energy generator for wave energy harvesting.

11213320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213320.value: New design principle: Developing a “transistor-like” architecture that overcomes the interfacial effect imposed on conventional triboelectric generators and results in three orders of magnitude enhancement in the energy conversion efficiency. This design was highly recognized by the American Physical Society as: “a water energy generator that cleverly combines the 2,600-year-old electrostatic effect and the 3,800-year-old hydrophobic effect”. New mechanisms: Revealing the “bulk effect” endowed by the “transistor-like” architecture which can fully leverage the water kinetic energy and high-density surface charges pre-stored in dielectric materials, rather than the limited charges generated during liquid-solid contact electrification. New applications: Providing a new paradigm for efficient water energy harvesting, leading the way for harvesting of waters of various interfaces and environments (published in Nat. Commun., Sci. Adv., Joule, and other journals), including electricity generation from single droplet to droplet arrays, from natural tree leaves and rocks to artificial windows and solar panels, from bubbles to water waves, with a continuous leap in peak power density from 50 W/m^2 to 104 W/m^2 that can drive a light bulb of 20 W. The related invention promotes new explorations and applications in many fields, such as biomedicine, the Internet of Things, and blue energy, as evidenced by winning the highest prize at the Geneva International Exhibition of Inventions.

11213320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213320.value: Our previous works have sparked a wave of global exploration, however, further exploiting the gold mine demands innovative strategies, concerted efforts, and sustained support. Further development will focus on systematic and in-depth research on the unresolved scientific and technical problems in the interfacial water-electric conversion technology and applications, further breaking the efficiency limit of the existing interfacial water-electric energy conversion, and developing multiple applications. For example, fundamentally, what is the nature of the charge and microscopic interaction mechanism dominated in the water-solid interaction? Technically, can we pursue a generic and holistic design that applies to different water and energy functions, and is robust against diverse application environments? We envision that future work will further reshape the way we understand interfacial water-electric interaction, the way we utilize and manage resources (water and energy), the way we sustain our environment and society, and collectively foster an energy-efficient and environment-friendly society over the long term.

11213320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213320.value: Global water energy has the potential to generate nearly 60 trillion watt-hours of electricity annually. Our “transistor-like” water energy generator fundamentally transforms the water-electric interaction at the liquid-solid interface, such as the generation, enrichment, and transfer of surface charge, resulting in water/bubble energy harvesting with an unprecedented thousand-fold enhancement in energy conversion efficiency and peak power density. Our work opens up a new avenue for efficient energy harvesting from water on various interfaces and environments (published in Nat. Commun., Sci. Adv., Joule, and other journals), allowing for a continuous leap in peak power density from 50 W/m^2 to 104 W/m^2, which has garnered over 1100 citations in four years and won the highest prize at the Geneva International Exhibition of Inventions.

11213420.label: Project Objectives
11213420.value: To investigate a novel regression-based model for gaze tracking. A region-wise regression model is proposed based on the idea of partitioning the input space of pupil centers into a set of sub-regions to control the point of regard (POR) to the locations where the 3D object may appears. Furthermore, some highly complex regression between eye images and gaze directions will be explored. An Asymmetric regression-evaluation network (ARE-Net) is proposed to enhance the gaze estimation performance to its full extent by using simple eye images as input. To develop some flexible and automatic calibration methods. To support flexible calibration, a new data acquisition method will be developed in which the user needs to fixate at only one calibration point while changing his head pose. With the changes in the head pose, a manifold is generated as the geometrical locus of the projection point of the scene camera projection points. Furthermore, an automatic calibration method is proposed with an RGB-D camera as the scene camera to acquire accurate 3D structure of the environment. The automatic calibration is achieved by uniting gaze vectors with saliency maps of the scene aligned depth information. To model human intention from gaze tracking. We propose to investigate human intention with both salience information from the scene images and the gaze information from the gaze tracking. Aiming at the intention understanding, we will study the problem of attention state representation and intention recognition. A probabilistic inference method will be studied to investigated the eye-controlled interactive mechanism with self-recovering capability. To integrate gaze tracking in human-robot interactions. In order to achieve natural and efficient human-robot interactions, some key issues need to be addressed including the eye-control instruction design and interaction paradigm, the eye-control interaction event detection and tracking, and the eye-control interaction instruction recognition. For implementation of the human-robot cooperation tasks, we will develop the integrated system including the mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) and the computer hardware with multiprocessor architecture to support highly parallel high speed processing.
