A region-wise regression model is proposed based on the idea of partitioning the input space of pupil centers into a set of sub-regions to control the point of regard (POR) to the locations where the 3D object may appears. Furthermore, some highly complex regression between eye images and gaze directions will be explored. An Asymmetric regression-evaluation network (ARE-Net) is proposed to enhance the gaze estimation performance to its full extent by using simple eye images as input.

To develop some flexible and automatic calibration methods. To support flexible calibration, a new data acquisition method will be developed in which the user needs to fixate at only one calibration point while changing his head pose. With the changes in the head pose, a manifold is generated as the geometrical locus of the projection point of the scene camera projection points. Furthermore, an automatic calibration method is proposed with an RGB-D camera as the scene camera to acquire accurate 3D structure of the environment. The automatic calibration is achieved by uniting gaze vectors with saliency maps of the scene aligned depth information.

To model human intention from gaze tracking. We propose to investigate human intention with both salience information from the scene images and the gaze information from the gaze tracking. Aiming at the intention understanding, we will study the problem of attention state representation and intention recognition. A probabilistic inference method will be studied to investigated the eye-controlled interactive mechanism with self-recovering capability.

To integrate gaze tracking in human-robot interactions. In order to achieve natural and efficient human-robot interactions, some key issues need to be addressed including the eye-control instruction design and interaction paradigm, the eye-control interaction event detection and tracking, and the eye-control interaction instruction recognition. For implementation of the human-robot cooperation tasks, we will develop the integrated system including the mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) and the computer hardware with multiprocessor architecture to support highly parallel high speed processing.

11213420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213420.value: Gaze tracking as an eye monitoring method has found applications in various fields including marketing, automotive industry, rehabilitation, education, and virtual reality. In this project, we propose to extract human intentions from gaze tracking and integrate it as a kind of human-robot interface for robotic tasks. The project aims to develop a suitable head-mounted gaze tracking (HMGT) system and integrate it in human-robot cooperative tasks via communicating human intentions to the robot. We propose to approach the problem from different perspectives including (i) adopting a new regression-based model in the gaze estimation, (ii) developing flexible and automatic calibration for the gaze tracker, (iii) detecting human intention from the gaze tracking, (iv) introducing the human intention in human-robot cooperative tasks. With the fusion of gaze perception in robotic tasks, natural interactions between human and robots can be achieved. The challenging issues in the modeling and calibration methods for gaze tracking and human intention detection and integration in robot control need to be addressed in the project. A prototype of the integrated robotic system will also be developed for implementation of the proposed methodology. The results of the project will contribute the development of the technology and system to provide better robotic assistance to humans. As collaborations between robots and humans are becoming increasingly important for many robotic applications, this project will have significant impact on the theoretical studies in gaze tracking and gaze integrated human-robot interface, and the practical applications in robotics and automation. With the flexible and effective methodology to develop, the head-mounted gaze tracking device will be useful for interfacing humans with robots for advanced robotic tasks. This work will promote engineering applications of human-robot interaction technology in many areas, such as robot assisted rehabilitation, medical surgery, assisted driving and virtual reality. 凝视跟踪以跟踪眼运动为技术基础已经获得广泛应用。本项目拟由凝视跟踪得到人的关注点，围绕人与机器人协作过程中注意力融合的需要，开展凝视交互系统理论与关键技术的研究，旨在建立凝视追踪实现的眼动监测技术，探索意图理解和眼控指令两种凝视交互模式。进而突破外部物理信息交互的模式，跨越内部心智状态交互的盲区。特别地，研究凝视数据获取的问题，建立在线快速的自主标定方法，保证非理想情形下凝视测量和估计的可靠性；针对主动自发的意图理解交互模式，研究注意力状态识别和意图表征的问题，形成相应的意图识别研究范式；建立眼控交互指令完整性的推理方法，形成有自修复能力的眼控交互机制。针对视觉注意力驱动的人机协作任务，开展系统集成技术研究，并进行关键技术应用验证。研究成果将为人与机器人自然交互过程中场景学习、认知反馈与凝视感知融合研究提供新方法、新技术和评价方法，促进人机交互技术在医疗健康、腹腔镜手术治疗、辅助驾驶和虚拟现实等领域的工程应用。

11213420.label: Realisation of objectives
11213420.value: In this project, the proposed objectives are mostly well realized, through extensive studies conducted and implementation efforts made. Objective 1 has been studied to the depth. Related to modeling of human eyes, different approaches for modeling were studied with focus on regressions based method. Building on previous experiences, a regression-based model was developed and implemented for gaze tracking. In this project, the region-wise polynomial model is proposed to approximate the relationship between visual direction and pupil centers. To infer the partition structure, a homography-like relationship is derived from the local back-projection approximation, and then the Leave-One-Out criterion is leveraged to cluster the input-space into multiple overlapping sub-regions. Meanwhile, image points of eyeball centers are estimated based on the measured parallax errors, which are used to initialize the 3D eyeball centers. With the sensible starting point and the feasible region, a nonlinear optimization problem is formulated to minimize the geometrical errors, by which eye positions and back-projection matrices for each subregion can be inferred. We also set the principle for selecting the calibration depths, which might considerably affect the estimation accuracy. Implementation of this method consists of four parts. The first part introduces a training data acquisition method, which can be easily implemented and allow the training data to cover the user’s field of view. The second part proposes the gaze data prepossession method to remove the outlier training data. The third part designs a local-learning based gaze estimation model. To strike the balance between the model capacities and empirical risks, the rational lens distortion model is leveraged as a local model for approximating the process of back-projecting 2-D pupil centers to their corresponding 3-D gaze directions. The fourth part presents a learning process for the designed estimation model given the training gaze data. Our implementation results show the superiority of our proposed gaze estimation framework, especially in the space within or close to hand reach distance. Objective 2 aims to develop some flexible and automatic calibration methods for gaze tracking. To this end, we proposed a ﬂexible calibration framework to answer the question how to accurately learn the relation between the pupil center and point of regard (POR) projected from different depths. To reduce the extrapolation error, we adopt a gaze data acquisition approach to acquire densely distributed calibration points in a wide ﬁeld of view. Meanwhile, the nonparametric model is applied to approximate the residue ﬁeld unmodeled by the polynomial function. To improve the robustness of the learning process, a distraction detection method is also introduced to detect the outlier training data. To reduce the parallax error, the epipolar geometry of HMGT and user’s eyes is recovered by calculated virtual parallax errors. Thus, the POR unaffected by the parallax error can be estimated as the intersection of two epipolar lines inferred from both eye images. The proposed calibration framework is successfully implemented. The experimental results show that the calibration method achieved a satisfactory POR estimation precision for HMGT in the mobile environment. With this method, we can calculate the 2-D and 3-D gaze points for the wearable device. This technique serves as one of the useful human-machine interaction tools. To study human intention from gaze tracking proposed in Objective 3, we propose to investigate the relevant issues with both salience information from the scene images and the gaze information from the gaze tracking. To this end, a top-down fusion structure is constructed for cross-modal cross-level interactions. This resembles a kind of mechanism in human attention, the top-down approach. The experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed cross-modal distillation scheme in learning from a new modality, the advantages of the proposed multi-modal fusion pattern in selecting and fusing cross-modal complements, and the generalization of the proposed designs to different tasks. We implemented this attention model in guiding combination of RGB images and depth modalities. The challenges are addressed with a novel framework developed to adopt the task-understanding knowledge of the RGB-induced saliency detection network to depth modality and fuse the deep representations of both two modalities adaptively to obtain the final saliency map. In studying issues related to tracking tasks via deep learning, we proposed a multi-view attention-aware network. The attention mechanism was used to boost the complements in different streams for better joint inference. Comprehensive experiments conducted showed superiority of our model over state-of-the-art methods as well as the efficacy of our framework. The insights gained from this work will allow us to learn better representations from other new modalities and enable sufficient fusion for other multi-modal systems. With the salience-based bottom-up approach and a top-down fusion structure constructed for cross-modal cross-level interactions, Objective 3 is well explored. The top-down approach paves the way for object detection and tracking in the subsequent works. In the related studies, thorough investigations were made in exploring Multi-Modal Fusion Networks in the learning framework for target detection, semantic segmentation, facial expression recognition, and human pose estimations, with both event and traditional images. Objective 4 is investigated to a great extent. We have explored event cameras in studying the method in eye-control interaction event detection and tracking, and the eye-control interaction instruction recognition. Our event camera in our previous work in dynamic vision played an important role in this. For Implementation of the human-robot cooperation tasks, we have developed an integrated system including the mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) and the computer hardware for implementing the methodology for gazing tracking and robotic interactions. Related to motion tracking, we also studied efficient tracking with event based vision and have set up the basic modules for tracking applications. For object detection, we introduced an adaptive motion-agnostic encoder which can extract indistinguishable semantic information behind event signals under various motion conditions by encoding events with integration block and adaptive motion-agnostic filter. The performance of our proposed method in motion consistency and inconsistency evaluations shows that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and motion robustness. The event based learning network introduces a novel attention-aware model (EVSTr) for spatiotemporal representation learning on event streams. EVSTr takes event voxel sets as input to fit the sparsity of event data and hierarchically learns robust representations for recognition tasks. The proposed event voxel transformer encoder efficiently extracts spatiotemporal features from event voxels in a local-to-global manner. To model the long-range temporal structure for action recognition, a segment modeling strategy is designed to learn temporal dynamics from a sequence of segmented voxel sets. Comprehensive experiments on object classification and action recognition show that EVSTr achieves significant accuracy gains and impressively low model complexity compared to state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, we have built a new event-based action recognition dataset (NeuroHAR) with multiple modalities recorded in challenging visual scenarios, allowing convincing evaluation for event-based models.

11213420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213420.value: In this project, we investigated gaze tracking for human-robot interactions. A mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) was developed [Patent #2]. The problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are solved with a new flexible calibration method [Patent #2]. A local-learning based gaze estimation model is developed. To strike the balance between the model capacities and empirical risks, the model is leveraged as a local model for approximating the process of back-projecting 2-D pupil centers to their corresponding 3-D gaze directions. To improve the robustness of the learning process, a distraction detection method is introduced to detect the outlier training data. With this system, the user is only required to change his head pose while gazing at a calibration marker. This results in flexible calibration for the gaze tracker. In studying human intention via gaze tracking, we investigated both the salience information from the scene images and the gaze information from the gaze tracking. A top-down fusion structure is constructed [J2,3], which resembles a kind of mechanism in human attention. In studying issues related to tracking tasks via deep learning, we proposed a multi-view attention-aware network [J4,8], where the attention mechanism was used to boost the complements in different streams for better joint inference. With the studies on salience-based bottom-up approach [J1] and a top-down fusion structure constructed, the investigations have led to some Multi-Modal Fusion Networks in the learning framework useful for target detection [J1,4], semantic segmentation [J8], facial expression recognition [J10,12], and human pose estimations [J5,6,7], with both event and traditional images. Another finding is the event camera that is useful for eye-controlled interactions with event detection and tracking [J2,3,4], and instruction recognition. The event camera played an important role in the dynamic visual tracking tasks. For Implementation of the human-robot cooperation tasks, we have integrated the mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) with the computer hardware for implementing the methodology for gaze and pose tracking [J5,6], for robotic interactions. With the event based learning network, we introduced a novel attention-aware model for spatiotemporal representation learning on event streams [J11]. To model the long-range temporal structure for action recognition, a segment modeling strategy is designed to learn temporal dynamics from a sequence of segmented voxel sets [J8]. Moreover, we have built a new event-based action recognition dataset with multiple modalities recorded in challenging visual scenarios, allowing evaluation for event-based models, for public use in benchmarking [J11].

11213420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213420.value: In this project, we investigated gaze tracking for as a new way of input for human-robot interactions. A mobile head-mounted gaze tracker (HMGT) was developed. The problems in rigid and tedious calibration in traditional approaches are solved with a new flexible calibration method. Distraction can be detected in the training, which improves the quality of the training data. With the flexible calibration of such a system, the user is freed from the traditional problems in using gaze trackers. This makes the system suitable for non-expert users and it has high potential for robotic applications as an interface between the operator and robots. In studying human intention via gaze tracking, we investigated both the salience information from the scene images and the gaze information from the gaze tracking. A top-down fusion structure is constructed, which resembles a kind of mechanism in human attention. This together with the salience-based bottom-up approach, have led to a multi-modal fusion networks in the learning framework. This will invite more explorations in deep learning for this purpose. The insights gained from this work will be useful for robotic applications. We have planned some further work along this direction and have prepared a proposal for NSFC application.

11213420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213420.value: Interactions between human operators and robots are important for robotic applications. In this project, we investigated the use of gaze tracking to extract the intentions of human from their eyes, to provide a new means for passing human commands to robots. A new calibration framework is developed, making it easier for non-expert users to work on. Together with the study in visual attention learning, the methodologies explored will be useful for enhancing human-robot interactions. In studying human attention, we have looked into both model-based top-down and the salience-based bottom-up approaches. This will invite more explorations in applying AI for such robotic applications. The insights gained from this work will lay a foundation for further works in the relevant areas. The system and methodologies developed here will have their impact on the applications of gaze trackers as a new way of input in human-computer interface in general and in human-robot interactions in particular. As robots are now finding wide domestic applications, the new way to interact with robots through users eyes provides a promising alternative for teaching robots to work and for human-robot cooperation tasks.

11213620.label: Project Objectives
11213620.value: Designing faster distributed algorithms on large-scale graphs for solving problems such as all-pairs-shortest-paths, graph spanners, and diameter verification, as well as local problems such as computing maximal independent sets, maximal matchings, and ruling sets. We also plan to address these problems on dynamically-changing graphs. This includes an experimental evaluation of the resulting algorithms in real-world graph processing frameworks. Obtaining complexity lower bounds for the message-time trade-off inherent to algorithms for global graph problems. Due to the relationship between the message complexity of CONGEST algorithms and fast k-machine algorithms, we will derive lower bounds in both models for problems such as graph spanners, broadcast (in the CONGEST model), and constructing breadth first search trees. Developing a complexity theory for large-scale graph processing and investigating the formal relationship between models for massive graphs such as the k-machine model and the MPC model. We will propose time complexity classes in the k-machine model and study the existence of minimal problems with respect to these classes.

11213620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213620.value: Achieving efficient computation on massive graph data sets is a fundamental challenge with numerous applications, ranging from social network analysis and machine learning to protein interaction graphs studied in computational biology. The scale of such massive graphs, which often exceeds the memory and bandwidth capabilities of a single machine has prompted practitioners to develop distributed graph processing frameworks such as Google Pregel, Apache Spark/GraphX and Giraph. The overarching goal of this project is to develop the theoretical foundations of algorithms for efficient distributed computation on massive graphs in computing models that capture the main features of real-world graph processing frameworks. This includes the design of new distributed algorithms that scale to massive graphs for problems such as computing shortest distances between vertices, computing maximal independent sets, and finding sparse subgraphs (i.e. with few edges) that exhibit certain properties. Given that real-world data sets are continuously evolving, we also plan to derive new algorithms that can handle dynamically-changing input graphs. The obtained algorithms will be experimentally evaluated by implementing them in open source graph processing frameworks, which will have a tangible impact on industrial practice. A crucial challenge for performing fast distributed computation on large graphs is to come up with algorithms that do not send too many messages, i.e., are communication-efficient. We will explore new algorithmic techniques to overcome this obstacle and we anticipate that this also provides insights on designing communication- and time-efficient solutions for classic distributed computing models, where each graph vertex represents a computational entity. A complementary goal of the project is to understand how much communication a distributed graph algorithm needs to perform, while still being able to quickly arrive at a correct solution. More specifically, this work will reveal the complexity lower bounds on the trade-offs between time and the required communication in distributed computing models, which is still an open question for many fundamental graph problems. 11213620.label: Realisation of objectives
11213620.value: For the first objective, we have the following outcome. 1.Maximal Matching in k-machine model. We study maximal matching in the k-machine model and give some efficient algorithms. 2.Dynamic maximal matching in the k-machine model. We give algorithms for dynamic maximal matching in the k-machine model with batches of updates, where there are two different adversaries, i.e., oblivious adversary and adaptive adversary and the dynamic updates include edge deletions and edge insertions. 3.Correlation clustering in the MPC model. We give two efficient algorithms for correlation clustering in the MPC model for random graphs created from the SBM model. 4.Perfect Matching in complete bipartite graphs. We give several different algorithms for finding perfect matching in complete bipartite graphs in different distributed models. We also have some experiment, which demonstrates our results. Publications: ESA 2023, ITCS 2024, SIROCCO 2025(short) (will submit to Journal TCS). For objective 2, we have the following outcome. 1. Leader Election. We consider leader election in clique networks. In the synchronous setting with simultaneous wake-up, we prove there is a trade-off between messages and rounds. We also improve the best known upper bounds. In addition, we also give many efficient algorithms under different settings. 2. Dynamic Maximal Matching in the k-machine model. We give lower bounds for dynamic algorithms dealing with batches of updates. For oblivious adversaries and adaptive adversaries, we give two different lower bounds. Publication: PODC 2023 (Invited to Journal Distributed Computing). ITCS 2024. This objective is finished by 90%. We did not give lower bounds for the CONGEST model. The major reason is that we do not find a good/meaningful candidate problem to show a lower bound for CONGEST model. For objective 3, we found that the relationship between k-machine model and the MPC model is not that interesting. Basically, if we make the bandwidth of them to be the same, it is the relationship between the vertex-partition model and the edge-partition model. We can transform one to the other.

11213620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213620.value: Leader election is the fundamental tool in most of distributed systems. Our major finding is the new trade-offs for leader election, which improves the previous results significantly (PODC 2023). We give lower bounds and upper bounds in several settings. Data is inherently dynamic, and how to deal with dynamic data becomes more and more important and challenging. We establish new upper bounds and lower bounds for dynamic problems in the large-scale distributed model (ITCS 2024). Since nowadays, data are stored in a distributed way, our dynamic algorithms will save time and money for updating the systems, database and so on when the data changes. Our lower bound will show the bottleneck of dealing with updates. It is known that clustering plays important roles in data mining. We give near optimal algorithms for the correlation clustering (ESA 2023) which will make many applications using this kind of clustering more efficient than before.

11213620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213620.value: Dynamic problems have many open questions in distributed models. One of the most important tasks is to design distributed data structures for maintaining solutions. It is not clear how to design such algorithms, and also it is hard to show the lower bounds. A good start of exploring this direction is to start from some famous and important problems like graph coloring and matching. To make it possible to utilize distributed data structures, it is allowed to increase the power of the model by introducing some auxiliary equipment. To show the lower bounds, the possible tools are from communication complexity and information theory.

11213620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213620.value: We study different topics including leader election, matching, dynamic problems, clustering. For these problems, we give algorithms under different settings. Most of our results are theoretical, but these theories have real applications. It means that one can improve the performance of information technology in the industry by implementing our results. We also prove that it is impossible to achieve better than some targets, which can save a lot of unnecessary efforts.

11213720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213720.value: Based on light-induced oscillations of electrons, surface plasmons generated from metallic nanoparticles or other nanostructures have been proposed for intracellular exploration such as optical detection of mRNA in living cells, gene delivery and regulation, rapid precision molecule diagnostics, and other in vitro and in vivo biomedical applications. Making these plasmonic structures movable in a controlled manner using microrobots as carriers will remarkably broaden their capability for scanning or mapping the stimuli, entering or leaving from a cell, and targeting a specific area of interest. Based on this insight, the objective of this project is to investigate the integration of plasmonic nanostructures onto microrobotic carriers for extending their potentials to serve as mobile transducers for molecule detection, as antennas for boosting the energy harvesting efficiency for microrobots, and heating spots for thermal therapy. Specifically, three tasks are planned: (1) Design, optimization and fabrication of plasmonic detectors of molecules, (2) Integration of plasmonic antennas onto helical microrobots for enabling molecule mapping, and (3) Superposition of plasmonic devices with dimer microrobot swarms for boosting energy harvested for thermal therapy. Simulations using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) will be applied to evaluate and optimization of the design. Plasmonic nanostructures will be fabricated onto microrobots by rolling up prestressed bilayers with nanoparticle arrays. Microrobotic swarms will be formed with core-shell gold-ferromagnetic nanoparticles for intracellular exploration. Energy harvested and boosted by the antennas from an infrared laser beam will be used as a thermal energy source for heating up a cell to demonstrate cellular thermal therapy to show energy transmission. The proposed research will enable new technologies for the design, simulation, optimization, fabrication, and characterization of nano-sized functional elements for microrobotic agents. Plasmonic structures will be used as sensing elements based on the sensitivity of surface plasmons on the segment separation or environmental stimuli, besides of the new signal transduction principle, the mobility of them enabled by microrobotic carries will greatly expand their mapping and targeting capability. External power supply to microrobots have been a major bottle neck for the evolution of microrobots from particles into systems, the success of this project will pave a new avenue of micro-/nanorobots not only from the aspect of integration, but also the remote signal and energy transmission; highlighting the emerging of more intelligent and powerful tools for such applications as microrobotic thermo-surgery and gene therapy. 基于光激发的电子振荡，金属纳米颗粒或其他纳米结构产生的表面等离激元已被提出用于细胞内的探索，如活体细胞中mRNA的光学探测、基因传输和调控、快速精确的分子诊断以及其他体外和体内的生物医学应用。利用微机器人作为载体，使这些等离激元结构以可控的方式运动，将极大地拓宽其扫描或映射激励信号，进入或离开细胞，以及针对特定的感兴趣的区域的靶向能力。有鉴于此，本项目旨在探索将等离激元纳米结构集成到微机器人载体上，以扩大其在生命科学中的潜力，例如作为分子探测的移动传感器，作为提高微机器人能量收集效率的天线，以及热疗的加热点。具体而言，计划开展以下三项工作：(1)等离激元分子探测器的设计、优化及制造，(2)等离激元天线在螺旋形微机器人上的集成及分子映射，(3)等离激元器件与二聚体微机器人的叠加及群控，以提高热疗的能量收集效率。具体方法如下：将采用有限差分时域（FDTD）的仿真进行设计的评估和优化；通过预加应力的双层纳米薄膜与纳米粒子阵列的自卷曲实现等离激元纳米结构在微机器人上的集成；以金铁壳核磁纳米粒子形成微机器人群实现细胞内探索；由天线从红外激光束中收集和提升的能量将被用作加热细胞的热能源，以展示细胞热疗、显示能量传输。 拟开展的研究将为微机器人系统上纳米尺度功能元件的设计、仿真、优化、制造和表征提供新技术。基于表面等离激元对子结构间距或环境刺激的敏感性，等离激元结构将被用作敏感元件，除了新的信号传感原理外，以微机器人携带的方式，其可移动性将大大扩展其映射和靶向定位能力。一直以来，能量供给是微机器人从粒子进化为系统的一大瓶颈，本项目的成功，将不仅从系统集成度方面，而且从远程无线信号和能量传输方面，为微/纳米机器人开拓一条通往智能、自主的新途径，预示微机器人在热疗和基因治疗等应用中作为更智能、更有力的工具的出现。

11213920.label: Project Objectives
11213920.value: Design a blockchain-based federated framework that supports task recommendations across multiple crowdsourcing systems. The difficulties of achieving this task lie in the fact that there does not exist a (centralized) trusted party in the whole system. Existing crowdsourcing systems assume the existence of a trusted authority that can faithfully perform key management. However, in a blockchain network, such a trusted party may not exist anymore. It is difficult to encrypt information about tasks and workers and perform task-worker matching over encrypted data without involving a third party of authority. Design an efficient and secure on-chain task-worker matching scheme that can support task matching over encrypted data for large scale of tasks and workers in crowdsourcing. The key to the success of the proposed federated crowdsource system is the security and scalability. Existing encryption schemes for secure task matching [5][6] require linear scan on the entire encrypted tasks, which is too costly for the blockchain-based federated platform. Moreover, it is still an unexplored topic about how to preserve the security property of volume-hiding in encrypted crowdsourcing research. Design a secure and fair scheme for collection and evaluation of crowdsourcing results, such that it will make an unbiased evaluation of collected results and reward only the honest workers with contracted payment. In the blockchain paradigm, the peer nodes in the blockchain network usually perform the verification or evaluation task. However, it is difficult to design such a scheme that allows the peer nodes to evaluate the quality of crowdsourcing results without exposing what the actual results are.

11213920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213920.value: Crowdsourcing is an emerging technology that utilizes the collective intelligence to solve complex tasks. In a crowdsourcing system, there are three parties, task-requesters, a crowdsourcing server (called broker), and task-workers. The requesters publish their tasks and the workers submit their interests to the broker. The broker matches the task requirements with the worker’s interests and recommends the best matched tasks to workers. The current crowdsourcing systems have three major problems: 1) lack of a federated platform that interconnects ask-requesters to all potential workers crossing the boundary of individual systems; 2) lack of a privacy-preserving mechanism that protects the confidentiality of tasks and interests of workers against untrusted brokers; and 3) lack of a fair mechanism that can enforce the execution of the contracts between the task-requesters and the workers and reward the honest workers. The principal goal of this project is to develop a federation of crowdsourcing systems by using the blockchain technology. The project work consists of three major tasks: 1) Design a blockchain-based federated framework that supports task recommendations across multiple crowdsourcing systems; 2) Design an efficient and secure on-chain task-worker matching scheme that can support task matching over encrypted data for large scale of tasks and workers in crowdsourcing; 3) Design a secure and fair scheme for crowdsourcing results collection and evaluation that can make an unbiased evaluation of collected results and reward honest workers with contracted payment. 眾包是一種新興的技術，可以利用集體智慧來解決複雜的任務。在傳統的眾包系統中，包括三個主要的參與者，即任務請求者，眾包服務器（稱為代理）和任務工人。請求者發布任務而工人提交查詢請求給代理。代理將任務要求與工人的請求相匹配，並向工人推薦最匹配的任務。然而，目前的眾包系統存在三個主要問題：1）缺乏將任務請求者與不同系統中的潛在工人互聯的聯邦平台；2）缺乏隱私保護機制，以保護工作任務和工人請求的機密性；以及3）缺乏公平的機制來強制執行任務請求者和工人之間的合約並獎勵誠實的工人。 本項目的主要目標是通過使用區塊鏈技術開發一個聯邦眾包應用平台。具體包括三個主要研究任務：1）設計基於區塊鏈的聯邦平台框架，支持跨平台的眾包任務匹配服務；2）設計一種高效且安全的鏈上任務匹配方案，支持對加密數據的快速匹配；3）設計一種安全且公平的評估方案，對眾包結果進行公正的評估，並通過鏈上簽約付款的方式獎勵誠實的工人。

11213920.label: Realisation of objectives
11213920.value: This is a very successful project with fruitful research results. It generated 20 high quality research outputs in top-tier journals and conferences in the field, including 17 papers in IEEE/ACM transactions and journals. Regarding the three objectives, i.e.,1) Design a blockchain-based federated framework that supports task recommendations across multiple crowdsourcing systems; 2) Design an efficient and secure on-chain task-worker matching scheme that can support task matching over encrypted data for large scale of tasks and workers in crowdsourcing; and 3) Design a secure and fair scheme for crowdsourcing results collection and evaluation that can make an unbiased evaluation of collected results and reward honest workers with contracted payment; we have successfully realized all of them as followings. We first developed a federated system, called FedEDB [TKDE2024], which is a blockchain-based federated data store for encrypted data. This work serves as the foundation of the proposed “federated crowdsourcing platform”. To further increase the efficiency and system throughput, we proposed an “AdaptChain” [TPDS2023] and “PuffChain” [TNSE2024] that can adaptively scale up and down the system throughput according to traffic demands for PoS and PoW blockchains respectively, and an “X-shard” [TPDS2024] method that divides the transactions into shards to process transactions optimistically and efficiently. These works fulfill the requirements of achieving objective 1. Regarding objective 2, we proposed an attribute-Based Encrypted Search scheme (AESM) for multi-owner and multi-user distributed systems [TPDS2023], which is the theoretical foundation for privacy-preserving tasking match in federated crowdsourcing systems. We also proposed a verifiable search over encrypted data and integrity auditing algorithm for a decentralized environment [TC2025]. We further proposed privacy-preserving range query and arbitrary queries [TIFS2023] processing schemes [TCC2022, TDSC2021] and developed an application of privacy-preserving online ride-hailing system [NSS2022]. We also proposed general purpose data sharing scheme over encrypted data, which allows interoperations among federated crowdsourcing systems [TIFS2023, TSC2023]. To remove the redundant data among multiple local systems, we developed a privacy-preserving deduplication scheme various types of data, such as media data [TDSC2023] and compressed data [TPDS2023]. All the research issues along with objective 2 have been completely addressed. For objective 3, we focused our effort on the development of encrypted machine learning [ICDE2024] and unlearning algorithms [TIFS2023], and develop secure and efficient payment scheme for crowdsourcing workers [TRIDENTCOM2023]. To increase the throughput of a distributed system, we also proposed a service migration algorithm [IoT2025].

Finally, we focused our effort on the development of encrypted machine learning [ICDE2024] and unlearning algorithms [TIFS2023], and develop secure and efficient payment scheme for crowdsourcing workers [TRIDENTCOM2023]. To increase the throughput of a distributed system, we also proposed a service migration algorithm [IoT2025].

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213920.value: Crowdsourcing is an emerging technology that utilizes the collective intelligence to solve complex tasks. In a crowdsourcing system, there are three parties, task-requesters, a crowdsourcing server (called broker), and task-workers. The requesters publish their tasks and the workers submit their interests to the broker. The broker matches the task requirements with the worker’s interests and recommends the best matched tasks to workers. The current crowdsourcing systems have three major problems: 1) lack of a federated platform that interconnects ask-requesters to all potential workers crossing the boundary of individual systems; 2) lack of a privacy-preserving mechanism that protects the confidentiality of tasks and interests of workers against untrusted brokers; and 3) lack of a fair mechanism that can enforce the execution of the contracts between the task-requesters and the workers and reward the honest workers. The principal goal of this project is to develop a federation of crowdsourcing systems by using the blockchain technology. The project work consists of three major tasks: 1) Design a blockchain-based federated framework that supports task recommendations across multiple crowdsourcing systems; 2) Design an efficient and secure on-chain task-worker matching scheme that can support task matching over encrypted data for large scale of tasks and workers in crowdsourcing; 3) Design a secure and fair scheme for crowdsourcing results collection and evaluation that can make an unbiased evaluation of collected results and reward honest workers with contracted payment.

11214020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214020.value: The mammalian neural system continues to evade a full quantitative characterization. Advances in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNN) have provided new opportunities for computational neuroscience to pose new questions regarding the structure and function of biological neural networks, particularly the visual system. Some attempts have been made to utilize advances in machine learning to answer neuroscientific questions, but how to appropriately make comparisons between the biological neural systems and DCNN models is an open question. To better understand biological neural network, neural recordings during animal behavior are necessary. However, current experimental techniques impose spatial limits on the number of neuronal units that can be recorded. To model neural dynamics in response to stimulus, various mathematical models have been developed to link external stimuli to the electrical or chemical activities of neurons. Yet, difficulty in performing in vivo experiments result in the limited quantity of training data, which could still severely affect the accuracy of the modeling of the biological neural network, as the neural spiking activity is already quite sparse. The spatiotemporal limitations in recordings also affect the reconstruction of networks, which describe the connections between the neuronal units recorded. In order to investigate the similarities and differences between network properties of biological nervous system and artificial neural networks, it is necessary to first investigate how sampling affects complex network measures. We will focus on the mouse visual system and different DCNN architectures for machine vision, to determine if this comparison is appropriate. Utilizing weighted graph-theoretic measures, we will investigate the connectivity patterns in the modern artificial computer vision system and the biological vision system. We will then extend the work to investigate the network properties of other brain regions and artificial neural networks for unique functions, such as motor and auditory functions, and to examine how different neural network structures relate to function and/or performance. A better understanding of how information is processed in biological neural circuits will in turn contribute to the development of artificial neural networks and neuromorphic circuits. 深度卷積神經網絡（Deep Convolutional Neural Networks，DCNN）的發展為計算神經科學提供了新的方法去探索有關生物神經網絡在結構和功能上的問題。以往有研究嘗試利用機器學習來探討神經科學課題，但是如何合適地比較生物神經系統和DCNN模型是一個懸而未決的問題。 另外，在動物行為期間記錄神經活動，是了解生物神經網絡的必要實驗過程。然而，當前的實驗技術對可記錄的神經元數量有空間限制。同時，執行動物實驗十分困難，訓練數據數量有限，加上神經的活動本身非常稀疏，嚴重影響生物神經網絡建模的準確性。 為了研究生物神經系統和人工神經網絡的網絡特性的異同，必要首先了解採樣如何影響複雜的網絡度量。我們將重點研究小鼠視覺系統和機器視覺的不同DCNN架構，以確定這種比較是否合適。另外，我們將利用加權圖理論研究現代人工計算機視覺系統和生物視覺系統中連接模式的相似性或差異。然後，我們將擴展網絡特性研究到其他大腦區域和具獨特功能的人工神經網絡，並研究不同的神經網絡結構與功能及性能的關係。這個項目對生物神經迴路中的信息處理方式發現將更促進人工智能和仿神經晶片的發展。

11214020.label: Realisation of objectives
11214020.value: Objective 1. Simulate and Quantify How Sampling Affects Complex Network Measures The project has successfully fulfilled the first objective by simulating and systematically quantifying the impact of sampling on complex network measures through a series of robust experiments and analyses. In "Comparing biological and artificial vision systems: Network measures of functional connectivity" (2020), simulations were employed to examine sampling biases by randomly sampling a subset of units from the VGG16 neural network and comparing them to the biological network of the mouse primary visual cortex. The study demonstrated that sampling biases could significantly distort network properties, leading to deviations in calculated measures such as node density, clustering coefficient, and path length. The findings suggested that the incomplete sampling inherent to biological recordings may obscure the true global network properties, emphasizing the need for caution when interpreting results from sparse datasets. This analysis provided a direct quantification of how sampling impacts network measures and allowed for adjustments to improve the accuracy of these estimates. Additionally, in "Latent Variable Models Reconstruct Diversity of Neuronal Response to Drifting Gratings in Murine Visual Cortex" (2021), the effects of subsampling were implicitly addressed through the use of latent variable models (RLVM and NNMF) to reconstruct neuronal activity from calcium imaging data. These models demonstrated the ability to infer hidden network-level features from limited data, effectively overcoming the constraints of sparse sampling in biological recordings. The study further highlighted how node density acts as a dominant predictor of model reconstruction accuracy, emphasizing the importance of sampling density in preserving network properties. Objective 2. Investigate Whether Network Properties of Biological and Artificial Neural Networks Can Be Compared Appropriately and How These Properties Relate to Functions and Performance The second objective has been fully achieved by systematically comparing the network properties of biological and artificial neural networks. In "Comparing biological and artificial vision systems: Network measures of functional connectivity" (2020), direct comparisons were made between the mouse primary visual cortex and the VGG16 artificial neural network using graph-theoretic measures such as node density, path length, clustering coefficient, and betweenness. The results revealed significant differences between the two systems. The biological network exhibited distributions closer to Poisson-like behavior, with longer path lengths and lower clustering coefficients, indicative of a less densely connected and more irregular structure. In contrast, the VGG16 network displayed highly organized, Gaussian-like distributions, with shorter path lengths and higher clustering coefficients. These findings suggest that while VGG16 shares some architectural inspiration with the mammalian visual system, its functional connectivity patterns diverge significantly. The functional implications of these differences were explored in multiple studies. First, in "An Efficient and Flexible Spike Train Model via Empirical Bayes" (2021), it was shown that biological networks handle over-dispersed spiking behavior more effectively than artificial networks. Unlike artificial systems, biological systems excel at managing noise and variability, which are critical for performance in dynamic or noisy environments. Second, in "Power Law in Deep Neural Networks: Sparse Network Generation and Continual Learning with Preferential Attachment" (2022), the existence of power law dynamics in artificial networks was investigated. While truncated power law distributions were found in artificial systems. Power law distributions, often observed in biological neural networks, describe a scale-free topology where a small number of nodes (neurons) have disproportionately high connectivity, while the majority have fewer connections. This structure enables robust information propagation and fault tolerance. The study revealed that artificial networks, particularly sparse deep neural networks (DNNs), can exhibit truncated power law distributions when certain connectivity constraints are applied, such as through preferential attachment mechanisms. Scale-free connectivity allows biological networks to balance efficiency and robustness, as critical nodes facilitate global communication while peripheral nodes specialize in local processing. Mimicking this topology in artificial networks could potentially enable benefits such as reduced redundancy, faster training convergence, and continual learning through dynamic network growth. The functional implications of this finding are significant. In earlier study "Towards Lifelong Object Recognition: A Dataset and Benchmark" (2022), the OpenLORIS-Object dataset demonstrated how lifelong learning algorithms could adapt to dynamic environments with varying difficulty levels. The study revealed that while existing algorithms perform well in controlled settings, their ability to generalize and retain performance across diverse tasks is limited, reflecting differences in functional priorities between biological and artificial systems. These findings highlighted the unique adaptability of biological systems in handling complex, changing environments. The final paper of this project, “Community Channel-Net: Eﬃcient channel-wise interactions via community graph topology” (2023), then introduces community-based graph topologies that optimize channel-wise interactions in DNNs, mimicking biological principles such as sparsity and modularity, which are essential for efficient information processing. By leveraging dense intra-community connections and sparse inter-community connections, the method reflects structural features of biological systems, such as local specialization and global integration. These graph-based designs lead to significant improvements in classification accuracy, channel diversity, and computational efficiency compared to existing methods like SE-Net and ECA-Net, demonstrating how structural properties impact functional performance. The paper’s use of small-world properties and biologically inspired connectivity indirectly supports the investigation of how biological principles can inform artificial designs. In conclusion, the project has successfully demonstrated that while biological and artificial neural networks can be compared to some extent, their network properties reflect fundamentally different design principles and functional priorities. Biological systems prioritize adaptability, robustness, and variability, whereas artificial systems are optimized for efficiency and precision in specific tasks. These findings provide a better understanding of the relationship between network properties and system performance, offering valuable guidance for future research and the design of artificial neural networks.

11214020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214020.value: This project has provided significant insights into the relationship between biological and artificial neural networks, focusing on the impact of network properties, sampling strategies, and structural designs on system performance. The findings highlight the critical role of sampling in understanding and interpreting network measures. In "Comparing Biological and Artificial Vision Systems: Network Measures of Functional Connectivity" (2020), it was shown that sampling biases can severely distort key network properties such as node density, clustering coefficient, and path length. These distortions obscure the true global network characteristics, particularly in biological recordings where incomplete sampling is inherent. The study emphasized the importance of addressing these biases to improve the accuracy of network analyses. Further advancements were achieved in "Latent Variable Models Reconstruct Diversity of Neuronal Response to Drifting Gratings in Murine Visual Cortex" (2021). Latent variable models (RLVM and NNMF) were applied to reconstruct neuronal activity from calcium imaging data, revealing diverse tuning profiles often absent in artificial networks. The findings highlighted how node density influences reconstruction accuracy. The OpenLORIS-Object dataset (2022) then provided a framework for evaluating lifelong learning algorithms, exposing the limitations of existing approaches under varying environmental conditions. When comparing biological and artificial networks, key structural and functional differences emerged. In "Comparing Biological and Artificial Vision Systems" (2020), biological networks demonstrated longer path lengths and lower clustering coefficients, while artificial networks like VGG16 exhibited shorter path lengths and higher clustering coefficients, optimized for task-specific efficiency. The study in "Power Law in Deep Neural Networks" (2022) further revealed that well-performing artificial networks exhibit truncated power law distributions. Introducing power law dynamics in artificial networks provides significant benefits, such as enabling continual learning improvements and reducing network size without compromising performance. Sparse networks generated through power law principles improve adaptability, allow dynamic growth, and optimize resource utilization, making them better suited for evolving tasks. Finally, biologically-inspired designs showed promising applications in artificial systems. The work in "Community Channel-Net" (2023) introduced community-based graph topologies that mimic sparsity and modularity in biological networks, resulting in significant improvements in classification accuracy, channel diversity, and computational efficiency. These findings highlight how optimizing connectivity through principles like small-world networks and modularity can enhance artificial network performance. Collectively, this project emphasizes the adaptability and robustness of biological systems compared to the efficiency-driven optimization of artificial systems and offers valuable insights for designing artificial networks that better emulate biological principles to improve connectivity, scalability, and continual learning capabilities.

11214020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214020.value: Our established research trajectory in neural computation and motor control has laid a strong foundation for advancing biologically-inspired computational frameworks. The success of community-based neural networks ("Community Channel-Net") in demonstrating how biological network topologies enhance system performance naturally extends to understanding motor control architectures. This aligns with our work on latent variable models reconstructing neuronal response diversity, which established robust methods for handling complex biological signals. The power law dynamics we identified in deep neural networks, particularly in sparse network generation and continual learning, provides insights into network efficiency and adaptability. Our recent application of RLVM in identifying inhibitory components in muscle synergies represents a practical integration of these theoretical frameworks, by combining network topology analysis, latent variable modeling, and biological signal processing. This convergence suggests a promising direction for developing unified computational models that can better capture the complexity of natural motor control systems while maintaining biological plausibility. By integrating these various approaches, we can advance both our fundamental understanding of motor control mechanisms and the development of more effective neural engineering applications.

11214020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214020.value: Our research explores the fundamental differences between biological and artificial neural networks, leading to practical advances in AI system design. Through analyzing mouse brain recordings and artificial networks, we discovered that biological networks show distinctive connectivity patterns compared to artificial ones like VGG16. This insight led us to develop improved computational models, including a Rectified Latent Variable Model that accurately reconstructs diverse neural responses without complex pre-processing, and Community Channel-Net which enables efficient channel-wise interactions through graph topology. We also found that well-performing artificial networks trained can demonstrate power law dynamics similar to biological networks, a principle we leveraged to enhance both sparse network generation and continual learning tasks through preferential attachment. These findings not only deepen our understanding of neural computation but also provide concrete ways to develop more efficient, adaptable AI systems inspired by the brain's organizational principles. The research spans from fundamental neuroscience insights to practical AI applications, contributing both theoretical understanding and engineering solutions to the field of neural computation and machine learning.

11214620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214620.value: Authentication decisions often need to be based on physical proximity to a location. For instance, a contactless payment card must be physically presented to a payment terminal before payment is taken. Linking the physical proximity of a device to a cryptographic authentication protocol is however a challenging problem. One of the most prominent approaches to addressing this challenge is distance-bounding protocols. In theory, these protocols simply work on the basis of measuring the round-trip time of carefully defined cryptographic challenge-response exchanges, which it uses to estimate the upper distance bound between the devices. In practice, the security of these protocols depends on the device’s communication channel as its characteristics effects the round-trip time measurement and the correctness of the bounding exchanges. Only if the full protocol implementation is both secure and reliable can we have confidence in the distance bound. Traditionally, RFID/contactless card systems would benefit from distance bounding but such devices have simple and limited bit-rate communication channels. In practice, if such channels are to be made more resistant to known distance-bounding channel threats it would reduce the reliability of the channel and introduce channel errors. Some distance-bounding protocols do not allow for errors during the bounding phase, while most simply set an acceptance threshold for total incorrect exchanges. When a protocol is made tolerant to incorrect responses, we need to consider the protocol’s false accept (which sees an adversary’s incorrect response as a channel error) and false reject probability (which rejects an honest device as there were too many channel errors). Current proposals for resilient distance-bounding require additional communication, either additional challenge-response exchanges or verification messages, to reach similar levels of false reject and false accept rates as error-free channels. Although transmitting some additional bits seem trivial it is a valid performance issues if there is a time limit on protocol execution and we are using slow channels for exchanging protocol data and challenge-response exchanges. In this project we investigate response functions that incorporate error-correcting codes to tolerate channel errors during the bounding stage, with the goal of achieving acceptable security performance in terms of false accept and false reject rates, but while reducing the amount of additional challenge-response exchanges and verification message data. We also consider response function implementation that have short, consistent computation time and prevents early leakage of the response(s). This improves protocol reliability and execution time, and contributes to distance-bounding becoming a practical security mechanism. 一些交易的授权需要受到物理距离的限制。例如，一张无线支付卡必须靠近支付终端才能进行交易，当实体卡与支付终端的物理距离过大时，交易需要被判定为无效。如何制定基于设备间的物理距离的安全授权协议是一个有挑战性的问题。 距离限制协议（Distance-bounding protocol）是其中一种知名的解决方案。理论上来说，这个协议要求设备进行多轮询问-响应（challenge-response exchange），然后计算这个过程的时间，最后用这个时间估计设备间的距离。在实际应用中，这种协议的安全性基于设备的通信频道（communication channel），频道的特征会影响询问-响应的时间，从而影响距离估计的正确性。只有当协议被完整的执行的时候，我们才能确保距离限制的可靠性和安全性。 传统上来说，距离限制协议可用于加强射频识别（RFID）/无接触卡类系统的安全性。然而这类设备的通信频道通常较为简单，传输速率有限制。在实际应用中，如果我们加强这种频道抵抗距离相关的攻击的能力，这个频道的可靠性就会降低，同时会产生频道的错误。部分距离限制协议在交换询问响应信息的时候不能容忍错误，它们只是简单地设定了一个可接受的错误阈值。如果我们想建立一个可容忍错误响应的协议，我们需要考虑协议的错误接受（把攻击者的信息视为频道错误并且接受）以及错误拒绝（拒绝了正确的设备或者信息）的概率。现有的可容忍错误的距离限制协议需要额外的通信，例如额外的询问响应或者验证信息，从而达到与无错误容忍协议接近的错误接受和错误拒绝率。尽管传输额外的信息是一个有效的解决方案，然而当传输时间有限制，并且协议的通信频道速度较慢时，额外的信息交换就会影响性能。 在这个项目中，我们将研究如何在响应功能（response function，用于回应challenge询问）中加入错误改正的代码，在距离估计的步骤中能容忍更多的错误，从而获得可接受的错误接受和错误拒绝率，同时减少额外的询问响应以及验证信息的数据。我们也会考虑尽量做到较短的功能执行时间，一致性强的功能执行过程，从而防止早期响应信息的泄露。这些改进会加强距离限制协议的可靠性，减少协议的执行时间，从而使距离限制协议变成一个更加实用的安全机制。

11214620.label: Realisation of objectives
11214620.value: All three objectives of the project were fully achieved. In Objective 1, we considered the use of error-correcting codes (ECC) in pre-commitment distance-bounding (DB) protocols. We demonstrated that a resilient protocol using an ECC approach to cryptographic exchange errors can provide improved performance over the currently used threshold system. To validate our idea, we integrated a ECC (Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH)) into a prominent pre-commitment protocol design by Brands and Chaum (BC), finding that the use of non-systematic codes improves protocol security (decreased attack success probability). Moreover, we provided further discussion on how to configure ECCs and protocols to minimize the protocol failure rate while maintaining adequate attack success probability. For previous works on using ECC in DB the success probability of adversaries increases compared to a simple error threshold method for the same number of n exchange rounds. This was due to systemic codes being used, which results in some of the exchange rounds being calculated with redundant error checking bits and these bits being predictable. Our work mitigated this issue by integrating non-systematic ECCs, which do not contain original messages and reduce the predictable bits. This allows the protocol to achieve similar security as an error threshold, but without the need to transmit all the exchanges messages and do reconciliation between the parties after the timed distance-bounding stage. This results in a protocol that can execute faster while being resilient to errors, thus reducing the need to rerun the protocol. We evaluated the security levels achieved by non-systematic codes by first applying both systematic and non-systematic codes into the BC distance-bounding protocol and comparing performance with existing other error-resilient DB protocols. A journal article on this work has been published in IEEE TII (C.8.1). In response to question raised in mid-term report feedback on choice of TII, we note that our work intersects security and reliability. At this time there is more similar work in the field of industrial communication, where security, timeliness and the resilience to errors is seen as equally important in process control and factory automation. IEEE TII is the leading publication in industrial communication and related areas. In Objective 2, we considered the use of ECC types into pre-computation DB protocols. The ECC method developed in Objective 1 is not appropriate taken the difference between pre-commitment and pre-computation protocols in calculating cryptographic responses. DB protocols are mainly composed of three phases: an initialization phase, a timed (distance) bounding phase and an optional verification phase. Communication during the initialization and verification phases are not time critical. In these two phases the verifier and the prover exchange messages over a normal ‘slow’ channel and perform conventional cryptographic operations. Communication during the bounding phase is obviously time critical and involves the use of a special `fast’ channel and response function. Variability in the time needed to calculate and send the response would influence round-trip time and result in an inaccurate bound. In a pre-commitment protocol the ECC can be applied during the initialization phase (to a single string of possible responses), while in a pre-computation protocol the ECC needs to be applied during the timed phase (as there are two strings of possible responses). We studied different ECCs and developed a response-function design integrating a convolutional code. Depending on choice of code, this design has the added advantage of providing error correction at the verifier of the challenge and the response. This design significantly differs from previous works on error-corrected DB protocols, which only considered pre-commitment protocols. We provide analysis of both the False Accept Rate (FAR) and False Reject Rate (FRR) under distance and mafia fraud attack scenarios. We simulated the performance of the protocol design for both attack scenarios at different noise levels if implemented using a ISO 14443 channel (used in contactless payment, which is prominent use case for DB protocols) validating our analysis. This work is completed but still under review (Part C.8.4) and includes findings from Objective 3. We will continue to revise this output until successful dissemination and any publication costs has been budgeted for from other projects. In Objective 3, we consider the feasibility of implementing error correcting response functions. In implementing DB response functions integrating ECCs our main concern at the time of writing the proposal was timing side-channels, i.e. that different inputs would yield variable processing delay and this would leak information about the pending response. When working on this objective and studying related literature this remained the only feasible security issue, so we focused on evaluating ECC implementations from this perspective. In addition, based on feedback on our work in Objective 2 we realised that apart from the security aspect there was also concerns about the feasibility of implementing the ECC function during the timed phase. The ECC in pre-commitment protocols was executed before the timed phased of the protocol so less concern with implementation. However, when integrating ECC into pre-computation protocols the computation is done during the timed phase. So aside from possible timing side-channel issues, the speed of implementation in addition to the timing consistency of the response needed further consideration. The findings from Objective 3 would therefore contribute towards showing that the design in Objective 2 can be practical. The timing side-channel issue was also primarily a concern in the pre-computation protocol as the timing variation resulting from the ECC would be observable when observing the Prover’s responses, while in the pre-commitment protocol it is not. The dissemination of Objectives 2 and 3 therefore converged with the main focus being the protocol design, with the results of Objective 3 supporting the design’s feasibility. To evaluate timing, we implemented selected ECCs (convolutional codes) that are publicly available, e.g. FPGA IP cores. We implemented in Verilog a response structure, approximating the DB response with the integrated ECC. These were simulated in ModelSim ME and evaluated on a Microchip Polarfire FPGA. As the project progressed, we learned that FPGA-like hardware implementation of ECCs are more representative of what is integrated into transceivers. The simulation and experimental results show that there is a limited scope for timing side-channels as output timing is consistent regardless of input/current state, with response computed in a clock cycle. For example, a device with a 50 MHz clock will compute in 20 ns. This shows that the ECC response is feasible during the timed phase as it executes fast and with consistent/predictable timing. During this project we also worked on ideas that links closely to the purpose of distance bounding in terms of the assurance of device proximity. It was challenging to recruit research staff/student early on during Covid (most of the core work was done by a graduating PhD student that transitioned to post-doc) so the additional work was done to aid PhD training (work done by Liu towards his thesis was supported with this grant C.9.5, the grant supported some works by later PhD students Boshoff/Nkrow C.8.2, C.8.3, C.9.3, C.9.4) and undergraduate research experience (C.9.6 is not closely linked to project but supported an undergraduate student’s project).

11214620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214620.value: 1) We developed an improved error-resilient pre-commitment distance-bounding protocol design, that integrated a BCH ECC into the seminal Brands-Chaum protocol. Our design improved on prior works on ECC into pre-commitment protocols, providing the same benefits of reduced overhead while offering reduced attack success probability(C.8.1). 2) We developed an error-resilient pre-computation distance-bounding protocol, that integrated convolutional codes into the Hancke-Kuhn protocol. This is the first design that uses ECC for error-resilience in pre-computation protocols. We also implemented response functions based on convolutional codes and demonstrated that these can do the required computation in a consistent and fast manner, which allows for the response function to be realistically used during the timed distance-bounding phase(C.8.4). Early on in the project, while studying efficient cryptography implementation and security for resource constrained devices as preparation for protocol implementation, two papers were published at ICPADS(C.9.1+C.9.2) on IoT security and optimized implementation of the Kyber cryptographic mechanisms. We worked on ideas that are not necessarily related to core Objectives, but links closely to the purpose of distance bounding in terms of having some assurance that devices are within close proximity. We focused on whether devices on a person could more reliably pair by sensing behavioural characteristics of the host, i.e. same observed behaviour can yield shared secret and assurance that located on the same person. 3) In preparation, we studied a large body of work on continuous behavioural biometrics and developed a framework for comparison focused on data sampling method(C.8.2, this paper was submitted April 2022 and under first-round review for 2 years). 4) We demonstrated the feasibility of two devices using rotational data (gyroscope) instead of the more comment acceleration data to pair(C.9.5). 5) We developed a gait-based key sharing/paring method based on signal morphing. This allowed two devices at any location on a person to reliably pair and recognise that they are the same person. Our method exhibits much faster training and inference times, while requiring much less initial observable training data (15s of walking vs more than 3 minutes of walking)(C.8.3). 6) We evaluated the use of ultra-wideband(UWB) channel impulse response(CIR) data to do device pairing. UWB CIR results from multi-path propagation of transmission and is very environment dependent. We showed that it is feasible for UWB devices to pair, using data easily extracted from existing off-the-shelf modules(C.9.3).

We are continuing to work on these and other approaches to secure ranging and have prepared a GRF proposal on this topic in the 2025/26 call.

11214620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214620.value: Authentication decisions often need to be based on physical proximity to a location. For instance, ideally a payment card must be physically presented to a payment terminal before payment is taken. One of the prominent approaches to provide secure proximity verification is distance-bounding protocols but implementing these protocols is challenging because the security of these protocols depends both on cryptographic and time-of-flight channel design. In practice, if we implement these protocols over a channel that is resistant to known distance-bounding attack scenarios it would reduce the reliability of the channel and introduce channel errors, which will cause the protocol to fail. Current proposals for error-resilient distance-bounding require additional data transmission that extends the protocol execution time. At the same time allowing for errors also impacts security, i.e. if we allow incorrect responses an attacker trying to guess the responses has an increased chance to get enough correct. Our work integrated error-correcting codes into distance-bounding protocols, producing response functions that allows for errors during protocol execution without additional data transmission while achieving acceptable security performance. This improves protocol reliability and execution time, which contributes to distance-bounding becoming a practical security mechanism.

11214820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214820.value: 第四代先进核反应堆的发展对核结构材料在高温、高剂量环境下的性能提出了更严峻的挑战。近年来，新型高熵合金的出现受到材料科学家的广泛关注。研究报道指出仅依赖成分调控，体心立方（FCC）高熵合金能大幅度地提升材料的抗辐照性能，为发展抗辐照材料提供了新的设计理念。具体来说，材料主元素的增大能够有效的缩短电子和声子的平均自由程，改变缺陷的形成能、迁移能，从而推迟缺陷的演变（如位错环、空洞的长大等），获得更好的抗辐照性能。然而，大多数FCC高熵合金的组织结构简单，其强度往往在高温很难维持，这大大地限制了其在第四代先进核反应堆高温、高剂量环境下的实际应用。为了满足第四代核反应堆高温、高剂量的要求，本项目旨在设计并研究具有“FCC+L12”双相结构高熵合金的辐照性能。这样的设计具有两点优势，第一，高密度多主元共格纳米析出相的引入能有效地触发析出强化，有望获得优异的高温机械性能；其次，高密度多主元共格纳米析出相能提供更多缺陷阱，同时FCC基体又维持高熵合金原有成分复杂且可控的特点，两者的结合有望获得材料抗辐照性能的进一步提升。以上两点包括优异的高温机械性能和抗高剂量辐照对安全可靠的核应用问题至关重要。 为了更深入的理解辐照对多主元共格纳米析出强化高熵合金的影响，本项目将以三个科学问题为出发点加以研究。首先，我们将定量地分析辐照诱导缺陷的产生，如点缺陷团簇、位错环、空洞等的分布及数量等。其次，结合透射电镜及三维原子探针等先进表征手段，从原子层面揭示辐照诱导的偏析行为，着重关注元素在晶界、位错以及空洞上的偏析情况，讨论并揭示辐照诱导偏析机理。最后，我们将评估不同成分多主元共格纳米相的在辐照下相稳定性问题，探索成分与相稳定性的内联关系，揭示结构稳定性的机制。 本项目的完成为多主元共格纳米析出强化高熵合金在极端环境下的辐照行为提供了更全面和深入的理解，为加速抗辐照高熵合金的开发提供了有效的指导。

11214820.label: Realisation of objectives
11214820.value: In the project, we designed three different L12-strengthened multicomponent alloys, i.e., Ni59.9-xCoxFe13Cr15Al6Ti6B0.1 (x=0, 15, 30 at.%), to study the influence of coherent nanoparticles on the radiation defects behavior. The three alloys are hereafter referred to as 0Co, 15Co and 30Co. The ion irradiation experiments were carried out at the University of Michigan and National Tsing Hua University. The post-irradiation characterizations including TEM and APT analysis were performed at the City University of Hong Kong. All the proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. The details of objectives realization were illustrated one by one, as follows: 1. To design high entropy alloys (HEAs) reinforced by various L12-type multicomponent nanoparticles (MCNPs). Nanoparticles provide a crucial basis for developing high-performance structural materials with potentially superb mechanical properties and radiation resistance for nuclear applications. However, the general wisdom often fails to work well due to the poor thermal stability of nanoparticles, and the rapid coarsening of these particles will lead to the accelerated failures of these materials especially at elevated temperatures. Through a combination of various complementary experimental techniques and theoretical simulations, we find the key to effectively stabilizing the second-phase nanoparticles in a chemically complex high-entropy metallic system, i.e., Ni59.9-xCoxFe13Cr15Al6Ti6B0.1. The morphology and chemical composition of the L12-type MCNPs were characterized by SEM, TEM and APT. The thermal stability of the three alloys were tested by evaluating the coarsening behavior of the L12-type MCNPs after isothermal aging treatments at different temperatures. 2. To reveal the effect of the novel L12-type MCNPs on the irradiation response of the dual-phase HEAs under irradiation. Two sets of ion irradiation experiments were carried out for the developed materials, i.e., the 0Co, 15Co and 30Co alloys. The first set of ion irradiation was conducted at the University of Michigan with 8 MeV Ni ions to a peak damage of 30 dpa and 100 dpa at 873 K, 30 dpa at 973 K and 30 dpa at 1073 K. The second set of ion irradiation was conducted at National Tsing Hua University by 275 keV He ions at 1073 K to a peak damage of 1.5 dpa. Based on the irradiation experiments, the radiation defect behaviors were fully explored at various temperatures and dose conditions. The microstructural evolution of irradiated samples was examined by TEM. The crystalline structure of radiation induced defects were characterized. Different types of defects were identified and their size and number density were quantify through the obtained TEM images. 3. To explore the radiation-induced segregation (RIS) and reveal the underlying segregation mechanisms of the irradiated MCNP-strengthened HEAs. We investigated the radiation-enhanced heterogeneity of RIS in the Ni30Co30Fe13Cr15Al6Ti6B0.1 HEA. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) analysis coupled with EDS maps of the individual elements provides insight into the local RIS effects at the SF plane and He bubbles. A strong RIS at the SF plane and He bubbles was clearly detected by quantitatively correlative TEM/APT measurement. The results showed that a strong Ni depletion and Co enrichment can be observed at the SF plane. The chemical profile across the SF plane and the bubble revealed a significant Co enrichment of up to ∼32 at.% and ~78 at.%, respectively. 4. To evaluate the elemental effects on the phase stability of the L12-type MCNPs in the irradiated dual-phase HEAs. To reveal the phase stability of the developed alloys under irradiation at different temperatures, the distributions of ordered L12-type MCNPs after irradiation were evaluated through the TEM. From the representative DF-TEM images of the L12-type MCNPs acquired from regions subjected to different irradiation doses, with the corresponding selected area diffraction patterns (SADPs) along the <112>zone axis, all the 600℃-irradiated alloys displayed a gradual shrinkage of the ordered L12-type MCNPs as the dose level increases, together with the gradually fainted superlattice diffraction spots. This means that the irradiation-induced disordering of the ordered nanoparticles occurred in all the alloys. In strong contrast, the morphology of the high-density nanoprecipitates in all the three alloys remain stable and unaffected by radiation at 700 and 800 °C. Simultaneously, the nearly constant intensity of superlattice reflections and ordering parameters confirm that L12-type MCNPs maintain their stability during ion irradiation at high temperatures. 5. To establish the composition-microstructure-property relationship and guide the further design of irradiation-tolerant HEAs. Based on the experimental observations and atomistic simulations, increasing Co content in the studied alloy system can not only increase the density of the coherent nanoparticles but also decrease the vacancy diffusivity. The effects of composition on the radiation defects were obtained that the evolution of voids and bubbles were delayed by increasing the Co content of alloy system. Thus, we draw a guideline for the development of the radiation tolerant materials.
