11214820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214820.value: 1. We demonstrated that ultra-stable nanoparticles at 800~1000 °C can be achieved by a controllable sluggish lattice diffusion (SLD) effect in the alloys. Our diffusion kinetic simulations reveal that the Co element leads to a significant reduction in the interdiffusion coefficients of all the main elements, especially for the Al element, with a maximum of up to 5 orders of magnitude. Utilizing first-principles calculations, we further unveil the incompressibility of Al induced by the increased concentration of Co plays a critical role in controlling the SLD effect. 2. We found that void growth was effectively suppressed in the alloys with a high density of coherent nanoparticles. The void swelling rates of the three alloys were less than 1% after the radiation at 873 K to a peak damage of 100 dpa. In the He-radiated materials, most of the bubbles were found to be entrapped at the phase boundary of the L12-type MCNPs. Those results suggested that the precipitates/matrix interface can act as effective trapping sites for vacancies and He atoms. Meanwhile, the void swelling and bubble growth tends to be suppressed with the increasing Co content. Based on the diffusion kinetic simulations, the suppressed growth of vacancy-type defects can be attributed to the restrained vacancy diffusivity. Meanwhile, the higher density of nanoparticles in the Co-rich alloy may provide more sinks to suppress the growth of the vacancy-type defects. 3. Compared to the chemical composition, radiation temperature plays a more important role in the phase stability of the MCNP-strengthened alloys. Under certain high temperature irradiation conditions, the radiation damage (disordering and dissolution) and recovery (reverse ordering and reverse precipitation) of the MCNP-strengthened alloys can reach a dynamic balance, that is, the "self-healing" effect under irradiation. 4. The RIS behavior was determined to be associated with inverse Kirkendall mechanism which suggested that the diffusivities of the elements either via vacancies or interstitial atoms play a critical role in the evolution of RIS. In the ordered L12 phase, Ni defects including Ni vacancies and Ni antisite defects were generally the majority defects in the irradiated Ni 3Al-type phase, implying that Ni has the largest diffusion coefficient in the L12 phase. Whereas, Co is often suggested to be the slowest diffuser in many multicomponent alloys and Ni-based alloys. Consequently, the fastest Ni element diffuses away and leaves an enrichment of Co, the slowest diffusing species, at sinks such as SF, bubble and void.

11214820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214820.value: For the future work, we highly encourage the colleagues in the nuclear material community to do the following works along our track: (1) Conducting dual-beam ion irradiation experiments (Ni+He) on the MCNP-strengthened HEAs is recommended to emulate the neutron irradiation damage in the advanced nuclear systems; (2) Examine the phase stability of MCNP-strengthened HEAs irradiated at high temperatures to a higher damage value. So that we can provide useful guidance for irradiation-resistant materials design and greatly accelerate the development of the science and engineering of the L12-strengthened HEAs for nuclear applications. (3) Employ state-of-the-art machine learning methods to discover more effective alloying strategies for developing structural materials for nuclear applications, ensuring a balance of phase stability, low activation, and high strength.

11214820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214820.value: Faced with growing global energy challenges and increasing environmental pollution, there is an urgent need for sustainable clean energy to achieve carbon neutrality. Among the various options, generation-four nuclear energy systems are notable for their enhanced safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Since the advent of nuclear fission energy, global research has prioritized developing high-performance structural materials to ensure reactor safety. Consequently, innovating radiation-tolerant structural materials is crucial for the deployment of advanced nuclear reactors. In this project, we successfully tune the vacancy diffusivity and densities of coherent nanoparticles by adjusting the chemical composition of MCNP-strengthened HEAs. We find that the radiation-induced void welling, bubble growth and dislocation loops can be tailored by this method with careful design. The outcome of this project will certainly benefit the development of novel materials for nuclear application and embody the contribution of HK scientists for the nuclear energy.

11215220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215220.value: 近些年来，小型飞行机器人的研究受到格外多的研究者的关注，这得益于它们在侦查、运输等方面的可观的应用前景。这些小型机器人未来可能彻底改变我们的生产生活方式。然而受限于空气动力学的尺度效应，小型飞行机器人的飞行效率显著低于传统的大型飞行器，这直接影响了这些小型飞行机器人的滞空时间和工作效能。 在一些常见的小型飞行机器人平台中，多旋翼飞行器受到了格外多的关注，这是由于其具有的简单的机械结构和悬停的飞行能力。这种飞行器虽然具备优良的可操作性，但飞行效率明显低于具有较大翼面面积的固定翼飞行器。在一些需要装备更多传感器、执行器的飞行任务中，其较低的飞行能量效率就成为了主要的限制条件。 本提案提出了一种具备更高能量效率和更佳的飞行操作性能的飞行机器人——RRR（Reconfigurable Revolving-Wing Robot）。在所提的研究中，我们将通过以下三个步来解决飞行器的效率和功能问题。首先，我们将研究并提出一种厘米尺度的，仿翼果旋翼飞行机器人。该机器人具备一对的反向固定的翼和两个螺旋桨驱动器。通过自旋，RRR可以悬停于空中。较大的翼面面积则可保障了该机器人更佳的飞行效率。独特的设计使得该机器人可以独立的控制其三个平动自由的和两个姿态自由度——虽然机器人本身是欠驱动的，但一定程度上可视为全驱动的飞行机器人，这将赋予该机器人卓越的操作控制性能。第二步，受到折纸技术启发，我们将设计一种可折叠的机架结构。通过折叠机翼，两台RRR可以结合在一起并形成一台常规的四旋翼飞行机器人——RRR2。这种模块化的设计赋予该机器替代性的飞行模式，从而增强了该平台的多功能性。最后，我们实现太阳能动力的飞行。小尺度飞行器具备更高的表面积-质量比，另外，固定翼的引入也进一步增加了该比值。这使得太阳能动力下的永久飞行成为可能。这一成就将显著提升小型飞行器的滞空飞行时间。 本研究从根本上提升了小型飞行机器人的滞空飞行时间并扩大了飞行机器人的应用范围，其主要贡献如下：1）开发了一种具有更高飞行能量效率和可控制性的小型欠驱动飞行机器人；2）提出一种模块化的多模态的飞行机器人；3）利用小尺度机器人更大的表面积-质量比，为太阳能动力的小型飞行机器人提供可能性。

11215220.label: Realisation of objectives
11215220.value: The RRR2 (Reconfigurable Revolving-Wing Robot with Modular Multi-Locomotion) project set out to advance the field of bio-inspired aerial robotics through three main objectives: (1) the design, fabrication, and characterization of a highly controllable revolving-wing robot; (2) the development and demonstration of a modular, reconfigurable airframe capable of bimodal aerial locomotion; and (3) preliminary integration of lightweight, high-efficiency solar cells to explore extended mission endurance for micro aerial vehicles (MAVs). Objective 1 This objective has been fully realized and culminated in the publication in Science Robotics. Inspired by autorotating samara seeds, the robot employs two large revolving wings for lift and two motor-driven propellers to induce yaw torque, enabling sustained gyration. The design optimization process integrated blade element theory and momentum analysis to balance aerodynamic efficiency and actuation dynamics. Wings with a 19.5° pitch angle and tapered profiles were optimized to exploit unsteady aerodynamics, maintaining a stable leading-edge vortex (LEV) for enhanced lift-to-drag ratios. The fabricated prototype, weighing 35.1 g, utilized lightweight polyimide film wings reinforced with carbon fiber ribs, ensuring rigidity during high-speed rotation (≈18.8 rad/s) while minimizing structural deformation. Passive attitude stability was achieved by positioning the center of mass below the aerodynamic center, allowing the robot to remain upright without active feedback, as validated through open-loop tests where inclination angles stayed below 20° despite perturbations. A tailored control strategy addressed underactuation by modulating differential propeller thrust to stabilize altitude and track trajectories, enabling precise position control in laboratory flights. The robot demonstrated a power loading of 8.0 g/W—double that of comparable multirotor drones—and a flight endurance of 14.9 minutes (extending to 24.5 minutes with a larger battery). Applications such as environmental mapping and panoramic imaging were showcased using onboard sensors, leveraging the revolving motion for 360° sensing. These results collectively satisfy the objectives: the optimized design and fabrication yielded a highly efficient platform, while dynamic modeling and control strategies enabled stable, controlled flight, validated through extensive laboratory experiments. Objective 2 The second objective consisted of fabricating and testing a modular airframe that allows for human-assisted transformation, targeting the demonstration of bimodal aerial locomotion—specifically, combining revolving-wing and quadrotor flight configurations. Passive Sweep Mechanism and Bimodal Flight: Building on the samara-inspired revolving-wing robot from Objective 1, we introduced a passive sweep angle mechanism that enables seamless transitions between revolving-wing and forward flight modes within a single platform. This mechanism employs an adaptive hinge joint, allowing the wings to passively change sweep angle in response to aerodynamic loads, which shifts the center of pressure relative to the center of mass and generates the required pitch torque for mode switching. Unlike earlier designs that required additional actuators, this approach achieves bimodal flight with reduced mechanical complexity and mass. Flight tests with a 30 g prototype demonstrated robust performance, including controlled transitions between revolving and forward flight, thereby significantly broadening the robot’s operational envelope and validating the effectiveness of passive mode switching. SplitFlyer Concept and Modular Locomotion: Further advancing modularity,we present SplitFlyer Air, a modular quadcopter capable of autonomously separating into two independently controllable bicopters during flight. Each bicopter module is powered by only two propellers and operates with severe underactuation, maintaining stable flight with yaw rates exceeding 50 rad/s. Both the quadcopter and bicopter configurations are described and controlled using a unified dynamic framework derived from reduced attitude dynamics. The transformation is enabled by a preloaded elastic catapult mechanism actuated by a shape memory alloy, which delivers a rotational impulse of up to 18.3 rad/s to each bicopter upon separation. Experimental results demonstrate reliable mid-air disassembly at altitudes as low as 0.8 meters, as well as trajectory tracking with a root-mean-square position error of 8.9 cm (helical path) and 25.0 cm (step path) for the bicopters. The adaptive scalability of SplitFlyer Air highlights its potential for search and rescue operations and dynamic swarm deployment, allowing rapid multiplication of agents in response to mission demands. Objective 3 Feasibility Analysis of Solar-Powered Flight for Revolving-Wing Drones Our analysis demonstrates that sustained, solar-powered flight is achievable for lightweight, samara-inspired revolving-wing drones, provided that key quantitative criteria are met. For a 70-gram vehicle equipped with four large wings, each with an area of 150 cm² (totaling 600 cm²), the power required for continuous flight is estimated at 8.8 W. This means each wing must generate at least 2.2 W under standard solar irradiance (1 kW/m²). We account for practical limitations by assuming that only 80% of the wing area is effectively covered by solar cells, leading to an effective area of 120 cm² per wing. To meet these power demands, the integrated solar cells must achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of at least 18.3%. Additionally, given a strict weight budget of 5 grams per wing for the solar panels, the specific power output required is no less than 0.44 W per gram. These benchmarks—wing area, effective coverage, PCE, and specific power—form the quantitative foundation confirming that solar-powered, enduring flight is indeed feasible for our platform. Strategy for Achieving Sustained Solar-Powered Flight To realize this vision, our research plan proceeds in a series of integrated tasks. We begin by refining our vehicle sizing and energetics model to optimize the mass and power allocation, ensuring that the drone remains highly efficient even as it incorporates the additional weight of solar panels. The next step is to develop lightweight, flexible perovskite solar cell modules by scaling up from small prototypes to large-area devices suitable for wing integration. This involves innovating both in the fabrication process—using blade-coating for uniform, high-quality films—and in material selection, including engineering additives for optimal crystal growth and robust, ultra-thin encapsulation layers for environmental protection. Our goal is to consistently achieve PCE above 18% and specific power output greater than 0.44 W/g in panels of 150 cm² area. Alongside this, we will design and integrate lightweight, efficient power electronics to manage solar energy harvesting with maximum power point tracking (MPPT), ensuring stable operation under variable sunlight. Initial flight tests with weighted dummy wings will verify aerodynamic performance and stability, paving the way for full integration and demonstration of sustained, solar-powered flight. This research pathway systematically addresses the technical challenges and establishes a clear route to practical, enduring, and autonomous solar-powered aerial robots. Summary In summary, the RRR2 project has delivered on its three main objectives: (1) achieving state-of-the-art performance in samara-inspired revolving-wing robotic flight; (2) pioneering modular and bimodal airframe architectures with robust experimental results; and (3) laying the groundwork for solar-powered MAVs through rigorous component characterization and preliminary integration.

11215220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215220.value: The RRR2 project has delivered several key breakthroughs in the field of bio-inspired aerial robotics, as evidenced by multiple peer-reviewed publications and technical milestones. First, the project achieved the successful design, fabrication, and experimental validation of a samara-inspired revolving-wing robot, which demonstrated highly efficient hovering and passive attitude stability. By optimizing wing geometry and integrating a unique under-actuated design—featuring two large wings and dual propeller actuation—the robot achieved a power loading of 8.0 g/W, significantly surpassing conventional multirotor MAVs, and achieved flight endurance up to 24.5 minutes with an extended battery [1]. The design’s passive stability was validated through open-loop disturbance tests, and its 360° panoramic sensory capabilities were demonstrated for mapping and imaging tasks [Bai et al., Science Robotics, 2022]. Second, the project advanced the concept of modular and reconfigurable MAVs by developing two distinct platforms. The first, a passive sweep angle mechanism, enabled seamless transitions between revolving-wing and forward flight modes within a single platform. This actuator-free transition, achieved by an adaptive hinge joint, validated robust bimodal performance and expanded the operational envelope for small aerial robots [Bai et al., IEEE RA-L, 2022]. The second, SplitFlyer Air, realized in-flight modularity by autonomously separating a quadcopter into two independently controllable bicopters. This system, based on a preloaded elastic catapult and shape memory alloy actuation, demonstrated reliable mid-air disassembly, with each module maintaining stable, high-rate yaw flight and trajectory tracking [Bai et al., IEEE/ASME TMECH, 2022]. These results establish a new benchmark in the field for both passive morphing and active modular transformation in MAVs. Third, the project systematically analyzed the feasibility of solar-powered flight for revolving-wing MAVs. Through detailed energetic modeling and component testing, the team identified the power and mass requirements for sustainable solar-powered flight. The integration of lightweight, high-efficiency solar modules and custom power electronics demonstrated that solar-assisted flight is attainable for samara-inspired platforms within target mass and efficiency constraints, laying the groundwork for future fully autonomous and enduring aerial robots. Importantly, these findings formed the scientific and technical foundation for a Collaborative Research Fund (CRF) proposal submitted to the RGC in the 2023/24 round. The proposal was positively received, making it to the final shortlist for full proposal submission and interview, although it was ultimately not funded. In terms of knowledge transfer and impact, the project resulted in several high-impact publications, a filed patent on reconfigurable quadrotor design, and the successful training of postgraduate researchers. Collectively, these outcomes significantly advance the state-of-the-art in bio-inspired, modular, and sustainable aerial robotics

11215220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215220.value: The outcomes of the third objective provide a strong technical and analytical foundation for resubmitting a proposal focused on solar-powered revolving-wing MAVs. The quantitative benchmarks and integration strategies established, covering power requirements, efficient solar coverage, and lightweight power electronics, directly inform a revised research plan that addresses the technical feasibility of sustained solar-powered flight. Building on the positive reception and shortlist status of our previous CRF proposal, we will refine our application by incorporating the latest results, emphasizing both technical readiness and the broader impact of long-endurance, autonomous MAVs for persistent aerial tasks. In parallel, we will explore real-world applications where the unique features of these platforms—namely, high efficiency, low noise, and human-friendly design—can be leveraged despite known limitations. Potential use cases include indoor or urban environmental monitoring, crowd observation, and infrastructure inspection, where wind disturbances are minimized and payload demands are moderate. Further research will focus on improving wind disturbance rejection through advanced control algorithms and optimizing payload integration for lightweight sensing modules. Collectively, these efforts will demonstrate practical relevance while refining the platform for broader deployment, thereby strengthening the case for renewed funding and collaborative development.

11215220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215220.value: The RRR2 project aimed to create new types of small flying robots inspired by nature, particularly the spinning seeds of maple trees. Our team successfully built a tiny robot that flies using large revolving wings, similar to how these seeds glide and spin through the air. This innovation allows the robot to hover and maneuver much more efficiently than traditional drones, using less energy and staying stable even without constant adjustments. We also developed new designs that let the robot change its shape and flying modes. For example, switching from spinning flight to gliding, or even splitting into two separate flying units mid-air for more versatile missions. In addition, we explored how to power these lightweight robots using solar cells, taking early steps toward drones that could fly for long periods without needing batteries. These advances could lead to safer, quieter, and more energy-efficient drones for tasks like environmental monitoring or search and rescue in places where traditional drones struggle [2][4].

11215420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215420.value: Microwave imaging for medical diagnostics is a hot topic in academia and industry over the past decade. Much effort has been dedicated to the detection of breast cancer and detection of brain stoke. Microwave imaging diagnostics is non-invasive as microwave is non-ionized radiation. More importantly, microwave imaging systems can be a transportable device. The brain stroke is one of the major causes of death on this planet. There are two types of strokes. The course of treatment for these two types of strokes is not the same. Early thrombolytic therapy is effective for ischemic stroke patients but it can be damaging for hemorrhage patients. Doctors nowadays mainly rely on CT scan or MRI for the diagnosis. These systems are expansive, slow in measurement time and bulky in structure. A compact and mobile imaging system that can be used to monitor a patient in real time continuously anywhere would be attractive in comparison to the existing medical imaging systems. Breast cancer might be the most frequently diagnosed disease for females globally. This cancer is a fast growth of malignant cells that can circulate to other parts of the human body. To reduce the risks of the mortality of the breast cancer, the malignant tissue should be diagnosed and the serious illness should be treated at the early stage. The X-ray mammography might be the most efficient imaging tool. However, this method has several weaknesses. In particular, it is not accurate to identify breast tumors at their stages. The other two techniques - ultrasound and MRI – are not used in routine breast cancer screening as they have difficulty in early breast cancer detection. For obtaining accurate measurement result, microwave imaging techniques require wideband antenna elements with compact size. Low mutual coupling between antenna elements is a necessary. Many antenna structures have been proposed in the literature for microwave medical imaging. In general, they are either narrow in bandwidth or large in size. The magneto-electric dipole antenna was invented by the principal investigator of this project. It has been developed as a high-performance wideband antenna technology for mobile communications and radar applications. This antenna technology is proposed for microwave medical imaging in this project. The success of this project will help to enhance the performance of future microwave medical imaging systems for early breast cancer detection and early stroke detection which can help to save a lot of lives of human beings. 在過去的十年裡，微波成像在醫療診斷中的應用均是學術界和工業界的熱門話題。人們在乳腺癌的檢測和治療方面作出了很多努力。在腦中風的檢測方面亦做了大量的研究。因微波是非電離輻射，所以微波成像診斷是非侵入性的。更重要的是，微波成像系統可以是個可攜的設備。 腦中風是地球上人類死亡的主要原因之一。腦中風有兩種類型，其治療過程是不一樣的。早期溶栓治療對缺血性腦中風患者有效。但對於出血患者，醫生主要依靠CT掃描或MRI進行診斷。但這些系統體積大，測量時間慢，結構笨重。而緊湊的移動成像系統可用於實時監測病人的情況，與現有的醫療設備相比，具一定的吸引力。 乳腺癌可能是全球女性最常被診斷的疾病。這癌症是一種快速生長的惡性細胞，可感染至人體的其他部位。為降低乳腺癌的死亡風險，惡性細胞或重症應及早確診並治療。乳房的X光檢查可能是最有效的成像工具，但這種方法有幾個弱點。特別是，在乳腺腫瘤時，X光對腫瘤進行辨識時的結果並不準確。現階段，有其他兩種技術-超聲波和磁力共振成像，但不應用於常規的乳腺癌篩查，因他們在辨識早期乳腺癌中有困難。 為獲得準確的測量結果，微波成像技術需要具備以下條件，體積小巧的寬頻天線元件，而天線間的低相互耦合元素亦是必要。文獻中提出了許多天線結構可用於微波醫學成像。一般來說，它們是窄頻寬，或是大頻寬的尺寸。而磁電偶極子天線是由主要研究者發明。它已被開發為高性能的寬頻天線技術，可用於移動通信和雷達應用中。這種天線技術是本項目中提出的微波醫學影像技術。本項目將成功有助提高未來微波醫學成像系統的性能，以利於早期乳腺癌檢測和早期腦中風的檢測，可幫助挽救大量的乳腺癌患者的生命。

The first objective is to develop wideband linaealy polarized and circularly-polarized ME dipole for brain stroke detection and breast cancer detection. We have been able to enhance the design of the ME dipole significantly enabling it to match very well with human bodies with much more bandwidth and good radiation efficiency compared to that for applications for wireless communications. 11215420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215420.value: (1) First, an on-body matched 3-D magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is proposed for EM head imaging systems to detect strokes [1]. The ME dipole, with its differential feed, achieves a wide impedance bandwidth. The antenna exhibits unidirectional and symmetrical radiation patterns in the near-field region, resulting in a stable main beam directed toward the 2-D imaging domain inside the human head. The high front-to-back ratio (FBR) above 18 dB is realized across the entire frequency band by this antenna. The specific absorption rate (SAR) values consistently remain at safe levels throughout the band with an input power of 10 dBm. A head imaging system comprising eight antenna elements is designed and fabricated to validate the detection capability of the proposed antenna. The reconstructed 2-D images of the head interior, using a confocal imaging algorithm, demonstrate the successful detection and localization of different bleeding areas, indicating the potential of the head imaging system for use in clinical trials. (2) Second, a detection capability enhanced antenna with a planar and compact configuration is proposed for portable EM head imaging systems, overcoming the problem of limited detection capability in existing designs for this application [2]. The proposed antenna, developed based on multiple dipoles, exhibits multi-mode resonances and complementary interaction. In the frequency domain, simulated and measured results with the presence of head phantoms show that this compact planar antenna achieves improved performance in both impedance bandwidth and near-field radiation within head tissues, which all contribute to enhancing its stroke detection capability in radar-based EM diagnosis. An array of 12 elements is numerically and experimentally tested in a lab-setting EM head imaging system to validate the detection capability of the proposed antenna. The reconstructed 2-D images inside the head demonstrate successful detection of different stroke-affected areas, even as small as 3 mm in radius, significantly smaller than those reported in relevant works under the same validation setting, confirming the enhanced detection capability of the proposed antenna. (3) Third, an antenna array with high detection capability and implementability is proposed for 3-D EM head imaging systems [3]. The antenna elements are compact with unidirectional radiation patterns over the utilized low-frequency range, ensuring portability and high-energy penetration of the antenna array. An effective array layout is designed based on investigations into the impact of array layouts on the detection capability of the antenna array. This enables accurate localization of stroke-affected areas along three dimensions, addressing the limitations of poor performance along some dimensions in the existing radar-based 3-D EM head imaging systems. A 3-D imaging system based on the proposed array is constructed and validated in stroke monitoring scenarios. The reconstructed 3-D head images demonstrate the accurate localization from three dimensions for variation of stroke-affected areas as small as 2 cm3 in a numerical realistic head model and 5 cm3 in experimental head phantoms, confirming the high detection capability of the antenna array. Furthermore, the proposed array demonstrates implementability in further clinical trials regarding portability, 3-D positioning, and independence from numerical model aid in experiments. A compact wideband antenna for EM breast imaging systems was designed. The antenna achieves an extremely compact size and a significantly improved bandwidth of 160% over the frequency range of 0.8 - 7.2 GHz. Additionally, the antenna presents safe levels of SAR values and fine EM near-field radiation characteristics inside breast tissues. The reconstructed high-quality images of the breast interior in imaging validations demonstrate the promising potenital of the design for further clinical trials.

In fact, the PI has obtained an AoE project as PC, which has an objective to continue this research for medical imaging of various parts of human bodies.

11215420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215420.value: Microwave imaging offers a potential solution by providing a safer, more accessible, and potentially more accurate diagnostic tool. To achieve accurate measurement results, microwave imaging techniques require compact, wideband antenna elements with low mutual coupling between them. Minimizing mutual coupling is essential to ensure high-quality imaging performance. Numerous antenna designs have been proposed in the literature for microwave medical imaging; however, many of these solutions suffer from either limited bandwidth or bulky physical dimensions. The magneto-electric dipole antenna, invented by the principal investigator of this project, has been developed as a high-performance wideband antenna technology, originally for mobile communications and radar applications. In this project, this advanced antenna technology has been developed for use in microwave medical imaging. Its integration is expected to significantly enhance the performance of future imaging systems, particularly for early detection of breast cancer and stroke—potentially saving countless lives through timely and accurate diagnosis.

11215620.label: Project Objectives
11215620.value: To design a high performance microchannel heat sink with hybrid micro/nano structured mesh for high heat flux applications. This novel design integrating with a uniform liquid distribution manifold at a demand-based flow rate will enable optimized liquid and heat transport to obtain high heat transfer performance. To design and construct a test rig to investigate thin-film evaporation/boiling heat transfer in this hybrid mesh microchannel heat sink. The working liquid is provided at a demand-based flow rate, which is of significant difference from the conventional jet impingement. To understand detailed mechanism of thin-film evaporation/boiling heat transfer enhancement through analytical modeling and data obtained. To acquire the boiling curve to the maximum possible heat flux and heat transfer coefficient under various conditions. The effects of structural parameters of the heat sink designed, including those for the mesh (porosity, thickness, and wire diameter), at a demand-based flow rate, will be investigated. To acquire the maximum possible heat transfer capability of the present innovative microchannel heat sink with hybrid micro/nano structured mesh.

11215620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215620.value: 提高能源效率和減少二氧化碳排放量對世界的可持續發展至關重要。由於純電動或混合動力汽車具有高能效和低碳排放的潛力，電動汽車的推廣對於中國大陸或香港而言，是實現降低碳強度的國家目標的重要舉措之一。例如，絕緣柵雙極電晶體（IGBT）之類的功率電子逆變器模組的熱管理，是電動汽車進一步發展的技術挑戰之一。IGBT模組可能會產生很高的熱通量，同時又必須將其保持在相對較低的溫度以下才能保證其功能的正常運轉。相對低溫下如此高的極限熱通量需求，極需合理設計的功能化結構來實現高效氣液相變冷卻。 本計畫將開發一種高性能的微通道熱沉。該熱沉具有跨尺度的微納米結構絲網，並且可以通過導流體實現工質流量按需主動輸入。在該熱沉中將發生劇烈的薄膜蒸發/沸騰傳熱，以冷卻具有高熱通量的電子設備，例如電動汽車中的逆變器模組。具體而言，燒結在基板上的商用微細銅絲網將經過鐳射加工工藝以形成平行微通道，再通過三維導流體提供均勻的工質分佈，且工質流速恰好匹配蒸發沸騰潛熱，以帶走施加的熱量。為了進一步增強工質毛細擴散能力，本項目將在微通道化絲網進行簡單化學鍍膜和額外燒結工藝，製造出穩固的多尺度微納米結構特徵。通過導流體將工質引導到每個微通道的多孔絲網中，這種具有多級微/納米結構絲網的新型熱沉將有望憑藉著增強的毛細性能呈現出非常高效的薄膜蒸發/沸騰效果。該設計優化的熱沉可能會以相對較低的過熱度達到前所未有的臨界熱流密度，以滿足高熱通量電子設備（例如電動汽車中的下一代逆變器模組）的冷卻要求。 本計畫將探索新型多尺度微納米結構絲網熱沉中的薄膜蒸發/沸騰傳熱機理。此外，本項目將研究所開發熱沉的傳熱係數、臨界熱流密度與液體流速的變化關係。本項目的研究成果將有望促進電動汽車或其他高散熱需求電子設備的發展。

11215620.label: Realisation of objectives
11215620.value: Objective 1 was achieved by 100%. An efficient and sustainable hybrid mesh heat sink was developed, as shown in our published paper [1]. The heat sinks were fabricated through high-temperature sintering and chemical treatment. The copper substrates (10 × 10 mm) with ten meniscus microchannels were created via wire electrical discharge machining. Three commercial mesh layers and the copper substrate were diffusion bonded at a high temperature in a reducing atmosphere. The bonded microchannels were then cleaned and chemically treated in a NaOH and (NH4)2S2O8 solution for 30 minutes at 70 ℃. This process produced superhydrophilic nanostructures, enhancing capillary wicking and bubble nucleation, as shown in our previous study [2]. Finally, the heat sinks were rinsed with water and air-dried. From the Scanning Electron Microscope images, the three mesh layers are tightly bonded to the copper substrate. Micropores are formed and nanostructures are uniformly produced on the mesh surface. This configuration provides superior capillary force for liquid wicking. Each microchannel has a height of 0.35 mm, width of 1 mm, and radius of 0.4 mm, while the triple-layer hybrid meshes have a thickness of 0.15 mm and porosity of 66.4%. A uniform liquid supply manifold was developed as seen in our published paper [1], comprising connected parts and a liquid supply layer array. This array includes ten units, each of which was designed to provide liquid into every microchannel. The connected parts secure the layer array and pump the water to every unit. Every unit comprises a liquid channel layer, a container layer, and a spacing layer to ensure precise liquid delivery to each microchannel. The manifold could supply liquid uniformly across the heating surface of the samples. Objective 2 was achieved by 100%. A test rig was constructed to study liquid film boiling heat transfer in the heat sink with the uniform liquid supply manifold, as shown in our published paper [1]. The test setup included a heating block containing 12 heaters for supplying power. Each heater provides up to 150 W. Liquid metal alloy was applied between the copper block and sample to minimize contact thermal resistance. Thermal insulation materials were used to minimize heat losses. Three thermocouples were inserted in the sample to extrapolate heat flux and wall superheat. The top part of the sample with dimensions (10 × 10 × 17.5 mm³) ensured a heating area of 1 cm², while the bottom part (20 × 20 × 1 mm³) connected to the heating block. This setup ensures reliable data collection. Objective 3 was achieved by 100%. The visualization analysis was shown in our published paper [1]. At a low heat flux, bubble nucleation density and departure frequency are low. As the heat flux increases, bubble nucleation density and frequency increase while the diameter decreases when compared with that at the low heat flux, contributing to the heat transfer coefficient (HTC) enhancement. When approaching critical heat flux (CHF), HTC slightly decreases due to the partial dry-out, where vapor bubbles isolate parts of the liquid from the mesh. Even under these conditions, the remarkable capillary wicking of the hybrid meshes continued to promote liquid flow across the entire heat sink surface. The vapor retention within the hybrid mesh layer may be the main factor in degrading heat transfer performance. Then the detailed mechanism of liquid film boiling heat transfer was analyzed through theoretical modelling. The CHF achieved by the heat sink resulted from the liquid wicking and the vapor escape and was theoretically derived. The detailed derivation can refer to our published paper [1]. It can be concluded that the CHF of our developed heat sink was mainly limited by the vapor escape. Objectives 4 and 5 were achieved by 100%. The boiling curves and heat transfer coefficients for different heat sinks and flow rates were obtained as shown in our published paper [1]. The control samples, such as flat surface, microchannel surface, microchannels with a single layer of hybrid mesh, and our proposed heat sink, microchannels with triple layers of hybrid mesh were investigated at various flow rates. The CHFs of the developed heat sink and other control samples were also acquired. The proposed heat sink presents the best heat transfer performance across all the flow rates among all the samples, exhibiting a CHF of over 600 W/cm² at a flow rate of only 0.4 ml/s and a maximum HTC of 38 W/cm²K on the heating surface of 1 cm². The water conversion efficiency and coefficient of performance are much higher than that of control samples, reaching up to 61.2% and 550,000, respectively. Reference: [1] G. Chen, X. Jiang, Y. 11215620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215620.value: This research project has successfully developed an efficient and sustainable hybrid mesh heat sink integrated with an active manifold to harness the benefits of liquid film boiling. Upon the completion of the project, several key findings are revealed as below: 1. Boiling heat transfer enhancement via hybrid meshes: Fundamental pool boiling experiment results showed that the hybrid mesh structures significantly enhance boiling heat transfer. This is due to their exceptional capillary wicking capability and the provision of abundant nucleate sites. The visualization experiments further supported these findings, showing an increase in bubble generation frequency and a reduction in bubble departure diameters. The proposed concept of designing hierarchical structures to enhance bubble nucleates and liquid transport for two phase heat transfer opens a new avenue for cooling electronics. This finding has been published in Applied Thermal Engineering (see Part C, Section 8 [1]). 2. New strategy for superior heat transfer performance and high sustainability: The hybrid mesh heat sink with a manifold demonstrated superior boiling heat transfer performance including high heat transfer coefficients and critical heat flux. Specifically, the heat sink achieved a CHF exceeding 600 W/cm² at a low flow rate of 0.4 ml/s, with a maximum HTC of 38 W/cm²K on the heating surface of 1 cm². Meanwhile, the cooling system exhibited a remarkable water conversion efficiency of 61.2% and a coefficient of performance of 550,000, corresponding to the high CHF. This work provides new guidance on employing boiling in a thin liquid film with minimal liquid transport distance to achieve efficient and sustainable cooling. These findings have been published in Energy Conversion and Management, (see Part C, Section 8 [2]). 3. Theoretical modelling of boiling in thin liquid film: The underlying heat transfer mechanisms were elucidated through theoretical modelling and visualization experiments. The flow visualizations revealed that the hybrid mesh layers maintained sufficient capillary wicking, ensuring that liquid was driven to the top of the channels during vigorous boiling, even approaching CHF. The theoretical predictions, concerning the liquid wicking and vapor escape, indicated that the vapor escape limit was the primary constraint on heat transfer performance. This finding provides a foundation for future design improvements aimed at facilitating vapor escape, which is the critical factor in maximizing CHF. This will be the direction of our future research endeavours.

11215620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215620.value: Based on the research outcomes, there is significant potential to further enhance the critical heat flux (CHF) by optimizing designs to facilitate more efficient vapor escape. Currently, we have designed superhydrophilic nanostructured copper pillars with superhydrophilic insulating membrane to separate the liquid wicking and vapor escape, which has made substantial progress. This design effectively separates the liquid wicking and vapor escape, achieving a CHF of over one thousand and two hundred watt per centimeter square, which is the double of the performance of the hybrid mesh heat sink. This breakthrough confirms that facilitating vapor escape is the key to enhancing the CHF. However, further research is required to fully understand the role of each component in this design. The specific contributions of the copper pillars and the membrane need to be thoroughly investigated. To move forward, we plan to conduct detailed experiments to recover these effects. Furthermore, we are preparing a manuscript that will present these findings.

11215620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215620.value: With the rapid development of electronics, such as computers, electric vehicles, and other advanced electronic equipment, a huge amount of heat may be generated during their operation. Efficient removal of such heat is essential to ensure the reliability and durability of the electronics, in particular for high-power devices. Traditional cooling systems may be unable to dissipate such high heat loads, causing malfunction and/or potential damage to the devices. In this regard, our research project has developed a highly efficient and sustainable cooling system for electronic devices. The designed cooling systems consist of a hybrid mesh structured microchannel heat sink and an active liquid supply manifold. Combining these two features, the cooling systems facilitate the liquid supply and vapor escape, allowing the liquid to evaporate and boil more efficiently, further removing a lot of heat from the heating surface. The results indicate that the cooling system can remove a very high heat flow rate per unit area with minimal energy. This advanced thermal management technology may offer significant benefits for cooling high-power electronics with little energy consumption, promoting the development of the electronics and contributing to a more sustainable future.

11215820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215820.value: 由於深度神經網絡強大的模型容量和允許學習複雜模型的訓練經驗，它已經成為機器學習及其相關領域如計算視覺領域的一種標準模型。然而，對抗樣本是深度神經網絡面臨的一個挑戰，即對網絡的輸入進行人類察覺不到的修改之後神經網絡就會做出錯誤的預測。對抗樣本對深度神經網絡有嚴重的安全威脅，尤其是那些不需要直接接觸深度神經網絡內在推理機制的“黑盒”攻擊。這種不會引起人類注意就可以使深度神經網絡做出錯誤預測的能力會導致惡性的後果，尤其是當下深度神經網絡在一些自動化系統如自動駕駛汽車中變得越來越普遍。因此，為了保證深度神經網絡和基於深度神經網絡的系統在對抗惡意攻擊者時的安全性，防禦對抗樣本變得越來越重要。 防禦對抗樣本的典型方法有對輸入圖片或者圖片的特徵進行去噪和對訓練數據進行增強。然而，這些方法只能解決對抗樣本的“症狀”。對抗樣本的存在揭示了在深度神經網絡訓練中的一個嚴重的根本性缺陷——有越來越多的證據表明對抗樣本是由於神經網絡的泛華誤差，即雖然測試集的精度很好，但是深度神經網絡還是受到過拟合的困擾。因此，防禦對抗樣本最根本的方法是提升深度神經網絡的泛化性或者說防止其過拟合。 在本項目中，我們提出通過改善約束和訓練方法以防止深度神經網絡過拟合來防禦對抗樣本。首先，我們會從理論上探究為何本應該控制網絡複雜度的網絡權重約束在深度神經網絡中失敗，然後提出一個新的約束項來改善這些缺陷。第二，我們會研究使容易受攻擊的特徵被更好地抑制的對抗訓練方法。第三，我們會從理論上分析為什麼在貝葉斯神經網絡中本來應該更少地受到過拟合影響的高斯先驗會變得無效，然後提出新的先驗來解決這些問題。最後，我們對貝葉斯神經網絡提出新的近似推理方法，使后驗的集成網絡在推理時可以被動態地重新採樣從而改善固定的后驗集成網絡在面對對抗樣本時的穩健性。 本項目會解決引起對抗樣本的基本問題，即防止深度神經網絡過拟合，而且會推動我們更好地理解深度神經網絡現在面臨的問題。當深度神經網絡在我們日常生活中的自動化系統中變得越來越普遍，提高我們對深度神經網絡的理解以及使他們在對抗攻擊下具有安全性是一個重要的問題。

11215820.label: Realisation of objectives
11215820.value: 1. We investigating regularization and training methods for training adversarially robust DNNs. We considered both regularization and training approaches. Details in points 2 and 3 below. 2a. We have investigated why standard L2 regularization on weights is not effective, which is due to the weight scale invariance. We propose a new regularization method [C3] that is invariant to weight scaling. The weight-invariant regularizer improves adversarial robustness on MLPs, CNNs, and ResNets, as compared to L2 regularization. 2b. We also investigate effective margin regularization, which can push the classifier margin away from the training samples, and is a complementary approach to adversarial training (which pushes the data points onto the desired the margin). Using both margin regularization and adversarial training improves the adversarial robustness of small-scale MLP an CNNS, as well as large-scale ResNet and WideResNet [C15]. 2c. We develop XAI methods [C9] for investigating failure modes of object detectors, including adversarial attacks. 3a. We investigate a more robust training procedure that can replace batch normalization. The new procedure renormalizes the weights in each iteration of training, and helps to improve the accuracy on a variety of computer vision tasks. We are preparing a paper on this work [J2]. 3b. We derived new loss functions that make training robust for crowd counting [J4]. 3c. We developed new algorithm for better fine-tuning using pre-training data to improve accuracy and robustness [C4], as well as improving generalization and robustness under distributional shifts [C6]. 3d. Besides these works, we also considered improved training and robustness in various applications, including multi-view crowd counting [J1, J3, C12, C14], image captioning [J5, C2], active learning and multiple-instance learning [C1, C5, C7, C14], visual object tracking and segmentation [C8, C10]. 4. Bayesian NNs (BNNs) are computationally expensive for larger models, while using conformal prediction (CP) is more tractable for larger models and also provides confidence values on prediction sets. Thus, rather than investigate adversarial robustness and training for BNNs (which has limited scalability), instead we decided to investigate adversarial robustness for conformal inference models. We find that CP is vulnerable to adversarial attacks, especially the prediction set size will be increased significantly, reducing the usefulness of CP [C13]. We then propose adversarial training methods to defend CP methods from attack [C13]. 5. We propose new training methods to improve uncertainty calibration of BNNs, which is useful for robustness, while also improving efficiency [C11].

11215820.value: This project on adversarial defense has inspired our current project on using adversarial attacks for social good, i.e., instead of attacking the deep neural network, we use adversarial attack to embed imperceptible watermarks into images that can be recovered using the deep neural network. 11215820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215820.value: In this project, we investigate the vulnerabilities of deep neural networks to being fooled by images with imperceptible perturbations. We find that common regularization methods that should prevent overfitting are not effective as the neural networks get deeper, and we thus propose several methods to address this. Improving the robustness of deep neural networks to adversarial attacks is important for guaranteeing their reliability in critical situations.

11215920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215920.value: 異質性是一種在生物系統中廣泛存在且十分重要的特徵，具體表現為生物體的遺傳、表觀遺傳、蛋白質組學和功能表型在時空上的差異性。其中，一種非編碼的小RNA——微小RNA(miRNA)，被發現可以通過與特定mRNA結合以調節其降解或翻譯，從而對細胞的異質性產生重大影響。近年來，利用多靶標的miRNA進行診斷和治療的潛力被逐漸重視，但相關的原位檢測技術，尤其是活細胞內的miRNA原位檢測技術仍然嚴重的缺乏。因此，我們旨在開發一種新穎的，具有革命性的，基於細胞內活檢技術（inCell-Biopsy）的平台，從而實現活細胞異質性在時間上動態變化的監測。技術上來說，該平台基於一個我們持續開發中的利用金剛石納米針作為載體的生物傳感系統。在之前的工作中，該金剛石納米針平台已被證明可通過可逆的，無傷的在細胞膜上打孔來促進細胞內遞送或分離各種活細胞內分子靶標。對監測活細胞內的miRNA來說，金剛石納米針會被修飾上一種具有尺寸選擇性的功能蛋白，並利用功能化的納米針作為“釣魚竿”，從而將miRNA從細胞質中分離並保持細胞存活。然後，每個納米針將充當一個單獨的反應腔，通過在上面進行原位擴增，可視化和定量分析，實現細胞內miRNA的平行，高通量和高靈敏度的分析，從而實現細胞內單拷貝豐度的miRNA的檢測。 隨著inCell-Biopsy技術的進一步發展，我們可以將該方法進一步應用於研究正常和疾病的神經組織中的細胞異質性，通過檢測它們的miRNA表達譜在時空上的不同來幫助診斷，而這是任何現有的任何RNA分析方法都無法實現的。基於大量的納米針個體（每個芯片上萬個針），我們可以對一個大的細胞合團中的每個細胞實現准單細胞分析。此類離散的miRNA表達數據將通過定制的生物信息學和機器學習方法進行分析，以推導複雜生物系統中不同細胞亞群的固有相干性，其中，每個亞群又均具有獨特的miRNA表達譜。這種表達譜在不同時間點上的關聯性將可以進一步揭示細胞狀態從正常狀態轉變為患病狀態的過程，反之亦然。同時，這一信息有助於揭示miRNA表達的動態變化對細胞狀態產生影響的機制。預計該項目的成功將為miRNA分析提供一個革命性的工具，並且在協助開發涉及細胞成分的新興治療策略及相應的質量把控等方面具有巨大的潛力。

11215920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215920.value: This project develops a series of research outcomes centered on the development and application of a nanoneedle-based platform for sequencing-free, high-throughput, and spatially resolved analysis of RNA, particularly focusing on microRNAs (miRNAs) and mRNA methylation. This platform enables non-destructive intracellular "biopsy" by using arrays of vertically aligned diamond nanoneedles functionalized with RNA-binding proteins or antibodies. These nanoneedles can extract targeted RNA molecules directly from live cells or acute tissue slices without the need for amplification, sequencing, or complex tissue processing. The platform allows for multiplexed, single-cell level miRNA profiling, capturing both expression levels and spatial distribution of miRNAs across tissues. It achieves subcellular resolution and is sensitive enough to detect single-copy miRNA molecules, with specificity to single-nucleotide variations. By combining fluorescence imaging with machine learning-based decoding, the system quantifies multiple RNA species in parallel, making it suitable for large-scale studies of cellular heterogeneity. A key application of this technology is in spatial transcriptomics, where it has been used to uncover spatial dynamics of miRNA expression in brain tissues and disease models. For example, it revealed region-specific dysregulation of miRNAs in astrocytes within the hippocampus of schizophrenia model animals, providing new insights into cell-type-specific molecular alterations. Additionally, the platform was extended to analyze m⁶A and m¹A RNA methylation at the gene-specific level. It successfully detected both single and dual methylation events on individual mRNA transcripts, revealing their dynamic regulation under cellular stress conditions. The nanoneedle platform has also demonstrated strong potential in clinical applications, particularly in hematologic cancers. It enabled discrete single-cell miRNA profiling in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), accurately classifying AML subtypes and identifying drug-responsive subpopulations. The integration of machine learning algorithms further enhances its analytical power and diagnostic potential, especially for rare or limited clinical samples. In summary, this research establishes a versatile, amplification-free, and cost-effective platform for spatial and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, capable of profiling post-transcriptional regulation with high sensitivity and precision. Its applications in developmental biology, neuroscience, and oncology highlight its value as a translational tool for both fundamental research and precision medicine.

11215920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215920.value: The nanoneedle-based platform for sequencing-free RNA profiling presents significant potential for further development across both technological and translational domains. Future research can focus on expanding the range of detectable RNA species, including other non-coding RNAs, RNA-protein complexes, and RNA modifications beyond m⁶A and m¹A, by introducing new molecular "baits" on the nanoneedles. The multiplexing capacity can be further enhanced using advanced spectral encoding and multi-round hybridization strategies, enabling whole-transcriptome-scale analysis at single-cell resolution. On the translational front, the platform's compatibility with fresh clinical biopsies positions it as a powerful tool for real-time diagnostics and personalized medicine. Its low cost, high speed, and minimal processing make it ideal for point-of-care applications, especially in oncology and neurodegenerative diseases. A proposed course of action includes clinical validation studies using patient samples from diverse disease backgrounds, followed by integration with AI-driven diagnostic models to establish robust, predictive biomarkers. Additionally, miniaturization of the system and development of automated analysis pipelines will enable broader adoption in clinical laboratories. These steps will bridge the gap between cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and routine clinical diagnostics, accelerating the translation of spatial omics into standard-of-care practices.

11215920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215920.value: This research project introduces a new, non-invasive technology that allows scientists and doctors to “fish out” small genetic materials—called microRNAs and methylated RNAs—from living cells and tissue samples without destroying them. These tiny molecules play important roles in controlling how our genes function and are often linked to diseases like cancer, brain disorders, and other health conditions. The technique uses microscopic diamond needles arranged on a small chip to gently pull these molecules from cells. Once captured, researchers can identify and count them using special fluorescent labels. This method does not require complex procedures like gene sequencing, making it faster, cheaper, and easier to use—especially in clinical settings. With this tool, researchers were able to track how cells change during development, how brain cells are affected in a model of schizophrenia, and how different types of cancer cells respond to treatment. It even helped identify subtypes of leukemia and predict which cells were more likely to resist drugs. In simple terms, this technology provides a powerful new way to study diseases, discover hidden patterns in tissues, and support better diagnosis and treatment decisions—paving the way for more personalized and precise medicine in the future.

11216120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216120.value: 電子顯微鏡技術雖然在傳統的納米尺度成像領域中有著不可替代的作用，但是電子顯微鏡在成像時所產生的高能電子束對樣品造成的輻射劑量相當於在約30米外引爆一枚1000萬噸級的氫彈，因此該技術無法實現對集成電路設備的非破壞性檢測，同時對生物樣品的活體觀測也無法完成。另一方面，傳統光學顯微鏡在非侵入式、實時、大面積和熒光/白光成像等方面依然具有其獨特的優勢。雖然傳統光學顯微鏡技術中近場倏逝波所攜帶高空間頻率的樣品表面信息在遠場光場中的丟失會導致傳統光學顯微鏡無法突破阿貝衍射極限（約一半波長的尺度）。針對傳統光學顯微鏡衍射極限導致光學成像分辨率受限的問題，我們團隊提出利用微流體滲透蒸發裝置制造出基於納米顆粒的超透鏡（NPMs），以實現超分辨光學成像的全新制成方法。目前現有技術還不能夠可靠、精確地制備出具有可控形貌的半球形NPM。因此，本項目提出使用三維微流道裝置，將納米顆粒膠體溶液輸送並填充流道末端的透鏡制備腔室（透鏡室），然後通過滲透蒸發過程得到固化的NPM。與現有基於微球的超透鏡相比，本項目具有兩個主要優點：a）通過增加接觸面積（即從“點”接觸到“面”接觸）來提升透鏡對樣品表面倏逝波的收集效率；b）不受限於微球超透鏡成像中，需要透鏡/浸沒介質折射率比小於2的約束，這也限制了微球超分辨成像的放大倍率和最高分辨率。為了實現具有可控半球形態的超分辨NPM，需要解決的關鍵工程和科學問題如下：1）通過對甘油微液滴大小和形態的調控（如液體表面張力和基底表面的疏水性等因素），制備 “透鏡室”微流道模具；2）優化微流體滲透蒸發的制備條件，以提升NPM的生產效率和可重復性；3）運用數值分析法進一步闡明NPM對表面倏逝波收集與傳播的超分辨成像機制。基於納米顆粒的超透鏡制成方法的研究工作將提升光學顯微鏡在幹燥工作環境中的分辨率和視場，並極大促進可見光超分辨成像等研究領域的發展。本項目將為集成電路檢測和故障分析、基於光學的納米光刻技術和超靈敏光子探測等領域的應用提供一種全新的解決方案，並提升香港在科研及工業領域的國際競爭力。

11216120.label: Realisation of objectives
11216120.value: This project aimed to develop an advanced microfluidic pervaporation system to fabricate nanoparticle-based metalenses (NPMs) for super-resolution imaging in air. The research focused on creating lenses with controlled size, morphology, and H/D ratio, investigating liquid-to-surface interactions, performing quantitative analysis of imaging results, and systematically analyzing the optical properties of the fabricated lenses. Below, we address the extent to which each of the four objectives has been achieved, highlight challenges encountered, and outline the solutions implemented to overcome them. Objective 1: Develop a Microfluidic Pervaporation Device for Fabricating NPMs The project successfully designed and fabricated a microfluidic pervaporation device that incorporates a “lens-chamber,” pervaporation membrane and microfluidic channel specifically for producing NPMs. The device enabled the controlled solidification of TiO₂ nanoparticles within hemispherical molds created from glycerol droplets. By precisely controlling the evaporation rate through the pervaporation membrane, the morphology of the NPMs, including their size and H/D ratio, was systematically controlled. The fabricated NPMs demonstrated very good optical properties in air, achieving super-resolution imaging of subdiffraction-limited features, which was demonstrated by resolving nanoscale features on IC chips. These results validate the effectiveness of the microfluidic device for producing high-quality NPMs tailored for air-medium applications. This objective has been fully completed. The microfluidic device demonstrated reliability and reproducibility in fabricating NPMs with controlled geometries suitable for systematic nanoscale imaging experiments. Objective 2: Manipulate the Morphology of Liquid Molds and Investigate Liquid-to-Substrate Interactions Our team also extensively investigated the manipulation of liquid molds, such as glycerol droplets, used for casting PDMS lens chambers. By applying surface free energy theories, the team optimized substrate properties, including hydrophobicity and surface roughness, to control droplet shape and size. A systematic study of liquid-to-substrate interactions revealed how modifying the substrate’s surface energy could influence the morphology of the droplets, including their height-to-diameter (H/D) ratio. The findings allowed excellent control over the H/D ratios of the glycerol molds, ensuring near-hemispherical shapes for the fabricated NPMs. This control was critical for achieving consistent optical properties across multiple lenses. This objective has been successfully achieved. The team developed a robust understanding of liquid-to-surface interactions, enabling the precise manipulation of liquid mold geometries to optimize lens performance. Objective 3: Quantitative Analysis of Super-resolution Imaging Results The project carried out a quantitative analysis of super-resolution imaging results obtained with NPMs. Using image analysis tools such as ImageJ and MATLAB, our team compared images acquired with NPMs to those obtained using atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and conventional optical microscopy. The analysis demonstrated that NPMs achieved resolutions comparable to AFM and SEM, with clear visualization of nanoscale features. These acquired images could also be enhanced using machine-learning based image processing algorithms. The quantitative comparison confirmed that the NPMs provided a significant enhancement in resolution over traditional optical microscopy techniques. We also characterized the field-of-view (FOV) and imaging contrast, confirming that the NPMs offered a larger FOV than conventional microsphere lenses. This objective has been fully achieved. The quantitative analysis validated the super-resolution capabilities of NPMs and demonstrated their effectiveness for imaging nanoscale features in air. Objective 4: Analyze Imaging Properties of NPMs and Investigate Resolution Enhancement Mechanisms The optical properties of NPMs were systematically analyzed, with experimental results compared to numerical simulations. Our team studied the effect of varying the H/D ratio and lens size on imaging resolution and contrast, revealing that tightly packed nanoparticles within the lens enhanced light focusing and resolution. Numerical simulations supported these findings, illustrating how the nanoparticle packing density influenced light propagation and focusing within the lens. The study also explored the underlying mechanisms of resolution enhancement, particularly the role of nanoparticle-induced near-field effects. These effects were shown to improve the lens’s ability to capture and magnify subdiffraction-limited details, such as nanoscale patterns on IC chips. This objective has been successfully completed. The experimental and numerical analyses provided a comprehensive understanding of the optical properties of NPMs and the mechanisms driving their resolution-enhancing capabilities. Challenges and Mitigation Measures: The key challenges encountered in the project and their mitigation methods are described below. • Initial challenges included ensuring uniform nanoparticle distribution during solidification, which affected the optical performance of the lenses. This issue was resolved by refining the pervaporation membrane material to achieve more consistent evaporation rates and optimizing the nanoparticle concentration in the solution. • Another key challenge was variability in droplet shapes due to environmental factors such as temperature and humidity. To address this, experiments were performed in controlled environments, and surfactants were introduced to the glycerol solution to improve droplet consistency. • Another obstacle during this project was aligning imaging data from different modalities (e.g., SEM and optical microscopy) for direct comparison. This was addressed by calibrating all imaging systems using standard reference samples and implementing software-based alignment techniques. • The computational complexity of simulating the interaction of light with densely packed nanoparticles was another major challenge in the project. This was mitigated by using simplified models and leveraging computing resources to perform detailed simulations. Conclusion All project objectives have been successfully achieved. The team developed a robust microfluidic pervaporation device for fabricating NPMs, manipulated liquid mold geometries based on surface energy theories, conducted quantitative imaging analysis, and systematically studied the optical properties of the lenses. Although minor challenges were encountered, such as variability in droplet shapes and computational complexities in modeling, these were effectively addressed through optimization of experimental conditions and numerical techniques. The outcomes of this project have demonstrated the potential of NPMs as a transformative tool for nanoscale imaging in air, with broad applications in biological imaging, integrated circuit defect analysis, and beyond.

11216120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216120.value: This project successfully developed a microfluidic pervaporation device to fabricate nanoparticle-based metalenses (NPMs) optimized for super-resolution imaging in air. Below is a summary of the major findings and outcomes of the project. 1. Development of the Microfluidic Pervaporation Device A novel microfluidic pervaporation device was designed and fabricated, incorporating a “lens-chamber,” pervaporation membrane, and air channel. This device enabled precise control over the solidification of TiO₂ nanoparticles into hemispherical metalenses with tailored size, height-to-diameter (H/D) ratio, and morphology. The controlled pervaporation process ensured uniform nanoparticle distribution, resulting in reproducible and high-quality lenses. The fabricated NPMs demonstrated exceptional optical properties and were tailored for systematic super-resolution imaging experiments in air. 2. Manipulation of Liquid Mold Morphology The morphology of liquid molds, such as glycerol droplets used for PDMS casting, was systematically controlled by leveraging surface free energy theories. The research explored the interactions between liquid molds and substrate surfaces, optimizing substrate hydrophobicity and surface roughness to achieve desired droplet shapes and H/D ratios. These efforts enabled the production of molds with various H/D ratios, ensuring near-hemispherical geometries, which are critical to achieving consistent optical performance. 3. Quantitative Analysis of Imaging Results Quantitative analysis of super-resolution imaging results was carried out using tools such as ImageJ and MATLAB. The NPMs demonstrated the ability to resolve subdiffraction-limited features on IC chips. Experimental comparison with imaging from atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and conventional optical microscopy were also performed to quantify the performance of the NPMs. 4. Systematic Analysis of Imaging Properties The imaging properties of NPMs were systematically analyzed through experimental and numerical studies. The research revealed that tightly packed nanoparticles within the lenses enhanced light focusing and resolution through near-field effects. Numerical simulations supported these findings and clarified the relationship between lens geometry, nanoparticle density, and resolution enhancement. This project successfully achieved its objectives, demonstrating the potential of NPMs for nanoscale imaging in air. The findings represent significant advancements in lens fabrication and imaging technology, with potentially broad applications in biology, microelectronics, and materials science. Furthermore, with implementation of machine-learning based image processing algorithms, the images acquired by the NPMs could potentially produce SEM-like nanoscale images (i.e., see “Deep Learning-Driven Conversion of Scanning Superlens Microscopy to High Depth-of-Field SEM-like Imaging” as described in #10 publication listed in Part C: Research Output).

11216120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216120.value: By addressing key limitations of current microsphere-based superlenses, such as restricted field-of-view and limited resolution due to material constraints, the project introduces an innovative pervaporation microfluidic device to fabricate metalenses with controllable morphology. This approach has the potential to establish a paradigm shift in lens fabrication technologies and enable high-contrast, sub-diffraction imaging for diverse applications, including biological imaging, integrated circuit defect detection, and live-sample observation. To further develop this research, our team will focus on optimizing the fabrication process by exploring alternative materials for pervaporation membranes and refining the inkjet printing of glycerol molds to achieve consistent and reproducible lens geometries. Additionally, integrating the fabricated lenses with advanced imaging systems, such as Scanning Super-resolution Microscopy (SSUM), should be prioritized to validate their performance in real-world applications. Collaboration with industrial partners specializing in imaging technologies could accelerate the transition from laboratory-scale fabrication to commercialization. We propose to apply for ITF funding to expand the project scope to include scalability studies for mass production and explore the use of hybrid nanoparticle compositions to further enhance lens performance. A dedicated effort to disseminate findings through industry engagement will ensure the broad impact of this research.

11216120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216120.value: This project developed advanced nanoparticle-based metalenses for super-resolution imaging, enabling visualization of features much smaller than the diffraction limit of light. Unlike traditional microsphere-based lenses, which are limited by narrow fields of view and constraints on refractive index, these metalenses use densely packed nanoparticles (e.g., TiO₂) to enhance resolution and imaging contrast. The proposed innovation lies in using a pervaporation microfluidic device to create metalenses with controllable shapes, sizes, and curvatures. This process involves solidifying nanoparticles within a hemispherical chamber, shaped using inkjet-printed glycerol droplets as molds. This project addressed critical limitations of existing lens technologies and enabled applications in fields like nanoscale imaging of biological samples, integrated circuits, and live-cell observation. By improving the fabrication process, the project aims to achieve higher spatial resolution (down to ~50nm or better) and larger imaging areas, while maintaining cost-efficiency and scalability. The value of this research lies in its potential to impact various fields, from medicine to electronics, by providing affordable, high-resolution imaging tools. The integration of these lenses with advanced imaging systems, such as Scanning Super-resolution Microscopy (SSUM), could further enhance their utility, paving the way for breakthroughs in both fundamental science and applied technologies.

11216220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216220.value: To date, microfluidics enables quantitative measurements of cell properties which have been difficult for the traditional cell research techniques. For instance, the biomechanical properties of floating cancer cells can be measured with multiple microfluidic techniques based on cell-solid or cell-flow interactions. The biomechanical properties have been proven of reflecting metastatic tendency and status of cancer cells; and therefore some of these characteristics, e.g. whole-cell stiffness, can be considered as the diagnostic biomarkers. In particular, cancer metastasis involves large deformation and migration of cancer cells from sites to sties through tiny tissue gaps and vessel walls; and hence the viscoelasticity properties of the cancer cells should take an important role. Considering that the effective identification of metastasis using the cancer patient’s blood is yet challenging, quantifying the viscoelasticity cell properties may provide additional information on the metastatic status and enhance the diagnostic precision and specificity for the related clinical applications. We propose to develop a fully automated microfluidic viscoelasticity microcytometer based on dynamic cell deformation along funnel-shaped confining microchannels. This microfluidic device is integrated with a computer-controlled system for achieving fully automated size and viscoelasticity quantification of every cell in a bio-sample. Technically, we first configure the device as multiple-stages of the confining microchannels with different dimensions. The nuclear elasticity and whole cell viscoelasticity properties can then be resolved from the cell movements along the confining channels, based on a Standard Linear Model together with the hyperelastic Tatara theories we developed previously. We design also cell focusing microstructure to ensure most (~100 %) cells in a biosample are quantified along the confining microchannels. The system automation includes elimination of imaging under a microscope. Instead, we adopt electrokinectic sensing via multiple groups of electrodes fabrication along the confining microchannels in order to achieve the full automation toward the translational research with clinical applications. The system automation also includes a biosample release module with a feedback control manner to realize the sequential single cell quantification, i.e. only one cell is detected along the confining channels at a time. Afterward, we optimize the system for the high detection throughput (>100 cells/min) by adjusting the key operation parameters of the system. Altogether, with further development the proposed fully automated viscoelasticity microcytometer can realize the high-throughput biomechanical phenotyping of floating cancer cells, offering additional cell characteristics for more promising cancer diagnosis as well as general cell/clinical analysis applications. 當前的微流體技術可實現對於傳統細胞技術而言艱難的任務，包括細胞特性的定量測量。例如，我們可以利用微流體技術來測量細胞與固體間或細胞與液流間的相互作用，從而導出漂浮癌細胞的生物力學性質。至今學者們已經證明了細胞生物力學特性能夠反映癌細胞的轉移趨勢和狀態，而細胞硬化可以視為癌症診斷的一個指標。癌症轉移涉及癌細胞在通過微小組織間隙和血管壁過程中的大幅度變形。癌細胞的粘彈性應起重要作用。因此，對細胞的粘彈性進行定量分析可以提供有關癌細胞轉移狀態的更多信息，並提高相關臨床的癌症診斷準確性。 我們將開發一種全自動的微流體粘彈性微細胞計數器，實現生物樣品中單一細胞的大小和粘彈性定量。當中我們會利用多個不同尺寸的漏斗形微約束通道來測量動態細胞變形。然後，我們可以根據超彈性Tatara理論將細胞通過沿約束通道的運動導出細胞的粘彈性。我們還設計了微結構聚焦細胞，以使絶大部分（〜100％）細胞都能流入微通道而被定量。透過多組電動感應電極和反饋控制，此系統能夠實現順序的單細胞定量。我們更會優化系統以實現高檢測通量（> 100個細胞/分鐘）。總括而言，此全自動粘彈性微細胞計數儀可以實現漂浮癌細胞的高通量生物力學表型分析，應用於各種癌症診斷以及細胞分析。

11216220.label: Realisation of objectives
11216220.value: The project has successfully achieved its primary objectives, with significant progress made in each area: 1. Design and Characterization of Multi-Stage Confining Microchannel Structure: Achievement: We successfully designed and characterized a multi-stage confining microchannel structure capable of measuring size, viscosity, and whole-cell/nuclear elasticity for every floating cancer cell in bio-samples. The structure demonstrated high precision and reliability in capturing the desired measurements. Challenges: Initial challenges included optimizing the microchannel dimensions to ensure accurate measurements across different cell types. Solutions: Iterative design and testing, along with computational modeling, helped refine the microchannel structure to achieve the desired performance. 2. Embedding Microelectrodes and Developing Electronics and Interface Program: Achievement: Microelectrodes were successfully embedded in the microchannels, and an electronics interface program was developed for cell counting and position detection in microfluidics. This system provided real-time data with high accuracy. Challenges: Integrating the microelectrodes without affecting the fluid dynamics within the channels was a significant challenge. Solutions: Advanced fabrication techniques and careful placement of electrodes ensured minimal disruption to fluid flow. 3. Integration of Microelectrodes and Automated Viscoelasticity Microcytometer: Achievement: The integration of microelectrodes along the confining microchannels was achieved, resulting in the development of an automated viscoelasticity microcytometer. This device enabled high-throughput biomechanical phenotyping of floating cancer cells. Challenges: Ensuring seamless integration and synchronization between the microelectrodes and the microcytometer was complex. Solutions: Extensive testing and calibration were conducted to ensure the system operated smoothly and accurately. 4. Development of Cell Extraction Unit: Achievement: A cell extraction unit based on pneumatic microvalves and electrodes for flow control and position detection was developed. This unit ensured that only one cell flowed along the downstream microchannels, which was then combined with the automated viscoelasticity microcytometer for fully automated viscoelasticity phenotyping. Challenges: Achieving precise control over cell flow and extraction was challenging. Solutions: Fine-tuning the pneumatic microvalves and optimizing the control algorithms helped achieve the desired precision. 5. High-Throughput Biomechanical Phenotyping: Achievement: The automated viscoelasticity microcytometer was successfully implemented for high-throughput biomechanical phenotyping of floating cancer cells. The system demonstrated excellent performance, with optimized operation parameters ensuring reliable and reproducible results. Challenges: Scaling up the system for high-throughput applications required careful optimization of various parameters. Solutions: Systematic experimentation and parameter optimization were conducted to achieve high-throughput performance without compromising accuracy. Overall Impact: The project has made significant strides in developing a robust and high-throughput system for biomechanical phenotyping of floating cancer cells. The successful integration of microelectrodes, microchannels, and automated systems has resulted in a powerful tool for cell research and potential clinical applications. While some challenges were encountered, they were effectively addressed through iterative design, testing, and optimization. 6. Future Directions: Future work will focus on further refining the system for different cell types and expanding its capabilities to include additional phenotypic parameters. Integration with other analytical techniques and exploring label-free sensing schemes for biochemical characteristics are also planned to enhance the system's versatility and applicability.

11216220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216220.value: The research project has successfully developed a high-throughput, multi-physical single-cell phenotyping device capable of measuring uncoupled geometric, mechanical, and electrical properties of individual cells. This innovative device was used to characterize normal (MCF-10A) and cancerous (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231) breast cell lines. The measured elasticity moduli and dielectric constants were consistent with existing literature, confirming that cancer cells are generally softer than normal cells. Additionally, the device demonstrated its ability to assess the effects of various drug treatments, such as Cytochalasin D, Cetuximab, and Lysophosphatidic Acid, on cell properties, providing valuable insights into drug-induced changes in cell elasticity and permittivity. The device's high sensitivity in classifying mixed populations of normal and cancerous cells was validated using both principal component analysis (PCA) and machine learning approaches. The neural network classification achieved even higher sensitivity levels, indicating the robustness of the device in distinguishing cancerous cells from normal cells. This capability is particularly important for clinical applications, where accurate identification of cancerous cells is crucial. One of the key advantages of this device is its label-free approach, which eliminates the need for fluorescent labeling or magnetic tags. This reduces potential alterations to the cells and allows for more accurate subsequent analyses. The measured cell properties, including size, elasticity modulus, and dielectric constant, were shown to be clinically and biologically relevant, providing a complementary measurement scheme for further cell biology and clinical applications. Overall, the project has made significant strides in developing a powerful tool for high-throughput, multi-physical cell phenotyping. The device offers precise, label-free measurements of cell properties, demonstrating its effectiveness in characterizing both untreated and drug-treated cells. The successful classification of mixed cell populations and the ability to quantify drug effects on cell properties highlight the device's potential as a valuable asset in cell research and clinical diagnostics.

11216220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216220.value: The potential for further development of this research is substantial. Future work can focus on redesigning and refabricating the device to accommodate different cell types and physical phenotypes. For instance, adjusting the channel dimensions and adding more measurement regions can enhance the device's versatility. Additionally, integrating alternative label-free sensing schemes, such as those for biochemical cell characteristics, will expand the phenotypic spectrum covered by the device. The proposed course of action includes optimizing the device for various cell types by refining the microchannel structure and incorporating additional sensing modalities. This will involve iterative design and testing to ensure accurate measurements across a broader range of cell properties. Furthermore, exploring the integration of the device with existing analytical techniques, such as commercial flow cytometry, can provide a more comprehensive phenotypic analysis. By addressing these areas, the research can advance towards creating a more versatile and powerful tool for cell phenotyping, with applications in basic cell research, disease prognosis, and diagnostics. This will ultimately enhance our understanding of cell properties and their implications in various biological and clinical contexts.

11216220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216220.value: This research project developed a new device that can measure important properties of individual cells, such as their size, stiffness, and electrical characteristics, without using any labels or dyes. The device was tested on normal and cancerous breast cells and was able to accurately distinguish between them. It also measured how different drugs affected the properties of cancer cells, providing valuable information on how these drugs work. The device uses tiny channels and embedded electrodes to capture and analyze cells as they flow through. It can process a large number of cells quickly, making it a powerful tool for studying cell behavior and identifying cancer cells. The results showed that cancer cells are generally softer than normal cells, and the device could detect changes in cell properties caused by drug treatments. Overall, this research has created a highly sensitive and efficient tool for studying cells, which could help in diagnosing diseases and understanding how different treatments affect cells. The device's ability to measure cell properties without altering them makes it a valuable addition to cell research and medical diagnostics.
