11216620.label: Realisation of objectives
11216620.value: Obj 1: We propose a new efficient optimization method for the optimization of matrix factorization problem. The developed recommender system combines novel correlation mapping method, matrix factorization approach and efficient optimization technique, is tested to outperform existing models in terms of computational efficiency and recommendation performance. The work has been published as a journal paper "Modeling Self-Representation Label Correlations for Textual Aspects and Emojis Recommendation"). Obj 2: We propose a novel topic-based instance and feature selection methods for multi-label learning, aiming to exploit the dependence between features and labels in a topic space. The proposed method can identify latent topics in various kinds of data, and can therefore be applied to recommendation scenarios to help extract topics and relationships between users, items and other labels, such as emoji. The work has been published as a journal paper "Topic-Based Instance and Feature Selection in Multilabel Classification". Obj 3: We design a framework with local feature selection and local label correlation to solve a multi-label learning problem. By clustering the data into different groups and then mining the intra- and inter-group correlations, we can improve the performance of multi-label learning. We also propose a cross-view correlation mapping method to mine relationships between texts and emojis, enhacing the performance of emoji recommendations. The work has been included in journal paper "Multilabel Classification With Group-Based Mapping: A Framework With Local Feature Selection and Local Label Correlation" and "Modeling Self-Representation Label Correlations for Textual Aspects and Emojis Recommendation"). Obj 4: We introduce a model designed specifically for large-scale recommendation scenarios. Drawing inspiration from existing graph convolutional network models, we incorporate a graph partitioning strategy for grouping the item set. By leveraging the potential community structure of items, we significantly reduce the computational cost of linear autoencoders while maintaining accuracy. Our approach proves valuable for practical applications at scale. This method is an efficient solution of collaborative filtering, thus can be applied to the emoji recommendation system we aim to design. The work has been included in conference paper "Fine-tuning Partition-aware Item Similarities for Efficient and Scalable Recommendation"). Obj 5: Through theoretical analysis of existing neighborhood-based collaborative filtering methods, we have designed varied new models to enhance the efficiency, scalability and novelty. Since only item relationships are modeled, those designed models can be easily generalized to out-of-sample unseen users without retraining the models. The work has been included in conference paper "Fine-tuning Partition-aware Item Similarities for Efficient and Scalable Recommendation" and "Collaborative Residual Metric Learning"). Obj 6: We have published serveral journal and conference papers to report our reserach outcome. The corresponding runnable program is also already online and open source.

11216620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216620.value: In this project, we have conducted an in-depth investigation into how to effectively mine the intricate relationships between emojis and other heterogeneous information sources, such as textual content and user collaborative behavior data. First, due to the lack of large-scale emoji datasets, we first constructed a large-scale emoji dataset by collecting data from various social media platforms. This dataset was carefully curated and made publicly available to the research community, alleviating the long-standing problem of emoji data scarcity and fostering further research in this field. Building upon this dataset, we developed novel sparse factorization methods to model the intricate relationships between emojis and heterogeneous information, such as textual content, user interactions, and contextual metadata. Our proposed methods leveraged the complementary nature of these heterogeneous data sources, effectively capturing the underlying patterns and semantics associated with emoji usage. Extensive experiments demonstrated that mining and exploiting these rich relationships significantly improved the performance of emoji recommendation systems, outperforming traditional approaches that relied solely on homogeneous data. To enhance the practical applicability of our methods in large-scale real-world scenarios, we devised efficient and highly scalable optimization techniques. These techniques enabled our models to handle massive amounts of data while maintaining computational efficiency, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments or latency-sensitive applications. Furthermore, our research efforts extended beyond emoji recommendation itself. We explored various related problems that arose during different stages of the process, such as multi-label learning for relationship modeling and explainability issues in recommendation scenarios. By addressing these challenges, our research outcomes became applicable to a broader range of problems and scenarios within and beyond emoji recommendation. Overall, our work provides a comprehensive framework for mining and leveraging the relationships between emojis and heterogeneous information sources, contributing to the advancement of emoji recommendation systems and paving the way for further research in this emerging field.

11216620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216620.value: The rise of unified foundation models like Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened up exciting new avenues across various artificial intelligence domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Integrating these powerful models with recommender systems holds the promise of unlocking novel approaches and pushing the boundaries of recommendation technology. LLMs already possess robust encoding and representation capabilities for diverse forms of information, such as text and images. Moreover, most Transformer-based models inherently excel at processing temporal sequential data, a desirable trait for recommender systems. However, the question of how to efficiently incorporate user-item interaction sequences into the training and fine-tuning processes of foundation models remains largely uncharted territory. Consequently, our future research efforts will focus on developing effective methodologies to seamlessly combine interaction sequence data with large foundation models, paving the way for innovative and powerful next-generation recommender systems.

11216620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216620.value: In this project, we effectively leverage the rich relationships between emojis and various heterogeneous information sources, such as texts and user interactions, and propose a effective emoji reommendation methods. One of the key outcomes of our work is the ability to improve user trust in recommendation systems. By accurately recommending relevant and contextually appropriate emojis, users can express themselves more effectively. This increased trust encourages greater user participation and interaction, ultimately enriching the quality of online content. Moreover, we have introduced efficient and scalable optimization techniques that enable large-scale recommendation systems to operate with higher efficiency, thereby providing better quality services to users. These advancements are crucial in today's data-driven world, where the volume of information continues to grow exponentially. Furthermore, our commitment to open-source principles and data sharing has led to the public release of a large-scale emoji dataset and the associated codebase. This valuable resource empowers the academic community to conduct further research more conveniently, fostering collaboration and accelerating progress in the field of emoji recommendation and beyond. In summary, by combining innovative techniques with open-source practices, we are contributing to the advancement of recommendation systems and paving the way for future research in this exciting domain.

11216920.label: Project Objectives
11216920.value: To review the current research studies, engineering practice and legislative requirements on fire protection and evacuation for hospitals and elderly homes. To identify the fire risk levels and protection measures in hospitals/elderly homes, including the building layouts/ structures, equipment/ facilities, chemicals/ drugs, radioactive matters, combustibles and building users. To formulate a Building Information Modeling (BIM) platform to facilitate the information and documentation generated from hospitals and/ or elderly homes, with Internet of Things (IoT) system, to store static information (building and facilities information) and dynamic real-time information concerning objects, drugs, sensors, patients and medical staff (the number, type, and location). Information in the platform will serve as the basis and the input parameters for ranking hazardous zones and developing evacuation strategies. To compile a dynamic hazardous-zone ranking algorithm by object-oriented approach, based on information from sensors, detectors, videos, furnishing, and equipment, to rank the fire risk of zones in the buildings for establishing fire protection strategies. To develop an evacuation model on the basis of cellular automaton (CA) approach that can integrate the environmental information and established egress strategies to mimic the evacuation process of heterogeneous occupants, including wheelchair and bed-lying patients, clinical staff, general visitors in hospitals and elderly homes. To establish a notional case for examining the implementation of the system described in objective 5 above. To study the implementation issues, in particular the legislative implications and the associated privacy issues for tracking the positions of some occupants.

11216920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216920.value: By mid-21st century, the elderly population in Hong Kong will exceed 35%. Aging population is the world’s emerging problem. Medical and elderly care services will be in great demand. Rapid urbanization leads to densely populated cities with limited space for constructing elderly homes and hospitals and complex high-rise hospitals appear in many Asia region. In view of the complexity of high-rise hospitals, fire safety will be a significant concern of building designers and facility management. It is unlikely that zero fire risk situation will exist and safe evacuation of users in the buildings will become a means of mitigation. Complex building structures, diversified combustibles, large variety of chemicals and drugs, complex equipment and medical treatment facilities, multiple usage and a large number of patients, clinic staff, visitors make fire protection and evacuation process complicated. It is well recognized that evacuation process and the associated fire protection strategy for hospitals should not be the same as general type buildings as it involves wheelchair and bed-lying patients. Moreover, in fire incidents, the dynamic and sometimes unpredictable process of fire and smoke development may cause evacuation process more complicated. In the past decades, there existed many hospitals or elderly homes fire disasters with large fatality. While expecting the construction of more large and complex hospitals and elderly homes, we should improve fire protection for hospitals and elderly homes, especially safe evacuation, by integrating latest technology. With the advancement of computer technology, the internet of things (IoT) system has nowadays been widely developed for equipment, objects and people that are provided with unique identifiers for collecting and sharing data to transfer over internet for control and management with built-in intelligence. Such system can effectively identify the location and needs of each patient that can support safe process. The aim of this project is to develop a smart safe evacuation system based on IoT for hospitals and elderly homes. Building Information Modeling (BIM) with building and facilities information will serve as a platform to integrate the information concerning objects, drugs, sensors, patients and medical staff. Data transmission over internet will be dynamically managed. The IoT-based safe evacuation system for hospitals and elderly homes will be established to control the evacuation process by guiding occupants to escape through safe routes, medical staff to assist limited mobility patients to escape by elevators or other mechanical means and rescue and firefighting personnel to take appropriate actions. 人口老龄化是当今世界正面临的难题，到21世纪中叶，香港的老年人口将超过35%。因此，医疗和养老服务将会有巨大的发展需求，然而亚洲地区快速发展的城市化进程使得城市内人口愈加稠密，可用于建造养老院和医院和复杂的高层医院建筑的土地十分有限。对于这些复杂的高层医院建筑，消防安全往往是建筑设计师及设施管理人员的重点关注内容。虽然我们无法将这些建筑控制在零风险，但对建筑内人员的成功安全疏散是一项能够实现的风险控制策略。医院建筑中复杂的内部结构、种类繁多的可燃物、大量化学物品和药品、多用途的设备与医疗设施以及大量的医护人员、患者以及访客使得这类建筑物内部的消防及疏散工作难以开展。众所周知，针对医院这类建筑物的疏散及消防策略与其他常规建筑有所不同，尤其是医院内存在使用大量人员使用轮椅及卧床的现象。此外，火灾发生后动态和不可预测的火势及烟气蔓延可能会导致医院内人员的疏散过程变得更加复杂。在过去的几十年中，医院或养老院发生过许多火灾且伤亡惨重。因此在建设更多大型、复杂的医院及养老院时，我们也应该利用当前的最新科技来提高医院和养老院的消防水平，尤其是安全疏散能力。如今，随着计算机技术的发展，物联网（IoT）系统已广泛应用于设备、物体和人员中，通过物联网对特定信息的收集、共享和传输，从而实现对系统的控制和管理。这样的系统可以有效地识别出每位患者的位置及需求，从而更好地支持人员的安全疏散过程。因此，本项目旨在为医院及养老院开发一个基于物联网的智慧消防疏散系统，其中建筑和设施信息的建筑信息模型（BIM）将作为平台，整合有关物体、药品、传感器、患者和医务人员的信息，并对数据传输进行动态管理。通过建立针对医院和养老院的物联网智慧消防疏散系统，引导人员通过安全通道进行疏散，指示医务人员帮助行动不便的病患通过电梯及其他机械设备进行疏散，并辅助救援和消防人员你采取合适的措施，从而对疏散过程进行控制和管理。

11216920.label: Realisation of objectives
11216920.value: (1) Fire safety is crucial in hospitals and elderly homes, particularly as the global population continues to age. With the increasing number of elderly individuals, the importance of fire safety in these facilities has become even greater. However, current research on fire and evacuation risks for hospitals and elderly homes remains limited. Unlike typical public buildings, hospitals contain a variety of combustible, chemical, and toxic materials and house more vulnerable populations, such as elderly individuals and patients. Additionally, the existing building codes and regulations regarding the legislative requirements on fire protection and evacuation for hospitals and elderly homes in many countries do not differentiate them from normal buildings. Neglecting these critical fire risks may lead to severe consequences. Therefore, there is an urgent need for research focused on fire protection and evacuation strategies specifically designed for hospitals and elderly care facilities. (2) To identify the fire hazards and protection measures in hospitals and elderly homes, this study investigated the hazards across three stages: before the event, during the event, and after the event. Before the event refers to the combustibles and ignition sources present in hospital and elderly home environments. For instance, equipment like lasers and electrocautery devices introduce the risk of surgical fires. Additionally, alcohol-based disinfectants are located throughout these facilities, posing a significant fire hazard. During the fire involves actions that cause fires. Upon thorough investigation, it was found that careless use of electrical devices and arson are two major causes of fires. Furthermore, some facilities are constructed based on residential or commercial building standards, leading to inherent deficiencies in building design, such as inadequate fire detection and sprinkler systems, which increase the likelihood of a fire occurring. After the fire refers to elements that may exacerbate risks during a fire. In hospitals and elderly homes, the sickest and elderly individuals are often mobility-impaired, making it difficult to evacuate them quickly. Additionally, critically ill patients can only be moved to specific locations with their life support systems intact. The diverse and specific requirements of patients pose significant challenges in planning and executing evacuations effectively. (3) The research team also developed a software platform to facilitate information collection for fire detection and occupant count monitoring. With the visualization of this information, building managers and Incident commanders can more easily guide evacuations and respond to fire emergencies. The visualized information includes both static and dynamic data. Static information encompasses the building's geometry and compartments, locations of various fire protection and evacuation equipment, and maintenance details. Dynamic information is collected from local sensors and includes people counts, statuses of various facilities, and detections of the fire environment. By attaching dynamic information to the corresponding equipment or spaces within the Building Information Modeling (BIM) model, real-time sensor data can be browsed through a 3D interface. Beyond visualizing these monitoring data, the BIM model also serves as a platform for exchanging data with fire prediction and evacuation planning modules, thereby offering more useful services. (4) In considering the application of elevators for evacuation in hospitals and elderly homes, we have divided fire severity levels and designed corresponding rules and constraints for an Elevator Evacuation Dispatch Strategy (EEDS). The fire severity level is crucial in the design of EEDS because high temperatures and dense smoke pose significant risks to elevator systems during a fire. For a fire at a low severity level, where the fire may still be confined in a single room and undergo its incipient stage, we allow elevators to evacuate occupants freely but follow specific rules. For instance, elevators should only stop on one floor at a time to avoid frequent stops on each floor. When the fire intensifies to a medium severity level, normal passenger elevators must cease evacuation operations on the fire floor. At this point, only safety-enhanced elevator systems, such as firefighter elevators, will be permitted to evacuate occupants from the fire floor. As the fire reaches a high severity level, all elevator evacuation services on the fire floor should be completely stopped to prevent smoke from entering the elevator shaft. Occupants on the fire floor will need to use stairs or take elevators from other floors. As the fire reaches a severe severity level, the fire extends between floors, compromising the fire compartment. High temperatures and dense smoke may have reached stairwells or elevator shafts, causing the fire to spread. In this scenario, elevator evacuation should be completely halted, and stair evacuation needs careful evaluation before it can continue. (5) A CA-based elevator-assisted evacuation simulation model was developed in this project. The model utilizes a static floor field to characterize regions within spaces, such as rooms, stairwells, elevator lobbies, and exits, and a dynamic floor field to specify the attractive interactions between pedestrians. For the static parameters in the simulation model, occupant profile parameters (e.g., occupant motion speed, occupant profiles) and elevator operation parameters (e.g., elevator acceleration speed, elevator door open time, elevator capacity) are defined with specific values based on the actual situation or worst-case scenario of the target building. Dynamic parameters in the model, such as the location of occupants and the corresponding elevator evacuation dispatch strategies, are defined based on sensor monitoring data. With these integrated information inputs, the simulation model can accurately reflect the actual fire evacuation dynamics in a real environment. (6) A simplified prototype for planning the optimal evacuation strategy suitable for an elderly home or hospital environment was developed. The development of the system follows the general architecture of an IoT system. In the perception layer, fire detectors and visual-based occupant counters were installed to measure environmental temperatures and occupant counts. Hereafter, the network layer was established. The collected sensor data was transmitted through a wire connection to input into an IoT gateway, which directly connects with a local computer. With the collected sensor data successfully stored in a local database, we were able to recall the data and analyze the optimal vertical evacuation strategy based on a series of self-developed program modules. The evacuation strategy planning program was developed based on Python 3.8 and Qt C++. Ultimately, a GUI platform based on LabVIEW was established to visualize the monitoring data and output the suggested evacuation strategy. (7). While the research outputs have demonstrated the effectiveness and efficiency of smart fire evacuation systems, there are practical challenges that need to be addressed. Using a vision-based approach to track the positions of occupants may raise privacy issues under current legislation. Therefore, we believe that only occupant count information should be collected, and multiple applicable techniques can be employed. For instance, a turnstile gate and swipe card system can be used at building entrances to count the total number of occupants entering and leaving them premises. Additionally, for room-level occupant counts, it is recommended to use infrared beam counters. These devices can detect general movement without collecting any personal information. This approach ensures that occupant privacy is maximally protected.

11216920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216920.value: To ensure effective and efficient fire evacuation in hospitals and elderly homes, research on developing an IoT-based smart fire evacuation system was undertaken. In this project, a smart elevator-aided fire evacuation scheme for high-rise apartment buildings for the elderly was developed. The model utilized fire spread data to determine fire risks and combined occupant counts, as well as a CA-based evacuation simulation model to determine the optimal strategy for combining elevator and staircase evacuations. The smart scheme was successfully tested in simulations and small prototypes, and the research findings were published in reputable SCI journals (refer to Part C 8.1). Additionally, to find the optimal elevator-assisted evacuation mode for older people in high-rise elderly housing, we considered three possible elevator dispatch strategies to accommodate diverse groups of elderly individuals, such as those assisted in wheelchairs and those assisted by others. The outcomes of this research work were published in an architecture engineering SCI journal (refer to Part C 8.2). Moreover, the research output of the project (refer to Parts C 8.3 and 8.4) proposed a Directed Rooted Forest (DRF)-based planning method that can boost the efficiency of iterative optimization with heuristics from simulation. This research output can be combined with our CA-based evacuation model to increase the calculation speed in determining the optimal evacuation strategy during the strategy planning phase. Furthermore, to facilitate the identification of risk areas in hospitals /elderly homes, we also investigated various fire risk analysis methods. A Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) method was applied to analyze fire risks in forest fires, which drew useful information for our project (refer to Part C 8.5). Additionally, optimization of fire detection systems in building rooms was conducted (refer to Part C 8.6). This research facilitates the optimization of sensor numbers and placement in building rooms, which can provide effective and efficient sensor placement strategies for fire detectors in hospitals and elderly homes. Finally, a PhD student (expected to graduate in October 2025), under the supervision of the PI, is under training [Part C 11.1 refers]. The student’s research focuses on the optimization of the evacuation algorithm, facilitating the real-time application of the system in this project.

11216920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216920.value: Currently, fire evacuation in hospitals and elderly homes has received less attention. Our research provides insight into the application of smart systems for conducting fire and evacuation control. Although simulations and small demonstrations were presented, many issues still require further research. First, substantial research efforts can be dedicated to extending and modifying the evacuation simulation model for real-time application. By integrating real-time occupant counts and fire detection information, the simulation model needs to perform adequately to handle rapid changes and analyze possible evacuation strategies in real time. Furthermore, comprehensive testing and validation procedures need to be established. The proposed system should be tested under large environments and more complex situations to ensure reliability and effectiveness during fire emergencies. Finally, gathering occupants' and users’ attitudes regarding the use of the smart fire evacuation system during emergencies is essential. The feedback provides useful information for further improvement in system development.

11216920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216920.value: With the growing number of senior citizens living in elderly homes and visiting hospitals, fire evacuation in these areas becomes increasingly critical. Traditional fire evacuations that rely solely on staircases may not be suitable because the physical limitations and mobility impairments of elderly individuals can hinder successful evacuation. Therefore, it is reasonable to consider using elevators as part of the overall evacuation strategy, especially in response to dynamically changing fire situations during emergencies. In this study, a smart elevator-aided fire evacuation scheme for high-rise apartment buildings for the elderly was proposed. This solution utilized occupant count and fire situation information as model inputs to organize evacuation strategies. Additionally, a Directed Rooted Forest (DRF)-based planning method that can boost the efficiency of iterative optimization with heuristics from simulation was proposed. This optimization method is expected to facilitate the planning of evacuation strategies in real-time. The findings and outcomes of this study provide valuable insights into the potential of using smart systems to monitor fire risks in hospitals and elderly homes and coordinate fire evacuations in response to dynamic fire situations.

11217020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217020.value: 通过自修复和隔离技术管理超大规模闪存芯片提高性能和可靠性

11217020.label: Project Objectives
11217020.value: Chip management with flash self-healing: the large number of flash chips on servers will be partitioned into different groups with different key purposes. This project focuses on two purposes: one group to provide stable access performance in the foreground and one group to be healed for better reliability in the background. Together, these two purposes lead to better system performance, better system reliability and performance predictability; Flash self-healing: by exploiting the abundant idle time on healing group, healing flash chips will be well healed without affecting the performance of host requests; Space allocation for active group: all the write requests are served by the active flash chips in the active group. How to effectively manage these chips is critical for access performance and later background data management. Several approaches will be proposed by taking hotness in multiple levels into consideration to allocate space for write requests; Flash chips relocation and data migration: the activities on the flash chips of healing group have a large impact on the performance and reliability when they are switched to the active group. We propose approaches to relocate data and conduct garbage collection operations on these chips for the benefits of both performance and lifetime improvement.

11217020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217020.value: Modern server infrastructure can employ a large number of flash chips in order to provide large capacity and lower data access latency. Recent reports also show that these flash-based servers can provide high I/O bandwidth (e.g., 3-10GB/s). Hence, the storage bandwidth can easily surpass the network bandwidth even with a part of flash chips installed in the servers. Instead of using all the flash chips at the same time, we should better manage chips so that a sufficient portion of chips are used for serving requests, while other chips can be healed, and data can be better reorganized, such as relocation, to improve the overall system performance and reliability. To achieve this goal, this project proposes to use a portion of flash chips to serve write requests called active flash chips. The active flash chips aim to provide sufficient bandwidth while the remaining chips, called the healing chips, are enrolled into flash self-healing in order to provide better system reliability and performance. These active flash chips can avoids the interference from garbage collection (GC) operations on the host requests and provide a stable performance guarantee by simply precenting GC operations. To issue write requests, address location is critical on active flash chips, which considers three aspects: 1) workload-aware allocation for performance isolation; 2) host-level allocation to exploit application behaviors; and 3) hotness-aware allocation to separate hot and cold data. The healing chips are enrolled into self-healing and data management as running in the background. We must emphasize that self-healing becomes more feasible because of a huge number of flash chips. Flash self-healing means that the trapped charges from program and erase operations dissipates over time, which can be accelerated by heating. We explore the abundant idle time on healing chips to heal by utilizing either long dwell period or heating. We conduct three types of internal activities on healing chips: 1) data relocation for performance improvement; 2) relocation for reliability improvement by avoiding excessive wears; and 3) the switch between active chips and healing chips. The success of this project enable better system performance, better reliability and performance predictability, all of which will enable better server designs. Efficiently handling data and storage are the key for the success in handling a huge amount of data in big data analysis and machine learning. This project will provide a tremendous drive for the innovation industry of Hong Kong. 现代服务器基础架构采用大量闪存存储芯片，以提供大容量和较低的数据访问延迟，这些基于闪存的服务器可以提供较高的I / O带宽（例如3-10GB / s）。因此，即使只使用服务器中的一部分闪存芯片，存储带宽也可以轻松超过网络带宽。与其同时使用所有闪存芯片，不如更好地管理芯片，以便将足够的一部分芯片用于处理请求，同时对其他芯片做修复以及数据重组，例如重定位，以改善整体系统性能和可靠性。 为实现此目标，该项目建议使用一部分闪存芯片为活跃芯片来满足写入请求,旨在提供足够的带宽，而其余的芯片作为修复芯片将加入闪存自我修复中，以提供更好的系统可靠性和性能。这些活跃闪存芯片可以避免主机请求上垃圾回收操作的干扰，从而提供稳定的性能保证。在处理写请求时，活跃芯片上的地址分配主考虑三个方面：1）工作负载感知的性能隔离； 2）主机分配以利用应用程序行为； 3）热度感知分配以分离冷热数据。 修复芯片在后台运行时被纳入自我修复和数据管理中。我们必须强调，由于服务器中闪存芯片数量众多，自我修复变得更加可行。闪存自我修复是指随着时间的流逝，编程和擦除操作中捕获的电荷会消散，而这个过程可以通过加热来加速。我们通过长时间空闲或加热来探索愈合芯片上的大量空闲时间以进行治疗。在修复芯片上进行三种内部活动：1）数据重定位以提高性能； 2）数据搬迁达到均衡磨损以提高可靠性； 3）活跃芯片和修复芯片之间的相互转换。 该项目的成功将实现更好的系统性能和更好的可靠性，所有这些都将使服务器设计更好。在大数据分析和机器学习中，有效处理数据和存储数据是成功处理大量数据的关键。这个项目将为香港的创新产业提供巨大的动力。

11217020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217020.value: Through a large set of experiments with characterisation of modern 3D NAND Flash memory chips from multiple major vendors, this project results in the following major findings. First, using optimal reference voltage leads to optimal Raw-Bit-Error-Rate (ORBER), as a result, we can significantly reduce the number of un-necessary refeshes, which leads to improves Flash performance and reliability; Second, as model 3D NAND Flash memory grow in capacity, open blocks become a new reliability and performance bottleneck. We proposed a novel framework to resolve open block issues; Third, modern Flash memory chips have a large number of layers, layer variation leads to different strengths. A layer variation aware bad block management is proposed to improve NAND Flash memory reliability further.

11217020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217020.value: From this project, we found there is a large room for improvement on reliability and performance of modern NAND Flash memories. In the future, we plan to continue to improve reliability and performance of Flash memory.

11217020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217020.value: Flash memory is now part of everyone's daily life. All mobile devices use Flash memory as the storage media. All data centers now use Solid-State-Drives, which are powered by Flash memory chips. The findings and outcome of this project can improve the performance as well as enhance the reliability of modern 3D NAND Flash memories, which have a positive impact on everyone's daily life, for example, longer life of mobile devices.

11217320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217320.value: 隨著社會對環境保護意識的增加，分散式電網系統（DPGS）日漸普及並可單個或多個行與微電網或公用電網運行。舉例來說，香港政府已循序漸進地實施可再生能源措施並由政府主導。再者推出不同的獎勵計劃和政策以及大規模的可再生能源項目，最近更引入了上網電價政策計劃，以鼓勵個人和非政府機構投資可再生能源。 典型的分佈式發電系統將微電源（如風力渦輪機和太陽光電）產生的電能轉換為直流電（DC）及穩定控制電壓。然後，直流電通過並網逆變器（GCI）轉換成為公用電網的交流電（AC）。分散式電網系統與傳統的集中式電源系統相比具有多個潛在優勢，例如提供清潔的電力，減少碳排放，提高能源效率，優化系統利用率。但隨著分散式電網系統的普及，並行連接的並網逆變器的數量將大大增加。逆變器之間的牽引和耦合，以及不同的負載包括線性和非線性都連接在公用電網上形成一個複雜的高階電網。更重要的是，在公共耦合點（PCC）不確定的阻抗變化使產生的電力和電網電壓變得敏感和波動性。該系統會產生出多種類型的共振，這些共振可以被識別為由逆變器中的濾波器產生的共振，或與其他並聯逆變器產生的並聯共振以及與公用電網的串聯共振。分散式電網系統的可靠性和公用電網穩定性會因為多個並網逆變器連接運行而有所挑戰，並引起了學術界和工業界研究人員的極大關注。 該項目旨在解決上述問題。將研究一種寬帶諧波電壓補償器的技術，該技術可以增強系統的穩定性包括載有多個並網逆變器及線性和非線性負載。此外，補償器將集成具演化性的演化計算法，以提取一些關鍵參數來描述，監視和預測系統性能的特徵和穩定性。該項目將與政府部門機電工程署合作，研究團隊將安排在政府辦公室中將把技術雛型應用在單相和三相系統並進行評估，並與混合式可再生能源建築物系統一起使用。

11217320.label: Realisation of objectives
11217320.value: All objectives have been achieved. A wideband series harmonic voltage compensator (WSHVC) with an operating bandwidth of 10kHz for microgrids with a plurality of grid-connected inverters (GCIs) has been studied. The compensator consists of several components including the an active common-mode filter, a nonlinear inductor for stabilizing system operation, and the operation at the system level. We introduce a high-attenuation wideband active common-mode filter (ACF) section composed of an active capacitor and a small common-mode (CM) inductor. The active capacitor utilizes multiple coupling capacitors and a class-A bipolar-junction-transistor based amplifier. This design offers advantages such as low cost, fast response, and immunity to high voltage transients. The amplifier structure comprises a common-collector amplifier and a high-gain common-emitter amplifier with an active load. The ACF operates within a working bandwidth of 150 kHz to 30 MHz. To achieve high filtering attenuation, multiple ACF sections can be cascaded in a multistage configuration. The optimal number of cascaded sections is determined based on the required filtering attenuation. We evaluated the performance of both single-stage and multistage ACFs on two commercial power supplies rated at 90 and 1000 W, respectively. A comparison between the CM noise of the power supplies equipped with the proposed ACF and the original passive filters was conducted. The results demonstrate that the ACF has a significantly smaller physical volume compared to the passive filter, while exhibiting similar power dissipation. Detailed report can be found in [J1]. In typical distribution networks, constant power loads (CPLs) are supplied by source-interface converters. However, instability can arise if the interaction between the converters' output impedance and the CPLs' input impedance fails to meet stability criteria. To address this issue, a simple technique has been proposed. Instead of employing complex control strategies or introducing passive or active damping, the idea focuses on incorporating a nonlinear inductor in the converter's output filter to enhance both small-signal and large-signal stabilities. This approach ensures that the eigenvalues of the Jacobian at equilibrium points remain in the left-half plane. Additionally, it guarantees that the system's state can always return to the target operating point after encountering large-signal disturbances. Moreover, the physical size of the nonlinear inductor is comparable to that of the fixed-value inductor in the output filter, without compromising the ripple current requirement. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments were conducted on a downscaled system with a power level of 80W and a bus voltage of 24V. The experimental results align well with the theoretical predictions. Detailed report can be found in [J2]. The WSHVC generates a compensating voltage to mitigate high-frequency harmonic voltage at the point of common coupling (PCC). This leads to a nearly zero high-frequency impedance at the aggregate output of the GCIs, thereby enhancing system stability. The generation of the harmonic voltage relies on predicting the state trajectory of the WSHVC, determining the switching instants of the WSHVC switches during each half-switching cycle. The PCC impedance and the equivalent impedance of the GCI network are obtained by analyzing the system response to particle-swarm-optimization (PSO)-optimized multi-sine power disturbances. This analysis enables the prediction of system stability. Additionally, the values of passive components in the WSHVC are monitored by estimating their parameters using sampled state variables. To evaluate the performance, we conducted experiments on a 6.5 kVA testbed consisting of three commercial GCIs, a nonlinear load, and an adjustable grid impedance. The prototype, controlled by a 500VA, 1 MHz FPGA, and based on GaN technology, was utilized. A comparative study was conducted to assess system performance with and without the WSHVC. The experimental results align favorably with theoretical predictions. Detailed reports can be found in [J4] and [J5]. The research team has studied a system stability at the system level. A feasibility study on utilizing a TCP-based MMS report gateway model for transmitting type-1 messages over a Wide Area Network (WAN) has been carried out. The IEC61850-90-5:2012 Standard suggests using UDP-based R-GOOSE for exchanging type-1 messages, such as trip signals and other fast messages defined in the Standard, over WAN. However, the cyclic retransmission inherent in GOOSE introduces unnecessary network traffic as R-GOOSE messages are repeatedly sent. The proposed model eliminates unnecessary re-transmissions, thus preserving bandwidth for accommodating more Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) in the existing smart grid. To accomplish this, two IEC61850-based gateways have been designed and implemented to translate GOOSE messages to and from the MMS report over WAN. We utilize an HLA-compliant co-simulation platform to simulate a distance protection scenario through the gateways, investigating communication latency with different link speeds and WAN utilization rates. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MMS report gateway model for various WAN link speeds, ranging from DS3 to 1000BaseX. Additionally, the results highlight the importance of introducing Quality of Service (QoS) control to WAN routers to ensure latency requirements are met according to the IEC61850 standard. This feasibility study confirms that the TCP-based MMS report gateway model can be utilized as an extended feature for transmitting type-1 messages between substations over WAN. Furthermore, this method is suitable for connecting additional IEC61850-based Distributed Energy Resources (DER) to the existing smart grid involving WAN. Detailed report can be found in [J3].

11217320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217320.value: The research team has successfully achieved all objectives in their study. They have focused on various aspects related to power systems and communication networks. Here is a summary of their findings: 1. Wideband Active Common-Mode filter [J1]: The team studied a WSHVC for microgrids with multiple grid-connected inverters (GCIs). The compensator includes components such as an active common-mode filter, a nonlinear inductor for system stabilization, and overall system operation. They developed a high-attenuation wideband active common-mode filter (ACF) section, which exhibited advantages such as low cost, fast response, and immunity to high voltage transients. Experimental evaluations demonstrated that the proposed ACF had a significantly smaller physical volume compared to passive filters, while maintaining similar power dissipation. 2. Stability Enhancement in Distribution Networks [J2]: Typical distribution networks face instability issues when the interaction between source-interface converters' output impedance and constant power loads' (CPLs) input impedance fails to meet stability criteria. To address this, the team proposed a simple technique involving the incorporation of a nonlinear inductor in the converter's output filter. This approach enhances small-signal and large-signal stabilities, ensuring the system remains stable under various conditions. Experimental results on a downscaled system validated the effectiveness of this method. 3. Wideband Series Harmonic Voltage Compensator for System Stability [J4], [J5]: The WSHVC was designed to mitigate high-frequency harmonic voltage at the point of common coupling (PCC) in microgrids. The compensating voltage generated by the WSHVC results in a nearly zero high-frequency impedance at the aggregate output of the GCIs, thereby enhancing system stability. The team developed a prediction model to determine the switching instants of the WSHVC switches during each half-switching cycle. Experimental evaluations on a testbed confirmed the effectiveness of the WSHVC in improving system stability. 4. TCP-based MMS Report Gateway Model for WAN Communication [J3]: The team conducted a feasibility study on using a TCP-based MMS report gateway model for transmitting type-1 messages over a Wide Area Network (WAN). They proposed this model as an alternative to the UDP-based R-GOOSE communication method. The TCP-based model eliminates unnecessary re-transmissions, preserving bandwidth for accommodating more Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) in the smart grid. Through simulations, the team demonstrated that the proposed model is effective for various WAN link speeds. They also emphasized the importance of introducing Quality of Service (QoS) control to WAN routers to ensure latency requirements are met, according to the IEC61850 standard. Two PhD students were successfully trained.

11217320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217320.value: Future developments can focus on the following areas. First, advanced control strategies can be explored to enhance the performance of wideband series harmonic voltage compensators (WSHVCs). By incorporating advanced algorithms like model predictive control or adaptive control, the compensator's adaptability and performance can be further improved. Second, the integration of energy storage systems with WSHVCs can be investigated. Energy storage can help mitigate voltage fluctuations, improve power quality, and provide backup power during grid disturbances. Third, hybrid active/passive filtering techniques can be developed. Combining the advantages of active and passive filters can lead to improved filtering performance, higher efficiency, and reduced costs. Fourth, future developments in TCP-based MMS report gateway models should address scalability, compatibility, and security. Techniques for handling a larger number of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs), accommodating different communication protocols, and ensuring secure and resilient communication in the face of cyber threats are essential for the expansion and reliability of smart grid systems. Finally, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques can enhance power system stability, wideband compensation, and WAN communication. AI and ML algorithms can optimize control strategies, detect faults, analyze system behavior, and improve decision-making processes.

11217320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217320.value: The increasing emphasis on environmental protection has led to a rise in the popularity of distributed power generation systems (DPGSs) that operate independently or in parallel with the utility grid. In Hong Kong, the government has implemented renewable energy measures and incentive schemes to encourage investment in renewable energy. DPGSs convert electrical energy from microsources like wind turbines and photovoltaics into regulated DC power, which is then converted into AC power using grid-connected inverters (GCIs) for the utility grid. DPGSs offer advantages such as clean power, reduced carbon emissions, improved energy efficiency, and optimized asset utilization. However, the growing penetration of DPGSs results in a higher number of parallel GCIs, forming a complex electric network with correlations and coupling among inverters, loads, and the utility grid. Uncertain impedance changes at the point of common coupling (PCC) can make the grid voltage sensitive to power fluctuations, leading to resonances within the system. These resonances, including internal resonance, parallel resonance, and series resonance, pose challenges to the reliability of DPGSs and the stability of the utility grid. To address these issues, this project aims to study a wideband harmonic voltage compensator technology that enhances system stability with multiple parallel GCIs and linear/nonlinear loads. The compensator will integrate an evolutionary computation-based algorithm to extract critical parameters for system performance monitoring, prediction, and stability assessment.

11217420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217420.value: In this project, we investigate a wearable-based technique to track the 3D hand pose of 14 hand skeleton points using the Electromyography (EMG) and motion sensor data from a commercial wearable armband only. This tracking system is not intended to be designed by employing machine learning algorithms to train it on a specific set of pre-defined hand gestures. We instead strive to track the movement of 3D hand skeleton continuously over time, which can thus serve as a generic and portable platform for the hand-pose oriented applications with new potentials. To track hand poses, existing methods mainly deploy external devices, e.g., cameras and depth sensors, or paste many sensors on forearm by assuming no arm movements. Our technique adopts all the sensory data from only one armband (for one hand), and it is intended to be portable and lightweight to execute on user’s smartphone directly to support upper-layer applications. Recently, researchers find that EMG sensors can measure muscles’ electrical activities and they can be integrated into small devices. Hence, many lightweight EMG-based armbands and methods appear. However, these designs are still limited to recognize a set of pre-defined hand gestures, which cannot track continuous hand-pose motions for applications yet. This project plans to take one step further to track 3D hand poses using the same set of EMG data from commercial armband, while encounters two main challenges. First, armband’s EMG sensors inevitably collect mixed EMG signals from multiple forearm muscles because of the fixed sensor positions on the device, but the prior bio-medical hand-pose models are built on the isolated EMG signal inputs collected from different forearm spots for different muscles. In this project, we will propose a novel wearable sensing based solution to fulfill the hand-pose tracking still using armband's EMG data as input. Second, even the hand pose could be tracked well finally, the system is still not immediately usable if two practical issues are not addressed, including the system setup overhead and the position difference in how the user wears armband each time. In this project, we will propose effective countermeasures to enhance the system’s applicability significantly. In summary, the idea to investigate a wearable-based hand-pose tracking design is of essential novelty, which could offer a fully portable and ubiquitous solution and allow users to bring along the hand-pose tracking ability, without deploying external cameras or depth-sensors. Moreover, technical contributions of our wearable sensing designs are also innovative and useful. 在此項目中，我們計劃研究一項可穿戴技術。該技術僅僅使用可穿戴式臂環的肌電傳感器和運動傳感器的感知數據，來追踪包含14個骨骼點的手部姿態。該設計不是為了進行預定義手勢的識別，而是為了實時地追踪手部骨骼點的空間位置，從而可以為面向手部的上層應用提供更加通用和便攜式的平台。為了追踪手勢，現有的方法主要是部署外部設備，例如攝像機和深度傳感器，或者在假設手臂沒有運動的情況下，將許多傳感器粘貼在用戶的前臂上。而我們的技術將僅僅使用一個臂環所感知的數據來追踪一隻手的骨骼點。並且我們的設計致力於是便攜式和輕量級的，可以直接在用戶的智能手機上運行來支持上層的應用。最近，研究人員發現肌電傳感器可以測量肌肉的電活動，並且可以集成到小型設備中。因此，出現了許多基於肌電的輕型臂環和設計。但是，這些設計仍然僅限於識別一組預定義的手勢，尚不能追踪連續的手勢運動。該項目計劃再向前邁進一步，使用商用臂環感知數據進而來進行手部姿態的追踪，但面臨兩個主要的挑戰。首先，由於設備上固定的傳感器位置，臂環的肌電傳感器不可避免地會從多個前臂肌肉收集混合的肌電信號，但是先前的生物醫學手部姿態模型主要是基於從不同前臂點針對不同肌肉收集分離的肌電信號作為輸入而構建的。在該項目中，我們將提出一種創新的基於可穿戴式傳感器的解決方案，從而仍然使用臂環可以完成手部姿態的追踪。其次，即使最終可以很好地追踪手勢，如果沒有解決系統可用性的問題，例如系統設置開銷和用戶每次佩戴臂環的位置差異，該設計仍然無法很好的在現實中使用。在此項目中，我們將提出有效的對策，以提高系統的適用性。總而言之，該研究中提出的基於可穿戴式的手部姿勢追踪設計的想法非常新穎。該項目可以提供一種完全便攜且普適的解決方案，並允許用戶在不部署外部攝像機或深度傳感器的情況下實現手部姿態追踪功能。此外，我們的設計也具有技術方面的創新和貢獻。

11217420.label: Realisation of objectives
11217420.value: The project successfully accomplished all three proposed objectives, which centered on the development of a 3D hand-pose tracking technology, enhancement of the system’s practical applicability, and the implementation and evaluation. The first objective focused on developing a 3D hand pose tracking technology leveraging EMG sensors from commercial wearable armbands. Three key innovations were designed to address core challenges. First, the primary design challenge stems from the degraded quality of EMG data collected from the wearable armband due to the fixed location of the sensors on the device and the twisted muscles on the forearm. To address this challenge, a biomedical-guided neural network architecture was developed to overcome limitations in existing models, which assume isolated muscle EMG data and fail to account for signal degradation caused by fixed sensor placement and twisted muscles. Second, an attention-based neural adapter was designed to dynamically weight EMG and gyroscope inputs, ensuring accurate global coordinate alignment of reconstructed hand poses. Third, to expand compatibility with wrist-worn wearables (e.g., EMG sensors installed on smartwatches or wristbands, which can avoid wearing an additional wearable if the user already owns such a device), we designed solutions to optimize sensor placement and mitigate low signal quality, inheriting the advantages and tracking capabilities of our armband-based tracking designs while accommodating flexible but more challenging sensor deployment areas (e.g., on the back of a watch and on a watch band). These advancements enable robust hand pose tracking across diverse wearable configurations. The second objective targeted applicability improvements through three critical enhancements proposed as follows. EMG signals collected from different users (for training the system) inevitably contain some user-specific characteristics. If the user does not have the required devices to start the system training, the user will not be able to use the hand motion sensing service. In addition, the position where the wearable is worn may vary each time, including the possible distance difference between the device and the wrist, and the rotation of the device along the arm. To this end, a plug-and-play scheme was designed to address user-specific signal variability and an easy-to-perform calibration gesture to compensate inconsistent device positioning (e.g., rotational or distance shifts on the arm), requiring only a one-time calibration gesture. On the other hand, to mitigate weak EMG signals from suboptimal sensor placement, a dynamic regression method was introduced to adaptively constrain the search space, improving robustness of the tracking performance. Finally, a data synthesis technique was developed to automate training data generation for application-specific tasks (e.g., sign language translation), eliminating the need for extensive manual data collection. These innovations collectively enhance applicability in practice. The final objective focused on system implementation and validation. We have developed and prototyped our proposed designs. Based on the development, we have evaluated the system performance. The system’s adaptability was further extended through the scenarios that ambient sensors such as RFID have been installed already, enabling device-free gesture recognition by employing fine-grained channel state information from sensing signals. This design, has the potential to sense the user’s hand, such as gesture recognition, with less requirements for a device worn on the user's arm, i.e. in a device-free manner. In addition, we also applied our tracking design experiences to wearable-based continuous authentication and attention tracking that, combined with hand tracking, can improve the quality of service when users control or interact with small-screen devices. In summary, all the objectives proposed in this project have been achieved.

11217420.value: The major findings and resource outcome of this project are as follows. We found that to achieve accurate hand-pose tracking using EMG sensors in wearable devices, although existing biomedical models cannot be used directly, they provide useful tips to convert EMG data into hand poses, and we can leverage them to design biomedically guided deep learning solutions. We can further use IMU data and deep learning techniques to place the tracked hand poses in a global coordinate system. Our design has been reported at IMWUT/UbiComp 2021 (Part-C-8-[1]). If EMG sensors are moved from the forearm area to the wrist area, the muscle distribution will be further distorted and the signal quality will become lower. We need to carefully plan the location of EMG sensors and propose effective countermeasures to improve the signal quality. Our design to address these challenges has been reported at IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[2]). To improve the applicability of hand-pose tracking, we found that the system needs to adapt to the diversity of users and the inconsistency of device positions. In addition, when some sensor positions are not ideal and affect the signal quality, we also need to overcome this problem. When applying hand tracking to downstream applications, extensive manual data collection is usually required. We proposed effective countermeasures to address these applicability issues and reported them at IMWUT/UbiComp 2021 (Part-C-8-[1]), IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[2]), IEEE INFOCOM 2022 (Part-C-9-[1]), and IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[3]). Finally, the hand-pose tracking performance of our designs have been evaluated and reported at IMWUT/UbiComp 2021 (Part-C-8-[1]) and IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[2]). Through our development and prototyping, we further found that environmental sensors can also benefit hand tracking to achieve device-free gesture recognition. Our design was reported in IEEE INFOCOM 2022 (Part-C-9-[2]) and IEEE/ACM ToN (Part-C-8-[4]). Our tracking design experience can also inspire other sensing modalities with broader uses, including wearable-based authentication and attention tracking, which can potentially be combined with hand tracking to improve the quality of service when users control or interact with small-screen devices. Our designs have been published in ACM UbiComp/ISWC 2023 Adjunct (Part-C-9-[3]) and ACM SenSys 2022 (Part-C-9-[4]).

11217420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217420.value: In the future, we plan to explore the following directions, including: 1) Multi-sensor fusion in smart homes: combining hand-pose tracking results from different sensors, where cameras can provide high-quality tracking results but may have many blind spots, while wearable sensors can provide continuous tracking; 2) Semantic gesture interpretation: combining large language models with tracking results to enhance interactive intelligence by linking tracked hand poses with contextual meaning; and 3) Edge computing optimization: optimizing the execution of the deep learning models involved on mobile edge devices for efficient execution.

11217420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217420.value: This project designs a smart system that tracks hand movements using signals from the EMG sensors on wearable devices. These devices detect muscle activity (similar to how fitness trackers measure heart rate) to figure out how your fingers and hands are moving in 3D space. The goal was to make tracking more accurate, user-friendly, and practical for everyday life. First, we solved a main challenge, that is, muscle signals from wearables are often messy because sensors cannot be placed perfectly on user’s arm. We thus designed an AI-powered solution that learns to clean up these signals and turn them into precise hand poses in 3D space, even when sensors shift slightly or are installed closer to the wrist. Next, we identified and solved a set of applicability issues to make the system easier to use. Instead of requiring complex setups or hours of training, users just perform a quick calibration gesture. The system also adapts to different users and weak signals, making it reliable. Finally, we have developed and prototyped our proposed designs for validation and evaluation. The research outputs have great potentials to enable useful applications and made meaningful contributions to wearable sensing and mobile computing.

11217620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217620.value: Under active research for years, encrypted databases are considered as a primary line of defence against the ever-growing data and privacy breaches. They allow users to make confidential queries directly over encrypted data, reducing information disclosure to well-defined leakage profiles. Despite the fruitful progress on enriched query types and improved efficiency, encrypted databases have not yet achieved widespread adoption for commercialization, because they may not be as secure as claimed in practice. Recent studies revealed that the legitimately admitted leakage profiles, while seemingly innocent, can be exploited to recover the queries and eventually devastate the system's privacy guarantee. Several countermeasures were subsequently proposed to patch the exploitations, but still with limits in theoretical account on either security or efficiency. Moreover, today's scientific knowledge on how the well-defined leakage relates to the broader privacy risk is still lacking. Our preliminary findings have shown potentials to fill such knowledge gap, and, surprisingly, further suggest possible pathways towards stronger attacks and defences. These insights open up completely new perspectives for reasoning the security of encrypted databases. In this proposal, we will conduct systematic investigations on leakage exploitation and corresponding mitigation in modern encrypted searchable databases. Our plan involves two parts: 1) understanding why the leakage is fundamentally exploitable; 2) investigating how to harden encrypted databases accordingly. We begin with the investigation on new algebraic approaches to model the indexing information transformation between the original and encrypted databases, and explain the inherent privacy risks mathematically. Grounded on these theoretical results, we will then develop a systematic leakage-abuse attack procedure that aims to improve and generalize all existing ones. With these findings, we hope to further establish an information-theoretic framework to quantitatively measure the privacy risks and guide the design of effective mitigation techniques. In the second half, we will study how to refine the security definitions of existing encrypted search schemes, by formally capturing the security against attackers capable of mounting leakage-abuse attacks. We will then investigate proactive defence strategies, by designing self-adjustable probabilistic perturbation mechanisms, to construct encrypted databases with stronger security against generalised attacks. Besides, we will also explore a reactive protection strategy with possibly better efficiency, which avoids the cost of perturbation and on-demand rebuilds the encrypted database through privacy risk monitoring. Our results will establish theoretical foundations for exploring the fundamental security limit of encrypted databases, provide effective hardening techniques, and push forward the scientific frontier of this research area. 近年來，伴隨著數據洩露事件的頻發，人們對於數據安全的重視與日俱增，加密數據庫被視為抵禦不斷增長的數據和隱私洩露的主要防御手段。它使用戶可以直接對加密數據進行機密檢索，從而將信息洩露減少到定義明確的洩漏配置文件中。目前，儘管密文檢索在豐富查詢類型和提高檢索效率方面取得了豐碩的成果，但是加密數據庫離商業化還有著明顯的差距，因為加密數據庫在實踐中無法達到所聲稱的安全性要求。最近的研究表明，加密數據庫中定義的洩漏函數雖然看似無害，但可以用來恢復查詢並最終破壞系統的隱私保證。儘管目前已提出了若干對策以修補相應的缺陷，但結果仍不盡人意。一方面，目前的修復方案在安全性或效率上存在相當的局限性，不利於實際部署。另一方面，人們對洩漏函數與隱私風險之間關係仍缺乏科學的認識以及深刻的理解。因此，從根本上理解加密數據庫的洩漏原因並消除數據庫的安全隱患迫在眉睫。這些問題的解決可以進一步促進實現更強大的攻擊和防禦的可能途徑，這為推理加密數據庫的安全性開闢了全新的視角。 針對上述問題，在本項目中，我們將對現有加密數據庫中的洩漏模式和相應的防護措施進行系統的研究。我們的主要研究內容包括兩個部分：1）了解數據庫的洩漏模式並從根本上探究它可以被利用的原因； 2）研究如何相應地加強加密數據庫的安全性。我們首先以數學建模的方式，用索引矩陣之間的線性變換描述原始數據庫和加密數據庫之間的索引信息的轉換關係，並以數學方式解釋固有的隱私風險。基於這些理論結果，我們將開發一種系統的數據庫洩漏解析和攻擊算法，旨在改進和歸納現有的工作。然後，基於這些發現，我們希望進一步建立一個信息理論框架，以定量地衡量隱私風險並指導有效緩解技術的設計。緊接著，我們將研究如何通過形式化捕獲針對能夠發起洩漏濫用攻擊的攻擊者的安全性來完善現有加密搜索方案的安全性定義。然後，我們將通過設計可自行調整的概率擾動機制來研究主動防禦策略，以構建應對足以應對目前常見攻擊的具有更強安全性的加密數據庫。最後，我們還將探索一種可能具有更高效率的實時保護策略，該策略以上述隱私衡量技術為基礎，通過隱私風險監控按需重建加密的數據庫，從而節約數據庫安全防護所需要引入的額外存儲和通信開銷。 我們的結果將為探索加密數據庫的基本安全性分析建立理論基礎，提供有效的強化技術，並推動該研究領域的科學前沿。

11217620.label: Realisation of objectives
11217620.value: The mid-term progress has been reported before. Below, we briefly conclude major achievements of the project objectives. ## Realizations of objectives 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 #### Leakage-Abuse Attacks Against Forward and Backward Private Searchable Symmetric Encryption. In this research activity, we revisit the spectrum of forward and backward private DSSE schemes over the past few years, and unveil some inherent constructional limitations in most schemes. Those limitations allow attackers to exploit query equality and establish a guaranteed linkage among different (refreshed) query tokens surjective to a candidate keyword. Besides, we refine volumetric leakage profiles of updates and queries by associating each with a specific operation. By further exploiting update volume and query response volume, we demonstrate that all forward and backward private DSSE schemes can leak the same volumetric information (e.g., insertion volume, deletion volume) as those without such security guarantees. To testify our findings, we realize two generic LAAs, i.e., frequency matching attack and volumetric inference attack, and we evaluate them over various experimental settings in the dynamic context. These findings are published in ACM-CCS-2023 (Part-C-9-[1]). #### Attribute-Based Encrypted Search for Multi-Owner and Multi-User Distributed Systems. In this research activity, we propose AESM2, a new attribute-based encrypted search with ownership enhancement scheme for multi-owner and multi-user distributed systems. Our design enables users to search data from authorized owners with only one trapdoor. Owners can enforce owner level permission on users and encrypt their data individually with fine-grained attribute level permission. For practical consideration, we further devise an efficient revocation method of the owner level permission for users, where ciphertexts do not need to be updated. We formally define and prove the security of our design. Moreover, we implement a system prototype and analyze the performance from theoretical and experimental aspects. The evaluation results demonstrate that our scheme is effective and efficient. These findings are published in IEEE-TPDS-2023 (Part-C-8-[5]). ## Realisations of objectives 3, 4, 5, and 6 #### An Encrypted Document Database With Padding Countermeasures. In this activity, we present the design of ShieldDB, an encrypted document database. ShieldDB adapts the searchable encryption technique to preserve the search functionality over encrypted documents without having much impact on its scalability. Further, ShieldDB is designed with tailored padding countermeasures against known leakage-abuse attacks. Unlike prior works, we target a more realistic adversarial model, where the database gets updated continuously, and the adversary can monitor it at an (or multiple) arbitrary time interval(s). ShieldDB’s padding strategies ensure that the access pattern to the database is obfuscated all the time. We present a full-fledged implementation of ShieldDB and conduct intensive evaluations on Azure Cloud. These findings are published in IEEE-TKDE-2023 (Part-C-8-[6]). #### Oblivious Attributed Subgraph Matching. Focusing on the recent trend of outsourced graph analytics, in this activity, we design, implement, and evaluate OblivGM, a new system aimed at oblivious graph analytics services outsourced to the cloud. OblivGM focuses on the support for attributed subgraph matching, one popular and fundamental graph query functionality aiming to retrieve from a large attributed graph subgraphs isomorphic to a small query graph. Built from a delicate synergy of insights from attributed graph modelling and advanced lightweight cryptography, OblivGM protects the confidentiality of data content associated with attributed graphs and queries, conceals the connections among vertices in attributed graphs, and hides search access patterns. Meanwhile, OblivGM flexibly supports oblivious evaluation of varying subgraph queries, which may contain equality and/or range predicates. Extensive experiments over a real-world attributed graph dataset demonstrate that while providing strong security guarantees, OblivGM achieves practically affordable performance (with query latency on the order of a few seconds). These findings are published in IEEE-TIFS-2022 (Part-C-8-[7]). #### A Query Control Framework for Encrypted Range Query. In this activity, we focused on encrypted range query schemes. We identify and investigate two major aspects that have been largely overlooked in prior leakage analysis: 1) lack of a comprehensive approach for coordinating access, volume, and search patterns simultaneously, resulting in separate resolutions for each type of leakage; 2) absence of granular leakage quantification aimed at individual queries, leading to the gradual accumulation of imperceptible leakage over time. Based on this understanding, we present the query control framework RangeQC that provides a novel uniformed viewpoint of all three primary patterns at a per-query level. At the core of our techniques is a set of customized entropy analyzes tailored for the representative structures extracting various types of patterns. We further develop feasible countermeasures to suppress pattern leakage with tunable query control rules. Extensive evaluation results on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of RangeQC for leakage quantification and mitigation effectiveness. These findings are published in IEEE-ICDCS-2023 (Part-C-9-[2]). ## Realizations of objectives 1, 4, 5, and 6 #### Privacy-Preserving Content-Based Similarity Detection. In this activity, we focus on encrypted content-based similarity detection, which has wide applications. The design is based on hardware-assisted enclaves. To cope with the constrained enclave memory, we adopt the caching technique and devise a compact index to increase the cache hit rate for effective similarity detection inside the enclave. We also present a parallel algorithm for performance speedup, with an efficient enclave thread management mechanism. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that the overhead of our system compared to native processing (without SGX) is limited to 2.1x. Meanwhile, our tailored design can achieve up to 14.4x better computational efficiency compared to simply moving the target functionality to the SGX enclave via existing popular library operating systems like Graphene-SGX and Occlum. Our secure system can achieve a normalized similarity detection precision of about 90%. These findings are published in IEEE-TCC-2023 (Part-C-8-[8]). #### Privacy-Preserving Graph Similarity Search. In this activity, we initiate the study on privacy-preserving graph similarity search in cloud computing. We design, implement, and evaluate PrigSim, a novel system allowing the cloud to host an outsourced encrypted graph database and support secure graph similarity search, where the graph similarity is measured by the well-known metric called graph edit distance. PrigSim is built from a customized and delicate synergy of insights on graph modelling, lightweight cryptography, and data encoding and padding, providing protections for the confidentiality of data content associated with graphs, as well as hiding the connections among vertices. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the security design of PrigSim is accuracy-preserving, and presents modest performance overheads (with 9×-15× higher query latency than the plaintext baseline). These findings are published in IEEE-TKDE-2023 (Part-C-8-[9]). #### Privacy-Preserving Skyline Queries Over Encrypted Databases. Continuing the line of work on versatile search over encrypted data, in this activity, we focus on the support for secure skyline query processing over encrypted outsourced databases, where little work has been done. Skyline query is an advanced kind of database query which is important for multi-criteria decision-making systems and applications. We propose SecSkyline, a new system framework building on lightweight cryptography for fast privacy-preserving skyline queries. SecSkyline ambitiously provides strong protection for not only the content confidentiality of the outsourced database, the query, and the result, but also for data patterns that may incur indirect data leakages, such as dominance relationships among data points and search access patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SecSkyline is substantially superior to the state-of-the-art in query latency, with up to 813x improvement. These findings are published in IEEE-TKDE-2023 (Part-C-8-[10]).

11217620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217620.value: - Developed new models and analytical frameworks to quantify the privacy risks in encrypted databases. These new findings push forward the boundaries of leakage-abuse attacks and countermeasures in the searchable encryption contexts. Specifically, we have identified new ways to possibly expose the encrypted queries in various encrypted search settings with various adversarial assumptions. These findings have greatly enriched the frontier understanding of the encrypted search primitives and their associated potential risks. Jointly, they will provide more well-informed options for future adoptions in the real-world. The results were majorly reported at IEEE TDSC, IEEE TIFS, and ACM CCS. - Developed new countermeasure mechanisms and frameworks to mitigate the risks of encrypted search. These findings, such as principled paddings / perturbations designs, proactive query countrols, fine-grained query result access mechanisms, and even strong oblivious algorithms, offer various balancing points among protection strength and performance. Jontly, these findings provide a suite of new countermeasure options, greatly enriching the existing methods to protect against known leakage-abuse attacks. The results were majorly reported at IEEE TDSC, IEEE TKDE, TPDS, ICDCS, and also ACM CCS. - Developed new encrypted search primitives for various versatile query scenarios. These include encrypted skyline queries, encrypted content-based similarity search, encrypted range queries, and encrypted graph analytics. These primitives greatly enhance the existing landscape of encrypted search primitives, and open up new application scenarios. The results were majorly reported at IEEE TKDE, TCC, and more. Moreover, during this project period, we have also systematically summarised the latest advancement of the fast-developing field on searchable encryption, from theories to practices, and these summaries were reported at our published book in 2023 (see Part-C for further details).

11217620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217620.value: - Full-fledged encrypted datastores with system-wide leakage mitigation. Building on top of our findings so far, the immediate next step would be to study the interplay of various individual defence mechanisms and how to make them work together in a systematic way over a fully-functional encrypted data stores. The problem is of particular importance, as specific privacy requirements might be needed for specific workload (e.g., key-value, range, and dynamic workloads). Ideally, we would prefer a tunable design to flexibly strike the right balance over security and performance for various application needs. - Real-time risk assessment over encrypted database. Since leakages in SSE are revealed incrementally with each query, there is a pressing need for risk assessments to be conducted on the fly, enabling prompt alerts to clients about potential privacy threats. Existing methods for quantifying leakage typically require a comprehensive analysis of all queries, unsuitable for real-time risk assessment. We will explore machine learning based approaches to give this challenging task a best-effort try. Our hypothesis is to leverage learning algorithms to automatically identify keyword features from public auxiliary information, memorizing them as a classifier for efficient prediction on the likelihood of leakage associated with each query (on the fly).

11217620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217620.value: Encrypted databases are designed to safeguard data by allowing queries on encrypted information, but they're not as secure as we might hope. Recent research has shown that even the allowed "leakage" of information can be used by attackers to compromise privacy. In this project, we have pushed forward a comprehensive study to explore why these leaks occur and how to mitigate the risks associated with them. First, we have looked at new ways to model how the adversary's view might change from plain data to its encrypted form in the searchable encryption context, pinpointing where privacy risks might come from. Then, we have developed new attack methods to understand these risks fully, and createed frameworks to measure and reduce them, respectively. We have also redefined what security means for these databases to better defend against such attacks, using strategies like adaptive paddings / perturbations, proactive query countrols, fine-grained query result access mechanisms, and even strong oblivious algorithms. These new options offers various balancing points among protection strength and performance, and could lead to stronger, more practical encrypted databases.

11217720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217720.value: Mueller polarimetric imaging (MPI), as one of polarimetric imaging modalities, is an effective tool for enhancing the imaging contrast. It can also decipher additional information on the material and structural properties of the imaged object due to their different responses to various polarization states of the probing waves. MPI is a proven imaging approach in microwave and optical domains. However, little work has been done at THz regime on its distinctive advantages in areas where the subjects under study are characterized by non-ionizing, high sensitivity to water molecules and low-energy vibrations of macromolecules. The lack of commercially available THz linear and circular polarizers discourages the popular use of MPI. We have successfully demonstrated MPI at 0.3 THz both in reflection and transmission modes. MPI results in 4-by-4 Mueller matrix images that can further be decomposed to reveal the degree of depolarization of the polarized incident wave upon interaction with the imaged object; the transmittance or reflectance of the object depending on incident polarization; and the phase difference between the orthogonally polarized components of the incident wave reflecting from or propagating through the object. The linear and circular components of these decomposed images are sensitive to oriented and chiral structures, respectively. Nevertheless, these THz wave interactions with the materials, in particular biomaterials, are frequency dependent. Furthermore, Mueller matrix images are 2D projection of a 3D object. With a raster scanning mechanism in the transverse plane using translational stages, THz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) can provide axial resolution and form 3D image of an object. This is achieved by using deconvolution signal processing of the measured reflected or transmitted signal against a reference signal. Taking advantages of the distinctive properties of THz waves, we propose to combine the high polarization sensitivity of MPI and the axial resolution of the TDS imaging to advance THz 3D imaging. In this project, we propose to design, fabricate and test THz wideband polarizers and reflectors using metasurface technologies. Wideband linear and circular polarizers make it possible for MPI to have a wide range of frequencies using TDS. Reflectors with focal planes vary with frequencies and this allows us to revolve the axial resolution with higher accuracy. To address the time-consuming raster scanning, we propose to adopt a two-rotating-mirror approach for the 2D scanning with emphasis on uniform spot shape across the scanning region. Successful designs will be incorporated into our time-domain and frequency-domain THz spectrometers for 3D imaging. 穆勒偏振成像（MPI）是一種偏振成像方式，可以有效地增強成像對比度。同時，由於成像物體的材料和結構特性對探測波的各種偏振狀態有不反應， MPI也可以提取成像物體的材料和結構特性資訊。在微波和光學頻段 MPI效果已經被證明。 太赫茲波譜具有非電離、對水分子的高敏感性和低能量大分子的振動等優勢，但是至今有關太赫茲的MPI工作仍然很少，主要是因為商用太赫茲線極化和圓極化偏振器的缺乏限制了太赫茲MPI的廣泛使用。 在0.3 THz頻率，我們成功地演示了反射和透射模式下的MPI。 MPI生成了4 x 4 的穆勒矩陣圖像，其可以被進一步分解來顯示：與成像物體相互作用時偏振入射波的去極化程度；與入射波極化相關的成像物體的透射率或反射率；以及從成像物體反射或透射的正交偏振分量之間的相位差。這些分解圖像的線極化和圓極化分量分別對定向和手性結構敏感。然而，這些太赫茲波與材料的相互作用取決於工作頻率，尤其是與特定的生物材料相互作用。 此外，穆勒矩陣圖像是對3D物體的2D投影。 太赫茲時域光譜（TDS）能夠在橫向平面進行光柵掃描，通過對參考信號和測量的反射或透射信號進行解卷積信號處理，可以提供軸向解析度並形成物體的3D圖像。利用太赫茲波的獨特特性，我們提出結合高極化靈敏度的MPI和高軸向解析度的TDS成像來提高THz 3D成像。 在本項目中，我們利用超表面技術設計、製造和測試了THz寬頻偏光片和反射器。 寬頻線極化和圓極化偏振片使MPI具有較寬的工作頻率。反射器的焦平面會隨頻率變化而移動，這能夠使我們獲得更高的軸向解析度。 為了解決柵格掃描的耗時問題，我們提出採用雙旋轉鏡方法，在整個掃描區域上形成均勻的斑點形狀進行2D掃描。 該設計將會集成到我們的時域和頻域THz光譜儀進行3D成像。
