11217720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217720.value: The Mueller matrix (MM) and its polar decomposition are employed to enhance the quality of imaging. A typical 4×4 MM requires 36 different polarization states of incident and received waves, including vertical, horizontal, and ±45-degree linear polarizations (LPs) and left-handed (LH) and right-handed (RH) circular polarizations (CPs). We constructed multispectral Mueller matrices using terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy, extending the 2D image of the object-under-test (OUT) into 3D with the third orthogonal dimension in time. Papers 1 and 2 successfully demonstrated 3D multispectral Mueller polarimetric imaging, addressing Objective 2. However, broadband THz CP polarizers are rather difficult to achieve. Paper 1 demonstrated that the 3×3 MM using only LPs is sufficient for the characterization of non-depolarizing samples. Wideband LP polarizers working from 0.2 to 1 THz, addressing Objective 1, were designed, and +45-degree (P), 90-degree (V), and -45-degree (M) LPs were employed to compute the 3×3 MM. P and M LP were achieved by rotating the orientation of the polarizer. In Paper 2, the 36 measurements for the 4×4 MM were substantially reduced to 4 measurements of 2 orthogonal LPs, namely, P and M, nullifying the necessity of wideband CP polarizers. Nevertheless, wideband CP polarizers (DOI:10.1364/OL.488037) and a CP polarization selective surface (DOI:10.1364/OL.488037) working from 0.57 to 1 THz and 0.6 to 1.08 THz, respectively, have been achieved, addressing Objective 1. These devices were not used in the 3D MM imaging and are not listed as project outputs. The crux of Objective 4 is to achieve beam scanning with minimized spot distortion. Paper 3 presented a novel approach to reducing coma for transmitarray off-axis scanning at THz frequencies. The scanning angle can be up to 50-degree with a -3dB spot size of less than 4 mm at 290 GHz. The measured sidelobes are all below -10dB within the whole scanning range. The approach can be generalized to 2D focus scanning. Paper 4 realized achromatic super-resolution focusing with a high numerical aperture (NA) of 0.555 across the 0.2 to 0.9 THz range. Subwavelength features separated by approximately 0.2 mm can be resolved with high precision at 700 GHz. Paper 5 addressed Objective 3 by designing two metalens; one increases its focal length by varying the frequency of the incident wave while the other one reduces its focal length by the same amount, i.e., from 30.4 to 35.6mm and from 52.2 to 47mm, respectively, from 250 to 300 GHz.

11217720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217720.value: Paper 5 was a joint research with MIT and Georgia Tech. We agreed that the MIT group, led by Professor Steve G. Johnson, would work on the design, and we would work on the fabrication of the prototypes and experimental validation. It turned out the resolution of our 3D printer was insufficient for their design, and they had to combine several pixels into one. While the experimental results showed the correct trends, they did not compare well with simulation results with higher resolutions. Objective 3 would have excellent practical value, and we hope to continue to look into validating the design using 3D printers with much higher resolutions. In Paper 4, we achieved achromatic super-resolution focusing using a gradient-index (GRIN) lens. Pixels of the GRIN with a constant thickness have different fractional volumes of air void to control the effective refractive index and, therefore, the phase distribution on the radiating aperture of the lens. We believe that the anisotropic pixel structures introduce scattering loss. The phase distribution can also be controlled by manipulating the thickness of the lens at the pixel level, i.e., by shaping the surface curvature of the lens, leading to easier lens prototyping.

11217720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217720.value: In this project, we have demonstrated the use of Mueller polarimetry to enhance the imaging quality at terahertz (THz) frequencies. Recognizing that imaging of the object-under-test (OUT) is done using a THz time-domain spectrometer, both the amplitude and phase of the transmitted THz wave penetrating through the OUT are recorded. The construction of a 4×4 Mueller matrix, typically requiring 36 measurements of different polarization combinations of incident and transmitted waves, can be substantially reduced to that of 4 measurements of two orthogonal linear polarizations, saving much of measurement time and alleviating the need for wideband polarization converters from linear to circular polarization. Beam deflection normally comes with spot distortion; we devised metasurfaces to minimize the distortion when the focused beam is scanning away from the normal direction. We also designed super-resolution metalens to enhance the imaging quality substantially. At 700 GHz, we achieved a spatial resolution of 0.2 mm. In collaboration with MIT, we demonstrated a pair of metalenses whose focal length can be increased with increasing frequencies or reduced with the same amount. This pair of metalenses could facilitate a better 3D volumetric imaging of the OUT.

11217820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217820.value: Engineering skeletal muscle sheet has drawn increasing attention because of its immense potential for repairing impaired muscle or building bionic machines. Spatial patterning cues have been widely used to align muscle precursors to facilitate their fusion and differentiation during myogenesis. Comparing to nano-topographic cues, micropatterning offers superior advantages in reproducing intricate patterns and providing significantly greater length and alignment of myotubes. However, on micropattern, cells were reported with an unexpected, unidirectional slanting angle deviating from the pattern boundary. Such deviation is consistently and independently observed by many groups, but has long been unattended and unexplained. When uncontrolled, it can disorganize muscle fibers, creating significant difficulty when engineering skeletal muscle tissue. Rather than a random, noisy event, recent investigation found that the slanting angle of cell orientation is indeed due to an intrinsic chirality of cells. Here, combining our expertise in cell chirality and pattern formation, we aim at engineering skeletal muscle sheet with scalable, intricate and more importantly, controlled patterns of myotubes. To achieve it, we will first systematically study the chiral orientation of myoblasts on micropatterned stripe during myogenesis (Task 1). The analysis will be based on our developed “outline-etching image segmentation” to extract the orientation of cell nucleus with respect to the micropattern boundaries. Next, we will explore an engineering strategy to guide the direction of myotube formation (Task 2). We will first investigate the possible suppression of cell chirality through image-based analysis of spatial distribution and chiral-biased swirling pattern of actin filaments upon treatment of actin inhibitors. As an alternative plan, we will also design the orientation of micropatterned stripe with a “compensation angle” relative to the desired myotube direction. Compared to the chiral orientation, the compensation angle will be the same amount of deviation but in opposite direction. Thus, when the chiral orientation subsequently emerges, the muscle fiber can be eventually aligned toward the desired direction. Finally, we will guide the formation of functional skeletal myotubes into desired, intricate, and function patterns by either compensating or suppressing the chiral orientation. Moreover, using soft material as the substrate, we will construct skeletal muscle sheets as bionic machines with a central ring lining with rounded myotubes and radial branches with longitudinally aligned myotubes to explore the corresponding locomotion and applications (Task 3). As a new perspective of incorporating the chiral orientation for building muscle pattern, our project would establish the knowledge foundation for tissue engineering in bionic applications. 骨骼肌層片工程在肌肉組織修復與仿生機械上的廣泛潛力引起相當多的關注。空間圖案因子經常被使用在對齊肌肉母細胞以促進成肌過程中的細胞融合與分化。相較於奈米級的拓樸因子，微圖案有卓越的優勢在再現複雜精細的圖案與產生較長且對齊的肌管。然而，細胞經常在微圖案上展現出非預期的、相對於圖案邊界的單一方向傾斜偏離。此偏離現象雖被許多研究團隊獨立觀測到，但卻是長期被忽略且未加解釋。一旦失控，此將打亂肌纖維，造成骨骼肌層片工程上的困難。 不同於隨機、雜亂的事件，新興研究發現此細胞傾斜指向乃出自於一種自發性的細胞手性。在此結合本團隊在細胞手性與圖案化生成的專長，我們著眼於研製一種可擴增且可控複雜精細的肌管圖案化工藝。我們首先將系統化地研究成肌過程中成肌細胞在條紋微米圖案上的手性排列（研究任务一）。此分析將基於本團隊研發的外輪廓蝕刻影像分割技術以擷取細胞核相對於圖案邊界的指向。接著，我們將探索引導肌管形成方向的工程策略（研究任务二）。借影像分析肌動蛋白纖維的空間分布與手性渦旋圖形，我們將首先嘗試藥物抑制細胞手性的可能性。另外，作為替代方案，我們也將設計鋪排條紋微米圖案的補償角度，使其具有相對於肌管最終期望方向的反向偏離角。因此，當手性排列浮現後，肌纖維即可對準於目標方向。最後，我們將借補償角度或手性抑制的手段以引導功能性骨骼肌管至期望的精細功能性圖案。再者，在軟性材料為基板上，我們將建造骨骼肌層片為基礎的仿生機械，其中縱向肌管將沿中央環狀圍繞的肌管放射性分支延伸，借此探索相應的位移運動與應用（研究任务三）。基於囊括手性排列以興建肌肉圖案的新觀點，本計畫預期奠定知識基礎於組織工程在仿生的應用。

11217820.label: Realisation of objectives
11217820.value: For the objective 1, we first characterized the chiral orientation of myoblasts cultured on micropatterned stripes. By leveraging our developed algorithm, “outline-etching image segmentation,” we are able to segment single nucleus from the dense cell population, enabling automated and quantitative measurement of cell chiral orientation. In this project, we have achieved a systematic study of chiral orientation on micro-grooves during myogenesis. As known, alignment of myoblasts prior to cell fusion is vital in skeletal muscle tissue engineering. By inducing C2C12 myoblasts on the groove patterns with different widths ranging from 0.4 to 200 μm, we analyzed the orientation of stained nuclei at 3 hours after seeding in growth medium (GM), Day 1 in GM until confluence, and Day 2 in differentiation medium (DM). It was found that cells were highly aligned to the edge of 0.4 and 2 μm grooves at all three measurements. However, the alignment of cells on wide grooves (50, 100, and 200 μm) uniformly distributed in all angles at the first measurement (3 hours in GM). Afterward, a negative-biased chiral alignment of nuclei emerged as cells become confluence (Day 1 in GM). This chiral alignment later became more coherent at Day 2 in differentiation medium, which is a very early stage of differentiation. Noticeably, the chiral alignment occurred after confluence is reached, indicating a subsequent movement of nuclei after initial alignment. This negative-biased chiral alignment was also inherent to the final myotube formation. To explore the chiral nematics of cells, we further studied the nucleus rotation narrow (2 μm) and wide grooves (100 μm) during migration. It was found that the cell nucleus rotated unbiasedly on 2-μm grooves, while the cell nucleus exhibited an anticlockwise (ACW)-biased rotation on 100-μm grooves on both days. Thus, our results suggest that nucleus rotating actively and chirality inside cells may guide the establishment of chiral orientation and cell migration, and eventually lead to a unified chiral orientation throughout the entire culture via the active nematics of cells. For the objective 2, we aim at development of an engineering strategy to guide the direction of myotube formation. We have adopted two strategies: chemical inhibitor and compensation angle that works in concert with such chiral orientation. We first examined actin inhibitors by single-cell rotational analysis on circular micro-islands. Cells spread on finbronectin-coated isolate circular islands (2,500 μm2) surrounded by cell-repellent Pluronic coating. Only single cells with round shapes were counted in the rotational analysis during the 2 hours and 10 minutes. The transient angular velocity of each nucleus was recorded to determine the clockwise (CW) or ACW rotational bias. According to the results, myoblasts exhibited a significant ACW rotational bias of 55.5%, which was enhanced to 62.08% by 50 μM of NSC, and 57.01% by 5 μM of Simfh2. However, cells presented a 56.4% of reversed CW bias by 50 nM of Lat A treatment. Therefore, Lat A was selected to regulate and study the effect of cell chirality on myotube formation. For Lat A-treated myogenesis, myoblasts were cultured on 500 μm plasma-treated microstrips in GM for a day till confluence but not formed chiral alignment yet before induction. Cell rotation and migration on the stripes were simultaneously monitored on Day 2 in DM with or without 50 nM of Lat A. Myoblasts stayed ACW-rotational bias in the control, while CW bias with Lat A treated medium. In the meantime, the migration (including lateral movement) was also inhibited by Lat A. Moreover, the orientation of cell nuclei was analyzed before, and after differentiation. For the control group, the orientation of myotubes (-15.61o ± 0.49o, mean ± SEM) and their cell nuclei (-7.14o ± 0.42o,) exhibited a significant negative-biased alignment after differentiation. However, both the orientation of the myotubes and nuclei exhibited a reversed bias with Lat A supplemented in DM during differentiation, i.e., they were aligned on the stripes with a positive-biased angle at 17.54o ± 2.07o and 7.68o ± 0.51o, respectively. Notably, the myotube formation rate was deducted by around 10% by Lat A treatment (Control: 49.45% ± 2.29%; + Lat A: 39.65% ± 2.68%). Thus, Lat A treatment inhibited the migration and intrinsic chiral bias of myoblasts finally led to the decreased myotube formation. As chemical inhibitor may lead to decreased differentiation, we next explored designs of micropatterned stripes with a compensation angle that works in concert with such chiral orientation. Hydrogels substrate is used here for its greater potential for applications such as tissue repair or biohybrid actuator. The compensation angle is designed based on the measured chiral orientation of the myotubes on the groove patterns. By designing and arranging the grooves with a pre-set orientation angle that compensates the chiral orientation of myotubes, the expression of chiral orientation of the muscle fiber would be expected to be aligned toward the designate direction. We first determine the angular distribution of myotubes formed on groove-patterned hydrogels. The mean the myotube orientation were aligned at -15o and -25o on 50-μm and 100-μm grooves, respectively. Accordingly, we made the new designs by arranging the wide grooves (50 or 100 μm) with appropriate compensation angles (+15o for 50-μm grooves and +25o for 100-μm grooves), which could shift the negatively aligned myotubes to be 0o. For the objective 3, we aimed at construction of muscle sheet with engineering pattern of skeletal myotubes. Here, using the hydrogels substrate released from the underneath substrate, the contractility of the aligned myotubes formed on 2-μm and 100-μm grooves (with 25o compensation angle) was investigated by the displacement of released hydrogels under electrical pulse stimulation. We found that the aligned myotubes on the hydrogel with 100-μm grooves were able to exhibit an 8-μm displacement, which is around 4 times more than the 2-μm grooved hydrogels, again demonstrating the better contractility of myotubes formed on wide grooves. To conclude, the lateral migration and intrinsic chiral alignment of C2C12 myoblasts are vital for developing functional myotubes. Hence, wide groove patterns could promote myotube formation by preserving the lateral migration and chirality during myogenesis. Finally, by arranging wide groove/stripe patterns with corresponding compensation angles to synergize microtopographic cues and chiral nematics of cells, intricate and scalable patterns of myotubes with enhanced length, diameter, and contractility are formed, providing a strategy for engineering skeletal muscle tissue formation. All results mentioned above have been published in an international journal (S. Wu, L. Ruan, J. Wu, M, Wu, L T Chu, H. K. Kwong, M. L. Lam, and T.-H. Chen*, Scalable Pattern Formation of Skeletal Myotubes by Synergizing Microtopographic Cues and Chiral Nematics of Cells, Biofabrication, 15, 025015, 2023 (IF: 11.061, Rank 6/115, 5.2% in Engineering, Biomedical, JCR2021)).

11217820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217820.value: Topographical cues have been widely used to facilitate cell fusion in skeletal muscle formation. However, an unexpected yet consistent chiral orientation of myotube deviating from the groove boundaries is commonly observed but has long been unattended. By inducing C2C12 myoblasts on the groove patterns with different widths (from 0.4 to 200 μm), we observed an enhanced chiral orientation of cells developed on wide grooves (50 and 100 μm of width) since the first day of induction. Active chiral nematics of cells involving cell migration and chiral rotation of cell nucleus subsequently led to a unified chiral orientation of the myotubes. Importantly, those chiral myotubes were formed with enhanced length, diameter, and contractility on wide grooves (50 and 100 μm) as compared to those on narrow grooves (0.4 to 2 μm). Thus, this active chiral nemtatics of cells including cell orientation, migration, and nucleus rotation is essential to promoted myotube differentiation. As the chiral alignment of myotubes is unavoidable and natural consequence of active chiral nemtatics, we developed a strategy that uses compensation angles to synergize microtopographic cues and chiral nematics of cells to guide the pattern formation of myotubes into designed, intricate and scalable patterns. Our results will have significant implications for pattern design in tissue rebuilding studies.

11217820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217820.value: We anticipate the construction of skeletal muscle sheet will offer a new strategy for future tissue engineering. Regenerative medicine aims at providing therapies for restoring or repairing impaired tissue since most adult tissue or organ contains only limited self-healing ability. Although skeletal muscle is highly regenerative, loss of muscle function still occurs if significant amount of muscle is severely damaged. Considerable efforts have been invested to build scaffolds that assist the tissue regeneration. However, so far, the intrinsic chiral bias in the tissue construction has been unattended and ignored in the most approaches. If uncontrolled, such cell chirality may defeat and frustrate the artificial allocation, leading to disorganized tissue patterns and functions. In contrast to others, we provide a possible strategy coupling the intrinsic cell chirality for guiding the development of skeletal muscle tissue as a patch of tissue regeneration. Thus, instead of using brutal forces to artificially dictate the tissue growth, we will provide a new concept of building tissue construct combining spatial pattern cues that works in concert with the cell mechanics. The success of this will benefit the medical practitioner by providing new therapeutic strategies for patients suffering from non-regenerative diseases.

11217820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217820.value: Do cells have chirality, or left-right asymmetry? If yes, how to measure and use it? It is a fundamental question in basic science. In recent years, researchers observed that cells can orient and migrate with left-right bias, or chiral bias, and such bias can later cause formation of tissue architecture with left-right asymmetry. As such, it is important to understand how cell chirality emerges and how it interacts with the microenvironment. Here, by culturing skeletal muscle cells on the groove patterns with different widths, we found that cells do exhibit chirality that causes chiral orientation of myotube deviating from the groove boundaries. More importantly, such chirality promotes myotube’s length, diameter, and contractility, suggesting the essence of cell chirality in tissue formation. Finally, we have applied our understanding of cell chirality to reconstitution of skeletal muscle tissue. At the end, we expect to deliver a method for guiding the formation of functional skeletal myotubes into desired, intricate, and function patterns for tissue repair or bionic machines.

11218020.label: Project Objectives
11218020.value: To investigate Beamforming (BF) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array with a wide scanning range: The scanning range of a planar BF phased antenna array (PAA) with patch or slot antenna elements is generally not wide. For instance, a conventional patch PAA has a typical 3-dB scanning angle of ~100°. Such a narrow scanning range cannot provide satisfactory wireless connections, especially at low elevation angles. In general, a wide scanning range is desirable from the system point of view because it can mitigate the problem of blind-spot typical of a BF PAA. A small scanning range is mainly caused by the narrow beamwidth of the radiating elements. A solution to this can be found in the DRA. This project will study the characteristics of the wide-beam DRA by changing the DRA structures and combinations of dielectric constants. The DRA elements and array will be fabricated with a 3-D ceramic printer. Also, efforts will be made to obtain the desired radiation patterns which can improve the overall radiation pattern of the array. After obtaining wide-beamwidth DRA elements, a DRA array will be built and optimized to maximize the scanning range. It will be done by changing the array shape and element spacing. Also, the methods which reduce the mutual coupling between the DRA elements will be developed. The results will be useful for obtaining an adaptive wireless connection. To investigate low-cost, low-loss, beam-locking DRA array for backhauling applications: The backhaul infrastructure is an essential part of a mobile telecommunications network. All of the voice traffic, instant messages, mobile data, and video traffic need to be backhauled from the base stations to the core network through wireless or fixed-line connections. For wireless connections, the high-gain antennas with fixed narrow beams are usually used to mitigate the path loss. A beam misalignment between the transmitting and receiving antennas may occur due to a subtle displacement or vibration by a gust, affecting the reliability of signal transmissions. Having an automatic beam alignment will solve this problem and a beam-tunable antenna is the required device. Beam-tunable DRA elements will be investigated in this project. Conventional PAAs are not suitable for a massive commercial deployment due to their high cost. Therefore, low-cost, low-loss beam-controlling techniques will be developed in the project for designing beam-locking DRA arrays. To investigate the mmWave dielectric resonator (DR) transmitarray: Like Objective 3, this objective focus on the design of a high-gain mmWave antenna, not on the PAA. Since 1960s, a number of transmitarrays with metal parts have been studied to provide a high antenna gain. However, they usually have the drawback of low antenna efficiencies at mmWave bands because of their severe conductor loss. In this project, the mmWave transmitarray will be fabricated with the 3-D ceramic printer. Novel DR unit cells will be studied. Since the DR elements have no metallic parts, the DR elements of the transmitarray have no surface-wave loss or conductor loss. As a result, our proposed DR transmitarray has lower loss than those having the metal parts. Also, it will use a 3-D printing material with a dielectric constant of ~10. This value is higher than that used in the substrate-based designs, giving the lowest profile among all the reported transmitarrays.

11218020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218020.value: For all wireless communication systems, the antenna is the front end that directly affects the quality of the signal transmission and reception. For a mobile antenna, a significant amount of the radiated power is dissipated in air without contributing to the information-exchange process. It is because a mobile antenna generally emits power to all directions, giving rise to free-space loss. This power loss can be reduced by increasing the antenna gain or equivalently narrowing the antenna beam. A direct method to provide a high antenna gain is to combine antenna elements to form an array. Over the last three decades, the dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been widely studied due to its many advantages such as its small size, low loss, light weight, and ease of excitation. As compared with the 2-D patch antenna, the DRA is a 3-D structure and therefore provides one more degree of freedom for its designs. However, most studies of DRAs have only concentrated on the single element and much less attention has been paid to the array design. In this project, three different kinds of DRA arrays will be investigated for the first time. First, the wide-beam DRA element will be investigated and used to design a square phased antenna array (PAA). The PAA can steer its beam to connect with a moving object. The element spacing and array shape will be studied to maximize the scanning range. Next, a beam-locking DRA array will be investigated for backhauling communications. The phase shifters realized by varactors will be integrated with the feed network of the DRA elements. The DRA array will have a narrow scanning range, about +/- 6 degrees for backhauling communications. The narrow scanning range is for the array to agilely steer and lock the beam. This enables the array to communicate with the other side of the wireless link effectively. Finally, the DR reflectarray and transmitarray will be investigated. Our proposed DR reflectarray can convert a linearly polarized wave to a circular polarized (CP) wave, giving the first CP DR reflectarray. For our proposed DR transmitarray, it has the lowest profile among all transmitarray designs reported in the literature. A design guideline will be devised for each of the antenna element and array to facilitate their designs. 在所有無線通信系統中，天線是直接影響信號發送和接收質量的前端。對於一個移動天線，大量輻射功率會耗散在空氣中，這無助於信息交換過程。這是因為移動天線通常會向所有方向發射功率，從而導致自由空間損耗。此功率損耗可以通過提高天線增益或等效地減小天線波束寬度來減少。實現高天線增益的一種直接方法是組合天線單元以形成陣列。 介質諧振器天線（DRA）具有許多優點，例如體積小，損耗低，重量輕和易於激勵；因此在過去的三十年中，DRA得到了大量的研究。相比於2-D貼片天線，DRA是一種3-D結構，這爲其設計多提供了一個自由度。然而，大多數關於DRA的研究僅關注單個DRA單元的設計，而對DRA陣列設計的研究則少得多。 在此項目中，三種不同類型的DRA陣列將首次得到研究。首先，將研究一種具有寬波束的DRA單元，並將其用於設計方形相控天線陣列（PAA）。此PAA可以操縱其波束以追蹤某個移動物體。我們將研究天綫單元間距和陣列形狀的設計，從而最大化掃描範圍。 接下來，我們將研究一種用於回傳通信的具有固定波束的DRA陣列。通過變容二極管實現的移相器將與DRA單元的饋電網絡集成在一起。此DRA陣列的掃描範圍較窄，約為+/- 6度，以適用於回傳通信。此窄掃描範圍是為了使陣列靈活地操縱並鎖定波束。這使得該陣列可以有效地與無線鏈路的另一端進行通信。 最後，我們將研究DR反射陣和透射陣。我們所設計的DR反射陣可以將綫極化電磁波轉換為圓極化電磁波，這將是第一個圓極化的DR反射陣。在所有已報導的透射陣的設計中，我們提出的DR透射陣具有最小的厚度。 此項目中的每個天線單元和陣列都會有一份設計指南，以方便其設計。

11218020.label: Realisation of objectives
11218020.value: (a) To investigate Beamforming (BF) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array with a wide scanning range: The objective has been realized successfully. To facilitate our DRA design, we have developed an artificial neural network (ANN) to identify resonance modes of a rectangular DRA. A large dataset was generated by simulating various rectangular DRAs using ANSYS HFSS. The resonance frequencies, physical dimensions, and three-dimensional electric field distributions of the DRAs were used as input features for training the ANN. The output of the network is a 12-element vector representing the probabilities associated with 12 distinct resonant modes. To increase the recognition accuracy, the method has been improved by processing and extracting E-field features of the DRA with a convolutional neural network. Also, a focal loss function has been used to handle the issue of imbalance dataset. We have proposed a gain-compensation technique to mitigate the gain degradation problem when scanning over wide angular ranges. It has been done by jointly considering the isolated element pattern (IEP) and the array factor, with mutual coupling effects included in the array factor calculation. The IEP has been optimized such that the element gain is approximately inversely proportional to the peak gain of the array factor, enabling the overall array gain to remain nearly constant across a wide scanning range. For demonstration, we have designed a X-band cylindrical DRA array in which a dip is introduced at the top of its element pattern to offset the peak of the array factor. Its beam has been shaped by a peripheral metal ring and two dielectric slabs placed atop the DR. We have used a multi-slot ground-plane structure and a dielectric superstrate atop the array to increase the H-plane and E-plane beamwidths, respectively. In array designs, it is important to reduce the mutual coupling between the antenna elements. We have proposed a novel decoupling technique that simultaneously achieves high port isolation with undistorted radiation patterns. The method has been demonstrated on a 1×2 DRA array, with zero inter-element spacing. Conformal strips have been attached to the DR sidewalls, aligned parallel to the E-plane. These strips, excited by coupling from the resonant DR, induce currents that generate secondary fields within the DRs. Notably, the resonant field and the strip-induced field within each DR exhibit antiphase and in-phase relationships, respectively. By tuning the conformal strips, the amplitude ratio and phase difference between these fields can be controlled, enabling field cancellation inside the adjacent DR based on the principle of superposition. As a result, when one DR is excited, the field inside the other is significantly suppressed, allowing each element to independently operate in its fundamental TEδ11 mode with minimal mutual distortion. To quantify the decoupling performance, a new metric named as energy storage proportion (ESP) has been introduced. When the ESP approaches unity, both high isolation and restored radiation patterns can be observed. We have also investigated a decoupling technique by enclosing two DRAs inside a dielectric decoupler. It makes use of the dielectric boundary of the decoupler to obtain internal reflected fields, which superimpose the direct fields to obtain a null field at a DRA position. This leads to a good reduction of mutual coupling. It has been shown that it is an effective approach. (b) To investigate low-cost, low-loss, beam-locking DRA array for backhauling applications: The objective has been achieved successfully. We have investigated a low-cost, low-profile, high-gain antenna array with flexible beam steering enabled by reconfigurable array elements. Far-field phase control has been achieved by integrating low-cost varactors into the feed lines of DRA elements, allowing for continuous beam scanning. Each DRA element incorporates two varactors, whose equivalent capacitance, and thus radiated phase, can be tuned via bias voltage. A stacked low-profile DRA configuration has been employed to achieve high gain and wide bandwidth. This compact phase-reconfigurable DRA design can be scaled to form a larger array with continuous electronic beam steering. Also, to change the radiation beam direction, we have investigated two pattern-reconfigurable antenna elements using diodes. By changing the ON/OFF states of the diodes, different feed networks can be switched. As a result, different operating modes and, hence, different radiation directions of the DRA can be obtained to change the radiation direction. (c) To investigate the mmWave dielectric resonator (DR) transmitarray:: Again, this objective has been achieved successfully. We have investigated a DR transmitarray for redirecting incident waves toward a specified direction. Each unit cell consists of symmetric upper and lower DR grids, functioning as receiving and transmitting layers, respectively. These grids are interconnected through cross-slots on metal plates, enabling energy coupling between them. Each DR grid comprises a 4×4 array of small rectangular DRs supported by a hollow substrate. Beam steering is achieved by tuning the size, and thus the resonant frequency, of the DRs to realize a full 0°–360° phase range. Notably, this work presents the first DR-based transmitarray with integrated filtering functionality. The lower-band transmission zero arises from destructive interference due to odd-mode coupling between the cross-slots. The upper-band transmission zero is attributed to harmonic-mode resonance of the DR grid, resulting in field cancellation. This dual-band edge behavior enables the transmitarray to simultaneously perform beam steering and frequency filtering. Also, an X-band DR transmitarray design has been investigated using a two-head deep learning model based on the ResNet architecture. This model has been developed to efficiently predict the phase value and transmission coefficient from the input height and diameter distributions of the DR elements. The trained model achieves a low mean squared error of 0.2855 and a high Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9954 on the test dataset. Its effectiveness has been demonstrated through the optimization of a transmitarray using a sliding window strategy, resulting in a synthesized window-based transmitarray with superior gain performance compared to conventional design methods. Finally, a wideband CP DR transmitarray based on rotated DR elements has been investigated. The sectored cylindrical DR enables polarization conversion through the rotation-phasing technique, providing a full 360° phase shift for effective wavefront control. A high dielectric constant of εr=16 has been used to miniaturize the DR elements, thereby enhancing phase resolution.

11218020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218020.value: (a) Beamforming DRA array with wide scanning range: Our trained ANN has achieved a DRA mode recognition accuracy of 96.74% ([1] of Section 8, Part C). The recognition accuracy has increased to 97.8% by using a convolutional neural network and focal loss function ([1] of Section 9, Part C). An X-band H-plane 9-element cylindrical DRA array has been studied ([2] of Section 8). This array achieves H-plane beam scanning from −72° to +72°. Multiple slots can be introduced into the ground plane to broaden the H-plane beamwidth to 217° ([3] of Section 8), although the E-plane beamwidth decreases to 68°. Applying a dielectric superstrate to an E-plane DRA array can lead to a wide angular range of ±80° ([2] of Section 9). Our dielectric decoupling technique ([4] of Section 8) has been demonstrated on a 1×2 DRA array, giving an isolation > 20 dB. It has been applied to an X-band 12 circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input–multiple-output antenna ([5] of Section 8). The measured −10 dB impedance bandwidth is 21.7% (8.88–11.04 GHz), with the axial ratio < 3 dB and mutual coupling < -21.4 dB. (b) Beam-locking DRA array for backhauling applications: A 1×8 H-plane DRA array with a narrow beam scanning range of ±6° has been designed for wireless backhauling ([3] of Section 9). Furthermore, an 8×8 DRA array has been developed. Its E-plane gain ranges from 21.69 to 23.37 dBi across a scanning range of −6° to +6°, while the H-plane gain varies from 21.69 to 23.28 dBi over the same range. In addition, we have studied two pattern-reconfigurable antenna elements for changing the radiation direction ([6], [7] of Section 8). (c) mmWave DR transmitarray: Our 26-GHz DR filtering transmitarray ([8] of Section 8) has a measured peak gain of 19.07 dBi, a compact structural profile of 0.33λ₀, a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 15.4% (23.9–27.9 GHz), and a frequency selectivity of 0.61. Our DR transmitarray designed with deep learning ([4] of Section 9) has a peak gain of 23.94 dBi and side-lobe level of below -15 dB. The CP DR transmitarray design ([5] of Section 9) has achieved broad 1-dB and 3-dB gain bandwidths of 17.1% (7.32–8.69 GHz) and 35.4% (6.17–8.82 GHz), respectively. A wide 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth of 19.2% (7.03–8.52 GHz) has been obtained. Additionally, we have integrated a DRA array with a substrate ([9] of Section 8) and verified by measurement.

11218020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218020.value: We have used full arrays in this project, i.e., there is a DRA element at each element position of the array. However, it is possible that we use sparse arrays to achieve the same radiation pattern, with some DRA elements left empty for some element positions. By using sparse arrays, we can save antenna elements, reducing the weight and cost of the array. Sparse arrays can be designed with machine learning. Traditional convex L₁-norm relaxation offers a computationally tractable approximation but does not guarantee true sparsity. In contrast, L₀-norm methods like Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) directly enforce sparsity through iterative selection. However, OMP often suffers from unstable, non-monotonic error behavior, including sharp increases in mean squared error (MSE) as residual tolerance tightens. To address the problem, an L₀-norm optimization framework based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) can be developed. This method overcomes limitations of OMP while preserving exact sparsity control. When applied to antenna array synthesis, this proposed approach yields sparser arrays with more accurate far-field radiation patterns than L₁-based approaches. The method should be useful for efficient antenna array designs.

11218020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218020.value: Dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) have been developed to enhance wireless systems including 5G systems. When forming an array, these compact and efficient antenna elements can steer a signal across wide angles for more directional transmission. A key advancement in DRA arrays is a technique that maintains a certain signal strength even as the beam direction changes. To minimize interference between closely spaced elements, innovative solutions using metal strips or dielectric covers have been developed to reduce unwanted signal overlap. This project has successfully developed a low-profile, high-gain DRA array with electronically tunable beam steering, ideal for wireless backhaul communications between base stations and core networks that use optical fibers. The use of varactors, which are small voltage-controlled components, can enable smooth beam direction control without mechanical movement, increasing the system flexibility. Additionally, flat antenna panels known as transmitarrays have been explored. These can redirect signals by adjusting the shape and size of their internal elements. Artificial intelligence has been used to optimize and improve the performance of a transmitarray, while rotating components that produce circularly polarized signals have been used for others. Together, these innovations provide useful antenna solutions for future high-speed and adaptable wireless communication networks.

11218420.value: Develop controllable MEMS compatible in situ synthesis processes for nanostructured energetic composites based on energetic coordination polymers and aluminum. 11218420.label: Realisation of objectives
11218420.value: (1) This project successfully prepared a series of aluminized energetic coordination polymers (ECPs) with different Al/Me ratios (0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5) and metal centers (Co, Ni and Cu). Their exothermic, pressure and combustion performance were systematically studied and compared. DSC results prove the existence of thermite reaction with exothermic ability and low onset temperature (<660 ˚C), which is beneficial to the maintenance of the hot environment and the post-combustion effect of aluminized ECPs. The results of close bomb experiment and open burning experiment prove that the thermite reaction greatly promotes the combustion propagation of aluminized ECPs. The most suitable Al/Me molar ratio is 3 or 4, where the peak pressures and pressurization rates of the three aluminized ECPs are relatively high. In addition, the type of metal is the key to determining pressure and combustion performance, because it determines the reactivity of ECPs. Among the three kinds of aluminized ECPs, the aluminized ECP(Co) has the best energetic characteristics and can be used as a preferred choice for applications. However, when long-time heat supply is required, the long-time stable combustion of aluminized ECP(Cu) can come in handy. (2) In this project, graphene oxide (GO)-ECP(Co) energetic film was also successfully prepared with excellent film-forming ability and energetic characteristics, and the role and mechanism of GO in the formation of its structure were analyzed. The heat release, combustion and pressure generation properties of the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film with different GO contents were systematically studied. GO-ECP(Co) with 7.5 wt% GO content was determined to possess the best comprehensive energetic performance due to its high heat release of 3389.9 J/g, large maximum flame area, high peak pressure (3 Mpa) and pressurization rate (40.3 MPa/s). The drop test proves the strong binding between the energetic film and the substrate. (3) More importantly, in this project, a transient microchip based on the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film and Au/Pt/Cr microheater was fabricated by a simple drop-casting method. The self-destruction of the silicon based transient microchip was successfully achieved by the local high pressure and heat generated by the exothermic reaction of the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film. The silicon chip was found to be crushed within 4 ms. The entire transient process including heating of the microheater, ignition of the energetic film and crushing of the silicon chip was completed within 1 s. (4) Many interesting results based on the developed nanomaterials in this project have been achieved (please refer to the publications in item 8 of Part C: Research Output), which are considered as the by-products of this project.

11218420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218420.value: Although much progress has been made in this project, further promising investigations can be carried out. MEMS-compatible preparation methods presented in this project can be applied to other metals. Co, Ni and Mn-based hydroxides are expected to be used as sacrificial templates to synthesize corresponding MEMS-compatible energetic coordination polymers (ECP) arrays. Graphene oxide (GO)-ECP(Co) has been found to have excellent energetic characteristics, so flexible GO-ECP films can be developed for ignition, propulsion, and explosion propagation. It is expected to become a new generation of universal energetic materials with various applications. The bimetallic ECPs have been proven to have a better catalytic decomposition effect on ammonium perchlorate. Accordingly, layered double hydroxide (LDH) can be used as a template for the development of bimetallic ECP arrays. LDH-based Al/ECPs are expected to have a faster energy decomposition rate and a higher pressurization rate. Special attention will be given to the combustion/explosion behavior at micro scale.

11218420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218420.value: Energetic materials including explosives, pyrotechnics, and propellants are widely used. Integrating energetic materials with microelectromechanical system (MEMS) to achieve miniaturized integrated smart energetic microchips is promising. The potential applications include actuation in lab-on-a-chip devices, ignition in automobile airbags, propulsion and attitude control of micro/nano satellites, and miniaturized electro-explosive devices. This project successfully prepared a series of aluminized energetic coordination polymers (ECPs) with different Al/Me ratios and metal centers. Their exothermic, pressure and combustion performance were systematically studied. Graphene oxide (GO)-ECP(Co) energetic film was also successfully prepared with excellent film-forming ability and energetic characteristics. The heat release, combustion and pressure generation properties of the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film were systematically studied. More importantly, a transient microchip based on the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film and Au/Pt/Cr microheater was fabricated by a simple drop-casting method. The self-destruction of the silicon based transient microchip was successfully achieved by the local high pressure and heat generated by the exothermic reaction of the GO-ECP(Co) energetic film. This project provides not only new nanostructured high performance energetic materials, but also controllable compatible technology for integrating energetic materials with MEMS to achieve energetic microchips. The research output can provide a theoretical basis for the research and design of energetic microchips in the scientific community as well as a scientific basis for the application of energetic microchips.

11218520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218520.value: Recording molecular motion on ultrafast timescales in real space has been a longstanding goal for unravelling detailed information about molecular dynamics. In situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) observations have become a powerful analytical tool for observing the dynamics or reactions of nanosized particles. However, there are three bottlenecks for imaging soft materials (including biological and polymers), namely, radiation damage, lack of time resolution and two-dimensional projection. It has been reported that the radiation damage of soft materials can be mitigated by a pulse electron source. To facilitate in situ TEM imaging of soft materials with well-controlled radiation damage while maintaining high space (x, y, z)/ time(t) resolution at room temperature, we propose to employ a high brightness/ high coherent pulse electron source produced by a high-frequency beam chopper for dynamic observations. The pulse electron source plays two roles: (1) controlling the dose rate and therefore minimizing the radiation damage to the observed object, while at the same time (2) recording high space/time resolved dynamics for the observed object in either single shot or stroboscopic imaging mode. In this proposed research, we intend to study the dynamics of conformation evolution and atomic dynamics for molecular motor proteins, Ni2+-DNA complexes, and organic molecules inside a carbon nanotube in either a dry environment or liquid phase using state-of-the-art ultrafast TEM. By implementing the graphene sandwiched liquid cells that we developed recently, the radiation damage to the biological samples can be reduced dramatically. With sufficient time resolution and no artifacts from radiation damage, we can capture the nonequilibrium intermediate states in the dynamic processes at near atomic resolution that may offer new insight into molecular science. The three-dimensional information of a specimen can be recovered from exit-wave reconstruction of the through-focal series image. Although it usually requires approximately twenty images to reconstruct the exit wave function for retrieving the three-dimensional atomic structure, the time resolution still falls well within the microsecond range in single shot imaging mode. In addition to the experimental observation, molecular dynamics simulations will be performed for the interpretation and support of the experimental observations. 利用超快原位電子顯微鏡研究液相中的分子動態 紀錄分子在超快時間尺度中實空間的動態影像是研究分子動態長久以來的目標。原位穿透式電子顯微鏡目前已經成為觀測奈米尺度顆粒的動態與反應的強大分析工具。然而對於軟物質材料（生物分子或高分子）的觀測仍存在著三個關鍵問題，分別是輻射損傷、缺乏時間分辨率以及二維投影。近期的研究已展示可藉由脈衝式電子源來避免對軟物質的輻射損傷。因此為了達到抑制對軟物質樣品的輻射損傷，同時還能在室溫下維持高時空分辦率，我們提出利用高頻電子斬束器來產生高亮度/高相干性的電子源進行動態原位穿透式電子顯微鏡觀測。脈衝式電子源將扮演兩個重要角色：（1）控制電子劑量率，並藉此最小化對被觀測物的輻射損傷。（2）在單次模式或閃頻模式下，以高時空分辨率紀錄被觀測物的動態行為。 在這份研究計畫中，我們預計將以香港城市大學最先端的高時空分辨電子顯微鏡研究在真空或液相環境中，蛋白質馬達、複合鎳離子去氧核糖核酸以及奈米碳管中的有機分子的動態構造形態變化。在具備足夠的時間解析度與去除掉人為輻射損傷後，我們將可以近乎原子尺度的解析度，捕捉到動態過程中的非平衡中間態，這將對分子科學研究帶來嶄新的見解。最近我們發展了利用石墨烯上下夾住而形成的液相環境式載台，利用此環境式載台將更能降低對樣品分子的輻射損傷。 先前的研究已顯示樣品分子的三維原子結構可藉由一系列不同對焦面的影像進行出射波重建獲得。雖然通常需要至少二十張影像才能重建出出射波函數以獲得三維原子結構，時間解析度在單次模式下仍可落在微秒範圍內。除了實驗觀察外，我們也會進行分子動力學模擬來幫助解釋實驗上的觀察。

11218720.label: Project Objectives
11218720.value: Reliability aware tail latency optimization schemes: First, the distinct reliability characteristics of QLC based server SSDs will be studied and modeled. Then, based on the reliability characteristics, refresh based tail latency optimization scheme, and latency variation aware data placement scheme are proposed to exploit the specific reliability features. Different from previous work, the proposed scheme focuses to cut tail latency for QLC based server SSDs, which is critical for servers. Access conflict minimization schemes: Due to the significant latency variation, the access conflict is more significant than previous SSD, which will introduce tail latency for server SSDs. To solve this issue, schemes are proposed from read and write view and multiple application view. We proposed to partition reads and writes into different areas to minimize their conflicts and proposed to partition different applications into different chips to minimize their conflicts. With these schemes, the tail latency of server SSDs due to access conflicts will be significant improved. Hybrid SSD design for tail latency optimization: By exploiting the state-of-the-art non-volatile memories, such as Optane, we are able to boost the performance of QLC based server SSDs but with new tail latency due to that these two-storage media need to communicate with each other. We proposed schemes to optimize the tail latency by minimizing the impact from the internal operations.

11218720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218720.value: While server SSDs are now considering using Triple Level Cell (TLC), low-cost high-density Quadruple Level Cell (QLC) soon becomes a candidate for server SSDs. The benefit for moving toward a higher density is lower cost for server SSDs. The challenges in adopting low-cost high-density flash chips are characterized by its low reliability and huge latency variations. First, the low reliability will introduce significant tail latency, which is critical to servers. Second, the access latency can be varied up to 30X based on our preliminary studies. Even though there exist some works proposed in optimizing SSDs for performance, little work has been done with considerations of server SSD’ reliability-induced tail latency. With our preliminary studies of the error models of TLC and QLC and the specific needs for server SSDs, optimizing tail latency of future server SSDs relies on good latency control with reliability enhancement. This project aims to optimize tail latency for low-cost high-density server SSDs by developing a set of optimization schemes with considerations of reliability. Due to the significant reliability issue of low-cost high-density server SSDs, it is prone to significant tail latency. In this proposal, we take QLC as an example for study, and the results will be applied for future low-cost high-density flash chips. Furthermore, we must emphasize that tail latency might also come from large latency difference between reads and writes, so called read and write conflicts, and execution interference among applications, so called application conflicts. This project proposes a set of tail latency optimization schemes for QLC based server SSDs by exploiting the characteristics of QLC: First, a set of reliability optimization or awareness schemes will be developed, including a refresh scheme for tail latency optimization, and a data placement scheme for performance optimization. Second, a set of conflict minimization schemes will be developed, including a read and write conflict minimization scheme, and an application isolation scheme for conflict optimization. Finally, a design with hybrid SSD will be further proposed to enable high density NAND flash with high performance and improved tail latency. The proposed schemes will be verified on an industry testing platform. The success of this project will enable low-cost high-density server SSDs with (reliability-induced or unreliability-induced) tail latency and reliability optimization. Those server SSDs could help to satisfy the needs of big data and machine learning applications. 11218720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218720.value: Guided by experimental results from a large suite of QLC Flash memory chips from major vendors, this project has the following major findings and research outcomes. First, we proposed a refresh reduction scheme to cut down tail latency while retaining required reliability, as we found that using optimal reference voltage to read leads to minimal Raw-Bit-Error-Rate; Second, we propose access pattern aware read-write conflict minimisation via partitioning of SSD, as read-write conflicts are often the main cause for the tail latency; Finally, to cut down tail latency, considering different access granularities, we proposed an IO framework for different IO granularities.

11218720.value: As we all interact with Flash memories/SSDs each day, either with mobile devices ( with Flash memory as storage ), or through interacting with servers, cutting down the tail latency is significant in terms of better user experience. Less waiting time in view web pages, and instant response from our laptop or servers are all critical in our daily lives, which the findings of this project can boost significantly.

11219420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11219420.value: Major findings are mostly reflected in the following three journal papers: 1. We identified an important limitation in classical Domain Adaptation methods, which fail to distinguish between marginal distribution shifts and changes in dependence structures, rendering them suboptimal for correlation-sensitive applications like finance. To address this, we proposed a Copula-based Domain Adaptation Network that utilizes Sklar's Theorem to explicitly decouple domain divergence into marginal differences and a novel Copula distance. Major theoretical findings establish the boundedness and monotonicity of this Copula distance, ensuring algorithmic convergence, while a proposed tanh-based approximation for Kendall's tau resolves gradient vanishing issues and reduces computational complexity from O(N^2) to O(N). This is mostly related to the TNNLS paper: Deep into The Domain Shift Transfer Learning through Dependence Regularization. 2. We bridged a theoretical gap in Unsupervised Domain Adaptation by proposing a unified generalization bound that's better than the classical limitations restricted to binary classification. By introducing "discrepancy distance," we provided a flexible framework applicable to general classification and regression tasks, theoretically unifying diverse divergence measures, including Wasserstein distance, MMD, and f-divergences—and grounding existing models like MCD and DAN. We then conducted a comprehensive comparative analysis of these metrics based on norm topology, convergence rates, and computational costs, revealing that no single measure is universally superior. This is mostly related to the TMLR paper: A Unified Domain Adaptation Framework with Distinctive Divergence Analysis. 3. We introduced the Dynamic Generative Factor Model with Attention-GRU (GF-AGRU) for portfolio construction, addressing the challenge of modeling time-varying joint distributions and tail risks in multivariate stock returns. By combining a single-factor structure with a non-linear transformation for asymmetric heavy tails, the model utilizes an Attention-GRU network to forecast dynamic parameters. We proposed a novel two-step iterative training algorithm to efficiently learn these parameters and simulate forward-looking returns for Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization. Empirical experiments on Dow Jones constituents demonstrate that GF-AGRU consistently outperforms benchmarks, including Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC) and static Sample Average Approximation. The strategy yields superior risk-adjusted returns and significantly reduces tail risks such as Maximum Drawdown. Crucially, ablation studies confirm that the attention mechanism and explicit heavy-tail modeling are the primary drivers of the model's success and robustness against market fluctuations. This is related to the JEDC paper: Dynamic CVaR portfolio construction with attention-powered generative factor learning.

11219420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11219420.value: Potential for further research: 1. Future research could extend this framework beyond the Gaussian assumption by incorporating more generic copula structure to better capture asymmetric tail dependencies common in finance. Additionally, developing adaptive mechanisms to automatically tune the trade-off weights would enhance flexibility and eliminate the computational cost of manual grid searches. (The TNNLS paper: Deep into The Domain Shift Transfer Learning through Dependence Regularization.) 2. Future research could focus on developing adaptive meta-learning frameworks to automatically select the optimal divergence measure for specific datasets, addressing the finding that performance varies by task. Additionally, extending the unified bound to explicitly account for conditional distribution shifts would further strengthen the framework's robustness in complex, real-world transfer scenarios. (The TMLR paper: A Unified Domain Adaptation Framework with Distinctive Divergence Analysis.) 3. Future research could extend the current single-factor framework to multi-factor models to capture complex systematic risks more effectively. Additionally, replacing the GRU architecture with Transformer-based models could improve long-term dependency learning. Incorporating realistic transaction costs and testing on alternative asset classes like cryptocurrencies would further validate the strategy's practical applicability. (The JEDC paper: Dynamic CVaR portfolio construction with attention-powered generative factor learning.)

11219420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11219420.value: These research collectively advance distribution-aware, regime-robust generative modeling for financial data. The JEDC paper frames dynamic portfolio construction as forecasting the time-varying joint distribution of multivariate stock returns, proposes an attention-enabled generative factor model that targets dependence and tail (crash-side) behavior, then simulates forward-looking return scenarios from the learned distribution and feeds them into CVaR optimization to form a dynamic strategy with stronger reward–risk performance and lower tail risk in empirical tests. The TNNLS paper clarifies why models trained in one regime can fail in another, the domain shift may arise from marginal changes or dependence-structure changes, and collapsing both into one discrepancy is often non-diagnostic in finance. It therefore regularizes marginals and copula-based dependence separately and learns their relative importance. The TMLR paper provides the theoretical backbone by deriving a unified generalization-bound framework that accommodates common divergence measures and tasks, and by systematically comparing divergence choices (e.g., f-divergences, MMD, Wasserstein) to guide principled model design and calibration.

11300020.label: Realisation of objectives
11300020.value: The PI has closely worked with his PhD students, Dr. ZHANG Jieru [Small 2022, 18, 2104844] and Dr. ZHANG Shengpei [Chem. Mater. 2024, 36, 4204], during the reporting period. The discussions on the realization of objectives below were mainly extracted from these two works. While many reports claim that single-atom nanozymes (SAzymes) bridge nanozymes and horseradish peroxidases (HRP), our findings [Small 2022, 18, 2104844] show they still follow the OH radical-mediated pathway like most nanozymes, lacking an HRP reaction pocket. Additionally, the positively charged single-atom centers may reduce their peroxidase-like activity compared to conventional nanozymes. Using Ru as an example, its chemical state on the MgO(111) surface is closely linked to its chelating atoms (e.g., cationic Ru–O3 and metallic Ru–Ru3 sites). The local structure of Ru atoms was found to be closely linked to their loadings on MgO(111) support. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) measurements were conducted and the corresponding x-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) and extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) were analyzed. In SAzymes, the positively charged Ru (+1.27 |e|) in the pyramidal Ru−3*O3c (i.e., Ru coordinated by three three-coordinated surface oxygens) configuration hinders H2O2 (or O2) reduction and H2O desorption, resulting in low peroxidase-like activity. In contrast, the metal-like Ru (≈0 |e|) in cluster nanozymes significantly enhances these processes. This difference in activity also affects their sensitivity in glucose/glutathione detection, with cluster nanozymes demonstrating higher atom efficiency and better performance as peroxidase/oxidase mimetics. We thus concluded that while single-atom catalysis maximizes active site utilization and aids in understanding product distribution, mimicking peroxidases/oxidases requires focusing on the balanced use of metal atoms and their reactivity, as the reduction of H2O2 (or O2) is the rate-limiting step in these reactions. To investigate the local structure of MgO supports and their interaction with Ru, we further employed MgO supports predominantly enclosed by (110) and (100) surfaces for an in-depth comparison [Chem. Mater. 2024, 36, 4204]. In the work, we found a strong correlation between the adsorption energy (Ead) of Ru atoms on various MgO surfaces and the local structure of their coordination sites. Notably, the pyramidal Ru−3*O3c configuration on the (111) surface exhibited significantly higher Ead compared to the bridging Ru−2*O4c and atop Ru−O5c configurations on the (110) and (100) surfaces, respectively. Due to lower degree of orbital hybridization, the latter two surfaces showed insufficient Ead to overcome Ru’s cohesive energy when a second Ru atom was added, especially on the (100) surface. We also explored the cases involving two Ru atoms on the MgO supports in the form of 2*Ru SAs and Ru2 dimmer. The 2*Ru case exhibits weaker adsorption and reduced stability compared to the Ru2 dimer on the (100) and (110) surfaces. In contrast, on the (111) surface, both the Ru2 dimer and 2*Ru cases show extensive coupling between the Ru4d and O2p states. Although Ru NMR was not available, our TMP−31P NMR spectra for MgO(111) and Ru/MgO(111) show a dominant δ31P peak at −48.8 ppm for Ru/MgO(111), attributed to positively charged Ru species, with the peak area corresponds to their concentration. The narrow full width at half-maximum (fwhm) of 1.5 ppm indicates a highly uniform local structure for the hosted Ru, likely in the pyramidal Ru−3*O3c configuration. For comparison, the TMP interaction with three-coordinated Zn2+ in pristine ZIF-8 yields a sharper δ31P peak at −44.8 ppm with a fwhm of 0.7 ppm, indicating high uniformity. However, after pyrolysis at 800 °C, a broad δ31P peak at −43.9 ppm with a fwhm of 15.0 ppm suggests that many Zn2+ ions were exposed but coordinated by varying numbers of N/O/C atoms, which cannot be distinguished by EXAFS. This variability highlights that atomic models of single-atom catalysts with poor site uniformity may not accurately reflect the coordination structure critical for catalytic activity. Beyond Ru, this work holds great potential in guiding the rational selection of surfaces to achieve a uniform atomic dispersion of other elements. Based on the discussion above, objectives 1-4 of the project have thus been successfully achieved. These include confirming the local structure of Ru single atoms on MgO supports, correlating Ru concentration with NMR peak area, and exploring their capability for H2O2 activation as HRP mimetics for biomolecule detection.

11300020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300020.value: Based on our understanding of H2O2 activation on Ru species, we also elucidated the mechanism for transition metal oxides as peroxidase mimetics, which is linked to the production of OH radicals through the radical activation pathway of H2O2 [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 14, 22728]. The debate regarding the peroxidase-like activity of Fe3O4 nanozymes compared to horseradish peroxidase was thus resolved [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2022, 13, 8872]. For CeO2 nanozymes, we demonstrate that Ce electron richness is the key to precisely controlling the radical/peroxo activation pathways of H2O2 on CeO2 surfaces, effectively mimicking peroxidase and haloperoxidase activities [ACS nano 2023, 17, 17383]. Using aniline as the sole substrate, it was found that these pathways occurring on CeO2 surfaces play a key role in determining the observed product distribution [J. Mater. Chem. A 2023, 11, 14034]. Building on this, we spatially decoupled H2O2 activation pathways and multi-enzyme activities in rod-shaped CeO2, chemically unraveling its facet distribution for the first time [Small 2024, 20, 2401032]. Recently, we further developed a one-step mass-production of CeO2 nanoparticles embedded in free-standing porous carbon with fully controlled haloperoxidase-like activity to combat biofouling on steel surface [Appl. Surf. Sci. Adv. 2025, 25, 100670]. A similar synthetic method was adopted to develop a one-pot, gram-scale synthesis of Fe-based nanozymes. These nanozymes were employed to demonstrate that the O2 activation pathways can also be controlled by tuning the electron richness of the Fe active sites for associated enzymatic reactions [Small 2025, 21, 2408609]. Insights gained from these CeO2/H2O2 systems were applied to the study of cyclohexene oxidation with H2O2 over layered HNb3O8 [Appl. Catal. B 2022, 313, 121461] and TiO2 [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2024, 15, 11620], where the Lewis and Brönsted acidity were found to regulate H2O2 activation pathways and hence the product distribution. In addition to H2O2/O2-relevant redox reactions, this funding also supports the investigation of hydrolytic reactions. For instance, the strong Lewis acidity of the CeO2(111) and TiO2(001) surfaces effectively catalyzes the dephosphorylation of phosphorylated substrates [Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, e202200202] and the hydrolysis of amide compounds [ChemCatChem 2024, 16, e202301585], respectively. A positive correlation was observed between the Ce acidity and methanol activation in the synthesis of dimethyl carbonate (DMC) with CO2 [Appl. Catal. B 2023, 336, 122914]. The production of DMC can be further enhanced by coupling 2-cyanopridine hydrolysis on the CeO2(111) surface [ACS Catal. 2024, 14, 16861].

11300020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300020.value: Our understanding of H2O2 (and O2) activation on Ru species, CeO2, and other transition metal oxides in 6.1 will guide the design and synthesis of relevant nanozymes with enhanced performance in the corresponding applications. Further development can explore the activation of H2O2 (and O2) through surface modifications and doping of specific nanozymes. The optimization of their radical activation pathway will benefit applications in the field of biomolecule detection. In contrast, the optimization of their peroxo activation pathway should improve their performance in environmental remediation efforts such as anti-bacterial/fouling applications. Overall, our work aims to facilitate the design and synthesis of nanozymes with controlled activation pathways for H2O2 (and O2), optimizing their performance for targeted applications.

11300020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300020.value: In this project, we established a guideline for the rational design of peroxidase nanozymes with improved activity based on their interaction with H2O2. Using advanced surface techniques, our findings indicate that the atomic arrangement of the MgO(111) surface can orderly accommodate Ru single atoms (SAs) at a high concentration, unlike the (110) and (100) surfaces. Thanks to the uniform coordination environment provided by MgO(111), the chemical state distribution of Ru SAs, revealed by probe-assisted NMR, is as narrow as that found in reported metal-organic frameworks. The chemical state of Ru on the support surface is closely linked to its chelating atoms and configuration. In the single-atom sample, the positively charged Ru (+1.27 |e|) in the Ru–O3 configuration hinders both H2O2/O2 reduction and H2O desorption, resulting in low peroxidase/oxidase-like activity. In contrast, cluster nanozymes feature metallic Ru (≈0 |e|), facilitating these processes. This difference in activity is also reflected in their sensitivity to glucose/glutathione detection, with cluster nanozymes demonstrating superior efficiency as peroxidase/oxidase mimetics. Our in-depth surface study of adsorbed H2O2/O2 on Ru/MgO(111) provides valuable insights for the future design of nanozymes with enhanced peroxidase/oxidase-like activity for biomolecule detection.

11300220.label: Project Objectives
11300220.value: The only objective of this proposal is to show that by using norms other than the Bombiery-Weyl for a polynomial system, and by consequently adapting the definition of several condition numbers for these systems, it is possible to modify well-known algorithms and their analyses to obtain a substantial decrease in their complexity.
rows: The only objective of this proposal is to show that by using norms other than the Bombiery-Weyl for a polynomial system, and by consequently adapting the definition of several condition numbers for these systems, it is possible to modify well-known algorithms and their analyses to obtain a substantial decrease in their complexity.

11300220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300220.value: Numerical algorithms are commonly analysed in terms of a condition number. In numerical linear algebra the norms involved in the definition of these condition numbers are carefully picked in each case to minimise complexity. In the analysis of algorithms dealing with polynomial systems, in contrast, the so called Bombieri-Weyl norm dominates the literature. The goal of this project is to introduce other norms in the numerical analysis of polynomial systems. Following the lead of numerical linear algebra, we want to consider a version of the spectral norm and analyse some of the best-known numerical algorithms for polynomial systems, both over the real and the complex numbers. We expect to be able to show that this new choice of norm leads to a marked improvement in the cost of the algorithm at hand. 通常根據條件編號來分析數值算法。在 數值線性代數這些條件數的定義所涉及的範數 在每種情況下都經過精心挑選，以最大程度地減少複雜性。在算法分析中 相比之下，處理多項式系統的所謂Bombieri-Weyl範數 主導文學。該項目的目標是在 多項式系統的數值分析。 遵循數值線性代數的先導，我們要考慮 譜範數，並分析一些最著名的多項式數值算法 系統，包括實數和復數。 我們希望能夠證明 這種新的規範選擇導致算法成本顯著提高， 手。

11300220.label: Realisation of objectives
11300220.value: The only objective of the proposal has been fully achieved. A functional norm on the space of polynomials was defined and, based on this norm, condition numbers for various problems were revisited. Equipped with these modified condition numbers a number of algorithms (for computing homology groups, the Plantinga-Vegter algorithm, and a linear homotopy algorithm) were, if needed, slightly modified and their complexity was re-assessed obtaining improved complexity bounds. With more time, I would have more broadly disseminated the result. My retirement in June 2023 did not allow for this. Hence, the 90% instead of 100% in the table below.

rows: The only objective of this proposal is to show that by using norms other than the Bombiery-Weyl for a polynomial system, and by consequently adapting the definition of several condition numbers for these systems, it is possible to modify well-known algorithms and their analyses to obtain a substantial decrease in their complexity.

11300220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300220.value: We defined a functional (i.e., defined in terms of function values as opposed to being defined in terms of coefficients) norm on spaces of multivariable polynomials. We redefined various condition numbers replacing the Bombieri-Weyl norm occurring in these condition numbers by this functional norm. The advantage of the functional norm is a considerably smaller expectation (when the space of polynomials is endowed with a normal distribution). A clear drawback is the absence of an efficient algorithm to compute it. In spite of this drawback, we managed to show improved complexity bounds for three different algorithms: grid algorithms to compute homology groups of semialgebraic sets, the Plantinga-Vegter algorithm, and the linear homotopy algorithm to compute zeros of complex polynomial system.

11300220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300220.value: Our results open possible research in two directions: the search for an efficient algorithm to approximate the functional norm, and the search for new algorithmic problems whose analysis can be improved by using these norms.

11300220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300220.value: The analysis of algorithms of a certain kind (usually called "numerical") relies on a quantity (the condition number) associated to the data at hand. To evaluate the efficiency of these algorithms a common approach passes through estimating the value of this condition number on a typical data (probability theory helps to give substance to this typicality). In this project we improved estimates for the efficiency of three known algorithms via a sharpening of their respective condition numbers.
