11300320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300320.value: 近紅外(NIR)響應的光療藥物因為其巨大的潛力被廣泛關注，且可廣泛用於光熱(PTT)和光動力治療(PDT)。近紅外光療的主要原理是光激發材料誘導局部熱或是細胞毒性活性氧從而殺死癌細胞。儘管當前的光熱和光動力治療已經被證明取得了長足的進步，但是光療治療效應往往因為深部組織的穿透性和光照安全性問題被大打折扣，因此極大地限制了它們進一步應用。 迄今為止，開發具有強近紅外吸收和高光轉換效率的光療藥物是研究熱點，且相關研究已經發表在一些重要出版物(Nature Photonics. 2014, 8, 455, Nature comm. 2019, 10, 767; Nature comm. 2019, 10, 1192; Nature comm. 2019, 10, 2206)。雖然吸收峰超過800 nm 的PPT試劑已經被大量報道，但吸收峰超過800 nm的PDT試劑鮮有開發。因此，高性能近紅外 PTT/PDT試劑依然十分稀缺，且有待進一步發展。更重要的是，製備這些材料通常需要複雜的合成過程。到目前為止，市面上只有少數幾種試劑在~ 800 nm 的激光激發下具有良好的性能，然而沒有一種試劑可以在超過1000 nm 的長波長下表現出PDT潛能。 在我們的初步研究中，項目負責人團隊已經利用商業化的電子供體(D)和電子受體(A)分子製備了一種新型的水分散性有機電荷轉移複合納米顆粒有機納米顆粒，其光響應波長可達1500 nm。本項目中，我們將對這類有機電荷轉移複合納米顆粒體系進行系統的研究，並探索具有PTT/ PDT性能的CTC納米顆粒的基本設計規則用於篩選D和A分子。本項目取得的結果將為優化商用D和A分子組合提供依據，使其相應的有機電荷轉移複合納米顆粒的吸收峰在可見光到近紅外區域自由可調。進一步地，我們將考察這些有機電荷轉移複合納米顆粒在細胞水平的PTT/PDT性能和生物安全性，並篩選合適的體系進行活體動物的腫瘤治療研究與安全性評估。

11300320.label: Realisation of objectives
11300320.value: The figures in this section were additionally appended. This project aims to utilize commercially available donor (D) and acceptor (A) molecules to develop charge-transfer complex nanoparticles (CTC NPs) with long-wavelength absorption for applications in near-infrared (NIR) photothermal therapy (PTT) and photodynamic therapy (PDT). A series of D and A molecules have been carefully selected, leading to the successful preparation of several CTC NPs exhibiting long-wavelength absorption ranging from 700 nm to 1300 nm (Figure 1). These CTC NPs have undergone comprehensive characterization of their photophysical properties, resulting in the formulation of guidelines for preparing CTC NPs with diverse absorption ranges. Furthermore, these selected CTC NPs have demonstrated satisfactory performance in vitro and in vivo by effectively enabling photodynamic or photothermal therapy on cancer cells or bacteria under laser irradiation at wavelengths of 808 nm and 1064 nm. All objectives have been successfully accomplished. Additionally, the application potential of CTC materials has been extended beyond biomedical fields into information security and actuator applications. Details are presented below: 1. A D-A type small molecule (TTP) with efficient intermolecular charge transfer (ICT) was designed for cancer phototheranostics (Figure 2a). The TTP NPs’ size was characterized to be approximately 33 nm (Figure 2b). Its NPs exhibited an apparent red shift in absorption and emission, indicating its CT properties (Figure 2c). Under 808 nm laser irradiation, TTP NPs can efficiently eradicate mice tumors through their PDT and PTT effect (Figure 2d). (Published in Adv. Funct. Mater. 2024, 34, 2407317) 2. A twisted D-A type BT6 small molecule was designed (Figure 2e). The the average diameter of BT6 NPs was approximately 40 nm (Figure 2f). The absorption and emission spectra of NPs exhibited a significant red shift towards the NIR-I and NIR-II regions, respectively, implying its obvious CT effect (Figure 2g). Crystallographic analysis demonstrated a slipping molecular packing in the BT6 single crystal, indicating its CT J-aggregates characteristics (Figure 2h). Under irradiation with an 808 nm laser, the BT6 NPs exhibited both thermal effect generation and ROS production capabilities (Figure 2i and j), which can guarantee high-performance cancer therapy. Furthermore, the NIR-II fluorescence imaging (FLI) using BT6 NPs enabled clear visualization of whole-body blood vessels in mice (Figure 2k). (Published in Adv. Mater. 2023, 35, 2211632) 3. Through combining PO (D) and CPM (A), another intramolecular CT compound NSM2 was prepared for PTT applications (Figure 3a). The NSM2 NPs showed a uniform size distribution at around 55 nm (Figure 3b). As shown in Figure 3c, the NPs have a strong absorption at 600-1000 nm region. The photothermal performance was illustrated using 808 nm laser (Figure 3d). (Published in Adv. Mater. 2021, 33, 2102799) 4. By using BTA donor and BTMM acceptor, we also prepared an intramolecular CT compound BthB for PTT and PDT (Figure 3e). The prepared NPs has a strong absorption between 600-900 nm (Figure 3f). Under 808 nm laser excitation, the NPs showed remarkable ROS generation, confirming its photodynamic effect (Figure 3g). As shown in Figure 3h, the NPs showed negligible dark toxicity to cell and excellent killing effect under laser irradiation. (Published in Nanoscale 2021, 13, 8012) 5. We have extended the application range of CTC materials to the field of information security. By doping TTF as donor and TCNB as acceptor into a poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) polymer matrix, a CTC film (named as TBC) was formed as an optical filter (CTC-F) (Figure 4a). Via regulation of the intermolecular interaction between TTF and TCNB in the polymer network, the CTC-F shows tunable absorption from the visible to the NIR region with a relatively high penetration of NIR radiation (~80%, Figure 4b). The CTC-F can successfully highlight NIR information hidden in a complex environment and allows reading of NIR security images for advanced anti-counterfeiting. By fitting the CTC-F into a digital camera (Figure 4c), NIR encoded information that cannot be observed with naked eye can be revealed by the modified camera (Figure 4d) with good resolution, and thus provide a convenient tool for different security applications. (Published in Adv. Mater. 2022, 34, 2204749) 6. The CTC materials have also been utilized as an actuator. A liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) film was fabricated by incorporating CTC materials (donor: DBTTF, acceptor: TCNB) into the LC polymer matrix (Figure 4e). Upon exposure to NIR light, the green-colored polymer film undergoes contraction. The film exhibits fully reversible actuation over at least five irradiation cycles, demonstrating the photothermal stability of the actuator. (Published in J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2023, 145, 19347) 7. PT and IC were used as the acceptor and donor to prepare H-CTC NPs stabilized by hydrogen bonding (Figure 5a). DFT calculations showed that the energy gap of the donor and acceptor decreased to 1.45 eV after forming NPs (Figure 5b). The aqueous dispersion of NPs exhibited a color change to aquamarine blue, with a significantly red-shifted absorption peak at approximately 720 nm (Figure 5c). ESR spectra indicated that the aqueous dispersion of NPs displayed a typical open-shell radical feature (Figure 5d). Their photothermal stability was demonstrated through negligible changes in performance during ten cycles of laser irradiation followed by natural cooling to room temperature (Figure 5e). The photothermal anticancer performance of NPs was further evaluated on the MCF-7 cancer cell line, and the results demonstrated that H-CTC NPs efficiently killed cancer cells under 808 nm laser irradiation (Figure 5f). Additionally, tumor-bearing mice experiments were conducted, showing that a single-dose photothermal treatment with H-CTC NPs inhibited tumor growth (Figure 5g). (Manuscript submitted to Matter for peer review) 8. A A-D-A-D-A configured oligomer, with efficient ICT, has been developed for PTT (Figure 5h). As shown in Figure 5i, the absorption of the CN molecule remained unchanged while that of the 2F molecule exhibited a red shift after forming nanoparticles, indicating its efficient intermolecular CT. The optimized dimer of 2F demonstrated close intermolecular packing, promoting efficient CT between donor and acceptor within each unit (Figure 5j). Under 808 nm laser illumination, the 2F NPs can produce heat (Figure 5k) and resulted in effective anticancer effects on the 4T1 cancer cell line (Figure 5l). Finally, successful evaluation and confirmation of in vivo photothermal anticancer performance were achieved (Figure 5m). (Manuscript submitted to Adv. Funct. Mater. for peer review) 9. PXZ and TCNQ were chosen as the donor and acceptor to prepare CTC NPs (Figure 6a). The orange-colored PT NPs exhibited a red-shifted absorption in the NIR-II range, making them suitable for excitation by a 1064 nm laser (Figure 6b). ESR spectra indicated that the dispersion of PT NPs displayed typical open-shell radical characteristics (Figure 6c). Under irradiation from a 1064 nm laser, the NPs could raise the temperature to 65 °C, demonstrating their excellent photothermal performance (Figure 6d). The colony-forming units of viable methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in treated biofilms were visually depicted in Figure 6e. Furthermore, combining NIR-II laser with PT NPs significantly kill bacteria by up to approximately 4.3 log (~99.995%) (Figure 6f). Under laser irradiation, the temperature at the wound sites increased to around 45 °C for killing MRSA bacteria (Figure 6g). Moreover, after treatment, complete healing of mice wounds was observed after two weeks compared to obvious wound infections still present in the group without laser treatment. (Manuscript under preparation)

11300320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300320.value: This project on developing charge-transfer complex nanoparticles for photodynamic therapy (PDT) and photothermal therapy (PTT) shows significant promise for further advancement. The potential for further development lies in several key areas: 1) Enhanced selectivity and efficacy: future research can focus on improving the targeting capabilities of these nanoparticles, ensuring they selectively accumulate in cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue. This can be achieved by modifying the surface properties of the nanoparticles or by attaching specific ligands that bind to cancer cell markers. 2) In vivo testing and clinical trials: To transition from the lab to clinical use, comprehensive in vivo studies are necessary to evaluate the safety, biodistribution, and therapeutic efficacy of the CTC nanoparticles. This will involve animal models and, eventually, human clinical trials. 3) Scalability and production: developing scalable and cost-effective methods for synthesizing these CTC nanoparticles will be crucial for their widespread application. Research can investigate large-scale production techniques while maintaining the quality and consistency of nanoparticles. 4) Regulatory approval and commercialization: preparing for regulatory approval involves ensuring the nanoparticles meet all safety and efficacy standards set by health authorities. This process will require extensive documentation and proof of the nanoparticles' benefits. Proposed course of action: 1. Conduct targeted in vivo studies to gather more data on the nanoparticles’ behaviors in living organisms. 2. Develop scalable production methods to facilitate widespread use. 3. Engage with regulatory bodies early to ensure compliance and streamline the approval process. 4. Collaborate with industry partners to transition from research to commercial application, ensuring the innovative nanoparticles reach patients in need. This course of action will drive CTC NPs toward real-world application and ultimately improve cancer treatment options.

11300320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300320.value: In this project, we have successfully developed organic nanoparticles that help in cancer treatment. These nanoparticles can be easily created using readily available chemicals and can be tailored to absorb light in the near-infrared-I (NIR-I) and near-infrared-II (NIR-II) ranges. This method is advantageous compared to the commonly used organic synthesis approach for developing near infrared materials, particularly in simplicity, time and cost spent. The significance of this work lies in its potential to improve two types of cancer therapies: Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) and Photothermal Therapy (PTT). PDT uses light to activate a drug that kills cancer cells, while PTT uses light to produce heat and destroy cancer cells. The developed nanoparticles can be used in both treatments, offering a dual approach to combat cancer. The value of this research is substantial because it provides a straightforward and efficient method to produce nanoparticles that work effectively in near-infrared light (NIR-I and NIR-II). This could lead to more effective and less invasive cancer treatments, ultimately benefiting patients by reducing side effects and improving treatment outcomes.

11300420.label: Realisation of objectives
11300420.value: 1. We justified the incompressible limit of compressible viscoelastic systems with vanishing shear viscosity in dimension three and two. The incompressible limit is characterized by the large volume viscosity. This kind of incompressible limit is different from the classical one by Mach number. In the limit, the dispersive effect of pressure waves disappears and the global convergence to the limit system around an equilibrium is justified with the help of vector fields. 2. We justified the vanishing shear viscosity limit and incompressible limit of two dimensional compressible dissipative elastodynamics systems near the equilibrium. The large value of the volume viscosity forces the limit system to be incompressible, and the vanishing shear viscosity indicates that the limit system is inviscid. Due to the weaker dispersive estimate in low dimension, the two-dimensional case is much harder to justify. 3. We concern the dynamical properties of topological defects in two dimensional flows of liquid crystals modeled by the Ginzburg-Landau approximations. It is proved that the fluid is transported by a nonlocal (an averaged) velocity and is coupled with effects of the elastic stress. The defects move along the trajectories of the flow associated with an averaged velocity. 4. We establish the global-in-time wellposedness and asymptotic behavior of solutions to compressible viscoelasticity when the background is an affine solution in $H^2$ framework. Different from the constant background, the affine solution induces a linear system with variable coefficients. As a conference, a new flux is introduced to deal with the global estimate by handling the variable coefficients. 5. We study three dimensional compressible viscoelastic flows with zero shear viscosity and a general class of pressure waves. We deal with the compressible components and the incompressible components seperately. We introduce "good unknowns" to deal with the difficulty of the lack of dissipation for incompressible components.

11300520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300520.value: Random matrices are matrices whose entries are random variables. They have many applications in various areas of mathematics, physics and engineering, such as number theory, combinatorics, statistics, string theory, condense matter physics, classical and quantum optics, complex networks, wireless communications, etc.. In random matrix theory, one of statistical quantities of basic interests is the probability that there are certain number of eigenvalues in a given interval. When the number is zero, this is the well-known gap probability. These probabilities give us important information about the spacing of eigenvalues. In this project, we plan to study gap probabilities for various matrix models on different intervals. We will derive the large gap asymptotics of the probability, that is, the asymptotic expansion when the width of the given interval tends to infinity. We will also investigate the transition properties when certain parameter changes together with the width of the gap. 隨機矩陣是矩陣元素為隨機變量的矩陣。它們在數學，物理，工程的許多領域都有著眾多應用；例如，數論，組合學，統計學，弦論，凝聚態物理，經典與量子光學，複雜網絡，無線電通訊，等等。在隨機矩陣理論研究中，人們感興趣的一個基本問題是：在特定區間中有給定數量特徵值的概率。當特徵值的數量為零時，此概率即為著名的間隙概率。這些概率包含著隨機矩陣特徵值分佈的重要信息。 在本項目中，我們計畫研究多種矩陣模型在不同區間上的間隙概率。我們會推導此概率的大間隙漸進性質；即當區間長度趨於無窮大時，此概率的漸進展開式。我們也會研究當特定參數變化時，此概率漸進展開的相變性質。

11300520.label: Realisation of objectives
11300520.value: The primary objective of this project is to explore the gap probabilities associated with various kernels in random matrix theory and models within determinantal point processes. Our first focus is a comprehensive investigation of the gap probability related to the Pearcey kernel, including both the undeformed and deformed cases. Given the integrable nature of the Pearcey kernel, our approach involves establishing a Riemann-Hilbert problem associated with the relevant Fredholm determinant. This process is facilitated through the application of the Deift-Its-Zhou lemma. As the Pearcey kernel holds an explicit expression in terms of a Riemann-Hilbert problem, we derive a third Riemann-Hilbert problem by combining the aforementioned ones, offering a more direct link to the logarithmic derivative of the Fredholm determinant. Based on the third Riemann-Hilbert problem, we explore the associated Lax pair. Consequently, we construct an integral representation of the Pearcey determinant, involving the Hamiltonian associated with a family of special solutions to a system of nonlinear differential equations. This outcome holds significance within this field of study as it can be regarded as a generalization of the renowned Tracy-Widom formula. This expression establishes an important and crucial connection with integrable systems, enhancing our understanding of this research domain. We would like to emphasize that the integral representation remains consistent across both deformed and undeformed scenarios, with identical algebraic formulations for the Hamiltonians in both cases. The key disparity lies in the asymptotic behavior of the Hamiltonian. Moreover, by employing the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method, we derive the large gap asymptotics of the gap probability. Our asymptotic analyses reveal a notable contrast between the undeformed and deformed cases, manifesting in super-exponential and exponential decay regions when the gap becomes large. For the nondeformed case, there is still an undetermined constant in the asymptotic expansion. For the deformed case, although an additional deforming constant is introduced, we make use of the Hamiltonian structure and establish a crucial differential identity with respect to the deforming parameter. In this way, we are able to derive the constant term in the asymptotic expansion explicitly. Through these findings, we have successfully realized the first primary objective of this project. Next, we explore gap probabilities associated with the confluent hypergeometric kernel and the hard edge Pearcey kernel. The confluent hypergeometric kernel features prominently in describing a universality class marked by a Fisher-Hartwig type singularity appearing the bulk of the limiting spectrum. The gap probability corresponding to this kernel extends that associated with the classical sine kernel. The integral representation involves the Hamiltonian of a coupled Painleve V system. 11300520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300520.value: The Pearcey process represents one canonical universality class in random matrix theory and determinantal point processes. A recent classification theorem concerning the singularities of the solution to the underlying Dyson equation also shows that the Pearcey process represents the third and last universal statistics arising from the generalization of Wigner matrices. Furthermore, connections have been established between Pearcey statistics and non-intersecting Brownian motions at critical times, as well as a combinatorial model based on random partitions. In this project, we deepen our understanding about the Pearcey process by investigating its large gap asymptotics across both undeformed and deformed scenarios. Our asymptotic findings provide substantial support for the Forrester-Chen-Eriksen-Tracy conjecture within this research field. Additionally, the asymptotic results for the deformed distribution hint at a modified interpretation of the conjecture. Next, we move to Fredholm determinants associated with the confluent hypergeometric kernel and the hard edge Pearcey kernel. Each of these kernels represents a significant universality class, generalizing the classical sine kernel in the bulk and the Bessel kernel at the hard edge. Employing the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, we successfully derive the large gap asymptotics, establish central limit theorems, and validate a global rigidity upper bound for the maximum deviation for the respective point processes. Our comprehensive and systematic asymptotic analysis of Fredholm determinants not only enriches the existing literature with new asymptotic expansions, but also enhances our understanding of the transition properties between deformed and non-deformed distributions. Alongside our asymptotic study, we investigate a total integral for a special solution of the second equation within the Painleve I hierarchy. The outcome, along with the methodology employed, guides us towards determining the celebrated constant term in the large gap asymptotic expansion, which remains undisclosed in numerous instances. The key observation holds the potential to make a substantial breakthrough within this specific realm of research.

11300520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300520.value: In the study of asymptotics of gap probabilities, a significant and challenging task involves is the determination of the constant term in the asymptotic expansion. Despite one can get a full asymptotic expansion for the logarithmic derivatives of the Fredholm determinants, the difficulty lies on the fact that the integration of the highly transcendental function is almost impossible by using the current methods. However, this constant attracts a lot of research interests for the following two primary reasons: 1. Together with other terms in the asymptotic expansion, it explicitly quantifies the probability when the gap is large. 2. It interacts with interesting special functions such as the Riemann Zeta function or the Barnes G-function, and exhibiting universal characteristics. Based on our systematic asymptotic analysis completed in the current project, we are poised at the brink of a breakthrough in developing existing methodologies and proposing a comprehensive approach to obtain the constants across diverse situations. This endeavor involves a new choice of integration path, and some delicate uniform asymptotic analysis with one or more variables become large. We aim to address this challenge in an upcoming project.

11300520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300520.value: Random matrices are matrices whose entries are random variables. They find applications in diverse fields spanning from pure mathematics to engineering disciplines, such as number theory, combinatorics, statistics, complex networks, wireless communications, etc.. Within these contexts, one of the most important problems is to understand the distribution of eigenvalue spacing when the matrix size is large. In this project, we studied gap probabilities associated with various kernels with the aid of the Fredholm determinants. Our investigation not only yield explicit integral expressions for these probabilities but also give crucial information about their large deviation properties, in particular the large gap asymptotics. We explore several typical kernels, which represent different universality classes in random matrix theory. Our findings in the project have provided a systematic understanding of the large gap asymptotics within unitary ensembles and their transition behaviors in various situations. In addition, our results offer valuable insights into orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, which builds a solid foundation for the future study in this research area.

11300720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11300720.value: 拉製微結構光纖的穩定性

11300720.label: Project Objectives
11300720.value: We will start with the full three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation for a thread with multiple holes and develop a technique that uses asymptotic techniques based on the slenderness of the thread to derive a model that will decouple the along-thread mechanics from the transverse flow. This model will be appropriate for drawing, extrusion flows and gravitational extension. In the case of drawing, we will obtain the steady-state solution to this problem for various different types of physically relevant boundary conditions. This involves solving a Stokes flow problem in two dimensions for the transverse flow. In order to achieve this we will develop a spectral code that will be very robust in dealing with the arbitrary shapes that we need to consider. We will also obtain some analytical and pseudo-analytical solutions to the transverse flow problem that will allow us to obtain significant insight into the problem. These include the simple case of an axisymmetric tube with a single hole and more complicated cases that can be dealt with using complex variable techniques. These solutions will also allow us to perform careful tests on our spectral code. We will then go on to study the linear stability of the steady state by solving for the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the appropriate boundary value problem. We will first examine how the classical isothermal draw resonance threshold is affected by the presence of a single internal hole. We will explore the effects of the hole by considering an aperture with a circular outer boundary and a circular hole. We will then vary the radius and location of the hole. By examining the eigenfunctions and comparing them with the eigenfunctions for a solid thread, we will attempt to understand the role of the hole in modifying the stability characteristics. We will extend this analysis to multiple holes and determine how the stability varies according to the sizes and locations of the holes. In order to generate more elaborate patterns of holes in the final fibre, industrial processes often pressurise the holes during the drawing process. We will therefore develop the theory under which the stability of the fibres with pressurised holes can be determined and carefully examine the effects on single and multiple holes. Of particular interest are cases in which different holes are subjected to different pressurisation. Thermal effects are crucial in almost all applications and we will therefore extensively study their effects. In particular, we will determine how these effects will modify the stability properties in the presence of holes. In some industrial processes, complex polymers are used to produce structured fibres. These can have a variety of complicated rheological properties. In order to investigate these non-Newtonian effects, we will consider how different constitutive laws (e.g. shear thinning and visco-elasticity) affect the stability properties.

11300720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300720.value: In recent years, there has been an enormous increase in the need for novel optical fibres with highly specialised optical properties. Achieving such properties generally requires that the fibres are fabricated with numerous cylindrical air holes with irregular shapes arranged in complicated patterns. The fibres typically have diameter of a few hundred micrometers and can have lengths of more than a kilometre. However, they are drawn from a preform that is a few centimetres in diameter. This implies that the fibres leaving a drawing device must exit with a speed of up to tens of thousands times faster than the preform is fed into the device. During the drawing process, the shapes and locations of the air holes evolve under the influence of surface tension. Therefore, one of the major challenges in the fabrication of optical fibres is to design a preform with an appropriate pattern of holes such that the elongated fibre when it exits the device has required shape with the required pattern of holes. An additional complication to this process is the fact that significant heating is needed to ensure that the viscosity of the glass is sufficiently low that drawing can be achieved with moderate stretching forces. The glass used in optical fibres has the property that its viscosity varies by many orders of magnitude for the temperature ranges that are typically used. In light of all these complications (complicated evolving free boundaries, complicated coupling between the thermal and momentum equations, and large viscosity contrasts), this clearly represents an extremely challenging problem. However, it is made even more challenging by the fact that the fabrication process is highly prone to instabilities that lead to oscillations in the fibre radius. Fibres with such oscillations will certainly not have the required optical properties and so suppressing such instabilities is crucial. There are a number of further complications in the drawing process. These include surface tensions that can depend on the temperature and hence give rise to Marangoni-type effects, pressurisation of the internal holes that is often used to generate the required hole patterns and Non-Newtonian rheology that is appropriate when using polymer materials. The goal of this proposal is to understand how the presence of complicated hole patterns, temperature, internal pressure and non-Newtonian rheology affects the instabilities that occur in fibre drawing. 近年來，對具有高度專業化的光學特性的新型光纖的需求已大大增加。為了獲得這樣的性能，通常要求纖維製造成具有許多圓柱形的氣孔，這些氣孔具有以復雜的圖案佈置的不規則形狀。纖維的直徑通常為幾百微米，並且長度可以超過一公里。但是，它們是從直徑為幾厘米的預成型坯中拉製而成的。這意味著離開拉絲裝置的纖維必須以比將預成型坯進給到裝置中的速度快幾萬倍的速度退出。在拉伸過程中，氣孔的形狀和位置會在表面張力的影響下發生變化。因此，光纖製造中的主要挑戰之一是設計具有適當孔圖案的預成型件，以使得細長纖維在其離開裝置時具有具有所需孔圖案的所需形狀。該方法的另一個複雜之處是，需要大量加熱以確保玻璃的粘度足夠低，從而可以在中等拉伸力下進行拉伸。光纖中使用的玻璃具有以下特性：在通常使用的溫度範圍內，其粘度變化許多數量級。鑑於所有這些複雜性（複雜的自由邊界演變，熱和動量方程之間的複雜耦合以及較大的粘度對比），這顯然是一個極具挑戰性的問題。但是，由於製造過程極容易產生導致光纖半徑振蕩的不穩定性，這使挑戰變得更大。具有這種振蕩的光纖肯定不會具有所需的光學特性，因此抑制這種不穩定性至關重要。在繪製過程中還有許多其他復雜情況。其中包括可能取決於溫度並因此產生Marangoni型效應的表面張力，通常用於生成所需孔圖案的內部孔的加壓以及使用聚合物材料時合適的非牛頓流變學。該建議的目的是了解複雜的孔型，溫度，內部壓力和非牛頓流變學的存在如何影響纖維拉伸中的不穩定性。

11300720.label: Realisation of objectives
11300720.value: We explored the stability of drawing a long, thin viscous thread that incorporated an arbitrary number of internal holes of various shapes, influenced by axial drawing, inertia, and surface tension. To address this complex problem, we employed asymptotic techniques to derive a formulation of the equations of motion that was particularly well-suited for stability analysis, thus achieving our first objective of simplifying the mathematical framework despite the intricate boundary geometries involved. We proceeded to determine explicit asymptotic solutions for steady states under two distinct conditions: first, when surface tension dominated and inertia was negligible, and second, when inertia was significant. In both scenarios, we successfully identified the emergence of complex boundary layer structures, thereby fulfilling our goal of understanding the dynamics under different physical regimes. Our linear stability analysis revealed that the presence of an axisymmetric hole destabilized the flow for finite capillary numbers, thereby answering an important question that had been previously raised in the literature. This analysis demonstrated not only the impact of geometrical features on stability but also allowed us to extend our findings to more generalized configurations. By considering arbitrary hole structures and non-axisymmetric shapes, we established that any configuration with holes was inherently less stable than a solid axisymmetric thread, thus achieving our objective of broadening the scope of our analysis. Additionally, we derived a closed-form expression that delineated the unconditional instability boundary for solid axisymmetric threads, highlighting conditions under which the thread became unstable for all draw ratios. This was crucial in providing a comprehensive understanding of stability limits. Finally, we investigated how the specific characteristics of the microstructure affected stability. Our analysis revealed that these effects manifested through a single function incorporated into the stability problem, illustrating that, surprisingly, the detailed microstructural variations had a limited impact on overall stability. This insight was instrumental in achieving our objective of clarifying the relationship between microstructure and stability in the drawing process. We also addressed the significant role of temperature-dependent viscosity in the fabrication of optical fibres, particularly how heat transfer influences the deformation of fibre geometry. Previous models of fibre drawing processes have either assumed isothermal conditions or focused on advective heat transfer while neglecting conduction. Although the neglect of conduction can be valid in the rapid process of drawing a preform into a fibre, we recognised the importance of heat conduction in the slower process of extruding a fibre preform. To fulfill our objectives, we derived and solved a coupled heat and fluid flow model that incorporates heat conduction within the context of pulled extrusion. We acknowledged the challenges posed by the dramatic variation of viscosity with temperature, which complicates the solution of this problem using standard numerical techniques. Consequently, we developed a novel finite-difference numerical solution method that proved highly robust. This method enabled us to demonstrate that heat conduction significantly impacts the size of internal holes at the exit of the device, revealing crucial implications for the optical fibre manufacturing process. Through this work, we advanced the understanding of heat transfer dynamics in fibre drawing and established a more comprehensive model that accounts for the complexities of heat conduction in the extrusion process.

11300720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300720.value: We employed asymptotic techniques to derive a formulation of the equations of motion conducive to stability analysis, simplifying the complex mathematical framework. This allowed us to investigate the stability of drawing a long, thin viscous thread with various internal holes, influenced by axial drawing, inertia, and surface tension. We obtained explicit asymptotic solutions for steady states under two conditions: one where surface tension dominated and inertia was negligible, and another where inertia was significant. In both cases, we identified complex boundary layer structures. Our linear stability analysis demonstrated that the presence of an axisymmetric hole destabilised the flow for finite capillary numbers. This addressed a long-standing question in the literature. We established that any configuration with holes was inherently less stable than a solid axisymmetric thread. Additionally, we derived a closed-form expression delineating the unconditional instability boundary for solid threads. Finally, our findings showed that microstructural variations had a limited impact on overall stability, clarifying the relationship between microstructure and stability in the drawing process. This work was published in Journal of Fluid Mechanics. We also studied the critical influence of temperature-dependent viscosity on the fabrication of optical fibres, specifically highlighting the role of heat transfer in fibre deformation. We formulated and solved a coupled heat and fluid flow model that incorporates heat conduction, thereby addressing limitations in existing models that typically assume isothermal conditions or neglect conduction in favour of advective heat transfer mechanisms. Our results demonstrated that heat conduction significantly influences the size of internal holes at the exit of the extrusion device, with substantial implications for the optical fibre manufacturing process. To address the complexities arising from the pronounced viscosity variations with temperature, we developed a robust finite-difference numerical solution method. This method effectively captures the interplay between heat transfer and fluid dynamics. Overall, this work advances the understanding of heat transfer phenomena in fibre drawing and contributes to improved modelling of the extrusion process, ultimately enhancing the quality of the resulting optical fibres. This work was published in Physics of Fluids.

11300720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300720.value: The equations that we developed to determine the stability of microstructured threads represents an important breakthrough since it does not require complicated perturbation analysis of the locations of the holes that compose the microstructure. Therefore, similar techniques can be readily applied to similar flows in which heating is important. Equations of this type can also be used when the holes in the microstructure are pressurised. The novel finite-difference method that we developed is quite general and is easy to implement and hence may be used in future work involving large viscosity contrasts. In particular, the study of the stability of such flows will be accessible via the use of this method.

11300720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300720.value: We have determined how the presence of holes in a long, thin thread made of a liquid material affects the stability of a process in which the thread is stretched. We used asymptotic techniques to fully understand the effects of inertia and surface tension. We found explicit solutions for two situations: one where surface tension was strong and inertia was weak, and another where inertia was strong and surface tension weak. In both cases, we showed that complicated boundary layer structures could arise. Our analysis showed that having a holes in the thread made the stretching process less stable than a solid thread. We also showed that the details of the thread's structure didn’t significantly affect its overall stability, helping us understand how these features relate to the drawing process. Our findings also revealed the way in which heat conduction along the axis of fibres significantly affects the internal hole structure at the exit of the device. This has important implications for the optical fibre manufacturing process. Our work enhances the understanding of heat transfer dynamics in fibre drawing and contributes to more accurate modelling of the extrusion process, ultimately improving the quality of manufactured optical fibres.

11300820.label: Project Objectives
11300820.value: Achieve controllable and reversible phase transition and lattice direction switching in CVD grown anisotropic 2D TMDs and TMD alloys, via designed structure/composition and electrical/optical/mechanical control strategies. Understand the mechanisms of the nucleation and phase/lattice transition dynamics of the two-dimensional phases down to the atomic scale. Optimize the 2D materials and the phase/lattice control strategies to achieve a complete transition/switching (>95% conversion) and fast response for device applications with memory functions.

11300820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300820.value: The polymorphism (spanning from semiconductive to metallic phases) in the two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) has been found effective in modulating the electrical and optical properties, which has great potential for future smart electronic applications especially for memory devices. There have been a few strategies developed for the phase control, e.g., the electronic doping (either by voltage or exotic donor/acceptor), atomic doping, strains, defects, etc. However, owing to the high surface ratio and instability nature of the 2D materials, to achieve a reversible, complete and atomically-precise phase transition in monolayer 2D TMDs is challenging. It is also necessary to explore more polymorphic 2D materials/structures with more facile phase transition control, in particular, with anisotropic crystal lattices such as (tetragonal) ReS2 or MoTe2 (attached Figure 1a). The anisotropic lattices in distorted tetragonal phases (such as ReS2 and MoTe2) provide one more degree of freedom in the lattice direction switching (attached Figure 1b), e.g., under certain strain conditions, providing controllable anisotropic electrical and optical properties along different lattice directions, promising for the novel sensor applications and changeable electronic/optoelectronic devices/circuits, etc. Therefore, in this project we plan to systematically study the phase transition and lattice switching mechanisms in these 2D anisotropic TMDs and TMD alloys. We will use the optical, mechanical, electrical approaches to control and investigate the phase transition/lattice switching mechanisms down to the atomic scale. The in situ scanning probe microscopy (atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive-AFM (CAFM), Kelvin force microscopy (KFM)), in situ polarized Raman/PL spectroscopy and in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) will be mainly employed to search for the optimized 2D TMD structures/compositions and the best external control strategies which can achieve reversible, facile and quick phase transition/lattice switching. The phase transition atomic mechanisms related to the nucleation of secondary phases/lattice directions, the structures of the phase boundaries or grain boundaries, and the changes in electrical/optical properties after transitions will be investigated in detail, to support the phase control development. Furthermore, the optimized approaches will be applied in applications such as electronic devices with memory functions. 已發現二維過渡金屬硫化物（TMD）中的多態性（從半導體相到金屬相）有效地調節了電學和光學性能，這對於未來的智能電子應用（尤其是存儲設備）具有巨大的潛力。已經開發出一些用於相位控制的策略，例如電子摻雜（通過電壓或外來的施主/受主），原子摻雜，應變，缺陷等。但是，由於二维材料的高表面比率和不穩定性，在單層二维 TMD中實現可逆，完全和原子精確的相變是具有挑戰性的。還需要探索更多的多態二维材料具有更容易的相變控制的材料/結構，尤其是具有各向異性的晶格，例如（四方）ReS2或MoTe2。畸變四方相（例如ReS2和MoTe2）中的各向異性晶格（例如，在某些應變條件下）在晶格方向切換中提供了另一種自由度，可沿不同晶格方向提供可控的各向異性電和光學特性，對於新穎的傳感器應用和可變的電子/光電設備/電路等提供了希望。因此，在這個項目中，我們計劃系統地研究這些2D各向異性TMD和TMD合金中的相變和晶格轉換機理。我們將使用光學，機械，電氣方法來控制和研究低至原子級的相變/晶格切換機制。原位掃描探針顯微鏡（原子力顯微鏡（AFM），導電原子力顯微鏡（CAFM），開爾文力顯微鏡（KFM）），原位偏振拉曼/ PL光譜和原位透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）將主要用於尋找最佳的二维TMD結構/組成和最佳的外部控制策略，這些策略可以實現可逆，便捷和快速的相變/晶格切換。我们將詳細研究與次級相/晶格方向成核，相界或晶界的結構以及相變後電/光學性質的變化有關的相變原子機理，以支持相控的發展。此外，優化的方法將應用於具有存儲功能的電子設備等應用中。

11300820.label: Realisation of objectives
11300820.value: We have successfully achieved all the objectives of this project. In this project, we have prepared all the ultraclean 2D materials via the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and our in-house developed ice-transfer technique (Advanced Materials 2023a,b, Chem Mater 2021). We have also observed some abnormal lattice switching in 2D ReS2, We can trigger the phase transition in 2D ReS2 via electron beam irradiaiton(Advanced Science 2022). Regarding objective 1: To date, we have been able to control the phase transition of ReS2 (Adv Funct Mater 2021, Advanced Science 2022) and In2Se3 (Science Advances 2022, Nature Nanotechnology 2023) through the electrical, optical, electron beam and mechanical strategies. Regarding objective 2: We have been able to understand the phase transition mechanisms, which are related to the strain, defects, temperature, through in situ TEM and AFM experiments (Chemical Review 2023, Accounts of Chem Res 2021, Accounts of Mater Res 2021, Commun Mater 2021). Regarding objective 3: We have been able to apply the complete and reversible phase transition for the memory transitor device applications (Nature Nanotechnology 2023). In summary, all the objectives have been successfully achieved.

11300820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300820.value: Some major findings are listed below: 1. We have achieved the reversible phase control of 2D ReS2 by introducing oxygen groups on the vdW surfaces, which is facilitated by simple optical methods. Such optical direct-writing and rewritable capability via solvent/contaminant-free approach for chemical doping are compelling (Adv Funct Mater, 2021, 31, 2009166). 2. We have shown in 2D ReS2, the martensite-like domain structures can form via a diffusionless lattice transformation, involving small lattice deformations. The strain-induced lattice reconstructions are rationalized and possibly lead to ferroelastic effects. (Commun Mater, 2021, 2, 87) 3. We have summarize our previous works on the phase control, 2D material functionalization and defect engineering in three review works (Acc Mater Res, 2021, 2, 863, Acc Chem Res, 2021, 54, 4191, Chemical Review 2023, 123, 18, 10990). 4. We have proved that the focused electron beam is capable of triggering the phase transition from the semiconducting T’’ phase to metallic T’ and T phases in 2D rhenium disulfide (ReS2) and rhenium diselenide (ReSe2) monolayers, rendering ultra-precise phase patterning technique even in sub-nanometer scale is found. This patterning method exhibits great potential in ultra-precise electron beam lithography as a scalable top-down manufacturing method for future atomic-scale devices (Advanced Science, 2022, 9(23), 2200702). 5. We have triggered reversible phase transition in 2D In2Se3 with reversible AFE and out-of-plane FE phase transition in 2D In2Se3 by delicate strain control inside a transmission electron microscope. In addition, the polarizations in 2D FE In2Se3 can also be manipulated in situ at the nanometer-sized contacts, rendering remarkable memristive behavior. (Science Advances, 2022, 8, 42, abo0773) 6. We have further achieved growth of centimetre-scale 2D β-In2Se3 film by chemical vapour deposition including distinct centimetre-scale 2D β′-In2Se3 film by an InSe precursor. The as-grown 2D β′-In2Se3 films on mica substrates can be delaminated or transferred onto flexible or uneven substrates, yielding α-In2Se3 films through a complete phase transition. Thus, a full spectrum of paraelectric, ferroelectric and antiferroelectric 2D films can be readily obtained by means of the correlated polymorphism in 2D In2Se3, enabling 2D memory transistors with high electron mobility, and polarizable β′–α In2Se3 heterophase junctions with improved non-volatile memory performance (Nature Nanotechnology 2023, 18, 55-63). These major finding above will guide and open new avenues for 2D materials research and 2D device development.

11300820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300820.value: In future, we will continue to develop the new approaches and improve the performances of 2D phase transition materials, e.g., enhance the stability, increase the electon mobility, the retention time, recyclibility, and the phase transition response rate. New 2D materials and heterostructures will be investigated to improve the overall properties. Overall, the potential for the phase transition 2D materials are enormous and can be potentially combined with the other ferrroic properties, such as ferroelectricity, ferrromagnetism, etc. New functionalities, new devices, and smart devices could be potentially developed based on our research. We will continue to develop a number of in situ techniques, such as in situ TEM, AFM, KFM, PFM, and in situ Raman approches, to develop and search for new materials. Meanwhile, we will also develop new CVD techniques that could achieve large area growth and especially phase controlled growth of these 2D phase transition materials.

11300820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300820.value: Owing to the high surface ratio and instability nature of the 2D materials, to achieve a reversible, complete and atomically-precise phase transition in monolayer 2D TMDs is challenging. Therefore, this project is to understand and develop phase transition 2D materials towards scalable applications. In this project, we have successfully achieved all the objectives in the proposal. Specifically, we have prepared ultraclean 2D materials via the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and our in-house developed ice transfer method, and triggered the phase transition in 2D ReS2 via electron beam irradiaiton. The phase transition of ReS2 and In2Se3 have been successfully reversibly controlled through the electrical, optical, electron beam and mechanical strategies. Meanwhile, we have understood the phase transition mechanisms, related to the strain, defects, temperature. In the end, we have been able to apply the complete and reversible phase transition for the memory transitor device applications. These attractive novel properties in these 2D TMD phase transition materials will boost the application developments in novel IC/memory device designing. Changeable, faster and smaller integrated circuits will be achievable if using these new materials and designs. The semiconductor industry, as well as the entire IT technology/society will be continually evolving and improved.

11300920.label: Realisation of objectives
11300920.value: We recently achieved our objectives and have finished 11 papers, ten of which have been published. Another manuscript ”Pacific Oceanic Front Amplifies the Impact of Atlantic Oceanic Front on North Atlantic Blocking” has finished and is ready to submit. (1) Relationship between ENSO and Winter Synoptic Temperature Variability over the Asian–Pacific–American Region In our study, the relationship between ENSO and winter synoptic temperature variability (STV) over the Asian–Pacific–American region is examined in 26 CMIP5/6 model outputs. On the one hand, both HPS and LPS models can overall reproduce a reasonable relationship between STV and the mean-flow conditions supporting extratropical eddy development. On the other hand, only HPS models can well capture the relationship between ENSO and the development of extratropical eddies, while LPS models fail to simulate this feature, indicating that the bias in the simulated ENSO–STV relationship among CMIP5/6 models can be traced back to ENSO simulation. Furthermore, the bias of the ENSO simulation is characterized by an unreasonable SST pattern bias, with an excessive westward extension of warm SST anomalies over the western Pacific and weak warm SST anomalies over the equatorial central-eastern Pacific, resulting in the underestimation of the zonal SST anomaly gradient among models. In addition, the ENSO–STV relationship over the Asian–Pacific–American region is still robust in future projections based on HPS models, providing implications for the selection of future climate predictors. Based on observational data from 1951 to 2018, we also investigated the interdecadal variability of the relationship between ENSO and winter synoptic temperature variability (STV) over the Asian–Pacific–American region and the possible reason for this interdecadal shift in the ENSO–STV relationship over Eastern China. During P1, the ENSO pattern is significantly correlated to the temperature gradient over Northeast Asia, which is the key region influencing the intensification of extratropical eddies. But in P2, the ENSO pattern is not related to the temperature over Northeast Asia. Therefore, the change in the ENSO pattern from P1 to P2 contributes to the interdecadal shift in the ENSO–STV relationship in the 1980s over Eastern China by influencing the temperature gradient over Northeast Asia, while ENSO can influence the temperature gradient over North America for the whole period. Furthermore, the possible role of the ENSO patterns in P1 and P2 is also examined by using an atmospheric general circulation model, highlighting that the pattern of SST variation is a determining factor in regulating STV in different regions. (2) North Atlantic as a Trigger for Pacific-Wide Decadal Climate Change In this study, we show that an AMV-SST cooling can initiate a pan-Pacific response. The North Atlantic cooling induces westerly wind anomalies over the central-western equatorial Pacific as Kelvin-wave responses and easterly wind anomalies over the far-eastern equatorial Pacific as Rossby-wave responses. Additionally, anomalous lows are generated over the extratropical North and South Pacific through the midlatitude Rossby wave propagation. The tropical and midlatitude teleconnections act together to develop into a warm-phase IPO-like pattern through the wind-induced latent heat. Our results suggest a potential of advancing the predictability of IPO through a skillful simulation of AMV. (3) Individual and Joint Effect of Atlantic and Pacific Oceanic Fronts on Ural Blocking This study investigates the impact of climatological Atlantic and Pacific oceanic fronts on the winter Ural blocking using semi-idealised experiments of the MAECHAM5 model. The Atlantic oceanic front acts to enhance the northeastward extension of the Atlantic storm tracks and strengthen the planetary-scale ridge over the Ural Mountains; these favour the occurrence of Ural blocking. On the other hand, the Pacific oceanic front acts to strengthen the annular-like response, with a northward shift of the climatological-mean eddy-driven jet and a stronger north-south pressure gradient in the midlatitudes circumglobally. This stronger mean circulation inhibits the occurrence of Ural blocking. Overall, the two oceanic fronts have an opposite effect on the Ural blocking frequency climatologically, where the Pacific oceanic front has a stronger impact on the Ural blocking frequency than the Atlantic oceanic front. Our results highlight the importance of the Pacific oceanic front in a comprehensive understanding of Ural blocking. (4) Atlantic and Pacific Oceanic Fronts Shape North Atlantic Blocking In this study, we use novel semi-idealized experiments of MAECHAM5, which has a small bias in Atlantic blocking, to demonstrate that the mid-latitude Atlantic and Pacific oceanic fronts jointly shape the climatological Atlantic blocking pattern. Our experiments show that the Atlantic and Pacific oceanic fronts increase Euro-Atlantic blocking frequency via enhancing the Atlantic storm track and the permanent pressure ridge over the eastern Atlantic, respectively. The oceanic fronts also act to suppress Greenland blocking frequency via strengthening the Atlantic eddy-driven jet. Our results reveal that the two oceanic fronts primarily determine the observed blocking activity centre in the Euro-Atlantic and Greenland. Therefore, the air-sea interaction along both the mid-latitude Atlantic and Pacific oceanic fronts are indispensable for Atlantic blocking activity. (5) Pacific Oceanic Front Amplifies the Impact of Atlantic Oceanic Front on North Atlantic Blocking We use semi-idealised experiments of MAECHAM5 to demonstrate that the mid-latitude Pacific oceanic front is crucial for climatological Atlantic blocking activity. The front enhances the Pacific eddy-driven jet that extends eastward toward the North Atlantic. The eastward-extended Pacific jet reinforces the North Atlantic circulation response to the Atlantic oceanic front, including the storm track and the eddy-driven jet. The strengthening of the eddy-driven jet reduces the Greenland blocking frequency. Moreover, the Pacific oceanic front greatly strengthens the stationary planetary-scale ridge in Europe. Together with a stronger northeastward extension of the Atlantic storm track, enhanced interaction between extratropical cyclones and the European ridge favours the occurrence of Euro-Atlantic blocking. Therefore, the North Atlantic circulation response, amplified remotely by the Pacific oceanic front, substantially increases Euro-Atlantic blocking frequency but decreases Greenland blocking frequency.

11300920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300920.value: We recently explored the relationship between ENSO and winter synoptic temperature variability over the Asian–Pacific–American region based on observational data and models, providing implications for the selection of future climate predictors. What’s more, we also achieved some results about the individual and joint effect of Atlantic and Pacific Oceanic fronts on ural blocking, suggesting a potential of advancing the predictability of IPO through a skillful simulation of AMV and highlighting the importance of the Pacific oceanic front in a comprehensive understanding of Ural blocking.

11300920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300920.value: This study can help improve the predictability of extreme cold events and better understand the sub-seasonal variation of the East Asian winter monsoon (EAWM) and large-scale atmospheric circulation, these results can advance our understanding of the physical mechanisms controlling sub-seasonal variability of cold surges in South China and its relationship with various climate drivers such as Atlantic multi-decadal variability (AMV) and Pacific multi-decadal variability (PMV). The findings can explain the dominant sub-seasonal variations of the EAWM and the underlying mechanisms, show the atmospheric response to AMV and PMV in climate models, and demonstrate the impact of the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) on Ural blocking and the EAWM using a new conceptual model and dynamical framework.

11301120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301120.value: Single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) was awarded the 2014 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for bypassing the optical resolution limit of traditional microscopy. The main idea is to use laser to turn the fluorescence of individual molecules on and off. Then one can take the images of the same area multiple times with just a few interspersed molecules glowing each time. Superimposing these images, usually thousands of them, yields a dense super-resolution image resolved at the nanolevel. Many point source localization algorithms have since been developed for localizing the positions of the fluorescing molecules. A major difficulty of traditional microscopes is that they cannot determine the depth position of a point source because its image is roughly the same above or below the focal plane. Therefore, the traditional imaging techniques to obtain 3D information is to take 2D images slice by slice in the depth direction. For 3D SMLM, we will have to take thousands of images in each depth level and composing them all into a 3D image of the object of interest by image reconstruction techniques. One of the newer optical techniques to obtain 3D positions of points simultaneously is by using specially designed optical elements, e.g. rotating point spread function (rPSFs). These rPSFs encode the depth information of the point sources into one single 2D snapshot. The amount of rotation of the PSF in the snapshot gives the depth of the point source. The depth can then be recovered by image processing techniques. However, the inverse process of going from the 2D snapshot to the 3D positions of the point sources is a large scale and highly ill-posed problem. This project is to develop novel and efficient algorithms for getting the locations and the intensity of the point sources accurately. We will design optimization methods based on the sparsity information of the solution and also methods from deep neutral networks. The successful implementation of our algorithms will be profitable to a broad spectrum in science where 3D SMLM is used, such as cell imaging in biology, spectral diffusion in chemistry, and quantum optics in physics. We will also consider its application in locating and classifying debris in outer space. On the theoretical side, new techniques for image processing, optimization, convex analysis, and machine learning will arise through the study of our algorithms and their convergence analysis. A better understanding of these techniques will be beneficial to all fields concerned. 单分子定位显微镜(SMLM)由于突破了传统显微镜光学分辨率的极限, 因而荣获2014年诺贝尔化学奖. 这一技术的主要思想是使用激光打开和关闭单个分子的荧光. 然后每次通过少量插入的发光分子, 我们可以多次拍摄这些图像的同一区域. 最后叠加这些图像(通常是数千张), 就可以产生纳米级的稠密超分辨率图像. 自2014年起, 为了确定荧光分子的位置, 很多点光源定位算法相继被提出. 传统显微镜的主要缺陷在于它们无法确定点光源的深度位置, 因为其图像在焦点平面的上方或下方是模糊的. 因此, 获取3维信息的传统成像技术是在深度方向上逐层切片而形成2维图像. 对于3维的单分子定位显微镜, 我们必须在每个深度方向上取数千幅图像, 并且通过图像重建技术将它们组合成感兴趣的目标-三维图像. 同时获得一些3维点的位置的一种较新的光学技术是使用专门设计的光学元件, 例如旋转点扩散函数(rPSF). 这些旋转点扩散函数将点光源的深度信息编码为一个2维图像. 2维图像中点扩散函数（PSF）的旋转程度给出了点光源的深度, 而点光源的深度可以通过图像处理技术来恢复. 然而, 从2维图像中获得3维点光源的位置的这个逆过程, 是一个大规模且高度非适当性问题. 本文这个项目, 目的在于发展能精确获取点光源的位置和强度的新颖且有效的算法. 我们将基于所求解问题的解的稀疏信息, 设计出优化方法和深度神经网络方法. 我们设计的算法的成功, 将在使用三维单分子定位显微镜的科学领域有广泛的应用, 例如生物学中的细胞成像, 化学中的光谱扩散, 物理学中的量子光学. 我们还将考虑将其应用于对外太空中的碎片进行定位和分类. 此外, 从理论上讲, 在我们的算法及其收敛性分析研究中, 将出现有关图像处理, 优化, 凸分析和机器学习的一些新技术. 更好地理解这些技术, 所有相关领域都将受益.

11301120.label: Realisation of objectives
11301120.value: Regarding Objective 1: The variational models for 3D point sources localization problem have a data-fitting term and one or two regularization terms to guarantee that the solution is in the function space that satisfies some a priori assumptions on the solution image, e.g., sparsity, as we are looking for point sources in three-dimensional space. There are parameters, called regularization parameters, that balance these terms. The choice of these parameters is difficult, and may require solving the problem multiple times (e.g., in L-curve method). Papers 2 and 10 in Section 8 are two papers to try to find these parameters using only one solve of the system. Papaer 2 deals with the case when the regularization term is of nuclear-norm type--a standard type for sparsity requirement on the solution. Paper 10 deals with the situation when there are two regularization terms, one to ensure sparsity and the other to ensure smoothing. Regarding Objective 2: Since 2018, when we wrote the proposal, neural networks have taken over variational methods as the method of choice. In this regard, we have also spent a lot of time developing neural networks to solve the 3D point source localization problem. Paper 3 is our first attempt at this. Instead of minimizing the cost functional with a data-fitting term and a regularization term, we propose to solve the inverse problem using neural networks. We artificially generate training data following the forward problem and design a neural network to solve the inverse problem. The loss function is the L2 error of the neural network output and our generated ground-truth (mean squared error). The results are better than the variational method and we published it as Paper 3. Paper 4 developed another approach of designing the neural network. In Paper 3, we use the standard loss function where we measure the neural network output and the generated ground-truth. There is no aprior physical information used in the neural network so designed. Thus in Paper 4, we developed our physics-informed neural network for the problem. Precisely, the regularization terms used in the variational problem are used as loss function now, forcing the neural network output to satisfy the physical constraint that should be on the solution. The results are better than that using only the standard mean squared error. Papers 1, 8, 9 are papers related to design of better neural networks or machine learning methods. Precisely, Paper 1 developed a tensor method for classification when we have multiple view of the data, usually from different modality. Paper 8 gave a mathematical explanation of encoder-decoder nerual networks and Paper 9 gave a new clustering method for classification. Papers 5, 6, 7 are related to hyperspectral imaging in remote sensing for clustering, classification and segmentation. Our 3D point source localization can be incorporated with different spectral frequencies to detect not only the 3D location of points but also their composition by using one 2D single shot. Preliminary results are promising and this is the direction we are working on.

11301120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301120.value: We have designed a fast and accurate neural network to solve the 3D point source localization problem. Instead of minimizing a cost functional with a data-fitting term and a regularization term, we solve the inverse problem using neural networks. We artificially generate training data following the forward problem, i.e., the randomly generated 3D point source images are acquired by the microscope or telescope in a 2D setting with noise added. Then we design a neural network to solve the inverse problem, i.e, given the artificially generated 2D images, we train a network to generate the 3D point source images. The loss function is the L2 error of the neural network output and our generated ground-truth (mean squared error). The results are better than the mathematical variational method, and we published the results in Optics Express. However, using the standard loss function (mean squared error) basically means that we are assuming the error is Gaussian. In many microscopic or telescopic imaging setting, especailly when the number of photons is not high, the noise are of the Poisson type rather than of the Gaussian type. Moreover, there is no aprior physical information used in the neural network so designed, except in generating the training data. Thus in our newest paper, we developed our physics-informed neural network for the problem. Precisely, the regularization terms used in the variational problem are incorporated into the loss function of the neural network now, forcing the neural network output to satisfy the physical constraint that should be on the solution. The results are better than that using just the standard mean squared error. The results are accepted for publication in Applied Optics. Besides these results, we also developed new ways to find the regularization parameters between the data-fitting term and the regularization term used in the variational formulation. These theory may be applicable in choosing the hyper-parameters in the neural network settings as the regularization parameters also appear now in the loss function of the physics-informed neural networks. We also have papers on improving the clustering, classification and segmentation of hyperspectral images. These can later be incorporated into 3D point source localization for space debris to not only detect their locations but also their composition. Preliminary results using NASA dataset are promising.

11301120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301120.value: So far, we have only used the physical equation of the rotating point-spread function (rPSF) to artificially generate training data to train our neural network. Although the results are good, these are not real data. In the past year, we have been provided with some real data from a biologist and his team in the US and France. We are working on the given data and adapting our neural network to perform on the real data. Preliminary results on DNA dynamics are promising. We are also developing algorithms for rPSF with two light sources (multi-spectral) that can give us two views of the cell functions. Our previous results on hyperspectral imaging and multi-view classification will be useful here.

11301120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301120.value: Single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) is to use a laser to turn the fluorescence of individual molecules on and off. Then, one can take the 2D images of the same area multiple times with just a few interspersed molecules glowing each time. Superimposing these 2D images, usually thousands of them, yields a dense super-resolution image resolved at the nanolevel. However, to get the 3D location of the molecules, we will have to take thousands of images in each depth level and compose them all into a 3D image of the object of interest by image reconstruction techniques. A new optical technique to obtain 3D positions of points simultaneously is by using specially designed optical elements, e.g,. rotating point spread function (rPSFs). These rPSFs encode the depth information of the point sources into a single 2D snapshot. The amount of rotation of the PSF in the snapshot gives the depth of the point source. The depth can then be recovered by image processing techniques. Our project has designed a fast and accurate neural network that accepts one 2D image from the rPSF microscope or telescope, and outputs the 3D locations of the molecules or space debris in the 2D image.
