11301220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301220.value: This is a chemistry proposal focusing on the design, synthesis and applications of two-photon photoactivatable nucleic acids in DNA nanotechnology. Recently, the development of two-photon photoactive molecules is emerging because the use of two-photon excitation light source is beneficial to biological systems. Unfortunately, synthesis of the reported two-photon photoactive groups does not allow for oligonucleotide conjugation. Many of them are only restricted to mono-functionalization. They are highly limited by experimental and synthetic complexities. To address these problems, we propose to 1) re-design the synthetic pathways of these photoactive molecules and synthesize a series of bi-functional two-photon photocleavable phosphoramidite molecules via typical chemical reactions such as Heck, Suzuki and Sonogashira coupling reactions; 2) to effectively introduce these molecules to DNA strands in a sequence anywhere via standard solid-phase synthesis by well-established cyanoethylphosphoramidite chemistry to form light-activatable nucleic acids; 3) to employ these photocleavable nucleic acids as building scaffolds for construction of DNA-based nanocarriers used in light-triggered cargo release. As expected, these newly synthesized organic molecules will exhibit large two-photon photolysis cross-section values and high photocleavage efficiency. The integrated photoactivatable nucleic acids will irreversibly break in a site-specific manner upon near infrared (NIR) exposure, leading to light-triggered control of oligonucleotide hybridization. This photolysis will give rise to the opening of the self-assembled 3D DNA nanostructures and the release of encapsulated cargos simultaneously. As compared to other photoresponsive nanocarriers, the proposed DNA-based system is highly biocompatible and non-toxicity. The regulation of cargo release by light is in a clean, remote-control, non-contact and non-invasive manner. This would create a new paradigm of inputs that allows for temporal and spatial control with high specificity and overcoming the drawback of chemical inputs including waste accumulation and delivery kinetics. We anticipate that the facile design of synthetic pathways and the synthesis of a new series of two-photon photocleavage phosphoramidite molecules are beneficial to the synthetic chemists and DNA chemists for further development of new caged compounds as light triggers in DNA nanotechnology. Additionally, this proposed work also leads to a step towards employing photon-responsive DNA nanocarriers as versatile tools in controllable drug delivery. In the future, we envision that this newly developed two-photon photoactive DNA nanotechnology can be adopted to function in clinical applications and will be beneficial to the community of human healthcare in strengthening therapeutic activity, reducing the side effects, diminishing the needed drug dosage during treatment. 最近，發展二光子光敏分子的出現是因為兩光子的使用激發光源對生物系統有益。不幸的是，報導的雙光子光敏基團不允許寡核苷酸綴合。它們中的許多僅限於單功能化。他們受到高度限制實驗和合成的複雜性。為了解決這些問題，我們建議1）重新設計這些光敏分子的合成途徑，並合成一系列雙官能雙光子光解磷酰胺分子的典型化學反應Heck，Suzuki和Sonogashira偶聯反應等反應； 2）有效通過標準的固相合成，通過公認的氰基乙基亞磷酰胺化學，將這些分子以任何順序引入到DNA鏈中，形成可光激活的核酸； 3）將這些可光裂解的核酸用作構建體用於光觸發貨物的基於DNA的納米載體構建的支架釋放。這些新合成的有機分子將表現出大的雙光子光解橫截面值和高的光解效率。綜合可光活化的核酸在接近時將以位點特異性方式不可逆地斷裂紅外（NIR）曝光，導致對寡核苷酸的光觸發控制雜交。這種光解作用將導致自組裝3D DNA的開放納米結構與封裝貨物的釋放同時進行。相比於其他光響應納米載體，建議的基於DNA的系統具有生物相容性和無毒性。光線對貨物的放行規定是乾淨的，遠程控制，非接觸式和非侵入式方式。這將創建一個新的輸入範式，可以進行高度的時間和空間控制，並克服包括廢物積累和輸送在內的化學輸入的缺點動力學。我們預計合成途徑的簡便設計和一系列新的雙光子光解亞磷酰胺分子對合成化學家和DNA化學家進一步開發新籠子化合物是DNA納米技術中的光觸發物。此外，這項擬議的工作還導致朝著將光子反應性DNA納米載體廣泛應用的方向邁出了一步可控藥物輸送的工具。將來，我們可以預見雙光子光敏DNA納米技術可在臨床中發揮作用的應用，將有益於人類保健領域增強治療活性，減少副作用，減少所需的治療期間的藥物劑量。

11301220.label: Realisation of objectives
11301220.value: Synthesis of ANBP Phosphoramidites We successfully synthesized the proposed photocleavable π-conjugated molecules through typical chemical reactions including bromination, palladium-mediated borylation, Sonogashira reaction, methylation, Stille reaction, phosphitylation, etc. Intermediates and final compounds such as s-ANBP-phosphoramidite and t-ANBP-phosphoramidite were characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopies and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. Synthesis of ANBP-based DNAs Once the pure ANBP phosphoramidites were ready, they were separately conjugated into DNA strands via solid-phase synthesis. An ANBP molecule was inserted between two different lengths of DNA oligonucleotides, d15 (sequence: 5’-CTGAGACTTTAATAA-3’) and d19 (sequence: 5’-TTGAAATTCACCTGGTAGC-3’), to facilitate the characterization of fragments after photolysis. The commercially available Cyanine 3 (Cy3) and 6-carboxyfluorescein (FAM) non-nucleosidic phosphoramidites were designed to be conjugated to the 5’ and 3’, respectively, while these fluorophores were utilized for the visualization of DNA fragments and to increase the polarity difference between d15 and d19. The synthetic protocols for the photocleavable DNA oligonucleotides, including Cy3-d15-s-ANBP-d19-FAM and Cy3-d15-t-ANBP-d19-FAM, as well as the reference DNA oligonucleotides (e.g. Cy3-d15 and d19-FAM), were based on our previous study. The stability of the modified DNA oligonucleotides containing s-ANBP and t-ANBP linkers was also tested in different media. No degradation of the DNA oligonucleotides was observed in any of these treatments, as shown by denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis analysis. This strongly confirms that the ANBP-based photocleavable linker is stable under acidic, alkaline, and high salt content conditions, as well as at high temperature. The one-photon photolytic efficiency of Cy3-d15-s-ANBP-d19-FAM and Cy3-d15-t-ANBP-d19-FAM was first examined through PAGE analysis. The Cy3 and FAM fluorescence signals from the DNA bands corresponded to the photocleaved d15 and d19 fragments increased with increasing irradiation time for both s-/t-ANBP-conjugated oligonucleotides, while the fluorescence intensities of their parent bands decreased over time. From the HPLC chromatograms of photocleaved Cy3-d15-s-ANBP-d19-FAM and Cy3-d15-t-ANBP-d19-FAM, it was found that photocleaved d19-FAM eluted at 8 min while Cy3-d15 eluted at 15 min. The maximum cleavage yields of Cy3-d15-s-ANBP-d19-FAM and Cy3-d15-t-ANBP-d19-FAM were determined to be 51.2 ± 2.0 % and 61.5 ± 4.2 % after irradiating for 120 s, respectively. The molecular masses of the two eluted fragments were confirmed by mass spectrometry. Quantitative One and Two-photon Uncaging One photon uncaging quantum yields have been determined using s-ANBP- and t-ANBP-conjugated DNA oligonucleotides and DEACAS as reference at 405 nm. The two systems show low uncaging quantum yields, 0.9 and 1.1 % for s-ANBP- and t-ANBP-conjugated DNA oligonucleotides respectively. This low uncaging quantum yield is not surprising as it is reported that cleavage of nucleic acids is less efficient that the one of other small molecules such as neurotransmitters. In a similar way, two-photon uncaging action cross-section have been determined using DECAS as reference40 at 740 and 800 nm using a fs pulsed laser. The smaller conjugated system compound s-ANBP, based on a biphenyl system, shows low two-photon induced photolysis efficiencies, with values of two-photon uncaging action cross-section under 0.5 GM both at 740 and 800 nm (0.40 and 0.39 GM respectively). These values are one order of magnitude lower than the ones reported for neurotransmitter uncaging, mainly because of the diminution of the uncaging quantum yield of nucleic acid uncaging. However, the extended pi-system molecule t-ANBP, with an ethynyl bridge between the two phenyl rings exhibits higher two-photon uncaging action cross-section values of 1.6 GM at 740 nm and 2.7 GM at 800 nm. Construction of a Photoactivatable DNA Cage Using s-ANBP for Controlled Oligonucleotide Release In this study, we used a self-assembly strategy similar to previously reported methods to construct the DNA nanocages. The assembly involved mixing the two pre-formed triangular-shaped DNAs, three linking strandsfunctionalized with four ANBP molecules, and three rigidified strands (ASO 4625). Specifically, the rigidified strands were designed to have the same sequences as the antisense oligonucleotide 4625 and were labeled with BHQ at both terminals. The middle part of the linking strands was designed to be complementary to the sequence of ASO 4625, facilitating the formation of a stable DNA nanocage structure. Upon cage formation, the fluorescence signal of the DNA band associated with ANBP-Cage was significantly diminished. After irradiating the ANBP-Cage with 415 nm, the original DNA band of ANBP-Cage disappeared, and a new fluorescent DNA band with higher mobility was observed. Additionally, a faint band appeared near the bottom of the gel, with mobility comparable to that of ASO 4625. These results confirmed the photo-triggered release of the target oligonucleotide, ASO 4625, from the ANBP-Cage. The fluorescence changes observed upon light irradiation of the ANBP-Cage in solutions were consistent with the PAGE analysis. However, the fluorescence signal did not fully return to its original state, suggesting that while the cage was partially or fully destroyed, some structural elements or residual interactions may still have been present, preventing complete fluorescence recovery. The fluorescence intensity increased gradually with longer irradiation times, eventually reaching a maximum increase of approximately 65 %. This increase in fluorescence was indicative of the progressive dissociation of the DNA nanocage and the release of the target oligonucleotide. The kinetics of the fluorescence recovery for the ANBP-DNA cage closely matched that observed in the s-ANBP-ds system, showing a similar magnitude of fluorescence increase and a similar time to reach a plateau. Evaluation of Antisense Function of Photo-released ASO 4625 Using RNase H-mediated RNA Digestion To evaluate the antisense function of the photo-released ASO 4625, we conducted an in vitro RNA digestion assay using RNase H, an enzyme that specifically cleaves the RNA strand in RNA-DNA hybrids. RNase H cleaves the RNA strand when it forms a duplex with a complementary DNA strand. The experiment was designed to assess whether ASO 4625, once released from the ANBP-Cage, could hybridize with its complementary RNA and restore its antisense function, leading to RNase H-mediated RNA cleavage. ANBP-Cage was mixed with the sense RNA, followed by 415 nm irradiation. This PAGE analysis allowed us to confirm the release of ASO 4625-BHQ from the ANBP-Cage upon irradiation and to determine whether it could function as an antisense molecule by hybridizing with the target RNA. Light-irradiated ANBP-Cage successfully released ASO 4625-BHQ, which then hybridized with the sense RNA to form a DNA-RNA duplex. Upon the addition of RNase H, the hybridized target RNA was digested, resulting in the fragmentation of the RNA strand and the release of single-stranded ASO 4625-BHQ. This confirmed that the photo-released ASO 4625-BHQ retained its antisense function, as it was able to hybridize with the complementary RNA and trigger RNA cleavage via RNase H. In contrast, when RNase H was added to the non-irradiated ANBP-Cage, the band corresponding to the target RNA remained intact, indicating that ASO 4625-BHQ remained sequestered within the cage and was unable to hybridize with the target RNA. These findings suggest that the designed ANBP-Cage can act as a versatile tool for the controlled release of therapeutic agents, such as antisense oligonucleotides, in response to specific external stimuli (e.g., light). This system holds potential for drug delivery applications, where spatial and temporal control over the release of therapeutic agents is crucial for targeting specific tissues or disease sites, thereby minimizing off-target effects and enhancing therapeutic efficacy. We strongly believe that we have successfully addressed the objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 in this funded project.

11301220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301220.value: We have synthesized novel ANBP derivatives, s-ANBP and t-ANBP, functionalized with dimethyltrityl and phosphoramidite groups to enable seamless integration into DNA backbones via solid-phase synthesis. These derivatives exhibit excellent chemical stability under acidic, alkaline, high-salt, and high-temperature conditions, making them robust for various applications. Single-stranded s-/t-ANBP-conjugated DNA oligonucleotides demonstrated reasonable one-photon photolytic efficiency under 415 nm LED irradiation, while t-ANBP, with an ethynyl-bridged extended π-system, showed enhanced two-photon absorption properties with two-photon uncaging action cross-section values of 1.6 GM at 740 nm and 2.7 GM at 800 nm. In duplex forms, the stability and dissociation of complementary antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) depended on the number of ANBP molecules incorporated and adjacent nucleotide deletions, highlighting the tunable hybridization behavior conferred by ANBP modifications. Leveraging these properties, we constructed a 3D DNA nanocage incorporating ANBP-conjugated DNA for light-triggered ASO 4625 release, which was validated by an in vitro RNA digestion assay using RNase H. This platform demonstrates precise, light-mediated therapeutic delivery and offers potential for broader applications in drug delivery and clinical use. The research findings have been published in three articles: "Biomacromolecules, 2025, 26, 5, 3113–3127", “Bioconjugate Chem. 2024, 35, 5, 623-632” and "ACS AMI 2023, 15, 1, 1944-1957". Furthermore, the PI presented the findings titled "Design, Synthesis and Applications of Photoactivatable Nucleic Acids in DNA Nanotechnology" at the 30th CANADA International Conference on Research in Chemical, Biological & Environmental Sciences held in Montreal, Canada, in July 2023; 7. “Unlock the Mysteries of Nucleic Acids in Chemistry and Materials Science” 3rd Edition of Sensors and Sensing Technology Virtual (V-Sensors2025), March 2025. 11301720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301720.value: 基於近年來對偏微分方程數值近似的無網格計算方法的發展,我們嘗試在本建議中開發一種高效的數值演算法,用於求解(2+1)維非局部和非線性薛定方程(NNLSE)。我們將其中非線性項以非局部相互作用的形式進行。NNLSE 是標準非線性薛定方程 (NLSE) 的重要延伸。一般來說,NNLSE 由於其非線性卷積值,因此以計算方式解決是非常昂貴的。無網格計算方法(基於局部徑向基函數的偽光譜方法(LRBF-PSM)的主要優點在於使用分散的搭配點在不規則邊界下解決高維問題。LRBF-PSM 的思路基於在每個重疊子域上通過無網格徑向基函數 (RBFs) 構建一組正交函數。利用LRBF的無網格優勢,可以擴展偽光譜方法,解決不規則域下的多維問題。具體來說,我們將使用隱式顯式 (IMEX) 和分時 (TS) 方案來近似時間變數。通過將無網格計算方法與自適應點分配和無條件穩定集成方案相結合,將進一步提高數值演算法的計算效率。

11301720.label: Realisation of objectives
11301720.value: Realisation of objectives Objective #1: To investigate the soliton-like waves from analyzing the nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equations. Based on convolution theory we derived a new formulation of nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equations (NNLSE) which involve a system of two partial differential equations. This approach can be used immediately as long as the nonlocal response corresponds to the inverse of a known differential operator. For more general nonlocal response, the finding of an equivalent partial differential equation is impossible due to the fact that its Fourier transform is not the inverse of any differential operator. To tackle this difficulty, we apply a rational approximation to the Fourier transform of nonlocal response, where polynomials are expressions with respect to the square of variable. As long as this rational approximation has a high accuracy, the obtained system of partial differential equations gives the similar solutions to the NNLSE. Objective #2: To develop a meshless computational method which is efficient and effective for solving the nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation for simulating soliton-like waves. Based on this newly proposed method, the numerical approximation to the solution of NNLSE is transformed into solving equivalent or approximate system of partial differential equations (PDEs). Using our recently developed finite integration method (FIM) for solving system of PDEs we further developed an improved FIM (IFIM) owing two improvements: (1) multi-layer integral is equivalently converted into one-layer integral; (2) the FIM only needs to work on one-layer integral for multi-dimensional problems. Numerical simulation of soliton-like waves for the NNLSE was obtained with very good approximation. A paper entitled “An improved finite integration method for nonlocal and nonlinear Schrodinger equation” on applying the FIM for solving the NNLSE had been published at the journal of Engineering Analysis with Boundary Elements (SCI-indexed journal with impact factor 3.25). Another paper entitled “Generalized finite integration method with Volterra operator for pricing multi-asset barrier option” has also just been accepted for publication at this journal.

11301820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301820.value: Reciprocity in optics requires symmetric response of light with respect to the interchange of source and observation point. Nonreciprocity (i.e. breaking of reciprocity) can give rise to one-way transport of light, which can generate practical applications such as invisible sensing, full-duplex communications, and noise-tolerant quantum computing. Only a few approaches can be applied to achieve optical nonreciprocity, among which structural rotation has been drawing considerable attention due to its magnetless and broadband characteristics. Structural rotation induces a synthetic gauge field that breaks the time-reversal symmetry and leads to nonreciprocity. Despite the challenges such as the requirement of high rotation speed, this approach has been employed to achieve novel nonreciprocal functionalities like optical isolation. More applications can emerge with the development of nanofabrication techniques and optomechanics. Structural rotation has inspired interesting physics in topological photonics and acoustics, where the synthetic gauge field can give rise to robust one-way edge states. Conventional studies mainly focus on light manipulation by single rotating structure. In this proposed project, we plan to investigate the nonreciprocal coupling between multiple rotating structures and the resulting novel properties for light manipulation. The project is grounded on the PI’s previously research about coupled resonators, pseudo nonreciprocity, and synthetic gauge fields, and it goes one step further. To be specific, we will study the nonreciprocal coupling of rotating cylinders in presence of rotation-induced gauge field and understand how it affects the vector properties of light. By considering a metasurface consisting of periodic rotating cylinders, we will explore novel nonreciprocal effects to control light’s propagation. We will also investigate possible mechanisms to enhance the nonreciprocal effects at low rotation speed and the possibility of experimental implementation. The results of this project could uncover the mechanism of nonreciprocal coupling in rotating optical structures and its effects on light’s properties. It can not only deepen our understanding of electrodynamics in non-inertial systems but also nourish the fields of non-Hermitian optics and topological photonics with novel structures and new insights. The results could find applications in the development of nonreciprocal optical devices for next-generation communication technologies and topological quantum computations. 光學互易性要求光響應相對於源點和觀測點的互換保持對稱。非互易性（即互易性的破壞）能夠導致光的單向傳輸並產生實際應用，例如隱形感應、全雙工通信和耐噪量子計算。僅有幾種方法可實現光學非互易性，其中結構旋轉因其無磁和寬帶特性而備受關注。結構旋轉產生的人工規範場打破了時間反演對稱性，進而導致非互易性。儘管面臨諸多挑戰（例如對於高轉速的要求），這種方法已經被用於實現新穎的非互易功能，例如光隔離。隨著納米加工技術和光機械的發展，更多的應用可能湧現。在拓撲光學和拓撲聲學中，結構旋轉啟發了很多有趣的物理，其中人工規範場可以產生具魯棒性的單向傳輸邊界態。 傳統研究主要關注單個旋轉結構的光調控，在本項目中，我們計劃研究多個旋轉結構之間的非互易耦合以及由此產生的可用於光調控的新特性。該項目基於負責人先前關於耦合諧振器、贗互易性和人工規範場的研究並更進一步。具體來說，我們將研究人工規範場下旋轉柱的耦合性質，理解其如何影響光的矢量特性。通過考慮週期性旋轉柱構成的超表面，我們將探索新穎的非互易效應用於調控光的傳播。我們還將研究在低轉速下增強非互易性的可能機制以及實驗驗證的可能性。 該項目的成果可以揭示旋轉光學結構中非互易耦合的機制以及其對光性質的影響，不僅可以加深我們對非慣性系統中電動力學的理解，而且可以產生新穎的光學結構和物理見解，促進非厄米光學和拓撲光學的發展。項目的成果可應用於開發非互易光學器件，發展下一代通信技術和拓撲量子計算。

11301820.label: Realisation of objectives
11301820.value: [Objective 1] We have considered a rotating dielectric cylinder sitting on a dielectric waveguide. The rotation of the cylinder induces a synthetic gauge field that breaks the time-reversal symmetry and mirror symmetry. By employing finite-element simulations, we find that the chiral modes of the cylinder are spectrally separated in the scattering spectrum due to the relativistic Sagnac effect. The chiral modes can give rise to unidirectional coupling with the waveguide via the transverse spin-orbit interaction, leading to different transmissions for guided waves propagating in opposite directions and thus optical isolation. We reveal the dependence of the nonreciprocal properties on various system parameters including mode order, rotation speed, and coupling distance. This work has been published in Optics Express 30, 27993 (2022). To achieve strong nonreciprocal effects, we then designed a spinning cylinder by using hyperbolic metamaterial and investigated its nonreciprocal coupling with a silicon waveguide. We find that this spinning cylinder can be applied to achieve 95% isolation of infrared light, which is attributed to the unique dispersion relation (unbounded wavevector) of the hyperbolic metamaterial and the Mie-type resonances of the cylinder at deep subwavelength. The mechanism can be employed to develop magnetic-free yet compact nonreciprocal devices for applications in optical communications, chiral quantum optics, and topological photonics. This work is published in Physical Review B 103, 094105 (2021). The nonreciprocal properties of the spinning cylinder are fundamentally attributed to the excitation of chiral multipole modes in the cylinder and its asymmetric coupling with guided modes under spin-orbit interaction. This indicates that similar properties and phenomena can be realized with a particle that exhibits rotating dipole fields, i.e., the dynamic rotation can be mimicked with stationary systems. Inspired by this, we apply a subwavelength helical particle to induce rotating electric dipole (i.e., circular dipole). We observe the unidirectional coupling between the particle and the waveguide, i.e., a signature phenomenon of the spinning cylinder coupled with a waveguide. This work is published in PNAS 120, e2301620120 (2023). [Objective 2] By applying full-wave simulations and coupled mode theory, we demonstrate that two rotating cylinders can induce a non-Hermitian exceptional point due to their unidirectional coupling. Under the excitation of a linearly polarized plane wave, the chiral mode of one cylinder can unidirectionally couple to the same mode of the other cylinder via the spin-orbit interaction. The resulting exceptional point is robust against spin-flipping perturbations. The system provides a simple platform to realize non-Hermitian exceptional points and explore their novel properties and applications. This work is published in Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021). To understand the difference between the effects induced by nonreciprocity of rotating cylinders and those induced by pseudo nonreciprocity, we further investigate the coupling of rotating dipoles in two helical particles. By tuning the polarization of the rotating dipoles and exploiting transverse spin-orbit interaction, we can control the asymmetric Pancharatnam-Berry geometric phase for the excited guided waves propagating in opposite directions. The interference of the guided waves excited by the two particles can give rise to transmissions with various line shapes, including Lorentzian-like, antiresonance-like, Fano-like, and EIT-like line shapes. Unlike the guided waves excited by rotating cylinders, the guided waves in this system exhibit pseudo-nonreciprocity, thus, optical isolation cannot be achieved. These results demonstrate that, while asymmetric coupling can also be realized in stationary particles-waveguide system, the rotating cylinders carry unique nonreciprocal properties that cannot be found in stationary systems. The results are published in Physical Review A 108, 043511 (2023). [Objective 3] To achieve the third objective, we considered multiple rotating cylinders periodically arranged into a one-dimensional lattice. We find that this system can give rise to arbitrary order exceptional points with the order directly determined by the number of cylinders. In addition, we show that higher-order EPs are accompanied by enhanced optical isolation, which may find applications in designing novel optical isolators and nonreciprocal optical devices. These results are reported in Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021). Then, we investigated the nonreciprocal properties of the metasurface composed of periodic rotating cylinders sitting above a dielectric substrate. We find that the metasurface can realize both asymmetric and nonreciprocal reflection/transmission of the incident plane wave. The underlying mechanism is attributed to the Sagnac effect associated with the chiral multipole modes of the coupled rotating cylinders. By introducing dielectric pillars to control the propagation phase, we achieve nonreciprocal wavefront manipulations with the metasurface. The proposed metasurface can find applications in designing thin nonmagnetic nonreciprocal optical devices. The results are summarized in arXiv:2411.15928 (2024). To understand the differences between the metasurface composed of rotating cylinders and the metasurface composed of rotating dipoles, we further investigate the light transmission, absorption, and scattering in the waveguide metasurfaces composed of multiple helical/chiral particles. We find that the waveguide metasurfaces can enable intriguing modulations of the guided light. It can convert free-space incident light to guided light and give rise to a light funnelling phenomenon [Optics Express 30, 42495 (2022)]; it can induce strong lateral optical forces on the helical particles for applications in optical micromanipulations [Optics Express 31, 28929 (2023)]; it can induce broadband unidirectional absorption of guided light [arXiv:2402.06686 (2024)]. [Objective 4] We discovered two mechanisms to enhance the nonreciprocal effects at low rotation speed. First, we find that a rotating cylinder made of hyperbolic metamaterial can give rise to much larger nonreciprocal effects at the resonance frequencies of the chiral modes. The mechanism is attributed to the unbounded wavevector in the hyperbolic metamaterial and the large quality factor of the chiral modes [Physical Review B 103, 094105 (2021)]. Second, we find that the coupling between multiple rotating cylinders through guided waves can also enhance the nonreciprocal effects at low rotation speed. This is attributed to the constructive interferences between the chiral multipole modes in the rotating cylinders and the strong cylinder-waveguide coupling through evanescent fields [Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021); arXiv:2411.15928 (2024)]. The key property of the rotating cylinder is the asymmetric coupling with the waveguide substrate under the spin-orbit interaction. We demonstrated by experiments that this property can be realized with helical particles supporting rotating electric dipoles [PNAS 120, e2301620120 (2023)]. [Others] One objective of the project is to investigate the non-Hermitian phenomena induced by the nonreciprocal coupling of rotating cylinders. The results of this objective have inspired us to explore a one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model with asymmetric coupling. We studied the localization properties in this model and designed a photonic lattice with coupled cylinders to distinguish the extended and localized single-particle states [Physical Review B 105, 014207 (2022)]. Objective 3 inspired us to realize metasurfaces for asymmetric manipulation of guided waves through transverse spin-orbit interaction. We designed such a metasurface and demonstrated asymmetric focusing and steering of surface plasmon polaritons [Optics Letters 49, 1915 (2024)].

11301820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301820.value: This GRF project has generated 9 journal publications, including 3 papers in Physical Review A/B, 5 papers in Optics Express/Letters, and 1 paper in PNAS. In addition, there is one manuscript currently under review in Physical Review A, and one manuscript under revision. The major findings are summarized as follows: We find that the rotation of a dielectric cylinder induces a synthetic gauge field that breaks the time-reversal symmetry and mirror symmetry. This gives rise to the relativistic Sagnac effect and the frequency splitting of chiral multipole modes [Optics Express 30, 27993 (2022)]. The chiral modes can induce unidirectional coupling with the waveguide, leading to optical isolation. The isolation can be enhanced by using rotating cylinders made of hyperbolic metamaterials [Physical Review B 103, 094105 (2021)]. For two rotating cylinders coupled through a waveguide, their chiral modes can unidirectionally couple via the spin-orbit interaction. This gives rise to a second-order non-Hermitian exceptional point robust against spin-flipping perturbations [Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021)]. For periodic rotating cylinders, we find that the system can give rise to arbitrary order exceptional points. The higher-order EPs lead to larger optical isolation of the guided wave [Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021)]. In addition, periodic rotating cylinders coupled through a dielectric waveguide can serve as a nonreciprocal metasurface, which can induce both asymmetric and nonreciprocal manipulations of light [arXiv:2411.15928 (2024)]. We find two mechanisms to enhance the nonreciprocal effects induced by rotating cylinders. One mechanism is to employ the unique dispersion relation of hyperbolic metamaterials [Physical Review B 103, 094105 (2021)]. Another mechanism is to use the collective resonances in a lattice of rotating cylinders coupled through a dielectric waveguide [Optics Express 29, 29720 (2021); arXiv:2411.15928 (2024)]. We apply rotating dipoles (i.e., circular dipoles) in stationary structures to achieve similar asymmetric coupling as in rotating cylinders. We find a simple helix particle can give rise to rotating dipoles under the illumination of a plane wave [PNAS 120, e2301620120 (2023)]. The pseudo-nonreciprocal coupling of two helix particles enables the realization of asymmetric transmission spectra for the guided waves propagating in opposite directions [Physical Review A 108, 043511 (2023)]. For multiple helix particles coupled through a waveguide, the system can give rise to arbitrary order exceptional point, which leads to intriguing phenomena including light funnelling [Optics Express 30, 42495 (2022)], enhanced lateral optical force [Optics Express 31, 28929 (2023)], and broadband unidirectional absorption of light [arXiv:2402.06686 (2024)].

11301820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301820.value: There are a few directions for further development of the research. First, the third objective of this completed project has focused on manipulating free-space light with the metasurface composed periodic rotating cylinders. In fact, the metasurface can also enable efficient manipulation of on-chip guided light. Since on-chip nonreciprocal optical devices play an essential role in optical communication and computation, it will be interesting to explore the application of rotating cylinders in manipulating the wavefront of guided waves. Second, while this project has focused on the nonreciprocal properties of rotating cylinders, the interplay of non-reciprocity, non-Hermiticity, and topology can give rise to rich physics and phenomena. In particular, the periodic rotating cylinders coupled through a waveguide can serve as a very convenient platform to explore non-Hermitian topology, which is an emerging field of research attracting significant attention. Third, the research can be further developed to explore the quantum optical properties of rotating cylinders for applications in quantum information processing. We can explore the above directions by collaborating with experts of topological photonics and quantum optics.

11301820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301820.value: Nonreciprocal optical properties enable the realization of one-way light propagation with essential applications in invisible sensing, full-duplex communications, and noise-tolerant quantum computing. This project investigated the nonreciprocal optical properties of rotating cylinders and their applications in light manipulations. We find a number of intriguing properties of single rotating cylinder, coupled multiple cylinders, and periodic rotating cylinders, including Sagnac frequency splitting, unidirectional coupling, non-Hermitian exceptional points, and nonreciprocal transmission/reflection of light. We also uncover several mechanisms to enhance the nonreciprocal properties of the rotating cylinders, which pave the way for their practical applications. The results deepen our understanding of the relativistic effects on the nonreciprocal properties of moving medium and offer robust mechanisms for achieving one-way light manipulations. The results also offer insights into the interplay between nonreciprocity, non-Hermiticity, and topology, thus nourishing the fields of non-Hermitian optics and topological photonics. The uncovered mechanisms and the proposed structures in this project can find applications in developing novel nonreciprocal optical devices for optical communications, optical imaging, and on-chip optical computations.

11302020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302020.value: 作為邊界層理論的奠基者，Prandtl在1904年從帶非滑移邊界條件的不可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程導出了Prandtl 方程。該方程可以捕捉到在粘性消失過程中流體在邊界附近運動的行為。更加精確地來講，在邊界附近的一個薄層中，對流和粘性效應可以平衡，從而在這個薄層中流體可以近似的由一個簡化的不可壓Navier-Stokes方程，即Prandtl 方程來描述。而在遠離這個薄層的區域，粘性對於流體的影響可以忽略不計。對於邊界層數學理論的研究始於Oleinik在二十世紀六十年代先驅性的工作。雖然在這方面有豐富的結果，但是除了1998年Sammartino-Caflisch在解析函數框架下的結果和最近在Gevrey函數框架下的一些結果之外，絕大多數的理論均局限於二維空間，並且流體的速度場要滿足Oleinik單調性條件。 Prandtl方程早期被應用到空氣動力學中，隨後又被廣泛地應用到流體力學及工程的各種領域中。不僅如此，在數學上， Prandtl方程可以看作是帶有退化耗散和混合型結構的偏微分方程的一個典型範例。所以，研究這個方程的過程會給我們帶來很多具有挑戰性的問題，並且許多問題即使在距離提出此方程一百年多後的今天仍然是未被解決的。 另一方面，我們知道磁流體方程組是描述電導流體的一個基本的方程組。在當Reynolds數和磁場Reynolds數以同一量階趨於無窮，並保持Hartmann數有界時，從該方程組出發也可以推導出一個Prandtl型的邊界層方程組。通過利用切向磁場的穩定性效應，我們最近在Sobolev空間中建立了该邊界層方程組的兩維適定性理論並嚴格證明了對應的Prandtl ansatz。 基於我們關於磁流體邊界層方程組的一些工作，本研究項目致力於探索磁流體邊界層理論與其他物理系統之間的關係，譬如帶毛細效應的Navier-Stokes-Korteweg系統及帶內蘊彈性結構的粘彈性力學系統。事實上，我們將會看到，無磁阻的兩維磁流體方程不僅與不可壓的Navier-Stokes-Korteweg方程之間有一個內在的聯繫，並且它的邊界層方程有着一些和粘彈性力學系統模型相似的穩定性機制。所以，相信基於對磁流體邊界層的理解，我們可以發展一套新的途徑去研究上述物理模型中的邊界層方程，進而研究它們所對應的粘性消失極限問題。

11302020.label: Realisation of objectives
11302020.value: We study the well-posedness theories of the boundary layer systems and the vanishing viscosity limits for several physical models that include those from MHD. The research results were written in four research papers. Three of them have been published in international refereed journals. And the fourth paper will be completed within one month and then will be submitted afterwards. Some details of the research results are given as follows. First of all, it has been a fascinating topic in the study of boundary layer theory about the well posedness of Prandtl equation that was derived in 1904. Recently, new ideas about cancellation to overcome the loss of tangential derivatives were obtained so that Prandtl equation can be shown to be well-posed in Sobolev spaces to avoid the use of Crocco transformation as in the classical work of Oleinik. The first paper aims to show that the cancellation mechanism is in fact related to some intrinsic directional derivative that can be used to recover the tangential derivative under some structural assumption on the fluid near the boundary. In this paper, both the classical Prandtl equation and the boundary layer systems are discussed about the good unknown functions for well-posedness theory and also for the study on vanishing viscosity limit for MHD. In the second paper, we consider a hyperbolic version of three-dimensional anisotropic Navier-Stokes equations in a thin strip and its hydrostatic limit that is a hyperbolic Prandtl type equations. We prove the global-in-time existence and uniqueness for the two systems and the hydrostatic limit when the initial data belong to the Gevrey function space with index 2. The proof is based on a direct energy method by observing the damping effect in the systems. In the third paper, we review our recent study on boundary layer problems in compressible non isentropic flows with non-slip boundary condition for the velocity, in the small viscosity and heat conductivity limit. By multi-scale analysis, we derive the problems of viscous layer profiles and thermal layer profiles for different scales of viscosity and heat conductivity, from which we obtain the interaction mechanism of viscous layers and thermal layers. Then, when the viscosity goes to zero slower than or at the same rate as the heat conductivity, we give a well-posedness result of the two dimensional viscous layer problem, which is the Prandtl type equations coupled with a degenerated parabolic equation, in the class of tangential velocity being strictly monotonic in the normal variable. Last, when the viscosity goes to zero faster than the heat conductivity, we study the stability of the thermal layer problem at a shear flow in two or three space variables, which is an inviscid Prandtl type equations coupled with a degenerated parabolic equation. Finally, the stability and instability of the boundary layer is a fundamental problem in the boundary layer theory and there are very few works on the compressible fluids. In the fourth paper, we show the nonlinear stability of the shear flow for two dimensional steady compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a torus under the no-slip boundary condition in Sobolev spaces. Compared with the incompressible case, the interaction between density and velocity causes more difficulties both in the analysis of linear and nonlinear systems.

11302020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302020.value: With the study on this research project, we have several new observations and introduce some new approaches to study the boundary layer problems. First of all, we introduced a new understanding on the cancellation of loss of tangential derivatives in the analysis through the directional derivatives. We show that this is consistent with the recent study on the two space dimension models such as the classical Prandtl equation and the system derived from MHD in which some new unknown functions were used. For the compressible fluid with strong boundary, we investigate viscous and thermal layers in the vanishing viscosity and heat conductivity limits for the non-isentropic fluid. For the isentropic fluid, we firstly justify the structural stability of the steady compressible Navier-Stokes equations with strong boundary layer. For this, the newly introduced quasi-compressible-Stokes iteration is fully used through the analysis on the compressible Orr-Sommerfeld equation in the subsonic regime. We believe that the analytic techniques and approaches can be applied to or shed some light on the future study of other boundary layer problems, in particular those in three dimensional space and compressible flow in the high Reynolds number when the corresponding physical parameters in different regimes.

11302020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302020.value: The study on the boundary layer arised from the development of aerodynamics in 1900 and the system of equations for modelling this phenomena was formulated by Ludwig Prandtl in 1904. It can be used to calculate the drag force experienced by a body with boundary, such as the wing of an airplane, and has vast applications and substantial impact on engineering and society. Now systems to describe similar phenomena in different physical settings have been derived and widely investigated both in physics and mathematics. The project aims to study the behavior of some physical phenomena modelled by several typical physical systems with boundaries and to explore their intrinsic mechanisms. The potential beneficiaries of the proposal research are some practical applications in engineerings. For example, by some detailed description of the phenomena of some physical quantitities near boundary, one can have better design of equipments with different purpose of applications. In a short term, the study will enrich the mathematical theories. In the long run, we hope some of these studies can reveal some essential structures in these typical physical models so that it can be helpful to establish a strong foundation on boundary layer theories for applications to daily life.

11302120.label: Project Objectives
11302120.value: To design, synthesize, and characterize a series of boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers that are functionalized with a 3-isocyanopropyl group as a removable bioorthogonal component on a self-immolative 2,6-bis(hydroxymethyl)-p-cresol platform. To enhance the therapeutic efficacy, these conjugates will also be linked with an anticancer drug to induce chemotoxicity after controlled release. To study the spectroscopic and photophysical properties of these conjugates in N,N-dimethylformamide and aqueous media. The effects of a range of substituted tetrazines on the restoration of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation of these photosensitizers, as well as the release of the anticancer drugs will also be investigated. To conjugate tetrazines with a monoclonal antibody (e.g. cetuximab) or peptide (e.g. GE11) that can target the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and by using these conjugates to tag EGFR-overexpressed cancer cells (e.g. A431 human epidermoid carcinoma cells and HT29 human colorectal carcinoma cells) with tetrazine moieties. These labeled cells will then be incubated with the activatable BODIPY-based photosensitizers to perform in vitro site-specific [4+1] cycloaddition followed by a cascade of disassembling processes. The activation in intracellular fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species generation will be monitored and compared with suitable controls. The cytotoxicity of these systems under different conditions will also be examined. To perform these bioorthogonal decaging reactions in tumor-bearing nude mice. The in vivo biodistribution and light-induced antitumor efficacy of these bioorthogonally assembled photosensitizing systems will be studied using appropriate controls.

11302120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302120.value: Photodynamic therapy is a promising and minimally invasive therapeutic modality for cancer. It requires a photosensitizer, light of appropriate wavelength, and molecular oxygen to induce a series of photochemical reactions, resulting in generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) to eradicate cancer cells. Over the past decade, there has been considerable interest in exploring effective means for targeted delivery of photosensitizers. Conjugation with tumor-targeting ligands, such as monoclonal antibodies, tumor-homing peptides, and folate is one of the most common strategies. This approach, however, has intrinsic limitations, such as the tedious procedure of bioconjugation and the uncertain expression levels of cellular receptors due to the heterogeneity of cancer cells. The steric hindrance exerted by the photosensitizers may also alter the configuration of and affect the binding with the targeting domains. As another promising approach to confine the photodynamic action at the tumor, activatable photosensitizers have also been actively explored. These smart therapeutic agents are quenched in the native state either by the neighboring quencher or via the self-quenching mechanism. Upon activation by cancer-related stimuli, such as the acidic and thiol-enriched tumor microenvironment and tumor-associated proteases and mRNA, the photoactivities of the photosensitizers are restored. However, certain cleavable linkers have been proven to be unstable in circulation, leading to premature activation of the photosensitizers before being delivered to the desired site. Moreover, the concentration of endogenous stimuli may vary in different types of tumors. To circumvent some of these drawbacks, we plan to utilize bioorthogonal chemistry to achieve tumor targeting, specific activation of photosensitizers, and controlled release of anticancer drugs simultaneously. We will first prepare a series of boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers functionalized with a 3-isocyanopropyl group as a removable bioorthogonal component and an anticancer drug through a self-immolative 2,6-bis(hydroxymethyl)-p-cresol platform. The meso-position of the BODIPYs is caged with an ester group, which can inhibit their fluorescence emission and ROS generation. The 3-isocyanopropyl unit of these conjugates will then be subject to [4+1] cycloaddition with tetrazine moieties which have been tagged on cancer cells through conjugation to tumor-targeting antibodies or peptides. After site-specific ligation and a cascade of disassembling reactions, the photosensitizers will be activated by removing the meso-ester protecting group and the anticancer drugs will be released to induce an additional chemocytotoxic effect. These bioorthogonal decaging reactions leading to specific activation of photosensitizers and controlled release of anticancer drugs will be validated in a range of cancer cells and tumor-bearing nude mice. 光動力學治療(PDT)因其獨特的微創特性成為一種具有發展潛力的新型癌症治療手段。 其治療原理為通過光化學反應產生活性氧物質(ROS),從而起到殺死腫瘤細胞的目的。 因此,光敏劑,光源以及氧氣被稱為光動力學治療三要素。 與傳統的抗腫瘤藥物一樣,光敏劑自身缺乏腫瘤特異性,因此,近幾十年來,有越來越多的研究報導了關於靶向遞送光敏劑的手段和方法。 例如,在光敏劑上連接一些腫瘤特異性配體,像單克隆抗體,腫瘤靶向肽以及葉酸等。 然而,這些方法具有其自身的局限性,如合成過程較為繁瑣,不同腫瘤細胞受體表達類型及程度不盡相同。 除此之外,光敏劑的剛性骨架結構帶來的位阻效應,在一定程度上也會影響配體與受體的結合過程。 腫瘤靶向前葯策略是指將原本具有藥理活性的藥物製備成無活性的前藥化合物,且該前藥能在腫瘤組織中,利用其一定的特異性,如較低的pH,較高的GSH,特有的蛋白酶或是mRNA釋放出原藥。 考慮到腫瘤特異性配體策略的種種缺陷,靶向啟動策略逐漸被應用於光動力學治療的研究中。 但是,靶向啟動策略同樣也存在一些缺陷,其主要包括兩方面。 首先,某些連接鏈在體迴圈中就開始分解,並不能像預期設想的那樣,百分百的到達腫瘤細胞並釋放。 其次,不同腫瘤細胞的"啟動物"濃度並不相同,很難保證對某一腫瘤能產生回應的連接鏈對另一腫瘤也能夠產生回應。 基於此,我們將生物正交手段引入靶向啟動策略中,設計了一種新型的具備腫瘤靶向,特異性啟動,以及選擇性釋放抗腫瘤藥物功能的光敏劑。 首先,我們合成了一系列硼-吡咯二甲基(BODIPY)光敏劑,並將BDP與其他抗腫瘤藥物連接到"自殺式"連接鏈骨架1-(3-異氰基丙基)-4-甲基-2,6-二羥甲基苯酚上。 在該分子中,由於BDP meso位的羧基被酯化的緣故,其產生螢光和ROS的能力將會喪失。 而1位的3異氰基丙基可以與腫瘤特異性靶向的四嗪(Tetrazine)化合物發生4+1環化反應,隨後經過水解,1,3消除,1,4-消除釋放出BDP原藥以及抗腫瘤藥物。因此,我們將會在細胞以及動物水準證實利用生物正交反應來實現光敏劑在腫瘤細胞特異性啟動,釋放,以達到選擇性抗腫瘤目的這一設計的合理性。

11302120.label: Realisation of objectives
11302120.value: This project aims to develop boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers that can be specifically activated in a bioorthogonal manner for precise photodynamic therapy (PDT). Owing to the superior spectroscopic and photophysical properties and ease of chemical modifications, this class of functional dyes have been widely studied as photosensitizers for this application. Recently, it has been reported that by changing the meso substituent from an ester group to a carboxylate moiety, the fluorescence of the BODIPY core can be greatly increased due to their different electronic property, and this “ester-to-carboxylate” effect has been utilized to develop several activatable BODIPY-based photosensitizers. On this basis, we employed a distyryl BODIPY as the photosensitizing unit in our design, of which the absorption and fluorescence emission can extend to the far-red region. In the first project, we caged this photosensitizing unit with a 3-isocyanopropyl group via a self-immolative linker (J. Controlled Release 2023, 353, 663-674). With a meso-ester functionality, this compound labelled as NC-DSBDP was largely quenched in terms of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation. Interestingly, upon interactions with tetrazines, this group could be removed rapidly to release an activated species through a cascade of processes, including [4+1] cycloaddition, expulsion of N2, tautomerization, hydrolysis, followed by beta-elimination. The phenol generated in situ then underwent self-immolation to release a photodynamically active carboxylated distyryl BODIPY (CO2-DSBDP), by which the photosensitizing property of NC-DSBDP could be activated. For the tetrazine component, two targeting moieties were introduced to demonstrate the versatility of this approach. The first one contains a galactose moiety, which can target the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) overexpressed on the surface of hepatoma cells. The second one involves the peptide sequence YHWYGYTPQNVI, labelled as GE11, which shows high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpressed in a wide range of cancer cells. With these functional tetrazine derivatives, labelled as gal-Tz and GE11-Tz, respectively, we performed a detailed study on the bioorthogonal activation of NC-DSBDP toward precise PDT. We first studied the activation effects in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at pH = 7.4 in the presence of dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) (10% v/v), including the restoration of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation of NC-DSBDP upon addition of gal-Tz or GE11-Tz. The decaging kinetics were also studied spectroscopically. The activation through the “ester-to-carboxylate” process was also revealed by confirming the conversion of NC-DSBDP to CO2-DSBDP by high-performance liquid chromatography. In addition, the selectivity of the activation was also studied by monitoring the fluorescence response of NC-DSBDP toward various biological species. The overall results showed that NC-DSBDP was stable and remained largely quenched in this aqueous medium, but its fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation properties could be remarkably and selectively activated upon the reaction with these tetrazine derivatives. The bioorthogonal activation was further demonstrated at the cellular level. For the activation with gal-Tz, the ASGPR-positive HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells and the ASGPR-negative HeLa human cervical carcinoma cells and MCF-7 human breast cancer cells were used. For the activation with GE11-Tz, the EGFR-positive A431 human epidermoid carcinoma cells and HT29 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells and the EGFR-negative HepG2 cells were used. The activation in fluorescence emission was monitored by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, while the activation in photocytotoxicity was examined by MTT assay. In addition, we also examined the subcellular localization of NC-DSBDP after activation with GE11-Tz and the intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation using 2′,7′-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (H2DCFDA) as the probe. The tetrazine-triggered activation of NC-DSBDP was finally investigated in vivo using A431 tumor-bearing nude mice as an animal model. The mice were intravenously injected with NC-DSBDP followed by intratumoral injection with GE11-Tz. For comparison, the mice without receiving the injection of GE11-Tz were also studied. The whole-body fluorescence imaging and ex vivo imaging of the tumors and some major organs were performed using an in vivo imaging system. In addition, the in vivo bioorthogonal activation of the photodynamic activity of NC-DSBDP by GE11-Tz was also investigated using various experimental conditions as controls. The size of the tumor and body weight of the mice were monitored over a period of 14 days. After all these treatments, the tumors and some major organs were harvested and subject to hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining to reveal the treatment efficacy and systemic toxicity. The results were compared with those of various control groups to validate unambiguously that this bioorthogonal activation strategy could be utilized for in vivo targeted PDT. With a view to amplifying the activation effects, an analogous BODIPY dimer linked on a 3-isocyanopropyl-modified 2,6-bis(hydroxymethyl)-p-cresol platform was also synthesized. Unfortunately, upon addition of tetrazine, we found that the fluorescence could only be partially restored and only one activated carboxylated BODIPY unit could be released. Attempts were made to change the self-immolative linker and the BODIPY moieties, but the “click-to-release” process did not proceed smoothly. Hence, we did not pursue further this approach and extend the study to replace one of the BODIPY units with an anticancer drug. In fact, the tetrazine-triggered activation of NC-DSBDP already could achieve a very high antitumor effect. Instead of developing therapeutic agents for dual chemo and photodynamic therapy, we aimed to expand the toolbox of bioorthogonal activation of photosensitizers, using transition metals to promote the decaging and activation processes as this bioorthogonal bond-cleavage chemistry could achieve rapid kinetics and high efficiency, which enable it to be utilized for in vivo applications. While transition metals have been widely used for activation of chemotherapeutic prodrugs, to the best of our knowledge, this strategy has not been reported for activation of photosensitizers for PDT. To this end, we prepared a series of BODIPY-based photosensitizers connected to an allyl group with or without a self-immolative spacer via an ester caging unit at the meso position and studied their activation upon treatment with several ruthenium complexes. To enable targeted activation, a biotin moiety was incorporated in one of these ruthenium complexes (submitted to J. Am. Chem. Soc.). As an extended study, we also used a propargyl group instead of an allyl group as the caging unit and a palladium(II)-incorporated cyclic RGD peptide as the activator (to be submitted to J. Med. Chem.). The decaging efficiency of these systems via Ru-promoted deallylation and Pd-promoted depropargylation, respectively, was first evaluated in PBS at pH = 7.4 with 10% DMSO (v/v) and 0.1% Tween 80 (v/v), which were added to enhance the solubility of the compounds and prevent their self-aggregation, by monitoring the restoration in fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation. The in vitro activation in terms of intracellular fluorescence emission and ROS generation as well as photocytotoxicity was then investigated using a range of cancer cell lines with different expression levels of the corresponding receptors (biotin receptor or αvβ3 integrin) and various controls. The cell death mechanism for the bioorthogonal system involving Ru-promoted deallylation was also studied in detail. Finally, the in vivo activation was demonstrated for both systems using HeLa or 4T1 tumor-bearing nude mice by monitoring the growth in intratumoral fluorescence and inhibition in tumor growth. With all these results, all the objectives set in the proposal are deemed to be fully achieved.

11302120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302120.value: With this funding, we have developed several bioorthogonal strategies for site-specific activation of far-red-absorbing photosensitizers. The first system involves the use of an isonitrile-caged distyryl BODIPY (NC-DSBDP), which can be activated through the “ester-to-carboxylate” transformation initiated by the [4+1] cycloaddition with a tetrazine derivative. By conjugating tetrazine with a tumor-targeting group (gal-Tz and GE11-Tz) and pre-labelling the cancer cells or tumors with these conjugates, it can confine the bioorthogonal activation at the target site. We have demonstrated the activation of NC-DSBDP in terms of fluorescence emission and ROS generation by gal-Tz and GE11-Tz in aqueous media, in a series of cell lines with different expression levels of ASGPR and EGFR, as well as in A431 tumor-bearing nude mice. The results show that the activation is highly specific and efficient, rendering this approach highly promising for precise PDT. This work has been published in J. Controlled Release 2023, 353, 663-674. The second approach involves the use of ruthenium-mediated bioorthogonal deallylation for on-demand activation of BODIPY-based photosensitizers. In this study, we first prepared a series of these photosensitizers connected to an allyl group with or without a self-immolative spacer via an ester caging unit [Pro-BDP-n (n = 1-4)] and studied their activation upon treatment with several ruthenium complexes [RuLn (n = 1-3)]. Pro-BDP-3 having a methoxy substituent at the self-immolative linker was found to exhibit the highest release efficiency and fastest decaging kinetics. Using RuL3 as activator, which was modified with a biotin moiety, Pro-BDP-3 could be selectively activated in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of biotin receptor-overexpressed cancer cells. The induced ER stress disturbed the intracellular calcium homeostasis and ER-mitochondria crosstalk, resulting in mitochondria dysfunction and eventually cell death via apoptosis. The high treatment efficacy of this approach was also demonstrated in vivo. This work has just been submitted to J. Am. Chem. Soc. for publication. Moreover, we have also utilized the highly efficient palladium-promoted depropargylation for spatiotemporal activation of BODIPY-based photosensitizers. Similar to the above study, a series of these photosensitizers substituted with a propargyl caging unit and a palladium(II)-incorporated cyclic RGD peptide were synthesized. The bioorthogonal reaction between these two components led to selective activation in fluorescence emission and ROS generation in PBS solution and in αvβ3-overexpressed cancer cells. The activation was also demonstrated in vivo, resulting in significant tumor regression upon light irradiation and minimal systemic toxicity. The results will soon be submitted to J. Med. Chem. for publication.

11302120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302120.value: Bioorthogonal activation of photosensitizers has emerged as a promising strategy for precise PDT. This study has demonstrated that the “ester-to-carboxylate” transformation is an effective approach for activation of BODIPY-based photosensitizers, and this process can be triggered through the novel [4+1] cycloaddition reaction between isonitrile and tetrazine as well as by transition metal-promoted deallylation and depropargylation reactions. By varying the caging units and the activators, it is expected that the decaging and activation processes could be further accelerated, which can facilitate the in vivo applications. Some other extremely fast click reactions, such as the inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder reaction, can also be used to trigger the decaging. Moreover, tumor-specific moieties, such as antibodies, can also be introduced to the activators to further enhance the specificity of the photodynamic action. This remains as a particular challenge for metal-based activators because of the lack of effective bioconjugation strategies and the potential hindering effect on the catalytic activity. It is envisaged that this highly versatile strategy can also be used to specifically target other biomarkers for other biomedical applications. Hence, the results of this study have provided the ground for further investigation in all these areas.

11302120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302120.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising and minimally invasive treatment modality for cancer. It requires a photosensitizer, light of an appropriate wavelength, and molecular oxygen to produce cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) for eradication of cancer cells and tumor tissues. To improve the treatment outcome, targeted delivery of the photosensitizer to and controlled photosensitization at the tumor site are crucial. To address these challenges, we initiated this project to develop boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers that can be activated in a specific manner. It involved the conjugation of a far-red-absorbing distyryl BODIPY with a 3-isocyanopropyl, allyl, or propargyl group via a self-immolative linker. With a meso ester functionality, these compounds were largely quenched in terms of fluorescence emission and ROS generation. Upon addition of tetrazines, ruthenium complexes, or palladium complexes, the respective caging units could be effectively removed, triggering a cascade of elimination steps to release an activated form of the photosensitizers. By conjugating a tumor-targeting moiety to these activators, the activation occurred preferentially in the target cancer cells and tumors, leading to selective elimination of these malignancies. Through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, we demonstrated that this bioorthogonal activation approach is highly promising toward precise PDT.

11302320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302320.value: Affinity-based proteome profiling (AfBP) has provided powerful tools to study drug and protein interactions in complex proteome. AfBP strategy relies on the usage of photo-cross-linkers to convert the noncovalent interactions between the drug and the protein targets. A major problem associated with the existing photo-cross-linkers is that due to their bulky sizes, the biological activity of the designed probe often decreases. To tackle the problem, we seek to develop novel photo-cross-linkers based on pharmacophore, which is commonly found in drugs and bioactive molecules. This strategy does not require the introduction of an extra photo-cross-linker, thereby maintaining the biological activity of the probe to the maximum extent and facilitating target identification process. By examining the literature, we have identified isoxazoles that can be promising intrinsic photo-cross-linkers for AfBP design. Isoxazoles are commonly found in drugs and bioactive molecules. Numerous compounds with isoxazole rings have shown interesting biological activity including anti-cancer and anti-microbial activity. Our preliminary study has shown that isoxazoles can potentially serve as excellent photo-cross-linkers for AfBP design. We will further synthesize a library of isoxazoles probes and analyze the photo-cross-linking efficiency with various small molecules and proteins to gain a better understanding of how the photo-cross-linking efficiency of isoxazoles will change with different chemical structures. Subsequently we will design an AfBP probe based on Hsp90 inhibitor, AUY922, bearing an isoxazole unit. AUY922 has been found with potent anti-cancer activity. However, during clinical trials with the inhibitor, patients showed various side effects, such as night blindness. To investigate the side effects, we will install an alkyne moiety onto AUY922 and use chemical proteomics approach to decipher the biological target under native cellular environment. Through chemical proteomics study, the off-targets of AUY922 could be identified and help elucidate the side effect of this drug. Such information will aid in further optimizing the structural design of AUY922 analogues and accelerating the drug discovery process. We will also employ the same strategy to investigate the sulfamethoxazole/protein interactions in bacteria cells. Sulfamethoxazole is an antibiotic exhibiting a wide spectrum of antimicrobial activity. However, no systematic study has been conducted to investigate its interactions with bacteria proteomes. Through chemical proteomics analysis, we believe a comprehensive understanding of the sulfamethoxazole/protein interactions can be acquired. The identified protein hits can allow us to uncover new biological targets for antibiotic design. Through the study, we hope to generate useful tools for combating the antibiotic resistance problem prevalent today. 光亲和标记蛋白质组学为研究蛋白质与药物的相互作用提供了强有力的工具，光亲和标记蛋白质组学策略依赖使用光交联基团将药物与靶标蛋白质之间的非共价相互作用转化为共价键。目前使用的光交联基团存在较大问题，例如体积大，这严重影响了基于药物设计的化学探针的生物活性。为解决这一问题，我们致力于开发基于药效基团的新型光交联基团，该药效基团在理想情况下将广泛存在于药物或活性天然产物中。基于该策略，我们不需要引入额外的光交联基团，最大程度保留了探针的生物活性，有利于靶标蛋白的鉴定。通过仔细查阅文献，我们发现异恶唑可作为一类非常有希望的新型内嵌型光交联基团用于光亲和标记蛋白质组学研究。异恶唑被发现存在于诸多药物和活性分子中， 许多含异恶唑结构的化合物显示了抗肿瘤和抗菌活性，我们的初步研究显示异恶唑具有良好的光交联活性，在此基础上，我们将合成一个异恶唑的小分子文库来探究光交联活性与化学结构的具体构效关系。 在第二部分工作中，我们将设计并合成基于Hsp90抑制剂AUY922的化学探针。AUY922含有异恶唑结构，该化合物亦具有优良的抗肿瘤活性，但在临床实验中它也表现了强烈的副作用，如眼盲症等。为研究其副作用，我们将通过化学合成在AUY922中引入一个小基团--炔基，再利用化学蛋白质组学探究该探针在生理环境下的相互作用蛋白。通过这项研究，我们将鉴定出 AUY922的脱靶蛋白，这不仅有助于阐述AUY922在临床试验中的副作用，也为后续优化AUY922衍生物治疗癌症奠定了基础。 接下来，我们也将利用相似策略来研究药物sulfamethoxazole和细菌蛋白质组的相互作用。Sulfamethoxazole是一类具有广谱抗菌能力的抗生素，其化学结构也含有异恶唑，迄今为止仍没有科研团队系统地研究该抗生素与细菌蛋白质组的相互作用。通过化学蛋白组学研究，我们期待获得sulfamethoxazole与细菌蛋白质组相互作用的系统认知，该研究也将有助于鉴定新的靶标蛋白用于新一代抗生素的设计，我们期望为对抗细菌的耐药性发展强有力的化学工具。

11302320.label: Realisation of objectives
11302320.value: All the objectives were accomplished before the completion date. Specifically, we developed isoxazoles as novel photo-cross-linkers for affinity-based proteome profiling. The isoxazole group was shown to generate highly reactive aziridine intermediates upon ultraviolet light irradiation, which subsequently crosslinked with nucleophilic amino acids. Crosslinking site studies revealed that the isoxazole group exhibited superior photocrosslinking activity, particularly with acidic amino acid residues. Furthermore, we synthesized a series of isoxazole-based functional probe molecules and evaluated their photoaffinity labeling efficacy in both purified protein and whole-cells. Notably, probes containing aromatic-substituted isoxazole demonstrated excellent photoaffinity labeling capabilities. This strategy was also applied to investigate the target identification of the drug molecule Luminespib, a potent inhibitor of heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) that has shown significant efficacy in clinical cancer research. However, its potential off-target effects contribute to severe toxic side effects. We constructed the probe isx10, based on the native isoxazole group present in Luminespib, and employed proteomics to identify and validate several endogenous targets, including Hsp90, PTGES2, and NASP. Additionally, we explored the potential targets of Danazol, a molecule containing isoxazole pharmacophores, and conducted a detailed investigation into the role of isoxazole groups in the development of light-activated drugs. These findings advance the understanding and application of isoxazole-based tools in chemical biology and drug discovery.

11302320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302320.value: This study introduces isoxazole as a novel native photo-cross-linker for photoaffinity labeling and chemoproteomics, addressing the limitations of reduced bioactivity often associated with traditional photo-cross-linkers. By leveraging the unique properties of isoxazole, we demonstrated its efficiency in forming covalent bonds with amino acids, peptides, and proteins, providing an effective method to minimally perturb drug structures in chemoproteomic applications. Isoxazole-based probes were successfully utilized in chemoproteomic studies of drugs such as Danazol and Luminespib. These investigations revealed potential cellular targets and provided insights into drug mechanisms. Furthermore, the study explored UV-triggered covalent inhibition strategies, expanding the scope of isoxazole-based drugs in cancer therapy and diagnostics. These findings significantly enhance the chemical toolbox available for drug discovery and proteomics, underscoring the potential to drive the development of advanced therapeutic and diagnostic technologies.

11302320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302320.value: The research on isoxazole-based photo-cross-linkers opens for several avenues of future development. These include expanding the chemical toolbox with other photoreactive pharmacophores and optimizing isoxazole derivatives for diverse applications in drug discovery and diagnostics. Future efforts could focus on employing proteomics strategies to identify unknown drug targets and developing UV-activated covalent inhibitors. Moreover, isoxazole-based imaging probes hold significant potential for achieving high specificity and sensitivity in detecting biomarkers, particularly for cancer and infectious diseases.

This isoxazole-based photo-cross-linking strategy has been successfully applied to investigate biological targets of various drugs in living cells. The newly developed photo-cross-linking group provides a valuable addition to the toolkit for chemical proteomics studies.

11302820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302820.value: 本項目旨在開發發光無機和有機過渡金屬絡合物交聯劑，並將其應用於生物偶聯、成像、光激活治療及生物材料的製備。由於交聯所得產物有助於了解生物過程、設計醫療診斷工具及開發新藥物，因此，探究生物分子與其他生物分子、合成聚合物、成像探針及藥物分子的交聯擁有高度重要性。在標記時才開啟螢光特性的交聯劑極具吸引力，因為它們無需洗滌步驟也可以用於體內標記和即時成像。但是，由於迄今為止幾乎所有已報導的交聯劑都是螢光有機染料衍生物，所以其發光本質是螢光，且應用大都局限於螢光成像。在過去十年，因為發光過渡金屬絡合物具有良好的光物理和光化學特性，例如：長發光壽命，高光穩定性，雙光子誘導發光以及單線態氧的有效光敏化，所以人們對它們的生物成像和光激活治療應用越來越感興趣。我們相信，過渡金屬絡合物有趣的光物理和光化學性質和生物正交標記相關特異性的結合將可產生新一代的創新交聯劑。在本項目中，我們將利用過渡金屬絡合物設計具有磷光開啟性質的均雙功能和異雙功能交聯劑。我們將利用兩個同時擁有生物正交反應性的相同或不同的發光猝滅基團來修飾過渡金屬絡合物。猝滅基團將會在反應中消失，這不僅令交聯產物表現出極具吸引力的光物理性能，而且使其擁有有效的單線態氧光敏能力，從而具有可控的光細胞毒性。在本項目中研發的交聯劑將用於：（1）通過在肽序列上交聯兩個具有反應功能的基團來鑒定新型肽標籤；（2）利用其富特異性和磷光開啟性的蛋白質分子交聯來檢測蛋白質—蛋白質的相互作用；（3）使用經以下基團修飾的多臂聚乙二醇衍生物來製備響應性生物材料：（a）反應性官能團，（b）對刺激敏感的活潑銜接基團，（c）腫瘤靶向分子，及（d）發光猝滅基團。在本項目中開發的新型交聯劑不僅令被肽標記的蛋白質、相互作用中的蛋白質—蛋白質對和生物材料具有發光特性，而且使其擁有單線態氧光敏化功能；此性能並不能通過現有的有機交聯劑來實現。

11302820.label: Realisation of objectives
11302820.value: All the project objectives have been achieved, as illustrated by the following results. We have demonstrated the specific labeling of endogenous proteins in live cells by utilizing their substrates as a crosslinking unit. A series of iridium(III) tetrazine complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-Tz-Ph)](PF6) (HN^C = Hdfppy, Hppy, Hpq, and Hpqe) has been designed as bioorthogonal labels for protein substrates appended with a strained alkyne. The complexes are weakly emissive in fluid solutions due to efficient quenching by the tetrazine unit. However, the addition of a strained alkyne BCN-OH to the solutions results in significant emission enhancement and strong singlet oxygen (1O2) photosensitization due to the conversion of the tetrazine unit into its non-quenching pyrimidine derivative after the inverse electron-demand Diels–Alder (IEDDA) cycloaddition reaction. The ppy complex has been applied to label HaloTag protein expressed in human cervical carcinoma HeLa cells. When cells are incubated with a BCN-modified substrate BCN-C6-Cl and subsequently the complex, strong emission signals originated from labeled HaloTag protein are observed in the cytoplasm. The labeled protein retains the complex in cells to a high extent, leading to strong cytotoxicity upon photoirradiation. We have developed monochromophoric iridium(III) bis-tetrazine complexes [Ir(dptz)2(N^N)](Cl) (N^N = en, Ph2-phen, and biq) for fabricating polymers as new platforms for cargo delivery and cell imaging. The complexes consist of two tetrazine moieties that serve as emission quenchers and crosslinking units for cyclooctynylated derivatives. The direct coordination of the tetrazine units to the iridium(III) center leads to high reactivity and significant emission enhancement upon the IEDDA reaction of the complexes with a bis-cyclooctynylated derivative, bis-BCN. Impressively, the fast reaction kinetics enable the complexes to react selectively with bis-BCN over its mono-cyclooctynylated counterpart mono-BCN in a cross-labeling study. A multi-arm poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) containing four BCN units has been functionalized by the Ph2-phen complex to afford a luminescent nanosized iridium(III) hydrogel. When HeLa cells are incubated with the hydrogel encapsulating BODIPY dyes, the emission signals of the iridium(III) hydrogel and BODIPY dyes are colocalized in the lysosomes, confirming the efficient lysosomal accumulation and cargo delivery properties of the resulting hydrogel. We have designed rhenium(I) carbamate–tetrazine complex [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-Tz-NHBoc)](CF3SO3) (N^N = phen, Me4-phen, and Ph2-phen) as bioorthogonal photosensitizers to control the induction of immunogenic cell death (ICD). ICD involves the release of tumor-associated antigens and their subsequent presentation to immune effector cells, effectively inhibiting tumor growth and recurrence. The carbamate–tetrazine moiety plays three roles: (1) an emission quencher, (2) a cytotoxicity regulator, and (3) a labile crosslinking unit between the metal complex core and a PEG pendant. When the PEG-modified complex reacts with a strained cycloalkene TCO-OH, the carbamate group undergoes 1,4-elimination to release a highly cytotoxic metal complex core, a rhenium(I) aminomethylpyridine derivative. This complex is also a highly efficient 1O2 photosensitizer. Further photoirradiation of live cells after treatment with the complex and TCO-OH leads to a cascade of cellular events, including lysosomal dysfunction, autophagy suppression, and ICD. We have developed a concerted strategy of enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) and bioorthogonal chemistry to effectively accumulate bioorthogonal functionality in live cancer cells. Ruthenium(II) tetrazine complexes [Ru(N^N)2(py-Tz-Ph)](Cl)2 (N^N = bpy, Ph2-phen, and biq) and a BCN-modified EISA-active peptide, FFBCN, have been designed. Alkaline phosphatase, which is overexpressed in many cancerous cells, catalyzes the removal of the phosphate group of FFBCN and allows their self-assembly via π–π and hydrophobic interactions to form larger supramolecular assemblies. Hence, the BCN moieties are accumulated in cancer cells, providing a high number of bioorthogonal functional groups to react with the ruthenium(II) tetrazine complexes to modulate their phosphorescence and 1O2 photosensitization. The accumulation of the assemblies has been achieved in both intra- and extracellular regions, and higher photocytotoxicity is found in intracellular regions due to the closer proximity of photogenerated 1O2 with subcellular organelles. We have utilized peptides as a crosslinking unit between transition metal complexes and functional moieties to construct photofunctional conjugates for bioimaging and photodynamic therapy (PDT). Three rhenium(I) perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-PFBP)](CF3SO3) (N^N = phen, Me4phen, and Ph2phen) have been developed for the fabrication of peptides incorporating the π-clamp sequence (FCPF). The complexes are conjugated with the cysteine residue of the π-clamp sequence in a rapid and specific manner to afford luminescent peptide conjugates with efficient 1O2 photosensitization. The Ph2phen complex has been modified with organelle-targeting sequences, and the resulting peptide conjugates act as imaging reagents for various subcellular components such as mitochondria and lysosomes, and PDT agents as well. Additionally, a caspase-3/7 cleavable sequence (DEVD-FCPF) has been designed as a crosslinking unit between the Ph2phen complex and the emission quencher QSY-7. Caspase-3/7 specifically cleaves the DEVD sequence in the conjugate and separates the complex from QSY-7, leading to emission enhancement, which signals the activation and intracellular activity of caspase-3/7 during cell apoptosis. We have designed three iridium(III) methylsulfone complexes [Ir(bpz)2(N^N)](PF6) (N^N = bpy-btz, bpy-mstp, and bpy-odz) to functionalize cysteine-bearing peptides and proteins for bioimaging and photocytotoxic applications. As the near-infrared (NIR)-emitting mstp complex features high reactivity and selectivity toward the cysteine residue in peptides and proteins, it allows the rapid preparation of luminescent bioconjugates targeting different organelles such as mitochondria, lysosomes, and plasma membranes. These new bioconjugates display negligible cytotoxicity in the dark but become significantly photocytotoxic toward cancerous cells. We have developed four rhenium(I) 2,4-dinitrophenylsulfonamide (DNPS) complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-DNPS)](CF3SO3) (N^N = bpy-tosylamide, Me4-phen, Ph2-phen, and phen) as imaging reagents and photocytotoxic agents. These complexes are weakly emissive due to photoinduced electron transfer from the excited rhenium(I) diimine moiety to the DNPS unit. Upon reaction with glutathione (GSH), the DNPS moiety is degraded, resulting in emission turn-on and significant photosensitization efficiency of the complexes. When HeLa cells are incubated with the complexes, intense intracellular emission and potent photocytotoxicity are both observed. We have explored polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (POSS) as novel crosslinked hybrids with transition metal complexes. POSS are nanosized, cage-like molecules that are highly symmetric and easy to modify. Cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine complexes have been conjugated with POSS to afford three crosslinked hybrids [Ir(N^C)2(L1-POSS)]. These neutral and lipophilic hybrids exhibit efficient accumulation in lipid droplets in live HeLa cells. They display much higher photostability than commercial lipid dyes, allowing prolonged imaging studies of the droplets. Interestingly, when a linker is installed between the metal complex core and the POSS unit, the cellular localization of the resulting crosslinked hybrids can be fine-tuned; for example, the addition of a pyridinium moiety confers a positive charge to the hybrid and redirects it to the lysosomes after cellular uptake. In summary, we have designed transition metal complexes featuring bioorthogonal or bioconjugation functional groups that show fast reaction kinetics, significant emission enhancement, and high photosensitization efficiencies. Additionally, their reactions with different molecular entities such as peptides, proteins, and polymers, have afforded crosslinked products with intriguing photophysical and photochemical behavior. These crosslinked products have great potential to serve as novel diagnostic and therapeutic tools.
