11302820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302820.value: Iridium(III) tetrazine complexes have been designed as bioorthogonal probes for protein substrates appended with a strained alkyne. The complexes are weakly emissive due to efficient quenching by the tetrazine unit. However, their reaction with strained alkynes results in significant emission enhancement and efficient singlet oxygen photosensitization. One of the complexes has been applied to label and visualize HaloTag proteins expressed in live HeLa cells. The labeled protein retains the complex in cells, leading to strong cytotoxicity upon photoirradiation. Monochromophoric iridium(III) bis-tetrazine complexes have been utilized in the fabrication of polymers for cell imaging and cargo delivery. The two tetrazine moieties of the complexes act as both emission quenchers and crosslinking units. An iridium(III) hydrogel has been prepared by the reaction between one of the complexes and a multi-arm poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) containing four BCN units. The resulting hydrogel displays significant phosphorescence and efficient encapsulation of BODIPY dyes, which are delivered to the lysosomes of HeLa cells. Rhenium(I) carbamate–tetrazine complexes have been developed to control the photoinduction of immunogenic cell death (ICD). The carbamate–tetrazine moiety serves as a quencher, a cytotoxicity regulator, and a labile crosslinker between the metal complex core and a PEG pendant. Upon reaction with a strained cycloalkene, the 1,4-elimination releases the metal core as a highly photocytotoxic aminomethylpyridine derivative from the PEG pendant. Photoirradiation of live cells after treatment with the complex and TCO-OH leads to a cascade of cellular events, including lysosomal dysfunction, autophagy suppression, and ICD. We have utilized peptides as a crosslinking unit between transition metal complexes and functional moieties to construct photofunctional conjugates. Rhenium(I) perfluorobiphenyl complexes have been developed to fabricate peptides containing π-clamp sequence (FCPF). Organelle-targeting peptide conjugates, which serve as imaging reagents and PDT agents, have been developed. A caspase-3/7 cleavable sequence has been utilized to crosslink one of the complexes and an emission quencher QSY-7. The activity of the enzymes can be monitored by the resulting conjugate. Additionally, iridium(III) methylsulfone complexes have been designed to functionalize cysteine-bearing peptides and proteins as photofunctional bioconjugates. Furthermore, rhenium(I) 2,4-dinitrophenylsulfonamide complexes have been utilized to detect biothiols in live cancer cells. We have modified transition metal complexes with polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (POSS) to afford crosslinked hybrids. Iridium(III) POSS crosslinked hybrids have been found to accumulate in lipid droplets in HeLa cells. The intracellular localization of these hybrids can be tuned by incorporating different linkers between the complex core and the POSS unit.

11302820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302820.value: We have successfully developed crosslinkers using transition metal complexes to create photofunctional products for various applications such as bioconjugation, imaging, photoactivated therapy, and biomaterial fabrication. Our research has revealed that the intriguing photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes can be easily adjusted by incorporating bioorthogonal groups and reacting them with complementary partners. This enables us to design versatile crosslinking units in transition metal complexes that can specifically target biological molecules or polymers. The crosslinked and fabricated products have been successfully utilized in bioimaging of organelles, sensing enzyme activities, and photoactivated therapy. Moving forward, we believe that the performance of transition metal complexes in in vivo studies of animal models can be further improved by developing complexes with stronger two-photon absorption and emission at longer wavelengths. Additionally, while most of the reported complexes and crosslinked products have focused on visualizing intracellular targets such as organelles and enzymes, we envision expanding the scope of these studies to include cell-cell interactions. This can be achieved by modifying the complexes with other biomolecules like receptors on plasma membranes, collagen, and enzymes expressed in the extracellular matrix. Exploring these less explored areas will broaden our understanding of cell-cell interactions and their implications.

11302820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302820.value: The objective of this project is to develop photofunctional transition metal complexes that can serve as crosslinkers for various applications, such as bioconjugation, imaging, photodynamic therapy, and biomaterial fabrication. Crosslinked products of biological molecules have proven to be valuable in studying biological processes, designing diagnostic tools, and developing pharmaceuticals. Crosslinkers, especially those with fluorogenic properties, have enabled real-time imaging and in vivo tagging. However, these crosslinkers are typically derived from organic dyes, which limits their usefulness in fluorescence imaging. In recent years, the photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes have gained attention in the field of bioimaging and phototherapy. In this project, we have successfully developed transition metal complexes as crosslinkers that exhibit phosphorogenic responses, resulting in photofunctional conjugates. These complexes are initially non-emissive due to the presence of a quenching moiety with bioorthogonal activity. However, when they react with complementary groups, they undergo emission enhancement, lifetime extension, and singlet oxygen photosensitization. These complexes and conjugates have been utilized for cell imaging, monitoring enzyme activity, and delivering cargo. Additionally, they have shown promise in phototherapeutic applications. We believe that crosslinkers based on transition metal complexes will significantly expand the range of applications for crosslinked products in biomedical research.

11302920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302920.value: Hydrogel-elastomer hybrid has drawn intensive research and development interests in recent years for its rapidly growing applications. Meanwhile, hydrogel and elastomer have significantly dissimilar physical and chemical properties such that they intended to repel and detach from each other by nature, especially when subjected to mechanical loads. Separation resistance to mechanical loads of most of the current hydrogel-elastomer hybrids is far from satisfactory, which hinders the utilization of hydrogel-elastomer hybrids in many of the next generation applications. PI’s team has invented a new method to connect hydrogel and elastomer into hybrid structure. The method is purely physical and therefore chemical hazard minimized and not depending on the chemical properties of hydrogel and elastomers. More importantly, the new method was able to enhance separation resistance of the hydrogel-elastomer for several times when comparing to the conventional method. Yet, this method involves fabrication of a 3D knot-like physical interphase whose deformation and fracture behaviors are complicated. Although PI’s preliminary work has demonstrated the effectiveness of the new method, in-depth understanding on the deformation and fracture mechanisms of the knot-like physical interphase and their impact on enhancing separation resistance of hydrogel-elastomer hybrid are imperative to be obtained. Following research tasks will be carried out by this project in the goal of gaining interactive design guidance of a separation resistant hydrogel-elastomer hybrid knotted by a novel physical interphase. Firstly, hierarchical finite element analysis (FEA) models will be constructed to simulate deformation and fracture behaviors of physically knotted hydrogel-elastomer hybrid, and validated by comparing with experimental results. Secondly, validated FEA models will be utilized to optimize architecture of knot-like physical interphase in the goal of maximizing separation resistance of the hybrid. Thirdly, optimal design achieved through FEA will be examined by fabrication and mechanical tests. This task can provide feedback to the FEA guided design. In summary, this project will conduct comprehensive research that combines computational simulation, 3D printing facilitated materials fabrication and mechanical testing. The long-term goal is to establish a mechanistically determined, computation/modeling guided and experimentally validated framework which can guide the design of next generation failure resistant hybrid structures. 近年來，水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的應用迅速增長。這使得與其相關的研究和開發也被廣泛關註。水凝膠和彈性體的物理和化學性質具有顯著差異。兩種材料自然地互相排斥和分離，被力學加載時尤甚。目前大多數水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構在力學載荷下的分離阻力遠不能令人滿意。這阻礙了水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的進一步發展。 本項目負責人的團隊發明了一種以純物理方法連接水凝膠和彈性體，使其成為雜化結構的新方法。新方法與水凝膠和彈性體的化學性質無關，可將化學危害降至最低。更重要的是，新方法能夠將水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的抗分離性能提升至以傳統化學方法聯接的水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的數倍以上。然而，新方法所涉及的類結狀三維純物理界面結構的形變和斷裂機理都非常復雜。本項目團隊的前期工作只是通過制備和力學實驗證明了新方法的有效性。若想將此新方法的研發推向下一階段，仍需大量工作來深度解析類結狀純物理三維界面結構的形變和斷裂機理及其對提高水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的抗分離性能的影響。 本項目擬進行以下研究工作，以期為以新型類結狀純物理三維界面結構提升水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構抗分離性能的交互式設計提供指引。首先，構建多層級有限元分析模型以模擬類結狀純物理三維界面結構的變形和斷裂行為並與前期工作已獲得的實驗結果進行比較和驗證。其次，利用驗證過的有限元模型對類結狀純物理三維界面結構進行優化設計。設計目標是最大限度地提高水凝膠-彈性體雜化結構的分離阻力。第三，制備有限元分析獲得的最優方案並進行力學測試。此任務可為有限元指導下的優化設計提供反饋。綜上所述，本項目將進行計算機模擬、三維打印輔助的材料和結構制備、以及力學測試。長期目標是建立一個以計算/建模為指導、以實驗為驗證方法的研究框架，來指導新一代抗失效雜交結構的設計。

11303320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303320.value: Drug resistance remains one of the biggest challenges in the clinical application of chemotherapeutic drugs and it is a primary cause of treatment failure. Additionally, systematic toxicity is another obstacle from conventional small-molecule anticancer drugs. Novel anticancer agents utilizing unique mechanisms of action are in high demand, as such agents have the potential to overcome drug resistance. Recently, we have made significant progress in the development of controllably activated platinum-based anticancer prodrugs, with the aim of reducing the toxicity associated with the conventional platinum drugs that are extensively used in the clinic. Our preliminary study indicates that we have successfully obtained a photocaged platinum prodrug that can accumulate efficiently in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of cancer cells. Upon irradiation with near-infrared light, the photocage is activated via two-photon activation, releasing the original platinum drug to exert its cytotoxic effects, and the cell death mode is different than that from the original drug. This prodrug is significantly effective in platinum-refractory human cancer cells. Based on our preliminary data, we plan to design and synthesize several photocaged and ER-targeting platinum prodrugs. The stability of the prodrugs under physiological conditions and their photoactivation properties will be investigated. After confirming the subcellular localization of the synthetic complexes, their photocytotoxicity will be assessed, particularly in platinum-resistant cells including cancer stem cells. We will further investigate their possible mechanisms of action in cancer cells, including their ability to trigger immune response. In vivo evaluation of the prodrugs will also be carried out. The project will generate several new platinum-based anticancer agents targeting the ER, an emerging anticancer drug target. These new complexes are likely to utilize a distinct mode of action to kill cancer cells and thus, conquer drug resistance. A greater understanding of these compounds’ mechanism of action may also shed light on the contribution of the ER to the cytotoxicity of the original platinum-based drugs. 傳統小分子化療藥物由於在人體內的活化過程不可控，會導致多種毒副作用，進而嚴重製約化療的治療效果。開發和傳統化療藥物作用機理不同並且活化可控的新型抗腫瘤藥物，對於攻克腫瘤細胞耐藥性，提高腫瘤治療效果具有非常重要的意義。我們課題組近期在構建活化可控的鉑類抗腫瘤前藥方面取得了顯著的進展，所獲得的前藥有望在降低臨床鉑類藥物的毒副作用的同時，提高藥物的抗腫瘤活性。初步研究結果表明，我們所合成的光籠型鉑類前藥有效地富集在腫瘤細胞的內質網，並且能夠在非光照的條件下保持穩定。在低劑量的近紅外光照射下，該光籠型鉑類前藥能夠以雙光子激發的方式被還原為臨床鉑類藥物，進而消滅腫瘤細胞。雖然該前藥光照活化後的產物為臨床鉑類藥物，其導致的細胞死亡方式卻與臨床鉑類藥物截然不同。在此研究基礎上，我們計劃合成一系列光籠型、靶向內質網的鉑類前藥，並研究其在生理環境下的穩定性以及光激活特性。隨後，我們將檢測前藥在腫瘤細胞內的分佈，以及前藥對不同腫瘤細胞系，特別是包括腫瘤幹細胞在內的腫瘤耐藥細胞的光照抗腫瘤活性。在此基礎上，我們將進一步分析前藥的作用機理，包括研究前藥引起腫瘤細胞死亡的信號通路以及前藥能否激活免疫系統響應等。此外，我們還將構建動物模型進一步評估前藥的抗腫瘤效果。該項目將構建一系列能夠靶向腫瘤細胞內質網，且活化可控的鉑類前藥。通過研究該類前藥的作用機理，有助於更進一步揭示內質網在鉑類藥物作用機理中的重要作用，豐富我們對鉑類藥物作用機理的認識，進而為後續開發高效低毒的新一代抗腫瘤藥物提供科學依據。

11303320.label: Realisation of objectives
11303320.value: Objective 1: Design, synthesis, and characterization of ER-targeting Pt(IV) prodrugs Two clinical platinum-based anticancer drugs, carboplatin and oxaliplatin, were used as parent compounds to develop Pt(IV) prodrugs. A coumarin derivative was employed as the photo-caging group and conjugated at the axial position of the Pt(IV) prodrugs. Another axial ligand, 5,6-Dimethylxanthenone-4-acetic acid (DMXAA), was also conjugated. The resulting complexes, 5a and 5b, were fully characterized using ESI-MS, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, 195Pt NMR, and HPLC. Both complexes could be photo-reduced by 880 nm laser irradiation via two-photon excitation. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting ability of the complexes was examined in cell-based models. Complexes 5a and 5b specifically accumulated in the ER region of cancer cells, with their fluorescence colocalizing well with that of an ER tracker. The Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) value was higher than 0.9, indicating excellent ER targeting ability. Objective 2: In vitro evaluation and mechanistic study of the prodrugs We initially used the SRB assay to evaluate the anticancer activity of complexes 5a and 5b against various cancer cell lines. Carboplatin, oxaliplatin, and the photoactivation ligand served as controls. The lung fibroblast cell line MRC5 was used to assess the dark toxicity of the tested complexes in normal cells. Both complexes 5a and 5b were found to be nontoxic under dark conditions, with IC50 values exceeding their maximum solubility concentrations. Upon activation with 880 nm NIR light, the photocytotoxicity of both complexes dramatically increased, showing enhancements of up to more than 38.5-fold. Compared to their corresponding Pt(II) drugs, the photoactivated forms of 5a and 5b exhibited up to a 461-fold increase in cytotoxicity in the tested cell lines. Importantly, we discovered that complexes 5a and 5b maintained their photocytotoxicity even under hypoxic conditions, a major limitation for conventional photodynamic therapy (PDT), suggesting that these complexes can eliminate cancer cells in an oxygen-independent manner. The mechanism of action of coumaplatin was investigated. Both complexes accumulated in the ER region, and upon photoactivation, they robustly damaged ER-resident biomolecules (e.g., proteins and lipids), inducing intense ER stress and disrupting the intracellular redox balance. Notably, we observed that activation of complexes 5a and 5b also led to a decrease in intracellular pH, which synergistically contributed to cancer cell death. Unlike carboplatin and oxaliplatin, 5a and 5b do not bind to nuclear DNA nor induce DNA damage, effectively overcoming the resistance of cancer cells to platinum drugs. Additionally, we found that complexes 5a and 5b could effectively induce immunogenic cell death (ICD), further activating T cell proliferation and activation. Objective 3: In vivo evaluation of the prodrugs The in vivo evaluation of complex 5a was conducted in a tumor-bearing mouse model. Initially, we examined the tumor accumulation of 5a following administration. Major organs, including the heart, liver, lungs, spleen, kidneys, and tumor, were collected at various time points after intravenous administration of the complexes. The concentration of complex 5a in the tumor reached its peak level 4 hours post-injection; therefore, this time point was selected for irradiation. Compared with mice treated with PBS, the tumor volume and weight in the group treated with photoactivated 5a decreased by 89 ± 8% and 76 ± 4%, respectively. More importantly, photoactivated 5a successfully inhibited tumor metastasis and activated the immune system, further highlighting its potential for development. Throughout the treatment, no significant body weight loss or damage to major organs was observed in the 5a-treated groups, indicating the safety of 5a. In conclusion, we successfully developed photoactivatable and ER-targeted Pt(IV) prodrugs, which not only exhibit high anticancer potential but also effectively activate the immune system. By investigating the mechanism, we provide a novel strategy to enhance the anticancer activity of platinum-based drugs.

11303320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303320.value: Platinum-based drugs are widely used in chemotherapy, but they face challenges such as drug resistance and severe side effects. To address these issues, we've developed a novel approach using photoactivatable platinum prodrugs that target the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of cancer cells instead of DNA. Traditional platinum drugs primarily damage DNA, which cancer cells can repair, leading to resistance. Our new prodrugs, activated by near-infrared (NIR) light, specifically target the ER, damaging its biomolecules and decreasing intracellular pH. This mechanism helps overcome drug resistance and triggers immunogenic cell death (ICD), activating an immune response against cancer cells. In animal studies, our prodrug effectively inhibited tumor growth and metastasis while showing minimal toxicity. This research opens up new possibilities for developing next-generation platinum anticancer complexes and highlights the ER as a promising target for future cancer treatments. Our approach offers a strategy to create more effective and less toxic cancer therapies that can potentially overcome the limitations of current platinum-based drugs.

11303320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303320.value: Our research has shown that near-infrared (NIR) light-activated platinum prodrugs targeting the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) have potential for future cancer treatment. However, we need to address several challenges: 1. Improving photoactivation efficiency; 2. Using longer wavelengths of light for better tissue penetration; 3. Enhancing tumor-targeting ability; Our next steps include: 1. Developing prodrugs with higher photoactivation efficiency to boost anticancer effectiveness; 2. Exploring longer excitation wavelengths to increase tissue penetration depth; 3. Improving tumor-targeting capabilities to minimize side effects. After these improvements, we'll select the most promising prodrugs for pre-clinical testing and further development.

11303320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303320.value: Platinum-based cancer drugs are common but have drawbacks like drug resistance and side effects. Therefore, better alternatives are highly desired. Instead of targeting DNA like traditional drugs, new "prodrugs" are being developed that target a different part of cancer cells called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). These prodrugs are activated by near-infrared light and work by damaging proteins in the ER and inducing acidosis of cancer cells. This approach helps overcome drug resistance and triggers the immune system to against cancer. In animal tests, these prodrugs effectively inhibited tumor growth and spread, with minimal side effects. This research opens up new possibilities for developing new platinum-based anticancer drugs that target the ER instead of DNA.

11303720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303720.value: 氣溶膠污染對空氣質量和氣候具有負面影響。而有機氣溶膠是亞微米級氣溶膠中普遍存在的組成部分。大氣凝聚相水（如氣溶膠水、雲水）在有機氣溶膠的形成和氧化過程中起着越來越重要的作用。水溶性有機氣體分配到凝聚相，並在其中進行液相反應，形成液態二次有機氣溶膠。液滴和氣溶膠中吸光有機物的光解可產生液相光氧化劑（如1O2、OH自由基），這些光氧化劑可以快速氧化液態有機氣溶膠。氣溶膠水改變氣溶膠的相態和粘度，這將影響非均相反應速率和液態有機氣溶膠的氧化途徑。研究表明，大氣模型不能捕捉到有機氣溶膠的環境觀測值的一個主要原因是我們對液態複合相有機氣溶膠化學反應的認識不足。 本研究旨在爲潮溼城市環境中形成和氧化有機氣溶膠的液態複合相化學反應提供新的科學認識。首先，我們將研究人爲源水溶性有機氣體及其形成液態二次有機氣溶膠的液相反應。水溶性有機氣體將在香港的一個城市工地用噴霧室裝置從周圍空氣收集到去離子水中。利用這些水樣進行模擬大氣雲水中液態二次有機氣溶膠形成反應的液態光氧化實驗。我們將使用不同的分析技術（例如，液相色譜-質譜法、離子色譜法）來識別和量化這些液態樣品中的主要成分。這些成分將用於闡明所收集的水溶性有機氣體、氧化產物和形成液態二次有機氣溶膠的液相反應機理。第二，我們將測量一個位於香港的城市採樣點的液態氣溶膠樣品，分析這些氣溶膠樣品的光解所形成的不同液相光氧化劑。我們將描述其光吸收特性，並量化環境液態氣溶膠樣品中光解形成的液相1O2和OH的濃度。第三，通過對環境氣溶膠樣品和實驗室生成的模擬有機氣溶膠進行系統的實驗室氧化實驗，研究人爲源無機氣相污染物NOx和SO2對液態有機氣溶膠非均相氧化的影響。這項提案的成功實施將填補潮溼城市環境中有機氣溶膠液態複合相化學反應的關鍵認識空白。所提出研究的成果包括測量反應速率常數，反應動力學機理，反應壽命和反應機制。在潮溼的亞熱帶城市（如香港），這些數據是制定空氣質量政策所用大氣模型的有用輸入數據。

11303720.label: Realisation of objectives
11303720.value: The goal of objective 1 was to characterize the composition and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases, and elucidate their aqueous-phase photooxidation reactions that form aqueous secondary organic aerosols in Hong Kong. We chose to conduct our field sampling study in December/January (Winter) and June/July (Summer) in order to investigate how seasonality influences the composition and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases. The field sampling study was conducted in urban Kowloon Tong. Using several mist chambers, ambient mixtures of water-soluble gases were scrubbed from the atmosphere into ultrapure water. Ultrahigh performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was then used to analyze the aqueous mixtures collected to characterize the composition and concentrations of the scrubbed ambient water-soluble organic gases. Additionally, we performed a series of aqueous direct photolysis and hydroxyl (OH) radical photooxidation experiments with the collected aqueous mixtures to elucidate the aqueous-phase photooxidation reactions that form and transform aqueous secondary organic aerosols. The organic compositions of the collected aqueous mixtures were highly complex, with hundreds of identified organic compounds. Some of the identified organic compounds could be characterized as multi-functional phenolic compounds, green leaf volatiles, and organic acids, which are known to be water soluble. The winter samples had a higher number of detected organic compounds than the summer samples, suggesting that more water-soluble organic gases are present in the air in the winter. Clean marine air masses are transported from southwestern sea areas to Hong Kong in the summer, whereas polluted air masses are transported from northern continental areas to Hong Kong in mid-fall and winter. This suggested that a significant fraction of the water-soluble organic gases in Hong Kong in winter likely originated from continental areas north of Hong Kong. Additionally, it was likely that a large fraction of the water-soluble organic gases in Hong Kong in summer originate from local sources. Aqueous OH photooxidation led to rapid depletion of many organic compounds (e.g., phenolic compounds, green leaf volatiles) and the formation of others (e.g., organic acids). The significance of this work is that it enabled us to gain a better understanding on the composition and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases in humid urban Hong Kong and their propensity to form aqueous secondary organic aerosols. Our findings can be applied to other urban locations within the Greater Bay Area (GBA) which share similar seasonal air quality characteristics as Hong Kong. The goal of objective 2 was to quantify the formation rates and concentrations of different aqueous-phase photooxidants produced from the photolysis of light absorbing organic compounds (aka brown carbon (BrC)) in PM2.5 in Hong Kong, with a focus on how seasonality and location influenced the production of two aqueous-phase photooxidants, singlet oxygen (1O2*), and reactive organic triplet excited states (3C*). We quantified the production of 3C* and 1O2* in illuminated aqueous extracts of PM2.5 collected in different seasons at two urban sites (Tsuen Wan and Kowloon Tong) and one coastal semi-rural site (Hok Tsui) during a year-round study conducted in Hong Kong. Variations in the water-soluble organic compounds (WSOC) concentrations and light absorption properties of water-soluble BrC in the PM2.5 extracts across the three sites were found to be statistically insignificant. In contrast, variations in the WSOC concentrations and light absorption properties of water-soluble BrC across the four seasons were significant. Higher concentrations of WSOC and more light-absorbing water-soluble BrC were present in the PM2.5 during the fall and winter months. This could be attributed to monsoon-influenced seasonal variations in long-range air mass transport to Hong Kong. We found that both 3C* and 1O2* were produced year-round. The steady-state concentrations of 1O2* in the illuminated aqueous extracts were nearly 2 orders of magnitude higher than the steady-state concentrations of 3C*. The quantum yields of 3C* and 1O2* also spanned wide ranges across the samples, with a range of 1.19 to 13.74 % for 1O2* and a range of 0.05 to 3.24 % for 3C*. The [1O2*]ss and [3C*]ss correlated with the concentration and absorbance of BrC, thus implying that the amount of BrC drives the steady-state concentrations of these photooxidants. The locations (urban vs. semi-rural) did not have a significant effect on [1O2*]ss and [3C*]ss, which indicated that BrC from local sources did not have a significant influence on the year-round 3C* and 1O2* production. 3C and 1O2* productions were found to be the highest in winter and the lowest in summer for all three sites. The observed seasonal trends of 1O2* and 3C* production could be attributed to the seasonal variations in the long-range air mass transport. Correlations between [1O2*]ss or [3C*]ss and various absorption and fluorescence parameters allowed us to develop multiple linear regression models that could be applied to predict [1O2*]ss and [3C*]ss based on the measured absorption and fluorescence parameters in future studies. The significance of this work lies foremost in the seasonal trends observed for [1O2*]ss and [3C*]ss and how they correlated with the seasonal variations in the long-range air mass transport. Since many GBA cities share similar monsoon-influenced seasonal air quality and aerosol pollution characteristics to that of Hong Kong, we anticipate that many GBA will have similar seasonal trends of 1O2* and 3C* production in atmospheric aerosols. Additionally, we found that despite the lower reactivities of organic aerosol compounds with 1O2* and 3C* compared to their corresponding reactivities with OH radicals, 1O2* and 3C* are present at high enough concentrations that they are competitive photooxidants to OH radicals under aerosol liquid water conditions. Thus, we expect 1O2* and 3C* reactions to be significant contributors to aqueous secondary organic aerosol formation and transformation in Hong Kong and the GBA. The goal of objective 3 was to investigate the effects of anthropogenic gases on the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols during heterogeneous photooxidation by gas-phase OH radicals. Results from our experiments showed that anthropogenic gases, nitric oxide and sulfur dioxide, did not have a significant effect on the heterogeneous oxidation rate of aqueous aerosols that comprised of water and organic compounds. However, we observed that significant quantities of inorganic nitrate and sulfate were formed within the aqueous aerosols during the oxidation, which is significant since both inorganic nitrate and sulfate can undergo aqueous photolysis to produce reactive species that can react with the organic compounds within the aqueous aerosol. Additionally, sulfate and nitrate are the two most abundant inorganic components in aerosols, clouds, and fogs in most parts of the world. Thus, we focused on the effect that co-present inorganic nitrate and sulfate have on the aqueous photooxidation of organic compounds within the aqueous aerosol. Using green leaf volatiles, a class of organic compounds that we found to be prominent water-soluble organic gases in Hong Kong (results from objective 1), as a model system, we found that under more dilute conditions (i.e., aqueous aerosols have a higher water content), the reactive species produced from nitrate photolysis dominated the reactions of green leaf volatiles. In contrast, under more concentrated conditions (i.e., aqueous aerosols have a lower water content), the reactive species produced from sulfate photolysis dominated the reactions of green leaf volatiles. The significance of this work is that it enabled us to gain a better understanding on how common inorganic salts influence the reactivities (and hence, lifetimes) of aqueous organic aerosols.

11303720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303720.value: This project's results have been published in several high impact journals, with additional publications expected. Objective 1's goal was to characterize the ambient water-soluble organic gases in Hong Kong, and investigate their aqueous-phase photooxidation reactions. Ambient water-soluble organic gases were collected, analyzed, and used for experiments. The mixtures of water-soluble organic gases contained hundreds of organic compounds. The winter samples had a higher number of organic compounds than the summer samples, suggesting that more water-soluble organic gases are present in winter, which could be attributed to the monsoon-influenced seasonal variations in long-range air mass transport to Hong Kong. Sources in continental areas north of Hong Kong and local sources likely contributed to the water-soluble organic gases in winter and summer, respectively. Aqueous photooxidation led to the rapid depletion of many organic compounds and the formation of others, with oxalate comprising a significant fraction at the end of photooxidation. Objective 2's goal was to investigate how seasonality and location influenced the formation of aqueous-phase photooxidants, single oxygen and reactive organic triplet excited states, from the photolysis of ambient aqueous aerosols in Hong Kong. As reported by Lyu et al. (2023), both photooxidants were produced year-round. Their concentrations correlated with the concentration and absorbance of brown carbon, implying that the amount of brown carbon drives the concentrations of photooxidants. Locations had an insignificant effect on the photooxidants’ concentrations, so local sources had an insignificant influence on photooxidant production. Photooxidant production was the highest in winter and the lowest in summer, which could be attributed to the seasonal variations in the long-range air mass transport to Hong Kong. Correlations found between the photooxidants’ concentrations and absorption/fluorescence parameters allowed the development of multiple linear regression models that could be applied to predict photooxidant production based on the measured absorption and fluorescence in future studies. Objective 3's goal was to investigate the effects of nitrogen oxide and sulfur dioxide on the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols during heterogeneous photooxidation by gas-phase OH radicals. While these two gases had insignificant effects on the heterogeneous oxidation rate of aqueous organic aerosols, their presence led to the formation of inorganic sulfate and nitrate in aqueous aerosols. The inorganic sulfate and nitrate subsequently served as photochemical precursors for reactive species. The contributions of reactive species from the photolysis of inorganic sulfate vs. nitrate to the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols depended on the aerosols’ water content.

11303720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303720.value: The PI has established new collaborations with researchers in Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences to study the multiphase aqueous chemistry of organic aerosols in different parts of Guangzhou. Plans are currently being made to collect water-soluble organic gases using the PI's collection setup in different parts of Guangzhou for chemical analysis of their concentrations and composition as well as for experiments to investigate aqueous-phase photooxidation reactions that form aqueous secondary organic aerosols. Additionally, ambient cloud water samples have already been collected by the PI's new collaborators. The PI plans to use these cloud water samples to conduct comprehensive investigations on how aqueous-phase photooxidation reactions in cloud water form aqueous secondary organic aerosols in this region.

11303720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303720.value: Atmospheric organic aerosols have negative environmental and health effects. Formulating air quality policies based on current atmospheric models is challenging due to knowledge gaps on how multiphase aqueous chemistry contribute to the evolution of aerosol mass concentration and composition. Although multiphase aqueous chemistry contributes to organic aerosol formation in humid urban Hong Kong and the GBA, several knowledge gaps remain, including the compositions and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases and aqueous-phase photooxidants that contribute to organic aerosol formation and evolution. In this study, we characterized the compositions and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases and aqueous-phase photooxidants produced from PM2.5 in Hong Kong, as well as investigated how their reactions in aqueous phases lead to organic aerosol formation and evolution. We found that the compositions and concentrations of ambient water-soluble organic gases and aqueous-phase photooxidants produced from PM2.5 are seasonal-dependent, with the highest concentrations observed in winter. The contributions of different aqueous-phase photooxidants to aqueous reactions that lead to organic aerosol formation and evolution ultimately depended on the photooxidant precursors and water content in the aerosol. Overall, findings from this project enhanced our fundamental understanding of multiphase aqueous chemical processes in urban environments, which is crucial for the improvement of atmospheric models used in air quality policy formulation in Hong Kong and the GBA.

11304420.label: Project Objectives
11304420.value: The key object of this proposed research aims to identify the key conditions and chemical compositions for achieving high quality perovskite crystals and films during the fabrication process. Ultimately, it would shed light on the fundamental crystallization process and bring insight into developing perovskites with better stability and environmentally friendly compositions. To develop in-situ photoluminescence (PL) technique which can probe the ion coordination process during perovskite film formation. The setup includes several essential features. (i) As perovskite formation is very sensitive to the fabrication environment, the in-situ PL technique will be developed for use inside a nitrogen-filled glovebox, with the same environment that is used for device fabrication. (ii) Since the intermediate state might not be stable and could be affected by the probing light beam, a co-axial optical fibre fluorescence probe will be used. The probe can be brought to a close proximity on the film surface, which can significantly reduce the required laser power for measurable signal in sub-micron Watt. (iii) Since the ion coordination is fast, a thermoelectric cooled CCD spectrometer with high sensitivity will be used which has data acquisition rate down to millisecond scale. To identify the intermediate states responsible for high perovskite crystallinity. It is expected that ions have different complexity towards each other would induce different intermediate states. However, the knowledge regarding the effect of the intermediate states on the crystallization process remains unclear. By investigating the ion coordination process in multiple-ion composited perovskites with in-situ PL, and comparing the calculated electronic structures, we are aiming at identifying the intermediate states that are responsible for achieving high crystallinity. To identify the role of polymer additives in promoting perovskite crystal growth. We are aiming at investigating the effects of polymer additives on the ion coordination process. By correlating the intrinsic properties of polymers, such as the dielectric properties and dipole moments of different moieties, it would bring insight into developing approaches to control the ion coordination process to improve the crystallinity of perovskites.

11304420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304420.value: Solution-derived organometal halide perovskites are an intriguing class of materials for opto-electronic applications. Recently, a high power conversion efficiency over 25% has been achieved in photovoltaic devices. However, stability and toxicity still pose a threat to the commercialization of the technology. Theoretically, perovskite compositions with more stable crystal structure and environmentally friendly elements have been predicted. However, there is only little success in experiment to obtain high quality perovskite crystals and films. Thus, understanding the ion coordination and crystallization processes is essential to overcome the aforementioned challenges. In this proposed research, we are aiming at developing an in-situ photoluminescence (PL) technique to monitor ion coordination during the perovskite formation process, from solution preparation to spin-coating and thermal annealing. The proposed in-situ PL is fast (millisecond-scale) and capable to detect non-crystalline phase compositions. Notably, the intermediate state formed at the beginning of the crystallization process is crucial for the final perovskite composition and film quality. The preliminary results of the study on a multiple-ion composited perovskite material support the aforementioned statement. Technically, we will setup a high-sensitivity in-situ PL technique inside a nitrogen-filled glovebox. The probe will be equipped with a motorized translation stage to reduce any possible damage from photo-excitation. Scientifically, we will apply the technique to systemically investigate the crystallization process in multiple-ion composited perovskites and to understand the origin of the enhanced crystallinity with polymer additives. In order to have a qualitative understanding of the intermediate states, density-functional-theory (DFT) will be used to identify the possible compositions. The theoretical results will be further correlated to the experimental results obtained by the in-situ PL. Ultimately, the key formation step or composition of the intermediate state can be identified, and bring insight into the fabrication process of high quality new perovskite materials. 新型有機金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料（CH3NH3PbI3）憑藉其可溶液加工及優異的光電性能等特點成為光電應用領域的明星材料，特別是在太陽能電池領域受到研究者的廣泛關注，其公證的光電轉換效率已經超過25％。然而，目前該類光伏技術的商業化直接受限於鉛基鈣鈦礦材料的穩定性和毒性。雖然理論上已經有文獻報導預測了更為環保及穩定的非鉛基鈣鈦礦材料組分，但實驗上想要獲得穩定的無毒的鈣鈦礦晶體材料絕非易事。因此，研究並調控鈣鈦礦材料結晶過程中的離子配位將有助於高質量薄膜材料的製備，以克服該技術的發展瓶頸。 在本項目中，我們旨在開發一種原位光致發光（PL）光譜技術，以實時監測鈣鈦礦材料從溶液製備到旋塗及退火的整個過程中的離子配位情況。該原位PL光譜技術的分辨率高達毫秒級別，能夠迅速檢測到非晶相的組成。眾所周知，在鈣鈦礦材料結晶開始時形成的中間相對最終的鈣鈦礦組分和薄膜質量起重要作用。目前，我們已經初步利用PL光譜技術開展了基於多離子復合鈣鈦礦材料的研究，初步結果證實了該項目的可行性。在本項目的實施過程中，首先在技術上，我們將在手套箱內搭建具有高靈敏度的原位PL光譜測試平台，並且為PL光譜探頭配備電動平移台，以降低由光激發可能造成損耗。隨後，在科學研究上，我們將利用該原位PL光譜技術系統地研究多離子復合鈣鈦礦中的離子配位過程，並探索聚合物添加劑增強鈣鈦礦結晶度的物理機制。我們還將利用密度泛函理論（DFT）結合原位PL光譜結果進一步定量分析鈣鈦礦中間相組分變化。最終，可以確定結晶過程中化學鍵的形成步驟及中間相組分的演化過程，並利用該結果指導高質量新型鈣鈦礦材料的製備。

11304420.label: Realisation of objectives
11304420.value: O1: To identify the key conditions and chemical compositions for achieving high-quality perovskite crystals and films during the fabrication process. Achieved: 100% The goal of understanding the conditions and chemical compositions critical for achieving high-quality perovskite films was successfully met through in-situ photoluminescence (PL) and UV-Vis absorption measurements. These methods provided real-time observations of the crystallization process, correlating fabrication parameters with film quality. 1. Effect of Ambient Temperature on Crystallization Using in-situ optical techniques, we investigated how ambient temperature affects perovskite crystallization in multiple cation-composited perovskites. We find that lower temperatures (22 °C) encouraged nuclei aggregation, while higher temperatures (30 °C) facilitated solute depletion, leading to poorer film morphology. These findings confirmed that ambient temperature is a key condition for achieving high-quality films. The results were published in Advanced Materials (Wang et al., Adv. Mater. 36, 2307635, 2023). 2. ffect of Precursor Composition on Crystallization We also studied the impact of precursor composition by replacing iodide (I⁻) with bromide (Br⁻) to achieve wide-bandgap perovskites. We find that MAPbI2Br exhibited slower nucleation rates (~2.5s) and fewer nuclei compared to MAPbI3, resulting in heterogeneous growth and deteriorated morphology. An additional preheating process was introduced to promote nucleation and ensure uniform material distribution before annealing. These findings demonstrate that in-situ optical techniques can guide the development of optimal fabrication protocols for various perovskite compositions. The results were published in Small Methods (Zeng et al., Small Methods 8, 2300899, 2023). ________________________________________ O2: To develop an in-situ photoluminescence (PL) technique to probe the ion coordination process during perovskite film formation. Achieved: 100% We successfully developed an in-situ PL technique to monitor the ion coordination process during perovskite film formation. Key features of the setup include: 1. Operation within a nitrogen-filled glovebox to replicate the fabrication environment. 2. A co-axial optical fiber fluorescence probe positioned close to the film surface to minimize required laser power (sub-micro-Watt scale). 3. A thermoelectric-cooled CCD spectrometer with millisecond-scale data acquisition rates. Additionally, a motorized X-Y stage was introduced to allow the optical fiber head to move in a circular motion above the sample, preventing localized damage caused by continuous laser excitation. This enhancement improved the reliability of the in-situ PL results and the mechanisms derived from them. ________________________________________ O3: To identify the intermediate states responsible for high perovskite crystallinity. Achieved: 100% We identified intermediate states that play a critical role in achieving high perovskite crystallinity. During spin-coating, the PL spectra revealed asymmetrical patterns, indicating the presence of a mixture of nuclei and bulk crystal phases with distinct emission wavelengths. By adding DMPU as a solvent, we induced a stable DMPU-coordinated intermediate phase that slowed the conversion of nuclei to the bulk phase. This intermediate state delayed crystallization, enabling the formation of high-quality films even at elevated ambient temperatures. The findings, supported by in-situ PL and XRD measurements, demonstrate how intermediate states can enhance film quality under varying processing conditions. The results have been submitted for publication in ACS Energy Letters (Wang et al., under review). ________________________________________ O4: To identify the role of polymer additives in promoting perovskite crystal growth. Achieved: 100% We investigated how polymer additives influence the ion coordination process and enhance perovskite crystallinity. Polymers with larger dipole moments were found to increase crystallinity and suppress ion migration, improving tolerance to electric-field stress. In-situ PL measurements revealed that the intermediate phases induced by polymer additives facilitated the crystallization process, resulting in more homogeneous and higher-quality films. These findings highlight the effectiveness of polymer additives in improving perovskite stability and film quality for photovoltaic applications. ________________________________________ Summary The project successfully achieved all four objectives, advancing the understanding of perovskite crystallization mechanisms and enabling the development of high-quality, stable films. These insights provide a strong foundation for optimizing fabrication protocols and improving perovskite materials for commercial applications.

11304420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304420.value: • Development of In-Situ PL Technique We successfully developed an in-situ photoluminescence (PL) technique to investigate the crystallization mechanism of perovskite during its formation process, as proposed in our research plan. By integrating the setup into a nitrogen-filled glovebox, we ensured that the measurement environment matched the fabrication conditions. Additionally, a high-sensitivity, thermoelectric-cooled CCD spectrometer enabled data acquisition at the millisecond scale, allowing us to track subtle changes in perovskite properties during rapid crystallization. • Expansion to UV-Vis Absorption We further enhanced the technique to perform both PL and UV-Vis absorption measurements, providing more comprehensive information to propose reliable crystallization mechanisms. Due to its strong capabilities and versatility, our in-situ optical method has gained significant recognition, resulting in over 20 journal publications and fostering numerous local and international collaborations in the past three years. • Effect of Precursor Composition on Crystallization Using our in-situ optical techniques, we demonstrated that perovskite crystallization is highly sensitive to precursor composition. Specifically, we found that incorporating Br⁻ ions suppresses nucleation, leading to poor film morphology. To address this, we proposed adding FA⁺ ions to promote nucleation during spin-coating and simplify the annealing process. [Zeng et al., Small Methods 8, 2300899 (2023)] • Season-Dependent Film Quality We experimentally revealed the effect of ambient temperature on perovskite film quality, which explains the season-dependent performance of perovskite solar cells. [Wang et al., Adv. Mater. 36, 2307635 (2023)] • Widening the Temperature Processing Window To broaden the temperature processing window for FA-based perovskites, we demonstrated that adding DMPU as a co-solvent induces a strong intermediate state. This retards fast crystallization and improves film quality, paving the way for reliable large-scale production. [Wang et al., submitted to ACS Energy Lett., under review] • Additives in FA-Based Perovskite Formation We systematically investigated the effects of Cl-based volatile additives and MA-based additives on the crystallization of FA-based perovskite. [Bi et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 145, 5920 (2023)]

11304420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304420.value: This project successfully investigated the crystallization mechanisms of perovskite materials using in-situ optical methods, including PL and UV-Vis absorption. As demonstrated in this study, these techniques have been effectively applied to small-scale perovskite thin films. To expand their potential, future research could focus on utilizing in-situ probing techniques for large-scale fabrication methods, aligning with the current push toward the commercialization of perovskite technologies. Additionally, the existing setup can be adapted to incorporate in-situ FTIR or in-situ Raman spectroscopy by simply modifying the light source and spectrometer. These advanced techniques would provide valuable information on changes in bonding characteristics, offering deeper insights into the crystallization process. This would enable a more comprehensive understanding of both ion coordination and ion dissociation in perovskite crystals, further advancing the study of their formation mechanisms.

11304420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304420.value: In this project, we conducted in-situ observations of the optical properties of materials to study how ions behave not only during crystallization but also during material degradation. To begin, we tested the feasibility of using in-situ optical techniques with a simple perovskite material system. During this process, we improved the experimental setup and developed a foundational understanding of how in-situ results relate to material formation. Our experiments revealed that the quality of the perovskite films is highly sensitive to both the material composition and the surrounding environmental conditions. By comparing different perovskite systems, we investigated the role of various ions in the crystallization process, particularly focusing on the complex interactions between ions. Additionally, we found that intermediate states—induced by additives or solvents—significantly influence the crystallization rate, allowing us to tailor the process to suit different fabrication conditions. This study provides valuable insights into the formation mechanisms of perovskite materials and offers guidance for optimizing fabrication protocols to improve material performance.

11304520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304520.value: 本項目旨在發展基於一個拓撲層的估計大規模有向無環圖（DAG）的有效算法。DAG是因果推斷中的一個常用結構，以用於通過結點及有向邊來表示隨機向量的聯合分佈。估計DAG的一個主要挑戰在於結點的順序未知，從而使得DAG的離散搜索空間的大小是結點的指數階。本項目提出的拓撲層的概念提供了一個確定結點順序的辦法，並能極大的提高估計大規模DAG的效率。在此基礎上，本項目申請人將會基於不同的模型假設提出有效的估計算法，包括線性和非線性結構方程模型（SEM）。我們也會考察新方法的大樣本理論性質，針對大規模估計發展有效的算法，並將新方法應用到基因網絡中以理解基因之間的因果關係。

11304520.label: Realisation of objectives
11304520.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators develop an efficient method to learn linear non-Gaussian DAG in high dimensional cases, where the noises can be of any continuous non-Gaussian distribution. The proposed method leverages the concept of topological layer to facilitate the DAG learning, and its theoretical justification in terms of exact DAG recovery is also established under mild conditions. Particularly, we show that the topological layers can be exactly reconstructed in a bottom-up fashion, and the parent-child relations among nodes can also be consistently established. The established asymptotic DAG recovery is in sharp contrast to that of many existing learning methods assuming parental faithfulness or ordered noise variances. The advantage of the proposed method is also supported by the numerical comparison against some popular competitors in various simulated examples as well as a real application on the global spread of COVID-19. The concept of topological layer is also extended to a special class of non-Gaussian DAG models, where the conditional variance of each node given its parents is a quadratic function of its conditional mean. Such a class of non-Gaussian DAG models are fairly flexible and admit many popular distributions as special cases, including Poisson, Binomial, Geometric, Exponential, and Gamma. To facilitate learning, we introduce a novel concept of topological layers, and develop an efficient DAG learning algorithm. It first reconstructs the topological layers in a hierarchical fashion and then recovers the directed edges between nodes in different layers, which requires much less computational cost than most existing algorithms in literature. Its advantage is also demonstrated in a number of simulated examples, as well as its applications to two real-life datasets, including an NBA player statistics data and a cosmetic sales data collected by Alibaba. The PI and his collaborators further consider a more flexible chain graph model admitting both undirected and directed edges in one graph, where symmetric conditional dependencies are encoded via undirected edges and asymmetric causal relations are encoded via directed edges. Though frequently encountered in practice, the chain graph model has been largely under investigated in the literature, possibly due to the lack of identifiability conditions between undirected and directed edges. In this article, we first establish a set of novel identifiability conditions for the Gaussian chain graph model, exploiting a low rank plus sparse decomposition of the precision matrix. Further, an efficient learning algorithm is built upon the identifiability conditions to fully recover the chain graph structure. Theoretical analysis on the proposed method is conducted, assuring its asymptotic consistency in recovering the exact chain graph structure. The advantage of the proposed method is also supported by numerical experiments on both simulated examples and a real application on the Standard & Poor 500 index data. All proposed methods are implemented in Python, and available upon request. The PI is also closely working with one of the collaborators to wrap up all the implementations in both Python and R packages for dissemination in the coming year.

11304520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304520.value: The major findings of this project are three-folds. First, the PI and his collaborator develop a novel concept of topological layer to facilitate the DAG learning (Part C Output 1). The key advantages of topological layer are that it can be exactly reconstructed in a bottom-up fashion, and the parent-child relations among nodes can also be consistently established via the structural equation model, which greatly simplify the complexity of the DAG learning. Second, the concept of topological layer is implemented in both linear non-Guassian DAG and non-linear non-Guassian DAG, and attain superb numerical and theoretical performances (Part C Outputs 1 & 2). Thanks to the simple topological layer structure, we cast these DAG learning tasks into a sparse structural equation model to attain various modelling purposes. The asymptotic consistency of the proposed methods in terms of exact graph structure recovery is established without assuming parental faithfulness or ordered noise variances. Extensive numerical experiments also illustrate the superior performance of the proposed methods against some state-of-the-art competitors. Third, this project also develops tools for a more general graph structure - chain graph, that admits both undirected and directed edges in one graph (Part C Output 3). Particularly, an efficient learning algorithm is built upon a set of novel identifiability conditions and the topological layer structure, leading to efficient computational schemes, and superior numerical performance.

11304520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304520.value: One potential development is to extend the developed method to financial data, which often exhibits heavy-tailed behaviours due to extreme financial crisis and black swan events. Heavy-tailed data can be modelled via Pareto, Frechet, log-normal, Cauchy distributions, and so on, which calls for a novel reconstruction method of its topological layers. The PI and his former PhD student are now working on this extension, by fully leveraging the properties of the heavy-tailed distribution. The preliminary numerical experiments are very promising, and the required computational cost can be substantially reduced without any sacrifice of the estimation accuracy. The PI plans to admit a Postdoc or Research Assistant to join the research team and complete the theoretical guarantees of these extensions.

11304520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304520.value: The proposed research project develops novel concepts and methods for learning directed acyclic graph structure, which has been commonly used for causal inference. All the objectives are achieved, and an efficient statistical machine learning framework is developed, which is in sharp contrast to most existing methods in literature. The research findings have a wide spectrum of applications in practice, ranging from biomedicine, economics and finance, and information technology. The proposed research not only develop a novel perspective of DAG learning, but also provide rich opportunities for postgraduate students to participate in cutting-edge researches. With the support of this project, the PI and his collaborators published 3 research articles on leading statistics and machine learning journals, and trained one Ph.D. student, Dr. Ruixuan Zhao. Dr. Zhao is currently working as Postdoc fellow at University of Toronto. More importantly, this project also opens up a few potential directions for future research on learning complex structure in large-scale unstructured data.

11304620.label: Project Objectives
11304620.value: A Smooth Path to a Stationary Equilibrium: By introducing an extra variable ranging between zero and one and applying logarithmic-barrier terms, we will formulate a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game. In this barrier game each player solves a strictly convex optimization problem such that the player’s best response is a totally mixed strategy for a positive value of the extra variable. An application of optimality conditions to the barrier game together with a fixed-point argument will produce an equilibrium system, which can be exploited to establish the existence of a smooth path to a stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic game. One more scheme we will explore is to constitute a convex-quadratic-penalty robust stochastic game and attain with this penalty game a smooth path to a stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic game. A Smooth Path to a Perfect Stationary Equilibrium: A generalization of the notion of perfect equilibrium in strategic games will create a strict refinement of stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games and the concept of perfect stationary equilibrium. To find a perfect stationary equilibrium, we will make up a perturbed robust stochastic game depending on the extra variable such that a stationary equilibrium of this perturbed game is an epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium provided that the extra variable is positive. We will employ a differentiable increasing function of the extra variable, which takes values between zero and one and becomes zero before the extra variable descends to zero. Utilizing the perturbed game and the increasing function, we will make up a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game, which becomes identical with the perturbed game if the function’s value equals zero. We will make use of the barrier game and changes of variables to assure the existence of a smooth path to a perfect stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic game. An alternative scheme we will investigate is to devise a convex-quadratic-penalty robust stochastic game and reap with this penalty game a smooth path to a perfect stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic game. A Smooth Path to a Proper Stationary Equilibrium: An extension of the concept of proper equilibrium in strategic games results in a strict refinement of perfect stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games and the notion of proper stationary equilibrium. To compute a proper stationary equilibrium, we will set up a perturbed robust stochastic game depending on the extra variable and satisfying that a stationary equilibrium of the perturbed game is an epsilon-proper stationary equilibrium for a positive value of the extra variable. We will utilize this perturbed game and the increasing function to gain a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game, which equals the perturbed game when the function takes the value of zero. We will apply the barrier game and changes of variables to acquire a smooth path to a proper stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic game. Another scheme we will examine is to formulate a convex-quadratic-penalty robust stochastic game and attain with this penalty game a smooth path to a proper stationary equilibrium. Efficient Procedures to Numerically Trace Smooth Paths: When a smooth path is constructed, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be established to characterize the path. We will propose an efficient predictor-corrector method to solve the system. The emphasis will be on the full exploitation of special structures for numerical stability and efficiency. As in interior-point methods, scaling technique will be put to good use. A lifting procedure will be exploited to significantly reduce the number of variables in the computation of a proper stationary equilibrium. Various alternative schemes will be explored for efficiently tracing the path. Numerical Implementations: When differentiable path-following methods are successfully developed in this research, we will code them in both MATLAB and C++. We will reduce the computational burden by exploiting special structures whenever possible. Comprehensive numerical experiments will be systematically carried out this this research. A software package of the methods will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for solving robust stochastic games from applications.

11304620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304620.value: As an effective paradigm for modeling and analysis of the interactions among competitive players over time, stochastic games have been successfully applied in various fields. In these applications, the computation of stationary equilibrium plays an important role. The integration of robust optimization into stochastic games results in robust stochastic games and provides an effective alternative to deal with uncertainty in both payoffs and state transition probabilities that frequently occurs in the applications. When robust stochastic games are finite (a finite number of players and a finite number of pure strategies for each player in each state), one can naturally extend to them the concepts of perfect equilibrium and proper equilibrium in strategic games and create two strict refinements of stationary equilibrium: perfect stationary equilibrium and proper stationary equilibrium. This project aims at developing effective and efficient differentiable path-following methods to compute a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium and a proper stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games when uncertainty in payoffs and state transition probabilities can be presented as bounded polyhedrons. We will exploit in the developments a differentiable increasing function of an extra variable, which takes values between zero and one and vanishes before the extra variable descends to zero. Utilizing the function and logarithmic-barrier terms, we will constitute a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game and establish the existence of a smooth path to a stationary equilibrium. We will formulate a perturbed robust stochastic game depending on the extra variable such that a stationary equilibrium of this perturbed game is an epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium for a positive value of the extra variable. Applying this perturbed game, we will make up a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game and reap a smooth path to a perfect stationary equilibrium. Moreover, we will set up a perturbed robust stochastic game satisfying that a stationary equilibrium of this perturbed game is an epsilon-proper stationary equilibrium provided that the extra variable is positive. Making use of this perturbed game, we will devise a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game and acquire a smooth path to a proper stationary equilibrium. We will also explore convex-quadratic-penalty robust stochastic games to arrive at the existence of smooth paths that meet the requirements. By fully capitalizing on special structures and scaling techniques, efficient procedures will be attained to numerically trace the smooth paths and a software package of the methods will be made available for solving robust stochastic games from applications.

11304620.label: Realisation of objectives
11304620.value: As an effective paradigm to deal with payoff and transition probability uncertainty in stochastic games, robust stochastic games are formulated in the literature. When the payoff and transition probability uncertainty is characterized by a polytope with an interior point for each player, the concept of stationary equilibrium or stationary Markov perfect equilibrium (MPE) is extended to robust stochastic games by demanding that each player chooses the worst-case payoff. As a strict refinement of stationary equilibrium, the concept of perfect stationary equilibrium is formulated for robust stochastic games by introducing epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium. As a strict refinement of perfect stationary equilibrium, the concept of proper stationary equilibrium is formulated for robust stochastic games by introducing epsilon-proper stationary equilibrium. By introducing an extra variable ranging between zero and one, we formulate perturbed robust stochastic games such that every Nash equilibrium of the perturbed robust stochastic games are an epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium and an epsilon-proper stationary equilibrium of the original robust stochastic game, respectively. To make use of these perturbed robust stochastic games and fully exploit differentiability of the robust stochastic games, we define logarithmic-barrier payoff functions for each player from a convex combination of a logarithmic barrier term and the player’s payoff function. Applications of the logarithmic-barrier payoff functions lead to logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic games that deform from a trivial robust stochastic game to the original robust stochastic game as the extra variable varies from one to zero. The logarithmic barrier term forces every Nash equilibrium of the logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic games to stay in the interior of the strategy space of the perturbed robust stochastic games. Since the equilibrium systems of the logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic games are completely characterized by a finite number of polynomials, an error bound theorem in the literature guarantees that, when the extra variable is sufficiently small, the corresponding coefficients of the logarithmic-barrier terms are so small that every Nash equilibrium of the logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic games can closely approximate to some epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium and epsilon-proper stationary equilibrium of the original robust stochastic games, provided that the power of the extra variable is large enough. An application of the well-known Sard’s theorem and implicit function theorem shows that there exist smooth paths to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium and a proper stationary equilibrium in the original robust stochastic game, respectively. A predictor-corrector method is adapted for numerically following the smooth paths. To enhance the performance of the methods, sparsity of the robust stochastic games has been fully exploited in the implementation. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the paths indeed lead to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium and a proper stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games. As an alternative scheme, we have constituted convex-quadratic-penalty robust stochastic games and established the existence of smooth paths to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium and a proper stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games. All the objectives of the project have been successively achieved.

11304620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304620.value: Stationary equilibrium or subgame perfect equilibrium in stationary strategies in robust stochastic games has many applications in economic analysis. The computation of such an equilibrium plays an important role in these applications. In order to select a stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games, we constitute with an extra variable varying between zero and one a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game in which each player selects her best response by solving against a given stationary strategy profile and a given payoff and transition probability a strictly convex optimization problem and determines her worst-case payoff by solving against a given strategy stationary strategy profile a strictly convex optimization problem. An application of the optimality condition to the logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game yields a polynomial equilibrium system that approaches the equilibrium system of the original robust stochastic game as the extra variable vanishes. As a result of the polynomial equilibrium system, we establish the existence of a smooth path to a stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games [1]. Stochastic games are special cases of robust stochastic games. As a result of the developments in this project, we propose an interior-point differentiable path-following method to compute a stationary equilibrium in stochastic games [3]. A perfect stationary equilibrium can be acquired from a limit point of a sequence epsilon-perfect equilibrium with epsilon approaching zero. We formulate with an extra variable ranging between zero and one a logarithmic-barrier robust stochastic game whose polynomial equilibrium system yields an approximate epsilon-perfect stationary equilibrium and establishes the existence of a smooth path to a perfect stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games. An application of this idea leads to a variant of Harsanyi’s tracing procedure for selecting a perfect equilibrium in normal-form games [2]. The computation of an economic equilibrium in incomplete markets can be formulated as abstract stochastic games. Exploiting the idea in this project, we attain a smooth homotopy method to compute an economic equilibrium in incomplete markets [4, 5]. Single principle and multi-agent repeated games are special stochastic games. The developments of this project provide effective solutions to these special stochastic games [6].

11304620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304620.value: The idea formulated in this project can be extended to robust extensive-form games to compute a Nash equilibrium in behavioral strategies (NashEBS) and its refinements. One can first formulate a perturbed robust extensive-form game and constitute a barrier robust extensive-form game such that there exists a smooth path of NashEBS of the barrier game, which starts a unique solution and leads to a NashEBS or one of its refinements of the original robust extensive-form game. Then a predictor-corrector method can be adapted for numerically tracing the path to a NashEBS or one of its refinements in robust extensive-form games.

11304620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304620.value: Robust stochastic games have many applications in economic analysis. The computation of stationary equilibrium and its refinements plays a significant role in these applications. As a refinement of stationary equilibrium in robust stochastic games, perfect stationary equilibrium is a more rational stationary equilibrium and proper stationary equilibrium is a more rational perfect stationary equilibrium. This project has developed effective and efficient logarithmic-barrier path-following methods for computing a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium, and a proper stationary equilibrium. The methods have fully exploited differentiability of the barrier robust stochastic games. By introducing an extra variable for deforming from a trivial game to the original one, smooth paths have been constructed, which lead to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium, and a proper stationary equilibrium. Sard’s theorem and implicit function theorem have been applied to derive the existence of smooth paths to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium, and a proper stationary equilibrium. An efficient predictor-corrector method has been adapted for numerically tracing the smooth paths to a stationary equilibrium, a perfect stationary equilibrium, and a proper stationary equilibrium. Comprehensive numerical experiments have been carried out to show the effectiveness and efficiency of the methods. The research of the project will further promote the applications of robust stochastic games.

11304820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304820.value: 這一個項目的目的是建立一個嚴格的高超音速相似率的理論並且進行薄激波層的相關數學理論的研究。特別的，我們主要關注於二維定常可壓縮高超音速完全歐拉流流經彎曲邊界的問題，以及其它相關問題。 高超音速流體是接馬赫數大於五的流體。正如[2, pp.12]所說，它在物理上是不同於超音速流體，而且對於二十一世紀的高超音速飛行器的設計非常重要。對於高超音速流體的研究是有挑戰性的，因為薄激波層、熵層、高溫度流、以及低密度流等現象。因此，對於高超音速流體的數學理論，我們需要研究在非常狹窄的角點區域上帶自由邊界的弱解。並且密度很小，熵的變化很大，或者帶有反應和輻射效應。在這一個項目中，我們會選擇一個在[2]討論的典型問題，即二維定常可壓縮高超音速完全歐拉流流經彎曲邊界的問題。特別的，我們將要研究這一個問題的高超音速相似率，薄激波層的數學理論，以及其它相關的模型，比如反應歐拉方程組和輻射歐拉方程組。 自從Courant-Friedriches的經典書籍[16]以來，關於超音速定常歐拉流體流經二維楔形物體或者椎體建立了相對滿意的數學理論(見[6,7,9-14,20,24- 26,30,32-34])。但是，對於高超音速流體的研究，儘管有著很多文獻(如[28.29])，卻遠遠沒有完善。因為高超音速流體力學有著許多重要的應用，我們研究這裡提出來的幾個課題是有意義的。我們已經在相關領域做過幾年的研究。比如我們證明了二維無旋歐拉流體的高超音速相似率[22]。一維雙曲守恆率的非線性幾何光學的適用性[8]。帶激波或者疏散波的輻射歐拉流體的漸進穩定性[18,19]。帶接觸間斷波流經李普希茲邊界的定常反應歐拉流體全局存在性[31]。在這一個項目中，我們關注於繼續發展這裡應用過的數學技巧，以研究這裡提到的課題。

11304920.value: Applying reinforcement learning to quantum gate optimization Applying reinforcement learning to quantum metrology

11304920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304920.value: Quantum technology is believed to be much more powerful than present-day computational technologies in many problems. Lying at its heart is quantum control, that is, the precise manipulation of quantum systems robust to noises. Various numerical techniques have been employed to find control protocols that achieve maximum accuracy while costing minimum resources. However, traditional algorithms such as gradient-based ones and the Krotov method have limitations under various situations. On the other hand, machine-learning techniques have demonstrated great power in many problems. Reinforcement learning, a main branch of machine learning, is particularly suitable for quantum control as it casts the control problem into a "game", with rules and goals derived from the desired problem. In this game, an agent seeks for the maximum reward following the prescribed rules, which, at the same time, gives optimal solutions. The reinforcement learning have been found to be more efficient than traditional methods under some situations. In this work, we will further reveal the power of reinforcement learning in quantum control problems. We will apply reinforcement learning to quantum gate optimization, quantum metrology, and other problems such as shortcuts to adiabaticity. As the outcome of this project, we expect that the control protocols suggested by reinforcement learning would be much easier to be experimentally implemented than those exist in the literature, which should greatly improve the accuracy of quantum control, providing a solid foundation stone for quantum technology. 量子技術被認為在諸多方面大大優於現有的計算技術。其核心是對量子系統的抗噪精確調控。人們利用了多種數值方法尋找消耗最小資源而能達到最高精度的控制途徑。然而，傳統優化算法，例如基於梯度的算法以及Krotov方法，在不同的情況下有著各自的極限。 另一方面，機器學習技術在諸多問題上表現出巨大的潛力。強化學習——機器學習的一個主要分支——特別適用於量子控制，因為其將控制問題轉化為一個“遊戲”，而規則和目標則由目標問題所刻畫。在這個遊戲中，一個智能體在這些預設的規則下尋求最大的獎勵，並與此同時給出問題的最優解。在一些情況下，強化學習被發現比傳統的方法更優。 在這項工作中，我們進一步挖掘強化學習應用在量子控制中的潛力。我們將強化學習應用在量子門優化、量子測量等問題上。我們期待強化學習產生的控制序列能夠比文獻中現存的更簡單易行，從而提高量子控制的精度，並為量子精密測量打下堅實的基礎。

11304920.label: Realisation of objectives
11304920.value: Over the project period, we have made substantial progress toward the objectives, which integrate reinforcement learning (RL) with quantum gate optimization and quantum metrology. For Objective 1 (Reinforcement learning for quantum gate optimization), we built upon the foundation of generic detection-based error mitigation using quantum autoencoders [1] to develop strategies for mitigating errors in RL-based gate design. This detection-based approach allows RL algorithms to preemptively adjust to system imperfections, a crucial capability for achieving high-fidelity gates. Our work on charge noise suppression in capacitively coupled singlet-triplet qubits [2] provided insight into realistic qubit-environment interactions, which informed the training environments used in RL simulations. We expanded on methods of robust entangling gates for capacitively coupled few-electron qubits [4], incorporating counterdiabatic ansatz strategies to accelerate quantum optimization [10]. Furthermore, group sparse matrix optimization techniques [8] contributed to reducing computational overhead in multi-qubit RL optimization by focusing on critical control pathways. Decoherence effects, especially those arising from multi-qubit interactions and geometric connectivity [6], were incorporated into RL models, enabling the algorithms to develop control strategies resilient to real-world noise and connectivity constraints. For Objective 2 (Reinforcement learning for quantum metrology), our advances in generalizable control methods for multiparameter quantum metrology [3] established a strong foundation for integrating RL. These methods facilitate adaptive measurement protocols that dynamically respond to environmental changes, and RL algorithms further optimize these adjustments by learning from repeated experiments. Quantum hypothesis testing via robust quantum control [5] provided a conceptual framework for developing reinforcement learning strategies aimed at maximizing sensitivity while maintaining robustness against decoherence and noise. In addressing the computational challenges of high-dimensional quantum system simulations, we leveraged the quantum modeling framework developed for simulating nutrient effects in bioplastic PHA production [7]. This approach demonstrated efficient handling of complex, interacting systems, which was adapted to simulate multi-qubit dynamics during RL training. Additionally, our investigation into entanglement spectra and phase diagrams in multi-electron quantum dot chains [9] informed the design of reinforcement learning architectures that respect system symmetries and entanglement structures. The integration of reinforcement learning with our previous work has significantly advanced the project’s objectives. The RL-based approaches we developed demonstrate adaptability, scalability, and resilience to noise, laying the groundwork for future quantum control protocols that are both efficient and robust.
