11304920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304920.value: This project has delivered a comprehensive set of advances in quantum control, metrology, and optimization, with significant implications for the development of scalable and adaptive quantum technologies. Our research systematically integrated reinforcement learning (RL) with established quantum control frameworks, resulting in enhanced performance and robustness in both quantum gate design and quantum sensing. A key result was the development of generic detection-based error mitigation strategies using quantum autoencoders [1], which provided a model-independent approach to detect and correct errors in quantum systems. This method was critical for enabling optimization algorithms to operate effectively in noisy environments. Complementing this, we investigated charge noise suppression mechanisms in capacitively coupled singlet-triplet qubits under magnetic fields [2], offering practical insights into reducing decoherence. Our work on robust entangling gates for capacitively coupled few-electron qubits [4] provided optimized gate protocols resilient to environmental fluctuations. These advancements were further enhanced by applying counterdiabatic ansatz strategies [10], which accelerated gate operations without sacrificing fidelity, an improvement for near-term quantum devices. In quantum metrology, we developed a generalizable control framework for multiparameter estimation [3] that serves as a platform for integrating RL, enabling real-time adaptive measurements that maximize precision. The theoretical foundation of quantum hypothesis testing with robust quantum control [5] demonstrated how optimized measurement protocols can be systematically designed to distinguish quantum states with high confidence, even in the presence of noise. These insights were complemented by our studies of decoherence in multi-qubit spin systems [6], which revealed how interaction networks and connectivity influence system robustness. The exploration of entanglement spectra and phase diagrams in multi-electron quantum dot chains [9] provided a deeper understanding of quantum correlations and their implications for control and sensing strategies. In addition, our study on simulating nutrient effects in Pseudomonas putida for bioplastic production using quantum-inspired modeling techniques [7] highlighted the interdisciplinary potential of these tools, bridging quantum physics with biological systems. The incorporation of group sparse matrix optimization techniques [8] further improved computational efficiency in quantum state transformations, supporting scalable applications in both quantum computing and metrology. Together, these findings chart a clear path forward for scalable, robust, and adaptive quantum control and metrology. By combining RL with advanced quantum control methodologies, we have developed solutions that not only address current technical challenges but also pave the way for next-generation quantum technologies in computation, sensing, and even interdisciplinary applications.

11304920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304920.value: Future work will focus on deepening the integration of reinforcement learning (RL) with quantum control protocols for multi-qubit systems and multi-parameter metrology. Building on our achievements in error mitigation [1], entangling gate design [4], and counterdiabatic optimization [10], we aim to develop scalable RL algorithms that adapt to complex noise environments. By incorporating insights from charge noise suppression [2] and decoherence in spin systems [6], we will enhance robustness against hardware imperfections. We plan to implement and test these RL-enhanced strategies on experimental platforms such as superconducting qubits and semiconductor spin qubits, collaborating with experimental groups to bridge theory and practice. Feedback from these collaborations will inform refinements of our algorithms, ensuring adaptability to real-world conditions. Additionally, we will explore interdisciplinary applications inspired by quantum modeling of biological systems [7] and efficient quantum state transformations [8], aiming to extend quantum optimization frameworks into areas like sensing, materials discovery, and biological modeling. These efforts will contribute to the development of next-generation quantum processors and high-precision sensors, advancing scalable and adaptive quantum technologies.

11304920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304920.value: This project explored how machine learning, particularly reinforcement learning (RL), and quantum technologies can work together to tackle the challenges of building more powerful quantum computers and high-precision sensors. Quantum computers rely on delicate quantum states, which are easily disrupted by noise and errors. To address this, we applied RL—a form of artificial intelligence—to help quantum devices learn optimal ways to operate, adaptively adjusting to environmental fluctuations and imperfections. Our research developed methods to design faster and more reliable quantum gates, the fundamental operations in quantum computing, and improve precision measurements in quantum metrology, which helps scientists detect extremely small signals. By integrating RL with quantum control strategies, we showed how future quantum systems can operate more efficiently and robustly, even in noisy conditions. Beyond quantum computing, our approaches also demonstrated potential applications in areas like secure communication technologies, advanced material discovery, and even biological modeling. For example, we explored how quantum-inspired modeling can simulate complex biological systems, offering new insights for biotechnological applications. Overall, our findings open the door to smarter, more adaptive quantum systems, paving the way for breakthroughs in science and technology.

11305220.value: Fabricate and optimize nano-porous silicon (Si) for battery applications

11305220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305220.value: Lithium-ion batteries such as the one in our cell phones store energy by transferring lithium ions between the materials in the two electrodes. How fast the battery can be charged and discharged depends on the particle size of the materials – smaller particles can accept lithium ion faster and thus allow the use of larger current. Therefore, there have been many research works focusing on nano-sizing battery materials. However, nano-particles are difficult to handle and manufacture from an industrial point-of-view. They also have large surface area for side reactions and low packing density, which prevent their practical use in batteries. Nano-porous materials having a Swiss cheese or a sponge-like structure can be a good compromise. Apart from having smaller transport lengths, the pores can also allow penetration of electrolyte and can accommodate volume changes when incorporating lithium ions into the material during charging. Porous materials can be fabricated by first making an alloy with two elements, and then selectively removing one of the more reactive elements by methods such as etching and vacuum annealing/distillation etc. The objectives of this project are to fabricate nano-porous antimony (Sb), silicon (Si) and tin (Sn) with micron-sized particles to increase the amount of stored energy in lithium-ion batteries. Our plan is to control the particle size, porosity, pore size distribution and surface area of the nano-porous materials to optimize the corresponding battery performances. This is one step further than previous works, which only show the formation of nano-porous materials without much systematic control. We plan to achieve our objectives by fine-tuning the microstructure of the initial alloys through controlling the concentration of the alloying materials and cooling rate during solidification. This is a well-known process in metallurgy and will be applied here for energy storage applications. We expect the technologies from the development of nano-porous materials in this project can also be applied to other areas such as gas adsorption, catalysis, drug delivery, etc. in the future. 鋰離子電池（例如我們手機中的一種）通過在兩個電極材料之間傳遞鋰離子來儲存能量。電池的充電和放電速度取決於材料的顆粒大小較小的顆粒可以更快地接受鋰離子，從而可以使用較大的電流。因此，已經有許多研究工作集中在納米尺寸的電池材料上。然而，從工業角度來看，納米顆粒難以處理和製造。另外，它們較大的表面積導致副反應的發生和較低的堆積密度，這妨礙了它們在電池中的實際應用。 具有瑞士奶酪或海綿狀結構的納米多孔材料是一個好的選擇。這些孔除了具有較小的傳輸長度外，還能使電解質滲透並緩解在充電過程中鋰離子與材料結合時的體積變化。可以通過首先用兩種元素製成合金，然後通過蝕刻和真空退火/蒸餾等方法選擇性地去除反應性更高的元素之一來製造多孔材料。 該項目的目的是製造具有微米級顆粒的納米多孔矽（Si），以增加鋰離子電池的儲能。我們的計劃是通過控制納米多孔材料的粒徑，孔隙率，孔徑分佈和表面積來優化相應的電池性能。這比以前的工作更進了一步，以前的工作僅展示了納米多孔材料的形成，而沒有太多的系統控制。我們計劃通過控制合金材料的濃度及固化過程中的冷卻速率來微調初始合金的微觀結構，以實現我們的目標。這個冶金學中眾所周知的過程將被用於能量存儲應用。我們希望本項目中納米多孔材料的開發技術將來也可以應用於其他領域，例如氣體吸附，催化，藥物輸送等。

11305220.label: Realisation of objectives
11305220.value: The project has been 100% achieved. Nano-porous silicon was synthesized first by making Mg-Si alloy and then removing Mg from the alloy through vacuum annealing. The porosity of the product is found to depend on the starting composition of the Mg-Si alloy and also the annealing temperature of the alloy. Specifically, higher porosity is obtained from materials with larger Mg content, but increased brittleness of the material is noted. The nano-porous silicon materials were made into electrodes for lithium-ion batteries, and stable capacity with cycling is shown by them. In-situ dilatometer experiments that can measure the change of the thickness of the electrode during charge and discharge show that the electrode with nano-porous Si is only expanded by about 50% after full lithiation, as opposed to about 400% for electrodes with bulk Si particles. The results are currently being summarized, and a journal paper on it is intended to be written. During the project, collaboration was started with a local Hong Kong-based company, and the process is now able to be scaled up by the company to make large batch nano-porous Si. Towards the end of the project, electrolyte additives were being developed that can increase the Coulombic efficiency of LiCoO2-Si full batteries. Apart from synthesizing Si materials, methods to improve the thermal stability of Si material with the use of an electrolyte additive were also studied, and a simple annealing process to increase the first Coulombic efficiency of SiO material was developed. The project has also been extended to other metals such as tin, copper, and lithium for battery applications. One PhD student (Dr. Tian TAN) was trained under this project. Five papers were published throughout the course of the project. One online poster was given at the International Meeting on Lithium Batteries 2022. Unfortunately, due to COVID lockdown and travel restrictions, attendance at more conferences to disseminate the information was not possible, so online attendance was conducted instead.

11305220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305220.value: A major finding in the project is that nano-porous Si can be made by the alloying/de-alloying process, and the volume expansion of Si during lithiation is suppressed by the pores, enabling good cycling stability. To further improve the thermal stability of Si, it was found that the addition of 3-Aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) into the electrolyte results in a reduction of heat generation from lithiated silicon in the presence of the electrolyte. This is attributed to the polymerization of APTES during thermal abuse, which forms a protective layer on top of the Si materials to prevent further reaction. Si monoxide (SiO) is also considered a potential high-capacity anode material for lithium-ion batteries. However, the oxygen reacts irreversibly with lithium during initial lithiation, which decreases the initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of the material. The ICE of the SiO material has been successfully increased by first reacting it with Na2CO3, which disproportionates SiO into Si embedded in a matrix of SiO2. The SiO2 matrix is also able to suppress the expansion of Si particles, improving the cycling stability of the material.

11305220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305220.value: The mechanical and thermal stability of Si-based materials was increased by the synthesis of nano-porous silicon and silicon in a matrix of SiO2. Further work will include collaborating with industry to apply the technologies to practical applications.

11305220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305220.value: Battery is an essential device for energy storage in our daily life. For future applications, batteries with higher energy density, better stability and safety are desired. This project aims at developing high-capacity silicon-based anode for lithium-ion batteries. This is achieved by making nano-porous silicon where the pores can accommodate the volume expansion of the material during lithiation, thereby improving the mechanical stability of the material. High-capacity SiO electrode with improved first cycle efficiency was also demonstrated during the project. In addition, thermal stability of the Si-based material is enhanced by addition of a silane coupling agent, which forms a protective layer on the surface of the material to reduce heat generation. The project was further extended to improve stability and power of other materials such as tin, copper and lithium.

11305420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305420.value: 全球大約一半的雲是由水蒸氣凝結到氣溶膠顆粒上形成的，這些氣溶膠顆粒是由微量大氣蒸汽通過成核而生長的。這些大氣粒子可以通過吸收和散射太陽光來影響地球的輻射預算。因此，了解這些大氣基本原理對全球氣候有重大意義。儘管實驗進展揭示了許多成核顆粒的化學組成，但它們的化學結構和性質對成核機理的影響仍未得到很好的理解。許多實驗證據表明，高度氧化的有機分子和陰離子可能在成核過程中發揮重要作用。最近，我們發現，由二氧化碳分子的單電子還原形成的二氧化碳自由基陰離子的水合簇可以與不飽和碳反應形成氣相的羧酸根陰離子。根據它們的極性，有機化合物可能會多次吸收到水團簇上，形成水性有機納米液滴。這些液滴可能能夠與其他微量大氣進一步反應形成更大的顆粒。然而，這些液滴的溶劑化結構在很大程度上是未知的。在這項工作中，我們建議通過使用密度泛函理論來表徵最初由二氧化碳自由基陰離子向各種不飽和有機化合物的自由基加成反應生成的羧酸有機陰離子形成的水性有機納米滴的結構和化學性質。它們的溶劑化結構和反應動力學將通過在有限溫度下使用分子動力學模擬進行檢查。還將從理論上確定常見的生物揮發性有機化合物（例如異戊二烯和萜烯）和痕量大氣氣體（例如H2SO4，HNO3和NH3）對這些水性有機納米滴的結合親和力，以探索這些水性有機納米滴在地層中的潛力。我們的研究結果將為成核過程中氣態分子的初始組裝提供基本分子原理的寶貴理論見解，從而可以增進我們對地球大氣的了解。

11305420.label: Realisation of objectives
11305420.value: Solvation structure of hydrated carbon dioxide radical anion and their cluster-size dependent vibrational spectra and reactivity towards unsaturated organic compounds were assessed by extensive conformational sampling and density functional theory based molecular dynamics (DFT-MD) simulations. A database consisting of CO2•−(H2O)n and respective vibrational spectra were obtained for selected sizes from n = 4 up to our current computational limit of 40 (Objective 1). Unsaturated organic compounds (including methyl acrylate and allyl alcohol) were equilibrated on selected geometries of CO2•−(H2O)n at each studied size at a constant temperature of 100 K, similar to the experimental condition, and the time evolution of the carboxylation reaction and charge migration process were monitored (Objective 2 and Objective 3), aiming to understand the effects of hydration site on CO2•− radical towards its reactivity and subsequent reaction pathways at different cluster sizes. The solvation structure and its dynamics around the unsaturated carbons and their vicinal environment were simulated to evaluate their influence on their reactivity with solvation molecules and/or multiple-uptake unsaturated molecules (Objective 3). These tasks were performed by one PhD candidate and three MSc students, overseeing by a Senior Research Associate and the PI. Technical details of our results addressing these achieved objectives are highlighted as follows. The database of CO2•−(H2O)n was obtained by first sampling of about 10,000 conformers using CHARMM forcefield via ABCluster for each cluster size. Subsequently, all conformers were subjected to a similarity check to filter off redundant conformers via the smooth overlap of atomic positions (SOAP) descriptor using DScribe library. Remaining conformers were optimized at B3LYP/6-31G* level with loose convergence criteria and subjected to another similarity check. Finally, the remaining distinctive conformers were further refined by optimization at M06-2X/6-311++G** level with tight convergence criteria. All harmonic frequency calculations were performed at B3LYP/6-311++G** using Gaussian 16 program. Anharmonic frequency calculations were simulated by the Fourier transform of the dipole time-correlation function (DTCF). This was achieved by subjecting the lowest-lying structures for a DFT-MD run under NVT ensemble at 100 K (close to temperature of experimental setup) at B3LYP level for 5 ps. DFT-MD simulations were performed with CP2K Quickstep module. The solvation structures of CO2•−(H2O)n can be divided into two categories: CO2•− is solvated exclusively by O…H2O hydrogen bonds (OH conformers) and solvated additionally by an unusual C…H2O hydrogen bond (2.0 – 2.8 Å) (C-hydrated; CH conformers). Solvation structures of each cluster size were represented by a population of low-lying geometries resulting from their significant structural diversity and fluxionality under the gas-phase condition at finite temperatures; interestingly, low-lying geometries shifted from exclusively OH conformers (n = 4, 5) to a coexistence of CH and OH conformers (n = 6 – 10, 20, 30). This shift of hydration site of CO2•− radical was highly associated with solvation shell structure. For n = 4 and 5, arrangement of water molecules was spatially restricted due to their small solvation shell, thus O…H hydrogen bonds was exclusively observed because the highly polarized C=O bond provided a more favorable site for solvation compared to the carbon atom, where spin density was only partially localized. From n = 6 and onwards, the C…H hydrogen bond was observed due to available water molecules solvating the spin density at the carbon atom, which provided further stabilization. The coexistence of conformers lacking C…H hydrogen bond was driven by the formation of specific low-energy water arrangements (e.g., tetramer, pentamer and hexamer and multi-ring-stacking structures). These thermodynamically favorable configurations did not promote C…H hydrogen bonding. For each cluster size, about 10 energetically lowest-lying minima from the refined database were selected as input geometry for calculating vibrational spectra for comparison with available experimental spectral data. There are two IR-active vibrational modes of CO2•− radical: symmetric C=O stretch (νs) at 1254 cm−1 and antisymmetric C=O stretch (νas) at 1658 cm−1. From n = 4 – 40, the νs experienced a progressive blue-shift from the νs of a non-solvated CO2•− radical. When water cluster size approached n = 20, both experimental and theoretical νs were close to the bulk value at 1298 cm−1. While the νs could not distinguish the presence of C…H hydrogen bond, the νas portrayed significant difference, where theoretical peak of νas with C…H hydrogen bond was much more blue-shifted. For n = 4,5, theoretical spectra without C…H hydrogen bond showed qualitative agreement with experimental spectra. From n = 6 and onwards, the νas of the conformers started to show inconsistent trend where qualitative agreement appeared intermittently between theoretical spectra with and without C…H hydrogen bond. Interestingly, theoretical spectra of surface-solvated CO2•− radical were highly aligned with experimental spectra. The reliability of the simulation method used had also been tested with other similar systems, including inorganic ion ([Na3(CO3)]+) and organic ions (fragments of model tripeptides GGG, AAA and FFF that contain a variety of functional groups, such as the polar amide, iminium and aminium groups, and the non-polar aliphatic and aromatic side chains). Solvent reorganization-induced dynamics is significant when the vibrational modes are coupled to electronic transitions during reactions such as the addition of radical anion towards unsaturated organic functional groups. Hydrogen bond to a carbonyl group in an unsaturated ketone can weaken the C=O bond and increase the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Simultaneously, hydrogen bonding to the reacting radical anion can restrict its molecular motion and introduce new low-frequency vibrational modes. These specific solvation effects alter the charge and spin density distribution within the radical anion and intermediates, guiding the reaction towards different pathways. The reactivity of different solvation modes have been hypothesized and theoretically examined with the reactions of hydrated Mn+ clusters toward olefin molecules. The evolution of solvation structure is also crucial for growth of atmospheric (H2SO4)x(NH3)y(H2O)n clusters into cloud condensation nuclei. Hydration drives ion formation, and the extent of this hydration dictates whether ions exist primarily as contact ion pairs (CIPs) such as [HSO4−−NH4+] or transition to solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIPs), like [HSO4−−H2O−NH4+], with increasing water molecules. This transition to SSIPs, facilitated by water insertion between the constituent ions, creates a more extensive hydrogen bond network around them. Crucially, by separating the original ion pair, SSIP formation can increase the accessibility of individual ionic sites to incoming sulfuric acid or ammonia molecules, thereby potentially enhancing the cluster’s growth and nucleation rate.

11305420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305420.value: This research aims at investigating the cluster-size dependent reactivity of solvated ions, including the degrees and sites of their hydration and the influence of the vicinal chemical environment around reaction sites of unsaturated organic compounds and selected atmospheric gases, such as CO2 and N2O, in hydrated clusters [1-3,5-8] and H2SO4-NH3-H2O clusters [11] with extensions to other similar systems [4,9,10]. These investigations, employing theoretical quantum chemical calculations corroborated by experimental mass spectrometric measurements, have elucidated the critical role of solvent dynamics and hydration on dictating the reaction pathway within the studied systems. These findings are detailed in six published articles in prestigious international science journals and have been publicized through presentations at recognized international conferences. A central theme emerging from this work is the profound influence of solvent dynamics on the reactivity of small, charged/neutral clusters with excess electrons as well as anions and metal cations. Specifically, the preferential stabilization of substrate molecules, particular functional groups, or electron-rich metal ions by solvent molecules were found to be remarkably influential in either masking or promoting overall reactivity. For instance, studies on hydrated metal ion clusters demonstrated that the gradual evolution of solvation structures with increasing hydration can stabilize certain conformers [1,2,5-7]. While these conformers might be thermodynamically favored, they can be chemically inactive for reaction pathways observed in smaller cluster sizes [7]. Different chemical forms of the solvated ions, depending on cluster sizes, were predicted to undergo various reactions with unsaturated organic functional groups, such as hydrogen transfer and/or polymerization reactions through multiple molecular uptakes [8]. Changes in the degree of hydration were shown to alter the vibrational modes near the reaction sites [1,5,6]. This, in turn, led to cluster-size dependent reactivity. This phenomenon was particularly evident in the decomposition of nitrous oxide by hydrated cobalt(I) clusters, where hydration determines the major ligand-binding modes and hence influences reactivity by altering reaction mechanisms [2]. Similarly, cluster-size dependent effects were crucial in hydrogen evolution reactions involving hydrated aluminum hydride-hydroxide species and other metal centers [1,3]. Size-dependent alterations of solvation structures were also applied to other systems, such as metal ions solvated in organic environments, which have potential implications on biochemical reactions and chiral differentiations based on ion-molecule assemblies [4,9]. These studies underscore the ability of the immediate solvent environment to alter energy barriers, thereby controlling reaction mechanisms and chemical reactivity.

11305420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305420.value: This project aimed to improve our understanding on the cluster-size dependent reaction mechanism of hydrated carbon dioxide radical anion by means of quantum chemical calculations. Elucidating the evolution of solvation structure of hydrated carbon dioxide radical during the chemical reaction was experimentally challenging, therefore necessitating an atomistic, time-resolved perspective using finite hydrated clusters via computational studies. We had identified a several crucial factors governing the cluster-dependent reactivity. One of the factors was the competition of enthalpic effect between maximizing hydrogen bonding for favorable water rearrangements and providing stabilization of hydrated ions through additional hydrogen bonding. Both effects resulted in a mixture of conformers and presumably influenced the reactivity of the reaction sites. As the cluster size increased, the entropic advantage of more flexible water arrangements which still adequately solvate the anion might start to play a more significant role. Further studies on larger cluster sizes and on the preference of surface or internal ionic hydration and their respective reactivity toward organic substrates would be beneficial for further understanding the reactivity of carbon dioxide radical anion in bulk water and at air/water interface. We will examine their detailed ionic structures experimentally by gas-phase action spectroscopy in the future.

11305420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305420.value: This research has demonstrated the profound influence of solvation on mediating the reactivity of highly reactive radical, anions or cations, species critical to reactions across diverse chemical environments, from gas-phase clusters to condense phases, by employing advanced quantum chemical calculations. Our simulations of hydrated clusters, serving as model systems, revealed that the sites of hydration around a charged solute are highly fluxional and critically dependent on the number of solvating water molecules. Our theoretical results suggested that varying degrees of hydration can either mask or promote the intrinsic reactivity of the solvated species. These findings affirm the crucial role of water molecules as active participants in influencing reaction mechanisms within charged systems. The outcomes of this research have been published in several prestigious international journals and presented at recognized international conferences. Future research will extend these investigations to larger clusters, aiming to understand the reactivity of these solvated species in bulk water, at air/water interface, or organic media, which could have wide implications for both fundamental chemistry and the gas-phase sciences community.

11305920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305920.value: Heterocycles are a class of important compound not only because of their ubiquitous presence in nature, but also their widespread applications in medicinal chemistry and materials science. Although organic heterocycles have been the main focus in the exploration and development of heterocyclic compounds, research on metalated heterocycles (M-Het) is falling behind presumably because of the sparseness of general synthetic methods. To tackle this issue, we propose to develop a “metal-induced alkyne cycloisomerization” strategy to prepare a variety of new M-Het. Our preliminary results not only demonstrate that a number of unprecedented M-Het can be prepared through this approach, but also reveal the existence of unconventional metal-alkyne reaction pathways. Moreover, the resultant M-Het exhibit interesting biological and material properties which deserve further exploration. Overall, this study will offer useful insight into the rational design of functional M-Het and catalytic cycloisomerization reactions for various applications. 11305920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305920.value: This research successfully achieved the proposed objectives through systematic investigations of metal-induced alkyne cycloisomerization strategies, leading to the discovery of novel metalated heterocycles and mechanistic insights. The key findings are summarized below: (1) Diverse Alkyne Activation Pathways (Objectives 1 & 3): Reactions of cis-[M(dppm)₂Cl₂] (M = Ru/Os) with pyridine/quinoline-substituted homopropargylic alcohols revealed temperature-dependent selectivity between vinylidene and non-vinylidene pathways. At lower temperatures, alkyne cyclization proceeded via a non-vinylidene route, yielding alkenyl intermediates that further transformed into metallapyrroloindolizines. Conversely, higher temperatures favored vinylidene-mediated cyclization, producing cyclic oxacarbene complexes. A rare decyclization mechanism was identified, converting a metallacyclization-resistant alkenyl complex into an oxacarbene structure. DFT calculations corroborated these experimental observations, providing a deeper understanding of pathway selectivity. (2) Synthesis and Anticancer Applications of Metallafurans (Objectives 1 & 4): A series of Ru(II) metallafuran complexes were synthesized from reactions involving diphosphine/diarsine ligands and ynones. Notably, these complexes, including methoxy-substituted and phosphonium-ring-fused ruthenafurans, were derived from Ru(II)–vinylidene intermediates. In vitro cytotoxicity studies against HeLa cancer cells demonstrated that these metallafurans exhibit ~10× higher potency than cisplatin, highlighting their potential as next-generation anticancer agents. (3) Controlling Indole Metalation Pathways (Objectives 2 & 3): Studies on Ru(II)-catalyzed cyclization of 2-alkynylanilines revealed that temperature, solvent polarity, and substrate structure dictate pathway selectivity between C2- vs. C3-metalated indole zwitterions. A rare decyclization mechanism was observed, enabling conversion of C2-metalated indoles into C3-metalated species. These findings provide practical strategies for designing selective catalysts and functionalized metal-heterocycles. (4) Unprecedented Halogenated Metallacycles (Objectives 1 & 3): Introduction of halide substituents on pyridyl-alkyne substrates led to the formation of Ru(II)/Os(II)–haloquinolizine complexes, featuring unique M–X–C–N–C rings (X = F, Cl, Br). These complexes displayed atypical metal–halocarbon bonding interactions, which were reversible under basic conditions, yielding quinolizinium-fused ruthenaoxazoles. This work underscores the significance of halogen–metal interactions in coordination chemistry and catalysis. Conclusion: This project has significantly advanced the understanding of metal-induced alkyne cycloisomerization, demonstrating precise control over reaction pathways and yielding structurally diverse metalated heterocycles with promising applications in medicinal chemistry and catalysis. The mechanistic insights, supported by kinetic studies and DFT calculations, provide a foundation for future catalyst design and functional material development.

11305920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305920.value: This research opens exciting opportunities for further development across multiple fronts. Building on our mechanistic insights, future work will systematically investigate how reaction conditions govern selectivity between vinylidene and non-vinylidene pathways, with the goal of developing catalytic versions of these transformations for sustainable heterocycle synthesis. We will expand the structural diversity of these systems by exploring new alkyne substrates containing thiophene or carbazole moieties, while also examining how different transition metals like iridium or rhodium influence reactivity patterns. The promising anticancer activity observed in our metallafuran complexes warrants detailed structure-activity relationship studies to optimize their potency and selectivity, followed by in vivo evaluation of the most promising candidates. Concurrently, we will explore materials applications by characterizing the photophysical properties of these metalated heterocycles for potential use in optoelectronic devices. Our proposed timeline allocates the first two years for fundamental mechanistic studies and substrate expansion, followed by catalytic applications and preclinical biological testing in years three to four. This balanced approach ensures both continued scientific discovery and practical translation of our findings, with potential impacts spanning synthetic chemistry, medicinal development, and materials innovation.

11305920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305920.value: This research developed innovative methods to synthesize metal-containing heterocyclic compounds through controlled alkyne cyclization reactions. By systematically investigating ruthenium and osmium complexes, we established how reaction conditions determine whether these transformations proceed through vinylidene or non-vinylidene pathways - a fundamental mechanistic distinction in organometallic chemistry. The significance lies in our demonstration that simple modifications in temperature or substrate structure can selectively direct these metal-mediated cyclizations toward distinct product classes. Particularly noteworthy is our discovery of novel ruthenafuran complexes exhibiting remarkable cytotoxicity against cancer cells, surpassing cisplatin's potency by an order of magnitude. These findings provide valuable insights for several applications: (1) rational design of new catalytic systems for heterocycle synthesis, (2) development of next-generation metallodrug candidates, and (3) creation of functional metal-organic materials. The work advances fundamental understanding of metal-alkyne interactions while offering practical methodologies with potential pharmaceutical and technological applications. Our mechanistic elucidation, supported by computational studies, establishes general principles that will guide future research in transition metal chemistry and its interdisciplinary applications.

11306220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306220.value: 高維區域上積分離散化的逼近理論

11306220.label: Project Objectives
11306220.value: The first objective of this project is to investigate error analysis for the integral discretization with probabilistic techniques. The class of functions we shall consider are piecewise polynomials define on unit spheres and some related domains. The approximation error will decay in a universal order without effect of dimensionality. The second objective is to explore a constructive proof for error analysis of the integral discretization by ``derandomization'' methods. The desired result would give the same bound as the probabilistic approach does. The third objective is to apply desired results in above to study approximation on spheres by deep ReLU neural network. Based on specific topological structures, the existing approximation analysis is expected to be improved.

11306220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306220.value: To make a continuous problem computationally feasible, it is often desired to approximate an integration by a discrete summation. Then it is natural to ask how to choose the sampling points and what decay of the error with the growing number of sampling points is. Investigation in this direction includes cubeture formulas, Marcinkiewcz-Zygmund inequalities and sampling discretization. Recently, a systematic study of these problems has begun and gained attraction in different areas of research, ranging over supervised learning theory, numerical integration and discrepancy theory. Modern problems are often formulated on various regular domains, such as spheres, cubes, balls, and simplexes, driven by applications in engineering and data analysis. At the current stage, however, in contrast to the situation in low dimensional domains, many fundamental problems are in demand. Actually, only with classical smoothness assumptions (such as Lipschitz or Besov regularity) on the underlying functions, approximation rates deteriorate severely with the dimensionality. This is the so-called curse of dimensionality. The purpose of this project is to investigate integral discretization on unit spheres for a certain class of functions without suffering the effect of dimensionality. Precisely, we aim at building a good finite set of points on a multidimensional domain and investigating the error analysis of integral discretization by using function values on the points. Then we shall apply the expected results to study approximation on spheres by ReLU neural networks. 為使連續問題在計算上具有可行性，人們通常需要通過離散求和來近似積分。那麼自然我們要研究如何選擇採樣點以及隨著採樣點數量的增加誤差的衰減量速率怎樣。在這個方向上的研究包括求積公式，Marcinkiewcz-Zygmund不等式和採樣離散化。最近，對這些問題系統的研究已經開始，並在不同的研究領域中引起了廣泛關注，其中涉及到監督學習理論，數值積分和差異理論。 在现代工程和數據分析的應用中，需要解決的問題大多發生在多維規則區域，如，球面，方體，球體和單純形。然而，當前階段 除了在低維領域，許多基本問題還亟待解決。實際上，在只對函數光滑度作基本假設的情況下（例如Lipschitz或Besov正則性）,積分 逼近速率會隨維度增長而嚴重惡化。這就是所謂的維數災難。該項目的目的是研究一類特定函數在單位球面上積分離散化而不會遭受維數的影響。具體地說， 我們的目標是在高維區域建立一個具有良好性質的有限點集並探究通過此點集上進行採樣的積分離散化的誤差分析。隨後這樣的預期結果將會應用於研究ReLU神經網絡在球面上的逼近。

11306220.label: Realisation of objectives
11306220.value: By methods to obtain the integration discretization results on unit spheres and balls, we achieve an extensive estimate of approximation error by deep neural networks. The work on approximation analysis using tools related to spherical analysis (which can be part of broader efforts in integral discretization) shows progress. The consideration of approximating functions in the Lp space when dealing with the classification problem on spheres is related to understanding approximation errors in a different context. The analysis provides rates of Lp-approximation when the approximated function lies in a Sobolev space, which is part of building a framework for analyzing errors in a relevant setting, thus contributing to the overall goal of error analysis for integral discretization in the domain of spherical functions. The objectives have been also achieved to a significant degree by developing generalization analysis of a deep CNN algorithm for binary classification and pairwise learning with data on spheres. It makes use of efficient cubature formulae on spheres and other tools from spherical analysis and approximation theory. By leveraging these elements, the team was able to present generalization bounds and learning rates for the excess misclassification error of the deep CNN classification algorithm. This application not only studies approximation on spheres using neural networks but also advances the theoretical understanding of the generalization ability of CNN algorithms in this specific context, thereby improving on existing approximation analysis in the sphere-related domain. On the other hand, through the construction of the novel area-regular hierarchical discretization on the 2-sphere and the corresponding spherical Haar tight framelets with directionality, we develop a general theoretical frame work for constructing Haar-type tight framelets on any compact set with a hierarchical partition. We conclude by evaluating and illustrate the effectiveness of our area-regular spherical Haar tight framelets in several denoising experiments. Furthermore, we propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for spherical signal denoising which employs the fast framelet decomposition and reconstruction algorithms. Experiment results show that our pro-posed CNN model outperforms threshold methods, and processes strong generalization and robustness properties. In addition, by developing a novel integral operator approach using spherical quadrature rules, we manage to derive optimal approximation rates for DWRLS. We also theoretically prove that DWRLS functions similarly to running a weighted regularized least squares algorithm on all the data stored on a sufficiently large machine. This gives rise to a distributed weighted regularized least squares algorithm (DWRLS) with radial basis functions, which is designed to handle spherical data that are distributed across numerous local servers and cannot be shared among them. This intriguing finding suggests that distributed learning can effectively exploit the potential values of distributively stored spherical data, even when local servers cannot access the entire dataset.

Precisely, the method was developed to obtain integration discretization results on unit spheres and balls, enabling an extensive estimate of approximation error by fully connected neural networks. And an area-regular hierarchical discretization on the 2-sphere was constructed, and the corresponding spherical Haar tight framelets with directionality were established. This led to the development of a general theoretical framework for constructing Haar-type tight framelets on any compact set with a hierarchical partition. With the constructions, for functions defined on spheres (such as piecewise polynomials), approximation error decay in a universal order. Furthermore, rates of Lp-approximation were provided when the approximated function lies in a Sobolev space, and generalization bounds and learning rates for the excess misclassification error of deep CNN classification algorithms were presented. This was achieved by leveraging efficient cubature formulae on spheres and other tools from spherical analysis and approximation theory. For the applications in Neural Network-based Approaches, the integral discretization tool was applied to develop generalization analysis of a deep convolutional neural network for binary classification with data on spheres, enhancing the theoretical understanding of the generalization ability of CNNs in this context. A convolutional neural network (CNN) model for spherical signal denoising was proposed, which employed the fast framelet decomposition and reconstruction algorithms based on the developed spherical Haar tight framelets. Experiment results showed that this CNN model outperforms threshold methods and has strong generalization and robustness properties. In the paper [5], via developing a novel integral operator approach based on spherical quadrature rules, we succeed in deriving optimal approximation rates for DWRLS and theoretically demonstrate that DWRLS performs similarly as running a weighted regularized least squares algorithm on the whole data stored on a large enough machine. This leads to a distributed weighted regularized least squares algorithm (DWRLS) with radial basis functions to tackle spherical data that are stored across numerous local servers and cannot be shared with each other. This interesting finding implies that distributed learning is capable of sufficiently exploiting potential values of distributively stored spherical data, even though local servers cannot access the whole data.

11306220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306220.value: The research has potential for further development. One possible course of action could be to deepen the exploration of construction of area-regular hierarchical discretization for error analysis. This would help in strengthening the theoretical foundation and providing more robust error analysis techniques. Additionally, expanding the application of the developed methods and frameworks to other types of neural networks and a wider variety of data sets on spheres could enhance the generality and practicality. For example, testing on different types of spherical data from various scientific and engineering domains. Further research could also focus on optimizing the performance of the spherical signal denoising CNN model, perhaps by incorporating advanced optimization algorithms or novel architectural designs. Investigating its potential in more complex signal processing tasks, such as multi-modal spherical signal processing or real-time applications, would open up new avenues for practical implementation and innovation.

11306520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306520.value: When electronics and optoelectronics meet in a same affordable device platform, they can enable many unique applications to enhance our life quality. For example, it would be feasible to have a device with multi-functionality that emits and detects light as well as simultaneously switches current as a transistor for next-generation digital displays. However, until now, the conventional electronic material (i.e. silicon) still cannot satisfy the need of active materials for such a device. The challenge is that there is always a lack of low-cost high-performance materials with the capability not only to generate (or absorb) light but also to have charge carriers transported efficiently. Recently, the advent of organic-inorganic hybrid lead halide perovskite nanomaterials has led to a major step forward in light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and solar cells, and pathed promising avenues for transistors; but at the same time these perovskites are quite restricted by the complexity of preparing organic components, air instability, lead toxicity concern and incompatibility with standard integrated circuit processes (e.g. lithography) for practical utilizations. More importantly, these perovskites are usually polycrystalline with lots of grain boundaries, which make the performance of their electronic devices far behind the optoelectronic counterparts. As a result, there are still many issues and opportunities in the fundamental studies and the performance evaluation of high-performance nanostructured perovskite transistors. In this proposal, we will investigate the direct synthesis of single-crystal, all-inorganic, air-stable and lead-free perovskite (e.g., cesium tin halide and cesium bismuth halide) nanowires and the efficient doping scheme to enhance the nanowire electronic transport properties. Perovskite-compatible fabrication processes will also be studied to achieve the advanced nanowire device structures on silicon, glass and plastic substrates. Utilizing the nanowire printing technique, uniform perovskite nanowire parallel arrays will as well be assembled at large scales for the construction and the device performance limit assessment of high-performance thin-film transistors and integrated circuits. Combined with the well-known excellent optoelectronic properties of perovskite nanostructures for LEDs and solar cells, our ultimate goal is to achieve a versatile and promising device platform for highly-efficient and low-cost integrated optoelectronic circuits and systems that purely base on crystalline, all-inorganic and lead-free perovskite nanowires. 當電子器件和光電子器件相互融合時，它們會產生許多獨特的應用，這會對我們的生活產生深遠的影響。以新一代顯示為例，我們期望多功能的器件可以同時實現光發射和光探測，並且能像晶體管一樣實現電流開關。然而，目前為止，現有的傳統半導體材料（如，矽）並不能滿足上述的需求。所以，開發既能產生（或探測）光又具有優良載流子傳輸能力的低成本材料是亟需解決的問題。最近，有機-無機雜化鈣鈦礦材料的進步促進了發光二極管和太陽能電池領域的跨越式發展，也在晶體管等領域展現了巨大的潛力。同時，鈣鈦礦材料在空氣穩定性、毒性和與現有半導體工藝（如，光刻）兼容性等方面的問題也為其實際應用設下了障礙。另外需要注意的是，鈣鈦礦材料通常是多晶態的，含有大量的晶界，這使得鈣鈦礦電子器件的性能遠不如其在光電子器件中的性能。因此，研究基於單晶鈣鈦礦納米結構的高性能晶體管需要克服很多的問題，但這也展現了前所未有的機遇。在本申請書中，我們計劃合成單晶、全無機、空氣穩定的無鉛鈣鈦礦（如，銫錫基、銫鉍基鈣鈦礦）納米線，通過有效的摻雜方法調控其電子傳輸性能。我們也會開發與鈣鈦礦材料兼容的半導體製備工藝，進而實現鈣鈦礦納米線器件在矽、玻璃、塑料等襯底上的集成。另外，利用成熟的納米線印刷技術，製備得到大面積的鈣鈦礦納米線平行陣列，實現薄膜晶體管和集成電路等應用。結合其優異光電性能（如在發光二極管和太陽能電池中所展現的），我們的目標是構建一個完全基於單晶、全無機、無鉛鈣鈦礦納米線的多功能器件平台，最終建成一個高效、低成本的集成光電電路和系統。

11306520.label: Realisation of objectives
11306520.value: In this project, we have accomplished all the objectives with 100% completion. Specifically, we developed an enhanced synthesis technique to obtain high-quality all-inorganic, air-stable, and lead-free perovskite nanowires (NWs), such as Cs3Sb2I9 and Cs3Sb2Br9, with well-controlled physical, chemical, and electrical properties using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method (Objective 1). In the scientific community, Sb and Sn are common species that are suggested to replace Pb for Pb-free all-inorganic halide perovskites. However, the large difference in the melting points of the precursor materials (e.g., CsBr and SbBr3 precursors for Cs3Sb2Br9) makes the CVD growth of high-quality Pb-free perovskites a very challenging task. Here, we came up with a two-step CVD approach to grow Cs3Sb2Br9 NWs to overcome these challenges encountered in a conventional CVD process. In this two-step CVD process, after the sequential deposition of binary compounds in step I and step II, a low-temperature annealing process was used to form the ternary products. Using this new CVD approach, we successfully synthesized all-inorganic and lead-free Cs3Sb2Br9 NWs with regulated geometries, including length, diameter, and surface conditions. Once the lead-free perovskite NWs were fabricated, we assessed the effect of NW stoichiometries, surface conditions, diameters, orientations, and device channel lengths on their intrinsic carrier transport characteristics and operational stabilities (Objective 2). For example, We utilized these Cs3Sb2Br9 NWs to fabricate photoconductive devices with a metal/semiconductor/metal (MSM) configuration. Before manufacturing the device, we determined the metal's electronic band alignment. Using ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy, we determined the position of the valence band maximum of Cs3Sb2Br9 to be 5.51 eV below the vacuum level. Au has a work function of 5.1 eV and is considered a good contact metal for this MSM photodetector. The fabricated device exhibited a reasonable performance with an on/off current ratio reaching 2.36E2, responsivity of up to 36.9 mA/W, and detectivity of up to 1.0E10 Jones at an irradiation wavelength of 450 nm. Moreover, relatively fast rise and decay times of 61.5 and 24 ms, respectively, were demonstrated. These results clearly suggested that the two-step CVD process could be used to synthesize high-quality all-inorganic and lead-free Cs3Sb2Br9 perovskite materials for the fabrication of high-performance optoelectronic devices. Subsequently, employing the NW contact printing, we were able to achieve the highly dense, regular, and uniform perovskite NW parallel arrays (Objective 3). Notably, apart from the developing process of assembling NW arrays, it is also critical to control the surface orientation of the assembled NWs since the degree of surface passivation is highly dependent on the NWs’ orientation. Also, such surface passivation has also been developed to enhance the electronic and optoelectronic performance and long-term stability of perovskites. Environmental gases are especially well known to have a considerable regulatory effect on the properties of halide perovskite surfaces.[7] In this project, surface passivation with oxygen gas has been found to enhance light-emission efficiencies and spontaneous carrier recombination lifetimes, owing to the passivation to surface traps induced by bromine vacancies. Based on these selective (100) NW surfaces, the fabricated photodetectors (PDs) with oxygen passivation exhibited excellent optoelectronic performance with a high on/off ratio of 5E4, a large responsivity of 263 AW−1, an impressive detectivity of 1.06E12 Jones. The NW parallel arrayed PDs unveil an outstanding long-term ambient stability >3000 h. Apart from single devices, the NW arrays were further explored to construct thin-film transistors (TFTs) and their integration into functional circuits (Objectives 4 and 5). Generally, one-dimensional NWs with good waveguiding and oscillating cavities offer robust material platforms for complex nano-photonics and functional optoelectronic devices. Using the phase segregation characteristics of perovskite alloy components under laser illumination, we could then construct an optical switch by defining the output intensity ratio of the low energy band (IO-LEB) to the high energy band (IO-HEB). When the NW array was excited by a 375 nm focused laser, the output waveguide signal was changed with the phase separation at the excitation positions. Initially, an active waveguide occurred along the wire through re-absorption and re-emission processes for the high energy band emission. Then, with the emergence of phase segregation, the PL emission (690 nm) of the low energy band was expected to be passively guided along the axial of the wires through total internal reflections. It could be seen that the IO-LEB was increased with the decrease of IO-HEB, which meant that the ratio of IO-LEB /IO-HEB was increased. This way, the optical switch of 0 and 1 was defined by IO-LEB/IO-HEB<1 and IO-LEB/IO-HEB≧1. Thus, according to the results, a time-delay optical switch was realized based on these perovskite NW arrays controlled by a laser beam. On the other hand, when integrating with n-type 2D materials forming 2D/1D n/p heterostructures, the multifunctionality of multi-value logic and frequency doubling was demonstrated synchronously. Through stoichiometric variation, the multi-element feature of perovskite allowed the modulation of electronic properties and band alignment with MoS2 nanoflake. Owing to the strongly coupled heterointerface and high intrinsic carrier mobility of both constituents, the developed mixed-dimensional heterojunctions presented pronounced anti-ambipolarity and gate-tunable rectifying behavior. A multi-valued inverter exhibiting three true logic states was achieved by engineering the partition load based on 2D/1D anti-ambipolar transistor (AAT) devices. Besides, anti-ambipolarity also facilitated the realization of analog signal processing, like frequency multipliers. In light of this, the frequency-doubling performance was evaluated using the AAT unit device based on the output voltage frequency on the loading resistance doubled relative to the input signal. These high-performance devices herald the technological potential of the mixed-dimensional anti-ambipolar heterojunction for future versatile electronics. Overall, we have successfully fabricated high-quality, all-inorganic, and lead-free perovskite NW arrays. The crystalline and inorganic nature could enable efficient charge carrier transport and sensitive photodetection. More importantly, we established a versatile and powerful technology platform to develop a robust large-scale integration path to realize thin-film transistors and functional circuits compatible with current TFT technologies.

11306520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306520.value: Specifically, as reported in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2021 (Output Paper #4), a two-step chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method was developed to synthesize high-quality all-inorganic, air-stable, and lead-free perovskite nanowires (NWs) and nanoplates, such as Cs3Sb2I9 and Cs3Sb2Br9, with well-controlled physical, chemical, and electrical properties. In this two-step CVD process, after the sequential deposition of binary compounds in step I and step II, a low-temperature annealing process was used to form the ternary products. We obtained all-inorganic and lead-free perovskite nanomaterials with regulated geometries, including length, diameter, and surface conditions, using this new CVD approach. The lead-free perovskites were then constructed into photoconductive devices that gave a reasonable performance with an on/off current ratio reaching 2.36E2, responsivity of up to 36.9 mA/W, and detectivity of up to 1.0 × 1010 Jones at an irradiation wavelength of 450 nm. More importantly, as illustrated in Nature Materials 2023 (Output Paper #8), morphing all-inorganic perovskite nanomaterials into specific shapes and geometries without damaging their intrinsic functional properties was demonstrated for designing devices and manufacturing. By in situ compression, the single-crystal perovskite micro- and nano-pillars could be substantially deformed into distinct shapes (cubic, L, and Z shapes, rectangular arches, and so on) without localized cleavage or cracks. Such exceptional plasticity was enabled by successive slips of partial dislocations on multiple systems, as evidenced by atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy, first principles, and atomistic simulations. The electronic, optoelectronic performance and bandgap of the devices were unchanged. Later, as reported in Small Methods 2023 (Output Paper #9), one kind of new electrode, the metalloids, was revealed, which are much more stable than the conventional noble metals as electrical contacts for halide perovskites. The degradation mechanism of halide perovskites with noble metal electrodes was carefully studied and compared with the metalloid electrodes. It is found that the iodide ions could easily halogenate Cu and Ag in halide perovskites. Although Au was almost not halogenated, it could also decompose the perovskite film. On the contrary, after long-term storage, the metalloid electrodes remained intact on perovskites without degradation. The long-time operation stability of the perovskite devices with metalloid electrodes was much higher than that of noble metals. First-principles calculations confirm the exceptional stability of the metalloid electrodes. In summary, all these major findings are significant and create relevant design guidelines for lead-free perovskite nanowires-based electronic and optoelectronic devices to go beyond the conventional thin-film technologies for future utilizations.

11306520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306520.value: While this work has generated many significant results, further investigation is needed in several areas to advance lead-free perovskite nanowire-based electronics and optoelectronics. For example, surface passivation can help isolate material defects on the surface, minimizing their adverse effects on the nanowires' chemical and physical properties. It is crucial to explore different surface passivation techniques and evaluate their impact on various surface orientations of the nanowires. Different surface orientations may yield different results due to variations in defect characteristics and concentrations. Moreover, most current perovskite nanomaterials have carrier mobility values significantly lower than their theoretical limits. One limiting factor could be the nature of the electrical metal contacts. Therefore, it is essential to conduct systematic studies to improve their charge transport properties and understand their underlying mechanisms. Enhancing these properties would significantly facilitate the deployment of perovskite-based electronics and optoelectronics. Further research in these areas will push lead-free perovskite nanowire-based systems closer to practical applications.

11306520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306520.value: When affordable electronics and optoelectronics are combined in a single device, they can create many unique applications that improve our quality of life. For example, imagine a device that can emit and detect light while also acting as a transistor to switch current for next-generation digital displays. Traditional electronic materials like silicon haven't been able to meet the needs of such multifunctional devices. However, recent advances in organic-inorganic hybrid lead halide perovskite nanomaterials have made significant strides in LEDs and solar cells, and have shown promise for transistors. Despite these advances, these perovskites face challenges such as complex preparation, instability in air, lead toxicity, and incompatibility with standard integrated circuit processes. In this work, we developed a method to directly synthesize all-inorganic, lead-free perovskite nanowires with controlled physical, chemical, and electrical properties. We successfully created nanowire arrays to build large-scale thin-film transistors and functional circuits. By combining the excellent optoelectronic properties of perovskite nanostructures for LEDs and solar cells, we can now create a versatile and promising device platform. This platform is highly efficient, low-cost, and based entirely on crystalline, all-inorganic, lead-free perovskite nanowires, paving the way for advanced integrated optoelectronic circuits and systems.

11306720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306720.value: Dion-Jacobson层状钙钛矿的局域结构以及铁电弛豫行为研究

11306720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306720.value: 铁电材料具有自发极化并且极化方向可由外电场反转。近几十年来，铁电材料因其独特的介电、压电、热释电、光电以及铁电性能得到固体物理学家以及材料学家的广泛研究。铁电材料在电容器、传感器、驱动器、非易失性存储器、能量获取装置以及电信等领域都有着重要应用。最常见的铁电材料是分子通式为ABO3、具有钙钛矿晶体结构的复杂氧化物。由于在极端工作条件下应用的需求，对其他结构复杂氧化物的铁电性能的研究显得十分必要。在这一方面，层状钙钛矿因其较高的Tc而展现出了巨大的应用前景。层状钙钛矿包含类钙钛矿层，而层间分布第三种阳离子A'或者A'-O。特别地，化学式为A' [An-1BnO3n+1]的 Dion-Jacobson结构具有高的理论极化强度、极高的Tc（800-1000℃）以及低介电损耗，因而受到广泛关注。尽管如此，需进一步增强Dion-Jacobson铁电材料的介电及压电性能，才能促进Dion-Jacobson铁电材料的应用。 研究表明，可以通过引入弛豫相来提高具有钙钛矿结构以及Aurivillius层状钙钛矿结构的铁电材料的性能。一般的铁电材料存在长程极性有序以及窄的顺电-铁电相转变区域，而弛豫铁电体则存在着纳米极性有序区域以及一个较大温度范围的相转变区间。不同原子位置的固溶取代可引起纳米区域内成分以及结构的不均匀，从而引起弛豫铁电性能。本项目的目标是研究新型的Dion-Jacobson基的弛豫铁电体。为采取合理的方法开发具有Dion-Jacobson结构的弛豫铁电材料，对局部原子相关性的研究显得格外重要。我们使用对分布函数法在该领域的初步研究表明，Dion-Jacobson化合物中的氧八面体旋转与极性原子位移之间的相互作用会导致局域结构偏离长程平均结构。基于这一点发现，我们提出通过在不同原子位置(A/B/ A’)上进行适当的化学取代来改变局部的氧八面体旋转以及阳离子-氧键的共价性，从而在Dion-Jacobson相中引入纳米极性有序域和弛豫相。我们的初步研究已经验证了这一假设的可行性，在Dion-Jacobson相结构中，可以通过化学取代改变局域原子的有序性，从而引入类弛豫性能并增强其性能。 在本项目中，我们提出通过对A' [An-1BnO3n+1]化合物中的不同原子位置的固溶取代进行系统的研究，从而引入弛豫行为。取代原子的选择原则是一般通用的晶体化学原则，我们之后会做进一步阐明。本项目的最终目标是发展应用于极端条件下的新型铁电材料。

11306820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306820.value: The design and study of mechanoresponsive polymers is a rapidly developing field. The crosslinking of known mechanophore in polymers represents one of the most effective strategies to develop mechanoresponsive polymers. This strategy enables designing polymers with predictable mechanoresponsive properties. However, the design of crosslinking mechanophores is still in its infancy. Mechanophores capable of undergoing reversible chemical transformation are mainly confined to those of photochromic systems. This limits the development of polymers with desirable mechanoresponsive behavior. In this project, we will developed new classes of crosslinking mechanophores based on our recently developed phosphorescent transition metal complexes showing solid-state luminescent mechanochromism. We anticipated that their mechanoresponsive properties can be systematically modified by varying their coordination system and ligands. As demonstrated in our preliminary results, it is expected that the incorporation of these mechanophores into the polymeric systems would lead to the development of luminescent mechanochromic polymers derived from the mechanochemical changes in these complexes. The proposed design of mechanophores based on luminescent transition metal complexes represents an unexplored area and would definitely initiate new development on mechanoresponsive polymers and soft materials. On the other hand, applications of these polymers as mechanical and chemical sensors will be explored. 力響應性聚合物的設計和研究是一個快速發展的領域。透過力敏團作交聯的聚合物是開發力響應性聚合物的最有效策略之一。這種策略可用於設計不同力響應性能的聚合物。但是，設計含力敏團的交聯劑仍處於起步階段。現時，能夠進行可逆化學轉化的力敏團主要限於光致變色分子系統。這限制了具有力響應性聚合物的開發。 基於最近我們開發的力致發光變色磷光過渡金屬配合物，我們將在這個項目開發出新型的力敏交聯劑。我們預期它們的力響應特性可通過配位系統和修飾配體改變。由初步結果所示，將這些力敏交聯劑引入聚合物體系中，可衍生出力致發光變色的聚合物。這個設計嶄新，並且肯定會帶動力響應性聚合物和軟材料的新發展。另一方面，本項目將研究這些聚合物作為傳感器的應用。

11306820.label: Realisation of objectives
11306820.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details findings are summarized as follows: Objectives 1 and 2: New crosslinker-containing phosphorescent Ir(III), Ru(II), and Re(I) transition metal complexes exhibiting solid-state luminescent mechanochromic properties have been successfully designed, synthesized, and fully characterized using various spectroscopic techniques, including IR, NMR, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis. The molecular structures of several newly designed complexes have also been determined by X-ray crystallography. These complexes have been incorporated or immobilized into a wide range of polymer backbones, including bulk polymers, elastomers, imprinted polymers, and microspheres, resulting in luminescent mechanoresponsive oligomers or polymers. The successful immobilizations have been characterized by IR, Raman, and XPS spectroscopy. The incorporation efficiency was evaluated by determining the percentage of metal complexes in these polymers using ICP-MS after acid digestion. The key results have been reported in journal articles, including Chemical Science (2021), Journal of Catalysis (2022), Dalton Transactions (2023), and Biosensors (2023), as listed in the research output. Additionally, these findings have been presented at international conferences, including the 31st International Conference on Photochemistry and the 49th IUPAC World Chemistry Congress. Objective 3: All newly designed transition metal complexes and their immobilized polymers exhibit intriguing luminescent and mechanoresponsive properties. These properties have been extensively studied using steady-state UV-vis absorption, diffuse reflectance, and emission spectroscopy. Furthermore, the excited-state properties of these materials have been examined using time-resolved emission and transient absorption spectroscopy. Some of these results have been published in Chemical Science (2021), Journal of Catalysis (2022), Dalton Transactions (2023), European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry (2022), and Materials Chemistry Frontiers (2023), as listed in the research output. These findings were also shared through invited lectures at Pacifichem 2021 and the 31st International Conference on Photochemistry. Objective 4: Beyond their mechanoresponsive behavior, some of the newly designed complexes and polymers with immobilized transition metal complexes exhibit excellent photocatalytic, chemosensory, and surface functionalization properties. The photocatalytic applications of these complexes and their polymers for carbon dioxide reduction and organic transformations have been investigated. Notably, the polymer-immobilized photocatalysts demonstrated performance comparable to their solution-state counterparts while offering the added advantage of recyclability. Key results have been published in Langmuir (2021), Energy and Fuels (2021), Journal of Catalysis (2022), and Materials Chemistry Frontiers (2023). In addition to photocatalysis, the luminescent transition metal complexes immobilized on polymers have shown potential as reporters for host-guest interactions between the polymers and analytes, resulting in observable changes in luminescent properties. The chemosensory applications of these complexes and polymers have been published in Chemical Science (2021), Biosensors (2022), and Dalton Transactions (2023). These application studies have also been presented at international conferences, including the 31st International Conference on Photochemistry, the 49th IUPAC World Chemistry Congress, and the 29th IUPAC Symposium on Photochemistry.

11306820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306820.value: This research successfully achieved the design, synthesis, and characterization of new crosslinker-containing phosphorescent Ir(III), Ru(II), and Re(I) transition metal complexes exhibiting solid-state luminescent mechanochromic properties. These complexes were fully characterized using techniques such as IR, NMR, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis, with the molecular structures of several complexes determined by X-ray crystallography. The complexes were incorporated or immobilized into various polymer backbones, including bulk polymers, elastomers, imprinted polymers, and microspheres, to produce luminescent mechanoresponsive oligomers and polymers. The successful immobilization of the complexes was verified through IR, Raman, and XPS spectroscopy, while ICP-MS analyses after acid digestion quantified the incorporation efficiencies. The newly designed transition metal complexes and their immobilized polymers exhibited intriguing luminescent and mechanoresponsive properties, which were extensively studied through steady-state UV-vis absorption, diffuse reflectance, and emission spectroscopy. Their excited-state properties were further characterized using time-resolved emission and transient absorption spectroscopy. Beyond the mechanoresponsive and phosphorescent materials applications, the newly designed transition metal complexes and their immobilized polymers demonstrated excellent photocatalytic, chemosensory, and surface functionalization applications. The photocatalytic performance of these materials for carbon dioxide reduction and organic transformations was comparable to their solution-state counterparts, with the added advantage of recyclability. Moreover, the luminescent complexes immobilized on polymers also served as chemosensors, detecting host-guest interactions of the polymer backbone through observable luminescent changes. These application studies were published in Chemical Science (2021), Langmuir (2021), Energy and Fuels (2021), Journal of Catalysis (2022), Materials Chemistry Frontiers (2023), Biosensors (2022), and Dalton Transactions (2023). Additionally, these results were presented at the 31st International Conference on Photochemistry, the 49th IUPAC World Chemistry Congress, and the 29th IUPAC Symposium on Photochemistry. Building on this work, a new design strategy has been established for developing functional materials with mechanoresponsive, photocatalytic, and chemosensory properties.

11306820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306820.value: As discussed in Section 6.1, the outcomes of this project have resulted in the development of new classes of recyclable heterogeneous photocatalysts and chemosensors. Detailed mechanistic studies of these photocatalysts and chemosensors revealed that the quenching rate constants of the polymer-bound guest molecules (quenchers) are several orders of magnitude higher than the diffusion limit. Building on these findings, we have initiated new research directions to develop heterogeneous photocatalysts for the selective activation of target substrates. Preliminary experiments have already demonstrated the feasibility of this proposed approach, and a research proposal focused on the development of photocatalysts for selective substrate activation has been submitted. In parallel, efforts are underway to develop new luminescent chemosensors, based on the strategies established in this project, for applications in environmental monitoring. These ongoing developments aim to expand the practical utility of the materials designed in this work, addressing critical challenges in catalysis and sensing.

11306820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306820.value: This research focused on developing new materials that emit light (emission) and respond to mechanical stimuli, such as grinding, pressure, or stretching. These materials were created using metal-based compounds, such as those of iridium, ruthenium, or rhenium metal centers, linked to flexible or solid plastics. The materials were carefully studied to understand their light-emission properties and how they react to external stimuli or changing conditions. In addition to their ability to change color or emission brightness under stimulations, these materials demonstrated important practical applications. For example, they can serve as photocatalysts to facilitate the conversion of carbon dioxide into useful chemicals or assist in other chemical reactions. Notably, these photocatalysts are reusable, making them more sustainable for industrial processes. Additionally, they can function as chemical sensors, detecting specific compounds by altering their light emission, which makes them valuable for environmental and pollution monitoring. The findings from this research introduce a new approach to designing advanced materials that combine light-emission capabilities with practical applications in areas such as sustainable energy, environmental monitoring, and smart sensors. This work has the potential to drive innovations in material science, benefiting both industry and sustainability initiatives.

11306920.value: 基於電化學的合成技術用於開發太陽能水分解的納米光電極

11306920.label: Project Objectives
11306920.value: Establishment of two new anodisation-based technologies for photoelectode fabrication (method development). The first method will combine anodisation with pulse-electrodeposition and the second will use a hydrothermal treatment to modify anodised oxide films. Fabrication of optimised photoelectrodes, using these two methods, of novel structure and composition for efficient photoelectrochemical water splitting (materials development). The photoanodes will be based on anodised films of three metal oxides – TiO2, WO3, and MoO3 – which will be transformed to enhance visible-light absorption and improve charge separation and transport. Assessment of photoelectrode performance followed by advanced in-situ PEC water splitting testing. Photoelectrodes will be made into devices and the water splitting efficiency will be evaluated using a closed gas circulation-low pressure system coupled with Pyrex/quartz inner-irradiation configuration. Mechanistic understanding of the relationships between efficiency of photoelectrodes and the nanostructure-induced modulation of optical/electronic properties.
