11306920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306920.value: Photoactive materials in thin film configuration (i.e. photoelectrodes) are promising for harnessing solar energy. With current fabrication methods, these thin films often suffer from poor charge transport and stability, hindering their wider application. Fabrication by electrochemical-based methods could potentially overcome these problems. In this project, innovative thin film fabrication methods based on anodisation will be developed that allow synthesis of robust, nanostructured films with compositions and structures optimised for high efficiency. This will lead to new photoelectrodes for efficient solar hydrogen generation, which is crucial for a sustainable energy future. New knowledge will also be developed, resulting in general design principles for photoelectrodes for a range of devices. The goal of this research is conversion and chemical storage of solar energy in the form of hydrogen. This will be achieved through development of novel photoelectrode thin film fabrication methods, which will allow the design of photoactive thin films that have higher efficiency and better long-term stability than has been possible in the past. By developing robust and efficient photoelectrodes, the proposed research aims to address key challenges for sustaining Hong Kong’s energy future. 薄膜構造的光敏材料（即光電極）有望有效利用和轉化太陽能。在當前的製造方法中，這些薄膜經常遭受較差的電荷傳輸和穩定性，從而阻礙了其更廣泛的應用。通過基於電化學的方法製造可以潛在地克服這些問題。在這個項目中，我們將開發基於陽極氧化的創新薄膜製造方法，該方法可合成具有為高效而優化的成分和結構的納米薄膜。這將有助於開發高效太陽能產氫的新光電極，對於發展可持續能源的未來至關重要。嶄新的知識也將得到發展，從而形成一系列光電極器件通用的設計原理。 這項研究的目標是以氫的形式轉化和存儲太陽能。這將通過開發新穎的光電極薄膜製造方法來實現。光活性薄膜的設計將具有比過去更高的效率和更好的長期穩定性。通過開發耐用及高效的光電極，這項研究將可提升香港對於能源挑戰的能力。

11306920.label: Realisation of objectives
11306920.value: In this Completion Report, the PI and his research team have investigated comprehensively the elements covered in all four project objectives with measurable success. The details are as follows: 1. Objective 1: Establishment of two new anodisation-based technologies for photoelectode fabrication (method development). The first method will combine anodisation with pulse-electrodeposition and the second will use a hydrothermal treatment to modify anodised oxide films. Anodisation-based electrochemical methods have been developed. A number of oxide photoelectrodes have been investigated. For instance, Bi2WO6/WO3 heterojunction thin films with low or high interfacial contact between the Bi2WO6 and WO3 photocatalyst were employed as the photoanode for photoelectrochemical (PEC) reactions. By modulation of the transformation of WO3 to Bi2WO6 via a combined electrodeposition and hydrothermal reaction, a controlled degree of interfacial contact between Bi2WO6 and WO3 was achieved. An increase in the anodic photocurrent was observed from the PEC measurement, which was further supported by the conductive atomic force microscopy analysis under a low applied bias when the higher Bi2WO6/WO3 interfacial contact photoelectrode was examined. Experiment results suggested that the improvement was ascribed to a lower density of surface trap of the photoelectrons that reduced the charge recombination rate within the bulk photocatalyst. 2. Objective 2: Fabrication of optimised photoelectrodes, using these two methods, of novel structure and composition for efficient photoelectrochemical water splitting (materials development). The photoanodes will be based on anodised films of three metal oxides – TiO2, WO3, and MoO3 – which will be transformed to enhance visible-light absorption and improve charge separation and transport. Visible light absorption and charge separation and transport of oxide photoelectrodes have been investigated thoroughly. For instance, we reported the modulation of the metal–support interaction by depositing copper nanoparticles on anatase TiO2 with different facet exposures, i.e., (001) and (101) facets. The result of copper nanoparticles being deposited on TiO2 with dominant (101) facet exposure is an enhanced ammonia yield rate of 447.5 μg mgcat−1 h−1 at −0.9 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), which is 4.2 times higher than the pristine TiO2 counterpart. The strong interaction between copper nanoparticles and TiO2 with dominant (101) facet exposure contributes to a greater increase in catalytic performance than TiO2 with dominant (001) facet exposure. The strong interaction leads to electron-deficient copper nanoparticles, and efficient electron transfer. 3. Objective 3: Assessment of photoelectrode performance followed by advanced in-situ PEC water splitting testing. Photoelectrodes will be made into devices and the water splitting efficiency will be evaluated using a closed gas circulation-low pressure system coupled with Pyrex/quartz inner-irradiation configuration. Assessment of photoelectrochemical water splitting via in-situ PEC setup has been investigated and hence efficiency of the reaction can be estimated. In this project, we demonstrate the unusual effectiveness of phosphorus doping into bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photoanode for efficient low-bias PEC water splitting. The resulting BiVO4 photoanode shows a separation efficiency of 80% and 99% at potentials as low as 0.6 and 1.0 VRHE, respectively. Theoretical simulation and experimental analysis collectively verify that the record performance originates from the unique phosphorus-doped BiVO4 configuration with concurrently mediated carrier density, trap states, and small polaron hopping. With NiFeOx cocatalyst, the BiVO4 photoanode achieves an applied bias photon-to-current efficiency of 2.21% at 0.6 VRHE. The mechanistic understanding of the enhancement of BiVO4 properties provides key insights in trap state passivation and polaron hopping for most photoactive metal oxides. 4. Objective 4: Mechanistic understanding of the relationships between efficiency of photoelectrodes and the nanostructure-induced modulation of optical/electronic properties. Mechanistic studies revealing the relationships between performance and photoelectrodes have been documented in more than 10 journal output in this project. For instance, we report a simple alkaline solution treatment of the (010) faceted bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photoanode to increase the surface ratio of bismuth to vanadium, thus improving the performance of photoelectrochemical water oxidation. This study demonstrates that the preferential vanadium dissolution occurs in an alkaline solution, resulting in a bismuth-rich surface on the outer region of the pristine BiVO4 to afford the formation of homojunction within BiVO4. The homojunction promotes the charge separation efficiency of the treated BiVO4 photoanode to reach an almost ∼100% enhancement at 1.23 VRHE under simulated sunlight. Upon further loading NiFeOx cocatalyst, the maximum applied-bias photon-to-current conversion efficiency (ABPE) of treated BiVO4 photoanode also shows a further 100% enhancement in 0.1 M KPi electrolyte. This study sheds light on the critical role of surface termination/composition on the photoelectrochemical properties of the BiVO4 photoanode.

11306920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306920.value: Throughout this project, we have published a total of 18 peer-reviewed papers. All these papers were focused on the photocharge investigation of photoelectrodes prepared with electrochemical treatment process. Typically, TiO2, WO3 and bismuth-based ternary oxide such as bismuth vanadate were investigated thoroughly. (a) Noticeable outcome of these 18 peer-reviewed research output are: - One paper is currently recognised as Highly Cited Papers (by Clarivate); - Four papers were selected as the journal covers, in which the journal are all top tier journals in the field (including Advanced Energy Materials and ACS Energy Letters); - One paper award (by Royal Society of Chemistry, UK) (b) Additionally, the PI and his research team have presented the findings in international conference. PI-Ng has delivered seven invited or keynote talks in Hong Kong and other international platforms: - PI-Ng was invited to deliver an Award Presentation at the Annual Meeting of the Japanese Photochemistry Association (JPA) held in Niigata Japan in September of 2021. PI-Ng gave an Award Talk on the topic “Charge Transportation in Photoactive Semiconductors for Solar Fuels Generation”. - PI-Ng invited to deliver a Keynote speech in Energy Future Conference (EF4) in October 2021, in Sydney Australia, with the title “Solar Fules from Photocatalysis”. - Another six talks were in Hong Kong (by HKIE), USA (by Electrochemical Society Meetings). All talks are about solar fuels from photoactive semiconductor. (c) The findings in photocatalysis studied in this project also appeared in Hong Kong Media (RTHK) and a number of international outlets (e.g. Eurekalert). - https://podcast.rthk.hk/podcast/item.php?pid=42&eid=231574&lang=en-US (香港家書) - https://phys.org/news/2023-01-method-efficient-hydrogen-production-voltage.html (New method to introduce efficient water splitting for hydrogen production at low voltage) Overall, this GRF project has enabled the promotion of photocatalytic technology and helped in expanding fundamental and applied science boundary.

11306920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306920.value: The successful execution of this research project has served as the solid foundation for more rapid development of photocatalytic science and technology. It has enabled the PI-Ng and CityU to attract attentions from governmental department (including EMSD and EPD) and industrial sectors on the potential usefulness of photocatalysis (including Towngas and CityBus). Sparkled by this project, PI-Ng is now actively involved in the development of solar fuels project in Hong Kong (both fundamental research and applied-driven application) via multiple funded platforms.

11306920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306920.value: Photoactive semiconductors are promising candidates for harnessing solar energy. A number of potentially impactful photoactive materials can be further modified to improve their performance in light-to-chemicals conversion. This research project has enabled the design of novel photoactive materials through innovative electrochemical fabrication and engineering methods to modulate their charge transportation and surface chemistry. Fundamental knowledge attained on charge interaction at the interface of electrochemically-derived photoelectrodes and the liquid state reactants has helped to develop thorough understanding and is crucial for further development of solar fuels in Hong Kong. The project has brought the community to approaching the ultimate goal in converting and storing solar energy with promising robustness and efficiency.

11307020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307020.value: Transition metal cations play a central role in many research fields, particularly in catalysis and organometallic chemistry. The ability of atomic transition metal cations to mediate the activation of selected chemical bonds is one of their distinct features for allowing the observation of speciﬁc chemical outcomes. The transition metal ion has partially filled d or f orbitals and the interactions between valence electrons and orbitals play an important role in its chemical reactivity. The spin-orbit (SO) interactions give rise to dense manifolds of low-lying electronic states and of various spin multiplicities, making the fundamental understanding of chemical reactivity of transition metal cations difficult. Practical catalytic processes occur mostly in condensed phases and solvated medium, however, chemical dynamics and kinetics studies of gas phase reactions involving transition metal ion and simple molecules such as CO2, H2 and CH4 provide an unambiguous insight to chemical reactivity of the idealized catalytic model without the influence of solvent, substrate and ligands. To unravel the complex chemistry of transition metal cations, it is important to investigate reaction mechanism by mapping out the landscape of potential energy surface (PES) from reactant molecules to reaction products, with emphasis relevant reaction energetics and activation barrier heights. Under the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation, the electronic conﬁguration of a molecule largely governs its geometry. In other words, changing the quantum electronic state, by altering the electron spin angular momenta (S), orbital angular momentum (L), and total SO angular momentum (J) of a transition metal ion should have a signiﬁcant effect on its chemical reactivity. In the circumstances when the BO approximation fails due to the rapid change of adiabatic electronic configuration with nuclear coordinates, chemical reaction no longer occurs on a single PES but must evolve between two or more PESs, giving rise to nonadiabatic effect. The nonadiabatic effect is even more significant in the region near the PES’s crossing such as conical intersection or avoided crossing. In this proposal, we investigate the reaction dynamics of CO2, H2, and CH4 activation mediated by quantum state-selected 3d transition metal ions. We study the nonadiabatic effect on the dynamics of the reactions, especially at the conical intersection or avoided crossing on PES, and how the nonadiabatic effect and SO coupling enhance or inhibit the chemical reactivity. 過渡金屬陽離子在許多研究領域中發揮著核心作用，尤其是在催化和有機金屬化學。過渡金屬原子陽離子其一獨特特徵為介導所選化學鍵活化的能力。過渡金屬離子具有部分填充的d或f電子軌道，價電子與軌道之間的相互作用對過渡金屬離子化學反應性起重要作用。自旋軌道相互作用產生了低電子態和各種不同緻密的電子態，這使得了解過渡金屬陽離子的化學反應性十分困難。此外實際的催化過程中，溶劑化介質和配體確實影響探討過渡金屬離子和中性分子（例如CO2，H2和CH4）的化學反應動力學和動力學。 為了揭示過渡金屬陽離子的複雜化學性質，我們通過計算反應勢能面，研究反應機理，獲得相關反應能和活化勢壘高度。在Born-Oppenheimer（BO）近似理論下，分子的電子配置很大程度上決定了其結構形狀。換句話說，通過改變過渡金屬離子的電子自旋角動量，軌道角動量和總自旋軌道角動量能夠對其化學反應性產生重大影響。在有核坐標的絕熱電子構型的快速變化下，Born-Oppenheimer近似理論失敗，化學反應不再發生在單個反應勢能面上，而在兩個或多個勢能面之間演化，從而產生非絕熱效應。非絕熱效應在勢能面交叉點附近的區域將更加明顯。 在這項建議書，我們研究由介導性3d過渡金屬離子與中性分子的反應動力學。我們研究非絕熱作用對反應動力學的影響，特別是在勢能面上的圓錐形交叉點或避免交叉處，以及非絕熱作用和自旋偶聯如何增強或抑制化學反應性。

11307120.label: Project Objectives
11307120.value: To design and synthesize multifunctional, fluorescent organic molecules featuring the desired geometric feature for building porous frameworks, as well as the chemical functions (e.g., the thiol -SH groups) for effective binding and sensing of heavy metal species (e.g., Hg) in natural waters. To assemble the synthesized multifunctional molecules into porous framework crystals (e.g., using the chemically hard metal zirconium, Zr4+ ion), and to achieve the desired properties of well-defined porosity and tailored-made chemical functions for heavy metal uptake. For better uptake from the very dilute natural water analytes, we will to install dense arrays of thiol binding units within the pores for optimizing the concerted chelation effect. To examine and screen the assembled porous crystals for pre-concentration and fluorescent sensing of heavy metal species from natural water samples. We aim to systematically quantify and optimize the sensitivity and selectivity in heavy metal detection (e.g., Hg and Pb, at sub-ppb levels), and to achieve binding strength (as measured by the distribution coefficient Kd) over a million times that of the commonly used commercial resin sorbents.

11307120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307120.value: To advance the technologies for environmental pollution monitoring, we here propose crystalline metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) combining robust porous, high-surface-area structures and extensive sulfur functions that proffer highly strong and selective binding affinities for convenient enrichment and sensing of heavy metal species in natural waters. For this, we will synthesize molecular building blocks equipped with two distinct sets of organic functions: one is the chemically hard and hydrophilic carboxyls that favor chemically hard metal ions (e.g., Zr4+); the other is the chemically soft sulfur (thioether and thiol) function that does prefer heavy metal species. Thus, the hard carboxyl groups can be first engaged with a hard metal ion to form single crystals of porous network based on the reversible metal-carboxylate coordination bonds, while the soft sulfur groups remain free-standing inside the pores. Because of the large surface area of the porous crystal, heavy metal species from water will be able to quickly diffuse into the pores and access the chemical groups to trigger the color/emission changes for detection purposes. Moreover, the heavy metal species thus trapped and concentrated can be conveniently eluted by the very cheap I2/NaI solution for further quantification and for recycling the original sorbent material. 為進一步發展環境污染檢測技術，我們提出結合擁有穩定的多孔、高比表面積結構和多功能巰基的晶態金屬-有機框架（MOFs），該框架具有高強度和高選擇性的結合親和力，便於富集和檢測天然水體中的重金屬。 為此，我們將合成攜帶兩種不同有機官能團的分子配體：其一為傾向與（化學）硬金屬離子（如Zr4+）配位的硬親水羧基；另一為可吸附重金屬離子的、軟的含硫官能團（例如，硫醚和硫醇）。因此，硬羧基可先與硬金屬離子結合，形成基於可逆金屬-羧酸配位鍵構建的多孔網狀單晶，而軟的含硫基團則在孔隙內保持獨立。由於多孔晶體的大比表面積，水中的重金屬能夠迅速擴散到孔隙中，並接觸到化學基團，從而觸發可用於檢測的顏色/發光變化。此外，被捕獲和富集的重金屬可以用非常便宜的I2/NaI溶液方便地洗脫，以進行進一步的定量分析和原始吸附材料的回收。

11307120.label: Realisation of objectives
11307120.value: The realization of the objectives are well illustrated by the three publications generated from the support of this research grant, including the synthesis of multifunctional, fluorescent organic molecules featuring the desired geometric feature for building porous frameworks, with the equipped chemical functions (e.g., the thiol -SH groups) for effective binding and sensing of heavy metal species (e.g., Hg) in natural waters for selected linker molecules successfully prepared in this report period); also the objective of framework crystallization and testing the desired properties of well-defined porosity and tailored-made chemical functions for heavy metal uptake has also been well accomplished. A key highlight of our functionalization achievement is included in Paper 1, in which we have successfully incorporated multiple dithiolene groups into the molecular building block, as more superior chelating motifs for heavy metal binding, in comparison with the monodentate thiol groups. Specifically, with 2-COOH and 4-SH donors all packed onto the benzene ring, tetrasulfanyl terephthalic acid (TST) is a simple yet fully equipped ligand to move the field of metal-coordination materials--it is now accomplished. The hard-soft carboxyl-thiol synergy is leveraged here in selectively bonding the carboxyl units to Zr(IV) ions to form the same cubic net of UiO-66 (this being based on the terephthalic linker)--with the free-standing dithiolene units equipping the grid of ZrTST. The 3D network of ZrTST averages about 7.6 connections [as in Zr6O4(OH)4(C8H4O4S4)3.8], with the other 4.4 sealed by acetate ions. The ZrTST solid is stable in boiling water (it is formed in water/acetic acid/ethane dithiol), and remains ordered even above 300 °C. The thiol-enabled ZrTST (powder) takes up mercury from water with a high distribution coefficient Kd (e.g., 1.2 × 106 mL·g−1); it also shows proton conductivity (1.9 × 10−3 S·cm−1 at 90 °C and 90% relative humidity), which, most notably, increases to a highest value of 3.7 × 10−1 S·cm−1 after oxidizing the -SH into -SO3H groups. Beyond the symmetrical, chemically well-defined dithiolene units, we have also, for the purpose of future industrial scale-up, achieved a molecular linker system that can be post-synthetically sulfurated to install effective metal binding or heavy metal removal capabilities, as is illustrated in paper 2. In that work, we have attached pentaflorophenyl groups efficiently onto an as-made metal-organic framework host, which will allow easy replacement of the fluoro groups by sulfur atoms through the cheap sulfurating agent like sodium sulfide. Our designer linker molecule here features: 1) pyrazole donors masked by t-butyloxycarbonyl (Boc) and 2) ethynyl side units protected by triisopropylsilyl (TIPS) groups. The former solvothermally demasks to synthesize the Ni8-pyrazolate framework, in which the TIPS groups can be post-synthetically cleaved by guest fluoride ions to unveil the terminal alkyne group (-CCH). The ethynyl groups of the framework solid offer versatile reactions for functionalization, as with perfluorophenyl azide (PFA; a click reaction) to afford the two prongs of the 1,2,3-triazole base unit and the perfluoro unit. With the current functional linker system, in the spirit of free exploration of fundamental studies, we have also reached beyond the original objective of heavy metal removal, and accomplished (to our pleasant surprise) an effective adsorbent for the topical acid pollutants of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), with high apparent rate constant (kobs) of 0.99 g mg-1 h-1 and large maximum uptake capacity (qmax) of 268.5 mg g-1 for PFOA, and kobs of 0.77 g mg-1 h-1 and qmax of 142.1 mg g-1 for PFOS. Behind this practical application also stand fundamental advances in the synthesis of functional coordination polymers, as is highlighted by the ethynyl-equipped Ni8-pyrazolate scaffold NiL1-CCH in several regards. First, the recovery of the free-standing terminal alkyne functions by means of the incoming F- guests showcases the stability of this host network, as strong bases like F- are detrimental to the structural integrity of most MOF solids. Second, uniting stability and reactivity: i.e., the stability of the host net is complemented by the versatile reactivity of the ethynyl group (-CCH), as is illustrated by the CuAAC click reaction that installs the triazole and the perfluorophenyl (C6F5-) functions. Third, broader functionalization is now opened up, as one should be able to replace the fluoro groups on the installed C6F5- unit--e.g., with amino acids and other amine nucleophiles (while maintaining the crystalline order of the host net). Moreover, the open metal sites on the Ni8-oxo cluster (due to linker deficiency) of the NiL1-CCH framework also allow coordinative anchoring of guest Lewis bases for further functionalization within this reactive yet robust open framework. The objective of fluorescent sensing of heavy metals is also achieved in Paper 3. Herein, to expedite future practical applications, we expand on a versatile metal-organic framework system developed earlier in our group, and use simple and efficient post-synthetic oxidation and metalation to impart strong fluorescence properties, which respond highly sensitively to the presence of heavy metal species, even in strongly acidic industrial wastewater environments. Specifically, trivalent europium (Eu3+) can be implanted via post-synthetic metal insertion into the porous matrix of a robust a sulfonic acid (-SO3H) rich Zr-based MOF (Zr-DSBDS). The thus-prepared Zr-DSBDS-Eu exhibited excellent fluorescence stability in acidic aqueous medium and showed promising high sensitivity and recyclability in the detection of toxic heavy metal ions. This is a straightforward post-synthetic method to incorporate one Eu3+ atom into each MOF octahedral cage to form a Ln-MOF, preserving the emission property by effectively isolating the Eu3+ ions from deactivating groups in the surrounding aqueous environment.

11307120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307120.value: Thanks to the steady funding from RGC over the past 16 years, we have had the fortune to consistently pursue the synthesis and design of a variety of linker molecules featuring unique (e.g., sulfur-based) multi-functional architectures, thus opening broad new horizons for the development of framework solid-state materials with diverse structural and functional motifs as well as strong-performing physical properties. A key finding of this project is embodied in the simple yet beautiful and highly functional molecule tetrasulfanyl terephthalic acid (TST; see paper 1). This compact yet highly functionalized building block is especially suited for constructing MOF and other coordination/framework materials. In particular, we have now developed an efficient way to prepare the molecule tetrasulfanyl terephthalic acid (TST), which features the simple terephthalic acid fully functionalized by two dithiolene units. This simple yet functional molecule stands to open a crosscutting research direction by interfacing the two thriving systems of metal-dithiolene and metal-carboxylate networks. Another cutting-edge crystal engineering approach developed in this project is the two-pronged design of the Ni8-pyrazolate framework as showcased in Paper 2. By way of an efficient click reaction, we have simultaneously anchored two key metal-binding functions onto a robust Ni8-pyrazolate coordination framework: the polar hydrophilic triazole function and the hydrophobic perfluorophenyl function that can be conveniently converted into the strong donating thiol groups using a cheap nucleophile like sodium sulfide. Although the current work is primarily concerned with the removal of perfluorooctanoic acid and analogs, its potential impact on heavy metal removal applications is significant and obvious. On the front of heavy metal detection, we have developed a highly sensitive for sensor based on Eu(III) sensitized by a metal-organic framework, as shown in Paper 3. In particular our sensor can perform in real, acidic industrial waterwater conditions--with highest selectivity and sensitivity (namely ZrDSBD-Eu). The key chemistry is the dense arrays of free-standing sulfonic groups (-SO3H) on a framework solid easily derived from H2O2 oxidation of a commercialized MOF material (first developed by our group: Journal of the American Chemical Society 135 (21), 7795-7798). The sulfonate group enables facile ion exchange for anchoring and sensitizing the Eu(III) ions, with the resultant strong luminescence being stable in strong acids for the sensing applications. The MOF host recovers can be re-used many times, and the sulfonate groups also afford excellent water dispersion to form stable suspensions for the sensing application.

11307120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307120.value: Besides heavy metal removal applications, the outstanding stability and versatile functions of the metal-organic framework systems developed in this project also open up broad vistas for further materials development studies. In the fully thiolated dicarboxyl linker H2TST-based MOF solid ZrTST, many other reactions can be tried to tap the rich synergy of the sulfur and oxygen functions of TST, e.g., one can use transition metals like Cu(I), Co(II) and Eu(III) to bond both the S and O donors, in order to enhance electronic and magnetic interactions in the resultant networks. The organic synthesis protocol disclosed here is also applicable for accessing other carboxyl-dithiolene motifs. For the C6F5-functionalized MOF solid, broader functionalization is also now opened up, as one can replace the fluoro groups on the installed C6F5- unit--e.g., with thiol and amino acids for metal uptake uses. Moreover, the open metal sites on the Ni8-oxo cluster (due to linker deficiency) of the NiL1-CCH framework also allow coordinative anchoring of guest Lewis bases for further functionalization within this reactive yet robust open framework.

11307220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307220.value: Adhesives that can bind to diverse synthetic and biological surfaces in wet environments have great technical implications in areas ranging from aquatic vehicles and underwater soft robotics, to tissue engineering, wound dressing and biomedical devices. Current design strategies are mainly focused on hydrogels or hydrogel-derived adhesives. However, there are intrinsic limitations for the hydrogel-based adhesives, such as the lack of mechanical strength, insufficient interfacial toughness/adhesion, and the incompatibility with water-insoluble drugs. To address these challenges, developing organogel-based supramolecular adhesives with high mechanical stability and controlled inclusion of bioactive oils could be an alternative approach. The PI’s group recently made a couple of achievements on the chemistry synthesis and molecular engineering of supramolecular polymer, gels and adhesives. We demonstrated hydrogen-bond crosslinked supramolecular polymers in coating and adhesive applications. Particularly, comparing to traditional supramolecular organogel, our results revealed that multiphase assembly of siloxane oligomers may help better engineer materials mechanics and interfacial bonding with a certain amount of oil inclusion. In this project, we propose to synthesize a variety of oligomers that can be crosslinked through hierarchical hydrogen bonds and assemble into continuous networks. We expect that biogenic antimicrobial oils may serve as organic solvent in the preparation of organogel-based supramolecular adhesives, and be incorporated into the gel matrix afterwards. The encapsulated oils could further serve as a structural/functional component in controlling the interfacial and mechanical properties of supramolecular adhesives. The associated mechanistic study will not only help us elucidate the molecular mechanism on performance regulation of supramolecular adhesives with a wide range of oil inclusion, but also guide us on the implementation of the developed antimicrobial adhesives to fulfill specific requirements in practical applications. The outcome of this project will advance our fundamental understanding on the molecular engineering of organogel-based supramolecular adhesives, and provide new insights into the design of supramolecular materials which will benefit their potential applications in soft robotics, flexible electronics, and biomedical applications. 能应用在水下等湿条件下的高性能粘接材料在水下机器人、组织工程和生物医学器件等领域有着广阔的需求。现有的设计策略主要是基于水凝胶发展的粘接材料。但是这些基于水凝胶的粘接材料有一些明显的缺点，例如缺乏高的机械强度、界面韧性和粘附能力不足，以及无法匹配非水溶性的药物等。因此，针对这些问题，需要发展新的设计策略用于制备高性能水下粘接材料。项目负责人团队最近在超分子聚合物、凝胶和粘接剂的分子设计和材料合成等方面取得了一些进展。我们证明了氢键交联的超分子聚合物在粘接和涂层材料等领域的应用。和传统的超分子油凝胶相比，我们的结果表明多相分离的寡聚体设计辅以有机液体的可控包裹或可帮助协同提高材料的力学性能和界面粘附能力。本项目中，我们提出设计制备具有可控分子骨架和氢键给受体的寡聚体，通过控制寡聚体分子在天然功能有机液体中的自组装过程，协同调控聚合物网络的结构和表界面性质，最终制备得到具有高力学性能、高界面粘附和界面可控释放的超分子粘接材料。我们会系统研究具有生物活性的有机液体与聚合物网络的相互作用，并探索这些超分子粘接材料在水下封装材料和伤口敷料等特定应用场景的表现。该项目的实施将拓展我们对超分子有机凝胶的分子工程设计的基本认识，也将为多功能有机凝胶的设计以及它们在生物医学等领域的应用提供新的见解。

11307220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307220.value: We have developed a series of hydrogen-bonds crosslinked supramolecular polymer and polymer assemblies. Specific functional liquids have been incorporated into the polymer network to further tune the function of the polymer composites. For example, we develop a supramolecular adhesive coating which is composed of polyurea polymer, carvacrol oil, and silicone oil for pathogen disinfection in diverse conditions. The supramolecular adhesive in which competitive hydrogen bonds regulate the assembly status of all components and thus guide the performance of the adhesive coating based coating. The gained knowledge from the development of supramolecular assemblies helps us reveal the tunability and more importantly, such design principles can be applied to other polymer-liquid systems for diverse applications. New research directions have been implemented in the PI’s lab.

11307320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307320.value: 近臨界森林大火過程的“反集中”性質

11307320.label: Project Objectives
11307320.value: Analyze the successive freezings in volume-frozen percolation, when “boundary rules” are tweaked (such rules may perturb significantly the macroscopic behavior of the process). A deconcentration property was obtained recently for the “original” boundary rules, and we hope to obtain a more general result, bringing us closer to the burning mechanism in forest fires. Obtain an analogous deconcentration result for forest fire processes without recovery, yielding an accurate picture of the final configuration. This would require incorporating the additional randomness produced by the ignition mechanism. Recent results about near-critical percolation with heavy-tailed impurities should also be instrumental, to understand the cumulative effect of early fires. Analyze the effect of “recoveries” for volume-ignited forest fire processes, with a view to comparing this process with volume-frozen percolation, on an interval beyond the critical time (the time when an infinite connected component of trees would emerge if the ignitions were not present). Finally, combine the improved understanding obtained in 1)-3) to analyze the Drossel-Schwabl process, in particular to establish a form of deconcentration beyond the critical time. We expect it to be a first crucial step to understand the long-term behavior of that process.

11307320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307320.value: 在統計物理中，自組織臨界性是壹個十分有趣的現象，可以被用來解釋自然界中出現的復雜性。由Drossel和Schwabl在1992年引入的“森林大火過程”就是這種現象的壹個典型。在這壹過程中，新樹在格點上以1的強度出現（即普通滲流過程），同時閃電以極小的強度zeta出現：當壹棵樹被劈中，此樹及與之相連的所有樹都會被大火燒掉。 雖然森林大火過程引起了許多關註，但人們對這壹過程的長期行為所知甚少。研究這類問題極其困難，因為有兩種相對立的效果互相競爭：假如有很多樹，導致出現了大的連通簇，它被燒掉時就會留出大片空地。由於這種非單調性，統計物理中用來研究格點模型的常規方法不能用來研究這類問題，人們需要引入新的技術和想法。這個研究計劃的目的正是在數學層面上增進對於這類模型的理解，而研究方法來源於近年來在“近臨界性滲流”以及於之相關的其它過程中發展出來的壹些突破性想法。最近，我們得出了壹些新的結果，是關於壹個有限盒裏的森林大火過程，其盒子的邊長是強度zeta的壹個合適的函數。證明過程中，我們精確地理解了臨界時間t之前出現的大火的累積效應 （t為普通滲流過程的臨界時間）。 在這份計劃中，我們想進壹步研究，在臨界時間t後的壹個近臨界時間段裏（時間段長度以zeta的壹個小的指數的速度趨於零），壹個給定的格點周圍相繼發生的大火。更確切的，我們最近在壹個相關的模型“體積凍結滲流”上得到了壹個令人驚奇的“反集中”結果。我們想把這個結果推廣到“森林大火過程”，這樣就可給出關於它們在時間t後的行為的非常精確的描述。為達成這個目標，我們準備相繼地考慮幾個不同版本的“森林大火過程”，以便把潛在的壹些難點分離開來。

11307320.label: Realisation of objectives
11307320.value: Objective 1 has been fully addressed in the preprint “A 2D forest fire process beyond the critical time”, joint with Prof. Jacob van den Berg (CWI and VU, Amsterdam). It has been posted on the ArXiv preprint server in October 2022 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05642), and it is currently submitted for publication in a top Mathematics journal. It is a rather long and technical work (53 pages), where we study volume-frozen percolation with parameter N, as N tends to infinity. We were able to establish the exact deconcentration property that we were aiming to, i.e. in the case when boundary rules are tweaked, although it required more effort than we expected: in the final configuration, any given vertex (such as the origin 0) lies (with high probability) in a mesoscopic island, with a volume which is much larger than 1, and much smaller than N. In particular, 0 freezes with vanishing probability. More concretely, we show that for every fixed k, the modified boundary rules rules do not perturb the last k freezings around 0 (in the limit as N tends to infinity). This allows us to harness the deconcentration property established in [Jacob van den Berg, Demeter Kiss, Pierre Nolin. Two-dimensional volume-frozen percolation: deconcentration and prevalence of mesoscopic clusters. Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4), 51(4):1017–1084, 2018]. We believe that it is an important step toward analyzing forest-fire processes beyond the critical time, since the modified boundary rules are closer to the burning mechanism in forest fire processes, thus improving our understanding of the self-organized critical (SOC) nature of such processes. When trying to compare the modified process to the process with original boundary rules, several difficulties arose. We needed to analyze geometric features of the infinite connected component in supercritical percolation. In particular, we had to study the existence of narrow "corridors" in its complement. In principle, such passageways could distort substantially the successive freezings around a given vertex, since they give rise to "bubbles" along the boundaries of the islands created by frozen clusters. In addition, we had to take into account some subtle measurability issues, which appeared when adapting the reasonings of Section 7 in the aforementioned article. These results and ideas are used to compare the full-lattice process to the process in a finite (random) domain (large enough in terms of N). Objective 3 is also fully addressed in the same preprint. There, we explain how to extend the results obtained for frozen percolation with modified boundary rules to the N-forest fire process, where trees may recover after burning, i.e. become occupied again. These recoveries cause a major technical difficulty, since they destroy the nice spatial Markov property that frozen percolation (with original or modified boundary rules) possesses. In order to tackle this issue, a key input is the paper [Demeter Kiss, Ioan Manolescu, and Vladas Sidoravicius. Planar lattices do not recover from forest fires. Ann. Probab., 43(6):3216–3238, 2015]. The geometric ideas from that paper are instrumental, in particular to analyze the cumulative effect of recovered sites, through the appearance of "necklaces" of six-arm sites. Our proof relies on the introduction of a well-suited six-arm event, whose probability can be upper bounded through an induction procedure. In this way, we managed to improve and extend the results of the afore-mentioned paper, making them more robust and flexible for applications. As for Objective 2, it is now completely addressed, in a joint work with my Prof. Jacob van den Berg and my postdoctoral fellow Yifan Gao. However, we are still in the process of checking carefully all the technical details. As we expected, the percolation process with "heavy-tailed" impurities, introduced and studied in our earlier work [Jacob van den Berg, Pierre Nolin. Near-critical 2D percolation with heavy-tailed impurities, forest fires and frozen percolation. Probab. Theory Related Fields, 181(1-3):211–290, 2021], plays an instrumental role. More specifically, the impurities are used to take into account the effect of "early" fires, taking place before the near-critical window. The process is thus used to require the existence of occupied connections at some prescribed times, which allows us to study the successive clusters that burn around a given vertex (in the same way as to establish the existence of exceptional scales in the above paper). We also need to incorporate the fact that the ignition process produces extra randomness (compared to the frozen percolation case), which is in some sense helpful for the deconcentration result. In this way, we show that for the forest fire process without recoveries, with parameter z tending to 0, any given vertex lies in a mesoscopic island (and thus does not burn) with high probability. Regarding the final Objective 4, we are currently addressing it at the moment, based on the improved understanding obtained for Objectives 1, 2 and 3. We have already devised the whole proof strategy and all the intermediate steps, so we are convinced that this objective can be achieved in the near future. However, we first need to finish writing carefully the results obtained in Objective 2 for the Drossel-Schwabl process without recoveries, before checking carefully how to incorporate the recoveries. We plan to write the detailed proof in the coming months, but this requires significant effort. Indeed, as with the N-forest fire process, recoveries destroy the nice spatial Markov properties. Moreover, a key step in our proof consists in extending the above stability result for "modified" six arm events, which was for Bernoulli percolation, to the forest fire process at a time when fires have already destroyed large regions. Finally, our work on the role of recoveries in forest fires, and in particular the induction argument on modified six-arm events, led us to collaborate with Wei Qian and Yifan Gao (both at City University of Hong Kong) on seemingly unrelated questions, for the classical discrete Gaussian Free Field (in 2D). We were able to derive percolative properties of the field below level √log N, which was completely open. This led to a series of three preprints, posted on ArXiv recently: "Percolation of discrete GFF in dimension two I. Arm events in the random walk loop soup" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16230), "Percolation of discrete GFF in dimension two II. Connectivity properties of two-sided level sets" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16273), and "Up-to-constants estimates on four-arm events for simple conformal loop ensemble" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06202). The main goal consists in proving the non-existence of blocking paths, along which the field remains high. When doing so, we uncovered a very similar structure to the one studied with J. van den Berg in forest fires. In particular, in the associated random walk loop soup (at criticality), we use a peculiar "four-arm event", encoding that two large connected components of loops come close to each other without touching. Since the corresponding exponent is larger than two, we get a picture which is analogous to that with six-arm events in Bernoulli percolation. Of course, the technical details are completely different, and we had to develop a completely new toolbox to work with such arm events in the loop soup. Hence, the whole series of three papers turned out to be quite long and technical. Moreover, we believe that these tools and ideas can be useful for other models.

11307320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307320.value: In this project, we have improved significantly our understanding of the near-critical behavior of two families of planar stochastic processes, namely volume-frozen percolation and forest fires, which are both related to the statistical physics phenomenon of self-organized criticality. In particular, we consider the "island" where a given vertex ends up though the evolution of the process. Our main objective was to establish a deconcentration property for that island, i.e. that its size is truly random, and also mesoscopic - which means that it is neither big nor small. We established that property for a version of frozen percolation, and then for a particular forest fire process. This improved understanding is now used to establish deconcentration for the celebrated Drossel-Schwabl forest fire process. We have also identified clearly the role played by boundary rules in such processes, which had remained quite mysterious so far. We showed that they create macroscopic bubbles along the boundaries of islands, which do not have a significant effect on the global evolution. Finally, our work on this project, as well as on related questions in percolation theory, also led us to collaborate on geometric properties of the level sets in the two-dimensional Gaussian Free Field.

11307320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307320.value: We hope to extend the results obtained in this project to derive an improved description of the behavior of the Drossel-Schwabl process beyond the critical time. One of our long-term goals is to analyze its equilibrium distribution, which is the distribution obtained in the long-term limit. We also plan to look for further applications to other real-world processes, e.g. studied in condensed matter physics, ecology (patterns in vegetation), or epidemiology (the spread of epidemics).

11307320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307320.value: In this project, we obtained novel results for two families of models introduced in physics, known as frozen percolation and forest fires. These models appear naturally, but they are still poorly understood. We were able to rigorously establish the emergence of a deconcentration property in both cases: the process creates spontaneously islands with a random size, which are neither big nor small. This is quite peculiar, and it seems to be a key property of such processes, which had not been observed earlier. This provides a better understanding of real-world complex systems with analogous freezing/burning mechanisms.

11307420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307420.value: In this project, the PI proposes to study the long time well-posedness and dynamics for he plasma-vacuum interface problem of ideal incompressible MHD equations. The interface is a free surface which cannot be determined a priori, but is a part of solutions. The specific issues to be explored in this project include: 1) For the initial data being small perturbations of the background solution and satisfying the stability condition, determine whether the plasma-vacuum interface problem of ideal incompressible MHD equations is well-posed global-in-time in Sobolev spaces. If the global-in-time solution is not available, identify the life-span of the solutions in terms of the size of the initial perturbation; 2) determine the long time dynamics and behavior of solutions related to the celebrated Alfven wave of MHD equations, achieve some understanding of the interaction of Alfven-type waves and the surface waves of the interface. Compared with topic of the long time well-posedness and dynamics for fluid equations without taking into account of magnetic effects, few results are available for ideal MHD equations with free surfaces. The problems proposed to study in this project are challenging and difficult. They involve complicated wave interactions such as the interaction of Alfven-type waves and the surface waves of the interface, an issue not addressed in literature. New analytic and geometric ideas and techniques need to be developed to deal with those issues. Besides dealing with the evolution of the free interface, ideas and techniques of higher order hyperbolic weighted quasilinear energy energy estimates in the spirit of those used in the proof of global nonlinear stability of Minkowski space-time for vacuum Einstein equations of Christodoulou and Klainerman in domains with free surfaces will be developed in this project. 在本項目中，項目主持人提出研究理想不可壓縮磁流體方程等離子體-真空分界面問題的長時間適定性及動力學行為。 所研究分界面不能預先確定， 而是求解的一部分。在本項目中將要研究的具體問題包括： 1）當初值為背景解的小擾動並滿足穩定性條件時， 確定理想不可壓縮磁流體方程等離子體-真空分界面問題是否在索伯列夫空间中是整体適定的。 如果不可能获得整体解， 確定解的生命区间和初始擾動大小的关系； 2） 確定与磁流體方程著名阿尔文波有关的解的長時間動力學行為， 并对阿尔文型波和分界面的表面波之间的相互作用获得理解。 与忽略磁场效应的流體方程相应问题的長時間適定性及動力學行為的课题相比， 带自由界面理想磁流體方程的结果很少。 本項目中提出研究的问题具有挑战性且困难， 涉及复杂的波的相互作用， 例如在文献中很少涉及的阿尔文型波和分界面的表面波之间的相互作用。 需要发展新的分析和几何思想和技巧来解决这些问题。 除了处理自由界面的发展， 我们将发展在带有自由界面的区域中在精神上与Christodoulou 和 Klainerman 证明真空Einstein 方程Minkowski时空的整体非线性稳定性的所使用的高阶双曲带权拟线性能量方法一致的思想和技术。

11307420.label: Realisation of objectives
11307420.value: 1)We first organized and reviewed the key results and techniques in studying free boundary problems for incompressible ideal MHD, focusing on stability conditions (Taylor-sign condition) for well-posedness. This set a basis for the further investigation of the related problems. This was written and published in a journal. 2) For MHD equations of plasma in an exterior domain in 3-spatial dimensions with the curved boundary and vanishing the first Betti number, we proved the global well-posedness and long time dynamics and behavior of solutions for initial data being small perturbations of the background equilibrium solutions. We developed some analytic and geometric approaches, such as using the hodge estimates for vector fields in the presence of the curved boundary. This is directly related to objective 1 and objective 3. 3) For a vacuum free boundary problem with the interface separating the self-gravitating fluids and vacuum states modeling viscous gaseous stars in 3-spatial dimensions with spherical symmetry, we proved the global well-posedness and long-time dynamics of strong solutions. The obtained results are applicable to white dwarfs under a critical mass constraint and general pressure law with the polytropic index greater than 4/3. It should be noted that the study white dwarfs is important in astrophysics . However, due to the degeneracy, it is challenging in nonlinear PDE theory. This is particular so for the fluid-vacuum interface problem. The key analysis is to deal with the difficulty caused by the vacuum states and identify suitable weights to detect the behavior near the interface separating the fluids and vacuum and investigate the long-time dynamics of the interface. We developed the weighted energy estimates and the way to deal with the issue of the evolution and long-time dynamics of the interface. This is directly related to objectives 1 and 3. 4) We investigated the formation of splash singularity for the free boundary problem which can be used to model the plasma-vacuum interface for incompressible MHD, and proved the formation of this kind of singularity for certain class of initial data. It is showing that the formed singularity occurs on the interface. We also gave a clear description of the nature of the singularity. Understanding the formation and nature of the singularity for the free interface problem requires sophisticated analytic and geometric tools which we developed in this project to tackle the problem. The analysis is also related to the understanding of the interaction of Alfven wave with the free interface (free boundary) and the surface wave. This result shows that the life span of the solutions on which one has the well-posedness for the interface problem for the incompressible MHD can only be finite for a class of initial data. This is directly related to three objectives of the project. 5) We investigated the uniform regularity (and thus the uniform well-posedness) of solutions to the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system in the presence of boundaries so that the plasma is confined in a domain with a boundary separating the plasma and exterior environment which can be vacuum, in small Alfven and Mach numbers. The small Alfven number means that the speed of Alfven wave is much faster than the flow speed so that the magnetic forces play a dominating role to the inertial forces, and Alfven waves become very significant. We identify the condition to ensure the uniform regularity of solutions for the small Alfven and Mach numbers. This research discloses the interaction of the Alfven wave with the boundary, and identifies the conditions of the uniform well-posedness. This research directly related to three objectives of the project. 6) We investigated and obtained the uniform well-posedness (in particular uniform regularity) in the functional spaces of co-normal Sobolev and Lipschitz regularity in normal direction of incompressible MHD in small viscosity in a domain with boundary in three dimensions. This research highlights how magnetic fields and plasma interact with solid or structured surfaces, which significantly influences the behavior and stability of such systems. The case we first investigated is the perfect conducting boundary condition for the magnetic field in a domain with the general curved boundary. In this case, the tangential component of the electric field is zero and the magnetic field lines tangentially at the boundary. This case may involve the interaction of Alfven waves with the general curved surface with complicated geometry. We developed analytic and geometric approaches to deal with the intricate and rich interactions. We also investigated and obtained the uniform regularity (uniform well-posedness) when the magnetic field satisfies the insulating boundary condition, so that the magnetic field is transversal to the boundary in half space in three dimensions. In this case, the propagation and interaction of the Alfven wave is quite different from the case of the perfect conducting boundary conditions. This research is directly related to three objectives of this project.

11307420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307420.value: 1) In Article 2, we established the global well-posedness and long-time behavior of solutions to the viscous and resistive MHD equations in a 3D exterior domain with a curved boundary (vanishing first Betti number). For small perturbations of equilibrium, we develop analytic and geometric techniques to overcome challenges posed by boundary curvature. 2) In article 3, for a vacuum free boundary problem with theinterface separating the self-gravitating fluids and vacuum states modeling viscous gaseous stars in 3-spatial dimensions with spherical symmetry, the global existence and long- time dynamics of strong solutions are proved. The results are applicable to the case of white dwarfs under a critical mass constraint and general pressure law with the polytropic index greater than 4/3. We developed the weighted energy methods to deal with the difficulty caused by the vacuum states and detect the behavior near the interface separating the fluids and vacuum. This research highlights the evolution and long-time dynamics of the interface. 3) In Article 4, we proved the formation of splash singularity for the free boundary problem which can be used to model the plasma-vacuum interface for incompressible MHD, for certain initial data, demonstrating that the life span of the solutions for the interface problem can only be finite for a class of initial data. 4) In article 6, we examine the uniform regularity (uniform well-posedness) of solutions to the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system in the presence of boundaries so that the plasma is confined in a domain with a boundary separating the plasma and exterior environment which may be vacuum, in small Alfven and Mach numbers. In this case the Alfven waves become very significant. We identify the condition to ensure the uniform regularity of solutions for the small Alfven and Mach Numbers. This research discloses the interaction of the Alfven wave with the boundary. 5) In Article 5, we derive uniform regularity (well-posedness) for incompressible MHD with small viscosity in 3D domains with curved boundaries under perfect conducting boundary conditions. The strong Alfvén wave-boundary interactions in complex geometries is involved in this case. Uniform well-posedness result (Article 7) is obtained for insulating boundary conditions.

11307420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307420.value: For magnetic stars modeled by the compressible Euler (or Navier-Stokes) equations coupled with the Possiion equation of the gravitation field and pre-maxwell equations of the magnetic fields, investigate the properties of the stationary solutions, especially the behavior of solutions near the plasma-vacuum interface. This is a interesting topic for its own sake, and set up a basis for the further investigation of the nonlinear asymptotic stability which is the next research topic: Consider the free interface problem for the initial data being small perturbations of the stationary solution, investigate the long-time well-posedness of the problem, capturing the behavior of stationary problem near the plasma interface, and investigate the decay of the perturbations. This research requires to development of novel analytic and geometric ideas to deal with the rich interaction of the evolution of free interface (in particular the evolutionary geometry), interior solutions of plasma density, velocity, magnetic fields and gravitation, and Alfven waves. Dealing with these strong interaction and coping with the strong degeneracy of nonlinear PDES near plasma-vacuum interface will be a big challenge. Magnetic stars, such as white dwarfs, neutron starts and magnetars, are important astrophysical objects for which the strong magnetic field play a crucial role.

11307420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307420.value: This research project explores how electrically conducting fluids (plasmas) and magnetic fields behave in different settings, investigating the interaction of Alfven waves with surfaces (interface or solid walls). 1) We first studied how plasma evolves near curved surfaces, proving that small disturbances stay controlled over time and tends to zero for large time. This is crucial for confining plasma in devices. 2) We then analyzed fluid-vacuum interfaces in stars, proving long-term stability for white dwarfs (dense stellar remnants) below a critical mass. This helps understand stellar evolution . 3) We showed that certain plasma-vacuum interfaces can develop "splash" singularities—sharp, finite-time breakdowns—revealing limits on stable plasma confinement. 4) When magnetic forces dominate (fast Alfvén waves), we identified conditions ensuring smooth plasma behavior near walls, key to understanding the interaction of Alfven waves with the boundary. 5) We examined how magnetic fields and curved surfaces interact, proving stability under the perfect conducting boundary condition. Results were also obtained for insulting boundary conditions for a flat boundary in 3 spatial dimensions. By combining advanced math and physics, this work improves our ability to predict and control plasma behavior in different settings and may have potential applications to astrophysics.

11307720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307720.value: 用綁定態來增強波的非線性現象

11307720.label: Project Objectives
11307720.value: To analyze harmonic generation enhanced by strong resonances near bound states in the continuum, and study the dependence of conversion efficiency on quality-factors and the intensity of the incident wave. To analyze optical bistability for weak incident waves enhanced by strong resonances near bound states in the continuum, and determine the interval of incident field intensity where optical bistability occurs. To analyze symmetry breaking near bound states in the continuum, determine the stability of asymmetric solutions, and study the switching process.

To analyze optical bistability for weak incident waves enhanced by strong resonances near bound states in the continuum, and determine the interval of incident field intensity where optical bistability occurs.
To analyze symmetry breaking near bound states in the continuum, determine the stability of asymmetric solutions, and study the switching process.

11307720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307720.value: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a trapped or guided mode with a frequency in the radiation continuum. It corresponds to a discrete eigenvalue embedded in the continuous spectrum of a linear operator, and it is where a related boundary value problem loses uniqueness. On open structures, a resonant state is a complex-frequency solution that radiates power to infinity. Near a BIC, resonant states with arbitrarily large quality factors can be created by changing the structure or varying a physical parameter slightly, and they can be used to enhance nonlinear wave phenomena. In this project, we study a number of applications of BICs in nonlinear optics, including harmonic generation, optical bistability and symmetry breaking. Harmonic generation is a process that converts power from an incident wave of a fixed frequency to higher harmonic waves. Optical bistability is the case where two stable solutions exist for identical incident waves. Symmetry breaking refers to the situation where asymmetric solutions exist on symmetric structures with symmetric incident waves. We aim to realize these nonlinear wave phenomena in tiny structures (of wavelength size at least in one direction) consisting of ordinary nonlinear materials. For harmonic generation, we aim to increase the percentage of power converted to higher harmonic waves. For optical bistability and symmetry breaking, we aim to reduce the intensity of the incident waves and minimize the energy needed to switch from one solution to another. The realization of these nonlinear optical phenomena may lead to practical applications as light sources and optical switches. 連續譜中的綁定態(BIC)是一種在輻射頻率區間內的局部化的特解，也就是線性算子連續譜中的離散特徵值，對應的遍值問題無唯一解。在開放的結構中，共振態是一種複頻率向外發射能量的特解。接近BIC時，共振態的質量因子會發散，因而可以增強各種非線性效應。本研究項目將探索BIC在非線性光學中的應用，包括諧波生成，雙穩定及對稱波缺。諧波生成是指用低頻的波來生成高頻的波。雙穩定是指一個入射波所對應的兩個穩定的解。對稱波缺是指對稱結構對稱入射波時的非對稱解。利用BIC，我們希望將這些非線性現象在波長尺寸的結構中實現。對於諧波生成，我們希望提高能量從低頻轉入高頻的比率。對於雙穩定及對稱破缺，我們希望降低從一個解轉換到另一個解所需要的能量。解決好這些問題對工程應用(包括光源及光學開關)有重要的意義。

11307720.label: Realisation of objectives
11307720.value: The first objective is fully realized. Since optical nonlinear effects are usually very week, it is important to use resonances to enhance nonlinear effects such as harmonic generation. A resonance can produce a strong local field, even if the incident wave is not very strong. Harmonic generation can be enhanced by strong resonances. For second harmonc generation, if local field is enhanced by a factor of E, second harmonic can be enhanced by a factor of E^2. On the other hand, the local field enhancement factor E is related to the square root of the resonance Q factor. Therefore, second harmonic can be enhanced by a factor on the order of Q. However, for practical application of harmonic generation, the pump (incident waves given at the foudamental frequency) frequency may be not exactly the resonant frequency. This implies that the local field enhancement may be not as large as that obtained at the perfect resonant frequency. In Paper [1], we developed a theory on frequency perturbation of bound states in the continuum (BICs), Although the Q factor can be arbitrarily large near a BIC, the field enhancement is always finite when the pump frequency is not exactly the BIC frequency. This study helps to understand harmonic generation enhanced by BICs in realistic conditions. The second objective is mostly realized. Unlike second harmonic generation which relies on second order nonlinearity, optical bistability relies on the third order nonlinearity, but both second and third order nonlinear optcal effects are weak, and need to be enhanced by strong resonances associated with BICs. For harmonic generation, under the undepleted pump approximation, the effect of incident wave intensitity is quite simple. But for optical bistability, the situation is more complcated, since the field intensity effectively changes the refractive index profile, and the probem is always fully nonlinear. To understand this complicated process, we developed a general theory on how BICs depend on parameters in Paper [2]. The theory indicate that a generic BIC is associated with an integer n. If n=0, then the BIC is robust in the sense that the BIC can continue to exist under generic structural perturbation. The third objective is also mostly realized. In nonlinear systems, when the structure has certian symmetry, the solution may or may not retain the same symmetry, giving rise to symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking solutions. Near a BIC, there could be symmetry-breaking solutions associated with relatively weak incident fields. Near some special BICs, when a structural parameter is tuned, there can be pairs of generic propagating BIC solutions that break the symmetry in a spatial variable. In Paper [3], such BIC bifurcation phenomena are analyzed. We indentify conditions, so that BICs appear as saddle-node and pitch-fork bifurcations, respectively. For all three objectives, BICs play a fundamental role, since resonances near a BIC (due to structural perturbations that break the relevant symmetry) can have a very large Q factor which gives rise to large local field and enhances noninear optical effects. A kind of BICs, the so-called Fabry-Perot BICs, is formed in structures consisting of two scatterers separated by a distance, where the scatterer may be a periodic array. A single scatterer may have special frequencies at which the reflected wave is totally evanescent (i.e. zero reflection for propagating waves). The relationship between zero reflection and Fabry-Perot BICs is investigted in Paper [4].

11307720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307720.value: Major findings of this project are give in four publications. In Paper [1], entitled "Frequency perturbation theory of bound states in the continuum in a periodic waveguide", waves at a frequency slightly different from that of a BIC are analyzed. The paper reveals an interesting difference between perturbations in wavevector and in frequency, and shows that frequency perturbation can gives rise to leaky modes (as expected) and also unexpectedly the so-called complex modes that de not radiate power to infinity. The study is helpful to analyz wave phenomena, such as harmonic generation, operating near the frequency of a BIC. Paper [2], entitled "Parametric dependence of bound states in the continuum: A general theory", shows that a generic BIC is associated with an integer n. If n=0, the BIC is robust. If n>0, the BIC is not robust, but if the structure is perturbed with n parameters properly tuned, the BIC still can exist continuously. The study is relavent for study of optical bistability, since in such cases, the dielectric profile is effectedly perturbed by a small nonlinear coeffiient mulipled to the field intensity. Paper [3], entitled "Bifurcation of bound states in the continuum in periodic structures", analyzes the emergnece of BICs that break the symmetry in a special variable. More specifically, in structures which are periodic in spetial variable y, if the original structure has reflection symmetry in y and the BIC is even in y, then under perturbations that preserve the reflection symmetry of the structure, a pair of BICs that break the reflection symmetry may appear, leading to the saddle node bifurcation. On the other hand, if the BIC is odd in y, symmetry-breaking BICs can only appears if the BIC satisfies a special condition. This leads to pitch-fork bifurcations. Paper [4], entitlded "Relationship between total reflection and Fabry-Perot bound states in the continuum", analyze the relationship between zero reflection and Fabry-Perot BICs. The paper shows that if the structure has no reflection symmetry in the periodic direction y, then the existence of a total reflection at some frequency and some non-zero wavevnumber, may not imply the existence of a BIC with nearby frequency and wavenumber, even when additional structural parameters are tuned. In other cases, the existenve of a zero reflection leads to the existence of a BIC if one additional parameter is tuned. In such case, we have a simple approach to construct BICs for applications such as hrmonic generation, optical bistability and symmetry breaking.

11307720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307720.value: The fact that BICs can be used to enhancement nonlinear optical effects is now well-known and supported by some excellent experimental works. While an ideal BIC is a special resonance with an infinite Q factor, in practice, there is only a resonant mode with a relatively large Q factor due to fabrication errors, material losses, and finite size of the structure. That means that the practical enhancement of nonlinear effects is still limited. However, it has been realized that under the same practical conditions, the so-called super-BICs can give rise to resonances with much higher Q factors. We have recently developed a comprehensive theory on super-BICs in the preprint: "N. Zhang and Y. Y. Lu, Super Bound States in the Continuum: Analytic Framework, Parametric Dependence, and Fast Direct Computation, arXiv:2505.00235." We hope the theory can help physicists and engineers to realize much stronger nonlinear effects based on structures with super-BICs.

11307720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307720.value: Harmonic generarion, optical bistability and symmetry breaking are well-known nonlinear phenomena that can be realized when light is illuminated on a nonlinear material. However, these nonlinear effects are usually very weak. To observe these phenomena, usually one has to use a very powerful laser or a very large structure (compared to the wavelength of light). To realize their applications in nanophotonic devices, we have to use high-Q resonances to enhance the nonlinear effects. The so-called bound states in the continuum (BICs) are resonances with an infinite Q-factor, and they lead to high-Q resonances in actually fabricated structures. The purpose of this project is to reveal how BICs can be wisely used to enhance different kind of nonlinear optical effects.

11308020.value: Approximation theory of deep CNNs induced by 2-D convolutions and channels.We propose a new distributed scheme of deep CNNs induced by 2-D convolutions without zero-padding, and plan to establish an approximation theory for this deep CNN scheme in terms of the number of channels, and regularity and tensor type sparsity of the approximated function. First we plan to study localization of deep neural networks by means of sparsity of the approximated function. Then we consider approximation by ReLU deep neural networks of functions from Sobolev spaces of mixed smoothness. For functions of tensor structured matrices, we plan to investigate the approximation and learning by 2-D multi-channel distributed deep CNNs and drive error bounds in terms of the sparsity of the variable matrix, properties of the function, and the number of channels.

11308020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308020.value: Deep learning has been a powerful tool in many practical applications. In computer vision, deep learning based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of matrices by 2-D convolutions is very efficient in capturing features of natural images, but its mathematical theory, especially its approximation ability, is not well understood. The goal of this project is to study the approximation ability of deep CNNs induced by 2-D convolutions and parallel channels, and to investigate related approximation theoretical problems. First we propose a new distributed scheme of deep CNNs induced by 2-D convolutions and channels without zero-padding which can be applied in mobile devices and is related to depth wise separable CNNs. We plan to establish an approximation theory for these CNN schemes in terms of the number of channels. Then we consider some approximation theoretical problems arising from deep learning, including localization of deep neural networks, approximation by ReLU deep neural networks of functions from Sobolev spaces of mixed smoothness, and approximation and learning of functions of tensor structured matrices by 2-D multi-channel distributed deep CNNs in terms of sparse tensor structures of matrices and the induced functions. Interactions among deep learning, approximation theory, and wavelets are crucial in the project. 深度學習已成為許多實際應用中的強大工具。在計算機視覺中, 基於深度卷積神經網絡（CNNs）通過二維卷積對矩陣進行深度學習在捕獲自然圖像的特徵方面非常有效，但是其數學理論，尤其是其逼近能力，尚未完全了解。本項目的目的是研究由二維卷積和並行通道引起深層CNN的逼近能力，並研究相關的逼近論問題。首先，我們提出一種由二維卷積和通道誘導的深度CNN的無需填充零的新分佈式格式，可以應用於移動設備，並且與深度可分離CNN有關。我們計劃根據信道數量為這些CNN格式建立一個逼近理論。然後我們考慮深度學習引起的一些逼近論問題，包括深度神經網絡的定點，通過ReLU深層神經網絡逼近來自混合光滑度Sobolev空間的函數, 應用二維多通道深度CNN對有張量結構的矩陣的函數進行逼近與學習。深度學習，逼近論和小波分析之間的互動在本項目中至關重要。

11308020.label: Realisation of objectives
11308020.value: An approximation theory for this deep CNN scheme in terms of the number of channels, regularity, and tensor type sparsity of the approximated function has made significant progress in achieving the project objectives. The published paper titled "Approximation analysis of CNNs from a feature extraction view" has made important contributions to this objective. In the paper, analysis for linear feature extraction by a deep multi-channel convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has been established. This demonstrates the power of deep learning over traditional linear transformations like Fourier, wavelets, and redundant dictionary coding methods. An exact construction presenting how linear features extraction can be conducted efficiently with multi-channel CNNs has been given. This can be applied to lower the essential dimension for approximating a high-dimensional function. Rates of function approximation by such deep networks implemented with channels and followed by fully connected layers have been investigated. Harmonic analysis for factorizing linear features into multi-resolution convolutions has played an essential role in the work, furthering the understanding of the approximation theory. On the other hand, the project has made substantial progress in achieving its application-related objectives. A generalization analysis of a deep CNN algorithm for binary classification with data on spheres has been developed. This analysis is based on efficient cubature formulae on spheres and other tools from spherical analysis and approximation theory, contributing to a better theoretical understanding of deep CNNs in binary classification tasks. A distributed weighted regularized least squares algorithm (DWRLS) with radial basis functions was proposed to handle spherical data stored across numerous local servers that cannot be shared. By developing a novel integral operator approach based on spherical quadrature rules, optimal approximation rates for DWRLS were derived. For some Approximation problems arising from deep learning. The completion of the paper on convergence analysis for deep sparse coding via convolutional neural networks is a major achievement. A novel class of Deep Sparse Coding (DSC) models has been introduced, and a thorough theoretical analysis of their uniqueness and stability properties has been established. Convergence rates for convolutional neural networks in their ability to extract sparse features have been derived through iterative algorithms, providing a solid theoretical foundation for sparse feature learning tasks. The convergence analysis has been extended to more general neural network architectures, including those with diverse activation functions, self-attention, and transformer-based models, broadening the applicability of the findings.

An approximation theory related to aspects like the number of channels, regularity, and tensor type sparsity of the approximated function was explored, with foundational work laid through published papers. For example, in the published paper[3], the power of deep learning over traditional linear transformations in linear feature extraction by deep multi-channel CNNs was demonstrated. Exact constructions for efficient linear feature extraction and investigations into function approximation rates by such networks with channels followed by fully connected layers were presented. 2. Generalization Analysis for CNNs: Generalization analysis for a deep CNN algorithm in binary classification with data on spheres was developed in the paper [4]. By considering function approximation in the Lp space and leveraging tools from spherical analysis and approximation theory, rates of Lp-approximation, generalization bounds, and learning rates for the excess misclassification error of the algorithm were provided. A distributed weighted regularized least squares algorithm (DWRLS) was proposed for handling spherical data across local servers. Optimal approximation rates for DWRLS were derived, and it was shown that distributed learning can effectively exploit the potential of such data even without access to the whole dataset. 3. Deep Sparse Coding and Convergence Analysis: In the paper [7], A novel class of Deep Sparse Coding (DSC) models was introduced. Thorough theoretical analyses of their uniqueness and stability properties were established. Convergence rates for convolutional neural networks in extracting sparse features were derived through iterative algorithms. The convergence analysis was extended to more general neural network architectures, and training strategies to encourage neural networks to learn sparse features were explored. Numerical experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of these strategies, offering valuable insights for designing efficient and interpretable deep learning models. Overall, the research has made significant contributions to the understanding of deep learning from multiple aspects, including approximation theory, generalization analysis, and sparse coding, and has provided theoretical foundations and practical insights that can be applied to further develop and optimize deep learning models in various application scenarios.

11308020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11308020.value: The research has made significant progress but there's room for more. To further develop, refine the approximation theory for deep CNNs, expand generalization analysis to other tasks and data, explore sparse coding training strategies and applications. Combine findings, collaborate with other fields, conduct large-scale experiments. Also, focus on interpretability. This will enhance our understanding and performance of deep learning models, opening new avenues for research and practical applications. Study how the approximation theory and sparse coding can contribute to the interpretability of deep models. For example, analyze how the sparsity of the approximated function relates to the interpretability of the model and how it can be used to provide insights into the model's behavior.

11308020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11308020.value: This research project focuses on the approximation theory of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). It proposes innovative distributed schemes and conducts in-depth analyses of deep learning algorithms. The significance lies in providing a deeper understanding of why deep learning is highly effective in fields such as speech recognition and computer vision. By exploring novel approaches, it offers means to enhance the efficiency and interpretability of these networks. This research is extremely valuable as it builds a bridge between theoretical understanding and practical applications. It paves the way for more intelligent and useful implementations of deep learning in a wide range of real-world scenarios, advancing our technological capabilities.

11308120.label: Project Objectives
11308120.value: To develop a new diamond-based single-atom catalyst (SAC) through loading single metal atoms (M, M=Fe, Co, and Ni) on nanostructured and boron-doped diamonds. The atomically dispersed metal atoms will be anchored through coordination with surface modified N- or O-containing groups. The effects of the different diamond nanostructure, surface functional groups, metal atom binding conditions on the loading efficiency, dispersion degree, and chemical states of metal atoms will be disclosed. To evaluate the catalytic performance of SACs/diamond as electrodes for CO2 reduction reaction, and to reveal the effects of the doping level and surface nanostructure of diamond, the type of metals, loading amount and coordination structure of metal atoms, and electrochemical test conditions on the CO2 reduction performance including yield, Faraday efficiency, selectivity and stability. Through comprehensive characterization and theoretical simulation, to identify the preferential binding sites of metal atoms on diamond surfaces modified with different functional groups, and to understand the origin of CO2 reduction activity of SACs/diamond and the corresponding reaction paths.
