11308120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308120.value: As a greenhouse gas, the increasing CO2 in the atmosphere has a profound impact on global climate change. Capturing and reutilizing CO2, in addition to curbing the reliance on fossil fuels, is an effective strategy to decrease the atmospheric concentration of CO2. For recycling CO2, the electrochemical reduction of CO2 is a promising approach. However, the conversion efficiency and selectivity of the current electrochemical CO2 reduction processes are still unsatisfactorily enslaved by the weak CO2 adsorption on the active sites of an electrocatalyst and the difficulty in C=O cleavage there. Developing an electrocatalyst with high-efficiency active sites for promoting CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) has thus important scientific and application values for the advance of the technique. Basically, an ideal CO2RR electrocatalyst should possess high intrinsic catalytic reactivity and selectivity toward CO2RR, large active surface, and outstanding mechanical and chemical stabilities. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) of selected transition metals hosted on carbon substrates have emerged as a promising system for CO2RR because of the maximal atom utilization (approximate to 100%) and the resultant high efficiency. As a distinctive member of carbon family, sp3-configurated diamond has a series of inherent properties favorable for electrocatalytic CO2RR, particularly a large electrochemical window in comparison with other sp2 carbon phases, which enables to suppress the competitive hydrogen evolution reaction and thus to achieve a high CO2RR selectivity. In this project, we propose to develop a new high-efficiency SAC for CO2 conversion through loading single metal atoms (M, M=Fe, Co, and Ni) on nanostructured and boron-doped diamond films. The basic idea is to endow diamond with good electrical conductivity and large active area through doping and surface nanostructuring, respectively; and the atomically dispersed metal atoms will be anchored through coordination with surface modified N- or O-containing groups on diamond surface. The effects of the factors such as the doping level and surface nanostructure of diamond, the type of metals, and the loading amount and coordination structure of metal atoms, on the CO2RR performance will be elucidated. Through comprehensive characterization and theoretical simulation, the preferential binding sites of metal atoms, the origin of CO2RR activity of SACs/diamond and the corresponding reaction paths will be demonstrated. Implementation of this project will provide further understanding for the design and development of new diamond-based SACs for high-efficiency CO2RR and promote the advance of CO2 conversion technology. 二氧化碳是一種溫室氣體，其大量排放對全球氣候變化會產生深遠的不利影響。捕獲和再利用二氧化碳是降低大氣中二氧化碳濃度以及緩解社會對化石燃料依賴的有效策略。通過電化學技術將二氧化碳還原以製備碳基化學品是一種實現碳迴圈的有前景的途徑。然而，受到C=O裂解的困難以及電催化劑活性不高的制約，目前二氧化碳電還原（CO2RR）的轉化效率和選擇性仍然較低。因此，設計開發高活性、高選擇性的電催化劑對於CO2RR技術的進步具有重要的科學意義和應用價值。 理想的CO2RR電催化劑一般應具有對CO2RR高的本征催化活性和選擇性，大的活性比表面積，優異的機械和化學穩定性。單原子催化劑具有最大的原子利用率（接近100%），及高的催化效率，是一類非常有潛力的CO2RR電催化劑。 作為碳材料家族的獨特一員，sp3雜化的金剛石具有一系列益於CO2電還原的特性，尤其是與其他sp2雜化的碳材料相比，它具有更寬的電化學窗口，從而可以抑制CO2還原過程中的析氫反應，實現較高的CO2還原轉化率。在本課題中，我們擬將金屬單原子（M，M=Fe、Co和Ni）負載在硼摻雜的納米結構金剛石上，開發一類新的高效CO2電還原單原子催化劑。實驗中將通過摻雜和表面納米化製備高導電性和大比表面積的硼摻雜納米結構金剛石電極，通過在金剛石表面修飾含氮或含氧基團作為配位元點實現金屬原子的錨定和原子級分散。我們將研究金剛石的摻雜水平、表面納米結構、金屬種類、金屬原子的負載量和配位結構等因素對CO2RR性能的影響。通過綜合表徵及理論模擬，揭示金剛石基單原子催化劑催化CO2還原的活性位點及反應機理。本項目的實施將為CO2電還原領域中新型高效催化電極的製備提供實驗基礎和理論依據。

11308120.label: Realisation of objectives
11308120.value: 1. Preparation of single-metal active site/diamond electrodes. We have synthesized boron-doped sub-micron diamond films (referred to as D films) on silicon substrates by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD) with a gas mixture of trimethylborane (TMB)/CH4/H2. To adjust the electrical conductivity of diamond films, the atomic ratio of boron to carbon (B/C) was varied from 1000 ppm to 5000 ppm. The as-synthesized D films were then subjected to bias-assisted reactive ion etching (RIE) in the electron cyclotron resonance enhanced microwave plasma (ECR-MPCVD), with a gas mixture of 40% Ar and 60% H2, to prepare the nanostructured diamond electrodes at a negative bias ranging from -100 V to -350 V. It was revealed that diamond nanocone arrays (denoted as Dcone) were obtained at a negative substrate bias of -125 V, while diamond nanorod arrays (denoted as Drod) was achieved at an elevated bias of -325 V. The surfaces of both the D films and the nanostructured D films were further treated with oxygen plasma, introducing surface oxygen functionalities (denoted as OD) to facilitate the anchoring of single-metal sites. Single-metal active sites (SAS) were attached to the oxygen-functionalized diamond electrodes via a hydrothermal method. Comprehensive characterization techniques, including scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, were employed to confirm the successful attachment of single metals to the diamond electrodes. It was shown that the surface functional groups, nanostructures, and hydrothermal reaction conditions significantly influenced the loading of single-metal sites. Specifically, surface oxygen functionalization, the formation of surface nanoarrays, and higher temperatures in hydrothermal reactions enhanced the attachment of single-metal centers, leading to improved loading efficiency. Furthermore, surface oxygen functionalization was crucial for the dispersion, chemical states, and stability of single-metal sites. For instance, in the absence of oxygen functional groups, Co sites tended to aggregate on the diamond surface through physical deposition. In contrast, with oxygen functional groups present, Co sites could chemically bind to the diamond surface, resulting in single-atom dispersion. The formation of Co-O bonds not only created electron-deficient Co centers, which enhanced electrocatalytic activity for CO2 reduction by lowering the *CO2− formation free energy, but also improved the stability of the electrode. 2. Evaluation of the catalytic performance of single-metal active site/diamond as electrodes for CO2 reduction reaction. We directly utilized the SAS/OD electrode as a self-supporting electrode for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (CO2RR), eliminating the need for binders or additional preparation steps. The study revealed that increasing the B doping level in the diamond led to an initial rise in CO2RR activity, which subsequently declined due to the competitive hydrogen evolution reaction. Electrochemical test conditions also affected CO2RR activity and electrode stability, with higher applied potential or current resulting in increased hydrogen evolution and reduced stability. The SAS/OD electrode exhibited a higher current density and a lower onset potential compared to SAS/D and OD. It maintained a high CO Faradaic efficiency (FE) across a wide voltage range, reaching 86.3% at -0.97 V vs. RHE, with its partial current density of CO surpassing that of SAS/D. Moreover, the SAS/OD demonstrated superior stability. The enhanced electrochemical performance of SAS/OD electrodes in CO2 reduction can be attributed to the following factors. 1) The highly dispersed active sites: The immobilized hydroxyl groups promote greater exposure of active sites. 2) The coordination between the O and Co: The interaction between oxygen in hydroxyl groups and cobalt results in the formation of electron-deficient Co centers. This facilitates easier electron delocalization from the Co 3d orbital to the π* orbital of CO2, enhancing the bonding with CO2 molecules and thereby increasing CO2 catalytic activity. In addition, since the intrinsic catalytic centers derive from the metal sites, factors such as the type of metals, loading amount, and coordination structure of metal sites significantly influence the CO2RR performance of the electrodes. To further improve the electrocatalytic CO2RR performance of SAS/diamond electrodes, we utilized a surface nanostructuring strategy to increase the reaction surface area and manipulate the adsorption-desorption dynamics. In CO2RR, SAS/ ODcone and SAS/ODrod exhibited higher current density and lower onset potential compared to SAS/OD, confirming the significant enhancement from surface nanostructuring. SAS/ODcone maintained a steady current density across various voltages, reaching a peak current density of 14.8 mA cm-2 at -1.17 V vs. RHE, with the CO FE exceeding 80% across a potential range of -0.67 V to -1.07 V vs. RHE, peaking at 94.1% at -0.97 V vs. RHE. SAS/ODcone also demonstrated stable performance over 200 minutes at -0.97 V vs. RHE, maintaining an average current density of -7 mA cm-2 and consistently achieving a CO Faraday efficiency exceeding 90%. 3. Understanding on the origin of high CO2 reduction activity of SAS/ODrod. We employed various techniques to investigate the origin of the high CO2 reduction activity of SAS/ODrod, demonstrating that its outstanding performance results from the synergistic effects of the diamond nanocone surface and the SAS. The oxygen atoms of surface hydroxyl groups (or nitrogen atoms in surface nitrogen-containing functional groups) serve as preferential binding sites, facilitating the anchoring of SAS and bonding with Co atoms, which in turn modifies Co's electron density and chemical properties. Additionally, the enhanced intrinsic activity of SAS/ODcone is closely related to the field-induced reagent concentration effect (FIRC). The rate-determining step of CO2 reduction on SAS/diamond electrodes involves converting CO2 to *CO2, making the initial adsorption of CO2 critical. The high tip curvature of diamond nanocones promotes the gathering of CO2 molecules near the sharp tips due to the tip-induced electric field. Consequently, the adsorption and subsequent single-electron reduction of CO2 are significantly accelerated, leading to remarkable enhancements in CO2 reduction activity for SAS/ODcone.

11308120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11308120.value: In this project, we have fabricated single-atom sites (SAS)/oxygen-terminated diamond nanocone electrodes for efficient CO2 electrochemical reduction, employing an innovative approach through plasma-enhanced surface engineering. The SAS/ODcone electrode demonstrates remarkable performance, achieving a maximum Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 94.1% for CO at -0.97 V vs. RHE, and maintaining an FE for CO higher than 80% across a broad potential range of -0.67 V to -1.07 V vs. RHE. The outstanding efficacy of the SAS/ODcone electrode can be attributed to the synergistic effects of the unique diamond nanocone surface and the SAS. The hydroxyl-rich nature of the diamond surface not only facilitates the anchoring of SAS but also fosters the bonding with Co atoms. This interaction modifies the electron density of Co, significantly altering its chemical properties and enhancing its catalytic capabilities. Additionally, the field-induced reagent concentration effect plays a crucial role in accelerating CO2 electroreduction on the SAS/ODcone electrode through enhancing CO2 adsorption and promoting more efficient electrochemical reactions. These findings provide valuable insights into the potential of carbon materials, particularly diamond, as effective catalysts for the electrochemical reduction of CO2. The study also highlights the advantages of using diamond electrodes, such as their robustness and stability, while addressing the inherent challenges like suboptimal current density and insufficient Faradaic efficiency. Overall, this study paves the way for the development of more efficient catalysts for CO2 electroreduction by leveraging the unique properties of diamond nanostructures. The approach not only improves performance metrics but also opens up new avenues for research into the design of advanced electrode materials, contributing to the broader goal of sustainable energy solutions and carbon capture technologies.

11308120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11308120.value: The development of high-efficiency catalysts offers a promising pathway for advancing CO2 electroreduction techniques. The SAS/oxygen-terminated diamond nanocone electrodes have demonstrated exceptional performance in converting CO2 to CO, achieving impressive Faradaic efficiency and partial current density. The synergistic effects of the diamond nanocone surface and the SAS have been crucial in achieving this remarkable performance. To further advance this research, future efforts should focus on enhancing diamond-based catalysts' current density and Faradaic efficiency. Exploring novel surface engineering techniques, such as tailored functionalization or advanced nanostructuring, could unlock even higher efficiencies and improve stability across broader electrochemical windows for CO2 reduction. Additionally, assessing these diamond-based catalysts' scalability and long-term stability in practical applications will be essential for their commercial viability. Addressing these aspects could lead to the development of more efficient and stable catalysts not only for CO2 electroreduction but also for nitrate electroreduction, oxygen electroreduction, and organic electrosynthesis. This would significantly contribute to the sustainable utilization of carbon materials in electrochemical processes and support broader goals in energy conversion and environmental remediation. By focusing on these key areas, we can pave the way for innovative solutions in the field of electrocatalysis, enhancing both performance and practicality in real-world applications.

11308120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11308120.value: CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion pose a serious threat to the environment and hinder sustainable development. Electrochemical conversion of CO2 into useful chemicals and fuels is a viable solution for reducing emissions and providing alternative energy sources. However, the strong C=O bond (799 kJ/mol) in CO2 presents significant challenges for transformation. The development of efficient electrocatalysts is thus vital to boost reaction rates and enhance the selectivity of CO2 electroreduction. In this project, we developed an innovative strategy using plasma-enhanced surface engineering to fabricate single-cobalt active sites on diamond nanocone electrodes. This approach resulted in an electrode that demonstrates outstanding performance, achieving a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 94.1% for CO at a potential of -0.97 V versus RHE. Furthermore, the electrode maintains a CO Faradaic efficiency consistently above 80% across a broad potential range from -0.67 V to -1.07 V versus RHE. These findings provide valuable insights into the potential of carbon materials, particularly diamond, as effective catalysts for the electrochemical reduction of CO2 and other electrocatalytic reactions. By harnessing the unique properties of diamond, we can advance the development of high-performance catalysts, contributing to more sustainable energy solutions and the mitigation of environmental impacts associated with CO2 emissions.

11308220.label: Project Objectives
11308220.value: To design and prepare shape-persistent binuclear complexes bearing chelating C-donor ligands that display predetermined to adjustable intermetallic distances and geometry. 11308220.label: Realisation of objectives
11308220.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. In addition, the training of one PhD student was completed, and a Plenary Lecture was presented at the International Symposium on Homogeneous Catalysis in Lisbon. Objective 1: In this project, new classes of shape-persistent bimetallic complexes supported by multidentate ligands, bearing diverse C-based aryl and alkyl bridging moieties, have been prepared. In particular, the C-based bridging groups developed here are designed to engender predetermined [mu-(sigma-aryl)] and adjustable [meta- and para-(di-methine)phenylene] metal-metal distances and geometry. In this connection, complexes bearing the unusual chelating C(arylmethine) ligand, which would afford a more accessible active site that would facilitate insertion of bulky substrates, have also been developed. For the rigid [mu-(sigma-aryl)] binuclear series, metal-metal distances are fixed yet amenable for cooperativity, and the binding sites are aligned to promote substrate enchainment. The [(di-methine)phenylene] bimetallic frameworks are devised to exhibit a degree of rotational and conformational flexibility, thereby minimizing activation energies. Combined with the chelating bis-[pyridine-phenolate] units, these C-based bridging assemblies have been designed to afford bimetallic complexes in which the metal centers are in sufficiently close proximity, so that synergistic reactivity and cooperative effects (such as bimetallic enchainment interactions) can occur. Objective 2: The new families of complexes have been characterization by various spectroscopic techniques (including multinuclear NMR spectroscopy), investigated using DFT calculations, and in many instances structurally characterized using X-ray crystallography. The binuclear [mu-(sigma-aryl)] complexes are generated in a regioselective manner to yield syn-type structures with para hydrogen atoms at the central mu-aryl moiety (formation of ortho hydrogens would give undesirable anti-type products). Characterization by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy revealed that for all bis-titanium derivatives, the benzyl groups adopt eta(2)-coordination and rotations of the Ti−C(benzyl) bonds are impeded. The molecular structures of six syn-type bimetallic derivatives have been determined by X-ray crystallography, which revealed relatively close M…M distances of 6.3–6.7 angstroms, and binding sites that are aligned to promote substrate enchainment. The bimetallic bis-[(pyridine-2-phenolate-6-methine)M] (M = Ti, Zr, Hf) complexes bearing meta- and para-phenylene bridging groups have been synthesized and characterized by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, together with [1H, 1H]-COSY and ROESY, [13C, 1H]-HSQC and DEPT-135 experiments. There are two chiral centers in each binuclear complex, which exists as two diastereomers [namely meso (RS) and rac (RR, SS)], and two sets of NMR resonances are observed due to symmetry. Regarding the (pyridine-2-phenolate-6-arylmethine) complexes, [1H,19F]-COSY and -HOESY experiments have been conducted to elucidate the environment around the fluorine atoms at the aryl substituent, which revealed close proximity between the H(methine) proton and ortho-F atoms on the aryl group, and consequently a weak C–H(methine)...F–C interaction. The molecular structures of two Zr derivatives have been determined by X-ray crystallography, which confirmed that the tridentate C(sp3)-chelate affords a relatively small bite angle. Importantly, for both [mu-(sigma-aryl)] and [(di-methine)phenylene] binuclear systems, DFT calculations have been performed for plausible catalytic intermediates to model bimetallic enchainment interactions. Hence, the energy-minimised calculated (Gaussian) structures of (pi-coordinated)-octene bis-titanium dicationic species reveal agostic interactions with the supplementary Ti center, signifying bimetallic, cooperative enchainment of the alpha-olefin. Objective 3: The olefin polymerization reactivity of the newly developed catalysts have been investigated. In olefin polymerization, cooperative effects for bimetallic catalysts can transpire when the secondary metal center interacts with and stabilizes the propagating chain, thereby suppressing chain transfer/termination rates to give increased molecular-weight polymers. Furthermore, bimetallic enchainment of a vinyl-ended oligomer/polymer fragment can facilitate its reinsertion and also produce higher molecular-weight polymers, while enchainment of alpha-olefin comonomers in copolymerization reactions can lead to enhanced selectivity and incorporation. For the binuclear [mu-(sigma-aryl)] system, good efficiencies for ethylene and ethylene/1-octene polymerization reactions have been observed for bis-titanium catalysts, and evidence of octene incorporation have been obtained. Significantly, compared with mono-Ti and control derivatives, the bis-titanium catalysts show enhanced activities and produced polymers with higher molecular weights, thus indicative of favorable enchainment interactions and cooperative reactivity at the bimetallic centers. The meta- and para-[(di-methine)phenylene] bis-titanium catalysts exhibit excellent olefin homo- and copolymerization activities in conjunction with trityl borate. For ethylene polymerization, the highest activity was observed for the meta-(bis-titanium) catalyst, and importantly, the bimetallic catalysts display higher activities than mononuclear congeners. For ethylene/1-octene copolymerization reactions, the 1-octene incorporation ratio for both the para- and meta-(bis-titanium) catalysts are significantly higher than for the mononuclear controls, indicating enhanced 1-octene enchainment and hence bimetallic cooperativity. The (pyridine-2-phenolate-6-arylmethine) catalysts display excellent activities for ethylene polymerization reactions. In general, they are more active than the previously developed sigma-aryl relatives, and produced polymers with relatively narrow MW distributions, suggestive of single-site character. Significantly, the observed properties of polymers produced by fluorine-substituted catalysts indicate behavior consistent with the previously established, novel concept of ‘weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions’.

11308220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11308220.value: Coplanar, rigid bimetallic assemblies have been developed through the expansion of the M-[O,N,C] [pyridine-2-phenolate-6-(sigma-aryl)] catalyst system. The resultant complexes afford metal-metal distances that are amenable for cooperativity, as well as locked-in “syn” orientation of binding sites that offer the same direction of access to promote substrate enchainment. The binuclear complexes are generated in a regioselective manner to yield para hydrogen atoms (not ortho) at the central mu-aryl moiety, and have been characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. Six syn-type bimetallic derivatives of Ti, Zr and Hf have been characterized by X-ray crystallography, to reveal metal-metal separations of 6.3–6.7 angstroms. For ethylene and ethylene/1-octene polymerization reactions in conjunction with trityl borate, the bis-titanium catalysts display superior efficiencies and produced polymers with higher molecular weights than for mono-Ti and control derivatives, thus indicating favorable enchainment interactions and cooperative reactivity at the bis-titanium sites. [Publication 1] A series of Ti(IV) and Zr(IV) post-metallocene precatalysts containing an unusual C(sp3)-chelating [O,N,CH(Ar)] ligand has been synthesized and fully characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. Compared with sigma-aryl, the C(sp3) donor (without pi-donation) produces a more electrophilic active site and engenders greater flexibility, and the four-membered N,C-donor chelate is anticipated to engender more accessible active sites. The molecular structures of two Zr derivatives have been determined by X-ray crystallography. For olefin polymerization reactions in conjunction with trityl borate, the C(sp3)-donor titanium catalysts display excellent activities and are more efficient than sigma-aryl congeners, and polymers are produced with relatively narrow MW distributions, indicative of single-site character. Importantly, the results for fluorine-substituted catalysts indicate polymerization processes consistent with the previously established, novel concept of ‘weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions’. [Publication 2] Shape-persistent binuclear bis-[(pyridine-2-phenolate-6-methine)M] (M = Ti, Zr, Hf) complexes bearing meta- and para-phenylene bridging groups, which can offer variable intermetallic distances and geometry, have been prepared and characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. Studies have been undertaken to assess their olefin polymerization reactivity, and DFT calculations have been performed to investigate the nature of the active species. The bis-titanium catalysts display superior olefin homo- and copolymerization activities in conjunction with trityl borate. For ethylene/1-octene copolymerizations, the levels of 1-octene incorporation for the bis-titanium catalysts are higher than for the mononuclear control, indicating enhanced 1-octene enchainment and hence bimetallic cooperativity. [Publication 3]

11308220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11308220.value: Several families of shape-persistent bimetallic complexes bearing C-based bridging cores with predetermined or tunable intermetallic distances and geometry have been developed, and the design and synthetic investigations towards new and modified C-based bridging moieties may be undertaken. Further studies by various spectroscopic techniques, X-ray crystallography and DFT calculations can be performed to provide greater insights into the nature of the bimetallic complexes and develop strategies to modify and control the relative arrangement of metal-ligated moieties. It is envisaged that conformational and steric effects within the frameworks, and the important factor of the intermetallic separation between catalytic centers, can be examined. Bimetallic catalysts featuring more accessible active sites that can mediate high comonomer incorporation levels, and new reactivity and transformations for related C(sp3)-chelating catalysts, should be pursued. Future work to broaden the scope of catalytic applications, probe the bimetallic cooperativity (and enchainment interactions, with regards to copolymerization of alpha-olefins), and develop new catalyst systems for the production of valuable and desirable polymers are suggested. In general, the design and development of new multimetallic systems that can support novel catalytic processes, as well as cooperative reactivity, is proposed.

11308220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11308220.value: The project concerns the design and synthesis of shape-persistent bimetallic catalysts supported by chelating (non-cyclopentadienyl) C-donor ligands, investigation of the nature of the reaction environment and active sites, and the development of novel and cooperative reactivity for polymerization processes. Taking inspiration from nature, this project employed a modular strategy in the construction of coplanar and shape-persistent bimetallic systems with predefined to adjustable intermetallic separations and geometry, in anticipation of synergistic effects between adjacent catalytic centers as well as significant rate and selectivity enhancements in olefin polymerization reactions. Detailed investigations using a range of spectroscopic techniques (including multinuclear NMR spectroscopy) and DFT calculations have been undertaken, and the molecular structures of several key complexes have been characterized by X-ray crystallography. The ability of the complexes to catalyze olefin polymerization processes have been examined. Significantly, excellent activities have been observed for bimetallic catalysts that are superior to monometallic analogues, while evidence from copolymerization reactions signify favorable enchainment and elevated incorporation of alpha-olefins, and hence cooperative reactivity at the bimetallic centers. Furthermore, the copolymers produced display appealing rheological and mechanical properties, and are applicable as energy- and resource-efficient packaging materials that contribute towards greater sustainability.

11308620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308620.value: Nanopore sequencing technique is promising in breaking the limitation of the traditional sequencing method and reducing sequencing time in clinical applications, which would speed up disease diagnostics and enable precision medicine. Nanopore sensing based on 2D materials has attracted extensive attention for its atomic-scale resolution since the thickness of sensor is a single-atom layer. However, this novel technique is confronted with difficulties in sensor selection, stable driving force and distinguishable sensing signals. Among these difficulties, the selection of sensing signals is the most challenging due to the diversity of amino acids (AAs). So far no single detecting signal has been reported to reliably distinguish all the 20 AAs. Our goal is to identify all the 20 types of AAs by their characteristic signals. To achieve this, graphene nanoslit is adopted as sensor, by whose special geometry multi-dimensional sensing signals could be collected to enhance the distinguishability. We propose to simultaneously measure the constant-velocity pulling force and ionic current during residue permeation to provide improved distinguishability. Based on that, the translocation processes of 20 homogeneous polypeptide consisting one type of AA are simulated to obtain characteristic signals and get the force-ionic current profile of the residues. The primary relationship of signals and AA types will be established. We will also study the translocation of heterogeneous peptide chains consisting several types of AAs. The collected data will be used to train machine learning models, through whose classification function the ultimate relationship of signals and AAs will be established and all residues will be identified. Molecular Dynamics (MD) will be used to simulate the sequencing process during the translocation of different peptide through graphene nanoslit in potassium chloride solution. The peptide chain is facilitated through nanoslit by constant-velocity pulling under applied bias. Characteristic force and current signals could be collected during the translocation of every single residue, thus achieving sensing. The corresponding experiments will also be performed to verify our simulation predictions. Herein, force and current signals will be detected simultaneously using MD simulations, which provides a new way of sensing. Other sensing signals could also be combined to further address the difficulty of distinguishing all 20 types residues. Studying the correlation between signals and residues in different sequences will give insights on the sequencing mechanism. Most importantly, completely identifying different residues will pave the way for rapid diagnosis of diseases and personalized precision medicine. 納米孔測序技術有望突破傳統測序方法的局限性，並減少臨床應用中的測序時間，這將加快疾病診斷並實現精密醫學。由於器件的厚度為單原子層，因此基於2D材料的納米孔傳感因其原子尺度的分辨率而受到廣泛關注。然而，這種新技術在傳感器選擇，穩定的驅動力和可區分的感測信號方面面臨困難。在這些困難中，由於氨基酸（AA）的多樣性，選擇感測信號進行區分非常具有挑戰性。到目前為止，還沒有報告能夠可靠地區分所有20種AA的檢測信號。 我們的目標是通過其特徵信號識別所有20種類型的AA。為此，採用石墨烯納米縫作為傳感器，通過收集其特殊的幾何形狀多維感測信號來增強可分辨性。我們建議同時測量殘留物滲透過程中的恆速拉力和離子電流，以提供更好的可分辨性。在此基礎上，模擬由單一AA組成的均質多肽的穿孔過程，獲得殘基的特徵信號力-電流圖。將建立信號和AA類型的關聯關係。我們還將研究由幾種不同類型的AA組成的異源肽鏈的穿孔。收集的數據將用於訓練機器學習模型，通過其分類功能，將建立信號和AA的最終關係，並識別所有殘基。 分子動力學（MD）將用於模擬不同肽在氯化鉀溶液中通過石墨烯納米縫隙時的測序過程。通過在施加偏壓下以恆定速度拉動納米縫隙，可促進肽鏈穿孔。可以在每個殘基的易位過程中收集特徵力和電流信號，從而促進穿孔過程。還將進行相應的實驗以驗證我們的模擬預測。 在此建議中，將使用MD模擬同時檢測力和電流信號，這提供了一種新的傳感方式。其他傳感信號也可以組合起來，以進一步解決區分所有20種殘基的困難。研究不同序列中信號與殘基之間的相關性將為測序機制提供深刻見解。最重要的是，完全識別不同的殘留物將為疾病的快速診斷和個性化的精密醫學鋪平道路。

11308620.label: Realisation of objectives
11308620.value: We designed a special nanopore structure, nanopore, with a lower symmetry than circular nanopore; We identified the optimised geometry, i.e. the width and length of the nanoslite for best signal collection purpose for sequencing; We quantified the force and ionic currents for both homogenous and heterogeneous polypeptides; We are able to differentiate 20 different residues into 6 groups. We further applied this nanopore to control the translocation speed of DNA for sequencing; A hetero-planner 2D materials with both graphene and hexagonal BN can further differentiate four DNA bases apart. Finally, we test a new 2D materials Mxene for protein sequencing. We found nanopore with different terminal groups can further adjust the translocation time of protein residues.

11308620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11308620.value: A graphene nanoslit sensor is adopted to collect force and current signals to distinguish 20 residues. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations are performed on sequencing peptides under pulling force and applied electric field. Results show that the signals of force and current can be simultaneously collected. Tailoring the geometry of the nanoslit sensor optimizes signal differences between tyrosine and alanine residues. Using the tailored geometry, the characteristic signals of 20 types of residues are detected. (JPCL2021) To control DNA translocation speed and maintain sequencing sensitivity, the graphene nanoslit sensor is proposed and molecular dynamics simulations are performed to investigate geometric and electrophoretic effects. Results show that the translocation speed is slowed down and the detection range of nanoslit sensors maintains when reducing nanoslit width. Adjusting applied voltage can further control the translocation speed but in a non-linear way. Generally, the speed of a single-base translocation is expected to be well adjusted. (Carbon 2022) Molecular dynamics simulations are performed on investigating the motion of DNA molecules on the heterostructure with a nanoslit sensor. Results show that the DNA molecules are confined within the hexagonal boron nitride (HBN) domain of the heterostructure. Besides, there are two ways of DNA permeation through nanoslits: cross-slit and trans-slit, respectively. In both modes, the ionic currents and dwell times can be simultaneously detected to identify the four different DNA bases. (ACS Nano 2023) We designed a heterostructure with an hexagonal boron nitridehBN strip embedded in the graphene sheet. PolyQ peptides can spontaneously and linearly stretch out on the hBN stripe. By tuning the strength of an external in-plane electric field, molecular transportation of polyQ peptides along the hBN stripe can be effectively regulated. Subsequent cross-nanoslit motion can be applied to record time-dependent electric signals. The machine-learning-assisted recognition enables accurate determination of the protein’s length. (Huang, JPCL 2024 ) We investigate the influence of −F, −O, and −OH surface terminations on the translocation of peptides through MXene nanopores. We find that the longest dwell time always occurs when peptides pass through the Ti3C2O2 nanopores. This elongated dwell time is induced by the strongest interaction between peptides and the Ti3C2O2 membrane, in which the van der Waals interactions dominate. Our work demonstrates that membrane surface chemistry has a great influence on the translocation of peptides, which can be introduced in the design of nanopores for a better performance. (Chen, JPCL 2024)

11308620.value: The project aims to design a nanopore structure for protein sequencing. This nanopore has a rectangular geometry. We collected the ionic signal and forces of nanoslit with different width and length. We identified the optimised structure for sequencing. We further analysed the force and ionic currents for both homogenous and heterogenous polypetides, and were able to group 20 residues into six clusters. We hope in the future, we are able to utilize machine learning algorithm to further tell the residues in each cluster apart. Furthermore, we applied this nanopore for DNA sequencing, to control the translocation speed and differentiate 4 bases apart using dwell time and ionic current signals. Finally, we utilized Mxene nanopore with different functional group to test the ability of protein sequencing.

11308720.label: Realisation of objectives
11308720.value: To achieve Objective 1, the effects of the supporting electrolyte and the pre-treatment of carbon-based electrodes on bismuth electrodeposition and dissolution were investigated. The electrodeposition and dissolution of bismuth in methanesulfonic acid (MSA) were studied for the first time. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) was employed to determine the potential window, nucleation overpotential, and reaction kinetics of the three-electron bismuth reaction. Furthermore, the impact of nitrate and chloride additives on the bismuth reaction was analyzed. CV was used to investigate the reaction kinetics of the bismuth reaction with and without the additives. Tafel plots were employed to determine the exchange current density and equilibrium potential of bismuth reduction in the presence of the additives. Additionally, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed to elucidate the reaction mechanism and the effects of the additives. Finally, flow cells employing bismuth negolyte and cerium posolyte were assembled to evaluate the electrochemical performance of a bismuth-based flow battery in a full-cell operation. In addition, other redox couples with multi-electron transfer, such as zinc and tin deposition/dissolution were investigated. Objective 1 was completed to the extent of 100%. To achieve Objective 2, mixed redox couples of cerium and vanadium were adopted in the posolyte to increase the overall energy density of the Bi-Ce flow battery. The reaction kinetics and electrochemical performance of the mixed electrolyte were assessed using CV and full-cell characterization. During full-cell operation, multiple charge-discharge platforms were observed and analyzed. To further enhance the reaction kinetics of the cerium and vanadium redox couples, corresponding electrode engineering were applied, resulting in improved cell performance and stability. Moreover, to extend the application of the cerium electrolyte to other hybrid flow batteries with multi-electron transfer, such as zinc, a new cell configuration with an electrolyte decoupling characteristic was designed, which can mitigate incompatibility between the highly acidic cerium posolyte and neutral anode. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed in conjunction with experimental electrochemical measurements to study the effect of mixed supporting electrolytes on the cerium redox reaction. Objective 2 was completed to the extent of 100%. However, it was observed that the vanadium reaction was compromised in the mixed electrolyte. The underlying reasons for the compromised kinetics remain unclear and require further study. To achieve Objective 3, a comprehensive phase-field method was proposed to simulate the bismuth electrodeposition and dendrite growth in the Bi-Ce hybrid flow battery. The model unveiled the complex morphological evolution at the solid-liquid interface and the underlying mechanisms of dendrite growth. Concentration gradients and electric field intensity were identified as critical electrochemical driving forces for dendrite growth. The simulation also examined the impact of electrode surface conditions (smooth, seeded, and rough surfaces) on bismuth deposition morphology. In addition, operational parameters such as flow rate, current density, and deposition capacity were optimized using the simulation in conjunction with performance evaluations. The simulation model can also be extended to other multi-valent redox couples involving metal deposition and dissolution, providing valuable guidance for the development of other hybrid flow batteries. Objective 3 was completed to the extent of 100%.

11308720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11308720.value: 1. The electrochemical performance of the bismuth redox reaction in MSA is studied for the first time. Optimized concentration (3.5 M MSA) enhances the reversibility and activity of bismuth electrodeposition and dissolution [1, 2]. 2. The effects of nitrate and chloride additives on the bismuth reaction are evaluated. Nitrate additives improve diffusion and electron transfer due to smaller ligand size, reducing diffusion resistance and energy. Chloride additives show limited improvement due to the larger ligand size of BiCl₆³⁻. 3. The Bi-Ce flow cell with 1 M Bi³⁺ ions in the anolyte have a theoretical and experimental volumetric capacity of 80.4 Ah L⁻¹ and 72.4 Ah L⁻¹, respectively (90% utilization at 20–50 mA cm⁻²). [1] Additional studies on multi-electron redox couples, such as zinc (two-electron transfer) and alkaline tin (four-electron transfer), were carried out aiming to develop high-energy-density hybrid flow batteries [4, 7, 8]. 4. A mixed cerium-vanadium electrolyte is explored for the posolyte in Bi-based flow batteries. While cerium kinetics remain unaffected, vanadium kinetics are compromised. However, combining the mixed electrolyte with a porous electrode allows the use of 1.5 M Bi³⁺ ions in the anolyte, achieving a volumetric capacity of 120 Ah L⁻¹ with nearly 100% utilization [1]. Electrode engineering enhances cerium kinetics and stability against Ce⁴⁺ corrosion [3]. A new cell design with electrolyte decoupling mitigates incompatibility between acidic cerium posolyte and neutral anolyte, extending cerium posolyte to other hybrid flow batteries [5]. 5. A phase-field model simulates Bi-Ce hybrid flow batteries to reveal the morphological evolution of bismuth deposition. Concentration gradients and electric field intensity were identified as critical electrochemical driving forces for dendrite growth. Further, dendrite grow is influenced by current density, with higher densities causing aggregated growth. Flow rate considerably hinders dendrite growth, however, increase in flowrate to > 60 mL/min shows insignificant effect on the rate of dendrite growth. Rough surface generates strong electric field and fast diffusion on the tip leading to vigorous dendrite growth.[6]

11308720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11308720.value: 1. In the mixed electrolyte, the reaction kinetics of the vanadium species is compromised, and the underlying reason is not fully understood. Investigating the interaction mechanism of multiple redox couples and developing electrode/electrolyte engineering specifically for the mixed electrolyte is critical for performance enhancement. In addition, vanadium cross-over is a long-standing issue for the long-term cycling of flow batteries. Therefore, improving membrane selectivity is a necessity for the utilization of mixed electrolytes. 2. Although we tried to push the electrolyte utilization to 90% to show the potential of the system, such a high utilization rate induces a significant change in electrolyte composition affecting the system's stability. Thus, a comprehensive system engineering should be performed, in which the cell performance and stability should be evaluated against different current densities and SOC, and thus developing a more practical charge-discharge protocol.

11308720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11308720.value: Flow battery is a promising energy storage technology for facilitating renewable energy utilization, which stores the energy through the electrochemical reaction of active species in electrolytes. Increasing the concentration of the active species increases the energy density while hampering the power density due to high electrolyte viscosity and sluggish reaction kinetics. Thus, active species with multi-electron transfer reaction is favorable for both high energy and power densities due to its multiple charge stored at the same concentration. In the project, bismuth deposition/dissolution is investigated and pioneered as negative electrolyte for hybrid flow batteries owing to its three-electron reaction and the significantly increased solubility in methanesulfonic acid. A bismuth-based flow battery is demonstrated delivering a high volumetric capacity of 120 Ah L-1 and electrolyte utilization of >90% via adopting 3D graphite felt electrode and a 1.5 M bismuth electrolyte. Further, a mixed positive electrolyte containing cerium and vanadium species is utilized, which effectively increase the energy density of the full cell due to the increased charge stored in the mixed electrolyte. Moreover, a phase-field method is developed to study the morphological evolution at the solid-liquid interface and optimize operation parameters for hybrid flow batteries.

11500120.value: 社交媒體對中國職場數字化關係形成的影響

11500120.label: Project Objectives
11500120.value: The first objective is to create a comprehensive list of the different component concepts related to guanxi. This will draw on reviews of the literature already undertaken by members of the project team, as well as other published studies. We will also undertake qualitative interviews with employees in organizations in China in order to obtain corroboratory evidence for this list. In these interviews, we will also explore how the affordances of social media technology support different aspects of the guanxi formation process. The second objective is to undertake in-depth case studies into the digital guanxi formation processes developed by employees at a small number of firms that mandate the use of ESM applications. So far, three such firms have been identified: Fedex, Jacou and Weqia. In these case studies, we aim to explore how employees approach digital guanxi formation. We expect that while they are required to use ESM, they may also use PSM, other technologies, and face-to-face communication. The case studies will afford us the unique opportunity to examine when the various communication mediums are particularly appropriate or useful in facilitating the different phases of digital guanxi formation. The third objective is to develop a theoretically robust model that draws together the various component concepts into a nomological network. The model will capture and explain the interrelationships between digital guanxi (and its many sub-components) the different features available in social media technologies, and the affordances that exist for employees at the interstices between the two, as well as the outcomes of this process at individual, team and organizational levels.

11500120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500120.value: Organisational employees spend much of their working lives communicating with both proximate and remote colleagues. They rely on a wide variety of information systems to accomplish this work, with social media applications playing an increasingly prominent role in professional communication. Employees routinely need to connect with a large number of people and in order to enhance their communications, they often attempt to develop relationships online. Stronger relationships are often essential to the completion of work tasks. In the Chinese context, these relationships are referred to as guanxi. Although guanxi itself is well researched, there are a dozen or more sub-components that require careful examination. These include mianzi (face), ganqing (affection), renqing (empathy, favour), huibao (reciprocity), and hexie (harmony). Traditionally, guanxi was established through face-to-face communications that took place in private and were thus invisible to people outside the relationship. A few Information Systems scholars have explored digital guanxi, but these studies tend to focus on instrumental purposes, notably between buyers and sellers on e-commerce sites, with public social media (PSM) applications. They neglect the nuances of the enterprise social media (ESM)-based guanxi development process between employees and their interlocutors within organisations. Further, researchers have yet to explore the sociotechnical imbrications between guanxi (and its sub-components), the affordances of social media technologies, and employees’ desire to function effectively in the digitally-centric workplace. In this project, we propose to investigate the development of digital guanxi in the workplace. Our overarching research question is: How do organisational employees leverage the affordances of social media as they develop guanxi in the workplace? Our specific contextual focus is China. Although many ESM applications exist in China, we will focus on Alibaba’s Dingtalk and Tencent’s Enterprise Wechat. We will also examine Wechat’s PSM application, as this is extensively used across China and often used in combination with the ESM applications. From a thorough review of the literature, as well as qualitative interviews with organizational employees, we will compile a comprehensive set of concepts pertaining to digital guanxi and affordances of ESM. Next, we will undertake case studies in selected Chinese organisations in order to explore the full depth of the social media-based guanxi development process and its links to professional communication. Finally, from these multiple sources, we will develop a theoretical model that captures the many factors associated with digital guanxi development in the Chinese organizational context. 企業僱員在日常工作時都需要與身邊和異地同事進行頻繁的溝通交流。他們借用多種信息系統工具進行工作協同，而社交媒體應用程序在其中扮演著越發重要的角色。企業僱員通常需要與大量人員建立聯繫，為了提高溝通效率，線上交流方式日漸成為一種趨勢。一個高效穩固的聯繫對於完成一項多方參與的複雜工作起到關鍵性作用。在中文語境中，我們稱之為“關係”。儘管先前學術界對於 “關係”在已有大量的研究，但仍有許多細節值得更加深入的探索，其中包括面子，感情，人情，回報，以及和諧等因素。傳統上，關係是通過面對面交流而建立的，而且這種交流是私下進行的，因此對於關係之外的人是不可見的。一些信息系統領域的學者已經對數字關係進行了研究，但是這些文章局限於探索數字關係的實用性和工具性，特別是集中在電子商務網站上關於買賣雙方之間使用公共社交媒體應用程序（PSM）的情況。他們忽視了企業內部和企業間員工使用企業社交媒體（ESM）發展關係過程中的細微差別。此外, 學者尚未探索關係（及其影響因素）之間的社會技術聯繫，社交媒體技術的能供性，以及員工在數字化辦公時代下如何實現高效工作的願望。 在這個項目中，我們計劃研究在工作場所中如何建立數字關係。與之對應，我們的研究課題具體圍繞在：企業僱員如何利用社交媒體工具在工作場所中建立關係？我們的研究是基於中國背景而展開。儘管中國有很多ESM應用程序，但我們將重點關注于阿里巴巴的Dingtalk和騰訊的企業微信。我們還將研究微信的PSM應用程序，因為該應用程序在中國擁有數以萬計的用戶，並且經常與ESM應用程序結合使用。通過對文獻的全面回顧以及對企業僱員的定性訪談，我們將創造性地提出一系列與數字關係和ESM特性相關的概念。接下來，我們將在選定的中國企業進行案例研究，以全面深入地探究基於社交媒體的關係發展過程及其在工作協同中所扮演的重要角色。最後，通過整合多樣的數據來源，我們將建立一個理論模型，該模型包含在中國企業背景下發展數字關係所需要綜合考量的多種因素

We also examined the different ways in which social media technology support different aspects of the guanxi formation process. The second objective was completed. We completed case studies into several organisations in order to document digital guanxi formation. These organisations include IKEA, iSoftStone, and Jacou. The third objective has been completed. Based on the outcomes of the first two objectives, we have completed a theoretically robust model. We have developed the instrumentation for the model and have collected data from a 4th organisation (Fedex China) to validate the model.

11500120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500120.value: Social media applications are ubiquitous in today's society. In China, a particularly salient aspect of work communication is guanxi (pervasive reciprocal relationships between people). Traditionally these relationships were formed and maintained in a face-to-face context, but increasingly we see these activities online, in social media. In this study, we explore how organisational employees use both private and enterprise versions of social media applications to create and maintain these relationships, and then we model the impact of these relationships on (inter alia) their work peformance. We find a significant link and thus suggest that organisations should permit employees to use both their own private social media applications and the official corporate social media applications, as each has an important role to play in guanxi formation, and then work performance.

11500420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500420.value: This project will investigate a worker's attention allocation between job search and portfolio investment in a life-cycle search and matching model. On one hand, a working-age worker has new job offers arrive during the career, and the compensation of the new job may increase or decrease relative to the current job. Attention allocated to job search reduces the uncertainty in the new job match. On the other hand, the worker saves for future consumption because of labor income uncertainty and retirement. A risky asset pays a higher interest than the risk-free asset but carries a risk in the return. Attention allocated to portfolio investment reduces the uncertainty in the excess return of the risky asset. The worker has limited attention hence there is a tradeoff between job search and portfolio investment. If the worker pays more attention to the new job offer, he or she learns more about the quality of the new job match and makes a better decision on whether to accept or reject new job offers hence increases the total wage income over the career. However, the attention paid to learn the excess return of the risky asset is reduced, which increases the risk in the worker's portfolio investment. Hence the expected investment return decreases, which reduces the future consumption and savings to retirement. The project will first set up the life-cycle attention allocation problem between job search and portfolio investment of a worker in a search and matching model. Then the worker's optimal decisions on attention, job search, and portfolio investment over the career and after retirement in equilibrium will be solved by backward induction. After that, comparative statics will be studied and the model results will be simulated using the parameters calibrated from the data of Panel Study of Income Dynamics. The effects of the worker's risk aversion, the attention limit, the mean and variance of the new job quality, the risk-free interest rate, the average return and risk on the risky assets, the initial wealth endowment, and how the income after retirement depends on the labor income during the career on the worker's life-cycle attention allocation, job turnovers, and portfolio risk will be explore. Suggestive policies on pension or retirement plans and saving subsidies will also be investigated to improve the worker's life-time welfare given the challenge of ageing population in Hong Kong. 本項目將研究生命週期搜索和匹配模型中工作搜索和證券投資之間的注意力分配问题。一方面，员工在職業生涯中会遇到新的工作機會，而新工作的報酬可能多于或少於當前工作。分配給求職的注意力可以減少新工作匹配中的不確定性。另一方面，由於勞動收入的不確定性和退休，员工為未來的消費儲蓄。有風險的資產比無風險的資產支付更高的利息，但在收益中承擔風險。對證券投資的關注可以減少風險資產超額收益的不確定性。员工的注意力有限，因此在求職和證券投資之間需要權衡。如果员工更多地關注新工作機會，他或她會更多地了解新工作機會的質量，並在接受還是拒絕新工作機會上做出更好的決定，從而增加整個職業的總工資收入。但是，學習風險資產超額收益所花費的精力減少了，這增加了工人投資組合中的風險。因此，預期的投資收益減少，從而減少了未來的消費和退休儲蓄。該項目將首先在搜索和匹配模型中建立求職與员工投資組合之間的生命週期關注分配問題，再由後向前推算出员工在整個職業生涯中以及退休後在註意力分配，求职，以及證券投資方面的最佳決策，然後比較靜態关联，之后使用動態面板數據校準參數和對模型結果進行仿真。员工的風險規避，注意力極限，新工作質量的均值和方差，無風險利率，平均收益率和風險對風險資產，初始財富以及退休後收入的影響取決於職業生涯中的勞動收入，生命週期中的注意力分配，工作流失和投資組合風險。鑑於香港的人口老齡化，本項目還將研究有關退休計劃以及儲蓄補貼等建議性政策以改善员工的終生福利。

11500420.label: Realisation of objectives
11500420.value: The objectives proposed in the original application have been realized in our complete working paper entitled: "Information Rigidity and Elastic Attention: Evidence from Japan" and a companion paper entitled: "Optimal Attention Allocation and Heterogeneous Consumption Responses." Specifically, in the main paper we examined an investor's effort allocation problem between working and managing her investment portfolio over the life cycle. We solved the life-cycle model with attention allocation between job search and portfolio investment, and showed how this attention allocation channel affects job turnovers and portfolio risk. Furthermore, we also quantitatively examine the impact of risk aversion, attention limit, quality of new job matches, interest rate, risk of portfolio, wealth endowment on the optimal attention allocation, job turnovers, and portfolio investment during a worker’s career.

11500420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500420.value: We first assume that the investor is endowed with a fixed effort every period, which can be used to either work harder or learn more information about the financial market. If she exerts more effort into working, her current and future wages increase. But if she puts more effort into investing, she gets more precise signals of the returns of risky assets. We found that an investor's working effort is hump-shaped over her career: she works harder when young because her potential promotion for work is higher, but she exerts more effort into learning information about the financial market later on. Her risky asset investment reaches a peak near retirement. The results may also vary when the retirement plan changes. Using some results obtained in the main paper, the companion paper, "Optimal Attention Allocation and Heterogeneous Consumption Responses," also addresses the optimal attention problem between labor income risk and equity return risk. The paper is now under review at International Economic Review. Furthermore, two other papers generated from this project are now under 2nd round review at Journal of Economic Theory and Journal of Monetary Economics, respectively. (Please see Part C for the details.)

11500420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500420.value: Our study is related to the literature on optimal attention; see Sims (2003) and Sims (2010). We contribute to this literature by presenting a specific model with optimal attention allocation between two major risks in a typical household's life-cycle: labor market risk and stock market risk. These results can be combined with some new empirical evidence on households' heterogeneous consumption responses to shocks to labor income and equity returns, and help us better understand the consumption behavior. In the future, we will apply the results obtained in this project to generate quantitative consumption responses to different income shocks and then compare them with the empirical counterparts.

11501420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501420.value: 消費者對移動商務中數據洩露的反應

11501420.label: Project Objectives
11501420.value: This project seeks to investigate how consumers react to a data breach in m-Commerce business: whether consumers decrease their usage time for a breached mobile application or not and whether they switch to non-breached competitors after a breach. This project will further examine how consumer reaction varies with consumer characteristics (i.e., age, gender, loyalty, and online shopping behavior). This project will identify how a firm’s market power influences consumer reaction to the firm's breach. Based on the findings from the above investigations, this project aims to provide policy insights on effective security programs by identifying the market effect of data breaches on security in complex m-commerce environments.

11501420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501420.value: 作為一種創新的經商模式，移動或電子商務平台已成為企業與消費者進行有效交互的主要界面。公司和消費者數據的很大一部分已通過Internet傳輸。但是，這種高度連接的Internet業務格局遇到了越來越多的數據洩露。數據洩露已引起越來越多的媒體報導和公眾關注。但是，幾乎沒有經驗證據來描述消費者在移動或電子商務環境中如何實際應對數據洩露。只有少數安全經濟學研究人員指出，股市對數據洩露的反應似乎是短暫的，並且僅限於最嚴重的數據洩露。儘管公眾對數據洩露的擔憂已經廣泛傳播，但是消費者是否對破壞的公司採取了任何行動尚不明確。因此，本研究旨在確定消費者對數據洩露的反應（即，消費者對違規企業的使用時間以及他們對違規企業的競爭對手的轉換傾向）。對於這項調查，本研究計劃通過利用2016年7月在韓國主要在線平台參與者之一中發生的數據洩露（影響超過1000萬消費者）來採用準實驗設計。本研究建議使用個人級別的移動使用數據，比較大規模數據洩露前後消費者行為的變化。在準實驗環境中使用差異差異方法進行了初步測試。結果表明，在數據洩露之後，消費者減少了對洩露的移動應用程序的使用，並增加了其未違反競爭者的使用率。對於對違規公司具有高度消費者忠誠度的消費者，這種反應變得更加強烈。但是，一家受侵害的公司的強大市場力量限制了這種影響。這項研究進一步探討了消費者對違規行為的反應如何改變其多樣化的在線行為。例如，與在相當長的時間前拜訪該公司的消費者相比，經常在違約之前頻繁訪問該公司的消費者對違規的反應可能有所不同。了解消費者對違規行為的反應中的這些變化可以為程序提供重要的政策見解，這些程序可以有效地誘使移動或電子商務公司像對其他基於市場的品牌建設計劃那樣進行安全投資。

11501420.label: Realisation of objectives
11501420.value: First, our empirical analysis shows that consumers do decrease their usage time for a breached mobile application and tend to switch to non-breached competitors. The study highlights the significant negative impact of data breaches on user engagement and brand loyalty in the m-commerce sector. This finding underscores the critical need for mobile applications to prioritize data security to maintain user trust and retention. Second, although we analyzed survey data to understand variations in consumer reactions based on characteristics such as age, gender, loyalty, and online shopping behavior, it is challenging to perfectly identify consumers' intentions behind their reactions. One notable limitation is that the primary data breach under study occurred at Interpark in 2016, while our survey was conducted in 2022. The survey targeted randomized consumers, regardless of their direct experience with the Interpark breach. This temporal discrepancy has been critiqued by reviewers, who argue that it may affect the accuracy of our findings. To address this concern, we included a question asking respondents whether they used the Interpark mobile app during the breach period. However, this solution significantly reduced our sample size, as only a limited number of respondents met this criterion. Despite this limitation, our analysis provides valuable insights into the general trends and factors influencing consumer reactions to data breaches. Third, our findings suggest that firms with greater market power experience less severe consumer backlash following a data breach. Consumers of market-leading firms tend to exhibit more resilience, possibly due to limited alternatives and higher perceived switching costs. However, as noted earlier, the challenge in perfectly capturing consumer intent and the reduced sample size due to the Interpark-specific question limit the generalizability of our results. Nonetheless, these findings highlight the importance of robust security measures even for firms with strong market positions to prevent erosion of consumer trust over time. Finally, the comprehensive analysis provides actionable insights for policymakers and businesses. Effective security programs should focus on enhancing safeguard effectiveness and communicating these safeguards to consumers, especially in m-commerce. Policies should emphasize the importance of transparency, quick response to breaches, and the implementation of robust security measures to mitigate perceived threats. These steps can help maintain consumer trust and reduce the negative market effects of data breaches. Through these investigations, the project has met its objectives to a significant extent, offering a detailed understanding of consumer reactions to data breaches in m-commerce and providing valuable insights for improving security policies and practices. Despite the challenges and limitations encountered, the study’s findings contribute to the theoretical literature on security-related behaviors and offer practical recommendations for enhancing data security in m-commerce environments.

11501420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501420.value: This study offers the first empirical evidence of the impact of a data breach on mobile commerce (m-commerce) users by examining changes in their app usage patterns and their propensity to switch to competitors. First, this study demonstrated the vulnerability of m-commerce to customer attrition after security failures. A contrasting case is Liang and Telang (2020), who suggested that customers maintained their regular use of debit cards in stores after the 2014 Home Depot data breach, and the authors found no significant differences in the impact of the data breach on Home Depot stores facing different levels of competition. Given that the switching costs are relatively low for m-commerce compared to physical stores such as Home Depot, we find that consumers tend to reduce the usage of mobile apps after data breaches, especially when their market share is low. Furthermore, data breaches place a greater burden on the breached firm by causing losses of consumers to competitors. Not only is our observed negative reaction impact on focal firm in the short term, but it is also sustained for the longer-term, i.e., three months after the data breach. Second, Second, drawing upon the Technology Threat Avoidance Theory (TTAT), this study clarified and tested how different levels of perceived threat and avoidability in m-commerce, compared to e-commerce, influence negative reactions to data breaches. Our survey analysis elaborates on the differential perceptions and reactions to data breaches between m-commerce and e-commerce consumers. Previous studies have suggested that while the TTAT model is generally valid, the roles of predictors in determining avoidance behavior may depend on the context of security failures. In this regard, our work is among the first to validate the TTAT model for data breaches in both e-commerce and m-commerce contexts. We find that for perceived avoidability, safeguard effectiveness plays a critical role in leading to avoidance behavior, compared to safeguard cost and self-efficacy, whereas perceived threats particularly influence avoidance behavior among m-commerce consumers. Taken together, our mixed-method approach, combining a field study based on a natural experiment and survey analysis, provides a comprehensive picture of how consumers react to data breaches in m-commerce.

11501420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11501420.value: First, our data were limited to individuals who had downloaded a mobile analytics app, which may bias our sample towards users with higher self-control. To enhance the generalizability of our results, future empirical analyses should extend to other m-commerce contexts and settings. Investigating data breaches across various m-commerce platforms and industries would provide a more comprehensive understanding of consumer reactions. Second, while our mobile usage data offer valuable insights into consumer behavior in response to data breaches, they do not capture specific actions within the m-commerce app, such as which items were purchased or browsed. Future studies should collect granular-level data on user behavior within apps to explore how different activities impact consumer perceptions and reactions to data breaches. In conclusion, these proposed developments aim to provide more generalizable and nuanced insights into consumer reactions to data breaches, contributing to the development of more effective security policies and practices in the m-commerce sector.

11501420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501420.value: With the rise of smartphones and mobile devices, more people are using mobile apps for shopping. However, this shift has also brought concerns about the security and privacy of these apps. Despite the rapid growth of mobile commerce (m-commerce), there hasn't been much research on how consumers react to data breaches in these apps. This study investigates how a major data breach at a popular online retailer affects users' behavior. By analyzing individual-level mobile usage data, we look at how much time people spend on the affected app and whether they switch to apps from competitors that weren't breached. Our findings show that after a data breach, users not only reduce their usage of the compromised app but also increase their usage of competitors' apps. However, this switching behavior is less noticeable among users who are very loyal to the breached app. Loyal customers tend to stick with the app despite the breach, and apps with a larger market share see less drop-off in user numbers. These results offer important insights for regulators and business managers about the importance of security and privacy in m-commerce, highlighting the need for robust measures to protect user data and maintain customer trust.

11501520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501520.value: In recent years, online peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform, a new channel of financing through which lenders are matched with borrowers, has become increasingly prevalent. Because of the low overhead and efficient electronic distribution of funds, P2P lending can lead to higher returns for both borrowers and lenders. However, there could also be significant risks associated with such practice involving borrower defaulting, fraud, platform insolvency and bankruptcy. According to statistics from wdzj.com, the number of problematic P2P platforms totalled 2,856 in August 2019. Ezubao, a P2P lending platform for example, allegedly attracted about 50 billion yuan ($7.6 billion) in funds from 900,000 investors and was shut down in 2016 due to fraudulent activities. These problematic P2P platforms, if undetected, could cause immeasurable damage to the investor confidence and the overall economy. In this research, we aim to examine the risks associated with P2P lending at a macro level. Specifically, we seek to (1) identify factors that help predict the failure and bankruptcy risk of a P2P lending platform, (2) evaluate how does the risk of one P2P lending platform propagate to other platforms, and (3) analyse how the government regulatory policy influence the development of the P2P financial industry. In order to answer the above questions, we propose a novel analytic framework to extract structural characteristics from the P2P network, which will be developed using both external news information and internal registry associations. We will then train machine learning algorithms to predict the probability of platform bankruptcy using data from multiple sources. We will further use probability-generating function to analyse the risk contagion mechanism of platform bankruptcy based on the P2P network. Finally, we will conduct rigorous empirical analysis to study the effect of three influential Chinese policy events on the risk-taking activity (operational risk, credit risk, and users’ perceived risk) of the P2P lending platforms. Findings from this research project will have significant theoretical as well as practical implications. From a theoretical perspective, we believe that an effective and efficient algorithm to evaluate risk will mitigate the issue of adverse selection commonly observed in online marketplaces due to information asymmetry. From a practical perspective, this study can help government regulators and investors to achieve their investment objectives goals while protecting the public interest and the overall health of the financial industry. We also expect that this project will provide additional insights for the development of financial technology industry in Hong Kong. 近年來，一種新的融資渠道——P2P借貸平台日益流行起來。貸款者與借款者可以通過P2P借貸平台直接匹配來進行借貸交易。而且，較低的間接費用和高效的資金分配使其能為借貸雙方都帶來更高的回報。然而，通過P2P平台進行借貸交易可能存在重大風險，例如借款人違約、欺詐、平台資不抵債和破產等。據網貸之家統計，直到2019年8月問題P2P平台總數為2856家。例如，E租寶從90萬投資者吸引了約500億人民幣 (即76億美元)的資金，並於2016年因欺詐行為而被關閉。如果這些問題P2P平台未被及時發現，將會對投資者的信心和整體經濟造成不可估量的損害。 在本研究中，我們的目的是在宏觀層面上研究與P2P借貸相關的風險。具體來說，我們致力於：（1）識別出有助於預測平台破產的重要風險因素；(2)評估一個平台的風險如何傳播到其他平台；(3)分析政府監管政策對P2P金融行業發展的影響。為解決上述問題，我們首先提出了一個新的分析框架來提取P2P網絡的結構特徵。其次，我們利用多來源數據訓練機器學習算法來提高預測平台破產的概率。我們將進一步利用概率生成函數來分析P2P平台破產的風險傳染機制。最後，我們將通過實證分析來研究三個重要監管政策事件對P2P借貸平颱風險承擔行為(操作風險、信用風險和用戶感知風險)的影響。 本研究的結果將具有重大的理論和實際意義。從理論角度來看，我們相信有效的風險評估算法可以緩解線上市場由於信息不對稱而出現的逆向選擇問題。從實踐的角度來看，本研究可以幫助政府監管機構和投資者實現他們的投資目標，同時保護公眾利益和金融業的整體健康。該項研究為香港金融科技業的發展提供更多有意義的見解。

11501520.label: Realisation of objectives
11501520.value: Our research background highlights the significant risks associated with P2P platforms. These platforms in China experienced rapid growth from 2013 to 2017, with a peak transaction volume of CNY 2.8 trillion in 2017(Huang, 2022). This growth in P2P platforms has led to heightened concerns about the risks involved. In 2018, due to a combination of global factors like the international environment and macroeconomic instability, along with domestic deleveraging efforts, P2P platforms began to encountered issues, and 848 P2P platforms were exposed to problems throughout the year according to data online(Sina Tech, 2020).Although related government departments issued policies to governance P2P platforms, the humpty’s fall of P2P lending market finally came. According to the data of Online Loan Home, until June 2019, only 844 of the 6,618 P2P online lending platforms were in normal operation, and nearly 90% of the P2P online lending platforms withdrew or transformed. In 2019, the policy of "retreating as much as possible, closing as much as possible" represented that the regulatory authorities gave up on rectification and gave an ultimatum to P2P platforms. Finally on November 27, 2020, all P2P platforms were cleared. China's P2P lending market ultimately have no surviving platform any more. In this case, on one hand, we are unable to collect data related to P2P platforms, including news data and platform registration data. Without this data, we cannot conduct data-driven text analysis or extract various features from the data (static features, dynamic features, network features). On the other hand, we cannot establish a prediction model for P2P default, as almost all P2P platforms have already gone bankrupt. Therefore, we are unable to continue conduct research on P2P platforms any more, which leading to a discontinue of the project objectives which were set in the beginning of our research. So we turn to explore other Fintech products which was increasingly coming into focus at that time, that is the cryptocurrency. Cryptocurrency is a digital currency designed on the basis of blockchain technology to operate through a computer network and does not rely on any central authority such as government or bank to maintain. Cryptocurrency has brought new business models, technological innovations and market opportunities to various digital platforms. Some platforms are exploring decentralized way to circulate and generate cryptocurrencies through blockchain-based infrastructure. This process virtualizes important operations as a tool for incentives and governance, thus introducing new financing and management mechanisms. But at the same time, while cryptocurrencies bring new opportunities, new challenges and risks exist as well. Factors such as technological developments, regulatory changes, and speculative behavior can lead to volatility in the cryptocurrency market, causing prices to rise or fall significantly in a short period of time, which brings a high risk to users. We seek to study the impact of the risk of price volatility on user behavior. (1)To investigate how the token price volatility affects user behavior, including users’ token selection and contribution, in a tokenized platform from the micro and macro perspectives This research work is published on one top Information Systems Journal—Journal of Management Information Systems. Taking steemit, a blockchain-based social community, as an example, we conduct an empirical study on the impact of token price volatility on user contributions in tokenized digital platforms and explore underlying mechanisms. We develop our hypothesis through decision-making theory and motivation crowding theory, and propose direct impact of token price volatility on the quantity and quality of user contribution and indirect pathway mediated by user preference towards transactional and governance tokens during periods of volatility shocks. Then we construct variables to test our hypotheses using regression model. To corroborate our empirical results, a series of robustness tests were also conducted. Firstly, we use two-way fixed-effect model to examine the relationship between relative volatility and user contributions and obtained consistent result. Secondly, we choose two instrument variables to address endogeneity concerns. Thirdly, we test with the “cryptocurrency” topic and consistent results were obtained as well. Finally, we conduct some post hoc analysis, including estimation of dynamic effects, exploring trade-off between post quantity and quality, moderation effect of price trend and review of the platform-level user participation in different development stages. In addition to exploring the risks-related topics of new fintech product, we also conduct research on the impact of risks on financial markets and specific stakeholders from the perspective of macro and micro separately. (2)To investigate the impact of risk of emergencies on stock markets from the perspective of spillover effect and how the impact varies. First, for a panel dataset of stock market indices for 40 countries or regions, we use Granger causality tests and network analysis to examine spillover effects between the markets, showing the intercorrelation between any paired markets. We then use the rolling window to build a series of interconnected networks and explore the dynamics of the network structure based on three global interconnectivity metrics, namely concentration, transitivity, and density. Second, we construct econometric models to examine how the impact of risk of emergencies on the stock markets has changed by considering the interconnected structure, which is measured by degree, proximity, and average nearest neighbour degree(ANND), government response stringency index (GRSI), and other characteristics of country-level. (3)To explore how the risk of consumers’ loss fairness concerns impact a two-period partial refund policy in advance selling and how companies respond to the impact. The study is conducted by analytical modelling. First, a mathematical model including two stages after advanced selling is established, in which firms sell at different prices and refund policies, and consumers decide whether to buy and return product. Then, two models, namely NLFC and CLFC, are established to analyze consumer behavior. NLFC is used to analyze consumers' purchasing decisions when they are only concerned about economic gains. CLFC is used to analyze consumers' purchase decisions when they are concerned about loss fairness, and a loss fairness parameter α is introduced to measure consumers' sensitivity to loss fairness. Next, we analyze the optimal refund policy of firms under the above two models and compare the firm’s profits under different refund policies and the impact of loss fairness concerns. In order to alleviate consumers' concerns about the fairness loss, we also propose mechanisms for multiple refund stages and analyze their impact on consumer and firm benefits. (4)To extract useful information from large collections of documents with topic modelling technique. In our Journal of Management Information Systems paper, we use topic modelling technique to identify topic-level innovation, we also apply this method in other text documents. A comparative study of topic modelling of full-text papers and corresponding abstracts respectively is conducted to assess the impact of different types of documents used as input for topic modelling. In particular, we use a large number of research literature as a case study and propose a research framework, which contains three main steps, namely pre-processing, topic modelling and topic analysis. LDA method is used for topic modelling. Then we conduct topic analysis, including research trend analysis and topic similarity analysis and topic visualization to illustrate the research themes, research trends, and topic similarities of research.
