11501520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501520.value: Marjor findings: During the ongoing of our project period, we experienced risk of collapse of P2P platforms in China. The focus of research has to be shifted to another Fintech product, namely cryptocurrency, to study the impact of token price volatility on the contribution of tokenized digital platform users, which also plays a crucial role in the survival of such platform. Our research outcome shows that token price volatility contributes to the network of platform in the short term but in the long run it hurts the creativity of users which may lead to the decay of platforms. In addition, we discussed some other financial risk related topics. From the perspective of financial market and industry, we find strong evidence of spillover effects between stock markets the risk of emergencies arises, indicating the interconnectedness of the industry. The differences of interconnectedness structure significantly and robustly affects stock returns in the markets. Higher interconnectedness between countries positively impacts stock returns, suggesting that a strong network can help diversify risks and stabilize markets. From the perspective of stakeholders in industry, we find that the risk of customers' fair loss concerns would have a negative impact on the firms, so we proposed a mechanism that provides multiple refund stages to effectively mitigate this risk. 11501520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11501520.value: This project encountered significant limitations due to the objective reasons of collapse of the P2P lending platform, which was the single data source of our initial research design. In response to this setback, the focus of our current research redirected towards another innovative fintech product—cryptocurrency. We explore the impact of tokenized price volatility on users’ contribution in a blockchain based platform called Steemit. Currently we just focus on a single platform with specific rules for managing token rewards. Future research could explore the unique reward mechanisms on other tokenization platforms and conduct some comparative analysis. For the future discussion on risks about financial market and stakeholders, we can try to find more factors that impact market returns that are not captured, as well as compare the differences between the impacts on general market and specific industry market. Regarding the firms and customers who have fairness loss concerns in specific market, the heterogeneity of consumers can be considered and dynamic pricing is also a direction worth considering, as market demand is changing constantly. In addition, we could also try more text analysis methods to have deeper understanding of the text data to enrich our research in the future.

11501520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501520.value: This research mainly focus on investigating the impact of the token price volatility on user contribution in a tokenized digital platform, which is of vital importance for the survival of such platforms. Stockholders could be inspired by our research to design a proper incentive scheme, for example, adjust the tokens’ s supply to prevent extreme price volatility, and maintain relatively stable price volatility to retain the quality of user posts, so as to keep the healthy development of the platforms. This research is also significant in the literature of blockchain economics and cryptocurrencies. We find that token prices affect the operation of the underlying digital platform, which could inspire more research on combining crypto markets and blockchain platforms with these two token circulation contexts when studying blockchain economics. In addition, our research contributes to the decentralized governance. The findings we obtained from Steemit could be generalized to other decentralized autonomous organization. Other studies in the project are also valuable. We discussed the risks of financial markets, industries and related stakeholders from macro to micro perspectives, and corresponding countermeasures are proposed, which is of great significance to the stability of development.

11501820.label: Project Objectives
11501820.value: To determine the initial procurement decision of a new, short-life-cycle product, whose attributes share similarities with those of historical products in varying degrees. Machine learning methods taking into consideration attribute information will be adopted, under the framework of profit maximization and value-at-risk (VaR) constraint. To establish asymptotic optimality to guarantee that the decisions implemented will have performance reaching the best possible, a critical limiting property for a decision maker. To address the following two research questions: 1) As compared with the risk-neutral setting, how are the decision quantities affected by the profit-risk-averse framework as shown in the demand distribution-based models? That is, is the stock of a risk-averse newsvendor less than that of a risk-neutral newsvendor? 2) How does risk aversion (reflected by the VaR threshold values) affect the stocking (order quantity) decision? That is, is the stock of a more-risk-averse newsvendor less than that of a less-risk-averse newsvendor? To extend Objective 1 for allowing two procurement decisions, where the first decision occurs before the launch of the new product; i.e., an initial order is placed before any demand has been observed; and the second is made at a given point in time after some demand has been observed.

11501820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501820.value: Fashion and seasonal products, which are characterized by short selling seasons, highly uncertain demand, and often long lead times, have brought a great challenge for retailers trying to match supply with demand. As a result, retailers often suffer from significant losses in profit due to either lost sales from stockouts or clearances of excess inventory at the end of the selling season. The situation for new, seasonal products is even worse, as new products do not have historical demand/sales data. However, a firm may have been selling similar products in the past and keeps a record of them. In addition to demand/sales figures, the data record may contain rich information about the attributes (features) of the products, such as retail price, colour, item type (e.g., shirt, pant), fabric, design style (e.g., casual, sporty), store type, and season, in the case of fashion cloths. Such attributes are called covariate information to demand. In this project we attempt to link a new product, by using covariate information, to "similar" products that were sold historically. Weights are used to measure similarities between the new product and historical products, and the values of those weights are estimated by employing machine learning methods such as k-nearest neighbours, classification and regression tree, and random forests, to the data. Then, the pair of the realized demand of a similar historical product and its associated weight, together with those from other similar products, are utilised to approximate the expected profit and other quantities which take on the (conditional) demand distribution. Two basic model settings are considered. The first is the single-period/newsvendor type, and the second is the two-period type, which we believe to be most representative of realistic situations for many short-life-cycle products. As to the objective criterion, the firm determines the order quantities with a chance constraint that requires meeting a profit target at a chosen confidence level, while maximizing expected profit. The chance constraint is also called a value-at-risk (VaR) constraint, reflecting the fact that managers seek to meet profit targets because missing a target affects both the stock price and bonuses. The approximated formulation using weights can be transformed into a mixed integer programming, for which an efficient algorithm will be developed. We will prove the proposed approximation to be asymptotically optimal even with the sample-dependent approximation for the VaR constraint. We will also use real-world data to verify our models and methods. 時尚和季節性產品的特點是銷售季節短，需求高度不確定，交貨期通常較長，這給試圖使供需匹配的零售商帶來了很大的挑戰。結果，零售商通常會因庫存不足而失去銷售或在銷售旺季結束時清除過剩的庫存而蒙受重大的利潤損失。新的季節性產品的情況甚至更糟，因為新產品沒有歷史需求/銷售數據。但是，公司過去可能一直在銷售類似產品，並保留它們的數據記錄。除了需求/銷售數字之外，數據記錄還可能包含有關產品屬性（特徵）的豐富信息，例如時尚衣服裝， 零售價格，顏色，物品類型（例如襯衫，褲子），織物，設計風格（例如休閒裝，運動裝），商店類型和季節。這些屬性稱為需求協變量信息。在這個項目中，我們嘗試使用協變量信息將新產品連接到歷史上已售出的“類似”產品。權重用於衡量新產品和歷史產品之間的相似性，而這些歷史產品的權重值是通過使用機器學習方法（例如k最近鄰，分類和回歸樹，以及隨機森林）從數據中估算得出的。然後，每支相似歷史產品的已實現需求及其權重， 聯同其他類似產品的已實現需求及其權重， 用於近似期望利潤和其他數量 （它們理論上是可以通過條件概類計算出來的）。 考慮了兩個基本模型設置。第一種是單週期/報童類型，第二種是雙週期類型。我們認為這對於許多短生命週期產品來說是最具代表性的。關於問題的目標指標，公司確定訂單數量時要考慮一個機會限制，該機會限制要求在選定的置信度下達到既定的利潤目標，同時使預期利潤最大化。機會約束也稱為風險價值（VaR）約束，體現了經理尋求實現利潤目標的現象， 因為錯失目標會影響股價和經理的獎金。使用權重的近似目標函數可以轉換為混合整數規劃，為此將開發一種有效的算法。我們將證明所提出的近似值即使在VaR約束的依賴於樣本的近似值下也是漸近最優的。我們還將使用實際數據來驗證我們的模型和方法。

11501820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501820.value: Major outcome: 1. Published one paper "Data-driven Newsvendor Problems Regularized by a Profit Risk Constraint." Lin, Shaochong; Chen, Youhua (Frank); Li, Yanzhi, and Max Shen. In: Production and Operations Management, Vol. 31, No. 4, 04.2022, p. 1630-1644. 2. One working paper "Dynamic Inventory Control with Covariates: Risk Constraints, Regularization, and Folding-horizon Plan." Lin, Shaochong; Chen, Youhua (Frank); Li, Yanzhi, and Max Shen. Reject and Resubmission at Oper. Research. 3. Graduated one PhD, who is currently Research Assistant Prof. In Paper 1, we use machine learning methods to weight the similarity between the new product and the previous ones based on covariates. The sample-dependent weights are then embedded to approximate the expected profit and the profit risk constraint. We show that the data-driven risk-averse newsvendor solution entails a closed-form quantile structure and can be efficiently computed. Finally, we prove that this data-driven solution is asymptotically optimal. Experiments based on actual and synthetic data demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. We observe that under data-driven decision-making, the average realized profit may benefit from a stronger risk aversion, contrary to that in the theoretical risk-averse newsvendor model. In fact, even a risk-neutral newsvendor can benefit from incorporating a risk constraint under data-driven decision-making. This situation is due to the value-at-risk constraint that effectively plays a regularizing role (via reducing the variance of order quantities) in mitigating data-driven decision-making issues, such as sampling error and model misspecification. In Paper 2, we develop a data-driven approach to dynamic inventory planning for new products. Specifically, we employ non-parametric machine learning methods to model the uncertain future demand and incorporate the newly available demand information in a folding-horizon manner. To alleviate the issues of sampling errors and model misspecification commonly seen in data-driven decision-making, we introduce profit-risk constraints to regularize the prescription of order quantities. The model with profit-risk constraints and information update brings computational and analytical challenges, e.g., time inconsistency issues. To analyze the performance of the proposed approach and address the challenge of time inconsistency, we develop a time-consistent folding-horizon model, against which we benchmark the original, profit risk-constrained model with folding-horizon planning. We can establish the asymptotic optimality of the original model concerning the sample size, i.e., the number of similar products. Extensive numerical experiments with real and synthetic data demonstrate consistently superior performance than the existing approaches in the literature.

11501820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501820.value: The proposal was motivated by an industrial project in an online retailer that regularly launched new, short-life-cycle products. We consider and analyze a data-driven approach to determine the optimal order quantities before the focal firm launches a new product. Although lacking historical sales data, a new product typically shares many attributes with past products sold before. Weights are employed to measure the relative similarities between the new product and historical ones, and machine learning methods are used to estimate the weights. The resulting weights are then embedded into an estimated formulation to approximate the value in the profit.t function. It is shown that using a constraint to limit a commonly used financial risk could result in higher realized profits than the model without such consideration. This finding is important as it can benefit firms when applying machine learning to procurement decision-making.

11502020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502020.value: High-dimensional factor models are powerful tools to analyze the common driving force of a large number of variables in economics and finance. These models are usually estimated under the assumption that the parameters in the model are stable over time. This assumption is likely to be violated in practice. We are interested in the setup where the factor loading coefficients change at a certain point of time, which is the so called structural break. Once practitioners know the existence of a break in the model, the next question of interest is to find the date of the break. Some methods have been developed to estimate the break point, but most of them cannot characterize the estimation uncertainty of the estimator in finite samples. In contrast, confidence intervals provide interval estimates instead of point estimates, so they account for the estimation uncertainty in finite samples. This project is interested in how to construct valid confidence intervals, which contain the true break point at a pre-specified probability level. The computation of confidence intervals is usually based on the limiting distribution of the estimator. To the best of our knowledge, our previous work (Bai, Han and Shi, 2019, BHS hereafter, accepted at Journal of Econometrics) is the only study that considers the limiting distribution of the break point estimator in factor models. BHS show that the distribution depends on the data generating process of the unobserved factors. Hence, it is practically difficult to directly apply the result of BHS to construct confidence intervals. Moreover, BHS only considered factor models with long time span. Their theory cannot be applied when the time span is short. This project plans to extend the theory of BHS in several aspects. First, we will develop theoretically valid and practically feasible methods to construct confidence intervals for the estimated break point. These methods are based on the bootstrap and simulation techniques. The distribution of the estimated break point based on the resampled data resembles the distribution of the estimator based on the original data. Preliminary simulation experiments show that these methods are promising. We will develop a theory for these methods. Second, we will develop a method to estimate break points in factor models with short time span to complement the BHS theory. The new method allows practitioners to detect the break soon after the break date so that forecasts and policies can be promptly updated and adjusted. 高維因子模型是分析經濟和金融中大量變量共同驅動力的有力工具。這些模型通常是在參數隨時間穩定的假設下進行估算。在實踐中可能會違反此假設。我們對因子加載係數在某個時間點發生變化(也就是所謂的結構性變化)的設置感興趣。一旦從業者知道模型存在斷點，下一個感興趣的問題就是找到變化的日期。目前已經開發出一些方法估計斷點，但是其中大多數無法刻畫有限樣本中估計量的不確定性。相反，置信區間能提供區間估計而不是點估計，因此它們考慮到了有限樣本中估計的不確定性。該項目致力於如何構造有效的置信區間，它以預先確定的概率水平包含真實斷點。 置信區間的計算通常基於估計量的極限分佈。據我們所知，我們之前的工作（Bai，Han和Shi，2019年，BHS，在計量經濟學雜誌上接受）是唯一考慮在因子模型中斷點估計量極限分佈的研究。 BHS顯示分佈取決於數據生成過程中不可觀測的因素。因此，它實際上很難直接應用BHS的結果來建立置信區間。此外，BHS僅考慮了具有較長時間跨度的因子模型。他們的理論時間間隔短時無法應用。

11502020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502020.value: Structural changes in factor models have received significant attention in recent studies. While several consistent estimators have been proposed, the inferential theory for the estimated break point remains inadequately developed. To the best of our knowledge, the study by Bai, Han and Shi (2020, BHS hereafter) is the only one that addresses the asymptotic distribution of the break point estimator in factor models. They demonstrate that the estimated break point possesses a nondegenerate asymptotic distribution when the magnitude of the break in each factor loading coefficient is of the order 1/sqrt(N). However, this asymptotic distribution relies on the data generating process of the unobserved factors and error terms, making it challenging to apply for statistical inference due to the involvement of unknown parameters. To bridge this gap in the literature, this paper proposes a bootstrap method for constructing confidence intervals for the BHS break point estimator. Unlike regressions with observed regressors, direct resampling using the factor estimators is not feasible because pre- and post-break factor estimators undergo different rotations even under the null hypothesis of no break. To address this issue, we propose rotating the post-break factor loadings by minimizing the L2 distance between the estimated pre- and post-break factor loading matrices. This rotation is then applied to adjust the post-break factor estimators, ensuring that the pre- and post-break factor estimators undergo the same rotation under the null hypothesis. We introduce a block bootstrap procedure using the adjusted factor estimators. We also propose two approaches to mimic the random walk components in the asymptotic distribution of the estimator: one based on simulation from the estimated distribution, and the other based on a resampling procedure employing the residuals. Our theoretical findings show that the proposed bootstrap method produces asymptotically valid confidence intervals. Simulation results indicate that our method yields confidence intervals with good coverage rates.

11502020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502020.value: Our current result only covers the case of a single break in factor models. The least squares estimator can also be applied to estimate multiple break points in factor models. Thus, one possible future extension is to generalize our bootstrap method to construct confidence intervals for multiple breaks. Another potential extension is to develop a bootstrap method for the quasi-maximum likelihood break point estimator in factor models.

11502020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502020.value: Recent studies have paid a lot of attention to structural changes in factor models. While researchers have proposed several methods to consistently estimate the break point, developing statistical inference (e.g., confidence intervals) for the estimated break point has been a challenge. The key issue is that the factors are unobserved, so the distributions needed for constructing confidence intervals involve unknown parameters from the data generating process. This paper aims to fill this gap by proposing a bootstrap method to obtain valid confidence intervals for the break point estimator. The main difficulty is that the estimated factors before and after the break are rotated differently, even if there is no true break. To overcome this, the authors first re-rotate the post-break factor loadings to align with the pre-break rotation. They then introduce a block bootstrap procedure using these re-rotated factors. Two approaches are suggested to mimic the random walk behavior seen in the break point estimator's asymptotic distribution. Theoretical results show the proposed bootstrap yields asymptotically valid confidence intervals. Simulation studies confirm the bootstrap intervals have good coverage rates in finite samples.

11502320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502320.value: 商品規劃決定售賣的商品組合，是對於零售商最重要的決策之一。傳統的商品規劃方法首先預測商品的需求然後基於此做出商品選擇。這一方法有幾方面的缺點。首先，歷史數據可能有限，導致商品需求預測不夠準確；如果是全新商品，缺乏歷史數據可用。其次，需求預測都是針對單品，商品之間的相互影響被忽略。最後，先預測再優化的兩步走策略忽略了探索-利用的權衡，導致次優的決策。 在本項目裡，基於我們在阿里巴巴公司的諮詢經驗，我們考慮一個電商環境下的動態商品規劃。對於消費者偏好選擇不做假設的前提下，我們提出一個“邊學邊做”的動態商品規劃框架。框架分為兩步。第一步，我們維護一個有效商品組合的集合，把其中的每一個商品組合當作一個臂。在這個基礎上實施一個訂製化的多臂老虎機算法，最大化我們的收益。第二步致力於發現一個新的、收益更好的商品組合。我們採用MaxMin的優化框架來處理當前信息不完美的問題。 為了在實踐中的應用，我們選用基於消費者偏好排序的選擇模型，它允許我們能捕捉到消費者在商品之間的替代行為。考慮到這個模型導致的複雜度，本項目的其中一個重點是開放高效的算法來解決MaxMin模型的優化問題。我們會與業界緊密合作，不但保證科研成果的嚴謹性和前瞻性，也會確保項目產出能對實踐產生良好的經濟效益。

11502320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502320.value: Major findings: 1. We have developed a data-driven approach to robust assortment planning. Based on historical sales data, we build an integrated optimization model aimed to estimate customer preferences and yield the optimal assortment simultaneously. Compared to two-stage estimate-then-optimize approaches, our integrated model results in high-quality assortments that are robust to sampling error (i.e., sales data uncertainty). An efficient algorithm is developed to solve the optimization model. The algorithm greatly expands the applicability of the ranking-based choice model. We illustrate both theoretically and numerically the robustness of our approach in terms of finding optimal or nearly optimal assortments. We have implemented our approach at Tmall Supermarket. An A/B test over a 20-day period shows that our approach achieves superior performance. Compared to the existing deep learning-based method, our approach has improved the user conversion rate by 7.4% and user value by 16.9% on average and thus led to a significant gain in the firm's revenue. Please refer to the paper titled "Data-driven Robust Assortment Planning" 2. We expand the work on assortment planning to joint assortment and inventory control. We give an approximation framework for the joint assortment planning and inventory management problem and derive a constant-factor guarantee for a broad class of choice models, including the Markov chain choice model. Our algorithm starts from a fluid approximation to identify a profitable assortment and uses rounding and greedy heuristic methods to decide the inventory level of the products restricted to the profitable assortment. Our approach outperforms the existing methods both theoretically and experimentally. 3. Motivated by the increasing concern over personalized assortment recommendations, we study a dynamic assortment planning problem where a firm aims to maximize profit by offering personalized assortments to users over a planning horizon of T periods. We consider inventory constraints, under which the firm must stop sales when resources are depleted, and differential privacy guarantees, under which adversaries are less likely, based on a privacy parameter, to infer the contextual information of customers. In particular, we consider two types of privacy concepts, central differential privacy (CDP) and local differential privacy (LDP). We develop online learning algorithms that respect inventory requirements as well as privacy guarantees and prove that the algorithms exhibit sub-linear regret bounds. The project has resulted in three research papers, all under review/revision for or targeting high-quality journals. One PhD student has graduated with part of his thesis works on the project's topic and another PhD student is in her fourth year and expected to graduate next year.

11502320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502320.value: Our line of work can be further generalized to consider the fairness and diversity concerns, which receive increasing attention from the research community.

11502320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502320.value: The research team has developed a robust, data-driven approach to assortment planning. By integrating customer preference estimation and assortment optimization, their model produces high-quality assortments that are resilient to uncertainty in sales data. An efficient algorithm was created to solve the optimization problem, expanding the applicability of ranking-based choice models. Through A/B testing at Tmall Supermarket, their approach demonstrated superior performance, improving user conversion rate by 7.4% and user value by 16.9% compared to a deep learning-based method. The team has also extended their work to the joint problem of assortment planning and inventory control. Their approximation framework provides constant-factor performance guarantees for a broad class of choice models. The algorithm starts with a fluid approximation to identify a profitable assortment, then uses rounding and greedy heuristics to set inventory levels. Recognizing the importance of personalized assortments, the researchers have also studied a dynamic assortment planning problem under inventory constraints and differential privacy guarantees. They have developed online learning algorithms that respect both inventory requirements and privacy, with sub-linear regret bounds. Overall, this multifaceted research project has made significant theoretical and practical advancements in assortment optimization, with several high-quality publications and student training outcomes.

11502520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502520.value: 在资产定价文献中对罕见灾害风险或尾部风险的研究可以追溯到Rahtz（1988），Kahneman等（1990）和Barro（2006）。大量文献记载，极端事件可能会解释一些经验难题，例如股票风险溢价和低利率。最近发生的全球金融危机的经历重新吸引了研究人员的注意力去准确评估尾部风险及其对股票或期权收益的可预测性。通常投资者承担极端事件风险需要额外的正溢价。 尽管在股票市场上得到广泛认可，但有关公司债券市场尾部风险定价的研究很少。Chava等（2014）发现债券发行收益率与金融机构的尾部风险呈正相关，但仅确定每个发行人的尾部风险。Li 和 Song（2014）引入了基于利率互换的尾部风险度量。Bai等（2019）通过汇总单个债券的特质风险来考虑下行风险因素，这需要债券交易的流动性比较好。在此项目中，我们旨在找到适当的尾部风险度量，并在公司债券市场的背景下研究系统性尾部风险的定价模式。 特别是，我们计划直接利用债券收益率提出两种尾部风险度量。一种是通过遵循Kelly 和 Jiang（2014）的观点来强调公司债券投资者的风险意识，他们汇总了所有每月债券收益以捕捉尾部行为。另一种则从动态统计评估的角度，类似于Acemoglu等（2017）描述偏离标准正态分布的左尾行为。 有了这两个度量，我们就可以全面解决债券收益率横截面中尾部风险的可预测性。我们推测，对过去尾部风险更敏感的债券会表现出更高的预期横截面回报，因为投资者需要承担极端不确定性的赔偿。将采用标准的资产定价方法。通过进行投资组合分析（按尾部风险beta进行单变量排序，对固定收益市场和债券特征的有据可查的定价效应进行双变量/三变量排序控制），以及采用规范的Fama和MacBeth（1973）截面回归，我们将努力解释公司债券收益中是否计及尾部风险定价的程度以及程度。 我们的项目是有理论贡献的。因为我们是第一个通过考虑公司债券交易的独特属性（例如，流动性的稀缺性和由机构投资者主导）来提出适用于公司债券数据的系统化尾部风险度量方法。与股东不同，债券持有人更容易遭受尾部风险的下行风险，而且他们的上行现金流量收益也受到限制（Hong和Sraer，2013）。我们关于以信用风险为条件的尾部风险如何影响横断面债券收益的发现，为债券投资者在制定对冲策略和投资组合配置时提供了重要的启示。此外，我们的研究通过阐明公司债券尾部风险定价的来源以及不同类型的债券和投资者的影响如何变化来补充资产定价框架。

11502620.value: 股權債務同持如何影響公司披露

11502620.label: Project Objectives
11502620.value: It is ex ante not clear whether a drop in shareholder-creditor conflicts would positively or negatively affect corporate disclosure. We will firstly construct a comprehensive sample of mergers between shareholders and lenders of the same firm. We will start by identifying all completed mergers between financial firms from the Thomson Reuters Securities Data Corporation (SDC) M&A database. The pooled names of all the acquirers and targets will be matched with the lender names of the LPC DealScan database and the institutional investor names of the Thomson Reuters 13F database, respectively. We will construct a sample of treated firms and matched control firms using the mergers sample constructed from the previous step. The matched sample based on merger events will allow us to perform a differences-in-differences (DID) analysis on the impact of shareholder-creditor merger events on corporate disclosures. Before running the DID analysis, we will begin with regression analysis by investigating the impact of the existence of dual holders, who simultaneously hold stocks and lend money to the same firm, on corporate disclosures. We will follow Jiang et al. (2010) and identify a sample of dual holders. Evidence obtained from the dual holders regression analysis could potentially be subject to endogeneity concerns, and we will focus on the mergers between shareholders and lenders as an exogenous shock to the shareholder-creditor conflict in our main regression. We try to establish a causal impact of shareholder-creditor conflict on corporate disclosures by the following approach. Using the treated and matched control firms constructed from the aforementioned procedures and adopting a DID regression framework, we will examine whether the voluntary disclosures of the treated firms significantly increase after the mergers between a firm’s institutional investors and lenders, compared with the matched control firms. Cross-sectionally, we will examine whether any impact of mergers on firms’ voluntary disclosure is stronger when the merging dual holders possess stronger monitoring incentives. Further, in the expectation that mergers between shareholders and creditors enable dual holders to gain more information advantage over the other capital providers in the market, we will test whether the impact of mergers on corporate disclosure is stronger for firms with worse information environment. 11502620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502620.value: The divergence in objectives between lenders and equity holders has drawn attention from theoretical research since the 1970s (Jensen and Meckling 1976; Myers 1977; Smith and Warner 1979; Leland 1994). Lenders have a fixed claim on firm value, while equity holders have a residual claim. Shareholders, or managers acting on behalf of shareholders, possess the incentives to expropriate wealth from the creditors through taking more risks, which is commonly known as the asset substitution problem. Despite prior theoretical work on the divergence in incentives between equity holders and creditors, empirical evidence on shareholder-creditor conflicts is relatively scarce and mixed. Emerging literature tries to shed light on the impact of incentive misalignment between shareholders and creditors through examining the simultaneous holding of equity and debt claims of the same firm (dual ownership or dual holding). For example, Jiang, Li and Shao (2010) and Chava, Wang and Zou (2019) propose that dual holders possess better aligned shareholder-creditor objectives, as manifested by lower loan yield spreads and less frequent use of capital expenditure restrictions in loan contracts. Chu (2018) finds that dual ownership reduces dividend payout. However, the literature has paid little attention to how dual holding affects corporate disclosure. To fill this void in the literature, this study tries to provide direct causal evidence on how incentive conflicts between shareholders and debtholders affect corporate disclosures by exploiting mergers between lending banks and institutional investors of the same firm following Chu (2018). It is important to examine this research question given the current debate on how lender and shareholder interactions affect corporate disclosures. Looking at debt covenant violations, Vashishtha (2014) contends that bank intervention benefits both creditors and shareholders by reducing managerial agency problems, thus shareholders delegate monitoring to creditors and demand fewer public disclosures. However, Christensen, Pei, Pierce and Tan (2019) hold the opposite view and argue that covenant violation intensifies shareholder-creditor conflicts, which induces higher shareholder scrutiny and accordingly improved disclosure quality. The dual holder merger creates negative shocks to the shareholder-creditor conflict, which provides a cleaner setting for testing how changes in shareholder-creditor conflicts affect corporate disclosures.

11502620.label: Realisation of objectives
11502620.value: I have achieved all the research objectives in a paper, “Simultaneous Equity-Debt Holdings and Corporate Disclosure” (R1). In that paper, we showed that both the likelihood and the frequency of management earnings forecasts significantly increase after the mergers between lenders and equity holders. Cross-sectionally, we showed that the impact of dual holder mergers on management disclosures is more salient when the merging dual holders possess stronger monitoring incentives and for firms with a worse information environment. Our findings suggest that firms increase voluntary disclosures to mitigate the information asymmetry caused by dual holders’ information advantage. While we were revising to submit R1 to a top journal in the accounting area, we received a first round Revise and Resubmission invitation on 7 April 2022 from Contemporary Accounting Research (CAR, A journal in accounting) on a related paper, “Institutional Dual Holdings and Expected Crash risk: Evidence from Mergers between Lenders and Equity Holders” (R2). The same as R1, R2 exploits the manually cooked data on mergers between lenders and equity holders of the same firm. Different from R1, which investigates how dual holder mergers affect management disclosures, the initial version R2 examined the effect of dual holder mergers on firms’ ex ante expected stock price crash risk evident in the options implied volatility smirk. In R2’s first round Revise and Resubmit decision letter received from CAR, the editor and two reviewers requested us to also examine management disclosures, which was the main focus of R1. Specifically, the editor (Linda Myers) mentioned that “both reviewers request some direct evidence about how dual holdings impact disclosure”. On page 2 of Reviewer 1’s review report, she/he asked “how dual holders affect corporate disclosure?”. Reviewer 2’s Comment #2 mentioned that “It would be helpful if the authors provide some empirical evidence that managers indeed provide more information, particularly bad news, to the market after the merger.” Together with my co-authors on R2, we spent almost one year addressing all the comments from the editor and two reviewers at CAR (not just the comment on additional evidence of management disclosures). We struggled a lot on whether we could manage to handle the revision of R2 without influencing R1. After a serious consideration and discussion with my co-authors, I eventually decided to combine R2 with R1 to fully address the CAR editor’s and reviewers’ requests for additional evidence of management disclosures. We held off on the circulation and submission of R1 to any journals because we wanted to hear back from CAR first. In case the combined paper gets rejected by CAR, we might consider separating R1 and R2 again and separately sending them to different journals. On 13 April 2023, the combined paper got a second round of Revise and Resubmit invitation. Both the editor and the two reviewers quite liked our combined paper and provided additional comments. Subsequently, we went through two more rounds of revisions at CAR and eventually got conditional acceptance for the combined paper on 24 March 2024. The combined paper was formally accepted by CAR on 3 June 2024 (CAR paper). All the main results in R1 are now presented in Table 8 and discussed in Section 5.4 of the combined paper, which has been officially published at CAR (doi: 10.1111/1911-3846.12966). Below, I explain in more detail how I achieved the project objectives in the CAR paper. I cooked a comprehensive sample of mergers between shareholders and lenders of the same firm. I started by identifying all completed mergers between financial firms from the Thomson Reuters Securities Data Corporation (SDC) M&A database. The pooled names of all the acquirers and targets were matched with the lender names of the LPC DealScan database and the institutional investor names of the Thomson Reuters 13F database, respectively. I constructed a sample of treated firms and matched control firms using the mergers sample constructed from the previous step. The matched sample based on merger events allowed me to perform a differences-in-differences (DID) analysis on the impact of shareholder-creditor merger events on management disclosures (management earnings forecasts). We established a causal impact of shareholder-creditor conflict on corporate disclosures by the following approach. Using the treated and matched control firms constructed from the aforementioned procedures and adopting a DID regression framework, we examined whether the management earnings forecasts of the treated firms significantly increase after the mergers between a firm’s institutional investors and lenders, compared with the matched control firms. Specifically, all these results are presented in Table 8 of Section 5.4 of the CAR paper. In Panel B of Table 8, we report in Column 1 a positive and significant coefficient on Treatment×Post, suggesting that the overall frequency of management earnings forecasts increases following the mergers. Moreover, we find in Columns 2 and 3 that the coefficients on Treatment×Post are positive and significant (insignificant) when the dependent variable is bad (good) news management earnings forecasts; that is, the increase in the frequency of earnings forecasts is concentrated among bad news forecasts. We also investigated the impact of the existence of dual holders, who simultaneously hold stocks and lend money to the same firm, on management disclosures. We followed Jiang et al. (2010) and identified a sample of dual holders. The results are consistent with those reported in Table 8 of the CAR paper. In addition, we undertook cross-sectional tests to further validate our main results. First, we showed that the impact of dual holder mergers on management disclosures is more salient when the merging dual holders possess stronger monitoring incentives. Second, we found that the effect of dual holder mergers on corporate disclosure is stronger for firms with a worse information environment. However, we did not tabulate these results in the CAR paper due to space limitations.

11502620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502620.value: This study looks at what happens when the same people or groups own both shares and debt in a company, using situations where lenders and shareholders merge as a surprise event. It focuses on how this affects the information companies share. These dual holders have inside knowledge because they are lenders, giving them an edge over other investors and creating an imbalance in the information available to everyone. This project finds that when these dual holders appear, companies are more likely to share their earnings forecasts more often. This change in how companies share information is mostly seen in businesses whose dual holders have a greater motivation to keep an eye on things, and in firms that already have a big gap in information among investors. Overall, the findings suggest that companies try to share more information voluntarily to balance the advantage that dual holders have.

11503120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503120.value: 企業信用風險的共性与信用評級

11503120.label: Project Objectives
11503120.value: Investigate the commonality of corporate CDS spreads within and across industries. Identify any relations among corporate credit risk across industries and how credit ratings relate to the common components of credit risk. These empirical studies will shed light on the cross-sectional nature of the corporate credit risk and the role of credit ratings in pricing credit risk. Based on the empirical studies in objective 1, develop a no-arbitrage model that can accommodate some critical features of credit risk, credit rating and migration, industrial classification, systematic and idiosyncratic factors, and time-varying price of risk, and that yields explicit solutions to credit products, especially to CDS spreads. Thus, MLE estimations based on a large cross-sectional CDS spreads are possible. Estimate several specifications of the model with different combinations of systematic factor(s), idiosyncratic factors, and drivers of rating transition probabilities. Based on the estimated specifications, we can perform variant tests and investigate important questions regarding credit risk and credit ratings. Based on the estimations, we can further investigate the accuracy and relevance of corporate credit rating and its relation with issuers' fundamentals. Thus, we can study the performance of rating agencies through a window of our no-arbitrage credit risk model. To better understand the nature of the systematic factor(s) of credit risk, we can follow previous studies to investigate how these factors relate to the other well-known macroeconomic and financial variables.

11503120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503120.value: Previous empirical studies show that corporate credit risk, including default probabilities and credit risk premium, is driven by common factors. Credit rating is the key measure of corporate credit risk in practice, given the large cross-section of corporate borrowers. Our preliminary empirical study also shows that there exists a common factor across average CDS spreads across industries. Furthermore, the dependency on the common factor is monotone across credit rating in each industry. However, this strong commonality in the corporate credit risk has not been incorporated in any credit risk model in the literature. Based on these observations, we build a parsimonious no-arbitrage reduced-form model of corporate credit risk with credit rating and industrial classification as the key cross-sectional variables. The hazard rate of default is driven by a set of common factors and an issuer-specific factor, and the common factors are driving the rating transitions and credit risk premium. To fully capture the dynamics of the common factors, we use the full spectrum of the corporate CDS spreads to estimate and test the model. The estimated model and the associated common factors enable us to study the properties of the common factors and their relations with other macroeconomic variables and how these common factors, in conjunction with credit rating and industrial classification, drive the corporate credit risk. The results of the project should shed new light on the interactions of credit rating, industrial classification, and common risk factors in shaping the corporate credit markets. 以往的經驗研究表明，企業信用風險，包括違約概率信用風險溢價是由共同因素驅動的。信用評級是關鍵措施鑑於公司借款人的橫截面很大，因此在實踐中對公司信用風險的評估也是如此。我們的初步實證研究還表明，存在一個共同的因素平均CDS跨行業分佈。此外，對共同的依賴在每個行業的信用評級中，因素都是單調的。但是，這種強大公司信用風險的共同性尚未納入任何信用風險 文獻中的模型。基於這些觀察，我們建立了一個簡化的套利交易 信用等級和行業的企業信用風險的簡化形式模型分類作為關鍵的橫截面變量。違約風險率由驅動由一組共同因素和特定於發行人的因素組成，共同因素是推動評級過渡和信用風險溢價。充分捕捉動態 共同因素，我們使用企業CDS利差的全部範圍進行估算並測試型。估計的模型和相關的共同因素使我們能夠研究共同因素的性質及其與其他宏觀經濟的關係變量以及這些共同因素如何與信用評級和工業分類，驅動企業信用風險。該項目的結果應該嶄新根據信用評級，行業分類和共同風險的相互作用影響企業信貸市場的因素。

11503520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503520.value: Participative leaders share influences and decision-making power with their subordinates (Armenakis et al., 1993) and scholars have acknowledged the potential motivational benefits of this as well as the positive performance implications (Randolph, 2000). The linkage of participative leadership with performance has been extensively examined from the direct leader perspective (Huang et al., 2010; Lam et al., 2002), but research has rarely focused on the effect of participative leadership exercised by leaders with higher hierarchical positions (skip-level leaders who are one level above direct leaders; Detert & Treviño, 2010). Very little is known about: (1) how subordinates and their direct leaders react to skip-level leaders’ participative behaviors toward subordinates; and (2) how direct leaders shape the impact of skip-level participative leadership on subordinates. This oversight is surprising because contemporary organizations’ development provides employees with ample opportunities to interact directly with leaders other than their direct supervisors (e.g., hierarchy elimination; Rajan & Wulf, 2006; Peters & Waterman, 1982). Skip-level leaders usually have remarkable influence on subordinates’ promotion, resources, well-being, and work outcomes (Detert & Treviño, 2010). Furthermore, workplace trends for contemporary businesses such as employee participation plans (Lawler et al., 2001) form the basis for the implementation of participative leadership among higher-ups. Therefore, it is critical to understand the impact of skip-level participative leadership on employees’ performance. Following our previous work on the exchange-based model of participative leadership (Huang et al., 2010), we propose that skip-level leaders’ participative behaviors promote employee performance by nurturing a positive exchange relationship with employees (skip-level leader–member exchange; SMX; Liu et al., 2013). However, our recent research on triadic relationships (three parties involved; Tse, Lam, Lawrence, & Huang, 2013) suggests that vertical exchange relations are embedded such that the exchange relationship with one partner (e.g., skip-level leader; SMX) is influenced by the relationship with another partner (e.g., direct leader; leader–member exchange [LMX]; Sherony & Green, 2002). Furthermore, these intertwined exchange relations may be shaped by teams’ contextual factors (i.e., empowerment climate; Zhou et al., 2012). Building on this foundation, we propose a multilevel model positing that: (1) skip-level participative leadership may influence SMX; (2) subordinates may positively reciprocate skip-level leaders’ actions by improving their performance; (3) the indirect relationship between skip-level participation and performance through SMX depends on LMX; and (4) team empowerment climate may function as a cross-level moderator, influencing this conditional indirect linkage. Multimethod studies will be used to address these issues. 我喜欢我的大领导超过我的直接领导：跨层级参与式领导对绩效的影响以及不同领导间的交换关系的作用 摘要 参与式领导是指那些与下属分享影响力和决策权的领导 (Armenakis et al., 1993)，学者们已经认识到了这种领导风格的潜在激励作用以及其对绩效的积极影响 (Randolph, 2000)。参与型领导与绩效之间的联系已经从直接领导的角度被广泛的研究 (Huang et al., 2010; Lam et al., 2002) ，但是以往研究很少有关注具有较高等级职位的领导者（那些比直接领导高一等级的跨层级领导；Detert & Treviño, 2010）采取参与式领导风格时对绩效的影响。目前，人们对以下两个方面知之甚少：（1）下属和他们的直接领导如何回应跨层级领导对下属的参与行为；以及（2）直接领导如何塑造跨层级参与式领导对下属的影响。这些研究的缺失令人惊讶，因为当代组织的发展为员工提供了大量的机会与直接主管以外的其他领导互动 (例如，层级结构的消除；Rajan & Wulf, 2006；Peters & Waterman, 1982) 。跨层级领导通常对下属的晋升，资源分配，幸福指数以及工作结果都有着十分显著的影响 (Detert & Treviño, 2010) 。此外，当代企业的工作场所发展趋势，如员工参与计划 (Lawler et al.，2001) ，构成了企业高层管理者实施参与式领导的基础。因此，了解跨层级参与式领导对员工绩效的影响是十分重要的。 基于之前对参与式领导的交换模型的研究(Huang et al.，2010) ，本文认为跨层级领导的参与式行为通过与员工建立积极的交换关系从而促进了员工的绩效提升(跨层级领导-成员交换[SMX]；Liu et al.，2013)。然而，最近对三元关系（三方参与; Tse, Lam, Lawrence, & Huang, 2013）的研究表明，纵向交换关系是嵌入式的，即与一方 (例如，跨级领导；SMX) 的交换关系会受到与另一方(例如，直接领导；领导-成员交换[LMX]；Sherony & Green, 2002) 的关系的影响。此外，这些错综复杂的交换关系可能还会受到团队环境因素的影响（例如，授权氛围；Zhou et al.，2012）。在此基础上，本文提出了一个多层次模型，假设：（1）跨层级参与式领导可能会影响跨层级领导-成员交换（SMX）；（2）下属可以通过提升他们的绩效来积极回应跨层级领导的行为；（3）跨层级参与通过跨层级领导-成员交换（SMX）和绩效间的间接关系依赖于领导-成员交换（LMX）；（4）团队授权氛围可能作为跨层次调节因子，影响这种条件性的间接关系。多种方法研究将用来检验这些问题。

11503520.label: Realisation of objectives
11503520.value: Across two independent field studies, we investigated how skip-level leader participation and SMX affect individual performance and behaviors. In the first survey, we aimed to examine how skip-level participation is relevant to employee performance, through the mediating role of relational factor (i.e., exchange relationship quality between the skip-level leader and employees (SMX)) and individual factor (i.e., organizational self-esteem). The results revealed a positive indirect relationship between skip-level participative leadership and employee performance, through SMX and self-esteem. That is, employees supervised by skip-level participative leadership is more likely to have a higher level of work performance because participation into higher level decision making boosts their self-importance and positive self-evaluation as reflected by their increased organizational self-esteem. In addition, it also explained by their exchange relationship with the skip-level leader because a good relation with the skip level leader allows them to get access to important resources and support which are essential for performance. The second survey tested how exchange relationship between skip-level leader and leader (LLX) and between leader and member (LMX) moderate the indirect linkages between skip-level participation and employee performance. Specifically, we tested how LLX and LMX may moderate the relationship between the indirect linkages between skip-level participation and employee performance, as measured by organizational citizenship behavior (e.g., OCB including helping organizations and co-workers). Study 2 constructively replicated Study’s 1 results. That is, we again found the indirect relationship to be mediated by both relational and individual factors. Essentially, our analyses also suggested that LLX moderated the positive indirect linkage between participation and organizational citizenship behaviour (via organizational selfesteem) whereas LMX moderated the positive participation – OCB linkage (via SMX). Specifically, these positive indirect linkages were strengthened when LLX and LMX were higher; by contrast, they were buffered when the LLX and LMX were lower. Overall, these investigations have satisfied both objectives 1-3. In addition, in two other independent samples, we further examined how skip-level leader trust affect abusive supervision and whether/how this relationship is moderated by LMX and LLX (as a proxy of ' empowerment climate), therefore satisfying objective #3 and #4. Specifically, In the third survey, we examined whether different types of skip-level leader influence on employee participation (e.g., skip-level leader trust on employee) may influence employee performance through the impact of SMX in a similar way as the skip-level participative leadership does. In addition, we examine what is the role of direct leader on this relationship. Specifically, we study how the direct leader who is less trusted by the skip-level leader reacts to the employees who is highly trusted and well-liked by the skip-level leader. We measured abusive supervision as a reaction of the direct leader. We found, across a field study and an MBA sample, that when direct leader is less trusted by the skip-level leader, direct leader more accurately perceived the relationship quality between the skip-level leader and the subordinate. In turn, the more that the direct leader perceived a high-quality relationship between the skip-level leader and the subordinate, the lower the levels of abusive supervision. This satisfies both 3 and 4.

11503520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503520.value: In both Studies 1 and 2, we found that employees supervised by skip-level participative leadership are more likely to have a higher level of work performance because participation into higher level decision making boosts their self-importance and positive self-evaluation as reflected by their increased organizational self-esteem. Study 2 further showed that LLX moderated the positive indirect linkage between participation and organizational citizenship behaviour (via organizational self-esteem) whereas LMX moderated the participation – OCB linkage (via SMX). Specifically, these positive indirect linkages were strengthened when LLX and LMX were higher; by contrast, they were buffered when the LLX and LMX were lower. In essence, these studies show that skip-level participative leadership is critical toward employee success. Across another field study (Study 3) and an MBA sample (Study 4), we found that when direct leader is less trusted by the skip-level leader, direct leader more accurately perceived the relationship quality between the skip-level leader and the subordinate. In turn, the more that the direct leader perceived a high-quality relationship between the skip-level leader and the subordinate, the lower the levels of abusive supervision. Based on these results, we have produced a conference paper that were presented at the Annual Conference of the Society of Industrial and Organizational Psychology. We are developing a journal article which is currently in the advanced stage of revision at a high-quality journal (Academy of Management Journal).

11503520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503520.value: For our journal revise-and-resubmit, we are planning to conduct another field study to replicate our finding constructively and to control for known antecedents of abusive supervision. We will then submit our findings as a revision to the Academy of Management Journal. Finally, we plan to present our findings to the management public at Society for Industrial/Organizational Psychology (SIOP) in April 2025, and the Academy of Management in August 2025.

11503520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503520.value: We find that when the boss' boss engages their subordinate in decision making, the subordinate performs better in their job and engage in more citizenship behaviors because they experience higher levels of self-esteem and think more positively about themselves. This effect is especially strong when the boss' boss also has a positive relationship with the boss or when the boss has a positive relationship with the subordinate. Finally, we also found that direct leader direct leader can more accurately perceive the relationship quality between the skip-level leader and the subordinate when they have a poor relationship with the skip-level leader. In turn, the more that the direct leader perceived a high-quality relationship between the skip-level leader and the subordinate, the less likely that they will abuse their subordinates. These findings offer new insights with respect to avoiding abusive supervision by direct leader: (1) ensure a positive relationship with skip-level leader when direct leader does not have a positive relationship with skip-level leader, and/or (2) increase direct leader's perception that they have a good relationship with skip-level leader.

11503720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503720.value: 信息科技如何影响审计市场? -- 基于网上招聘信息的实证研究

11503720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503720.value: 快速发展的信息科技在深刻的影响和改变着现代经济的方方面面。各个行业的公司都在加大对信息科技的投入。信息科技的应用不仅限于公司的生产运营，也改变着公司的营销方式，财务信息披露，以及内部的审计工作。审计市场也不例外地经历着信息科技所带来的变革。一方面，审计公司有动力积极的采用信息科技提高工作效率。另一方面，随着越来越多的审计客户在运营与管理中采用信息科技，审计公司也必须掌握信息科技知识，从而能搞提供高质里的审计。美国上市公司会计监管委员会的调查显示，在过去的十年里，审计公司每年在信息技术方面的投入都要在30亿到50亿美元。信息科技的应用给审计市场带来了如何的改变？由于信息科技的应用往往需要较大的前期投入，信息科技的应用使得小审计公司相对于大审计公司失去市场竞争力吗？这些问题对审计行业的政策制定有着重要的影响。如果信息科技所需要的前期投入已经成了小审计公司提升竞争力的障碍，政策制定者需要考虑信息科技对整个审计市场竞性的影响。在英国竞争与市场监管局所做的一项关于非四大审计公司在市场竞争中所面临的主要困难的调查中，审计公司Crowe已经把需要大量前期资金投入的信息科技列为主要的困难之一。在这个科研项目中，我们计划通过公司的网上招聘信息量化公司（包括审计公司与被审计公司）的信息科技应用，从而对信息科技如何影响审计市场进行实证研究。

11504020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504020.value: 投資者與消費者：眾籌項目不同類型支持者之間的交互

11504020.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11504020.value: Dr Gao, Haibing Dr Tan, Ricky Yinliang

11504020.label: Project Objectives
11504020.value: Should a given project use multiple forms of crowdfunding? This question is relevant to all crowdfunding projects. This is especially true where different motivations (e.g., consumption utility and investment return) commonly exist. Our theoretical development suggests that major reward-based platforms such as Kickstarter consider backers’ demand to invest and provide investment options to fund an innovation. Similarly, p2p lending platforms such as Prosper may add consumption options if some backers are more interested in a product offering. For either situation, offering a mix of funding forms may expand the market. More importantly, backers of different motivations can interact, creating a positive effect beyond simple addition. As more entrepreneurs are using both reward- and investment-based crowdfunding, how to better launch a successful crowdfunding campaign? With the rise of investment-based crowdfunding platforms, more and more startups are seeking capital through both reward- and investment-based crowdfunding platforms. Our hypotheses reveal that early investors who are more sophisticated can better predict a crowdfunding campaign’s success, and more importantly, voluntarily recruit potential consumers. That is, entrepreneurs can launch their projects on the investment-based crowdfunding platforms first and leverage investors’ network to reach more consumers. Our findings may encourage collaboration and coordination between different types of platforms (investment-based and reward-based) in order to enhance efficiency (e.g., by saving sunk cost, administration cost, as well as marketing cost). For example, through mechanism design, the investment platform can specify that lenders' financial return (i.e., interest) depends solely on the crowdfunding performance in the reward-based platform, which as a result may motivate early investors to persuade potential consumers to support reward-based crowdfunding. To coordinate well, the two platforms should design tools to facilitate information dissemination as well as interactions between early investors and prospective consumers. More aggressively, the entrepreneur may use an adapted all-or-nothing policy across the two platforms, i.e., the joint performance of two platforms determines crowdfunding success. How to attract early contribution by investor backers? Our hypotheses remind startups that a promising innovation can attract investor herding early. That is, to encourage investors’ early contribution, entrepreneurs should release information about the innovation in a timely manner. For example, they should provide details about the innovative technology, quickly respond to concerns from potential backers, and periodically update progress of the innovation project. Alternatively, entrepreneurs may use high return as the economic incentive. Both strategies can signal entrepreneurs’ confidence, which can be efficiently detected by competent investors. How to encourage interactions between backers with different motivations? Our hypotheses offer three suggestions for promoting backer interactions. First, entrepreneurs may properly design crowdfunding campaigns. In our research setting, consumers and investors jointly contribute to the funding goal. In particular, investors’ return heavily depends on consumers’ purchases. Therefore, investors who participate early interact with consumers to encourage purchases. Second, to facilitate backers’ interactions, the platform should offer a channel for backers to disseminate project-relevant information. In our empirical setting, committed backers can request referral links from the platform to invite potential backers. Third, to increase effectiveness of early investors’ interactions with consumers, entrepreneurs can customize reward-based options to effectively segment different consumer groups. This is particularly important when consumers have different valuation or preferences. These valuable insights also provide guidance toward the crowdfunding platform design.

11504020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504020.value: Crowdfunding has changed the way startups, entrepreneurs, and individuals raise capital by harnessing the power of the crowd. Backers can choose from two types of crowdfunding: reward-based crowdfunding is an established and attractive fundraising option for entrepreneurs with creative projects, while investment-based crowdfunding has also gained popularity thanks to the progress of related regulations. Different types of crowdfunding backers (i.e. consumers and investors) exhibit distinct motivations. The goal of this research project is to understand the behavior and interaction of different types of backers, and to help entrepreneurs make decisions on when to use each type of crowdfunding in order to launch a successful fundraising campaign. To address this issue, we plan to conduct a field study on a popular crowdfunding platform, where each campaign can offer both reward- and investment-based funding. Specifically, we will test the relationship between investors’ contribution in the early stage of the campaign and the likelihood of the campaign’s success. We propose two mechanisms to explain our theoretical development: a screening effect, in which early investors can better extract information about the innovation project to predict crowdfunding success, and a cheerleading effect, in which early investors voluntarily act as sales agents to encourage purchases by potential consumers of reward-based crowdfunding. Moreover, we further argue that despite these critical roles (predictors and sales agents) of early investors, the funding goal of a successful campaign is mainly accomplished by consumers in the later stage. Upon completion of this project, our findings will provide relevant managerial implications for entrepreneurs and valuable insights towards crowdfunding platform design. 眾籌通過向大眾籌款的方式改變了初創公司、企業家和個人尋找資金來源的模式。項目支持者可以選擇兩種中籌模式：回報型眾籌和投資性眾籌。不同類型眾籌項目的支持者也展示出不同的動機，對應於上述兩種眾籌模式，我們在下文中把對應的支持者分別稱為消費者和投資者。本研究的目的是要理解不同類型眾籌支持者之間的交互，並幫助企業家決定何時採用何種眾籌模式以達到籌款目標。為此，我們在一家業界領先的眾籌網站上設計並實施了一次田野研究。此眾籌網站的每個項目都可以選擇採用回報型或者投資型模式。我們測試在眾籌項目早期投資型支持者的貢獻與項目成功率的關係。為了解釋本研究的理論，我們提出了兩個機制：早期投資者可以更好的收集項目相關信息，稱之為篩選效應；早期投資者為了達成投資目的獲得回報而去號召更多投資者加入本項目，稱之為加油效應。進一步我們提出，雖然早期投資型支持者的作用很關鍵，但決定一個眾籌項目成敗更依賴於後期消費型支持者的貢獻。我們在本研究的結尾會提出對眾籌行業從業者的建議。

11504020.value: First, entrepreneurs should disseminate more project-relevant information in a timely fashion, and our findings remind startups that a promising innovation can attract investor contribution early on. For example, entrepreneurs should provide details about the innovative product, quickly respond to concerns from potential backers, and periodically make progress updates on the project throughout the funding cycle. Alternatively, entrepreneurs may use high investment return as an economic incentive. Both strategies can signal an entrepreneur’s confidence, which can be detected by com- petent investors. Campaigns offering more project-relevant information are also appealing to early investors. Second, entrepreneurs should customize reward-based options for their crowdfunding campaigns, which is partic- ularly important when consumers have different valuations or preferences. Crowdfunded products offered by campaigns with product customization can better satisfy a consumer market with heterogeneous demand and gain popularity among various types of consumers. This is crucial, because investors are concerned about the success of the crowdfunded products across the whole consumer market. Early investors interpret this information as a positive signal of a successful crowdfunding outcome, and so will be attracted to campaigns utilizing product customization. Third, these valuable insights also provide guidance toward the design of crowdfunding platforms. Our findings may encourage collaboration and coordination between different types of platforms (investment-based and reward-based) to enhance efficiency (e.g., by saving sunk costs, administrative costs and marketing costs). In one possible mechanism design scenario, an investment-based platform can specify that a lender’s financial return (i.e., interest) depends solely on crowdfunding performance in the reward-based platform. As a result, early investors may be motivated to persuade potential consumers to support reward-based crowdfunding. To better coordinate, the two platforms should design tools to facilitate information dissemination as well as interactions between early investors and prospective consumers. To be even more aggressive, the entrepreneur may use an adapted all-or-nothing policy across the two platforms, in which the joint performance of both platforms determines crowdfunding success.

11504020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504020.value: The first opportunity for future studies can be to make direct comparisons by designing a field experiment. Researchers can also poten- tially clarify the value of multiple forms of crowdfunding when directly comparing the hybrid approach against the single approach, or they could investigate whether the simultaneous- or sequential-launching approach to the two types of crowdfunding works differently than the other. Another direction for future research can examine whether our findings can be extended to other types of crowd- funding, like reward-based and equity-based funding. It would be interesting to explore whether shareholders in equity-based funding exhibit behavior similar to lenders in investment-based crowdfunding.

11504020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504020.value: We find a positive relationship between investor contributions in the early stage of the campaign and the likelihood of the campaign’s success. Our empirical analysis reveals that investor–consumer interaction mediates the main effect of early investor contributions. Moreover, the positive main effect is stronger when a larger amount of project-relevant information is released and when a higher level of customization (using price discrimination or product differentiation) is offered in reward-based funding options. These results are consistent with several robustness checks.

11504620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504620.value: Upon arrival at emergency departments (EDs), patients are classified into different triage levels indicating their urgency. Using data from an urban hospital in Canada, we find that within the same triage level, the average waiting time (time from triage to physician initial assessment) of discharge patients is shorter than that of admit patients for middle-to-low acuity patients, suggesting that the order of patients being served deviates from FCFS (first-come-first-served), and to certain extent, discharge patients are prioritized over admit patients. This observation is intriguing as among patients of the same triage level, admit patients - who need further care in the hospital - should be deemed no less urgent than discharge patients who only need treatment at EDs. To understand the prioritization behaviors of ED decision makers (nurses and physicians) in choosing the next patient for treatment, we carried out a preliminary study using a discrete choice model to develop our hypotheses. Based on the preliminary results, we conjecture that decision makers apply urgency-specific delay-dependent prioritization. Moreover, such prioritization behaviors also depend on the system congestion level, especially the ED blocking level -- the percentage of beds occupied by boarding patients. We conjecture that (i) when ED blocking level is sufficiently low, admit patients are prioritized over discharge patients for high acuity patients, and the first-come-first-served rule is followed for middle-to-low acuity patients; (ii) otherwise, the risk of ED being blocked becomes sufficiently high, decision makers start to prioritize patients who are less likely to be admitted after treatment at the ED. Our hypotheses imply that the prioritization decisions at EDs are not purely clinical driven but also takes capacity rationing into account. While there have been behavioral studies on medical decision making, the patient prioritization behavior at EDs, i.e., which patient to treat next, has not been investigated. This proposed study aims to shed light on this problem. Our objective is to test our hypotheses through sophisticated econometric models and investigate the impact of the patient prioritization decisions on ED operational performances. Physicians and nurses are central to the daily ED operations. By testing and highlighting their patient prioritization behaviors, this paper will advance our understanding of ED operations and patient flow. In this proposal, we present our preliminary results and describe a set of tasks for achieving our goals. Our team's training and research experiences in emergency medicine and operations management have prepared us to carry out the proposed research.

11504620.label: Realisation of objectives
11504620.value: We are pleased to report that all three objectives have been fully realized. The research findings, detailed below, highlight the significant progress made in each area. Objective 1: Empirical Investigation of ED Decision-Makers' Behavior The primary focus was to investigate the patient prioritization behavior of emergency department (ED) decision-makers (nurses, physicians) under congestion. Utilizing a discrete-choice model and analyzing data from a tertiary hospital in Alberta, Canada, we found that ED decision-makers prioritize patients based on both the urgency of their condition and the delay they have experienced. This approach ensures that high-acuity patients receive timely care, reflecting a nuanced understanding of patient needs. We find that when the ED blocking level is low, admitted high-acuity patients are prioritized over discharged patients. For middle- and low-acuity patients, disposition does not significantly influence prioritization. As blocking levels rise, decision-makers shift their focus to prioritize discharged patients, alleviating congestion by expediting the discharge process for those who can leave the ED sooner. Our analysis of a stylized model suggests that prioritizing discharged patients under high congestion helps mitigate further blocking, enhancing overall ED efficiency and reducing system pressure. Objective 2: Impact of ED on ED Decision-Makers' Behavior on Operational Performance To study the impact of these behaviors on ED operational performance, we developed a data-calibrated simulation model. Our key findings include: The prioritization policies developed based on our insights can reduce average patient waiting times and lengths of stay. Furthermore, incorporating observed prioritization behaviors into predictive models significantly improved the accuracy of ED waiting time predictions. This allows for better anticipation of patient flow and resource allocation. Objective 3: Development of Prioritization Policy to Support ED Decision Making Based on our findings, we developed new prioritization policies aimed at improving ED operations. We show that adjusting prioritization criteria according to current blocking levels to optimize patient flow and reduce congestion. This project has advanced our understanding of ED operations and patient flow by emphasizing the critical role of decision-makers' patient prioritization behaviors. The findings provide actionable insights that can be leveraged to optimize ED management, demonstrating significant progress in all three objectives. No under-achievements were encountered, and all objectives were met to their fullest extent, confirming the success of the project. By integrating empirical investigations, simulation models, and practical policy recommendations, this project offers a comprehensive approach to improving emergency department performance and patient care.

11504620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504620.value: The primary objective of this project was to investigate the patient prioritization behavior of emergency department (ED) decision-makers (nurses, physicians) under congestion. By employing a discrete-choice model and analyzing data from a tertiary hospital in Alberta, Canada, we uncovered several critical insights: 1. Urgency-Specific, Delay-Dependent Prioritization: ED decision-makers prioritize patients based on both the urgency of their condition and the delay they have experienced. This urgency-specific, delay-dependent approach ensures that high-acuity patients receive timely care, reflecting a nuanced understanding of patient needs. 2. Influence of ED Blocking Levels: When the ED blocking level is low, admitted high-acuity patients are prioritized over discharged patients. For middle- and low-acuity patients, disposition (whether admitted or discharged) does not significantly influence prioritization. As blocking levels rise, decision-makers shift their focus to prioritize discharged patients. This strategic change aims to alleviate congestion by expediting the discharge process for patients who can leave the ED sooner, thereby preventing further blockage. 3. Rationale Behind Prioritization Shifts: A stylized model was analyzed to explain the rationale behind these shifts. It suggests that prioritizing discharged patients under high congestion helps mitigate further blocking, thereby enhancing overall ED efficiency and reducing systemic strain. 4. Development of Optimized Prioritization Policies: Based on our findings, we developed new prioritization policies to improve ED operations. These policies are designed to reduce average patient waiting times and lengths of stay by dynamically adjusting prioritization criteria according to the current blocking level. 5. Enhanced Accuracy of Waiting Time Predictions: Our insights can significantly improve the accuracy of ED waiting time predictions. By incorporating observed prioritization behaviors into predictive models, EDs can better anticipate patient flow and manage expectations, leading to more informed decision-making and resource allocation. By examining and emphasizing the critical role of decision-makers' patient prioritization behaviors, this project advances our understanding of ED operations and patient flow. The findings provide actionable insights that can be leveraged to optimize ED management, enhancing both patient outcomes and operational efficiency. This finding has been published at Operations Research, one of the flagship journals in the field of operations management.

11504620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504620.value: In the current project, the decisions made by nurses and physicians are aggregated into a single decision step. However, in reality, nurses first decide which patient to room from the waiting area of the ED. Then, physicians select which patient to treat next from the roomed patients. It would be interesting to investigate the prioritization behavior of nurses and physicians separately, especially given that nurses and physicians may apply different criteria for patient prioritization. However, the challenge is that this would require a more granular level of patient flow data. We would like to collaborate with our partner hospitals to explore the feasibility of further developing this research idea.

11504620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504620.value: This research project aimed to understand how nurses and doctors in emergency departments (EDs) decide which patients to treat next and how these decisions impact the overall efficiency of the ED. We studied data from a hospital in Alberta, Canada, and found that decision-makers prioritize patients based on the urgency of their condition and how long they've been waiting. They also take the pressure on ED resourses (specifically, ED beds) into consideration. For example, they give quicker care to seriously ill patients but also try to manage congestion by prioritizing patients who is likely to be discharged after ED treatment. Our findings led to the development of new policies that can help reduce waiting times and improve patient care. These policies adjust the prioritization of patients dynamically based on current congestion levels in the ED. We also created tools to help ED managers make better decisions, improving both patient outcomes and operational efficiency. Overall, our work provides valuable insights that can make EDs more efficient and improve patient care.

11505420.label: Project Objectives
11505420.value: We conceptualize the theoretical duality of firm diversification—reflected in the internal and external facets of diversification. The internal facet depicts the resources and behaviors of a diversified firm, and the external facet encompasses those of the firm’s rivals across diverse markets. Existing research largely studies either facet separately and hence suffers from omitted variable biases. We are among the first to empirically examine the two facets of diversification simultaneously. We pinpoint two issues in the extant studies on diversification and multimarket competition: observation interdependence, and intertemporal correlation of dependent variable. We pioneer a method to address these empirical issues. We are the first to propose the adoption of spatial econometric models in diversification research. We argue that this technique can be instrumental for not only diversification research but also other studies in strategic management. We are the first to introduce the Dunbar’s number to the literature of strategic management. We pioneer the theoretical conceptualization of the organizational Dunbar’s number—an instrumental index for policymakers to gauge industrial competition intensities and protect consumers.
