11505420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505420.value: The relationship between diversification and firm performance stands central in strategic management scholarship. In the diversification literature, studies examine potential synergy from a firm’s internal resources and behaviors, to which we refer as the internal facet of firm diversification. In a parallel vein, multimarket competition research investigates how external rivals across diverse markets—coined here as the external facet of firm diversification—may influence firm performance. These two research streams remain largely separated, albeit their common theorization target. Such intellectual disjunction hinders the development of unbiased knowledge on the performances of diversified firms. For example, omitted variable biases have plagued empirical analysis in both the internal-focused diversification studies and the external-oriented multimarket competition investigations. In this research proposal, we develop two studies that build towards a unified theory of diversified firm performance. In Study One, we cross-pollinate firm diversification and multimarket competition research. On the theoretical front, we conceptualize both internal and external diversification facets as firm performance antecedents. On the empirical front, we identify three critical issues of prior studies in addition to omitted variable bias: observation dependency, intertemporal correlation of firm performance, and endogenous process of multimarket contact. Due to these issues, empirical findings remain contended in the literature, and the conflicting interpretations have thwarted theoretical understanding and practical insights about the performances of diversified firms. To address such deficiencies, we use the spatial econometric model developed by Qu and colleagues (2015; 2017; 2016) to investigate how internal and external diversification facets influence the performances of general insurance firms in China. In Study Two, we conceptualize the organizational Dunbar number. First developed by Robin Dunbar (1992), the individual Dunbar number is the maximum size of an average person’s friendship (acquaintance) network, which is determined by individual cognitive capacity for social network maintenance. Per Dunbar’s research, such a number for the average person is about 150. Like individuals, organizations are embedded in relational networks and subject to managerial cognitive limitations. Hence, we ask a fundamental research question: For an organization, is there a Dunbar’s number? To answer this question, we define three size-weighted forms of organizational Dunbar’s number—the maximum form, the intended form, and the realized form. We develop a novel method to empirically identify the realized form of organizational Dunbar’s number in the general insurance industry in China. 企業產品多元化與企業績效之間的關系在戰略管理學中處於研究的中心地帶。在現有的企業產品多元化文獻中，前人的研究考察了企業內部資源和行為的潛在協同作用。這類研究專注於企業多元化的內部維度。同時，前人的多市場競爭的研究調查了企業在不同市場的外部競爭對手，而這類研究專注於企業多元化的外部維度如何影響企業績效。盡管前人這兩種研究有共同的理論目標，但它們在很大程度上沒有相互融合。這種脫節阻礙了對多元化企業績效研究的發展。例如，在以內部為中心的多元化研究和以外部為導向的多市場競爭調查中，遺漏的變量偏差困擾著實証分析。因此，我們開展了兩項研究，以建立一個統一的多元化企業績效理論。 在研究一中，我們融合企業多元化和多市場競爭研究。在理論上，我們將內部和外部維度都概念化為企業業績的先決條件。在實証方面，除了遺漏的變量偏差外，我們還確定了先前研究的兩個關鍵問題：研究樣本中的數據相互連系性，以及企業績效的時間間相關性。由於這些問題，在現有文獻中實証研究結果存在相互矛盾的研究發現。為了解決這些缺陷，我們使用空間計量經濟學模型，研究多元化企業的內部和外部維度如何影響中國財產保險企業的業績。 在研究二中，我們鄧巴的理論應用在企業多元化研究中。羅賓·鄧巴（Robin Dunbar）於1992年首先提出，一個普通人的友誼（熟人）網絡的是有限的，它由個人對社交網絡維護的認知能力決定。根據鄧巴（Dunbar）的研究，對於普通人來說，這個數字約為150，我們稱這個數字為鄧巴數字。與個人一樣，企業也嵌入到關系網絡中，並受到企業管理人員認知的限制。因此，我們提出一個基本的研究問題：對於一個企業，是否也有企業的鄧巴數字？為了回答這個問題，我們定義了組織企業的鄧巴數字的三種形式-最大形式，預期形式和實現形式。我們開發了一種新穎的方法來實証確定中國財產保險企業的鄧巴數字。

11505420.label: Realisation of objectives
11505420.value: The objectives have been achieved, despite the negative impact of COVID-19. In the first study of this project, we have investigated the performance impact of intra-industry diversification. The existing literature on diversification emphasizes the synergies that arise from the allocation of resources within a firm across different markets, which we refer to as the internal configuration. Another line of research, known as Multimarket contact (MMC) research, examines the performance implications of competitive dynamics between firms across markets, which we refer to as the external configuration. However, despite the coexistence of these two configurations in firm diversification, MMC research rarely intersects with diversification studies, resulting in biased results regarding the linkage between diversification and performance (D-P). Our project has bridged these two research streams and conceptualize the duality in diversification. To achieve this, we employ spatial econometrics to address two critical empirical issues in existing studies on D-P linkage and MMC—omitted variable bias and observation dependence. Through our analysis, we uncover the performance effects of both configurations and their interaction in the general insurance industry. Seminal studies on diversification have recognized the fundamental differences between inter- and intra-industry diversification, which compel us to further scrutiny on the latter as a unique phenomenon. Most critically, intra-industry diversification involves related markets in which firms offer products with overlapping functionalities. Market relatedness entails unique impediments for adjusting and coordinating the internal resource allocation at a firm. Moreover, market relatedness evolves alongside firm diversification in the industry, which will elicit major changes in the external competition patterns between firms. Namely, intra-industrial diversifiers establish multimarket contacts (MMC) with one another. Through MMC, the actions and performances of different firms in the industry become interdependent—a phenomenon theorized as “mutual forbearance”. As a focal firm diversifies, its MMC with direct rivals will alter, which can trigger widespread reactions from other firms in the industry as they coordinate to uphold mutual forbearance. These external changes in inter-firm competition and coordination affect the performance of intra-industry diversifiers. However, extant diversification studies have primarily focused on the internal changes of intra-firm coordination on resource deployment, while glossing over the external changes of inter-firm coordination on competitive interactions. Our first study of this project is motivated to settle these controversies. We merge the theoretical insights from MMC and diversification research to tackle several problematic assumptions and omissions, which have begotten conceptual calamity and empirical inconsistency regarding the intra-industry D-P linkage. First, extant diversification research implicitly assumes that a focal firm will not provoke competitive reactions from its rivals as it diversifies in an industry. Second, researchers assume that, even if competitive provocation occurs, the intra-industry diversifiers may buffer themselves from the rivals’ retaliation flawlessly. We argue that these assumptions are unrealistic because few firms are capable of shielding themselves from the actions of their competitors. Unfortunately, these unrealistic assumptions have engendered a critical conceptual deficiency—failure to recognize the inherent coupling between a diversifier’s adjustment of internal resources and its rearrangement of external competition. In the first study of this project, we remove the above unrealistic assumptions. We cross-pollinate diversification and MMC research to develop a holistic portrayal of intra-industry diversification. Firms that overlap in multiple markets strategize to uphold mutual forbearance. Hence, they maintain “coordinated rivalry” as a hybrid relationship that is both competitive and cooperative, or “coopetition”. These relationships form an inter-firm network that mirrors the external coordination among the diversified firms in an industry. Our conceptualization of the duality in diversification allows us to embrace fully inter-firm coordination and interdependence. In the second phase of our first study within this project, we focus on examining the potential interaction between internal configuration and external configuration. We conceptualize this interaction as the linkage between the markets that firms within an industry diversify into. These markets are referred to as categories. Participants in the market, such as producers and audiences, commonly utilize a list of categories to classify, assess, or promote products. Existing research on categories predominantly concentrates on the social properties and connectivity of a category, aiming to explain why a category is employed to describe a product. However, categories often cluster together, and little is known about the impact of this clustering on the representation of a category in a product's description. In this article, we define the easily replicable clustering of categories as a category bundle and introduce a novel measure, bundle congruence, to assess the compatibility of the category bundle. We argue that audiences utilize bundle congruence to select or exclude categories. In markets where audiences play a dominant role in product categorization, the bundle congruence of a category in a product's description increases the likelihood of its usage for that product. Furthermore, the overall bundle congruence of a product enhances its economic returns. Due to data availability issue, our arguments cannot be tested in the financial industries. However, our arguments are supported by an empirical analysis of feature films produced in North America. Our examination of the interplay between the internal and external configurations of diversification not only enhances our understanding of the structure of the category system but also offers a fresh explanation for the persistence of category-spanning, despite previous findings suggesting that products that straddle categories are susceptible to financial penalties. Our second study in this project seeks to examine the level of influence exerted by a firm on its competitors, commonly known as the Dunbar's number of the firm. By conducting a thorough analysis, we aim to refine this number and determine if other firms within the strategic group of this particular firm can be regarded as a parsimonious approximation of the Dunbar number. To address this research question, we integrate the literature on optimal distinctiveness (OD).The optimal distinctiveness (OD) literature proposes a focal firm is able to differentiate away from the industry prototype to obtain competitive advantage, whereas the strategic group (SG) literature suggests a focal firm conforms to the group prototype. The study proposes a cross-level perspective to integrate the two bodies of literature. We theorize that a focal firm’s performance is mutually determined by the interplay of between-group distinctiveness (BGD, defined as the extent of differentiation between the strategic groups with which the focal firm affiliates) and within-group distinctiveness (WGD, defined as the extent of differentiation between the focal firm and other firms of the strategic group with which the focal firm affiliates), because the drivers of legitimacy and competition vary across the two levels. In other words, firms must tradeoff its strategic positions at the between-group and within-group levels. In our empirical analyses, we developed a novel method based on the algorithm of fuzzy clustering to construct BGD and WGD. In addition, we employed an efficient GMM model with three instrumental variables to address the endogenous concern. In further support of the cross-level perspective, analysis results show that the classic argument of “optimal distinctiveness” only applies to the firms which affiliate with more than one strategic group, and a focal firm’s perception on the “optimal position” within an industry is determinant by the number of strategic group memberships.

We pinpoint two issues in the extant studies on diversification and multimarket competition: observation interdependence, and intertemporal correlation of dependent variable. We pioneer a method to address these empirical issues.

We are the first to propose the adoption of spatial econometric models in diversification research. We argue that this technique can be instrumental for not only diversification research but also other studies in strategic management.

We are the first to introduce the Dunbar’s number to the literature of strategic management. We pioneer the theoretical conceptualization of the organizational Dunbar’s number—an instrumental index for policymakers to gauge industrial competition intensities and protect consumers.

11505420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505420.value: We present and validate the dual nature of firm diversification, which is evident in both internal and external dimensions. The internal dimension pertains to the resources and behaviors of a diversified firm, while the external dimension encompasses those of the firm's competitors across various markets. Through our empirical analyses, we establish the existence of these two dimensions of diversification. Furthermore, we shed light on and empirically demonstrate the interplay between these dimensions. Our findings indicate that this interplay can be examined through the concept of "categories," which represent the markets into which firms diversify. We provide evidence that these categories are interconnected, and the linkage among certain categories is so strong that we refer to them as "category bundles." We have identified two key issues in existing studies on diversification and multimarket competition: observation interdependence and intertemporal correlation of the dependent variable. We address these empirical challenges by introducing a novel method -- spatial econometric models. We argue that this technique not only holds significance for diversification research but also has implications for other studies in the field of strategic management. We are the first to introduce Dunbar's number to the literature on strategic management. We reframe Dunbar's number as a firm's scope of impact on its rivals. We incorporate strategic group analysis to decipher Dunbar's number, which serves as a valuable index for policymakers to assess the intensity of industrial competition and safeguard consumer interests.

11505420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505420.value: The Dunbar's number signifies the extent of a company's competitive influence on its rivals. The data requirement for determining the Dunbar's number is extensive. Subsequent research can employ various techniques, such as surveys and data simulation. The utilization of strategic groups as a means to measure the Dunbar's number is an innovative approach, and further investigation is warranted to compare theoretical methodologies in identifying the Dunbar's number (e.g., cognitive mapping of CEOs, strategic group analysis, and data simulation).

11505420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505420.value: Our project investigates the performance impact of intra-industry diversification. The existing literature on diversification emphasizes the synergies that arise from the allocation of resources within a firm across different markets, which we refer to as the internal configuration. Another line of research, known as Multimarket contact (MMC) research, examines the performance implications of competitive dynamics between firms across markets, which we refer to as the external configuration. However, despite the coexistence of these two configurations in firm diversification, MMC research rarely intersects with diversification studies, resulting in biased results regarding the linkage between diversification and performance (D-P). Our project bridges these two research streams and conceptualize the duality in diversification. To achieve this, we employ spatial econometrics to address two critical empirical issues in existing studies on D-P linkage and MMC—omitted variable bias and observation dependence. Through our analysis, we uncover the performance effects of both configurations and their interaction in the general insurance industry.

11505920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505920.value: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) was mandated by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX) to inspect all auditors that audit companies registered with the Securities Exchange Commission (SEC), including non-US auditors of SEC registered companies located abroad. Recent studies show that the foreign clients (SEC registered or not) of the PCAOB inspected foreign auditors all exhibit improved accounting quality post PCAOB inspections. The proposed study aims to exploit the international inspection program introduced by the PCAOB to examine the relation between accounting quality and the use of accounting measures in debt covenants. The evidence from extant studies regarding the relation between accounting quality and the use of accounting covenants in debt contract is rather puzzling. While some studies find that poor accounting quality is associated with a reduction of accounting covenants in debt contracts (e.g., Costello and Whittenberg-Moerman 2011; Chen, He, Ma and Stice 2016), other studies find poor accounting (audit) quality increases accounting covenants (Kim, Song and Zhang 2011; Robin, Wu and Zhang 2017). The mixed evidence is largely caused by the positive relation between a firm’s accounting quality and its financial health. Compared to financially distressed firms, financially healthy firms are less likely to use covenants in order to preserve their flexibility in investing and financing. As a result, it is likely to find financially distressed firms with lower accounting quality associated with more use of accounting covenants, although the contracting value of poor quality accounting information should be lower. The PCAOB international inspections provide a shock to the accounting quality of the foreign clients of PCAOB inspected foreign auditors. Using a difference-in-difference (DiD) design, we will utilize PCAOB international inspections as a shock to the accounting quality of the foreign clients of PCAOB inspected foreign auditors and provide causal evidence on the relationship between accounting quality and accounting covenant use in debt contracts. Armstrong, Guay and Weber (2010) point out that there is a lack of understanding regarding the role and design of accounting covenants and call for more research on how attributes of financial reports affect features of the covenant package such as the number of accounting covenants. In addition, the findings from this study will provide policy implications regarding the consequence of strengthened regulation of the audit profession. This study will also add to our understanding about cross-country variations in the use of accounting covenants. 2002沙賓法授权成立了美国公众公司会计监督委员会来对所有美国上市公司的会计师事务所进行审查，即使是國外的會計師事務所也不例外。近期研究发现经由美国公众公司会计监督委员会审查的外国會計師事務所在被审查之后，他们客户的会计质量都有显著提高。本研究打算利用美国公众公司会计监督委员会的国际审查计划来研究会计质量对债务契约中会计衡量指标的使用的影响。 现有研究发现会计质量和债务契约中会计衡量指标的使用之间的关系非常不确定。有的研究发现会计质量的提高会增加会计衡量指标的使用(e.g., Costello and Whittenberg-Moerman 2011; Chen, He, Ma and Stice 2016)， 但也有研究表明会计质量的提高会减少会计衡量指标在债务契约中的使用 (Kim, Song and Zhang 2011; Robin, Wu and Zhang 2017)。原因是公司的会计质量和財務健康往往是正相关的。財務健康的公司倾向于在债务契约中少使用限制性的指标，这样它们在投资和融资的时候更有灵活性。所以在财务上有困难的公司反而会更多的使用这些限制性的指标，但它们的会计质量其实相对较低。 美国公众公司会计监督委员会的国际审查计划对受审查的外国會計師事務所的客户的会计质量有个正的冲击。我们因此可以使用差異中的差異的研究方法， 来研究会计质量是否和债务契约中会计衡量指标的使用有因果关系。Armstrong, Guay and Weber (2010)指出我们目前的研究对会计衡量指标在债务契约中的作用以及对债务契约的设计的影响是十分有限的，我们应该对此提供更多的证据。而且本研究对审计行业加强法规约束之后的后果也能提供一些参考依据。本研究提供的证据也有助于理解为什么不同国家之间会计契约使用的程度会有所不同。

11505920.label: Realisation of objectives
11505920.value: The first two objectives are realized and significant results are obtained. For the third and forth objectives, we do not find any significant results. Particularly, for objective 4, the sample size is too small to obtain expected result. However, for the first two objectives, as explained in the mid progress report, Shroff (2020) publishes similar results (Shroff, N. (2020). Real effects of PCAOB international inspections. The Accounting Review, 95(5), 399-433). Therefore, we added two more objectives to the project. However, the results are not good for those two objectives. We therefore conduct another research to change the setting from PCAOB to the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) to examine bank loans.

11505920.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505920.value: For the PCAOB project: Our empirical analyses reveal that PCAOB international inspections lead to an increase in the use of accounting covenants. In addition, this effect is more pronounced for firms in countries with a higher level of credit rights protection and audit professional development. Furthermore, we find that PCAOB international inspections do not lead significant changes in the use of general covenants and secured loans, but can lead to a significant decrease in loan spread. However, we do not find any evidence that PCAOB inspection increases the use of accounting covenants for public bonds. In addition, we examine the effect of PCAOB inspections on the accounting covenants issued by foreign firms to the US investors. Due to the small sample size, we do not find any significant results. For the FCPA project: Using a stacked difference-in-differences analysis on a large sample of international syndicated loans, we show that the extraterritorial enforcement of the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) in foreign OECD countries leads to a reduction in the borrowings from US banks by firms in those countries. The reduction effect is stronger for borrowing firms with operations in high-corruption countries, those in countries with a greater cultural difference or geographical distance from the US, or those in countries with greater credit availability. In addition, the reduction is concentrated among US lead banks and US non-relationship banks. Furthermore, we find that domestic banks in foreign OECD countries that experience FCPA enforcement capture a portion of the market share previously held by US banks. Finally, we show that FCPA enforcement is associated with a decline in US banks’ short-term operating performance.

11505920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505920.value: The FCPA project is quite comprehensive and ready for submission. We plan to submit it to journal of accounting and economics soon. After submission, we will further develop the project based on reviewers' comments. The PCAOB project has low potential given that similar results are already published by Shroff (2020).

11505920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505920.value: In our study, we wanted to see how a US law called the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) affects borrowing by companies in other countries. We found that when the FCPA is enforced in certain foreign countries, companies in those countries borrow less money from US banks. We noticed that this reduction in borrowing is more significant for companies that operate in countries with a lot of corruption, countries that are far away or have different cultures compared to the United States, or countries where it's easier to get loans. Additionally, the decrease in borrowing mostly happens with US banks that are leading the loans or don't have a strong existing relationship with the borrowing companies. Interestingly, we also found that local banks in the affected countries are able to attract more borrowing business from the companies because of the FCPA enforcement. Lastly, we discovered that the enforcement of the FCPA has a negative impact on the short-term performance of US banks. Overall, our findings show that companies in foreign countries are less likely to borrow money from US banks because borrowing from US banks can increase their chances of being investigated related to following the FCPA rules.

11506320.value: 主流金融機構的可持續發展變革：一個混合方法的制度分析

11506320.label: Project Objectives
11506320.value: To contribute to a more systematic understanding of how organizations integrate practices that contradict prevalent values and norms. To contribute to a better knowledge of how the financial sector can be a more positive force for societal development.

11506320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506320.value: As the engine of market capitalism, the financial sector has played an important role in fueling economic growth. Increasingly, a global movement towards sustainable development and pro-social considerations have permeated the financial sector. A variety of novel organizational forms have emerged, such as socially responsible investment funds (Yan, Ferraro, and Almandoz, 2018), micro-finance organizations (Zhao and Wry, 2016), and community banks (Almandoz, 2012), all of which innovatively utilize finance as a means to achieve pro-social missions. However, we still lack a systematic understanding of how established, incumbent, and mainstream financial organizations integrate pro-social considerations, such as environmental, social, and ethical factors. The call for sustainable development has already happened in the mainstream financial sector. In 2018, The CEO of Blackrock, arguably the largest and most powerful asset managers worldwide, warned business leaders that if they wish to receive support from Blackrock, they must do good for society, not just enrich their shareholders. Hence, a fundamental cultural and institutional change is unfolding in front of the world. Despite the need for a change, it is not obvious how to overcome the organizational barriers in this mission. To address this gap, I adopt an institutional lens to analyze the integration of sustainability concerns with existing values, norms, and practices of mainstream financial organizations. Institutional theory is particularly apt at analyzing cultural aspects of practice emergence, organizational form, and institutional orders. Given the emergent nature of the phenomenon, I opt for a qualitative method approach to identify key actors in the field and to understand the evolving dynamics in the 1st phase. In the 2nd phase, I will leverage insights gained from the 1st phase to construct panel data describing organizations that integrate sustainability factors for regression analysis. I expect to generate 3 or more papers at top tier management journals from this project. This research will make a few contributions to extant literature. First, it will enhance our theoretical understanding of organizational change, using the financial sector as a setting, which is critical for finance and other sectors to play a more positive role in the society. Second, it will explore the moral capacity of finance in concrete terms, such as how organizations can be sustainable at the practice level, and hence contribute to managerial practice. 金融機構作為市場經濟的重要引擎，為經濟發展做出了重要貢獻，但社會對於可持續的發展越來越高，也對金融機構提出了新的挑戰。當前的文獻，對於新型金融機構的崛起，例如社會責任投資基金(Yan, Ferraro, and Almandoz, 2019),小微貸款(Zhao and Wry, 2016)和社區銀行(Almandoz, 2012)有着豐富的論述，但對於傳統主流金融機構如何轉型卻鮮有論述。我們採用制度理論的視角，來探索主流金融機構如何把可持續發展的概念、規則和價值觀植入到現有的組織文化、實踐和程序中。組織理論，尤其是制度邏輯視角，適合探索組織文化，也適合探究組織和宏觀社會的聯繫。通過這些研究，我們希望以金融機構可持續發展轉型為機遇，探索組織變革的新理論。我們也希望探索以逐利為目的的金融機構，如何發揮超越逐利的作用。

11507120.value: 關系的雙棲性與尋求新的聯盟夥伴

11507120.label: Project Objectives
11507120.value: This study attempts to propose a new concept of relational ambidexterity, defined as a balance between the number of rivals and collaborators in a firm’s alliance portfolio, and also examines its impact on new partner addition. This study aims to apply network pluralism perspective in examining how a firm's configuration of its alliance portfolio may affect its network expansion and consolidation. This study investigates the boundary condition of relational ambidexterity by examining two environmental uncertainties, namely firm-specific uncertainty and market uncertainty, and show their distinct moderation effects.

11507120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507120.value: Firms often form alliances with new partners to maintain organizational viability. However, such endeavor is often constrained by its existing network relationships. This dilemma leads to the following question: How can firms offset the network constraints on new partner addition given that they are embedded in their current alliance networks? This study reconciles this dilemma from the perspective of relationship configuration at the alliance portfolio level. We propose a new concept of relational ambidexterity, defined as a balance between the number of rivals and collaborators in a firm’s alliance portfolio, and further draw on network pluralism literature to contend that relational ambidexterity helps firms offset network constraints, and encourages the addition of new partners. We also argue that the positive effect of relational ambidexterity on new partner addition is attenuated by firm-specific uncertainty, but amplified by market uncertainty. We plan to examine the above hypotheses using both qualitative and quantitative methods. Qualitative approach will help us better understand managers’ considerations behind the configuration of both rivals and collaborators in a firm’s alliance portfolio and the implications arising from it, while quantitative analyses in US. biopharmaceutical industry during 1990 and 2016 will help us examine our hypotheses in a large scale of representative sample firms. Our study will contribute to the literature on network constraint, network expansion, the interplay between cooperation and competition, as well as alliance portfolio management. Findings from this project will help firm managers to strategically configure their alliance portfolio for new partner addition and exploratory innovation.

11507320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507320.value: 代理人冲突，投资和企业的演化

11507320.label: Project Objectives
11507320.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to develop a tractable and fully dynamic model to study the agency problem of control-ownership wedge in a realistic corporate setting where the controlling shareholder, in addition to her stealing technology, make a battery of corporate decisions on half of the firm. Specifically, we build our model in a continuous-time framework for which many powerful techniques can be applied to solve the model and generate economic implications in a transparent manner. Based on the theoretical model developed, we will quantify both the direct and the indirect cost of the agency problem arising from the control-ownership wedge under incomplete markets, and then compare the results to those under the complete-market case as well as to what are documented in the literature. Pursuing the tractability of the model, we will thoroughly examine the the distorted corporate decision making at the presence of control-ownership wedge. Given the investment-specific technology shock, we will also thoroughly examine the entanglement between controlling shareholder's investment policies and her strategy on taking the market portfolio taking into account the agency problem. We will study the time-varying wedges between i) marginal q vs. average q, ii) private qs from the controlling shareholder's perspective vs. qs from the perspective of the firm, iii) qs with agency problem vs. qs without agency problem, iv) qs under incomplete market vs. under complete market. These dynamics, as well as dynamics of qs themselves, will highlight the cost of control-ownership wedge in terms of the valuation of invested capital. We will also study several variations of the model to reinforce the main argument, and to understand the roles of different model elements, e.g., autarky vs. restart as the controlling shareholder's outside options; TFP shocks vs. investment-specific shocks for the capital accumulation process. Since only transitory shocks are involved in the baseline model, we will furthermore study an extend version of the model for changes in the controlling shareholder's policies at the presence of persistent productivity shocks.

11507320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507320.value: The efficiency of corporate decisons can be compromised by various frictions. One important source of financial market frictions involves agency problems. Corporation in many countries are run by controlling shareholders whose cash flow rights in the firm are substantially smaller than their control rights (La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, and Shleifer al (1999), Claessens, Djankov, and Lang (2000)). The separation of ownership and control allows controlling shareholders to pursue private benefits at the cost of other investors. While there are already extensive empirical studies on the economic and financial consequences resulting from the divergence between control rights and cash-flow rights, theoretical treatment of this critical agency friction lags behind. In this project, we introduce a tractable stochastic equilibrium framework to study both the direct and indirect costs that are resulting from the divergence between control rights and cash-flow rights as well as the associated distortions in corporate decisions. In our setting, the controlling shareholder makes all decisions on behalf of the firm and steals from the firm, while she is only entitled to a (fixed) fraction of the firm's cash flow. Our model yields closed-form characterizations of the controlling shareholder's corporate strategies which suggest that she over-invests, is over-exposed to the market, and liquidates the firm earlier. Due to the premise of market incompleteness, we need to solve the value functions for the controlling sharehoder and the firm numerically, by which we will show that the indirect cost to the firm resulting from the controlling shareholder's distorted policies substantially dominates the direct cost of stealing. Specifically, the controlling shareholder effectively own the firm in the limiting case when firm's liquidity approaches infinity. We will examine different investment technology and outside option for the controlling shareholder to make a robust argument. Since only transitory shocks are involved in the baseline model, we will furthermore study an extend version of the model for changes in the controlling shareholder's corporate policies at the presence of persistent productivity shocks. Overall, this project will advance our understanding on the corporate and financial consequences of the control-ownership wedge from a theoretical perspective. 公司决策的效率可能会因各种摩擦而受损。金融市场摩擦的一个重要来源涉及代理人问题。在许多国家/地区，公司由控股股东经营，而这些控股股东的现金流量权远小于其控股权。所有权和控制权的分离允许控股股东以其他投资者为代价追求私人利益。尽管已经对控制权和现金流量权之间的差异所产生的经济和金融后果进行了广泛的实证研究，但这种关键代理摩擦的理论处理却滞后了。 在这个项目中，我们引入一个易于处理的随机均衡框架以研究由于控制权和现金流量权之间的差异导致的公司决策失真的直接和间接成本。在我们的模型中，控股股东代表公司做出所有决定并从公司那里窃取部分收益，而她仅仅承担由其现金流量权决定的那部分损失。通过求解分析控股股东的行为我们发现她过度投资，过度暴露于市场并过早的让公司破产清算。通过对对控股股东和公司的价值函数的数值解，我们发现控股股东扭曲的决策导致的企业间接成本大大超过了因窃取造成的直接成本。 在论证过程中我们将考虑不同的投资技术和控股股东若干种外部选择权。我们还将考虑存在持续性生产力冲击的情形并将其作为模型的扩展版本。总体而言，该项目将从理论角度加深我们对控制权和所有权不匹配所产生后果的理解

rows: One of the main objectives of this project is to develop a tractable and fully dynamic model to study the agency problem of control-ownership wedge in a realistic corporate setting where the controlling shareholder, in addition to her stealing technology, make a battery of corporate decisions on half of the firm. Specifically, we build our model in a continuous-time framework for which many powerful techniques can be applied to solve the model and generate economic implications in a transparent manner.

Based on the theoretical model developed, we will quantify both the direct and the indirect cost of the agency problem arising from the control-ownership wedge under incomplete markets, and then compare the results to those under the complete-market case as well as to what are documented in the literature.

Pursuing the tractability of the model, we will examine the the distorted corporate decision making at the presence of control-ownership wedge. Given the investment-specific technology shock, we will also thoroughly examine the entanglement between controlling shareholder's investment policies and her strategy on taking the market portfolio taking into account the agency problem.

We will study the time-varying wedges between i) marginal q vs. average q, ii) private qs from the controlling shareholder's perspective vs. qs from the perspective of the firm after excluding the private benefit paid to the controlling shareholder, iii) qs with agency problem vs. qs without agency problem, iv) qs under incomplete market vs. under complete market. These dynamics, as well as dynamics of qs themselves, will highlight the cost of control-ownership wedge in terms of the valuation of invested capital.

We will also study several variations of the model to reinforce the main argument, and to understand the roles of different model elements: i) TFP shocks vs. investment-specific shocks for the capital accumulation process; ii) restart with a smaller firm vs. retire as a Merton consumer as the controlling shareholder's outside options; iii) only transitory shocks vs. both transitory shocks and the presence of persistent productivity shocks. 11507320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507320.value: The paper provides a systematic analysis on the financial and welfare implications of corporate control frictions. The dynamic stochastic model used in the paper features control-ownership wedge where outside investors have imperfect control over the decisions of their firm, and a rich opportunity set available to the firm that allows it to trade unconstrainedly in financial markets. The model makes numerous predictions. A deterioration of the protection for outside investors initially depresses but later on raises the firm's dividend payouts. The firm's controlling agent exploits the control friction by over-investing and taking more aggressive positions in the stock market. The empire building motive of the controlling agent at a lower degree of investor protection may actually drive up the firm valuation. The controlling agent generally gains from a lower degree of investor protection and the implied utility gains are higher for a lower investment risk, a lower degree of risk aversion, a lower equity risk premium, and a more stringent asset allocation constraint. The paper further shows that more frequent auditing or internal inspection for stealing leads to a higher cash-flow right chosen by the controlling agent.

11507320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507320.value: While the paper generates numerical empirical predictions. In the paper, I provide evidences documented in existing literature that support some of the predictions and I leave the test of other predictions to future work.

11507320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507320.value: We analyze the financial and welfare implications of corporate control friction and its endogenization from the lens of a dynamic stochastic model. The model makes numerous predictions. Following a deterioration of investor protection, firm valuation may rise; welfare loss of outside investors is particularly large when the firm is in financial distress; the controlling agents' welfare gain is lower for a higher investment risk, a higher degree of risk aversion, or a less constrained opportunity set for the firm. A more frequent auditing induces a lower control-ownership wedge. We provide evidences that support some of the predictions.

11507420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507420.value: Firms these days invest a lot in IT security but the effect has been mixed – while firms are more informed and well-prepared than in the past, breach incidents continue to occur. It is also an on-going process for firms to assess the IT security risk that they face. One way that they can discover potential major weaknesses of their IT infrastructure is through internal audits of the firm’s functional IT assets (data, processes, systems, etc.). Alternatively, firms may also learn about their potential IT weaknesses through breach incidents that have occurred. They represent the preventive and reactive approach to discover weaknesses in IT assets. The discoveries of major weaknesses have severe impact on how we manage our IT assets, and directly affect board-level and management-level IT governance structure and decisions. For example, major weaknesses may reveal ineffective IT leadership in the organization. In other cases, it indicates an inappropriate attitude towards the management of IT assets. Therefore, prior literature has often examined the impact of IT material weaknesses (ITMW) on IT governance, as well as the subsequent impact of changes in IT governance on ITMW. However, prior literature often takes the internal control viewpoint, i.e., the major IT weaknesses are discovered through using preventive approach. So far, there has been limited literature that examines how the reactive approach affects IT governance and vice versa. We propose to fill the gap in the literature by examining the interrelationship between breach incidents and IT governance, along with the interrelationship between ITMW and IT governance. By doing so, we contrast the interplay of the different approaches of IT system weakness discovery and IT governance. Our study has broad normative implications on how we should manage our IT assets. Currently, firms and industries are spending millions of dollars on auditing IT controls. One criticism is that such an approach decouples firms from addressing cybersecurity issues that are genuinely relevant to them. Instead, firms focus on achieving routine self-assessment exercises. Our study can shed light on whether practicing such IT audit paradigm is indeed effective, or whether a more market-based approach should be embraced. Furthermore, there is also debate about whether board-level decision-makers truly care about cybersecurity. By contrasting the impact of preventive and reactive approach-led incidents, we aim to learn more about the predispositions of firms on cybersecurity issues. 如今，企業在IT安全方面投入的資金，但效果卻參差不齊；甚至企業比過去更了解情況和準備充分，數據事件事件卻持續發生。公司需要持續地評估其面臨的IT安全風險。對公司功能性IT資產（數據，流程，系統等）的內部審核是發現IT架構地潛在重要缺陷的其中一種方法。或者，企業也可以通過發生的數據變化事件了解其潛在的IT缺陷。它們代表了發現IT資產缺陷的預防和被動方法。 重要缺陷的揭露會深刻影響IT資產的管理方式，並直接影響董事會和領導的IT治理結構和決策。例如，重要缺陷表明組織中IT領導能力低下，或者對IT資產的管理態度不當。因此，過去文獻經常檢查IT重大缺陷對IT治理的影響，以及IT治理變更對IT重大缺陷的後續影響。然而，現有文獻經常採用內部控制的觀點，即，通過使用預防方法發現IT重大缺陷。到目前為止，很少有文獻研究反應式方法如何影響IT治理，反之亦然。 我們建議通過檢查數據垂直事件與IT治理之間的相互關係以及IT重大缺陷與IT治理之間的相互關係來關聯文獻中的空白。通過這樣做，我們對比了IT系統缺陷的發現和IT治理的不同方法之間的相互作用。 我們的研究對我們應如何管理IT資產具有廣泛的意義。當前，公司和行業在IT審計上花費了數百萬美元。一種批評是，這種方法使公司無法處理與他們真正相關的網絡安全問題，公司應專注於實踐例行的自我評估。我們的研究可以揭示實踐這種IT審核範式是否確實有效，或者是否應該採用基於市場的方法。盡可能，關於董事會級決策者是否真正關心網絡安全也存在爭議。通過對比預防性和反應性方法導致的事件的影響，我們預測更多地了解公司在網絡安全問題上的可能性。

11507420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507420.value: This study investigates how firms' responses to ITMWs impact information systems governance (ISG) through IT strategies. We analyze over 4,000 U.S. firm-year observations, and deepen the understanding between ITMW, ISG and cybersecurity. This study aims to explore how ISG interacts with firms’ IT strategies, such as IT outsourcing, in addressing ITMWs and how security awareness moderates this interaction. Enhanced top management’s security awareness, in line with the deliverer responsibility of Bright Internet principles (Lee 2015; Lee et al. 2018) is seen as beneficial for the improvement of ISG and the achievement of Bright Internet goals by preventing the firm's IT misuse in cyberattacks. The results show that firms suffering ITMWs increase IT outsourcing for operation while reducing IT outsourcing for maintenance. These findings align with earlier observations that firms opt for rapid solutions to IT challenges (Benaroch and Chernobai 2017), viewing outsourcing as a means to mitigate reputation risks or lower compliance costs. In the second stage of analysis, we evaluate the effects of different IT outsourcing strategies on ISG. The results suggest that IT maintenance outsourcing stimulates more improvement in ISG than IT operation outsourcing. This finding lends support to the argument that selective outsourcing is better than total outsourcing because firms can retain some control over their IT and improve their IT capability by gaining best practices from the IT vendors (Aubert et al. 2012; Aydin and Bakker 2008). Additionally, the non-significant effect of operation outsourcing on improving governance could be attributed to its focus on short-term operational efficiencies rather than on building long-term IT capabilities and board-level expertise. Furthermore, operation outsourcing might dilute the firm's control over strategic IT functions, limiting opportunities for internal knowledge accumulation and expertise development essential for governance enhancement. Finally, firms with a higher level of security awareness increase their IT maintenance outsourcing. This complements the earlier stages of our analysis, which indicated a preference for operational outsourcing in immediate response to ITMWs, albeit at the expense of maintenance activities. The shift towards maintenance outsourcing among security-aware firms suggests a strategic pivot to bolstering internal capabilities and resilience, reflecting a long-term vision for ISG enhancement. This strategic alignment underlines the critical role of security awareness in steering firms toward more sustainable governance practices.

11507420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507420.value: Future studies could further the discussion by examining whether and to what extent ISG plays a mediating role between different types of IT strategies and ITMWs and investigating the subsequent effects of firms’ remediation efforts by considering the possible interactions between different IT strategies (e.g., IT outsourcing and internal IT investment). Last but not least, this study mainly focuses on the aggregate effect of different ISG mechanisms on ITMWs. Future studies may want to investigate the synergetic effects between different governance mechanisms and investigate under what conditions such synergies become more effective.

11507420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507420.value: This study seeks to understand how significant security incidents (e.g., data breaches, hacking attempts, or system malfunctions) or problems within a company's information technology (IT) systems (ITMW) could affect the way that firms manage IT (IT governance). The study also seeks to understand the role of IT strategies used to address ITMW, as well as whether the firm's security awareness affects the process. The results show that ITMW improves IT governance through a specific type of IT outsourcing that focuses on leveraging external expertise while concentrating on core activities, thereby maintaining system reliability and quality. Hence, we highlight IT maintenance outsourcing as pivotal for fostering greater governance involvement. Furthermore, we find that a firm's increased security awareness contributes positively to the improvement of IT governance following ITMW.

11508120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11508120.value: 使用定价在搜索平台上吸引客户的理论和实证分析

11508120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508120.value: 在旅游网站（例如Expedia.com和Trip.com）上，消费者可以搜索无数卖家，以查找有关产品的信息，例如酒店和航班。要进行预订，消费者必须单击搜索结果页面上的卖方链接，该页面上只有信息摘要可用于产品列表中的条目。该搜索结果页面上最突出的信息是标价或基本产品的最低价格；例如，标价可能显示不可退款的单人间或经济舱机票的价格。该标价可能与消费者最终支付的最终价格有所不同，因为基本产品可能已经售罄（容量限制），或者消费者可能想购买价格更高的产品，或者包含附加组件，例如早餐，互联网，或停车（附加定价）。该项目旨在研究显示在搜索结果页面上的标价对消费者的点击决定以及最终对他们的购买决定的影响。了解了这种影响后，我们将确定竞争条件下卖方的最优定价策略。特别是，我们询问所显示的标价是否可以提供有关隐含溢价的信息。为了实现这些研究目标，我们首先分析一个博弈论模型，该模型捕获了该平台上定价游戏的两个主要特征：容量约束和附加定价。然后，我们使用来自主要国际旅行网站的个人级别点击流数据，以经验方式测试理论发现。该项目中的发现将为卖方在搜索平台上提供实用的指导，以指导他们在搜索结果页面上向消费者显示哪些价格，以提高点击率和转化率。最后，除了其他信息（例如客户评分）以外，我们还提供了有关平台如何根据卖家的标价对卖家进行排名的见解。

11508620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508620.value: Portfolio risk measurement has been an important computational problem in financial engineering and risk management, especially when the portfolio involves complex financial derivatives and/or sophisticated mathematical models. Under these settings computer simulation is usually required in portfolio reevaluation, and a central research question is then how to improve the computational efficiency of the risk estimation via simulation. In this proposal, we propose new simulation methods for portfolio risk measurement, based on machine learning techniques. The main theme of these methods is to borrow the ideas behind the balance of the trade-off between exploration and exploitation in machine learning techniques to guide the allocation of simulation budgets for portfolio risk measurement, thus increasing the efficiency of the risk estimators. In particular, we consider several important classes of risk measures and plan to develop tailored-made methods by examine carefully their unique structures. In addition, we plan to study the statistical properties of these machine learning methods, including their consistency and central limit theorems, providing theoretical supports and better understanding of the insights of these methods. 投資組合風險度量是金融工程與風險管理中的一個重要計算問題。當投資組合包含複雜金融衍生品或是設計複雜數學模型的時候，如何解決此計算問題變得尤爲關鍵。在此情形之下，計算機模擬被廣汎用於投資組合風險度量。其中，一個核心的問題在於如何提高風險估計的計算效率。 在此項目中，我們基於機器學習技術提出新的用於投資組合風險度量的模擬方法。我們的主題圍繞如何利用機器學習算法中取得探索-利用之間平衡的思想，去指導如何把模擬預算更高效得分配，從而提高估計量的準確性。其中，我們考慮了幾類常用的風險度量，並提出具有針對性的模擬方法。此外，我們還將研究所提出方法的統計性質，包括一致性和中心極限定理，從而為此類方法提供理論依據。

11508620.value: All three objectives have been successfully achieved. In particular, for the first objective, we have proposed an upper-confidence-bound approach to estimating coherent risk measures, which can be generally written as the maximum of means taken over a set of probability distributions. For the second objective, we have successfully developed machine learning methods for estimating several popular risk measures, including conditional value-at-risk, value-at-risk, and probability of large losses. In addition, we have incorporated the maximum mean estimator into Markov decision processes, and proposed a new algorithm with theoretical guarantee on its consistency.

11508620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508620.value: 1. We developed a new upper-confidence-bound method to estimate coherent risk measures.The main result is summarized in a working paper titled "An upper confidence bound approach to estimating the maximum mean". This paper is currently under Reject & Resubmit for Operations Research. 2. We developed machine learning techniques to estimate popular risk measures used in finance, such as Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), Value-at-Risk (VaR), and probability of large losses. Some of the results appears my PhD student Dr Qi Liang's thesis, and in a paper titled "Nested Simulation for Conditional Value-at-Risk with Discrete Losses" that is published in Asia-Pacific Journal of Operational Research. 3. We incorporated maximum mean estimators into Markov decision processes and proposed a new algorithm with theoretical guarantee. The main result of this part is summarized in a working paper titled "Solving Markov Decision Processes via Largest-size Average Estimator". Currently this paper is under review with Journal of Machine Learning Research.

11508620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508620.value: In the current project, our investigation has largely been focused on the upper confidence bound approach. For future research, it would be meaningful and interesting to study other approaches such as successive elimination.

11508620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508620.value: This project focused on developing new methods for estimating financial risks using machine learning techniques. We successfully achieved three main objectives. First, we developed a new upper-confidence-bound method to estimate coherent risk measures. Second, we developed machine learning techniques to estimate popular risk measures used in finance, such as Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), Value-at-Risk (VaR), and probability of large losses. These measures help financial institutions and investors understand and quantify the potential risks associated with their investments or portfolios. Third, we incorporated maximum mean estimators into Markov decision processes, which are mathematical models used to make decisions in uncertain situations. This led to the creation of a new algorithm with proven consistency, meaning it reliably produces accurate results over time. Overall, this project has advanced the field of risk management by introducing new, more accurate methods for estimating and analyzing financial risks, potentially leading to better decision-making in finance and investment.

11509220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11509220.value: 正如眾所周知的口號“位置，位置，位置”反映的決定商業成功的因素，地理位置被認為是公司運營成功的最有影響力的因素之一。但是，最近的市場研究指出，公司位置策略的有效性不僅取決於的地理位置，還取決於業務的管理方式。在當前的研究中，我們的目的是走出地理位置的局限，研究營業地點和企業治理機制的共同影響。我們的研究關注特許經營，在此行業中許多特許經營授權商（例如，星巴克，7-11，漢堡王）採用了區域集群策略，即將特許經營網點集中在地理上的特定區域，以實現其係統擴展目標。儘管區域集群化可以增加品牌知名度、降低監控成本並改善對知識和其他無形資源的獲取，但它也可能引起市場侵佔並導致特許經營店的終止。因此，本研究項目的是研究特許人如何對具有不同屬性的集群採用適當的治理機制，以提高特許經營店的生存率。 該項目主要研究如下幾個問題。首先，如果區域集群對加盟商既有利因素又有不利影響，那麼區域集群對加盟商生存率的總體影響是什麼？其次，我們將研究經營店層（即總部距離），主加盟商層（即銷售點共用所有權）和特許經營系統層（即由特許人主導的社交活動）三種特許經營治理機制，並對每種機制與區域集群對特許經營店生存率的共同作用進行實證檢驗。最後，我們將進一步探討治理機制的調節作用如何在具有獨特地理和結構特徵的集群之間變化。根據我們的發現，我們將對公司應如何針對不同集群屬性選擇適合治理機制提供可行的見解。 我們將使用申請的研究基金來獲取至少50家公司在過去的10年（2008-2018年）的特許經營披露文檔（FDD）。我們將從FDD中提取有關美國境內所有特許經營網點的數量，位址和所有者的資訊，然後使用Quantum Geographical Information System（QGIS）2和R軟件包將其轉換為地理編碼數據（即經度和緯度）。我們還將採用半參數Cox比例風險回歸方法來實證檢驗我們的假設。

11509220.label: Realisation of objectives
11509220.value: 1. To identify the distinctive features of regional clustering of franchised outlets, in comparison to regional clustering of independent firms identified in extant strategy research. Realization of research objectives and related research activities: We have conducted a thorough literature review in related disciplines, including the economics literature on clustering of independent firms (e.g., Porter 2000), marketing literature on franchise clustering and management literature on chain store clustering. Based on the synthesis of these studies, a comparison has been made between regional clustering of independent firms and that of clustering of franchised outlets. This is the conceptual foundation of the entire study and the theoretical base for follow-up studies. We have fulfilled this objective 100%. 2. To examine the overall effects of regional clustering on franchisee survival rate. Realization of research objectives and related research activities: First, a conceptual framework has been constructed to examine the relationship between the regional clustering and franchised outlet survival rate, as well as the role of governance in moderating this relationship. Second, based on this conceptualization, we constructed our database using multiple sources, including Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDDs), the U.S. Census Bureau, the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, and the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER). Specifically, we used FDDs to identify and record the geographic locations of franchised outlets from their Exhibits and convert the text information (i.e., addresses) to geographic coordinates (i.e., longitude and latitude) using the Bing Maps application programming interface, together with R package “RCurl” and “RJSONIO.” After generating a map of store locations, we delineated the contours of high- and low-density regions using our proposed algorithm, laying a foundation for comparing the efficacy of governance instruments across those regions. For the records concerning outlet failure, we checked whether an individual outlet was open to serve customers in a particular year and recorded whether it survived. We then match-merged those location and survival data with other cluster-, system-, and market-level variables, including governance instruments and control variables obtained from FDDs and the companies’ websites. We acquired economics and demographics data from the U.S. Census Bureau, the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, and the NBER. Compiling and merging those data sources left us with 35,199 observations (8,625 franchised outlets across 18 franchisors) located within the 50 states during a 14-year time window (2008–2021). We then use complementary log-log model to test the hypothesized relationship between clustering and franchised outlets survival. The results show that being in a cluster enhances the likelihood of franchised outlet survival. This research objective has been fulfilled to the extent of 100%. 3. To identify franchise-specific governance mechanisms at outlet-, subgroup-, and system-level, respectively, and conduct empirical tests on the joint effects of each governance mechanism employed and being located in a regional cluster on franchisee survival rate. Realization of research objectives and related research activities: My coauthors and I have coded the outlet-, subgroup-, and system-level governance mechanism variables from three different sources, including Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDDs), Entrepreneur Magazine, and Bonds’ Questionnaires, with the financial aid for research staffs and data purchase from this GRF. We then conducted empirical data analysis on its moderating effects of the main effect between clustering and franchised outlet survival. The results suggest that the governance mechanisms, such as franchisor support, franchisor-directed socialization among franchisees significantly moderate the main effect of clustering on franchised outlet survival. We have realized this research objective 100%. 4. To understand how the moderating effects of governance mechanisms vary across clusters with distinctive cluster (i.e., geographical and structural) properties. Realization of research objectives and related research activities: We have identified two cluster properties, i.e., cluster density and ownership size imbalance. We define cluster density as the number of outlets divided by the total area of the cluster and ownership size imbalance as the standard deviation of the sizes of multiunit franchisees within the cluster so that greater deviation indicated a greater level of ownership size imbalance. We found that cluster density strengthens the moderating effects of aforementioned governance mechanisms and ownership size imbalance weakens them. We have realized this research objective 100%.

11509220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11509220.value: Franchisors use a variety of usually identical governance instruments to manage their franchised outlets and sustain the franchise system. However, as franchises have proliferated into less populated areas, creating a mix of outlets in high-density versus low-density regions, the issues faced by those outlets have diverged. In our research, we call for the deployment of “density-based governance,” in which franchisors can use governance tools that vary at the outlet and/or region level to manage the franchised outlet survival contingent upon whether the outlet is in a high- versus low-density region. Using a unique dataset that includes 35,199 observations (i.e., 8,625 outlets across 18 franchisors over 14 years (2008–2021) in all 50 states in the US) and a novel algorithm-based clustering technique to distinguish high- from low-density regions, our results show a differential effect of key governance tools on outlet survival in high- versus low-density regions. Specifically, we find that the more fragmented the franchisee ownership structure in a region the higher the outlet failure rate in high-density regions. However, such an effect does not hold in low-density regions. Likewise, the more the difficulty in the provision of on-site supervision by the franchisor, the higher the outlet failure rates in both high- and low-density regions. We find a significant moderating effect of business environments that are economically adverse. Specifically, we find that during times of economic adversity the more fragmented the franchised ownership structure the lower the outlet failure rate in high-density regions only, suggesting franchised outlets curb their competitive spirits and behave cooperatively and seek wisdom from each other to improve survival in trying economic times. Outlets in low-density regions face even higher failure rates in adverse economic periods when franchisors have difficulty in providing on-site supervision, which does not appear to be an issue for those located in high-density regions.

11509220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11509220.value: Our research suggests the following avenues of future research development. First, our study considers only two governance instruments: franchisee ownership fragmentation and franchisor on-site supervision. While those two are common mechanisms that can vary at the regional and outlet level, they certainly do not form an exhaustive list. Future research can explore the effects of alternative governance mechanisms, especially when considering the benefits and costs of clustering (Tracey, Heide, and Bell 2014). Second, although our study proxies for the overall competitive intensity between franchisees in a cluster, we did not account for the interaction between franchisees and the focal franchisor. Future research can examine the dynamic relationships between those franchised outlets and the franchisor. For example, how does the entry and exit of outlet competitors affect the efficacy of franchisor governance? Third, our results show the outlet failure rate was higher when franchisors faced more difficulty in on-site supervision in high-density clusters than in low-density regions. Future research can investigate that anomalous reason in more depth. Finally, we conducted our study within two specific industries, and future research can explore whether those effects are generalizable beyond the current context and industry sectors.

11509420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11509420.value: 蘋果和Firefox等主要軟件公司已採用基於平台的技术模型，該模型允許第三方開發人員為平台（例如Web瀏覽器平台）提供應用程序。為了滿足客戶不斷變化的需求並保持競爭力，平台需要進行自我更新（例如，通過更新平台應用程序編程接口（API）或通過更改平台發布過程），同時期望其應用程序能夠響應更新平台更改[1，51]。但是，尚不清楚應用程序是否會根據平台運營商的隱式期望，在時間和質量上進行更新以響應平台級實踐的這些變化。很少有研究檢查這些更改對應用程序更新性能的潛在影響。該項目（以下有兩個研究目標）旨在通過在更新響應速度，頻率，大小和質量方面解釋應用程序更新性能來填補這一空白。 第一個目標是調查平台級實踐（即平台API和平台發布過程）的變化對應用更新性能的影響程度。作為一種技術實踐，在不同級別上提供平台API可以授予應用程序訪問權限以進行集成[26，57]。平台發布過程作為一種策略實踐，對平台發布新版本的方式進行了規範[29]。如前所述，只有在及時且高質量地更新應用程序時，平台級實踐的變化才能被視為增強競爭力的成功舉措。先前的研究很少了解和探索這個關鍵問題。因此，基於邊界資源的觀點[20，21]，我們通過將平台API概念化為技術邊界資源，並將平台發布過程概念化為社交邊界資源，來理論化這些平台變更對應用程序更新性能的影響。 第二個目標是研究應用程序級別的情境特徵在改變平台級別實踐的更改與應用程序更新性能之間的關係中的偶然作用。我們認為，第一個目標中檢驗的關係可能因應用程序而異。基於軟件生態系統中的開發人員參與邏輯[39]，我們討論了兩種邏輯的調節作用，即軟件專業領域中的開發人員專業身份和軟件市場領域中的市場激勵，分别表現為開源身份和市場強度。邊界資源的觀點是在平台級實踐作為邊界資源的有效性的前提下擴展的，它應取決於開發人員如何考慮其平台參與邏輯來激勵他們響應平台更改。

11509420.label: Realisation of objectives
11509420.value: Overall, the three research objectives of this project are well realized through two papers currently under revision at top journals, including Production and Operations Management (POM) and Information Systems Research (ISR). The first study (Manuscript-Synchronized Rapid Release: Examining the Impact of the Rapid-Release Model on App Updates in Software Platforms, currently under major revision at Production and Operations Management), investigates how the adoption of a rapid-release model by the platform influences third-party app update behavior. The second study, titled Third-Party SDK Utilization and Mobile App Market Performance: An Empirical Study from the Boundary-Spanning Perspective, currently under minor revision at ISR, further examines the impact of platform-level practices on app performance. Objective 1: Understand the impacts of changes in platform-level practices on app update performance by drawing on boundary resource theory. The first study mentioned above shows that rapid-release model negatively impacts app update responsiveness. Also, this study draws on the boundary resources perspective to investigate how the rapid-release model of the platform alters the effects of technical and market boundary resources on third-party app update behavior. The findings indicate that the rapid-release model enhances the effect of platform API usage on app update responsiveness and amplifies the negative (positive) impact of customer review volume on app update responsiveness (quality). The second study uses difference-in-differences-style analyses on a longitudinal dataset of 335,958 multi-homing mobile apps released on the Apple App Store and Google Play. It reveals that platform updates of its operating system will mitigate the positive impacts of third-party software development kits (SDKs) on mobile app updates and their market performance. Therefore, the studies based on the project offer significant theoretical and practical implications by clarifying both the direct and indirect impacts of the platform-level practice on third-party app update behavior and outcomes in the platform ecosystem context, offering actionable managerial implications for app developers, platform managers, and third-party SDK providers. Objective 2: Investigate the role of developer professional identity in moderating the impact of changes in platform-level practices on app update performance. This research project, based on the two studies mentioned above, thoroughly examines developer professional identity in mobile app updates and the enhancement of market performance under platform-level conditions. Particularly, the second study mentioned above investigates how a developer’s professional experience within the platform ecosystem affects the performance of app updates, as well as the resulting market outcomes through moderating the influence of the use of development toolkits and the performance of app updates. While the previous literature has shown the advantages of app developers’ experience in app development practices within the range of the platform, this study sheds light on the understudied relationship between app developers and third-party SDKs, enriching our understanding of the two-sided role of mobile app developers as complementors of the platform versus boundary spanning using third-party toolkits. The findings offer guidance to mobile app developers on how to formulate effective development strategies to mitigate the challenges of improving their app market performance and reducing development costs. Considering the notion that experience plays a key role in software development, platform governance designers need to seriously consider the characteristics of developers, which are shaped by their engagement in the platform ecosystem. Objective 3: Investigate the role of market intensity in moderating the impact of changes in platform-level practices on app update performance. This research project, based on the two studies mentioned above, thoroughly examines the role of market intensity in mobile app updates and the enhancement of market performance under platform-level practices. Drawing on the boundary resources perspective, the first study introduces customer review volume as a critical form of market feedback, which can be interpreted as a market boundary resource that facilitates app updates. Specifically, customer review volume (a market boundary resource) is shown to increase the quality of app updates while decreasing their responsiveness. This finding suggests that platform owners could consider selectively displaying customer reviews to mitigate their negative influence on app update responsiveness. By elucidating how customer review volume affects both app update responsiveness and quality, this study provides a holistic view of the roles and effects of boundary resources within the platform ecosystem. It offers an empirical basis for platform owners and third-party developers to better understand the relationship between technical resources and market intensity and their impact on third-party app update behaviors. Overall, the findings from this research project expand upon the existing literature and provide a comprehensive understanding of how platform-level practices influence software development behavior within the platform ecosystem, particularly under the contingencies of app developer identity and mobile market conditions. This understanding not only supports platform owners and developers in optimizing their operations but also contributes to improving the overall efficiency and effectiveness of the platform ecosystem.

11509420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11509420.value: The two studies provide valuable insights into platform-level practices and their impact on mobile app development and market performance. The first study finds that the rapid-release model, which accelerates platform version updates, negatively affects third-party app update responsiveness, as developers take longer to adapt to frequent updates. However, it indirectly enhances responsiveness through increased platform API usage. It also intensifies the effects of customer reviews: a high review volume hinders responsiveness but improves app update quality. The study suggests that platform governance practices, like rapid-release models, significantly influence third-party app behavior by shaping how developers respond to technical and market boundary resources in terms of platform APIs and user reviews. The second study focuses on the performance impact of third-party software development kits (SDKs) in mobile app development. It finds that using more third-party SDKs leads to increased daily active users, a key performance metric. This effect is significant for tool-type SDKs, which function as standalone toolkits, but not for platform-type SDKs that are embedded within other platforms. However, the positive impact of SDKs is reduced by frequent platform updates and higher levels of developer platform-specific experience, as experienced developers may rely less on external SDKs. These findings highlight the role of third-party resources in facilitating innovation but also suggest limitations based on platform changes and developer expertise. Together, the studies reveal how platform-level practices—such as rapid-release models and platform operating system updates — directly and indirectly impact mobile app development processes and outcomes. Rapid-release models pose challenges for update responsiveness but can foster app quality by leveraging customer feedback. Conversely, third-party SDKs enhance app development and performance but are sensitive to platform updates and developer experience. These findings underscore the need for developers to strategically manage trade-offs between responsiveness, quality, and resource utilization. For platform managers and SDK providers, the studies highlight the importance of supporting third-party developers through stable platform environments and effective boundary resources to sustain innovation.

11509420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11509420.value: The research can be further developed in several directions to deepen understanding of platform-level practices and their broader impacts. First, future studies could explore how the rapid-release model influences developers’ usage of platform-provided toolkits versus third-party toolkits. This would provide insights into whether developers shift their reliance between these resources under rapid-release conditions and how this affects innovation and app quality. Second, further research could examine whether and how the direction of platform-level practices, such as rapid release and toolkit improvement, is affected by the usage of third-party SDKs in apps. Understanding this dynamic could help clarify whether platform providers adapt their tools to complement or compete with third-party resources, shaping the overall ecosystem. Lastly, exploring how rapid-release models impact the user-side experience would provide a more holistic view of their effects. This could include studying user satisfaction, retention, and engagement in response to frequent app updates driven by the rapid-release model. By linking developer behaviors to user outcomes, this research could offer actionable strategies for balancing platform innovation with user satisfaction. These avenues of research would provide practical guidance for platform managers, developers, and third-party providers, enabling them to better align strategies to sustain innovation, ensure quality, and improve user experience within platform ecosystems.

11509420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11509420.value: This research focuses on how platform-level practices, like frequent platform updates (rapid-release models) and the use of third-party software development toolkits (SDKs), impact mobile app development and performance. Mobile platforms, such as iOS and Android, regularly release updates to their operating systems, which can help developers respond quickly to changes. However, this study found that frequent updates can slow down how quickly app developers release their own updates, although they can also improve app quality by encouraging developers to respond to user feedback. Another part of the research examines third-party SDKs, which help developers implement app features. The study shows that using these tools can increase app performance, but the benefits vary depending on the type of tool, platform updates, and the developer’s experiences within the platform. This research is important because it sheds light on how the choices made by platform owners (e.g., iOS or Android) not only influence how and to what extent developers create sustained and successful apps but also impact several key factors that shape developers’ ability or development environments to innovate and succeed. The findings can help platform managers develop better strategies to support developers, assist developers in balancing speed and quality, maintain control and value appropriation, and ensure that apps remain innovative and user-friendly. Overall, it provides valuable insights for enhancing the mobile app ecosystem as a whole.

11600020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600020.value: In a recent worldwide survey of 540,000 schoolchildren (OECD, 2017), Hong Kong ranked first in terms of school bullying severity among 72 countries and regions. Specifically, 32.3% of Hong Kong students said that they had suffered from bullying in the previous month, which was three times higher than the rate in Taiwan (10.7%) and nearly double that in the United States (18.9%). The Principal Investigator’s (PI’s) recent findings showed that among 9,958 local schoolchildren, 11.2% were reactive aggressors, 2.6% were proactive aggressors, 5.9% were occurring reactive-proactive aggressors, and 22.3% were victims of school bullying (Fung, 2019). Notably, the critical social movement in Hong Kong since June 2019 has seriously affected bullying. The level of aggressiveness, measured by the number of incidents of street fighting, assault, attacks on property and arson, has escalated, and many young protestors have been arrested. In addition, parent-child conflicts intensified after the social movement started. Thus, parental distress and pressure have been increasing, and they showed helplessness in rebuilding the parent-child relationship. Yet, no prior study has investigated the promotion of parenting efficacy and parental involvement to reduce reactive and proactive aggression among children and adolescents. The PI found that authoritarian and permissive parenting styles are positively correlated with developing children with reactive aggression and proactive aggression, respectively, in Hong Kong (Fung, Gerstein, Chan, & Hurley, 2013). Childhood and youth aggression have a high positive correlation with criminal behaviours in adulthood, with the level of aggression at a young age serving as the best predictor of criminal activity over the next 22 years (Huesmann, Eron, & Dubow, 2002). Negative short-term and long-term impacts on schools, families, communities and society, including school bullying, peer victimisation, assaults, family violence, murder and homicide, will continue to increase if no intervention is taken for high-risk youth. The proposed study will fill this research gap and create impact by reducing the number of children and adolescents with reactive and proactive aggression by enhancing parenting efficacy and parental involvement through an innovative parent-child intervention. In past studies, the PI identified controversial results for whether mothers or fathers play a key role in reducing children’s aggression. In the proposed study, we will further explore whether the mother, the father or both parents play the most significant role in reducing reactive and proactive aggression among children and adolescents. The proposed study will be timely and address an important ongoing challenge in Hong Kong. 最近一個全球性的調查（OECD, 2017），訪問了540,000位學童，發現在72個國家及地區中，香港的校園欺凌情況最為嚴重。有32.3%受訪的香港學童表示，過去一個月內曾受到欺凌，是台灣的（10.7%）三倍，亦差不多是美國的（18.9%）兩倍。是次首席研究員的研究亦發現，9,958個本地學童當中，11.2%為反應型攻擊者，2.6%為操控型攻擊者，5.9%為反應型及操控型攻擊者，而22.3%則為校園欺凌的受害者（Fung, 2019）。此外，香港由2019年6月開始，發生一連串的社會運動，暴力的情況更令人憂慮。各種暴力行為，包括街頭歐鬥、襲擊事件、毀壞財物、縱火等等，不斷升溫，更有不少的年輕示威者被捕。這次社會運動亦令親子之間衝突加劇，家長為此都感到苦惱和壓力，對重建親子關係覺得無助。可是，過往並沒有研究探討過，透過提升家長的管教效能及參與程度，以減少兒童及青少年的反應型及操控型攻擊行為。是次首席研究員發現，威權型及放任型的教養風格，分別與香港兒童的反應型及操控型攻擊行為有正相關（Fung, Gerstein, Chan, & Hurley, 2013）。兒童及青少年的攻擊行為，與成年後的犯罪行為有正相關，而年幼時的攻擊行為，是往後22年犯罪活動的最強預測因子（Huesmann, Eron, & Dubow, 2002）。若果沒有為高風險的兒童及青少年提供適切的介入，將會為學校、家庭、社區及整個社會帶來短期及長期的負面影響，包括校園欺凌、襲擊事件、家庭暴力及謀殺等等。是次研究計劃將會填補這個研究缺口，並透過創新的親子介入方式，提升家長的管教效能及參與程度，以減少兒童及青少年的反應型及操控型攻擊行為，為社會帶來正面影響。從過往的研究結果所知，父親抑或母親在減少子女的攻擊行為有較大的作用，是較有爭議性的，無法得到定論。所以，是次研究計劃，我們會進一步探討，父親、母親，還是雙親對減少子女反應型及操控型攻擊行為有較大的作用。這個研究希望針對香港一個持續及重大的挑戰，提供一個解決方案。

11600520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600520.value: 儀式與文章：唐玄宗朝的太平敘事

11600520.label: Project Objectives
11600520.value: 文學與史學家對於「盛唐」已有討論，但多是以現代學術眼光界定盛唐，而未能關注唐人對於太平盛世的觀念與論述。唐代諸多政治活動如獻瑞、封禪等，必須在致太平的觀念脈絡下才能被理解。因此本計畫將以「太平敘事」爲基本的觀念架構，論述與詮釋當時的太平觀念、實踐與書寫，冀能有助史學界重新認識所謂「盛世」。 在太平社會的觀念脈絡底下，唐人舉行諸多儀式典禮，與之相應，出現大量的賦、頌、碑、銘等作品。這些作品未能得到文學史家應有的關注，但在當時的地位重要。因此，本計畫將以儀式與文章為中心，重建當時的文體生態，以彌補文學史以僅詩歌為盛唐文學中心的缺憾，呈現完整圖景。 因儀式而產生的文本是以張說等人的「大手筆」為典範。這些被清人姜宸英所概括為「高文典冊大文字」的作品，其美感有別於詩歌所代表的「盛唐氣象」。這類作品往往「代擬王言」，風格上亦體現出帝王氣象。本計畫將比較「大手筆」所代表的太平氣象、帝王氣象與詩歌的「盛唐氣象」，重審盛唐文學的審美格局及其影響，冀能深化現有的文學史論述。 盛唐以張說、張九齡為代表的文儒以潤色鴻業作為參與盛時的重要途徑。潤色鴻業為極重要之文學觀念與創作傳統，本計劃研究其與太平觀念之關係及其在政治實踐中之應用，力圖揭示中國古代政治文化與文學生產之關係與機制。
