11600520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600520.value: This project aims to research the concept of a society of great peace, activities meant to construct such a state, and the pertinent literary production, during the reign of Emperor Xuanzong 玄宗 (712-756) of the Tang, from interdisciplinary perspectives on governance, thought and literature. The concept of great peace was mainly advocated by Zhang Yue 張說 (667-731) and Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 (678-740). Discourse on great peace centered on three aspects: a Sage King who accepts the Mandate of Heaven, the great peace of governance by ritual-and-music, and reporting great successes to the spirit world. At the time, a society of great peace was built according to this set of discourses; at its center was the revival of governance by ritual-and-music, and it deployed various ceremonies and rites that supported this central concept. The discourse that surrounded the concept of great peace and the implementation of ceremonial ritual produced various recorded texts such as hymns, rhapsodies and inscriptions, forming a huge “Great Peace Narrative,” which not only embodied the value of mainstream thought, but also demonstrated the ethos—or the aesthetic image—of great peace and of its emperor, to constitute an “imperial aesthetics.” Literary history discussing high Tang literature—which actually began in conceptual understandings originating in the Song and thereafter—centered on poetry, believing this embodied the “the ambient ethos of the high Tang.” This project uses interdisciplinary methods to explore and reconstruct the “Great Peace Narrative” of the reign of Xuanzong, and demonstrates a different schema of literature in the age of Xuanzong, hoping to be able to provide a new angle of investigation for research into the relevant political history, intellectual history and literary history in the Tang dynasty, as well as a reference point to investigate the relations between the culture of ancient Chinese governance and its literary products. 本計劃擬從政治、思想與文學的跨領域視角硏究唐玄宗時代(712-756) 的太平社會觀念、營構活動與文學生產。太平觀念主要由張說（667-731）、張九齡(678-740)二人提出，圍繞聖王受天命、禮樂致太平、成功告神明三個方面展開太平論述，當時正是按照這一套論述構建太平社會，以興禮作樂為中心，展現為各種典禮儀式。圍繞太平觀念的論述、典禮儀式的舉行產生了頌賦碑銘等各種體裁的文本，形成宏大的「太平敘事」，不僅體現出主流思想價値，而呈現出太平氣象與帝王氣象，構成「帝王的美學」。文學史論及盛唐文學，以詩歌為中心，認為體現「盛唐氣象」，實源自宋以降之認識。本計劃運用跨學科的方法探討並重建玄宗朝之「太平敘事」，呈現玄宗時代文學之另一圖景，冀能為唐代政治史、思想史及文學史相關方面的硏究提供一新的觀察角度，亦可為考察中國古代政治文化與文學生產之關係提供借鑒。

11600520.label: Realisation of objectives
11600520.value: 一、 PI收集唐人有關太平盛世的論述，發現可以以唐玄宗的宰相張說在《封禪頌》的論述概括之，那就是皇帝受命，致太平，最後封禪，宣告盛世建成。由此出發，PI首先探討唐玄宗的天命論述。玄宗繼承漢代以來的傳統，認為天子受命必有符瑞作為天命的依據，而他最重要的符瑞便是長安的龍池與潞州上黨的十九瑞。PI對後者曾有研究，發表一篇論文（2018）。PI又考察長安興慶宮龍池的符瑞化過程，揭示它從一個積水池變成天命象徵的過程，又研究圍繞池水產生的三組重要文本，分別是景龍四年的《興慶池侍宴應制》、開元二年的《龍池樂章》和二十三年的《龍池聖德頌》。這些文本的書寫對象相同，但卻從屬於不同的政治脈絡，又同歸於一套盛世敘事，是天命觀念在不同層次上的展現。PI就此發表論文一篇(2022)。符瑞是陰陽二氣和諧的結果，災異和符瑞一體兩面，乃是陰陽二氣乖舛的產物。為了進一步揭示這種天人觀念在古代盛世論述中的影響，PI又考察唐人作品中的災異書寫，以及隱藏在時事討論背後的災異脈絡，撰成論文一篇(2020)。玄宗的符瑞具有形象，出現在城市，也是城市景觀的組成，PI在上述兩篇論文的基礎上，以「城市」為研究對象，撰成專著一部(2025)。 二、 天命王者以致太平為目標，根據漢儒的說法，太平以禮樂和頌聲為標誌。就禮樂而言，唐玄宗在開元十三年成功封禪泰山，PI就此撰寫論文一篇(2025)，討論玄宗在封禪前夕如何透過一系列的典禮實踐證成盛世已然建成，封禪的時機成熟。圍繞這一系列典禮又產生諸多文本，包括賦、頌、碑、銘以及朝廷的詔、表等，這些文體長期受到文學史研究者的忽視，但PI指出，它們闡釋典禮的意義，也揭示其背後的天人秩序，在古代的政治文化中有重大的價值，也是盛唐文學的重要組成。 三、 受命天子興禮樂，人臣則要隆頌聲。盛唐諸位「大手筆」作有大量的頌碑，但卻因其頌美的性質而有諛上之嫌疑，長期處於文學史的邊緣。PI考察現存頌碑，發現這些文本服務於一套天人秩序，他們的意義在於揭示帝王與天道之間的關係，因天道至公，故頌碑等文體以文字為天道言說，也是至公的表現。除頌體之外，盛唐還有其他文類也是盛世頌聲。應制詩因其歌詠帝王的特徵而被視為缺乏情志之作，但是，應制詩對於自然山水、宮廷景觀的描寫亦是一套理想的自然和人間秩序的呈現，它們也是盛世敘事的重要環節。PI就唐代頌聲的問題撰成一篇論文(2023)，指出唐人實際上極為重視這些頌體或頌聲，這是他們參與盛世文化建設的重要途徑，亦力圖揭示盛唐氣象在言志之歌以外的表現。 四、 因為隆頌聲是盛世文儒的責任，故而盛唐文士多以潤色鴻業為職志，作有大量的志美文章，PI對盛唐文儒的志美觀念和實踐之研究可見於上述的論文當中。同時，為了進一步突出盛唐的盛世觀念與敘事，PI又將眼光延續至安史之亂後，指出歷經戰亂的文士面對秩序重建的需求，提出另一套以「感人心」為出發點的秩序論述，其所嚮往之文章亦隨之一便，潤色鴻業的理想轉變為對美刺褒貶之文的追求。PI針對此一重大的觀念變化撰寫兩篇文章（2022、2023）。

在太平社會的觀念脈絡底下，唐人舉行諸多儀式典禮，與之相應，出現大量的賦、頌、碑、銘等作品。這些作品未能得到文學史家應有的關注，但在當時的地位重要。因此，本計畫將以儀式與文章為中心，重建當時的文體生態，以彌補文學史以僅詩歌為盛唐文學中心的缺憾，呈現完整圖景。
因儀式而產生的文本是以張說等人的「大手筆」為典範，其美感有別於詩歌所代表的「盛唐氣象」。這類作品往往「代擬王言」，風格上亦體現出帝王氣象。本計畫將比較「大手筆」所代表的太平氣象、帝王氣象與詩歌的「盛唐氣象」，重審盛唐文學的審美格局及其影響，冀能深化現有的文學史論述。
盛唐以張說、張九齡為代表的文儒以潤色鴻業作為參與盛時的重要途徑。潤色鴻業為極重要之文學觀念與創作傳統，本計劃研究其與太平觀念之關係及其在政治實踐中之應用，力圖揭示中國古代政治文化與文學生產之關係與機制。

11600520.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600520.value: PI在本項目的支持下發表七篇論文和一部專著。本研究提出唐玄宗朝的盛世觀念有異於現代政治的觀念，是以受命、興禮樂和隆頌聲為觀念框架。在此觀念框架下，唐人重視符瑞的詮釋，儀式的展演與潤色鴻業的價值。圍繞唐人的盛世觀念產生碑、銘、頌、賦和詩歌等文體的諸多文本，它們是盛世的頌聲，內容則體現為一套盛世的敘事。 傳統文學史對於盛唐的論述集中在詩歌，特別重視其抒情言志之價值，對於以頌聖為職志的文體，如賦、頌、碑、銘則多有輕視，認為它們只是歌功頌德的諛上之作。但是，本研究揭示在唐人的盛世觀念中，這些頌聖的文體承擔溝通天人，展示天人秩序的任務，在唐代的政治文化中有重要的地位，應為文學史所重視。

11600520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600520.value: PI已經和北京大學出版社簽約，將在此項目的基礎上再完成一部專著，書名為:太平:唐玄宗時期的盛世敘事。同時，PI亦將繼續討論唐人在安史之亂後，有關秩序重建也就是中興的論述。新的秩序觀念將進一步影響文學生態，催生出心得文類和文學主題。

11600520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600520.value: 本研究揭示盛唐文學的另一面貌。受到純文學觀念的影響，文學史研究者認為表達個人情志的文章才是有價值的文學。因此，有關盛唐文學的討論偏重在詩，對於頌美文學則斥之以阿諛奉承，鮮少關注。但是，回到盛唐政治文化的脈絡當中，天人感應的秩序觀念依然深刻地影響唐人的思考與實踐，並由此催生大量的符瑞書寫與頌聖文章，在文體則表現為賦頌碑銘等。它們是唐人參與理想秩序建設的重要途經，在盛唐文學中有極為重要的地位。

11600720.value: 小提琴、夏威夷滑音棒結他及班祖的“粵化”：西洋樂器在粵劇棚面的應用與調適

11600720.label: Project Objectives
11600720.value: EXAMINE under what historical circumstances violin, Hawaiian slide guitar, and banjo were introduced major Chinese port cities, notably Shanghai, Canton, and Hong Kong in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century. ANALYZE how these western instruments were adapted to become part of the Cantonese opera ensemble in such a way that they are able to express a regional character and musical flavor recognized by practitioners from the 1920s to 40s, and how such adaptations are continued and regarded by practitioners today. DOCUMENT primary data collected from digital newspaper and journal sources. By means of archival research, we will track the contacts and interactions between Cantonese musicians and jazz musicians, municipal band musicians, nightclub musicians, etc. who regularly play these instruments and who very likely influenced them into learning to play and integrate them into the Cantonese music ensemble. INVESTIGATE newspaper advertisements and articles, archives and museum collections which hold materials such as playbills and salary slips that indicate the personnel and, thus, the instrumentation of Cantonese operatic ensembles in the first half of twentieth century. INTERVIEW current practitioners who are playing or have had the experience of playing violins, Hawaiian slide guitars, and banjos in Cantonese operatic troupes and ensembles, as well as in night clubs settings which were common between the 1950s and 1990s in Hong Kong in order to find out how they came about being exposed to and learning to play them. OBSERVE the techniques and skills applied by current practitioners and conduct musical analysis which would show the stylistic characteristics of Cantonese music and its relation to the Cantonese dialect, techniques of melodic ornamentation by traditional Cantonese ensemble instruments and by each of these three adopted Western instruments. This will be done through ethnographic fieldwork with Cantonese musicians and by holding one performance workshops to be participated in by musicians from Hong Kong and Guangzhou, and overseas, as well as by researchers from both Hong Kong and overseas. CONNECT the historical findings with the results of ethnomusicological fieldwork and musical analysis, including the historical episodes related to the incorporation of the above-mentioned three instruments in different regions and cities which had/ have Cantonese opera performances by looking at Cantonese opera and music in California (and possibly Hawaii), Shanghai, the Pearl River Delta centering around Hong Kong and Guangzhou, both diachronically and synchronically. The eventual goal is to be able to compare the use of these three instruments in Cantonese opera ensembles abroad and within south China, and with the cases of other non-Western music cultures.

11600720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600720.value: This project examines how Western instruments are introduced and adapted in Cantonese operatic music in the twentieth century. It is well known among professional Cantonese operatic musicians and researchers that from the 1920s on, a number of western instruments, namely, violin, xylophone, mandolin, saxophone, banjo, Hawaiian slide guitar, and cello, have been used side by side with their Chinese counterparts in the instrumental ensemble accompanying Cantonese opera troupes. Among these western instruments, violin is the most noteworthy as it plays the lead melody in Cantonese opera ensembles similar to the high-pitched gaohu. By contrast, both Hawaiian slide guitars and banjos play merely a supportive role rhythmically and harmonically. But both are favourites among Cantonese string musicians as the former produce a sonic effect which local players cherish, most likely due to its ability to bend pitches and produce tonal glides which imitate the linguistic intonation of the Cantonese language while the latter are a favorite among blind singers and expand the range and timbral capabilities of the qinqin, its Chinese counterpart among the traditional Cantonese musical instruments. Both historical and ethnomusicological approaches will be adopted in this research. Preliminary studies show that these instruments were introduced to such port-cities as Shanghai, Canton (Guangzhou), Hong Kong, and Macau in the early twentieth century, presumably from the US West Coast via the Pacific. This coincided with the large scale movement of labourers and traders from south China to Hawaii and California between the mid-nineteenth and the mid-twentieth century. It was the time when banjos and Hawaiian slide guitars were fashioned in the United States and shaped the folk and country music there. It was also the time when Cantonese opera troupes thrived in North America. To establish evidential relationships between various movements and trends, a systematic documentation of primary source materials is needed. Alongside documentation, an ethnomusicological approach will be applied in order to determine how these instruments had been adapted and are used by practitioners. Through the collection of oral histories, ethnographic interviews and first-hand observation of actual contexts in which Cantonese opera music is often performed as well as planned music performance workshops, this project will not only record the personal experiences and the instrumental music practices of current practitioners, but will also collect their opinions regarding why they think “Western” instruments are able to express “Chinese” regional character. 小提琴、夏威夷滑音棒結他及班祖的“粵化”：西洋樂器在粵劇棚面的應用與調適 本計劃旨在研究20世紀上半葉西洋樂器被引進及應用在粵劇棚面（樂隊）的過程。熟悉粵劇粵樂歷史的人都知道，自20世紀20年代始，粵劇棚面所使用的樂器，除傳統中樂外，還加入了各色西洋器具，包括小提琴、木琴、曼陀鈴、色士風、班祖、夏威夷滑音棒結他、大提琴等，為粵劇粵曲的伴奏增添了其他地方戲曲所沒有的音樂元素。在各種西洋樂器中，被本地樂師稱為“梵鈴”的小提琴，以其在棚面中擔演相當於胡琴的頭架（領奏）角色而最值得重視。相形之下，夏威夷滑音棒結他和班祖主要在節奏和旋律方面發揮支援作用。然而不應忽略的是，夏威夷滑音棒結他和班祖也為好些粵樂樂師所鐘愛，前者能產生接近人聲（粵語音聲）的效果，後者以其輕便但聲量較大，音域比形態類似的秦琴稍廣，而為街頭樂人尤其是瞽師樂用。 本研究將採用歷史學和民族音樂學的方法，雙管齊下地探討小提琴、夏威夷滑音棒結他及班祖這三種樂器引進和應用在粵劇棚面的過程。19世紀中至20世紀中，大量華人從華南地區到夏威夷和加州謀生，恰好夏威夷結他和班祖也在此時在美國西部流行，塑造著美國當時的“鄉村音樂”，由此可以估計，20世紀初西洋樂器主要從美國西岸經太平洋進入上海、廣州、香港和澳門等口岸城市的。與此同時，粵劇戲班在北美華人社區中亦非常活躍，也是使用西洋樂器的重要場所。多重多向的人群流動，呈現出物質（樂器）流動的複雜態勢，需要系統查閱文獻資料才能較清楚呈現。本研究也會運用口述歷史、田野調查以及現場觀察等民族音樂學的方法，探討樂師如何使用、改造以及理解西洋樂器，並邀請樂師舉辦工作坊，讓其示範相關技巧，交流經驗和心得，從中探討一個最關鍵的問題：“西洋”樂器緣何能表現“中國”的“地方”特色。

11601720.label: Project Objectives
11601720.value: Exploratory research, particularly attendance at the 2018 Global Residence and Citizenship Conference in Dubai with seed funding from the university, led me to identify a puzzle suited to a multi-year analysis: why are CBI/RBI programmes proliferating despite substantial international opposition to them? To determine the most convincing interpretation of the puzzle, I propose to investigate four explanatory factors bridging Asian demand, European supply, global networks and the durability of national sovereignty despite political pressures. My research will ascertain the weight that should be attributed to each of these processes and how they are inter-related. Several distinguished legal scholars have gone so far as to call CBI/RBI “one of the most disturbing developments in 21st century citizenship” (Shachar and Hirschl 2014: 246). The research funded by this grant would contribute to emerging normative, empirical and policy-oriented discussions of the global availability of CBI/RBI. I will collect data to test the explanatory factors across one crucial demand-centred case (mainland China) and three supply-side test cases (Cyprus, Greece and Malta). Far more is known about the supply of CBI/RBI than the demand for such services by global elites (Harpaz 2019). The proposed project will seek to fill the gap in knowledge of how individuals from Asia have become the largest source of buyers of additional passports and residency in other countries. Here, the focus must be trained on mainland China, which is the most substantial source of CBI/RBI clients. The findings are expected to provide a better understanding of how Asian demand and European supply fit together and how this dynamic is affected by pressures from a range of national and global actors. Cyprus and Malta are the most important European countries offering CBI/RBI. The timing of the proposed project will afford the unique opportunity to study the launch and reception of the new Greece CBI programme that will be offered from 2020. To collect evidence, I will use a range of methods appropriate to solving the research problem: interviews, roundtable discussions, drawing on the expertise of a financial investigator and observation at industry gatherings and at CBI/RBI promotion events. Although I established numerous connections at the Dubai industry conference mentioned above, there is a much broader universe of informants whom I will need to meet to thoroughly approach the issue from the perspectives of clients, industry advisors and regional/international officials and critics. I have demonstrated my ability to secure elite interviews and to use this material effectively in previous publications (see enclosed CV). One of the crucial empirical questions concerns the utility of holding CBI/RBI to avoid asset and tax scrutiny. Under the OECD’s Common Reporting Standard (CRS), launched in 2014, banks in signatory jurisdictions report account details to the tax authority of the resident. To gather new data on the technically challenging relationship between Asian elites holding CBI/RBI and the CRS, it is necessary to go beyond interviews. I plan to look inside financial institution operations using the skills I developed researching US dollar clearing banks servicing offshore clients (Robertson 2019a). I have also found a specialist in the intricacies of compliance and due diligence practices to serve as an informal advisor on the planned banking research. The project will adopt an open perspective and test CRS compliance empirically with the hypothesis that the CRS represents an as yet incomplete check on financial movements by global elites. One of the most widely cited US legal scholars maintains that CBI/RBI schemes are simply a means for affluent citizens in poorer countries to travel to Europe and the US more easily, and that this conduct should be sanctioned as i) it is economically beneficial for these developing countries ii) it promotes tourism in Europe and the US and iii) due diligence of CBI/RBI applicants has been upgraded because of heightened international pressure in the last decade (Posner 2019). While in agreement on higher due diligence checks, the proposed project will seek to illustrate that the key issue is not excluding criminals, but rather, it is how CBI/RBI can be incorporated into the toolbox for shifting the financial wealth of elites offshore. It is important to delineate what will not fall within the project’s remit. The project will not engage with the economic merits of CBI/RBI, either in terms of the optimal programme design for developmental outcomes (Van Fossen 2018) or whether it spurs as high a level of investment as CBI/RBI issuing governments anticipate. These lines of enquiry can be addressed by Economists. To remain focused, several geographies must be left aside for future research. This includes the vulnerabilities of Caribbean countries, which face downward pressure on what they can charge for CBI/RBI while struggling with the exit opportunities of their own elites (Christians 2018). Also excluded is the Middle East, which provides another significance source of demand for CBI/RBI programmes.

11601720.label: Realisation of objectives
11601720.value: China is the world’s largest market for individuals seeking to obtain a second passport or foreign residency by means of making an investment. Despite recent outstanding scholarship on such investment migration, the China piece of this puzzle is least understood. Thankfully, despite delays, this project will fill a major hole in the literature with the publication of a manuscript and a top-tier journal article. No comprehensive analysis of China’s investment migration story is available and the publication of the aforementioned material should be well received. The original proposal outlined several key factors: Asian demand, European supply, global networks, and the durability of national sovereignty. All of these elements feature prominently in the project analysis. METHODS Three research methods proved most valuable: observation at industry gatherings and at promotion events, elites interviews, and following WeChat channels. In-person and online events highlighted the thinking of lead industry practitioners and opened up interview possibilities. 11 in-person events and 22 online events were attended. Interviews were often lengthy exchanges, sometimes more than two hours. The level of interest in roundtables proved disappointing. The financial investigator’s revised terms placed this expert beyond reach. Also, it had become clear that tax avoidance and criminality was a less important pattern in the process of seeking out second passports and residencies than suspected. Instead, the project frames much of this activity, including the associated capital outflow, as falling into grey zones rather than being criminal like tax avoidance. STAFFING The budget shifted more intensively over time to staffing. Covid is the primary explanation. The secondary reason is that I recruited a talented and motivated RA, with whom I developed a strong partnership. I have shared my knowledge with the RA and also learned new information, especially reflections from monitoring mainland China event as well as immersion in WeChat groups. This project has served as an important training ground in this young scholar’s development, a likely future PhD student. WRITING AND OUTPUTS Because the themes coherently fit together, I chose to combine the planned papers into one book manuscript and then encapsulate the best points in an overall article in a high ranking journal. The goal is to position the book as a must read alongisde the two major works in this field, Harpaz’s Citizenship 2.0: Dual Nationality as a Global Asset and Suraks’s The Golden Passport: Global Mobility for Millionaires. The book offers a different framing to these authors and presents the neglected China case. Both conceptually and empirically, the primary themes raised in the mid-term report, “Globalization and Grey Zones”, “Globalization the Ground”, and “China-Europe intersections”, are developed at length in the book. My father’s death was devastating and had an unfortunate impact on my writing. The book manuscript is now thankfully weeks away from being ready for submission. After final edits and work on the references, Golden Gambits: How Chinese Elites Navigate the Grey Zone for Passports and Residencies will be sent to four university presses, along with the book proposal. The manuscript is enclosed for your review. I believe there is a reasonably good chance of a book contract with a university press given the project’s originality, the conceptual contribution (grey zones, practice-based globalization, investment migration for both foreign and domestic purposes), and the richness of the empirical findings (capital exit, education, European pressure, hedging, marketing approaches). I would be happy to share the summary journal manuscript (entitled “Grey Zones in the Global Political Economy: The Search for Second Passports and Residencies in China”) with you in March. It will present the best conceptual and empirical points from the book manuscript. ARGUMENT Operating in Grey Zones Chinese elites have devised sophisticated methods of navigating regulatory barriers through informal networks and legal loopholes, operating within what I call “grey zones”, where laws exist but enforcement is inconsistent. Despite China's recent tightening of restrictions, these grey zones continue to provide elites with opportunities to transfer funds offshore and secure foreign residency. Unlike outright criminal activity, these grey zones are characterized by weak rule of law, where unwritten rules often take precedence over official policies. While state power is extensive, it remains incomplete in certain areas, leading to tactical tolerance until specific loopholes become too visible or widely exploited. Economic Uncertainty and Tax Concerns in Particular Existing literature presents competing explanations for Chinese investment migration. Some scholars, such as Harpaz, frame it as a reaction to democratic backsliding, suggesting that migration is a strategic response to declining political freedoms. Others, like Liu-Farrer, emphasize social status motivations, arguing that global mobility serves as a marker of elite distinction rather than political/economic necessity. Instead, economic uncertainty is the driving factor in my analysis, associated in particular with the implementation of a tougher new tax regime. Historically, many companies operated with irregular accounting methods, with business owners often retaining company dividends. A key source of anxiety among China’s economic elite is the absence of a statute of limitations on tax violations. Many businesses, particularly those established during China’s early liberalization, were not tax-compliant by today’s standards. With the state’s expanded data collection capabilities, retroactive investigations have become a looming threat. The situation has been exacerbated by reports of local officials using bank records to threaten tax audits. Domestic Advantages and Strategic Usage An often overlooked aspect of investment migration has been its strategic use within China's domestic system itself. Many Chinese citizens obtained foreign status to navigate domestic constraints more effectively. For instance, mainland Chinese investors leveraged foreign status from African countries to participate in Hong Kong's residence scheme. In the business sphere, entrepreneurs with citizenship from Caribbean jurisdictions bypassed regulatory restrictions and accessed global capital markets. Stricter regulations, Beijing's enhanced oversight, and new policy priorities emphasizing educational equity and domestic financial control have made such strategies increasingly untenable. Capital Exit and Changing Landscape The environment for capital movement has changed from its once-permissive state to one characterized by closed loopholes and reduced support from immigration agents. While Covid policies and regulatory crackdowns have further complicated outbound capital flows, the system continues to function, albeit in altered forms. High-risk underground banking networks persist, and alternative destinations, particularly Singapore, have gained prominence. Investment migration remains viable, though in a more discreet form. Questioning the Insurance Policy Narrative The conventional wisdom that second citizenship serves as an effective insurance policy is backed up by little research. Russia's sudden exclusion from citizenship programs demonstrates how geopolitical shifts can rapidly devalue these rights. China’s exit bans and extraterritorial reach further complicate the ability of individuals to execute departures. Even those who successfully relocate often remain subject to Chinese tax laws and legal obligations. Furthermore, the necessity of investment migration to facilitate global financial opportunities is overvalued with many offshore services available without additional papers. The experiences of Chinese billionaires illustrate the fine line of trying to maintain positions inside and outside China. Some successfully secured offshore footholds, enabling them to protect their wealth and personal security. Others failed, leaving them and their assets exposed.

11601720.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601720.value: In what will be the first book-length study of the China case within the larger global investment migration story, the key conceptual and empirical results can be noted. First, there are grey zones within regulatory gaps in many countries. The contribution here is to sketch out the concept and explore how and why these grey zones materialize in China. Second, the book distinguishes between two different forms of investment migration: for foreign purposes and also for domestic purposes. Third, the book proposes asset separation as a less known but important impetus. Fourth, researchers should be attuned to on-the-ground actions and informal practices rather than regulations according to the practice-based model. Empirically: -Over time, China’s trajectory of investment migration has shifted from closed to a limited opening—in which the word immigration was prohibited and raids were directed on immigration firms—to a wider opening, and finally to narrowing today. -Chinese immigration agents are the lead actors, and global firms are overrepresented in existing studies, especially the overhyped role of Henley & Partners. -China has transformed its tax collection system away from its previously lenient approach, with a sophisticated integration of AI and big data to monitor transactions in real-time. This system connects central, provincial, and municipal tax databases while incorporating corporate and personal banking information. It acts as a cause of economic anxiety for Chinese elites. -After asking nearly all the interviewees to estimate the number of investment migrants who have fully resettled abroad, the consensus is that close to 90% have retained Chinese citizenship. Migration without relocation is the term we attach to this phenomenon. -The proliferation of capital transfer mechanisms illustrates a paradox: restrictions often catalyze more evasion strategies, creating a cycle of regulatory tightening and attempted circumvention. Still, the landscape has turned from its earlier relative permissiveness. China's enhanced capital controls, tax surveillance, and closure of loopholes like UnionPay and Macau gambling channels have made large-scale wealth transfers increasingly challenging. -Caribbean citizenship of a number of Chinese firm executives listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange, found through database searches, points to tolerated grey zones. -When one of China’s most established investment migration firms openly coaches potential clients on WeChat on how to set up Hong Kong and Singapore offshore accounts and how to answer questions posed by banks and authorities, China’s grey zones are in full view.

11601720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601720.value: The follow-on project idea is rooted in the number of interactions the research team had with migration agents and middle class Chinese clients. The strong impression was that uninformed middle class clients were making questionable choices in investing in European residency. China’s middle class emerges as an influential but understudied group, distinct from HNWIs. While HNWIs focus on strategic risk management, segments of the middle class are driven by narratives around education opportunities and lifestyle benefits and rely heavily on agents for guidance. The marketing practices we observed raise significant concerns. Agents often employ aggressive tactics, particularly in our observations of Greece’s golden visa. The absence of professional standards and minimal regulatory oversight has led to poorly trained agents focused primarily on sales targets. Commission structures create concerning incentives where properties valued at €250,000 might be marked up to €500,000. WeChat marketing content often appears to face limited scrutiny. This digital ecosystem can facilitate the spread of misinformation about investment migration opportunities. More detailed analysis of WeChat could be an important research source. The goal is to write up this story in one journal article, although the analysis might justify two journal articles.

11601720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601720.value: This project is the first to examine how wealthy Chinese obtain foreign passports and residency rights through investment, despite China's restrictions on dual citizenship and strict controls on moving money abroad. These actions take place in grey zones, areas where rules exist but are not strictly enforced. These individuals would earlier use investment migration to gain advantages both internationally and within China itself, like better school access or raising business financing. Recent years have seen increased restrictions from both China and other countries, making it harder but not impossible to pursue these strategies. The domestic benefits, in particular, have virtually disappeared. Despite tighter regulations, the conclusion is that investment migration continues because of enduring grey zones in China's system founded upon economic uncertainty and complex governance structures. Even so, the findings challenge the common belief that second passports provide reliable insurance against political or economic instability. The larger significance is three-fold: to affirm the place of practice-based analyses of globalization; to raise questions about the two leading perspectives in the field—that China’s investment migration is the product of democratic backsliding or social status seeking; and, to recognize that global China studies should incorporate the hedging strategies of Chinese elites.

11602620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11602620.value: Electronic health records (eHR) systems promise a new frontier for improved healthcare quality and safety for patients as well as promoting health system resource efficiency. The benefits of eHR include clinical (reduced medical errors), organizational (providing financial and operational benefits) and societal (improved population health through medical research) improvements. However, because eHR contain longitudinal patient histories meant to be shared for clinical and therapeutic purposes, eHR systems have amplified the concerns surrounding data confidentiality and privacy. An opt-in eHR sharing system (eHRSS) was launched in Hong Kong in March 2016. By April 2019, approximately 1,050,000 patients were registered. Sources referencing enrolment numbers are limited, but based on the available numbers, it appears most of the enrolment with the eHRSS were patients migrating from the Hospital Authority’s old Public Private Interface-Electronic Patient Record one-way patient information sharing program. This reflects difficulties in recruiting new members to join the system. Our pilot study of 25 subjects on the level of patient and public’s attitude and trust towards the eHRSS reveals some support for the eHRSS and an overwhelming ‘data trust deficit’. However, given the sample size, the data captured is inadequate and needs to be expanded. EHR are 'socially-critical' communications because the disclosure of personal health information highlights privacy and security concerns that becomes more complex with digitization and the interoperability of health records. If these concerns are not addressed in a way that patients and public understand and accept, the lack of institutional trust will correspondingly result in the sharing of health records lacking social credibility. The correlation of trust to personal privacy and security and the levels of positive attitudes and support towards eHR sharing from Hong Kong’s health consumer perspective is an understudied area which warrants greater investigation. Additionally, an investigation into how Hong Kong resolves its own concerns in the broader healthcare efficiency vs privacy trade-off lends its practice out to other jurisdictions. The Project adopts a socio-legal perspective involving comparative and empirical studies. First, the Project will evaluate the extent to which perceived importance of trust, privacy and security can over-ride privacy concerns thereby providing a supportive attitude towards eHR sharing. Second, by comparatively examining key facilitators and barriers in promoting acceptance and use of eHR in the US, Australia, and Singapore against Hong Kong’s framework, the Project will examine whether an appropriate ecosystem exists which renders well-intentioned policies and institutional efforts achievable. 電子健康紀錄（eHR）系統可有效提高醫療質素、確保病人的安全，以及優化衛生系統資源的使用。eHR的好處包括對臨床（減少醫療失誤）、組織（提供財務及運營利益）以及社會（通過醫學研究改善人口的健康）等各方面的改善。不過，由於eHR系統包含為臨床及治療目的而共享的縱向患者歷史紀錄，帶來了公眾對個人資料私密性的憂慮。香港於2016年3月推出了一個自願參與的eHR互通系統（eHRSS），而截至2019年4月，已有約1,050,000名病人註冊登記。根據現有的數據，似乎大部分註冊eHRSS的病人是從醫院管理局舊有的公私營醫療合作—醫療病歷互聯的單向患者資料共享計劃而來，可見新成員登記加入此系統的人數不多。根據我們對25名病人進行的試點研究，從病人及公眾對eHRSS的態度及信任程度看來，他們對eHRSS基本支持，但卻對資料保密嚴重缺乏信任。不過，由於研究樣本人數偏低，我們所獲得的數據還須擴大。隨著數位化和健康紀錄的相互操作變得更加複雜，洩露個人健康信息將引起公眾對個人私隱及安全的高度關注，而eHR亦成為關鍵的社會通信。若這些問題得不到病人及公眾的理解和接受，他們對醫療機構的不信任將會相應影響健康紀錄互通的可信程度。我們以為，以香港健康消費者的視角看個人資料使用的信任和電子病歷共享的支持之間的關聯仍有待更深入的研究。此外，對其他司法管轄區就相似項目的做法進行調查，亦有助我們研究在更廣泛的醫療保健效率與隱私權衡的背景下，香港可如何解決自身在此方面的憂慮。本研究將採取社會法律觀點進行比較及實證研究。首先，本研究將探討信任、私隱及安全的重要性能在多大程度上克服私隱方面的顧慮，從而建構對eHR共享的積極

11604120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604120.value: A large number of joint projects are undertaken between the Hong Kong government and local governments in mainland China, in which collaborative actions are designed to tackle a wide range of policy and service delivery issues, from cross-border transportation to water supply to regional economic planning. Institutional differences between the quasi-democratic Hong Kong and the authoritarian mainland have often created friction in these collaborative projects. In some cases, the central government in Beijing has been brought in to resolve disputes, either with a one-off leadership directive or through long-term engagement in a project. The implementation of “one country, two systems” (1C2S) in Hong Kong thus provides a rare opportunity to examine how a central authority influences collaboration between institutions with very different institutional settings. Indeed, 1C2S implementation in Hong Kong involves partners with (a) significant institutional differences (“two systems”) and (b) elements of imposed collaborative authority from the central government (“one country”). The proposed study seeks to exploit this unique opportunity to pursue the following guiding research question: Given significant institutional differences between collaborating partners, how does an authoritative imposition moderate these differences to influence collaborative actions, and how effective is this moderation? There is little evidence to draw on in answering this question. This may be because in the Western context, which is the focus of most of the literature on collaborative actions, the institutional differences lack saliency, with the collaborating partners consisting of liberal democracies featuring a separation of powers, and an authority is less likely to become involved given the voluntary nature of the collaborations. Evidence is therefore needed from non-Western contexts, where a central authority is more likely to engage to improve collaborative actions. The proposed research will take as case studies of four projects undertaken with the collaboration of the Hong Kong government and local governments in China: the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, Express Rail Link, Dongshen Water Supply, and Food Supply Scheme. Projects with greater levels of central government involvement will be compared with those with lower levels in terms of how the central government’s engagement moderates the institutional differences and what effects this moderation has on the collaborative actions. The analysis will take a mixed methods approach consisting of content analysis and field interviews. In the first stage, government documents will be examined using structured content analysis to test key hypothesized relationships. In the second stage, key stakeholders will be interviewed to substantiate the research findings. 在過去幾十年，香港政府與中國大陸的地方政府在公共治理方面的合作已經由淺至深，其合作項目廣泛地包含了从跨境交通、跨區供水到区域經濟發展等一系列議題。然而，在“一國兩制”的背景下，中港兩地政府間的制度差異導致了合作中的摩擦，並明顯制約了雙方的合作效率。在一些合作案例中，北京的中央政府不得不透過一次性的行政指令或長期參與來幫助解決地方合作中的爭端。在協同治理理論及相關實踐中，現有文獻所關注的協同治理主要在制度背景相似或相同的主體間展開，鮮有研究關注存在制度差異的府際間協同合作。本研究採用協同治理網絡作為分析框架，以中港跨境合作為切入點，探究程序和制度設計的差異對協同治理的過程和產出是否存在影響。基於港珠澳大橋建設、高鐵香港段、東深供水工程和供港食物管理四個案例，本研究從正式和非正式程序兩條路徑分析了程序和制度因素對協同行動的作用和影響。通過對案例進行比較分析，本研究試圖解釋中央政府的參與程度對緩和中港程序和制度差異的作用，以及這種介入對協同行動究竟有哪些方面的影響。本研究將以文本分析和深度訪談為主要研究方法，並將研究過程劃分為兩個階段。在第一階段，研究者將使用結構化的文本分析來檢視政府文件，以發掘和測試關鍵的理論假設。在第二階段，研究者將採訪關鍵利益相關者以對前一階段的研究成果做進一步證實。

11604120.label: Realisation of objectives
11604120.value: This project aims to examine the role of external imposition in collaborative actions, contributing to theory and practice of the collaborative governance, through five specific project objectives. In this section, I will discuss the research process and outcome related to each of these objectives. Objective 1. Advance the collaborative governance literature by examining how institutional and design differences between collaborating partners influence collaborative actions The key contribution this research has made so far is to improve the Collaborative Governance Regime CGR model significantly by increasing a dimension of external policy engagement in the collaborative capacity building process. This was done not only by this research providing a novel theoretical framework but more importantly by providing necessary empirical evidence on how such an enhanced model may work. More specifically, I looked into one specific capacity factor, known in the literature as the procedural and institutional design PIDs, and examine how collaborative frictions were generated during a collaborative process where partners with different PIDs struggled to work together--- measured by "collaborative friction"(the use of such a novel concept itself is also a key contribution of this research), and examine how effective an external intervention was in resolving these frictions. The empirical findings suggest a moderate external imposition effect in the short term by resolving immediate collaborative frictions but in the longer term such effect could diminish. This finding is so impressive and its theoretical contribution to the collaborative governance literature is so significant that the results are published in the top-ranked journal in public administration and policy Public Administration Review PAR (Zhao, C., Wang, X., Cheung, P., Xu, J. 2023 "Influence of external authorities on collaborative frictions", Public Administration Review 83(3): 603-622. Listed in the Output section), and eventually wins the 2023 Best Article of the Year Award by American Society for Public Administration ASPA Section on Chinese Public Administration SCPA for its "exceptional research quality" (SCPA Citation). Objective 2: Advance the Institutional Collective Action (ICA) literature by enriching understanding of how authoritative imposition influences collaborative actions Two findings of this research are directly related to the ICA literature where there is almost complete absence on the adoption of so-called "externally imposed authority" in collaborative actions. First, the introduction of such a mechanism in this research and the empirical observations made from this research sets the first foundational baseline argument that such authority could be effective. Nevertheless, the effect could be short lived as the collective action process involves other factors that could interact with such external engagement, eventually leading to the effect being moderated or even offset. This is this latter point that gives a strong reason for the ICA research to explore for its future research agenda. Second, the research identifies a significant, sometimes dominating, effect of macro-level sociopolitical and economic contextual factors that could be interacting with the effect of external imposition in collaborative dynamics. To a certain extent, this is an even more important finding than the effect of the external imposition because such contextual forces show a persistent and long term effect on collaborative actions in many cases greater than external imposition. The ICA model, as well as many other collaborative models such as CGR or the trust-building approach, never seem to be able to acknowledge the role of such contextual influence. In this sense, this research contributes significantly to the ICA model. Objective 3: Policy recommendations for the local governments (including Hong Kong government) on how to engage the central government in regional collaboration This research has led to the formation of several important policy recommendations that have been published by Public Administration Review in its section "Evidence for Practice" (Also see Zhao, C., Wang, X., Cheung, P., Xu, J. 2023 "Influence of external authorities on collaborative frictions", Public Administration Review 83(3): 603-622). These policy recommendations were presented with local policy makers (especially HK government) in mind. They intend to help HK policy makers to make informed decision on possible external influence (mainly the central government in Beijing) in engaging collaborative activities. These recommendations are: • A large number of collaborative frictions can occur when collaborating institutions with different governing procedures and institutions interact • The engagement of an external authority may improve collaboration through reducing collaborative frictions in short term • External imposition may not necessarily improve collaboration in long term • Controversial political issues could increase difficulty for collaboration through creating or augmenting frictions in collaborating institutions • Controversial political issues could also make the external authority’s engagement in collaboration difficult to achieve expected outcomes Objective 4: Policy recommendations for the central government and mainland local governments on how to engage collaborative activities in regional collaborative networks Besides the above five recommendations for policy makers including the central policy maker and Mainland local government authorities, this research also specifies several key conditions for the central government who is pondering when to engage in local collaborative activities. These conditions are two fold. At the very fundamental level, the central government engages based on the strategic significance of a policy issue. In most cases in policy fields that are not in the strategic significant areas of the central government, the government most likely chooses not to engage at all even if collaborative disputes evolve to create significant difficulty. We demonstrate this point in a debate article published in Public Money and Management PMM (Wang X., and Xu, J., 2022: "The central government's capacity building role in policy implementation in China, 42(2)), in which most collaborative activities in this research setting between HK and mainland local governments can be classified as "normal" instead of "campaign-style" or "war-like". The second set of conditions conners on when the central government may choose to engage during a "normal" policy dominance when collaborative frictions accelerate. There are three such recommendations for the central government made by this research: (1) The frictions happen frequently and they concentrate in a certain project or a policy area, (2) These frictions may be caused by certain macro-level contextual factors that suggest, without external intervention, the frictions would continue due to these contextual causes, (3) it is commonly perceived by the external authority that the external engagement designed (with various forms of strategies) could bring a significant benefit with manageable cost. All these conditions have to be met for the external authority to engage. These recommendations were made explicitly in our article accepted by The China Review (Wang, X., Li, J., Yuan, Z., and Xu, J. forthcoming "Chinese Central Government Intervention in Local Policy Implementation Capacity Building—When and Why", The China Review). Objective 5: Publications in high-quality academic journals and textbooks I have published three articles in top-ranked SSCI journals. (1) Wang X., and Xu, J., 2022: "The central government's capacity building role in policy implementation in China, Public Money and Management 42(2) (2) Zhao, C., Wang, X., Cheung, P., Xu, J. 2023 "Influence of external authorities on collaborative frictions", Public Administration Review 83(3): 603-622. SCPA Best Article Award (3) Wang, X., Li, J., Yuan, Z., and Xu, J. (forthcoming) "Chinese Central Government Intervention in Local Policy Implementation Capacity Building—When and Why", The China Review. Accepted 9 January 2024. Paper and evidence of acceptance attached in the Output section)

11604120.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604120.value: We use the grant to collect a large database measuring the stakeholders' disagreements and disputes during collaboration. We call these disagreements "collaborative friction". We collected more than 960 frictions in four major collaborative infrastructure projects between Hong Kong and mainland China due to the adoption of the one-country-two-system IC2S model of governance. This large and unique database allow us to conduct comprehensive analysis on the research questions raised in the GRF proposals. The results can be generally grouped into three sets of findings on (a) the general theoretical implication on the role of external imposition, (b) more specific implication on the circumstances in which the Chinese central government engages as a key external force, (c) the ability of these findings to be employed more generally to provide a generic explanation on the so-called China Model on policy implementation. (a) The findings on general theoretical implication Finding 1: There are a large number of frictions in collaborative projects. These frictions are concentrated in certain projects during institutional players’ interactions, and they are often contextualized by political issues Finding 2: The central government’s engagement appears to be part of a governing response or reaction to the frictions Finding 3: There may be a significant, but limited, effect of central imposition Finding 4: Socio-political issues could hinder collaboration (b) The findings specific on the circumstances in which the Central government engages Finding 1: the Central government engages when collaborative frictions become frequent and more importantly concentrated in a project Finding 2: the Central government engages when the frictions are caused or contextualised by certain types of contextual forces (socio-political or those of national security for example) Finding 3: the Central government engages when such interventions are perceived to lead to significant policy outcomes (c) The findings on the generic China model of central imposition in local policy implementation We develop three policy implementation capacity-building scenarios based on the strategic significance of a policy domain for normal, campaign-style, or warlike circumstances. In a generic model that considers the purpose, time range, spatial scale, policy goal ambiguity, changing pattern, capacity-building focus, and local autonomy, the central government's role can be classified as (a) guiding and collaborating for a policy of normal significance, (b) driving for a policy of campaign-style implementation, and (c) dominating in a warlike policy circumstance.

11604120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604120.value: These above findings have been integrated into my current and future research, in three generic directions. First, the finding that sociopolitical and other contextual factors play an interacting role with the external imposition has led to a new research effort to examine the role of contextual forces in collaboration, and how such role interacts with external imposition in influencing collaborative actions. Second, I am developing a study, with potential future GRF funding, to study the role of external imposition in resolving collaborative disputes, and this effect is framed within the existing literature on collaborative capacity building (especially the collaborative governance regime CGR) model. Third, I am starting an idea to examine how external imposition may lead to collaborative institutional development. In this effort, I would like to examine the role of external engagement in collaborative institutionalisation, and examine if institutionalisation leads to an outcome commonly desired by collaborating partners

11604120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604120.value: When institutional frictions threaten to disrupt collaborations, an external authority can be brought in to resolve disputes. How effective is such external imposition? What are the institutional circumstances in which it works? Framed within the latest literature, specially the collaborative governance regime literature, which sees established procedures and institutions as a critical collaborative capacity, this project collects a comprehensive database on a unique concept—collaborative friction—to explore the role of external imposition in collaboration among entities with significant institutional differences in Hong Kong and mainland China. I examined 965 recorded collaborative frictions from four large collaborative infrastructure projects between governments in Hong Kong and mainland China. The finding suggests a significant, but limited, effect of the central government’s imposition on collaborative frictions. I find the specific circumstances in where such central intervention is effective. I also find a significant role of sociopolitical circumstances in collaboration. Based on the findings, I make several theoretical propositions articulating external imposition’s role in collaboration. I make policy recommendations based on these findings

11604420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604420.value: 冷戰初期美新處在香港資助的翻譯研究

11604420.label: Project Objectives
11604420.value: To review current literature on USIS-Commissioned translations and identify the social and cultural context against which these translation are shaped; To Study the Chinese translations by Mae Soong. Mae’s husband, Stephen Soong served the USIS as the director for the Book Translation Program in the 1950s, and Mae, a full time employer with USIS, was also engaged in the program by translating American books, both literary pieces and non-fictions. Through textual analysis and close reading of paratextual materials, it aims to identify how Mae Soong works, or collaborate to be more specific, with her patrons in materializing the propaganda purpose; To study the English translations of the USIS-funded anti-communism writings by Maria Yen and Chen Chi-ying. Different from the USIS-commissioned translations of American books, these anti-communist writings were expected to disclose the brutality of communist rule in the newly founded People’s Republic of China to win Chinese readers in South Eastern Asian area and beyond. Then, some of these writings were further sponsored by USIS to be translated into English for a different readership who has no access to the Chinese language. Therefore, it merits further academic attention on how they were shaped through translation or adaptation to use the exact term by the translators for these writings. Both the Cold War Studies and Translation Studies have developed fast in the past decades, and this project aims to provide interdisciplinary research bridging Translation Studies and Cold War studies.

11604420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604420.value: 冷戰研究與翻譯研究之間錯綜複雜的關係近年來得到學界越來越多的關注。二十世紀五十年代，與中國南部邊界毗鄰的香港在時間和空間維度上佔據重要位置，在這裡英國殖民政府、美國新聞處和剛剛執政的中國共產黨展開隱蔽戰爭；而撤退到臺灣的國民黨也參與到香港的政治與意識形態鬥爭中來。在冷戰格局中，美國採取圍堵的外交政策，而美新處的主要職能和目的就是進行反共宣傳。美國的這一政策如何落實與實現呢？香港的美新處主要負責生產反共材料，包括譯書計畫和支持反共的中文寫作。 本項研究以冷戰為背景，首先探討美新處在港資助的翻譯。通過譯書計畫，美國書籍的中文翻譯一方面服務于美國的文化輸出政策——以宋鄺文美的美國文學中譯為例，另一方面，美新處授意或資助的中文寫作，也進一步受資助翻譯成英文。美新處資助的中文寫作的英文翻譯也得到學界越來越多的關注，如燕歸來和陳紀瀅的作品英譯。本項研究將從微觀史角度出發，結合政府檔案館相關史料，對文本進行深度描述。研究計畫希望可以將冷戰研究與翻譯研究 聯繫起來。

I managed to settle down at my current host institution, Lingnan University and conducted the research there. The pandemic also made data collection difficult. Even though, I visited local libraries and record office for materials related to the project. My gratitude goes to all those who helped in the past few years.

Then, some of these writings were further sponsored by USIS to be translated into English for a different readership who has no access to the Chinese language. Therefore, it merits further academic attention on how they were shaped through translation or adaptation to use the exact term by the translators for these writings.

Both the Cold War Studies and Translation Studies have developed fast in the past decades, and this project aims to provide interdisciplinary research bridging Translation Studies and Cold War studies.

11604420.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604420.value: My literature review reveals that USIS-Commissioned translations are gaining more and more attention, and against this backgroud, my study is well situated in these attempts. Mae Soong and her husband are two key figures in my research and their translation activities are explored in my research output (LI 2022; 李波、刘美隆2022）. Mae Soong's case is put in a big picture, i.e. the translations in World Today, a USIS-Funded periodical at the beginning years of the cultural cold war in Hong Kong. Stephen Soong is a key figure in the history of Hong Kong Translation Society, which was explored in my Chinese article with Miss Liu Meilong. With a thick description of the social cultural background in Hong Kong, I did close reading to Maria Yen's self-translation of her Chinese work into English with the help of McCarthy. The article has been accepted for publication in a collected volume to be published in 2025 (please see Part C, LI 2025). The archives for this study have been read carefully and it has been developed into a journal article submitted to a reputable journal (LI 2024, submitted).

11604420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604420.value: The magazine, World Today, carried many book reviews, including reviews of translated works. I have presented the findings at an international conference and will develop it into a journal article to be submitted to a reputable journal soon.

11604420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604420.value: The research findings are materialized in several journal articles both in Chinese and English, which help us to understand what happened to the translation scenario in the early years of the cold war in Hong Kong. The intertwined relationship between the Btitish colonial government, the USIS, the Chinese Communist Party and Kuomintang in Taiwan, etc, proves to be very complicated. The ideological conflict among these stakeholder are elaborated in the published papers. The research project is of interest to scholars in Cold War studies and translation studies as well, and I was invited by the Hong Kong Translation Society to give a public talk on the research findings.

11605020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605020.value: 探究香港對自動駕駛汽車的道德困境的社會共識

11605020.label: Project Objectives
11605020.value: To gain a comprehensive understanding of the process by which individuals interpret and respond to the moral dilemmas involved in the use of autonomous vehicles, and how it is influenced by cultural differences between Hong Kong, China, and the United States. To provide practical guidelines for developing and implementing culturally specific public policies for the promotion and regulation of autonomous vehicles. To offer a framework for reaching social consensus about the moral dilemmas pertaining to autonomous vehicles. To initiate global research and promote collaboration with the industry by providing strategic plans and guidelines for autonomous vehicle-related business ventures and policy implementation. To disseminate the key findings of this study by publishing at least one article in a top journal and presenting the work at a high-profile international conference.

To provide practical guidelines for developing and implementing culturally specific public policies for the promotion and regulation of autonomous vehicles.
To offer a framework for reaching social consensus about the moral dilemmas pertaining to autonomous vehicles.

To disseminate the key findings of this study by publishing at least one article in a top journal and presenting the work at a high-profile international conference.

11605020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605020.value: Autonomous vehicles are fast becoming a reality. There is a corresponding need to protect the public interest and address the moral dilemmas that arise from the adoption of this technology. For example, an autonomous vehicle may encounter situations in which it must sacrifice its passenger to save one or more pedestrians (or vice versa), but there is no current social consensus on the moral acceptability of such a decision. Thus, an empirical investigation is warranted into how individuals interpret and respond to the moral issues involved. To investigate these issues, the proposed study will involve an online experiment in which participants are exposed to three variations of a sacrificial dilemma that requires an autonomous vehicle to make a non-utilitarian (self-interested/protective), utilitarian (self-sacrificial), or strongly utilitarian decision to save or kill its passenger, while imagining themselves to be either a bystander or as a passenger in the vehicle. Participants will complete a survey questionnaire that elicits their moral judgment, moral reasoning, attitude toward the vehicle and purchase intention, and their perceptions of its intelligence and safety. The proposed study will thus shed light on how individuals adopt different moral reasoning strategies (rationalization vs. decoupling) to process moral dilemmas according to their viewpoint (bystander vs. passenger), and how this process shapes their moral judgment and perceptions of the vehicle. This experiment will be conducted in Hong Kong, China, and the United States to examine how culture shapes perceptions of autonomous vehicles. Different cultures have their own standards and moral systems (Cook, 1999), and many researchers have described the cultural differences between Eastern and Western cultures according to a dichotomy between collectivism and individualism (Siegal et al., 2001; Jackson et al., 2008). Given that collectivist and individualist values co-exist in Hong Kong (Lee & Choi, 2006; Hofstede Insights, 2017), the study findings will help us understand how hybrid (Hong Kong), collectivist (China), and individualist (United States) cultures construe and resolve the ethical dilemmas involved in the use of autonomous vehicles. These findings will provide evidence for the notion that morality is “culturally variable” (Haidt, 2007). 隨著自動駕駛汽車的普及，公眾對於技術帶來的潛在道德困境的關注也隨之增加。例如，自動駕駛汽車可能會面臨必須犧牲其乘客以拯救一個或多個行人的情境（反之亦然），但公眾對此類現實問題尚未達成共識。 本研究將採用線上實驗的方式，讓參與者想像自己作為目睹困境的旁觀者或者車上乘客的身份，面對三種道德困境——非效益性，效益性或高度效益性。隨後，參與者將完成一份調查問卷測量其道德判斷、道德推理策略（合理化或解耦）、對汽車的態度和購買意圖以及對汽車智能性和安全性的感知。 除香港以外，此實驗還將在中國大陸和美國開展。不同的文化擁有不同的道德判斷標準（Cook, 1999）。東方（集體主義）和西方（個人主義）文化差異也體現在道德價值體系中（Siegal等, 2001; Jackson等, 2008）。鑑於集體主義和個人主義價值觀並存於香港（Lee & Choi, 2006; Hofstede Insights, 2017），此研究將有助於理解不同文化如何詮釋和解決自動駕駛汽車帶來的道德困境，從而驗證“道德作為文化變量”的概念（Haidt, 2007）。

11605820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605820.value: 情感和網絡在當代社運中的展現：香港抗議之夏的公眾情緒和動員結構

11605820.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11605820.value: Prof Fu, King Wa Prof Ma, Ngok

11605820.label: Project Objectives
11605820.value: To explain the emergence, dynamics, and significance of the massive and resilient protests in Hong Kong in 2019; To examine the interconnected roles of different protest actors and organisations, and unpack the mobilising structure through a social network analysis; To explain the changing public sentiments and meaning-making processes of the protesters through a computational content analysis; To develop middle-range theories on modern-day collective actions through the communication and cultural approaches; and To generate evidence-based data that can effectively map public sentiments and enhance public policy planning in Hong Kong.
rows: To explain the emergence, dynamics, and significance of the massive and resilient protests in Hong Kong in 2019;
To examine the interconnected roles of different protest actors and organisations, and unpack the mobilising structure through a social network analysis;
To explain the changing public sentiments and meaning-making processes of the protesters through a computational content analysis;
To develop middle-range theories on modern-day collective actions through the communication and cultural approaches; and
To generate evidence-based data that can effectively map public sentiments and enhance public policy planning in Hong Kong.

11605820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605820.value: This study will examine the public sentiments and mobilising structure in Hong Kong’s summer of dissent. Following increased crackdown on social activists and tightened controls over civil liberties after the Umbrella Movement in 2014, the opposition is marginalised and its movement networks are impeded. Despite the absence of visible political opportunities and organisational resources, millions of Hong Kong citizens took to the streets in summer 2019 to protest against a proposed extradition bill. The mass mobilisation evolved from a single-issue contention to incorporate structural claims, escalated tactics, and inter-group solidarity unparalleled in Hong Kong’s activism. It is imperative, therefore, to explore which groups of citizens choose to engage in collective action, and how they coordinate with others, deliberate on tactics, and construct protest frames. Borrowing from the cultural and communication approaches in social movement studies, this study will examine the formation of new meanings and networks during what perceived to be a leaderless movement. The alternative lens infers that culture or digital tool is not only a formative condition of social movements, but also comprises a constitutive role in shaping movement characteristics and dynamics. First, we will apply computational content analysis to trace the meaning-making process among diverse groups of protest actors. Meaning-making refers to the process of articulating and disseminating a set of coherent narratives and frames for the movement. Second, we will conduct social network analysis and interviews with activists to reveal the characteristics of connective action during online and offline interactions. Mobilising structure is measured by the degree of connectiveness among individual protestors, channels of mobilisation, and mechanisms of deliberation. Third, we will assess if increased length of protest amplifies certain actors’ credibility and intensifies polarisation of opinion, producing informal leaders and trusted networks. This project aims to survey whether Hong Kong’s summer of dissent features an ideal form of leaderless movement sustained by digital information technologies, and if so, what networks and mechanisms ensure mobilisation and coordination over time? By blending content analysis and network analysis, this study will produce original and rich data to explain the pattern, trajectory, and meaning of contentious politics in Hong Kong. This evidence-based research will advance the comparative study and conceptualisation of modern-day protests, inform policymakers on how to map public sentiments and provide insights on political reconciliation after upheaval. It will also address the growing academic and public interest in Hong Kong politics and society following the summer of dissent. 這項目將研究「香港抗議之夏」的公眾情緒和動員結構。2014年「雨傘運動」後，國家對社會的抓控有所增加，反對派的運動資源也受約束。儘管缺乏明顯的政治機會和組織資源，但2019年夏季仍有數以百萬計香港市民上街反引渡條例。大規模動員從單一問題的爭論，演變成包含結構主張，激進行動和集體團結。這些現象都是香港社運歷史所不常見的。因此，有必須探究哪些民眾選擇參與集體行動，他們如何相互配合、考量抗議策略、並建立運動架框。 借鑒社會運動研究中的文化和傳播方式，本研究將考察抗爭的含義和網絡，如何在被視為無領導的運動形態中形成。這種切入點，視文化或數字工具不僅是社會運動的形成條件，更有塑造運動特徵和動態起構成作用。首先，我們將應用計算機內容分析來追踪抗議者不同群體之間的抗爭含義形成過程。含義的產生是指為運動表達和傳播一套連貫的敘述和框架的過程。其次，我們將進行社交網絡分析並與活動家進行訪談，以揭示在線和線下互動過程中的動員結構特徵。動員結構是通過各個示威者之間的聯繫程度，動員渠道和審議機制來衡量的。第三，我們將評估抗議活動的持續時間，是否加劇了輿論的分化、增加了某些個人或組織的公信力、並形成非正式領導人及某些信賴的網絡。 這項目旨在調查「香港抗議之夏」是否具有一種無領導者的運動形式，即由數字信息和情感支持的；如果是，那麼哪些網絡和機制可以確保長期動員和協調？結合內容分析和網絡分析，本研究將產生原始且豐富的數據，以解釋香港爭議性政治的模式，軌跡和含義。這項基於證據的研究，將推進現代社運的比較研究和概念化，為決策者提供有關如何繪製公眾情緒的信息，並為劇變後的政治和解提供素材。

11606420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606420.value: 阿爾瓦爾·阿爾托： 有機都市主義

11606420.label: Project Objectives
11606420.value: Reposition the work of Aalto between the mid-1930s and the mid-1950s as the historical moment in which the first coherent conception of organic urbanism was proposed within modern planning. Investigate the technical advancement that enabled Alvar Aalto to split maps into layers for further analysis, producing an embryonal version of contemporary geographic information systems. Analyze the morphology of the constitutional elements (buildings and related open spaces, lots, and streets) of plans and urban design projects drafted between 1934 and 1956 to individuate generative patterns at different scales (building/lot, street/block, city, region) and prove the hypothesis of their being homothetic. Examine the archetypical typology of the pavilion in light of the findings of the morphological analysis to prove the hypothesis that the pavilion is the basic unit for Aalto’s conception of organic urbanism. Act as a catalyst for stronger interdisciplinarity among the contiguous fields of architecture and urban planning by demonstrating their mutualism in Aalto’s conception and thereby challenging current hegemonic discourses which advocate their independence.

Investigate the technical advancement that enabled Alvar Aalto to split maps into layers for further analysis, producing an embryonal version of contemporary geographic information systems.

Analyze the morphology of the constitutional elements (buildings and related open spaces, lots, and streets) of plans and urban design projects drafted between 1934 and 1956 to individuate generative patterns at different scales (building/lot, street/block, city, region) and prove the hypothesis of their being homothetic.

Examine the archetypical typology of the pavilion in light of the findings of the morphological analysis to prove the hypothesis that the pavilion is the basic unit for Aalto’s conception of organic urbanism.

11606420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606420.value: Alvar Aalto is Finland’s world-renowned architect, a notable pioneer of the Modern Movement, and a leading exponent of an organic approach to architecture. His long-celebrated work is currently of rising interest, considering its still unsurpassed capacity to offer high degrees of well-being. Yet, his work has been interpreted almost exclusively as a contribution to the field of architecture and furniture design. Such interpretation leads to the underestimation of the fundamental role played by urbanism in his proposition. What are the characteristics of Aalto’s conception of urbanism? Can the revelation of this conception contribute to a better understanding and conservation of his work? What lessons can we learn from Aalto’s approach to urbanism? This research aims to reestablish the relevance of Aalto’s work in the field of urbanism by producing new evidence thereof, originating from an organic proposition based on the “pavilion” as a structural and functional unit. This project originates from the research by design carried out for the restoration of the Finnish Pavilion at the Venice Biennale, and the observation of undisclosed original documents and drawings recently discovered in the private archive of one of Aalto’s former collaborators. This research will primarily rely on the analysis of the recently found materials, and others made available by the Alvar Aalto Foundation. This mixed methods research combines historical-contextual, document, morphological, and typological analyses. Using the masterplans, projects, writings, and speeches that Aalto produced from the mid-1930s to the mid-1950s, this research aims to provide evidence on how his conception of organic urbanism is (1) groundbreaking and not adequately valued; (2) made possible by a technical innovation; (3) formed as a fractal; (4) based on the archetypical typology of the pavilion as the fundamental unit of structure and function; and (5) the framework that can offer a new key for the analysis of his work. The significance of this research does not only lie in the rehabilitation of Alvar Aalto as an urbanist, nor solely in the implications for the conservation of his work. The findings will redound to the benefit of large portions of the urban population, providing an alternative to our current mode of haphazard suburban development that is producing alienating living and working conditions. 阿爾瓦爾·阿爾托（Alvar Aalto）為世界著名的芬蘭建築師，同時為現代主義及有機建築倡導者，他的作品久負盛名，有效提高人們生活質素，因而受到越來越多關注。因他在建築及傢俱設計領域的貢獻尤其顯著，人們往往低估/忽視了由他所提出的都市主義概念及其基本功能。到底阿爾托的都市主義有什麼特徵呢？這種概念的啟示能否更有助後人理解其作品，繼而把其作品保育得更好呢？而我們又可以從了解阿爾託的城市化方法有什麼得著呢？ 這項研究以阿爾托把亭樓視為一結構和功能單元的有機主張為本，整合出新論據，以重新確立其作品與都市主義的關聯性。此研究以威尼斯雙年展 (La Biennale di Venezia)芬蘭館所進行的設計研究為本，透過觀察曾與阿爾託合作的建築師的私人檔案內未被公開的原文和圖紙，連同最近發現的資料，及由Alvar Aalto基金會提供的材料，進行分析。研究方法結合了歷史背景，文獻， 型態學和類型學。利用阿爾托從1930年代中到1950年代中的總體規劃、 項目、 著作及演講， 有效闡述他所提出的有機都市主義的特徵包括：（1） 有突破性但未被充分重視； （2）需依靠新科技才得以發展 ；（3）以碎片形成 ；（4）以原型的亭樓結構及功能為基礎； （5）以新角度/方法分析其作品的框架 這項研究的意義不僅在於阿爾瓦·阿爾托（Alvar Aalto）作為一名城市主義者的思想復興，也不僅在於加強對其作品的保育工作。是次研究能讓大多數城市人口受益，為我們目前的郊區無序發展模式提供了另一選擇，使人們不至於在日常生活及工作中與人關係疏離。

11606620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606620.value: 家庭風險如何影響股票市場的參與

11606620.label: Project Objectives
11606620.value: By examining the portfolio investment behavior of households in 20 countries, we aim at examining how households’ pension and insurance coverage affect their portfolio choice on risky assets. In particular, we will examine how different sources of uncertainty affect the decision to invest. We will generate policy implications by analyzing 1) how country-heterogeneity in the completeness of the insurance/pension market affect households’ risky asset holdings; 2) how household demographics and risks affect their investment in risky assets.
rows: By examining the portfolio investment behavior of households in 20 countries, we aim at examining how households’ pension and insurance coverage affect their portfolio choice on risky assets. In particular, we will examine how different sources of uncertainty affect the decision to invest.

We will generate policy implications by analyzing 1) how country-heterogeneity in the completeness of the insurance/pension market affect households’ risky asset holdings; 2) how household demographics and risks affect their investment in risky assets.

11606620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606620.value: 選擇家庭投資組合的重要部分是風險的選擇。正如Kimball（1993）所說, 家庭背景風險的程度（這種風險不能完全保險，無法控制）會影響他們承擔其他風險的意願。有不同的不確定性來源自年齡差異。處於工作年齡的年輕家庭主要面臨收入不確定性，而年齡較大的家庭家庭面臨壽命、醫療費用和醫療保健需求的不確定性。對於工作家庭，針對工人的社會福利計劃，例如社會保障計劃和職業退休金計劃對於使收入不確定性多樣化至關重要。對於老年家庭，健康保險可以說是針對醫療保險最重要的保險之一。 這個項目旨在研究中央養老金/保險計劃如何影響收入和醫療費用風險，因而影響家庭承擔財務風險的意願。隨著醫療成本的上升，來自對財富的負面健康衝擊可能非常嚴重。 Himmelstein等人的研究（2005）發現在2001年，在五個聯邦法院提出的所有個人破產申請中，有一半是由於醫療費用引起的。 就我們所知，我們的項目為有關股票市場投資的文獻做出了貢獻是第一個使用統一的國際家庭數據研究家庭風險與金融投資行為之間的關係。數據取自歐洲的歐洲體系家庭財務和消費調查（HFCS）數據庫，其中包含來自20個歐盟國家的個人和家庭數據，以及涵蓋其資產持有情況、不同類型資產的價值的詳細信息、養老金和保險計劃，個人和家庭人口統計數據。在實證分析中，我們採用了Hu，Munkin和Trivedi（2015）的內生模型來說明購買補充保險或自願退休金的決定。 該項目的結果可以闡明家庭的股票市場參與率以及風險資產的持有可能會受到以下因素的影響：1）保險/養老金制度和 2）家庭特徵。

11606620.label: Realisation of objectives
11606620.value: (1) To examine how different sources of uncertainty (background risk) affect ones’ investment in risky assets: (a) Model set up This paper realized the objectives by performing an in-depth examination of the portfolio investment behaviors of households over two decades in relation to three important types of background risks (uncertainties) --- income risk, unemployment risk and health risk. Background risk refers to risk that is not fully insurable and is beyond one’s control. As Kimball (1993) put it, the degree of background risk of households would affect individuals’ willingness to bear other risks, including financial risk. Background risk is generally closely related to ones’ attributes and family profile. To garner the background information of investors, we explore a longitudinal survey dataset spanning two decades to examine the effects of households' background risks on their portfolio choices. The dataset contains 30,898 year-household observations, covering detailed information on income, employment status, health status, financial wealth composition, portfolio investment and a wide range of demographics (e.g. marital status, number of children, household size, age, gender, educational attainment, working hours, and parents' financial background). The richness of the data allows us to amalgamate various background risks in one reduced form model. (b) Findings Towards this objective, the major findings of our paper are as follows: Health risk emerges as the most significant factor, reducing participation probability by 5.21% and lowering the risky asset ratio by 17.2% for those involved. Structural income risk exerts a stronger influence on financial risk-taking compared to transitory income risk, with a non-monotonic effect observed - individuals at both the lowest and highest income risk quantiles demonstrate a stronger interest in financial risk-taking. Perceived unemployment risk acts as a deterrent, with a one-standard-deviation increase lowering participation by 4.23% and the risky asset ratio by 11.27%. Prolonged unemployment exacerbates this effect, reducing participation by 1.55% and the risky asset ratio by 3.41% for every 3-month increase in duration. (c) Economic Significance To contextualize our empirical findings, we report heatmaps to illustrate the predicted participation probability and the risky asset ratio in relation to various degrees of background risks. It is observed that (1) higher health risk is associated with lower intensity in risky asset investment. The predicted participation probability reduces from 9.32% to 4.09% and the predicted risky asset ratio lowers from 26.75% to 21.45% when the health risk deteriorates from “Excellent” (level 1) to “Poor” (level 5), evaluated at the median level of income risk (the 5th decile). Similarly, the predicted participation probability reduces from 15.28%to 5.98% and the predicted risky asset ratio lowers from 31.90% to 22.79% when the health risk deteriorates from “Excellent” (level 1) to “Poor” (level 5), evaluated at the median level of unemployment risk. On the other hand, the predicted participation probability reduces from 12.76% to 2.41% and the predicted risky asset ratio lowers from 29.85% to 18.60% when the unemployment risk (probability of job loss) increases from the bottom decile to the top decile, evaluated at the median level of income risk (the 5th decile group of income risk). Similarly, the predicted participation probability declines from 7.12% to 2.27% and the predicted risky asset ratio lowers from 24.73% to 18.56% when the unemployment risk (unemployment duration) increases from below the median to above the median, evaluated at the median level of income risk. Furthermore, along the income risk spectrum, we observe that income risk has a U-shaped impact on the predicted participation probability and risky asset ratio. We find higher predicted probability and ratio at the two tails of the distribution of the income risk, and the predicted probability and ratio decline in the middle range of the distribution. For example, the predicted participation probability is 15.7% at the left tail and 14.73% at the right tail of the income risk, and declines to 9.32% at the middle level of income risk, when evaluated at a health status of “good” or better (health risk at level 1 to 3). Similarly, the predicted risky asset ratio is at 31.40% and 31.12% at the two extremes of the income risk distribution, and lowers to 26.75% in the middle percentile. The same pattern is found when evaluated at most levels of unemployment risk. Lastly, we find that the predicted participation probability is highest at 13.77% for individuals with the best health level (level 1 of health risk) and lowest unemployment risk (level 1 of unemployment risk), and lowest at 1.18% at the opposite ends of the risk spectrum (level 5 for both risk types). (2) To generate policy implications by analysing how country-heterogeneity in the completeness of the insurance market affect households’ risky asset holdings (a) Findings We perform a counterfactual analysis to predict the potential increase in the participation rates and risky asset ratios if universal health service coverage were extended to the entire population across 20 European countries surveyed in European Central Bank’s Household Finance and Consumption Survey (HFCS) alongside the US. The predicted increments in participation probability and risky asset ratios for each country are depicted, varying from 0.29% for the US, Finland, and Belgium to 0.86% for Latvia in participation probability, and from 1.13% in countries like the US, Luxembourg, Belgium, Italy, Germany, and Poland to 2.49% in Finland for the risky asset ratio. (b) Policy implications Our findings confirm the positive impact of health insurance in promoting financial risk-taking, thus underscores the importance of universal health insurance coverage in addressing under-participation and suboptimal allocation in the risky asset market. Utilizing the estimated effects of health insurance, a counterfactual analysis is performed on 193 countries, ranging from low-income, middle-income and high-income. Our analysis predicts potential global increases in participation probability ranging from 0.57 to 2.1 percentage points and corresponding rises in the risky asset ratio from 2.27 to 8.38 percentage points if health service coverage were to transition to full universal coverage from the 2021 level. These findings underscore the transformative potential of universal health insurance in enhancing financial risk-taking behavior globally.
