11606620.label: Major findings and research outcome
11606620.value: (1) Major findings This paper explores how income, health, and unemployment risks influence households' decisions to engage in the risky asset market. Analysing a longitudinal dataset, we find distinct effects of these risks on participation and asset allocation. Health risk has the strongest negative impact, reducing participation by 5.21% and asset allocation by 17.2%. Structural income risk significantly impacts financial risk-taking, with a non-monotonic effect observed. Higher perceived unemployment risk decreases participation by 4.23% and asset allocation by 11.27%. Health insurance positively influences financial risk-taking, increasing participation by 2.97% and asset allocation by 11.33%. Utilizing the estimated effects of health insurance, a counterfactual analysis on 193 countries predicts that universal health insurance coverage could improve participation by 0.57 to 2.1 percentage points and asset allocation by 2.27 to 8.38 percentage points globally. (2) Research outcome This research funding has supported several scholarly activities and generated the following outcomes. First, a research paper entitled “Impact of Background Risks on Household Financial Risk-Taking: Insights and Policy Implications” has been written and will soon be submitted for journal publication. This paper has engaged an international research team, which includes faculty from Columbia University and a PhD student from my university. Second, the paper was accepted for presentation at the Annual Western Economic Association International Conference in San Diego. The presentation facilitated valuable scholarly exchanges with the discussant and conference participants. Third, this project has provided an opportunity for a PhD student from my university to contribute as a co-author. This collaboration has been useful in enhancing the student’s research skills and experience in writing professional academic papers.

11606620.value: Given the finding from this project that background risk has significant impact on individuals’ motivation to invest in risky financial assets, we can expand the scope of research in the future to cover a wider range of asset classes, such as cryptocurrencies and speculative real estate.

11606820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606820.value: The proposed research project conceptualizes and investigates the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR)’s international trade law and policy as a triangular structure (composed of unilateral, bilateral, and multilateral rules). While we know that the HKSAR does act in these three ways, it is not always clear why it pursues different strategies or whether there are any discernible patterns to its behavior. Examples of the HKSAR’s unilateral behavior can be found in its extra-territorial application of competition law or when it applies trade defence instruments. Bilaterally, the HKSAR concludes agreements with states individually, in group units, or with international organizations, while the most obvious expression of its multilateral approach in international economic relations lies in its membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO). This research project is not limited to a classic doctrinal analysis of the law in Hong Kong; instead, the research focuses on the law in motion, i.e. the logic and consequences of Hong Kong Triple-Track Strategy in international trade rules and policies. More specifically, the proposed research examines how the legal order of the HKSAR shapes its international behavior, and the impact of the triangular approach on domestic laws and policies. In this respect, this project uses a multifaceted research methodology which will primarily be qualitative in nature, employing, in particular, scoping round-tables and qualitative interviews. The research topic s important. While the HKSAR’s political project remains specific, its central characteristic remains that of an economic unit, and its international relations continue to be dominated by this feature. Although the HKSAR’s economic relations cover a wide array of areas ranging from competition policy to international aviation law, we propose to focus our research on the international relations of the HKSAR as they relate to trade and investment. Trade is the only area of international relations where the HKSAR acts as a single unit under a legally binding multilateral framework — at the WTO. Despite being one of the leading trade and investment world center trading blocs, however, the HKSAR is obliged to conform to the rules of the multilateral trading system, which places restrictions on its freedom to act unilaterally and bilaterally. The project examines these issues in detail, analysing the HKSAR’s motivations and methods for pursuing these objectives at different levels or venues, and exploring the consequences for the domestic structure of the HKSAR system and its stated policy goal of coherence in its international relations. 香港國際貿易投資法之剖析：單邊主義、雙邊主義與多邊主義的理論和影響 該項目的目的是解釋香港特別行政區為何在其國際貿易和投資關係中採用這種方法，描述其如何運用必要的方法來管理三軌戰略，並確定香港特別行政區的法律，政治和經濟影響。它的方法。追求這些目標將加深我們對香港特別行政區國際關係的了解，並為我們提供機會分析香港特別行政區不斷變化的機構動態以及其政策和行動在國內和國際層面之間的關係。在香港特別行政區的貿易戰略背景下探討這些關係，將有助於更清晰地描述香港特別行政區在當代區域和全球事務中的作用，並就香港特別行政區如何提高其實現地區政策目標的有效性提出建議。 。為了實現這些目標，需要採用多方面的研究方法來調查香港特別行政區的國際經濟關係。該研究項目旨在研究這種三角方法的邏輯，方法和後果，從而實現該項目的總體目標-加強對多邊主義及其與雙邊和單邊主義關係的理解。

11606820.label: Realisation of objectives
11606820.value: In pursuing the comprehensive mapping and examination of the HKSAR's strategic use of various negotiating venues, this project has notably achieved all its primary objectives. One of the chief accomplishments was a detailed assessment of the HKSAR's deliberate exploitation of different venues in the pursuit of trade and trade-related policy objectives. This exploration revealed how these venues served as an indispensable tool in the territory's global trade dynamics, offering insights into the territory's overarching strategies and positioning in the international trade arena. A meticulous mapping exercise was undertaken to understand the past and current practices of the HKSAR in these venues. This activity involved a thorough examination of archives, records, and pertinent literature. In doing so, we unravelled a tapestry of practices that displayed both consistency and evolution in HKSAR’s approach to trade negotiations. It is worth noting that the historical trajectory of HKSAR’s strategies offered a rich understanding of its contemporary stances. In addressing the third objective, a multilayered analysis was conducted to determine if the chosen negotiating venue correlates with the HKSAR’s objectives. The findings were illuminating. For market access, certain venues seemed more favourable, providing the HKSAR with a platform to assert its interests effectively. Meanwhile, other venues were identified as optimal for deeper economic integration, offering insights into HKSAR's strategic choices. A pivotal aspect of this examination was understanding which venues or levels were conducive for shaping sustainable international rules or norms for trade and associated issues. Our research highlighted that the venue chosen indeed had implications for the success of implementation. Additionally, it was discerned that while some venues were apt for HKSAR’s defensive strategies, others were more aligned with its offensive interests. These nuances provided a robust understanding of the territory’s strategic intent and approach in various circumstances. However, the journey to achieving these objectives was not without its challenges. Political events in the HKSAR and the global pandemic posed significant hurdles, especially when it came to engaging with key stakeholders and officials. Their reluctance, given the sensitive nature of the topic, was understandable, but it meant that our primary data gathering took a hit. Nevertheless, to overcome this, the team redoubled efforts in desktop research, and a more intensive analysis of available data was conducted. This, coupled with the virtual engagements and seminars, ensured that the quality of the research was not compromised. The culminating task of this project centred around developing criteria to direct HKSAR in its selection of negotiating venues. It wasn't merely about creating a list; it was about devising a roadmap anchored in historical data, current practices, and future aspirations of the territory. This facet of the project proved to be, in many ways, the most arduous. It required a holistic understanding of the nuances of each venue and how these intricacies intertwined with HKSAR's goals and strategic outlook. Drawing from our vast collection of data, several patterns began to emerge. For instance, venues that were historically favoured for market access negotiations exhibited attributes such as transparency, flexibility, and an established reputation in international trade. An example could be the HKSAR's inclination towards venues like the World Trade Organisation (WTO) when negotiating certain market access provisions. These venues allowed for a comprehensive platform that catered to HKSAR's requirements while simultaneously providing a structured yet adaptable negotiating environment. On the other hand, for objectives tied to deeper economic integration, venues that fostered bilateral or multilateral relationships were observed to be of preference. For instance, in situations where HKSAR sought to build upon existing trade relationships and extend them into areas like services, investment, or intellectual property, venues that allowed for a more nuanced, relationship-driven dialogue seemed the most fitting. The Asian-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum is illustrative in this regard, facilitating engagements that transcend mere trade barriers. With the historical and current practices serving as a robust foundation, we ventured into the realm of prospective strategy. And it was here that the real challenge lay. The global trade landscape is in a state of flux, with emergent powers, shifting alliances, and evolving economic dynamics. Yet, amidst this volatility, HKSAR needed a guiding light, a set of criteria that would not only be relevant today but would remain pertinent in the coming decades. These guidelines were thus crafted to be both specific, capturing the essence of HKSAR's present strategies, and adaptive, encapsulating a vision that aligns with the territory's ambitions. To illustrate, while one criterion emphasised the importance of considering the geopolitical implications of a venue, another stressed the need to evaluate the economic potential and growth trajectories of the partners involved. Furthermore, criteria like these are not stagnant; they evolve and adapt, underscoring the forward-looking perspective we aimed to instil. The research project has generated a variety of outcomes that contribute significantly to our understanding of Hong Kong's place in international economic law and its negotiation strategies. Within the realm of academic publications, five journal articles were produced. Notably, Chaisse and Ji's paper in the Asian Journal of WTO law & Health Policy examined the changing nature of Hong Kong's approach to international dispute settlements. Another piece in the Hong Kong Law Journal highlighted the evolving challenges Hong Kong faces in the context of tax agreements. Other collaborations brought forward discussions about hybrid dispute resolution in Hong Kong and the interplay of international banking with the investment treaty regime. Additionally, the analysis of the United States' Origin Marking Requirement in the American Journal of International Law shed light on specific aspects of international trade laws. The Cambridge University Press featured a chapter that revolved around Hong Kong's approaches in resolving international disputes. This piece gave a comprehensive view of the territory's strategies, integrating both historical and contemporary practices. For a wider audience, a series of blog posts were crafted. Here, Chaisse articulated potential benefits and implications of Hong Kong's prospective RCEP membership. Another post addressed the shifting dynamics of investment treaty arbitration in Hong Kong, offering a broad overview of the subject. The research's findings were further discussed and disseminated through a selection of conferences and workshops. Topics ranged from the intricate relationships between China, Hong Kong, and commercial law, to in-depth examinations of Hong Kong's potential trajectory in trade services and investments. Each presentation served to enhance the discourse and provided an avenue for feedback and collaboration. Professor Chaisse's advisory role with the HK Law Society's Committee on the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership underlined the practical implications and relevance of the research. This collaboration offered an opportunity for the research findings to potentially influence broader strategies and decisions. Lastly, a forthcoming book by Chaisse aims to consolidate the extensive research undertaken during this project. This publication is set to offer an in-depth perspective on Hong Kong's roles and choices in the sphere of international economic law. In sum, despite the roadblocks, the project has not only met its objectives but has also paved the way for future research in the domain, ensuring that HKSAR remains at the forefront of strategic trade negotiations.The project has methodically addressed and examined its core objectives, resulting in a well-rounded set of findings that both inform and shape the discourse on Hong Kong's strategies in international economic law.

11606820.label: Major findings and research outcome
11606820.value: The journey of examining the HKSAR's strategic use of negotiating venues for trade and trade-related objectives led to a plethora of significant findings that have broad implications for both the region and wider international trade paradigms. Delving deep into the historical and present-day practices of the HKSAR revealed a sophisticated blend of strategies that have evolved over time, responding to both internal dynamics and external pressures. One of the most striking revelations was the nuanced way in which the HKSAR positions itself in different venues. For instance, when seeking market access, the HKSAR displayed a preference for venues that provided not just a platform for negotiations but also an environment conducive to fostering long-term relationships. These venues, it became clear, allowed the HKSAR to leverage its historical ties and economic clout to maximum advantage. On the other hand, when the agenda shifted to deeper economic integrations, the choices reflected a pragmatic approach. The HKSAR seemed to gravitate towards platforms that offered not only a space for dialogue but also robust mechanisms for dispute resolution, ensuring that any agreements reached would stand the test of time. Furthermore, the research unearthed a remarkable adaptability in the HKSAR’s approach, especially when navigating the intricate waters of international norms and rules pertaining to trade. There seemed to be a clear understanding that the choice of venue could significantly influence the prospects of successful implementation. Consequently, the HKSAR appeared to carefully calibrate its strategies, using some venues for more defensive postures, while adopting a more assertive stance in others. This intricate dance between defence and offence in its strategic choices provided a fascinating glimpse into the region's understanding of global trade dynamics. Another salient finding was the clear evidence of the HKSAR's forward-thinking approach. While it was evident that past and present strategies were firmly rooted in practical realities, there was also an unmistakable vision for the future. The criteria developed to guide the HKSAR's interactions across venues is a testament to this. These guidelines, while based on historical and current practices, were not merely retrospective. Instead, they offered a strategic blueprint, anticipating potential shifts in global trade dynamics and ensuring that the HKSAR remains agile and proactive in its future engagements. However, it would be remiss not to mention the challenges encountered during the research, particularly in the light of political events and the global pandemic. Yet, these challenges also underscored the resilience of the HKSAR's trade strategies. Even in the face of adversity, the region's commitment to robust and strategic trade negotiations remained unwavering. In essence, this exploration into the HKSAR's negotiating strategies has shed light on a complex web of decisions, priorities, and foresights. While the objectives set out at the beginning provided a roadmap, the findings have enriched the discourse, offering a nuanced understanding of the HKSAR's role and strategy in the ever-evolving world of international trade.

11606820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11606820.value: The research on HKSAR's trade negotiation strategies has opened doors to several intriguing avenues for further exploration. There's potential to delve deeper into how HKSAR's strategies might evolve in response to global economic shifts and geopolitical tensions. Comparing the HKSAR's approach with other key trading entities could offer insights into global best practices. Additionally, the impact of digital transformation on trade negotiations warrants investigation, given the increasing importance of digital economies. A proposed course of action includes: 1. Initiate a comparative study involving HKSAR and other major trading hubs. 2. Explore the nuances of digital trade and how HKSAR could leverage it. 3. Engage with policymakers in HKSAR to understand potential future directions. 4. Collaborate with international trade bodies for a broader perspective. 5. Organise workshops to share findings and gather feedback from stakeholders.

11606820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11606820.value: Our research looked at how Hong Kong, known as HKSAR, makes trade deals with other countries. We studied the different places and methods they use to negotiate these deals. We wanted to understand if they have a strategy for choosing where and how to talk about trade, and if some methods are better than others for certain goals. We also tried to come up with guidelines to help HKSAR decide the best way to negotiate in the future. We found that HKSAR has been active in defending its trade interests, especially when dealing with big players like the US. Our work also showed that understanding HKSAR's approach can teach other places about good trade strategies. In simpler terms, we studied how and where Hong Kong talks business with other countries and made suggestions for them to do it even better. This is important because good trade deals can help Hong Kong's economy and its people.

11607220.value: 中國歷史關於十月妊娠的最早記載

11607220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607220.value: This project investigates the earliest account of the ten-month gestation period in Chinese history, found in a newly discovered manuscript from roughly the Fourth Century B.C.E., and traces the evolution of this and related accounts throughout the First Millennium. By establishing a critical edition for this new discovery, equipped with a full scholarly apparatus, the project will recover an important episode in the history of the reproductive sciences; allow for an opportunity to observe the development of a singular topic from the Warring States down to the Song; and provide a new perspective for considering all of the sources featuring the gestation account. The results will make a significant contribution in the history of science, culture, and the textual traditions of China. 本項計畫研究的是中國歷史關於十月妊娠的最早的描述，根據的是一件新近發現、大約公元前四世紀的竹簡寫本，同時也對相關論述進行上下一千年的追溯。計畫將為新材料整理一個可供閱讀與繼續研究的定本；為古代生殖醫學找回一段失落的歷史；為一個上起戰國、下至宋代的議題進行歷時的個案研究；為所有描述十月妊娠的記載提供一個嶄新的視角。本計畫將對中國的科學史、文化史以及文獻傳統作出一定的貢獻。

11607920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11607920.value: 美國英譯《易經》I Ching 對推廣寰球易學的意義

11607920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607920.value: Originally a divination manual in ancient China, the Yijing 易經 (Book of Changes) has been repeatedly translated into Western languages. Of these translations, only the joint translation by Richard Wilhelm (1873-1930) and Cary Baynes (1883-1977) has made a lasting impact upon Western society. Entitled The I Ching or Book of Changes, the Wilhelm/Baynes translation was first published in the United States in 1950 and then re-issued in the 1960s. At the height of the Vietnam War, it became an icon of the Counter-Culture Movement. To this day, it remains popular in the US and Europe. This research examines the complex process through which the Wilhelm/Baynes translation successfully transformed the Yiing into a “book of wisdom” for Western readers. The research will demonstrate that its success was due to cross-cultural collaborations: (1) the collaboration between Lao Naixuan 勞乃宣 (1843-1921) and Richard Wilhelm in the 1910s to translate the Yijing into German; (2) the collaboration between Richard Wilhelm and Carl Jung (1903-1955) in the 1920s to interpret Chinese divination from the perspective of analytical psychology; and (3) the collaboration between Hellmut Wilhelm (1905-1990, the son of Richard Wilhelm) and Cary Baynes (1883-1977) in the 1960s to render Richard Wilhelm’s I Ging into the American I Ching. To highlight the transformative values of the American I Ching, this research focuses on Cary Baynes. Although not a sinologist by training (and hence often ignored by Yijing scholars), Cary Baynes grew up in a German-American family in Louisville, Kentucky and lived in Europe for a long time. After successfully translating several Carl Jung’s works into English, she was appointed by Jung to translate Richard Wilhelm’s I Ging. Based on archival research and oral interviews, this research will trace the steps by which she transformed the I Ging into the I Ching. Through careful textual analysis, this research will also assess her contributions as a cultural interpreter who, in translation, successfully combined three distinct cultural systems—the process cosmology of Chinese divination, the discovery of the unconscious of Jungian psychology, and the self-help genre of the American popular culture. When completed, the research will shed a new light on the globalization of the Yijing, showing the importance of a “fusion of horizons” between the foreign and the domestic, the global and the local.

11608120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11608120.value: 商業與知名度：十七世紀造園家的生意經營

11608120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11608120.value: 是次建議的研究旨在解答有關十七世紀中國造園家的問題，包括： 1. 像計成(生於1582年)和張南垣 (1578年¬-約1671年)等造園家如何管理他們的商業運作？ 2. 這些造園家如何跟園主溝通和互動？ 3. 不同稱號會用作稱呼各造園工匠，例如「花園子」、「石匠」、或「山師」。到底這些工匠或手工藝人跟其他同業員會如何分出高下？造園家又如何將自己從工匠區別出來並獨當一面？ 4. 造園家如何說服客人，證明自己是從事該項手藝的「大師」？ 現今有關十七世紀中國庭園和造園家的研究可以分為討論有關設計的概念、理論、和哲學；討論部分著名造園家的家世及生平；以及討論造園家從工匠變成文人的社會地位轉變。這些研究沒有提及到造園家怎樣經營自己的生意。 在近期有關工匠的學術研究中，高彥頤教授表示要從文人的寫作中了解墨硯工匠如何營運是十分困難的。雖然造園家都只是工匠，但是有造園家編寫了一本名為《 園治》的書籍。這次研究會運用園主和造園家記載下來的記錄，重現建造一個庭園的商業運作，包括¬：園主怎樣選擇造園家？造園家如何展示自己的技術？園主怎樣與造園家進行協商？造園家如何互相較量？造園家如何建立自己的形象？研究主要會補充有關中式庭園歷史的商業資訊，以及加以解說過去有關十七世紀工匠的商業營運。

11608320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11608320.value: The project will examine government service delivery and how citizens ascribe blame or success for its outcomes to politicians. This includes elements that have formed the cornerstone of public management research over recent decades: publicness, institutional design, citizen-state relationships and public organizations’ performance. The project will seek to make a major contribution to the public management literature by implementing a novel replication framework developed by Walker et al. (2018a) as part of a previous GRF grant. More precisely, the project will replicate James et al’s (2015) study on negativity bias, by testing and extending the theoretical and empirical scope of that study from the West (UK) to East Asia (Hong Kong, South Korea) thereby developing middle range theory. In the project, we ask: how do citizens attribute the success or failure of service delivery to politicians when institutional design choices are subject to either strong or weak publicness? We examine this question by replicating and extending James et al.’s (2015) UK study in which citizens were asked to assess blame (negativity bias) for poor service delivery based on information cues for alternative service delivery arrangements. The proposed project will make a strong theoretical contribution on this topic by substantially extending the original study through the following goals: (1) locating the original study in a publicness framework to fully capture economic as well as political theories of institutional design; (2) focusing on success (positivity bias) in addition to blame (negativity bias); and (3) examine the generalizability of the elements of the project by testing boundary conditions. The project explicitly focuses on testing these core public management concepts in East Asia. We do this because these concepts were developed in relation to public organizations operating in Western democracies, where boundary conditions are different. The research design will follow Walker et al.’s (2018a) seven decision points of experimental replication to allow a fine-grained step-by-step extension of the original study to understand how boundary conditions influence study findings. The replication will be conducted through three waves of survey experiment in each country, sampling 1,000 subjects in each wave in each country. By examining how comparative contexts influence citizens’ assessment of public service delivery the project will contribute towards the development of middle range theory in public administration, inform the practice of public administration and deliver long-term impact. 是項研究將檢測政府提供的服務，以及巿民如何將其成果或過失歸因於政客。當中包括構成過去幾十年公共管理研究基礎的要素：公共性、制度設計、巿民與政府的關係以及公共機構的績效。是項研究將透過以之前的優配研究金的研究成果Walker et al (2018a)發展出的嶄新複制框架，為公共管理文獻作出重大貢獻。更準確地說，是項研究將複制James et al (2015)關於消極偏見的研究，測試並將該項研究的理論和實驗範圍從西方（英國）擴展到東亞（香港，韓國）。 是項研究的問題是：制度設計的選擇在強或弱的公共性下，巿民如何將公共服務的成功或失敗歸因於政客？我們通過複製和擴展James et al（2015）的英國研究來探討這個問題，在該研究中，巿民需要根據替代公共服務安排的信息提示來評估服務不佳的責任（消極偏見）。是項研究將通過以下目標擴展原始研究，從而為本研究主題做出重大的理論貢獻： （1）將原始研究放在公共性的框架內，以充分掌握制度設計的經濟和政治理論； （2）除了責備（消極偏見）外，還探討成功（積極偏見）；以及 （3）通過測試邊界條件來檢查研究要素的可概括性。 是項研究明確地專注於測試東亞地區的這些核心公共管理概念，因為這些概念是針對邊界條件不同的西方民主國家中運作的公共機構而發展的。是項研究設計將遵循Walker et al（2018a）的七個實驗複製決策點，以允許對原始研究進行細粒度的逐步擴展，以了解邊界條件如何影響研究結果。複製研究將於每個國家進行三輪調查實驗，而每個國家的每一輪抽樣數目為1,000。通過比對環境如何影響巿民對公共服務的評估，是項研究將有助於公共行政中層理論的發展，為公共行政實踐提供信息並產生長期影響。

11608320.label: Realisation of objectives
11608320.value: We undertook survey experiments of service failure (street maintenance) and provided subjects (N=7200) in England and East Asia (Hong Kong and South Korea) with different institutional arrangements that offered different degrees of shelter from blame in four cues: no information, contracted to private firm, delegated within government and politicians’ involvement in service delivery. [A parallel replication has been conducted by one of the PIs PhD students in Mainland China.] Objective 1: The collected data were used to test three sets of theories: (1) Theories of blame suggest that the institutional design of public service delivery affects citizens’ blame of politicians for service failure, with delegation or contracting out reducing citizens’ blame of politicians. James et al.’s (2016) experimental study in England found supportive evidence that the in-house delegation cue reduced blame of politicians compared to the politicians’ direct involvement cue, while the blame reduction effect was not evident in the contracting out to a private firm cue. Our replication results largely coincide with the original study, while also both providing new evidence to support the theoretical expectations and variations across different contexts that in turn suggest the need for theoretical refinement. -Our English replication findings show support for contracting out to the private sector is a potentially effective institutional arrangement for politicians to avoid blame – this differs from the original English study’s finding – as does delegation whereas politicians’ involvement in service delivery heightens blame. -Results tend in the same direction in East Asia but are typically weaker, which was anticipated because of cultural differences. We consider the differences in local citizens’ perception of politicians and their embedded knowledge of public service delivery as major contributors to the varied results across contexts. While our results offer broad support for blame shift theory, our evidence points towards the need for further refinement of the blame shift theory to take account of political, environmental, cultural and governance variations. (2) Theories of publicness decompose institutional designs into levels of political and economic control of organizations. Few studies have tackled the question of how different levels of publicness influences citizens’ blame of politicians with no studies conducted in different contexts. To address this gap, we extended James et al.’s (2016) blame study to a 2×2 framework with high vs. low levels of political and economic control indicated by public service arrangement descriptions through experimental vignettes. Evidence from England suggests that a cue indicating high political control in service delivery increases citizens’ blame of politicians for public service failure, while a cue indicating high economic control decreases citizens’ blame of politicians. In Hong Kong and South Korea, the political control effect was also detected, while the economic control effect was not statistically significant. Our findings broaden the depth and width of the publicness theory, contributing to the debates on the effects of publicness in institutional design. (3) Theories of cognitive bias indicate that citizens tend to blame more for public service failure than praise for public service success. We contribute to this stream of literature by extending James et al.’s (2016) blame study to the service success cases showing good street maintenance photos instead of the poor street maintenance photos. Regarding citizens’ praise for politicians with different institutional designs, no consistent findings were observed across the three contexts. The English evidence suggests that a cue indicating high economic control decreases citizens’ praise of politicians, while the Hong Kong evidence suggests that a cue indicating high political control increases citizens’ praise of politicians. In South Korea, no statistically significant results were detected. Nonetheless, results from the pooled sample strongly support the cognitive bias theory that citizens blame politicians for service failure than praise them for service success. Outputs: -A registration file containing all our experimental design was published on the OSF platform (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/YGU2F). -Papers were presented at: International Research Society for Public Management (IRSPM) conference 2023; Public Management Research Conference 2023; forthcoming at IRSPM 2024. -Manuscript status: *second review at Public Administration Review (#1 SSCI), *submitted to Public Management Review [Parallel replication] *under preparation for Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory. -Presentations: Rutgers Newark, Seoul National and Yonsei universities. Objective 2: This project objective was successfully achieved. We replicated and extended James et al.’s (2016) survey experiment study on blame, generating a nested experimental design containing a 2×2×2 framework which includes: service failure vs. success vignettes; poor vs. good street maintenance photos; high vs. low level of political control and high vs. low level of economic control. Online survey experiments were conducted simultaneously in England, Hong Kong, and South Korea September to October 2022. Participants were randomized into one of the eight treatment groups derived from the 2×2×2 framework. Each treatment group collected 300 responses: 2400 for each of the three contexts, N=7200. Regression models were used to analyse the data. Evidence from England suggests that a cue indicating high political control in service delivery increases citizens’ blame of politicians for public service failure, while a cue indicating high economic control decreases citizens’ blame of politicians. In Hong Kong and South Korea, the political control effect was also detected, while the economic control effect was not significant at the p<0.05 level. Results strongly support the cognitive bias theory that citizens blame more to politicians for service failure than praise to politicians for service success. Objective 3: This project objective was successfully achieved. Following Walker et al.’s (2019) best practice recommendations for experimental replication, we developed rigorous extension design and implemented robust replication. However, the research design took substantially longer than that anticipated: some 6 months in total. Developing appropriate language in Traditional Chinese and Korean proved demanding as did developing locally specific vignette material. The pilot study pointed towards over 60% of participants in each region failing the factual manipulation check which necessitated changes to our research design. To extend the theoretical debates in the original study, we made novel extensions based on the original study, which mainly includes (1) adding a new vignette describing high levels of both political and economic control in service delivery arrangements, thus constructing a 2×2 institutional design in the political and economic control dimensions; (2) adding a set of new experimental groups with good street photos comparable to the original ones, thus making it possible to test the negativity/positivity bias; (3) tailoring the survey instruments from the West (England) context to the East Asia contexts (Hong Kong and South Korea), thus enabling comparisons between different culture backgrounds and contributing to develop middle range theories. Objective 4: This project objective was equivalently achieved. Specifically, a Hong Kong Scholar postdoc (Wen Wen) has been participating throughout the project and trained with related theories and experimental skills, including experimental design, implementation, data curation and analysis, etc. Two PhD students have been involved in the project receiving training in experimental replication research. Wu Peiyi, graduated 2022, was appointed as Assistant Professor in Beihang University. Dong Binzizi (defends 2024) has a chapter in her thesis on experimental blame shifting research in authoritarian China (manuscript is under review at Public Management Review).

11608320.label: Major findings and research outcome
11608320.value: Scholars in public management have sought to understand and explain how institutional design in public service delivery, particularly the publicness of service arrangements, impacts citizen-state relationships given certain public service performance. We contribute towards this stream of theoretical debates by experimental replicating (N=7200) and extending James et al.’s (2016) study of citizen’s blame of politicians for service failure (using the example of street maintenance) comparatively from the West (England) to East Asia (Hong Kong and South Korea). Our direct replication findings in England show support for contracting out to the private sector is a potentially effective institutional arrangement for politicians to avoid blame – this differs from the original study’s findings. We also find that results are typically weaker in East Asia, which were anticipated because of cultural differences. We consider the differences in local citizens’ perception of politicians and their embedded knowledge of public service delivery as major contributors to the varied results across contexts. Beyond our replication of the original study we firstly examined publicness, or public-private differences by including a 2×2 framework with high vs. low levels of political and economic control indicated by public service arrangement descriptions through experimental vignettes. Evidence from England suggested that a cue indicating high political control in service delivery increases citizens’ blame of politicians for public service failure, while a cue indicating high economic control decreases citizens’ blame of politicians. In Hong Kong and South Korea, the political control effect was also detected, while the economic control effect was not significant. We undertook a second extension drawing on theories of cognitive bias which indicate that citizens tend to blame more for public service failure than praise for public service success. In the prior studies we presented citizens with negative images of street maintenance, and for this study we showed good street maintenance. However, we find no consistent results across the three contexts (England, Hong Kong, South Korea). The English evidence suggests that a cue indicating high economic control decreases citizens’ praise of politicians, while the Hong Kong evidence suggests that a cue indicating high political control increases citizens’ praise of politicians. In South Korea, no statistically significant results were detected. Nonetheless, results from the pooled sample strongly support the cognitive bias theory that citizens blame more to politicians for service failure than praise to politicians for service success.

11608320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11608320.value: We conducted the first experimental replication study of a blame shift study by conducting a direct replication in England over a decade after the original study was conducted and extended our replication to East Asia. We further extended the original study by examining publicness – public-private differences – and the cognitive bias of negativity bias. While our replication work and extensions provide valuable and important insights they present case for a continuation of research and the further development of this area of study. 1. Within public administration replications remain limited. Our study has shown the utility of replication by identifying different findings from the original study that are in keeping with theoretical expectations. Replication of blame studies in other public services is required to fully test the theory. 2. In extending the replication to new contexts we had to conceptualise our expectations for how blame shift theory would play out. We suggested findings would tend in the same direction but with weaker results, which were empirically verified. However, we only examined two contexts. Further study is required in other context that present different institutional arrangements. The same applies to the need for extensions in of publicness and cognitive biases.

11608320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11608320.value: Institutional design have been developed to protect politicians from blame for public service delivery failure. This includes delegation within government and contracting to the private sector for service delivery. We contributed towards these debates by experimentally replicating (N=7200) and extending James et al.’s (2016) study of citizen’s blame of politicians for service failure (using the example of street maintenance) comparatively from the West (England) to East Asia (Hong Kong and South Korea). We argued that in the West institutional designs of delegation and contracting would shield politicians from blame but that these relationships would be weaker in East Asia: our findings supported these expectations. We extended the original study to examine how variations in public-private differences would affect these relationships but did not uncover strong results. We also examined the proposition of negativity bias – that citizens would blame politicians for service failure and not reward them for success. At the aggregate level, negativity bias has strong explanatory power. Further research is required to address limitations in our design, including the examination of other contexts and the inclusion of more complex public services, notably less technical and human-orientated services.

11608820.label: Project Objectives
11608820.value: To present empirical evidence on the dual-track legal mobilization in China’s environmental public interest litigation (EPIL) practice, including EPIL brought by environmental non-governmental organizations (ENGOs) and that brought by procuratorates. To examine the respective roles and limitations of ENGO-led EPIL and procuratorate-led EPIL in enforcing the environmental law in China. To investigate how the factors of capacity, autonomy, accountability, goals and legal opportunity shape ENGOs behaviors in mobilizing EPIL in China. To explore how the changes in the legal, political and organizational settings that procuratorates are situated in through different phases of legal mobilization impact their mobilization behaviors. To discuss what are contrastive behaviors and interactions between grassroots-actor (ENGOs) and public-actor (procuratorates) in mobilizing EPIL in a responsive authoritarian regime like China. To provide the Chinese experiences in the dual-track legal mobilization through EPIL and bring the Chinese insights into the global discourse on legal mobilization and regulatory pluralism

11608820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11608820.value: 幾十年來，中國將經濟發展優先於環境保護。政府與民眾直到最近才開始對日益惡化的環境表示越來越多的關切。面對環境污染嚴重、合規行為不理想、公共執法不力等問題，中央政府被迫考慮在最初由行政機構主導的環境監管領域引入多元行動者，並且認可了環境公益訴訟制度這項源於地方實踐的法律創新。中國的環境公益訴訟制度允許非政府的環保組織和政府的檢察機關對污染環境者提起民事環境公益訴訟。檢察機構其後被授予對執法不力的環保局提起行政環境公益訴訟的資格。作為基層行動者的環保組織代表公共環境利益自下而上地動員民事環境公益訴訟，而作為公共行動者的檢察機構則自上而下地動員由政府驅動的民事及行政環境公益訴訟。這樣，雙軌制的法律動員應運而生，並已經在中國環境公益訴訟領域持續了十年。鑒於環保組織和檢察機構具有迥異的性質、處於不同的法律、政治和社會佈景和法律機會結構中，兩者在保護公共環境利益時是否表現出不同的法律動員行為，如果是，那麼具體的差異何在？由於較少文獻從實證的角度討論中國環境公益訴訟的法律動員，更不用說對比研究由環保組織主導的法律動員和由檢察院主導的法律動員，本項目旨在填補該項空白。本項目將利用由環保組織和檢察機關在2008年至2020年間提起的環境公益訴訟案件之判決文書構建的數據庫，採用多種研究方法（包括統計分析、深入訪談和個案研究）研究四個問題：（1）自2008年以來，環保組織和檢察機關如何通過環境公益訴訟來動員法律，它們在執行環境法律中各自發揮了什麼作用？（2）能力、自主性、問責性、目標和法律機會等因素如何塑造眾多環保組織在提起環境公益訴訟時不同的法律動員行為？（3）法律、政治和組織架構上的變化如何影響檢察機關提起環境公益訴訟時的法律動員行為？（4）在中國這樣的回應型專制政權中，作為基層行動者的環保組織和作為公共行動者的檢察機關在通過環境公益訴訟進行法律動員時彼此的差異和互動又是怎樣？本研究項目將就中國由環保組織提起的環境公益訴訟與由檢察院提起的環境公益訴訟形成豐富的實證發現，對影響其動員行為之決定因素的實證發現進行法社會學上的分析，並就環保組織和檢察機構通過環境公益訴訟來執行和重構環境法律中的作用和局限性進行全面且深入的探討，從而為如何改善中國的環境公益訴訟制度和加強環境規管提供啟示。最後，本項目亦將中國的經驗見解帶入有關法律動員和監管多元化的全球性討論。

11609020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11609020.value: 價值觀相似性與浪漫關係：外顯和內隱價值觀的差別角色

11609020.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11609020.value: Prof Bardi, Anat Dr Hu, Xiaoqing

11609020.label: Project Objectives
11609020.value: To examine the differential roles of explicit and implicit values in the development of romantic relationships (Studies I, II, and III); To investigate the effects during initial attraction (Study I) and dating (Studies II and III) stages in the development of romantic relationships; To study the processes in both laboratory (Study I) and real-life settings (Studies II and III); To triangulate the findings with experimental (Study I), correlational (Study II), and longitudinal (Study III) research designs.
rows: To examine the differential roles of explicit and implicit values in the development of romantic relationships (Studies I, II, and III);
To investigate the effects during initial attraction (Study I) and dating (Studies II and III) stages in the development of romantic relationships;
To study the processes in both laboratory (Study I) and real-life settings (Studies II and III);
To triangulate the findings with experimental (Study I), correlational (Study II), and longitudinal (Study III) research designs.

11609020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609020.value: Romantic relationships have significant implications on health and well-being at both individual and societal levels. Previous research has suggested that couple similarity in various aspects (e.g., ethnicity, religious belief, and personality) is positively related to the development of romantic relationships. Little is known, however, about the role of couple similarity in core beliefs such as personal values. Built upon dual-process theories, which differentiates between explicit processes (i.e., involves slow, deliberative, and controlled thinking and responses) and implicit processes (i.e., involves fast, intuitive, and automatic thinking and responses), the current project endeavors to disentangle the roles of explicit and implicit personal values during early stages of romantic relationships. Study I examines whether and how similarity in explicit and implicit values may affect initial romantic attraction to potential partners among single people. Participants will complete both explicit and implicit measures of personal values. Perceived attractiveness towards potential partners, which have been linked with different values in a training session, will be assessed by both explicit and implicit measures. The unique effects of explicit and implicit personal values on explicit and implicit attraction will be estimated by cross-lagged modeling and compared by equality constrains. Study II examines whether and how similarity in explicit and implicit values may affect relationship satisfaction among dating couples. Similar to Study I, both explicit and implicit measures will be employed to measure personal values and relationship satisfaction. The explicit and implicit values between the dating couples will be used to predict relationship satisfaction using response surface analysis (RSA), which is a versatile tool in examining similarity effects. Study III is a longitudinal study to examine how similarity in explicit and implicit values is related to the development of dating relationships over time. Findings from this study would substantiate the findings from the previous two studies in a real-life setting and, more importantly, further clarify the directionality of the effects. Latent change modeling will be used to analyze how the initial levels and subsequent changes in explicit and implicit value similarity and relationship satisfaction are related to each other and the effects will be compared by equality constrains. Upon successful completion, findings from the current project would contribute not only to research on personal values and dual-process theories, but to practices regarding the development and maintenance of romantic relationships. 在個體和社會層面上，浪漫關係對健康和幸福感都有重要的意義。過去研究發現，配偶之間在種族背景、宗教信仰、性格等方面的相似性與浪漫關係的發展有正相關。然而，關於核心信念（如個人價值觀）的相似性對浪漫關係的作用目前仍然所知有限。基於雙過程理論（即包含緩慢的、刻意的、受控的思維和反應的外顯過程，和包含快速的、直覺的、自動的思維和反應的內隱過程），本研究致力於區分外顯和內隱價值觀在浪漫關係早期的不同影響。 研究一探討外顯和內隱價值觀的相似性如何影響單身人士選擇潛在配偶。參與者將會完成外顯和內隱價值觀的測量。潛在配偶的圖片在訓練環節中與特定的價值觀相匹配，然後用外顯和內隱方法測量參加者所認為的吸引度。交叉滯後模型和等同限制將被用於估算外顯和內隱價值觀對外顯和內隱吸引度的獨特影響。 研究二探討外顯和內隱價值觀的相似性如何影響戀愛情侶中的關係滿意感。如研究一，個人價值觀和關係滿意感均會用外顯和內隱方法進行測量。響應曲面分析將被用於估算戀愛情侶外顯和內隱價值觀的相似度對關係滿意感的影響。 研究三以追蹤設計瞭解外顯和內隱價值觀的相似性如何影響戀愛情侶關係滿意感的跨時間變化。此研究結果將在更為貼近自然生活的環境中進一步證實前兩項研究的發現，並澄清各種效應的因果方向。在資料分析上，潛變化模型和等同限制將被用於估計和比較外顯及內隱價值觀和關係滿意感的初始水準和後續變化如何互相影響。 本研究的發現將有助於進一步瞭解個人價值觀和雙過程理論，以及促進在現實生活中發展和維持戀愛關係。

11609020.label: Realisation of objectives
11609020.value: The research project, launched in early 2021, aimed to investigate the roles of explicit and implicit personal values in romantic relationships through three distinct studies: an experimental study (Study I), a correlational study with dating couples (Study II), and a longitudinal study (Study III). The onset of the COVID-19 pandemic introduced significant disruptions, including widespread lockdowns, sporadic outbreaks that halted in-person interactions, and limited access to essential resources such as laboratory facilities and participant pools. These challenges tested the project’s execution, requiring innovative solutions to maintain progress. Despite these obstacles, the research achieved notable success, frequently surpassing the goals outlined in the original proposal, and produced valuable data and research papers that contribute meaningfully to the field. Studies I and II encountered substantial hurdles in data collection, yet both exceeded their planned targets through effective adjustments to unforeseen circumstances. For Study I, restrictions on laboratory access and unpredictable in-person recruitment posed immediate barriers. To address this, the project shifted to online platforms for data collection and established collaborations with other universities to broaden participant reach. These efforts resulted in a robust sample of 120 participants—far exceeding the proposed 66—enabling the completion of a comprehensive experimental study. Similarly, Study II faced the challenge of gathering data from dating couples during a period marked by social distancing mandates, which limited traditional recruitment methods. By leveraging digital tools and persistent outreach, the study secured data from 152 couples, well above the target of 112. These findings have been compiled into a manuscript for submission to the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships (impact factor 2.3), reflecting how strategic responses transformed potential setbacks into opportunities for success. Study III, however, encountered greater difficulty due to its longitudinal design, which required collecting multiple waves of data over an extended period—a task made exceptionally challenging by the pandemic’s unpredictability. Initial efforts saw 190 participants recruited at Time 1, but retention proved difficult, with only 66 returning at Time 2. This sample size was insufficient to support the planned three-wave structure, as participant engagement waned amid ongoing uncertainties. Recognizing these limitations, the project team took decisive action by restarting data collection at a university outside Hong Kong, where conditions allowed for a renewed effort. This adjustment produced a more substantial two-wave dataset, with 242 participants at Time 1 and 181 at Time 2. Although this fell short of the original three-wave ambition, it preserved Study III’s ability to provide longitudinal insights into value dynamics over time. These results are detailed in a paper accepted by Personality and Individual Differences (impact factor 3.5), underscoring the value of adaptability in maintaining research quality. The broader context of these disruptions highlights the project’s resilience. The pandemic’s impact extended beyond data collection, affecting other project activities such as attending international conferences to disseminate findings. Major conferences were canceled, while others were postponed, disrupting plans to share results with the academic community. Lockdowns not only restricted physical access to research facilities but also limited participant availability, as many potential volunteers faced personal and logistical constraints. The sporadic nature of outbreaks further complicated scheduling, often reducing data collection to intermittent bursts when conditions briefly stabilized. The ability to exceed sample size expectations—120 versus 66 for Study I and 152 versus 112 for Study II—demonstrates a commitment to rigorous outcomes, while Study III’s redesign offered a foundation for future exploration despite curtailed plans. Overall, the project successfully navigated the pandemic’s challenges, delivering significant results across all three studies. The larger-than-anticipated samples in Studies I and II provided robust datasets that enriched the research’s scope, while Study III’s adjusted approach maintained its relevance despite a scaled-back design. These efforts ensured that the project not only met but often advanced its original objectives, contributing meaningful data and insights to the study of romantic relationships. In addition, this project has provided valuable training opportunities to eight undergraduate students and three PhD students, who actively participated in research tasks and lab meetings, gaining hands-on experience and relevant skills in the process.

11609020.label: Major findings and research outcome
11609020.value: This research offers significant insights into the role of personal values in romantic relationships, reframing understanding through a dual-process lens that captures both explicit (conscious) and implicit (unconscious) dimensions. As reported in two papers, the findings illustrate how values drive attraction, shape relationship dynamics, and adapt to life’s shifting tides. Rather than static traits, values appear as dynamic forces, integrating deliberate choice and automatic impulse to influence love and connection. A key finding, detailed in a manuscript prepared for the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships (impact factor 2.3), supports the similarity-attraction theory through dual-process cognition. Explicit values, particularly those contrasting self-enhancement with self-transcendence (SE-ST), strongly predict attraction to partners who share these values, with women showing greater sensitivity to this alignment. This gender difference raises theoretical questions—possibly tied to evolutionary drives or socialized priorities in mate selection—while implicit values exert a subtler, distinct influence. Together, these results highlight how romantic bonds emerge from a blend of conscious intent and unconscious influence, broadening perspectives on human connection. Methodologically, an Implicit Association Test (IAT) for higher-order values was validated, as outlined in a paper accepted by Personality and Individual Differences (impact factor 3.5). This tool effectively probes the unconscious mind, reinforcing the study of implicit values and confirming their independence from explicit ones, aligning with the dual-process model’s premise of separate yet complementary systems. Notably, both value types shifted toward self-focus following COVID-19 policy relaxation, indicating adaptability to external changes. This plasticity challenges static views of values, presenting them as evolving constructs responsive to circumstance. These findings extend beyond academia, enhancing relationship science by revealing the complex interplay of values in attraction and satisfaction. They point to practical applications—such as counseling to align partners’ values or interventions addressing value shifts during crises. Looking ahead, the research encourages exploration of how values sustain long-term relationships or adjust during life transitions.

11609020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11609020.value: Future research can explore how shared implicit values affect conflict resolution in married couples. Through longitudinal surveys and interviews, we can test if implicit value congruence enhances conflict management, building on Study I’s findings of gender differences, where women emphasize value alignment. Another study will examine how mismatches in explicit and implicit values predict relationship dissolution in dating and married couples. We may also evaluate the lasting effects of value changes on relationship satisfaction during major life transitions like the pandemic. These studies fill gaps in understanding later-stage relationships and negative outcomes, offering practical benefits for couples therapy and relationship education. By deepening insights into how conscious and unconscious values shape romantic bonds, this research aims to support stronger, lasting partnerships.

11609020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11609020.value: This research investigates the reasons behind romantic attraction and relationship satisfaction by examining personal values, such as the importance of kindness or ambition. Beyond traditional surveys, it employed a specialized computer task to reveal subconscious preferences, providing a fuller picture of how values influence relationships. The study focused on singles and dating couples, revealing that individuals—particularly women—are more attracted to partners with similar values, and this alignment enhances relationship quality. These findings have been documented in manuscripts submitted to leading academic journals. The significance lies in its potential to improve relationship outcomes: understanding value compatibility can strengthen partnerships, much like aligning complementary strengths. This knowledge could inform counseling practices, enabling professionals to better support couples in fostering mutual understanding, or enhance educational programs to promote lasting relationships. By clarifying how both conscious and subconscious values shape romantic connections, this work offers valuable insights for building stronger, more enduring bonds.

11609220.value: 住宅社區的反社會行為及社會解組﹕香港的空間多層研究

11609220.value: To provide an overview of the problems related to ASB proliferation in residential neighborhoods and the controls of ASB in Asian cities, particularly with respect to the difficulties encountered in the control processes; To develop an analytical model for explaining variations in ASB perception by incorporating the theories related to social disorganization and housing tenure; To investigate the extent of the ASB problem as perceived by residents in selected residential neighborhoods in Hong Kong; To empirically test the applicability of the social disorganization theory in explaining the perceived level of ASB proliferation in Hong Kong, and to explore the determinants of the perception of ASB; To elucidate how differences in the institutional settings of housing governance affect ASB proliferation in the selected housing developments; and To engage with relevant policymakers and housing managers to discuss research findings to explore possible ways of improving ASB control in Hong Kong.

11609220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609220.value: 住房的反社會行為在全球各地都很常見，香港亦不例外。儘管大量學術文獻曾以個人或社會結構角度，對反社會行為進行探討，鮮有研究在鄰里層面上分析反社會行為激增的情況。此外，不少社會學理論（如「社會解組理論」）假設犯罪感知與社區社會資本相關。雖然犯罪感知乃是大量與相關研究的焦點，但是這些理論在解釋反社會行為之應用實是被忽略了。再者，大多數與住房反社會行為相關的研究均着眼於西方的低層住宅環境中，反社會行為在亞洲城市高層住宅環境中的情況則未曾引起學術界的廣泛關注。反社會行為一般被誤以為是公營房屋獨有的問題；然而，這個問題亦會出現在私營房屋。為了填補上述空缺，本研究旨在探討在香港的住宅社區內，社區社會資本對居民的反社會行為感知程度之影響。另外，本研究亦會研究房屋權屬的類型會否影響住宅社區內的反社會行為的程度。本研究將採用定量和定性的研究方法，進行仔細分析，以探討這些課題。 為了評估「社會解組理論」能否應用於解釋在不同住宅社區間反社會行為程度之差異，本研究通過問卷調查獲得數據，並進行定量分析。研究團隊會開發一個嶄新的貝葉斯空間多層模型，用作分析反社會行為感知之社會空間變化。這個研究方法提供一個靈活的框架，在明確地考慮聚類數據結構及有可能的空間自動調節及異質性影響之同時，把空間聚類的調查數據用模型展示出來。在定性研究方面，研究團隊會對不同持分者（如居民及物業管理人員）進行訪談及語境分析，從而作出深入的個案研究。定性研究的結果有望能反映不同控制反社會行為的制度，如何調節社會解組對反社會行為感知程度的影響。本研究將為香港居民如何看待其住宅社區內反社會問題的嚴重性，提供寶貴的見解。本研究的結果可望幫助政策制定者和房屋經理在處理與住房有關的反社會行為時，做出更明智及全面的決定。此外，本研究將就如何控制反社會行為提出建議，以改善現行的房屋管治制度。

11609220.label: Realisation of objectives
11609220.value: To realize the project objectives, the research team has undertaken or completed the following activities: 1) The problems of housing-related anti-social behaviour (ASB) in Hong Kong and other cities were overviewed through a background study. The background study covers academic literature, guidelines of professional bodies (e.g. Chartered Institute of Housing), government publications and media reports. 2) A comprehensive literature review on the concepts of ASB, social disorganization and housing tenure was conducted. Based on the findings of the literature review, a conceptual framework that investigates the effects of social disorganization and housing tenure on the extent of the ASB problem in a residential neighborhood was constructed. Other possible explanatory variables affecting ASB proliferation were identified in the literature review. Based on the findings of the literature review, an analytical model was developed for subsequent empirical research. 3) Rosters of medium- and large-scale housing developments in Shatin, Tai Po and Tseung Kwan O, Hong Kong were compiled based on the information from the governmental sources and publicly accessible geographical information systems. These rosters formed the sampling frames for the questionnaire surveys in the three study districts. 4) A questionnaire set was designed, pretested and fine-tuned for obtaining the data for the empirical research. 5) Questionnaire surveys were conducted in 40, 40 and 32 housing developments in Shatin, Tai Po and Tseung Kwan O respectively to investigate the extent of the ASB problem as perceived by residents in these housing developments in Hong Kong. 6) Housing development-level data of the 2021 Population Census were mapped to the dataset of the questionnaire surveys. Statistical analyses performed on the combined dataset (with both survey data and Census data) to identify the determinants of the perception of ASB and test the applicability of the social disorganization theory in explaining the perceived level of ASB proliferation in Hong Kong. 7) In-depth case studies were conducted on six housing developments sampled for questionnaire surveys to investigate how the institutional design of ASB control may moderate the effects of social disorganization and housing parameters on ASB perception. In-depth interviews were held with the representatives of the resident associations (e.g. chairpersons of owners’ corporations or owners’ committees), individual residents and staff of property management agents of these six housing developments. Documentary review was performed on the deeds of mutual covenant, house rules and minutes of resident association meetings. Contextual analyses were conducted on the materials posted on the online resident forums of these housing developments. 8) Drawing on the findings of the case studies, analyses were conducted to compare the influences of different institutional settings of housing governance (e.g. formation of owners’ association) on ASB proliferation. 9) Based on the findings of the research, practical and policy implications have been drawn and recommendations regarding how housing-related ASB in Hong Kong should be controlled have been formulated. Overall speaking, the six project objectives as per original application have been substantially achieved.

11609220.label: Major findings and research outcome
11609220.value: The results of the quantitative analysis generally confirm the applicability of the social disorganization theory (SDT) in explaining the variations of the levels of anti-social behaviour (ASB) perceived by residents in selected housing developments in Hong Kong. The analysis results revealed that residents living in housing communities that were more social disorganized, as exemplified by higher degrees of residential instability and resident heterogeneity, were more likely to perceive serious ASB problems in their housing communities. As far as the housing tenure is concerned, tenants tended to rate ASB problems in their housing communities more serious than owner-occupiers did in private housing communities. Besides, among private housing communities, ASB problems tended to be more serious in those with a higher level of renting. Other significant determinants of ASB level perceived by an individual resident identified in this research include the perceived level of sense of community, length of residence and development scale. The qualitative inquiry based on the case studies discovered noticeable dissimilarities in the institutional settings of ASB control and management between private housing and subsidized housing. The marking scheme for estate management played a significant role in deterring ASB in public rental housing while private housing relied heavily on clear provisions in the deed of mutual covenant and house rules in enforcement against residents’ ASB. On the other hand, informal control measures that fostered social engagement and strengthened and social cohesion among residents were found to be equally important as formal control in dealing with housing-related ASB problems. Interestingly, the utilization of social media groups, community apps or online forums for residents to share concerns and updates or report ASB incidents was found to have a strong potential to reduce ASB problems within a housing community. With reference to the findings of the research, the following recommendations for better ASB control in housing governance in Hong Kong were drawn: 1) fostering a harmonious climate within a housing community through a multipronged community-building approach (e.g. amicable dispute resolution, induction programme for new residents, activities organized for social networking, and better housing design with more communal facilities for social interactions); 2) formulating and enforcing a clear set of house rules related to noise, pet keeping and shared spaces; and 3) promoting the use of social media groups, community apps or online forums as tools for reinforcing informal control of ASB within housing communities.

11609220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11609220.value: The principal investigator compared the findings from the survey conducted in Tseung Kwan O against those from a prior project to examine how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced housing-related ASB level. A paper detailing this empirical research was presented at an academic conference, and a manuscript was submitted to the journal Behavioral Sciences for publication consideration. Currently, three manuscripts are under preparation. The first validates the relevance of social disorganization theory in explaining ASB proliferation in Hong Kong’s housing communities. The second one discusses how housing tenure influences perceived levels of ASB within these communities. The third one presents a comparative analysis of formal and informal institutions related to ASB control in housing communities in Hong Kong. This research can be further developed in two ways. First, it can be extended to cover other high-rise Asian cities facing similar challenges related to housing-related ASB. Second, in addition to exploring the determinants of ASB proliferation, it is essential to investigate the impacts of ASB on residents’ health and property values. A manuscript reporting a preliminary study which examined the relationship between ASB and housing prices in Northern Ireland was submitted to the Journal of Housing and the Built Environment.

11609220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11609220.value: The prevalence of anti-social behaviour (ASB) within housing communities constitutes a significant global concern. While the social disorganization theory has been effectively employed to elucidate variations in crime rates across neighbourhoods, its applicability to explaining disparities in ASB proliferation remains underexplored. Furthermore, existing research on housing-related ASB predominantly focuses on low-rise residential settings in Western contexts, leaving the issue of ASB in high-rise housing within Asian cities largely unaddressed. This study endeavours to investigate the influence of social disorganization and housing tenure on the perceived extent of ASB in housing communities of Hong Kong. A mixed-methods approach, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative methodologies, was implemented to conduct this investigation. The findings of this research hold significant implications for informing strategies aimed at mitigating ASB within the context of high-rise housing governance. Such insights are crucial for ensuring the sustainable management of housing stock. Moreover, this study serves as a foundational framework for broader comparative research across other Asian metropolises, including Shanghai, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur, and Singapore, where ASB challenges within high-rise housing are also prevalent. By examining these diverse urban contexts, a more comprehensive understanding of the factors contributing to ASB and the most effective interventions can be achieved.

11609420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11609420.value: 績效薪酬是否損害公共服務工作的滿意度？透過「全循環」的研究方式收集問卷和實驗證據

11609420.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11609420.value: Dr Chen, Chung-An Dr Wang, Chun-yuan Dr WEN, Bo

11609420.label: Project Objectives
11609420.value: To build a theoretical model to explain whether and how pay for performance (PFP) undermines the relationship between public service motivation (PSM) and job satisfaction (JS). Scholars have previously assumed that (1) those who are attracted to public service work due to PSM experience substantial satisfaction, because the work offers an abundance of opportunities to fulfill their prosocial goals, and (2) PFP is detrimental to the satisfaction of high PSM workers, because it shifts their motivation from individual to external incentives. Although these are critical assumptions of public human resource management, they have seldom been examined. Based on the relevant literature, the proposed project aims to build a theoretical model to explain (1) whether public service delivery mediates the positive effect of PSM on JS and (2) whether PFP leads to self-control depletion at work and thus undermines the PSM-JS relationship. To offer validated empirical insights into the effect of PFP on the PSM-JS relationship. Many scholars have lamented that PFP may crowd out PSM and subsequently erode JS. However, is it true that PFP will bring more harm than good? If so, under what conditions is it harmful? Answers to these questions will inform effective management, yet the extant literature on the topic is sparse and even contradictory. Thus, our primary research question in the proposed project will be whether and how PFP undermines the PSM-JS relationship. We will approach this question with a rigorous “full-circle” design. This approach begins with observational research to develop an initial theory concerning a natural phenomenon, proceeds with manipulation-based inquiries to verify the existence of the observed phenomenon, and ends with more scientific tests to increase theoretical generalizability and robustness. In doing so, we will offer a coherent set of empirical insights into the effect of PFP on the PSM-JS relationship. To inform ways of balancing altruistic and materialistic motivations in the public service workplace. As both a field of study and a profession, the value and reality of public administration ought to coincide. Yet, public service values that emphasize “benevolence to all” among public service workers are increasingly at odds with the new workplace reality that embraces PFP. Based on research findings generated by our “full-circle” inquiries, the proposed project will offer recommendations to avoid adverse effects when leveraging rewards to motivate public service workers.

11609420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609420.value: The main impetus behind the proposed project is to investigate whether pay for performance (PFP) undermines job satisfaction (JS) derived from public service. Studies of public service workers’ satisfaction have recently gained momentum due to growing scholarly inquiry into public service motivation (PSM)—the desire to serve the public. Clear empirical evidence has been found for a positive PSM-JS relationship, yet questions have also been raised about whether the strength and direction of this relationship can withstand different employment conditions. This issue is of particular concern in the wake of recent administrative reforms, which have sought to improve employee motivation and performance through PFP. Unfortunately, there is no scholarly consensus to date on the effect of PFP on the PSM-JS relationship. Thus, our primary research question will be whether and how PFP modifies the JS of public service–motivated workers. The context of public service work serves as an ideal backdrop for our inquiries, because it is easier to observe the effect of PFP in workplaces where PSM is most required. Based on the relevant literature, we posit the following hypotheses: 1. PSM will lead to JS directly and indirectly through public service delivery. 2. PFP will undermine the PSM-JS relationship if perceived job control is diminished. We will address our research question using a “full-circle” multimethod design to circumvent the limitations of any single method and to allow us to investigate our theoretical conjectures thoroughly. The “full-circle” approach begins with observational research of natural phenomena and proceeds by alternating manipulation- and observation-based inquiries. Following this principle, we will perform three studies: (1) a survey study of public service workers across occupations in Hong Kong, (2) an experimental public service simulation with Hong Kong college students, and (3) an “empirical generalization” type of replication study using a sample of Taiwanese police officers. These studies will serve as a strong basis for developing and validating insights derived from different methodologies and samples. In conclusion, the proposed project will advance scholarly knowledge concerning the effect of PFP on the morale of public service workers and develop interventions to balance motivating service performance and maintaining employee satisfaction. The research team will be led by two public administration scholars with extensive experience collaborating with each other on PSM studies. Two additional researchers, specialists in experimental and police studies, will assist with research design and data collection. The synergy of the research team’s complementary strengths will help bring this project to fruition. 本研究項目背後的主要推動力是為了調查績效薪酬是否損害公共服務工作的滿意度（job satisfaction, JS）。由於公共服務動機（Public Service Motivation, PSM）的研究日益增多，公務員對公共服務工作的滿意度也連帶引起學界廣泛注意。當前學術研究已經找到諸多明確證據來支持PSM-JS之間的正向關係，然而，人們也質疑這個關係的強度和方向會不會因爲就業條件的差異而有所不同。在新公共管理改革浪潮下，這個問題格外引人關注，因為這些行政改革試圖引進私部門績效薪酬（pay for performance, PFP）制度，來提高公務員的積極性和業績。然而，迄今為止，關於PFP對PSM-JS關係的影響，仍然沒有學術上的共識。 因此，我們的主要研究問題是：PFP是否以及如何改變公共服務對公務員JS的激勵作用？公共服務工作是我們調研的理想背景，因為我們能夠在最需要 PSM 的工作場所來檢驗 PFP 的影響。根據相關文獻，我們提出以下假設： 1. PSM 將直接影響JS和間接地通過公共服務工作來提高JS。 2. 然而，如果公務員認知到自身的工作控制度減少，PFP 將破壞PSM-JS的關係。 我們將使用「全循環」多種方法的研究設計來回答我們所提出的問題和假設，此舉可有效規避任何單一研究方法的局限性，並使我們能夠徹底檢驗我們的理論推測。「全循環」方法從自然現象的觀察研究開始，然後交替使用實驗控制和觀測性的調研工作。按照這個原則，我們將進行三項研究：(1)對香港公務員進行問卷調查研究、(2) 以香港大學生為對象的公共服務模擬實驗、(3)利用臺灣員警為樣本進行「經驗概括」類型的複製研究。這些不同的方法和樣本，將為本研究所得出的發現之嚴密性和可靠性提供牢固基礎。 本研究項目將能提高關於PFP對公務員士氣影響的學術知識，並將有助政府制定有效的管理干預措施，以保持激勵員工績效和保持工作滿意度的妥善平衡。研究小組將由兩名公共行政學者領導，他們在PSM研究方面具有廣泛的合作經驗。另外兩名研究人員，則是實驗設計和員警研究的專家，他們將協助研究設計和數據收集。本研究團隊成員之間的協同互補，將有助本研究項目取得豐碩的成果。

11609420.label: Realisation of objectives
11609420.value: The main impetus behind this project is to investigate whether pay for performance (PFP) undermines job satisfaction (JS) derived from public service. Studies of public service workers’ satisfaction have recently gained momentum due to growing scholarly inquiry into public service motivation (PSM)—the desire to serve the public. Clear empirical evidence has been found for a positive PSM-JS relationship, yet questions have also been raised about whether the strength and direction of this relationship can withstand different employment conditions. This issue is of particular concern in the wake of recent administrative reforms, which have sought to improve employee motivation and performance through PFP. Unfortunately, there is no scholarly consensus to date on the effect of PFP on the PSM-JS relationship. To address this gap, our project employed a "full-circle" design consisting of three main components: (1) a survey study involving public service workers across various occupations in Hong Kong, (2) an experimental public service simulation with Hong Kong college students, and (3) a replication study conducted in another Asian context involving public service workers. When this project concluded in December 2023, we have completed all of the three proposed studies and published two manuscripts, one in International Public Management Journal and another in Public Personnel Management. In the below section, I will detail how these studies were conducted and how they helped the research team to meet proposed project objectives. In Study 1, the research team outsourced the survey work to a data collection company, Dynata, who helped us collect responses from 220 front-line public service workers in Hong Kong. Based on the survey data, we drafted a manuscript titled “Public Service Motivation, Performance-Contingent Pay, and Job Satisfaction of Street-Level Bureaucrats” (published by Public Personnel Management). In this paper, we present findings that uphold the strong, positive influence of PSM on public service workers’ JS, while PFP can indirectly boost JS through perceived job control. As for Study 2, we conducted a lab experience with CityU students. However, the collected data were not reliable due to the fact that students participated in the experiment for course credit and some of them did not take it seriously. Therefore, we opted to collaborate with Dr. LI Ming of Henan Normal University (China) by leveraging the Chinese data with an identical research design. Together, we published a manuscript, titled “Understanding the Role Reward Types Play in Linking Public Service Motivation to Task Satisfaction: Evidence from an Experiment in China”, in International Public Management Journal. In our analysis, results revealed that when nonmonetary rewards were given, participants with low implicit PSM were less enthusiastic about completing the assigned task whereas their high-PSM counterparts were much keener about accomplishing the same task. For the third study, we originally targeted police officers but later changed our focus to those who participated in epidemic control measures in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were collected both in mainland China and Taiwan. However, the research team has not yet been able to produce a publishable paper based on the data collected, although we have drafted a manuscript with a working title, “Investigating the Influence of Risk Perception on Females’ Public Service Motivation during Public Health Emergencies.” Through these studies and the resulting research outputs, our research team has achieved the following objectives: 1. To build a theoretical model to explain (1) whether public service delivery mediates the positive effect of PSM on JS and (2) whether PFP leads to self-control depletion at work and thus undermines the PSM-JS relationship. 2. To offer validated empirical insights into the effect of PFP on the PSM-JS relationship. 3. To inform ways of balancing altruistic and materialistic motivations in the public service workplace.
