12301320.label: Realisation of objectives
12301320.value: We have developed a general synthetic route to the picrotoxane natural product family and achieved formal syntheses of several picrotoxane members. Our synthetic route features a Wharton transposition strategy for inversion of the stereochemistry of the sidechain and a Lewis acid-mediated epoxide-ring opening ring-closing strategy for establishing the key motif of the picrotoxane skeleton (AB ring system). Gratefully, all the synthetic work proposed in this project has been completed and the synthetic picrotoxane natural products and their analogues have been submitted to our collaborator (Dr. William Chi Shing Tai, Polytechnic University) for biological studies. Some of the synthetic picrotoxane compounds showed some exciting results and we are considering filing a patent to cover the new structures and functions of the synthetic picrotoxane compounds. Our synthetic route began with (R)-carvone (a commercially available starting material), which required only 8 steps for conversion to the cyclization precursor. After the stereospecific inversion of the stereochemistry of the sidechain using a modified Wharton transposition strategy, Lewis acid-mediated epoxide-ring opening ring-closing reaction using TMSOTf and 2,6-lutinide at -78 °C successfully established the key motif of picrotoxane skeleton (AB ring system) in 71% yield. The cyclization product was then converted to Yoshikishi’s and Trost’s intermediate (in 9 – 10 steps respectively), which contain the core structure of the picrotoxane skeleton with all the required functionalities. These advanced intermediates can be readily elaborated to other members in the picrotoxane family including dendrowillins A (objective 1) and their structural analogues. We have also employed the Barton–McCombie deoxygenation strategy for converting the Yoshikishi’s and Trost’s intermediates to other picrotoxane members with the C6-H including dendrowillins B (objective 1), flakinin A (objective 2) and picrodendrin Q (objective 3). With the newly developed synthetic route, we have also prepared a focus library of 15 picrotoxanes and their structural analogues (objective 4). All the synthetic picrotoxanes and their structural analogues have been submitted to our collaborator for biological studies and some of them showed promising results as a GABA antagonist (objective 5). During the course of study, we found that the originally proposed oxidative radical cascade cyclization strategy is problematic. Because of this, we have overcome the challenge by developing a novel epoxide ring-opening ring-closing strategy for establishing the major motif of picrotoxane skeleton (AB ring system). For the synthesis of the cyclization precursor, the installation of the sidechain via 1,2-nucleophilic addition gave a roughly 1:1 diastereomeric mixtures. Fortunately, we found that the undesired diastereomer can be completely converted to the desired one using a modified Wharton transposition strategy with 49% overall yield. During the COVID-19 pandemic, we encountered great difficulties due to the lockdown of the laboratories, delay of chemical delivery and cancelation of conferences (Part 1, 4.2 -HK$1000 in Expenditure in current report). We tried our best effort to catch up with our schedule after everything had been back to normal. As a result, there is a little delay in our publication schedule. We are currently preparing a manuscript with natural product synthesis using the modified Wharton transposition strategy, which is intended to be submitted for publication by the end of 2024. Moreover, we are currently compiling all the required experimental data in this project and will start to prepare a draft for publication in early 2025.

Major findings and research outcomes in the synthesis of picrotoxane natural product family An efficient and divergent synthetic route for the picrotoxane natural product family have been developed. Totally 15 picrotoxanes and their structural analogues have been prepared for biological studies and some of the synthetic picrotoxane compounds showed exciting results, and we are considering filing a patent to cover their new structures and biological functions. Moreover, we have also developed new cyclization and oxygenation strategies, which can be applied to the synthesis of other classes natural products. 2. The results of the study have been incorporated in the published paper in ChemistrySelect (Part C, 8, no. 1). Moreover, the modified Wharton transposition strategy can also be employed for installation of different oxygenation patterns in several sub-class of ent-kaurane diterpenoids (Submitted to The Journal of Organic Chemistry, manuscript no.: jo-2024-029324, under view, Part C 8, no. 2) and triquinane-containing natural products (in preparation, a draft has been attached, Part C, 8, no. 3). Moreover, we are currently compiling all the required experimental data in this project and will start to prepare a draft for publication in early 2025.

12301320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301320.value: The results of the biological studies will guide us to design the second generation of picrotoxane compounds that may lead to a potential drug candidate with a good safety profile. Moreover, the newly developed methods in this project including the Lewis acid-induced epoxide ring-opening ring-closing cyclization and the modified Wharton transposition strategy have high potential for applications in other natural product synthesis. We are currently exploring their utilities in the synthesis of miliusanes, its dimers and rearranged derivatives. This class of natural products is recently isolated by my collaborator in the School of Chinese Medicine in HKBU and they exhibited potent cytotoxic activities towards a variety of human cancer cell lines.

12301320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301320.value: Compounds that isolated from nature, especially herbal plants, have proven to be a fertile ground for development of new drugs. However, many natural of these compounds are difficult to obtain from the nature due to their low natural abundance. In this project, we have developed a new chemical method that can efficiently prepare a class of natural compounds that isolated from a poisonous plant and study the correlations between their structures and biological functions. Moreover, the new chemical methods developed in this project can be applied for preparation other classes of natural compounds that show promising anti-cancer activities.

12301420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301420.value: This project is concerned with the mathematical study of three classes of spectral problems. We aim to characterise the geometric structures of various associated eigenfunctions as well as to consider the corresponding applications to inverse problems and material sciences. It is a continuation and an extension of the PI's recent work initiated with his coauthors on this intriguing and important topic. The first class of spectral problems is concerned with the eigenfunctions associated to three partial differential operators (PDOs) including the Laplacian, Lame and Maxwellian operators. We shall study the geometric properties of the nodal or generalised singular sets of the corresponding eigenfunctions. Indeed, we shall establish the sharp quantitative relationship between the analytic behaviours of the eigenfunctions at certain nodal/generalised singular points and the curvature of the nodal/generalised singular curve/surface at those points. In particular, in the corner/edge point case, we shall accurately characterise the vanishing order of the eigenfunction and its relationship to the corresponding corner/edge angle. The results obtained can be used to establish novel unique identifiability results for several geometrical inverse scattering problems by at most a few far-field measurements, as well as to produce important applications for the Pompeiu's problem in integral geometry. The second class of spectral problems is concerned with the interior transmission eigenfunctions associated to acoustic and elastic wave scattering. We aim to characterise the geometric behaviours of the transmission eigenfunctions at a corner point or an admissible high-curvature point. For the acoustic problem, we are mainly interested in the anisotropic case, whereas for the elastic problem, we shall study the case that the Lame parameters possess jump singularities. The results obtained have fundamental implications to invisibility cloaking. They can also be used to establish novel unique identifiability results in determining the shapes/supports of a general class of inhomogeneous media, independent of their contents, by a single far-field measurement. The third class of spectral problems is concerned with the eigenfunctions of the Neumann-Poincare (NP) operators. The NP operators are a type of boundary layer potential operators. We aim to quantitatively characterise the localisation/concentration behaviours ("quantum ergodicity") of the NP eigenfunctions at high-curvature boundary points within both quasi-static regime and the frequency regime beyond the quasi-static approximation. The results obtained shall have significant implications to plasmonic resonances and plasmonic imaging. 此項目主要考慮三類微分/積分算子特徵值問題中特徵函數的幾何結構及其在反問題和材料科學中的應用。該課題為項目負責人近幾年研究的延伸和拓展。 第一類問題是關於Laplacian、Lame和Maxwellian算子的特徵函數的幾何結構。我們將要刻畫此類特徵函數的零點集或廣義奇異點集的一些獨特的幾何結構。尤其是，我們將要建立特徵函數在一個給定零點/廣義奇異點附近的解析行為與此零點/廣義奇異點所在曲線（二維）或曲面（三維）的曲率之間的量化關係。在零點集/廣義奇異點集為直線（二維）或平面（三維）的特殊情形下，我們將精確刻畫兩個或多個零點（廣義奇異點）直線/平面相交出的多面角的角度與特徵函數在相交處的消失階的關係。所得到的相關結果將用來針對若干幾何反問題建立新穎的唯一重構結果，以及對積分幾何中的Pompeiu問題產生重要應用。 第二類問題是關於聲波或彈性波散射理論中的傳輸特徵值問題。我們將要刻畫傳輸特徵函數在角點或高曲率點處的幾何行為。對聲波問題，我們主要考慮各向異性的情形，而對於彈性波問題，我們主要考慮Lame係數有跳躍奇性的情形。相關的結果對隱形現象有重要蘊含意義，同時可以用來建立利用一次遠場測量來重構一個聲波/彈性波散射體形狀的唯一性結果。 第三類問題是關於Neumann-Poincare（NP）算子的特徵函數的幾何結構。我們將要刻畫NP特徵函數在高曲率點的局部能量集中現象。所得的結果將對等離子激元共振及相關的成像技術有重要蘊含意義。

12301420.label: Realisation of objectives
12301420.value: All the research objectives have been accomplished and the results obtained within this project are fruitful. The first two objectives are concerned with quantitatively characterising the vanishing order of the Laplacian/Lame/Maxwellian eigenfunctions at geometrically singular points as well as the corresponding application to inverse scattering problems. Based upon our earlier efforts, we established the desired vanishing properties in different scenarios and applied them to the corresponding inverse problems to derive novel identifiability results. The 3rd and 4th objectives are concerned with the local geometric property of transmission eigenfunctions as well as the corresponding applications to inverse medium problems and invisibility cloaking. We have achieved both objectives by establishing the desired properties and applying them to inverse problems. It is worth mentioning that the mathematical findings in Objectives 3 and 4 provide theoretical foundation for a new framework of wave super-resolution imaging as well as a novel imaging scheme in our study. The 5th and 6th objectives are concerned with the local geometric properties of the so-called Neumann-Poincare eigenfunctions as well as their applications to plasmon resonances and metamaterials study. We have achieved these objectives by establishing the localization/concentration properties and applying them to the metamaterial study.

Nevertheless, emerging new applications in mathematics, physics and engineering give rise to new spectral studies. 12301420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301420.value: This project is concerned with the mathematical study of three classes of spectral problems. We aim to characterise the geometric structures of various associated eigenfunctions as well as to consider the corresponding applications to inverse problems and material sciences. We have accomplished the research goals by unveiling several intriguing spectral patterns including the local vanishing properties around singular points and the curvature concentration phenomena in different physical contexts. Moreover, we applied those spectral results to the mathematical study of inverse problems to derive novel unique identifiability results as well as to derive new quantitative understandings of metamaterials. The research findings in this project mutually enrich the spectral theory, the theory of inverse problems and the theory of metamaterials.

12301520.label: Project Objectives
12301520.value: To compare the accuracy and efficiency of kernel-based regularized least-squares approximation methods, which include both level-set and parameterized surface approaches, for estimating normal vectors from some raw point cloud based on the nearest neighborhood search. Both noise-free and noisy cases will be addressed. To develop data-dependent neighborhood search algorithms that avoid selecting data points in regions where the function has rapid variations or discontinuities. Developed algorithms will be applied and verified by the normal estimation methods in the above objective. To develop nonlinear refinement schemes for normal vector estimation and study their convergence behaviors with respect to the number of data points and employed kernel under the hood. To extend the kernel-based regularized least-squares approximation methods in Objective 1 to compute curvatures with analytic formulas and to study the effect of using regularization techniques in different order of differentiation. To develop kernel-based curvatures estimation schemes using first order differentiation only. Compare the numerical performance of the proposed schemes with those obtained in the above objective. To apply the developed algorithms in this project, along with other appropriate techniques and nonlinear solvers, to various applications of shape processing based on point cloud.

12301520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301520.value: 本項目擬考慮基於原始點雲上的數值微分問題。其中，原始點雲是由來源於物體表面的點雲的三維坐標構成，且存在一定誤差。本項目將應用成熟的基於核函數方法求解點雲方法和其理論基礎，研究一類新型的、用於求解原始點雲上的法向量和曲率的算法。針對法向量的數值估計，本項目擬採用基於核函數的離散最小二乘法近似估計局部點雲所構成曲面的表達函數（水平集法或參數表示法）。該方法具有 $W_2^\mu(\Omega)$ -收斂性（$\mu\geq0$）。同時，通過目標點處的數據誤差估計，本項目也將發展一種自適應地、基於點雲數據的局部影響域搜索算法。並且，依據法向量與拉普拉斯-貝爾特拉米算子的表達關係，本項目將進一步研發一種點雲加密算法來提升精度。針對點雲上的曲率估計，本項目擬通過使用更高階的數值微分估計拓展以上算法進行求解。其次，為提高算法的魯棒性，本項目將僅使用一階數值微分估計，並應用於各類基於核函數的數值方法中以計算曲率。最後，本項目擬應用所提出的算法用於解決兩類幾何處理的實際問題中。

12301520.label: Realisation of objectives
12301520.value: The project aimed to develop and analyze kernel-based approximation methods for estimating curvatures and applying them to raw point clouds. Objectives, which were not explicitly addressed in the midterm report, have been comprehensively realized through a combination of theoretical advancements and practical applications. The project's adaptability in shifting focus from kernel-based methods to alternative techniques where necessary ensured that the overarching goals were met. Below is a detailed discussion on how the objectives have been realized, including the extent of achievement, challenges encountered, and attempts to overcome them. The work described in [7] primarily addressed Obj. 1 by reformulating the interpolation framework for point cloud data. Traditional regularization techniques, while effective for smooth approximations, were found to be inadequate for noisy or high-curvature data, as they inherently smoothed out the features that point cloud processing aims to preserve. A constrained optimization model based on kernel-based interpolation was introduced instead, significantly improving the accuracy of normal vector estimation. This work allows application of point cloud process in Obj. 6 to balance smoothness in flat region with the preservation of high-curvature features. As reported in the midterm report, extended Rippa's algorithm in [1] for leave-p-out cross-validation, reducing computational costs and improving robustness in kernel-based interpolation. For Obj. 2, [2] developed an adaptive stencil size selection algorithm that worked effectively with non-uniform data distributions. Although originally designed for kernel-based meshless methods for solving PDEs, this algorithm provided a robust foundation for data-dependent neighborhood search algorithms required for this objective. The primary contribution came from [8], which developed a B-Spline-based interpolation framework to interpolate point cloud. Unlike surface graph setting, this approach interpolated parameterized equations of unknown surfaces, avoiding the challenges associated with jumps or discontinuities in data. The B-Spline framework proved particularly advantageous for stable and efficient computations, as well as for curvature estimation independent of parameterization. Challenges in interpolating over discontinuities were addressed by splitting the interpolation into multiple dimensions, and B-Splines were chosen over kernel methods for their adaptability and efficiency, especially for evolving surfaces. While nonlinear refinement schemes were initially explored for Obj. 3, their high computational cost made them impractical for large-scale applications. Instead, as demonstrated in [8], the use of B-Splines offered an efficient alternative. B-Splines enabled dynamic addition and removal of interpolation points, effectively mimicking the benefits of nonlinear refinement without the associated computational overhead. This approach simplified algorithm design while maintaining accuracy and efficiency, addressing the core requirement of this objective. Obj. 4 highlighted the limitations of regularized least-squares methods in curvature computation, as illustrated in [7]. Traditional regularization techniques tended to smooth out high-curvature features, contradicting the goals of point cloud processing. To address this, the focus shifted to finding the best interpolation framework, leading to notable improvements in curvature computation accuracy. The constrained optimization framework developed in [7] proved particularly effective in resolving this issue, while [1] indirectly supported this objective by providing robust algorithms for interpolation that could be extended to curvature computation. These advancements formed the theoretical foundation for further studies in curvature estimation. For Obj. 5, first-order differentiation schemes for curvature estimation were explored. However, numerical tests revealed no significant advantage in using kernel-based methods for this purpose. Instead, the work in [6] pivoted to a non-kernel-based meshfree method that relied on Taylor series expansion using nodal values to approximate the shape operator and subsequently curvatures. This shift allowed for more effective curvature estimation without the limitations of kernel-based methods. The results demonstrated that while kernel-based schemes are feasible, non-kernel alternatives provide greater flexibility and efficiency. This outcome highlighted the project's adaptability in shifting focus from kernel-based methods when they were found to be less effective, ensuring that the overarching goals of the project were achieved. Obj. 6 was realized through a series of studies that applied the developed methods to practical shape processing problems. In [4], Laplace-Beltrami diffusion-based shape processing algorithms were explored, emphasizing the importance of oversampling ratios in achieving stable and accurate solutions. This work validated the applicability of the developed algorithms to surface diffusion problems. In [5], the effects of surface roughness on pattern formation were investigated, providing a deeper understanding of how roughness impacts point cloud processing. This reverse approach offered insights into processing noisy or rough surfaces. Furthermore, [8] proposed a B-Spline-based method for evolving point cloud data, which provided an efficient alternative to radial basis functions for dynamic surface processing. This approach minimized computational overhead while maintaining accuracy, making it particularly suitable for applications involving evolving surfaces. The findings from these studies demonstrated the versatility and robustness of the developed algorithms, enabling their successful application to a wide range of shape processing tasks. Overall, the project has successfully achieved its objectives, with significant advancements in both kernel-based and alternative methods for curvature estimation and point cloud processing. Key challenges, such as the limitations of regularization techniques and the computational cost of nonlinear refinement schemes, were addressed through innovative approaches such as B-Splines and adaptive algorithms. These outcomes reflect the robustness and flexibility of the methodologies developed in this project, paving the way for future research and applications in shape processing and point cloud analysis. 12301520.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301520.value: The project made significant advancements in developing efficient methods for curvature estimation and point cloud processing, focusing on a novel kernel trial space and extending B-Spline-based methods to handle evolving surfaces. These contributions address challenges in interpolation and curvature estimation, moving beyond static setups to enable more practical applications. A key theoretical achievement lies in the reformulation of the kernel trial space for interpolation. Traditional kernel-based methods, while effective for smooth functions, often fail to handle sharp features or noisy data effectively. This project introduced a constrained optimization model within the kernel-based interpolation framework, which improved the accuracy of normal vector estimation. The new trial space balances the trade-off between smoothness and preserving high-curvature features, providing a robust foundation for curvature computations. This approach enhances numerical stability and enables precise feature detection, making it well-suited for real-world point cloud data. The project also extended interpolation methods to dynamic, evolving surfaces using a B-Spline-based framework. Unlike static setups in kernel-based methods, this framework allows for the interpolation and evolution of point cloud data over time, addressing the need to handle moving surfaces. B-Splines were chosen for their adaptability and computational efficiency, enabling dynamic addition or removal of interpolation points and handling complex, time-varying geometries. This approach minimizes computational overhead while maintaining accuracy, making it an effective alternative to radial basis function methods. The ability to process evolving surfaces represents an advancement over static configurations, offering solutions for applications such as shape deformation, surface reconstruction, and dynamic simulations. These findings show that the methodologies developed in this project are both theoretically robust and practical.

12301520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301520.value: The findings from this project open up several research opportunities in numerical analysis and computational methods. The B-Spline-based framework for evolving surfaces offers potential for applications in problems involving free or moving boundaries. PDEs with such boundaries could benefit from kernel-based methods using the new trial space for solving governing equations, while boundary motion could be addressed using the B-Spline framework. Data points in meshfree methods could align with an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian formulation, with efficient solutions provided by the Method of Fundamental Solutions. The novel kernel trial space also has potential applications in physics-informed neural networks or DeepONets for solving PDEs with complex geometries or noisy data. These results suggest exciting directions for expanding the project's impact, whether through neural network approaches or advanced numerical methods. Potential applications include biomechanics, material sciences, and fluid-structure interaction problems, where the ability to handle evolving geometries and irregular data is crucial.

12301520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301520.value: This project focused on developing new mathematical tools to better understand the shapes and surfaces of objects represented by scattered data points, often called point clouds. Point clouds are used in many technologies, such as 3D scanning, computer graphics, and engineering simulations. However, analyzing these raw data points, especially for calculating surface properties like curvature or tracking how surfaces change over time, is both challenging and computationally demanding. This research introduced two key advancements: a new mathematical framework for accurately estimating surface features (like sharp edges or curves) and a method using smooth curves called B-Splines to handle surfaces that move or deform over time. These methods go beyond traditional approaches, which are often limited to static surfaces or fail to handle noisy data effectively. The B-Spline-based approach, in particular, allows for fast and efficient analysis of evolving surfaces, making it practical for real-world applications.

12301720.label: Project Objectives
12301720.value: Method to realize broad-spectrum MALDI imaging mass spectrometry (IMS) of bacteria MALDI-IMS is a powerful tool that shows the spatial distribution of molecules on a sample. Although the MALDI-IMS of bacteria has been reported (Nat.Chem.Biol.2009), it’s far from fully developed; especially, there hasn’t been report about IMS of proteins in bacteria, probably due to the challenge of ionization through the cell wall. Current MALDI protocol for intact bacteria is incompatible with IMS due to the destroyed spatial pattern of molecules by strong solvents for extracting proteins. In our preliminary work, we found some conditions to realize MALDI-IMS of bacteria that includes protein signals; we will develop this into a general method. This method will be broadly used in studies of bacterial interspecies communication and mechanisms of drug resistance. As discussed in 2(a), antibiotic resistance is a growing threat to human, and researchers have been developing rapid, effective, and low-cost ASTs. There are generally two categories of methods; each has fundamental drawbacks. Recently we created a novel phenotypic method using “cell-on-hydrogel” microfluidic device to test the antimicrobial susceptibility of multiple drugs and their combinations at high speed and throughput. The device generates stable 2D gradients of drug combinations to test the individual or synergistic effects of drugs in parallel fashion. This device has an inherent advantage for MALDI-IMS as cells are cultured on device surface and form spatial pattern according to the drug gradient. In this work we aim to couple this device with IMS. For the objectives discussed below, the capability of obtaining full spectrum of analytes will be beneficial. Fingerprint-based MALDI-IMS Current MALDI-IMS is based on the signal of individual m/z ratios, i.e., single molecule types. This strategy is straightforward and useful for the understanding of pathways. In this work, however, we will try to introduce an additional way of data usage which may realize fingerprint-based imaging. In MS analysis of bacteria, a fingerprint is a spectrum correlating to a specific species or subspecies, which can be used in identification through comparing with a database. In our design, the signal from a particular bacteria’s fingerprint will be rendered into an image showing a distribution. In short, while current IMS commonly uses the raw signal of a specific type of molecules, our fingerprint-based IMS uses processed signal from a specific group of molecules. Simultaneous microbial identification and AST through combining cell-on-top hydrogel microfluidic chip with MALDI-TOF IMS In this part, we aim to apply MALDI-IMS to our cell-on-top hydrogel microfluidic chip to realize identification through algorithm. By doing this, we will have chance to skip the tedious isolation process and thus accelerate the drug resistance test. As discussed in 2(a), ASTs are not widely used to guide prescriptions; one fundamental reason is that it takes too long to complete a relatively reliable phenotypic test. Before ASTs, identification of the species is necessary. At present, the most convenient method is to use the MALDI-TOF fingerprints. However, to ensure the reliability, only single strains can be identified, making isolation necessary beforehand, which takes at least 24 hours. That is to say, any effort in rapid and reliable AST has to address this challenge first. Our “cell-on-hydrogel” device enables a chance to address this challenge. As the cells loaded to the testing region face 2-D gradients of drugs and form different spatial distributions, there could be an analogous isolation effect on the device during the AST process. Accordingly, it becomes possible to capture data and realize identification based on the difference in signal over the tested surface. By combining identification with AST, we will be able to greatly reduce the total turnaround time from days to hours. A new-generation drug-resistance testing technology to guide medication and assist drug discovery - rapid, low-cost, capable of testing mixed species and drug combinations, and rich in resistance mechanism information Another reason that ASTs have not been widely used to guide prescriptions is that the results are often inconsistent with the patient outcome especially when the patient is taking other medication. A main challenge is that current ASTs only test single drugs but cannot simulate the synergistic effects of drugs or in-vivo effects. There is no standard tests for drug combinations yet, although they are commonly used in prescription. While our method has chance to replace and upgrade the current standard method, it also has chance to address the above demand. As our platform has chance to skip isolation process before tests, it may better retain the coexistence state of the bacteria, and has chance to introduce various factors to simulate the real environment, which is expected to bring ASTs and the actual drug effect together. Furthermore, the large volume of MALDI-TOF IMS information obtained from our system may provide abundant information of resistance mechanism.

This strategy is straightforward and useful for the understanding of pathways. In this work, however, we will try to introduce an additional way of data usage which may realize fingerprint-based imaging. In MS analysis of bacteria, a fingerprint is a spectrum correlating to a specific species or subspecies, which can be used in identification through comparing with a database. In our design, the signal from a particular bacteria’s fingerprint will be rendered into an image showing a distribution. In short, while current IMS commonly uses the raw signal of a specific type of molecules, our fingerprint-based IMS uses processed signal from a specific group of molecules.

Simultaneous microbial identification and AST through combining cell-on-top hydrogel microfluidic chip with MALDI-TOF IMS In this part, we aim to apply MALDI-IMS to our cell-on-top hydrogel microfluidic chip to realize identification through algorithm. By doing this, we will have chance to skip the tedious isolation process and thus accelerate the drug resistance test. As discussed in 2(a), ASTs are not widely used to guide prescriptions; one fundamental reason is that it takes too long to complete a relatively reliable phenotypic test. Before ASTs, identification of the species is necessary. At present, the most convenient method is to use the MALDI-TOF fingerprints. However, to ensure the reliability, only single strains can be identified, making isolation necessary beforehand, which takes at least 24 hours. That is to say, any effort in rapid and reliable AST has to address this challenge first. Our “cell-on-hydrogel” device enables a chance to address this challenge. As the cells loaded to the testing region face 2-D gradients of drugs and form different spatial distributions, there could be an analogous isolation effect on the device during the AST process. Accordingly, it becomes possible to capture data and realize identification based on the difference in signal over the tested surface. By combining identification with AST, we will be able to greatly reduce the total turnaround time from days to hours.

A new-generation drug-resistance testing technology to guide medication and assist drug discovery - rapid, low-cost, capable of testing mixed species and drug combinations, and rich in resistance mechanism information Another reason that ASTs have not been widely used to guide prescriptions is that the results are often inconsistent with the patient outcome especially when the patient is taking other medication. A main challenge is that current ASTs only test single drugs but cannot simulate the synergistic effects of drugs or in-vivo effects. There is no standard tests for drug combinations yet, although they are commonly used in prescription. While our method has chance to replace and upgrade the current standard method, it also has chance to address the above demand. As our platform has chance to skip isolation process before tests, it may better retain the coexistence state of the bacteria, and has chance to introduce various factors to simulate the real environment, which is expected to bring ASTs and the actual drug effect together. Furthermore, the large volume of MALDI-TOF IMS information obtained from our system may provide abundant information of resistance mechanism.

12301720.value: 抗菌素耐藥性（AMR）是微生物對抗生素產生耐藥性的現象。對全球公共衛生和現代社會而言，AMR已是迫在眉睫的威脅。 在以經驗為標準的現代醫療系統中，濫用抗生素大大加快了這種自然現象。 另一方面，新型抗生素的發展停滯不前-已有20年時間沒有新型抗生素能被開發，因此保留有效製劑成為當務之急。在這情況下，重要的是仔細研究這現象及相關技術，以防止發生這末日現象。 除了經驗療法外，最佳治療將需要配以最合適的劑量和服藥時間，才能給予最合適的藥物。這一目標只有在獲得有關特定病原體對不同藥物耐藥性的關鍵信息，例如最小抑制濃度（MIC），才能實現。在微生物學中，MIC是指最低濃度化學的物質（通常是藥物），能防止細菌的可見生長，這可以通過抗菌藥敏試驗（AST）獲得。然而，由於當前方法有顯著局限性，例如速度慢和低效率，AST因而並未得到廣泛採用。 在此，我們旨在開發一種細菌研究平台，該平台不僅可以滿足臨床AST的需求，並有助於研究耐藥機制和開發新藥物。該平台基於我們小組開發的水凝膠微流控芯片，並將MALDI-TOF成像質譜（IMS）作為下游處理。雖然同為基於微流體的設備，但與以往不同的是，細胞是在設備的頂部培養，而不是培養在微通道內部。這種設計使我們的平台更具通用性和用戶友好性，並且更接近於當前的培養皿培養標準方法，例如，它消除了基於通道培養物的剪切應力問題，並易於收穫細胞。我們的設計允許以2D方式可靠地生成穩定的線性藥物梯度。經過簡單的樣品處理後，可以在此設備上進行混合培養的AST。可以同時測試不同的藥物組合，並根據它們在抗菌敏感性上的差異，將培養的細菌在空間上分離到培養表面的不同區域。因此，該平台希望開發成為一種新的AST範例，該範例可以實現同時進行的微生物AST和細菌鑑定，並成為抵抗AMR的有力武器。 我們的設備可以在一個芯片上支持多種細菌，並藉助顯微鏡技術和成像質譜技術，監測受藥物處理或動態環境影響的細菌生長變化。擬議的系統可就有關患者提供快速而關鍵的數據，從而指導抗生素的處方並在臨床環境中促進謹慎用藥。這不僅能改善單個患者的治療結果，亦有助降低細菌產生耐藥性的機會。

12301720.label: Realisation of objectives
12301720.value: Overall, all objectives were fully achieved during project period. We have established an MSI method for bacterial metabolites and ribosomal proteins, which can be used to visualize signals of bacteria cultured on microfluidic devices, as well as cell responses under gradient drug concentrations were monitored (Objective 1&2). Based ribosomal proteins, simultaneous microbial identification and AST were able to be achieved (Objective 3), which provides a more powerful tool for mechanism study and rapid AST of mixed species (Objective 4). Below are the detailed outcomes for each objective. 1.We developed microfluidic based methods to realize broad-spectrum MALDI imaging mass spectrometry (IMS) for both gram positive and negative bacteria. Not only can we obtain spatial distribution of small molecules but also can generated results of peptides with m/z 3000-20000. Current protocols which mainly detect small molecules are based on growing bacteria directly on solid agar media. However, the existence of agar brings a lot of difficulties, such as analytes migration, static electricity under laser irradiation, and difficulty in sterilization. These limitations made current methods can only generate IMS results of small metabolites with m/z less than 2000. However, to achieve identification of bacteria through MALDI, signals of ribosomal proteins, whose m/z is around 3000-20000, are necessary. Therefore, we invented a method removing agar residue from the bacteria without destroying bacteria themselves. This method is inspired by our previous work, which transferred bacteria grown on hydrogel microfluidic chip onto glass slides for microscopic observation. Due to different surface properties between glass and ITO used in MALDI IMS, we made a lot of modifications. We also designed different sample treatment protocols for different kinds of bacteria. By using this method, we mapped ribosomal proteins of single colonies and co-cultured colonies of E.coli, S. aureus and P. aeruginosa without disturbing spatial pattern of molecules and cells. Apart from this, we also developed a moisture-assisted cryo-section method (MACS) realized 3D-MS-imaging of biofilms. In combination with MALDI-MSI, the distribution of endogenic metabolites, including isomeric pairs, as well as exogenous molecules were obtained with high resolution. We also revived the analyzed colonies into 3D models, which clearly showed the various molecular distribution from the inner to the outer layers of the biofilm. The results revealed the complex cell activities inside biofilm colonies, indicating a great potential in studying microbe communities. 2. In this work, we have developed the fingerprint-based MALDI-IMS, an algorithm which can realize distribution of different fingerprints. In MS analysis of bacteria, a fingerprint is a spectrum correlating to a specific species or subspecies, which can be used in identification through comparing with a database. That is to say, the signal from a particular species' fingerprint will be rendered into an image showing a distribution of the species. During the processing of the dataset, we employed a Multilayer Perceptron Classifier (MLPC). This system is composed of multiple layers of perceptrons, each one mimicking the operation of human neurons. The architecture of the classifier includes an input layer that receives the input data, hidden layers that lie between the input and output layers, and an output layer that delivers the final prediction results. With the aid of activation functions that decide whether a neuron should be activated, and the assistance of backpropagation and gradient descent processes to adjust weights and biases based on output errors, the multilayer perceptron is capable of handling complex nonlinear problems. Through the aforementioned data processing procedures, the classifier can also be applied to our classification of bacterial species and their concentrations. 3. We have settled the experimental parameters for polymicrobial AST and the research model, including the single and co-cultured S. aureus and P. aeruginosa under the treatment of gentamicin and polymyxin B. This platform has a hydrogel microfluidic chip, on which bacteria can form spatial pattern under effect of antibiotic or other stimulates. This spatial distribution can provide a direct observation of cell growth and also quantitative MIC. After that, bacterial pattern can also be transferred onto MALDI-TOF target plates to obtain molecular information, no matter small molecular metabolites or protein. Combined with MALDI methods illustrated in Objective 1&2, this platform can gain both identification results and AST results simultaneously within 6 hours, which can meet the real requirements of rapid AST in practical use. This platform can not only process isolated species but also be compatible with mixed culture, which fundamentally saved time of the entire process and hoped to become a new paradigm of AST and a powerful weapon against AMR. 4. In order to maximize the potential of this platform, we developed algorithms which can perform optical image analysis and spectra analysis for digging obtained information to the maximum extent. In this platform, as bacteria were transferred onto transparent ITO substrates without cell migration, optical information at single-cell level can also be obtained. With the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, we developed convolutional neural network (CNN) models that can recognize bacteria types and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) boundaries of AST results. For molecular information, we investigated the distribution of metabolites in microbial communities from P. aeruginosa colonies of 36h or 96h old. We traced 2-heptyl-3- hydroxyquinolone (PQS) and 4-hydroxy-2-heptylquinoline-N-oxide (HQNO) and other metabolites to reveal the specific location of different isomers of quinolines inside a biofilm for the first time. Based on this method, 3D models of bacteria colonies were successfully reconstructed with high precision, which help display the true location of different chemical substances in colonies, which is crucial for understanding the regulatory network of biofilms.

12301720.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301720.value: This project successfully achieved its objectives, marking significant advancements in microbial analysis through the development of innovative Mass Spectrometry Imaging (MSI) techniques coupled with microfluidics. We established a groundbreaking microfluidic-based MALDI-IMS method, effectively overcoming the limitations associated with traditional agar-based protocols, which face challenges with large molecules. This new method allows for the precise mapping of ribosomal proteins and metabolites in both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, maintaining spatial integrity while enabling the visualization of small molecules and peptides with m/z values ranging from 3000 to 20000. These capabilities are essential for accurate microbial identification and provide a robust platform for studying bacterial interactions [2, 7]. In addition, we developed a sophisticated fingerprint-based MALDI-IMS algorithm employing a Multilayer Perceptron Classifier (MLPC) to enhance species identification through detailed spectral analysis. This approach allows for the visualization of species-specific distributions, greatly improving classification accuracy and enabling more precise concentration assessments. This advancement provides a powerful tool for microbial identification, offering new insights into microbial diversity and behavior. This platform integrates identification and AST results within a rapid six-hour timeframe, providing a practical solution for real-world applications. Its compatibility with mixed cultures offers substantial time savings, positioning it as a transformative tool in the fight against antimicrobial resistance and setting a new standard for rapid AST methodologies [1, 3]. To maximize the platform's potential, we developed advanced algorithms for optical and spectral analysis, leveraging cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) technology. We created convolutional neural network (CNN) models capable of accurately identifying bacterial types and determining minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) boundaries [8]. Our investigation into metabolite distributions within P. aeruginosa colonies led to the successful reconstruction of high-precision 3D models, revealing the spatial organization of chemical substances within biofilms. This insight is crucial for understanding the complex regulatory networks within microbial communities and has significant implications for future research [2]. In conclusion, the outcomes of this project represent substantial advancements in microbial analysis, providing innovative tools and methodologies that enhance our understanding of bacterial interactions. These developments not only contribute to a deeper understanding of microbial communities but also offer practical solutions in the global fight against antimicrobial resistance. Our work lays a robust foundation for future research and applications in microbiology and biotechnology, with the potential to transform current practices and significantly improve our ability to address pressing global health challenges. In the meantime, the microfluidic technologies developed herein are also useful in other applications.

12301720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301720.value: Through this project, we have significantly advanced our research towards clinical implementation. We have established a robust collaboration with the Prince of Wales Hospital on rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Doctors and professors from PWH are working alongside our team to validate and enhance next-generation testing technologies aimed at improving prescriptions and, ultimately, patient outcomes. This collaboration has deepened our understanding of the needs and constraints in clinical practice, allowing us to identify further development directions for future upgrades. These enhancements will focus on shortening analytical turnaround times, tailoring processing protocols for different sample types, and reducing resource requirements for facilities and operators. While there is a trade-off regarding result accuracy, the benefits will enhance clinical implementation impact. Going forward, we will study the balance between reducing turnaround times and maintaining test accuracy, enabling us to develop a technical solution that is readily applicable in clinical settings. Additionally, we have initiated discussions with professors specializing in genetic analysis of drug resistance and professionals in the testing industry to explore combining phenotypic and genotypic approaches for drug resistance analysis in healthcare and drug discovery applications.

12301720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301720.value: In this project, we developed new techniques to study bacteria more effectively. Traditionally, scientists use methods that have limitations, like growing bacteria on agar, which can interfere with results. We created a new method using microfluidic devices and special imaging techniques that allow us to see important bacterial proteins and metabolites clearly. This helps us identify different bacteria more accurately. We also developed a system that can quickly test how bacteria respond to antibiotics. Using a special chip, we can observe bacteria growth patterns and identify them within six hours, which is much faster than traditional methods. This rapid testing is crucial for fighting antibiotic resistance because it helps doctors choose the right treatment quickly. To enhance our analysis, we used algorithm to create models that can detect different types of bacteria and their reactions to antibiotics. We also studied how chemicals are distributed in bacterial communities, which gives us a better understanding of how bacteria interact and survive. Overall, our work provides new tools and insights that can improve how scientists study bacteria and help in developing better treatments for infections, ultimately contributing to global health efforts against antibiotic resistance.

12301820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301820.value: This project is to seek the solution for better estimating the change of water resources in Central Asian aridzone. The aim of this project is two-folds: (1) to develop a new methodology to assess and simulate regional terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), and (2) to reveal the spatiotemporal pattern of water resources for the evaluation of the impacts by climate change and human activities on the water cycle over Central Asian aridzone. Two scientific questions/issues will be addressed. First, can the change of TWSA, hence the components of the regional water resource, be monitored more efficiently and practically by integrating remote sensing technology and global hydrological models (GHMs)? Second, what is the eco-hydrological response of the regional water cycle, which is revealed by the application of above integrated approach, to climate change and human activity in Central Asian aridzone? A new and innovative approach is proposed to derive TWSA by the assimilation and integration of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) data and the global hydrological models (GHMs). The proposed TWSA estimation methodology overcomes the drawbacks of GHMs due to their uncertainties caused by the limited availability of in situ observations as the model inputs, and the restricted applicability due to structural limits of the model. On the other hand, the proposed approach also seek the solution to improve the TWSA assessment by the GRACE alone, which the short time series and coarse spatial resolution are widely identified as major limits in application. Three research outcomes are expected, including (1) a TWSA estimation method by the assimilation and integration of GRACE and GHM, which, with the proper calibration and validation, can be applied to water resource applications in an arid environment at a regional scale; (2) an improved TWSA dataset covering Central Asian aridzone with a better spatial resolution and longer time series, and derived hydrological components of water cycle such as soil moisture, groundwater, snow water equivalent and ice; and (3) a better understanding about the relationships between the regional water resources and climate change and human activity in Central Asian aridzone. Scientific evidences and advices can therefore be provided to the local policy maker in sustainable water resource management, which is a core element to achieve for solving the international water resource disputes between Central Asian states. 本專案探索更好估計中亞乾旱區水資源變化的研究方法。 研究目標主要包括兩個方面: (1) 發展新的研究方法,評估和類比區域陸地水儲量距平(TWSA)變化; (2) 揭示中亞乾旱區在氣候變化和人類活動作用下水資源的時空變化特徵。 對應的科學問題包括: 第一, 陸地水儲量距平和區域水資源組分能否被遙感技術和全球水文模型有效地檢測? 第二, 中亞乾旱區區域水資源變化對氣候變化和人類活動的回應如何？ 一種新的研究方法將通過融合和同化GRACE數據和全球水文模型數據, 反演陸地水儲量距平數據。 該方法一方面克服作為模型輸入的觀測數據不足和模型結構局限性導致的模型不確定性; 另一方面,提高單獨利用GRACE數據反演TWSA的數據精度, 包括時間序列長度和空間解析度的精度方面。 相關的研究成果包括三個方面: (1) 融合和同化GRACE數據和全球水文模型, 反演TWSA的方法將應用於區域尺度上乾旱區水資源的研究; (2) 提高中亞乾旱區TWSA數據 的空間解析度和構建更長的時間序列, 並反演對應的水迴圈的組分, 如土壤濕度、地下水和雪水當量; (3) 更好的認識中亞乾旱區氣候變化和人類活動對區域水資源的影響。 為當地水資源的可持續利用和管理提供科學依據, 緩解中亞五國之間跨境水資源的矛盾。

12301820.label: Realisation of objectives
12301820.value: This project assessed terrestrial water storage in the Central Asian arid region and its response to climate change. It conducted the analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics, influencing factors, simulation predictions, and the monitoring and application of dry and wet changes in the region. Through methods such as lagged correlation, the study examined the relationships between hydrometeorological factors (temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, and soil moisture) and terrestrial water storage components, demonstrated the impacts of different hydrometeorological factors on terrestrial water storage. Using partial least squares regression, a simulation and prediction model for terrestrial water storage in Central Asia was established based on hydrometeorological elements. Additionally, the impact of human activities on terrestrial water storage was revealed. The relationship between temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, and terrestrial water storage was analyzed to construct a global drought index using GRACE terrestrial water storage data, successfully monitoring dry and wet changes in Central Asia. Objective 1: To investigate an approach/methodology of integrating GRACE and GHMs for monitoring the spatiotemporal change of the water cycle over a large and arid environment. This project developed a comprehensive method that integrates GRACE satellite data with GHMs to monitor spatiotemporal changes in the water cycle in the Central Asian arid region. The integration of these data sources allowed for detailed assessments of terrestrial water storage, capturing both seasonal and long-term variations. It revealed the long-term variation characteristics and evolution patterns of terrestrial water storage across multiple temporal scales—monthly, seasonal, interannual, and decadal. We also identified spatial variations in water storage across different countries, regions, and basins, such as the Aral Sea basin and Tarim River basin. The developed model proved effective in capturing the complex dynamics of water resources in a large and arid environment, providing valuable insights for broader applications in similar regions globally. Objective 2: To examine the relationships between the water cycle and hydro-climatic factors and human activities in Central Asian arid zone. This project constructed a standardized hydrological drought index, Standardized Terrestrial Water Storage Index (STI), for the drought monitoring in Central Asian. STI reflected the deficits of various hydrological components including groundwater and soil moisture. Based on GRACE TWS data, STI provides reliable global observations and more accurately reflects hydrological drought changes, particularly in vegetation and arid regions. By comparing GRACE data with temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and drought index data, we validated the consistency and differences in drought monitoring, providing reasonable explanations based on hydrometeorological variations. The impact of human activities particularly irrigation practices on terrestrial water storage was explored. The increase in agricultural activities in response to growing food demand has led to greater water consumption, further stressing the already limited water resources in the arid region. Large-scale irrigation activities in the region have significantly modified water availability and distribution. These activities lead to the over-extraction of groundwater, reducing terrestrial water storage and altering the hydrological balance.

This integration allowed for detailed assessments of water storage changes across multiple temporal scales (monthly, seasonal, interannual, and decadal) and spatial variations across different basins (Hu et al., 2022). 2. This project analyzed significant long-term variation characteristics and evolution patterns of terrestrial water storage. Regression models were established to quantify the influence of hydro-climatic factors (temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration) on terrestrial water storage. their spatial correlations and dependencies were clarified. The trends and multi-period changes in water storage were identified, providing insights into the complex dynamics of water resources in the arid environment (Hu et al., 2021). 3. The impact of human activities, particularly large-scale irrigation, on terrestrial water storage was highlighted. By analyzing irrigation practices and land use changes, the project demonstrated how over-extraction of groundwater and modifications to natural water cycles have significantly altered water availability and distribution in the region (Zhou and Ismaeel., 2021). 4. A standardized hydrological drought index, STI, based on GRACE TWS data was proposed. STI proved more accurate in reflecting hydrological drought changes, particularly in vegetation and arid regions, compared to other indices. the project validated the consistency of drought monitoring and provided reasonable explanations based on hydrometeorological variations (Cui et al., 2021).

12301820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301820.value: 1. Expanding the study to include other arid and semi-arid regions globally to validate the proposed methodology's robustness and provide comparative insights into different hydrological and climatic conditions. 2. Further research into the specific impacts of various human activities, such as urbanization, deforestation, and industrial water usage, can enhance understanding and management strategies for water resources. Utilizing higher-resolution data and more sophisticated models could improve the accuracy of these assessments. 3. Developing climate change scenarios and integrating them with the existing models and predicting future water storage trends and their implications. This would be valuable for long-term water resource planning and adaptation strategies.

12301820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301820.value: This research project focused on the Central Asian arid region, an area with limited water resources and significant climate challenges. We used satellite data from GRACE, combined with global water models and weather data, to understand how water storage in this dry region changes over time and what influences these changes. By integrating these data sources, we developed a reliable method to monitor water availability, revealing patterns and trends in water storage across different seasons and years. We also explored how factors like temperature, rainfall, and human activities (such as irrigation) affect water levels. One key finding was the significant impact of large-scale irrigation, which often depletes groundwater and alters natural water cycles. We also introduced a new drought monitoring index, the STI, which provides a more accurate picture of drought conditions by considering multiple water components like groundwater and soil moisture. This research is valuable because it offers better tools and methods for tracking and managing water resources in arid regions, helping policymakers and communities make informed decisions to address water scarcity and climate change impacts.

12302020.value: To investigate the influence of MnO2 and light-assisted MnO2 oxidation on the transformation chemistry of UV absorbing agents; To identify all transformation products (TPs) produced by MnO2 oxidation and light-assisted MnO2 oxidation of UV absorbing agents, and to determine how they are formed. To identify all transformation products (TPs) produced by MnO2 oxidation and light-assisted MnO2 oxidation of UV absorbing agents, and to determine how they are formed. This will be accomplished through systematic instrumental characterizations using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QTOF-MS), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR);

12302020.label: Realisation of objectives
12302020.value: The stated project objectives have been completely and satisfactorily achieved. The degradation behaviors of the selected UV absorbing agents under the influence of MnO2 and photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation were investigated. For MnO2 oxidation, all three selected UV absorbing agents (i.e., AVO, BP-3 and UV-320) were degradable, with the degradation efficiency in the decreasing order of AVO, BP-3, UV-320 at the 240 min time interval. For photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation, only a slight enhancement of degradation efficiency (c.a. 5%) was observed. This is because both BP-3 and UV-320 are photo inert UV absorbing agents. However, for photo-sensitive UV absorbing agent (i.e., AVO), photolysis takes a major role and dominates the degradation process. For AVO, the degradation efficiencies of MnO2 oxidation, photolysis and photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation were in the decreasing order of photolysis, MnO2, photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation. Furthermore, the transformation products (TPs) were also identified and structurally elucidated. For the TPs formed under MnO2 and photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation, 16, 13 and 2 TPs were identified for BP-3, AVO and UV-320, respectively. In particular, the generated radical-coupled TPs of BP-3 and AVO are all observed to be formed only in the presence of MnO2. Through structural elucidation and the purported transformation pathways of these TPs, there is a significant contribution of MnO2 in both MnO2 and photolysis-assisted MnO2 oxidation. [fulfilled objectives 1 and 2] To evaluate the ecotoxicological impact of MnO2 oxidation, the toxicity of the identified TPs of UV absorbing agents were predicted through in silico ECOSAR estimation. In general, the radical-coupled TPs formed were predicted to have an increase in ecotoxicities. Furthermore, with the genetically modified yeast strain recombinant assay, an increase in estrogenic activity was observed after undergoing MnO2-mediated transformations. The combination of in silico toxicity, mobility and persistence prediction, together with the genetically modified yeast strain recombinant assay, allowed a more comprehensive evaluation of the toxicity impact of the TPs generated by MnO2-mediated transformation. [fulfilled objective 3] Based on the findings in objectives #1, 2, and 3, it can be demonstrated that under MnO2-mediated transformation, UV absorbing agents are transformed into different TPs. Particularly, the formation of radical-coupled TPs is alarming, since these TPs are predicted to have increased toxicity, mobility and persistence as compared to their respective parent compounds. Moreover, an increase in estrogenic potential was also observed when the TPs were evaluated with a genetically modified yeast strain recombinant assay. Therefore, the potential in forming more toxic compounds when treating micropollutants with MnO2 should be carefully evaluated. To achieve a better removal performance of MnO2, future development may consider the combination of MnO2 with other water treatment techniques for safety removal of micropollutants.

12302020.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302020.value: In the present study, the transformation chemistry of organic UV absorbing agents was studied under MnO2 reactions, including MnO2 oxidation and photolysis-assisted MnO2 transformation. Benzophenone-3 (BP-3), avobenzone (AVO) and UV-320 are the major organic UV absorbers that were used in a variety of personal care products. After MnO2-transformation, the potential risk of the transformation products (TPs) derived from these UV absorbing agents to both environment and human health was evaluated by in silico prediction and in vitro bioassay. Laboratory simulated experiments have revealed that UV absorbing agents are degraded under MnO2 transformations. For photo-inert UV absorbing agents (i.e., BP-3 and UV-320), MnO2 transformations have shown higher degradation efficiency compared to photolysis alone. To further evaluate the impacts of real water constituents to the transformation of UV absorbing agents by MnO2-mediated oxidation, the presence of chloride ions, bromide ions, carbonate ions and humic acid were studied. The higher the concentration of these water constituents, the lower the degradation efficiencies of UV absorbing agents that were degraded by MnO2-mediated oxidation. Degradation of UV absorbing agents by MnO2-mediated oxidation will also be affected by the presence of dissolved organic matters in aquatic sources. The TPs of UV absorbing agents transformed by MnO2-mediated oxidation were then identified and structurally elucidated by UHPLC-QTOF-MS and UHPLC-MS/MS analyses. The environmental impacts of these TPs have been evaluated by ECOSAR, OECD LRTP and Pov screening tools based on their chemical structures. Among different TPs formed under MnO2-mediated transformation, TPs formed by radical coupling were predicted to increase in both acute and chronic toxicities towards aquatic organisms compared to the parent compounds, potentially threatening aquatic lives with increased toxicity. Also, the environmental fate of these TPs has shown significant increase in terms of mobility and persistence compared to the parent compounds. From these predictions, these TPs may transport further in distance and retain longer in the environment. For the estrogenic activity, A-YES bioassay was conducted by using BP-3 as a model compound. Through MnO2-mediated transformation, the estrogenic activity of TPs derived from BP-3 were enhanced as compared to the parent compound and TPs generated under photolysis alone. Radical-coupled TPs have been suspected of causing adverse impacts to the environment, with increased ecotoxicities and enhanced estrogenic activity. Research articles addressing details of the above findings were published in the (1) Science of the Total Environment, 2023, 901, 166481 and (2) Science of the Total Environment, 2024, 915, 170121.

12302020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302020.value: The present study focused on the transformation chemistry of UV absorbing agents after entering the natural environment. The environmental fate and toxicological effects of TPs formed under MnO2-mediated transformation were also evaluated. With these findings, the transformation pathways of TPs derived from the micropollutants with similar chemical structures can be further deduced. TPs with suspicious adverse impacts to the ecosystem and environment can then be monitored in advance. Moreover, from the results of in silico predictions and in vitro estrogenic activity bioassay, radical-coupled TPs have been reported with potential risks to the environment and human health. Further toxicological assessments of these TPs must be conducted to assess the potential hazards to both the environment and living organisms. For instance, a systematic evaluation of the toxicity of radical-coupled TPs has been planned, which allowed the comprehensive elucidation of the potential hazards of the radical-coupled TPs. The ultimate goal of these studies will serve as the important basis for developing new water treatment techniques that can safely remove micropollutants and avoid the formation of their corresponding toxic TPs.

12302020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302020.value: UV absorbing agents, as one of the widely used chemicals in various personal care products, have raised concern due to their wide spread occurrence in the natural environment and potential endocrine disrupting effects. From our present research findings, it is revealed that once these compounds enter the environment, they will be degraded and transformed by manganese dioxide (MnO2). However, undesired coupled transformation products (TPs) were formed upon this type of transformation. These coupled TPs have shown alteration in toxicity than the original UV absorbing agents with potential risk in causing higher estrogenic activities. These findings suggested that those coupled TPs are worthy for further toxicological investigation. The success of this research project will serve as the basis for the development and improvement of current water treatment techniques in preventing the formation of hazardous TPs to preserve our valuable environment, water resources and human health.

12302320.label: Realisation of objectives
12302320.value: The three objectives, which have been proposed in the GRF proposal, have been completely fulfilled. Objective 1. Devising a versatile method (i.e., LbL-GLAD) to produce MPEA-CNPs Layer-by-layer glancing angle deposition (LbL-GLAD) was devised to generally fabricate multi-principal element alloy chiral nanoparticles (MPEA-CNPs). The LbL-GLAD is composed of GLAD of host CNPs followed by sequential GLAD of dopants on the host CNPs. The handedness of MPEA-CNPs is determined by that of the host CNPs. During GLAD of the host, clockwise and counterclockwise rotation of supporting substrates, on which the host is deposited, lead to the formation of right-handed and left-handed host CNPs, respectively. Then no substrate rotation is applied to perform the GLAD of dopants, so that the dopants inherit the host’s handedness. The atomic ratios of multiple elements in MPEA-CNPs are flexibly tuned with the duration of GLAD of the host and dopants. Objective 2. Compiling a fabrication library of MPEA-CNPs LbL-GLAD has been applied to produce MPEA-CNPs made of binary, ternary, quaternary and ten-element CNPs. The host CNPs are usually made of silver (Ag), and the dopants include aluminum (Al), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), nickel (Ni), gold (Au), platinum (Pt), palladium (Pd), indium (In), tin (Sn) and titanium (Ti). Most of MPEA-CNPs are composed of solid-state solutions, and some have phase segregation. Objective 3. Understanding the microstructures and formation mechanisms of MPEA-CNPs The host CNPs have the atomic-scale chirality, including multi-layer chiral twisting of achiral facets, wave-like chiral lattices, and chiral defects formed at the cores of chirally twisting twin boundaries. The GLAD of dopants on the host causes the heat-stimulated dopant diffusion into chiral lattices of the host, resulting in the formation of MPEA-CNPs. The MPEA-CNPs intrinsically show chiroplasmonic optical activities, characterized with circular dichroism (CD) denoting the differential extinction of left-handed and right-handed circular polarized light. Compared to the host CNPs, the doping generally causes the MPEA-CNPs to amplify their chiroplasmonic optical activities.

12302320.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302320.value: Metallic CNPs promisingly function as asymmetric catalysts but lack an important study in thermal stability of optical activity that stems from metastable chiral lattices at the atomic scale, which can be characterized with CD and second-harmonic generation [Part C. 8-2]. Annealing of the host Ag CNPs at 200 °C eliminates the chiroplasmonic optical activities, mainly ascribed to chiral-to-achiral lattice transformation [Part C. 8-4]. Doping the host with Al, via LbL-GLAD to create binary Ag:Al CNPs composed of solid-state liquids, remarkedly enhances the thermal stability, whereby the optical activities vanish at 700 °C. It is mainly ascribed to an ease in the diffusion of Al atoms in the host and thermal insulation from the Al2O3 layers partially covering the binary CNPs effectively, which prohibit structural relaxation of the metastable chiral lattices. Alloying overwhelmingly involves high-energy fabrication, whereby, however, metastable chiral lattices will unavoidably undergo the chiral-to-achiral relaxation. Hence, the fabrication of MPEA-CNPs is very challenging. The work of [Part C8-4] essentially motivated us to use LbL-GLAD for producing MPEA-CNPs. LbL-GLAD at a low substrate temperature of ≈−40 °C, consisting of GLAD of the host CNPs and the subsequent GLAD of dopants, is devised to extend the alloy compositional space to the ternary (e.g., Ag:Al:Cu and Ag:Al:Au) and quaternary (e.g., Ag:Al:Cu:Au and Al:In:Sn:Ti) [Part C. 8-6]. The low-temperature GLAD-induced alloying facilitates the formation of the metastable multi-layer chiral twisting of achiral facets, chiral defects due to the diffusion of the guests, and chiral electronic bands, leading to a significant amplification of chiroplasmonic optical activities in 20–30 folds. Another method to generate MPEA-CNPs is to perform galvanic replacement reaction (GRR) of the host CNPs in an aqueous electrolyte containing dopant ions, through the galvanic replacement of the host atoms with the dopants. Doping the host Cu CNPs with Au, via LbL-GLAD, facilitate the formation of ternary Cu:Au:M (M: Pt and Ag) CNPs, whereby the dopants Au function as a structural scaffold to assist the GRR-mediated chirality transfer from the host to dopant [Part C. 8-1]. Furthermore, the GRR of the host Ag CNPs with Au leads to the formation of mesoporous binary CNPs, with a significant enhancement of surface areas required by asymmetric catalysis. However, the GRR-mediated chirality transfer is not efficient. We doped the host with Au to significantly enhance the chirality transfer, and additionally employ the Au adhesion layer to increase production yield [Part C. 8-8].

12302320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302320.value: As further development of this GRF project, it is necessary to apply the MPEA-CNPs to asymmetric synthesis and biochemical applications via photo-induction, electrochemical induction, and photoelectrochemical induction. Some prototype asymmetric reactions will be performed, whereby an enantioselectivity induced by the MPEA-CNPs will be engineered and optimized, and the enantiopreferential mechanisms will be studied with an assistance of numerical simulations.

12302320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302320.value: Structural chirality has been imposed onto nano-alloys to introduce diverse new properties. Chiral nanoparticles (CNPs) with the atomic scale chirality are composed of metastable chiral lattices having low thermal stability, so multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) CNPs are very challenging to produce using traditional high-energy fabrication methods. In this project, layer-by-layer glancing angle deposition (LbL-GLAD) is devised to be generally adapted to fabricate MPEA-CNPs composed of a wide range of elements (including silver (Ag), and the dopants include aluminum (Al), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), nickel (Ni), gold (Au), platinum (Pt), palladium (Pd), indium (In), tin (Sn) and titanium (Ti)) and compositional spaces (including the binary, ternary and quaternary). Galvanic replacement reaction of the host CNPs leads to the formation of mesoporous MPEA-CNPs, with significantly enhanced surface areas. This project provides a prospective application of asymmetric catalysts to synthesize an enantiomer with designable chirality, one of the most important topics in modern chemistry and biochemistry to solve the problems of health and environmental pollution.

12302420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302420.value: The discovery of topologically non-trivial phases has revolutionized our understanding of matter and materials. Topology is an important development of traditional band theories. As a previously unexplored degree of freedom, it describes the global properties of wavefunctions over an entire band and it is robust against local perturbation unless the perturbation is strong enough to close the gaps between bands. Such robustness of topological phases makes them fascinating and useful. Topological phases have their root in geometric phases, a universal concept arising from adiabatic evolution, which was first explored in optics and later generalized to all areas of physics. Topological matters were first investigated in condensed matter physics and expanded to electromagnetic waves, optics, and acoustic systems. The emergence of “topological acoustics” is a major breakthrough that has reinvigorated the study of phononic crystals, which are the acoustic analog of electronic bands in solids. In conventional topological phases, an n-dimensional system can sustain (n-1)-dimensional topological edge modes. These edge modes are robust against local perturbations and in some cases can even be immune to back-scattering, making them scientifically fascinating and potentially useful as efficient conducting channels, or, in the case of light and sound, one-way waveguides. Recently, a new class of topological phases named higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs) have been proposed, in which n-dimensional system can have (n-m)-dimensional topological boundary states, with m>1. For example, 0D topological “corner modes” have been found in 2D systems. These modes are localized at corners where two or more edges meet. Similarly, 3D systems can support 1D “hinge modes.” In this proposal, we aim to study novel HOTIs in acoustic systems. First, we plan to use a theoretical approach that constructs finite-sized 2D HOTIs from 1D topological systems, which are much easier to analyze and construct. Specifically, we propose to use this approach to design exactly quantized topological dipole insulators and quadrupole insulators from a 1D Su-Shrieffer-Heeger model. We will also design an experimental platform to realize these 2D HOTIs and observe topological corner modes therein. Moreover, our approach allows us to analyze, from a transfer-matrix point of view, the evanescent coupling effect among corner modes. We hope to identify an experimentally observable effect that can be used to distinguish HOTIs with different physical origins. Lastly, we expect to extend our theoretical framework for the exploration of new topological phases by combining different classes of 1D topological systems. 非平庸拓撲相的發現刷新了人們對材料和物質的認識。作為壹個全新的自由度，拓撲被用作描述波函數在整個能帶的總體性質，如對稱性。這些性質不會因對系統的局部擾動而改變。能帶拓撲是壹個源於對波函數的絕熱演化的描述，因此具有很強的普適性，故在許多不同的物理分支內都能夠體現出來。近年來，拓撲概念在電磁波、光學、聲學等領域得到全新的發展。本課題著眼於聲子晶體中的拓撲。 在傳統拓撲相中， n維的系統中能出現n-1維的拓撲邊界態。這些手性拓撲邊界態具有單向傳播、免於被散射的獨特性質，因此對於能量和信息的輸送等應用具有很高的潛在價值。最近，科學家發現了壹種全新的“高階拓撲絕緣體(HOTI)”，n維的系統中能出現n-m維的拓撲邊界態(m>1)。例如，二維HOTI系統中會出現局域在系統邊角的零維的“拓撲角態”，三維HOTI系統裏會出現壹維的“拓撲棱態”。本課題中，我們將致力實現聲學系統中的高階拓撲態。我們計劃首先通過理論模型，通過壹維拓撲系統（SSH模型）構建二維高HOTI，從而實現量子化的偶極和四極極化。我們將設計聲學系統，並在實驗上觀測這些HOTI中的拓撲角態。另外，擬通過對不同拓撲角態的消逝耦合的研究，找到區分偶極和四級拓撲角態的實驗依據，並深化對其認識。最後，我們將嘗試通過類似手段尋找全新的高階拓撲態。

12302420.label: Realisation of objectives
12302420.value: We have successfully completed all project tasks and achieved all project objectives. 1. Designing higher-order topological insulators from 1D Su-Shrieffer-Heeger (SSH) models Objective 1 is fully achieved. We used Kronecker product to fuse the Hamiltonian of two 1D SSH model to form both 2D SSH lattice and a 2D topological quadrupole lattice. The latter is a higher-order topological insulator that sustains second-order topological corner modes. The same method can be used to construct higher-order topological insulators in 3D or even higher dimensions. The results are published in [1]. 2. Designing acoustic systems for the realization of different classes of higher-order topological insulators Objective 2 is fully achieved. We have designed and fabricated several acoustic crystals based on coupled acoustic cavities. Such acoustic crystals offer tunabilities in onsite energy, hopping strength, hopping sign, and can be tailored to respect various symmetries, such as the chiral symmetry. Detailed design methodology is summarized in [2]. On the other hand, we have also designed and fabricated elastic-wave crystals that can achieve the similar [3]. 3. Distinguishing topological corner modes Objective 3 is fully achieved. By exploring the symmetry in topological dipolar insulators and topological quadrupole insulators, we are able to identify the line shape differences of the topological corner modes in these systems. The theoretical analysis is published in [1] and the experimental verification using acoustic higher-order topological insulators is reported in [4]. 4. Extending the theoretical model to possible new classes of HOTIs Objective 4 is fully achieved. Using the Kronecker product approach, we have theoretically designed and experimentally realized a four-dimensional higher-order Chern insulator [5] and a three-dimensional layered Chern insulator [3] for the first time. The former was realized in a 2D acoustic crystal and the latter in a 2D elastic-wave crystal. In addition, we have explored the potential applications of topological modes in wave manipulations in 3D. Several novel wave-steering effects, including negative refraction enabled by first-order topological surface modes, wave bending by second-order topological hinge modes, and wave localization by third-order topological corner modes, have been successfully demonstrated in the same phononic crystal [6].
