12302420.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302420.value: Two main breakthroughs have been achieved by using the Kronecker product approach mentioned in the proposal. In the first work, we have designed a four-dimensional (4D) higher-order Chern insulator by fusing two copies to AAH models, with each being a two-dimensional Chern insulator belonging to the Z-classification in Class A. The 4D system sustains 3D topology hypersurface modes and 2D second-order topological surface modes. The system is successfully realized in a phononic crystal with two spatial dimensions and two synthetic dimensions. The synthetic dimensions that effectively introduce quantized magnetic fluxes are experimentally realized by tuning the onsite energies, which are the resonant frequencies of the acoustic modes. The real-space projections of the 3D topology hypersurface modes and 2D second-order topological surface modes are observed as 1D edge modes and 0D corner modes. The results are published in Phys. Rev. X 11, 011016 (2021). In the second work, we combined an AAH model with an SSH model to form a 3D Layered higher-order Chern insulator, which we classify as Z x Z2. The topological invariants of the system are a four tuple consisting of three Chern numbers and a bulk polarization. The system was successfully realized using an elastic-wave crystal. The results are published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 214302 (2021). In addition to the proposed works, we have also explored several related topics under the support of this project. In the first work, based on the AAH model, we build an acoustic waveguide system that enforces an adiabatic evolution driven by the synthetic dimension. This allows us the realize the pumping of topological edge modes and observe the adiabatic-nonadiabatic transition (Landau-Zener transition) of topological pumping. The results are published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 054301 (2021). The second work focused on investigating how topological modes can be utilized for manipulating waves in three dimensions. Various innovative wave-steering effects were achieved, such as negative refraction through first-order topological surface modes, wave bending through second-order topological hinge modes, and wave localization through third-order topological corner modes. The results are published in Science Bulletin 66, 1740-1745 (2021).

12302420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302420.value: First, we have thoroughly studied the physics and design methods of higher-order topological modes and explored their potential applications. Second, we have introduced non-Hermitian skin effect to higher-order topological systems and successfully realized, for the first time, topological modes that are no longer bounded to edges or interfaces. These “extended topological modes” break the common understating that the topological modes must be bound states. Their realization drastically broadens the application potential of the topological systems and opens new avenues for the study of topological insulators and higher-order topological insulators. The results are published in Nature 608, 50-55 (2022).

12302420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302420.value: The research outcomes deepen our understanding of higher-order topological modes. Higher-order topological systems are a class of topologically nontrivial systems that can protect robust topological modes at different dimensionalities. For example, a two-dimensional higher-order topological insulator sustains zero-dimensional, point-like topological defect modes that are often found at the corner of a specimen. We have investigated the physics and explored the potential applications of several new types of higher-order topological systems in the context of acoustics and mechanical systems. We have also found that they can benefit rich wave-based applications that are otherwise difficult to obtain. For example, topological hinge modes in a 3D higher-order topological system can sharply bend waves without reflection or distortion.

12302620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302620.value: Amyloid-β plaques are one of the pathological hallmarks found in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) brain, which are believed to be closely related to its pathogenesis. Thus, amyloid-β species are a cardinal feature/biomarker to monitor for diagnosis of the disease and evaluate for efficacy in the drug development. Current plaque imaging in humans based on positron emission tomography (PET) is expensive and requires a radioactive tracer affording relatively low spatial resolution. Thus, PET would not be able to provide for prognosis and early diagnosis as well as a population-wise and routine screening of the disease. In contrast, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), commonly available in clinical setting and being a powerful non-invasive and non-radiative diagnostic technique offers excellent spatio-temporal resolution and unlimited depth of tissue penetration. Therefore, it could provide a reliable and widely accepted alternative for cerebral amyloid-β species imaging. Because of its intrinsic low sensitivity, a contrast agent would often be required to enhance the specificity and image contrast of tissues/pathology of interest in MRI. On the other hand, near infrared (NIR) fluorescence imaging being highly sensitive with good penetration depth and low auto-fluorescence from biological tissues has been widely applied for imaging of cellular structure and amyloid plaques in AD mouse model despite its limitation for cerebral imaging in humans. Intriguingly, multimodality imaging can overcome the limitations of the single modal imaging, which provides complementary and expanded scope of information for more accurate disease diagnosis and pathological features investigation. Toward this end, we propose herein to develop oligomeric Aβ-specific Gd³⁺-based nanoparticle (NP) as a multimodal (MR/NIR) imaging contrast agent for in vivo detection and imaging of oligomeric Aβ species in AD mouse model for early screening and diagnosis of the disease as well as the assessment of the efficacy of potential AD drugs. Such oligomeric Aβ-specific Gd³⁺-based NP would provide a practical and indispenable tool to visualize and monitor the pathological features of AD, particularly Aβ oligomers by NIR/MR imaging for research and drug development in AD mouse model. Furthermore, findings of this research will open up an alternative vista to develop practical MRI contrast agent for diagnosis of AD in humans. β-澱粉樣蛋白(Aβ)斑塊是阿爾茨海默病（AD）腦組織病理學特徵之一，與AD的發病機理密切相關。因此，β-澱粉樣蛋白物種是主要特徵/生物標記，可監測疾病的診斷和評估藥物開發療效的功效。基於斑塊成像在正電子發射斷層掃描（PET）的成本昂貴，並且需要放射性示踪劑 只提供相對較低的空間分辨率。因此， PET將無法提供預後和早期診斷，也無法對該疾病進行人群和常規篩查。相反 通常在臨床環境中使用的磁共振成像（MRI）是一種強大的非侵入性和非放射性診斷技術，可提供出色的時空分辨率和無限的組織穿透深度。因此，它可以為β-澱粉樣物質成像提供可靠且廣泛接受的替代方法。由於其固有的低靈敏度，通常需要造影劑來增強MRI中感興趣的組織/病理學的特異性和圖像對比度。另一方面，或者它對人體大腦成像有局限性，但是近紅外（NIR）熒光成像具有靈敏度高，穿透深度好，並且來自生物組織的自熒光強度低等優點，已被廣泛用於AD小鼠模型的細胞結構和澱粉樣斑塊成像。有趣的是，多模態成像可以克服單模態成像的局限性，從而為更準確的疾病診斷和病理特徵研究提供補充和擴展的信息範圍。為此，我們建議開發針對寡聚聚態Aβ的Gd³⁺-納米顆粒（NP），其作為一種多模態（MR / NIR）成像造影劑，既可以用於AD小鼠模型中寡聚Aβ類的體內檢測和成像，還可以用於疾病的早期篩查和診斷以及潛在的AD藥物的療效評估。 這種針對寡聚聚Aβ的Gd³⁺-納米顆粒（NP）為AD小鼠模型的研究和藥物開發提供了一種實用的，不可替代的工具。通過NIR / MR成像來可視化和監視AD的病理特徵，特別是Aβ寡聚聚體，可用於AD小鼠模型的研究和藥物開發。此外，這項研究結果將為開發實用的MRI造影劑以診斷人類AD開闢了新的前景。

12302620.label: Realisation of objectives
12302620.value: We have developed the first Aβ oligomer-specific Gd3+-based core–shell structured nanoparticles (NPs), NP@SiO2@F-SLOH with a particle size of ~55 nm in diameter as a multimodal near-infrared imaging (NIRI)/T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agent for real-time visualization of Aβ contents in an AD mouse model. The longitudinal relaxivity (r1) was determined to be ~5.56 mM−1 s−1. This NP@SiO2@F-SLOH was successfully applied for in vivo and ex vivo NIRI with high sensitivity and selectivity for Aβ oligomers and for MRI with good spatial resolution in different age groups in an AD mouse model. Furthermore, the NP probe exhibits a noticeable inhibitory effect on Aβ fibrillation and neuroprotection against Aβ-induced toxicity indicating its desirable therapeutic potential for AD. All these results illustrate the tremendous potential of this versatile and sensitive nanomaterial as an effective theranostic MRI nanoprobe for practical use. (1) We have designed and developed the first amyloid-β (Aβ)-targeted, blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetrable theranostic Gd(DOTA)-cyanine dyad, which was synthesized by the conjugation of Gd(DOTA) complex and carbazole-based cyanine dye by the copper(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition click reaction for imaging of Aβ in vivo and ex vivo in AD mouse models. This dyad, as a multimodal probe, possesses desirable multifunctional properties, including good biocompatibility, low cytotoxicity, high Aβ selectivity, strong fluorescence enhancement upon binding with Aβ species, good paramagnetic properties, high stability, good BBB penetrability, and fast elimination from the mouse. The longitudinal relaxivity (r1) of the dyad was found to be 4.42 mM−1 s−1 at 3 T, suggesting it to be promising as a T1-weighted MRI contrast agent. The probe has been successfully demonstrated to be able to be applied for one- and two-photon excited fluorescence and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging of Aβ in transgenic mouse models of AD. In addition, it can inhibit Aβ aggregation, protect against toxicity induced by Aβ, and suppress Aβ-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. (2) We have developed the first Aβ-targeted ratiometric H2O2-responsive fluorescent probe for real-time detection and monitoring of the Aβ-induced H2O2 level in cell and AD mouse models. The H2O2-responsive probe is constructed based on a methylamino-substituted quinolinium-based cyanine as the fluorescence moiety and a phenylboronate ester as the sensing reaction site. This sensing probe exhibits a large emission wavelength shift of ~87 nm upon reacting with H2O2, a high binding selectivity for Aβ and a faster response toward H2O2 in the presence of Aβ, concomitant with an enhanced fluorescence intensity, hence greatly boosting the sensitivity of in situ H2O2 detection. This biocompatible and nontoxic probe is capable of ratiometrically detecting and imaging endogenous H2O2 induced by Aβ in a neuronal cell model. Remarkably, this Aβ-targeted H2O2-responsive probe is also able to detect, monitor, and differentiate different Aβ-induced H2O2 levels in real-time in different age groups of transgenic AD mice, in which the cerebral H2O2 level increases age-dependently concomitant with the plaque contents. Therefore, this smart probe can act as a powerful tool to diagnose high-risk subjects and diseased brains of AD and to further study the role of ROS in AD pathology. (3) We have synthesized a multifunctional theranostic cyanine, SLCOOH and F-SLCOOH, which serves not only as a highly sensitive fluorescence probe for real-time imaging of amyloid-β (Aβ) contents in different age groups of transgenic (Tg) AD mice but also as an effective therapeutic agent for early AD intervention via multiple pathological targets in AD mouse model. Remarkably, treatment with SLCOOH gives rise to multiple therapeutic benefits, including the amelioration of cognitive decline, a reduction in Aβ levels, a decrease in hyperphosphorylated tau proteins and tau depositions, and the alleviation of synaptic loss and dysfunctions in young triple Tg AD mice. Our results have demonstrated that in addition to superior Aβ imaging capability, SLCOOH exhibits versatile and effective multiple modes of drug action, signifying an outstanding therapeutic potential to treat early onset AD. In addition, F-SLCOOH shows highly selective binding toward the extracellular Aβ aggregates in real-time in live animal imaging of a 5XFAD mice model. The ex vivo confocal imaging of hippocampal brain slices indicated excellent colocalization of F-SLCOOH with Aβ positive NU1, 4G8, 6E10 A11 antibodies and THS staining dye, affirming its excellent Aβ specificity and targetability. Besides, F-SLCOOH exhibits remarkable anti-fibrillation properties against toxic Aβ aggregate formation of Aβ1–42, Iowa mutation Aβ, and Dutch mutation Aβ. F-SLCOOH treatment also exerts high neuroprotective functions and promotes autophagy lysosomal biogenesis in neuronal AD cell models. (4) We have developed highly sensitive and effective ratiometric Aβ-guided H2O2-responsive theranostic probes for sensing and tracking of endogenous H2O2 in AD mouse models. Among the probes synthesized, HY3 was shown to possess superior multifunctional properties including low cytotoxicity and good biocompatibility, strong binding with Aβ and large Aβ binding-induced fluorescence enhancement, excellent H2O2 specificity, superior stability, and of particular importance, rapid response, and high sensitivity toward H2O2 in the presence of Aβ for selective imaging and monitoring of endogenous H2O2 in real time in AD mouse model. Molecular docking revealed the difference in the binding motif and interactions of the probe HY3 and its H2O2-oxidized product, HY2 with Aβ fibrils giving rise to the difference of Aβ binding-induced fluorescence enhancement between them. Impressively, with the promotion of Aβ, HY3 was able to detect the endogenous H2O2 level ratiometrically in AD cell model and differentiate the difference between the normal and AD cells. More importantly, the excellent BBB permeable and biocompatible HY3 probe enabled it to target the senile plaques and serve as an effective and highly sensitive ratiometric fluorescent probe to image and monitor endogenous H2O2 level in vivo in different age groups of AD mice. (5) We have developed for the first time the design and development of a H2O2-responsive probe surface-coated Gd3+-based multimodal nanoprobe capable of Aβ targeting and NIR imaging, selective/ratiometric sensing of endogenous H2O2 induced by Aβ, and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging of Aβ aggregates for AD. This nanoprobe was highly selective to bind Aβ and ratiometrically image the endogenous H2O2 level in an AD cell model as well as to effectively target Aβ plaques and specifically detect and monitor the Aβ-induced H2O2 level in vivo in different ages of APP/PS1 transgenic mice over time. Furthermore, this Aβ-targeted nanoprobe could serve as a highly effective and sensitive MRI contrast agent to detect and differentiate the Aβ content in different ages of AD mice. These results demonstrate that this ROS-responsive multimodal design strategy opens up a new avenue to develop a smart class of multimodal nanoprobe for complementary investigations of cerebral Aβ by multiple imaging techniques. This nanoprobe is highly promising for improved early diagnosis and prognosis of AD.

12302620.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302620.value: We have developed the first Aβ oligomer-specific Gd3+-based core–shell structured nanoparticles (NPs), NP@SiO2@F-SLOH with a particle size of ~55 nm in diameter as a multimodal near-infrared imaging (NIRI)/T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agent for real-time visualization of Aβ contents in an AD mouse model. The longitudinal relaxivity (r1) was determined to be ~5.56 mM−1 s−1. This NP@SiO2@F-SLOH was successfully applied for in vivo and ex vivo NIRI with high sensitivity and selectivity for Aβ oligomers and for MRI with good spatial resolution in different age groups in an AD mouse model. Furthermore, the NP probe exhibits a noticeable inhibitory effect on Aβ fibrillation and neuroprotection against Aβ-induced toxicity indicating its desirable therapeutic potential for AD. All these results illustrate the tremendous potential of this versatile and sensitive nanomaterial as an effective theranostic MRI nanoprobe for practical use. To achieve a higher r1 relaxivity for superior image contrast, the size of the paramagnetic nanoparticles is crucial to be reduced/optimized. Therefore, we have synthesized smaller NaGdF4 nanoparticles with an average particle size of ~5.9 nm which was also protected by a silica shell, further coated with a mesoporous silica layer and followed by surface-adsorbed with Aβ oligomer-specific cyanine dyes with a total size of ~20 nm. The r1 relaxivity of mesoporous SiO2 covered NaGdF4 nanoparticles and Dye-NPs are found to be 10.89 and 9.40 mM−1 s−1, respectively as determined by a 3T magnetic resonance scanner. These r1 values are much higher than that of core-shell structured upconversion NPs, showing great promise for superior image contrast in MRI. Meanwhile, in addition to developing oligomeric SLTAD and SLFAD probes, we have synthesized theranostic SLCOOH and F-SLCOOH probes, H2O2-responsive probes as well as Gd(DOTA)-cyanine molecular dyad which can be served as a functional agent to surface-coat onto the nanoparticles for the development of multifunctional multimodal nanoprobes. Toward this goal, a novel Aβ-targeted H2O2-responsive NIR/MR multimodal NaGdF4 NP-based nanoprobe has been developed. This versatile nanoprobe was able to ratiometrically visualize the endogenous H2O2 level in an AD cell model and distinguish between the AD and non-AD cells. This Aβ-targeted responsive nanoprobe was also highly sensitive for in vivo imaging of H2O2 level in AD mouse model in which the Aβ-induced H2O2 level could be visualized ratiometrically and monitored in APP/PS1 AD mice with various ages in real time. Most impressively, this Aβ-targeted nanoprobe has been successfully applied as an effective and sensitive MRI contrast agent for ex vivo and in vivo T1-weighted MRI of Aβ content in different age groups of an AD mouse model. This newly developed multimodal responsive nanoprobe can provide complementary and expanded information of cerebral Aβ through different imaging modalities.

12302620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302620.value: In practice, there are two types of MRI contrast agents, namely T1-weighted and T2-weighted contrast agents. Each of them has its pros and cons in bio-imaging applications. One way to overcome each of its limitations in imaging is to acquire a dual-mode T1- and T2-weighted MRI. Therefore, multimodal imaging probe with dual-mode T1- and T2-weighted MRI capability would be an important advancement. Toward this goal. Gd(III)-based molecular dyad developed in this project can be used to surface-functionalize the superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (NP) to develop dual-mode MR/NIR multimodal imaging nanoprobe for visualization of A𝛽 aggregates for AD.

12302620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302620.value: Each imaging technique has its own unique features and limitations; therefore, no single technique can provide complete information and assessment of the hallmarks of AD. Multimodal imaging probes can provide multiple imaging capabilities from a single administration with the same pharmacokinetics and colocalization of the signal for each modality. They are emerging as a more powerful and holistic tool in which different imaging modalities can provide complementary and expanded information on the ROI. Multimodal probes with imaging capabilities of A𝛽 aggregates at different levels of organization from the microscopic level (TPE/NIR imaging) to the macroscopic level (MRI) would be valuable and indispensable for etiological studies, precise disease diagnosis, and the investigation of the treatment efficacy and the mode of action of new therapeutic agents. Our results demonstrate that the multifunctional multimodal imaging probes that we developed are highly promising for precise early diagnosis of AD with extraordinary potential for MRI of Aβ in humans.

12302720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302720.value: Causal effect is an important issue in diverse research fields. When some confounders are given, we then need to study the causal effect in a conditional manner and estimate the relevant unknown quantities such as conditional treatment effect. In this project, we will construct conditional M-quantile treatment effect (CMqTE), which is robust against outliers, to capture the heterogeneity through, say, quantile or expectile sheet, that is a function of quantile levels and given confounders, to examine one more type of heterogeneity in specific subpopulations decided by the confounders. We will then investigate the asymptotic properties of propensity score-based under nonparametric, semiparametric, parametric and true (oracle) regression structure. Through these studies, we can, when the model is correctly specified, then provide the comparisons among the methods in the asymptotic manner and insight into the pros and cons under different model structures. Due to their advantages of alleviating curse of dimensionality and model misspecification, we will pay a particular attention to the semiparametric estimations. Also we investigate properties of these methods when the underlying models are misspecified globally and locally and discuss the bias correction. Numerical studies will also be conducted to examine the finite sample performance of the methods. This research project will provide insight into the asymptotic efficiency of various estimations such that the results can guide the use of the methods in practice and expect the new theory developed in the course of the project will have a lasting impact in the relevant fields. 因果效應是眾多研究領域中的一個重要問題。當一些混雜因素給定的情况下，我們需要研究條件因果關係和相關未知量的估計。在這個項目中，我們將構造條件M-分位數處理效應（CMqTE）。這個量對异常值是穩健的，以便通過分位數或期望值錶來瞭解處理效應的異質性。這是一個分位數水准和給定的混雜因素函數，囙此可以用於檢測由混雜因素决定的特定子集上的異質性。在這個項目中，我們將研究在非參數、半參數、參數和真實的回歸結構下，基於傾向得分的估計量的漸近性質。通過這些研究，我們可以在假設的模型是正確的情况下，研究估計量在不同模型結構的漸近管道以及利弊。由於它們具有降維的優點，我們將特別關注半參數估計。我們還將研究當假定的模型在全域和局部的意義上是偏離真實模型時如何校正偏差。也要進行數值模擬檢測估計在有限樣本下的效能。 這項研究專案將深入瞭解各種估計方法以便指導這些方法在實踐中的應用。期望新的理論可以在相關領域產生持久影響。

12302720.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302720.value: We investigated the estimation of the average treatment effect (ATE) and conditional average treatment effect (CATE) using both propensity score-based and outcome regression-based methods. Our systematic analysis compared the asymptotic efficiencies of various estimators across nonparametric, semiparametric dimension reduction, and parametric structures. We found that no single method consistently outperforms others in all scenarios. Impact of Covariate Affiliation Given that the conditional mean of the treatment effect (CMqTE) is a function of specified covariates, and the arguments of the propensity score function don't necessarily include all covariates, we also examined how the affiliation of given covariates to the set of arguments affects the asymptotic efficiency of different estimators. This investigation revealed that while nonparametric estimators can be asymptotically efficient, their performance is severely impacted by dimensionality. Consequently, semiparametric estimators, which can automatically adapt to both nonparametric and parametric structures, are highly recommended. Causal Structural Learning for Adjustment Sets Beyond our initial objectives, we extended our research to include causal structural learning for all adjustment sets. This area, closely related to dimension reduction, focuses on identifying and removing unnecessary covariates from the model, further refining the estimation process.

12302720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302720.value: The current objectives appear to have systematic solutions. Based on these findings, we may have interest to account for potential issues when unobservable confounders are present. The key challenge lies in effectively applying analytical techniques to address them.

12302720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302720.value: We systematically analyze the asymptotic efficiencies of various propensity score-based and outcome regression-based estimators for both average treatment effect (ATE) and conditional average treatment effect (CATE). Our analysis considers nonparametric, semiparametric dimension reduction, and parametric structures. Generally, nonparametric estimators offer superior asymptotic efficiencies but at the significant cost of suffering from the curse of dimensionality. Therefore, semiparametric estimators are recommended. These estimators can automatically adapt to both nonparametric and parametric structures, leading to substantially improved estimation performance when the underlying models intrinsically possess low-dimensional structures. Our findings are further supported by numerical studies.

12303220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303220.value: With the advent of data science, healthcare is booming and becoming one of the biggest and fastest-growing fields in recent years. Precision medicine aims to tailor healthcare or treatment to the individual characteristics of each patient, which has been attracting more and more attention along with the advance in diagnosis and treatment as well as the increasing adoption of electronic health records by hospitals. The data collected nowadays is usually massive, complex and high dimensional, but also contains interesting and vital information. There is a pressing need to respond to these challenges and opportunities. The goal of this project is to investigate theoretical properties and application perspectives of outcome weighted schemes for some problems that arise in precision medicine from the perspective of learning theory. We shall first consider a general framework for learning an optimal individualized treatment rule that maximizes the expected clinical outcomes from randomized trial data within the framework of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, where the error analysis will be conducted and fast learning rates will be derived under general convex loss functions. Outcome weighted classification algorithms with nonconvex loss or differential privacy will also be studied. We shall then propose a unified learning framework involving two types of kernels to study the generalization abilities of outcome weighted learning schemes for personalized dose finding, where the minimax optimal learning rate will be derived and gradient descent with early stopping will be employed to solve the corresponding optimization problem. The idea of online learning in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces will be introduced to outcome weighted schemes to tackle data that arrives sequentially in a streaming way, where error analysis will be conducted and high-probability convergence rates will be derived. Finally, we will study some other topics in deep learning related to this project, such as deep neural networks for outcome weighted schemes. 隨著數據科學的出現，醫療保健行業蓬勃發展，並已成為近年來增长最快的領域之一。精準醫學旨在基於患者的個性特徵量身定制醫療方案，其隨著現代診斷和治療的進步以及醫院開始採用電子病歷而獲得了越來越多的關注。現實世界中數據一般都是龐大，複雜和高維的，但其同時也包含了大量有趣而重要的信息，因此我們迫切需要建立相關理論基礎以回應隨之而來的挑戰與機遇。該項目的目的是從學習理論的角度研究結果加權算法在一些精準醫學相關問題中的理論性質及其應用前景。我們首先考慮基於隨機試驗數據估計可最大化預期臨床結果的最佳個性化治療規則的學習算法。我們將在再生核希爾伯特空間的框架中對基於一般凸損失函數的結果加權分類算法進行誤差界和學習率的分析。我們也將研究與差分隱私相關的結果加權分類算法。然後，我們將提出一個涉及兩類核函數的結果加權學習框架並研究其在個性化劑量查找問題中的泛化能力，我們將導出最佳學習率以及考虑使用梯度下降结合早停法求解相應的優化問題。另外我們將在結果加權算法的基础上引入在線學習的想法處理以流方式順序到達的大數據，並進行误差分析推導出高概率收斂階。最後，我們將研究一些與本項目相關的深度學習課題，例如基於深度神經網絡的結果加權算法。

12303220.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303220.value: This project explores advanced learning algorithms in functional data analysis, robust deep learning, and precision medicine, highlighting novel approaches and theoretical advancements to improve performance and efficiency in various contexts. Six papers have been published. [1] investigates reproducing kernel-based online learning for functional data, emphasizing the effectiveness of functional linear models in large-scale infinite-dimensional data analysis. The study establishes convergence rates for expected excess prediction risk, demonstrating that these rates can be achieved without regularity in the slope function, highlighting a critical difference between estimation and prediction tasks in functional data learning. [2] presents a new prediction method for a semi-functional linear model that combines functional and nonparametric components. It establishes minimax optimal convergence rates, showing that the functional component can be learned at the same rate as if the nonparametric component were known, and vice versa. Utilizing a double-penalized least squares method in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, the approach benefits from the representer theorem, enabling efficient algorithms without iterations. Numerical studies validate its effectiveness and theoretical claims. [3] explores the generalization error of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in robust regression, pointing out the limitations of least squares loss in the presence of heavy-tailed noise. It introduces the maximum correntropy criterion as an alternative loss function, showing that CNNs with ReLU activation can achieve fast convergence rates. When the regression function has an additive ridge structure and finite p-th moment noise, the empirical risk minimization aligns with mini-max optimal rates akin to fully connected networks using the Huber loss. [4] combines information-theoretic learning with deep learning, focusing on generalization for deep CNNs in robust regression. By examining correntropy-induced loss functions, it establishes explicit convergence rates when the target function is in the Korobov space, enhancing the theoretical understanding of CNNs and their performance in big data contexts. [5] addresses the application of kernel methods in large-scale functional data analysis through the Nyström subsampling method within functional linear regression and reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This algorithm reduces computational complexity and achieves minimax optimal convergence rates for excess prediction risk, contingent on appropriate subsampling sizes. [6] introduces a framework that integrates outcome weighted learning with online gradient descent to enhance precision medicine. This framework tackles the challenges posed by high-dimensional electronic health records and establishes convergence rates for online outcome weighted learning algorithms, thus extending online classification to optimize clinical outcomes for diverse patient responses.

12303220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303220.value: To advance the study of large-scale infinite-dimensional data, it is worthwhile to leverage the capabilities of neural networks as a replacement for kernel methods. This exploration can yield valuable insights into the effectiveness of deep learning techniques for functional data analysis, particularly in healthcare contexts where data complexity is paramount. Furthermore, developing efficient optimization algorithms tailored for functional learning using neural networks will be of significant interest. By investigating these areas, we can deepen our understanding of how to apply modern learning techniques to manage large-scale, high-dimensional healthcare data effectively. In precision medicine, the two primary tasks (individualized treatment rules and personalized dosage finding) often face challenges related to privacy concerns and the curse of dimensionality. It would be beneficial to implement differentially private stochastic gradient descent to not only enhance the convergence speed of these algorithms but also safeguard patient privacy. Additionally, integrating cutting-edge techniques such as transformers and large language models can significantly broaden the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed methods, enabling more robust analyses and improved decision-making in personalized healthcare solutions. By addressing these critical areas, we can pave the way for innovative approaches that enhance patient care while maintaining data integrity and security.

12303220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303220.value: This research project tackles the growing complexity and volume of healthcare data, which makes effective analysis challenging. We explored advanced learning techniques to improve how we analyze this data, leading to six published papers. Our work began with online learning methods that can handle large, high-dimensional data streams, making it easier to process information in real-time. We developed a new predictive model that efficiently combines different data types, enhancing our ability to interpret functional and vector data. To streamline analysis, we implemented Nystroem subsampling, which improves computational efficiency for large datasets. We also addressed issues with noisy data by using convolutional neural networks and deep learning algorithms, ensuring our models remain accurate despite data challenges. Finally, we focused on personalizing treatment plans in medicine, helping healthcare providers make better decisions tailored to individual patient needs. Overall, this research is significant because it not only helps manage large-scale and complex health data more effectively but also aims to improve patient care through more informed and personalized medical decisions.

12303320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303320.value: 大氣污染是一個全球性的環境問題。PM2.5是大氣中粒徑小於2.5μm的細顆粒物，是大氣污染的關鍵指標，也是一類至關重要的大氣污染物。幾乎每個人都暴露於大氣PM2.5顆粒物中。流行病學和毒理學研究表明，PM2.5的環境暴露與心血管疾病的惡化和發展顯著相關，但PM2.5對心血管系統的作用機制十分複雜且尚未明確。PM2.5來源廣泛且成分複雜，研究發現來自燃燒源的PM2.5可顯著增加心血管疾病的死亡風險，因而本項目擬選用典型碳源的PM2.5顆粒物作為研究目標。基於質譜技術的代謝組學和脂質組學是研究生物樣品中內源性生物標誌物的強有力手段。本專案首先將建立PM2.5誘發心血管功能紊亂的動物模型和細胞模型，通過非靶向代謝組學和脂質組學方法，鑒定大鼠心臟組織和血漿以及人源心肌細胞中潛在的生物標誌物，利用靶向代謝組學手段對特定代謝途徑和通路中的生物標誌物進行定量，並採用質譜成像代謝組學揭示大鼠心臟組織中生物標誌物的空間分佈。PM2.5顆粒中的多環芳烴（PAHs）及其衍生物是與心血管疾病相關的重要污染物，本項目同時將檢測PM2.5顆粒及其生物樣品中此類物質的含量水準，並結合動物的生理指標及其生物標誌物的含量水準進行相關性分析。基於以上質譜技術和手段，我們將提出PM2.5顆粒引起心血管功能紊亂的毒性機理並進行生物學驗證。本研究有助於揭示PM2.5暴露誘發心血管疾病的潛在分子機制，同時為評估大氣污染的人體暴露健康風險提供重要的科學依據。

12303320.label: Realisation of objectives
12303320.value: In this project, to seek biomarkers and explore the mechanisms of PM2.5-induced cardiovascular diseases, we have carried out the following investigations during this reporting period. 1) Installation of the real-ambient PM2.5 exposure system To simulate real-ambient PM2.5 exposure was necessary to better evaluate the health risk of airborne PM2.5 and explore the underlying mechanism. As most popular exposure method, intratracheal instillation could not completely mimic the deposition of ambient PM2.5 in the lung. Therefore, the real-ambient PM2.5 exposure system was constructed firstly. Two identical whole-body inhalation systems were installed, which used high- and low-efficiency filters, respectively. After testing, Linear regression results illustrated that PM2.5 concentration in the exposure chambers was equivalent to 61.6% of outdoor PM2.5. The applications of real-ambient PM2.5 exposure systems showed that PM2.5 increased body weights and heart rate in aged mice and increased weights of liver, spleen and kidney in the rat model, suggesting that the real-ambient PM2.5 exposure system could simulate experimental conditions similar to the daily PM2.5 exposure scenario of human life. Therefore, the system was used in the mechanism exploration of PM2.5-induced cardiovascular disease. 2) Studies on PM2.5-induced lipidome alteration in high cholesterol mice model High cholesterol is an increased risk of developing cardiovascular diseases, like coronary heart disease, stroke and hypertension. To reveal the impact of PM2.5 on cardiovascular system with the intervention of high cholesterol, high cholesterol mice model was developed. The metabolomic analysis showed that amino acids in serum were significantly changed after 6-month exposure to PM2.5 with the addition of high cholesterol. In addition, lipidomic studies in serum suggested that PM2.5-induced obviously lipidome alteration in both control and high cholesterol groups. Considering that liver was the main organ to metabolize cholesterol, lipidomics was also conducted in liver tissues, and TG was found to be significantly reduced in high cholesterol groups surprisingly. Besides that, intestinal microbiota was also reported to be associated with cardio-metabolic diseases. 16s RNA sequencing demonstrated that levels of many bacteria related to cardiovascular diseases were changed after PM2.5 exposure in both control and high cholesterol groups and cholesterol groups showed higher changes than control groups. 3) Studies on PM2.5-induced atherosclerosis in APOE-/- mice model Apolipoprotein E (APOE) was recognized for its ability to suppress atherosclerosis and usually applied in atherosclerosis research. In this study, APOE-/- mice models were developed to reveal whether PM2.5 promoted atherosclerosis. We firstly examined the atherosclerotic palques area in the entire aortic area with oil red O to quantify the atherosclerotic palques promoted by PM2.5 and found that lesion area was increased in APOE-/- groups after 6-month PM2.5 exposure. Metabolomics was conducted to explore the mechanism and purine metabolism which was related to oxidative stress was identified, suggesting that oxidative stress might be an important contributor to exacerbate atherosclerosis. TG was also detected and decreased in the APOE-/-- PM2.5 groups. In vitro studies were then applied to verify results obtained from mice model. 4) Cardiotoxicity of PM2.5-bound benzotriazole and its derivatives Benzotriazole and its derivatives (BTRs), which was classified as high-volume production chemicals, have been widely detected in various environmental media. However, studies on the pollution characteristics and health impact of PM2.5 related BTRs are still limited. In this study, the regional scale distribution and the potential cardiotoxicities of PM2.5-bound BTRs were studied. The concentrations of PM2.5-bound BTRs from three cities in China during the winter of 2018 were analyzed. The results showed that the concentration of ΣBTRs in Taiyuan was more than three times that in Shanghai and Guangzhou. BTR and 5-methyl-1H-benzotriazole (5TTR) was found to be the major pollutants among three cities. The correlation analysis indicated that there was a positive correlation between temperature and concentration of BTR and a negative correlation between temperature and concentration of 5TTR. According to the human exposure assessment, the risk of BTRs exposure to toddlers should be paid more attention in Taiyuan. In addition, the toxicity screening demonstrated that 4-methyl-1H-benzotriazole (4TTR) was the most toxic to cardiomyocytes. The western blot assay showed a ROS-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis signaling pathway was activated after exposure.

Untargeted and targeted strategies will be carried out sequentially. The biomarkers will be identified through MS acquisition and multivariate analysis. Metabolic pathway and network analysis will be carried out using the relative databases.

To investigate the correlations among levels of PAHs, OH-PAHs and nitro-PAHs in PM2.5 and biological samples, animal physiological indicators, and levels of endogenous metabolites. Correlation analysis will be conducted for a better elucidation of cardiovascular disorders induced by PM2.5 exposure

To reveal the spatial distribution of the biomarkers in heart tissues from in vivo exposure experiments by using MALDI-MS imaging metabolomics. The obtained results will provide new insights on the localization of the potential biomarkers.

To explore the mechanism of PM2.5-induced cardiovascular disorders at the metabolic level from the in vivo and in vitro results. The investigations of this project are expected to reveal the metabolic mechanisms through the analysis of the biomarkers, metabolic pathways and networks related to cardiovascular dysfunction induced by PM2.5 exposure.

12303320.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303320.value: 1. Real-ambient PM2.5 exposure systems were established and validated, providing a reliable model for long-term cardiovascular studies. 2. Lipidomics and metabolomics analyses identified TG reduction and purine metabolism disruption as significant pathways linked to PM2.5 exposure. 3. APOE-/- mice studies confirmed the role of PM2.5 in exacerbating atherosclerosis, likely through oxidative stress mechanisms. 4. Benzotriazole derivatives were identified as novel cardiotoxic agents associated with PM2.5, with 4TTR demonstrating the highest toxicity via ROS-mediated pathways. 5. Significant alterations in gut microbiota linked to cardiovascular risk were observed in high cholesterol mice exposed to PM2.5. Outcomes were disseminated through 14 peer-reviewed publications in leading journals such as PNAS, Science Bulletin.

12303320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303320.value: This research has significant potential for further development in multiple directions: 1. Mechanistic Insights: The study's findings open opportunities to investigate the interaction of lipidomic and purine metabolic pathways in cardiovascular disorders using advanced in vitro models. 2. Biomarker Validation: Identified biomarkers will be validated across broader populations and integrated into predictive models for PM2.5-associated cardiovascular risks. 3. Exposure Mitigation Strategies: Data on regional differences in PM2.5 composition and toxicity will guide targeted policies for air quality improvement and public health interventions. 4. Technological Innovation: MALDI-MS imaging will be further developed for high-resolution spatial biomarker profiling in various tissues, improving localization insights.

12303320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303320.value: Air pollution, particularly PM2.5, is a critical global environmental challenge that severely impacts human health. This project aims to uncover the biological mechanisms through which PM2.5 contributes to cardiovascular diseases. Using advanced animal models and cutting-edge metabolomics and lipidomics technologies, we identified changes in critical metabolic pathways and biomarkers linked to cardiovascular dysfunction. A key breakthrough was the development of real-ambient PM2.5 exposure systems that closely mimic human exposure. Additionally, we identified benzotriazole derivatives in PM2.5 as highly toxic to the heart and explored their mechanisms of toxicity. These findings will guide public health policies and pave the way for new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, ultimately reducing the burden of air pollution on cardiovascular health.

12303920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303920.value: Organic photodetectors (OPDs) are a promising alternative optical detecting technology to conventional wafer-based inorganic counterparts, because the optical and electric properties of the organic semiconductor materials can be tailored accordingly. They offer additional advantages such as having a solution-processable fabrication process, which also leads to significant cost benefits, thereby creating next-generation solution-processable, flexible and low-cost photodetectors. In general, the spectral responses of the photodetectors are determined by the absorption of the active materials and optical profile in the devices. Single-mode OPDs optimized for photodetection at the specific spectral ranges have been reported. Realizing dual-mode OPDs with high detectivity in two bands are very attractive for different applications. However, the reports on spectral tunable OPDs are rather rare. It is a great challenge to achieve a high performance OPD with dual-mode photo-responses in two distinct bands. In this application, we propose to develop a novel dual-mode photomultiplication OPD with a unique tunable photodetection capability, particularly over the near-infrared (NIR) and visible light wavelength ranges, that can be operated by adjusting the polarity of the biases. A dual-mode OPD comprises a tri-layer visible light absorber/optical spacer/NIR absorber configuration. In the presence of NIR light, photocurrent can be produced in the NIR absorbing layer, due to the trap-assisted charge injection at the NIR absorber/cathode interface under a reverse bias. In the presence of the visible light, photocurrent can be produced in the visible light absorbing layer, enabled by the trap-assisted charge injection at the anode/visible light absorber interface under a forward bias. A bias-switchable spectral response dual-mode photomultiplication OPD offers an attractive option for a plethora of applications in environmental pollution, bio, medical, agricultural, automotive and security monitoring, detection and imaging in two distinct bands. 有機光電探測器是一種有望替代傳統的基於晶片型無機半導體探測器的光學探測技術，原因是有機半導體材料的光學和電學性質可以相應地調整。有機光電探測器還具有可溶液加工製備的額外優勢，為實現下一代可溶液加工的大面積光電探測器提供了技術支持。一般來說，光電探測器的光譜響應是由光敏材料的吸收和器件中的光學分佈決定的。用於特定波段光探測的單模式有機光電探測器已有報導。然而，具有不同波段光電探測功能的雙模式有機光電探測器的研究進展緩慢。實現電壓控制的波段可調的光電探測器仍然是一個研究挑戰。 本課題研究一種近紅外和可見光雙波段可調的雙模式光電倍增型有機光電探測器，其工作模式可通過調節電壓的極性來控制。雙模式光電倍增型有機光電探測器的器件結構主要包括可見光吸收層、光學間隔層、近紅外吸收層。在近紅外光照射下，光電流從近紅外吸收層產生，其工作原理是在負偏壓下，有機薄膜層和陰極電極的界面發生陷阱導致的近紅外光響應的載流子注入。而在可見光的照射下，光電流則從可見光吸收層產生，原理是在正偏壓下，可見光響應的載流子注入發生在陽極電極和有機薄膜層的界面。探測波段可調節的雙模式光電倍增型有機光電探測器為光探測領域提供更多可能性，未來可用於不同波長的成像、環境污染探測、醫療健康和安防監測等應用。

12303920.label: Realisation of objectives
12303920.value: We have carried out a systematic study on the development of solution-processable high-performance dual-mode organic photodetectors (OPDs). The research work has been focused on the realization of three objectives. (1) To profile the optical field and charge generation distributions in a tri-layer visible light absorber/optical spacer/near-infrared (NIR) absorber dual-mode photomultiplication OPD, examine the dual-mode photo responses and responsivity in the NIR mode and visible light mode, (2) to investigate the effects of noise current, including the shot noise, thermal noise, 1/f noise and generation-recombination noise, on the specific detectivity (D*) of the dual-mode OPD, and (3) to understand the unique spectral responses of the tri-layer photomultiplication OPD, the distinct dual-mode NIR and visible light detection phenomena of the OPD operated under the reverse and forward biases. This project has attracted one MPhil student and two PhD students to do research in photodetectors with partial financial support from this project. We have published 13 high impact journal publications, one book chapter in photodetector research, and filed one patent application on the development of filter-free organic photodetectors. PI was also invited to give 7 plenary/invited talks at the related international conferences during the project reporting period. This project was completed successfully. The achievements of the project are highlighted below: (1) To profile the optical field and charge generation distributions in a tri-layer visible light absorber/optical spacer/NIR absorber dual-mode photomultiplication OPD, examine the dual-mode photo responses and responsivity in the NIR mode and visible light mode. We have obtained many original and interesting results for bias-controllable dual-mode detection in two distinct bands. The correlation between the optical profile and responsivity spectrum of the novel OPDs having photoactive layer with different heterojunction structures was investigated. Our results show that the responsivity spectrum of the OPDs can be effectively modulated by managing the optical profile in the multilayered heterojunction photoactive layer. Bias-controllable dual-mode detection devices were adopted for full color imaging. The present full-color imaging techniques rely on the use of broadband inorganic photodetectors with dedicated color filters, which is one of the practical challenges for large-area, flexible, and high-solution imaging applications. The development of high-performance bias-controllable dual-mode detection, e.g., for color-selective detection, is one of the key solutions to overcome this challenge. In this research project, an electrically switchable color-selective OPD comprising a double bulk heterojunction structure was developed for full-color imaging. The color-selective sensing capability over the visible spectrum ranges was realized by controlling the bias across the OPD, achieving a high responsivity of ~200 mA/W, a large dynamic range of over 122 dB, and a high -3 dB cutoff frequency of ~100 kHz. Dual-band photodetection is realized by selective extraction of the photo-generated charge carriers, due to the absorption of different portions of the incoming light, in the dual-mode OPDs. The OPDs have a high responsivity, a large dynamic range, and a high -3 dB cutoff frequency over the visible light wavelength range. A full-color imaging function has been demonstrated using an electrically switchable red-, green-, and blue-color selective OPD. The results of the work are very encouraging and provide a practical solution for applications in high-resolution full-color imaging and artificial vision. The filter-free band-selective photodetection is realized by adjusting the difference in wavelengths between the transmission cut-off wavelength of the organic semiconducting light depletion layer and the absorbing edge of the BHJ layer. As an example, a filter-free visible-blind NIR OPD has a simultaneous excellent NIR band selectivity with a spectral rejection ratio, and a high responsivity. (2) To investigate the effects of noise current, including the shot noise, thermal noise, 1/f noise and generation-recombination noise, on the specific detectivity (D*) of the dual-mode OPD. Specific detectivity D* of the OPD is associated closely with the dark current due to the carrier traps in the device. The use of an Al2O3-based interlayer, prepared by the atomic layer deposition method, for mitigating the dark current in photomultiplication OPD (PM-OPD) has been analyzed. It shows that a low dark current of ~10^-3 mA/cm^2 can be realized for the PM-OPD with an Al2O3 interlayer, which is almost five orders of magnitude lower than that of the control PM-OPD without Al2O3 interlayer. Based on the noise current characteristic, D* of 1.13x10^15 Jones is obtained for the PM-OPD, with an Al2O3 (0.8 nm) interlayer, under illumination of 520 nm light with a low intensity of 2.5 nW/cm^2, approaching the best D* reported for a PM-OPD with a PVK:ZnO interlayer (3.4x10^15 Jones). It shows that reduction in dark current mainly originates from the built-in anode Schottky junction because of a reduced charge injection barrier and chemical reaction between the Al2O3 interlayer and the contact, which otherwise would take place at the contact/hole-transporting layer interface. Such a strategy of suppressing dark current is not averse to charge injection under illumination. As a result, the reduced dark current enables the weak-light detection to reach a light intensity level of 2.5 nW/cm^2, outperforming that of the conventional OPDs. (3) To understand the unique spectral responses of the tri-layer photomultiplication OPD, the distinct dual-mode NIR and visible light detection phenomena of the OPD operated under the reverse and forward biases. We have studied the performance of the band-selective OPD that is realized without using a filter. A dual-mode OPD, having a tri-layer visible light absorber/optical spacer/NIR light absorber configuration photoactive layer, has been analyzed. The dual-mode OPD exhibits an electrically switchable NIR response operated under a reverse bias and visible light response operated under a forward bias. In the presence of NIR light, the trap-assisted charge-injection behavior at the organic/cathode interface in the OPDs operated under a reverse bias. The photocurrent is produced in the visible light-absorbing layer, enabled by the trap-assisted charge injection at the anode/organic interface under a forward bias. The research of the dual-mode OPDs was further extended to study the spectral selective detection of filter-free OPDs with a bilayer device architecture, comprising a shorter-wavelength light depletion layer/longer-wavelength light-absorbing layer photoactive layer. The optical depletion layer in the filter-free OPDs has a dual-function serving as a shorter-wavelength light-absorbing layer and a hole-transporting layer. The photodetection spectrum window of the filter-free band-selective OPDs, defined by the difference in wavelengths between the transmission cutoff of the shorter-wavelength light depletion layer and the absorption edge of the longer-wavelength light-absorbing layer, can then be tuned over the different wavelength ranges by using an appropriate combination of the shorter-wavelength light depletion layer and the longer-wavelength light-absorbing layer.

12303920.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303920.value: A dual-mode OPD has been demonstrated, which is critical for a plethora of applications in imaging, indoor light fidelity (Li-Fi), and light communications. The present band-selective photodetection is realized by incorporating different optical filters with broadband photodetectors. However, the use of optical filters reduces the overall sensitivity of these photodetectors. We have developed a high-performance filter-free band-selective OPDs with a heterostructure photoactive layer, comprising an organic semiconducting shorter-wavelength light depletion layer and an organic bulk heterojunction (BHJ) layer with an extended absorption to longer wavelengths. The front junction responds to short-wavelength (e.g., visible) light, whereas the rear junction responds to near-infrared (e.g., NIR) light. The double BHJ OPD allows multispectral detection that is controlled by the polarity of a bias applied between the two contacts in the device. The OPD also exhibits a broadband photoresponse when it is operated using a 50% duty-cycled square-wave voltage supply. The resulting technology enables high-performance multispectral OPDs for applications in areas such as security monitoring, artificial intelligence, high-resolution image sensing, Internet of Things, and optical communications [Part C, publications 1-5, 7]. A high-performance filter-free OPD with a double BHJ heterostructure for visible-blind NIR detection has been demonstrated. The visible-blind NIR photodetection is realized by eliminating the photocurrent generated in the front visible light-absorbing BHJ optical depletion layer, due to the suppression of electron transport by incorporating a copper thiocyanate-based electron-blocking layer in the OPD. Only the excitons generated in the rear NIR-absorbing BHJ in the OPD contribute to the photocurrent, thereby achieving visible-blind NIR photodetection. The OPD has a high responsivity of 0.38 A/W at 1050 nm and a specific detectivity of over 10^13 Jones over the wavelength range from 800 to 1050 nm, making it an ideal candidate for applications in optical communication, food quality detection, wellness monitoring, and NIR image sensors [Part C, publications 1, 2, 8, 12]. Dual-mode OPD with well-defined spectral responses, e.g., selective spectral photodetection over the visible and NIR wavelength ranges, is a prerequisite for realizing visible blind NIR sensing. We anticipate that the results of the dual-mode OPDs developed in this project will offer an exciting opportunity for new device concepts and different applications [Part C, publications 9-14].

12303920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303920.value: The present photodetector market is still dominated by the broadband photodetectors that use silicon, germanium and III-V compound semiconductors. These photodetectors require optical filters to realize spectral selectivity in the photodetection and cannot be used in curved or flexible imaging sensors. The recent progress made in the development of solution-processable OPDs offers a great opportunity for the advancement of next-generation photodetectors. The responsivity and light detectivity of the OPDs are comparable to that of the conventional inorganic semiconductor-based photodetectors. The understanding of the dynamics of the charge carriers in the spectral selective dual-model OPDs offers a greater freedom for device fabrication and engineering, achieving spectral selective and narrowband photodetection. The bias-switchable spectral selective OPDs hold the promise of breaking out some limitations of conventional complementary-metal-oxide-semiconductor imaging techniques, such as high pixel resolution and broad-angle view. It is anticipated that the outcomes of the project will enable high-performance multispectral OPDs for applications in areas such as environmental monitoring, artificial intelligence, high-resolution image sensors, Internet of Things, and optical communications.

12303920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303920.value: Dual-band organic photodetectors (OPDs) detect incoming light selectively in two different bands. In this project, a systematic study has been carried out to understand the performance of the bias-controllable dual-band OPDs, achieving filter-free visible blind near-infrared (NIR) photodetection. The project team has successfully developed a practical solution for overcoming the issue of accurately measuring visible and NIR light separately through developing a dual-band OPD that has a bias-controllable visible/NIR dual mode. The dual-band OPDs comprise a multilayer configuration of visible light absorber/NIR light absorber, achieving a fast-switching speed of over 1000 times per second for high-speed optical communications in two distinct bands. A full-color imaging function has been demonstrated using electrically switchable red-, green-, and blue-color selective OPD sensors with excellent operational stability. The dual-mode OPDs are an attractive alternative optical detecting technology to the conventional single-mode photodetectors. The solution-processable fabrication processes also lead to significant cost benefits, thereby creating next-generation large-area and flexible OPDs. The outcomes of this research project offer an attractive option for new photodetector concept and the applications in high-resolution full-color imaging, artificial vision, image sensors, and multi-channel optical communications.

12304020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12304020.value: Homogeneous cell populations are able to exhibit a rich variety of organized behavior, among which periodic oscillations. In many well-studied examples of collective motion in biology, cells communicate with each other through a chemical signal. Very recently, the Co-I’s group demonstrated noisy but robust synchronized motion of swarming bacteria confined in a thin layer of fluid [Nature 542, 210-214 (2017)]. The interplay between geometry, symmetry and hydrodynamics in the experimental setup is intriguing and poses new fundamental questions in active matter research. We have recently developed a general linear response theory to study spontaneous oscillations in a communicating cell population. The theory takes input from single-cell measurements to predict collective motion. Of particular interest is the phase relationship between cellular activity and the perturbing signal. Cells that respond adaptively to a changing environment are phase-leading at low frequencies. This property can be leveraged to yield quantitative predictions on the emergence of collective behavior above a threshold cell density. In the proposed work, we will follow the scheme outlined above to develop a detailed kinetic model of swarming bacteria in a thin liquid film. Experimentally, it has been shown that the fluid flow as well as the averaged bacterial motion is uniform over distances much greater than the size of individual cells. Therefore a mean-field Smoluchowski type description for the vertical profile of bacterial density and orientational distribution is appropriate. Our preliminary work on a minimal model identified a novel oscillatory instability as the cell density increases. The eigenmodes are the left and right polarized swarming motion in the plane, whose linear superposition gives rise to the elliptical orbits observed in experiments. Improved models need to be introduced to treat confinement and surface effects more accurately. Statistical analysis of single-cell trajectories collected in Co-I’s lab will be performed to provide information about bacterial motion near the surface. Guided by general results from the linear response theory and symmetry, the research should yield fresh knowledge and insight towards the circularly polarized average motion in an active and highly noisy population that has remained elusive till now. More broadly, progress made in this project could inspire new approaches to self-organization of microswimmers in other biological contexts. 均勻細胞群体能夠展現多種自組織行為，如週期性振盪等。通過分泌和感應化學信號實現相互通信，是細胞集體運動的常見模式，在生物學有多年的深入研究。最近，本項目合作團隊展示了含有懸浮大腸桿菌的薄薄液體的環狀流動，而單個細菌的游動卻沒有明顯規則[Nature 542，210-214（2017）]。實驗中，培養盤的幾何形狀，對稱性及液體流動之間的相互影響可以影響到結果，為活性物質研究提出了新的基本問題。 我們最近發展了一種通用的線性響應理論來研究通信細胞群體中的自發振盪。該理論通過單細胞測量獲取響應函數，以預測集體運動的發生。一個重要的個體特征是細胞活性與乾擾信號之間的相位關係。適應不斷變化的環境的細胞在低頻時處於相位領先狀態。利用此屬性，理論可以定量預測集體行為出現的閾值細胞密度及系統的其他性質。 在此項目中，我們將在以上理論工作的基礎上，開發在薄液膜中游動的細菌的細緻動力學模型。實驗表明，在遠大於單個細胞大小的距離上，流體流動和平均細菌運動是均勻的。因此，對細菌密度和方向分佈的垂直剖面進行平均場Smoluchowski型描述是合理的。我們的簡化模型的初步研究發現，隨著細胞密度的增加，會出現新型的振盪不穩定。本徵模是平面中的左右極化群運動，其線性疊加會產生實驗中觀察到的橢圓軌道。在後續的工作中，需要引入改進的模型來更精確地處理薄膜約束和液體表面效應。 合作者實驗室收集的單細胞軌蹟數據將提供有關表面附近細菌運動的信息。以線性響應理論和對稱性的一般結果為指導，這項研究将為仍難以捉摸的高噪聲环境下的圓周極化平均運動提供新的认識。從更廣泛的意義上說，該項目的進展可以为激發生物微游泳者的群体自我組織提供新思路和知识。

12304020.label: Realisation of objectives
12304020.value: During the course of this project, we developed a kinetic model of active micro-swimmers in a thin liquid film (objective 1). The model demonstrates that when cell density is sufficiently high and the spatial and orientation diffusivity of rod-like swimmers is low, the active film exhibits uniform circular motion but an interesting shear flow profile in the vertical direction, extending previous findings in Co-I’s lab (objective 2). The precise phase boundary between uniform and chiral symmetry-breaking solutions depends on the assumptions about bacterial swimming at the upper and lower boundaries of the liquid film, whose determination requires detailed input from experiments and simulations (objective 3). 1. A kinetic model for active swimmers in a liquid film -- The model we considered is essentially the one of polar swimmers proposed by Saintillan and Shelly [Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 178103 (2008)], but adapted to a quasi-2D liquid film with suitable boundary conditions. The film geometry with a finite thickness, we believe, is essential for the observed behavior in the experiments performed in Co-I‘s lab [Nature 542, 210-214 (2017)]. The model we used is a mean-field type equation where the effect of bacterial swimming on the fluid flow u(r,t) (the mean-field) is considered in a locally averaged sense (i.e., through the probability distribution function P(r, p, t) of polarity/orientation p). Furthermore, swimmers affect each other’s motion only through the flow field u(r,t) instead of direct collisions. As a convention, P(r, p, t) is normalized to the mean cell density c. We have collected rheological parameters that correspond to the experimental system where uniform elliptical oscillations with periods 4-12 seconds were observed, with circulation size/amplitude of 20-50 μm. From them we may form two dimensionless parameters that span the “phase diagram” of the model where the weakly synchronized motion is identified. 2. Condition for the onset of uniform circular motion -- The kinetic model has a trivial solution P(r, p, t) = c/4π and u = 0. To look for the stability condition of this solution, we considered an expansion of P in spherical harmonics of the polarization vector p, with coefficients that depend on the coordinate z perpendicular to the film. Correspondingly, the fluid velocity field u acquires a laminar shear flow profile along the z direction that rotates at a constant angular velocity. We performed linear stability analysis of the problem and obtained the critical cell density ϕ_c for the onset of the instability against 2⁄(π Pe_R ). Using the estimated dimensionless parameter values given above, the onset oscillation period at a film width of 10 μm is about 5 sec, in quantitative agreement with experimental observations. 3. Study the confinement effects of the film surface -- The results above were obtained by assuming no-slip (bottom) and free (top) boundary for the laminar fluid flow, while the transport equation (Smoluchowski) for the bacterial orientational distribution is unaffected by the boundaries. This is certainly an approximation that needs to be examined both theoretically and in comparison with experimental trajectory studies (e.g., S. E. Spagnolie and P. T. Underhill, Swimming in Complex Fluids, Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 2023. 14:381–415). Regrettably, the planned work was not completed within the project duration due to lack of student to work on the experimental setup in Co-I’s lab, and inability of a postdoctoral fellow to perform the simulations. In June 2022, the PI had preliminary discussions with Prof. Xiangjun Gong at the South China Univ of Tech for cell tracking experiments which was slowed down by COVID. Lack of progress on the experimental side delayed publication of a comprehensive study per original proposal.

12304020.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304020.value: The modelling work and results mentioned in Sec. 5.3 have been reported in several regional, national and international conferences as invited talks, including the prestigious 2022 Nobel Symposium "Predictability in Science in the Age of AI" first held outside Scandinavia, co-organized by the STIAS and the Nobel Foundation in Cape Town, South Africa. Our adaptation of a mean-field model that takes into account the experimental geometry and realistic parameter values gave a physical and semi-quantitative explanation of collective oscillations observed in Co-I's lab. The theoretical work is described in the manuscript with Bing Miao which is in the final stage of revision. Meanwhile, the PI worked on two other problems in a similar spirit as the mean-field approach adopted for the active liquid film project. Each led to a publication or a nearly accepted paper. In the first work, the PI led a team of young colleagues and students, mostly from HKBU, to investigate epidemic spreading particularly by presymptomatic and asymptomatic carriers, and the effectiveness of facemasks in slowing down virial transmission. Starting with a compartmentalized description, we introduced several data-analysis procedures to facilitate direct calibration of model parameters against COVID-19 incubation period and pairwise transmission statistics [Nature Communications 12, 1147 (2021)]. The scheme is easily adaptable to social contact pattern in specific communities or viral mutations. We then applied various analytical techniques, including perturbative expansions, to obtain interpretable mathematical expressions and results. The work attracted broad attention of academics, public health organizations and interested individuals and from a number of countries. It also contributed to an influential review published in PNAS 118, e2014564118 (2021), whose preprint version attracted 430,000 views at the time of the mid-term report. In the second work, my PhD student Ding Wang and I carried out a theoretical study of the hidden Mattis order in the annealed SK model, related to dynamic heterogeneity in glass materials. We obtained an exact maximum likelihood estimation of the associated random matrix spectrum for systems of finite size. The work was published in SciPost Physics 17, 106 (2024).

12304020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304020.value: The boundary effects for bacterial motion, especially bias towards in-plane alignment, can be treated analytically for different choice of the asymmetry parameters, to be tested later by direct or indirect experiments. In the longer term, we would like to look into the possibility of waves and defects on top of a circulating population, and see if interesting phenomena that could arise from such situations. This will require extending the current calculation to beyond the initial instability by including nonlinear terms. As the field of active matter physics is becoming very crowded, we would like to turn more into morphogenesis and pattern formation in tissues, guided by work from the experimental side.

12304020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304020.value: In this project, we created a model to study tiny swimming organisms in a thin layer of liquid. Our main goals were to understand how individual random run-and-tumble motion, in all directions, could produce organised flow. To achieve this, we developed a model based on earlier research that looks at how these swimmers (like bacteria) move in a thin film of liquid. Our findings show that when there are many swimmers and they don’t change direction often, the liquid moves in circles. The model also helps us identify the conditions under which the swimmers drive the helical shear flow. Our calculations even predicted frequencies of oscillations that match well with experiments conducted in Yilin Wu's lab at CUHK that were published in Nature magazine. The theoretical understanding achieved through model construction and analysis should inspire further experiments that aim at manipulating the collective motion by modifying system geometry, fluid properties, or behaviour of individual bacterium. It also suggests new questions such as whether swimmers that mostly lying parallel to the film would enhance or weaken the synchronised rotational motion. Answers to these questions will contribute to future applications in the field of synthetic biology.

12304120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12304120.value: In the recent two decades, as technology for data collection and data storage advances , functional data are increasingly common in various subject areas including chemometrics, climatology, biology, medical study, finance etc. Motivated by analysis of a Lingzhi (a traditional Chinese medicine) data set, this project considers the function-on-scalar regression in which the response is a random function and the covariates is a random vector. There exist numerous models for function-on-scalar regression. We focus on functional linear regression and explore in the directions of structure identification and the subsequent estimation, inference and interpretation. That is, we assume that the vector of coefficient functions in the functional linear regression model possesses some unknown lower-dimensional structure formulated in an innovative way. The goals are to develop a data-driven algorithm to identify the unknown lower-dimensional structure and then to obtain a intrinsically parsimonious model built on it so that we can sharpen the inference and interpretation. Specifically, suppose that the vector of coefficient functions are linear combinations of some unknown smooth functions, called essence codings. We first impose some constraints on the essence codings to deal with the identification problem, and then we develop a projection-based method to estimate them. Difference-based methods will be employed to achieve smoothness of the estimated essence codings. The smoothing parameter in the difference-based curve estimation is determined by cross-validation. Theoretically there are many essence codings, yet arguably only a few of the essence codings are important. We develop a criterion to determine the number of essence codings to be included in the model. Next, we can estimate the coefficients of the essence codings, called essence effects, and interpret them. Finally we can make inference based on the estimated essence effects. Simulation studies will be conducted to examine finite sample performance of the proposed method and to compare with existing function-on-scalar regression models. 12304120.value: As mentioned in the mid-term report, the main difficulty encountered was that the covid-19 pandemic made it hard for the PI to recruit research postgraduate students to and research assistants to come to Hong Kong and involve them in realizing all the objectives. Then, during the project period, the PI and collaborators focused on investigation of related topics on identification and inference for complex structures in multivariate functional data and non-stationary time series. Specifically, we develop a new approach to testing group effects in multivariate functional data, a new algorithm to estimate both the periodic component, smooth trend and additive covariate effects in time series, and a new test for specification of distribution in stochastic frontier analysis. In these studies, the proposed methods have been implemented, applied to some real world data sets and evaluated using extensive simulation studies, and their theoretical properties have been established. These investigations has resulted in three journal publications and be regarded as 60% fulfillment of Objectives 5 and 6 as stated in the original proposal.

12304120.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304120.value: We consider testing equality of vectors of mean functions for multivariate functional data. To this aim, we study asymptotic null distribution of the functional Lawley–Hotelling trace (FLH) test statistic and approximate it by a Welch–Satterthwaite type χ2-approximation. The resulting FLH test has the correct asymptotic level, is root-n consistent in detecting local alternatives, and is computationally efficient. In terms of numerical performance, while it is much faster to compute, the proposed FLH test is comparable with four existing tests based on permutation in terms of size control and power. We study time series that contain a nonparametric periodic component with an unknown period, a nonparametric trending behavior and also additive covariate effects. A two-step estimation procedure is proposed to estimate accurately the three components. First,we estimate the period by a penalized M-estimation method with the trend and covariate effects being approximated by B-splines Next, given the period estimate, we estimate the amplitude, trend and covariate effects. Consistency of the period estimator and asymptotic normality of the estimated periodic sequence, trend and covariate effects are established.Simulation studies confirm superiority of our method, and applications to global warming and monthly total import and export by China demonstrate it utilities. We develop new tests for specification of distribution of the inefficiency in stochastic frontier analysis. We focus on simultaneous relaxation of two common assumptions: (1) parametric frontier which may lead to false conclusions when misspecified, and (2) homoscedasticity which can be easily violated when working with real data. We propose novel bootstrap and asymptotic distribution-free tests with neither parametric frontier nor homoscedasticity assumptions, in both cross-sectional and panel settings. Our tests are asymptotically consistent, simple to implement and widely applicable, and they can detect root-n order local alternatives. We demonstrate their efficacies through extensive simulation studies. When applied to a banking panel dataset, our tests provide sound justification for the commonly used exponential specification for banking data, and the results indicate that a new parametric frontier model is more plausible than the conventional translog frontier.

12304120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304120.value: The Lawley–Hotelling trace test statistics assumes equal matrices of covariance functions of the multivariate functional samples. It can be extended to testing the equality of vectors of group mean functions with unequal matrices of covariance functions. The periodic component and/or the trend in time series may exhibit abrupt changes at change-points, in which case change-point detection for either or both of them requires further study. Testing determinants of the inefficiency is an important problem in stochastic frontier analysis. Current state-of-art approaches are built on some separability assumptions. Extension of the proposed inference method to address this question warrants future study. These topics would be very good PhD research projects.

12304120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304120.value: Multivariate functional data arise in many fields of contemporary study and applications. In this project, we show that our proposed inference method is able to cope with the computational issue existing permutation-based approaches suffer from while enjoying sound theoretical properties and numerical performance. Time series analysis is high relevant in prediction and forecasting in various areas of applications. The convention to deal with periodicity, trend and covariate effects separately or ignore the others when studying one of them may be inefficient and even inadequate. In this project, we consider a model that takes into account the three components simultaneously. We demonstrate that the proposed method can estimate all of them accurately in simulation studies, and our theoretical study show that it possesses desirable theoretical properties. Stochastic frontier analysis is the workhorse in evaluation of the efficiency of a firm or a policy. We develop novel specification tests for the inefficiency distribution that simultaneously relaxes the parametric frontier and homoscedasticity assumptions commonly imposed previously. We establish theoretical justifications of the proposed tests and demonstrate their superior numerical performance. Application to a banking dataset provides a good ground for the commonly used exponential specification, and it reveals a new parametric frontier model that worth further investigation.
