12605820.label: Realisation of objectives
12605820.value: Firstly please note, funding of this project from GRF was heavily cut from the original budget, especially for the part regarding web site/video production and community workshops. Funding here mainly for research itself only. Hence, the project objectives have been fully achieved with additional items accomplished due to extra funding especially for point 5-6, advocating and promoting the importance, effectiveness, of mindfulness practices to art educators and students. I am leaving HKBU at the end of Oct 2022 (the project is expected to be finished in June 2023 and the report due on Feb 2024). As we had a limited time-frame on such a big project, we worked non-stop (1-2 day rest in a month for 10 months) and was able to finish it. I shall explain in detail the items done below. I am grateful to the research assistants and the whole crew for video productions, bi-lingual website and exhibitions, artists collaborators, plus, the instructors for workshops and interns. Because I have to do the report now (before I leave HKBU), there is one item undone. The journal writing is still on-going. I did a conference presentation just last week 17th Oct 2022 but I need more time for the writing. I shall submit the paper soon. Point 1 - identify Hong Kong contemporary artists who practise mindfulness and meditation. We have promoted both in the traditional ways on emails, and also spread the radar on social media like facebook (it is rather outdated already) and IG (most people use). I also did scatter the radar from friends in Buddhist organisations. In the end, we got 27 questionnaires back from the first round of research, which is out of my expectation that the number is low. After analysing the data, I understood that NOT many artists actually learn and practice mindfulness. Even some of them think they are, but it is not. Those practices are more like the new age stuff but not proper mindful practices in psychology, neuroscience or religion. There is a surprise for me that, out of the 27, only 13 practise mindfulness. The popular commercial zen tea, zen walk, and gong bath are here and there. However, they are not proper practices but more like commercial activities of mental massage for busy Hong Kongers. Point 2 and 3 - discover reasons why they choose to practice study and what types of mindful practices artists do - study and who types of mindful practices artists do In the questionaries for first-round research, there are questions about types of practices and reasons they do mindfulness practices, plus a remark on unique experiences they want to share. 2/3 of the subjects wrote on this. From that information, I chose 11 for in-depth interviews and 8 of them for ethnographic documentary videos. Point 4 -examine the ways mindful practices are effective in: contemplation of concepts for artworks, art-making process, aesthetics decision on ways of representation and performance of the artworks, shaping interaction with the viewers/audiences; Eleven in-depth interviews were conducted (4 men and 7 women, aged from 20’s to 50’s). We did ethnographic observation of eight artists on their everyday-life, practices, art-making or performances. The artists are from various fields, including drawings, illustrations, music, dance, Cantonese opera, contemporary arts, inter-disciplinary arts, new media arts, and sound art. All of them find the practices very useful in dealing with stress and hectic schedule in Hong Kong life. A few of them have life crises: loss of hearing of a musician, fear of going on stage for performance, divorce, as caregivers to ill and cancer parents, suffering from depression and panic disorder, total loss of meaning of life and attempts to suicide, menopause and physical illness of middle age woman, problems facing cultural identities. The artists all find mindfulness practices greatly help them, not just to “deal with the problems” but rendering mental transformation on ways of thinking similar to cognitive therapy and deep psychological self-reflection. Most importantly, they can resume interests and enjoyment in life, thus realise meaning in life. Some artists will take art-making, especially performance, as the mindful practice itself. All of them will not claim they are doing mindfulness practice for their art, but the practice is there, like embedding in everyday life. Part 5 and 6 (these were done by extra funding) - advocate the need to include mindfulness practices to art education; - produce ethnographic video to demonstrate artists' mindful practices in Hong Kong and share on a web site for free public access as well as future researchers With extra funding, it has become a super big project with web-based documentaries, mindfulness exercise guidance, workshops, and exhibitions. details in IG: https://www.instagram.com/mindfulness.hkartists/?hl=bg The website for public access https://mindfulnessart.hk/ From launching on 28th July to 28 Sept 2022, in two-month time, there are 2500 hit rates. The website will run for five years. The website has the following content to advocate the need to include mindfulness practices in art education and the general public: - Eight short documentaries of the artists regarding types of practices, reasons for practices and relations with their art-making or work - Eleven mindfulness exercises guided by a certified MBCT instructor (Mindfulness- based cognitive therapy), which the public can follow to do daily - We organised 8 workshops (ALL FULL) dedicated to teachers organised in Kai Tak Campus of HKBU, and for students, organised in a BookPunch in Sum Shui Po Tai Nan Street. There are three edited video documentation of the workshops hosted on website for people to have a taste of the workshop experience. We particularly want to advocate mindful practices to art educators stressing on self-care and well-beings hence to enhance quality of education and inter-disciplinary collaboration of artists/art-making with psychology/therapies. - Six young women artists, 4 of them are AVA alumni, were funded to do 32 stationaries with drawings and illustrations related to the teaching and explanation of mindfulness from Zen Master Thích Nhất Hạnh/ These are also hosted on the website for free download for writing letters to connect with their friends and loved ones. We hope to stress on sharing and self-expression via letter writings connecting one and other. 2. We edited a longer version documentary (for cinema) on one of the research subjects -- Sam Chuk Lui Chan, titled The Black Wall, is nominated for Best Documentary Short in Taiwan Golden Horse Film Festival and will be world premiered there as well. I expect this short documentary will be touring in Europe and East Asia in 2023-24. It will help to advocate the importance and benefits of mindfulness practices to audience around the world. 3. Lastly, I did a presentation in Kyoto Arts Media Culture Conference 2022 just last week (Oct). Video recording is available on the conference website and my own IG for public access to further advocate the notion and practices of mindfulness, together with the website to various fields of people. https://kyoto- amc.iafor.org/kamc2022/

12606320.label: Realisation of objectives
12606320.value: (As I am going to retire from my position as a professor at HKBU on September 1, 2024, I would like to submit the completed research report in advance of the December 2024 deadline.) All four proposed objectives were successfully completed. In the study, a total of 96 participants were recruited, surpassing the proposed number of 80. Initially, 14 participants confirmed their participation but later withdrew. Out of the 96 participants, an equal number of 48 were randomly assigned to the treatment group and the control group. Both the treatment and control groups underwent 12 ECOP sessions. Due to participant dropouts in both groups during the intervention period, a total of 73 responses were collected for the pre-, post-, and six-month follow-up tests, resulting in a dropout rate of 23.95% (25 participants). To address missing data, an expectation maximization algorithm was used. The subsequent analysis included samples from 48 participants in the treatment group and 25 participants in the control group. The ECOP group intervention program consisted of 12 planned sessions, each lasting 1.5 hours. The sessions were led by an experienced social worker with expertise in counselling people with mental illness, especially those with schizophrenia. Additionally, to enhance the social impact and sustainability of the intervention, a peer support worker who had successfully recovered from a mental illness and had over a year of experience as a peer worker in Hong Kong was recruited to lead three sessions on disclosing mental illness in each ECOP intervention group. The research team provided regular training and supervision to the social worker and peer support workers to ensure that they adhered to the principles and concepts of the ECOP intervention program. The main measure of this study was the Chinese version of the Internalized Stigma of Mental Illness (IISMI) (Ritsher et al., 2003). The secondary measures included the Chinese version of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) (Beck, Steer & Brown, 1996) and the Chinese version of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) (Leung & Wong, 2008). Additionally, the study included the Personal Empowerment Self-Assessment Scale (PESAS), which was not originally proposed in the research. The PESAS is a self-reported measure developed as part of the Coming Out Proud program (Corrigan et al., 2013) and was used to evaluate individuals’ perception of their own empowerment in two domains: self-empowerment (HOP-SE) and community empowerment (HOP-CE). Data analysis is conducted using SPSS 26.0 (IBM Corporation, Armonk, NY, USA). Statistical significance is indicated by two-tailed p values < .05 for all analyses. The data analysis follows the intention-to-treat principle and uses the expectation maximization algorithm for handling missing data. A comparison of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics between the treatment and control groups is performed using chi-squared ('2) tests for categorical variables and an independent t-test for continuous variables. In analyzing the repeated outcome measures, a General Linear Model (GLM) for 2×3 repeated measures Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) was employed. This methodology entailed identifying two distinct groups (namely, the treatment and control groups) as factors between subjects, and three separate outcome evaluations (namely, baseline, post-treatment, and 6-month follow-up after treatment completion) as within-subject factors. The determination of the effect size for the ANCOVA hinged upon the utilization of the partial eta squared statistic. According to the typology proposed by Cohen (1988), partial eta squared values of 0.01, 0.06, and 0.14 are indicative of small, moderate, and large effect sizes, respectively. In the examination of hypotheses (1) and (2), the data were subjected to several statistical analyses: independent sample t-tests, paired-sample t-tests, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) within a general linear model framework. The experimental design incorporated the distinction between the treatment and control groups as between-subjects factors, and the sequential outcome measures (baseline, post-treatment, and follow-up at 6 months post-treatment completion) as within-subjects factors. Concerning hypothesis (3), the analysis was confined to participants within the treatment cohort who successfully completed the ECOP group program. The exploration for demographic and clinical variables correlated with enhancements in outcome assessment scores (i.e., change in BDI, RSES, HOP-SE, and HOP-CE) was conducted through a one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for categorical variables, and Spearman’s correlation analysis for continuous variables.

12606320.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606320.value: The analysis conducted via repeated measures ANCOVA revealed significant Group x Time interaction effects on the metric of internalized self-stigma (F(1, 66) = 4.20, p = .044, eta squared = .060), denoting a medium to large effect size. This finding underscores that the intervention’s efficacy in mitigating participants' self-stigma endured for a duration of six months post-intervention. Notably, within the treatment group, a discernible decrease in levels of internalized stigma was observed from pre-test (Mean = 2.29, Standard Deviation = 0.45) to post-test measurements (Mean = 2.02, Standard Deviation = 0.44), reaching statistical significance (t = 5.13, df = 47, p < .001) alongside manifesting a pronouncedly large effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.61). These results compellingly suggest that the intervention effect attributed to the ECOP group significantly diverged between the treatment and control groups in terms of reducing self-stigma among Chinese individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia, with these effects demonstrably preserved beyond the six-month post-intervention period. No significant Group x Time interaction effects were observed on depressive emotion (F(1, 66) = 0.91, p = .345, eta squared = .014). However, there was a significant reduction in depressive symptoms from the pre-test (mean = 28.9, standard deviation = 17.72) to the post-test (mean = 13.67, standard deviation = 16.71) within the treatment group (t=7.73, degrees of freedom=47, p< .001), accompanied by a large effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.87). These findings indicate a significant disparity between the treatment and control groups concerning the immediate efficacy of the ECOP group intervention in diminishing depressive symptoms. The analysis did not reveal any significant Group x Time interaction effects on the increase of self-esteem (F(1, 66) = 2.99, p = .088, eta squared = .043), Hop-SE (F(1, 66) = 3.12, p = .082, partial eta squared = .045), or Hop-CE (F(1, 66) = 1.23, p = .27, partial eta squared = .018). However, paired sample t-tests revealed a statistically significant enhancement in Hop-SE from pre-test (Mean = 17.06, SD = 3.72) to post-test (Mean = 18.90, SD = 3.31) within the treatment group (t = -4.08, degrees of freedom = 47, p < .001), indicating a substantial effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.52). Similarly, a significant increase in Hop-CE was observed from the pre-test (Mean = 17.23, SD = 2.78) to the post-test (Mean = 18.31, SD = 2.63) within the treatment cohort (t = -2.81, degrees of freedom = 47, p = .01), also exhibiting a substantial effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.39). The findings of the study indicate that the ECOP group constitutes an efficacious intervention strategy for mitigating internalized self-stigma among individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia in Hong Kong. This intervention amalgamates the empowerment model inherent in the COP approach with a tailored version of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Consequently, the ECOP group intervention shows promise in aiding participants to confront and modify self-stigmatizing beliefs specific to schizophrenia, as cited by Corrigan & Rao (2012) and Ng et al. (2013), thereby enhancing their recovery capabilities. The primary aim of the ECOP group intervention—to alleviate the internalized self-stigma in individuals with schizophrenia through a novel integration of COP's empowerment strategy and an adapted CBT framework—has been successfully achieved.

12606320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606320.value: 1. The ECOP program is based on the COP model, with enhancements from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to address self-stigmatization among Chinese individuals with mental illness. Further studies on the impact of ECOP group with other targets are encouraged. 2. The ECOP group uses a culturally adapted version of CBT to help individuals change negative self-stigmatizing beliefs. Further research is recommended to explore the impact of Chinese cultural elements on reducing self-stigma in people with mental illness. 3. The objective of the ECOP program was to assist participants in diminishing self-stigma through the enhancement of positive self-beliefs rather than the direct confrontation of negative self-stigmatizing beliefs. Future research could be oriented towards investigating how personal, familial, and social strengths might play a role in diminishing the self-stigma experienced by individuals with schizophrenia. 4. Through facilitated open discussions within the intervention group, participants could normalize their experiences, alleviate feelings of inadequacy and isolation, and address challenges related to both self and public stigma. This contributed to fostering a sense of solidarity and empowerment among the group members. Future investigations could focus on the effects of mediating variables, such as group dynamics, on ECOP group. 5. This study contributes to the existing knowledge about innovative interventions designed to reduce self-stigma among individuals with schizophrenia. It has important implications for community-based mental health services. To apply the findings more broadly, further research that combines the benefits of the COP model and culturally adapted CBT for individuals with mental health issues in various Chinese societies should be promoted. 6. The study delineated the primary and secondary outcomes of the ECOP group. Subsequent studies could aim to delineate the predictive effects of various therapeutic components of the ECOP group which were instrumental in reducing the internalization of self-stigma among the participants.

12606320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606320.value: The issue of self-stigma is prevalent among individuals with severe mental illness. Self-stigma has been found to have negative effects on the recovery of individuals with mental illness by reducing their quality of life, self-esteem, and treatment compliance. This, in turn, leads to increased psychiatric symptoms and relapse. This research project aims to investigate the effectiveness of an innovative intervention group called Expanded Coming Out Proud (ECOP) in reducing self-stigma among Chinese individuals with schizophrenia in Hong Kong. The results indicated that participants in the 12-session ECOP group experienced reductions in internalized self-stigma and depressive symptoms, as well as an enhancement in their sense of empowerment compared to those who did not attend the group. The study provides evidence supporting the effectiveness of the ECOP group, which incorporates both COP and culturally adapted CBT, in reducing self-stigma and depressive symptoms and enhancing self and community empowerment among individuals with schizophrenia in Hong Kong. The study not only adds to the existing literature on innovative interventions for reducing self-stigma among individuals with schizophrenia, but it also holds significant implications for community-based mental health services by enhancing their capacity for recovery.

12606520.label: Project Objectives
12606520.value: To survey the HK live music ecology made up of hard (live music venues) and soft (live music organization and promotion companies) infrastructures - currently active in HK across all musical genres and types of events. To assess the 'health' of the HK live music sector as a whole and within its sub-sectors by considering the diversity of its live music venues – with respect to both size and musical styles –, and their overall capacity to cater to different music audiences and to bring diversity to the local music landscape on a regular basis. To use quantitative and qualitative methods to better understand the affordances and difficulties faced by these infrastructures in relation to: public policy, economic factors (access to funding, income, expenses, etc.), COVID-19 pandemic, real estate markets, cultural positioning, perception and function, as well as other relevant aspects. To examine how this ecology generates economic, social and cultural ‘value’ for the city through the ways in which live music events and the structures that organize events foster and sustain local artistic communities and/or scenes, generate discourses about the cultural life of the city, act as platforms for artists, audiences and other industry actors to interact. To generate the following deliverables: 1) an annotated data set about the infrastructures currently involved in the HK live music sector; 2) a report featuring both quantitative and qualitative aspects of the data set assessing the general landscape of the live music sector in HK; 3) academic publications following conference papers; 4) one public lecture. To assess and understand, where possible, the impact of Covid-19 on the HK live music sector. To use this data and analysis to a) to contribute a significant Asian case study to the existing English-language live music scholarship; b) to make recommendations pertaining to policy-decisions and funding allocation under the HK government leadership in order to protect and develop the HK live music sector in the future; c) to promote a greater overall understanding of the social and cultural value of live music and of its infrastructures among the wider HK public.

To examine how this ecology generates economic, social and cultural ‘value’ for the city through the ways in which live music events and the structures that organize events foster and sustain local artistic communities and/or scenes, generate discourses about the cultural life of the city, act as platforms for artists, audiences and other industry actors to interact.

To generate the following deliverables: 1) an annotated data set about the infrastructures currently involved in the HK live music sector; 2) a report featuring both quantitative and qualitative aspects of the data set assessing the general landscape of the live music sector in HK; 3) academic publications following conference papers; 4) one public lecture.
To assess and understand, where possible, the impact of Covid-19 on the HK live music sector.

To use this data and analysis to a) to contribute a significant Asian case study to the existing English-language live music scholarship; b) to make recommendations pertaining to policy-decisions and funding allocation under the HK government leadership in order to protect and develop the HK live music sector in the future; c) to promote a greater overall understanding of the social and cultural value of live music and of its infrastructures among the wider HK public.

12606520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606520.value: At a time during which the importance of live music sector has been growing economically, socially and culturally across the globe in the face of deep changes to the ways in which recorded music is produced, circulated and consumed, the live music industry in Hong Kong (HK) has not yet become the focus of academic analysis. HK’s live music ‘ecology’ (the ecosystem of locally and materially embedded hard and soft infrastructures engaged in the production and promotion of live music) is active and diverse in terms of its venues – from stadiums, mid-scale concert spaces, bars featuring live music, and small-scale or underground venues –, of musical styles – from classical and jazz music, to Cantonese pop, to independent and experimental music – and of demographics. Yet no sustained study has analyzed the characteristics and role of the HK live music sector across a comprehensive range of hard and soft infrastructures. This project will address this gap and attempt to explore the economic, cultural and political conditions under which live music infrastructures operate in HK. Taking the cue from recent research on the live music sector in popular music studies, the research team for this project asks: what is the structure of the live music ‘ecology’ in HK? How does this ecology not only create economic, but also social and cultural value for HK? What are the specificities of HK’s live music ecology as an East Asian urban center compared to the more documented live music ecologies of Western Europe, Australia and North America? Using both quantitative and qualitative methods, the research team will a) map the local live music hard and soft infrastructures and their practices currently active in the city; b) produce a data set aimed at understanding the ‘health’ of the live music ecology in HK – as a whole and per venue-size categories and broad genre sectors – by conducting detailed surveys targeting musicians, venues and promoters, as well as audiences; c) conduct qualitative profile interviews with specific promoters, venues and musicians; d) use the data gathered through desk research, surveys and interviews to produce two academic articles as well as a report aimed at being a resource for policy planning and funding allocation under the HK government’s leadership. The results from this research will provide important and wide-ranging insights into the strengths and difficulties of the live music ecosystem in HK for the first time. 在唱片行業的製作、發行和消費方式正在發生深刻變化的當下，現場音樂無論是在經濟方面，還是在社會、文化方面，都在發揮日漸增長的影響力。然而，香港的現場音樂產業卻尚未被學界關注。事實上，香港的現場音樂“生態”（指稱一整套用以支撐本地現場音樂的製作與推廣的軟硬設施的生態系統）在場地上、音樂風格上和觀眾群上都充滿活力並且形態多元。在場地上有大型的體育館，中型的表演空間和酒吧，以及小型的和地下的表演空間。在音樂風格上則涵蓋古典樂、爵士樂、粵語流行歌曲，還有獨立音樂及實驗音樂。目前尚無研究對香港現場音樂產業的一系列軟硬設施的特徵與作用進行全面分析。該研究項目旨在填補這方面的知識空缺，並且嘗試探討香港現場音樂設施所處的經濟、文化與政治條件如何。受到近期流行音樂研究領域裏關於現場音樂的研究成果啟發，該項目提出以下問題：香港現場音樂的生態結構是什麼樣的？該生態如何為香港本地貢獻出不僅是經濟的，而且還有社會及文化方面的價值？香港作為東亞的一個重要都會，與現有文獻討論的西歐、澳大利亞與北美的現場音樂生態相比，其現場音樂生態有何特別之處？該研究採用量化與質化的研究方法，將1）描述本地現場音樂的軟硬設施及其當前活躍的系列活動；2）通過對相關的音樂家、場地、活動發起人和觀眾進行問卷調查而生成一個數據庫，該數據庫旨在幫助理解如何在香港形成一個良性的現場音樂生態，不僅通過考察整體的生態系統，而且通過分析每個場地的運作和每種音樂類型的接受情況；3）對部分活動發起人、場地負責人和音樂家等相關人物進行訪談；4）運用案頭調研、問卷調查和訪談所收集的數據撰寫兩篇學術論文和一篇報告。該報告將對香港政府在該領域的政策規劃和財政撥款有所裨益。該研究成果將首次對香港的現場音樂生態的優勢和困境提供極為重要及具有廣泛參考價值的見地

12606520.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606520.value: More than 20 venues (out of 63 active regularly) permanently closed within the project timeframe. Most venues which ceased activities reported social unrest in 2019 and Covid-19 having negatively impacted foot traffic and the staging of planned or future events as reasons to stop operations. Among the remaining active venues, the following trends emerged: A roughly equivalent number of small-scale (0 - 250 persons) and medium-scale venues (250 – 3,200 persons) ) operated in Hong Kong, with the vast majority of those venues located on the Hong Kong Island and on the Kowloon peninsula. There is a significant number of small venues offering the possibility for musicians to kickstart or maintain a small-audience music performance career in HK, but due to reported costs of operation and licensing difficulties, many of these venues also relied on food and/or alcohol sales as their primary income . This has implications for the genres of music whose live performance is being supported: many of these food & beverage-reliant venues will favour music styles/genres - i.e. pop, jazz, r'n'b, folk - that are considered suitable for food and alcohol consumption, with fewer venues supporting genres that are (according to informants) not seen as suitable to these activities - i.e. rock-based styles, electronic music, etc. There are therefore fewer small-scale venues dedicated primarily to these genres. Many artist informants operating in indie pop, rock and electronic music reported not having enough suitable venues catering to the full spectrum of their career stages, early/mid/mainstream success. Many such artists pointed out that while they could perform in small venues at the start of their careers, and potentially in large venues (e.g. the HK Coliseum, Queen Elizabeth Stadium, and the Hong Kong Convention & Exhibition Centre) if they attained mainstream success, there were few mid-sized venues to cater to mid-career levels of live music audience in HK. Several promoters at such mid-sized infrastructures (i.e. McPherson Stadium) reported that demand for bookings from artists far outnumbered the availability they could provide. In other words, for multiple genres of popular music, the Hong Kong venue ecosystem did not appear balanced. There was a sharp rise in 'soft infrastructures' - i.e. concert promoters staging one-time events at multiple official and 'pop-up' venues -, highlighting the financial and licensing difficulties of sustaining the operations of hard live music infrastructures. These findings are reported in published and soon-to-be published academic outputs (see Part C).

12606520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606520.value: Findings from the project indicate the need to continue assessing the evolutions and needs of the live music sector in Hong Kong, particularly in relation to the following: - Specific genres of popular music, which appeared to be very unevenly promoted across the local infrastructure ecosystem. Reasons for these discrepancies require fuller analysis. - the number and suitability of hard infrastructures available to musicians in relation to specific career stages and needs. While the number of small-scale venues fluctuated - with multiple closings and new openings - throughout the duration of the research and there was a clear push from the public and private sector to support larger-scale music events, mid-scale venues - crucial to the development of longer-term music performance careers - appeared to be under-represented in the sector. - the need to have a finer-grained assessment of diversity - gender, ethnicity and age-related, among other factors - and inequalities across the live music sector in HK. Various artists and music promoters reported such factors impacted their overall careers in different ways. Members of the research team will aim to pursue this finding in further grant applications.

12606520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606520.value: The Hong Kong live music sector is more diverse in terms of infrastructures and music genre than typically accounted for. The music industries in the city are usually discussed in relation to Cantonese pop music, but the city's performance ecosystem caters to an increasingly broader range of styles, and performances in other popular music genres are - rap, rock, electronic music, jazz, etc. - are becoming more and more popular. However, particularly since the Covid-19 pandemic, more live music promoters and artists are finding it difficult to stage live music in stable and profitable conditions. Small-scale venues have opened and closed at a rapid rate, mid-scale venues (which are important to musicians for developing their careers and present their music to larger audiences) are lacklustre, and there is currently a lack of large-scale live music-focused venues susceptible to hosting arena-level international touring acts. In contrast to this, a growing number of music promoters have adopted a flexible 'pop-up' approach, staging live music events in various locations and venues across HK. There is a need for specific live music oriented policy attention in order to help local musicians develop sustainable careers as part of the city's creative industries ecosystem.

12607020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607020.value: 從邊緣走向中心：荷屬東印度華人在帝國競爭時期的國籍論從邊緣走向中心：荷屬東印度華人在帝國競爭時期的國籍論及身份認同（1854-1930）

12607020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607020.value: This project examines the shaping and reconfiguration of nationality, subjectness, and race of an overseas Chinese community in times when Chinese expansionism, Western colonialism, and Japanese imperialism intersected in Southeast Asia. By focusing on the Chinese under Dutch colonial rule the aims of this proposed project is two-fold. First, it will examine how Dutch Indies Chinese changed their status from being “stateless subjects” to becoming nationals and subjects of the Chinese, Dutch, and Japanese empires. Second, this project aims to help develop a novel paradigm to contextualize the study of Diaspora, Empires, and Nationality from the perspective of “inter-imperial rivalry” and "recurrences of diasporic temporality" within the study of the Chinese Diaspora. By studying the developments of Dutch Indies Chinese from 1854 to 1930 this study aims to identify the stimuli and processes of diasporization and un-diasporization within the context of competing empires. Such phenomena was, in the case of Dutch Indies Chinese, often temporal in nature. Research shows that the Dutch colonial government officially ‘racialized’ Dutch Indies Chinese by assigning people of both full and mixed Chinese descent into the racial category of “Chinese”. Despite that the Dutch colonized the Indies, the Dutch did not give Dutch Indies Chinese an official status of subjectness, however. Their perceived status as “stateless subjects” changed in 1893 when the first official petition to acknowledge overseas Chinese as being subjects of China was presented to the Qing court, which caused an increasing number of Dutch Indies Chinese to become ‘diasporized’. Their status was further solidified with the declaration of the Chinese nationality law. This project suggests that their change from being stateless to obtaining a national status became possible when empires were competing with one another for Dutch Indies Chinese support. The proposed project ends at circa 1930 when the significance of Dutch Indies Chinese voices for manoeuvring states’ policies began to decrease due to the Civil War between nationalists and communists in China, Japan’s intensified aggression of imperial expansion, and the rise of Indonesian nationalism during the waning days of the Dutch empire. 海外華人在國籍和國民身份等問題研究裏大多扮演著一個被動性的角色，導致他們對國籍論和國民身份問題的影響力被邊緣化。因此，為了考察華人對此問題的重要性和影響，本研究把荷屬東印度華人的角色從邊緣移到中心。此研究項目主要針對兩個問題：一、荷屬華人的身份如何被清國、中華民國、荷國、日本帝國認同。二、帝國競爭和華僑政策如何互相推動。 本研究集中於1854至1930的時期。那時中、荷、日等國給予荷屬華人不同的待遇和身份，使得華人由非國民取得多國身份認同。十九世紀中葉荷蘭殖民政府正式使用種族分類的方法來組分被統治者。除了新客之外本土華人和華人混血也被列入「中國人」的族類。荷方的種族分類直接關涉到殖民管理。使得華人在殖民政策下持續地受到歧視待遇。可是，中華民族主義擴展、清政府對海外華人的重視，在加上華人在日本南進初期取得優勢地位的環境下，荷政府也開始改變華人政策方針。在處於帝國競爭的環境之下，海外華人如何影響國籍和殖民身份等問題？除了以荷屬華人為中心探討華人在這時期的多重身份和認同外，這研究會分析華人如何由棄民轉為國籍論的推動力。

12607220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607220.value: 以痰論情——以960年 — 1911年中醫痰學説為例

12607220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607220.value: Today and going back for almost one thousand years, phlegm has figured as a major cause and symptom of disease and disorders of the mind in traditional Chinese medicine. Curiously, however, when we go back to the ancient classics, such as the Huangdi neijing and the Nanjing (ca. 100 BC), the very notion of phlegm is entirely absent. The rise of the pathology of phlegm is one of the fundamental transformations in the historical development of Chinese medical thought. This suggests two basic questions: a) when, how, and why did the discourse of phlegm arise and take root in China? b) how did the rise of phlegm alter the Chinese understanding of disease, the body, and the self? Answering these questions will entail research into the entangled relations of developments in medical thought and in the cultural and socio-economic sphere (i.e. neo-Confucian thought, and the rise of a nascent monetary market economy) during the Song period (960-1279). Remarkably, these questions have gone almost entirely unstudied—perhaps in part because the thousand-year reign of phlegm has made it seem so integral to traditional Chinese medicine that its absence from the foundational classics of traditional Chinese medicine has been forgotten. Elucidating these questions is crucial for: (a) understanding the historical evolution of traditional Chinese medicine and (b) excavating the archaeology not only of contemporary Chinese medical thought and practice, but also of the contemporary everyday experience of the embodied self. Addressing these questions will open up new horizons for the study of emotions. On the one hand, the proposed project will contribute to the historical study of emotions in China; on the other hand, the project will function as a case study that can offer hints about the concepts and methods needed to study the history of emotions more generally. In this respect, the study will add to the growing corpus of studies on embodied emotions, and it will draw attention to the extraordinary importance of phlegm for the study of emotions, as to date phlegm has received virtually no attention in emotion history despite its undisputed importance as emotion fluid in Chinese, Greek, and Indian medicine . This will contribute to establishing a scholarly framework for a psychology built on emic Chinese medical conceptions rather than on Western categories, and will also contribute to contemporary discourses in the philosophy of mind and in clinical psychology. 從今至回溯近一千前，傳統中醫學視痰為疾病的主因、症狀及精神紊亂的代表。有趣的是，痰的概念並沒有記載在《皇帝内經》及《黃帝八十一難經（難經）》等古籍内，而痰液病理學的興起也是中醫思想史發展上一項重要的轉變。這個思想的轉變帶來了兩個基本的問題：一、何時、如何以及爲何痰的論述被提出並扎根在中國社會中。 二、有關痰的論述如何改變中國對於疾病、身體及自我的理解。爲了解答這兩個問題，我們需要深入探討宋代（960-1279）的醫學思想及文化和社會經濟領域（即新儒家思想和新興的貨幣市場經濟）之間錯綜複雜的發展關係。值得注意的是，上述的問題甚少被研究過，也許是因為至古以來，痰都是傳統中醫藥中不可或缺的元素，以致人們遺忘了其被排除在傳統中醫基礎知識外。 闡明這些問題有助於：一、理解傳統中醫藥的歷史演變及；二、發掘不局限於當代的中醫思想及實踐，深究體現當代自身日常經驗的人類學，為這個範疇的研究開拓了新方向。另一方面，是次研究企劃將有助於中國的情感史研究，並且作為個案研究，普遍化研究的理論和方法。研究將補充有關自我情感的語料庫，引起大家關注痰在當中的重要性。儘管痰在中國、希臘乃至印度醫學中作為情感液體（emotion fluid）而有舉足輕重的重要性，但其在情緒史研究中則沒有受到太大的關注。因此，是項研究將建基於中國特有的醫學理念並為當代心理哲學及臨床心理學研究作出貢獻。

12607620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607620.value: The elderly population in worldwide is expected to increase exponentially. There will be a higher percentage of older adults suffering cognitive decline in the coming decades. Cognitive impairment, being the most common health problem associated with ageing, contributes to possible loss of functional independence and disability. The purpose of this study is to determine the effectiveness of four mixed modalities of three training programs (combined cognitive and physical training, cognitive or physical training only) on cognition and fitness of community-dwelling older adults in Hong Kong. The study hypotheses will be set as the integrated format of all three training will have higher cognition and fitness scores than other combinations of two training modes and all these mixed modalities will have greater positive outcomes than the active control subjects. The study design is a cluster randomized controlled trial. Twenty-four elderly centers as clusters will be randomly selected and assigned to be intervention (n=20) or control groups (n=4) in two study phases. A total of 18-20 older adults (age ≥ 60) meeting the inclusion/exclusion criteria from each cluster (total subjects = 480) will be invited to be study participants. Each intervention cluster will receive either an integrated training format or one out of three combinations of two training modes. Each intervention training mode will last for 2-month of 16 sessions in total, 2 sessions per wk and 60 min per session, hence, the total intervention will last for 4 months for two training modes or an integrated training format. Assessments will be conducted at pre-test, two post-training tests, and a 2-month follow-up test after completion of all training. The primary outcome measures in cognition include tests of execution and memory: Chinese nonverbal Stroop test, trail making test, Chinese Rey auditory learning test with a secondary measure of Montreal Cognitive Assessment (HK-MCoA). The outcome measures in physical fitness include chair stand, arm curl, 6-min walk, 8-feet up-&-go, and four square step test (for dynamic balance). Data analyses will be performed by mixed effects modeling. 預計世界的老年人口將以指數級增長。在未來的幾十年，患有認知能力下降老年人的比例將會更高。認知障礙是與衰老相關的、一個最常見的健康問題，可能導致喪失身體功能獨立性和殘疾。目的：這項研究是為了確定三項訓練（認知和健體相結合、僅認知和僅健體訓練）在四種混合模式下對社區居住老年人的認知和體能影響的有效性。研究假設將為：在所有三項訓練的綜合形式中，重覆的認知和健體相結合會有更佳的認知和體能能力，其效果將高於單獨兩項訓練的混合模式，並且所有四種混合模式將比主動控制組有更大的積極成果。研究設計是一項整群隨機對照試驗。二十四個長者中心集群將被隨機選擇並分配為干預（n = 20）或對照組（n = 4）。每中心共有18-20位年齡在60歲以上符合納入標準的老年人將受邀請成為研究參與者（總數為480人）。每個干預小組將接受重覆的認知和健體相結合綜合培訓模式、或是三種由兩項訓練混合的模式之中的一種。每個干預訓練項目將持續2個月，共16節，每星期2節，每節為60分鐘，因此，整個混合模式包括２個訓練項目的總干預時間將持續4個月。評估將在測試前，兩個培訓測試後及所有培訓完成的2個月跟踪測試後進行。認知的結果指標主要包括執行力和記憶力的測試：中文非語言Stroop測試，連線測試，中文雷伊聽覺學習測試以及蒙特利爾認知評估（HK-MCoA）的輔助測量。而體能測試包括椅子站立，手臂彎曲，步行6分鐘，起步8英尺和四平方測試（用於動態平衡）。數據分析將使用混合線性模式。

12607820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607820.value: 《易經》及其相關文獻在戰國時期的運用

12607820.label: Project Objectives
12607820.value: This research plan is a continuation of the applicant’s work on this manuscript. To date, and starting in Spring 2018, I have published three articles about of it in top-tier journals in both English and Chinese. The present project is an extension of these articles, this time focusing analytically on the relationships between numbers and images and between images and text. I will do research on the manuscript itself, and use the systems of knowledge available in it to do research outside of it. Apply a hermeneutical approach to write individual essays on knowledge systems at work in the text. The topics include: a) the relationship between numerical diagrams and the predictions associated with them in the “case examples” section of the text (Sections 1-17). b) detecting what images were keyed to what trigrams. c) tracing evidence of how different images were associated to the same trigram and how the same image was associated to different trigrams. d) a comprehensive study of the “Hexes” section of the manuscript. e) a reevaluation of the Hexagram “Mingyi明夷” based on the “Diagram of Trigram Position, Diagram of the Human Body” (section 24/30). Based on data in this manual and other archaeological discoveries from the Pre-Han period, reconstruct and arrange all of the numerical “alloforms” of the eight trigrams. Provide examples of how the “conversion” of numerical trigrams/hexagrams into yin and yang lines after the Qin dynasty led to a disconnection between images and the diagrams they were once based on. Recognize ideas of problems in reading and studying literature on this topic, and provide a methodology with solutions based on working with an intact manuscript like this. To demonstrate that the language in this text is not strange and can be understood. To demonstrate that the systems of knowledge in this text were part of a wider tradition in use during the Warring States period.

12607820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607820.value: A study guide from fourth century BCE China about predicting the future was rediscovered in the summer of 2008. The text was buried along with the tomb occupant from the ancient kingdom of Chu (modern Hubei province) who once commissioned its compilation and used it both to gain knowledge of the subject and to demonstrate his expertise about it by predicting his future and the future of others. Yarrow Stalk Divination (Shifa筮法) has text and illustrations written in a regional script on sixty-three bound and numbered bamboo-strips 35 cm long. It is the most pristine and intact Warring States bamboo-strip manuscript ever encountered. Underground and idle for millennia, this genuine Warring States period technical handbook for use with numerical divination in the “Changes易” tradition converges diverse systems of material knowledge from earlier times and places, much of which was subsequently lost or not transmitted intact. One of the most important features of this manuscript is that it demonstrates beyond any doubt that at this time hexagram pictures were still written with numerals and not yet with solid yang and broken yin lines as substitutes. A clear model of what the text says and means is required before proceeding to do other things with it. Qinghua University’s Warring States bamboo-strip manuscripts, received as an anonymous gift in 2008, was once the library of a man (probably a low-level official) who lived in what is now modern Hubei province. Totalling 2388 individual bamboo-strips, this collection stands as one of the most significant finds of material literature. What the field of Early China and Ancient World studies has needed for some time is intact Warring States versions of literary and non-literary texts that were extant and in circulation during the vibrant period of the “Hundred Philosphers” and before the Qin’s “burning of the books” in 213 BCE. The ideal Warring States manuscripts are those that have come to us intact. The most pristine and intact bamboo-strip manuscript not only amongst the Qinghua University collection but since the discovery of Warring States manuscripts written on this stationary is Yarrow Stalk Divination (Shifa筮法). My project applies the knowledge systems in this text to a larger and more comprehensive study of Warring States uses of the Yijing and other literature in the “Changes易” tradition. 2008年夏天，一篇來自公元前四世紀中國的、用以預測未來的文獻（《筮法》）重現於世。這篇文獻隨古楚國（今湖北省）的墓主埋葬入墓。墓主指示編纂這篇文獻，以便用來掌握卜筮知識，並通過預卜他和他人的未來，發揮他的專業占卜技能。《筮法》圖文並茂，抄寫在63枚以繩編聯的、記有編號的、35釐米長的竹簡上。它是目前所見最原始、最完好無缺的戰國竹簡。這本戰國時期繼承《易》傳統的數字占卜手冊深藏地下數千年，匯集了早期不同時地的物質文化系統，其中許多已失傳於世或沒有完整地保存下來。這篇簡文最重要的特點之一，是它確切地證明了當時的卦象是用數字來記錄的，而不是用陽爻和陰爻來記錄的。在進一步研究之前，必須對這篇文獻所講所述有明確的認識。 清華大學所藏的戰國竹簡，於2008年由匿名者捐贈，屬於一個生活在楚國的古人（可能是低級官吏）的藏書。這批竹簡共有2388枚，是最重要的物質文獻之一。早期中國和古代世界研究亟需完整的戰國時期的文學和非文學文本，這些文本保存和流通於蓬勃的諸子百家爭鳴時期，並倖免於公元前213年秦所施行的焚書令。 理想的是，呈現於我們眼前的是完好無缺的戰國簡文。《筮法》不但是清華簡中最原始、最完整的竹簡，而且是目前所見戰國竹簡中最原始、最完整的竹簡。我的研究計劃利用這篇簡文的知識系統，更全面、深入地研究戰國時期《易》類文獻。

12607920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607920.value: People often assume that scientific discourse is – or, at least, should be – free of metaphor. However, this is not in fact the case: specialist scientific terminology is largely metaphorical in nature, while science authors adopt metaphor either to explain difficult ideas or because that is the only language available for describing a certain concept. Additionally, authors of popular science – the genre on which this research focuses – use figurative language for more striking communicative purposes. Metaphor is deeply rooted in thought, and there is even evidence that it can help shape the direction in which scientific research advances. Its significant role also ensures that it exerts a powerful influence on the language used to discuss scientific ideas, an influence that is perhaps particularly strong in popular science texts. In this research, we will be applying metaphor theorist Elena Semino’s ideas on how metaphorical expressions occur and interrelate within and across texts to a set of popular science articles taken first and foremost from Scientific American, a monthly periodical that appears in multiple international editions. We will analyse a set of articles from this publication to see how the various configurations of metaphorical expressions that they contain place the spotlight on specific aspects of the concepts described. Moving on to the translation angle, we will look at the corresponding metaphor patterns in the translations of these articles that appear, for example, in various international editions of the periodical. Up to now, analysis of metaphor in translation has focused almost exclusively on isolated expressions, an approach that has yielded some useful insights but is ultimately somewhat limited given the role of metaphor in mediating scientific concepts and the fact that individual expressions belonging to a particular metaphor pattern are often not translated consistently. We therefore aim to look at what happens to entire patterned groups of metaphorical expressions, an approach that we believe will make available to us new insights into translator action on a much higher level of generality. The distribution of metaphorical expressions in translations is likely to differ from what can be observed in original texts, which will in turn influence the way in which readers of the translations understand the subject matter. This we believe to be the most innovative aspect of the proposed research. 人們通常認為，科學話語是（或至少應當是）不使用隱喻的。然而事實卻並非如此。本質上，專業科學術語在很大程度上就是隱喻性的，科學作者也會採用隱喻手法來解釋複雜難懂的理論，或許因為這是可用來描述某種概念的唯一方式。此外，科普類（亦即本研究關注的文本類型）作者會為了更顯著的交流目的而使用比喻性語言。隱喻深深植根於思想之中，甚至有證據顯示它可以幫助確定科學研究的前進方向。它的重要作用也保證了其對用來討論科學思想的語言能夠產生強大的影響，這種影響可能在科普文本中表現得尤為強烈。 在本研究中，我們會將隱喻理論家埃琳娜·塞米諾（Elena Semino）關於隱喻表達如何在文本內部和文本之間發生並相互關聯的觀點應用於一組科普文章。這些文章首先取自《科學美國人》（Scientific American）這部擁有多個國際版本的月刊。我們將通過分析該期刊中的一組文章，了解其所包含的各種隱喻表達的建構如何聚焦於所描述概念的特定方面。然後，我們將從翻譯的角度觀察這些文章的譯文中所出現的對應隱喻規律，並對比該期刊不同的國際版本。到目前為止，對翻譯中隱喻的分析幾乎完全集中在孤立的表達上。考慮到隱喻在傳達科學概念方面的作用，且屬於特定隱喻規律的個別表達往往得不到一致的翻譯，所以之前的方法雖產生了一些有用的見解，但終究有所局限。因此，本研究旨在觀察隱喻表達的完整、群體性規律。我們相信，這種方法將使我們對譯者的行為產生新的認識，更具普遍性。隱喻表達在譯文中的分布可能與原文不同，這反過來又會影響譯文讀者對主題的理解方式。我們相信，這正是此項研究最具創新性的一面。

12608320.label: Project Objectives
12608320.value: To explore Xi Xi’s fiction through a practice-based research method that focuses on the creative writing process; To create a series of three new fictional works in response to the city spaces of Hong Kong today by apply “defamiliarizing” techniques inspired by Xi Xi’s work; To understand how creative writing practices can bring insights into our contemporary experience of Hong Kong; To complete three scholarly articles on how different defamiliarizing writing techniques can change our perceptions of a place; To share creative writing exercises arising from the findings of the research with the public.

12608320.label: Realisation of objectives
12608320.value: One of the primary objectives of this research project is to examine Xi Xi’s fiction through a practice-based research approach centered on the creative writing process. This objective has been achieved through two main components: first, my own writing practice, and second, a series of writing workshops developed based on the findings of the project. Across 24 workshops, 269 participants from diverse backgrounds—including secondary school students, rehabilitation groups, ethnic minorities, and breast cancer patients—engaged with three of Xi Xi’s literary works. The workshops emphasized Xi Xi’s writing strategies, fostering connections between her methods and participants’ personal experiences in Hong Kong. Participants were guided through three writing exercises: 1) “I-Space Revisited” (inspired by Xi Xi’s Mourning a Breast to reflect on their experiences with their living environments; 2) “A Stranger Nearby” (inspired by The Merry Building) to practice observing others in the city without bias; and 3) “I-City in a Dream” (inspired by The Marvels of a Floating City) to explore their subconscious relationships with the city. A survey completed by all 269 participants revealed that 85% responded positively to the question: “Do the works and writing methods introduced in the workshop inspire you to observe and understand the place where you live from a new perspective?” In addition, we successfully launched an interactive online creative writing platform, Our Xi Xi, Our City, in February 2023 to share creative writing exercises derived from the project’s research findings with the public. In addition to introducing three of Xi Xi’s literary works and providing writing prompts, the platform provides research materials related to Xi Xi’s works and features a word game inspired by her poem “Can We Say.” Creative pieces from workshop participants are also showcased on the website. For more details, please visit: https://www.ourxixiourcity.com/en/resource-area/word-game/ The goal of creating a series of three new fictional works inspired by Xi Xi’s work was only partially achieved, due to my late-stage breast cancer diagnosis in June 2023 and the subsequent progression of my illness. Originally intended as a component of this project’s study, Xi Xi’s Mourning a Breast became deeply intertwined with my personal journey of confronting and navigating my illness. As a result, rather than fully developing all three fictional works, I focused on exploring writing strategies in connection with Mourning a Breast. Similarly, the progress on completing three scholarly articles was interrupted, due to treatment related to my diagnosis, include two major surgeries, radiotherapy, and drug treatments, which have significantly limited my ability to attend international conferences and conduct research. (A summary of my medical condition from my doctor is available upon request.) However, having already gathered data from workshop participants and continuing to reflect on my writing practice, I plan to develop my drafts of scholarly articles and aim to submit my articles within a year.

12608320.label: Major findings and research outcome
12608320.value: The PI has participated in four academic conferences to present the outcomes of this project (please refer to part C). Three nonfiction works in response to Mourning a Breast have been written and published in a top-tier creative writing journal (please refer to “Other Impact” in part C). Additional research outputs include a creative writing website: https://www.ourxixiourcity.com/en/resource-area/word-game/. In addition to the virtual platform, selected works from our workshops were showcased at knock knock, Boundary Bookstore, and Book Punch from June 26 to July 10, 2024. A creative writing competition was also launched in these bookstores to encourage the use of the website. One of the key findings of this project is that, when focusing on the writing strategies of the three works written by Xi Xi over a span of 30 years, from the 1970s to the 1990s, the writing practices inspired by them can still generate new insights into understanding Hong Kong today. As stated in my proposal, this research does not aim to reach an absolute, irrefutable kind of knowledge, but instead seeks to explore “situated knowledge” (a term in reference to Donna Haraway) through literary practice. One of my central findings is the ability of creative writing as a tool for producing situated knowledge, contributing to empowerment and community-building. For example, by organizing a workshop with breast cancer patients that emphasized defamiliarization strategies adapted from Xi Xi’s Mourning a Breast, the work not only served as a powerful model for women facing the same illness to reflect on their challenges, and on their identity as women and their relationships with others in the city. Xi Xi’s work has demonstrated how literary works can transform a crisis, in this case, breast cancer, into a vital resource for producing situated knowledge within a community.

12608320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12608320.value: I am keen to extend this research by focusing on the development of situated knowledge and community-building among various marginalized groups in Hong Kong. Upon completing my personal reflections on my illness and treatment experience, I plan to design further creative writing exercises aimed at engaging breast cancer patients. This will allow me to explore the potential of literary practice as a therapeutic tool within the realm of medical humanities.

12608320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12608320.value: This research project examines how creative writing can change the way we see a place and our connection to it. It focuses on three works by the well-known Hong Kong writer Xi Xi, identifying her respective writing techniques and applying them to writing about Hong Kong today. This method helps us better understand her style and shows how creative writing practices can be a way to observe a place and create new insights. By turning these findings into teaching tools and sharing them with the public, the research project also helps build community and support marginalized groups in Hong Kong.

12609220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609220.value: With a long, prolific, and influential career spanning the second half of the twelfth century and through the first decade of the thirteenth, Lu You produced a rich collection of poems that allows us to take a sustained look into the issues of the past as it shaped the literary pursuits in the mid-Southern Song. He was very much a product of his time in his manner of writing, committing himself to discover poetry in small moments of ordinary life and seeking to record them exhaustively with a sense of urgency and compulsion. But in a deeply personal turn, he directly engaged the central questions about the nature, function, and methods of writing poetry in his time – and of literary writing and learning in general. Poetry was the very ground where he sought to work out the deep and persistent questions about poetry: what did it mean for him to be a poet, and what was the place of poetry among a scholar’s commitments in vast continuity of the past, the present, and the future. At the very least, poetry to Lu You was a daily commitment, or as he himself put it, a habit that had become second nature. In a poetics primarily grounded in the everyday present, strands of ideal, historical, literary, and autographical past are structured into the experiences of the present in varied and interesting ways. The sense of temporality in Lu You’s poetry – of experiences oriented in a present imbued with the meaning of the past while gesturing toward the future – is a manifestation of the poet’s directly engagement with the issues about learning and the received textual tradition that defined the course of Song poetry up to and during his time. To a great extent, these questions also have and still shape the reception of Song poetry through the modern era. This project seeks to conduct a literary historical study of Lu You’s poetry, to address these broader issues based on a focused study of the past taking shape as it is mediated by the poet in the poem’s temporality. 陸游是一位多產且有影響力的詩人.從第十二世紀後半葉直到十三世紀的前十年，他創作了內容豐富的詩集，使我們能夠深入觀察南宋中期的文學追求中對於“往昔”這一主題的處理。陸游是時代的產物，致力於在小處和平凡的生活中發現詩歌，並且有一種用詩將生活經驗全面記錄下來的緊迫感。在他主要紮根於日常的生活的詩學中，理想，歷史，文學和個人經歷中的“往昔” 通過各種有趣的方式被融入現時的經驗。該項目旨在從文學史角度進行陸游詩研究，重點探討陸游在創作中對詩歌的性質，功能和方法等等問題的理解。

12609320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609320.value: 珍奥絲丁與美麗政治經濟學

12609320.label: Project Objectives
12609320.value: To investigate the Regency beauty myth in relation to the nineteenth-century political economy and how (beauty) capitalism was backed by political changes, the freedom to trade, the democratization of dress, and the division of (beauty) labour in Austen’s time. To map out the links between the Austens’ (social, sartorial) anxiety and the ideology of beauty in different newspaper discourses, noting that ideology’s impact on the transformation of beauty capital, commodity culture, and the justification of gender or class difference. To examine Austen’s critical evaluation of the gentry and beau monde along with her views on the links between fashionability and the micropolitics of self-management, the family’s microfinance, the making of marriage decisions, the perpetuation of patriarchy, and the building of an empire. To publish three single-authored papers in reputable journals. To launch a specially designed public website.

12609320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609320.value: 人的共性就是選擇貌美者生存。這項研究著重珍奧絲丁與美的關係，運用理論，歷史古籍與文本研究的方式探討三個問題：19世紀英國如何介定美的標準？美男美女的塑造與政治經濟學有何關係？珍奥絲丁對美麗意識型態作出什麼回應？ 這項研究有三個重點：首先，19世紀的「美麗傳說」不能與政治經濟學分割。自然美包括天生麗質更包括後天經濟學的自然律，亞當斯密夫認為美與經濟人的社會性大有關係。而這項研究課題也旨在分析初期資本主義如何配合政府政策，自由貿易，勞工分配制度而生產美的觀念和實踐。 第二，由於珍奧絲丁飽閲報章，這項研究也探討傳媒如何影響19世紀的美貌標準和美容產品，從而合理化政治社會階級，和種族意識型態。傳媒渲染的美麗論述不單牽涉歐陸時裝美學，更激勵英國的經濟發展。這項研究將會致力討論人美化自己的過程，（國際)消費品的購置，美與不公義的關係。 最後，這項硏究側重分析珍奧絲丁對美麗意識型態的回應。在她筆下的世界中，美貌和優美代表文明和社會共融，另一方面，她也批判當時的士紳階級和時髦界。這項研究探討珍奧絲丁闡釋追求時髦美麗如何影響人的自我管理，家庭的經濟規劃，年輕人的婚姻訣擇，男權社會的延展和國家的命脈。 這是一個為期兩年的研究，將會為珍奧絲丁文學和美麗政治經濟學帶來新的啓發。

12609820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609820.value: 升級再造香港：珠三角珠寶設計中循環物質文化的循環經濟

12609820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609820.value: For centuries, jewelry makers and goldsmiths have worked sustainably and created circular economies by melting and reshaping precious metal objects and by dismounting and reframing valuable gemstones. This longstanding practice of recycling has also informed recent practices by which jewelry designers have creatively reused waste materials alongside pearls and silver to turn “trash into treasure.” This proposed project will research upcycling practices in contemporary art and design in Hong Kong, a city that connects local with global practices while remaining rooted in Asia, one of the world’s top waste-producing and waste-receiving areas. Understanding craftsmanship as a way of thinking, we will map and investigate the pioneering roles of jewelry designers’ sustainable practices. We will seek to further develop their practices as a means to find creative solutions for Hong Kong’s 21st- century waste pollution problems, and make these solutions accessible to members of the public, designers, and students. Although prior studies have focused on creative strategies of reuse in contemporary art and design, they have remained Western-centric. No study has examined Chinese and, in particular, Hong Kong practices. We will fill this lacuna by adding a focused Asian case study to the field of global art and design studies that complements extant theorizations of creative reuse. This project will be particularly innovative in its combination of artistic research with ecology. It will contribute to the larger paradigm shift affecting the humanities in the Anthropocene and pave the way for future innovations in jewelry design and recycling. The primary aims of the project will be to (i) research, contextualize, and theorize Hong Kong jewelry design (ii) add an Asian case study to Western-centric research on artistic practices of reuse (iii) demonstrate the pioneering role of designers in the development of sustainability (iv) educate students and members of the public, thereby creating greater social awareness about waste pollution and options for recycling (v) enhance and share creative solutions to environmental problems The project will produce the following outputs: (i) One peer-reviewed research publication (ii) An article of public interest on recycling in Hong Kong arts (iii) A body of jewelry design works and small sculptural objects (iv) The exhibition HongKong ReCycled (v) A digital archive of Hong Kong recycled art and design works (vi) A materials library of recyclable and recycled Hong Kong materials (vii) Conference presentations (viii) A hands-on workshop for members of the public (ix) An international academic workshop on practices of reuse in jewelry (x) A teaching component for arts curricula 升級再造香港： 珠三角珠寶設計中循環物質文化的循環經濟 幾個世紀以來，珠寶製造商和金匠一直在持續努力，創造出通過熔化和重塑貴重金屬，和拆卸及重新鑲嵌有價值寶石的循環經濟。這種長期回收的實踐也啟發了近代設計師對「把廢物變成寶物」的最新實踐。 今次的建議項目，將在香港這一個把本土跟國際連接的城市，研究「升級再造」在當代藝術和設計的實踐。香港位於亞洲，一個世界上最大的產生廢物和接收的區域，將令這個研究別具意義。將工藝理解為一種思維方式，我們將會探索珠寶設計中對可持續實踐的先鋒作用。我們將進一步發展這思維，為香港的21世紀廢物污染，尋找創新的解決方案，並將方案連接公眾，設計師和學生們。 儘管先前的研究曾聚焦於當代藝術及設計中重複使用的創造性策略，但這些研究一般保持以西方為中心。到目前為止，尚無針對中國，特別是香港做法的研究。我們將通過一個把重點放在亞洲的研究，來填補這一個全球藝術和設計研究中的罅隙，並互補素材重用的理論化。這個項目的創新處，在於它把藝術研究與生態議題相結合。它將有助於未來珠寶設計和回收方面的創新。 這項目的主要目標為： （i）對香港首飾設計的研究，情境化和理論化 （ii）在以西方為中心的重用藝術實踐研究中，增添亞洲案例研究 （iii）展示設計師在可持續發展中的先鋒作用 （iv）教育學生和公眾，從而創造更多社會對於廢物污染的認識和回收選擇 （v）加強和分享對環境問題有創造性的解決方案 該項目將產生以下產出： （i）一份經同行審閱的研究出版物 （ii）一份有關將回收用於香港藝術的文章 （iii）一組首飾設計作品和小型雕塑品 （iv）Hong Kong ReCycled展覽 （v）有關香港回收藝術品和設計作品的數字檔案 （vi）關於香港可循環再造物料的資料庫 （vii）於學術會議的報告 （viii）向公眾公開的實踐工作坊 （ix）一個關於將回收應用於首飾的國際學術會議

12610420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12610420.value: Since the 1990s, Tibetan Buddhism has made deeper missionary inroads in the Sinophone world than ever before. Not only have Tibetan Buddhist teachers garnered dedicated followings in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, the past two decades have also seen Tibetan Buddhism establish popular roots among mainland China’s urban middle class. As hundreds of thousands have embraced the Tibetan Buddhist tradition, a missionary transmission of consequential dimensions has been set in motion. The present study begins with the observation that transmission always entails transformation as religions adapt to the host ideologies and cultural practices of the places they travel. While scholars might be quick to suggest that Tibetan Buddhism is undergoing a process of ‘sinicisation’ as it adapts to the contemporary mainland Chinese sociocultural matrix, there have been few efforts to understand this process, much less investigate it ethnographically. In tackling this issue, the present study zeroes in on a vibrant but thus far under-researched domain with considerable implications for understanding Tibetan Buddhism’s transformation in mainland China: namely, the mobile media platform WeChat and its Sinophone milieu of ‘public pages’ (intraplatform microblogs) dedicated to Tibetan Buddhism. Since the onset of the smartphone era, hundreds of grassroots Tibetan Buddhist teachers and Han Chinese followers have embraced the technological and communicative affordances of WeChat to propagate Tibetan Buddhism among Sinophone audiences. In view of the largescale creative labour that has been invested in producing and curating public pages with content that is accessible, relevant and appealing to Chinese audiences – and the popular consumption of this content – the WeChat milieu must be recognised as a crucial site for investigating Tibetan Buddhism’s sinicisation in the contemporary Chinese context. This project will undertake an in-depth study of the digital mediation of Tibetan Buddhism in the WeChat domain, with a focus on Tibetan Buddhism’s construction as an object of knowledge and religious consumption for Sinophone audiences. Not only will it critically examine the prisms and practices through which Tibetan Buddhism is represented on public pages, it will also ethnographically explore the social processes through which these pages are produced and consumed. The impact of this content among ethnic Tibetans in China and Tibetan Buddhist followers in Hong Kong and Taiwan will also be investigated. The present study expects to significantly enrich understandings of the locally inflected transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in the contemporary Sinophone world and the importance of the digital in this process. 以數字媒體向漢族群眾傳播藏傳佛教：對微信上藏傳佛教華語傳教環境的研究 摘要 自1990年代以來，藏傳佛教比以往任何時候都更深入地在華語社會中傳播。在過去的二十年中，藏傳佛教不僅在台灣，香港和東南亞吸引了眾多的信徒，而且在中國大陸的城市中產階級中也被廣為人知。隨著成千上萬的人開始信奉藏傳佛教，隨之而來的傳教趨勢也陸續形成。 本研究首先觀察到，宗教傳播總是伴隨著宗教的轉變因為宗教需要適應所傳播到的東道國意識形態和文化習俗。盡管學者們很快地下了結論表示藏傳佛教正在適應“當代中國大陸”的社會文化形態，且正在經歷“中國化”的過程，但人們對這一過程本身並未付出太多精力去了解，更不用說從人類學上的角度對其進行研究了。為了解決這個問題，本研究將重點放在一個充滿活力但至今尚未深入研究的領域：即移動媒體平台微信及其以漢語為媒介傳播藏傳佛教的的公眾號（平台內微博）。這對於理解藏傳佛教在中國大陸的轉型具有重要意義。 自智能手機時代開始以來，數百名基層的藏傳佛教上師和漢族信徒已經利用微信的技術和交流能力在華語社會中傳播藏傳佛教。微信平台作為一個投入了大量的創意勞動來制作和策劃具有易訪問，有關聯和吸引中國觀眾的公共頁面，以及人們對該內容高頻率的訪問，它必須被視為一個重要的站點來了解和研究當代中國語境下的藏傳佛教的中國化。 本研究將對微信領域以數字媒體傳播藏傳佛教進行深入研究，重點研究藏傳佛教作為華語受眾的知識和宗教消費對象的構建。它不僅將全范圍地了解藏傳佛教在公眾號上所代表的角度和做法，還將從田野研究的角度探索生產和使用這些公眾號上的頁面的社會過程並對這些內容給中國藏族以及香港和台灣藏傳佛教徒產生對影響進行了解。本研究希望能夠極大地豐富人們對藏傳佛教在當代華語世界中局部影響和傳播的認識，以及在這一過程中數字化的重要性。

12610420.label: Realisation of objectives
12610420.value: 1. To provide the first in-depth study of the digital mediation of Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone audiences in the context of the contemporary transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in mainland China. The publications associated with my project are in different states of progress. I anticipate they will all be completed by the end of 2024 and published in 2025. These publications, taken as a whole, will represent the first in-depth study of the digital mediation of Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone audiences in the context of transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in mainland China. These publications centre on the pivotal role of grassroots engagement with the digital – and the affordances of WeChat, in particular – in the mainstreaming of Tibetan Buddhism in the 2010s, continuing until the present day. My analysis makes sense of the teeming multiplicity of WeChat’s digital missionary milieu. It shows how the technological affordances and the myriad and diverse creative agencies of grassroots religionists brought Tibetan Buddhism into the everyday lifeworlds of urban-based Han Chinese. 2. To critically analyse, applying textual and multimodal approaches, Tibetan Buddhism’s construction as an object of knowledge and religious consumption for contemporary Sinophone audiences on WeChat public pages. After compiling a database and digital archive of more than 2000 WeChat official accounts dedicated to Tibetan Buddhism, I critically analysed, applying textual and multimodal approaches, the ways that WeChat content creators and curators construct and represent Tibetan Buddhism for Chinese-speaking WeChat audiences. In a public lecture titled ‘“Mediating Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone audiences on WeChat” at HKU in October 2022, I examined the primary visual and linguistic discourses used to represent Tibetan Buddhism within this digital ecosystem. The content of this lecture served as the basis for a journal article, currently in progress, titled ‘Down to earth and close to life: Mainstreaming Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone audiences on WeChat.’ This publication goes a large way to fulfilling the above objective within the current project's parameters. 3. To examine the politics of discursive legitimation involved in mediating Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone WeChat audiences. As for politics of discursive legitimation, the portrayal of Tibetan Buddhism on WeChat official accounts throughout the 2010s revolved around presenting Tibetan Buddhism to Chinese audiences as a vibrant locus of authentic Buddhist teachings and practices. There is ample evidence of ‘hybridising strategies’ across many accounts, whereby Tibetan Buddhist content is situated side-by-side Chinese Buddhist content, or is visually represented in ways that draw on Chinese aesthetic conventions. I discuss these dimensions of ‘sinicisation’ in the article mentioned above. 4. To produce an ethnographically informed analysis of the production and curation of Tibetan Buddhist WeChat content from the perspective of creative stakeholders, paying particular attention to the agencies involved in generating content that is appropriate for and within the contemporary PRC context; Despite the fact my project period coincided with the Covid pandemic, meaning that I was ultimately unable to conduct as much in-person fieldwork as I had planned, I was nevertheless able to conduct several high-quality, in-depth interviews with creative stakeholders that furnished me with excellent perspectives on the agencies involved in generating content that is appropriate for and within the contemporary PRC context. A strong message that came through these interviews was the impetus to create content that was ‘jie di qi’ (down to earth) and ‘tiejin shenghuo’ (close to life). This finding has formed the basis of bottom-up theory-making about the role of WeChat in the mainstreaming of Tibetan Buddhism. I also presented a paper discussing this at the European Association of Social Anthropologists conference 2022. Overall, I consider this objective to be well achieved. 5. To understand how consumption practices and ideologies on the part of Han Chinese WeChat users contribute to Tibetan Buddhism’s sinicisation or domestication; Concerning this objective, one clear finding that emerged from my project research was that the WeChat platform and smartphones played a decisive role in the type of Buddhist content users accessed. These essential digital infrastructures enabled users to integrate Tibetan Buddhism into their daily routines, fostering close, frequent, and familiar connections with content from official accounts. In addition, the nature of WeChat’s interface and standard micro-blog templates flattened the differences between Tibetan Buddhist content and other traditions, thereby creating a digital environment conducive to the eclectic consumption of Buddhist content. These factors made Tibetan Buddhism more accessible and less distant to Han Chinese WeChat users, reinforcing a tendency to perceive it as simply another form of Buddhism. I write about this in two of the publications mentioned in part 6. I consider this objective to be quite well accomplished. 6. To explore issues of ideational interpenetration between different cultural constituencies in the broader Tibetan Buddhist world by investigating the consumption of Sinophone WeChat content by ethnic Tibetans and Chinese followers of Tibetan Buddhism in Hong Kong and Taiwan; By compiling a database and digital archive of Chinese and Tibetan language WeChat accounts dedicated to Tibetan Buddhism, I could investigate how Tibetan Buddhism was mediated differently as an object of religious consumption for Sinophone and Tibetophone audiences. In a public lecture titled 'Digital Religiosities in China’s Contemporary Tibetan Buddhist Landscape' at HKU in October 2022, I discussed this insight and analysed differing patterns of digital engagement among ethnic Tibetan and ethnic Chinese Tibetan Buddhist constituencies. Key insights from this talk have been integrated into the abovementioned journal article, 'Down to earth and close to life.' Further scope still exists for exploring issues of translation and ideational penetration between Chinese and Tibetan audiences within the dataset I have collected. Interviews with Chinese followers of Tibetan Buddhism in Hong Kong and Taiwan provided insights into the consumption of Sinophone WeChat content in these places. 7. To contribute to the steadily growing literature on the contemporary transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in the Sinophone world and the locally inflected processes of sinicisation by which it is taking place. Three articles/book chapters related to this project are currently in progress. Upon publication, they will contribute to the growing literature on the contemporary transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in the Sinophone world. I look forward to updating my profile in the RCG system as these works are published.
