To explore issues of ideational interpenetration between different cultural constituencies in the broader Tibetan Buddhist world by investigating the consumption of Sinophone WeChat content by ethnic Tibetans and Chinese followers of Tibetan Buddhism in Hong Kong and Taiwan;

To contribute to the steadily growing literature on the contemporary transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in the Sinophone world and the locally inflected processes of sinicisation by which it is taking place.

12610420.label: Major findings and research outcome
12610420.value: The project was initiated upon observing the widespread adoption of the WeChat platform by hundreds of Tibetan Buddhist lamas and Chinese Dharma practitioners as a digital interface for the propagation of Tibetan Buddhism. It was posited that the platform offered a fertile space to observe the construction of Tibetan Buddhism as an object of knowledge and religious consumption for Sinophone audiences, thereby providing insights into the domestication and sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism during China's “smartphone era” from the 2010s until the early 2020s. The principal finding to emerge from the project is that WeChat played a pivotal role in facilitating the mainstreaming of Tibetan Buddhism among contemporary Han Chinese audiences. By constructing and analysing an extensive database of WeChat official accounts as well as conducting interviews with creative stakeholders, content creators, and users, I identified three salient dynamics: an impetus to represent Tibetan Buddhism in a way that was ‘down to earth’ and ‘close to life’ for urban Chinese users; a tendency for hybridise Tibetan Buddhism, or, at least align it harmoniously, with Chinese Buddhism; and a diverse array of approaches among individual content creators to representing Tibetan Buddhism, leading to broad diffusion of its portrayal. These dynamics saw Tibetan Buddhism resonate more closely with the values, interests, needs and trends of Han Chinese audiences, making it more visible and appealing. At the same time, the fact users were accessing this content on a smartphone-based app meant that Tibetan Buddhism became more accessible, familiar, and parsed into attention-grabbing bite-sized chunks suitable for frequent consumption. Another significant contribution of WeChat to the mainstreaming of Tibetan Buddhism was its role as a vital infrastructure for delivering Buddhist education and supporting the formation of Buddhist textual communities. The results of this research are two international conference paper presentations, three public lectures, and three publications (currently in progress). These publications are: ‘Down to earth and close to life: Mainstreaming Tibetan Buddhism for Sinophone audiences on WeChat.’ (12, 000 word article), to be submitted to the journal Religions); ‘The Transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in Han China’ (10, 000 word article under contract with the Oxford Encylopedia of Buddhism); ‘Innovations in Lay Buddhist Education in New Era China’s Sinophone Tibetan Buddhist milieu: the rise of the Larung textual community’ in David Wank and Zhe Ji (eds.), The Metamorphosis of Buddhism in New Era China, Bloomsbury Press, forthcoming (12, 000 word chapter).

12610420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12610420.value: During the project period, I created a sizeable database and digital archive of more than 2000 WeChat accounts dedicated to Tibetan Buddhism using data scraping methods. Some of these WeChat official accounts span eight years of continuous activity, while others offer snapshots of digital Dharma outreach during short time periods. This archive, taken as a whole, represents an extremely valuable resource for future research into the digital dissemination of Tibetan Buddhism in China. This is especially so because of new regulations introduced by the Chinese government in 2022 that have imposed considerable restrictions on the use of the Internet to promote religion in mainland China. As a result, many accounts have closed, making historical data even more crucial for understanding the evolution and impact of digital Dharma outreach in Tibetan Buddhist’s contemporary transmission in China. In the future, I plan to further explore the considerable amount of Tibetan language WeChat content collected while conducting this project. This content presents an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the digital dissemination of Tibetan Buddhism within Tibetan society, offering a valuable counterpoint to the current study's focus on the Sinophone world.

12610420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12610420.value: This research project focused on WeChat as a platform for studying the dissemination of Tibetan Buddhism in China, approaching it as a fertile space for investigating dynamics of religious domestication and sinicisation. By compiling and analysing a database of WeChat official accounts dedicated to Tibetan Buddhism, and interviewing grassroots creative stakeholders and content users, I examined the ways that Tibetan Buddhism was mediated for and by Sinophone audiences. My key research finding revealed that WeChat, and digital infrastructures more generally, have played an important role in the mainstreaming of Tibet Buddhism in China through various means. In my analysis of the WeChat official accounts, I identified several dynamics facilitating the mainstreaming of Tibetan Buddhism’s mainstreaming, with the primary one being an impetus to represent Tibetan Buddhism in a way that was ‘down to earth’ and ‘close to life’ for urban Chinese users. This allowed Tibetan Buddhism to resonate more closely with the values, interests, needs and trends of Han Chinese audiences. The results of this project have contributed to understandings of the contemporary transmission of Tibetan Buddhism in the Sinophone world, and the vital role of the digital in this process.

12611020.label: Realisation of objectives
12611020.value: 1. 從中、韓在地文化差異，闡釋朝鮮學者批判康有為儒家學說的原因。 朝鮮時代依據儒家經典所建立的五倫觀念，延續至現今韓國社會仍難以撼動。朝鮮學者如田禹對康有為的嚴厲批判，便是因其學說脫離傳統儒家思想所提倡的三綱五常，違反父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友之倫常秩序。此外「儒學」一語，在韓國有其在地的文化背景，慣稱「儒教」，與其他國家不同。儒教不僅是學術思想上的儒學，也同時包含宗教意義。在信仰的精神加持下，這種在地文化的形成是他們批判康有為的原因。 2. 從朝鮮學者考辨康有為今古文經的真偽，探討儒家經典意識在域外的呈現。 康有為認為所有的古經皆是劉歆所偽造，《古文尚書》便是其中之一。然若辨證晚出《古文尙書》為偽，那麼遵奉朱子學為至高無上真理的朝鮮，便得承擔文化思想崩解帶來的衝擊。故而朝鮮學者也對《古文尚書》的真偽問題，展開熱烈且有別於明清學者的討論。大體而言，朝鮮學者試圖在漢學與宋學中尋求平衡點，使得朝鮮時代在這場論爭中，最後採取與中國不同的對應方法，為了保全受朱子思想影響深遠的朝鮮文化，最終未能屏棄《古文尙書》。 3. 從朝鮮學者對《公羊》「張三世」、「通三統」學說的存疑，分析康有為倡導時代進步主義的局限。 如同康有為為圓其說，甚至提出劉歆為了欺瞞後世，事先鑄造鐘鼎彝器埋下，驚世駭俗之語般，其所提倡諸多學說亦不乏牽強附會之處，故朝鮮學者亦對「張三世」、「通三統」學說存疑。然朝鮮學者對康有為的批判，實與開化期後的韓國所面臨的近代改革與國家情勢有關。河謙鎭等朝鮮學者或能明白知識份子欲脫離舊有階級桎梏，西學思潮亦為當時潮流，但與儒家思想、五倫綱常牴觸時，便有違其自身理念，故對康有為之說強烈批判。 4. 從朝鮮學者批判漢代《公羊》「春秋新王」、「素王改制」學說，反映他們對康有為變法改革的政治主張所持的不同態度。 經筆者深入研究後，雖未能進一步發現朝鮮學者對此題的批判，但確實發現其對康有為變法改革的關注。原因在於朝鮮晚期與清代晚期同樣面臨列強侵擾，如同康有為想利用變法來救國，朝鮮文人亦想從儒教改革著手，尋求救亡圖存之道。如仿效康有為，於韓國創設的培山書堂，現位於慶尚南道山清郡丹城面培養里中。時至今日，仍每年定期舉辦祭享活動。 5. 從朝鮮學者批判康有為追求「大同」社會理想，分析他們重新詮釋《禮記》的世運嬗變規律。 康有為大同說立基於《禮記》〈禮運〉篇，其中內容之一便是將「不獨親其親，不獨子其子」闡發延伸為「兒童公育主義」。康有為提倡男女同居滿一年需易人，若婦女有孕，則入胎教院，嬰兒一出生旋入育嬰院，用意在於淡化家庭觀念，以達到去私之利。但對恪守儒家五倫思想的朝鮮學者而言，此為違反人倫之想法，如田愚便曾批評之：「渠不過耶穌之家奴，禽獸之同類也。」故此，促使朝鮮學者重新詮釋《禮記》的世運嬗變規律，以應對康有為之說。此外，朝鮮學者對此論題的熱烈迴響，亦可由《韓國禮學叢書》續編中，收錄朝鮮晚期禮經論著近百種獲得旁證。

12611020.label: Major findings and research outcome
12611020.value: 本課題從康有為對朝鮮晚期的儒學影響出發，發現當時的朝鮮學者進入二十世紀的中國有相當深入的了解與接觸。根據研究成果統計，與康有為有直接見面和書信往來的朝鮮晚期學者，有李炳憲、李東祐、朴殷植、李承熙、李忠鎬、朴箕陽等；其他雖無直接見面，而讀過或知悉康有為著作，並對其作專門論述者，有田愚、郭鐘錫、朴文鎬、河謙鎭、金榥等人。可見朝鮮晚期的學者對康有為的關注，並不是單一學術現象，乃具有一定的數量和份量。對於研究朝鮮後期乃至現代韓國儒家經典詮釋的課題，具有相當重要的意義和價值。 延續現代且具有顯著影響的是，康有為於1891年設立萬木草堂，旨在用教育的改革推動政治的改革，李炳憲亦仿效康有為，於韓國創設的培山書堂。經筆者實地考察，從康有為所題匾額、相關碑文看來，此書院確實是在康有為的指導下設立，書堂外亦立有康有為題字之「復原儒教之本山碑」等史料遺跡。內部建築除了文廟，另有道東祠、講堂。該文廟除奉養孔子外，亦是韓國第一個民間設立之文廟，直至今日李氏後孫仍會定期舉行祭祀儀式及相關活動。 (參見〈今文經學在韓國的傳衍：真庵李炳憲與培山書堂〉、〈寒州學派對康有為經學思想的接受與批判〉、〈강유위의 경학사상에 대한 하겸진의 비판(河謙鎮對康有為經學思想的批判)〉、〈周誥殷盤，詰居聱牙——以《尚書》為例的漢文教育方案〉、〈朝鮮時代對《尚書》〈金縢〉的剳疑與化用〉、〈西陂柳僖《尚書》學研究〉。)

12611020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12611020.value: 綜觀中韓學界目前出版的朝鮮儒學史、韓國儒學史等專書論著，往往於高麗末期、朝鮮時代大書特書，論述至朝鮮晚期之儒學，則簡筆帶過，尤其是與近代中國的儒學交涉上幾乎未見。本課題從康有為對朝鮮晚期的儒學影響出發，發現當時的朝鮮學者進入二十世紀的中國有相當深入的了解與接觸，除康有為外，亦對梁啟超亦多有談論。日後持續拓展深究，可彌補韓國儒學史研究上，於朝鮮晚期儒學一塊的缺憾。

12611020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12611020.value: 本計劃通過朝鮮晚期學者與康有為的接觸交流，以及他們對其孔學思想的接受和批判，探討朝鮮半島因為受到康有為學說的影響，導致在中國儒家經典詮釋上出現轉變。無論其立場為欣然接受或嚴厲批判，這個研究課題揭示出朝鮮晚期學者在解讀儒家經典時，已經偏離過去朝鮮王朝五百多年，絕對尊崇朱熹、墨守遵循的學習方式，也帶領我們重新發掘周邊國家在中國儒家經典研究上的獨特視角和重要地位。

12611220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12611220.value: 早期中國哲學與政治背景下的《文子》

12611220.label: Project Objectives
12611220.value: • In the course of the current investigation, I first intend to establish a reliable version of the Dingzhou-Wenzi. It has been recovered in a highly-fragmented state and there is evidence that some of the fragments identified by paleographers as parts of the Wenzi actually belong to other manuscripts from the same tomb (Fech 2012: 41-43). Therefore, a comprehensive comparison between the published Dingzhou manuscripts is in order to exclude material originally not belonging to the Wenzi. This will provide a solid foundation for further scholarship on the Wenzi and other aspects of the Dingzhou discovery. • Secondly, by comparing the Laozi’s exegesis as carried out in the Wenzi and other works, the study attempts to gain insights into the different early interpretive approaches to this “Daoist” classic. Unlike many other early sources, which explicitly reference the Laozi, the Wenzi does not seem to treat this text as an esteemed authoritative canon but rather as a reservoir of textual material the content of which could be unreservedly alternated to make a specific philosophical point (Mukai 2001: 758-760). The Wenzi’s “willful” handling of this source will be examined in the context of other examples of early Laozi exegesis to provide a comprehensive classification of different approaches to the latter. Moreover, this study aims to identify and juxtapose most of the Laozi’s explicit and (the obvious cases of) implicit mentions in the works of the period, to provide a full picture of how often and in what context a particular Laozi passage was used. • Thirdly, the present study will demonstrate how the Wenzi developed the Laozi’s thought to incorporate ideas from a number of works associated with different schools. Among these, the manuscripts Wuxing pian 五行篇 from Mawangdui 馬王堆 (1973) and Guodian 郭店 (1993) appear to be particularly important, as follows from the Wenzi’s main philosophical tenet: a synthesis between the notions of the Way (dao 道) and wen 文, understood as a combination of “virtue” (de 德), “benevolence” (ren 仁), “righteousness” (yi 義) and “propriety” (li 禮). While similar approaches can be found in a number of works (for instance, the Huainanzi), which are also to be investigated, I contend that interpreting “Confucian” moral norms as the necessary preconditions for the existence of things comes very close to Dong Zhongshu’s position (see below). 12611220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12611220.value: The main objective of the current project is the publication of a monograph dealing with the philosophy of the early Chinese treatise Wenzi 文子 or Master Wen. This objective is laid out as a continuation and further elaboration of the PI’s PhD project, which addressed the main linguistic and thematic features of the fragments of the text excavated in Dingzhou 定州 (1973). The main difference from the PI’s previous work on this subject will be the examination of the text’s standpoint in the broader context of Chinese philosophy and politics from the late Zhanguo to early Han times. To this end, it will be compared to transmitted and newly discovered writings of the period with similar philosophical tenets. As previous studies have shown, only the passages of the transmitted Wenzi with parallels in the Dingzhou fragments, particularly the “dialogic” sections of chapter 5, “The Way and Virtue” (Dao de 道德), can be, with some caveats, regarded as authentic (Le Blanc 2000: 83-84; van Els 2018: 82-87). Therefore, all other parts of the textus receptus will be excluded from the analysis. The Wenzi’s connection to other works will be scrutinized from different perspectives. Firstly, I take into consideration the text’s use and interpretation of the Laozi 老子. Here, a comparison will be made to the earliest examples of the Laozi exegesis, such as the Hanfeizi 韓非子, Huangdi sijing 黃帝四經, Huainanzi 淮南子 and others. Secondly, the text’s main philosophical precept, highlighting the notion of wen 文 (civility) as functioning of the Way (dao 道) on the phenomenal level, will be examined in the context of writings with a similar philosophical message, above all, the Huainanzi and the works attributed to Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒. Thirdly, I will also compare the Wenzi to the works featuring Xin Jiran 辛計然, given his identification as the Wenzi’s alleged author, Master Wen. To this end, I focus on extant fragments of the Fanzi Jiran 范子計然, as well as the Yuejue shu 越絕書 and Wu Yue chunqiu 吳越春秋. The current study aims to shed light not only on the early developments of the Daoist intellectual tradition, but also on the interrelation between different philosophical schools in Early China. 本項目旨在研究《文子》的哲學。首先，PI要分析《文子》對《老子》的引用和解釋。其次，本計劃將要研究《文子》對「道」與「文」之間的關係的理解。按照這部書的看法，「文」是「道」的具體表現。為了更好地把握《文子》的理論，本項目也要考慮到 同時代（西漢）其他的思想家對這個問題的看法，尤其是《淮南子》、董仲舒的作品等等。第三，我還將文氏與辛計然的作品進行比較。因為辛計然被看成《文子》的作者。為此，我將重點放在現存的《范子計然》的片段，以及《越絕書》和《吳越春秋》。 本研究的目標不僅在於闡明道家的早期發展，而且在於揭示中國早期不同哲學流派之間的關係。

12611220.label: Major findings and research outcome
12611220.value: The in-depth investigation of the Bamboo-Wenzi validated the initial hypothesis that many fragments of this manuscript have been misattributed, i.e., that they belong to other Dingzhou-texts. The PI identified as many as eighteen bamboo strips which, most likely, were part of the manuscript Liutao (see relevant attachment in Part C). Any study of Dingzhou fragments of the Wenzi and Liutao should take this into consideration. The study shows that the authors of the Wenzi appear to have had at their disposal a version of the Laozi which is closer to the excavated editions (Mawangdui, Beida) than the transmitted Laozi (see relevant attachments in part C). They also pay greater attention to the ideas contained in the “De” part of the latter. In doing so, the Bamboo-Wenzi shows a greater affinity with the Hanfeizi than the Huainanzi. Compared to other works of the period, the Bamboo-Wenzi is unique by not treating the Laozi as an authoritative text but, instead, as the main source for borrowing textual material. In addition to using the Laozi, the authors of the Wenzi appear to have borrowed several important ideas and formulations from Confucian works, such the Wuxingpian and the Xunzi. The resulting synthesis is characteristic of the early Han period but is particularly close to the ideas promoted by Dong Zhongshu. Even though Dong never quotes the Wenzi by name, it is likely that he was influenced by this work. With regard to the appearance of King Ping of Zhou in the Wenzi, the PI has come to the conclusion that this feature reflects the influence of the Chunqiu tradition, which treats this monarch much more positively than the Shijing (in Mao’s interpretation) and most other works. Therefore, for the authors of the Wenzi, this Zhou ruler, most likely, represented a monarch who, after initial difficulties, was able to establish order in All-under-Heaven. King Ping’s reliance on zhuhou in this process might also have motivated his choice as the royal protagonist of the Wenzi, reflecting the political realities of the Western Han. Finally, while the reasons for Master Wen’s association with Jiran may have been manyfold, the almost miraculous turn of fortune for their rulers, King Ping of Zhou and King Goujian of Yue respectively, might have played a role. Once established, this connection proved to be very influential for the interpretation of the Wenzi.

12611220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12611220.value: Some results of this investigation can have a direct impact on the study of the received Wenzi. Namely, the PI argues that Master Wen’s association with Jiran may have played an important role in the transformation of the early Wenzi versions into the transmitted edition. It is a well-known fact that the received Wenzi was composed by borrowing large portions of text from the Huainanzi. Several explanations have been proposed for this phenomenon, but the identity of Master Wen as Jiran has not yet been considered. It is regrettable, because Jiran’s most prominent ideas have clear counterparts in the Huainanzi and its choice as textual source for the new version of the Wenzi may have been motivated by these parallels. Furthermore, Jiran’s ideas regarding the balance of and interaction between yin and yang were possibly at play when the Yijing related materials were included in the new version of the Wenzi. The proposed course of action to validate these hypotheses is to conduct a close comparison of Jiran’s yin-yang thought and the relevant ideas featuring in the transmitted Wenzi.

12611220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12611220.value: This research project deals with an ancient Chinese text, the Wenzi, which is associated with Daoist tradition. An early version of the Wenzi was excavated in Dingzhou in 1973. The official transcription of the excavated manuscript in the journal Wenwu contains several problematic points. One of the important results of this study was to show that up to seven percent of the unearthed Wenzi were attributed to this text erroneously. This calls for a revision of the Wenwu transcription and the creation of a new edition, not only of the Wenzi but of all Dingzhou manuscripts, based on a more thorough comparison of the calligraphic style and physical characteristics of all relevant strips. Furthermore, by investigating several aspects of the work, the study demonstrates that the Wenzi played an important role in the development of the political strand of Daoism. The study also shows how early Daoist lore was developed, modified and combined with notions associated with other traditions to adapt to the political realities of a particular era.

12611420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12611420.value: When the renowned American composer Steven Stucky died in 2016, he left behind a body of creative work—orchestral, chamber, and vocal music, which has yet to be fully assessed. Among the limited number of previous studies of Stucky’s music, most have focused on individual compositions from either analytical or performance practice perspectives. What they lack is a more holistic assessment of Stucky’s compositional style. This proposed research seeks to bridge aspects of the existing analytical and performance practice approaches while addressing the broader style question with a focus on Stucky’s orchestrational technique: a study of the detailed orchestrational choices and patterns that reveal the composer’s timbral palette. The first stage of the project will be devoted solely to Stucky’s Second Concerto for Orchestra, one of his most popular works, which received the Pulitzer Prize in 2005. Allusion to other compositions, in particular twentieth-century masterworks, is an important element of this work. In fact, a number of specific works are cited by Stucky in his program note. The task of the first stage of the project, therefore, will be to “uncover” these direct influences through a series of precise analyses, in order to describe their scope and function and clearly outline the key elements of Stucky’s approach to orchestration in a representative example of his mature work. The second stage of the project will apply these findings to Stucky’s broader orchestral output of approximately two dozen works for full orchestra, spanning 1977 to 2012. By considering the entire output, the goal of the second stage will be to trace the development of Stucky’s orchestrational technique, providing further nuance to the key elements outlined in the first stage of study. In addition to musical analysis, the research will be informed by study of the Steven Stucky Papers at the Library of Congress. The findings of this research will be outlined in two published articles, one for each respective stage and focus of the project. The longer-term goal of the research is to treat these articles and broader findings as a pilot study for a comprehensive monograph on Stucky’s life and work. As this proposed research will be the first to address what is the most essential unanswered question in any future Stucky studies, namely a clear assessment of his style or compositional voice, the project will be influential to composers, theorists, musicologists, performers, and a general music audience. 迄今為此，對於美國作曲家史塔基（1949-2016）的音樂研究還是十分有限。有見及此，本研究將會著重於史塔基的管弦樂編曲法。在計劃的第一部份，將探討史塔基《第二管弦樂協奏曲》內所引用的音樂及其影響，並概述史塔基的管弦樂編曲法。根據第一部份所得的分析及結論，在第二部份，本計劃將延伸至史塔基其餘所有的管弦樂作品。本計劃亦會研究收藏在美國國會圖書館內史塔基曾撰寫的文章。這將是首次對史塔基音樂風格作的研究。最後，本計劃將分成兩份論文發表，相信對作曲家、音樂理論家、音樂學家、演奏家及一般大眾都大有裨益。

13500020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500020.value: 激励在食品供应链中全系统采用区块链技术：一种合作博弈方法

13500020.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13500020.value: Prof Parlar, Mahmut Prof Sosic, Greys

13500020.label: Project Objectives
13500020.value: We will study the adoption of blockchain technology in a three-echelon food supply chain. A number of firms (e.g., Wal-Mart, Carrefour, Nestle, etc.) have joined the IBM Food Trust Blockchain to adopt blockchain technology to improve traceability and transparency in their food supply chains. Blockchain technology is an effective tool to trace the food product flow in real time, and it can be used to help all firms better control food quality and deliver greater transparency to consumers. Its wider application in food supply chains can thus improve consumers' confidence in their purchases. However, for a firm, the adoption of blockchain technology to replace its old information system may be costly. Hence, some firms in a food supply chain may have no incentive to use blockchain technology. It behooves us to explore whether we can incentivize the system-side adoption of blockchain technology. We will analyze the impact of technology adoption on demand as well as wholesale pricing and order decisions. In reality, blockchain technology may benefit a food supply chain in two ways. First, if food deteriorates at a supply chain echelon, then the technology allows downstream firms to instantly identify the deteriorated food and dispose of it prior to processing it. With the adoption of blockchain technology, the downstream firms do not need to waste their production/handling costs on such foods, and the most downstream firm (i.e., retailer) does not absorb any penalty generated due to the sales of deteriorated foods. This means that blockchain technology could help reduce costs in the food supply chain, which is also dependent on the cost of the technology adoption. Secondly, consumers can acquire more information about the food product through the blockchain database, thus ascertaining the food quality prior to buying it from the retailer. The supply chain transparency resulting from the adoption of blockchain technology may increase the consumers' purchase interests. However, the cost of adopting blockchain technology may induce the supply chain members to increase their prices, which usually discourages consumers from shopping at the retail store. The above exposes some critical research questions worth investigating. These questions include, but are not limited to, the impact of blockchain technology on the demand, wholesale pricing decisions, and supply chain profitability as well as the incentives of all firms in a food supply chain to adopt blockchain technology. We will examine whether the supply chain profit can increase as more firms adopt blockchain technology. In this project, we will consider a food supply chain involving a farmer, a manufacturer, and a retailer, who are free to decide whether or not to adopt blockchain technology. A necessary condition for all firms to willingly use the technology is that the system-wide profit can increase with the number of the firms using the technology. This condition is considered because, if more technology adoptions in the supply chain result in a lower system-wide profit, then it is impossible to ensure that every firm gains more from the technology use and has an incentive to adopt the technology. We will use cooperative game theory to obtain a fair allocation of the total profit among all firms that adopt blockchain technology, and compute the corresponding wholesale prices in a food supply chain. Since this project is concerned with the supply chain members' incentives to adopt the technology, cooperative game theory is an effective methodology for our analysis. We will consider all possible scenarios about which firm(s) adopt blockchain technology. For each scenario, we will find optimal decisions and compute each firm's maximum profit. Then, we will use cooperative game theory to obtain a fair allocation of the total profit (resulting from the system-wide technology adoption) among the three firms, which uniquely determines the wholesale prices in the supply chain. That is, the wholesale pricing scheme can be implemented to ensure all firms' willingness to adopt blockchain technology. We will explore which firm has the greatest incentive to adopt blockchain technology. All firms in the food supply chain may obtain different profit surpluses resulting from their adoptions of blockchain technology. A natural question is about which firm benefits the most from the technology adoption and thus has the greatest motivation to use blockchain technology. Our managerial insights for the question can help understand whether a firm at a higher or lower echelon of a food supply chain is more likely to advocate the adoption of blockchain technology.

13500020.label: Realisation of objectives
13500020.value: 1. For objective 1, we considered a three-level food supply chain that involves a farmer, a manufacturer, and a retailer. The manufacturer purchases an agricultural product from the farmer and creates a food product. The manufacturer then sells it to the retailer, who finally sells it to consumers. Each supply chain member can independently decide whether to adopt blockchain technology and makes the decision based on the impact of such an adoption on its profit. When a firm adopts the technology and traces products, its downstream partner and/or consumers can monitor food deterioration at the firm's site. Deteriorated food identified as a result of blockchain technology adoption can be disposed of and thus does not reach consumers, who are typically sensitive to the quality of purchased food products. In this paper, we used cooperative game theory to find the conditions under which all supply chain members have an incentive to adopt the blockchain technology. 2. For objective 2, we considered a demand function that depends both on the retail price and the deterioration rate of food products sold to consumers. We have investigated the impact of technology adoption on the supply chain. We have shown that the retailer traces all products (hence all deteriorated products are removed from the supply chain) if he is charged a sufficiently high penalty when deteriorated products reach consumers. However, for the upstream supply chain members, the tracing decision does not depend just on their own penalty costs; it also depends on the penalty costs of all downstream supply chain members and the processing/production cost of its immediate successor in the supply chain. We find that a firm in the food supply chain is more likely to trace all products at its site if its upstream partners absorb lower penalty costs, but the firm itself and its downstream partners incur higher penalty costs. 3. For objective 3, we found that all the firms have an incentive to jointly adopt blockchain technology if and only if the fixed technology adoption cost is smaller than a pre-determined threshold. Moreover, we proved that the cooperative game always satisfies all conditions for convexity and superadditivity except for v(FR)≥v(F)+v(R). Thus, if adoption of blockchain technology is beneficial for the farmer and the retailer, the game is convex. Thus, we concluded that in an n-level supply chain with n≥3, adoption of technology by non-successive levels may be unstable. That is, supply chain-wide profit may always increase as more firms adopt blockchain technology. 4. For objective 4, we showed that our game always has a non-empty core, but it might not be superadditive or convex, hence the Shapley value might not belong to the core. The center of gravity of the imputation set-based value (CIS-value) is always a core allocation for our game, and it coincides with the nucleolus if and only if the marginal contribution of the upstream supply chain members (the farmer-manufacturer coalition) is not too large. However, the CIS-value cannot always guarantee that each player receives a positive allocation. As a remedy, we proposed the cost-deducted CIS-value (CDCIS-value, for short) that allocates the fixed cost of blockchain technology proportionally among three firms. We showed that the CDCIS-value always belongs to the core and assigns a positive allocation to every player when the supply chain benefits from system-wide technology adoption. We showed that this condition is satisfied rather easily and holds when the fixed cost of the technology is low enough (with a rather high bound). 5. For objective 5, we found that under a system-wide technology adoption, a high penalty cost charged to the manufacturer or farmer is not a necessary condition for the firm to trace all products at its own site. In fact, if both the retailer's penalty cost and the manufacturer's (resp., retailer's) processing costs are sufficiently high, then all the products at the manufacturer's (resp., retailer's) site should be traced. Moreover, the retailer is less likely to trace all products when all firms choose the blockchain technology than when he is the only one doing so. The findings indicate that the manufacturer in the supply chain is likely to have the greatest incentive to adopt the blockchain technology.

13500020.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500020.value: We have analyzed the strategic adoption of the blockchain technology in a three-echelon food supply chain by using a transferable utility coalitional game. Our initial analyses showed that the demand, the rate of good quality products, and the supply chain-wide profit may increase as more firms adopt the blockchain technology. Upper stream members of the supply chain play more important role in the supply chain with the adoption of blockchain technology. We have also found that the core of the food supply chain coalitional game is always non-empty. An allocation scheme that distributes the marginal contribution of the grand coalition evenly among all members is always stable. If and only if the cooperation between the farmer (at the most upstream) and the retailer (at the most downstream) is profitable, the TU coalition game is superadditive and convex. For this research project, we have proposed an initial draft (see, Zhong, Leng, Sošić, and Parlar 2023) and will submit it to a top-tier journal, e.g., Operations Research, Manufacturing & Service Operations Management, and Production and Operations Management. In addition, we identified three similar research projects that are both concerned with the game-theoretic design of incentive schemes for the adoption of a new technology (e.g., electronic vehicles). In the first similar paper entitled “Incentivizing the Adoption of Electric Vehicles under Subsidy Schemes: A Duopoly Analysis” (Gao and Leng 2021), we used game theory to analyze the competition between an electric vehicle manufacturer and an internal combustion vehicle manufacturer under a government's subsidy scheme. This paper was published in Operations Research Letters. In the second similar paper entitled “Incentivizing the Adoption of Electric Vehicles in City Logistics: Pricing, Driving Range, and Usage Decisions under Time Window Policies” (Gao, Leng, Zhang, Liang 2022), we investigate a logistics service provider’s fleet renewal decision. This paper has appeared in International Journal of Production Economics. In the third similar paper entitled “Game-theoretic analysis of trade-in services in closed-loop supply chains” (Quan, Hong, Song, Leng 2021), we developed a two-period model to investigate the trade-in service in a closed-loop supply chain consisting of a manufacturer and a retailer. This paper has appeared in Transportation Research Part E.

13500020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500020.value: In the research project regarding the system-wide adoption of blockchain technology, we considered a three-level supply chain in which each level involves a single firm. As in practice, the farmer and the distributor may sell products to multiple retailers. Accordingly, in future, we will consider such case to analyze a corresponding cooperative game. In addition, there are many farmers or distributors serving a single retailer. It would be interesting to investigate such case using the cooperative game theory.

13500020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500020.value: Blockchain technology can help firms trace products in their supply chains and prevent deteriorated products from flowing downstream and/or reaching consumers, thus improving customer experience and product quality. In this paper, we use cooperative game theory to investigate conditions for strategic adoption of blockchain technology in a three-level food supply chain involving a farmer, a manufacturer, and a retailer. We showed that the supply chain can always benefit from the system-wide adoption of blockchain technology. We also developed an approach for the fair allocation of the system-wide profit among three firms to ensure they have an incentive to use blockchain technology. We developed a cost-relevant concept that ensures a positive profit allocation to each firm whenever the system-wide adoption of blockchain technology benefits the all-firm coalition. We also derived the conditions under which all firms can benefit from such adoption.

13500820.label: Realisation of objectives
13500820.value: The objectives are successfully realized, as evidenced by a publication in Management Science, which is a top-tier academic journal in business and is also in the UTD-24 journal list (i.e., the 24 leading business journals in the database created by The University of Texas, Dallas, Naveen Jindal School of Management). During the process to the publication, issues in all objectives were addressed. For example, we exploit the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)’s announcement of the phase-out of LIBOR as a semi-natural experiment and show that the transition of LIBOR to risk-free rates leads to significant changes in loan contracting, including the price and other non-price terms. We have also discussed related bank behaviors relating to their lending operations. Please refer to the paper as attached in Part C of this report for details.

13500820.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500820.value: We show that loans issued by banks exposed to larger LIBOR transition risk exhibit a significant increase in interest rate spread subsequent to the FCA announcement. This evidence supports the view that borrowers share (at least part of) the risks from LIBOR discontinuation. We find no evidence that borrowing firms’ fundamental risk changes with LIBOR transition, suggesting that the documented loan spread increase is unlikely to be driven by heightened borrower risk. We find that the impact of LIBOR discontinuation on loan spread is weaker if multiple rates are already used in bank funding, if banks are engaged in relationship lending, and if banks operate in a more competitive loan market. These findings are consistent with the cushioning effect of a multireference scheme, the reduced information asymmetry and renegotiation cost in relationship lending facilitating LIBOR transition, and the market competition pressure hindering the risk-transferring mechanism, respectively. We also find that after the FCA announcement of LIBOR discontinuation, LIBOR-referenced loans are more likely to include collateral and covenant requirements. These results imply that banks proactively secure collateral protection for potential losses (especially during distress when RFRs are likely pressured downward) and enhance the flexibility of loan renegotiation during the process of a benchmark rate change. Lastly, we examine banks’ switch from LIBOR to alternative non-LIBOR benchmarking and find that they increase the use of non-LIBOR reference rates in loan contracts following the announcement of the LIBOR phase-out. We interpret this outcome as banks’ understanding the evolution of the system to replace LIBOR as an outlet for addressing the problem of LIBOR transition.

13500820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500820.value: As pointed out in our paper published in Management Science, our results call for regulators to acknowledge the importance of securing a resilient, workable new benchmarking system that has minimal burdens on market participants if the LIBOR transition to RFRs warps normal bank loan pricing behaviors. Switching from LIBOR to replacement benchmarks is likely to move banking behaviors to a new equilibrium, and our study can serve as an inference for and path to that equilibrium. Such a new equilibrium is of vital importance because the influences of banking behaviors are not confined to their loan operations—they also include the intensive connections between banks and borrowing firms because bank funds are an important source for firms to finance their projects. The change in the cost of bank funds is likely to have non-trivial impacts on business activities of the whole economy. Future research could examine how LIBOR discontinuation and the induced enhancement in bank funding costs actually change business activities such as corporate financing decisions and firms’ engagement in hedging behaviors in the derivatives markets.

13500820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500820.value: Business transactions, especially those related to borrowing and lending, require a benchmark interest rate to facilitate the setting of the credit cost. LIBOR used to be the most important benchmark rate across the globe. However, LIBOR was also manipulated by several large banks, which led the regulators to decide to gradually abandon LIBOR starting from 2017. Different jurisdictions have introduced various alternative rates to replace LIBOR, but these rates lack the viability of LIBOR in facilitating business transactions. We find that transitioning away from LIBOR to alternative benchmark rates makes bank loans more expensive, that is, borrowers have to pay a larger amount of interest to banks. Firms also have to set aside more collaterals and face more restrictions when they borrow from banks after LIBOR was transitioned to alternative rates. To the extent that LIBOR discontinuation imposes costs to banks, our findings suggest that banks transfer at least part of these costs to borrowers.

13600720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13600720.value: This project seeks to investigate how young women understand and experience intimacy in the age of social media. Specifically, it looks at negotiations around the institutions of family, marriage, and tertiary education, all three of which appear to be undergoing profound transformation due to digital mediation. It will carry out a multi-sited study of young university-going women in four cities: Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Singapore, and Bangalore, chosen for their high percentage of social media usage in Asia among women in the 18-24 age group.. It will focus on three aspects of social media, namely microblogging, file-sharing and services (eg., provided by dating apps such as Tinder, Tantan, Bumble), as well as on communicative media (eg., WeChat, WhatsApp, Instagram), deploying in-depth, qualitative methodologies to generate rich site-specific data. 1. Using a qualitative ethnographic approach, the project will track 120 women (30 in each of the 4 locations) over 24 months to throw new light on emerging practices of digital intimacy, with specific reference to how young, college-going women cultivate a digital persona of their selves, and how such personae forge new ways of negotiating and navigating the realms of (a) courtship/marriage, (b) kinship/family and (c) tertiary education. 2. Such data will provide insight into whether and how new forms of intimacy and self-representation are transforming key social institutions of marriage, kinship and tertiary education in Asia. 3. The project investigates whether digital platforms create behavioural uniformity or whether there is local variance in the ways such platforms are used. Specifically, do diverse local cultural histories impact digital habits? Do different conditions of access, across contexts, impact digital use? Do different legal and technological restrictions (e.g. firewalls) that create new conditions for innovation (hacking/bypassing/jumping) also have social consequences? Such local variance poses new challenges for understanding how apparently universally applicable platforms such as Facebook, Pinterest, Instagram and Google Hangouts, as well as Asian variants (WeChat, Weibo, Viber, Kik, Kakao), actually work within diverse contexts. 4. The study expects to contribute to an expanding literature, across cultural studies, anthropology and media studies, that highlights the role and importance of young women and their digital technology use for understanding how social institutions are changing.

13600720.label: Realisation of objectives
13600720.value: With the launching of the project in January 2021, the research team achieved all the original proposed key project objectives for this study. During the duration of this project, the major challenge was a change of Principal Investigator as Tejaswini Niranjana left Lingnan University for a new position at Ahmedabad University on August 15, 2021. She remains as a Co-PI for this project. Denise Tse-Shang Tang became the PI as a result. In order to coordinate and manage a multi-site ethnographic study, the entire research team met frequently online and offline to review literature, to discuss ongoing methodological issues, to refine the conceptual framework and to present at international conferences. Experienced research assistants were hired in Bangalore, Hong Kong and Singapore to assist with literature review, participant recruitment and fieldwork interviews in respective sites. Chinmayi Ramaiah (India), Man Yin Chung (Hong Kong) Farah Bawany and Chau Kam Sing (Singapore) joined our team as research assistants (RAs), under supervision of PI & Co-PIs in various locations. Research assistants attended training sessions on literature review and methodology facilitated by the PI and Co-Is. They conducted literature review on digital communication, intimate relationships, dating apps and digital subcultures, as well as participated in fieldwork interviews. The research assistants also took turns as moderators of the Digital Intimacy mini-symposium series. A quantitative summary of research activities is listed with details to follow in this report: • 2 research methodology training workshops on July 16 & 17, 2021 and 2-day writing workshop on April 29 & 30, 2022 (Project Objectives 2 & 3) • 120 interviews have already been conducted with 30 interviews in each research site. Participants were recruited through snowballing method, social media sites and references from faculty members from various educational institutions in the city. (Project Objectives 1, 2 & 4) • 9 international conference and workshop presentations attended and presented by the research team. • 6 Digital Intimacy mini-symposiums organized by the research team. (Project Objectives 3 & 4) • 1 journal article and 1 book chapter published. One meeting with the National University of Singapore press on potential book publication in April 2024 (Project Objective 4). This project is grounded in in-depth qualitative interview practices in each of the four sites. Each site recruited 30 informants (an adequate qualitative sample size for comparative analysis) for conducting interviews and for tracking digital technology use. A team of research assistants in each site contacted interviewees, conducted the interviews, and fully transcribed and translated them into English from the relevant languages. Since the demographic in all 4 cities is young women in universities, and tertiary education is mandated to be in English in India, Singapore and Hong Kong, most interviewees spoke in English. But because closeness and intimacy are often manifested in the mother tongue rather than in the language of higher education, interviewees sometimes switched from English to a local language. These languages include Kannada, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam in Bangalore; Cantonese, Mandarin, and English in Guangzhou; Cantonese, Mandarin, and English in Hong Kong; and English, Malay, Tamil, Mandarin, and Chinese dialects in Singapore. Working closely with our PI & Co-Is, research assistants in each location recruited informants within college and university contexts, collected information about app usage, and conducted in-depth interviews. The interviews were semi-structured and open ended and lasted from two to three hours each. Some interviews happened across multiple occasions. During the process of conducting interviews, throughout the process of transcribing, coding and data analysis, we met online regularly to discuss and share data and analysis between research assistants and Co-I in each specific site, as well as meeting online with the entire research team. Questions were also modified and transformed in response to cross-site conversations our research team had. In these ways, while located within sites and drawing on the expertise and language skills of researchers very much grounded in one site, the project generated cross-site and comparative conversations at every stage in the research process. This generated new questions for each site. These meetings facilitated data analysis and writing across the sites. In addition to the in-depth, qualitative interviews and digital technology use, we also collected documentary and media materials that mapped the digital ecologies of each city. Apart from online meetings, the research team also attended and participated in the following international conferences and seminars: Inter-Asia Cultural Studies Summer School at University of the Philippines Diliman (August 2024), Global Digital Intimacies at the University of Amsterdam (June 27 & 28, 2024), Symposium at National University of Singapore (April 8, 2024), Inter-Asia Cultural Studies Society Conference at Ahmedabad University (2023) and National University of Singapore (2021), International Summer Workshop on Social Inclusion in the Digital Era: Social Activism and Youth Wellbeing (July 24, 2023), International Master’s Program in Inter-Asia Cultural Studies at National Central University Taiwan (February 6, 2023), seminars at Lingnan University (June 1, 2023 & June 3, 2024). Each conference presentation or talk marked a significant stage and research progress in our multi-site ethnographic study. As an Inter-Asia project, we organized webinars by pulling in researchers in the region who shared their empirical and theoretical formulations with our research team and wider audiences through a series of symposia. These webinars generated a shared collaborative intellectual space for researchers, research assistants and a wider audience to engage the project and generated much cross-fertilization between the qualitative research process and wider engagements with digitality in the region. These symposia were crucial for situating our project within on-going research not only through the traditional means of conducting literature reviews of existing, already published research generally, but also generated a more dynamic process with researchers, activists and writers situated in the region engaged in affiliated and adjacent research and writing projects. We logged in over 500 registered participants with an average of 60 actual participants at each mini-symposium. 13600720.label: Major findings and research outcome
13600720.value: Digital mediations of everyday life in Asian contexts must be situated within regimes of liberalisation and the deepening of consumer culture which is spawning all kinds of value transformations, potential selves and futures to normalise aspiration as a form of social belonging, with female selves in particular being re-made as aspiring individuals. How do the newer cultural practices around the digital relate to longer histories that entwine gender and sexuality with constructions of nation and modernity in Asia? The present-day context of digital mediation is undergirded by processes of social transformation that unfurled as societies worldwide became modern from the nineteenth century onwards. While this was indeed a worldwide process, the specific emergence of modernity within Asian contexts helps us better understand the contemporary dynamics of digital mediation. These dynamics are both similar and different across Guangzhou, Bangalore, Singapore and Hong Kong, the sites that our project examines. Drawing out trajectories of modernity and the constitutive role of gender and sexuality in their formations provides a crucial frame for understanding the contemporary transformations that continue to shape and reshape these locations. 19th and early 20th century debates around culture, tradition, women and modernity in our four locations intersect with the formation of 'national' identities. Our contention is that the specific and dense historical trajectories we investigate are crucial for understanding how the digital is experienced by the young women at the centre of our project.

13600720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13600720.value: We are in the midst of writing up our book publication for this project. The PI and Co-Is are responsible for writing up the chapter for each specific field research site. The entire book manuscript is overseen by the first PI of this study, Tejaswini Niranjana and Ritty Lukose. As a research team, we have all met with the publisher of National University of Singapore Press to discuss book proposal development. We are also considering other university press publishers including Duke University Press as both Niranjana and Lukose have published with them before.

13600720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13600720.value: Recent technological upheavals, including the embedding of social media and the advent of generative AI, have radically altered young women’s understanding and experience of intimacy. This three-year, multi-sited qualitative and ethnographic study of young university-going women in four cities: Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Singapore, and Bangalore, examines how young women negotiate the institutions of family, marriage, and tertiary education which have undergone profound transformation due to digital mediation. How do young women understand and experience intimacy in the age of social media? What impact do these digital experiences and understanding of intimacy have on how millennial subjects experience, understand, and negotiate social relations in globalising Asia? Our findings thus far suggest that social institutions such as family and marriage are being redefined through digital mediation in aspects including boundary-drawing, creating zones of intimacy, and the reconfiguration of relationships in the digital domain.

13601020.label: Project Objectives
13601020.value: Develop a theoretical tractable model for assessing the strategic effects and antitrust implications of a dominant firm’s adoption of “market-share contracts,” which involve “market-share discounts.” Solve the dominant firm's optimization problem with market-share discounts, taking into account the responses of competitors, through the equilibrium analysis of game theory. Examine the qualitative features of the dominant firm's profit-maximizing solution. For example, under what circumstances (in terms of degree of dominance or degree of substitutability between competing products, for example) can a dominant firm facing smaller competitors raise its profits by adopting market-share contracts, relative to using simple linear pricing? Under what circumstances is an exclusive contract (which is an extreme form of market-share contracts) optimal for the dominant firm? Examine how the adoption of market-share discounts affects industry efficiency, the dominant firm's profits, competitors' profits, downstream firms' profits, and consumer welfare, by comparing the equilibria with and without the adoption of market-share discounts. Conduct the comparative statics analysis for the above variables on the changes of the degree of dominance and the degree of substitutability between the dominant firm's and its competitors' products. Complement the above qualitative analyses with numerical simulations. Provide policy suggestions on how to regulate the use of market-share discounts and exclusive contracts in intermediate-goods markets.

13601020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601020.value: In many recent antitrust cases in the U.S., Europe, Canada, and China, a dominant upstream supplier in an intermediate-goods market is alleged to have used conditional pricing practices (CCP) with its downstream buyers to fully or partially exclude its rival firm(s). The plaintiffs claimed that such practices had harmed competition and consumer welfare. The use of CCP by dominant firms in intermediate-goods markets and the resulting concerns of abuse of dominance have become prominent antitrust issues. In this project, the strategic effects and antitrust implications of a dominant firm’s CCP will be examined, with a focus on “market-share contracts.” These involve “market-share discounts,” with which the buyer can enjoy certain discounts, provided the firm’s share of the buyer's total purchases exceeds specific thresholds (i.e., discounts conditional on market share). More specifically, the baseline model we plan to study is a duopoly price competition game with the following timing. First, a firm, known as the dominant firm, offers its pricing scheme with market-share discounts; second, another competing firm offers its price; and third, a downstream buyer chooses her purchases from the two firms. The products of the two competing upstream firms may be perfect or imperfect substitutes; the dominant firm may enjoy a cost advantage over the second-mover firm, and the second-mover firm may be capacity constrained. Our three main objectives are first to understand how a dominant firm, facing smaller competitors, should optimally design a market-share contract; second, to assess the impact of the adoption of market-share contracts on competitors, downstream buyers, consumers, industry efficiency, and social efficiency; and third, to shed lights on antitrust cases and competition policies and regulations. This study contributes to the literature on nonlinear pricing with competition between asymmetric firms. Most previous studies in this literature focused on the adoption of pricing contracts referencing only own sales. However, market-share contracts, which reference not only own sales but also rivals' sales, have been observed in many recent antitrust cases. Intuitively, market-share contracts appear to be more exclusionary and anti-competitive than contracts only referencing own sales. It is important to deepen our understanding on the impact of exclusionary contracts by formally studying how the equilibrium outcome qualitatively and quantitatively changes when a dominant firm adopts market-share discounts. This project will therefore benefit not only academia but also antitrust policymakers and practitioners, consumers, and the economy in general. 在中國、美國、加拿大和歐洲等地近期發生的反托拉斯案件中，有許多案例牽涉到一個在中間產品市場中占主導地位的上游供應商對其下游買家使用某種條件定價，其目的據稱是完全或部分排除其競爭對手。案件中的原告聲稱這些定價方式損害了市場競爭和消費者福利。因此，中間產品市場主導企業採用條件定價，以及由此引起的濫用市場支配地位的潛在問題已經成為反托拉斯領域中的重要課題。 本項目將集中研究一類條件定價方式：市場份額合約。所謂「市場份額合約」，意思是：該合約規定，在某時期內，如果簽約的買方於簽約的賣方中的購買額達到買方在該時期內的購買總額中的某個預定份額，則該賣方將給予該買方一定的「市場份額折扣」（即，以市場份額作為折扣的條件）。我們將研究主導企業所採用的市場份額合約在反托拉斯層面上的影響。更具體地說，我們將研究一類價格競爭博弈，其基準模型可簡述如下：首先，企業甲（主導企業）提出其市場份額合約；然後，企業乙（競爭對手）提出其價格；第三，下游買家選擇從兩家企業的購買額。在上述模型中，企業甲和企業乙的產品可能是完美的替代品，也可能是不完美的替代品；企業甲可能比企業乙享有成本優勢；企業乙可能有產能限制。 我們的主要目標有三個方面：第一，了解主導企業，當面對較小競爭者時，應如何設計最優市場份額合約；第二，了解市場份額合約的採用對競爭者、下游買家、消費者、行業效率和社會效率的影響；第三，為市場競爭政策和法規提出建議。 本研究將為非對稱競爭下的非線性定價的文獻作出貢獻。該文獻中以前的大多數研究集中在僅參考自己的銷售的定價合約上。但是，市場份額合約不僅參考自己的銷售而且還參考競爭對手的銷售。直觀地講，與僅參考自己的銷售的合約相比，市場份額合約通常被認為更具有排他性和反競爭性。通過研究市場份額合約使市場均衡產生甚麼變化，以加深我們對這類排他性合約帶來的影響的理解，是很有重要性的。因此，本項目不僅將使學術界受益，還將為反托拉斯政策制定者和從業人員、消費者以及經濟效率帶來益處。

13601020.label: Realisation of objectives
13601020.value: Objective 1 (model building): We have developed a game-theoretic model in which a dominant upstream firm, competing with a minor firm, optimally designs a market-share contract to its downstream buyer. Each of the two firms can produce a product at a unit cost. These two products are differentiated imperfect substitutes. The buyer has a gross utility/revenue function over the two products. The three parties play the following three-stage game. First, the dominant firm offers a market-share contract (MSC) with a per-unit price for its product and a required minimum market share. Second, after observing the MSC, the minor firm offers a per-unit price for its product. Third, after observing both firms’ offers, the buyer decides how many units to purchase from the two firms, subject to the constraint that the share of her purchase from the dominant firm needs to satisfy the required minimum market share set by the dominant firm, or her purchase from the dominant firm being zero. Such zero-purchase is interpreted as that the buyer rejects the MSC contract. Our equilibrium concept is pure strategy subgame perfect equilibrium. In other words, we look for firm 1's optimal MSC, taking into account the minor firm's and the buyer's reactions in sequence. Objective 2 (model solving): In our working paper entitled “Market-Share Contracts by a Dominant Firm”, we first analyze the dominant firm's optimization problem contingent on an arbitrary minimum market-share threshold and characterize the resulting contingent optimal price for the dominant firm, taking into account the equilibrium in the subgames. This in particular includes the special cases of optimizing over exclusive contracts and optimizing over linear pricing. Then we proceed to optimize over the choice of the minimum market-share threshold to solve, and prove existence of, the fully optimal MSC for the dominant firm. As a result, the equilibrium outcome, in particular the dominant firm's optimal MSC, is characterized as the solution of a nonlinear programming problem. We prove a set of theoretical results that apply for our model with the general demand. Using the graphical tools we develop along the way, the fully optimal MSC and its existence are visualized by a set of nice diagrams. In order to derive explicit solution and provide further intuitions and insights, we also study a more specific linear demand model, in which the buyer's utility is quadratic, with two demand-size parameters (one for each firm) and a product substitutability parameter. We also provide a set of clear-cut results and numerical simulations that apply for this more specific linear demand model. Objective 3 (qualitative features of solution): We show that the equilibrium outcome can be linked to two economic factors: the degree of product substitutability between the two firms and the competitive advantage of the dominant firm. Here our definition of the degree of competitive advantage is based on the relative magnitudes of the maximum surpluses generated by the firm’s product alone and by its rival’s product alone, and so it depends on both the cost advantage and the product superiority of a firm. (In the original project proposal, the degree of competitive advantage is called “the degree of dominance”.) For any given degree of product substitutability, the full-exclusivity contract arises in equilibrium when the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is significant, and less-than-100% MSC is optimal for the dominant firm when its competitive advantage is moderate. On the other hand, when the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is small, the equilibrium outcome involves simple linear pricing. Moreover, the larger the degree of product substitutability, the larger the dominant firm's competitive advantage is required to justify the exclusivity. Objective 4 (impact of market-share contracts): We provide welfare implications of MSCs as compared to a benchmark of linear pricing. First, when it is optimal for the dominant firm to adopt a partial or full-exclusivity contract over linear pricing, its profit is clearly improved, and this is at the expense of its rival if the rival firm is able to make a positive profit under linear pricing. Second, when the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is strong, for any degree of product substitutability, the adoption of a partial or full-exclusivity contract reduces the buyer’s surplus. However, when the dominant firm has some competitive advantage but it is not strong, the buyer can benefit from partial or full-exclusive contracts if the degree of product substitutability is moderate. Third, the ranking of the total surplus associated with the adoption of MSC over linear pricing is similar to the ranking of the buyer’s surplus, except for different thresholds. That is, for any degree of product substitutability, when the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is strong, the adoption of a partial or full-exclusivity contract reduces the total surplus. On the other hand, when the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is not so strong and the degree of product substitutability is moderate, the emergence of MSC enhances the total surplus. Objective 5 (comparative statics): We find that when the degree of competitive advantage of the dominant firm increases, the dominant firm's market share, output level, and profit level increase, while the minor firm's market share, output level, and profit level decrease. The comparative statics results with respect to product substitutability and the welfare effect of competitive advantage are not clear-cut and are omitted here. Objective 6 (numerical simulations): We conducted numerical simulations based on the “quadratic utility model”. Details are omitted here. Objective 7 (policy suggestions): Our analysis offers two insights for antitrust investigations into exclusive and market-share contracts practiced by dominant firms. The first is that when the dominant firm has a strong competitive advantage in terms of either cost efficiency or product superiority, or both, it is more likely to adopt exclusive contracts, full or partial-exclusivity, and such a contractual practice tends to hurt its rival’s profits, the buyer’s surplus and total surplus. The second insight of our analysis illustrates a tradeoff between the degree of product substitutability and the extent of competitive advantage of the dominant firm. When the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is moderate, the degree of product substitutability plays a crucial role in welfare comparison, and in such situations, exclusive contracts can be welfare-enhancing over linear pricing (in terms of both the buyer’s surplus and total surplus). Since the parameters of the demand system (demand sizes and product substitutability parameter) can be estimated if relevant data are available, these thresholds of the competitive advantage required for welfare inferences can then be computed, once we have estimates of the costs of the two firms. In other words, instead of banning full or partial exclusive contracts used by a dominant firm, antitrust regulators should look for information that would help quantifying the degree of product substitutability and competitive advantage of the dominant firm.

13601020.label: Major findings and research outcome
13601020.value: Our study provides an explanation for the emergence of market-share contracts in intermediate goods markets. When a dominant firm in the market has a strong competitive advantage in terms of either cost efficiency or product superiority, or both, it is more likely to adopt exclusive contracts, full or partial-exclusivity, and such a contractual practice tends to hurt its rival’s profits, the buyer’s surplus and total surplus. Our analysis also illustrates a tradeoff between the degree of product substitutability and the extent of competitive advantage of the dominant firm. When the competitive advantage of the dominant firm is moderate, the degree of product substitutability plays a crucial role in welfare comparison, and in such situations, exclusive contracts can be welfare-enhancing over linear pricing (in terms of both the buyer’s surplus and total surplus). Instead of banning full or partial exclusive contracts used by a dominant firm, antitrust regulators should look for information that would help quantifying the degree of product substitutability and competitive advantage of the dominant firm. Our findings have been presented in seven international conferences specialized in industrial economics and competition policy (listed in Part C). And, there is one more coming conference, CRESSE 2024 18th International Conference on Competition and Regulation (Advances in the Analysis of Competition Policy and Regulation), scheduled in July 2024, Chania, Crete, Greece, in which our findings will be presented. Those conferences are participated by not only scholars but also antitrust/competition policy practitioners. Except for the aforementioned international conferences, our findings have also been presented in a number of seminars in universities/research institutes, including Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Tsinghua University, University of Southern California, The Chinese University of Hong Kong Shenzhen, University of California Riverside, and Academia Sinica. This project also results in a working paper entitled “Market-Share Contracts by a Dominant Firm”. An earlier version of the paper is publicly available in the repository of the International Industrial Organization Conference website. The latest version of the paper is available on the PI's personal research webpage. It is also to be submitted to a top-tier academic journal for publication.

13601020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13601020.value: In the current project we focus on a simple class of market-share contracts, which specifies a per-unit price conditional on the share of the buyer's purchase from the dominant firm as a fraction of the total purchase satisfying a minimum threshold. As a further development, we may consider an alternative model in which the dominant firm is allowed to use a more general form of contracts. For example, the dominant firm can be assumed to be able to offer a nonlinear tariff to the buyer, under which the buyer's payment may be contingent on the purchase volumes of the buyer not only from the dominant firm but also from other competing firms. In this type of settings, we may ask similar questions that we asked in the current project: How is the dominant firm's optimal contract determined? What are the qualitative features of the optimal contract? What are its implications for industry efficiency, social efficiency, consumer welfare, and competitors' profits?

13601020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13601020.value: A variety of supply contracts are observed in business environments. Instead of offering per-unit prices, companies often specify payments conditional on the number of units of the products to be purchased by their buyers. One extreme form of such requirements is an exclusivity contract in which a buyer is required to purchase exclusively from the supplier. Other contracts involve partial exclusivity in the sense that the buyers are required to purchase a minimum fraction of their needs from the supplier. Such contracts have been used by many suppliers, including Intel, Alibaba, and other prominent companies. We study business justifications for a dominant supplier to adopt full-exclusivity or partial-exclusivity contracts and government policy implications of these conditional pricing practices. We find that the emergence of full-exclusivity or partial-exclusivity depends on a tradeoff between the degree of product differentiation between the dominant firm and its competitor and the relative strength of the dominant supplier. For any degree of product differentiation, a full-exclusivity contract arises when the relative strength of the dominant supplier is significant, and a partial-exclusivity contract is optimal for the dominant supplier when its relative strength is moderate. We offer government policy recommendations on how to regulate these exclusivity contracts.

13601920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601920.value: Given the shortage of living space, why do people buy what they buy, and where do they keep them? How do they decide what to get rid of, and by what means? How are these decisions and practices related to family dynamics? This research examines the relationship between consumerism and sustainable consumption in Hong Kong, whose unique socio-spatial context makes for an interesting study. Like all global cities, consumerism is a way of life in Hong Kong and most people live in small, expensive apartments. Sustainable consumption is an issue that ranks high on the global agenda, but compared to other global cities, Hong Kong’s severe lack of sustainable waste treatment options means that waste reduction and effective recycling are urgent social issues. This study investigates two relatively neglected areas in the sociology of consumption – spatial materiality and relational embeddedness. Firstly, little is known about how the placement and storage of consumer goods are related to domestic spaces and disposal practices. These issues are very likely heightened in Hong Kong given its highly developed consumer culture and the shortage of living space. Secondly, most studies on consumption rely on a conception of consumers as rational individuals, when many consumption decisions and practices are in fact relationally embedded. In Hong Kong, where family co-residence is the norm, the mutually constitutive relationship between the family and consumption practices is particularly relevant. Based on the above, a mixed methods study (questionnaire survey plus visual ethnography) will be used to address three research objectives: (1) To identify factors shaping the purchase, placement/storage and disposal decisions and practices of non-depletable consumer goods by typical Hong Kong families; (2) to analyse these factors in terms of consumer culture, family relational dynamics and domestic space utilisation; and (3) to delineate implications of the above for domestic waste treatment and sustainable consumption policies and practices in high-density urban contexts. Actor-Network Theory will inform the conceptual framework for this study. Our findings will enrich the literature on consumption by contributing to the neglected areas of spatial materiality and relational embeddedness, and will also help advocates and policy makers better understand consumers’ decisions and practices of buying, keeping and throwing in the context of limited home space. Last but not least, findings can inform the formulation of public education and policy initiatives that enhance sustainable consumption in urban contexts. 在缺乏生活空間的情況下，人們如何決定購買什麼東西和把它們存放在哪裡？是如何決定棄掉物件，及用什麼方式棄掉？這些決定和做法與家庭動態又有何關係？本研究的主題是消費主義與可持續消費之間的關係，而香港獨特的社會空間背景是我們選擇它為研究地點的原因。像其他全球城市一樣，消費主義是香港重要的生活方式之一，而多數人住在昂貴但細小的公寓。可持續消費是全球議程上的重要事項，但與其他全球城市相比，香港嚴重缺乏可持續處理廢物的方案，令減少廢物和有效回收成為迫切的社會問題。這項研究針對消費社會學中兩個相對被忽視的領域–空間物質性和關係嵌入性。首先，我們對人們如何放置和存儲消費品與家居空間和棄掉消費品方法之間的關係所知甚少。香港高度發達的消費文化和居住空間的短缺更加令這些問題的加劇。第二，大多數消費研究都假設消費者是理性的個體，但事實上許多消費決策和實踐是嵌於關系內的。香港大部分人與家人同住，所以家庭與消費實踐的相互構成尤為重要。基於以上所述，本研究將使用混合方法研究（問卷調查和視覺民族志）處理三個研究目標：（1）確定哪些因素影響典型香港家庭購買，存儲和處置不易腐爛消費品的決定和做法；（2）從消費文化，家庭關係動態和家庭空間利用分析這些因素；（3）分析上述內容對高密度城市家居廢物處理及可持續消費政策與實踐的影響。消費者文化理論和行動者網絡理論將為這項研究提供概念框架。研究成果將可彌補現實消費文獻對空間和關係嵌入性的忽視，也可以幫助倡議者和政策制定者了解消費者在有限的家居空間前提下對購買，存放和棄掉消費品的決策和實踐。研究結果也會為都市可持續消費的公共教育和政策提供有用的資訊。

13602120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13602120.value: 二戰後的駐華美兵與中國社會

13602120.label: Project Objectives
13602120.value: Examine the roles of sociocultural elements in causing frictions between American soldiers and Chinese society between 1945 and 1949, and how grassroots interactions affected national politics and international relations. Using new archival sources, my project will examine how local and individual agents such as rickshaw pullers, dance girls, college students, traffic police, shop owners, coolie laborers, and local gangsters actively interacted with American soldiers in their daily lives and shaped national politics through collective appeals, strikes, and demonstrations. It will also analyze how differences in legal systems, cultural misunderstanding, and mutual biases based on race, gender, and class contributed to the increasing frictions and their (mis)interpretations. This project will complicate existing studies of Cold War history and Sino-U.S. relations by showing the crucial roles that sociocultural elements played in causing Sino-U.S. tensions. It will also expand the study of the American military overseas by adding the history of American soldiers’ interactions with Chinese civilians in the 1940s, a largely forgotten chapter in the existing scholarship on the American empire. Analyze the watershed in Chinese perceptions of America between 1945 and 1949, the critical moment in Sino-U.S. history when the peak positive image of war-time allies rapidly declined. 13602120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13602120.value: Between 1945 and 1949, up to 113,000 U.S. servicemen were stationed in China for various missions from repatriating Japanese soldiers and civilians to maintaining peace in the resuming Civil War. This large-scale interaction between Chinese and American individuals was unprecedented in Sino-U.S. history and drastically transformed Chinese perceptions of America. Soon after the American soldiers’ arrival, frequent incidents started to occur in major cities: a rickshaw puller in Qingdao was beaten to death by two drunk U.S. sailors, a Shanghai student was shot by Military Police for wearing U.S. military pants, and a Peking University student was raped by two Marines in downtown Beijing. These incidents led to a radical change in dominant Chinese perceptions of America, from a liberator to an imperialist aggressor. Hundreds of demonstrations called “anti-atrocity movements” broke out over what appeared to be isolated incidents of physical and sexual violence toward Chinese civilians. Protestors called for the complete withdrawal of the U.S. military from China. The new anti-American movement and rhetoric had a long-term impact on the construction of Chinese nationalism to the present. This project will be the first comprehensive sociocultural history of American servicemen in China from the end of World War II to the founding of the People’s Republic of China. Traditional Cold War historiography largely examines anti-Americanism in terms of ideological conflicts and political struggles, focusing on diplomatic, military, and political histories. The existing scholarship on Sino-U.S. relations tends to attribute Chinese anti-American sentiments to Communist propaganda alone. In contrast, this project will focus more on the roles that sociocultural elements played in causing such tensions, and how local and individual interactions affected national politics and international relations. Furthermore, my study positions Sino-U.S. frictions more broadly in the global context of American occupation, conflict over sovereignty, capitalist consumption, and Westernization. In addition to Communist propaganda and political manipulations, my working hypothesis is that Chinese grievances caused by American servicemen’s misbehaviors and the rising social tensions concerning race, gender, and class fueled anti-American sentiment across a broad range of urban elites. Conflicts over territoriality, actual or imagined, led to clashes between American GIs and Chinese society. The research will deepen our understanding of Sino-U.S. relations and the Chinese Civil War period, and expand the existing research on the American military overseas. 1945至1949年間，駐華美軍達到了歷史最高點的十一萬三千人。如此大規模和深度的個體互動，在中美交往史上實屬首次。可以說，駐華美軍一定程度上改變了二戰後中國城市的地理面貌和當地居民的心理圖景。美軍與中國草根社會的直接交往給當時的中美關係帶來了深遠的影響，它不僅直接導致了普通市民和左翼知識份子“從友邦到仇敵”的美國觀的轉變，同時也深刻影響了美國人對中國的理解和想像。駐華美軍關乎中國史，也關乎美國史，更是一個全球史的題目。本研究將駐華美兵與中國社會的關係置於美軍全球駐紮這一大歷史的背景下重新審視，著重分析種族、性別和階級等社會文化因素怎樣影響了這段複雜的交往史，並試圖揭示實際與觀念的領土與主權是如何成為此時中美衝突的核心。

13602120.label: Realisation of objectives
13602120.value: All of the objectives have been achieved. During the period of the grant, I have done extensive archival research into official, popular, and personal sources to examine the sensorial, material, and symbolic exchanges between GIs and Chinese civilians, such as rickshaw coolies, “Jeep girls,” suspected thieves, and black-market dealers and customers. I examined and engaged with both American and Chinese sources deeply and critically to interpret the complex linguistic, social, and legal exchanges and manipulations, shaped by local and global knowledge, cultural beliefs, and mutual prejudices. Archival materials include a large collection of incident reports, local negotiations, diplomatic correspondence, government instructions, intelligence reports, and court-martial records. Newspapers, both broadsheets and tabloids, journals, and military guides provide information on popular views, propaganda efforts, and transpacific networks of cultural production. Published and unpublished memoirs and oral history records enrich the available information on individual experiences, complementing official and popular sources.
