13602120.label: Major findings and research outcome
13602120.value: This project sheds light on the complicated history of grassroots U.S.–China interactions in the late 1940s that mixed military occupation, economic expansion, imperialist aggressions, nationalist assertions, fear of Communism, and everyday struggles, mundane resistance, quotidian desires, and hopes for new beginnings. It provides comparative insights into the workings and impacts of American empire by adding the uniquely complex case of China. Similar power asymmetries were embedded in Sino-U.S. interactions at the national and individual levels. Racial, sexual, and national prejudices similar to those found in occupied Japan and Korea permeated GIs’ everyday lives in China. But unlike occupied former enemies, China was a U.S. ally, and GIs were officially “invited guests” of the nation. U.S. troops were located in the very center of Chinese cities rather than in separate camp towns, and no black units were allowed after the war, thanks to the Nationalist government’s racist restrictions. In the contentious environment of the civil war and the early Cold War, the American government promoted a liberal image of itself as a “benevolent leader of the world,” in contrast to the Soviet Union, and attempted but failed to appease anti-American sentiment among the Chinese public. This project, therefore, on the one hand complicates the triumphalist tale of the American occupation in East Asia and on the other challenges the hegemonic view of U.S. imperialism, which often reduces this complex encounter to a dichotomous story of brutalities against Chinese victims. This research has led to the following major research outcomes: First, I have published three peer-reviewed English journal articles in leading international journals (rank 4 or 3, listed in Part C) as well as one edited volume and one book chapter in Chinese. Second, I have presented at five major international conferences, including the annual conference of the Association for Asian Studies, the American Historical Association annual conference, and AAS-in-Asia, being the most important conferences in my field. Third, I have completed a book proposal, including sample chapters, and the proposal is under review at a major university press. I have also added a new website section on American Servicemen in China.

13602120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13602120.value: This historical project provides the first comprehensive study of the everyday interactions between American servicemen and Chinese civilians from the end of World War II to the founding of the People’s Republic of China. Expanding its presence from wartime hinterland to urban centers, over one hundred thousand U.S. troops were stationed in postwar China, performing various occupation missions, including accepting Japanese surrenders, repatriating Japanese soldiers and civilians, and transporting Nationalist troops to former Japanese-controlled areas. This large-scale American military presence created unprecedented grassroots interactions, with far-reaching consequences that have yet to be recognized. This project expands existing studies of Sino-U.S. relations in the late 1940s by shifting the focus from dramatic nationwide anti-American protests and international mediations to micro-arenas of mundane struggles. Drawing upon official, popular, and personal accounts from both countries, it examines the sensorial, material, and symbolic exchanges between GIs and ordinary Chinese, such as rickshaw coolies, “Jeep girls,” suspected thieves, and black-market customers. By focusing on the politics of the everyday and the experience of both sides, the project uncovers a forgotten history of embodied entanglement that transformed the political, cultural, and mental geography of postwar China and shaped American identities in an era of global expansion.

13602720.label: Project Objectives
13602720.value: We aim to provide a new perspective on the parsimony assumptions in the Boolean approach to inferring deterministic causal structures, and reach a thorough understanding of the rationale for the minimization operations in Boolean methods. As this approach originated with the INUS account of causation, we also expect this inquiry to produce a penetrating critique of that influential account. We aim to devise and test new methods in the Boolean approach to causal inference based on the theoretical investigation in relation to the previous objective. We aim to explore learning-theoretic justifications for various parsimony assumptions in statistical inference of causal structures over random variables, in both relatively simple and more complex settings, including especially those that allow the presence of latent confounding variables and those where the joint probability distribution can change over time or across domains. We aim to refine existing methods and invent new methods in the statistical approach based on the theoretical work in relation to the previous objective.

13602720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13602720.value: In scientific inference it is commonplace to use parsimony or simplicity as a criterion for selecting theories or models: other things being roughly equal, more parsimonious theories or models are preferred. However, there is a philosophical debate over whether this preference for parsimony can actually be justified and, if so, how. This project aims to advance the study of this topic in the context of inferring relations of cause and effect. Specifically, we will examine in depth some important minimality assumptions or constraints---which manifest preferences for parsimony---in two complementary approaches to inferring causal structures from data, and leverage our theoretical findings to better understand and improve the methods in both approaches. The first approach is known as the Boolean or logical approach to causal inference, which targets deterministic causal relations among factors and is often featured in the toolbox for qualitative data analysis in social science. This approach was inspired by the well-known INUS account of causal regularities in the philosophical literature. The "N" in "INUS" stands for "non-redundancy", which is a minimality constraint and so the main target of our critique. We will examine several variations of this constraint, and study which conception of causation and goal of inference justifies which variation. We expect to refine existing methods and invent new methods in this approach in light of the results of the study. The second approach that concerns us is an influential approach to inferring probabilistic causal relations among random variables, which has attracted increasingly more attention in several fields, especially artificial intelligence. In this approach a number of parsimony-related assumptions are employed in various causal inference algorithms, including the Faithfulness assumption, which has been criticized or defended by several prominent philosophers of science. We recently developed a learning-theoretic justification for (a minimality component of) the Faithfulness assumption. This novel account is not only superior to standard defenses of the assumption, but also raises a number of interesting questions that call for further investigations, including especially the prospect of extending the account to address more complex problems of causal inference, such as inference of causal structures that allow latent variables, and causal inference in nonstationary or heterogeneous settings where the data generating process changes over time or across regimes. We aim to tackle these questions in this project, and produce both epistemological insights and new methods of causal discovery. 科學推理時常訴諸簡單性原則。其它方面差不多的情況下，科學家通常選擇更簡單的理論或模型。這種偏好是否真有道理？如果有，如何在知識論的意義上證成？此類問題在方法論的哲學探討中極其重要。本課題在因果推理的背景下探究此類問題，期望既取得方法論上的理論進展又能對實際的因果推理方法有助益。 更具體地說，本課題會聚焦兩種從數據中推斷因果結構的進路。一種稱爲布爾或邏輯進路，以推斷決定性的因果關係為目的。此進路的方法常在社會科學中用作定性數據分析，其基本思想源於哲學文獻中關於因果規律的所謂INUS理論。INUS中的N意思是“非冗餘”(non-redundancy)，相當於要求最簡化，因此是我們重點考察的對象。我們會對非冗餘條件的幾個版本做細緻分析，把各個版本與不同的因果推理的目標聯係起來，看是否每個版本都能在某個合理的目標下被證成。預計這個部分的研究結果會導致新方法的出現或者對現有方法的改進。 另一種進路以推斷非決定性的概率因果關係為目的，在人工智能領域方興未艾。這個進路已經產生了大量的因果推斷算法和與之對應的一些簡單性原則。一個比較知名的簡單性原則叫做“忠誠假設” ，在科學哲學的文獻中屢被提及。我們基於形式學習理論發展了一套針對該假設的證成方式。這個新穎的論證不僅在某些方面優於以前的論證，也催生了一組值得深入探討的問題，尤其是如何把這種證成方式擴展到更複雜的因果推理上面去的問題。比如推斷包含隱變量的因果結構，或者在因果生成機制不穩定的情況下進行因果推斷，在這樣的任務中是否能用相似的方式證成同忠誠假設類似的簡單些原則。通過對這些問題的探究，我們希望既獲得知識論上的洞見，也發展出新的因果推斷的方法。

13602720.label: Realisation of objectives
13602720.value: In connection with the first project objective, we obtained at least three novel and significant results. First, we found a new angle to criticize and improve the Boolean or INUS approach to defining and inferring causal relevance. The new angle is that each minimality or parsimony constraint implies a difference-making criterion for causal relevance, a criterion that specifies that a causally relevant factor should make a difference to the effect in a certain sense, and we can assess the adequacy of a parsimony requirement by examining the associated difference-making criterion. This perspective enables us to substantially strengthen and expand an earlier draft mentioned in our research proposal. The result is an article titled “A New Minimality Condition for Boolean Accounts of Causal Regularities”, in which we developed a suite of arguments in support of a novel minimality condition we recommend to the Boolean approach. The key arguments in this paper convinced us that appearances to the contrary, the minimality constraints in the Boolean approach are better construed as methodological principles of parsimony rather than conceptual or ontological conditions. Once we view the minimality constraints this way, there are potentially many more minimality assumptions we can put to good use in the context of Boolean causal discovery, in view of the multitude of such assumptions employed in statistical causal discovery. In another paper written in Chinese (“Regularity-theoretic Causal Inference and Occam’s Razors”), we demonstrated, for example, how an assumption known as “frugality” in statistical causal discovery can be adapted to provide a new solution to the so-called “causal chain problem” for Boolean causal discovery. This is the second notable finding in relation to the first project objective. The “methodological turn”, however, applies only to minimality constraints as they are used in the inference of causal regularities from observations. We do not deny that some minimality constraints in the Boolean or INUS approach still play a proper and important conceptual role in the definition of what is often called “token-level causation” or “actual causation”. In this light, another interesting finding emerged toward the end of this project, which is concerned with the use of the INUS-style minimality condition in popular counterfactual or interventionist definitions of actual causation. In collaboration with metaphysician R. De Clercq and a research assistant for this project, J. Fang, we produced an article (“Actual Causation and Minimality”) showing that the INUS-style minimality condition and counterfactual theories of causation interact in intricate and metaphysically significant ways that are underappreciated in the literature. Moreover, this investigation made a strong case for taking the oft-discussed proportionality condition in the literature to be a more appropriate minimality condition in counterfactual theories of causation than the INUS-style minimality condition. Interestingly, this connected back to an issue explored but left open in the PI’s previous GRF project and resulted in a new joint paper with F. Eberhardt and W. Fang (“Proportionality and the Effect-of-Cause Question”). Regarding the second project objective, with the help of another research assistant trained in political science, we managed to sharpen our understanding of various solution types of the Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) mentioned in our research proposal. A slightly unpleasant and discouraging finding was that the main idea outlined in our original proposal had already been put forward in the literature as a solution type for QCA, known as Enhanced Parsimonious Solution (EPS). We tried EPS empirically on some datasets we collected from the literature and confirmed that its behavior was indeed very similar to how we proposed to refine the so-called Intermediate Solution. Although this corroborated our original idea, it frustrated us a little by showing us that our idea did not enjoy as much originality as we thought. Nonetheless, we have been working on a paper that attempts to provide a unified foundation for all the solution types we have found in the literature, including EPS, using E. Sober’s distinction between Occam's razor of silence and Occam's razor of denial. We have not given much priority to this paper though, due to the unexpected finding that disrupted our ambition to develop an entirely novel method. On the other hand, it is worth noting that the second finding mentioned above in connection with the first project objective, also contributes to the second objective, in that it points to more possible ways to improve the Boolean methods than we originally envisaged. In particular, our new solution to the so-called “causal chain problem” by employing a parsimony principle called “frugality” is readily implementable as a new method. Toward the third project objective, we discovered a relatively simple but philosophically significant answer to the challenge of generalising the learning-theoretic framework we developed in previous work to more settings. Instead of considering specific parsimony assumptions in specialised causal discovery settings as we originally planned, we found an elegant generalisation to an abstract setup of statistical model selection, which shows that our framework can provide a compelling epistemic, truth-related justification for K. Popper’s set-inclusion criterion of simplicity in very general terms. It also suggests that his dimension criterion of simplicity is not really relevant to our learning-theoretic framework. We presented this new result and the contrast between these two conceptions of simplicity in two conferences and got encouraging feedback. We are now finalizing a paper (“Simplicity Criteria and Epistemic Goals”) for submission. In addition, in thinking about epistemic justifications for principles of simplicity, we were drawn to some novel attempts in the literature on algorithmic fairness to seek an epistemic justification for certain fairness constraints. Contrary to a rather common belief that there is a trade-off between fairness as an ethical value and accuracy as an epistemic value in training predictive machine learning models, these attempts tried to show that sometimes fairness requirements serve an epistemic function. We delved deeper in this literature and published a survey paper. More importantly, we developed a philosophical argument to show that there is never really a trade-off between fairness and a genuinely valuable epistemic goal, just as there is no trade-off between a properly formulated preference of simplicity and truth seeking. Finally, in relation to the fourth project objective, we did various work in collaboration with other researchers, both in academia and in industry, to refine or reframe some classical search procedures for learning graphical causal models from data (e.g., “Reliable Causal Discovery with Improved Exact Search and Weaker Assumptions” and “Reframed GES with a Neural Conditional Dependence Measure”) and to design new methods for identifying and estimating causal effects (e.g., “Causal Identification under Markov equivalence: Calculus, Algorithm, and Completeness”). A most recent further development is that we applied a novel minimality principle to regulate the extent of backtracking in counterfactual reasoning. Overall, we believe we can claim 100% for all but the second objective (and significantly more than what we initially anticipated for the first objective), and we estimate the extent of realization of the second objective to be about 85%.

13602720.label: Major findings and research outcome
13602720.value: 1. We proposed a novel minimality condition for the Boolean approach to causal inference and developed several arguments in support of the proposal, in an article accepted (and already published online) by Erkenntnis, a leading journal for scientific philosophy. 2. In a follow-up paper in Chinese, published in Science, Economy and Society, we argued that minimality constraints in the Boolean approach should be regarded as methodological assumptions rather than ontological or conceptual principles, and showed how fruitful such a perspective is by developing a new solution to the so-called "causal chain problem" in Boolean causal discovery. This paper has immediately attracted attention in China and has been reprinted in Social Sciences Digest and in Chinese Social Sciences Digest. 3. In collaboration with two other philosophers, we found some intricate and significant consequences of the use of the INUS-style minimality condition in counterfactual or interventionist definitions of actual causation. This resulted in an article currently under view with Philosophical Studies. 4. An interesting implication of our discussion of minimality and actual causation is to view a popular requirement called proportionality on causation as a minimality constraint. A related article on this issue was accepted by the 29th Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association in November 2024 and is currently being considered for publication in Philosophy of Science. 5. We generalised our previous result to justify an important parsimony principle in the statistical inference of causal structures to a much more general theorem providing an epistemic, truth-related justification for Popper's set-inclusion criterion of simplicity for statistical model selection in general. This finding has been presented in three conferences (including a keynote) and will be submitted to a journal soon. 6. A notable spin-off from our work on the epistemic justification of simplicity assumptions is an examination of an alleged trade-off between fairness and the epistemic goal of accuracy in training predictive machine learning models. We published a survey article in ACM Computing Surveys on algorithmic fairness and developed a philosophical argument against the significance of the said trade-off (which was presented in a keynote address in a conference). 7. We collaborated with several teams of computer scientists on improving existing methods for causal structure inference and causal effect estimation based on various parsimony assumptions. Four co-authored papers were published in top conference proceedings in AI (NeurIPS, UAI, and IJCAI), and another one is currently under review.

13602720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13602720.value: As already mentioned, we are in the process of finalizing at least three more articles, one on a unified theoretical foundation for the various solution types of QCA in light of the contrast between Occam's razor of silence and Occam's razor of denial, one on the general learning-theoretic justification for the inclusion criterion of simplicity in statistical model selection, and one on a master philosophical argument against the alleged trade-off between fairness and accuracy in algorithmic predictions. More importantly, several findings of this project, especially those in relation to the first project objective, but also our most recent work on counterfactual reasoning in connection with the last project objective, indicate strongly that it will be fruitful, both philosophically and for practical purposes, to carry out a systematic exploration of the extent to which we can unify the regularity-theoretic, Boolean approach to causal reasoning, and the interventionist, probabilistic approach. The PI has submitted an application for RGC funding to support a project along this line of further development and is waiting for the result.

13602720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13602720.value: Other things being equal, parsimony or simplicity is usually regarded as a virtue of a scientific theory or model. Consequently, scientific inference is often guided, in one form or another, by a preference for parsimony. However, why we should value simplicity if our goal is to find truth in this apparently complex world, has been a nagging problem in the epistemology of science. This research project aims to improve our understanding of some philosophical and methodological issues related to this problem, primarily in the context of causal reasoning and discovery. It examines two popular frameworks of causal reasoning, one concerned with the inference of deterministic causal relations and the other with the inference of probabilistic or statistical causal relations. The results of this research consist of not only novel philosophical and mathematical arguments in support of new ways of thinking about and working with parsimony or simplicity constraints in both frameworks, but also practical improvements on some classical and popular methods for causal inference. They therefore have a potential to impact researchers in both theoretical and applied fields, as well as the practice of causal inference in various contexts.

13602820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13602820.value: 關於實踐理性的懷疑論

13602820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13602820.value: This project will explore the possibility of skepticism about practical reason and the associated idea of normative authority. Since both of these phrases are philosophical terms of art, some background is in order. A standard philosophical problem is that of providing a justification of morality--that is, providing an answer to the question of why a person should do what is moral (or, for the ancient Greeks, what justice requires) even at the cost of their own interests. In the classic example from Plato, the character Gyges can kill the king of Lydia to make himself king. Obviously, killing the king is immoral (or unjust). But given the personal benefit, why should Gyges do the moral thing? This is the standard philosophical problem. To adopt skepticism about practical reason is to argue, in effect, that the question itself is ill-formed. The issue is this: the question asks why someone should be moral at personal cost. But what is the sense of 'should' at work? If the question is, 'Why morally should Gyges do the moral thing?' the answer is trivial. If the question is, 'Why self-interestedly should Gyges do the moral thing?' the answer is similarly trivial. So we must be asking what Gyges should do in some third sense of 'should'. But not any third sense will do. We could ask, 'Why legally should Gyges do the moral thing?' While this is no longer trivial--it is substantive question whether a local legal code tells us to act morally or immorally on some occasion--it isn't what we were after. We need a sense of 'should' distinct from the moral ‘should’, which also possesses an unquestionable authority, so that if this sense applies to the moral act, there is no further question. I deny the existence of such a sense of 'should'. Since philosophers have typically identified this sense of 'should' with practical reason, this can be called skepticism about practical reason. While such skepticism has been defended in a few papers, it has not been systematically explored within contemporary analytic philosophy. This project will examine the various reasons for adopting it, ways of resisting it, and what becomes of normative thought and deliberation if we do adopt it. I am especially interested in the last, in which our fundamental relation to values and reasons is not one of discovery or responsiveness, but something closer to existential choice.

13603220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13603220.value: 如果你在繁忙的街道上行走時，眼前閃過一張看似熟悉的面孔。你會上前寒喧，還是繼續走路？簡單而言，這取決於你有多大的信心，肯定你認得那張臉。這種對置信度作出判斷的能力，或評價自己於工作或任務上的表現，是一種後設認知過程。後設認知可讓我們意識到自己內在思維對外在世界的詮釋，以至評估或反思自己的行為表現。 我們的行為，往往基於外在刺激所引發的內在感知。而根據內在感知所作出合適的行為或決定，則建基於判斷置信度的能力。可是，直至現時，我們仍不甚了解這種置信判斷的能力。 究竟設認知系統是靠接收甚麼資訊，才能讓我們擁有置信判斷的能力？這是推動本項目的大問題。 不確定性是其中一項會影響置信度的資訊來源。過往對於不確定性的研究，多集中於包含在主體裏的不確定性，例如使外在刺激物變得模糊或增加行為任務的難度。然而，本項目建議把焦點拉後，著眼於從周邊環境所產生的不確定性。這建議其實是對現有假定的反思：在後設認知系統判斷置信度的過程中，除了採用與任務相關的信息外，是否還會考慮周邊環境的信息。事實上，在日常生活中，我們每一次對置信度作出的判斷，都是在一個獨特的周邊環境裏進行。因此，本項目有助於連繫實驗室的發現和日常生活， 本項目將關注與感知處理有關的三種周邊環境類型：刺激的周邊環境，任務的周邊環境和知識的周邊環境。 本項目的所採用的研究方法，是建基於心理物理學的實驗基礎上。這使我們能夠定量地控制周邊環境的特徵及屬性，並準確量度周邊環境因素對置信判斷的影響。為了確定這種方法的可行性，我們已經進行了三個先導實驗。從這些先導實驗中，我們發現周邊環境的不確定性，在上述的周邊環境類型，對置信判斷均有實在的影響。本項目將以此為起點進行一系列實驗，以進一步找出周邊環境的不確定性如何影響置信判斷。 本項目的結果對日常生活有多方面影響。其中包括用於研發新的心理治療方法，讓病者更能處理感知上的病徵；用於設計電腦或機器介面上，使用家能夠更方便及準確判斷置信度；或用於開發更像人類的人工智能，使機器有自省及籌劃策略能力。

13603220.label: Realisation of objectives
13603220.value: Objective 1: We have identified various types of information that the metacognitive system takes as input for computation. These include stimulus uncertainty in the spatial surrounding, confidence judgments in previous decisions, and environmental factors that depend on the decision context. Objective 2: Throughout the project, we have designed new paradigms to measure the extent to which confidence judgments can be influenced by contextual uncertainty. These include the center-surround stimulus uncertainty manipulation and the serial dependence in confidence judgments. Objective 3: We have demonstrated, across multiple experiments, that classical psychophysical and computational paradigms for perception can be transformed and utilized in studying confidence judgments. Objectives 4-6: The findings of the studies have demonstrated that we have characterized the effects of contextual uncertainty related to stimulus context, task context, and knowledge context. These findings of these studies as articles in peer-reviewed journals and refereed conference abstracts via oral or poster presentations.

13603220.label: Major findings and research outcome
13603220.value: 1. Stimulus context (Study 1): Uncertainty in surrounding stimulus, despite being task-irrelevant, can influence our confidence judgment on the task focused on a central stimulus. 2. Effects of task contexts (Study 2): Confidence judgments tend to be biased towards those made in previous perceptual decisions. Despite constant performance, our confidence on our own task performance tends to be similar to confidence in our previous judgments. 3. Effects of knowledge context (Study 3): Our task performance in memory depends on the context in which the information has been learned, resulting in context-dependent biases in confidence judgments. These findings have led to 3 manuscripts (2 published in international peer-reviewed journals, 1 full draft in preprint and to be submitted for publication after finalization) and 1 conference abstract.

13603220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13603220.value: Our findings suggest that, when we make confidence judgments, the metacognition system does not only take into consideration task-relevant information. Many types of task-irrelevant information related to the stimulus, task, and knowledge in context can also influence our judgments, resulting in biases in our confidence judgments that may not accurately reflect our own task performance. This suggests that the metacognition system naturally tends to consider a wide range of information, including task-irrelevant information, when generating confidence judgments. While this natural tendency could lead to biases in confidence judgments (i.e., confidence not accurately reflecting task performance), one immediate question is whether humans can be trained to ignore task-irrelevant information, and make better confidence judgments. In fact, the PI has submitted a GRF proposal to follow up on this. Furthermore, future studies will be conducted to investigate the limits of this wide input range of information, as well as their realization in the performance of everyday tasks by the general public and/or those in certain professions requiring specifically-trained skills.

13603220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13603220.value: When we perform certain tasks such as visual or memory tasks, in addition to the task performance, we often need to consider our confidence in performing the task, which can guide our decisions and actions on performing the task. The present project found that, when we make our confidence judgment for a task, we do not only consider information related to the task, but also consider information that is irrelevant to the task. Across situations, we have demonstrated that these task-irrelevant contexts can lead to biases in our confidence judgments, leading to a potentially undesirable consequence in which our confidence does not accurately reflect our task performance. These findings will inspire future research on how humans can be trained to make better confidence judgments in various situations, including both in everyday tasks and in professional settings.

13605120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13605120.value: Hong Kong has topped the world's most expensive housing market for the 9th straight year. The city has witnessed house prices surging from one record high to another over the past decade, coinciding with twelve rounds of cooling measures aimed at reining in the overheated property market. It is noteworthy that house prices are at the intersection of both demand and supply. However, the government's interventions have mostly emphasized on suppressing the ever-stronger demand rather than relaxing the supply constraint, thus leaving the acute demand-supply imbalance to remain unsolved. Understanding the underlying supply and demand fundamentals in the local housing market is of first-order importance. In the proposed project, we will first estimate both short-term and long-term supply-demand imbalances in housing across various sub-markets in Hong Kong. We then analyze whether (and to what extent) local price growth can be explained by supply and demand fundamentals, particularly, whether supply-shortage overhang can predict future price growth. Through the twelve rounds of cooling measures beginning from October 2009, the LTV ratio caps were reduced to 50% for properties valued at or above $10 million, and 60% for those valued below $10 million (subject to a loan cap of $5 million) as of Oct 15, 2019. However, price growth more than tripled in the secondary residential market, concurrent with a decline in homeownership from 53.63% in 2008 to 49% in 2018. Meanwhile, the number of shadow banks surged from 779 in 2009 to 2173 in 2018, which reportedly extended 97% of their personal loans to borrowers below the better-than-prime rating in 2017 (TransUnion (2017)). Have the cooling measures achieved their initial goals or, instead made housing less affordable to needy homebuyers? Have policy interventions unintentionally distorted the sub-housing markets and contributed to concurrent prosperity in the non-banking sector (mainly shadow banks)? What are the transmission mechanisms of the government's interventions in distorting the housing market and the broader banking industry? In the proposed project, we will conduct consolidated analyses and provide empirical analysis to answer these questions. 截至2019年，香港已經連續第九年位居全球最昂貴的住房市場之首。在過去的十年中，香港樓價不斷創下新高記錄。與此同時，政府亦推出了十二輪包括宏觀審慎措施以及徵收各類印花稅在內的「樓市辣招」，意圖抑制過度熾熱的樓市。眾所周知，樓價是需求及供給兩方作用的結果，然而政府的幹預重點始終為抑制日益強烈的需求，而非放寬供應限制，從而無法根本解決日益嚴重的供需失衡問題。 瞭解香港樓市的基本供求基本原理具有首要意義。在這個項目中，我們將首先估算香港各個住房市場上房屋的短期和長期供需失衡。然後，我們將分析是否可以用供求基本原理來解釋（或在何種程度上解释）樓價的上漲，特別是供應短缺是否可以預測未來價格的上漲。 經過多輪宏觀審慎政策的調節，截至2019年10月15日，價值在1000萬港元或以上的住宅申請按揭上限已降低至五成，對於價值在1000萬港元以下的住宅，其按揭上限降至六成（按揭額度上限為500萬港元）。然而對比2009年第一輪降溫政策出臺之前，二手住宅市場的價格卻增長超過三倍，同時，房屋擁有率從2008年的53.63％下降至2018年的49％。此外，影子銀行（shadow banks，又稱為財務公司）的數量從2009年的779家激增至2018年的2173家。TransUnion 在2017發佈的報告中指出，影子銀行在2017年將97％的個人貸款發放給了低於優等評級的借款人。基於以上客觀事實，我們提出以下研究問題：多輪樓市降溫措施是否達到了最初的目標？是否提高了購房者的住宅承擔能力？政策的干預是否帶來了不同住宅市場之間的扭曲，是否導致了非銀行市場（影子銀行）市場的繁榮發展？我們將進行嚴謹的實證分析，以解答這些問題。

13605120.label: Realisation of objectives
13605120.value: We use a comprehensive transaction-level data to explicitly evaluate the net impact of each round of intervention measures by conducting a regression discontinuity design (RDD) analysis. Outcome variables include 1) real transaction price and 2) daily transaction volume. Controlling for a vector of property attributes, any discontinuity in the conditional mean of the outcome variable observed around the implementation date should be attributed to the “pure” effect of the given cooling measure. For each of the selected measures, we conduct the RDD analyses by type of transaction (first-hand v.s. second-hand) and class (small, medium-sized, and large units). The event window is restricted to 98 or 60 days before and after the implementation date to capture the short-term policy pass-through. Objective 1 and 3: We provide empirical results suggest that mortgage-tightening measures effectively curbed the overheated property market by reducing price and trading volume in the short term. However, some submarkets still experienced volatility, with occasional price hikes and increases in trading volume. Notably, the various transaction taxes meant to curb speculation appear to have impeded the trading-up process. By significantly reducing the supply of existing homes, especially starter homes, an unintended consequence was much sharper price increases for starter homes compared to larger homes. The surge in smaller flat prices began after the launch of the Sellers Stamp Duty (SSD), which had directly reduced the supply of smaller flats in the existing housing market. In addition, we note that besides the shortage of developable land and ultra-low mortgage rates, fundamental factors are the major reasons for Hong Kong's high housing prices in the private market. These include the availability of low-cost Public Rental Housing (PRH), desirable amenities, and a low, simple and competitive tax system. Construction costs play a minor role. The PRH is a long-established housing program for qualified low-income families in Hong Kong. Since the handover, public pressure to freeze rent has been mounting and public housing rent has increasingly lagged behind private sector rent. However, the policy that a PRH tenant who owns a home in Hong Kong should move out has not been effectively implemented as late as 2023. It was not uncommon for public housing tenants, who were better able to save money compared to private housing tenants, to buy homes in the private market. In general, the huge savings garnered by virtue of the low rent of PRH and upward earnings mobility of tenants were a factor behind the strong buying power for Hong Kong’s homes. At one time, PRH tenants accounted for as much as 24% of home purchases. The bidding among well-off tenants with handsome savings pushed starter-home prices up, which in turn pushed up the prices of higher and higher “quality tiers”. We find that Hong Kong's competitive tax system is another key reason for its high housing prices. Hong Kong is well known for its low income and property taxes (much lower compared to most other jurisdictions) and the absence of a retail sales tax and value-added tax. All the tax savings are capitalized into land rent and reflected in home prices. Additionally, the value of local public goods, such as desirable amenities and a cheap, well-developed public transport system, may also be captured in land values. Objective 2: A back-of-the-envelope calculation indicates that from 2009 to 2018, the short-term supply-demand imbalance was most pronounced in the Class A market—that is, in livable areas smaller than 40 square meters—with the imbalance ranging between 70-98%. The long-term imbalance is estimated to be at a similar rate of 88%. This suggests that the demand for starter homes significantly exceeds supply, both in the short term and long term. In the Class B and C markets, the imbalance stood at approximately 47% and 88%, respectively. However, these two markets occasionally experienced an oversupply. Objective 4: We find that while tax-driven measures were intended as well-intentioned policies, they inadvertently had adverse effects on genuine homebuyers. Originally designed as a demand management tool to deter speculators and thereby facilitate homeownership, these stamp duties, though highly successful in achieving this aim, also discouraged homeowners from trading up. The second-hand supply from existing homeowners fell sharply after the implementation of stamp duties. The policy slowed down the rise of bigger homes but accelerated the rise of smaller homes. Starter homes became more unaffordable and the effect was immediate. More importantly, the significant decline in housing market turnover also aggravated the decline in economic growth due to the social unrest in 2019 and the COVID-19 pandemic. Objective 5: our findings suggest a thriving first-hand market at the expense of shrinking second-hand market. The secondhand market was disproportionally subdued in terms of both price and volume compared to the firsthand market. The first reason is that transaction volume in the firsthand market increases occasionally because developers attract liquidity-constrained home buyers by offering additional financing packages in response to tightened mortgage measures. The second reason is that the firsthand market is less responsive to tax-driven measures than to mortgage-tightening measures. Stamp duties may cause a reduction in listings of flats in the secondhand market. Consequently, prospective homebuyers are gravitating towards the primary market to compete for new flats, resulting in price increases driven by heightened demand. Another unintended consequence impacts the subsidized public housing market (HOS). Cooling measures are specifically designed to temper an overheating housing market by curbing speculative transactions. Ideally, if these measures are correctly designed and applied, they should not affect the non-private residential sectors, primarily the HOS market. However, evidence indicates a spillover effect of the intervention measures on HOS units, including impeded residential mobility and increased price volatility. A third unintended consequence is the deterioration in home quality. These policy interventions have arguably led to the proliferation of "nano flats"—with an average livable area of 219 sqft— which accounted for almost 13% of the first-hand sale residential properties in 2019. Consequently, the average size of units under construction dropped by 40% during 2013-2018. Objective 6: We also find suggestive evidence indicating that credit-rationed genuine homebuyers, in response to increasingly stringent mortgage policies, have been directed towards securing their loans through the unregulated shadow banking industry. Liquidity-constrained homebuyers are drawn to first-hand small flats over second-hand flats of similar characteristics because they can obtain financial assistance from developers, many of whom operate their own financial companies. These non-bank lenders have jumped into the credit void, financing over 15% of mortgages for first-hand flats. However, we find no evidence that borrowing from these shadow banks spreads risk across the financial sector. Objective 7: Our findings carry implications for policymakers aiming to evaluate and amend property market intervention policies, both in Hong Kong and beyond. It is critical to carefully assess the potential impact on the Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) market when crafting policies directed at the private residential sector. Policymakers should also account for the varied responses across different submarkets when devising future housing strategies. Additionally, efforts should be made to address the disparity between the primary and secondary markets.

13605120.label: Major findings and research outcome
13605120.value: In this research project, we find that the effect of each round varied significantly across submarkets. As elaborated in the published paper “The effectiveness and consequences of the government’s interventions for Hong Kong’s residential housing markets,” there are notable heterogeneous responses across the submarkets. Specifically, while the first-hand market experienced a price hike and a decrease in volume after the Round 5 measures, a closer investigation shows that the price hike was attributable to the first-hand high-end market, whereas the decrease in volume was mainly observed in the first-hand mass market. Similarly, the price hike in the second-hand market after the Round 2 measures came from its mass submarket. We document in the published paper that cooling measures, notably stamp duties, were well-intended policies but induced unintended consequences. These tax-driven measures were originally desired as a demand management tool to chase away speculators and thus make homeownership easier. Although they were highly successful in this regard, they also discouraged trading-up, causing the prices of smaller flats to rise significantly relative to those of bigger flats. In addition, the second-hand market was disproportionally subdued in terms of both price and volume compared to the first-hand market, and a spillover effect was observed in the HOS market, including impeded residential mobility and price volatility. Future policies should be designed to avoid such unintended consequences and to ensure that liquidity in the HOS and public rental markets is unaffected or less affected. Overall, mortgage-tightening measures worked more efficiently in cutting housing prices than reducing transaction volume. Tax-driven measures were more efficient in suppressing trading activities; they also triggered price volatilities over time. As we show in the published paper “The Hong Kong Housing Market,” we also find that a shortage of developable land, low-cost PRH, desirable amenities, a competitive tax system, and ultra-low mortgage rates are the major reasons for Hong Kong’s high housing prices in the private market.

13605120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13605120.value: This project investigates the short-term effects of each of the 12 rounds of interventions enacted from October 2009 to May 2017. The interventions were clustered within short periods, for example, four rounds in 13 months. For this reason, the analysis compares the responses in price and volume in the 98 days before each round of measures with those after the effective date of a round of measures. A comprehensive analysis of the long-term/cumulative effects of the collection of (or selected) intervention measures may offer insights that complement this project’s findings regarding the measures’ short-term effectiveness.

13605120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13605120.value: Since the global financial crisis, house prices in Hong Kong have continuously hit record highs. Beginning in 2009, the government implemented several interventions, known as cooling measures, to control the overheated property market. We find that the various transaction taxes, intended to curb speculation, appear to have hindered the trading-up process. By significantly reducing the supply of existing homes, and especially that of starter homes, an unintended consequence is much sharper price increases for starter homes than for larger homes. Consequently, this has led to the proliferation of so-called nano flats—tiny yet very expensive units. These findings offer insights into the puzzle of why homeownership in Hong Kong increased at a painfully slow pace from 46.7% to 52.6% during 1997-2022, marking a modest 5.9 percentage point rise over 25 years. This is in stark contrast to the steady 18 percentage point growth observed in the 15 years prior to 1997. We also observe that the second-hand market was disproportionally subdued in volume compared to the first-hand market. We document a spillover effect on subsidized public housing units. These findings highlight the need for further market segmentation when reviewing current measures and, more importantly, when designing future housing policies.

13605220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13605220.value: 漢代經濟思想論文選集

13605220.label: Project Objectives
13605220.value: This project aims to advance the scholarship on the history of economic thought of early China. It is an important but seriously understudied area in the history of ancient China across all the major research languages. This project will make a significant contribution to begin filling this glaring lacuna in the scholarship on the intellectual and political history of early China. More specifically, this research project will help advance the scholarship on the history of the Han empire (206 BCE - 220 CE). The history of the Han empire is a generally well-studied field, with a large body of scholarship on its many different aspects. Economic thought and debates, as well as broader discussions of political economy, of the Han empire however is not a well-developed subfield. With a few exceptions, much of the earlier scholarship tend to focus on a few key texts, such as the _Yan tie lun_, the “Huozhi liezhuan” chapter of the _Shiji_, or the “Shi huo zhi” chapter of the _Hanshu_. This proposed critical anthology will present a much wider spectrum of ideas in the political economy of the Han empire. To put all these writings in a single volume, with both the original text and all-new annotated translation, in a conceptually and linguistically coherent framework, this anthology will enable a clear and comprehensive view of the complex development of economic thought in the four centuries of Han imperial rule. This research project also aims to introduce early Chinese economic ideas to the scholarship on global history of economic thought. The relative dearth of scholarship, especially in the English language, has preempted wider appreciation for this body of economic thought from ancient China by scholars outside the Sinological circle. In the study of the history of political economy, there is already a tendency to privilege the works from the modern European tradition, and for more recent studies that attempt to write a global history of economic thought, the engagement with materials from Chinese world, early or otherwise, has been rather superficial. I hope that this prospective volume will facilitate a proper introduction of these powerful economic ideas of the ancient Chinese to a broad scholarly audience. These texts convey such powerful and interesting ideas for reflecting on the complexity of the material world and economic order. They should not only interest historians of early China but also global historians of economic thought.

13605220.label: Realisation of objectives
13605220.value: This project had 3 closely-related research objectives. They are, in short, to advance our understanding of the history of economic thought in ancient China (i.e., objective #1), introduce this history to the scholarship on global history of economic thought (i.e., objective #2), and then relatively more narrowly, advance our understanding of the intellectual history of the Han empire (206 BCE - 220 CE). In the original application, I propose to achieve all three of these objectives via a single research output, namely a critical anthology of writings about economic matters from the Han dynasty, presented in both the original Chinese texts and all-new English translations. There will also be annotations that are designed to make the translation readable by a wide range of audiences, espeically those who do not read classical Chinese or are relatively with the history of ancient China. More specifically, it will include 56 texts from 14 major collections, presented chronologically from the start to the end of the Han empire. I am happy to report that I have completed the manuscript of this critical anthology in 2024, as proposed in the original application. It is now under consideration at Columbia University Press. Relatedly, the research findings of this project has also contributed to another monograph that I have written, namely _Traditions of History and Historiography in Ancient East Asia_. It has been under contract with Cambridge University Press since May 2022, has been going through various revisions, and is expected to be published in 2025. In my earlier monograph _The Politics of the Past in Early China_ (Cambridge University Press, 2019), I have already made a strong argument for the close relation between economic theories and historical thought in the Han empire (i.e., Chapter 5, “Sima Qian’s Critical Past,” pages 153-176). It was not surprising to me, therefore, that the new insights I gained from the compilation of the critical anthology would also find their way into this monograph on history and historiography in ancient East Asia. It turns out that in fact, during the Han empire, much economic debates took the form of historical narratives, and conversely, a lot of the historical writings focused on the development of economic relations. Similarly, the research findings also informed my interpretation of Sima Qian, the Han Empire’s grand historian, in another accepted publications in 2024. Titled “Sima Qian and the Records of the Grand Scribe: Historicism Under the Early Han Empire,” it is part of an edited volume on East Asian historiography both ancient and modern, forthcoming from Routlege. Since it is a critical anthology of translated texts, it does not explicitly advance a new thesis about the history of economic thought in ancient China. Nevertheless, let me now elaborate briefly on new findings in relation to each objective. For objective #1, this anthology enriches our understanding of the history of economic thought in ancient China by emphasizing on the development within the span of four centuries of the Han empire. Much earlier scholarship on ancient Chinese economic thought rarely looks at this specific period but often situates it within the broader development from the Late Bronze Age that came before and the Early Medieval Period that came afterwards. It is my contention, and my inspiration for compiling this volume, that the Han Empire deserves our special attention. The Han Empire marked the beginning of the imperial period in Chinese history, and in its four centuries of rule, it radically remade the entire political, intellectual, and cultural landscape of ancient China. It initiated a sustainable political order and established intellectual and cultural ideals that would have, in many ways, persisted until the collapse of the last empire the Qing Dynasty (1644-1912) in the early twentieth century. New economic ideas, especially the role that the imperial state should play in the world of exchanges of goods, was an important part of the complex history of the Han. This critical anthology, by focusing solely on the period of the Han Empire, demonstrate the richness of this debate about economic matters and argues that the specific hsitory of this debate under the Han Empire deserves our special, sustained, and close attention. Objective #2 is closely related to objective #1, of course. This volume presents these documents as an very important part of the intellectual history and ideological legacy of the Han Empire. Presenting them chronologically, as I have done in this volume, demonstrates to readers the complex evolution of the debates from the start of the empire to its slow demise over the course of four centuries. Readers see clearly the sophisticated theories that the early empire had inherited from the earlier Warring States period, the intense debates that took place under and immediately after the pivotal reign of Emperor Wu (r. 141 - 87 BCE), and the greatly different focus and nature of the debates, which saw a gradual withdrawl of the imperial state from the economic world, in the second half of the empire. This critical anthology did not only demonstrate the richness of economic thought of the Han Empire, but also shows how integral and constitute these economic debates were to understanding the history of the Han Empire. Finally, for objective #3, this critical anthology is prepared in such a way that makes it accessible and readable to scholars outside of the field of Chinese history. The introduction and the copious annotations were written with these readers, not only the specialists of early China studies, in mind. Therefore, upon its publication, it can be perused and studied by scholars of global history of economic thought for comparative purposes. Given the relative dearth of scholarship on the history of ancient Chinese economic thought, especially in English-language academia, there has been relatively limited understanding of this history and body of ideas from the Han Empire. This volume, with its great accessibility by non-specialists, aims to introduce them to a wider audience of global historains of economic thought.

13605220.label: Major findings and research outcome
13605220.value: The mansucript of the critical anthology _Economic Thought of the Han Empire: A Critical Anthology_ demonstrates the history of the economic thoughts under the Han Empire, by presenting a wide range of key documents in this debates over four centuries. It also shows, by way of these primary documents, the pivotal role played by the reign of Emperor Wu (r. 141-87 BCE) which intensified the great debate on the role that the state should play in regulating the economic world, or in simpler terms, the proper nature of state-socity relationship. In the monograph _Traditions of History and Historiography in Ancient East Asia_, as well as the book chapter "Sima Qian and the Records of the Grand Scribe: Historicism Under the Early Han Empire" in the edited volume _Routledge Companion for East Asian Historiography_, I made the finding that oftentimes, economic debates during the Han times took on the form of historical narratives. By writing a history of the origin of currencies, for example, Sima Qian subtly argued for the autonomy of the economy and therefore the potentially negative consequences of excessive government regulations in the world of exchanges of goods.

13605220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13605220.value: The most immediate plan for further development is in pedagogy. I have already integrated materials from this project into my existing course _History of Early China_ (HST2003) at Lingnan University (last offered in spring 2024). I also plan to develop a new course based on the critical anthology on the history of economic debate in ancient China, to be offered in 2025-2026. For research, there is no plan for further specific action at this time, as I have moved on to a new project, also funded by GRF, on the history of homosexuality in early China (Project No.: 13608122).

13605220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13605220.value: This research project culminated in the compilation of a critical anthology of writings about economic matters during the Han Empire (206 BCE - 220 CE). In chronological order, the texts are presented in both the original Chinese and new English-language translations. As such, this anthology is a collection of documents that embodies the history of economic thoughts of the Han Empire, which in many ways served as the foundation for the structure of all subsequent regimes in East Asia till the early modern period. This is the first anthology of its kind in the English language, and readers will find many ideas in it that are both surprisingly familiar and excitingly strange. The early empire builders in ancient China were very concerned with defining the precise role of the state in the economy, like many other regimes in the ancient world as well as nation-states in the modern world. This is in fact a key theme that runs through many of the documents collected in this volume, in addition to a variety of sophisticated economic theories concerning monetary valuations, monopolies of essential industries such as salt and iron, as well as the rights to coinage.

13605620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13605620.value: Science changes often, in ways that aren’t easily predictable. Theories change. Claims about what exists – and what doesn’t exist – change. Methods and instruments change. But how can we tell which changes are progressive, and which are not? Historians and philosophers of science, and indeed scientists themselves, have struggled to reach a consensus on how this question should be answered. Consider only the non-ethical dimension of the question, for the sake of illustration. Some think that scientific progress is made only via the discovery of new truths about fundamental reality, whereas others think that science makes progress primarily by enabling us to solve new practical problems. The two sides argue back and forth, but there is little prospect of their disagreement being resolved at present. Why is the disagreement so hard to resolve? One key reason is that insufficient work has been done to tackle several foundational problems, which underlie the debate. What exactly does the concept of progress involve, and how does it link to aims, values, and rationality? And what counts as a good argument that something is progressive in a particular context? Most authors in the current debate about scientific progress don’t adopt explicit positions on how these questions should be answered, and they talk past one another, to a considerable extent, as a result. My aim in this project is to to remove some of these obstacles to understanding scientific progress, by producing a book on these foundational problems concerning scientific progress. 科學經常改變，其變往往不易預測。理論會變。關於某物存在與否的宣稱會變。方法、儀器也會變。不過，我們如何辨別哪些改變能算是進展，哪些不算呢？史學家與科學哲學家一直琢磨著如何就回答此問題的方法達成共識。科學家也一樣。為作一簡介，不妨先擱置倫理因素來考慮此問題。有學者認為，只有在科學能對世界根本之真實有新的發現，也就是發現新的真理時，才可算作進展。但也有學者認為科學進展之要點在於它能使我們解決日新月異的實際問題。兩邊意見的論辯你來我往，可是現時要解決他們的分歧，機會不大。為甚麼要解決此分歧這麼難呢？關鍵理由之一，是學者對根本問題還研究得不夠深入。這些根本問題是整場論辯的前設。「進展」這概念確切來說究竟包含甚麼內容？「進展」與目標、價值、理性等概念又有甚麼連繫？還有，在某脈絡之中，假如要論證某事為「進展」，應根據甚麼標準判別該論證的優劣？目前就科學進展這一課題論辯的學者們，大多沒有選定回應這些問題的明確立場。結果他們往往各說各話。本次計劃的目標，即在寫作專書，針對上述的根本問題，為理解科學進展清除理論障礙。

13605620.label: Realisation of objectives
13605620.value: Objectives 1, 2, and 4 have been completed. This is evidenced primarily by the book produced, which is in press. (At the time of writing, I am going through the second proofs.) Objective 3 was discontinued because the work on the other objectives resulted in a different outcome than anticipated. Ultimately, the position I developed - detailed in the monograph - is such that historical case studies of the kind originally envisaged _do not_ directly bear on what scientific progress consists in. However, the book does develop a view of how the history of science can legitimately inform conceptions of scientific progress. It also identifies how the history of science might be used to challenge the core position defended therein.

13605620.label: Major findings and research outcome
13605620.value: Primary, the project resulted in a monograph, 'Scientific Progress', which will appear later this year (probably September) with Cambridge University Press. Here is the abstract: What constitutes cognitive scientific progress? This Element begins with an extensive survey of the contemporary debate on how to answer this question. It provides a blow-by-blow critical summary of the key literature on the issue over the past fifteen years, covering the central positions and arguments therein. It also draws upon older literature, where appropriate, to inform the treatment. The Element then enters novel territory by considering meta-normative issues concerning scientific progress. It focuses on how the standards involved in assessing progress arise. Does science have aims, which determine what counts as progress, as many authors assume? If so, what is it to be an aim of science? And how does one identify such things? If not, how do normative standards arise? After arguing that science does not have overarching aims, the Element proposes that the standards are ultimately subjective. I was also prompted to reconsider some aspects of existing conceptions of progress, especially as they relate to the scientific realism debate. I produced another couple of pieces on this topic, published in _Philosophy of Science_ and an edited volume (Springer). My most significant idea was that a theory might be approximately true, or true to a significant degree, despite being neither true nor false. This is a radical idea - normally, approximate truth is taken to require falsity - but it fits well with the metaphorical character of much scientific discourse. I presented this work in various contexts (either online or in person). These include Pittsburgh University, University of British Columbia, University of Oxford, and Virginia Tech.

13605620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13605620.value: This will bring to a close my work on scientific progress, as, in effect, the conclusion is that the problem is not as pressing as many have thought. However, the image formed as a result will be relevant in my future work in the philosophy of science, especially since this pertains to the increasing role of AI in science. For example, we should avoid worrying about whether the introduction of AI will impede the pursuit of 'the aims of science', such as increasing our understanding of the unobservable world. Instead, we should have an open debate about what *we* value about science, and what *we* (most) want from it. (The trick here is to clarify that we're not arguing about some essential 'aim' of the activity, linked with some fixed sense of 'progress'. Rather, we have the freedom to choose, to shape science to achieve what we value.)

13605620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13605620.value: This project resulted in a book. First, this provides a critical survey of all the recent work on how we should understand the intellectual aspects of scientific progress. Second, it develops a new perspective on the issue. It argues that science doesn't progress in any objective sense, despite appearances to the contrary. There's no aim of science, beyond the aims we have in doing it. Science only makes progress relative to different standards that people and groups have had for evaluating changes therein; those standards have changed over time (and will probably change in the future).

14100120.label: Realisation of objectives
14100120.value: Objective 1 was completed. N-utilisation substance (Nus) B is an essential bacterial antitermination factor, of which heterodimerisation with NusE presents the key regulatory step during rRNA synthesis. Targeting the protein-protein interaction (PPI) interface of the NusB-NusE dimer, we previously identified a group of antimicrobial compounds, collectively termed nusbiarylins which derives its name from the target protein NusB and its biaryl chemical structure. In this work, we examined a nusbiarylin compound mini-library composed of over 160 candidates. Antimicrobial susceptibility tests were performed using the broth microdilution assay according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. A panel of clinically important pathogens will be tested, including but not limited to “WHO priority pathogens list for guiding R&D of new antibiotics” E. faecium; S. aureus, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa, E. cloacae and S. pneumoniae, as well as the Gram-positive Enterococcus casseliflavus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus saprophyticus, Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus agalactiae. Several of these derivatives exhibited remarkable antimicrobial potency, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) below 1 μg/mL against clinically important bacterial strains. Compared to other derivatives, compounds like MC4-134, MC4-135, MC4-190, and MC4-205 demonstrated outstanding antimicrobial activity (minimum inhibitory concentration, MIC, 0.25 to 2 μg/mL) against all tested Gram-positive pathogens, including Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. Notably, several Gram-negative bacteria, such as Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter cloacae, and Escherichia coli, were found to be susceptible (MIC = 64 to 32 μg/mL) to MC4-134. Additionally, all tested drug-resistant bacteria, comprising vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE), penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae (PRSP), methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), and vancomycin-resistant S. aureus (VRSA), were susceptible (MIC = 0.25-1 μg/mL). To further assess the in vitro antibacterial effects, time-kill kinetics and ATP production assays were conducted. The staphylococcal type strain ATCC 25923 and the resistant lineage USA300 were challenged with either MC4-134, MC4-135, MC4-190, or MC4-205 at a series of concentrations (¼, 1, 4, and 16  MIC) over the course of 6 hours. While both MC4-134 and MC4-135 were bacteriostatic at ¼, 1, and 4  MICs, MC4-134 at 16  MIC was bactericidal to both type and drug-resistant strains. Significantly repressed ATP production was observed for both type and drug-resistant staphylococci treated with MC4-134 and MC4-135. To identify any synergism between the nusbiarylins and current antibiotics on the market, checkerboard assays were performed using MC4-134 in combination with either fusidic acid, vancomycin, linezolid, chloramphenicol, or rifampicin against the staphylococcal type and drug-resistant strains. No antagonism was observed as illustrated by the fractional inhibitory concentration (FIC) greater than 0.5. Objective 2 was completed by establishing the molecular mechanism of transcription inhibition exerted by the anti-NusB compounds. Nusbiarylins were designed to prevent the NusB-NusE PPI, thereby inhibiting rRNA synthesis. Mechanistic investigations were conducted to characterise the target protein-ligand interaction and compound effects on rRNA transcription. To verify the NusB-nusbiarylins interaction, two biophysical assays, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and microscale thermophoresis (MST), were carried out. While ITC data showed the binding between MC4-134 and purified NusB proteins, with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 31.5 µM, MST assays revealed that MC4-135 interacted with NusB, with a Kd of 122 µM. In both cases, the interaction was abolished when key amino acids on NusB was mutated to alanine, confirming the target specificity. Following the quantification of the compound binding affinity to NusB, we attempted to confirm PPI inhibition by the compounds using our in-house developed luciferase complementation assay. In the presence of MC4-134 or MC4-135, a dose-dependent PPI inhibition was observed with IC50 values of 80.2 ± 17.6 µM and 58.4 ± 10.9 µM, respectively. To confirm the compound impacts on rRNA synthesis, in vitro transcription assays were performed. Relevant proteins were cloned, overproduced, purified before In this assay, rRNA transcription complexes assembled using E. coli RNA polymerase (RNAP) and the five Nus factors (NusA, NusB, NusE, NusG, and SuhB) for producing RNA in vitro. In the presence of MC4-134 and MC4-135, a significant decline in RNAP processivity was observed in a dose-dependent manner, akin to the effects of the removal of NusB-NusE heterodimers. These results collectively confirmed that representative nusbiarylin compounds inhibit NusB-NusE mediated rRNA transcription through specific binding to their target protein NusB and disrupt the NusB-E interaction at the molecular level. Objective 3 was completed. The mechanism of nusbiarylins was confirmed at the cellular level. Cell-based transcription assays were performed using the recombinant E. coli K12 strain, in which NusB was required for stable expression of the reporter genes bla and cam. The reporter strains were treated with either MC4-134 or MC4-135 for later extraction of cellular RNA and detection of the reporter gene transcripts by quantitative PCR (qPCR). Compared to the untreated group, diminished reporter gene expression was observed for the nusbiarylin-treated cells in a dose-dependent manner. To evaluate the possibility of resistance generation, staphylococcal cells were repeatedly exposed to the selected nusbiarylins and the control drug rifampicin at ½  MIC. While MC4-134, MC4-135, MC4-190 caused no significant increase in MIC against drug-resistant staphylococci, rifampicin resistance (MIC > 256 µg/mL) was observed. The rifampicin-resistant cells were then tested for their susceptibility towards nusbiarylins. Compared to the type strain, the rifampicin-resistant lineages remained susceptible to the nusbiarylin compounds tested. To fully understand the impact of nusbiarylins in bacterial cells, RNA sequencing was performed to dissect the transcriptomic changes of MRSA in the presence of MC4-134. Compared to the untreated group, MC4-134 downregulated the expression of 38 ribosomal proteins, genes (fusA, secY, rpoA ,rim ,trmD ,tsf , and infC) located within the ribosomal protein operons, and the genes encoding tRNA synthetases. On the other hand, rifampicin, however, stimulated the expression of those genes suppressed by MC4-134. Additionally, MC4-134 reduced expression levels of toxin-producing genes, such as hla in S. aureus. The compound effects on the bacterial transcription machinery in live cells were examined by fluorescent microscopy. Fluorescent B. subtilis strain BS61 producing GFP-tagged NusB was cultivated with or without MC4-134/MC4-135. The cellular NusB proteins in the control group were identified at the sub-nucleoid regions of transcription foci. Compared to the untreated cells, while the translation inhibitor chloramphenicol did not affect the NusB alignment, substantial diffusion of the GFP signals into the cytosol was seen in rifampicin and nusbiarylins-treated B. subtilis. To further distinguish the mode of action of MC4-135 from CHL and colistin which disrupted cell membrane, experiments were conducted using the engineered B. subtilis strains producing GFP-tagged RpoC (the catalytic RNAP subunit), ribosomal protein RpsB, or membrane protein MreB. Whilst the localisation of RNAP, RpsB, and MreB was interrupted by the antimicrobials with corresponding mechanisms, MC4-134/MC4-135 did not cause any observable difference compared to the untreated cells. These results suggested that nusbiarylins affected rRNA transcription at the cellular level and affected the subcellular localisation of transcription machineries.

14100120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100120.value: We discovered a new class of chemical agents with outstanding antimicrobial activities and a well-demonstrated mechanism. The NusB-NusE dimerisation presents an essential step in bacterial rRNA transcription, rendering this protein-protein interaction (PPI) a potential target for novel antibiotic development. We previously discovered the class of NusB-NusE PPI inhibitors, namely nusbiarylins, with antibacterial effects. In this work, we assessed the antimicrobial activities of the nusbiarylin mini-library, and validated the mechanism using four representative nusbiarylin compounds MC4-134, MC4-135, MC4-190, and MC4-205. These compounds demonstrated potential for further development into antimicrobial candidates, suggested by their particular antimicrobial effects against various Gram-positive pathogens, including multiple drug-resistant lineages of VRE, PRSP, MRSA, and VRSA. Remarkably, MC4-134 could also arrest the growth of several significant Gram-negative bacteria that are considered as the WHO bacterial priority pathogens. Subsequent assays demonstrated their bacteriostatic effects, suppression of cellular ATP levels, low chances of resistance generation, and no antagonism with all tested marketed drugs in clinical staphylococcal strains. Our data implicated the possibility of nusbiarylin compounds as novel antimicrobial candidates. Following the characterisation of antimicrobial potency, we also established the molecular mechanism of nusbiarylins in this work. Nusbiarylins were rationally designed to disrupt the NusB-NusE PPI during bacterial rRNA synthesis, thereby affecting cell viability. In this work, we selected MC4-134 and MC4-135 for mechanistic studies due to their antimicrobial effects. These two derivatives were verified to bind to NusB proteins, inhibit the NusB-NusE PPI, reduce RNAP processivity, and suppress the gene expression for ribosomal proteins. The experimental data provide evidence that our nusbiarylin compound acted as the bacterial rRNA transcription inhibitor, with a novel mode of action compared to current antibiotics on the market. In summary, this work provided a set of compounds, with two more potent derivatives, MC4-134 and MC4-135, with potential for developing novel antimicrobial agents with a unique mode of action. The discovery of bacterial rRNA transcription inhibitors with antibacterial effects could also expand the antimicrobial classes for combating the re-emergence of drug-resistant pathogens worldwide. Additionally, our data validated the use of the pharmacophore-based in silico screening approach in identifying PPI inhibitors. This screening platform could be expanded for discovering other inhibitors of essential PPIs for bacterial proliferation, with a focus on prokaryotic RNA synthesis.

14100120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100120.value: Future research on nusbiarylins will be conducted for a more comprehensive mechanism and later in vivo efficacy. Understanding the mode-of-action of MC4-series compounds is crucial to establishing a complete molecular mechanism and validating this class of bacterial rRNA synthesis inhibitors. New nusbiarylin compounds will also be tested for antimicrobial activity to identify more potent derivatives. Future studies will focus on the efficacy, druggability, and safety profiles of the selected nusbiarylins. Cytotoxicity will be investigated to examine if any toxicity of compounds against human cells. Subsequent pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic assays will be carried out to understand the compound distribution in different tissues, penetration into target sites, and in vivo toxicity for optimising compound doses prior to setting up animal infection models. Eventually, animal models with either localised or systemic bacterial infections such as wound infection, lung infection, and CNS infection could be established for testing the compound in vivo antibacterial effects. This work paves the way of development of a new class of antimicrobial drug.

14100120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100120.value: We have developed a new group of antibiotic compounds called nusbiarylins, designed to target a crucial protein interaction in bacteria that is essential for making ribosomes, the cell’s protein factories. By blocking this interaction, nusbiarylins can stop bacteria from growing and multiplying. In laboratory tests, several nusbiarylin compounds were highly effective against a wide range of dangerous bacteria, including drug-resistant strains like MRSA and VRE. Some compounds worked at very low doses, and even bacteria that were resistant to other antibiotics remained sensitive to nusbiarylins. The researchers confirmed that these compounds work by specifically binding to their target protein and disrupting the process bacteria use to make ribosomes. Further tests showed that nusbiarylins reduce the activity of key bacterial genes and proteins, and do not easily lead to resistance. Importantly, these new antibiotics did not interfere with other common antibiotics, suggesting they could be used together. Overall, nusbiarylins represent a promising new approach to fighting bacterial infections, especially those that no longer respond to existing drugs

14100420.label: Realisation of objectives
14100420.value: There are three aims proposed for this 36-month project, and we have successfully finished all the aims according to the original proposal (and also expanded findings on microRNAs and microRNA clusters to test in more insects and other animals). All in all, this is a truly very successful project, and we are very grateful and would like to sincerely thank for the generosity, trust and continuous support of the RGC such that we can achieve what we propose. In terms of publications, 12 research papers have been resulted as to date, including 9 research articles and 3 review articles.
