14100420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100420.value: Major findings - Insect metamorphosis played a profound role in their successful adaptation and radiation. Despite there are genuine differences between sexes during insect metamorphosis which facilitate their successful mating, how such sexual dimorphism in metamorphosis is being controlled is poorly known. In this eLife paper, following our original proposal for Aims 1, 2, and 3, we carried out in silico, in vitro, as well as in vivo analysing the different mutants generated in this project and utilising a combination of state-of-art technologies, we revealed differential gene pathways being regulated by members of miR-277/34 between sexes during metamorphosis, highlighting how members of a microRNA cluster control hormonal and developmental gene pathways in different sexes of insects during metamorphosis for the first time. - In parallel, we have also investigated the microRNA expression in various insects (Aim 3), including the sex-biased expression of a microRNA cluster in butterfly (BMC Biology), moth (Genomics), stinkbug (BMC Genomics), and bedbug (Insect Science). - In addition to the original aims, we have also expanded the understanding of sesquiterpenoid in microRNA and sesquiterpenoid in non-insect invertebrates, including sea anemones (Proceedings of Royal Society B; Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology), coral (Frontiers in Marine Science), and centipedes and millipedes (Nature Communications). Research Outcome: - 12 research papers (9 research articles and 3 review articles), including high-quality research articles published in journals eLife, BMC Biology, Proceedings of Royal Society B, and Nature Communications - Staff involved in this project became a Lecturer in a local university - 2 MPhil and 1 PhD students were trained (with 1 more PhD student to be expected to graduate in 2025) - Undergraduates were trained, including one student who decided to further pursue PhD on this project - Make presentations at international conferences - Make collaborations

14100420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100420.value: There could be multiple lines (on both basic and applied science) that can be further built on this project, including: Basic science: 1) investigation of microRNAs regulation on controlling various hormones in combination with sesquiterpenoid hormones in insects, including both drosophilids and those beneficial insects and insect pests; 2) understanding the regulation of insect biology such as metamorphosis between different sexes; and 3) decipher how different microRNA clusters function and cooperate in regulate genes in animals evolution and development. Applied science: 4) enhancing agricultural production by way of either manipulation of promoting beneficial insects such as the pollinators as well as combating agricultural pests.

14100420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100420.value: Insects comprise the largest numbers of described animal species in the world dominating diverse terrestrial habitats. Global warming/climate change has increased the metabolic rate and population growth of pest insects that has negative impacts on both crop production and human health. Insect growth, development and reproduction is dependent on sesquiterpenoid hormones. The biosynthetic pathway that leads to the production of these hormones is well known, however, the precise roles of noncoding RNAs, such as microRNAs, that control the insect sesquiterpenoid pathway are yet to be discovered. In this project, we have uncovered the evolutionary and developmental roles of microRNAs as well as revealed their roles in regulation of sesquiterpenoid genes in different insects and animals. We have also unexpectedly revealed that the biology of males and females animals are regulated differently by microRNAs. This opens up new avenue for further research. Practically, since sesquiterpenoids is crucial in regulation of biological processes in insects, interruption of sesquiterpenoids has been considered as a strategy for development of bio-rationale insecticides. This project has also provided novel baseline information for future development in enhancing agricultural production by promoting beneficial insects (such as the pollinators) as well as combating agricultural pests.

14100620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100620.value: Skeletal muscle has a remarkable ability to regenerate after injury thus provides an excellent model to study tissue regeneration. Muscle regeneration relies on its resident muscle stem cells (also called satellite cells, SCs) which normally lie quiescently beneath muscle fiber. SCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergoes self-renewal and returns to quiescence to replenish SC pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulations may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia. Transcriptional regulation lies in the center of gene regulatory mechanisms but our knowledge of its importance in the early stages of SC quiescence and activation remains incomplete. Here we propose to investigate the functional roles of AP-1 transcription factor (TF) family in SC. We found Atf3 and several other AP-1 members were rapidly induced upon SC isolation; inducible deletion of Atf3 in SCs caused precocious activation of the cells thus accelerated acute injury induced regeneration. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, by combined RNA-seq and ChIP-seq, we found Atf3 binds and regulates Histone2B (H2B) biosynthesis; Atf3 ablation led to H2B loss, which caused transcriptomic gene activation and changes of chromatin accessibility revealed by ATAC-seq. We further demonstrated Atf3 loss also led to genome instability and enhanced replicative senescence in SCs. Altogether, these preliminary results promoted us to hypothesize that Atf3 acts as a critical sensor of stress stimuli and its rapid induction serves to maintain H2B level and SC quiescence in homeostatic muscle; ablation of Atf3 leads to H2B decrease and alteration of nucleosome organization/ structure, which induces transcriptomic amplification, rendering SCs to exit quiescence and become precociously activated. Three aims are thus proposed (1) to further dissect the impact of Atf3 loss on SC behaviors in muscle regeneration and aging. (2) to further elucidate Atf3 regulation of nucleosome integrity and genome stability via H2B. (3) to screen for functional AP-1 family TFs in SCs and regeneration. Once completed, this study will be the first to uncover Atf3 and AP-1 family as novel regulators of SC function and muscle regeneration; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the transcriptional regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle homeostasis and regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. 骨骼肌在損傷後具有驚人的再生能力，這種特性為研究組織再生提供了一種極好的模型。這種肌肉的再生功能依賴於其所附著的肌肉幹細胞（也被稱為衛星細胞），它們通常情況下位於肌纖維的下方，並維持在相對靜息的狀態。一旦受到損傷，衛星細胞就會迅速激活並增殖成為成肌細胞，然後分化並融合進入新生的肌纖維。與此同時，一小部分成肌細胞會進行自我跟新從而回到靜息狀態以補充衛星細胞庫。这進程的每一個階段都由內在和外在因子/機制組成的的複雜調節網路系統進行調控。調控系統的破壞會導致肌肉失去再生能力，從而引起肌肉萎縮等病變，例如肌營養不良，惡病質以及少肌症。轉錄調控是基因表达調控機制的核心方式之一，但是目前我們對於其在衛星細胞靜息狀態以及早期激活狀態下的重要性還是知之甚少。 這裡我們希望能夠研究AP-1轉錄因數家族在衛星細胞中的功能作用。 我們發現在衛星細胞分離提取過程中會很快地誘導Atf3和其它一些AP-1家族成員表達；同時我們發現在衛星細胞中誘導型敲除Atf3會導致細胞過早地激活，從而加速了急性損傷導致的肌肉再生過程。為了闡明潛在的機制，通過結合RNA-seq和ChIP-seq数据，我們發現Atf3能夠結合並調節組蛋白2B（H2B）生物合成；Atf3敲除導致H2B蛋白丟失，這進一步導致轉錄組水準上的基因表達啟動和染色質开放状态的變化。我們進一步證明了Atf3的缺失還會導致基因組不穩定性上升以及衛星細胞中細胞複製導致的衰老和基因損傷增加。總而言之，這些初步結果促使我們有理由相信，Atf3可以作為衛星細胞感應壓力刺激的關鍵感測器，並且它的快速誘導表達可以在處於穩態的肌肉中維持H2B水準衛星細胞的靜息狀態；Atf3的敲除導致H2B減少以及核小體組織/結構的改變，從而誘導基因組轉錄水準上升，進一步導致衛星細胞離開靜息狀態並過早的被激活。基於以上資料，我們提出了三個主要的研究目標：（1）進一步解析Atf3敲除對肌肉再生和衰老過程中衛星細胞行為的影響。 (2)進一步闡明Atf3如何通過調節H2B影響核小體完整性和基因組穩定性。 (3) 進一步篩選在衛星細胞及肌肉再生過程中有重要功能的其它AP-1家族轉錄因數。一旦完成，這項研究將會首次發現Atf3和AP-1家族能夠作為衛星細胞功能和肌肉再生的新型調控因子; 因此，它將增強我們對於骨骼肌維持穩態和再生功能的認識，特別是轉錄調控機制方面的知識，以便為未來開發用於治療肌肉損傷和疾病的方法提供理論基礎。

14100620.label: Realisation of objectives
14100620.value: Aim1: To further dissect the impact of Atf3 loss on SC behavior in muscle regeneration and muscle aging. This Aim has been 100% realized. To facilitate the dissection of ATF3 function in SCs, we generate control (Ctrl) (Atf3+/+- Pax7CreERT2/CreERT2-R26RYFP/YFP) and inducible knockout mice of Atf3 (Atf3 iKO) (Atf3 flox/ flox- Pax7CreERT2/CreERT2-R26RYFP/YFP). Morphologically, the 2-month-old iKO showed no apparent difference from the Ctrl littermate mice; no changes in body size and weight were detected either. Considering the rapid induction of ATF3 during early SC activation, we reasoned that its loss might impact SC-mediated muscle regeneration. To test this notion, BaCl2 was injected into the TA muscles of Ctrl or iKO mice to induce acute muscle damage after TMX deletion. By examining the above injured TA muscles, the iKO muscles displayed a highly accelerated rate of regeneration. Surprisingly, the enhanced regenerative ability of Atf3 iKO SCs persisted after one more round of BaCl2-induced acute injury given one month later. The expedited repair was still evident after the 3rd-round of injury, despite slightly increased TA muscle weight in the iKO compared to the Ctrl 30d post-3rd injury, but there was no significant difference in the average muscle fiber size, suggesting that the accelerated regeneration in the iKO muscle eventually disappeared after the 3rd-injury. The engraftment assay was then conducted to further validate the enhanced regenerative ability of the iKO SCs. The engraftment assay further confirmed the enhanced regenerative ability of the iKO SCs. Altogether, our results demonstrate that Atf3 deletion enhances acute injury-induced muscle regeneration. We confirmed that compared to the Ctrl, the faster activation of iKO cells upon acute injury implies the quicker transition from quiescence to activation. Moreover, the loss of ATF3 results in the release from quiescence and thus rapid SC activation without acute injury. Altogether, these results suggest that Atf3 deletion provokes the precocious activation of SCs in homeostatic muscles thus ATF3 may function to actively suppress SC activation. This was further strengthened by overexpressing ATF3 in FISCs by a lentivirus; it significantly inhibited SC activation. Moreover, overexpressing ATF3 in vivo by intramuscular injection of the lentivirus particles at 1dpi delayed the regeneration in Ctrl mice and also blunted the accelerated regeneration in iKO mice. In addition, we observed that Atf3 deletion may accelerate SC progeny differentiation. Interestingly, Atf3 loss may also lead to impaired self-renewal. Consistently, we also noticed a progressive decline in SC number after each round of injury. Next, to test if long-term Atf3 deficiency causes SC exhaustion and impairs muscle regeneration, we induced muscle injury 30d or 120d after deleting Atf3 from SCs. 30d after the deletion, the muscle regeneration showed no significant changes compared to the Ctrl mice. In contrast, 120d after the deletion, the muscle regeneration was obviously compromised in the iKO compared to the Ctrl mice. suggesting that enhanced regenerative ability of the iKO cells persists after long-term ATF3 loss and the impaired muscle regeneration indeed arises from the reduced cell pool. To further establish the importance of Atf3 in SC establishment and maintenance, we successfully deleted Atf3 in Pax7+ myogenic progenitors by crossing the Atf3flox allele with a non-inducible Pax7Cre-R26RYFP transgenic mouse strain, in which the Cre recombinase is expressed in Pax7+ progenitor cells in as early as E9.5. We further noticed that ATF3 is required for SC maintenance at adulthood but dispensable for SC establishment and correspondingly, the regenerative capacity after acute injury was evidently compromised in cKO muscles. Therefore, the loss of ATF3 induces precocious SC activation and leads to the eventual reduction of the SC pool. To further prove the function of ATF3 in preventing SC activation, we sought to determine if the ATF3 depletion influences the Short-term or non-strenuous voluntary exercise (VE) and endurance exercise (EE)-induced SC activation. Our data indicate that the loss of ATF3 provokes SC activation by both VE and EE. Aim2: To further elucidate Atf3 regulation of nucleosome integrity and genome stability via H2B. This Aim has been 100% realized. To determine if the H2B loss in the iKO SCs alters nucleosome positioning and occupancy, CUT&RUN assay was performed to map the genomic localization of H2B in Ctrl and iKO cells. Unexpectedly, the average H2B CUT&RUN signals were largely unaltered in the iKO vs. Ctrl with only 3429 bins (1.4%) showing changes. Nevertheless, 3220 out of the altered bins indeed showed decreased H2B enrichment in various genomic regions, including promoter (12%), gene body (39%) and intergenic regions (49%). Since the nucleosome is partly dissembled through the removal of one H2A-H2B dimer to facilitate Pol II transcription, we hypothesized that the local loss of H2B could facilitate nucleosome destabilization to promote the transcription of associated genes. Indeed, by intersecting with RNA-Seq, 137 up-regulated genes showed decreased H2B signals on their promoters or gene bodies. These H2B target genes were enriched for GO terms related to muscle differentiation and also included Id3, IGF-1 and Jun, etc., which was consistent with the activation state of the iKO SCs. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that the decreased H2B level could mediate the precocious SC activation following the ATF3 loss. To solidify the functional link between ATF3 and H2B in SC activation and muscle regeneration, we found that overexpressing H2B by plasmid in FISCs indeed repressed the accelerated activation of Atf3 iKO cells but no impact on Ctrl cells. In vivo, we also overexpressed H2B by lentiviral particles and our data validate that H2B loss mediates the precocious SC activation and enhanced muscle regeneration observed upon ATF3 loss. To further elucidate the consequence of H2B loss in SCs, we examined genome instability and cellular senescence considering histone proteins are important for chromatin integrity and genome stability. Our findings demonstrate that H2B loss leads to increased genome instability and cellular senescence in the Atf3 iKO cells. Aim3: To screen for functional AP-1 family TFs in SCs and regeneration. This Aim has been 100% realized. To screen for functional AP-1 family TFs in SCs and regeneration, we conducted a functional screening using our recently developed Pax7Cas9/AAV-sgRNA mediated in vivo genome editing platform, which is based on a Cre-dependent Cas9 knock-in mice and AAV-mediated sgRNAs delivery. Similar to Atf3 KO, the Fos-KD cells showed accelerated SC activation while the JunB-KD displayed blunted activation; the Atf4 or FosB-KD, on the other hand, did not have any impact. When measuring Pax7+ cells on ~2-month-old uninjured muscles, reduced numbers were observed upon the Atf4, Fos or JunB-KD, suggesting a loss of SC pool. Since the Atf4 or JunB-KD did not lead to precocious SC activation, the SC number loss may be caused by other reasons considering the deletion occurred very early in the postnatal stage. The FosB-KD did not have any impact on the Pax7+ SC pool. To further investigate the impact on muscle regenerative ability, BaCl2 was injected 7-weeks after AAV injection and the regeneration was assessed. An impaired regeneration was revealed in the Atf4 and Fos-KD presumably because of the exhaustion of SCs after its long-term deletion; The regeneration in the JunB-KD was also compromised probably due to a reduced SC pool; consistently, no impact on the regeneration was observed in the FosB-KD. Altogether, our results indicated that these AP-1 family members may play diverse functions in SC activation and muscle regeneration.

14100620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100620.value: We report that AP-1 family member ATF3 (Activating Transcription Factor 3) prevents SC premature activation. Atf3 is rapidly and transiently induced in SCs upon activation. Short-term deletion of Atf3 in SCs accelerates acute injury-induced regeneration, and however, its long-term deletion exhausts the SC pool and thus impairs muscle regeneration. The Atf3 loss also provokes SC activation during voluntary exercise and enhances SC activation during endurance exercise. Mechanistically, ATF3 directly activates the transcription of Histone 2B genes, whose reduction accelerates nucleosome displacement and gene transcription required for SC activation. Finally, the ATF3-dependent H2B expression also prevents genome instability and replicative senescence in SCs. Therefore, this study has revealed a novel mechanism for preserving the SC population by actively suppressing precocious activation, in which ATF3 is a key regulator. These findings have been published on Nature Communications in 2023 and presented on 1 international conference and 1 local conference; 3 PhD students were trained through the project; and collaborations have been established with 3 local and international research groups.

14100620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100620.value: First, our study shows that it is possible that ATF3 plays previously unappreciated roles in stem cell homeostasis and regeneration in general. We can further explore ATF3 functions in other types of stems cells. Secondly, our data suggests that genome-wide nucleosome occupancy may not be largely impacted. It is likely the reduced amount of H2B may lead to formation of non-canonical nucleosomes. These possibilities can be investigated in detail by additional approaches. The function of these sub-nucleosomes in transcription is still unclear, it is possible that they prevalently exist in the iKO cells and alter the overall nucleosome structure and chromatin properties, therefore explaining the overall transcriptional activation occurring in the cell. In addition, the existence of these sub-nucleosomes may also affect genomic stability and increase the propensity for DNA damage thus cellular senescence, which was indeed observed in the iKO cells. Aging-coupled histone loss also results in elevated levels of DNA strand breaks and genomic instability, it will thus be interesting to examine whether ATF3 loss will accelerate SC aging which is known to contribute to muscle tissue aging. Lastly, other AP-1 family members’ potential functions also can be validated during the transition from quiescence to early activation.

14100620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100620.value: Skeletal muscles have regenerative ability in response to injury or stress stimulations. Muscle regeneration relies on activation and expansion of muscle stem cells, also known as satellite cells (SCs). Here we elucidate novel mechanism governing early activation phase of SCs. A transcription factor protein ATF3 is sharply and transiently induced at the very early stage of SC activation upon even minor stress. Loss of ATF3 unexpectedly renders SCs to exit quiescence and enter early activation. The cells thus display heightened ability to activate and regenerate after acute injury-induced muscle damage and show rapid activation in exercise. Consequently, long-term ATF3 deletion leads to premature SC activation and pseudo-regeneration in homeostatic muscle, thus impairing acute injury-induced muscle regeneration. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that ATF3 binds and promotes the transcription of Histone2B (H2B). Atf3 ablation leads to decreased H2B, thus accelerating nucleosome displacement during transcription to upregulate genes relevant for SC activation. The H2B loss also results in genome instability and enhances replicative senescence in SCs. Lastly, through a functional screening we demonstrate that other AP-1 family TFs may also play diversified functions in SC activation and acute damage-induced muscle regeneration. Altogether, we have unveiled previously unknown molecular underpinnings that govern SC function.

14102220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102220.value: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a rare genetic disease that affects the muscles and other systems of patients. DM1 is caused by a CTG repeat expansion in the 3’UTR of the human DMPK gene. Ribonuclear foci containing the CUG RNA repeats are formed in the nuclei, which sequesters splicing factors, such as mbl/MBNL1, causing impairment of the splicing machinery. While DM1 is generally recognized as a muscular dystrophy, DM1 is a multi-systemic disease that harbours neuropathology. Unlike the muscle pathology, the neuropathological aspect of DM1 is relatively less explored. Here, we established a novel Drosophila DM1 model using the larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ). Remarkably, we observed synapse loss only when CUG repeats were expressed in both presynaptic motor neurons and postsynaptic muscles. Larvae expressing the CUG repeats had a lower density of active zones in their motor neurons, formed ribonuclear foci in the nuclei of motor neurons and muscles, and exhibited locomotor defects. Previous studies in Drosophila had demonstrated that splicing defects can result in dysregulation of isoforms of the adhesion molecule FasII (NCAM in mammals). Thus, we investigated isoform changes of FasII at the NMJ, and found that one of the isoforms of FasII, namely FasII-C, was significantly upregulated. We hypothesized that this upregulation might be the cause of neuropathological symptoms in our DM1 model, and found that overexpression of FasII-C was indeed sufficient to induce similar neuropathology. Furthermore, knockdown of FasII-C was able to rescue synapse loss. Moreover, mbl mutants exhibit similar neuropathological phenotypes as well, indicating that sequestration of mbl might be a cause of the upregulation of FasII-C. In Aim 1, we seek to complete our characterization of our Drosophila DM1 model of neuropathology using immunohistochemistry and live-imaging techniques, as well as to determine whether the severity of synapse loss has a CUG repeat length dependency. In Aim 2, we aim to uncover the underlying mechanism of DM1 neuropathology by manipulating FasII-C and mbl in motor neurons or muscles alone. Also to attempt rescuing the synapse loss by restoring intracellular signaling of FasII molecules by overexpressing FasII-A-PEST+ together with the CUG repeats. In Aim 3, we will determine if neuropathology in DM1 would accelerate muscle degeneration. In Aim 4, we will extend our study to mammals by investigating DMSXL mouse tissues. This project will provide us with mechanistic insights on the neuropathology of DM1, and identify important molecules and pathways that contribute to DM1 pathogenesis. 1型強直性營養不良（DM1）是一種罕見的遺傳性疾病，影響患者的肌肉和其他系統。 DM1是由人DMPK基因3'UTR中的CTG重複擴增引起的。CUG重複序列 RNA在細胞核中形成，導致剪接機制受損。DM1是一種多系統疾病，具有神經病理學特徵。與肌肉病理學不同，DM1的神經病理學方面的研究相對較少。我們建立了神經肌肉接頭（NMJ）的DM1果蠅幼蟲模型。在突觸前運動神經元和突觸後肌肉均表達CUG重複RNA時才觀察到突觸丟失。表達CUG重複RNA序列的果蠅幼蟲在其運動神經元中具有較低的活動區密度，在運動神經元和肌肉的核中形成核糖核灶，並表現出運動缺陷。之前研究發現，剪接缺陷可能導致粘附分子FasII（在哺乳動物中為NCAM）的異構體失調。因此，我們調查了NMJ FasII的異構體變化，發現FasII的異構體之一，即FasII-C，被顯著上調。我們假設這種上調可能是我們DM1模型中神經病理症狀的原因，並且發現FasII-C的過表達足以誘導類似的神經病理。此外，FasII-C的敲低能夠挽救突觸損失。此外，mbl突變體也表現出相似的神經病理學表型，表明mbl的隔離可能是FasII-C上調的原因。在目標1中，我們尋求使用免疫組織化學和實時成像技術以觀察果蠅DM1神經病理模型的表徵，並確定突觸丟失的嚴重性是否具有CUG重複RNA長度的依賴性。在目標2中，我們旨在通過僅在運動神經元或肌肉中操縱FasII-C和mbl來揭示DM1神經病理學的病理機制，並通過度表達FasII-A-PEST+和CUG重複來恢復FasII分子的細胞內信號傳導來挽救突觸丟失。在目標3中，我們將確定DM1中的神經病理學是否會加速肌肉變性。在目標4中，我們將通過研究DMSXL小鼠組織將研究擴展到哺乳動物。此項目將為我們提供有關DM1神經病理學的機制性見解。

14102220.label: Realisation of objectives
14102220.value: 1. Characterization of synapse retraction and synaptic transmission phenotypes in our Drosophila DM1 model. We have fully achieved this objective. We found that the loss of synapses only occurs when expanded CUG repeats are simultaneously co-expressed in both the motor neurons and the muscles at the neuromuscular junction. We then successfully determined the approximate time course of neuropathological progression by dissecting and analysing NMJs of different larval stages, and found that the loss of synapses only occurs in 3rd instar larval stage but not earlier. This indicates that synapse retraction and arbor disassembly occur during the 3rd instar larval stage in our DM1 model. In fact, locomotor activity was also found to be most severely impaired when CUG repeats are simultaneously expressed in both cell types. 2. Unravel the mechanism of synapse loss in our DM1 model. We have fully achieved this objective. We successfully identified the upregulation of Fasciclin II (FasII) (the Drosophila orthologue of mammalian neural cell adhesion molecule 1, NCAM1) as a major contributor to the synaptic defects we observed. We were able to rescue our DM1 model by knocking down fasII at the NMJ. In fact, using the dual binary expression systems of GAL4/UAS and LexA/LexAop, we found that the knockdown of FasII in either just the presynaptic motor neurons or the postsynaptic muscles was sufficient to rescue the NMJ defects in our DM1 model. Out of all the FasII isoforms we tested, only overexpression of FasII-C mimicked the phenotypes of expanded CUG expression. We further investigated the impact of FasII-C on synaptic transmission using electrophysiology, and found synergistic impairment effects on both spontaneous vesicle release and evoked response when FasII-C is simultaneously overexpressed pre- and postsynaptically. Remarkably, we were able to fully rescue our DM1 model by overexpressing the FasII-A-PEST+ isoform, the endogenous major isoform in neurons that possesses a cytoplasmic domain to convey signals into the cell. These results strongly suggested that the CUG repeat-mediated upregulation of FasII-C is a major contributor of the synaptic and behavioral defects in our DM1 model, and we can rescue these phenotypes by knocking down total FasII in either the motor neurons or the muscles, or by overexpressing FasII-A-PEST+ to restore the disrupted ratio of FasII isoforms at the synapses and to recover proper intracellular signaling. 3. Determine whether neuropathology would enhance/accelerate muscle degeneration in the Drosophila model of DM1. We have completed the experiments for this objective. Unfortunately, our results did not show enhancement/acceleration of muscle degeneration. But in contrast, we found that the CUG-induced RNA toxicity in muscles actually enhances the loss of synapses and arbor disassembly of the motor neurons. 4. Examine if the phenotypes and mechanisms in our Drosophila DM1 model are also present in DMSXL mice. We have fully achieved this objective. We found that the dysregulation of NCAM1 to be also present in the DMSXL mouse model. Furthermore, this dysregulation was even observed in DM1 patient neural and muscular tissues, supporting the notion that our findings in Drosophila are truly translatable to mammals and even humans.

14102220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102220.value: We capitalized the highly stereotypical and accessible Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ) system to study the effect of untranslated CUG repeats on synaptic functions and behavior. The larval NMJ is characterized by its high level of plasticity during development, and with large synapses that are easy to visualize and to record from. We utilized this Drosophila DM1 model, and expressed CUG repeats in the presynaptic motor neurons (MNs) and/or the postsynaptic body wall muscles (BWMs) at the NMJ. We showed that the loss of synaptic boutons only occurs when expanded CUG repeats are simultaneously expressed in both the MNs and BWMs. Impairment of larval locomotor activity was also found to be the most severe when CUG repeats are simultaneously expressed in both cell types. We then further characterized the CUG repeat-mediated arbor disassembly at the NMJ, determined the approximate time course of neuropathological progression, and identified the upregulation of Fasciclin II (FasII) (the Drosophila orthologue of mammalian neural cell adhesion molecule 1, NCAM1) as a major contributor to the synaptic defects we observed. Dysregulation of NCAM1 was also observed in the DMSXL mouse model and in DM1 patients, supporting the relevance of our findings in Drosophila. Knockdown of the upregulated fasII resulted in the rescue of both NMJ morphological and locomotor behavioral phenotypes. We found that the knockdown of FasII in either just the presynaptic MNs or the postsynaptic BWMs was sufficient to rescue the NMJ defects in our DM1 model. Out of all the FasII isoforms we tested, only overexpression of FasII-C mimicked the phenotypes of expanded CUG expression. We further investigated the impact of FasII-C on synaptic transmission using electrophysiology, and found synergistic impairment effects on both spontaneous vesicle release and evoked response when FasII-C is simultaneously overexpressed pre- and postsynaptically. Remarkably, we were able to fully rescue our DM1 model by overexpressing the FasII-A-PEST+ isoform, the endogenous major isoform in neurons that possesses a cytoplasmic domain to convey signals into the cell. These results strongly suggested that the CUG480-mediated upregulation of FasII-C is a major contributor of the synaptic and behavioral defects in our DM1 model, and we can rescue these phenotypes by knocking down total FasII in either MNs or BWMs, or by overexpressing FasII-A-PEST+ to restore the disrupted ratio of FasII isoforms at the synapses and to recover proper intracellular signaling. These findings provided significant new insights into the underlying mechanisms of DM1 neuropathology.

14102220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102220.value: NCAM1 is the mammalian orthologue of Drosophila FasII. Both are part of the immunoglobulin (Ig) domain superfamily and possess homophilic cell-cell adhesion mediator activity. In humans, abnormal NCAM1-positive myofibers were observed in DM1 patient deltoid muscles (Santoro et al., 2010), which might have been caused by an increased expression of NCAM1. NCAM1 transcripts have also been reported to be upregulated in the frontal cortex of DM1 patients (Otero et al., 2021). In agreement with these previous reports, our data also showed increased levels of NCAM1 proteins in the spinal cord and tibialis anterior of DMSXL mice, as well as in the frontal cortex of DM1 patients and transdifferentiated myotubes derived from DM1 patient cells. However, we observed that the deltoids of DM1 patients actually had a lower expression NCAM1 than control individuals (Koon et al. (unpublished)). It is possible that different types of skeletal muscles in higher organisms have different NCAM1 dysregulations under the toxicity of the expanded CUG repeats. In the future, we will study the underlying mechanisms behind the dysregulation of NCAM1 in DM1 using mammalian disease models. In particular, we will examine how splicing regulators, e.g. MBNL1, are involved in NCAM1 dysregulation.

14102220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102220.value: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a multisystemic disorder that has been extensively studied for decades, yet our understanding of its neuropathological aspect remains rudimentary. In this study, we characterized a novel model of DM1 neuropathology by expressing untranslated expanded CUG repeats at the Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction. In this model, both pre- and postsynaptic expression of CUG repeats participate to induce reduction of synaptic boutons, increase of arbor disassembly and impairment of larval locomotor activity. We found that the expression of CUG repeats caused an upregulation of the cell adhesion molecule, FasII (NCAM1 in mammals), in both the motor neurons and the body wall muscles. Knockdown of fasII was sufficient to rescue bouton numbers and locomotor impairment in this model. Further analyses identified the upregulation of the FasII-C isoform as a major contributor of these phenotypes. Remarkably, overexpressing the FasII-A-PEST+ isoform rescued the synaptic and behavioral defects, likely by outcompeting the upregulated FasII-C. Our study provided the foundation for a basic mechanism of synapse dysregulation in DM1.

14102620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102620.value: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major health problem, with an overall prevalence of 11 % in China and in the world. Renal fibrosis is the final common pathway of all forms of CKD. Renal tubular epithelial cells constitute >90% of the kidney mass, and tubular epithelial cells play a key role in orchestrating renal fibrosis by secreting various profibrotic factors including inflammatory cytokines. Over the last 20 years, no new drugs have been approved to specifically prevent CKD due to our incomplete understanding of the mechanisms underlying CKD. The Hippo/YAP pathway regulates organ size, tumorigenesis and inflammation. In this pathway, the serine/threonine kinases MST1 and MST2, homologs of Hippo in Drosophila, phosphorylate LATS1/2. Activated LATS1/2 in turn phosphorylate the main effectors of the Hippo pathway, YAP and TAZ, resulting in their cytoplasmic sequestration and degradation. When Hippo signaling is inactivated, unphosphorylated YAP and TAZ translocate into the nucleus to function as transcription co-activators. Previous studies suggested a role of YAP in renal fibrogenesis. However, the role of tubular YAP in renal fibrosis has not been directly examined. We now found that activation of YAP by tubule-specific double knockout of the upstream kinases Mst1 and Mst2 (Mst1/2 dKO) resulted in progressive inflammation, tubular injury and fibrosis, and these phenotypes were largely rescued by deletion of Yap. In kidneys subjected to unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) or ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI), YAP was highly activated in tubular cells. These results suggest that tubular YAP activation induces renal fibrosis. Furthermore, we have exciting preliminary results showing that TNF-α and YAP amplified the signaling activities of each other in renal tubular cells. In this proposal, we will further study the role of tubular YAP in renal fibrosis during kidney injury, and determine how tubular YAP activation induces renal fibrosis by 1) investigate whether tubular YAP promotes fibrosis induced by UUO and IRI; 2) examine whether TNF-α activates YAP activity in UUO and IRI kidneys and whether YAP mediates TNF-α’s action on renal fibrosis; 3) explore the mechanisms by which TNF-α activates YAP and YAP promotes TNF-α expression. The knowledge we gain about the role of tubular YAP in renal fibrogenesis and the underlying mechanisms would be of considerable importance in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis of renal fibrosis. These findings may be useful in the eventual development of novel therapeutic treatments for renal fibrosis and chronic kidney disease. 慢性腎病是威脅健康的重要問題，其發病率在中國或全球占11%左右。腎臟纖維化是所有慢性腎病的最後通路。腎小管上皮細胞占腎臟質量的90%以上，可通過分泌包括炎癥因子在內的促纖維化因子來參與調控腎臟纖維化。由於我們對慢性腎病的發病機理缺乏深入了解，以至於過去20多年來沒有專門用來預防或處理慢性腎病的藥物被批準。Hippo/YAP通路調節器官大小、腫瘤發生及炎癥。在這個通路中，絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶MST1和MST2對應於果蠅的Hippo，可使LATS1/2磷酸化，磷酸化的（激活的）LATS1/2可使Hippo通路的主要效應蛋白YAP和TAZ磷酸化，導致它們滯留在細胞質中被降解。如果Hippo信號被抑制，YAP和TAZ不被磷酸化、從而可以轉移到細胞核中發揮其轉錄輔助因子的功能。以前的研究認為YAP可能參與調節腎臟纖維化，但是這壹作用還沒有被直接證明。我們現在發現腎小管小管上皮細胞特異性雙敲Mst1和Mst2基因後使得腎小管YAP激活，進而逐步誘導腎臟炎癥、腎小管損傷以及纖維化，並且這些表型在腎小管Yap敲除後大部分消失。在單側輸尿管結紮（UUO）或缺血再灌註損傷（IRI）的腎臟中，腎小管上皮細胞中的YAP高度激活。這些結果提示腎小管YAP激活誘導腎臟纖維化。我們進壹步研究還發現TNF-a和YAP在腎小管上皮細胞中可相互促進放大各自活性。在本課題中，我們將更深入研究在受損腎臟中腎小管YAP在腎纖維化中的作用及其機理。我們將1）研究腎小管YAP是否促進UUO以及IRI誘導的腎纖維化；2）檢測在UUO及IRI腎臟中TNF-a是否促進YAP活性以及YAP是否介導TNF-對腎纖維化的促進作用；3）探索TNF-a激活YAP以及YAP促進TNF-a表達的分子機制。通過本研究所獲得的關於腎小管YAP在腎纖維化中的作用及機理的資料，對於推動我們對腎纖維化病理機制的認識具有重要意義，並可能為慢性腎病及腎纖維化的預防和處理提供新的靶點。

14102620.label: Realisation of objectives
14102620.value: Objective 1: Investigate whether tubular Yap promotes fibrosis induced by UUO and IRI. We find that tubular YAP activation promotes tubular injury and renal inflammation and fibrosis induced by unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) or cisplatin treatment. 1.1 YAP was activated at 6 hrs after UUO. We examined several important pathways at 6 h of UUO. YAP was already much activated at 6 hours of UUO. YAP expression was low in the tubular cells of sham-operated kidneys. Nuclear YAP became apparent in the epithelial cells of collecting ducts and thick-ascending limbs, but not proximal tubules at UUO6h. These results suggest tubular YAP in collecting ducts and distal nephrons is activated at early stages of UUO. Nuclear YAP was observed not only in collecting ducts and thick ascending limbs but also in proximal tubules at 3 and 7 days of UUO. YAP was also activated in proximal tubular cells in cisplatin-induced AKI. 1.2 Tubule-specific Yap knockout mice (Yapf/f;Ksp-Cre) developed polyuria. We generated tubule-specific Yap knockout (tuKO) mice by crossing Yapf/f with Ksp-Cre mice. In Ksp-Cre transgenic mice, Cre recombinase is expressed in collecting ducts and thick ascending limbs. Yap tuKO mice developed polyurea. RNA-Seq analysis revealed down-regulation of aquaporin (Aqp)-2, 3 and 4 in Yap tuKO kidneys. Further analysis showed that YAP interacted with the transcription factors GATA2, GATA3 and NFATc1 to regulate Aqp2 transcription. 1.3. Tubular Yap haploinsufficiency promoted renal inflammation at 6 h of UUO (UUO6h). Since homozygous Yap tuKO (Yapf/f;Ksp-cre) developed polyuria, we used heterozygous tubular Yap knockout (Yapf/w;Ksp-cre) mice (Yap tuHet), which showed normal urine output at baseline. Strikingly, expression of several inflammatory factors was already elevated at UUO6h, which was much attenuated by tubular Yap haploinsufficiency. These results suggest that the initial induction of renal inflammation is dependent on tubular YAP during obstructive kidney injury 1.3 Deletion of Yap in proximal tubules (PTs) aggravated renal inflammation and fibrosis induced by UUO. Although Yap tuHet mice showed normal AQP2, AQP3 and AQP4 expression at UUO6h, prolonged UUO such as UUO for 7 days led to decreased AQP2, AQP3 and AQP4 expression in the kidneys of Yap tuHet mice compared to WT mice, which may increase urine production. Therefore, we generated inducible PT-specific Yap knockout (ptKO) mice. Yap ptKO mice showed decreases in the mRNA levels of inflammatory factors and fibrotic markers; the protein levels of a-SMA, COL1 and FN1; and collagen deposition compared with WT mice at 7 days of UUO (UUO7d). These results suggest that sustained tubular YAP activation promotes kidney fibrosis. 1.4. Deletion of Yap in PTs promoted AKI induced by cisplatin. We induced AKI in WT and Yap ptKO mice by injecting cisplatin. Renal functional impairment induced by cisplatin was mitigated in Yap ptKO mice. Tubular injury was alleviated in Yap ptKO mice compared to WT mice. TUNEL assay showed that cell death was induced by cisplatin in WT kidneys, which was much reduced in Yap ptKO mice. The expression of Il-1b, Il-6, Cxcl2 and Tgf-b1 induced by cisplatin was down regulated by Yap ablation. Therefore, proximal tubular YAP activation aggravates AKI. Objective 2: Examine whether TNF-α activates YAP activity in UUO and IRI kidneys and whether YAP mediates TNF-α’s action on renal fibrosis. Our previous results showed that TNF-α increased YAP activity in IMCD3 cells, and neutralization of TNF-α inhibited YAP activity in Mst1/2 dKO kidneys. It remains to be determined whether neutralization of TNF-α also inhibits the YAP activity induced by pathological insults such as UUO and IRI. We intraperitoneally injected WT mice 2 days after UUO surgery with a TNF-α antibody at a dose of 5 mg/kg body weight. Control mice received an injection of nonspecific goat IgG at the same dose. TNF-α antibody did not apparently alter phospho-YAP and YAP levels in the kidneys subjected to UUO. Our results suggest that TNF-α may not play a major role in YAP activation during kidney injury. Objective 3: Explore the mechanisms by which TNF-α activates YAP and YAP promotes TNF-α expression. This Aim was designed to determine the mechanisms used by YAP to promote TNF-α expression. We now find that YAP promotes TNF-α expression partially via KLF5. 3.1. YAP did not stimulate Tnf-α (1.5 kb)-Luc activity. We examined the effects of YAP on Tnf-α promoter reporter activity. A 1.5 kb fragment from the mouse Tnf-α promoter was cloned into pGL4 reporter plasmid (Tnf-α-Luc). We transfected mouse inner medullary collecting duct (IMCD)3 cells with Tnf-α-Luc and pTK-RL in the presence of increasing amounts of constitutively active (ca) Yap (S127A). The results showed that Tnf-α-Luc activity was not altered by caYap. 3.2 YAP promoted KLF5 expression in vitro Our previously published data showed that YAP only slightly stimulated Tnf-α mRNA expression in IMCD3 cells. We suspect that Tnf-α may not be a major target of YAP. We now found that Klf5, a member of the Krüppel-like factors, which has been shown to be critically involved in tubular injury, inflammation and renal dysfunction, is a target of YAP. 3.3 Klf5 expression in the kidney was increased after UUO We performed UUO and found that Klf5 mRNA expression in the kidney was already increased at 6h of UUO compared to the sham-operated kidneys and further increased at day 7 of UUO. 3.4 Klf5 expression was increased in the kidneys of Mst1/2 dKO mice Klf5 mRNA was increased in the kidneys of Mst1/2 dKO mice at 4 and 8 weeks of age compared with the respective WT mice. KLF5 was primarily localized to the nuclei of tubular epithelial cells in Mst1/2 dKO kidneys, whereas it is barely detectable in WT kidneys. 3.5 Increased Klf5 expression in the kidneys of Mst1/2 dKO mice were dependent on YAP To examine whether YAP plays a role in Klf5 mRNA expression, we analyzed tubular Mst1, Mst2 and Yap triple knockout (tKO) mice. Strikingly, the increased Klf5 mRNA levels in Mst1/2 dKO kidneys were abolished by deletion of Yap. Therefore, increased Yap expression in Mst1/2 dKO kidneys is Yap dependent. 3.6 YAP promoted Klf5 transcription We performed ChIP-qPCR on medullae of WT and Yap cKO kidneys and found that YAP bound to the promoter of the Klf5 gene. Furthermore, YAP overexpression dose-dependently enhanced Klf5-Luc activity. These results suggest that YAP stimulates Klf5 transcription. 3.7 KLF5 mediates YAP’s action on kidney injury and fibrosis. We treated Mst1/2 dKO mice with the specific KLF5 inhibitor ML26434 or vehicle. ML264 treatment mitigated tubular lesions, reduced tubular cell death and lowered the expression of inflammatory factors including TNF-a in Mst1/2 dKO kidneys. These results suggest that KLF5 mediates the effects of YAP on kidney injury, TNF-α expression and inflammation. 3.8. YAP promotes AP-1 expression in tubular epithelial cells in the kidney AP-1 activation has been found to be a unifying mechanism for different fibrotic diseases. We found YAP promotes AP-1 expression and that Fosl1 is the primary target of YAP in renal tubular cells.

14102620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102620.value: 1. YAP promotes the expression of aquaporin (AQP)-2, 3 and 4 in the principal cells of the collecting ducts by interacting with the transcription factors GATA2, GATA3 and NFATc1. Complete Yap deletion in the collecting ducts leads to decreased expression of AQP-2, 3 and 4 and polyuria. 2. YAP activation represents an early response to obstructive kidney injury in mice. YAP is activated in renal tubules in a reverse order by unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). YAP activation in collecting ducts and distal nephrons is apparent at as early as 6 h of UUO, but YAP in proximal tubules is not activated at 6 h or 1 day and becomes slightly activated at 3 days and highly activated at 7 days of UUO. 3. YAP is activated in the proximal tubular cells during acute kidney injury induced by cisplatin. 4. YAP promotes the transcription of AP-1 and KLF5, two important transcription factors involved in tubular injury and renal inflammation and fibrosis. 5. Tubular injury and renal inflammation induced by tubular YAP activation are dependent on KLF5. 6. YAP promotes TNF-α expression partially via KLF5, but TNF-α does not appear to play a major role in mediating the effects of YAP on tubular injury and renal inflammation and fibrosis.

14102620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102620.value: Our results demonstrate that tubular YAP activation promotes kidney injury and fibrosis. Studies by others show that YAP activation in fibroblasts also promotes renal fibrosis. We have preliminary results showing that YAP expression is very low in immune cells, and may not play a major role in kidney disease. These results suggest that the overall role of YAP in the kidney is expected to be injurious and profibrotic. Therefore, targeting YAP may turn to be a novel therapeutic treatment for kidney disease. However, since complete deletion of Yap in the principal cells of the collecting leads to polyuria while tubular Yap haploinsufficiency did not alter the expression of AQP2, AQP3 and AQP4 and urine output. Therefore, the doses of the YAP inhibitors need to be titrated to make sure the inhibition of YAP is sufficient to protect kidney injury but not too low to induce polyuria.

14102620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102620.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects up to 20% of all hospitalized patients and up to 50% of intensive care unit patients and is associated with a 4-fold increase in mortality. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects around 11% of the population worldwide. CKD can eventually progress to end-stage kidney disease and is also a strong risk factor for cardiovascular disease. CKD is estimated to become the 5th leading cause of death worldwide by 2040. Over the last 20 years, no new drug has been approved to specifically treat AKI and CKD due to a lack of understanding of the underlying mechanisms. We now find that YAP is activated in renal tubular epithelial cells during kidney injury. Tubular YAP activation promotes the expression of the transcription factors KLF5 and AP-1, thereby inducing tubular injury and elevating the expression of inflammatory factors including TNF-α and fibrotic factors.

14103420.value: 肌肉疾病，比如老年肌肉減少症和杜氏肌營養不良症等，皆可導致嚴重的健康後果。但是，許多藥物治療方法由於缺乏肌肉細胞靶向性而導致全身給藥時藥效低下及脫靶等不良反應，使得臨床應用受限。適配體是單鏈寡核苷酸，以高親和力和特異性結合靶標，適合成爲藥物遞送系統的靶頭。然而，目前仍缺乏有應用前景的肌肉靶向適配體。 利用基於細胞的指數富集適配體系統進化技術（cell-SELEX），通過對小鼠C2C12成肌細胞進行正篩，對肝細胞和外周血單核細胞進行負篩，我們篩選了對C2C12細胞具有高親和力的適配體候選物。從中確定了一個在體內和體外實驗中表現出極高肌肉親和力和特異性的適配體（SkMApt1）。SkMApt1也被證實對人肌肉細胞亦具有高親和力。我們曾報導過microRNA-487b（miR-487b）是肌肉減少症發展過程中骨骼肌的合成代謝抑製因子，並培育了肌肉特異性miR-487b敲入小鼠。與對照組小鼠相比，miR-487b肌肉敲入小鼠骨骼肌萎縮程度明顯。為了評估SkMApt1是否可以促進antagomiR-487b靶向骨骼肌遞送並抑制miR-487b水平，我們將包裹了antagomiR-487b的納米脂質顆粒（LNPs）與SkMApt1偶聯（Apt1-LNPs-antimiR）。 Apt1-LNPs-antimiR具有均一的顆粒形狀，良好的血清穩定性，無明顯細胞毒性和對肌細胞的高親和力。在經Apt1-LNPs-antimiR處理的C2C12細胞中，miR-487b的表達水平明顯低於對照適配體脂質顆粒藥物（sApt-LNPs-antimiR）。我們進一步確定了Apt1-LNPs-antimiR的給藥策略。綜上所述，根據以上前期研究可得出以下假設：SkMApt1可以促進包裹了antagomiR-487b的納米脂質顆粒針對肌肉的靶向遞送，並挽救肌肉特異性miR-487b敲入小鼠的肌量和功能。 為了檢驗假設，本課題將完成三個目標。 1）研究SkMApt1是否有助於在成年小鼠體內肌肉靶向遞送包裹了antagomiR-487b的納米脂質顆粒； 2）研究SkMApt1是否有助於包裹了antagomiR-487b的納米脂質顆粒拯救肌肉特異性miR-487b敲入小鼠的肌量和肌肉功能； 3）研究在肌肉特異性miR-487b敲入小鼠中SkMApt1預處理後Apt1-LNP-antimiR處理對肌量和功能的影響。 此課題將有助於確立SkMApt1為有應用前景的肌肉靶向遞送靶頭，並促進開發新型的以肌肉組織為靶標的治療策略。

14103420.value: For aim 1, 6-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into three groups. The animals in each group will be intravenously injected with Cy3-labeled LNPs-antimiR, sApt-LNPs-antimiR and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR, respectively, at a Cy3-antimiR dose of 1.0 mg/kg. The gastrocnemius muscles, heart, lung, liver, spleen and kidney of each animal were collected at 4 hours and 12 hours post-administration, respectively. The Cy3-labeled antimiR distribution in different tissues were evaluated by ex vivo florescence imaging and fluorescence intensity in different organ samples was calculated. The results showed that the fluorescence signal intensity of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR in skeletal muscle was significantly higher, whereas the fluorescence signal intensities in liver and kidney were significantly lower when compared to LNPs-antimiR and sApt-LNPs-antimiR at each time points. For aim 2, 6-month-old male muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice were randomly divided into four groups: baseline group, LNPs-antimiR group, sApt-LNPs-antimiR group and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR group. The mice were treated with eight periodic intravenous administrations (once per week) of LNPs-antimiR, sApt-LNPs-antimiR and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR, respectively, which were sacrificed at eight weeks later after the first treatment. The dosage of antimiR was 1.0 mg/kg. Before animal sacrifice, the muscle strength of gastrocnemius muscle was evaluated by in situ muscle functional testing. Then the gastrocnemius muscles were collected and weighed, followed by cryosectioning. Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining was performed to determine the mean muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA) of muscle samples. The expression levels of miR-487b were assessed by real-time PCR. The Wnt5a protein level was evaluated by western blot analysis. The results showed that Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment could promote the muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength of muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice. Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment inhibited miR-487b level and elevated Wnt5a protein level in skeletal muscle of muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice, while LNPs-antimiR and sApt-LNPs-antimiR treatment failed to achieve the above results. For aim 3, 6-month-old male muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice were divided into four groups: baseline group, Apt1 only group, Apt1-LNPs-antimiR group and Apt1 pre-treatment plus Apt1-LNPs-antimiR group (Apt1-pre). The mice in Apt1 only group and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR group were treated with eight periodic intravenous administrations (once per week) of Apt1 and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR, respectively. The animals in the last group were intravenously treated with Apt1 and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR 12 hours after the Apt1 pre-treatment. The Apt1 pre-treatment and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment were performed once a week for eight weeks. All the animals were sacrificed at eight weeks later after the first treatment. The dosage of antimir and Apt1 will be both 1.0 mg/kg. Before animal sacrifice, the muscle strength of gastrocnemius muscle were evaluated by in situ muscle functional testing. Then the gastrocnemius muscles were collected and weighed, followed by cryosectioning. H&E staining was performed to determine the mean muscle fiber CSA. The expression levels of miR-487b were assessed by real-time PCR. The Wnt5a protein level was evaluated by western blot analysis. The results demonstrated that Apt1 pre-treatment could inhibit the effect of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment in muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice, indicating that the muscle targeted delivery contributed to the beneficial effect of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR.

14103420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103420.value: The ex vivo florescence imaging showed that at both 4 hours and 12 hours post administration of Cy3-labeled LNPs-antimiR, sApt-LNPs-antimiR and Apt1-LNPs-antimiR, the fluorescence signal intensity of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR in skeletal muscle was significantly higher, whereas the fluorescence signal intensities in liver and kidney were significantly lower when compared to LNPs-antimiR and sApt-LNPs-antimiR, indicating that SkMApt1 could facilitate the skeletal muscle specific distribution of the drug and suppress the accumulation of the drug in liver and kidney. Furthermore, in muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice, the muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength were significantly higher in Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment group. Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment inhibited miR-487b level and elevated Wnt5a protein level in skeletal muscle of muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice, while LNPs-antimiR and sApt-LNPs-antimiR treatment failed to achieve the above results. Moreover, the Apt1 pre-treatment could inhibit the effect of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR treatment in muscle-specific miR-487b knockin mice, indicating that the muscle targeted delivery contributed to the beneficial effect of Apt1-LNPs-antimiR. These findings has been reported in two international conferences and one manuscript is in preparation. The project also facilitated other aptamer-based studies.

14103420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103420.value: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is caused by a mutation in the dystrophin gene, resulting in progressive muscle weakness, wasting, and premature death. The effects of current pharmaceutical therapies are far from satisfactory, about 24% of DMD trials terminated because of the unsatisfied outcomes. The lack of skeletal muscle targeting strategy is a major reason. The application of SkMApt1 in skeletal muscle-targeted therapy for DMD will be further studied. Moreover, the aptamer-based drug delivery system will be further developed, including different conjugate or package strategies to achieve better safety and efficacy of the treatment.

14103420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103420.value: Skeletal muscle is one of the largest organs in the body. The skeletal muscular disorders, such as sarcopenia and DMD, are related to serious health consequences. However, one major bottleneck of current pharmacological therapies for skeletal muscle disorders is lack of muscle cell selectivity, leading to low efficacy and off-target side effects when administered systemically. Nucleic acid aptamers are promising escort molecules for drug delivery systems due to their high affinity and selectivity to target molecules. We identified one aptamer SkMApt1 showing higher affinity and selectivity to skeletal muscle. We previously reported microRNA-487b (miR-487b) is an anabolic suppressor in skeletal muscle during sarcopenia development. In animal studies, it is demonstrated that SkMApt1 could facilitate muscle-targeted drug distribution, therefore promote the efficacy of the treatment. The current project helps to establish SkMApt1 as a promising skeletal muscle-target moiety to facilitate developing a novel skeletal muscle-targeted therapeutic strategy.

14104620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104620.value: Ageing-related osteoporosis contributes to the progressive loss of physical autonomy in the ageing population, especially in postmenopausal women. Osteoporosis results in increased bone fragility, and increased risk of fall and fracture that cause heavy socioeconomic burden and an alarming health problem in Hong Kong and globally. Bone remodelling cycle, including consecutive bone resorption and bone formation, is coordinated by bone-resorbing osteoclasts and bone-forming osteoblasts. Tilt of the balance toward bone resorption during ageing associated with loss of bone mass and the deterioration of micro-architecture collectively result in the compromise of structural strength. For years, the conventional treatment for treating osteoporosis, such as bisphosphonates, is to inhibit osteoclastic bone resorption; however, that will bring along side effects and complications such as osteonecrosis of jaw bones and atypical femoral fractures. Meanwhile, anti-bone resorption by majorly targeting on osteoclasts may cause repression in bone formation. To date, the treatment for osteoporosis remains a considerable challenge, and there is urgent unmet need for the development of novel therapies to rejuvenate the skeletal system in an integrated manner i.e. promoting bone formation and repressing bone resorption simultaneously. There is growing evidence that natural products derived from plants are able to treat ageing-related diseases. In particular, ginkgo biloba extract (GBE), a phytochemical product from ginkgo biloba leaf, exerts therapeutic efficacy on a number of ageing-related degenerative conditions. However, the efficacy of GBE on osteoporosis remains elusive. In our pre-clinical study, oral gavage of GBE dose-dependently reversed loss of bone mineral density in the ovariectomized (OVX) mice, which is a well-established model for postmenopausal osteoporosis. Also, GBE promoted osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and inhibited osteoclastogenic differentiation of macrophages. Moreover, we have identified that ginkgolide B, a unique component from GBE, responses for the promotion of osteogenic differentiation in MSCs. Due to these reasons, we hypothesize that ginkgolide B ameliorate osteoporosis. In this pre-clinical study, we will investigate the effect of ginkgolide B, given by oral gavage, on OVX-induced osteoporosis. We will also explore the underlying mechanism of how ginkgolide B regulates bone remodelling. It is expected that the use of ginkgo may serve as a new approach for treating osteoporosis. 14104620.label: Realisation of objectives
14104620.value: This project has been completed successfully despite there was a change of PI during the project. Below are the key methods employed: 1. Chemicals Ginkgolide B (#G6910), ginkgolide C (#18309), (−)-bilobalide (#B9031) and Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) (#NIST3247) were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich. Ginkgolide J (#ASB-00007186-010) was purchased from ChromaDex. 2. Animal models For the aging models, 3- and 20-month-old female C57BL/6 mice were administered GB (12 mg/kg) for two months. For the steady-state condition model, 6-month-old female C57BL/6 mice were administered GB (12 mg/kg) for two months. For the ovariectomy (OVX) mouse model, 6-week-old C57BL/6 female mice underwent ovariectomy or sham operation. At three weeks after ovariectomy, OVX mice received a daily oral gavage of GB (3 and 12 mg/kg) for two months. For glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, female C57BL/6 mice (10 weeks old) were intraperitoneally injected with dexamethasone (Dex) (20 mg/kg) daily to induce bone loss, and then the Dex-injected mice were subjected to Dex and Dex + GB treatment for an additional 14 days. GB was diluted to the appropriate concentration in 100 μL of PBS for daily oral gavage. Mice were obtained from Laboratory Animal Services Centre, the Chinese University of Hong Kong and randomly assigned to control and experimental groups in all experiments. Animal experiments were conducted in a blinded manner where possible. 3. Blood biochemical analyses Serum was collected by cardiac puncture to perform biochemical analysis. Briefly, serum was placed on SPOTCHEM test strips and measured by using a SPOTCHEM™ dry-chemistry clinical analyzer. 4. Skeletal phenotyping BMD and the trabecular bone morphological parameters of isolated femurs were analyzed by microcomputed tomography as previously described. Briefly, the isolated femurs were fixed in formaldehyde overnight. The scanning was performed at a maximum tube voltage of 50 kVp, a current of 0.48 mA, an integration time of 200 m s, and a resolution of 20 μm. The scanning angular rotation was 360° with an angular step of 0.25°. Bone reconstruction of the femur was performed using 3DimViewer software and SCANCO Medical microCT software. 5. Quantitative proteomics analysis Quantitative proteomics analysis was performed as previously described. Briefly, the extracted peptides from serum samples were analyzed by LTQ-Orbitrap hybrid tandem mass spectrometry. Protein identification and quantification were performed by using PEAKS software. The DEP list was obtained using a 1.5-fold cutoff, a false discovery rate <1%, and a significance threshold of p < 0.05. The PANTHER classification system (www.pantherdb.org) was applied to the DEPs for Gene Ontology annotation. Heat maps were created of the collected protein expression levels through the data visualization tool BioVinci (version 1.1.5). 6. Cell culture Mouse mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) were isolated from bone marrow collected from 20-month-old female C57BL/6 mice. The characteristics of MSCs were determined by morphology, surface markers, and multipotency (Figure S1), similar to our previous description. For maintenance, mouse MSCs were grown in low-glucose DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% PSG. Osteogenic differentiation of MSCs was performed according to a previous study. Briefly, MSCs were cultured in osteogenic induction medium with or without various GBE compounds, and the medium was changed every three days. Osteogenic induction medium consisted of high-glucose DMEM supplemented with 0.1 μm dexamethasone, 10 mM β-glycerol phosphate, 0.2 mM ascorbic acid, and 1% PSG. Adipogenic medium consisted of DMEM supplemented with 1 μM dexamethasone, 50 μM indomethacin, 5 μg/mL insulin, 0.5 mM 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine, and 10% fetal bovine serum. Chondrogenic medium consisted of high-glucose DMEM supplemented with 0.1 μM dexamethasone, 50 μg/mL ascorbic acid, 100 μg/mL sodium pyruvate, 40 μg/mL l-proline, 10 ng/mL hTGFβ1, and 50 mg/mL ITS+ premix. Monocytes were isolated from 20-month-old female C57BL/6 mice and differentiated into macrophages in RPMI 1640 supplemented with 10% FBS and 20 ng/mL M-CSF. For osteoclastogenic induction, macrophages were cultured in α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS, M-CSF 50 ng/mL, RANKL 50 ng/mL, and 1% PSG with or without 5 mg/L GB, and the induction medium was changed every three to seven days. For the H2O2 experiment, osteoclasts were treated with 5 mg/L GB 24 h prior to treatment with 300 μM H2O2 for 24 h. 7. Flow cytometry For surface phenotyping, mouse MSCs were stained with CD29, CD34, CD44, CD45, CD105, CD117, CD73 and CD31 antibodies and were analyzed by using FACScan flow cytometer. The results were visualized by FlowJo version 10. 8. RNA isolation and gene expression analysis RNA was isolated by using TRIzol® reagent and reverse transcribed by High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit. Real-time PCR was performed using a StepOnePlus™ Real-time PCR System. 9. Alkaline phosphatase, Alizarin red S, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase, and F-actin staining For alkaline phosphatase histochemistry, cell layers were fixed with 3.7% formaldehyde, washed with distilled water (ddH2O), and stained with BCIP/NBT solution for 30 min in the dark at room temperature. ALP activity was measured using an ALP assay kit and normalized to the total protein content according to the manufacturer's instructions. To assess mineralized matrix, cells were fixed with 3.7% formaldehyde, washed with ddH2O and stained with 40 mM Alizarin red S solution for 30 min at room temperature, and the stain was extracted by acetic acid and semiquantified as previously described. For tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) staining, cells were fixed and stained with an acid phosphatase leukocyte assay kit according to the manufacturer's instructions. TRAP-positive cells with three or more nuclei were counted as osteoclasts. Fluor 488-labeled phalloidin was used to stain F-actin. The average area and number of osteoclasts and nuclei per multinucleated cell were measured following phalloidin or TRAP staining. 10. Cell viability assay Cells were treated with GB for 48 h, and cell viability was determined by a CCK-8 kit. 11. ELISA analysis of OPG, RANKL and OCN The expression levels of OPG and RANKL were quantified by ELISA and analyzed by a microplate reader. 12. ROS and SOD activity measurement Total ROS and superoxide were measured by a ROS/Superoxide Detection Assay kit, and SOD activity was determined by Superoxide Dismutase Activity Assay Kit according to the manufacturer's instructions. 13. siRNA transfection Control siRNA and target siRNA were transfected with RNAiMAX transfection reagent. After 18 h of transfection, the cells were washed with PBS, and the medium was replaced with fresh medium as appropriate. The siRNA sequences used were siSod2: UAUACUGAAGGUAGUAAGC and siCat: UGGCUAUGGAUAAAGGAUG. 14. Statistical analysis Quantitative data are presented as the means ± SD in histograms with data points. Statistical analyses were performed using one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA or Student's t-test by GraphPad Prism 8 (GraphPad Software, Inc.) depending on the experimental design. A value of P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

14104620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104620.value: Osteoporosis is characterized by reductions in bone mass, which could be attributed to the dysregulation of bone homeostasis, such as the loss of balance between bone-resorbing osteoclasts and bone-forming osteoblasts. Elevated levels of oxidative stress increase bone resorption by promoting osteoclastogenesis and inhibiting the osteogenesis. Ginkgolide B (GB), a small natural molecule from Ginkgo biloba, has been reported to possess pharmacological activities by regulating reactive oxygen species (ROS) in aging-related degenerative diseases. Herein, we assessed the therapeutic effects of GB on the bone phenotypes of mice with osteoporosis induced by (I) aging, (II) ovariectomy, and (III) glucocorticoids. In all three animal models, oral gavage of GB significantly improved bone mass consistent with the increase in the OPG-to-RANKL ratio. In the in vitro experiments, GB promoted osteogenesis in aged mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and repressed osteoclastogenesis in aged macrophages by reducing ROS. The serum protein profile in GB-treated aged mice revealed moderate rejuvenating effects; signaling pathways associated with ROS were also regulated. The anabolic and anti-catabolic effects of GB were illustrated by the reduction in ROS. Our results indicate that GB is effective in treating osteoporosis. The use of GB in patients with osteoporosis is worthy of further clinical investigation.

14104620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104620.value: To clearly and comprehensively characterize the serum protein profile of GB-treated aged mice, a label-free proteomics approach using LC-MS/MS was used. A total of 347 proteins were identified as differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between the young and aged groups, 47 proteins were identified as DEPs between the aged + vehicle and aged + GB groups, and 17 DEPs were identified in both datasets. The hierarchical clustering heatmap revealed that GB partially shifted the serum DEP profile of aged mice toward that of young mice. Regarding biological processes, DEPs between the aged + vehicle and aged + GB groups were related to cellular processes, immune system processes, and metabolic processes. Furthermore, gene ontology analysis revealed 149 different GO terms associated with DEPs between the aged + vehicle and aged + GB groups that were highly associated with the inflammatory response, aging, and oxidative stress pathways. Given the serum DEPs of GB-treated aged mice were correlated with oxidative stress, we sought to determine whether GB modulates bone metabolism by inhibiting ROS. In brief, our results indicate that GB regulates osteogenic differentiation and osteoclastogenic differentiation through the inhibition of ROS in aged cells.

14104620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104620.value: Using mouse model of osteoporosis, we demonstrated that oral administration of ginkgolide B, a natural ingredient extracted from Ginkgo, reduces bone loss via its positive action on bone formation and inhibiting effect on bone loss. Since patients with osteoporosis require a long-term regimen, oral ginkgolide B administration provides a convenient, reliable, and highly accessible method for sustained delivery.

14104820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104820.value: 肝臟是惡性腫瘤常見的轉移部位。作為新陳代謝和免疫反應的主要器官之一，肝臟豐富的血液供應和解剖學結構已知與癌症，特別是消化道癌的肝轉移相關。同時有研究指出肝臟獨特的免疫代謝微環境也與癌症轉移的肝組織嗜性密不可分。肥胖作為一個全球性的問題，其相關的慢性炎症、代謝異常以及免疫抑制等，與多種癌症，如肝癌、腸癌的發病機率以及轉移增加顯著相關。我們近期的研究表明，肥胖引起的炎症和肝纖維化可以促進髓源性抑制細胞的擴增和免疫抑制性，從而導致肝細胞癌的惡化和對免疫治療的耐藥性。通過靶向髓源性抑制細胞來改善肝臟的免疫抑制微環境可以有效恢復肝臟的免疫應答，聯合檢查點免疫抑制劑可清除小鼠體內的肝細胞癌，達到治癒的效果。基於肝臟免疫代謝的重要性，我們認為肥胖引起的免疫代謝異常可導致肝臟微環境的改變，並可能對癌症的肝轉移起促進作用，我們會在本項目中對該問題進行研究證實。 研究發現肥胖病人體內膽固醇含量的增加與多種癌症的發病機率增加呈正相關性。而降膽固醇藥物（如他汀類藥物等）則與原發性和轉移性肝癌的發病率降低以及病人生存率延長有關。在前期的工作中，我們用高糖高脂食物，成功誘導了與病人症狀相似的高膽固醇肥胖小鼠。有趣的是，我們發現相比於正常小鼠，肥胖小鼠肝臟中的自然殺傷性T（NKT）細胞出現特異性的下降，並和肝臟中膽固醇的增加，以及黑色素瘤和腸癌的肝轉移幾率增加相關。使用臨床上處方的瑞舒伐他汀治療肥胖小鼠，不僅可以顯著性降低膽固醇的水平，而且可以恢復肝臟中NKT細胞的比例和其對癌細胞的殺傷功能。我們進一步用單細胞測序技術，對肝臟中分離純化得到的NKT細胞進行了分析，結果發現瑞舒伐他汀治療後的NKT細胞中一種絲氨酸蛋白酶抑制劑A3K（Serpina3K）的水平明顯增加。該基因編碼的蛋白是一種分泌型的抗炎和抗氧化蛋白，有報導指出該蛋白可介導細胞對腫瘤的殺傷作用和抑制腫瘤細胞的組織浸潤侵襲。利用體外建立的NKT細胞模型，我們進一步發現NKT細胞可以通過攝取過量的外源型膽固醇來減低Serpina3K的表達水平，從而抑制其增殖和殺傷功能。同時，對比正常人，在肥胖病人和腸癌肝轉移的病人樣本中，我們也觀察到了膽固醇增加和NKT細胞的減少，而且兩者呈負相關性。所以，在本項目中我們希望通過建立原位癌的肝轉移模型以及體外NKT細胞的培養模型，結合病人樣本，來闡明高膽固醇對NKT細胞的調節作用和機制，及其對癌症肝轉移的促進作用和原理，從而對肥胖相關性癌症的預防和治療提供理論依據和研究策略。

14105320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105320.value: 原發性閉角型青光眼（PACG）的特徵是前房引流角閉合，從而阻止房水流出並導致眼內壓（IOP）升高，進而引起青光眼的特徵性，進展性和不可逆性視神經病變。閉角型青光眼的發生是廣泛的。其患病率在中國人中最高（達1.26％），佔中國雙眼失明性青光眼的91％。在2010年，PACG影響了超過700萬中國人。在香港，青光眼仍是不可逆性失明的最重要原因，佔所有不可逆失明情況的近四分之一病例。 PACG是一種具有多種危險因素的複雜疾病。 PACG患者的一級親屬承受更大風險以及不同種族群體中PACG患病率的差異佐證了PACG的遺傳基礎。最近，在三個多中心全基因組關聯研究（GWAS）和大規模遺傳薈萃分析（meta-analysis）中，我們確定了14個遺傳基因座，包括PLEKHA7，COL11A1，PCMTD1-ST18，ABCC5，EPDR1，CHAT，GLIS3，FERMT2，和DPM2-FAM102A，與PACG相關聯。然而，大多數報導的變體位於生物學功能未知的非編碼區。 因此，在這項研究中，我們計劃在香港中國人口中招募的1000名PACG患者（具有5年的隨訪數據）和2000名對照使用新一代深度測序（next-generation sequencing）技術，鑑定這14個基因中的所有編碼變異體，以及闡明PACG中每個常見和稀有變異的影響。此外，我們將把這些變異單獨或成組地與PACG的臨床表型和進展作相關研究。 這項研究的結果將使我們鑑定出14個已知PACG遺傳基因座的編碼變異，使我們能夠更好地了解PACG的遺傳結構和分子機制。此外，這項研究還可能提供與PACG臨床表現相關的潛在遺傳生物標記，以及預測PACG發生和發展風險的生物標記。這項研究的發現將對患者和眼科醫生在製定PACG的治療，監測和隨訪計劃時有十分重要的意義。

14105320.label: Realisation of objectives
14105320.value: This project has comprehensively achieved and, in several critical areas, substantially exceeded its original objectives through a multi-faceted research strategy that evolved from targeted candidate analysis to large-scale genomic and systemic investigations. Objectives 1 & 2 (Variant Identification & Association): We successfully completed the targeted genotyping/sequencing of the 14 pre-specified susceptibility genes within our Hong Kong Chinese PACG cohort. This led to the confirmation of significant associations for key genes, most notably LOXL1. Furthermore, by leading a major international exome-wide collaboration, we powerfully superseded the candidate approach, discovering UBOX5 as a novel, functionally validated PACG gene—a landmark achievement that fully satisfies the aim to "confirm the causal variant for each associated gene locus" for this new gene. Objective 3 (Mutation-Load Analysis): This was directly and successfully executed via the gene-based burden test within the exome-wide study, which identified the significant aggregated burden of rare, damaging variants in UBOX5. Objectives 4 & 5 (Correlation with Endophenotypes & Progression): These were fully addressed. We correlated genetic variants (VAV3) with long-term PACG progression in a longitudinal cohort. Importantly, we expanded the scope to identify lung function as a novel, significant systemic biomarker correlated with glaucomatous structural damage (RNFL, GCIPL thickness), providing major new insights into clinical endophenotypes. Objective 6 (New Candidate Genes): Exceeded. We not only identified the major new candidate UBOX5 but also, through our comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis (JAMA Ophthalmol 2024), newly confirmed seven additional loci associated with PACG (e.g., ATOH7, FBN1, VAV3), dramatically expanding the known genetic landscape. Objective 7 (PACG vs. POAG Comparison): Our direct case-control analysis validated AFAP1, FNDC3B, GAS7, and SPRED2 as specific to the High-Tension Glaucoma (HTG) subtype of POAG, confirming a distinct genetic architecture from PACG. The meta-analysis further refined this by identifying specific loci (e.g., ABCC5, COL11A1) with potential shared effects across disease spectra. In addition, for endophenotypes in different age groups: Achieved through analyses in adult populations (UK Biobank, linking lung function to structural traits) and within a dedicated PACG patient cohort. In summary, the project evolved from a focused candidate gene study into a program that delivered a high-impact novel gene discovery, a global genetic synthesis, and the identification of a novel systemic biomarker. All original objectives have been fulfilled, with the work generating a more complex and ethnically nuanced understanding of PACG genetics, providing a robust platform for future translational research.

14105320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105320.value: The research program generated high-impact findings that significantly advanced the genetic understanding of primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG). The major outcomes are: Discovery of a novel causal gene, UBOX5, via International Collaboration: In the largest exome-wide study of PACG to date, we identified UBOX5 as a novel susceptibility gene (Pmeta = 1.25 × 10⁻¹⁰, OR = 2.13). Functional characterization demonstrated that rare, protein-altering variants conferring risk were enriched for those deficient in ubiquitinating the chaperone protein BIP (Binding Immunoglobulin Protein), implicating the UBOX5-BIP pathway in PACG pathogenesis for the first time (Nat Commun, 2025). Global synthesis and confirmation of PACG-associated loci: Our comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis provided the definitive global summary, confirming significant associations for PACG with LOXL1, ATOH7, CALCRL, FBN1, IL6, MMP19, and VAV3. Crucially, this work highlighted substantial ethnic diversity in genetic associations and cataloged shared loci, such as ABCC5, COL11A1, and PCMTD1-ST18, that influence both PACG and primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) phenotypes (JAMA Ophthalmol, 2024). Validation of genetic associations and identification of sex-specific effects: In our Hong Kong Chinese cohort, we confirmed LOXL1 rs3825942 as a key protective variant for PACG and identified a female-specific protective association for ABCA1 rs2422493, underscoring the importance of sex-stratified analysis (Clin Exp Ophthalmol, 2025). Distinct genetic architecture between PACG and POAG subtypes: We validated AFAP1, FNDC3B, GAS7, and SPRED2 as genetic loci specific to the high-tension glaucoma (HTG) subtype of POAG in Asian populations, demonstrating a clear genetic divergence from PACG and supporting their classification as etiologically distinct entities (Br J Ophthalmol, 2025). Identification of novel systemic biomarkers and progression modifiers: We established impaired lung function (lower FVC and FEV1) as a significant biomarker associated with glaucomatous structural damage (thinner RNFL and GCIPL), independent of intraocular pressure (Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci, 2025). Furthermore, longitudinal analysis suggested VAV3 rs6689476 as a potential genetic modifier of PACG disease progression (Clin Exp Ophthalmol, 2025). These outcomes collectively map a complex genetic architecture for PACG, involving both unique and shared pathways with other glaucomas, and bridge genetic risk with systemic physiology and clinical disease course.

14105320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105320.value: The discoveries from this project create a strong foundation for translational research. The immediate priority is to mechanistically dissect the UBOX5-BIP pathway using cellular and animal models to understand how its disruption leads to angle closure, offering a direct route to novel therapeutic targets. To achieve clinical impact, we propose a two-pronged course of action. First, develop a polygenic risk score (PRS) for PACG that incorporates the newly identified and validated loci (e.g., UBOX5, LOXL1, VAV3), stratified by ethnicity, for improved population risk stratification. Second, initiate a prospective biomarker study to validate the utility of lung function as a clinical indicator for glaucoma monitoring, particularly in high-risk groups. Furthermore, the shared genetics between PACG and POAG phenotypes (e.g., ABCC5, COL11A1) warrant focused functional studies to elucidate common biological pathways in optic nerve vulnerability, which could reveal neuroprotective targets applicable across glaucoma subtypes. Establishing an international PACG progression consortium is essential to robustly validate genetic and systemic modifiers of disease course, enabling personalized prognosis and management.

14105320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105320.value: This research project aimed to find the genetic causes of a major eye disease called Primary Angle-Closure Glaucoma (PACG), a leading cause of blindness worldwide, especially in Asia. We discovered a new gene, UBOX5, that significantly increases a person's risk of developing PACG when it doesn't work properly. This is a crucial finding as it points to a completely new biological process behind the disease. We also confirmed several other important risk genes and found that the genetic causes of PACG are different from other common types of glaucoma, explaining why they are distinct diseases. Furthermore, we identified a link, that people with weaker lung function are more likely to have signs of eye damage from glaucoma, suggesting shared factors between lung and eye health. These findings are significant because they move us closer to predicting who is at highest risk, understanding exactly how the disease starts, and ultimately developing new, more targeted treatments to prevent blindness from this condition. The research provides a valuable genetic roadmap for future medical advances in eye care.

14105820.value: PCA is one of the major metabolites of dietary polyphenols in the intestine. The present study is to test the hypothesis that PCA is the active metabolite of dietary polyphenols accountable for cardiovascular benefits by reducing blood cholesterol and atherosclerosis throughout modulating the gut microbiota profile via decreasing the Firmicutes/Bacteriodetes ratio, decreasing the growth of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-producing bacteria, and increasing the growth of SCFAs-producing bacteria.
