14105820.value: 假設：多酚廣泛地存在於蔬菜，水果和茶葉中，大量的研究表明多酚的攝入與心血管疾病的降低和血液膽固醇的減少有關。 但是，食物中的多酚生物利用率卻非常低，在腸道中的吸收率僅為1％左右。 因此，多酚對心血管疾病和血液膽固醇的改善效果不能完全歸功於食物中的多酚本身。 原兒茶酸（PCA）是腸道中多酚衍生的主要代謝產物之一。鑒於此，我們提出PCA作為膳食多酚的主要代謝物，可通過改善腸道菌群來保護心血管和降低血液膽固醇。 目的：本研究旨在探討PCA對腸道菌群變化的影響，特別是厚壁菌、擬桿菌、短鏈脂肪酸（SCFAs）產生菌和脂多糖（LPS）產生菌；同時探討這些菌群的變化對血液膽固醇和動脈粥樣硬化的影響。 其中，SCFAs可抵抗動脈粥樣硬化，而LPS可促進動脈粥樣硬化。 實驗設計：本研究擬選用倉鼠為實驗模型。實驗中，40只倉鼠被平均分為四組（n = 10），分別餵食高膽固醇糧（HCD），低劑量實驗組糧（PL， HCD+0.5％PCA）,高劑量實驗組糧（PH，HCD+1％PCA）和陽性對照實驗組糧（CT，HCD+0.5%膽甾胺），其中膽甾胺是具有降膽固醇效果的陽性對照藥物。 檢測指標：測定血液膽固醇、動脈粥樣硬化斑塊、肝臟膽固醇和三醯甘油、糞便膽汁酸、糞便中性固醇、糞便SCFAs、LPS和腸道菌群；同時測定PCA和腸道菌群參與的與膽固醇代謝相關的基因和蛋白的表達，如肝臟3-羥基-3-甲基戊二醯基CoA還原酶、LDL受體、膽固醇7α-羥化酶、固醇調節元素結合蛋白2、肝X受體α和法尼酯X受體。 預期結果：在初步實驗資料的基礎之上，申請者預期PCA可通過降低血液膽固醇、減少動脈粥樣硬化和改善腸道菌群（如降低Firmicutes / Bacteriodetes的比值；減少LPS產生菌；增加SCFAs產生菌）來維護心血管的健康。

14105820.label: Realisation of objectives
14105820.value: We have achieved all the objectives as stipulated in the original proposal. A healthy diet plays an essential role in the prevention of cardiovascular diseases. In recent years, phytochemicals and nutraceuticals have been extensively studied for their blood cholesterol-lowering activity. Protocatechuic acid (PCA) is a hydroxybenzoic acid rich in plants including chicory, olives, and white grapes. Gut fermentation of anthocyanidins can also produce a considerable amount of PCA. Previous research has shown that PCA protects against atherosclerosis and attenuates hypercholesterolemia. We hypothesized that the cholesterol-lowering activity of anthocyanins and other polyphenols may be mediated by the action of their gut-derived metabolite PCA. The present study was to study how PCA affects the cholesterol absorption and metabolism. It is known that diet is a most important factor modulating gut microbiota. The present project is therefore to (i) investigate how PCA supplementation affects blood lipids; (ii) study how PCA supplementation interacts with these genes encoding the sterol transporters and proteins in cholesterol absorption and metabolism; and (iii) explore how PCA supplementation modulates gut microbiome in hypercholesterolemia hamsters. Objective 1 was to test the hypothesis that PCA is the active metabolite of dietary polyphenols accountable for cardiovascular benefits by reducing blood cholesterol and atherosclerosis throughout modulating the gut microbiota profile via decreasing the Firmicutes/Bacteriodetes ratio, decreasing the growth of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-producing bacteria, and increasing the growth of short chain fatty acids (SCFAs)-producing bacteria. We choose hamsters as a model. The major finding was that feeding hamsters with two experimental diets (0.1% PCA) (PL) and 0.5% PCA (PH) could reduce plasma total cholesterol (TC) by 18% and 24% compared with the control diet. Feeding PCA for six weeks substantially reduced liver cholesterol in the PL and PH groups. PCA supplementation significantly increased fecal output of primary, secondary, and total bile acids in a dose-dependent manner compared with the HCD group. Dietary PCA significantly down-regulated the mRNA and protein abundances of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase (HMGCR), a key enzyme in cholesterol synthesis, in a dose-dependent way. Dietary PCA significantly up-regulated the mRNA expression of cassette transporters 5 (ABCG5) but not its protein mass compared with that in HCD hamsters. Feeding PCA diets had no effect on mRNA or protein expressions of Niemann-Pick C1 like protein 1 (NPC1L1), acyl CoA: cholesterol acyltransferase 2 (ACAT2), microsomal triacylglycerol transport protein (MTP), or ABCG8. These genes of NPC1L1, ACAT2, MTP, or ABCG8 are the transporters and enzymes in cholesterol synthesis. As hypothesized, PCA significantly increased the amount of fecal SCFAs and decreased LPS. The spearman rank correlation analysis demonstrated that the fecal excretion of each individual SCFA and total SCFAs were strongly associated with the higher abundance of Bacteroidales S24-7 family within the Bacteroidetes phylum. It was also found that each individual bile acid, primary, secondary, and total bile acids were significantly correlated with the lower relative abundance of Lactobacillaceae, the major bacteria with low bile salt hydrolase activity in the gut. PCA feeding dramatically reduced Lactobacillaceae abundances in the gut microbiome after six weeks. In addition, PCA supplementation for six weeks caused a dose-dependent increment in Alcaligenaceae, accompanied by a decrement in Lachnospiraceae. The present study demonstrated that dietary PCA dose-dependently decreased plasma cholesterol and prevented the accumulation of hepatic cholesterol and lipid disposition in hypercholesterolemia hamsters. Such effect was mediated at least partially by increasing gut production of SCFAs and fecal excretion of bile acids via modulating gut microbiome. Objectives 2 was to test the effect of PCA on blood cholesterol and atherosclerosis in hypercholesterolemia hamsters. It is known that trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) is a risk factor for atherosclerosis. One experiment was designed to investigate the effect of PCA on TMAO-aggravated atherosclerosis in ApoE−/− mice. The mice were randomly divided into five groups and fed one of the following five diets for 12 weeks: namely a low-fat diet (LFD), a western diet (WD), a WD + 0.2% TMAO diet (WDT), a WDT + 0.5% PCA diet (WDT + LPCA), and a WDT + 1.0% PCA diet (WDT + HPCA). Results demonstrated that dietary TMAO exacerbated the development of atherosclerosis by eliciting inflammation and disturbing lipid metabolism. The diet with PCA at 1% reduced TMAO-induced aortic plaque by 30% and decreased the levels of plasma pro-inflammatory cytokines. PCA also improved lipid metabolism by up-regulating the hepatic gene expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα). In addition, PCA supplementation enhanced fecal excretion of fatty acids and decreased hepatic fat accumulation. PCA supplementation favorably modulated gut microbiota by increasing the α-diversity with an increase in the abundance of beneficial genera (Rikenella, Turicibacter, Clostridium_sensu_stricto and Bifidobacterium) and a decrease in the abundance of the harmful Helicobacter genus. In summary, PCA could alleviate the TMAO-exacerbated atherosclerosis and inflammation, improve the lipid metabolism, and modulate gut microbiota. Objectives 3 was to investigate the effect of PCA and polyphenols on gut microbiota profile. We have sequenced and analyzed the 16S rRNA to quantify the relative abundance of phylum and family levels of gut microbiota with focus on Firmicute, Bacteroidetes, SCFAs-producing and LPS-releasing bacteria. The 16S rRNA gene sequencing analysis revealed that the major bacteria phyla were Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, and the major bacteria families were Rumnococcaceae, Bacteroidales S24-7, Erysipelotrichaceae, Eubacteriaceae, and Lachnospiraceae in the gut microbiome of hamsters. After the 6-week intervention, feeding PCA diets did not significantly modulate the gut microbiome diversity at the phylum, family, or OTU levels as indicated by the Sobs, Chao, and Shannon indexes in hamsters. However, feeding PCA diets significantly increased the relative abundances of Bacteroidetes in the PH group and lowered the ratio of Firmicutes to Bacteroidetes. Higher microbial production of SCFAs in the gut is suggested to be beneficial for the host. Dietary supplementation of PCA markedly increased the amounts of acetic acid, propionic acid, and total SCFAs in a dose-dependent manner. The spearman rank correlation analysis demonstrated that the fecal excretion of each individual SCFA and total SCFAs were strongly associated with the higher abundance of Bacteroidales S24-7 family within the Bacteroidetes phylum, suggesting a high capacity of carbohydrate utilization and SCFA production in the gut. It was also found that each individual bile acid, primary, secondary, and total bile acids were significantly correlated with the lower relative abundance of Lactobacillaceae, the major bacteria with low bile salt hydrolase activity in the gut. PCA feeding dramatically reduced Lactobacillaceae abundances in the gut microbiome after six weeks. In addition, PCA supplementation for six weeks caused a dose-dependent increment in Alcaligenaceae accompanied by a decrement in Lachnospiraceae. Objective 4 was to prove that PCA is well absorbed and reach the liver, the present study will examine the bioavailability and pharmacokinetic characteristics of PCA in given various doses of PCA. We have generated the plasma concentration–time profile of PCA. After the oral administration of 50 mg/kg body weight PCA, plasma concentration of PCA in mice progressively increased and peaked (Cmax = 22.5 μg/mL) at 10 min (Tmax = 10 min), indicating that PCA could be rapidly absorbed. Then, plasma PCA level decreased and the area under curve (AUC) was calculated to be 451.2 mg min/L.

14105820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105820.value: We have conducted all experiments as planned in the original proposal. The first outcome of this project was to examine the effect of PCA on blood cholesterol. The present study demonstrated that dietary PCA dose-dependently decreased plasma cholesterol and prevented the accumulation of hepatic cholesterol and lipid disposition in hypercholesterolemia hamsters. Such effect was mediated at least partially by increasing gut production of SCFAs and fecal excretion of bile acids via modulating the gut microbiome. The second major finding was that PCA could significantly reduce the atherosclerosis. TMAO is an independent risk factor in causing the heart diseases. PCA could alleviate TMAO-exacerbated atherosclerosis via mitigating inflammation and improving lipid metabolism. Gut microbiota was also believed to partially mediate the beneficial effect of PCA at least in mice. The third major finding/outcome was that PCA was effective in reducing plasma glucose as α-glucosidase inhibitor. The present project was the first time to probe the inhibitory mechanism of PCA on α-glucosidase. In vitro, PCA inhibited α-glucosidase activity in a concentration-dependent pattern and it was a reversible mix-type α-glucosidase inhibitor. PCA spontaneously combined with α-glucosidase to form an α-glucosidase-PCA complex, which hindered substrates from entering catalytic sites and resulted in decreased α-glucosidase activity. In vivo, PCA significantly reduced postprandial blood glucose levels with a decreased AUC of blood glucose in STZ-induced diabetic mice. We also found that PCA possessed a strong anti-inflammatory activity on endothelial cells and could ameliorate the endothelial dysfunction through enhancing Akt/eNOS pathway. The current findings suggest that acquisition of PCA from daily diets may be beneficial to the vascular health in diabetic patients. In summary, the whole project was well executed as planned. The results of the whole project have led to 7 SCI papers. Five papers (1, 4-7) were directly derived from the project, while paper 2 and 3 were published before the project commencement as data in paper 2 and 3 were the parts of preliminary results of the project and GRF should be credited and acknowledged.

14105820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105820.value: The present project investigated plasma TC-lowering and hypoglycemic activity of PCA, demonstrating that it is very effective and can be further developed as a functional ingredient in management of hypercholesterolemia and diabetes. Even though the data are promising in animal experiments, it may not be directly extrapolated into application in treatment of human patients. The clinical trial is in need to validate the results obtained in the animal experiments.

14105820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105820.value: It is recommended that humans should consume 3-5 servings of vegetables and 2-4 servings of fruits per day. Protocatechuic acid (PCA) is rich in some vegetables and fruits. This study is the first of its kinds in Hong Kong to address the benefits of protocatechuic acid (PCA) as a gut metabolite of dietary polyphenols on plasma cholesterol and gut microbiota. The present study clearly demonstrated that PCA is potential in reducing plasma cholesterol and improving the growth of beneficial bacteria in the intestine. In Hong Kong, about 25% adults suffer from hypercholesterolemia. The findings from the proposed study shall provide new mechanistic insights into both therapeutic and dietary use of PCA in treatment of hypercholesterolemia and improvement of gut health. In addition, it was found that PCA was able to reduce plasma glucose and had some potential in application to manage the complication of diabetes. The finding in these animal experiments would probably lead to develop PCA as an alternative therapy for patients whose plasma cholesterol and glucose are moderately high but not warrant a prescription of medications.

14106120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106120.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids are common phytochemicals present in ~3% of flowering plants, and are known to cause hepatotoxicity, genotoxicity, and carcinogenicity. Over 660 PAs have been identified with a wide spectrum of different chemical structures. Humans are readily exposed to PAs via the ingestion of herbal products that are directly derived from PA-producing plants (e.g., herbal medicine, plant-derived health product) or foodstuffs that are frequently contaminated with PAs (e.g., grains, tea, honey). To minimize and/or avoid human PA exposure, several regulations have been set up by food and/or drug administration authorities of different countries. However, all PA intake thresholds in the regulations are set up for a sum of different PAs assuming that all PAs have an equal toxic potency. On the other hand, increasing evidences have suggested that structurally diverse PAs differ significantly in their toxic potency, despite the identical metabolic activation-mediated toxic mechanism underlying all PAs to exert hepatotoxicity. Although, cytotoxic and genotoxic effects of different PAs have been extensively assessed on various in vitro cell models to illustrate the broad toxic potency of different PAs, toxicokinetics (TK), especially absorption and metabolism processes, has been proved to significantly affect PA intoxication. Therefore, there is a high demand for a better understanding of differences in relative toxic potency of different PAs, by considering TK profiles of different PAs to establish a more rational evaluation approach for the establishment of exposure limits and the risk assessment of PA exposure. Considering the unrealistic in vivo studies, especially in human, to obtain TK profiles of all PAs, an alternative strategy is required. Physiologically based kinetics (PBK) modelling is an ideal mathematical approach capable of incorporating the in vitro data to predict the in vivo kinetics of drugs/xenobiotics and conducting interspecies extrapolation. Therefore, in the proposed study, we aim to 1) investigate absorption and metabolism differences of different PAs using in vitro tests to generate absorption and metabolic kinetic data for PBK modeling; 2) establish and verify PBK models to describe TK fates of different PAs and their toxicity-related metabolites; and 3) investigate in vitro genotoxicity of different PAs followed by extrapolating them into the verified PBK models to obtain in vivo outcome for toxicity ranking of different PAs. The results obtained will provide a more rational approach for assessing relative toxic potencies of different PAs and thus for future establishment of a more appropriate regulation of human PA exposure. 吡咯裡西啶類生物鹼（PA）是一類常見的具有肝毒性、基因毒性及致癌性的化合物，存在於近3%的開花植物中。目前已發現超過660種具有不同化學結構的PA。人們很容易通過以下兩種方式攝入PA，1）服用含PA的草藥或由天然产物製成的健康食品；2）服用被PA污染的食物，如穀物、茶和蜂蜜等。 目前各國的食品和藥品監管部門都設置了多種不同的法律法規，以減低或避免人們對PA的攝入。這些法規中對PA攝入的限量規定都是以所含不同PA的總含量為依據，並默認所有PA的毒性程度相同。然而越來越多的證據表明儘管所有PA都會通過相同的代謝激活途徑致毒，但不同化學結構的PA毒性差別巨大。目前，已有多種體外細胞模型應用於PA細胞毒性及基因毒性的評估研究，然而PA的體內毒物代謝動力學行為，尤其是其體內的吸收及代謝，可顯著影響PA的最終體內毒性。因此，急需一種可以考慮到不同PA毒物代謝動力學行為的毒性評價方法用以更深入的瞭解不同化學結構PA的毒性差異，從而建立更加合理的不同PA攝入限量及風險評估方法。 由於直接通過體內研究，尤其是相關的人體研究，來獲取PA毒物代謝動力學特徵並不現實，因此我們需要尋找一種替代方法。基於生理的藥物動力學（PBK）建模便是一種十分理想的方案。PBK建模是一種數學建模方法，它可以利用體外的相關數據來預測藥物或外源性物質的體內動力學行為，並可進行不同種屬間的推算。因此，本項目旨在：1）利用多種體外實驗來研究不同PA的吸收和代謝差異，並獲取相關的體外吸收及代謝動力學參數用於之後的PBK建模；2）建立並驗證不同PA及其毒性相關代謝產物的體內PBK模型；3）檢測不同PA的體外基因毒性，並通過已驗證的PBK模型外推得到其體內毒性結果，從而對不同化學結構的PA進行毒性評級。預期取得的結果將提供一個更加合理的方法來評估不同PA的相對毒性，並有助於建立一個更加合適的PA攝入限量的法律法規。

14106120.label: Realisation of objectives
14106120.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are common phytochemicals present in ~3% of flowering plants and known to cause hepatotoxicity and genotoxicity. Till now, ~660 PAs have been identified with a wide spectrum of different chemical structures. Humans are readily exposed to PAs via ingestion of herbal remedies made from PA-containing plants or foods contaminated with PAs. For risk assessment on PA exposure, regulations have been set up by several food and/or drug administrative authorities based on the sum of different PAs, assuming that all PAs produce an equal toxic potency. However, individual PAs differ significantly in their toxic potency, the assessing approach based on total PA exposure is apparently inaccurate, thereby dampening the precision risk assessment on real-life PA exposure. Hepatotoxic PAs are divided into two types: retronecine-type and otonecine-type, and the majority of reported toxic PAs belongs to retronecine-type. Toxic PAs are pro-toxins and have the same metabolism-mediated intoxicating mechanism: metabolic activation. Mediated by hepatic cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, all toxic PAs are metabolically oxidized to the corresponding dehydro-PAs, which contain an identical structure of the core pyrrole moiety ((+/-)-6,7-dihydro-7-hydroxy-1-hydroxymethyl-5H-pyrrolizine) regardless of structures of the parent PAs. Dehydro-PAs are biologically active and can rapidly bind with cellular proteins or DNAs to form pyrrole-protein adducts (PPA) or pyrrole-DNA adducts (PDA), leading to hepatotoxicity or genotoxicity. The toxic potency of different PAs depends mainly on their different absorption and metabolism processes, which are encompassed by toxicokinetic profiles of PAs. Physiologically based kinetics (PBK) modeling is an ideal mathematical approach capable of incorporating the in vitro data to predict the in vivo kinetics of drugs/xenobiotics and conducting interspecies extrapolation. Therefore, the delineation of toxicokinetic profiles of different PAs, by means of PBK modeling, can facilitate a rational evaluation of exposure limits and the previse risk assessment of PA exposure. The present project aims to develop a PBK model for predicting toxicity of different PAs, and thus reducing animal toxicity tests in the future. To investigate hepatotoxic potency of different PAs, a zebrafish model, which mimics physiological processes of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion, was used to evaluate hepatotoxicity of commercially available 9 different PAs. The results demonstrated that PAs caused distinct structure-dependent hepatotoxicity in zebrafish (Paper 1 and Abstracts 1-2 in Part C). In addition, a rat model was also utilized to investigate PA-induced hepatotoxicity caused by individual PAs or PA-containing herbal extracts, and both administrative approaches demonstrated significant and dose-dependent hepatotoxicity. The toxic potencies correlated well with amounts of PA exposure and the formation of PPA for all exposed PAs, suggesting that regardless of the structure, all PAs cause dose-dependent hepatotoxicity and PPA can be used as a biomarker to screen PA-induced liver injury (PA-ILI) and rank toxic potency caused by different PAs and PA-containing natural products, which generally contain multiple PAs with different structures (Papers 2-3 in Part C). To develop PBK modelling, toxicokinetics and metabolism of different PAs were firstly investigated in rat model. In particular, the detailed toxicokinetic studies of the parent PA, PA N-oxide (major metabolite of retronecine-type only) and toxicity-related PPA were studied for the representative and structurally diverse retronecine-type PAs: retrorsine (RTS) and monocrotaline (MCT), and otonecine-type PA: clivorine (CLI). The kinetic parameters of PAs and PA N-oxides were determined from plasma concentration-time profiles, while PPAs were assessed from both plasma and erythrocyte concentration-time profiles. The results demonstrated that dramatic toxicokinetic differences, including not only PAs but also PA N-oxides and the derived PPAs were found among structurally diverse PAs in rats, laying the basis for varied hepatotoxic potencies induced by different PAs, PA-containing herbal products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs (Paper 4 and Abstract 3 in Part C. Yuen Ching To Thesis). Further, the parameters regarding absorption, metabolism, and distribution of PAs, including apparent permeability coefficients (Papp), kinetic parameters (Vmax and Km) and plasma protein binding of PAs were obtained from in vitro assays. The obtained toxicokinetic data of each representative PA (i.e. RTS and CLI) of two different types were used to validate the established PBK models and limited deviation between the observed and simulated data for both types of PAs proved that the developed PBK modelling has a potential to extrapolate in vitro kinetic data to in vivo situation. In addition, sensitivity analyses were performed to identify important parameters that may significantly affect the simulation of toxicokinetic profiles of PAs. Population simulations were carried out to assess the combined effects of variations in population physiology. More importantly, interspecies extrapolations on PA intoxication were also conducted to make predictions of in vivo time-plasma concentration profiles in human in which the maximum concentration (Cmax) was used to translate the in vitro concentration-response curves obtained from CYP3A4-expressing human liver sinusoidal endothelial cell model into the dose-response relationship in human by the PBK model-facilitated reverse dosimetry approach, the 40% maximal effective concentration (EC40) value was obtained to quantify the toxic potency of PAs. The established PBK model was further applied to predict TK of other structurally diverse PAs based on the available in vivo and/or in vitro data and the toxicity in both animal and human HepaRG cells, and the results demonstrated that our establishment of PBK model could provide a more rational approach for the risk assessment of relative toxic potency of different PAs (Papers 4-5 and Abstracts 3-4 in Part C. Yuen Ching To Thesis). In addition, it was interesting and unexpected to overserve that retronecine-type PA produce more toxicity-related PPA via oral than intravenous administration, indicating more server PA-ILI via oral administration, suggesting that P450-mediated PA-ILI is much severer via oral than intravenous administration of retronecine-type PA. Whereas otonecine-type PA showed an opposite trend, the common phenomenon in that more PPA formed via intravenous than oral administration. Although such results obtained from retronecine-type PAs were unexpected and not proposed in the original study plan, we carried some preliminary study and the results demonstrated that via oral administration, the gut microbiota was responsible, at least in part, for enhancing PA-ILI via mediating redox biotransformation between PA and PA-NO, suggesting that modulation of gut microbiota and/or intestinal microenvironment might be an innovative intervention for mitigating PA-ILI (Abstracts 5-7 in Part C), and further investigation is warrened. In conclusion, the results demonstrated that structurally different PAs have significantly varied oral absorbability, metabolism, metabolic rates, and elimination. Therefore, toxicokinetic is of utmost importance in determining relative toxic potency of structurally diverse PAs. Dramatic toxicokinetic differences, including not only PAs but also PA N-oxides and PPA, were found among structurally diverse PAs, laying the basis for varied hepatotoxic potencies induced by different PA-containing herbal remedies and PA-contaminated food stuffs. Notably, our results for the first time uncovered an unexpected novel finding in that oral administration of retronecine-type PA causes significantly severer hepatotoxicity than that via intravenous injection, which warrants further in-depth exploration.

14106120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14106120.value: The major outcome of this project is that the physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modelling for predicting the relative hepatotoxic potency of individual PAs has been developed. This PBK model can provide the important parameters to relevant international authorities for their considerations to develop more appropriate and practicable regulations of PA exposure. Collectively, our findings for the first time provide solid evidence and comprehensive information on the hepatotoxicity induced by different PAs and the relative toxic potencies of structurally diverse PAs. Comparing with the current assessment based on a total PA content, the use of toxicity of individual PAs will facilitate more accurate ranking of different PAs and provide scientific rationale for future establishing more suitable and appropriate regulations for human PA exposure. Furthermore, our findings offer an alternative approach via using in vitro toxic data to predict in vivo toxic outcomes with the aid of our developed PBK modelling to achieve a more reliable toxicity ranking of different PAs. Such a study using PBK modelling to predict the in vivo toxicity of structurally diversified PAs also sets up a good example for incorporating the reduction of animal use for toxicity studies. In addition, unexpectedly an unusual and interesting phenomenon was discovered for the first time in that oral exposure of retronecine-type PA but not otonecine-type PA induce significantly severer hepatotoxicity than their intravenous administration regardless of their lower oral bioavailability. Our hypothesis and possible explanation for this disparity is due to gut microbiota and liver mediated redox metabolism, i.e. N-oxidation of retronecine-type PA to form the corresponding PA N-oxide, which can be further reduced back to the corresponding PA, and thus extend remarkably longer time in the body, forming significantly higher level of PPA and leading to more severer toxicity via oral administration. Further studies are needed to approve such hypothesis. Currently, more relevant studies have been careering in our research team, and hopefully the mechanism underlining such an unusual and interesting phenomenon will be discovered in the near future. Parts of the results have been published in scientific papers and/or reported in conferences (Papers 1-5 and Abstracts 1-7 in Part C). Further, few more manuscripts reporting the above-mentioned findings are currently under preparation for future publication.

14106120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14106120.value: With the availability of our developed PBK model, the hepatotoxic potency of individual PAs can be predicted in the future, which will certainly facilitate more accurate ranking of the relative hepatotoxic potencies of different PAs by the relevant international organizations and authorities in different countries, and also be utilized by the researchers in the field for their investigation on hepatotoxicity of individual PAs and/or extracts of PA-containing herbal and PA-contaminated-food stuffs. In addition, with a comparison of intravenous administration, our novel finding on the significantly severer hepatotoxicity via oral administration of retronecine-type PA but not otonecine-type PA open a light in the research on PA-induced hepatotoxicity. On the other hand, the detailed mechanism underlying such an unusual phenomenon is far from fully delineated. Therefore, further in-depth mechanistic investigation is warranted, and in fact has already been conducting by our research team.

14106120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14106120.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are natural toxins widely present in ~3% flowering plants. Currently ~6000 PAs have been identified. Humans are readily exposed to PAs by ingestion of PA-containing herbal remedies or PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Due to liver metabolism to produce toxic metabolites, PAs are known to cause hepatotoxicity. Various international organizations and authorities in different countries have established regulations for PA exposure. However, because toxic potencies of individual PAs are largely unknown, current regulations are based on the concept of equal toxic potency for all PAs, although it is well-accepted that different PAs induce different toxic potencies. Therefore, our study developed a novel physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modelling for predicting hepatotoxic potency of individual PAs by incorporating the parameters of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and hepatotoxicity of various PAs. Our developed PBK model can predict hepatotoxic potency of individual PAs and therefore can be used for food and/or drug administration/regulation authorities to establish more suitable regulations for PA exposure, for academic researchers to predict more reliable scientific data for risk assessment of different PAs, and for relevant manufacturers and consumers to have well-regulated natural products with rational quality control for prevention of PA intoxication.

14107420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107420.value: 高等生物的基因組具有復雜的三維（3D）結構，與各種類型的分子活動（包括轉錄調控）緊密相關。這個3D架構涉及許多不同級別的結構組件，當中包括百萬核酸規模的拓撲關聯域（topologically associating domain，簡稱TAD）。TAD是一種連續的基因組區域，其間的染色質相互作用頻率比跨越TAD邊界的頻率高出很多。TAD其中一個最為人所熟知的功用是轉錄隔離，即調控元件如增強子通常調節同一TAD中的基因。但是，這種絕緣並不完全；有時調節元件可以調節同一染色體上相距很遠的基因，甚至在另一個染色體上的基因。理論上，這可以用TAD的3D結構來解釋，即TAD必定有一些基因座位於它的“表面”上，因此它們可以更容易與TAD外部的基因座進行相互作用。但是，到目前為止TAD的3D結構還沒有被詳細研究，原因包括細胞之間的可變性以及現有數據不足以同時測量TAD當中不同基因座的位置。 這裡，我們建議使用一種可以從染色體構象捕獲（chromosome conformation capture簡稱3C）類方法（例如Hi-C）的數據計算出來的度量來研究TAD的3D結構。此度量稱為TAD內比率，定義為一個基因座興其他基因座的相互活動中，位於同一TAD的比率。如果一個基因座位處TAD的核心，它只能與該TAD中的其他基因座相互作用，因此它將具有非常高的TAD內比率。相反來說，如果一個基因座位處TAD的表面，它可以更頻繁地與TAD外部的基因座相互作用，因此其TAD內比率會比較低。TAD內比率可以從多細胞（bulk）、複合（multiplex）或單細胞（single-cell）數據計算，其中後兩種數據受細胞間變異性的影響較小。 在初步研究中，我們使用人類GM12878細胞系的複合數據產生了多項證據表明TAD內比率確實反映TAD的3D結構。有趣的是，我們發現基因的TAD內比率與它們的表達水平呈明顯的反比，而高度表達的基因的TAD內比率從未大於0.2，說明它們傾向於駐留在TAD表面。我們還發現位於不同TAD的高表達基因可以擁有相近的3D位置，形成一個組合。 基於這些初步發現，我們計劃進行四部分的研究。首先，我們將使用更多細胞類型和物種的複合和單細胞數據來大規模地證明TAD內比率的有效性。第二，我們將擴大TAD內比率與基因調控之間的關係研究範圍至調節元件和轉錄因子，以查看它們的位置是否趨向出現在TAD核心或TAD表面上。我們還將研究這些情況的細胞特異性。第三，我們將研究TAD的3D結構是否和細胞分化及疾病有關。我們將使用細胞類型的主要調控分子和與疾病有關的遺傳變異資料庫來研究它們的位置是否與TAD的3D結構有關，並使用肌肉幹細胞和全能擴增多能幹細胞（totipotent expanded pluripotent stem cells）來測試部分發現。最後，我們將使用TAD內比率來定義新的能量項，以改善現有的計算基因組結構模型。

14107420.label: Realisation of objectives
14107420.value: We have successfully carried out the project and obtained a lot of novel biological findings. Objective 1: We have established the intra-TAD ratio as a measure of the "coreness" of a genomic region with respect to the three-dimensional (3D) structure of the chromatin domain that it belongs. We have developed ways to compute intra-TAD ratio from different types of data, including bulk Hi-C, SPRITE, single-cell Hi-C, and structural models derived from single-cell Hi-C data. In addition, we have defined a related measure, the intra-single cell domain ratio (intra-scDomain ratio) that quantifies the coreness of a genomic region using super-resolution imaging data. We have confirmed that i) intra-scDomain ratio is a suitable measure of "coreness" in individual cells, and ii) despite cell-to-cell variability, intra-TAD ratio computed from bulk-sample data correlates well with intra-scDomain ratio averaged over a small number of cells, which shows that there are strong tendencies of the chromatin domain 3D structures even though they are not identical in different single cells. We observed these findings using imaging and sequencing data from human IMR-90 and GM12878 cells and mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Objective 2: Using data from GM12878, mESC, and other ENCODE cell lines, we have made a series of interesting findings related to functions of chromatin domain 3D structures. Specifically, we found that the surfaces of these 3D structures are enriched for, in a cell-type-dependent manner i) high gene expression, ii) chromatin accessibility and active histone marks, iii) active cis-regulatory elements, iv) binding of transcription factors, v) early-replicating DNA regions, and vi) disease-associated non-coding genetic variants. Objective 3: We have proposed several molecular mechanisms that underlie the findings we obtained in Objective 2. First, we propose that the enrichment of molecular activities on chromatin domain surfaces is due to accessibility. Specifically, while genomic regions buried in the core of a chromatin domain 3D structure are insulated from the outside, those that reside on the surface of the 3D structure can more easily interact with genes, regulatory elements, and protein factors from outside their domains. Second, we propose that this core-versus-surface distinction is more important for the heterochromatin loci in the B compartment. The B compartment contains larger and more compacted chromatin domains than the A compartment. Therefore, genomic regions in the cores of the 3D structures are more insulated in the B compartment case. In contrast, compartment A contains chromatin domains that are smaller and less compact, which provide weaker insulation of the core regions, and thus there is less functional difference between core and surface regions. Third, smaller DNA binding proteins can more easily diffuse into the cores of chromatin domain 3D structures. As a result, the heterochromatin mark H3K9me3 is more enriched in chromatin domain cores than the repressive mark H3K27me3, since the histone writers for the former have lower molecular weights than the latter. We propose that this difference allows H3K27me3-marked regions to be more easily de-methylated and subsequently reactivated, which means surface regions are more facultatively repressed and core regions are more constitutively repressed. Objective 4: We have identified interesting genomic regions that are functionally regulated by chromatin domain 3D structures. We have verified their molecular activities using independent experimental data. We are now planning functional studies of these regions, which will evaluate the extent to which chromatin domain 3D structures affect gene regulation in normal and disease states.

14107420.value: The major findings are summarized in Section 5.3 above. These findings are reported in a manuscript currently under review in Nature Communications, with a preprint deposited to bioRxiv. Some bioinformatics methods involved in this project were also used in some other relevant projects (see Part C).

14107420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107420.value: There are two important future developments that we plan to work on. The first is extending the study to include molecular activities measured by single-cell assays. Although we have used imaging and sequencing data obtained from individual single cells to compute intra-scDomain ratio and intra-TAD ratio, the functional activity data (gene expression, transcription factor binding, etc.) we used all came from bulk-sample assays. We will find single-cell multi-modal data with both chromatin interactions and molecular activities measured from the same cells to see whether our findings still hold true at the single-cell level. The second future development is confirming the causal roles of chromatin domain 3D structures. Most of our current findings are based on correlations, which cannot tell the causal direction. We will use time-course data to check whether migration of a genomic locus to the chromatin domain surface precedes or follows its molecular activities.

14107420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107420.value: In this project, we have proposed a new way that genes are regulated, which is related to 3D structures of local structural components (called chromatin domains) in the DNA. We have found that there is an enrichment of disease-associated DNA changes on the surface of these structures. This finding may be used in the future to identify DNA changes that cause diseases among the large number of DNA changes typically observed in disease studies.

14107520.label: Realisation of objectives
14107520.value: We have generally achieved the first objective successfully, with some limitations in relation to subject recruitment. The recruitment was below our target. COVID was a significant factor that majorly affected our recruitment progress, especially in the first 2 years of the project. This is because many of our assessments, such as polysomnography, are hospital-based. Therefore, our assessment was subjected to stringent infection control measures of the hospital during the period. To address this obstacle, we accelerated our recruitment process in the following year after major infection control measures were eased. However, since our target populations were mainly in the middle to old age range, they were generally more reluctant to come to the hospital for assessment, even in the early post-pandemic period. To improvise, we performed some assessments that can be performed outside of the clinical area, before updated PSG data can be available. Under this new workflow, the recruitment selection would be based on previous assessment data and clinician impressions. While our measures improved our recruitment figures by a lot, and we almost made up for the lost progress during the pandemic, upon the final review of the updated PSG data, about 20 subjects were found to be ineligible due to a higher-than-expected level of RSWA, reducing our final subject pool. In this accelerated recruitment process, we also could not match the sex of the case and control group. Nevertheless, we conducted our intended assessment for our eligible subjects and have successfully run predefined comparisons between the two groups. For the second objective, again, we achieved the objective with limitations in recruitment. The same COVID factor is also in play here. However, it causes even more difficulties in this second part of the study because the PET scan needs to be done in our partner hospital, which has its own infection control measures. Furthermore, after two years of recruitment hiatus, there were additional unforeseen obstacles to conducting PET scans in our partner hospital. First, the hospital had newly implemented additional in-house approval procedures in addition to the research ethics approval we already obtained from the Joint CUHK-NTEC Research Ethics Committee. This unexpected process caused a further 6 months of delay in the study process. Second, due to the rising in cost of manpower and material over the years since the drafting of the proposal, our partner hospital needed to charge us a much higher sum per scan when we finally were able to start scanning. The charge was further increased by 50% during the last phase of the study. Overall, the average cost per scan was more than double the amount built-in in our initial budget. During this process, we try to overcome this obstacle by active negotiation with our partner hospital to secure the most discounted charge possible. However, despite our best effort, we need to reduce the number of scans that we can perform, resulting in a smaller sample size. However, we have successfully completed as many scans as possible, and run our predefined analyses.

14107520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107520.value: For the first part of the study, we recruited 24 patients with dream-enactment behaviour without sufficient REM sleep without atonia (DEB) and 51 control subjects. The two groups are matched in age (DEB vs controls = 58.7 vs 59.1 years, p=0.69), but not in sex (DEB vs controls = 25% vs 65% female, p=0.001). The two groups have significant differences in self-reported dream enactment (mean RBDQ -HK factor 2 score, DEB vs control = 16.6 vs 0.73, p<0.001) and level of REM sleep without atonia as recorded in the chin EMG channel (DEB vs control = 6.2 % vs 3.6 %, p =0.001). For their individual prodromal PD markers, the DEB group are more likely to have lifetime depression (DEB vs controls = 42.0% vs 9.8%, p=0.002), and have more daytime sleepiness (ESS score, DEB vs controls = 12.4 vs 9.3, p <0.001). The DEB group has a significantly higher probability of prodromal PD than the control group (DEB vs control = 0.11 vs 0.01, p<0.001). This difference remains significant even if we take out the factor of sex and the presence of clinical RBD. For the second part of the study, we randomly recruited 16 DEB subjects and 15 controls from the subject pool of the first part of the study to undergo dopamine PET imaging. The two groups are matched in age (DEB vs controls = 58.6 vs 59.0 years, p = 0.8) and sex (DEB vs controls = xxx). Among this set of subjects, the DEB group also has a significantly higher probability of prodromal PD than the control group (DEB vs control = 0.16 vs 0.01, p<0.001). None of the dopamine PET parameters measured, including the F18-FDG and F18-DOPA measures using cerebellum as the references, and the K-values, significantly differ between the DEB and control group. Exploratory analysis did not find any significant correlation between the probability of prodromal PD and any of the dopamine PET parameters measured among the DEB subject groups with adjustment for age. In conclusion, our findings support the hypothesis that patients with with dream-enactment behavior without sufficient REM sleep without atonia have a higher probability of prodromal PD than controls. Yet the hypothesis that patients with with dream-enactment behavior without sufficient REM sleep without atonia have a lower level of dopamine in putamen compared with healthy controls was not supported by our results.

14107520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107520.value: The result of our study suggests that patients with DEB but without sufficient RSWA might have a higher risk of Parkinson's disease compared to controls by clinical assessment, although the dopamine PET scan does not reflect it. The reason for this discrepancy is currently unknown and worth further examination. Further research should focus on longitudinal follow-up of these subjects.

14107520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107520.value: In this study, we recruited 24 subjects who acted out their dream at night but were not noted to have excessive muscle activity when measured, and 51 subjects without such problem as control. We found that the group who act out dreams (DEB) is more likely to have depression, and they also reported more daytime sleepiness when compared to the control group. When we calculate their risk score in predicting how likely they will develop into Parkinson’s disease, the DEB group also had a higher risk score compared to the control group. We further recruited 16 subjects from the DEB group and 15 subjects from the control group to receive a brain scan that can reflect the level of dopamine, the neurotransmitter lost in Parkinson’s disease, in the brain. However, we did not find a significant difference in the level of dopamine in the brain between the two groups.

14107920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107920.value: 血紅素加氧酶(HO) 在多種細胞中介導血紅素氧化代謝,生成內源性一氧化碳(CO),包括氣道上皮細胞。目前發現, 人體組織細胞中存在兩種HO亞型,即HO-1 和HO-2。其中HO-2為組成性表達,而HO-1的表達則可被多種外部應激反應誘導性上調。大量研究表明,HO-1具有廣泛的生物學活性,尤其在抗炎及抗氧化方面發揮重要作用。 HO-1/CO系統對氣道上皮功能的調節,至少通過兩方面起著關鍵性作用:離子轉運和免疫反應。 然而,其潛在的分子機制尚未完全清楚。 我們早前的研究數據表明,並非所有的HO-1/CO系統引起的生物學效應都依賴於HO-1的酶活性,提示我們某些生物學功能並不依賴CO來介導。 為了更好地瞭解和研究CO的作用,實現細胞內CO水平的實時監測是十分關鍵的一步。 我們初步研究發現,CO的特異性螢光探針與活細胞成像技術的聯合應用,能很好的實時監測活細胞內CO水準的動態變化。 基於此,我們計劃開發一種全新的,能同時測量活細胞內CO和Ca2+/cAMP水準的方法,來量化氣道上皮內的離子運輸,以進一步闡明HO-1/CO系統在氣道上皮功能調節方面的作用及其機制。 我們推測CO很可能通過調控內質網-線粒體Ca2+轉運,線粒體功能依賴的信號通路(例如活性氧及炎症小體的形成)以及內質網應激反應等細胞功能來發揮其抗炎效果,因此我們將合成靶向內質網及線粒體的CO特異性螢光探針,以觀察CO的亞細胞定位。 除了以上在細胞水準的體外研究,CO的抗炎效果還將在屋塵蟎(HDM)誘導的過敏性氣道炎症模型小鼠中進行驗證。 在此體內研究階段,我們將從以下三個方面驗證HO-1/CO系統對氣道上皮功能的調節作用及潛在機制:(1)電解質轉運和氣道表面液體形成的潛在細胞信號機制;(2)炎症相關細胞因數分泌;(3)在HDM誘導的過敏性氣道炎症小鼠模型中的抗炎作用。 本研究的結果將加強目前對HO-1/CO系統在人類上皮細胞中生物學功能的認識和理解,併為HO-1/CO系統在炎症相關呼吸系統疾病中的潛在治療前景提供新的思路及策略。

14107920.label: Realisation of objectives
14107920.value: Objective (1) Carbon monoxide (CO) altered the transcriptome profiles of primary human bronchial epithelial cells HBEs in airway-liquid interface (ALI) culture: We studied mRNA expression in CO-exposed airway epithelial cells using state-of-the-art single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq), provided by Single Cell Omics Core at our School of Biomedical Sciences, rather than conventional qRT-PCR as mentioned in the grant proposal. This novel approach allowed us to fully evaluate the transcriptional differences between control and treated cells, rather than being limited to changes in the expression of a few mRNAs. Specifically, we were able to identify novel biological processes or signalling pathways in bronchial epithelial cells affected by exposure to CO. More importantly, this approach enabled us to observe transcriptional differences between fully differentiated airway epithelial cell types while identifying the epithelial cell types and associated biological processes affected by CO. In our previous report, we mentioned that CO could delay oxidative stress-induced senescence in bronchial epithelial cells. We used the primary HBEs to test the effects of CO and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) on the bronchial epithelium and further explored the potential molecular mechanisms of these effects using scRNA seq and REACTOME pathway analysis. We discovered that in secretory cells, CO significantly inhibited the upregulated expression of interleukin (IL)-related genes and pathways stimulated by H2O2, including IL-6, IL-10, IL-13, and IL-20, suggesting that CO can markedly suppress oxidative stress-induced secretion of inflammatory factors. In basal cells, CO primarily upregulated genes such as ATR and WNT5A and pathways such as transcriptional regulation of pluripotent stem cells and activation of the pre-replicative complex. Different cellular functions have been linked to these genes and pathways, including regulating cell proliferation, serving as DNA damage sensors, and activating cell cycle checkpoint signalling upon DNA damage. Given that bronchial epithelial basal cells possess some stem cell characteristics, oxidative stress induced by H2O2 may suppress the replicative proliferation of these cells, whereas CO partially restores the expression of related genes. In ciliated cells, CO mainly upregulated genes and signalling pathways related to integrins, cell surface adhesion, and cytoskeletal proteins, suggesting that it may restore the motility of ciliated cells by counteracting the inhibitory effects of H2O2. In summary, CO exerted distinctly different effects on gene expression in different airway epithelial cell types. Overall, our findings suggest that CO maintains functional homeostasis of the airway epithelium under oxidative stress conditions by inhibiting the secretion of inflammatory factors by secretory cells, preserving the stemness and proliferation of basal cells, and restoring the adhesion and motility functions of ciliated cells. CO exposure did not affect cAMP- and Ca2+- dependent ion transport activities in ALI-cultured primary HBE and 16HBE14o- epithelia: ALI cultures of primary HBEs and 16HBE14o- epithelia were stimulated with Uridine-5′-triphosphate (UTP) and forskolin to induce Ca2+- and cAMP- dependent ion transport in the presence or absence of CO. Ca2+ or cAMP was monitored simultaneously with ISC (short-circuit current, an index of electrogenic ion transport). We found that CO had no effect on either the Ca2+- or cAMP- dependent increase in ISC and did not induce the expected changes in airway surface liquid height due to its lack of effect on active ion transport activities. To extend our study to a more clinically relevant condition, we exposed primary HBEs and 16HBE14o- epithelia to traditional cigarette smoke, a readily available and standardised source of CO in daily life. Interestingly, cigarette smoke significantly reduced UTP-induced increases in Ca2+ signalling and subsequent changes in ISC in both primary HBEs and 16HBE14o- epithelia. Cigarette smoke also inhibited forskolin-evoked increases in cAMP levels and ISC. However, the reductions in epithelial ion transport activities were not correlated with changes in the expression of various ion channel (e.g. cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator, Ca2+- activated K+ channels, cAMP-activated K+ channels) and transporter proteins (e.g. Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter) involved in ion transport. Therefore, the detrimental effects of cigarette smoke on airway epithelial ion transport functions may not be directly related to CO. Objective (2) CO suppressed H2O2-induced increases in intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mitochondrial superoxide in airway epithelial cells: We used Nile red CO, a fluorescent molecular chemosensor, to determine intracellular CO levels in a human airway epithelial cell line. In our models, we used H2O2 to induce oxidative stress/damage and ROS generation. We measured the intracellular CO and ROS levels simultaneously and verified that CO inhibited H2O2-induced total and mitochondrial ROS production, suggesting that CO inhibits the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines by airway epithelial cells through this mechanism. We also verified that CO protects against H2O2-induced senescence in airway epithelial cells. Specifically, CO protects cells by inhibiting intracellular ROS formation via activation of the SIRT3/MnSOD/p53/p21 pathway. CO exerted anti-inflammatory and other cellular effects on airway epithelia: We conducted proteomic analysis to identify differentially expressed proteins and pathways in three human bronchial epithelial (16HBE14o-) cell models: wild-type, an H25A (HO-1 inactive) mutant, and HO-1 knockdown. We also differentiated the cellular effects mediated by the enzymatic function of HO-1 from those mediated by its non-enzymatic (non-canonical) function. The cells were subjected to oxidative stress by hemin, and inflammation was induced by lipopolysaccharides and an inflammatory cytokine cocktail including TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-1β.Additionally, we explored the HO-1/CO axis by introducing CO-releasing molecules (CORMs) into our cell models. We determined that the HO-1/CO axis is a significant regulator of cell morphology and growth and of various cellular functions, including migration and wound healing, cytosolic ROS production, inflammatory cytokine and growth factor secretion, apoptosis, and mitochondrial functions. Our findings suggest that HO-1 regulates cellular oxidative stress (anti-inflammatory effect) by modulating the protein expression of NF-κB, MAPK, p21, and E-cadherin in human bronchial epithelial cells. In conclusion, these findings offer insights into some of the mechanisms underlying HO-1 activity as a therapeutic strategy for oxidative stress-related respiratory diseases. Objective (3) CO inhibited airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) development and airway inflammation in a house dust mite (HDM)-induced mouse model of allergic asthma: In this study, we sought to examine whether CO gas or CO released from CORMs had any therapeutic effect in an HDM-sensitised mouse model of allergic asthma. We used whole-body plethysmography to monitor airway AHR, a cardinal feature of asthma. We observed markedly increased methacholine-evoked AHR in the HDM group, which was significantly decreased with CO but not CORM-2 treatment. Histological assessment of airway inflammation and tissue damage in lung sections showed that mice treated with CO had thinner airway walls, lower eosinophil accumulation, and decreased goblet cell hyperplasia, as well as less mucus production compared to HDM mice. Taken together, our results suggest that CO exposure, but not i.v. injection of CORM-2, blocks AHR development, thereby improving lung function and mitigating the airway inflammation associated with allergic asthma. As demonstrated by the above results, we have successfully met all three objectives of the research project. We have identified novel mechanisms underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of the HO-1/CO axis, including a role in mediating anti-inflammatory processes and other functions in in vitro models, as well as an anti-asthmatic effect in an in vivo mouse model. Our successful research has laid a foundation for the further exploration and development of therapeutic interventions targeting the HO-1/CO axis for the treatment of respiratory disorders such as asthma.

14107920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107920.value: To model in vivo effects, we established an ALI interface culture, enabling the differentiation of primary HBEs into a pseudostratified mucociliary epithelium consisting of ciliated cells, goblet/secretory cells, club cells, and basal cells [1]. In vivo, prolonged or excessive exposure to inhaled toxins (e.g. cigarette smoke) may stimulate oxidative stress and DNA damage, leading to stress-induced respiratory damage and various lung diseases. We found that exposure to H2O2 impaired the integrity of ALI cultures by inducing a vacuolated structure with increased goblet cell numbers, p21 protein levels, and SASP gene transcription and decreased SCGB1A1+ club cell numbers. However, treatment with CO attenuated these effects. We also found that CO plays a key role in epithelial senescence by regulating ROS production via the SIRT3/MnSOD/p53/p21 pathway [1]. This finding may have important implications for the prevention and treatment of age-associated respiratory pathologies. We subjected ALI-cultured HBEs to multiplex single-cell RNA sequencing to reveal novel transcriptional heterogeneity within the human bronchial epithelium [3] and cell type-specific responses to CO under oxidative stress conditions. Under such conditions, CO maintained the functional homeostasis of the airway epithelium by inhibiting the secretion of inflammatory factors in secretory cells, preserving the stemness and proliferation of basal cells, and restoring the adhesion and motility functions of ciliated cells. Our data thus offer a fresh perspective on CO-induced changes in the cellular landscape and cell type-specific responses in human bronchial epithelium. We studied three human bronchial epithelial (16HBE14o-) cell models – wild-type, H25A (HO-1 inactive) mutant, and HO-1 knockdown – to further elucidate the enzymatic and non-enzymatic (non-canonical) functions of HO-1 in modulating cellular functions. The HO-1/CO axis is an important regulator of cell morphology and growth, as well as various cellular functions such as migration and wound healing, cytosolic ROS production, inflammatory cytokine and growth factor release, cell death, and mitochondrial functions. Our findings suggest that HO-1 regulates cellular oxidative stress, an anti-inflammatory effect, by modulating NF-κB, MAPK, p21, and E-cadherin expression in HBEs. We also observed differences between the enzymatic and non-enzymatic effects of HO-1 on the abovementioned cellular functions [5]. In our in vivo study, we discovered that CO modulates the pathogenesis of type 2 immune responses against an experimental allergen in a mouse model of HDM-induced asthma. These findings may increase the therapeutic potential of CO for allergic asthma.

14107920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107920.value: The outcomes of this research have the potential to influence future grant applications and to advance knowledge in the fields of airway epithelial cell biology and respiratory diseases. We have demonstrated the importance of the HO-1/CO axis in mediating anti-inflammatory effects in the airway epithelia. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with chronic airway inflammation and is the third-ranked cause of death in the US; therefore, it is important to investigate the involvement of the HO-1/CO axis in this disease. I have invited Prof. Chan Wan-Yi (Department of Paediatrics, CUHK) to initiate a pilot project to investigate the relationship between HO-1 mRNA and protein expression in human non-COPD and COPD airway organoid models. Prof. Chan is a molecular and cellular biologist in respiratory medicine with strong expertise in using ex vivo cultures of human respiratory tissues for phenotypic characterisation and risk assessment. Our preliminary data suggest that HO-1 expression is decreased in COPD organoids, and this decrease might contribute to airway remodelling and inflammation. I expect to collaborate further with Prof. Chan and to submit a joint GRF and/or HMRF grant proposal in 2025/2026.

14107920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107920.value: In this study, we developed a powerful air–liquid interface airway culture model to emulate respiratory tract characteristics in vitro. We found that oxidative stress disrupted the cell structure of the modelled bronchial epithelium, whereas exposure to carbon monoxide (CO) seemed to counteract these negative effects through anti-oxidative effects. This protective mechanism involves several cellular pathways, with significant implications for treating age-related respiratory diseases. We also used advanced single-cell RNA sequencing techniques to understand how individual bronchial epithelial cell types respond to oxidative stress and CO treatment. We discovered that CO helps to maintain balance and function in the airway lining by reducing inflammation and preserving the properties of various cell types. Furthermore, we explored the roles of the enzymatic and non-enzymatic functions of HO-1 in managing cellular stress and inflammation. We demonstrated that HO-1 is a crucial regulator of cell growth, inflammation, and other important functions such as wound healing. Finally, we found that CO modulated immune responses in a mouse model of allergic asthma, suggesting that it might play a therapeutic role in managing this disease. All these discoveries have opened new avenues to the potential use of CO in treating respiratory diseases such as asthmatic inflammation.

14108420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108420.value: 心血管疾病，包括與糖尿病和糖尿病有關的血管並發症與急性和慢性炎症相關的血管疾病是導致人類死亡的主要原因。最近，我們已經證明免疫細胞例如調節性T細胞（Treg）促進新生小鼠心臟的修復和再生。而且，Treg可直接增強2型糖尿病（T2D）缺血性損傷後外周血管內皮細胞的增殖和再生。然而，免疫細胞介導的心血管疾病的分子機制修復和再生的研究較少。內皮轉錄因子或其在免疫反應下游的相互作用可能是在T2D小鼠中促進血管再生的另一種方法。在此補助金申請中，我們建議確定可能調節血管的假定轉錄因子。在此提案中，我們調查YY1是如何在糖尿病EC中被下調（目標1），YY1如何調節缺血後血管生成（目標2）以及YY1的過表達是否可以拯救T2D小鼠的血管再生（目的3 ）。我們的建議將描述YY1在血管修復和再生中的作用機理及針對肥胖和糖尿病相關血管疾病的潛在治療方案。

14108420.label: Realisation of objectives
14108420.value: We have finished this project with completion of all objectives and the work has contributed to publication of 9 journal articles. Diabetes is a chronic inflammatory disease, we have previously reported that CD4 and CD8 T cells play an indispensable role in causing diabetic vascular complication as depletion of either subset promotes vascular regeneration even in diabetes. Here, we particularly found that YY1 is the major regulator of endothelial cell function, and its expression was controlled by CD4 T cells via cytokine expression (Objective 1). We further demonstrated the effect of endothelial-specific YY1 by crossing Cdh5-Cre with YY1 fl/fl, with an aim to generate an endothelial YY1 knockout mice model. We found that a complete endothelial YY1 knockout caused embryonic lethality. Using heterozygous Cdh5-Cre;YY1 fl/+ as the conditional knockout (cKO) model and wildtype (WT) mice as control, we found a decreased revascularization in cKO mice after ischemic injury. To further understand how YY1 regulates endothelial cell function in angiogenesis, we utilized siRNA to produce an in vitro YY1 knockdown model in hESC-ECs and MS1. We identified three key processes that are involved in regulating and maintaining normal vascular function, namely cell proliferation and migration, vasodilation and vascular barrier permeability. By assessing these processes related to vascular function, we demonstrated that YY1 regulates angiogenesis through cell proliferation and migration, but not vasodilation or vascular barrier function (Objective 2). Lastly, we showed that CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T-cells (Treg) promote YY1 expression in endothelial cells. We used Treg as a stimulation of endothelial YY1 expression which directly regulates endothelial cells proliferation. We demonstrated such stimulation of YY1 promoted vascular regeneration in T2D mice (Objective 3).

14108420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108420.value: In this project, we studied the functional role and regulatory mechanism of endothelial YY1 in vascular repair and regeneration with a focus on the pathogenesis and potential therapeutic regimen targeting vascular diseases associated with obesity and diabetes. We revealed that YY1 is a key regulator of endothelial cells (ECs). In diabetic ECs, YY1 expression is modulated by CD4 T cells via cytokine expression. To understand how YY1 regulates angiogenesis after injury, we generated an endothelial-specific YY1 knockout mice model by crossing Cdh5-Cre with YY1 fl/fl. We found that a complete endothelial cell specific ablation of YY1 led to embryonic lethality. The Cdh5-Cre;YY1 fl/fl embryos also exhibit impaired limb growth and vasculature formation, indicating a critical role of YY1 in endothelial cells. We also utilized siRNA to create a YY1 knockdown model in hESC-ECs and MS1 in vitro. Through assessing three processes that are crucial to regulating and maintaining vascular function, we found that YY1 regulates angiogenesis through cell proliferation and migration, while not affecting vasodilation or the vascular barrier function. In examining the rescue of vascular regeneration in T2D, we showed that CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T-cells (Treg) promote YY1 expression in endothelial cells. We used Treg to increase YY1 expression in ECs in T2D mice. Through the direct increase of YY1 expression level in EC, our results showed increased EC proliferation and vascular regeneration. We are preparing the manuscript upon completion of this study. In parallel, we identified the functional role of YY1 in controlling glucose homeostasis by directing regulating insulin transcription that has been published in Diabetes, 2022, as a project supported from findings of this granted study.

14108420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108420.value: To further expand the study of the regulatory mechanism of endothelial YY1 in vascular regeneration, we plan to investigate the downstream mechanisms of endothelial YY1. During this study, we found that YY1 regulated Notch signalling especially Notch1. We have confirmed their transcriptional activation activity by luciferase reporter assay. In further research, we will study how YY1 regulates endothelial cell function through Notch signalling. Moreover, we have also been collaborating with industry with the hope to generate RNA medicine targeting vascular diseases associated with obesity and diabetes for clinical use in the future.

14108420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108420.value: Cardiovascular diseases associated with diabetes mellitus is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. This project studies the mechanism of the zinc finger nuclear protein Yin Yang 1 (YY1) in regulating vascular regeneration after ischemic injury. Under diabetic condition, expression of YY1 in endothelial cells is downregulated. We found that different T-cell subtypes could control the production of endothelial YY1 via cytokine expression. Using conditional YY1 knockout and knockdown models, we then investigated how YY1 regulates angiogenesis after ischemic injury. A complete endothelial-specific knockout of YY1 in mice leads to embryonic lethality. We investigated the vascular function in an in vitro YY1 knockdown model. Among the three key processes, we showed that YY1 regulated angiogenesis through cell proliferation and migration, while not affecting vasodilation or the vascular barrier function. From the translation aspect, we have demonstrated the therapeutic efficacy of using regulatory T-cells to rescue vascular regeneration in T2D via the control of YY1 expression. We believe that our results give insights to generate safe medicine such as RNA medicine for treatment of vascular diseases associated with obesity and diabetes in the future.

14108720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108720.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive joint disorder characterized by cartilage degeneration. Articular cartilage facilitates the frictionless motion of synovial joints. However, when cartilage is damaged from trauma or excessive loading in daily use, repair is poor and may lead to OA. One reason for poor cartilage repair is due to limited number of stem/progenitor cells within cartilage. Many cartilage and progenitor cell types are investigated for cartilage repair with some success, but long-term outcomes are not always satisfactory. There are still burning needs in searching better cell source for cartilage repair. Lgr5 (Leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein coupled receptor 5) is a Wnt target gene, modulates Wnt signaling strength. Lgr5 is widely used as a molecular marker for self-renewing and multipotent adult stem cell populations in multiple organs, including the gut, stomach, hair follicle, and cartilage and bone. We recently reported that overexpression of Lgr5 in MSCs exhibited increased osteogenic capacity, which results in elevated expression of β-catenin and phosphorylated ERK1/2 within the nuclei region of cells. In contrast, loss of Lgr5 expression decreased the osteogenic differentiation ability of MSCs, accompanied with increased mitochondrial fragmentation and impaired mitochondrial dynamics in fusion and fission. Local transplantation of Lgr5+MSCs at fracture sites accelerated fracture healing. We and others also found that Lgr5 is highly expressed during embryonic cartilage development, cartilage repair and OA development, suggesting Lgr5’s important roles in cartilage development and regeneration. We hypothesize that Lgr5 may be an important regulator for cartilage development, chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and Lgr5+ MSCs, may be a better cell source for cartilage repair. The planned investigations are: (1) To study the roles of Lgr5 in MSCs chondrogenic differentiation, MSCs migration, and the underlying molecular mechanisms. (2) To identify the roles of Lgr5+ cells during cartilage development and OA progression in a mouse OA model. (3) To study the effect on cartilage development and cartilage lesion repair in Lgr5 cartilage cKO (conditional knockout) mice. (4) To evaluate and compare the therapeutic effects of Lgr5+MSCs in mouse OA model in Lgr5 cKO and normal mice. This study will clarify whether Lgr5 is an important regulator for cartilage development and cartilage repair. The current study will also define if Lgr5+MSCs may be used as cell source for cartilage lesion repair. 14109420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109420.value: 番茄是獨特的植物模型，可讓我們直接檢查表觀基因組與植物發育之間的關係。我們以前的工作表明，多種表觀遺傳因素（例如DNA甲基化，組蛋白修飾H3K27me3和染色質可及性）參與調節果實成熟基因。但是，全基因組研究通常在單個基因水平上缺乏清晰度。例如，成熟基因的上調富含啟動子hypo-DNA甲基化，基因體hypo-H3K27me3或啟動子染色質可及性的增加。儘管這些富集分析均具有統計學意義，但我們無法解釋為什麼某些基因具有相反的行為。我們的假設是水果果皮組織內部存在多種細胞類型/種群，它們的轉錄組和表觀基因組不一致，並且我們過去一直在記錄它們的平均表觀基因組和轉錄組信號。只有單細胞水平的分析才能使我們測試成熟的基因表達是否與特定細胞類型的表觀基因組變化相關。商業單細胞測序平台無法處理番茄樣品。果皮果皮細胞比微米級哺乳動物的果皮細胞大得多，有些甚至可以在成熟前生長到亞毫米大小。它們還具有難以消化的富含果膠的細胞壁和可抵抗用於哺乳動物單細胞測序的溫和裂解條件的大核。我們已經與工程部門合作構建了可處理大顆粒的定制微流控芯片。我們還開發了新穎的熱水瓶-液滴合併系統和芯片上裂解化學試劑，以及新的測序化學試劑，以應對堅韌的番茄細胞/細胞核。我們已經成功地使用約100個細胞進行了單細胞測序實驗，以證實我們系統的適用性。我們相信，這個擬議的項目可以以獨特的單細胞角度為水果成熟的機制提供有價值的見解。它還提出了重要的問題，即當數據通常來自多種細胞類型時，我們應該如何解釋全基因組分析。

14109720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109720.value: 動脈粥樣硬化是一種與肥胖、糖尿病及高血壓等密切相關的慢性炎症性疾病。內皮細胞氧化應激、炎症及內膜完整性的降低是動脈粥樣硬化發生的重要環節，上述病理改變可導致脂質在內膜下異常沉積，形成“脂質斑塊”。因此，抗炎和抗氧化應激是動脈粥樣硬化治療的重要手段。動脈粥樣硬化最常見的臨床治療藥物（如他汀類藥物）亦兼備抗氧化及抗炎功能。 核因子類胡蘿蔔素衍生2樣因子2（Nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2, Nrf2）是一種在氧化應激/炎症反應中起關鍵調控作用的轉錄因子。當被活性氧（Reactive oxygen species, ROS）或細胞內的親電子體活化後，Nrf2可通過結合靶基因啟動子區中的抗氧化反應元件調控相關基因的轉錄，防止細胞出現過度的氧化應激和炎症反應損傷。 Nrf2在內皮細胞炎症和氧化應激的調控作用雖然較為明確，但是目前並無直接證據證明內皮細胞表達的Nrf2參與動脈粥樣硬化的發生。本項目擬從炎症、氧化應激及代謝三個角度明確內皮細胞表達的Nrf2在動脈粥樣硬化發生中的作用。本項目研究成果可為動脈粥樣硬化的防治提供新的思路，為動脈粥樣硬化的新藥開發提供新靶點。

14109720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109720.value: The present project uncovers the importance of endothelial Nrf2 in the inflammation-lipid peroxidation cascades in the early stages of atherosclerosis. Endothelial cell inflammation and lipid peroxidation are linked in the early stages of atherosclerosis. Endothelial inflammation precedes and serves as an inducer of subsequent lipid peroxidation. The end products of lipid peroxidation and pro-inflammatory stimuli stimulate Nrf2 signalling, which attempts to limit further endothelial inflammation. Nrf2 plays a fundamental role in the interaction of atherogenic risk factors with lipid peroxidation and inflammation-lipid peroxidation cascades during the initiation of atherosclerosis. Compensatory activation of endothelial Nrf2 is likely to mediate the anti-atherogenic inflammation-lipid peroxidation cascade in ApoE-/- mice fed a Western diet. However, such a compensatory mechanism is usually unrecognizable because it is overridden by much stronger or dominant inflammatory forces during atherogenesis. Endothelial-specific Nrf2 deficiency accelerated atherosclerosis development in vivo, highlighting its critical role in regulating inflammation and lipid peroxidation processes during atherogenesis. In contrast, activation of Nrf2 by CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing can attenuate inflammation and lipid peroxidation, offering potential therapeutic avenues for the treatment of atherosclerotic diseases. DMI was identified as an Nrf2 activator that inhibits endothelial cell inflammation and oxidative stress-induced lipid peroxidation. In vivo administration of DMI reduced atherosclerotic plaque formation in mice, further supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting the Nrf2 pathway. In conclusion, this research highlights the importance of Nrf2 in the management of inflammation and oxidative stress in endothelial cells and suggests that enhancing Nrf2 activity may be a promising strategy for the treatment of atherosclerosis and related vascular diseases.

14109720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109720.value: Our project suggests several avenues for further research and development. Here are the proposed courses of action based on the findings: 1.Exploration of molecular mechanisms: Further studies should investigate the detailed molecular pathways by which Nrf2 activation exerts its protective effects against inflammation and lipid peroxidation. Understanding the downstream targets of Nrf2 may reveal additional therapeutic targets. 2.Long-term effects of Nrf2 activation: Conduct studies to evaluate the long-term effects of sustained Nrf2 activation on the progression and regression of atherosclerosis in various animal models. This will help determine optimal dosing regimens and treatment duration. 3.Combination therapies: To explore the potential benefits of combining Nrf2 activation with existing therapies for atherosclerosis, such as statins or anti-inflammatory drugs, to improve therapeutic outcomes. 4.Nrf2 and ferroptosis mechanisms: To further explore the relationship between Nrf2 signalling and ferroptosis in endothelial cells, in particular how this pathway may contribute to vascular health and disease. 5.Targeted delivery systems for Nrf2 activators: Develop and test novel drug delivery systems that can specifically target endothelial cells for more effective delivery of Nrf2 activators while minimizing systemic side effects.

14109720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109720.value: Our project focuses on understanding how Nrf2 can help prevent a serious disease known as atherosclerosis, the build-up of fatty deposits in the arteries that can lead to heart attacks and strokes. The study shows that inflammation and oxidative stress play an important role in the development of atherosclerosis. Activating Nrf2 was found to reduce inflammation and limit oxidative damage in blood vessel cells. The significance of this research lies in its potential to develop new treatments for cardiovascular disease. Targeting Nrf2 may be able to develop therapies that not only slow the progression of atherosclerosis, but also improve overall heart health. The findings suggest that the use of compounds that activate Nrf2, such as dimethyl itaconate, may be a promising strategy for the treatment and prevention of cardiovascular disease, making this research valuable for future medical advances.
