14109920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109920.value: Aim: The aim of this project is to elucidate the mechanistic origin of the short stature commonly observed in Werner syndrome (WS), thus providing a basis for the rational design of new therapeutics. Background: WS is a premature aging disease characterized by early onset of many age-related phenotypes. It is a monogenic disease caused by recessive mutations in the WRN gene. The first sign of WS is short stature, which is reported in approximately 95% of WS cases. Individuals with WS have an abnormally slow growth rate, and growth stops at puberty. As a result, affected individuals develop short stature. However, the mechanism through which WRN loss causes short stature as well as the genetic basis are not clearly elucidated. To determine the cause of short stature in WS, we used a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) model for identifying deferentially expressed genes in mesenchymal cells. Transcriptome analysis revealed that short stature homeobox (SHOX) was one of the downregulated targets in WS. SHOX is known to play an vital role in chondrogenesis and bone development. SHOX deficiency is a frequent cause of short stature. So, what is the role of SHOX in WS pathogenesis? To answer this question, we investigated the temporal expression of SHOX and WRN during chondrogenesis and revealed a high correlation between these 2 genes. Knockdown or knockout of WRN or SHOX in human stem cells impaired chondrocyte differentiation. Based on these observations, we hypothesized that the short stature in WS is caused by SHOX insufficiency as a consequence of WRN loss. Objectives: We plan to employ the human stem cell model for studying the mechanism of the WRN and SHOX in bone development. Furthermore, done development will be illustrated in transgenic animal model. Among the different vertebral models commonly used in the lab, only zebrafish and chick have both WRN/wrn and SHOX/shox orthologs. Therefore, the objectives of this project are to: 1) to elucidate mechanisms through which WRN loss leads to SHOX insufficiency and interruption of genetic pathways during chondrocyte differentiation 2) to study the skeletal development in a zebrafish model of WS (wrn−/−) and short stature (shox+/− and shox−/−) Significance: The current work under this grant suggests a novel mechanism through which SHOX insufficiency in WS is connected with bone development. The results from the proposed study will answer our question that whether the short stature in WS is related to SHOX dysregulation due to WRN loss. 目標： 該項目的目的是闡明在成人早衰綜合徵 Werner syndrome（WS）中通常觀察到的矮小身材的機制，為設計新療法提供合理基礎。 背景： WS是一種過早衰老疾病，其特徵在於許多與年齡有關的表型的早期發作。它是由WRN基因的隱性突變引起的單基因疾病。 WS的第一個徵兆是身材矮小，約95％的WS病例中有報導身材矮小。WS病人的生長速度異常緩慢，並且在青春期停止生長。結果，受影響的個體身材矮小。但是，WRN缺失導致身材矮小的機制以及其遺傳基礎尚不清楚。為了研究造成WS身材矮小的原因，我們使用了人誘導的多能幹細胞（iPSC）模型來鑑定間充質細胞中表達差異的基因。轉錄組分析表明，SHOX基因是WS中下調的基因之一。SHOX在軟骨形成和骨骼發育中起著至關重要的作用。 SHOX缺乏症是身材矮小的常見原因。那麼，SHOX在WS發病機理中的作用是什麼？為了回答這個問題，我們研究了軟骨形成過程中SHOX和WRN的時間表達，並揭示了這兩個基因之間的高度相關性。敲除或敲除人幹細胞中的WRN或SHOX會損害軟骨細胞分化。基於這些觀察，我們假設WS矮小是WRN丟失導致SHOX功能不全引起的。 項目目標： 我們計劃採用人類幹細胞模型來研究WRN和SHOX在骨骼發育中的機制。此外，我們也計劃使用轉基因動物模型來研究骨骼發育過程。在常用的實驗椎骨模型中，只有斑馬魚和小雞同時具有WRN/wrn和SHOX/shox的直系同源基因。因此，該項目的目標是： 1）闡明在軟骨細胞分化過程中WRN缺失導致SHOX功能不足和遺傳途徑中斷的機制 2）研究WS（wrn-/-）和矮身材（shox +/-和shox-/-）的斑馬魚骨骼發育 重要性： 本項目的前期工作提出了一種新穎的機制，該機制提出，WS中的SHOX功能不足與骨骼發育有關。研究結果將回答我們的問題：即WS中矮小的身材是否與WRN丟失引起的SHOX失調有關。

14109920.label: Realisation of objectives
14109920.value: In this project, we proposed two objectives. Objective 1 is to elucidate mechanisms through which WRN loss leads to SHOX insufficiency and interruption of genetic pathways during chondrocyte differentiation. To achieve this goal, we first examined whether WRN, a G-quadruplex (G4) resolvase, is associated with G4 abundance. We found that loss of WRN in different cell types consistently induced more G4 signals, as revealed by immunofluorescence (IF) staining. We thus examined whether the SHOX promoter regions contained any G4 motif. SHOX has two promoters (P1 & P2). In silico analysis by G4Hunter revealed 14 putative G4 sequences in the two promoters. Using slot-blot analysis, we confirmed the presence of six G4 sequences, namely P1-338, P1-117, P1+163, P2-740, P2-103, and P2+152. Using promoter luciferase activity assay, we found that only P2 had a strong promoter activity. Thus, we focused on the three G4 sequences in P2. We next confirmed the binding of WRN to the three G4 sites of P2 by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP). As anticipated, SHOX promoter (P2) could be activated by wild-type (WT) WRN, but not helicase-dead WRN (K577M). These data suggested that the helicase activity of WRN was required to promote SHOX transcription. Next, we investigated the effects of WRN or SHOX loss in chondrogenesis. We generated WRN-/-, SHOX-/- and hypomorphic SHOX+/- hESC lines. Directed differentiation of hESC to chondrocyte through mesodermal intermediate revealed poor differentiation results for all these mutant cells. This could be attributed to the failures to induce SHOX expression at Day 5 and SOX9 expression at Day 9 during the differentiation. As a result, COL2A expression (a chondrocyte marker) was reduced at Day 18. To demonstrate that the poor chondrogenesis result was due to the loss of WRN, we performed gene rescue experiment in which WRN-/- MSC was rescued by either WT or mutant WRN. Consistent with the observation that the WRN helicase was required for resolving the SHOX G4 promoter sequences, overexpression of WT but not helicase-dead WRN could rescue the chondrogenesis defect in WRN-/- cells. Interestingly, overexpression of SHOX in WRN-/- MSC could also rescue chondrogenesis, suggesting that SHOX is a downstream target regulated by WRN. To substantiate our findings on the determinant G4 sequences in the control of SHOX expression, we explored the possibility of mutating the suppressive G4 structures by gene editing approach. We designed guide RNAs (gRNAs) to target the two G4 sequences on SHOX P2. As a result of the G4 mutagenesis, SHOX expression was increased in WRN-/- MSC. The gene-edited MSC, despite losing WRN, showed improved chondrogenesis. These results suggested a potential gene editing approach to rescue the chondrogenic defect in Werner syndrome patients without the need to replace the mutated WRN gene. To dissect the molecular mechanism by which WRN regulates chondrogenesis, we performed ChIP-seq and RNA-seq when hESCs were induced to chondrocyte differentiation. Gene ontology analysis of the RNA-seq data revealed downregulations of chondrocyte differentiation, cartilage development, and helicase activity in WRN-deficient cells. As anticipated, SHOX and COL9A3 were among the genes that decreased significantly in WRN-deficient cells. We then combined the RNA-seq data with the ChIP-seq data, and identified 380 genes directly regulated by WRN in chondrocyte homeostasis (116 regulated and 264 downregulated). The downregulated genes were related to cartilage development, cell growth, and regulation of cell adhesion. The representative genes clustered in bone development, cell growth, and spinal cord development were subsequently validated by qRT-PCR in both hESC- and hMSC-derived chondrocytes. Among the genes, SHOX was significantly downregulated. Similar results were obtained from 40 dpf zebrafish with wrn KO. Together, these results suggested that SHOX is a downstream transcriptional target of WRN during bone development. WRN regulates SHOX by resolving the promoter G4 structures to facilitate transcription. We concluded that Objective 1 was 100% achieved (Research Output #1). Objective 2 is to study the skeletal development in a zebrafish model of WS (wrn-/-) and short stature (shox+/- and shox-/-). To achieve this goal, we obtained heterozygous wrn+/- and shox+/- mutant zebrafish from ZIRC. Crossing of heterozygous mutants could give rise to WT and homozygous KO fish. We observed that as early as 40 h post-fertilization (hpf), the body length of the wrn-/- embryos was significantly shortened. In addition, wrn-/- fish showed a decreased growth rate, as measured between 4-14 dpf (days post-fertilization). During this period of development, wrn-/- fish showed retarded skeletal development, as indicated by calcein staining of the vertebrate columns. Similar results were obtained when using wrn-specific morpholino to inhibit wrn expression in WT fish embryos. Next, we analyzed the expression profile of wrn and shox in zebrafish. By whole-mount in situ hybridization (WISH), wrn was expressed in the cartilage and vertebrae of WT but not wrn-/- fish by 7 dpf and 10 dpf. We observed the lack of notochord structures in wrn-/- fish at 14 dpf. In addition, cartilage and extracellular matrix could not be detected at this stage. By 40 dpf, wrn-/- fish showed underdevelopment of the notochord sheath, intercentral joint, and centrum. Concordant with the impaired skeletal development, fewer proliferative chondrocytes (as indicated by BrdU+ cells) were observed in wrn-/- fish. WISH analysis of hypertrophic chondrocyte markers (sox9a, col2a1a, col10a1a) showed decreased or undetectable expression in wrn-/- fish. The decrease of chondrocytes in the mutant fish was associated with increased apoptosis and DNA damage signals. Together, these analyses in the zebrafish model revealed an important role of wrn in the regulation of bone development. As our cellular model suggested that SHOX transcription was regulated by WRN with its helicase activity, we examined whether deficiency of shox in zebrafish displayed similar skeletal developmental defect as in wrn-/- fish. In shox+/- and shox-/- mutant fish (7 dpf), shox transcript was not detected in the vertebrae. As a result, chondrocyte markers sox9a, col10a1a and col2a1a were decreased. Similar to wrn-/-, shox mutant fish showed short body length and bone developmental defect. To test whether the short stature observed in wrn-/- fish could be rescued by shox overexpression, we injected shox mRNA into one-cell embryo. FISH analysis at 14 dpf and 21 dpf showed increased expression of the chondrocyte markers. Significantly, body length was increased in wrn-/- fish rescued with shox mRNA. In addition, more BrdU+ cells were detected, suggesting that shox re-expression restored chondrocyte proliferation and promoted chondrogenesis and bone development. As loss of WRN has been known to cause premature aging in humans, we asked whether cellular senescence is a key mechanism for controlling bone growth. Indeed, in hESC-derived chondrocytes, senescent cells were increased in the WRN knockdown group. Overexpression of SHOX could decrease the proportion of senescent cells. Concordant with this finding, cell cycle regulators, p53 and p16, were found decreased when WRN-deficient cells were rescued with SHOX expression. Similar results were observed in the zebrafish model. Together, these results indicate that loss of WRN led to senescence, which could be prevented by SHOX overexpression. We concluded that Objective 2 was 100% achieved (Research Output #2).

14109920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109920.value: In this project, we employed both human stem cell model (human pluripotent stem cell and human mesenchymal stem cell) and animal model (zebrafish) to study the role of WRN helicase in the regulation of bone development, the defect of which is linked to the short stature phenotype in Werner syndrome (WS) patients. First, we analysed the G-quadruplex (G4) sequences in the promoter regions of SHOX. As G4 is a preferred DNA substrate of WRN helicase, the loss of WRN stabilizes of the G4 structure and thus hindering transcription. We thus validated the critical promoter G4 sequences for the transcriptional regulation of SHOX. WRN was required to resolve the G4 structure for the active transcription of SHOX during chrondrocyte differentiation, and this process required the helicase activity of WRN. By the stem cell model, we found that complete loss of WRN or haploinsufficiency of SHOX resulted in impaired chondrogenesis. Such defect could be rescued by WRN or SHOX overexpression. Interestingly, we could rescue chondrogenesis in WRN-null cells by targeting the G4 structure. Gene editing of the promoter G4 sequences resulted in increased SHOX expression and thus promoting chondrocyte differentiation. This was a proof-of-principle that gene editing on the regulatory sequence (promoter G4) might be applied to treat short stature caused by WRN helicase deficiency such as those in WS patients (Research Output #1). Our second major finding was that zebrafish could be successfully used for modeling the skeletal developmental defect in WS (Research Output #2). Using this vertebrate animal model, we observed several phenotypes resembling the human disease. First, shorter body length was observed, in addition to the slow growth rate at the larval and juvenile stages. This was consistent with the short stature and skinny phenotypes in WS patients. Second, wrn mutant fish showed short lifespan - most of the mutant fish could not survive beyond 2 months (unpublished data), which was consistent with the short lifespan in WS patients. The zebrafish model allowed us to demonstrate the developmental defect in the bone, and from this WS model we identified key molecular events underlying the pathogenesis: shox downregulation, decreased chondrocyte proliferation and increased apoptosis, increased senescence and DNA damage, activation of p53 and upregulation of p16. Together, these findings illustrate the importance of WRN helicase in the regulation of chondrogenesis and bone development.

14109920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109920.value: Through this project, we discovered that WRN is an upstream regulator of SHOX, the key transcription factor for bone elongation. This explained the common short stature phenotype in WS patients. We further elucidated this mechanism by analyzing the G4 sequences in the SHOX promoter, and revealed the requirement of the helicase activity of WRN in unwinding the G4 structures. We demonstrated that through targeted mutagenesis of the G4 sequences in human stem cells, we could restore SHOX expression and promote chondrogenesis. We can further harness this approach to treat bone underdevelopment caused by DNA helicase deficiency and SHOX insufficiency. The future research can focus on applying the gene editing technique for in vivo therapy. I propose to use our wrn-/- zebrafish model to do gene editing, as this vertebrate animal showed bone developmental defect resembling human WS. Deletion or mutagenesis of the G4 sequence in the promoter may promote shox expression and thus rescue the bone developmental defect related to shox insufficiency. The development of gene editing tools (e.g. a CRISPR/Cas9 complex that can mutate the G4 sequence) is pivotal for this research. It could be further translated to human patients by targeting the developing chondrocyte precursors in pediatric patients.

14109920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109920.value: The causes of short stature in children are multifactorial. It could be caused by genetic reasons (familiar short stature), undernutrition and growth hormone deficiency. Bone elongation is a critical process for growth. During this process, chondrocytes (a type of soft tissue cells) in the growth disc are stimulated to proliferate and mature, and finally becoming bone cells. Bone growth can be impaired if one does not produce sufficient amount of SHOX protein to drive chondrocyte proliferation. Thus, in some syndromic diseases such as Werner syndrome, the lack of WRN protein is a cause of SHOX insufficiency. In this study, we investigated the molecular mechanism as how WRN controls SHOX expression. We demonstrated this by analyzing the molecular action of WRN in unwinding the DNA sequences that control SHOX expression. Failure in unwinding such regulatory sequences resulted in poor bone development, as demonstrated in human stem cell and zebrafish models. We thus developed a gene editing approach to change the DNA sequences that inhibit SHOX expression. This approach could be potentially translated to treat some short stature patients if their primary causes are SHOX insufficiency or DNA helicase deficiency.

14110820.value: 黃桿菌（Flavobacteriia）是擬桿菌門（Bacteroidetes）中一個重要的綱。它們生存于多種海洋和非海洋的生態位中，并富集于水生藻類和陸生植物根際附近的微環境中。黃桿菌的許多類群是水生和陸生動物的病原體，他們會使水產養殖行業蒙受巨大經濟損失並造成人類的嚴重疾病。迄今為止，已有近2000個公開的黃桿菌基因組可供研究，他們或來自於純培養的菌株，或由不可培養菌株的序列裝配而成。這些基因組的共同特徵是編碼了大量的碳水化合物活性酶和肽酶，這使得黃桿菌被普遍認爲對環境中多糖和多肽的降解起到重要的作用。黃桿菌科是黃桿菌綱中物種多樣性最爲豐富的一個類群，涵蓋了超過170個已知的屬。他們中大部分生存于海洋環境，只有小部分生存于非海洋環境，這種不均匀的分佈很大程度上是古代黃桿菌生態位遷移的結果。 微生物不同的進化軌跡產生了細菌豐富的基因組構成和多樣的生活方式。因此，研究發生在過去的進化事件是我們瞭解微生物多樣性的關鍵。對黃桿菌來説，其多樣的生存環境和生活方式衍生出多樣的基因組信息，這使得我們可以構建一個基於基因組的全面可靠的系統發育樹。在此基礎上，通過分析現存黃桿菌中基因存在和缺失的信息，我們可以重構其祖先的進化過程，揭示黃桿菌基因組大小和代謝方式在進化過程中的變化。 基於上述系統發育樹，另一個重要的分析是估算物種進化的時間，建立物種進化事件的時間軸。這種技術被稱為分子測年法，它建立在“分子錶”的基礎之上。“分子鐘”理論指出兩條同源序列的分化時間和其遺傳距離呈綫性關係。然而，考慮到不同物種之間的進化速率的不同，另一個被稱爲“寬鬆分子鐘”的模型則更為常用。一旦進化事件的時間通過上述方法被確定，那麽生物學中的進化事件諸如黃桿菌海洋到非海洋的生態位遷移，基因組大小和代謝方式的變化將可以被關聯到已知的古代地球化學和地球生物學事件上。 我們的分析初步表明，黃桿菌的祖先出現在16-19億年前，這是最古老的真核生物出現的時間。另外，我們認爲黃桿菌海洋到非海洋生境的三次遷移很可能是由三個不同的原因驅動的。第一個原因是中元古代海洋真核光合生物向低鹽度環境擴張，第二個原因是新元古代雪球地球事件導致全球範圍内的鹽濃度降低，第三個原因是寒武紀陸地動物的爆發。總之，本研究將通過多種分析揭示黃桿菌基於時間尺度的基因組多樣性和生活方式多樣性的形成過程。

14110820.label: Realisation of objectives
14110820.value: Objective 1: To establish a robust timeline of flavobacteria evolution This objective was achieved through advanced molecular dating techniques that significantly refined preliminary estimates. Leveraging plastid-encoded genes vertically inherited from Cyanobacteria, we calibrated relaxed molecular clocks (MCMCTree) using 8 eukaryotic fossil constraints, 2 cyanobacterial fossils, and 1 biomarker-based calibration. This approach dated the origin of flavobacteria to 2.15-1.98 billion years ago (Gya), postdating the Great Oxidation Event (2.5-2.3 Gya). The crown group of flavobacteria (Flavobacteriaceae + Weeksellaceae) diverged at 1.98 Gya, preceding the assembly of the Columbia supercontinent. Crucially, extensive sensitivity analyses validated timeline robustness: alternative cyanobacterial calibrations (e.g., Nostocales age: 1.2 vs. 2.0 Gya), eukaryotic topologies, and root age priors (3.8-5.0 Gya) yielded congruent estimates (95% HPD). This timeline superseded the proposal’s preliminary estimate (1.6-1.9 Gya) with higher precision and methodological rigor, resolving deep-node uncertainties in bacterial evolution. Objective 2: To correlate the multiple ocean-to-land transitions during flavobacteria The manuscript identified three Proterozoic marine-to-non-marine transitions, unequivocally linking them to tectonic dynamics of the Columbia supercontinent, replacing the proposal’s initial geobiological hypotheses. The first transition (1.98-1.70 Gya) coincided with Columbia’s assembly, where orogenies (e.g., Trans-Hudson Orogeny) created mountain foreland basins and lacustrine habitats. The second (1.72-1.40 Gya) and third (1.28-1.14 Gya) transitions aligned with Columbia’s fragmentation, during which continental rifting formed brackish basins (e.g., Cryogenian Nanhua Basin). Physiological evidence supported this mechanism: basal non-marine lineages (e.g., Sinomicrobium, Myroides) exhibited brackish salinity tolerance (4-8%), consistent with transitional habitats. Crucially, BiSSE model analysis of 17,244 16S rRNA sequences revealed asymmetric transition rates: marine-to-non-marine shifts (1.59 events/Gya) vastly outpaced reversals (0.52 events/Gya; P < 0.001), attributed to genome erosion in non-marine clades (elevated dR/dC ratios). This tectonic paradigm displaced the proposal’s preliminary links to Snowball Earth or Cambrian animal radiation, demonstrating that supercontinental cycles, not substrate availability, drove habitat transitions. Objective 3: To reconstruct the ancestral genome size expansion events in flavobacteria and link them to ancient Earth events The initial aim to correlate genome expansion events with ancient Earth phenomena encountered significant challenges. Ancestral genome reconstruction required advanced analytical tools not anticipated in the original proposal, necessitating extensive development and validation of new methods. Substantial effort was invested in establishing mitochondrial-based dating frameworks (Liao et al. 2022 MBE) and plastid-based divergence time estimation (Zhang et al., under review in MBE) to resolve deep-branching clades. Concurrently, we implemented genome-wide dR/dC ratio metrics (Zhang et al. 2024 ISME J; Luo 2025 ARMS) to infer historical changes in effective population size, a critical proxy for interpreting gene loss/retention patterns in ancient lineages. These methodological developments, while time-intensive, were essential for robust evolutionary inference of the core objective. During analysis, no strong signals of punctuated genome expansion emerged; instead, gradual size increases in Group V precluded correlation with discrete Earth events. However, this work revealed an unanticipated pattern: pronounced genome reduction in novel free-living lineages. Through co-assembly of 72 single-cell amplified genomes (SAGs) from oligotrophic marine environments, we identified eight streamlined flavobacteria genomes (2.41-3.58 Mbp), exhibiting 25-40% size reduction compared to host-associated relatives. These SAGs universally retained proteorhodopsin for light-driven energy conservation but showed systematic loss of energetically costly traits, including adhesin genes (sprB, remA) essential for gliding motility, de novo thiamine biosynthesis pathways (thiD/thiS/thiG), and 15-30% of CAZyme genes. Objective 4: To provide evidence for temperature-driven ecotype diversification of a flavobacteria lineage and associate this event with ancient Earth warming The objective has been achieved. The integration of mitochondrial/plastid dating (Liao et al. 2022; Zhang et al., under review) and dR/dC ratio analytics (Zhang et al. 2024; Luo 2025) extended timelines but ultimately strengthened the study’s evolutionary framework. These tools enabled precise dating of Polaribacter’s origin (~500 Mya) and critical ecotype transitions, including a shift to psychrophily during Carboniferous glaciation (~350 Mya) and reversion to psychrotrophy amid Mesozoic warming (~200-100 Mya). Phylogenomic and metagenomic analyses confirmed distinct cold-adapted (Group B: Antarctic P. irgensii and SAGs) and warm-adapted ecotypes, with ancestral state reconstruction revealing reversible transitions between psychrophilic and psychrotrophic states, challenging unidirectional adaptation models. Transcriptomic profiling under cold stress (0°C vs. 10°C) further delineated molecular strategies: psychrophiles exhibited osmolyte rewiring (betaine accumulation/histidine degradation) and suppressed energy metabolism (TCA cycle downregulation), while psychrotrophs upregulated spermidine synthesis to detoxify arginine.

14110820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110820.value: To overcome the critical limitation of scarce bacterial fossils for molecular dating, particularly for non-cyanobacterial lineages like flavobacteria, we pioneered novel plastid-based and mitochondria-based molecular clock strategies. These leverage abundant eukaryotic fossil calibrations by exploiting genes from ancient endosymbiotic events (plastid and mitochondrial) as evolutionary bridges, enabling robust transfer of age constraints to bacterial nodes. The plastid-based approach was rigorously developed through studies of Prochlorococcus cyanobacteria (Zhang et al. under review MBE), while the mitochondria-based method was validated using anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing Planctomycetes (Liao et al. 2022 MBE). Both strategies demonstrated superiority over traditional cyanobacterial fossil calibrations (Zhang et al. 2021. Proc. R. Soc. B), which lack maximum age constraints and yield high uncertainty. Applying these integrated methods to flavobacteria (Zhang and Luo, under review ISME Comm), we established their origin at 2.15-1.98 billion years ago (Gya), immediately postdating the Great Oxidation Event. Subsequent diversification involved three unidirectional marine-to-non-marine transitions during the Proterozoic (1.98-1.70 Gya, 1.72-1.40 Gya, and 1.28-1.14 Gya). These transitions temporally aligned with Columbia supercontinent assembly (2.1-1.8 Gya) and fragmentation (1.6-1.2 Gya), where tectonic processes like orogeny and rifting created brackish transitional zones (e.g., rift basins) that facilitated ecological shifts. Genomic analyses revealed transitions coincided with genome erosion and reduced effective population sizes (Ne) measured through elevated genome-wide dR/dC ratios, a validated proxy for selection efficiency loss in deep lineages (Zhang et al. 2024 ISME J; Luo 2025 ARMS). Non-marine lineages exhibited 1.8× higher species turnover but 40% lower net diversification than marine counterparts, reflecting habitat fragmentation challenges. Critically, transition rates showed extreme asymmetry (marine-to-non-marine: 1.59 events/Gya vs. reverse: 0.52 events/Gya), linked to irreversible genomic erosion in terrestrial clades that constrained evolutionary reversibility. These results establish planetary-scale tectonics as a fundamental driver of microbial biogeography, creating niches that parallel macroevolutionary patterns in eukaryotes. While glycan specialization (via CAZyme evolution) mediated local adaptation, flavobacteria’s global distribution reflects ancient tectonic reconfigurations that generated the niches themselves. This “top-down” geological control complements traditional “bottom-up” environmental drivers. In summary, this project delivered a robust evolutionary framework for flavobacteria by innovating cross-domain dating methods, elucidating tectonics as an important diversification driver, and redefining microbial biogeography through deep-time lenses. The expanded scope, developing mitochondria-based dating via anammox bacteria, plastid-based dating via Prochlorococcus, and dR/dC -Ne validation, was essential to overcome bacterial divergence dating limitations and achieve the proposal’s core objectives.

14110820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110820.value: The discovery that supercontinental cycles (Columbia assembly/fragmentation) drove flavobacteria's marine-to-land transitions presents a transformative paradigm. Future work should test its universality by applying integrated plastid/mitochondrial dating and dR/dC analytics to other widespread bacterial phyla (e.g., Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria). This will determine if tectonic reconfiguration is a general driver of microbial biogeography, particularly for clades with documented habitat transitions. Two additional manuscripts addressing Objective 2 & 3 are under preparation and will be submitted in 2026.

14110820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110820.value: We cracked the code on how ancient bacteria evolved by borrowing clues from plant and animal fossils. Since bacteria themselves don’t leave clear fossils behind, we invented a new way to connect their genetic history to well-dated fossils of complex life forms. This “molecular time machine” revealed the story of flavobacteria, tiny but mighty recyclers in oceans and soils that break down complex organic matter. Our discovery shows these microbes first emerged over 2 billion years ago, right after Earth’s atmosphere gained oxygen. They later made three great leaps from oceans to land, each timed with the cracking apart of ancient supercontinents. As continents split, they created new environments like coastal lagoons that helped bacteria transition ashore. Once on land, flavobacteria changed so much genetically that they could never return to ocean life. This work matters because it reveals how the slow dance of continents shaped even the smallest life forms. The same geological forces that built mountains and oceans steered the evolution of these vital carbon-recycling bacteria. By linking Earth’s deep history to modern microbial ecosystems, we better understand how our planet functions and how it might respond to future changes.

14110920.label: Project Objectives
14110920.value: Subjecting ADMSCs to hypoxic (5% O2) culturing condition has been reported to enhance motility and paracrine activity of stem cells, thereby may improve the therapeutic potential. Here, the secretome profile of ADMSCs under hypoxic culturing condition and normoxic culturing condition will be demonstrated by RT2 Profiler PCR array (Qiagen) and Luminex assay (Millipore) at first. We will then examine the possible ADMSCs-derived paracrine effector(s) that mainly contributes to the ulcer healing effects through immunodepletion assay in vitro. The impact on the cell survival, migration, apoptosis, and angiogenesis will be compared between normal conditioned medium and effectors-deleted conditioned medium. Since ErK/MAPK pathway is crucial for cell survival, migration, and angiogenesis, we will investigate whether the activation of ErK/MAPK cascade is involved in these effects. We will then have a large animal study to investigate the therapeutic efficacy of endoscopic submucosal injection of hypoxia-conditioned medium, compared with normoxia-conditioned medium or Omeprazole treatment (40mg/day; positive control), on promoting healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer in pigs. In order to assess the ulcer healing effects, re-epithelization, neovascularization, inflammatory infiltration, and oxidative stress will be evaluated between groups treated with conditioned medium and PBS. We will also determine the expression of genes related to wound healing after conditioned medium treatment through mRNA sequencing.

14110920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110920.value: 香港乃至全球人口的老齡化導致退行性疾病的增長。非甾體類抗炎藥（NSAIDs）越來越多地用於風濕性關節炎的治療，而阿司匹林通常用於動脈堵塞性疾病。然而，長期使用NSAIDs和阿司匹林的患者胃腸道（GI）並發症（如消化性潰瘍，出血和穿孔）的發生率高達30％。這些胃腸道事件的發生可以誘發大量不良反應和死亡。儘管目前使用質子泵抑製劑（PPI）的酸抑制療法是消化性潰瘍的標準策略，但近年來使用PPI的安全性和長期反應引起越來越多的關注。 脂肪來源的間充質乾細胞（ADMSC）被認為是具有多種分化能力，並可以釋放不同種類的細胞因子和營養因子的成年祖細胞。本團隊及 PI之前已經證明了MSC在外科手術修復後增強胃病理學和穿孔癒合的能力 (Br. J. Surg (2015); Biochim. Biophys. Acta Mol. basis Dis. (2018))，最近團隊在Science Translational Medicine（DOI：10.1126 / scitranslmed.aat7455）上發表了研究ADMSCs治療NSAID相關性胃潰瘍的論文。基於這些證據和初步結果，在這個項目中，PI和團隊成員將引入一種無細胞療法，該療法使用ADMSCs衍生的條件培養液治療NSAID相關性胃潰瘍。我們將在缺氧培養條件下從ADMSCs中收集條件培養液，因為已證明缺氧預處理可以增強細胞活力和旁分泌能力，從而可能提高治療潛力。團隊將首先探索低氧條件下細胞旁分泌的能力，然後通過體外細胞實驗研究負責促進胃粘膜上皮細胞的活力，遷移以及增強血管內皮細胞的毛細血管形成的主要旁分泌效應子，也將研究涉及該效應的ErK / MAPK途徑的信號轉導機制。在體外完成這些實驗後，我們將使用NSAID相關性胃潰瘍的豬模型進行大動物研究，與目前的標準奧美拉唑治療相比，研究內鏡下粘膜下注射缺氧條件培養液的療效。潰瘍癒合過程將通過內窺鏡進行監測，並通過組織學和轉錄組學評估潰瘍樣本。

14110920.label: Realisation of objectives
14110920.value: 1. We modulated NSAID-related gastric ulcers through the administration of Indomethacin and created artificial gastric ulcers via endoscopic submucosal surgery in a porcine model to evaluate the therapeutic effects of Hypo-MSC-CM. By utilizing post-translational modification sequencing of phosphorylated proteins, we identified potential mechanisms involved in tissues following the local injection of Hypo-CM. Furthermore, we validated the previously identified mechanisms in human gastric epithelial cells (GES-1) and human vascular endothelial cells to assess the effects of Hypo-MSC-CM on these specific human cell types. 2. Results showed the administration of Hypo-MSC-CM has significantly reduced the gastric ulcer index in the porcine model. The histological evaluation indicated that the effects involved multiple functions, including cell proliferation, angiogenesis, collagen formation, anti-apoptosis, and mucosal defense. Endoscopic surveillance demonstrated that the combined application of Hypo-MSC-CM and Omeprazole presents a synergistic effect that promotes gastric ulcer healing during the early stages of wound recovery. The post-translational modification of differentially phosphorylated proteins in the group treated with conditioned medium is closely associated with cell adhesion, angiogenesis, and the signaling pathway involving the cell actin cytoskeleton, with the MAPK signaling pathway identified as the most enriched. Furthermore, the functional assay of Hypo-MSC-CM on human cell lines demonstrates that treatment with the conditioned medium enhances cell migration, proliferation, anti-toxic responses, anti-apoptotic effects, and tube formation, thereby aligning with the results obtained from animal experiments and post-translational modification analysis. 3. In summary, our study encompassed a multitude of perspectives, including porcine animal experiments, protein analyses, and validation through human cell lines, to demonstrate the therapeutic effects of Hypo-CM on NSAID-related gastric ulcers. This research provides preclinical insights aimed at reducing ulcer formation and enhancing healing.

We will also determine the expression of genes related to wound healing after conditioned medium treatment through mRNA sequencing.

14110920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110920.value: 1. Hypo-CM promotes NSAID-related gastric ulcer healing in the porcine model The endoscopic injection of Hypo-CM facilitated NSAIDs related to gastric ulcer healing compared to the Control group. The ulcer index was significantly reduced in the Hypo-CM-treated group compared to the Control group. 2. Hypo-CM and Proton Pump Inhibitors have a co-effect on NSAID-related gastric ulcers in a porcine model. The combined administration of Hypo-CM and Omeprazole achieved the lowest ulcer index on day 3 compared to other groups. The combined administration of Norm-CM and Omeprazole resulted in a lower ulcer index than the Control group on day 14. The combined use of Hypo-CM with Omeprazole promotes gastric ulcer healing more effectively on day 3 than treatment with Omeprazole alone. 3. Hypo-CM enhanced Angiogenesis and Cell Proliferation Immunohistochemistry staining showed that capillary density was higher in Hypo-CM group and Hypo-CM + Omeprazole group than in control group. The ulcer base staining also demonstrated a more pronounced angiogenic effect of Hypo-CM than in other groups. The administration of Hypo-CM on NSAIDs related to gastric ulcers facilitates cell proliferation at the base of ulcerations more than the control group after 14 days. 4. Hypo-CM facilitates collagen formation and remodeling Hypo-CM enhanced the percentage of collagen fibers, especially collagen I, more than other groups, thereby affecting collagen formation for wound healing. 5. Hypo-CM’s anti-Apoptotic Effects and Mucosal Defense Activation The treatment with Hypo-CM alleviated cell apoptosis than Control group, exhibited better anti-apoptotic effects than Control group. Additionally, the administration of Hypo-CM elevated the expression level of iNOS in the related gastric ulcer porcine model, indicating the protective effects of Hypo-CM on gastric ulcers. 6. Detection of potential mechanisms involved in Hypo-CM treatments through proteomic analysis The phosphorylation proteomic analysis identified 10,695 proteins, 14,478 modified peptides, 13,035 comparable sites, and 2,895 comparable proteins between groups. GO enrichment analysis in molecular functions showed the most prominent GO terms (Top 10) include actin binding, calmodulin binding, kinase binding, cell adhesion molecule binding, chromatin binding, mRNA binding, basal transcription machinery, ATP-dependent activity, GTPase binding, and Protein domain-specific binding. The top common KEGG pathways included MAPK signaling pathways, adherens junction, Notch signaling pathway, and Wnt signaling pathway. 7. Validation of the potential effects and identified mechanisms from Hypo-CM in human cell lines-GES-1 and HUVECs In GES-1, Hypo-CM exhibited facilitated anti-apoptotic, enhanced proliferative, and facilitated migratory effects. In HUVECs, Hypo-CM presented enhanced angiogenesis and facilitated migration effects.

14110920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110920.value: Research on Hypo-CM has demonstrated promising outcomes in facilitating the healing of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers within a porcine model. Significant findings include improved angiogenesis, increased cell proliferation, enhanced collagen formation, and anti-apoptotic properties. These outcomes emphasize the need for further investigation in human clinical trials to evaluate safety and effectiveness. To further this research, it is crucial to conduct mechanistic studies that examine the molecular pathways revealed through proteomic analysis, particularly the MAPK and VEGF signaling pathways. Additionally, investigating combination therapies with current medications may enhance treatment outcomes. Longitudinal studies will also provide insights into the long-term impacts of Hypo-CM on gastric health and recurrence rates. Lastly, refining the formulation of Hypo-CM and preparing for regulatory approval are essential steps for its clinical use. Early engagement with regulatory agencies will enhance treatment options for patients suffering from NSAID-related gastric ulcers.

14110920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110920.value: This research investigates a treatment called Hypo-CM, which shows promise in healing stomach ulcers caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in pigs. The study found that injecting Hypo-CM significantly improved ulcer healing compared to standard treatments, especially when combined with Omeprazole, a common medication for stomach issues. Hypo-CM promotes the growth of new blood vessels, which are essential for healing, and increases collagen production, thereby helping to repair tissue. It also reduces cell death in ulcer areas, protecting the stomach lining from further damage. These findings suggest that Hypo-CM could be an effective new option for treating NSAID-related stomach problems in humans. Future research will involve conducting clinical trials to assess the safety and effectiveness of this treatment, exploring combination therapies, and collaborating with regulatory agencies to bring it to patients. Overall, this research could lead to better management of gastric ulcers.

14111320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111320.value: 延遲婚姻和父母身份越來越普遍，並已成為全球問題，導致高齡產婦的母親大量增加。許多高齡產婦都依靠輔助生殖技術（ART）來恢復生育能力。但是，許多人沒有意識到成功率也受年齡的影響。衰老導致卵母細胞質和量的下降，這轉化為胚胎髮育不良和可用於體外受精（IVF）的成熟卵母細胞。目前，尚無行之有效的方法來挽救或增加ART手術中可用的成熟卵母細胞的數量。 為了避免這種情況，我們最近開發了一種方法來增加成熟卵母細胞。這種新穎的非侵入性方法可以為IVF產生更多的成熟卵母細胞並提高質量。 為了允許人類IVF應用，我們已經確定了一種新型的人類經血來源細胞群體可以在動物模型中發揮功能。人類經血來源細胞群體具有乾細胞TNT形成特性。我們的初步研究表明人類經血來源細胞群體顯示出比小鼠模型更高的性能。與常規IVM相比，具有人類經血來源細胞群體的人GV卵母細胞的體外成熟, 使成熟卵母細胞產生增加了154％。我們假設人類經血來源細胞群體所帶來的改善不僅限於通過TNT的線粒體轉移，還包括諸如RNA和蛋白質之類的生物分子。因此，我們建議解剖人類經血來源細胞群體的基因組特徵，並通過單細胞RNA測序揭示對老年卵母細胞的關鍵調控。為了提高人類經血來源細胞群體處理的性能和一致性，我們將設計一種微流控設備，以最大程度地提高人類經血來源細胞群體和卵母細胞之間的TNT形成。我們希望與生殖和乾生物學，基因組學和生物醫學工程領域的專家團隊一起，對人類經血來源細胞群體及其在IVF中的應用提供紮實的科學理解。

14111720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111720.value: Cancer is still the top leading causes of death worldwide, but treatments are still unsatisfactory. As cancer cells are heterogeneous and adaptable that lead to drug resistance, therapies that target tumor microenvironment (TME) show promise. Cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) are the most prominent stromal component that notably enhances cancer development and progression. Nevertheless, origins of CAF are highly heterogeneous and still controversial which largely limits its therapeutic development. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a newly emerging approach to resolve cell-to-cell transcriptomic diversity in TME, which helps to better understanding pathogenic mechanisms and uncover novel therapeutic targets for cancer. Recently, we identified a Smad3-dependent TME (Smad3-TME) is essential for cancer progression, but its pathogenic mechanisms are still largely unclear. Interestingly, by scRNA-seq, we revealed that bone marrow derived macrophages (BMDM) are highly associated with cancer in a TGF-β1/Smad3-dependent manner. Surprisingly, our preliminary results discovered a novel tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) subpopulation co-expressing CAF antigen in both experimental and human TME, whose abundance was significantly associated with a poorer survival of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). By macrophage-linage tracing with 10X scRNA-seq, we found these alpha-SMA+CD68+ cells showed strong CAF signatures and largely contribute to angiogenesis during tumorigenesis; suggesting a novel phenomenon termed “TAM-to-CAF Transition” (TAM-CAF) for CAF formation. Mechanistically, unbiased bioinformatic analysis revealed a Smad3-centric gene network as the underlying mechanism for TAM-CAF. We further identified a hematopoietic transcription factor Runx1 as a specific regulator for TAM-CAF in the TGF-β1/Smad3 downstream signalling. More importantly, inhibition of Runx1 effectively blocked TAM-CAF and cancer progression in mice with syngeneic lung carcinoma. Based on these novel and exciting findings, we would hypothesis that TAM-CAF is a novel pathogenic mechanism of Smad3-TME, which may represent as a new and effective therapeutic target for NSCLC. Thus, we plan to examine this hypothesis by studying 3 specific aims: 1) identify the evidence and pathogenic role of TAM-CAF in human and experimental TME; 2) investigate the regulatory role of Smad3-TME in TAM-CAF at single-cell level; 3) finally, elucidate the working mechanism of TGF-β1/Smad3/Runx1 axis in TAM-CAF at transcriptional level. By completing this study, we expect to identify TAM-CAF as a common phenomenon and rich source of protumoral CAF in cancer, reveal regulatory roles of Smad3-TME in TAM activity and CAF formation, and uncover a novel pathogenic role of the TGF-β1/Smad3/Runx1 axis in NSCLC. Thus, outcomes from this study will be highly innovative and significant both scientifically and clinically. 癌症仍然是世界範圍內主要的死亡原因，但是治療仍然不能令人滿意。由於癌細胞適應性強導致耐藥性。近年，靶向腫瘤微環境（TME）的療法顯示出新希望。TME包含大量癌症相關成纖維細胞（CAF），他們可顯著增強癌症的發生和發展。然而，CAF的來源是高度異質的並且仍存在爭議，大大限制了其治療轉化的發展。單細胞RNA測序（scRNA-seq）是解決TME中細胞間轉錄組多樣性的一種新興方法，有助於更好地了解致病機制並發現新的癌症治療靶標。最近，我們確定了依賴Smad3的TME（Smad3-TME）對於癌症的進展至關重要，但其致病機制仍不清楚。有趣的是，通過scRNA-seq，我們發現以TGF-β1/ Smad3依賴的方式，骨髓衍生的巨噬細胞（BMDM）與癌症高度相關。出乎意料的是，我們初步發現了在實驗性和人的TME中勻存有共同表達CAF抗原的新型腫瘤相關巨噬細胞（TAM）亞群，其豐度與非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）較差的存活率顯著相關。通過10X scRNA-seq進行巨噬細胞-血統追踪，我們發現這些alpha-SMA + CD68 +細胞顯示出強大的CAF標記，並在腫瘤發生過程中極大地促進了血管生成。提出了一種新的現象，稱為“ TAM-CAF轉化”（TAM-CAF），用於CAF的形成。機理上，無偏見生物信息學分析表明，以Smad3為中心的基因網絡是TAM-CAF的潛在機制。我們進一步確定了造血轉錄因子Runx1作為TAM-β1/ Smad3下游信號傳導中TAM-CAF的特異性調節劑。更重要的是，Runx1的抑制可有效阻斷TAM-CAF和同基因肺癌小鼠的癌症進展。基於以上新穎而令人興奮的發現，我們假設TAM-CAF是Smad3-TME的一種新型致病機制，它可能是NSCLC新的有效治療靶點。因此，我們計劃通過研究3個具體目標來驗證以上假設：1）確定TAM-CAF在人和實驗性TME中的證據和致病作用； 2）在單細胞水平上研究Smad3-TME在TAM-CAF中的調控作用； 3）最後，從轉錄水平闡明了TAM-CAF中TGF-β1/ Smad3 / Runx1軸的工作機制。通過完成本項目，我們希望將TAM-CAF確定為癌症中常見的現象和癌變CAF的豐富來源，揭示Smad3-TME在TAM活性和CAF形成中的調節作用，並闡明TGF-β1/ Smad3 / Runx1軸在NSCLC中的致病機制。研究結果將會是高度創新，並於科學和臨床上均具有重要意義。

14112020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112020.value: Defecatory disorders affect 25% of the population, the incidence is rising and poses a major health care burden. Defecatory disorders are poorly diagnosed and treated. The lack of physiologically relevant and practical diagnostic tests for identifying the underlying mechanisms is hindering treatments for patients with defecatory disorders. Current diagnostic tests such as the balloon expulsion test, high-resolution anorectal manometry, defecography, and dynamic pelvic MRI are surrogates for the act of defecation and provide incomplete and often conflicting information. Not surprisingly results of these tests correlate poorly with symptoms and treatment outcomes. Our goal is to address the problem of mechanistic understanding of obstructed defecation by using an greatly improved version of the Fecobionics device (originally developed in Hong Kong), now with the capability of simultaneously measuring pressures, sensitivity, orientation, bending (anorectal angle) and shape and being battery-powered (wireless). These measures constitute the basis for computation of novel parameters such as friction force, preload-afterload diagrams and tension distribution. Fecobionics was successfully used in a recently completed GRF supported project that provided proof of concept technologically and clinically. Our central hypothesis is that the novel Fecobionics device that mimics natural defecation will provide new mechanistic insights in patients with obstructed defecation, i.e. we will be able to demonstrate specific signatures for the four defined subtypes of dyssynergia when compared to current technology. Our objectives are to address the significant gaps in knowledge and possibly to develop new classification based on the opportunities opening up with the new technology. Our expected outcome is to characterize the pressures, forces and topographic changes in the rectum and anal canal, during defecation in obstructed defecators, and to provide the ground work for later development of specific biofeedback therapy for obstructed defecators. The impact of our project is to use the safe, low cost, less invasive, low risk, radiation-free Fecobionics device to provide new knowledge and scientific basis for understanding defecation disorders. It will provide the knowledgebase for developing innovative biofeedback therapies at the point-of-care (home of patients) monitored remotely by healthcare personnel, thus improving diagnostic capabilities, treatment modalities and reduce costs of healthcare delivery. 排便失調症影響大約人口的25%，比率近數年有增加趨勢並對醫療系統構成負擔。排便失調症是較難診斷及進行治療，這是由於缺乏有關生理系統及臨床有實證的檢査，從而在治療上無法徹底根治問題。近代的檢測方式包括氣球排出測試，肛門直腸壓力測試，排便造影及功能性盆腔磁力共振均為排便失調症檢測的替代品，但是這些測試也不能反影患者的排便問題，有些檢測結果更和患者的情況有抵觸，令治療效果並不理想。 我們的目標是研發改良版本的Fecobionics，進行排便困難的各項研究。改良版本的Fecobionics除了在檢測壓力，敏感度，方向性和角度加以改善外，還有能無線傳輸數據。這些改善可令各項參數如摩擦力，前後負荷和張力得以獲取並規劃。Fecobionics亦在最近完成的優配研究金項目上證實其功能效果及臨床上的應用。 我們大膽假設Fecobionics能模擬人體的排便過程，並提供阻塞性排便的機制，從而令我們更有效了解阻塞性排便背後的原因及開發其新的分類。 我們期望硏究結果能將排便困難的患者於排便期間的肛門和直腸的壓力，以至其過度信息製作數據，並進行分析，用以開發新的生物回饋特別地用於排便困難的病人身上。我們的研究影響是希望利用安全，低成本，低入侵性及風險以至沒有幅射的Fecobionics來解釋科學上未能了解阻塞性排便的機理，從而開發更多創新的生物回饋治療，應用於家中進行治療，並由醫護人員緊密監察。這樣便能改善阻塞性排便的診斷，治療方式，以及減低醫療系統的成本。

14112020.label: Realisation of objectives
14112020.value: All objectives were realized and were not revised at any point during the grant period. The gross objective of the study was to use the high-tech simulated stool named Fecobionics that mimics normal defaecation to obtain integrative pathophysiological signatures of anorectal function, in particular manometric-geometric profiling during defecation for diagnosis and characterization of subtypes of patients suffering from obstructed defecation, i.e. dyssynergia. In brief about the realization of the objectives and specific aims, 1) Characteristics of subtypes of patients with obstructed defecation. We studied patients who presented with symptoms of obstructive defecation with difficulty in having their bowels open. All studies were carried out without any complications. A few patients could not expel the fecobionics but with data collected during the contractions, we were still able to get meaningful data during the assessment in comparison to ballon expulsion test where it just measures the time taken to expel the balloon. 2-30 contractions were required to expel the Fecobionics. Five distinct patterns were identified: Type 1 - Similar patterns to normal subjects (but patients reported feeling of obstruction and passing hard stool) Type 2 - Poor, ineffective push effort Type 3 - Sustained low amplitude contractions Type 4 - Multiple simultaneous contractions Type 5 - Paroxysmal anal contractions 2) In-depth analysis of data using preload -afterload characteristics and computation of defecation indicies, to compare different patterns seen in patients with obstructed defecation. Nice defecation indicies were developed to quantify pressure data. Novel analysis using a preload-afterload diagrams were used for rear-front anorectal pressure. In patients with obstructed defecation, several different patterns were identified during defecation. although clinical symptoms were similar, their patterns were different, highlighting need for different treatments. Some patients however had some overlapping features. In comparison to previous cohort's data with normal subjects and patients with constipation, preload-afterload characteristics and defecations indicies were significantly different. Defecation indicies multiplied by volume were most effective in distinguishing obstructive defecation from patients with slow transit constipation or normal subjects. Fecobionics data was compared with our current conventional assessments using high resolution anorectal manometry. Resting anal pressure, anal squeeze pressure, desire to defecate volume and expulsion duration time were all significantly different. This is likely due to difference in device design, bag behaviour during distension and placement of the probe.

14112020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112020.value: The following major findings are worth mentioning: 1) Subtypes of dyssnergia: Many patients with constipation on further questioning present with symptoms of obstructive defecation. Conventional assessment may identify patient with absent recto-ano inhibitory reflex or true anismus, but Feconbionics study further identified different defaectory patterns, which may allow more personalized treatment plans for each patients. 2) Stool consistency: By using different stiffness probes, we have proven that harder feces required more force and time to evacuate. The bending angle and pressure data also varied with consistency, suggesting that consistency of stool has an impact on anorectal dynamics and supports the physiological relevance of fecal consistency in defecation mechanics. Often there is discrepancy between patient's symptoms and conventional test results, especially in patients with obstructive defecation. By performing the assessment using different stiffness probes, may allow us offer more detailed assessment in more physiological setting, similar to when patients have their symptoms. 3) Repeatability of Fecobionics: Reviewing patients who had repeated their fecobionics study showed stable measurements and most parameters including the pressure, bending angle and expulsion duration showed acceptable repeatability even in symptomatic patients. 4) On performing the fecobionics assessment with Defaecating proctogram, we managed to confirm that Fecobionics can accurately give information on anorectal angle. It also showed that the Fecobionics anorectal angle showed stronger correlation with constipation score than the traditional Defecography measurements. Fecobionics may be able to replace defecating proctogram and avoid unnecessary radiation and embarrassment of performing the test in front of radiologist and radiographers.

14112020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112020.value: We are pleased with the results of the studies using Fecobionics to date. Fecobionics can be safely performed in a clinic setting as a one stop test and produce reliable data for the diagnosis of different types of defecatory disorders, especially for patients suffering from obstructive defecation. It would be useful to further study patients outside our unit to see if the results are achievable in other centres, as well as other types of patients such as caucasian patients through multicentre, international studies. This will also allow us to identify if there are any further subtypes of obstructive defecatory disorders to be considered for the classification. We also hope to integrate the use of Fecobionics into the treatment of patients with defecatory disorders. Many patients with defecatory disorders require Biofeedback therapy. If we can use Fecobionics to carry out Biofeedback therapy, it will allow patients to learn and practise defecation using simulated stool. It can also be used for simultaneous ongoing assessments to monitor progress, personalize treatments and fine tune their therapy.

14112020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112020.value: Many patients suffer from difficulty in defecation. Assessments of these patients with current technology is suboptimal requiring multiple tests. Many tests are carried out in a lying position, which is not how we defaecate normally. A novel device named Fecobionics can be used as a simulated stool to assess these patients in a more physiological manner as one stop test in clinic. In this study, we have identified different characteristics to further subtype patients having difficulty in having their bowels opened. We demonstrated that Fecobionics test give reliable, reproducible data. We also demonstrated that the consistency of simulated stool has an impact on defecation and test results. With more accurate assessment of these patients suffering from difficulty in having their bowels opened using Fecobionics, we hope that treatments can be personalized for more effective, efficient treatment. In the near future, we hope that Fecobionics can also be used for treatments, such as Biofeedback therapy.

14112920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112920.value: The origin of unevenly distributed biodiversity on Earth has been an intriguing topic in ecology and evolution. Biodiversity hotspots harbour richer evolutionary history than reflected by species number alone, and hence are important reservoirs of adaptive potential for species to survive future changes. While energy, habitat heterogeneity and historical biogeographic factors have been hypothesized as key drivers for speciation and diversity accumulation in biodiversity hotspots in general, empirical evidence for testing these ecological/evolutionary hypotheses remain sparse, particularly for freshwater invertebrates, creating a critical knowledge gap in our comprehensive understanding of how the remarkable species richness originated and maintained in freshwater ecosystems. With these ecosystems increasingly threatened by anthropogenic activities and climate change, answering these fundamental ecological/evolutionary questions has become more pressing than ever. The southwestern region of China represents one of the most spectacular biodiversity hotspots, the origin of which is poorly understood. The complex geological history, diverse habitats and generally mild climate provide a rare and pertinent setting to test how these attributes, in particular or in concert, render fauna in this region exceptionally diverse. This study aims to use shrimps in the family Atyidae, which are integral to freshwater ecosystems and attains the highest species richness in Southwest China among continental regions, as a model to test the hypotheses that various geological, climatic and biogeographic factors shaped the evolution of freshwater fauna in this region. Through extensive sampling, comprehensive morphological and molecular analyses, combined with cutting-edge phylogenetic, biogeographic and phylogeographic analyses, this study will for the first time elucidate the evolutionary history and population genetics structure of these ecologically important freshwater invertebrates in China, and, more importantly, shed light on the mechanisms that generate the freshwater biodiversity hotspot in Southwest China. Since several of the atyid species have been recognized as threatened by IUCN Red List assessment, the resulting atyid phylogeny and updated systematics, species distribution and abundance data from this comprehensive study will also contribute to the conservation management of the threatened atyid shrimps in this precious biodiversity hotspot. 生物多樣性在全球並非均勻分佈的原因，一直是進化學和生態學的熱門課題。其中生物多樣性熱點不僅物種數量多且積存豐富的進化歷史，具有更高的適應未來變化的潛能，因此分析生物多樣性熱點的成因有極高的科研及保育價值。當中能量、環境異質性和生物演化歷史被普遍認為是物種豐度的決定因素，但具體的生物多樣性積累機制除了少數研究外便鮮有分析，在淡水無脊椎動物中的研究更是酋為缺乏，形成了一個重大學術盲點。然而，因著氣候變化和城市發展等原因，全球的淡水生態系統正受到前所未有的威脅，使我們對淡水生物多樣性的探索和其源起的暸解變得日益迫切。中國西南地區是國際公認的生物多樣性熱點之一。該區域新生代晚期的造山運動以及古紅河與長江水系的重組都被認為是豐富多樣性的成因，但目前驗證這些假說的實驗證據尚少，以致無法全面地暸解該熱點的起源。本項目擬以匙指蝦作為模式生物驗證不同因素對此熱點之淡水生物進化的影響。通過大規模採樣，結合形態與分子資料，以及嶄新的譜系地理、系統發育、生物地理分析，本研究將厘清我國西南部匙指蝦物種多樣性、深入剖析其進化史、為該生物多樣性熱點尚未清晰的源起與演化機制提供新視角。另外，部分匙指蝦品種嚴重地受環境問題威脅，因此本研究所取得的分類系統修定、物種分佈與豐度等資料，也將在保育的實用範疇上作出貢獻。

14112920.label: Realisation of objectives
14112920.value: Objective 1: Elucidate the species richness and genetic diversity of atyid shrimps in the Southwest China biodiversity hotspot through extensive field surveys and species delineation based on morphological and genetic analyses. Significant progress was achieved in assessing the diversity of atyid shrimps. Field surveys in the southwestern China region, including poorly explored karst region, with approximately 60 species out of the documetned130 species collected in the present study, including 27 cave-dwelling species. Notably, we discovered at least five new species in southern China: Caridina danxiaensis sp. nov. from Danxia Mountain National Nature Reserve in Guangdong Province, Caridina ngankeeae sp. nov. from Hong Kong, and three unpublished species (Caridina chui sp. nov., C. bauhinia sp. nov., and C. aquilaria sp. nov.) also from Hong Kong. These species were delineated using integrative taxonomic approaches combining morphological traits (e.g., rostrum, pereiopods, and uropodal diaeresis) and genetic analyses (e.g., 16S rRNA sequence divergence). An updated checklist for Hong Kong and Guangdong Caridina shrimp species is under preparation and will be published for community use in the future. Objective 2: Reconstruct the phylogeny and infer historical biogeography of Southwest China atyid shrimps using cutting-edge sequencing and analytical methods. Phylogenetic relationship of shrimp in S China was further analyzed by sequencing mitochondrial genomes of 55 species and population genetic studies on over 400 individuals of Neocaridina palmata and Caridina cantonensis in Guangdong, as well as fine-scale population structure analyses of five Caridina species in Hong Kong using cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) and microsatellite markers were conducted. These efforts revealed distinct genetic structures and species-specific phylogeographic patterns, fulfilling the aim of delineating species diversity and genetic variation and the result will be elucidated below. A phylogenetic analysis was conducted using complete mitogenome sequence as molecular markers from 61 samples (55 species) to construct phylogenetic trees for Chinese cave and surface-dwelling atyid shrimps (Decapoda: Atyidae) employing both Maximum Likelihood (ML) and Bayesian Inference (BI) methods. The BI tree demonstrated higher nodal credibility compared to the ML tree. Based on the BI tree, divergence times were estimated, and ancestral habitats were reconstructed. The results indicate that Chinese cave atyid shrimps originated at least four times independently. Most cave lineages emerged between approximately 40 and 30 million years ago, coinciding with a period of climatic cooling and drying. During this time, tectonic activities in southwestern China, coupled with the Eocene-Oligocene climatic transition, likely led to the extinction or migration of adjacent surface populations. The majority of findings support the climate relict hypothesis for cave species formation, suggesting that these species are remnants of surface populations isolated by environmental changes. Additionally, a smaller subset of recently and rapidly evolving cave lineages suggests that the adaptive shift hypothesis may also play a role in cave speciation, indicating potential adaptation to subterranean environments. These insights contribute to understanding the evolutionary mechanisms driving cave biodiversity in China. At species level, phylogenetic analyses on Caridina and C. serrata species group in Hong Kong indicated polyphyly for both groups, prompting discussions on redefining the group at two levels (sensu stricto and sensu lato). Here, we examined the fine-scale population structure of five atyid species in Hong Kong using the mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunit I (COI) gene and four to six microsatellite markers. The results reveal species-specific contrasting phylogeographic patterns, ranging from wide-range genetic panmixia to population differentiation at an extremely small scale of ,1 km. This pronounced population structuring may be attributed to the freshwater obligates’ limited dispersal ability, high level of inbreeding and marked demographic fluctuations associated with climate changes since the Pleistocene. Notably we recovered historic introgressive hybridisation from the sharing of COI haplotypes between C. logemanni and C. cantonensis species and the more extensive inter-specific microsatellite admixture than inter-population admixture, such that both C. logemanni populations were of hybrid origin. The hybridization was likely promoted and/or driven by water channel modifications and aquarium trade harvesting/releasing. Objective 3: Test the hypotheses that (1) energy, (2) habitat heterogeneity, and (3) historical biogeographical factors shape large-scale biodiversity distribution by modelling species richness and genetic diversity against environmental data and results from biogeographic analyses. This objective was addressed through the integration of genetic diversity data and biogeographic analyses. Our findings linked the emergence of cave lineages to climatic shifts approximately 40 to 30 million years ago, supporting the role of historical biogeographical factors in shaping biodiversity distribution. Ancestral habitat reconstruction supported the Climatic Relict Hypothesis (CRH) as the primary mechanism for cave species formation, with a potential secondary role for the Adaptive Shifts Hypothesis (ASH). Population genetic studies in Hong Kong further revealed species-specific patterns ranging from panmixia to differentiation at scales of <1 km, suggesting habitat heterogeneity and limited dispersal as contributing factors. While direct modelling of species richness and genetic diversity against energy was not fully detailed in the current scope due to data constraints, the observed genetic barriers (e.g., between Shaoguan and Yingde) and fine-scale structuring provide partial evidence for habitat-driven diversity patterns. Partial progress was achieved, with future work needed to fully model environmental variables. Objective 4: Provide scientific resources for formulating conservation planning of freshwater shrimps by (1) revising their taxonomy, (2) preparing species identification guide, (3) building DNA barcode database, and (4) evaluating potential threats to atyid shrimps. Substantial resources were developed for conservation planning. Taxonomic revision was supported by identifying non-monophyletic groupings in Caridina and describing five new species with detailed morphological and genetic diagnoses, providing a molecular basis for future classification updates. A DNA barcode database was enriched with sequencing data from COI, NaK intron, and microsatellite markers for multiple species, including N. palmata, C. cantonensis, and C. logemanni. Complete mitogenome sequence were obtained from 55 species that will facilitate future population and DNA barcoding analyses. Quantitative conservation metrics prioritized protection for different populations, while population studies in Hong Kong highlighted threats such as low genetic diversity, hybridisation (e.g., between C. logemanni and C. cantonensis), and small population sizes, offering specific conservation recommendations. Future conservation efforts should aim at (1) minimising waterway modifications to prevent potential anthropogenic hybridisation, (2) fortifying conservation legislations to stop its harvesting, and (3) conducting continuous monitoring in case of stochastic events associated with small population size and linear habitat. While the preparation of a species identification guide was not explicitly completed within the reported scope, the genetic and taxonomic data generated serve as foundational resources for such efforts. This objective was largely met, contributing actionable scientific resources for conservation. In summary, the project achieved significant progress across all objectives, with comprehensive data on species diversity, phylogeny, biogeographic history, and conservation resources for atyid shrimps in Southwest China. Minor gaps, such as full environmental modelling and completion of an identification guide, do not detract from the overall success of the research outcomes.

14112920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112920.value: This study yielded significant insights into the evolutionary biology and genetic diversity of Atyidae in southern China, with implications for taxonomy and conservation. First, our analysis of cave and surface Atyidae species provided evidence on cave species formation mechanisms. Through mitochondrial genome sequencing of 55 species, we constructed phylogenetic trees and estimated divergence times, revealing that Chinese cave shrimp have multiple origins, with lineages emerging between 40 and 30 million years ago. This period aligns with climatic shifts causing surface population extinction or migration, supporting the Climatic Relict Hypothesis (CRH) as dominant, with a potential role for the Adaptive Shifts Hypothesis (ASH). Second, we discovered five new atyid species in southern China: Caridina danxiaensis sp. nov. from Danxia Mountain, Guangdong, distinguished by rostrum and genetic divergence (5.7% from C. clinata via 16S rRNA); Caridina ngankeeae sp. nov. from Hong Kong, related to the C. serrata group; and three unpublished species (tentatively named as C. chui sp. nov., C. bauhinia sp. nov., C. aquilaria sp. nov.) from Hong Kong, also within the polyphyletic C. serrata group, prompting redefined diagnoses at sensu stricto and sensu lato levels. Phylogenetic analyses of 40 species further confirmed taxonomic inconsistencies, with Caridina being non-monophyletic, enriching the mitochondrial genome database for future revisions. Finally, population genetic studies on selected species revealed distinct genetic structures. In Guangdong, sequencing of over 400 individuals of Neocaridina palmata and Caridina cantonensis identified genetic barriers between Shaoguan and Yingde, unique N. palmata lineages in Danxia, and strong C. cantonensis differentiation in Shenzhen. In Hong Kong, fine-scale analysis of five Caridina species using COI and microsatellite markers showed patterns from panmixia to differentiation at <1 km, attributed to limited dispersal and Pleistocene climate fluctuations. Studies of C. logemanni revealed low genetic diversity, strong differentiation at <1.5 km, and historic hybridisation with C. cantonensis, evident in shared COI haplotypes and microsatellite admixture. These findings enhance the Atyidae DNA barcode database and provide scientifically grounded recommendations for conserving spoon shrimp biodiversity in southern China’s freshwater ecosystems amidst environmental pressures.

14112920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112920.value: The findings of this study open several aspects for future research and application in evolutionary biology and conservation. First, the support for the Climatic Relict Hypothesis (CRH) and partial role of the Adaptive Shifts Hypothesis (ASH) in cave species formation warrants deeper investigation into ecological and genetic drivers. Future studies could employ comparative genomics and ecological niche modelling to clarify these mechanisms in China’s karst regions. Second, the discovery of five new Caridina species and the non-monophyletic nature of the genus highlight the need for comprehensive taxonomic revision of Atyidae. Expanding molecular datasets (both taxon and marker coverage) and integrating multi-locus sequencing could refine phylogenetic relationships, particularly for the polyphyletic C. serrata group, establishing a natural classification framework. Lastly, the distinct genetic structures, low intra-population genetic diversity, and hybridisation risks identified in Caridina species across southern China and Hong Kong suggest targeted conservation programs. Future efforts could focus on monitoring genetic diversity, mitigating anthropogenic hybridisation through waterway management, and fortifying legislation against harvesting. Extending similar analyses to other Atyidae species and collaborating with environmental agencies could translate these findings into actionable policies for freshwater ecosystem protection, addressing urgent biodiversity challenges in urbanized regions.

14112920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112920.value: This research explored the diversity and evolution of freshwater atyid shrimp in southern China. We discovered five new species in Guangdong and Hong Kong, adding to the known 130 species, and studied how some adapted to life in caves millions of years ago due to ancient climate changes. This helps explain how nature shapes life in unique environments. We also found that the current way of classifying these shrimps by appearance isn’t accurate, as genetic data revealed unexpected family ties, especially with new species showing distinct traits. Additionally, by examining shrimp populations in Guangdong and Hong Kong, we learned they have unique genetic patterns, sometimes differing over tiny distances due to barriers or past mixing between species, which can affect their dispersal and survival. Finally, our work offers guidance on protecting these shrimps by identifying at-risk groups, especially in urban areas like Hong Kong where they face threats from low diversity and habitat changes. This research helps us better understand nature’s history and provides a foundation to safeguard these important species and their freshwater homes for the future, ensuring their role in healthy ecosystems.

14113620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113620.value: 鼻咽癌是在包括香港在內的華南地區流行的頭頸癌。它與EB病毒感染和大量免疫細胞浸潤有高度關聯。大多數鼻咽癌患者在晚期被診斷出，並可能在初級治療後最終發展為局部復發和遠處轉移。在過去的十年中，我們和其他人進行了全基因組分析，以尋找鼻咽癌的可靶向突變。僅在總共少於6％的鼻咽癌病例中檢測到了常見的可靶向突變，包括PIK3CA，EGER，FGFR1 / 2/3/4和BRCA1 / BRCA2 / ATM。但發現鼻咽癌表現出明顯的“非典型” NF-κB途徑，歸因於體細胞遺傳變異和EB病毒編碼癌蛋白。有超過95％的鼻咽癌細胞檢測到核BCL3-p50 / 50複合物，這是“非典型”的NF-κB信號。這與在其他顯示p65（RelA）核易位的癌症中觀察到的“經典”NF-κB激活不同。由於BCL3並不參與正常發育，因此它代表了鼻咽癌的獨特治療靶標。我們的初步數據表明，敲除BCL3可以抑制生長和細胞集落形成。它還下調了癌基因和促腫瘤細胞因子的表達，這些因子可以調節免疫細胞的募集。為了利用BCL3靶向作為一種新型的鼻咽癌治療策略，我們已經開發了一種基於納米顆粒的方法將BCL3的siRNA遞送至鼻咽癌細胞。生物相容性樹狀聚合物(dendrimer)是納米尺寸的顆粒，可以自組裝以封裝siRNA，同時保護它們在體內遞送中不降解。我們的初步研究表明，siBCL3-dendriplex可有效抑制小鼠模型中鼻咽癌細胞的腫瘤生長。重要的是，與單獨順鉑治療相比，同時使用此siBCL3-納米顆粒和順鉑可產生更高的腫瘤抑製作用。此外，我們已經建立了人源化的小鼠模型，以研究在siBCL3-dentriplex處理下鼻咽癌腫瘤的免疫環境的調節。已經開發了多重熒光染色和微流體系統來分別檢查鼻咽癌組織和血清中細胞因子環境的免疫情況。在這項研究中，我們將（1）進行RNA測序，ChIP測序和功能測定，以全面闡明BCL3信號傳導調控的靶基因； （2）進行前臨床評估siBCL3-樹突狀複合體和順鉑單一和聯合使用的療效； （3）在人源化小鼠模型中研究siBCL3-dentriplex的治療效果及其對腫瘤免疫微環境的調節作用。

14113620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113620.value: In this study, we show that knockdown of BCL3 expression suppresses growth and colony formation of NPC cells as well as downregulates several oncogenes and pro-tumorigenic cytokines that modulate immune cell recruitment. We have characterized the genome-wide binding sites of BCL3 transcriptional complexes via chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) using antibodies against BCL3, p50 and p52. Notably, HILPDA, EBI3, NCF2 and BATF were identified to be downstream targets of BCL3 complex binding. As there are currently no available small molecule inhibitors for BCL3, we leveraged on the usage of dendrimers to efficiently deliver BCL3 siRNA into NPC cells. We demonstrate that siBCL3-dendriplexes were able to strongly inhibit tumour growth of NPC cells in vivo. Additionally, concurrent treatment of siBCL3-dendriplexes and gemicitabine, showed a synergistic tumour suppressive effect in a patient-derived xenograft mouse model. We have also evaluated the efficacy of the siBCL3/dendrimer treatment in humanized mice. An upregulation of CD8+ NK-T and Treg populations was observed, suggesting BCL3 inhibition may reshape the immunosuppressive environment in NPC tumors. Our findings highlight the translational potential of BCL3-targeting in the treatment of EBV-associated NPC. Most of these results were summarized in Research output 6: Chan M et al. Manuscript attached. The investigation of NF- kB pathway was also reported in a comprehensive genomic analysis of 70 NPCs, combining whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of microdissected tumor cells with EBV oncogene expression. Genomic aberrations along with EBV-encoded LMP1 expression underpin constitutive NF-κB activation in 90% of NPCs. [Research output 1: Bruce JP et al., Nature Communications, 2021] The continuous investigation in understanding the pathogenic roles of EBV and its encoded viral genes have provided direct and indirect druggable targets for effective NPC therapies [Research Output 2-5]. Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid models of EBV-positive and EBV-negative NPC cells were utilized in identifying new drug targets [Research output 2: Yi C et al., Journal of Cell Science, 2021]. One of these outputs unveils the interplay of EBV and stromal components in driving the invasive potential of NPC via unleashing the propulsion of invadopodia in overcoming matrix hurdles [Research output 3: Tang WC et al., Journal of Pathology, 2022]. It also led to innovative method to eradicate EBV-infected cancer cells through reactivation of EBV lytic cycle [Research output 4: Man Wu et al, Nat Comm, 2024] as well as through aptamer-targeting to EBV EBNA1 protein [Research output 5: Ji D et al, Angew Chem Int Ed, 2024].

14113620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113620.value: The results of this research project implicate a new treatment option for EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The project has provided insights into the biological mechanisms of BCL signaling in NPC, establishing a foundation for using BCL3 targeting as an effective treatment strategy. Various research groups will collaborate on cross-disciplinary studies to leverage the dendrimer technology for RNA delivery. Clinical efficacy assessments of siBCL3-dendriplexes can be conducted in partnership with pharmaceutical companies and clinical laboratories. To achieve these objectives, additional funding will be sought, including applications for the Innovation and Technology Fund, alongside ongoing evaluations of the nanoparticles' safety and efficacy, and proactive engagement with biotechnology firms for clinical trials. Long term, the goal is to translate these findings into tangible benefits for NPC patients, potentially transforming clinical practices and improving patient quality of life. This treatment could serve as an adjunct therapy alongside traditional chemoradiation, particularly for recurrent or metastatic cases, thereby reducing toxicity and socio-economic burdens.

14113620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113620.value: The research project “BCL3 as a unique therapeutic target for EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma” focuses on a specific type of cancer that significantly impacts certain regions, particularly Southern China and Southeast Asia. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is often diagnosed late, leading to limited treatment options and systemic side effects from current therapies. This project is significant because it identifies BCL3 as a novel target for therapy. Nanoparticles has been utilized to deliver small RNA molecules to inhibit BCL3, aiming to enhance treatment effectiveness while minimizing side effects. The results indicate that reducing BCL3 levels significantly suppresses tumor growth in mice models, and combining this approach with existing chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine) shows synergistic suppressive effect on tumorigenesis. Additionally, the study suggests that targeting BCL3 may modulate the tumor microenvironment with recruitment of tumor-suppressive immune cells. Ultimately, this research could lead to innovative, less toxic therapies for NPC patients, significantly improving their quality of life and treatment outcomes. The findings will also provide vital information to support the planning of clinical trials to test these BCL3 regimes in humans.
