14118620.label: Realisation of objectives
14118620.value: Aim 1. Develop a tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold. To attain successful tendon repair in cases of large-to-massive tendon defects, we developed a tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold with a focus on addressing two pivotal factors: sustained mechanical support and enhanced regenerative bioactivity. The UV-crosslinkable polyurethane elastomer (QHM) core portion was designed to provide long-term mechanical support and durability while the tECM-GelMA hydrogel shell section of the scaffold for enhancing pro-tenogenic bioactivity. Aim 1.1. Examine the tenogenic effect of a tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold in vitro. In vitro evaluations were performed to investigate the effectiveness of tECM bioactivity as well as it pro-tenogenic effect in tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold. hASCs were encapsulated in the gel layers of hybrid scaffold or the scaffold without tECM supplementation, and a set of experiments were performed to characterize cell viability, proliferation, and tenogenic differentiation. Live/Dead assay showed that from day 7 to day 14, both the scaffold without tECM supplementation and tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group exhibited high cell viability (more than 90%). A significantly higher amount of double stranded DNA (dsDNA) in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group was detected than that in the scaffold without tECM group after 14 days of culture. After 10 and 14 days of culture, significantly increased expression of Scleraxis (SCX), Mohawk (MKX), Tenascin C (TNC), and Type I collagen (COL1A1) was observed in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold relative to the scaffold without tECM groups. Consistently, immunofluorescence staining results showed enhanced expression of all tenogenesis associated markers (COL1, TNC, and Tenomodulin (TNMD)) in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group relative to the scaffold without tECM group. Taken together, these findings suggest that tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold exhibited excellent cytocompatibility and markedly promoted hASC proliferation and tenogenic differentiation in vitro compared to scaffold without tECM group. Aim 1.2. Fabricate and characterize tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold ex vivo. The bonding integrity of a hybrid construct is essential for its successful in vivo application. Delamination between the core and shell structure during the early stages of tendon healing would impede our intention to simultaneously provide bioactive factors and mechanical support. The interfacial bonding strength was first assessed by analyzing the force-displacement profile and failure mode analysis. Our results showed that bonded tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold yielded significantly higher peeling force and peak load compared to nonbonded scaffold. In bonded tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold, failure occurred within the GelMA hydrogel bulk rather than at the GelMA hydrogel-QHM interface as shown by the residual layer of GelMA hydrogel remaining on the QHM elastomer. In contrast, failure of nonbonded tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold occurred at the GelMA hydrogel-QHM interface rather than within the GelMA hydrogel bulk, with the hydrogel being easily peeled off from the QHM elastomer surface. Additionally, in vivo results showed that degradation of GelMA was observed at 7- and 18-days post-surgery, and the remaining hydrogel was attached to the surface of the QHM elastomer, indicating that robust bonding could be maintained in vivo. Overall, our results demonstrated that benzophenone-mediated photocrosslinking treatment produce bonded tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold with strong interfacial attachment strength between its hydrogel and elastomer layers. The tensile and suture retention tests were performed to confirm that benzophenone-mediated photocrosslinking during tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold fabrication does not negatively impact scaffold mechanical properties. Representative force-displacement profiles showed that both the QHM elastomer and tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold exhibited an initial steep increase in load-displacement, followed by sustained plastic behavior before failure. In contrast, the commercially available acellular human dermal matrix (ADM as a clinical scaffold control) displayed a gradual increase in load-displacement, culminating in failure after sustained deformation. The stress at yield, strain at yield, tensile modulus, ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and stiffness of the QHM elastomer and tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold were similar. In suture retention test, when a 25 N force was applied, neither the QHM elastomer nor tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold exhibited any significant suture migration (less than 0.1 mm) or scaffold deformation, whereas ADM displayed substantial elongation and approximately 1.72 mm suture migration, which were around 30-fold higher. Overall, these results indicate that tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold possesses human SSPT-like tensile properties and superior suture retention properties compared to a leading commercial scaffold ADM, which are essential for rotator cuff repair stability. Aim 2. Evaluate the healing efficacy of the hybrid scaffold for tendon repair in a rabbit rotator cuff injury model. The tendon healing efficacious of tECM-supplemented hydrogel-elastomer hybrid scaffold was further evaluated in a rabbit massive rotator cuff tendon defect model. A 1-cm tendon defect gap was created on rabbit SSPT and implanted with scaffold without tECM supplemented or tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold to completely bridge the tendon defect, and the contralateral shoulder was used as an intact control group. At 1-month post-surgery, there were no obvious symptoms of severe inflammation in either scaffold without tECM supplemented or tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold groups based on the gross appearance of tendons. Histologically, H&E staining images revealed that both defect groups exhibited complete bridging of the 1-cm tendon defect and increased cellularity relative to the intact control group. However, notable differences in the quality of the healing tissue were observed among the groups. Semiquantitative cellular orientation analysis showed that cells were more aligned in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group than in scaffold without tECM supplemented group at both 1- and 3-months post-surgery. Also, picrosirius red staining and polarized light microscopy were employed to assess the birefringent nature of anisotropic ECM molecules, as well as the size of deposited collagen fibers, with the color hue of the images representing the relative collagen fiber thickness (in order of thinnest to thickest: green, yellow, orange, and red). A typical feature of tendon scar tissue is less birefringence [52]. The results showed that the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group had more pronounced birefringence than the scaffold without tECM supplemented group. Additionally, tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group had more orange-to-red (thicker) fibers, while scaffold without tECM supplemented group had more yellow (thinner) fibers. Overall, the histological analysis demonstrated that tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold exhibited enhanced collagen content and better cellular and ECM organization at both 1- and 3-months post-surgery compared to the control group, which lacked tECM supplementation. Ultrastructural analysis using SEM showed that fibers in the intact control and the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold were aligned along the longitudinal direction of the tendons, while fibers were discretely oriented in the scaffold without tECM supplemented group. Interestingly, the collagen fibers in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold and scaffold without tECM supplemented groups were comparable in diameter and smaller than those in the intact control group. The nanoindentation test revealed that the intact control group exhibited a higher elastic modulus of collagen fibers than that in the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold and scaffold without tECM supplemented groups, while no significant difference was observed between tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold and scaffold without tECM supplemented groups. The bulk tensile test results showed that the tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group achieved a comparable ultimate load and stiffness with the intact control group. Furthermore, although scaffold without tECM supplemented group showed a comparable ultimate load with the intact control and tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group, its stiffness was significantly lower than that of tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold group.

14118620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14118620.value: A significant clinical challenge in large-to-massive rotator cuff tendon injuries is the need for sustaining high mechanical demands despite limited tissue regeneration, which often results in clinical repair failure with high retear rates and long-term functional deficiencies. To address this, an innovative tendon substitute, tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold, is engineered, which uses (i) tendon extracellular matrix (tECM)'s rich biocomplexity for tendon-specific regeneration and (ii) a mechanically robust, slow degradation polyurethane elastomer to mimic native tendon's physical attributes for sustaining long-term shoulder movement. Comprehensive assessments revealed outstanding performance of tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold, characterized by robust core-shell interfacial bonding, human rotator cuff tendon-like mechanical properties, excellent suture retention, biocompatibility, and tendon differentiation of human adipose-derived stem cells. Importantly, tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold, when used as an interpositional tendon substitute, demonstrated successful integration with regenerative tissue, exhibiting remarkable efficacy in repairing large-to-massive tendon injuries in two animal models. Noteworthy outcomes include durable repair and sustained functionality with no observed breakage/rupture, accelerated recovery of rat gait performance, and >1 cm rabbit tendon regeneration with native tendon-like biomechanical attributes. The regenerated tissues showed tendon-like, wavy, aligned matrix structure, which starkly contrasts with the typical disorganized scar tissue observed after tendon injury, and was strongly correlated with tissue stiffness. Our simple yet versatile approach offers a dual-pronged, broadly applicable strategy that overcomes the limitations of poor regeneration and stringent biomechanical requirements, particularly essential for substantial defects in tendon and other load-bearing tissues. This work has been published in Bioactive Materials entitled Engineering an extracellular matrix-functionalized, load-bearing tendon substitute for effective repair of large-to-massive tendon defects and other journals. This work also has been presented at 2023 Annual meeting of Orthopaedic Research Society and 2023 Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine International Society-Asian Pacific conference. Our post-graduate student Huang Shuting and undergraduate students Chan Ka Lun Galen and Seto Chun Him Thomas have participated in this project.

14118620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118620.value: Although our data indicated that the implantation of tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold, led to early and fast tendon fiber alignment and enhance tendon stiffness, the repaired tendons in tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold groups were still at the early healing phase compared to the intact tendon group at 3 months post-surgery. However, we did not observe any breakage in our scaffolds, suggesting that the elastomer core with its excellent biomechanical strength and suture retention value, could sufficiently and permanently support the dynamic loading strain during the tendon healing phase and prevent early tendon retear or scaffold failure after surgery. Additionally, we lack long-term evaluation of mechanical performance of tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold in vivo which is a crucial feature for design of nondegradable materials. Our prior study estimated demonstrated the slow-to-no degradation of QHM elastomer, estimated to be on the order of several years which is ideal for tendon repair, as tendon repairs slowly over months and years. In this context, slow degradation can maintain repair integrity and minimize clinical complications. Moreover, as our strategy focuses on specifically addressing the repair of large tendon defects, it is important to evaluate the healing efficacy of our scaffold in a clinically relevant large animal model.

14118620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118620.value: Tendons are strong fiber bands that are essential for transmitting force between muscles and bones. However, serious tendon injuries like large rotator cuff tears pose major challenges for shoulder surgeons because tendons have limited natural healing abilities. Even with treatment, these injuries often don't heal well, leading to a high failure rate. This happens because of the formation of scar tissue that weakens the repaired tendon. To tackle this problem, a novel tendon scaffold (tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold) has been developed. It contains the natural composition of tendons for targeted regeneration and uses durable polyurethane materials to mimic the strength of natural tendons. Our experiments have shown that tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold works really well—it is safe for the body, has strength similar to human tendons, and promotes stem cell differentiate to tenocyte. In animal studies, tECM-supplemented hybrid scaffold effectively integrates with regenerated tissue, promotes tendon-like structure formation (wavy and aligned matrix structure) and restores similar natural tendons strength. This straightforward and adaptable approach offers a practical solution to enhance tendon healing, addressing the challenges posed by poor nature tendon healing abilities and demanding biomechanical requirements in critical tendon and load-bearing tissue injuries.

14119020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119020.value: Young-onset diabetes is highly heterogeneous with respect to aetiology and pathophysiology which in turns determine clinical phenotypes and mode of presentation. Efforts to delineate the different forms of diabetes in this young group are in progress with the goal to personalise treatment regimen tailored to specific disease subtypes and improve prognosis. From the Hong Kong Diabetes Register, among people with diabetes diagnosed below 40 years, 10% have type 1 diabetes and another 8% habour anti-islet autoantibodies deemed to have latent autoimmune diabetes. Monogenic diabetes contributes to 3-5% of young-onset diabetes in Chinese although inadequacies with existing methods to detect mutations pose limitations in diagnosis. Of the remaining, two thirds are overweight or obese with features of the metabolic syndrome in keeping with close relationships between obesity, insulin resistance and diabetes. Up to one third, however, are uncharacteristically lean and maintain higher blood glucose than their overweight or obese counterparts. The metabolic architecture underlying non-autoimmune diabetes among normal weight individuals is not well defined. It is postulated that they have greater loss of beta-cell function compared with those who are obese, but may also have reduced insulin sensitivity despite their normal body built. In Caucasian cohorts, a cluster of people with a similar phenotypic profile was recently identified. In this proposal, we first seek to characterise the metabolic alterations in normal weight type 2 diabetes as compared with obese type 2 diabetes and weight-matched healthy controls. Twenty-four people aged <40 years with type 2 diabetes and body mass index (BMI) <23 kg/m2, 24 people aged <40 years with type 2 diabetes and BMI >=27.5 kg/m2, and 24 age- and weight-matched (12 normal weight, 12 obese) euglycaemic control will be recruited for hyperglycaemic clamp to evaluate insulin sensitivity and beta-cell function, in addition to body fat assessment. Next, we will examine glycaemic effectiveness of different classes of anti-hyperglycaemic drugs according to BMI and other relevant clinical variables by interrogating the database of a large prospective cohort of over 300,000 Hong Kong Chinese with type 2 diabetes. This research will serve to enrich our understanding of the pathophysiology underlying this unique but prevalent cluster of people with normal weight type 2 diabetes in Asia. Results from the detailed mechanistic study and corresponding findings from analysis of real-world data will contribute to the knowledge base for the selection of anti-hyperglycaemic drug treatment most appropriate for this group. 早發性糖尿病患者與年老糖尿患者的病因有所不同。早發性糖尿病以40歲前確診為分水嶺，當中有10％患有1型糖尿病，8％患有latent autoimmune diabetes in adult, 而單基因型糖尿病佔3-5％。其餘六成是超重或肥胖者，具有代謝綜合症的特徵，然而，多達三成的病人體重正常。體重正常糖尿病的代謝結構尚不明確。我們推測，體重正常糖尿病人的胰島β細胞功能比較肥胖者缺乏。儘管他們的體重正常，其胰島素作用仍然不足。 本研究主要目的是要評估正常體重或超重的糖尿病患者或非糖尿病患者的胰島素作用和胰島β細胞功能, 以及其他代謝變化。本研究將招募 24 名早發性 (40歲前確診) 體重正常 (body mass index [BMI] <23 kg/m2) 2型糖尿病患者, 24 名早發性肥胖 (BMI ≥27.5 kg/m2) 2型糖尿病患者, 以及24 名非糖尿病健康志願者 。參加者會給邀請進行”高血糖鉗夾”測試, 評估胰島素作用和胰島β細胞功能。此外, 我們將會分析約30萬香港2型糖尿病患者的臨床數據, 了解 BMI 和其他臨床及生物指標對降血糖藥反應的影響。這項研究將有助於加深對體重正常2型糖尿病患者病理的了解, 推動個人化糖尿病的治療。

14119020.label: Realisation of objectives
14119020.value: Asia has a high burden of young-onset diabetes and one fifth of the population with type 2 diabetes are diagnosed below the age of 40 years. Accumulation of glycaemic burden from a young age increases the lifetime risks of developing complications from diabetes. Emergence of new anti-hyperglycaemic drug classes in the past decade has resulted in improved blood glucose control in older but not young people with diabetes. Existing treatment guidelines have not fully considered the heterogeneity in disease aetiology and pathophysiology in the selection of anti-hyperglycaemic drugs especially in young-onset diabetes. From a disease register in Hong Kong, people with young-onset diabetes are phenotypically diverse and up to one third are lean but have no evidence of autoimmunity or monogenic diabetes. Limited evidence suggests that normal weight individuals are predominantly insulin insufficient, however the extent to which insulin resistance also contribute to diabetes development and progression in this group is not known. The present proposal is motivated by the unfilled gap in evidence related to pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes with lean phenotype common in Asia. In addition, no previous studies have systematically addressed glucose-lowering effects of the different classes of anti-hyperglycaemic drugs in lean as compared with overweight or obese people with young-onset diabetes in Asia or elsewhere. To address Objective 1 and 2, we aimed to recruit 24 normal-weight (body mass index [BMI]) 18.5-22.9 kg/m2) and 24 obese (BMI ≥27.5 kg/m2) Chinese with young-onset type 2 diabetes, and 12 healthy normal weight and 12 healthy obese Chinese without diabetes to undergo hyperglycaemic clamp for assessment of insulin sensitivity and beta-cell function. Participants with young-onset diabetes were selected based on fulfilling the following criteria: 1) age at diagnosis under 40 years, 2) diabetes duration <10 years, 3) HbA1c value <7.5% within the past 3 months to minimize the impact of glucose toxicity on beta-cell function, 4) not currently using long-term insulin therapy to avoid the influence of exogenous insulin on insulin measurements, 5) absence of anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibodies to exclude immune-mediated diabetes, and 6) no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in monogenic diabetes genes to exclude monogenic diabetes. This objective was fully achieved. Between 26 February 2021 and 14 August 2023, 20 normal-weight, 24 obese individuals with young-onset type 2 diabetes, and 24 healthy normal-weight or obese Chinese were recruited. The mean age and BMI were 40 years and 21.5 kg/m2 in normal-weight group with diabetes, 38.5 years and 33.0 kg/m2 in obese group with diabetes, 39 years and 21.6 kg/m2 in normal-weight healthy controls, and 31.5 years and 32.4 kg/m2 in obese healthy controls. Participants had screening assessment at the Diabetes and Endocrine Research Centre, the Prince of Wales Hospital, including collection of information on demographics, past medical history and current medications. We measured body weight, body height, waist circumference and vital signs (blood pressure, pulse rate). We measured body fat percentage using Tanita Body Composition Analyser (Model TBF-410). Blood samples after an overnight fast were collected for plasma glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, kidney and liver function, and complete blood count. In individuals with type 2 diabetes, additional blood samples were collected for measurement of anti-GAD antibodies and genetic screening for monogenic diabetes. In healthy control, a 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test was performed to establish euglycaemia. Participants underwent hyperglycaemic clamps at the Phase 1 Clinical Trial Centre at the Prince of Wales Hospital, as per protocol. No major adverse events were recorded after the procedures in any of the participants. The hyperglycaemic clamp was a 2-hour procedure during which the participant was infused 20% dextrose intravenously through one arm and have blood collected for glucose, C-peptide and insulin at frequent interval from the other arm. At the start of the clamp, an initial bolus of 20% dextrose was administered over a period of 15 minutes aiming to rapidly elevate the blood glucose level to 12 mmol/L. Subsequently a hyperglycaemia state at 12 mmol/L was maintained for 120 minutes through adjustment of the dextrose infusion rate, guided by real-time measurements of blood glucose obtained at 5-minute interval. The adjustment of dextrose infusion rates according to real-time glucose values was conducted using the algorithm developed and validated in a previous study. These measurements were obtained using a bedside glucose analyser, the YSA 2300 from Yellow Springs Instruments. Serial blood samples for insulin and C-peptide values were obtained at baseline, followed by every two minutes within the initial 10 minutes, and at 10-minute intervals until the end of the 120-hour clamp procedure. Measurements of insulin and C-peptide were performed in the Diabetes Research Laboratory, Li Ka Shing Institute of Health Sciences at the Prince of Wales Hospital. We calculated acute (0-10 minutes) and steady-state (100-120 minutes) beta-cell responses during the hyperglycaemic clamp. Acute insulin response and acute C-peptide response were calculated as the mean values of insulin and C-peptide at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 minutes after intravenous dextrose administration subtracting the basal values of insulin and C-peptide. Steady-state insulin response and C-peptide response were determined as the mean values of insulin and C-peptide at 100, 110 and 120 minutes during the clamp. Insulin sensitivity index was defined as the mean glucose infusion rate divided by the mean insulin values during steady state (100-120 minutes). Disposition index, reflecting the hyperbolic relationship between acute insulin response and insulin sensitivity index, was computed as their product. We also calculated quantitative insulin sensitivity check index (QUICKI) and HOMA2-%S as additional indices of insulin sensitivity. Objective 3 involved analysis of clinical data of people with type 2 diabetes within the electronic medical record repository of Hong Kong Hospital Authority. We included data of people newly initiated metformin (n=15,433), sulphonylurea (n=15,190), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) (n=4,947), thiazolidinedione (n=4,107) and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) (n=1,883). We used linear regression to examine the association between clinical features and 1-year glycaemic response to glucose-lowering drugs. This objective was fully realised.

14119020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119020.value: Objective 1 - Normal-weight individuals with diabetes had lower beta-cell responses including acute insulin response, steady-stage insulin and steady-state C-peptide, and higher insulin sensitivity index, QUICKI and HOMA2-%S than obese individuals with diabetes. No difference was detected in disposition index between the two groups. - Inverse correlations were observed between log-transformed beta-cell responses and insulin sensitivity index in both normal-weight and obese individuals with diabetes. The slopes of beta-cell responses relative to insulin sensitivity index did not differ between the two groups. Adjusted for insulin sensitivity index, normal-weight individuals with diabetes had similar beta-cell responses compared to obese individuals with diabetes. Objective 2 - Normal-weight individuals with diabetes had lower beta-cell responses including acute insulin response, acute C-peptide response, steady-stage insulin and steady-state C-peptide than healthy normal-weight counterparts. No difference was detected in insulin sensitivity index, QUICKI and HOMA2-%S between the two groups. Normal-weight individuals with diabetes had lower disposition index than healthy normal-weight counterparts. - Obese individuals with diabetes had lower acute insulin and acute C-peptide response but similar steady-state insulin and steady-state C-peptide response to healthy obese counterparts. Insulin sensitivity index did not differ between the two groups but QUICKI and HOM2-%S were lower in obese individuals with diabetes. Obese individuals with diabetes had lower disposition index than healthy obese counterparts. - Adjusted for insulin sensitivity, acute insulin and C-peptide response were lower in individuals with diabetes than healthy controls irrespective of BMI. However, impairment in adjusted steady-state insulin and steady-state C-peptide response in individuals with diabetes compared with healthy controls were detected only in normal-weight but not obese group. Objective 3 - The initiation of metformin, sulphonylureas, DPP-4i, thiazolidinediones and SGLT-2i was associated with mean reduction of HbA1c ranging from 0.7% to 1.3% at one year, but individual glycaemic response varied according to sex, age at drug initiation, diabetes duration, general adiposity and triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol-ratio (surrogate of insulin resistance). - Men had a greater glycaemic response to sulphonylureas but smaller response to metformin and thiazolidinediones. Older age predicted greater response to most glucose-lowering drug classes except SGLT-2i, whereas increasing diabetes duration was associated with poorer response to most drug classes except DPP-4i. - Obese individuals had greater glycaemic response to thiazolidinediones and SGLT-2i but poorer response to sulphonylureas than normal-weight individuals. Individuals with higher triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol-ratio had greater response to thiazolidinediones but smaller response to sulphonylureas and DPP-4i. Notably, neither adiposity nor triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio predicted response to metformin.

14119020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119020.value: From the hyperglycaemic clamp study, we confirmed that normal-weight individuals with young-onset type 2 diabetes had decreased beta-cell responses and greater insulin sensitivity than obese individuals with type 2 diabetes. Furthermore, when compared with healthy individuals, the impairment in beta-cell responses was more pronounced in the normal-weight group. These findings underscored the importance of beta-cell detects in young-onset type 2 diabetes presenting in normal-weight people and are in concordance with our retrospective analyses of people with type 2 diabetes showing that low adiposity and low triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio indicating low insulin resistance were associated with better glyacemic response to insulin secretagogues including sulphonylureas and DPP-4i. Further research will include 1) exploration of HbA1c trajectories following initiation of insulin secretagogues stratified by BMI to determine if there are differences in achieving glycaemic durability with these drugs between normal-weight and overweight/obese individuals, 2) genetic analysis to identify novel risk variants for type 2 diabetes presenting in normal-weight versus overweight/obese individuals and to correlate these variants with age at diagnosis, 3) extension of our ongoing pragmatic clinical trial on the effect of multicomponent care model in young-onset diabetes updating our treatment algorithm for normal-weight participants specifying preferential and early initiation of insulin secretagogues.

14119020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119020.value: Up to one in five Chinese with type 2 diabetes presented below the age of 40 years. Although obesity is a key driver in the development of type 2 diabetes, around one third of Chinese with young-onset type 2 diabetes have normal body weight. In this research, using complicated assessment procedures called the “hyperglycaemic clamp”, we showed that normal-weight individuals with young-onset type 2 diabetes had more severe impairment in pancreatic beta-cell function while they had less insulin resistance compared with obese counterparts with type 2 diabetes. When compared with healthy individuals, the defect in beta-cell function was more pronounced in the normal-weight group with type 2 diabetes. Using a large dataset of Chinese with type 2 diabetes, we found that normal-weight and low insulin resistance were associated with better response to drugs that stimulate insulin secretion including sulphonylureas and dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitors. Our results have implication on how clinicians should consider body weight when selecting therapy especially in young individuals.

14119120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119120.value: Ras suppressor 1（RSU1）在胚胎發育過程中調控血管生成的機制研究

14119120.label: Project Objectives
14119120.value: Objective #1: To characterize the effects of RSU1 deletion during angiogenesis in mouse and zebrafish models. We will delineate the defect of blood vessels in RSU1 KO mouse embryos, and examine whether alternation of Rsu1 will affect angiogenesis in zebrafish embryos. Objective #2: To investigate the role of RSU1 in HUVECs as an in vitro model of angiogenesis. We will study whether overexpression of RSU1 promotes, while disruption of RSU1 inhibits tube formation of HUVEC cells in the co-culture system. Objective #3: To study mechanisms as to how RSU1 regulates filamentous actin assembly. RSU1 is a focal adhesion protein, and we have identified a few potential RSU1 interaction partners, including Myosin phosphatase Rho-interacting protein (MPRIP), which is implicated in F-actin assembly. We will study the interaction of Rsu1 with MPRIP on F-actin assembly. The effects of rus1 on filamentous actin assembly will be examined using the Tg(fli1a:LIFEACT-mCherry) zebrafish embryos, in which the F-actin is labeled by mCherry. The ECM protein of endothelial cells, such as vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-Cadherin) and ZO-1, will also be studied upon knockdown of zebrafish Rsu1.

14119120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119120.value: 血管生成對於胚胎發育、器官發生并且同許多新生兒缺陷密切相關。胚胎發育過程中血管生成異常還可能引起多種新生兒疾病，如肺和支氣管發育異常和早產兒視網膜病變等。此外，很多疾病如糖尿病，視網膜病變和癌症也可以引起成人的異常血管生成。血管生成很大程度上依賴於受Integrin蛋白信號調節的細胞粘附和細胞遷移來完成。最近的研究表明， Ras suppressor1（Rsu1）參與Integrin蛋白信號傳導。這一蛋白通過與PINCH-1結合而定位於細胞粘著斑， 而PINCH-1是一種含有Lim蛋白功能域，並與Integrin相互作用的激酶。為了闡明Rsu1在胚胎髮育過程中的功能，我們使用CRISPR / Cas9製備了RSU1敲除小鼠。在小鼠中敲除RSU1引發妊娠中期胚胎死亡。進一步研究發現敲除RSU1會導致E16.5〜E19.5胚胎大面積皮下出血和血管網絡發育缺陷。這些結果暗示血管生成異常是導致胚胎在後期死亡的原因。組織化學分析進一步證實Rsu1基因敲除後小鼠胚胎血管形成發生嚴重異常。利用 CRISPR / Cas9在HUVEC細胞中敲除或使用siRNA敲低Rsu1顯著抑制HUVEC細胞成管反應。我們同時利用免疫沉澱質譜法（IP-MS）鑑定出調節細胞骨架所需的Myosin Phosphatase Rho-interacting protein是RSU1互作蛋白。基於以上的研究結果，我們假定Rsu1通過調節內皮細胞中肌動蛋白組裝從而調控血管生成。我們將通過以下方法驗證我們的假說：1）利用小鼠和斑馬魚模型研究RSU1敲除後血管生成過程中發育異常的特徵； 2）利用HUVEC細胞作為血管形成體外研究模型明晰RSU1在的血管生成過程的作用；3）研究RSU1如何調控內皮細胞中絲狀肌動蛋白組裝的分子機制。成功完成這些研究目標，將幫助我們闡明Rsu1調節血管生成的分子機制。雖然現在Rsu1生物學功能尚不清晰，許多生物信息學研究表明Rsu1與許多人類疾病如神經膠質瘤和乳腺癌相關。闡明這些機制將有助於預防血管生成異常相關疾病， 並為制定新的治療方案提供理論基礎。

14119120.label: Realisation of objectives
14119120.value: Rsu1 is required for angiogenesis and heart development No viable Rsu1-/- mice were born, although the mating yielded viable Rsu1+/+ and Rsu1+/- offspring at approximately Mendelian ratios, indicating Rsu1 KO causes lethality during embryogenesis. Massive hemorrhages in RSU1-null embryos occurred at late gestation. Moreover, we assessed the embryonic vasculature in RSU1-/- embryos with iodine staining and micro-CT imaging. Compared to wild-type littermate controls, by E16.5, an elaborated vascular network in the liver, head, and other parts of wild-type embryos they were largely absent in Rsu1-null embryos. The interventricular septum (IVS) separating the two ventricles was complete in wild-type (WT) hearts on E16.5 in WT hearts. In contrast, an apparent opening between the two ventricles was still apparent in Rsu1-KO hearts. Moreover, compared to the WT heart, the myocardial wall appears thinner in Rsu1 KO hearts. Defective vascular remodeling in the yolk sac of RSU1KO embryos We examined the vascular structure of the yolk sac at these stages between E12.5 and E16.5. By E16.5, vitelline vessels were no longer observed in Rsu1-/- yolk sac, and Rsu1-/- embryos underwent developmental arrest, suggesting a failure in developing blood vessels in Rsu1-null embryos by E16.5. Rsu1-/- yolk sac showed striking abnormalities in the vascular organization at both E12.5 and E16.5 compared to the wild-type yolk sac. At E12.5, the Rsu1-/- yolk sac displayed numerous small-caliber vessels sprouting from the large-diameter vessels. The vessel density, vessel junction, and total vessel length were all significantly increased in Rsu1-/- yolk sac, indicating that the yolk sac vasculature is less organized or defined. By E16.5, while the wild-type yolk sac showed further remodeled and pruned vasculature network with large avascular intervessel spaces, Rsu1-/- yolk sac was in striking contrast, exhibiting even higher vessel density, significantly increased vessel junction and total vessel length as well as many small intervessel spaces. Moreover, at both E12.5 and E16.5, while vessels in the wild-type yolk sac appeared smooth, vessels in the Rsu1-/- yolk sac showed increased numbers of lateral filopodia. Collectively, these data suggest that angiogenic remodeling leading to the formation of a hierarchy of large- and small-caliber vessels is impaired in Rsu1-null embryos from the mid- to late gestation. We investigated the level of phosphorylated VEGFR2 in Rsu1 KO yolk sac and found activation phosphorylation of VEGFR2 was significantly increased in response to the loss of RSU1, suggesting an upregulation of the VEGF signaling pathway. Defective vascularization of the placental labyrinth in RSU1-depleted embryos During placenta development, a key process is the formation of the branching morphogenesis of the labyrinth, which creates a path for fetal vasculature to grow. We examined the labyrinth zone histologically at E12.5 and E16.5, respectively. At E12.5, Rsu1-null placenta had the labyrinth of branching morphogenesis, many of which however, were devoid of red blood cells (RBC), suggesting that the invasion of embryonic blood vessels is impaired. In addition, the villous branches in labyrinth of Rsu1-/- placenta were relatively larger compared to those in Rsu1+/+ placenta. By E16.5, the labyrinth in Rsu1+/+ placenta was exquisitely branched and vascularized, while in sharp contrast, the Rsu1-/- labyrinth remained cell-dense, and the morphogenesis of the labyrinth was diminished. PECAM1 staining confirmed that the vascularization was even more significantly decreased in Rsu1-/- labyrinth at E16.5, suggesting that the growth of fetal blood vessels in the labyrinth villi is severely impaired. Regarding the weight of the placenta, the weight of the Rsu1-/- placenta was significantly decreased compared to that of Rsu1+/+ or Rsu1+/- embryos by E16.5, aligning with the underdevelopment of Rsu1-/- embryos at this stage. Collectively, vascularization is impaired in Rsu1-/- placentas at mid-gestation. By late gestation, the branching and vascularization of Rsu1-/- placentas are drastically reduced. These observations align with the late embryonic lethality phenotype of Rsu1-null embryos and provide further evidence that Rsu1 deficiency is associated with vascularization defects. Loss of Rsu1 attenuates the expression of Notch target genes in mouse embryos. The phenotype of defective vascular remodeling in the Rsu1-/- yolk sac and impaired vascularization in the placenta of Rsu1-/- embryos resembled the phenotype of Dll4- or Notch1-KO or Hey1 and Hey2 double-KO mice. Hand2 was reported as a critical mediator of Notch signaling during cardiac morphogenesis. RT-PCR results indicated that the expression of Hes1 and Hey1, two well-known Notch target genes, were significantly reduced in Rsu1-/- embryos compared with WT embryos, while the expression of Dll4 ligand and Notch1 receptor remained unchanged. Moreover, Hand2 and Numbl, two Notch signaling modulators, were increased. Thus, the loss of Rsu1 leads to dysregulation of the Notch signaling pathway, which is involved in cardiovascular development. Transcriptome analysis revealed aberrant up-regulation of multiple pathways involved in cardiovascular development in Rsu1-null yolk sac Transcriptome analysis of the Rsu1-null yolk sac using RNA-Seq revealed significant gene expression changes. Gene ontology and enrichment analyses showed that upregulated gene were linked to development, cell-ECM adhesion, migration, and proliferation, while downregulated genes were associated with amino acid and fatty acid metabolism. Notably, numbl, a known inhibitor of Notch signaling pathway, was significantly increased in the Rsu1-null yolk sac, as confirmed by RT-qPCR. Since Notch signaling is essential for vascular development, and the vascular defects in Rsu1-null embryos resembled those seen in Notch pathway mutants (e.g., Dll4, Notch1, Hey1/2 knockouts), further analysis was conducted. The expression of Notch target genes Hes1 and Hey1 was significantly decreased in Rsul-null yolk sacs, indicating downregulation of Notch signaling. Conversely, Hand2, a Notch-related gene involved in heart development, was upregulated in Rsu1-null yolk sac. We examined the mRNA level of the receptor Notch1 and the ligand Dll4, which was not statistically altered in Rsu1-null yolk sac. Disruption of rsu1 displays a dominant-negative effect in zebrafish, leading to pericardial edema. We examined the spatial expression pattern of rsu1 using whole mount in situ hybridization and found it is expressed in the heart field and tube, lens, and pharyngeal arches. We generated an rsu1 mutant line using the CRISPR/Cas9 system. This mutant line carries a 21-base pair (bp) insertion, resulting in seven additional amino acids at position 81. Protein structure modeling suggests this insertion creates a loop at the end of the second LRR. Indeed, the homogenous rsu1+21 bp mutation is lethal. Moreover, 44% of heterozygous rsu1+21 bp embryos displayed failure of heart tube looping and pericardial edema, indicating that the rsu1+21 bp mutation has a dominant-negative effect on cardiac development. Overexpression of rsu1+21 bp in zebrafish embryos caused pericardial edema and failure of heart tube looping. We also performed loss-of-function assays using rsul-specific morpholinos, which led to similar phenotypes, including pericardial edema and heart tube looping defects. Furthermore, we found that rsu1 knockdown leads to a reduction in the expression levels of nkx2.5, cmlc2, Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that WT Rsu1-FLAG interacts with both WT Rsu1-MYC and mutant Rsu1+21 bp-MYC, suggesting that Rsul may function as a dimer or oligomer. The interaction between mutant and WT proteins may interfere with normal Rsu1 function, explaining the cardiac phenotype seen in heterozygotes. Collectively, our data strongly suggest that Rsu1 plays a critical role in heart development in zebrafish and mouse models.

14119120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119120.value: We have investigated the function of RSU1 in embryonic development using RSU1 knockout (KO) mice and rsu1-disrupted zebrafish lines. The main fundings are listed below. 1. RSU1 is indispensable for the development of mouse embryos Homozygous (Rsu1-/-) mice were lethal during embryogenesis. From E16.5, all Rsu1-/- embryos exhibited severe hemorrhaging and developmental delays. The heart interventricular septum (IVS) failed to fully form by E16.5 in mutants, and the myocardial wall was thinner than those in WT embryos. These observations suggest that RSU1 is crucial for both vascular and cardiac development. Zebrafish rsu1 is expressed in the developing heart. Disruption of rsu1 displays a dominant-negative effect in zebrafish, leading to pericardial edema. Loss-of-function assays were also performed using rsu1-specific MOs. Consistent with the findings for rsu1 mutants, a similar phenotype, i.e., defective heart tube looping and pericardial edema, was observed in rsu1 morphants. 2. Knockout of RSU1 caused defective vascularization and impaired interventricular septum formation. Further analysis of the yolk sac vasculature showed impairments in vascular remodeling. Vitelline vessels were regressed by E16.5 in KO embryos. Disorganized vascular networks, with increased vessel density and abnormal sprouting in Rsu1-/- yolk sacs. These abnormalities indicate compromised angiogenesis and vascular hierarchy formation. The upregulation of VEGF signaling in the absence of RSU1, revealed by VEGFR2 phosphorylation. 3. Defective vascularization of the placental labyrinth in RSU1-depleted embryos. Loss of Rsu1 impaired vascularization in Rsu1-/- placentas, especially by E16.5. Although branching morphogenesis was present at E12.5, many branches lacked red blood cells, and vascularization was significantly reduced. By E16.5, labyrinth development was severely diminished, and placental weight was reduced, corresponding to the overall developmental delay of Rsu1-/- embryos. 4. Transcriptome analysis revealed aberrant up-regulation of multiple pathways involved in cardiovascular development in Rsu1-null yolk sac. Transcriptomic analysis of the yolk sac highlighted the pathways involved in cell adhesion, migration, and ECM interactions upregulated, and metabolic pathways downregulated. Notably, Notch signaling, critical for vascular development, was disrupted. The changes in Notch signaling target genes were confirmed by RT-PCR. Overall our study demonstrates that RSU1 is essential for embryonic vascular development, placental vascularization, and cardiac septum formation. Its absence results in late gestation vascular failure and embryonic lethality, underpinned by dysregulation of key developmental pathways including VEGF and Notch signaling. We published six papers and delivered oral presentations at two international conferences. Additionally, I supervised and trained five Ph.D. students during the funding period.

14119120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119120.value: Ras suppressor 1 (Rsu1) has been implicated in integrin signaling and is localized at focal adhesions. We found that Rsu1 is expressed in the developing heart in the zebrafish model. Knockdown or disruption of rsu1 in zebrafish interfered with heart development, leading to pericardial edema. Consistent with these observations, the expression levels of nkx2.5, cmlc2, and gata4, which are genes critical for cardiac development, were reduced upon the knockdown of rsu1. Our further study will focus on (1) characterizing the effects of the loss-of-function effects of Rsu1 during cardiac development, (2) elucidating the cellular mechanisms by which Rsu1 influences the differentiation of cardiomyocyte progenitors, (3) identifying the signaling pathways and specific cell types affected by rsu1 disruption in the developing heart through single-nucleus RNA sequencing and single-nucleus ATAC-seq. We aim to investigate the underlying mechanism whereby Rsu1 regulates heart development.

14119120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119120.value: The formation of the functional cardiovascular system is essential for embryonic development. During angiogenesis, on the one hand, new vessels are formed via angiogenic sprouting from existing vessels, and on the other hand, the vessels undergo further remodeling processes, including localized proliferation, regression, pruning, and migration to establish a mature vascular network. Ras suppressor 1 (RSU1) is an evolutionarily conserved consensus component of the integrin adhesome. We studied the function of Rsu1 in the developing mouse embryo using Rsu1 knockout mice. Rsu1-null embryos die between E12.5 and E18.5, which shows high penetrance of cardiovascular defects, including defective vascularization and impaired interventricular septum formation at late gestation. We found evident defects in angiogenic remodeling in Rsu-1 null yolk sacs from mid- to late gestation. Histological analyses of the placenta of Rsu1-null embryos showed severely impaired vascularization at late gestation. Transcriptomics at late gestation identified aberrant up-regulation of multiple pathways involved in cardiovascular development. We also generated the rsu1-disrupted zebrafish line, showing malformation of blood vessels and heart defects. Our study demonstrated that the loss of Rsu1 impacts the homeostatic regulation of cardiovascular development, resulting in embryonic lethality at a late stage of mouse embryogenesis.

14119320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119320.value: Childhood asthma and allergies have become the common chronic disorders affecting almost one third of children in the developed world. The increase has been linked closely to the process of economic improvement, urbanization and westernization. Within the Chinese population, we have confirmed that the prevalence rates of childhood asthma, allergic sensitization are highest in Hong Kong schoolchildren when compared with other cities in Mainland China. Using the standardized and validated methodology of the International Study of Asthma and Allergies (ISAAC) phase III results showed that the prevalence rates in urban and rural Beijing were relatively low at 8% and 5%. Furthermore, we have documented rapid increase in the prevalence of asthma in Guangzhou over the past 15 years. With such rapid economic improvement across China, it is conceivable that the prevalence of the asthma and allergies will continue to increase. With the biggest population in the world (almost 1.4 billion, 26% of which are children), a one percent increase in China’s childhood asthma prevalence results in 3 million more cases of pediatric asthma. The associated economic burden is daunting. One of the strongest asthma protective factor is the early exposure to a rural environment. Recent studies from European and American farms suggested that exposure to microbes and consumption of farm milk may be associated with modulation of the early immune system leading to protection against asthma and allergies. Such protection has been linked to the communication between barrier epithelial cells and dendritic cells through induction of ubiquitin-modifying enzyme A20. As the farming environment in China is very different from European farms, we have conducted pilot study of children from rural Conghua area (Southern China). The results revealed a very low prevalence of asthma (2%). The exact reasons and the possible underlying immunological changes associated with such protection are not clear. Our preliminary data suggested that household exposure to poultry was a major factor explaining the rural protection against asthma. To identify and successfully address the modifiable risk factors for asthma are of paramount importance if China is to avoid the asthma prevalence rates observed in Australia or England. We hypothesize that the rural exposure may result in changes in the children’s immune responses in relation to their production of cytokines and increase gene expression which are different from urban children. Such immune changes in the rural children are associated with protection against the development of asthma and allergies.

14119320.label: Realisation of objectives
14119320.value: We achieved our two objectives in determining the immune profiles of children from urban and rural China and the difference in gene expression related to the immune pathways concerning poultry exposure in the environment. The pandemic restriction has caused some delay in our progress as we could not collect biological samples from the rural areas, and traveling between mainland China and Hong Kong was severely restricted for a prolonged period. However, we were able to carry out our bench experiments and animal model experiments when we were not able to travel to the research sites. The findings were reported in detail in the following high-impact publications: one in the top journal in the field of allergy, Allergy (published in October 2022; Impact factor 14.71) and two in Pediatric Allergy and Immunology (published in December 2022 and February 2024). The results related to immune gene expression, Treg cell and cytokine measurements have been presented at several international conferences and have been published in Gut Microbes (Impact factor 9.434 in 2022). Specifically, the second paper published in Pediatric Allergy and Immunology has been chosen to be one of the top 3 papers published in the Journal (PAI-APAPARI Award). Dr Xing Yuhan is the current post-doc working on this project. She represented our team in presenting the work in various international meetings. Although it was challenging to carry out our studies during the pandemic period due to travel restrictions, we were able to complete our objectives and tasks related to this project.

14119320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119320.value: The major research outcomes included the determination of immune system regulation when children are exposed to the rural environment. A broad range of immune regulatory genes were suppressed in rural children compared to urban children. Our analyses of the gene expression, cytokine profile, and differential cell counts indicated a broad suppression of the immune system, including Th1 and Th2 pathways, in children from rural areas compared to children from the city. In vitro stimulation of dust extracts from various rural environments consistently downregulated the expression of inflammatory genes related the central nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways, while upregulated the anti-inflammatory molecules including negative regulator of NF-κB pathway A20/tumor necrosis factor α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) and dual-specificity phosphatase 1 (DUSP1). We confirmed that children in rural environments were strongly protected from the development of asthma due to exposure to agricultural environments and domestic poultry. We further evaluated using an asthma animal model to validate our findings. The extracts of the dust samples from the rural areas showed consistent suppression of asthma-related airway inflammation in the animal model experiments. The diversified microbial environment in the rural areas associated with farming and domestic poultry stimulated the early immune system to reduce future development of asthma as demonstrated in our animal model experiments.

14119320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119320.value: The next step is to determine the types of microbes and microbial metabolites responsible for modulating the early immune system. The timing and dosage of exposure must be quantified and tested in an animal model for efficacy and safety. We can then move on to prospective human studies.

14119320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119320.value: The results of this project revealed that children raised in a rural environment were protected from asthma due to early exposure to the diversified microbial environment. Such exposure helps the immune system mature and not develop excessive inflammatory responses. Careful clarification of the factors and confirmation in further animal studies will help develop preventive human treatment.

14119420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119420.value: Allergic diseases are common in developed countries, causing significant social and economical burden to individuals and government. Among the various causes for allergic diseases, food allergy is one of the most prevalent causes of allergic sensitization. Procambarus (P.) clarkia, also called red swamp crayfish, has served as a local favourite in China and has played an important role in the history of human nutrition among indigenous people. Because of its nutritional characteristics, crayfish has become the most important economic resource among freshwater shrimp. Meanwhile, the increased production and consumption of P. clarkia have been accompanied by more frequent allergic reactions, involving diverse clinical symptoms that vary from local to life-threatening anaphylaxis. In this study, the high-quality reference genome and transcriptome datasets of P. clarkia will be constructed using single molecule real-time sequencing. After genome assembly and subsequent annotation, novel allergen groups as well as members of known allergen groups will be identified by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry. Finally, the comparative genomics analysis of P. clarkia using bioinformatics tools will unlock the mystery behind the special features of this species including the high moulting rate, survival in brackish water, sensitivity to insecticide and resistance to diseases.

14119420.label: Realisation of objectives
14119420.value: Objective 1: Sequencing and assembling the genome of P. clarkii In this study, a hybrid assembly approach was utilized by the combination of both long-read Single Molecule Real-Time (SMRT) sequencing (PacBio Sequel) and short-read sequencing (Illumina HiSeq 2500). We generated a complete genome of P. clarkii with 3.2 Gb in size and 93.4% BUSCO completeness. The total number of scaffolds in the de novo assembled P. clarkii genome is 49,332, with a scaffold N50 of 189 kb and the longest scaffold size of 4,313 kb. Compared with the previously published P. clarkii genome solely based on short-read sequencing data, the genome assembled in this study demonstrated a remarkable 166-fold improvement in scaffold N50. In addition, the completeness of our assembled P. clarkii genome (93.4%) was also comparable to that of the previously reported genome assembled at chromosome level (94.15%). These statistics revealed that we have successfully constructed a high-quality genome of P. clarkii. To construct the transcriptome of P. clarkii, the RNA of tail muscle, hepatopancreas, antennal gland, ovary, and gut tissues were sequenced by next generation sequencing (Illumina HiSeq 2500). We mapped the RNA sequencing reads to the genome of P. clarkii by Hisat2 and Trinity, resulting in 96.4% and 98.7% BUSCO completeness, respectively. Based on the masked genome, transcriptome, and protein homology evidence from closely related species, the genome annotation was performed by Maker2 pipeline. We identified a total of 79,626 protein-coding genes in the P. clarkii genome with 88.4% BUSCO completeness, suggesting a high quality of genome annotation. Objective 2: Identification of novel allergen groups by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry Based on the high quality and well-annotated genome, a genome-wide analysis was conducted to discover novel allergen groups in P. clarkii. The sequences of reported allergens in P. clarkii and other decapods from WHO/IUIS allergen nomenclature database were used as reference genes to identify the putative allergens in P. clarkii genome by TBLASTN search. The sequence homology between the reference allergen groups and the putative allergens was determined by BLASTP analysis. A comprehensive allergen profile consisting of eleven allergen groups was identified in the P. clarkii genome. Based on the sequence homology to the reported allergens, we characterized all the homologs and isoforms of each allergen group, along with their respective gene loci within the genome. Multiple homologs have been identified in most of the allergen groups, and massive tandem duplication events were observed in group 6 (troponin C) and group 7 (hemocyanin) allergen. We further examined the gene expression levels of all putative allergen groups in four different tissues, including tail muscle, hepatopancreas, ovary and antennal gland. Pro c 2.0101, a homolog of Pro c 2 (arginine kinase), exhibited a notable expression level across all tissues, particularly in muscle. As for Pro c 5 (myosin light chain 1), it was highly expressed in muscle and antennal gland. These findings provided evidence of subfunctionalization and tissue-specific expression patterns among the allergen homologs in P. clarkii. Based on the gene expression profile, the homologs from each allergen group with the highest transcript level in muscle tissue were selected for allergenicity evaluation. We examined the allergenicity of the recombinant putative allergens based on IgE reactivity using ELISA with crayfish-sensitized patient sera (N=30). The allergenicity of the reported allergens Pro c 1, Pro c 8, and Pro c 9 was confirmed, with IgE reactivity rates of 36.7%, 26.7%, and 6.67%, respectively. Pro c 3.0301 and Pro c 6.0201, which had not been reported as allergens in P. clarkii previously, exhibited significant allergenicity rates of 33.3% and 20.0%, respectively. Our findings suggested Pro c 3.0301 and Pro c 6.0201 as two novel allergens in P. clarkii. In addition to our in silico prediction of putative allergens in P. clarkii, we have identified and characterized IgE-binding proteins in crayfish muscle protein extracts using pooled patients' sera. The proteins were separated by 2-dimensional gel electrophoresis and six protein spots were targeted for. After sequencing the peptides by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry and identifying the protein identities by amino acid sequence mapping, we discovered three putative allergen groups that had not been previously reported in decapods. These groups included nesprin-1-like protein, ATP synthase subunit beta, and actin-3. Objective 3: Special features analysis of P. clarkii by bioinformatics tools To investigate the special features of P. clarkii, comparative genomic analysis was performed using the genomes of the six species: P. clarkii, P. monodon, P. vannamei, H. americanus, C. opilio, P. trituberculatus. The phylogenetic orthology and gene family changes were analyzed by OrthoFinder and CAFE to investigate the evolutionary dynamics of gene families. A total of 845 rapidly evolving gene families were identified in P. clarkii genome. GO and KEGG enrichment analysis revealed the fast evolution of gene families related to proteolysis and metabolism, including chitinase, ionotropic glutamate receptor and the detoxification enzyme UDP-glycosyltransferase and cytochrome P450. Notably, P. clarkii had the greatest number of the detoxification enzyme UDP-glycosyltransferase (18 genes) among the six species. This suggested that the significant expansion of UDP-glycosyltransferase was likely to provide P. clarkii with enhanced capabilities to metabolize and eliminate toxins, increasing their resilience in polluted habitats. We also observed that P. clarkii possessed the highest number of cysteine proteases, with a total of 57 genes identified. This number is more than twice the count found in other species. P. clarkii has been reported to have resistance to crayfish plague fungus A. astaci, implying its efficient immune system. Cysteine proteases are proteolytic enzymes that have been indicated in the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses. The expanded cysteine protease family observed in P. clarkii suggested its potential involvement in the defense mechanisms against pathogen infections. P. clarkii is able tolerate lower oxygen concentrations compared to other crustacean species and can maintain high survival rates in oxygen poor environments. Hemocyanin, reported as group 7 allergen, is a copper containing protein responsible for oxygen transport in invertebrates. In P. clarkii, we observed a significant expansion of hemocyanin genes, in which there was a duplication in the gene number compared to other crustacean species. This finding suggested that gene expansion by tandem duplication might facilitate the emergence of allergenic hemocyanin in decapods. The expansion of hemocyanin could contribute to the ability of P. clarkii to enhance oxygen intake, thereby enabling them to adapt to hypoxic conditions. The comparative analysis also revealed the diversification of tropomyosin in P. clarkii. Tropomyosin, the major allergen (group 1) in P. clarkii, is a double-stranded α-helical actin associated protein present in cytoskeleton and muscle. We identified the tropomyosin gene in seven crustaceans and illustrated the gene structure. In P. clarkii, the gene structure of tropomyosin consists of nine exons, with five of these exons undergoing alternative splicing. Similar gene structures were observed in other decapods including P. monodon and H. americanus, but not in C. torosa, a more distant relative of decapods. These findings indicated that the subfunctionalization of tropomyosin in P. clarkii was achieved by increasing gene complexity and deriving isoforms instead of gene duplication. Furthermore, the diversification of tropomyosin by alternative splicing occurred in a later stage of crustacean evolution, with a predominant presence observed in the decapod lineage.

14119420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119420.value: Crustacean shellfish is among the eight most common food allergens, and the red swamp crayfish (P. clarkii) is a highly valued shellfish species for consumption in China. However, the complete allergen profile of P. clarkii remains unknown, and the detailed investigation of specific genes associated with the special characteristics of P. clarkii is limited as well. In this study, we constructed a high-quality P. clarkii genome using a hybrid assembly approach and annotated it with multi-omics data. The P. clarkii genome achieved a high level of completeness in both assembly and annotation, serving as an efficient platform to study the allergen profile and special features of P. clarkii. Based on the high-quality genome, we identified a total of 14 putative allergen groups through in-silico prediction, followed by the allergenicity evaluation using IgE ELISA. Proteomic identification of novel allergens was also performed by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry. Through our investigations, we confirmed Pro c 3.0301 and Pro c 6.0201 as two novel allergens in P. clarkii. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the significant expansion of multiple gene families associated with metabolism and proteolysis in P. clarkii. These findings provided insights into the distinctive characteristics of P. clarkii, particularly its abilities in detoxification, oxygen intake, and immune response. Our manuscript related to novel allergens of P. clarkii is currently under review in World Allergy Organization Journal. The research findings were also presented at the World Allergy Congress (WAC 2023) held in Bangkok, Thailand, on 1-3 December 2023. In summary, we report a complete and well-annotated genome of P. clarkii, serving as a solid bedrock to investigate its allergen profile and special features. By providing a comprehensive understanding of the complete allergen profile, our study presents a foundation for comprehending P. clarkii-associated allergy. The expanded gene families identified through comparative genomic analysis shed light on the genetic mechanisms underlying the special traits in P. clarkii, contributing to a deeper understanding of its evolution and adaptation. The knowledge gained could facilitate the implementation of a components-resolved diagnostic test and preventive immunotherapy based on molecular allergens for crayfish allergy.

14119420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119420.value: In this study, we revealed the comprehensive allergen profile of P. clarkii using a multi-omics approach. The establishment of a high-quality genome facilitated the thorough understanding of the allergenic potential of P. clarkii, providing valuable insights into the component-resolved diagnosis of crayfish allergy. The complete genome of P. clarkii also enabled the comparative analysis of diverse gene families, elucidating the special characteristics of P. clarkii and enhancing the understanding of its adaptation. Our findings shed light on the development of novel component-resolved diagnostic test and therapeutic agents specific to P. clarkii allergens. Exploring the potential of utilizing recombinant allergens as immunotherapy for crayfish allergy is a promising avenue for future investigation. The multi-omics approach employed in this study could be applied to other species to reveal their complete allergen profile, contributing to the development of customized diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

14119420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119420.value: Shellfish is recognized as one of the eight major food allergens and has a significant impact on over 2% of the general population. In Asia, shellfish allergy has been reported to exhibit a notably high prevalence of 7.7%. Red swamp crayfish (P. clarkii) is a famous seafood and one of the most widely cultivated species in China. In this study, a high-quality genome of P. clarkii was constructed using the state-of-the-art genomics and bioinformatics tools. The research outcomes in this project contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the allergenic properties of P. clarkii. The complete genome also assisted in unraveling the distinctive characteristics of P. clarkii, thereby facilitating the understanding of its biology. The deliverables will provide valuable insights into the future development of novel diagnostic tests and therapeutic agents for shellfish allergy. The approach utilized in this study can be extended to other species for the identification and characterization of their complete allergen profiles.

14120420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120420.value: Our genome is not organized in a simple linear manner within the nuclear space, instead in a delicate hierarchical 3D structure. Emerging evidences unequivocally support the chromosome 3D organization instructs pivotal regulatory information underlying major biological processes impacting development, differentiation, and diseases. Characterization of chromosome 3D organization in different settings has been the focus of many research groups recently. However, our understanding of 3D genome organization in adult skeletal muscle stem cells (also called satellite cells, SCs) remains largely elusive. SCs are the main cell type responsible for muscle regeneration and normally lies quiescently beneath the muscle fiber. SCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergo self-renewal and return to the quiescent state to replenish the adult stem cell pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulation may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia that are prevalent in our society. Here we propose to study the 3D genome reorganization during SC lineage development and SC aging. In the pilot study, our in situ Hi-C results demonstrate a 3D genome rewiring at compartment and TAD levels during SC lineage progression and SC aging. In depth analysis on Pax7 locus reveals a novel regulatory circuitry surrounding the genomic locus of this master transcription factor. These preliminary results lead us to hypothesize that 3D genome organization plays active roles in SC functionality, Pax7 expression and SC aging. Three aims are proposed to (1) further characterize 3D genome reorganization during SC lineage progression at a high-resolution level; (2) further dissect the regulatory mechanism of Pax7 expression in SC; (3) further characterize 3D genome reorganization during SC aging. Once completed, this study will for the first time uncover 3D genome rewiring underlying SC lineage development and aging and pinpoint the key regulatory circuitry responsible for Pax7 temporal expression; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases.

14120420.label: Realisation of objectives
14120420.value: In the original proposal, we proposed to study the 3D genome reorganization during muscle stem cell (SC) lineage development and SC aging. Three objectives were proposed and all of them have been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. The findings are now published on Science Advances (2023) (see Research Output). AIM 1: To further characterize 3D genome reorganization during SC lineage progression at a high-resolution level. To delineate the remodeling in genome architecture during SC lineage progression, freshly isolated SCs (FISCs) were obtained from Pax7-nGFP mice using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), while quiescent SCs (QSCs) were prepared through in situ fixation before isolation. FISCs were cultured for 1 to 3 days to develop into activated SCs (ASC-D1), proliferating cells (ASC-D2), and early differentiating cells (DSC-D3). Using in situ Hi-C, the 3D genome organization was analyzed, resulting in over 2 billion uniquely aligned contacts. TAD organization was analyzed, revealing over 3,000 borders identified across stages. While TAD borders remained largely stable, notable changes in insulation scores (IS) indicated that local chromatin insulation varied with SC activation. A significant proportion of invariant TAD borders exhibited substantial differences in IS, correlating with gene expression dynamics. We also found TAD reprogramming was associated with local transcriptional changes, with many instances of concurrent changes in IS and gene expression. Further analysis of inter-TAD interactions demonstrated that TAD clusters underwent dynamic reorganization from QSC to FISC. Genes within these clusters exhibited higher expression levels, suggesting a relationship between TAD interactions and transcriptional activity. Super enhancers (SEs) present in TAD clusters were linked to longer interaction distances and more pronounced expression changes, highlighting their role in SC lineage progression. Additionally, chromatin loops were analyzed, revealing a drastic reduction in loop numbers and interaction strength during early SC activation. Specific enhancer-promoter (E-P) and enhancer-enhancer (E-E) interactions were identified, with dynamic looping correlating with changes in gene expression. For instance, certain E-P loops were lost in FISC, leading to decreased expression of associated genes, while new loops emerged for others, facilitating transcriptional activation. AIM 2: To further dissect the regulatory mechanism of Pax7 expression in SC. PAX7 is a crucial transcription factor (TF) that regulates the myogenic potential and function of SCs. We investigated the 3D organization of the Pax7 locus and identified a prominent TAD encompassing the Pax7 locus in QSCs, which contained four sub-TADs. In contrast, these sub-TADs vanished in FISCs, leading to altered interaction strengths among them and a notable reduction in chromatin loops. To explore the elements influencing this 3D reorganization, we identified four putative regulatory elements (REs) based on chromatin interactions and ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq signals. All four REs exhibited high ATAC-seq signals, with R4 located in the Pax7 promoter and R2/R3 marked by H3K27ac signals in QSCs, which were absent in FISCs. To validate the functionality of these REs, we utilized CRISPR-Cas9/AAV-sgRNA technology to delete each RE in QSCs. Notably, deletions of R2, R3, and R4 caused smaller decreases in Pax7 levels in FISCs, aligning with the loss of RE-mediated loops. A control element, C1, exhibited no impact on Pax7 expression upon deletion. Further analysis using in situ Hi-C demonstrated that the deletion of REs significantly increased inter-TAD interaction strength between the Pax7 TAD and neighboring TADs. The intra-Pax7 TAD interaction strength varied with each RE deletion, highlighting the complex role of these elements in regulating Pax7 expression and chromatin architecture. Removal of certain REs also affected insulation strength at TAD boundaries and led to the formation of new loops. To investigate whether these 3D changes were driven by reduced Pax7 levels, we analyzed Hi-C data after PAX7 knockdown (KD), which showed increased inter- and intra-Pax7 TAD interaction strengths, similar to RE deletions. Additionally, PAX7 KD led to decreased insulation strength at Pax7 TAD boundaries. We also searched for TF motifs within the RE regions, identifying PAX7 motifs in R2 and R4, suggesting autoregulation. MYC motifs were present in R1 and R2, hinting at a role for MYC in downregulating Pax7 during the transition to FISCs. Other motifs included FOXO3, which promotes quiescence, and NFIA, which is highly expressed in QSCs but diminished in FISCs. These findings suggest multiple TFs collaborate to regulate Pax7 expression, highlighting pathways for future exploration. Aim 3: To further characterize 3D genome reorganization during SC aging. SCs experience a decline in regenerative capacity with aging, linked to changes at transcriptomic and epigenomic levels. This study investigates whether 3D genome rewiring occurs in SCs during physiological aging in mice. We analyzed FISCs from wild-type C57BL/6 mice at three ages: young (2 months), aged (23-24 months), and geriatric (28-32 months). Consistent with previous findings, we observed a decrease in FISC numbers: 4.3% in young, 3.3% in aged, and 1.8% in geriatric mice. RNA-seq revealed distinct gene expression profiles between young and aged SCs, becoming more divergent in geriatric cells. Notably, Pax7 expression increased with age, alongside stress-responsive genes like Egr1 and Atf3. In total, 1,122 genes were up-regulated and 1,016 down-regulated in aged versus young SCs, while geriatric versus aged comparisons showed 910 up-regulated and 1,104 down-regulated genes. GO analysis identified enriched terms related to cell adhesion and immune response in aged SCs, while geriatric SCs showed enrichment in membrane and extracellular space terms. To assess 3D genome organization, we performed in situ Hi-C across all age stages, yielding over 300 million uniquely aligned contacts. Young SCs exhibited a distinct 3D genome organization compared to aged and geriatric SCs. Long-range interactions (>3 Mb) significantly increased in geriatric SCs. A compartmental analysis revealed increased A compartment (A-A) interaction strength during the transition from young to aged, which remained constant in geriatric SCs. Conversely, B compartment (B-B) interactions declined in the transition to geriatric SCs. While compartmentalization changes did not correlate directly with gene expression shifts, an increase in A-A interactions coincided with the upregulation of aging-related genes like Il-6 and Ccnd2. Overall, we noted a decrease in intercompartment contacts at aged SCs, followed by a reduction in geriatric SCs. Compartment switching was limited, with only 6.5% of the genome transitioning between compartments. At the TAD level, ~70% of TAD borders remained stable throughout aging. However, IS at TAD borders decreased significantly in geriatric SCs. A marked increase in IS was observed, with 38.3% of borders showing >20% increase, indicating a loss of insulation as SCs aged. Local gene expression changes correlated with TAD border dynamics, contrasting with findings from SC lineage progression. PCA analysis of RNA expression, compartmentalization, IS, and TAD dynamics indicated similar trajectories for transcription and IS from young to aged stages. However, TAD connectivity altered significantly during the geriatric transition. Chromatin looping analysis revealed 11,180, 10,131, and 11,104 loops across young, aged, and geriatric SCs, respectively, with an increase in interaction strength during aging. In particular, the Pax7 locus showed a new chromatin loop formation at the geriatric stage, correlating with increased Pax7 expression. Furthermore, de novo motif searches identified distinct TF binding motifs at stage-specific loop anchors, suggesting their roles in loop remodeling during SC aging. Notably, geriatric SCs favored long-range chromatin interactions, paralleling cultured SC behavior during lineage progression. This comprehensive analysis illustrates the dynamic changes in 3D genome organization and gene expression throughout SC aging, highlighting potential regulatory mechanisms involved in the aging process.
