14120420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120420.value: Little is known about three-dimensional (3D) genome organization in skeletal muscle stem cells. In this study, we comprehensively map the 3D genome topology reorganization during mouse SC lineage progression. Specifically, rewiring at the compartment level is most pronounced when SCs become activated. Marked loss in topologically associating domain (TAD) border insulation and chromatin looping also occurs during early activation process. Meanwhile, TADs can form TAD clusters and super-enhancer–containing TAD clusters orchestrate stage-specific gene expression. Furthermore, we uncover that transcription factor PAX7 is pivotal in enhancer-promoter (E-P) loop formation. We also identify cis-regulatory elements that are crucial for local chromatin organization at Pax7 locus and Pax7 expression. Lastly, we unveil that geriatric SC displays a prominent gain in long-range contacts and loss of TAD border insulation. Together, our results uncover that 3D chromatin extensively reorganizes at multiple architectural levels and underpins the transcriptome remodeling during SC lineage development and SC aging. Our findings were published on Science Advances, Nature Communications, Cell Reports and other Journals with high impact. Moreover, two PhD students obtained their PhD degree with the support of this project.

14120420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120420.value: In this study, we provided a comprehensive view of 3D genome organization in SC lineage progression and SC aging. Future studies could focus on elucidating the specific TFs involved in chromatin loop remodeling and their regulatory roles in SC activation and aging. Investigating the interplay between these TFs and environmental factors may provide deeper insights into SC dysfunction during aging. For example, we could investigate the roles of identified TFs, like PAX7, using CRISPR/Cas9 to manipulate their expression and assess impacts on chromatin architecture and gene expression. Based on the findings from this study, we could develop strategies to manipulate chromatin structure or enhance TF activity to rejuvenate aging SCs, potentially improving muscle regeneration. We could also extend findings to other tissues and human muscle SCs to understand common mechanisms of 3D genome regulation and aging, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of stem cell biology.

14120420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120420.value: In this study, we explored how the three-dimensional (3D) structure of chromatin in muscle stem cells changes as these cells develop and age. Muscle stem cells are crucial for repairing and regenerating muscle tissue, but their ability to function declines with age. We mapped how the organization of chromatin affects gene expression during different stages of cell activation and aging. Understanding these changes is significant because it sheds light on the mechanisms behind muscle regeneration, especially how aging impacts stem cell function. Our study highlights the role of a key protein, PAX7, in regulating chromatin structure and how its own expression was regulated by the 3D chromatin, which is vital for muscle health. The findings have valuable implications for developing treatments for muscle-related diseases and age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia). By uncovering the 3D organization of chromatin and its influence on gene expression, our study paves the way for new strategies to enhance muscle regeneration and maintain muscle function throughout life.

14120520.label: Realisation of objectives
14120520.value: Osteoporosis is a prevalent disorder that disrupts bone quality, mainly in aged people, and frequently results in devastating osteoporotic fractures. Magnesium (Mg) deficiency is a marked characteristic of osteoporosis, and magnesium level in serum is positively associated with bone mineral density. Mg supply can reverse the progression of osteoporosis, but the Mg content in bone is relatively unaffected, suggesting a distinct mechanism with our previously reported sensory nervous system activated by local implantation of Mg metal. Recent studies report that the central nervous system orchestrates bone remodeling via various mechanisms and molecules. The central nerve system (CNS) projects sympathetic nerve endings to the bone and inhibition of sympathetic nerve activity with β-blocker improved bone mass. Oral magnesium-L-threonate (MgT) supplementation improved memory, suggesting its actions on CNS. However, it is still unclear if Mg regulates bone metabolism via acting on CNS. If yes, which brain region is the target of Mg ions also remains unknown. Ovariectomy (OVX) surgery was performed to construct the osteoporotic mice model. The MgT was injected intraperitoneally (i.p). We selected two different dosages (50mg/kg/day and 100mg/kg/day) to test if MgT could prevent osteoporosis. The mice were treated with either MgT or saline for 4 weeks and 8 weeks, respectively. Micro-CT and histological staining were used to determine bone quality. Peripheral nerve staining and labeling were used to determine the change in the peripheral nerve. Activity-labeled neuron and c-Fos staining were used to determine the brain region affected by MgT treatment. The retrograde tracing technique based on the fluorescent pseudorabies virus (PRV) was used to identify the brain region connecting with bone. To achieve optimal viral expression in certain brain nuclei, stereotactic injection of adeno-associated virus was performed to yield optimal expression of certain gene elements. Chemogenetics techniques were applied to manipulate certain brain nuclei and their upstream nuclei. Transcriptome analyses were performed on the femur upon brain manipulation to analyze the downstream signaling pathways in the skeletal system. Our result suggested that MgT injection increased the Mg2+ level in the cerebrospinal fluid. After 1-month, MgT treatment increased BV/TV by 35% and Tb.Th by 15% compared with osteoporotic mice treated with saline. The elevated bone formation marker ALP and OPG marker suggested increased osteogenesis after MgT’s treatment. By activity labeled neurons technique, we found a 40% increase of the c-Fos positive neurons in the parabrachial nucleus (PBN) after MgT’s treatment. We injected PRV into the trabecular bone region of the femur. The PBN region was labeled by green fluorescent protein (GFP), suggesting an anatomical connection between bone and the PBN region. PBN hosted most Calca-positive neuron subpopulations as confirmed by immunofluorescent staining, and chemogenetic activation of this subpopulation increased the trabecular bone parameters [comment: not clear, please list out] and bone mass. When retrograde tracing AAV was injected into the PBN, several upstream nuclei that project to PBN were identified. Among these nuclei, the projection from the central amygdala showed the greatest fluorescent intensity. Chemogenetic inhibition of the GABAergic neurons of CEA, which consist of the majority of the neurons in CEA, also increased bone mass. By gene expression analysis, we found that several magnesium channels were downregulated in the OVX model, and magnesium transporter-1 (Magt1) was enriched in the brain and downregulated in osteoporotic mice. Knocking out Magt1 in Calca+ neurons resulted in a 30% decrease in BV/TV. More importantly, Global and PBN-specific Magt1 knockout abolished the bone morphology difference between MgT and saline. Transcriptome analysis of the femur suggested the upregulation of neuroactive-ligand receptor interaction and neurotensin (Nts) is the crucial regulatory gene in this brain-bone axis. Although the protective effect of Mg on the skeletal system has been reported for many years, very few studies have linked the central nervous system with Mg-promoted bone regeneration. In this study, we identified brain penetrable Mg2+ activated the PBN, a novel brain nucleus that regulates bone mass and participates in other important biological processes. In this study, the downstream effectors and upstream nuclei were identified. Therefore, we have discovered a new brain-to-bone axis that participates in Mg-related bone regeneration under osteoporosis. Overall, our study suggested that the CNS may serve as a potential target for bone disorders, while supplementation of MgT improves bone quality by acting on specific CNS regions.

14120520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120520.value: We found that a systemic brain penetrable magnesium form, MgT’s treatment prevents osteoporosis and increases bone mass. Magnesium activates multiple brain regions, among which the PBN nuclei are the most significant activated brain nuclei. Using the retrograde tracing technique, a direct connection between the PBN region and the femur is identified. CGRP+ neurons in the PBN region are significantly activated upon MgT treatment, while chemogenetic activation of CGRP+ neurons in the PBN region mimics the effect of MgT. Transcriptome profile suggests that activating Mg responding neurons in the PBN region the upregulated gene enriched in ossification and skeletal development, may be associated with neurotensin (Nts) downregulation and neuroactive-receptor interaction. Several magnesium channels are downregulated in the OVX mice, including Magnesium transporter 1 (Magt1). Magt1 is widely expressed in the PBN region and knocking Magt1 in either Calca-cre mice or local injection of AAV-Cre abolishes the beneficial effect of MgT. We are revising a review paper entitled ‘Targeting the central and peripheral nervous system to regulate bone homeostasis: observations, mechanisms and potential therapies’ summarizing the brain-bone axis in Military Medical Research (IF=16.70). The main body of this research is currently under polishing and ready to submit. One PhD was trained. This work was selected for oral presentation at several international conferences, including the Orthopaedic Research Society (ORS) 2024 Annual Meeting and the International Chinese Musculoskeletal Research Conference 2024.

14120520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120520.value: As we have identified, CGRP neurons in the central nervous system are essential in regulating bone mass during the stimulation of magnesium. Although we elucidate a brain-dependent mechanism of magnesium in the phenomenon of promoting bone regeneration, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that magnesium mediates its effect on bone via a direct local mechanism. A lot of previous works by our group have demonstrated that local magnesium implants can promote the regeneration of the callus during fracture healing. As we have proved that the PBN nuclei and related circuits are crucial in mediating magnesium-related bone regeneration, whether PBN can directly regulate the level of magnesium in serum and CSF remains unknown. Besides, whether this neural circuit mediated the bone-protective effect in aging-associated osteoporosis remains unclear. In addition, we would like to investigate whether non-invasive neuromodulation using new techniques like transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) and transcranial magnetic stimulation can improve bone quality by acting on PBN.

14120520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120520.value: We discovered that a type of magnesium called MgT, which can enter the brain, helps prevent osteoporosis and boosts bone strength. This magnesium activates several brain areas, with the PBN region being the most notably affected. Using advanced tracing techniques, we identified a direct connection between this brain region and the femur. Specific neurons called CGRP+ neurons become highly active after MgT treatment. Interestingly, artificially stimulating these neurons produces effects similar to those of MgT. By studying the genes involved, we found that activating these magnesium-responsive neurons promotes bone growth and development, potentially linked to changes in neurotensin and interactions with nerve receptors. In mice with osteoporosis, certain magnesium transporters were less active. The Magt1 transporter is essential in the PBN region, and its absence cancels out the benefits of MgT. This highlights the critical role of magnesium in connecting brain activity to bone health.

14120620.label: Project Objectives
14120620.value: This is a prospective, phase 2, single-arm study investigating the efficacy of modified EBR for large bladder tumours of ≥ 3cm. Primary outcome is a composite outcome on the rate of complete resection for NMIBC and proper staging for MIBC. Secondary outcomes include the proper staging rate for NMIBC, complete resection rate for MIBC, successful modified EBR rate, circumferential resection margin, deep resection margin, presence of detrusor muscle in the modified EBR specimen, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative mitomycin C instillation, duration of bladder irrigation, duration of catheterization, hospital stay and the 30-day complications following modified EBR. The findings of this study can establish the role of modified EBR for large bladder tumours of ≥ 3cm. Together with our on-going EBR clinical trial for patients with bladder tumours of ≤3cm, the role of EBR for the whole spectrum of bladder tumours including both NMIBC and MIBC can be determined.

14120620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120620.value: 背景 經尿道膀胱腫瘤整塊切除術是一種比常規零碎切除術簡單而優越的技術。這手術可以確保膀胱腫瘤標本能保持完整以進行適當的組織學評估，並可以確定膀胱腫瘤是否完全切除。我們正在針對小於三厘米的膀胱腫瘤患者進行一項多中心隨機對照試驗。在這項擬議的研究中，我們旨在研究改良的整塊切除術對大於三厘米的膀胱腫瘤患者的療效。 目的和假設 這項研究旨在探討改良的整塊切除術對大於三厘米的膀胱腫瘤的療效。我們假設改良的整塊切除術對非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌可以達到很高的完全切除率，及對肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌可以達到很高的適當分期率。 方法 這是第二階段單臂研究，將在香港的兩家本地醫院進行。將對所有診斷出患有膀胱腫瘤的患者進行研究資格篩選。主要結果是包括非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的完全切除率和肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的正確分期率的綜合結果。次要結果包括非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的適當分期率，肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的完全切除率，整塊切除術的成功率，環切和深層切除切緣，逼尿肌採樣率，閉孔反射的發生率，手術時間，術後立即給予絲裂黴素C滴注的成功率，膀胱沖洗和導管插入的持續時間，住院時間以及術後30天的並發症。 研究對象數目計算 根據以前的數據，假設我們至少有90％的研究對象通過改良的整塊切除術可以完成非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的完整切除和肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的適當分期，預計這項研究需要納入二十一人。假設流失率為20％，研究對象數目則需要二十六人。在這項研究中，我們旨在招募總共三十位研究對象。 時間表和可行性 納入時間預計為二十個月。根據以往的數據，我們預計在納入時間期間將有一百零七個位潛在的研究對象。這項研究預計將會在兩年內完成。 未來的研究 這項研究是一項開拓性的項目，以確立改良的整塊切除術在大於三厘米的膀胱腫瘤患者中的作用。連同我們正在進行的針對小於三厘米的膀胱腫瘤患者的整塊切除術臨床試驗，我們可以確定整塊切除術在治療非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌和肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌的作用。

14120820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120820.value: The aim of this project is to improve our understanding of the functions and maturation of embryonic stem cells (ESCs)-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). ESCs are capable of self-renewal and are pluripotent, meaning that they can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in our body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. For successful transplantation, transplanted cells must survive and integrate to native myocardium. These transplanted cardiomyocytes also have to be mature enough so as to functionally couple with native myocardium and not to result in harmful conditions such as arrhythmia. Therefore, the functional properties and maturation process of these potential replacement cells must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. Under conventional protocol of ESC-CM culture, ESC-CMs are regarded as immature both structurally and functionally. It is known that increase in mitochondrial biogenesis and changes in mitochondrial dynamics are needed for native heart to mature. Interestingly, previous studies showed that increased mitochondrial biogenesis/altered metabolic pathways are associated with enhanced ESC-CM maturation in vitro. In addition, altering mitochondrial dynamics was found to increase cardiac differentiation of ESCs. However, whether increasing mitochondrial biogenesis and/or changing mitochondrial dynamics would enhance the maturation of ESC-CMs is unexplored. Transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) channels are non-selective cation channels that permeate calcium. Our recent findings showed that TRPA1 channels are expressed in ESC-CMs. Intriguingly, our preliminary data showed that blocking TRPA1 decreased calcium transients and action potentials (important determinants for the functions of cardiomyocytes) of ESC-CMs, while opening TRPA1 exerted opposite effects. In addition, blocking TRPA1 decreased mitochondrial biogenesis and altered mitochondrial dynamics towards less fusion/more fission, while opening TRPA1 led to the opposite effects. In this proposal, we hypothesize that TRPA1 positively regulates the functions of ESC-CMs. In addition, we hypothesize that TRPA1 positively regulates mitochondrial biogenesis, positively regulate mitochondrial fusion/negatively regulate mitochondrial fission, and increasing TRPA1 activity would enhance the maturation of ESC-CMs. These hypotheses would be tested by a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiological and genetic manipulation techniques. This project will provide novel information on the role of TRPA1 in regulating the functions and maturation of ESC-CMs. In addition, the knowledge generated in this project can be used for enhancing maturation of ESC-CMs and would therefore put these cells a step towards their future therapeutic uses. 這個研究計劃的目的是認識胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞（ESC-CMs）的功能特性和成熟過程。 胚胎幹細胞能夠自我更新和擁有萬能的特性，這意味著它們可以無限地被培養，並有能力分化為體內所有的細胞類型，包括心肌。因此胚胎幹細胞是科學研究和未來治療應用極好的心肌細胞來源。能夠達致成功移植，移植的細胞必須生存，並與心臟的天然心肌整合。這些移植的心肌細胞還必須足夠成熟，以便與天然心肌功能性結合，並且不會導致有害的狀況，例如心律不整。因此，在將這些潛在的替代細胞用於治療目的之前，我們必須更好地理解其功能特性和成熟過程。 在ESC-CMs培養的常規方案下，ESC-CMs在結構和功能上都被認為是不成熟的。已知線粒體的增加和線粒體動態平衡的變化對於天然心臟的成熟是必需的。有趣的是，以往的研究表明，線粒體的增加/代謝途徑的改變與體外ESC-CMs成熟度的提高有關。另外，改變線粒體動態平衡的變化亦被發現可增加胚胎幹細胞的心肌分化。然而，能否通過增加線粒體的形成和/或改變線粒體的動態平衡來增加ESC-CMs的成熟度尚待探討。 瞬時受體電位錨蛋白1（TRPA1）通道是滲透鈣的非選擇性陽離子通道。我們最近的發現表明，TRPA1通道在ESC-CMs中表達。有趣的是，我們初步的數據顯示，阻斷TRPA1可以降低ESC-CMs的鈣瞬變和動作電位（決定心肌細胞功能的重要決定因素），而打開TRPA1則起到相反的作用。此外，阻斷TRPA1會減少線粒體的形成，並改變線粒體的動態平衡（減少融合/增加裂變），而打開TRPA1則產生相反的效果。 在這個研究計劃中，我們假設TRPA1正調節ESC-CMs的功能。此外，我們假設TRPA1正調節線粒體的形成，正調節線粒體的融合/負調節線粒體的裂變；再者，我們假設增加TRPA1活性將增加ESC-CMs的成熟度。 這些假設將通過細胞生物學、分子生物學、電生理學和基因操作技術的結合進行檢驗。 這個研究計劃將對有關TRPA1在調節ESC-CMs功能和成熟中所發揮的作用提供嶄新的資訊。此外，這個研究計劃所產生的知識可用於增加ESC-CMs的成熟度，因此將使這些細胞朝著其未來的治療用途邁出一步。

14120820.label: Realisation of objectives
14120820.value: Aim 1. To investigate if transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) channels regulate the calcium transients and action potentials of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). As indicated in the progress report submitted in 2022, our results showed that TRPA1 positively regulates the cytosolic CaTs and the action potentials of ESC-CMs. Therefore, this aim was 100% achieved. Aim 2. To investigate if TRPA1 channels regulate the mitochondrial biogenesis and/or dynamics in ESC-CMs. Firstly, MitoTracker Red staining followed by live-cell imaging was performed to examine if mitochondrial morphology and biogenesis change upon treatment with TRPA1 activator or blocker. TRPA1 blocker decreased mitochondrial size (mitochondrial area and branch length) and complexity (number of branches and junctions per mitochondrion) and increased mitochondrial number gradually, indicating an increase in mitochondrial fission/decrease in mitochondrial fusion. On the other hand, TRPA1 activator induced the opposite effects. Notably, the mitochondrial occupancy, which indicated mitochondrial biogenesis, did not change much with a short-term treatment with drugs. However, with the extension of treatment time, TRPA1 blocker not only resulted in more fragmented and smaller mitochondria but also significantly reduced mitochondrial occupancy, indicating changes in both mitochondrial dynamics and biogenesis. On the other hand, TRPA1 activator induced the opposite effects. In addition, TRPA1 knockdown induced fragmented, small mitochondria while TRPA1 overexpression induced interconnected mitochondria. TRPA1 KD-CMs exhibited reduced mitochondrial area, number of branches per mitochondrion, number of junctions per mitochondrion, mitochondrial fractional occupancy, and elevated mitochondrial number compared with control CMs. In contrast, TRPA1 OE-CMs showed increased mitochondrial area, number of branches per mitochondrion, number of junctions per mitochondrion, and mitochondrial fractional occupancy compared with control CMs. There is no apparent difference in the mitochondrial number between TRPA1 OE-CMs and control CMs. Overall, TRPA1 negatively regulates mitochondrial fission and/or positively regulates mitochondrial fusion and biogenesis. Also, by qPCR, a number of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes, including PGC-1alpha, was found to be downregulated and upregulated in TRPA1 KD-CMs and TRPA1 OE-CMs, respectively. Western blotting further confirmed the change in expression of the PGC-1alpha at protein level. In contrast, expressions of most of the mitochondrial dynamics-related genes were not altered by change in TRPA1 expression. Mitochondria are not merely the center for energy metabolism but are also the headquarters for ROS production. To determine if changes of TRPA1 activities influence the function of mitochondria, ROS level was measured. TRPA1 blocker increased while TRPA1 activator decreased the cellular ROS level. Further, mitochondrial membrane potential was significantly reduced (depolarized) by TRPA1 blocker and elevated (hyperpolarized) by TRPA1 activator compared with control group. In summary, our results showed that TRPA1 positively regulates mitochondrial fusion/ negatively regulates mitochondrial fission, and positively regulates mitochondrial biogenesis at organelle and functional levels. Overall, this aim was 100% achieved. Aim 3. To investigate if TRPA1 channels regulate the maturation of ESC-CM. TRPA1 knockdown decreased while TRPA1 overexpression decreased the ratio of CMs with organized sarcomere. In addition, TRPA1 knockdown decreased while TRAP1 overexpression increased the size of CMs. The percentage of multi-nucleated cells tended to be decreased by TRPA1 knockdown and increased by TRPA1 overexpression. These results suggested that TRPA1 positively regulates the structural maturation of ESC-CMs. Functionally, TRPA1 was found to positively regulate both the calcium handling and the electrophysiological properties of ESC-CMs (in Aim 1). By Seahorse assay, TRPA1 knockdown decreased while TRPA1 overexpression increased the oxidative metabolism of ESC-CMs, suggesting that TRPA1 positively regulates the metabolic maturation of ESC-CMs. Moreover, TRPA1 knockdown decreased and TRPA1 overexpression increased the expression of genes positively related to the function and maturation of mitochondria and CMs as assessed by qPCR. In summary, our results showed that TRPA1 positively regulates the structural, functional and metabolic maturation of ESC-CMs. Overall, this aim was 100% achieved. Aim 4. To investigate if TRPA1 channels regulate the maturation of ESC-CMs through regulating mitochondrial biogenesis and/or dynamics. Our data have demonstrated that TRPA1 improved mitochondrial fusion and biogenesis and promoted CM maturation. Next, we investigated the mechanism underlying how TRPA1 exerts its role on CMs. As mentioned above, PGC-1alpha is a transcriptional coactivator that controls energy homeostasis by regulating glucose and oxidative metabolism. TRPA1 knockdown was shown to decrease PGC-1alpha at mRNA and protein levels, suggesting that PGC-1alpha may be the mediator in the regulation of CM maturation by TRPA1. We further tested whether PGC-1alpha overexpression could reverse the impaired maturation of CMs caused by TRPA1 knockdown. As expected, overexpression of PGC-1alpha in TRPA1 KD-CMs significantly increased the mitochondrial area, complexity, and occupancy compared with TRPA1 KD-CMs. Importantly, overexpression of PGC-1alpha in TRPA1 KD-CMs increased the ratio of CMs with organized sarcomere and increased CM size compared with TRPA1 KD-CMs. In addition, PGC-1alpha overexpression in TRPA1 KD-CMs markedly improved the electrophysiology properties hindered by TRPA1 knockdown as shown by an increase in DDR, Vmax-upstroke, and amplitude of action potential. These results suggested that TRPA1 improves CM maturation via PGC-1alpha. Some previous studies showed that p38 MAPK activation downregulated PGC-1alpha expression in CMs. In our study, western blot results revealed that the level of phosphorylated p38 MAPK was significantly elevated by TRPA1 knockdown, indicating increased activation of p38 MAPK. In addition, MAPK phosphatase-1 (MKP-1), which can selectively inactivate MAPKs. was markedly reduced by TRPA1 knockdown both at mRNA and protein levels. As calcium is both necessary and sufficient for the induction of MKP-1 expression, our results suggested that the decreased calcium influx from TRPA1 downregulation reduced the expression of MKP-1, further causing the unrestrained p38 MAPK activation, leading to a decrease in PGC-1alpha expression and mitochondrial biogenesis. To confirm that TRPA1 regulates PGC-1alpha expression via modulating the activity of p38 MAPK, SB203580, a specific inhibitor of p38 MAPK, was applied to TRPA1 KD-CMs. While TRPA1 knockdown decreased the expression of genes involved in ion channels, calcium handling, t-tubule formation, mitochondrial biogenesis/ dynamics, and oxidative phosphorylation, p38 MAPK inhibitor reversed the downregulation of these genes. In summary, our results showed that TRPA1 regulates the maturation of ESC-CMs through MKP-1-p38 MAPK-PGC-1alpha pathway. Overall, this aim was 100% achieved.

14120820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120820.value: Major findings of this project are listed below: i) TRPA1 is expressed in ESC-CMs and positively regulates the calcium transients and action potentials of ESC-CMs. ii) TRPA1 positively regulates the mitochondrial biogenesis of ESC-CMs. TRPA1 positively regulates the mitochondrial fusion and/or negatively regulates the mitochondrial fission of ESC-CMs. iii) TRPA1 positively regulates the structural, functional and metabolic maturation of ESC-CMs. iv) TRPA1 regulates the maturation of ESC-CMs through MKP-1-p38 MAPK-PGC-1α pathway. All of the above results were published in form of conference abstracts and in a full-length peer-reviewed research paper as documented in Part C. These results were also presented in regional meetings as documented in Part C. Results generated in this project were reported in the PhD thesis of Dr. Qianqian Ding. Since this project revealed the importance of mitochondrial biogenesis in the maturation of ESC-CMs, another project related to mitochondrial transcription factors (carried out by Dr. Yanxiang Qi) was also initiated with the help of Dr. Qianqian Ding. Therefore, this project has allowed the training of several postgraduate students.

14120820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120820.value: Since this project has revealed the importance of mitochondrial biogenesis in the maturation of ESC-CMs, another project related to mitochondrial transcription factors (which are important for the transcription of mitochondrial DNA-encoded genes and thereby are important for mitochondrial biogenesis) was also initiated. In the latter project, the role of mitochondrial transcription factor A, mitochondrial transcription factor B1, and mitochondrial transcription factor B2 in the maturation of ESC-CMs was investigated. We are currently in the process of elucidating the mechanisms underlying the effects of these mitochondrial transcriptional factors.

14120820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120820.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. However, in the conventional differentiation protocol of ESCs, ESC-derived cardiomyocytes are not mature. The maturation process must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. In this project, a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiology and genetic manipulation techniques were employed to investigate the role of transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) channels in the maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. TRPA1 channels were found to be important for the structural, functional and metabolic maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. TRPA1 regulates the maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes by increasing mitochondrial biogenesis and by altering mitochondrial dynamics towards fusion. Detailed mechanisms of how TRPA1 channels exert their effects were also elucidated in this study. This project has generated novel and important information on the role of TRPA1 in regulating the maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. Altogether, this project is crucial for understanding the complex developmental biology of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes and is pivotal for revealing the therapeutic potentials of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes.

14121520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121520.value: Over 14 million people currently suffer from cancer. Treatment options involve the use of chemotherapeutic drugs and/or radiation therapy. During treatment, the patient may experience unwanted side effects that may compromise treatment strategies, delay potential life-saving treatment, and reduce quality of life measures. In recent years, the central pathways mediating nausea and emesis have received considerable attention, but pathways and mechanisms arising from the periphery have not. Drugs targeted to the level of the brainstem may not necessarily prevent those mechanisms perturbed in the gastrointestinal tract. Gastric myoelectrical activity (GMA) comprises low-frequency slow waves and neuronal spike activity. Gastroenterologists use electrogastrography, a technique in which electrodes are placed on the skin above the stomach, to investigate abnormalities in gastric slow waves. However, this approach only permits short recording periods. For long erm recordings, we developed a radiotelemetric recording techniques to study GMA, where electrodes are surgically implanted directly into the antrum of the stomach. This revealed that cisplatin increased the dominant frequency of slow waves and decreased the dominant power (DP) during acute emesis. There was a reduction of DP during delayed emesis, where normogastria predominated. Using advanced statistical techniques, we showed that the slow wave signal shape (SWSS) became significantly more simplistic. Cisplatin caused a change in the shape of the current, which indicates that ion channels may have been affected. The mechanism of action of cisplatin to simplify SWSS is unknown. However, clues from the cardiac myometrium reveal that cisplatin affects sodium NAV1.5 channels. These channels are also present in ICC and are responsible for the majority of the rising current. It is possible that cisplatin treatment has actions toxic actions on ICCs via these channels. If we block these channels when plasma levels of cisplatin are high, we may prevent the changes in SWSS and reduce nausea and emesis. In the present investigations, we aim to determine if the NAV1.5 channel blocker, flecainide, can be used to protect ICCs against cisplatin, whilst also reducing ‘nausea’ and emesis. Comparative studies will be done with standard antiemetics. Our studies may uncover a novel mechanism to restore power SWSS to reduce the side effects of chemotherapeutic challenges leading to an improved outcome of cancer treatment. Given that flecainide is already in man, repurposing it as an anti-emetic, or adjunct, should be relatively straightforward pending the outcome of the proposed studies. 當前有超過一千四百萬人患有癌症，化學療法藥物和/或放射療法的使用是 是癌症治療的常用手段。然而，在利用這些治療手段進行治療的過程中，患者可能會遇到不良的副作用，這些副作用可能會損害治療策略，延遲潛在的挽救生命的治療並降低 患者的生活質量措施。 近年來，介導噁心和嘔吐的中樞途徑已受到相當多的關注，但由外周產生的途徑和機制尚未引起重視。針對腦乾水平的藥物不一定能預防胃腸道中的這些作用機制。胃肌電活動（Gastric myoelectric activity, GMA）是包括由Cajal間質細胞（interstitial cells of Cajal, ICC）和神經元活動產生的低頻慢波。胃腸病學家使用胃電描記法（一種將電極放置在胃上方皮膚上的記錄技術）來研究與噁心和嘔吐相關的胃慢波異常。但是，這種方法僅允許較短的時間記錄。對於長期記錄，我們開發了一種無線電遙測記錄技術（將電極直接通過外科手術植入胃竇）來研究胃GMA。我們的研究發現在急性嘔吐過程中，順鉑增加了慢波的主頻，並降低了主頻功率（dominant power, DP）。在嘔吐延遲期間，DP進一步降低, 而慢波的主頻以處於正常的範圍。使用先進的統計方法，我們發現慢波信號形狀（slow wave signal shape， SWSS）變得更加簡單。順鉑處理能夠明顯的引起肌電信號形狀的改變，這表明ICC的離子通道和細胞功能可能已受到影響。 順鉑簡化SWSS的作用機制尚不清楚。目前尚不明確目前的止吐藥是否能阻止順鉑引起的SWSS變化。但是，有證據表明順鉑影響心臟肌膜層的鈉NAV1.5通道。這些通道也存在於ICC中，並參與形成大部分上升電流。我們的研究假設是，順鉑可能通過這些途徑對ICC產生毒性作用，從而影響SWSS。我們擁有的科學方法是阻止這些通道，以 阻止順鉑的毒性和SWSS的變化以減少噁心和嘔吐。我們將會使用已經在人中用於治療心律不齊的NAV1.5通道阻滯劑flecainide以實現這一主要目標。 本研究將確定flecainide是否可以預防順鉑引起的SWSS改變，以及這種方法是否具有減輕嘔吐和噁心相關的生理參數變化的能力。在實驗過程中，我們還將確定順鉑誘導的SWSS變化是否對止吐藥palonosetron，netupitant和輔助藥dexamethasone敏感。我們的研究可能會發現一種新穎的機制，以恢復SWSS的功能，減少化療挑戰帶來的副作用，從而改善癌症治療的效果。從雪貂模型產生的數據在產業界已證明具有明顯的轉化價值，從而導致工業界決定將新化合物引入人類。flecainide已應用於人體內，因此在擬議的研究結果出台之前，將其重新用作止吐藥或輔助藥應該相對簡單。

14121720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121720.value: The primary aim of this pragmatic, randomized controlled trial is to determine the effectiveness of colchicine, given 4 hours before and continuing for the first 10 postoperative days, to prevent perioperative atrial fibrillation in patients receiving major noncardiac thoracic surgery. Perioperative atrial fibrillation is one of the most common and serious complications after thoracic surgery. In previous randomized trials and prospective observational studies, we found that perioperative atrial fibrillation affects up to 20% of patients having major thoracic surgery, and is associated with increased risk of death, stroke and prolonged hospital stay. Therefore, the search for an effective, safe and inexpensive intervention to prevent postoperative atrial fibrillation is a priority for research in contemporary thoracic surgical practice. The development of atrial fibrillation is tightly linked with perioperative inflammation. Colchicine blocks leukocyte mitosis and inhibits granulocyte activation and may therefore reduce the risk of perioperative atrial fibrillation. In open-heart surgery, colchicine decreased the risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation (3 trials, n=912), pooled relative risk reduction (95% confidence intervals): 35.2 (9.6-53.5)%, p=0.011. Although these results are encouraging, they cannot be extrapolated directly to noncardiac thoracic surgery. We therefore proposed to conduct an international, randomized, pragmatic trial to compare the effect of colchicine with matching placebo on perioperative atrial fibrillation in 2,800 patients having major thoracic surgery. Our secondary goals are to determine the effect of colchicine on myocardial injury, perioperative strokes, hospital stay and quality of recovery. Four hundred patients will be recruited in Hong Kong, and the requested funding is being sought to support local contribution to the trial. We anticipate the findings of this study will have considerable scientific, social and economic significance. Given that over 5 million of patients are having thoracic surgery worldwide every year, an effective strategy to prevent perioperative atrial fibrillation would spare millions of patients from the distress of devastating vascular complications, life-long anticoagulation and repeat monitoring. As colchicine is widely available, a positive finding could also be readily translated into perioperative medicine practice. 是次隨機對照研究的主要目標是確定胸科手術患者在術前4小時及術後10天內，連續服食癒風錠對預防圍術期心房纖顫的有效性。 圍術期心房纖顫是病人進行胸科手術後其中一個最常見和嚴重的併發症。在過去的隨機對照試驗和前瞻性觀察研究中，我們發現有 20% 的病人在胸外科手術後會發生心房纖顫，並因而有可能增加死亡、中風的風險，或延長住院時間。所以，尋找一個有效，安全及低成本的治療方案以預防圍術期心房纖顫是現代胸外科實踐研究的重點。 心房顫動與圍手術期身體發生炎症有密切關係。癒風錠 (Colchicine) 能夠阻截白血球的有絲分裂和抑制粒細胞活化，從而有可能降低手術後發生心房顫動的風險。在開胸心臟手術中，癒風錠 (Colchicine) 能減少手術後發生心房顫動的風險 (3個醫學臨床試驗，n = 912) ，並降低匯聚的相對風險 (95% 置信區間)：35.2 (9.6-53.5)%, p=0.011。儘管這些結果令人鼓舞，它們不能直接外推至非心臟胸外科手術中。 有見及此，我們建議展開一個國際性、隨機對照研究。通過招募2800名進行胸科手術的病人參與是次研究，以比較安慰劑和癒風錠在預防圍術期心房纖顫的有效性。我們的另一個目標是確定癒風錠對預防心肌損傷、減少圍術期中風、縮短住院時間和提升康復質量的有效性。我們計劃在香港招募400名病人參與此項研究，而所申請的資金將用於支持本地參與此研究。 我們預期是次研究的結果將具有重大的科學、社會和經濟意義。由於每年全球有超過500萬人進行胸外科手術，一個有效預防圍術期心房纖顫的策略因而可讓數百萬名患者免受壞性血管併發症、終生抗凝治療及和重複監測的困擾。亦由於癒風錠能容易獲取，一個正面的研究結果可被轉化應用於圍術期的醫療實踐。

14121720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121720.value: Higher levels of inflammatory biomarkers have been associated with an increased risk of perioperative AF (POAF) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS). Colchicine exerts anti-inflammatory effects and may therefore reduce perioperative complications. In the COP-AF trial, a total of 3,209 patients having major noncardiac thoracic surgery were recruited. Patients were randomized to receive colchicine 1 mg per day or matching placebo, starting 4 hours before and continued for 10 days after surgery. During 14 days postoperative follow-up, the composite outcome of clinically important POAF, and MINS occurred in 22.4% patients in the colchicine group and in 25.9% patients in the placebo group (HR 0.84; 95%CI 0.73-0.97). Colchicine, compared with placebo, however did not affect POAF (6.3% vs 7.4%; HR (95%CI): 0.84 (0.64-1.09), p=0.19) or MINS (18.0% vs 20.3%; HR (95%CI): 0.87 (0.74-1.02), p=0.09. alone. As a post-hoc analysis, colchicine also significantly reduced the composite of vascular death, non-fatal MINS, non-fatal stroke, or clinically important POAF (HR (95%CI): 0.83(0.72-0.96)). Non-infectious diarrhoea was more common in colchicine group than placebo group (8.3% vs 2.4%; HR (95%CI): 3.64 (2.54-5.22). Colchicine had no significant effect on sepsis, infection, all-cause mortality, acute heart failure, number of days alive and at home, life-threatening or major bleeding.

14121720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121720.value: Adverse cardiovascular events continue to be among the most common complications for patients undergoing noncardiac surgery, and they are associated with a poor prognosis. In COP-AF, colchicine reduced the risk of adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease. COP-AF also demonstrated a promising signal among patients undergoing thoracic surgery. No major safety signal emerged from these trials. Based on these data, colchicine has the potential to safely reduce the risk of ischemic cardiovascular outcomes in at risk patients having boarder noncardiac surgery. We are planning a large randomized controlled trial to examine the cardioprotective effects of colchicine (POISE-4 Trial).

14121720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121720.value: Perioperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) are common complications after noncardiac thoracic surgery, and affected patients have a worse prognosis. Colchicine is an established anti-inflammatory drug that may decrease inflammatory response, POAF and MINS. We conducted the largest randomised trial so far to assess the efficacy and safety of colchicine daily in patients undergoing major noncardiac thoracic surgery. Colchicine reduced POAF and MINS. Colchicine however, increased the risk of non-infectious diarrhoea, but not sepsis or infection. These potential benefits of colchicine on POAF and MINS are in line with previous studies in patients with coronary artery disease. Future studies should further investigate the role of colchicine in the prevention of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients undergoing border types of surgery.

14200120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200120.value: The aim of this project is to conduct multi-scale studies to comprehensively improve our understandings of the in-situ discharge behaviors observed in the triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) and to develop discharge-based practical applications of TENGs. Given the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence and smart cities, and their subsequent requirements for energy, an urgency has been developed in research to identify sustainable power sources. TENG is a cutting-edge technology that can harvest ambient mechanical energy – which is available ubiquitously in various forms regardless of location, time, and weather – and convert it to electricity. Previous research in TENG technology has focused on the electrical output, with minimal studies regarding in-situ discharge and whether it can be productively harnessed. An objective and controlled evaluation of in-situ discharge behaviors will not only contribute to our ever-growing knowledge base on the fundamentals of TENG technology, but may also provide a breakthrough enabling novel applications of TENGs. These proposed studies are therefore imperative in both fundamental and practical contexts, to further the development and applications of TENGs. Through theoretical simulations and experiments, this project is designed to conduct multi-scale studies of the in-situ discharge behaviors observed in TENGs to collect fundamental data to be used in developing related applications. We will explore the following components: the characterization of the discharge behaviors of TENGs; the repeatability of in-situ discharge, the optimization strategies and the resulting applications. Research will be conducted in four phases. First, theoretical models will be established and simulated. Next, we will develop experimental platform and methods for characterizing discharge behaviors. Then, TENGs will be adjusted to optimize the discharge behaviors to encourage increased repeatability. Lastly, novel applications for the TENG such as a motion sensor and an ionization source will be demonstrated. The findings of this study will be of considerable value in terms of both fundamental studies and practical applications. This proposed research will represent the first study of its kind that systematically examines in-situ discharge behaviors in TENGs by theoretical and experimental approaches, and the findings will greatly improve our understandings on the in-situ discharge in TENGs. The study will also significantly contribute to the paradigm-shift strategy regarding applications for TENGs that operate using the discharge phenomena. The data resulting from our work will be of interest to scholars in various research fields including energy harvesting, sensing, electrostatic discharge, high-voltage applications, and chemical analysis. 本項目旨在進行多方位的研究，以全面提高我們對摩擦納米發電機(TENG)的原位放電行為的認識，並發展TENG基於放電的應用。 隨著物聯網、人工智慧和智慧城市的快速發展，大量相關設備的能源需求加大了開發可持續能源的緊迫性。TENG是一種可以收集無處不在的各種形式環境機械能並轉化為電能的尖端技術，且不受地點、時間和天氣的影響。然而，以往對TENG的研究僅集中在電力輸出方面，對TENG內部放電及其相關應用的研究較少。對放電行為的研究不僅可以從根本上改變對TENG的理解，而且可以利用這種放電行爲產生新的應用。因此，本文所提出的研究無論在理論意義上還是實踐意義上都是迫切需要的。 本項目擬通過理論模擬和實驗，對TENG的放電行為進行多尺度研究，並開發相關應用。我們的研究包括以下幾個方面：TENG的原位放電行為及其表徵方法；放電的可重複性及優化方法；以及潛在的應用。我們將分四個階段進行研究。首先，開發放電行為表徵平臺。接下來，我們將發展放電行為的相關理論和實驗表徵方法。然後將優化TENG原位放電行為，提高可重複性。最後，新的應用，如運動傳感器和電離源將被演示，用於發展一套自供電、便攜、安全的系統。 本研究的結果將在基礎研究和實際應用方面具有相當大的價值。本研究將是首次從理論和實驗兩方面系統性的對TENG放電行為進行研究，將極大地提高我們對TENG放電的認識。這項研究也將極大地促進利用放電現象應用TENG的範式轉變策略，其研究結果將引起各個研究領域包括能量收集、傳感、靜電放電、高壓應用和化學分析相關學者的興趣。

14200120.label: Realisation of objectives
14200120.value: All objectives have been achieved. Details are stated below: Objective 1 was fully completed before the midterm, so the activities have been reported in the midterm report. Objective 2 was completed by 70% in the previous report. During this reporting period, we have systematically studied electrical and optical emission behaviors of discharges, including emission spectra, discharge images, wired and wireless electrical signals, which are affected by gas species and pressure. We studied discharge behaviors in air, 4 pure gases (He, Ar, N2, CO2) and their mix, with varied pressure. By means of machine learning, the optical emission signals process the ability to recognize 60 gas atmospheres simultaneously, with an accuracy of 97.67%. With the assistance of the mobile phone or closed-circuit television, a self-powered gas sensing system based on TD may serve as a portable detecting device and a vital component of the Internet of Things system. With deep learning analysis on the wired and wireless signals, it can recognize up to 60 different types of gas atmospheres with 93.8% accuracy, including 5 gas components with 12 different gas pressures. The system with a visualization program is designed for wireless, real-time gas monitoring toward applications in health monitoring, precise manufacturing, and high-tech fire rescue operations. These study results were published as Advanced Optical Materials 11 (9), 2202697, 2023 and Nano Energy 121, 109156, 2024. Objective 3 was completed by 30% in the previous report. In that report we have developed a modified TENG device named “self-powered wireless sensing e-sticker” (SWISE) to generate self-powered wireless signals through the discharge effect. To develop SWISE to be self-powered wireless sensing platform, we need to redesign it to ensure a low threshold voltage, high charge output, and high repeatability. We package the discharge structure in a sealed environment with low-pressure Ar inside, which has been proved in our study in objective 2 to lower the threshold voltage. The oil-solid surface was used to suppress triboelectric discharge on the surface, so that the charge can be accumulated to a higher level, and repeatable discharge in the discharger location. Eventually, we achieved very low threshold voltages of down to 70 V, high charge output of up to 800 nC, with high repeatability of >99.2%, which satisfy the original objectives. The study has been published in Small Methods 2301670, 2024; Device 1 (6), 2023; Nano Energy 105, 107982, 2023. Objective 4 was completed by 50% in the previous report. In that, the SWISE was demonstrated as a motion sensor and a gas sensor based on the ionization of the gas molecules during discharge. In this report, the advantages of the SWISE platform, as the TENG-based in-situ discharger, have been demonstrated, since it is fully self-powered and can be combined with many existing sensing technologies to make it self-powered and wireless. The additional demonstrated functions include sensing temperature, humidity, flow rate, as well as metal detection. These results have been reported in papers listed for objective 3.

14200120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200120.value: (1) Outcome 1: developed theoretical models and simulated in-situ discharge behaviors of basic-mode TENGs. The theoretical models of the in-situ discharge of triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) were established using COMSOL Multiphysics software, and simulated. The results showed that sliding freestanding (SFT) and contact-separation (CS) modes TENGs demonstrate the highest breakdown voltage and lowest breakdown charge density. And their discharge intensity is relatively high. SFT mode TENG can involve discharge in both air and dielectric, which is preferred to study multiple types of discharge. We discovered the time-lag behaviors of discharge, which was published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 14 (39), 44398-44404. Therefore, in the following experiments, we mainly used SFT mode TENGs for discharge generation and characterization. (2) Outcome 2: developed the characterization platform and experimental methods for discharge behaviors, characterized TENGs using the developed experimental methods. We have developed the characterization platform including the electrical measurement system, the optical observation instrument, and a glove box. In this setup, the test TENG was set in a sealed chamber (as plotted in two triangle shapes to illustrate their discharge function). The gas to be filled in the chamber includes air, Ar, CO2, He, and N2. We characterized discharge characteristics from CS and SFT modes TENGs. The discharge sparks were recorded and the electrical data was recorded to determine the discharge points. The generated wireless signals were also recorded and carefully compared. In the meanwhile, we also studied different discharge behaviors under different gas environments. The different plasma and discharge patterns with varied colors were recorded. These study results were published as Advanced Optical Materials 11 (9), 2202697, 2023 and Nano Energy 121, 109156, 2024. (3) Outcome 3: optimized TENG designs to encourage repeatable discharge behaviors through optimizations of structure design, materials/surfaces, and gas medium. To achieve repeatable discharge behaviors, the modified TENG device named “self-powered wireless sensing e-sticker” (SWISE) is rationally designed, where two mirrored symmetric metal electrodes with sharp tips for discharge were sandwiched between a substrate film polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and a tribo-charge layer film made from fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP). The SWISE has been redesigned as a self-powered wireless sensing platform, with very low threshold voltages of down to 70 V, high charge output of up to 800 nC, with high repeatability of >99.2%, which satisfies the original objectives. The study has been published in Small Methods 2301670, 2024; Device 1 (6), 2023; Nano Energy 105, 107982, 2023 (4) Outcome 4: developed novel in-situ discharge based TENG applications We have developed the well-designed SWISE to work as sensors for motion, gas, temperature, humidity, flow rate, as well as metal detection. It can also work as an ionization source to generate plasma for visible wireless sensing. The studies were published in papers mentioned for outcome 3.

14200120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200120.value: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things toward the 4th industrial revolution, trillions of widely-distributed devices are implemented in every corner of the world. Powering these large-quantity mobile devices, especially wireless sensors becomes a huge issue. Using the batteries to power them brings demands of regular replacement and maintenance, while the cable connections are not preferred for wireless devices. The newly invented SWISE provides a new potential solution toward self-powered wireless sensors. The SWISE obtains energy from triboelectricity and provides the wireless solution through triboelectric discharge. We believe this new technology will initiate applications of varied types of self-powered wireless sensors used in human-machine interfaces, health monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, etc. In light of that, we propose to increase the efforts on the research and development of this new self-powered wireless sensing technology, and develop products for applications in wearable systems, robotic systems, infrastructure, etc. Considering the commercialization needs and the demands on sustainable development, evaluations of this new technology on carbon footprint and economic aspects are required to understand the commercial potential and its contributions to carbon neutrality. Related financial support from funding bodies such as innovation and technology commissions is needed to develop technological know-how, address the issues of long-term stabilities, and reduce prices.

14200120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200120.value: This project is about fundamental studies on in-situ discharge behaviors in triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), including theoretical simulations to experimental results. With that, we have demonstrated a revised design for TENG toward repeatable discharge for applications in wireless sensing, etc. The results of this study will be very important for both basic research and real-world applications. This research will be the first of its kind to carefully look at how TENGs release energy in real time, using both theoretical and experimental methods. The findings will greatly enhance our understanding of how TENGs discharge energy. Additionally, this study will play a key role in changing how we think about using TENGs that rely on this energy release. The data we gather will interest researchers in various fields, including energy harvesting, sensors, electrostatic discharge, high-voltage applications, and chemical analysis.

14200220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200220.value: 自動識別構音障礙語音的深度學習架構

14200220.label: Project Objectives
14200220.value: Auto-configured deep acoustic models for limited disordered speech A key problem in disordered speech recognition is the difficulty of collecting large amounts of impaired speech. The resulting data sparsity issue presents a fundamental challenge: how to optimize the trade-off between model complexity and accuracy performance when designing ASR systems using data intensive deep learning technologies on limited dysarthric speech data? A range of neural network structure design decisions over the suitable network topology, number of hidden nodes, connectivity and the choice of hidden activations need to be made. Due to a general lack of well-established model selection methods for neural networks, these design decisions are largely empirically based in current speech recognition systems. In the machine learning community, this problem also remains an active research topic to date. In order to solve this problem, the proposed novel auto-configured deep neural networks not only allow a wide range of neural structural configurations to be considered, but also jointly models the uncertainty over both the network architectures and their parameters consistently under the same framework. This allows the performance rank ordering of a large number of candidate neural architectures, without the need of training them individually, to be accurately predicted for fast and automatic deep model selection. This research is expected to be the first to apply automated DNN design to speech recognition tasks. Learning speech impairment invariant features The large mismatch between normal and impaired speech is another main contributor to the difficulty in disordered speech recognition. The proposed disorder invariant feature learning methods can connect normal and disordered speech data at feature representation level. First, the conversion from normal speech to disordered speech features also serves as an effective data augmentation method. This can help to expand the limited disordered speech available for ASR system development, thus help alleviate the above data sparsity issue. Second, this also allows state-of-the-art ASR systems constructed using large amounts of healthy speaker’s data to be rapidly deployable for recognition of impaired speech, without the need of redeveloping systems from scratch. Deep model adaptation to speaker and impairment dependent characteristics The large variation among impaired speakers originates from their diverse vocal characteristics, types of speech disorder, and varying stages of medical condition progression. The proposed novel adaptation methods can provide both rapid and longitudinal adaptation to the above mentioned speaker and impairment variabilities. These techniques allow systems to exploit the commonalities among multiple speakers’ speech of similar impairment characteristics to facilitate data sharing, and to improve modelling robustness, generalization and coverage. They also allow speaker dependent systems to rapidly adapted to individual speakers’ voice characteristics at the onset of user enrollment with very limited data, as well as subsequent changes of their voice over a longer time if the underlying speech disorder progresses. Such user-centric adaptation features are crucial for speech based conversational systems in commercial applications to ensure a high level user satisfaction from impaired speakers. Developing exemplar systems and recipes for disordered speech recognition Exemplar systems and recipes developed on publicly available disordered speech data sets provide rapid pathways to disseminate our research outputs and deliver impact within the speech technology community and beyond. Such efforts can provide insights on how to design ASR systems that are tailored for accurate recognition of disordered speech in commercial applications. This can allow commercial product systems’ wider deployment with the support of natural and user-centered speech based assistive technologies, and to enhance quality of life, social inclusion and cost-effectiveness of care for all those living with speech impairments. The developed exemplar systems will also be made available to people with speech disorders. This allows the further collection of more disordered speech data to support future research and development.
rows: Auto-configured deep acoustic models for limited disordered speech A key problem in disordered speech recognition is the difficulty of collecting large amounts of impaired speech. The resulting data sparsity issue presents a fundamental challenge: how to optimize the trade-off between model complexity and accuracy performance when designing ASR systems using data intensive deep learning technologies on limited dysarthric speech data? A range of neural network structure design decisions over the suitable network topology, number of hidden nodes, connectivity and the choice of hidden activations need to be made. Due to a general lack of well-established model selection methods for neural networks, these design decisions are largely empirically based in current speech recognition systems. In the machine learning community, this problem also remains an active research topic to date. In order to solve this problem, the proposed novel auto-configured deep neural networks not only allow a wide range of neural structural configurations to be considered, but also jointly models the uncertainty over both the network architectures and their parameters consistently under the same framework. This allows the performance rank ordering of a large number of candidate neural architectures, without the need of training them individually, to be accurately predicted for fast and automatic deep model selection. This research is expected to be the first to apply automated DNN design to speech recognition tasks.

Learning speech impairment invariant features The large mismatch between normal and impaired speech is another main contributor to the difficulty in disordered speech recognition. The proposed disorder invariant feature learning methods can connect normal and disordered speech data at feature representation level. First, the conversion from normal speech to disordered speech features also serves as an effective data augmentation method. This can help to expand the limited disordered speech available for ASR system development, thus help alleviate the above data sparsity issue. Second, this also allows state-of-the-art ASR systems constructed using large amounts of healthy speaker’s data to be rapidly deployable for recognition of impaired speech, without the need of redeveloping systems from scratch.

Deep model adaptation to speaker and impairment dependent characteristics The large variation among impaired speakers originates from their diverse vocal characteristics, types of speech disorder, and varying stages of medical condition progression. The proposed novel adaptation methods can provide both rapid and longitudinal adaptation to the above mentioned speaker and impairment variabilities. These techniques allow systems to exploit the commonalities among multiple speakers’ speech of similar impairment characteristics to facilitate data sharing, and to improve modelling robustness, generalization and coverage. They also allow speaker dependent systems to rapidly adapted to individual speakers’ voice characteristics at the onset of user enrollment with very limited data, as well as subsequent changes of their voice over a longer time if the underlying speech disorder progresses. Such user-centric adaptation features are crucial for speech based conversational systems in commercial applications to ensure a high level user satisfaction from impaired speakers.

This can allow commercial product systems’ wider deployment with the support of natural and user-centered speech based assistive technologies, and to enhance quality of life, social inclusion and cost-effectiveness of care for all those living with speech impairments. The developed exemplar systems will also be made available to people with speech disorders. This allows the further collection of more disordered speech data to support future research and development.

14200220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200220.value: Dysarthria is a common form of speech disorder that refers to neuro-motor problems leading to weakness or paralysis of muscles used in articulation. Its causes include neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) or cerebral palsy, and brain damages due to stroke or head injuries. Dysarthria leads to low intelligibility of the resulting speech for human listeners. This makes current automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems designed for normal speech unsuitable to be used to recognize such data. In the speech technology industry, apart from Google’s recent efforts on ASR technologies for ALS speakers, there is very limited research providing more general solutions to disordered speech recognition. Speech disorders particularly affect the elderly. The Hong Kong population are ageing rapidly. The number of people who suffer from speech disorder is expected to further increase. People with speech disorders often have physical disabilities and other co-occurring conditions that make them rely on care. The difficulty of such people in using keyboard, mouse and touch screen based interfaces makes voice control a more natural alternative. Speech driven assistive technologies can allow such people to live more independently and to reduce the cost of care for their families and the society. Hence, there is a pressing need to develop new technologies for disordered speech recognition. By building on our previous research producing the best published recognition performance on the UASpeech dysarthric English corpus, this project aims to derive novel ASR technologies that are tailor designed for disordered Cantonese and English speech recognition. These include auto-configured deep acoustic models that can robustly model limited disordered speech; neural network architectures learning speech disorder invariant and restoration features; model adaptation techniques to handle speaker and impairment dependent characteristics; and learning disordered pronunciation variants. We will cater for the need of the Cantonese speaking population with speech disorder in Hong Kong and neighboring Chinese provinces. Exemplar systems and recipes will be developed and made publicly available to provide insights on how to design state-of-the-art disordered speech recognition systems for commercial applications. The outcomes of this research allow people suffering from speech disorders to communicate more easily and naturally with the outside world. We will focus on Cantonese and English as an initial step. 14200220.label: Realisation of objectives
14200220.value: 1. Auto-configured deep acoustic models for limited disordered speech have been achieved using neural architecture search (NAS) approaches that can automatically adjust the trade-off between modelling complexity and generalization for dysarthric speech recognition tasks that are by nature data resource constrained. These approaches have been successfully applied to both: a) hybrid LF-MMI TDNN based ASR models (Shoukang Hu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2022, Shoukang Hu et al. IEEE ICASSP2021, Shansong Liu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2021, Jiajun Deng et al. ISCA Interspeech2021); and b) end-to-end Conformer AED based ASR models (Tianzi Wang et al. ISCA Interspeech2023). 2. Learning speech impairment invariant features have been achieved on the following fronts: a) SVD based speech spectrum decomposition approaches are used to disentangle the spectral basis features (that are more time-invariant and dysarthric speakers’ voice characteristics dependent) from the temporal basis features (that are more speech content dependent). These are further exploited for: i) performance-effective and data-efficient ASR models adaption to diverse dysarthric speakers (Mengzhe Geng et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2022, Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2021, Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2023a); and ii) GAN based personalized dysarthric speaker data augmentation approaches that can flexibly operate on non-parallel (control versus dysarthric or elderly) speech data (Zengrui Jin et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2024, Zengrui Jin et al. ISCA Interspeech2021); b) Articulatory features that are more speech impairment invariant, together with the required acoustic to articulatory inversion approaches for their practical application to audio-only speech datasets, are integrated into TDNN, Conformer and speech foundation models based ASR systems to improve their performance on dysarthric speech (Shujie Hu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2024, Shujie Hu et al. IEEE ICASSP2023, Zengrui Jin et al. IEEE ICASSP2023); c) state-of-the-art foundation models and their extracted speech features that are more domain invariant and task agnostic have also be successfully applied to improve dysarthric speech recognition performance (Shujie Hu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2024, Shujie Hu et al. IEEE ICASSP2023, Zengrui Jin et al. IEEE ICASSP2023, Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2023b). 3. Deep model adaptation to speaker and impairment dependent characteristics have been achieved on the following fronts: a) Considering the differences between impaired and normal speech, e.g. reduced speech clarity and volume, slower speaking rate, articulatory imprecision and increased dysfluencies, spectro-temporal neural features based dysarthric speaker adaptation approaches were developed for hybrid DNN/TDNN and Conformer end-to-end ASR systems. Experiments conducted on the English UASpeech and TORGO dysarthric speech; the English DementiaBank Pitt and Cantonese JCCOCC MoCA elderly speech suggest the spectro-temporal deep features based speaker adaptation outperformed i-Vector and x-Vector adaptation by statistically significant WER reductions up to 2.63% absolute (8.63% relative). These gains were also found to be additive to those obtained using model based LHUC speaker adaptation (Mengzhe Geng et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2022, Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2021). More data-efficient on-the-fly dysarthric speaker adaptation approaches using speaker-level variance regularized spectral neural embedding features have also been developed (Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2023a). b) More fine-grained dysarthric speaker adaptation approaches that account for both speaker-identity and speech impairment severity using: i) multitask training incorporating the additional speech impairment severity prediction error; ii) speaker-severity aware auxiliary feature adaptation; and iii) structured speaker-severity transforms. Experiments on the UASpeech dysarthric speech data suggest incorporating speech impairment severity into hybrid DNN, E2E Conformer and domain fine-tuned Wav2vec2.0 ASR systems produced statistically significant WER reductions of 4.78% absolute (14.03% relative). The lowest WER of 17.82% (51.25% and 17.41% on Very Low and Low intelligibility) was also obtained on the UASpeech test set (Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2023b). 4. Developing exemplar systems and recipes for disordered speech recognition: Our published IEEE/ACM TALSP journal article (Shansong Liu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2021) presents our exemplar system development efforts on the largest publicly available UASpeech dysarthric speech corpus. A set of modelling techniques including neural architectural search, data augmentation using spectra-temporal perturbation, model based speaker adaptation and cross-domain generation of visual features within an audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR) system framework were employed to address the above challenges. The combination of these techniques produced the lowest published word error rate (WER) of 25.21% on the UASpeech test set 16 dysarthric speakers, and an overall WER reduction of 5.4% absolute (17.6% relative) over the CUHK 2018 dysarthric speech recognition system featuring a 6-way DNN system combination and cross adaptation of out-of-domain normal speech data trained systems. Bayesian model adaptation further allows rapid adaptation to individual dysarthric speakers to be performed using as little as 3.06 seconds of speech. The efficacy of these techniques were further demonstrated on a CUDYS Cantonese dysarthric speech recognition task. More recent update of our systems involves incorporating speech foundation models and their features as well as ultra-sound tongue imaging (UTI) articulatory features (Shujie Hu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2024) and their speech impairment aware adaptation (Mengzhe Geng et al. ISCA Interspeech2023b).

14200220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200220.value: Speech disorders such as dysarthria affect millions around the world. They are often found the elderly adults. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) technologies tailored for these users can help improve their quality of life and social inclusion. Efforts on developing dysarthric speech recognition technologies are confronted by the data scarcity, large mismatch against normal speech and speaker level diversity associated with such data. To this end, in this project we have developed a range of technology solutions addressing these challenges: 1) neural architecture search (NAS) based auto-configured deep acoustic models that can automatically adjust the trade-off between modelling complexity and generalization for dysarthric speech recognition systems; 2) speech impairment invariant features that are based on time-invariant and dysarthric dependent spectral basis features, video lip or ultra-sound tongue imaging based articulatory features, and speech foundation models extracted features that are inherently more domain invariant and task agnostic; 3) performance-effective and data-efficient adaptation to speaker and impairment dependent characteristics using speaker-level spectro-temporal basis embedding features and more fine-grained speaker identity plus impairment severity aware adaptation approaches; and 4) development of exemplar speech recognition systems and recipes on the largest publicly available dysarthric speech corpora including UASpeech and TORGO. The efficacy of our approaches are demonstrated in a series of state-of-the-art speech recognition accuracy results that have been published on benchmark dysarthric speech datasets. The research efforts under this project have led to a total of 16 publications. These include 5 journal articles and 11 conference papers, all of which are published at top tier speech technology venues such as IEEE/ACM TASLP, IEEE ICASSP and ISCA Interspeech.

14200220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200220.value: Further development of the research work conducted under this project has led to a following up RGC funded research project on high-performance and data-efficient on-the-fly dysarthric and elderly speaker adaptation approaches for pre-trained ASR systems.

14200420.label: Project Objectives
14200420.value: MOTIVATION: Community exploration (CE) is a fundamental problem and is a flexible abstraction to model real-world applications. The goal of CE is to obtain as much reward as possible under an exploration budget constraint. CE can be informally described by the following hypothetical scenario: Alice wants to meet as many new friends as possible when she enters a university which has many student clubs (communities). Suppose Alice only has limited time to explore each community, then how should she allocate her time to maximize the total number of ``new friends'' she could meet. One can extend this to many real-world applications: 1) Data collection in data mining area: A researcher wants to crawl a number of online social networks(OSNs) so to get as many new data as possible. She has a limited budget and needs to allocate it to crawl different OSNs. One may allocate more budget to large-sized OSNs, but this may increase crawling duplicated data. So how to allocate crawling budget to each OSN to maximize the total amount of new data collection? (2) Social advertising in OSNs: An advertiser wants to promote a new product via different OSN platforms. One way is to offer incentives (e.g, coupons/discounts) to random chosen users in each OSN, which is modeled as a community. The question is how to allocate a given budget to make the advertisement reach as many unique customers as possible via the word-of-mouth cascade? (3) device-to-device communication in wireless-networks: Assume a wireless-network coverage is divided into cells (communities) and there are many embedded/IoT devices within each cell. How to measure the number of ``unique'' D2D communication in all cells so to quantify their signal/communication strength under a measurement budget? For the CE problem, the ``community structure'' (or graph topology) and the ``exploration rules'' are two core components. Our work in[4] in the pioneering work in this direction. We proposed a simple abstraction, in which communities are modeled as disjoint sets of members. The exploration rule is to randomly and uniformly select a member in each community. That is, each exploration step is independent, identical, and one can access any member in a community with equal probability. In real world, however, these assumptions may too restrictive. In particular, if we do not have the community (or graph) topology, it is impossible to randomly and uniformly select a member. Also, in many real life applications, each exploration step may be dependent upon previous exploration steps in that community, and at each step, one can only access a small portion of members (e.g., neighbors of the previously visited member). For example, for community exploration, we usually meet a new friend by our old friends' recommendation. For data collection, OSNs operators only allow crawlers to do restrictive crawling. Therefore, to apply the CE framework to real life applications, one needs to remove the graph topology availability assumption, and consider information exploration by only random walk based sampling techniques. The objectives of our research are: To generalize our work in[4] to a setting that one does not possess the community (or graph) topologies. Instead, one has to explore the network by random walks and perform online optimization via reinforcement learning techniques. To consider the ``full-knowledge scenario'' where the community topologies are known but exploration has to be done via random walks. Through this, we seek to derive the explicit expression of cumulative regards and a greedy algorithm which can satisfy the optimality condition. This setting allows us to gain the basic understanding of the problem structure so to explore a more realistic setting, which we will describe next. In this setting, we do away with the knowledge of the community topologies, but instead ``learn'' about their structures via reinforcement techniques such as the multi-armed bandit framework. We consider series of exploration algorithms which have an attractive ``sub-linear'' regret bounds on the cumulative reward. We propose to apply our CE framework to number of important applications like: (a) Viral advertisement in online social networks, (b) traffic measurement for IoT D2D communication in wireless networks, and (c) workers selection in crowdsourcing applications. We will collaborate with our sponsors in applying our CE framework for social advertisement (with Tencent) and traffic measurement (with Huawei) in wireless networks.

We propose to apply our CE framework to number of important applications like: (a) Viral advertisement in online social networks, (b) traffic measurement for IoT D2D communication in wireless networks, and (c) workers selection in crowdsourcing applications.
We will collaborate with our sponsors in applying our CE framework for social advertisement (with Tencent) and traffic measurement (with Huawei) in wireless networks.

The goal of CE is to obtain as much reward as possible under an exploration budget constraint.
