So how to allocate crawling budget to each OSN to maximize the total amount of new data collection?

For the CE problem, the ``community structure'' (or graph topology) and the ``exploration rules'' are two core components. In real world, however, these assumptions may too restrictive. In particular, if we do not have the community (or graph) topology, it is impossible to randomly and uniformly select a member. Therefore, to apply the CE framework to real life applications, one needs to remove the graph topology availability assumption, and consider information exploration by only random walk based sampling techniques. The objectives of our research are:

To generalize our work in[4] to a setting that one does not possess the community (or graph) topologies. Instead, one has to explore the network by random walks and perform online optimization via reinforcement learning techniques.

To consider the ``full-knowledge scenario'' where the community topologies are known but exploration has to be done via random walks. Through this, we seek to derive the explicit expression of cumulative regards and a greedy algorithm which can satisfy the optimality condition. This setting allows us to gain the basic understanding of the problem structure so to explore a more realistic setting, which we will describe next.

In this setting, we do away with the knowledge of the community topologies, but instead ``learn'' about their structures via reinforcement techniques such as the multi-armed bandit framework. We consider series of exploration algorithms which have an attractive ``sub-linear'' regret bounds on the cumulative reward.

We propose to apply our CE framework to number of important applications like: (a) Viral advertisement in online social networks, (b) traffic measurement for IoT D2D communication in wireless networks, and (c) workers selection in crowdsourcing applications.
We will collaborate with our sponsors in applying our CE framework for social advertisement (with Tencent) and traffic measurement (with Huawei) in wireless networks.

14200420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200420.value: In this research. we proposed novel mathematical techniques and algorithms to carry out community exploration for many real-world applications, i.e., large scale online social networks, online advertisement in large social networks so as to create a large information cascade (e.g., many people can receive such advertisements), as well as application to large scale IoT systems wherein devices are often communicate in a D2D manner. The proposed new algorithms to "explore" information, and the algorithms can guarantee a large degree of information spreading, which is extremely useful for online advertisement. In addition, our algorithms can also performa statistical sampling and to give an accurate estimate about the amount of D2D communications in a large scale wireless networks. Note that our algorithms DO NOT need to rely of the full knowledge of the underlying network/graph topology, but instead, the algorithms use "random-walk" procedure to explore information. This is essential since one can apply our algorithm to explore any unstructured graphs. Also, by applying our exploration algorithms, one can also explore the community structure, i.e., workers and their respective association, so that one can do a better job in worker selection for crowd-sourcing systems. Last but not least, we have been collaborating with companies to explore the licensing of our software so that they can use our research results on their projects.

14200420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200420.value: Since this is a fundamental research, we only produce academic papers and software for our community exploration. Since there is no "hardware" involvement, we do not plan to apply for ITF for further improvement. However, we are currently exploring to extend our software and consider software licensing to various companies, and we may need to modify our algorithms for each company's individual needs.

14200420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200420.value: In this research, we aim to devise efficient algorithms for 'information exploration'. For example, how one can find structural information of users in online social networks. We consider to explore information such as user association, users' preferences and their likes and dislikes. This type of information exploration is specially important since one can use this information to carry out online advertisement so as to boost sales or revenues for companies. We also propose information exploration algorithms for Internet-of-things (IoTs) systems, in which there are many communication between different sensing devices. One can use our algorithms to discover the communication patters so that one can devise many network bandwidth for IoT systems so that they can be more efficient and applications running on top of these IoT systems will achieve better performance. Beside the scholarly publications, our research work can also help out high-tech. industries in Hong Kong and China.

14200620.label: Project Objectives
14200620.value: We propose a new framework for generating text responses or recommendations in response to information-seeking queries or utterances with the capability of producing tailor-made, either long or short, responses taking into consideration of different intents. The information sources are of heterogeneous nature composed of a collection of unstructured question answering (QA) forums and history conversation repository, as well as structured knowledge bases or knowledge graphs (KBs). Our proposed framework tackles the challenges by representing queries/utterances and questions in QA collections as semantic graphs. The user utterance is transformed into a semantic graph, which is utilized for coordinated retrieval of relevant questions in the QA collections. The user utterance semantic graph is also used for finding relevant entities and relations in the KBs. A knowledge-guided response template is generated. This response template is utilized by the text generation component that conducts re-writing guided by utterance intents and factual information verification. We intend to apply the proposed framework and build an intelligent information-seeking agent for E-Commerce.

14200620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200620.value: Generation of text responses for information-seeking user utterance/queries is a core technology for a wide range intelligent information agents such as question answering, personal assistant agents, information-seeking chatbots, etc. Most existing systems assume that the information source comes from existing or available historical utterance-response repositories or question-answer collections. On the other hand, some existing systems output responses or answers solely from knowledge bases typically composed of entity relation triplets. We investigate a new framework that can generate text responses from a coordinated understanding or analysis of heterogeneous information composed of both historical utterance-response repositories and knowledge bases. Such requirement poses some new research challenges. Existing state-of-the-art methods employ data-driven models which can be broadly categorized as two paradigms, namely, response retrieval approaches, and generation-based paradigm. Retrieval-based approaches can output informative and grammatical responses. However, the performance is constrained by the size and relevance of the historical or training repository. It is common to find that even the best retrieved response is not a good response. Generation-based paradigm can synthesize a new output response, which is more flexible and tailor-made. However, the quality degrades drastically when the response length is long. Another drawback is that it sometimes generates universal and uninformative responses. We propose to develop a new framework for constructing responses which are more tailor-made with the consideration of different information-seeking intents such as experience seeking, recommendations, explainable answers, etc. Different from existing approaches, our proposed framework is more robust and flexible with respect to response generation. Another characteristic is that the response is constructed via digesting heterogeneous information sources composed of unstructured QA collections, history conversation repositories, as well as structured knowledge bases (KB), which can facilitate the construction of some useful new information derive from heterogeneous sources for the output response. In contrast, existing approaches assume that the response content is retrieved from a mainly single particular type of information source. Recently several works consider knowledge bases or commonsense knowledge in conversation or dialogue systems. But their models cannot construct new responses. Another recent work has proposed a knowledge-grounded model that can condition responses based on both historical conversation data and external “facts”. However, the structure of response generation is quite limited. 文字回應生成是一項核心技術用於尋求信息的用戶話語/查詢在廣泛智能信息代理（例如問題解答，個人助理代理，尋求信息的聊天機器人等）。大多數現有系統都假定信息源來自現有或可用的話語-回應存儲庫或問答集。 另一方面，某些現有系統僅從通常由實體關係三元組組成的知識庫輸出響應或答案。我們打算研究一個新框架，該框架可以通過對由話語-回應存儲庫和知識庫組成的異構信息的協調理解或分析來生成文本回應。這種要求帶來了一些新的研究挑戰。 現有的方法採用數據驅動的模型，可以將其大致分為兩個範式，即回應檢索方法和基於生成的範式。基於檢索的方法可以輸出信息和語法回應。但是，性能受到培訓存儲庫的大小和相關性的限制。即使檢索到的最佳回應也不是一個好的回應。基於世代的範式可以合成新的輸出回應，該輸出回應更加靈活且量身定制。但是，回應句子長時，質量會急劇下降。另一個缺點是，它有時會產生普遍性和無信息的回應。我們建議開發一個新的框架來構建更個性化的回應，同時考慮到不同的信息搜索意圖，例如經驗，建議，可解釋的答案等。與現有方法不同，我們提出的框架更加高質和靈活回應生成。另一個特徵是，回應是通過消化由非結構化QA集合，歷史對話存儲庫以及結構化知識庫（KB）組成的異構信息源構建的，這些信息源可以幫助構建從異構源中獲取的一些有用的新信息，以用於輸出回應。相反，現有方法假定回應內容是從主要單一特定類型的信息源中檢索到的。近來，一些方法考慮了對話或對話系統中的知識庫或常識知識。但是他們的模型無法構建新的回應。最近有另一方向是一種基於知識的模型，該模型可以基於歷史對話數據和外部“事實”來調節回應。但是，回應生成的結構非常有限。

14200720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200720.value: Motivated by the global environmental concern, the power and transportation sectors are undergoing worldwide radical transitions to a greater reliance on renewable energy resources (such as wind and solar) and plug-in (hybrid) electric vehicles (EVs). As non-dispatchable generation, the intermittent renewable generation poses significant challenges on power system operation. The current practice of uncoordinated EV charging (i.e., EVs are continually charged whenever plugged in until they are fully charged or disconnected) cannot scale with the quickly growing EV adoption, as the simultaneous charging of many EVs will lead to severe power quality degradation and operation cost increase. As a stochastic optimal control problem, the scheduling of EV charging has been mostly explored through online optimization based approaches, mainly due to the intractability of classical dynamic programming (DP) methods for even medium-size problems (with 20 EVs). Stochastic optimal control based approaches, on the other hand, can potentially outperform optimization based counterparts, as large amount of (renewable generation and electricity price) data are becoming available for extracting probabilistic information on system uncertainties. This project will develop new methodological approaches to tackle the tractability issue of a general DP formulation that explicitly incorporates stochastic renewable generation, electricity price, and EV arrivals/departures. We will establish structural characterizations of optimal control policies, and apply them to develop new, scalable computational approaches that optimally coordinate the charging of a large number of EVs and the operation of an energy storage system to minimize the long-term expected system cost. For the coordinated charging of a large number of EVs in a power distribution network (under power flow and voltage security constraints), we propose a new methodological approach that utilizes structural characterizations of optimal control policies (e.g., optimal priority rules among multiple charging requests) to accelerate and improve (both value- and policy-based) deep reinforcement learning algorithms through significant dimensionality reduction of the action space. The broader impact of this work will be twofold. On the application side, the research will provide a set of novel control theoretic and computational tools to advance the state-of-the-art theory and practices, so as to unleash the full potential of the synergy between deferrable EV charging load and intermittent renewable generation. On the intellectual side, new knowledge on structural optimal policy characterizations (for an important class of stochastic deadline scheduling problems) and the developed new methodological approach (combining the advantages of data-driven reinforcement learning and model-based optimal policy characterization) are expected to cross-fertilize various application fields. 全球能源與運輸產業正在經歷革命性變革，對可再生能源發電和電動汽車的依賴度不斷升高。隨著電動汽車滲透率不斷提高，當下“隨到隨充”的做法不具可持續性，將造成配電網電能質量嚴重下降並影響系統穩定性。另一方面，可延遲的電動汽車充電需求與隨機可再生能源發電存在巨大協同發展潛力。由於眾所周知的維度災難，隨機可再生能源出力下大規模電動汽車的充電調度問題無法應用經典隨機最優控制方法求解。針對本項目構建的普適性的數學框架，我們將刻畫最優控制策略的結構性解析性質（如電動汽車充電需求間的優先級全排序），以降低最優策略的計算維度。基於本項目建立的最優策略解析性質，我們还將開發結合隨機最優控制與深度強化學習兩者長處的技術路線：深度強化學習算法感知外部環境（例如可再生能源出力、電力市場價格）隨機演化並決定每時刻充電總量，充電總量的分配則由最優控制策略解析性質決定。

14200720.label: Realisation of objectives
14200720.value: For deadline scheduling in heavy traffic, we established and proved the optimality of an “earlier-deadline-and-less-demand-first” (EDLDF) priority rule under arbitrary dynamics. Numerical benchmarking shows this characterization significantly enhances DRL algorithm performance by reducing the action space dimensionality (published in IEEE IoT Journal). For cases with power network and voltage security constraints, we formulated a stochastic DP framework integrating renewable generation, EV arrivals, and electricity prices to minimize long-term cost. We conjecture an optimal partial policy structure: EVs with the same deadline at the same bus should be charged toward a common remaining energy target. We integrate the optimal policy characterization into DEL algorithms for dimensionality reduction, and numerical results confirm our characterized structure greatly improves DRL performance. Future work will seek to rigorously prove its optimality. For the joint EV routing and charging scheduling problem in a multi-BSS network, we formulated a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process model. To overcome the curses of dimensionality and unknown dynamics, we innovatively proposed a Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Hypergraph Attention Actor-Critic framework. This framework enhances multi-agent deep reinforcement learning efficiency using hypergraph attention networks. Validation on a real-world 180-node transportation network showed that our approach reduced system costs by 23.5%, 18.9%, and 13.3% compared to state-of-the-art benchmarks (IPPO, MAPPO, and HMA-GAPPO), respectively. The aformentioned research results have led to two publications at IEEE Trans. Smart Grid. For the joint battery charging and inventory replenishment scheduling problem within a BSS, we formulated a Markov Decision Process to minimize operational and customer waiting costs. To mitigate the action space dimensionality, we successfully integrated proven operational structures into the scheduling policy: a Threshold-Charging and Least-Demand-First structure for charging, and an (s, S) policy for inventory replenishment. Numerical experiments using real-world data demonstrated that this structured approach (SAC+TC+(s, S)) achieved significant cost savings, ranging from 6.53% to 93.73%, compared to various benchmark policies and the vanilla Soft Actor-Critic algorithm under different operational settings. For the more challening objective with uncertain EV deadline, we develop a DRL based framework to schedule the charging order of EVs based on predicted charging deadlines. Numerical results on real-world data demonstrate that the developed DRL framework significantly improves the performance of charging efficiency and customer satisfaction. The developed algorithms have been rigorously tested and validated through extensive simulations using real-world data, including renewable generation, pricing, and EV arrivals from the Caltech Adaptive Charging Network. All proposed frameworks demonstrated significant performance gains, achieving cost reductions of up to 23.5% compared to leading benchmarks. The work also includes preliminary steps toward direct implementation in real-world charging facilities, with validation pathways designed for integration into the Caltech Adaptive Charging Network infrastructure.

14200720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200720.value: Structural Policy Insights for Scheduling: We established and proved an "earlier-deadline-and-less-demand-first" (ED-LDF) priority rule as optimal for deadline scheduling under heavy traffic. For EV charging with grid constraints, we formulated a stochastic DP model and conjectured a novel optimal structure: EVs sharing a deadline and bus should be charged toward a common energy target. These structures significantly boost Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) performance by reducing action space dimensionality. Advanced Multi-Agent DRL for Networked BSS Operations: To solve the joint EV routing and charging problem across a BSS network, we developed a novel Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Hypergraph Attention Actor-Critic (HMA-HGAAC) framework. It uses hypergraph attention to model complex agent interactions efficiently. In a 180-node real-world network simulation, it reduced system costs by 13.3% to 23.5% versus state-of-the-art benchmarks like MAPPO and IPPO. Hybrid DRL for Single BSS Management: For a single BSS, we integrated classical operational structures—Threshold-Charging, Least-Demand-First, and an (s,S) inventory policy—into a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm. This hybrid SAC+TC+(s,S) approach leverages domain knowledge to simplify learning. Experiments with real data show it reduces total costs by 6.53% to 93.73% compared to baseline policies and vanilla SAC. Validation with Real-World Data: All models were rigorously tested using real-world data on renewable generation, pricing, and EV arrivals from the Caltech Adaptive Charging Network. The work provides validated frameworks and a direct pathway for implementing these efficient scheduling solutions in real-world EV charging infrastructure.

14200720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200720.value: Future work will focus on three key directions: 1) Theoretical Proof – Formally establishing the optimality of the conjectured charging structure under general dynamics. 2) Real-World Pilot – Advancing from simulation to deploying and testing the algorithms in a live environment, such as the Caltech Adaptive Charging Network. 3) Model Expansion – Incorporating more complex factors like vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services and detailed battery degradation models.

14200720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200720.value: Consider the challenge of operating a network of battery swap stations for electric vehicles. Managers must juggle unpredictable customer demand, variable solar and wind power, and fluctuating electricity prices—all while minimizing costs and wait times for drivers. This research developed intelligent AI solutions to act as a highly efficient, automated station manager. We created algorithms that optimally guide EVs to the best station and schedule their battery swaps. For individual stations, another algorithm smartly manages battery charging and inventory using effective, intuitive rules (such as prioritizing the most depleted batteries and restocking before running low). Rigorously tested with real-world data from sources like the Caltech charging network, these AI systems reduce operational costs by up to 23% compared to current leading methods. By making electric vehicle infrastructure more cost-effective and reliable, this work supports a smoother, faster transition to sustainable transportation for both operators and drivers.

14201420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201420.value: A typical multi-agent system consists of a so-called leader system and a group of so-called follower systems. The leader system produces reference trajectories for the followers to track and/or the disturbances imposed on the followers systems. Since the control inputs of various followers are subject to communication constraints, the overall control law must be distributed in order to satisfy these communication constraints. The distributed observer was first developed in 2010, which aims to estimate and transmit the leader's signal to every follower through the communication network of a multi-agent system. Since then, it has been a systematic method for handling various cooperative control problems of complex multi-agent systems. The original form of the distributed observer requires every follower know the dynamics of the leader, it is not fully distributed. In 2016, a so-called adaptive distributed observer was further constructed. Under the assumption that the leader’s children know the information of the leader, this observer is capable of estimating both the leader’s signal and the dynamics of the leader assuming that, thus is fully distributed. To deal with the case where the leader system contains unknown parameters, since 2018, the PI has been establishing an adaptive distributed observer for an uncertain leader system, which estimates not only the leader’s signal but also the unknown parameters in the leader system. However, up to now, the result on the adaptive distributed observer for an uncertain leader system is only limited to static and undirected communication networks. In practice, due to the change of the environment or the failures of the sensors and actuators of a multi-agents system, the communication networks are often directed and switching. In this project, we will first endeavor to enhance the capability of the adaptive distribute observer so that it can handle the uncertainty in the leader system for switching and or directed networks. Then, by utilizing this adaptive distribute observer, we will establish a unified framework for synthesizing a distributed control law for various cooperative control problems for complex multi-agent systems. This framework will be applied to solve several cooperative control problems of nonlinear systems subject to uncertain leader systems such as the leader-following consensus problem for Euler-Lagrange systems, the attitude synchronization problem of multiple rigid-body systems, coordination of multiple mobile robots, and the formation flying of multiple spacecraft systems. 一個典型的多智能體系統由一個所謂的領導者系統和一組所謂的跟隨者系統組成。領導者系統用來產生供跟隨者追踪的參考軌跡和對跟隨者系統施加的干擾信號。由於各個跟隨者的控制輸入都受到通信約束，為了滿足這些約束，總體的控制律必須為分佈式的。分佈式觀測器最早於2012年提出，它的宗旨在於通過多智能體系統的通信網絡來為每一個跟隨者估計並傳送領導者的信號。從此之後，它就成為了處理複雜多智能體系統的各種協同控制問題的系統方法。由於原始形式的分佈式觀測器要求每一個跟隨者都要知道領導者的動力學模型，因此它不是完全分佈式的。在2016年，一種所謂的自適應分佈式觀測器被提出。這個觀測器可以在僅領導者的子系統知道領導者信息的假設下，估計出領導者的信號和動力學模型，因此，它是完全分佈式的。自2018年以來，為了處理領導者系統包含未知參數的情況，項目負責人著手於為不確定的領導者系統建立自適應分佈式觀測器。該觀測器不僅可以估計領導者的信號，還可以估計領導者系統中的未知參數。然而，到目前為止，在對不確定的領導者系統的自適應分佈式觀測器上的結果僅限於能夠處理靜態和無向通信網絡的情況。在實踐中，由於環境的變化或多智能體系統傳感器和執行器的故障，通信網絡通常是有向和切換的。在此項目中，我們將首先著力於增強自適應分佈式觀測器的功能，以使其能夠對抗切換和定向網絡中的領導者系統的不確定性。隨後，利用這個自適應分佈式觀測器，我們將建立一個用於為各種複雜多智能體系統的協同控制問題設計分佈式控制律的統一框架。該框架將用來解決在不確定的領導者系統下的若干非線性系統的協同控制問題，例如歐拉-拉格朗日系統的領導者-跟隨者一致性問題，多個剛體系統的姿態同步問題，多個移動機器人的協作，以及多個航天器系統的編隊飛行。

14201420.value: The project aims to achieve the following four objectives: 1. Develop the adaptive distribute observer so that it can handle the uncertainty in the leader system subject to directed switching networks. 2. Establish a unified framework for designing the distributed control law utilizing the adaptive distributed observer for uncertain leader systems. 3. Evaluate and validate the general results by specific applications such as the coordination of multiple mobile robots, and the coordinate control of multiple spacecraft systems All four objectives are fully accomplished. The research has led to 6 journal papers and five conference papers. The six journal papers include two papers in Automatica and one paper in IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, both journals are among the top journals of the control field. Details of the research outcomes can be found in Section 6.1. Two Phd students Tianqi Wang and Xiongnan He have been trained through conducting this project. The project has led to collaboration with Prof. Tao Liu of Southern University of Science and Technology. Prof. Liu and PI have jointly published three journal papers and two conference papers supported by this project. The PI has delivered plenary speeches in three conferences under the support of this project including the flagship conference of IEEE Control Systems Society with the following details: “The Evolution of the Distributed Observer and Its Applications”, The 62nd IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, December 13-15, 2023, Marina Bay Sands, Singapore.

14201420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201420.value: We have fully achieved all four objectives and the main findings are summarized as follows: 1. The existing results on the adaptive distributed observer for an uncertain linear leader system are established over static networks, and hence do not apply to a switching network. In this project, we have proposed a novel adaptive distributed observer and show that it can estimate both the state, the unknown parameters and the output matrix of the leader system exponentially over the class of switching networks under consideration. To achieve this objective, we have overcome the challenges caused by the switching network by introducing a switching gain for the adaptive distributed observer and invoking the so-called generalized Barbalat's lemma instead of the conventional Barbalat's lemma. As an application of the adaptive distributed observer, we have further solved the leader-following attitude consensus problem of multiple rigid body systems with an uncertain leader system over a switching network. These findings are reported in Journal paper 1. 2. We have studied the leader-following consensus of uncertain multiple Euler-Lagrange systems subject to unknown disturbances over jointly connected communication networks. 2. We have employed an adaptive distributed observer to provide each follower an estimation of the reference trajectory over jointly connected switching networks, and apply the adaptive control technique to estimate both the uncertain parameters of the plant and the upper bound of the external disturbance. As a result, the approach of this paper can handle a large class of reference trajectories and any bounded disturbance with unknown upper bound. These findings are reported in conference paper 1. 3. We have applied the adaptive distributed observer approach to solve the attitude control for multiple rigid body systems. Moreover, to save the computational resource and improve the computational efficiency, we have implemented the control law using both event-triggered control and sampled-data control. These findings are reported in journal paper 5 and conference papers 3 and 5. 4. We further expanded the scope of the project to develop the distributed observer for discrete-time systems. These findings are reported in journal papers 2-4 and conference papers 2 and 4. 5. We have applied the distributed observer to study the distributed Nash equilibrium seeking for high-order integrator dynamics subject to disturbances of unknown bounds. The main finding is reported in journal paper 6.

14201420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201420.value: Two potential expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. The distributed observer technique can be further explored to study the distributed Nash equilibrium seeking for non-cooperative games of nonlinear systems over switching communication networks. 2. In conjunction with the reinforcement learning techniques, the distributed observer can be applied to solve the data-driven cooperative output regulation problem for unknown linear systems.

14201420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201420.value: Multi-agent control systems arise from numerous engineering applications such as formation flying of multiple fight vehicles, mobile sensor area coverage, control of power grids. What distinguishes the control of multi-agent systems from the conventional control law for a single system is that the control law for multi-agent systems has to be distributed in order to satisfy communication constraints. In 2018, the PI developed a so-called adaptive distributed observer based framework for designing the distributed control law for complex multi-agent systems. Nevertheless, by 2020, the adaptive distributed observer was only established over static and undirected communication networks. In practice, due to the failures of the sensors and actuators of a multi-agents system, the communication network is often directed and switching. In this project, we have first enhanced the capability of the adaptive distribute observer so that it can handle the uncertainty in the leader system for switching and / or directed networks. Then, by utilizing this adaptive distributed observer, we have established a unified framework for synthesizing a distributed control law for various cooperative control problems for complex multi-agent systems. This framework has been applied to solve several cooperative control problems of nonlinear systems subject to uncertain leader systems.

14201520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201520.value: Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) problem refers to a class of sequential decision making problems where in each step one needs to choose an arm (or option) from which a random reward will be generated. The distribution of the reward depends on each arm and it is unknown to the decision maker. The goal of the decision maker is to maximize the expected total reward over some horizon. The MAB problem has a large number of applications including internet advertising, dynamic pricing, recommender systems, clinical trials etc. In several application domains, the rewards of different arms can depend on a common unobservable state variable that may dynamically switch between different states or regimes. In this project, the PI will study the MAB problem with regime-switching rewards, and develop algorithms and theories for this new problem. Specifically, the project will 1) develop novel learning algorithms for the MAB problem with regime-switching rewards; and 2) analyze the performance of learning algorithms/policies by deriving the rate of convergence of the accumulated reward relative to the benchmark policies. The proposed research will contribute to the theoretical and algorithmic developments of MAB problems with non-stationary rewards. In addition, given the wide applications of MAB and the ease of getting and processing information nowadays, the proposed research will also potentially help firms improve their business efficiency and financial performance. 多臂老虎機(MAB)問題是概率論和強化學習裡的一類經典動態決策問題. 在這類問題裡，決策者需要在每個步驟中在K個選項中做出一個選擇. 每個選擇將會產生隨機獎勵， 而決策者並不知道獎勵的概率分佈。決策者的目標是通過學習來最大化在一定時間範圍內的預期總收益。多臂老虎機問題在商業中應用廣泛，包括互聯網廣告，動態定價，推薦系統，臨床試驗等。在一些應用領域中，不同選擇對應的獎勵可以依賴於一個共同的不可觀察的狀態變量，而該變量可以在不同的狀態或體制之間進行轉換。在這個項目中，PI將研究這一類體制轉換獎勵模型下的多臂老虎機問題，並為這個新問題開發算法和建立理論. 具體來說，該項目將1）針對具有體制轉換的獎勵下的MAB問題開發新的學習算法；和2）分析在線學習算法的表現. 本項研究將有助於非平穩獎勵下的多臂老虎機問題的理論和算法發展。此外，鑑於MAB的廣泛應用以及當前獲得和處理信息的能力，本項研究也將可能潛在地幫助企業提高他們的業務效率和財務績效。

14201520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201520.value: We have successfully published three papers with the support of the grant. One paper appeared in NeurIPS (Neural Information Processing Systems), a top machine learning conference. Another paper appeared in a conference AISTATS (Artificial Intelligence and Statistics) 2022, and was selected as orals (only 44 out of 1685 submissions were selected as orals). The third paper was published in Production and Operations Management, a top journal in the field of operations research and management. We next summarize the major contributions and research findings from each paper. Our paper "Regime Switching Bandits" features novel designs in three regards: we propose a new bandit problem formulation, develop a new learning algorithm, and prove regret bounds with new techniques. In particular, we establish a regret bound of T^{2/3} (ignoring logarithmic factors) for the proposed learning algorithm where T is the learning horizon. In the paper "Debiasing Samples from Online Learning Using Bootstrap", we propose a bootstrap-based algorithm to debias the sample means and provide more reliable estimators for the mean rewards of the arms for the multi-armed bandit. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effective bias reduction for samples generated by popular bandit algorithms. Finally, in the paper "Sublinear regret for learning POMDPs", we study the model-based undiscounted reinforcement learning for partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). The oracle we consider is the optimal policy of the POMDP with a known environment in terms of the average reward over an infinite horizon. We propose the first learning algorithm that achieves sublinear regret with respect to our oracle for learning general POMDPs.

14201520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201520.value: The major area for further development is to establish square-root of T regret bounds for learning regime-switching bandits and average-reward partially observable Markov decision processes. We hope to investigate them in the future.

14201520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201520.value: This project studies Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) problems with regime-switching rewards where arms' rewards depend on a common unobservable state variable that dynamically switches between different states. We present an efficient learning algorithm with theoretical guarantees, advancing MAB problems with non-stationary rewards. We also extend the study to online learning in partially-observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). POMDPs stand as a critical framework for dynamic decision-making scenarios where certain evolving system states remain hidden from observation. In this context, we introduce a learning algorithm engineered for average-reward POMDPs, and provide theoretical guarantees of the algorithm. Additionally, we address a critical statistical issue in MAB experiments where sample averages may exhibit bias in estimating mean rewards. We offer a debiasing procedure using bootstrapping, applicable across adaptive policies without requiring prior reward distribution knowledge. Our research outcomes contribute substantively to the expanding body of knowledge concerning online learning in MABs and POMDPs.

14201620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201620.value: 不利的天氣和光照條件（例如，霧，雨，低光照，夜間和陰影）會降低視覺傳感器的可見度，從而影響自動化系統的性能。一個有挑戰性的問題是戶外視覺系統（例如自動駕駛汽車，無人駕駛飛機和監控系統）需要在惡劣的天氣條件下正常運行。現有的性能最佳的視覺處理算法在這種不利條件下精度也會嚴重下降。 現有的方法主要集中在通過構造卷積神經網絡在惡劣天氣或不利光照的環境下，利用有標記的數據進行訓練，從而學習如何從捕獲到的輸入圖像中恢復清晰的圖像。雖然這種方法提升了圖片的可見性，但是也存在一些問題。首先，我們很難甚至不可能從現實的有雨的場景中獲得配對的乾淨和有雨的圖像。現有方法通常通過採用Photoshop軟件或簡單的圖像建模方程來合成配對的圖像作為訓練數據。然而，合成的圖像和真實的圖像存在一定的差距，用這些合成的數據訓練的網絡在處理真實圖像的時候往往表現出有限的性能。其次，收集大量的配對的訓練樣本既費時又費力。但是，我們通常很容易收集到大量的真實的無監督（非配對）的樣本，即真實的雨天或霧霾圖像，而沒有它們相對應的干淨的圖像。在這個項目中，我們將收集大量的真實數據，並開發學習算法，以便在網絡訓練過程中可以同時利用有標記的合成數據和未標記的真實數據，從而提升不利天氣和光照條件下的視覺處理算法的性能。本項目旨在解決的研究問題包括：通過非配對的數據學習圖像去雨，通過分解的平均教師算法學習圖像去霧，通過邊界輔助和知識蒸餾算法進行實例陰影檢測以及通過基於掩膜的相互學習算法進行陰影去除。 總而言之，該項目旨在開發一系列針對惡劣天氣和光照條件下的視覺處理算法，這些算法將通過未標記的數據進行學習，從而大大減輕甚至完全避免戶外視覺系統精度的下降。我們的主要想法是利用大量的未標記的真實數據來幫助訓練網絡，從而實現比現有的利用“假的”合成的數據進行訓練的工作更好的性能。我們團隊已經提出了各種可靠的半監督學習方法（例如，無監督域適應算法，半監督教師學生算法框架）。這些算法為我們實現利用未標記數據開發新的學習算法提供了技術支持。此外，我們還進行了一系列基於有標記的訓練數據的圖像復原任務的初步研究（例如，去雨、去霧、低光照圖像增強和陰影去除）。本項目的成果是開發一系列算法，從而利用未標記的訓練數據，學習處理惡劣天氣和光照條件下的視覺信息。

14201620.label: Realisation of objectives
14201620.value: In this project, we aim to develop a set of deep-learning-based algorithms to address vision problems under adverse weather and illumination conditions. The key research and development issues include the creation of learning algorithms to enhance image visibility through deraining, dehazing, shadow detection, and removal. These advancements will aid outdoor vision systems (e.g., autonomous cars, unmanned aerial vehicles, and surveillance systems) to operate smoothly under challenging weather and lighting conditions. To tackle these issues, we have developed various deep models to remove rain streaks and fog, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both effectiveness and efficiency. We formulated a real-world adverse weather removal method by leveraging advanced vision-language models. Additionally, we collected shadow images to build a large-scale dataset for shadow analysis, developed deep-learning-based methods to automatically refine noisy shadow labels, and formulated a stage-by-stage method to detect objects and their shadows simultaneously. Our project has resulted in the publication of six journal papers and ten conference papers. The major findings are summarized below: Summary of Major Findings • [J1] analyzes the visual effects of rain concerning scene depth, formulates a rain imaging model incorporating rain streaks and fog, and introduces a new rain removal dataset, RainCityscapes. This dataset synthesizes realistic rain images using ground-truth rain-free photos from the Cityscapes dataset. A depth-guided non-local module and a lightweight deep convolutional neural network are designed to achieve real-time removal of rain streaks and fog. • [J2] presents a gated non-local deep residual learning framework for image deraining, avoiding over-deraining or under-deraining caused by global residual learning in existing networks. A non-local guided attention module learns attentional non-local features for global residual prediction, and a channel-wise gated prediction module models channel-wise dependencies of feature maps for obtaining derained results. • [J3] compiles a new dataset of 10,500 shadow images, each with a labeled ground-truth mask, supporting shadow detection in complex environments. The dataset covers various scene categories, shadow sizes, locations, contrasts, and types. A fast shadow detection network with a detail enhancement module is presented to capture shadow details and demonstrate the proposed method's effectiveness. • [J6] introduces the novel instance shadow detection task, aiming to detect shadows and their corresponding objects. A new dataset with labels indicating shadows and their objects is collected. An end-to-end one-stage detector is formulated to predict shadow and object instances directly, along with developing an evaluation metric for instance shadow detection. This paper is published in the prestigious pattern recognition journal TPAMI. • [C1] proposes a new single-stage fully convolutional network architecture with a bidirectional relation learning module to learn the relations of shadow and object instances in an end-to-end manner. This method explores the internal relationship between shadows and objects to enhance the overall performance of instance shadow detection. • [C8] introduces a novel framework to explore physical haze priors and aggregate temporal information effectively. A memory-based physical prior guidance module encodes prior-related features into long-range memory, and a multi-range scene radiance recovery module captures space-time dependencies in multiple ranges, aiding in temporal information aggregation from adjacent frames. • [C9] proposes the Shadow-aware Iterative Label Tuning (SILT) framework, explicitly considering noise in shadow labels and training the deep model in a self-training manner. This approach significantly improves the accuracy of labeled shadow masks in current training datasets, enhancing shadow detection performance. • [C10] addresses the limitations of existing adverse weather image restoration methods trained on synthetic data when applied to real-world scenarios. A semi-supervised learning framework utilizing vision-language models enhances restoration performance across various adverse weather conditions in real-world settings, providing supervision signals for training restoration models. Development of Fundamental Deep-Learning Techniques In addition to the main tasks, we developed fundamental deep-learning techniques for object recognition and localization, 3D information analysis, video prediction, semi-supervised semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and self-supervised learning: • [J4] presents a robust sim-to-real deep-learning framework for fast and accurate object recognition and localization. An automated synthetic data generation pipeline produces large-scale photo-realistic data with precise annotations, followed by an instance segmentation network for object recognition and a 6D pose estimation network for localization. • [J5] introduces a new low-level rotation-invariant representation replacing common 3D Cartesian coordinates as network inputs. A network architecture embeds these representations into features, encoding local relations between points and their neighbors, and the global shape structure. • [C2] proposes a disentangled refinement framework for point cloud upsampling, separating the task into generating coarse but dense points and refining them by adjusting each point's location. Experimental results show this method's superiority. • [C3] introduces a new grid keypoint learning framework for stochastic video prediction, aiming at a robust and explainable intermediate keypoint representation. The method detects key points in a grid space, formulates a condensation loss for meaningful key points, and propagates keypoint locations with stochasticity. • [C4] presents C3-SemiSeg, improving consistency-based semi-supervised learning for semantic segmentation by enhancing feature alignment under perturbations. A cross-set region-level data augmentation strategy and cross-set pixel-wise contrastive learning facilitate feature representation ability. • [C5] develops a novel regularizer loss function for depth estimation, guided by a high-level semantic information provider, Regularizer Net. The model outperforms current methods on the NYU-Depth-v2 benchmark, preserving richer geometric details and more accurate object boundaries. • [C6] presents a self-supervised method for learning reliable visual correspondence from unlabeled videos. The method formulates correspondence as finding paths in a joint space-time graph, improving instance discrimination by exploring neighbor relations of central instances. • [C7] proposes the Flattening Sharpness for Dynamic Gradient Projection Memory (FS-DGPM) method for continual learning. A soft weight represents each basis's importance, and Flattening Sharpness (FS) regulates the flatness of the weight loss landscape, reducing the generalization gap. These advancements collectively enhance our understanding and capability in handling vision tasks under adverse weather and illumination conditions, significantly contributing to the field of computer vision and deep learning.

14201620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201620.value: In this project, we developed a suite of deep-learning-based algorithms to address vision challenges under adverse weather and illumination conditions. Our research focused on enhancing image visibility through tasks such as deraining, dehazing, and shadow detection and removal, thereby improving the performance of outdoor vision systems like autonomous cars, unmanned aerial vehicles, and surveillance systems. Key findings and outcomes include: Rain and Fog Removal: We created a rain imaging model incorporating rain streaks and fog, leading to the development of the RainCityscapes dataset, which synthesizes realistic rain images using ground-truth rain-free photos from the Cityscapes dataset. A depth-guided non-local module and a lightweight deep convolutional neural network were designed to achieve real-time removal of rain streaks and fog. Image Deraining: A gated non-local deep residual learning framework was introduced to avoid over-deraining or under-deraining. It features a non-local guided attention module for learning attentional non-local features and a channel-wise gated prediction module for deriving derained results. Shadow Detection: We compiled a dataset of 10,500 shadow images with labeled ground-truth masks, supporting shadow detection in various environments. A fast shadow detection network with a detail enhancement module was developed, demonstrating effectiveness in general situations. Instance Shadow Detection: A novel task was proposed to detect shadows along with their corresponding objects. An end-to-end one-stage detector was formulated, and a new dataset with labels indicating shadows and their objects was collected. This work was published in the prestigious TPAMI journal. Dehazing: A framework was introduced to explore physical haze priors and aggregate temporal information. A memory-based physical prior guidance module encodes prior-related features into long-range memory, and a multi-range scene radiance recovery module captures space-time dependencies. Shadow Detection: This deep framework addresses noise in shadow labels by training deep models in a self-training manner, significantly improving the accuracy of shadow masks and enhancing shadow detection performance. Real-world Adverse Weather Restoration: A semi-supervised learning framework utilizing vision-language models was formulated to enhance image restoration across diverse adverse weather conditions, providing supervision signals for training restoration models. Additionally, we developed fundamental deep-learning techniques, including object recognition and localization, 3D information analysis, video prediction, semi-supervised semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and self-supervised learning. These advancements collectively enhanced our understanding and capabilities in handling vision tasks under adverse conditions, contributing to the field of computer vision and deep learning. Our work resulted in six top-tier journal papers and ten top-tier conference papers, showcasing our contributions and innovations.

14201620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201620.value: Our research can be further developed for real-world applications, such as enhancing algorithms for autonomous vehicles and surveillance systems to improve performance in adverse weather and lighting conditions. Optimizing our models for efficiency and scalability will enable real-time applications and large-scale deployments. Additionally, integrating vision and language models can provide richer contextual information, while adapting our techniques for different domains like maritime, aviation, and robotics can expand their applicability. To support these developments, we will continue collecting and annotating diverse datasets and advancing synthetic data generation techniques. Collaboration with academic institutions, technology companies, and industry stakeholders will facilitate the co-development and testing of new applications. Publishing our findings and organizing workshops will disseminate our knowledge and foster further research in the field.

14201620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201620.value: Our project focused on improving how machines see and understand the world in bad weather and poor lighting. Imagine trying to drive a car through heavy rain or fog; it’s challenging because you can’t see clearly. We developed advanced computer programs to help machines like self-driving cars and drones see better in these conditions. These programs can remove rain and fog from images and detect shadows, making the visuals clearer and more detailed. The significance of this research lies in its potential to make outdoor systems safer and more reliable. For instance, self-driving cars equipped with our technology can navigate more safely in bad weather, reducing the risk of accidents. Security cameras can also function better in low-light or rainy conditions, enhancing public safety. Overall, our work aims to make technology more robust and dependable, ensuring it can operate smoothly regardless of weather and lighting conditions.

14201820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201820.value: Researchers have devoted to developing a variety of soft robotic systems in the laboratory to take advantage of compliance introduced by soft materials. While being able to mimic natural systems and building compatible robots working together with humans, the challenge of lacking computational tools in design also dampens the development of soft robotics in industrial applications. Specifically, the design and control practices taken in soft robotics at present are mainly based on intuition and trial-and-error empirical tests. The research proposed in this project aims at changing this situation by investigating a new computational framework to optimize the design and actuation of soft robots with complicated shape and material distribution. Enabling a computational framework for optimizing the actuation and design of soft robots is challenging because no formulation can establish direct mapping between actuation parameters and the configurations of a soft robot made by elastomers in complex structures. Conventional methods for computing kinematics of articulated rigid-bodies become insufficient to capture the deformation of soft robots. Instead, numerical simulation of elastomers’ physical behaviour based on Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is usually employed for this purpose. However, the FEA computation is cumbersome - especially when simulating the deformation with large rotation, which is a very common phenomenon to be modeled in many applications of soft robotics. When attempting to optimize the design parameters or the material distribution of soft robots by numerical computation, the simulation based on FEA is not efficient enough to be used in the loop of optimization. Research will be conducted in this project to tackle the aforementioned technical challenge by 1) investigating a geometry-based formulation that enables the efficient simulation of elastomers through a local / global optimization process with iteratively applied local projection and global blending, 2) incorporating the response of interference into the geometry-based framework, 3) investigating two optimization approaches for position-oriented and strain-oriented tasks. By the outcome of these research activities, our computational framework can generate optimized actuation parameters and material distributions for soft robots with advanced design. Physical experiments will be developed to calibrate the coefficients employed in our simulator and verify the performance of results generated by our framework. The successful development of this computational framework is an essential and important step to move the soft robotic systems out of laboratory. N/A

14201920.label: Project Objectives
14201920.value: To design a message-passing based sparse matrix factorization algorithm for estimating the mobile-to-RIS and RIS-to-BS channels with tractable convergence and low complexity. In particular, we plan to exploit the characteristics of RIS channels to reinforce and accelerate the convergence of the message passing algorithm. We will also derive the mean square error (MSE) evolution and the state evolution of the proposed algorithm, so that the algorithm convergence becomes theoretically tractable. To design a joint channel-and-signal estimation algorithm. Our prior work suggests that the training overhead for channel estimation can be significantly reduced if channels and signals are jointly estimated, because the signals can be used as “soft pilots” to iteratively enhance the channel estimation accuracy. In RIS-assisted MIMO systems, joint channel-and-signal estimation yields a challenging trilinear matrix factorization problem. We plan to address the problem using turbo-type message passing approaches. Moreover, we will devise an analytical framework to optimize the training pilot length. To investigate the tradeoff between the channel estimation accuracy and channel estimation cost, including training overhead and computational time. In particular, we shall characterize the sensitivity of system performance with respect to the channel estimation error. This, together with the convergence and phase transition analysis, will allow us to strike an optimal tradeoff between the pilot sequence length, the number of message-passing iterations, and the achievable system performance.

14201920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201920.value: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has recently emerged as a revolutionary technology that conceptually goes beyond the contemporary massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) technology. By reflecting the incident signals with reconfigurable phase shifts, RISs are capable of manipulating the signal propagation to achieve unprecedented energy focusing at the receivers. With RISs, the wireless environment is no longer an uncontrollable entity, but rather can be configured to suit diverse system requirements. Having drawn attention worldwide, RIS-assisted massive MIMO has been envisioned as a key enabler for future 6G mobile networks. Recent studies show that the performance of RIS-assisted MIMO systems critically depends on the knowledge of channel state information (CSI) on both the transmitter-to-RIS and the RIS-to-receiver links. A main challenge here is that RISs, unlike BSs and mobile devices, are made of passive elements and do not have much signal processing capability. As a result, the receiver is solely responsible for estimating both the transmitter-to-RIS and RIS-to-receiver channels by observing only a cascade of the two links. Existing channel estimation methods do not work in this case, unless excessively long training periods are involved. Therefore, to render RIS a viable 6G solution, it is of paramount importance to understand how to perform cascaded channel estimation with affordable training overhead and computational complexity. In this project, we formulate the cascaded channel estimation problems in RIS-assisted massive MIMO systems as bilinear and trilinear sparse matrix factorization over probabilistic graphical models. Our goal is to develop fast, scalable, and convergent algorithms that can estimate the RIS channels with high accuracy. To achieve this goal, we plan to explore message-passing based Bayesian inference approaches. More specifically, we will focus on three tasks: (i) bilinear matrix factorization through message passing for cascaded channel estimation in RIS-assisted MIMO systems, (ii) trilinear matrix factorization through message passing for joint channel and signal detection, and (iii) optimal management of computation and communication resources for cascaded channel estimation. RIS technology undoubtedly constitutes an essential part of the paradigm shift towards 6G wireless systems. This proposal addresses a fundamental issue, namely, to acquire the knowledge of cascaded RIS channels, based on which many physical layer algorithms can be developed. The work, if successful, paves the way for massive deployment of RISs in future systems. With the PI’s solid expertise in MIMO signal processing, wireless system optimization, and Bayesian inference, this proposal is deemed very feasible. 近年來，智能反射面(RIS)已逐漸超越現有超大規模天線陣列(Massive MIMO)，成為未來通信系統中大幅提升信道容量的關鍵革命性技術。它可以通過在平面上集成大量低成本的無源反射元件，智能地重新配置無線傳播環境，從而顯著提高無線通信網絡的性能。具體地說，RIS的不同元件可以通過控制其幅度和/或相位來獨立地反射入射信號，從而協同地實現前所未有的定向信號增強。在智能反射面的幫助下，無線通信信道不再是隨即而不可控制的，相反，智能反射面可以通過軟件控制反射來主動修改無線信道，已滿足不同的系統需求。因此，智能反射面已被視為實現未來第六代(6G)無線通信系統的關鍵技術。 最近的研究表明，RIS輔助MIMO系統的性能關鍵取決於發射機到RIS和RIS到接收機鏈路上的信道狀態信息（CSI）。 這裡的主要挑戰是，RIS與BS和移動設備不同，是由無源元件製成的，並且不具有任何信號處理能力。 結果，接收器僅可通過觀察兩個鏈路的級聯，獨自負責估計發送器到RIS和RIS到接收器的信道。 除非涉及到過長的信道訓練時間，否則現有的信道估計方法在這種情況下不起作用。 因此，為使RIS成為可行的6G解決方案，了解如何以可承受的導頻開銷和計算複雜性來了解如何執行級聯信道估計至關重要。 在本項目中，我們將RIS輔助大規模MIMO系統中的級聯信道估計問題建模為概率圖形模型上的雙線性和三線性稀疏矩陣分解。 我們的目標是開發快速，可擴展和收斂的算法，以高精度估算RIS通道。 為了實現此目標，我們計劃探索基於消息傳遞的貝葉斯推理方法。 更具體地說，我們將專注於三個任務：（i）通過消息傳遞進行雙線性矩陣分解以在RIS輔助MIMO系統中進行級聯信道估計；（ii）通過消息傳遞進行三線性矩陣分解以進行聯合信道和信號檢測；以及（iii） 級聯信道估計的計算和通信資源的最佳管理。 毫無疑問，RIS技術構成了向6G無線系統轉變的重要組成部分。 該提議解決了一個基本問題，即獲得級聯的RIS通道的知識，基於該知識可以開發許多物理層算法。 如果成功，這項工作將為將來的系統中大規模部署RIS鋪平道路。 憑藉PI在MIMO信號處理，無線系統優化和貝葉斯推理方面的紮實專業知識，該項目是非常可行的。

14201920.label: Realisation of objectives
14201920.value: The project objectives have all been fulfilled satisfactorily. In particular, we have comprehensively studied cascaded channel estimation when a passive reconfigurable intelligent surface is deployed to enhance the capacity of wireless communication systems. The project has led to numerous publications in top journals and conferences. Regarding the first objective, we studied how to avoid excessively long training overheads in conventional channel estimation methods, where the cascaded channel estimation problem is converted into a sequence of conventional MIMO channel estimation problems by turning on one RIS element at a time. In particular, we formulated the cascaded channel estimation task as a matrix-calibration-based sparse matrix factorization problem by exploiting the knowledge of the slow-varying channel components and the hidden channel sparsity in the angular domain. Then, we proposed a novel message-passing-based algorithm to infer the cascaded BS-to-RIS and RIS-to-user channels. Furthermore, we developed a framework to analyze the estimation accuracy of the considered system. Regarding the second objective, we addressed the problem of joint channel and signal estimation. We exploited the burst-sparse structure of angular-domain propagation channels in massive MIMO and RIS systems. We proposed a sparse channel representation with a super-resolution sampling grid and a hidden Markovian support. Based on this, we developed a novel approximate inference-based blind estimation algorithm to estimate the channel and the user signals simultaneously, with emphasis on the adoption of the expectation-maximization method to learn the angle information. Furthermore, we demonstrated a low-complexity implementation of our algorithm, making use of factor graph and message passing principles to compute the marginal posteriors. Regarding the third objective, we have conducted extensive analysis on the mean-squared-error of channel estimation as a function of the number of BS antennas, number of RIS elements, number of users, and the signal-to-noise ratio. Interestingly, we find the existence of sharp phase transitions for the analytical MSEs when these parameters vary.

In particular, we plan to exploit the characteristics of RIS channels to reinforce and accelerate the convergence of the message passing algorithm. In RIS-assisted MIMO systems, joint channel-and-signal estimation yields a challenging trilinear matrix factorization problem. We plan to address the problem using turbo-type message passing approaches. Moreover, we will devise an analytical framework to optimize the training pilot length.

In particular, we shall characterize the sensitivity of system performance with respect to the channel estimation error. This, together with the convergence and phase transition analysis, will allow us to strike an optimal tradeoff between the pilot sequence length, the number of message-passing iterations, and the achievable system performance.

14201920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201920.value: There are several major research outcomes from this work, leading to a good number of referred publications in top-tier journals and conferences listed in Part C. The detailed findings are as below. 1. We characterize the slow-varying and fast-varying channel components of the RIS-to-BS channel by the Rician fading model. Based on this assumption, we formulate the cascaded channel estimation problem as a joint task of the RIS-to-BS channel matrix calibration and the RIS-to-user channel matrix estimation. 2. We develop the posterior mean estimators under the Bayesian inference framework to infer the two cascaded channels and adopt the sum-product message passing algorithm to approximately compute the estimators. We introduce additional approximations to the messages based on the approximate message passing (AMP) framework. 3. Based on the replica method from statistical physics, we analyze the asymptotic performance of the posterior mean estimators in the large-system limit. We show that, with perfect knowledge of the channel prior distributions and under some appropriately chosen angle sampling bases, the mean square errors (MSEs) of the posterior mean estimators can be determined by the fixed point of a set of scalar equations. 4. We develop a novel blind channel-and-signal estimation method based on EM principles. Under the EM framework, angle-tuning and hyper-parameter learning are employed to learn the angle of arrivals automatically without any prior knowledge of the channel state information. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity implementation of the proposed algorithm. Specifically, as the EM involves the calculation of marginals, we construct an associated factor graph and apply the message-passing principles to achieve this purpose. To further reduce the computation complexity, additional approximations are introduced to particular messages based on the general approximate message passing (AMP) framework.

14201920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201920.value: In this study, we have studied cascaded channel estimation when the reconfigurable intelligent surface is fully passive. Moving forward, we may investigate the scenario where the RIS is partially active, i.e., a subset of reflective elements is active.

14202820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202820.value: 仿DNA分子結構的多螺旋連續體機構及其在微創手術機器人中的應用

14202820.label: Project Objectives
14202820.value: In this project, we intend to explore a continuum mechanism suitable for developing flexible robots with large bending angle and large payload ability in minimally invasive surgery (MIS), particularly laparoscopic bariatric surgery for treating obese patients. To achieve this, we would like to seek inspiration from nature, particularly the DNA structure, and design a class of multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM). To investigate the MHCM, we wish to study how the structure topology (such as number of helixes, helix direction and pitch) would affect the deformation of the mechanism under pure bending, pure compression, pure twisting and combined loading. To achieve these, the finite element analysis (FEA) will be utilized and a static model will be developed and validated experimentally. To evaluate if the designed MHCM is suitable for developing flexible instruments/robots for MIS, we would select to design and prototype a modular robotic flexible grasper and integrate it with a robot arm. The proposed benefits, i.e., large internal workspace, small shaft pivoting motion and large payload will be evaluated and quantified with lab tests. In addition, a mockup laparoscopic bariatric surgery using ex vivo pig stomach will be adopted to evaluate the feasibility of the robotic flexible grasper.

14202820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202820.value: 肥胖正在成為全球性的挑戰。根據世界衛生組織（WHO）的估計，全世界超過10％的成年人肥胖（BMI> 30）。減肥手術是治療病態肥胖的有效途徑，比非手術式治療更為有效。根據肥胖症外科聯合會（IFSO）的最新報告，腹腔鏡手術即微創手術（MIS）由於具有失血量少，住院時間短，創傷小的優勢，在減肥手術中佔比99.3％。然而在MIS中，由於剛性器械的工作空間小和靈巧性差，通常需要多於三個手術切口。在腹腔鏡減肥手術中，由於患者體型大、脂肪層厚，上述缺點被進一步放大。通過開發可在腔內靈活彎曲的柔性手術器械或機器人可有效解決上述問題。 開發柔性手術器械或機器人的關鍵是柔性機構。在腹腔鏡減肥手術中，柔性手術器械應具備結構緊湊、高度靈巧以及大載荷的特點。這需要具有易彎曲、高扭轉剛度、高軸向剛度且易於小型化的柔性機構。然而，現有柔性機構無法同時滿足上述要求。現有柔性機構可分為蛇形機構和連續體機構。蛇形機構由若干短的椎骨鏈接而成，相鄰椎骨形成一個鉸鏈。其缺點在於結構複雜，製造和組裝困難，不利於小型化。連續體結構為一個彈性結構，其末端位置通過彈性體的變形控制。相比於蛇形機構，連續體機構更易於小型化，但負載能力低。這使得連續體機構不適合大負載場合，例如手術吻合和縫合。而吻合與縫合是腹腔鏡減肥手術中的常用手段。因此，在推進MIS特別是腹腔鏡減肥手術的發展方面，需要一種能夠滿足上述性能的新型柔性機構。 DNA分子結構是柔性的。在DNA分子力學中發現，雙鏈DNA的剛度是單鏈DNA的約50倍。這啟發了我們設計一類多螺旋連續體機構（MHCM）用於開發腹腔鏡減肥手術柔性手術器械/機器人。初步結果表明，與傳統的彈簧狀連續體機構相比，MHCM的軸向剛度和扭轉剛度都得到了大幅提高，而彎曲剛度可以通過驅動繩的張力來調節。 MHCM可以通過3D打印試製或編織批量生產，是一種有前景的柔性機構。我們計劃開發一種模塊化柔性吻合器，並通過模擬腹腔鏡減肥手術進行測試。研究團隊在開發柔性機構和醫療機器人方面擁有超過九年的經驗，前述工作得到同行認可。我們有信心順利完成該項目，並推進柔性機器人在微創手術以及其它狹窄空間作業下的發展。

14202820.label: Realisation of objectives
14202820.value: This project aims to investigate a continuum mechanism and its applications in minimally invasive surgery. Specifically, a multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM) inspired by the DNA double helix structure will be studied and flexible surgical manipulators will be developed. We have fully achieved the objectives specified in this project. We designed the multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM) with several variations and studied their performances, including bending, payload, statics model, and control. By using FEA and analytical models, we analysed the influence of helix number, helix direction and pitch on the bending performances. These works correspond to the objectives 1 and 2. Secondly, we designed a flexible endoscope based on the optimized MHCM and integrated it with the UR5 robot arm. Artificial intelligence based visual servo control of the flexible endoscope was performed and evaluated with ex vivo pig stomach. This corresponds to the objective 3. The results were published in leading journals and conferences in mechanical engineering and robotics, including mechanism and machine theory (MMT), Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics (TMRB), Advanced intelligence systems (AIS), robotics and automation letters (RAL), Transactions in industrial electronics (TIE), Transactions on mechatronics (TMECH), international conference on robotics and automation (ICRA), etc. With the support of this project, we have trained a total of 5 PhD students and 1 MPhil student. The detailed project findings are summarized in the research outcome.

rows: In this project, we intend to explore a continuum mechanism suitable for developing flexible robots with large bending angle and large payload ability in minimally invasive surgery (MIS), particularly laparoscopic bariatric surgery for treating obese patients. To achieve this, we would like to seek inspiration from nature, particularly the DNA structure, and design a class of multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM).

To investigate the MHCM, we wish to study how the structure topology (such as number of helixes, helix direction and pitch) would affect the deformation of the mechanism under pure bending, pure compression, pure twisting and combined loading. To achieve these, the finite element analysis (FEA) will be utilized and a static model will be developed and validated experimentally.

To evaluate if the designed MHCM is suitable for developing flexible instruments/robots for MIS, we would select to design and prototype a modular robotic flexible grasper and integrate it with a robot arm. The proposed benefits, i.e., large internal workspace, small shaft pivoting motion and large payload will be evaluated and quantified with lab tests. In addition, a mockup laparoscopic bariatric surgery using ex vivo pig stomach will be adopted to evaluate the feasibility of the robotic flexible grasper.

14202820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202820.value: In this project, we intend to explore a continuum mechanism suitable for developing flexible robots with large bending angle and large payload ability in minimally invasive surgery (MIS), particularly laparoscopic bariatric surgery for treating obese patients. Inspired by the DNA double helix structure, we come up with the multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM) design and investigated how its structure topology (such as number of helixes, helix direction and pitch) influencing the performance by using both finite element analysis (FEA) and analytical static models. It is found that at the same bending stiffness as conventional helix structure, the MHCM could improve the compressional stiffness by 12.3 times and torsional stiffness by 3.2 times. The proposed static model could also accurately predict the deformation error, with a mean error of 1.01 mm (1.7%). The result is published in a leading mechanical engineering journal (MMT_2022). Based on the MHCM design, we developed several flexible instrument/robot modules (including a grasper and an endoscope) for MIS and integrated them with a robot arm. The kinematic model and vision based autonomous control of robotic flexible endoscope have been investigated (ICRA_2021, AIS_2024). The benefits, including large internal workspace, small shaft pivoting motion have been quantified. Compared to rigid robots, both the space occupation outside of the patient body and inside of the patient body have been reduced over 85%. Furthermore, mockup laparoscopic bariatric surgery using ex vivo pig stomach has been carried out to evaluate the developed flexible robots, verifying the previous benefits. To optimize the layout of the flexible robot and facilitate its operation in a clinical setting, we developed the pose-constrained visual servo control (AIS_2024) and integrated with image AI (RAL_2022, RAL_2023) and AR technologies (TMRB_2022). This paves the way toward future clinical adoption. In addition, to address the fundamental control problem of flexible robots, we developed a series of neural network control based on our flexible endoscope robot (TIE_2022, TIE_2024, TMECH_2024, TSMC_2025). This helps to provide a more robust control of flexible robots with faster convergence and better noise resistance. Based on this project, we have trained five PhD students and one MPhil student.

14202820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202820.value: In this project, we studied the design, modelling and control of the multi-helix continuum mechanism (MHCM) and developed exemplary flexible robot with the MHCM. Results show the proposed mechanism is promising. To achieve the final goal of benefiting patients with flexible instruments and flexible robots, there is still a long journey to pass. At first, materials and manufacturing process of the MHCM need to be refined. The current prototype is based on 3D printing and polymer materials. To further improve the performance and cover a wider range of dimensions, metal and machining should be adopted. Second, sensing of the MHCM needs be investigated, including shape sensing and force sensing. This helps with the fine control of MHCM based flexible robots. Thirdly, the prototypes developed in the project are mainly for experimental purposes and the type is limited. In clinical operation, a wider range of instruments/robots need to be developed. Additionally, investigations in system development, human-robot-interface, and clinical evaluation are necessary for the MHCM to benefit real patients.

14202820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202820.value: Obesity is becoming a worldwide health challenge. In treating morbid obesity, bariatric surgery is most effective. Over 90% of bariatric surgeries are performed minimally invasively. However, due to the thick fat layer, operating with rigid laparoscopic instruments is challenging and one promising solution is to develop high performance flexible instruments. This project proposes a novel flexible mechanism (MHCM) with outstanding performance by learning from the DNA double-helix structure. Compared to conventional flexible mechanisms, it has excellent bending behaviour while reducing the axial compression and twist significantly. In this project, we comprehensively studied the design, modelling and control of the MHCM. Based on this innovative design, we further developed several flexible medical robots, particularly a flexible endoscope robot, and investigated its vision-based autonomous control for bariatric surgery. Compared to rigid counterparts, the flexible robot could significantly reduce the space occupation and pivoting torque applied to the trocar, reducing the operation complexity and improving safety to the patient. In the future, continued investigations will be made to develop flexible instruments and robots to benefit a broader patient population.

14202920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202920.value: This project aims to develop cell-adaptable supramolecular hydrogels with biomimetic heterogeneous nanoscale local mechanical properties to enhance mechanosensing-dependent differentiation of stem cells in 3D culture and tissue regeneration in vivo. Cells typically reside in the three-dimensional (3D) extracellular matrix (ECM). The hierarchical and heterogeneous ECM structure not only provides the dynamic pericellular microenvironment but also offers local rigid cell anchorage sites to enable various cellular events. Specifically, the soft and weakly-crosslinked gel-like ground substance provides expandable space for cellular developments such as division and assembly. Meanwhile, the dense nano-fibrous ECM components such as collagen fibres offer an enhanced local mechanical rigidity for the attached cells to develop traction forces, which are required for many cellular events. Due to their chemically defined composition, hydrogels are widely used as a synthetic 3D matrix for delineating the effects of matrix properties on cell–matrix interactions and the resultant cellular behaviours, with reduced confounding factors. However, conventional hydrogels typically lack the sophisticated heterogeneous structures of ECM, and these limitations seriously hamper cell–matrix interactions and associated cellular developments in these hydrogels. Developing hydrogels with a structurally-biomimetic network to recapitulate the normal cell behaviours in 3D is critical to diverse basic and translational studies based on 3D cell cultures. We will synthesize cell-adaptable supramolecular hydrogels which will be regionally reinforced by nanostructures with defined physical and chemical properties. The peri/intercellular network of the hydrogels will be stabilized by weak and reversible host–guest crosslinks to support the cellular adaptation of hydrogel networks. The reinforcing nanostructures will condense and immobilize cell-adhesive biomacromolecules to enhance the mechanosensing feedback of cells. We will examine the efficacy of nanostructures with different aspect ratios for generating the heterogeneous hydrogel network and enhancing cell mechanosensing and development. we will also study the development of cell adhesion structures, the activation of mechanotransduction signaling, and the mechanosensing-dependent differentiation of stem cells encapsulated in the biomimetic hydrogels. We will further investigate the molecular mechanism underlying the enhanced mechanosensing-dependent differentiation of stem cells. We will evaluate the efficacy of the structurally-biomimetic hydrogels as the delivery vehicles of stem cells to promote in situ tissue regeneration in an animal model. The findings of this project will provide valuable guidance for the design of synthetic 3D biomaterials matrix. This will not only assist future basic studies on stem cells in a well-controlled biomimetic 3D microenvironment but will also facilitate the translation of stem cells for use in a range of clinical applications. 該項目旨在開發具有仿生異質納米級局部機械性能的細胞適應性超分子水凝膠，以增強幹細胞在3D培養和組織再生中的機械傳感依賴性分化。 細胞通常駐留在三維（3D）細胞外基質（ECM）中。分層且異質的ECM結構不僅提供了動態的細胞周圍微環境，而且還提供了局部剛性細胞錨定位點以實現各種細胞事件。具體而言，柔軟且弱交聯的凝膠狀研磨物質為細胞發育（例如分裂和組裝）提供了可擴展的空間。同時，緻密的納米纖維ECM組件（例如膠原纖維）為附著的細胞提供增強的局部機械剛度，以產生牽引力，這是許多細胞事件所必需的。由於其化學成分確定，水凝膠被廣泛用作3D細胞培養所需基質材料，用於探究基質特性對細胞-基質相互作用和所產生的細胞行為的影響，並減少了混雜因素。但是，常規水凝膠通常缺乏複雜的ECM異質結構，這些限制嚴重阻礙了這些水凝膠中的細胞-基質相互作用和相關的細胞發育。開發具有結構仿生網絡的水凝膠以研究3D中的正常細胞行為對於基於3D細胞培養的各種基礎和轉化研究至關重要。 我們將合成具有細胞適應性的超分子水凝膠，該凝膠將通過具有確定的物理和化學性質的納米結構進行局部增強。水凝膠的細胞周圍/細胞間網絡將通過弱且可逆的主客體交聯來穩定，以支持水凝膠網絡的細胞適應性。增強的納米結構將凝聚並固定細胞粘附的生物大分子，以增強細胞的機械傳感反饋。我們將檢查具有不同縱橫比的納米結構產生異質水凝膠網絡並增強細胞機械傳感和發育的功效。我們還將研究細胞粘附結構的發展，機械轉導信號的激活以及封裝在仿生水凝膠中的干細胞的依賴機械傳感的分化。我們將進一步研究幹細胞增強機械傳感依賴性分化的分子機制。我們將評估結構仿生水凝膠作為乾細胞的傳遞載體在動物模型中促進原位組織再生的功效。 該項目的發現將為人工合成3D生物材料基質的設計提供有價值的指導。這不僅將有助於在可控的仿生3D微環境中對乾細胞進行進一步的基礎研究，而且還將促進乾細胞的一系列臨床轉化應用。

14202920.label: Realisation of objectives
14202920.value: In this work, we assembled a biomimetic hyaluronic acid nanocomposite hydrogel (HA-BP hydrogel) by coordination bonds with bisphosphonates (BPs), which are anti-osteoclastic drugs. The HA-BP hydrogel exhibited expedited release of the loaded BP in response to an acidic environment. Our in vitro studies showed that the HA-BP hydrogel inhibits mature osteoclastic differentiation of macrophage-like RAW264.7 cells via the released BP. Furthermore, the HA-BP hydrogel can support the initial differentiation of primary macrophages to preosteoclasts, which are considered essential during bone regeneration, whereas further differentiation to mature osteoclasts is effectively inhibited by the HA-BP hydrogel via the released BP. The in vivo evaluation showed that the HA-BP hydrogel can enhance the in situ regeneration of bone. Our work demonstrates a promising strategy to design biomimetic biomaterial scaffolds capable of regulating bone homeostasis to promote bone regeneration. We introduce a peptide fiber-reinforced hydrogel in which the stiff s-sheet fiber functions as a multivalent cross-linker to enhance the hydrogel’s macroscopic stability. The dynamic imine cross-link between the peptide fiber and polymer network endows the hydrogel with a microscopically dynamic network. The obtained fibrillar nanocomposite hydrogel, with its cell-adaptable dynamic network, enhances cell−matrix and cell−cell interactions and therefore significantly promotes the mechanotransduction, metabolic energetics, and osteogenesis of encapsulated stem cells. Furthermore, the hydrogel can codeliver a fiber-attached inductive drug to further enhance osteogenesis and bone regeneration. We believe that our work provides valuable guidance for the design of cell-adaptive and bioactive biomaterials for therapeutic applications. Cellular energetics plays an important role in tissue regeneration, and the enhanced metabolic activity of delivered stem cells can accelerate tissue repair and regeneration. However, conventional hydrogels with limited network cell adaptability restrict cell–cell interactions and cell metabolic activities. In this work, it is shown that a cell-adaptable hydrogel with high network dynamics enhances the glucose uptake and fatty acid 𝜷-oxidation of encapsulated human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) compared with a hydrogel with low network dynamics. It is further shown that the hMSCs encapsulated in the high dynamic hydrogels exhibit increased tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle activity, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) biosynthesis via an E-cadherin- and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent mechanism. The in vivo evaluation further showed that the delivery of MSCs by the dynamic hydrogel enhanced in situ bone regeneration in an animal model. It is believed that the findings provide critical insights into the impact of stem cell–biomaterial interactions on cellular metabolic energetics and the underlying mechanisms.
