14203020.label: Project Objectives
14203020.value: Develop a new laser nanomanufacturing platform based on the concept of temporal focusing and ultrafast LIPSS that together enable 2-D and 3-D parallel laser machining with sub-wavelength resolution. Develop models and experimental methods to engineer the light sheet generated by temporal focusing with goals to control the intensity, thickness, 2-D & 3-D geometries, and the position of the light sheet. Generate complex periodic nanoscale structures via temporal focusing-based LIPSS with single and double femtosecond beams, such as light-trapping structures on thin film photovoltaic materials, hierarchical superhydrophobic surfaces etc. Develop multi-physics molecular dynamics (MD) models to investigate the formation mechanism of LIPSS. Study and characterize the temporal focusing LIPSS processes on selected material systems, including metals (i.e., tungsten and gold) and semiconductors (i.e., silicon). 14203020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203020.value: This proposal aims to (1) develop a new nanofabricating method for enhancing the resolution and controllability of laser induced periodic surface structuring (LIPSS) via temporal focusing; and (2) study the formation mechanism of LIPSS via molecular dynamics simulation and pump-probe systems. To achieve the goal, an ultrafast laser will be spatially and temporally focused to an area of interest to confine the pulse energy and the LIPSS processing field within a thin sheet of light (<1µm). Accordingly, the fabrication results can be enhanced by adjusting the characteristics of the light sheet, including the thickness, intensity, 2-D, and 3-D geometries. Ultrafast lasers have been extensively used in micromachining due to their unique characteristics. For example, they can process practically any material with high precision and minimal thermal damage through the control of laser fluence. Present manufacturing approach based on scanning the laser focus is sequential and inherently slow. LIPSS may address the issue as it is an area processing method with sub-wavelength resolution. However, currently the formation mechanism of multi-beam LIPSS processes are not fully understood; and the fabrication results are limited to simple 2-D periodic patterns. To improve the fabrication resolution and realize 3-D nanofabrication via LIPSS, we propose to combine temporal focusing with the LIPSS system, i.e., a digital micromirror device (DMD) diffracts the femtosecond laser and subsequently the spatially chirped pulses are temporally focused on the sample, inducing LIPSS. Importantly, the DMD will simultaneously be used to modulate the beam intensity profile and rapidly form arbitrary 2-D patterns for micromachining. Next, we will engineer the light sheet to form patterned 3-D surfaces, where LIPSS is induced on nonplanar substrates for precise nano-patterning. To study the formation mechanism of LIPSS, multi-physics molecular dynamics simulations will be performed; and a pump-probe system will be built to verify the model and reveal the ultrafast formation process of LIPSS by monitoring the temporal evolution of the electron density distribution on the target surface. Lastly, we will study and characterize two material systems, i.e., metals and semiconductors. The results will guide us to design and generate complex LIPSS patterns and predict best processing parameters. The result of this work will substantially improve the precision and throughput of ultrafast laser machining and the fundamental understanding of LIPSS. The results may be used in a variety of scientific and engineering applications, e.g., fabrication of functional surfaces such as superhydrophobic or antibacterial at arbitrarily selected areas. 本項目旨在（1）開發一種新的納米製造方法，通過時域聚焦的方法增強激光誘導製造周期性表面結構（LIPSS）的分辨率和可控性；（2）通過分子動力學模擬和泵浦-探測系統研究LIPSS的形成機理。為了實現這一目標，將在空間和時間上將超快激光聚焦，將脈衝能量和LIPSS處理場限制在一薄光片（<1µm）內。因此，通過調整光片的特性，包括厚度，強度，2-D和3-D幾何形狀，可以提高製造結果。 超快激光由於其獨特的性能已被廣泛用於微加工中。例如，通過控制激光能量密度，它可以以高精度及低熱損傷來處理任何材料。當前激光製造的主流方法是以振鏡掃描激光焦點，速度緩慢。由於LIPSS是一種具有亞波長分辨率的面加工方法，因此可以解決點掃描的限制。目前對多光束LIPSS工藝的形成機理尚不完全了解。並且製造結果僅限於簡單的二維周期性圖案。 為了提高製造分辨率並通過LIPSS實現3-D納米製造，我們將時域聚焦與LIPSS技術結合使用，即以數字微鏡器件（DMD）衍射飛秒激光，隨後將分散的激光光譜聚焦在樣品上，誘發LIPSS。在此系統中，DMD將同時用於調製光束強度輪廓，并快速形成用於微加工的任意二維圖案。接下來，我們將設計光片以形成圖案化的3D表面，在非平面基板上產生LIPSS以製造精確的納米圖案。為了研究LIPSS的形成機理，將進行多物理場分子動力學模擬。然後將建立一個泵浦-探測系統，以驗證模型並通過監視目標表面電子密度分佈的時間演變來揭示LIPSS的超快形成過程。最後，我們將研究和表徵兩種材料系統，即金屬和半導體。結果將指導我們設計和生成複雜的LIPSS圖案，並預測最佳處理參數。 這項工作的結果將提高超快激光加工的精度和生產率，並提高對LIPSS的基本了解。結果可用於各種科學和工程應用中，例如在任意選擇的區域製造功能性表面，如超疏水或抗菌表面。

14203020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203020.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a parallel laser fabrication system based on temporal focusing and LIPSS. The system was integrated with a custom-built pump-probe module to study the ultrafast evolution process of electron density distribution on laser irradiated target surfaces, which induces the formation of different LIPSS structures. In the experiments, we used single and double femtosecond laser beams to generate many sub-diffraction limit complex structures, including hexagonally arranged nanoholes, nano-square array, and periodic ripples etc., on silicon, gold, and tungsten substrates. Assisted by the analytical model and MD model, for the first time we understood and investigated the formation process of these nano-structures. Specifically, the formation mechanisms of the nanostructures can be explained and predicted by the coupled mode theory, where a transient plasmonic waveguide array (TPWA) is formed by the interference between the preceding laser and the induced surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). The SPPs induced by the subsequent laser propagates through the TPWA, resulting in conical diffraction, which demonstrates the first practical application of the massless Dirac dynamics in nanofabrication, a major step in understanding LIPSS. (Part C: Research Output #1 and #7) In parallel, inspired by the concept of temporal focusing and programmable light sheet, we have developed a new multi-material 3D nanofabrication platform based on hydrogel substrates, achieving record-breaking speed (466 mm3/hr), resolution (20 nm), and material variety. The results have been published in Science (Research Output #8). By applying multi-focus scanning, our team has realized stich-free ultrafast two-photon lithography at a record printing rate of 2,000,000 voxels/sec (Research Output #9 and #4). We also developed new femtosecond laser designs to improve the fabrication results (Research Output #10). With the project fund support, we also developed advanced fluorescent imaging systems via digital holography (Research Output #2, #3, and #5). Lastly, an invited review paper on micro-additive manufacturing was published in 2020 (Research Output #6).

14203020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203020.value: In this study, the concept of spatial and temporal focusing was developed and applied to a regenerative femtosecond laser amplifier to generate a programmable light sheet for generating complex sub-diffraction limit patterns at high throughput on silicon and metal substrates. The enhanced understanding of LIPSS structures will allow us to generate more 2D and 3D LIPSS structures/patterns for different engineering applications. On the other hand, during the project, the femtosecond light sheet was also applied to hydrogel substrates, which enables a new class of 3D nanofabrication method that can achieve 20 nm resolution for a wide variety of materials, including metals, semiconductors, polymers and even bio-materials. These results provide a solid foundation to design and fabricate functional micro- and nanodevices at large scale. A GRF proposal based on the extension of this idea was award in 2024. (“High-throughput 3D Nanofabrication based on Line-illumination Temporal Focusing,” General Research Fund, CUHK 14211224, 8/2024 - 7/2027.)

14203020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203020.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a parallel laser fabrication system based on temporal focusing and laser induced periodic surface structuring (LIPSS), which enables low-cost and large-scale fabrication of nanoscale 2D and 3D structures for many emerging engineering applications, such as superhydrophobicity and light-trapping etc. To better understand the LIPSS process, we designed a pump-probe spectroscopy system, which was integrated with the fabrication platform, to study the nanostructure formation process in situ. The results show our system can rapidly generate a suite of complex nanostructures, including hexagonally arranged nanoholes, nano-square array, and periodic ripples etc., on silicon, gold, and tungsten substrates. The substantially enhanced resolution, fabrication rate, and reproducibility of LIPSS structures warrant their application in real world engineering fields.

14203420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203420.value: HomeSense：一種基於聯合學習進行家庭活動識別的普適系統

14203420.label: Project Objectives
14203420.value: We will develop a novel clustered federated multi-task learning (cMTL) framework for home activity recognition. cMTL solves a new optimization problem through collaboration between server and distributed nodes, with the objective of maximizing the overall learning accuracy while capturing the clustered structure among the local models. cMTL explores the similarities that naturally exist in many nodes (e.g., the nodes that reside in the same home or a population with common behavior/physical pat-terns due to diseases like dementia). In addition, cMTL only requires each node to share model loss or weight gradients, which not only preserves user privacy, but also significantly reduces communication overhead, compared with existing federated learning paradigms. We will design a suite of lightweight acoustic/motion features and local data fusion schemes based on in-depth analysis of data we collected from multiple families. These features can be extracted in real-time on device and preserve the characteristics of home activities. They will enable HomeSense to achieve robust performance for complex, concurrent, and potentially interfering family activities, such as recognizing conversations and participants of a family dinner accompanied by TV viewing. We will develop a novel approach called Automated Local Learning, which optimizes the local learning accuracy subject to the given bounds on compute and communication overhead. This approach draws on AutoML, automatically searching for the structure (including dropout rate and number of training epochs) of local model while accounting for the compute and communication resource constraints. We will develop a new method called Adaptive Local Model Update that enables a device to selectively update its own model based on the local learning accuracy and the impact on global convergence of federated learning. We will develop an experimental testbed of smartwatches and smartphones for sensor data collection and performance measurement. We will recruit 20 volunteer families (totally around 50 subjects) for evaluating the real-world performance of our systems in comparison of state-of-the-art activity recognition systems. Lastly, we will work with experts in aging research community to validate the results and transfer the technologies by leveraging our existing collaborations and new collaborations to be initiated in this project.

14203420.value: 研究家庭活動對於健康，社會學和家庭經濟至關重要。例如癡呆症和兒童肥胖的危險因素與家庭的日常活動密切關聯。活動記錄被證明是一種有效的提高自我意識並激勵人們改變自己的行為以適應健康的生活方式的方法。但是迄今為止還沒有一種簡便易行的便捷方法來記錄家庭活動。該項目旨在開發一個名為HomeSense的系統，利用無處不在的智能設備來識別重要的家庭活動。基於聯邦學習，本系統使智能設備能夠協同改進而無需共享傳感器數據，因此可確保家庭活動感應的準確性並保護用戶隱私。首先，我們提出了一個新穎的聯邦多任務學習框架， 通過利用本地學習中的類似結構任務，我們的方法不僅可以提高系統精度，還可以減少訓練和通信開銷。其次，我們將設計一套輕巧的聲學/運動特徵和數據融合算法。這些功能可以在設備上實時提取並捕獲複雜的多個家庭活動的特徵。第三，我們提出一種新穎的自動本地學習方法，在考慮計算和通信資源的情況下自動搜索局部模型的結構約束。第四，我們提出了一種自適應局部模型更新方法，該方法可以根據本地學習的準確性和對聯合學習的全局影響更新本地模型。

14203420.label: Realisation of objectives
14203420.value: Objective 1. We complete the design and implementation of ClusterFL, a similarity-aware federated learning system designed to achieve high model accuracy with low communication overhead for human activity recognition applications. ClusterFL uses the cluster-wise straggler dropout and correlation-based node selection to detect to detect events in home environments while significantly accelerating convergence without compromising accuracy. We evaluated performance of ClusterFL on an NVIDIA edge testbed using collected human activity recognition datasets. The results show that ClusterFL outperforms several state-of-the-art federated learning paradigms in overall accuracy and improves model accuracy for the majority of nodes. Additionally, the two communication optimization mechanisms in ClusterFL reduce communication time by over 50% while maintaining accuracy improvements across various system settings, demonstrating its scalability and effectiveness. Objective 2. We complete the design and implementation of a multi-modal sensor system capable of extracting acoustic and motion features for the automated, privacy-preserving detection of dyadic digital biomarkers of Expressed Emotion (EE). Specifically, our system integrates motor and acoustic biomarkers collected through depth cameras and microphones installed in the homes of dementia patients, enabling objective and scalable detection of EE. To evaluate the system’s performance, we deployed it in the homes of 99 dementia patients and their caregivers in Hong Kong SAR, China, collecting data over one month. Among these, 66 participants provided valid data for analysis. The results indicate that our EE detection algorithm achieved an AUROC of 94.29%. Objective 3. We complete the design and implementation of a novel federated learning system designed to enable dynamic runtime inference through multi-scale training, focusing on optimizing local learning accuracy while adhering to compute and communication overhead constraints. This system leverages data resolution to automatically determine the optimal resolution for training data. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative frame resolution selection strategy for inference, based on the similarity of adjacent frames. To further enhance efficiency, we incorporate a latency-based dynamic data-dropping mechanism, which systematically reduces overall training time by minimizing waiting times in FL while respecting resource limitations. For evaluation, we develop two real-world FL testbeds targeting smart vehicle and healthcare applications, utilizing a heterogeneous edge platform to demonstrate the system's effectiveness and robustness. Objective 4. We complete the design and implementation of EdgeML, an AutoML framework that offers flexible and fine-grained control over DNN model execution by integrating a workload offloading mechanism with a dynamic progressive neural architecture. To achieve an optimal balance between latency, accuracy, and energy efficiency on edge platforms, EdgeML leverages reinforcement learning to automatically update model execution policies in real-time based on runtime dynamics. We have implemented EdgeML for several widely used DNN models on the latest edge devices, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability in edge computing environments. Objective 5. We validate the design of the proposed systems and evaluated their performance through real-world experiments involving over 50 volunteers in 20 families in Hong Kong. The results demonstrate that our proposed systems outperform existing state-of-the-art systems across various settings.

We will design a suite of lightweight acoustic/motion features and local data fusion schemes based on in-depth analysis of data we collected from multiple families. These features can be extracted in real-time on device and preserve the characteristics of home activities. They will enable HomeSense to achieve robust performance for complex, concurrent, and potentially interfering family activities, such as recognizing conversations and participants of a family dinner accompanied by TV viewing.

We will develop a novel approach called Automated Local Learning, which optimizes the local learning accuracy subject to the given bounds on compute and communication overhead. This approach draws on AutoML, automatically searching for the structure (including dropout rate and number of training epochs) of local model while accounting for the compute and communication resource constraints.

We will develop a new method called Adaptive Local Model Update that enables a device to selectively update its own model based on the local learning accuracy and the impact on global convergence of federated learning.

We will develop an experimental testbed of smartwatches and smartphones for sensor data collection and performance measurement. We will recruit 20 volunteer families (totally around 50 subjects) for evaluating the real-world performance of our systems in comparison of state-of-the-art activity recognition systems. Lastly, we will work with experts in aging research community to validate the results and transfer the technologies by leveraging our existing collaborations and new collaborations to be initiated in this project.

14203420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203420.value: 1. We propose ClusterFL [1], a similarity-aware federated learning system designed to achieve high model accuracy with low communication overhead for human activity recognition applications. ClusterFL introduces a novel clustered multi-task federated learning framework that enhances training accuracy across multiple learned models while automatically identifying the intrinsic clustering relationships among data from different nodes. Leveraging these learned cluster relationships, ClusterFL employs two key mechanisms: cluster-wise straggler dropout and correlation-based node selection. These mechanisms efficiently exclude nodes that either converge slowly or have minimal correlation with other nodes within each cluster, thereby significantly accelerating convergence without compromising accuracy. 2. We introduce EdgeML [2], an AutoML framework designed to provide flexible and fine-grained control over Deep Neural Network (DNN) model execution by integrating a workload offloading mechanism with a dynamic progressive neural architecture. To achieve an optimal balance among latency, accuracy, and energy efficiency on edge platforms, EdgeML leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adapt its model execution policy in response to real-time runtime conditions. 3. We propose BalanceFL [3], a federated learning framework designed to robustly handle both common and rare classes in long-tailed real-world datasets, effectively addressing global and local data imbalances simultaneously. Unlike traditional approaches where nodes upload class-drifted models trained on imbalanced private data, BalanceFL introduces a novel local update scheme that corrects class imbalances. This scheme ensures that local models behave as if they were trained on ideally balanced, uniformly distributed data, thereby improving the learning performance across all classes. 14203420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203420.value: Objective 1. Data quality plays a crucial role in Home Activity Recognition. In future research, we will incorporate tools and methods to assess and enhance data quality. This will enable a deeper analysis of the factors affecting recognition accuracy and consistency, providing valuable insights for improving system performance and reliability in real-world applications. Objective 2. We note that in real-world scenarios, the long-tailed distribution of training data may differ significantly from that of testing data, which poses challenges for accurate and robust IMU-based analysis. This discrepancy highlights the need for further investigation into the effects of distributional differences on model performance. In future work, we aim to perform an in-depth analysis of these long-tailed distributions, focusing on how variations in activity frequency, intensity, and user diversity impact the generalizability of IMU-based models. By addressing these challenges, we hope to improve the robustness and applicability of such models in real-world settings.

14203420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203420.value: Home Activity Recognition (HAR) plays an important role in understanding and improving daily living experiences, particularly for individuals in need of health monitoring, such as older adults or those with chronic conditions. HAR has numerous applications, ranging from identifying irregular activity patterns for early health intervention, assisting in rehabilitation programs by tracking physical activities, to improving the management of smart homes through personalized automation. However, existing systems often rely on complex setups, expensive equipment, or intrusive monitoring, making them unsuitable for everyday use. This project develops a novel and practical system for home activity recognition using affordable and widely available sensors, such as those in smartphones, wearables, and home IoT devices via federated learning. The system operates in a privacy-preserving manner, ensuring that sensitive information remains secure while providing real-time feedback on activity patterns. Specifically, it helps users monitor their daily routines, detect unusual behaviors, and support caregivers in managing health and safety. This unobtrusive solution makes home activity recognition accessible, personalized, and scalable, offering long-term benefits for health, wellness, and smart home applications.

14203620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203620.value: Mode division multiplexing in few-mode or multimode optical fibres is one of the most promising emerging technologies which can enable optical fibre interconnects to increase their data transmission capacity and improve the bandwidth density needed in data center interconnects. This project is aimed at making mode division multiplexing suitable for practical use in future data center optical interconnects. The introduction of mode division multiplexing will facilitate the enormous increases in data transmission capacity needed for meeting the continuing exponential increases of data traffic in data centers and the internet. In this proposal we shall design and experimentally validate a novel device which can provide the fully integrated interface between industry standard multimode fibres and future integrated mode division multiplexed optical transceivers. Unlike the previously demonstrated approach of using direct laser writing to craft a three-dimensional optical waveguide array (photonic lantern) for launching light into a multimode fiber, the proposed device can be made using mature and standard semiconductor manufacturing processes available in a foundry, and can thus be easily scaled to large volume production. The proposed multimode waveguide grating coupler introduces a novel method for launching mode multiplexed signals into multimode optical fibres and avoids the need for using any additional fibre devices or free space optics to separate out the modes in the multimode fiber into an array of single mode fibers. The proposed multimode waveguide grating coupler thus offers a compact and direct interface between the multimode fiber and future mode division multiplexed integrated optical transceiver. In order to demonstrate the capability of the proposed multimode waveguide grating coupler to simultaneously launch different data channels into different degenerate mode groups of a graded index multimode optical fibre, we shall integrate the novel multimode waveguide grating coupler with the standard micro-ring optical modulators and integrated waveguide photodetectors available from commercial foundries. We shall design on-chip mode multiplexers to combine different data channels into a mode-multiplexed silicon multimode waveguide which is connected via the proposed multimode grating coupler to the multimode fibre. The project aims to demonstrate the capability of launching six different data channels into different mode groups of a multimode fibre using the multimode silicon waveguide grating coupler. If successful, the project will lead to the world’s first monolithic integrated mode division multiplexed optical transceiver which can operate with existing industry-standard graded-index multimode optical fibres. 多模光纖中的模分復用是最有前途的新興技術之壹，可以大幅增加光纖互連數據傳輸容量並顯著提高數據中心互聯帶寬密度。該項目旨在實現模分復用技術在未來數據中心光互連的實際應用。在這個項目中，我們將設計並實驗驗證壹種新穎的設備，即多模波導光柵耦合器，它可以為標準多模光纖和模分復用光收發器之間提供完全集成的光接口。我們設計的器件可以使用代工廠中標準生成工藝來制作，因此可以輕松地進行大規模生產。我們所提出的多模波導光柵耦合器可以將多路模分復用信號耦合到標準多模光纖中並解復用到單模光纖陣列中，整個過程無需使用任何其他額外光纖設備或自由空間光學器件。我們將把設計的多模波導光柵耦合器與光電調制器和探測器進行集成，並且設計片上多模復用系統，以將不同的數據通道耦合到與多模光纖相連的多模波導中。該項目旨在展示使用多模波導光柵耦合器將多達6個不同的數據通道耦合到多模光纖不同模式中的可行性。如果成功，該項目將實現壹個單片集成模分復用光收發系統，該系統可以與行業標準的漸變折射率多模光纖進行集成。

14203620.label: Realisation of objectives
14203620.value: In this project we completed the detailed designs for multimode waveguide grating couplers which can launch 3 different spatial modes (TE0, TE1 and TE3) into the LP01, LP11 and LP 12 modes of OM4 multimode fiber [1] and our 3D FDTD simulations predicted insertion losses between -3.8dB to -4.4dB for the selective launch of the three different modes [Objective 1]. We also fabricated and tested the performance of multimode silicon waveguide couplers, and introduced a new design geometry which greatly improved the performance of grating couplers by the use of a novel shifted polysilicon overlay grating above the silicon grating: By proper positioning of the polysilicon grating on top of the silicon grating we showed the structure could improve the directionality and mode matching of the whole device, and thus enable a reduction of losses which were experimentally confirmed to reduce the insertion loss down to -1.3dB for the coupling between the TE1 mode and the fiber LP01 mode, and -2.21dB for coupling of the TE2 mode to the LP11 modes of few-mode fiber respectively [2] (Objective 2). The same approach could be used to improve the coupling efficiency to single mode fibers, and attain a record low loss of 0.89dB for a foundry fabricated grating which did not have any bottom metal mirrors to improve directionality, nor required the use of feature sizes below 170nm [3]. We also found that the shifted polysilicon overlay grating could be used to make the first truly polarization independent grating couplers, and these are important for use in integrated optical receivers when the optical polarization arriving at the receiver is randomly orientated [4]. Using actively controlled phase shifters to control the phase of different waveguide modes launched by two orthogonally orientated waveguides to a two-dimensional grating structure, we were able to demonstrate the successful launch of 8 different spatial and polarization modes in few mode fibers [5] [objective 1 and 2]. This work made use of our patented Mikaelian lens mode size convertor, the concept of which was conceived during the writing of the proposal for this project and we were able to quickly demonstrate the proof of concept for the Mikaelian lens mode size converter for multimode grating coupler [6] by using our university's clean room facility to make the device by borrowing the necessary research raw materials (after the project funding was announced but before the funding for the project was received) [6]. To enable the use of mode division multiplexing with distinct data lanes transmitted by different mode channels [objective 1 and objective 4], it is also necessary to develop compact integrated modulators which could be integrated in large numbers for the different wavelengths and mode channels that could be supported. We therefore turned our attention to modulators which did not require the larger footprint of Mach Zehnder modulators, and we developed compact silicon modulators based the Franz-Keldysh effect electro-absorption modulators [7], and silicon microring modulators [8] for PAM4 modulation at over 100Gbaud per data lane [objective 4]. To mitigate the mode mixing and crosstalk between different data lanes in mode division multiplexed transmission we also developed the photonic signal processor for unscrambling the crosstalk using integrated interferometers to implement the optical unitary matrix operations for mode unscrambling [9] (Objective 3 and Objective 4). Another problem that hinders the development of mode division multiplexing optical fiber communications with our integrated multimode waveguide grating couplers is the randomly orientated spatial modes arriving at the receiving multimode grating coupler, which can introduce large coupling losses because of the misalignment of the spatial modes with the intensity pattern needed for efficient diffraction into the waveguide modes. We developed a novel solution to this problem by using phase control at the transmitter to control the orientation of the spatial modes at the distal end of the fiber [10] [Objective 3 and objective 4]. Finally as an example of the use of the multimode waveguide grating in a communication system [Objective 4] we collaborated with Peking University in developing a quantum key distribution communications system which used the novel multimode grating couplers developed in this project to launch different spatial and polarization modes from the integrated source of entangled photon pairs and we successfully showed that we could build a large scale quantum entanglement distribution network for use in quantum secured communications involving the use of different spatial and polarization modes to distribute the four dimensional Bell state entangled photon pairs generated by the integrated microring resonators [11] [Objective 4]. 14203620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203620.value: The main outcomes of this research include 1. Advances in the technologies for multimode waveguide grating coupler, including how to reduce their insertion losses to under 2dB and how to control the spatial mode pattern at the distal end to ensure high coupling efficiency at the receiver. 2. Advances in the technology of how to mitigate mode crosstalk introduced in the transmission of different spatial modes in optical fibers: we developed novel integrated photonic signal processors which we demonstrated experimentally to unscramble the mode crosstalk introduced in fiber transmission. 3. Demonstration of the feasibility of using the multimode grating couplers with few mode fibers for optical communications using the different spatial modes to transmit different information lanes. The technoology was also demonstrated experimentally for use in high order quantum entanglement distribution in a collaboration with Peking university and published in Science, 381 (6654), 221-226 2023.

14203620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203620.value: There is enormous potential for this technology of mode division multiplexing (MDM) to make a great impact in optical fiber communications systems. By using different modes to transmit different data lanes the impact may become as important as the introduction of wavelength division multiplexing which used different wavelengths to transmit different data lanes. As one of the first groups to develop the silicon photonics technology to enable MDM in multimode fibers, we seek collaborations with more groups around the world to disseminate our advances, and perhaps explore the possibility to commercialize this technology. Students graduating from this project are forming a spin-off company OptiHK Ltd to commercialize the technology.

14203620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203620.value: In this project we showed how silicon photonics could be used to increase the number of data lanes in multimode fiber communications by using the different spatial modes in multimode fiber to transmit different data lanes. The technological advances in this project enabled the practical coupling of light from different spatial modes in multimode silicon waveguides to different spatial modes in optical fibers. Furthermore we showed how to correct for the mixing of modes from mode-coupling during the optical fiber transmission by using integrated silicon photonic signal processors which implemented the unitary matrix operations to recover the original data lanes despite the mode mixing. We also demonstrated how the multimode grating coupler could be used to launch different modes in few mode fiber and build a multi-chip multidimensional quantum network with entanglement self-retrieving that may find applications in quantum secured communications and distributed quantum computing. In summary the academic research results achieved in this project could have the potential to be used in next generation optical fiber communications as it provides a practical solution to increase the number of data channels and data transmission capacity of multimode fibers.

14203920.value: 經驗風險最小化乃機器學習中經常出現的一類優化問題。為了解決學習過程中的過度擬合，一般會在目標函數裏加上一個正則函數。近年來，不同的研究結果發現正則化方法跟分佈魯棒優化有著密切的關係，而且從分佈魯棒優化的角度出發更能解釋不同正則函數的統計意義。可是迄今爲止，求解分佈魯棒優化問題大致上就只有内點算法，而這類算法并不能有效地解決大規模的學習問題。這項研究的目的是要提出能有效解決大規模學習問題的分佈魯棒優化算法框架，並從理論上分析這類算法的收斂性能，使分佈魯棒優化的好處能在機器學習問題上體現出來。

14203920.label: Realisation of objectives
14203920.value: We achieved Objective 1 in two ways: First, we proposed the first distributionally robust optimization (DRO) formulation of the problem of learning a graph from noisy observations of smooth graph signals. The formulation is designed so that its solution is robust to the uncertainty in the probability distribution that generates the graph signals, which helps to alleviate the problem of overfitting. We showed that the DRO formulation admits an equivalent finite-dimensional non-convex optimization formulation and proposed a projected gradient-type method to solve the latter. We then established the global convergence of the proposed method under the assumption that the objective function has a locally Lipschitz gradient, which is satisfied by a wide variety of graph learning tasks. Our work also provides a new perspective on regularization in the graph learning setting. Second, we designed the first first-order method, called the inexact linearized proximal alternating direction method of multipliers, for solving Wasserstein distance-based DRO formulations of a class of regression and classification problems in machine learning. Our proposed method exploits the structure of the said class of problems and achieves up to a thousandfold speedup over existing methods. We then established the convergence rate of the proposed method under various settings. The work opens up an exciting new direction for DRO research and also contributes to Objective 2 of this project. We achieved Objective 2 also in two ways: First, we proposed a novel universally applicable single-loop algorithm that is capable of solving non-convex--concave, convex--non-concave, and non-convex--non-concave with one-sided Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) minimax problems. These minimax problems encapsulate different variation-regularized DRO formulations in machine learning. The universality here refers to the algorithm's ability to tackle the said classes of problems without knowing the one-sided information (i.e., convexity, concavity, or KL). We then established sharp iteration complexity results for the proposed algorithm. Second, we considered the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is a powerful modeling technique for aligning heterogeneous data for a wide range of graph learning tasks, and introduced its robust counterpart to address the presence of outliers. The resulting measure, which we call the Robust Gromov-Wasserstein (RGW) distance, is the first of its kind in the literature. To realize the benefits of RGW, we developed a Bregman proximal alternating linearized minimization algorithm. Through extensive numerical experiments, the algorithm was shown to be computationally efficient. Furthermore, we provided theoretical guarantees on the algorithm's convergence behavior.

14203920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203920.value: The major findings of the project have already been summarized in Section 5.3 above. The research outcomes for Objective 1 have led to the publication of a journal article in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, a premier journal in the field of signal processing, and a manuscript that is to be submitted to Mathematical Programming, one of the top journals in the field of mathematical optimization. The research outcomes for Objective 2 have led to two articles that were accepted to the 37th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023), which is one of the top conferences in the field of artificial intelligence.

14203920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203920.value: The outcomes of this project open up several directions for further research. Here, we discuss two of them. First, there has been significant interest in DRO models recently that can facilitate decision making under both perturbations and adversarial contaminations of the data points. These models tend to give rise to non-convex optimization problems, and it is of great interest to develop efficient iterative methods that can find near-optimal solutions to these problems with provable guarantees. Second, many data analytics applications, such as sparse/fair principal component analysis and sparse spectral clustering, involve manifold optimization formulations. It will be interesting to study distributionally robust versions of these formulations, particularly their algorithmic and statistical properties.

14203920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203920.value: In this project, we considered optimization problems whose data are generated by probability distributions that are unknown a priori. We developed novel computationally efficient algorithmic frameworks for computing solutions to such problems that are robust to uncertainties in the probability distributions and provided strong theoretical guarantees for their convergence performance. Our results not only advance the algorithmic theory of distributionally robust optimization but also open up a number new directions for further research.

14204520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204520.value: Severe outdoor air pollution, especially smog, has become a major threat to public health in China. Exposure to PM2.5 of both indoor and outdoor origin occurs in indoor environments, where people spend most of their time. Filtration is among the most effective measures for removing indoor PM2.5. However, traditional high-efficiency HVAC filters usually result in high pressure drop. Therefore, it is worthwhile to develop novel air filters with low pressure drop for effective indoor PM2.5 control. Electrospun nanofiber filters exhibit several advantages over traditional high-efficiency HVAC filters. With the same PM2.5 removal efficiency, nanofiber filters cause a lower pressure drop, and they are thinner, more flexible, and more lightweight. Therefore, nanofiber filters can be potentially installed in indoor fan-driven devices as an add-on filtration component to remove indoor PM2.5. However, few studies, if any, of this novel intervention approach have been reported in the literature. In the proposed project, we will first develop a structure optimization and fabrication method to enhance the performance of nanofiber filters and then install the filters in various fan-driven devices to test their effectiveness in indoor PM2.5 control. This project will start with experiments in a laboratory setup to measure the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop of various nanofiber filters with different materials, filter thicknesses, fiber diameters, and packing densities under different face velocities. Semi-empirical models will be developed for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop using the filter structure parameters. On the basis of the semi-empirical models, a structure optimization method will be developed to determine the specific filter thickness, fiber diameter, and packing density that will achieve the target PM2.5 removal efficiency with the lowest pressure drop. This project will also develop a fabrication method to obtain the optimized filter structure by setting the appropriate electrospinning time and material solution concentration. Finally, this study will install the optimized nanofiber filters as an add-on filtration component in axial fans, fan-driven air cleaners, and air conditioners in real-life apartments and conduct field tests on their long-term performance. The proposed project will increase our understanding of the effects of the filter structure parameters on the performance of electrospun nanofiber filters. The structure optimization and fabrication method will enhance the performance of nanofiber filters as an add-on filtration component in indoor fan-driven devices. The findings from both the laboratory and field tests will advance the development of this novel intervention technology for effective indoor PM2.5 control. 室外空氣污染已經成為公共健康的巨大威脅，其中的細顆粒物污染很容易進入到建築中。而人們大多數時間生活在室內，因此會長期暴露於室內的細顆粒物，從而存在健康風險。空氣過濾是一種有效去除室內細顆粒物的方法。然而，傳統的高效過濾器通常伴隨著較高的壓降損失。因此，我們應當開發低阻高效的空氣過濾器以更有效地控制室內細顆粒物污染。 相較於傳統的高效過濾器，電紡納米纖維過濾器在同樣的過濾效率下，能擁有更低的壓降損失，並且更薄，更靈活，重量更小。因此，納米纖維過濾器可以安裝於室內的風機驅動設備以去除室內的細顆粒物。然而，對於這種創新方法的研究目前還鮮有報道。在此項目中，我們首先將開發一種結構優化及製備方法以提高納米纖維過濾器的性能，並且將其安裝於幾種室內風機驅動設備中以測試其對室內細顆粒物的控制效果。 本項目首先將通過實驗研究以測量不同納米纖維過濾器在不同風速下的過濾效率和壓降。這些過濾器將由不同的材料製備，並且有不同的濾網厚度，纖維直徑，以及組裝密度。基於實驗數據和理論模型，本項目將開發針對於過濾效率和壓降的半經驗公式。基於這些半經驗公式，本項目將開發一種結構優化方法以確定最優的濾網厚度，纖維直徑，和組裝密度以得到在指定過濾效率下最低的壓降損失。此外，本項目還將開發一種基於電紡時間和材料溶液濃度的製備方法。最終，本項目將優化過的納米纖維過濾器安裝於風扇，空氣淨化器，以及家用空調中，並且在實際住宅中進行長期測試，以評估其實際效果。 本項目將會提升我們對電紡納米纖維過濾器的結構參數和性能的理解。所開發的結構優化和製備方法將提升納米纖維過濾器的性能，使其能更好的應用于室內的淨化設備。本項目的理論研究以及實驗室和現場的測試將推進這種新型淨化技術的發展，並且更有效地控制室內的細顆粒物污染。

14204520.label: Realisation of objectives
14204520.value: All of the 6 objectives have been fully achieved. This project fabricated a number of nanofiber air filters by the electrospinning technique with nylon and polyacrylonitrile (PAN) as the nanofiber materials. Nanofiber air filters with different filter structure parameters of fiber diameter, filter thickness, and packing density were prepared. The PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop of each sample were measured at different face velocities. A database was obtained to understand the relationship between PM2.5 removal efficiency/pressure drop and the filter structure parameters for electrospun nanofiber filters. It was found that the PM2.5 removal efficiency was negatively associated with the fiber diameter, and positively associated with the thickness of the filter. However, there was no clear correlation between PM2.5 removal efficiency and packing density. Furthermore, the pressure drop was proportional to the face velocity and filter thickness. The product of drag coefficient and Reynolds number was a function of both packing density and Knudsen number. In general, Objective 1 “To experimentally investigate the relationship between PM2.5 removal efficiency/pressure drop and the filter structure parameters of fiber diameter, filter thickness, and packing density for electrospun nanofiber filters” has been fully achieved. With the experimental data, this project developed semi-empirical models for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop of nanofiber air filters. Based on the database, the dimensionless parameters such as Reynolds number, Knudsen number, Stokes number, Peclet number were calculated. With the dimensionless parameters, the semi-empirical models were developed for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop based on the classic filtration model and the drag force theory, respectively. The developed models were then validated using the experimental data. The results show that the semi-empirical models reasonably predicted the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop of the electrospun nanofiber air filters with a median relative error less than 8% and 5%, respectively. In general, Objective 2 “To develop and validate semi-empirical models for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop of electrospun nanofiber filters using the filter structure parameters of fiber diameter, filter thickness, and packing density” has been fully achieved. With the semi-empirical models, this project proposed an optimization approach to minimize the pressure drop under a given PM2.5 filtration efficiency and face velocity. It was found that, given a specified air velocity and PM2.5 filtration efficiency, the pressure drop can be minimized by identifying the optimal solution concentration based on the semi-empirical models. Meanwhile, adjusting the electrospinning time allows us to reach the desired PM2.5 filtration efficiency. The results show that the proposed optimization approach successfully minimized the pressure drop for electrospun nanofiber air filters with an average reduction of over 30%. In general, Objective 3 “To develop a structure optimization method to identify the specific fiber diameter, filter thickness, and packing density for an electrospun nanofiber filter that will provide the target PM2.5 removal efficiency with the lowest pressure drop” has been fully achieved. To facilitate the fabrication of the optimized nanofiber air filters, this project established the functions between the nanofiber filter parameters and the fabrication parameters. The filter parameters included fiber diameter, filter thickness, and packing density, while the controllable fabrication parameters included the electrospinning time nanofiber material solution concentration, and applied voltage. Experimental data of the nanofiber filter parameters and the fabrication parameters were measured to establish the functions. With the functions, the pressure drop and PM2.5 filtration efficiency of the nanofiber filters can be directly determined from the electrospinning fabrication parameters. In the latest development, this project proposed a more efficient method for producing electrospun nanofiber air filters that achieve a minimized pressure drop while meeting the target particle filtration efficiency. Specifically, this method decoupled the influence of applied voltage and electrospinning time, enabling the identification of the optimal applied voltage to minimize pressure drop and the calculation of the electrospinning time needed to achieve the target filtration efficiency. Compared with the previous approach, this method eliminated the need to measure structural parameters, thereby significantly simplifying the optimization process. In general, Objective 4 “To develop a method for fabricating electrospun nanofiber filters with the desired structure parameters, using the electrospinning parameters of electrospinning time and material solution concentration” has been fully achieved. This project then fabricated large-scale nanofiber air filters using the proposed optimization method, and installed them in fan-driven air cleaners, air conditioners, and mechanical ventilation systems. Specifically, we designed and created a portable, battery-operated air cleaner equipped with these optimized nanofiber air filters. This device was further integrated with a user-tracking robotic car to provide efficient personal air cleaning in large spaces. Additionally, we fabricated thin nanofiber air filters and installed them in split-type and window-type home air conditioners as an add-on component, aiming to reduce indoor PM2.5 levels when the air conditioners operate without ventilation. Moreover, we installed large-scale nanofiber air filters in the mechanical ventilation system of our 7-row full-scale aircraft cabin mockup, which features a high airflow rate, to effectively lower particle concentration within the cabin. In general, Objective 5 “To fabricate nanofiber filters using the structure optimization and fabrication method, and install them as an add-on filtration component in indoor fan-driven devices, including axial fans, fan-driven air cleaners, and air conditioners” has been fully achieved. Finally, this project conducted experimental measurements to test the performance of the optimized nanofiber air filters installed in the fan-driven devices for indoor PM2.5 control. First, we conducted field measurements of a moving person’s exposure to indoor PM2.5 in a large work space with the utilization of the user-tracking robot equipped with nanofiber air cleaner, which successfully achieved lower personal exposure. Second, we conducted filed tests of indoor PM2.5 concentrations in an apartment with a split-type air conditioner and an office with a window-type air conditioner equipped with nanofiber air filters in Hong Kong. However, the indoor PM2.5 levels were not significantly reduced due to the reduction in airflow rate. Finally, we conducted experimental measurements of person-to-person particle transport in the 7-row full-scale aircraft cabin mockup with nanofiber air filters installed in the mechanical ventilation system. It was found that the passengers’ exposure to exhaled particles was significantly reduced compared with the case with HEPA filters. In general, Objective 6 “To conduct field measurements to test the performance of the optimized nanofiber filters as an add-on filtration component in the indoor fan-driven devices for indoor PM2.5 control in a number of apartments” has been fully achieved. Brief responses to the Panel’s comments on Mid-Term Report: 1. The Completion Report has been written in the form of summarizing what was done and achieved. 2. We tried to use PI as the material but found that the mechanical properties were weak. Therefore, we focused on PAN and nylon. 3. Some publications were supported by multiple grants, and we utilized resources such as testbeds and equipment from various projects to enhance the quality of our work. To avoid confusion, the Completion Report includes only those publications that are directly relevant to this specific project. 4. We utilized internal resources to recruit additional manpower for this project. Combined with the manpower funding from the project itself, this allowed us to achieve results of higher quality.

14204520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204520.value: There are two main directions for further advancing this research. First, the structure optimization approach developed in this project was designed for clean electrospun nanofiber air filters. However, dust accumulation over time can adversely affect particle filtration efficiency and pressure drop. Therefore, it would be beneficial to refine the optimization approach to account for dust loading, aiming to achieve optimal performance throughout the entire lifecycle of the nanofiber air filters. Second, leveraging the proposed optimization approach, a technology development project could be initiated to enable the scalable and efficient production of high-quality nanofiber air filters at relatively low costs. Advancements in manufacturing technologies could significantly enhance the practical application of this innovative technology.

14204820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204820.value: Partitioning biochemical reactions in tiny droplets simulates the format of existing microtiter wells in conventional screening, yet there are many unprecedented advantages when the droplets have volumes in the pico- to femto-litre regime. Together with the development of droplet microfluidics, high-throughput analysis of biochemical reactions is made possible with these uniform miniaturised reactors. The increasing demand for digital droplet polymerase chain reaction and single-cell sequencing has made the use of droplet microfluidics for the screening of biochemical reactions appealing. However, practical barriers such as costly surfactants and complicated processing have delayed the wide adoption of droplet microfluidics in the biological and clinical communities. The proposed project will seek to eliminate these barriers by introducing functionalised photoresponsive nanoparticles as a novel class of surfactant that is expected to provide new droplet manipulation techniques fully controlled by light. These photoresponsive nanoparticles will act as both a droplet-stabilising surfactant and as localised plasmons responsive towards light illumination. This project is expected to realise the all-optical manipulation of droplets, as demonstrated by an integrated platform for droplet analysis and sorting fully controlled by light. Such an all-optical controlled platform is expected to significantly simplify microfabrication procedures and equipment setup, allowing widespread use of droplet microfluidics for routine biochemical analysis, particularly in multi-omic single-cell analysis. 將生化反應分配至微小液滴中可模擬常規篩選中現有微量滴定孔的形式，且當液滴的體積在皮升至飛升範圍時，其具有許多前所未有的優勢。隨著液滴微流控技術的發展，這些均勻的微型反應器使生物化學反應的高通量分析成為可能。對液滴數字PCR和單細胞測序的需求不斷增長，也使得使用液滴微流控技術篩選生化反應具有吸引力。然而，諸如表面活性劑昂貴和操作複雜之類的實際障礙，延遲了液滴微流控技術在生物學和臨床中的廣泛使用。擬議的項目將尋求通過引入功能化的光響應納米顆粒作為一類新型的表面活性劑來消除這些障礙，該表面活性劑有望實現完全由光調控的新型液滴操作技術。這些光敏納米顆粒將既充當液滴表面活性劑，又提供對光響應的局域等離子體激元。該項目有望實現對液滴的全光學操作，如集成的平台所演示，用於完全由光調控的液滴分析和分選。這種全光學控制平台有望顯著簡化微細加工程序和設備設置，使液滴微流控技術可廣泛用於常規生化分析，尤其是在多組學單細胞分析中。

14204820.label: Realisation of objectives
14204820.value: The aim of this project is to eliminate barriers to the use of droplet microfluidics by introducing a novel class of gold-nanoparticle-based surfactant, which is expected to provide a new generation of droplet manipulation technique fully controlled by light. The proposed objectives have been realised as the following: Aim 1: Synthesise and Characterise the Fluorinated Nanoparticles as a Surfactant We have developed the synthesis of fluorinated silica-coated AuNPs (f-Au@SiO2) and systematically correlate these geometries with their interfacial characteristics. Task 1-1: Fluorination of Silica-coated Gold Nanoparticles. The core AuNPs were synthesized by the classic Frens method. 10 mL of Na3Ct aqueous solution (38.8 mM) was injected to 100 mL of HAuCl4 aqueous solution (0.9 mM) and the mixture was heated to reflux under vigorous stirring for 20 min. Secondly, a shell of silica was coated onto the gold core by the condensation of Na2SiO3 with APTMS as the surface primer. Briefly, 2.5 mL of APTMS aqueous solution (1 mM) was mixed with 100 mL of AuNPs solution and stirred for 20 min at room temperature. Subsequently, 20 mL of Na2SiO3 aqueous solution (0.54 %, pH = 10.2) was added to the reaction mixture, stirred for 5 min at room temperature. The mixture was then placed in a 90 ̊C water bath under stirring for another 1 hr, which determined the thickness of silica shell. The reaction was stopped by transferring the mixture into the ice bath. The resulting gold-silica core-shell nanoparticles (Au@SiO2) were then washed with water and ethanol followed by centrifugation. Lastly, the Au@SiO2 were functionalized with PFOTES to render the surface fluorophilicity. The Au@SiO2 were concentrated in 40 mL ethanol, where 0.8 mL of ammonia solution (28 %) and 0.2 mL of PFOTES (97 %) were added. The reaction was incubated at room temperature for 24 hrs under sonication, followed by washing and desiccation. The collected solid was weighted, and redispersed in HFE-7500 according to the designated weight percentage. Task 1-2: Characterisation of the Produced f-Au@SiO2 as a Stabiliser. Prior to the droplet formation, the produced f-Au@SiO2 was investigated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The size-characterised f-Au@SiO2 were dispensed in fluorocarbon oil (i.e., HFE-7500 or FC-40) at different concentrations to evaluate its performance as a surfactant between the fluorinated oil and the aqueous phase. Uniform w/o droplets (100 m in diameter) were produced by the previously developed microfluidic flow-focusing droplet generator. The functionality of f-Au@SiO2 as a stabiliser was evaluated from several perspectives: (1) the interfacial tension between the fluorocarbon oil containing f-Au@SiO2 and the water, (2) the attachment of f-Au@SiO2 to the w/o interface as evidenced by confocal microscope observation of Rhodamine B adsorption at the droplet interface, (3) the stability of droplets under the experimental conditions, such as long term incubation, reinjection and heating and (4) the inter-droplet transport of small fluorescent molecules such as Rhodamine B. The obtained characteristics were compared and contrasted with those of commercially available PFPE-PEG and the in-house–prepared silica-NP–based surfactants. Aim 2: Study the Thermoplasmonics of f-Au@SiO2 at the Liquid–Liquid Interface The sample geometries considered in most thermoplasmonic studies are centred on either a two-dimensional (e.g. flat metal nanoarray produced by e-beam lithography) or a three-dimensional (e.g. AuNPs dispersed in a volume, such as within a tumour) geometry. The f-Au@SiO2 surrounding the Pickering emulsions, forming highly ordered AuNPs on a spherical surface, presents a previously unexplored geometry in thermoplasmonics. We have employed theoretical prediction and empirical validation to describe the photothermal responses and the thermodynamics of this unique geometry upon laser illumination. Task 2-1: Considerations for the Photothermal Responses. According to the model established by Baffou, the configuration of f-Au@SiO2 densely packed surrounding the Pickering emulsions renders the distance between thermoplasmonic NPs much shorter than the size of NPs; therefore, the collective photothermal response is dominant. However, due to the coupling of plasmonic effect of f-Au@SiO2 at such a short distance, there is not an analytical solution to calculate the electromagnetic field loss and thus Baffou’s formula is not applicable. Therefore, we have numerically calculated the absorptance of f-Au@SiO2 array based on effective medium theory to account for the light-to-heat conversion effect. Task 2-2: Description of the Light-Induced Thermophoresis. The absorptance calculated in Task 2-1 have been used in a finite element simulation model based on COMSOL Multiphysics to illustrate the temperature profile at the interface of the Pickering emulsion under laser illumination, allowing for the modulation of interfacial tension (i.e. enabling merging of droplets) and the quantitative description of the thermophoretic force (i.e. governing the movement of droplets). We have shown the combinatorial photothermal responses of f-Au@SiO2 array and the resulting temperature distribution at the liquid–liquid interface. Task 2-3: Empirical Measurements of Temperature Profile. Rhodamine B is widely used as an optical thermometer for its temperature-dependent fluorescence quantum yield. Upon illumination, the temperature profiles of both the interior (aqueous phase) and exterior (fluorinated oil) of the droplets will be measured. Although Rhodamine B is soluble in the water, Rhodamine B itself is insoluble in fluorinated oil. However, the interaction of Rhodamine B with fluorocarbons can be mediated by chemicals such as 1H,1H,-perfluorobutan-1-ol. Thus, the photothermal responses of the f-Au@SiO2-stabilised droplets was studied under a static format (i.e. no flow is involved) via measuring the droplet surrounding temperature by a thermocouple. Aim 3: Integrate the Droplets Analysis and Manipulation Modules Combining the above-mentioned development, we have demonstrated the potential of plasmonic NP-based droplets with an integrated platform for droplet analysis and manipulation controlled solely by light. Task 3-1. Light-Mediated Droplet Manipulation. We have demonstrated the optical toolbox enabled by the f-Au@SiO2-produced droplets through optimisation of the input illumination (i.e., laser power and illumination duration) for (a) Droplet Merging, (b) Whole Droplet Moving, (c) On-demand Droplet Sorting, and (d) Heating the Droplet. Task 3-2. Demonstration of the All-Optical Fluorescence-activated Droplet Sorting. We have established the platform technology needed to conduct photothermal fluorescence-activated droplet sorting (PFADS) based on light illumination of the Au@SiO2-stablised droplets. A customised Labview program has also been developed to interface the PMT and FPGA card for issuing a trigger to turn on the 532 nm laser with a proper delay when a positive signal is received by the PMT. A microfluidic device was optimised for the analysis and droplet sorting manipulated by light. The features of droplet sorting such as the sorting speed and error rates was compared with the DEP-based FADS.

14204820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204820.value: The synthesis and applications plasmonic nanoparticle-based fluorosurfactant technology has been patented into two non-provisional US patents [(a) "Light-mediated Manipulation of Droplets Stabilized by Fluorinated Nanoparticles with Photothermal Effect," US Provisional Patent, Application No. 62/892,101, 2019; PCT/CN2020/110715; US Patent No. WO 2021/036967 A1 @ March 4, 2021. (b) "Methods and Apparatus for The Trapping and Rapid Light-driven Selective Release of Droplets," US Provisional Patent, Application No. 63/413,933, 2022; US Patent No. 18/370,820 @ Sep. 20, 2023.] We have wrapped up the findings and the applicability of plasmonic nanoparticle-based fluorosurfactant for droplet manipulation in different configurations. The results are published in three peer-reviewed journal articles [(a) "Photo-Responsive Fluorosurfactant Enabled by Plasmonic Nanoparticles for Light-Driven Droplet Manipulation," ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 13 (18): 21914-21923, 2021. (b) "On-Demand Light-Driven Release of Droplets Stabilized by Photo-Responsive Fluorosurfactant,” Microsystems & Nanoengineering, 9 (1), 89, 2023. (c) "Light-Driven Spatiotemporal Pickering Emulsion Droplet Manipulation Enabled by Plasmonic Hybrid Microgels," Small, 2304207, 2023.] We have also summarised the latest development in the field and published a review article ("Light-Responsive Materials in Droplet Manipulation for Biochemical Applications," Advanced Materials, 2313935, 2024). Given the potentials of this novel fluorosurfactants, our research group has gone to a series of local and international conferences to promote the technologies. To name a few, the technologies are presented in [(a) "Fluorinated Plasmonic Nanoparticles: A Novel Photo-Responsive Surfactant for Droplet Microfluidics," 25th International Conference on Miniaturized Systems for Chemistry and Life Sciences (MicroTAS), Palm Springs, California, USA, 2021, where the presenter Guangyao Cheng has received the LMIC Student/Young Researcher Awards, (b) "Automation of Fluorescence-Activated Droplet Release by Deep Learning-Based Droplet Detector," 28th International Conference on Miniaturized Systems for Chemistry and Life Sciences (MicroTAS), Montreal, Canada, October 2024, and (c) "On-demand Light-driven Release of Droplets Stabilized by A Photo-responsive Fluorosurfactant," IEEE International Conference on Bionanotechnology and BioMEMs (BNM2024), Hong Kong, December 2024.] We have also extended the hardware and software development to build a prototype in a project sponsored by the Innovation and Technology Support Programme in Hong Kong (“Plasmonic Pickering Emulsions-based Bio-Analytic System, Innovation and Technology Support Programme”, Project No: ITS/217/21, HK$ 1,399,644.30, 10/01/2022-09/30/2024), further demonstrating the promising translational capacity of the developed technology.

14204820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204820.value: As part of our collaborative effort with Prof. To NGAI at CUHK, we have furthered the study to practical applications, particularly under the scope of droplet-based polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) and single cell analysis. A project furthering the prototype development was funded by the Innovation Technology Fund in Hong Kong. We are exploring the possibility to commercialize our platform and are in dialogues for potential licensing possibility. Our team members will apply for the Pre-Incubation Centre supported by CUHK, and the Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities to support the subsequent commercialization effort. Our team will also showcase our technologies and seek potential investors by joining the 50th International Exhibition of Inventions to be held in Geneva between April 9-13, 2025 as a delegate of CUHK. In parallel, we have established research collaborations with colleagues in CUHK and other research institutions to explore the possibilities of promoting the platform for single cell analysis for such as single-cell sequencing (Prof. Silin ZHONG, School of Life Sciences, CUHK), single-cell mechanomics (Prof. Youhua TANG, Biomedical Engineering, Hong Kong Polytechnic University), and the analysis of environmental DNA (Prof. Meng YAN, State Key Laboratory of Marine Pollution, City University of Hong Kong).

14205020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205020.value: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is a new vision that in general refers to the application of advanced information and communication technologies in industrial control and manufacturing. Connectivity in today’s factories has until now been dominated by wired systems due to the stringent latency and reliability requirements, which are far beyond what today’s wireless technologies can achieve. Future production systems are expected to meet the demand for flexibility up to a ‘batch size of one’, which is not achievable without more mobile production, more adaptable tools and more dynamic logistics. In such a context, wireline systems will quickly come up against technical and economic limits, and there is an urgent need to develop ultrareliable low-latency wireless communication (URLLWC) techniques for critical IIoT use cases. Motivated by this urgent need, this project aims to systematically design and optimize a noncoherent multiuser massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) framework towards enabling URLLWC for the IIoT. In this framework, the large diversity gain associated with the large-scale antenna array is harnessed to provide ultrahigh reliability. Besides, we apply the noncoherent communication at the physical layer and the non-orthogonal multiple access at the data link layer to effectively reduce the channel estimation delay and the channel access delay, respectively. This is driven by the fact that industrial communication networks are typically based on reduced protocol stacks and the end-to-end latency is dominantly contributed by the bottom two layers. Two practical noncoherent maximum-likelihood (ML) detectors with low implementation complexity, termed symbol-by-symbol detector (SBSD) and joint two-symbol detector (JTSD), are investigated in this proposal, which only need channel statistical information to perform information decoding. In our design, a modulation domain-based non-orthogonal multiple access (MD-NOMA) mechanism is adopted to empower the simultaneous access of multiple users and ensure the unique decoding of their concurrent transmission without the availability of instantaneous channel information. More specifically, in this project we will (i) jointly design and optimize the constellations of multiple users to minimize the system error probability of the SBSD based on its error performance analyzed in our preliminary work, (ii) thoroughly analyze the accurate and asymptotic error performance of the JTSD, and (iii) design and optimize the transmitted signal matrices of multiple users to minimize the system error probability of the JTSD. If successful, this project will present a new wireless communication paradigm that allows the replacement of wireline systems with comparable wireless solution in critical IIoT applications. 工業物聯網（IIoT）是一種新的願景，通常是指先進的信息和通信技術在工業控制和製造中的應用。由於嚴苛的延遲和可靠性要求，這遠遠超出了當今無線技術所能達到的範圍；因此，有線系統在當今工廠的連接性到現在仍佔據統治地位。 未來的生產系統有望滿足“一個批量生產”的靈活性需求，而如果沒有更多的移動生產，更適應性的工具和更動態的物流，這是無法實現的。 在這樣的背景下，有線系統將很快受到技術和經濟上的限制，因此迫切需要為關鍵的IIoT用例開發超可靠低延遲無線通信（URLLWC）技術。 出於這一迫切需求，本項目旨在系統地設計和優化非相干多用戶大規模多輸入多輸出（MIMO）框架，以實現用於IIoT的URLLWC。在此框架中，我們利用大型天線陣列所帶來的大分集增益來提供超高可靠性。此外，我們在物理層應用非相干通信，在數據鏈路層應用非正交多址接入，以分別有效地減少信道估計延遲和信道接入延遲。這是由以下事實驅動的：工業通信網絡通常基於簡化的協議堆棧，最下面的兩層則主要貢獻了端到端延遲。在此提案中，我們將研究兩個實用的，具有較低實現複雜度的非相干最大似然（ML）檢測器，稱為逐符號檢測器（SBSD）和聯合雙符號檢測器（JTSD），它們僅需要信道統計信息即可執行信息解碼。我們擬採用基於調製域的非正交多址訪問（MD-NOMA）機制，以實現多個用戶的同時信道接入，並確保其並發傳輸的唯一解碼在沒有即時信道信息下的可用性。更具體地說，在這個項目中，我們將（i）根據我們在初步工作中分析的錯誤性能，聯合設計和優化多個用戶的星座圖，以最大程度地降低SBSD的系統錯誤概率；（ii）全面分析JTSD機制的準確以及漸近錯誤性能，以及（iii）設計和優化多個用戶的傳輸信號矩陣，以最小化JTSD機制的系統錯誤概率。 如果成功，該項目將提出一種新的無線通信範式，允許在關鍵任務IIoT應用中採用可達相同性能的無線解決方案代替有線系統。

14205020.label: Realisation of objectives
14205020.value: The project has fully achieved all originally stated objectives and has also led to further research directions that go beyond the original scope. The main aim of the project was to systematically design and optimize a noncoherent multiuser massive MIMO framework to enable ultra-reliable low-latency wireless communication (URLLWC) for critical Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications. This involved three core objectives: 1. Joint design and optimization of user constellations for symbol-by-symbol detection (SBSD): This goal was addressed in conference paper #1, which proposed a new joint constellation design framework for two-user noncoherent massive SIMO systems. By leveraging minimum Euclidean distance (MED)-based design criteria and bit-level rate allocation strategies, the work achieved better BER performance than conventional designs, validating the theoretical framework proposed in the project. Conference paper #2 further extended the research to the more general X-channel scenario, where the constellation design methodology was generalized to accommodate the increased complexity and multiple communication pairs inherent in this setting. 2. Accurate and asymptotic error performance analysis of joint two-symbol detector (JTSD): 3. Design and optimization of transmitted signal matrices for JTSD: These two objectives were fulfilled through rigorous theoretical derivations and performance evaluations in journal paper #2. This work developed a uniquely factorable multi-user space-time modulation scheme and optimized transmitted signal matrices based on Kullback–Leibler divergence criteria, ensuring reliable decoding under noncoherent conditions. We further extended the KL-divergence-based design to correlated channels (journal paper #1) under single-user SIMO setup, in which we develop tractable optimization algorithms that significantly improve system error performance under realistic assumptions. All of the above works align directly with the proposal's objectives and demonstrate that the theoretical, algorithmic, and simulation-based goals have been fully realized. These works have been peer-reviewed and published in reputable journals and conferences. Extended Research Contributions During the project’s execution, the research team identified a critical limitation of focusing solely on packet-level latency and reliability: in many real-world status update applications (e.g., in industrial control, sensor monitoring, and robotics), information freshness becomes more critical than just minimizing packet delay. This realization inspired an additional research agenda focused on the Age of Information (AoI) minimization, which better captures the significance of data in real-time applications. This reflection motivated the development of a line of new scheduling and communication protocols, addressing both uplink and downlink scenarios, and covering MIMO, SIMO, device-to-device (D2D), and WiFi networks. Notably: 1. We developed low-complexity dynamic scheduling policies to minimize AoI in uplink MIMO/SIMO status update systems under various system setups. See journal paper #3, journal paper #4, and conference paper #3 for more details. 2. We extended AoI minimization-oriented scheduling strategies to downlink MU-MIMO systems with perfect CSI in conference paper #4. 3. We proposed neural-network-based and heuristic scheduling for D2D networks for AoI optimization. See journal paper #5 and conference paper #5 for more details. 4. We provided the first analytical framework for AoI in WiFi uplink orthogonal frequency division multiple access-based random access networks in journal paper #6. 5. We introduced a Whittle index-based approach for pull-based wireless systems optimizing query-based AoI (QAoI) in journal paper #7. These additional outputs broaden the scope and the potential impact of the project, contributing new knowledge and tools for practical deployment of IIoT networks under real-time constraints. In summary, the project has not only met but exceeded its original objectives. The foundational goals related to constellation design, performance analysis, and multiuser signal processing were fully achieved. Furthermore, the project adapted to address emerging practical challenges by extending into the domain of real-time status update systems and AoI optimization, resulting in a rich body of practically meaningful research.

14205020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205020.value: The project has yielded several meaningful findings and has contributed both theoretically and practically to the field of wireless communication for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications. Major Findings from Original Objectives: 1. A new energy-based joint constellation design was proposed for two-user noncoherent SIMO systems. By optimizing the bit-level rate allocation under average power constraints, the design achieved a larger MED in the received constellation, thus significantly improving BER performance. Similar design and performance gain can be extended to X channels. 2. A uniquely factorable multi-user space-time modulation scheme was proposed to enable noncoherent multiple access with ultra-reliability. A max–min KL divergence-based optimization was developed to jointly design user constellations and transmission powers. The proposed design achieves better reliability performance compared to the state-of-the-art benchmarking schemes. 3. Practical factors such as channel correlation should be properly modeled and considered when designing noncoherent constellations. The KL divergence can also be used as a design criterion under correlated channels. The optimization challenge was overcome using Szegö’s theorem, leading to significant performance gains over uncorrelated benchmarks. Extended Findings on AoI Optimization: 1. AoI-aware Scheduling in Uplink/Downlink MIMO Systems: Dynamic and low-complexity scheduling strategies were developed using POMDPs, Lyapunov optimization, and Whittle index approaches. These methods significantly improve freshness of information in multiuser systems. 2. AoI Optimization in D2D and WiFi Networks: Age-aware link scheduling policies were proposed using graph neural networks and analytical modeling. The results offer practical solutions in D2D and WiFi networks. 3. Query-based AoI Optimization: A new QAoI minimization problem was formulated and addressed using Whittle index theory. The resulting policy achieves near-optimal performance in pull-based networks. Overall outcomes: The project generated 12 high-quality research publications, addressing both the original and extended objectives. These contributions have the potential to contribute to the design of next-generation IIoT networks, enabling ultra-reliable, low-latency, and fresh data transmission.

14205020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205020.value: Building upon the strong theoretical foundations and algorithmic innovations developed in this project, several promising directions have been identified for further research. First, while our current joint constellation design for SBSD in noncoherent massive MIMO systems has been successfully demonstrated in two-user multiple-access and X-channel scenarios, we aim to generalize this framework to support an arbitrary number of users. This extension will significantly enhance the scalability and applicability of the proposed methods in dense IIoT networks. Second, our current consideration of channel correlation is limited to the single-user case. Future work will extend this to multiuser systems for both SBSD and JTSD, enabling more robust and realistic performance analysis and design under practical channel conditions. Third, while our work on AoI optimization assumes perfect CSI, we will develop new scheduling and access strategies for imperfect CSI and noncoherent scenarios, aligning with real-world constraints. Finally, to bridge the gap between theory and deployment, we plan to experimentally validate our proposed schemes using software-defined radios. This will demonstrate the practical feasibility and performance of our designs in real-time wireless IIoT scenarios.

14205020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205020.value: This research project addresses a key challenge in the next generation of smart factories and industrial automation: how to wirelessly send small, critical pieces of information between machines quickly and reliably. Today’s industrial networks mostly rely on wired connections because existing wireless technologies cannot meet the extreme demands for speed and reliability required by machines in manufacturing, power systems, or robotics. However, wired systems are expensive and limit flexibility on the factory floor. To solve this, we designed a new type of wireless system that does not rely on traditional methods of estimating the wireless channel. Instead, it uses innovative signal designs and advanced mathematical tools to ensure ultra-reliable and low-latency communication. Our research showed that noncoherent massive MIMO techniques with carefully designed constellations represent a promising solution to fulfill the stringent performance requirement of industrial wireless networks. During the project, we also identified that in many real-world applications, it is not just speed that matters, freshness of the information is critical. So we developed new scheduling strategies that prioritize sending the most up-to-date data. In the future, we aim to test our designs with real-world experiments towards bringing smarter, more responsive wireless systems to industrial environments.
