14205420.label: Project Objectives
14205420.value: To investigate the fault-error-failure propagation behavior of modern DNN architectures used in safety-critical intelligent systems. The error resilience of a DNN system depends on the system architecture and the data types and values in the design. There is a large body of research in accelerated DNN designs (e.g., various types of DNN compression methods) over the years, and it is crucial to understand the impact of these techniques on DNN reliability and security. We plan to develop high-performance fault simulators to study this issue, and accomplish this objective in the first six months of the project. To develop novel lightweight anomaly detectors for deep neural networks with emphasis on recall. Existing online fault detection techniques for DNN systems typically require high redundancy costs to achieve sufficient fault coverage. We plan to analyze the statistical properties of the inputs and outputs of each layer under transient faults and detect anomalies whenever possible. For the anomaly detector design, we favor recall (i.e., the ability to find all faulty cases) over precision (i.e., the ability to identify only the faulty cases). That is, we strive to reduce the number of missed faults in this step and rely on the following dynamic verification techniques to ensure precision. This objective is expected to be accomplished during the first half period of this project. To design dynamic verification techniques for DNN systems with approximators. The lightweight anomaly detector may lead to some false-positive results (i.e., flag a fault when it does not exist). Triggered by the anomaly detector, the approximator performs dynamic verification in an end-to-end manner to detect whether errors actually propagate to the outputs of the system. Combining these two techniques, we can achieve a better tradeoff between fault coverage and computational cost by the end of this project.

14205420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205420.value: Deep learning with neural networks produces state-of-the-art results that have surpassed human-level performance in many challenging tasks. Therefore, it has become one of the critical enabling technologies in emerging intelligent systems. For example, well-trained deep neural networks (DNNs) are at the heart of self-driving cars to perceive the environment and handle complex traffic scenarios. No doubt to say, the reliability of the DNN itself is of grave concern for such safety-critical intelligent systems. Generally speaking, faults are inevitable in complicated electronic systems, and they may occur due to environmental disturbance, circuit aging, or malicious attacks. DNN-based intelligent systems are no exceptions. They are further susceptible to hardware faults with the ever-shrinking feature size of semiconductor technology used by DNN accelerators and the growing size of the latest DNN models. There were a few fault-tolerant DNN designs proposed in the literature recently. However, most of them require significant overhead to achieve sufficient fault coverage. The goal of this proposal is to develop lightweight fault-tolerant techniques to improve the safety and reliability of DNN-based systems. To achieve this goal, we plan to combine anomaly detection and dynamic verification techniques. To be specific, we will design low-cost anomaly detectors to monitor the input/output properties of each layer in the DNN structure. If an anomaly is detected, we will turn to pre-trained neural networks that are far simpler and smaller than the original DNN for dynamic verification. The key to enabling lightweight checking with the smaller neural networks is that they only need to produce approximate results for the initial task without sacrificing fault coverage much. In the end, we expect that the proposed solution can reduce up to 99% of the errors in deep neural networks at the cost of 5-10% overhead, and it has a transformative impact on how future safety-critical DNN-based systems are designed. 基於神經網絡進行深度學習所產生的最新結果在許多具有挑戰性的任務中已經超過了人類水平。因此，它已成為新興智能係統中的關鍵使能技術之一。例如，深度神經網絡（DNN）是自動駕駛汽車的核心技術之一，用於感知環境並處理複雜的交通情況。毫無疑問，DNN本身的可靠性對於這種智能係統至關重要。 由於環境干擾、電路老化或惡意攻擊，故障在復雜的電子系統中是不可避免的。基於DNN的智能係統當然也不例外。隨著DNN加速器使用的半導體工藝不斷進步以及DNN模型尺寸的不斷擴大，它們也更容易受到硬件故障的影響。未解決這個問題，近期的一些工作提出了多種容錯DNN設計。然而，它們都需要大量開銷才能實現足夠的故障覆蓋率。 本專案的目標是開發輕量級的容錯技術來提高基於DNN的系統的安全性和可靠性。為了實現這一目標，我們計劃將異常檢測與動態驗證技術結合起來。具體來說，我們將設計低成本的異常檢測器，以監視DNN結構中每一層的輸入/輸出屬性。如果檢測到異常，我們將轉向經過預訓練的小型神經網絡進行動態驗證。使用比原始DNN簡單得多的神經網絡進行輕量級檢查的關鍵在於，它們只需要為初始任務生成近似結果，而只會對故障覆蓋率有較小影響。 我們期望所提出的解決方案能夠以5-10％的開銷減少多達99％的深度神經網絡錯誤，對那些安全性至關重要的基於DNN的智能系統設計產生巨大的影響。

14205420.label: Realisation of objectives
14205420.value: We have realized the project objectives in the following aspects. Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become one of the enabling technologies in many safety-critical applications, e.g., autonomous driving and medical image analysis. DNN systems, however, suffer from various kinds of threats, including adversarial example attacks, fault injection attacks, and out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. Moreover, a well-trained DNN often cannot achieve the expected performance after deployment due to the mismatch between the distributions of the training data and the field data in the operational environment. Therefore, repairing DL models is also critical, especially when deployed on increasingly larger tasks with shifted distributions. Generally speaking, it is easy to obtain a large amount of field data. Existing solutions develop various techniques to select a subset for annotation and then fine-tune the model for repair. While effective, achieving a higher repair rate is inevitably associated with more expensive labeling costs. To mitigate this problem, we propose a novel annotation-efficient repair solution for DL models, namely HybridRepair, wherein we take a holistic approach that coordinates the use of a small amount of annotated data and a large amount of unlabeled data for repair. Our key insight is that accurate yet sufficient training data is needed to repair the corresponding failure region in the data distribution. Under a given labeling budget, we selectively annotate some data in failure regions and propagate their labels to the neighboring data on the one hand. On the other hand, we take advantage of the semi-supervised learning (SSL) techniques to further boost the training data density. However, different from existing SSL solutions that try to use all the unlabeled data, we only use a selected part of them considering the impact of distribution shift on SSL solutions. Experimental results show that HybridRepair outperforms both state-of-the-art DL model repair solutions and semi-supervised techniques for model improvements, especially when there is a distribution shift between the training data and the field data. Our code is available at: https://github.com/cure-lab/HybridRepair. We developed AppealNet, a novel edge/cloud collaborative architecture that runs deep learning (DL) tasks more efficiently than state-of-the-art solutions. For a given input, AppealNet accurately predicts on-the-fly whether it can be successfully processed by the DL model deployed on the resource-constrained edge device, and if not, appeals to the more powerful DL model deployed at the cloud. This is achieved by employing a two-head neural network architecture that explicitly takes inference difficulty into consideration and optimizes the tradeoff between accuracy and computation/communication cost of the edge/cloud collaborative architecture. Experimental results on several image classification datasets show up to more than 40% energy savings compared to existing techniques without sacrificing accuracy. While there are many defense methods proposed against maliciously crafted inputs, solutions against faults presented in the DNN system itself (e.g., parameters and calculations) are far less explored. In this paper, we develop a novel lightweight fault-tolerant solution for DNN-based systems, namely DeepDyve, which employs pre-trained neural networks that are far simpler and smaller than the original DNN for dynamic verification. The key to enabling such lightweight checking is that the smaller neural network only needs to produce approximate results for the initial task without sacrificing fault coverage much. We develop efficient and effective architecture and task exploration techniques to achieve optimized risk/overhead trade-off in DeepDyve. Experimental results show that DeepDyve can reduce 90% of the risks at around 10% overhead. Finally, we proposed a novel OOD detection framework named MoodCat for image classifiers. MoodCat masks a random portion of the input image and uses a generative model to synthesize the masked image to a new image conditioned on the classification result. It then calculates the semantic difference between the original image and the synthesized one for OOD detection. Compared to existing solutions, MoodCat naturally learns the semantic information of the in-distribution data with the proposed mask and conditional synthesis strategy, which is critical to identify OODs. Experimental results demonstrate that MoodCat outperforms state-of-the-art OOD detection solutions by a large margin. Our code is available at https://github.com/cure-lab/MOODCat.

The major findings of this project include efficient and effective Edge/Cloud collaborative architecture for deep learning Inference, novel dynamic verification techniques for deep learning, and state-of-the-art deep learning debug and repair solutions for vision tasks. These works have attracted lots of attention in related fields and there are plenty of follow-up works based on our findings.

14205420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205420.value: Recently, large language models (LLMs) have reshaped many domains with their incredible generative capabilities. At the same time, they also pose severe security and reliability concerns. Some of the techniques developed in this project can be adapted to protect LLM-based applications, and we are actively exploring such potential.

14205420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205420.value: Deep learning is a technology that powers many intelligent systems, like self-driving cars, helping them to understand and respond to their environment. However, deep learning systems can be prone to faults, especially due to physical issues like environmental disturbances, aging electronics, or even attacks. These faults are a serious concern for safety-critical applications where reliability is essential. Our research aimed to create a more reliable version of these systems by developing lightweight techniques to detect and address faults in deep neural networks (DNNs). We focused on building low-cost detectors that monitor how the DNN is functioning. When something unusual is detected, a smaller, simpler model steps in to verify the results. This solution helps ensure safety without adding too much extra cost or complexity to the system. The techniques we developed can reduce errors in deep learning systems by up to 95% while keeping additional costs low (about 5-10%). This work paves the way for safer and more efficient use of deep learning in critical applications like autonomous vehicles and other safety-sensitive technologies.

14205520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205520.value: Graph has been widely used to model complex structural relationships among objects in real applications. Real graphs are large in size and are being changed from time to time. To understand such large and complex graphs, many graph algorithms have been developed. Among many graph algorithms, as an example, dense subgraph is studied in social networks, web networks and the like. There are many dense subgraphs being studied from the ones that are hard to solve (e.g., k-clique) to the ones that can be computed in polynomial-time (e.g., k-truss) to the ones that can be computed in linear (e.g., k-core). In the literature, almost all graph algorithms being studied focus on a static graph G, which can be large but is unchanged. In this project, we concentrate ourselves on dynamic graphs rather than static graphs, where graphs will be changed including vertex/edge insertion/deletion. To be more specific, let G be a graph, and assume G is changed to G’ by adding/deleting vertex/edges into/from G denoted as deltaG. In other words, the graph G’ is composed of G and deltaG. Suppose that we need to query (e.g., k-core or k-truss) the graph G’. An important issue is whether we have to query G’ from starch like we do so for G or we can query G’ by utilizing the querying result of G with some additional effort over deltaG. The latter is efficient, since G’ is G plus deltaG and G is large whereas deltaG is small. The graph algorithms to do the latter are incremental graph algorithms. An important issue to be studied for incremental algorithms is the boundedness, which says how much we need to know about “change” in order to find the querying result for G’, where the “change” is related to both the graph change (from G to G’) and the querying result change (from the querying result over G to the querying result over G’). An incremental algorithm is bounded if its cost is bounded in a certain form. In this project, we study new incremental graph algorithms, and explore the boundedness of incremental graph algorithms. The academic significance of the project is of two folds. In addition to conference and journal publications reporting the project finding, the methodology and techniques developed will be implemented in a prototype system to demonstrate the strength of our approach 在實際應用中，圖已被廣泛用於對象之間的複雜結構關係的建模。現實的圖的規模很大，並且會不時更改。為了理解這種大而復雜的圖，已經有許多圖算法被提出和應用。例如，在社交網絡等中研究密集子圖。目前正在研究的密集子圖包括了難以求解的子圖（例如，k-clique）、可以在多項式時間內計算的子圖（例如，k-truss）和可以線性地計算的子圖（例如，k-core）。在文獻中，幾乎所有正在研究的圖算法都集中在靜態圖G上。靜態圖G可能很大，但其結構不會發生變化。在這個項目中，我們將精力集中在動態圖上，而不是靜態圖上，即圖有可能發生頂點/邊的插入/刪除。更具體地講，令G為圖，deltaG表示對G的改變（例如頂點/邊的插入/刪除），G'表示改變后的圖（換句話說，圖G’由G和deltaG組成）。假設我們需要查詢（例如，k-core或k-truss）圖G'。一個重要的問題是，我們是通過重新計算來查詢G'，還是可以通過利用G的查詢結果和額外處理deltaG來查詢G'。後者是有效的，因為G’是由G加deltaG構成，並且deltaG相較G而言要小得多。我們稱後者為增量圖算法。增量算法要研究的一個重要問題是有界性，它表示我們需要了解多少“變化”才能找到G'的查詢結果，這裡的“變化”與圖的變化（從G到G'）和查詢結果的變化（從G上的查詢結果到G'上的查詢結果）都有關。如果增量算法的複雜度能以某種形式限制，則它是有界的。在這個項目中，我們研究新的增量圖算法，並探索增量圖算法的有界性。該項目的學術意義有兩個方面。除了報告項目的研究發現的會議和期刊出版物之外，還將在原型系統中實現開發的方法和技術，以證明我們方法的優勢。

14205520.label: Realisation of objectives
14205520.value: There are two main interrelated objectives. The primitive objective is to study incremental graph algorithms, and study boundedness for incremental graph algorithms. The second objective is to explore new incremental graph algorithms with possible parallelism and possible new ways to handle the boundedness. We report our research activities below. Relative Subboundedness: As an important class of graphs in graph analytics, road networks have attracted much attention. Given a road network, the problem of efficiently computing the shortest path or distance between two given vertices is important for route planning, POI recommendation and GPS navigation. Many path and distance oracles (oracles for short) have been proposed, such as contraction hierarchy (CH), arterial hierarchy (AH), hierarchical 2-hop index (H2H) and projected vertex separator based 2-hop index (P2H). All these oracles are for static networks. Since real road networks are dynamically updated due to real-time traffic conditions and it is costly to recompute the oracle O from scratch. Formally, let O(G) be the oracle currently in use, ∆G be a set of weight updates to G and G⊕∆G be the resulting network after applying ∆G to G. Given ∆G, the problem of oracle maintenance is to update O, thereby obtaining O(G ⊕ ∆G). Obviously, it is too costly to compute O(G ⊕ ∆G) starting from scratch. It is more practical to maintain O incrementally by using an incremental algorithm. Specifically, fed with G, ∆G and O(G), an incremental algorithm A∆ for O computes an update ∆O to O(G) such that O(G ⊕ ∆G) = O(G) ⊕ ∆O. An incremental algorithm A∆ for O is desired to be bounded. Specifically, A∆ is bounded if there exists a polynomial function f such that the cost of A∆ is bounded by O(f (|CHANGED|)), where |CHANGED| = |∆G| + |∆O| is the amount of changes in the input and output after applying ∆G to G. Intuitively, |CHANGED| represents the minimum amount of work that any incremental algorithm for O needs to do. Therefore, a bounded A∆ guarantees the efficient updatability of O, compared with recomputing O from scratch. The problem of maintaining oracle O is bounded if a bounded A∆ for O exists and is unbounded otherwise. Our work is one of few works that study boundedness. Under the class of locally persistent (LP) algorithms to study boundedness, we prove both the problems of maintaining CH and H2H are unbounded even for single weight updates. We also consider two classes of incremental algorithms, denoted INCCH and INCH2H, that include practically efficient algorithms for CH and H2H, respectively. We prove that the algorithms in INCCH and INCH2H are also unbounded for single weight updates. In spite of the impossibility results, we show that both CH and H2H can still be maintained more efficiently than recomputing from scratch. Specifically, as an alternative to boundedness, we propose relative subboundedness for CH and H2H. In detail, let Q be either the problem of constructing CH or the problem of constructing H2H on a graph G. Let Q(G) denote the result of Q on G. Then the incremental counterpart of Q is to update the result from Q(G) to Q(G ⊕ ∆G) when an update ∆G is applied to G. The introduction of relative subboundedness is to characterize the efficiency of an incremental algorithm A∆ that maintains Q(·). Let D(G) and D(G ⊕ ∆G) denote the data that every algorithm for Q needs to inspect when computing Q(G) and Q(G ⊕ ∆G), respectively, and AFF be defined as the part of D(G ⊕ ∆G) that differs from D(G). Intuitively, it captures the part affected by ∆G. Let A be any algorithm for Q. We define ||AFF|| as the part of time spent on AFF by A when computing Q(G ⊕∆G) and say an incremental algorithm A∆ that updates the result from Q(G) to Q(G ⊕ ∆G) is subbounded relative to A if its cost is of O(||AFF|| log ||AFF||). By definition, we have ||AFF|| ≤ TA, where TA is the cost of A to compute Q(G ⊕ ∆G), i.e., the cost to deal with ∆G by recomputing from scratch. Hence, an incremental algorithm A∆ subbounded relative to A is likely to outperform recomputing from scratch using A. Our study on CH and H2H shows that relative subboundedness alone is enough to warrant efficiency. We report our work in SIGMOD’22. Parallelism and Boundedness: Together with relative boundedness proposed, we propose a new incremental algorithm IncH2H to maintain H2H. We prove that IncH2H (1) is subbounded relative to H2HIndexing under weight-increase updates, where H2HIndexing is the state-of-the-art algorithm to construct H2H, and (2) is both subbounded and bounded relative to H2HIndexing under weight-decrease updates. The parallelism is based on the super-shortcuts used in IncH2H that are processed in non-ascending order of π(u). We show that, without affecting the correctness of IncH2H, the super-shortcuts in CHANGED can also be processed in non-descending order of the depth of nodes, depth(u). We proved that, when processing CHANGEDi, for any two distinct processors p1 and p2, the work assigned to each processor is independent. Based on the theorem, we design ParIncH2H+ and ParIncH2H− to deal with weight increase and weight decrease, respectively. We report our work in SIGMOD’22. Dynamic graphs and Boundedness: Graphs have been widely used in many applications. One important graph analytics is to explore cohesive subgraphs in a large graph. Among several cohesive subgraphs studied, k-core is one that can be computed in linear time for a static graph. Since graphs are evolving in real applications, we study core maintenance which is to reduce the computational cost to compute k-cores for a graph when graphs are updated from time to time dynamically. We observe that maintenance of only a small subset of the top cores brings improvement in performance as vertices with high core numbers account for only a small proportion of all vertices. Hence, by concentrating on those vertices and reducing work wasted on the rest vertices, more efficiency can be obtained. In the light of above discussion, we maintain only a small subset of the top cores. Let t be a user-defined positive integer. We study the problem of maintaining core numbers only for the vertices in the top-t cores of G. We call this the partial core maintenance (PCM) problem and call the problem of maintaining core numbers for all vertices the full core maintenance (FCM) problem. We study the hardness of PCM using the theory of boundedness of incremental problems. We prove that, unlike FCM which is unbounded under edge insertion but is bounded under edge removal, PCM is unbounded for both edge insertion and edge removal, making PCM interesting from a theoretical perspective. In addition, we further propose practically near-bounded algorithms for the partial core maintenance problem. Our experimental results show that, by maintaining only the top cores, we can obtain up to three times performance improvement compared with full core maintenance. We report our work in TKDE 2024.

14205520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205520.value: First, we study relative subboundedness with a focus on road networks over which efficiently computing the shortest path or distance between two given vertices is important for route planning, POI recommendation and GPS navigation. We prove both the problems of maintaining SOTA algorithms, CH and H2H, are unbounded even for single weight updates. We also consider two classes of incremental algorithms, denoted INCCH and INCH2H, that include practically efficient algorithms for CH and H2H, respectively. We prove that the algorithms in INCCH and INCH2H are also unbounded for single weight updates. In spite of the impossibility results, we show that both CH and H2H can still be maintained more efficiently than recomputing from scratch. We propose relative subboundedness for CH and H2H. Our study on CH and H2H shows that relative subboundedness alone is enough to warrant efficiency. We also study parallelism with relative boundedness. We report our work in SIGMOD’22. Second, to explore cohesive subgraphs in a large dynamic graph, we study core maintenance to reduce the computational cost to compute k-cores. We study the problem of maintaining core numbers only for the vertices in the top-t cores of G. We call this the partial core maintenance (PCM) problem. We propose practically near-bounded algorithms for the partial core maintenance problem. We report our work in TKDE 2024. Third, we study two problems over large dynamic graphs, efficient indexing and time-optimal (k, p)-core community search, and report the results in PVLDB’22 and ICDE’22. We also study scalable time-range k-core query on temporal graphs, and report it in PVLDB’23 and PVLDB’24. Fourth, we study graph ordering, which is to make graph algorithms faster by reordering the vertices in a graph. We did it by learning, and report our findings in WISE’21. Fifth, we study graph isomorphism and automorphism on large graphs, and report it in SIGMOD’21. Sixth, we study parallel processing, to separate communication from computation, to handle graph problems, in a distributed system. We report our work in ICDE’21 and SIGMOD’22. Seventh, we study fast continuous subgraph matching over streaming graphs via backtracking reduction, and report it in SIGMOD’23.

14205520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205520.value: The boundedness is an important topic to guarantee the quality of an incremental algorithms to deal with graph problems when a graph is evolving or dynamically changing. It is difficult to have a general solution for many graph algorithms. But there exist possible solutions to some graph algorithms that have not been well studied, which we plan to study in near future.

14205520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205520.value: This project focuses on incremental graph algorithms—methods that efficiently update solutions when graphs change, rather than recomputing everything from scratch. A key issue is the boundedness whether updates can be performed in time proportional to the size of the changes. The main theoretical contributions in this project is as follows. First, we propose relative subboundedness, a novel way to measure incremental algorithm efficiency when perfect boundedness is impossible for path and distance oracles for route planning, POI recommendation and GPS navigation. We show that relative subboundedness is enough to warrant efficiency. Second, we study cohesive subgraphs in large graphs with a focus on k-core which can be computed in linear time for a static graph. We study core maintenance to reduce the cost to compute k-cores when graphs are updated dynamically. We focus on how to maintain only a small subset of the top t-cores. We call this the partial core maintenance (PCM) problem and call the problem of maintaining core numbers for all vertices the full core maintenance (FCM) problem. We study the hardness of PCM/FCM. We propose practically near-bounded algorithms for PCM. We can obtain up to three times performance improvement compared with full core maintenance.

14205820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205820.value: 現今，光纖已被廣泛認同為一種很實用的傳輸媒介，實現超大數據傳輸容量的短距離互連以至長距離骨幹網絡。隨著先進數字處理器和數字計算算法的日益發展，支持了各種先進的信號調制技術來增強光纖傳輸系統的頻譜效率，從而提高系統傳輸能力。光學多載波系統是現時最可行，最有效的傳輸方法之一，它利用多個緊密間隔且經過數字編碼的頻率載波，在較長的傳輸距離上以高數據速率傳輸信號。通過這種高效的頻譜設計，實現出色的傳輸性能，高系統容量以及對各種光纖傳輸效應的兼容性。正交頻分複用（OFDM）便是一個好例子，在近年引起了廣泛的研究關注。最近，非正交頻分複用（NOFDM）系統亦被提出，進一步節省了系統帶寬，並進一步增強系統容量。對於這樣的高容量光傳輸系統，除了系統覆蓋和數據速率的關鍵參數外，數據安全也是關鍵課題，以確保數據隱私，並防止可能的網絡監聽和網絡竊聽。在物理層或網絡層上已有一些方案來實現安全的光纖通信。在這個項目中，我們嘗試利用數字混沌加密技術，將光混沌信號的隨機性結合到光多載波信號的合成，以增強傳輸信號的機密性。如果數字混沌加密是未知的，則其偽隨機性質，較大的密鑰空間，較寬的頻譜，以及對初始值的高靈敏度，增加了信號解密的難度，從而確保了安全通信。雖然在光學OFDM系統中已經積極地研究了數字混沌加密，在這項目裡，我們提出了在光NOFDM系統中，利用信號合成過程中帶寬壓縮的特點，執行數字混沌加密的新方案。我們應用混沌密鑰來更改NOFDM系統中子載波的數量，以及將混沌項合併到信號預編碼矩陣中，並進行系統評估和優化。這些方案提供了有效的解決方案來欺騙潛在的竊聽者，從而確保了光纖傳輸系統中的安全通信。

14205820.label: Realisation of objectives
14205820.value: This project aims to investigate digital chaotic encryption schemes to enhance data security of a high-capacity optical fiber transmission system using highly spectral-efficient optical frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation format. Data security is a critical issue to assure data privacy and prevent possible network sniffing and network eavesdropping. The proposed digital encryption schemes are further enhanced by the unpredictable randomness nature of chaos phenomenon to realize a secure transmission system with pseudo-random nature, large key space size, wide spectrum and high sensitivity to the initial value of digital chaotic encryption. We have exploited, for the first time, a new dimension of non-orthogonality in digital encryption. The input data are scrambled by a set of proposed chaotic non-orthogonal matrices (CNOMs), which are determined by a chaotic system and security keys (to achieve project objective #1). CNOM can dynamically scramble the number of subcarriers in an OFDM signal while maintaining the same bandwidth to further deceive potential eavesdroppers. By simultaneously using faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling and redundant precoding, the proposed digital chaotic encryption scheme with CNOMs can achieve the compromise between spectral efficiency and resilience against system impairments, while drastically increasing the overall size of key space (about 3.7 × 10218 times in a 5-D hyperchaotic system) against the exhaustive search attack, compared to the conventional chaotic orthogonal matrix (COM) based encryption schemes. In the next step, we have explored extending the investigation in applying the proposed CNOM encryption to multiple sub-bands of the system bandwidth for further enhancement of the physical-layer security in OFDM-PONs (to achieve project objective #1). The results have shown that encryption over multiple sub-bands can further increase the size of key space to guarantee good security and performance. For example, when the number of sub-bands is increased from 1 (single-band) to 10 and 15, by employing the proposed multi-band CNOM encryption with the optimal dynamic range, the size of the key space can be increased by 1.4×10482 and 1.72×10653 times, respectively; the complexity of complex-valued multiplication can be reduced by 90% and 93.33%, respectively; and the complexity of complex-valued addition can be reduced by 90.76% and 94.12%, respectively, in encrypting one OFDM symbol. We have further investigated the impact of the number of sub-bands and the corresponding dynamic range in encryption on transmission performance, security performance, and computational complexity. We have obtained the optimal values of the number of sub-bands to balance the trade-off among the size of key space, the computational complexity, and the transmission performance, (to achieve project objective #2). Besides, we have further proposed a variable scheme to vary the number and the size of sub-bands for each OFDM symbol, entirely determined by the chaotic sequences, thus increasing the transmission and security performance (to achieve project objective #1). The results have shown that the transmission performance can be improved through the variable scheme compared to the fixed scheme when the number of sub-bands exceeds a critical value, and the upper bound of the security performance presented in the conventional fixed scheme can be easily broken by also enabling a variable number/size of sub-bands without degrading the transmission performance. We have carefully characterized the impact of the number and the size of the sub-bands for each OFDM symbol on the system performance (to achieve project objective #2). In addition, we have also tried another pre-coding matrix, Chaotic Frank Sequence-Based Circulant Matrix, and have obtained satisfactory results (to achieve project objective #1). For all the proposed schemes, we have performed numerical simulations, proof-of-concept experimental demonstrations and experimental characterization of the system parameters to confirm their feasibility and robustness (to achieve project objective #2). All results have indicated the great potential of the proposed single-band or multi-band CNOM-based encryption schemes to enable future highly secure and high-speed PONs.

14205820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205820.value: The project has led to several research outcomes. First, chaotic non-orthogonal matrices (CNOM) have been proposed to perform chaotic digital encryption (Journal #1). The non-orthogonal dimension in encryption has been explored and carefully characterized, showing its feasibility and robustness in enhancing physical layer security of optical fiber systems. By employing a 5-D hyperchaotic scheme on the CNOM to encode the OFDM symbols in an OFDM-PON, the size of the key space is largely increased, while complexity and performance have been well-compromised. Second, the idea has been extended to perform multi-band CNOM encryption (Journal #2, Conference #1). The results have shown that the size of the key space is further drastically increased while the complexity has been largely reduced and the performance can still be compromised. The impact of the number of sub-bands has been carefully characterized and optimization has been carried out. Third, a variable scheme has been further proposed to vary the number and the size of the sub-bands based on a chaotic sequence (Journal #3). CNOMs have been applied to realize highly feasible and robust encryption for enhanced security in the optical system. The results have shown that the transmission performance can be improved through the variable scheme compared to the fixed scheme when the number of sub-bands exceeds a critical value, and the upper bound of the security performance presented in the conventional fixed scheme can be easily broken by also enabling a variable number/size of sub-bands without degrading the transmission performance. Besides, we have proposed and investigated another pre-coding matrix, Chaotic Frank Sequence-Based Circulant Matrix, and have obtained satisfactory results (Conference #2). Finally, we have also explored and investigated the digital precoding to realize multi-band Faster-than-Nyquist non-orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (FTN-NOFDM) (Journal #4), which has shown good robustness against the steep frequency roll-off in a bandwidth-limited optical communication system, leading to better utilization of the low-pass-like channel as well as reduced computational complexity. This approach has shown to be a good multicarrier modulation scheme for highly spectral efficient optical transmission systems.

14205820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205820.value: The CNOMs could be further analyzed with different orders of the chaotic systems with the trade-off in the respective complexity. The scalability of the proposed CNOM for encryption can be further characterized with respect to system capacity.

14205820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205820.value: This project aims to investigate digital chaotic encryption schemes to enhance data security of a high-capacity optical fiber system using optical frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The proposed digital encryption schemes are enhanced by chaos phenomenon to realize a secure transmission system with large key space size, wide spectrum and high sensitivity to the initial value of digital chaotic encryption. We have exploited a new dimension of non-orthogonality in digital encryption. The input data are scrambled by a set of proposed chaotic non-orthogonal matrices (CNOMs), which are determined by a chaotic system and security keys, to dynamically scramble the number of subcarriers in an OFDM signal while maintaining the same bandwidth to further deceive potential eavesdroppers. The proposed encryption scheme with CNOMs can drastically increase the size of key space to assure security. Further investigations have been performed with multiple sub-bands in the system bandwidth for further enhancement of the physical-layer security in OFDM-PONs, with much reduced complexity. The number and the size of the sub-bands are further varied to increase the size of the key spaces, thus largely enhancing the data security. The results showed great potential for the proposed encryption schemes to enable future highly secure passive optical networks.

14206020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206020.value: Financial engineering employs quantitative methods and engineering techniques to solve various types of decision making problems in financial applications such as option pricing and hedging, utility maximization, algorithmic trading and management of complex systems like power plants and energy storage facilities. To solve such problems, a model-based approach is typically adopted in practice. That is, a parametric stochastic model is assumed for the underlying random process based on which optimal decisions are derived. The solution quality apparently relies on how well the proposed model captures the reality. Despite many efforts to develop realistic models for practical needs, this widely used approach is prone to model risk and it has been reported that losses due to model misspecification can be substantial in practice. In this project, we formulate financial decision making problems as discrete time stochastic control problems and aim to develop a data-driven approach that is free of parametric models for solving them. We propose to apply resampling techniques to market data together with deep neural network approximations of controls to obtain data-driven solutions. The availability of massive computing power makes it possible to implement our approach within time constraints in reality. The quality of our solutions will be assessed theoretically and via simulation studies for a variety of applications. We anticipate that our approach will equip financial decision makers with effective tools to mitigate losses due to model risk. 金融工程采用量化方法和工程技術來解決金融應用中的各類決策問題，例如期權定價和對衝，投資效用優化，算法交易以及對複雜系統比如發電廠以及能源儲藏設備的管理。現實中爲了解決這些問題，通常采用基於模型的方法。也就是說，將問題中的隨機過程假設成一個參數化的隨機模型，在此基礎上推導出最優策略。 這種方法的決策質量明顯取決與模型近似現實的程度。儘管過去有很多努力來開發出更真實的模型，這個常用的方法仍然易受到模型錯誤的影響，在實踐中可能帶來大量的損失。 在本課題中， 我們把金融決策問題考慮成離散時間隨機控制問題。我們的目標是開發出一種數據驅動的方法（不基於參數化的模型）來解決它們。我們提出對市場數據再抽樣結合神經網絡近似控制策略來得到數據驅動的解決方案。現有的大規模計算能力使得我們的方法能夠滿足現實中對時間的限制。 我們將在理論上還有模擬實驗中評估我們方法的在解決多種問題中的效果。我們期望這種數據驅動的方法能夠在實踐中幫助金融決策者有效地減少由於模型不確定導致的損失。

14206020.label: Realisation of objectives
14206020.value: (1) For objective 1, we have developed data-driven methods with deep learning for four important problems in financial engineering. The first problem is forecasting the implied volatility surface, which is important for option pricing, trading and risk management. The second problem considers hedging the risk of derivatives. We studied the problem using two approaches, namely local and global risk minimization, which are both used in practice. The third problem concerns options market making, where a dealer needs to optimally post the bid and ask quotes of options to maximize her expected utility. The fourth problem deals with enhanced index tracking (EIT), which attempts to obtain excess returns by benchmarking against an index while still controlling the deviation from it. EIT funds are appealing to investors nowadays as they offer the potential to capture higher returns than the index. Classical model-based methods were developed for these problems. In this project, we take a data-driven approach with deep learning to tackle them. For each problem, we carefully designed the neural network model and engineerd the features to consider the special characteristics of the problem. We performed extensive experiments and empirical studies to compare our methods with the classical benchmarks. Our results clearly demonstrated that using the data-driven approach with deep learning can bring significant gains for complex and challenging real-world problems. The results for these four problems are published in five papers, which appear in the top-tier journal Quantitative Finance and other high-quality journals in the field of financial engineering. (2) For objective 2, we studied general discrete-time stochastic control problems where neural networks are used to approximate the control functions. The decision-making applications we considered fit into this framework. In practice, one only observes a single time series path for a financial variable from the financial market, which is insufficient for training. To solve the data insufficiency problem, we used the resampling technique. Thus, our theorical analysis focused on analyzing the convergence of resampling-based deep learning for stochastic control problems. We have proved the convergence of our deep learning solution of the control problem under some regularity conditions that hold in typical cases, and the results can be found in the PhD thesis of Zhiwen Dai. Overall, we have achieved both objectives to the full extent. Throughout the project, I trained four PhD students: Qianhui Lai (output 4), Jie Chen (output 2), Wenyong Zhang (output 1) and Zhiwen Dai (ouput 3 and 5). The output in the parenthesis contributes to the student's PhD thesis as a major part. Upon graduation, Qianhui worked as Assistant Professor in Qingdao University. Jie worked for Aqumon while Wenyong worked for JP Morgan, both as quants in Hong Kong. Zhiwen became a postdoctoral fellow at the Hong Kong Center for Logistics Robotics. Students of my group involved in the project presented their works at two leading international conferences for financial engineering during the project period, namely the 11th World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society and the 22nd Conference of the International Federation of Operational Research Societies. Unfortunately, due to travel restrictions in the pandemic, these conferences were held online, which is why we did not spend much on conferences. I also presented a work at the conference Recent Adances on Quantitative Finance, which attracted several leading experts in financial engineering to Hong Kong.

14206020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206020.value: In output 1, we develop a two-step data-driven framework to forecast the implied volatility surface. In the first step, we construct features based on the implied volatility surface data to represent the surface and predict the features using LSTM. In the second step, we use the predicted features to construct the implied volatility surface using a deep neural network model by incorporating constraints that prevent static arbitrage. We have found two successful feature construction methods using real market data and we show that our method substantially outperforms a standard method used in practice. In output 2, we develop neural network models to obtain the hedge ratio that minimizes the mean squared hedging error over one time step. Using stock index options data, we demonstrate the significant advantages of our model over some standard models in the literature. Our research also reveals the importance of market sentiment for hedging. In output 3, we consider minimizing the mean squared hedging error over the entire period by deep learning. The hedging decision at each time point is output from a neural network. We compare three architectures of neural networks through extensive numerical experiments to obtain insights into their advantages and drawbacks. We also propose a data-driven method based on resampling to generate data to train the neural networks. Our results provide useful guidance on the choice of the neural network, data generation and training for solving the hedging problem by deep learning. In output 4, we study options market making, where a dealer needs to optimally post the bid and ask quotes of options to maximize her expected utility. We first provide an empirical study on the behavior of options market orders using options market data. Based on the empirical findings, we develop a realistic model of options market order arrivals. We solve the market making problem using deep learning based on this model and show that our method significantly outperforms some standard benchmarks. In output 5, we develop a deep learning method for the enhanced index tracking problem. We propose a novel neural network structure to handle different types of features. We test our model on several indexes in empirical studies based on real market data. Out-of-sample results reveal the importance of different features and demonstrate the ability of our method in obtaining excess returns while effectively controlling the tracking error, downside risk, and transaction costs.

14206020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206020.value: For the implied volatlity surface forecast, we can consider adding exogenous variables, such as the index return and VIX, to the feature set, which can potentially boost the prediction power of our models. We can also use more sophisticated deep learning models to predict the features. For the hedging problem, we plan to consider alternative objectives, such as minimizing the conditional value-at-risk of the hedging loss instead of the mean squared hedging error. For the options market making problem, we can expand our empirical study to consider options of longer maturity and multi-asset options. For the enhanced index tracking problem, there are two interesting directions to explore in future research. One is considering alternative models for predicting the stock and index regimes, which is done by filtering in our study. The other direction is improving the selection of stocks, which clearly matters for investment performance.

14206020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206020.value: Financial engineering deals with financial decision making problems such as option pricing and hedging, market making, and algorithmic trading. To solve such problems, a model-based approach is typically adopted in practice. That is, a mathematical model with some parameters is assumed for the underlying random process based on which optimal decisions are derived. The solution quality apparently relies on how well the proposed model approximates the reality. Due to the highly complex nature of financial markets, this widely used approach is prone to model risk and could lead to bad decisions. In this project, we develop a data-driven approach to solve financial decision problems by using neural networks to approximate the decision. Our approach lets data speak rather than prespecifying any mathematical model that may not fit the data well. Furthermore, the use of neural networks can capture highly nonlinear behavior and thus can make the generated decision more realistic. Our approach brings significant improvement over the classical model-based approach as demonstrated in the empirical studies we conducted for four important applications.

14206320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206320.value: 深度神經網絡是非常強大的機器學習工具，可以從數據中有效地提取特徵和構造，從而解決許多實際存在的難題。但是，它的成功主要體現於擁有網格結構的數據上，例如圖像，視頻和一維信號等。在此研究項目中，我們的目標是超越現有技術並創新可以學習設計和構造三維裝配結構的機器學習方法，同時考慮各種實際問題，例如可加工性，功能性和穩定性。這是一個尚未探索的新的研究問題，我們將基於兩個最新研究成果來進行：首先，包括基於圖的捲積神經網絡在內的最新技術，以及採用神經網絡來解決複雜組合問題的最新工作，以及其次，首席調查員(PI)在計算和構造三維物體製造和裝配方面的相關研究經驗，其中大多數結果都發布在計算機圖形學研究的頂級旗艦期刊和會議當中。 總括而言，我們將在本項目中探索以下的三個研究題目: • 首先，我們旨在開發新的機器學習方法，以能夠學習2D結構中的局部格局，然後利用該知識來設計2D結構，特別是將機器學習應用到設計拼貼設計當中。 • 其次，我們將推廣此方法到3D，以能夠學習3D裝配體中的局部結構，並將學習的特定應用基於現有模型中的局部結構設樂高机械(Technic)模型。 • 第三，我們將進一步擴展計算方法的功能，以創建具有功能性的3D動態結構並有效評估其局部結構的穩定性。 在此項目的過程中，我們將生成虛擬並真實三維模型，構建三維裝配體並通過進行各種物理實驗以評估結果。 通過此項目，首席調查員(PI)將能夠更一步推進他在計算製造領域的研究，繼續創新方法，並努力產生達到頂級研究期刊和會議的高質量水平。

14206320.label: Realisation of objectives
14206320.value: This project aims to develop computational methods for constructing shapes and structures. In recent years, we witness the significant development of AIGC (Artificial Intelligence Generated Content) in generating texts and images, and also its impact to our society. In this project, we developed several new techniques on shape generation. These works were all published in top-tier international research journals and/or conferences. Also, we started a new collaboration with a leading 3D design company, Autodesk Inc. First, we developed a family of deep generative methods on creating 3D shapes. First we presented a new unsupervised learning approach, which is a sphere-guided generative model, for direct synthesis of 3D shapes in the form of point clouds. Our method incorporates a global prior (uniform points on a sphere) to spatially guide the generative process and attach a local prior (a random latent code) to each sphere point to provide local details. This novel mechanism disentangles the complex 3D shape generation task into a global shape modeling and a local structure adjustment to ease the learning process. Also, our model forms an implicit dense correspondence between the sphere points and points in every generated shape, enabling various forms of structure-aware shape manipulations. Subsequently, we propose to further disentangle the 3D generative process into shape and topology by considering a topology-aware neural template specific to each input then deform the template to reconstruct a detailed mesh while preserving the learned topology. One key insight is to decouple mesh reconstruction into two sub-tasks, topology formulation and shape deformation. Thanks to the decoupling, we can implicitly learn a disentangled representation for the topology and shape in the latent space, enabling novel disentangled controls for supporting various shape generation applications, e.g., remix the topologies of 3D objects, that are not achievable by previous reconstruction works. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method can produce high-quality meshes with diverse topologies, compared with the state-of-the-art methods. Next, we aim for high-quality shape generation that can capture more details. To start, we propose a novel neural wavelet representation that enables direct generative modeling on a continuous implicit representation in wavelet domain. Specifically, we design a compact wavelet representation to implicitly represent 3D shapes via truncated signed distance functions and multi-scale biorthogonal wavelets, and formulate a pair of neural networks: a generator based on a diffusion model to produce diverse shapes in the form of coarse coefficient volumes; and a detail predictor to further produce compatible detail coefficient volumes for enriching the generated shapes with fine structures and details. Both quantitative and qualitative experimental results manifest the superiority of our approach in generating diverse and high-quality shapes with complex topology and structures, clean surfaces, and fine details, exceeding the 3D generation capabilities of all prior works. Beyond this, we extend our framework for shape inversion and manipulation beyond shape generation, by proposing to jointly train an encoder network to learn a latent space for inverting shapes, allowing us to enable a rich variety of whole-shape and region-aware shape manipulations. Very recently in 2024, we continue to explore this research direction and collaborate with Autodesk Inc., Toronto to design a new wavelet-tree-based shape learning model that can efficiently train on over ten millions of shapes, beyond the capabilities of all the prior shape models. Further, we explore manipulation and control strategies in the generative process. In early 2023, we started to explore the use of a vision-language model to help us explore the 3D shape space. Many methods have been developed to encode 3D shapes into a learned latent shape space for generative design and modeling, yet the existing ones lack effective exploration mechanisms. Our idea here is threefold. First, we couple the CLIP and shape spaces by generating paired CLIP and shape codes through sketch images and training a mapper network to connect the two spaces. Second, to explore the space around a given shape, we formulate a co-optimization strategy to search for the CLIP code that better matches the shape geometry. Third, we design three exploration modes to locate suitable exploration trajectories in shape space and induce meaningful changes to the shape. Comparing our approach with various baselines shows that we can produce many meaningful exploration results that cannot be achieved by the existing solutions. On the other hand, we developed new approaches for text-based shape generation. First, we introduce 2D image as a stepping stone to connect the text modality with the shape modality and to eliminate the need for paired text-shape data. Our key contribution is a two-stage feature-space-alignment approach that maps CLIP features to shapes by harnessing a pre-trained single-view reconstruction (SVR) model with multi-view supervisions: first map the CLIP image feature to the detail-rich shape space in the SVR model, then map the CLIP text feature to the shape space and optimize the mapping by encouraging CLIP consistency between the input text and the rendered images. Further, we formulate a text-guided shape stylization module to dress up the output shapes with novel textures, and then exploit pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models to enhance the generative diversity, fidelity, and stylization capability. Our approach is generic, flexible, and scalable, easily integrate-able with various SVR models to expand the generative space and improve the generative fidelity. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of generative quality and consistency with the input text. More recently, we design a hybrid shape representation, namely EXIM, combining the strengths of an explicit stage, which controls the topology of the generated 3D shapes and enables local modifications, and an implicit stage, which refines the shape and paints it with plausible colors. Our hybrid approach separates the shape and color and generates shape-conditioned colors with high shape-color consistency. Unlike the existing works, we demonstrate high-fidelity shape generation from natural-language descriptions without the need for time-consuming per-shape optimization or reliance on human-annotated texts during training or test-time optimization. Further than that, we demonstrate the generation of indoor scenes (which is essentially an assembly of 3D objects) with consistent styles using text-induced 3D shapes.

(1) Summarizing major findings in 3D shape generation: - [J01]/[C01] presents a novel unsupervised sphere-guided generative model for diverse high-quality generation of 3D point clouds. - [C05] presents a framework for 3D mesh reconstruction and generation via disentangled topology. - [C07] presents a novel approach beyond [C05] for 3D shape generation by innovating a new neural wavelets representation for direct generative modeling of a continuous implicit representation, achieving a compact shape representation. - [C08] presents a new framework for text-guided 3D shape generation, bridging the gap between text and shape modalities without paired text-shape data. - [J06] extends [C08] by levering images as a stepping stone to bridge the gap between text and shape modalities. - [J08]/[C10] presents a new hybrid explicit-implicit 3D shape representation to consider topology, local shape modifications, and colors. - [J09] extends [C05] with various new capabilities (3D shape generation, inversion, and manipulation). (2) Summarizing major findings on 3D reconstruction and 3D understanding: - [J02]/[C02] presents a novel path-oriented drone trajectory planning algorithm, jointly optimizing image acquisition and path quality. - [J03] presents a rotation-invariant neural network architecture for processing 3D point clouds. - [J04] presents a novel approach to locate floor-level lines in street-view images with our multi-task learning network. - [J05]/[C06] presents a novel learning-based reconstructability predictor for large-scale 3D scene acquisition. - [J07] presents a new human-centric two-stage approach for automated floorplan design by synthesizing human-activity maps and predicting room types, considering the human activities. - [C03] presents a novel pipeline for 3D hand-mesh reconstruction from RGB images by decoupling the task into three stages. - [C04] presents a semi-supervised point cloud semantic segmentation method with our guided point contrastive loss. - [C09] presents a novel diffusion-based approach for 3D shape completion on 3D range scans. - [C11] presents a novel 3D shape exploration framework that leverages the vision-language model CLIP.

Beyond texts and images, we innovated several deep-learning-based methods and representations for generative 2D/3D shapes and structures, including a sphere-guided generative model for direct synthesis of shapes in the form of point clouds, a topology-aware neural template that enables us to first learn the topology then generate shapes with learned topology, a neural wavelet representation that enables direct generative modeling on a continuous implicit representation in wavelet domain with shape inversion and shape manipulation capabilities, a family of shape-space exploration strategies that leverages a large vision-language model to inform the generative process with shape semantics, a two-stage feature-space-alignment approach for text-guided shape generation with the 2D image as a stepping stone, a hybrid explicit-implicit latent shape representation that delivers shape-conditioned colors and generates scene-level object assemblies, etc. All these research works were published in top-tier international research journals and/or conferences, and we also started a new research collaboration with Autodesk Inc. on developing a large 3D shape generative model.

14206820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206820.value: 多主體強化學習動力學的形式化建模：平均場理論方法

14206820.label: Project Objectives
14206820.value: We shall develop a general model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which there are many agents (the number of interacting agents tends to infinity). Specifically, a general model will be able to handle the following situations. a) We shall first consider the situation that the game of interaction is a general bi-matrix game. In the current model we have developed and presented (Hu, Leung & Leung 2019), the game of interaction is restricted to symmetric games. While symmetric game is an important subclass of games used in multi-agent reinforcement learning, in particular in the research in norm emergence phenomena, a general model for agents interacting using general bi-matrix games is significant and necessary. This is because in different scenarios agents are generally interacting using different bi-matrix games, which are generally not symmetric. A general model to formally describe the dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning with general bi-matrix games is hence the first objective we aim at achieving in the project. b) Another situation that we target at is that agents are joint action learners, instead of individual action learns. They observe the actions played by its opponents, and try to learn the best joint actions. The significance of this situation is that in many situations, researchers find that joint action learners are found to be more efficient than individual action learners. A model that can formally describe such situations is hence significant. 2) The other objective we aim at achieving in this project is to build a formal model that incorporates the effects of additional external factors in the process of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning. This will be done on the basis of the general model we obtain as in the first objective. Examples of such factors are social values (Hu & Leung 2018a), influencer agents (Hao & Leung 2012a, 2015b), inequity-aversity (Hao & Leung 2010), and gist traces (Hu, Leung, Leung & Liu 2019), to name a few. When we have a formal model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning, we anticipate that we shall be able to analyse the effects of these external actors mathematically. We note that this has not yet been possible with only the research results obtained from agent-based simulations. We hope that the effects of these factors, both on the learning dynamics and on the final outcome, can be analysed theoretically. They will also be verified experimentally if possible.

14206820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206820.value: Research into learning through repeated agent interactions in multi-agent systems has become an active topic in the field of multiagent systems. It finds applications in a wide variety of domains. We note that a thorough understanding of multi-agent reinforcement learning is a current topic of research. There has been no research work reported on the formal modelling of the dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning for the general n-agent settings, in particular, when n is very large. However, this is an important research topic. It enables researchers to give a detailed explanation of the process and find out the implications of the process. Generally, there is also a potential that the models can be further developed mathematically. Last but not least, a mathematical model might highlight the importance of certain parameters that would otherwise be overlooked in experimental studies. In this project, we propose to research into the dynamics of such systems with a mean field theoretic approach. We have obtained some very good initial results, which is presented in one of the most prestigious conference in Artificial Intelligence. There are two specific objectives to be achieved in the project. First, we shall develop a general model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which there are many, many agents. Specifically, a general model will be able to handle the situations that the game of interaction is any game that allow agents to have one-to-one interactions. The model will also be able to allow agents to learn to cooperate with the opponents. The other objective is to build a formal model that incorporates the effects of additional external factors in the process of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning. Examples of such factors are social values, influencer agents, inequity-aversity, and gist traces, to name a few. We hope that the effects of these factors, both on the learning dynamics and on the final outcome, can be analysed theoretically. They will also be verified experimentally if possible. 在多主體系統中通過重複的主體交互進行學習的研究，已成為多主體系統領域中的一個活躍主題。這項研究在廣泛領域中都有應用。我們注意到，當前一個研究的主題是對多主體強化學習的透徹理解。我們注意到，對於一般性的n個主體的多主體系統強化學習動力學的形式化建模，還沒有相關研究結果發表（尤其是當n很大時）。然而，這是一個重要的研究課題，因為它使研究人員可以對過程進行詳細說明，並找出過程的含義，而且通常還存在可以在數學上進一步開發模型的潛力。一個數學模型有可能會突顯了某些參數的重要性，而在實驗研究中可能會忽略了這些參數。在本項目中，我們建議使用平均場理論方法研究此類系統的動力學。我們已經獲得了一些非常好的初始結果，並已經發表在人工智能領域中最負盛名的其中一個會議上。 本項目有兩個具體目標要實現。首先，我們將建立一個包含許許多多的主體的多主體強化學習動力學的通用模型。尤其是，模型中主體可以以各種博弈進行一對一交互。這個模型還將能夠允許主體學習與對手合作。另一個目標是建立一個形式化模型，在多主體強化學習的動力學過程中納入其他外部因素的影響，如社會價值、影響者主體、不公平厭惡、要旨痕跡等。我們希望可以從理論上分析這些因素對學習動力學的影響和對最終結果的影響，並在可能情況下進行實驗驗證。

14206820.label: Realisation of objectives
14206820.value: In this project, we have focused on developing models of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which there are many agents (the number of interacting agents tends to infinity). In the literature, there are a number of models the dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which agents play bi-matrix games and learn with global interactions. The first research result of this project is a paper published in the prestigious conference ICTAI 2021, in which we investigate the reinforcement learning of agents playing bi-matrix games with local interactions. In this scenario, agents learn their policies playing with some other agents only locally. We first capture the Q-values dynamics of each individual agent under the stochastic environment by stochastic differential equations. The time evolution of the probability distribution (PDF) of the population Q-values are subsequently also obtained. These theoretical results are validated with agent-based simulations. It is shown that the model can precisely capture the behaviour of the multi-agent system. Another result that is published in the top-tier conference IJCAI 2022, in which we consider agents performing reinforcement learning using the generalized social learning protocol. In the previous models, the effects of local interactions and incomplete information that arise from generalized social learning are conventionally ignored, which generally leads to imprecision in the resulting model of dynamics. The correctness of the more accurate model that we propose is validated through extensive comparisons with agent-based simulation results across different types of symmetric games. In addition, we show that the population can actually converge to an outcome that is qualitatively different from that predicated in previous models, and such phenomena are precisely forecast using out new model. Another important result that we have is published in the flagship international conference AAMAS 2022, in which we investigate the dynamics of population games. The new model that we present in this scenario bears a formal connection with the continuity equation in physics. We show that the new model always accurately describes the Q-learning dynamics in population games across different initial settings of multiagent systems and game configurations, including different exploration mechanisms. We also show how the insights the model provides can be used to facilitate parameter tuning that have different effects on convergence. We also extend our previous work published in AAMAS’19 and report the findings in a journal paper published in ACM TAAS. We study the emergence of conventions from repeated n-player coordination games, where agents can observe their neighbours and learn based on gist trace instead of verbatim trace. A novel learning method is proposed, which is shown to establish conventions much faster than the state-of-the-art learning methods. The most recent scenario we investigate is that agents learn using the SoftMax policy gradient algorithm under symmetric games. In particular, we characterize the effect of stochasticity, which has long been neglected in previous studies. The stochastic dynamics model we propose models the parameter dynamics of the learning agent as a stochastic process known as the multidimensional Wiener process. We present the sufficient conditions for the stochastic stability of the pure Nash equilibrium strategy, and evaluate the sufficient conditions for the existence of stationary distribution for strictly stable games. We also show that the dynamics of the parameter distribution can be expressed by the Fokker-Planck equation. Experiments confirm that our stochastic dynamics model always provides a significantly more accurate description of the learning dynamics than the previously proposed models in which stochasticity in the actual dynamics is neglected. These results are published in the flagship international conference AAMAS 2024. Therefore, we have successfully accomplished Objective 1(a) and Objective 2. On one hand, we have considered the situation that the game of interaction is a general bi-matrix game. We propose general models that formally describe the dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning with general bi-matrix games. We have also consider the effects of different external factors, including local interactions, incomplete information, population games and SoftMax policy gradient learning. Verified experimentally, the results produced by our new models are always more accurate than those proposed before, in which some details are ignored. In Objective 1(b), we propose to investigate joint action learners, as they are found to be more efficient than individual action learners. To this end, we start to formally investigate the complexity of reinforcement learning in multiple scenarios. The first result was published in the prestigious international conference AISTATS 2023. We study the regret for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning with the exponential utility in the episodic MDP. We show that a regret that matches the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors can be attained within a rich class of MDPs, which improves an exponential factor over the best previously known bound. Further, we derive a novel information-theoretic lower bound, which shows that the problem-dependent regret bound achieved by a variant of UCB-Advantage algorithm is optimal. Another theoretical result is published first in the flagship international conference AAMAS 2023 as an extended abstract and then in the top-tier conference NeurIPS 2023 as a full paper. We consider the scenarios of agents using options (closed-loop policies) instead of primitive actions, and they learn using offline reinforcement learning, namely, it learns from a dataset provided and no further interaction with the environment is allowed. we show that using PEVIO protocol that we propose, we achieve near-optimal information-theoretic lower bound for offline reinforcement learning with options. We also show that in the offline setting, it is more sample-efficient to learn with options than with primitive actions. We note that there is an unspent balance of HK$229,075.23, which is 32.52% of RGC budget. The main reason for the unspent balance is that we budgeted HK$654,212 for Research Staff. It was our plan to recruit a research assistant who would help in the project. However, due to the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, the University announced enhanced infection control measures. We had difficulties in recruiting suitable person for the position. Eventually there was an unspent balance of HK$228,170.87 for Research Staff.

We capture the Q-values dynamics of each individual agent by stochastic differential equations. The time evolution of the probability distribution of the population Q-values is also obtained. These theoretical results are validated with agent-based simulations. (2) We develop a model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which agents use the generalized social learning protocol. The correctness of the model is validated through agent-based simulation. We show that our model can precisely forecast that the population converges to an outcome that is qualitatively different from that predicated in previous models. (3) We develop a model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which agents play population games. Bearing a formal connection with the continuity equation in physics, the new model accurately describes the Q-learning dynamics in population games across different initial settings. We also show how the model can be used to facilitate parameter tuning that have different effects on convergence. (4) We develop a model of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in which agents learn using the SoftMax policy gradient algorithm under symmetric games. We present the sufficient conditions for the stochastic stability of the pure Nash equilibrium strategy, and evaluate the sufficient conditions for the existence of stationary distribution for strictly stable games. We express the dynamics of the parameter distribution by the Fokker-Planck equation. Experiments confirm that our stochastic dynamics model always provides a more accurate description of the learning dynamics than the previous models. (5) We study the regret for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning with the exponential utility in the episodic MDP. We show that a regret that matches the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors is attainable within a rich class of MDPs, which improves an exponential factor over the best previously known bound. Further, we derive a novel information-theoretic lower bound, which shows that the problem-dependent regret bound achieved by a variant of UCB-Advantage algorithm is optimal. (6) We consider the scenarios of agents using options (closed-loop policies), and learning using offline reinforcement learning. We show that using PEVIO protocol that we propose, we achieve near-optimal information-theoretic lower bound for offline reinforcement learning with options. 14206820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206820.value: One possible further development of the research is to investigate more scenarios and develop models of dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning in these scenarios. In this project we have investigated some of the most typical scenarios of multi-agent reinforcement learning, but we have not been able to investigate all scenarios that have been proposed before. It would be beneficial to the research community if theoretical models can be developed for more scenarios. Another possible further development is the investigation of the complexity of more complicated scenarios. The investigations that we have carried out in the project have shown that research in this direction is generally interesting yet challenging. It generally requires a better mathematical background than typical computer science graduates usually possess.

14206820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206820.value: Research into learning through repeated agent interactions in multi-agent systems has become an active topic in the field of multiagent systems. A thorough understanding of multi-agent reinforcement learning is a current topic of research. This project investigates the formal modelling of the dynamics of multi-agent reinforcement learning for the general n-agent settings when n is very large. This is an important research topic that enables researchers to give a detailed explanation of the process and find out the implications of the process. In this project, we model various typical scenarios of multi-agent reinforcement learning. These formal models are shown to produce predictions that are consistent with the agent-based simulations. These results have been presented in prestigious top-tier international conference in Artificial Intelligence. In addition, we have studied the theoretical efficiency of reinforcement learning in various settings. We have proposed novel approaches and mathematically proved that these approaches are better than best known results, and some are even theoretically proved to be the best. 14207220.label: Project Objectives
14207220.value: To establish a model to quantify the effects of bubbles and waves on underwater and air-water OWC transmission. Simulations based on the model will be implemented to gain insights on the impact of the effects and set the strategies for transmission performance optimization. Experimental verification of the model will be followed for model refinement. When optical signals pass through a swarm of bubbles with different sizes and density, the optical signal will experience time-varying attenuation, refraction, and scattering, thus resulting in signal fluctuations that affect different communication performances such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and bit-error-rate (BER). For the air-water link, the direction of light after passing through the wave surface is strongly affected by the instantaneous incident angle to the wave surface. As the wave is temporal- and spatial-varying, the received optical signal may exhibit very large fluctuation that results in total loss of signal. The above effects by wave and bubble on OWC will be extensively studied in order to establish a comprehensive communication channel model. This will lay a solid foundation for the performance optimization of the OWC system by adopting novel impairment mitigation schemes. After the establishment of the simulation model, it will be validated by an experimental testbed. A water-tank testbed with the controllable wave and bubble generation will be designed to emulate the different wave and bubble characteristics. With these controllable parameters, the testbed can emulate different wave and bubble conditions, which is important for a precise validation of the model. • To optimize the OWC system under the influence of bubble and wave by (i) adaptive spatial diversity and (ii) adaptive signal processing By using the established model, the comprehensive effects of bubbles and waves on OWC can be well understood. For this objective, we will investigate the mitigation of the impact caused by bubbles and waves, and two specific optimization schemes for underwater and air-water OWC will be considered. The first one is the optimization of the adaptive spatial diversity scheme. This scheme will investigate on how to optimize the transmitters/receivers placement and information loading, based on the characteristics of bubble and wave, to mitigate the bubble and wave effects. The second one is to leverage on the obtained bubble and wave information to implement the most suitable signal processing techniques to adaptively adjust the signal modulation and channel coding for error correction. This objective is to find the optimization strategies based on the bubble and wave statistics in a controlled environment in the lab, and the output will be valuable for the field experiments that have a more complex environment. • To develop an OWC system that can provide a data rate beyond 50 Mbps over a 50-meter underwater link or a (20+20) meter air-water link. Eventually, after the investigation of communication channel modeling and the optimization of impairments mitigation schemes, we will develop an OWC system based on our proposed and validated schemes and conduct field experiments to be carried out at the seaside of our university water sports center. The target of the developed OWC system is to provide beyond 50-Mbps data rate with robust communication over a 50-m underwater link or 20-m air plus 20-m underwater transmission link under the effect of bubbles and waves. This study will further provide feedback for the refinement of our communication model and optimization strategies. It also facilitates the engineering of the system to pave the way for possible future industrial collaboration or ITF grant applications.
