14207220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207220.value: The underwater resource expeditions are under high pursuit worldwide due to the diminishing land-based resource. Environmental sensing, such as the health monitoring of coral reefs, is also important for safeguarding the oceanic ecosystem. To facilitate these activities, high-speed and robust underwater communication systems are much needed. The communication may take place in (i) a purely underwater link or (ii) an air-water optical link involving both air-path and water-path. The former is for the communication between two underwater devices, like two autonomous underwater vehicles. The latter is for the case when the underwater device wants to communicate with an airborne, such as a relay drone, for real-time data collection. Optical wireless communication (OWC) is a promising candidate owing to its flexibility, high bandwidth, and environmental friendliness (without cable). However, many factors, including ocean turbulence, water impurity, unpredictable bubbles, and sea waves, imped the communication channel significantly, especially for the upper-layer ocean. The issues of ocean turbulence and impurity are similar to that of atmospheric turbulence and air visibility in traditional free-space OWC. On the other hand, waves and bubbles are new challenges for underwater and air-water OWCs. The light passing through wave can be significantly affected, as manifested by the distorted underwater images taken from surveillance airplanes or satellites. Besides, bubbles swarming is another common phenomenon in the sea that imposes great communication obstacles, especially for near-surface communication with bubbles generated by breaking waves. Hence, to optimize the said OWC system, a thorough understanding of the channel affected by the aforementioned factors is essential. Albeit light propagation through bubbles and waves has been investigated, most studies are on the scattering, reflection, refraction, and attenuation of light. In this proposal, the investigation will mainly focus on the dynamic effects of wave and bubble on the OWC channel, an area with very limited studies so far. We will investigate the enhancement of the OWC system to combat the effects of wave and bubble through optimizing the proposed adaptive spatial diversity scheme and advanced signal processing. A field experiment will be conducted to demonstrate the feasibility of the OWC system. Hong Kong is a harbor city with rich marine resources. The project will facilitate the green exploration of marine resources. The project outcomes will benefit the marine environment surveillance and underwater resource excavation industries, and the proactive environment protection will have a long term impact on healthy ecosystems for a sustainable fishing industry. 由於陸上資源的快速消耗，水下資源探索越來越受到全世界範圍的重視。環境監測對於保護海洋生態系統也很重要，例如珊瑚礁的變化監測。為了推動和促進這些日益增加額的水下活動，搭建高速且高效的水下通信系統是必需的。該通信可以在（i）純水下鏈路或（ii）同時涉及空氣和水下的空氣-水光學鏈路中進行。前者用於水下設備之間的通信，例如兩個智能水下機器人。後者用於水下設備想要與空中通信（例如中繼無人機）進行通信，以便進行實時數據收集。光學無線通信由於其靈活性，高帶寬和環境友好性（無電纜）而成為有競爭力的候選方案。但是，許多因素（包括海洋湍流，水中的雜質，難以預測的氣泡和海浪）嚴重影響了通信通道，特別是對於上層海域。海洋湍流和雜質的問題類似於傳統自由空間無線光通信中的大氣湍流和空氣可見度的問題。另一方面，氣泡和波浪是水下無線光通信和空氣-水下無線光通信的新挑戰。從監測飛機或衛星拍攝的變形的水下圖像可以證明，穿過海浪的光會受到嚴重影響。此外，氣泡也是海洋中的一種普遍現象，它構成了很大的通信障礙，特別是對於與由波浪產生的氣泡進行近海面通信時。因此，為了優化所述無線光通信系統，必須全面理解受到上述因素影響的通信信道。儘管已經研究了光通過氣泡和波傳播的情況，但大多數研究都是關於光的散射，反射，折射和衰減。在本研究計劃中，將主要集中於波浪和氣泡對無線光通信通道的動態影響。到目前為止，該領域的研究非常有限。我們將通過優化建議的自適應空間分集方案和高級信號處理來增強無線光通信系統性能，以對抗波浪和氣泡的影響。我們還將進行現場實驗來證明系統的可行性。香港是擁有豐富海洋資源的港口城市。該項目將促進海洋資源的綠色勘探。該項目的成果將有益於海洋環境監測和水下資源開採行業，同時也將促進環境保護以對可持續漁業的健康生態系統產生長遠影響。

14207220.label: Realisation of objectives
14207220.value: Object 1 To establish a model to quantify the effects of bubbles and waves on underwater and air-water OWC transmission. We studied the air bubble and water wave effects in underwater and air-water optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Based on Snell's law, we have simulated the laser beam propagation when passing through air bubbles and waves and derived the received optical power distribution using the Monto-Carlo method. In the invited papers [1][2], we comprehensively reviewed the recent progress in the underwater and water-air OWC system and investigated channel characterization, communication system design, and performance. [Bubble models] A 3-dimensional wave and bubble model was developed, and the distribution of received light intensity from a Gaussian beam propagating through 3-dimensional dynamic waves was analyzed. We have investigated the BER performance under the effect of bubbles with three different bubble sizes and at three different positions [2]. For a SISO scheme, it is shown that the bubble may block the line-of-sight light path and cause severe performance degradation. With the bubble position moving away from the transmitter, the number of packets suffering severe fading is reduced. [Wave models] We compared different wave parameters that directly influence the performance of the communication system. We found that even a minute wave slope variation can cause beam deflection, leading to the fluctuation of the received optical power. Then, we analyzed the wave slope’s inherent periodic characteristics in space and time domains. In this study, a wave model was synthesized by eight sine waves and then was used for subsequent wave slope prediction with the acquired time-variant wave slope trace [3]. Object 2 To optimize the OWC system under the influence of bubble and wave by (i) adaptive spatial diversity and (ii) adaptive signal processing. [Adaptive spatial diversity] Spatial diversity, including SIMO, MISO, and MIMO schemes, significantly reduces the bubble-induced BER fluctuation and increases the link stability. A robust 2×2 MIMO system was demonstrated under different scenarios of bubble size and position. Enhancements in both BER and link reliability were achieved [2]. For wave mitigation, we proposed a 1×2 SIMO system combined with the wave-aware scheme. Utilizing the proposed scheme and spatial diversities of two receivers under a wave with a maximum slope of 14.7 degrees, a maximum of 96.2% increase in throughput was achieved [3]. [Adaptive signal processing] We have explored the possibility of utilizing the wave characteristics for adaptive loading in an OWC system [3]. A novel wave-aware adaptive loading scheme was proposed to exploit the predicted wave slope to derive the expected received power and adjust the loaded bit accordingly. An adaptive SIMO system further improved the system throughput by 49.3% and 30.4% compared with using one diversity in the time or space domain, with a reduced packet loss rate of 8.4%. We employed an advanced DSP algorithm to improve the performance of the visible light communication systems for blue-green wavelength [4]. A simplified third-order Volterra equalization and orthogonal circulant matrix transform (OCT) precoding were proposed to realize a 4.5-Gbit/s WDM transmission with 50% capacity enhancement. In addition, we proposed two compensation signal processing methods to achieve higher device linearity [5]: a passive nonlinear compensation scheme [6] and a programmable anti-logarithm linearization scheme [7]. To simplify the accurate photovoltaic detection, a dynamic AC model is proposed for frequency response optimization [8]. Object 3 To develop a real-time OWC system that can provide a data rate beyond 50 Mbps over a 50-meter underwater link or a (20+20) meter air-water link in the sea. [Beam-steering] To compensate for the wave-induced beam deflection, we utilized the light intensity distribution of a feedback beam from the receiver and controlled the beam-steering angle. In [9], we developed a stable 50-Mbps optical wireless link over a 0.8-m air path and 0.1-m water path using real-time MEMS mirror-based beam tracking. Then, we comprehensively investigate the performance of the beam tracking system under different wave conditions, data rates, modulation formats, and air-path height [10]. To characterize the dynamic wave, a new parameter, average wave slope changing rate (ASCR), was proposed, and it showed ASCR is highly related to communication performance. With beam tracking, a maximum throughput of 1.25 Gb/s was achieved, and the packet loss rate (PLR) was significantly reduced from 75% to 11% for the OWC system with a 1.2-m air distance at an ASCR of 0.34 rad/s. In communication, one critical and more general performance metric is the product of transmission distance and data rate for characterizing the performance of a communication link. In our objective, we targeted a data rate of 50 Mbits/s over a distance of (20+20) meters, which corresponds to a value of 2 Gbits*m/s if we treat air and water distances roughly the same. With a limited working space in our lab and the feedback from our industrial partner, we reduce the working path distance but highly enhance the data rate. Through our work, we successfully realized a data rate of 1.25 Gbits/s over a distance of (1.2+0.14) meters, achieving a value of 1.675 Gbits*m/s. [Data-rate enhancement] To further increase the system’s data rates, wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) can be employed. The superior beam steering ability of OPA can be used for beam wandering compensation to realize robust water-air OWC systems. We have realized a blue-green WDM-VLC system using an OPA with narrow channel spacings for WDM to boost the system capacity in a proof-of-concept demonstration [4]. [1] L. -K. Chen, Y. Shao, and Y. 14207220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207220.value: In this project, we investigated the effects of bubbles and waves on underwater and water-air OWC systems. To improve the data rate and robustness of the systems, we have proposed methods: adaptive spatial diversity, adaptive signal processing, and beam-steering. The main findings and outcomes are: • Adaptive spatial diversity scheme Spatial diversity techniques like SIMO, MISO, and MIMO were developed to mitigate the effects of bubbles and waves. A robust 2x2 MIMO system is demonstrated with significant BER reduction and link reliability enhancement under different bubble sizes and positions [J1]. For wave mitigation, a 1x2 SIMO scheme combined with a wave-aware adaptive loading algorithm exploiting predicted wave slopes achieved a maximum 96.2% throughput increase [C2]. • DSP and coding scheme Advanced signal processing algorithms enabled higher data rates and capacity. A simplified 3rd-order Volterra equalization combined with orthogonal circulant transform precoding realized a 4.5-Gbit/s WDM visible light transmission with 50% capacity enhancement [C5]. A novel wave-aware adaptive bit loading scheme adjusting the loaded bits based on predicted wave slope further improved throughput by 30.4% compared to using diversity in the space domain [C2]. Via DSP approaches, we realized the reduction of distortion-induced BER degradation [J3]. The passive diode array scheme achieved one order of BER reduction for a 1-Mbit/s link [C4]. • Real-time beam tracking scheme To mitigate wave-induced beam wander in water-air OWC system, we have proposed a beam tracking system based on a microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) mirror, realizing a maximum throughput of 1.25-Gbit/s with a 1.2-m air path and 0.14-m water path [J2, C3]. In theory, this solution can be adapted for mobile scenarios. It is worth noting that no feedback channel is required for the beam tracking scheme. In addition, a new parameter, the average wave slope changing rate (ASCR), was proposed, which provided a unified standard for others to evaluate the severity of the wave conditions.

14207220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207220.value: For further wave modeling, we can investigate the wavefront of the distorted beam through the water-air interface. Such modeling will give a clearer picture of how to characterize wave-induced wavefront distortion and how to mitigate related degradations. For the beam tracking system in the water-air OWC system, the image-based beam tracking method can be considered in order to mitigate beam wandering induced by time-varying waves and the transceiver’s mobility. Advances in deep learning and computer vision can be leveraged to restore wave-induced image distortion despite the refractive effects of the water-air interface. In addition to MEMS mirrors, we can explore other advanced beam shaping and beam steering techniques to demonstrate improved resilience against wave-induced distortions. This could include using deformable mirrors, spatial light modulators, or optical phased arrays (OPA) that can dynamically compensate for the aberrations caused by the dynamic wave conditions.

14207220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207220.value: This research project studied the fundamental challenges of optical wireless communications (OWC) underwater and across the air-water surface that enable various applications, such as remote environmental monitoring, offshore infrastructure inspection, and underwater exploration. However, the harsh underwater environment, with bubbles, waves, and turbidity, severely impacts optical signal transmission and reception. Advanced technologies were developed to overcome these challenges and realize robust optical wireless links in water-air OWC systems. Key innovations, including spatial diversity, advanced signal processing algorithms, and dynamic beam steering techniques, were proposed to mitigate the detrimental effects of waves and bubbles. The developed technologies allow an autonomous underwater vehicle to utilize a high-speed beam tracking system to continuously steer the laser beam to the center of an aerial drone, ensuring reliable data transfer across the air-water interface. In addition, signal processing methods are employed to mitigate wave-induced power fluctuations at the receiver side. We also implement multi-laser transmitters that can help ensure reliable data even in channels with dynamic waves. These technical breakthroughs pave the way for the practical deployment of OWC systems to unlock new possibilities for remote sensing, infrastructure monitoring, and underwater exploration applications.

14207320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207320.value: Many construction and maintenance tasks, such as painting, cleaning, and repairing, of exterior walls of high-rise buildings are being performed by human workers standing on a cage hung from the top of the building by ropes. There are strong concerns on the operational safety because a number of death accidents happened last a few years. Tremendous efforts have been made to developing robots for this purpose, but none of them can work reliably due to the complicated wall environments. A feasible solution is to replace the workers by a robot manipulator installed on the cage. In order for such a rope-cage-manipulator system to perform the tasks satisfactorily, there are several technical challenges to solve. First, the hung cage in the sky is subject to vibration due to various factors, such as winds, motion of the robot manipulator, disturbance, etc., so it is challenging to control the manipulator stably regardless of the vibration. Second, it is not trivial to measure, with good accuracy, position and orientation of the vibrating cage in the 3D space. Third, the dynamics of the rope-cage-manipulator system is difficult to develop and identify, and hence leads to great challenges in the controller design and stability analysis. This project aims at solving the following challenging technical issues: 1) dynamic modeling of the rope-cage-manipulator system, 2) measurement of position and orientation of the cage floating in the sky, 3) controller design for position and trajectory control of the end-effector and the stability analysis, and 4) validation of the developed approaches by field experiments on walls of a real high-rise building. Since Hong Kong is featured by high-rise buildings, so the outputs of this project will not only advance the technology in robotics and automation but also have direct applications in Hong Kong. 14207320.label: Realisation of objectives
14207320.value: 1. To develop a dynamic model of the rope-cage-manipulator system We have fully achieved this objective. The system exhibits complex nonlinear dynamics due to strong coupling between flexible ropes and rigid components, where unmodeled vibrations can severely compromise system stability. To tackle these modeling complexities, we have developed a hybrid dynamic framework integrating both analytical and data-driven approaches. First, we employed principles from antagonistic pump research to characterize tension dynamics in suspension ropes. Then, we used stability analysis methods from floating ROV studies to model the cage's inertial properties. To overcome the challenge of viscoelastic rope behavior, we adapted advanced modeling techniques from soft actuator research. We have designed an uncertainty quantification module to address measurement noise issues, while global optimization approaches were implemented to fulfill the need for robust parameter identification. This comprehensive modeling framework successfully captures the system's dynamic characteristics across various operational scenarios. 2. To develop a sensing system for real-time measurement of motion of the floating cage We have fully achieved this objective. Accurate motion tracking is challenged by multi-axis vibrations and potential sensor occlusions in constrained environments. To solve these sensing problems, we have developed a vision sensing system to precisely measure the motion of the cage in the horizontal direction. An algorithm has been developed to fuse the information to estimate the 6D pose on-line. Experiments were conducted to validate the performance of the pose estimation algorithm. To fulfill the need for robust visual perception, we incorporated cutting-edge depth estimation and 3D reconstruction techniques. We have designed a sophisticated sensor fusion framework using precision calibration techniques and neural network-based stereo matching. The spherical mapping methodology was employed to overcome orientation estimation difficulties, resulting in an integrated sensing solution that provides reliable motion tracking under various operational conditions. 3. To design controllers for regulation and trajectory tracking of the robot manipulator using sensor feedback and to analyze the stability We have fully achieved this objective. The control system must maintain precise positioning despite significant base vibrations and time-varying dynamics. To tackle these control challenges, we have developed a hierarchical control architecture with multiple innovative features. We developed a motion controller to decouple the control of the hung aerial cage and the motion control of the 7 DOF robot manipulator based on the joint space orthogonalization principle for decoupling position and force controls of a robot manipulator interacting with a physical environment. Adaptive-template matching principles were implemented to overcome vibration compensation challenges in a changeable environment. Then, we used reinforcement learning strategies from pump control research to address dynamic load adaptation needs. We have designed a stability-guaranteed controller incorporating global optimization and predictive modeling to overcome tracking performance limitations. Advanced state estimation approaches were employed to address challenges under disturbances, creating a robust control system capable of maintaining precise operation in dynamic environments. The intuitive teleoperation framework was adapted to fulfill human-machine control interface requirements. 4. To develop a prototype system and validate the controllers by experiments We have fully achieved this objective. The validation process faces significant challenges in maintaining measurement accuracy while replicating real-world operational conditions, where unpredictable disturbances and system nonlinearities may compromise controller performance. To validate the practicality and calibration effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we established an outdoor gondola aerial construction robot to scan the walls. The LiDAR calibration and mapping experiments shows the online 2D LiDAR calibration method eliminates the need for special artificial markers or extensive environmental feature scanning on a mobile platform. To verify the vibration suppression capability of our adaptive controller, we constructed a scaled-down test platform with adjustable rope tension and base excitation mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrated the controller's effectiveness in maintaining end-effector positioning accuracy. To validate the trajectory tracking performance under dynamic loading, we developed a movable payload system that could introduce variable disturbances. The tests showed our hierarchical controller successfully maintained tracking errors during payload variations. For teleoperation validation, we implemented a console interface adapted from human teleoperated robotic arm platforms, which verified the intuitive control mapping in all operational modes. These results conclusively demonstrate the viability of our proposed sensing and control approach in real-world high-rise construction applications.

14207320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207320.value: In the research project, we have developed dynamic modeling, sensing systems, and control strategies for the rope-cage-manipulator system, extending the algorithms to diverse applications. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows: (1) We developed a dynamic model of the rope-cage-manipulator system by integrating motion and dynamic constraints, enabling precise pose estimation under environmental disturbances. The work led to one journal paper (Part C-8-2) and one conference paper (Part C-9-7). (2) We designed a sensing system using LiDARs and FBG sensors for real-time motion measurement and force estimation. The system achieved high accuracy in shape reconstruction and environmental mapping. The work led to two journal papers (Part C-8-1, Part C-8-6) and two conference papers (Part C-9-1, Part C-9-9). (3) We developed robust controllers for trajectory tracking and stabilization, leveraging adaptive-template matching and uncertainty-aware neural rendering. The work led to one journal paper (Part C-8-4) and two conference papers (Part C-9-2, Part C-9-8). (4) We created a prototype system with soft pneumatic actuators and real-time vision-based control, validated through experiments in surgical and aerial construction scenarios. The work led to one journal paper (Part C-8-5) and two conference papers (Part C-9-3, Part C-9-4). (5) We advanced vision-based control with globally optimal camera orientation estimation and neural Markov random fields for stereo matching. The work led to one journal paper (Part C-8-3) and one conference paper (Part C-9-5). (6) We introduced novel probabilistic methods for vanishing point estimation and 3D scene reconstruction, enhancing robotic perception in dynamic environments. The work led to one conference paper (Part C-9-6).

14207320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207320.value: This project focuses on developing a rope-suspended robotic manipulator system for high-rise construction and maintenance tasks, integrating dynamic modeling, real-time sensing, adaptive control, and experimental validation. Its significance lies in enhancing automation, safety, and efficiency in hazardous and labor-intensive environments, particularly in construction, infrastructure inspection, and urban maintenance. The system’s ability to operate in dynamic, unstructured settings make it applicable to building facade cleaning, structural assembly, and disaster response. Further development of this research could focus on enhancing the system's adaptability, precision, and autonomy while expanding its applications in construction, inspection, and collaborative robotics. The following research directions are proposed: (1) Develop more advanced control and planning algorithms for large scale vision reconstruction method in close and featureless environment; (2) Integrate more deep learning and reinforcement learning into the control system for better environment understanding and task planning; (3) Developing more efficient real-time control and sensing algorithms for cooperation in the rope-manipulation system with human interaction; (4) Explore multi-robot coordination for collaborative tasks like facade maintenance using shared control and distributed sensing.

14207320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207320.value: This project developed an innovative robotic system suspended from tall buildings to perform high-altitude maintenance and construction tasks. The main challenge was creating a stable, precisely controlled robotic arm that could work effectively while swinging on ropes hundreds of meters above ground, dealing with wind, vibrations, and constantly changing positions. We successfully created mathematical models to predict the system's movements, designed special sensors to track its position in real-time, and developed smart control algorithms that automatically adjust for stability. The robotic system proved capable of performing delicate operations like structural inspections and component installations at extreme heights. Through extensive testing, we demonstrated the technology's reliability in real-world conditions, resulting in 6 journal publications, 9 conference presentations. This research provides a groundbreaking solution for safer and more efficient high-rise building maintenance. By replacing human workers in dangerous aerial jobs with these robotic systems, we can significantly reduce workplace accidents while improving construction and maintenance quality. Further investigation could be the improvement of the system for practical applications.

14207520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207520.value: 長途重型卡車限时运输的節能优化：動態速度和機會駕駛

14207520.label: Project Objectives
14207520.value: We will construct models of heterogeneous road conditions and time-varying traffic conditions and validate them using real-world data. We will formulate the energy-efficient timely transportation problem for heavy-duty trucks based on the model. We will then investigate the performance limit of timely transportation optimization and design efficient and effective schemes to approach the limit. We will take into account the impact of opportunistic driving on traffic conditions in the performance optimization and investigate the system performance under the strategic behaviors by individual trucks/vehicles and the background traffic. We will extend the solutions to the (more) realistic settings where the traffic conditions need to be predicted, by using highway traffic prediction schemes (to be developed) with unique considerations posed by long-haul transportation. We will also consider the problem of minimizing emission instead of fuel consumption, which is more relevant for reducing the negative societal impact and has a non-convex objective instead of a convex one as in the fuel minimization. We will develop an online software tool for drivers to obtained fuel-optimized solutions with path planning, dynamic speed planning, and opportunistic driving into consideration.

14207520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207520.value: 目的 我們將優化重型卡車運營的一個關鍵模塊，限時運輸。我們的目標是通過動態速度規劃和機會性駕駛，在時變的交通條件下最小化燃油消耗。 項目背景和項目描述 在美國，重型卡車只佔車輛總數的4%，卻消耗整個運輸部門，包括車輛和飛機[1]，18%的能源。同時，燃料費用佔卡車運營成本的26~34%，達數百億美元[1]。這些的觀察，加上到2050年全球貨運活動將預計增加2.4倍，使得降低重型卡車運營的燃料消耗至關重要。在這個項目裡，我們通過優化一個關鍵的卡車操作模式，限時運輸，來最小化燃料消耗。重型卡車在國家公路系統兩個地點之間行駛，有嚴格的運輸時限。與已有的研究不同，我們考慮了時變交通條件，並探討了兩類新的優化空間：動態速度規劃和機會性駕駛 (分鐘級)動態速度規劃:我們最近的研究表明，基於gps導航和自適應巡航控制的分鐘級速度規劃可以為重型卡車節省10%的燃料[3]。因此，在燃料最小化中考慮動態速度規劃是既實用又有前景的。 機會性駕駛:這種新的設計空間是時變交通條件的結果。這個想法是為了讓卡車策略性地等待(例如在高速公路休息區)良好的交通狀況，以合適的速度穿越後續路段，從而節省燃料。我們基於美國高速公路實際數據的案例研究表明，在道路和速度規劃的基礎上，機會性駕駛可以額外節省11%的燃料[4]。因此，我們希望進一步探索這一新的優化空間，最大限度地節約能耗。 同時，探索這些新的優化空間也給系統建模和解決方案設計帶來了前所未有的挑戰。我們將解決這些挑戰，並開發算法，在實際情況下為重型卡車節省20-30%的燃料。首先，我們將開發一種考慮時變交通條件、動態速度優化和機會駕駛的新型限時運輸方案。其次，我們將開發具有良好性能的算法。我們將解決關鍵問題，將我們的方案擴展到實際的設置，包括高速公路交通預測和在線決策面對交通不確定性。我們還將在一個在線軟件工具中實現我們的解決方案，以便在實踐中使用。在一個案例研究中，我們觀察到通過優化限時運輸，節省了約20%的燃料。我們將在初步成功的基礎上，開發切實可行的解決方案，以充分利用動態速度規劃和機會性駕駛在限時運輸節能中帶來的好處。 項目的意義 該項目的成功完成將產生新的理論技術和在線軟件工具，以優化限時運輸的重型卡車。所獲得的策略也可以作為未來解決方案設計的基準。

14207520.label: Realisation of objectives
14207520.value: For objective 1, we have successfully constructed models of heterogeneous road conditions and time-varying traffic conditions and validated them using real-world data. We have formulated the energy-efficient timely transportation problem for heavy-duty trucks based on the model. We have investigated the performance limit of timely transportation optimization and designed efficient and effective schemes to approach the limit. The results have been published in IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems. For objective 2, we have established a game theory model to investigate the system performance under the strategic opportunistic-driving behaviors by individual trucks/vehicles and the background traffic. The results suggest interesting interaction among trucks carrying out opportunistic driving, under popular traffic models. The results have been documented and are under submission. For objective 3, we have developed a model for highway traffic prediction with experimental results. Further, we have investigated the problem of minimizing emission instead of fuel consumption, which is more relevant for reducing the negative societal impact and has a non-convex objective instead of a convex one as in the fuel minimization. We have published a paper on ACM BuildSys 2020. Its substantially revised version has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems (currently in the 2nd round review, where the 1st round decision is Minor Revision). For objective 4, we have developed an online platform for drivers to obtained fuel-optimized solutions with path planning and dynamic speed planning. We have implemented an iOS APP to give GPS-like instructions for the drivers to use in real-time on the road. See www.e2pilots.com for more information and demos.

14207520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207520.value: Our research project successfully achieved its objectives, significantly advancing the understanding and optimization of energy-efficient timely transportation for heavy-duty trucks. Below is a summary of our major findings and research outcomes based on our five key publications: Model Construction and Validation: We developed comprehensive models capturing heterogeneous road conditions and time-varying traffic dynamics. These models were rigorously validated using real-world data from the US national highway system. Using these models, we formulated the energy-efficient timely transportation problem, proving it to be NP-hard. We then designed efficient algorithms to approach the performance limits of timely transportation optimization. Our simulations showed up to 21% fuel savings, demonstrating the effectiveness of our models and algorithms. Opportunistic Driving and Traffic Impact: We explored the concept of opportunistic driving, where trucks strategically wait for favorable traffic conditions to improve fuel efficiency. Our studies revealed that opportunistic driving could reduce fuel consumption by up to 20% and driving time by 6% compared to traditional methods. We also examined the impact of opportunistic driving on overall traffic conditions and found that it could be a win-win strategy, reducing congestion and benefiting both individual trucks and background traffic. Traffic Prediction and Emission Minimization: Extending our solutions to more realistic settings, we developed traffic prediction schemes tailored for long-haul transportation. These schemes improved the accuracy of traffic condition forecasts, enabling better optimization of truck operations. Additionally, we addressed the problem of minimizing emissions instead of fuel consumption, which is critical for reducing societal impacts. We formulated the emission minimization problem, accounting for non-convex objectives due to multiple fuel injection strategies and gear positions. Our algorithms achieved up to 46% NOx emission reduction, highlighting the importance of considering heterogeneous speed profiles and adaptive control strategies. Development of Online Software Tool: We created an online software tool for drivers, integrating path planning, dynamic speed planning, and opportunistic driving into a unified solution. This tool provides fuel-optimized routes and schedules, considering real-time traffic conditions and predictive models. The tool's user-friendly interface and robust backend algorithms ensure practical applicability for truck drivers, contributing to significant fuel and emission savings in real-world operations. Overall, our research provides a comprehensive framework for optimizing the energy efficiency and environmental impact of heavy-duty truck transportation. Our findings and developed tools offer valuable insights and practical solutions for the trucking industry, promoting sustainable and efficient freight transportation.

14207520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207520.value: Pilot Programs: Implement pilot programs with logistics companies to validate the effectiveness of the developed solutions in real-world settings. Collaborations: Partner with automotive and technology firms to integrate our algorithms with cutting-edge vehicle and traffic management systems. Policy Advocacy: Engage with policymakers to promote regulations and incentives that support the adoption of energy-efficient transportation technologies. Continuous Improvement: Establish a feedback loop with industry stakeholders to continuously refine and enhance the algorithms based on real-world performance data.

14207520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207520.value: Nature of the Research Our research focused on making heavy-duty trucks more energy-efficient and environmentally friendly. We developed advanced models to understand how different road conditions and traffic patterns affect fuel consumption and emissions. We also explored innovative strategies like "opportunistic driving," where trucks wait for better traffic conditions to save fuel. Significance of the Research This research is crucial because heavy-duty trucks contribute significantly to pollution and fuel consumption. By optimizing routes, speeds, and charging stops for electric trucks, we can reduce their environmental impact. Our findings show that strategic driving can lower fuel use by up to 21% and emissions by up to 46%, which is a substantial improvement. Value of the Research The practical value of our work lies in its potential to transform the trucking industry. We developed an online tool to help truck drivers plan the most fuel-efficient routes and schedules, considering real-time traffic. This tool can lead to significant savings in fuel costs and reduce harmful emissions, benefiting both the environment and the economy. Our research thus provides a comprehensive framework for promoting greener and more efficient freight transportation.

14207620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207620.value: 兩個時間不壹致資產定價問題的研究

14207620.label: Project Objectives
14207620.value: We plan to study asset pricing in an endowment economy in which a representative agent has horizon-dependent risk aversion and acts in a sophisticated way when facing time inconsistency, and to study the effect of horizon-dependent risk aversion on asset prices. We plan to study asset pricing in an endowment economy in which a representative agent is ambiguous about the random outcomes in the economy and has alpha-maxmin expected utility preferences. Assuming that the agent is sophisticated, we plan to derive asset prices in market equilibrium and study the effect of ambiguity aversion on the asset prices. We plan to generalize the models in Objectives 1 and 2 by incorporating the framework of recursive utility. To this end, we plan to develop new tools to solve time-inconsistent stochastic control problems involving recursive utility components.
rows: We plan to study asset pricing in an endowment economy in which a representative agent has horizon-dependent risk aversion and acts in a sophisticated way when facing time inconsistency, and to study the effect of horizon-dependent risk aversion on asset prices.

We plan to study asset pricing in an endowment economy in which a representative agent is ambiguous about the random outcomes in the economy and has alpha-maxmin expected utility preferences. Assuming that the agent is sophisticated, we plan to derive asset prices in market equilibrium and study the effect of ambiguity aversion on the asset prices.

We plan to generalize the models in Objectives 1 and 2 by incorporating the framework of recursive utility. To this end, we plan to develop new tools to solve time-inconsistent stochastic control problems involving recursive utility components.

14207620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207620.value: Many existing models of intertemporal choices, such as expected utility theory, recursive utility theory, and habit formation, imply time-consistency. However, it has been found that when making intertemporal choices, individuals' behavior can be time-inconsistent: an action that is optimal under the decision criterion today may no longer be optimal under the decision criterion at certain future time. In the presence of time-inconsistency, the agent can be naive in that she is not aware of the inconsistency and thus keeps re-optimizing and changing her action over time or be sophisticated in that she is aware of the inconsistency, has no control of her future selves, and chooses her action today by anticipating the action of her future selves. In this proposal, we plan to study consumption-based asset pricing under two models of intertemporal choices that lead to time-inconsistency, assuming that the agents in the market are sophisticated. The first one is a model of horizon-dependent risk aversion, a phenomenon that individuals are more risk averse regarding a risk that is temporally close than a risk that is distant. The second one is the alpha-maxmin expected utility model that describes individuals’ preferences under ambiguity. We plan to apply existing methods in the literature on time-inconsistent problems and develop new tools as well to solve the above asset pricing problems and study the effect of horizon-dependent risk aversion and ambiguity aversion on asset prices. 文獻中許多跨期選擇的模型，譬如期望效用理論、遞歸效用理論、以及習慣形成模型等，都是時間壹致的。然而，很多研究表明，人們在面臨跨期選擇的時候會表現出時間不壹致的行為：壹個從現在來看是最優的決策到了將來就不壹定是最優的了。如果壹個人沒有意識到她的時間不壹致行為，那麽她就會每時每刻不停地重新規劃她的決策，導致她不停地改變她的決策。如果她意識到了自己的時間不壹致行為，但又沒有辦法控制她將來的自己來執行今天設定的策略，那麽她就會基於對將來自己行為的預期而選擇今天自己的策略。 在這個提案中，我們計劃研究在兩個涉及到時間不壹致性的跨期選擇模型下的資產定價問題。我們假設投資者意識到了自己的時間不壹致行為但卻沒有能力控制自己將來的行為。我們首先考慮壹個關於依賴於投資期限的風險厭惡模型。在該模型下，當面臨壹個離當前時間更近的風險時，投資者會表現得更加風險厭惡。我們接著考慮所謂的alpha-maxmin期望效用模型。該模型用以描述投資者面臨不確定性時的行為：投資者不僅關心可能發生的最壞的情況，也關心可能發生的最差的情況。我們計劃運用文獻中已有的、研究時間不壹致性問題的方法，並且發展壹些新的工具和理論來研究上述兩個模型下的資產定價問題。然後，我們計劃研究投資者的風險厭惡和不確定性厭惡對資產價格的影響。

14207620.label: Realisation of objectives
14207620.value: We study the effect of horizon-dependent risk aversion on portfolio selection by considering a portfolio selection model in which the investor is more risk averse when the time horizon becomes shorter. This portfolio selection is time-inconsistent because of the horizon-dependent risk aversion. To address the issue of time inconsistency, we consider the notion of intra-personal equilibrium. We derive the investor's intra-personal equilibrium strategy in closed form and make a connection with the fractional Kelly strategy commonly used in the market. The intra-personal equilibrium strategy has a good empirical performance. We find that under the intra-personal equilibrium strategy, the investor allocates more of her wealth in the equity market compared to another myopic investor. Thus, horizon-dependent risk aversion can imply a large demand for equities and thus push up equity prices in the market. The above results can be found in Research Output C-8-1. These results show that Objective 1 has been completely achieved. We consider an asset pricing model in which a representative agent invests in a risk-free asset and two risky assets and consumes continuously in a pure-exchange economy. The agent’s preferences for consumption are represented by the alpha-maxmin model. Due to time inconsistency, we consider intra-personal equilibrium strategies for the agent. We then define market equilibrium to be the one in which the strategy of consuming the aggregate endowment and investing all her wealth in the risky assets is an intra-personal equilibrium. We characterize the asset prices in the market equilibrium by a nonlinear ordinary differential equation. By studying this equation, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the market equilibrium. We then study the impact of ambiguity aversion and the degree of ambiguity on asset prices. The above results can be found in Research Output C-8-3. These results show that Objective 2 has been completely achieved. We have also generalized the alpha-maxmin expected utility preferences by incorporating the recursive utility framework. More precisely, we have derived the equilibrium asset prices when the dividend process is equal to the consumption process and follows a geometric Brownian motion and studied the effect of elasticity of intertemporal substitution on asset prices. These results are in a working paper under preparation. We have also studied the effect of introducing a recursive structure to time-inconsistent portfolio selection problems and found that it can lead to extreme investment strategies: Investors do not diversify between risky and risk-free assets. These results can be found in Research Ouput C-8-2. The above results show that Objective 3 has been completely achieved.

14207620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207620.value: First, we find that horizon-dependent risk aversion can lead to larger demand for equities that horizon-dependent risk aversion is consistent with the life-cycle investment wisdom. Moreover, the use of fractional Kelly strategies in the market implies horizon-dependent risk aversion. These results are in Research Output C-8-1, which is under the 2nd round review in Operations Research, one of the flagship journals in the area of operations research and management science. Second, we derive asset prices in a pure-exchange economy where the agents have alpha-maxmin preferences for consumption. We find that the risk-free rate is decreasing and the stock equity premium is increasing with respect to the ambiguity aversion degree. These results are in Research Output C-8-3, which is to be submitted to Management Science, one of the flagship journals in the area of operations research and management science. Third, we combine a recursive structure with the alpha-maxmin preference model and derive equilibrium asset prices in a pure-exchange economy. We also study the effect of the recursive structure on portfolio selection and find that such a structure can lead to non-diversified investment in risk-free and risky assets. The latter result is in Research Output C-8-2, which is under the 3rd round review in Management Science, one of the flagship journals in the area of operations research and management science. Fourth, we apply the methodologies developed in this project to another time-inconsistent problem. In this problem, an agent has a preference that is a mixture of the classical expected utility theory and the prospect theory and decides when to stop a diffusion process. We consider two types of strategies, naïve strategy and sophisticated strategy, and find that the agent will never stop under the naïve strategy and will never start under the sophisticated strategy. The results are published in the Journal of Economic Theory, one of the leading journals in theoretical economics; see Research Output C-8-4. Finally, the PI has trained a PhD student to complete part of the project. The student graduated in 2023; see Research Output 10.

14207620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207620.value: First, we can develop a new preference model that combines horizon-dependent risk aversion and counter-cyclical risk aversion. The latter pattern of risk aversion is also observed in the market. Then, we can study portfolio selection and asset pricing under this new model. Second, we can compare the asset pricing results under the alpha-maxmin preference model and under other preference models that exhibit the so-called first-order risk aversion, such as the model of disappointment and the model of narrow framing with loss aversion.

14207620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207620.value: Horizon-dependent risk aversion is commonly observed in experiments and a common wisdom. For example, investors tend to be more conservative when approaching retirement age. On the other hand, economic models, such as the mean return rate of a stock, are difficult to estimate using market data. Thus, the investment environment is ambiguous to investors. Experimental evidence shows that individuals can be ambiguity-averse and ambiguity-seeking simultaneously. In this project, we show how investors with horizon-dependent risk aversion or facing ambiguity should make their investment decisions and how they affect the asset prices in the market. These results are useful to guide investment in the market.

14207820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207820.value: 大規模並行多路聯接算法

14207820.label: Project Objectives
14207820.value: Our first objective is to develop massively parallel, communication-economical, algorithms for processing multiway joins with strong performance guarantees. The second objective is to engineer the discovered theoretical algorithms into practical solutions that have excellent efficiency on existing platforms for large-scaled parallel computation such as Hadoop, Spark, Dremel, Hive, etc. The third objective is to maximize the influence of the algorithms in the preceding two objectives by adapting them to concrete applications such as subgraph isomorphism, mining social networks, entity matching, online analytical processing, machine learning, etc.
rows: Our first objective is to develop massively parallel, communication-economical, algorithms for processing multiway joins with strong performance guarantees.

The second objective is to engineer the discovered theoretical algorithms into practical solutions that have excellent efficiency on existing platforms for large-scaled parallel computation such as Hadoop, Spark, Dremel, Hive, etc.

The third objective is to maximize the influence of the algorithms in the preceding two objectives by adapting them to concrete applications such as subgraph isomorphism, mining social networks, entity matching, online analytical processing, machine learning, etc.

14207820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207820.value: In the current big-data era, massively parallel systems (such as Hadoop, Spark, Dremel, Hive, etc.) have emerged as a major computing paradigm to cope with the gigantic data volumes encountered in many applications. These systems use a large number (usually hundreds or thousands) of servers to carry out computation in parallel. Conventional algorithms which were designed to maximize CPU efficiency are not suitable on such systems, because the new performance bottleneck is no longer CPU computation, but rather the shuffling of data, or more specifically, the communication required to exchange information among the servers. Minimizing such communication demands techniques drastically different from those developed in sequential or small-scaled parallel systems. This project plans to study massively parallel algorithms for multiway joins, which constitute a very frequent operation demanded by database queries, and yet unfortunately are by far the most expensive operation in database systems today. Optimizing the performance of joins has always been a central topic in database research, and especially so in recent years due to the urgent need to design efficient computing solutions applicable on massively parallel platforms. While significant progress has been gained on binary joins (i.e., joins that have only two participating relations), to process multiway joins (i.e., involving three or more relations) the current systems largely follow the textbook approach that "joins two relations at a time". That approach, unfortunately, suffers from the serious drawback of generating huge immediate results, namely, tuples that are produced by the binary joins performed early in the plan, but then need to be discarded eventually in the binary joins performed subsequently. Motivated by this, we will carry out a systematic study to design algorithms that departs from the join-two-relations-at-a-time approach, generate provably small intermediate results, carry excellent performance guarantees, and have robust performance on real-world data. We will also explore the influence of the proposed multiway join algorithms on other application scenarios including subgraph isomorphism, mining social networks, online analytical processing entity matching, matrix analysis for machine learning, etc. 在當前的大數據時代，海量並行運算系統（例如Hadoop，Spark，Dremel，Hive，等）在現實應用中已經成為必不可少的組成部分。此類系統通常使用數以百計的服務器來合作完成計算任務。它們的性能瓶頸在于服務器之間的通信量而不是CPU的工作時間。正因爲如此，算法設計不應再常規性地去優化CPU的效率，而是應該盡可能地減少通信。這就要求我們在算法設計上要實現一反常規的突破。 本項目將研究用於解決“多路聯接”問題的海量並行算法。“多路聯接”是數據庫系統中最頻繁出現的操作之一而卻恰恰又是最昂貴的操作之一，所以優化聯接算法一直是數據庫研究的中心主題，尤其是近年來由於海量並行運算的興起更是如此。雖然前人對此課題的研究已取得了一定的進展，大部分的工作停留在“雙聯接”（即只有兩個關系表參與的聯接）。而對于 “多路聯接”（即有多個關系表參與的聯接），當今系統在很大程度上仍依賴教科書中“一次連接兩個關係”的方法，盡管這種方法衆所周知在性能上有著嚴重缺陷。 本項目旨在擺脫傳統的“一次連接兩個關係”的思維從而開發新的多路聯接算法。我們的初步研究顯示，通過減少中間的運算結果我們可以設計出具有出色性能保證的算法，並且大幅度減少實際應用中的通信量。本項目將深化完善我們研究團隊的多路聯接算法，還將探討此類算法在其他重大相關問題上的應用，例如子圖匹配，社交網絡挖掘，在線實體匹配，矩陣分析，等等。

14207820.label: Realisation of objectives
14207820.value: The description below refers to the publications listed at the end of this report. J_i [resp., C_i] stands for the i-th journal [resp., conference] article; e.g., J_1 is the first journal article, and C_2 is the second conference paper. In C_1, we revisited an algorithm developed by Hu In PODS21 in the massively parallel computation [MPC] model that processes any acyclic join with an asymptotically optimal load. We presented an alternative analysis of her algorithm. The novelty of our analysis is in the revelation of a new mathematical structure - which we name canonical edge cover - for acyclic hypergraphs. We proved non-trivial properties for canonical edge covers that offer us a graph-theoretic perspective about why the algorithm of Hu works. This research output contributes to the realization of Objectives 1 and 2. In J_4, We study equi-join computation in the massively parallel computation [MPC] model. Currently, a main open question under this topic is whether it is possible to design an algorithm that can process any join with load O[N polylog N / p^{1/rho*}] - measured in the number of words communicated per machine - where N is the total number of tuples in the input relations, rho* is the join fractional edge covering number, and p is the number of machines. We settle the question in the negative for the class of tuple-based algorithms [all the known MPC join algorithms fall in this class] by proving the existence of a join query with rho* ≈ 2 that requires a load of Omega[N/p^{1/3}] to evaluate. Our lower bound provides solid evidence that the AGM bound alone is not sufficient for characterizing the hardness of join evaluation in MPC [a phenomenon that does not exist in RAM]. The hard join instance identified in our argument is cyclic, which leaves the question of whether O[N polylog N / p^{1/rho*}] is still possible for acyclic joins. We answer this question in the affirmative by showing that any acyclic join can be evaluated with load O[N / p^{1/rho*}], which is asymptotically optimal [there are no polylogarithmic factors in our bound]. The separation between cyclic and acyclic joins is yet another phenomenon that is absent in RAM. Our algorithm owes to the discovery of a new mathematical structure of acyclic hypergraphs, which has numerous non-trivial properties and makes an elegant addition to database theory. This research output contributes to the realization of Objectives 1 and 2. In J_2, we developed a constant-round algorithm in the massively parallel computation [MPC] model for evaluating a natural join where every input relation has two attributes. Our algorithm achieves a load of O[m / p^{1/rho}] where m is the total size of the input relations, p is the number of machines and rho is the fractional edge covering number of the join. The load matches a known lower bound up to a polylogarithmic factor. At the core of the proposed algorithm is a new theorem [which we name the isolated cartesian product theorem] that provides fresh insight into the mathematical structure of the problem. Our result implies that the subgraph enumeration problem, where the goal is to report all the occurrences of a constant-sized subgraph pattern, can be settled optimally [up to a polylogarithmic factor] in the MPC model. This research output contributes to the realization of Objectives 1 and 2. In J_1, we considered intersection joins. In that problem, we are given t sets R_1, ..., R_t of axis-parallel rectangles in d-dimensional space, where d ≥ 1 and t ≥ 2 are constants, and a join topology which is a connected undirected graph G on vertices 1, ..., t. The result consists of tuples [r_1, ..., r_t] in R_1 x ... x R_t where the intersection of r_i and r_j is not empty for all vertices i, j connected in G. A structure is feasible if it stores O[n] words, supports an update in O[1] amortized time, and can enumerate the join result with an O[1] delay [ignoring polylogarithmic factors], where n is the total input size. We provided a dichotomy as to when feasible structures exist. They do when t is 2 or d is 1. Subject to the OMv-conjecture, they do not exist when t at least 3 and d at least 2, regardless of the join topology. This research output contributes to the realization of Objectives 2 and 3. Selecting the best items in a dataset is a common task in data exploration. However, the concept of best lies in the eyes of the beholder - different users may consider different attributes more important and, hence, arrive at different rankings. Nevertheless, one can remove dominated items and create a representative subset of the data, comprising the best items in it. A Pareto-optimal representative is guaranteed to contain the best item of each possible ranking, but it can be a large portion of data. A much smaller representative can be found if we relax the requirement of including the best item for each user and, instead, just limit the user regret. Existing work defines regret as the loss in score by limiting consideration to the representative instead of the full dataset, for any chosen ranking function. However, the score is often not a meaningful number, and users may not understand its absolute value. Sometimes small ranges in score can include large fractions of the dataset. In contrast, users do understand the notion of rank ordering. In J_3, we consider item positions in the ranked list in defining the regret and propose the rank-regret representative as the minimal subset of the data containing at least one of the top-k of any possible ranking function. This problem is polynomial time solvable in 2D space but is NP-hard on 3 or more dimensions. We design a suite of algorithms to fulfill different purposes, such as whether relaxation is permitted on k, the result size, or both, whether a distribution is known, whether theoretical guarantees or practical efficiency is important, etc. Experiments on real datasets demonstrate that we can efficiently find small subsets with small rank-regrets. This research output contributes to the realization of Objectives 2 and 3.

14207820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207820.value: All findings from this project have been published in esteemed computer science venues, including JACM (Journal of the ACM), ACM TODS (ACM Transactions on Database Systems), JCSS (Journal of Computer and System Sciences), LMCS (Logical Methods in Computer Science), and the Proceedings of ICDT (the International Conference on Database Theory). Notably, JACM, recognized as the most prestigious journal in theoretical computer science, publishes only breakthrough results. Our collective research has advanced the field of massively parallel computation (MPC) by refining our understanding of algorithmic capabilities and limitations, particularly regarding join operations in distributed computing environments. Our work elucidates the intricate relationship between mathematical structures and algorithm efficiency, providing foundational insights that influence both theoretical and practical applications. The three most important discoveries of this project are: 1. Resolution of an Open Question in MPC We addressed whether all joins could be processed under MPC with an AGM-derived bound. Our findings include a definitive "no" through the construction of a delicate class of joins called boat joins. Conversely, we demonstrated that all acyclic queries could be processed with an AGM-derived load, thanks to the discovery of the canonical edge cover - a new mathematical structure for acyclic hypergraphs. 2. Optimal Algorithm for Binary Relation Joins We developed an algorithm to compute natural joins over binary relations within the MPC model. This algorithm operates within a constant number of rounds and achieves optimal load, adjusted by a polylogarithmic factor. Our approach, which hinges on the newly discovered isolated cartesian product theorem, resolves the classical problem of subgraph enumeration under MPC. 3. Feasible Structures for Intersection Joins We have settled critical questions regarding when feasible structures - those using linear space, supporting near-constant time insertions/deletions, and enabling near-constant delay in reporting join results - exist for intersection joins. Subject to the OMv-conjecture, we established that such structures are viable if there are only two relations to be joined or the dimensionality is 1.

14207820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207820.value: A natural (and promising) direction for future research is to study how to relax the feasibility requirements to support intersection joins under updates in the scenarios where feasible structures do not exist, namely, t ≥ 3 and d ≥ 2 (multidimensional multiway joins). An interesting question is: if the update time has to be near-constant amortized, what is the smallest delay (in join result reporting) achievable? An equally interesting question lies in the other extreme: if the delay has to be near-constant, what is the fastest amortized update time possible? Settling these questions would provide helpful hints towards resolving the ultimate puzzle: what is the precise tradeoff between the amortized update cost and the delay? We suspect that joins with different topology graphs G may exhibit various tradeoffs.

14207820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207820.value: In today's era of big data, massively parallel systems like Hadoop, Spark, Dremel, and Hive have become essential for handling vast amounts of data. These systems utilize hundreds or thousands of servers to perform computations concurrently. Traditional algorithms, designed for maximizing CPU efficiency, fall short in such environments where data shuffling and server-to-server communication pose the primary bottlenecks. This project focuses on optimizing multiway joins, a common yet computationally expensive database operation. Existing methods, which typically join two relations at a time, often produce large intermediate results that are inefficient and ultimately discarded. Our research has developed new algorithms that deviate from this conventional approach by minimizing intermediate results, offering strong performance guarantees, and demonstrating effectiveness with real-world data. Additionally, these multiway join algorithms have implications for various applications, including subgraph isomorphism, social network analysis, online analytical processing, entity matching, and matrix analysis in machine learning, showcasing their broad utility and impact on modern computing challenges.

14207920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207920.value: The detection of biomolecular species such as viruses, pathogens, antibodies, DNA, bacteria and pollutants with the highest specificity and sensitivity is fundamentally important for all branches of life sciences. Ultimately, we want a device that can sense and identify a single molecule in its natural state. Until now, fluorescence-labelling is a common approach to achieve bio-detection with molecular sensitivity. However, two major and persistent drawbacks – photo-bleaching of fluorescence tag and modification of intrinsic molecular properties – have driven researchers to explore alternative “label-free” techniques, in which the inert physical properties such as molecular vibrations and mass-loading are detected, for achieving single-molecule bio-detection. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), which detects dielectric loading of molecular adhesion/binding using localised evanescent optical energy density introduced by metallic nanostructures, has been identified as a promising approach. This project proposes to develop a fully solid-state SPR imaging instrument for label-free detection of multiple targets simultaneously. While SPR is inherently a real-time monitoring and label-free technique, the novel features of the proposed design include: (i) self-balanced differential polarization phase detection, afforded by the sharp phase jump across the SPR optical absorption dip and common-mode noise rejection, offering significant (~2 orders of magnitude) resolution improvement compared to conventional angular or intensity schemes; (ii) fast and user-programmable on-demand image scanning operation enabled by digital micromirror devices (DMD); (iii) pixel-by-pixel dual single-detector strategy to fully utilize photon-counting performance of photomultiplier tubes. As an enabling platform, the proposed high-performance label-free bio-detection scheme has many application possibilities in the fields of life sciences and healthcare including drug screening, biomolecular interaction kinetics, real-time monitoring of biological reactions, experimental verification of new biosensing schemes, investigation of photonic properties of nano- and meta-materials. Success of this project will remove a long-standing bottleneck of SPR bio-detection in relation to resolution limit. By detecting a panel of target molecules simultaneously with minimal sample preparation, the proposed instrument has immediate impact in high-throughput disease identification and monitoring of medical treatment. In addition, its unique capability of providing real-time quantitative data will also enable more accurate administering of drugs. By bring improvements in cost, speed and accuracy of disease detection and treatment, the proposed research will contribute towards the medical healthcare services in Hong Kong, which is a major social and economic sector of the region. 基於生物分子，如病毒、病原體、抗體、DNA、細菌和汙染物等的高特異性和敏感性檢測對於生命科學的發展至關重要。最終，壹種能夠感知和識別單個自然狀態分子的檢測設備是發展迫切需要的。到目前為止，作為基於分子敏感性的生物檢測常用手段，熒光標記的兩個重要缺陷，即熒光標記的光漂白效應和對分子特性的改變，促使研究人員探索可替代的“無標簽”型檢測技術。在這種技術中，單分子生物檢測是基於探測惰性物理特性，如分子振動和質量加載實現的。表面等離子體共振(SPR)作為壹種基於金屬納米結構引入的局部倏逝光能量密度來檢測分子黏附/結合的介電載荷的方法，已成為被廣泛認可的檢測手段。 本項目擬研制壹種全固態SPR成像儀器，用於同時無標簽檢測多個目標。基於SPR的實時監測和無標簽技術特征,此項目的優勢主要包括:(1) 與傳統的基於角度或強度檢測方案相比，自平衡差分偏振相位檢測技術通過SPR光學吸收傾角的急劇相位跳變和共模噪聲抑制，可以顯著提高檢測分辨率(約2個數量級);(2)數字微鏡設備(DMD)可提供快速及用戶可編程的按需圖像掃描操作;(3) 充分利用光電倍增管的光子計數性能實現了逐像素雙單探測器策略。 作為壹個可靠的平臺，其高性能無標簽生物檢測方案在生命科學和醫療保健領域有巨大的應用潛能，包括藥物篩選、生物分子相互作用動力學研究、生物分子反應的實時監測、新的生物傳感方案的實驗驗證、納米和超級材料的光子特性的研究。 該項目的成功將消除長期存在的限制SPR生物檢測率的瓶頸。通過以最少的樣品制備同時檢測壹組目標分子，該儀器可實現高通量疾病檢測和醫療監測。由於其獨特的實時監測能力，該設備將通過濃度量化實現更準確的給藥方案。通過改善成本，速度和準確性，我們可顯著提高疾病檢測和治療的速度和準確度，由此進壹步提升香港地區在社會和經濟領域極為重要的醫療保健服務。

14207920.label: Realisation of objectives
14207920.value: The primary goal of this project is to develop a 2-dimensional label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor platform based on the use of digital micromirror devices (DMD). To achieve very high sensor resolution, we propose to measure the phase parameter of the SPR effect. During the hardware implementation stage of the project, we decided to measure the SPR phase through detecting the Goos–Hänchen (GH) effect. The GH effect, which is observable by measuring the lateral shift between the s-polarised and p-polarised beams imposed by SPR reflection at the sensor surface under attenuated total-internal reflection (ATR) conditions, is directly proportional to the SPR phase shift. By adopting this approach, we bypassed the requirement of an interferometer, we also reduced the overall complexity of the optical setup and was able to achieve very high sensing resolution. In addition, we optimized the optical parameters of the sensing surface by depositing a thin layer of Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST) on a gold film. Because of our efforts in the implementation of GH shift detection platform and sensor layer optimisation, we successfully demonstrated a record-breaking maximum GH shift of 439.3μm. This level of GH shift resulted in biosensing resolution of small cytokine biomarkers (TNF-α and IL-6) with a lower detection limit of 1 × 10E−16M. Two journal papers were published directly from this work (Wang, et al (2021). Nano-Micro Letters, 13(1), and Zhu, et al (2024). Light, Science & Applications, 13(1), 2). We later further optimised the sensor surface by adding an atomically thin vanadium dioxide (VO2) layer, the maximum GH shift was further increased to 2.997 × 10E3μm, which corresponded to a refractive index sensitivity limit of 10E−10RIU. The work was reported in another journal publication (Youssef, et al. (2022). Biosensors, 12(10), 866). Regarding the delivery of a 2-dimensional SPR sensor arrays. We conducted a ray-tracing analysis of the optical beam interacting with the DMD pixels and showed that diffraction associated with pixel arrays has imposed significant optical power reduction in the system for SPR excitation. We subsequently opted for using a high power (50mW) 785nm single-frequency semiconductor laser source. The final system was 6 × 7 array of GH shift-based SPR sensor array. The experimental DNA sensing limit was in the order of 100nM. The relatively low sensor counts of 6 × 7 (instead of 50 x 50 as proposed) is primarily limited to the pixel count of the DMD module (Texas Instruments, DLP4500), which is 912 × 1140 pixels and the laser power. If there is sufficient funding available for the acquisition of multiple DMD modules with higher pixel counts, e.g. DLP911U, 4096 x 2176 pixels, and a higher power laser source, the issue of increasing the number of sensor sites should be readily resolvable. This project has achieved the most important step of performing simultaneous biosensing with 2-dimensional array of GH shift-based SPR sensors. To report this work, a manuscript is now under preparation (“Journal_publication_4” attached to this report). Results from this project has led to the award of a France-Hong Kong Joint Research Scheme (Project Reference: F-CUHK402/19), through which personnel involved in this project (PI’s from France and HK: Shuwne Zheng and Ho-Pui HO, Research Staff: Shaodi Zhu, Yuanyuan Wei, Flavien Beffara) have been given the opportunity make several research visiting and research trips between France and Hong Kong. In 2023, as a follow-up of this project, and ANR-RGC proposal (Reference: A-CUHK401/24) entitled “Photothermal plasmonics and IR absorption spectroscopy coupled with AI for the study of bio-species” has been selected by our university for full proposal submission. Apart from providing funding for a PhD student (Shaodi Zhu), who has published several journal papers with results generated from this project, one undergraduate student (Sik To CHAN) has been supported by this project for a summer internship at the project Co-I’s location in France. The trip has been very successful. Due to his contribution during that time, the student is co-author of one the publications generated from this project (Zhu, Chan, et al (2024). Light, Science & Applications, 13(1), 2). In addition to results that have direct relevance to this project, during the implementation stage of the SPR imaging scheme, a PhD candidate (Yuanyuan WEI) of the PI’s team conceived the idea of applying artificial intelligence (AI) for accurate colour analysis of fluorescent droplet-based microreactors. An AI tool with sufficient training will be able to perform rapid analysis of fluorescence emission from a 2-dimensional array of droplets simultaneously using imaging techniques. Indirectly this project has led to the publication of two journal papers on the AI image analysis concept (Wei, et al (2024). Small Methods, 8(3), 2301293 and Wei, et al (2024). Advanced Science (Accepted for publication)).

14207920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207920.value: 1) Measurement of quantitative SPR phase can be implemented by detecting the Goos–Hänchen (GH) shift, which corresponds to the latter positional separation between the s- and p-polarisation beams after the excitation of surface plasmons. 2) By adding an atomically thin layer of Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST) or vanadium dioxide (VO2) on the SPR-active gold sensing surface, it is possible to further enhance the SPR excitation characteristics, which lead to extremely large GH shifts. Our experimental results demonstrated a SPR sensing resolution of refractive index sensitivity limit of 10E−10RIU and target biomolecules in the 1 × 10E−16M regime. 3) A DMD-based 2-dimensional SPR senor array system with simultaneous monitoring of individual sensor outputs has been constructed. The system has been shown to be capable of detecting target DNA strands at 100nM levels. At present, the maximum array counts are 6 × 7 sensor sites. A linear 2-dimensional cascading of DMD modules, together with the use of a high-power laser source, will readily increase the 2-dimensional SPR sensor sites by many-fold.

14207920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207920.value: As mentioned in previous sections, the present single-DMD setup only provides 6 × 7 sensor sites. Through linear 2-dimensional cascading of multiple DMD modules, it is possible to increase the sensor counts by many-fold. Also, the team has started exploring the possibility of using AI to enhance the resolution limit as well as sampling time of the system. Based the results from ongoing collaboration between the French and Hong Kong sides, the team will continue to apply for further funding support for further exploitation of ultra-sensitive SPR sensors based on the detection of GH shifts. With the PhD student supported under this project (Shaodi ZHU) graduating in July 2025, the team is also exploring the possibility of commercialising our imaging SPR sensing technique based on GH shift detection and light processing with DMD.

14207920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207920.value: This project aims to develop a 2-dimensional label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor platform based on the use of digital micromirror devices (DMD). To achieve very high sensor resolution, we propose to measure the SPR phase shift, which also manifests itself through the Goos–Hänchen (GH) effect - the lateral shift between the s-polarised and p-polarised beams imposed by SPR reflection at the sensor surface under attenuated total-internal reflection (ATR) condition. This platform offers label-free detection of multiple target molecules in their unmodified state. Within this project, we have enhanced the resolution limit by adding an atomically thin layer of Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST) or vanadium dioxide (VO2) on the SPR-active gold sensing surface. The experimental sensing limit is in the 1 × 10E−16M regime for target protein molecules or 10E−10RIU for refractive index changes. This is among some of the best levels reported in the literature. Using an imaging device and light processing capability of DMD, we have achieved simultaneous sensing from 6 × 7 sensor sites. The long-term impact of this project is low-cost point-of-care rapid detection of biomolecules without the need of any sample treatment.

14208020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208020.value: Human speech contains a rich variety of paralinguistic information, of which a major part is related to the speaker's physical condition. Speech production and breathing are two closely coupled processes that present competing needs in using the same set of organs. During or after demanding physical exercises like running or biking, speaking becomes laborious and difficult due to the increase of respiratory rate. This makes the produced speech very different from that in the non-exercise state. The proposed research examines the influence of physical activity as manifested in the exerciser's speech and voice characteristics and aims to develop a speech based approach to objective assessment of physical competence and wellness. The research also investigates the use of voice features in classifying body constitution type of a person, which is an important concept in traditional Chinese medicine diagnoses. The first and most critical task is the construction of a multi-modal database that contains parallel recordings of speech and physiological measurement before, during and after vigorous exercises, as well as physical competence assessment and body constitution assessment results. Advanced signal processing algorithms and the latest machine learning models are applied to design, compute and evaluate a wide range of speech features that can be used to detect and quantify the effect of physical activity and to predict physical competence level and body constitution type. Specifically, a domain-adapted automatic speech recognition (ASR) system is developed to facilitate structural analysis of speech and purposeful extraction of acoustic, phonetic, prosodic and paralinguistic features. Features extracted from speech under different exercise intensity levels are used for the training of different classifier and regression models, in order to achieve speech-based estimation of physical activity intensity, prediction of physical competence and assessment of body constitution. The overarching goal of the research is to establish speech as a major component in objective assessment of health condition and physical wellness for general population. The project team comprises experienced researchers and practitioners with inter-disciplinary knowledge background in speech processing, machine learning, physical fitness, physical literacy, and traditional Chinese medicine. We seek for a funding of about HK$1,194,000 to support this project for 36 months. 語音信號包含著豐富的周邊語言學信息，其中很大部分跟說話人的身體狀況有關。說話與呼吸是兩個緊密耦合的過程，需要使用同一組器官。我們參與體育鍛鍊的時候，呼吸率會上升，說話變得比較吃力和困難，這種情況下發出的語音與非運動狀態下的語音有不同的特徵。本項研究主要關注體能運動如何影響運動者的語音，藉此探討一種基於語音的運動能力及身體狀況的客觀評估方法。我們也會研究通過分析運動中或靜止狀態下的語音，判別說話人的中醫體質種類。本研究的重點之一是建立一個大型數據庫，包括數百名測試者運動前，運動過程中，運動後的語音音頻和生理數據，以及對應的運動能力和中醫體質標準測試數據。我們將運用最新最前沿的信號處理算法和機器學習模型，計算和測試多種語音特徵在（1）偵測身體活動強度；（2）預測運動能力；和（3）判別中醫體質這三個方面的功能。我們將開發一個語音識別系統，用它來幫助從自然語音中分析和提取聲學，語音，韻律及周邊語言學等方面的特徵。從不同運動狀態時的語音中提取出來的特徵會用來訓練各種分類模型和回歸模型，以實現估計活動強度，評估體能水平和判別中醫體質的任務。項目的最終目標是把語音作為評估健康狀況和身體狀態的一種客觀依據。項目團隊由來自語音處理，機器學習，體育科學，中醫學等多個領域的專家組成。項目實施期為36個月，申請經費港幣約一百一十九萬四千元，獲批經費約六十萬元。
