14208620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208620.value: The proposed research project aims to develop a functional expansion based approach to deriving approximations to the transition densities of multivariate continuous-time jump-diffusion processes. This broad class of processes are widely used in finance and economics to capture the aggregate effect of the complex interactions between different but correlated risk factors on the evolution of market variables. However, except a handful of trivial single-dimensional models, most of them are analytically intractable. That poses a substantial research challenge for us, when we attempt to apply them to extract information from the trading data of both underlying assets and derivatives in order to develop more managerial insights for investment and risk management decision making. The transition probability density proves to be the key object in numerous applications related to multivariate continuous-time jump-diffusion processes. First, it is an essential input for the method of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) that can yield the most efficient consistent estimators based on discretely observed market data. Second, it can be used to construct computable explicit approximates to option prices. The analytical forms of such pricing formula will enable us to assess the first-order contributions of different modelling components, providing valuable references for model selection. Third, we may utilize it to introduce a constrained MLE formulation to carry out statistical analysis on the sets combining underlying asset price time-series data and cross-sectional option data to produce more accurate and timely estimation. Some preliminary investigations led by the PI show that the new approach demonstrates a great potential in leading us to obtain accurate analytical density approximations for a very broad class of jump-diffusion models in a computationally efficient manner. The outcomes from the projects will yield long-term impacts on both the academic research and financial practices about financial data analysis. 本研究項目旨在構建一種基於函數展開的方法，用於推導連續時間的多元跳躍擴散過程的轉移概率密度函數的近似表達式。連續時間的多元跳躍擴散過程廣泛使用於經濟和金融學，用以刻畫相互關聯的不同風險因子之間的相互作用如何影響市場變量的演化。然而，除去一小部分極為退化的模型而外，絕大多數這樣的過程並不顯式可解。當我們想利用它們對衍生產品及其標的物的交易價格建模，並試圖從中提取出有用的信息以指導投資或者風險管理的決策時，這種不可解性往往會帶來極大的挑戰。 多元跳躍擴散過程的轉移概率密度函數在各種應用場景下都扮演重要角色。比如，它是極大似然估計的重要輸入量，可以用來構建基於離散觀察數據的最有效估計。又如，可以用它來推導期權價格的顯式近似，使我們能夠直觀地評估模型各組分在定價時的貢獻，從而為模型選擇提供依據。另外，我們也可以利用轉移概率密度函數構建帶約束的極大似然估計，結合標的物的時間序列數據和衍生品的面板數據得出更加準確及時的統計估計。 該項目的一些初步的研究成果表明，新方法在針對一類極其廣泛的跳躍擴散過程的密度函數展開方面具有很高的計算效率。項目成果將會對金融數據分析的科研和實踐都產生長期和深遠的影響。

14208620.label: Realisation of objectives
14208620.value: The Principal Investigator (PI) has successfully achieved the first objective of this project. In this context, the PI and their research team (mainly two former PhD students, Xiangwei Wan and Nian Yang) developed an innovative Ito-Taylor expansion-based approach to derive explicit approximations for the transition probability densities of a general multivariate jump-diffusion process. Compared to existing literature, this new approach offers several advantages: 1. It introduces a quasi-Lamperti transform that involves the process diffusion matrix at the initial time, which significantly simplifies the convergence analysis. 2. It can yield closed form expressions for conditional expectations of a general function applied to the process. This generality allows for various applications. For instance, selecting that function to be a Dirac function yields approximate transition probability densities for the process, which are essential inputs for performing the maximum likelihood inference; using ReLU functions as that function results in approximate option prices under the process. 3. Our approach accommodates time-varying jump risks. Empirical studies highlight the importance of incorporating time-varying jump intensities and sizes in standard equilibrium-based asset pricing models to explain market data abnormalities. Currently, no general option pricing formulas exist in the literature, and researchers often rely on simulations, which can be inaccurate and time-consuming. Our approach addresses this gap in the literature. 4. We established a convergence guarantee that provides insights into how to control the approximation errors associated with our expansion. Additionally, as a theoretical contribution to the statistics of stochastic processes, our research reveals a fundamental equivalence between two major density expansion methods in the literature: the pathwise density expansion proposed by Li (2013) and the Hermite polynomials-based density expansion introduced by Yang, Chen, and Wan (2019). Furthermore, the asymptotic analysis tools employed in developing our convergence guarantee have significantly inspired the PI's related research (with the PI's coauthos, Xiang Ma, Yanchu Liu, and Wei Yu) in stochastic dynamic programming, particularly regarding the error analysis of the dual dynamic programming method. The research conducted by the PI and his PhD student (Chengli Ren) has successfully fulfilled the second and third objectives of the project. As mentioned previously, the Ito-Taylor expansion-based approach serves as a foundation for developing a new method for option pricing under general jump-diffusion models. By incorporating time-varying jump risks for both jump sizes and intensities, our method produces accurate closed-form formulas for a variety of jump-diffusion processes, including multivariate processes with jump risks affecting both underlying asset prices and volatilities as well as processes characterized by nonlinear and time-inhomogeneous structures. These models encompass numerous important examples that are widely utilized in market practice. In addition to the computational advantages provided by the closed-form pricing formulas, our research reveals how specific model features influence option prices. For instance, the choice of volatility function significantly impacts the slope of implied volatility curves derived from option price data; the selection of jump risk components can lead to high-order effects on the dynamics of the implied volatility surface. These insights contribute new knowledge to the literature, thereby achieving the second objective of the project. The pricing formula developed in the second objective lays a solid foundation for PI to achieve the third objective. Utilizing this formula, the PI and his PhD student (Chengli Ren) formulated a recovery theorem that connects the characteristics of implied volatility surfaces to the modeling parameters of jump-diffusion models. By integrating local polynomial kernel regression techniques from non-parametric statistics, we established a systematic approach to estimate the drift, volatility, and jump components of a jump-diffusion model based on option market price data. Numerical experiments demonstrated that this method yields highly accurate predictions for option prices. During this process, the PI discovered that simultaneous jumps—where multiple asset prices and their volatilities experience significant dislocations in a short time frame—have a considerable impact on the prediction accuracy of the method, particularly for short-term options. Consequently, he conducted a series of investigations with his co-authors on financial systemic risk to deepen the understanding of this critical factor contributing to simultaneous jump risks. Two main results emerged from this research: 1. The PI and his co-authors (Dohyun Ahn and Kyoung-Kuk Kim) proposed a robust optimization approach to determine the worst-case probabilities of simultaneous defaults in an interconnected banking network, along with an associated estimation of losses stemming from this financial systemic risk. This result has practical applications in banking regulation. Using this tool, we analyzed the effects of various incomplete network information structures on these worst-case quantities and provided regulatory insights on how to collect network information and establish capital adequacy requirements for systematically important financial institutions (SIFIs). 2. The second result focuses on liquidity-related systemic risk. The PI and his co-authors (Cong Sui and Mo Yang) introduced a novel framework to analyze how fire sales can trigger and exacerbate a market crash, establishing a market-level measure of fire sale amounts from various financial institutions and their contributions to stock price declines. The outcomes provide regulatory insights into the causes of the 2015–16 Chinese stock market turbulence. With these results, the PI has successfully fulfilled the third objective set for the project.

14208620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208620.value: 1. Related to Objective 1, the PI published one paper (cf. no 1. Item 8, Part C) in Operations Research, the flagship journal of the field. In that paper, we develop a duality-driven iterative approach (DDP) to obtain and improve confidence interval estimates for the true value of finite-horizon stochastic dynamic programming problems. We also introduce a regression-based Monte Carlo algorithm for implementing DDP and establish its convergence rates. The PI also has submitted one paper (cf. no 4. Item 8, Part C) to Journal of Applied Probability. We just finished the first round of major revision and sent it back to the journal. The paper derives explicit pathwise expansions for the conditional expectation of a general function applied to multivariate diffusion processes. Our approach can find wide applications in maximum likelihood estimations, option pricing, and risk management practices. It has a high chance to be accepted according to the editor’s comments. 2. Related to Objective 2, the PI supervised one PhD student, Dr. Chengli Ren, to finish his PhD thesis on the Ito-Taylor expansion-based approach for approximations to the density of a multivariate jump diffusion process with state-dependent, time-varying drift, volatility, and jump components. For ease of reference, the PI attached the entire thesis with this completion report (cf. no 1. Item 10, Part C). Chapter 3 is related to this topic. The PI has been working on revising this chapter into a paper and is about to submit it to a leading FE/Financial Econometrics/Statistics journal. The resulting expansion are highly computable. We also establish the convergence of the expansions to the true probability densities of processes. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach under a wide spectrum of models with important financial applications in option pricing and jump risk prediction. 3. Related to Objective 3, the PI published two papers on financial systemic risk. The first paper (cf. no 2. Item 8, Part C) appeared in Operations Research. It focuses on robust risk quantification for network-caused systemic risk. The other paper (cf. no 3. Item 8, Part C) was published in Pacific-Basin Financial Journal, an outlet for high quality empirical investigation on capital markets in Pacific Asia. This paper explores liquidity-caused systemic risk. 4. The grant also provided financial supports to 3 more PhD students to finish their PhD thesis. The research included reinforcement learning, optimal investment strategies, and adversarial learning.

14208920.label: Project Objectives
14208920.value: To develop an efficient coupling matrix reconfiguration method for a coupled resonator filter of an arbitrary filter coupling topology. The verification of the developed algorithm can be firstly conducted on filters with regular coupling topologies whose analytic solutions are known. With the predetermined target (golden) coupling matrix, the reconfigured coupling matrix can provide a clear direction to tune the filter to the desired response. Based on the reconfiguration algorithm developed, a certified homotopy continuation algorithm will be further developed to rigorously warrant that the observed solution doesn’t deviate to other solutions. The verification of the developed algorithms will be tested through the computer aided tuning (CAT) and Automatic Robot Tuning (RAT) platform built in PI’s research group on various practical filters, particularly the filter modules for 5G applications.

14208920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208920.value: Microwave filters are among the most critical components in terrestrial and space communication systems. Filters suppress the interference among the different communication systems. Due to stringent electrical specifications, tuning of the screws on the top lid of a filter device is inevitable, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, developing a computer-aided tuning (CAT) platform for guiding human tuning or enabling automatic robotic tuning (RAT) would be a fundamental cornerstone. Two major challenges encountered in manufacturing of high quality filters are (1) slow tuning process for higher-order filters with irregular coupling topologies; and (2) poor yield in tuning dielectric monoblock filters since tuning of such a filter relies on scratching the silver-plated surface, and is a noninvertible process. The key issue in CAT and RAT is to extract the filter circuit model represented by the coupling matrix for the filter response at a tuning stage. Such extraction theory for the microwave filters with regular coupling topologies has been mature enough. But for most of practical filters, whose coupling topologies are likely to be irregular, there is no theory for effectively conducting coupling matrix reconfiguration. This theoretical gap prevents people from tuning filters using an advanced computer-aided means. The objective of this proposed research is to develop an efficient numerical reconfiguration method that can systematically convert the filtering function of a filter with an irregular coupling topology, which is extracted from the measured response, to the circuit model that matches the filter physical realization without being trapped in other unwanted solutions. The proposed method will be based on homotopy continuation algorithm, which has been known and applied to many engineering problems. The basic concept of the homotopy continuation method is to track the change of the solution to the unknowns with reference to a start solution. In CAT, the target golden coupling matrix will serve as a good start system. The method will iteratively convert the coupling matrix from a known canonical form, e.g. folded form, which can be easily obtained from the identified filtering function, to the coupling matrix in the desired coupling topology. The develop algorithm will possess the following attributes: 1) To be generic to any irregular coupling topology; 2) To be comprehensive to a wide range of filter physical realization; 3) To be efficient for practical automatic tuning process; and 4) To be scalable to high order filters and to be extendable to other filtering networks. 微波濾波器是地面和空間通信系統中最關鍵的組件之一。濾波器可以抑制不同通信系統之間的干擾。由於嚴格的電氣規範，在製作過程中，其性能是通過調整頂蓋上的多個調諧螺釘來完成的，這既費時又費力。因此，開髮用於指導人工的計算機輔助調試（CAT）或啟用自動化機器人調試（RAT）的平台將是這個產業的基石。製造高質量濾波器時遇到的兩個主要挑戰是：（1）具有不規則耦合拓撲的高階濾波器的緩慢調試過程；（2）在調試單體介質濾波器時良品率低，因為這種濾波器的調試依賴於劃傷鍍銀表面，並且是不可逆的過程。 CAT和RAT中的關鍵問題是在調試階段提取由耦合矩陣表示的濾波器電路模型以實現濾波器的目標響應。對於具有規則耦合拓撲的微波濾波器來說，這種提取理論已經足夠成熟。但是對於大多數實際的濾波器，其耦合拓撲可能是不規則的，目前沒有理論可以有效地進行耦合矩陣重構。這種理論上的差距使人們無法使用先進的計算機輔助手段來調試濾波器。 這項擬議研究的目的是開發一種有效的數值矩陣重構方法，該方法可以系統地將具有不規則耦合拓撲的濾波器的濾波函數轉換為與濾波器的物理實現相匹配的電路模型，而該濾波函數是從測量的響應中提取的。 所提出的方法將基於已應用於許多工程問題的同倫延拓算法。同倫延拓方法的基本概念是用一已知的參考起始解來追踪求解一組未知參數的狀態。在CAT中，目標耦合矩陣可作為一個良好的初始系統。該方法迭代地將耦合矩陣從已知的規範形式（例如，折疊矩陣形式）轉換到一給定不規則耦合拓撲形式。而折疊形式可以很容易地從濾波函數中獲得。所研究的算法將具有以下屬性： 1）適用於任何不規則耦合拓撲； 2）可廣泛應用於各類濾波器的物理實現； 3）可高效地 運用在實際的自動調整過程；及 4）可擴展至高階濾波器及其他濾波網絡中。

14208920.label: Realisation of objectives
14208920.value: Object 1 is accomplished by developing a general numerical algorithm for coupling matrix reconfiguration of arbitrary coupling topology based on the continuation process with a coefficient-parameter homotopy. To provide a physical sensible starting solution for the continuation process, a direct preconditioner that can be physics based and easily obtained by reconfiguring the regular coupling topology is applied. With the preconditioner, the continuation method can be effectively used for filter synthesis and model extraction of bandpass filters with irregular couplings. The details of this work is published on paper "A direct preconditioner for coupling matrix reconfiguration of bandpass filters with irregular couplings using continuation method," (Yan Zhang; K.-L. Wu; and Fabien Seyfert, IEEE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., Vol.69, No.2, pp.1394-1403, 2021.) The shortcomings of this approach include its ability to deal with multiple solutions and the lack of physical insight to the solution. To tackle the problem defined in object 2, which is the ultimate way to solve the multiple solution problem, we proposed a rigorous framework for exhaustive search of not only all viable coupling topologies but also all their real coupling matrices for a given filtering function, the most general description of a coupled resonator network. The proposition that provides sufficient and necessary condition for a viable coupling topology with finite real coupling matrices is proposed. The uniqueness of the folded coupling topology is proved for establishing the equations for a numerical solution. This work is published in paper "Exhaustive Synthesis Framework of Coupled Resonator Microwave Bandpass Filters," (Junyi Liu and K.-L. Wu, IEEE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., Vol.71, No.10, pp.4483-4493, 2023.) Object 3 is addressed by developing an analytical solution for a specific irregular coupling topology a dispersive box topology, which also reflects the dispersion in a physical coupling structures. The comprehensive theory for synthesis and model extraction of a dispersive box coupling section is presented and applied to the design of high- Q monoblock dielectric resonator (MDR) filters. In this work, instead of using numerical methods, the analytic transformation for converting a box section with diagonal cross coupling to a dispersive box is found to validate the numerical approaches. A practical eight-pole MDR filter with an asymmetric response is designed and prototyped using the CAT model extraction theory, showing excellent filtering performance. The work is published in the paper "Dispersive box section and its applications to quasi-TEM mode monoblock dielectric filters," (Yan Zhang; F. Seyfert, K.-L. Wu, IEEE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., Vol.71, No.3, pp.1136-1147, 2023.)

rows: To develop an efficient coupling matrix reconfiguration method for a coupled resonator filter of an arbitrary filter coupling topology. The verification of the developed algorithm can be firstly conducted on filters with regular coupling topologies whose analytic solutions are known. With the predetermined target (golden) coupling matrix, the reconfigured coupling matrix can provide a clear direction to tune the filter to the desired response.

14208920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208920.value: In this research, three aspects regarding to the model extraction of a microwave bandpass filter with an irregular coupling topology are studied, which lead to three significant research outcomes. (1) A general numerical algorithm for coupling matrix reconfiguration of arbitrary coupling topology is developed based on the continuation process with a coefficient-parameter homotopy. To provide a physical sensible starting solution for the continuation process, a direct preconditioner that can be physics based and easily obtained by reconfiguring the regular coupling topology is applied. With the preconditioner, the continuation method can be effectively used for filter synthesis and model extraction of bandpass filters with irregular couplings. The shortcomings of this approach include its ability to deal with multiple solutions and the lack of physical insight to the solution. (2) Irregular coupling topology is also a reflection of the dispersion of physical coupling structures. Dispersion effect can be parasitic and inevitable. On the other hand, it can be used to create more transmission zeros (TZs). A good practice is the dispersive “box” topology. To this end, the comprehensive theory for synthesis and model extraction of a dispersive box coupling section is presented and applied to the design of high- Q monoblock dielectric resonator (MDR) filters. Compared to traditional coupling sections, the dispersive box section provides high flexibility in controlling TZs, a wide spurious free rejection band, simplicity in physical realization, and higher unloaded Qs. Instead of using numerical methods, the analytic transformation for converting a box section with diagonal cross coupling to a dispersive box is found to facilitate the direct model extraction. A practical eight-pole MDR filter with an asymmetric response is designed and prototyped using the model extraction theory, showing excellent filtering performance. (3) To ultimately solve the multiple solution problem, more follow-up works in the subject of the original project continue. One representative work is the rigorous framework for exhaustive search of not only all viable coupling topologies but also all their real coupling matrices for a given filtering function, which is the most general description of a coupled resonator network. The proposition that provides sufficient and necessary condition for a viable coupling topology with finite real coupling matrices is proposed. The uniqueness of the folded coupling topology is proved for establishing the equations for a numerical solution. This work provides the industry with the most powerful tool to model extraction synthesis of coupled resonator filtering networks.

14209020.label: Project Objectives
14209020.value: For complicated and cluttered environments, the first objective of the proposed research is to generate the motion primitives through dynamic programming and a polynomial based trajectory generation approach. The key idea is to produce a set of motion primitives that satisfy all the boundary, state, and input constraints of the physical system (such as input saturation level and the constraints on velocity and acceleration). For the primitives generated in the step above, we next design an appropriate neural network (using a deep learning approach if necessary) as a function approximator to estimate the mapping relation between the boundary conditions and the resulting trajectory. It is noted that in our approach, it is possible to map the entire trajectory to the selected end boundary conditions with satisfied constraints. Through the approach in the second objective, it might become difficult to find the derivative from the cost function to the boundary conditions due to the introduction of the neural network. To overcome such a problem, our third objective is to adopt a derivative-free optimization method called the particle swarm optimization to optimize a model predictive control (MPC) problem. Once the trajectory reference profile is generated in the previous objectives, our next objective is to adopt the robust and perfect tracking (RPT) control framework to control the actual unmanned vehicle. The RPT control technique is capable of tracking the position, velocity and acceleration references perfectly and robustly in face of external disturbance and uncertainties. Even though the RPT control has been proven to be efficient and effective in many control applications, to show the advantages of adopting the RPT control in the proposed unmanned systems, we will implement and demonstrate the control strategy with physical UAV platforms housed at CUHK. Lastly, the above overall navigation and flight control framework are to be implemented and tested through some real applications, such as bridge and tunnel inspections. To link our research with the currently funded Hong Kong Centre for Logistics Robotics by Innovation and Technology Commission - InnoHK, we will definitely adopt the proposed solutions to tackle the problems initiated by the Centre.

14209020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209020.value: In recent years, research and development of autonomous unmanned systems have gained much attention in academic and industrial communities worldwide. Topics such as unmanned aircraft, underwater explorers, satellites, and intelligent robotics are widely investigated as they have potential applications in many domains. An autonomous unmanned vehicle is a mechanical machine equipped with necessary data processing units, sensors, automatic control, and communications systems, and can perform autonomous missions without the interference of a human operator. It is much more challenging to carry out autonomous missions intelligently in complicated environments, especially in GPS-denied or cluttered environments. It is observed that autonomous systems, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), with the integration of intelligent elements and functions, are set to play significant roles in real life applications and generate remarkable long term impact to human societies. In order to make an unmanned system fully autonomous and intelligent, we to fully understand the dynamical model of the unmanned hardware platform and integrate some key components in the overall unmanned system framework, including the systems for mission and task management (to manage application tasks), motion planning (to generate feasible motion paths), sensing and positioning (to detect and sense the surrounding environment), and automatic control (to control and guide the unmanned vehicles). In this research project, we propose to study and investigate a robust and sophisticated flight control system framework with intelligent motion planning techniques using model predictive control (MPC) and a robust and perfect tracking (RPT) control method for unmanned aerial vehicles. The MPC-based motion planning is incorporated with an appropriate neural network and a derivative-free optimization to generate optimal paths and trajectory references for UAVs. This allows the UAV to be operated in real and complex environments. The RPT control is used to perfectly and robustly track the resulting reference, and yield good flight performance. The proposed research, once realized, is expected to play an instrumental role for unmanned aerial systems in numerous industrial applications, such as reconnaissance for search and rescue, environment monitoring, security surveillance, powerline and pipeline inspection, and geographical mapping. More importantly, the proposed system can be easily adopted for UAVs to carry out fully autonomous flight missions in GPS-denied environments, such as for tunnel inspection, under-bridge inspection, warehouse management, logistic checking and goods delivery. The proposed system can also be easily adopted for other types of unmanned systems. 近年來，自主無人系統的研究與開發在全世界的學術界和工業界引起了廣泛關註。無人飛機，水下探險器，衛星和智能機器人技術在許多領域都有潛在的應用。自主無人系統是一種配備了必要數據處理器，傳感器，自動控制和通訊系統的機械設備單元，並可執行自主操作而無需人工幹預，可在覆雜的環境中（尤其是在GPS受限或混亂的環境中）執行任務。據觀察，自主系統，例如無人機（UAV），無人車（UGV），無人船（USV）和水下無人艇（UUV）等，將在實際應用中發揮重要的作用，並對人類社會產生深遠的影響。 為了使無人系統完全自治和智能，我們要了解無人系統硬件平台的動力學模型並進行集成整個無人系統框架中的一些關鍵模塊如任務管理（用於管理和分配任務），運動計劃（用於生成可行的運動路徑），感應和定位（以檢測和感應周圍環境）和自動控制（以控制和引導無人系統硬件平台）。 在此研究項目中，我們將使用智能運動計劃技術來研究和搭建高效的飛行控制系統框架，其中包括模型預測控制（MPC）和魯棒和完美跟蹤（RPT）控制方法。 基於MPC的運動計劃與適當的神經網絡以及無導數優化方法生成最佳的無人機參考路徑和軌跡，使無人系統可以在實際覆雜的環境中，得到魯棒和完美跟蹤（RPT）控制和跟蹤，並產生良好的飛行性能。 擬議的研究項目一旦實現，預計將發揮無人機在許多工業的應用，例如偵察，搜索和救援，環境監控，安全監控，電力線和管道檢查和地理制圖。 更重要的是，開發的系統可以很容易地被用在無GPS環境中執行完全自主的飛行任務，例如隧道檢查，橋下檢查，倉庫管理，後勤檢查和貨物交付等。

14209020.label: Realisation of objectives
14209020.value: The project successfully developed a robust and sophisticated flight control system for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), integrating intelligent motion planning and control techniques. The key objectives, such as generating motion primitives that satisfy system constraints, designing neural networks to map boundary conditions to trajectories, employing derivative-free optimization methods to refine control models, and implementing a resilient tracking control framework (RPT), were achieved, resulting in a system capable of precise and reliable flight performance. The developed system was demonstrated and tested on physical UAV platforms, showcasing its effectiveness in various real-world scenarios, including inspections and monitoring. This work significantly advanced autonomous UAV capabilities in complex environments. Generation of Motion Primitives for Complex Environments: The project successfully created motion primitives, fundamental movement patterns, using dynamic programming combined with polynomial-based trajectory generation. These primitives satisfied all system constraints, such as input saturation, velocity, and acceleration limits, ensuring they were physically feasible for execution in cluttered or challenging environments. Design of Neural Networks for Trajectory Mapping: Neural networks (including deep learning models) were developed to approximate the relationship between boundary conditions (initial and final states) and resulting trajectories. This enabled the system to efficiently map feasible trajectories to specific boundary conditions, providing flexible and adaptive motion planning capable of accommodating varying environmental and mission requirements. Optimization Using Derivative-Free Methods: To address the challenges of derivative calculation with neural networks, the project adopted derivative-free optimization techniques, specifically, particle swarm optimization, to refine the model predictive control (MPC) framework. This approach ensured that trajectories were optimized effectively despite the complexities introduced by neural network approximations. Implementation of Robust and Precise Tracking Control: Following trajectory generation, a Robust and Perfect Tracking (RPT) control framework was implemented, enabling accurate following of planned trajectories. RPT proved capable of robustly tracking position, velocity, and acceleration references even in the presence of external disturbances and uncertainties, ensuring stable and precise flight performance. Practical Demonstration on Physical UAV Platforms: The control strategies were validated through implementation and demonstration on CUHK’s physical UAV platforms. These tests confirmed the system’s real-world applicability, performance, and robustness. Application Testing in Real-World Scenarios: The entire navigation and control system was tested in practical scenarios such as bridge and tunnel inspections. These applications demonstrated the system’s operational effectiveness in complex, real-world environments. Moreover, the solutions developed were aligned with the Hong Kong Centre for Logistics Robotics, addressing challenges in logistics and infrastructure inspections, thereby bridging academic research and industry needs. Overall Impact: This project resulted in an integrated, intelligent UAV navigation and flight control system capable of reliable operation in complex environments. The system demonstrated adaptability to real-world conditions and has potential applications across various industrial fields, including rescue missions, environmental monitoring, and infrastructure inspection. The project successfully resulted in the publication of 13 journal papers and 11 conference papers. Additionally, three PhD students were trained as part of this research effort.

14209120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209120.value: Modern wireless communication systems often utilize complex modulation techniques (such as OFDM or QAM) for multi-media applications that require high data-rate and channel capacity. However, these requirements will lead to signal waveform with high Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR). In practice, the power stage of the RF transmitter has to operate at the highest output power level but without severe distortion (e.g. voltage clipping). Unfortunately, conventional linear PA (e.g. class A & B) operated deeply in their back-off region (to avoid distortion) will suffer from low power efficiency. In recent years, the Doherty power amplifier (DPA) architecture has been widely deployed by mobile communication industry due to its relatively simple structure and excellent power efficiency over a wide dynamic range. However, the basic Doherty amplifier is known to have poor linearity performance due to the adoption of the nonlinear amplifiers (e.g. class C). On the other hand, modern digital communication systems demand linear amplification to minimize undesirable out-of-band emission that may violate the FCC specification. Digital pre-distortion (DPD) methods, when used in conjunction with a DPA, can provide good linearity with the major drawbacks of additional power consumption and cost. In this project, we aim to develop advanced linearization techniques for the design and realization of Doherty power amplifier with both enhanced power efficiency and linearity performance. The proposed methods are based on a self-linearizing principle to compensate for AM/AM and AM/PM distortions. The key findings thus obtained will eventually lead to the development of RF transmitters that can offer a high performance, compact and cost effective solution. This research work is essential to existing 4G-LTE and emerging 5G markets and will have a significant impact on the design of future micro-base-stations and mobile terminals.

14209120.label: Realisation of objectives
14209120.value: All objectives have been successfully realized. Objective 1 & 3 (4 implemented tasks): 1. A new design methodology of symmetrical DPA has been proposed which features compact size, simple layout, wide OBO range, and high back-off power efficiency. It takes into consideration the effect of drain parasitic and the suppressed peak current of class-C amplifier (due to reduced conduction angle). For verification, a symmetrical DPA with OBO of 10 dB and output power of 42 dBm was designed, fabricated and measured. GaN HEMTs (CGH40006S) were used as the active devices with drain bias of 28V, main gate bias of -3.1 V (quiescent drain current of 15 mA) and auxiliary gate bias of -7.5 V. Over the operating frequency from 1.85 to 2.15 GHz, the measured DE were found to be 70-77% at saturation and 50-57 % at 10 dB back-off. By using a 20-MHz 256-QAM LTE signal (PAPR of 9.64 dB), the DPA was measured to exhibit an average drain efficiency of over 52 % and adjacent channel leakage power ratio (ACLR) of ~ -28dBc at an average output power of 32 dBm. 2. In this work, a new analytical method has been developed for the study of two-tone intermodulation distortion behavior of class-C amplifier (building block of DPA). Based on the proposed simple current profile and waveform sampling theory, closed-form expressions for IMD evaluation are derived. For further study, GaN transistor CGH40006S and its device model (provided by Foundry) are adopted, with gate voltage of -3.65V (class-C), pinch-off voltage of -3.0V, maximum gate-source voltage of 1.5V, a drain bias of 28V and a fundamental drain load of 40 Ohm (intrinsic current plane). The power performance of the fundamental, IMD3 and IMD5 frequency components were simulated by using two-tone signal (with center frequency of 2 GHz and tone spacing of 10 MHz). Close correlation between the theoretical and simulated behaviors was observed. For validation, an experimental class-C PA was designed, fabricated and characterized. The measured results reveals that the power levels of the fundamental, IMD3 and IMD5 frequency components agree favorably with the calculated values. 3. A novel peak-current-ratio enhanced symmetrical DPA architecture has been developed featuring large OBO range, compact size, and simple layout. Based on the principle of active harmonic control (AHC), the load modulation depth (and hence the saturation power) of the DPA is enhanced, leading to ideal class-B/-B case, which can deliver 25% more saturation power than conventional class-B/-C design. Moreover, the realization of AHC can simply be attained by the combining load network and therefore conventional harmonic injection circuits are no longer needed. A simple and compact combiner structure has been developed with explicit closed-form design equations. The experimental DPA exhibits remarkable power performance with OBO range of 11 dB and PUF of 1.25. The main device is biased in deep class-AB (gate voltage of −3 V) with quiescent current of 15 mA. The auxiliary device is biased in class-C with gate voltage of −7.5 V. Both drain biases are set equal to 28 V. Under continuous wave excitation (2 GHz), peak power of around 43.0 dBm, DE of 74% at saturation, and DE of 52% at 11-dB back-off were observed. Under 20 MHz LTE signal excitation (PAPR = 11 dB), an adjacent channel leakage power ratio (ACLR) of −28dBc at an average power of 32 dBm and average efficiency of 53.2% was attained. Compared with the state-of-the-art symmetrical DPA designs, the proposed work features simplified circuitry, compact size, extended OBO range, high efficiency, boosted output power, and lifted PUF. 4. In this task, the nonlinearity generation mechanism in DPA designs (due the voltage clipping effect) has been thoroughly investigated. Unlike most traditional studies, the non-ideal current profile of the auxiliary device (due to drive-dependent conduction angle under class-C operation) is exploited and its harmful impact on Doherty operation is revealed. Theoretical analyses show that insufficient load modulation can appear inside the Doherty region, thus leading to undesirable voltage clipping and distortion in conventional DPA designs. To circumvent the above issue, a modified design is proposed to offer substantial linearity enhancement with minimal reduction in power efficiency. To verify the proposed theory, two prototypes, DPA-I (conventional) and DPA-II (new), with operating frequency of 2 GHz, targeted saturation power of 42 dBm and OBO range of 6 dB were implemented. The main device was biased in deep class-AB with quiescent current of 36 mA. Under continuous-wave excitation (2 GHz), DPA-II (DPA-I) achieves a saturation power of 42.3 dBm (42.4 dBm) with efficiency of 71.5% (73%). At 6-dB power back-off (36 dBm), DPA-II offers slightly lower efficiency of 54% than DPA-I (56.5%). Under 5-MHz WCDMA (PAPR of 7.3 dB) signal excitation, the measured ACLR (inside the Doherty region) was largely improved from -32dBc (DPA-I) to -40dBc (DPA-II), at an average output power of about 35 dBm, and average DE of approximately 50%. Objective 2 & 3 (2 implemented tasks): 1. A mode-extended non-Z0 pseudo-Doherty LMBA (N-PD-LMBA) has been proposed for enhanced efficiency profile and output power (i.e., improved load modulation and PUF). For verification, a N-PD-LMBA with 12dB OBO and 40% fractional bandwidth was designed and fabricated. This PA was implemented using commercial substrate RO4003C (with thickness of 0.813 mm and dielectric constant of 3.55) and GaN transistors (CGH40006S and CGH40010F from CREE). Under CW signal excitation (1.6-2.4 GHz), the fabricated circuit achieves a DE of 58.2%-70% @saturation, 46.6-59% @6dB OBO, 48-63%@12dB OBO, with saturation power of 42.8-44.1 dBm and PUF of 0.73-1.0. When modulated input (20 MHz LTE) was applied, the prototype offers an average DE of 47.8-56.9%, at average output power of 32.6-33.9 dBm, and ACLR of around -25dBc. Compared to prior designs, the proposed N-PD-LMBA features wide bandwidth, enhanced drain efficiency and PUF. 2. A novel three-stage LMBA has been developed using asymmetric coupling and non-Z0 matched load. Closed-form design equations are derived. Theoretical and measured results indicate that this new technique allows high efficiency profile to be maintained over a wide dynamic range of output power. For verification, the proposed LMBA was designated, fabricated and characterized. Under CW signal excitation (1.8–2.05 GHz), the measured results show that the prototype can deliver a saturated DE of 48.2%–63.2%, and saturation output power of 42–44.4 dBm. Meanwhile, at OBO of 7.5 and 15 dB, DE of 50.8%–59.5% and 37.9%–49.2% are achieved, respectively. Under 10 MHz LTE (PAPR of 10.2 dB) signal excitation, a measured average DE of 49.8%–55.5% at the average output power of 31.8–34.2 dBm, with ACLR ranging from −31 to −23dBc.

14209120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209120.value: The major findings (and related publications) of this project are summarized as follow: (C1) A compact design of symmetrical Doherty amplifier with wide OBO range was reported. This study reveals that the drain parasitic effect of the active devices as well as the reduced peak current ratio of DPA (due to class-B/C operation) can be taken into consideration by employing explicit drain circuit model and closed-form design formulas. (C2) A new and simple analysis technique has been developed for the two-tone intermodulation distortion study of class-C amplifier under large-signal excitation. Simulation and experimental results reveal that the nonlinear characteristics of the PA (e.g., gain compression, IMD3 and IMD5 frequency components, sweet-spot generation) can be accurately predicted by the proposed simple drain current model of the active device and the derived formulas. (C3) This study reveals that the proposed N-PD-LMBA can effectively combine the high power/PUF capability of PD-LMBA and the high-efficiency profile of HA-LMBA for enhanced efficiency operation. (J1) The concept of harmonic load control has been thoroughly exploited to extend the power/current handling capability of symmetrical DPA. Both theoretical and simulation results reveal that the active harmonic injection can enhance peak-current-ratio and load modulation depth (i.e., close to the idealized class-B/-B operation). Compared to conventional DPAs, the proposed combiner enables compact layout with size reduction of over 50%. In addition, both peak output power and OBO range of DPA can be substantially improved. (J2) New insights into the distortion generation of DPA has been disclosed. Analytical study reveals that the non-ideal auxiliary current profile (class-C) incurs insufficient load modulation, thus leading to undesirable voltage clipping inside the Doherty region. For compensation, the designated back-off load can be modified to circumvent the excessive voltage swing. Through mitigating the above issue, the linearity of DPA can be effectively enhanced with minimal impact on power and efficiency performance. (J3) In this work, an OBO-extended three-stage LMBA architecture is proposed by utilizing novel load modulation network with asymmetric coupling and non-standard load termination. In the proposed design, the interaction between different amplifying stages is attained by the output coupler only (without impedance inverter), thus simplifying the structure. Unlike PD-LMBA designs, the strong saturation of the main PA is alleviated, thus leading to enhanced reliability. Theoretical and experimental studies confirm the effectiveness of the proposed LMBA, demonstrating an outstanding OBO of 15 dB, which can accommodate modulated signals with very large PAPR.

14209120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209120.value: In modern communication systems, the increasing complexity of modulation schemes has created a significant need for power amplifiers (PA) that are efficient, wideband, and highly linear. The nonlinearity characteristics of PA can lead to the generation of unwanted harmonics and spurious signals. These distortions contribute to spectral regrowth (strong adjacent channel interference) and degradation in signal quality (increased bit-error-rate). Digital Predistortion (DPD) method is effective for PA linearization, but at the expense of increased hardware complexity, cost and power budget. Some potential PA linearization techniques for further research include: 1. Exploration of power-dependent source impedance matching network design (due to nonlinear input capacitance of active device) may help to compensate the gain compression of PA for enhanced linearity with negligible additional power consumption and circuit complexity. 2. Linearizer designs based on principle of Analog Predistortion (APD) is a compelling solution, due to its design flexibility, circuit simplicity, compact size, tunable, and low power requirement.

14209120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209120.value: Owing to the use of advanced modulation schemes (e.g., 256 QAM) in modern wireless communication systems, the transmit signal usually exhibits high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), which results in low average efficiency when conventional PA designs are deployed. Load-modulated PA (e.g., Doherty PA) has been regarded an ideal candidate for efficient amplification due to its excellent efficiency profile over a wide dynamic power range. However, DPA is also well known for its poor linearity. Though digital predistortion (DPD) technique has been widely employed for the linearization of PA, it also suffers from complex implementation issues, overhead power consumption, and high cost. In this research project, the nonlinearity generation mechanisms in load-modulated PA configurations are thoroughly investigated. New circuit techniques are developed for advanced PA designs with improved efficiency, linearity and power utilization. In summary, existing 5G and future 6G systems can benefit from the proposed low-cost and compact PA solutions, targeting wireless networks based on small-cell and multi-antenna configurations.

14209220.label: Project Objectives
14209220.value: To study fiber coupling methods for the novel dual-comb mode-locked fiber laser and hollow-core negative curvature fiber (HC-NCF) so that the minimal coupling loss and single-mode light delivery are both achieved. The major issue is that the solid-core single mode fiber (SMF) used for dual-comb output has a different core size and numerical aperture from that of the HC-NCF. We propose to investigate two methods using butt coupling and micro lens to solve fiber-to-fiber coupling issues. When investigating the butt coupling method, we will perform the modeling analysis of the variation of the coupling loss with the gap distance between the two fiber facets. We will also study experimentally the coupling efficiency and mode interference. When investigating the use of ball micro lenses, we will evaluate the coupling performance of spherical ball lenses with different diameters (generally less than 1 mm). To develop an all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor for the simultaneous detection of acetylene and ammonia in the near-infrared spectral range 1530-1550nm. Despite its superior performance, dual-comb spectroscopy with two independent optical frequency combs normally requires a complex and high-cost frequency stabilization system, thus hindering its practical application out of laboratory. We plan to exploit the state-of-the-art phase-coherent dual combs generated by a single free-running mode-locked Erbium-doped fiber laser with significantly reduced complexity and cost. Through device engineering, the proposed optical sensor consists of the dual-comb seed laser, dual-comb spectroscopic system, and signal processing system. We will conduct proof-of-principle measurements of acetylene and ammonia, and optimization of spectral resolution, data averaging, detection limit and long-term stability. To investigate experimentally noise and uncertainty factors with the use of a HC-NCF in the dual-comb gas sensor. Fiber bending noise is an important performance-limiting factor for fiber-based optical sensors. The fiber bending may introduce transmission loss and mode interference due to the excitation of higher-order modes. We will systematically characterize the transmission loss and relevant noise by varying the bend radius of the HC-NCF. In addition, the adhesive molecules like ammonia may cause a large measurement uncertainty due to the unwanted wall adsorption of molecules inside the tiny hollow core of the fiber. The HC-NCF gas cell could be continuously heated up to prevent wall adsorption of adhesive molecules, which will be systematically examined in this project. We will also test the influence of temperature and pressure on absorption measurement in the HC-NCF. To design and investigate a high-finesse fiber cavity to significantly increase the absorption path length. The detection sensitivity of the proposed dual-comb gas sensor is limited by the length of the HC-NCF (85 cm) to be used in this project. To increase the effective path length (thus to enhance the detection sensitivity) and maintain the all-fiber sensor configuration, we propose to design a fiber cavity composed of the HC-NCF gas cell sandwiched by two solid-core SMFs. The concave surfaces of the two SMF facets will be shaped by CO2 laser pulses and coated with alternating dielectric layers. With a reflectivity of 99.9% at 1.5 μm, we expect to achieve an absorption path length of 850 m that enhances the detection sensitivity by three orders of magnitude. The outcome of this research project includes the development of a novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor and the relevant scientific understanding of the emerging techniques of dual-comb spectroscopy and HC-NCF. We aim to get the developed dual-comb sensor out of laboratory and into practical use. Such a new optical sensor with high resolution, broad bandwidth, and fast response can be used in many important applications such as environmental monitoring and industrial process control.

14209220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209220.value: This project aims to study dual-comb spectroscopy in gas-filled hollow-core negative-curvature fibers and to exploit the use of such an all-fiber dual-comb sensor for trace gas detection. Laser spectroscopic techniques using optical frequency combs (OFCs) with many equally spaced, mutually coherent, narrow spectral lines are attracting a lot of attention. Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) by adopting two OFCs with slightly different repetition rates is an emerging tool that performs Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy without any moving parts. However, the implementation of DCS with two independent mode-locked femtosecond lasers requires sophisticated phase-locking systems to establish the mutual coherence between the two comb sources, making it difficult to get DCS out of laboratory for practical use. Recently, we demonstrated DCS with a single free-running mode-locked fiber laser that establishes intrinsically mutual coherence without any phase locking. To enhance the detection sensitivity, one comb pulse train was carefully collimated into a multipass gas cell to increase the light-matter interaction length. However, the use of such a multipass cell composed of two or more strictly aligned large mirrors normally leads to a bulky optical sensing system. Gas sensing in a long coiled hollow-core fiber offers a compact all-fiber sensor configuration. We recently proved the feasibility of employing a new type of hollow-core negative curvature fiber (HC-NCF) for optical sensor development. In this project, we propose to study a completely novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor by merging the single-laser-based DCS with the HC-NCF-based gas cell. The free-running dual-comb mode-locked fiber laser enables high-resolution and broadband spectroscopy without the need for sophisticated phase-locking systems. The use of HC-NCF gas cell provides the perfect light-gas interaction over a broad spectral range and long distance, as well as the advantage of fast gas sampling. To our knowledge, such an all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor has not been researched previously. We will investigate the methods of coupling the dual-comb fiber laser with the HC-NCF; demonstrate the simultaneous detection of acetylene and ammonia, and evaluate the sensor performance including spectral resolution, response time, detection limit, and long-term stability; and study cavity-enhanced all-fiber dual-comb spectroscopy with a high-finesse fiber cavity for trace gas detection. In the long term, our proposed optical sensors will provide a new opportunity for environmental monitoring and industrial process control with remote interrogation, multi-point detection, and integrated photonics systems. 本項目旨在研究空芯負曲率光纖中的雙光梳光譜技術，利用該全光纖雙光梳傳感器實現痕量氣體探測。 光學頻率梳（簡稱光頻梳，OFCs）由一系列等間距、窄線寬且具有相干穩定相位關係的譜線構成，基於光頻梳的光譜技術近年來引起了廣泛關注。採用兩個重複頻率略有差異的OFCs實現的雙光梳光譜（DCS），可以執行傅立葉變換紅外光譜（FTIR），而無需任何移動部件。但是，為了在這兩個獨立的光頻梳之間建立相干性，需要採用復雜昂貴的鎖相繫統，因此很難將DCS帶出實驗室開展現場測量。最近，我們基於單個自由運行的鎖模光纖激光器，在無任何鎖相的情況下實現雙光梳的內在相干性，其中一個光頻梳導入一個多次反射氣體吸收池，以增加氣體的有效吸收長度，提高DCS探測靈敏度。然而，該系統需要將光纖激光輸出轉為空間光，並且該氣體吸收池的使用會增加傳感器體積以及系統複雜度。 空芯光纖為氣體傳感提供了一種緊湊型的全光纖傳感器結構，我們最近證明了採用新型空芯負曲率光纖（HC-NCF）實現氣體傳感的可行性。因此，本項目將基於單激光的DCS與HC-NCF氣室相結合，研發一種新型全光纖雙光梳氣體傳感器。其中，自由運行的雙光梳鎖模光纖激光器提供高分辨率的寬帶光譜，HC-NCF在較寬的光譜範圍和較長的距離內實現激光與氣體的充分相互作用，且具有快速氣體採樣的優勢，目前文獻中尚沒有相關研究的報道。我們將重點研究雙光梳與HC-NCF耦合的方法與機制；開展乙炔和氨氣的同步檢測，並評估光譜分辨率、響應時間、檢測限和長期穩定性等性能指標；研究腔增強型全光纖雙光梳光譜技術，用於痕量氣體探測。從長遠來看，該新型傳感技術為實現遠程多點探測和光子系統集成提供了的新機遇。

14209220.label: Realisation of objectives
14209220.value: All the research objectives have been achieved in the project period. We have made significant progress in all respects of this project on experiments and modeling. Our research findings have resulted in 12 papers published in peer-reviewed journals such as Nature Communications, Light: Science & Applications, Optics Letters, Journal of Lightwave Technology, and Sensors and Actuators B: Chemical. Here we explain how the project objectives have been achieved. Objective 1: Study fiber coupling methods for the novel dual-comb mode-locked fiber laser and hollow-core negative curvature fiber (HC-NCF) so that the minimal coupling loss and single-mode light delivery are both achieved. The dual-comb source used in this project has a repetition frequency rate of 61.15 MHz with a frequency difference of ~1 kHz. The generated two comb pulse trains were divided by a two-stage dense wavelength division multiplexer to form the two arms of an interferometer. We have first realized optical coupling between the solid-core fiber that is used for dual-comb output and the HC-NCF that is used as the gas cell. One of the pulse beams was delivered by a coupler into the HC-NCF, and then the transmitted laser pulse was coupled by the second coupler into the optical fiber with a controlled polarization state for coherent detection. The HC-NCF has a 40-μm inner air core surrounded by a single layer of eight tubular rings. The node-less cladding structure formed by capillaries serves as a free core boundary. To enhance the coupling efficiency, we adopted free-space coupling optics to transport the pulse light between the optical fiber and the HC-NCF and achieved a coupling efficiency of 65%. Objective 2: Develop an all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor for the simultaneous detection of acetylene and ammonia in the near-infrared spectral range of 1530-1550 nm. We demonstrated a dual-comb gas sensor for the sensitive and broad-band detection of acetylene and ammonia near 1.5 μm using the all-fiber dual comb source combined with an in-line Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI). Because of the inherently high mutual coherence of this dual-comb source and the exquisite frequency agility, the dual-comb generates the multi-heterodyne modulation of the refractive index of the gas sample in the HC-NCF. A moderate optical span of hundreds of GHz is mapped to the frequency response range of the FPI. The photothermal spectra of C2H2 pumped by the dual-comb source can be obtained by the Fourier transform of the interferograms generated from the FPI within a short measurement time, i.e., as short as 10 ms in this study. The spectra of acetylene and ammonia over 1 THz are obtained by simply tuning the optical frequency of the ECDL. We achieve a minimum detection limit of 8.7 ppm of acetylene for the dual-comb power of 15 mW and fiber length of 7 cm. Our study opens a new opportunity to realize broadband, high-resolution and sensitive gas detection. Objective 3: Investigate experimentally noise and uncertainty factors with the use of an HC-NCF in the dual-comb gas sensor. We verified the advantage and necessity of selecting the HC-NCF to minimize the mode noise when conducting comb pulses through the gas-filled core. Compared to commercial HC-PCF (NKT Photonics), it shows that the additional capillaries in the structure of HC-NCF decrease the mode coupling of core and cladding. This can suppress the higher-order modes excited in fiber and increase the guidance of the single-mode 1533-nm laser beam in the sensing arm. The transmission spectrum retrieved from the signal conducted by HC-PCF is presented as a superposition of multiple sub-spectra, which is influenced by the noise caused by multi-mode interference. In addition, fiber bending was noticed to introduce transmission loss and mode interference due to the excitation of higher-order modes. Hence, a straight HC-NCF without bending was needed in the setup. The spectrum obtained by the HC-NCF system was retrieved from the beatnote of single-mode beams and keeps the spectral shape of the bandpass filter, which offers the possibility to do next analysis for the absorption spectral features on the uninfluenced spectrum. The influence of spectral averaging time on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was also investigated by measuring 0.3% C2H2 at 1 bar in the HC-NCF of this dual-comb sensor. We measured the representative absorption spectra from a single-shot interferogram and with 1500 averaging times of the Fourier-transformed spectra near the central wavelength 1532 nm. Additional phase correction was applied to compensate for the residual noise caused by fluctuations in the long interferometric path. Although hardly identified from a single-shot trace, the absorption features of 0.3% C2H2 from 6515 cm-1 to 6535 cm-1 become analytical with the spectral SNR more than 600 when the averaging time increased to 1500. Objective 4: Design and investigate a high-finesse fiber cavity to increase the absorption path length. The detection sensitivity of the dual-comb gas sensor is limited by the physical length of the HC-NCF. To increase the effective path length and maintain the all-fiber sensor configuration, we designed and fabricated a fiber cavity composed of the HC-NCF gas cell sandwiched by two solid-core SMFs. We expanded the core of the SMF through thermal expansion, increasing the MFD to approach that of the HC-NCF. A multi-layer dielectric coating of Ta2O5/SiO2 is applied to the fiber facet, forming dielectric mirrors with reflectivity exceeding 99.9% over the 1500–1600 nm wavelength range. As a result, we can increase the absorption path length by three orders of magnitude. The fiber cavity was characterized to achieve a record finesse beyond 1400 and boosted intracavity optical intensity for each pair of comb lines along the cavity length. Based on the HCF cavity, we studied fiber cavity-enhanced dual-comb photothermal spectroscopy for ultrasensitive, broadband, and high-resolution spectra measurement. With dual-combs and a probe laser locked to the cavity, the results show the comb line resolved photothermal measurements of the rovibrational combination band of acetylene over 1.6 THz. Our study achieved a record minimum detection limit of 0.24 ppb over the integration time of 320 s. Objective 5: The outcome of this research project includes the development of a novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor and the relevant scientific understanding of the emerging techniques of dual-comb spectroscopy and HC-NCF. To further enhance the performance, the straightforward method is to amplify the comb power using a fiber amplifier, one order of magnitude amplification is reasonable. The cavity coupling efficiency and finesse can be improved to achieve higher intracavity intensity. The mode matching can be optimized by trying different interconnections between SMF and HCF. Considering the response bandwidth of the interferometer and the cavity mode width, our system can detect much wider phase modulations. Such a new optical sensor with high resolution, broad bandwidth, and fast response can be used in many important applications such as environmental monitoring and industrial process control.

To develop an all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor for the simultaneous detection of acetylene and ammonia in the near-infrared spectral range 1530-1550nm. Despite its superior performance, dual-comb spectroscopy with two independent optical frequency combs normally requires a complex and high-cost frequency stabilization system, thus hindering its practical application out of laboratory. We plan to exploit the state-of-the-art phase-coherent dual combs generated by a single free-running mode-locked Erbium-doped fiber laser with significantly reduced complexity and cost. Through device engineering, the proposed optical sensor consists of the dual-comb seed laser, dual-comb spectroscopic system, and signal processing system. We will conduct proof-of-principle measurements of acetylene and ammonia, and optimization of spectral resolution, data averaging, detection limit and long-term stability.

To investigate experimentally noise and uncertainty factors with the use of a HC-NCF in the dual-comb gas sensor. Fiber bending noise is an important performance-limiting factor for fiber-based optical sensors. The fiber bending may introduce transmission loss and mode interference due to the excitation of higher-order modes. We will systematically characterize the transmission loss and relevant noise by varying the bend radius of the HC-NCF. In addition, the adhesive molecules like ammonia may cause a large measurement uncertainty due to the unwanted wall adsorption of molecules inside the tiny hollow core of the fiber. The HC-NCF gas cell could be continuously heated up to prevent wall adsorption of adhesive molecules, which will be systematically examined in this project. We will also test the influence of temperature and pressure on absorption measurement in the HC-NCF.

The detection sensitivity of the proposed dual-comb gas sensor is limited by the length of the HC-NCF (85 cm) to be used in this project. To increase the effective path length (thus to enhance the detection sensitivity) and maintain the all-fiber sensor configuration, we propose to design a fiber cavity composed of the HC-NCF gas cell sandwiched by two solid-core SMFs. The concave surfaces of the two SMF facets will be shaped by CO2 laser pulses and coated with alternating dielectric layers. With a reflectivity of 99.9% at 1.5 μm, we expect to achieve an absorption path length of 850 m that enhances the detection sensitivity by three orders of magnitude.

The outcome of this research project includes the development of a novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor and the relevant scientific understanding of the emerging techniques of dual-comb spectroscopy and HC-NCF. We aim to get the developed dual-comb sensor out of laboratory and into practical use. Such a new optical sensor with high resolution, broad bandwidth, and fast response can be used in many important applications such as environmental monitoring and industrial process control.

14209220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209220.value: We experimentally studied the methods for coupling the optical frequency combs into novel hollow-core negative curvature fibers (HC-NCFs) so that the minimal coupling loss and single-mode light delivery are both achieved. To enhance the coupling efficiency, we adopted free-space coupling optics to transport the pulse light between the optical fiber and the HC-NCF and achieved a coupling efficiency of 65% (Journal of Lightwave Technology, 40). Then we demonstrated a dual-comb gas sensor for the sensitive and broad-band gas detection using the all-fiber dual-comb source combined with an in-line Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI). We achieve a minimum detection limit of 8.7 ppm of acetylene for the dual-comb power of 15 mW and fiber length of 7 cm. Our study opens a new opportunity to realize broadband, high-resolution and sensitive gas detection (Nature Communications, 13). In addition, we studied mid-infrared absorption spectroscopy for gas detection using a quantum cascade laser coupled with a custom-made tellurite HC-NCF with a length of 21 cm. This spectroscopic system was demonstrated for nitric oxide detection by exploiting its strong absorption line at 1900.08 cm-1. By quickly filling gas mixtures into the HC-NCF, we conducted wavelength modulation spectroscopy and achieved a minimum detection limit of 6 ppb at the integration time of 30 s, corresponding to 1.0×10-7 cm-1 in NEA (Journal of Lightwave Technology, 39). To increase the effective path length and maintain the all-fiber sensor configuration, we designed and fabricated a fiber cavity composed of the HC-NCF gas cell sandwiched by two solid-core SMFs. The fiber cavity was characterized to achieve a record finesse beyond 1400 and boosted intracavity optical intensity for each pair of comb lines along the cavity length. Based on the HCF cavity, we studied fiber cavity-enhanced dual-comb photothermal spectroscopy for ultrasensitive, broadband, and high-resolution spectral measurement (Light: Science & Applications, 13). The outcome of this research project includes the development of a novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor and the relevant scientific understanding of the emerging techniques of dual-comb spectroscopy and HC-NCF. As the current system features an all-fiber configuration and low power consumption, we can move the developed dual-comb instrument out of the laboratory. Such a new optical sensor with high resolution, broad bandwidth, and fast response can be used in many important applications such as environmental monitoring and industrial process control (Optics Express, 29; Sensors and Actuators B, 363; Optics Letters, 47; Photoacoustics, 27).

14209220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209220.value: With the completion of this project, we have demonstrated an all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor for sensitive and broadband gas detection by combining the free-running mode-locked fiber laser with hollow-core fiber techniques. When employed as part of an environmental monitoring system, we aim to improve the detection accuracy while decreasing the cost and size of the system which could encourage the widespread adoption of this new technique. Due to its expected low cost, high sensitivity, and fast response, the new sensing system would support more targeted monitoring schemes for power plants, gas leakage sites, and indoor air quality. For the initial market entry of the developed new technology, we will focus on the area of energy saving and emission control for boilers in gas-fired power plants. It requires continuous monitoring of NOx and NH3 to ensure effective NOx removal and also to get rid of the possible ammonia slip. Particularly, we will seek funding support from innovation and technology commissions to realize the technology transfer and even commercialize the proposed novel gas sensing approach.

14209220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209220.value: Gas sensing in a hollow-core fiber (HCF) offers a compact all-fiber sensor configuration. This research studied a novel all-fiber dual-comb gas sensor by merging dual-comb spectroscopy with a novel hollow-core negative curvature fiber-based gas cell. By successfully coupling the optical frequency combs into HCF with high efficiency, we demonstrated a highly sensitive dual-comb photothermal gas sensor for the sensitive and broad-band gas detection of multiple species. We achieved a minimum detection limit of 8.7 ppm of acetylene for the dual-comb power of 15 mW and fiber length of 7 cm. Our study opens a new opportunity to realize broadband, high-resolution and sensitive gas detection. To increase the effective path length and maintain the all-fiber sensor configuration, we designed and fabricated a fiber cavity composed of the HCF gas cell sandwiched by two solid-core SMFs. We investigated fiber cavity-enhanced dual-comb photothermal spectroscopy for ultrasensitive (ppb) and broadband spectral measurement. As the current system features an all-fiber configuration and low power consumption, we can move the developed dual-comb instrument out of the laboratory. Such a new optical sensor with high resolution, broad bandwidth, and fast response can be used in many important applications such as environmental monitoring and industrial process control.
