14210320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210320.value: In total, four conference papers [C1]-[C4] and two journal papers [J1]-[J2] are published, covering the project's objectives from various perspectives. Please note that we use the notation [C1] to refer to the conference publication [1] and the notation [J1] to refer to the journal publication [1], etc. For Objective 1, we have proposed a dynamic hashing scheme to strike a good balance between performance throughput (i.e., efficiency) and performance isolation (i.e., predictability) for the multi-tenant system [C1]. Also, we have identified and resolved a performance issue of high-density NAND flash memory, which stems from the superpage organization in the modern SSD [C3]. For Objectives 2 and 3, we have developed several new solutions to maximize the access parallelism utilization of an SSD and to minimize the performance interference among multiple tenants [C3, C4]. Specifically, we have put forward a practical and near-optimal solution to organize superblocks on demand, developed a self-governing block-interface all-flash array (AFA) based on zoned namespace (ZNS) SSDs, and proposed a novel erase suspension policy to maximally circumvent the observed over-suspension issue. For Objective 4, we have developed a vertical simulation framework (that can coordinate the multi-queue resources of NVMe protocol, SSD controller, and micro-controller of flash dies) and built up evaluation platforms based on real NAND flash memory or SSD devices for performance characterization and investigation [C2, C3, C4]. For Objective 5, we have built up a multi-tenant testbed for evaluation using various representative benchmarks/traces [C1, C2, C4, J1, J2]. Specifically, we have studied various benchmarks (such as TPC-C, TPC-E, Filebench, Postmark, and YCSB), evaluated diverse I/O traces collected from productions (including FIU, Microsoft MSRC, Microsoft MSPC, SYSTOR, and Tencent Block Storage), and analysed representative traces collected from 875 file system snapshots by Microsoft Research. For Objective 6, apart from those common performance metrics such as the total execution time and overall throughput/latency, we have also implemented and examined several QoS-related performance metrics including tail latency at different percentiles and real-time throughput in the evaluation [C1].

14210320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210320.value: The proposed schemes aim to enhance the Quality of Storage (QoS) for multi-tenant systems utilizing modern, high-density solid-state drives (SSDs). One valuable direction for further development is to support the emerging protocols, such as Zoned Namespace (ZNS) and Flexible Data Placement (FDP), which enable host software to actively participate in or guide the data placement process for modern SSDs. This opens new opportunities to integrate the semantics of host software into the performance optimizations of data storage. Additionally, expanding the concept of QoS to encompass a broader context of data storage presents another avenue for further development. For instance, exploring how to adapt the proposed schemes to support cutting-edge storage technologies with varying characteristics, such as Persistent Memory (PM) and Compute Express Link (CXL), is a worthwhile area for further investigation.

14210320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210320.value: As more services and data transition to the cloud, multi-tenant systems utilizing high-density solid-state drives (SSDs) have become the mainstream option in enterprise infrastructure. However, our investigation reveals that while existing performance isolation solutions reduce performance variations among tenants, the throughput for individual tenants is often constrained by the reduced access parallelism of a partition. To address this issue, this research introduces several new schemes (which coordinate the NVMe interface, SSD controller, and microcontrollers on flash dies) to enhance the Quality of Storage (QoS) by co-optimizing performance throughput and I/O determinism. Also, this research conducts extensive evaluations using developed simulation and real platforms, along with multi-tenant testbeds featuring representative benchmarks and traces, to validate the effectiveness of the proposed schemes. The success of this research is particularly significant for Hong Kong, as it offers substantial commercial value and benefits to service users and providers by enabling low-cost yet high-quality data storage in multi-tenant environments.

14210920.label: Project Objectives
14210920.value: Anomaly Detection in Virtual Layer using Sequence Modelling Anomaly detection plays an important role in the reliability management of cloud computing environment. It employs a learning-based method to better monitor the cloud status by extracting information from the system-generated raw log messages. Traditional methods do not consider the sequential information among the logs properly, which is very common and important in the program execution flow. Besides, concurrent logs that occur at almost the same time (i.e., within one second) are not properly handled in previous study. To tackle these two problems, we propose a sequence modeling method, which models the sequence of concurrent logs. Our method not only captures the sequential order information among the logs, but also avoids the confusion caused by the interleaving of logs due to concurrent processes. Fault Localization in Physical Layer with Distributional Anomaly Score Nowadays cloud systems heavily rely on rule-based alerting mechanisms and machine learning-based detection models, which are often trained with insufficient data and may produce a large number of false positive alarms. To solve this problem, we propose a distributional anomaly score framework based on topic modelling and the probability distribution. With this method, we could help on-call personnel in clouds to reduce the time needed for the root cause identification in physical components. Due to the limitation of single physical devices, we propose a novel graph modelling and algorithms by leveraging system topology data, severity of anomaly, and detection results of physical components to identify the location of failure at the physical level. Log Data Collection Public log data is scarce in both industry and academia. Due to the confidential and safety reasons, companies are generally not willing to open their log datasets for public reuse. In this objective, to mitigate the deficiency of the log data, we plan to release a set of open-source datasets collected from our simulation environment. The environment will be built on the top of Kubernetes, which is a popular open source virtual container management tool. Specifically, we will conduct various representative software-intensive tasks in the containers such as Spark, Hadoop, etc.

14210920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210920.value: 雲計算系統的可靠性非常重要，因為一個微小的錯誤都可能導致巨大的收入損失和用戶的不滿。本項目提出的雲計算可靠性研究旨在提供一種先進的解決方案來解决可靠性問題，確保云計算系統能够正常工作。為此，我們擬從虛擬層和實體層兩個層面，根據云計算環境中異常狀態的不同特點，對其進行異常檢測和故障定位。更具體地說，我們設計了兩個新的深度學習算法，用於云計算中基於日誌的異常檢測和故障定位。通常，雲計算系統由虛擬層和實體層組成。由於服務運行所需的容器在基於分佈式節點的群集中，並且每個節點至少承載多個虛擬容器，囙此我們在檢測虛擬層中進行異常檢測，並在實體層（即雲中的節點）中定位故障。 在虛擬層中，異常檢測在雲計算系統的可靠性管理中起著重要作用。現時的趨勢是使用基於學習的方法，通過從系統生成的原始日誌消息中選取資訊來更好地監控雲系統狀態。然而，傳統的方法並沒有很好地考慮日誌之間的順序資訊，這在程式執行過程中是非常常見和重要的。此外，在以前的研究中，幾乎同時發生（即在一秒鐘內）的併發日誌處理不當。針對這兩個問題，本文提出了一種序列建模方法，對併發日誌序列進行建模。該方法不僅能捕捉到日誌之間的順序資訊，而且避免了日誌併發帶來的混亂。 在實體層，雲系統嚴重依賴於基於規則的警報機制和基於機器學習的檢測模型。然而，這些方法通常是在沒有足够數據的情况下訓練的，並且可能產生大量的假陽性警報。為了解决這個問題，我們提出了一個基於主題建模和概率分佈的分佈异常評分框架。通過這種方法，我們可以幫助雲系統中的運維人員减少在物理組件中查找錯誤根本原因所需的時間。針對單個物理設備的局限性，我們提出了一種新的圖模型建模方法和相關算法，利用系統拓撲數據、異常嚴重程度和物理部件的檢測結果來確定實體層的故障位置。 另一個問題是公開日誌數據在工業界和學術界都是稀缺的。出於保密和安全原因，公司不願意公開其日誌數据集供公眾使用。為了減輕日誌數據的不足，我們計畫發佈一組從我們的類比環境中收集的開源數据集。這個環境將建立在Kubernetes之上，Kubernetes是一個流行的開源虛擬容器管理工具。具體來說，我們將在容器中執行Spark、Hadoop等各種具有代表性的軟件密集型任務。為了推廣本項目中開發的科技，並促進在實際使用場景中的無縫銜接，我們計畫實施一個基於日誌的異常檢測的開源工具包。該項目將有利於學術界的研究人員和工業界的從業人員。該項目所公佈的資料可以使這一研究領域的多種相關工作成為可能，使研究人員能够對相同的數据集進行可重複的研究。此外，從業者可以直接在他們的公司使用我們的工具箱，或者根據他們的特殊需要基於我們的工具箱開發出一個定制的工具。

14210920.label: Realisation of objectives
14210920.value: All project objectives have been either fully achieved or even surpassed. For the virtual layer, we developed a sequence modeling method that not only captures the sequential order of log entries but also minimizes confusion caused by interleaving logs from concurrent processes. For the physical layer, we introduced a distributional anomaly score framework based on topic modeling and probability distributions, designed to assist on-call cloud personnel in reducing the time needed for root cause identification in physical components. Additionally, we proposed a novel graph modeling approach, leveraging system topology data, anomaly severity, and detection results from physical components to pinpoint failure locations at the physical level. Furthermore, we released a set of open-source datasets collected from our Kubernetes-based simulation environment, which includes various representative software-intensive tasks performed within containers. To achieve the project objectives, several machine learning and data mining algorithms were developed and deployed in real-world log-based anomaly detection and fault localization models in cloud computing systems. Some of these algorithms and datasets have been made publicly available to support future research in this field.

14210920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210920.value: In total, four journal papers and 20 conference papers were published, addressing the project's objectives from various perspectives. All of these publications acknowledge the support of this grant. The key outcomes are summarized below. Note that the cited publications are considered most relevant to this project. (We use [C1] to denote conference publications [1], and [J1] to denote journal publications [1], etc.) The first objective was to develop a sequence modeling method to capture the sequence of concurrent logs. This method is needed to retain sequential information among logs and mitigate confusion caused by the interleaving of logs from concurrent processes. To achieve this, we introduced an interpretable and adaptive approach for performance anomaly detection based on pattern sketching, which enhances interpretability by identifying groups of anomalous metric patterns that correspond to different types of performance issues. When similar patterns reappear, the underlying issues can be quickly recognized. Additionally, we designed an adaptive learning algorithm to accommodate new patterns arising from service updates or changes in user behavior [C5]. The second objective focused on supporting on-call personnel in cloud environments to reduce the time required for root cause identification in physical components. In cloud systems, unplanned service failures can have severe cascading impacts on dependent services. Accurate and efficient prediction of these cascading effects is thus essential for the operation and maintenance of cloud systems. To address this challenge, we first categorized the types of dependencies in cloud systems and developed the Dependency Management System (DMS), a platform to manage service dependencies in a production cloud system, where we defined the dependency intensity between services [C19]. We also pioneered an approach to predict the intensity of dependencies between cloud services [C3]. Subsequently, we built a comprehensive incident detection framework comprising data-driven methods to ensure timely, accurate, and thorough incident detection in cloud environments [J3]. In addition, we developed an efficient alert management method that quickly aggregates related alerts to narrow down the scope of issues [C2]. Beyond reactive alert management, we also examined existing alert generation rules and conducted the first empirical study on mitigating anti-patterns in alerting practices within an industrial cloud system [C20]. The third objective centered on implementation and dataset publication. We implemented the techniques outlined above and conducted extensive experiments. To support further research in log analysis, we also maintain a public repository on GitHub, OpsPAI (https://github.com/OpsPAI), where we share source code and data.

14210920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210920.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives stated in our project, where we proposed methods to manage concurrent log sequences effectively, designed a distributional anomaly score framework to assist cloud personnel with faster root cause analysis, and developed novel graph-based methods to localize failures while also publishing datasets and tools to support further research in cloud log analysis. For future development, our research aims to advance cloud anomaly detection, adaptive failure diagnosis, and efficient fault localization to address the complexities of modern cloud systems. As these environments are dynamic and ever-evolving, a key focus will be on creating adaptable models that can learn from new patterns and respond effectively to concept drift, ensuring resilient performance even as log behaviors shift. Additionally, by integrating human expertise into these systems, we envision a model that can continually refine itself through interaction, enhancing its accuracy in detecting critical but rare failures. Lastly, as cloud architectures grow increasingly interdependent, we aim to explore dependency-aware techniques for fault localization, leveraging the relationships between services to enable faster and more precise root cause identification. Together, these developments promise to make cloud systems more robust, adaptive, and responsive to complex challenges in real-world settings.

14210920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210920.value: This research focuses on enhancing the reliability and performance of cloud systems by analyzing and interpreting vast amounts of system-generated operational data. By developing advanced data analysis and machine learning methods to identify and manage technical issues, this project has made cloud systems more dependable and efficient. Key achievements include new approaches for recognizing log patterns, pinpointing hardware-related issues faster, and reducing false alerts that often flood cloud management teams. Additionally, a publicly available dataset was created to support future research and development in cloud reliability. The research outcomes offer valuable tools and insights to improve cloud reliability and ensure seamless operation, benefiting businesses and users who rely on stable cloud services daily.

14211120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211120.value: Recently, the rapid growth of cloud computing and data storage have raised a demand of higher data capacity in optical networks. Apart from the well-established wavelength division multiplexing technology, multi-core and multi-mode based spatial division multiplexing (SDM) begins to play an important role in bringing capacity breakthroughs per fiber. Meanwhile, higher order modulation formats are adopted to improve the spectral efficiency, leading to single channel capacity over hundreds of Gb/s. However, the increase of constellation size results in a reduction of the Euclidean distance between neighboring constellation points under the consideration of a fixed transmitted power. Therefore, a more stringent requirement on the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is introduced. An effective scheme to shrinken the SNR gap between the traditional quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signals and the Shannon limit is by applying constellation shaping to the transmitted signal. Constellation shaping can be categorized into probabilistic shaping (PS) and geometric shaping. PS is more popular than geometric shaping considering the flexibility of rate adaptation and the compatibility with standard QAM signals. In recent years, there has been extensive research on exploring the application of PS in optical communication systems. Unfortunately, investigation on the optimum PS design is rare. In this proposal, we aim to optimize PS by analyzing and carefully choosing the constellation size, distribution function and entropy loading. In the first stage, we evaluate the performance of PS-signals with different constellation sizes under limited resolutions of the digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital converters in the system. The analysis will be performed taking into account the nonlinear transfer functions of different electronic and optoelectronic components at the transmitter and receiver. In the second stage, the optimal probability distribution function for a nonlinear fiber channel is studied, including the scenarios of both single channel and multi-channels. When SDM technique is applied, the entropy value assigned to each core or mode should be properly designed to mitigate the crosstalk at utmost priority while maintaining the total transmission capacity. The above practical constraints will be jointly considered to determine the optimum PS design for the communication system. In the final stage, we investigate the incorporation of PS design for optical links with silicon-based integrated photonic transceivers. Such low-power consumption links play an important role in handling high-capacity intra and inter data-center traffic. Practical considerations will be analyzed including the limited bandwidth, finite extinction ratio, frequency chirp and nonlinear transfer function of the modulator devices. 近來，雲計算和數據存儲的快速增長對光網絡中的數據容量提出了更高的需求。 除了已經成熟的波分複用技術之外，基於多核和多模的空分複用在單根光纖容量的突破方面也起著重要的作用。 與此同時，還可以採用更高階的調製格式來提高頻譜效率，從而使單通道容量超過數百Gb / s。 然而，如果保持發射功率固定不變，星座圖尺寸的增加會導致相鄰星座點之間的歐幾里得距離減小，從而對信噪比有更高的要求。 一個行之有效的解決方案是對傳輸的信號進行星座圖整形，從而縮小傳統正交幅度調製信號和香農極限之間的信噪比間隔。 星座圖整形可以分為概率整形和幾何整形這兩大類。考慮到速率調節的靈活性以及與標準正交幅度調製信號的兼容性，概率整形比幾何整形更受歡迎。近年來，學術界針對概率整形在光通信系統中的應用進行了廣泛的研究。很遺憾的是，關於最佳概率整形設計的研究很少。在此研究計劃中，我們旨在通過分析並仔細選擇星座圖大小，分佈函數和熵負載來優化概率整形。在第一階段，我們在光通信系統中數模轉換器和模數轉換器的有限分辨率下評估具有不同星座圖大小的概率整形信號的性能。於此同時，我們還會結合發送器和接收器中涉及到的不同電器件和光電組件的非線性轉換函數進行分析。在第二階段，我們將研究在非線性光纖通道下的最優概率分佈函數，包括單通道和多通道傳輸。當應用空分複用技術時，應適當設計分配給每個光纖核或模的熵值，從而在保持總傳輸容量的情況下最大程度地緩解串擾。我們將同時考慮以上的實際約束條件來確定通信系統的最佳概率整形設計方案。在最後階段，我們嘗試將概率整形設計用在基於矽光集成器件的光鏈路上。這樣的低功耗鏈路在處理高容量數據中心内部和數據中心之間的信號傳輸方面起著重要作用。我們將把所涉及到的實際因素納入分析範圍，包括有限的帶寬，有限的消光比，頻率啁啾和調製器設備的非線性轉換函數等。

14211120.label: Realisation of objectives
14211120.value: 1. To investigate the optimum constellation size for probabilistic shaping under the constraints of limited resolution and dynamic range of optical transmitter and receiver components We have analyzed the influence of constellation size on the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and the sensitivity to the effective number of bits (ENOB) of the Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) and the Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) used in optical transmitters and receivers. Our study examines both conventional constellation sizes, governed by a power of two, and non-conventional sizes. Higher cardinality modulation formats are typically adopted for probabilistic shaping (PS) signals; however, they exhibit increased sensitivity to laser phase noise. We conduct experimental comparisons of signal performance among US-64 QAM, PS-100 QAM, PS-144 QAM, PS-196 QAM, and PS-256 QAM signals, maintaining the same information rate under both homodyne and heterodyne detection scenarios. As anticipated, PS-256 QAM demonstrates the best performance in the absence of laser phase noise. When the total linewidth is increased to 200 kHz, PS-100 QAM becomes the preferred format due to its shaping gain and relatively large phase margin [J1, C2]. Additionally, we perform numerical simulations to explore the effects of code rate and information rate on optimizing constellation size [J1]. In wavelength-division multiplexing systems, channel crosstalk introduces design complications. To mitigate this impact, it is essential to optimize the PS constellation size and its distribution function. By characterizing channel asymmetry in terms of noise variance and error matrix, we optimize PS 64-QAM signals to enhance system performance across various optical signal-to-noise ratios [J3, C6]. The optimization of PS signals is particularly challenging in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks, where multiple signals are transmitted over the same spatial, spectral, and polarization domains. To demonstrate probabilistic shaping in NOMA networks, we propose the transmission of 8-QAM and PS 16-QAM signals alongside a QPSK signal over distances of 5 and 20 km, utilizing a two-stage joint carrier phase recovery approach to support capacity enhancement [C9]. 2. To determine the optimum probability mass function in the presence of transmission fiber nonlinearity and to design related entropy loading algorithm for a multiplexing system Our research focuses on developing effective algorithms for phase recovery of PS signals. We compare the performance of the Viterbi and Viterbi (V&V) algorithm against the blind phase search (BPS) algorithm for PS-64 QAM and PS-256 QAM, assessing window size and signal-to-noise ratio under varying laser linewidth conditions. Results indicate that both algorithms yield similar performance for PS-64 QAM when linewidth is below 1 MHz; however, the BPS algorithm requires approximately 45 times longer running time than the V&V algorithm. We also investigate combinations of entropy values and code rates, revealing that under finite laser phase noise, PS signals with intermediate constellation sizes exhibit superior performance across various combinations of entropy values and code rates [J1]. The impact of fiber transmission on a multiplexing system is examined using a multichannel Kramers-Kronig detection-based communication system [C1]. We demonstrate the generation of 5×10-Gbaud 16-QAM single-sideband signals via an optical frequency comb. After 80 km of transmission, the carrier frequency comb is recovered through stimulated Brillouin scattering and successfully employed for multi-wavelength homodyne detection. Furthermore, we propose a probability mass function (PMF) optimization scheme that reallocates symbol probabilities based on constellation point performance within the training sequence. This PMF reallocation results in an improvement in generalized mutual information (GMI) of approximately 0.06 and throughput enhancement of about 1.5 Gbit/s [J3, C6]. The dynamic nature of PMF in the network necessitates an efficient method to monitor its shaping and scaling factors. As such, we propose a feed-forward fitting artificial neural network (ANN) to accurately estimate these factors in adaptive communication systems supporting probabilistically shaped QAM signals with variable entropy [J4]. A transfer learning (TL)-enhanced entropy and performance estimation scheme is developed to monitor a rate-continuous coherent optical transmission system across various signal-to-noise ratios [J6]. Adaptive entropy loading has also been demonstrated on a wavelength-division multiplexing platform sourced from an optical frequency comb [J5, J7, C8]. Lastly, we showcase a joint non-orthogonal multiple access probabilistic constellation shaping coherent passive optical network with a peak rate of 160 Gbps, catering to both fixed-rate and flexible fine-grained access [C9]. This approach offers an efficient and scalable solution for future optical access networks, addressing the growing demands for bandwidth and flexibility. 3. To demonstrate effective probabilistic shaping for short-reach optical links driven by integrated silicon-based modulators or receivers We have designed and fabricated silicon photonic transceivers based on GeSi electro-absorption modulators (EAM) and GeSi waveguide photodiodes using a commercial foundry (IMEC). These transceivers have been tested for 112-Gbaud transmission in PAM-4 modulation format, suitable for short-reach interconnects. Our investigation extends to nonlinear processing of optical signals on the silicon photonic platform, with potential applications in ultrafast all-optical modulation and photonic signal buffer storage. We demonstrate cross-phase modulation in a silicon-on-insulator waveguide using an ultrafast pulse train for the programmable generation of optical frequency combs up to 50 GHz [C4-C5]. Additionally, we explore fast switching and magnification of optical delay achieved through stimulated Brillouin scattering slow light. This switching and magnification are realized via a four-wave mixing interferometer on the silicon photonic platform [C3]. An initial slow light delay of 300 ps, introduced by a spectrally broadened Brillouin optical pump, has been successfully varied from -160 to +1140 ps. Utilizing cross-phase modulation on silicon waveguides, we generate optical frequency combs with tunable spacing in the 100-GHz range at around 1550 nm [J2]. This is accomplished through repetition-rate multiplication by Talbot processing, and subsequently leading to spectral spacing multiplication by cross-phase modulation. A maximum carrier-to-noise suppression ratio of approximately 45 dB was achieved. The comb source serves as a robust carrier bank for wavelength multiplexing in short-reach optical links. Furthermore, we demonstrate reconfigurable wavelength multicast utilizing the silicon-based frequency comb source [J8]. We simulate the NGMI performances of PS 64-QAM and PS 256-QAM multicast under varying signal-to-noise ratios and across different laser linewidths. Experimentally, we achieve 9 to 15-channel multicast with spectral spacings ranging from 75 to 150 GHz for PS 64-QAM signals at 32 Gbaud. This scheme can be extended to spatially multiplexed communication signals on the silicon photonic platform using wideband and high-efficiency mode converters [C7].

14211120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14211120.value: This research encompasses three primary objectives focused on optimizing probabilistic shaping (PS) for optical communication systems. First, we analyzed the impact of constellation size on the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and sensitivity to the effective number of bits (ENOB) in optical transmitters and receivers. Our experiments compared various modulation formats, including US-64 QAM, PS-100 QAM, and PS-256 QAM, revealing that PS-256 QAM performs best without laser phase noise, while PS-100 QAM is preferable when the linewidth increases to 200 kHz. This highlights the trade-offs between signal quality and modulation complexity. Additionally, we optimized PS 64-QAM signals in wavelength-division multiplexing systems to enhance performance amid channel crosstalk and developed a two-stage joint carrier phase recovery approach for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks, successfully transmitting multiple signals over distances up to 20 km, demonstrating the system's robustness and scalability. Second, we advanced algorithms for phase recovery of PS signals by comparing the Viterbi and blind phase search (BPS) algorithms. We found that while both algorithms yield similar performance for PS-64 QAM under certain conditions, the BPS algorithm is significantly slower, which raises concerns about its practical application in real-time systems. Moreover, we developed a probability mass function (PMF) optimization scheme that reallocates symbol probabilities based on constellation performance, resulting in a 0.06 improvement in generalized mutual information (GMI) and a throughput increase of 1.5 Gbit/s. This substantial gain underscores the importance of adaptive signal processing techniques. We also proposed a feed-forward fitting artificial neural network (ANN) to monitor and estimate shaping factors in adaptive communication systems, demonstrating the feasibility of adaptive entropy loading in wavelength-division multiplexing platforms. Finally, we designed silicon photonic transceivers utilizing GeSi electro-absorption modulators and waveguide photodiodes, achieving 112-Gbaud transmission in PAM-4 format. Our work included demonstrating cross-phase modulation for generating optical frequency combs up to 50 GHz, which is crucial for future high-capacity networks. We achieved significant carrier-to-noise suppression and successfully created reconfigurable wavelength multicast systems, demonstrating the potential for multicast with PS 64-QAM across various signal-to-noise ratios and achieving 9 to 15 channels with spectral spacings of 75 to 150 GHz. In summary, our findings contribute valuable insights into optimizing optical communication systems, addressing emerging demands for bandwidth and flexibility in future networks while paving the way for innovative applications in high-speed data transmission.

14211120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14211120.value: The potential for further development in optimizing probabilistic shaping, particularly concerning constellation size and probability mass function (PMF) optimization, is substantial. Future research can focus on refining algorithms to dynamically adjust constellation sizes based on real-time channel conditions, which would enhance performance and reduce sensitivity to noise and interference. Implementing adaptive entropy loading techniques will allow for more efficient data transmission, maximizing throughput while minimizing errors. Integrating machine learning approaches could significantly improve the PMF allocation process, enabling systems to learn from historical data and optimize symbol probabilities for varying operational environments. This could lead to enhanced generalized mutual information (GMI) and overall system performance. Additionally, advancements in silicon photonics present a unique opportunity to integrate these optimized probabilistic shaping techniques into compact, high-performance transceivers. Developing silicon-based devices that can support higher baud rates and more complex modulation formats will be crucial for future optical networks. The proposed course of action includes conducting extensive simulations and experimental trials to validate these optimizations within silicon photonic platforms. Collaborations with industry leaders in photonic integration can accelerate the transition from theoretical models to practical applications, ultimately enhancing the scalability and flexibility of next-generation optical communication systems.

14211120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14211120.value: This research focuses on improving optical communication systems, which are essential for transmitting data quickly and efficiently. We have three main goals. First, we examine how the size of signal constellations - groups of symbols used in transmission - affects performance. Through our tests, we discovered that while larger constellations can offer advantages, their performance varies depending on conditions such as bandwidth limitation of the transmitter and receiver, as well as interference and noise. Second, we develop smarter algorithms to recover signals that may get distorted during transmission. These algorithms help improve the clarity and speed of data transfer, particularly in challenging conditions. A key part of our work includes optimizing the way probabilities are assigned to different symbols, which can enhance overall performance and increase data rates. Finally, we designed advanced silicon-based devices that can handle high-speed data transmission, ensuring that these systems remain compact and efficient. By integrating these new technologies, we aim to create faster, more reliable communication networks that can meet the growing demand for bandwidth in our increasingly connected world. Overall, our findings have the potential to significantly enhance the way we transmit information over long distances.

14211320.value: 在微創手術（例如清創術和鑽孔術）中，骨骼手術是一項常見且至關重要的任務。現有的手動和機器人骨科工具是剛性的，缺乏足夠的靈活性，使得外科醫生無法將其用於精細的骨骼手術，更無法用於鉆彎曲的孔道。當在狹窄的人體内空間中操作時，醫生常常難以找到合適的骨骼工具位置以優化和被操作組織的接觸角度和穩定性。與手術工具限制有關手術引起的常見併發症如後腦脊液漏，骨骼孔錯位和股骨頭塌陷。傳統的柔性機器人解決方案無法提供骨科手術所需的靈活性和剛度，並且缺乏臨床可行的內置式力感測解決方案。 該項目的總體目標是開發和驗證一種機器人狹窄空間骨骼手術系統，該系統集成混合鉸接式機械手與可調節的柔性錨固系統、力感測和分層軟件虛擬障礙架構，以實現更安全、更精確和有效的骨科手術。與其他現有解決方案不同，我們擬議的系統由四個創新組件組成：（1）與常見的柔性機械手不同，我們的機器人同時包含主動柔性部分和剛性鉸接腕部分，並具有可調節的柔性錨固系統。它使我們能夠與硬組織牢固地相互作用，並承受較高的外部載荷，而錨固系統是根據鎳鈦樑的屈曲原理設計的，可為骨骼的精細手術提供額外的穩定性，並有助於操縱機械手進行鑽彎曲孔。（2）內置式力感測解決方案緊湊，只需要在錨固系統內部嵌入微型的基於FBG光纖的傳感器即可估算相互作用力大小和接觸位置。 （3）提出了一種層次化的軟件虛擬障礙控制框架，用於直觀的遠程操作。這種方法使我們能夠重塑任務空間的用戶輸入的空間範圍，以滿足機械極限約束，同時管理刀尖的剩餘誤差分佈，以避免在受約束的邊界區域發生自身產生的，用戶不想要的前端運動。（4）提出一種具有零空間迴避約束的混合位置/力控制方法，用於鑽彎曲孔。該控制器將允許我們提出的機械手自動調節鑽孔方向和相互作用錨固力，即使這些相互作用具有未知約束。我們將設計，製造實驗器械的原型，並將其與我們的達芬奇研究套件（dVRK）和我們的內部機械手進行集成。我們將進行實驗以驗證整個系統的跟踪性能，魯棒性和交互穩定性。 擬出的平台將是第一個與可調節的柔性錨固系統和力感應相集成以進行精確的骨科手術和鑽彎曲孔的系統。我們的分層軟件虛擬障礙也是第一個為運動學約束設計任務空間中的軟件虛擬障礙幾何的架構，它同時解決工作空間不匹配的問題，實現直觀運動控制和高保真自然觸覺。我們的研究可以作為一種新型的醫療機器人設備的骨科手術工具設計，傳感方法和遙控控制方法的基準。

14211320.label: Realisation of objectives
14211320.value: Aim 1: Design and fabricate the proposed instrument with adjustable force-sensing anchoring system For Aim 1, the PI and his collaborators have developed a new set of articulated tools including drills, screwdrivers, and high-speed burrs, with diameters ranging from 4.5mm to 8mm, designed for bone work in confined spaces. The innovative articulated joint design enables sharp bending with high stiffness, achieving angles up to ±65 degrees. This overcomes limitations of previous mechanisms, allowing precise navigation in confined spaces and enhancing outcomes in procedures such as minimally invasive spine fusion and core decompression while minimizing invasiveness. To enable force feedback capability, these articulated tools have been integrated into slim, lightweight handheld devices for convenient single-handed operation. The design allows for attachment to a UR5e robotic manipulator with two force/torque (F/T) sensors installed to decouple the measured wrenches from both the operator and the environment. This integration provides crucial force feedback, enhancing surgical outcomes and safety. Aim 2: Develop the proposed control algorithms (12-30 months) For Aim 2, the PI and his collaborators have developed a shared-control framework for an articulated drill system to enable safe and dexterous drill bit control. Taking advantage of the off the shelf force-torque sensor, the control framework allows the robotic system to measure and respond to the interaction forces with the operator as well as the environment. To improve the quality of executing drilling tasks in orthopedic procedures, virtual fixture constraints are added such that the robot is confined to a linear motion during drilling. The articulated structure, together with the assistance of the virtual fixture constraints allows the surgeon to complete drilling at hard-to-reach sites with large bending angles. As the algorithm explicitly accounts for both the operator and environment interaction forces, simultaneous position-force control can be achieved where the operator controls the robot’s motion through virtual fixture constrained admittance control while the environment contact force can be attenuated with the environment contact force measurement. This ultimately achieves safe and dexterous drilling tool control. Aim 3: Evaluate the pre-clinical performance of the proposed system (30-36 months) For Aim 3, the overall performance of the robot assisted drill system has been evaluated through a cadaver trial. In the cadaver trial, Transoral Mandibular Fracture Reduction was performed with the drilling system, which was conducted in a minimally invasive manner where no extra incision was created. Through the trial, the dexterous manipulation performance, the virtual fixture assistance, as well as environment contact force attenuation in the confined operation site of a real clinical setup was tested. The test successfully demonstrated the efficacy of the proposed robot assisted drilling system in the minimally invasive fracture reduction procedure. Although we acknowledged the RGC funding support in all relevant publications, we regret to note that we did not provide the correct reference number in the first three publications. It was only in the final publication that we included the correct reference number.

14211320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14211320.value: This project allowed us to investigate various aspects of robot-assisted debridement and drilling system, and eventually push towards pre-clinical trial. To enable angled drilling and milling in confined space, an instrument with large bending angle articulation joint and high-speed rotating tool bit was made [Yan Wang et al., 2021]. The proposed design managed to bring a high-level of dexterity while maintaining a good mechanical performance (e.g. stiffness and repeatability). To minimize collateral damage to the healthy tissue during procedure and to enable operations in extremely confined space, a miniaturized hand-held drill/burr [Yan Wang et al., 2022] was developed and tested based on the proposed articulated drill design. The miniaturized tool achieved 4.5 mm diameter while maintaining sufficient mechanical strength to complete bone work. Based on the proposed articulated drilling tools, a robot assisted drilling system was designed with the relevant control algorithms developed [Yan Wang et al., 2023], where a shared-control scheme was implemented, helping the operator to easily manipulate the drilling tool and complete orthopedic procedures with safety-critical constraints followed. The proposed system was successfully tested in a pre-clinical cadaver trial with positive surgeon feedback.

14211320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14211320.value: The research has developed a new set of articulated drilling tools for bone surgery, including drills and screwdrivers, designed for tight spaces with diameters of 4.5mm to 8mm. These tools can bend sharply while maintaining strength, enabling precise navigation in minimally invasive procedures. They can be used by hand or attached to a robotic arm equipped with force sensors to enhance safety and accuracy. A control system allows for safe robotic assistance by measuring the surgeon's movements and interaction forces, incorporating "virtual fixtures" to guide the tool's motion in a straight line for accurate drilling in hard-to-reach areas. The robotic assisted drilling system was validated through cadaver trials, successfully demonstrated the system's potential for safe and effective use in orthopedic procedures, confirming its ability to improve surgical outcomes while minimizing invasiveness.

14211420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211420.value: 增強現實 (AR) 已成為機器人、計算機視覺和生物醫學工程领域大家非常感興趣的課題。微創手術(MIS)在現代醫學領域吸引了越來越多的關注。由于減少了對病人的損和不舒服的感覺，微創手術通常是由外科醫生通過自然腔或非常狹小的通道完成的。在本研究中，我們將開發先進的增強現實手術導航，應用於諸如圖像引導股骨/肝臟手術這類的微創手術系統。更具體地說，在這項研究中，我們確定並解決幾個在完成增強現實手術導航系統的過程中存在的具有挑戰性的理論和實施問題。這項研究的新穎性是其新的解決方案和所涉及的兩個科學問題：能適用於外科手術的算法的準確性和魯棒性。首先是增強現實眼鏡中的手眼校準問題。目前還沒有好的解決方案。 手眼校準的已有解決方案存在噪音和異常值問題。第二個關鍵問題是剛性/非剛性註冊問題。我們的解決方案是進一步提高註冊方法的精度和魯棒性。非剛性註冊問題是一個在計算機視覺和機器人領域根本性的、仍然具有挑戰性的問題。我們以概率方法，使用從原始原始數據中提取的其他要素，解決非剛性註冊問題，開發快速和準確的註冊方法。我們將解決這兩個關鍵科學問題，整合完成一套先進的用於微創手術的增強現實手術導航系統。

14211420.label: Realisation of objectives
14211420.value: For the 3 Objectives as per original application 1. Development of a novel and robust hand-eye calibration approach for acquiring the relationship between the frame of the markers attached to the augmented glass and the image plane of the glass. 2. Development of a novel rigid/non-rigid point set registration algorithm based on probabilistic models, which is used to map the pre-operative space with the intra-operative space. 3. Development of a state-of-the-art mixed-reality system prototype, which we will validate in both mimic experiments and clinical experiments. The team successfully completed all project objectives as outlined in the original application. The primary focus was on developing advanced technologies for augmented reality (AR) in surgical navigation. This involved three key objectives: the development of a robust hand-eye calibration approach, the creation of a novel algorithm for rigid/non-rigid point set registration, and the construction of a mixed-reality system prototype. Each objective made a significant contribution to enhancing surgical precision and improving the overall experience for surgeons during minimally invasive procedures. Objective 1: Development of a Robust Hand-Eye Calibration Approach The first objective was to develop a robust hand-eye calibration method to establish the relationship between the markers on the augmented reality glasses and the image plane. This calibration is critical in computer-assisted interventions, where multiple coordinate frames must align for effective surgery. Achievements: 1) Calibration Approach: The hand-eye calibration problem was approached as a mathematical challenge where the relationship between different coordinate frames needed to be defined accurately. We formulated this problem using the AX=XB equation, where "A" represents the transformation of the camera's coordinate frame and "B" denotes the transformation of the tool's coordinate frame. To enhance robustness, we incorporated high-level features into the calibration process. By extracting more information from the calibration data, we significantly improved the accuracy of the calibration results. This was achieved by leveraging features such as geometric patterns and spatial relationships among the markers. 2) Implementation: The calibration procedure was meticulously tested and validated in a series of experiments. We conducted preliminary tests using simulated environments before transitioning to real-world scenarios. The results showed a marked improvement in calibration accuracy, which is essential for ensuring that the augmented reality system can overlay digital information accurately onto the surgical field. This foundational step not only solidified our calibration approach but also set the stage for subsequent clinical applications, ensuring that the system is reliable and efficient for real-time surgical navigation. Objective 2: Development of a Novel Rigid/Non-Rigid Point Set Registration Algorithm The second objective focused on creating a fast and accurate registration algorithm to map pre-operative images to the intra-operative environment. This is pivotal for ensuring that the surgical navigation system operates effectively in real-time. Achievements: 1) Algorithm Development: We successfully developed a novel registration algorithm that addresses both rigid and non-rigid transformations. Rigid transformations are typically simpler, involving the alignment of point sets that do not change shape. In contrast, non-rigid transformations account for changes in shape and configuration, which are common in biological tissues during surgery. By leveraging local features extracted from point sets, we addressed significant challenges, including outliers and anisotropic noise. Outliers can distort the registration accuracy, while anisotropic noise—where positional noise varies in different spatial directions—complicates the registration process. Our algorithm incorporates robust statistical techniques to mitigate these issues. 2) Methodology: The developed algorithm employs a two-step process for registration: o Rigid Transformation: In this step, we extract tangent vectors from the sparse intra-operative data, which helps compute the transformation matrix necessary for aligning the two point sets. This step ensures that the basic structure and orientation are correctly aligned before addressing more complex transformations. o Non-Rigid Transformation: Utilizing a Coherent Point Drift (CPD)-based method, we address the non-rigid transformation while considering anisotropic noise. This method improves registration accuracy by dynamically adjusting to the variations in positional noise across different spatial axes. These advancements have established our registration algorithm as a state-of-the-art solution in the fields of computer vision and augmented surgery, significantly enhancing the capabilities of the surgical navigation system. Objective 3: Development of a Mixed-Reality System Prototype The final objective was to construct a mixed-reality surgical navigation system prototype and validate it through rigorous experimentation. Achievements: 1) System Integration: We successfully integrated several essential components within the AR system, including optically-tracked surgical tools, intra-operative imaging modalities, and the augmented reality glasses themselves. This integration facilitated real-time visualizations of pre-operative scans overlaid onto the surgical field, providing surgeons with crucial contextual information during procedures. The use of infrared retro-reflective markers allowed for precise tracking of the surgical tools and the AR glasses, ensuring that the system operated seamlessly in real-time. 2) Calibration and Registration: The hand-eye calibration and point set registration methods were effectively implemented in the mixed-reality system. This allowed for seamless alignment between pre-operative and intra-operative data, ensuring that the digital overlays matched the physical anatomy precisely. The successful calibration and registration processes ensured that the navigation system could function effectively, providing real-time feedback and guidance to surgeons. 3) Validation: The system underwent rigorous evaluations through a series of lab experiments designed to assess its accuracy and functionality in a controlled environment. These initial tests demonstrated high accuracy in navigation and highlighted the system's robustness under various conditions.

14211420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14211420.value: In 3D Rigid Point Set Registration (RPSR): • Registration is accomplished for accurately aligning pre-operative patient-specific surgical plans with the intra-operative patient space [Min et al. 2023a, Zhang et al. 2024]. • Proposed normal-assisted RPSR methods, such as Anisotropic Generalized Bayesian Coherent Point Drift (AGBCPD), significantly improve accuracy and robustness by explicitly modeling anisotropic error distributions for both positional and normal vectors [Min et al. 2023c, Zhang et al. 2022, Zhang et al. 2023b]. These methods consistently outperform other probabilistic and deep-learning-based approaches in various experimental settings, including high outlier percentages [Min et al. 2023c, Zhang et al. 2023b]. • Bidirectional registration mechanisms, like in Bi-AGCPD, further enhance performance, particularly when noise and outliers are present in both point sets, by reducing confidence bias [Zhang et al. 2023b, Zhang et al. 2022]. This approach demonstrates quick convergence [Zhang et al. 2023b]. In Augmented Reality (AR) Assisted Surgery: • AR-assisted surgical systems provide intuitive guidance by overlaying internal patient structures over real patients in real-time, effectively giving surgeons "see-through" abilities highly desirable for minimally invasive surgery [Zhang et al. 2024]. • A novel AR-assisted orthopedic surgical robotic system successfully aligned pre-operative and intra-operative spaces [Zhang et al. 2024, Zhang et al. 2023a]. • AR-assisted bone-drilling systems are feasible for precise procedures [Wang et al. 2024a]. • Web-based AR platforms offer a cost-effective and collaborative solution for neurosurgical planning and education, achieving high overlap (IOU of 80.87 ± 4.42%) in auto-scaling and real-time head tracking [Ho et al. 2024]. In 3D Reconstruction Techniques for Tissues: • 3D reconstruction from endoscopic video is a crucial and intricate task for augmented reality and precise surgical navigation in robotic minimally invasive surgery [Xu et al. 2025]. • NeRF-based methods like LerPlane have significantly reduced training time for deformable tissue reconstruction [Xu et al. 2025]. • Gaussian Splatting (4D-GS) offers very fast inference speeds for dynamic scene rendering, though it currently faces challenges in generalizing to surgical scenes due to domain gaps [Xu et al. 2025]. • Real-time head pose estimation and 3D neural surface reconstruction using monocular cameras can provide a feasible, low-cost simulation platform for medical procedures like nasopharyngeal swab collection or intubation [Tang et al. 2024].

14211420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14211420.value: The successful completion of the augmented reality surgical navigation system opens several avenues for further research and development. Potential for Further Development: Enhanced Features: Future iterations could incorporate machine learning algorithms to improve real-time data analysis and decision-making, enhancing surgical precision and efficiency. Broader Applications: Expanding the system’s capabilities to include various surgical specialties, such as orthopedics and neurosurgery, could significantly benefit a wider range of medical procedures. User Interface Improvements: Ongoing user feedback will guide enhancements to the user interface, ensuring it meets the needs of diverse surgical teams. Proposed Course of Action: Clinical Trials: Conduct extensive clinical trials to validate the system in different surgical environments and procedures, gathering comprehensive data on its performance and usability. Partnerships: Collaborate with medical institutions and technology firms to refine the system and explore commercialization opportunities. Funding and Support: Seek additional funding to support ongoing research, development, and testing, ensuring the system remains at the forefront of surgical technology advancements. By strategically addressing these areas, we can maximize the impact of our research and make a significant contribution to the future of surgical navigation.

14211420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14211420.value: The research project focused on improving surgical procedures using augmented reality (AR) technology. Imagine wearing special glasses that overlay important information directly onto a surgeon's view of the patient, helping them perform operations more accurately and safely. The project aimed to solve three main challenges: first, ensuring that the glasses accurately align with the surgical tools; second, developing a fast and reliable way to match pre-surgery images with what the surgeon sees during the operation; and third, creating a practical AR system that doctors can use in real-life surgeries. This research is significant because it enhances the precision of surgeries, potentially leading to better patient outcomes and quicker recovery times. Making surgeries less invasive and more efficient can reduce risks and improve overall healthcare quality. In simple terms, this project utilizes advanced technology to enhance the efficiency of medical professionals, ultimately benefiting patients and the broader healthcare system.

14300120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300120.value: Atherosclerosis is a pathological process that underpins the progression of cardiovascular diseases such as stroke and coronary heart disease, both leading causes of death globally in the past 15 years according to the World Health Organization. Innovative, effective, and non-invasive technologies for inhibiting atherosclerosis are in urgent demand. Advances in nanotechnology supports the construction of bionanomaterials with architectural control by using various types and amounts of biomolecules as building blocks. Bionanomaterials are under active investigation as carriers of therapeutic agents to atherosclerotic plaques. Past researchers employed nanoparticles that are composed of lipids, lipoproteins, or sugars to encapsulate therapeutic cargoes and deliver these cargoes to atherosclerotic plaques, yet the use of nucleic acid-based nanostructures remains scarce. Recently, we have demonstrated that attaching non-coding DNA oligonucleotides to the surface of nanoparticles to form DNA-coated nanostructures significantly enhances and accelerates the intravenous delivery of nanoparticles to the macrophages of atherosclerotic plaques in mice (Zhang et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2019). Based on these published data, we hypothesize that oligonucleotide-coated nanostructures represent a suitable platform for delivering functional oligonucleotides [e.g., microRNA (miRNA)] to atherosclerotic macrophages for suppressing biological pathways that are linked to the development of atherosclerosis. In this proposal, we explore the application of oligonucleotide-coated nanoparticles as a dual agent for targeting atherosclerotic plaques and delivery of miRNA to atherosclerotic macrophages for inhibiting plaque progression. In our preliminary studies, we prepare nanoparticles that contain an outer shell of mature miR-146a, a 22-base oligonucleotide that negatively regulates the proinflammatory signalling pathways linked to atherosclerosis. Our miR-146a-coated nanoparticles effectively enter RAW264.7 mouse macrophages. These data motivate us to address the trafficking and disassembly of miR-146a-coated nanoparticles inside macrophages. Next, our miR-146a-coated nanoparticles specifically bind to the macrophages of the plaque-rich aortas that are excised from plaque-bearing mice. These data prompt us to elucidate the distribution of intravenously injected miR-146a-coated nanoparticles inside the plaques at the tissue and cellular levels. Finally, our miR-146a-coated nanoparticles effectively inhibit the expression of genetic markers that are linked to the NF-κB and IRF5 pathways in RAW264.7 macrophages. These data encourage us to evaluate the anti-atherosclerosis efficacy of miR-146a-coated nanoparticles in atherosclerotic mouse models. Our results will offer mechanistic insights into the in vivo interactions of miRNA-based nanostructures in atherosclerotic plaques. It will lay the technological foundation for designing nanomedicines against atherosclerosis in animal models. 14300120.label: Realisation of objectives
14300120.value: The two objectives have been achieved in full. We prepared the miRNA-conjugated superparamagnetic iron oxide (SPION) nanoparticles (NPs) by synthesizing carboxy-terminated PEG (polyethylene glycol)-SPIONs with a core diameter of 20 nm and covalently conjugated amine-terminated miR-146a oligonucleotides with the PEG via carbodiimide cross-linker chemistry to construct a 3D miRNA shell. The NPs were stable in serum and blood. In Objective 1, we investigated the intraplaque tissue-level distribution of SPIONs by intravenously (i.v.) injecting Cyanine 5 (Cy5)-labeled SPIONs into plaque-bearing apolipoprotein knockout (ApoE KO) mice fed on a high-fat diet (an established model for atherosclerosis). As control groups, we injected miR-nc-SPIONs (with scrambled miRNA sequences in the outer shell) and PEG-SPIONs (without miRNA). At 2 h post-injection, representative confocal images revealed stronger Cy5 fluorescence in the aortic roots from the miR-146a-SPION and miR-nc-SPION groups than the PEG-SPION group, indicating more abundant accumulation of miR-coated SPIONs in the plaque. We next quantified the intraplaque cellular-level distribution of SPIONs by measuring Cy5 fluorescence of different aortic cell types by flow cytometry. Data were expressed in terms of the fraction of Cy5-labeled SPION-positive cells in SPION-injected mice compared to uninjected mice for setting the negative gate. The mean fractions of Cy5-positive total macrophages for the miR-146a-SPION group (3.7%) and miR-nc-SPION group (3.5%) are 3 times higher than that of Cy5-PEG-SPION group (0.8%). Likewise, the mean fractions of Cy5-positive ECs for the miR-146a-SPION (24.7%) and miR-nc-SPION groups (13.7%) are significantly higher than that of the PEG-SPION group (2.1%). As control studies, we confirmed that the Cy5 fluorescence detected originated from Cy5-labeled NPs but not free Cy5 and that miR-146a-SPIONs more efficiently deliver miRNA to aortic macrophages and aortic ECs than Lipofectamine, a commercial transfection agent. Our in vivo data indicate preferential uptake of miRNA-coated SPIONs by the two major aortic cell types over PEG-SPIONs. In Objective 2, we evaluated the efficacy of miR-146-coated SPIONs in inhibiting the progression of plaques in atherosclerotic mouse models. Here, we i.v. injected them into ApoE KO mice that were fed with HCD for the first 9 weeks. Besides uninjected mice as negative control, our treatment groups include miR-146a-SPIONs, miR-nc-SPIONs, PEG-SPIONs, and miR-146a complexed with Lipofectamine (Lipo+miR-146a). Our injections took place twice a week from Weeks 10 to 12, keeping the amounts of miR strands and iron oxide injected constant across all groups. All mice were sacrificed 24 hours after the final dose. In our first set of studies, we extracted the RNA from intact aortas and examined the expression of target genes of miR-146a that are related to the NF-ĸB pathway by qRT-PCR. Injections of miR-146a-SPIONs significantly reduced the aortic expression of IRAK2 (direct target gene of miR-146a), IL-1beta, VCAM-1, and TNF-alpha (downstream genes of the NF-ĸB pathway) when compared to uninjected or Lipo+miR-146a; such treatments also significantly inhibited the first three marker genes in the aorta when compared to PEG-SPIONs. Although compared with miR-nc-SPION group, only the expression of VCAM-1 was significantly downregulated. The mean expression of other three marker genes in miR-146a-SPION group was lower than that in miR-nc-SPION group. Next, we evaluated the effect of miR-146a-SPIONs on plaque size by staining whole aortas and aortic root sections with Oil Red O. The lesion areas in the aortas of mice from the miR-146a-SPION group were significantly smaller than those for all other groups, with 30% reduction for miR-146a-SPION-treated mice than uninjected mice. The lesion areas in the aortic roots of mice from the miR-146a-SPION group were significantly smaller than those from the uninjected, miR-nc-SPION, and Lipo+miR-146a groups, with 20% smaller lesion areas for miR-146a-SPION-treated mice than uninjected mice. Furthermore, we assessed the effect of miR-146a-SPIONs on plaque stabilization. Sirius Red staining of the aortic root sections showed significantly thicker collagen cap around the plaques for the miR-146a-SPION group than other groups. We also addressed the plaque contents and inflammatory cell types in the aortic root in various treatment groups. Our immunofluorescence (IF) data reveal smaller CD68-positive regions (an indicator of macrophage contents) and ICAM-1-positive regions (an indicator of endothelial inflammation) of the miR-146a-SPION treatment group than all other treatment groups. Analysis of the fluorescence signals of the plaque area showed that the aortic CD68- and ICAM-1-positive areas for the miR-146a-SPION group were 30% and 20% smaller than other groups, respectively. Moreover, immunohistochemistry showed higher expression of alpha-SMA, a marker of the contents of vascular smooth muscle cells contributing to collagen production and fibrous cap formation, in the miR-146a-SPION treatment group than in all other treatment groups. The aortic alpha-SMA-positive area for the miR-146a-SPION group is 20% higher than other groups, indicating plaque stabilization and matching the Sirius Red staining data. Furthermore, treatment with miR-146a-SPIONs significantly reduced the size of the necrotic core, a key contributor to plaque vulnerability and rupture, compared with other treatments; the area of the necrotic core for the miR-146a-SPION group is 40% smaller than other groups. In short, miR-146a-SPIONs regressed and stabilized atherosclerotic plaques.

14300120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300120.value: We developed a spherical nucleic acid nanostructure with a superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (NP) core and a therapeutic miRNA (miR-146a) shell to alleviate atherosclerosis (Bai et al., Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA, 2022). Our study began by analyzing the distribution of miR-146a-coated NPs in atherosclerotic mice at the organ, tissue, and cellular levels. miR-146a-coated NPs significantly accumulated in aortic plaques (1.3% of the injected dose), and there is ~9.5-fold increase in miR-146a expression in the aorta compared to uninjected mice, confirming the effective delivery. At cellular level, miR-146a-coated NPs preferentially targeted aortic macrophages and endothelial cells. We found that class A scavenger receptors (SR-A) were crucial for mediating NP distribution, resulting in significant accumulation in SR-A-rich cells. In vivo data showed that miR-146a-coated NPs significantly reduced the expression of several target genes linked to miR-146a and NF-kB pathways in the plaque. We assessed plaque size via whole aorta and aortic root staining, revealing a ~30% reduction in lesion area with miR-146a-NP treatment compared to controls. Additionally, miR-146a-coated NP treated mice showed stabilized plaques, characterized by smaller necrotic cores and thicker collagen caps. Notably, repeated injections of miR-146a-coated NPs did not induce toxicity, with pronounced clearance from internal organs observed up to four weeks post-treatment. To further explore the mechanism underlying the anti-atherosclerotic efficacy of miR-146a-coated NPs, we performed RNA sequencing on isolated RNA from intact aortas. Comparing miR-146a-coated NPs with miRNA-free NPs revealed enriched gene ontology (GO) terms related to lipid metabolic process and immune system process. The GO term regulation of I-kB kinase/NF-kB signaling was significantly enriched, aligning with our in vivo findings. GO terms related to atherosclerosis, including immune system process and Wnt signaling pathway, were identified in comparisons with untreated groups. In conclusion, the efficacy of miR-146a-coated NPs in atherosclerosis results from their ability to inhibit endothelial cell activation, modulate immune responses, and regulate cholesterol transport and vascular remodeling. [We filed a patent based on this work and presented the research outcomes in multiple international conferences in Asia Pacific. This work also forms the basis of the thesis of PhD student of PI (Qianqian Bai), who won the best poster award in 2022 AsiaNANO Conference]. We also elucidated the intracellular trafficking of the spherical nucleic acid nanostructures (Li et al., Nano Lett., 2022) and reviewed the in vivo interaction of nucleic acid nanostructures with cells (Xiao et al., Adv. Mater., 2024).

14300120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300120.value: PI will elevate the biomedical impact of SNA nanostructures for managing cardiovascular diseases. He was conferred a fellow in the 2023/24 RGC Research Fellowship Scheme (RFS). In the new RFS project, he will elevate the research and translational impact of this GRF project, using microRNA-based SNA nanostructures for managing cardiovascular diseases in large animals, including plaque-bearing rabbit models and pig models with myocardial infarction. To undertake these studies, he will collaborate with a cardiovascular biologist, cardiovascular surgeon, electrical engineer, and radiologist. Moreover, for regulatory compliance in future clinical studies, he will liaise with qualified contract research organizations to evaluate the safety of microRNA-based SNA nanostructures in healthy rats and a pilot cohort of healthy monkeys. These future efforts will offer important insights into the bio-nano interactions, efficacy, and safety of nucleic acid nanostructures for clinical translation. The long-term goals are to reduce the morbidity and mortality of patients with cardiovascular diseases and to catalyze the development of nanomedicines that are conceptualized and translated in Hong Kong.

14300120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300120.value: Atherosclerosis underpins the progression of stroke and myocardial infarction, both leading causes of death globally. Gene therapy is an emerging therapeutic approach for atherosclerosis, but the delivery of gene cargoes to the atherosclerotic plaque remains inefficient. This project has expanded our understanding of how miRNA-coated nanoparticles distribute to targeted plaques and interact with cells in vivo. These data are valuable, as nucleic acid nanotechnology has advanced the field of gene therapy for the management of various diseases. Regarding biodistribution, we found that the three-dimensional therapeutic miRNA shell of the nanoparticle leads to significantly higher accumulation in plaque areas, primarily targeting atherosclerotic macrophages and endothelial cells (both key cell types involved in the development and progression of atherosclerosis). This unique design demonstrates that the miRNA shell serves not only as gene cargo for alleviating atherosclerosis but also as a targeting component to enhance accumulation at the targeted plaques. Furthermore, after repeated intravenous injections of the miRNA-coated nanoparticles into atherosclerotic mice, we observed that the nanoparticles modulate genes related to immune response and vascular inflammation, resulting in reduced and stabilized plaques without causing severe toxicity. Our findings offer insights into the translation of nucleic acid nanotechnology for treating and understanding cardiovascular diseases.

14300220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300220.value: There are two very important and active areas in modern mathematics: algebraic geometry, which studies solutions to systems of polynomial equations and their geometric structure; representation theory, which studies the symmetries arising in mathematics and natural science via linear algebra. In this proposal, the central objects are the affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties, an important object in algebraic geometry. Roughly speaking, the affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties describe the intersection of a linear structure (the Iwahori double cosets) and a highly nonlinear structure (the Frobenius-twisted conjugacy classes) inside a loop group. It plays an important role in the study of Shimura varieties, a central object in the number theory. Recent work of the PI shows that there is a surprising and mysterious connection between algebraic geometry and representation theory, namely, the structure of the geometric object, affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties and the representations of an algebraic object, affine Hecke algebras. In this proposal, the PI plans to understand further this connection, and to investigate several open problems on affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. This includes the studies of the nonemptiness pattern of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties, the asymptotic behavior of the dimension, and the irreducible components. The progress on these open problems has important applications to the study of Shimura varieties as well. This research will enhance our understanding of algebraic geometry, number theory and representation theory. 在現代數學裏面有兩個非常重要的領域：代數幾何，研究多項式方程的解及其幾何性質；表示論，通過線性代數研究在數學和自然科學中產生的對稱性。這個研究項目中的研究對象是仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇。簡單來說，仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇研究在一個線性結構（Iwahori雙陪集）和一個高度非線性的結構（Frobenius共軛類）的交集。仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇在志村簇（數論中的一個核心的研究對象）的研究中起了重要作用。 本人近期的研究揭示了在代數幾何和表示論之間有一個意想不到的神秘的聯繫。在這個研究項目中，本人準備繼續沿着這個方向深入下去，研究在仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇中的幾個未解決的大問題：仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇在什麼時候非空；維數公式的漸進特徵；以及仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇的不可約分支。在這些問題中的進展將會在志村簇的研究中發揮重要作用。這項研究將會加強我們對代數幾何，數論和表示論的理解。

14300220.value: Affine Deligne-Lusztig variety is the group-theoretic model of the reduction of Shimura varieties. It plays an important role in the arithmetic geometry and Langlands program. Dimension formula of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties is a fundamental problem in this topic. These works will shed new lights on the study of Shimura varieties.

14300220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300220.value: In this project, the PI made considerable progress in the study of symmetries and obtain several important applications to arithmetic geometry and representation theory. Symmetries appear in most physical system, and has found applications throughout mathematics and the natural science, including particle physics, string theory, signal processing and genetics. By understanding several important aspects on the Weyl groups, the symmetry appears in many topics in the study of Shimura varieties and representation theory, the PI opens a new door to approach many important problems in these field. Combining the new knowledge on the Weyl groups, together with some novel ideas in arithmetic geometry and representation theory, the PI has successfully solved several important long-standing problems in these field. This project reveals the close relations between combinatorics, representation theory, and geometry and thus has an impact in these fields.

14300320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300320.value: The nature of dark matter remains one of the most important open questions in Astrophysics, Cosmology, and Particle Physics, in spite of decades of direct and indirect searches. The goal of this project is to make use of white dwarfs - Earth-sized stars with sun-like mass, supported by electron degeneracy pressure - as 'detectors' for dark matter. It builds on our long track record of studying dark-matter admixed white dwarfs. We have previously shown that massive non-self-annihilating degenerate fermionic dark matter may form a compact and static core in a white dwarf, leading to significant changes in the structure and Chandrasekhar limit of the latter. The light curves of the subsequent Type-IA supernova explosions of such dark-matter admixed white dwarfs are consistent with several observed sub-luminous Type-IA supernovae. We have also shown that the accretion-induced collapse of dark-matter admixed white dwarfs would be weakened, but future neutrino and gravitational-wave observations can help to identify such objects and constrain dark matter properties. We propose to extend these studies to relatively light fermionic and bosonic dark-matter admixture in white dwarfs, particularly when both the normal and dark matter components have comparable spatial extents. The dynamics and interaction of the two fluid components will be important and may give rise to interesting new phenomena. We will investigate the equilibrium properties, collapse and explosion of such a two-fluid white dwarf. We look for observational signatures of such objects, particularly their neutrino and gravitational-wave signals, so as to constrain the properties of dark matter. 儘管科學家從事了數十年的直接和間接搜索，暗物質的性質仍然是天體物理學，宇宙學和粒子物理學最重要的未解問題之一。這項目的目標是利用白矮星作為黑暗的“探測器”。白矮星是具有類似太陽的質量，卻只有地球大小的星星。它們受到電子簡併壓力的支持。先前我們已經證明，非自我毀滅性簡併暗物質可能在白矮星中形成緻密的靜態核，導致後者的結構和最大質量發生了重大變化。此類暗物質混合白矮星隨後的IA型超新星爆炸的光曲線與幾個觀測到的黯淡IA型超新星一致。我們還證明，暗物質混合白矮星因質量吸積而坍塌將被削弱，但是未來的中微子和引力波觀測可以幫助識別此類星體並限制暗物質的性質。我們將延續這些研究，針對白相對較輕的簡併費米子和玻色子暗物質混合白矮星，特別是當正常物質和暗物質佔比相若的蜻況。兩種流體成分的動力學和相互作用將很重要，並且可能會引起有趣的新現象。 我們將研究這些雙流體白矮星的平衡特性，坍塌和爆炸。 我們尋找此類物體的觀測特徵，尤其是它們的中微子和引力波信號，以限制暗物質的性質。

14300320.label: Realisation of objectives
14300320.value: 1. Extend our Newtonian hydrodynamics code to a two-fluid hydrodynamics code: fully achieved. Our two-fluid hydrodynamics code is discussed in detail in Ho-Sang Chan, Ming-chung Chu, Shing-Chi Leung, and Lap-Ming Lin, Astrophysical Journal 914:138 (2021). We have used this code to study both Accretion-induced collapse and Type IA Supernovae. 2. Study equilibrium properties of light fermionic and/or bosonic dark-matter admixed white dwarfs: fully achieved. Our results lead to three published papers: Billy K. K. Lee, Ming-chung Chu, and Lap-Ming Lin, Astrophysical Journal 922:242 (2021) for bosonic dark matter admixed white dwarfs (and whether the GW190814 Secondary could be such an object), Ho-Sang Chan, Ming-chung Chu, and Shing-Chi Leung, Astrophysical Journal 941:115 (2022) for fermionic dark matter admixed rotating white dwarfs (which could account for some peculiar white dwarfs observed that do not follow their usual mass–radius relation), and Kwing-Lam Leung, Ming-chung Chu, and Lap-Ming Lin, Physical Review D 105, 123010 (2022), demonstrating that the dimensionless tidal deformability showss harp change from being similar to that of a pure normal matter star to that of a pure dark matter star, within a narrow range of intermediate dark matter mass fraction, for both fermionic and bosonic dark matter. 3. Study Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of a light fermionic dark-matter (DM) admixed white dwarf: fully achieved. Our results are published in Ho-Sang Chan, Ming-chung Chu, and Shing-Chi Leung, Astrophysical Journal 945:133 (2023). We find that the DM component follows the collapse of the normal matter (NM) component to become a bound DM core. Thus, we demonstrate how a DM-admixed neutron star could form through DM-admixed AIC (DMAIC) for the first time, with the dynamics of DM taken into account. Our study is not only the first-ever computation of GW from a collapsing DM object but also provides the key features to identify DM in AIC events through future GW detections. We have also calculated the nucleosynthesis of AIC. We find that the ejecta mass of AIC could be up to ∼ 0.01M⊙, and the first neutron-capture peak elements (Sr, Y, and Zr) could be abundantly synthesized, with an overproduction of ∼ 10^6 relative to the solar abundances. Dark matter admixture does not change the nucleosynthesis significantly. Our results are presented in a preprint submitted to https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03798. 4. Study Type IA supernova of a light fermionic dark-matter admixed white dwarf: fully achieved. Our results are published in Ho-Sang Chan, Ming-chung Chu, Shing-Chi Leung, and Lap-Ming Lin, Astrophysical Journal 914:138 (2021). We find that dark matter admixed models give dimmer but slowly declining light curves, consistent with some observed peculiar supernovae. Our results suggest a formation path for dark compact objects that mimic sub-solar-mass black holes as dark gravitational sources. 5. Study Accretion-induced collapse of a light bosonic dark-matter admixed white dwarf: largely done. We have finished the two-fluid Newtonian hydrodynamics code. See 1 and 3 above. Light bosonic DM presents quite a challenge for numerical simulation because the quantum pressure easily induces numerical instability. After searching for a stable method for a long time, we found that an Implicit-Explicit Method (IMEX) can solve the Gross-Pitaevskii equation with good stability. 6. Study Type IA supernova of a light bosonic dark-matter admixed white dwarf: largely done. We have finished the two-fluid Newtonian hydrodynamics code. See 1, 4, and 5 above.

14300320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300320.value: Publications from this project (numbers in [] correspond to those in Part C): [1] (Lee 2021)We calculated the equilibrium structures of bosonic DM-admixed compact stars. The GW190814 Secondary cannot be a neutron star (NS) admixed with QCD axions. However, it can still be an NS admixed with at least 2.0 solar mass of axion-like particles (AXP), or even a pure AXP star. [2] (Yeung 2021) We study how the two-fluid dynamics might affect the I-Love-Q relations. We find that the I-Love-Q relations can still be satisfied to high accuracy for superfluid NSs as long as the two fluids are nearly co-rotating. [3] (Tang 2023) We investigate how a crystalline core may affect the properties and dynamics of white dwarfs (WDs). The i and s mode frequencies depend sensitively on the core size, while the f mode frequency is affected by at most a few percent for our chosen WD models. The effect of crystallization on the tidal deformability becomes significant only when the core radius is larger than about 70 percent of the stellar radius. [4] (Chan 2022) We compute the equilibrium structures of fermionic DM-admixed rotating WDs. We find that admixing DM to rotating WDs could: (1) account for some peculiar WDs that do not follow their usual mass-radius relation; (2) allow stable rapid-rotating WDs that are free from thermonuclear runaway to exist, which could explain some soft gamma-ray repeaters/anomalous X-ray pulsars; and (3) produce universal I-Love-Q relations that span bands above those without DM admixture. [5] (Leung 2022) We computed the dimensionless tidal Love number and tidal deformability for both fermionic and bosonic DM-admixed stars. The latter shows a sharp change from being similar to that of a pure normal matter (NM) star to that of a pure DM star, within a narrow range of intermediate DM mass fraction. [6] (Chan 2023) We present 2D hydrodynamic simulations of the accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of rotating WDs admixed with an extended component of sub-GeV fermionic DM. The DM component follows the collapse of the NM component to become a bound DM core. Thus, we demonstrate how a DM-admixed neutron star could form through DM-admixed AIC. [7] (Yip 2023) We show that a minimum-mass neutron star undergoes delayed explosion after mass removal from its surface. A robust r-process nucleosynthesis is realized in the ejecta, suggesting that sub-minimal neutron star explosions could be an important source of solar chemical elements.

14300320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300320.value: The possibility of DM-admixed compact stars has attracted more and more attention recently. In this project, we have shown the rich phenomenology of such compact stars, from static structures to their collapse and explosion. In particular, we have shown ways to search for the DM admixture in white dwarfs, neutron stars, AIC, and Type 1A supernovae. These are all excellent targets for multi-messenger astronomical observation. It will be interesting to extend the study to DM-admixed Core-collapse supernovae. Another direction is to include the effects of magnetic fields since WDs and NSs with strong magnetic fields have been discovered.
