14301820.label: Realisation of objectives
14301820.value: We have successfully realized all the objectives listed in section 5.2 1. We have developed a copper-catalyzed hydroboration reaction of trifluoromethyl alkenes. The reaction provided an efficient method for the synthesis of valuable difluoromethylated alkenes in high diastereoselectivities via a net protodefluorination process. Furthermore, a ligand-controlled regiodivergent asymmetric copper-catalyzed hydroboration of trifluoromethyl alkenes was discovered leading to chiral trifluoromethylated products in high enantioselectivities. 2. We have developed other types of metal-catalyzed functionalization of fluoroalkenes. These include: (1) palladium-catalyzed diastereoselective Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes for the synthesis of monofluorostilbenes; (2) palladium-catalyzed diastereoselective Stille cross-coupling of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes for the synthesis of monofluorinated 1,3- and 1,4-dienes; (3) palladium-catalyzed enantioselective domino dearomative Heck/Suzuki reaction of trifluoromethyl indoles for the synthesis of chiral indolines.

14301820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301820.value: In this project, we have studied the copper-catalyzed hydroboration of trifluoromethyl alkenes which led to two important findings. First, the construction of stereogenic carbon centres containing the trifluoromethyl group was successfully demonstrated through an asymmetric hydroboration/oxidation protocol using the CuCl/(S,S)-Me-DUPHOS catalytic system. Chiral trifluoromethylated alcohol products could be obtained in high enantioselectivities. Second, an unexpected protodefluorination process was discovered which gave access to valuable difluoromethylated alkene products in good yields. Both findings have been recently published (Chem Asian J. 2023, 18, e202300655). Moreover, by developing an asymmetric palladium-catalyzed domino dearomative Heck-Suzuki reaction of trifluoromethyl indoles, we were able to synthesize chiral indolines with stereocentres containing the trifluoromethyl group (Chem. Commun. 2022, 58, 6200). We have also described a novel domino acylation/trifluoromethylation of bicyclic amidines to access N-heterocycles with quaternary carbon centres containing the trifluoromethyl group (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 5656). Building on these works, we have developed two related methods for the synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant difluoromethylated compounds. Our expertise in copper and alkene chemistry led to the discovery of a copper-catalyzed/visible-light-induced allylic difluoromethylation of unactivated alkenes for the construction of allylic CF2H bonds (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 1045). We have also reported an organocatalytic three-component acyldifluoromethylation of styrenes for the synthesis of beta-difluoromethyl ketones (Org. Lett. 2022, 24, 4840). Besides trifluoromethyl alkenes, we have studied transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes for the synthesis of monofluoroalkenes. A palladium-catalyzed stereoselective Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of gem-difluoroalkenes was successfully developed (ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 4799). Both experimental and computational studies were employed to decipher a key C-F bond activation step in the reaction mechanism. Structurally diverse (E)-monofluorostilbenes were synthesized in excellent diastereoselectivities. The stereoselective palladium-catalyzed Stille-type cross-coupling of gem-difluoroalkenes gave access to novel monofluorinated 1,3- and 1,4-dienes, which were useful building blocks for further derivatizations (Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 8072). We have also found that trisubstituted monofluoroalkenes could undergo nucleophilic vinylic substitution reaction for the synthesis of stereodefined trisubstituted alkenes and divinyl ethers (Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6169). Overall, this project has led to the publication of 8 original research articles in international peer-reviewed journals and 4 international conference presentations. Two Ph.D. students have received training from this project and successfully graduated.

14301820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301820.value: We will continue to explore the construction of stereogenic carbon centres containing the fluoroalkyl group. The asymmetric copper-catalyzed hydroboration protocol can be extended beyond trifluoromethyl alkenes to include difluoromethyl and monofluoromethyl alkenes for diverse product structures. Recently we have also developed the synthetic method for accessing pentafluoroethyl alkenes, which can be used to generate stereocentres with pentafluoroethyl group. The domino acylation/fluoroalkylation of bicyclic amidines can lead to chiral compounds with quaternary centres. We will explore the asymmetric version of this reaction by using chiral Lewis acids to achieve enantioselectivity. The stereoselective transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes has great potential. We will continue to explore various palladium-catalyzed cross-couplings for the synthesis of functionalized monofluoroalkenes. Other metals including rhodium and nickel will also be employed to broaden the reaction scope and investigate reaction mechanisms. The monofluoroalkene products are prochiral building blocks and their applications in asymmetric transformations will also be explored.

14301820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301820.value: The construction of stereogenic carbon centres containing a trifluoromethyl group is a long-standing challenge in organic synthesis. Important pharmaceuticals including the anti-HIV drug Efavirenz have such motif. With the financial support from RGC in this General Research Fund, we were able to develop a novel asymmetric copper-catalyzed hydroboration reaction of trifluoromethyl alkenes to synthesize chiral compounds featuring stereocentres with a trifluoromethyl group. Building on this work, we have also developed methods for the synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant difluoromethylated compounds. Furthermore, the stereoselective palladium-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes has also been developed to generate valuable monofluoroalkene products towards drug discovery. The outcome of this project has led to the publication of 8 original research articles in international peer-reviewed journals and 4 international conference presentations. Two Ph.D. students have received training from this project and successfully graduated.

14301920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301920.value: 在時間-事件/生存數據的建模中，分位數迴歸已經成爲替代Cox比例風險模型和加速失效時間模型的一種不可或缺的方法。其在生存時間的個別分位數上區分開協變量影響的能力，使得這一類的模型在不施加傳統上的限制（包括在前述兩種模型中分別假設的成比例風險，以及殘差同質性）時，允許建模中數據的異質性。與傳統的均值迴歸模型相比，分位數迴歸也因其對異常值的穩健性而著稱。這些優點解釋了它作爲標準的建模工具之一，在經濟學、生物統計學和其他學科的流行。它也是一個在生存分析方向上活躍的研究領域。 本研究題嘗試擴大刪失分位數迴歸模型的適用範圍，以便妥善處理一般的時依協變量。同時，我們也提供了處理有偏抽樣數據的相應方法。面對大數據時代，我們不可避免地需要對樣本量巨大的數據集擬合合適的刪失分位數迴歸模型。儘管已經有各種各樣的解決方案去對非刪失觀測數據進行分位數迴歸的建模，然而，對部分數據無法觀測到的（右）刪失時間-事件數據來説，我們仍然缺少相對應的解決方法。 考慮到這些開放性問題的重要性，本研究旨在於更少限制條件下提供這些問題的解決方案，並填補文獻空缺。根據我們在初步/前導研究中觀察到的滿意結果，我們預料所提出的方法在理論上是合理的，在實際中也是可行的。我們所提出的研究方法將為生存分析和分位數迴歸的前沿研究作出貢獻，而由於刪失分位數迴歸已被廣泛應用於各個學科以滿足建模和預測的各類需要，這些方法也將因此而裨益廣大受衆。

14301920.label: Realisation of objectives
14301920.value: The three objectives of the project have been achieved in this proposal for various projects. One of the main publication outputs entitled “Censored quantile regression model with time-dependent covariates” (see Publication #7 in Part C) proposes a new class of quantile-based regression models with time-dependent covariates for censored data. Our model offers a significant advancement in survival analysis and related fields. Time-dependent covariates frequently arise in practical studies that seek to examine the relationship between explanatory variables—such as biomarkers, clinical indicators, or environmental factors—and the time to a particular event, such as equipment failure, disease recurrence, or mortality. Conventional methodologies for censored quantile regression often focus on settings with independent censoring or rely heavily on longitudinal frameworks that treat repeated measurements and time-dependent factors in specific, constrained ways. By contrast, our approach embraces the natural variability of time-dependent covariates in a more flexible and comprehensive fashion, thus broadening the applicability of quantile regression to a wide spectrum of real-world challenges. A key novelty of our proposed framework lies in its ability to extend established methods to accommodate genuinely time-dependent predictors within quantile regression structures. This is accomplished by redefining quantiles to be dynamic over time, rather than statically calculated under a simplistic data assumption. In doing so, our work provides a fundamentally new perspective on how quantiles can be understood, analysed, and interpreted in the presence of right-censoring. Instead of relying on a conventional notion of quantiles that might be rendered inaccurate or incomplete when faced with time-dependent information, we propose a paradigm that integrates evolving covariate values into the quantile estimation procedure. This leads to a richer, more nuanced portrayal of the conditional distributions of failure times, capturing the complexity of how covariates’ effects may change or manifest at different points in the time horizon. Furthermore, we establish rigorous asymptotic properties for our recursive estimator, ensuring that practitioners can trust its theoretical soundness and reliability in handling varying types of censoring patterns. By proving consistency and other large-sample properties, we provide confidence that the parameter estimates generated by our approach will remain accurate and stable as sample sizes grow and as patterns of time dependence become more complex. This analytical foundation is complemented by a series of numerical studies, which illustrate the practicality and effectiveness of our proposal across a range of scenarios. These experimental evaluations not only showcase notable gains in estimation accuracy and interpretability, but also highlight the robustness of our method to different assumptions about censoring and data collection protocols. Overall, this paper contributes a powerful new tool to the methodological toolbox for survival analysis, expanding the frontiers of censored quantile regression and underscoring the importance of time-dependent models for uncovering intricate patterns in event-time data. By merging statistical theory with practical applications, our framework can benefit a variety of research domains, from clinical trials and epidemiological studies to engineering reliability and beyond. Another major publication entitled “Distributed censored quantile regression” presents a novel extension of censored quantile regression to a distributed computing environment, addressing the growing need for scalable methods that can handle massive datasets efficiently while maintaining rigorous statistical properties. In modern data-centric applications, it is increasingly common to encounter large-scale survival data, especially in biomedical, engineering, or financial studies. Traditional centralised estimation approaches often become infeasible when data volume and dimensionality exceed the limits of available memory and computational power in a single machine. By leveraging distributed architectures, our framework enables researchers to explore and analyse right-censored event-time data more effectively, without compromising on the theoretical guarantees that underscore robust inference. Our proposed method consists of two fundamental steps. First, we estimate both the Kaplan-Meier estimator and the model coefficients in parallel across multiple machines. This step allows the data to be divided among different computational nodes, thus alleviating memory constraints and reducing individual runtime per machine. Second, we aggregate local coefficient estimates into a unified global estimator through an efficient communication and synchronisation protocol. Critically, we study the upper limit on the order of the number of machines to ensure that the distributed estimator converges at a rate comparable to its oracle counterpart. This theoretical investigation confirms that, when the number of machines remains within the specified bound, the distributed estimator enjoys asymptotic properties akin to the centralised approach, thereby guaranteeing reliability and accuracy in large-sample settings. In addition to the core method, we explore two adaptations that broaden its applicability in different distributed scenarios. First, we introduce a communication-facilitated strategy, which enhances coordination among machines and reduces potential biases arising from the partitioning scheme. Second, we incorporate a nonparametric extension, allowing more flexible modeling of complex relationships in censored quantile regression settings. These systematic advances enable practitioners to select or combine strategies most appropriate for the specific nature of their data and computational landscape. The first objective of the proposal is hence satisfied also for the above two related projects. We demonstrate other results using numerical simulation and a real data illustration which makes us hopefully fulfil the objectives #2 and #3 of the proposal. The three objectives are also achieved for other two related papers Publications #4 and #5. Publication #3 presents a robust multi-period portfolio model that specifically addresses uncertainty in the correlation between assets. Using flexible spectral risk measures, including CVaR, to cater to diverse investor profiles, the model defines this ambiguity with data-driven bounds on the correlation matrix. The authors' key contributions include providing both a semi-analytical solution and developing a novel, modified Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (SDDP) algorithm to solve the problem. A significant finding is that correlation uncertainty leads to an optimal strategy of "anti-diversification," which the research shows is highly effective at protecting investments during financial crises, proving the model's practical value. Other projects, say Publications #6 and #8, also achieve the three objectives stated for portfolio optimisation and AI-based modelling for analysing football match events. All of these results are presented in regional/international conferences also. A book chapter was also prepared under the census period on estimating a new type of extreme value index (EVI) estimator. With regard to Publications #5, we wish to clarify that while these manuscripts were initially submitted before the grant period began, the subsequent revision process required substantial additional work that was partially supported by the current grant. As such, we considered it appropriate to acknowledge the grant's support, as it played a crucial role in bringing these publications to completion. In reference to Publication #6, we must address a typographical error in the Acknowledgment section, where the grant number was incorrectly listed as 14301921 rather than 14301920. Despite our efforts to contact the publisher for a correction, we were informed that such changes were not feasible at this stage. We deeply regret this inadvertent error and have implemented measures to prevent similar oversights in future publications.

14301920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301920.value: The main focus of this research project is to develop proper treatments for handling various issues related to censored quantile regression. Existing methods, although have been recognised as effective tools in modelling specific quantile level(s) of event time distribution given covariates, some of the technical issues remain unanswered. A novel and insightful idea in the literature reframes the conventional quantile regression check function framework into a martingle-based, counting process formulation (see Peng and Huang, 2008; JASA and Wang and Wang, 2009; JASA). While this idea intricately and naturally makes use of the conventional techniques in survival analysis, there was, however, to the best of our knowledge, no discussion on how the Time-dependent covariates can be properly handled under the said martingale framework. We (see Publications #2 and 7) have established computable inference procedures which achieve cases with (#2) and without (#7) local homogeneity assumption. Both works have been published/accepted for publications in reputable journals; see Section C for more details. Another main work developed for this project is Publication #1 in which it extends censored quantile regression to distributed computing. Data are split across machines, where each node independently computes Kaplan–Meier curves and regression coefficients; these local estimates are then aggregated. We derive an upper bound on the allowable number of machines that preserves the oracle convergence rate. Two refinements are added: a communication-enhanced variant à la Chen et al. (2019) and a non-parametric extension following Kong and Xia (2017). A cross-validation scheme is also proposed for hyper-parameter selection for right-censored data. This work is published at Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics. Other publications including Publications #4 and 5 discuss other various issues related to censored observations under the network context, non-parametric MLE consideration and a distributed setting, respectively. Some works on quantile-related risk management models are also published (see, e.g. #3 and #6). They appear in reputable journals and/or book series. All the aforementioned results are also presented in various regional/international conferences. References: Chen, X., Liu, W., and Zhang, Y. (2019), “Quantile Regression under Memory Constraint,” The Annals of Statistics, 47, 3244–3273. Kong, E., and Xia, Y. (2017), “Uniform Bahadur Representation for Nonparametric Censored Quantile Regression: A Redistribution-of-Mass Approach,” Econometric Theory, 33, 242–261. Peng, L.,and Huang, Y.(2008),“Survival Analysis with Quantile Regression Models,” Journal of the American Statistical Association, 103, 637–649.

14301920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301920.value: Although the methods proposed in this work perform well, they share an important limitation: none can analyse massive data streams that include time-varying covariates while maintaining the usual conditional-independence assumption between failure and censoring times. Existing procedures are batch-oriented and often rely on local homogeneity, rendering them unsuitable for true online implementation. In modern medical studies, subject characteristics routinely evolve over time and new records arrive continuously. An inference framework that can incorporate such time-dependent covariates in an online fashion would greatly enlarge the practical reach of censored-data models. The need is especially acute in the big-data era, where the volume of information generated by connected IoT devices and stored in contemporary systems (e.g., NoSQL databases) is rapidly escalating. Developing statistically efficient online estimators under these conditions therefore represents a promising research direction. Preliminary simulations and theoretical analyses have already begun to lay the necessary foundation.

14301920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301920.value: Traditionally, distributions are summarized with the mean or median, but a richer picture emerges when we model their quantiles directly with quantile regression. Besides offering a fuller description, quantile-regression estimates are notably robust to outliers in the response variable. These advantages make the technique especially attractive for applied modelling. In medical research, however, time-to-event outcomes are often censored, and the current censored-quantile-regression literature is still limited. Existing approaches may require restrictive conditions in order to handle time-dependent covariates. The extensions proposed in this project address those gaps, turning censored quantile regression into a more reliable and broadly applicable tool. The resulting methodology should benefit a wide range of practitioners who need fast, accurate quantile estimates for censored survival data.

14302120.label: Realisation of objectives
14302120.value: There are three objectives in this project and the details of the realization to each objective are as follows: 1. To synthesize and characterize ligand-functionalized nanoparticles. A series of gold (Au) nanoparticles with varying sizes and surface characteristics were synthesized and characterized using zeta-potential measurements, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. Additionally, monodisperse polystyrene (PS) particles coated with silica were synthesized through dispersion polymerization. These PS-silica hybrid particles were subsequently modified with (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) to introduce amine functional groups, followed by re-dispersion in N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS)-ester labeled fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) to coat the hybrid surface with FITC biomolecules. We also demonstrated a flexible method for preparing polystyrene/silica nanocomposite particles by subjecting commercially available non-functionalized silica nanoparticles to Pickering emulsion polymerization. All synthesized particles were utilized as probes to investigate particle-surface interactions by tracking the settling of nano/microparticles near the solution surface using total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) integrated with video microscopy (VM) under non-equilibrium conditions. 2. To extend our established TIRM-VM technique to allow the characterization of ligand functionalized nanoparticles interacting with functional surfaces in physiological media. While most studies on PEG SAMs focus on the interactions between biomolecules and substrates, there are few investigations into the direct interactions between fluorophores and organosilane SAMs. We conducted a study to clarify the interactions between fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) and PEG SAMs in solutions with varying ionic strengths using TIRM-VM. In low ionic strength solutions, we observed long-range attractions between FITC-modified polystyrene-silica particles and PEG SAM-grafted substrates, despite both having an ensemble-averaged negative charge. This attraction may be attributed to their nonuniformly charged surfaces. At high ionic strength, we measured van der Waals attraction at short distances, as electrostatic interactions were completely screened. Additionally, we investigated the structure-rheology relationships of soft colloidal particles near wall regions using TIRM-VM. This technique allowed us to assess the specific contribution of interfacial hydrophilic-hydrophobic interactions to the structural relaxation dynamics of certain soft particles. We found significant differences in rheological behavior and structural heterogeneity between bulk and near-wall scenarios, indicating that the presence of a wall or interface influences the local microstructure and cooperative motion of soft particles, revealing divergent interfacial relaxation behaviors depending on wettability. Our results also illustrate how structural relaxation heterogeneity evolves in response to particle volume fraction and interfacial wettability. We anticipate that our evanescent-field speckle imaging approach can be applied to other soft and dense colloidal gel systems, including those experiencing physical aging and out-of-equilibrium dynamics. 3. To apply the extended techniques to the measurement of ligand-functionalized nanoparticles interacting with cell membranes. In this project, we employed a unique surface-sensitive technique, evanescent-light scattering from total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM), to investigate how surface properties influence the relaxation behavior, aging process, and dynamic heterogeneity of NP–fibrinogen (NP–FIB) aggregates at interfaces. The spatiotemporal characteristics of relaxation were analyzed using a density-fluctuation autocorrelation function (δACF) derived from interfacial speckle images. Our findings revealed that the relaxation dynamics exhibit a two-stage decay pattern (fast and slow modes), which corresponds to the dual timescale relaxation of coronated NPs and aggregates. Notably, the fast relaxation mode showed a stretched exponential time dependence for weakly bound proteins on NPs or clusters, while strongly connected NPs or clusters demonstrated a slow mode with a compressed exponential time dependence. This indicates that both types of processes can coexist in NP–protein aggregates, a behavior we believe reflects interfacial or near-wall effects. The insights gained from this near-surface study complement existing bulk research on NP–protein adsorption and aggregation, benefiting both in vitro and in vivo assessments of novel antitumor targeted nanomedicines and drug delivery systems for cardiovascular therapies.

14302120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302120.value: This research project has been successfully completed by our team. We synthesized a series of engineered nanoparticles to serve as probes for measuring particle–surface interactions by tracking the behavior of nano/microparticles near the surface of a solution using total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) integrated with video microscopy (VM). We utilized TIRM-VM to directly measure the interactions between fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) and self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), shedding light on the interactions between fluorophores and organosilane SAMs, which have been scarcely reported. Additionally, TIRM-VM was employed to investigate how surface properties influence the relaxation behavior, aging process, and dynamic heterogeneity of nanoparticle–fibrinogen (NP–FIB) aggregates at interfaces. We examined the relaxation dynamics of coronated or engineered nanoparticles and aggregates near surfaces, with findings that could benefit both in vitro and in vivo evaluations of novel antitumor targeted nanomedicines. Furthermore, we explored intracellular microrheology in living cytoplasm using TIRM-VM. Our studies demonstrated solid-like behavior in living cells at low frequencies, characterized by a weak power-law dependence. However, providing direct evidence for this behavior necessitates more in-depth observations of the intracellular reorganization of the meshwork and fluid in living cytoplasm. This project has produced 9 peer-reviewed papers in the fields of colloid, surface chemistry, and materials science, and the results have been presented at several international and regional conferences. The project also trained one PhD student and two postdoctoral researchers. Dr. Wu Jiahao, who graduated, has joined the global chemical company BASF in Shanghai, while Dr. Liu Wei is currently an Associate Professor at Jiangnan University, and Dr. Liu Yang holds the position of Associate Professor at Sichuan University.

14302120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302120.value: In the future, we plan to enhance the TIRM-VM setup by implementing a feedback loop that can automatically manipulate the probe particles at a constant amplitude of oscillation. We are also considering integrating this technique with optical tweezers to selectively trap specific probes when solution conditions change. Additionally, we may introduce a microfluidic device to optimize the current flowing cell in our TIRM-VM setup, which would help conserve valuable biological samples. Moreover, combining fluorescent imaging or super-resolution microscopy will enable us to investigate ultrafast dynamics and complex microstructures in biological materials and their adjacent surfaces. With these modifications, our TIRM-VM will be capable of measuring the sticking processes of colloidal particles near surfaces, as well as grafted interfaces with polymers or proteins. We anticipate that our single-particle TIRM-VM will have significant potential for revealing the dynamics of soft matter at interfaces.

14302120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302120.value: With the rapid advancement of nanotechnology, nanoparticles are increasingly being utilized not only in various industrial products but also in biomedical applications, including drug delivery and gene therapy. Despite recent manufacturing innovations that allow for the synthesis of diverse nanoparticles with controlled composition, size, shape, and surface functionalization, there is still limited understanding of the diffusion dynamics of nanoparticles near lipid membranes prior to the endocytosis process. Furthermore, the influence of weak colloidal interactions between lipid membranes and nanoparticles or nanocarriers on targeting remains poorly explored. In this project, we developed a novel strategy to directly measure particle-surface interactions by tracking the behavior of nanoparticles or microparticles near the surface of a solution using total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) integrated with video microscopy (VM). We quantified the extremely weak interactions between fluorophores and organosilane self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), as well as between nanoparticles and proteins, to investigate how surface properties affect the relaxation behavior, aging process, and dynamic heterogeneity of nanoparticles or nanocarriers as they approach the interface or cell membrane. This project establishes a powerful technique for characterizing nanoparticle-surface interactions and contributes valuable insights into designing functional nanocargoes for optimal cell targeting and drug delivery.

14302220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302220.value: The mean residual life (MRL) function measures the remaining life expectancy of a subject who has survived up to a certain time point. As a useful alternative to the hazard-based approach, the MRL model, which directly examines how potential covariates affect the MRL function, is widely applied in biomedical sciences, industrial reliability research, and actuarial studies. The class of transformation MRL (TMRL) models is a general framework that involves several commonly used MRL models as special cases. It also provides great flexibility and capability in modeling covariate effects in various forms. However, the existing TMRL models seldom consider time-varying covariates and nonlinear covariate effects. Furthermore, the existing inverse probability censoring weighting (IPCW) approach to TMRL models requires either assuming the independence of censoring time from covariates or modeling the dependence of censoring time on covariates. Such requirement is restrictive when the independence assumption is untrue. Moreover, the model might suffer from information loss when the censoring mechanism is misspecified. These limitations narrow the applicability of TMRL models to real-world problems and might disable the incorporation of complex data structures. Therefore, coping with possibly time-varying covariates and/or nonlinear covariate effects in the context of TMRL models and developing new inference methods that can be exempted from the preceding restriction are necessary. This study aims to investigate extended TMRL (ETMRL) models that provide a new framework to accommodate time-varying covariates, nonlinear covariate effects, and other complex data structures in a flexible manner. Moreover, a novel counting process-based estimating equation approach, which neither assumes independence between the censoring time and covariates nor models the conditional censoring distribution based on the covariates, is proposed for ETMRL models. In contrast to the existing IPCW method that requires estimating/modeling the censoring distribution, the proposed approach only requires conditional independence between the survival and censoring times given covariates, but allows the censoring distribution to be unspecified. We develop easy-to-implement algorithms for parameter estimation and establish the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Moreover, ETMRL models under the presence of length-biased data, missing covariates, and longitudinal latent variables, are considered. In addition to estimation, other relevant statistical inferences, such as model/variable selection and model checking/diagnostics, are investigated. Efficient and user-friendly computer programs are developed for the implementation of the proposed methods. These computer programs will be made freely available for practitioners. The developed methodologies are applied to real problems in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

14302220.label: Realisation of objectives
14302220.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. We have developed ETMRL models that incorporate time-varying covariates and nonlinear covariate effects and established a counting process-based estimating equation approach. Valuable extensions and multiple variants of the proposed models have also been considered. The objective in Item 1 of Section 5.2 related to the model establishment is fully achieved. 2. We have developed novel and sound statistical methods to analyze ETMRL models with various types of data. Multiple comprehensive statistical methods for parameter estimation and model/variable selection are developed, and the related asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators are investigated. The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 related to inference methodology are fully accomplished. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs for producing accurate results and made these programs freely available on the Internet for general use. We utilize freely available software, such as R, MATLAB, C++, and Python, to ensure the code is user-friendly. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 related to computer programs are fully achieved. 4. We have applied the developed methodologies in analyzing real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The real-life applications include but are not limited to (1) type 2 diabetes and its complications data collected by the Prince of Wales Hospital at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, (2) various cancer data (Items 2, 16, 19, and 20 in Section 8), (3) general public health (Items 5, 6, 10, 13, and 18 in Section 8), (4) Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data (Items 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 22, 23, and 25 in Section 8), (5) medical cost study of chronic heart failure patients (Item 11), (6) microarray gene expression data (Item 21 in Section 8), (7) a corporate default study in Mainland China (Item 7 in Section 8), and (8) HIV data from AIDS Clinical Trail (Item 24 in Section 8). The objectives in Item 4 of Section 5.2 related to applications are fully achieved.

14302220.value: Our main findings and research outcomes are represented by 25 research papers (see Research Outputs in Section 8 of Part C). Specifically, 1. We have developed ETMRL models that incorporate time-varying covariates and nonlinear covariate effects and established various estimation methods, including a counting process-based estimating equation approach, hybrid approaches combining EM and estimating equation or EM and nonparametric maximal likelihood procedures, and Bayesian approach. Asymptotic properties are established for the proposed methods. Please refer to Items 1, 2, 5, 10, 11, 17, 18, and 19 in Section 8. In addition, we have developed several valuable extensions of the proposed model to address other complex research settings, accommodating multivariate, longitudinal, functional, imaging, interval-censored, and/or recurrent event data. Please refer to Items 3, 7, 8, 9, 13, 15, 16, 22, 23, and 25 in Section 8. Moreover, we have developed parametric and nonparametric Bayesian approaches to conduct causal mediation analysis with survival outcomes. Please refer to Items 12, 20, and 24. 2. We have developed several comprehensive statistical methods for parameter estimation and variable selection and investigated the related asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Please refer to Items 1, 2, 4, 6-11, and 17-21 in Section 8. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs and published the corresponding codes in papers or on freely accessible websites for general use. 4. We have applied the developed methodologies in analyzing real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and other settings. The real-life applications include but are not limited to (1) type 2 diabetes and its complications data collected by the Prince of Wales Hospital at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Items 1, 3, 4, and 15 in Section 8), (2) various cancer data (Items 2, 16, 19, and 20 in Section 8), (3) general public health (Items 5, 6, 10, 13, and 18 in Section 8), (4) Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data (Items 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 22, 23, and 25 in Section 8), (5) medical cost study of chronic heart failure patients (Item 11), (6) microarray gene expression data (Item 21 in Section 8), (7) a corporate default study in Mainland China (Item 7 in Section 8), and (8) HIV data from AIDS Clinical Trail (Item 24 in Section 8). Note: In Items 4 to 8 of Part C (Research Output), I made typos in acknowledging the GRF grant 14302222. I meant 14302220; I don't have other grants with the number 14302222. I sincerely apologize for my carelessness.

14302220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302220.value: The models considered in this project can be extended to accommodate the presence of competing risks and block-wise missingness. Moreover, incorporating machine learning techniques, such as deep neural networks, federated learning, and transfer learning, is particularly interesting and warrants further investigation. We will consider the above potential topics for future development.

14302220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302220.value: Mean residual life (MRL) models directly examine how potential covariates affect the MRL function. Due to their straightforward interpretations in terms of remaining life expectancy regarding the potential benefits of a treatment or drug, MRL models have attracted considerable attention from biomedical science, reliability research, actuarial studies, and social-economic theories. Existing studies on MRL models rely on strong assumptions and seldom consider time-varying and nonlinear covariate effects, thereby limiting their applicability to complex data structures. Therefore, coping with possibly time-varying covariates and/or nonlinear covariate effects in the context of MRL models and developing new inference methods that can be exempted from the preceding restriction are necessary. The methods developed in this project have addressed challenging issues and filled the gap in survival analysis with complex data structures. The applications of the developed methodologies have yielded new insights into problems in various research areas. A total of 25 papers in international journals, such as Biometrics, AOAS, JCGS, Statistica Sinica, JRSSC, The American Statistician, Bayesian Analysis, Electronic Journal of Statistics, Statistics in Medicine, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, and Structural Equation Modeling, represent the primary outputs. Some extensions of the proposed methods beyond the project objectives have also been considered.

14302320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302320.value: 利用鑽石機械及熱傳感技術研究聚合物薄膜的玻璃化轉變

14302320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302320.value: Mechanical and thermal properties of polymer ultrathin films are important in many applications such as photolithography, organic semiconductors, biomedical devices, and electronic packing. Polymer films transfer from the glassy phase to the rubbery phase while the temperature increases across the glass transition temperature. As results of the confinement effect in decreasing the film thickness to nanoscale, it has been observed that the elastic modulus of free-standing polymer films decreases in the glassy phase due to the highly mobile free surfaces, accompanying with an unexpected stiffness in the rubbery phase. Meanwhile, the confinement effects have been also predicted in reducing the thermal conductivity of the polymer thin films. However, the in-plane thermal properties of the polymer films and their relation to the stiffness need further exploration. Mechanical properties of polymer thin films are usually measured with large scale deformation where the information of cross-plane heterogeneity in nanoscale is missed. In contrast, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based nanoindentation and scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) techniques are widely applied to study the mechanical and thermal properties in nanoscale. However, only the local responses are obtained which limits the mechanical analysis by the choice of contact models and prohibits the in-plane thermal analysis. Previously we developed a novel method, non-locally sensed the surface deformation upon an AFM nanoindentation by the rotation of attached nanodiamonds (NDs) containing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. Meanwhile, the thermal response of the NV centers makes the attached NDs to be sensitive in-situ thermometers. We plan to use the developed diamond sensing techniques to study the mechanical and thermal properties of polymer thin films. The films will be suspended on template with holes to eliminate the substrate effect. The non-local deformation and temperature distribution of the film induced by the thermal AFM tip indentation will be measured by simultaneously sensing the rotations and the temperature of the attached NDs via wide-field-AFM correlation microscopy. Non-local mechanical and thermal responses of the polymer films upon thermal AFM indentation can be obtained, which can be used to reveal the elastic moduli of the multi-layer structure and the in-plane thermal conductivity, respectively. Relation between the mechanical and thermal properties based on the polymer chains conformation in the ultrathin films can be studied across the glass transition temperature. The investigation not only is important in applications but also gives insight into the nature of vitrification. 隨著聚合物薄膜在光刻、有機半導體、生物醫學設備和電子封裝等領域的廣泛應用，對其力學和熱學性質的研究變得越來越重要。 聚合物薄膜會在溫度升高到玻璃化轉變溫度時從玻璃態轉變到高彈態。當聚合物薄膜的厚度降低到納米級，空間受限效應會影響聚合物薄膜的力學性能：在玻璃態中，薄膜表面會出現分子運動性較高的區域並使薄膜的硬度下降；在高彈態中，空間受限效應反而會增強薄膜的硬度。 空間受限效應同時也會降低聚合物薄膜的熱導率。 然而，聚合物薄膜的熱學和力學性能及其之間的關係仍需要進一步研究。 聚合物薄膜的力學性能通常會透過大尺度的受力形變來測量，這些測量並不能反映薄膜在納米尺度下的多層結構。在納米尺度下，材料的力學和熱學性能一般可以利用原子力顯微鏡（AFM）中的納米壓痕技術和熱掃描顯微鏡來研究。但這兩種技術只能測量探針下材料的局域響應，局限了對材料力學和熱學性能的進一步分析。 我們早前開發了一種用於測量納米壓痕實驗中材料非局域形變的新方法。實驗中，我們在材料表面附上一些含有氮空位色心的納米鑽石。利用鑽石傳感技術測量這些納米鑽石的轉動和温度，我們便可同時得到材料表面的形變和温度分佈。在本項目中，我們將使用上述鑽石傳感技術來研究聚合物薄膜的力學和熱學性能。 為了消除襯底對薄膜的影響，我們會將薄膜平舖在帶有圓孔的模板上。 利用集成AFM-寬場光學顯微鏡和鑽石傳感技術，我們可以得到由高溫AFM探針按壓薄膜導致的薄膜形變和溫度分布。這些非局域的力學和熱學響應可以分別用於揭示薄膜的層狀結構和面內熱導率。 利用這些信息，我們可以研究空間受限的聚合物在玻璃化轉變時的力學和熱學性能及其之間的關係。本項研究不僅對聚合物材料的應用提供重要信息，還可以為探索聚合物玻璃化的本質帶來新的思路。

14302420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302420.value: 底棲微藻通常被認為是熱帶紅樹林生態系统中可以忽略的一部分。有限的光照條件限制了底棲微藻的生長，同時，有限的研究方法也導致了人們對底栖微藻群落結構和營養功能的認識不足。紅樹林中的底棲微藻很難被特徵化，因為它們個體很小，而且微藻细胞很難從沉積物中分離出來。有機碎屑的滲雜降低了同位素分析的效用，底棲微藻較小的個體（大部是< 50微米的殼縫羽紋硅藻和藍綠藻）也增加了测定初級生產力的困難度。紅樹林中有限的光照條件暗示了底棲微藻對生態系統生產力的貢獻可能非常有限。然而，近期使用穩定同位素技術研究營養關係的相關結果表明，紅樹林樹葉和動物之間的分餾因子高達約+5‰，而一般認為這些動物(例如相手蟹)主要以食用紅樹樹葉為生。雖然可有不同的推論，較高的分餾因子也可被解釋為這些動物也依賴其它食物來源，例如底棲微藻。與紅樹林樹葉相比，底棲微藻碳13同位素的含量較高。然而，該解釋尚未被證明。近年來有限的研究數據表明紅樹林沉積物可能支持着豐富的底棲微藻群落，而這些群落則明顯不同於數據較多，在潮間光灘帶生長的底棲微藻群落。底棲微藻的功能重要性也包括它們的功能與一些重要但缺少數據的碳通量(特别是孔隙水中溶解性無機碳動態變化及泥-空氣-水接合面的二氧化碳排放)的相藕合。然而這些方面都普遍缺乏相關研究。因此，我們假設紅樹林底棲微藻群落：（1）其結構和功能與在光線充足條件下生長的底棲微藻明顯不同；（2）具有很高的生產力；（3）是紅樹林中消費者的重要食物來源；及（4）在調節紅樹林沉積物可溶解無機碳動態變化和二氧化碳的循環中發揮着重要的作用。我們將使用多種研究方法并結合穩定同位素技術，開展以下工作：（1）研究在各種環境條件下熱帶紅樹林底棲微藻的群落特徵；（2）評估底棲微藻的豐富度和生產力；（3）揭示底棲微藻對紅樹林消費者的重要性和其作為生態系統碳庫的重要性；（4）提出底棲微藻在可溶解無機碳動態變化和沉積物二氧化碳排放過程中的作用。我們的研究結果將會從根本上修正以往對紅樹林碳預算和營養結構的認知。

14302420.label: Realisation of objectives
14302420.value: Objective 1 We conducted an assessment of the composition of the MPB assemblages at two contrasting mangrove forests, namely Mai Po (MP) with silty substrate and brackish influence and Ting Kok (TK) with sandy substrate and oceanic influence, over a year. Ten samples were collected from the mangrove forests and adjoining unvegetated tidal flat at each of the two study sites over nine occasions in summer (June–September 2021), and five occasions in winter (December 2021–March 2022). MPB was extracted using the density separation method. The MPB composition experiment was conducted by viewing the samples contained in a Sedgewick rafter cell at 400X under a phase-contrast microscope (Primovert Compact Inverted Microscope, ZEISS, Germany). The MPB cells were identified to genus level as much as possible. The MPB taxonomic richness (at genus level) of each sample was measured using the method of rarefaction and extrapolation with Hill numbers. The composition of MPB community was characterized and compared among habitats, sites and seasons. Objective 2 We carried out an assessment of the abundance of MPB in the two contrasting mangroves by sampling the top sediments in both the mangrove forests and adjoining tidal flats in the summer and winter over one year. The abundance of MBP was determined by measuring the concentration of chlorophyll a as a proxy. Sediment samples were placed in acetone and the absorbance of the supernatant after centrifugation was measured at three different wavelengths with a spectrophotometer. In addition, the photosynthetic performance of MPB was measured using a chlorophyll fluorometer. The productivity measurements were made for MPB samples collected from TK one day in summer (July 2022) and one day in winter (February 2023). On each occasion, MPB were collected randomly, at least 5 m apart, from the mangrove forest and tidal flat during low tide in the morning, and processed immediately in the laboratory to avoid potential alteration to the MPB’s photosynthetic performance. The light response parameters were determined and then compared among habitats and seasons. Objective 3 We conducted a series of experiments to improve the assessment of the potential trophic contribution of MPB to the mangrove food web. We carried out a feeding experiment using the pulmonate slug, a common inhabitant of the local mangrove forest floor and a presumed specialist grazer, to estimate the MPB-specific trophic discrimination factor. We fed the slug with purified MPB and detritus, and monitored the changes in stable isotope values of the slugs over nine weeks. Another similar batch of experiment was conducted using the Metaplax varunid crab. In addition, we collected functionally important benthic animals from the mangrove forests for natural abundance analysis. Furthermore, we carried out mesocosm experiments using isotope (13C and 15N, separately in two treatments) enriched MPB, with mangrove leaves labelled using the other isotope in the same treatment to investigate the role of mangrove MPB in the nutrition of dominant sesarmid crabs. We kept the sesarmid crab Parasesarma affine in the mesocosms with MPB or leaves for four weeks and then sacrificed them for the measurement of stable isotope values (delta 13C and 15N) to confirm if MPB was a nitrogen source and leaf was a carbon source. We also carried out feeding experiments using another crab species Neosarmatium smithi with four types of foods to test for opportunistic consumption of high0quality foods, and with 15N-enriched atmosphere and leaves to test if the crabs receive nitrogen supplement from nitrogen-fixing microbes. Objective 4 We used paired light-dark domes to measure the MPB productivity and investigate the influence of MPB on sediment carbon dioxide emissions. Paired light and dark domes were set up on undisturbed sediment surfaces at five replicate locations from each of the three habitat types at MP and TK during daylight hours at low tide. The carbon dioxide concentrations inside the chamber headspace were monitored over the chamber deployment period for subsequent carbon dioxide flux calculation. Environmental and biological variables were monitored at each location simultaneously. The difference in sediment carbon dioxide flux between the light and dark domes was taken as the net photosynthetic capacity of the MPB. Moreover, we carried out an in-situ isotopic enrichment experiment at MP and TK to investigate the coupling between MPB and porewater dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) dynamics. 13-C enriched sodium bicarbonate was added to ten small vertical cavities made in the sediment just after the substrate was exposed during an ebb tide. Label uptake by the MPB was then assessed using surface sediment samples collected at 5 cm depth at half-hourly intervals over two hours. Simultaneously, we used dark domes to measure the carbon dioxide concentration and isotopic values of headspace air at half-hourly intervals over two hours at five enriched cavities and five adjacent non-enriched areas to estimate the contribution of MBP to the sediment-atmosphere carbon dioxide emission. Furthermore, we carried out an enrichment mesocosm experiment to assess the coupling between MPB, mangroves, and mangrove-derived nutrients. A factorial design was adopted with three treatments, namely, (1) enrichment (dual 13C and 15N labelling using urea; unenriched urea); (2) seedling density (4 or 8 seedlings per mecosom); and (3) enrichment time (at 10-day intervals over 30 days). The concentrations of carbon and nitrogen in MPB, DIC and total nitrogen concentrations in porewater, as well as the isotopic values of MPB, porewater DIC, and mangrove leaves, roots and sediments were measured.

14302420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302420.value: The results of this study suggested that microphytobenthos in the mangroves were abundant and different from that in the tidal flat. As reported in our Loo et al. (2024) paper, the MPB abundance in the mangroves was not significantly lower than that in the tidal flats throughout the year. The estimated median number of MPB genera in the mangrove and tidal flat sediments ranged between 23 and 45, with no difference in MPB genus richness across all sites and habitats. Yet, significant differences in MPB genus composition were found among all habitats, sites, seasons and their interactions, with Pinnulara, Navicula, and Nitzschia being the typifying genera. About 23% of the variance in MPB assemblages among sampling groups could be explained by a combination of porewater salinity, porewater temperature, irradiation level, porewater pH, and surface soil temperature in decreasing order of contribution. Moreover, we found that the tidal flat MPB showed higher light response parameters than the mangrove MPB, thereby exhibiting higher light acclimation. In general, MPB showed higher photosynthetic capacities in summer than in winter, with a taller and wider rapid light curve of MPB in the warmer and wetter season. The results of our mesocosm feeding experiments showed that for crab species spending most of their time outside burrows during the low tide (e.g. Parasesarma affine), the nitrogen-rich MPB in surface sediment could serve as an important nitrogen source while the mangrove leaves would serve as a key carbon source, as reported in our Gao & Lee (2022) paper. On the other hand, for crab species that spend most of their time inside burrows (e.g. Neosarmatium smithi), they did not feed on MPB but could meet their nitrogen requirements through consumption of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria, or other seasonally available higher-quality food items such as calyx. The results of our isotopic enrichment experiments showed that there was a flow pathway of MPB nutrient acquisition via the leaf-root-porewater-MPB continuum. There was a significant relationship between δ13C of MPB and porewater DIC concentrations as well as δ13C-DIC. Also, the component 13C and/or 15N of MPB decreased in the sequence of leaves, roots, sediments, porewater DIC and MPB in the enriched mesocosms, suggesting the transfer of nutrients from mangrove leaves to roots, with subsequent exudation in porewater and assimilation by MPB. Overall, the findings of this study enhanced our scientific understanding of the ecological and biogeochemical role of MPB in mangrove ecosystems.

14302420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302420.value: In this study, we showed that MPB was abundant and played a key role in mediating carbon fluxes in tropical mangrove ecosystems based on the work done in two contrasting mangrove forests with difference substrate and water salinity. However, future work should be done to cover more mangrove sites spanning across different latitudes and environmental conditions for a more comprehensive assessment of the ecological and biogeochemical role of mangrove MPB. Through mesocosm experiments, we identified a new pathway of the leaf-root-porewater-MPB continuum by which MPB could obtain carbon and nitrogen. Further modelling studies should try to incorporate this pathway in the biogeochemical models to provide a more realistic estimation of carbon and nitrogen dynamics in mangroves.

14302420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302420.value: This project aims to characterize the abundance, community composition, and productivity of microphytobenthos (MPB) in the tropical mangrove ecosystems, and assess the trophic and biogeochemical roles of MPB. Our results showed that the abundance of MPB in the mangrove forests was not lower than that in the open tidal flats. While sediments in the mangroves had an equally rich MPB assemblage as those in the adjacent tidal flats, the MPB genus composition was different across all habitats, sites and seasons in response to changing environmental conditions. MPB were dominated by pennate diatoms at all sites, while cyanobacteria were common in the estuarine site. MPB generally showed higher photosynthetic capacities in summer, and it showed a higher light acclimation in the tidal flats than in the mangrove forests. The results of our mesocosm feeding experiments showed that MPB could serve as an important nitrogen source for crab species spending most of their time outside burrows during low tides, but not for those that spend most of their time inside burrows. Moreover, we found a tight coupling between mangrove-derived carbon and MPB. Overall, our findings highlighted the key biogeochemical role of MPB in mangroves, which should not be overlooked in future researches.

14302620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302620.value: Mathematical models, formulated as coupled system of nonlinear partial differential equations, are widely used to describe the underlying physical process in science and engineering disciplines. These large-scale nonlinear systems are of multiscale and multi-physics nature and efficient numerical simulations of these complex systems are challenging. Multiscale methods is a useful class of techniques in obtaining efficient approximations, which use a significantly reduced computational cost by constructing suitable coarse scale models. Due to the high heterogeneity and nonlinearity, some nonlinear multiscale techniques are necessary. There are some existing nonlinear multiscale methods based on nonlinear numerical homogenization. However, these methods have only limited accuracy for practical applications. Moreover, the numerical homogenized systems are very expensive to compute. Thus, there is a need to develop a systematic framework to formulate nonlinear multiscale models that are accurate and are efficient to compute. In this project, we propose a new mathematical framework to learn computational multiscale models using deep neural networks. The proposed research are motivated by the fact that learning computational models require model reduction as it allows a more robust learning process. Furthermore, coarse scale models for complex nonlinear multiscale problems require nonlocal and multicontinua approaches. To formulate the required multiscale model, a lot of local problems defined on oversampled regions are needed, and these local solutions will be used together with suitable global couplings. However, these local computations are expensive and, instead, we will develop deep learning algorithms to learn the macroscopic parameters in these multiscale models. In addition, the coarse scale variables in our multiscale model have physical meaning, and the proposed techniques are therefore capable of incorporating available observed data in order to obtain data-driven upscaling models. Our methodology is general, and we can also use adaptive online technique to perform online learning during the online simulation process in order to refine the multiscale model beyond the offline stage. The proposed research provides a novel framework for learning multiscale model for complex nonlinear multiscale systems without expensive local computations. The methodology has a wide range of applications in mathematical sciences and engineering applications, where nonlinear multiscale and multi-physics models are involved. We expect both the academia and the industry will benefit from the proposed techniques in their research and applications. 公式化為非線性偏微分方程耦合系統的數學模型被廣泛用於描述科學和工程學科的基礎物理過程。這些大規模的非線性系統具有多尺度和多物理性質，並且對這些複雜系統的有效數值模擬具有挑戰性。多尺度方法是獲得有效逼近的一類有用的技術，該方法通過構建合適的粗尺度模型來顯著降低計算成本。由於高度的異質性和非線性，一些非線性多尺度技術是必需的。現有一些基於非線性數值均化的非線性多尺度方法。但是，這些方法對於實際應用僅具有有限的準確性。而且，數值均化系統的計算非常昂貴。因此，需要開發一種系統的框架來製定準確且有效地計算的非線性多尺度模型。 在此項目中，我們提出了一個新的數學框架，以使用深度神經網絡學習計算多尺度模型。提議的研究的動機是，學習計算模型需要模型簡化，因為它允許更強大的學習過程。此外，複雜非線性多尺度問題的粗尺度模型需要非局部和多連續性方法。為了製定所需的多尺度模型，需要在過採樣區域定義許多局部問題，並將這些局部解與合適的全局耦合一起使用。但是，這些局部計算非常昂貴，因此，我們將開發深度學習算法來學習這些多尺度模型中的宏觀參數。另外，我們的多尺度模型中的粗尺度變量具有物理意義，因此，所提出的技術能夠合併可用的觀測數據，以便獲得數據驅動的尺度放大模型。我們的方法是通用的，並且我們還可以使用自適應在線技術在在線仿真過程中執行在線學習，以便在離線階段之外完善多尺度模型。 所提出的研究提供了一種新穎的框架，用於學習複雜的非線性多尺度系統的多尺度模型，而無需進行昂貴的局部計算。 該方法在涉及非線性多尺度和多物理場模型的數學科學和工程應用中具有廣泛的應用。 我們希望學術界和行業都將從提議的技術的研究和應用中受益。

14302620.label: Realisation of objectives
14302620.value: All the objectives have been achieved successfully. First of all, we have developed a new nonlinear multiscale method, which is called the nonlinear nonlocal upscaling method, and applied to some complex nonlinear multiscale problems such as multiscale transport equations and multiscale convection-diffusion equations. Secondly, in the construction of these upscaling models, one needs to compute some model parameters, which are very expensive to compute due to nonlinear nature of the problem and multiscale nature of the coefficients. In order to address this challenge, we have developed a machine learning approach to learn these unknown model parameters. Our method is based on some supervised learning techniques and deep neural networks. In order to incorporate real data, our method’s design allow the coupling of both simulated and real data. This gives a practical method for realistic simulations. Finally, we have developed successfully a new data-driven method for modeling of complex multiscale problems.

14302620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302620.value: In this project, the nonlinear upscaling method developed is inspired by the general framework, called Nonlinear Nonlocal Multi-continua Upscaling (NLNLMC). This framework originates from the Constraint Energy Minimizing Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (CEM-GMsFEM), and continued with the Nonlocal Multi-continua Upscaling (NLMC). The CEM-GMsFEM involves solving several spectral problem, and produce localizable multiscale basis functions even with the presence of highly heterogeneous and high contrast media. The key idea hinges on devising of an auxiliary space and the construction of the basis functions arising from the energy minimization principles. The basis functions are constructed by solving problems on some oversampling regions. One disadvantage of the method is the lack of physical meaning in the degrees of freedoms. NLMC mainly follows from CEM-GMsFEM framework, with a modification that the multiscale basis functions are constructed that the degrees of freedoms represent the mean of the solutions. Therefore, the resulting coarse scale equation gives a relation between the cell averages and the solutions on the coarse grid, and we give an analysis of the convergence that is independent on the high contrast medium is the oversampling domain is large enough. Both CEM-GMsFEM and NLMC methods are dealing with linear multiscale problems, which works well in their respective settings. However, the basis functions constructed in both CEM-GMsFEM and the NLMC method is only applicable to linear problems. As a result, basis functions are not constructed under the new framework, and different local problems with augmented continuity is constructed instead. In general, the NLNLMC framework has three important methodological ingredients, macroscopic variables, local downscaling functions, and combination of global downscaling functions to solve global coarse scale equation. The macroscopic variables stay the same in the use of cell averages. Next, the local problems will be constructed on some oversampling regions in the fine grid to recover some fine scale properties, using the cell averages as the input. The oversampling domains will enhance the continuity between consecutive local regions. After computing the local problems, the solutions are then grouped together to obtain a global downscaling function. At last, the downscaling function is used to solve the problem on a coarse grid using some coarse grid solver. The resulting scheme is a coarse scale solver that relates the macroscopic variables. We have shown the development of this NLNLMC can be combined with machine learning to give a practical simulation tools for science.

14302620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302620.value: The results in this project have solved some of the problems arising in the development of mathematical models for practical simulations. There are certainly rooms for further developments. For example, the results of this project provide foundation for the development of more advanced learning techniques for complex models such as multiphase flow and atmospheric models. In particular, the techniques developed in this project can be used and extended to these more complex models, and provide an efficient and accurate simulation models for these applications.

14302620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302620.value: In this project, we have developed machine learning techniques to construct computational models for complex systems. For realistic applications, traditional methods can fail due to lack of computational power or lack of knowledge of the real model. By using multiscale techniques, we can learn the unknown parameters in the unknown model, so that simulations become possible. Due to the large amount of degrees of freedom, one needs some type of multiscale methods to reduce the model complexity. It is also the outcome of this project that the developed methods in this project can address this issue by reducing significantly the amount of computational demands.

14302920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302920.value: Image recovery refers to the procedure of building clear and sharp image from degraded observation corrupted by noise and blur. This is extremely important for further image analysis and understanding, and it has many scientific, engineering, and medical applications. For instance, the health condition of a patient can be better estimated if the quality of the computed tomography images is enhanced dramatically. As there are various types of images contaminated by different types of blurs and noises, image recovery remains a challenging task. For many important applications, the celebrated variational method often leads to a non-convex programming which is notoriously difficult to handle. The classical algorithm for non-convex problems could get stuck at an unwanted local minimizer. In this project, we develop a new effective approach based on our recent works where the convexity of the optimization problem is augmented by some smartly designed extra convex term. The novel approach can lead to stable numerical results with better image quality. In this project, one of our main focuses is to adapt our recently proposed convex augmentation approach to design new high-quality models and efficient solvers for the image recovery with applications to two major imaging fields: blind image deblurring and phase retrieval. Unlike the standard image deblurring, the blind image deblurring is much more challenging since the blurring kernel is also unknown. The aim is to recover the clear image and the blur kernel simultaneously. This usually leads to a difficult non-convex problem and we need careful investigation to get a stable solution. We will apply our convex augmentation technique to handle this problem. Phase retrieval is another extremely important task where the phase information is completely missing. This is a non-convex problem as the phase information and the clear image are needed to be estimated simultaneously. We extend our convex augmentation approach to handle this challenging task. To better suit the two fields, we also propose the Plug-and-Play framework to integrate deep learning denoising prior. Many well developed deep learning approaches can be considered for the purpose, and their effectiveness has already been demonstrated in the literature. We will design new efficient solvers for our new models, and provide new theories to help analyzing the convergence performance of the solvers. Extensive numerical experiments and comparisons on real imaging data with other state-of-the-art methods will also be provided. 圖像恢復是指從被噪聲和模糊破壞的退化觀察中構建清晰圖像的過程。這對於進一步進行圖像分析和理解非常重要，並且具有許多科學，工程和醫學應用。例如，如果大大提高了計算機斷層掃描圖像的質量，則可以更好地估計患者的健康狀況。由於存在由不同類型的模糊和噪聲污染的各種類型的圖像，因此圖像恢復仍然是一項艱鉅的任務。對於許多重要的應用程序，著名的變分方法通常會導致非凸編程，這是眾所周知很難處理的。用於非凸問題的經典算法可能會卡在不需要的局部極小值上。在這個項目中，我們根據最近的工作開發了一種新的有效方法，其中通過一些巧妙設計的額外凸項來增加優化問題的凸度。該新穎方法可以產生具有更好圖像質量的穩定數值結果。在該項目中，我們的主要重點之一是使我們最近提出的凸增廣方法適應設計用於圖像恢復的新的高質量模型和有效求解器，並將其應用於兩個主要成像領域：盲圖像去模糊和相位檢索。與標準圖像去模糊不同，由於模糊內核也是未知的，因此盲圖像去模糊更具挑戰性。目的是同時恢復清晰的圖像和模糊內核。這通常會導致困難的非凸問題，我們需要仔細研究以找到穩定的解決方案。我們將應用凸增廣技術來解決此問題。相位檢索是另一個極其重要的任務，其中相位信息完全丟失。這是一個非凸問題，因為需要同時估計相位信息和清晰圖像。我們擴展了凸增廣方法來處理這一具有挑戰性的任務。為了更好地適應這兩個領域，我們還提出了即插即用框架來集成深度學習去噪先驗。為此目的，可以考慮許多發達的深度學習方法，並且其有效性已經在文獻中得到證明。我們將為新模型設計新的高效求解器，並提供新的理論來幫助分析求解器的收斂性能。我們還將提供大量的數值實驗，以及使用其他最新方法對實際成像數據進行的比較。

14302920.label: Realisation of objectives
14302920.value: The project objectives outlined in Section 5.1 have been systematically addressed and achieved to a significant extent. Below is a detailed account of each objective, the progress made, and any challenges encountered: 1. Development of the Convex Augmentation Approach Achievement: We successfully developed a convex augmentation framework that integrates various data fitting terms and both smooth and nonsmooth regularizers. This framework has been implemented and tested across multiple datasets. Extent: The approach has shown promising results in preliminary experiments, demonstrating improved stability and convergence in reconstruction tasks. 2. Design of Efficient Optimization Models Achievement: We designed several optimization models tailored for general image recovery, specifically targeting real data images. These models leverage advanced mathematical techniques to enhance recovery accuracy. Extent: Our models outperformed existing methods in several benchmark tests, validating their efficiency and accuracy. 3. Improvement in Phase Retrieval Results Achievement: New models have been formulated for phase retrieval that showed significantly better recovery outcomes with real data compared to previous approaches. Extent: Extensive testing revealed a 15-20% improvement in recovery metrics over state-of-the-art methods. 4. Design of Efficient Numerical Algorithms Achievement: We developed and optimized numerical algorithms that are both efficient and effective for the proposed models, ensuring rapid computation without sacrificing quality. Extent: Algorithm performance was benchmarked, with results indicating a reduction in computation time by approximately 30% compared to traditional algorithms. 5. Systematic Use of the Plug-and-Play Technique Achievement: The Plug-and-Play technique was integrated into our methodologies for blind image recovery and phase retrieval. This facilitated easier model adaptation and improved results in practical applications. Extent: The application of this technique has enhanced model flexibility, leading to more robust recovery in challenging scenarios. 6. Conducting Extensive Numerical Experiments Achievement: A series of comprehensive numerical experiments were conducted, comparing our reconstruction algorithms against leading methods. The experiments were designed to rigorously evaluate performance across various imaging scenarios. Extent: The results have been documented, showing our methods consistently outperforming others, particularly in noise robustness and recovery fidelity. Challenges and Under-Achievements: Despite the significant progress, a few objectives experienced challenges: 1. Data Diversity: While our models performed well on the datasets used, the diversity of real-world images posed challenges. Some images exhibited characteristics that our current models struggled to accommodate. Attempts: We are currently expanding our dataset to include a broader range of image types, with ongoing adjustments to our models to enhance adaptability. 2. Computational Resources: The optimization models and algorithms required substantial computational resources, leading to delays in experimentation. Attempts: We attempt to address this by optimizing code and utilizing parallel computing resources, which has improved processing times. 3. Integration of Techniques: The application of the Plug-and-Play technique proved more complex than anticipated, requiring additional iterations to fine-tune its integration. Attempts: Continuous testing and refinement have been undertaken, resulting in improved implementation strategies. Overall, the project objectives have been largely achieved, with notable advancements in the field of image recovery and phase retrieval. Future work will focus on addressing the challenges encountered, refining models, and expanding the breadth of our experiments to further validate and enhance performance. We remain committed to overcoming obstacles and advancing our research in this domain.

14302920.value: There is significant potential for further development in image restoration research. Key areas for exploration include integrating advanced deep learning techniques, such as transformers and GANs, to improve image quality and detail, as well as optimizing algorithms for real-time processing for applications like live video analysis and medical imaging. To advance this research, we propose the following actions: collaboration: partner with academic institutions and industry leaders to leverage expertise and resources; prototype development: create and test prototypes of promising models in real-world scenarios to assess effectiveness; funding: seek grants and funding to support ongoing research and development; dissemination: publish findings and present at conferences to share knowledge and gather feedback; continuous improvement: implement a framework for ongoing evaluation to enable iterative enhancements based on feedback and performance metrics. By pursuing these initiatives, we can maximize our research impact and contribute to advancements in image processing technology.

14302920.value: This research project focuses on improving how we recover images, especially when some information is missing or distorted. Think of it like trying to piece together a puzzle where some pieces are lost. Our goal is to develop smarter techniques that can fill in these gaps more accurately, making the final image clearer and more reliable. The significance of this work lies in its applications. Better image recovery methods can enhance everyday technologies, such as medical imaging, photography, and even satellite imagery. For instance, clearer medical scans can lead to better diagnoses, while improved photos can help preserve important moments in our lives. In essence, this project aims to create tools that allow us to see and understand images better, even when they are incomplete or noisy. The value of this research extends to various fields, potentially improving outcomes in healthcare, science, and everyday life, ultimately helping us make better decisions based on clearer visual information.
