14303320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303320.value: The cell membrane is a complex surface composed of different biomolecules. It is crucial for intracellular metabolism, cell-cell interactions, cell differentiation, and the control of the transportation of molecules into and out of the cell. Alteration of the biological properties of the cell membrane could allow us to manipulate the behavior of the cells as well as to develop new cell-based drug delivery systems. However, the present cell surface modification methods remain limited with tedious procedures, low conjugation efficiency, and exhibit different degrees of cytotoxicities. Recently, we reported a novel bioconjugation method called phthalaldehyde-amine capture (PAC) reaction. It allows the rapid formation of stable covalent isoindole linkage between amine and phthalaldehyde (OPA) under the physiological condition without the generation of any by-products. Interestingly, our recent preliminary data has confirmed that the PAC reaction is also capable of conjugating different molecules on the cell surface with a high rate and efficiency. Our results showed that the PAC reaction could alter the cell surfaces of red blood cells and cancer cells with a fluorescent probe and tumor-targeting peptides. The modified cells have the ability to specifically bind to target tumor cells in vitro, which results in unnatural cell-cell interaction. In this proposal, the PAC reaction will be investigated as a novel approach to label, conjugate, and modify the live-cell surface. We will use the PAC reaction to develop a cell-based photosensitizer carrier for tumor-targeted photodynamic therapy. To go beyond the state-of-the-art, we will explore the use of PAC reaction to generate the chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-macrophage mimetics. CAR-macrophage is one of the recent hottest topics in immunotherapy. By installing highly specific cancer-binding protein on the macrophage surface, the macrophage gained extra tumor recognition ability and enhanced the phagocytotic process of tumor cells. However, the present genetic modification approach of macrophage has the disadvantages of unpredictable efficiency and irreversible effect leads to long-term adverse events and safety concerns. Thus, we envisage that the PAC reaction can mimic the genetic approach to producing CAR-macrophage with fewer uncertainties, decrease batch-to-batch variation, and reversible effect. The success of the proposal demonstrates the ease of membrane modification, novel red blood cells as a tumor-targeted drug carrier, and novel CAR-macrophage mimetics. The method will facilitate the future researches of studying cell-cell interaction, immunology, facilitating drug discovery, and biological tools development. 細胞膜是由不同生物分子組成的複雜表面。它對於細胞內代謝，細胞間相互作用，細胞分化以及控制分子進出細胞的運輸至關重要。細胞膜生物學特性的改變可以使我們操縱細胞的行為以及開發新的基於細胞的藥物遞送系統。然而，目前的細胞表面修飾方法仍然受限於繁瑣的程序，低的綴合效率，並且表現出不同程度的細胞毒性。最近，我們報導了一種新的生物共軛方法，稱為苯二醛-胺捕獲（PAC）反應。它允許在生理條件下在胺和鄰苯二甲醛（OPA）之間快速形成穩定的共價異吲哚鍵，而不會產生任何副產物。有趣的是，我們最近的初步數據已證實PAC反應還能夠以高速率和高效率結合細胞表面上的不同分子。我們的結果表明，PAC反應可以通過熒光探針和腫瘤靶向肽改變紅細胞和癌細胞的細胞表面。修飾的細胞具有在體外特異性結合靶腫瘤細胞的能力，這導致非自然的細胞-細胞相互作用。在這項建議中，將對PAC反應進行研究，以作為​​標記，綴合和修飾活細胞表面的新方法。我們將使用PAC反應來開發基於細胞的光敏劑載體，用於腫瘤靶向的光動力療法。為了超越最新技術水平，我們將探索使用PAC反應生成嵌合抗原受體（CAR）巨噬細胞模擬物。 CAR-巨噬細胞是免疫療法中最近最熱門的話題之一。通過在巨噬細胞表面安裝高度特異性的癌癥結合蛋白，巨噬細胞獲得了額外的腫瘤識別能力並增強了腫瘤細胞的吞噬過程。然而，目前的巨噬細胞遺傳修飾方法具有效率不可預測的缺點，並且不可逆的作用導致長期的不良事件和安全性問題。因此，我們設想PAC反應可以模仿遺傳方法生產CAR巨噬細胞，不確定性更少，減少批次之間的差異，並且具有可逆的作用。該建議書的成功證明了膜修飾的簡便性，新型紅細胞作為靶向腫瘤的藥物載體以及新型CAR-巨噬細胞模擬物。該方法將促進未來研究細胞間相互作用，免疫學，促進藥物發現和生物工具開發的研究。

14303320.label: Realisation of objectives
14303320.value: Our research project, titled "Novel Live Cell Membrane Modification Chemistry for Efficient Chemical Modification of Blood Cells as Anticancer Agents," focused on developing innovative chemical modification strategies for the surface of live cells to enhance their efficacy as anticancer therapeutics. This work centered on utilizing the phthalaldehyde-amine capture (PAC) reaction to efficiently modify the cell membranes of red blood cells (RBCs) and macrophages, transforming them into targeted drug delivery vehicles and immune activators. The approach, which involved a one-pot peptide cyclization and conjugation method, allowed for high specificity, rapid production, and the incorporation of tumor-targeting peptides on the cell surface for targeted delivery of therapeutic agents. Throughout the course of this research, we successfully synthesized and characterized various cell-based conjugates. Specifically, we developed RBCs conjugated with cyclic RGD peptides, designed to selectively target and bind to cancer cells overexpressing the αvβ3 integrin receptor. The modified RBCs carried a photosensitizer that, upon light activation, produced reactive oxygen species (ROS) to selectively induce cytotoxicity in cancer cells. Using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, we demonstrated the successful surface modification and target-specific binding of these conjugates. The therapeutic efficacy of the modified RBCs was validated through in vitro studies involving cancer cell lines such as A549 lung carcinoma and U87-MG glioblastoma cells, where enhanced tumor cell binding and significant phototoxicity were observed. For the macrophage-based component of our research, we fabricated tumor-targeting peptidic CAR-macrophages (pCAR-M) using the PAC reaction to conjugate epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeting cyclic peptides on their surface. These pCAR-M exhibited significantly improved binding to EGFR-overexpressing tumor cells and enhanced phagocytosis compared to unmodified macrophages, making them a promising candidate for cell-based immunotherapy, particularly for targeting solid tumors. Flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, and in vivo studies in mouse models were performed to further assess their targeting efficiency, phagocytic ability, and safety profile. The results showed notable improvements in tumor suppression and minimal off-target effects, indicating the safety and potential of these modified macrophages for further clinical applications. In addition to advancing our experimental work, we actively disseminated our findings at international conferences, fostering discussions and collaborations with leading scientists in the field of biomaterials, peptide chemistry, and cell-based therapies. In December 2023, we presented our findings at the IUPAC-ISBoc13 Symposium in Singapore, which brought together researchers from across the globe working on peptide and protein-based therapeutics. This platform allowed us to share our novel methodologies for live-cell surface modification and targeted anticancer applications, receiving valuable feedback from experts in peptide science. Furthermore, we participated in the Chinese Peptide Symposium held in Hong Kong in July 2024. This conference provided an excellent opportunity to showcase our latest work on macrophage modification and the development of peptidic CAR-M for immunotherapy. Our presentations were well-received, stimulating discussions on the future of non-genetic cell modification strategies and their potential applications in cancer treatment. These conference attendances played an important role in establishing new connections and collaborations, leading to further insights that have shaped our current research direction, focusing on trispecific antibodies and expanding the use of chemically modified immune cells for novel cancer therapies.

14303320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303320.value: One of the major outcomes of our research is the successful development of a one-pot peptide cyclization and surface modification method for photosensitiser-loaded red blood cells (RBCs). This work was published in Biomaterials Science (Chu, J. C. H., Shao, C., Ha, S. Y. Y., Wong, C. T. T., & Ng, D. K. P., 2021, Biomater. Sci., 2021, 9, 7832), under the title "One-pot peptide cyclisation and surface modification of photosensitiser-loaded red blood cells for targeted photodynamic therapy." The study demonstrated the use of a bifunctional linker containing bis(bromomethyl)phenyl and ortho-phthalaldehyde units to modify RBCs with cyclic RGD peptides, enabling selective binding to αvβ3 integrin-overexpressing cancer cells. The photosensitiser-loaded RBCs exhibited enhanced photocytotoxicity upon light activation, leading to targeted cancer cell destruction. This innovative live-cell surface modification strategy holds promise for a wide range of therapeutic applications. In addition to the RBC-based platform, our research also focused on macrophage modification to develop tumor-targeting peptidic CAR-macrophages (pCAR-M). These pCAR-M demonstrated significantly improved targeting and phagocytic abilities in both in vitro and in vivo studies, offering a promising new avenue for cell-based immunotherapy, particularly against solid tumors that are typically resistant to conventional CAR-T cell therapies. Furthermore, we are in the process of preparing a 2 manuscripts based on our ongoing work involving animal experiments with pCAR-M. We have completed significant animal experiments involving tumor-bearing mouse models to assess the therapeutic efficacy of pCAR-M. These experiments demonstrated substantial tumor growth suppression compared to control groups treated with unmodified macrophages or PBS. The modified macrophages showed effective tumor targeting, minimal off-target effects, and enhanced safety profile, with no significant systemic toxicity observed. In addition, we conducted detailed analyses of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, which indicated increased immune cell recruitment and activation in tumors treated with pCAR-M. We are currently awaiting results from patient-derived cancer samples to further confirm the efficacy of our approach in a more clinically relevant setting. This work has received positive preliminary feedback from peers and is planned for submission to a high-impact journal (impact factor > 15) in the near future.

14303320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303320.value: Our research holds significant potential for further development. We plan to submit two high-impact publications detailing our work on macrophage-based cell modification strategies. We received GRF-RIF funding based on the conceptual work from this project. This funding has laid the foundation for a new project titled "A Novel Approach to Target Cancer Stemness Using Peptidic Chimeric Antigen Receptor (pCAR) Macrophages" (RIF: R5008-22). The new project will expand on our current work, specifically targeting cancer stem cells, which are known to contribute to tumor recurrence and resistance to conventional therapies. We are also preparing a provisional patent to protect our chemical modification methodologies for targeted cancer therapies. We are planning to establish a spin-off company from the university, focusing on the commercialization of our cell modification technologies. We will be applying to the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks (HKSTP) to support this venture, which aims to bring these novel therapeutics closer to clinical application and commercialization.These actions reflect our commitment to transforming our research into impactful cancer therapies, offering new treatment options for patients with challenging tumors.

14303320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303320.value: Our research focuses on improving cancer treatment by modifying the surface of blood cells to make them better at fighting tumors. We used a chemical process to attach special molecules to red blood cells and immune cells called macrophages. These modified cells are designed to find and destroy cancer cells more effectively. For example, we loaded red blood cells with a light-activated drug that kills cancer cells when exposed to light, and we equipped macrophages with molecules that help them recognize and eat cancer cells. This approach could lead to more precise cancer treatments that target tumors without harming healthy tissues. Our work shows promise for developing new therapies that are less toxic and more effective, especially for cancers that are difficult to treat with current methods.

14303420.label: Project Objectives
14303420.value: We shall derive a diffuse interface model for two-phase flows with micropolar fluids and moving contact lines using the Coleman-Noll procedure. We shall establish the existence of weak solutions to the diffuse interface model derived in Objective 1, and include the case where certain viscosity functions are degenerate. We shall develop an energy stable and efficient fully discrete numerical scheme for the diffuse interface model derived in Objective 1, and prove the existence and uniqueness of fully discrete solutions, as well as the convergence as the discretisation parameters tend to zero. We shall investigate the sharp interface limit of the diffuse interface model with the method of formally matched asymptotic expansions, and pursue supporting numerical evidence using the scheme proposed in Objective 3.

14303420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303420.value: Micropolar fluids are among the simplest cases of fluids with microstructures, where each fluid particle has its own internal rotations. Examples include ferrofluids, blood flows, bubbly liquids and liquid crystals, all of which play significant and important roles in various industries and also in the human body. Therefore, it becomes essential for scientists to effectively capture the behaviour of these kinds of fluids with the appropriate mathematical models, and to better analyse and simulate their flow dynamics. The classical Navier-Stokes equations that are well-studied by the mathematical community is not a suitable description for micropolar fluids, as the internal rotations of each fluid particle are not accounted for. Through the works of A. Cemal Eringen and his coworkers, we now have mathematical models that extend the Navier-Stokes equations to capture these internal rotations. However, in many real world applications we often encounter mixtures of multiple kinds of fluids. In these situations we have to further extend previous models to account for the interactions between individual fluids that can influence the gross motion of the mixture. The main aims of this proposal are to develop new mathematical models for mixtures of micropolar fluids, study their mathematical properties, and derive stable and efficient fully discrete numerical schemes for simulations. The key ingredient is the diffuse interface methodology which offers a model that is amenable to further mathematical analysis and allows us to address the existence of weak solutions and the stability of discrete solutions. Also included in the modelling is the dynamics of the contact line that is created when two or more fluids meet at the same solid boundary. This describes wetting and dewetting processes crucial in modern-day applications such as inkjet printing and lubrication. We believe the proposed model and the accompanying analytical and numerical ideas can provide a theoretical foundation for many industrial and biological processes that involve mixtures of non-standard fluids. 微極性流體是具有微觀結構的流體的最簡單情況，其中每個流體粒子都有自己的內部旋轉。例子包括鐵磁流體，血液流動，氣泡狀液體和液晶，它們在各個行業以及人體中都起著重要的作用。因此，對於科學家來說，用適當的數學模型有效地捕獲這些流體的行為，並更好地分析和模擬其流動動力學就變得至關重要。 數學界精心研究的經典Navier–Stokes方程不適用於微極性流體，因為它沒有考慮每個流體粒子的內部旋轉。通過A. Cemal Eringen和他的同事的工作，我們現在有了擴展Navier-Stokes方程以捕獲這些內部旋轉的數學模型。但是，在許多實際應用中，我們經常會遇到多種流體的混合物。在這些情況下，我們必須進一步擴展先前的模型，以考慮可能影響混合物總運動的各個流體之間的相互作用。 這個建議的主要目的是為微極性流體的混合物開發新的數學模型，研究其數學性質，並推導穩定有效的全離散數值模擬方案。關鍵因素是擴散界面方法，該模型提供了可用於進一步數學分析的模型，並使我們能夠解決弱解的存在和離散解的穩定性。建模中還包括當兩種或多種流體在同一固體邊界處相遇時創建的接觸線動力學。這描述了在現代應用中至關重要的潤濕和反潤濕過程，例如噴墨打印和潤滑。我們相信，提出的模型以及隨附的分析和數值思想可以為涉及非標準流體混合物的許多工業和生物過程提供理論基礎。

14303420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303420.value: We extend the current state-of-the-art and developed new diffuse interface models describing the motion of a mixture of two incompressible and immiscible micropolar fluids. These differ from traditional mathematical descriptions of Newtonian fluids by the addition of a new set of equations for the micro-rotation. Utilizing recent results established by many authors, we study the solvability of the new model, and in particular, we include in our analysis the important case of moving contact lines, which appear in industrial applications such as inkjet printing and coating processes. Furthermore, our results pave the way for a theoretical comparison between micropolar and Newtonian fluid mixtures, where key estimates capturing the gap between these two different types of models are derived.

14303420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303420.value: An interesting direction is to consider optimal control of micropolar fluids. The micropolar description serves as a simplified setting for magnetic-influenced ferrofluids, which are applied in versatile settings, such as sealing, coolants, lubricants, and in display devices. Hence, the analytical results developed from the project provide a stepping stone in the study of optimal control involving micropolar fluid mixtures. Another direction worthy of pursuit is to develop effective models for micropolar flow in thin domains, which can be applied for example to curved electronic displays. The idea is to employ asymptotic expansions to derive the effective equations of a two dimensional model that captures the dynamics of the flow when the height of the domain is significantly smaller than all other length scales. Such models would also generalize the current state-of-the-art for Darcy--Cahn--Hilliard systems. These topics would make very good PhD research projects.

14303420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303420.value: Micropolar fluids are fluids with internal rotations, and appear for instance in bubbly liquids, blood flow and ferrofluids. In industrial and biological settings, mixtures of micropolar fluids are often present and so it is essential to develop mathematical models that can accurately capture the relevant physical phenomena. In this project we developed new mathematical models for mixtures of micropolar fluids, and our theoretical investigations demonstrated that these models are mathematically sound. This opens up further studies in related optimal control problems and development of efficient numerical schemes. Our ideas developed in this project can also be used to tackle more challenging and interesting problems prevalent in other areas of scientific applications.

14304120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14304120.value: 關於高階等周不等式的問題

14304120.label: Project Objectives
14304120.value: The Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality for non-convex is not known for some cases. We will try some methods especially optimal transport method to prove some case of Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities in a non-convex domain. There are few Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities in hyperbolic space even in the convex case. 14304120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304120.value: Isoperimetric inequality is an old and classical mathematical problem which is a central research subject in geometry. The higher-order version of the isoperimetric inequality which comes from convex geometry is sometimes called Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. There are many interesting questions related to Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. The classical Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality holds for convex hypersurfaces. It is natural to ask whether this convex condition can be weakened into some weak convex conditions. In this project, we will use PDE's methods to find some case of Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities in the non-convex domain. We expect this approach can not only prove the geometric inequality but also inspire the study of more interesting geometric PDEs. In Euclidean space, some special cases of Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities can be proved by several methods such as geometric flow method or optimal transport method. But in hyperbolic space, there is no optimal transport proof for the corresponding isoperimetric inequality. The other aim of the project is to find an optimal transport proof for isoperimetric type inequalities in hyperbolic space. This method will be useful to prove many more geometric inequalities in space form or more general Riemannian manifold. Establishing Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality may be helpful to do analysis in the Riemannian manifold. 等周不等式是一個古老而經典的數學問題，是幾何學的中心研究課題。由凸幾何產生的等周不等式的高階版本有時稱為Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式。有許多與Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式有關的有趣問題。經典的Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式在凸超曲面成立，有時可以將凸條件減弱為一些弱凸條件。 Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式的等式情形也非常重要，有時甚至非常不平凡。我們想找到並證明弱凸條件下的Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式的一些加權和最優形式。在歐幾里得空間中，可以通過幾何流方法或最優輸運法等幾種方法證明Alexandrov-Fenchel不等式的一些特殊情況。但是在雙曲空間中，沒有相應等周不等式的最優輸運證明。該項目的另一個目的是找到雙曲空間中等周型不等式的最優輸運方法證明。該方法將有助於證明更多的空間形式或更一般的黎曼流形的幾何不等式。

14304120.label: Realisation of objectives
14304120.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have explored several different methods to approach the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality for non-convex domains. These include optimal transport method, variational method and integral method. It turns out that the absence of boundary convexity still creates substantial difficulty in the optimal transport approach. We adopt alternative methods using variational approach and integral methods from nonlinear partial differential equations which are effective in attacking this particular problem at hand. We have made important progress by establishing uniform estimates for a class of curvature-type equations in hypersurface geometry. On the other hand, we have also studied a related prescribed curvature measure problem and showed C^{1,1} estimates for the solutions even when the prescribed function is touching zero somewhere. Moreover, we use the integral method of Warren and Yuan to prove new a-priori interior Hessian estimates for the fully nonlinear sigma-two equation in dimension three. These results are helpful in establishing the existence of solutions for these equations, ultimately enabling the proof of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities for non-convex domains. Regarding Objective 2, we have adopted variational techniques to study a rigidity problem related to Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities in non-convex domains of hyperbolic spaces. In particular, we used the theory of constant mean curvature capillary surfaces to prove a comparison theorem for certain types of polyhedra in three-manifolds with negative scalar curvature lower bound. This result confirms some cases of the celebrated Gromov dihedral rigidity conjecture in hyperbolic space. Moreover, we have made significant progress in the existence theory of free boundary minimal annuli based on min-max constructions. We expect that this theory will play a major role in studying Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities in hyperbolic space and more generally in arbitrary Riemannian manifolds. In summary, both objectives set out in this project has been successfully completed. Our work has also opened up new directions for further investigations.

14304120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304120.value: In Research Output 1, the PI has trained a PhD student Gaoming Wang to work on a problem related to this research project. We successfully extended the classical uniformization result for smooth Riemann surfaces with boundary to the singular setting which allows triple junction singularities. This result is fundamental in the existence theory for any variational construction of singular minimal or constant mean curvature surfaces in Riemannian manifolds. In Research Output 2, the PI has trained an MPhil student Ho Tin Leung to work on the general existence theory for free boundary minimal annuli in Riemannian manifolds with boundary using min-max methods. The second work is under final preparation and the first work has been submitted to journal for publication and is currently under the peer-review process. In Research Output 3, we prove a comparison theorem for certain types of polyhedra in a three-manifold with negative scalar curvature lower bound and confirms in some cases the Gromov dihedral rigidity conjecture in hyperbolic three-space. This work has been published in the journal Transactions of the American Mathematical Society. In Research Output 4, we established a-priori estimates for solutions of prescribed curvature measure problems when the prescribed function may touch zero somewhere. This work has been published in the journal Advanced Nonlinear Studies. In Research Output 5, we proved new interior Hessian estimates for sigma-2 equations in dimension three generalizing Warren-Yuan's result. This work has been published in the journal Frontiers of Mathematics.

14304120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304120.value: Many of the results obtained in the research outputs are special to three dimensions. However, we expect that some of the techniques developed can be carried over to the higher dimensional setting. We hope to address in future work the scalar curvature equations and the fully nonlinear sigma-2 Hessian equation in high dimensions. We also expect further development in the remaining open cases of Gromov's dihedral rigidity conjecture in hyperbolic spaces. Other approaches like Dirac operators may be combined with the techniques developed in this project to yield satisfactory results. Such scalar rigidity results are closely related to positive mass theorems in mathematical general relativity and we shall study these extensions in future projects.

14304120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304120.value: This project has initiated a systematic study of various Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities which are higher order versions of the classical isoperimetric inequality. Isoperimetric-type inequalities are fundamental tools in the study of geometry and they have profound applications, for example in mathematical general relativity. Together with his students and collaborators, the PI and co-PI have developed new techniques from partial differential equations and geometric variational tools to study such nonlinear isoperimetric inequalities in curved spaces. These new techniques have opened up new directions to study problems arising in a range of research areas including differential geometry, optimal transport and partial differential equations.

14304320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304320.value: 治療性抗體因為其臨床療效而日益受到關注。隨著越來越多的臨床試驗，抗體生產，改造和修飾方面的研究也在蓬勃發展。雜交抗體是一類新型的抗體分子。也稱為雙特異性單克隆抗體，這些人工蛋白可引導免疫細胞結合併殺死腫瘤細胞。另一個例子是抗體-藥物結合物，可特異性殺滅腫瘤細胞，同時保留健康的細胞。 這些例子表明了新的抗體修飾或者改造技術的重要性。位點特異性抗體反應就是這樣一種技術。基於我們先前在蛋白質反應方面的經驗，我們開發了一種僅修飾IgG的一個賴氨酸殘基（Lys 248）的位點特異性反應。該反應有效地在天然人類IgG上安裝了一個疊氮基團，而無需進行基因工程改造。這項技術與基於外泌體的藥物輸送技術，為實現當前標書中的目標鋪平了道路。我們計劃構建兩種類型的雙特異性治療性抗體偶聯物：雙特異性抗體偶聯和抗體偶聯的納米囊泡，用於癌症免疫治療和有針對性的藥物輸送。 新的化學往往推動醫學的新突破。不只是小分子藥物，生物大分子也越來越受到生物製藥的重視。我們新的Fc結構域的位點特異性乙酰化反應具有無與倫比的功能：對天然IgG的條件溫和，反應速度快（完成一小時內完成約70-80％），而且副反應水平非常低。另一方面，外泌體/miRNA的自組裝體被證明可以為骨關節炎的治療提供靶向治療。基於在化學上的這兩個進步，我們的抗體偶聯物的構建將把位點特異性的生物交聯反應擴展到功能性抗體複合物，從而為靶向癌症治療的研究提供了新的工具和分子，並有望開發出新的癌症療法。

14304320.label: Realisation of objectives
14304320.value: In this project, we proposed to develop lysine-selective site-specific reactions for the modification of antibodies, to construct antibody conjugates, and to apply these conjugates for cancer immunotherapy and targeted drug delivery. Both objectives have been successfully realized. (1) We successfully constructed bispecific antibody conjugates (bsAbCs), and prove their use in targeted cancer immunotherapy. (2) We successfully constructed antibody-conjugated nanovesicles (AbC-NVs), and also proved their application in targeted drug delivery. Chemical modifications of antibodies will enhance the therapeutic index of mAbs and expand their applicability to targeted immune therapies of cancers. Since the approval of the first ADC by the FDA, researchers have developed many chemical reactions to modify antibodies. However, only a limited number of synthetic methods can achieve high site-selectivity. The precise control of the reaction sites is highly valuable, as nonselective reactions result in a heterogeneous population of modified antibodies, complicating quality control, and clinical use. To address this challenge, we harnessed the principle of proximity-driven group transfer reaction, and synthesized an antibody-binding peptide to realize site-selective acetylation of a single lysine residue, Lys 248, of the fragment crystallizable region (Fc region) in the heavy chain of the human Immunoglobulin G (IgG). Briefly, an Fc-interacting peptide bound with the Fc domain and positioned a phenolic ester close to Lys 248, which induced a nucleophilic reaction and resulted in the transfer of an acetyl group to Lys 248. We found that the acetylation reaction proceeded to a decent yield under the physiological condition without the need for deglycosylation, unnatural amino acids, or catalysts. After the antibody is acetylated, the azide moiety can be further functionalized with biorthogonal reactions at Lys 248. We then synthesized an antibody−lipid conjugate and constructed antibody-conjugated liposomes (immunoliposomes), targeting HER2-positive (HER2+) cancer cells. We also built a bispecific antibody complex (bsAbC) covalently linking an anti-HER2 antibody and an anti-CD3 antibody. The immunoliposomes can efficiently deliver drugs into cancer cells in a targeted manner. The bsAbC showed in vitro effector-cell- mediated cytotoxicity at nanomolar concentrations. This reaction was also extended to the functionalization of red blood cells (RBCs). Site-selective antibody-lipid conjugates can insert into red blood cells and display antibodies on the surface, forming immunoRBCs. The immunoRBCs can effectively deliver photosensitizers to cancer cells and induce photo-responsive cell killing. We also applied the antibody-lipid conjugates to functionalize exosomes, one type of natural nanovesicles secreted by cells. The immunoEVs can also deliver drugs into cancer cells, and they can also modify immune cells and grant them cancer-targeting capability. Taken together, this new technology of site-selective antibody modification enables the construction of a variety of antibody conjugates, which can be found in multiple cancer therapies.

14304320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304320.value: Site-selective lysine reaction of antibodies is challenging. By screening a set of Fc-binding peptides, we developed a peptide-guided antibody acetylation reaction for the first time. We showed that commercially available antibodies can be modified and assembled into conjugates for immunotherapies. Several papers have been published to report the results above. A US patent has been approved, together with PCT approval. This work was also reported at international conferences as invited or keynote talks. Several Ph.D. students received training under this project, and graduated with a Ph.D. degree during the period.

14304320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304320.value: This research project significantly advanced the study of site-selective antibody reactions. It will have significant applications in the area of antibody drugs, ranging from antibody-drug conjugates to bispecific antibodies, to immune cell therapies. We will team up with biomedical scientists, cancer biologists, and immunologists to apply for joint collaborative grants from RGC and ITC. We also plan to seek opportunities to commercialize our technology and products.

14304320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304320.value: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins secreted by plasma cells in the immune system for targeting and neutralizing foreign substances such as viruses and bacteria. Due to their excellent capability of binding with disease-related molecules, antibodies are emerging as potent therapeutic agents, targeting a wide range of diseases. Since the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first monoclonal antibody (mAb) muromonab-CD3 in 1986, many antibody drugs have entered clinical use or are in clinical trials. Moreover, chemical modification greatly expands the applications of antibodies. Here we developed a unique chemical reaction to modify a single amino acid of a commercially available antibody. Such a reaction has led to immunotherapies which will benefit patients in the future.

14304420.label: Project Objectives
14304420.value: Generality: A general framework for variance estimation will be studied. We plan to (a) rigorously formulate the framework based on difference statistics; (b) demonstrate that this framework covers a wide variety of existing estimators; and (c) derive a neat representation of the estimator for practical implementation. Consistency: Asymptotic properties, including consistency and admissibility, will be investigated. We plan to (a) derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for consistency; (b) develop easily verifiable conditions for consistency and admissibility; and (c) demonstrate that many existing estimators are either inconsistent or suboptimal. Invariance: The degree of invariance to time-varying mean will be examined. We plan to (a) propose a new measure of robustness against time-varying mean to characterize the degree of invariance; (b) prove that the proposed estimators have the same convergence properties in the presence of arbitrary time-varying mean structure; (c) analyze the tradeoff between efficiency and robustness; and (d) study some implementation issues, including finite-sample adjustment. Optimality: Detailed statistical properties, e.g., mean-squared error and convergence rate, will be inspected. We plan to (a) derive the optimal estimator, and show that it achieves the optimal rate of convergence; (b) demonstrate that it is asymptotically as efficient as the oracular estimator; and (c) propose the optimal bandwidth selector. Applications: Direct and non-direct applications of the proposed variance estimators will be considered. We plan to (a) implement the proposed variance estimator to some standard procedures and demonstrate the improvement over some existing methods; (b) propose some new statistical procedures inspired by the differencing framework; and (c) generalize the variance estimator to other more complicated situations, e.g., spatial data, time series with covariates, etc.

We plan to (a) implement the proposed variance estimator to some standard procedures and demonstrate the improvement over some existing methods; (b) propose some new statistical procedures inspired by the differencing framework; and (c) generalize the variance estimator to other more complicated situations, e.g., spatial data, time series with covariates, etc.

14304420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304420.value: 方差估算在統計推斷中起著重要作用。但是，數據經常被以下兩種多餘的結構所影響：（i）隨時間轉變之平均值及 （ii）時間序列的自相關性。在這情況下，方差估算會變得不簡單。現有方法一是忽略它們或是以非最佳之方法處理。本研究計劃旨在開發用於方差估計的通用最佳框架。所提出的框架將在以下五個階段中進行全面研究：（1）通用性，（2）一致性，（3）不變性，（4）最優性和（5）應用。 階段1：通用性。我們提出一種通用的方差估計方法。此方法建基於差異統計量，它們是權重總和為零的數據線性組合。我們推測，此類估計量足以函蓋許多常用的估計量。因此，可以為所有估計量開發出一個統一的理論和計算程式。 階段2：一致性。我們對一致性的必要和充分條件進行了研究。一個有趣的斷言是，均值估計不應該包含在方差估計中。出現此現象的原因是，均值估計的誤差會累積並嚴重影響最終的方差估計量。因此，許多估計量（包括依賴於局部趨勢的常用方差估算器）要麼不一致，要麼次優。 階段3：不變性。差分操作自動濾除均值結構，因此我們不需進行均值估算。此類估計量不僅對任意均值結構不變，而且避免使用錯誤的均值模型。我們提出了一種新的穩健概念來測量無差異程度。我們亦計劃推導由非恆定均值結構引起的偏差，並證明其可以快速收斂至零。它有助於研究統計效率與穩健性之間的權衡。 階段4：最佳性。在所有一致且穩健的估計量中，我們計劃推導它們的均方誤差，從而為最佳窗寬選擇提供理論指導。此外，我們猜想我們提出的穩健估計量的L2效率可以任意接近非穩健的估計量。 階段5：應用。一方面，我們將執行方差估計量的直接應用。另一方面，我們所提出的差異概念會引導構建出全新的假設檢定統計方法。這些假設檢定方法可能比現有方法更有效。例如，我們提出了兩個新的假設檢定統計量，以用於檢測均值的恆定性和測試存在均值變化時的方差變化點。

14304420.label: Realisation of objectives
14304420.value: The objectives of the proposal have been fully achieved. The proposed methodologies, outlined in the proposal, have been completed. The general framework stated in Objective 1 has been realized in a published article entitled 'Optimal Difference-based Variance Estimators in Time Series: A General Framework' (Publication #1 in Part C), which also partially resolves the consistency results stated in Objective 2, the invariance results stated in Objective 3, and the optimality stated in Objective 4. The consistency and optimality properties stated in Objectives 2 and 4 were then fully addressed in 'Asymptotically Constant Risk Estimator of the Time-Average Variance Constant' (Publication #5 in Part C) and 'Positive-definite Converging Kernel Estimation of Long-run Variance' (Publication #7 in Part C). In particular, these articles derive a new class of difference-based variance estimators that achieve the optimal rate of convergence as in the standard estimator. They also derive both a data-driven bandwidth selector and a universal bandwidth that does not depend on the data-generating mechanism. The realization of these objectives enables the next stage of the project. The invariance properties stated in Objective 3 have been fully addressed in 'Mean Stationarity Test in Time Series: A Signal Variance-based Approach' (Publication #3 in Part C) and 'Testing for Variance Changes under Varying Mean and Serial Correlation' (Publication #4 in Part C). These two articles successfully study robustness against mean trends and use this to perform inference on mean and variance stability, respectively. These two research outputs also contain applications that partially address Objective 5. Finally, Objective 5 is further studied in 'A General Framework for Constructing Locally Self-Normalized Multiple Change-Point Tests' (Publication #2 in Part C) and 'Inference in Coarsened Time Series via Generalized Method of Moments' (Publication #6 in Part C). They utilize and generalize the proposed methods for handling multiple change-point problems and addressing incompletely observed time series. In particular, the proposed methods have been applied to several real-data problems, including inference on air quality in the USA and analysis of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect turnover. It is noted that Publications #3 and #6 in Part C are partially funded by this grant. The results obtained in these two publications were presented at international conferences #1, #2, #5, #7, and #8 in Part C, where the funding acknowledgments were verbally mentioned during the presentations.

14304420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304420.value: The proposal aimed to develop a general framework for estimating long-run variance in time series when the mean is not constant over time. The main idea is to use differencing. This project ultimately yielded five major findings. First, we propose a general framework for a difference-based variance estimator. We found that it includes a large class of existing methods. The major finding is that when differencing is applied to time series, the ratio of the lag used in the differencing to the bandwidth used in kernel variance estimators must be at least 2 for standard optimality to hold for arbitrary kernels under regularity conditions. This finding differs from the usual practice of using equal lag and bandwidth in many existing articles. We prove that our proposed estimator is better than all existing estimators as far as we are aware of; see Publication 1 in Part C. Second, we showed that the optimal bandwidth for the kernel variance estimator for raw data is no longer optimal once differencing is applied. There is an extra multiplier to the traditional optimal bandwidth. This multiplier depends on how the differencing is used. Interestingly, the optimal multiplier is a universal constant; see Publication 1 in Part C. Third, we derived a universal bandwidth selector for straightforward practical implementation. The estimator is shown to have constant risk asymptotically. This was first partially resolved in Publication 5 in Part C and then fully addressed in Publication 7 in Part C. Fourth, we noticed that the traditional variance estimator is biased when the mean is not constant, while the proposed estimator is always consistent under regularity conditions. We utilize the difference between them to measure the nonconstancy of the mean. This leads us to a new mean stationarity test in Publication 3 in Part C. This idea is then generalized to a variance stationarity test in Publication 4 in Part C from another perspective. Both of them use the same logic as proposed in Objective 3 of this project. Fifth, we applied the proposed ideas to resolve several complicated time series problems, such as multiple change point testing and coarsened time series. We found that an efficient and robust long-run variance is important for many problems; see, e.g., Publications 3, 4, and 6 in Part C. We also used the proposed estimator for calibrating critical values in other types of test statistics; see Publication 2 in Part C.

14304420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304420.value: Although all objectives of the proposal have been achieved, several directions can be further developed to improve the proposed methodologies. First, we found that the lag-to-bandwidth ratio must be at least 2 for standard optimality to hold for all kernels. However, Publication 1 in Part C also provides hints on relaxing this assumption. In particular, the lag-to-bandwidth ratio can be reduced to 1 by utilizing a special type of kernel. This smaller ratio may lead to higher robustness properties; see Publications 3 and 4 in Part C. This motivates us to consider the differencing with the smallest lag. Second, when data arrive very quickly, the computational cost can be high. This situation may arise for streaming data, high-frequency data, and online big data. This calls for generalizing the proposal to an online estimator that allows for quick updates when new observations arrive. Third, the differencing idea can be generalized to different types of dependent data, such as spatial data, network data, functional data, etc. We conjecture that the estimator may still work for these complicated data types; however, the theory may be more involved. Given the popularity of such data types, this is an interesting research topic for future study.

14304420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304420.value: Time series data with a time-varying mean trend are commonly seen in practice. Statistical analysis of such data usually requires our ability to distinguish the variability driven by the trend from the variability driven by noise. This distinction allows us to determine with statistical significance whether the trend is constant or varies significantly relative to the random errors. This project provides a handy tool for completing this task. We provide theories for optimally implementing the proposed estimator and offer several applications related to analyzing the stability of the mean, the stability of the trend, and the existence of sudden jumps in the data. Notably, we identify several misconceptions or suboptimal practices commonly used by practitioners. For example, the lag parameter and the bandwidth parameter should not be chosen to be the same for convenience; their ratio should be at least two instead. Additionally, the originally optimal tuning parameter is no longer optimal once several methods are used together. We provide a simple rule to correct this. We also offer implementationally simple methods for universally selecting the bandwidth. Several real-data applications are illustrated in financial data and environmental data. Insightful conclusions were obtained in various publications.

14304520.label: Project Objectives
14304520.value: This project aims to develop low-cost and eco-friendly aqueous electrolyte with a wide electrochemical window by using water-miscible polymers (WMP) to confine and stabilize water and to reveal how water-polymer and anion-polymer interactions affect the water stability, coulombic efficiency, and cycling stability of the full aqueous Li-ion batteries. The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows: Develop structure-property-performance relationship of WMP aqueous electrolyte system by correlating the water-polymer bonding interaction to the electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity and flammability of WMP electrolytes. Investigate the effects of anion on the (a) ionic conductivity of WMP electrolytes; (b) chemical stability of SEI formation in the WMP electrolytes; and (c) corrosion effect of current collector in WMP electrolytes. Develop four strategies to further improve the developed WMP electrolytes, including co-solvent strategy to improve ionic conductivity, pH adjustment to further expand voltage window, ceramic surface coating, and gel pre-coating methods to stabilize graphite/lithium metal. Develop WMP-based full aqueous Li-ion batteries, perform full cell safety and abuse tests, and investigate its degradation mechanisms.

14304520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304520.value: 此項目計劃利用水溶性聚合物(WMP)以穩定水分子，研發低成本、環保的穩定水系電解液，並揭示水-聚合物、陰離子-聚合物的相互作用是如何影響水的穩定性以及水系鋰離子全電池的庫倫效率與循環穩定性。 用不可燃的水系電解液替代可燃的非水電解液可有效地解決傳統非水系鋰離子電池的安全問題，並降低材料與生產成本。然而，受限于水的電化學穩定性，傳統水系鋰離子電池的電壓低，導致其能量密度低下。 新興的高濃度（21m-55m）“水溶鹽”及“水溶雙鹽”電解液的電化學穩定窗口較寬，可增加水系電池的能量密度。然而，該電解液含有高濃度的氟化鋰鹽，存在成本及毒性問題。因此我們需要采取新的策略研發低成本、環保的穩定水系電解液，以用於高能量、可持續發展的水系電池。 在這一研究項目中，我們將采用低成本、環保的水溶性聚合物（WMPs），在低鹽濃度（例如2m）的條件下穩定水分子及擴寬電池的電壓窗口。我們挑選了三種分子量相近（Mn≈400）的水溶性聚合物：聚乙二醇（PEG）、聚丙二醇（PPG）及聚乙烯亞胺（PEI），它們的重複單元能與水分子形成强度不同的氫鍵。具體而言，我們將（1）探究在WMP電解液中，水－聚合物相互作用與電化學穩定性、離子電導率、可燃性的關係，以建立WMP電解液的結構、性質、性能閒的聯係；（２）研究陰離子對離子電導率、SEI穩定性的影響及其對集流體的腐蝕情況；（３）采取四種策略以提升WMP電解液的性能，包括通過共溶劑提高離子電導率、調節ｐＨ以進一步拓寬電壓窗口，采用陶瓷及凝膠包覆的方法穩定石墨／鋰金屬；（４）構建基於WMP電解液的水系鋰離子全電池，進行全電池的安全測試，並探究其性能衰減機制。 通過本項目的研究，我們將研發一種基於低成本、環保的水溶性聚合物的新型水系電解液系統，並深入瞭解其衰減機制，這將為設計低成本、可持續發展的高能量水系鋰離子電池提供指導。

14304520.label: Realisation of objectives
14304520.value: Objective 1: We developed a new crowding agent, polyethylene glycol dimethyl ether (PEGDME) 450, which demonstrated significantly higher conductivity (2.4 mS cm−1) compared to the state-of-the-art polyethylene glycol (PEG) 400 (0.8 mS cm−1), without compromising the voltage window (3.2 V). This new electrolyte enabled high-power and high-voltage aqueous Li4Ti5O12/LiMn2O4 cells to operate efficiently for 800 cycles, showcasing a universal strategy for advanced aqueous electrolyte design and high-performance batteries. To enable wide operating temperature aqueous batteries, we apply the design concept into aqueous potassium-ion batteries (AKIBs) as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage due to their low cost and high safety. The newly proposed 10 m KCF3COO electrolyte has a low freezing point (−35.5 °C) and high average ice formation energy, resulting in high energy density (56.3 Wh/kg at 25 °C, 41.9 Wh/kg at −35 °C) and a long lifespan (87.5% capacity retention over 1000 cycles at −35 °C). In addition, we developed anti-freezing electrolyte concentrations for low-temperature aqueous batteries. Traditional methods of identifying suitable concentrations are inefficient, especially for multiple-solute systems. The proposed freeze concentration process allows for the efficient and rational design of electrolyte concentrations by concentrating dilute solutions through ice or hydrate precipitation at target low temperatures. This method was successfully demonstrated in H2O–LiCl, H2O–NaClO4, and H2O–NaClO4–NaCF3COO systems, showing superior performance in Li-based and Na-based full cells. This work provides a universal and efficient strategy for designing electrolyte concentrations for aqueous batteries. This project developed new aqueous electrolyte systems based on inherently low-cost and eco-friendly materials for high-voltage aqueous battery applications, and created comprehensive understanding of the degradation mechanism of new aqueous electrolytes to guide further improvement for low-cost, sustainable and high-energy aqueous batteries. Objective 2: We investigated how different terminal groups and the number of functional groups in crowding agents influence agent-agent and H2O-agent intermolecular interactions, thus determining electrolyte conductivity and voltage window. Techniques such as linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy were used to probe these interactions. The findings showed that weak interactions between crowding agents decrease viscosity and increase conductivity, while strong H2O-crowding agent interactions weaken the hydrogen bond strength of H2O-H2O, thereby increasing the O-H covalent bond strength of H2O and improving the electrolyte's electrochemical voltage window. The PEGDME450 electrolyte demonstrated superior safety and ionic conductivity compared to conventional polymer electrolytes. The project illustrated the design principles of high-voltage and high-conductivity molecular crowding electrolytes, showing that weak crowding agent-crowding agent interactions lead to low viscosity and high conductivity, while strong H2O-crowding agent interactions widen the voltage window. The PEGDME450 molecular crowding electrolyte achieved a higher ionic conductivity (2.4 mS cm−1) and a stable voltage window (3.2 V) compared to the PEG400 molecular crowding electrolyte (0.8 mS cm−1, 3.2 V). Objective 3: We probed the influence of the solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on battery performance using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM). The findings revealed that the SEI film helps protect the anode by inhibiting hydrogen evolution, confirmed by LSV and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data. The decomposition of TFSI anion before hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) was observed, indicating its role as a protective layer. The project demonstrated that the SEI film on the L-LTO electrode developed a new F 1s component attributed to LiF after cycling, and the C=O and C-O signals increased due to the decomposition of PEGDME. HRTEM images showed that the cycled L-LTO surface was covered by a 5nm-thickness amorphous SEI, which helps protect the anode by inhibiting hydrogen evolution. Objective 4: We developed an efficient ceramic surface coating (LiAlO2) to further improve the cycling stability of full aqueous Li-ion batteries. The coating effectively inhibited hydrogen evolution, as confirmed by LSV measurements and online electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS) monitoring. The LSV test of pristine, LiAlO2, Al2O3, and LATP-coated LTO electrodes showed that the LiAlO2 coating was the most effective in suppressing hydrogen evolution. This strategy demonstrated superior effectiveness compared to other coatings like Al2O3 and LATP. The project also explored other strategies, including co-solvent strategy to improve ionic conductivity, pH adjustment to further expand the voltage window, and gel pre-coating methods to stabilize graphite/lithium metal. Objective 5: We successfully assembled full cells using the PEGDME450 electrolyte, achieving high power, high energy density, and non-flammability. The PEGDME450 molecular crowding electrolyte was non-flammable, demonstrating superior safety compared to commercial LiPF6 in ethylene carbonate (EC)/diethyl carbonate (DEC) electrolyte. The full cells showed excellent long-term cycling stability and superior performance compared to PEG400-based electrolytes. The L-LTO-LMO full cell in the PEGDME450 electrolyte achieved a capacity of 50 mAh g-1 and an energy density of 120 Wh kg−1 at 1 C, with excellent cycling stability for 300 cycles at 1 C and 800 cycles at 5 C. The degradation mechanisms were investigated using OEMS, revealing the elimination of common side reactions (HER/OER) during cell operation. The project also examined the influence of SEI on battery performance, showing that the SEI film helps protect the anode by inhibiting hydrogen evolution. Overall, the project objectives have been fully addressed, with significant advancements in the development of low-cost, eco-friendly aqueous electrolytes, understanding of structure-property-performance relationships, and improvement of battery performance and safety. The research provides a comprehensive foundation for further development of high-energy, sustainable aqueous batteries.

The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows:

Develop structure-property-performance relationship of WMP aqueous electrolyte system by correlating the water-polymer bonding interaction to the electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity and flammability of WMP electrolytes.

Investigate the effects of anion on the (a) ionic conductivity of WMP electrolytes; (b) chemical stability of SEI formation in the WMP electrolytes; and (c) corrosion effect of current collector in WMP electrolytes.

Develop four strategies to further improve the developed WMP electrolytes, including co-solvent strategy to improve ionic conductivity, pH adjustment to further expand voltage window, ceramic surface coating, and gel pre-coating methods to stabilize graphite/lithium metal.
Develop WMP-based full aqueous Li-ion batteries, perform full cell safety and abuse tests, and investigate its degradation mechanisms.

14304520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304520.value: We study the use of cost-effective and environmentally friendly water-miscible polymer molecular crowding agents to replace highly concentrated salts in electrochemical energy storage devices. This approach aims to suppress water decomposition, a common issue in electrochemical devices. The study focuses on understanding how the structure of water-miscible polymer crowding agents, specifically their terminal groups and chain lengths, affects the key properties of electrolytes, such as conductivity and voltage window. We developed a new crowding agent, polyethylene glycol dimethyl ether (PEGDME) 450, which demonstrated significantly higher conductivity (2.4 mS cm−1) compared to the state-of-the-art polyethylene glycol (PEG) 400 (0.8 mS cm−1), without compromising the voltage window (3.2 V). This new electrolyte enabled high-power and high-voltage aqueous Li4Ti5O12/LiMn2O4 cells to operate efficiently for 800 cycles, showcasing a universal strategy for advanced aqueous electrolyte design and high-performance batteries. To enable wide operating temperature aqueous batteries, we apply the design concept into aqueous potassium-ion batteries (AKIBs) as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage due to their low cost and high safety. The newly proposed 10 m KCF3COO electrolyte has a low freezing point (−35.5 °C) and high average ice formation energy, resulting in high energy density (56.3 Wh/kg at 25 °C, 41.9 Wh/kg at −35 °C) and a long lifespan (87.5% capacity retention over 1000 cycles at −35 °C). In addition, we developed anti-freezing electrolyte concentrations for low-temperature aqueous batteries. Traditional methods of identifying suitable concentrations are inefficient, especially for multiple-solute systems. The proposed freeze concentration process allows for the efficient and rational design of electrolyte concentrations by concentrating dilute solutions through ice or hydrate precipitation at target low temperatures. This method was successfully demonstrated in H2O–LiCl, H2O–NaClO4, and H2O–NaClO4–NaCF3COO systems, showing superior performance in Li-based and Na-based full cells. This work provides a universal and efficient strategy for designing electrolyte concentrations for aqueous batteries. This project developed new aqueous electrolyte systems based on inherently low-cost and eco-friendly materials for high-voltage aqueous battery applications, and created comprehensive understanding of the degradation mechanism of new aqueous electrolytes to guide further improvement for low-cost, sustainable and high-energy aqueous batteries.

14304520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304520.value: Further research could be placed on the development and practical application of the developed electrolytes for energy storage. This involves large-scale synthesis and production, ensuring cost-effective and sustainable methods. Partner with battery manufacturers to incorporate the advanced electrolytes into existing battery designs. Conduct extensive testing under real-world conditions to evaluate performance, safety, and longevity. Focus on applications such as electric vehicles, grid storage, and portable electronics, ensuring the new electrolytes meet industry standards and requirements. Optimize the electrolyte composition to further lower the freezing point and enhance electrode stability. Explore the use of the developed aqueous batteries in cold climate regions and for backup power in critical infrastructure, ensuring they maintain high energy density and long lifespan under extreme conditions. Additionally, environmental and economic impact assessments will support the benefits of the new technology. Forming research consortia, securing funding, launching pilot projects, obtaining regulatory approval, and developing marketing strategies will drive the successful integration of these advanced electrolytes into practical applications, leading to more efficient, sustainable, and high-performance energy storage solutions.

14304520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304520.value: Replacing flammable nonaqueous electrolytes with non-flammable aqueous electrolytes is an effective approach to alleviate the safety concerns of conventional nonaqueous Li-ion batteries and reduce materials and manufacturing costs. This project aims to develop new strategies to develop low-cost and eco-friendly aqueous electrolytes with a wide voltage-window to achieve high energy and sustainable aqueous batteries. We several new aqueous electrolyte systems that are low-cost and suitable for wide-temperature applications. For instance, we developed a water-miscible polymer crowding agent, polyethylene glycol dimethyl ether (PEGDME) 450, which demonstrated significantly higher conductivity (2.4 mS cm−1) compared to the state-of-the-art polyethylene glycol (PEG) 400 (0.8 mS cm−1), without compromising the voltage window (3.2 V). This new electrolyte enabled high-power and high-voltage aqueous Li4Ti5O12/LiMn2O4 cells to operate efficiently for 800 cycles, showcasing a universal strategy for advanced aqueous electrolyte design and high-performance batteries. The next steps involve optimizing the additives, scaling up production, and integrating these advanced electrolytes into commercial batteries for real-world applications like renewable energy storage. Overall, this project leads to safer, and more efficient batteries for a wide range of applications.

14304820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304820.value: Plate bending occurs ubiquitously within incoming plates before they enter subduction zones. The bending-induced faults provide pathways for water to enter subducting plates and eventually into the Earth’s interior, indeed the only way of transporting water into deep Earth, which plays critical roles in material cycling in the Earth system. Moreover, bending-induced faults in the outer rise may generate large earthquakes that may trigger devastating tsunami and more damaging megathrust earthquakes. Therefore, understanding plate bending and faulting is not only important for our Earth system, but also critical for seismic and tsunami hazard. However, they are less understood compared with megathrust earthquakes because of infrequent occurrence and the lack of near-field data. In the proposed work, Ocean Bottom Seismograph (OBS) will be used to detect and locate earthquakes near the Challenger Deep, the deepest spot (~10.9 km) on Earth, in the southern Mariana subduction zone. Using OBS on the overriding plate, we have identified a group of outer-rise earthquakes. Here we add new data from OBS located on the incoming plate and will derive a local shear wave velocity model, which can definitely improve the location accuracies of outer-rise earthquakes so as to better delineate faults in the region. We will also develop a 3D plate bending model by incorporating curvatures of trench and slab, based on which we will compute stress concentration within the incoming plate so as to better understand how outer-rise faults were formed and activated. The anticipated results will not only advance our understanding of the plate bending and faults in southern Mariana, but will also produce a high-resolution local shear wave velocity model and seismic dataset allowing for further investigations to better understand material cycling and subduction zone dynamics. Such work is of significant societal relevance as it can advance our understanding of earthquake physics and subduction zone dynamics, which is critical for mitigating risk associated with strong-shaking and tsunami generation of subduction zone earthquakes. One graduate student and one postdoc fellow will be supported and trained to conduct seismic data analysis and to develop the 3D numerical model of plate bending, respectively. All research from this project will be presented at professional meetings, and the work will be integrated into the teaching curriculum of H. 14304820.label: Realisation of objectives
14304820.value: To tackle the above scientific objectives, we have used the near-field Ocean Bottom Seismograph (OBS) data to investigate seismic structure and estimate the degree of hydration in the southern Mariana subduction zone. In addition, we have applied machine learning technique to detect arrivals of P and S waves, for the first time on OBS data in the region, and then performed high-resolution relocations of outer-rise earthquakes. Furthermore, we have developed an algorithm to compute 3-D bending of the incoming plate by incorporating curvatures of trench and slab, based on which we derive stress conditions within the incoming plate. One graduate student and two postdocs are trained during the project, who are leading authors of the following work. (1) Deriving a S-wave model using near-field OBS data We first derive the S-wave structure across the Challenge Deep in the southern Mariana subduction zone using 12 broadband OBS data. Both surface wave tomography (Zhu et al., 2021 GRL) and body wave travel time tomography (Wang et al., 2024 Tectonophysics) were used, and the two independent approaches got consistent results. The new S-wave velocity model clearly shows velocity reduction in the upper mantle of the incoming plate, which is characterized by velocities as low as 3.6 km/s in the outer rise. Based on the experimental relationship between seismic velocities and serpentinization degree, shear wave velocities of 3.6–4.1 km/s are likely related to the serpentinization of ∼19–41 vol% (i.e., ∼1.9–4.3 wt%). We therefore interpret the seismic images as the evidence for a 25-km-thick, partially serpentinized (∼1.9–4.3 wt% water) slab-mantle zone near the trench. Our interpretation of serpentinization extending to depths of ∼32 km below the seafloor in the incoming plate indicates great hydration (water content) of the incoming plate at the southern Mariana. Our results have fully addressed objective 1. (2) High-resolution earthquake location in the outer rise To further improve the accuracy of earthquake location in the outer-rise, we use data recorded by the near-field OBS network. We apply two machine-learning-based phase pickers (PhaseNet and EQTransformer) in the data and then derive a high-resolution earthquake catalog. The newly relocated outer-rise earthquakes provide unique constraints on the distribution and depth extent of the outer-rise faults. We find the clear along-trench variation of seismicity in the outer rise. Despite the pervasive normal faults, the seismicity shows one cluster extending to nearly 60 km in depth (Chen et al., 2022, GRL). We infer that these are normal faulting earthquakes by comparing the waveform similarity of events at different depths, which is the first case of extensional faults at such depth and thus is highlighted by EOS of American Geophysical Union. Objective no.2 has been fully addressed. (3) Developing a 3-D plate bending model and compute stress conditions within the incoming plate We have developed a 3D model of the entire Mariana subduction zone to estimate the hydration degree from the yielding depths of normal faults (Zhang et al., 2021, Tectonophysics). By calculating bending stress and brittle failure of the incoming plate, we find that the yield zone depth increases from the northern to southern Mariana trench (16-20 km). Consequently the water flux is estimated to be ~15% greater at the southern Mariana trench than in the north. We also extend the 3D model by considering along-strike variation in slab geometry and find that the variation of plate deflection along the trench may cause the change of the direction of the maximum extensional bending stress in the variable zone which provides greater possibilities for reactivation of preexisting weak faults, resulting in unevenly distributed outer rise earthquakes, reactivation of remnant fabric or earthquake. (Zhang et al., 2023, Tectonophysics). These results addressed objectives 3 and 4. We also apply such 3D model in other settings such as the transition zone from subduction to collision (Zhang et al., 2022, GRL). The results demonstrate how orogeny and boundary loading influence inter-plate stress, plate bending, and seismicity. (4) Intermediate-depth earthquakes We have extended our original objectives to intermediate-depth earthquakes in Mariana, Manila, and Yap subduction zones. By applying the state-of-the-arts machine learning phase pickers, we successfully build high-resolution earthquake catalogs in these subduction zones from which we delineate the slab geometry and its associated dynamic mechanisms. In southern Mariana, we have located 1172 events and found a contrast of event depths from east to west. Near the Caroline segment a single seismic zone was identified while in the Pacific segment double seismic zones existed. The difference is likely caused by the different hydration degree of the incoming plate (Chen et al., 2024 EGU). We also conducted similar seismic research in the Manila Trench (Zhu et al., 2023, SRL) and the Yap Trench (Zhu et al., 2024, SRL). In the Manila Trench, we find that most slab-related earthquakes gradually deepen to approximately 200 km southward along the trench, indicating slab tears related to the extinct mid-ocean ridge or sharp bending of the slab. In the Yap Trench, using one year of OBS data, we located 712 out of the 2,138 detected events. A large number of earthquakes occurred on the inner trench slope, while some occurred on the outer rise. Notably, the seismicity delineates a nearly vertical subducted slab in the Yap Trench, likely related to the blocking of the buoyant Caroline Plateau. In summary, we have successfully achieved the original objectives of the project, providing new scientific insights into the tectonics process and earthquakes at the southernmost Mariana subduction zone. Additionally, we have expanded our research to other subduction zones to explore the interactions between subduction zones and continental margins. Furthermore, we have made new advancements in data utilization and methodological innovation, demonstrating the effectiveness of machine learning based methods on OBS data.

14304820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304820.value: We published 9 papers in peer-review journals, with CUHK authors leading or corresponding to 8. One PhD student (Han Chen) graduated during the project and two postdoc researchers (Gaohua Zhu and Jiangyang Zhang) were trained. Dr. Gaohua Zhu became a research professor at the Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Science. Dr. Jiangyang Zhang became a Research Associate Professor at the South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Science. Our major findings include determination of seismic structure (Zhu et al., 2021 GRL; Wang et al., 2024 Tectonophysics) and development of 3D bending models (Zhang et al., 2021 and Zhang et al., 2023 Tectonophysics) in the southern Mariana subduction zone, which were used to estimate the hydration degree of the incoming plate. We also identified a deep earthquake cluster in the outer rise (Chen et al., 2022 GRL), the first of its kind and thus being highlighted highlighted by EOS of American Geophysical Union. Furthermore, we carried out comparative studies in Manila and Yap subduction zones (Zhu et al., 2023 and Zhu et al., 2024 SRL) and highlighted the effects of incoming plate on subduction dynamics.

14304820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304820.value: Intermediate-depth earthquakes in the southern and central Mariana should be further investigated to advance our understanding of mechanisms of these earthquakes and subduction zone dynamics.

14304820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304820.value: The southernmost Mariana subduction zone hosts the deepest spot on Earth, Challenger Deep, with water depth of ~11 km. It remains mysterious partly because nearby observations were not available. We have conducted the first near-field seismic experiments and derived high-resolution earthquake locations using the state-of-the-art machine-learning techniques. Together with our newly developed three dimensional plate bending model, we have revealed the subducting plate geometry, degree of water being carried into subduction zones, and mechanisms controlling the subduction plate geometry and dynamics. We also find a deep earthquake cluster in the outer rise of the incoming plate, shedding new insights on how much water was stored in the subducting plate.

14305420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305420.value: Chirality is an important issue in life sciences as well as modern organic chemistry. Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric reaction is a promising strategy to obtain enantiomerically enriched compounds to support the ever-growing needs of pharmaceutical industry. Although carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, are finding many important applications in supramolecular design, optoelectronics, nanomaterials, boron neutron capture therapy agents and organometallic/coordination chemistry, the study of chiral-at-cage carboranes is still very rare, which is mainly restricted to chiral resolution due to the absence of asymmetric synthetic methods. Different from the general sense of chiral organic molecules, chirality of icosahedral carboranes is determined by the substitution patterns on the polyhedron as the addition of substituents to o-carborane cage can lower the symmetry of the resultant molecules. For example, the presence of a substituent at the position 4/5 of 1-substituted o-carborane results in the chirality of the cage molecule. Very recently, we report an efficient method to achieve chiral-at-cage o-carboranes with high regio- and enantio-selectivity by a strategy of palladium-catalyzed asymmetric intramolecular B−H arylation. This proof-of-concept study represents the first example of the enantioselective reaction on carboranes, providing an efficient way for the construction of chiral-at-cage compounds with new skeletons (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2018, 140, 4508-4511). On this basis, we plan in this proposal to systematically develop enantioselective synthetic methods for the facile preparation of chiral-at-cage carboranes via transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric and regioselective cage B−H functionalization. The role of transition metals and chiral ligands in the above asymmetric catalysis will be examined to understand structure/reactivity/selectivity relationships and associated reaction mechanisms. The resultant chiral molecules bearing chiral-at-cage carborane moiety could be used as chiral ligands for asymmetric catalysis or bioactive compounds for drug screening. It is anticipated that the results of this research would enhance our fundamental understanding of the chirality of polyhedral molecules and open new avenues to carborane chemistry. 手性是生命科學與現代有機化學的一個重要命題。為了滿足製藥工業對於高對映純度化合物日益增長的需求，過渡金屬催化的不對稱反應是一種極具發展潛力的策略。作為一類碳硼分子簇，碳硼烷在超分子設計、光電子、納米材料、硼中子捕獲治療及金屬有機/配位化學等領域有着非常重要的應用。然而，由於缺乏不對稱合成方法，籠手性碳硼烷的獲得局限於手性拆分，因此關於籠手性碳硼烷的研究仍然十分罕見。 不同于手性有機分子的一般識別方法，二十面體碳硼烷的手性取決於多面體上的取代基分佈模式，因為增加鄰碳硼烷籠上的取代基會降低所得分子的對稱性。例如，1-取代鄰碳硼烷的4位/5位存在一個取代基時，這個籠分子便具有了手性。近期，我們通過鈀催化不對稱分子內硼-氫鍵芳基化的策略，以高區域選擇性和對映選擇性實現了籠手性鄰碳硼烷的高效合成。這個概念驗證性研究代表了第一例碳硼烷的對映選擇性反應，為構築籠手性化合物新骨架提供了一種有效的途徑 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2018, 140, 4508-4511)。在此基礎上，我們計畫通過過渡金屬催化的不對稱及區域選擇性籠硼-氫鍵官能團化，系統性地發展立體選擇性合成方法，以期實現簡單快捷地製備籠手性碳硼烷。在上述不對稱催化中，我們將會對過渡金屬和手性配體的作用進行研究，從而來理解結構/反應性/選擇性之間的關係和與之關聯的反應機理。反應所得含有籠手性碳硼烷基團的手性分子，可作為手性配體用於不對稱催化，或者作為生物活性化合物用於藥物篩選。我們期望這項研究的結果將會增加我們對於多面體分子手性的基本理解，開闢碳硼烷化學的新方向和新領域。

14305420.label: Realisation of objectives
14305420.value: Carboranes are finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed toward the area of carborane functionalization. In this project, we have developed new methodologies for region- and enatio-selective cage boron functionalization of o-carboranes via transition metal catalysis. One needs to solve the regioselectivity problem before tackling the enantioselectivity issue. Otherwise, a mixture of regioisomers and enantiomers will be generated. In this regarding, we have developed several methods for regioselective cage BH functionalization via transition metal (Ir, Rh or Pd) catalysis, realizing annulation, alkylation, alkenylation and amination using diverse coupling agents. With carboxyl as directing group, a regioselective and atom-economy iridium-catalyzed alkyne annulation of o-carboranes has been developed, leading to the synthesis of a series of carboranoisocoumarin derivatives in high yields with broard substrate scope. These new carborano-isocoumarins enrich the family of isocoumarins for biological evaluations. On the other hand, the products could be further transformed to polyaromatic arenes via Scholl coupling reaction. A highly efficient Ir-catalyzed regioselective cage B(4)−H acylmethylation of o-carboranyl acids with sulfoxonium has been developed under redox neutral conditions, leading to the preparation of a large class of B(4)-acylmethylated o-carborane. The-COOH moiety serves as the traceless directing group and controls the regioselectivity and monoselectivity. Assisted by picolyl group, an efficient Ir-catalyzed cage boron alkenylation of 1-(2’-picolyl)-o-carboranes with diarylacetylenes has been developed, leading to a wide variety of B–H geminal addition products via 1,2-carbon migration of alkynes. On the other hand, with a very low palladium catalyst loading, a picolyl group enabled B(3,5)-dialkenylation and B(4)-monoalkenylation of o-carboranes has been developed. The steric effect of cage carbon substituents has a great impact on the regioselectivity and the degree of substitution in such two alkenylation reactions. Besides construction of B-C bonds, B-N bonds at B(3) or B(4) vertices were built smoothly through transition metal catalysis. With the assistance of carboxyl directing group, two catalytic systems for regioselective B(3/4)-amination of o-carboranes with free amines were established. In the presence of Ir(III), a batch of B(4)-aminated o-carboranes have been prepared, while a Rh(III) catalytic system led to a range of secondary carboranyl amines. Employing anthranils as aminating agents, an Ir(III)-catalyzed selective cage B4−H amination has been developed under mild conditions without any oxidants. In the absence of directing group, an efficient and convenient strategy for Ir-catalyzed selective B(3)-amination of o-carboranes with amines via acceptorless BH/NH dehydrocoupling has been developed with H2 gas as a sole by-product. Such an oxidant-free system endues the protocol sustainability, atom-economy and environmental friendliness. The asymmetrical version of these aforementioned reactions is under investigation. Our proof-of-concept study has shown that utilization of commonly used chiral phosphine ligands could lead to the feasible construction of chirality-at-cage in a palladium-catalyzed asymmetric intramolecular B–H arylation and cyclization process. We speculate that such strategy can be extended to intermolecular cage B-H functionalization transformations, leading to the formation of a wide range of chiral cage B-substituted carboranes. Accordingly, an acylamino-enabled intermolecular asymmetric B(5)-alkenylation of 1-acylamino-o-carboranes with internal alkynes was accomplished in the presence of an iridium catalyst and a chiral (S)-phosphoramidite ligand. This synthetic approach led to the formation of a batch of (S)-B(5)-alkenyl-o-carboranes with remarkable yields and enantioselectivity. Detailed computational analysis revealed that the transition state TS-S was 4.1 kcal/mol more energetically favorable than TS-R. This disparity can be attributed to the presence of additional C-H...π interactions in TS-S, enhancing its stability eventually. Based on the results of control experiments and isolation of the key intermediates, a possible reaction mechanism is then proposed, involving a six-membered iridacycle. Following the same strategy, an asymmetric (S)-B(4)-alkenylation of 3-acylamino-o-carboranes with diarylacetylenes was achieved via iridium catalysis under mild reaction conditions with excellent efficiency and enantioselectivity. DFT calculations demonstrated that the transition state TS-S for (S)-B(4)-alkenylation exhibited greater thermodynamic stability compared to the transition state TS-R for (R)-B(7)-alkenylation by a margin of 3.8 kcal/mol. It was suggested that the electronic characteristics of the hydridic B−H bond might exert significant impact on the enantioselectivity of this reaction. In summary, we have developed two new methods on the basis of transition metal catalyzed cage B-H activation with assistance of chiral phosphine ligands for the preparation of a series of chiral-at-cage carborane molecules, which might find valuable applications in many realms. The related reaction mechanisms have also been investigated through the combination of control experiments and DFT calculations. The results offer a better fundamental understanding of the chirality of polyhedral molecules, which in turn would shed light on how to control the enantio- and regio-selectivity for the effective synthesis of target products. This project has been very successfully carried out and all objectives have been achieved.
