14305420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305420.value: (1) Development of enantioselective cage B-alkenylation functionalization of o-carboranes via Ir catalysis (Pub. #1 and #8): The first intermolecular asymmetric B−H functionalization of 1-acetylamino-o-carborane with alkynes has been developed via Ir catalysis for enantioselective synthesis of chiral-at-cage o-carboranes with up to 99% ee. This work successfully explored the potential of asymmetric synthesis beyond conventional organic chemistry into the chemistry of chiral-at-cage o-carboranes. An Ir-catalyzed asymmetrical (S)-B(4)-alkenylation of 3-acylamino-o-carboranes with diarylacetylenes has been achieved in high efficiency and enantioselectivity. (2) Development of regioselective cage B functionalization of o-carboranes via transition metal catalysis (Pub. #6, #9, #10, #11, #14, #17 and #18): An iridium-catalyzed alkyne annulation of o-carboranyl carboxylic acids has been developed, synthesizing a class of carboranoisocoumarins in high yields. Using sulfoxonium ylides as alkylating regents, an Ir-catalyzed regioselective cage B(4)−H acylmethylation of o-carboranyl acids has been developed. Through Ir or Pd catalysis, cage boron mono-/di-alkenylation of 1-(2’-picolyl)-o-carboranes with diarylacetylenes has been developed. Regioselective cage B(3/4)-H amination of o-carboranyl carboxy acids with free amines or anthranils have been realized via Ir/Rh-catalysis efficiently. Through acceptorless BH/NH dehydrocoupling strategy, an Ir-catalyzed B(3)-amination of original o-carboranes with amines has been developed with H2 as a sole by-product. (3) Development of selective cage B functionalization of o-carboranes via base metal catalysis (Pub. #5): The first example of Fe-catalyzed intramolecular B–H/C–H dehydrogenative cyclization of o-carboranyl amides has been developed, furnishing diverse C,B-substituted carborane fused phenanthroline derivatives. (4) Development of selective cage B functionalization of o-carboranes via Pd catalysis combined with visible light (Pub. #12).: Cage B(3/4/9)-centered carboranyl radicals have been generated smoothly from iodo-o-carboranes via a visible-light-promoted palladium(0)/palladium(I) pathway, which serve as vital intermediates for various cage B-(hetero)arylated o-carboranes. (5) Understanding the reaction mechanisms (Pub. #1, #8 and #17):Control experiments and DFT calculations indicated that chiral phosphine ligands play a crucial role in the control of enantioselectivity. In summary, this original work has resulted in 19 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including Nat. Commun. (x1), Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (x 1), Acc. Chem. Res. (x1), ACS Catal. (x2), J. Org. Chem. (x2), Bull Chem. Soc. Jpn (x1), Org. Lett. (x4), Chem.Commun. (x2), Org. Chem. Front (x1), Chem. Asian J. (x2), Adv. Catal. (x1) and Synthesis (x1). Two PhD students are under training, of which one will be graduated in Aug 2024. PI/Co-PI has been invited to give 3 lectures at international conference.

14305420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305420.value: Diverse reactions for regioselective cage B functionalization of o-carboranes via transition or base metal catalysis with/without combination of visible light have been achieved. We wonder if these transformations could be explored into asymmetric versions.

14305420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305420.value: Chirality is an important issue in life sciences as well as modern organic chemistry. Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric reaction is a promising strategy to obtain enantiomerically enriched compounds to support the ever-growing needs of pharmaceutical industry. Although carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, are finding many important applications in supramolecular design, optoelectronics, nanomaterials, boron neutron capture therapy agents and organometallic/coordination chemistry, the study of chiral-at-cage carboranes is still very rare, which is mainly restricted to chiral resolution due to the absence of asymmetric synthetic methods. In this project, we have developed several asymmetric transformations for the construction of chirality at o-carborane cage, leading to the invention of several methods for the efficient synthesis of a large class of cage B functionalized o-carboranes with excellent enantioselectivity under mild conditions. The results of this research would enhance our fundamental understanding of the chirality of polyhedral molecules and open new avenues to carborane chemistry.

14305520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305520.value: 這項提議的工作的目的, 是開發基於路易斯配合物的高效非典型氫鍵有機催化劑, 並且應用於各種化學轉化。 非典型氫鍵供體通常源自與吸電子取代基非常接近的碳氫鍵。眾所周知的非典型氫鍵供體例子, 是四烷基銨鹽中氮原子旁的碳氫鍵。與常見的布朗斯台德酸性的典型氫鍵不同, 非典型氫鍵為非布朗斯台德酸性。由於碳氫鍵的高鍵能, 非典型氫鍵供體一般比較穩定。非典型氫鍵供體可以通過非共價相互作用輕鬆地與電子供體（例如羰基氧）相互作用。 在催化化學轉化中, 引入非共價相互作用已引起了科學界越來越多的關注。一個新興的研究領域涉及非典型氫鍵供體在有機催化中的應用。非典型氫鍵具有高方向性和疏水性。此外, 非典型氫鍵具有布朗斯台德弱酸性性質, 增加了它們在化學轉化中官能團的相容性。有機催化劑也被認為是金屬催化劑的綠色替代品。 非典型氫鍵系統的氫鍵強度和空間需求很容易調節, 使其成為具有吸引力的非典型氫鍵催化劑的開發平台。在文獻中, 有一些使用四烷基銨鹽作為非典型氫鍵催化劑加速反應的例子。但是, 這些非典型氫鍵催化劑的強度通常較弱, 因為其陰離子（例如, 氯化四甲基銨中的氯離子）仍與銨部分相互作用並毒害非典型氫鍵。 近年來, 我們的研究小組從事基於非共價鍵有機催化的開發（例如 Yeung, Y.-Y. et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3485; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 12869）。我們還成功發現兩性離子是有效的非典型氫鍵催化劑（Yeung, Y.-Y. et al. ACS Catal. 2019, 9, 8083）。儘管兩性離子可以在酯化反應中通過非典型氫鍵活化羰基，但我們的目標是開發更強大的非典型氫鍵供體，以更廣泛地應用。 最近, 在一項未發表的工作中, 我們發現源自路易斯配合物的非典型氫鍵供體可以有效激活烯酮和N-溴代琥珀酰亞胺的羰基, 並分別催化Diels-Alder反應和親電鹵化反應。從胺和三氟化硼之間的反應可以很容易地製備路易斯配合物。它們的非典型氫鍵強度要比源自四烷基銨鹽的非典型氫鍵供體的強度高得多, 這歸因於有效地分離了陰離子, 從而避免了非典型氫鍵的毒害化。基於這些試驗結果, 在這項擬議的工作中, 我們計劃進一步開發和探索路易斯配合物非典型氫鍵催化劑在各種轉化中的應用。我們預期新的催化方案將成為有機合成中的有力工具。

14305520.label: Realisation of objectives
14305520.value: 1. Prepare a series of non-classical hydrogen bond organocatalysts. At the initial stage of the project, we prepared some non-classical hydrogen bond (NCHB) donors by reacting Lewis bases with boron compounds. For example, reaction of tricyclohexylphosphine oxide with boron trifluoride gave trialkylphosphonium oxoborate (TOB) in 85% yield. The structure of TOB was unambiguously be confirmed by an X-ray crystallographic study. Stability of TOB was then studied by treating it with water. TOB was dissolved in water for two days and the water was then removed under high vacuum. The proton and heteroatom NMR experiments showed no change in chemical shift of the respective signals before and after the water treatment. These results indicate that the complex is not in equilibrium with its Lewis base/Lewis acid components and does not decompose under moisture and aqueous environment. To further investigate the NCHB between our newly design complex and electron donor, we performed a 1H NMR titration experiment between TOB and chlorodiphenylmethane. The result of the titration showed a clear up-field chemical shift of the alkyl C-Hs of TOB upon the addition of chlorodiphenylmethane. We believe that the chemical shift is due to the interaction between the chloride in chlorodiphenylmethane and the C-Hs in TOB via NCHB, resulting in the up-field shift due to the shielding effect. 2. Examine the performance of the non-classical hydrogen bond organocatalysts in various transformations that involve the activation of carbonyls and imines. The catalytic ability of the TOB complex in Diels-Alder reaction were investigated. In the absence of a catalyst, the Diels-Alder reaction between acrolein and 2,3-dimethyl-1,3-butadiene proceeded was sluggish. In the presence of the TOB catalyst, the desired product was obtained in good yield. We also studied other phosphonium salts including tetraalkyl- and tetraarylphosphonium halide salts, and the performance of these catalysts was far inferior to that of the TOB complex. We further optimized the Diels-Alder reaction catalyzed by the TOB complex using different solvent systems. Generally, the chlorinated solvents gave better performance than in non-polar solvents. To further expand the utility of the TOB, we next investigated the catalytic ability of acetalization of alcohol and thiol and good yields of the desired products were obtained. We believed the absence of the free counter anion in the TOB, the alpha-hydrogens are more available to activate the benzyl alcohol for acetalization. Satisfactory performance was still observed even when the catalyst loading was reduced to 0.1 mol%. The scope of the acetalization was then expanded by using different alcohols. In general, the reaction worked well with benzyl alcohols bearing various substituents including halogens, alkyl, nitro, and ether. These reactions were compatible with both dihydropyran and dihydrofuran. Substituted phenols were also studied and the corresponding products were obtained in good-to-excellent yields. Other hydrocarbon alcohols bearing alkyl, cycloalkyl, olefin, and alkyne were well-tolerated under the catalytic protocol. Other than alcohol, thiols were also examined and satisfactory performance was observed. Since the catalyst is non-Brønsted acidic, acid-sensitive functional groups well-survived under the catalytic protocol. In a study using equimolar amounts of 4-methylphenol and 4-methylthiophenol together with dihydropyran in chloroform, S-acetal product was obtained as the dominated product using 0.2 mol% of TOB or BF3 as a catalyst. Interestingly, when the less polar solvent toluene was used, 48% O-acetal product was obtained and no S-acetal product was formed when using the TOB catalyst. The yield of O-acetal product was improved by prolonging the reaction time. Satisfactory performance could also be achieved by using 1 mol% of TOB for 24 h. In contrast, a mixture of O-acetal and S-acetal products was obtained when using the Lewis acid catalyst BF3 in toluene. The Brønsted acid catalyst camphorsulfonic acid (CSA) was also examined and the chemoselectivity was unsatisfactory. These results clearly show that: (1) the TOB catalyst appears to have different catalytic mechanisms compared with typical Lewis or Brønsted acid catalysts; (2) the catalytic performance of TOB is not due to trace Lewis or Brønsted acid. Competition experiments were then performed with different combinations of alcohols and thiols. To our delight, excellent chemoselectivity was observed in various examples using alcohols/thiols bearing the same substituents. Satisfactory chemoselectivity was also obtained with alcohols and thiols with different substituents. In particular, in the competition experiment using 2-tert-butylphenol and 2-methylthiophenol, the less bulky 2-methylthiophenol reacted to give the corresponding thioacetal (56%) as the sole product using BF3 as the catalyst, attributed to the steric effect. In sharp contrast, the inherent preference was overridden with the TOB catalyst; the O-acetal product was obtained in 76% yield and no S-acetal product was detected. It is intriguing that the TOB catalyst shows chemoselectivity in distinguishing the structurally similar alcohol and thiol. Thus, NMR studies were also performed to compare the interactions between the TOB and different alcohols/thiols. It was found that the TOB readily interacts with the alcohols as indicated by the magnitude of TOB C(sp3)–H chemical shift. In contrast, the chemical shift was much less significant when the alcohols were replaced with thiols. Based on these results, it appears that the NCHB from TOB C(sp3)–H favors the interaction with oxygen over sulfur, which follows the hard-soft acid-base principle. We believe that the TOB catalyst can effectively promote O-acetalization over S-acetalization because of the specific alignment of the oxygenated reactants in the oxyanion hole by multiple NCHBs in the favorable trilateral complex. During the research endeavor, we also developed some catalytic protocols based on NCHB catalysis. These include the phosphonium salt-catalyzed rearrangement of cyclopropene carboxylic acids, olefin isomerization, and aerobic oxidation of hydroxyl compounds. 3. Explore the asymmetric variants of the transformations using the chiral nonclassical hydrogen bond organocatalysts. By taking advantage of the NCHB interaction of onium salt, we have developed a catalyst-controlled enantiodivergent bromolactonization with both (R)- and (S)-products in good yield and optical purity. Quinine-derived amino-amides bearing the same chiral core but different achiral aryl substituents were used as the catalysts. Switching the methoxy substituent in the aryl amide system from meta- to ortho-position results in a complete switch in asymmetric induction to afford the desired lactone in good enantioselectivity and yield. Mechanistic studies suggest that the amides in the 2,3,4-trimethoxyphenyl catalyst and the 2,4,6-trimethyloxyphenyl catalyst might serve different functions, leading to the enantiodivergent behavior. In addition, the NCHB was found to be crucial to stabilize the transition state in the major pathway. This research highlights the importance of NCHB that can dictate the stereoselectivity in asymmetric reactions. 4. Publish the results in world-class peer-reviewed international journals Under this project, six publications including Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 7353-7357, Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 9533-9537, ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 3498-3506, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2021, 143, 12745-12754, J. Org. Chem. 2021, 86, 1183, and Chem. Sci. 2023, 14, 12684-12692 were produced. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes is shown below.

14305520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305520.value: 1. The use of trialkylphosphonium oxoborates (TOB) as catalysts is reported. The site-isolated borate counter anion in a TOB catalyst increases the availability of C(sp3)–H to interact with electron donor substrates. The catalytic protocol is applicable to a wide range of substrates in the acetalization reaction and provides excellent chemoselectivity in the acetalization over thioacetalization in the presence of alcohols and thiols, which is otherwise hard to achieve using typical acid catalysts. Experimental and computational studies revealed that the TOB catalysts have multiple preorganized C(sp3)–Hs that serve as a mimic of oxyanion holes, which can stabilize the oxyanion intermediates via multiple C(sp3)–H non-classical hydrogen bond interactions. 2. Fumaric acid diesters are important building blocks for organic synthesis. A class of zwitterionic organocatalysts based on an amide anion/iminium cation charge pair were found to be effective in catalyzing the isomerization of maleic acid diesters to give fumaric acid diesters. Comparison of the performance of different zwitterionic organocatalysts toward the reaction revealed that nonclassical hydrogen bonding was involved in the stabilization of the Michael adduct intermediate. 3. γ-Butenolides are useful structural motifs in many pharmaceutically relevant compounds. In particular, halogenated γ-butenolides are attractive building blocks because the halogen handles can readily be manipulated to give various functional molecules. In this study, a catalytic synthesis of halogenated γ-butenolides from cyclopropene carboxylic acids was developed using zwitterionic catalysts and N-haloamides as the halogen sources. The catalytic protocol could also be applied to the synthesis of halogenated pyrrolones by using cyclopropene amides as the starting materials. 4. In many metal catalyses, the traditional strategy of removing chloride ions is to add silver salts via anion exchange to obtain highly active catalysts. In this study, we developed an alternative strategy of removing chloride anions from ruthenium trichloride using an organic [P+-N−] zwitterionic compound via multiple hydrogen bond interactions. The resultant organic−metal hybrid catalytic system has successfully been applied to the aerobic oxidation of alcohols, tetrahydroquinolines, and indolines under mild conditions. The performance of zwitterion is far superior to that of many other common Lewis bases or Brønsted bases. Mechanistic studies revealed that the zwitterion triggers the dissociation of chloride from ruthenium trichloride via nonclassical hydrogen bond interaction. Preliminary studies show that the zwitterion is applicable to catalytic transfer semi-hydrogenation.

14305520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305520.value: Acid catalysts are very useful in various chemical transformations. While acid catalysis is well established, some acid catalysts involve toxic metals. In addition, many acids are moisture sensitive and tedious reaction setup is needed. In some other cases, substrates containing acid-sensitive functional groups or Lewis basic substituents are incompatible. In this research project, trialkylphosphonium oxoborate catalysts are used to activate electron-donor substrates such as carbonyl and imine compounds. The steric and electronic demands of the catalysts can be altered easily by changing the substituents. These catalysts are insensitive to moisture and the catalytic reactions can be operated under ambient conditions. In addition, the catalytic performance of trialkylphosphonium oxoborates is superior to some commonly used Lewis acid catalysts due to minimized poisoning effect. Moreover, highly chemoselective reactions can be achieved using the trialkylphosphonium oxoborate catalysts. In future, we will further explore the applications of trialkylphosphonium oxoborate catalysts in other chemo and/or stereoselective reactions that can be operated under ambient conditions and has high functional group compatibility.

14305520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305520.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amounts of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. Catalysis underpins many industries as over 90% of chemicals produced rely on the use of a catalyst to certain extent. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of useful catalytic protocols using trialkylphosphonium oxoborate catalysts. Our work on the novel catalysis provides a very useful tool for various transformations. In addition, organocatalysis is mild and metal-free, which are attractive features to the manufacturing sectors. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14306020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306020.value: The aim of this proposed project is to develop statistical methods to conduct fine-scale inference for aggregate-level DNA methylation data. Although single-cell sequencing experiments have become popular, it is still infeasible to conduct single-cell experiments for dozens or hundreds of patients. Therefore, association studies that link genomic features to phenotypes continue to rely on bulk data, which measure signals aggregated from a mixture of cell types for each patient. Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) aim to identify the associations between the DNA methylation levels of cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites and phenotypes. As cellular compositions vary from person to person, classic association detection methods for EWAS can suffer from a high false-positive rate and very low statistical power. Recently, we and other researchers independently proposed statistical methods for EWAS that not only substantially improve the power in determining whether a CpG site is associated with phenotypes but also enable, for the first time, association detection to be performed for each cell type. However, although the power of association detection at the aggregate level has significantly improved, the accurate detection of cell-type-specific risk CpG sites still requires very large sample sizes. Meanwhile, how to borrow strengths from nearby CpG sites, how to take advantage of data collected from pure cell types and how to cluster patients according to their cell-type-specific methylation profiles all remain open questions. In this project, we will develop hierarchical models that build upon Gaussian process regression to (a) detect genomic regions, instead of individual CpG sites, whose methylation levels are associated with phenotypes for each individual cell type and (b) identify disease subtypes based on patients' cell-type-specific methylation profiles. Our proposed models will automatically leverage information shared by nearby CpG sites and conveniently incorporate external methylation data measured for pure cell types. To the best of our knowledge, no clustering algorithm that considers patient-specific and cell-type-specific information has been developed for aggregate-level genomic data. We will develop efficient parallel algorithms for statistical inference and provide them as a free software package. We will apply the developed methods to publicly available and our internal datasets to solve health problems. This project will develop statistical methods for solving cutting-edge scientific problems in genomics and make profound contributions to statistical modeling, statistical computing, and parallel programming. The scientific discoveries from this project will greatly deepen our understandings of disease mechanisms, help develop new diagnostic methods for diseases, and ultimately promote personalized medicine in Hong Kong and elsewhere. 本項目旨在開發對DNA甲基化數據進行細尺度推斷的統計方法。 儘管單細胞測序已經很流行，但對數十或數百名患者進行單細胞測序仍然不可行。因此，將基因組特徵與表型特徵相聯繫的關聯分析仍然依賴於bulk數據。Bulk數據測量所得的是每個患者多種細胞類型的混合信號。表觀基因組關聯研究 (EWAS) 旨在確定CpG位點的甲基化水平與表型之間的關聯。 由於每個人的細胞組成比例不同，傳統的關聯分析方法往往有很高的假陽性率和很低的統計功效。 最近，我們和其他的研究人員獨立地提出了針對EWAS數據的新的統計方法。新方法不僅大大提高了檢測CpG位點甲基化水平與表型之間關聯的統計功效而且第一次能對每個細胞類型做關聯分析。然而，雖然在混合信號尺度的統計功效顯著提高了，但在細胞類尺度的關聯分析的精確推斷依舊要求非常大的樣本量。與此同時，如何整合臨近的CpG位點的信號、如何利用測量純細胞類所得的數據、如何將患者按他們各個細胞類中DNA甲基化水平進行分類都是亟待解決的問題。 在本項目中，我們將開發層次模型來 (a) 識別每個細胞類中DNA甲基化水平與表型相關的區域而不是單個的CpG位點和 (b) 按照患者各個細胞類甲基化的水平來確定疾病的亞型。我們的模型將自動利用相鄰CpG位點的信息和對純細胞類測得的外部數據。據我們所知，尚未有任何針對bulk數據的聚類算法考慮了患者細胞類尺度的DNA甲基化水平。我們將開發用於統計推斷的高效並行算法並將其開發成免費的軟件包。我們將把開發的算法應用於分析實際的EWAS數據。 本項目將開發用於解決基因組學前沿科學問題的統計方法並對統計建模、統計計算、並行計算做出深遠貢獻。該項目的科學發現將大大加深我們對疾病機理的認識、有助於開發疾病的新的診斷方法、並最終促進個性化醫療的發展。

14306020.label: Realisation of objectives
14306020.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the proposal. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed in Part C. First, we have proposed a statistical method, clusterHIRE, to cluster DNA methylation data collected from epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) by accounting for cell-type-specific methylation profiles [4]. We have developed a generalized expectation-maximization algorithm for the statistical inference and implemented parallel programming to speed up the computation (https://github.com/tomleee012/clusterHIRE ). We applied clusterHIRE to a famous benchmark dataset for EWAS, and clusterHIRE grouped samples into two groups and identified the gender for all the individuals perfectly. Second, we proposed a Bayesian hierarchical model based on Gaussian process functional regression to detect cell-type-specific differentially methylated regions for EWAS data [5]. We developed a generalized expectation-maximization algorithm for statistical inference (https://github.com/JiaRuofan/Detection-of-Cell-type-specific-DMRs-in-EWAS). Compared to previous method for detecting cell-type-specific associations with EWAS data, our proposed method improves the power substantially for EWAS with moderate sample sizes. Moreover, based on the idea of deconvoluting bulk data into cell-type-specific signals, we have developed a deep learning method, TAPE, to deconvolute bulk RNA-seq data by integrating bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq data [1]. The idea of decomposing mixed genomic data into individual components also helped us to develop a risk prediction method, Prism Vote, for genetic data collected from admixture populations [2]. Motivated by performing fine-scale inference for aggregated-level data, we have also developed a hierarchical model based on the mixed membership stochastic blockmodel to learn the network structure with heterogeneous time-to-event data collected from social networks [3]. We have also worked together with our colleagues at Prince of Wales Hospital and Faculty of Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong to perform cell-type-specific association detection for DNA methylation data collected from liver cancer patients and collected longitudinally over 16 years from a group of elderly Hong Kong people. The preliminary findings are very interesting, and we are currently collecting more samples to increase the sample size. Due to the pandemic, the planned research trips were not carried out, and the conference attendance were mainly virtual. As a result, the actual expenditure is lower than the budget.

14306020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306020.value: DNA methylation at CpG sites is an important type of epigenetic modifications that has been associated with phenotypes. Therefore, in recent years, EWAS have been widely adopted in epidemiology studies to identify CpG sites that are associated with disease-risk factors. However, the biopsies collected by EWAS, either tissue samples or blood samples, always consist of different cell types. As a result, because different subjects can have different cellular compositions and cell-type-specific methylation profiles, traditional association detection methods that directly compare the raw observed signals at the aggregated-level can suffer from a large number of spurious associations and have very low statistical power. Recently, the PI’s team and other research groups independently proposed statistical methods that enable the detection of risk-CpG sites for individual cell types for EWAS. However, although these methods significantly increase the power of association detection at the aggregate-level, the power of association detection at the cell-type level is still limited, especially given that a typical EWAS usually has a sample size below 1000. In this project, we have developed a hierarchical model based on Gaussian process functional regression to detect cell-type-specific differentially methylated regions for EWAS data so that information from nearby CpG sites can be borrowed [5]. Compared to previous methods for detecting cell-type-specific CpG sites, the proposed method has similar performance when the sample size is very large and substantially outperforms existing methods when the sample size is below 1000, which is the common case for a typical EWAS. In addition, we have developed a clustering method for EWAS data which considers the variations in both cellular compositions and in cell-type-specific methylation levels [4]. Application of the proposed method to real data shows that the proposed method adjusts for the confounding caused by variations in cellular compositions and enables the identification of subtype-specific cell-type-specific methylation profiles. Therefore, the proposed methods will greatly facilitate the analysis of EWAS data. The fine-scale inference of EWAS data enlightens the fine-scale inference for other genomic data types and heterogeneous data collected from social networks. In particular, we have developed a deep learning method to deconvolute bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type-specific gene expression signals [1], a risk prediction model for genotype data collected from admixture populations [2] and a mixed membership model for modeling time-to-event data collected from social networks [3]. We have also worked together with our colleagues at Prince of Wales Hospital and Faculty of Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong to perform fine-scale inference for EWAS data to study the associations between DNA methylation and liver cancer and dementia.

14306020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306020.value: In the current project, when we cluster samples according to EWAS data, we use the EWAS data only and do not consider other covariates of the subjects such as age. In the future, we can generalize the model to further consider the impact of known covariates in clustering, although the biological interpretation will be different. Scientifically, both covariates-adjusted and covariates-unadjusted clustering would be of interest for different biomedical problems. Moreover, it would be of great interest to apply the proposed methods to systematically analyze the DNA methylation data collected by large consortium projects such as the Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA), which will greatly deepen our understandings of disease mechanisms and help to identify potential biomarkers for early disease diagnosis. Nevertheless, very careful preprocessing of the data, including batch effects correction, would be needed.

14306020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306020.value: Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) aim to identify the associations between the DNA methylation levels of CpG sites and phenotypes of interest, such as age, disease status, and smoking history. Because the epigenome can be modified, new therapies can be developed if we can accurately identify the associations for EWAS. Unfortunately, the samples collected in EWAS usually consist of a mixture of different cell types instead of a single pure cell type. As a result, if we ignore the mixture nature of EWAS and perform traditional association tests, we can end with many spurious associations. Therefore, in the past several years, there has been very active research on deconvoluting cell-type-specific signals with EWAS data, and we were among one of the groups who proposed methods for detecting cell-type-specific associations with EWAS data for the first time. However, precious methods suffer from low power and cannot perform sample clustering. In this project, we propose statistical methods to improve the association detection power by borrowing strengths from nearby CpG sites and to simultaneously cluster EWAS samples and decompose bulk EWAS data into cell-type-specific signals. Similar ideas can be applied to perform fine-scale inference for gene expression data, genetic data and social network data.

14306220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306220.value: 本研究旨在評估21世紀全球土地覆蓋變化將如何影響地表臭氧空氣質量，並特別考慮各種社會經濟情景下不同的土地利用策略和大氣與生物圈的相互作用。涉及地表臭氧的空氣污染是嚴峻的環境問題，對人類健康、植被和農作物均具深遠而有害的影響。雖然人為排放的臭氧前驅物是臭氧污染的主因，但過去研究已發現土地覆蓋和陸地生物圈的變化也會顯著改變臭氧空氣質量。未來的土地覆蓋變化將繼續在臭氧污染的形成過程中發揮關鍵作用，但對其影響的預測高度不確定，部分原因是不同植被和農作物類型的全球分佈將因各種各樣的土地利用而有所變化，而這些土地變化將取決於不同國家為著實現多重、往往相互矛盾的社會目標（包括糧食和能源安全、環境保護、緩解氣候變化等）而採取的各種社會經濟路徑。再者，各種大氣與生物圈的相互作用將進一步增加這些不確定性，尤其是在氣候變化下，二氧化碳濃度升高、活性氮沉降和臭氧破壞對植被密度和生理均會有顯著的影響，從而進一步調整土地覆蓋變化對臭氧的影響。要對不同土地利用情景下未來臭氧空氣質量有更準確的評估，深入了解這些複雜的大氣與生物圈相互作用更尤其重要。 因此，本研究擬在IPCC第六次評估報告中考慮的各種社會經濟情景下，全面評估土地覆蓋變化和不同土地利用策略對臭氧空氣質量的影響。將使用地球系統模型來模擬大氣化學、氣候和陸地生物圈之間的相互作用和反饋，並進行新的模塊開發，以探討二氧化碳和氮沉降的施肥作用、以及臭氧的損害將如何進一步修改臭氧與植被的關係，並更準確表示不同土地利用策略下（包括植樹造林、具有碳捕獲和存儲的生物能源開發等）的植物類型分佈。研究將得出更可靠的未來臭氧預測，並可將其用於評估對人類健康、森林、農業和氣候的影響，對於更好地制定有關空氣質量、土地使用、糧食安全和緩解氣候變化的政策至關重要。

14306220.label: Realisation of objectives
14306220.value: Both major objectives of the project have been fully achieved. For Objective 1, we successfully developed a robust coupled climate-chemistry-land modeling framework using the Community Earth System Model (CESM), featuring enhanced representation of biosphere-atmosphere feedbacks that impact surface ozone. This framework accounts for biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) emissions and dry deposition processes with improved representation of their meteorological dependence, as well as ozone-vegetation interactions and feedbacks under various climate and land-use scenarios. The model was validated with an extensive array of observational datasets, ensuring both accuracy and global applicability. For Objective 2, the project conducted a comprehensive ensemble of simulations across multiple Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), including SSP1, SSP3, and SSP5. These experiments assessed the impacts of climate change, land-use and land-cover change (LULCC), and emissions control strategies on surface ozone and PM2.5 air quality by mid-21st century. The results, published in Science of the Total Environment (Bhattarai et al., 2024a, 2024b), highlighted the complex interplay between anthropogenic emissions, forest cover, biosphere-induced emissions, and meteorological dynamics. While the effects of rising CO2 on biosphere-atmospheric interactions were accounted for, what we did not do in accordance with the original proposal was to have a comprehensive sensitivity study on the exact contribution of rising CO2 concentration to different biosphere-atmosphere interaction pathways, due to both computational resource and time constraints. In total, six peer-reviewed papers stemmed from this project. Two core publications by Bhattarai et al. (2024a, 2024b) directly addressed the primary objectives. Four additional studies have stemmed from these objectives to examine more specifically each of those biosphere-atmosphere interaction pathways using a variety of modeling tools. They include representing plant ecophysiological processes in the GEOS-Chem and TEMIR models to examine ozone dry deposition and BVOC emissions (Sun et al., 2022; Lam et al., 2023), satellite-based constraints on isoprene emissions (Wang et al., 2022), and coupled ozone-vegetation feedbacks in China (Zhu et al., 2022), all of which were derived and benefited from the scientific objectives, modeling frameworks and datasets developed in this project.

14306220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306220.value: The project’s most significant findings are presented in two key publications by Bhattarai et al.: • Bhattarai et al. (2024a) investigated how climate change, land-use patterns, and emissions interact to affect future surface ozone (O₃) levels. Using the Community Earth System Model (CESM), the study revealed that climate-driven increases in biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) emissions and forest cover can elevate ozone in urban areas where nitrogen oxides (NOx) levels are already high, particularly in East China and northern India. Despite emissions controls, ozone pollution could persist or worsen in some regions due to the counteracting climate effects. The study emphasized the need for integrated strategies that simultaneously consider land use, air quality and climate management to mitigate ozone pollution under changing environmental and socioeconomic conditions. • Bhattarai et al. (2024b) extended the analysis to PM2.5 air quality, showing that while sustainable pathways (e.g., SSP1) can reduce PM2.5 by over 70% in the US and Europe, regions like India and China may experience increases under fossil-fueled development scenarios (e.g., SSP3), driven by biomass burning and anthropogenic emissions. Climate and land-use changes had modest but regionally significant impacts on PM2.5, underscoring the continuing importance of emissions control. These two studies together provide a comprehensive understanding of how land use, climate, and emissions policies will shape global air quality in the coming decades, highlighting the importance of coordinated strategies that integrate multiple sustainable development objectives including human health, ecosystem resilience, and climate action. The following additional research outcomes extend the above main research themes to examine in greater detail the specific processes relevant to biosphere-atmosphere interactions and ozone air quality: Lam et al. (2023): Developed an ecophysiology module in GEOS-Chem, improving the representation of vegetation-mediated BVOC and ozone fluxes; Sun et al. (2022): Compared photosynthesis-based and multiplicative ozone dry deposition schemes, emphasizing model biases under rising CO2; Wang et al. (2022): Derived satellite-based constraints on BVOC emissions under drought stress in the southeastern US, enhancing emissions and ozone air quality modeling; Zhu et al. (2022): Demonstrated ozone–vegetation feedbacks in China, revealing how ozone damage alters meteorology and further increases ozone levels. Together, these outputs advance the understanding of biosphere-atmosphere interactions, improve modeling capabilities, and provide crucial insights for air quality management under climate change.

14306220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306220.value: The modeling framework developed in this project provides a strong foundation for further research. Potential directions include: • Expanding the model to assess co-benefits of climate, air quality and land management policies, especially in the Global South. • Integrating fire emissions and their feedbacks under future climate scenarios. • Coupling the model with crop productivity and public health impact assessments to evaluate socioeconomic consequences. • Collaborating with policy makers to develop scenario-based decision tools for sustainable land and air quality management. These directions will extend the policy relevance and scientific depth of the project outcomes.

14306220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306220.value: Ground-level ozone and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) are harmful air pollutants that threaten human health, agriculture, and the environment. This project investigated how changes in climate, land use (like deforestation or reforestation), and pollution emissions will affect air quality in the future. Using advanced computer models, the project team found that even if we reduce emissions, climate change and land-use changes could still worsen air pollution in some regions. For example, rising temperatures and increased forest cover can lead to more natural vegetation emissions that react in the air with vehicle and industry pollutants to form more ozone. In countries like China and India, this means people may still breathe unhealthy air for much of the year, even under optimistic scenarios. The research also showed that reducing emissions, especially from human activities and burning biomass, remains the most effective way to improve air quality. However, we must also consider how land-use and climate changes interact with pollution control efforts. Overall, these findings help us understand the complex puzzle of air pollution and guide smarter policies to protect human health and the planet in a changing world, achieving multiple Sustainable Development Goals in a coordinated and optimal manner.

14306320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306320.value: Dopamine is a well-known neurotransmitter that can control the release of hormone in the brain. It can undergo self-polymerization readily in a mixture of water, ethanol, and ammonia, forming polydopamine nanospheres in which the repeating units are linked through covalent bonding, hydrogen bonding, and pi-pi interactions, etc. With reactive functionalities such as amine, imine, and catechol on the surface, this polymeric material is highly reactive, enabling it to adhere to almost all material surfaces and crosslink with thiol- and amino-terminated molecules. As a result, this material can facilitate the loading of various noble metals, biomolecules, and theranostic agents. Together with its biocompatibility, low cytotoxicity, biodegradability, fluorescence quenching ability, and photothermal conversion characteristic, polydopamine has been widely used to prepare a wide range of nano- and micro-structures for various biomedical applications. This project aims to develop stimuli-responsive polydopamine nanoparticles encapsulated with phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers for targeted photodynamic therapy (PDT), which is a promising and clinically approved anticancer modality involving reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly singlet oxygen, as the cytotoxic species. Owing to the self-quenching effect, the phthalocyanine molecules in the nanoparticles are photodynamically inactive. By using a disulfide or thioketal linker for the bis(dopamine) monomers, the nanoparticles can be dissociated upon interactions with thiols or ROS inside the cells. Higher intracellular thiols (e.g. glutathione) and ROS (e.g. H2O2) concentrations are characteristic features of cancer cells. The use of ROS-responsive polydopamine could also accelerate the photodegradation of the nanoparticles. The release of phthalocyanine molecules would trigger the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation. To our knowledge, degradable polydopamine nanoparticles for PDT have not been reported so far. In this project, we will prepare a range of these nanoparticles with different size and loading of phthalocyanines, and then examine the restoration of these photoactivities upon interactions with the corresponding stimuli. To enhance the tumor-targeting property, the nanoparticles that exhibit the best responsive behavior will be conjugated with a tumor-targeting peptide, such as the heptapeptide QRHKPRE and the GE11 sequence, which show high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpressed on the membrane of most cancer cells. Their cellular uptake and photocytotoxicity against a range of EGFR-positive and negative cancer cell lines will be examined and compared. Finally, the biodistribution and photodynamic efficacy of these nanoparticles will also be investigated in tumor-bearing nude mice. It is expected that these multifunctional nanocomposites can serve as promising tumor-selective and activatable photosensitizing systems for targeted PDT. 多巴胺是一種眾所周知的神經遞質，可以用來控制大腦中激素的釋放。它很容易在水，乙醇和氨水的混合物中發生自聚合，形成聚多巴胺納米球，其中的重複單元通過共價鍵，氫鍵和π-π鍵等相互作用連接。這種聚合材料表面有胺，亞胺和鄰苯二酚等官能團，具有很高的反應活性，使其能夠粘附到幾乎所有材料表面並能與硫醇和氨基封端分子交聯。因此，這種材料可以裝載各種貴金屬，生物分子和治療試劑。連同生物相容性，低細胞毒性，生物降解性，熒光猝滅能力和光熱轉化特性，聚多巴胺已被廣泛用於製備各種納米和微結構並用於多種生物醫學應用。此項目旨在開發以酞菁為基礎的光敏劑封裝於具腫瘤選擇性和可激活性能的聚多巴胺納米顆粒中，用於靶向光動力治療。光動力治療是一種有前境且經過臨床批准的抗癌療法，其中涉及活性氧特別是單線態氧作為細胞毒性物質。由於自猝滅作用，納米顆粒中的酞菁分子是光動力學惰性的。通過使用二硫鍵或硫代縮酮連接兩個多巴胺單體，所組裝成的納米顆粒可以在與細胞內的硫醇或活性氧相互作用時降解。較高的細胞內硫醇（例如穀胱甘肽）和活性氧（例如過氧化氫）濃度是癌細胞的特徵。活性氧響應性聚多巴胺的使用也可以促進納米顆粒的光降解。酞菁分子的釋放將觸發熒光的發射和單線態氧的產生。據我們所知，到目前為止，尚無可降解聚多巴胺納米顆粒用於光動力治療的報導。在這個項目中，我們將製備一系列具有不同大小和酞菁負載量的納米顆粒，然後研究它們與相應刺激物相互作用後光活性的恢復情況。為了增強靶向腫瘤的性能，表現出最佳響應行為的納米顆粒將與靶向腫瘤的肽（例如七肽QRHKPRE和GE11序列）偶聯，這些肽對很多腫瘤細胞膜上過度表達的表皮生長因子受體（EGFR）具有很高的親和力。我們將測試並比較它們被一系列EGFR陽性和陰性細胞系的攝取能力以及產生的光細胞毒性的能力。最後，我們還將研究這種納米材料在荷瘤裸鼠中的生物分佈以及光動力治療功效。我們預期這種多功能的復合納米材料有希望成為有腫瘤選擇性的可激活光敏系統並應用於靶向光動力學治療。

14306320.label: Realisation of objectives
14306320.value: This project aims to develop a series of multifunctional polydopamine (PDA)-based nanomaterials for targeted phototherapy. To develop the first nanosystem, we first synthesized a glutathione (GSH)-responsive disulfide-linked L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) dimer and studied its self-polymerization in the presence of different amounts of ammonia solution (NH4OH) (Biomater. Sci. 2022, 10, 189). A series of PDA-based spherical nanoparticles with different size (140-350 nm in diameter) were obtained. These nanoparticles were then treated with a zinc(II) phthalocyanine-based photosensitizer (labeled as Pc) in deionized water containing 0.5% Tween 20. With a nucleophilic amino functionality, Pc could be immobilized readily on the surface of these nanoparticles through Schiff base reaction or Michael addition. The Pc loading was estimated to be 19-24% (by weight) by electronic absorption spectroscopy. Finally, these nanoparticles were mixed with the peptide sequence QRHKPREGGGSC (labeled as QRH), which can target the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpressed in cancer cells, in deionized water to give the corresponding conjugates via coupling between the thiol group of the cysteine residue of QRH and the reactive functionalities (e.g. quinone via Michael addition) on the PDA surface. By replacing the GSH-cleavable disulfide linker with a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-sensitive thioketal bond and adding doxorubicin (Dox) during the self-polymerization of this L-DOPA dimer, a new batch of Dox-encapsulated PDA-based nanoparticles was obtained, which was then modified sequentially with Pc and QRH as mentioned above to give the corresponding nanocomposites (Nanoscale 2021, 13, 15899). To extend the study, we further replaced the linker of the L-DOPA dimer with an azo bond, which is cleavable under a hypoxic or reducing environment. This dimer underwent copolymerization with dopamine to form spherical nanoparticles. Similarly, we also introduced an anticancer drug, namely the hypoxia-activatable prodrug tirapazamine (TPZ), during the copolymerization and Pc after the formation of nanoparticles to give corresponding nanocomposites for dual photodynamic and chemo therapy (ACS Pharmacol. Transl. Sci. to be submitted). The size and morphology of these nanoparticles were determined using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS), while the loading of different components was determined by electronic absorption or fluorescence spectroscopy. To demonstrate the versatility of polydopamine, this material was also used to coat high-entropy MXene nanosheets with a composition of TiVNbMoC3Tx (T = surface terminations). Followed by conjugation with Pc and QRH, the resulting multifunctional nanocomposite was used for targeted photothermal anticancer therapy (Adv. Sci. submitted). Moreover, the aforementioned disulfide-linked L-DOPA dimer and dopamine were also copolymerized on the surface of Cr nanoparticles. The biodegradable coating further encapsulated the anticancer drug alpelisib for combating advanced breast cancer harboring the PIK3CA mutation and immobilized Pc for tumor imaging. These tailor-fabricated Cr-based nanocomposites were used for photo-metallo-immunotherapy to enhance CAR-T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity against solid tumors (Adv. Mater. 2024, 36, 2407425). The scope of the PDA-based nanomaterials studied was broader than that proposed originally, and hence the first objective was exceedingly achieved. The electronic absorption and fluorescence spectra of these nanosystems were recorded in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with 0.5% Tween 20. The absorption spectra showed the Q-band absorption of Pc at ca. 700 nm, which was significantly broadened and weaker compared with that of free Pc. The fluorescence due to Pc was also largely diminished for these nanosystems. By using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as a singlet oxygen probe, the singlet oxygen generation of these nanosystems was also found to be negligible. All these results strongly indicated that the Pc molecules were significantly stacked and self-quenched in these nanoparticles. In the presence of the corresponding stimuli, including GSH, H2O2, and sodium dithionite (Na2S2O4), which is a typical deoxidizer that can mimic the hypoxic tumor microenvironment, the disulfide, thioketal, and azo bonds are cleaved, respectively, triggering the degradation of the nanoparticles and the release of Pc, eventually leading to the restoration of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation. For the ROS-responsive nanosystem, the ROS generated could further boost the degradation of the nanoparticles and the release of Pc and Dox. In the absence of these stimuli, these nanoparticles remained intact as shown by fluorescence spectroscopy and DLS. With these studies, the second objective was also accomplished. The in vitro properties of these nanosystems were then systematically investigated. For the QRH-conjugated nanosystems, we first examined their cellular uptake by confocal fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry, using a range of cell lines with different expression levels of EGFR, including the EGFR-positive A549 human lung carcinoma cells and A431 human epidermoid carcinoma cells, as well as the EGFR-negative HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells and HEK293 human embryonic kidney normal cells. To examine the effect of GSH and ROS in promoting the degradation of the corresponding nanoparticles, the cells were either post-treated with GSH‐OEt or irradiated that can trigger in situ formation of ROS. The cytotoxicity of these nanosystems due to the photodynamic action of Pc and the chemotherapeutic effect of the encapsulated drug was also investigated. For the azo-bridged PDA-based nanosystem, the in vitro properties in both hypoxic and normoxic conditions were also compared. For the PDA-coated MXenes, their photothermal cytotoxicity was also investigated against a range of EGFR-positive and negative cell lines. In addition, the cytotoxicity of the PDA-coated Cr nanoparticles and their effect on the cell-killing ability of B7-H3 CAR-T cells were also studied. Through a series of in vitro experiments, the third objective was fully achieved. To accomplish the last objective, various animal models were established for studying the biodistribution, tumor-localization property, therapeutic effect, and systemic toxicity of these nanosystems. To demonstrate the EGFR-targeting effect of the QRH-conjugated nanosystems, competition experiments using free QRH or control experiments using the non-QRH-conjugated analogues were performed. The dual therapeutic effect of the Dox-encapsulated nanosystem on inhibition of tumor growth was also examined using various controls. For the PDA-coated MXene and Cr nanoparticles, the photothermal effect in direct elimination of tumor and warming the cold tumor microenvironment for boosting the therapeutic efficacy of CAR-T cells, respectively, was also evaluated, using 4T1 murine mammary tumor-bearing nude mice and NOD severe combined immunodeficiency gamma mice bearing a human hepatoma or PIK3CA-mutated breast tumor as the animal models, respectively. The systemic toxicity of these nanosystems was also determined by measuring the standard blood biochemical indexes for liver and kidney functions and performing hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining of the major organs of the mice over a period of time (1-90 days) after intravenous administration.

14306320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306320.value: A series of GSH-responsive PDA nanoparticles were prepared using a disulfide-linked L-DOPA dimer as starting material, of which the size could be tuned systematically by adjusting the amount of ammonia solution used. Further immobilization of Pc and QRH afforded an EGFR-targeting GSH-activatable nanophotosensitizer. The nanoparticles with the smallest size (ca. 200 nm in diameter) exhibited the highest cellular uptake against EGFR-positive cancer cells and high photocytotoxicity with IC50 values as low as 0.05 μM based on Pc. They could also accumulate and be activated in the tumor of A431 tumor-bearing nude mice, leading to effective elimination of the tumor upon laser irradiation. The results were published in Biomater. Sci. 2022, 10, 189. By replacing the linker of L-DOPA dimer with a thioketal bond and adding Dox during the self-polymerization, the multifunctional nanosystem PDA-Dox-Pc-QRH was obtained. It could be internalized selectively into EGFR-positive cancer cells, in which the nanoparticles were degraded gradually via cleavage of the thioketal linkages by the intrinsic ROS, leading to activation of the immobilized Pc to generate additional ROS to promote further degradation of the nanoparticles and release of Dox. It resulted in enhanced cytotoxicity by synergistic chemo and photodynamic therapy as demonstrated both in vitro and in vivo. These results were published in Nanoscale 2021, 13, 15899. To extend this study, we also synthesized an azo-bridged L-DOPA dimer. Co-polymerization of this dimer and dopamine in the presence of TPZ, followed by immobilization of Pc gave the nanosystem PDA-TPZ-Pc. Under hypoxic conditions, the endogenous overexpressed azoreductase in cancer cells cleaved the azo linkages and triggered the degradation of the nanoparticles and release of TPZ and Pc for synergistic antitumor therapy. This work will soon be submitted to ACS Pharmacol. Transl. Sci. for publication. Polydopamine was also used to coat high-entropy MXene and Cr nanoparticles. The former exhibited high biostability and an excellent photothermal property with a light-to-heat conversion efficiency of 67% under 808 nm laser irradiation. With immobilized QRH, it also showed an EGFR-targeting property, causing high photothermal efficacy toward the target cancer cells and tumors. The results have just been submitted to Adv. Sci. for publication. For the latter, it was used to induce photo-metallo-immunotherapy for enhancing CAR-T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity against solid tumors as demonstrated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments. The results of this systematic study have been published in Adv. Mater. 2024, 36, 2407425.

14306320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306320.value: This study has demonstrated the high versatility of PDA. Apart from the solid PDA nanoparticles formed by self-polymerization of dopamine derivatives, two core@shell-type nanosystems have also been prepared and used for various therapeutic applications. By introducing a cleavable linker for L-DOPA dimers, the resulting PDA can become biodegradable, which provides an effective strategy for controlled drug release and activation of the immobilized photosensitizers. Apart from the disulfide, thioketal, and azo linkers used in this study, linkers that are responsive to other tumor-associated stimuli can also be used, such as the cathepsin B-cleavable GFLGK peptide sequence. In addition, it is envisaged that various therapeutic agents and inorganic materials can also be loaded into the PDA-based nanosystems to exert additional therapeutic functions. The addition of different amount of dopamine during the self-polymerization of these dimers could adjust the rate of degradation, which enables fine tuning of the therapeutic actions. Moreover, the high adhesive property of PDA could also facilitate the immobilization of various functional components to further enhance the therapeutic efficacy of the nanodrugs. All these are some of the areas that can be further pursued.

14306320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306320.value: Dopamine is a well-known neurotransmitter, which undergoes ammonia-promoted self-polymerization to form polydopamine nanospheres. With various reactive functionalities on the surface, this polymeric material is highly reactive, enabling it to adhere to almost all material surfaces and load various noble metals, biomolecules, and theranostic agents. This project aims to further enhance the properties and extend the applications of this material. To this end, we designed and synthesized a series of dopamine dimers that were responsive toward the elevated glutathione level, higher reactive oxygen species content, and hypoxic environment in tumors. Self-polymerization of these dimers gave spherical nanoparticles, which were further anchored with a tumor-targeting peptide and a photosensitizer on the surface for targeted delivery and controlled photosensitization. Selected anticancer drugs were also encapsulated to afford multifunctional nanodrugs for synergistic photodynamic and chemo therapy as demonstrated through a series of experiments at the cellular and animal levels. These biodegradable materials were also used as coating for high-entropy MXene and Cr nanoparticles to enhance their efficacy in photothermal therapy and in promoting the cell infiltration and cytotoxicity of CAR-T against solid tumors, respectively. The overall results show that these newly developed polydopamine-based nanomaterials are highly versatile and efficient for biomedical applications.

14306420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306420.value: 壹個世紀前，對稱性這壹重要觀念被引入了物理學。Noether定理揭示了對稱性和守恒律之間的深刻聯系，並且成為了現代物理學的奠基石之壹。隨後，對稱破缺這壹概念進壹步統壹了電磁力和弱力，並最終導致了基本粒子標準模型的建立。在凝聚態物理學中，長期以來人們壹直相信朗道對稱破缺理論可以描述所有的物質相和連續相變。直到分數量子霍爾效應和高溫超導銅氧化合物的發現，文小剛等人指出分數電荷和分數統計可以用壹種全新的超越朗道理論的物質相 – 拓撲序來刻畫。此後，對稱性和拓撲的內在聯系開啟了現代物理學的新篇章。 最近幾年來，用帶有分數統計的元激發來構建無需糾錯的量子計算機使得人們深化了對拓撲序的認識，並且提出了用幺模張量範疇論這壹全新數學框架來系統的刻畫和分類拓撲序。最近，壹個更為壹般的數學框架 – 所謂的G擴展幺模張量範疇論使得人們可以研究更為壹般的具有全局對稱性系統的拓撲序，即對稱富化拓撲序。但是很不幸這壹數學框架只適合於波色子系統，無法用於研究壹般的費米子系統，例如實際材料中的電子系統。 目前，對稱富化拓撲序這壹領域正在飛速發展，人們迫切的想理解和構建二維強關聯電子體系中的全新的對稱富化拓撲序。在這個研究計劃中，我們會構造並且的系統的研究二維相互作用費米子體系中的對稱富化拓撲序。費米型對稱局域幺正變換等價類這壹觀念會為我們研究二維相互作用費米子體系中的對稱富化拓撲序開辟新的道路。 特別的，我們會:（1） 構造二維相互作用費米子體系中的非手征對稱富化拓撲序的不動點波函數和嚴格可解哈密頓量。（2） 構造二維相互作用費米子體系中的非手征對稱富化拓撲序的拓撲不變量。（3）研究壹些本征的費米對稱富化拓撲序 （無法在相互作用波色子體系中實現）的例子，並且計算描寫元激發對稱分數化譜的特征代數。（4）考慮在實際體系，例如具有對稱性p+ip超導體中的應用。

14306420.label: Realisation of objectives
14306420.value: Similar to the construction and classification of symmetry-enriched topological (SET) phases in bosonic systems, the concept of fermionic symmetric local unitary (FSLU) transformation will provide us with a guiding principle to understand SET phases in fermionic systems. Based on such a principle, we systematically derived all the algebraic conditions for fixed-point wave functions of all non-chiral SET states in interacting fermion systems. Moreover, we even discussed general construction schemes for fixed-point wave functions for anomalous SET phases that can only be realized on the surface of 3D fermionic topological phases. Building upon the foundational algebraic data for fermionic SET phases, our research has advanced to develop their corresponding topological invariant partition functions. This progression led to the establishment of a novel mathematical framework known as the G-grading superfusion category description, enhancing our understanding of fermionic SET phases and their intricate topological properties. Moreover, our investigation delved into numerous non-trivial examples exemplifying intrinsic fermionic SET phases, showcasing their unique characteristics that differentiate them from bosonic systems combined with free fermion systems. Notably, we conducted detailed examinations of anomalous fermionic SET phases, revealing their exclusivity to the surfaces of 3D fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases, highlighting the richness of topological phenomena in fermionic systems. In a pioneering move, we introduced the concept of enforced symmetry breaking for p+ip topological superconductors. This concept challenges the conventional notions of symmetry by revealing instances where specific global symmetries are fundamentally incompatible with such topological systems. Furthermore, we explored the potential practical applications of this concept for experimental realizations, offering new perspectives for manipulating and understanding topological phenomena in the context of topological superconductors.

14306420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306420.value: Through innovative concepts like equivalence classes of fermionic local unitary (FLU) transformations, our research has made significant strides in systematically constructing and categorizing non-chiral topological phases in 2D fermion systems. Our published paper in this realm marks a crucial step in this exploration. Expanding on this foundation, the introduction of equivalence classes of symmetric fermionic local unitary (SFLU) transformations has enabled us to methodically develop and classify non-chiral symmetry-enriched topological phases in 2D fermion systems. Additionally, leveraging the framework of fermion condensation, we have advanced to construct the partition function of fermionic symmetry-enriched topological order, with a paper on this work currently under review. Furthermore, the novel concept of equivalent classes of SFLU transformations has empowered us to delve into the classification of 2D electronic insulators within interacting fermion systems. Our published paper in this domain signifies a significant contribution to this line of inquiry. Moreover, utilizing SFLU transformations has provided us with a structured approach to explore the stacking group structure of fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases, leading to a publication that extends beyond the original scope of our project. Finally, our investigation into enforced symmetry breaking (ESB) phenomena of a finite symmetry total group G_f for p+ip topological superconductors has revealed intriguing insights, with a published paper illuminating our findings in this area. These collective endeavors underscore our commitment to advancing the frontiers of theoretical physics and expanding our understanding of complex quantum phenomena.

14306420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306420.value: Looking ahead, key challenges remain in fully understanding fermionic symmetry-enriched topological (SET) phases. Currently, our mathematical framework, the G-grading superfusion category theory, only covers cases where the system's total symmetry Gf is a direct product of bosonic and fermionic parity symmetries. Expanding this framework to accommodate a wider range of scenarios is crucial for a comprehensive understanding of fermionic SET phases. Additionally, a major upcoming task is to tackle the construction and classification of lattice models for fermionic SET phases, especially concerning chiral topological phases. This represents a significant and demanding frontier that requires innovative strategies and in-depth exploration. By overcoming these obstacles and venturing into new mathematical and construction territories, we aim to advance our comprehension of fermionic SET phases. Addressing these challenges not only enhances our theoretical knowledge but also holds the potential for groundbreaking discoveries in the field of quantum physics.

14306420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306420.value: The study of fermionic systems, aided by the fermionic symmetric local unitary transformation method, is instrumental in understanding how fermions organize themselves. This method acts as a crucial tool, guiding scientists through the complexities of these systems and revealing insights into their unique properties. By uncovering the rules that dictate the stability and arrangements of fermions, researchers are unveiling the underlying order in quantum systems. Exploring anomalous fermionic SET phases, which manifest under specific conditions, showcases the diverse behaviors within these systems. The development of the G-grading superfusion category description provides a more robust mathematical framework for analyzing these particle structures. This research not only enriches our theoretical comprehension but also hints at practical applications and potential technological advancements. By deepening our understanding of these intricate quantum phenomena, scientists are paving the way for innovative discoveries that could reshape our technological landscape in the future.

14306620.value: 有些數字是非常驚人的： 比如在2017年，癌癥奪走了880萬人的生命；只有心臟病導致了更多的死亡。當面對這些疾病和其他罕見病這樣人類共同的敵人時，人們只能寄望未來科技突破可以為疾病帶來治癒的可能。在最近十多年裏，從基因測序到量身定制療法的發展，讓癌癥病人的存活率已經變得越來越高。當前，分析人類健康數據的前沿統計學方法正在飛速發展。數據體量的快速增長和與之相關日益復雜的內在機制，急需發展更好的方法進行研究。該項研究將專註於發展新的統計方法用於分析間隔結尾數據，以及建立新的分位數回歸框架。隨著統計學和計算機計算能力的快速發展，解決該項研究相關的技術/數值計算難題和建立嚴格的理論保證是非常有希望的。我們提出的研究是重要的基礎性問題，相信該項研究成果將產生深遠的影響。

14306620.label: Realisation of objectives
14306620.value: The PI and her coauthors have delivered a number of research outputs to achieve the objectives in this research. 1. During the project period, we focus on developing novel methodologies to analyze time-to-event data. Our major research outputs along this line include two papers published in Electronic Journal of Statistics and Biometrika respectively. Below I elaborate the details of the two papers. (1a) The PI and her co-authors studied a penalized nonparametric likelihood-based estimator for an unknown cumulative hazard function in analyzing the current status data (a special type of censored data), and establish the pointwise asymptotic normality of the resulting nonparametric estimate. We also propose the penalized likelihood ratio tests for local and global hypotheses, derive their limiting distributions, and study the optimality of the global test. Simulation studies show that the proposed method works well compared to the classical likelihood ratio test. This research output has been published in Electronic Journal of Statistics and has largely addressed objectives 1-5. This publication is directly arising from this project, as we came up its key idea in 2019 when this proposal was submitted to RGC. And we completed drafting this manuscript in August 2020, prior to the starting project commencement date. (1b) Meanwhile, we propose a linearized maximum rank correlation estimator for the single-index model. Unlike the existing maximum rank correlation and other rank-based methods, the proposed estimator has a closed-form expression, making it appealing in theory and computation. The proposed estimator is robust to outliers in the response and its construction does not need knowledge of the unknown link function or the error distribution. Under mild conditions, it is shown to be consistent and asymptotically normal when the predictors satisfy the linearity of the expectation assumption. The proposed method can be easily modified to accommodate censored data. It can also be extended to deal with high-dimensional data combined with a penalty function. This research output has been published in Biometrika and has partially addressed objectives 1-4. 2. We also focused our research efforts on developing new statistical methodologies for quantile regression. Our main outputs in this area are two papers published in mainstream statistical journals. Below, I elaborate on the details of these two papers. (2a) In the publication in Journal of Machine Learning Research titled `` Nonparametric Estimation of Non-Crossing Quantile Regression Process with Deep ReQU Neural Networks ”, we propose a penalized nonparametric approach to estimating the quantile regression process (QRP) in a nonseparable model using rectifier quadratic unit (ReQU) activated deep neural networks and introduce a novel penalty function to enforce non-crossing of quantile regression curves. We establish the non-asymptotic excess risk bounds for the estimated QRP and derive the mean integrated squared error for the estimated QRP under mild smoothness and regularity conditions. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method is competitive with or outperforms two existing methods, including methods using reproducing kernels and random forests for nonparametric quantile regression. This research output utilizes the state-of-the-art deep neural networks for nonparametric function estimation. It is directly arising from this project and has partially addressed objectives 1 and 3. (2b) The publication in Computational Statistics & Data Analysis entitled ``Nonparametric inference of smoothed quantile regression processes” is closely related to this project. It addressed Objectives 2-4 by considering global estimation in semiparametric quantile regression models. For estimating unknown functional parameters, we propose an integrated quantile regression loss function with penalization. We obtain a vector-valued functional Bahadur representation of the resulting estimators in a Sobolev space equipped with a proper inner product, and then derive the asymptotic distribution of the proposed infinite-dimensional estimators. Furthermore, a resampling approach that generalizes the minimand perturbing technique is adopted to construct confidence intervals and to conduct hypothesis testing. - 3. In the pursuit of the main objectives in this project, the PI got new insights and findings during the exploration for possible extension to nonparametric inference, semi-supervised inference and high dimensional analysis. The related research output have been published in Annals of Statistics, Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR) and Biometrika. (3a) We study the properties of nonparametric least squares regression using deep neural networks. We derive nonasymptotic upper bounds for the excess risk of the empirical risk minimizer of feedforward deep neural regression. Our error bounds achieve minimax optimal rate and improve over the existing ones in the sense that they depend polynomially on the dimension of the predictor, instead of exponentially on dimension. We also establish the optimal convergence rate under the exact manifold support assumption. To establish these results, we derive a novel approximation error bound for the Hölder smooth functions using ReLU activated neural networks. Our results are derived under weaker assumptions on the data distribution and the neural network structure than those in the existing literature. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1, 3-5. Detailed results can be found in the publication entitled “Deep nonparametric regression on approximate manifolds: Nonasymptotic error bounds with polynomial prefactors”, which has been published in Annals of Statistics. (3b) To accommodate more complicated data, we consider statistical inference for single or low-dimensional parameters in a high-dimensional linear model under a semi-supervised setting. Our proposed method utilises both labelled and unlabelled data without any imputation or removal of the missing observations. The asymptotic properties of the estimator are established under regularity conditions. Hypothesis testing for low-dimensional coefficients are also studied. Extensive simulations are conducted to examine the theoretical results. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1, 2, 4, 5. Details can be found in the publication entitled “Semi-supervised inference for block-wise missing data without imputation”, which has been published in Journal of Machine Learning Research. (3c) Last but not least, in order to partially address objectives 3-5, the PI and her coauthors proposed a debiased stochastic gradient descent algorithm for online statistical inference with high-dimensional data. Our approach combines the debiasing technique developed in high-dimensional statistics with the stochastic gradient descent algorithm. Our proposed algorithm has several appealing aspects: as a one-pass algorithm, it reduces the time complexity; in addition, each update step requires only the current data together with the previous estimate, which reduces the space complexity. We establish the asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator under mild conditions on the sparsity level of the parameter and the data distribution. This paper titled “Online inference with debiased stochastic gradient descent“ has been published in Biometrika. (3e) The PI and CI had numerous discussions focusing on how to use the penalized expected quantile loss function within the framework of a partial linear quantile model to address globally concerned quantile regression. The CI provided several ideas to solve this sophisticated problem including B-splines, DNNs, GANs. It is a pity that its related theoretical justification is very challenging and we still don’t have a satisfactory solution yet.

14306620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306620.value: To summarize, the main findings of this research are several new and efficient statistical technologies to model and analyze complex data under different settings, including 1. A Penalized nonparametric likelihood-based statistical inference procedure for current status data model. 2. A new linearized maximum rank correlation estimation method for single-index model. 3. A novel nonparametric estimation of non-crossing quantile regression process with deep ReQU neural networks. 4. An nonparametric inference on smoothed quantile regression process. These methods have been shown to enjoy appealing theoretical properties in low-dimensional case. During the exploration of possible extension of these methods to high dimensional setting or semi-supervised setting, the PI and her coauthors have new findings associated with this project: 1. A semi-supervised inference procedure for blockwise missing data. 2. Nonasymptotic upper bounds for deep nonparametric regression. 3. A high dimensional online inference with debiased stochastic gradient descent.

14306620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306620.value: One possible direction for further development is to extend the technologies developed in this project to handle censored data. Meanwhile, the methodologies developed in the main outputs of this project do not incorporate density estimation. However, estimating the density function remains a fundamental challenge in various modern statistical and machine learning applications. An intriguing avenue for future research is to adapt the proposed methodologies—both semiparametrically and nonparametrically—to integrate density estimation or distribution learning procedures using deep neural networks for enhanced accuracy. A preliminary idea is to explore a general approach to nonparametric regression and conditional distribution learning, which would allow for the simultaneous estimation of a regression function and a conditional generator within a generative learning framework. The conditional generator serves as a function that generates samples from a conditional distribution. Given the recent advancements in generative learning, this approach is both meaningful and attainable.

14306620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306620.value: Overall, we believe the outputs of this project are sufficient and all objectives have been addressed and achieved, which might provide better ways for practitioners and researchers to analyze complex dataset or datasets from multiple sources and identify significant important variables. We are fortune to have the timely support from RGC, without which everything would not have been possible.

14306720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306720.value: Lagrangian submanifolds are natural geometric objects in symplectic geometry, they are also boundary conditions in string theory. They play very important roles in geometry as well as in mathematical physics. In this proposal, the PI plans to study the geometry of the moduli spaces of Lagrangian submanifolds and their duality transformations. This research will enhance our understanding of mirror symmetry, algebraic geometry, symplectic geometry and Rozansky-Witten theory. Lagrangian 子流形是辛幾何中自然的幾何結構，也是弦論中的邊界條件。它們在幾何以及數學物理學中都扮演著非常重要的角色。 在此提案中，研究員計劃研究Lagrangian子流形的模空間的幾何及其對偶轉換。這項研究將增進我們對鏡對稱，代數幾何，辛幾何和Rozansky-Witten理論的理解。

14306720.label: Realisation of objectives
14306720.value: For objective 1 ‘Enhance our understanding of the geometry of moduli spaces of Lagrangian suhmanifolds and complex Lagrangian submanifolds’, the PI has made numerous new discovery, including a proof of the Fukaya conjecture on SYZ proposal in the paper ‘ Smoothing, scattering, and a conjecture of Fukaya’; describing deformation quantization and Berezin-Toeplitz quantization for symplectic manifolds with real polarisations, possibly singular in the papers ‘ Berezin-Toeplitz Quantization in Real Polarizations with Toric Singularities’ and ‘ Deformation quantization via Toeplitz operators on geometric quantization in real polarizations’; discovering hidden symmetry for brane quantization of complex Lagrangian submanifolds inside hyperkahler manifolds in the paper ‘ Hidden Sp(1)-Symmetry and Brane Quantization on HyperKähler manifolds’; constructing elliptic Hypertoric varieties and proved a version of Hikita conjecture for them in the paper ‘ Elliptic Hypertoric Varieties’ and so on. For objective 2 ‘Stuides of duality transformations of Lagrangian submanifolds and complex Lagrangian submanifolds’, the PI developed the theory of equivariant Lagrangian correspondences to explain the equivariant mirror duality transformation conjecture of Teleman in the paper ‘ Equivariant Lagrangian correspondence and a conjecture of Teleman’, developed the SYZ mirror duality transformations near singular limits using scattering in the paper ‘Smoothing, scattering, and a conjecture of Fukaya‘.

14306720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306720.value: In the paper ‘ Equivariant Lagrangian correspondence and a conjecture of Teleman’, the PI studied the Floer theory of equivariant Lagrangian correspondences and apply it to deduce a conjecture of Teleman, which finds the relation between the disc potential of an invariant Lagrangian submanifold and that of its quotient. A main step is to extend Fukaya's construction of an A∞ tri-module for Lagrangian correspondences to Borel spaces. We find that the equivariant obstruction of a Lagrangian correspondence plays an essential role, which leads to quantum corrections in the disc potentials of quotients. We solve the obstruction in the toric setup and find the relation with mirror maps for compact semi-Fano toric manifolds. In the paper ‘ Smoothing, scattering, and a conjecture of Fukaya’, the PI proved a reformulation of the main conjecture in Fukaya's second correspondence, where multi-valued Morse theory on the base Bˇ is replaced by tropical geometry on the Legendre dual B. In the proof, we apply techniques of asymptotic analysis developed in our previous works to tropicalize the pre-dgBV algebra which governs smoothing of a maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau log variety introduced in another of our recent work. Then a comparison between this tropicalized algebra with the dgBV algebra associated to the deformation theory of the semi-flat part Xsf⊆X allows us to extract consistent scattering diagrams from appropriate Maurer-Cartan solutions. In the paper ‘ Hidden Sp(1)-Symmetry and Brane Quantization on HyperKähler manifolds’, for a fixed prequantum line bundle L over a hyperKähler manifold X, we find a natural Sp(1)-action on Ω∗(X,L) intertwining a twistor family of Spinc-Dirac Laplacians on the spaces of L-valued (0,∗)-forms on X, noting that L is holomorphic for only one complex structure in the twistor family. This establishes a geometric quantization of X via Gukov-Witten brane quantization and leads to a proposal of a mathematical definition of Hom(B¯¯¯cc,Bcc) for the canonical coisotropic A-brane Bcc on X and its conjugate brane B¯¯¯cc. In papers ‘ Deformation quantization via Toeplitz operators on geometric quantization in real polarizations’ and ‘ Berezin-Toeplitz Quantization in Real Polarizations with Toric Singularities’, the PI obtained many new results on various quantization schemes for symplectic manifolds with real polarizations, possibly singular.

14306720.value: The work on equivariant Lagrangian correspondences will be useful for the future studies of 3d mirror symmetry and symplectic duality.
