14306820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306820.value: In this project we will study a novel form of self-organized collective motion recently discovered in bacterial colonies, aiming to elucidate the mechanism of this phenomenon and to understand its physiological functions. Collective motion is ubiquitous in multicellular systems and it plays important roles in many biological processes. Here we focus on collective motion of motile cells in bacterial colonies. Heterogeneous populations, including motile and non-motile populations, often coexist in bacteria communities. However, the physiological functions of motile subpopulations in bacterial communities are largely unclear, although these cells are believed to be important to dispersal, quest for food, and material transport. We recently discovered that motile cells in sessile colonies of peritrichously flagellated bacteria can self-organize into two adjacent, centimeter-scale motile rings surrounding the entire colony. As a result of this motile-ring self-organization, cells generate directed fluid flows that circulate counterclockwise around the colony at a constant peak speed of ~30 µm/s, providing a stable and high-speed avenue for material transport at the macroscopic scale. Our findings revealed a unique form of bacterial self-organization and active transport in bacterial colonies. Based on these established findings, here we aim to understand the biophysical mechanism underlying motile-ring formation via manipulating the self-organization process. We will also study how the self-organized motile rings control collective motion in the bulk part of colonies and will explore whether motile rings contribute to the development of colonies. The project lies at the interface of physics and biology, and the obtained results will be of substantial interest to both fields. Understanding the dynamics of self-organized collective motion in confined bacterial suspensions will provide new insights to flagellar hydrodynamics and to the control of collective dynamics in general active matter systems. Results obtained from this study may also find applications in engineering self-assembled microfluidic systems for long-range fluid pumping and cargo transport. In addition, the findings will advance our understanding of the behavior and the potential physiological functions of motile cell populations in heterogeneous bacterial communities. 此項目將研究最近在細菌菌落中發現的運動環現象，意在理解這一現象產生機制以及生理功能。 在自然界和人體中，細菌普遍以群落的形式生存，例如生物被膜。細菌群落中通常具有環境的非均一性和群體的多樣性，不同群體的生理作用和分工是微生物生態學的重要問題。我們最近發現，尋常培養的細菌菌落中處於運動狀態的亞群體能以類似相分離的方式在邊界層聚集，並且自組織成為高度有序的“運動環”環繞整個菌落。運動環中細菌的鞭毛活動產生了環繞菌落的定向流場，流速高達約30微米/秒。該定向流場有助於菌落內部物質的長距離（厘米尺度）輸運。 基於已有的發現，我們在此項目中計劃研究運動環的形成機制和生理功能，並探索該現像對菌落的發育有何影響。此項目涉及物理學和生物學的交叉領域，所得到的結果對相關領域都有重要的意義。細菌集體運動可以認為是自驅動或者活性物質體系的典型例子，因此此項目的研究結果會加深我們對活性物質體系的認識。同時，細菌集群運動與細菌表面定植和微生物膜的形成初期行為相似，因此對細菌集群運動的研究有助於理解細菌的多細胞狀態和致病過程。

14306820.label: Realisation of objectives
14306820.value: With the funding from this grant, we have realized both objectives. For Objective 1, we studied the development of motile rings into globally rotating colonies; for Objective 2, we elucidated how cells self-organized into local oscillatory motion and further gave rise to the global motion modes in the bulk part of colonies following the onset of motile rings, using multiscale imaging and computational modeling with an active bead-spring model. These results were presented in the publication “Xu et al, 2023”. Meanwhile, inspired by the capability of long-range material transport via motile rings and with funding from this grant, we have been investigating long-distance material transport in other bacterial communities. Long-range material transport is essential to maintain the physiological functions of multicellular organisms such as animals and plants; by contrast, material transport in bacteria is often short-ranged and limited by diffusion. In structured communities of P. aeruginosa, We discover a large-scale and temporally evolving open channel system spontaneously develops in the colony via shear-induced banding (see publication “Li et al, 2022”). Moreover, extending our study of single-cell swimming behavior at air-liquid-solid three phase interfaces during motile ring formation, we also studied how flagellated swimmers interact with solid boundaries. We found that in the presence of viscoelastic polymers flagellated cells swim in less curved trajectories and display reduced near-surface accumulation due to a generic lift force acting on bacterial flagella (see publication “Cao et al, 2022”). Taken together, our findings reveal previously unrecognized facets of bacterial transport and surface exploration that are pertinent to diverse microbial processes and may inform the design of artificial microswimmers capable of navigating through complex geometries.

14306820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306820.value: Three major research outputs arose from this project: 1. Xu H., Huang Y., Zhang R., Wu Y (2023) Autonomous waves and global motion modes in living active solids. Nature Physics: 19, 46–51 Using a biofilm-based bacterial active solid, here we discovered self-sustained elastic waves with unique wave properties not seen in passive solids, such as power-law scaling of wave speed with activity. Under isotropic confinement, the active solid develops two topologically distinct global motion modes that can be selectively excited, with a surprising step-like frequency jump at mode transition. Our findings reveal novel spatiotemporal order in elastic active matter and may guide the development of solid-state adaptive or living materials. [2] Ye Li, Shiqi Liu, Yingdan Zhang, Zi Jing Seng, Haoran Xu, Liang Yang & Yilin Wu (2022) Self-organized canals enable long range directed material transport in bacterial communities. eLife, 11:e79780. Here, we report a unique form of actively regulated long-range directed material transport in structured bacterial communities. Using Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonies as a model system, we discover that a large-scale and temporally evolving open-channel system spontaneously develops in the colony via shear-induced banding. Fluid flows in the open channels support high-speed (up to 450 µm/s) transport of cells and outer membrane vesicles over centimeters, and help to eradicate colonies of a competing species Staphylococcus aureus. The open channels are reminiscent of human-made canals for cargo transport, and the channel flows are driven by interfacial tension mediated by cell-secreted biosurfactants. The spatial-temporal dynamics of fluid flows in the open channels are qualitatively described by flow profile measurement and mathematical modeling. [3] Ding Cao, Mariia Dvoriashyna, Song Liu, Eric Lauga & Yilin Wu (2022) Reduced surface accumulation of swimming bacteria in viscoelastic polymer fluids. PNAS, 119(45):e2212078119. Many bacteria live in natural and clinical environments with abundant macromolecular polymers. While geometrical confinement or surfaces are prevalent in the living environment of bacteria, it is unclear how flagellated bacteria interact with surfaces in polymeric fluids. Here, we found that non-Newtonian hydrodynamic interaction between flagellated bacteria and a solid surface gives rise to a viscoelastic lift force acting on the cells; this lift force leads to several unusual behavioral patterns in contrast to swimming in Newtonian viscous fluids. Our findings will help to understand the transport of bacteria and artificial helical microswimmers in macromolecular environments with ecological and clinical relevance.

14306820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306820.value: Our findings of global motion modes following the onset of self-organized motile rings reveal novel spatiotemporal order in elastic active matter and may guide the development of solid-state adaptive or living materials, such as autonomous actuators for soft robotics, programmable tissues, and synthetic microbial consortia with mechanical functionalities. The discovery of canal-like long-range material transport in Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonies demonstrate that mechanochemical coupling between interfacial force and biosurfactant kinetics can coordinate large-scale material transport in primitive life forms, suggesting a new principle to engineer self-organized microbial communities that we are currently actively exploring. The study on bacterial swimming pattern near solid surfaces will help to understand the transport of bacteria and artificial helical microswimmers in macromolecular environments with ecological and clinical relevance.

14306820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306820.value: Like in animals and plants, long-range directed material transport would undoubtedly bring profound effect to the development, structure, and stress response of bacterial communities. In this project we have studied the self-organization processes underlying two unique forms of long-range material transport in structured bacterial communities, namely motile rings and bacterial canals. We elucidated how cells developed into local oscillatory motion and further gave rise to the global motion modes in the bulk part of colonies following the onset of motile rings, using multiscale imaging and computational modeling. We also understood how a large-scale and temporally-evolving open channel system spontaneously developed in bacterial colonies, forming the bacterial canals. Moreover, we found that in the presence of viscoelastic polymers flagellated cells swim displayed reduced near-surface accumulation due to a generic lift force acting on bacterial flagella. Taken together, our findings reveal previously unrecognized facets of bacterial transport and surface exploration that are pertinent to diverse microbial processes and may inform the design of artificial microswimmers capable of navigating through complex geometries.

14306920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306920.value: This project aims to study the impact of non-spherical droplets onto a dry smooth substrate, and systematically illustrate the effect of droplet shape on the impact dynamics and splashing outcome. Impact of liquid drops onto a solid substrate is ubiquitous in our daily life: it occurs when raindrops hit the ground or when coffee spills onto the floor. It also takes place in many industrial applications, such as ink-jet printing, plasma spraying, and spray coating. Despite numerous studies about spherical droplets impinging a solid substrate, a systematic study of impact by non-spherical droplets is still lacking. In many occasions, however, the shape of droplets is non-spherical: raindrops are deformed by aerodynamic stress and have flattened bottoms [1], many meteoroids are conical due to the interaction with the atmosphere [2], charged droplets have sharpened tips when they approach oppositely charged substrates or objects [3, 4], and oscillating droplets have a variety of non-spherical shapes due to different oscillation modes [5]. How does droplet shape influence the impact dynamics and the splashing outcome? This question remains as an important knowledge gap in the research field of droplet impact . To tackle this fundamental issue, we propose to generate different shaped droplets with ferrofluid under a tunable magnetic field, and experimentally study the effect of shape in the impact process. By fine-tuning the magnetic field, we can systematically obtain different droplet shapes, and study its influence on two fundamental impact subjects: the impact dynamics and the splashing outcome. As an experienced researcher on droplet impact and splashing, the applicant has extensive and strong background in the droplet-impact research: we have studied impacts on smooth, rough and textured substrates and illustrated the complex interaction between droplet and air [Xu1-Xu6]. Based on our excellent track record, we propose this three-year project with a total budget around US$200,000, to further study the important issue of droplet shape effect on impact and splashing. We expect this study to bring new knowledge to droplet impact research and provide useful technological guidance to related industrial processes. 本項目旨在研究非球形液滴對乾燥光滑表面的撞擊，並系統地說明液滴形狀對撞擊動力學和液滴飛濺的影響。在我們的日常生活中，液滴對固體表面的撞擊無處不在：比如當雨滴落到地面上或咖啡濺到地板時。它也發生在許多工業應用中，例如噴墨打印，等離子噴塗和表面噴塗。儘管有許多關於球形液滴撞擊固體表面的研究，對非球形液滴撞擊的系統研究仍然很缺乏。但是，在很多情況下水滴的形狀是非球形的：比如雨滴 [1]，流星[2]，帶電液滴[3，4]和振蕩的液滴等[5]。液滴的形狀會如何影響撞擊動力學和液滴飛濺呢？這個問題仍然存在作為液滴衝擊研究領域的重要知識缺口。 為了解決這個重要問題，我們計劃使用磁場下的鐵磁流體，並通過實驗研究形狀在衝擊過程中的影響。通過微調磁場，我們可以系統地獲得不同的液滴形狀，並研究其對兩個重要問題，撞擊動力學和液體飛濺的影響。 申請人具有對液滴撞擊和飛濺豐富的研究經驗：我們課題組研究阐明了光滑和粗糙的表面對液滴撞擊的影響，並說明了液滴與空氣之間的複雜相互作用[Xu1-Xu6]。基於我們過去的研究經驗，我們提出耗時三年，總預算約為20萬美元的本項目，以進一步闡明液滴形狀對撞擊和飛濺的重要影響。我們期待本研究會帶來新的基礎認知並為相關的工業應用提供有用的技術指導。

14306920.label: Realisation of objectives
14306920.value: Both objective 1 and objective 2 are completely realized. More specifically, for objective 1 we have realized different droplet shapes with ferrofluid under a magnetic field, and used high speed photography to record detailed dynamics with side and bottom views simultaneously. We proposed a super-ellipse model which describes the motion of various droplet shapes, which agrees excellently with the experiment and gives a universal description of impact dynamics across different droplet shapes. For objective 2 we measured the total area of black ferrofluid splatters on surrounding white paper, which reflects the total splashing amount. We then constructed an energy model to describe the relation between droplet shape and splashing amount, and observes a good agreement with the experimental data. All these results are summarized in our publication, "The role of drop shape in impact and splash", Nature Communications, Volumn 12, 3068, 2021.

14306920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306920.value: While extensive studies have been performed on the spherical drops, much less is understood on the non-spherical counterparts, which frequently appear in many actual situations. For example, raindrops are deformed by aerodynamic stress and have flattened bottoms, charged drops develop sharp tips when they approach oppositely charged substrates or when the charge amount is close to the Rayleigh limit, oscillating drops exhibit a variety of non-spherical shapes, and the external electric or magnetic field may also change the shape of drops. As a result, our knowledge is largely limited to one specific drop geometry, and the general picture across different shapes remains missing. In this project, we illustrate the fundamental role of drop shape in impact and splash by experimentally realizing various drop shapes. Experiments show that different drop shapes produce large differences in spreading dynamics, splash onset, and splash amount. However, underlying all these differences we discover universal mechanisms which are valid across various drop shapes. Our study generalizes the basic understanding of drop impact beyond the spherical geometry and brings a fundamental breakthrough in this research field. It also reveals the potential of using drop shape to control impact and splash for practical applications, which is distinct from the conventional parameters like impact velocity, air pressure, material properties of liquid, and substrate. These results have been summarized in our publication in Nature Communications ("The role of drop shape in impact and splash", Q. Liu, J. H. Y. Lo, Y. Li, Y. Liu, J. Zhao, L. Xu, Nature Communications, Volumn 12, 3068, 2021). Moreover, inspired by the droplet shape effect, we further realized the control of flow shapes with flow dipoles, and realize active hydrodynamic metadevices, which enable an active manipulation of the flow field with various functionalities. By adjusting the magnitude and direction of the flow-dipole moment, this device can easily achieve invisibility, flow shielding, and flow enhancing. Furthermore, it is environmentally adaptive and can maintain proper functions in different environments. It is anticipated that this design will significantly enhance tunability and adaptability of hydrodynamic metamaterials in complex and ever-changing environments. These results are summarized in our recent publication in Advanced Materials ("Achieving Environmentally‐Adaptive and Multifunctional Hydrodynamic Metamaterials through Active Control" Chaoran Jiang, Haoran Nie, Mengyao Chen, Xiangying Shen, Lei Xu, Advanced Materials 2313986, 2024).

14306920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306920.value: For the future development, we are currently studying the impact force of the different shaped droplets. Our preliminary data show that the maximum impact force can vary by one order of magnitude for different shaped droplets even at the same impact speed. Moreover, we plan to further vary the topology of the droplet shape and create concave droplets, and compare the impact phenomena of concave droplets versus the convex droplets. This study will further illustrate the role of topology for droplet impact.

14307220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307220.value: Catalytic cross-coupling process has emerged as one of the most straightforward and widespread used protocols for scientists to produce chemical modifications for assembling structurally unprecedented, yet materially and pharmaceutically attractive compounds. Indeed, these methods have revolutionized the way chemists to perform complex organic synthesis. At the center of these synthetic technologies, catalyst development which allows difficult or problematic bond construction process to be proceeded smoothly would be highly attractive. Thus, catalyst exploration and development is particularly central to contemporary catalysis research for innovative organic synthesis. The new development of aromatic bond-construction methodology would advance the current coupling process and put forward of catalysis research. The purposes of this project are (1) to rationally design and explore a new family of tunable phosphine ligands via a facile approach; (2) to investigate the difficult sterically congested coupling process; and (3) to investigate efficient synthetic method for axially chiral ligand syntheses and establish a ligand-enable approach for asymmetric cross-couplings and related direct arylation processes. This project is expected to explore a new field in cross-coupling reactions. The fundamental knowledge obtained during the course of catalyst development and the rationale of stereocommunication of chiral metal complex to cross coupling partners (e.g. pi-pi-interaction) would be of significant value for academic interest and potential applications. The planned study is based on our previous success in the ligand/catalyst design and synthesis, and our extensive experiences in aromatic bond-construction research. These new areas will offer us an excellent opportunity in making a substantial advancement to the frontier of catalysis research and may help us to establish a foundation for fine-chemical industry in Hong Kong. 催化交叉偶聯工藝已經成為科學家進行化學修飾以組裝結構上空前的，但在材料和藥物方面具有吸引力的化合物的最直接，最廣泛使用的方案之一。實際上，這些方法徹底改變了化學家進行複雜有機合成的方式。在這些合成技術的中心，允許難於或成問題的鍵構建過程順利進行的催化劑開發將具有極大的吸引力。因此，催化劑的探索和開發對於當代有機合成催化研究的研究尤為重要。 芳香鍵構建方法的新發展將推動目前的偶聯過程，並提出催化研究。該項目的目的是（1）通過簡便的方法合理設計和探索新的可調膦配體家族； （2）研究困難的空間擁塞耦合過程； （3）研究軸向手性配體合成的有效合成方法，並建立用於非對稱交叉偶聯和相關直接芳構化過程的配體使能方法。 預計該項目將探索交叉偶聯反應的新領域。在催化劑開發過程中獲得的基本知識以及手性金屬配合物與交叉偶合夥伴之間進行立體通信的原理（例如pi-pi-interaction）將對學術興趣和潛在應用具有重要價值。計劃的研究基於我們先前在配體/催化劑設計和合成方面的成功以及我們在芳香鍵構建研究中的豐富經驗。這些新領域將為我們提供一個極好的機會，在催化研究領域取得重大進展，並可能有助於我們為香港精細化工行業奠定基礎。

14307220.label: Realisation of objectives
14307220.value: This is the completion report of the funding 14307220. The research activities under this project were conducted from January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2023. Despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic along with a number of quarantine period in the laboratory, we had tried the best to accomplish the objectives in this catalysis research project. The following sections provide a detailed account of the research activities conducted during this period. The main focus of this research proposal is to design and explore new series of easily modifiable phosphine ligands fit for challenging cross-coupling reactions. While focusing on synthesizing ligands to achieve pi-extended structures, we unexpectedly discovered a new synthetic pathway to access polyarene frameworks. Notably, we successfully synthesized a range of fused-arene and chromene structures without the use of any transition metal catalysts. This versatile protocol enables our research team to generate diverse ligand skeletons and precursors. This research contribution was published in 2021 in Organic Letters (Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6455). With our initial family of ligands in hand, we further investigated the perfluoroalkylation of sterically congested diarylamine compounds. We successfully accomplished the difluoromethylation of secondary anilines that were hindered by steric factors. Through meticulous screening of reaction conditions, we discovered that the difluoromethylation process is notably enhanced by the inclusion of appropriate bases. These research findings were published in 2022 in Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry (Org. Biol. Chem. 2022, 20, 1883). Utilizing our strategically designed indolylphosphine ligands, we embarked on investigating the challenging coupling of highly sterically congested ArCl coupling partners in the aromatic borylation process. Notably, employing only the -PPh2-containing ligand (in contrast to the commonly used and costly -PCy2 or -P(t-Bu)2 analogs), we successfully achieved the Miyaura borylation of extremely hindered aryl chlorides. These instances exemplify the most versatile borylation protocol for ArCl substrates. Moreover, theoretical studies elucidated that the specially-tailored ligand is exceptionally well-suited for accommodating highly sterically demanding substrates in cross-coupling reactions. This significant research breakthrough was published in 2022 in ACS Catalysis (ACS Catal. 2022, 12, 3507). With the newly developed ligand systems, we also extensively investigated the relevant C-H arylation process. Several of our findings showed great promise in aromatic bond-construction processes. Indeed, recognized for our expertise in the field of C-H arylation, we were invited by the Editor of Organic Chemistry Frontiers to contribute a Review on C-H bond functionalization. This comprehensive research summary was published in Organic Chemistry Frontiers in 2022 (Org. Chem. Front. 2022, 9, 1922). With respect to our fruitful finding published in ACS Catalysis in 2022, we were invited by the Editor of Chemistry An Asian Journal to contribute an overview of recent expedition of modern catalytic aromatic borylation processes and their potential applications. This contribution was submitted in mid-2023 and published in late 2023 (Chem. Asian J. 2023, e202300649). Following the COVID-19 pandemic, we dedicated significant efforts to conducting research on highly sterically hindered cross-coupling processes. Through strategic manipulation of the ligand structure, we successfully designed a fittingly tuned ligand suitable for facilitating extremely sterically congested cross-coupling reactions between ArCl and C2-H benzoxazoles. This research contribution was published in early December 2024 (Organic Letters, 2024, ASAP online, doi.org/10.1021/acs.orglett.4c04117). Additionally, we have made strides in desymmetrizing the phosphine ligands and attempted diastereoselective separation, although this endeavor proved to be unsuccessful. We have extensively conducted research activities focusing on highly tunable and easily modifiable ligand development. Given our current success, we were recognized and invited by the Editor of Organic Syntheses to contribute an article about the expedition of this type of ligand, along with the detail synthetic protocols for assembling new catalytic systems. This account was published in late 2024 (Organic Syntheses, 2024, 101, 423).

14307220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307220.value: Major finding and research outcome In this project, we have developed a new series of highly tunable phosphine ligands that effectively promote highly sterically hindered cross-coupling reactions. It is worth noting that we have achieved the lowest catalyst loading to date and demonstrated the broadest substrate scope for exceedingly hindered aromatic borylation. The key to the success of this process lies in identifying a well-suited ligand that balances the challenges of both oxidative addition and reductive elimination steps. Remarkably, this ligand utilizes only the -PPh2 moiety, making it the most cost-effective "P" group compared to other well-known and commercialized phosphines. This groundbreaking research finding was published in ACS Catalysis in 2022. As a recognition of our research, we were invited to contribute a comprehensive review on the new catalyst system for addressing the challenges of modern borylation processes. This review was published in Chemistry - An Asian Journal in 2023. In addition to traditional cross-coupling reactions, we have been actively exploring C-H bond arylation processes. Leveraging our newly developed ligand family, we successfully achieved highly sterically congested C-H arylation from ArCl. This significant discovery was published in Organic Letters in December 2024. Recognizing the innovative ligand skeleton, we were invited to provide a review detailing the design and development of these ligands. This review was published in Organic Syntheses in late 2024.

14307320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307320.value: The Standard Model of Particle Physics is one of the most successful predictive models that we have of Nature. Among many other predictions, it requires the existence of a spin-0 particle that gives mass to all other elementary particles, the Higgs boson. On July 4, 2012, the ATLAS and the CMS collaborations at CERN (the European Organization for Nuclear Physics), announced its discovery in the analysis of proton-proton collisions produced by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Subsequent studies demonstrated that it is indeed a scalar particle, as predicted by the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism. The discovery was recognized with the High Energy and Particle Physics Prize 2013 of the European Physical Society, among others. After an extended shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades, the LHC restarted operations with a collision energy of 13 TeV, in what is called the “Run 2” data-taking period, ended in December 2018. After another extended shut-down period, LHC collisions will resume in early 2021; Run 3 will then accumulate a total integrated luminosity of around 300 fb-1, which will significantly increase the sensitivity of several searches for new physics, as well as the precision reached in the measurement of related SM processes. The much larger run 3 sample will allow much more stringent constraints on the rates of Lepton-Flavor-Violating decays of the Higgs boson. Hong Kong institutions, working jointly as the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP), were accepted in June of 2014 as members of the ATLAS Experimental Collaboration. Since then, Hong Kong researchers and students have made strong contributions to the analysis of LHC data and have adopted a number of responsibilities within ATLAS. The goal of this project is to further strengthen the participation of Hong Kong at CERN through work on the following areas: 1. Search for decays of the 125 GeV Higgs boson in final states that violate lepton flavor conservation. 2. Study the performance of the charged lepton reconstruction and identification algorithms in ATLAS in the phase space relevant for the search. 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. These areas are designed to avoid overlap with the objectives of the JCFP proposals and, to the maximum extent possible, to complement them to build a solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14307320.label: Realisation of objectives
14307320.value: Objective 1. Search for decays of the 125 GeV Higgs boson in final states that violate lepton flavor conservation. Since the discovery of the Higgs boson [ATL12, CMS12], the study of its properties and its potential use as a tool in the search for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) remains one of the most important and active areas of research at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN. The Standard Model of particle physics (SM) predicts that the decay of the Higgs boson into lepton-flavor-violating (LFV) final states should be strongly suppressed; accordingly, the direct observation of such states at the LHC experiments would constitute an important and revealing sign of new physics, since LFV transitions would only be detectable at the LHC if they are as high as is predicted by some BSM theories (e.g., extensions of the Higgs sector or warped extra dimensions [AHR13, AGA09, ALB09]). During earlier studies, with strong contributions from our team, the ATLAS Collaboration published the results of searches for LFV decays of high-mass resonances using 3.2/fb of proton-proton collision data, at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, using the e-mu channel [LFV15], and also including the tau lepton channels (e+tau, mu+tau) [LFV16]; these results were superseded with 36.1/fb of data [LFV18]. Those searches have the same final state particle combinations studied in this project, but they focus on the high-mass region (above 600 GeV) instead of the range around the Higgs boson mass (125 GeV). Building upon our contributions to those searches (where we led studies of the selection criteria, the definition and validation of control regions to estimate standard model backgrounds, and were heavily involved in the approval and publication of the results), we became one of the main contributors to the search of possible LFV decays of the Higgs boson, and we were one of the main teams in charge of preparing the publication based on 36.1/fb of pp collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV [LFV20], for which we defined and added new signal regions in events where the Higgs boson is likely to have been produced through vector-boson-fusion (VBF), with independent regions defined depending on whether the tau leptons decayed hadronically or leptonically; we also implemented and optimized a multivariate analysis (MVA) based on boosted decision trees (BDT) to treat the VBF region, achieving a higher statistical significance than the corresponding cut-based analysis. We continued to refine the selection and statistical treatment of the search, and we became one of the main groups in charge of preparing the most recent publication, based on the full run 2 dataset (138/fb) and published in JHEP [LFV23]. While carrying out this work, in preparation for the Snowmass particle physics community planning exercise, we also prepared the first estimations of the limits on cross section times branching ratio for these final states that are expected with the full run 3 dataset (around 300/fb at 13.6 TeV). Objective 2. Study the performance of the charged lepton reconstruction and identification algorithms in ATLAS in the phase space relevant for the search. Our group has maintained a continuous involvement in the implementation, study and improvement of muon identification algorithms since the beginning of our work with the ATLAS collaboration. In collaboration with the Muon Combined Performance group, we have studied, characterized and improved the performance of the algorithms used in ATLAS to identify muons using only tracking and calorimeter information, using cut-based identification and also MVA techniques, both within the ATLAS Software framework (Athena/ROOT) and through the use of publicly available machine learning tools (TensorFlow [ABA15], Keras [CHO15] and PyTorch [PAS17]). We also carried out a re-tuning of the working points of one of these algorithms (specifically the CaloMuonScore algorithm within the ATLAS offline software) to account for the current physics environment. We also improved the muon subdetector validation code used to (A) monitor the performance of the muon algorithms during simulation, digitization and reconstruction, and to (B) study the plausibility of suitable modifications within the respective job transformation output. We also worked on the monitoring of muon reconstruction tests running daily on the ATLAS Release Tester (which is a system designed to run test jobs after a nightly release of the ATLAS offline software has been built). Objective 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One postdoctoral research associate, two PhD students (Minlin Wu and Michael Chu) and one undergraduate student (Siu Yin Fung) worked on the project. This work allowed them to benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), to work with recent machine learning and multivariate analysis techniques, to learn several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and to work with recent proton-proton collision and Monte Carlo simulation data from the Large Hadron Collider on searches and measurements at the energy frontier. 14307320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307320.value: Direct searches for lepton flavour violation in Higgs boson decays, H to e tau and H to mu tau, were performed using data collected with the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The searches are based on a data sample of proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138/fb. Leptonic (tau to l nu_l nu_tau) and hadronic (tau to hadrons nu_tau) decays of the tau-lepton are considered. Two background estimation techniques are employed: the MC-template method, based on data-corrected simulation samples, and the Symmetry method, based on exploiting the symmetry between electrons and muons in the Standard Model backgrounds. No significant excess of events is observed and the results are interpreted as upper limits on lepton-flavour-violating branching ratios of the Higgs boson. The observed (expected) upper limits set on the branching ratios at 95% confidence level, B(H to e tau) less than 0.20% (0.12%) and B(H to mu tau) less than 0.18% (0.09%), are obtained with the MC-template method from a simultaneous measurement of potential H to e tau and H to mu tau signals. The best-fit branching ratio difference, B(H to mu tau)-B(H to e tau), measured with the Symmetry method in the channel where the tau-lepton decays to leptons, is (0.25 +- 0.10)%, compatible with a value of zero within 2.5 sigma. Regarding the lepton reconstruction and identification algorithms, we improved the working points used in muon identification algorithms and improved the muon sub-detector validation code used to (A) monitor their performance on simulation, digitization and reconstruction, and to (B) study suitable modifications. We also worked on the monitoring of muon reconstruction tests running daily on the ATLAS Release Tester (which is a system designed to run test jobs after a nightly release of the ATLAS offline software has been built).

14307320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307320.value: There are several avenues to extend and/or refine the work done in this project. Regarding the search for LFV decays of the Higgs boson, both the MC-based method and the Symmetry method can be tuned to the larger pileup conditions present in run 3. Data-driven methods to estimate the fake-lepton background contribution, as well as dedicated control regions to validate the background modelling, can be further developed. The different trigger and detector efficiencies for electrons and muons will need to be recalibrated, and the strategies for one- and two- parameters of interest fits can be refined. Lepton reconstruction can benefit from the use of artificial neural networks and boosted decision trees. We will pursue these actions in GRF project 14308924, which will start in January 2025, aiming to enhance the sensitivity above the expected gain from luminosity, with the goal of resolving, if possible, the enticing marginal compatibility with the SM found in this project (2.5 sigma).

14307320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307320.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature on two fronts: (a) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories, and (b) improve the particle reconstruction tools used to study high- energy particle collisions. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the “Standard Model”, or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) measure the frequency with which the Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, decays into particles of different type (specifically, "flavour") pairs, to determine any possible discrepancies with the SM, and (b) improve the methods used to identify and reconstruct the particles that are produced in high-energy particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

14307420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307420.value: Statistical hypothesis testing is a critical tool to decide whether the data collected in the experiment contains sufficient information to confirm or discard a proposition. It provides a mechanism for making quantitative decisions and is widely used in almost all fields, including physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, economics, and social science. Recently the hypothesis testing has also been exploited in the emerging field of quantum information science where the data is obtained via the measurement of quantum systems. Due to the quantum correlations, the quantum hypothesis testing has many different features from the classical hypothesis testing. The aim of this project is to develop control-enhanced schemes for quantum hypothesis testing that can improve the success rate of confirming or discarding a quantum hypothesis. A typical scenario of quantum hypothesis testing is to discriminate two dynamical models, one represents the null hypothesis and the other as the alternative hypothesis. By preparing a probe state and let it evolve under the dynamics, we can get the output state and make a decision to accept either the null hypothesis or the alternative hypothesis based on the measurement performed on the output state. Besides optimizing the probe state and the measurement, additional controls can be added during the evolution to further improve the success rate of the decision. However, thus far the optimal controls that can lead to maximal improvement have only been identified under the ideal unitary dynamics. For general noisy dynamics, the controls that can improve the performance of quantum hypothesis testing are largely unexplored. In this project, we aim to develop systematic methods to obtain optimal controls to achieve the maximal success rate under realistic noisy dynamics. Our preliminary study has shown that for some noisy dynamics quantum error correction, a special control strategy, can be employed to improve the success rate up to 100 percent, which is otherwise impossible under the free evolution. This shows the potential of the controlled strategies in improving the success rate of quantum hypothesis testing. Although a 100 percent success rate is not always achievable, we expect the control-enhanced schemes can lead to significant improvement in general quantum hypothesis testing. Findings from this project will broaden the horizon of researches in quantum hypothesis testing and are expected to have wide implications for various applications of quantum hypothesis testing, such as quantum detection, quantum illumination, quantum metrology, etc. 統計假設檢驗是決定實驗中收集的數據是否包含足夠的信息以確認或丟棄命題的關鍵工具。它提供了一種做出定量決策的機制，並且幾乎在所有領域都得到了廣泛使用，包括物理，化學，生物學，工程學，經濟學和社會科學。最近，在量子信息科學的新興領域中也使用了假設檢驗，在該領域中，數據是通過測量量子系統獲得的。由於量子相關性，量子假設檢驗與經典假設檢驗具有許多不同的特徵。該項目的目的是開髮用於量子假設測試的控制增強方案，該方案可以提高確認或丟棄量子假設的成功率。 量子假設檢驗的一種典型情況是區分兩個動力學模型，一個代表原假設，另一個代表替代假設。通過準備一個探測狀態並使其在動態條件下演化，我們可以獲取輸出狀態，並基於對輸出狀態執行的測量來決定接受零假設或替代假設。除了優化探針狀態和測量之外，還可以在演進過程中添加其他控制，以進一步提高決策的成功率。但是，到目前為止，只能在理想的動力學條件下確定可以帶來最大改善的最佳控制。對於一般的嘈雜動力學，可以改善量子假設測試性能的控件在很大程度上尚未開發。在此項目中，我們旨在開發系統的方法來獲得最佳控制，以在現實的嘈雜動態下實現最大成功率。 我們的初步研究表明，對於某些嘈雜的動力學量子誤差校正，可以採用一種特殊的控制策略來將成功率提高到100％，這在自由進化下是不可能的。這顯示了控制策略在提高量子假設檢驗成功率方面的潛力。儘管並非總是能夠成功實現100％的成功率，但我們預計，控制增強的方案可以顯著改善常規量子假設檢驗。該項目的發現將拓寬量子假設檢驗的研究範圍，並有望對量子假設檢驗的各種應用產生廣泛的影響，例如量子檢測，量子照明，量子計量學等。

14307420.label: Realisation of objectives
14307420.value: The first objective sought to establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which two general Markovian quantum dynamics can be perfectly distinguished within a finite time. This aim has been thoroughly realized through rigorous theoretical advancement. In the publication , “Enhanced quantum hypothesis testing via the interplay between coherent evolution and noises” (Li et al., Commun. Phys. 8, 19 (2025)), we successfully moved beyond the traditional paradigm where noise is considered purely detrimental. We derived a general and verifiable criterion that provides sufficient conditions for noisy dynamics to surpass the performance limits set by noiseless, unitary evolution. This criterion elegantly connects the properties of the Lindblad noise operators with the spectral gap of the Hamiltonian difference, formally characterizing when noise dependency on the system’s Hamiltonian can enhance discriminability. The work thus provides a foundational theoretical framework for understanding perfect and enhanced distinguishability in open quantum systems, thereby fully accomplishing the theoretical core of this objective. This foundational work directly builds upon and extends the PI’s earlier research into the necessary and sufficient conditions for perfect distinguishability with quantum error correction (Chen & Yuan, Phys. Rev. A 100, 022336 (2019)). The second objective focused on developing optimal control strategies to improve the success rate of quantum hypothesis testing. This goal has been achieved comprehensively through a multi-faceted research effort. The theoretical insight that coherent control can strategically reshape the interaction between the system and its noisy environment was formulated and refined in several high-profile publications. Specifically, the study "Cooperation between Coherent Control and Noises in Quantum Metrology" (Chen, Miao & Yuan, Adv. Quantum Technol. 6, 2200165 (2023)) directly explored the synergistic potential of control and noise. Furthermore, the principles of optimal control were generalized in "Optimal Strategies of Quantum Metrology with a Strict Hierarchy" (Liu et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 070803 (2023)), establishing rigorous performance limits. Complementary foundational work on the role of measurement strategies was advanced in "Information Geometry under Hierarchical Quantum Measurement" (Chen, Chen & Yuan, Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 250502 (2022)). To translate theory into practice, the team developed and released “QuanEstimation,” an open-source software toolkit for quantum parameter estimation and optimal control design (Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. Research 4, 043057 (2022)). This toolkit empowers the broader research community to implement and test optimal control strategies, thereby extending the impact of the project’s findings. The combination of analytical control schemes and numerical optimization tools solidly fulfills the mandate of this objective. The third and final objective was to experimentally tailor and test the optimally controlled schemes. This objective has been successfully and elegantly realized in an experimental campaign using an ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance platform, a specialty of the Co-I’s laboratory. As detailed in the Communications Physics paper (Li et al., Commun. Phys. 8, 19 (2025)), we employed the proton spins in formic acid as a two-level system and utilized a sensitive rubidium atomic magnetometer for state readout. The experiment explicitly demonstrated two key phenomena predicted by the theory. First, it showed that in the presence of engineered dephasing and amplitude-damping noise with distinct relaxation times (T1 ≠ T2), the success probability for discriminating two magnetic fields could indeed exceed the fundamental limit imposed by unitary dynamics. Second, and more strikingly, the experiment implemented a control-assisted protocol where a coherent control field was applied to a scenario with initially harmful, Hamiltonian-independent noise. This intervention made the noise Hamiltonian-dependent, thereby boosting the discrimination success probability beyond the unitary ceiling for a tailored evolution time. The experimental data showed excellent agreement with theoretical simulations, validating the practical feasibility and effectiveness of the control-enhanced quantum hypothesis testing framework.

14307420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307420.value: This project has fundamentally re-evaluated the role of noise in quantum hypothesis testing (QHT), transforming it from a detrimental factor into a potential resource. The major theoretical finding is the establishment of sufficient conditions under which Markovian noise correlated with the system Hamiltonian can enhance the success probability of discriminating two quantum dynamics beyond the limit achievable under noiseless, unitary evolution (Li et al., Commun. Phys. 8, 19 (2025)). This challenges the long-held assumption that noise invariably degrades quantum information processing performance. Building on this, a second key outcome is the development of coherent control strategies that can actively engineer the system-environment interaction. We demonstrated that when noise is initially independent and harmful, the application of a tailored coherent control field can render the noise Hamiltonian-dependent, thereby converting it into a beneficial resource that boosts discrimination accuracy (Chen, Miao & Yuan, Adv. Quantum Technol. 6, 2200165 (2023)). This synergy between control and noise defines a novel paradigm for enhancing quantum sensing protocols. These theoretical advances were conclusively validated through experimental implementation on an ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance platform. The experiment successfully demonstrated both noise-assisted and control-enhanced QHT, with results showing a measurable increase in success probability that surpassed the unitary limit (Li et al., Commun. Phys. 8, 19 (2025)). This experimental proof-of-concept bridges theory and practice, showcasing the immediate applicability of these schemes in quantum metrology and sensing, such as in the precise discrimination of magnetic fields. In support of these core findings, the project also produced significant methodological outputs, including the open-source toolkit “QuanEstimation” for optimal quantum parameter estimation (Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. Research 4, 043057 (2022)) and foundational studies on the limits of quantum measurements (Chen, Chen & Yuan, Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 250502 (2022)). Collectively, these outcomes advance the theoretical framework of quantum hypothesis testing, provide practical control protocols, and offer a new perspective on leveraging environmental interactions for superior quantum technological performance.

14307420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307420.value: The findings of this project open several promising avenues for further development. The immediate next step is to extend the noise-enhanced hypothesis testing framework to non-Markovian environments, where memory effects could provide additional coherent resources for discrimination. Furthermore, the principles demonstrated in spin systems can be translated to other scalable platforms, such as nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond or superconducting circuits, to develop practical quantum sensors with enhanced robustness and precision.

14307420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307420.value: This research explored a surprising idea in quantum technology: sometimes, "noise" or interference can actually help rather than hinder a quantum measurement. Just as background chatter might sometimes help you pick out a specific voice, we showed that certain types of quantum noise can make it easier to tell two possible quantum signals apart—a process called hypothesis testing. We then went a step further. Even when noise is unhelpful, we demonstrated that by applying a carefully designed control signal—like using a remote control to adjust a TV’s reception—we can make the noise work in our favor. We successfully tested these ideas in a lab experiment using atomic-scale magnets. The significance of this work is that it turns a fundamental problem in quantum science (noise) into a potential tool. This could lead to more sensitive quantum sensors for medical imaging, more accurate navigation systems, and better methods for discovering new materials or fundamental particles. Our work provides a new way to build more powerful and reliable quantum technologies by cleverly using, rather than just fighting against, the noisy quantum world.

14307620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307620.value: Hydrogen energy holds the great promise as the next-generation energy-carrier, as it is green, sustainable, and carbon-footprint-free, and has a high specific enthalpy of combustion. Photocatalytic overall water splitting (POWS) driven by semiconducting materials provides an efficient avenue to hydrogen energy. An ideal POWS photocatalyst candidate is red phosphorus (RP), owing to its broad-range photo-absorption, superior charge separation and transportation, and suitable redox band potentials for water splitting. The bottleneck in utilizing RP for POWS is the lack of surface active sites for water oxidation into dioxygen and proton reduction in dihydrogen. One promising solution is the modification of RP’s surface with co-catalysts to increase its catalytic activity. However, constructing RP/co-catalyst motif to enable high-performance POWS remains challenging. One limitation is that the micron grain size, as the general feature of previously reported RPs, affords long distances for carrier diffusion from the bulk to the surface and small surface area that accommodates low density of co-catalyst loading. Moreover, introducing exotic, off-the-shelf co-catalysts usually results in poor interactions between RP and co-catalyst that disfavors their interfacial charge transfer and, in this case, co-catalysts tend to agglomerate or reconstruct to become inactivated. To circumvent these challenges, this project aims to in situ epitaxy of transition metal-phosphide nanocluster (TMPN) co-catalysts on zero-dimension (0D) RP quantum dots (RPQDs) by which to achieve efficient and stable POWS. The design of 0D/0D RPQDs/TMPN core-shell photocatalysts will bring benefits for photon to charge conversion, interfacial charge transfer, and surface catalysis, the entire procedures of POWS. RPQDs bear ultrastrong photon harvesting and the shortest carrier diffusion distance to enhance electron and hole availabilities. The in situ epitaxy, in partnership with the multivalence and nonmetal natures of elemental phosphorus, pose chemical and electronical coupling between RPQDs and TMPN to create interfacial charge transfer expressway. Nanosized TMPs have been demonstrated theoretically and experimentally as efficient water splitting catalysts and the ultrafine size of RPQDs enables high-concentration TMPN loading. Through these structural, compositional and electronic designs, we anticipate the realization of close-to-practical POWS systems. 氫氣是一種無碳且含有高燃燒焓的能源，有望成為新一代可持續能源載體。氫氣可以由半導體光催化分解水來產生。在各種半導體光催化材料中，紅磷能吸收較寬範圍的太陽光譜，擁有優良的電荷分離和傳輸性能及合適的價帶和導帶位置。紅磷光催化材料雖然憑借以上性質在光催化全分解水領域收到了廣泛的關注，但其表面缺少用於分解水的反應活性位點，大大限制了這個材料的實用性。常用的解決方法是在紅磷材料表面修飾助催化劑，但是通過構築紅磷/助催化劑異質結來實現高效的光催化全分解水性能仍存在巨大的挑戰。首先，紅磷的微米級別大粒徑不利於電子空穴從內部到外部的傳輸，其較低的比表面積容易導致較低的助催化劑負載濃度。再者，通常所採用的助催化劑負載方法通過非原位和非外延途徑來引入助催化劑，導致所合成的異質結構擁有較弱的界面相互作用，不利於界面的電子傳遞。此外，在這種情況下，助催化劑容易在催化過程中團聚，導致活性降低。針對以上難題，申請人將致力於把過渡金屬磷化物團簇原位生長在紅磷量子點上，合成出“零維/零維”型的紅磷量子點/過渡金屬磷化物核殼結構光催化材料，實現高濃度的磷化物負載、牢固的界面相互作用，以期調控光催化分解水全過程（光子到電子轉換、界面電子轉移、表面催化），進而構築出高效的光催化全分解水體系。在此設計中，紅磷量子點的寬吸光範圍、較短的電荷傳輸通道可以讓更多光生電子到達材料表面，原位外延誘導生長的界面化學鍵可以提供更多的界面電子傳輸高速路，促進電子從紅磷轉移到過渡金屬磷化物上，而過渡金屬磷化物用作助催化劑高效分解水產氫制氧。通過以上設計，申請人希望構建出能夠接近實際應用的光催化全分解水體系。

14307620.label: Realisation of objectives
14307620.value: Objective 1 has been fully addressed. Zero-dimension red phosphorus quantum dots (RPQDs) were prepared from a commercial bulk RP by a hydrothermal process. In detail, 1.5 g of commercial RP was dispersed in 30 mL deionized water, and the above mixture was sealed in a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave and heated at 200 °C for 12 h. Objective 2 has been achieved. Single-atoms of transitional metals including Fe, Co, W, Ni & Mo were implanted into RPQDs by a facile and simple ultrasonic method. Objective 3 has been realized. Photocatalytic and photoelectrochemical measurements were carried out to evaluate the efficiency of the new materials for overall water splitting. Objective 4 has been accomplished. Our experimental results indicated that Ni-RPQDs among all the samples had the best photocatalytic activity, and explanation has been proposed for this system as shown in the attached Research Output 4.

14307620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307620.value: Preliminary investigation on the fabrication of red phosphorus quantum dots revealed an interesting dendritic red P (DRP) photocatalyst. As shown in Publication 1, this new material is prepared by using a one-step CVD strategy with the assistance of Bi as a catalyst. The DRP product was found to consist of the Hittorf’s phase in the main stems and the fibrous phase in the lateral branches. The new photocatalyst has significantly extended lifetime by avoiding charge recombination and self-trapping. As a result, superior and stable photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance was achieved in the DRP product. The introduction of transitional metals into substrates other than red P was also investigated. Publication 2 reports the incorporation of Ni and Fe into CuCo layered double hydroxide (denoted as NiFe-CuCo LDH) that serves as an active and durable OER electrode for High performance seawater electrolysis. With abundant exposed multi-metal sites and well-defined micro/nanostructures, the NiFe-CuCo LDH catalyst requires very low overpotentials to yield high current density. Moreover, it exhibits very high OER selectivity (Faradaic efficiency of 97.4% for O2 at 500 mA/cm2) and superior durability during operation. Publication 3 represents the main findings from this project. Red phosphorus quantum dots (RPQDs) were fabricated, and a series of transition metal single atoms including Fe, Co, W, Ni and Mo were loaded onto it. Among the samples, the photocatalytic activity of Ni-RPQD is the highest for water splitting. The Ni single atoms (Ni SA) show a unique anchoring state by occupying the phosphorus vacancy of phosphorus. Interestingly, the Ni-P bonds function as electron antennas to largely facilitate charge extraction and transfer. Moreover, the introduction of Ni SA would reduce the band gap and broaden the absorption of light to improve the overall photocatalytic activity under visible light. Owing to the optimized electronic structure and optical property, the Ni-RPQD exhibits a remarkable hydrogen production efficiency, which is far beyond the pristine RPQD and most RP-based photocatalysts. DFT calculations indicate that the introduction of Ni SA significantly modulates the electronic structures, where Ni-3d orbitals display high activity to enhance the electron transfer and the neighboring P sites facilitate the band gap alleviation. This further leads to the more energetically preferred water adsorption and dissociation process for H2 generation of photocatalysis. This work reveals the great potential of combining advanced SA concepts with RP to enable efficient photocatalysis.

14500120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500120.value: Perishable inventory systems with fixed product lifetime are a fundamental class of inventory systems in inventory theory and have been studied extensively since 1960s. The optimal policy for these systems is very complex and intractable computationally in general due to the curse of dimensionality. Thus, researchers turned to develop effective heuristic policies since 1970s. Most of the existing heuristics focus on the setting with zero ordering lead time (i.e., the firm receives the orders immediately after they are placed). Only a few studies have developed heuristics for the systems with positive lead times, largely because these systems are more complex than their zero-lead-time counterparts. None of these studies explores the asymptotic optimality of their proposed heuristics when a certain system parameter is large. In this project, we consider a periodic-review perishable inventory system with positive lead times over an infinite planning horizon. The demands are independent and identically distributed random variables in different periods, and are satisfied by the on-hand inventory using the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) issuance policy (i.e., the oldest inventory is used first to satisfy demand). Unsatisfied demands are backlogged. For this system, we propose to conduct a comprehensive study on two classes of potentially asymptotically optimal policies. The first class is the constant-order policies (COP) that place a constant order in each period, regardless of the system state. Building on our preliminary results, we propose to investigate the asymptotic optimality of the best COP with large lead times and with large backlogging costs, and conduct an extensive numerical study to identify the scenarios where the best COP performs well. The second class is the projected inventory base-stock policies (PiBSP) that place an order in each period to raise the projected or expected inventory level at the order arrival to a base-stock level as much as possible. We propose to investigate the asymptotic optimality of the best PiBSP along several system parameters (e.g., lifetime and backlogging cost), and conduct an extensive numerical study to identify the scenarios where the best PiBSP performs well. If successful, the research output of this project will not only significantly advance the inventory theory on perishable inventory systems with positive lead times, but also help practitioners effectively manage their perishable products. 具有固定產品生命周期的易腐產品庫存系統是庫存理論中壹類非常重要的庫存系統，自二十世紀六十年代以來獲得了廣泛研究。這類系統的最優控制策略非常復雜，並且由於維數災難，通常是難以計算的。因此，研究人員早在二十世紀七十年代就開始開發有效的啟發式策略。現有的大多數啟發式策略都專註於訂貨提前期為零的情形，即企業在下達訂單後立即收到訂單。只有很少的研究為提前期為正的系統開發了啟發式策略，主要是因為這些系統比提前期為零的系統更為復雜。這些研究都沒有探索其建議的啟發式策略在某個系統參數很大時的漸近最優性。在這壹項目中，我們考慮壹個按周期盤點的提前期為正的無限周期易腐產品庫存系統。不同周期的需求是獨立且同分布的隨機變量，並且使用先進先出(FIFO)的發行策略通過現有庫存來滿足需求（即首先使用最老的庫存來滿足需求）。未滿足的需求會被延期到未來進行滿足。對於該系統，我們建議對兩類潛在漸近最優策略進行全面研究。第壹類是固定訂單策略。該策略不管系統狀態如何在每個周期下達相同的訂單。基於我們的初步結果，我們建議研究最優固定訂單策略在長訂貨提前期以及高缺貨成本的漸近最優性，並進行廣泛的數值研究以識別在何種情形下其表現良好。第二類是規劃庫存基本庫存策略。該策略在每個期間下達訂單以將訂單到達時的規劃或期望庫存水平盡可能提高到基本庫存水平。我們建議研究最優規劃庫存基本庫存策略在幾個系統參數（如：產品生命周期、缺貨成本）的漸近最優性，並進行廣泛的數值研究以識別在何種情形下其表現良好。如果獲得成功，該項目的研究成果將不僅大大推進訂貨提前期為正的易腐產品庫存系統的理論研究，並且還將幫助從業人員有效地管理其易腐產品。

14500120.label: Realisation of objectives
14500120.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. First, we found that the class of constant-order policies generally performs poorly in perishable inventory systems with positive lead times. Consequently, we expect these policies to be asymptotically suboptimal with large unit penalty costs, except under very specific settings (e.g., systems where the product lifetime equals one period). Considering their poor performance, we believe further investigation of this class of policies is not worthwhile. Therefore, we have achieved Objective 1 in a negative sense. Second, we have obtained significant results for the class of projected inventory base-stock policies, now renamed as projected inventory level (PIL) policies following recent literature. Notably, we proved that under a large class of unbounded demand distributions, the best PIL policy is asymptotically optimal with large unit penalty costs. For bounded demand distributions, we characterized its asymptotic performance and compared it with the best base-stock policy. Additionally, we established the asymptotic optimality of the best PIL policy with large demand population sizes and identified a large class of issuance policies under which the optimality gap decays exponentially in the backlogging system. To facilitate computation and enhance scalability, we also developed a class of approximate PIL (APIL) policies and proved that most of our results for the best PIL policy also hold for the best APIL policy. Our numerical results demonstrate that both PIL and APIL policies perform consistently close to optimal. In summary, we have not only fully achieved Objective 2 but also successfully met our ultimate goal of developing provably near-optimal heuristic policies for perishable inventory systems with positive lead times.

14500120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500120.value: First, we conducted a compressive study on the class of PIL policies in perishable inventory systems with positive lead times and obtained significant results. Notably, we proved that under a large class of unbounded demand distributions, the best PIL policy is asymptotically optimal with large unit penalty costs. For bounded demand distributions, we characterized its asymptotic performance and compared it with the best base-stock policy. Additionally, we established the asymptotic optimality of the best PIL policy with large demand population sizes and identified a large class of issuance policies under which the optimality gap decays exponentially in the backlogging system. To facilitate computation and enhance scalability, we also developed a class of APIL policies and proved that most of our results for the best PIL policy also hold for the best APIL policy. Our numerical results demonstrate that both PIL and APIL policies perform consistently close to optimal. Second, we obtained significant results for the base-stock policy in perishable inventory systems with positive lead times. Some results were reported in our recent paper, “Asymptotic optimality of base-stock policies for perishable inventory systems”, published in the flagship journal Management Science in 2023. Please refer to Part C for details. Recently, we obtained several new results for the base-stock policy in the asymptotic regimes of large unit penalty cost and large demand sizes. Together with my former and current PhD students, Jinzhi Bu and Huanyu Yin, we reported our initial results on the PIL policy in the working paper “Managing perishable inventory systems with positive lead times: Inventory position vs. projected inventory level”. We submitted the paper to Management Science in November 2023 and received Major Revision in March 2024. Please refer to Part C for details. During the revision, we proved several new results for the PIL policy, developed the APIL policy, and proved many results for the APIL policy as well as several new results for the base-stock policy. We are finalizing our revised paper and aim to submit it to Management Science in the spring of 2025. Finally, as a byproduct of this project, we investigated the asymptotic optimality of base-stock policy for three multidimensional inventory systems and reported our findings in the paper “Asymptotic scaling of optimal cost and asymptotic optimality of base-stock policy in several multidimensional inventory systems”. This paper was recently published in another flagship journal Operations Research. Please refer to Part C for details.

14500120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500120.value: First, there is still room for further investigation into the asymptotic optimality or performance of the best PIL, APIL, and base-stock policies with large unit penalty costs. When demand has an unbounded distribution, it remains unknown if the best PIL and APIL policies are asymptotically optimal when our imposed assumption fails. Additionally, for bounded demand distributions, our characterizations of the asymptotic performances of the best PIL, APIL, and base-stock policies are incomplete. It also remains unknown if they are asymptotically optimal under certain conditions. We leave these problems open for future research. Second, there is potential for developing more effective heuristic policies than the current PIL and APIL policies for perishable inventory systems with positive lead times. Our numerical study identifies instances where the relative optimality gap of both policies can be up to 3.5%. Developing new heuristic policies that can outperform both PIL and APIL policies would be valuable. Finally, it is practically important to develop offline or online data-driven algorithms for managing perishable inventory systems with positive lead times. We have shown that PIL and APIL policies perform consistently close to optimal. The data-driven algorithms may use either policy as a learning benchmark.

14500120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500120.value: Perishable inventory systems with fixed product lifetime and positive lead times are a fundamental class of inventory systems in inventory theory. The optimal policy for these systems is notoriously complex and computationally intractable due to the curse of dimensionality. In this project, we conducted a comprehensive study on a class of projected inventory level (PIL) policies for a general class of perishable inventory systems with positive lead times. Theoretically, among many other results, we proved that this class of policies is asymptotically optimal with large unit penalty costs and with large demand population sizes, under certain conditions. To facilitate computation and enhance scalability, we also developed a class of approximate PIL (APIL) policies and proved that most of our results for the best PIL policy also hold for the best APIL policy. Numerically, we showed that both PIL and APIL policies perform consistently close to optimal. Our research findings not only significantly advance the inventory theory on perishable inventory systems with positive lead times but also provide practitioners with simple and effective policies to manage their perishable products.

14500320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500320.value: Digital media is increasingly replacing print media and, as a result, many local print newspapers have been forced to downsize or close entirely. This is particularly troubling because the local press has historically acted as both an information intermediary and “watchdog” for local economic activity. Furthermore, prior studies find evidence that online substitutes do not appear to fully fill the local information void left by these local print newspapers. Anecdotally, evidence suggests that this is likely because online sources have less incentive to focus resources covering local events because their reader base is not geographically constrained. Thus, both the monitoring and information environment of local firms may suffer even though overall news coverage may not change. Prior research has predominately focused on how information dissemination by the business press influences how capital markets incorporate information into prices. In this study we build on Miller (2006) and other more recent studies to determine how a change in the content (not quantity) of news coverage, specifically a shift away from local coverage, influences capital market participants’ ability to process and incorporate information about local firms. First, we expect to find that analysts ability to make accurate forecasts decreases following a negative shock to the local newspaper environment. Second, we expect to find that market participants are more slow to incorporate earnings news into price. Overall, we expect to find further evidence that the change in information intermediary composition has a measurable effect on how information is used and incorporated in capital markets. In pilot testing, we find that the total level of press coverage does not change following a negative shock to the newspaper industry, but preliminary content analysis suggests that the focus of press coverage shifts from specific local information to more general financial information about the firm. We also find analyst forecast errors are greater and earnings response coefficients are smaller (and drift larger) following a shock to the local newspaper industry and these results are driven by more localized firms and firms that experienced the largest decrease in localized coverage. Finally, we find evidence that the market results, specifically, are driven by firms that experience more retail trading and were more heavily covered by now-defunct local newspapers. Overall, our results suggest that local newspapers play an important role in the information environment of local firms. 數字媒體正在逐步取代印刷媒體，結果之一是，許多地區性的印刷報紙被迫縮減規模甚至完全關閉。特別有問題的是，因為本地媒體過去在本地經濟活動中是信息中介和“看門人”的雙重角色。進一步，先前的研究發現，網絡替代品們看起來並不能完全填補這些本地印刷報紙留下的本地性信息空白。從個例來看，證據顯示這可能是因為其讀者受眾不受地區限制所以網絡媒體覆本地性事件的激勵較低。因此，本地公司的監督和信息環境都受到負面影響，儘管整體的信息覆蓋可能沒有變化。先前研究主要集中在商業媒體的信息傳播對資本市場如何運用信息定價的影響。在本研究中，我們基於米勒（2006）以及其他近期的研究來確定信息覆蓋內容（不是數量）的變化，特別是指失去地區信息覆蓋，如何影響資本市場參與者處理和內化本地公司信息的能力。首先，我們預期發現在本地報紙環境的一個負面衝擊之後，分析師做出準確預測的能力下降。其次，我們預期發現市場參與者把盈利信息內化到價格之中的速度變慢。總體而言，我們預期發現信息中介構成的變化對信息如何在資本市場中被使用和內化有可量度的影響。在引導測試中，我們發現報紙業的一個負面衝擊之後，媒體的總體覆蓋水平並沒有變化，但初步的內容分析顯示，媒體對於公司的本地特定信息的覆蓋轉向了更一般的財務信息。我們還發現在本地報紙業的衝擊之後，分析師的預測差錯變大和盈利反饋係數變小（偏移更大），而這些結果是由更本地化的公司和經歷了最大的本地媒體覆蓋縮減的公司驅動的。最後，我們發現，市場結果，特別是由經受更多散戶交易和曾被現已停業的本地媒體密集覆蓋的公司所驅動。總的來說，我們的結果顯示，本地報紙在本地公司的信息環境中扮演重要角色。

14500620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500620.value: Decision maker's preference in utility and risk plays a crucial role in decision making process. In behavioural economics and risk management, such preferences are often described by choice functions such as utility functions or risk measures. The current research of stochastic programming and robust optimization often assumes that decision maker's choice function is known. In practice, however, such assumption may not be fulfilled either because the problem involves several stakeholders who fail to reach a consensus or because the outcome space of random prospects is too large and/or complex to elicit the true utility /risk preference. To mitigate the risk arising from the ambiguity of such preferences, it may be sensible to base the optimal decision on the worst case utility function/risk measure from a set of plausible utility functions/risk measures elicited with partially available information. This leads mathematically to maximin or minimax preference robust optimization (PRO) models. The research on PRO is still in its infancy with only a few papers mainly focusing on expected utility models and convex risk measures for single-attribute decision making. The principal aim of this project is to advance the current research by developing PRO models for multi-attribute decision making (MADM) because MADM is ubiquitous in practical applications such as healthcare management, network management, airport operations management, finance and supply chain management. A key component of this research is to develop statistical methods which can be effectively used to elicit decision maker's preference. Differing from the existing research, we will consider a situation where the domain of decision maker's utility function is unbounded and his/her preferences may be dependent on the present decision rather than merely empirical data. This will significantly extend the scope of the PRO models. We will also develop robust spectral risk optimization model where decision maker's risk preference is captured by a risk spectrum. At least two approaches will be proposed to construct the ambiguity set of risk spectra including moment-type conditions and Wasserstein balls. Another important component of the research is to develop efficient computational methods for solving the associated maximin/minmax optimization problems and examine robustness of statistical estimators such as the optimal value and optimal solutions obtained from solving the PRO problems with empirical data. This is to ensure that an optimal decision can be obtained from the PRO models efficiently and the decision is resilient against minor perturbation of underlying exogenous uncertainty data in a data-driven environment. 決策者對效用和風險的偏好在決策過程中起著至關重要的作用。在行為經濟學和風險管理中，這種偏好通常由選擇函數來描述，如效用函數或風險度量。目前的隨機規劃和魯棒優化的研究往往假設決策者的選擇函數是已知的。然而，在實踐中，這樣的假設可能無法實現，要麽是因為問題涉及到的幾個利益相關者未能達成共識，要麽是因為隨機前景的結果空間太大和/或太復雜，無法得知真正的效用/風險偏好。為了減輕這種偏好的不確定性所帶來的風險，基於最壞情況下效用函數/風險度量的最優決策可能是明智的，這些效用函數/風險度量是由部分可用信息誘導的。這在數學上導致了極大極小偏好魯棒優化(PRO)模型。 關於PRO的研究仍處於起步階段,只有少數論文將期望效用模型和凸風險度量應用到單屬性決策問題中。這個項目的主要目的是推動PRO模型在多屬性決策(MADM)中的應用。這是因為MADM在醫療管理、網絡管理、機場運營管理、財務和供應鏈管理等領域廣泛存在。本項目的壹個關鍵組成部分是設計誘導決策者偏好的有效的統計方法。與現有的研究不同，我們將考慮決策者效用函數的定義域是無限的，他/她的偏好不僅取決於經驗數據，還可能依賴於當前的決策。這將大大擴展PRO模型的應用範圍。此外，我們也將提出魯棒譜風險優化模型，其中決策者的風險偏好由壹個譜函數來描述，並利用矩條件和Wasserstein球來構建譜函數的不確定集。 本項目的另壹個重要組成部分是設計有效的求解相關極大極小／極小極大優化問題的數值方法，並驗證統計估計量的魯棒性，如基於經驗數據的PRO問題的最優值和最優解。這是為了確保可以有效地從PRO模型中獲得最優決策，並且該決策在數據驅動的環境中對潛在的外生不確定性數據的輕微擾動具有彈性。

14500620.label: Realisation of objectives
14500620.value: Objective 1. Develop non-parametric preference robust optimization models which capture ambiguity of decision maker's utility/risk preference in multi-attribute prospect space. Particular focuses will be given to expected utility maximization models with utility functions having unbounded domain and the ambiguity set being dependent on decision variables. Develop efficient computational methods for solving the resulting maximin optimization problems. The objective 1 is achieved in three steps. Step 1, Develop PRO for single attributed decision-making problems where the DM’s preferences on gains/losses are described by a single univariate utility function. Step 2. Develop PRO for multi-attribute decision-making problems where the DM’s preferences are described by a single multivariate utility function. Step 3. Develop PRO for multi-attribute decision-making problems where the DM’s preferences inconsistent and described by a random multivariate utility function with additive form. In all of the cases, the ambiguity sets are of moment-type structure. The first two are deterministic PRO models (see publications [1,4] in this report) whereas the third is a distributional utility preference robust model, see [5]. Unbounded is considered in online publication chrome-extension://efaidnbmnnnibpcajpcglclefindmkaj/https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/8233.pdf which is an earlier version of [1]. The ambiguity set are decision independent because the decision dependent case will cause intractable reformulations. The decision dependent case is captured in the extended project work on multistage PRO models in the paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04789. Efficient numerical methods are developed via piecewise linear approximation of the utility functions and subsequently tractable formulations of the PRO models as a linear programming problem, or a mixed integer programming problem [1,4] or a cone constrained convex program [5]. Objective 2. Develop robust spectral risk optimization models where there is incomplete information on decision maker's risk preference. Develop statistical methods which may be effectively used to elicit decision maker's risk preference including pairwise comparison approach and Wasserstein ball, and efficient numerical methods for solving the resulting minimax optimization problems. The objective is achieved by developing preference robust distortion risk models in action space. Note that spectral risk measure is a subclass of distortion risk measures. Instead of considering preference robust spectral risk measure, we study preference robust distortion risk measure and its application in optimal decision making. Moreover, by considering the risk measure in action space, it allows the projects to be state-dependent which means the framework of the model is much larger. The ambiguity set is constructed with Kantorovich/Wasserstein ball. Tractable formulations are developed for both preference robust distortion risk measure and associated optimization problems (portfolio optimization), see [3]. In paper [2], PRO is applied to optimized certainty equivalent (OCE) which is widely used in risk measurement. Note that OCE is a convex risk measure, so this is also viewed as PRO model applied to a specific convex risk minimization problem beyond preference robust distortion risk minimization. Objective 3. Carry out qualitative statistical robust analysis for the developed preference robust optimization models by examining stability of the statistical estimators such as the optimal value and the optimal decisions obtained from solving the robust models with empirical data which may contain noise in data-driven environments. To address this objective, we consider application of PRO problems in data-driven problems where data errors/noises arise from exogenous uncertainty and/or in the process of preference elicitation. In both cases, we demonstrate stability of the PRO models in terms of optimal values and worst-case utility function, see [1,4]. Specific theoretical robust analysis is carried out for the preference robust OCE model in [2].
