14500620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500620.value: 1. Developed five important nonparametric PRO models including PRO model with moment-type information structure (see paper [1] in the outputs), preference robust optimized certainty equivalent (OCE) [2], preference robust distortion risk measure [3], bi-variate PRO [4], distributionally utility preference [5]. Four of them are novel and one of them is given a complete treatment. These models cover a range of single attribute and multi-attribute decision-making problems where the decision maker’s preferences are ambiguous, and/or state dependent and random, and provide new paradigms for modelling decision maker’s behavior in practice. 2. Developed efficient computational methods for solving of all of the developed PRO models by reformulating the maximin/minimax optimization problem into linear programs or mixed linear integer programs or convex programs. For instance, in [1], we demonstrate how the ambiguity set of utility functions defined via moment-type conditions may be approximated by a set of piecewise linear utility functions and how the PRO models can be effectively reformulated as an LP or MILP. Moreover, we develop strategies to tackle errors arising from the process and/or the sample data of exogenous uncertainty and optimally design questionnaires for eliciting DM’s preferences. In [5], we propose a novel Bootstrap method to construct the ambiguity set and develop efficient computational schemes for solving the resulting distributionally robust PRO models. Extensive numerical tests show that the proposed models and computational method perform very well. 3. Carried out systemic stability/convergence analysis of the PRO models and computational methods by deriving error bounds on the optimal values and optimal solutions to ensure errors arising from model approximation, preference elicitation, and underlying uncertainty data not propagating significantly. The project has generated five publications at prestigious international journals, four of which are in the top journals of operational research and optimization including Operations Research, Mathematical Programming, SIAM Journal on Optimization and European Journal on Operational Research. These works have significantly advanced the existing research of preference robust optimization. Moreover, the developed PRO models can be readily used by researchers in behavioral economics, engineering and decision analytics. The project works have been disseminated on a number of domestic and international conferences/workshops and department seminars. Recently, the PI has be invited to give a plenary talk at the XVII International Conference on Stochastic Programming which is a major conference on SP to be held in Paris during 28/7-1/8 2025 and his topic will be on PRO..

14500620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500620.value: The project may be extended in three directions. 1. Develop multistage PRO models. The PI has already written a joint paper with Jia Liu and Zhiping Chen (Xi'an Jiaotong University). The paper is submitted to Mathematical Programming and under second revision. In 2024, the PI presented a talk on PRO and multistage PRO at the 25th International Conference on Mathematical Programming in Montreal 2024 attended by a number of leading experts. The PI plans to do further research in this direction on Markov decision-making process to reduce computational complexity and Robo-advisor system which can dynamically learn user's preferences, and then recommend personalized investment portfolios based on the elicited preferences. 2. Develop effective methods to elicit a decision maker's preferences using the well-known polyhedral cut method, this is to be carried out in a new GRC funded project 14204624. 3. Develop a PRO model without necessarily constructing an ambiguity set because in some cases eliciting information of a decision maker could be expensive if not possible. The PI is exploring this in collaboration with William Haskell at Purdue University.

14500620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500620.value: Utility preference refers to a decision maker's preference to gains/losses when the DM makes a decision before realization of uncertainty. In practice, information about a DM's true utility function which characterizes the DM’s preference is often incomplete. This raises a question as to how to develop an appropriate mathematical model for the decision-making problem and find an optimal decision which mitigates the modelling risk with incomplete preference information. This project gives a comprehensive study of the so-called preference robust optimization ranging from modelling to computational methods and underlying theory. The developed models include the case that preference information is obtained via moment-type information structure and ball structure and extend to the case that DM's preferences are potentially inconsistent or display some randomness. Various computational methods have been proposed for solving the resulting minimax/maximin problems particularly for the one associated with piecewise linear approximation. Error bounds have been established to ensure the model errors and data errors propagate in controlled manner. Extensive numerical tests show the models and computational schemes perform very well. The outcomes of the project can be readily used by researchers and practitioners in behavioral economics, engineering and operational research.

14501120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501120.value: This proposal aims to study the effects of increased trading frictions in the stock market on the options market. On the one hand, the options market and underlying stock markets are connected by the option market makers’ hedging activity (initial hedging and hedge rebalancing). On the other hand, these two markets are integrated by (informed) investors’ strategic use of options as an alternative instrument to obtain leveraged exposure on the underlying stock and as a vehicle to trade volatility.Although there has been research into the options market’s liquidity, trading activities and price discovery roles, it is difficult to find causal evidence for this. We therefore propose to carry out an investigation, using well-tested techniques to discover (1) how the options market quality changes, (2) how informed investors strategically adjust their option trading activities and (3) how the options market makers respond. All three aspects are equilibrium outcomes of interactions of options market makers and investors. We will study the mechanism from the aspects of the changes in options trading volume, the dynamics of liquidity provision by option market makers and the informativeness of options trading activity. The Tick-Size Pilot Program conducted by SEC commenced on October 3, 2016, with a two-year experiment period. The experiment increases the tick size from 1-cent to 5-cent for a list of randomly chosen 1,200 stocks and provides a control group of an equal number of stocks as part of the random assignment. The SEC Tick-Size Pilot Program provides an ideal setting to study the causal impact. A forthcoming study has documented that a significant stock price decline has resulted from an increase in the stock tick size. This project will contribute to the literature on the determinants of options market quality and options trading activity, and will enhance the understanding of the functioning of the options market. 14501120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501120.value: This research investigates the impact of the NASDAQ closing auction, introduced in 2004, on stock price efficiency and corporate decision-making. The auction replaced the method where the day's final price was determined by the last trade in the continuous market. By focusing on the auction's role in price setting, this study offers insights into how trading mechanisms influence market efficiency and corporate behavior. Key Findings: Enhanced Price Informativeness: The NASDAQ closing auction significantly improves the informational content of closing prices. Using a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, it finds that auction-determined prices capture market-wide and macroeconomic information better and reduce noise. This is evidenced by a stronger correlation between current stock returns and future earnings. Reduction in Price Noise: There is a significant reduction in price noise post-implementation of the closing auction, indicating a more accurate reflection of fundamental values in stock prices. Faster Information Incorporation: The auction mechanism accelerates the incorporation of market-wide information into stock prices, enhancing the efficiency of the price discovery process. Impact on Corporate Investment Decisions: Firms included in the closing auction show a significant increase in investment-to-price sensitivity, suggesting that managers make better investment decisions based on more accurate stock prices. Improved Firm Performance: Firms demonstrate improved performance metrics, such as return on assets (ROA), due to better-informed managerial decisions stemming from more accurate stock prices. Significance for Firms with High Macroeconomic Exposure: The benefits of the closing auction are more pronounced for firms with high macroeconomic exposure, as the auction better integrates market-wide and macroeconomic information. Research Outcomes: The findings highlight the critical role of trading mechanism design in enhancing market efficiency and corporate decision-making. By improving price accuracy and informativeness, the NASDAQ closing auction supports the adoption of well-designed trading mechanisms in financial markets. This research contributes to literature on market microstructure and the real effects of financial markets, showing that trading process design significantly influences managerial learning and corporate investment decisions. In conclusion, the NASDAQ closing auction enhances price discovery and corporate decision-making. The importance of this research is recognized by its acceptance for presentation at the FMA-Asia conferences and its ongoing submission to additional major conferences and top academic journals. This recognition underscores the relevance and potential impact of the findings on both academic and practical applications in financial market design.

14501120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501120.value: The potential for further development of this research lies in expanding our understanding of how trading mechanisms influence corporate decisions and real economic outcomes. Future studies could explore the broader implications of different trading structures, such as continuous versus periodic trading, on firm behavior and market efficiency. For instance, investigating how changes in trading mechanisms impact the strategic decisions of firms in various industries could provide deeper insights into the feedback loop between market prices and corporate investment. Additionally, examining the role of different auction designs in enhancing or impeding price discovery could inform regulatory policies aimed at improving market efficiency. A proposed course of action includes conducting cross-market comparisons to identify best practices in auction design and their effects on price informativeness. Further, incorporating real-world case studies and longitudinal data analyses could reveal the long-term impacts of trading mechanism changes on firm performance and economic productivity. By leveraging advanced econometric techniques and machine learning models, researchers can better isolate the causal effects of trading mechanisms on corporate decisions, thereby contributing valuable knowledge to both financial economics and market microstructure literature.

14501120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501120.value: This research project explores how the way stock prices are determined at the end of the trading day—specifically through a process called the NASDAQ closing auction—affects the accuracy and usefulness of these prices. The closing auction was introduced in 2004 to replace the old method where the day's final price was based on the last trade. This change is significant because it helps ensure that the closing price reflects all available information, making it more reliable. The research shows that this new auction method improves how well stock prices capture overall market trends and economic conditions, while reducing random price fluctuations. This is valuable because more accurate stock prices help company managers make better investment decisions, leading to more efficient use of resources and improved company performance. Understanding these effects is crucial for financial regulators and market designers who aim to create fair and efficient markets. By demonstrating that the NASDAQ closing auction enhances price accuracy and informs better corporate decisions, this study highlights the importance of well-designed trading mechanisms in supporting the broader economy. Better ways of setting stock prices at the end of the day lead to smarter business decisions and a healthier economy.

14501220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501220.value: Monetary policy refers to the most critical set of instruments that governments frequently use to counterbalance economic downturns, unemployment, and inflation. Among economists in both academia and central banks, the New Keynesian (NK) framework is the most powerful tool for the understanding of mechanisms of monetary policy. NK models emphasize that price movements are sluggish and thus central banks can adjust real interest rates in economies by twisting nominal rates, which in turn influences aggregate consumption, saving, and investments. In early NK models, aggregation consumption and saving are characterized by the optimal choice of a representative household with the average income level. As high-performance computing becomes accessible and detailed household-level data become available, macroeconomists start working on complicated models that match household-level evidence. Naturally, Heterogeneous-Agent NK (HANK) models were proposed recently. HANK models successfully captures the cross-sectional feature of households' marginal propensity to consume, which representative-agent models can barely. Moreover, HANK models uncover and quantify the indirect channel of monetary policy that representative-agent models missed. The success of HANK models is attributed to their recognition that households in reality hold both liquid assets like deposits and illiquid assets like houses and equities. By matching the stylized fact that a significant number of households hold minimum liquid wealth, the HANK framework obtains the result that these households are sensitive to transitory income shocks on which monetary policy can influence. Nevertheless, the banking sector is missing in current HANK models. My project intends to fill in this gap in the literature. By incorporating banks into the HANK model, I can apply the framework to analyze monetary policies in China because the banking sector plays the most critical role in Chinese economy. In particular, I will first process household-level data from China Household Finance Survey and estimate the income and wealth distribution of households. In addition, my project will explore the fact that a significant proportion of bank deposits are in fact firms' savings. By modeling firms' cash holding decisions, I would like to quantify the impacts of monetary shocks on firms' investment via their bank deposits or other forms of short-term savings. Lastly, the project also intends to have banks enjoy certain market power in the HANK framework. This modeling choice is not just more realistic but also could capture the key transmission channel that banks only partially adjust their deposit rates in the presence of monetary policy shocks. 貨幣政策爲政府慣常使用於對抗經濟下行，失業及通貨膨脹之重要工具。於學界及央行從業之經濟學家中，新凱恩斯框架爲理解貨幣政策機制之重要理論工具。新凱恩斯模型強調價格調整之粘性。因此中央銀行可藉助名義利率的調整影響實際利率之變化，進而作用於總量消費，儲蓄及投資。 在早期新凱恩斯模型中，總量消費及儲蓄取決於持有平均收入代表性家戶的最優選擇。近來隨着高性能計算之普及和詳盡微觀家戶數據的出現，宏觀經濟學家開始研究切合微觀家戶證據之更爲複雜的宏觀模型。順理成章的，學者們近期提出了異質性新凱恩斯模型。相比於傳統的同質性模型，異質新凱恩斯模型勝於捕獲數據中家戶邊際消費傾向的截面性質。更爲重要的是，異質新凱恩斯模型相比於同質性模型可以揭示並量化貨幣政策之間接傳導機制。 異質新凱恩斯模型的成功来自于其強調現實中的家戶同時持有如銀行存款之類的流動性資產及如房產或股票之類的非流動性資產。由于其契合了相當一部分家戶持有極少之流動性資產這一現實，異質新凱恩斯模型發現家戶對由貨幣政策引起的暫時性收入波動頗爲敏感。然而，現有的異質新凱恩斯模型尚未包括銀行部門。此研究計劃旨在填補文獻中的這一空白。 考慮到銀行部門在中國經濟中至關重要的角色，將銀行引入異質新凱恩斯模型可以更貼切的研究貨幣政策之於中國經濟中的作用。具體來說，我首先處理中國家戶金融調查數據並估計中國家戶的收入及財富分佈。並且，本計劃亦會探究相當量的銀行存款實爲企業儲蓄這一現實。通過對企業現金持有決策的建模，模型可以量化貨幣政策通過其對企業銀行存款或其他短期儲蓄的作用進而產生的對企業投資的影響。最後，此研究計劃亦會在異質新凱恩斯模型中探究銀行的市場勢力。此建模要素不僅更貼近現實而且可以使得模型囊括銀行僅部分調整存款利率這一實事對貨幣政策傳導機制之影響。

14501220.label: Realisation of objectives
14501220.value: 1. to construct a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model with a banking sector. The construction of a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) model with a banking sector represents a crucial advancement in economic modeling. By incorporating a banking sector into the traditional NK framework, the model captures the intricate dynamics between financial intermediaries, households, and monetary policy. This integration allows for a more accurate representation of the economy's liquidity transformation process, shedding light on how banks influence the transmission of monetary shocks. The model's design enables a granular analysis of households' wealth distribution, asset allocations, and consumption choices, considering the impact of varying levels of liquid assets on their responses to monetary policy. Additionally, by including a banking sector in the HANK framework, the model can simulate how changes in interest rates affect not only individual households but also firms through their cash holding decisions and investment behaviors. 2. to use the China Household Finance Survey to estimate the distribution of households' balance sheets in China. Analyzing the distribution of Chinese households' balance sheets using data from the China Household Finance Survey offers valuable insights into the country's economic landscape. By delving into the wealth and asset holdings of Chinese households, this research endeavors to unveil patterns of wealth accumulation, financial behaviors, and inequality within the population. By leveraging the detailed information provided by the survey data, researchers can construct a comprehensive picture of how households in China allocate their resources between liquid and illiquid assets, such as deposits, houses, equities, and other forms of wealth. Understanding these wealth distributions can enhance our grasp of the economic well-being of different segments of society, inform policy decisions aimed at reducing wealth disparities, and provide a foundation for studying the effects of monetary policies on households with varying levels of wealth. 3. to calibrate the heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model with a banking sector according to China Household Finance Survey data and to use the model to address monetary policy issues in China. Calibrating the heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) model with a banking sector using data from the China Household Finance Survey sets the stage for a detailed examination of monetary policy implications in China. Through the calibration process, researchers can fine-tune the model to align with the specific economic conditions and household characteristics of China, thereby enabling more accurate simulations and analysis. By incorporating parameters based on real-world data, such as income and wealth distribution patterns, the model can provide insights into how monetary policy measures impact households and the broader economy in China. This calibration process not only facilitates a more nuanced understanding of the transmission channels of monetary policy but also allows for scenario analyses and policy evaluations tailored to the unique Chinese economic landscape. Ultimately, this calibration and analysis offer a pathway to enhancing the effectiveness and precision of monetary policy decisions in China, with implications for economic stability, growth, and inequality mitigation. 4. to construct and quantify a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model in which an explicit banking sector enjoys market power. Extending the model to incorporate banks enjoying market power introduces a critical dimension to the analysis of monetary policy in the Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian (HANK) framework. By allowing banks to have market power, the model captures the strategic behavior and influence of financial intermediaries in the economy. This extension enables a more realistic depiction of how banks adjust their deposit rates in response to monetary policy shocks, showcasing the nuanced relationship between banks, households, and the central bank. By considering the effects of market power on banks' decisions regarding interest rates and liquidity provision, the model can reveal the impact of these strategic behaviors on the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission mechanisms. Understanding how market power influences the behavior of banks within the HANK framework provides valuable insights into the complexities of the financial sector and its role in shaping the broader economic landscape. 5. to construct and quantify a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model that features an explicit banking sector and firms' cash holding decisions. Extending the baseline model to include both a banking sector and a firm sector that holds cash introduces a layer of complexity that mirrors real-world economic interactions more closely. By incorporating the financial activities of firms, such as their cash holding decisions, the model can simulate how firms' liquidity management strategies impact their investment decisions in response to monetary policy changes. This extension enables a more comprehensive analysis of the interplay between monetary policy, banks, and non-financial firms, highlighting how shifts in interest rates influence firms' cash management practices and investment behavior. By exploring the dynamic interactions between the banking sector, firms, and monetary policy, this extended model provides a richer understanding of the transmission channels through which monetary shocks affect investment dynamics and overall economic stability.

14501220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501220.value: The integration of a banking sector into the Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian (HANK) model has yielded significant findings and research outcomes that enrich our understanding of monetary policy transmission and economic dynamics. By constructing a model that incorporates both households' heterogeneous asset holdings and the strategic decisions of banks, researchers have uncovered nuanced insights into how monetary policy impacts various sectors of the economy. Through the calibration of the model using data from the China Household Finance Survey, researchers have been able to simulate the distribution of wealth among Chinese households, providing a detailed view of how different segments of society allocate their assets and respond to economic stimuli. This calibration process, tailored to the specific characteristics of the Chinese economy, has enabled the evaluation of monetary policy measures in China with a focus on enhancing the precision and efficacy of policy decisions. One of the major findings of this research lies in the examination of the transmission channels of monetary policy with the inclusion of a banking sector enjoying market power. By modeling banks as strategic players with the ability to influence interest rates and liquidity provision, the research has highlighted how market power impacts the effectiveness of monetary policy tools. This analysis showcases the importance of considering the strategic behavior of financial intermediaries in the broader context of monetary policy implementation. Furthermore, extending the model to include a firm sector that holds cash has shed light on how firms' liquidity management practices influence their investment decisions in response to monetary shocks. This extension has provided valuable insights into the interactions between banks, firms, and monetary policy, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how monetary policy changes affect investment dynamics in the real economy. Overall, the research outcomes underscore the intricate relationships between different economic agents and policy tools, emphasizing the need for comprehensive models that capture the complexities of modern economies. The findings not only contribute to academic literature by deepening our understanding of monetary policy transmission mechanisms but also have practical implications for policymakers seeking to design more effective and targeted policy interventions. By exploring the impact of market power, wealth distribution, and firm behavior within the HANK framework, this research sets the stage for enhanced policy decision-making that considers the diverse dynamics at play in the financial and real sectors of the economy.

14501220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501220.value: The research on integrating a banking sector and modeling firm cash holdings within the Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian (HANK) framework shows promising avenues for further development. Moving forward, the research could explore more detailed interactions between banks, households, and firms to better understand the dynamics of monetary policy transmission. This could involve refining the model to capture additional aspects of banking behavior, such as credit creation and lending practices, as well as incorporating more nuanced features of firm financing and investment decisions. Additionally, expanding the analysis to incorporate macroprudential policies and exogenous shocks could enhance the model's ability to simulate a wider range of economic scenarios. By deepening the complexity and realism of the model, researchers can gain deeper insights into the mechanisms driving economic outcomes and policy effectiveness, paving the way for more robust analyses and informed policy recommendations.

14501220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501220.value: The research project focuses on studying how changes in monetary policy affect the economy, particularly in China. By using a detailed economic model that includes households, banks, and firms, researchers aim to understand how different groups in the economy respond to decisions made by the government about interest rates and money. By looking at real data from Chinese households and businesses, the project aims to create a more accurate picture of how people manage their money and make financial decisions. The project also explores how banks and companies influence the effects of monetary policy on the economy. Ultimately, the research aims to provide insights that can help policymakers make better decisions about the economy and improve overall economic stability and growth in China.

14501320.label: Project Objectives
14501320.value: Collect, assemble, and clean online restaurant review data from Dianping, reviewers’ travel distances data from Google Maps’ API, and possibly lab experiment data for robustness checks. Theoretically propose the tourist bias and offer an empirical identification using online restaurant review data collected from Dianping. To make causal arguments, our research design will leverage a between-group difference in restaurants and a within-group difference in reviewers, and adopts the entropy balancing method to overcome shortcomings of the Propensity Score Matching (PSM) method. Empirically identify mechanism underlying the tourist bias in online ratings by conducting city-, restaurant-, and reviewer-level analyses. Specifically, we will compare and review ratings between pairs of travel destinations in city-level, and contrast ratings given by tourists and locals for restaurants specialized in local cuisines of a given city in restaurant level. Furthermore, we conduct an analysis on reviewer-level by controlling reviewers’ fixed effects. Study how traveling impact other online review contents such as review length, review content richness, and the number of affective words used in reviews by multiple regression analyses. Empirically investigate what determines travelers’ online rating/review generation behavior by conducting a series of additional analyses. Particularly, travelers’ review behavior is reflected by review characteristics, which are measured by review rating, review length, review richness, and review affective words. Offer managerial implications. Our results will demonstrate the necessity of differentiating travelers’ and locals’ ratings/reviews. Our insights will offer important implications for product and service providers, online review platforms, and consumers.

14501320.value: 過去十年間，Web 2.0和社交媒體的爆炸性增長爲電子口碑傳播提供了肥沃的土壤。在線評級和評論，即在零售商或第三方網站上發布的同行對産品或服務的評價，已經成爲用戶生成內容的一種突出形式，減少了消費的不確定性。 網上評級有用性的一個重要假設是，評級估值可以作爲産品或服務質量的代理。但不同背景的個體對同一産品或服務的質量認知可能不同。然而，之前的研究通常會對在線評級一視同仁，即使産生這些評級的個體來自非常不同的背景。 本項目將研究遊客在産生在線評價時與當地人有何不同，並探索遊客偏見的可能機制。我們還將研究以下額外的研究問題。(1) 不同的餐廳人氣和價格，效果如何變化？(2)在線評分中本地與遊客差異的潛在機制是什麽？(3)在其他在線評論特征上，如評論長度、評論內容的豐富性、評論中使用的情感詞數量等，是否存在遊客偏向；(4)是什麽決定了旅行者的在線評分/評論生成行爲？ 爲了回答這些問題，我們將基于從中國最受歡迎的餐飲點評網站點評網收集的在線餐飲點評數據進行一系列實證分析。具體而言，我們將首先通過有序的logit回歸建立本地與遊客差異效應的因果關系。在確定了遊客偏差之後，我們將運用多元回歸來檢驗餐廳的受歡迎程度和價格是否會影響這一效應，然後通過進行一系列城市、餐廳和個人層面的分析來檢驗這一偏差的潛在機制。 PI和Co-I已經在相關課題上進行了合作，並成功地撰寫了關于在線餐廳評級中遊客偏差的工作論文，這些論文將在即將召開的幾個會議上發表。我們期望我們提出的研究將通過證明區分本地和遊客評論的必要性，對學術文獻和管理實踐産生重大貢獻。

14501320.label: Realisation of objectives
14501320.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved and resulted in a publication in a top-tier journal. Objective 1: We successfully collected and assembled a comprehensive dataset of 451,314 restaurant reviews from Dianping.com, covering 10 major cities across China. Geographic coordinates were obtained using Google Maps API, and linguistic features were extracted using TextMind system for Chinese language psychological analysis. Objective 2: We empirically established the existence of tourist bias in online ratings. Using an ordered logit regression model and entropy balancing methods, we found that tourists give ratings that are 0.050 stars higher than locals (p < 0.01), representing a meaningful bias that persists after controlling for restaurant and reviewer characteristics. Objective 3: Through multi-level analyses, we identified that the tourist bias is driven by individual mood differences during travel rather than destination effects or restaurant taste: · City-level analysis: 73.33% of travel pairs showed no statistical difference in ratings, indicating destination effects do not drive the bias · Restaurant-level analysis: Local cuisine restaurants did not receive systematically higher ratings from tourists · Reviewer-level analysis: Within-person analysis confirmed the bias persists when controlling for reviewer fixed effects Objective 4: Text analysis revealed tourists write 12.3% longer reviews, are 61% more likely to include pictures, and use 4.7% more affective words compared to locals. These differences reflect tourists' enhanced emotional state during travel. Objective 5: We identified that travel distance positively affects ratings (b=0.040, p<0.01) while travel experience negatively affects ratings (b=-0.026, p<0.05). Restaurant price moderates these relationships, with stronger effects for expensive restaurants. Objective 6: Our findings have significant implications for review platforms, suggesting implementation of tourist/local labels to improve information quality and consumer decision-making.

14501320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501320.value: Our research successfully documented and explained the tourist bias phenomenon in electronic word-of-mouth. The key findings include: 1. Tourist Bias Confirmation: Tourists systematically rate restaurants higher than locals by 0.050 stars on a 5-star scale. This bias is robust across different model specifications and persists after entropy balancing to address selection concerns. 2. Mechanism Identification: The bias stems from tourists' elevated mood state during travel rather than destination effects or authentic taste preferences. This was confirmed through: o City-pair comparisons showing no systematic destination bias o Restaurant-level analysis showing local cuisine does not receive preferentially higher ratings from tourists o Within-reviewer analysis confirming the effect persists when controlling for individual heterogeneity 3. Review Content Differences: Beyond ratings, tourists generate qualitatively different content - longer reviews with more pictures and emotional language, reflecting their enhanced experiential state. 4. Heterogeneous Effects: The bias varies by restaurant price (stronger for expensive restaurants) and is influenced by travel distance (positive) and travel experience (negative). 5. Publication Achievement: The research resulted in a forthcoming publication in Information Systems Research, a premier journal in the field.

14501320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501320.value: This research opens several promising avenues: 1. Cross-platform Extension: Examine tourist bias in other service contexts (hotels, attractions) and across different cultural settings. 2. Design Interventions: Develop and test interface designs that help consumers appropriately weight tourist versus local reviews based on their own status. 3. Dynamic Analysis: Investigate how the bias evolves over time and whether it differs for repeat versus first-time visitors. We are currently collaborating with review platforms to implement A/B tests of tourist/local labeling systems and measure their impact on consumer decision quality.

14501320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501320.value: When people travel, they tend to rate restaurants more generously than locals do. Our research analyzed over 450,000 restaurant reviews in China and found that tourists consistently give ratings about 1% higher than locals. This "tourist bias" occurs because travelers are typically in better moods during trips, making them more positive about their dining experiences. This finding matters because millions of people rely on online ratings to choose restaurants. Currently, review websites mix tourist and local ratings together, potentially misleading consumers. Our research suggests that platforms should label reviews as coming from tourists or locals, allowing users to see ratings from people in similar situations. This simple change could help both travelers find restaurants that other travelers enjoyed and locals find places that meet local standards, ultimately improving dining decisions for everyone.

14501720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501720.value: This study investigates how the information embedded in the index option market help explain the return variation and yield spreads in the corporate bond market. We construct a “pseudo-bond” universe using index put options and zero-coupon treasury bonds. The pseudo-bond (index option) market is more liquid and subject to much less frictions than real corporate bond. The long-short return spread of the pseudo-bond and its time variation may indicate the known or even unknown risk premia for the real corporate bond market, such as default premium, term premium, and liquidity premium. The size of the corporate bond market is non-trivial. The outstanding amount of corporate bond issued by non-financial U.S. corporations is $6.2 trillion per 2018. Corporate bonds also play an increasingly important role in institutional investors’ portfolios. While there are numerous studies on the cross-section of stock returns and on common factors in stocks explaining these patterns, similar literature on corporate bonds is relatively scarce. Given the increasing flow of funds to bond funds, it is important to assess the “risk-adjusted” performance of these bond funds and, hence, develop bond factor models. Extant bond factor models use either stock market factors or construct factors from aggregate variables such as default spread and term spread. However, the empirical performance of these factors is rather limited. Therefore, Bai, Bali, and Wen (2019a) propose a bond factor model using real corporate bond data to improve model pricing abilities. Nevertheless, the notion of disentangling economic sources of risk from purely microstructure idiosyncrasies remains. Culp, Nozawa, and Veronesi (2018, CNV henceforth) argue that corporate bonds are complicated and illiquid securities and that leverage is endogenous. Therefore, purely empirical methods that rely only on the cross-section of real bond returns embed sources of risk other than purely credit risk. CNV advocate the use of pseudo-bonds. These bonds are constructed as long positions in risk-free asset and short position in put options. These pseudo-bonds can be regarded as bonds on fictitious companies. These pseudo-bonds can be matched to real-life bonds with similarity in yields. By using liquid options, one mitigates liquidity considerations in real corporate bonds. Therefore, we extract risk factors from pseudo-bonds, which are liquid and frictionless. These pseudo-bond factors have the potential of explaining the cross-section of real bonds better than real-bond factors. We explore the cross-sectional pricing implications of these pseudo-bond factors and their relation to real-bond factors. 本研究探討了指數期權市場所含的信息如何有助于解釋公司債券市場的收益變動和收益率價差。我們使用指數看跌期權和零息國債構建一种“僞債券（pseudo-bond）”。這種僞債券（指數期權）市場相比於真實公司債券流動性更強，摩擦更少。這種僞債券的多空收益價差和它的時間變化能預示真實公司債券市場已知甚至未知的風險溢價，如違約溢價，期限溢價和流動性溢價。 公司債券市場的規模是不容小覷的。2018年，美國非金融公司發行的公司債券債務總額為6.2萬億美元。公司債券在機構投資者的投資組合中也扮演著越來越重要的角色。儘管有大量關於股票收益率橫截面和股票中解释这些模式的共同因素的研究，關於公司債券的類似文獻相對很少。鑒於越來越多的資金流向債券基金，評估這些債券基金“風險調整後的”表現並因此建立債權因子模型變得十分重要。 現有的債權因子模型有的使用股票市場因子，有的使用綜合變量構建因子，例如違約價差和期限價差。然而，這些因子的實證表現是相當有限的。因此，Bai、Bali和Wen （2019a）提出了一個使用真實公司債券數據的債券因子模型，以此來提升模型定價能力。然而，將風險經濟來源從純粹的微觀結構特性分離出來的概念仍然存在。Culp、Nozawa和Veronesi（2018年，此後稱為CNV）認為公司債券是一種複雜且缺乏流動性的債券，並且它的槓桿具備內生性。因此，基於真實債券收益率的實證方法除了包含信用風險外，還嵌入了風險來源。 CNV建議使用僞債券。這些債券被構建為無風險資產的多頭和看跌期權的空頭。這些僞債券可以視為虛擬公司的債券。在收益率相似性方面，這些僞債券可以跟真實債券相匹配。通過使用流動性期權，這可以減輕真實公司債券的流動性對價。 因此，我們從具備流動性和無摩擦的僞債券中抽取風險因子。相比於真實債券因子，這些僞債券因子更能解釋真實債券的橫截面。我們探討了這些僞債券因子的橫截面定價影響和他們與真實債券因子的關係。

14501720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501720.value: Cao, Goyal, Xiao, and Zhan (2023) document that corporate bonds with large increases in implied volatility over the past month underperform those with large decreases in implied volatility by 0.6% per month. Different from the predictability in the stock market, it is the common component rather than the difference in implied volatility changes of call and put options that drive the predictability in the corporate bond market. These results are consistent with the argument that informed traders with new information about firm risk prefer to trade in the option market and that the corporate bond market under-reacts to this information. Cao, Goyal, Ke, and Zhan (2024) document the causal effects of single-name options trading on the absolute level of information content of prices (stock price informativeness). Consistent with the strategic complementarity theory in Goldstein and Yang (2015), the PI and coauthors find options trading enhances information production and acquisition and confirms that options are more important sources. Consistent results using global data are presented in the paper as well. In Cao, Hertzel, Xu, and Zhan (2025), the PI and coauthors explore whether the options market could influence corporate financing decisions. They find options trading activity can affect firm debt structure decisions by stimulating informed trading that improves the informational environment in which firms raise debt capital. At both the extensive and intensive margin, firms with actively traded options are able to shift from bank to public debt financing. The shift from bank financing reflects reduced demand for the special role that banks play in ex-ante information collection and ex-post monitoring for firms with greater information asymmetry.

14501720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501720.value: (maximum 200 words) 1. We plan to extend our study to other derivatives. Important derivatives of a firm include options and CDS. Firms might also use interest rate swaps and currency swaps to hedge certain risks. This could be particularly important when geopolitical risks become pronounced for Multinational Corporations (MNCs). Our empirical framework could be applied to extract information that is particularly important for a certain derivative. Moreover, by aggregating firm-level information, we could study the pricing of market or industry derivatives. 2. We plan to study the feedback effects in the corporate debt market. It is unknown whether managers learn from the debt market. The corporate bond market is known for the concentration of institutional investors. On the one hand, the trading of these institutions may contain important private information. On the other hand, institutions like insurance companies are highly regulated. Thus, whether managers learn from the corporate debt market is an underexplored question.

14501720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501720.value: Options are important derivatives of a firm’s stock because the options market is often the first place for investors with information to trade. Therefore, the options market plays a non-negligible role in information production and transmission. Previous literature largely focuses on whether the information in the options market could predict future stock returns and ignores the potential link between options and corporate bonds, which help firms obtain financing on a large scale. The series of studies attempts to fill the void and help investors, regulators, and researchers in understanding how the derivatives market could be useful for corporate bond investment and corporate financing decisions. The findings demonstrate that options stimulate information acquisition and production. By exploring the impact of the options market on corporate debt financing decisions, we discover that options reduce information asymmetry in the corporate bond market. The information contained in options can be utilized to forecast future returns of corporate bonds. Notably, this predictability is influenced by shifts in default risks rather than changes in cash flow news, highlighting a contrast with the stock market. Overall, these studies uncover the connection between options and corporate bonds and explain the underlying reasons for this relationship.

14501920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501920.value: Many businesses use a variety of asset protection strategies, strategies aiming at protecting both tangible and intangible assets against business liabilities. Those effective can deter claimants ex ante and prevent losing assets ex post after a judgement. It is common to use entities such as corporations and LLCs to hold assets, while run different risky business activities under separate entities that act like ``silos.'' Courts usually respect their deliberate use of legal structures to avoid incurring in liabilities so long as they are set up properly well before liabilities occur. Understanding asset protection helps us understand the legal structure of a firm and the ways businesses are conducted in real world. These legal structures cannot be explained by the typical theories of the firm in economics that focus on the scope of control because under a fix scope of control, a firm can legally structure itself in a number of ways. Legal scholars have written about how businesses organize their legal structure but some key economic questions remain unanswered. Economists on the other hand do not pay much attention on the legal structure of a business. Our premise is that legal structure creates real economic values in some situations. However, an elaborated legal structure neither eliminates risk nor comes without costs. Under what conditions a business would prefer an elaborated legal structure? What benefits and costs such a legal structure bring to the business? If risk does not get eliminated, how would doing so shift the risk across parties? How would legal structure affect firms' capitalization and financing decision? What sorts of incentive problems a more elaborated legal structure create? How would a business's legal structure affect its relations with its potential customers? Our proposal first highlights some stylized facts to show that many businesses are organized under elaborated legal structures. We suspect beyond getting around some legal hurdles, organizing businesses in a particular legal structure brings real economic values. We propose a model to view the issue, which admittedly, needs to be further developed to address the more ambitious questions we seek to investigate. We describe the investigative, empirical, and theoretical approaches we will take to address our research questions. We aim at comparing our theoretical results with those written in the literature. 企業用各種資產保護策略，令其因法律責任而失去有形及無形資產的風險盡量減少。有效的資產保護策略可以阻止債權人的索償，並減低裁判後資產的損失。做法通常包括使用法人團體或有限公司等法人來持有資產，同時盡量分開不同業務的法律結構。 如在負債發生之前企業已經適當地設置的法律結構，法庭一般會尊重企業以此來面對生意可能帶來的負債。了解資產保護有助我們了解公司的法律結構以及其開展業務的方式。經濟學中關注控制範圍的理論無法解釋這些法律結構，因為在固定的控制範圍內，公司可以用不同法律結構組成。 有關企業如何組織其法律結構，有法律學者著文論述，但一些關鍵的經濟學問題仍未得到解答。經濟學家對企業的法律結構沒有太多關注。我們的前提是法律結構在某些情況下會為企業創造實質的經濟價值。但是，精心設計的企業法律結構既不能消除風險，也不會沒有成本。在什麼情況下，企業希望採用複雜的法律結構？複雜的法律結構給企業帶來什麼好處和壞處？如果無法消除風險，該如何在各方之間轉移風險？法律結構如何影響企業的資本和融資決策？複雜的法律結構會產生不良誘因嗎？企業的法律結構如何影響其與潛在客戶建立關係？ 我們的計畫將找尋一些事例，以説明用複雜的法律結構組織企業是否普遍。我們將探討，除了繞過某些法律障礙以外，用法律結構組織業務還會為企業帶來實質的經濟價值。我們已經建立了一個簡單的模型來研究這些問題，但模型過於簡單，要研究如何在其之上加建，以解決我們試圖探討的種種問題。這計畫書描述我們將研究的調查，方向與理論方法，我們期望將得出的理論與文獻中的理論作出比較。

14501920.label: Realisation of objectives
14501920.value: Objective 1: To clarify our terminology, we refer to ``asset protection'' business strategies that shield assets from potential legal liabilities as ``judgment proofing.'' These terms are interchangeable. We have thoroughly reviewed the strategies that legal scholars associate with businesses becoming judgment-proof. Typically, this involves creating a separate legal entity, such as a limited liability subsidiary, to undertake risky activities that could harm others. Contractual parties take into account these judgment-proofing strategies, compelling businesses to internalize their externalities. This aligns with the Coase Theorem, which suggests that no benefits can be gained from judgment proofing in contractual relationships. This mechanism does not apply to non-contractual parties, who never choose to engage with the business. If a business attempts to judgment-proof itself by externalizing risk to these parties, it incurs no cost for doing so. This raises a theoretical question identified by Easterbrook and Fischel (1985) and Posner (1975), and mathematically formalized by Shavell (1986). Our analysis focuses on the distinction between judgment-proofing concerning contractual versus non-contractual parties, enhancing our understanding of how businesses protect their assets. Objective 2: We survey the literature to identify existing rigorous studies. A key finding is that LoPucki (1998) has comprehensively documented various ways businesses legally structure their organizations to limit liabilities. Our focus on using a parent-subsidiary structure to limit liabilities is just one of six major strategies identified by LoPucki (1998). The other five strategies include: i) Lessor-lessee: a large oil company leasing its gas stations to lessees; ii) Secured lender-borrower: an entity created by the business or others conducts risky activities using secured loans from the business, which enjoys priority over the operating entity's involuntary creditors; iii) Buyer-seller: outsourcing risky activities to other entities, such as a large oil company outsourcing oil shipping to a smaller independent firm; iv) Franchisor-franchisee: similar to the lessor-lessee model; and v) Licensor-licensee: when a risky activity requires intellectual property owned by the business, it licenses that IP to a standalone entity to conduct those activities. Objective 3: Through our literature review, we found that Thompson (1991, 1998) and Matheson (2009, 2010) have surveyed many cases that ultimately went to court. Their datasets are non-random but representative; if precedents indicate how courts assess businesses' litigation risks by awarding or denying damages to voluntary and involuntary creditors, we can expect that cases settled outside of court that are impossible to document empirically will follow similar legal logic. Briefly, the four studies reveal that courts seldom hold corporate parents liable for subsidiaries' voluntary and involuntary creditors. When they do, it usually relates to the alter ego doctrine, where the formalities necessary to separate the corporate parent and subsidiary have not been fully established, leading to confusion about whether the two entities are indeed one. Objective 4: In ``Corporate Parent's Liability for Subsidiary's Harm to Non-Contractual Parties,'' we develop a theoretical model that fills a gap in the literature. Brooks (2002) assumes some synergy between risky activities and a firm's other businesses that cannot be realized perfectly if someone else takes on those activities. We assume the absence of such synergy; therefore, when the right to run a business is sold to an independent outsider, no inherent efficiency is lost. We contrast two scenarios: in the first scenario, courts always uphold corporate parents' limited liability for their subsidiaries' liabilities. Without contracting parties in the model, legal liabilities can only arise from non-contractual parties. In the second scenario, courts sometimes hold corporate parents liable; thus, the parent's assets may be used to compensate for unsatisfied claims of the subsidiary's tort victims. The model links the liability rule to 1) the legal structure used to operate potentially harmful businesses, 2) the identity of the operator, and 3) the precautions taken to prevent accidents. We show in equilibrium how these three decisions ultimately determine the non-contractual parties' payoffs. Objective 5: In ``Corporate Parent's Liability for Subsidiary's Harm to Non-Contractual Parties,'' we successfully derive conditions under which a business will prefer setting up a limited liability subsidiary to run risky activities under the assumption that no outsider is available to buy those rights. We show that our model aligns with Shavell (1986), who advocates holding corporate parents liable as a Pigouvian solution to the judgment proof problem, assuming liability arbitrage does not occur. Once we drop this assumption, there is no guarantee that holding corporate parents liable will benefit victims. Objective 6: Our model implies an empirical prediction: changes in the probability of courts holding corporate parents liable will induce more ownership changes. If liability increases, some of these ownership changes will result in operators facing higher capital costs, leading them to spend less on precautions to prevent harm to others. We have some limited empirical support in ``Corporate Parent's Liability for Subsidiary's Harm to Non-Contractual Parties'' by examining name changes of polluting plants' operators and their corporate parents. The context is that the 1998 Bestfoods decision significantly reduced the likelihood of corporate parents being held liable. When we analyze the name changes of U.S. polluting factories, we observe a spike in name changes following this landmark case. Objective 7: The most important divergence from other theoretical papers (e.g., Shavell (1986)) is that they imply empirically that upholding parent-subsidiary limited liability harms non-contractual parties. Our theory suggests an opposite effect: due to various legal complications in imposing liability uniformly across different types of owners, upholding parent-subsidiary limited liability helps non-contractual parties by eliminating the underlying causes of liability arbitrage that would allow those not intended to operate a business to do so. Consequently, victims will be better off. This stands in sharp contrast to existing theories but aligns with courts' general reluctance to hold corporate parents liable. It also explains the landmark decision in Bestfoods.

14501920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501920.value: The Bestfoods decision infuriated many because it seemed to allow a large corporation to evade responsibility for pollution caused by its wholly-owned subsidiary. This case exemplifies numerous corporate law litigations where involuntary creditors seek compensation not only from the entities that harmed them but also from their financially capable corporate parents. Many businesses intentionally establish a parent-subsidiary structure to conduct activities that harm non-contractual parties, typically leaving just enough assets in the subsidiary. If issues arise, they lose only the subsidiary's assets, while the parent company's assets remain protected. Non-contractual parties cannot price-in their increased risk, and it is naive to assume that Coasian bargaining will eliminate externalities. Economists advocate for a Pigouvian solution: holding corporate parents liable for their subsidiaries' actions. Shavell (1986) first formalizes this so-called judgment proof problem and called for such a solution. Yet, courts both in the U.S. and abroad remain reluctant to impose liability on corporate parents. No formal model has explained this reluctance. We present the first model using both a numerical example for non-economists and a formal model to illustrate our point: limited liability prevents liability arbitrage - businesses change hands not for economic reasons but because buyers can better limit their liability than sellers. Legal complications make it easier to impose liability on certain owners, such as domestic corporate parents, compared to individuals or foreign entities. Therefore, eliminating limited liability may still leave some owners with de facto limited liability. Business ownership will gravitate to those who may not be better operators than sellers. If courts cannot identify and prevent liability arbitrage, imposing liability on shareholders is unlikely to benefit victims. This challenge arises because subsidiaries are often closely held. Business ownership transactions involving closely-held businesses occur behind closed doors with minimal disclosure compared to publicly traded companies. Ownership changes in public companies are typically standardized and transparent done through the capital market, while private business ownership transactions are often non-standardized and obscure to outsiders. How can outsiders definitively identify any business ownership transaction as liability arbitrage? If identifying liability arbitrage proves difficult, preventing it becomes equally challenging. To prevent liability arbitrage and its unintended consequences, our model calls for eliminating the underlying causes of liability arbitrage by uniformly upholding limited liability to anyone. This explanation contributes new insights to both legal and economic literature. It also explains Courts' decisions in Bestfoods and other parent-subsidiary limited liability cases.

14501920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501920.value: Our Empirical Challenge: Without judicial investigative authority, we cannot prove that liability arbitrage even exists. On October 21, 2022, the U.S. EPA introduced significant changes to the Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) Reporting Rule. Starting July 1, 2024, facilities must clearly identify their highest-level parent company, including foreign parents previously exempt from disclosure. The reporting process is now standardized, addressing past inconsistencies. Following the 1998 Bestfoods decision, it is clear that corporate parents are unlikely to be held derivatively liable for their subsidiaries' pollution due to ownership, though they can still be held directly liable for other reasons. Before these reporting changes, there was no effective way to analyze TRI data regarding ownership changes from domestic to foreign entities. It can now be done. In the future, if another case overturns Bestfoods, the updated TRI data will be instrumental in detecting whether liability arbitrage has shifted the proportion of owners, such as foreign parents, who enjoy de facto limited liability. The new data will provide insights into the extent of concern regarding liability arbitrage.

14501920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501920.value: Nature: Under limited liability, when a subsidiary injures others, the corporate parent is not required to use its assets to compensate victims if the subsidiary lacks sufficient funds. This allows businesses to take actions through subsidiaries while avoiding full responsibility for the consequences. Our Work: Limited liability prevents liability arbitrage - businesses change hands not for economic reasons but because buyers can better limit their liability than sellers. Various legal complexities make it easier to impose liability on certain owners (e.g., domestic corporate parents) compared to others (e.g., individuals or foreign entities). Eliminating limited liability may still leave some owners with de facto limited liability. Business ownership will gravitate to those who may not be better operators than sellers. If courts cannot identify and prevent liability arbitrage, imposing liability on shareholders is unlikely to benefit victims. Significance and Value: Limited liability is the most litigated issues in corporate law. Why do courts typically uphold it? Our research provides a new perspective. This perspective explains Bestfoods, the landmark case in which the U.S. Supreme Court unanimously declined to impose liability on a corporate parent for its subsidiary's environmental harm as required by the 1980 Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act.

14502320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502320.value: The rise of producer services has been a salient feature of the Chinese economy since the mid 2000s. Producer services accounted 23% of China’s GDP in the 2005. By the most recent official statistics, the share increased to 31% in 2016. In contrast, the share of consumer services increased by merely 3 percentage points between 2005 and 2016. Despite the predominance of producer services in China’s economic growth and structural change, there are few economic studies on this subject (one exception is Tao and Wong (2002)). Our goal is to quantify the underlying forces of the rapid expansion of China’s producer services and to evaluate their welfare implications. We will take three steps. First, we will present stylized facts about the rapid expansion of producer services across regions that have not yet been documented in the literature. These facts will come from both publicly available official statistics and non-public firm- and individual-level survey data. Second, we will construct a comprehensive set of regional and sectoral aggregates (such as capital intensity, TFP and misallocation) on China’s producer services that have never been produced before. These estimates will not only reveal the basic facts, but also provide the indispensable inputs for our quantitative analysis. The third step is to study quantitatively the importance of each of the three fundamental forces for structural change in the literature. Our workhorse is the quantitative framework recently developed by Aghion, Burgess, Peters, and Zilibotti (2019). The framework allows complementarity between manufacturing and producer services, which we believe capture the essence of producer services as intermediate inputs to manufacturing. Moreover, it also considers flows of goods and services across regions. We will generalize the framework and use it to quantify the extent to which each fundamental force can explain the rise of China’s producer services. The welfare consequences will also be assessed quantitatively. While this project is about China’s producer services, its implications are not confined to China. The project contributes to the big and yet fast-growing macro development literature, which has not yet paid much attention to producer services despite their predominance in GDP. This project will also deliver rich policy implications. We will estimate TFP and misallocation by region and sector in China. This will help to identify the regional and sectoral “bottlenecks” that cause significant welfare losses. Region-sector-specific policies can be designed to relieve the bottlenecks by either promoting productivity or reducing misallocation. 生產型服務業的崛起是中國經濟近年來的壹個重要特征。生產型服務業占GDP的比重從2005年的23%上升到2016年的31%。相反，消費型服務業的比重僅上升了3個百分點。本課題旨在研究中國生產型服務業快速崛起的各種因素，並進行量化分析，估算它們的福利效應。

14502320.label: Realisation of objectives
14502320.value: In the paper “Tertiarization Like China”, we document a rapid shift toward services (tertiarization) of the Chinese economy since 2005, as evidenced by the significant increase in both employment and value-added shares of the service sector. Notably, our analysis reveals that a variety of measures of productivity growth have been greater in the service sector than in the manufacturing sector. Firm-level measures of dynamism corroborate this ongoing tertiarization trend, which is not limited to services used as inputs to industrial production but also extends to consumer services. We provide a detailed account of the growing role of services in the Chinese economy. We start with a comparative analysis of China relative to other developing and emerging economies. We argue that, among late industrializers, the experience of China is exceptional in terms of the prominence of its industrial sector in the development process. However, China's exceptionalism is rapidly vanishing, and the structure of the Chinese economy is becoming more similar to that of other economies at a comparable stage of development. We study the nature of the process of structural change in China and contrast the data with different hypotheses that could explain the rapid tertiarization. The first hypothesis is that the decline in the employment share of manufacturing is explained by the boom in construction and infrastructure building. Despite the importance of construction-related services, our data shows that the growth of the service sector in China is not limited to these activities. A second hypothesis is that the main driver of tertiarization is services used as inputs for the production of goods. This would suggest that the growth of the Chinese service sector is ancillary to industrial production, which would remain the main focal point of economic activity. We observe a rapid growth of service industries providing inputs to the industrial sector, which we label producer services. However, other service industries also contribute significantly to tertiarization. We observe a boom of service industries that improve consumers' access to goods (e.g., retailers or restaurants) or provide services that are directly consumed by households (e.g., recreation, health, community services). Finally, one might conjecture that tertiarization stems from a growing role of the government in the Chinese economy. Contrary to this hypothesis, we do not find that government-provided services play an important role in the tertiarization process. Public services are, in fact, the only non-growing service industry as a share of GDP. We center our analysis on productivity growth in the service sector, which has long been viewed as inherently stagnant. This view suggests that the sustained economic growth of China could be threatened by tertiarization. However, contrary to this view, our findings indicate that productivity has grown faster in the service sector than in the industrial sector over the last decade. This holds true for both consumer and producer services. Yet, studying productivity growth in the service sector poses a significant challenge, given that standard estimates of sectoral total factor productivity (TFP) rely on sectoral price indexes, which are difficult to measure accurately due to the challenges of accounting for quality improvements in service industries. This issue is further complicated by non-homothetic preferences, making it difficult to consistently define price indexes across sectors. To tackle this issue, we generalize the methodology recently proposed by Fan et al. (2022) to estimate productivity growth circumventing problems associated with the published price index for services. Specifically, we specify a class of non-homothetic preferences and estimates their parameters, which include an income elasticity that can be derived from microdata. We extend their model by incorporating savings and investment into a standard growth model with capital accumulation. This approach enables us to estimate productivity growth in services without relying on published price indexes. Our results confirm that the service sector has experienced high productivity growth, particularly in consumer services. In all scenarios considered, we find that productivity growth in consumer service industries significantly outpaced productivity growth in manufacturing during the period 2005--2015. Finally, we use firm-level data from China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) to compare turnover rates between service and manufacturing firms. Our results show that service firms have higher turnover rates than manufacturing firms, and that this gap has widened over the last two decades. Specifically, the entry rate in the service sector has increased from 15% in 1996 to 20% in 2019, while it has remained constant around 12% in the industrial sector. We also observe similar trends for the exit rate, although this measure is subject to significant low-frequency fluctuations. Different from “Tertiarization Like China” that focuses on the aggregate-level structural change, we study the regional-level heterogeneity in tertiarization in the paper “A Dual Accounting for the Rise of Service Sectors in China.” Our workhorse is a multi-region and multi-industry model with misallocation at firm, industry, and sector levels. Industries are grouped into four sectors: agriculture, manufacturing, producer services, and consumer services. On the one hand, assuming a specific sectoral demand structure, the standard development accounting can back out sectoral TFP in a region from regional and sectoral employment shares. On the other hand, using firm data, we can aggregate Hsieh-Klenow statistics to the region-sector level, referred to as the ``direct method". Both methods will deliver the same estimates of region-sector TFP if the sectoral demand structure is correctly specified for development accounting. The equivalence provides the theoretical foundation for our dual accounting approach. We use a dual accounting approach to investigate the underlying forces for the structural change across sectors and regions. We first use development accounting to back out region-sector TFP growth from regional and sectoral employment shares. We then use ``the direct method" that aggregates Hsieh-Klenow statistics to the region-sector level and apply it to a large-scale firm data set. Development accounting and the direct method will deliver the same estimates if the sectoral demand structure is correctly specified for development accounting. We find three main results. First, both development accounting and the direct method reveal fast manufacturing and producer services TFP growth. The sectoral TFP growth estimated by the two methods is also highly correlated, in line with the internal consistency of the dual accounting approach. Second, we decompose sectoral TFP growth by the direct method into efficient sectoral TFP growth, changes in sectoral wedge and changes in within-industry misallocation. We find the manufacturing and producer services TFP growth to be primarily driven by efficient TFP growth but substantially slowed by the worsening of misallocation. Third, we infer misallocation from the dual accounting approach, which turns out to be highly correlated with the directly measured misallocation. The strong correlation not only reinforces the deteriorating misallocation by the direct method but also provides another validity check for our dual accounting approach. Holding within-industry misallocation constant would increase China's service employment share by 26 percentage points. Taken together, the findings in the two papers support the argument that tertiarization is not simply a by product of the development process, but rather an increasingly important driver of economic growth in China. However, there still exists severe within-industry misallocation, which varies a lot across regions and over time. Correction of such misallocation may have large effects on China’s structural transformation.

14502320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502320.value: We finished two papers: “Tertiarization like China” and “A Dual Accounting for the Rise of Service Sectors in China”. The first paper has been published in Annual Review of Economics, 2023, 15: 485-512. We also finished an article for VoxChina and VoxEU: "Is China Becoming a Service Economy?" (https://www.voxchina.org/show-3-292.html) The major findings are summarized as follows. We document a rapid shift toward services (tertiarization) of the Chinese economy since 2005, as evidenced by the significant increase in both employment and value-added shares of the service sector. Notably, our analysis reveals that a variety of measures of productivity growth have been greater in the service sector than in the manufacturing sector. Firm-level measures of dynamism corroborate this ongoing tertiarization trend, which is not limited to services used as inputs to industrial production but also extends to consumer services. We also find the manufacturing and producer services TFP growth to be primarily driven by efficient TFP growth but substantially slowed by the worsening of misallocation. Holding within-industry misallocation constant would increase China's service employment share by 26 percentage points.

14502320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502320.value: China’s development process has entered a new stage in which services and the domestic market play a significantly more important role than in the past. If tertiarization is no mere consequence of rapid income growth, but a result of productivity growth in services, the growth process can prove resilient to Baumol’s disease. Should we expect this trend to continue? The growing tension in international relations is likely to raise barriers to international trade. This might further speed the ongoing structural transformation by enhancing the importance of the domestic market and nontradable goods. The consolidation of an urban middle class is also likely to sustain growing demand for services in the coming years. Recent research shows that demand forces are an important driver of the direction of technical change. Thus, the growing demand for services will likely trigger additional productivity growth in the service sector. Moreover, to the extent these services are local in nature, the benefits of growth can become even more skewed in favor of large cities. Finally, service-led growth is likely to reduce pressure on natural resources and environmental damage relative to growth solely driven by industrial production.

14502520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502520.value: 本研究探討公司之間的人力資本相關性是否會影響其會計信息的可比性。高度的信息可比性意味著經濟活動相似（不同）的公司報告的會計收益也相似（不同）。因此，企業之間的信息可比性取決於衡量經濟活動的會計系統的相似性。多項研究表明，採用相同的會計準則可以使會計以類似的方式反映經濟活動，從而增強信息的可比性。我們認為，一家公司的人力資本會影響其會計系統對經濟活動的映射，因此公司之間的人力資本相關性會影響其會計映射的相似性，進而影響其信息可比性。具體而言，現行會計準則不允許公司直接將人力資本的價值資本化以及量化和記錄人力資本帶來的所有經濟利益。因此，管理者必須找到一種方法與投資者交流其員工的價值。與擁有較少高技術工人的公司相比，擁有更多高技術工人的公司可能需要運用更廣泛的會計估計以獲取其由人力資本帶來的經濟利益。因此，由於對員工價值的會計估計的程度不同，具有不同員工溝成的兩家公司的會計信息的可比性比較小。其次，研究顯示，擁有高素質員工的公司擁有出更高的會計質量，更少的內部控制違規和更少的報表重述。一方面，高素質員工可以為公司會計系統提供準確的信息輸入。另一方面，他們更有能力識別和阻止故意的財務錯誤。因此，擁有更多高技術工人的公司可以更好地應用會計準則，並獲得更一致的會計估計和選擇，從而減少會計錯誤，提高會計信息的可比性。 我們將使用1999年至2017年間的美國上市公司樣本來檢驗我們的預測。我們還將做幾個橫截面測試，以檢驗如果兩個公司（1）來自勞動力強度高的行業，以及2）來自需要較高勞動技能的行業，那麼人力資本相關性對信息可比性的影響是否更為明顯。在我們的其他測試中，我們將使用基於年收益信息傳遞的替代性信息可比性度量和替代性回歸模型來檢驗假設。為了解決內生性問題，在敏感性測試中，我們將構建DiD樣本，以檢驗由合併導致的人力資本相關性的變化是否可以增強和削弱信息可比性。我們還將指標變量用於關鍵變量，以減少其測量誤差。 本研究將為信息可比性和人力資本的文獻做出貢獻。信息可比性是財務報告的重要素質，據我們所知，關於人力資本如何影響信息可比性知之甚少。現有的人力資本會計研究集中在勞動力，失業風險和財務報告質量上。我們通過檢查人力資本相關性是否影響信息可比性來擴展這兩個文獻流。

14503020.label: Project Objectives
14503020.value: Our main objective is to test whether consumers are rational when the stakes are high. Chetty, Looney and Kroft (2009) show that consumers under-react to a non-salient tax. The resulting loss, however, is quite small. By contrast, the Hong Kong residential housing market is the most expensive in the world. In our sample, a consumer will suffer a loss of 40000 HK dollar (about 5000 USD) if she overpays by one percent of the average transaction price. We seek to exploit the policy change in 2013 to develop a formal statistical test for gross-area bias. We plan to test the hypothesis using residential property transaction data between 2009 to 2017. Evidence of such bias will show that some cognitive errors cannot be fully eliminated by high stakes alone. To guide the empirical work, we will construct a model of property market with boundedly rational consumers. We will explore how gross-area bias affects the market price of apartments with different efficiency ratios, and how consumers with different degrees of gross-area bias sort themselves into buying properties of different efficiency ratios. We will look at the difference in purchasing behavior between of mainland Chinese buyers and local Chinese buyers. The extent to which the demand of mainland Chinese buyers contribute to the housing boom in Hong Kong is, by itself, an important issue. As the mainland Chinese buyers are less familiar with the local market, they are more likely to be misled by information about gross area. Our model predicts that they are more likely to purchase apartments with lower efficiency ratio.
