14503020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503020.value: Two different measures of size are commonly used in the Hong Kong residential property market. The saleable area is the net internal area of a property, plus the thickness of the walls. The gross area is the saleable area plus a share of the common areas of the building or housing estate. The efficiency ratio---the ratio of saleable area to gross area---varies across housing developments. On average, the gross area of a flat inflates the size of a property by more than twenty percent. Before 2013, the common practice among developers and real-estate agents is to list only the gross area in sales brochures and advertisements. After 2013, a new rule requires that only saleable area can be provided in sales brochures, and that advertisements of second-hand properties must display the saleable area with a font size not smaller than that of gross area. If buyers are fully rational, the new rule, which affects only the presentation and not the content of information, should have no effect. Even prior to 2013, the saleable area of a flat is public information, and potential buyers can easily learn about it from real-estate agents. Given the high stakes, buyers should have every incentive to take into account of all available information. Behavioral economists, however, argue that consumers are not fully rational and the willingness to pay for a good can be unduly influenced by irrelevant information. According this view, buyers who first learn about the gross area of a flat may fail to fully adjust their perception afterwards. We propose to study the effect of the new rule using residential property transaction data in Hong Kong between 2009 to 2017. In particular, we shall look at how the new rule affects the price per saleable square feet for residential flats with different efficiency ratios. If buyers were confused about the size of the flats before 2013, then flats with high efficiency ratio should command a higher price after the new rule takes effect in 2013. We shall also investigate whether the new rule affects local and mainland Chinese buyers differently. The latter group, which represents about ten percent of the buyers, presumably is less familiar with the local market and, hence, more likely to be influenced by misleading information. 香港住宅的整合市場採用兩種不同的面積計算方法。 實用面積是物業的淨內部面積,加上牆的厚度。 建築面積是實用面積加上建築物或居住區公用面積的一部分。 實用率---實用面積與總面積之比---在不同房子會有所不同。 平均而言,建築面積比實用面積高20%以上。 在2013年之前,其房地產經紀人的普遍做法是僅在銷售手冊和廣告中列出建築面積。 2013年之後,一項新規則要求在銷售手冊中只能提供實用面積,並且二手房廣告必須顯示實用面積,且其字體大小不得小於建築面積。 如果購買者是完全理性的,則僅影響表示方式而不影響資訊內容的新規則將不會對房價做成影響。 在2013年之前,單位的實用面積就是公開資訊,買家可以輕鬆地從房地產代理商那裡瞭解到這一資訊。 考慮到香港的高房價,買家應有一切動機考慮所有可用資訊。 但是,行為經濟學家認為,消費者不是完全理性的,購買商品的意願可能會受到不相關資訊的過度影響。 根據這種觀點,買家可能不直覺地受房子建築面積誤導。 我們建議使用2009年至2017年之間香港住宅個人交易數據研究新規則的影響。 我們將研究新規則如何影響具有不同實用率的住宅單位的每平方英尺銷售價格。 如果買家對2013年之前被建築面積誤導,那麼高實用率的單位的價格應在2013年新規則生效後增加。 我們將研究新規則對本地和中國內地買家的影響是否不同。 後者大約佔購買者的百分之十。 由於大陸買家對當地市場瞭解較低,因此,更有可能受到建築面積誤導。

14503020.label: Realisation of objectives
14503020.value: 1. To study whether the new regulation affects the relative price of apartments with high efficiency ratios, we estimate the following hedonic price model: lnP_{i,t}=α_{t}ln e_{i}+β_{t}lnG_{i}+γ_{t}X_{i}+D_{i,t}+F_{i}+ε_{i,t}, where ∙ lnP_{i,t} is the log sales price of flat i sold in year t, ∙ ln e_{i} is the efficiency ratio of flat i, ∙ lnG_{i} is the gross area of flat i, ∙ X_{i} includes a set of flat i's characteristics, including age, building type (i.e, stand-alone building or multi-block housing estate), amenities (e.g, swimming pool or clubhouse), ∙ D_{i,t} is a set of region specific time dummies, ∙ F_{i} is an estate dummy. Our primary interest is see whether α_{t}, the coefficient of the efficiency ratio, increases after 2013 after a regulation requires real-estate agents to display the unit price in saleable area. We segment the market into three components according to an apartment's saleable area: small (250-400 sq. ft), medium (400-800 sq. ft), and large (800-1200 sq. ft) to allow for different market dynamics across segments. In the baseline, we include region, estate, and building specific time dummies to control for other potential confounding time trends, and we add housing-estate dummies to control for unobserved estate characteristics that may be correlated with an apartment's efficiency ratio. Overall, the results are consistent with our hypothesis. The coefficients of the variables are all of expected signs. In particular, the coefficient of the log efficiency ratio variable is positive and significant in all three market segments, which indicates that flats with a relative high saleable area commanded a higher price even prior to 2013. However, the coefficients further increase after 2013. The post-2023 coefficients are large, ranging from twenty (for small apartments) to fifty percent (for large apartments) of the corresponding baseline coefficients, and statistically significant in all three segments after controlling for estate fixed effects. The result indicates that apartments in housing estates with higher efficiency ratios command a higher price after 2013. The effects are small but statistically significant, with the price elasticity of the efficiency ratio ranging from 0.005 for smaller flats to 0.045 for larger flats. For robustness, we treat the apartments in a stand-alone building separately from those in a multi-block housing estate. We obtained similar results for small and large apartments. However, for medium sized apartments, the coefficient of the log efficiency ratio post-2013 is statistically significant only for apartments in stand-alone apartments. One possibility is that in the thicker medium sized housing estate market, less informed buyers can easily find recent transactions in the same development as benchmarks to avoid paying excessively for apartments with low efficiency ratios. 2. We construct a simple model to investigate the potential effects of the new rule. There are two types of flats. Both have the same saleable area, but one has a larger gross area, or equivalently a lower efficiency ratio, than the other. We follow Gabaix's (2019) simple framework for modeling attention. Buyers care about the saleable area of a flat but their perception may be anchored at the gross area. There are two types of consumers. Local homebuyers (i=l) are fully rational in that their perceived useable area of the flat is equal to its true saleable area. Buyers from mainland China (i=C) are less informed about the local market and they incorrectly anchor their perception on the gross area. We derive the equilibrium of this market. In equilibrium, mainland Chinese buyers will sort into purchasing lower-efficiency-ratio flats, and such flats will be sold at a premium. Both the sorting effect and the price premium are increasing in the degree of misperception of mainland Chinese buyers is larger. Our model thus predicts that the new regulation which will reduce the degree of misperception will unwind these effects---both the average efficiency ratio of flats purchased by the mainland Chinese buyers and the price of flats with a higher efficiency ratio should rise relative to the market average after 2013. 3. To quantify the sorting effect, we estimate the following model: e_{i,t}=αm_{i}.I_{t≥2013}+βm_{i}+γI_{t≥2013}+D_{i,t}+F_{i}+ε_{i,t}, where ∙ e_{i,t} is the efficiency ratio of a flat sold in time t, ∙ m_{i} is a dummy variable that equals one if the buyer is mainland Chinese, ∙ I_{t≥2013} is a dummy variable that equals one if the transaction occurred in 2013 or after, ∙ D_{i,t} is a set of controls, including transaction year, region, building type, size category, and age, ∙ F_{i} is an estate dummy. The result shows that mainland Chinese buyers tends to purchase properties of lower efficiency ratios compared to local buyers after controlling for apartment size, building location and type. As our model predicts, the gap narrows by about one third after 2013. Controlling for property age reduces the efficiency-ratio gap between mainland Chinese and local buyers by almost one half but does not affect the impact of the new regulation. We also find that controlling the estate fixed effects, there is no difference between the behavior between mainland Chinese and local buyers. Thus, the effect of the new regulation is to induce mainland Chinese buyers to shift to housing estates that have higher efficiency ratios.

14503020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503020.value: In 2013, the Estate Agents Authority introduced a new code of conduct to improve the clarity of the floor area information in advertisements. In particular, real estate agents are required to list the saleable area of a property as prominently as the gross area in all sales materials. Our objective is to studying the effects of the new rule both theoretically and empirically. We construct a simple model to under the potential effects. In our model, there are two types of flats. Both have the same saleable area, but one has a larger gross area, or equivalently a lower efficiency ratio, than the other. Some home buyers have limited attention and wrongly believe that lower-efficiency-ratio flats have a larger saleable area when real-estate agents misleadingly highlight the gross area in advertisements. Before the new regulation, buyers with stronger misperceptions will sort into purchasing lower-efficiency-ratio flats, and such flats will be sold at a premium. Our model predicts that these effects will be unwound after the new regulation took effect. We then estimate these effects empirically using a data set of second-hand property transactions between 2009 and 2017. We find that the new regulation produces small but statistically significant changes consistent with our theoretical predictions. Between 2009 and 2017, the average efficiency ratio of flats purchased by mainland Chinese buyers was about one percentage point lower (about 0.2 standard deviation) than that purchased by local buyers. After the new regulations took effect in 2013, the gap narrowed by 0.4 percentage point. Upon controlling for broad market segments, the result remains unchanged and is statistically significant at the one percent level. This suggests that mainland Chinese buyers switch to purchasing flats with relatively higher saleable areas after the new regulation. Controlling for the gross area, region-specific price trends, and housing-development-specific fixed effects, flats with a higher efficiency ratio sell at a slightly higher price after 2013. The effects are small but statistically significant, with the price elasticity of the efficiency ratio ranging from 0.005 for smaller flats to 0.045 for larger flats. Further robustness checks show that the effects for medium-sized flats are driven mainly by apartments in stand-alone buildings. The coefficients for the efficiency ratio for medium sized apartments have the correct sign but are insignificant when the analysis is restricted to multi-block housing developments.

14503020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503020.value: We will present the findings in international academic conferences. We will submit the research output to an academic journal after incorporating feedback we receive from conference audiences.

14503020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503020.value: We investigate the effects of a regulatory change in one of the most expensive residential property markets in the world. The floor areas of Hong Kong residential flats are quoted in two ways: saleable area and gross area. The former is a residential unit's floor area inclusive of enclosing and internal walls, while the latter is the saleable area plus a proportionate share of the common area. Before 2013, it was customary for developers and real-estate agents to quote properties in gross areas. New regulations require real-estate agents to list a property's saleable area as prominently as its gross area in all sales materials and advertisements. We find that before the new regulations, buyers less familiar with the market purchased flats with lower ratios of saleable to gross area. After the regulatory change, the price of flats with higher ratios of saleable to gross area increases. The evidence suggests that despite high stakes---an average flat costing close to one million US dollars---many buyers are influenced by the salience of information.

14503420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503420.value: This proposed study will examine how the introduction of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect affects the intraday price discovery between the dually-listed A-share and H-share in the two markets. Previous studies on the price discovery process between the A- and H-share are based on daily price data. Given that stock prices incorporate information quickly during the day, it is more thorough to investigate the price discovery process based on intraday price data. There are competing hypotheses on whether the A-share or H-share contribute more to the price discovery with Stock Connect. On one hand, if information is more likely to originate from the home market, then the A-share should play a more important role than the H-share in the price discovery. On the other hand, as the A-share market is dominated by retail investors who trade based on speculation, while the H-share market is participated by institutional investors who trade based on fundamental, the H-share can contribute more to the price discovery with Stock Connect. I follow the methodology in Hasbrouck (1995) to estimate Information Share (IS) of A-share and H-share, and compare the IS before and after the Shanghai Stock Connect. If Mainland investors are more informed, their trading in A-share and then H-share (via Soutthbound Trading) will result in larger price discovery for the A-share. On the other hand, if Hong Kong (institutional) investors are more informed, their trading in H-share and then A-share (via Northbound Trading) will result in larger price discovery for the H-share. I will also obtain Northbound daily trading volume and Southbound daily trading volume for individual stocks. This allows me to examine whether there is a relationship between relative IS of A-share and H-share and the amount of Northbound/Southbound trading volume. Finally, there are a few business days when both Shanghai and Hong Kong stock markets are open, Southbound Trading is allowed but Northbound Trading is dis-allowed. This gives me an opportunity to examine how the price discovery of A-share and H-share will be affected in those days. This proposed study will be the first to investigate the price discovery role of A- and H-shares based on intraday data. This is important as the Stock Connect Program allows the market to become more integrated and facilitate the information transmission. We will gain further insights by examining how the Northbound and Southbound trading activity affect the price discovery process.

14503420.label: Realisation of objectives
14503420.value: For the first objective, we constructed Hasbrouck (1995)’s Information Share to measure the relative contribution to the price discovery of 67 dually-listed listed A-H shares on both Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEx) from 2014 to 2016. We find, on average, the A-share (local market)’s contribution (56%) to the intraday price discovery is higher than the H-share (international market)’s contribution (42%) in the sample period. For the second objective, we find that the Information Share of A-share (H-share) increases (decreases) with the proportion of A-share’s trading volume. This shows that the trading activity in one market facilitates the price discovery in the other market. For the third objective, we find that the effect of cross-border trading activity on price discovery varies between southbound trading (trades placed by Mainland investors on the Hong Kong market) and northbound trading (trades placed by Hong Kong investors on the Shanghai market). When the proportion of northbound trading volume (as a percentage of total trading volume in the Shanghai market) increases, the Information Share of A-share will decrease, while that of H-share will increase. On the other hand, southbound trading does not have any effect on the Information Share of A-share or H-share. For the fourth objective, we don't find Information Share of A- and H-share are affected much during the days when northbound trading is closed.

14503420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503420.value: First, we constructed Hasbrouck (1995)’s Information Share to measure the relative contribution to the price discovery of 67 dually-listed listed A-H shares on both Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEx) from 2014 to 2016. We find, on average, the A-share (local market)’s contribution (56%) to the intraday price discovery is higher than the H-share (international market)’s contribution (42%) in the sample period. This is consistent with previous studies which report that price discovery happens in both markets, although the local market contributes more. Second, we examine the effect of cross-border trading activity on price discovery, and find that the effect varies between southbound trading (trades placed by Mainland investors on the Hong Kong market) and northbound trading (trades placed by Hong Kong investors on the Shanghai market). When the proportion of northbound trading volume (as a percentage of total trading volume in the Shanghai market) increases, the Information Share of A-share will decrease, while that of H-share will increase. On the other hand, southbound trading does not have any effect on the Information Share of A-share or H-share. This indicates that northbound trading from Hong Kong investors affects the price discovery process whereas southbound trading from Mainland investors does not. Third, besides the price discovery process, we also investigate the relationships between cross-border trading volume and the various intraday market quality measures. We construct volume-synchronized probability of informed trading (VPIN) based on Easley, et al. (2012) and intraday effective spread (ESPR) to measure the amount of information in stock prices. In addition, we also compute Hasbrouck (1993)’s pricing error (PE) and intraday volatility ratio (VR) to measure the extent to which the prices diverge from the efficient price (random walk). We find an increase in northbound trading is accompanied by a rise in VPIN and ESPR, a drop in PE and VR of A-share, while southbound trading does not affect the intraday market qualities of H-share. In decomposing southbound trading into institutional trading versus retail trading, we find institutional southbound trading is connected to higher VPIN and ESPR, as well as lower PE and VR of H-share, whereas retail southbound trading is not. Our findings indicate that northbound trading from Hong Kong investors contributes largely to price discovery and an improves price efficiency.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503420.value: We examine the price discovery process of Mainland Chinese companies dually-listed in Shanghai (home market) and Hong Kong (foreign market). Unlike previous studies that do the analysis based on daily data, our study is based on intraday price data, which allows us to examine the price discovery of these dual-listed stocks over very short-horizons within a day. Based on Hasbrouck (1995)’s Information Share, we find that the relative trading volume in Hong Kong (Shanghai) is positively related to the relative contribution to price discovery. Also, the northbound trading by foreign investors in Hong Kong has a greater contribution to price discovery than southbound trading by domestic investors in Mainland China. We also find that northbound trading and institutional southbound trading are informed and improve pricing efficiency. On the other hand, retail southbound trading does not improve pricing efficiency.

14503520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503520.value: Housing and equity account for a major proportion of households’ wealth. This project uses proprietary account-level data from the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and housing price indices for 120 Chinese cities from Fang, Gu, Xiong, and Zhou (2017) to study how the dynamics of housing markets affect people’s trading behaviors as well as the stock prices in equity markets. We plan to estimate structural breaks in the evolution of housing prices for each city based on procedures from the time-series econometrics literature (Bai 1997, Bai and Perron 1998). Following Charles, Hurst, and Notowidigdo (2018), we argue structural breaks in the evolution of housing prices are exogenous to confounders and conduct event study analyses of investor portfolios. We will test two competing hypotheses. The first is the “wealth effect hypothesis,” and the second is the “substitution effect hypothesis.” Hypothesis 1: Wealth Effect Hypothesis Appreciation in house prices would increase households’ investment in stock markets because households may feel more financial slacks and tend to invest more in stock markets or they may tend to realize gains by selling their homes when house prices increase and invest in stock markets with their profits from housing markets. In addition, wealth effect could increase investors’ risk appetite and households may invest more on risky assets. Hypothesis 2: Substitution Effect Hypothesis Appreciation in housing prices would reduce households’ investment in stock markets, because home purchases (or planned purchases) crowd out households’ investment in stock markets. Also, because of limited attention, people’s attention could drift from stock markets to housing markets. As such, people tend to trade less. We then further hypothesize that people may differently react to the evolvement of housing markets. Different reactions depend on whether or not households are financially constrained and whether or not they already own a home. Hypothesis 3: Heterogeneous Effects across Groups When housing prices increase, households who do not own a home and who are financially constrained are likely to reduce their investment in stock markets and save their money for the down payment of their future home. With the appreciation of their home equity, homeowners who are financially constrained may feel less constrained, but they cannot afford to invest more in housing markets. Therefore, these people tend to invest more in stock markets. Households who own homes and are less financially constrained may shift their investment from stock markets to housing markets. 房產和股票是壹般家庭的主要資產。本項目利用深圳證券交易所的帳戶數據以及中國120個城市的房價指數（Fang, Gu, Xiong, and, Zhou，2017）研究房產市場的變化如何影響人們的交易行為和股票價格。我們將依據時間序列計量經濟學文獻（Bai 1997, Bai and Perron 1998）中的方法估計每個城市房價的結構性變化。如Charles, Hurst, and Notowidigdo (2018) 中的討論，這些房價的結構性變化是相對外生的因素，我們可基於它們作事件分析，研究投資者的資產組合。 我們將檢驗兩個假說。第壹個是“財富效應假說”，第二個是“替代效應假說”。 假說壹：財富效應假說 房價的上漲會促進家庭在股票市場的投資。這是因為人們可能會感覺更寬裕，更願意投資股市，或者他們更有可能在房價上漲的情況下賣掉房產，用賺取的利潤投資股市。另外，財富效應可能會提高投資者的風險偏好，導致他們去投資更具風險的資產。 假說二：替代效應假說 房價的上漲會減少人們對股市的投資。這是因為購買房產會對股市投資有擠出效應。另外，人們有限的註意力會從股市分散到房市上，人們因此會減少對股市的交易。 我們進壹步假設人們可能會對房市的變化有不同的反應。這些不同的反應取決於家庭是不是有財務上的約束和他們是否已經擁有房產。 假說三：不同人群的異質性效應 當房價上漲時，沒有房產和同時有財務約束的家庭更有可能減少股市上的投資，為未來購買房產節省資金。 而有房家庭而又有財務約束的家庭會感覺約束放松，但他們可能不足以投資更多的房產。因此這些人會更多地投資到股市上去。 最後，有房家庭同時財務寬裕的家庭可能更傾向於將他們在股市上的投資轉移到房產上。

14503520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503520.value: In this study, we aim to understand the potential effects of increased climate change regulatory risks on households' willingness to engage in financial risk-taking. To achieve this, we employ a two-fold approach. Firstly, we utilize state-level measures of climate change regulatory risks, which provide a comprehensive view of the regulatory landscape. Secondly, we analyze micro-level household data that contains detailed information on household portfolios and job industries. Our findings reveal a notable pattern among households employed in high-emission industries. As regulatory policy risks related to climate change increase, these households tend to reduce their exposure to financial risks. This finding suggests that the presence of stricter regulations acts as a deterrent, leading households to adopt a more conservative approach towards their financial investments. Importantly, this effect holds true even when taking into account the implementation of climate change action plans and the level of stringency enforced by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Additionally, we observe an interesting trend of households transitioning from high-emission industries to non-high-emission industries in response to heightened climate change regulatory risks. This shift indicates that households recognize the potential risks associated with high-emission industries and seek alternative employment opportunities in more environmentally friendly sectors. Notably, those households who make this transition exhibit a significantly higher allocation of their wealth to risky assets compared to households who remain in high-emission industries. This suggests that individuals who proactively adapt to climate change regulatory risks are more inclined to take on greater financial risks in order to potentially achieve higher returns on their investments. Overall, our research sheds light on a novel economic pathway through which climate change risks influence households' risk-taking behaviors. By specifically examining the impact on households and their portfolio choices, we contribute to the existing body of literature, which has predominantly focused on the effects of climate change regulatory risks on firms. The significance of climate change regulatory risks in shaping household risk-taking behavior underscores the importance of considering these factors in policy-making decisions.

14503520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503520.value: An important implication arising from our findings is that climate regulations have unintended consequences for households employed in high-emission industries. These households tend to have lower levels of wealth, younger age groups, and lower levels of education. Moreover, it is the low-income and low-wealth households that are most affected by climate regulatory risks in terms of their willingness to take financial risks. As a result, climate regulations contribute to the reinforcement of wealth inequality at the societal level by discouraging financial risk-taking among less affluent households, thus hindering effective wealth accumulation. It is important to note that we are not suggesting that society is worse off as a result of climate regulations. However, our findings underscore the importance of implementing climate regulations in a manner that avoids exacerbating labor income risks for employees in high-emission industries.

14503520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503520.value: This research explores a new way in which climate risks can impact how households choose to invest in risky assets. When there are strict regulations in place to address climate change, it increases the risk of job instability for households working in industries that emit high levels of greenhouse gases. This, in turn, makes these households less likely to take financial risks. By analyzing the implementation of climate change action plans across different states, the study finds that these plans lead to a 15% decrease in the proportion of risky assets held by households in high-emission industries. Similarly, after the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) enforces stringent regulations, there is also a reduction in risky asset holdings. These effects are even stronger in areas that have experienced climate change-related disasters. The study highlights an unintended consequence of climate regulations, which is that they discourage low-wealth households from taking financial risks. This has the potential to worsen wealth inequality. Overall, the research suggests that climate regulations have broader impacts beyond their intended goals and should be implemented carefully to avoid discouraging financial risk-taking among low-wealth households.

14503720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503720.value: As disclosure rules have become more extensive over time, there are increasing concerns over the disclosure effectiveness in mandatory filings, e.g. the disclosure of qualitative risk factors. Despite ongoing regulatory concerns over boilerplate disclosure, early academic research found qualitative risk disclosures to be informative. However, more recent research suggests that earlier findings are only applicable in the period of global financial crisis. Additionally, it has been difficult to evaluate the extent to which the disclosure of a specific risk factor reflects its estimated impact on the firm as prior research largely focused on the entire qualitative risk disclosure section. These warrant further investigation into the nature of risk factor disclosure. We will examine a qualitative risk factor that can be assessed by standardized quantifiable benchmarks across all firms listed in the United States. This risk factor is share price volatility risk. To evaluate to what extent the disclosure of share price volatility risk is reflective of the underlying risk, we will examine its association with various total and idiosyncratic share price volatility measures as benchmarks. The availability of quantifiable benchmarks enables us to examine its time horizon, that is, whether the disclosure reflects share price volatility in a largely backward- or forward-looking manner. Through the standardized benchmarks, we are also able to identify instances of uninformative boilerplate disclosures and non-disclosure of high share price volatility risk and further examine their determinants. Finally, we will investigate whether the market reacts to the changes in the disclosure of share price volatility risk and the nature of its informativeness. With deeper insights into risk factor disclosure by using share price volatility risk as an instance, the proposed research adds to the current regulatory debate on this issue, as in August 2019, the SEC proposed rule amendments to modernize the description of risk factor disclosure and is soliciting public comments on this proposal. The use of standardized quantitative benchmarks can provide a clearer assessment of the nature of risk factor disclosure. Through examining the narratives in filings, the proposed project will also enhance our understanding on the nature of share price volatility, a very important dimension in the financial market, from a managerial perspective. Furthermore, it may aid in documenting the presence of specific managerial knowledge about second-moment of stock returns. 隨著披露細則變得越來越多，大家也越來越關注公司披露文件的成效，尤其是有關非量化風險因素的披露。儘管監管機構一直在關注其可能存在樣板式的披露，但早期的學術研究發現非量化風險披露具有參考價值。同時最近的研究也表明，此較早的發現僅適用於全球金融危機時期。但由於先前的研究主要集中在整個非量化風險披露部分，因此很難評估特定風險因素的披露在多大程度上反映了其對公司的潛在影響。因此風險因素披露的性質進一步研究。 我們計劃研究一種特定的非量化風險因素的披露，即股價波動風險。該風險因素雖屬於非量化風險因素的一種,但可以通過標準化的量化基准去進行評估。為了評估股價波動風險的披露在多大程度上反映了潛在風險，我們將考察其與各種股價波動率的關聯, 同時探索其在時間上的應用範圍。通過標準化的基準，我們還能夠識別出無參考價值的樣板式披露或者未披露的高股價波動風險實例，並進一步研究其決定因素。最後，我們將調查市場是否對股價波動風險的披露變化及其信息性質作出反應。 美國證監會在2019年8月提出了規則修正案，以使風險因素披露的描述現代化，並且徵求公眾對此提案的意見。通過以股價波動風險為例, 此擬議的研究有望促進對風險因素披露的了解。同時，使用標準化的定量基準可以更清晰地評估風險因素披露的性質。

14503720.label: Realisation of objectives
14503720.value: 1. To examine both cross-sectional and time-series variations in share price volatility risk disclosures The study successfully establishes that share price volatility risk disclosures are not random but are systematically driven by both time trends and industry characteristics. The study achieved this through a comprehensive analysis of 29,180 firm-year observations. Time-series analysis revealed a steady upward trend in disclosure propensity, rising from approximately 30% in 2006 to over 60% by 2018. This challenges the notion that risk factors are static, showing they track the general increase in regulatory filing length and concerns over boilerplate disclosures. Cross-sectionally, the research documented massive industrial dispersions; high-volatility industries like pharmaceuticals (78.99%) and computers (70.93%) show significantly higher disclosure rates than stable industries such as utilities (13.82%). Firm-fixed effects regressions confirmed that the disclosure decision varies significantly with contemporaneous variations in realized volatility within the same firm over time. Our study shows that despite the high "stickiness" of disclosures (92% persistence), managers do respond to within-firm changes in volatility. 2. To investigate the nature and informativeness of share price volatility risk disclosures The project finds that while informative of cross-sectional risk profiles, these disclosures are fundamentally backward-looking. By benchmarking against realized volatility, regression results showed that a move from the bottom to the top decile of historical volatility increases disclosure propensity by 29%. Both historical Volatility t and future Volatility t+1 volatility measures are significantly associated with the disclosure decision on share price volatility risk factor. However, when comparing measurement windows, the statistical association was significantly higher for historical measures than for forward-looking measures Volatility t+1. This confirms that the disclosure mainly reflects risks that have already been realized rather than acting as an early warning system for future volatility. The study further refines "informativeness" by showing that disclosures track idiosyncratic (firm-specific) volatility just as closely as total volatility, suggesting managers are capturing firm-specific nuances rather than just market beta. 3. To examine the determinant of uninformative boilerplate disclosures on share price volatility risk Our analysis of the "bottom quintile" volatility subsample provides a profile of firms that likely provide uninformative warnings. Examining the "bottom quintile" of realized volatility revealed that firms facing high litigation risks are the primary providers of boilerplate warnings. This suggests that firms in litigious industries provide these warnings defensively (to avoid lawsuits) rather than to signal actual economic risk. Smaller firms are also more likely to provide these boilerplate disclosures, potentially due to resource constraints leading them to copy "standard" disclosures rather than tailoring them to their actual low-risk profile. 4. To examine the determinant of withholding risk warnings on share price volatility risk The analysis of the "top quintile" volatility subsample identifies why risky firms might stay silent. By examining the "top quintile" of realized volatility, the study identified that firms with high financial leverage are most likely to withhold warnings. This implies a strategic incentive: highly levered firms may avoid highlighting their volatility to prevent alarming debt holders or increasing their cost of capital. Conversely, high analyst coverage and institutional investors reduce the likelihood of withholding. This suggests that external monitors effectively pressure managers into transparency, forcing them to disclose high-volatility risks they might otherwise hide. 5. To investigate market reactions to share price volatility risk disclosure We attempted to examine the market reactions to the initiation of a share price volatility risk factor warning and the stoppage of the disclosure of share price volatility risk factor. Due to the presence of multitude confounding variables present in 10-K filings, such as financial statements or MD&A disclosures which can distort market-based interpretations of individual risk factors, we did not incorporate them into our manuscript. To ensure higher validity, the project substituted this with standardized quantifiable benchmarks. By linking the qualitative disclosure directly to standard deviations of daily returns, the study provides a more objective assessment of informativeness than traditional market reaction tests alone could offer. 6. To explore managerial perspectives on the factors affecting share price volatility Textual analysis of the risk factor content revealed that managers perceive volatility through an operational and intermediary lens. Word cloud analysis identified that apart from stock-specific terms, "operating," "financial," and "analysts" are the most frequently cited words. Specifically, managers often supplement their disclosures with concerns regarding research analyst recommendations and meeting quarterly earnings estimates, viewing these as primary external drivers of their firm's stock risk. This contrasts with academic literature that often views analyst coverage as a stabilizer. Managers also tend to focus heavily on external factors ("earnings estimates," "valuation measures") and "competitors" rather than purely internal operational failures, perhaps in an attempt to share the blame with external forces. 7. To verify whether managers possess insights regarding the second-moment of future returns The project verified that managers possess limited predictive insights regarding future stock return volatility (the second-moment). Our current results indicate that the initiation of a risk factor warning corresponds with contemporaneous increases in volatility in the disclosure year, but not with future changes beyond that year. Furthermore, stoppage of the disclosure showed no association with future decreases in volatility. These findings collectively prove that these disclosures largely function as a summary of past events rather than a reflection of private managerial knowledge about future risk distributions. Overall, it confirms the disclosure is reactive, not proactive. As the SEC has made significant amendment on risk factor disclosure in 2020 (which is outside our initial sampling period) to improve the readability and usefulness of risk factor disclosures by focusing them on material, company-specific risks, and discouraging generic, boilerplate language, we have been working to expand our sample to include more recent years to examine the changes in risk factor disclosure practices after the new amendments. The disclosure on share price volatility risk can be used to examine the effect of the amendment due to its quantifiable benchmark. We are currently working on updating our manuscript with the more updated sample.

14503720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503720.value: We examine qualitative risk factor disclosures through the lens of share price volatility risk, a commonly disclosed risk factor that can be assessed through standardized quantifiable benchmarks. The primary research outcome confirms that these disclosures are generally informative regarding cross-sectional risk differences; firms with higher realized volatility are significantly more likely to disclose this risk factor. This association holds for idiosyncratic volatility as well, indicating that disclosures reflect firm-specific conditions rather than just market-wide trends. However, such disclosures are predominantly backward-looking. The statistical association between disclosure and volatility is significantly stronger for historical measures than for forward-looking ones, suggesting that managers use these disclosures to summarize past risks rather than to predict future volatility. This is reinforced by the finding that disclosures are highly "sticky," with a 92% persistence rate year-over-year. While the initiation of a disclosure correlates with a contemporaneous spike in volatility, the stoppage of disclosure does not reliably signal a decrease in risk. The study also identifies strategic determinants behind "boilerplate" and withheld disclosures. Small firms facing high litigation risks are found to provide boilerplate warnings even when their actual share price volatility is low, likely using the disclosure as a legal shield. Conversely, firms with high financial leverage are more likely to withhold this disclosure despite having high volatility, possibly to avoid signaling risk to creditors. However, the presence of external monitors, such as analysts and institutional investors, helps reduce this withholding behavior. Our textual analysis of managerial disclosures indicates that managers often mention the influence of external factors, specifically mentioning the impact of research analyst recommendations and the challenge of achieving quarterly earnings targets. These suggest managers often cite these external forces as drivers of their firm's share price volatility risk, potentially to mitigate the perception of internal failure. This finding also diverges from a significant body of academic literature that characterizes analyst coverage as a stabilizer of stock prices. The study significantly contributes to the literature on qualitative risk factor disclosure by utilizing share price volatility as a quantifiable benchmark. It advances the understanding of disclosure informativeness by distinguishing between backward-looking and forward-looking time horizons, revealing that these filings primarily summarize past risk exposures. Furthermore, by identifying systematic drivers of Type I and Type II errors—boilerplate and withheld disclosures—it provides crucial empirical evidence for current regulatory debates regarding disclosure modernization and the reduction of compliance-based reporting.

14503720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503720.value: As the SEC has made significant amendment on risk factor disclosure in 2020 (beyond our initial sampling period) to improve the readability and usefulness of risk factor disclosures by focusing them on material, company-specific risks, and discouraging generic, boilerplate language, we have been working hard to expand our sample to include more recent years to examine the changes in risk factor disclosure practices after the new amendments. We have tried to test and use the new genAI technology to help expand our sample to more recent time periods. However, due to concerns of AI hallucination, we are still conducting quality assurance work on the output. With more recent data samples, the disclosure on share price volatility risk can be used to examine the effect of new amendment due to the presence of quantifiable benchmark. After this is completed, we plan to submit our updated manuscript to a high-quality accounting journal for publication. Finally, our current study has not extensively looked into the granular details of risk factor descriptions under the header. With the proliferation of genAI, future research may tap into more granular disclosure details in risk factor descriptions to uncover more insights on risk factor disclosure quality.

14503720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503720.value: This research investigates the informativeness of qualitative risk factor disclosures in annual 10-K filings. By focusing on share price volatility—a risk that can be independently measured—the study provides a unique, quantifiable benchmark to test the value of these mandatory filings. While regulators and critics worry that these disclosures have become generic "boilerplate" items, this study show that such warnings are generally reflective of a firm’s actual risk profile. The decision to disclose volatility risk typically mirrors variations in share price fluctuations across different firms. However, these disclosures are often "sticky" over time and tend to be backward-looking, meaning they reflect past price instability rather than predicting future turbulence. While many use the disclosure to signal genuine risk exposure, certain small firms with high litigation risks may issue them as a compliance-based "boilerplate" even when their actual stock volatility is low. Ultimately, the project enhances our understanding of the nature and informativeness of mandated risk reporting, suggesting that while qualitative disclosures are informative cross-sectionally, they act more as a historical record of transparency than a forward-looking alert for investors.

14504320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504320.value: We evaluate the impact of environmental regulations on technological innovation. While there is growing evidence that environmental regulations help reduce pollution and improve the public health, evidence on the economic impact of environmental policy remains scarce and controversial. In this proposal, we focus on innovation, which is crucial for business competitiveness (Porter, 1992) and a key driver of a nation’s economic development (King and Levine, 1993), and investigate whether stringent environmental regulations enhance or impede innovative activities. Different views generate opposite predictions on how environmental regulations affect innovative outcomes. Professor Michael Porter of Harvard Business School suggests that stricter environmental policies incentivize firms to develop new technologies to reduce pollution or upgrade the production process that eliminate certain types of emissions. This view, known as the “Porter hypothesis”, indicates that stringent environmental regulations create incentives for invention, and thus have a positive impact on innovative output. The opposite view holds that strict environmental policies impose excessive economic burden on regulated industries, and thus stifle the invention of new technologies. According to this view, environmental compliance is very costly, and these large abatement investments and other compliance expenditures impede firms’ investment in innovative activities, such as a tightening in research and development (R&D) expenses, an attrition of human capital or other innovative resources. And this should be especially the case in the presence of capital market imperfections where firms face frictions in raising capital resources from external markets. Given these conflicting predictions, we aim to provide novel and systematic empirical evidence on how environmental regulations affect the invention of new technologies. To access this research question, we exploit regulatory shocks to individual plants induced by the policy change of the 1990 Clean Air Act (CAA) amendments. The 1990 amendments to the CAA expanded the national standards for ambient air quality and included PM10 as a new pollutant standard. Due to this policy change, plants emitting the regulated pollutants in nonattainment counties are subject to stricter regulatory oversight than other plants. Using (a) plant-specific variations in regulatory stringency, and (b) the detailed establishment-level data from National Establishment Time-Series Database that offers a complete spatial network of each firm, we compute a firm-specific exposure to the CAA regulatory shock, and evaluate the effect of a firm’s exposure to this regulatory change on its subsequent innovation. 本研究評估環境法規對技術創新的影響。儘管越來越多的證據表明環境法規有助於減少污染並改善公眾健康，但有關環境政策對經濟的影響仍有爭議。本研究將重點放在技術創新。創新對企業競爭力至關重要，也是國家經濟發展的關鍵驅動力，因此我們研究更嚴格的環境法規是否會增強或阻礙創新活動。對於環境法規如何影響創新成果，存在不同的理論觀點。哈佛商學院的邁克爾·波特教授認為，更嚴格的環境政策可以激勵企業開發新技術或升級生產工藝以減少排污。這種被稱為“波特假說”的觀點表明，嚴格的環境法規為創新創造了動力，因此對創新產生積極影響。相反的觀點認為，嚴格的環境政策給受管制的產業帶來了巨大的經濟負擔，從而不利於新技術的發明。根據該觀點，環境合規成本很高，而這些為減排而付出的大量投資和其他合規支出阻礙了企業對創新活動的投資（例如研究與開發費用的收緊，人力資本或其他創新資源的消耗）。在資本市場不完善的情況下，尤其是在企業從外部市場籌集資本面臨摩擦的情況下，情況尤其如此。鑑於這些不同的理論預測，我們旨在為有關環境法規如何影響技術創新提供新穎而係統的經驗證據。

14504320.label: Realisation of objectives
14504320.value: Objective 1: Our research achieves this objective by showing a strong connection between environmental regulation shocks induced by the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments and (a) research and development expenditures, (b) the quality of innovation outputs, measured by the scientific value and economic value of patents, and (c) product differentiation, using the text-based product similarity measure provided by Hoberg and Phillips (2010; 2016). Objective 2: We achieve this objective by examining the dynamic effects of the 1990 CAAA regulatory shock on firm innovation outcomes. We observe a significant effect only after, and not before, the treatment, suggesting that the change in investment and other outcomes is attributable to the implementation of more stringent regulations. In addition, we find that the 1990 CAAA regulatory shock has an enduring effect on corporate investment, innovative outputs, and product differentiation. Objectives 3, 4, & 5: After an extensive literature review, our study contributes to several strands of literature. First, we add new evidence to the debate on environmental regulation and economic consequences. Previous research yields mixed findings on how environmental regulations influence economic activities (Jaffe et al., 1995; Dechezleprêtre and Sato, 2017). Some studies find that stricter environmental rules impede industrial growth – for instance, polluting plants in non-attainment areas suffer output and productivity losses and employment declines (Greenstone, 2002; Walker, 2013), whereas others suggest improved worker productivity due to cleaner air (Graff Zivin and Neidell, 2012). In contrast, this paper evaluates the impact of the regulatory shocks on corporate investment, employment, innovation outputs, and product differentiation, and shows that a major environmental policy shock not only negatively impacts capital investment and employment but also stimulates innovation output and changes in product market behavior. In doing so, we extend this literature by uncovering a novel channel through which regulatory costs may be offset – technological innovation and product strategy adjustments. This integrated evidence offers a more complete understanding of how environmental regulations affect firm competitiveness and economic activities. Our study complements Aghion et al. (2016) and Brown, Martinsson, and Thomann (2022). Focusing on the automobile industry, Aghion et al. (2016) show that higher carbon taxes increase clean energy patenting. Brown, Martinsson, and Thomann (2022) show that higher taxes on SOx emissions induce firms to increase R&D investment, while producing no immediate surge in new patents. Our research distinguishes from theirs in at least three ways. First, rather than using country-level taxes on different emissions, our study exploits a different type of environmental policy – command-and-control regulations – and evaluates how firms respond to policies involving a more stringent pollution standard. Second, the 1990 CAA amendments enable us to use a firm-specific exposure to the regulatory shock, allowing comparison between treated and control firms operating in the same industry, country, and year, effectively holding constant many confounding factors. Third, we focus on the development of new products and technologies, proxied by patents and a text-based product similarity measure, as opposed to re-engineering production processes as in Brown, Martinsson, and Thomann (2022). We find that facing more stringent regulations, firms make strategic shifts in the product markets by shifting towards products more differentiated from competitors. Thus, our study provides novel evidence on the effects of environmental stringency and firm competitiveness. Finally, our work contributes to an extensive body of research on the determinants of corporate innovation activities, including R&D, technological and product innovation (e.g., Tian and Wang, 2011; He and Tian, 2013; Fang, Tian, and Tice, 2014; Chang et al., 2015). While existing research studied the impact of financial market development, legal and institutional determinants of innovation activities. we add to this literature by establishing a causal link between environmental regulations and subsequent innovation outcomes. We show that environmental regulations can prompt firms to invest in new technologies, produce higher quality patents, and generate more innovative products. Objective 6: To establish causality, our research exploits regulatory shocks to individual plants induced by the policy change of the Clean Air Act (CAA) Amendments of 1990, in which the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) adopted more stringent standards for ambient air quality and included PM10 as a new pollutant standard. Due to this policy change, plants emitting the regulated pollutants in nonattainment counties are subject to stricter regulatory oversight. Accordingly, we exploit plant-specific exposure to the regulatory shock and construct a firm-specific exposure to the regulatory-induced increase in environmental regulations. This empirical setting allows us to use the firm-specific exposure to the regulatory changes induced by the 1990 CAAA, and evaluate how changes in environmental regulatory stringency affect (a) corporate investment, (b) innovation outputs, and (c) product differentiation.

14504920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504920.value: While Apple actively expanded its labor force before launching iPhone 11, its main supplier in China, Foxconn, hired thousands of factory workers by offering an additional bonus of 4,500 RMB (approximately $675 USD). This example highlights the importance of human capital investment in supply-chain coordination where customers (e.g., Apple) and suppliers (e.g., Foxconn) adjust the numbers of employees simultaneously to meet the fluctuation of consumer demand in a product’s life cycle. At the same time, more than 50% of new employees of Foxconn were low-skill temporary assemblers, who works more than 10 hours per day but can be laid off easily without severance packages. This triggers a serious concern in labor ethics along the supply chain. Researchers have studied various aspects of supply-chain coordination, including inventory management (e.g., Cachon and Fisher, 2000), R&D and patents (e.g., Chu, Tian and Wang, 2019), and tax strategies (e.g., Cen, Maydew, Zhang and Zuo, 2018). While human capital investment is clearly an important aspect of supply-chain coordination, it has been underexplored in the academic literature primarily due to the lack of data. We aim to fill this gap in the literature by employing two novel datasets from Glassdoor and BGT (Burning Technologies Company). Specifically, the Glassdoor dataset provides information on potential job layoffs and searches of new jobs (i.e., the labor supply) while BGT dataset captures all job vacancies that companies have posted online (i.e., the labor demand). In both datasets, we are able to observe high-frequency fluctuations of employee “inflows and outflows” of customer and supplier firms and both datasets provide information that allows us to identify job types. In this project, my collaborators and I aim to investigate the following research questions. First, do changes in employment (e.g., recruiting and lay-offs) of customer and supplier firms comove? If yes, what are the determinants of this comovement? Second, how does supply-chain coordination of human capital investment affect corporate risk exposure? How do investors react when a supplier establishes relationships with important customers that require a high level of coordination in human capital investment? Finally, how do labor unions and labor regulations affect supply chain coordination in human capital investment, especially when the coordination involves employments and layoffs of low-skill temporary workers? Overall, we aim to understand the determinants of supply chain coordination in human capital investment and its impact on firms in important supply-chain relationships, their employees and investors, and regulators. 當蘋果公司在為iphone 11的銷售增雇人手的時候，蘋果公司在中國的主要供貨商——富士康公司——也同時以提供每人4500人民幣的額外雇傭獎金大力擴招勞工。這個例子提供一個供應鏈兩端企業的人力資本投資的協同效應的縮影：下遊企業(蘋果公司)和上遊供貨商(富士康)同時增加或者減少人力投資，來滿足消費者對產品的周期性需求變化。同時，由於富士康招聘的工人主要是低收入低技術的底層勞工：他們通常一天工作超過10個小時，臨時工沒有足夠的社會福利保障和勞動合同保障。由此，供應鏈人力資本協同效應可能會產生關於底層勞工福利的社會問題。 文獻中已經記載了很多基於供應鏈的協同效應，包括存貨管理(Cachon and Fisher, 2000), 技術和專利開發(Chu, Tian, and Wang, 2019), 和避稅策略(Cen, Maydew, Zhang and Zuo, 2018). 人力資本投資顯然是供應鏈協調效應中的重要一環，但是由於缺乏數據等各種原因沒有得到研究者足夠的重視。我們的研究項目將利用兩個新數據集來填補文獻上的這個空缺: Glassdoor數據主要提供了潛在的下崗員工網上的職位搜索行為（勞動力供給方）；BGT數據則提供了所有美國公司的網上招聘數據（勞動力需求方）。通過把兩個數據集的信息合並起來，我們能夠在高頻數據中觀察到勞動力在供應鏈協同效應中的進出和種類的變化。 在這個研究課題中，我和我的合作者計劃研究以下幾個問題：首先，下遊和上遊企業的雇傭行為高度相關嗎？如果確實如此，在橫截面上，什麽因素影響這樣的協同效應？再次，供應鏈人力資本協同效應如何影響公司的風險管理？投資者對供應鏈人力資本協同要求比較高的企業是如何定價的？最後，工會和勞動法規是如何看待和影響供應鏈人力資本協同效應的，特別是當該效應可能影響低收入低技術勞工福利的時候？總而言之，我們希望通過這個研究項目來理解分析供應鏈人力資本協同效應地決定因素，以及它對公司、勞工、投資者和監管方的影響。

14504920.label: Realisation of objectives
14504920.value: This project went extremely smoothly and all research objectives have been achieved. In the paper, "Human Capital Investment in Supply Chain Coordination: Evidence from Online Job Postings" (coauthored with Micheal Hertzel, Jing Wu, and Zi'Ang Wang), we have shown the following results responding to each objective: 1. For objective 1, we find a lead-lag effect of recruitment between principal customers and dependent suppliers. The effect cannot be explained by industry-level economic links; 2. For objective 2, we find that the supply-chain coordination is affected by relationship-specific investment, bargaining power, and the R&D intensity. 3. For objective 3, we find that, for specialized jobs, there exists a more intensive labor division along the supply chain (relative to firm-pairs without long-term relationships, which is efficient but at the cost of concentration risk); 4. For objective 4, our paper generates labor policy implications. For example, labor coordination along the supply chain leads to comovement of general occupations and specialization of industry-specific careers. 5. For objective 5, we find strong evidence showing that disruption of labor coordination along the supply chain generates poor performance, especially for dependent suppliers.

14504920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14504920.value: We present three sets of empirical findings in this study. First, in baseline regressions, we show a positive and significant contemporaneous correlation as well as a lead-lag effect in the $timing$ of job postings of principal customers and their dependent suppliers. While the results are insignificant for those identified in placebo relationship pairs. We employ these placebo pairs as a control mechanism throughout our analysis to account for the possibility that common market-wide or industry-specific factors may drive co-movement in recruiting activities. To address endogeneity concerns, we employ the outcomes of the customer H-1B visa lottery as an exogenous instrumental variable. By examining supply chain link formation ex-ante, we demonstrate that our findings are not driven by supply chain selection based on human capital investments. Next, we delve into the analysis of commonality in recruitment quality, focusing on the distinction between job postings that require general skills versus specialized skills. Jobs involving general skills pertain to positions associated with common tasks in various industries, such as sales and customer services. On the other hand, jobs involving specialized skills refer to positions that are particularly crucial and widely utilized within a specific industry, such as vehicle mechanics and technicians in the automobile sector. We construct a Euclidean distance measure to assess the similarity of skill requirements and uncover divergent patterns between jobs with general skills and those with specialized skills. Specifically, we find that supply chain partners are more inclined to recruit workers with similar general skills compared to firms in placebo relationship pairs. This outcome is to be expected, as common demand shocks diffuse along the supply chain. For instance, when a customer firm expands and recruits additional secretarial staff and customer service workers, its supplier firms are more likely to follow suit. However, concerning jobs that necessitate specialized skills, we observe that supply chain partners are more inclined to recruit workers with ``distant" specialized skills compared to firms in placebo relationship pairs. For example, when an automobile company recruits more automobile designers, one of its suppliers, a vehicle glass producer, may simultaneously be seeking glass scientists. This finding aligns with the notion that long-term supply chain relationships facilitate product specialization and labor division between upstream and downstream partners. Lastly, we explore the economic implications of suppliers' coordination of human capital investment with their major customers by examining the effects of disruptions to hiring coordination. To account for the potential endogeneity arising from unobserved economic factors that influence both recruitment decisions and real economic outcomes, we leverage exogenous shocks to hiring resulting from H-1B visa lottery outcomes. Our analysis reveals that ``unlucky" lottery outcomes, characterized by a significantly higher failure rate than the average, disrupt relationship-specific investments in human capital. This disruption is evident in the reduced labor coordination in recruiting workers with general skills and the diminished labor division in recruiting workers with specialized skills. By employing the H-1B visa lottery outcomes of both trade partners as an instrumental variable, we demonstrate that our measures capturing labor coordination in general skills and in specialized skills, particularly the latter, can predict the likelihood of relationship termination, as well as suppliers' future sales and market valuation.

14504920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14504920.value: 1. Build a deeper theoretical foundation for the labor coordination along the supply chain; 2. Find a better identification strategy for the labor shocks, to pin down causal inferences; 3. Use more dimensions in the data, such as geographical locations and skill specifications, to identify economic mechanisms more clearly.

14504920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504920.value: Using granular online job posting data, we examine the coordination of human capital investment between long-term bilateral supply chain partners. Using a unique dataset of online job postings from publicly listed firms and their supply chains, we show a significant and positive contemporaneous correlation and lead-lag effect between the job postings of principal customers and their dependent suppliers, which is stronger for supplier firms with higher dependence on their principal customers. Relying on the random outcomes of H-1B visa lotteries as an instrumental variable, we establish the causal relationship for suppliers' labor hiring catering to their major customers. Moreover, supply chain partners are more likely to recruit workers with similar general skills and distinct specialized skills simultaneously. At last, we find that the disruption of such relationship-specific human capital investment leads to negative economic consequences, i.e., higher supply chain discontinuity risk, lower future sales, and weaker market performance, along the supply chain. Overall, our paper shows that long-term supply chain relationships lead to human capital coordination, which provides valuable insights into the potential risks and benefits for policymakers, managers, and investors in understanding the importance of relationship-specific human capital investment in supply chain coordination.

14505120.value: 消費者對避稅的反應：共同基金的證據

14505120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505120.value: While survey evidence suggests that reputational concern is one of the important factors for corporate tax planning (Graham et al. 2013), empirical evidence has been limited. Prior literature has documented that, consistent with the loss of reputation from corporate tax avoidance, firms engaging in tax avoidance receive negative media attention and lower stock valuation and this reputational concern results in “under-sheltering puzzle.” We focus on the product market and investigate whether and how consumer fund choices are affected by the tax avoidance of mutual fund management companies. We predict that loss of reputation of fund management companies as a result of tax avoidance will be followed by declines in net fund flows. We also predict that the effects will be more pronounced in settings where consumers are more conscious about ESG issues, and when consumers easily recognize the affiliation between the fund management company and the mutual funds. Our findings not only will have implications for reputational costs of tax avoidance in financial industry, but also will contribute to the mutual funds literature, which has received little attention so far from accounting researchers, as well as the tax avoidance literature. 儘管調查證據表明聲譽問題是公司稅收籌劃的重要因素之一（Graham等，2013），但經驗證據卻很有限。先前的文獻記載，與避免公司避稅聲譽受損相一致，從事避稅行為的公司受到媒體的負面關注並降低了股票估值，這種聲譽關注導致“避險之謎”。我們專注於產品市場，調查共同基金管理公司的避稅行為是否以及如何影響消費者基金的選擇。我們預計，由於避稅而導致基金管理公司的聲譽損失將導致淨資金流量下降。我們還預測，在消費者更加了解ESG問題的環境中，以及消費者容易認識到基金管理公司與共同基金之間的隸屬關係時，這種影響將更加明顯。我們的發現不僅會對金融業避稅的聲譽成本產生影響，而且還將為共同基金文獻做出貢獻，到目前為止，會計研究人員和避稅文獻一直很少受到共同基金文獻的關注。

14505220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505220.value: 公司的風險決定了公司在經濟週期中的財務和投資決定。直覺上來說，高風險的公司通常貸款較少因為他們貸款後有更高的違約和破產風險。 但是，並不是所有的風險都是相同的。公司的風險可以被細分為系統性風險和非系統性風險。那些大量生產產品和向整個經濟提供服務的公司通常有較高的系統性風險。當整個經濟下行時，這些公司的運營收益也跟著下行。相反，那些和整體經濟關聯較小的公司受到市場的影響較小。這些“非系統性業務”在市場下行的時候會給公司增加收益來抵消市場下行造成的收益降低。換句話說，當市場處在下行中時，非系統性風險幫助公司減小了來自市場下行帶來的影響。因此，非系統性風險在總的系統中所佔的比例，在公司融資決定中扮演了一個很重要的角色。 在這個研究中，我們將研究一家公司的風險結構如何影響公司的資本結構，也就是負債在公司資產中的佔比。和上面所述的一致，我們發現那些有著更高的非系統性風險的公司通常有著更高的負債，因為他們不容易受到市場下行的影響。為了闡述這種現象，我們建立一個動態模型去理解公司的風險結構對資本結構的影響。 在檢驗我們的猜想的時候通常會遇到反向因果的問題，一個在實證公司金融研究中普遍存在的問題。反向因果指的是在實證研究中很難確定是風險結構決定資本結構還是資本結構決定了風險結構。公司可能根據風險結構來確定最優的貸款數量。然後也可能是，在貸款數量被確定之後，如果公司的收益下降，那麼他們將會有動機去增加高非系統性風險的投資來進行風險轉移。因此，在實證研究中，很難確定風險結構和資本結構之間的因果關係。 我們在研究中並沒有使用流行的（偽）自然實驗方法，而是審慎的使用結構估計來檢驗我們的模型。具體來說，我們估計模型，根據被估計出來的模型產生模擬數據，再對模擬數據使用雙重差分回歸（DID）。這個被模擬出來的經濟比起真實數據更像是一個沒有被干擾的實驗室。在這個實驗室中，因為模擬數據是我們生成的，所以風險結構和資本結構之間的因果關係是已知的。 因此，我們的結構估計方法克服了內生性問題和部分公司特征不可觀測的問題。並且其提供了一個理想的實驗場所來驗證我們的猜想和評估DID方法的有效性。

I have diligently worked towards achieving these objectives. In the report, I will discuss my progress and completion for each objective as follows: First Revised Objective: Build a Structural Model of Credit Risk to Understand the Capital Structure The continuous-time structural model of credit risk has undergone significant evolution throughout this project. The previous model proved too complicated for efficient implementation after several attempts. To address this, I proposed a more streamlined continuous-time model of credit risk. As noted in the justification for this revised objective, this simplification allows us to conduct structural estimation while maintaining methodological rigor and addressing the practical challenges associated with numerical computations. The simplified model presented in this report is based on the industry-leading CreditGrades model. This model assumes a zero growth rate for the underlying firm values and introduces uncertainty regarding the default boundary. This uncertainty helps to alleviate the well-known "credit risk puzzle". We extend this model by incorporating heterogeneity in payout rates, as detailed in Sections 2.1 and 2.2. The average payout rate is approximately 5% in the data, and introducing heterogeneous payout rates significantly enhances the model's performance in aligning model-implied credit spreads with actual observed spreads. Second Revised Objective: Perform Estimation for the Credit Risk Model We have conducted estimation for the structural model at the bond level on a monthly basis, calculating model-implied bond prices and credit spreads. This revised objective has been successfully implemented, as the computational intensity of the new credit risk model has been reduced without compromising rigor and accuracy. In Section 2.3 of the attached paper, I provide detailed descriptions of the procedure for estimating the extended credit risk model. Although the model performs reasonably well, discrepancies exist between actual and model-generated credit spreads across firms. Since the model utilizes observed equity prices as the state variable, we refer to the model-implied credit spreads as equity-implied credit spreads. The difference between the actual and equity-implied credit spreads is termed the debt-equity spread (DES) at both the bond and firm levels. We explore the causes of this measure and examine its impact on the relative mispricing between stock and bond markets. Additionally, we investigate how non-financial firms exploit the relative mispricing of their own stocks and bonds to issue equity and debt, ultimately influencing corporate finance and capital structure. Third Revised Objective: Construct a Novel Proxy for Market Segmentation In addition to a risk-based measure, the risk structure, we constructed a novel proxy for market segmentation: the debt-equity spread. This new measure serves as a proxy for the segmentation between debt and equity markets, contributing valuable insights into the decision-making processes underlying corporate financing choices. The execution of this revised objective has been successful. However, the final version of the paper will place greater emphasis on the debt-equity spread as the proxy for market segmentation. In Appendix B.5 of the attached output, I include findings related to the other measure, risk structure. In summary, I sincerely appreciate your approval of the revised objectives, which I have successfully implemented.

14505220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505220.value: The project has yielded numerous intriguing findings that extend beyond the original objectives. The key findings related to the aforementioned objectives are highlighted as follows: The first set of empirical results pertains to the performance of the extended credit risk model, addressing the first and second objectives. The extended model is detailed in Sections 2.1 and 2.2, with the estimation process outlined in Section 2.3. The main finding indicates that the difference between actual and model-implied credit spreads ranges from less than -400 basis points to 800 basis points. Consequently, our extended credit risk model has demonstrated strong empirical performance by incorporating heterogeneity in payout rates. Additionally, we construct the debt-equity spread based on the differences between actual and model-implied credit spreads. The second set of results directly relates to the third revised objective. We utilize the new measure, the debt-equity spread, to assess market segmentation and examine corporate financing decisions. In Section 3, our results suggest that firms with a high debt-equity spread (DES) engage in more capital structure arbitrage activities concerning their own securities. These firms are more likely to issue equity and retire debt, leading to a lower capital structure when their equity is perceived as relatively overpriced compared to their debt. These findings imply that potential valuation gaps between debt and equity should be a crucial consideration in studies of corporate financing decisions, with notable implications for cross-sectional stock and bond returns. Additionally, we examine the explanatory power of the other measure, risk structure, in Appendix B.5 of the attached output. Our findings reveal that the (idiosyncratic) risk structure encourages more debt issuance than equity issuance, resulting in a higher capital structure. This outcome aligns with our intuition that idiosyncratic volatility enables firms to hedge against downside risk. However, we have decided to place less emphasis on this measure and its related results in the evolution of this project. In summary, this project has generated a wealth of interesting outcomes that extend beyond the stated objectives. We have produced a high-quality paper titled "The Debt-Equity Spread," which has been accepted for presentation at major conferences, namely, the American Finance Association annual meetings, and other high-quality international conferences. Furthermore, the paper has received a revise-and-resubmit invitation from the Journal of Finance. I sincerely appreciate your support and have acknowledged the funding assistance from RGC in the paper.

14505220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505220.value: Extending the structural model to take into account jump risks (see, e.g., Bai et al., 2020), secondary market liquidity (see e.g., Chen et al., 2018), and more detailed information about the capital structure (such as debt seniority, callability, or maturity structure, as in Chen et al., 2021) could further improve the quality of the valuation gap measure. We leave these considerations for future research.

14505220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505220.value: Firms raise capital to finance their investment and operating costs by issuing stocks and bonds, leading to heterogeneous capital structures. In making financing decisions, firms may exploit capital structure arbitrage opportunities based on the prices of their own stocks and bonds. We introduce a measure, the debt-equity spread (DES), defined as the difference between actual and equity-implied credit spreads, to evaluate market segmentation. Our findings indicate that high-DES firms engage in more capital structure arbitrage activities concerning their own securities. These firms are more likely to issue equity and retire debt, resulting in a lower capital structure. Notably, while they may capitalize on the mispricing of their financial securities—which are less costly to adjust—managers do not alter their long-term physical and R&D investment decisions. The DES, arising from market segmentation, induces opposing movements in stock and bond returns. These findings on corporate financing behavior and asset pricing dynamics suggest that the DES effectively captures the relative mispricing between debt and equity, highlighting the prevalence of segmentation between these markets at the firm level.
