14601420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601420.value: First, as I reviewed the unearthed documents from Wuyi Square, these archives confirmed the population growth and mobility during the early Eastern Han period which aligned with the economic prosperity of the Changsha Commandery along the Xiang River and neighboring commanderies. Due to better job market and arable land availability, population nearby were attracted to Linxiang, the capital city of Changsha, for livelihood. Evidences showed that Linxiang metropolitan served as the logistics and business center at Jingzhou荊州Region. Changsha’s commercial network also extended to Lingling 零陵, Cangwu 蒼梧, Jiaozhi 交趾 and Nanhai 南海. Although Changsha was not counted as a major douhui 都會 in both Hanshu and Houhanshu, active merchants, huge amounts of cargo transportation and commercial litigations showed that Linxiang had already jumped up to be one of the national markets among Wan 宛, Suo 索, Jiangling 江陵, Linyuan 臨沅, Panyu 番禺and Luoyang 洛陽 etc. Second, more and more natural settlement qiu丘 were recorded in the documents from Wuyi Square. The establishment of Qiu can be traced back to early Eastern Han dynasty. During the early Eastern Han period, northern China was hit by warfare and natural disasters that pushing people to leave their homeland and causing dramatic increase of population in the south. Eventually the Eastern Han government allowed refugees to settle down and cultivate the imperial lands in remote areas that were governed by central government. Third, I hold that Linxiang became a multi-function metropolis during Eastern Han period. It integrated and crowded with administration, commerce, logistics, craft manufacture and residence into a very limited environment. The fire incidents reported in Wuyi Square documents reflected the damage to government property, commoner dwellings, warehouses, and disaster to many families. Similar fire cases frequently broken out at Qi Kingdom 齊國 and Cheng Duo 成都, they all had the same environmental characters, such as dense buildings, over-populated and illegal smelting industry.

14601420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601420.value: I have retired and will not going to teach any course. But I am now working on two book projects, namely Imperial Governance: Bureaucracy and Social Control as Seen from the Qin-Han Excavated Manuscripts 經國治民：秦漢簡牘中的官僚與社會控制 and The Society and Population of the Linxiang City: The Exploration of the Eastern Han Manuscripts from Wuyi Square 長沙臨湘社會與人口：五一廣場東漢簡牘研究. The former will evaluate the structure and integration of imperial orders, edicts, bureaucracy and control system of the Han government. The latter will be the research product of this project. By including those newly released Wuyi Square manuscripts, I shall expand the existing articles to cover issues such as population management and the conflicts between Han people and the manyi 蠻夷, such Wuling barbarians 武陵蠻 in south China.

14601420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601420.value: The author analyzed concrete cases of the unearthed documents from Wuyi Square. By examining concrete cases of the unearthed documents from Wuyi Square, the author analyzed, a) the impacts of population growth and economic prosperity on social life of the Linxiang community, and b) the impacts of water navigation of Xiang River and its tributaries on the commercial growth and population mobility to Linxiang County and Changsha Commandery. The author published 5 articles which explored Linxiang’s population growth, commercial prosperity, and her role of national market, as well as the development of natural settlement of qiu 丘 in remoted regions. The author also co-edited a book, namely, 臨湘社會的管治磐基：長沙五一廣場東漢簡牘探索The Foundation of Han Governance in Linxiang Society: A Study of the Texts from Wuyi Square. This collection has meticulous discussion on local governance, legal procedures, imperial edicts, spatial structure and lineage settlement. In brief, this project analyzed major changes of Linxiang from a local administrative city to a national metropolis that connected southern and northern China.

14601720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14601720.value: 中日戰爭時期中國現代派對歐洲戰爭文學的跨文化閱讀(1937-1945)

14601720.label: Project Objectives
14601720.value: To re-examine the complexity of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature from transcultural and trans-historical perspectives. Previous studies on Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature focused mainly on writers’ anti-war poetry, prose and fiction as well as their national purposes. It was not until the last three decades that scholars started re-examining the particular function of literary translation during the war-time period. Translating war literature has been considered as an important resistance strategy in the anti-war movements in nationalist-controlled areas, communist-controlled “liberated areas” and occupied areas of China during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Scholars have successfully argued the contribution of Chinese left-wing writers’ translated war literature, especially Russian-Soviet literature, to the construction of national identity (Chen 2005, Liao 2015, Xiong 2017). However, discussions on Chinese modernists’ attachment to the leftist ideology and their contribution to the war-resistance literature have been very limited. The investigation of this large corpus of Chinese modernists’ criticism and translations of European war literature from five countries including France, Germany, Spain, Poland and Russia, and in four languages (English, French, Spanish and Russian) in a particular historical context of China in the 1930s and 1940s, will certainly give us a better understanding of the complexity of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature. To investigate Chinese modernist writers’ reception of literary and political ideas demonstrated in European war literature. The proposed project will focus on three major Chinese modernist “writers-translators-editors,” namely Shi Zhecun (1905-2033), Ye Lingfeng (1905-1975) and Dai Wangshu (1905-1950). Despite the very different political-historical-cultural contexts of China and Europe, they introduced and translated over 200 titles of war literature concerning different wars such as the Franco-Prussian War (1870-1871), the First World War (1914-1918), the Russian Civil War (1917-1922), the Polish-Soviet War (1919-1921), the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939) and the Great Patriotic War in Russia (1941-1945). Deeply inspired by views of European intellectuals on aesthetics and politics, the Chinese modernists re-examine their own position of the controversial issue stemming from literature’s role in politics during the Anti-Japanese resistance period. Typical examples include Dai Wangshu’s translations of Alphonse Daudet’s short-stories concerning the Franco-Prussian War and his criticism on British, Spanish and French war literatures. His emphasis on artistic forms without sacrificing the exploration of humanity distinguished him from the mainstream idea of “Literature for National Defence” (Guofang wenxue) promoted by the Chinese Communist Party in the 1930s. To examine Chinese modernist writers’ reinterpretation of European war literature in the historical context of the Second Sino-Japanese war. In order to introduce diverse perspectives on war politics to the Chinese intellectual community, Chinese modernist writers discussed and translated war literature by European writers of different political views. It includes the works of humanists and pacifists (e.g. Romain Rolland), socialists (e.g. Henri Barbusse), anti-fascists (e.g. Heinrich Mann), communists (e.g. Rafael Alberti, Pyotr Pavlenko, Yuri Libedinsky) and fellow-traveller writers (e.g. Vsevolod Ivanov). By examining their criticism and translations, this project will look into Chinese modernists’ reconstruction of European intellectuals’ literary-political figures and their reinterpretation of European war literature in the historical context of the Second Sino-Japanese war. Representative examples include Ye Lingfeng’s translation of Barbusse’s famous anti-war novel Le Feu (Under Fire) and his reinterpretation about the author’s perspectives on war, internationalism and proletarian revolution, in response to the Anti-Japanese resistance movement. To investigate Chinese modernists’ translation strategy of war literature under the political censorship imposed by the British colonial government of Hong Kong. After the Japanese occupation of Shanghai in 1937, Ye Lingfeng and Dai Wangshu both went into exile in Hong Kong and became editors and contributors of important literary supplements of newspapers including Sing Dao Daily, Lih Pao and Overseas Chinese Daily. Different from the political situation of most occupied areas in China, Hong Kong was a British crown colony at the time. The Chinese modernists, making use of the special political position of the city, continued to promote Anti-Japanese resistance movement. Through their criticism and translations of war literature published in Hong Kong and other cities, this project will investigate how they tried to seek their freedom of speech by means of literary translation under the pressure of pro-Japanese “Peace Movement” led by Wang Jingwei as well as the severe political censorship imposed by the British colonial government of Hong Kong during the wartime. To investigate the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese literary modernity in the war context. Different from their western counterparts, Chinese modernists were never consigned to the realm of pure aestheticism. Chinese modernist literature found itself nurtured in the social-historical context of the Second Sino-Japanese War. Treating Shi Zhecun, Ye Lingfeng and Dai Wangshu as wartime Chinese modernists, this project will extend the scope of research into Anti-Japanese war literature of China by including the contribution from modernist writers. It will certainly deepen our understanding of the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese literary modernity.

14601720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601720.value: Since the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War, a great number of Chinese intellectuals immediately devoted their work to national salvation. European war literature, especially Russian-Soviet literature, became an important way for them to inspire a bellicose spirit as well as to nurture their own war-narratives for their national purpose. Previous studies have largely demonstrated the significance of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature, mainly by left-wing writers, and its contribution to the construction of national identity. However, discussions on Chinese modernists’ attachment to the leftist ideology and their contribution to the war-resistance literature have been very limited. A large corpus of Chinese modernists’ criticism and translations of European war literature concerning the Franco-Prussian War, the First World War, the Polish-Soviet War, the Spanish Civil War, the Russian Civil War and the Great Patriotic War in the particular historical context of China have been overlooked, thus making it a missing chapter in the study of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature as well as modernist literature. This project aims at carrying out research into the Chinese modernists’ reading, criticism, translation and reinterpretation of the European war literature from transcultural and trans-historical perspectives. It will focus on three major Chinese modernist “writers-translators-editors,” namely Shi Zhecun, Ye Lingfeng and Dai Wangshu, who have introduced and translated over 200 titles of European war literature from five countries and in four languages. By examining their criticism and translations, this project will examine how they reinterpret the war literature by European writers of different political views, including those of humanists and pacifists (e.g. Romain Rolland), socialists (e.g. Henri Barbusse), anti-fascists (e.g. Heinrich Mann), communists (e.g. Rafael Alberti, Pyotr Pavlenko, Yuri Libedinsky) and fellow-traveller writers (e.g. Vsevolod Ivanov). It will also investigate how they use the translations of war literature as a strategy in the anti-Japanese resistance movement in Hong Kong under the pressure of pro-Japanese “Peace Movement” as well as the severe political censorship imposed by the British colonial government. This project will bring forward an important but long-neglected chapter to the study of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature and shed new light on the association between this study and European ideological trends. It will extend the research scope of Chinese reception of European war literature and its literary-political ideas by including the contribution from modernist writers. It will also deepen our understanding of the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese literary modernity in a war context. 1937年中日戰爭爆發，促使大量的中國知識份子紛紛投身救國事業。歐洲戰爭文學，尤其是俄蘇文學，遂成為中國知識份子建構抗戰文學的理想資源並鼓舞群眾的抗戰意識。過往學者的研究集中於中國左翼作家書寫的抗戰文學及其對於建構國族身份認同的重要意義。然而，他們甚少討論中國現代派與左翼文藝思潮之間的複雜關係以及現代派作家對抗戰文學的貢獻。因此，中國現代派因應中國特殊的歷史語境而大量評論和翻譯有關普法戰爭（Franco-Prussian War, 1870-1871）、第一次世界大戰（First World War, 1914-1918）、俄國內戰（Russian Civil War, 1917-1922）、波蘇戰爭（Polish-Soviet War, 1919-1921）、西班牙內戰（Spanish Civil War, 1936-1939）以及蘇聯的衛國戰爭（Great Patriotic War, 1941-1945）等歐洲戰爭文學作品，一直被長期忽視，實為中國抗戰文學以及中國現代派文學研究之中的遺珠。 本計劃旨從跨文化和跨歷史的角度切入，探討中國現代派對歐洲戰爭文學的閱讀、評論、翻譯及再現。本計劃以中國現代派「作者—譯者—編輯」羣——施蟄存、葉靈鳳和戴望舒為考察對象，探討他們引介並翻譯來自五個國家、以四種語言書寫、合共逾二百部歐洲戰爭文學著作，如何再現由不同政治傾向的歐洲作家撰寫的戰爭文學，其中包括人文主義及和平主義者如羅曼．羅蘭（Romain Rolland），社會主義者如巴比塞（Henri Barbusse），反法西斯主義者如海因里希．曼（Heinrich Mann），共產主義者如阿爾維蒂（Rafael Alberti）、巴甫連科（Pyotr Pavlenko）、里別進思基（Yuri Libedinsky）以及「同路人」作家如伊凡諾夫（Vsevolod Ivanov）。本計劃將進一步研究中國現代派如何利用歐洲戰爭文學的翻譯作為「內在抵抗」的策略，支援在香港同時面對親日的「和平運動」以及英國殖民政府嚴苛的政治審查的雙重壓力之下掙扎求存的抗日文藝運動。 本計劃試圖點明中國抗日戰爭文學與歐洲文藝思潮之間的連繫，以期填補抗戰文藝研究長年遺漏的重要版塊。此外，本計劃通過重新考量中國現代派作家對歐洲戰爭文學乃至其中文學與政治思想的接受情況，開拓抗日戰爭文學的研究視野，並再次強調戰爭語境下中國文學現代性發展的混雜性和跨文化特點。

14601720.label: Realisation of objectives
14601720.value: Research Project Objectives: Our research project explores the engagement of Chinese modernists with European war literature through a transcultural and trans-historical lens. Specifically, our objectives are: (i) to re-examine the complexity of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature from transcultural and trans-historical perspectives, (ii) to investigate Chinese modernist writers’ reception of literary and political ideas demonstrated in European war literature, (iii) to examine Chinese modernist writers’ reinterpretation of European war literature in the historical context of the Second Sino-Japanese war, (iv) to investigate Chinese modernists’ translation strategy of war literature under the political censorship imposed by the British colonial government of Hong Kong, and (v) to investigate the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese literary modernity in the war context. As of the submission of this completion report, our research team has successfully met all the outlined objectives. Establishment of Archive: The research team has established a comprehensive archive that documents the engagement of Chinese modernists with European and American war literature during the Second Sino-Japanese War. This archive includes: (i) Chinese modernists’ translations of war literature originating from France, Germany, Spain, Poland, Russia, and the United States by Chinese modernists; (ii) Extensive critical essays and analyses by Chinese modernists on European war literature across various conflicts; (iii) Writings on Anti-Japanese War Literature: writings and critical reviews by Chinese modernists on Anti-Japanese war literature contemporary to their time. The database has provided a robust foundation for our research, enabling detailed investigations into how Chinese modernist writers received and interpreted literary and political ideas from European war literature. Publication of a Critical Anthology of Resistance Literature: Based on extensive research and analysis drawn from the database, an anthology titled “Across Eurasia: Translation and Selection of Resistance Literature from Hong Kong Newspapers (1937-1945)” is scheduled for publication by the end of May 2024. While earlier studies of Chinese resistance literature have focused on leftist writers and their use of British colony - Hong Kong’s “safe haven” during the war period, this book takes a different approach by examining (i) two of the most important newspaper literary supplements of the time: Xingzuo (Constellation) of the Sing Tao Daily, edited by Dai Wangshu, and Wenyi (Literature and Art) of the Tai Kun Pao, edited by Xiao Qian and Yang Gang, as well as (ii) materials from the Japanese edition of the Honkon Nippō during the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong. The anthology includes a preface, a critical introduction, and features selected and translated articles, accompanied by annotations, spanning over 550,000 words. These once-neglected source materials are indeed some missing pieces of a grand picture that reveal the transnational and transcultural perspectives of Chinese Anti-Japanese war literature. Across Eurasia is particularly notable for being the first anthology to translate and compile materials from the Japanese edition of the Honkon Nippō during the Japanese occupation, which illuminates Japanese literary and cultural policies towards Hong Kong during the occupation. Publication of Peer-reviewed Journal Papers: Derived from the research project’s findings, the PI has published three peer-reviewed academic papers in international academic journals including Modern Chinese Literature (Taipei), Literature (Shanghai) and Historical Studies of Modern Literature (Beijing). The paper titled “On Ye Lingfeng’s Editorship of the Literary Supplement Yanlin and his Translation of Red Planes Fly East” examines Ye Lingfeng’s reception and translations of European war literature during the Sino-Japanese War, focusing on Red Planes Fly East by Russian communist author Piotr Pavlenko, as a nuanced intellectual engagement with the wartime milieu. Another paper entitled “Transnational Literature and Art of Resistance: A Study of Orienta Kuriero (1938-39), a Hong Kong Esperanto Magazine” examines the nationalist Esperanto magazine’s affiliations with Japan, Korea, Mainland China, and Hong Kong’s resistance movements, situating these within the broader frameworks of political and literary translation as well as linguistic analysis. It further explores how Orienta Kuriero fostered a translingual practice during the wartime period, thereby crafting a transnational and cross-cultural narrative of resistance. Publication of Peer-reviewed Papers at International Conferences: The PI has actively participated in academic forums (Germany, Czech, and Hong Kong), presenting five conference papers centered on the research project. The paper titled “Literary Translation as Strategy of Resistance: Ye Lingfeng’s Transcultural Reading of European War Literature during the Second Sino-Japanese War,” explored how Ye Lingfeng’s literary translations served as a form of cultural and political resistance. Another significant contribution was the paper “Wars and Ideas: A Transcultural Reading of European War-narratives in Colonial Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War,” examining the influence of European war narratives on Chinese resistance literature during a tumultuous historical period. Additionally, the PI presented two other papers focusing on the transcultural aspects of Chinese revolutionary and resistance literature, which delved into the transnational and transcultural interrelations between literary canon formation, language use, and political dynamics in times of conflict. Organization of International Conference: Despite the challenges posed by travel restrictions and social distancing measures during the COVID-19 pandemic, the PI, in collaboration with the Institute of Literature and Philosophy at Academia Sinica, successfully co-organized an international conference on “Transcultural Dialogues, Negotiations, and Modernity in Sinophone Literature and Culture” at CUHK in December 2022. It brought together thirty scholars from Japan, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, provided a crucial platform for the research team and attending scholars specializing in transcultural studies from across America, Europe, and Asia, and facilitated meaningful exchanges of ideas. Knowledge Transfer (i) Development of a New Postgraduate Course (MPhil/PhD): The PI has established a new course for MPhil and PhD students titled “Selected Topics in Modern Chinese Literature: War, Revolution, and Transcultural Modernity.” This course, introduced in 2023, explores the impact of European revolution and war literature on Twentieth-century Chinese modernist literature, focusing on its transcultural reception and reinterpretation. (ii) Enhancement of an Undergraduate Course: Drawing on insights from the research project, the PI has integrated a new research topic into the existing undergraduate course “Modern Literary Criticism” in 2022. It re-evaluates the transcultural and hybrid qualities of Chinese literary modernity during the wartime era, providing undergraduate students with a nuanced understanding of modernist literature development. (iii) Guest Speaker in Public Lecture Series: The PI served as a guest speaker in two lecture series hosted by the Institute of Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Science at National Taiwan University and the Hong Kong Museum of Coastal Defence. The PI delivered “Negotiation and Inner Resistance: The Modernist School and European War Literature during the Sino-Japanese War” in November 2022 and “From the Homeland to the World: Literary Editing and Translation by Southern Intellectuals during the War of Resistance” in April 2024. Both lectures shared key project findings with a broad audience and are available on a YouTube channel for wider access. (URL: https://www.ihs.ntu.edu.tw/web/events/events_in_01.jsp?lang=tw&np_id=NP1667437436698 ; https://hk.coastaldefence.museum/en/web/mcd/literartureandotherpublications.html) (iv) Postgraduate students trained: Per the requirements of the RGC, we have uploaded the thesis title pages for six MPhil and PhD students. These students, partially trained by this research project on transcultural studies, include both graduates and those anticipated to graduate shortly.

14601720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601720.value: 1. The anthology titled “Across Eurasia: Translation and Selection of Resistance Literature from Hong Kong Newspapers (1937-1945)” is scheduled for publication by the end of May 2024. This comprehensive volume includes a preface, a critical introduction, and features selected and translated articles, accompanied by annotations. It spans over 550,000 words and examines the portrayal of European wars, political scenarios, and resistance literature during the Sino-Japanese War through the lens of Hong Kong newspaper literary supplements. It explores the role these supplements played in shaping national identity during wartime. Notably, this anthology is the first to translate and compile content from the Japanese edition of the Honkon Nippō, shedding light on Japanese cultural and literary policies in Hong Kong during their occupation and providing insights into their perspective on “Greater East Asian Literature” within the war context. 2. The project has yielded significant scholarly contributions, resulting in the publication of three peer-reviewed journal articles, including “On Ye Lingfeng’s Editorship of the Literary Supplement Yanlin and his Translation of Red Planes Fly East,” “Transnational Literature and Art of Resistance: A Study of Orienta Kuriero (1938-39), a Hong Kong Esperanto Magazine,” and “A Letter from Dai Wangshu to Réne Étiemble: On Translation of André Malraux’s Novels during the Second Sino-Japanese War”. These papers delve into various aspects of literary resistance and translation during the tumultuous period of the Second Sino-Japanese War. For more detailed information, please refer to Part C8. 3. The PI has actively disseminated the research findings through presentations at five international conferences across Germany, Czech Republic, and Hong Kong. The topics of these refereed conference papers include “Literary Translation as Strategy of Resistance: Ye Lingfeng’s Transcultural Reading of European War Literature during the Second Sino-Japanese War,” “Wars and Ideas: A Transcultural Reading of European War-narratives in Colonial Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War,” “Literary Canons and Warfare: A Sino-French Perspective on the Chinese Revolution and Literature,” and “ ‘Transparent” Language and Politics in the Context of War: The International Esperanto Magazine Orienta Kuriero and its Chinese Antiwar Literature and Art” etc. These presentations have contributed to advancing the academic dialogue on literary resistance and European war literature translation during wartime periods. Please refer to Part C9 for further details.

14601720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601720.value: Building on insights from our recent research project, we propose a study on Esperanto resistance literature in Hong Kong during World War II, a critical link between East Asia and Europe. This research, adopting a translingual and transcultural lens, will unfold in three stages. In the first stage, we will compile an archive of Esperanto magazines and writings from Hong Kong and other East Asian countries, alongside critical articles about the Esperanto movement in Asia during the war. In the second stage, we will examine how Hong Kong’s Esperanto publications, such as Orienta Kuriero (Eastern Courier), Tagiĝo (Daybreak), and the Bulletin of Hong Kong New Script Learning Society, diverge from the dominant nationalist anti-war Esperanto magazines in Mainland China in the wartime. The final stage will explore how these magazines fostered a transcultural resistance literature, influenced by European Esperantists and incorporating translations and transcriptions of anti-war works from China, Japan, and Korea. This project offers a unique lens to reevaluate the complex interplay between cosmopolitan ideals, which transcend nationalities and ethnicities, and the nationalist literary movements of resistance.

14601720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601720.value: This project aims to explore how Chinese modernist writers’ reading, criticism, translation, and reinterpretation of European war literature during the Second Sino-Japanese War, applying transcultural and trans-historical perspectives. Initially, it examines how these writers reinterpreted European war narratives authored by a diverse group of political voices, including humanists, pacifists, socialists, anti-fascists, communists, and fellow-traveller writers. The study then investigates how translations of this literature were used strategically in the anti-Japanese resistance movement in Hong Kong, amidst the pro-Japanese “Peace Movement” and stringent political censorship by the British colonial government. Furthermore, this research broadens the understanding of how Chinese modernists contributed to and influenced the reception of European literary-political ideas, thereby enriching our understanding of the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese literary modernity in a wartime context. Drawing on previously overlooked sources, the project will culminate in the publication of an anthology titled “Across Eurasia: Translation and Selection of Resistance Literature from Hong Kong Newspapers (1937-1945)” by the end of May 2024. Additionally, it has already yielded numerous peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers.

14601820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601820.value: 該項目旨在利用有監督的機器學習優化分類和模式識別的有效性和可靠性，以推進關於當代中國對政府的信任，民主支持和權利意識的研究。從事實角度看，它旨在辨析有關三個重要政治問題的少數群體。從概念上講，它旨在糾正對三個重要概念的過分拉伸。從理論上講，它旨在促進有關政府信任的來源和含義的辯論。 傳統分析方法不足以實現這三個目標。聚類分析，因子分析和潛在類別分析依靠基於方差的指標權重，幾乎沒有研究者根據理論介入分析過程的微調空間。涉及多維概念及其層次順序時，對邏輯相關的變量進行深入分析會生成太多類型和模式。 該項目將利用有監督的機器學習克服傳統分類和模式識別方法的局限性。它將分析十五個可使用的全國調查數據和四個本地調查數據，並將隨時納入新數據。關於每個數據的分析都分四個階段進行。首先，確定政府信任和民主支持的重要但不常見的類型。其次，將政府信任與民主支持相結合構建權利意識類型。特別是，確定兩個重要但較不常見的群體。一類是批判型公民，他們對政府服務公眾利益的承諾非常不信任，並強烈贊成程序民主；另一類是政權忠誠支持者，他們對政府的承諾非常信任，並強烈反對程序民主。第三，進行一系列多變量分析，以推進關於信任政府的來源和含義的辯論，以及關於普通中國人是否具有規則意識和權利意識的討論。最後，將來自不同數據集的結果進行交叉驗證和三角定位，以糾正由於依賴單個數據而可能產生的偏差。 該項目將於2021年1月1日至2023年12月31日進行。它將產生同行評審的期刊論文和可共享的機器學習程序。它的長期目標是在中國研究中開闢一條新路。

14602320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602320.value: 目標： 應用大型縱向性隊列研究社區易步行程度對居民健康的影響。 背景： 雖然體育鍛煉的益處眾所周知，但是超過25%的世界人口沒有足夠的體育鍛煉。我們對如何能促使人們增加體育鍛煉的有效策略知之甚少。最近一些西方研究指出，提高社區的易步行程度（walkability）有可能會使人們增加體育鍛煉。但目前這方面的研究非常有限，特別是在亞洲人群社區。與西方人群社區不同，亞洲人群社區通常具有比較高的人群密度以及不同西方的文化。此外，社區易步行程度（neighbourhood walkability）促進居民健康的機制也不清楚。雖然認為增加體育鍛煉是其中的一個重要因素，但是否有與其它環境因素如空氣污染互相作用也不得而知。 項目： 我們提出應用一個現存的大型醫學隊列來研究這個重要的公共衛生問題。這個大型隊列包括1996至2017年間的62萬名參與者合併144萬筆醫學檢查記錄。隊列也收集了其它相關資訊如人口學特徵、社會經濟地位、生活方式、和體育鍛煉等。我們在以前的研究中也獲得了其它資料比如空氣污染暴露濃度（包括PM2.5，二氧化氮和臭氧的）和生存狀況等。我們將會運用地理資訊系統從三個維度來評估參與者居住社區的易步行程度（walkability）。對於連續性的健康變項如肺功能、血壓和血糖等，我們將用linear regression 模型進行資料分析；對於兩分性的健康變項如疾病與死亡，我們將用Cox regression 模型進行資料分析。 意義： 世界衛生組織認為缺乏體育鍛煉是導致全球巨大疾病負擔的重要原因。因此，明白社區易步行程度、體育鍛煉與健康的關係非常重要。如果社區的易步行程度能有效促使人們增加體育鍛煉，將對促進人群健康具有重大意義。

14602620.label: Realisation of objectives
14602620.value: A total of 51 eligible patients were invited to take part in this study, of which six were unable to take part as they were overseas (n=3) or were otherwise unavailable (n=3). Three patients actively declined to take part. In total, 42 patients (response rate=82.4%) provided consent and completed the study. All patients are male. The median participant age was 32.0 (interquartile range: 16.8–39.7) years, consisting 11 pediatric patients (median age 15.6 years), 22 young adult patients (median age 33.0 years), and 9 older adult patients (median age 55.2 years). The research procedure included a prospective neurocognitive assessment, neuroimaging, and patient-reported questionnaires, and a retrospective review of the participants’ previous cancer treatment/clinical data from the Clinical Management System (CMS), an in-house electronic health record. In summary, all of the 3 research objectives have been met during the study period. Problems encountered and deviations from the original plan: 1. Recruitment Hemophilia is a rare disease so we expected recruitment to be difficult as the patient population is small and they received care from different hospitals. Furthermore, a subgroup of patients was not eligible for this study. For example, patients younger than 8 years old, patients with previous intracranial bleeds, or patients who had stents, were not eligible to undergo MRIs. To address this problem - Other than the Prince of Wales Hospital (primary recruitment site), we sought the collaboration from hematologists from 3 other hospitals (Princess Margaret Hospital, Tuen Mun Hospital and Hong Kong Children’s Hospital), as well as the Hong Kong Hemophilia Society (HKHS). I would like to thank the hematologists, nurses and the staff of the HKHS for their enthusiasm in referring patients to this study. The targeted sample size will not be achieved without their relentless support. 2. Research activities at the MRI center was affected by the pandemic Due to the pandemic, the MRI center had to minimize research activities. Priority is given to patients who have clinical needs, rather than for research purposes. Hence, there is usually just 1 slot available per week on a weekday and our research staff typically got informed 1 to 2 days before the allocated slot. Some hemophilia patients are working or attending school. Therefore, they were not able to make it for the MRI visit. To address this problem - We attempted to improve our communication with the MRI center and try to arrange for MRI visits on a weekend instead. We found that most of our patients do prefer weekends over weekdays. All 42 patients completed their MRI.

14602620.label: Major findings and research outcome
14602620.value: Objective 1 (Presented in Publication 2): The hemophilia patients performed worse than the age-matched controls in terms of motor processing speed (p=0.0009), visuomotor processing speed (p=0.025), inattentiveness (p=0.021), and cognitive flexibility (p=0.0032). Significant (i.e. moderate to severe) impairments were most commonly seen in the domains of cognitive flexibility (n=13; 30.9%), motor processing speed (n=11; 26.2%), and visuomotor processing speed (n=6; 14.3%). Objective 2 (Presented in Publication 2): Six patients (14.3%) showed signs of cerebral microbleeds on MRI scans, of whom 2 patients (33.3%) had mild disease severity and no previous documented history of intracranial bleeds. In terms of cognitive impairment, all patients (except 1) had moderate-to-severe impairment in at least one cognitive domain. Specifically, the youngest patient with cerebral microbleeds (<18 years old) had a history of intracranial bleeding and frequent episodes of hemarthrosis. Although he was on prophylactic treatment, he had developed inhibitors to the clotting factor concentrates. He had severe impairments in cognitive flexibility and motor processing speed, and moderate memory impairment. Objective 3 (Presented in Publications 1 and 3): In the entire sample, functional limitations were most frequently reported in the domains of work/school performance (54.8%), social activities (52.4%), mental health (35.7%), and intermediate activities of daily living (31%) and least frequently reported in the domains of basic activities of daily living (16.7%) and quality of social interactions (16.7%). We obtained novel findings on the associations between cognitive impairment and functional limitations in patients with hemophilia. Adjusting for age and hemophilia severity, the multivariable analysis showed that as compared with the participants with normal cognitive function, worse perceived work/school performance was reported by the participants who demonstrated impairments in memory (p=0.001), attention (p=0.028), and executive functioning (p=0.014).

14602620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14602620.value: 1. Patients with hemophilia may benefit from regular monitoring of cognitive function as part of standard care. Patients who report occupational or vocational problems may benefit from regular monitoring of cognitive function and psychosocial functioning as part of standard care. 2. Schools and non-governmental organizations should collaborate closely to identify pediatric and young adult patients displaying early signs of behavioral issues; these individuals should undergo regular neuropsychological screening and be monitored closely for cognitive deficits that could impact their academic and social performance. 3. Our findings suggest the need to reinforce age-appropriate education in self-management during early adolescence and throughout different stages of life with tailored supportive care and transition plans. - We have collaborated with the Hong Kong Haemophilia Society and have successfully obtained funding from the Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust to develop a mobile application to promote self-management. In the near future, we plan to add mindfulness and cognitive rehabilitation activities on the mobile application.

14602620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14602620.value: Our study found that encouragingly, the prevalence of cerebral microbleed in patients with hemophilia in Hong Kong is low (13%), reflect the improved prophylactic treatment strategies and quality of care seen in the past decade. However, up to 30% of the patients with hemophilia in Hong Kong demonstrated cognitive impairment, particularly higher-order thinking skills. Specifically, cognitive impairment was more pronounced in patients with hemarthrosis in the previous year, which is a marker of poor disease control. Depressive and anxiety symptoms were also associated with impairment in attention and executive function. We obtained novel findings on the associations between cognitive impairment and functional limitations in patients with hemophilia. As compared with the patients with normal cognitive function, worse perceived work/school performance and social interactions were reported by patients with cognitive impairment. To conclude, this was the first study to demonstrate the impact of cognitive function on functional limitations in patients with hemophilia. These results reinforce the need for regular screening of cognitive deficits and cognitive rehabilitation in this special population.

14603720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603720.value: Computational thinking (CT) is a powerful cognitive tool for solving problems, designing systems, and understanding human behaviour by drawing on concepts fundamental to computer science. It is helpful not only in maintaining competence in a technological society but also in supporting development in higher-order skills such as critical thinking, analysis, and scientific inquiry for the Science-Technology-Engineering-Mathematics (STEM) disciplines. Surrounding this, calls for incorporating CT into mathematics education are rapidly increasing. However, the mere presence of computers in the classroom does not ensure their effective use or quality education. Structural changes in the curriculum are needed to take full advantage of using CT to teach mathematics and problem solving. This study builds on the PI’s previously developed conception of “learning as Making” to envision a computationally enhanced mathematics curriculum—one that supports mathematical problem solving through digital Making (dM). Digital Making involves students’ active creation of both digital and tangible artefacts through block-based programming with physical input sensors and output devices. It promotes active learning and transforms mathematical problem solving beyond merely using formulae and performing arithmetic calculations procedurally. Rather, CT concepts and practices such as sequences, variable-naming, abstraction, algorithmic thinking, decomposing, and iterating are highlighted during problem-based dM activities, through which scientific inquiry, mathematical thinking, and engineering design can also be exhibited as integrated STEM learning. In this design-based study, a total of 20 lessons with problem-based dM tasks will be developed with content appropriate to senior primary and junior secondary mathematics curricula. These lessons will be implemented monthly to roughly 100 students in two primary and two secondary schools in Hong Kong longitudinally over two academic years. Data collection includes: (1) students’ digital artefacts and dM processes collected via code files and screen-capturing, (2) focus group interview and artefact-based interview data captured via video-recording. The study will adopt user analysis, thematic analysis, and case studies to delve into students’ acquired CT concepts, developed problem-solving practices, and formed computational perspectives in the course of the designed curriculum. This study will inform the “big picture” of how using computers might fundamentally change mathematics learning, with an emphasis on mathematical problem solving (and more generally, STEM education). Findings will contribute to extending academic and professional knowledge about learning mathematics with computational tools, in response to CT and Making as a social movement. Ultimately, it will provide evidence-based directions of enhancing CT as a new literacy and problem solving as a global competence in school settings. 計算思維（Computational thinking）是一種通過運用計算機科學的基本概念以理解人類行為，設計系統並最終解決問題的強大認知工具。它是當今科技社會的基礎之一。在教育中，計算思維也有助於很多進階思維能力的發展，例如STEM學科中所需要的批判性思維、分析能力和科學探究能力。因此，將計算思維融入數學教育，是未來科技社會的趨勢與需要。但僅僅增加在課堂中使用電腦的次數並不代表能有效地利用計算思維。要充分挖掘以計算思維教授數學的潛力，改變課程結構這一步必不可少。 本研究建基於首席研究員先前提出的概念「造中學」（learning as Making），以探尋未來的數學課堂——一個以「造中學」協助數學解難的課堂的可行性。「造中學」，即提倡學生在動手製作中學習，其中一個例子是學生通過編寫積木式程式，並使用硬體感測器和顯示器，製作電子硬體成品。「造中學」可以促進主動學習，並令數學解難不再局限於運用公式和運算過程。不僅如此，透過「造中學」的解難活動還可以體現計算思維的概念和做法，例如數列、變數命名、演算與概括、分拆與重複步驟等。同時作為STEM的學習活動，亦可訓練參與者的數學思維、科學探究能力和工程設計能力。 在這項基於設計的研究中，制定共20節包含「造中學」任務，並適合高中和初中數學課程的課堂。這些課堂於每月在香港兩所小學和兩所中學中分別實施。共約100名學生參與，為期兩個學年。數據收集包括：（一）以編程檔和螢幕截圖形式收集學生的電子成品和「造中學」的過程；及（二）以視頻錄製形式收集焦點小組訪談和基於成品的訪談數據。研究將採用使用者分析、專題分析和案例研究，深入調查學生在預設課程中形成的計算思維概念、解難技巧、以及計算機科學觀點。 這項研究將探尋如何從根本上將計算思維融入數學解難，數學學習以及更宏觀的STEM教育。研究結果將有助於擴展以計算機科學作為工具來學習數學的相關學術和專業知識，並回應科技社會中的計算思維和「造」 （Making）的概念。最終為「在學校環境中的計算思維及解難能力將分別成為新的素質及世界性能力」一說，提供實證支持。

14603820.label: Project Objectives
14603820.value: The central objective is to publish a set of four papers, which would clarify the concept of absorption and address it in the framework of a phenomenology of dreams, memory and phantasy. To this day, such a phenomenology remains to be worked out. Another objective is to organize an international conference, Varieties of Self-Awareness, that would demonstrate the large variety of its modes and clarify its diverse functions, as they have been conceptualized in a variety of philosophical traditions, such as phenomenology, hermeneutics, Kantianism, and the Kyoto school. The third objective is to publish an edited collection of articles on the varieties of self-awareness that would include some of the expanded and revised conference presentations as well as other papers, written by scholars who would not take part in the conference. The fourth objective is to demonstrate how phenomenology of absorption can impact media studies and related fields. The fifth objective is to develop a distinctive methodological approach to study such limit phenomena as absorption, which would both rely on the resources of classical phenomenology and simultaneously be dialogically oriented to such disciplines as psychology, psychoanalysis and cognitive science. The sixth objective is to show that phenomenology of absorption in significant ways enriches contemporary analyses of self-awareness by disclosing its diverse modalities and by clarifying their essential structural features. The seventh objective is to provide an essential clarification of the class of representations, which so far has been overlooked in the literature, viz., absorbed representations. Such a clarification is much needed, since on its basis one can further show that the whole life of intuitive representations fluctuates between two extremes: pure absorption, at the one end, and pure translucency, at the other.

14603820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603820.value: Although absorption is an underinvestigated phenomenon in philosophy and related fields, its analysis carries far-reaching philosophical significance. As a phenomenological concept, it designates a characteristic feature of experiences, which transfer the ego beyond the horizon of presence. While investigating different shapes of absorption entailed in such experiences as non-lucid dreams, unconscious memories and unconscious phantasies, and while focusing on the phenomenological meaning of absorption in virtual reality, this project will demonstrate that there are three fundamental spaces of experience that psychic life can inhabit: 1) here and now, 2) there and then, and 3) between here and there, now and then. My goal is to write five articles on the phenomenology of absorption. 1) “The Inner World: Phenomenology of Absorption” would determine the philosophical sense of absorption and elucidate the fundamental structures of absorbed experience. 2) “Phenomenology of Dreams” would demonstrate that dreaming consciousness entails a displaced self-awareness and would argue that non-lucid dreams constitute the purest type of absorbed experience. 3) “Memory and Self-Awareness,” would analyze the two senses in which consciousness of recollection is self-aware: the remembering ego is self-aware in memory as well as self-aware that it is remembering. 4) “Phantasy and Self-Awareness” would further show that although such a split self-awareness is also characteristic of phantasy, an overarching synthesis that binds the remembering and the remembered egos as two moments of personhood is not a necessary feature of phantasy. 5) “Absorption in the Cyber-World: Phenomenology of Virtual Reality,” would open a dialogue between phenomenology and media studies with the aim of showing that absorption is a graded phenomenon, which lends itself to a detailed phenomenological clarification. With the support of the GRF grant, I also plan to organize an international conference on the varieties of self-awareness and edit a volume on the same theme. The philosophical relevance of this project is fourfold. 1) It contributes to the philosophical discussions of the nature and variety of self-awareness by showing that there are other modes of self-awareness besides perceptual self-awareness. 2) It contributes to the philosophy of memory, phantasy and dreams, for it demonstrates that absorbed experiences constitute a separate and so-far overlooked class of intuitive representations. 3) It contributes to the phenomenological analyses of the unconscious, conceived as a type consciousness with specific structures. 4) It broadens the theoretical framework by opening a dialogue between phenomenology and media studies regarding the nature of absorbed experience.

14603820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603820.value: 1. The project traced the emergence and development of the concept of absorption in phenomenology. It demonstrated how a careful study of absorption compels us to rethink fundamental themes in phenomenology: it forces us to broaden our understanding of sensuous intuition, reconceptualize the nature of self-awareness, stretch the limits of intuitive re-presentations, and rethink the portrayal of phenomenology as a metaphysics of presence. It further demonstrated that absorbed experiences are characterized by a specific form of self-awareness, that they constitute a distinct type of intuitive re-presentations, that a new method is needed to investigate them, and that their analysis leads towards a phenomenology of the unconscious. 2. The project demonstrated that the well-established phenomenological distinction between reflective and pre-reflective self-awareness needs to be further supplemented with more refined distinctions between different modes of pre-reflective self-awareness. The project addressed different modes, which we come across in perception, lucid dreams, non-lucid dreams, daydreams, mind-wandering and episodic memory. The phenomenological analysis led to the conclusion that pre-reflective self-awareness need not be spoken of in the singular, but in the plural. 3. The project developed a phenomenological clarification of the concept of immersion in game studies. It demonstrated that immersion in digital games should be recognized as one modality of immersion among others. It showed that immersion in digital games is a hybrid phenomenon, which shares certain features with immersion in non-digital games and other features with immersion in other types of digital media. It further showed that immersion in digital games is characterized by a specific function of embodiment. 4. The project offered a critique of the dominant conceptions of mind-wandering in contemporary psychology and philosophy and against such a background, it developed a new, phenomenologically-grounded conception of mind-wandering as well as addressed the function of mind-wandering in conscious life. 5. The project developed a phenomenology of dreams and daydreaming, suggesting that they are unconscious phantasies. In its own turn, such an approach necessitated that one asks again: what is phantasy? According to the perspective developed in this project, phantasy is a specific field of experience that lies between two extremes: the fully translucent mode of the as if consciousness and the thoroughly opaque mode of absorption. Most phantasies, both conscious and unconscious, voluntary and involuntary, are lived somewhere between these two extremes.

14603820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603820.value: Against the background of this research, in the future years, I hope to be able to write a book which would offer the first phenomenological investigation of the structures of displaced self-awareness. The book would: 1) develop a distinctive methodological approach to study diverse modes of self-awareness, which would rely on the resources of classical phenomenology and which would open a dialogue between phenomenology and other disciplines, such as cognitive science, psychoanalysis, psychology, media studies and religious studies. 2) demonstrate that phenomenology of displacement enriches contemporary analyses of prereflective self-awareness in phenomenology, philosophy of mind and related fields by disclosing the diverse modes of self-awareness and by clarifying their structural features. 3) provide an essential clarification of the class of representations, which so far has been overlooked in the literature, viz., absorbed representations. Such a clarification is much needed, since on its basis one can show that the life of intuitive representations fluctuates between two extremes: pure absorption and pure translucency. 4) address the question concerning the relation between self-awareness and selfhood, while paying central attention to displaced self-awareness. To undertake such a project, I plan to apply for another research grant, or research fellowship.

14603820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603820.value: The project developed a phenomenological analysis of absorption, conceived of as the ego’s immersion in its own presentifications (memories, anticipations, phantasies, lucid and non-lucid dreams, daydreaming). It addressed absorption as a specific type of self-displacement, which is to be understood as the ego’s transference beyond the horizon of presence. Conceptualizing the relationship between absorption and affectivity, self-deceit, and captivity, the project showed that psychic life is oversimplified when one commits to the common view that the field of presence constitutes the exhaustive horizon of all possible experience. Resisting this generally accepted standpoint, the project developed a phenomenological perspective which shows that psychic life unfolds over a spectrum of experience and the ego can find itself at different locations across this spectrum: it can immerse itself in the here and now, absorb itself in the there and then, or live in between: between here and there, between now and then.

14604020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604020.value: Background E-waste production has increased rapidly in Hong Kong and worldwide. Since 2015, more advanced processing (e.g., dismantling, isolation) that was previously completed in mainland China now must be done locally. Also, with the launch of a new producer responsibility scheme by Hong Kong government in 2018, more e-waste will have to be diverted into the local recycling industry. These changes pose increasing challenges to the e-waste recycling industry in Hong Kong. Most local e-waste dealers are small enterprises with less than 50 workers, and they are generally lacking knowledge on occupational health and protection. Local e-waste recycling workers are expected to have high chemical exposures as a result of their work, however there is no exposure data to confirm this and we know nothing about the exposure prevention behavior of local e-waste recycling workers. Aims The primary objectives of this cross-sectional study are to (1) investigate urinary concentrations of selected chemicals among local e-waste recycling workers, compared to office workers (“unexposed”); (2) develop an Exposure Prevention Behavior model focusing on respiratory protective equipment (RPE); (3) identify factors (non-occupational and occupational) related to urinary concentrations of selected chemicals. The secondary objective is to identify predictors of workers’ willingness to wear RPE. Brief description We plan to recruit 200 eligible e-waste recycling workers (“exposed”) and 200 office workers (“unexposed”) through the network of local Labour Unions and the EcoTech Association. Workers will be invited to complete a 15-minute epidemiological questionnaire and 20-minute exposure prevention behavior questionnaire, and also to donate 50 ml morning spot urine sample. The exposure prevention behavior questionnaire will be based on the Robertsen’s conceptual behavior intention model and Occupational Safety Culture Index (Workplace) questionnaire. Factors associated with high urinary chemical concentrations and predictors of workers’ willingness to wear RPE will be examined. Significance Hong Kong is an important part of the Greater Bay Area, which is an area facing unique and acute challenges to the growing concerns of e-waste production. This is a timely project with important significance as the results will provide evidence from which policy and recommendations can be made to various stakeholders in order to reduce the hazards in the e-waste industry, safeguard worker’s health and protect the environment. The challenges with e-waste are global in nature and this research will also help guide other regions, and international initiatives to combat the challenges associated with increasing global production of e-waste. 研究背景 全球和香港的電子垃圾產量迅速增加。自2015年起，以前在中國大陸完成的電子垃圾深度處理（如拆解、金屬提取）現在必須在本地完成。另外，隨著香港政府在2018年推出新的生產者責任計劃， 更多的電子垃圾回收工作不得不在本地完成。這些變化給香港的電子垃圾回收業帶來越來越大的挑戰。本地電子垃圾處理商多是小型企業，工人數少於50人，普遍缺乏職業健康和防護知識。本地電子垃圾回收工人可能會因工作原因暴露於高濃度的化學物中。但目前沒有此類暴露的證據證實。我們也不知道本地電子垃圾回收工人為預防化學物暴露所採取防護措施的現狀。 研究目標 這項橫斷面研究的主要目標是：（1）調查本地電子垃圾回收工人尿液中選定化學物的水平；（2）建立一個以呼吸防護設備為重點的行為預防模型；（3）確定影響尿液中所選化學物水平的因素（包括職業性和非職業性的）。次要目標是：確定可以預測工人配戴呼吸防護設備意願的因素。 研究簡介 我們計劃通過工聯會和環保科技協會招募200名符合條件的電子垃圾回收工人和200名辦公室工作人員作為暴露和非暴露組。參與者將完成一個15分鐘的流行病學調查問卷和一個20分鐘的暴露預防行為問卷調查。參與者同時將捐贈50毫升晨間尿樣。我們將研究影響尿液中化學物濃度的因素，並確定工人配戴RPE意願的預測因素。 研究意義 香港是大灣區的重要組成部分，而大灣區正面臨著電子垃圾所帶來的嚴峻挑戰。這是一個具有重要意義的及時項目。研究結果將從實證角度向各持份者提出政策和建議，以減少電子垃圾回收行業的危害，保障工人的健康。電子垃圾回收是全球性的挑戰，這項研究將有助於指導其他區域，並倡議全球應對電子垃圾產量持續增加所造成的巨大挑戰。

14604020.label: Realisation of objectives
14604020.value: Among 109 e-waste and 109 office workers, 101 and 100 of them donated first-spot urine samples, and their urinary concentrations of two types of chemicals [metals and organophosphate esters (OPEs)] were analyzed according to the standard protocols. 5.3.1. How and to what extent the revised Objective 1 has been achieved: 5.3.1.1. Measurement for metals and OPEs As indicated in the revised proposal, the urinary concentrations of the metabolites of OPEs (mOPEs, including BBOEP, BCEP, BCIPP, BDCIPP, DBP, DOCP, DPCP, and DPHP) and metals (Li, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Ga, As, Se, Rb, Sr, Cd, Cs, Ba, Hg, Tl, Pb, and U) in the first-spot morning urine samples were analyzed. The analysis was conducted using HPLC-MS/MS, specifically a 20A high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) system coupled with a Q-Trap 5500 tandem mass spectrometer (MS/MS) for mOPEs, and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) for analyzing urinary metals. 5.3.1.2. Statistical analysis For chemical concentration below the limit of quantification (LOQ), a value of LOQ/2 was used for statistical analysis. Independent samples t-test and Mann-Whitney U test were employed for normal and abnormal distributed variables to compare the concentrations between e-waste and office workers, respectively. 5.3.1.3. Results Of the 21 tested metals, 15 were detected among over 70% of the overall participants (i.e., detection rate ≥ 70%), and these were used for further analysis. While only one metal, V, had a slightly higher urinary concentration in office workers, other metals were found at higher levels among e-waste workers, with eight metals having significant differences, including Li (26.62 ng/ml vs. 19.95 ng/ml), Mn (3.64 ng/ml vs. 1.97 ng/ml), Ni (2.38 ng/ml vs. 1.70 ng/ml), Cu (7.60 ng/ml vs. 5.18 ng/ml), Zn (359.58 ng/ml vs. 257.30 ng/ml), Sr (126.56 ng/ml vs. 100.63ng/ml), Ba (4.00 ng/ml vs. 2.87 ng/ml), and Pb (1.04 ng/ml vs. 0.52 ng/ml). The detection rate for all mOPE congeners exceeded 70%. Among the eight tested mOPEs, five metabolites (i.e., BCEP, DBP, DoCP, DpCP, and DPHP) were higher in the e-waste workers compared to office workers, with DPHP showing a statistically significant difference (0.31 ng/mL vs. 0.25 ng/mL). The concentrations of the remaining mOPEs were higher in office workers (i.e., BCIPP, BDCIPP, and BBOEP), with one significant difference for BCIPP ( 0.22 ng/mL vs. 0.16 ng/mL). 5.3.1.4. Percentage achieved According to the revised proposal, the goal was to collect 100 urine samples from both e-waste workers and office workers. We successfully collected 101 samples from e-waste workers and 100 samples from office workers. Additionally, all metals and OPEs specified in the revised proposal were tested. Therefore, the percentage achieved for the revised Objective 1 is 100%. 5.3.2. How and to what extent the revised Objective 2 has been achieved: 5.3.2.1. Development of Exposure Prevention Behavior model focusing on respiratory protective equipment (RPE) To develop the Exposure Prevention Behavior model, we employed Robertsen’s RPE Behavior Intention Model (RRPEBIM) and the Hong Kong Occupational Safety Culture Index in the Workplace (HKOSCI). The English version of the RRPEBIM was translated into Chinese by experts, ensuring cultural relevance to the Hong Kong context. 5.3.2.2. Statistical analysis All e-waste workers were interviewed using the newly developed Exposure Prevention Behavior questionnaire. We utilized the R package “lavaan” to conduct confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), refining the model structure and evaluating the indices derived from the final construct. Multiple parameters were employed to assess the model fit in CFA, including standardized root mean square residual (SRMR), goodness of fit index (GFI), parsimonious normed fit index (PNFI), root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA), comparative fit index (CFI), and normed fit index (NFI). Additionally, Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability (CR) were used to confirm the internal consistency of the remaining factors in the final model. To evaluate the convergent validity of the model, we calculated the Average Variance Extracted (AVE). 5.3.2.3. Results Based on the CFA results, variables with low path coefficients and composite reliability (i.e., factor loadings greater than 0.70) were removed. As a result, four latent factors comprising 17 variables were retained in the CFA-enhanced model, including subjective norms, supportive working conditions, autonomy, and perceptions and attitudes of employees on occupational safety and health. All factors in the final model demonstrated acceptable internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha and CR values exceeding the recommended threshold of 0.70. Additionally, the AVE values of the selected domains indicated satisfactory reliability (all AVE values exceeded 0.5) of the enhanced model. The fitness indices, except for GFI, reached exceptional levels (GFI = 0.889, SRMR = 0.054, PNFI = 0.751, RMSEA = 0.030, CFI = 0.990, NFI = 0.904), suggesting a good overall model fit. 5.3.2.4. Percentage achieved: 100% for Revised Objective 2. 5.3.3. How and to what extent the revised Objective 3 has been achieved: 5.3.3.1. Questionnaires for occupational and non-occupational information All participants were interviewed using a standardized questionnaire to gather both occupational and non-occupational details through face-to-face or phone interviews. The occupational questionnaire collected information from e-waste workers on job designation, type and size of the entity, length of employment in the e-waste industry, weekly working hours, practices such as changing clothes before returning home, history of exposure to occupational pollutants, and job rotation systems. The epidemiological questionnaire collected non-occupational factors from all participants, including age, gender, job type, smoking and drinking habits, family income, residential pollution levels, educational levels, and marine fish consumption habits. 5.3.3.2. Statistical analysis and results Among the non-occupational factors, being male was significantly associated with higher levels of mOPEs (BCEP, BDCIPP, DoCP, DpCP, and DPHP). Employed as an e-waste worker was strongly associated with increased urinary concentrations of metals, including Li, Mn, Ni, Sr, Tl, and Pb. Additionally, habitual alcohol consumption was linked to elevated urinary levels of As and Sr. The associations between urinary concentrations of the tested chemicals and occupational factors were further explored among e-waste workers. Engaging in tasks such as dismantling or repairing e-waste was associated with higher levels of DoCP and DpCP. Workers who reported a history of toxicant exposure had higher levels of V, Ni, and Ba. 5.3.3.3. Percentage achieved: 100% for Revised Objective 3. 5.3.4. How and to what extent the revised Objective 4 has been achieved: 5.3.4.1. Questionnaires about the occupational predictors, non-occupational predictors, and behavior intention to wear RPE The independent factors in Objective 3, along with the latent factors identified from Objective 2, were used for this objective. Additionally, in light of the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on the utilization of respiratory protective equipment (RPE), participants were asked, “Has the outbreak of COVID-19 changed the amount of time you wear RPE at work?” with response options including: Increased, Decreased, and No Change. The behavioral intention to wear RPE was measured by one of the factors (referred to as “RPE intention”) in the RRPEBIM scale, which solely assesses the willingness of workers to wear RPE in the workplace. 5.3.4.2. Statistical analysis and results Among the factors investigated, increasing age and longer working hours were positively associated with elevated RPE intention scores among e-waste workers. Additionally, two latent factors from Objective 2, subjective norms and supportive working conditions, were significantly associated with higher RPE intention scores. 5.3.4.3. Percentage achieved: 100% for Revised Objective 4.

14604020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604020.value: This study revealed that the concentrations of mOPEs were similar between e-waste workers and office workers, suggesting that e-waste recycling may not be the primary source of OPE exposure among Hong Kong e-waste workers. However, the levels of most tested metals were higher in e-waste workers than in office workers, indicating that e-waste recycling could significantly increase metal exposure among local e-waste workers. The different trends in the comparison of metal and OPE exposure levels suggested that e-waste workers in Hong Kong face more potential health impacts from metal exposure. Based on these findings, two peer-reviewed publications related to metal and OPE exposure have been published in international journals, Chemosphere (30/359, Environmental Sciences) and Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety (9/106, Toxicology). Another manuscript, which assesses neurobehavioral alterations among e-waste workers, has been published in the journal Safety and Health at Work (125/403, Public, Environmental & Occupational Health). One research article related to PAH in e-waste recycling work is under review now in a peer-reviewed journal. Another research article related to exposure Prevention Behavior model focusing on the use of respiratory protective equipment (RPE) among local e-waste workers has been drafted and will be submitted. The analysis identified that subjective norms and supportive working conditions were significantly associated with an increased intention to use RPE, highlighting potential targets for future interventions. Additionally, a systematic review summarizing the evidence on internal chemical exposure levels and neurological health issues related to e-waste recycling has been drafted.

14604020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604020.value: While the mOPE concentrations in e-waste workers and office workers were similar, the significantly higher urinary metal levels in e-waste workers indicate that e-waste recycling in Hong Kong poses a considerable health risk to e-waste workers. Future research should focus on assessing the effectiveness of targeted interventions, such as those based on subjective norms and supportive working conditions identified in this study, to increase the intention and use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Such interventions could reduce the internal exposure levels from e-waste recycling and alleviate the associated health burdens. Additionally, future studies should design and implement interventions aimed at specific job roles identified in this study, as they have higher exposure levels, to further mitigate risks. E-waste recycling presents significant challenges not only for industry workers but also for the general population and the surrounding environment. Our findings indicate that e-waste recycling increases internal metal levels among e-waste workers. As a next step, it would be valuable to investigate the levels of chemical exposure from e-waste affecting both citizens and the environment in Hong Kong, in particular, the most vulnerable population in the community, and assess environmental impact on sustainable development as well.

14604020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604020.value: E-waste, or electronic waste, is rapidly becoming the fastest-growing type of household waste in Hong Kong. Workers involved in recycling e-waste are exposed to significant health risks, particularly from hazardous chemicals released during the process. This study found that e-waste recycling in Hong Kong leads to increased levels of metals in workers' bodies, rather than higher concentrations of certain plastic additives (such as OPEs). Additionally, we developed a scale to measure e-waste workers' willingness to use respiratory protective equipment (RPE) at work. Our research also highlighted that fostering a supportive work environment and creating positive social norms can encourage workers to use RPE more consistently. The findings from this study will provide valuable, evidence-based insights for policymakers to enhance workplace safety and improve the occupational health of e-waste workers in Hong Kong.

14604120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604120.value: The project investigates the forces shaping Philippine society during American colonization’s concluding phase. Focusing upon the Bureau of Public Works (BPW) within the frame of the Commonwealth Era, the study examines environmental transition in the run-up to national independence. In 1898 the United States’ (US) colonization of the Philippines began. By the early-1900s public works schemes were initiated to help liberate the country from its allegedly ‘backward’ condition. In 1916, to bolster the ‘uplifting’ process, the Jones Act was passed. It permitted Filipinos to take control of government offices. With, in 1934, the Tydings-McDuffie Act being passed and the US announcing its intention to imminently withdraw from the Philippines, the Commonwealth Government (CG) set out on an ambitious nation-building course of action: a comprehensive urban and rural public works program was established and a new capital city, Quezon City, was devised. The inquiry will probe how the BPW’s operations aligned environmental development/betterment to the decolonization process in order to support the CG’s aspiration of constructing a modern nation in the lead-in to national independence. Accordingly, the project shall assess the achievements of the BPW in terms of both infrastructure and institution building. In doing this BPW staff will be examined. By researching their education and careers the study will thus reveal Filipino agency in the formation of the soon-to-be independent republic. Additionally, the study will evaluate the influence of President Manuel Quezon. Whilst it is known Quezon sought to promote social justice through, for instance, agrarian reform, new housing schemes, and urban planning projects, little is presently known about the creation and proliferation of his administration’s environmental management strategy. Likewise, by focusing on an important public office, i.e. the BPW, the investigation will uncover in what ways, or not, the CG conformed to the principles of American-styled democracy implanted by the colonial administration from 1916 in preparing Filipinos for self-rule. The study, in opening a new window to comprehend the American Empire, will present original insights of the association between societal progress, governance by native persons, and environmental management. In focusing upon a relatively unstudied era of the Philippines’ past, and in discussing national initiatives alongside local involvements to develop rural and urban environments, the project will be of interest to scholars interested in Philippine society’s evolution and the development of colonial and new postcolonial capitals in Asia, e.g. Putrajaya (Malaysia), Naypyidaw (Myanmar) and Islamabad (Pakistan). 此項目探究菲律賓在美國殖民時期的最後階段改變社會的力量，透過著眼於英聯邦時代內的公共工程局（BPW），研究國家獨立前夕的環境轉變。 1898年，美國開始對菲律賓進行殖民。到1900年代初，公共工程計劃開始實施，以幫助該國擺脫所謂的「落後」狀況。為了加強「振興」進程，1916年通過了《瓊斯法》允許菲律賓人控制政府機構。隨著1934年《丁丁—麥克杜菲法案》獲得通過，美國宣布打算盡快從菲律賓撤出，英聯邦政府（CG）制定了雄心勃勃的國家建設計劃：全面的城鄉公共工程計劃，並設計一個新首都—奎松市。 此研究探究在非殖民化過程中，公共工程局（BPW）的運作與環境發展或改善如何協助英聯邦政府（CG）達成建設現代化國家的願望，並引致國家獨立。因此，此研究會評估公共工程局（BPW）在基礎設施和機構建設方面的成就。過程中會探究公共工程局（BPW）的官員及其教育和職業，以揭示菲律賓的機構在即將成立的獨立共和國中的地位。此外，本研究還評估曼努埃爾·奎松總統(President Manuel Quezon)的影響力。眾所周知，奎松（Quezon）試圖通過土地改革，新的住房計劃和城市規劃項目來促進社會公義，但關於他在建立及擴展政府環境管理策略的研究目前知之甚少。本研究亦會透過公共工程局（BPW）探討英聯邦政府（CG）是否以某種方式採納了自1916年開始為使菲律賓人準備自治而植入的美國式民主原則。 這項研究為理解美國的殖民帝國打開了一個新窗口，將提出社會進程，本地人的治理與環境管理三者聯繫之間的原始見解。另外，本研究著眼於菲律賓歷史中相對尚未被研究的時代，討論國家措施與地方參與於農村和城市環境的發展，有助研究菲律賓社會的演變、殖民地的發展和後殖民新首都的發展，如在亞洲的布城（馬來西亞）、內比都（緬甸）和伊斯蘭堡（巴基斯坦）。 關鍵字：菲律賓；英聯邦時代；公共工程局；非殖民化民族。

14604120.label: Realisation of objectives
14604120.value: In January 2021 the project was commenced with four objectives. They were formed to guide the research process, thereby assisting in the acquisition of new insights as to the Philippines’ urban past and activities of Filipino civil servants. Objective #1, to be brief, sought to gather detailed information about the Filipino staff working in the Bureau of Public Works’ Division of Architecture, so as to grasp the interface between their training in the U.S., their career development, and their vocational activities after 1935 as part of the Commonwealth Government’s strategy to impart ‘betterment’. All in all, new data on Filipino civil servants was found, as was the generic ideology of their government post 1935. In particular, thanks to contacts at the Department of Public Works and Highways in Manila, the PI was able to acquire a database of more than 10,000 images, i.e. plans, architectural renderings, etc., re BPW projects before and after 1935. Although to catalogue the materials was a weighty task, with the RA the PI was able to not only map where projects occurred in the Philippine Archipelago but, critically, see what they were. This enabled a comparative perspective to be formed so that the BPW activities pre 1935 could be aligned against its projects/activities post 1935, and similarities and contrasts thus observed between the two time frames. More so, by gathering data re BPW budgets it was possible to note the growth of amount of money spent after 1935 on public works (in comparison to pre 1935), and to see how (via the use of different primary sources) the spending of money allied to new laws passed by the Commonwealth Government on, for instance, slum clearing, road planning, etc. Objective #2 was designed to provoke new comprehension of the challenges affecting the BPW’s practical operations. One element in this regard that was not overlooked was the rise of Japanese imperialism in Asia which, by late-1941, culminated in the Occupation of the Philippine Islands. Yet, the study was able to explore the Japanese imprint upon urban management from 1942-5 because the new colonial government sought to undertake public works, e.g. in Manila. These included the promotion of greening built fabrics too in the country, and turning open urban land into places for growing food. Furthermore, the Japanese introduced a scheme to encourage neighbourhood to self-manage local communities, and it awarded sums of money that were used for urban beautification. In the book Remodelling to Prepare for Independence a chapter is devoted to explaining the activities of the Japanese. Another chapter looks post the Japanese Occupation at attempts to redesign the public works system, particularly the setting up of new public agencies to oversee urban environmental design and management. Objective #3 sought to explore and explain what urban and rural transformations occurred between 1935 and 1946, and why. With luck having been allowed access to storerooms at the Department of Public Works and Highways, the PI was able to see how Manila was transformed during the final phase of American colonial rule. Because of this, a new balance was formed as to which BPW staff was of greatest importance to Commonwealth Government ventures; historiography traditionally exposes Juan Arellano as the most important person re public architecture and planning during the American colonial age, but from 1935, it was not Arellano, rather Antonio Toledo, who oversaw the transformation of Manila and many provincial towns and cities. He also designed rural roads, and proposed model housing alongside them. In contrast, Arellano was central to the establishment and initial development of Quezon City; it being the new settlement established in 1939 as the future postcolonial capital of the Philippines. Crucially too, through being able to find links between the BPW’s staff and contemporary urban design matters in places such as South America, the PI was able to see/explain the different plans composed for Quezon City before and after World War Two. The post war scheme, in particular, put much greater emphasis upon neighbourhood planning, and thus exposed the influence of South American Modernism upon Filipino thinking. Objective #4 was established so that an exploration of the ties between Philippine politics and infrastructure projects could be observed (and, of course, explained). The project was able to explicate that from 1935 not only President Quezon, but a number of other high ranking politicians in the Commonwealth Government, held well-defined views as to the social significance of public works. Books specifically on town planning (composed by politicians) were discovered, read, and evaluated, and so the potential of urban development as a Philippine society-advancing resource laid bare. Hence, in Manila, for the first time, debates raged as to the implementing of slum clearing schemes, and model housing was introduced in areas such as Tondo, i.e. an area renowned for poor housing, social problems, infectious illness, etc. In accomplishing the research aim, the project was able to uncover new data that showed President Quezon’s admiration for the New Deal in the U.S., and it made clear after national independence how the fracture of Filipino politicians into different camps lead to the corruption of public works funds for projects not deemed ‘socially beneficial’. The corruption of politics, and efforts to correct the political system’s flaws, formed part of Chapter Five in Remodelling to Prepare for Independence. In summary, as noted in the mid-project report, the inquiry started slowly but from mid-2022 onwards picked up pace to such an extent that all project aims were accomplished by the end date of the investigation. What is more, by that time, a major book project had been completed. Although the original goals re publishing project findings had to be re-evaluated given the lack of time in 2021 and 2022 to visit archives, nonetheless original data is now being put into the public domain and, in July 2024, this information will be used as part of a major international conference organised by the PI: in mid-2024 he will act as co-convenor of the International Planning History Society’s 20th Biennial Conference. To date, more than 325 abstracts for the event have been received, and titled The High Density City it will hopefully provoke new discourse on the history and management of cities in Asia. In addition, as listed elsewhere in this report, the recently-completed project’s findings are proving useful to the PI in the preparing of a Seed Grant application ahead of a future RGC CRF submission. Therefore, to close all remarks as to the project’s objectives and accomplishments, despite challenges to overseas travel and the recruitment of a RA from the Philippines, by 2023 great progress had been made, and original findings interpreted, explained, and published. No under-achievements of the project aims occurred from 2021-3. The aforementioned Routledge book produced from the inquiry, testifies to this. It has been nominated for the International Planning History Society Book Prize and World History Associate Book Prize given the original nature of its findings.
