14604120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604120.value: The inquiry produced original findings re the workings of the Bureau of Public Works (BPW). It reveals the importance of the BPW’s activities to the national advancement process, in so doing exposing what schemes the Bureau undertook, where, for what economic cost, and for what purpose. With clear objectives in mind, and through accessing previously unpublished archival materials, the PI was able to discover the sheer volume of urban planning activity occurring from 1935 to 1941. In alliance, through checking court records, see who disagreed with the BPW’s strategy, and why. Moreover, in utilizing reports held at various institutions in the Metro Manila area, the PI was able to examine the form of laws passed during the Commonwealth Era, note their impacts, and identify exactly their contribution to the public’s well-being. That said, flaws within the Commonwealth Government’s approach to national development was identified. This issue was then examined in more depth via reviewing urban management in the early-postcolonial period. All in all, what did the study find? It exposed the large amounts of money spent on public works, it showed the nationwide diffusion of schemes, it revealed their social meaning, and it took forward views of leading Filipino politicians as to why modern cities were critical to national progress, e.g. they would help build more advanced economies plus supply more high-quality living environments for the common person (tao). Furthermore, the study showed that influences other than from America affected BPW activities during the Commonwealth Era. Staff of the Bureau were aware of urban design advances in Europe and Latin America, and these influences took a more-full form by the early-postcolonial age. Finally, a major finding of the inquiry was that Filipinos, under the Presidency of Manuel Quezon, had a predetermined vision of what life in the postcolonial setting would be like. Given the interruptions of the Japanese Occupation, and the need after 1945 to rebuild war-damaged society, this vision became somewhat lost. Yet, despite its relatively short amount of time – 11 years – the Commonwealth Era was an epoch full of major advancements in urban management and law making. Grateful to the RGC for its funding, the PI and research findings put into the public domain will hopefully reshape the image of the years 1935-46, and demonstrate the true role of the urban variable to Philippine societal evolution.

14604120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604120.value: In January 2024 the PI commenced a new RGC GRF funded project. It will examine the nature of governance within the municipal council of Manila during the American colonial era. However, work undertaken for the prior GRF project will evidently be relevant to the new investigation, and, with the PI having now completed three monographs on Philippine urban history – and with a fourth soon to be completed - he intends, in May 2024, to apply for a Seed Grant at CUHK. This is so that he can seriously prepare the bedrock for a RGC CRF application in the future. The intention at present, thus, is to form a collaborative project with scholars overseas so as to compare processes of urban development, urban management, and decolonisation in Manila, Hanoi, Jakarta, and Taipei. Accordingly, the prior GRF has been critical to planning future endeavours in two fundamental ways: the advancement of factual knowledge, and, in conjunction, access to new archival materials; plus, the growth of self-confidence so as to feel able to submit a prospective competitive application to the RGC for CRF review.

14604120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604120.value: The inquiry has illuminated the implications of the U.S.’s final phase of colonial rule in the Philippines. It investigated the nature and practice of decolonisation with regard to the management and form of built environments in the years immediately prior to the granting of national independence (in 1946). The study, through its intensive use of primary sources, has thrown off the collaboration versus resistance paradigm that empire studies typically follow, and it has consequently yielded a monograph to comprehend transition within an Asian society before and after World War Two. The book, alongside other publications produced by the inquiry, has offered a new vantage point to grasp the winding-down of the American empire in Asia, and to rethink Filipino ethno-history given societal management after 1935. In embracing theory, the study has not only discovered what public works transpired, and by whose design, but also what they meant to national development. All in all, it has opened a new window to examine a society undergoing change, one guided during the last phase of colonial rule by Filipino political input. Therefore, what the postcolonial future was to be, and how urban fabrics were to articulate this, has been spelled out.

14604220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604220.value: A lack of preparation for old age is associated with negative health and well-being outcomes (Sörensen, Mak, Chapman, Duberstein, & Lyness, 2012). Yet, despite Hong Kong’s increasing aging population, our previous cross-cultural research has revealed that Hong Kong adults prepare the least for their old age, compared to those in other countries including Germany and the U.S (Kornadt, Voss, Fung, Hess, & Rothermund, 2019). We propose this study to understand the mechanisms behind the cross-cultural differences in old-age preparation and the psychological outcomes of preparedness across Hong Kong and Germany. Practically, this study may offer solutions to Hong Kong’s low old-age preparation rate. Theoretically, with many negative connotations associating old age with illnesses, vulnerability, and physical limitations (Rodin & Langer, 1980), many people see aging as a stressor (Lazarus & DeLongis, 1983). Existing research, however, has not systematically investigated the psychological mechanisms behind age-related preparation. Drawing from the stress and coping framework, we conceptualize preparation for old age as coping strategies dealing with the negative psychological impact of aging. According to the framework, to facilitate preparation, people need to perceive aging—a life transition that poses many challenges—as relevant to themselves. They also need to perceive sufficient control over the preparation process and see themselves as responsible for the preparation. Therefore, we hypothesize that individuals with higher perceived self-relevance, control, and responsibility are more likely to carry out preparation. We also hypothesize that, at the cross-cultural level, Hong Kong people’s less old-age preparation than their German counterparts may be attributable to their lower levels of perceived self-relevance, control, and responsibility. This innovative use of stress and coping theory will generate new insights about the psychological factors that motivate old-age preparation across cultures. Once people have successfully coped with the stress associated with aging through preparatory actions, they theoretically should be able to enjoy better psychological outcomes (Sörensen et al., 2012). We hypothesize that such benefits may occur to a greater extent among individuals (and cultures) that have higher perceived self-relevance, control, and responsibility regarding old-age preparation. Hong Kong people’s lower level of old-age preparation may be attributable to the lower level of benefits that they receive from preparation, relative to their German counterparts. To address the above hypotheses, we will collect another wave of data from a lifespan sample in Hong Kong and Germany who have been participating in a cross-cultural, longitudinal (four waves since 2012) study on aging and preparedness. 對很多人來說，老化給他們很大壓力，但只有小部份人有好好準備迎接老年生活。缺乏老年準備與很多負面的生理及心理影響有關。即使香港的高齡人口持續上升，我們以往的跨文化研究指出香港的成人在老年準備方面比起其他國家（例如德國、美國等）都要少。我們提出以下的研究來了解香港的成年人比起德國成年人更少為老年做準備的原因、以及老年準備為兩地成人在心理方面帶來的影響。在應用層面，這項研究或能為香港的低老年準備率提供一些解決方案。 至於在理論的層面，基於我們不經意間都會將老年與疾病、易受傷害與各種活動上的限制連在一起，很多人都會視老化為一個壓力源。但現有的研究中卻未曾有系統地研究老年準備背後的機制。根據壓力因應架構，我們提出老年準備是一個就老化帶來的負面心理影響所作出的對應策略。根據架構，要促成老年準備，人們要覺得老化——一個可能充滿挑戰的轉變過程——是與自己相關的，他們亦需要覺得自己有足夠能力控制老年準備，以及自己需要負起老年準備的責任。我們提出當人們覺得老年準備與自己相關（高相關度）、可以控制（高控制度）以及自己有責任為老年生活準備（高責任感），他們會較多為老年做準備，而香港的老年準備率較德國低，可能與上述三項因素（相關度、控制度及責任感）較低有關。在老年準備方面引入壓力因應理論能夠在影響老年準備的心理因素方面帶來新的思維。 當人們能夠成功通過老年準備來應對老化帶來的壓力，理論上他們會有更好的心理質素。我們提出當人們認為在老年準備方面有更高相關度、控制度及責任感，他們會得到更多上述心理上的好處，而香港人比起德國人更少為老年生活做準備，可能與他們從準備中得到較少心理上的好處有關。 為了驗證以上的假說，我們會邀請一個跨文化追縱實驗的參加者參與新一輪的研究（自2012年以來的第四輪），參加者將遍及不同年齡層。除了在以往的研究中一直使用的有關整體老年準備的量表，在新一輪的研究，我們將加入有關不同生活範疇上（例如：家居安排、未來照料需要等）老年準備的相關度、控制度及責任感等的量度工具，以闡明香港成人及德國成人在準備方面的簡況。

14604220.label: Realisation of objectives
14604220.value: We have recruited 362 participants from Hong Kong (Mage=57.6, SD=17.4, 49.17% male), and 1404 participants from Germany (Mage=57.2, SD=17.5, 35.54% male, 63.68% female). In the Hong Kong sample, 252 participants were retained from the previous wave (72.4%). In the Germany sample, 366 participants were retained from the previous wave (69.2%). So the longitudinal sample size is roughly comparable across cultures. To address Objective 1, we tested a lagged mediation model of cross-cultural differences in aging preparation. The culture (0 = Germany, 1 = Hong Kong) main effect on preparation for old age was significant (b = - 1.02, SE = .07, p < .001). This suggests that Hong Kong indeed prepared less for old age than did Germans. We then tested the mediation effect of perceived control, responsibility and self-relevance on the cultural differences between Hong Kong and Germany. We used the mediators of time point n to predict the preparation at time point n+1. There were cultural differences on perceived control (b = - 0.90, SE = .07, p < .001), perceived responsibility (b = - 1.176, SE = .08, p < .001) but not self-relevance (b = - 0.09, SE = .08, p = .25). Preparation for old age was significantly predicted by perceived control (b = 0.81, SE = .16, p <.001) and self-relevance (b = 0.99, SE = .14, p < .001). The direct effect of culture on preparation was still significant (b = -1.98, SE = .34, p < .001). The indirect effect of culture through perceived control was significant (b = - 0.72, SE = .15, p < .001). The indirect effects of culture through responsibility (b = - 0.25, SE = .20, p = .20) and self-relevance (b = - 0.09, SE = .08, p = .26) were nonsignificant. These results suggested that lower perceived control over preparation for old age partially explained why people in Hong Kong prepared for old age less than did Germans. To address Objective 2, we regressed preparation-related outcome (i.e., preparation readiness) and well-being outcomes (i.e., views on aging, positive affect, negative affect, depressive symptoms) on preparation for old age, and we tested whether culture moderated these links. We used time point n preparation to predict for time point n + 1 outcome. Preparation readiness was predicted by aging preparation (b = 0.11, p < .001). This link was moderated by culture (b = - 0.03, p = .04). The association between aging preparation and preparation readiness was stronger in Germany (b = 0.11, p < .001) than in Hong Kong (b = 0.08, p < .001). Views on aging was associated with preparation (b = 0.07, p < .001), but the association was not moderated by culture (b = - 0.03, p = .45). Positive affect was associated with preparation (b = 0.08, p < .001), and the association was moderated by culture (b = - 0.06, p < .01). Among German adults, aging preparation was associated with positive affect (b = 0.07, p < .001). The association between aging preparation and positive affect was nonsignificant in Hong Kong adults (b = 0.01, p = .42). Negative affect was associated with aging preparation (b = - 0.01, p = .048). The association was not moderated by culture (b = -0.005, p = .73). Depressive symptoms were also associated with aging preparation (b = - 0.06, p < .001), and the association was not moderated by culture (b = 0.02, p = .45). After controlling for perceived control, responsibility and self-relevance, the preparation × culture interaction on preparation readiness became nonsignificant (b = - 0.03, p = 0.06). Only perceived control significantly predicted preparation readiness (b = 0.03, p < .001). Controlling for perceived control, responsibility and self-relevance did not affect the culture moderation on positive affect. These results suggest that aging preparation brings more benefits (e.g., sense of readiness, positive affect) in German adults than Hong Kong adults. Perceived control in aging preparation accounts for cultural difference in the effect of preparation and preparation readiness. To address Objective 3, we ran the above models in five domains, including financial preparation, living arrangements, nursing care needs, loneliness, and death and dying. The indirect effect of perceived control was significant across all five domains (finance: b = 0.09, p < .001; living arrangements: b = 0.06, p < .01; nursing care needs: b = 0.06, p < .001; loneliness: b = - 0.18, p < .001; death and dying: b = - 0.10, p = .04). The indirect effect of self-relevance was significant only in the loneliness domain (b = - 0.03, p = .03). Responsibility did not mediate any culture differences in preparation for old age in any domain. This suggests that the mediators explaining cultural differences in aging preparation remain largely consistent across life domains. We regressed domain-specific outcome (perceived readiness of preparation) on domain-specific preparation. We only have cross-sectional data for these variables since they have just been added in this wave. For the financial, living arrangement and loneliness domains, aging preparation was related to greater sense of readiness. Yet, the association was not moderated by culture (ps > .08). In the future care needs domain, preparation predicted greater readiness (b = 0.75, p < .001). The effect was moderated by culture (b = 0.26, p < .001), and it was stronger in Hong Kong (b = 0.90, p < .001) than Germany (b = 0.64, p < .001). In the death and dying domain, aging preparation predicted greater readiness (b = 0.82, p < .001). The effect was moderated by culture (b = 0.17, p < .01), and the effect was stronger in Hong Kong (b = 0.92, p < .001) than in Germany (b = 0.74, p < .001). Controlling for perceived control, responsibility and self-relevance did not affect any of the moderations. Overall, the findings suggest that Hong Kong people prepare less for their old age than do Germans because they perceive less personal control over preparation for old age. Yet, they need to prepare for their old age because preparation actually has stronger benefits for them than for Germans in the future care needs and death and dying domains. All three project objectives have been achieved.

14604220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604220.value: Hong Kong adults prepared less than their German counterparts. Our findings suggested that perceived control over preparation for old age was the most consistent mediator of the cultural difference in aging preparation across life domains. This major finding has been presented at the European Congress of Psychology 2022 in Ljubljana and published in European Journal of Ageing (Park, Hess, FUNG et al., 2022; Output #2). We found that preparation for old age seems to lead to greater preparation readiness and positive affect in German adults than in Hong Kong adults. Yet, in specific domains such as future care needs and death and dying, preparation leads to greater preparation readiness in Hong Kong adults than their German counterparts. This finding has been presented at Ageing as Future 2nd Conference: Conceptions, Contexts, and Challenges. As the project period spans across the COVID-19 pandemic, we had the opportunity to observe that higher COVID-19 worries were associated with more pandemic-induced aging preparation, and this association was stronger for Germans in comparison to those from Hong Kong. These findings were published in a journal article at Journal of Gerontology: Psychological Sciences (Output #1). We also found that a combination of positive views on ageing and preparation for age-related changes is needed for one to make use of the time that is gained with retirement. This finding was published in a journal article at Acta Psychologica (Output #3). Although not directly related to the project objectives, data collected from the project also allowed us to address two research questions on views on aging. First, we found that more contact with older adults was related to more positive views of the self in old age and this effect was mediated by more positive stereotypes of older people. This finding was published in a journal article at Journal of Gerontology: Psychological Sciences (Output #4). Second, we found that experiences of age discrimination negatively affected psychological well-being, but a higher self-reported prevalence of perceived age discrimination in society weakened this negative association. This finding suggests that age discrimination could be getting used to. When age discrimination is more prevalent, it might be taken for granted. Its hurt was felt less although probably not less harmful in reality. This finding was published in a journal article at European Journal of Ageing (Output #5).

14604220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604220.value: Our findings suggested that perceived control in aging preparation played a major role in explaining the lower rate of preparation for old age in Hong Kong adults. We plan to expand on this to investigate autonomy support as a way to increase Hong Kong adults' perceived control over their own preparation. It focuses on nurturing motivational resources (providing a good rationale, encouraging taking initiative and conveying confidence), using noncontrolling language (giving choices), and acknowledging perspectives and feelings. Ongoing research has found autonomy support useful in promoting health-related intentions and planning behaviors (Chung et al., 2018; Legate & Weinstein, 2021; Levy et al., 2008). Following these principles, we initiated a knowledge transfer project and provided preparation for old age lectures and workshops to 144 older adults. We measured whether the lectures and workshops increased their sense of control over preparation for old age. Data analyses are in progress.

14604220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604220.value: Previous literature suggested that Hong Kong adults prepared less for their old age despite enjoying the world’s longest life expectancy. This study investigated what factors underlay the deficit in old-age preparedness in Hong Kong. Compared with German adults, we found that Hong Kong adults prepared less for their old age for two reasons: 1) they had a lower sense of control over their preparation for old age, and 2) aging preparation was less rewarding for them - it led to a lower sense of satisfaction in their preparation and less positive emotion. Findings pinpoint specific mechanisms that may make older adults doing less preparation for their old age. Future promotions in aging preparation should emphasize boosting the targets' sense of control over their preparation and making the preparation process more rewarding.

14604920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604920.value: 最近的證據表明，儘管中國已經達到了絕對高水平的收入不平等，但中國似乎已經達到了與美國相當的高水平的代際地位流動性。 中國是美國夢的新榜樣嗎？ 新中國在社會上的流動性如何，與其他社會的社會相比如何？ 大量有關社會流動性的文獻回顧顯示，社會流動性研究與“美國夢”的概念並沒有很好的聯繫。事實上美國夢不僅強調代際地位的流動性，而且強調流動是在擇優過程中一個人付出努力的結果。但是，流動性文獻幾乎沒有認真注意努力在分層過程中所扮演的角色，更不用說仔細定義此過程的擇優程度，這種概念和測量的欠發達嚴重限制了比較研究。 擬議研究的主要目的是填補這些重要空白。 起點是一個新的概念框架，該框架將努力的概念重新納入了所有社會流動性研究的經典概念框架。 伴隨的創新是開發一種衡量個人努力的新方法，並驗證其在地位獲得過程中的作用。新的框架能夠揭示看似相似的擇優制度中的重大差異。 通過對來自中國和台灣的數據進行初步的試點分析，新框架確實能夠發現兩個中國社會的流動體制之間的巨大差異。中國是同時擁有儒家文化底蘊和共產主義革命的獨特案例，因此，我們的主要目標之一就是將中國與其他兩種社會進行比較：東亞的3個儒家經濟體（日本，韓國，台灣）和5個後共產主義社會（捷克共和國，匈牙利，波蘭，俄羅斯，烏克蘭）。 通過提供一個更豐富的框架來討論和比較流動體制，本研究希望帶來與皮凱蒂(Piketty)和薩伊斯(Saez)相似的社會影響。他們基於收入最高的1％和0.1％的經濟不平等演變的創新測度方法，徹底改變了全球學者，公眾，決策者和選舉候選人之間有關日益嚴重的經濟不平等現象的辯論方式。

14605020.label: Project Objectives
14605020.value: To address social impairment in schizophrenia: Social impairment is pervasive for individuals with schizophrenia and intervention effect is modest. This project will study social motivation, a newer approach to understanding social impairment in schizophrenia. To examine the association between social motivation tendencies and specific schizophrenia symptoms: Rather than treating schizophrenia as a homogeneous clinical phenomenon, this project will examine the differential links between social approach/avoidance and persecutory delusions and social anhedonia respectively. Taking into account multi-dimensionality of schizophrenia and adopting sensitive measures of social motivation tendencies, this project will elucidate inconsistencies in previous studies. To examine social motivation tendencies and social functioning outcome in schizophrenia: For the first time, this project will estimate the extent to which social motivation tendencies contribute to social functioning in patients with schizophrenia at baseline and after 6 months.

14605020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605020.value: 研究目標 本研究項目旨在檢驗社會動機傾向與精神分裂特定癥狀，及其與社會功能之間的相關性。 項目背景 精神分裂症是嚴重的精神障礙，影響1%的人口，造成全球範圍巨大的公共衛生和社會成本。患有精神分裂症人士不僅受病癥影響，他們經受的社交孤立也導致進一步的身心健康困境。解釋患有精神分裂症人群社交孤立的傳統理論從“缺陷”視角入手，研究這一群體的社會認知能力和社交技能。本研究項目採取較為創新的“動機”視角，研究社會動機傾向（即社交中的接近與迴避）。 項目簡述 設計：本實證研究將採用重復量數設計，檢驗社交接近與社交迴避、被迫害妄想以及社會快感缺失之間不同的關係假設。本研究亦將檢驗社會動機傾向、社會功能和孤獨之間的橫向縱向關係。 樣本：我們將邀請126位處於精神分裂症早期的成年患者參加研究。實驗樣本由病程穩定、足以完成研究流程的患者組成，且患者未受到神經認知功能衰退（常見於長期病患）的嚴重影響。參加者事先由臨床專家判斷是否適合參與本研究。 時間：樣本數據於基線以及基線後六個月時收集。 方法：社會動機傾向由Approach-Avoidance Task（AAT，電腦行為範式）測量。臨床癥狀和社會功能由臨床訪談和自陳問卷測評。受試者對於獎勵性和懲罰性的社交刺激的接近與迴避傾向， AAT均具有良好的測量敏感度。臨床訪談評估收集每位參加者特定的病癥概況，使我們得以檢測社會動機傾向與特定的精神分裂症狀（即被迫害妄想與社交快感缺乏）的相對關係。 項目價值 社會動機傾向、特定精神分裂症狀以及社會功能之間的關係在本項目中被首次研究。鑒於社交障礙即使在服用藥物的情況下依然持續存在，而且社交技能與社會認知訓練的療效並不十分顯著，我們的結果將有助於闡明精神分裂症表現型、其背後社會動機傾向與社會功能的聯繫。我們的結果亦可能有助與識別減少精神分裂症狀患者社交障礙的創新療法。

14605120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14605120.value: 論晚清民初詞家對吳文英詞的仿擬

14605120.label: Project Objectives
14605120.value: To understand the transformation of the time-honored ci poetic traditions (eg. the choice of tune titles, allegorical images, and versification rules, etc.) during the end of Qing dynasty and early Republican era under the pressure of modernization. To analyze the poets’ creative emulation of exemplary works, i.e. the techniques deployed by poets to transform the exemplary works. To investigate how poets expressed themselves by drawing upon the experiences of previous works and precedent poets, especially seeking explanations of the popularity of modelling after Wu Wenying's works. To contextualize the poems under studied, which enables a exploration on how pastiches can be related to the poets’ present experiences and how these works can be woven into a complex circumstance in history. To evaluate the value of emulative ci poetry in the Chinese poetic tradition: Emulation works are often considered as unoriginal and are sometimes regarded merely as writing exercises. Works created under the “Fever of Mengchuang” also received similar criticisms. The study will examine and argue that these ci poets deployed innovative methods in their emulation and expressed through various features of Wu Wenying’s works. The traditional appearance can be considered as a “persona”, under which the poets expressed their subtle views and feelings that were relevant to their specific context. To examine the relation between Song and Qing ci poetry: While research has been done in discussing particular reception of Song poets, how Qing poets received the masterpieces in their writings is often neglected. By exploring the interaction between the canonical Song works and their emulative works, the project seeks to shed light on the discussion of the transformation of the genre in a historic sense. It will bridge the lack of research in the relationship between Song and Qing ci poetry.

14605120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605120.value: The project aims to examine and evaluate a large corpus of emulative ci poems written during the late Qing and early Republican era, focusing on its complex relationship with masterpieces of the Song dynasty and modern culture. It centers at the most discussed and controversial poet, Wu Wenying 吳文英, whom was raised to be one of the four leading poets of Song by Zhou Ji 周濟 and became increasingly important in both the fields of critiques and creative writing. Despite fierce criticisms by leaders of the New Cultural Movement, Wu continued to be the model poet among writers. By analyzing these emulative poems, it is hoped to understand how tradition was drawn upon, transformed, and produced new meanings for modern poets. Among Chinese poets, “tradition” is not only honored, but more importantly, gives value to present works. As early as in the Six dynasties, emulative poem (za ni雜擬) became a genre of its own. Ci poetry formed its unique form, subject matter and style in the Song dynasty. Emulation to famous poets, like Su Shi 蘇軾, Li Qingzaho 李清照and Xin Qiji 辛棄疾, started as soon as they finished their works. Wu Wenying, who was previously regarded only as a minor poet, became the canon among late Qing poets. Almost all ci poets in late Qing and after were influenced by Wu in one way or the other. The trend was described as “the fever of Mengchuan” (夢窗熱). In this respect, Wu serves to be the best example in analyzing how ci poets perceived the past works and how they placed their works within the tradition. The project approaches these emulative poems in two directions. First, emulation involves a rather complex process in which the poet tries to define his work by empathizing, challenging and altering the past works. The study explores how the modern poet interacts with the masterpieces and make his present works relevant and significant. Second, contextualization of these poems are essential not only for understanding the implied meanings of the poems, but also enabling an evaluation of emulation as a creative writing strategy deliberately deployed to express subtle present experiences. The study reconsiders the importance of these seemingly “conservative” and “unrelated to the real world” ci poems against the background of tradition forms of literature in the modern period. 在詞學史上，吳文英（1200-1260）詞的起伏升沈是一個值得研究的議題。南宋之時，吳文英雖有詞名，但整體評價不高。張炎將之與姜夔對舉，而貶之以「質實」，其著名的「七寶樓臺」之說非但不是美譽，更成為後人否定夢窗詞的主要論調。元明時期，夢窗詞幾乎無人提及。清初的重要選本中雖然保存了夢窗詞，但其詞名不彰，直到清代中後期才出現變化。周濟《宋四家詞選》以吳文英為一代領袖，且為由南追北之關鍵，欲以吳文英之深澀力矯姜白石之浮滑，夢窗詞之地位驟然提高，廣受詞家注意。晚清王鵬運、鄭文焯、朱祖謀、況周頤多次校勘夢窗詞，使其面貌日趨完善，又通過創作、選詞、評論等大力揄揚，夢窗詞一躍以為詞壇之圭臬，形成所謂「夢窗熱」之潮流。至此夢窗詞乃成為宋詞經典，其評價亦臻至頂峰。 夢窗詞經典化過程背後由許多因素互動而成，探討這些因素有助了解複雜的文學現象。前賢多從詞論入手，已有頗多成果。然而，「夢窗熱」不僅體現在詞學的範疇，對當時的詞家而言，創作才是最終目的，「夢窗熱」要能體現到實踐之中才算是成功。詞家如何在評論之餘，通過研讀揣摩，涵泳玩味，繼而將這些心得在創作中吸收、融化、延續夢窗詞的特點，並加以發揚、新變？學夢窗者半天下，但夢窗詞又是否可學？這些學夢窗者創作實踐的成績如何？凡此，固然屬於夢窗詞經典化所須探討的問題，而將之置於晚清民國文學的大背景中加以探討，更有助加深對這段時期詞壇發展的理解。

14605120.label: Realisation of objectives
14605120.value: The project has analysed a large corpus of emulative ci poems written during the late Qing and early Republican era. It has explored into the time-honored traditions of ci. In terms of tunes and versification rules, I have studied into a few popular tunes created by Song poets, eg. Manjiang hong, Yingti xu, Xihe, Nian nujiao, Yangzhou man, Qi tianle, Shuang huayu to name just a few. The reasons for poets to choose a particular tune can be complex, but some are chosen on purpose. For example Duanmu Cai wrote over 50 poems in the tune Qi tianle, and has influenced his peers, Wang Pengyun to write Qi tianle in Wang’s early years of ci writing. The effect masterpiece is also obvious, for example, after Zhou Banyan wrote about Jinling in the tune Xihe, many Qing and Republican poets followed suit. We observe a rise of popularity of this tune during the late Qing, and it has been used to write about themes related to mourning of a particular place (some about Jinling and some about other politically important places). We observe many recurring themes and tunes originated from the canonical works of the Song dynasty. In researching into these works, I have compared and contrasted how poets drew upon the masterpiece, appropriated it into a new creation against their unique cirumstances. Related to the choice of tune is the versification rules. As the music notes of ci did not survived after the Southern Song, poets could only imagine the melodic characteristics. Through the rise of evidential studies in the Qing era, poets studied the versification rules of Song ci poems. As they were unable to recover most of the music notes, they deduced the versification rules from previous canon works. Although the validity of this method is questionable, late Qing poets were quick to adopt to it as they were anxious to maintain the musical nature of ci poem, what they believed to be the most important characterisitc of ci. Wu Wenying was regarded as a model writer who had erudite knowledge of music (and he was also being described as following the versification rules of Zhou Banyan’s works word by word). Among the poets, Zhu Zumou is a typical example. He followed the versification rules of Wu’s tunes nearly word by word. Although Zhu seemed to be able to convey ideas comfortably under this painstaking practice, it raised heated debates about the purpose and feasibility of it in the 1940s in which poets evaluated again the essence of ci as a genre. As for the mode of allegorical writing, I observe that the Qing poets encountered difficulties when interpreting Wu’s works from the perspective of jitou. Wu’s poems are generally more traditional in themes and imageries. Wu’s writing stands out for its subjectivity. Wu’s works displays unusual way of narration of events and expression of feeling, centred around his very personal and sometimes sudden feelings. He used very subjective adjectives and imageries, that readers may find it hard to understand at the first glance. His poetry, therefore, are seen as rather untraditional, comparing to that of “the very obvious allegorical” poems. In the Reign of Daoguang, the poets focused mainly on adopting the "skills" of Wu’s works. I have regarded this period as the starting point of the “fever of Menchuang” by looking into how Wu was perceived before and after 1830s in anthologies, criticism and poems. Poets under the influence of the School of Changzhou and Wuzhong were obviously trying to change the writing practice by using Wu as an example. Their inspiration may come from Zhang Yan who posed Wu as an opposite to Jiang Kui. They then altered Zhang’s negative comments and regarded them as the unique characteristics of Wu that should be praised. In their poems, they did try to adopt Wu’s twisting narrating style, displaying of array of imageries without linking words, etc. But they have not solved the problem of allegorical writing in order to give Wu’s works more “substance”. In late Qing, Wang Pengyun and Zhu Zumou responded to the question of allegorical writing of Wu's works. They read his ci poems as having subtle allegorical meanings, pointing to his frustration to the waning Southern Song. This interpretation helps to place Wu in the general emphasis of "jitou", particularly popular during the late Qing. Wu’s subjectivity was seen as a vehicle to effectively express complex feelings of poets at the difficult times. They may not copy the imageries used by Wu (like their predecessors), but they adopted his way of creating strong and sometimes even awkward imageries in order to symbolise they feeling of unease. Their works are exceptional that they grasp the essence of Wu without forgoing their own style. They have slightly altered the emphasis of didactic intention in allegorical writing to "youzhong zhiyan" (one’s unique and true feeling). The third stage of “fever of Mengchuang” is from the early Republican period to mid 20th century. While extant research mingled the popularity of Wu’s style with Qing loyalists, the situation is far from a clear cut. Many non-loyalists are also delved into emulating Wu’s work. I have researched into works of Liao Entao, Wang Yi and Wang Pengsheng, all of them are not loyalists. Following the footsteps of former poets, especially Zhu Zumou, many of them followed the versification rules as strictly as possible. Thus, we observe of comeback of emphasis on “skills” (rather than “yi”). In the field of criticism, with the lingering influence of Zhu, many promising young poets studied Wu’s works in depth. Chen Xun, Yang Tiefu and Liu Yongji, all of them having a direct contact with Zhu, represent the most important scholars of Wu in the 20th century. Although all them analysed Wu’s work meticulously, they wrote their poems in different ways. Their works show different approaches in the “fever of Mengchuang”. My evaluation of these emulative poems is that these works requried close reading and should not be criticised as "unoriginal" or "conservative". In fact, in the pre-modern context, it is a compliment to have one's works commented as "like the master's". Poets are not so concerned with "newness" or "originality", instead they stress on whether they can deal with their unique feelings in a way that would fit in the tradition of ci genre. They turned to Wu (and other canonical works) and invented a tradition that they can safely write about subjective and personal feelings without worrying the criticisms that their works were not directly or explicitly reflecting the current affairs. The "tradition" became a "persona" that poets felt free to deal with their complex feelings.

rows: To understand the transformation of the time-honored ci poetic traditions (eg. the choice of tune titles, allegorical images, and versification rules, etc.) during the end of Qing dynasty and early Republican era under the pressure of modernization.
To analyze the poets’ creative emulation of exemplary works, i.e. the techniques deployed by poets to transform the exemplary works.

To investigate how poets expressed themselves by drawing upon the experiences of previous works and precedent poets, especially seeking explanations of the popularity of modelling after Wu Wenying's works.

To contextualize the poems under studied, which enables a exploration on how pastiches can be related to the poets’ present experiences and how these works can be woven into a complex circumstance in history.

To evaluate the value of emulative ci poetry in the Chinese poetic tradition: Emulation works are often considered as unoriginal and are sometimes regarded merely as writing exercises. Works created under the “Fever of Mengchuang” also received similar criticisms. The study will examine and argue that these ci poets deployed innovative methods in their emulation and expressed through various features of Wu Wenying’s works. The traditional appearance can be considered as a “persona”, under which the poets expressed their subtle views and feelings that were relevant to their specific context.

To examine the relation between Song and Qing ci poetry: While research has been done in discussing particular reception of Song poets, how Qing poets received the masterpieces in their writings is often neglected. By exploring the interaction between the canonical Song works and their emulative works, the project seeks to shed light on the discussion of the transformation of the genre in a historic sense. It will bridge the lack of research in the relationship between Song and Qing ci poetry.

14605120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605120.value: The research outcomes (published) are 3 referred journal articles, 5 presented articles given at local and international conferences, and 2 public talks. There are 3 more conference presentations and 1 public talk already arranged in June and August 2024. A monograph is in the process of writting up and is included in the publication plan organized by the Department of Chinese Language and Literature to be published in mid 2025 by the Commercial Press Hong Kong. Major Findings 1. The development of “fever of Mengchuang”: Extant research regards the “fever of Mengchuang” with negative connotation, presenting it as an opposite to the orginial literature, but it is more helpful to examined it from a historicist approach. The Reign of Daoguang is identified as the starting point as Wu appears important in anthologies, critiques and poem writing. Although "yi" (idea of the text) in criticisms, poets focused on Wu's skills in their emulation. The second stage is represented by Wang Pengyun and Zhu Zumou, the two leading ci poets of late Qing, who concerned more the subjectivity in Wu's works. We see in a delicate balance between skill and "yi" in their works. In the third stage, I have researched into two main streams of works. First, the tension between modern experiences and the emulative poem. Liao Entao’s works stand out to be exceptional as his strives to combine Wu's style with experiences in Cuba. For other more traditional poets, I investigated Chen Xun, Yang Tiefu and Liu Yongji, their ci poetry has shown different approaches towards emulation. Other poets like Wang Yi and Wang Pengsheng are also explored to show the different perceptions of ci writing. 2. The issue of emulative poems: Harold Bloom suggests that every new composition is a misreading of an earlier poem, highighting pote's anxiety in surpassing his precursors. In the context this research, whereas indeed poets are deeply influence by the masters, the poet may not be as “anxious”. Instead of aggressively seeking an overcome of Wu, I suggest that Wu is sought as a representation in the literary canon that poets can safely write within this invented “tradition”.

14605120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605120.value: The research has a broader aim in understanding and complicating the relations of masterpieces and works of later poets in a period from pre-modern to modern China. The current project has examined ci poems related to Wu Wenying as a starting point to observe how poets of a transformational time responded to masterpieces. Whereas I recognised Wu as the most influential canon writer, it is noticed, during the course of research, that Jiang Kui, Su Shi and Xin Qiqi also play important roles in shaping the development of republian ci poetry. Further investigation is necessary in order to chart a clearer picture of how the practice of ci poetry writing has changed overtime and how modern ci poetic thoughts are formed. In addition, the current project stressed mainly on the agency of the author (what authors can or choose to do), although I also explored into the circumstantial factors. However, ci poetry writing as practice, in this period in particular, is integrated in a complex network of artictic, philosophical, ideological and historical influences. I will move on to contextualise and theoize the writing practice of ci poetry by emplying a historicist approach to literary studies.

14605120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605120.value: The project has identified "emulative poetry" as an important writing practice of ci widely adopted during the late Qing and early Republican era. It examines and evaluates a large corpus of emulative ci poems, centering at the most discussed and controversial poet, Wu Wenying. Almost all ci poets in late Qing and after were influenced by Wu in one way or the other. The trend was described as “the fever of Mengchuan”. In this respect, Wu serves to be the best example in analyzing how ci poets perceived masterpieces and how they placed their works within the tradition. The project approaches these emulative poems by looking into the process of emulation, exploreing how modern poet appropriates masterpieces in an attmept to make his works relevant both to present and in the tradition. Emulation is seen as a creative strategy deliberately deployed to express the poet's subtle and modern experiences. Thus, the study reconsiders the artistic vaule of these seemingly “conservative” and “unrelated to the real world” ci poems against the background of tradition forms of literature in the modern period.

14605920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605920.value: There is a huge potential for reducing and preventing environment-related disease through a better understanding of the interactions between health and the environment. The proposed research seeks to more accurately assess individual exposure to noise and air pollution (NAP) and its health impacts using real-time individual data collected from human participants by global positioning systems (GPS), mobile noise and air pollutant sensors, and advanced geospatial analytics (e.g., geocomputation and 3D geovisualization). These methods and data will help mitigate three major methodological issues in past studies that can lead to inferential errors and erroneous results: the uncertain geographic context problem (UGCoP), the neighborhood effect averaging problem (NEAP), and the modifiable spatiotemporal unit problem (MSUP). Because of the use of high-resolution real-time GPS data and individual exposure data collected by mobile sensors, the study addresses four major limitations of past studies by taking into account: (a) individuals’ actual activity location and environment in space and time (e.g., workplace, shopping malls); (b) the high-rise living and working environments of the study areas (i.e., how far a participant is from the ground level at a particular moment); (c) indoor exposure to NAP, in contrast to an exclusive focus on outdoor exposure; and (d) the influence of the level of physical activity (through intake modeling) on individual exposure to NAP. By addressing the major methodological issues and limitations of past studies, the results of the proposed study will provide reliable scientific evidence for developing effective preventive measures and policies as well as improving urban designs through facilitating the creation of healthy living environments, which will in turn significantly benefit the residents of the two study areas (Hong Kong and Guangzhou) in the long run. The findings will reveal whether there is significant environmental injustice related to NAP exposure in the study areas and will help inform and encourage residents to adopt specific mitigation measures and modify their space-time behaviors to reduce their NAP exposure and health risk. For example, people with low mobility may reduce their NAP exposure by increasing their mobility (as postulated by the NEAP). If an individual is mobile but his/her daily travel does not lead to mitigation of his/her NAP exposure, the study would try to find out why and suggest measures for addressing the associated disadvantages. 更好地了解健康與環境之間的相互作用有助於減少和預防與環境有關的疾病。本研究計劃旨在使用全球定位系統(GPS)和實時移動感應收集實時個體數據, 通過結合高級地理空間分析方法, 更準確地評估個人的噪聲和空氣污染暴露及其對健康的影響。提出的方法和收集的個體數據將有助於減輕過去的研究中可能導致錯誤結果的三個方法論問題: 地理環境的不確定問題(UGCoP), 鄰里效應平均問題(NEAP)和可變時空單位問題(MSUP)。由於使用了高分辨率實時GPS數據和實時移動感應收集的個人暴露數據, 本研究通過考慮以下四個因素突破了以往研究的主要局限性: (a) 個人在空間和時間上的實際活動位置和環境(例如工作場所和購物中心); (b) 高層居住和工作環境; (c) 室內噪聲和空氣污染暴露; (d) 通過攝入模型研究身體活動水平對個人空氣污染暴露的影響。通過解決這些以往研究的方法論問題和局限性, 本研究的結果將為製定有效的預防措施和政策, 以及通過促進創造健康的生活環境而改善城市設計提供可靠的科學依據, 從而大幅改善居民的健康狀況。長遠來說, 本研究亦將使兩個研究區域(香港和廣州)的居民受益。研究結果將揭示兩個研究區域是否存在與噪聲和空氣污染暴露相關的不公現象, 並將有助於告知和鼓勵居民採取特定的緩解措施並改變其時空行為, 以減少其噪聲和空氣污暴露並降低健康風險。

14605920.label: Realisation of objectives
14605920.value: As described in the last project, the project's progress was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong. Due to the severity of the COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong, the progress of the project has been slower than expected because of the need to reduce the infection risks of the research assistants and participants. As a result, Objective 6 (i.e., to develop a suite of geographic information systems (GIS)-based analytical tools) was eliminated (as explained in the relevant project change request). Further, due to the delays and difficulties encountered in the data collection process, the sample sizes for both Hong Kong and Guangzhou were reduced from 400 to 200 participants for each study area (as explained in the relevant project change request). Since the last reporting period, we successfully collected the data sets from the study areas and analyzed them according to Objectives 1-5. Based on the data analysis, the project has published 13 journal articles. The major findings of these publications are summarized in Section 6.1 below.

14605920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605920.value: The project found that the relationships between individual exposure to noise and air pollution (NAP) and individual daily movement and health are highly complex. These relationships are influenced by the geographic context (new town vs old town), perceived exposures, and individual socioeconomic attributes (e.g., gender, age, income). For instance, Liu et al (2023) found a significant association between people's perceived air quality and their self-reported frequency of respiratory symptoms. However, there are disparities in such an association between different genders, age groups, household income levels, education levels, marital statuses, and geographic contexts. The most striking disparities are between genders and geographic contexts. Song et al (2023) found that people’s exposure to air pollution is significantly higher in residential areas and transportation land-use areas compared to commercial areas. Further, people tend to underestimate air pollution when they are in residential and transportation areas. Cai and Kwan (2023) observed that the associations between individual socioeconomic characteristics and perceived air pollution vary across communities and the value ranges of perceived air pollution, revealing both spatial and value-range nonstationarity. Further, the tendency of different social groups to perceive high levels of air pollution can differ considerably depending on whether they are in their residential or visited neighborhoods. Regarding noise exposures, Cai et al (2023) found that the effects of the real-time sound level and sound increment on personal momentary noise annoyance are nonlinear, despite the overall significant and positive impacts, and different sound characteristics can produce a joint effect on annoyance. The study also observed that the daily activity microenvironments and individual sociodemographic attributes can affect noise annoyance and its relationship with different sound characteristics to varying degrees. Li et al (2024) found that individual-level noise exposure is serious both on workdays and non-workdays in Hong Kong. There are significant inverse relationships between individual-level noise exposure with sleep quality and sleep duration. There are significant inverse relationships between individual-level exposure to noise and sleep quality and sleep duration. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of addressing the uncertain geographic context problem and nonstationary associations when examining the health impacts of noise and air pollution exposures. These factors heavily influence research findings on social inequality related to mobility-dependent environmental exposure. The results can inform the government and residents with scientific evidence to promote the creation of acoustically comfortable and low-air-pollution living environments.

14605920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605920.value: One limitation of the study is that we need more longitudinal data (covering longer periods of time) to conduct robust causal analysis. Future studies should try to use a longer timeline and collect individual-level longitudinal data. Also, future studies should also consider using other widely available big data sources (big mobile phone data sets). These big data sources can help to expand the scope of the study (especially including more people and geographic areas).

14605920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605920.value: There is a huge potential for reducing and preventing environment-related diseases through a better understanding of the interactions between health and the environment. The project assessed individual exposure to noise and air pollution (NAP) and its health impacts using real-time individual data collected from human participants by global positioning systems (GPS) and mobile noise and air pollutant sensors. These methods helped address the major methodological issues and limitations of past studies. The results of the study provide reliable scientific evidence for developing effective preventive measures and policies as well as improving urban designs by facilitating the creation of healthy living environments. The findings revealed complex relationships between environmental factors (noise and air pollution), their health impacts, human mobility, and individual socioeconomic attributes (e.g., gender, income, etc.). These relationships also vary across geographic contexts and value ranges of the environmental factor in question. The findings can help inform and encourage residents to adopt specific mitigation measures and modify their space-time behaviors to reduce their exposure to noise and air pollution and the associated health risks. They can also help the government to promote the creation of acoustically comfortable and low-air-pollution living environments.

14608120.label: Project Objectives
14608120.value: To profile risky online behaviors among early adolescents over three years; To identify the developmental trajectories of risky online behaviors and PTD; and To assess the complex relationships between the various profiles of risky online behaviors and the indicators of PTD.
rows: To profile risky online behaviors among early adolescents over three years;
To identify the developmental trajectories of risky online behaviors and PTD; and
To assess the complex relationships between the various profiles of risky online behaviors and the indicators of PTD.

14608120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14608120.value: This study examines the longitudinal profiles of risky online behaviors among early adolescents and their relationships with indicators of positive technological development (PTD) using a person-centered approach. It attempts to disentangle the complex relationships between risky online behaviors and PTD in order to engage youth in positive technology use. Adolescents living in the Internet era can freely navigate the so-called cyberspace. Whereas the Internet provides instantly available information for educational and entertainment purposes, it also affords anonymity for those who choose to take risks online. Recent years have seen an upsurge in such risky online behaviors as game addiction, online victimization, and cyberbullying. This phenomenon demands our collective efforts to devise appropriate strategies to deal with these behaviors. Whereas the negative impacts of technology on adolescents’ wellbeing have been extensively researched and reported in society and academia, this study uses the PTD framework proposed by Bers, Lynch, and Chau (2012) to delineate and promote the positive development of young people in technology-rich contexts. In the framework, there are six assets of PTD, called the six Cs: competence, confidence, character, connection, caring, and contribution. Specifically, this study extends previous research by adopting a person-centered approach to profile risky online behaviors among early adolescents over three years and identifying the developmental trajectories of their risky online behaviors and PTD. Most importantly, it assesses the intricate relationships between the various profiles of risky online behaviors and the indicators of PTD. In doing so, this study addresses the perennial issue that risky online behaviors are manifested differently in different young people and are differentially associated with different positive outcomes. Theoretically, the study will provide findings for researchers to understand interindividual differences in intraindividual characteristics of risky online behaviors and PTD and to articulate their complex relationships longitudinally. Practically, parents and teachers will be better informed as to how to communicate and negotiate with the current generation of adolescents about the importance of PTD. The Education Bureau may utilize the findings of the study to design and implement integrated and individualized evidence-based youth development programs to help those youth who suffer from online behavioral problems from the perspective of PTD. Policymakers will be more equipped with knowledge and understanding to formulate developmentally attentive youth policy to improve the lives of youth and their families. 這項研究使用以個體中心取向的方法，調查了早期青少年網上風險行為的縱向剖面及其與正面科技發展指標的關係。它試圖解開網上風險行為與正面科技發展之間的複雜關係，以使青少年參與正面的技術使用。互聯網時代的青少年可以自由瀏覽網絡空間。儘管互聯網為青少年的教育和娛樂提供了即時可用的信息，它亦為那些選擇網上冒險的人提供了匿名性。近年來，諸如遊戲成癮，網上受害和網絡欺凌等網上風險行為激增。這種現象需要我們共同努力，以製定適當的策略來應對這些行為。儘管社會和學術界已廣泛研究並報導了科技對青少年福祉的負面影響，本研究使用了Bers，Lynch和Chau（2012）提出的正面科技發展框架來描述和促進青少年在科技使用方面的正面發展。在這框架中，正面科技發展包含六項資產：能力，信心，性格，關係，關懷和貢獻。具體而言，本為期三年的研究通過採用以個體中心取向的方法來描述早期青少年的網上風險行為，並確定其網上風險行為和正面科技發展的軌跡，從而擴展了先前的研究。最重要的是，它評估了網上風險行為的各種特徵與正面科技發展指標之間的複雜關係。通過這樣的分析，本研究解決了長期存在的問題，即網上風險行為在不同的青少年中表現出不同的特徵，並且與不同的正面結果存在不同的關係。從理論上而言，本研究將為研究人員提供一些發現，以了解網上風險行為和正面科技發展的個別化特徵之間的個體差異，並闡明它們之間的複雜縱向關係。實際上，家長和老師將更加了解如何與當代的青少年溝通和協商有關正面科技發展的重要性。教育局亦可以利用本研究的結果設計和實施個體化的綜合青少年發展計劃，並從正面科技發展的角度幫助遭受網上風險行為問題困擾的青少年。決策者將對相關的問題更加了解，從而製定具有針對性的青年政策，以改善青少年及其家人的生活。

14608120.label: Realisation of objectives
14608120.value: All three objectives were achieved successfully. To address the first objective about profiling risky online behaviors among early adolescents over three years, we conducted latent class analysis (LCA) to identify distinct classes of early adolescents with specific risky online behaviors. Based on the survey data collected from the participants at the first three time points, we identified two classes of students, namely low- and high-risk classes, and most of them were found in the low-risk class. Latent transition analysis indicated that the low-risk class exhibited higher stability than the high-risk class over time. Those in the high-risk class were moderately likely to transition to the low-risk class (Lau et al., 2024b). We therefore expected that only one class of students will exist in the long term. LCA with the survey data at the six time points yielded one class of students with very few risky online behaviors at each time point; no class transition was observed between the time points (Lau et al., under review). Regarding the second objective about identifying the developmental trajectories of risky online behaviors and positive technological development (PTD), we constructed latent growth curve models (LGCMs). These models showed that risky online behaviors among students were stable and mild and yet a significant decrease in PTD over time was noted based on the survey data at the first three time points (Lau et al., 2024b). However, LGCMs indicated that students’ risky online behaviors increased over time, although their PTD did not significantly change considering the survey data at the six time points (Lau et al., under review). For the third objective about the complex relationships between the various profiles of risky online behaviors and the indicators of PTD, we performed multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) tests to examine any significant differences in PTD at the three time points across all classes of risky online behaviors. The MANOVA results revealed no significant differences in PTD between the two classes of students at the first three time points (Lau et al., 2024b). Because LCA identified one class of early adolescents at each time point over the six time points, no MANOVA test could be conducted to analyze any significant differences in PTD between the latent classes of risky online behaviors at the six time points. A parallel process latent growth model (PPLGM) was constructed to investigate the longitudinal associations between risky online behaviors and PTD among early adolescents. PPLGM showed that risky online behaviors and PTD were uncorrelated longitudinally (Lau et al., under review). This result concurs with the corresponding findings from parents’ interviews conducted both concurrently and longitudinally (Lau et al., 2022, 2024a). When parents were asked about the relationships between risky online behaviors and PTD in early adolescents in a cross-sectional interview, some parents claimed that their children exhibited PTD more often than they participated in risky online behaviors. Some parents reported that their children exhibited both positive and risky online behaviors equally, and others reported that their children exhibited either positive or risky online behaviors. Factors like personal interests and peer influence mediated these relationships (Lau et al., 2022). Longitudinally, parents also expressed diverse views about risky online behaviors and PTD among their children and the relationships between them. The father in one family said that both positive and negative influences of technology on his son were observed initially; however, he found more negative than positive influence of technology on his son one year later. The mother in another family reported no negative influence of technology on his son at first. By contrast, the father in this family believed that the influence of technology was more negative than positive one year later (Lau et al., 2024a).

14608120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14608120.value: Here are the major findings of the study: (1) Gender, computer experience, and computer proficiency significantly affected early adolescents’ risky online behaviors and PTD whereas average daily duration of computer/internet usage at home and at school significantly affected early adolescents’ risky online behaviors only (Lau et al., 2021). (2) When parents limited their children’s online activities, their children tended to refuse to share the Internet content they consume with their parents. When parents did not restrict their children’s Internet use, their children used the Internet either excessively or in moderation. Parents in a family typically adopted the same styles in regulating their children’s Internet use (Lau et al., 2022). Parents increasingly recognized the negative influence of technology on their children over time and their parenting styles changed between permissive and authoritarian styles contingent upon their children’s risky online behaviors (Lau et al., 2024a). (3) Across the six time points, on average, early adolescents never participated in risky online behaviors such as unauthorized acts, online pornography, or cyberbullying. They showed some dependence on the Internet but seldom used plagiarized materials. Over time, they demonstrated a considerable PTD. On average, they knew how they could utilize technology to make a positive impact on society and possessed a certain level of technological efficacy. They were also good at using technology to connect with people (Lau et al., under review). (4) Early adolescents cannot be differentiated into different classes based on their risky online behaviors over time, indicating that they were homogeneous in terms of such behaviors. However, such behaviors significantly increased over time. On the other hand, early adolescents’ PTD did not significantly change over time. There were no significant associations between risky online behaviors and PTD among early adolescents over time (Lau et al., under review).

14608120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14608120.value: Despite the contributions made by this study, researchers should consider the following issues in future studies. First, this study relied on self-report data provided by early adolescents. Early adolescents may not clearly know about their risky online behaviors and PTD, and response bias is possible. Future studies should collect additional data through other methods, such as behavioral observations or interviews, to provide a more comprehensive understanding of risky online behaviors and PTD among early adolescents. Second, future studies should invite a large sample of early adolescents with diverse sociocultural backgrounds to examine the effects of these backgrounds on their risky online behaviors and PTD. Third, future studies should collect views from both parents and teachers to understand early adolescents’ risky online behaviors and PTD holistically. Parents and teachers are crucial agents in shaping early adolescents’ digital experiences and can provide useful insights into these issues. Finally, factors influencing the longitudinal associations between early adolescents’ risky online behaviors and PTD should be investigated in future studies.

14608820.label: Project Objectives
14608820.value: Design and implement an SRL-based CC reading intervention program to enhance HK students’ CC reading comprehension and motivation: The study will extend the PI’s previous GRF project by adopting a longitudinal and holistic design to include both in-class instruction and out-of-class eLearning activities in a two-year instruction program. The program consists of four phases and aims to gradually guide students’ development of SRL through the observational, emulation, self-controlled, and self-regulation levels. Determine whether the inclusion of eLearning activities will strengthen the effectiveness of the program: Unlike previous studies that adopted either in-class instruction or eLearning to enhance students’ SRL, this study combines both types of instruction in the program. It aims to overcome the problem of a lack of student autonomy in traditional CL classes and provides sufficient teacher support for students when they have not fully developed into self-regulated learners. Provide rigorous data for program evaluation: In contrast to existing CC reading literature, which is mainly based on subjective observations or survey methods, this study adopts a quasi-experimental design to provide objective and reliable data to examine the effectiveness of SRL-based instruction in facilitating students’ CC reading development. Explore the applicability of SRL-based instruction in a Chinese context: The instructional principles of SRL are largely different from traditional Chinese instruction. By applying SRL-based instruction to teaching CC reading, a subject area that is deeply influenced by traditional Chinese culture, the study should shed light on the cross-cultural value of SRL-based instruction.
rows: Design and implement an SRL-based CC reading intervention program to enhance HK students’ CC reading comprehension and motivation: The study will extend the PI’s previous GRF project by adopting a longitudinal and holistic design to include both in-class instruction and out-of-class eLearning activities in a two-year instruction program. The program consists of four phases and aims to gradually guide students’ development of SRL through the observational, emulation, self-controlled, and self-regulation levels.

Determine whether the inclusion of eLearning activities will strengthen the effectiveness of the program: Unlike previous studies that adopted either in-class instruction or eLearning to enhance students’ SRL, this study combines both types of instruction in the program. It aims to overcome the problem of a lack of student autonomy in traditional CL classes and provides sufficient teacher support for students when they have not fully developed into self-regulated learners.

Provide rigorous data for program evaluation: In contrast to existing CC reading literature, which is mainly based on subjective observations or survey methods, this study adopts a quasi-experimental design to provide objective and reliable data to examine the effectiveness of SRL-based instruction in facilitating students’ CC reading development.

Explore the applicability of SRL-based instruction in a Chinese context: The instructional principles of SRL are largely different from traditional Chinese instruction. By applying SRL-based instruction to teaching CC reading, a subject area that is deeply influenced by traditional Chinese culture, the study should shed light on the cross-cultural value of SRL-based instruction.

14608820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14608820.value: Background Self-regulated learning (SRL) is an effective but demanding form of learning. While different SRL instructional principles and types of eLearning have been proposed to enhance students’ learning, both types of instruction have strengths and limitations. Previous experiences of implementing SRL-based instruction in Hong Kong (HK) Chinese language (CL) classes indicate that teachers and students are less favorable to instructional principles that place more emphasis on student autonomy. Due to the difficulties students experience in Classical Chinese (CC) reading, it is more demanding for them to develop SRL in CC reading. Aim The study adopts a holistic and longitudinal approach to integrate in-class instruction and out-of-class eLearning activities into a two-year SRL-based CC reading intervention program. In-class instruction will help students establish a good foundation for CC reading and compensate for the common problem of a lack of teacher support in eLearning, while eLearning activities will provide opportunities for students to apply their self-regulatory skills to independently read CC texts. By utilizing the strengths of both types of instruction, the program aims to gradually enhance students’ CC reading comprehension and motivation through the four developmental levels of SRL. Research Plan The study adopts a pretest-posttest treatment-control group quasi-experimental design. One secondary school will be invited to conduct the experiment. Students from one junior secondary grade in this school will be randomly assigned to two experimental treatments, one with in-class SRL-based instruction plus out-of-class eLearning (EG-I+E group) and one with in-class SRL-based instruction only (EG-I group). Another school with similar student backgrounds that uses the same CL textbook will serve as a control group (CG). Quantitative and qualitative methods, including reading tests, questionnaires, interviews, and classroom observations, will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the program. Teachers and students’ perceptions on what, how, and why the program may enhance students’ CC reading ability and motivation will also be explored through qualitative data analysis. Significance The study will extend the PI’s previous GRF project, which was the first to integrate SRL into CC reading instruction, by adopting a longitudinal and holistic design. The findings should provide valuable insights into the applicability of SRL-based instruction in non-Western contexts. The study also makes a first attempt to integrate in-class SRL instruction and out-of-class eLearning activities into CC reading instruction. The findings should shed light on the possibility of combining these two types of instruction to achieve greater positive effects on facilitating students’ SRL.

14609020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14609020.value: Loneliness is prevalent among older adults and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. With population ageing and changes in family structure, it is estimated that up to 30% of older adults experience loneliness. Despite this prevalence, limited evidence-based interventions are readily available in the community. Mindfulness-based interventions are group interventions that effectively improve mental well-being. Several studies have demonstrated their potential effectiveness for loneliness, although only one small study has been conducted in older adults and none have been conducted in Chinese. Therefore larger, better-designed studies are needed. We will perform a two-arm randomised controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a modified mindfulness programme, mindfulness-based intervention for older adults (MBOA), in reducing loneliness. Two hundred and forty Chinese older adults with loneliness in the community will be recruited and randomly assigned to MBOA or a group social contact control (SCC) with a 12-month follow up. We hypothesise that MBOA will have a positive effect on monitoring and self-acceptance, which mediate the effect on loneliness. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, immediately after intervention and six and 12 months after randomisation. Results from this study could provide an innovative intervention for older adults with loneliness, and this will be the first mindfulness-based intervention study for loneliness among older Chinese adults. 長者普遍感到孤獨，孤獨感常與高發病率和高死亡率有關。隨著人口老齡化和家庭結構的變化，估計多達30％的長者感到孤獨。儘管這種情況很普遍，現時社區提供的有科學依據的干預方法卻只有很少。基於靜觀的小組干預是有效改善心理健康的方法之一。雖然多項研究已證明靜觀對孤獨感的潛在效用，但是只有一項小型研究應用此方法在非中國籍的長者身上。因此，我們需要設計嚴謹的大型研究以評估其療效。本團隊將進行一項兩臂隨機對照試驗，以評估靜觀干預（MBOA）對減少長者孤獨感的功效。團隊將在社區中招募240名有孤獨情緒的中國籍長者，並被隨機分配至靜觀干預組或小組社交對照組（SCC）。我們預計靜觀干預對自我管理和自我接納有正面影響，從而減少長者的孤獨感。參加者將在干預前，干預後， 及隨機分配後6個月和12個月接受評估。這項研究可以為有孤獨感的長者提供創新的干預措施，這將是第一個運用靜觀干預改善中國籍長者孤獨感的研究。

14609820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14609820.value: 香港青年遊戲成癮：社會性代間傳遞理論

14609820.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14609820.value: Prof Lau, Joseph Tak Fai Prof Wong, Samuel Yeung-shan Prof Wu, Man Sze Anise

14609820.label: Project Objectives
14609820.value: Objective 1: This three-wave longitudinal study (T1, T2, and T3), with two 1-year interval periods, will investigate the prevalence of adolescent and parental Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), and rates of incidence (i.e., from non-IGD at baseline to IGD at follow-up), remission (i.e., from IGD at baseline to non-IGD at follow-up), recurrence (i.e., IGD at T1->non-IGD at T2->IGD at T3) of IGD in adolescents and parents (family dyads). Rationale: -----With the wide use of computer and smartphone, Internet gaming has become an indispensable part of the majority of adolescents’ daily life. However, Internet gaming can be addictive and problematic. IGD is defined as ‘a pattern of excessive and prolonged Internet gaming that results in a cluster of cognitive and behavioral symptoms, including progressive loss of control over gaming, tolerance, and withdrawal symptoms that are analogous to those of substance use disorders’ 1. According to American Psychological Association (APA, 2013) and World Health Organization (WHO, 2018), IGD is an emerging global health issue. ----Prevalence of adolescent IGD is high and has been rising dramatically, especially in Chinese and Asian populations 2. Little is known about the rates of incidence, remission and recurrence of adolescent IGD. ----Prevalence of Internet use and gaming among adults has been increasing 3. However, there is no study reporting prevalence of IGD of parents. Little is known about the rates of incidence, remission and recurrence of their IGD. Objective 2 (primary objective): This study will identify the relationships between parents self-reported IGD at baseline and adolescents’ self-reported IGD at baseline and follow-up, after controlling for important covariates at personal, interpersonal and familial levels. Rationale: ----The newly defined disorder implies quests for a better understanding of the predictive factors and effective treatment. The family has long been identified as important for health development and as the primary socialization agent for each new generation. Few studies have investigated family/parental (vs personal) factors of adolescent IGD 4. ----The transmission of behaviors (e.g., gambling) from parents to children is generally termed intergenerational transfer. Potential intergenerational transmission of problematic Internet gaming of parents may increase the risk of children’s IGD. There is a dearth of related studies. Identifying whether parents’ behaviors affect adolescent IGD will help to illuminate the dynamics of IGD at family levels and develop a healthy family system. Objective 3: This study will test two types of mediators at T2 of the associations between parental IGD at T1 and adolescent IGD at T3, after controlling significant covariates. The first type of mediator is parental modeling, assessed by adolescents’ self-reported perceived parents’ Internet gaming behaviors and attitudes. The second type of mediator is parenting practices, assessed by parents’ self-reported general parenting practices and specific parental mediation on Internet gaming. Rationale: ----Two socially-based (vs gene-based) theories may explain the intergenerational transmission of IGD: the social learning theory and parenting practice theory. Based on the two theories, this study will test two potential processes (mechanisms): parental modeling and parenting practices. These potential mediators (vs genetic predisposition) are modifiable, and can be used to develop family-based interventions for IGD prevention and reduction. ----1) Parental modeling mechanism: The social learning theory suggests that parents’ negative behaviors will have negative modeling effects on children; children may frequently observe their parents’ gaming and perceive their parents’ positive gaming attitudes. In turn, such negative modeling effects will increase the risk of children’s IGD. ----2) Parenting practices mechanism: Parents with problematic behaviors are more likely to reduce and have poor general parenting practices and specific mediation on children’s Internet gaming; in turn, reduced and poor parenting will increase the risk of children’s IGD. Objective 4: This study will test the moderation effects of gender on the direct and indirect associations between parents’ IGD and adolescent IGD. Rationale: ----There may exist gender-specific effects on the intergenerational transmission of IGD. For example, given that males are generally more likely to play games excessively, fathers may tend to be the stronger negative modeling influence. On this basis, including cooperative fathers who play games in future family-based interventions for adolescents may be beneficial to all parties. The gender-specific effects on intergenerational transmission of IGD have not been tested in previous studies.

14609820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14609820.value: Introduction Adolescent Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) causes severe physical, psychological, and social harms; the prevalence and incidence is unknown in Hong Kong. It is a newly defined disease according to WHO (2018). Family and parents play critical roles in adolescent IGD. Based on the socially-based intergenerational transmission theories, parental IGD may increase the risk of adolescent IGD directly and indirectly through two mechanisms: 1) parental modeling (behavior and attitudes) of the parent by the child, and 2) parenting practices (general parenting and parental mediation on Internet gaming). There is a dearth of related studies. Objectives The primary objective is to test the longitudinal association between parental IGD and adolescent IGD, after controlling for covariates at personal, interpersonal and familial levels. The secondary objective is to test the mediation effects of negative parental modeling (perceived parents’ behaviors and gaming attitudes) and compromised parenting practices (general parenting and parental mediation on Internet gaming) on the intergenerational transmission. Gender-specific effects on these associations will be tested. The prevalence and conversion rates of incidence, remission and recurrence of IGD over years will be investigated. Subjects and methods This study is a two-year 3-wave longitudinal study. Adolescents will be recruited from Secondary schools using stratified random sampling method. One parent of each adolescent will be invited. Students will finish a set of validated psychological scales in class-room settings, while parents will finish their questionnaires through telephone interviews at Time1, Time2, and Time3. Outcomes The primary outcome is adolescent IGD symptoms based on DSM-5 IGD symptoms checklist. The secondary outcomes include time spent on Internet-related activities including gaming and gaming attitudes of adolescents. Data analysis Univariate and multivariate linear/logistic regression analyses will be conducted to test the associations between parental factors (including parental IGD, parental modeling, and parenting practices) and adolescent IGD. Mediation effects of parental modeling, and parenting practices will be tested based on bootstrapping analyses. (Multigroup) Structural Equation Models are also used to test the mediation and moderation effects. SPSS 22.0, PROCESS and Mplus Version 8.1 will be used. Implications This study will clarify the level of adolescent IGD in Hong Kong to inform policy and planning. It delineates mechanisms concerning intergenerational transmission of adolescent IGD, and shed light on the development of timely and innovative prevention programs based on a family approach and evidence-informed parental training. 二零一八年，世界衛生組織正式列遊戲成癮為精神疾病，遊戲成癮會對青少年造成嚴重的生理、心理及社交損害，而家庭及父母對青少年遊戲狀況影響深遠，惟香港目前缺乏青少年遊戲成癮的相關數據及父母對子女影響的相關研究。根據社會性代間傳遞理論，父母遊戲成癮會透過兩個機制提高子女遊戲成癮的風險：1)父母示範（子女模仿父母的行為及態度）及2)管教模式（日常管教模式及對子女玩電子遊戲的介入方式）。 目的 主要目的為研究父母及子女遊戲成癮的關係（在控制個人、人際及家庭層面的協變量後）。次要目的為研究父母示範及管教模式對代間傳遞有何間接影響。同時研究性別對這些關係的影響及遊戲成癮的普及率、緩解率及復發率。 對象及方法 研究為期兩年，其中包括三次調查。團隊會透過中學以分層抽樣方式邀請青少年及其父或母參與研究。在三個時間點，學生均會在課室填寫經認證的心理量表，而家長會透過電話調查完成問卷。 結果 主要結果為青少年的遊戲成癮症狀（根據精神疾病診斷與統計手冊-第五版的遊戲成癮症狀列表量度）。次要結果為青少年的上網時間（包括網絡遊戲時間）及對遊戲的取態。 數據分析 研究將透過單元及多元線性/羅吉斯迴歸分析了解父母相關因素（包括：父母遊戲成癮、父母示範及管教模式）及青少年遊戲成癮的關係。另外以自助抽樣法研究父母示範及管教模式的中介效果，及以結構方程模型分析調節及中介效果。研究使用的軟件包括SPSS 22.0, PROCESS 及Mplus Version 8.1。 應用 本研究將釐清香港青少年的遊戲成癮率以助制定相關政策，亦會分析青少年遊戲成癮背後的代間傳遞機制，同時根據家庭理論及數據就發展適時及創新的管教模式提出建議。

14610020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14610020.value: 早期中華帝國的戰爭經驗與日常軍事史

14610020.label: Project Objectives
14610020.value: To facilitate a comprehensive understanding of the history of warfare in early and early medieval China, with a particular focus on the period between the late third century BCE and the sixth century CE, i.e., from the establishment of the Qin dynasty to the end of the Northern and Southern Dynasties. To study the practices and institutions of military logistics in early and early medieval China and their impacts on the ordinary soldiers. To reconstruct certain facets of battle scenes, combat experiences, and daily lives of common soldiers in early and early medieval China by making use of textual and pictorial materials. To examine the mechanism of military bounty, primarily with monetary but also with other forms of rewards, that was in practice during early and early medieval China. To realize points 2, 3, and 4 with the publication of three items of research output in the form of journal articles or book chapters. To provide substance for the writing of a book on war experiences of the soldiers in early and early medieval China. To offer a basis for comparative study of war with other pre-modern societies in a world historical context.
