14610020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610020.value: The reading of the earliest historical records informs us that war has been an essential feature of human civilization. A common thread runs through various narratives of the formation of early states—the legendary hero appeared on to save his people, he advanced their well-being, and established or restored order as a result of notable victories in decisive battles. Just as it appears to build states, war is the only devastating force apart from natural disasters that could bring apocalyptic scenarios to human societies. War terrifies people, but people keep making war. The leaders decide whether or not and where to go to war, but the ordinary soldiers have to do the fighting and endure hardships and sufferings during and after the campaigns. Studying what the ordinary soldiers experienced in the processes of preparing and conducting war will contribute to the study of a wide range of topics in the fields of military, social, and cultural history. While the study of the operation of warfare as well as the daily lives of soldiers and their combat experiences in ancient Mesopotamia, Greece, and Rome has increasingly expanded in depth and breadth in recent decades, research in similar topics about China still lags far behind. Yet, ancient China is important for its long and continuous history of warfare and also the varied development in certain aspects of war from that in western Eurasia. The Chinese cases therefore offer a trove of information to facilitate our understanding of world history of warfare. This project aims to synthesize historical materials, including received textual and non-textual sources and recent archaeological findings relevant to soldiers, armies, and warfare, to depict facets of the daily operation of military campaigns and fighting experiences of soldiers in early and early medieval China, with a particular focus on the late third century BCE to the sixth century CE. This project also brings together materials of military history from outside China. Based on a comparative perspective, stories from other earlier and contemporary civilizations will provide important insights into the soldiers’ lives in early and early medieval China. While this project will provide references for historians across various fields, as history of war is always a popular genre of reading, it will also interest the general public. 從遠古以來的證據所示，戰爭伴隨著人類文明而生。細究各項關於早期國家形成的論述，可以發現當中的一個共同線索——傳說中的英雄為了拯救他的子民而出現，並且為了保護人民的福祉，在決定性的戰役中取得了勝利而建立或恢復了秩序。儘管戰爭是建立國家的手段，但它也是除了自然災害以外唯一能給人類社會帶來災難性後果的毀滅性力量。人類懼怕戰爭，但仍不斷發動戰爭。要不要打仗？要到哪裡打仗？基本由在上位者決定，而普通的士兵卻要在戰場上和戰後，忍受傷痛和各類折磨。研究普通將士在戰前和戰時的經歷，將有助於軍事、社會和文化史領域研究的推進。 近幾十年來，學者們對古美索不達米亞、希臘、羅馬等地戰爭經驗的研究不斷發展，反觀對於同時期的中國史，在類似的問題研究上卻遠遠落後。然而，古代中國的戰爭史有著悠久的記錄，在某些方面還與歐亞大陸西部的文明有著不同的發展軌跡，仔細研究的話，當可以發現當中為我們理解世界戰爭史提供了寶貴的參考價值。 本項目旨在綜合各類史料，以描繪公元前3世紀晚期至公元6世紀之間，早期中華帝國一些軍事活動的日常運作與將士的作戰實態。本項目亦將透過中國以外地區的軍事史資料，在比較的視野下，為進一步理解早期中華帝國時期將士的生活提供參考。鑒於戰爭史長期備受讀者青睞，相信本項目不僅將為各個領域的史家提供參考，也可以激發公眾的興趣。

14610020.label: Realisation of objectives
14610020.value: To realize the objectives, I have produced journal articles and book chapters, finished a book manuscript, and delivered public lectures (details are in the section of research outcome) on the subject of the current project. The research outcome of this project has covered the history of warfare in classical and early medieval China, with special attention on the military logistics in the form of rivine warfare and the mechanism of pecuniary rewards for military merits. The research articles and book chapter have provided a solid base of a book manuscript that I have finished and sent to the press for review, which will be a monograph covering a range of topics about military history in early imperial China. It will certainly acjnowledge the support of RGC when the book is successfully published. The only shortcoming is that the time being taken for publication is longer than expected, therefore some of the research output have been accepted but still not out yet. The impact of the research output will be realized in the coming years.

14610020.label: Major findings and research outcome
14610020.value: For this project, I have published “The Tactical Role of Rivers in Early Chinese Warfare” in _Journal of Chinese Military History_, which provides a kaleidoscopic view of how the early Chinese military prepared for, carried out, and thought about riverine warfare. It focuses not only on the theoretical discussions in the military treatises but also on the routine tactical functions of waterways in military operations. This article advances our understanding of the significance of military logistics and its limitation and stimulation on the development of early Chinese military tactics. Meanwhile, another paper entitled "Quantifying Accomplishments, Rewarding Performance—Military Bounties in Early Imperial China"has been accepted by the _Journal of American Oriental Society_ and will be published in 2025. It illuminates one of the obscure aspects of military rewards in early imperial China and shows how the early empires employed material and monetary rewards rewards as a response to the changing political, social, and military circumstances. It provides a new understanding of early imperial Chinese military culture and institution and casts new light on comparing military bounties practiced by ancient empires. Furhermore, I have also contributed an essay entitled "Warfare in the Qin, Han, and Northern and Southern Dynasties" to the _Routledge Encyclopedia of Chinese Studies_, which will be fully launched in 2025/26. The essay provides a concise and upadted account the military lives, practices, and institutions of early imperial China, which forms a useful reference for those who are interested in the military history of the period. I have also collaborated with historians of late imperial China in a forthcoming edited volume about pre-modern statecraft, to which I contributed a chapter on early Chinese notions of warfare and military preparations and how this tradition influenced later imperial Chinese thinker. It is also a finding in the course of working on the present project. The volume has completed and is under contract with Cambridge University Press; it is expected to be published in 2025. Besides publications, I have taken opportunities to give several presentations and public talks to share my research findings with other colleagues and the general audience. To the public, they found the new interpretation and understanding of early Chinese warfare, particularly the daily life of soldiers, are interesting and inspiring.

14610020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14610020.value: Based on this research project, I have also completed a book manuscript on the interactive relationship between war, state, and society in early China, which is now under review by a university press. When it is published, it will definitely advance our understanding of the history of warfare in early China and also enhance comparative study on empire and warfare in the ancient world.

14610020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14610020.value: Through the cases of military logistics, tactics, riverine warfare, reward systems, and daily lives of soldiers, this provides a comprehensive and novel understanding of ancient Chinese warfare and the relationship between war and society. It concerns not only military leaders and politics but also the experience of ordinary soldiers, which is a perspective of history from below.

14610220.label: Project Objectives
14610220.value: To investigate how job applicants’ gender and family care responsibilities affect employers’ evaluation scores and hiring decisions in Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Six types of job candidates will be comparatively analyzed: (1) a man without family care duties; (2) a woman without family care duties; (3) a man taking care of young children; (4) a woman taking care of young children; (5) a man taking care of ageing parents; and (6) a woman taking care of ageing parents. To examine how employers’ evaluations and hiring decisions differ in different industries and sectors, in hiring units and establishments of different employment sizes, and for different job categories. These differences will be explored in both Hong Kong and Shenzhen. To understand how the different welfare arrangement and institutions in Hong Kong, in the public sector of Shenzhen, and in the private sector of Shenzhen shape employers’ attitudes and practices with job applicants of different gender and with different family care duties. Dual mechanisms through structural resource constraints defined by different welfare policies and cultural meaning construction of gender and family care responsibilities under different welfare orientations will be investigated in both locations. To generate implications for social service planning and policy making in Chinese societies, in the areas of family support, labor protection, work-family balance, sex and family status discrimination, and equal opportunities in employment, so as to achieve social equality, social justice, and better human societies.

14610220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610220.value: The aim of this project is to conduct mixed-methods and comparative research in Hong Kong and Shenzhen on how job applicants’ gender and various family care responsibilities affect employers’ evaluations and hiring decisions in different employment contexts and in different welfare systems. Although the world is rapidly ageing and birth rates are low, high-quality and affordable care outside the home for young children and elderly people remains paradoxically scarce. Family members, usually women, have to deliver and organize care for children and ageing parents inside the household. Although work-family balance is much emphasized in labor policies globally, the impact of family care responsibilities on employment and career development of family caregivers has not yet been sufficiently explored. Previous studies in various countries of the conflicts between family care responsibilities and labor force participation have mainly focused on “motherhood penalty”, and have closely examined the negative effects of child rearing on the mother’s career development (Correll, Benard, & Paik, 2007). Some comparative research on the impacts of fatherhood and caring for ageing parents in the workplace has recently emerged but the conclusions are often contradictory (Weicht, 2015). While systematic inquiries into the impacts of gender and family care duties in the job market are limited, the structural, social, and cultural contexts in which these impacts are constructed, practiced, and understood are even less examined. The proposed study aims to bridge these research gaps, by investigating how applicants’ gender and different family care responsibilities affect employers’ evaluations and hiring decisions in Hong Kong and Shenzhen. We will also investigate how the effects differ in different industries and sectors, in establishments of different employment sizes, and for different job categories. Based on a comparison of Hong Kong and Shenzhen, we will pay particular attention to the macro welfare institutions, and explore how structural resource constraints and cultural meaning constructions in different welfare systems shape employers’ views and practices regarding gender and family care duties. This study adopts comparative and cross-cultural perspectives to examine the separate and interwoven effects of gender and various family care responsibilities in the job market, and emphasizes the importance of further understanding these effects in different structural contexts and through different welfare systems. Its findings will not only enrich our theoretical knowledge of gender, family care, paid labor market, and workplace inequality, but also inform evidence-based service planning and policy-making to achieve family support, labor protection, work-family balance, and social justice. 本研究運用混合研究方法在香港和深圳展開比較研究，旨在探討在不同的雇傭環境和福利體系内，求職者的性別和家庭照顧責任會如何影響雇主對他們的評估和聘用決定。 雖然全球都面臨著人口老化和低出生率的挑戰，但是在家庭之外，依然很少有性價比高的兒童和老年人照顧服務。家庭成員，尤其是女性成員，仍需要在家中承擔照顧兒童和年邁父母的重責。儘管近來全球就業政策都强調工作和家庭之間的平衡，然而家庭照顧責任對家庭照顧者的就業和職業發展的影響卻沒有得到充分的探討。 關於家庭照顧責任和勞動力市場參與之間的衝突，很多國家已有研究。其中的主要發現都集中於“母職懲罰”——即照顧幼童給母親的職業發展所帶來的負面影響（Correll, Benard, & Paik, 2007）。最近也出現了一些比較研究，它們關注的是父職或是照顧年邁父母對雇員工作的影響，但尚未有清晰的結論（Weicht, 2015）。對於性別和家庭照顧責任在職場中的影響，我們依然只有極其有限的系統性理解；而對於這些影響是如何在結構、社會和文化的背景中被建構、實踐和理解接受的，我們則知之更少。 本研究旨在填補這些研究的空白。我們會調查在香港和深圳兩地，求職者的性別和不同的家庭照顧責任會如何影響雇主的評估和決定。我們還將考察這種影響在不同的工業界別、規模不同的企業及不同的工作崗位所可能存在的差異。在對香港和深圳所做的比較中，我們會尤爲關注宏觀的福利機制，研究不同福利體系中的結構性資源限制和福利文化意義建構，探索它們如何影響雇主對求職者性別和家庭照顧責任的看法和行動。 本研究會從跨文化的比較視角出發，審視性別和不同的家庭照顧責任在勞動力市場上的單獨和混合作用，并强調在不同的結構背景和福利系統中去進一步理解這些作用的重要性。研究的發現不但會豐富我們對性別、家庭照顧、勞動力市場和職場不平等的理論性認識，而且會為社會服務規劃和社會政策制定提供證據支持，並有助於實現家庭支持、勞工保護、工作和家庭之閒的平衡以及社會公義。

14610220.label: Realisation of objectives
14610220.value: For Objective 1: To investigate how job applicants' gender and family care responsibilities affect employers' evaluation scores and hiring decisions in Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Six types of job candidates will be comparatively analyzed: (1) a man without family care duties; (2) a woman without family care duties; (3) a man taking care of young children; (4) a woman taking care of young children; (5) a man taking care of ageing parents; and (6) a woman taking care of ageing parents. With the help of her research assistant and student helpers, the PI completed a thorough literature review on gender and work-family studies and relevant policy debates in Chinese societies and in the globe. Data from an earlier study in Hong Kong were re-analyzed from the perspectives of the new project. Field work was carried out in Shenzhen from 2020 to 2023, to conduct the CV-based survey and in-depth interviews with employers in the private and the public sector. The respondent-driven sampling (RDS) was adopted to reach our survey respondents. In total, 330 respondents from the private sector and 294 respondents from the public sector participated in the CV-based surveys, and 31 in-depth interviews were conducted in the private sector, and another 31 in-depth interviews were conducted in the public sector. The sampling goals in the research proposal were fulfilled. The research team has cleaned, transcribed, documented, and analyzed the collected data. Regular meetings were held to discuss and understand the patterns, the mechanisms, and processes embedded in the data. With the assistance of her RAs and student helpers, the PI has compiled complete survey data sets, coding documents for qualitative data, and analytic reports. Employers' evaluations and hiring decisions regarding the six types of job candidates were explored in both survey and in-depth interview data. Their preferences, discriminations, and penalty practices vary in the three labor regimes: Hong Kong, private sector of Shenzhen, and public sector of Shenzhen. Some major findings include caregiver bonus and motherhood penalty in Hong Kong, caregiver penalty in the private sector of Shenzhen, and gender discrimination in the public sector of Shenzhen. For Objective 2: To examine how employers' evaluations and hiring decisions differ in different industries and sectors, in hiring units and establishments of different employment sizes, and for different job categories. These differences will be explored in both Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Sub-group analyses were conducted using the CV-based survey data, to understand how different employment contexts and job specificities affect employers' evaluations and hiring decisions of each of the six CV types. The findings in the three different labor regimes were put into comparison for analysis. The PI has also explored the patterns in the survey data via in-depth interviews with employers to understand the mechanisms. In general, we found that job contexts and specificities restrained the employment opportunities of female family caregivers in Hong Kong, but did not play a significant role in Shenzhen's private and public sectors. For Objective 3: To understand how the different welfare arrangement and institutions in Hong Kong, in the public sector of Shenzhen, and in the private sector of Shenzhen shape employers' attitudes and practices with job applicants of different gender and with different family care duties. Dual mechanisms through structural resource constraints defined by different welfare policies and cultural meaning construction of gender and family care responsibilities under different welfare orientations will be investigated in both locations. The PI analyzed the in-depth interviews with employers in the three labor regimes, to navigate how welfare arrangements and institutions shape the rationales of employers. Particular attention was paid to the duality of structural constraints and cultural schemas. The facilitative and productivist welfare regime in Hong Kong, the defiance of labor protection laws and regulations in the private sector of Shenzhen, and socialist labor welfare in the public sector of Shenzhen were identified and discussed in our results. For Objective 4: To generate implications for social service planning and policy making in Chinese societies, in the areas of family support, labor protection, work-family balance, sex and family status discrimination, and equal opportunities in employment, so as to achieve social equality, social justice, and better human societies. The research team reviewed existing literature on comparative welfare policies and service programs regarding work and family in different social and cultural contexts. This topic was included in our data analyses, manuscripts, and public seminars. Our research implies that for work-family welfare policies and programs to take effect, they need to communicate with the rationales of employers in different labor regimes. In Hong Kong, the service-based approach is more appealing than the current leave-based policies; in the private sector of Shenzhen, consciousness raising programs to reflect on market meritocracy is necessary; and in the public sector of Shenzhen, multiple dimensions of inequalities need to be addressed. With the support of the grant, the PI developed important collaborations with colleagues and institutions in Hong Kong and Mainland China during the field work. Colleagues of the Equal Opportunities Commission of Hong Kong, Professor Cheryl Chui at the University of Hong Kong, Professor Juan Chen and Professor Qiaobing Wu at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Professor Lili Xia and Gaoming Ma at Zhejiang University, Dr. Hong Meng at Shenzhen University, and Dr. Xu Li at Southern University of Science and Technology have become important research partners. We are preparing several pieces of publications together and have made plans for future collaboration. Through research seminars and conference presentations, the PI has also built professional networks with colleagues and institutions in different parts of the world: for example, Columbia University, New York University, and Arizona State University in the USA; Seoul National University in South Korea; National Singapore University; University of Antwerp in Belgium; and Casa Asia in Barcelona, Spain. These networks were established based on common research interest and will facilitate future collaborative research projects. The PI often used the findings from this research in classroom teaching, research seminars, public lecture, and public events. The findings have been disseminated at the press conferences of the Equal Opportunities Commission and the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong, through South China Morning Post, Ming Pao, HK01, and RTHK, and in the Inclusive Video Project of CUHK. Thanks to this grant, positive social impacts are realized through academic research.

14610220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14610220.value: Through mixed-methods data and the lens of comparative research, the project investigated how employers evaluate and treat male and female employees with various family care responsibilities in three different labor regimes of Chinese societies: Hong Kong, Shenzhen's private sector, and Shenzhen's public sector. Particular attention was directed to four major schemes of rationales of employers, namely, market meritocracy, family moral virtuocracy, ideology of gender norms, and welfare resources and constraints. In Hong Kong, employers combined the logics of market meritocracy and family moral virtuocracy to reward favorable evaluations to family caregivers of young children and ageing parents in the labor market; yet, based on traditional beliefs in gender roles and little expectation of state welfare intervention in the workplace, they were loath to offer job opportunities to mothers of young children and senior positions to female caregivers of ageing parents. In the private sector of Shenzhen, where family moral virtuocracy was utterly disregarded and labor protection and welfare interventions were only to be defied, employers followed the simple and clear logics of market meritocracy to decide on job offers and conduct performance evaluations. Employees with family care duties were put into disadvantages in a gender-blind manner, although women, who disproportionally played the role of primary family caregiver, were further marginalized. In the public sector of Shenzhen, welfare institutions and workplace arrangements ensured comprehensive protections of the labor rights of family caregivers, and employers, as a result, reined in the power of market meritocracy and treated family care responsibilities as necessary needs of employees that ought to be considered in the workplace. Although family moral virtuocracy stayed irrelevant, employers managed to offer generous leave for family needs. However, in their practices, patriarchal and traditional gender norms and family orders were followed, intrusions in the private family life of employees were prevalent, and inequalities of gender and employment terms were highly visible. In the duality of structural resources and cultural schemas of different labor regimes, employers' rationales regarding family caregivers in the labor market evinced rich multiplicity and complexity, which challenged the prevailing assumption that market meritocracy dominates employers' evaluations and decisions. The multiplicity and complexity in employers' rationales might shed new light on a refreshed understanding of employers' role in shaping caregiver exclusion and penalty in the workplace, and possible policy interventions other than those echoing the logics of market meritocracy.

14610220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14610220.value: Research on work and family care responsibilities, gender inequality in family and workplace, and work-family policies in different social and cultural contexts will be continued in future. The PI has developed a new project to examine work and family life under the platform economy in China (GRF #14614322, Research Grants Council of Hong Kong). As the booming platform economy in China has changed the boundary between work and family life, the project sets out to understand how participants in the economy reorganize household division of labor, family care arrangements, and work schedules. Attention will be paid to the new patterns of gender and generational inequalities and new family dynamics in China. A new research initiative is also being developed to investigate the changing family life and work patterns in the new immigrant families from Mainland China to Hong Kong, through the new immigration schemes of the Hong Kong government. In practice, collaborating with universities and NGOs in Mainland China, the PI is starting an intervention program for families with young children in China, and one of the program themes is focused on promoting child development and wellbeing through family care arrangements and work-family balance of parents.

14610220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14610220.value: This project examines the multiple rationales of employers in different labor regimes in Chinese societies, to understand the dilemmas for family caregivers and the processes of social inequality in the contemporary labor market. The varied cultural schemas and structural constraints revealed in the study could enlighten us theoretically on the complexity in the relationships between workplace organization and labor rights, and practically on policy strategies and programs. In Hong Kong where gendered division of labor is an embraced cultural schema and moral virtuocracy of family care plays a role in the labor market, the residual intervention of leave policy renders little effect on employers. In the private economy of Shenzhen, despite the protective Labor Law, employers manage to push family care issues out of the concerns of the workplace. The public sector, on the other hand, leashes the power of market meritocracy through welfare and workplace organization, but meanwhile creates gender norms and new dimensions of inequalities. These findings contribute not only to the theoretical development in the fields of gender inequality, work-family studies, and social change, but also to the practices of policy interventions in labor protection, family welfare, and gender justice.

14610520.value: Objective 1: Examining the Spaces of Preattentive Colors and Orientations I will apply the DFD analysis of Huang (2019) to colors and orientations. For colors, pilot data suggested that the space of preattentive color features systematically differ from the perceptually uniform color space (CIELAB): the “red part” is expanded. For orientations, pilot data suggested a 3D space that is different from what is previously known. I will conduct experiments to complete these studies. Objective 2: Compare the Spaces of visual features in different tasks Huang (2019) used the texture segregation task. I propose to try two other tasks. First, I will conduct experiments with the pop-out task to determine the axes of feature spaces. Second, I will conduct experiments with the Perceptual discrimination task to provide rigorous baselines. Objective 3: Development of the SCS shape space in Huang (2019) The SCS shape space of Huang (2019) will be developed in two different ways. First, I will try a few additional sets of shapes, including real-world objects, 3D shapes, and 2D unfilled line-drawing shapes. Second, I will try to develop image-based algorithms to see how the 3 shape dimensions are calculated from Binary images.

14610520.value: 視覺註意幾十年的研究揭示了壹組基本視覺特征的維度，比如顏色，朝向，形狀，尺寸等 (e.g., Treisman & Gelade, 1980; Wolfe, 1994)。這些視覺特征的研究常常用到“特征空間”這個概念，也即壹種形式組織化的理解特征的方式。在壹項最近的研究中（Huang, 2019），我提出註意前形狀的空間與註意後任務（比如匹配和分辨等）的空間非常不同。其後，預實驗數據顯示註意前顏色和朝向的空間也和註意後任務中使用的顏色空間（比如CIELAB）和朝向空間非常不同。 在這裏提出的研究中，我將系統研究註意前的視覺特征空間。這裏提出的研究將有重要的意義。在理論方面，它將讓我們對視覺特征有更形式化和系統的理解，而這將對整個視覺註意和視覺工作記憶領域有重要的意義。在實用方面，這些註意前視覺特征空間的知識可以用於發展數據可視化，廣告，遊戲和軟件設計，以及其他需要有效視覺溝通的場合。 我提出（1） 用Huang (2019)的方法來確定視覺特征（比如顏色朝向）的空間；（2）比較不同任務中的視覺特征空間（比如凸顯任務，視覺比較任務）；（3）進壹步發展Huang (2019)提出的形狀空間。

14610520.label: Realisation of objectives
14610520.value: During the execution of this project, I have made a dramatic change in my research approach. As you can see from the attached research output (Huang, 2023, Nature Human Behaviour), I am now trying to combine the strengths of AI and experimental psychology in the hope of shedding new light on the latter. Specifically, in each project, I conduct a large-scale experiment to carefully measure a specific facet of human behavior. I subsequently conduct a “comprehensive exploration” of the relevant mechanisms and factors and try to build the most fitting model to interpret the accumulated data. This comprehensive exploration approach aims to combine the strengths of traditional experimental psychology with data-driven model development in the realm of artificial intelligence (AI). On one hand, this approach is theory-oriented: mirroring experimental psychology, it employs controlled experiments tailored to specific research objectives, striving to uncover theoretical insights. On the other hand, this approach is data-driven: similar to AI principles, it fundamentally relies on constructing an extensive, high-quality dataset as the cornerstone of model development, and iteratively refining the model to attain satisfactory performance. In brief, this is a theory-oriented, data-driven approach that uses AI tools (data-driven model development) to achieve the goals of experimental psychology (theoretical insights). In this context, this project has gone well beyond the original plan, resulting in several important changes. First, the original experiment in Objective 3 has been expanded into a large-scale experiment that provides a broader and more precise picture than originally planned. It now covers shape discrimination between approximately 160,000 shape pairs. With this large-scale experiment, we have developed an image-based neural network to predict how shapes are distinguished by the human visual system and are now working toward a theory-based model to reveal the conceptual interpretation of this neural network. Due to its much larger scale, the modeling process has gone well beyond the original plan. We have not been able to summarize the findings into a paper yet, but we hope to finish it and submit it for publication in six months. Second, knowing that upgrading Objective 3 would be extremely time-consuming (as explained in the preceding paragraph), I have added a simpler test-drive experiment to secure some more immediate outcomes. In this experiment, the “shapes” are not image-based shapes but dot-patterns, which can be manipulated and modeled much more easily. Although this side experiment is simpler, it already provides much richer information than a usual experimental psychology study, and it is well-received by peer researchers. Its importance is partly reflected by the outlet of this study (Nature Human Behaviour). Using this as a benchmark, it is reasonable to expect that the main experiment on image-based shape discrimination, although unfortunately delayed, will ultimately lead to an even more important study. Third, all the experiments outlined in Objectives 1 and 2 have been completed as planned. However, these results are relatively less important and less informative than the two completed/ongoing large-scale experiments. Therefore, I have chosen not to write them up for now. Hopefully, in the future, I will have the resources to run large-scale experiments on these topics.

14610520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14610520.value: The main findings of the present project are that visual processing of shapes (or spatial patterns as operationalized in Huang, 2023) consists of multiple mechanisms. For example, Huang (2023) found that the processing of spatial patterns is best modeled by a two-layer early-late representation framework. However, other mechanisms such as line detection, gap detection, Bayesian integration, and low-precision components also contribute to the process. This comprehensive exploration approach holds an important advantage over typical experimental psychology studies, which usually begin with a hypothesis and predict outcomes based on one or two pre-established dimensions. It is becoming evident that fragmented insights from these individual studies resemble puzzle pieces that do not automatically come together to form an overall picture. The key message of the present study is that a fairly complete overall picture is formed from these puzzle pieces, something rarely achieved or attempted for any cognitive task. The effectiveness of the comprehensive exploration approach is benchmarked against a neural network, which is usually assumed to be able to extract nearly all the underlying mechanisms. In this project, by summarizing the accumulated wisdom of decades of previous work, the comprehensive exploration approach provides an explanation of empirical observations that is nearly as good as a massive neural network.

14610520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14610520.value: There are two possible ways for further development of this project. First, regarding shape processing, we will try to expand the current set of spatial patterns and simple shapes to include shapes of real-world objects. Second, in a broader context, we will apply the current “comprehensive exploration” approach to other cognitive tasks.

14610520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14610520.value: Everyone knows what shapes are and has some intuitive understanding of how they are perceived by the human mind, but no one knows the exact algorithms or mechanics. For example, we know that colors can be attributed to variations on three dimensions: red, green, and blue components. However, no one knows what the basic dimensions of shapes are. In this project, we have taken an approach that is more comprehensive than usual experimental psychology studies, conducting a large-scale experiment and creating a theory-based model to reveal as much as possible of the underlying mechanisms. As a result, we have created a comprehensive framework for processing spatial patterns and are now working toward a comprehensive framework for processing image-based shapes.

14610820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14610820.value: 法律與騷亂：抗議警政的倫理

14610820.label: Project Objectives
14610820.value: The philosophy of policing: The first objective is to draw on the methods and approaches of analytical philosophy to address neglected ethical issues surrounding policing and frontline law enforcement. There is a substantial literature in political philosophy addressing the ethics of state or state-sanctioned coercive force in many areas. This includes extensive reflection on the legitimacy of the state, the ethics of subjecting citizens to coercive punishment for unlawful wrongdoing, and an extensive debate about the morality of warfare. It is therefore surprising, and perhaps even staggering, that there is a comparative lack of philosophical reflection on ethical issues surrounding the threat or use of force by the police. Philosophers in the analytical tradition care about the ethics of coercive force because of a tacit understanding of the high stakes involved in its usage, which makes it doubly surprising that they have not engaged policing in anything like as much depth as other usages of force by the state. The police are one of the principal mechanisms through which the state exercises its monopoly over legitimate force in society, as well as serving as one of the major points of contact between state and citizenry. The project will therefore initiate and contribute to much-needed philosophical conversations about the moral and ethical dimensions of policing. The ethics of protest policing: The second objective is to elaborate normative principles that should guide police forces in their responses to disruptive protest. Protest policing is an important example of the way in which police forces perform a frontline role in negotiating the sometimes competing normative imperatives of civil and political rights and public order. It is also a highly contentious topic in public debates across different societies, as police forces are routinely subject to countervailing pressures. On the one hand, police forces are criticized if their efforts to police protest are seen as insufficiently robust, thus failing to protect third-parties from significant levels of disruption or prevent breakdowns in public order. On the other hand, police forces are criticized if their efforts to police protest are seen as excessively robust, thus subjecting protesters to disproportionate shows of militarized force or curtailing opportunities for meaningful freedom of expression and assembly. This suggests pervasive disagreement about the weight that should be accorded to the various individual and public interests that are at stake in the policing of protest. Political philosophy cannot hope to resolve such disagreements, but it can make a modest contribution by clarifying the legitimate interests at stake and proposing defeasible standards that specify what is reasonable to expect of police forces in their approach to disruptive protest. The regulation of protest policing: The third objective is to show how principles of protest policing could be embedded within concrete institutional practices. This objective is included in order to demonstrate that a philosophical analysis of protest policing should not be limited to the elaboration of abstract standards but should also cast some light on how such standards can be adopted and implemented as regulatory norms by relevant actors. It is, for instance, important to consider whether and how normative principles of protest policing might be disseminated in the public sphere and adopted by police forces. It is, furthermore, important to consider whether and how normative principles of protest policing could function as standards of accountability for police forces in post hoc appraisals of their handling of protest events. And it is also important to consider whether and how normative principles of protest policing could be revised after their adoption in light of practical experience and societal feedback. The objective here is not to demonstrate that a normative argument about protest policing would necessarily take hold in institutional contexts. The objective, rather, is to show that the argument has been formulated in a way that anticipates some of the challenges and obstacles that would need to be addressed if it were to take hold in such contexts.

14610820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610820.value: The policing of public protest is a highly contentious topic across a number of societies, from controversy over policing of anti-austerity protest in the UK, anti-immigrant protest across Europe, white nationalist rallies in the US, to the recent anti-Extradition Bill protest in Hong Kong. Those who are sympathetic to protesters often condemn police forces for tactics that are seen as heavy-handed and disproportionate, such as preventative mass arrests, temporary enclosure of protesters in confined spaces, and the use of so-called ‘less lethal’ weapons like tear gas, tasers, and pepper spray against demonstrators. Those who are unsympathetic to protesters, on the other hand, often condemn police for tactics that are seen as timid, reactive or ineffectual, culminating in a perceived failure of police to enforce the law in defence of third-parties who are said to suffer the consequences of disruptive protest. The continuing proliferation of protest in response to alleged failures of government suggests that police forces across the world will grapple with the dilemmas of protest policing on an ongoing basis. This project explores the problem of protest policing from the perspective of normative political philosophy. It explores whether and to what extent ethical standards can be proposed to guide the strategies and tactics that police forces should utilize in their responses to disruptive protest. In so doing, it not only addresses a topic of profound societal importance but also redresses a significant gap in political philosophy. Political philosophers, among others, have long addressed ethical dilemmas confronted by states engaged in warfare, applying normative standards such as effectiveness, proportionality and non-combatant immunity to their use of force. Political philosophers have nonetheless failed to devote comparable attention to the threat or use of force by police officers in domestic contexts, including but not limited to the coercive mechanisms that are employed in response to protest. This project will thus look to initiate a philosophical dialogue about the ethics of policing, exploring the values that should underpin policing in general, the principles that should structure police approaches to protest, and the ways in which these principles might be institutionalized. 從英國反緊縮方案抗議、歐洲反移民抗議、美國白人民族主義集會到最近香港反修例抗議，公眾示威的警政問題在不同社會中都具有爭議性。那些同情示威者的人通常都會譴責警權過大，採用過分及不相稱的武力及戰術，例如預先大規模拘捕、暫時將示威者圍困於狹窄的空間，以及對示威者使用警方聲稱「較低致命性的」武器，如催淚氣體，電槍和胡椒噴霧。相反，那些不同情示威者的人，通常都會譴責警察的戰術太膽怯、反應遲鈍或無效，最終導致警察無法以法律捍衛因示威而利益受到破壞的第三方。持續出現針對政府失敗的示威活動揭示世界各地的警察都會繼續應對示威與警政間的困境。 這項目以政治哲學角度探討抗議與警政的問題。此項目探討能否以道德標準，以及何種程度的標準，指導警察在應對具破壞性示威時的戰略和策略。這不僅能處理現實社會中重要的課題，亦能夠填補政治哲學就有關方面討論的空白。長期以來，政治哲學家致力解決戰爭中國家所面臨的道德困境，並勾勒出在其使用武力時需採用的應然性標準，例如有效性、相稱性及非戰鬥豁免。儘管如此，政治哲學家卻沒有同等關注國家內警務人員擁有的武力及威脅，包括及不限於應對抗議時所用的強制性機器。因此，此項目旨在開啟政治哲學有關警政的討論，希望探討警政的價值基礎，構成警察處理抗議的原則以及該原則如何能制度化。

14610820.label: Realisation of objectives
14610820.value: The first objective was to draw on methods and approaches in contemporary political philosophy to address the neglected ethical dimension of policing. This objective has been achieved through elaborating an original and powerful normative account of policing that is informed by the political theory of civic republicanism. The cornerstone of the republican approach is freedom as non-domination, the achievement of which requires the state to implement a range of programmes, policies, and institutions that empower citizens to contest arbitrary exercises of power. The police, on this account, have important roles to play in insulating citizens against threats of inter-personal domination, insuring citizens against incapacitating emergencies and misfortunes, and maintaining the social order within which citizens pursue their plans and objectives. The police, at the same time, also pose a threat to freedom as non-domination, in the sense that their power and discretion may be exercised in a manner that is experienced as arbitrary by citizens. The republican account addresses this threat through ensuring that the policed have extensive opportunities to contest the police and that policing is subject to an inclusive and responsive process of deliberative regulation. This constitutes one of the first serious attempts to set out a comprehensive and coherent theory of policing within contemporary political theory, departing from the prevailing tendency to treat policing as a relatively minor element of a broader analysis of the criminal justice system. The second objective was to elaborate normative principles that should guide police forces in their handling of political protest. This objective has been achieved through applying the principle of impartiality to the policing of protest. The principle holds that law enforcement agencies involved in the policing of protest should act to uphold the equal rights of relevant parties, with no arbitrary discrimination in terms of race, gender, sexuality, nationality, or political allegiance of those parties. The principle of impartiality is contrasted with the more familiar principle of neutrality, which is often invoked in discussions about how the police should approach protest from across the political spectrum. The principle of impartiality is found to be preferable because of its comparative advantages in expressing and encouraging non-dominating forms of protest policing. The principle is, furthermore, preferable on pragmatic grounds, in that—unlike neutrality—it allows the officers to make discretionary, risk-reducing decisions about how to police protest in a way that is responsive to the political complexion of the protest. The research I have carried out in pursuit of this objective further explores how impartiality can serve as the foundation for a broader overhaul of protest policing, which includes the expectation that police should constrain the use of force according to principles of proportionality, necessity, and liability. The third objective is to explore how normative principles of protest policing can be embedded within institutional policies and practices. This objective has been achieved through setting out various ‘models’ of protest policing, which comprise both normative principles of protest policing and applied guidelines that shape police strategies and tactics during protest events. There are, in particular, three normative models of protest policing that can be reconstructed through a critical analysis of contemporary police practices toward protest across a range of democratic societies. These models are described as repressive order maintenance, negotiated order maintenance, and dialogic order maintenance. The first model adopts a punitive approach to protest policing, whereby police use pre-emptive force to mitigate the public order risks associated with protest. The second model adopts a more lenient approach, according to which negotiation with protesters is preferred to force as a means of achieving pre-determined ends. The third model is substantively similar to the second model, but differs in the crucial respect that police use dialogue rather than bargaining as a means of co-creating mutually acceptable solutions with protesters. The dialogic model has been found to be more compatible with the broader republican approach to policing that is endorsed in this project, because it offers greater prospects for a non-dominating and impartial form of protest policing.

14610820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14610820.value: The major findings and research outcomes relate to both the general theory of policing that has emerged and the specific application to protest policing. The finding that I believe is most significant relates to the republican theory of policing that I developed in realization of the first objective (see above section 5.3). The reason for its significance is, in particular, that the republican focus on ‘policing by contestation’ serves as a powerful alternative to the far more familiar idea of ‘policing by consent’, which underpins the ‘Peelian’ model of policing associated with the emergence of the first modern municipal police force in London, 1829. That model, I contend, is subject to devastating philosophical and political objections. The philosophy of policing that is elaborated in my single-author paper ‘Republican Policing: From Consent to Contestation’ constitutes a superior alternative to policing by consent as a public doctrine of policing. This paper has been accepted for publication in the prestigious journal ‘Perspectives on Politics’ (published by Cambridge University Press on behalf of the American Political Science Association). The high standing of this journal in the general field of political science means that the paper is likely to generate considerable impact and debate within and beyond the academe. A further significant finding relates to the normative account of protest policing that I have generated in the course of this project. The republican theory of policing serves as a crucial foundation for elaborating normative principles of protest policing, thus underscoring the applicability and resourcefulness of that theory. I have set out a preliminary statement of this account in my paper ‘Three Normative Models of Protest Policing’, which has already been presented at a symposium in Singapore (June 2023) and at the time of writing this completion report is under consideration for publication in the prestigious journal ‘Politics & Society’ (Sage). I have already published a paper setting out the case for impartiality as a core principle of protest policing and drawing out its relevance to a broader republican account of policing, entitled ‘The Politics of Protest Policing’ (published in The Harvard Review of Philosophy). I believe that the research carried out during the course of this project will serve as a basis for further publications in the coming years.

14610820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14610820.value: There are two particular areas for further development, one related to policing in general and the other related to protest policing in particular. First, the general republican theory of policing might be further developed and defended in various ways. This might include exploring whether and how its core normative commitments might shape a transformative approach to policing, potentially transcending the polarized debate between advocates of police reform and police abolition in contemporary democracies. Second, the research that I carried out during the current award revealed an important but hitherto entirely neglected ethical issue in protest policing. This is the role of private organizations and non-state actors in contributing to the policing of political protest events and movements. The existing normative literature focuses almost entirely on the role of public (i.e. state) law enforcement agencies in policing protest, thus neglecting ethical issues surrounding the role of corporate security agencies and ‘self-policing’ on the part of social movements. The issue of private protest policing seems particularly well-suited to a future application to the RGC general research fund for support.

14610820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14610820.value: This research project explores ethical and moral issues that arise in relation to policing in general and protest policing in particular. It draws on recent republican political theory to set out an original and timely doctrine of ‘policing by contestation’ as an alternative to the more familiar idea of ‘policing by consent’. This republican theory does not rest the legitimacy of policing on the supposed ‘consent’ of the public, but on the adequacy and accessibility of the means through which citizens can contest arbitrary interference at the hands of the police. The republican theory points toward a model of protest policing that is based on the principle of political impartiality and a tactical and strategic repertoire that encourages greater dialogue between police and protesters. The research is valuable because it constitutes one of the first attempts to think in a serious and sustained fashion about the ethical and moral issues surrounding policing and protest in liberal democratic societies.

14611420.value: 記憶檢索時的解釋水平和心理距離對降低消極自傳體記憶的情緒強度和提升心理幸福感的效應研究

14611420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611420.value: 目的 我們計劃研究年輕人在記憶檢索時，其心理距離和解釋水平對降低消極自傳體記憶的情緒強度和提升心理幸福感的影響效應。 項目背景 解釋水平理論（Trope & Liberman, 2010）認為，解釋水平和心理距離是相互關聯的：人們傾向於用更高、更抽象的解釋水平來表征心理距離較遠的事件，而用更低、更具體的解釋水平來表徵心理距離較近的事件。 這一觀點最近受到了挑戰（例如Gu & Tse, 2018）。 本研究項目將讓參與者回憶一件消極的自傳體事件，並同時操作回憶事件時的解釋水平和該事件的心理距離，從而檢驗解釋水平和心理距離的聯合效應。 結果變量是參與者感知到的事件的情緒強度和心理幸福感。以往研究發現，事件的情緒強度隨著心理距離的增大而降低（例如Van Boven et al., 2010）。 項目設計 在實驗一中，參與者將採用第一人稱來回憶一件消極的自傳體事件，一周後，他們採用第三人稱來回憶相同的事件。 在每一次回憶任務中，他們會被要求關注事件的意義（例如對他們生活的啟示）或者關注事件的背景細節（例如事件發生在哪裡），這樣他們分別採用高解釋水平或低解釋水平來詳細說明該事件。 然後，他們將評價事件的特徵（例如情緒強度），並完成心理幸福感的測量。 在實驗二中，流程與實驗一相同，唯一的不同之處在於，實驗二操作事件的時間距離（即一件發生在去年的事或者發生在至少八年前的事），而不是操作事件的敘事視角。 在兩次實驗開始的前兩天，測量參與者的抑鬱得分、特質性解釋水平得分和幸福感得分，這些分數作為基線值和控制變量。 此外，每個實驗都增加了兩個對照組，對照組將接受高解釋水平或低解釋水平的啟動，該啟動任務與自傳體記憶的檢索無關，以此來檢驗當本實驗把解釋水平的操作嵌入到記憶檢索任務中時，所得結論是否具有普遍性。 項目意義 理論上，解釋水平和心理距離對情緒強度和心理幸福感的交互作用將表明它們對記憶檢索產生的聯合影響，該結果對解釋水平理論有重要的啟示。 實踐上，本項目將闡明表達性書寫範式和採用高解釋水平的、基於意義的自傳體記憶干預方案的效果，類似於懷舊療法（例如Westerhof & Bohlmeijer, 2014）。

14611420.label: Realisation of objectives
14611420.value: We successfully recruited participants and collected data as outlined in our research proposal. In Experiment 1, we explored the effects of shifting narrative perspectives (as a change in psychological distance) and construal levels during the retrieval of negative autobiographical memories, and how these influenced post-recall affect and well-being. We engaged 128 college-aged participants who recalled a negative autobiographical event first from a 1st-person perspective and then from a 3rd-person perspective after several days later. During each session, participants were asked to elaborate on the event at a high construal level, reflecting on its broader life significance, or at a low construal level, focusing on specific contextual details such as time and location. Following each recall, participants assessed the mnemonic characteristics of the events, such as emotional intensity, and completed evaluations related to positive and negative affect and well-being. Additional measures including participants’ symptoms of depression, dispositional construal levels, and well-being were collected on a separate day. This comprehensive data collection allowed us to examine the main effects and interactions of construal level and psychological distance, successfully meeting all three objectives of the funded project. The results of this experiment have been written up as a manuscript and submitted for publication in the journal, Scientific Reports. Building upon the design of Experiment 1, Experiment 2 further investigated the project's objectives by manipulating psychological distance through temporal distance instead of narrative perspective. We recruited another group of 128 college-aged participants to study how the temporal distance and construal level associated with the recollection of negative autobiographical events impact post-recall emotions and psychological well-being. Participants recalled two events in separate sessions, one recent (within the past year) and one distant (at least eight years ago). As in Experiment 1, construal level was manipulated by instructing participants to reflect on either the broader significance of the event (high construal level) or to focus on specific details such as time and location (low construal level). After each retrieval, participants evaluated the mnemonic qualities of the event (e.g., emotional intensity, vividness of imagery, and ease of retrieval) and reported their positive and negative emotions and psychological well-being. Additional variables such as depression symptoms, subjective vitality, and self-esteem were also collected and used as control variables in our analyses. These also successfully met all objectives of our funded project. The findings will be presented in an academic conference on Oct 2024.

14611420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611420.value: In Experiment 1, we observed that participants reported higher subjective vitality and a greater pursuit of life meaning—both indicators of psychological well-being—and experienced reduced negative affect after recalling events from a higher, as opposed to a lower, construal level. In addition, participants reported a decrease in their perceived emotional intensity of events and an increased search for meaning in life when they shifted the narrative perspective from the 1st-person to the 3rd- person, thereby increasing psychological distance. However, the effect of high construal level on boosting psychological well-being was larger when recalling AM events from the 1st-person (vs. 3rd-person) perspective, contrary to the prediction of Construal Level Theory. This study was pioneering in its exploration of the separate effects of construal level and psychological distance, indirectly manipulated through narrative perspective, on the retrieval of autobiographical memories. In Experiment 2, we found that events recalled from a longer temporal distance (eight years or more) elicited less intense negative emotions post-recall compared to events from the previous year. This effect conceptually replicated the influence of psychological distance observed in Experiment 1, though here it was defined as temporal distance rather than narrative perspective. Interestingly, retrieving memories at a high construal level (focusing on life significance) was linked to lower psychological well-being compared to low construal level retrieval (focusing on details). Unlike Experiment 1, no interaction was found between construal level and psychological distance (as manipulated via temporal distance) on perceived emotional intensity or psychological well-being measures. These results underscore the distinct impacts of construal level and temporal distance on the process of autobiographical memory retrieval. Overall, the outcomes of these two experiments offer insights into Construal Level Theory, particularly noting that the lack of interaction between psychological distance and construal level may challenge the theory’s premise of a conceptual link between these variables. The findings also highlight the potential benefits of manipulating construal level and psychological distance to enhance psychological well-being in young adults, shedding light on the development of expressive writing paradigms as emotional intervention strategies within clinical or counseling settings.

14611420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611420.value: Given the findings regarding the role of psychological distance in moderating the effectiveness of memory retrieval strategies for negative autobiographical events—specifically in reducing perceived negative emotional intensity and enhancing psychological well-being—we intend to pursue further research. Our next step is to explore whether the benefits of increased psychological distance, achieved through switching to a third-person narrative perspective or recalling events from a more extended temporal distance, can also apply to the retrieval of positive autobiographical events. We aim to investigate whether recalling positive events can similarly intensify perceived positive emotions and further enhance psychological well-being. The contrasting effects of construal level manipulation observed across the two experiments present an intriguing dilemma. To address this, we plan to conduct a detailed examination of the event contents from both experiments and conduct content analyses to identify the factors related to the autobiographical events that might moderate the effect of high construal-level manipulation on psychological well-being in the two experiments. Should these additional analyses yield clear results, they may be developed into a separate manuscript for publication. This investigation will potentially clarify these conflicting findings and contribute further to our understanding of memory’s role in emotional regulation.

14611420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611420.value: In our study, we explore how changing the way we think about and recall personal memories can affect our emotional reactions and improve mental health in young adults. Specifically, we considered the level of details used when recalling memories and the perspective from which these memories are recalled. When remembering negative events, we can focus on their broader significance in our lives or on their specific details like where it occurred. We can recall the events from our own point of view (first-person perspective) or as if we were an observer (third-person perspective). We also considered whether event timing (recent versus several years ago) affects how we feel about it now. Our findings suggest that recalling negative events from a third-person perspective or as events that happened a long time ago make them feel less emotionally intense and enhance overall well-being. Sometimes, thinking about what these events mean in our lives can be more beneficial than focusing on the specific details. These insights lay the groundwork for further studies into how expressive writing and memory recall techniques can be used as tools to help young adults manage their emotions and improve their mental health.

14611820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611820.value: 本項目比較研究晚清時期兩位基督新教傳教士對《易經》的詮釋，分別為聖公會的麥克開拉啟(Thomas McClatchie, 1814-1885)以及倫敦會的理雅各(James Legge, 1815-1897)。麥克開拉啟採取神話學的視角，於1876年出版了首部《易經》英譯本；理雅各則主要從道德哲學的角度，於1882年完成另一英譯本。雖然兩部譯本風格迥然各異，詮釋大相逕庭，卻展示出《易經》最初進入英語世界的兩個獨特面向，並見證了十九世紀下半葉歐洲漢學以及比較宗教學的興起。麥克開拉啟的神話學詮釋遭理雅各以至不少傳教士同儕的大力抨擊，其譯介《易經》的開創之功亦長期受學界忽略，有待全面、深入的研究。本項目將發掘歐美的重要檔案資料，考察兩位傳教士各自的神學立場、翻譯目的，以及其時代及學術處境等，藉以推進學界對傳教士易學及歐洲漢學的認識。此外，細緻的文本比較分析有助揭示宗教經典跨文化傳播的複雜性與多樣性，亦能為當代的宗教對話提供借鑑和啟示。

14611820.label: Realisation of objectives
14611820.value: The current project has achieved all the four proposed objectives in the following manner: Firstly, this project has undertaken a critical and comparative study of two distinct interpretations of the Yijing (Book of Changes), the highly venerated and influential Chinese classic, by leading Protestant missionaries in late Qing China. These interpretations include the mythological interpretation of the Irish Anglican priest Thomas McClatchie, who published the first English translation of the Yijing in 1876, and the historical/moralistic approach of the Scottish Presbyterian James Legge, who produced its second English translation in 1882. By taking research trips to several European and United States archives and libraries (including the Bodleian Library, University of Oxford; School of Oriental and African Studies Library, London; New York Public Library; Library of Congress, Washington DC), the Principal Investigator has made exciting discoveries of the rare collections of primary materials consisting of McClatchie’s personal papers and unpublished manuscripts, and Legge’s unpublished manuscripts and personal library of Chinese classics, filled with his personal notes and commentary. A comprehensive and thorough analysis of these invaluable materials has enabled a more in-depth investigation of McClatchie’s and Legge’s understanding of the classic, their theological positions, and the intertextual connections with previous translations. This research has substantiated our understanding of early European sinology, particularly the genealogy of missionary studies on the Yijing, in late imperial China. Secondly, McClatchie, inspired by the embryonic ideas of comparative religion and mythology, adopted a mythological approach of interpreting the Yijing by making a distinctive, pioneering attempt to embark on a comparative study of the Chinese, Hindu, Babylonian, and Greek mythologies through his translation of the Yijing. Meanwhile, Legge fundamentally perceived the Yijing to be a “sacred book” of China containing distinctive Confucian moral principles, and more importantly, the divine revelation of Shangdi, the Chinese name for the Christian God. Undeniably Eurocentric and missionary-biased, these interpretations—or misinterpretations—may have deviated from traditional Chinese readings of the classic. However, from the perspective of hermeneutics, they exhibit the inevitable “prejudices” that presuppose total understanding on the part of the readers, as well as the multiplicity of any interpretative acts, particularly for religious classics. This project has supplemented the scholarship thus far, with a unique chapter on the rise of the comparative study of mythology and religions in the late nineteenth century. Thirdly, this project has scrutinized the distinctive translation approaches adopted by McClatchie and Legge to tackle the daunting challenges of rendering the ancient Chinese classic to the English-speaking world. Moving between the foreign and the domestic, as well as the global and the local, this unique case study has produced intriguing comparative perspectives for unveiling the complexity and creativity of transmitting a religious/philosophical classic to foreign cultural milieus. By offering a deeper understanding of the diversity of the Victorian Yijing translations, which were deep in theology and broad in their global reach and networks, this research also highlighted the importance of the transnational network of cross-cultural translations, in addition to the global circulation of knowledge, texts, and ideas. Finally, McClatchie’s and Legge’s provocative perspectives, albeit deviating from traditional Chinese reading, have expanded the possibility of diversified interpretations of this ancient Chinese classic imbued with multifarious layers of meaning and profuse symbolisms. Furthermore, their pioneering endeavors of rendering the Yijing for English‑speaking audiences also engendered extensive cross‑cultural encounters and profound inter‑religious intercourse between Christianity and Chinese religions. New light has been shed on the possibilities and prospects of contemporary cross-cultural exchanges and inter-religious dialogues in our glocalized world.

14611820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611820.value: The Principal Investigator has published four journal articles/book chapters and presented seven conference papers/public lectures in international venues, much more productive than the original anticipated output of two to three academic papers. “Thomas McClatchie’s Mythological Interpretation of the Yijing”, published in the groundbreaking volume “The Making of the Global Yijing in the Modern World”, critically examines the first English translation of the Yijing produced by the Protestant missionary Thomas McClatchie in 1876. This original study provides a fresh perspective on one of the earliest encounters between Christian theology and Chinese mythology amid the emergence of comparative study of religions in the late nineteenth century. With this Christian encounter with Chinese mythology, McClatchie also expanded the possibilities of diversified interpretations of the ancient Chinese classic. This study has carried out a close textual comparison between the original and translated texts in an effort to offer some explanations for the translation phenomena of these complicated cross-cultural activities, as well as to yield insights into the approaches to negotiating religious terms and concepts. “Moral Cultivation and Divine Revelation: James Legge’s Religious Interpretation of the Yijing” scrutinizes James Legge’s pioneering attempt of translating the Yijing into English in 1882, with a unique focus on his religious interpretation of the Chinese classic. Perceiving the Yijing as a Confucian classic with profound moralistic connotations, Legge even revered it as a “sacred book” containing certain elements of divine revelation. He asserted that the Chinese term Shangdi (Supreme Ruler) referred to the Christian God, and that the operations of nature in the different seasons are the work of Shangdi. By using Legge’s personal library and archival materials, this original output provides new insights into the inter-religious encounters and dialogues between Confucianism and Christianity. “Yi Study Resources and Interpretation Approaches: A Comparative Study of the English Translations of the Yijing by Thomas McClatchie and James Legge” investigates two earliest English translations of the Yijing which have drastically different styles and directions of interpretation. This paper adopts a comparative approach to analyze the background and religious thoughts of the translators in the study of their English translations and interpretation perspectives. Furthermore, this paper examines the Yi study resources referenced by the two missionaries during the translation process and places the two English translations in the context of the Yi study in the Qing Dynasty, which traces their possible influences from related works and ideas.

14611820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611820.value: On the basis of the substantial research findings of the current project, further research could be undertaken to examine other cross-cultural translations of the Yijing in the twentieth century. In particular, Richard Wilhelm (1873–1930), a German Protestant missionary to Qingdao, produced the German translation I Ging in 1924, which was re-translated into the English I Ching by Cary Baynes in 1950. The I Ching has made lasting impact on Western society, particularly the American postwar countercultural generations of the 1950s and 1960s. In this connection, the Principal Investigator has explored the possibility of academic collaboration with Prof. Hon Tzeki (BNU-HKBU United International College, Zhuhai), who is a leading expert in the field of the Yijing Studies. With Prof. Hon as the Co-Investigator, I have submitted a new GRF project (2025-26), entitled "The Making of Wilhelm/Baynes Translation of I Ching and Its Impacts on Postwar USA", to examine the globalization of the Yijing, showing a fascinating journey of this Chinese canon, from its translation and transformation into a world classic, to a tour-de-force of American counterculture. This will also further promote the cutting-edge research in the thriving field of the “Global Yijing Studies”.

14611820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611820.value: The research project has undertaken a critical and comparative study of two distinct English translations of the Yijing (Book of Changes) by two leading Protestant missionaries Thomas McClatchie and James Legge in the late nineteenth century. This project has made long-term academic impacts by helping both Chinese and Western scholars to gain a deeper understanding of the European genealogy of this work of world literature within a context of the global circulation of knowledge, texts, and culture. The juxtaposition of two distinctive yet interconnected English translations of the Yijing by two Protestant missionaries has not only yielded insights into the translations themselves, but also produced intriguing comparative perspectives for unveiling the complexity and diversity of transmitting a religious classic to foreign cultural milieus. Finally, these early Christian encounters in the Chinese context have thrown new light on the possibilities and prospects of contemporary cross-cultural exchanges and inter-religious dialogues in our glocalized world. The academic implications of this project for the Yijing scholarship, Translation Studies, and Religious Studies are profound.

14612220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612220.value: 該專案旨在探究強制披露規則（“披露規則”）的發展，分析在設計披露規則時所應進行的稅務政策考量，以及評估歐盟和經合組織近期制定的披露規則，同時，亦會闡述披露規則對香港及其他金融中心的影響。 該專案的第一部分將探討披露規則的擴展及變革，披露規則要求報告某些稅務計畫，在過去的四十年裡，披露規則已經從針對大眾避稅手段的國內措施演變成適用於各類中介機構的一般國內及國際報告準則。在一九八零年代，美國及加拿大採取了針對性措施，要求對大眾避稅手段進行登記。本世紀初，美國以及其他幾個國家開始要求報告某些特定交易。披露規則最引人矚目的擴展現時正在進行：歐盟近期通過，以及經合組織近期提議：披露規則應大幅擴大報告義務，將其適用於多類型的跨境安排，並要求各國間彼此分享相關資訊。香港以及其他未制定披露規則的金融中心可能面臨採取披露規則的壓力，而這將為稅務顧問、律師、金融機構以及其他中介機構設定重要義務。 專案的第二部分將分析在設計披露規則時應進行的稅務政策考量。考量因素包括：應予報告的稅務計畫，以及為金融機構及其他中介機構設定更多報告義務的大趨勢下披露規則的發展。相關報告義務包括以下國際自動交流機制：資訊制度、反洗錢法律規則、對超出某一閾值的交易的報告要求、以及實益所有權的登記。該專案將檢驗披露制度以及其他報告機制的既定目標是否能有效達成。 在分析完披露規則的設計考量後，該專案將從稅務政策角度評估歐盟和經合組織的披露規則。特別是，從披露規則對金融中心的影響方面考慮。金融中心，如香港，所舉辦的眾多活動以及眾多產業均可能受到披露規則的影響。這篇分析旨在促進就該等近期發展的稅務政策討論，以及香港和其他金融中心可能採取的披露規則。

14612220.label: Realisation of objectives
14612220.value: The discussion below explains how these objectives were achieved in the research outputs of this project. 1. Noam Noked, Zachary Marcone & Alison Tsang, The Expansion and Internationalization of Mandatory Disclosure Rules, 13 COLUMBIA JOURNAL OF TAX LAW 122-163 (2022) This publication analyzes the development of MDRs over the past four decades as a global phenomenon with three distinct phases beginning in the 1980s. The analysis reveals several trends: expansion in the types of schemes that are reportable, extension of reporting obligations to a great diversity of intermediaries, and increasing multilateralism in the effort to curb intermediary-enabled tax avoidance and evasion. This publication shows how developments in international tax policy have affected, and will likely continue to affect, the expansion and internationalization of MDRs. The publication covers the first objective of this research project by analyzing the development of mandatory disclosure rules (“MDRs”) in different jurisdictions over time from a comparative legal perspective. By examining the policy considerations and trends in the design and spread of MDRs, this article contributes towards the second and third objectives of the project. This article was published in the Columbia Journal of Tax Law, a prominent specialized tax law journal in the United States (it is ranked 3/45 in Taxation in the Washington & Lee Law Journal Rankings). This publication was authored by the PI, Zachary Marcone (then-Research Assistant at CUHK Law), and Alison Tsang (a tax lawyer in an international law firm in Hong Kong). The journal is available online (open access), which increases its visibility and potential impact. 2. Noam Noked & Zachary Marcone, Targeting Tax Avoidance Enablers, 13 U.C. IRVINE LAW REVIEW 1355-1397 (2024) How can a government counter the activities of professional enablers located in other countries? This has proven to be a formidable challenge. This publication proposes a novel solution: a new international reporting standard, referred to as Global Mandatory Disclosure Rules (GMDR), which will impose reporting obligations on intermediaries assisting taxpayers with designing and implementing cross-border tax schemes. This proposal builds on MDRs currently deployed in several countries, the European Union, and the OECD. Drawing upon these reporting regimes, this article proposes GMDR as a comprehensive standard. This article explains the need for GMDR, explores the relevant design options, and proposes an implementation strategy. By exploring the policy considerations in the design of MDRs, this publication covers the second objective of the project. The publication also evaluates the MDRs developed by the OECD and the EU and the implications of these MDRs for financial centers and various jurisdictions. This analysis covers the third objective of the project. This article was published in the UC Irvine Law Review, a reputable general law review journal in the United States. It is ranked 39/1,557 (top 2.5%) among all law journals in the Washington & Lee Law Journal Rankings. The journal is available online (open access), which increases its visibility and potential impact. We note the following concerning the potential impact of this publication: a. The article was cited in A study prepared at the request of the European Parliament’s Economic and Monetary Affairs Subcommittee on Tax Matters cited this article. See Regulation of intermediaries, including tax advisers, in the EU/Member States and best practices from inside and outside the EU, at 48 (July 2022). b. We submitted the proposal in this article to the European Union as part of a public consultation in October 20222 on “Proposal for a Council Directive to tackle the role of enablers that facilitate tax evasion and aggressive tax planning in the European Union.” This publication was authored by the PI and Zachary Marcone (then-Research Assistant at CUHK Law). 3. Eliza Mik & Noam Noked, Blockchain and Tax Administration: A Critical Assessment, 50 AUSTRALIAN TAX REVIEW 180-1397 (2021) This publication contributes to the emerging literature on blockchain and tax administration. In particular, it responds to recent publications proposing ways to use blockchain and distributed ledger technologies to improve tax administration and compliance. These changes could substantially impact the mandatory reporting obligations and disclosure requirements of intermediaries and taxpayers. This article assesses these proposals and evaluates their purported benefits for tax administration and reporting. It finds that these technologies are not a panacea for tax administration challenges. It shows that many of the problems that blockchains purportedly solve exist off-chain, in the real world, and cannot be addressed by a blockchain. This article also claims that the main benefit from several proposed use cases derives from digitalization in general, not from the deployment of any specific type of database. It remains to be determined whether blockchains are, in fact, superior to other digitalized systems that perform comparable functions in tax administration. This analysis contributes to the project's second and third objectives. This article was published in December 2021 in the Australian Tax Review, a reputable peer-reviewed journal rated “A” in the Australian Business Deans Council (ABDC) Journal Quality List. This publication was authored by the PI and Eliza Mik (Assistant Professor specializing in law and technology at CUHK Law).
