14612220.label: Major findings and research outcome
14612220.value: The Panama Papers, other leaks, and investigative reporting have exposed how tax advisers, lawyers, bankers, and other professionals have helped the world’s economic elites hold their wealth through corporations and trusts organized in tax havens. In response, mandatory disclosure rules (MDRs), which require that intermediaries report their clients’ tax schemes, are becoming prominent tools in the international fight against tax avoidance and evasion. This project analyzes the development of MDRs over the past four decades as a global phenomenon with three distinct phases beginning in the 1980s. The analysis reveals several trends: expansion in the types of schemes that are reportable, extension of reporting obligations to a great diversity of intermediaries, and increasing multilateralism in the effort to curb intermediary-enabled tax avoidance and evasion. This project shows how developments in international tax policy have affected, and will likely continue to affect, the expansion and internationalization of MDRs. It also analyzes the policy considerations for the design of MDRs. Drawing upon this analysis, the project explores an important tax policy question: How can a government counter the activities of professional enablers located in other countries? Addressing this problem has proven to be a formidable challenge. This project proposes a novel solution: a new international reporting standard, referred to as Global Mandatory Disclosure Rules, which will impose reporting obligations on intermediaries assisting taxpayers with designing and implementing cross-border tax schemes. This proposal builds on the legal mechanisms currently deployed in several countries, including the multilateral MDRs of the European Union and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. The project further examines the potential impact of emerging technologies (blockchain and distributed ledgers) on intermediaries and taxpayers’ mandatory reporting obligations and disclosure requirements. It evaluates several proposals for using blockchain in tax administration and finds that blockchain is not a panacea for tax administration challenges. It shows that many problems that blockchain purportedly solves exist off-chain and cannot be addressed by blockchain. This project also claims that the main benefit from several proposed use cases derives from digitalization in general, not from the deployment of any specific type of database.

14612220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14612220.value: This research could be further developed in several ways. More research is needed on the optimal regulation and deterrence of professional enablers of tax abuse. The regulation and deterrence of professional enablers of tax abuse attract increasing attention from policymakers, tax authorities, academics, and tax professionals. The European Union is considering adopting a new directive focusing on this matter. Such regulation could expand the existing MDRs and impose additional obligations. Research into this field should consider the costs and benefits of possible regulatory approaches, the effectiveness of different measures, privacy considerations, and other issues. The PI intends to build on this project to analyze the regulation of professional enablers in future publications. The PI is exploring writing a monograph on the regulation of professional enablers of cross-border tax abuse, which will draw on the work in this project and expand it further.

To address this problem, governments have been adopting mandatory disclosure rules (MDRs), which require that professional enablers report their clients’ tax schemes. This project analyzes the development of MDRs over the past four decades as a global phenomenon with three distinct phases beginning in the 1980s. The analysis reveals several trends: expansion in the types of schemes that are reportable, extension of reporting obligations to a great diversity of intermediaries, and increased multilateralism. 14613320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613320.value: The aim of this research is to review critically the Hong Kong Planning Standards and Guidelines (HKPSG) that provides parametres for land use planning and development control at different geographical levels in Hong Kong. The project endeavours to evaluate the HKPSG and ascertain if it satisfies people’s rights to spatial development for their physical, psychological and social well-being. Planning standards and regulations are under-researched in Hong Kong as well as in the planning profession across the world. The scientific foundation of the HKPSG is not published and its revision is done administratively, with minimal public involvement. As HKPSG is related to strategies, policies and regulations in other government departments, it is more accessible to professionals than the general public. Yet, planning standards are extremely important in shaping urban forms that in turn affect many aspects of our quality of life. The project aims to evaluate the HKPSG in three steps. First, to understand ‘who has what power’ in scoping, formulating, implementing and revising the HKPSG, the research team will review related documents and carry out in-depth interviews with government officials in different policy bureaux and departments, professional institutions, commercial and civil society organisations. Second, to assess from the people’s perspective if the HKPSG is adequate to produce spatial developments conducive to their multifaceted well-being, an innovative ‘time use’ survey to gauge people’s use of urban spaces and a ‘well-being’ survey will be conducted in the five geographical constituencies of the city (Hong Kong Island, Kowloon East, Kowloon West, New Territories East and New Territories West). Residents will be invited to record their current and desired urban activities during a 24-hour period in a weekday and in weekend for 'translation' into their existing and desired urban land use requirements, besides gauging their level of satisfaction. Third, after analysing the research findings, five seminars, organised in two stages, will serve as a platform to provide different stakeholders with the research findings in each step so that they can scrutinise and interrogate the power issues, adequacy of the existing HKPSG and reflect on people’s desired urban activities. All these will contribute to making pertinent recommendations on policies and planning standards. This project is first of its kind in the field of planning and hence it will not only help enhance the HKPSG in Hong Kong but will also have significant impact for theories and practices of planning standards throughout the world. 這項研究旨在嚴格地評估《香港規劃標準與準則》。此標準與準則為香港不同尺度的發展提供土地用途規劃和開發的參數。這研究項目致力探討《香港規劃標準與準則》能否保障市民在使用空間時得以滿足他們身心靈健康和得著社會幸福感的權利。 規劃標準與準則的研究不單只在香港付之闕如，相關的研究在世界的規劃界也屬少見。 《香港規劃標準與準則》的科學基礎未有發佈，並且其修訂是政府的內部行為，公眾參與的程度很低。《香港規劃標準與準則》與其他政府的策略，政策和相關的部門法規息息相關，一般專業人士會比市民大眾容易掌握其內涵。然而，《香港規劃標準與準則》在塑造城市的形態中扮演一個相當重要的角色，在在影響我們生活質素的各個方面。 此項目希望通過三個步驟來評估《香港規劃標準與準則》。首先，團隊會瞭解誰有權去設定準則的範圍，以制定、實施和修訂相關標準。研究小組將審閱相關文獻，並通過訪談不同政策局和部門的政府官員，專業機構，商業和民間社會組織來回答這個問題。第二，為了從市民的角度去瞭解以《香港規劃標準與準則》提供的城市空間，能否為他們帶來多維度的豐盛生命，研究團隊將在香港的五個地理區域（香港島，東九龍，西九龍，新界東和新界西），使用一個創新的「時間使用」表以及相關的「幸福感」問卷作詳細的調查。我們將邀請市民記錄他們的在平日和週末的24小時內的活動概況、滿足感和期望的城市活動，以瞭解現有和期望的城市土地使用要求有何落差。第三，在分析研究結果之後，團隊會分兩個階段來組織研討會，作為提供不同利益相關者審視研究結果的平臺，以便他們可以仔細考量相關權力問題，瞭解市民期望實現的城市活動，以反思現有規劃標準與準則是否合宜和足夠。相信結果將有助於提出具體建議，以改善相關政策和規劃標準。 這項研究在規劃界尚屬首次，因此研究成果不僅會提升香港的《香港規劃標準與準則》，但也會影響世界各地規劃界對規劃標準的理論和實踐底探索。

14613620.value: 清末民國的尺牘：日常生活、家庭與企業

14613620.label: Project Objectives
14613620.value: To compile a database of known Chinese letter-writing manuals published in the late Qing and the Republic (1870 to 1949). To examine changes in the style and content of those manuals over time. To compare changes in style and content to letters written within the period of research (actual letters, not sample letters). To explore the implications of letter content as reflections of changes in ordinary lives, families and business. In the longer-term, to draw attention to the importance of letter writing and letter-writing manuals as expressions of lifestyles in twentieth-century China. To explore if China, like Europe and America, reacted to the expansion of letter writing as brought about by reduced costs in postage in similar ways, especially with regard to personal expressions of intimacy.

14613620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613620.value: 本項目希望通過瞭解清末至於民國時期（1870至於1940年代）尺牘的歷史，展示在現代郵政發展的過程中，郵費下降，寫信普及化對於普通人的生活產生的影響。這個時代，大量的新式尺牘應運而生，同樣也是寫信大眾化的反映。 受到既往歐美學者對於書信的歷史研究的啟發，本項目將討論當寫信成為日常常態的過程中書信的風格如何改變。 我們知道在傳統時期書信遵循固定的格式由來已久。清末民國的政治與社會革命挑戰了原有的書寫格式所依據的傳統秩序；新式的尺牘出現了，代表著新的社會禮儀。在寫信的過程中，尺牘也教育寫信的人們以及讀信的人新禮儀。 由此產生的問題是與新禮儀結合的新尺牘是否提供了個人情感表達的方式，尤其是如何表達親密關係。我們發現晚清到民國的新式尺牘中同樣沒有為親密關係留下多少空間。似乎表達親密關係在書信的格式中仍不重要。但是，在這個時期的詩歌、雜誌文章、短文、小說中有時候會借書信的形式來表達情感。或者，我們可以假定人們確實需要，也確實在書寫親密的書信，但是寫信的人不是通過尺牘，而是通過通俗的文化來學習寫這一類的信。 本項目將搜集和研究清末民國時期的尺牘，並將其與人們寫的以及出版的信件相互比較，討論彼此的形式和內容。通過研究尺牘在時間上的改變，來展示近代中國普通人寫信的歷史。

14613720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613720.value: Intimate partner violence is not limited to adult dating, married, or cohabitating couples. It can emerge early in adolescence and is not unheard of among teenagers. Adolescent dating aggression is increasingly being recognized as a pressing issue because of its connection with maladaptive health and developmental outcomes. It has engaged the interest of sociologists in criminology, victimology, and youth/gender studies internationally, but the research focus has been limited to Western settings. In China, there has been a growing acceptance of romantic relationships and premarital sex amongst urban and rural high school adolescents since the 1990s. However, adolescent dating partner abuse in China remains a largely underexplored and seemingly invisible phenomenon. There is a severe lack of knowledge about the social mechanisms that generate dating aggression attitudes and behaviors among Chinese adolescents. The proposed study will examine the extent and pattern of dating aggression perpetration and victimization across genders and urban/rural settings in China. The analysis will be guided by a theoretical framework that considers the presumed risk factors, or protective factors, behind the perpetration and victimization of dating aggression in Chinese adolescents, including the structural-level mechanisms of relative socioeconomic deprivation and gender inequality, the meso-level mechanisms of social strain and social control, and the situational-level mechanisms of relationship dynamics. While the framework will build on the mainstream sociological and criminological theories of intimate partner violence developed in the West, it will situate the study more firmly in China by incorporating the Chinese cultural mechanisms of face concern and shame proneness. The theoretical significance of this study in China lies in unpacking the varied nature of dating abuse through a multilevel framework and extending the theories of intimate partner violence across urban/rural and cultural settings. The research design will feature a cross-sectional school-based survey of urban and rural senior high school students in Hunan and Guangdong provinces, located in central and southern China respectively, to control for the possible contextual influence of regional heterogeneity in socioeconomic disadvantage on dating violence. A sample of 5,120 students in the eleventh and twelfth grades will be selected using a stratified two-stage cluster sampling method based on the socioeconomic levels of the cities and rural counties in each province and on the high schools in the sampled cities and rural counties. Alongside the theoretical contributions, this study will inform approaches to sex education in relation to cultivating healthy relationships among Chinese adolescents. 親密伴侶暴力並不僅存在于成人約會、已婚或同居伴侶之間，它亦可早在青春期的時候出現，在青少年中並非不尋常。青少年約會侵害日益被意識到是一個緊迫的問題，因為它與適應不良的健康和成長後果有關。它吸引了國際上犯罪學、受害者研究學和青年/性別研究的社會學家的興趣，但目前研究的焦點依然局限於西方背景。自上世紀90年代以來，中國有越來越多的城市和農村高中青少年接受戀愛關係和婚前性行為。然而，中國青少年約會伴侶虐待在很大程度上仍是一個尚未被充分探索和似乎被忽視的現象。關於中國青少年的約會侵害態度和行為的社會產生機制，當前的認識十分匱乏。本項研究擬考察在中國不同性別和城鄉背景下約會侵害行為與受害的程度及模式。分析的理論框架考慮了中國青少年約會侵害行為與受害背後的假定風險或保護因素，包括相對社會經濟剝奪和性別不平等的結構層面機制，社會壓力和社會控制的中觀層面機制，以及關係動態學的情境層面機制。該框架將以西方發展的與親密伴侶暴力相關的主流社會學和犯罪學理論為基礎，並結合中國文化機制中的面子顧慮和羞恥傾向，使本研究更牢固地定位於中國背景之下。基於中國的本研究的理論意義在於，通過一個多層次的框架揭示約會侵害的多樣性質，並將親密伴侶暴力理論同時擴展到城市和農村以及不同的文化背景。研究擬設計一個針對城市和農村高中生的橫截面、學校為本調查。調查的地點分別是位於中國中部的湖南省和南部的廣東省，以控制因地區間社會經濟情況的差異性，對約會暴力產生環境影響的可能性。本研究擬採用分層兩階段整群抽樣法，基於各省城市和農村縣市的社會經濟水準、入選城市和農村縣市的高中，選取5,120名11年級和12年級的學生作為研究樣本。除了理論貢獻外，本研究還將提出與培養中國青少年健康關係相關的性教育方式。

14614120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14614120.value: 國家認同一向是晚清文學研究中重要的主題。《老殘遊記》以其藉由批評地方治理挑戰傳統官僚價值而聞名，標誌了中國知識人對於個人與國家之間關係的重要轉變。本計劃將分析《老殘遊記》對於地方治理的評論，並將之放置於作者劉鶚自身的河工專業的脈絡下加以審視。本計劃期望能夠對環境危機在晚清知識人的國族認同形塑過程中所扮演的角色，提供進一步的理解。 過去研究已經幫助我們瞭解小說中的地方治理之於晚清國族認同議題的重要性，但是學者通常忽略了以下事實：劉鶚真正關心的與其說是他在小說中所批評的地方治理，不如說是日趨敗壞的地方治安。正如關於19世紀中國地方史的研究所顯示的，做為小說地理背景設定的山東，其不斷惡化的地方治安，與這一時期反復發生的洪水氾濫有密切的關係。學者對於此一環境脈絡的忽略，導致沒有意識到環境危機在劉鶚的國族認同形塑中所扮演的關鍵地位。 本計劃希望能夠對晚清文學以及知識史做出如下貢獻：(一) 從環境危機的脈絡理解晚清知識人的個人層面的國家認同建構；(二) 透過說明水利工程與劉鶚對地方治理觀點的關係，對晚清知識人的政治論述提出新角度的觀察；(三) 將生態危機、科技史、文學文本與作者個人經驗納入一個整合性的理解架構。

14614120.label: Realisation of objectives
14614120.value: 1. To understand intellectuals' personal construction of national identity in late Qing literature from ecological perspective: This study illustrates how Liu E, a member of the foreign affairs faction (yangwu pai洋務派), constructs the national identity at the personal level in relation to his engineering concern. The study shows that the hydraulic informed approach of statecraft was also precisely what earned him a reputation as national traitor when he received backlash from conservative officials. To clear the infamy of a collaborator became the central concern in Liu E’s effort of proving himself as a patriot. As Liu E’s self-defense against accusations of treason, The Travels of Lao Can, ironically, adopts as its foremost ideological resource the very hydraulic approach and river work techniques that caused his condemnation. By exploring the paradoxical and ironical nature of Liu E’s effort in proving himself as identity, this study provides a new understanding of personal construction of national identity in late Qing literature from ecological perspective. 2. To illustrate the connection between ecology and late Qing political-philosophical thoughts through the analysis of the concept of "disinterest" in the novel: The idea of incorruptibility, as opposed to corruptibility, had been established by Liu’s time on the paired concepts of gong 公and si 私. Since ancient China, the term gong had been associated with the idea of government affairs and si, with that of civil (minjian 民間) and private (siren 私人) affairs. In terms of governance, gong has been used to refer to one holding public office, that is, the governor, and si to one who is not in office, that is, the governed or civilians. In this sense, this pair of concepts is essentially a domanial one. For those holding public office, the difference between gong and si also refers to the boundary between government affairs and private affairs. Avoiding the merging and intermingling of government money and private money is considered a must for one holding public office, who should be disinterested and thus free to act with perfect impartiality. In this second sense, this pair of concepts is essentially an ethical one. Corruption, defined as the abuse of power for one’s private gain, suggests confusion between government affairs and private affairs. Incorruption, accordingly, suggests that governmental affairs should be segregated from personal ties or interests to avoid the use of government office for private gain. This study shows that the novel not only criticizes incorruptible officials from a hydraulics-informed political perspective but also examines the political concept of gong on which the identity of the incorruptible official is based through the narration of a political consultation, a philosophical conversation, and a murder trial. 3. To explore the associations among Liu E's studies in oracle bone scripts, his devotion to river regulation, and the novel's utopian vision of China' future: This study indicates that the novel’s imagination of China’s revival not only reflects the philosophical legacy from the Taigu school, the Confucian sect of which Liu E was an adherent life-long follower, but also shows how Yellow River governance serves as a hidden context to the novel’s imagination of China’s rejuvenation. The novel’s political imagination that takes the form of the prophecy of China’s future reflects, on the one hand, the Taigu School’s proclivity for apocrypha and, on the other, flood control legends from which the study of apocrypha originated. In regards to the prophecy per se, both the prophetic rhetoric and the explanation of its theoretical grounds are closely related to Liu E’s abiding concern with Yellow River flooding and his profession in river work. By examining the metaphor used in the prophecy, this study illustrates how Liu E bases his political imagination on the model of hydraulic engineering at the very core of the narrative structure. This study illustrates that the novelist’s imagination of a nation-building agenda is through and through informed by his expertise in Yellow River governance. Though the study successfully addresses the associations among Liu E's devotion to river regulation and the novel's utopian vision of China' future, it pays less attention to Liu E's studies in oracle bone scripts. The PI will incorporate this aspect in relation to the hexagram in the legend of river taming in the final book manuscript to be published in 2023. 4. To provide a coherent framework to combine the studies of late Qing fiction, environmental studies, local social history, and the history of science: This study shows that Liu E considers the Yellow River floods and the incorruptible officials’ stringent governance as not only the problems of local governance but a microcosm of national problems. The study argues that the novel views the crises that China faced related to the environment, public security, national economy, and even international relations as the results of an ossified binarism governance discourse. Liu E suggests through the narrative of the novel that, the hydraulics-informed, more fluid strategy of governance that Lao Can proposes to solve the problems of local public security is also the remedy he proposes for the multiple political crises in late Qing China. This study provides a coherent and interdisciplinary study by incorporating the concern of environmental degradation, late Qing local public security, and the development of hydraulic technology into the analysis of late Qing literature.

14614120.label: Major findings and research outcome
14614120.value: The Travels of Lao Can addresses the vice of incorruptible officials along the lines of critical tradition passed down from the late Ming period. However, it also goes beyond traditional criticism of incorruptible officials in general and raises questions related to specific governance issues in Liu E’s own time. Why does the novel choose to launch its criticism of bureaucratic problems from this particular angle instead of another—for example, corruption, as other late Qing “novels of exposure” do? What unique perspective on governance at the local and national level drove Liu E to address the vice of incorruptible officials? And, finally, where did Liu’s unique perspective come from? This study aims to answer the above questions. The novel’s criticism of incorruptible officials, although seemingly centered exclusively on poor local governance, also take national malady as its object of criticism. For Liu E, China was brought into crisis at local and national level because of the very same rigid and stringent way of governance. As an alternative to what he viewed as a dysfunctional mode of governance, Liu E promoted more flexible one, informed primarily by his professional knowledge in hydraulic engineering. This alternative mode proposed a blurring between the government and civilian/private affairs, which Liu E presents as a remedy for local public security problems as portrayed in the novel and the national crisis that he had tried to help resolve, even at the cost of his reputation and life. The impact of the Yellow River floods and Liu E’s techniques of river control deeply shaped the novel and its criticism of local bureaucratic failure and his lifelong engagement in national rejuvenation. The Travels of Lao Can shows how Liu E, a seasoned river engineer, understands China’s crisis of governance and its appropriate remedy in a manner resembling how he understands the Yellow River.

14614120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14614120.value: The study demonstrates how to conceptualize nation-building and socio-political criticism in early 20th century Chinese literature from the lens of flooding. However, the increase in the frequency of flooding events began to take place three centuries earlier, that is, around the Ming and Qing transition. The study thus serves to provide an analytical model for the study of Ming-Qing literature from eco-critical perspective. While eco-critical readings of modern literature have been paid attention the the relation between the Yellow River and literary works, scholars of modern literature tend to focus on the Yellow River as an imagery and its symbolic meaning. This study offers a techno-center approach that would shed new light on the study of modern Chinese environmental literature. As the first eco-critical analysis of traditional Chinese fiction, this study also suggests the possibility of bringing traditional Chinese literature into the discussion of eco-criticism in world literature.

14614120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14614120.value: This study addresses the relation between environmental degradation and the emerge of the first political novel in China, The Travels of Lao Can. As a river engineer, the novelist Liu E bases his criticism of local governance on an intimate association between the Yellow River floods and the rigid mode of governance marked by self-willed incorruptible officials that he sees as the core problem of China at the turn of the twentieth century. The incorruptible officials adopt a harsh style of governance, which they maintain will solve the public security problems resulting from the Yellow River floods. However, this solution is the product of the very same ossified governance philosophy that gave birth to the devastating floods in the first place. For Liu, just as the Yellow River floods shaped the problems of local governance, the floods equally inspired the remedy to these problems. The strategy of governance that the novel proposes in place of the old philosophy of governance derives from the conceptual thinking behind Liu E?s hydraulic design. Rather than reading the novel solely from socio-political and historical context, perspective, this study provides the first eco-critical reading of one of the most important novels in the twentieth century.

14615320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615320.value: Ecosystems provide a variety of benefits to humanity which helps to sustain human well-being. Environmental ecosystem services (EES) and cultural ecosystem services (CES) are very important in communities where they exist. In most societies, the relevance of ecosystem services is centered around the natural environment like forest patches that provide, regulate and support the interactivity with humans. They also provide cultural and other nonmaterial services. In Hong Kong, the feng shui forests represent remnants of (sacred) groves mostly located at the periphery of urban areas. The forests, bequeathed by past civilizations engender substantial environmental services as well as cultural ecosystem services. It is therefore necessary to understand, quantify and analyze the significance of EES as they relate to CES of the feng shui forests that are currently, existing in Hong Kong. This study will therefore select feng shui forests, undertake to characterize, study and analyze their EES and CES; conduct surveys and establish an integration of quantitative and qualitative framework to better understand the importance of the EES as well as the CES. The specific objectives of the study will include 1) to investigate the major environmental and cultural ecosystem services of peri-urban forests in Hong Kong; 2) to study the quantitative characteristics of ecosystem services in the feng shui forests; 3) to identify the characteristics of the environmental and cultural ecosystem services that such forests provide in the Hong Kong context and 4) to understand the major linkages between environmental and cultural ecosystem services and their socioeconomic characteristics in Hong Kong. 生態系統為人類帶來各種好處，有助於人類的福祉。 環境生態系統服務（EES）和文化生態系統服務（CES）在其所在的社區中非常重要。在大多數社會中，生態系統服務圍繞自然環境（如森林區塊）出現，提供、調節和支持與人類之間的互動，還提供文化和其他非物質服務。在香港，風水林是（具有神聖意義的）樹林的殘留部分，大部分位於市區外圍。這些從過去文明遺留下來的森林，帶來了實質性的環境和文化生態系統服務。因此，我們有必要了解、量化和分析環境生態系統服務的重要性，因其與目前在香港存在的風水林的文化生態系統服務相關。因此，本研究將選擇風水林進行研究以了解、解讀和分析EES和CES兩者的特徵，並進行調查來建立結合定量和定性特徵的框架，以更好地了解兩者的重要性。具體研究目標包括：1）調查香港近郊森林的主要環境和文化生態系統服務；2）量化風水林生態系統服務的特徵；3）辨認在香港背景下此類森林提供的環境和文化生態系統服務的特徵；以及4）了解香港的環境和文化生態系統服務與其社會經濟特徵之間的主要聯繫。

14615820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615820.value: Young children in Hong Kong and Guangzhou are speakers of Cantonese, Mandarin and English to different extents, ranging from monolinguals to highly proficient trilinguals. For families who use Cantonese and Mandarin regularly at home, nurturing trilingual competence in the child through early exposure to English is a much-welcomed concept. Despite the widespread practice of introducing English to toddlers through daily interactions at home, it is not clear whether and to what extent the relatively small amount of English input provided by the child’s caretaker can stimulate acquisition of English and impact on the other two languages, which are still developing. The relation between language input and developmental outcome (“input-outcome relation”) is a key yet unresolved issue in psycholinguistic approaches to early trilingual development. For children being raised trilingually, their input in each language is likely to be reduced compared to their monolingual peers, but the few existing cases suggest that these children do not develop their languages more slowly than their monolingual and bilingual peers, and that the reported proportion of input in a language does not form a straightforward linear relation with the rate of acquisition in that language, pointing towards more accurate measures of input and a multi-factorial model of input-outcome relations. Building on the team’s previous research on bilingual children and a recent pilot study on a trilingual child, the proposed study investigates input-outcome relations in Cantonese-Mandarin-English trilingual children and their monolingual peers in Hong Kong and Guangzhou for two years from 1;00 to 3;00 (N = 35). Existing Cantonese-Mandarin bilingual infants will be introduced to a third language (English) through caretaker-child interactions from 1;00. The quantity and quality of the caretaker input and the child’s acquisition of the languages will be documented, assessed and correlated systematically through an array of methods including Language Input Diary, web-based caretaker-child interaction recording, standardized parental reports, as well as direct cognitive and language assessment. Our innovative use of web-based methods incurs lower costs and offers greater flexibility and has the potential to transform research on caretaker-child interactions. The resulting database will generate highly accurate measures of fine-grained aspects of both the input and the outcome while controlling for the child’s executive functioning. The findings will be a crucial step towards a multi-factorial model of input-outcome relations in trilingualism, and for the very first time empirically address the probing questions raised by parents who are nurturing Cantonese-Mandarin-English trilingual children at home. 香港和廣州的兒童都能夠在不同程度上使用粵語、普通話和英語，但是有些兒童只能流利使用其中一種語言，有些則能夠流利使用全部三種語言。對於那些已經在家中慣常使用粵語和普通話的家庭來説，很多家長都希望讓小孩儘早接觸英語，從而讓小孩發展出粵-普-英三語能力。雖然粵港兩地已經有很多家長和小孩在日常互動中使用英語，讓照顧小孩的家庭成員為小孩的英語發展提供語言輸入，但是這種英語輸入的數量與只講英語的單語家庭相比並不算多。這種少量的語言輸入能夠在多大程度上促進小孩的英語語言發展以及會否對他們尚未發展成熟的粵語和普通話產生負面影響？這個問題至今仍未研究清楚。在心理語言學理論框架下的早期三語研究中，語言輸入和語言發展成果的關係（“輸入-成果關係”）是一個非常關鍵但尚未完全解決的問題。如果小孩在家中接觸到三種語言，每一種語言他們得到的輸入都比對應的單語兒童少。但是現時僅有的少量關於三語兒童的研究表明，這些三語兒童的語言發展速度不一定會比相應的單語兒童慢，而且三種語言輸入的數量比例不一定與孩子的三語發展速度構成直接明確的綫性關係，説明我們需要更加精確地計算和衡量語言輸入的不同方面並建立一個綜合考慮多種因素的理論模型來預測三語發展的速度和路徑。本研究團隊曾進行大量關於粵-英雙語兒童的研究，最近也完成了對一個粵-普-英三語兒童的長期追蹤研究。以此為基礎，我們將展開一項關於香港和廣州的粵-普-英三語兒童及其對應的單語兒童的大型長期追蹤研究（共35名兒童），其中三語組的兒童需在1歲以前在家中已經接觸到粵語和普通話，並從1歲開始接觸英語。我們將會透過記錄他們1歲到3歲兩年間的三語發展來研究語言輸入與語言發展的關係。我們將使用語言輸入日記、家長報告、網絡互動錄影以及標準化語言及認知測試等一系列方法來記錄、評估和分析小孩的照顧者的語言輸入的數量和質量。其中使用網絡來搜集錄影數據是我們的創新做法，這種做法所需經濟成本較低、時間安排也更靈活，將有機會為語言輸入和語言發展領域帶來重要的方法論革新。本研究所建成的語言數據庫將有助於我們篩選出衡量語言輸入和語言發展成果的有效指標。這是我們建立一個有效預測三語發展的多因素模型的關鍵一步，也是學界首次以大量研究證據來回應粵-普-英三語幼兒家長所關心的問題。

14616520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616520.value: Caught between China’s ever-expanding urban centres and marginalized rural villages exists an amalgamated territory that has surprisingly been overlooked and dismissed by the profession and academics. We have coined this diffused landscape “Middle Ground”, a peripheral urban condition distinctive to China. China’s Middle Ground is not planned, it is continuously transforming and characterized by a series of generic buildings typologies: three-story concrete frame houses, corrugated pitch roofed warehouses, brick-clad factories and glass office buildings. Beyond these anonymous buildings, exists a complex network of once-rural historical villages, once the backbone of vital trade routes, that are today disappearing at alarming rates. The future existence and eventual integration of these traditional villages back into the daily life of China’s “Terrain Vague” is the topic of this research. By taking a network of Hakka villages centered around the village of He Xin Wu (何新屋), Guangdong Province, the proposal seeks to study a dozen traditional Hakka villages along the ancient Yue Gan Trade Route (粤赣驿道) connecting Guangdong and Jiangxi, with the aim to understand and assess their status vis-à-vis configuration, construction and potential revitalization. The urgency of the research relates to two critical issues: firstly the great majority of these rural settlements are not listed for preservation and hence will soon disappear – demolished and redeveloped. Secondly, the few examples that have been listed have been earmarked as future tourist destinations, a mixed blessing that most probably will act as a temporary solution with the risk of suffocating their existence and preventing a genuinely sustainable recovery. The research methodology relies on community participation, involving the public directly into the formulation of a new social framework to establish critical relationships between heritage and territory. Via a series of architectural prototypes, pilot projects that stimulate civic action and establish the “re-acquisition of historical consciousness” to quote the Italian architect Giancarlo De Carlo, this proposal seeks to recover existing historical structures via architectural operations. Without innovation and solutions that challenge China's Middle Ground, its rural DNA risks being lost and vanishing forever. Architecture through the integration of heritage and technology can facilitate a realignment and promote a positive change between rural traditions and the inevitable socio-economic restructuring. He Xin Wu represents a unique opportunity to stimulate a sense of place, instill civic pride and social engagement in a constantly mutating and often anonymous landscape. 在中國不斷擴大的城市中心和邊緣化的鄉村之間，存在著一個合併的領域，令人驚訝地被專業人士和學者所忽視和忽視。我們創造了這種分散的景觀“中間地帶”，這是中國特有的周邊城市環境。中國的中間地帶不是計劃中的，它正在不斷轉變並以一系列通用建築類型為特徵：三層混凝土框架房屋，波紋狀瀝青屋頂倉庫，磚砌工廠和玻璃辦公樓。除了這些匿名建築物之外，還存在一個由原本古老的鄉村組成的複雜網絡，這些鄉村曾經是重要貿易路線的支柱，如今卻以驚人的速度消失。 這些傳統村莊的未來存在和最終融合回到中國“地形模糊”的日常生活中是本研究的主題。通過以廣東省何新屋村為中心的客家村落網絡，該提案旨在研究連接廣東和江西的粵贛驛道沿線的十幾個傳統客家村落，目的是了解和評估它們相對於配置，構造和潛在的振興狀況。這項研究的緊迫性涉及兩個關鍵問題：首先，這些農村住區中的絕大部分未列入保護名單，因此將很快消失-拆除和重新開發。其次，已經列出的幾個例子被指定為未來的旅遊目的地，這是一種混合的祝福，很可能會作為一種臨時解決方案，存在使他們窒息的危險並阻止真正的可持續恢復。 研究方法依賴社區參與，使公眾直接參與製定新的社會框架以建立遺產與領土之間的重要關係。通過一系列建築原型，激發公民行動並建立“重新獲得歷史意識”的試點項目，引用意大利建築師Giancarlo De Carlo的建議，該提案旨在通過建築運營來恢復現有的歷史建築。沒有創新和解決方案來挑戰中國的中間地帶，其農村DNA可能會丟失並永遠消失。通過將遺產和技術融合在一起的建築可以促進結構調整，並促進農村傳統與不可避免的社會經濟結構之間的積極變化。和心舞代表了一個難得的機會，可以激發人們的處境感，在不斷變化的，常常是匿名的環境中灌輸公民的自豪感和社會參與感。

14616520.label: Realisation of objectives
14616520.value: The Living Heritage research project has enhanced our understanding of how heritage settlements in the Middle Ground territory of Guangdong adapt to and cope with rapid urbanization. Despite being impacted by the Covid-19 pandemic, which caused a delay in constructing the final prototype, we are pleased to report that the prototype is now being built and will benefit the local primary school of Luojing near the historic village of He Xin Wu. Justification: the percentages achieved for objective 4 and objective 5 are not 100% because the final prototype is currently under construction. Below is a summary of the progress made and goals achieved in this project. OBJECTIVE 01_ HERITAGE STATUS (COMPLETION 100%) Chart the history of Hakka villages along the Yue Gan Trade Route in Guangdong Province, China and contextualise the current heritage status. 1. In the past three years, centring on He Xin Wu, we have conducted Macro and Micro research on a dozen Hakka villages along the Yue Gan Trade Route, analysing how these villages have transformed into a Middle Ground morphology, from a socio-geographic and economic perspective. 2. Through the comprehensive literature review on the historical map, local chronicles, clan pedigree and oral history, we clarified the historical development of Yue Gan Trade Route and documented it in the midterm report. 3. We have closely tracked and mapped the heritage village of He Xin Wu, closely interacting with local villagers and collecting tangible and intangible materials helping us to understand the historical development of the settlement. 4. This material was translated into graphic mapping material that formed the basis of our journal article about the research. OBJECTIVE 02_ NETWORK OF OPPORTUNITIES (COMPLETION 100%) Identify tangible and intangible cultural elements associated with each village to establish a network of potential social infrastructures. 1. The midterm report mapped out the existing exchange network surrounding He Xin Wu, which includes traditional temporary and permanent markets. 2. Visits to the primary and secondary schools near He Xin Wu were conducted and documented to outline the educational network in the Guangdong Middle Ground. 3. Through our survey process, we indentified the ideal location for implementing the Mud Library prototype. 4. The research team interviewed various local craftsmen to explore traditional construction techniques and knowledge, specifically focusing on the creation of traditional mud bricks, as detailed in the midterm report. 5. The survey documented traditional Hakka architectural elements related to mud resources, carpentry tools, earth composition formulas, and cooperation systems, all of which represent significant Living Heritage in the Chinese Middle Ground. 6. Collaboration with a soil expert, Niko Leung, the founder of Hong Kong Soil, facilitated the integration of modern soil knowledge to enhance and adapt local practices into modern design solutions. 7. The findings mentioned above were directly incorporated into the construction of the final Mud Library prototype. OBJECTIVE 03_PARTICIPATORY WORKSHOPS (COMPLETION 100%) Coordinate a series of public workshops and exhibitions with the aim to stimulate design proposals for social interactive prototypes. 1. In Fall 2018, the Principal Investigator (PI) and Co-Investigator (CoI) coordinated a graduate International Design Studio for students from The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Guangzhou University. 2. During Spring 2022, a drawing workshop was held for 19 Grade Three students at Dahu Primary School, providing insights into the dreams and aspirations of the younger generation in Hakka villages. 3. In Fall 2023, a group game workshop was arranged for 9 Grade One students at Luojing Primary School, offering local children the opportunity to participate in the prototype design process. 4. In Spring 2024, the Mud Library took part in the Vice Versa public exhibition tour in Shenzhen, Guangzhou, and Shanghai to gather public reactions and feedback. OBJECTIVE 04_ PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION (COMPLETION 80%) Filter and coordinate a single prototype solution that can feasibly be implemented and contribute to the development of a Living Heritage paradigm. 1. Two prototypes were conceptualized and developed: one being the Heritage Workshop for a communal Centre situated in the northwest of He Xin Wu village, designed with rammed earth and bamboo, while the other was the Mud Library, serving as a conceptual model and integrated into the final prototype constructed with mud bricks at a nearby primary school, as illustrated in the Graphics section. 2. The PI successfully secured a donation of 500,000 HKD from the Chan Cheung Mun Chung Charitable Fund in Hong Kong, which covered the construction costs of the final prototype. 3. As of the time of writing this report, the final Mud Library has been completed up to 30%, to finish and inaugurate it for the school in Fall 2025. 4. The prototype serves as a vessel of knowledge, transforming modern earthen architecture by enhancing material properties and environmental performance while preserving the essence of Hakka culture throughout its design, construction, and utilization. 5. The prototype will help revive disappearing Hakka building techniques and craftsmanship, contributing to the preservation and development of local Hakka culture and the physical adaptation of Living Heritage in the Middle Ground. 6. The local Government Officials of Dahu Town, Lianping, approved the project and displayed significant interest in the project's potential and aims to showcase it as an exemplary representation of Hakka heritage. OBJECTIVE 05_PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION (COMPLETION 60%) Address how the lessons learnt from the implementation of the prototype can establish a framework for the integration of historical villages into China's Middle Ground. Despite facing challenges such as delays in project completion due to the COVID-19 pandemic and difficulties in fundraising for the prototype, we have gathered the following insights to create a framework for historical villages: SUSTAINABILITY EVALUATION 1. Traditional Hakka earth architecture has shown excellent environmental performance, especially in terms of thermal comfort and energy efficiency due to its material properties. 2. By enhancing the traditional Hakka soil formula in collaboration with local craftsmen and soil experts, and modifying the design of mud bricks and their connections, we can enhance the durability, lighting propoerties and ventilation of earthen architecture. 3. The Mud Library will serve as a model for integrating traditional materials and heritage into modern society. 4. Social Performance, through active involvement with the community, we have conducted thorough occupant assessments while implementing the final prototype. 5. These assessments have enabled the team to explore the project's impact on Hakka identity, cultural sentiment, and engagement with various stakeholders, including craftsmen, users, local habitats, and government authorities. These findings will help shape the final framework. POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS: 1. We aim to introduce an innovative community engagement approach for heritage preservation, promoting its application in various historical villages in the Chinese Middle Ground. 2. The knowledge acquired through this Active Participation can be used in future projects, both by the PI and the local authorities that will develop a strategy for the remaining Hakka Abandoned heritage villages. 3. With the completion of the final prototype, we intend to create a construction manual for Hakka earthen architecture to pass on local knowledge and heritage to the wider public.

14616520.label: Major findings and research outcome
14616520.value: This project has generated significant outputs and engaged the public through workshops and meetings, contributing to the study of rural heritage in China. The primary discoveries stem from the completion of a modern library building, a collaborative pilot project with the Hakka community and local Government. This initiative has reconnected local children with their cultural heritage. The project has provided valuable insights into traditional Mud architecture and its contemporary relevance. Additionally, the creation of a prototype has facilitated the establishment of a collaborative network with local community artisans and government officials, leading to key findings in two main areas that were basis of the journal paper written (see attachment). Relevance of Traditional Hakka Settlements Traditional Hakka settlements, characterized by clan-centric living arrangements and communal spaces like ancestor halls, reflect the importance of family structure and kinship in Hakka society. These settlements, guided by Fengshui principles, feature nucleated clusters with rows of identical dwelling units that optimize space and privacy for nuclear families within the clan structure. While traditionally built with materials like rammed earth and timber, modern construction methods are gradually replacing them. Hakka markets, serving as social and economic hubs, preserve traditions and support local economies through the exchange of agricultural products, livestock, and homemade goods. Towards an In-Place Urbanism with Dual Characteristics In recent years, Hakka villages like He Xin Wu have experienced depopulation as residents move to new concrete housing, leaving abandoned Wei Long Wu as the village core. Despite the younger generation's waning interest, the old village remains culturally significant for traditional rituals. The development of the G358 National Highway has led to the emergence of new linear settlements integrated into the highway economy. Hakka individuals are diversifying income sources by selling Hakka food and agricultural products, reducing dependence on clans and influencing the design of modern living spaces. The growth of small businesses, influenced by paddy cultivation seasonality and urbanization, has transformed traditional markets into modern retail outlets, catering to various needs and showcasing the adaptation of high-end consumption in commercial centers like Zhongxin town.

14616520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14616520.value: This project has introduced a novel approach to working and collaborating on heritage initiatives in China's intermediate regions. The PI successfully established trust and engaged directly with the community while also fostering connections with the local government. Moving forward, there is an opportunity to expand knowledge and monitor research progress on two fronts: evaluating the building's impact on primary school students and observing how the Heritage committee utilizes it as a model for living heritage preservation and cultural conservation.

14616520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14616520.value: This research explored the concept of the "Middle Ground," a hybrid architectural landscape blending traditional Hakka village elements with modern influences in peri-urban areas of the Pearl River Delta. The research examined the evolution of four Hakka villages, showcasing the transition from traditional to contemporary structures and lifestyles. The emergence of concrete housing has led to a spatial separation between residential and communal spaces, altering the traditional nucleated settlement pattern. While modern materials and styles are evident in the exteriors of houses, interior spaces still reflect traces of agricultural heritage. The study concludes that without intervention, the Middle Ground risks losing its unique cultural identity and becoming homogenized. Preserving the heritage of the Hakka people is crucial, with a focus on tangible and intangible assets that can adapt to contemporary needs. The term "Living Heritage" was introduced to emphasize the importance of integrating heritage into rural modernization efforts. Community involvement is highlighted as key to maintaining connections between heritage and the evolving Middle Ground, fostering a sense of place and identity. Architectural prototypes were employed as tools for aligning rural traditions with socioeconomic changes, promoting civic pride and distinct identity within the dynamic landscape.

The PI will create and manage a publicly available online database in the form of a website that will collect, archive, and share critical essays, journal articles, reading lists, course outlines, film and video extracts, and still and moving images of art performances and installations that engage with Southeast Asian critical theory. The PI will write an international refereed journal article that provides a critical survey of theoretical frameworks and vocabularies highlighted during the conference. The PI will draft a textbook proposal for an introductory reader on Southeast Asian critical theory that anthologizes and annotates a selection of texts from the website in English translation for classroom use at the university level.

14616920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616920.value: This General Research Fund (GRF) grant will contribute to the development of a preliminary corpus of critical theory in Southeast Asia, for which no publications exist. Although deemed to be problematic in its provenance and conceptualization from the colonial geopolitics of the Cold War, Southeast Asia offers a provisional frame for studying the diverse cultures of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations or ASEAN, which officially comprises Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore, Myanmar, Timor-Leste, and the Philippines. Most theoretical frameworks and vocabularies are developed and utilized with Western Europe and North America as their main frames of reference, then applied to different contexts without significantly altering their language or purview to suit the particularities of these contexts. The GRF will build on recent initiatives to decolonize theoretical frameworks and vocabularies away from dominant sites of knowledge production that have been concentrated in North America, Europe, and Australia. Because shifting the objects and terms of inquiry to Asia can result in the establishment of new hierarchies, this research proposal aims to expand the corpus and scope of critical theory beyond South Asia and Northeast Asia to elsewhere in the larger region. The output for the GRF grant will include: 1) an international conference in Hong Kong featuring critics, scholars, teachers, artists, filmmakers, and curators based in the region to discuss how they engage with theoretical frameworks and vocabularies drawn from local perspectives and experiences; 2) an open-access website that collects, archives, and shares critical essays, course outlines, reading lists, film and video extracts, and still and moving images of art performances and installations that engage with Southeast Asian critical theory; and 3) an international referred journal that provides a critical survey of theoretical frameworks and vocabularies highlighted during the conference; 4) a textbook proposal for an introductory reader that anthologizes and annotates a selection of texts from the website in English translation for classroom use at the university level. The goal of this GRF proposal is to explore how critical theory in or about Southeast Asia might assume several forms: 1) the description and conceptualization of social and political conditions drawn from vernacular understandings and keywords; 2) the reception and translation of critical theories from North America, Western Europe, Australia, and Northeast Asia in and for Southeast Asian contexts; 3) the engagement by artists and filmmakers based in the region with vernacular understandings and keywords. 本研究將有助於批判理論的基本語料庫在東南亞的發展，該基本語料庫目前暫無公開發表的資料。儘管從冷戰期的殖民地緣政治學来看，該理論的出處及概念化仍存在問题，但東南亞地區為研究東南亞國家聯盟（ASEAN）的多樣文化提供了一個由印尼、泰國、柬埔寨、越南 、老撾、馬来西亞、文莱、新加坡、缅甸、東帝汶和菲律賓官方組成的臨時框架。 大多數理論框架和詞彙的發展和運用都是以西歐和北美為主要的參考框架，然後於不同的語境中應用，當中並沒有為其語言或範圍作出顯著的改變，以切合這些語境的特殊性。是項計劃將建立在最近理論框架和詞彙的解殖倡議基礎上，以脫離集中在北美、歐洲和澳洲的知識生產主導場域。由於將研究對象和術語轉移到亞洲會導致新等級制度的建立，本研究計劃旨在將批判理論的文庫和範圍，從南亞和東北亞拓展至其他更大區域的地方。 研究成果包括：1）在香港舉行國際會議：邀請東南亞地區的評論家，學者，教師，藝術家，電影製片人和策展人，討論他們如何與源自本土視角與經驗的理論框架及概念互動； 2）建立一個開放式網站：收集，存檔和分享批判性文章，課程大綱，閱讀清單，電影和視頻的摘錄，以及東南亞批判理論相關的表演與裝置藝術的影像； 3）建立國際審閱期刊，深入闡述會議提出的理論框架和重要概念； 4）擬定針對入門讀者的教科書提案，摘選並註解上述網站文章的英文譯本，以供大學使用。 研究目的是探討東南亞或關於東南亞的批判理論如何呈現出幾種形式：1）從方言的理解和關鍵詞中提取的對社會和政治狀況的描述和概念化； 2）來自北美、西歐、澳洲和東北亞的在東南亞語境下或者關於東南亞語境的批判理論的接受與翻譯； 3）該地區的藝術家和電影製片人通過方言的理解和關鍵詞的參與。

14616920.label: Realisation of objectives
14616920.value: The PI was successful in realizing one of the key objectives of the GRF grant to organize an international conference about decolonizing theory in Southeast Asia featuring scholars, critics, teachers, artists, filmmakers, and curators based in the region to present papers about how their intellectual, creative, and pedagogical work engages with theoretical frameworks and vocabularies drawn from local perspectives and experiences. In fact, the PI was able to convene three such conferences in 2021 and 2022, which were forced to be held online because of pandemic quarantine and travel restrictions. Held on 27-29 May 2021, 'Doing Theory in Southeast Asia' featured over thirty speakers based in eight different time zones presenting in nine plenary panels. The papers explored a range of topics crossing the borders of Literary Studies, Film and Screen Studies, Gender and Queer Studies, Critical Race Theory, Cultural Anthropology, Folklore Studies, Memory Studies, Science and Technology Studies, Disability Studies, and Environmental Studies. The online event drew approximately 400 registrants over its three days. The three keynote speakers were Syed Farid Alatas, an expert on decolonizing theory who is a Professor of Sociology at the National University of Singapore; Sunil Manghani, Manager Editor of Theory, Culture & Society who is Deputy Dean at the University of Southampton’s Winchester School of Art; and Yee I-Lann, a globally renowned multimedia artist who is based in Kota Kinabalu. 'Inter-Asia Intermediality: A Two-Part International Workshop' was co-organized with Prof. Brian Bernards of the University of Southern California, a prominent scholar of Southeast Asian Literature and Cinema. Two separate conferences were held in Los Angeles on 25-26 May 2022 and in Hong Kong on 9-10 June 2022, featuring thirty speakers who are emerging and established scholars of Southeast Asian Film and Media Culture. The conferences explored how the vernacular processes of production, distribution, exhibition, and consumption of different forms of media within the region might challenge homogeneous disciplinary-bounded and regionally-bounded understandings of 'Asia.' The keynote speaker for the University of Southern California conference was Prof. Bliss Cua Lim, a prominent Film and Media Studies scholar at the Cinema Studies Institute of the University of Toronto who studies vernacular postcolonial experiences in Asian horror cinema. The USC conference opened with a poetry reading by Adrian de Leon, an award-winning public historian of transpacific Philippine migration and indigrneity. It featured a screening of 'Mekong 2030,' an omnibus film produced by the Luang Prabang Film Festival, with episodes by five different young filmmakers from Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam. The Director of the Luang Prabang Film Festival, Sean Chadwell, participated in a post-screening discussion. The keynote speakers for the Chinese University of Hong Kong conference were Prof. Patrick F. Flores, a world-renowned art historian who served as curator of the Singapore Biennale, which specializes in Southeast Asian contemporary art. The CUHK conference concluded with a talk by Ho Tzu Nyen, an international multimedia artist based in Singapore who created the Critical Dictionary of Southeast Asia, an interactive online database of keywords in Southeast Asian history and culture. Selected papers from the ‘Doing Theory in Southeast Asia’ conference have been collected in a special issue “Vernacular Theory in Southeast Asia,” which is under review with the journal 'Cultural Studies.' Twelve of the best papers from 'Inter-Asia Intermediality: A Two-Part International Workshop' will appear in an edited volume to be tentatively published with the University of Hawai`i’s Global Asias: Method, Architecture, Praxis book series. The CFPs for these three conferences were widely circulated via mailing lists and social networks such as Facebook, H-Net, and the Association for Cultural Studies. To draft the CFP, which delineated the themes and scopes of the conferences, the PI conducted extensive research about vernacular theoretical frameworks and vocabularies that draw from local perspectives and experiences in Southeast Asia. To develop the website, the PI has identified important texts, novels, and films from Southeast Asia. However, the PI’s access to texts, novels, and films from Southeast Asia in Hong Kong has been limited due to their lack of availability in Hong Kong’s university and public libraries. The PI had planned to visit libraries in Singapore where many of these materials are collected but was forced to cancel these travel plans because of the pandemic situation. To resolve this problem, the PI has needed to order books and DVDs. Because the covid-19 quarantine and travel restrictions prevented the PI from interacting in person with scholars, critics, teachers, artists, filmmakers, and curators based in the region, the PI has experienced difficulty in cultivating stronger ties with them. Without in-person interactions, the PI has been less successful at soliciting resources from them for the archive. As such, the website needed to be amended to focus less on uploading existing materials than on listing potential resources for further critical and creative work. Because of the failure to collect materials for the website, plans for a textbook proposal needed to be revised as well. The website ‘Doing Theory in Southeast Asia’ is divided into three main sections: ‘About,’ ‘Events’ and ‘Resources.’ The ‘Events’ page provides information about themes, panels, and papers at the three ‘Doing Theory in Southeast Asia’ and ‘Inter-Asia Intermediality’ conferences. The ‘About’ page presents preliminary thoughts on important questions such as ‘What is Southeast Asia,’ ‘What does it mean to ‘do theory,’ and ‘How can we ‘theorize’ Southeast Asian culture.’ The ‘Resources’ section is divided into two subsections. The first, ‘General Resources,’ provides a table with resources on Southeast Asian theory. The table categorizes sources based on country, year, and medium. Users are able to navigate the entries using search functions and rearrange columns according to their categories. The second ‘Resources’ subsection is entitled ‘Archipelagic Juxtapositions.’ It features pages that collect texts and materials on different emerging topics pertaining to the theorizing of Southeast Asian culture such as ‘myths,’ ‘music,’ and ‘Cold War.’ The vision is to expand this laboratory of ideas to cover new topics that uncover unexplored connections between seemingly unrelated objects. The PI has drafted a journal article that examines the imagination of ‘Southeast Asia’ in the omnibus film 'Mekong 2030' and interactive database 'Critical Dictionary of Southeast Asia,' the two creative works featured in the Inter-Asia Intermediality conferences. Because of the difficulties in gathering materials for a textbook of Southeast Asian theoretical texts, the PI used the teaching relief from the GRF grant to draft a book-length monograph based on some of the themes and keywords uncovered from his research for the conferences and website. Looking at images of verticality and ruin, the monograph elaborates about perceptions of capital development and flight in the films, visual art, and scholarship of Southeast Asian nations. It discusses how arthouse cinema in Southeast Asia produced for the international festival circuit is preoccupied with the representation of poverty and squalor by relying on legible tropes of ghettos and slums. Based on Thongchai Winichakul’s conception of mapping, it analyzes how tourist maps delineate the spatial environments of Southeast Asian cities. Lastly, it engages with notions of environmental vulnerability, emergency, catastrophe, and risk in coastal cities in the region that are in danger of being submerged and devastated by sinking land and rising oceans due to the climate crisis. To disseminate knowledge about the website and its findings, the PI has delivered presentations at several local and international conferences.

14616920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14616920.value: The General Research Fund grant financed the production of one open-access online archive, three international hybrid conferences, one special issue proposal, one journal article draft, and one book monograph draft and proposal. The research conducted for the GRF grant highlights how theory might assume several forms: 1) the description and conceptualization of social and political conditions drawn from vernacular understandings and keywords; 2) the reception and translation of critical theories from North America, Western Europe, Australia, and Northeast Asia in and for Southeast Asian contexts; 3) the engagement by artists and filmmakers based in the region with vernacular understandings and keywords. Papers presented at the conferences revealed more expansive understandings of theory and theorizing, which diverge from orthodox dictionary definitions. For them, theory is not simply as a “general” or “abstract” set of “principles”, which could be universally applied “to explain phenomena.” Expected to represent a comprehensive system of thought, theoretical frameworks are presumed to be the outcome of an exhaustive, scientific process of research, inquiry, and reflection. To be able to elucidate complex phenomena, their principles often rely on the dense language of abstraction. Instead of relying on ontological and epistemological traditions rooted in continental philosophy, theory could alternately draw on vernacular keywords or frameworks, which are grounded in the particularities of local contexts. It could encompass the generation of ideas, impressions, and sentiments through non-verbal forms of critical and creative expression, such as in cinema and visual art. Not just simply the product of a solitary genius isolated from social reality, it could involve the collaborative activity of speculation and imagination, which summon an alternate world into existence. Some recurrent theorizations in critical and creative texts from the region include the imagination of flexible, non-hierarchical, and archipelagic social formations beneath and beyond the nation in the form of localisms, postcolonialisms, and regionalisms. Such texts also conceptualize possible responses to urgent political, economic, and environmental issues pertaining to authoritarianism, migration, and development.

14616920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14616920.value: The 'Doing Theory in Southeast Asia' website will continue to incorporate more materials and resources as these become available. It is being expanded to include research findings from the CUHK Faculty of Arts Direct Grant (HK$86,000) about images of environmental vulnerability and catastrophe in Southeast Asia. The PI will disseminate knowledge about the website by delivering conference presentations at the Critical Island Studies conference in Yogyakarta in October 2023 and Southeast Asian Comparative Literature conference in Hanoi in December 2023. The PI and RA have also submitted proposals to publish chapters about Southeast Asian theory in the 'Routledge Handbook of Decolonisation' and 'SAGE Handbook of Decolonial Theory.' They plan to organize a 4th international conference featuring papers that engage with the materials and resources on the website. The PI is working on a new monograph entitled 'In Search of Critical Theory in Southeast Asia' based on the findings of this research project.

14616920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14616920.value: Amid the prevalence of critical theories produced in North America and Western Europe, the tendency in the humanities is to treat such theories as universal without questioning the applicability of their themes and purviews to other conditions and experiences. In response to this problem, the General Research Fund grant builds on recent initiatives to shift theory away from the dominant sites of knowledge production centered in these locations. This GRF grant has funded the development of the 'Doing Theory in Southeast Asia' website, a publicly accessible database for teachers, scholars, artists, and curators that makes available critical and creative resources which engage with theoretical frameworks and vocabularies drawn from local contexts in the Southeast Asian region.

14617220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14617220.value: 制定三維藍綠基建性能指數以促進可持續城市生活

14617220.label: Project Objectives
14617220.value: Field measurement, model calibration and validation: We will conduct field measurements of human bio-meteorological variables at realistic sites where urban green-blue infrastructures interfaced with the built-environment using coupled Human Biometeorological monitoring Systems (HuBioSys) in order to have a better understanding of the impact on their cooling effect and human thermal comfort. This measurement campaign will also provide input parameters, and basis for calibration and validation of the ENVI-met model that will be used for objective 2. Parametric model setup and simulation: Based on our knowledge of the urban morphological characteristics of Hong Kong, we will develop 768 sets of parametric urban models that are realistic in the context of high-density city design. These sets of urban models will be used for the parametric tests. Using the validated model setting, we will numerically test of the urban models under different combinations of building form, greening options and water coverage at the under typical summer and extremely hot weather conditions. Development of a green-blue index for urban cooling: We will evaluate and compare the cooling efficiency in terms of human thermal comfort among different parametric scenarios under typical hot summer weather condition noting the similarities or differences of their thermal performances. Based on the findings, a new green-blue index based on a multivariate regression model between the bare and green urban morphological parameters and the output thermal comfort benefit will be developed. Practicality sensitivity test and drawing up of design guidelines: the new performance-based green-blue infrastructure index will be applied and tested in a real-world construction project in collaboration with practitioners. Sensitivity tests, adjustments and simplifications will be carried out to ensure practicality of the new index. Then, we will draw up a set of sites and building design guidelines that are targeted at solving the urban overheating and human heat stress problem. The guidelines will be simplified and relatable by/for designers, planners and policymakers

14617220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617220.value: Urban overheating is a foremost environmental challenge facing tropical cities including Hong Kong, and results in several health impacts including heat stress and discomfort leading to illness and death (Kjellstrom, Holmer, & Lemke, 2009). One verified solution is the innovative integration of greenery and waterbodies into city design. Based on our previous study (Ng et.al 2012), 20 – 30% of the gross floor area is allotted for greening particularly to mitigate the heat island effect. This greenery coverage was based on ~1ᵒC temperature regulation and derived from ground-level tree planting numerical experimentation. However, when implemented, the government practice note included façade and rooftop greening, and waterbodies with variable reduction factor from 0 - 50% to allow practical flexibility. However, these variant combinations have no empirical evidence to ascertain equal thermal regulation performance. To fill this knowledge gap, this study will develop a new performance-based green-blue infrastructure index for urban overheating mitigation by conducting very-high-resolution microclimate analysis of the impact of different combinations of proportions of green-blue infrastructure coverage relative to the total surface area in the high-density context. The objectives are to: (1) Conduct field measurements of bio-meteorological variables at 12 realistic sites where green-blue infrastructures interfaced with the built-environment using coupled Human Biometeorological monitoring Systems (HuBioSys) to have a better understanding of the impact of their cooling effect and human comfort improvement, and to provide a basis to calibrate and validate the model to be used for objective 2; (2) 768 sets of parametric models composed of varying urban morphological parameters and realistic/practical green-blue infrastructure coverage options will be numerically tested for their heat mitigation performance in the prevailing hot-humid weather conditions. The obtained understanding will be used for objective 3; (3) Develop a new performance-based green-blue infrastructure index using multi-variate regression modelling which will be proposed as a new tool for climate-sensitive urban planning and design; and (4) Using the index, sensitivity test will be conducted on realistic sites and scientifically proven green-blue implementation strategies that could be used to modify the greening aspects of the Sustainable Building Design (APP-152) and Hong Kong Planning Standards and Guidelines (HKPSG) chapter 4 will be drawn. In conclusion, this study will respond to the need for a new “green index” for liveable high-density city proposed in the Hong Kong Government’s “Hong Kong 2030+” by providing the first green-blue infrastructure index that is transferable to other high-density cities in the region e.g. Singapore. 城市過熱是包括香港在內的亞熱帶城市所面臨的首要環境挑戰，而且影響健康，包括熱壓力和不適而引致疾病和死亡。其中一個行之有效的解決方案是將綠化和水體融合在城市設計中。根據本研究團隊以往的研究，建議20-30%的總樓面面積用作綠化以緩減熱島效應。此綠化覆蓋率是建基於1度的溫度調節及地面植樹的數值試驗所得。然而，在實際執行上，政府的作業備考包括外牆和天台綠化，以及水體的可變折減系數由0%至50%不等，以便靈活實施。不過，這些變體組合並無實際證明可以確定有同等的熱調節性能。為彌補認知不足，本研究將對於在高密度環境下的藍綠基建覆蓋率的不同組合相對於總表面績的比例所造成的影響，進行極高分辨率的微氣候分析，為緩減城市過熱而制定一個嶄新的藍綠基建性能指數。 研究目標為： (1) 利用耦合人體生物氣候監測系統，於12個藍綠基建與建設環境接合的實際地點進行生物氣候變數的實地測量，從而理解其降溫效益和改善人體舒適的作用，並為校準和驗證目標二所用的模型提供基礎； (2)對於由各種城市地表參數和實際/可行的藍綠基建覆蓋選項所組成的768組參數模型，就其在濕熱天氣狀況下的減熱性能進行數值測試，所得結果將用於目標三； (3)利用多元迴歸模型，制定一個嶄新的藍綠基建性能指數，並提出採用該指數作為應對氣候敏感的城市規劃和設計的新工具；以及 (4)利用該指數，將對實際地點進行敏感測試，並得出經過科學驗證的藍綠實施策略。有關策略可用以修訂《認可人士、註冊結構工程師及註冊岩土工程師作業備考》(APP-152)「可持續建築設計指引」的綠化方面與《香港規劃標準與準則》第四章。總括而言，本研究將提供首個藍綠基建指數，以回應香港政府的《香港2030+》中提出宜居的高密度城市對於一個新的「綠化指數」的需求，並可轉移應用於同一地區的其他高密度城市，如新加坡。

14617220.label: Realisation of objectives
14617220.value: All the study objectives have been realized during the project period. Based on the four study objectives, the PI and Co-I completed a four-step research plan which consists of four major research tasks (1-4) corresponding to the four objectives. Details on the objectives’ realization are documented in nine journal articles (six published, one under-review, two under preparation, see Part C). The present GRF funding is acknowledged in all the publications. The corresponding research task of Objective 1 is Task 1. It consists of four parts, which are (1A) Develop a coupled Human Bio-meteorological monitoring Systems (HuBioSys), (1B) Site selection and field measurement, (1C) Calculation of mean radiant temperature (MRT) using the integral method, and (1D) Real case modelling, model calibration and validation. In Task 1A, we have developed the HuBioSys system, which is suitable for outdoor thermal comfort measurements in Hong Kong. This system can simultaneously measure air temperature, humidity, wind speed, globe temperature, solar and terrestrial radiation at the pedestrian level, as well as ground surface temperature. The system is portable and easy to install. Technical details documented in the publication entitled " Microclimatic measurements in tropical cities: Systematic review and proposed guidelines " has been attached to this completion report as a part of outcomes. In Tasks 1B and 1C, we have measured the thermal effects of blue-green elements in typical urban environments in Hong Kong. The blue-green elements measured include trees, water bodies, green roofs, and vertical greening. At the same time, we have used the measured microclimate data and applied the integral method to estimate MRT. The optimization of the MRT calculation method has been documented in a publication entitled “Comparing different recalibrated methods for estimating mean radiant temperature in outdoor environment” which has been attached to this completion report as a part of outcomes. In Task 1D, we have conducted ENVI-met modeling for the actual measured sites and validated the applicability of ENVI-met in hot and humid subtropical regions such as Hong Kong. Technical details documented in the publication entitled “Evaluating the thermal-radiative performance of ENVI-met model for green infrastructure typologies: Experience from a subtropical climate” has been attached to this completion report as a part of outcomes. The modelling, validation, and scenario simulation technologies has been summarized in a review article entitled “Heat mitigation benefits of urban green and blue infrastructures: A systematic review of modeling techniques, validation and scenario simulation in ENVI-met V4”, which has been attached to this report. The corresponding research task of Objective 2 is Task 2. A parametric study of urban green and blue infrastructures needs to be setup and simulated. In this task, we found that accurately modeling urban blue-green elements is an essential prerequisite for improving simulation accuracy. Therefore, a series of sensitivity tests have been conducted under hot and humid meteorological conditions to identify microclimate-sensitive parameters and their relative cooling effects at the pedestrian level. Second, for the microclimate-sensitive parameters in modeling, we used commonly planted species in subtropical South China cities to demonstrate a systematic workflow for developing an ENVI-met vegetation model library. This library could include basic plant physical traits, plant images, reference values for the microclimate-sensitive parameters, and recommended alternative data sources for modeling. The vegetation model library could provide a useful, actionable resource from which researchers can quickly obtain accurate input values without needing highly specialized knowledge or instruments. Technical details documented in the publication entitled "Modeling microclimatic effects of trees and green roofs/façades in ENVI-met: Sensitivity tests and proposed model library " which has been attached to this completion report as a part of outcomes. The corresponding research task of Objective 3 is Task 3, development of new green-blue index for urban cooling. In this task, we summarized a generic model with a typical layout and building typology of Hong Kong’s residential areas and conducted a series of parametric studies. Hundreds of scenarios with different green-blue elements were simulated, considering characteristics of ground trees, ground cover, podium trees, podium ground cover, vertical greening, and water bodies. Considering more characteristics of green-blue elements such as plant physical traits, the proposed green factor metric is: ∆PET = -2.447 + Ground tree canopy coverage ratio×8.661 + Ground tree height×0.210 + Ground Tree LAI ×0.329 + Ground cover coverage ratio×1.539 + Water body coverage ratio×6.180. The proposed green factor metric is a designer-friendly tool; it develops an improved practical city and building greening guidelines derived from performance-based study to guide the decision designers and planners. A manuscript is planned to be submitted to the journal Landscape and Urban Planning, which is one of the top journals in this research field. The corresponding research task of Objective 4 is Task 4, drawing up of design strategies. In this task, we have summarized urban greening design strategies currently used in Hong Kong and other major cities worldwide. Based on this, we have developed design guidelines for urban greening at three scales: the city level, the neighbourhood level, and on the building envelope. Details are documented in a publication entitled "Creating a Thermally Comfortable City through Urban Green Infrastructure" ,which is currently under review by Urban Forestry and Urban Greening, one of the top journals in the field of urban greening research.

14617220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617220.value: In this project, the human bio-meteorological monitoring system developed in Task 1 can be applied to other urban (micro)climate-related studies. The microclimate data collected in this task can also be used for advanced data analysis. The urban microclimate field measurement guideline developed in Task 1 is useful for both research and teaching, guiding researchers and students to systematically design and conduct urban microclimate research and studies. The ENVI-met vegetation model library developed in Task 2 can be further enhanced using LiDAR technology. The urban green & blue index developed in Task 3 can be further developed by integrating machine learning techniques and data science. The workflow established in Task 4 is applicable not only to Hong Kong but also to other cities worldwide. The entire research framework, methodology, and some of the research findings have international applicability. This project’s research outcomes have attracted international attention, leading to research collaboration interests with various teams (including but not limited to urban climatology, urban planning, and landscape architecture) to pursue further studies—particularly to address the limitations and future work discussed in our publications. With such collaborative research and international impact, this study will further develop into interdisciplinary and cross-regional research.

14617220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617220.value: Landscape practitioners need clear, reasonably accurate information and quick methods to support evidence-based decision-making in the design phase. However, due to knowledge and practical barriers between scientific research and real-world practice, designers often struggle to access "evidence" that directly supports design decisions. There is also a lack of practical methods and transferable workflows between scientists and landscape design practitioners, stemming from mismatches in information, knowledge, and needs between the two groups. Traditional methods cannot effectively bridge this gap. To address this, we took the heat effects of urban blue-green infrastructure as a starting point and developed a green-blue index to directly guide thermal environment optimization for residential areas in Hong Kong. From a scientific perspective, this study maintained its rigor by using a microclimate simulation tool validated in Hong Kong, along with a vegetation model library. Every step of the research—from instrument calibration for data collection to quantitative modeling—underwent strict quality control to ensure the accuracy and robustness of the findings. From a practical perspective, this project developed a viable workflow that translates complex scientific findings into fit-for-purpose, actionable information that can directly guide landscape design practice.

14617420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14617420.value: 日本「過勞文化」和職場健康的人類學分析

14617420.label: Project Objectives
14617420.value: To identify the key legal and policy reforms regarding employment contracts and work-hour regulations since the implementation of Abenomics in the 2010s-2020s. To analyze how the diversification of workstyles due to the new reforms regarding overtime and the discretionary work system have affected workplace tensions and working conditions as well as individual employees’ work experiences and work consciousness. To locate the frictions between cultural values of work ethics and changing corporate practices by examining how the experience of “working overtime” has become recast as the pathology of “overwork” in post-bubble Japan from the perspective of employees and managers. To compare and contrast the social, cultural, and personal factors that lead to workplace stress and physical and mental suffering by analyzing the Japanese case alongside literature on workplace well-being around the world. To offer empirical data to inform policymakers in the development of strategies for working with existing cultural logics and work practices to prevent overwork and improve workplace morale and employee care, and to contribute to policy debates on legal, economic, medical, and social ramifications of growing workplace instability and alienation in Japan and other postindustrial societies. To use the case study of Japan to shed light on the tensions between health, work-life balance, and productivity in postindustrial societies for international academic journal publications. To critically interrogate anthropological theories regarding how the political economy of globalization intersects with local logics of work culture, life, and well-being.
