14617420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617420.value: 本研究檢視日本企業架構和工作方式的改變，並以僱員長時間工作所承受的生理及心理影響為切入點，分析「過勞文化」。眾所周知，日本僱員對工作抱有強烈責任感，難以取得工作與生活之間的平衡。源自二次大戰後的社會僱用契約下，僱員雖然要長時間工作，卻相應地得到穩定職位和足以養家活兒的薪金。如今超時工作的狀況已是屢見不鮮，但隨着職場風險及職權騷擾等社會經濟問題日益嚴重，包括剝削員工的「黑心企業」、「在職失業」以及愈來愈多的「過勞死」個案，社會不得不開始重視僱員的工作時數和身心健康。儘管日本首相安倍晉三曾推動「勞動改革」改善職場環境，卻無助矯正日本的過勞文化。故此，本研究趁着時宜，不但會探討戰後奉如至寶的長時間工作文化，何以淪落至泡沫經濟後的「過勞病態」，亦會探討僱員如何過勞文化下掙扎求存。 透過於三間公司進行民族誌研究，結合訪問和比較分析，本研究會分析「超時工作和過勞之間的界線」，找出工作環境轉變和僱員身心健康之間的關係。最後，本研究會揭示過勞在經濟、社會及心理層面對僱員造成的影響，再為僱員提供紓緩過勞及改善職場福利的策略。是次以日本僱員內心掙扎為重心的微觀研究，可作為其他地域社會面對職場不穩及異化加深等社會問題時的重要參考對象，藉此推動勞動改革的政策辯論，同時為納入工作、身心健康和全球資本主義的理論開拓新途徑。

14617420.label: Realisation of objectives
14617420.value: In fulfillment of Objectives 1, 3, 4, and 7, I conducted archival research and reviewed recent policy papers and ministry documents about current practices and debates. I analyzed the websites of the Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare and the Ministry of Justice as well as the business federation (Keidanren) with a focus on the government and corporate-level workstyle reforms, labor laws, and workplace health regulations. In fulfillment of Objectives 2 and 3, I also conducted online-based research, and I attended various lectures and workshops which were newly instituted by organizations in Japan. In addition to Japan’s work-style reforms, what contributed to the proliferation of online activities was also the pandemic which pushed telework and digitization. The unprecedented shift online for Japan’s workforce both positively and negatively affected working hours, overwork, and stress from work. These changes provoked the convening of various lectures and workshops on implementing telework, and thus I attended many of these newly emerging meetings and study groups. In fulfillment of Objective 5, aside from academic talks I attended, I participated in 35 workshops and events and contributed my own empirical results to attendees of these workshops, who included leaders from business, NPOs, and government. In fulfillment of Objectives 3 and 5, I conducted field research in Japan in June, July, September, and October 2022, in December 2023, and March 2024. Specifically, while there were still pandemic-related restrictions remaining in place at many companies, I conducted fieldwork with the HRO staff in 5 large and 8 medium-sized companies, and attended 8 NPO-sponsored workplace wellbeing-related workshops and symposia. At these events I conducted informal interviews with participants, which allowed me to gain insight into workers’ and employers’ perspectives on workplace wellbeing, work/life balance, and the subjective meanings of “overwork”. Also in fulfillment of Objectives 3 and 5, building off of the connections I made during fieldwork, I completed interviews with 22 informants who are in their 20s, 30s, and 40s, and conducted additional in-depth interviews with 10 informants, with the goal of identifying the challenges with workstyle reforms and examining the strategies being implemented to cope with problems. In fulfillment of Objective 6, I presented my research at the Association for Asian Studies Annual Meeting in Boston, USA in March 2023. Moreover, based on my research data, I am preparing an edited volume on Work and Leisure in Japan (MHM Limited, 2026). In addition, I have completed a draft of the co-authored book on Changing Japanese Employment, which has been accepted for publication with Oxford University Press in 2025/2026. Altogether, based on my research, conference presentation, and publications, I have accomplished all my objectives. Please note that there is more than 30% of the budget remaining. This is due to the changed research plan as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and my own illness. My original plan for long-term fieldwork followed by several research trips was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic and later by my own illness. This resulted in fewer trips and much lower travel costs. In addition, I originally had planned for more international conference trips, but most of the conferences were canceled due to the pandemic. Lastly, I originally budgeted for a Research Assistant, but in the end, I did not employ one, which resulted in reallocating funds to the general research expenses, which again I was not able to use as a result of the pandemic and my illness.

14617420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617420.value: My research examines issues of “workplace well-being” and “overwork” under the increasing neoliberalization of the Japanese economy. It is inspired by recent developments in economic anthropology that examine the effects of global capitalism on workers’ well-being, as well as Japan’s new attempt at “work-style reform”. It focuses on how the political economy of globalization intersects with local logics of work, lifestyles, and well-being, and offers a case study of the Japanese context as a comparative framework for studying similar issues in other societies. This project's innovative methodology combines ethnographic research and interviews at companies and a labor rights NPO, alongside comparative analysis of other major post-industrial economies (the US, Germany, South Korea, and Hong Kong). Further, it is among the first qualitative studies examining changes from pre-Covid to post-Covid times. This research is timely and significant in the context of the increasing precariousness of employment through the global expansion of irregular labor, which coincides with increasing exploitation of full-time workers and a growing awareness of “workplace burnout,” which the WHO officially classified as an occupational syndrome in 2019. However, the cultural dynamics and social meanings of work and overwork remain under-studied; while workplace burnout has become a universal problem, the particular mechanisms and cultural forms of overwork must be examined to understand the mechanisms and thresholds of “workplace burnout”. My findings suggest that issues of overwork and workplace well-being are not just about labor laws—they involve sociocultural issues. For example, discourse about various forms of “harassment” has given employees a new language to voice dissatisfaction, which also creates a new atmosphere of restraint and tension. Moreover, workers’ sense of well-being and attitudes toward their workplace are qualitatively driven--democratic and open working relationships and mutual respect and recognition from bosses/colleagues play an important role. Thus, improving workplace well-being requires legal, structural, and sociocultural reforms for enhancing workers’ sense of recognition, respect, and agency. Based on this research, I completed my book, Reworking Japan (Cornell, 2021). I presented my research at the Association for Asian Studies Annual Meeting (Boston, 2023). I published a chapter based on fieldwork for the Handbook on Teaching Japan (MHM Limited, 2024). In addition, I completed a draft of the co-authored book on Changing Japanese Employment, which is accepted for publication with Oxford University Press in 2025/2026.

14617420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617420.value: This research has laid the groundwork for understanding the ongoing and future changes in workways in Japan. Future research should continue to analyze the rollout of workstyle reforms in both large and small-medium corporation and the actual ways that these reforms are being implemented in workplaces. Further, future research should examine how incoming generations of workers (e.g., post-covid new employees) conceptualize the meaning of the workplace and workplace well-being. In addition, future research should pay attention to the forms and effects of “unconscious bias” among employees across generations, as well as among Japanese and non-Japanese employees in Japan. Lastly, future research should also look into the similarities and differences of post-covid workstyle reforms among companies in Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong, Taiwan, mainland China, the US, Germany, and the UK, to further scrutinize the global and local (legal, social, and cultural) dimensions that shape workplace well-being. In my future research, I plan to conduct additional global comparative archival and survey-based research into these topics by collaborating with other scholars who are experts in these societies.

14617420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617420.value: This research has laid the groundwork for understanding the ongoing and future changes in workways in Japan. Future research should continue to analyze the rollout of workstyle reforms in both large and small-medium corporation and the actual ways that these reforms are being implemented in workplaces. Further, future research should examine how incoming generations of workers (e.g., post-covid new employees) conceptualize the meaning of the workplace and workplace well-being. In addition, future research should pay attention to the forms and effects of “unconscious bias” among employees across generations, as well as among Japanese and non-Japanese employees in Japan. Lastly, future research should also look into the similarities and differences of post-covid workstyle reforms among companies in Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong, Taiwan, mainland China, the US, Germany, and the UK, to further scrutinize the global and local (legal, social, and cultural) dimensions that shape workplace well-being. In my future research, I plan to conduct additional global comparative archival and survey-based research into these topics by collaborating with other scholars who are experts in these societies.

14618820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618820.value: Since Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, the Chinese government has dramatically tightened its grip on the Chinese society, particularly targeting civil society groups. On the other hand, the Chinese government at various levels has invested an enormous amount of resources, and substantially simplified the registration procedures for social organizations to encourage their growth. Scholars have not yet provided an effective theoretical framework or conducted systematic empirical analysis to account for the seemingly contradictory tendencies of Xi’s policy on social organizations. This project aims to fill this gap. It posits that, rather than the conventional concepts of state corporatism or civil society, social engineering is a concept that can more accurately capture Xi’s style for managing social organizations. Under Xi, the Chinese state has tried to proactively create a cultivated ecosystem of associations by wiping out weeds, namely, unwelcome organizations, and nurturing flowers, their favored organizations. This project will investigate the origins and effects of such an approach. In particular, it will describe and explain the change and continuity of state strategies by investigating the multi-dimensional bargaining processes within the party-state (especially the negotiations between the central and local governments) and between the state and societal actors. Moreover, it will also identify and explain the impact of state strategies on the development of social organizations and civic activism. The impact will be assessed in four dimensions: organizational, behavioral, attitudal, and biographical. Finally, it will identify and explain the impact of state strategies on the dynamics and outcomes of transnational activism, especially activism of NGOs based in Hong Kong, which have thus far played a very important role in civic activism in the mainland. This project expects to provide a theoretical framework to conceptualize the dynamic relationship between the state and social organizations in a context of post-totalitarianism. 自從習近平主政以來，中國政府大大增强了對市民社會團體的管控。另一方面中國的很多地方政府卻放寬了社會組織注冊登記的手續，並投入大量資源促進它們的發展。對於爲什麽中國政府同時采取這兩種看似相互矛盾的政策學界至今沒有給出系統的學理解釋。本研究項目力圖彌補這一缺失。當前的理論將政府與社會組織的關係要麽描述為法團主義要麽描述為市民社會模式。本項目則將這一關係歸爲社會工程學模式。在這一模式裏，國家積極主動地清除它不歡迎的團體而積極培育它所喜愛的團體，如同園丁對於雜草和鮮花一樣。本研究追溯這一模式的起源也探究其實際效果。具體而言，本項目將會調查幾個維度的博弈關係如何構建了這個模式，包括中央和地方政府之間以及政府與組織之間的博弈。而這個模式的社會效果也會通過對各類組織，個人的行爲，態度，以及發展軌跡加以檢測。其中包括此政策模式對於社會組織與跨境團體（含香港）的關係的影響。本項目將會對后極權社會中國家與社會互動提出新的解釋框架。

14618820.label: Realisation of objectives
14618820.value: All the objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Through extensive field research across multiple locations, I have gathered rich qualitative and quantitative data on state strategies for managing social organizations and social networks. The project highlights three key aspects of state-social organization interactions in China. First, it provides a comprehensive account of the development of various social organizations in different local contexts in China. It reveals and explains significant variation in the number and strength of social organizations across localities. Second, the project examines the strategies of mobilization by various social groups and networks on a wide range of issues, including land acquisition, environmental pollution, women’s rights, and LGBTQ issues. Third, it explores the fundamental patterns of state responses to different types of social organizations. Specifically, it sheds light on how the Chinese government employs systematically distinct strategies to address non-civic and civic activism. Two primary strategies—repression and accommodation—are analyzed in depth. The study demonstrates how the Chinese state leverages grassroots institutions to deploy coercive force against social groups deemed a threat to the regime, such as religious cults. Conversely, it discusses how the political system exhibits notable responsiveness to various social groups, particularly to their grievances, as the state values negative feedback as a crucial source of information. The findings were presented at two international conferences, garnering significant attention from scholars in the fields of Chinese politics and contentious politics. Additionally, two articles based on the project have been accepted for publication in leading journals in the field.

14618820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14618820.value: The research project has produced three significant findings regarding the state’s management of social organizations as an important foundation of political order in China during the reform era. First, by analyzing the bargaining processes between the state and social organizations, the project highlights that the state has developed flexible strategies to contain social organizations, effectively neutralizing potentially threatening groups while leveraging the resources generated by these social groups. Second, the project uncovers the often-overlooked role of non-state and semi-state institutions in implementing coercive measures against social organizations and networks. These strategies offer relatively low-risk and highly efficient solutions for addressing the need for coercive actions. Third, by comparing different types of social networks and organizations, the project reveals the state's strengths and weaknesses in maintaining loyalty among alienated social groups. It sheds light on the challenges the state faces in engaging with youth groups, artists, journalists, and other urban groups. The relatively free spaces , including various subcultures, have opened opportunities for certain forms of civic activism, such as the White Paper Movement in late 2022.

14618820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14618820.value: This project has explored, but not sufficiently, the activism of youth groups in China. While I have collected extensive data, including more than 150 in-depth interviews, on this topic, further work is needed to analyze the data and develop appropriate theoretical frameworks to explain the findings. Youth groups are highly sensitive and can play a pivotal role in spearheading social movements, but the exact conditions and mechanisms underlying their activism still require detailed investigation. I am currently applying for a new grant to further study youth activism in China.

14618820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14618820.value: This project examines the sophisticated strategies employed by the state to manage social organizations and networks in the context of a market economy and the rapid advancement of communication technologies. It highlights how the state leverages non-state grassroots institutions to suppress threatening groups while maintaining a notable level of responsiveness to the grievances of ordinary groups. The project provides a nuanced and comprehensive account of state policies toward social organizations, along with a thorough evaluation of their effectiveness. In doing so, it offers valuable insights into how regime stability has been maintained during the reform era.

14619220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14619220.value: 1949-1976年華中農村地區的民間信仰變遷

14619220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619220.value: One of the most productive ways to understand rural historical change under Maoism continues to be to bring forward the perspective of those who experienced it. Most landmark studies to this end, however, have neglected rural people’s most essential idiom of expression: their local religious culture. The Chinese religion scholars who have elaborated the significance of the religious core to local rural society and PRC history scholars have, to date, taken little interest in the implications of their findings for each other. This disconnect needs to be addressed if we are to have a better understanding of both rural life under Maoism and the evolution of local Chinese religion. This study addresses the challenge with case-study examinations of developments in village religious culture in relation to local people’s existential concerns about sustenance, health and security from the 1950s through the early 1970s. The focus is on particular regions in the central provinces of Henan, Anhui and Jiangsu where rural people’s struggles for basic survival and security had long been acute and remained so well after 1949. This study moves away from the “suppression and elimination” or the “survival and revival” narratives to consider the Maoist era a critical moment in the transformative re-formation of religious culture in rural areas under duress. It concentrates on (1) cases in which state suppression of religion confronted communities experiencing insecurity of the kind that had long fuelled religious practice; and (2) cases of intensive party-state extraction of resources from and imposition of ideological claims, state ritual and rhetoric on communities suffering conditions of material deprivation. The study asks: how did changes in local religious culture represent a vital form of rural social expression under Maoism? What were the consequences of this transformation of rural religion? Preliminary research suggests that particular forms of local religious culture deserve close attention: 1) everyday religious cultures in the home; 2) village sacred places/earth-god shrines; 3) fengshui masters, burial and home construction; 4) Wuism (mainly women shamans) and healing; 5) redemptive societies; 6) healing cults. The seeming correlation between changes to religious culture and the subsequent spread of indigenous evangelical Christianity also deserves attention. This study will contribute to the historical study of Chinese rural society and local religion in the early decades of the PRC by combining historical and religious studies approaches and methods. 理解中國毛時代農村變遷的最有效方法之一就是繼續挖掘那些經歷毛時代的個體感受。然而，大部 分重要研究忽略了農村人民最日常的表達:民間信仰文化。雖然研究中國宗教的學者多強調信仰對 於鄉土社會的重要性，研究共和國史的學者至今對上述研究興趣寥寥。如果我們想要更好的同時了 解毛時代的農村社會和鄉土信仰的變遷，我們必須彌合這一認知上的斷層。本課題試圖用把二十世 紀五十年代到七十年代鄉村宗教文化與當地農民對溫飽健康安全的生存需求聯繫起來進行案例研 究。課題關注華中包括河南、安徽和江蘇在內的生存狀況嚴峻的農村地區。本課題擯棄「壓迫、滅 跡」或「幸存、重生」的傳統敘述，視毛時代為中國農村貧困地區信仰文化重塑的關鍵轉折期。本課題 將著眼於以下兩種案例:1)長期因生存壓力而擁有悠久信仰傳統的地區受到來自政府的壓制;2) 政府大量抽取當地資源被並大力宣揚意識形態和國家儀式的貧困地區。本課題旨在從鄉土信仰文化 的變遷中刻畫毛時代農村的社會表達，並理解其變遷的歷史意義。 本課題的初步研究顯示以下鄉土信仰文化的形式尤其值得關注:1)家庭內部的日常信仰文化;2) 村落的祭壇、土地廟;3)風水大師，葬禮及造房儀式;4)巫術(多為女性);5)救世社團;6) 治病秘笈儀式。信仰文化的變化與之後基督教本土傳播之間的關聯也值得研究。本課題整合了歷史 研究和宗教研究的脈絡和方法，將對共和國早期鄉土社會及本土信仰的歷史研究作出貢獻。

14619720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619720.value: Mental health problems such as anxiety and depression are the leading disease burden, affecting up to 20% of adolescents globally. Mental health problems are associated with risk behaviours such as school dropouts, aggression, suicidal ideation and suicide. Evidence indicates that adolescents with special educational needs (SEN) such as attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorders (ASD) have poorer mental health and higher risk behaviours than those with typical development. More than half of all mental health problems emerge during adolescence and continue into adulthood, so early effective interventions are therefore important. Little is known about the associations of physical activity with reduced mental health problems and risk behaviours in adolescents with SEN. Recently, our research team has conducted a pilot school-based physical activity intervention in this group and found immediate positive effects on increased physical activity and reduced anxiety, depression and suicidal ideation. We also found that physical activity was strongly associated with resilience, an ability to overcome obstacles and achieve positive outcomes in the face of diversity and life stresses. Future research is needed to determine whether improved mental health can translate into decreases in risk behaviours in the longer term. Grounded in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health for Children and Youth (ICF-CY) framework, this study is the first cluster randomized controlled trial (RCT) to examine the effects of a school-based physical activity intervention on the mental health and risk behaviours of adolescents with SEN. It is also the first study to use salivary cortisol as a biomarker of stress in Hong Kong adolescents with SEN. Based on a power calculation, 240 adolescents with SEN in twelve Hong Kong secondary mainstream schools will be cluster randomized allocated into either a 12-week physical activity intervention or a control condition. Measurements of mental health and risk behaviours will be conducted at (i) baseline, (ii) post-intervention (immediately after 12-week intervention), (iii) 3-month after post-intervention, and (iv) 12-month after post-intervention. This cluster RCT brings experts in physical activity interventions together, and the findings will assist educators and education and healthcare policy makers to develop early treatment strategies and to introduce school-based health promotion practices for adolescents with SEN. In the longer term, our aim is to develop a territory-wide school-based physical activity policy (lunchbreak “exercise-snack” program) in mainstream schools in Hong Kong. 心理健康問題如焦慮及抑鬱是主要的疾病負荷，影響全球多達20％的青少年。心理健康問題與危險行為相關，例如輟學、攻擊性行為、企圖自殺及自殺。證據顯示有特殊教育需要青少年（如注意力不足/過度活躍症、自閉症）的心理健康較一般青少年為差，而危險行為則較高。多於一半以上的心理健康問題於青春期出現，並持續到成年期，因此早期有效的干預是非常重要。對於有特殊教育需要的青少年，體力活動與減少心理健康問題及危險行為的關聯知之甚少。最近，我們的研究小組開展一項針對有特殊教育需要青少年的校本體力活動試驗，結果發現體力活動干預對增加體力活動，減少焦慮、抑鬱和企圖自殺有正面的影響。我們也發現體力活動與心理彈性密切相關，心理彈性是一種在面對多樣的生活壓力時，具有克服障礙及取得積極結果的能力。我們需要進行進一步的研究以確定改善心理健康是否可以長遠地降低危險行為。這項研究以國際健康功能與身心障礙分類系統-兒童和青少年版（ICF-CY）為理論框架，首次採用集群隨機對照的方法檢驗校內體力活動干預對有特殊教育需要青少年的心理健康和危險行為的影響。這也是香港首個採用唾液皮質醇來檢測有特殊教育需要青少年的壓力研究。根據統計功效計算，香港十二所主流中學的240名有特殊教育需要的青少年將以群組形式被隨機分為12週的體力活動干預組和控制組。心理健康和危險行為的評估將分別於（i）基線、（ii）干預後12週、（iii）干預後3個月、以及（iv）干預後12個月進行。這項集群隨機對照研究將會集多位體力活動干預專家之合作，研究結果將幫助教育工作者和教育、醫療保健政策制定者訂立早期干預政策，並為有特殊教育需要的青少年引入校本健康促進活動。長遠來看，我們的目標是在香港主流學校制定以全港學校為基礎的體力活動政策（午休「運動零食」計劃）。

14619720.label: Realisation of objectives
14619720.value: Grounded in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) framework, the study was the first cluster randomized controlled trial (cRCT) to examine the effects of a school-based physical activity intervention on the mental health and risk behaviours of Hong Kong adolescents with SEN. It was also the first study to use salivary cortisol as a biomarker of stress in adolescents with SEN. As proposed in the protocol, a total of 200 participants would be included, with consideration for potential attrition. Due to the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic, the research team faced unpredictable and significant challenges. Eventually, we recruited 170 participants from nine secondary mainstream schools in Hong Kong, encompassing the New Territories, Kowloon, and Hong Kong Island. Of the 170 participants, 48 were diagnosed with ADHD, 28 with ASD, and 94 with comorbid conditions such as ASD-ADHD. Among the nine participating schools, four were cluster-allocated to the intervention condition, while the other five were allocated to the control condition. A 12-week PA intervention was delivered in the intervention schools during school hours, and participants were required to perform activities at a moderate intensity level (50-60% of the maximum heart rate), which was objectively measured using a Polar heart rate monitor. To achieve Objective 1, a series of assessments at baseline (prior to intervention), immediately after intervention (immediate effect), 3-month post-intervention (short-term effect), and 12-month post-intervention (longer-term effect) were performed. Primary outcome variables consisted of mental health in terms of psychological ill-being (stress, anxiety, and depression) and psychological well-being (self-concept and resilience), which were assessed by self-reported questionnaires. In addition to self-reported measures, salivary cortisol was collected as an objective biomarker to assess the stress level of participants. Secondary outcome variables were risk behaviour involving aggression and suicidal ideation. To achieve Objective 2, information on gender and SEN types was collected through the participants’ schools and/or parents. Confounding variables were also collected. They were demographic variables (age and family socio-economic status), sex- and age-adjusted body mass index (BMI), cognitive ability using the Raven’s Colored Progressive Matrices Test, and health-related behaviours including accelerometer-measured physical activity, cardiorespiratory fitness measured with the Pacer test and the Brockport Physical Fitness Test Kit, and self-reported eating and sleep behaviours.

14619720.label: Summary of objectives addressed

14619720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14619720.value: This project was the first to employ a cRCT design to examine the immediate and sustained effects of a school-based physical activity intervention on mental health and risk behaviors among Hong Kong adolescents with SEN. Our results showed that all neurodevelopmental disorder groups, except for male adolescents with ADHD, exhibited at least one symptom of anxiety, depression, or stress (ranging from mild to severe). As predicted, we found that moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) significantly predicted lower self-reported anxiety and stress levels in adolescents with ADHD, with gender serving as a moderating factor. While we did not observe any significant differences in outcomes among the ASD, ADHD, and ASD-ADHD groups. Moreover, higher levels of MVPA in adolescents with ADHD were associated with improved psychological well-being (resilience and physical self-concept). In terms of behavioral risk factors, MVPA was linked to a statistically significant decrease in hostility levels in female adolescents with ADHD. Conversely, in male adolescents with comorbid ASD-ADHD, each additional minute of vigorous physical activity (VPA) was associated with a small but significant increase in physical aggression. After participating in a 12-week school-based physical activity intervention, adolescents with SEN showed significant reductions in self-reported stress, risk behaviors, and sleep disturbances. These improvements were maintained for three months following the intervention. Interestingly, we noted a temporary increase in cortisol levels immediately after the physical activity intervention among adolescents with ADHD, which suggests a potential regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis—often lower in individuals with ADHD. However, this increase did not persist at the three-month follow-up. Overall, our findings indicate that a school-based physical activity intervention, involving moderate to higher levels of physical activity, can be an effective strategy for improving mental health and reducing risk behaviors in adolescents with SEN, with some benefits remaining in the short term (up to three months).

14619720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14619720.value: ADHD and ASD are common neurodevelopmental disorders among school-aged adolescents worldwide, including in Hong Kong, where these conditions account for more than 40% of the SEN population in secondary schools. The development of feasible and cost-effective physical activity intervention strategies to alleviate primary mental health challenges and reduce secondary risk behaviors among adolescents with SEN is thus of considerable importance. Based on the key findings of this project, it is worth considering certain gaps and directions for future research in this field. First, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted school recruitment, data collection, and intervention implementation. Schools faced intermittent closures and stringent safety measures, which limited face-to-face interactions and delayed scheduled follow-up assessments. As a result, multiple project extensions were required to accommodate these unforeseen circumstances. Second, these pandemic-related challenges may have influenced the mental health of adolescents with SEN. Increased stress and anxiety during such a disruptive period could have affected the outcomes, and the results should be interpreted with caution. Future research should consider the pandemic context when examining mental health outcomes and be prepared for potential disruptions that can influence intervention delivery and data collection. Third, the pandemic experience highlights the need to integrate assistive technologies into PA intervention implementation. Virtual PA sessions, online platforms, and mobile applications could help maintain program accessibility and adherence, even when in-person activities are not feasible. Such technology-enhanced strategies offer a more flexible, scalable approach to delivering interventions under varying circumstances, ultimately contributing to more resilient and sustainable models for promoting mental health and reducing risk behaviors among adolescents with SEN.

14619720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14619720.value: Adolescence is a critical developmental period for establishing physical, mental and social well-being across the human life span. Mental health problems such as anxiety and depression affect up to 20% of adolescents globally. Mental health problems are associated with risk behaviours. Adolescents with SEN have poorer mental health and higher risk behaviours than those with typical development. Grounded in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, this project was the first to examine whether a 12-week school-based physical activity intervention was effective (both short- and long-term) in improving mental health and risk behaviours in adolescents with SEN using a cluster randomized controlled trial. The effectiveness of our intervention was determined using multi-dimensional outcomes, including psychological ill-being (stress, anxiety, and depression), psychological well-being (self-concept and resilience), and risk behaviour (aggression and suicidal ideation). Our findings showed that moderate physical activity reduced stress and improved resilience, which was sustained over a three-month follow-up. Our findings supported that our intervention appears to be effective in improving mental health and risk behaviours in adolescents with SEN. The findings gained are of significance in assisting educators and healthcare policymakers in introducing school-based health promotion practices for adolescents with SEN in Hong Kong.

14619920.label: Project Objectives

14619920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619920.value: This project will study the unique situation of the Hong Kong education system, which has different religious education courses being offered by a wide variety of religious bodies. The Hong Kong government acknowledges religious diversity, and it supports religious freedom and religious tolerance. Both religious and non-religious schools enjoy public funding while remaining relatively autonomous. Faith schools operate on a considerable scale with little governmental intervention with respect to religious education. These faith schools usually implement a compulsory sectarian religious education curriculum with a strong spiritual and moral dimension. However, there is considerable ambiguity surrounding the status, content and function of religious education. Arguably, religious education needs to be updated and reformed to keep abreast of social change and to address a number of social and pedagogical issues. It is important to consider how religious education curricula have changed over time and how curricular development takes into account the socio-cultural context and young people’s experiences. This 28-month project will explore the special role of religion education curricula in Hong Kong’s multi-religious society, a topic that is vital but that has remained unexplored. Relatively few scholars have attempted to address religious education other than Christianity and Islam. Taking into account the religious diversity within this unique education system and different religious bodies taking different approaches to religious education, a historical and intra-system comparative study can contribute to a broader and deeper understanding of the nature of religious education. By using a mixed research method with data collected through the documentation of teaching materials, and by conducting interviews with the authors and representatives of religious bodies, we will examine the curriculum development of four major religious bodies over time, with a special emphasis on the curricular components of aims/objectives, content, pedagogy and evaluation. We will also study the causes and factors behind changes in both religious education as a school subject and the production of learning and teaching materials. This project will have significant implications for understanding the relationship between religion and education – that is, the specific place and role of religious education accorded by different religious bodies in a highly secular and culturally diverse society. The findings of this study will allow us to understand the features of different religious education curricula. Insight into developing teaching and learning materials and practices that are conducive to fostering desirable values in adolescents will be shared with curriculum designers and practitioners. 此項目將研究香港教育體系的獨特情況：它由各種各樣的宗教團體提供不同的宗教教育課程。香港政府承認宗教多元化，並對宗教採自由和寬容政策。宗教學校和非宗教學校都獲公共資助，同時保持相對自主。宗教學校中的宗教教育規模龐大，幾乎沒受政府干預。這些宗教學校通常實行帶強制性的宗派的和富有強烈的靈性和道德色彩的宗教教育課程。但圍繞宗教教育的地位、內容和功能的理解仍有很大的分歧。宗教教育當然需要更新和改革以保持和社會與時俱進，並解決許多社會和教學問題。宗教教育課程如何隨著時間變化，以及課程發展如何考慮社會文化背景和年輕人的經驗乃是亟需考慮的要事。 這個為期28個月的研究項目將探討宗教教育課程在香港這多元宗教社會的獨特角色。這個課題雖然很重要，但至今仍未充分開發。相對而言，很少學者嘗試探討基督教和伊斯蘭教以外的宗教教育。考慮到香港這獨特教育體系當中的宗教多樣性和不同宗教團體採取不同的方法處理宗教教育，採取歷史和系統內部的比較研究可有助對宗教教育的性質有更廣泛和更深入的了解。使用混合研究法，包括收集教材文獻，以及與宗教團體的作者和代表訪談，我們將研究四個主要宗教團體隨著時間推移下的課程發展情況，特別強調課程的四大組成部分：目的/目標、內容、教學法與評估。我們還會研究宗教教育作為學校課程和學習與教學材料變化背後的成因和元素。 這項目將對理解宗教與教育間的關係具有重要意義，即在高度世俗化和多元文化的情況下不同宗教團體提供的宗教教育的特別角色和作用。研究結果將使我們能夠理解不同宗教教育課程的特徵；也可與課程設計者和從業者共享開發教材經驗，有助於在青少年中培育理想價值觀。

14619920.label: Realisation of objectives
14619920.value: The primary purpose of this project is to explore the unique role of religious education curricula in Hong Kong's multi-religious society, characterized by its rich religious diversity. We examine formal curriculum materials, including syllabi, teacher's manuals, textbooks, and workbooks related to religious education at the primary and junior secondary levels, employing both intra-system and historical comparisons. Together, the collected data provide a comprehensive overview of the trends in religious education in Hong Kong over the past fifty years. The project has gathered or generated the following data: a) A wide range of original primary materials since the 1960s, including major versions of textbooks and learning materials for religious education, such as: Catholic Diocese -《幸福的道路》(The Road of Well-being, 1973-74, 1981, 1996-98), and《踏上星光途》（Stepping on the Way under the Starlight, 2011-14）. The Anglican Church -《完美的人生》小學基督教教育課程 (Ideal Life - Christian Education for Primary Schools, 1981, 2006, 2019), 《同創新天地》中學宗教教育課程（Co-creation of a New Horizon–Series of Secondary Religious Education Textbook, 1993-1994）, and《聖經伴我行》 (A Journey with the Bible - Christian Religious Education for Secondary Schools, 2007-2008). Hong Kong Taoist Association - 《道教知識》(Knowledge of Taoism, 1986), and《校本課程發展: 道化教育》(Living Taoist Education (Junior Secondary) School-Based Curriculum, 2013). Hong Kong Buddhist Association - 《小學佛學課本》(Primary School Buddhism Textbooks, 1963), 《正覺大道》(The Grandway of Bodi, 2004), 《正覺的道路(緣起生命教育高小佛學輔助教材)》 (The Road to Enlightenment for Life Education based on the Concept of Dependent Origination (Senior Primary), 2010), 《初中佛學課本》(Secondary School Buddhism Textbooks, 1961), 《初中佛學課本》(Secondary School Buddhism Textbooks, 1989-1991), and 《正覺的道路:初中佛化德育及價值教育科教材》 (The Road to Enlightenment: Junior Secondary Buddhicised Moral and Values Education Curricular Materials, 2016-2019). The Confucian Academy of Hong Kong - 《香港小學儒家德育課程》(Confucian moral education curriculum for Hong Kong primary schools, 2004), and 《香港中學儒家德育與公民教育課程》(Confucian moral and civic education curriculum for Hong Kong secondary schools, 2006). b) Relevant reports from newspapers and websites, as well as available reports on major funding schemes. We performed a documentary analysis of the curricular materials, focusing on aims and objectives, content scope and topics, pedagogy, and evaluation methods. The materials were classified and coded using simple statistics across different dimensions of religious education. c) In-depth interviews with 32 informants involved in curriculum and textbook development provided insights into their experiences with curriculum planning and the production of educational materials. These interviews were transcribed for record-keeping and data analysis. The author has participated in three recognized international conferences where papers related to this research were presented. A book chapter outlining the status quo of religious education in Hong Kong was published in 2022, and a paper on Buddhism was published online in April 2024. Additional manuscripts are prepared for submission. These findings are crucial for expanding our understanding of the relationship between religion and education, particularly regarding issues of religious literacy and cultural diversity in non-Western societies. The study also sheds light on the religious education practices of Eastern religions, such as Buddhism and Taoism. List of manuscripts: Tse, T. K.C. (2024). 14619920.label: Major findings and research outcome
14619920.value: Religious education in Hong Kong’s public schools is notable for its prevalence, plurality, and vibrancy, fulfilling a vital role in moral and values education. The religious dimension fosters values that contribute to character development, morality, and citizenship. Faith schools leverage religious resources from their sponsoring bodies to uphold their specific traditions and core identities. However, changes in the social context — such as social issues, demographic shifts, and church-state relations — along with current education reforms and shortcomings in religious education practices, have led to shifts in the aims, content, and pedagogical approaches of religious education. Many religious education programs have undergone reforms to incorporate new elements into curriculum planning, learning content, and pedagogical strategies. In developing the religious education curriculum, we consider the biographies of participants in the compilation process, the organizational structure, available resources, objectives, autonomy, and the networks of religious bodies. The dynamics among these groups and between the state and civil society are also significant, as the state exercises direct influence through educational reforms. Since 2000, large-scale education reforms promoting student-centered learning have impacted religious education, emphasizing the development of specific values and generic skills, such as critical thinking and problem-solving. Faith schools must also align with the state’s goals for nation-building. The influence of religious studies movements, along with evolving theories of religious education, is noteworthy. Major religions, including Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism, have re-examined their traditions in the school curriculum, offering modern interpretations to address contemporary issues while highlighting their contributions to Chinese traditional cultures and wisdom. Common to these new initiatives in religious education programs is the blending of religious and non-religious elements in teaching and learning, integrating contemporary themes with traditional practices. Adjustments to pedagogical aims, content, and assessment methods are also significant. Teaching designs aim to inspire students through thought-provoking and diverse activities, such as games, case studies, group discussions, and experiential learning. Short stories and relevant scenarios are employed to encourage critical thinking and evaluation. Students are expected to engage in sharing experiences, reflecting on their learning, and applying it to their daily lives. Nevertheless, the ‘one school, one religion’ model remains the prevailing paradigm in Hong Kong’s faith schools.

14619920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14619920.value: Building on the findings mentioned above, future studies can examine the teaching and learning practices of religious education in various faith schools through general surveys and in-depth case studies. Practical suggestions include: 1. Encouraging liaison activities among religious bodies to exchange and promote best practices in religious education. 2. Recognizing the need to improve understanding of religions beyond one’s own, emphasizing the importance of inter-religious education. While the ‘one school, one religion’ model persists, it may not adequately address the realities of cultural and religious plurality. Notably, there are shifts toward multi-religious and interreligious models within the Catholic religious education curriculum, warranting specific investigation. 3. Further deliberation is needed regarding the appropriate roles of religious education, especially considering the evolving state-church relationship in recent years. The government’s role in guiding values education will significantly influence the directions and objectives of religious education.

14619920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14619920.value: This project highlights the vital role of religious education provided by different religious bodies in a highly secular and culturally diverse society like Hong Kong. Faith schools have long contributed significantly to values education. Over the years, the scope and topics of religious education have evolved, with curricula reflecting unique religious traditions while adapting to modern societal needs and pedagogical effectiveness. The project fosters mutual understanding among religious bodies regarding religious education and multiculturalism. The findings will help curriculum designers and practitioners understand the distinctive features of various religious education curricula, providing insights for developing materials and practices that promote proper values in adolescents. For additional details, please refer to articles in the Ming Pao column on September 17 and 24, 2024.

14620120.label: Project Objectives
14620120.value: To evaluate the influence of transcription skills, as compared to oral language and reading skills, on CSL writing development among Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students. A substantial body of research has supported the importance of transcription skills regarding the development of children’s writing in alphabetic languages (see the reviews by Kent & Wanzek, 2016, and Feng, Lindner, Ji & Joshi, 2019), while similar results were also found in studies on Chinese children’s writing (Yeung, Ho, Chan, and Chung, 2013, 2017, 2018). However, studies have yet to be conducted scrutinizing the role of transcription among CSL learners, for whom the Chinese writing system has represented a major learning hurdle. This issue is of particular concern for ethnic minority students in Hong Kong, whose families are mostly from South Asian countries, such as India, Nepal, and Pakistan. Constituting around 2.5% of the total student population of primary and secondary schools, these students’ Chinese language proficiencies, especially in reading and writing, are generally far lower than those of their Chinese-speaking counterparts (Wong, 2019). This has a detrimental effect on their academic advancement (Loh & Tam, 2016). The problems Hong Kong ethnic minority students have in learning to read and write in Chinese have also been widely observed among CSL learners worldwide. China’s growing global influence has been matched by a growth of interest in learning Chinese outside China. However, Chinese has long been considered a difficult foreign language because of its complex writing system (Everson, 2002). This proposed study aims to assess if transcription skills are a major constraint on the CSL students’ writing development. To evaluate the role of transcription in CSL learners’ writing development, giving consideration to the developmental, reciprocal relationships between writing and its component skills (Tolchinsky, 2018). Our understanding of CSL literacy development is far from adequate: Research to date has largely focused on Chinese character learning among adult learners (Shen, 2013), while comparatively few studies have investigated CSL learners’ reading and writing development beyond the beginning stage, particularly for young learners in a Chinese-speaking society. The PI and Co-Is have conducted studies with Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students in order to explore reading development among this under-represented demographic (e.g., Shum et al., 2014; Wong, 2017a; Zhou & McBride., 2015). The knowledge gained, measures, and analytic methods developed from these studies will be used in the proposed study. However, relatively little attention has been paid to CSL writing, especially regarding its developmental trajectory and relationships with critical component skills (Leong, Shum, Tai, Ki, & Zhang, 2018; Wong, 2018a). Using a longitudinal design, this study aims to fill this knowledge gap by exploring the roles of various component skills, focusing on transcription skills, played in the CSL writing composition development of Hong Kong’s primary ethnic minority students. The findings will advance our understanding of the developmental trajectory of CSL writing, using structural models (see graphic representations in Figures 1 and 2) to specify the relative influences of lower-level transcription skills compared to those of the higher-level linguistic processes, represented by oral language and reading. To identify the contribution of transcription to CSL writing and, consequently, to inform the design and implementation of the CSL literacy instruction provided both to CSL learners in general and Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students in particular. Writing is an important academic skill that students must acquire for expression, communication, and learning. Educators all over the world are concerned with students’ writing performance and are keen to explore methods through which to improve the writing instruction they provide. The need for a deeper understanding of the trajectory of literacy development in order to improve effective writing instruction is even more acute regarding second language learning. First, there are great variations in the acquisition and attainment levels of literacy skills among second language learners. This is especially for immigrant-learners learning a dominant second language, for whom literacy proficiency in that language has a major influence on their social integration (August & Shanahan, 2008). Learning to read and write fluently in the dominant language is critical for immigrant children. In terms of Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students, their Chinese teachers, who are mostly mainstream Chinese language teachers without formal CSL instruction training, find literacy teaching a challenge. There is also a broader need to provide better instructions to students in order to enhance their Chinese literacy skills. As shown by effectiveness of transcription skills training for enhancing writing in English (Alves et al., 2016), the findings of the study will help teachers to improve their CSL students’ writing by both attending to the component skills that matter and connecting transcription to writing in an informed manner.

The PI and Co-Is have conducted studies with Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students in order to explore reading development among this under-represented demographic (e.g., Shum et al., 2014; Wong, 2017a; Zhou & McBride., 2015). The knowledge gained, measures, and analytic methods developed from these studies will be used in the proposed study. However, relatively little attention has been paid to CSL writing, especially regarding its developmental trajectory and relationships with critical component skills (Leong, Shum, Tai, Ki, & Zhang, 2018; Wong, 2018a). Using a longitudinal design, this study aims to fill this knowledge gap by exploring the roles of various component skills, focusing on transcription skills, played in the CSL writing composition development of Hong Kong’s primary ethnic minority students. The findings will advance our understanding of the developmental trajectory of CSL writing, using structural models (see graphic representations in Figures 1 and 2) to specify the relative influences of lower-level transcription skills compared to those of the higher-level linguistic processes, represented by oral language and reading.

To identify the contribution of transcription to CSL writing and, consequently, to inform the design and implementation of the CSL literacy instruction provided both to CSL learners in general and Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students in particular. Writing is an important academic skill that students must acquire for expression, communication, and learning. Educators all over the world are concerned with students’ writing performance and are keen to explore methods through which to improve the writing instruction they provide. The need for a deeper understanding of the trajectory of literacy development in order to improve effective writing instruction is even more acute regarding second language learning. First, there are great variations in the acquisition and attainment levels of literacy skills among second language learners. This is especially for immigrant-learners learning a dominant second language, for whom literacy proficiency in that language has a major influence on their social integration (August & Shanahan, 2008). Learning to read and write fluently in the dominant language is critical for immigrant children. In terms of Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students, their Chinese teachers, who are mostly mainstream Chinese language teachers without formal CSL instruction training, find literacy teaching a challenge. There is also a broader need to provide better instructions to students in order to enhance their Chinese literacy skills. As shown by effectiveness of transcription skills training for enhancing writing in English (Alves et al., 2016), the findings of the study will help teachers to improve their CSL students’ writing by both attending to the component skills that matter and connecting transcription to writing in an informed manner.

14620120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620120.value: 本研究探查轉寫能力（包括抄寫流暢度和拼寫能力）對香港學習中文作為第二語言（中文二語）的少數族裔學生的寫作的影響。參考過往有關字母語言和中文學習者寫作構成要素能力的研究文獻，本研究採用縱向設計，評核學生的中文轉寫能力、口語、閱讀和寫作之間的關係。研究成果有助說明轉寫能力對中文二語學習者寫作能力發展的影響，並有利中文二語教學的設計及實施。 寫作對個人生活、升學及就業的影響巨大，相關研究甚多，惟大多以字母語言學習者為研究對象。這些研究確立了轉寫、口語及閱讀等作為關鍵要素能力對寫作發展的重要作用（Kent＆Wanzek， 2016）。但是，中文二語的研究一般集中在閱讀能力方面，我們對中文二語者寫作的了解相對較少。這種情況也見諸有關香港少數族裔學生中文學習的研究。這些學生的中文能力較弱，影響學習，因此引起社會的關注。我們對這些學生的中文寫作發展了解尤其不足，有礙為他們提供有效的中文學習支援。 本研究將使用回歸分析和結構方程模型，以評估香港約200名來自南亞裔高小學生的寫作及其要素能力（即轉寫、口語和閱讀）之間的發展關係。研究採縱向維期兩年的設計，共有三波的數據收集，以便建立模型及控制變量。研究工具及分析模型的發展都參考了有關中文母語及二語的寫作研究成果，其中包括研究團隊成員有關香港南亞裔學生中文二語發展的研究。 研究成果有助確定轉寫能力對中文二語寫作的影響，評定與口語及閱讀能力的相互影響，並由此提高我們對中文二語寫作發展的認識。研究成果亦有助發展有效的中文二語教育政策、課程及教學設計，特別是對香港少數族裔學生的中文教育。

14621220.value: • To identify the origins of important new terms in modern Chinese Buddhism, including fojiaotu (Buddhist), foxue (Buddhist learning), and zhixin (wise faith). • To trace the evolution of these and related terms during the late Qing and Republican periods. • To analyze these terms within their broader semantic fields. • To explain the emergence and the vicissitudes of such terms through reference to their historical contexts. • To demonstrate the impact of these new terms in shaping modern Chinese Buddhism and, to a lesser extent, in influencing modern Chinese concepts in general.

14621220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621220.value: 一個多世紀以來，通過在中文語彙注入的新詞，中國的知識領域發生了變化。無論是國外引進、本土發明還是兩者的結合，這些新概念改變了中國人的思維模式。該研究項目將研究這一過程在清末和民國時期（大約是1870年至1950年）的中國佛教中是如何發生的。 更具體地說，我的目的是闡明佛教中各種新術語是如緣起、演變以及有時成為佛教話語中的核心概念。通過這個研究項目，我希望發表三篇論文，每篇圍繞一個不同的佛教新詞語，即 「佛教徒」、「佛學」及「智信」。除了關注佛教概念的演變之外，我還將討論為什麼這類新詞的含義經常隨者社會的變化有所波動。因此，除了闡明中國佛教思想史之外，我還將探討現代宗教和中國思想觀念怎樣轉變的原則。

14621320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14621320.value: 中國耶路撒冷倒下的十字架：邁向中國當代政教關係的批判分析

14621320.label: Project Objectives
14621320.value: The Zhejiang Province cross-demolition campaign came forth under the heading of “three rectifications and one demolition” which is a policy set out to demolish different types of illegal constructions. The proposed research will use this policy as the background of analysis to reconstruct the ways in which the situation of religious premises (mainly involving Protestant, Catholic and popular religions) was affected by the “three rectifications and one demolition” campaign in order to evaluate the role of religious factors. Officially, the objective of the campaign claimed to be the demolition of illegal constructions. Is this a sufficient rationale? Behind the cross-demolition, are there any political or ideological considerations in regard to religion (Christianity in particular)? How is the campaign related to the adjustment of ideology and religious work under the central leadership since 2013? Are the actions taken by the Zhejiang Province interpreted as a “state” project? The proposed research tries to investigate whether there exist certain kinds of internal policy connection between the cross-demolition and the new policy line of political and religious works since 2013. On the one hand, this research will try to evaluate to what extent the provincial campaign can be understood as a “pilot scheme” for a new policy towards Christianity. On the other hand, the complex relationship within multiple levels and institutions of the state (for example, local, provincial, and central government; and multiple levels of state recognized patriotic religious organizations) will also be examined. Wenzhou as “China’s Jerusalem” is in a special position in the anti-demolition movement. The proposed research will conduct in-depth interviews with Christian leaders, Christian businessmen, pastoral workers and human rights lawyers to inform a critical evaluation of the impacts of the campaign on the Wenzhou model, in which Christian businessmen had played a central role in the past. The PI will also interview general non-believers to understand their perception and opinion about cross-demolition. The target of oral history is 65 to 75 interviews, hoping to collate and preserve first-hand information in relation to this cross-demolition campaign. What types of shock has the cross-demolition campaign brought to Wenzhou churches? The proposed research will analyze from three aspects: (i) the patriotic Christian organizations and their responses; (ii) the different responses and reflections of Christians affected by the campaign; (iii) the responses of house-churches which were not directly affected. What impacts does the campaign bring to Chinese Christianity under authoritarianism?

14621320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621320.value: The cross-demolition campaign in Zhejiang Province from 2014 to 2016 can be considered as the most large-scale state-church conflict levelled against Christianity since China’s economic reform and opening-up. According to some statistics, at least 1,500 crosses had been removed from churches by the government by force. In some regions, the campaign had triggered anti-demolition protests from local Christian communities. Why Zhejiang Province, where state-church relations were known to be relatively harmonious and Christianity was thriving, for such widespread and sweeping state-church conflict against Christianity (even government recognized and registered churches)? Why did the cross as a religious symbol of Christianity became the focus of this conflict? What is the connotation of religious symbol in the realm of politics and religion separately, and what are the interactions between the two? Undoubtedly, the cross-demolition campaign in Zhejiang Province makes a unique case in the study of contemporary Chinese state-church relations. The proposed research will focus on Wenzhou of Zhejiang Province. Wenzhou is the city where the fastest growth of Christianity in China was seen. The number of Christians has reached one million, accounting for 10 to 15 % of the city’s population. In the last ten years, the number of churches also saw rapid growth and the city has been known as “China’s Jerusalem”. In the cross-demolition campaign, Wenzhou warrants particular consideration in terms of the number of churches affected, the anti-demolition movements, and attention from international media. This research will examine the state-church relations and tensions revealed in the cross-demolition campaign (in relation to party-state and religion, party-state and Christianity, and Church and politics) and assess how the campaign would re-shape China’s state-church relations. What role does the case of Wenzhou state-church relations play in understanding the development of Christianity under the party-state authoritarian regime? 2014至2016年發生於浙江省的強拆十字架運動，可說是改革開放以來中國最大規模針對基督教的政教衝突。據統計全省最少有1500所教堂的十字架被政府強拆，而在部分地區更激發不少教會及信徒以反拆十為名的抗爭行動。為何在政教關係相對和諧，基督教發展取得長足發展的浙江省，竟在全省廣泛範圍發生針對基督教（政府認可及登記教會）的大規模政教衝突？「十字架」作為基督教標記的宗教符號，為何成為是次衝突的焦點所在？宗教符號在政治及宗教領域內分別具有甚麼含義，並產生怎樣的互動？毋庸置疑，浙江省拆十運動是當代中國政教關係研究中極具獨特意義的案例。本研究將以浙江省溫州為研究中心，溫州是全中國基督教發展最快的城市，基督徒人口高達100多萬，佔當地人口達10至15%之高；近十多年間，教堂也取有極快的增長，向來有「中國耶路撒冷」之譽。而在是次拆十運動中，溫州不論是受波及的教堂數目，及反拆十的抗爭運動方面，均具一定代表性，備受國際媒體的關注。本研究嘗試從黨國與宗教、黨國與教會、教會與政治等角度，分析拆十運動呈現的政教關係及張力，並評估其如何重塑中國的政教處境？溫州政教關係的個案，對了解黨國威權體制下的基督教發展，又有甚麼意義？

14621320.label: Realisation of objectives
14621320.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved despite challenges. This project commenced in January 2021 with a planned duration of 30 months, originally scheduled for completion on June 30, 2023. However, due to the significant disruptions caused by the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic during the research period, the project timeline was severely impacted, leading to a six-month extension to December 31, 2023. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the strict policy on quarantine measures, the original plan to conduct research and field trips to Wenzhou has been cancelled. As stated in the mid-progress report, two contingency plans have been implemented. First, conducting phone interview, instead of face-to face interview, with one Christian key figure in the protest campaign of Wenzhou; Second, conducting face-to-face interview with nine Christians from mainland China who are now studying theology in Hong Kong. Although the COVID-19 pandemic eased toward the end of 2022, and quarantine measures between Mainland China and Hong Kong were gradually lifted, the increasingly restrictive political climate in China presented significant challenges. Given the sensitive nature of the project's subject matter, the risks associated with conducting fieldwork and interviews in Wenzhou grew substantially, ultimately necessitating the cancellation of planned field investigations. The Principal Investigator (PI), with extensive experience in researching contemporary Chinese Christianity, has conducted numerous fieldwork studies and interviews in China in the past. However, the rapid political changes in recent years far exceeded the expectations at the time of the project's design. Many international scholars specializing in Chinese studies have voiced concerns about the increasing 'securitization' of Chinese society, which has made it difficult for foreign and overseas (including Hong Kong ) researchers to conduct fieldwork or interviews. Unfortunately, this project was no exception and was inevitably impacted by these developments. In response to the unforeseen challenges posed by the pandemic and external circumstances, the project proceeded according to its contingency plan. However, interviews conducted via telephone, online platforms, or in Hong Kong were less ideal than those conducted in person. Moreover, some interviewees expressed heightened concerns, making it difficult for them to speak freely and share their opinions openly. This represented the most significant difficulty and challenge for the project. Nevertheless, the project endeavored to meet its objectives under these constraints: 1. Policy documents related to the 'Three Rectifications and One Demolition' campaign and the Cross Demolition movement, along with relevant materials from the official Chinese Patriotic Christian Church (at both the national and Zhejiang provincial levels), have been successfully collected, organized, and analyzed. 2. Of the initially planned 65-75 interviews, 50 were completed via telephone, online platforms, or in Hong Kong. Invitations extended within the PI's personal network were largely successful; however, second-tier referrals encountered obstacles. Even though anonymity was assured, potential interviewees often expressed concerns about involvement. Among the 50 successful cases, 22 interviewees declined to have their responses recorded. 3. A detailed analysis was conducted from the perspective of church-state relations, focusing on the relationship between the Party-state and Protestant Christianity, the Party-state and the Three-Self Patriotic Movement organizations, and the political implications of various church responses to the Cross Demolition campaign. 4. In addition to examining responses from China's Three-Self Patriotic churches and house churches, the project also analyzed how Hong Kong churches responded to the Cross Demolition campaign.

14621320.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621320.value: The project has contributed to long-term impact brought by the following research findings and outcomes: 1. Contribution to the Study of Contemporary Chinese Christianity: This research project highlights the religious protests of Wenzhou Christians against the forced demolition of crosses, an event that stands out as one of the few regionally significant Christian protest campaigns in the post-1949 People’s Republic of China. While the topic of social protests in China since the reform and opening-up has garnered considerable attention from international scholars, protests involving religious dimensions remain underexplored. This study investigates the limitations of religious (Christian) protests and examines the significance of the anti-cross-demolition resistance from the perspective of public religion. (See research outputs: 8:3) 2. Comparative Analysis and Critical Reflection: The research compares the anti-cross-demolition protests in Wenzhou with the protest of Beijing house churches. Additionally, it situates these protests within the broader trajectory of China’s democratization process, offering critical reflections. Through this approach, the study seeks to provide a grounded examination of the relationship between Christianity and the democratization of China. (See research outputs: 8:4) 3. Revisiting Church-State Relations in Contemporary China: The study contributes to the understanding of the development of church-state relations in contemporary China in two key ways: (a) Focus on 2014-2016 Cross Demolition and Resistance: The project analyzes the evolving dynamics of church-state relations during this period, particularly the relationships between the Party-state and Protestant Christianity, the Party-state and the Three-Self Patriotic Movement, and the political positioning of Three-Self churches.(See research outputs: 8:3-5) (b) Historical Contextualization: The project places the church-state dynamics revealed by the 2014-2016 cross-demolition campaign within the broader historical context of church-state relations in China since 1949. This approach aims to reconstruct the developmental trajectory of Protestant Christianity in a socialist context and explore the reasons behind its transformations. (See research outputs: 8:2, 8:5) 4. From the Perspective of Sino-Hong Kong Church Relations: The unprecedented response of Hong Kong Christian churches to the Cross Demolition campaign not only reflects their concern for churches in Mainland China but also highlights a critical reflection on the state of religious freedom in China. (See research output: 8:1)

14621320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621320.value: By examining the Cross Demolition campaign and contemporary church-state relations in China, this research can be further developed in the following two ways: (1) Comparative research on post-2014 church-state relations in China, focusing not only on the Cross Demolition campaign in Zhejiang but also on developments in other key provinces for Christianity, such as Henan. (2) Analyzing the changes and continuities in New Hong Kong’s church-state relations within the context of the 'New Era' of church-state dynamics in China.

14621320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621320.value: The cross-demolition campaign in Zhejiang Province from 2014 to 2016 can be considered as the most large-scale state-church conflict levelled against Christianity since China’s economic reform and opening-up. According to some statistics, at least 1,500 crosses had been removed from churches by the government by force. In some regions, the campaign had triggered anti-demolition protests from local Christian communities. This project centers on Wenzhou, where authorities removed at least four hundred crosses from churches. It investigates whether the reasons offered for demolishing illegal buildings justify cross demolition, examines the role of the religious factor in the overall campaign, and determines whether the Zhejiang provincial leader attempted to tackle religion-related problems under the guise of demolishing illegal buildings. It will also examine the state-church relations and tensions revealed in the cross-demolition campaign (in relation to party-state and religion, party-state and Christianity, and Church and politics) and assess how the campaign would re-shape China’s state-church relations. What role does the case of Wenzhou state-church relations play in understanding the development of Christianity under the party-state authoritarian regime?

14621420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621420.value: 唐代魏徵等奉唐太宗勅命編《群書治要》（以下簡稱「《治要》」），採用唐前典籍六十五種，摘取其中與治國相關的文字，用以作為管治國家的參考。此書保留了不少典籍的舊貌。唐代以後，《治要》漸有散佚，至宋以後失傳。《治要》在晚唐已傳至日本，今所見重要版本俱源自日本所藏，其重要性可見一斑。本計劃擬從以下方面著眼： 第一，收集並整理日藏諸本《群書治要》。《治要》傳入日本以後，在平安時代有四位日本天皇嘗加誦讀。今存最早《治要》鈔本即屬平安時代九条家本，此為殘本，現藏東京國立博物館，屬日本國寶，筆致優雅而端正，部分內容更為天皇收藏。又，宮內廳書稜部藏有鎌倉時代金澤文庫本，此本與九条家本關係密切，乃現存時代最早之足本。又，元和活字刊本駿河版則以金澤文庫本為祖，屬現存時代最早之活字本，最堪閱讀。至於天明本，乃日人對照魏徵所引原書重新校刊之本，失卻《治要》存舊之真。考證日藏諸本《治要》之關係，自可得知諸本的流變過程，對了解此書的傳播與重要性有莫大幫助。 第二，利用日藏《群書治要》校勘其所引典籍，並作輯佚。《治要》引用唐前經、史、子文獻共六十五種，日藏諸本時代甚早，取《治要》以校勘所引典籍，可更正許多原典的問題。《治要》雖在清嘉慶初年回流中國，惜此本嘗經後人回改，不保《治要》原貌。今據日藏諸本重新勘正所引典籍，可補前人研究之未備。北京中華書局《新編諸子集成》、《新編諸子集成續編》每有據《群書治要》以作校正，然其所據僅為未臻完善的天明本，今據日藏諸本《治要》加以比較，更可校正原典裡之錯誤。此外，《治要》亦引佚書，以及典籍之中的佚篇；故利用《治要》所引，可為唐前舊典輯佚。 第三，討論《群書治要》的選文與治國之道。古代典籍浩如煙海，《治要》乃在群書之中摘引與管治國家相關者，勒成一書。其中《治要》選文與否，標準為何，可用敘事學之方法細考。《治要》編者以此書作諫書，以選文建議治國之道。今天雖無君臣關係，然而今天如能借助《治要》以管理企業，仍不失為古書今用之範例。 本研究計劃先將收集和整理日藏諸本《群書治要》，然後探討各本《治要》之承傳關係，以及其與所引原典之異同。接著，利用《治要》校勘和輯佚，補足文獻學上未備之處。最後，以《治要》所載典籍為例，從敘事學的角度分析《治要》之選文。具體方向主要有三：一、利用日藏諸本《治要》，討論此書在日本的流傳情況，以及各本之間的關係。二、利用《治要》校勘所引書及輯佚。三、探討《治要》之選文準則。四、《治要》治國之道的今用。 A research on Different Editions of Qunshu Zhiyao in Japan Wei Zheng compiled Qunshu Zhiyao (hereinafter referred to as Zhiyao), using 65 kinds of pre-Tang classics, extracting the text related to governing the country, as a reference for governing the country. This book retains the old features of many classics. After the Tang Dynasty, Zhiyao gradually disappeared and was lost after the Song Dynasty. Zhiyao was introduced to Japan in the late Tang Dynasty. Zhiyao has been spread to Japan in the late Tang Dynasty, and the important editions we see today are all from the collection of Japan. The plan is intended to focus on the following aspects: First, collect and collate different editions of Zhiyao collected in Japan. Including the earliest Kujō clan edition from the Heian period, this is the remnant edition, is now in the Tokyo National Museum. Secondly, there is a Kanesawa-bunko edition from the Kamakura period in the Shoryōbu of the Imperial Household Agency, which is closely related to Kujō clan edition and is the earliest complete version of Qunshu Zhiyao. Moreover, Suruganokuni edition is based on the Kanesawa-bunko edition, which is the earliest movable type printed edition that can be preserved at present and is the most readable. So far as the Tenmei edition is concerned, the Japanese re-proofread the original book quoted by Wei Zheng, and lost the significance of preserving the ancient edition of Zhiyao. Textual research on different editions of Zhiyao collected in Japan, discussing the similarities and differences of different editions, we can know the evolution process of various editions, which is of great help to understand the dissemination and importance of this book. Secondly, the collection of various editions of Zhiyao in Japan is used to collate the cited books, and the lost books can be compiled. There are sixty-five kinds of Pre-Tang documents cited in Zhiyao. The edition of Japanese collections dates back to a relatively early age. Taking Zhiyao to collate the quoted books can correct many problems of the original books. At present, the different editions collected in Japan can be used to re-collate the relevant books, which can supplement the previous studies. Zhuzi Jicheng(Collection of the hundred schools of thought) of Beijing Zhonghua Bookstore often uses Zhiyao as collation, but only the imperfect Tenmei edition is used. The errors in the Zhuzi can be corrected by using the editions collected in Japan. In addition, Zhiyao also quoted the lost books, as well as the lost articles in the ancient books, so we can use Zhiyao to retrieve the lost documents. Thirdly, this project will discuss the selected articles of Zhiyao and the ways of governing the country mentioned in the book. There are a large number of ancient books. Zhiyao selected some of them related to governing the country to form a book. Narratological methods can be used to examine the selection and criteria of Zhiyao. The compiler of Zhiyao used this book as an admonition book to recommend the way of governing the country by selecting articles. Today, although there is no relationship between the monarch and the minister, we can still manage the enterprise by means of the way of governing the country in Zhiyao, which is really a model used in ancient books today. This project will collect and sort out different editions of Zhiyao collected in Japan, and then explore the inheritance relationship of each edition of Zhiyao and its similarities and differences with the original books cited. Next, using the collation and compilation of Zhiyao to make up for the inadequacies in philology. Finally, taking the contents in Zhiyao as an example, this paper analyses the selected articles of Zhiyao from the perspective of narratology. Specific directions are as follows: 1. Discuss the spread of Zhiyao in Japan and the relationship between different editions by using the collection of Zhiyao in Japan. 2. Make use of the cited books in the collation of Zhiyao and compile the lost parts. 3. Discuss the attitude of selecting articles in Zhiyao and the application of the way of governing the country in the book today.

14621420.label: Realisation of objectives
14621420.value: Firstly, a comprehensive examination of the Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan is conducted to observe their textual differences and for collation. Through this research plan, different versions of Qunshu Zhiyao stored in Japan have been examined, including the Kujō clan edition from the Heian period, Kanesawa-bunko edition from the Kamakura period, and the most readable Suruga edition, and finally the Tenmei edition, etc., and the differences among them have been compared. This approach allows for the Qunshu Zhiyao to be more conveniently utilized in the future. Among all versions, the Suruga edition is used as the basis, and other versions are carefully compared to correct errors in different versions. Secondly, this research project uses Qunshu Zhiyao as an example to investigate the dissemination of ancient Chinese books in Japan. China and Japan are neighboring countries. Since the Tang Dynasty, many books have been transmitted from China to Japan. Some of these books have been lost in China but have been preserved in Japan, and Qunshu Zhiyao is such a classic. This research project has examined the Kujō family edition from the Heian period, the Kanazawa Bunko edition, the Suruga edition, and the Tenmei edition, etc., showing that Qunshu Zhiyao has been highly valued in Japan since the Heian period. In addition to the emperor once studying Qunshu Zhiyao, this book has also been highly valued among Japanese nobles. The specific circumstances of the dissemination of Qunshu Zhiyao in Japan are mentioned in several papers published in this research project. Thirdly, several editions of Qunshu Zhiyao stored in Japan have a very close relationship with each other, which has been explained in the papers written in this research project. The Kujō family edition and the Kanazawa Bunko edition are closely related. Where the Kujō family edition has errors, the same text in the Kanazawa Bunko edition often corresponds. In addition, the Suruga edition, as a printed version, is also based on the handwritten Kanazawa Bunko edition, which shows the relationship between the two versions. Finally, the Tenmei edition is based on the Suruga edition, as can be seen in the collation notes of the Tenmei edition. Therefore, the connections between the various versions have been resolved in this research project. Fourth, Qunshu Zhiyao quotes many classics, a total of 65 types. Using several versions of Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan, it can now be used to collate the originals quoted by Qunshu Zhiyao. The academic community has mostly used the Tianming version of Qunshu Zhiyao to collate the originals in the past, but the purpose of this research project is to add the versions collected in Japan, including the Kujo family edition, the Kanazawa Bunko edition, and the Suruga version. The publication of "Kujo Family Qunshu Zhiyao Collation" represents that the versions of Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan can be used to collate the originals quoted. Fifth, the classics cited by Qunshu Zhiyao are all classics before the Tang Dynasty, many of which have been lost today. Therefore, using the classics quoted by Qunshu Zhiyao can be used for the compilation of some lost classics. According to the data of several versions of Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan by this research project, it can supplement the shortcomings of only using the Tianming version of Qunshu Zhiyao for compilation in the past. Among the several versions of Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan, the Kanazawa library edition is earlier, and the Suruga edition is the most neatly transcribed, both can make the greatest contribution to the work of compilation. Sixth, when Qunshu Zhiyao chooses to adopt some of the texts from the classics, it is actually a choice of narrative studies. There are many contents in the ancient classics, and Qunshu Zhiyao adopts some paragraphs related to governing the country to form this book. However, when quoting the content of a book, what is used and what is not used, the meaning behind it is profound. In the thesis submitted by this research plan, one of the topics is based on the "Historical Records" quoted by Qunshu Zhiyao, discussing some of the reasons for the adoption or non-adoption of the Shiji. This is also a wonderful part of the citations in Qunshu Zhiyao. Seventh, Qunshu Zhiyao discusses the issue of how to govern the country. The whole book achieves this goal by quoting relevant quotations from ancient classics. In one of the papers I submitted, I discussed that Qunshu Zhiyao contains a rich consciousness of learning from history. What happened in ancient times is like a mirror, reflecting what can be done and what should not be done. These are the functions and meanings of reading ancient books today, and the important influence of ancient books on today's society.
