14621420.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621420.value: This project has deepened the academic community's understanding of the Qunshu Zhiyao, especially the different versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao held in Japan. Traditionally, the academic community has only focused on certain popular versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao for textual research. This research project particularly focuses on a few versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao held in Japan, which have rarely been utilized. For instance, many ancient books that use the Qunshu Zhiyao for textual research have never used the Japanese versions. In some of my papers, such as the one that cites The Garden of Persuasions from the Qunshu Zhiyao, the Japanese versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao can be used for textual research of the current version of The Garden of Persuasions. As for another paper, the focus is on the unique features of the Japanese versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao and the merits of each version. Of course, the most important task is the proofreading of the entire Qunshu Zhiyao. There has always been a lack of a well-proofread version of the Qunshu Zhiyao, especially since the use of the Japanese versions is minimal. Using this research project, I first used the Kujo family version of the Qunshu Zhiyao as the base text, referred to other versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao collected in Japan, organized and proofread, and published the first book in the academic community with this title, which pioneered in the academic community. In the coming days, with the research findings, further exploration can be conducted on the specific circumstances of the cited works in the Qunshu Zhiyao and the differences in the texts of different versions of the Qunshu Zhiyao. I have also signed a contract with the publisher to diligently proofread and organize the entire book of the Qunshu Zhiyao, not limited to the Nine Family Edition. Additionally, as one of the main organizers, I will continue to promote research in different fields of the Qunshu Zhiyao at the upcoming international conference.

14621420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621420.value: As mentioned earlier, the Qunshu Zhiyao extensively cites various works. Although this research project and my previous studies have covered most of the important topics, there are still many issues that can be further explored. For example, it would be interesting to examine the similarities and differences between the works cited in the Qunshu Zhiyao and those cited in the encyclopedic works of the Tang and Song dynasties. This may shed light on the differences in nature between the Qunshu Zhiyao and the encyclopedic works of the Tang and Song dynasties, as well as the variations in versions and the influence of different periods. Additionally, it would be valuable to explore the relevance of the Qunshu Zhiyao in today's society. For instance, examining the relationship between the teachings of the book and personal self-cultivation, as well as the connection between governing a nation and managing a business, can demonstrate how Qunshu Zhiyao remains relevant and continues to impact contemporary society.

14621420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621420.value: In the early Tang Dynasty, Emperor Taizong ordered Wei Zheng and others to compile the book Qunshu Zhiyao. The purpose was to select passages related to national governance from the classics of past dynasties for the emperor's reference in governing the country. Japan has collected several precious versions of Qunshu Zhiyao. This research project uses these versions to analyze the evolution process of these versions. It discusses the differences between these versions and the widely circulated version of Qunshu Zhiyao, supplementing the deficiencies of previous scholars when using this book. Today, people want to use Qunshu Zhiyao, but they lack a well-organized version as a basis. The results of this research project make up for this deficiency. On the other hand, this research project also conducts research from different perspectives on the classics cited in Qunshu Zhiyao, opening up a new path for the study of this book from the aspect of selected excerpts.

14621520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14621520.value: 從形成到轉化：柬埔寨吳哥早期高棉陶瓷的生產與中國的關係

14621520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621520.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research on Khmer ceramic production from its beginning in the 9th century formation to its 12th century transformation, when it shifted from green glazed ceramic to brown glazed ceramic techniques. This period was when Chinese ceramic production techniques appear to have been introduced to the Khmer Empire. However, existing scholarship does not explain the historical processes behind this introduction. Angkor was the capital of the Khmer Empire in mainland Southeast Asia during A.D. 802-1431. The Khmer Empire covered modern Cambodia, Northeast Thailand, Southern Vietnam, Laos and Tenasserim of Myanmar. Previous research focused on the internal relationship between Khmer ceramic production and distribution in archaeological, artistic, scientific, ethnological and historical aspects; the results, however, were inconclusive. This research will conduct systematic and integrated analyses on the technological, social and geopolitical aspects of Khmer ceramic production and its interactive relationship with China. It will no longer be mainly concerned with China’s impact on the outside world but will use Khmer ceramic studies to scrutinize China as a “foreign source” and bring out new details about the social life of the local inhabitants and how it changed over time. This project combines four different research techniques to conduct its analyses: 1) petrographic analysis of Khmer and Chinese ceramic samples; 2) scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis; 3) comparative study of the typological and stylistic differences and similarities between two regions; and 4) Chinese historical documents’ analysis of Angkor and the archaeological reports on both Khmer and Chinese ceramic production sites. The final outputs of this project will include an integrated analytical database of both stylistic and scientific analyses of Khmer ceramics that focuses on the interaction between the Khmer and Chinese cultural realms, and a monograph on Khmer ceramic production and consumption in the Angkorian region in correlation with China. It will provide a new placing of Angkor into the interregional trading networks of medieval Asia in world archaeological context. 此計劃旨在研究高棉陶瓷生產從九世紀初形成至十二世紀轉化，從青釉器發展至醬釉器的技術。中國陶瓷生產技術可能在此時期介紹到高棉王國。然而，現有研究尚未解釋這個重要的歷史進程。吳哥是高棉王國（公元802-1431）的首都，高棉王國位於今柬埔寨、泰國東北部、越南南部、老撾及緬甸的德林達依。以往研究集中以考古、藝術、科學、民族及歷史角度研究高棉陶瓷生產和分佈，但仍未有結論。此研究將系統地從技術、社會及地緣政治的角度分析高棉陶瓷生產與中國互動的關係。並以中國作為外國資料來源的角度，分析當地居民在不同時代社會生活的新細節。此計劃結合四個不同研究方法進行分析：1）高棉及中國陶瓷樣本的岩相學分析；2）掃描電子顯微鏡分析；3）兩個區域的陶瓷類型及風格異同的比較研究；4）有關吳哥的中國歷史文獻及高棉和中國陶瓷生產遺址考古報告的分析。計劃最終成果將包括高棉陶瓷與中國關係分析的綜合資料庫及吳哥地區高棉陶瓷生產和消費及其與中國關係的專著。此計劃將從世界考古的場域，把吳哥建置於中古時期亞洲跨區貿易網絡的研究。

14621720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621720.value: The project aims to study Robert Thom (1807-1846), a Sinologist who served as diplomatic translator at HMS at the Opium War. Born in Glasgow, Scotland, Robert Thom was employed and posted to China by the Matheson & Company in 1833. Upon arriving China, he made great efforts in learning Chinese. After publishing his translations of the Aesop’s Fables and a Chinese drama, he became well known in Guangzhou as a Chinese expert. He got involved in the opium ban and translated, in an unofficial capacity, many important documents. When the Opium War broke out, he was recruited as interpreter/translator and served the British expeditionary army throughout the war. He was one of the interpreters for the peace negotiation. Though he did not translate the Treaty of Nanking, he sat at the centre during the signing ceremony, occupying a position even more conspicuous than the signatory, Sir Henry Pottinger. He was assigned to draw up regulations to govern trade activity at the newly opened treaty ports. He translated the Supplementary Treaty, commonly known as the Treaty of the Bogue (1843), which unfortunately caused great controversy. He was then appointed the first British Consul at Ningbo, a position he held for less than three years before he died in 1846. The present project will first examine what Thom chose for translation before he was involved in the political struggles between the British government and the Chinese authorities, why these works were chosen, and how they were translated. We will then analyse how and why he was enlisted to translate and interpret as a diplomatic translator for HM government in the Opium War. An analysis into the translations he made after joining the British government, in comparison to his earlier translations, will tell how a diplomatic translator works differently from a non-official one. One main focus of our study is to examine the long-term historical consequences of his translations and mistranslations. While the project focuses on Robert Thom, it is not just about one individual. Firstly, it serves as a distinct case study to enhance our understanding of the very important topic “Sinologists as translators”. Secondly, it contributes to translator studies by looking into a less studied group of translators/interpreters, the diplomatic translators. Thirdly, it demonstrates the significant role played by translation in international conflicts. Lastly, it helps to provide a more comprehensive and accurate understanding of the Opium War. 本計劃旨在深入及全面研究第一次鴉片戰爭前後身兼漢學家並作為外交譯者的羅伯聃（Robert Thom, 1807-1846）的工作、貢獻和影響。 羅伯聃生於蘇格蘭，1833年受聘於怡和洋行，1834年2月到中國，積極學習中文，1838年即在廣州翻譯及出版《意拾秘傳》，在鴉片戰爭前夕發表過一系列翻譯和討論翻譯的作品，逐漸於來華外國人圈子中認受為中文水平較高的英國人，且已牽涉在中英糾紛中，曾陪同鴉片商人出席林則徐禁煙會議，更協助英方繳交鴉片，得到當時英國在華官員的信任。鴉片戰爭爆發後，羅伯聃加入遠征軍任翻譯官，發揮重要角色，不少英方將士的戰爭回憶錄都有所報導。羅伯聃更積極參與《南京條約》的談判，在簽署的儀式上，他坐在簽署桌的正中央，位置比負責簽約的英方代表璞鼎查（Henry Pottinger, 1789-1856）還要顯眼。《南京條約》開放中國五口通商後，羅伯聃被任命為寧波第一任英國領事，在這之前主力負責翻譯《中英五口通商章程》及《善後事宜清冊附粘和約》（《虎門條約》），而在寧波領事任內，由於缺乏譯員，羅伯聃也兼負翻譯的工作。不過，他的領事生命只有兩年半左右，1846年9月14日在任內去世，年39歲。 本研究集中探討羅伯聃來華12年多的活動，焦點放在他作為漢學家兼外交譯者的身份，在中英兩國交戰前後的背景下的工作、活動、貢獻和影響。毫無疑問，這方面的研究是嚴重不足的，因為已有的探討主要集中在羅伯聃翻譯《伊索寓言》以及編寫中文字典方面，幾乎全無觸及其外交翻譯以至外交活動，無法顯示他作為鴉片戰爭前後中英交往史上其中一位關鍵人物的貢獻和影響。 本研究先從羅伯聃來華後在怡和洋行工作期間、沒有加入英國政府前學習中文和發表翻譯開始，討論他在來華學習中文的情況、他在英商界的位置、他的翻譯選材以及一些政治活動，繼而考察他出任英方翻譯官後的工作，分析他的翻譯活動以及文本，並探討他所參與的一些翻譯以外的工作，包括戰爭期間英軍佔領地區的管治，重點在於他在《南京條約》談判前後所負責的翻譯；最後分析羅伯聃在出任寧波領事期的工作和活動，包括以領事身份與中國官員交往並兼任翻譯的工作。前期的資料主要來自劍橋大學怡和洋行檔案，後期則以英國外交部檔案為主。 本研究除加深對羅伯聃的貢獻和歷史地位的理解外，更期望能呈現鴉片戰爭前後中英交往的溝通狀況、模式和困難，並展現漢學家及外交譯者在中英語言、文化、政治交往上的角色和影響。

14621720.label: Realisation of objectives
14621720.value: It is a highly satisfying and rewarding experience in conducting the present project. By realizing the five objectives set in the proposal, I have been able to have a much complete and accurate understanding of not only the life and deeds of Robert Thom as a Sinologist and a diplomatic interpreter before and after the Opium War, but also in the ways a Sinologist contributes in different means and capacities to Sino-Western cultural exchanges as well as political and military interactions at a special time of history. It enhances our knowledge of a major figure in Sino-British relations in the first half of the 19th century, as well as the concept of Sinologists as translators, and the functions of diplomatic interpreters. Objective 1, to collect and read the relevant materials, is of prime importance. Much of those materials relating to Robert Thom’s career as a diplomatic interpreter can be found in the Foreign Office Records available in the National Archives. As the PI has been working on Sino-British relations for many years, there is no issue in getting access to them. The PI has also made a research trip to London and Cambridge, UK, in May 2023, to conduct research at the National Archives of the UK, British Library and the Cambridge University Library. The trip was fruitful as I was able to gather what I had wanted, thanks for prior arrangements with the libraries, as well as the assistance of a couple of my former students who were studying in London and Cambridge. A huge volume of materials were photographed. The only issue, a big one though, is to go over the mammoth volume so as to extract those materials that are related to Robert Thom. During the project period, I spent a lot of time in reading the Foreign Office Records. It is most rewarding that I have been able to dig out some very important materials. One particular piece is the will of Robert Thom, which allows us to know more about his family. Another set of materials worthy of special mentioning is the one about his consulship in Ningbo. After discussing with experts in Ningbo history, it is certain that such materials were not available in Ningbo or elsewhere. There has not been any thorough study of Robert Thom as the first British consul at Ningbo, probably because people have not been able to make use of the relevant materials in the Foreign Office Records. I have written and presented a conference paper on his deeds and achievements as the Ningbo consul in an international conference. This will soon be turned into a journal publication. One major discovery in connection with Objective 1 is the letters written by Robert Thom collected at the Jardine Matheson Archive of the Cambridge University Library. Other scholars have so far made use of only a couple of Thom’s letters from the Archive. With the kind permission of the Matheson & Co. and the assistance of the friendly staffs of the Cambridge University Library, I have been able to search over the Archive and successfully identified over two dozen letters written by Thom in different times, including the time when he was stationed in Central China during the War as a field interpreter. They told some unheard stories which enhance our understanding of Thom, the Opium War as well as the Canton trading system, of which Jardine, Matheson & Co. was an active player. There is one regret though. I have discovered from an auction website that about thirty letters written by Thom to his brother, Rev. David Thom, together with a sandalwood box which supposedly had contained the Treaty of Nanking, were put up for auction in 2017. Although I wrote many times to them, the auction firm refused to disclose information of the buyer or the whereabouts of the letters. It is a great regret because no other letter from Thom to his family members survives and thus these thirty odd letters must contain very important information of the life, feelings and deeds of Robert Thom. Objective 2 is relatively easy to achieve, as the published works of Robert Thom are available, mainly online. Some requires a little effort as they were published in newspapers in Canton. I have studied all his works, paying special attention to the para-texts such as the prefaces. They provide crucial information for writing up the journal papers and conference papers. For Objective 3, to re-examine the incidents during the Opium War that Robert Thom’s translations might have impacted, I have limited myself to a few incidents. Before the project, I wrote an article on the Article 13 of the Supplementary Treaty of 1843. I have expanded to include the translation issues of the other articles of this very important and controversial treaty. Another focus is on the attitude of Robert Thom towards the war. It is significant that Robert Thom was the only war time British interpreter who adopted a very friendly attitude towards the Chinese. He even published articles to openly condemn the British troops for doing injustices to the Chinese people. This makes Robert Thom a unique case of a diplomatic interpreter. By comparing him to the other British diplomatic interpreters such as John Robert Morrison and Charles Gutzlaff, we can see a clearer picture of the identities and roles of the diplomatic interpreters during the first major hostilities between the two great powers of the time. This serves Objective 5 quite satisfactorily. The research concept of “Sinologists as translators” has long attracted my attention as most studies on Sinologists focus on the intercultural exchanges contributed by Sinologists without much reference to the “tool” they adopted for realizing these intercultural exchanges, namely, translation. For the present project on Robert Thom, I study how Thom made use of translation to produce texts for language learning. It is of particular interest that Thom made use of translated texts to promote language learning in both English and Chinese. In this way, the project enhances our understanding of the concept of Sinologists as translators, hence the achievement of Objective 4.

14621720.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621720.value: The project is the first comprehensive study of Robert Thom in his capacity as a Sinologist and diplomatic interpreter. This is different from past studies which paid attention to his translations from a linguistics perspective and could not relate them to the socio-political and cultural background. So far I have published two journal articles and presented four conference papers. They cover different aspects of Robert Thom. The book chapter on his translation of the Supplementary Treaty of 1843 examines and explains the big discrepancies between the Chinese and English versions, contributing not only to the understanding of Robert Thom as the translator but more significantly, one major incident that affected seriously Sino-British relations after the war. The second journal paper is a comprehensive examination of the attitude of Thom towards China and Sino-British relations around the time of the Opium War. By analysing his private letters, translations, and articles he published openly, the PI finds that Robert Thom had changed his attitude drastically within the first two years of his stay in China. He at first had a strong distaste towards China, to a point that he wanted to break his appointment contract and left Canton. In less than two years, he became very friendly to the Chinese and began to urge his fellow countrymen to learn the Chinese language and culture so as to appreciate the greatness of the Imperial Empire. This marked him distinctly from most, if not all British who were then residing in Canton. Throughout the rest of his life, even though he participated the war as a diplomatic interpreter , fostering, of course, mostly British interests, he tried to make sure the general Chinese people did not suffer too badly. Other major findings include his use of translation to facilitate language learning, both for Chinese and English. Thom was eager that the Chinese and British should acquire the other’s language because he saw this the most effective means to promote better understanding and hence better relations. I have also completed the first in-depth study of Thom’s consulship in Ningbo. This should set an example in the examination of the setting up of British consulates in the new treaty ports after the Opium War.

14621720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621720.value: There are two directions for further development. First, the study of Robert Thom, the man. As I have done all the basic research related to Thom, it is possible that we can write up a detail and comprehensive biography of Thom. This is a worthy project because he is a very unique case of his time. The biography will enable us to see his role, position, and contributions in political history (Thom in Sino-British relations), translation history (Thom as a translator) and cultural history (Thom as a Sinologist). The PI has a plan to write up this biography. The second direction is to put Thom into the big circle of Sinologists in the 19th century to see how Sinologists of different backgrounds collectively constitute a cultural phenomenon in the specific time and space. There are, again, different directions for further development. We may study how Sinologists were involved in political interactions (as diplomatic interpreters or diplomats), and we may study how Sinologists contributed to cultural exchanges (through translations of works from and into China). The PI has published a well-received article in 2021 on how translators could be studied as a cultural phenomenon.

14621720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621720.value: The project has exhausted and studied the private letters, translations and all available published works of Robert Thom. Referencing to the relevant official documents of the British Foreign Office Records and those from Chinese sources, it establishes Robert Thom as a unique case of his time and hence is worthy of serious academic attention. First, he was an admirer of Chinese culture and adopted a most friendly attitude towards the Chinese people. Second, he was critical of his own fellow countrymen for not attempting to learn the Chinese language and know China better. He even condemned the British troops for doing injustice to the Chinese people during the war. Third, the main purpose of translating was to facilitate language learning, both for Chinese and English. Thom was eager that the Chinese and British should acquire the other’s language because he saw this the most effective means to promote better understanding and hence better relations. Lastly, the project examines Robert Thom as the first British consul at Ningbo, a topic that has not been studied by other scholars.

14621820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14621820.value: 新柏拉圖哲學的真相辯證法理論

14621820.label: Project Objectives
14621820.value: This project will demonstrate the presence of the dialetheic concept of truth in Pseudo-Dionysius and Meister Eckhart. This project will employ dialetheism as a principle by which to systematically elucidate the metaphysics and epistemology of Neo-Platonic philosophy. This new reading of the Neo-Platonic tradition aims to show the existence of a strong dialetheic tradition that stands in competition and dialogue with the more established traditions grounded in the principle of non-contradiction. This project will demonstrate the dialetheic structure of a number of concepts in the Neo-Platonic corpus, including the concept of the Trinity, Ecstasy, Freedom, Incarnation and Agape. Because many of these concepts are theological, or bear on theological discourse, this project will establish the necessity of developing a new kind of theological discourse that is nonetheless grounded in the tradition: dialetheic theology. This project will demonstrate that this historical analysis also has systematic value, for Neo-Platonic concepts can be successfully translated into non-theological terminology. For example, in the place of 'God' one can speak of the ‘Absolute’, and in the place of ‘creation’ one can speak about ‘relative (non-absolute) beings’ such that the three loci of true contradiction can be re-articulated as follows: (i) the being of the Absolute, ii) the methodology by which human beings can know the Absolute and iii) the relationship between the Absolute and relative beings. By drawing on Eckhart and Pseudo-Dionysius, this project will employ Neo-Platonic dialectical reason in order to clarify the dialetheic relation between absolute and non-absolute (or relative) concepts. This project will demonstrate the systematic connection between mysticism, dialetheism, and rationality. On the one hand, because human reason is governed by the principle of non-contradiction, in order to know the contradictory character of the Absolute, the human being must transcend discursive reason. On the other hand, this project will show that although the true contradictions concerning the Absolute can only be known by transcending discursive reason, I will demonstrate how the transcending of discursive reason in Neo-Platonic philosophy engenders the development of a non-discursive reason (nous) that is compatible with dialetheic utterances.

14621820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621820.value: During the past few decades, Graham Priest has advocated for dialetheism, the controversial position that some contradictions are true. In recent decades the philosophical community has begun to recognize the significant challenge posed by Priest’s arguments. Despite the increased interest in dialetheism, and the various attempts at discovering applications of this theory of truth in various philosophical traditions, philosophers and historians of philosophy have not yet applied a dialetheist conception of truth to Neo-Platonism. Although numerous scholars have investigated the role of contradiction in Neo-Platonic thought, scholars have not yet employed dialetheism as a principle by which to systematically elucidate the metaphysics and epistemology of Neo-Platonic philosophy. In a series of four articles, I aim to uncover the dialetheic concept of truth in the texts of two Neo-Platonic thinkers: Pseudo-Dionysius and Meister Eckhart. This will be achieved by means of a close reading of Eckhart’s German sermons, and Pseudo-Dionysius’ Greek texts. This initial research will prepare the way for a longer book-length project that will investigate the dialetheic concept of truth in the broader Neo-Platonic tradition, which will include investigation of further authors such as John Scotus Eriugena and Nicolas of Cusa. Because Eckhart drew heavily upon the theology of Pseudo-Dionysius for inspiration, the dialetheic concept of truth in Eckhart and other Neo-Platonic thinkers follows a common pattern that can be traced to Pseudo-Dionysius as a common source. I will argue that there are at least three loci of true contradiction to be uncovered in Eckhart and Pseudo-Dionysius: i) the being of the God, ii) the methodology by which human beings can know God and iii) the creative relationship between God and creation. Far from standing alone, I also mean to show how these dialetheic elements are systematically connected in the Neo-Platonic framework. Finally, I aim to show that there a number of derivative dialetheic concepts employed by these thinkers that depend up the three loci of true contradiction for their truth. These derivative concepts are the following: a.) The Holy Trinity, b.) Incarnation, c.) Freedom, d.) Ecstasy, and e.) Agape. This historical analysis also has systematic value, for although Pseudo-Dionysius and Eckhart express themselves with theological language, such concepts can be successfully translated into non-theological concepts. Thus, this project also means to show how the dialetheic insights of the Christian Neo-Platonists can be transferrable to secular philosophical research. 過去數十年間，格雷厄姆·普里斯特 (Graham Priest) 倡導雙面真理說 (dialetheism) ，此說認為某些矛盾為真，頗具爭議。近幾十年來，哲學界已開始意識到，普里斯特立論的重要性和挑戰性。人們對雙面真理說的興趣日增，也試圖發掘這種真理理論可如何應用於各種哲學傳統中；儘管如此，哲學家和哲學史學家尚未運用雙面真理說以解釋新柏拉圖主義。即使許多學者探討過矛盾在新柏拉圖思想中的作用，但他們仍未以雙面真理說為原則，系統地闡明新柏拉圖哲學的形上學和知識論。 在一系列的四篇文章中，藉著仔細閱讀埃克哈特大師 (Meister Eckhart) 的德語講道和偽狄奧尼修斯 (Pseudo-Dionysius) 的希臘文著作，我旨在揭示這兩位新柏拉圖思想家的雙面真理觀念。這項初步研究，實乃為下一個研究項目奠基：該項目擬將雙面真理觀的研究範圍，擴展至整個新柏拉圖思想傳統，對象包括約翰內斯·司各特·愛留根納 (John Scotus Eriugena)、庫薩的尼各老 (Nicolas [or Nicholas?] of Cusa) 等人。因為埃克哈特從偽狄奧尼修斯借鑒甚多，故此埃克哈特與其他新柏拉圖思想家的雙面真理觀念，皆遵循一種共通模式，而此模式可以溯源到偽狄奧尼修斯。本研究項目的成果，計畫出版成書。 我認為，必須從埃克哈特和偽狄奧尼修斯的作品中，找出至少三個真正矛盾的中心：(i) 上帝的存在，(ii) 人類可以藉此而認識上帝的方法論，(iii) 上帝與受造物之間的創造關係。我也要展示，這些雙面真理的元素，如何在新柏拉圖思想的框架中系統地聯繫起來。最後，我要表明，這些思想家採用了許多衍生的雙面真理概念，這些概念都要取決於上述三個真正矛盾的中心以得到真理。這些衍生概念是：(a) 三位一體 (The Holy Trinity)，(b) 道成肉身 (Incarnation)，(c) 自由 (Freedom)，(d) 出神 / 神魂超拔 (Ecstasy)，(e) 無私的愛 (Agape)。 上述的歷史分析在系統上也有其意義 (systematic value)。雖然偽狄奧尼修斯和埃克哈特以神學語言表達自己，但這些概念依然可以成功翻譯為非神學的概念。因此，本項目還可展示，基督教新柏拉圖主義者的雙面真理見解，可以如何轉移到世俗哲學研究。

14621820.label: Realisation of objectives
14621820.value: This project will demonstrate the presence of the dialetheic concept of truth in Pseudo-Dionysius and Meister Eckhart, This objective has been achieved in the published book chapter "An Ontology of Non-Discriminatory Love: The Resurrection of the Triune Self in Ueda Shizuteru’s Appropriation and Critique of Meister Eckhart." In this essay I elucidate the truth of contradiction in both Neo-Platonic metaphysics and epistemology with special attention to Eckhart and Dionysius. I elucidate Eckhart's concept of the birth of Christ in the Soul, his Trinitarian concept of reality, and his contradictory view of agape, among other key concepts, all of which were deeply inspired by Dionysius. In order to successfully highlight what is unique about the Christian Neo-Platonic approach, I compared Christian Neo-Platonism with Ueda Shizuteru, a thinker from the Kyoto School. During the project, I added a new objective: this project aims to consider the dialetheic theory of truth in comparative perspective with Japanese philosophy. Both traditions have a strong dialetheic element, and a comparative approach to both traditions can illuminate the dialetheic features of both. Although I originally planned only to investigate the dialetheic theology of Christian Neo-Platonism, as I conducted by research, I realised that the distinctive approach to contradictory theology could be best elucidated with a comparative approach to other traditions. For this reason, I compared Eckhart and Dionysius' approach with Ueda Shizuteru, a key proponent of the Kyoto School, who also advanced dialetheic views. Because Ueda was himself a distinguished Eckhart scholar, I found his work immensely beneficial in the elucidation of the Eckhart's views. I translated the essential part of his book on Eckhart where he compares Eckhart with Zen, and as a result, I was better able to demonstrate the cross-cultural and intercultural import of Neo-Platonic thought. This project will demonstrate the dialetheic structure of a number of concepts in the Neo-Platonic corpus, including the concept of the Trinity, Ecstasy, Freedom, Incarnation and Agape. This objective was achieved in two papers. In "An Ontology of Non-Discriminatory Love: The Resurrection of the Triune Self in Ueda Shizuteru’s Appropriation and Critique of Meister Eckhart" I discuss the dialetheic features of Trinity, Ecstasy, Freedom, Incarnation, and Agape in Eckhart and Dionysius. In the forthcoming paper "The Truth of Contradictions in Cusanus and Luther" I specifically focus on elucidating the truth of contradiction in the Incarnation and the Holy Trinity. In this essay I give special attention to Cusa, a 15th century Neo-Platonist who was deeply influenced by Eckhart. In the paper under review, "Contradictory Theology in Christian Neoplatonism" I show how a new theological discourse (grounded in the Neo-Platonic tradition) is enabled by Cusa, who offers a compelling theological paradigm. In the course of the study, I added a new objective: to demonstrate the presence of true contradictions in later thinkers, such as Nicolas of Cusa. In the course of my study, I learned that while Meister Eckhart was implicitly committed to dialetheism, the view that some contradictions are true, Nicolas of Cusa (a thinker deeply inspired by Eckhart) explicitly endorsed the truth of contradiction in theological discourse. For this reason, I re-focused my inquiries onto Nicolas of Cusa. In two articles (one forthcoming and one under review) I reconstruct his views on the truth of contradiction. The two articles are "Contradictory Theology in Christian Neoplatonism" and "The Truth of Contradictions in Cusanus and Luther." In the former I show how Cusa undermines Aristotle's Principle of Non-Contradiction, and how he develops a three-staged view of divine truth. In the latter, I explain why the Western tradition has traditionally rejected the truth of contradictions in negative theology. I elucidate how Eriugena developed a cataphatic and apophatic theory of divine knowledge that attempted to avoid contradictions. Finally, I show that Cusa has a more compelling theory that endorses a dialetheic view about divine truths. On the whole, I give a broad historical evaluation and overview of the place of contradiction in the history of Christian Neo-Platonism. This project will demonstrate that this historical analysis also has systematic value, for Neo-Platonic concepts can be successfully translated into non-theological terminology. For example, in the place of 'God' one can speak of the ‘Absolute’, and in the place of ‘creation’ one can speak about ‘relative (non-absolute) beings’ such that the three loci of true contradiction can be re-articulated as follows: (i) the being of the Absolute, ii) the methodology by which human beings can know the Absolute and iii) the relationship between the Absolute and relative beings. In the chapter entitled "Absolute Dialetheism" I develop the ideas of the Neoplatonists in non-theological and more secular language. I argue that the absolute exists as a true contradiction, and that nothing relative can exist without implicitly relying upon the contradictory truth of the absolute. I show that whether or not one advances a theory of knowledge by means of concepts or by a trans-conceptual method, knowledge of the absolute must also be contradictory in form. By putting the ideas into conversation with Markus Gabriel's ontology, this chapter shows how the ancient and medieval theories have a role to play in contemporary debates about knowledge and existence. The paper is still forthcoming, and I expect to edit it again, and to include more visible references to the Neoplatonic tradition. Finally, I resolved to investigate how the the systematic connection between mysticism, dialetheism, and rationality can be systematically understood. This objective is achieved in all of the articles I have published. In my articles on Eckhart, I show that reason achieves knowledge of the absolute through the "intellectual understanding." In the writings on Dionysius, I show how he endorses rational silence as the privileged mode of divine knowledge. In the work on Cusa, I show that divine knowledge is achieved by means of the self-transcendence of the discursive reason. Through the experience of the failure of discursive reason, one can intellectually intuit (nous) God as that which transcends language and concepts. I encountered one major obstacle in my investigations. Covid 19 was a major obstacle in the fullfillment of my grant project. I originally planned to host a face-to-face conference at CUHK in 2021 or 2022. Unfortunately, due to COVID 19 this was not possible. Participants would not travel to Hong Kong either due to risks to their own health or because of the quarantine policies. Thus, we held the conference online instead. In order to host an in-person conference, I required funding for accommodations (hotels), flights for keynote speakers, dinners and lunches for the participants, honoraria, and transportation to and from the venue. Due to the planned costs, I originally requested 100,000. Since the conference went online, I no longer had any of these expenses. For this reason, I could not spend the 100,000. I spent as much as was allowed for honoraria for the online speakers, and purchased books for research. Now that the quarantine restrictions are lifted, and travel has resumed, I do expect (and do hope) that I will not encounter this obstacle again in my future grant work. I ask the committee for their understanding on this matter and give my thanks in advance.

This project will demonstrate the systematic connection between mysticism, dialetheism, and rationality. On the one hand, because human reason is governed by the principle of non-contradiction, in order to know the contradictory character of the Absolute, the human being must transcend discursive reason. On the other hand, this project will show that although the true contradictions concerning the Absolute can only be known by transcending discursive reason, I will demonstrate how the transcending of discursive reason in Neo-Platonic philosophy engenders the development of a non-discursive reason (nous) that is compatible with dialetheic utterances.

14621820.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621820.value: Research Outcomes: (I) One published book chapter in the authoritative Tetsugaku series. (II) Two accepted (forthcoming) book chapters in two highly visible and prestigious books series [Synthese Library Book Series and Brill's Studies in the History of Christian Traditions. (III)One translation in a philosophical journal, Comparative and Continental Philosophy. (IV) One journal article currently under review at the Review of Metaphysics, a visible and respected journal of philosophy. (V)One major online conference on Truth and Contradiction in Christian Neo-Platonism that drew experts from around the globe to discuss the truth of contradiction in Christian Neo-Platonism. (VI) One major (week long) workshop at the University of Edinburgh that investigated (for the first time) the history of contradictory theology. The event drew experts from around the world to discuss the history of the concept, with Christian Neo-Platonism at the center of the discourse. Major Findings: 1. Nicolas of Cusa is the most explicit and demonstrable advocate of the dialetheic theory of truth in the Neo-Platonic tradition. He makes explicit what Meister Eckhart recognizes only implicitly.2. Eriugena's commentary on Dionysius in his Periphyseon was a significant contributor to rejection of the truth of contradiction in Christian Neo-Platonism. 3. Although Christian Neo-Platonism and Zen Buddhism have much in common (both advance dialetheic theories of truth), they are fundamentally distinct from each other. While both conceive of the absolute in terms of nothingness, the former preserves the concept of God while the latter does not. The category of relation is privileged by Zen while the concept of substance is privileged in Neo-Platonism. 4. The dialetheic theory of truth in Christian Neo-Platonism has significant relevance for contemporary debates in metaphysics and epistemology, for many of their arguments can be reformulated into secular terms that affect a wider set of fields and disciplines.

Based on my research and the workshop on the history of contradictory theology, I have teamed up with a theologian from the University of Edinburgh (Simon Burton) and Notre Dame (Richard Cross). We are currently editing a volume on the History of Contradictory Theology in the Catholic and Protestant traditions. We plan to submit a book proposal to Oxford or Cambridge University Press. This volume will be the first of its kind. 2. I am also planning a book entitled "The Freedom of Truth" that will heavily draw upon my researches into Christian Neo-Platonism. The book will incorporate key insights from Cusa, Eckhart, and Dionysius, and will show their contemporary relevance.

14621820.value: This research project has both systematic and historical objectives. The systematic objective is to investigate a new concept of truth, according to which there can be inconsistent truths. The historical objective is to inquire into Christian Neo-Platonism, and to investigate whether this tradition advances an inconsistent view of truth. These questions are relevant today because of the recent development of so-called "contradictory theology" recently developed by thinkers such as J.C. Beall, who has published two influential books on the subject with Oxford University Press.

14621920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621920.value: Conspiracy theories are widespread when there is a social crisis. During the anti-extradition bill movement, the Hong Kong society is rife with different conspiracy theories, ranged from “the cover-up of murdered protesters by government and police” to “the CIAs as the mastermind behind the movement.” To be clear, we do not aim at discerning the fact and truth pertaining to the accusations behind the conspiracy theories; instead of making any value judgment of the truth of the conspiracy, our aim is to investigate the antecedents and consequences of conspiracy theories in real life contexts. Indeed, conspiracy beliefs are prevalent across many parts of the world and different times in human history. Studies also have revealed that conspiracy beliefs oftentimes bring about negative rather than positive consequences (e.g., anti-vaccination, anomie, justification of radical political action, etc.). It is thus crucial to uncover the psychological mechanisms and consequences of conspiracy beliefs. This proposed project aims to systematically address these issues by integrating theories from social and cross-cultural psychology. This project seeks to uncover “when” people would believe in “what” specific conspiracy theories. By using a Situation X Person approach, we propose a threat compensation model that considers the joint influence of threat and personal factors on conspiracy beliefs. This model integrates situational (threat) and personal factors (worldview and intuitive thinking) into explaining conspiracy beliefs. We posit that worldview guides what conspiracy theories are more/less believable and intuitive thinking explains who are more/less prone to these theories. We will extend this model by exploring the spillover effect of conspiracy beliefs and the cross-cultural difference in conspiracy beliefs. As to the spillover effect, we posit that belief in one set of conspiracy theories would make people think in a more conspiracist manner. People may thus become susceptible to other threat-irrelevant conspiracy theories. As to the cross-cultural difference, we contend that conspiracy theories, as a group narrative, are more appealing in cultures that emphasize a lay belief of fixed (vs. malleable) social structure. We thus predict that the impact of threat on conspiracy beliefs is also stronger in such cultures. To test these ideas, we propose to conduct four experimental studies and an intervention study. By integrating these insights, this project seeks to build a theoretical framework that can integrate previous findings, generate novel predictions, and open new research directions. Our findings will shed light on developing intervention for combating conspiracy beliefs.

14621920.label: Realisation of objectives
14621920.value: We have realized all the objectives of the current research project. Specifically, we have conducted large-scale cross-sectional and longitudinal studies on conspiracies beliefs in both China and the United States and reported findings in 4 journal articles and 2 conference presentations, and edited a Special Issue on the topic (listed in Part C: Research Output). The overarching goal of the current research is to examine how widespread conspiracy beliefs were formed during social crisis and how such beliefs may have downstream consequences in different cultural contexts. The current project has capitalized on the COVID-19 pandemic, an unfortunate global crisis, and studied the conspiracy beliefs associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition, we have examined conspiracy beliefs related to climate change, which is also an urgent issue that has global significance. Below, we will first elaborate the details of how each objective was addressed; then we will discuss the impacts of the current project. To address Objectives 1 and 2, we analyzed the conspiracy beliefs (CB) related to the COVID-19 pandemic systematically. As a result, we are among the first few research teams to categorize the CB into two types: risk-acceptance CB (e.g., “COVID-19 is a man-made bioweapon”), and risk-rejection CB (e.g., “COVID-19 is a hoax; it is like influenza and was purposefully exaggerated”). Importantly, we found that believing in these two types of CB were systematically related to different level of engagement in disease preventive behaviors in the United States. Specifically, risk-acceptance CB was associated with higher level of preventive behaviors, whereas risk-rejection CB was related to lower level of preventive behaviors. These differential links were mediated by risk perception and negative emotions and modulated by the stage of the outbreak—the risk-acceptance CB predicted higher risk perception in the mild stage, whereas the risk-rejection CB predicted lower risk perception in the severe stage. To address Objective 3, we further extended these findings from the United States to China Mainland. We examined how Chinese participants endorsed the two types of conspiracy beliefs and whether they were related to different levels of national collective narcissism (a belief that one’s own country is superior and other countries have not adequately acknowledged it). We found that the Chinese participants who believed that COVID-19 was a bioweapon made by a foreign country also endorsed a higher level of national collective narcissism and attributed more responsibility of the pandemic to foreign countries. We published these findings in Wang et al. (2021), see Part C. To feature timely research on the topic of conspiracy theories about infectious disease, the PI has edited a special issue on the topic. The introduction of the special issue was published, see Hong et al. (2021) listed in Part C, which featured empirical research on the topic around the world. Specifically, the articles included in the special issue addressed the conspiracy beliefs of samples from a wide range of countries, including China, Chile, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, the United States, and South Korea. This collection of articles thus shows that disease-related conspiracy theories are relevant globally and across Eastern and Western cultures. This Special Issue was recognized as the most highly cited special issue by the Journal of Pacific Rim Psychology. Finally, to address Objective 4, we have conducted two additional studies, one examining conspiracy beliefs about COVID-19, and another about climate change. Through these two studies, we attempted to extend our framework to understand the antecedents of conspiracy beliefs, thereby reducing people’s conspiracy beliefs. First, in Chan, Hong, & Lin (2023; see Part C), we tested if COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs could be more appealing to people with heightened distress, as these theories apparently help people to make sense of the uncertainty and life-threatening disease outbreak. We found that this was not the case. Using the random intercept cross-lagged panel model analysis, we only found a between-person association but not a cross-lagged within-person relationship between the two. The endorsement of COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs was predicted by being more politically conservative in the U.S. context. These findings have implications on interventions that should pay attention to individuals’ personality and political ideologies. In Chan, Tam, & Hong (2023, see Part C), we extended our framework to climate change conspiracy theories. Our study was among the few attempts to examine the links between climate change conspiracy theories and everyday life pro-environmental behaviors longitudinally and in both the U.S. and China context. In both countries, we found consistent evidence that belief in climate change conspiracy theories was related to less engagement in everyday life pro-environmental behaviors concurrently and longitudinally. Our findings suggest that belief in climate change conspiracy theories could have a negative consequence on daily pro-environmental behaviors and highlight the need to understand the impact of such belief beyond the U.S. context. This provides an empirical basis for formulating interventions that combat climate change conspiracy beliefs across national boundaries. For practical impacts, we have applied our findings to understand the antecedent and consequence of conspiracy beliefs, especially across the U.S. and China context with regard to the pandemic. We have explored how some specific, national identities and political factors in the two countries could shape people’s conspiracy beliefs. Our analysis was included in the Introduction to the Special Issue we edited (Hong, Chan, & Douglas, 2021), see listed in Part C. This paper gives practitioners a better understanding of how to combat conspiracy beliefs across cultural contexts. For academic impacts, this project has resulted in 4 journal articles and 1 Special Issue. Some of the journal articles were published in top-tier journals, including Journal of Environmental Psychology (impact factor=6.8) and Social and Personality Psychology Compass (impact factor=4.8). Although all of the papers were published within the last three years, many have already been cited by other researchers in the field. For example, Wong, et al. (2021) has been cited 20 times (according to Google Scholar). All 4 journal articles have been cited 41 times in total already. Copies of these publications are attached in Part C. Aside from publications, this research project has also provided training for young research scholars. Some of them were co-Investigators of the current project. For example, Dr. H-W Chan, who was a postdoctoral fellow under my supervision. He was involved in the current project from start to end – from writing the grant proposal to finally publishing papers. He was the first author in half of the journal articles we published and also a co-editor of the special issue. He is currently an Assistant Professor at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Another example is Ms. Connie P-Y Chiu, who was a Research Assistant in my research team and was a co-author of 2 of the 4 journal articles. She is currently pursuing a PhD degree at The City University of New York.

These individuals also endorsed a higher level of national collective narcissism and attributed more responsibility of the pandemic to foreign countries. We published these findings in Wang et al. (2021), see Part C. (2) Hong et al (2021, see Part C) explained the three motives of believing in COVID-19 conspiracies. They are epistemic motives, i.e., reducing uncertainty; existential motives, i.e., defending against the threat of death; social motives, i.e., belonging to social groups. These motives were found to predict vaccination hesitation and disease preventive behaviors. (3) Chan, Hong, & Lin (2023, see Part C) tested if COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs could be more appealing to people with heightened distress, as these theories apparently help people to make sense of the uncertainty and life-threatening disease outbreak. We found that this was not the case. Using the random intercept cross-lagged panel model analysis, we only found a between-person association but not a cross-lagged within-person relationship between the two. The endorsement of COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs was predicted by being more politically conservative in the U.S. context. (4) Chan, Tam, & Hong (2023, see Part C) extended our framework to climate change conspiracy theories. In both the U.S. and China, we found consistent evidence that belief in climate change conspiracy theories was related to less engagement in everyday life pro-environmental behaviors concurrently and longitudinally. Our findings provide an empirical basis for formulating interventions that combat climate change conspiracy beliefs across national boundaries.

14621920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621920.value: We found that people endorsed specific COVID-19 conspiracy theories that were consistent with their political ideologies and national identity, and such conspiracy theories were significantly linked to disease preventive behaviors. We then extended our framework to examine the conspiracy theories about climate change, and found that endorsing such beliefs also predicted less engagement in everyday life pro-environment behaviors. Moving forward, we can examine the interaction between climate change conspiracy theories and global warming. While people across the world are experiencing hotter summers, there is still a considerable number of people who believe that climate change is a hoax. It thus raises the question of whether the experience of local temperature anomalies would influence people’s beliefs about climate change conspiracy. We expect that the experience of temperature anomalies would serve as a cognitive proxy that counteracts the hoax conspiracy narratives and thus would be negatively related to belief in such narratives. Finally, conspiracy theories about the Presidential election in the U.S. have soared in the past few months before the election. We can leverage on this opportunity to understand how believing in those beliefs get spill over to other types of conspiracies, such as climate change related conspiracy theories.

14621920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621920.value: Infectious disease outbreaks and epidemics are a hotbed of conspiracy theories; the COVID pandemic is no exception. The threat of getting sick or dying, the fear of uncertainty, misinformation, and mistrust in vaccines or treatment methods are all factors that play a role in spreading infectious diseases conspiracy theories. Unfortunately, just like a highly contagious virus, the faster a conspiracy theory spreads and infects a community, the harder it is to correct or eliminate it. In our project, we have examined how conspiracy theories about COVID-19 were related to individuals’ political ideologies and national identity, and in turn linked to disease preventive behaviors. Aside from the pandemic, we also found that conspiracy theories about climate change were related to people’s daily life pro-environmental behavior, such that those who felt that climate change was a hoax were less engaging in everyday pro-environmental behaviors. These findings were replicated in both the U.S. and China context. These findings were reported in 4 journal articles, 1 Special Issue and 2 talks at international conferences. Taken as a whole, our research findings shed light on understanding of conspiracy theories in Chinese and North American cultural contexts, and help practitioners to formulate interventions.

15100120.label: Project Objectives
15100120.value: The FIRST OBJECTIVE is to provide mechanistic evidence for the direct effects of TBS of healthy and presumed neuropathological prefrontal cortex. Specifically, we aim to assess excitability modulations of prefrontal oxy-haemoglobin (HbO) by TBS of the DLPFC in patients with MDD compared to healthy controls (HC). The hypotheses associated with this aim are: H1: iTBS will lead to an average increase in prefrontal HbO and cTBS will lead to an average decrease in HbO directly after stimulation, compared to baseline. Rationale: H1 is based on previous concurrent rTMS/fNIRS studies showing increased HbO directly after HF rTMS and decreased HbO directly after LF rTMS in HC [8, 9]. Hence, we aim to expand our knowledge by probing HbO modulations upon TBS, and investigating them in the diseased (MDD), in addition to the healthy human brain (HC). H2: Average changes in prefrontal HbO will also occur during stimulation, compared to baseline. Rationale: H2 is kept undirected given inconsistencies among previous results [8, 10] and our pilot data (Figure 3 vs. 5). H3: Stimulation will lead to an increased variance in HbO responses during and after stimulation compared to baseline. Rationale: H3 is based on previous research indicating significant individual variability in brain responses during and after brain stimulation [5, 6, 11-13]. H4: Individuals with MDD have a lower variability in TBS-induced HbO modulations compared to HCs. Rationale: H4 is based on evidence suggesting reduced neural plasticity and blunted cortical reactivity in MDD (e.g., [14, 15]). In other words, we hypothesize that patients with MDD are less sensitive to neuromodulatory effects of TBS compared to HCs [6]. The SECOND OBJECTIVE is to evaluate the relationship between immediate excitability modulations of the DLPFC and treatment response and thus provide a novel biomarker for individual patient selection. The hypothesis associated with this aim is: H5: Larger TBS-induced HbO changes in the DLPFC are associated with a better antidepressant response [6]. Rationale: H5 is based on evidence in support of the neural plasticity theory of MDD [14, 15]. We assume that individual variation in HbO responses to TBS primarily reflect individual differences in cortical excitability, in addition to structural variation, measurement reproducibility and the current neural state of the stimulated area [7]. Therefore, we hypothesize that individual variability in TBS-induced HbO modulations reflects the individual capacity to neural plasticity and hence predicts the individual variability in antidepressant response. As a first working hypothesis, we assume that stronger iTBS-induced HbO modulations (in terms of a mean increase within one min. post stimulation in the left DLPFC) predict a better antidepressant response. This is based on recent evidence that stronger responses in motor cortex excitability modulations (30s after stimulation) predict the individual antidepressant response of two weeks of rTMS treatment [6]. In addition, we postulate that HbO modulations in response to cTBS during and after stimulation contains crucial information for response prediction. Moreover, imaging endpoints will not be restricted to mean HbO values within one minute after stimulation but also include global and local amplitude maxima, duration of HbO increases, variability in HbO response and steepness in TBS induced modulations, among others (see section on data analysis below).

15100120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15100120.value: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) with theta bursts (i.e. TBS) of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is an innovative treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD). Indeed, the U. S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has only recently approved TBS (in August 2018). However, fewer than 50% of patients show sufficient response to this treatment; markers for response prediction are urgently needed. Moreover, there is a lack of knowledge of the mechanism of action of TBS of the DLPFC. This is due to difficulties of directly measuring prefrontal stimulation effects, as compared to the stimulation of motor cortex and utilizing motor evoked potentials as direct readout. However, knowledge of immediate DLPFC modulation by TBS is necessary to extrapolate downstream effects on the neural and symptoms level. Thus, there is a need for research that aims to quantify the direct and immediate after-effects of TBS on DLPFC function. Most importantly, with regard to precision medicine, there is a need for research that explores the utility of immediate DLPFC reactivity to TBS for the prediction of antidepressant treatment response. There is common agreement that certain forms of rTMS inhibit or excite brain activity, respectively. However, evidence indicates that there is considerable individual variability in the brain responses to rTMS. Whether differences in individual DLPFC modulation by rTMS can be utilized as a predictive marker for treatment response remains to be investigated. Here, we propose a research program that will exploit the combination of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) with brain stimulation. Concurrent TBS/fNIRS measurements will allow us to systematically investigate TBS-induced modulation of blood oxygenation as a proxy for induced brain activity changes. The findings from this study will (1) elucidate the immediate effects of excitatory and inhibitory TBS on prefrontal activity in TBS treatment-naïve patients with MDD and (2) validate the potential utility of TBS-induced brain modulation at baseline for the prediction of antidepressant response to four weeks of daily TBS treatment. Major depression is a severe mental disorder and is associated with considerable economic costs but adequate treatments are poorly explored. This research program will pave the way towards an affordable and easy-to-implement method for response prediction before treatment commencement. Thus, our research proposal has high potential to inform tailored treatment strategies, as envisaged in precision medicine. 摘要： 作用於背外側前額葉皮層（DLPFC）的間歇性的重複經顱磁刺激（rTMS）（即TBS）是治療重度抑鬱症（MDD）的一種新型方式。事實上，TBS最近得到了美國食品藥品監督管理局（FDA）認可（2018年8月）。然而，只有不到50%的病人對這種治療方式有反應，所以能預測是否有反應的標記物是所急需的。此外，TBS作用於DLPFC背後的機制也尚未明確。這是因為相對於運動皮層的刺激，效果可以直接從觀察的運動引出情況。可是，作用於前額葉的刺激效果則很難被觀察和測量。然而，必須瞭解TBS調控DLPFC的即時效果，才能對神經和症狀水準的繼發影響做出推斷。所以，需要開展旨在量化TBS作用於DLPFC後的直接功能和影響的研究。更重要的是，從精準醫學來考量，這是有必要開展利用TBS作用於DLPFC的即時反應來預測抗抑鬱結果的研究。現在普遍認為不同劑量的rTMS 可以啟動或抑制大腦活動。然而，有證據表明大腦對於rTMS 的反應存在很大的個體差異。因此，rTMS 對DLPFC調控的個體差異能否被用作治療效果的預測還是有待研究。 在這項研究計畫中，我們將會在功能性近紅外光譜技術（fNIRS）和腦刺激同時使用時進行探索。同時使用TBS和fNIRS的測量可以使我們更加有系統地研究TBS所引發的血氧狀態的調節情況，以作為其誘發大腦活動改變的指標。這項研究的結果將會（1）闡明興奮性和抑制性TBS對未接受過TBS治療的MDD患者的前額葉活動的即時影響（2）驗證TBS在基線時所引發的大腦調控能力，對於4周的TBS的抗抑鬱的治療有潛在的預測功能。 重度抑鬱是一種嚴重的精神障礙，並會為社會帶來較大的經濟損失，但仍缺少對於有效的治療方法的探索。這個項目將會為以後的治療開始前，開展一個低成本和易於實施的預測方法的相關研究提供一個參考。所以，我們的研究計劃具有極高的潛力，可以為精凖醫學所設想的定制治療策略提供參考。

15100120.label: Realisation of objectives
15100120.value: The first objective was to assess prefrontal brain excitability in response to TBS applied to the DLPFC in patients with MDD and HCs, and to provide mechanistic evidence for the effects of prefrontal TBS by investigating the hemoglobin concentration responses evoked by the stimulation. The second objective was to evaluate the relationship between baseline TBS-induced prefrontal hemoglobin responses and treatment outcomes, thereby contributing to the development of individualized treatment approaches. Both objectives were fully achieved (100%). To gain a comprehensive understanding of prefrontal TBS effects using a concurrent TMS/fNIRS setup, we also conducted a series of accompanying studies. These included a cross-diagnostic meta-analysis of TMS effects across various symptom domains, as well as three pilot studies demonstrating that concurrent TMS/fNIRS is a feasible setup. These pilot studies also highlighted the importance of considering intra- and inter- individual factors to ensure robust results. During the main experimental phase, aimed at achieving the two proposed objectives, we included 44 participants with MDD and 45 HCs. Both groups underwent baseline concurrent TMS/fNIRS measurements (including iTBS/fNIRS and cTBS/fNIRS). The MDD group subsequently received 20 sessions of iTBS treatment targeting the left DLPFC. Contrary to Hypotheses 1 and 2, we observed a statistically significant increase in HbR, rather than HbO, both during and immediately after iTBS and cTBS in both groups. Notably, these findings were replicated across multiple concurrent TMS/fNIRS experiments using different samples and fNIRS devices (Kan et al., 2025; Kan et al., 2024; Xia et al., 2025). Consistent with Hypothesis 3, we observed increased variance in HbO responses both during and after stimulation compared to baseline. Specifically, one of our pilots showed that baseline sex differences in prefrontal hemoglobin concentrations were amplified by iTBS, but not by cognitive tasks (Kan et al., 2024). Partially consistent with Hypothesis 4, participants with MDD exhibited lower variability in cTBS-induced HbO responses compared to HCs. Interestingly, this difference in variability was not observed for iTBS, and the reason for this remains unclear. Nevertheless, response variability can be influenced by various factors, including genetics, hormonal fluctuation, time-of-day (Corp et al., 2020; Wansbrough et al., 2024). Whether such influencing factors only pertain to some hemoglobin markers (HbO) but not others (HbR), and whether they differentially come into play for different stimulation protocols needs further investigation. In line with Hypothesis 5, our study demonstrated that baseline TBS-induced hemodynamic responses, combined with two demographic features, reliably distinguished responders from non-responders following four weeks of iTBS treatment. Interestingly, patients whose brains showed a greater decrease in HbO following iTBS exhibited better treatment outcomes, consistent with previous fMRI-BOLD findings (Smith et al., 2014). In summary, both objectives were successfully achieved. Robust TBS-induced prefrontal hemodynamic responses were observed during and after stimulation. These signals provided valuable information for predicting antidepressant treatment response, highlighting their potential as predictive imaging markers.

15100120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15100120.value: To begin, we conducted two meta-analyses summarizing the treatment efficacy of TMS across various symptom domains. We found that rTMS demonstrated a large effect size for craving and a medium effect for depressive symptoms (Publications No. 2, 5). In addition, we explored potential therapeutic mechanisms through a scoping review, which revealed that TMS may elevate serum serotonin levels (Publication No. 3). To gain a deeper understanding of the therapeutic effects of TBS targeting the DLPFC, we developed a concurrent TBS/fNIRS setup. Our findings showed that both intra-individual factors (e.g., caffeine intake, stimulation time, daily mood) and inter-individual factors (e.g., sex, age, education years) influenced TBS-evoked prefrontal hemoglobin responses, as reported in Publication No. 6, 9, and 10. These influences were also highlighted in our review (Publication No. 8). Notably, a significant increase in HbR was consistently observed during and after stimulation across several experiments. Following this, we investigated whether TBS-induced prefrontal hemoglobin responses could serve as predictive markers for treatment outcomes following four weeks of iTBS antidepressant therapy. As a foundation, we conducted a meta-analysis of neurophysiological and neuroimaging markers associated with rTMS for depression. The results indicated that no consistent predictive marker has yet been established (Publication No. 7). Given that acute cortical hemodynamic responses evoked by a standard daily iTBS session (i.e., 600 pulses) provide immediate feedback on the neurophysiological effects of therapeutic stimulation, we explored their predictive potential. We found that iTBS-induced prefrontal excitability did not predict subsequent working memory performance following a single iTBS session in HCs (Publication No. 11). Nevertheless, the potential of TBS-evoked responses as predictors of symptom improvement remains promising. Our study demonstrated that baseline TBS-induced hemodynamic responses together with two demographic features could reliably predict treatment outcomes after four weeks of iTBS in patients with depression (Publication No. 12). Additionally, changes in individual TBS-induced hemodynamic responses after treatment were significantly correlated with symptom reductions (Publication No. 13).

15100120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15100120.value: Firstly, the cross-diagnostic meta-analysis focusing on left DLPFC-rTMS across various symptom domains has attracted significant attention and demonstrated strong clinical application potential. Building on this, we are currently expanding the meta-analysis to compare the efficacy of left versus right DLPFC-rTMS on different symptoms. This aims to provide clear evidence to guide treatment protocol selection based on symptom profiles. Secondly, given the novelty of our current TMS/fNIRS setup and the unexpected nature of our findings, our work has sparked considerable discussion. We are now conducting two additional experiments to further validate our results. The first involves a concurrent TMS/fNIRS/fMRI setup to replicate the observed prefrontal hemodynamic responses to TBS-DLPFC. The second uses the gold-standard motor evoked potentials (MEPs) method to determine whether TBS-induced hemoglobin responses accurately reflect brain excitability. Thirdly, we are conducting an accelerated form of TMS treatment on a depression patient using the concurrent TMS/fNIRS setup, aiming to track hemodynamic response dynamics during treatment and explore links between these changes and daily clinical outcomes. Lastly, to investigate whether brain state during stimulation affects TBS responses, we are conducting an experiment using concurrent TMS/fNIRS combined with emotionally relevant auditory stimuli.

15100120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15100120.value: In the field of brain stimulation for depression, a major challenge is the lack of real-time information about how the brain, specifically the prefrontal cortex, responds during stimulation. This novel setup that combines brain stimulation (TMS) with brain monitoring (fNIRS) allows us to see how the brain reacts during stimulation. In this project, we summarized how TMS works across different mental health conditions and showed that it is possible to safely and effectively measure brain activity during TMS. Most importantly, we found that the brain's response to TMS could help predict how well a person with depression responds to the treatment. This is a step toward more personalized and effective care. Our research has attracted attention in the scientific community. For example, our team is frequently invited to present this work at international conferences, meetings and webinars. There is also growing interest in studying real-time brain responses to TMS, suggesting that our findings are pioneering and point to an important new direction in understanding how TMS works. More research with larger groups of patients is still needed to confirm these promising results.

15101520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15101520.value: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is an alarming public health problem. The global prevalence of NAFLD in the general population has been estimated at up one in four adults. Obesity, diabetes and dyslipidaemia are common risk factors of fatty liver. Abnormal fat accumulation in the liver is usually symptomless at the early stages, but if untreated, simple fatty liver will eventually lead to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), or even hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Liver transplantation is required for end-stage of NAFLD-related diseases. The exact mechanism causing disease progression is still unclear. Therefore, it is of great importance to understand the molecular mechanism and to explore new targets for the development of diagnostic tests and cost-effective therapies. Previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) strongly suggested that Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase Receptor Type D (PTPRD) is associated with various cancers and metabolic diseases, especially for the susceptibility and severity of HCC and NAFLD in recent studies. However, the function of PTPRD in hepatic lipid metabolism and its potential roles in the progression of liver damage have not been explored. In this study, we will (1) provide comprehensive experimental evidence to demonstrate the role of PTPRD in preventing fatty liver and progression of liver damage; (2) define the molecular mechanism underlying the repression of hepatic PTPRD in obese subjects; and (3) explore whether the chronic downregulation of hepatic PTPRD will promote the progression of NAFLD-related diseases such as NASH and HCC. Our findings will provide new insights in the pathogenesis of NASH and HCC in NAFLD and help the development of new therapeutic and preventive strategies. 据估计，NAFLD在普通人群中的全球患病率高达25%。NAFLD是包括单纯性脂肪变性 [非酒精性脂肪肝 (NAFLD)，无肝细胞损伤的脂肪变性] 、脂肪性肝炎 (NASH，脂肪变性伴肝细胞炎症和球囊变性) 、肝纤维化、肝硬化，甚至肝细胞癌 (HCC)在内的一系列疾病。高热量的饮食、久坐不动的生活方式和遗传易感性是NAFLD最重要的一些诱因。慢性过量的肝脂肪积累可通过脂毒性、氧化应激、炎症和细胞凋亡等多种机制对肝脏造成损害。然而，单纯脂肪变性发展为伴有纤维化、肝硬化甚至肝细胞癌的非酒精性脂肪性肝炎 (NASH)的机制尚不清楚。明确NAFLD的发病机制和发展机制是开发新的治疗方法和预防策略的必要条件。 NAFLD在肝组织严重受损、不可逆转时才会出现症状。因此，许多病人直到他们预后很差的时候才被诊断出来。虽然进行某些检测可能有助于判断脂肪变性的程度，如一些肝功能、血清标记物和影像技术，但它们并非特异性的。要想获得NASH的明确诊断，肝脏活检是必要的，因此NASH的非侵入性诊断显得尤为重要。许多肝硬化和HCC患者可能最终需要肝脏移植。在美国，治疗NAFLD及其相关并发症的经济负担每年超过1000亿美元。对香港来说，虽然没有治疗非酒精性脂肪肝的经济负担估算，但根据香港成人有脂肪肝的百分比来估计的同时，考虑到非酒精性脂肪肝在香港的高流行率，管理治疗它及其并发症的成本将是巨大的。随着NAFLD患病率的不断上升，需要准确、无创的方法来提高对NAFLD的风险预测和对NAFLD不同阶段的诊断。 NAFLD发展为肝癌的遗传易感性已被提出，但具体涉及的基因仍不清楚。我们对新出现的全基因组关联研究进行了分析，并假设蛋白酪氨酸磷酸酶受体D (PTPRD)在肝脂质积累和促进肝纤维化和癌症中发挥作用。在本研究中，我们将探究PTPRD在肝脏脂质代谢中的作用，探索其表达作为NAFLD及相关肝脏疾病的血清生物标志物的可行性。对NAFLD中NASH和HCC发病机制的新认识或将为NAFLD的治疗和预防策略提供依据。

15101520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15101520.value: Objective 1: Using a DIO mouse model, we evaluated the impact of hepatic PTPRD knockdown on lipid metabolism. Our findings revealed that while PTPRD knockdown primarily disrupted glucose regulation, it did not significantly affect hepatic lipid profiles. Specifically: • Hepatic PTPRD knockdown impaired glucose tolerance in STC mice. • Overexpression of PTPRD in DIO mouse livers restored glucose homeostasis. • Neither knockdown nor overexpression of hepatic PTPRD altered liver lipid content or metabolism within a one-month monitoring period. Importantly, the N-terminal cleavage product of PTPRD plays a central role in liver-pancreatic cross-talk, regulating insulin secretion and highlighting its mechanistic link to systemic glucose homeostasis. Objective 2: Building on prior evidence that PTPRD expression is regulated by promoter DNA methylation, we identified CTCF (CCCTC-binding factor) as a key repressor of PTPRD in DIO mice. Key findings include: • CTCF Binding and Regulation: CTCF binds to the PTPRD promoter with higher affinity in fed versus fasting states. Although feeding and fasting did not alter PTPRD mRNA levels, DIO mice showed significantly increased CTCF binding at the promoter compared to lean controls. • DNA Methylation Sensitivity: CTCF binding is methylation-sensitive, consistent with its role in genomic imprinting. • Functional Validation: Mutation of the CTCF cis-element in the PTPRD promoter increased transcriptional activity, confirming its repressive role. Luciferase assays validated that CTCF directly represses PTPRD expression. These findings demonstrate that CTCF-mediated repression of PTPRD in DIO mice occurs via a methylation-sensitive mechanism. Objective 3: We explored the role of PTPRD in liver disease progression, focusing on its involvement in the transition from steatosis to NASH and HCC. Key findings include: • Dysregulated glucose metabolism and insulin signaling were the primary metabolic phenotypes associated with altered PTPRD expression. • A two-hit model combining long-term PTPRD knockdown with N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) treatment in DIO mice over three months exacerbated liver damage and metabolic dysfunction, demonstrating PTPRD’s role in advancing liver disease. In summary, PTPRD is crucial for glucose metabolism and liver-pancreatic cross-talk, with transcriptional regulation mediated by CTCF. While hepatic lipid metabolism is largely unaffected, PTPRD is a potential therapeutic target for improving glucose homeostasis and mitigating liver disease progression.

15101520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101520.value: This study highlights the critical role of PTPRD in glucose metabolism and liver-pancreatic cross-talk, mediated by the cleavage of its N-terminal segment, soluble PTPRD (sPTPRD). Previous research has linked PTPRD single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) to type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Investigating sPTPRD and its associated SNPs could provide valuable insights for patient stratification and the development of personalized therapeutics for metabolic diseases and liver cancer. The role of sPTPRD as a potential mediator of liver-pancreatic signaling warrants further exploration. sPTPRD may serve as a biomarker for glucose homeostasis and insulin regulation. Understanding its influence on glucose metabolism and cross-organ signaling could pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic dysfunction. To expand on these findings, long-term studies using genetic models of PTPRD SNPs and sPTPRD manipulation are essential. These models should evaluate metabolic outcomes and the progression of fatty liver to NASH and HCC. Additionally, clinical studies measuring sPTPRD levels in patients with metabolic disorders could validate its potential as a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker. This integrated approach will deepen our understanding of PTPRD’s role in metabolic regulation and its translational potential in therapeutic development.

15101520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101520.value: Our research focuses on understanding the role of a gene called PTPRD in regulating blood sugar levels and its connection to liver health. PTPRD is a key player in how the liver communicates with the pancreas, which is vital for controlling insulin and maintaining normal blood sugar levels. We found that when PTPRD is reduced in the liver, it disrupts the body’s ability to regulate blood sugar, even though it doesn’t significantly affect fat buildup in the liver over a short period. Interestingly, a part of the PTPRD protein, called sPTPRD, appears to act as a messenger between the liver and pancreas, influencing how much insulin is released. In addition, variations in the PTPRD gene, known as SNPs, have been linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and liver cancer. By studying these genetic variations and the role of sPTPRD, we aim to uncover new ways to predict and treat these conditions. This research could lead to better tools for diagnosing metabolic diseases and identifying individuals at risk. It also opens the door to new treatments that target PTPRD or sPTPRD to improve blood sugar control and prevent liver-related complications.
