15102020.label: Realisation of objectives
15102020.value: 1. Functional characterization of CDK6 in the regulation of liver T-ICs (100%) i. To study the effects of CDK6 modulation on the T-IC phenotypes To examine whether CDK6 functionally drives self-renewal and tumor formation, we first manipulated CDK6 expression in HCC cells using lentiviral-based knockdown and the CRISPR/dCas9-VP64-p65-Rta gene activation system (Dharmacon). Using a limiting dilution assay, CDK6 knockdown significantly reduced the stem cell frequencies of MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells. In contrast, CDK6 overexpression enhanced the stem cell frequency of PLC/PRF/5 cells. In an in vivo tumorigenicity assay, knockdown of CDK6 significantly reduced the size and number of tumors formed. Consistent with our findings, CDK6 overexpression in PLC/PRF/5 cells significantly enhanced tumorigenicity with an increase in the estimated CSC frequency. ii. To study the effects of CDK6 modulation on HCC metastasis and drug resistance Using migration and invasion assays, overexpression of CDK6 increased the migration and invasion abilities of HCC cells; while opposite effects were observed upon knockdown of this protein. Given that CDK6 upregulation was found in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells, we investigated whether CDK6 suppression resulted in the sensitization of HCC cells to lenvatinib treatment. Annexin-V staining demonstrated decreased survival and reduced resistance to these drugs following CDK6 knockdown. In contrast, CDK6 overexpression conferred drug resistance in PLC/PRF/5 cells. In a panel of HCC cells with variable degrees of CDK6 expression, there was a positive correlation between CDK6 levels and lenvatinib resistance. The survival-enhancing effect of CDK6 was kinase dependent as transfection of the kinase-dead mutant, CDK6-K43M, did not rescue the apoptotic effect of lenvatinib treatment. Likewise, palbociclib, a CDK4/6 inhibitor, showed a synergistic effect when combined with lenvatinib. To further confirm that the sensitization effect of palbociclib is not dependent on CDK4, we examined the combination effect of PROTAC against CDK6 (CP-10 and BSJ-03-123) with lenvatinib in HCC cells. The MTT assay indicated that both CDK6 PROTAC degraders suppressed the growth of lenvatinib-resistant PLC/PRF/5 and Huh7 cells in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, we found that Palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor) combined with lenvatinib results in maximal tumor growth suppression in a lenvatinib-resistant HCC xenograft model and lenvatinib-resistant Trp53KO/MYCOE HCC mouse model. Specifically, Palbociclib remodeled of immune landscape after combined treatment with palbociclib and lenvatinib which favors immune suppression against HCC tumors. iii. To characterize CDK6 in the regulation of the liver T-IC phenotype by a cell sorting approach Using overexpression and knockdown approaches, alterations in CDK6 changed the expression levels of four known liver CSC markers namely, CD47, CD90, CD133, and EpCAM and pluripotency-related markers including SOX2 and OCT4. 2. Elucidation of the molecular mechanism by which CDK6 functionally contributes to tumor initiation, self-renewal, and drug resistance (100%) i. CDK6 upregulation is mediated by ERK/YAP signaling in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells CDK6 is upregulated by YAP, which is regulated by ERK1/2, in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells. Elevated levels of pERK1/2 and YAP were observed alongside increased CDK6 expression. Treatment with MEK and YAP inhibitors reduced CDK6 and YAP levels. Confocal microscopy confirmed the colocalization of ERK, YAP, and CDK6 in resistant cells. Additionally, qRT-PCR analysis showed that CDK6 mRNA was upregulated in these cells, correlating with YAP1 and ERK2 levels in clinical HCC samples. ii. CDK6 directly binds and phosphorylates GSK3β, leading to Wnt/β-catenin activation STRING analysis of the kinome profiles in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells showed that CDK6 had a potential protein-protein interaction with GSK3β. We examined this interaction using reciprocal immunoprecipitation in high-CDK6-expressing MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells. Immunoprecipitation assays confirmed a physical interaction between CDK6 and GSK3β, with GSK3β being a direct substrate for CDK6, evidenced by its phosphorylation at Ser9. This interaction was further confirmed in lenvatinib-resistant PLC/PRF/5 xenografts using confocal IF microscopy. Western blot analysis demonstrated that suppression of CDK6 inhibited phospho-GSK3β (Ser9) and β-catenin expression, while CDK6 overexpression had the opposite effects. CDK6 knockdown increased β-catenin ubiquitination and reduced transcription of Wnt target genes, while overexpression yielded opposite results. Additionally, β-catenin knockdown decreased survival and lenvatinib resistance in HCC cells, confirming its role as a downstream effector of CDK6. 3. To evaluate the correlation of CDK6 expression with prognostic and clinicopathological factors, liver T-ICs and drug resistance in human HCC (100%) By analyzing the GSE25097 dataset, a publicly available dataset, we found a stepwise increase in CDK6 expression from normal to cirrhosis to progressive HCC stages, suggesting an oncogenic role for CDK6 in liver carcinogenesis. To further confirm CDK6 overexpression in HCC, we used a tissue microarray consisting of 50 HCC samples and the corresponding matched nontumor liver tissue samples to evaluate CDK6 expression by immunohistochemical staining. Patients with high CDK6 expression had shorter disease-free survival (p=0.0412, respectively; log-rank test) and a higher recurrence rate (p=0.0078). To further examine whether the role of CDK6 in lenvatinib resistance is clinically relevant in HCC, we have examined CDK6 expression in tumors of seven HCC patients who received lenvatinib treatment. Among these patients, four of them were categorized as lenvatinib-sensitive while the remaining three were lenvatinib-resistant according to RECIST assessment. Upon analysis, we observed a significant upregulation of CDK6 in lenvatinib-resistant HCC patients when compared with sensitive group, further verifying the role of CDK6 in driving lenvatinib resistance in HCC. 15102020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15102020.value: Resistance to molecularly targeted drugs, such as tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), poses a significant challenge in cancer therapy, limiting long-term survival for many patients. Evidence suggests that cancer cells can acquire drug resistance by re-wiring kinase signaling pathways in response to TKIs. Measuring protein kinase expression on a large scale is technically challenging due to their dynamic range in the human proteome. In this study, we investigated this re-wiring mechanism in lenvatinib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells using a novel lysine-targeted sulfonyl fluoride probe, X044, which binds to 133 endogenous kinases. Our analysis revealed that CDK6 was the most prominently upregulated kinase in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cell lines. Functional studies indicated that CDK6 plays a crucial role in acquired lenvatinib resistance by enhancing liver cancer stem cells (CSCs), highlighting its clinical significance. During lenvatinib resistance development, CDK6 re-wiring occurs via the ERK/YAP1 signaling cascade. We identified a novel non-canonical pathway where CDK6 binds and regulates GSK3β activity, activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Inhibition of CDK6 using Palbociclib or degradation via proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) synergized with lenvatinib in both in vitro and in vivo immune-deficient mouse models, remodeling the immune landscape to favor immune suppression against HCC tumors. Overall, our findings reveal the relationship between CDK6 and GSK3β as a driving force behind CSC expansion and TKI resistance. Targeting the ERK1/2/YAP1/CDK6/GSK3β/β-catenin pathway may provide a promising strategy to enhance TKI treatment efficacy in HCC. Our research is both scientifically important and clinically relevant, conveying several key messages: (1) We used a novel chemical approach to profile human kinases in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells; (2) CDK6 overexpression correlates with poorer patient survival; (3) CDK6 regulates cancer stemness; (4) CDK6 re-wiring is mediated via the ERK/YAP1 pathway; (5) CDK6 regulates GSK3β, activating the Wnt/β-catenin pathway; (6) Combining lenvatinib with Palbociclib remodels the immune landscape; and (7) Targeting CDK6 with Palbociclib enhances lenvatinib's effect in HCC.

15102020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102020.value: Acquired resistance to cancer therapies often arises from changes in kinase activity, a phenomenon known as kinase rewiring. In this study, the authors utilized a broad-spectrum chemical probe to conduct kinome screening, identifying the accumulation of cancer stem cells mediated by cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) as a key factor driving resistance to lenvatinib, a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor, in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The successful development of this probe opens new avenues for detecting kinase alterations in various drug-resistant cell lines across different cancer types. This capability allows researchers to gain insights into the mechanisms of drug resistance in diverse cancers. Furthermore, this innovation can be applied to elucidate the functional roles of kinases in various cell types and diseases.In this proposal, we clearly demonstrate that targeting CDK6 can sensitize HCC cells to lenvatinib, potentially paving the way for new treatment regimens for this challenging cancer. Moving forward, it would be valuable to explore new CDK6 inhibitors in combination with lenvatinib, particularly using in vitro HCC organoid models, to further assess their efficacy and develop more effective therapeutic strategies.

15102020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102020.value: Researchers have found that cancer cells can become resistant to treatments due to changes in their protein kinases, which makes therapy less effective. Measuring these kinases in large numbers can be difficult, but a new chemical biology method allows scientists to study 133 kinases in liver cancer cells that resist a drug called lenvatinib. They discovered that cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) is increased in these resistant cells and plays a significant role in promoting the survival of liver cancer stem cells. CDK6 interacts with another protein, GSK3β, activating a pathway that encourages cancer growth. When they inhibited CDK6 using a drug called palbociclib, it worked well with lenvatinib, showing better results in lab tests. This combination not only slowed tumor growth but also improved the immune response around the tumor. Overall, this research highlights CDK6 as a potential target for new treatments in drug-resistant liver cancer and showcases innovative methods to study how cancer adapts to therapies.

15102220.value: 背景：結核病是傳染病中死亡率最高。結核性腦膜炎是該病最嚴重的表現，致命率亦最高。早期研究發現，一些結核分枝桿菌的菌株會傾向侵襲人類的中樞神經系統，因此被稱為“高毒力菌株”。 早前，我們的團隊使用多組學（即基因組，轉錄組和蛋白質組學）分析來鑑定高毒力菌株的獨有突變。這些突變會導致與結核分枝桿菌毒力相關的基因網絡中RNA表達和蛋白質合成失調。我們亦證明了這些突變會增強結核分枝桿菌在人類巨噬細胞內的存活力。然而，這些遺傳因素如何促進宿主內結核性腦膜炎的發展仍是未知的。 假設：高毒力菌株在巨噬細胞內的存活率提高，利用巨噬細胞為載體，以“特洛伊木馬”的方式穿透宿主的血腦屏障。 目的：闡明高毒結核分枝桿菌菌株引起結核性腦膜炎的致病機制。 設計：分別從香港，上海和埃塞俄比亞的結核性腦膜炎患者中收集了三種高毒結核分枝桿菌菌株。與其他臨床分離株相比，這些菌株顯示出在巨噬細胞內增強的存活力。 （i） 我們將比較多組學分析的數據來確定高毒力菌株的潛在毒力決定因素。具有相同系統發育譜系的低毒力結核分枝桿菌菌株將在所有的組學分析中用作對照。我們將選擇在高毒力菌株獨有的，並且會導致RNA表達和蛋白質合成失調網絡中的基因突變進行病因驗證。 （ii） 我們將使用多重熒光斑馬魚-海洋分枝桿菌模型驗證相關基因在形成結核性腦膜炎發中的致病作用。首先，在海洋分枝桿菌中的基因同源物將被敲除或過表達。在感染具有紅色熒光巨噬細胞和綠色熒光血管的轉基因斑馬魚胚胎之前，我們將用藍色熒光蛋白轉化野生型和基因敲除的海洋分枝桿菌菌株。細菌散佈，血腦屏障橫穿和肉芽腫形成的過程可以在熒光顯微鏡下觀察到，並在野生型和基因敲除菌株之間進行比較。 意義：該項目不僅將鑑定與增強的巨噬細胞內存活相關的突變，而且還將表徵其在由高毒性結核分枝桿菌菌株引起的結核性腦膜炎發病機理中的致病作用。旨在將其作為開發針對結核病的新療法和新疫苗的知識基礎。

15102220.label: Realisation of objectives
15102220.value: In this project, three hypervirulent M. tuberculosis clinical strains were collected from Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Ethiopia. These strains were isolated from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of young, HIV-negative patients who experienced aggressive disease progression from pulmonary tuberculosis to tuberculous meningitis. Compared to 115 other clinical isolates, these strains demonstrated enhanced intracellular growth in both human peripheral blood mononuclear cell-derived macrophages (PBMDMs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), confirming their hypervirulent phenotype. Based on 24-loci MIRU-VNTR typing, the strains belong to Beijing Lineage 2.2.1 (H112), Euro-American Lineage 4.6 (H107), and East-African-Indian Lineage 3 (H108). Comparator strains with similar phylogenetic backgrounds (>1 locus difference in MIRU-VNTR typing) but low intramacrophage survivability were selected as controls. Objectives 1-3: Multi-omics Analysis Comparative whole-genome sequencing identified 12 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 3 indels commonly shared among the three hypervirulent strains from different geographical locations. Of particular interest is a 2-bp deletion in the intergenic region rv0759c-rv0760c, which serves as a binding target for a putative regulator of phoP. Previous studies have established phoP as a global transcriptional regulator controlling lipid metabolism and hypoxic response, influencing approximately 2% of genes in M. tuberculosis. RNA sequencing was performed to characterize expression profiles of hypervirulent strains and low-virulent comparators during macrophage infection. Comparative transcriptional analysis revealed 493 differentially expressed transcripts common to all hypervirulent strains. To validate RNA-seq results, 15 genes were selected for RT-qPCR quantification based on their association with hypervirulent-specific mutations identified in whole-genome sequencing data and their significant expression differences between hypervirulent strains and respective comparators. RT-qPCR analysis confirmed the differential expression patterns observed in RNA-seq data. Eight of the fifteen genes harboring hypervirulent-specific SNPs showed significant differential expression, including higB. Up-regulation of higB resulted in universal repression of at least eight genes responsible for iron acquisition in M. tuberculosis. Additionally, phoP, located adjacent to the rv0759c-rv0760c intergenic deletion, was up-regulated in all hypervirulent strains. Notably, expression of various key reporter genes regulated by phoP was greatly suppressed, including those encoding sulfolipid and polyacyltrehalose biosynthesis. Label-free quantitative LC-MS/MS was conducted to characterize differential proteomes in hypervirulent strains. A total of 3,200 peptide ions were detected across all strains, which were annotated to 1,189 known proteins from reference strain M. tuberculosis H37Rv using the Mascot algorithm (FDR < 0.01 with two or more peptides per protein). Of these 1,189 proteins, 387 showed differential abundance with log2 fold-changes ranging from -4.9 to 6.45. Proteomic data corroborated RNA-level findings. PhoP showed significant increase in hypervirulent strains, resulting in strong repression of at least eight gene products regulated by PhoP, including pks2 and pks3, which are involved in acyltrehalose lipid biosynthesis such as sulfolipids and polyacyltrehalose lipids. The multi-omics analysis successfully identified key virulence factors that may account for the hypervirulent phenotype of M. tuberculosis, achieving objectives 1-3. Objective 4: Construction of Mycobacterium marinum Mutants A blue-fluorescent, phoP-overexpressing M. marinum mutant (TMm) was constructed by transforming the recombinant pVV16:phoP:BFP plasmid into M. marinum using electroporation. PCR-Sanger sequencing confirmed the presence of both phoP and blue fluorescent protein (bfp) genes in transformants. Fluorescent microscopy validated blue fluorescent protein expression. To determine phoP mRNA levels in transformants, RNA was extracted from broth cultures of both TMm and wild-type M. marinum (WMm) strains and analyzed using qPCR. Results showed that phoP expression in TMm was approximately 3-fold higher than in WMm (P=0.0241). Growth curve experiments were conducted for WMm and TMm strains to determine the effects of differential phoP expression on in vitro M. marinum growth. Objective 4 was successfully achieved. Objective 5: Bacteriological and Pathological Features in Zebrafish Model Survival Rate Analysis Three groups of zebrafish were injected with TMm (n=19), WMm (n=19), and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) (n=19) and monitored for 15 days to compare infection virulence based on survival rates. TMm-infected zebrafish showed lower survival rates (36.8%) compared to WMm-infected zebrafish (68.4%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (P=0.0809). Neurotropism Assessment Three groups of zebrafish were infected with TMm (n=64), WMm (n=64), and PBS (n=58), respectively. Zebrafish were monitored for gross infection signs and sacrificed upon showing moribund behavior. Brain tissues were collected from deceased, sacrificed, or euthanized zebrafish (day 30 post-infection) for histopathological analysis, including acid-fast bacilli (AFB) microscopy (n=52) and bacteriological culture (n=12). AFB microscopy detected bacilli in brains of 23.1% (12/52) and 5.8% (3/52) of zebrafish infected with TMm and WMm, respectively. Bacillary load in TMm-infected brain tissue was more abundant than in the WMm group. Using a semi-quantitative grading system, bacillary loads in TMm-infected zebrafish brains ranged from few (2+) to numerous (4+), while WMm infections were limited to rare (1+) and moderate (3+) levels. AFB culture was performed on brain tissues from 12 zebrafish infected with each strain. In the WMm group, one zebrafish (8.3%) was culture-positive with a bacterial load of 8 CFU/mL. In contrast, six TMm-infected zebrafish (50.0%) were positive, with bacterial loads ranging from 8-192 CFU/mL. Mycobacterial recovery from TMm-infected zebrafish brains was higher than from WMm-infected brains (P=0.0706). No growth was observed in PBS-injected controls. Combining AFB microscopy and culture results, 6.25% (4/64) of WMm-infected zebrafish developed brain infection, whereas 28.13% (18/64) of TMm-infected zebrafish had brain infection (P=0.0018), demonstrating that phoP-overexpressing M. marinum is significantly more neurotropic than the wild-type strain. Pathological Features Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining of brain tissue sections revealed granuloma-like lesions or immune cell aggregates in TMm-infected zebrafish (n=4 of 11 examined), but not in WMm-infected zebrafish. TMm strains were also found in brain-adjacent tissues, causing infiltration of distorted cells, while no structural changes were observed in similar regions of WMm-infected zebrafish. Immunohistochemical staining confirmed blue fluorescent protein expression in brain tissues, verifying the presence of bfp-transformed M. marinum strains. Anti-L-plastin antibody staining identified aggregated leukocytes in granuloma-like lesions in TMm-infected zebrafish brain tissue. Mortality and Brain Infection Association Among deceased WMm-infected zebrafish (n=16), only one (6.25%) was AFB-positive in brain tissue. In contrast, 47.37% (9/19) of deceased TMm-infected zebrafish had detectable brain AFB (P=0.0098), with 77.8% (7/9) dying within seven days post-infection. Mycobacterial Dissemination in Transparent Zebrafish Thirty transparent zebrafish were injected with blue fluorescent WMm (n=12), TMm (n=12), and PBS (n=6), then examined using fluorescence stereomicroscopy throughout infection. Among WMm-infected zebrafish, 50% (6/12) and 16.7% (2/12) developed blue fluorescent aggregates in bodies and brains, respectively, on average days 7 and 16. In the TMm group, 58.3% (7/12) showed body signals and 41.7% (5/12) developed brain signals on average days 6.6 and 12.4, respectively. Total aggregated blue fluorescent signals in TMm-infected zebrafish bodies (n=112) exceeded those in the WMm group (n=54). Two aggregated signals were detected in WMm-infected brains versus eight in TMm-infected brains. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that TMm exhibits greater neurotropism compared to WMm, indicating that increased phoP expression enhances mycobacterial virulence in CNS infections. Objective 5 was successfully achieved.

15102220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15102220.value: This study identified specific molecular mechanisms underlying M. tuberculosis hypervirulence through analysis of three clinical strains that caused rapid progression from pulmonary TB to tuberculous meningitis. The key discoveries provide precise insights into mycobacterial neurotropism and virulence regulation. Genomic Discovery: Comparative sequencing identified 15 genetic variants (12 SNPs and 3 indels) conserved across all three hypervirulent strains from different continents. The critical finding was a 2-bp deletion in the rv0759c-rv0760c intergenic region, which directly affects phoP regulation. Molecular Mechanism: Multi-omics analysis revealed that phoP upregulation triggers a specific regulatory cascade. RNA-seq identified 493 differentially expressed genes, with phoP upregulation causing repression of eight iron acquisition genes through higB activation. Proteomic analysis confirmed this pathway, showing differential abundance in 387 proteins with phoP-regulated lipid synthesis genes (pks2, pks3) significantly suppressed. Functional Validation: The engineered M. marinum strain with 3-fold increased phoP expression (TMm) provided direct evidence for phoP's role in virulence. This strain demonstrated enhanced neurotropism compared to wild-type controls. Quantified Neurotropism: In zebrafish infection experiments, TMm caused brain infection in 28.13% of animals versus 6.25% for wild-type (P=0.0018), representing a 4.5-fold increase. Bacterial loads in infected brains ranged 8-192 CFU/mL for TMm compared to a single case with 8 CFU/mL for wild-type. AFB microscopy detected bacilli in 23.1% of TMm-infected brains versus 5.8% for controls. Mortality Association: Brain infection strongly correlated with death. Among deceased zebrafish, 47.37% of TMm-infected animals had brain involvement compared to 6.25% of wild-type infected animals (P=0.0098). Most TMm-associated deaths (77.8%) occurred within seven days. Clinical Relevance: The study established phoP as a quantifiable biomarker for mycobacterial neurotropism. The 2-bp deletion and resulting phoP upregulation provide a specific genetic signature that predicts enhanced CNS invasion capacity, offering a molecular explanation for the aggressive clinical progression observed in the original patient cases. This research provides actionable targets for developing diagnostics to identify high-risk TB cases prone to meningeal dissemination and potential therapeutic interventions targeting the phoP regulatory pathway.

15102220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102220.value: Our findings demonstrate that phoP overexpression significantly enhances intracellular growth of M. tuberculosis in human macrophages and promotes central nervous system invasion in zebrafish models. These results establish phoP as a critical virulence determinant and validate it as a therapeutic target for developing first-in-class antivirulent tuberculosis drugs. Based on these discoveries, we hypothesize that pharmacological suppression of phoP expression could impair intramacrophage survival of M. tuberculosis, facilitating host immune system eradication of bacteria. This antivirulent approach offers advantages over traditional bactericidal drugs by potentially reducing resistance development and enhancing immune clearance. Our research strategy involves conducting structural studies of phoP protein to identify druggable binding sites, followed by high-throughput screening of compound libraries using our established M. marinum reporter system. We prioritize screening FDA-approved drug libraries to enable rapid clinical translation through drug repurposing approaches. Building on this foundation, we proposed a new General Research Fund project aimed at discovering and validating small-molecule compounds as anti-virulence agents against M. tuberculosis. This project was successfully approved and commenced in 2024 (GRF#15100422), providing resources to advance phoP-targeted therapeutic development from basic discovery toward clinical application for treating hypervirulent tuberculosis strains.

15102220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102220.value: Research Objective: This study investigated hypervirulent M. tuberculosis clinical isolates from patients who experienced rapid progression from pulmonary tuberculosis to tuberculous meningitis, aiming to identify genetic determinants of enhanced virulence and central nervous system invasion. Key Findings: Comparative genomic analysis of three geographically distinct hypervirulent strains revealed 15 conserved genetic variants, including a critical 2-bp deletion in the rv0759c-rv0760c intergenic region affecting phoP regulation. Multi-omics approaches (RNA-seq, quantitative proteomics) demonstrated that phoP upregulation triggers a regulatory cascade involving 493 differentially expressed genes and 387 proteins with altered abundance. Mechanistically, elevated phoP expression activates higB, leading to repression of iron acquisition genes, while simultaneously suppressing lipid biosynthesis pathways (pks2, pks3) involved in cell wall lipid production. Experimental Validation: Using an engineered M. marinum model with 3-fold phoP overexpression, zebrafish infection studies quantified enhanced neurotropism (28.13% vs 6.25% brain infection rate, P=0.0018) and increased mortality correlation with CNS involvement (47.37% vs 6.25%, P=0.0098). Clinical Significance: The identified phoP regulatory network provides mechanistic insights into mycobacterial virulence and establishes genomic biomarkers for predicting CNS dissemination risk. This research offers translational opportunities for developing both diagnostic assays for risk stratification and antivirulent therapeutic strategies targeting the phoP regulatory pathway.

15103520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103520.value: 肺癌是香港和世界範圍內最常見的癌症死亡原因。晚期非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）的標準治療方法之一是放射治療。當前的放射療法基於解剖學影像，而沒有考慮事實上肺組織的異質，尤其是肺癌患者的肺功能在不同部位存在顯著差異。功能影像引導放療是一種新興技術，可以有選擇地避免照射功能性好的肺區域，有望減少輻射引起的肺損傷。在實施功能影像引導的放療中，肺功能影像有多種選擇。當前，肺通氣（V）和肺灌注（Q）影像的臨床標準是單一光子發射計算機斷層掃描（SPECT）。然而，SPECT不是放療的常規影像，需要另外掃描，耗費更多臨床資源，增加病人負擔。為了克服這些困難，我們提出在此項目中開發一種新型的，人工智能（AI）輔助的，基於放療計劃計算機斷層掃描（CT）的肺功能影像（V / Q）合成方法。首先，我們將開發AI輔助的肺功能影像方法。基於先前採集的SPECT / CT圖像集，我們將開發完全卷積網絡的分層綜合深度學習模型（HSFCN）用以提取CT圖像內潛藏的肺功能信息，從而學習如何從CT 重建V / Q圖像。然後，我們會通過一項肺癌患者的前瞻性研究並利用轉移學習來調整和優化HSFCN模型。最後，我們將評估AI輔助肺功能影像方法的潛在臨床療效。與目前的肺功能影像方法相比，我們的方法更簡單，更快速，成本更低，並且更易於臨床實施功能影像引導放療。憑藉這些獨特的優勢，我們的方法將有望加快和擴大功能影像引導放療的臨床應用。最終，它可以減少放射線誘發的肺損傷，改善肺癌的治療結果，使得香港及全球的肺癌患者受益。

15103520.label: Realisation of objectives
15103520.value: We have largely achieved all objectives without encountering major challenges. Functional lung avoidance radiotherapy (FLART) represents a cutting-edge advancement in radiotherapy, particularly for lung cancer applications. Our development of CT-based pulmonary function imaging techniques—including artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted synthesis, 4DCT deformable image registration (DIR)-based methods, and combined texture-anatomy approaches are all considered novel and world leading. Notably, our AI-assisted perfusion (Q) imaging technique stands as the first and most advanced of its kind, as demonstrated by journal publications and recognitions. A key limitation of our study thus far is the relatively small patient cohort, which falls short of the extensive dataset typically required for robust deep learning model development. To mitigate this, we have explored transfer learning strategies to optimize training with limited sample sizes. For ventilation (V) imaging, we have pioneered multiple innovative methods, including AI-driven, DIR-based, and hybrid texture-anatomy techniques. These approaches provide multifaceted insights into pulmonary ventilation dynamics. Most importantly, our synthesized functional images have been successfully integrated into treatment planning, demonstrating promising potential to enhance lung function preservation in patients.

15103520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103520.value: We developed a novel deep learning-based computed tomography (CT) perfusion mapping (DL-CTPM) method for estimating perfusion-based lung functional images from the CT domain using a 3-dimensional attention residual neural network, which yielded moderate-to-high voxel-wise approximations of lung perfusion. The evaluation of the voxel-wise agreement showed a moderate-to-high voxel value correlation (0.6733 ± 0.1728) and high structural similarity (0.7635 ± 0.0697) between the SPECT and DL-CTPM predicted perfusions. To address the limitation of the small sample sizes and the generalizability of the deep learning-based model, we have explored transfer learning strategies to optimize training with limited sample sizes. The fine-tuned model yielded a high voxel-wise correlation (0.8142 ± 0.0669) and outperformed the pre-trained model by approximately 8%. We have developed three different methods for ventilation generation from CT images, including artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted synthesis, 4DCT deformable image registration (DIR)-based methods, and texture-anatomy approaches. Our AI-assisted method using a dual-path-aware neural network via combining anatomical information and motional information, achieved a voxel-wise correlation value of 0.70 (0.53~0.82). The DIR-based method was built based on the ventilation process. It captured both spatial and temporal heterogeneity changes over the respiratory cycle with voxel-wise correlation values of 0.600–0.561 across different cohorts. Our texture-anatomy approaches combined the texture and the pulmonary segments of the lung to generate the ventilation image from CT images, the voxel-wise correlation values were 0.60 ± 0.10 and 0.72 ± 0.05 for the patient with tumor blockage of the airway. We conducted a study investigates the impact of lung function images generated based on our methods on radiation pneumonitis prediction using a dual-omics (radiomics features (R), dose features (D)) analysis method. The study demonstrated that our functional images enhanced radiation pneumonitis prediction. The function-wise lung (FWL) model outperformed whole-lung (WL) analysis (AUC: 0.885 ± 0.028 vs. 0.762 ± 0.053, p < 0.001). We introduced an automated planning framework (AP-FLART) integrating functional data to redirect dose from high- to low-function lung regions. AP-FLART supports both contour-based (cFLART) and voxel-based (vFLART) optimization. Compared to conventional plans, cFLART reduced high function lung (HFL) mean dose by 1.13 Gy (p < 0.001) and V20 by 2.01% (p < 0.001); vFLART reduced functionally weighted mean lung dose and F20 by 0.64 Gy (p < 0.01) and 0.90% (p = 0.099), respectively.

15103520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103520.value: There are future developments to improve the performance of the research. First is to establish multi-institutional collaborations to significantly expand patient recruitment, which will not only enhance the statistical power of our findings but also improve model generalizability across diverse populations and treatment settings. Second, building upon our current technical achievements, we will develop an integrated V/Q optimization framework that simultaneously incorporates both ventilation and perfusion data into treatment planning, creating a more physiologically accurate representation of lung function for dose redistribution. Third, for cases involving tumor-induced airway obstruction, we will implement advanced modeling techniques to account for functional distortions in blocked regions, coupled with adaptive planning protocols to modify treatments in response to anatomical and functional changes during therapy. Last, a rigorously designed prospective clinical trial is needed for evaluating multiple endpoints: reduction in radiation pneumonitis incidence (validating our predictive models), quantitative assessment of functional lung sparing (dosimetric advantages), and longitudinal monitoring of pulmonary function preservation. This systematic, patient-centered approach - progressing from technical refinement to clinical implementation - will ensure our innovations translate into meaningful improvements in lung cancer radiotherapy outcomes while establishing a foundation for future research in functional image-guided adaptive radiotherapy.

15103520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103520.value: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer deaths globally. While radiotherapy is a crucial treatment, it often damages healthy lung tissue and impairs breathing function. To address this, we've developed an innovative "smart radiotherapy" system (FLART) that uses artificial intelligence to create detailed lung function maps from standard CT scans - showing both air flow (ventilation) and blood flow (perfusion) patterns. These advanced maps allow doctors to precisely target tumors while protecting the healthiest portions of the lung. Our breakthrough includes several world-first technologies: AI systems that accurately predict lung function from routine scans, automated treatment planning tools that intelligently redirect radiation away from functional areas, and new methods to predict and potentially prevent treatment-related lung damage. Early results demonstrate our approach can significantly reduce radiation exposure to working lung tissue, which may help patients maintain better breathing capacity after treatment. The next phase will expand testing across multiple hospitals and conduct clinical trials to confirm these patient benefits. This research represents a major step forward in making lung cancer radiotherapy both more precise and safer, with the potential to transform treatment standards worldwide and improve quality of life for countless patients.

15104520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104520.value: 使用非侵入性工具以高精準度調控特定神經元的活動對於理解大腦神經迴路和治療腦部疾病具有巨大的價值。現有的策略（例如，深部腦刺激，光遺傳學，經顱磁刺激，經顱電刺激等）具有其自身的優點，但是它們或者是侵入性的或者缺乏足夠的時空精度。因此，神經刺激不容易成功或伴有嚴重的副作用。 超聲腦刺激是一種令人鼓舞的新方法，具有無創性、良好的時空精度和穿透深的優點。被認為是一種大有前途的研究腦功能和治療腦疾病的方法。但是，超聲波束的焦點比單個神經元或一小群神經元大得多，因此當前的超聲刺激方法缺乏針對特定神經元或神經迴路的精確度，並且不容易預測刺激結果。因此，使超聲腦刺激實現對選定神經元的精準調控是其中的關鍵問題。 用於腦刺激的超聲強度低，關鍵的生物效應可能基於“機械敏感”離子通道。 “機械敏感”離子通道是細胞感受生物力的關鍵組成部分。我們的初步結果和最近發表的論文直接證實了超聲可以控制神經元和體內小鼠大腦中的機械敏感離子通道（例如Piezo1，MscL），這奠定了超聲神經刺激的重要研究基礎。因此，超聲刺激的選擇性可能依賴於通過使用遺傳修飾方法將機械敏感性蛋白插入選定的神經元來改變神經元的超聲敏感性，實現類似於光遺傳學的聲遺傳方法。 在這項研究中，我們計劃開發一種新的策略，通過操縱機械敏感蛋白在深部腦區特定神經元的表達，實現超聲敏感性調控，並在動物模型中實現選擇性超聲刺激。我們將根據時空精度，生物安全性以及合適的運動行為範式來驗證選擇性超聲刺激方法的特點。 這項研究的成功將為腦刺激研究帶來突破性的創新，為無創、深部選擇性腦刺激技術提供一種關鍵的腦刺激方法。該策略將為超聲腦刺激開闢一個新的領域，從而對與公共衛生相關的精神疾病和神經系統疾病產生重大影響，包括阿爾茨海默氏病，帕金森氏症和抑鬱症等。它也可能成為基礎神經科學中極為有用的研究工具。

15104520.label: Realisation of objectives
15104520.value: We examined the direct effect of MscL-sonogenetics on dSTR neuronal activation by measuring fluorescence changes of jRGECO1a (genetically-encoded calcium sensor with red fluorescence) in real-time using fiber photometry (FP). Neurons in the right dSTR were simultaneously transduced by hSyn-promoted jRGECO1a and EYFP-only, MscL-WT-EYFP or MscL-G22S-EYFP AAVs (Fig. 1A). We observed robust expression of EYFP and jRGECO1a colocalized in dSTR neurons (Fig. 1B). Four to five weeks post-transduction, the mice were transcranially stimulated with short US pulse train (parameters shown in Fig. 1C and acoustic intensity profile shown in Supplementary Fig. 1) and an optical fiber was used to monitor fluorescence intensity. Prior to US stimulation, both groups showed comparable levels of baseline fluorescence (Peak ΔF/F0 for EYFP = 1.21 ± 0.31%, MscL-WT = 1.35 ± 0.24% and MscL-G22S = 1.771 ± 0.47%, Fig. 1D, E). However, upon delivery of one 0.05 MPa pressure US pulse train, MscL-G22S expressing neurons showed a rapid and significant increase in jRGECO1a fluorescence intensity compared to EYFP-only or MscL-WT neurons (Peak ΔF/F0 for EYFP = 1.85 ± 0.52%, MscL-WT = 1.37 ± 0.23%, MscL-G22S = 4.857 ± 1.47%, Fig. 1D). Fluorescence responses to US in the MscL-G22S dSTR regions were 2.63-fold of the response from the EYFP dSTR. Acoustic pressures from 0.05 MPa – 0.2 MPa reliably evoked dSTR neural activity in MscL-G22S mice, and a generalized pattern of dose-dependence was observed (Fig. 1E). In contrast, the EYFP or MscL-WT expressing mice showed a small fluorescence change comparable to spontaneous activity after US stimulation. The latency range of neuronal responses in MscL-G22S expressing neurons was 327.3 ±29.05 ms to 341.7 ± 21.65 ms (Fig. 1F). To further evaluate the spatial targeting of our scheme, anesthetized mice were treated with US for 40 minutes and their brains were stained for the neural activation marker, c-Fos. Robust EYFP expression was seen in the dSTR of both EYFP-only and MscL-G22S mice (Fig. 1G). Average c-Fos expression in dSTR was found to be significantly higher in the stimulated side of the MscL-G22S mice (87 ± 8 c-Fos+ cells) than in the contralateral side of the same mice (11 ± 2 c-Fos+ cells) or in mice expressing only EYFP (stimulation side = 14 ± 3, contralateral = 8 ± 2 c-Fos+ cells) (Fig. 1H). Crucially, we found that the cortical regions located directly above the dorsal striatum on the stimulation side did not show a significantly higher level of c-Fos (Fig. 1H). This indicated that our setup was able to focus the effects of US in the region expressing MscL-G22S and not surrounding areas, consistent with our previous results. This is especially important because a single element plane traducer with a diameter of 5 mm was used, meaning that the cortical neurons above the dSTR were unavoidably sonicated as the ultrasonic waves propagated through the brain. The upregulation of c-Fos being restricted to the region of MscL-G22S expression clearly demonstrates the gain-of-function role of the mechanosensitive mediator in sonogenetics. We also stained for c-Fos in the auditory cortex of the brain slices and observed comparable c-Fos between EYFP and MscL-G22S mice (Supplementary Fig. 3). Thus, we confirmed MscL-sonogenetics could specifically activate neurons in the targeted dSTR of anesthetized mice. We next tested whether the MscL-sonogenetics was effective enough to modulate the expected asymmetric locomotion in freely-moving mice. A wearable US transducer was attached above the virally-transduced dSTR in freely moving mice and their locomotion was recorded during US stimulation (Fig. 2A, B). To prevent indirect activation of the auditory pathway rather than direct activation of motor circuits in awake mice, we sonicated the animals with both rectangular waveform and smooth waveform envelope (Fig. 2C), given the smooth waveform of ultrasound stimulation has been shown to minimize the auditory confound. Robust EYFP or MscL-G22S-EYFP signals were observed in the right dSTR region (Fig. 2D) confirming successful viral expression. Mice were then treated with ultrasound in an open field box and their movement behaviors were recorded and analyzed. Ultrasound stimulation consisted of three epochs (pre-stimulation (“Pre”), ultrasound stimulation (“US”), post-stimulation (“Post”). MscL-G22S expressing mice were seen to obviously increase their locomotion activity during both rectangular and smooth waveform ultrasound treatment, compared to negligible change for EYFP mice (Fig. 2E). The mobility speed of the MscL-G22S mice increased, while the EYFP mice did not show obvious change (Fig. 2F, H). MscL-G22S mice moved greater distances during the periods of US stimulation than EYFP mice (Fig. 2G, I). EYFP mice also showed small increases in their motor activity during higher US stimulation, but the magnitude of these changes was small. Stimulation with smooth waveform of MscL-G22S mice showed more activities compared to rectangular waveform, supporting that the auditory confound could be minimized by smooth waveform to enhance the sonogenetic effect. Thus, MscL-sonogenetics in the dSTR could effectively induce significant motor responses of awake mice, consistent with previous optogenetic neuromodulation targeting the same region. Taken together, our findings suggest that MscL-sonogenetics can specifically stimulate neurons in the dSTR and induce the characteristic asymmetric locomotion behavior. We next tested the feasibility of using MscL-sonogenetics to control higher-level behavior by targeting more specific neurons. The VTA was chosen as it is a midbrain reward center where the dopaminergic circuit is well-defined and involved in various reward related behavior and diseases [20]. In order to test whether MscL-sonogenetics could target specific circuits, dopaminergic (DA) VTA neurons were selectively made to express MscL-G22S. We used a dual-viral vector strategy: one vector delivered Cre recombinase under the modulation of a tyrosine hydroxylase promoter (TH-promoter), the other delivered a Cre-recombinase-dependent EYFP or MscL-G22S-EYFP fragment (Fig. 3A). Confocal imaging confirmed that TH+ neurons overlapped with EYFP or MscL-G22S-EYFP in the VTA region (Fig. 3B) indicating successful expression of MscL-G22S in dopaminergic neurons. We tested whether MscL-sonogenetics could specifically modulate appetitive conditioning using the real-time place preference assay. Habituated mice were placed in a rectangular open field box with two distinct chambers, one paired with US stimulation, the other paired without US stimulation (NUS), and mice could move freely between chambers (Fig. 3C). Mice were wearing a transducer aimed at the VTA. US stimuli were triggered immediately when a mouse entered the US chamber and turned off immediately when the chamber was exited. Unexpectedly, we found that US stimulation induced aversive responses in EYFP mice starting at 0.07 MPa (Supplementary Fig. 4A, B). In addition, increasing acoustic pressure to 0.16 MPa in EYFP mice induced further aversive behavior (Supplementary Fig. 4B). At the same time, MscL mice spent approximately equal time in both chambers for all pressures tested. Thus, we found that low US intensities affected appetitive condition in EYFP mice but not MscL-G22S mice, which might be due to non-specific stimulation of the VTA or auditory coufound. Meanwhile, we conducted the real-time place preference test with smooth waveform US. The smooth waveform US was delivered to mice for the duration of their stay in the stimulation chamber. Upon making this change, we found no significant aversive effect in either group, while MscL mice spent an increased proportion of time in the stimulation-paired side with increasing US pressure 0.04 MPa - 0.12 MPa. Thus, we found that sonogenetic stimulation of MscL-G22S expressing mouse VTAs could specifically modulate appetitive conditioning.

15104520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104520.value: The present study demonstrates an MscL-G22S-mediated sonogenetic approach capable of stimulating specific neural circuits with high spatiotemporal precision, providing a noninvasive way to modulate higher behaviors in mouse models. Our setup proved capable of activating neurons and modifying characteristic motor behaviors and appetitive conditioning in conscious mice through the administration of low-intensity ultrasound. Real-time recording of neuronal responses to US pulse train in deep-brain regions of MscL-G22S mice through FP showed the rapid and reversible neuronal activation triggered by MscL-sonogenetics. Mutant MscL-G22S sensitizes neurons to ultrasound more effectively than wild-type MscL. The latency of fluorescence change was consistent between the genetically encoded calcium and dopamine sensors in the two regions, at ~300 ms. Although the temporal resolution of sonogenetics could not be determined by patch clamp, due to its incompatibility with ultrasonic vibrations, the quick responses measured by FP suggest a subsecond temporal precision. Moreover, MscL-sonogenetics could elicit well-defined behaviors through specific activation of established neural circuitry. Finally, the present study demonstrates the noninvasive sonogenetic modulation of the specific brain circuit in parkinsonian mice to alleviate the motor symptoms. Our stimulation scheme showed good spatiotemporal resolution when targeted to brain regions at different depths, without obvious nonspecific activation and responses closely synchronized with US stimuli.

15104520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104520.value: Choosing a different transducer or ultrasound parameters, different brain region, or a different cell type for targeting could allow the study of other aspects of brain function. The discovery and development of other mediating molecules, such as other mechanosensitive ion channels or nonchannel transmembrane proteins, could provide ways to stimulate desired regions with ultrasound. It could also be possible to further reduce the invasiveness of the treatment by making use of genetic technologies. For instance, the AAV-PHP.eB virus has been shown to be capable of transducing cells in the brain through mere tail-vein administration. Such a system could be used to preferentially transduce targeted cells in the brain while also possibly reducing the need to deliver the virus directly into the brain. Finally, we found MscL-sonogenetics to be compatible with FP and free-moving recording without significant interference and crosstalk. Thus, integration of these important techniques could help for comprehensive study of the brain and how it works. For instance, sonogenetics could further be used with fMRI, a well-established technique, and could thus enable screening and dissection of neural circuits in large animals, e.g., nonhuman primates. Thus, sonogenetics offers an adaptable, modular approach that is amenable to integration with other modalities, which could allow for wide-ranging study.

15104520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104520.value: Noninvasive control of neuronal activity in the deep brain can be illuminating for probing brain function and treating dysfunctions. Here, we present a sonogenetic approach for controlling distinct mouse behavior with circuit specificity and subsecond temporal resolution. Targeted neurons in subcortical regions were made to express a mutant large conductance mechanosensitive ion channel (MscL-G22S), enabling ultrasound to trigger activity in MscL-expressing neurons in the dorsal striatum and increase locomotion in freely moving mice. Ultrasound stimulation of MscL-expressing neurons in the ventral tegmental area could activate the mesolimbic pathway to trigger dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens and modulate appetitive conditioning. Moreover, sonogenetic stimulation of the subthalamic nuclei of Parkinson’s disease model mice improved their motor coordination and mobile time. Neuronal responses to ultrasound pulse trains were rapid, reversible, and repeatable. We also confirmed that the MscL-G22S mutant is more effective to sensitize neurons to ultrasound compared to the wild-type MscL. Altogether, we lay out a sonogenetic approach which can selectively manipulate targeted cells to activate defined neural pathways, affect specific behaviors, and relieve symptoms of neurodegenerative disease.

15104620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104620.value: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is a devastating neurodevelopmental disorder with increasing prevalence worldwide. Because its etiology remains unknown, there is no cure for ASD. Identifying risk factors for ASD could inform novel developmental interventions for ASD. Adding to the limited knowledge about single-gene mutation causes, environmental factors are now understood to be as risk factors for ASD. Emerging clinical data has indicated that prenatal or postnatal chronic exposure to PM2.5 is associated with increased risk of having ASD children. Chronic exposure to PM2.5 induces system inflammatory responses, and neuroinflammation is thought to be a neurobiological basis for impaired neurodevelopment in ASD. Our previous work using a genetic Fragile X syndrome mouse model of ASD has shown that impaired hippocampal neuroplasticity is associated with behavioral deficits, similar to that observed in ASD patients. On the other hand, increasing hippocampal neuroplasticity via ani-inflammatory antibiotic minocycline improves behavioral outcomes. Based on these observations, we hypothesize that long-term exposure to PM2.5 during pregnancy is a significant risk factor for having offspring displaying autism-related behaviors, possibly by inducing neuroinflammation response, which consequently leads to impaired hippocampal neuroplasticity, and the resultant autistic-like behavior in the offspring. In this study, we aim to investigate how PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy affects brain structure and neural functions in the male and female offspring, and how this effect would be transmitted to offspring via neuroinflammation and hence generate adverse effects on the offspring’s brain health. The study will not only shed light on a viable model for explaining the increasing trend of common developmental disabilities in humans by air pollution, but will also provide knowledge that could lead to the development of effective and novel preventative measurements. 自閉症譜系障礙（ASD）是一種破壞性神經發育障礙，在世界範圍內患病率呈上升趨勢。由於其病因仍然未知，因此無法治愈ASD。確定ASD的危險因素可以為ASD新型乾預措施的開發提供信息。除了關於單基因突變原因的有限知識外，現在還認為環境因素是ASD的危險因素。例如，新出現的臨床數據表明，產前或產後慢性暴露於PM2.5與增加ASD兒童的風險有關。長期暴露於PM2.5會引起系統炎症反應，而神經炎症被認為是ASD神經發育受損的神經生物學基礎。我們以前使用ASD的基因脆弱X綜合徵小鼠模型進行的研究表明，與ASD患者相似，海馬神經可塑性受損與行為缺陷有關。另一方面，通過苯胺類抗生素米諾環素增加海馬神經可塑性可改善行為預後。基於這些觀察，我們假設懷孕期間長期暴露於PM2.5是後代表現出自閉症相關行為的重要危險因素，可能是通過誘導小膠質細胞介導的神經炎症反應，從而導致海馬神經可塑性受損，以及後代中類似自閉症的行為。在這項研究中，我們旨在研究懷孕期間暴露於PM2.5會如何影響後代的大腦結構和神經功能，以及這種影響將如何通過神經炎症傳播給後代，從而對後代的神經發育產生不利影響。該研究不僅將為闡明人類由於空氣污染導致的一般性發育障礙的增長趨勢提供一個可行的模型，而且還將提供可能導致有效和新穎的預防策略發展的知識。

15104620.label: Realisation of objectives
15104620.value: Aim 1: Determine whether maternal exposure to PM2.5 induces autism-like behaviors in the mouse offspring Results achieved: We have completed this part with behavioral tests for male and female offspring with dams exposed to PM2.5. Six behavioral tests were conducted to assess social behavior, memory performance and depression/anxiety-like behavior. Maternal exposure to PM2.5 impaired behaviors in adult male and female offspring. In three chamber social interaction test, all offspring mice spent significantly more time sniffing the unfamiliar stimulus mouse compared to the empty chamber, indicating a strong preference for the chamber containing the mouse. Maternal PM2.5 increased exploration index in both male and female offspring, suggesting maternal PM2.5 affected sociability in both male and female offspring. In the social novelty test, male offspring but not female offspring from dams with maternal PM2.5 exposure showed significantly higher exploration ratio to the stimulus mouse. There was no significant difference in exploration index among groups but a decreased trend decreased, suggesting maternal PM2.5 had a tendency to affect social novelty in both male and female offspring. To assess repetitive behavior using the marble burying test, no statistically significant differences in the number of buried marbles between groups. However, the data indicate a strong trend toward an increase in buried marbles in the PM2.5-exposed groups, suggesting increased repetitive behavior in offspring with maternal PM2.5 exposure. Maternal PM2.5 significantly reduced exploration index in male offspring, indicating impaired working memory compared to control male offspring. In contrast, PM2.5 exposure did not significantly affect working memory in female offspring compared to controls. Spatial memory was evaluated using the Y-maze test. Two-way ANOVA of the exploration index showed significant gender and treatment effects, but not interaction effect. There were no significant differences in exploration index. There was no difference in locomotor activity, time spent in the center and forced swimming test, indicating PM2.5 exposure did not affect mood-related behavior. Aim 2: Determine whether maternal exposure to PM2.5 impairs hippocampal structural and synaptic plasticity in mouse offspring Results achieved: We found that maternal exposure to PM2.5 enhanced hippocampal cell proliferation and mature neurons, showed no effect on number of newborn neurons, but reduced dendritic branching of newborn neurons and impaired synaptic plasticity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus. Our findings indicate that maternal exposure to PM2.5 significantly increased the number of Ki67+ cells and NeuroD+ cells in the hippocampal dentate gyrus of offspring, but did not affect number of newborn DCX+ cells. Sholl analysis revealed that maternal PM2.5 exposure impaired dendritic development immature neurons undergoing dendritic maturation specifically in female offspring, but no effect on male offspring. Golgi-Cox staining demonstrated that maternal exposure to PM2.5 did not affect the density of dendritic spines in the hippocampal DG region in either male or female offspring. Electrophysiology recording showed that maternal exposure to PM2.5 impaired hippocampal synaptic plasticity in both male and female offspring. Field recording revealed that maternal exposure to PM2.5 resulted in a significant reduction in LTP in both male and female offspring.The basal synaptic transmission remained intact. To evaluate short-term plasticity using a paired-pulse conditioning stimulation protocol, there was no significant difference. PM2.5 exposure did not significantly affect BDNF levels in either sex compared to controls and did not significantly alter the levels of synaptophysin and PSD-95 proteins. PM2.5 treatment did not affect GluN2A protein levels. Maternal PM2.5 exposure reduced GluN2B protein expression in the hippocampi of both male and female offspring, suggesting impaired LTP formation could be linked to reduction in GluN2B subunit of the NMDA receptors. Aim 3: Determine whether maternal PM2.5 -induced neuroinflammation is associated with hippocampal impairment in mouse offspring Results achieved: Maternal exposure to PM2.5 did not induce neuroinflammation in the hippocampus of offspring. We assessed neuroinflammation by examining the number of ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (IBA-1) positive microglial cells in the hippocampus using immunostaining, and HMGB1, TNF-α, and MMP-9 ELISA kits for hippocampal fresh tissue.Two-way ANOVA revealed no significant inflammatory response in the hippocampal subregions in the DG. Post hoc analysis confirmed no significant changes in the number of IBA-1 positive cells in the DG there were no significant changes in the levels of HMGB1, TNF-α, and MMP-9 proteins. The data indicated that neuroinflammation is not linked to PM2.5-induced autism-like behavior in offspring. Aim 4: Determine whether suppressing neuroinflammation by minocycline treatment restores the maternal PM2.5 -induced behavioral deficits and hippocampal impairments in mouse offspring Results achieved: Since neuroinflammation is not involved in maternal PM2.5-induced hippocampal impairment and behavioral deficits. We therefore performed 16RNAs microbiota analysis of fecal samples collected from male and female offspring. Significant lower diversity of gut microbiota was found in mother, however, there was subtle changes in gut microbiota abundance and diversit, there was a significantly lower relative abundance of the family Bacteroidaceae in PM2.5-treated male offspring compared to healthy groups. We therefore conducted metabolomic analysis of amino acid levels in the hippocampus of offspring. Amino acids play crucial roles in neurodevelopmental disorders associated with autism. To investigate the effect of maternal exposure to PM2.5 on hippocampal amino acid levels in both mothers and offspring mice, we measured the concentrations of twenty standard amino acids in the hippocampus. Offspring mice displayed significant decrease in cysteine levels. There was a significant treatment-specific effect on hippocampal cysteine levels, but no sex-specific effect was found. Specifically, both female and male offspring with dams exposed to PM2.5 exhibited significantly lower cysteine concentrations compared to those in the control groups, suggesting cysteine deficiency could be linked to hippocampal impairment and thus behavioral deficits.

15104620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104620.value: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by early-onset challenges in social communication and repetitive behaviors, influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. The global increase in ASD diagnoses has brought attention to air pollution as a significant environmental risk factor, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates the impact of maternal exposure to the air pollutant PM2.5 on ASD risk in offspring. In this study, female C57BL/6J mice were exposed to PM2.5 via intratracheal instillation every three days for two weeks prior to mating, with exposure continuing until birth. Both male and female offspring exhibited reduced social novelty and increased repetitive behaviors, only male offspring showed significant impairment in working memory. PM2.5 exposure led to an increased number of proliferating progenitor cells and immature neurons in the hippocampus of male offspring, a change not observed in females. However, PM2.5 exposure resulted in reduced dendritic length exclusively in female offspring, while both sexes experienced decreased long-term potentiation and synaptic GluN2B protein expression in the hippocampus. These structural and functional changes were associated with significantly lower cysteine levels in the hippocampi of offspring of both sexes, but not changes in gut microbiota abundance and neuroinflammatory response in the hippocampus. These findings suggest that maternal PM2.5 exposure may induce autism-like behaviors in offspring, potentially linked to reduced hippocampal cysteine levels and hippocampal dysfunction, but not neuroinflammatory response.

15104620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104620.value: Our findings suggest that PM2.5-induced autism-like behavior is in association with cysteine deficiency. It has been previously reported that prenatal supplementation with antioxidant N-acetyl cysteine offers protective effects for fetal neurodevelopment. Further study will be to examine whether prenatal supplementation with n-acetyl cysteine will prevent development of autism in offspring and its relationship to restore hippocampal neuroplasticity in offspring mice. Future study will also focus on detailed molecular pathways linked to oxidative stress in the hippocampus induced by PM2.5. Specific pregnacy period of naternal PM2.4 exposure has not yet been studied, future study will also extend to investigate which trimester is more susceptable to detrimental effects of PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy.

15104620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104620.value: This study investigates the impact of maternal exposure to the air pollutant PM2.5 on autism risk in offspring using a mouse model. In this study, female mice were exposed to PM2.5 via intratracheal instillation every three days for two weeks prior to mating, with exposure continuing until birth. Both male and female offspring exhibited reduced social novelty and increased repetitive behaviors, only male offspring showed significant impairment in working memory. PM2.5 exposure showed gender specific effects in hippocampal structural changes, with an increased hippocampal adult-born neuron in male offspring, reduced neuron dendritic length in female offspring, and impaired synaptic function in male and female offspring. These structural and functional changes were associated with significantly lower cysteine levels in the hippocampi of offspring of both sexes. These findings suggest that maternal PM2.5 exposure may induce autism-like behaviors in offspring, potentially linked to reduced hippocampal dysfunction and cysteine deficiency.

15106120.value: 骨質酥鬆是一個嚴重的公共健康問題，其併發症包括危及生命的髖部脆性骨折。骨質酥鬆不僅僅是單一的骨骼疾病，更是隨著年齡增長而出現的綜合性神經肌肉骨骼功能障礙。因此，治療骨質酥鬆需要一個對多系統功能障礙起作用的新靶標。 乙酰膽鹼酯酶（AChE）是催化乙酰膽鹼水解從而終止神經信號傳遞的酶，它是阿爾茨海默氏病的主要治療靶標。最新的研究發現，乙酰膽鹼酯酶抑制劑的使用與降低阿爾茨海默氏病患者髖部骨折的風險、增強骨質酥鬆性骨折的愈合以及降低總體死亡率有關。這項研究的發現表明乙酰膽鹼酯酶和骨質酥鬆症之間可能存在某種聯繫，其潛在機制值得進一步研究。 在骨質酥鬆病症發展過程中，骨吸收與骨形成之間的平衡遭到破壞，並逐漸向破骨和骨質丟失的方向發展。我們的初步研究發現，乙酰膽鹼酯酶除了其經典的酶解功能外，在破骨細胞形成中具有非酶解作用機制。 首先，乙酰膽鹼酯酶的表達隨著破骨細胞的形成而增加。活性狀態下和滅活狀態下的AChE都促進細胞向多核破骨細胞融合的作用。此外，使用乙酰膽鹼酯酶抑制劑可以阻斷該過程的發生，且同時抑制AChE的酶及非酶功能位點比單純選擇性阻斷其酶性位點更有效。所以，我們假設AChE可通過其酶解和非酶解雙重功能促進破骨細胞生成和骨質酥鬆，而具有雙重抑制效果的AChE抑制劑可以消除這種作用。 在之前的研究中，我們利用中藥石杉鹼甲片段及舊的抗阿爾茨海默氏病藥物他克林，開發了一系列具有雙重抑製作用的二聚體AChE抑制劑。此前，我們已在各類阿爾茨海默氏病模型中篩選出了一系列最有效的護神經系統二聚體。而我們在最近的工作中進一步在體外證明瞭這些二聚體對破骨細胞的抑製作用及對成骨細胞的促進作用，其效用均優於目前的一線骨質酥鬆藥物。 在本項目中，我們首先在卵巢切除小鼠模型中探究破骨細胞形成和骨質酥鬆發展過程中骨AChE的活性和表達，之後比較完整和熱滅活的AChE對AChE基因敲除小鼠骨髓單核細胞破骨細胞分化的影響，最後在卵巢切除小鼠模型中驗證我們的新型二聚體對破骨細胞生成和骨質酥鬆的影響。 我們希望通過本次研究，探索AChE作為多系統功能障礙的新靶標，為老年人提供大腦和骨骼雙重保護作用。

15106120.label: Realisation of objectives
15106120.value: 1. To delineate bone AChE activity and expression during osteoclastogenesis and osteoporosis in an ovariectomy mouse model; In this project, we firstly demonstrated an increase of AChE protein with bone loss after ovariectomy or in an age-dependent manner in vivo. AChE accumulated on the surface of trabecular bone over time. The orchestration between bone forming and bone resorbing cells, i.e. osteoclasts and osteoblasts, is essential for maintenance of bone homeostasis. Then we examined AChE expression pattern in osteoclasts and osteoblasts, respectively. We have examined the AChE expression pattern in an established osteoclastogenesis assay using RAW264.7 macrophage cell line. As shown in Western blot, AChE protein level slightly increased within 3 days and significantly decreased after 5 days post induction. We deployed siRNA to purposely knock down the endogenous AChE in RAW264.7 cells. We found knockdown of endogenous AChE would accelerate osteoclasts formation, verified by conventional TRAP staining. 2. To compare the effect between intact and heat-inactivated AChE on osteoclast differentiation of bone marrow monocytes from AChE knockout mice; As shown in others’ and our studies, addition of exogenous intact or heat-inactivated AChE protein could also facilitate cell-cell fusion of RAW264.7 towards multi-nucleated osteoclasts in vitro. The contradicting role of endogenous and exogenous AchE in osteoclastogenesis stimulated us to rethink about the origin of AChE during bone remodelling. Therefore, we purposely compared the amount of AChE expressed in osteoblast-like cells, MC3T3-E1S4, with RAW264.7. We observed the amount of AChE expressed by osteoblasts was at least 100 folds higher that by osteoclasts by estimation based on Western Blotting. So we refine our hypothesis that osteoblasts-derived AChE increased in ovariectomized and aged bone tissues to disrupt bone homeostasis and cause bone loss. By leveraging a microfluidic co-culture system. We observed that AChE stimulate osteoclastogenesis and also osteoblast senescence. AChE inhbitors, particularly those targeting peripheral active site of AChE such as donepezil or our novel dimeric compound, could attenuate such deleterious effects of AChE on both types of cells. 3. To examine the effect of our dimers on osteoclast formation and osteoporosis development in the ovariectomized mice. To test our hypothesis and to further validate our observation in vitro, we adopted a transgenic mouse model for conditional knockout of Ache in osteoblast lineage via crossing Ache fl/fl::osteocalcin-Cre mouse lines. We confirmed that conditional knockout of Ache in osteoblasts did not significant alter postnatal bone growth but prevent bone loss in the ovariectomized mice. We further employed FDA-approved AChE inhibitor, donepezil, as well as our novel dimeric compound A10E for treating bone loss in an ovariectomized mouse model. Donepezil could not only inhibit TRAP+ osteoclasts but also increase new bone formation. It ultimately facilitated bone mass accrual in the ovariectomized mice, rather simply slow down the rate of bone loss.

15106120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15106120.value: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE), originally known as a rate-limiting enzyme in cholinergic signalling, has been implicated in postnatal skeletal development in an acetylcholine-dependent and independent manner. Yet the role of AChE in bone homeostasis and disease remains less understand. As bone homeostasis is maintained by the balance between bone forming and bone resorbing cells, i.e. osteoclasts and osteoblasts. In this study, we exploited the expression amount of Ache in both osteoclasts and osteoblasts. We found osteoblasts, rather osteoclasts, were the major source of AChE. We further demonstrated an increased expression of AChE during osteoblast senescence in cell models, and both recombinant mouse AChE and heat-inactivated AChE can induce osteoblast senescence, followed by the influence of AChE inhibitors donepezil and galantamine. Moreover, the effects of AChE inhibitors on osteoporosis mice models were investigated. Our data confirmed AChE expression increased in osteoblast senescence. Subsequently, a microfluidic chip analysed the interaction between osteoclast progenitors and senescent osteoblasts. After induction of senescence, more displacement of the osteoclast precursor cells towards senescent osteoblast was observed compared to control osteoblast, indicating an important communication between the two main types of bone cells. Then, we further validated our findings by using a transgenic mouse model for conditional knockout of Ache in osteocalcin+ osteoblast lineage cells. We found cKO mouse model was resistant to ovariectomized bone loss. Finally, donepezil and ambenonium were successfully applied to reduce bone loss in an in vivo ovariectomized-induced osteoporotic model, demonstrating a role for peripheral-acting AChE inhibitors in the disease. In conclusion, this study showed the involvement of AChE in skeletal ageing and osteoporosis as demonstrated by its increased expression and stimulating function in osteoblast senescence, which is at least partly mediated by its non-enzymatic function through the peripheral anionic site and suggests that dual-acting AChE inhibitors with or without blood-brain barrier penetrating capacity form a promising new target for osteoporosis.

15106120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15106120.value: We are not only working on the role of AchE in osteoporosis, but also its role in osteoarthritis, the other prevalent age-related skeletal disorder. We have secured ANR/RGC grant recently to further exploit the role of cholinergic signalling in cartilage homeostasis and osteoarthritis together with French research group (A-PolyU503/24). In this new development, we are going to look into the interplay between systemic cholinergic signalling with local cholinergic components including AchE and alpha7 nicotinic receptor.

15106120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15106120.value: Our study looked at a protein called acetylcholinesterase (AChE), which is known for its role in nerve signalling, to see how it affects bone health. We found that bone-building cells (osteoblasts) produce much more AChE than bone-resorbing cells (osteoclasts). As osteoblasts age, they make even more AChE, and this seems to speed up their aging process. We also discovered that drugs which block AChE, like donepezil (used for Alzheimer’s), can slow down this aging in bone cells and help prevent bone loss in mice with osteoporosis. Using special mouse models, we showed that removing AChE from bone-building cells protects against bone loss after menopause. We also saw that aged bone cells attract more bone-resorbing cells, which could worsen bone loss. Overall, our research suggests that AChE plays a key role in bone aging and osteoporosis, and that medicines blocking AChE—especially those that act outside the brain—could be a new way to treat or prevent osteoporosis.

15106620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106620.value: 吸煙在全球具有很高的流行率，並增加了全因死亡率的風險。吸煙是慢性疾病如慢性阻塞性肺病（COPD）的主因。 運動時呼吸困難和通氣受限是限制COPD 患者的主要症狀。文獻顯示COPD除了影響肺部, 更會造成全身性影響, 包括肌肉功能紊亂, 導致肌肉萎縮,肌肉力量和耐力下降。 穴位經皮神經電刺激治療(Acu-TENS) 是無創性中西結合的治療。 文獻顯示Acu-TENS可以減輕呼吸困難和呼吸。 此外, 長期治療(20節的Acu-TENS)亦被顯示有效改善肺功能和運動耐量。 然而, 其治療機制仍需探討。 我們的早期研究顯示大鼠在香煙暴露的56天後出現明顯的肺功能降低和肺泡間隙增大, 與COPD造成的影響相若。此外, 我們發現大鼠在Acu-TENS刺激呼吸困難相關穴位後, 大鼠的β-內啡肽水準上升, 而結果與我們先前發表的COPD 患者研究結果相似。 基於這些研究結果,我們設計動物實驗以探討 1)Acu-TENS對肺功能及全身性身體功能的影響及其與β-內啡肽的相關性 2)Acu-TENS引起的生理機制 3)Acu-TENS的治療方案及對在香煙暴露後肺功受損大鼠的影響。

15106620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15106620.value: In study 1, we examined if Acu-TENS (AT) would induce changes in pulmonary and overall physical function and their associations with β-endorphin. Acu-TENS group exhibited significantly lower respiratory rate (RR) than control and Sham-TENS groups. AT-CS (Acu-TENS and cigarette-smoke) group had also significantly higher expiratory volume (EV) than the CS group. These results suggested that Acu-TENS may enhance expiratory function, particularly in the cigarette smoke-induced model. Airway resistance parameters like as sRaw, FEV0.1/FVC have been significantly improved in AT-CS groups when compared to other groups. Yet, changes in physical performance were not apparent. Pearson’s correlation showed that -endorphin were slightly negative correlated to respiratory rate. In study 2, we examined the role of β-endorphin on influencing respiratory center thereby reducing respiratory symptoms and promoting pulmonary function and physical function upon Acu-TENS stimulation. Our findings showed that Naloxone have been blocked the μ-opioid receptor (MOR) and suppressed the effects induced by Acu-TENS. The involvement of the opioid receptor preserved the respiratory stress by smoking. These suggested that β-endorphin as one possible mechanism leading to the functional changes. In study 3, we examined the synergistic effect of non-invasive multiple acupoints stimulation by Acu-TENS. Beneficial effects were demonstrated. In particular, when applied to ST-36, BL13 and EX-B1, it induced greater improvement in respiratory function. The anti-inflammatory response observed with multiple points stimulation was appeared to be more than that with single point suggesting the synergistic effects and the changes would be associated with functional specificity of acupoints.

15106620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15106620.value: The effects of Acu-TENS may also involve autonomic nervous system (ANS) modulation. Further studies could examine its impact on heart rate variability (HRV) and related outcomes.

15106620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15106620.value: Our study showed that application of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation on acupoint (Acu-TENS), i.e., EX-B1, was found to be effective on promoting lung function for animals exposing to Cigarette smoke (CS) and that the change of β-endorphin. Acupoint was function-specific. Stimulation of multiple acupoints (ST36, BL13 and EX-B1) was found to be significantly improve the CS-associated changes in lung function than single acupoint stimulation suggesting the synergistic effects of multiple acupoints stimulation.
