15200120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200120.value: Energy piles are an environment-friendly technology for space heating and cooling in buildings. During winter and summer, they can extract geothermal energy from and dissipate heat into ground respectively, where the temperature below a certain depth stays fairly constant. Compared to conventional heating and cooling systems, the utilization of energy piles can reduce energy consumption and CO2 emission by about 60% and 50%, respectively. Hence, energy piles are spreading rapidly in many countries such as Austria and China. Different from conventional piles, the circulation of heat-exchange fluid in energy piles subjects the piles, surrounding soils and their interfaces to many thermal cycles. The variation of temperature would affect engineering properties of soils and interfaces, and hence alter the pile settlement and bearing capacity, as supported by some theoretical and experimental studies. Most of the previous researchers focused on saturated soils and interfaces. There is a lack of fundamental understanding and proper modelling of the thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils and interfaces, particularly under three-dimensional stress condition (i.e., the three principal stresses are different). It is therefore challenging to accurately predict the performance of energy piles in many regions such as Beijing, where the groundwater table is currently about 25m below the ground surface. To address this challenge, this project will investigate cyclic thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils and interfaces through advanced laboratory testing and theoretical modelling. Some new apparatuses such as a suction and temperature controlled true triaxial system will be developed and used for testing soils and interfaces. Special attention will be paid to the cyclic thermal strains of unsaturated soils under three different principal stresses, cyclic shear behaviour of unsaturated soils and interfaces at various suctions and temperatures, and temperature-dependent water retention behaviour and permeability function at different stresses. Based on the unique data, two novel thermo-mechanical models will be developed for unsaturated soils and interfaces, respectively. Compared to existing models for unsaturated soils and interfaces, the new models will demonstrate unique ability to capture the influence of thermal cycles and stress anisotropy. Furthermore, the two models will be implemented into a finite element code and verified using physical model test results in the literature. Parametric studies will be conducted to reveal the performance of energy piles in unsaturated ground. The success of this project will enable researchers and engineers to analyze the performance of energy piles more accurately, and to encourage building owners to use energy piles. 能量樁是一種由地源熱泵技術與樁基埋管換熱器結合組成的新型空間供暖和製冷技術。該技術基於地表某個深度（約10米）以下全年溫度相對穩定的自然規律，在冬季提取地熱資源加熱空間，在夏季將室內餘熱轉移到地下。基於能量樁技術的供暖和製冷方式具有綠色低碳和清潔環保等特點，比傳統方式節省能源60%，減少二氧化碳排放50%。因此，能量樁技術在奧地利和中國等地得到了廣泛應用。 與常規樁不同，能量樁工作過程中的熱交換會導致樁身周圍溫度場發生週期性變化，改變土體及其與能量樁接觸面的工程性質，從而影響能量樁的沉降規律和承載力。以往的研究主要集中於飽和土與接觸面，對於非飽和效應的認識比較有限，難以預測低水位地區（如北京）能量樁的服役性能。 為了解決這一問題，本項目將研發一系列新的測試設備，比如吸力和溫度控制的真三軸系統。通過實驗研究非飽和土與接觸面的熱力學行為，主要包括不同應力條件下非飽和土的溫度應變、不同吸力和溫度條件下非飽和土與接觸面的剪切特性，以及不同應力和溫度條件下的持水特性和滲透係數。根據實驗結果，將分別為非飽和土與接觸面建立熱力學本構模型，並編入有限元程序，分析能量樁的服役性能。該項目的成功實施將使研究人員和工程師能夠更準確地分析能量樁的性能，並鼓勵業主使用能源樁。

15200120.label: Realisation of objectives
15200120.value: This project investigated the cyclic thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils and interfaces through advanced laboratory testing and theoretical modelling. The results are used for analysing the performance of energy piles and other geostructures in unsaturated ground. All of the five proposed objectives have been achieved through the following activities, in line with the original plan: (1) Several new apparatuses were developed by modifying existing equipment, including a new apparatus for measuring soil thermal conductivity with the capability to control stress and measure specimen deformation; a novel direct shear apparatus for studying the thermo-mechanical behaviour of saturated and unsaturated soils and soil-structure interfaces; a suction- and temperature-controlled triaxial apparatus; a suction- and temperature-controlled hollow cylinder torsional shear apparatus; and a physical model of energy piles. [Objective 1] (2) A comprehensive test program was carried out to reveal the influence of porosity, degree of saturation, stress level, and soil type. In total, around 60 tests were conducted, with three replicates for each condition. The experimental results are useful for improving the understanding of thermal conductivity, particularly in two aspects: (1) the mechanism of stress effects on thermal conductivity (i.e., the relative contribution of decreasing the void ratio and increasing inter-particle contacts) and (2) the stress effects on thermal conductivity at different degrees of saturation. Based on the thermal conductivity results, a new semi-empirical equation was proposed to model the thermal conductivity of saturated and unsaturated soils, considering the effects of stress on void ratio and inter-particle contacts. Compared to existing models, it has two major improvements: (i) it can accurately capture the influence of stress on the thermal conductivities of various soils, and (ii) it is able to capture the hysteresis of the stress–thermal conductivity relationship during loading and unloading processes. [Objectives 2 and 4] (3) By using the suction- and temperature-controlled triaxial apparatus (both conventional triaxial and true triaxial) and the hollow cylinder torsional shear apparatus, extensive tests have been carried out to understand the mechanical behaviour of soils along complex thermo-hydro-mechanical paths. The influence of several major factors on the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of soils has been revealed, including suction, temperature, principal stress rotation, intermediate principal stress, and fabric. Based on the test data, a new constitutive model was developed for anisotropic soils considering fabric evolution under proportional and non-proportional loadings. [Objectives 2 and 4] (4) By using the new temperature- and suction-controlled direct shear device, two types of tests were conducted to study the thermo-mechanical behaviour of a CDG-structure interface under saturated and unsaturated conditions. The first is constant-temperature direct shearing using displacement control loading mode, while the second is constant-stress heating–cooling with force control loading mode. Comprehensive tests were conducted at various temperatures (8, 20, and 42 °C), net normal stresses (25, 50, 100, 150, and 225 kPa), and suctions (0, 50, and 200 kPa). This study is the first to investigate the coupled effects of temperature, stress, and suction on the shear behaviour of unsaturated soil–structure interfaces. Based on the new data, a thermo-mechanical constitutive model was developed using the bounding surface plasticity framework to predict the thermo-mechanical behaviour of saturated and unsaturated interfaces. New formulations were proposed to model the critical state void ratio and shear strength. Comparisons between measured and computed results suggest that this model can effectively capture the coupled effects of temperature, suction, and net normal stress on the shear behaviour of interfaces at various suctions, stresses, and temperatures. [Objectives 3 and 4] (5) Furthermore, a small-scale physical model was set up to investigate the thermo-mechanical behaviour of energy piles. Several series of tests were conducted to examine the effects of soil suction and interface roughness on the bearing capacity and settlement behaviour of energy piles. These findings are explained based on the results of thermal conductivity and interface shear behaviour obtained from the above tests. [Objective 5] (6) The new models developed in this project were utilised in a finite element code to compute the behaviour of energy piles, including the heat exchange rate between the energy pile and the ground, the bearing capacity of energy piles, and the accumulation of pile head settlement during heating–cooling cycles under working conditions. Based on the results of numerical simulations, several design recommendations were proposed. [Objective 5]

15200120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200120.value: Key findings and outcome related to Objective 1: Several new apparatuses were developed, including a new device for measuring soil thermal conductivity at various stress conditions; a novel direct shear apparatus for studying the thermo-mechanical behaviour of soil-structure interfaces; a suction- and temperature-controlled triaxial apparatus; a suction- and temperature-controlled hollow cylinder torsional shear apparatus; and a physical model of energy piles. (References: Journal papers 1, 2, 3) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 2: (1) As stress increases, the thermal conductivity of soil rises significantly. This increase is attributed not only to a reduction in the void ratio but also to enhanced inter-particle contact. (2) Under cyclic loading, permanent strain increases and Young’s modulus decreases as temperature rises and suction decreases. (References: Journal papers 1 and 2) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 3: (1) Temperature has a minor effect on the friction angle of soil–pile interfaces. The interface strength increases nonlinearly with increasing suction, and the rate of increase is temperature-dependent. (2) At the interfaces, the forward displacement induced by cooling is approximately ten times greater than that induced by heating. The relationship between irreversible displacement and shear stress ratio suggests the existence of a threshold shear stress ratio, above which significant irreversible movement occurs. (References: Journal papers 3 and 4) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 4: Theoretical models have been developed to describe the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of soils and soil-pile interfaces. Three models have been published: (1) a constitutive model for anisotropic sand that considers fabric evolution; (2) a new model for the stress-dependent thermal conductivity of saturated and unsaturated soils; and (3) a thermo-mechanical model for saturated and unsaturated interfaces. (References: Journal papers 5 to 7) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 5: (1) The ultimate capacity of an energy pile increases with increasing initial suction, pile roughness, and temperature. The influence of roughness is more pronounced under unsaturated conditions than in saturated states. (2) During thermal cycles, irreversible pile head settlement is significant when the working load is high. The settlement is mainly due to a reduction in horizontal stress and, consequently, a decrease in the shaft resistance of floating piles. (3) Neglecting the effects of stress on thermal conductivity, as is common in conventional analyses, leads to an underestimation of the heat exchange rate between energy piles and the ground. (References: Journal papers 8 to 13)

15200120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200120.value: While this project primarily focuses on the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of energy piles, some preliminary and exploratory work has also been conducted on energy tunnels. Due to their larger contact surface, energy tunnels offer substantial potential for heat exchange. The results of our numerical simulation confirm that energy tunnels are an efficient method for capturing geothermal energy, comparable to energy piles in terms of effectiveness. So far, however, energy tunnels have been relatively less studied than energy piles. It is important to note that seasonal heating and cooling cycles may compromise safety by inducing additional stress and strain in the tunnel lining, potentially causing excessive ground settlement and posing risks to nearby tunnels. Therefore, further research is needed to develop a solid understanding of energy tunnels, and proper design is crucial to safely harness geothermal energy through them. Advancing research in this area can contribute to sustainable development by reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions.

15200120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200120.value: Energy piles are an environment-friendly technology for space heating and cooling in buildings. They can extract geothermal energy for space heating in buildings during winter and assist in cooling spaces in summer by dissipating heat into the ground, where the temperature remains fairly constant throughout the year in many parts of the world. Hence, energy piles are spreading rapidly in many countries, such as Austria and China. Most previous researchers have focused on saturated soils and interfaces, although soils surrounding energy piles are often unsaturated, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. This project has addressed this problem by investigating the cyclic thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils and interfaces through advanced laboratory testing and theoretical modelling. New apparatuses, such as temperature- and suction-controlled true triaxial and soil-structure interface shear systems, have been developed for testing soils and interfaces along various thermos-hydro-mechanical paths. Based on experimental results, new theoretical models have been developed to simulate the thermo-mechanical behaviour of soils and soil-pile interfaces under both saturated and unsaturated conditions. The experimental and theoretical results will be useful for engineers to analyse the performance of energy piles more accurately and to improve the current design methods of energy piles in unsaturated ground.

15200420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200420.value: Indirect evaporative cooling is a sustainable cooling technology that has been widely recognized by industrial and residential communities for its low energy consumption and highly efficient and environmental friendly features of air-conditioning systems in buildings. The technology relies on water evaporation for cooling fresh air. As reported, with the currently used aluminium sheet or polymer indirect evaporative cooler (IEC), a poor wetting condition in the wet channels is often encountered, which greatly degrades the evaporation process in the wet channels. Moreover, continuously circulated water is indispensable to ensure evaporation water films. To improve the surface wetting condition and reduce the energy consumption of water circulation, microporous aluminium sheet is proposed for manufacturing the channel walls of the IEC as a novel heat and mass transfer media for the IEC technology. Its high porosity, large specific surface area, high thermal conductivity, low cost and easy processing features make it an ideal material for IEC applications. The aluminium walls with microporous surfaces facing the wet channels and impermeable surfaces facing the dry channels enable intensive evaporation and sensible cooling to occur simultaneously inside the IEC. The microporous surface is characterized by its water storage behaviour and capillary action, contributing to effective evaporation by continuously transporting stored water to the metal surface and forming a thin and evenly distributed water film for enhancing the evaporatin process. Moreover, intermittent spraying of water can be realized owing to the water storage feature so that the energy consumption of the pump is reduced. This project is to propose a novel microporous aluminium IEC and investigate its improved energy performances. A theoretical simulation model will be developed to describe the heat and mass transfer processes on both sides of the two air flows. A test rig will be set up, on the one hand, to validate the thermal performance model, and on the other hand, to find an optimal intermittent spaying strategy for better thermal performance and lower energy consumption. The validated simulation model will be used to quantitatively analyze the cooling performance of microporous aluminium IECs under various operating conditions. The theoretical analysis will also identify the most influential parameters and provide optimal design parameters through numerical simulation. The outcomes of the research work will provide a reliable basis for performance evaluation of a next-generation IEC as well as useful guidelines for researchers, engineers, developers and manufacturers of IEC applications and productions. 間接蒸發冷卻技術是一種可持續冷卻技術，以其低能耗和高效環保的特點得到了工業界和使用者的廣泛認可。這項技術依靠水的蒸發吸熱來冷卻新鮮空氣。據研究表明，在目前使用的鋁板或聚合物間接蒸發冷卻器中，濕通道表面的潤濕性較差，這大大降低了蒸發作用。此外，持續的噴水是確保在濕通道內形成蒸發水膜的必要條件。本項目提出使用微孔鋁板作為新型傳熱傳質的介質，用於製作間接蒸發冷卻器，從而改善濕通道的表面濕潤度並減少水循環的能量消耗。微孔鋁具有高孔隙率、高熱導率、低成本和易於加工等優點，是製作間接蒸發冷卻器的理想材料。在冷卻器中，微孔表面面對濕通道，不透水表面面對幹通道，大量的蒸發和顯熱冷卻同時發生。微孔結構具有儲水性和毛細作用，毛細作用可將水連續輸送到金屬表面，形成薄而均勻分佈的水膜，有助於有效蒸發。由於多孔材料的儲水特性，水系統可以實現間接噴淋，從而降低了水泵能耗。本項目旨在研究這種新型微孔鋁間接蒸發冷卻器的性能提升程度。首先，建立幹通道和濕通道氣流的傳熱傳質理論模型，其次，搭建的實驗台一方面用於驗證理論模型，另一方面用於研究可實現更好性能和更低能耗的最佳噴淋策略。驗證後的模型將用於定量分析微孔鋁間接蒸發冷卻器在各種工況下的冷卻性能。理論分析還可以通過數值模擬找出影響最大的參數，並提供優化設計。該項目的研究成果將為下一代間接蒸發冷卻器的性能評估和工業製造提供可靠的依據，並為工程師和研究人員提供參考。

15200420.label: Realisation of objectives
15200420.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. Some achievements are even beyond expected outcomes. Here is a summary for each proposed objective: Objective 1: This project focuses on the use of porous media. After trials, sintered nickel on stainless steel plates is used instead of aluminium as the wetted channel wall material for indirect evaporative coolers (IECs). The research fully establishes the concept and practical feasibility of using porous metal walls to enhance water retention ability and cooling performance in the novel IECs. The studies focus on the innovation of IECs by integrating porous metallic materials, specifically, sintered porous nickel into the wetted channel surfaces. This design ensures enhanced water retention and sustains evaporative cooling, overcoming the limitations of traditional smooth metal walls. The research thoroughly discusses the rationale for choosing porous metals, highlighting properties such as high porosity, optimal pore size distribution, mechanical robustness, and corrosion resistance. Manufacturing and integration guidance has been presented as well (e.g., sintering, bonding to base plates, ensuring impermeability to the primary channel). Furthermore, the studies articulate the scientific principles underpinning the use of porous metals in IECs, laying out performance requirements and integration strategies. The impact of porous walls on water retention, wettability, and long-term structural integrity is analysed and compared to traditional plate-type IECs that needs consistent water spraying. The research concludes that the advantages demonstrated with porous nickel can be expected for other porous metals, including aluminium, provided that key structural and functional characteristics are maintained. Objective 2: The development of a simulation model for IECs with porous metal channels, capable of capturing heat and mass transfer processes under both continuous and intermittent water spraying, is thoroughly accomplished. The research presents a multiphysics modelling approach, using COMSOL Multiphysics, that couples fluid dynamics, heat transfer, mass transfer, and the unique effects of porous media. The models incorporate detailed physics such as phase change from liquid to vapor within the pores, and the evolving saturation and temperature fields within the channel walls. Both steady-state (continuous spraying) and dynamic (intermittent spraying) operational scenarios are modelled, enabling prediction of supply air temperature, humidity, and energy efficiency over time. These simulations also allow for the assessment of how quickly the stored water in porous walls is depleted during non-spraying periods and how quickly it can be recharged through brief spraying intervals. Besides, series of experiments have been conducted for data collection and the model validation. Particular attention is given to the unique characteristics of porous materials in wet channels. The models are parameterized with porosity, pore size, permeability, and thermal conductivity, making them adaptable to a range of materials. The simulation framework also accounts for the influence of channel geometry, airflow velocity, and inlet air conditions on the overall air-cooling performance, providing a valuable tool for optimizing design and operational strategies. Objective 3: Experimental validation of the simulation model is rigorously carried out through laboratory testing of IEC prototypes featuring porous metallic walls. The experimental setups, as described in our published papers related to this objective, include detailed instrumentation for monitoring air temperature, humidity, air velocity, and pressure drop on both the dry and wet sides of the IEC. The prototypes are constructed using sintered porous nickel, and the experimental results are compared with model predictions for a range of operating conditions, including both continuous and intermittent water spraying. The observed agreement between simulation and experiment, typically within 10% error margins, which confirms the reliability and accuracy of the developed model. Following validation, the simulation model is used to conduct comprehensive parametric studies, systematically varying key design and operational factors such as inlet air temperature, relative humidity, primary and secondary air velocities, channel gap size, porosity, and pore diameter. The results of these studies are synthesized to form clear, quantitative design guidelines. For example, the findings indicate that higher porosity and larger pore sizes in the channel wall material allow for greater water storage and longer non-spraying intervals, while narrower channel gaps and lower primary air velocities enhance wet-bulb efficiency. Objective 4: Quantitative evaluation of the performance improvements and energy savings achieved by using porous metal walls in IECs is comprehensively addressed. The studies provide detailed metrics such as wet-bulb efficiency, system COP, water pump operation time, and annual CO₂ emission reductions. The research demonstrates that incorporating porous metallic walls and implementing intermittent spraying strategies can result in substantial performance benefits: system COP can be improved significantly, water pump operation time reduced by over ninety percent, and annual CO₂ emissions lowered by a notable percentage. These benefits are further linked to cost savings, with daily operational cost reductions observed when the system is used for pre-cooling in conjunction with an air handling unit (AHU). Such comprehensive performance metrics are derived from both experimental data and simulation results, providing a holistic view of the benefits. While the experimental focus is on porous nickel, the simulation and analytical framework is readily adaptable to microporous aluminium by substituting appropriate material parameters—such as thermal conductivity, porosity, and pore size. The studies emphasize that the mechanisms driving energy savings and improved cooling performance, namely, enhanced water retention, efficient evaporation, and reduced reliance on continuous pumping—are inherent to the use of porous metallic materials and are expected to be at least as effective when using microporous aluminium. The research thus sets clear performance benchmarks and quantifiable expectations for the adoption of microporous aluminium in IEC applications, ensuring that future systems can be designed with confidence regarding their thermal and energy-saving advantages. In summary, all the four objectives have been substantially achieved based on the current work, and the findings offer a robust theoretical, modelling, experimental, and application foundation for the future use of microporous metal-structured high-performance IEC systems.

15200420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200420.value: This research systematically investigated the performance and optimization of novel plate-type indirect evaporative coolers (IECs) utilizing porous metallic wall materials, with a focus on both experimental validation and advanced numerical modelling. The key innovation lies in the use of sintered porous metal as the wetted channel wall, enabling enhanced water retention and supporting both continuous and intermittent water spraying strategies. The key findings include: 1) Enhanced Water Retention and Intermittent Spraying: The porous metallic walls exhibit strong water storage and retention capabilities, allowing the IEC to maintain cooling performance even during periods without water spraying. This enables the adoption of intermittent spraying strategies, significantly reducing pump operation time while maintaining stable supply air temperature within an acceptable fluctuation; 2) Energy and Thermal Performance Improvements: Experimental and simulation results consistently demonstrate that the novel porous IEC achieves much better thermal performance than conventional designs. With intermittent spraying, the coefficient of performance (COP) can be improved by 58%–161%, and wet-bulb efficiency as high as 0.63 has been achieved. The longest non-spraying interval reached 2410 seconds, reducing water pump operation time by up to 95.2% compared to continuous spraying; 3) Environmental and Economic Benefits: The use of porous metallic walls and intermittent spraying strategies not only improves energy efficiency but also leads to notable environmental and economic benefits. Annual CO₂ emissions can be reduced by 16%–24.2%, and daily operational costs can be lower; 4) Design Guidelines and Parametric Insights: Systematic parameter studies identified that higher porosity, larger pore size, reduced channel height, and optimized air velocities contribute to improved IEC performance. These insights provide clear guidelines for the design of highly efficient IECs.

15200420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200420.value: The outcomes of this research provide a solid platform for further advancements in the field of indirect evaporative cooling using porous metallic materials. Several promising directions can be identified for both scientific investigation and practical engineering applications. Model refinement is another key direction, including the incorporation of additional effects such as condensation, fouling, and operation in hot-humid climates. Development of intelligent control algorithms for adaptive intermittent spraying, integrated with building management systems, could further increase energy savings and operational flexibility. In addition, field demonstrations in actual air-conditioning or energy recovery systems are recommended to validate laboratory findings at scale, providing feedback for further optimization. In summary, advancing material innovation, enhancing modelling and controls, and conducting field trials form a comprehensive path forward, enabling the widespread adoption of highly efficient, sustainable indirect evaporative cooling technologies.

15200420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200420.value: This research project explored a new way for air-conditioning in buildings more efficiently and sustainably. Traditional air-conditioning systems use a lot of electricity, especially in hot climates. The project focused on a cooling device called indirect evaporative cooler (IEC), which can lower air temperature using water evaporation without adding moisture to fresh air supply. A key innovation was using a special metal material with tiny pores as part of the cooler. This porous metal can absorb and store water, allowing the cooler to work even when water is not sprayed continuously, which saves energy and water. Experiments and computer simulations showed that this new design can reduce electricity use, lower carbon emissions, and cut costs compared to standard cooling methods. The findings suggest that buildings could stay comfortable with less energy and less environmental impact. The next steps include making the device from lightweight, widely available metals and testing it in real buildings. If widely adopted, this technology could play a major role in making air-conditioning greener, more affordable, and more sustainable.

15201820.label: Project Objectives
15201820.value: [Filter techniques for vector data in smart memory/storage] Many data mining tasks (e.g., kNN classifier, k-means clustering) frequently invoke distance comparison, i.e., testing whether the distance dist(u,v) between two vectors is less than a threshold. The performance bottleneck is caused by the cost of transferring data between CPU and memory. This motivates us to develop filter techniques for vector data by utilizing smart memory/storage. [Compression techniques for vector data in smart memory/storage] A smart memory device may not have sufficient capacity to accommodate the entire dataset. In addition, smart memory supports running specific operations on certain types of data only, but not executing arbitrary code. We plan to develop a lossy compression scheme so that: (i) the compressed vectors approximately preserve the distances between the original vectors, and (ii) the compressed vectors can be readily used for computation within smart memory. We will also investigate the applicability of our techniques to smart SSD. [Performance optimizer for data mining tasks using smart memory/storage] With our proposed techniques in the first two objectives, there exist multiple possible plans to complete the same data mining task by using smart memory/storage. However, different plans may consume different amount of execution time. We plan to estimate the performance of each plan, then recommend the fastest plan.

15201820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201820.value: Vector data has been used to represent many types of data objects (e.g., feature vectors extracted from images, document vectors defined by documents, and user/item vectors obtained from user-item ratings). Data mining tasks on vector data (e.g., classification, clustering, and outlier detection) are frequently used in various applications such as customer segmentation, topic discovery, and fraud detection. In existing solutions, the performance bottleneck is caused by the transfer of data from memory/storage to processors. Recent advances in smart memory/storage (e.g., smart SSD, ReRAM, PCM, and STT-RAM) enable us to execute specific computation near data. By exploiting this capability carefully, it is possible to dramatically reduce the amount of data transferred to processors, thus alleviating the performance bottleneck between memory/storage and processors. In this project, we will exploit smart memory/storage to accelerate data mining tasks on vector data. The main challenge arises from the fact that smart memory/storage support running specific operations on certain types of data only (e.g., computing the inner product between integer vectors), but not executing arbitrary code. This makes it challenging to implement data mining tasks by using smart memory/storage. Our approach is to utilize the available operations in smart memory/storage to compute compact intermediate results, which enable filtering unnecessary data and substantially reducing the amount of data to be handled by processors. To tackle the above issues, we have formulated the following research objectives. First, we will design filter techniques for vector data by leveraging the available operations in smart memory/storage. Second, we will develop techniques to compress vector data for smart memory/storage based on capacity and local computation overhead. Third, we will develop a performance optimizer for data mining tasks (e.g., classification, clustering, and outlier detection) by exploiting smart memory/storage. Fourth, we will build a prototype software based on our proposed techniques and then release it to the public. In summary, this project will advance the techniques for accelerating data mining algorithms by utilizing smart memory/storage, enhance the efficiency in the aforementioned applications (e.g., customer segmentation, topic discovery, and fraud detection), as well as provide a prototype software to the public. 矢量數據已用於表示多種數據類型（例如，從圖像中提取的特徵向量，由文檔定義的文檔向量）。矢量數據的數據挖掘任務（例如，分類，聚類和離群值檢測）經常用於各種應用程序中，例如客戶細分，主題發現和欺詐檢測。在現有解決方案中，數據從內存/存儲到處理器的傳輸引起性能瓶頸。 智能存儲器/存儲（例如智能SSD，ReRAM，PCM和STT-RAM）使我們能夠在數據附近執行特定的計算。通過利用此功能，可以大大減少傳輸到處理器的數據量，從而減輕內存/存儲與處理器之間的性能瓶頸。在這個項目中，我們將利用智能內存/存儲來加速矢量數據的數據挖掘任務。這個項目的主要挑戰如下：智能存儲器/存儲僅支持對某些類型的數據運行特定操作（例如，計算整數向量之間的內積），而不執行任意代碼。我們的方法是利用智能內存/存儲中的可用操作來計算簡潔的中間結果，從而過濾不必要的數據並大大減少處理器要處理的數據量。 為了解決上述問題，我們制定了以下研究目標。首先，我們將利用智能內存/存儲中的可用操作設計矢量數據的過濾技術。其次，我們將開發技術來壓縮矢量數據。第三，我們將利用智能內存/存儲設計用於數據挖掘任務（例如，分類，聚類和離群值檢測）的性能優化器。總而言之，該項目將利用智能存儲/存儲來促進用於加速數據挖掘算法的技術，並提高上述應用中的效率（例如，客戶細分，主題發現和欺詐檢測）。

15201920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201920.value: 过去几十年里，基于振动的结构健康监测和损伤识别方法得到了飞速的发展，其中一些方法已经成功地应用在机械和航空航天结构上。然而，这些方法在实际土木工程结构上的应用还不成熟，其原因在于以下几个方面的困难或不足。首先，土木工程结构损伤识别不可避免地涉及到一些不确定性因素，比如测量噪声和模型误差；这些不确定性因素可能会引起结构振动特性的不确定性。然而，目前大多数损伤识别方法并未正确考虑这些不确定性，从而导致错误的识别结果。其次，相对于结构损伤，环境条件的变化―尤其是温度，可能会对土木结构的响应产生更大的改变。如果忽略温度变化对结构响应的改变，将很难得到可靠准确的损伤识别结果。最后，在损伤识别研究中，人们通常对钢结构模型进行人为切割来模拟损伤。然而，这种模拟的损伤并不能代表钢结构真实的损伤情况，比如节点板的开裂以及螺栓的松动等。 基于以上目前存在的问题，本项目将在贝叶斯的框架下，提出一种新的基于概率的损伤识别方法：通过稀疏贝叶斯学习，利用结构损伤的稀疏特性，仅使用少量的测量数据，就可以准确地求解结构的稀疏损伤指标。该方法在损伤识别中同时考虑了不确定性因素和温度变化的影响，进而使得结构状态的评估结果更为可靠。本项目将在以下几个方面展开研究： 1） 提出一种基于稀疏贝叶斯学习的损伤识别方法，实现稀疏损伤的定位并定量分析损伤的程度； 2） 通过贝叶斯回归分析，建立结构自振频率和温度的定量关系； 3） 将温度变化的影响纳入贝叶斯概率框架中，进而提高方法的鲁棒性和可靠性； 4） 模拟钢结构节点的力学行为，对节点和构件同步进行损伤识别研究。 本课题计划在实验室建造一个空间钢桁架和一个多层钢框架模型，在不同温度条件下进行振动测试，用来验证所提方法的有效性。

15201920.label: Realisation of objectives
15201920.value: 1) This project has developed a new probabilistic damage detection technique within the Bayesian framework using frequency and mode shape data. The measurement data is assumed with Gaussian noise, and the prior probability of the unknown damage index vector adopts the automatic relevance determination. By using an iterative expectation–maximization (EM) technique, the structural damage index and hyper-parameters are updated. The obtained damage index is zero except for several nonzeros at the damaged elements, realizing the sparsity of the damage identification results. Compared with the regularization-based sparse recovery theory, the EM-based sparse Bayesian learning is more general as more hyper-parameters are used and own clear physical meaning. Moreover, the hyper-parameters can be updated automatically, thereby avoiding the selection of the regularization parameter in the sparse recovery. 2) A new vibration based damage detection technique that simultaneously considers the uncertainties and varying temperature conditions is developed in the sparse Bayesian learning framework. The structural vibration properties are treated as the function of both the damage parameter and varying temperature. The temperature effects on the vibration properties are incorporated into the Bayesian model updating on the basis of the quantitative relation between temperature and natural frequencies. The structural damage parameter and associated hyper-parameters are then solved through the sparse Bayesian learning. An experimental frame is utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed damage detection method. The sparse damage is located and quantified correctly by considering the varying temperature conditions. 3) A two-step damage detection method for space frame structures with semi-rigid connections is developed in this study. Rotational springs with some flexibility are used to model the mechanical behavior of the joints, which enables identification of damage in the bar elements as well as in joints. The first step determines the existence and location of the damaged elements using the l1 regularization technique. In the second step, the damage locations and severities are then identified within the suspicious damaged elements only that are detected in the first step. This process progressively reduces the number of unknown parameters and thus alleviates the instability and divergence problems to improve the damage identification accuracy. An experimental 3D space structure is utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed damage detection method. The results show that damage in structural elements and joints can be correctly located and quantified progressively. The numerical investigation shows that the sensitivity of the modal properties with respect to joint damage is much smaller than to damage in bar elements.

15201920.value: Under the support of the grant, five refereed journal papers have been published; one PhD student was educated (Dr. Wang XY is a Research Assistant Professor at PolyU). The main findings and outcomes of the project include: 1) A new probabilistic damage detection technique within the Bayesian framework has been developed. It can detect sparse structural damage using a small number of sensors data. Moreover, the hyper-parameters can be updated automatically, thereby avoiding the selection of the regularization parameter in the sparse recovery. 2) The new vibration based damage detection technique simultaneously considers the uncertainties and varying temperature conditions. 3) A two-step method is developed for detecting damage in space frame structures with semi-rigid connections.

15201920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201920.value: The applications of vibration-based damage identification methods to practical civil engineering structures are far from maturity due to several difficulties. First, structural damage detection inevitably entails uncertainties, such as measurement noise and modelling errors. Second, varying environmental conditions, especially temperature, may have a more significant effect on structural responses than structural damage. Third, previous damage detection studies usually simulate damage by introducing artificial cuts to steel structures, which is unrealistic and does not represent the actual common damage of steel structures, such as cracks in gusset plates or looseness of bolts. This project has developed a new probabilistic damage detection technique within the Bayesian framework in consideration of the above-mentioned difficulties. The sparsity of structural damage is exploited on the basis of sparse Bayesian learning. Consequently, the sparse damage index will be solved accurately using only a small amount of measurement data. This new technique enables considering the uncertainties and varying temperature effect in the damage identification analysis. Accordingly, a robust assessment of structural conditions can be determined. The success of the project will advance the application of vibration-based damage detection methods to practical civil engineering structures. The proposed technique can also be applied to aerospace and mechanical structures.

15202020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202020.value: This project has led to three major findings: (1) Discovery and modeling of the gigantic effect of phase transition on TE performance. (2) High-performance printable flexible n- and p- TE composite materials. (3) Flexible TEG devices with the new TE composites and fabric sink structure. Two journal papers were published. A large SSRF grant of $7.8 m was secured for developing a rapid recovery wearable system for sportsmen.

15202020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202020.value: The technologies have been further critically assessed in potential applications for wearable systems as alternative microclimate control systems. TE devices equipped with forced convection was compared against fluidic heat exchange in terms of heat transfer, safety and energy consumption. The limitations have been identified, which require further investigation in the future. Another extension of the work is ionic thermoelectric polymers as this study and others discovered several orders of magnitude higher Seabeck coefficient and larger scope for improvement of current out put.

15202020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202020.value: In this project, we developed engineering design tools for FTEGs. Printable p- and n-type composite TE materials were developed together with fabric sinks. The FTEGs have designed, fabricated and evaluated. We discovered a gigantic effect of phase transition on the TE performance of ionic TE materials and have formulated multi-physics models to illustrate the mechanisms and potential application. We studied fabrication processes and fostered scalable FTEG manufacturing processes by optimizing the PEDOT:PSS/ Bi2Te3 or PEDOT:PSS/ Cu2Se or SnSe composite precursor in term of processibility and performance. We also demonstrated a prototype of smart wearable products with sensors, LED displays and FTEG. All the set objectives have been met fully. Our investigations have resulted in three journal publications. A large grant of $7.8 m from SSRF was obtained based on parts of the results of this project. Two PhD students have submitted thesis and now waiting for oral examination.

15202320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202320.value: The phenomenon of acoustic black hole (ABH) exhibits unique appealing features and opens new horizons for structure-borne wave manipulation inside thin-walled structures. Despite the ever-increasing enthusiasm towards this enabling technology, bottle-necking problems exist and hamper its practical applications, among which the deficiency of the current ABH-based technology in coping with low-frequency problems is the most critical. This project will address this issue by introducing intentional nonlinearities into an ABH structure, either mechanically or electromechanically, to create effective system coupling and nonlinear energy transfer across different frequency bands, towards the final objective of breaking down the existing frequency barrier of the ABH. Through systematic system modeling, simulations and experiments, the rich dynamics that nonlinearities can offer will be fully exploited to maximize the expected ABH effects. Among the anticipated benefits is the possibility of producing significant ABH features below the cut-on frequency, which cannot be achieved by the current ABH technology, using ABH elements with a reasonable physical size. The successful completion of the project will constitute a major step forward in the ABH research, promising numerous engineering applications such as vibration control, noise abatement and energy harvesting. Specifically, a new ABH-based energy harvesting (EH) device will be proposed and experimentally tested. Benefiting from the ABH-specific features in term of energy focusing, and thanks to the nonlinearity-induced enhancement in electromechanical coupling and the low-to-high frequency energy transfer, the proposed EH device will allow an effective energy harvesting at both low and high frequencies. 声学黑洞(ABH)现象具有独特的机械特性，为薄壁结构中的结构波的操纵开辟了新的视野。尽管研究者们对这技术的热情与日俱增，但瓶颈问题仍然存在，并阻碍了它的实际应用。其中最关键的是目前的ABH技术主要对低频问题方面的使用不足。本课题将通过在ABH结构中引入人为的机械或机电非线性来解决这一问题，通过有效的系统耦合实现跨越不同频段的非线性能量转移，最终目标是打破ABH现有的频率障碍。通过系统的建模，仿真和实验，充分利用非线性所能提供的丰富的动力学特性，最大限度地发挥和提高预期的ABH效应。预期在合理尺寸的ABH元件上，实现当前ABH技术无法实现的在截止频率下产生的显著ABH特征。本项目的成功完成将会使ABH研究向前迈出重要一步，有望在振动控制、噪声消除和能量回收等众多工程应用中发挥重要作用。

15202320.label: Realisation of objectives
15202320.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out, target the five research objectives summarized above in Section 5.2. A summary is given below: Using a PZT-coated ABH beam as a benchmark, an improved electromechanical semi-analytical model is first established based on Timoshenko theory (Obj.1). The model considers the high-frequency shear and rotational effects of the beam, as well as its coupling with PZT coating and other additional elements like damping layers. External electrical modules including both linear and nonlinear circuits are also integrated into the system, thus forming a complete set of fully coupled electromechanical model. Comparisons with FEM and experimental results validate the proposed model and confirm its higher accuracy and improved efficiency compared with the existing Euler-Bernoulli counterpart (Obj.4). The model allows for flexible design and optimization of the PZT layout and electrical circuits to maximize the EH efficiency or to tactically alter ABH effects in the host structure in views of achieving tactic energy manipulation and vibration control. The proposed model is then used to analyze typical ABH-specific features in an ABH beam such as energy focusing and wave compression. Numerical results demonstrate how PZT installation and layout would affect EH performance Design guidelines in relation to the targeted wavelength and frequency range are developed (Obj.3). To cope with the low frequency deficiency of existing linear ABH structures, electrical nonlinearities are intentionally imposed via PZT patches over an ABH beam to tactically influence its dynamics through electromechanical coupling (Obj.2). Results show the beneficial effects arising from the intentional electrical nonlinearity in terms of generating energy transfer (ET) from low to high frequencies, similar to a NES. Typical electro-mechanical energy transfer process is also enlightened. In addition, simultaneous low-frequency vibration mitigation is also considered. To tackle the problem, different solutions are exploited, exemplified by the use of negative capacitance in the nonlinear shunts with the embodiment of parallel linear branches for low-frequency vibration mitigation. Studies offer a comprehensive design methodology to realize multi-modal vibration control and enhanced ET in different frequency bands. Finally, the proposed linear and nonlinear digital vibration absorbers are implemented in experiments (Obj.5). Experimental results not only validate the basic beam model but also confirm typical phenomena which are predicted numerically such as typical ABH features, electromechanical coupling characteristics and the expected energy transfer using intentional nonlinear electrical shunts. The same issues are also investigated using mechanical nonlinearity using grounded cable. Before that, an inextensible condensation model, with the consideration of the initial curvature, is proposed based on a geometrically exact model for an Euler-Bernoulli cantilever beam (Obj.1). Specific techniques are proposed to numerically implement the developed model with increased accuracy and robustness. Numerical simulations are then conducted to validate the proposed model through comparisons with the finite element method (FEM), examine the assumptions underpinning the model and explore the salient physical features, in particular the inertia-induced effects in both linear and nonlinear cases. Then, the nonlinear features arising from these geometric factors in imperfect ABH beams are investigated, numerically and experimentally (Obj. 2&4). Due to the inefficiency of geometric nonlinearity, mechanical nonlinearity is then introduced into a cantilever ABH beam to enhance the low-frequency ABH effect through low-to-high frequency energy transfer (Obj.2 &3). Using a grounded cable with cubic stiffness, the sweeping results (with excitation frequency below the cut-on frequency) show that the displacement of the low-order modes of the nonlinear ABH beam decreases while the amplitude of its high-order harmonics increases compared to that of its linear counterpart, indicating a significant energy transfer phenomenon enabled by the cable in the nonlinear system. Experiments demonstrate the energy transfer phenomena, and the efficient damping effect achieved in the nonlinear system (Obj.5). Due to the needs arising during the execution of the projects, other aspects which were also specifically mentioned in the proposal but relevant to the present topic, have also been investigated. These include the studies on the effects of generic non-linear system in views of vibration and noise control, other types of ABH structure design benefiting from the aforementioned studies in both thin-and thick-walled structures etc. Listed publications reflect the related research outcomes. In this sense the executed study exceeded the original scope detailed in the original proposal.

15202320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202320.value: (1) The fully coupled electromechanical model of PZT-coated Acoustic Black Hole beams demonstrates its accuracy. The necessity of considering the shear and rotational effects of the beam is demonstrated. Comparisons with experimental and finite element results verify the validity of the model. (2)ABH effects entail effective EH upon a proper design with a due consideration of the PZT layout in relation to the wavelength and the targeted frequency range. ABH offers enhanced harvested power and energy conversion rate. As a rule of thumb, a PZT should be properly sized: the normalized PZT length is close, but slightly larger than 0.5 to ensure a high energy conversion rate. (3) Salient nonlinear features in the electro-mechanical coupled system and ABH-specific benefits are numerically demonstrated, physically explained, and experimentally validated. Electrical nonlinearity enables rich nonlinear phenomena. Two dominant energy transfer paths are shown: one through the formation of a branch/bridging of resonance modes and the other through the generation of higher harmonics. The latter is shown to be more compelling and predominant. Results are further substantiated by energy analyses, particularly in the energy dissipation by different components. Effects of the nonlinearity-enhanced ABH effects are verified through experiments. (4) Achieving broadband multimodal vibration mitigation is shown to be possible through proper circuit design. The addition of linear electrical resonant branches into the nonlinear shunt can deliver dynamic absorber (DA) effects without compromising the nonlinearity-dominated ET, also shown experimentally. 5). The proposed geomatical-nonlinear model explicitly shows nonlinear stiffness and inertia terms arising from the initial structural curvature, and their interplay. Nonlinear effects can be increased by intentionally introducing a platform of uniform thickness at the tip of the ABH beam. Experiments show that achieved energy transfer, however, is very limited. 6). Mechanical nonlinearity using grounded nonlinear cables prove to be a much effective ways to achieve the targeted objectives. A systematic enhancement of the ABH effect at the low frequency range are shown by sweeping analysis below the cut-on frequency. As the external force increases, large third harmonic is triggered, leading to an increase in the damping loss factor of most dominant lower-order modes. Results are also confirmed by experiments. 7). The above research enabled many innovative ABH designs and enlightened our understanding on ABH structures of various types. Studies also enriched our understanding in general nonlinear mechanical systems and elastic meta-materials. More technical conclusions are summarized in the published papers.

15202320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202320.value: Through four years efforts, our group consolidates it leading position, regarded as one of the most active research groups, in ABH area. Apart from the academic reputation gained out of this effort, we have successfully attracted strong interest from several companies, who decided to support our research through collaborative/consulting projects, which shows the great application potentials of the technology. This includes our on-going collaborations with Midea Ltd, one of the largest houseware products in China. The company is interested in exploring the technology for conceiving better and sound-proofing products. On-going collaboration is taking place with more opportunities to be materialized. The potential application of the technology goes way beyond this. In fact, vibration and noise reduction based on ABH technology starts to flourish in recent years, with significant impact in many application areas ranging from mechanical, civil, aeronautical and naval engineering. We’ll explore these opportunities in years to come.

15202820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202820.value: 眾多疾病，特別是心腦血管疾病，都與血液粘稠度相關。臨床上，用於標定血液粘稠度的方法多為侵入式測量 – 即需要採集病人的血液樣本。 在該研究中，基於團隊多年在納米傳感技術方面的研究成果，我們構思了一種全新概念的非侵入式血液粘稠度連續監測方法。我們初期研究結果表明，高頻超聲波對人造血液的不同特性非常敏感。基於此，我們將從機理研究開始，探尋血液粘稠度與高頻超聲特征之間的定量關係。我們將採用增層製造技術來製備一種基於carbon/graphene nanoparticles/polydimethylsiloxane的新型納米複合材料，通過納米尺度的優化使得其對超聲波特征非常敏感。結合超小型壓電激勵器及電子打印技術來構建一種可穿戴的柔性超聲設備。該設備可以用來捕獲不同血液粘稠度對超聲信號的改變程度。研究將從基本原理開始，逐步實現實驗驗證。 該研究的主要創新之處包括: (i) 一種納米技術驅動的可穿戴、柔性超聲技術，可用於捕獲血液粘稠度所誘發之高頻超聲波特征的改變；(ii) 一種非侵入式血液粘稠度連續監測技術。該研究結果將有助於探索一種全新的、低成本、方便操作的健康維護理念。

15202820.label: Realisation of objectives
15202820.value: Physiological disorders (e.g., cardiovascular diseases) are known to have an intrinsic link to blood viscosity (BV). In clinic, BV is usually calibrated with manual or automated viscometers – an invasive method requiring prior acquisition of blood samples. In this RGC-funded GRF project, we developed a new approach to realise non-invasive, in situ and continuous monitoring of BV. We demonstrated that high-frequency ultrasounds show sensitivity to subtle changes in blood simulacrum and investigated the modulation mechanism of BV on ultrasounds at megahertz theoretically and experimentally, leading to quantitative correlations between specific ultrasound features and variations in BV. Based on this, we fabricated a kind of new thin-film-type sensing units with carbon/graphene nanoparticles/polydimethylsiloxane nanocomposites, and inkjet-printed on flexible substrates upon morphological optimization at nanoscale. These sensing units exhibit an ultralight and flexible nature. We networked a multitude of such sensing units with miniaturized ultrasound actuators via stretchable electronics and prototyped a wearable sensing array for implementing non-invasive BV calibration. For proof-of-concept validation, a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-based microfluidic chip was configured to mimic skin with blood vessels, in which a delicate concentration gradient generator was integrated to regulate the viscosity of blood-mimicking fluid. We received very satisfactory results. Within a period of 3.5-year, all the key objectives that were proposed in the original proposal have been successfully accomplished, including: (1) We developed a new approach for non-invasive, in situ, and continuous monitoring of blood viscosity (BV), facilitating a quick, convenient, low-cost, and accurate access to blood-related bioinformation; (2) We theoretically and experimentally interrogated the modulation mechanism of BV on ultrasounds at megahertz, leading to quantitative correlations between subtle ultrasound signal features and variations in BV; (3) We prototyped a stretchable, conformal, and wearable sensing array comprised of innovative nanocomposite sensing units, miniaturized ultrasound actuators, and flexible electronics for non-invasive BV calibration; and (4) We configured a microfluidic chip containing viscosity-regulable blood-mimicking fluid, for proof-of-concept validation of the developed theory and prototyped wearable sensing array. (5) We experimentally validated the developed approach and the prototyped wearable sensing array. The outcomes from this completed GRF project are expected to provide an innovative path towards day-to-day, low-cost self-diagnosis or continuous surveillance of cardiovascular diseases at home, and facilitate clinical personnel to evaluate postoperative rehabilitation or drug absorption in a quick, non-invasive, quantitative, and precise manner.

15202820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202820.value: The key originality of this research include twofold: (i) a nano-engineered sensing array to circumvent a critical bottleneck of today’s wearable healthcare devices (responding only to low-frequency physical, physiological or biochemical signs such as heart rate, blood pressure, finger gesture, etc.; failing to perceive bioinformation in ultrasonic regimes); (ii) non-invasive and continuous monitoring of BV using ultrasounds, with theoretical interpretation and experimental validation. In this RGC-funded GRF project, we developed a new approach to realise non-invasive, in situ and continuous monitoring of BV. We demonstrated that high-frequency ultrasounds show sensitivity to subtle changes in blood simulacrum and investigated the modulation mechanism of BV on ultrasounds at megahertz theoretically and experimentally, leading to quantitative correlations between specific ultrasound features and variations in BV. We also prototyped a wearable sensing array for implementing non-invasive BV calibration. The research outcomes generated from this RGC-supported GRF project have provided an innovative path towards day-to-day, low-cost self-diagnosis or continuous surveillance of cardiovascular diseases at home, and facilitate clinical personnel to evaluate postoperative rehabilitation or drug absorption in a quick, non-invasive, quantitative, and precise manner. A number of high-level publications have been arising from this research project, including 15 papers in top-tier SCI journals, along with another 2 papers in the international conference proceedings. Kindly note that conference attendance during the project carrying-out period was very restricted due to COVID-19. And therefore we only presented two papers at international conference in 2023. Based on this project, a paper, which is intended to submit to Nature, is now under preparation. It takes immense time to prepare a paper to be considered by Nature, and thus it has yet been published before completion of this project. In addition, 2 PhD students were partially supported via this GRF project.

15202820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202820.value: All the proposed objectives have been adequately achieved, and in the meantime the team has also identified some potential directions along which deeper and broader research could be expanded. All work has been done in the laboratory, with mock-up structures. The team is now proactively coordinating with industrial partners, to seek opportunity to validate this technique in real engineering applications in railway industry and aerospace industry, via the team’s industrial partners.

15202820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202820.value: Physiological disorders (e.g., cardiovascular diseases) are known to have an intrinsic link to blood viscosity (BV). In clinic, BV is usually calibrated with manual or automated viscometers – an invasive method requiring prior acquisition of blood samples. In this RGC-funded research project, we developed a new approach to realise non-invasive, in situ and continuous monitoring of BV. We demonstrated that high-frequency ultrasounds show sensitivity to subtle changes in BV. Based on this, we fabricated a kind of new thin-film-type sensing units with carbon/graphene nanoparticles/polydimethylsiloxane nanocomposites We networked a multitude of such sensing units with miniaturized ultrasound actuators via stretchable electronics and prototyped a wearable sensing array for implementing non-invasive BV calibration. The outcomes are expected to provide an innovative path towards day-to-day, low-cost self-diagnosis or continuous surveillance of cardiovascular diseases at home and facilitate clinical personnel to evaluate postoperative rehabilitation or drug absorption in a quick, non-invasive, quantitative and precise manner.

15203120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15203120.value: 邊緣計算中的機器學習模型和數據保護

15203120.label: Project Objectives
15203120.value: To formalize the security challenges in model and data for machine learning at the edge. This objective enables us to understand the real security threats in machine learning at the edge as well as the challenges and limitations when designing protective schemes on edge devices. To design a model extraction framework for understanding and benchmarking blackbox model extraction attack and defense schemes. This framework can be used to understand the nature of model extraction attacks and conduct a fair evaluation on the protective schemes designed in this project. To design a differential privacy based protective schemes against blackbox model extraction attacks. Due to its ease of implementation and low computational cost, the scheme can be used for low-end edge devices, such as IP cams, IoT appliances, and single-board computers, to protect against blackbox model extraction attacks. To investigate a cryptography-based protective scheme against whitebox model extraction attacks where the adversary can penetrate the edge device and gain critical information about the model. This scheme can preserve classification accuracy at the cost of heavy cryptographic computation, so it is more suitable for powerful edge devices such as GPU workstations like Nvidia Jetson AGX Xavier. To design integrity proof and verification schemes against sample poisoning attacks for high-dimensional and high-volume sensory data on edge devices. This scheme prevents an adversary in a hostile edge computing environment to forge or modify sensory data, so that an edge device does not make a wrong control decision, for example, an autonomous vehicle failing to stop in front of a pedestrian due to a distortion of the video taken from the object tracking camera.

15203120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203120.value: 邊緣計算將數據的收集、分析和執行向網絡邊緣盡可能靠近數據源的方向拓展。有統計預測表明2021年將有超過250億個邊緣設備接駁互聯網並產生超過50%的企業數據。 邊緣計算的其中一個核心任務是將邊緣設備智能化，也就是利用這些設備的中央處理器和圖形加速器執行計算機視覺、智能人機交互和物聯網應用。基於邊緣計算的機器學習可以節省大量網絡帶寬和降低延遲。然而由於邊緣設備的軟件和硬件易受攻擊，其安全性備受關注。在本項目中我們將研究兩個常見的邊緣機器學習模型和數據威脅，即模型抽取和樣本污染。基於不同的邊緣計算環境和安全模型，我們將設計不同的保護方案。 本項目將推動邊緣機器學習的蓬勃發展，並為之提供安全性理論基礎。所提出的方案將有益於學術界、工業界和作為一個世界智慧都市的香港。

15203120.label: Realisation of objectives
15203120.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, all objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have achieved objective 3 by the end of year 2021, and objectives 1 and 2 by the year 2023, and objectives 4 and 5 by mid 2024. For objective 1, we first study the security challenges in "model" for machine learning at the edge. We identify model extraction attack as the first challenge we face. We try to understand the real model extraction threats by designing a Membership Inference-enhanced model extraction attack that leverages on in-distribution of "training samples" for pool-based active model extraction (PAME). This work with title "MExMI: Pool-based Active Model Extraction Crossover Membership Inference" is published in NeurIPS 2022. Second, we also study the security challenges in "model" for machine learning at the edge. In particular, we show poisoning attacks particularly in federated learning, can be very threatful and stealthy. To showcase this, we design 3DFed, an adaptive, extensible, and multi-layered framework to launch covert FL backdoor attacks in a black-box setting. It sports three evasion modules that camouflage backdoor models: backdoor training with constrained loss, noise mask, and decoy model. Through extensive experimental results, we show 3DFed can evade the detection of all state-of-the-art FL backdoor defenses, including Deepsight, Foolsgold, FLAME, FL-Detector, and RFLBAT. This work with title "3DFed: Adaptive and Extensible Framework for Covert Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning.” is published in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P), 2023. Second, we study the privacy challenges in "data" for machine learning at the edge. We focus on membership inference and model inversion attacks and study their impact and mitigation mechanisms. We first conducted a comprehensive survey on membership inference attack for edge devices and federated learning environment. This survey with title "Membership Inference Attacks and Defenses in Federated Learning: A Survey" has been published in ACM Computing Surveys in 2025. For edge-based diffusion models, we study new metrics for optimization in model inversion attacks, which show significant attack successful rate over existing methods. This work with title "A Sample-Level Evaluation and Generative Framework for Model Inversion Attacks" is published in AAAI '25. For edge-based federated learning, we study new membership inference attacks for vertical federated learning, which leverages on the mutual information exchange during the VFL training processing. This work with title "ProVFL: Property Inference Attacks against Vertical Federated Learning" is accepted by IEEE TIFS in 2025. As for defense, we also propose several mitigation mechanisms, such as "VAE-based Membership Cleanser against Membership Inference Attacks" published in IEEE TDSC, 2025. For objective 2, we have investigated the theoretical bound of all model extraction attacks using Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory. We then propose a framework, namely Model Extraction Risk Inspector (MER-Inspector), to compare the extraction risks of models under different model architectures by utilizing relative metric values. This work with title "MER-Inspector: Assessing Model Extraction Risks from An Attack-Agnostic Perspective" is published in The Web Conference (WWW) 2025. For large language models, we have also attempted to design a novel model extraction algorithm specifically designed for LLMs. In particular, this algorithm employs a newly defined policy-gradient-style training task that utilizes the responses of victim model as the signal to guide the crafting of preference for the local model. This work with title “‘Yes, My LoRD.’ Guiding Language Model Extraction with Locality Reinforced Distillation.” is published as a long paper in ACL, 2025. For objective 3, we have found existing literature shows that model parameters are vulnerable to extraction attacks which accumulate prediction queries and their responses to train a replica model. So we propose boundary differential privacy against such attacks by obfuscating the prediction responses with noises. This work with title "Protecting Decision Boundary of Machine Learning Model with Differentially Private Perturbation" is published in IEEE TDSC, 2022. For various machine learning tasks, we have also devised various differential privacy schemes to further protect the model and data at the edge. For example, we have trained differentially private GNN for prediction tasks (published in IEEE ICDE 2024 with title "Differentially Private Graph Neural Networks for Link Prediction"), extracted shapes from time series in IoT devices (published in IEEE ICDE 2024 with title "Differentially Private Graph Neural Networks for Link Prediction"), skip-gram learning and graph embedding synthesization (published in ICDE 2025 with title AdvSGM: Differentially Private Graph Learning via Adversarial Skip-gram Model and "Structure-Preference Enabled Graph Embedding Generation under Differential Privacy"), enhancing DP-SGD in standard setting (publised in PVLDB 2024 with title "DPSUR: Accelerating Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent Using Selective Update and Release", in ICDE 2025 with title "Analyzing and Optimizing Perturbation of DP-SGD Geometrically") and federated learning settings (accepted in IEEE TKDE 2025 with title "Analyzing and Enhancing LDP Perturbation Mechanisms in Federated Learning"), and high-dimensional IoT data (published in IEEE TKDE, 2024 with title "LDPTube: Theoretical Utility Benchmark and Enhancement for LDP Mechanisms in High-dimensional Space"). For objective 4, for crytography-based protection scheme on edge devices, we have proposed several homomorphic encryption and oblivious RAM based methods to protect data and model privacy on edge devices in a paper "Secure Traffic Monitoring with Spatio-temporal Metadata Protection Using Oblivious RAM.” published in IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, 2023. For objective 5, we focus on integrity and verification against sample poisoning attacks on edge devices, and have set out several detailed tasks along this line. We first target at edge devices in an IoT network since such a network is vulnerable to security breaches, authenticating the integrity of these messages is essential. In addition, the message may contain sensitive information, and a portion of the information in the message needs to be authenticated. We extend our previous work of Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code published in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing, which only works if the portion to be authenticated is a prefix of the message. A more general scheme called Scalable Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code (SPMAC) is designed and published in IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, 2022. We then extended this work to a fog computing environment where we have both edge and fog nodes. This paper with title "Partial Message Verification in Fog-based Industrial Internet of Things" is publised in Computers & Security in 2023. For more complicated collaborative edge computing scenarios, we also develop a collaborative digital signature scheme, which supports multi-hop verification to reduce the bottleneck cases of certain edge devices. This paper with title "Multi-hop Sanitizable Signature for Collaborative Edge Computing" is publised in Journal of Computer Security in 2024. To detect against GenAI fraud in multimedia, especially videos, we have investigated various integrity and verification techniques. The work is published in ACM Transactions on Privacy and Security, 2024 with title "DeepMark: A Scalable and Robust Framework for DeepFake Video Detection". In an earlier work, we target at edge devices in video surveillance system and propose Stateful-CCSH which adopts correlation coefficient sampling in image hash and learns from previous frames to sample those blocks with more dynamic contents and thus more likely to be tampered in a video forgery. The paper is published in IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 2022.

15203120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203120.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our existing schemes to make it suitable for commercial demonstration and knowledge transfer. We believe that the promotion of these protection schemes will further make an impact on both research and industry community.

15203120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203120.value: Edge computing brings data processing closer to where information is collected—like smart cameras, sensors, and voice assistants—instead of relying on distant cloud servers. This approach speeds up responses, reduces internet congestion, and avoids system-wide failures. With billions of edge devices now handling tasks like facial recognition, voice commands, and factory automation, they rely heavily on AI. However, these devices are more vulnerable to attacks than heavily guarded data centers. Hackers could steal AI models or feed them corrupted data to manipulate their decisions. This project tackles these risks by developing security solutions using cutting-edge encryption and privacy techniques. The goal is to protect AI on edge devices without sacrificing performance. By making edge AI more secure, this research supports smarter, safer technologies in homes, industries, and cities like Hong Kong, which aims to be a leading smart city. The results will benefit tech companies, researchers, and the public by ensuring reliable and trustworthy AI systems in everyday life.

15203520.label: Project Objectives
15203520.value: This project will develop a special element for slender members with end offset to cater for kinks due to spigot joints between vertical posts. Use of conventional modeling by addition of rigid links is impractical when dealing with design of a practical scaffold system with thousands of members. This lack-of-fit tolerance for vertical posts at spigot will be modeled as additional kink imperfection since too tightly fit spigot joints are difficult to construct in practice so impractical but too loosened spigot joints induce excessive imperfections in the post that lead to reduction in buckling resistance. Scissor joints for braces in scaffolds are modeled as scissor element with 4 nodes using the concept of static condensation combining two elements of two nodes each and with internal nodes sharing common displacement but not rotation and Independent computer simulation will be conducted for verification of the proposed computer model. Kink imperfections will be measured and used to compute the load capacity of the scaffold units.
