15203520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203520.value: Every year, people died and hurt in construction sites due to scaffolding collapse in different cities as can be easily seen in internet or news. The recent collapse of a scaffolding system in Hong Kong caused loss of millions of US dollars with great delay in construction time, which is critical for solving the serious housing problem in Hong Kong. In the investigation of the causes of collapse by the proposer in one of his recent projects, he reviewed the current design and found the current analysis and design method for this structural system are inadequate because of ignorance of many important effects such as finite joint stiffness, tolerance and kinks in spigot joints and scissor joint which allow share of displacement but not rotation of the cross bracing members. Although claimed by many as causes are due to workmanship which is admittedly another important factor, design calculation based on the coarse or approximate second-order analysis was found to be inadequate and the engineers over-estimate the capacity of some members leading to the overload of the collapsed scaffolds. As permanent structures, which are seldom loaded to their ultimate loads with 50 year return period, scaffolds are always loaded to close to their ultimate design loads during construction that leads to structural failure easily even though the design contains a factor of safety of 2 which is still insufficient in some cases. The proposer has developed a second-order direct analysis for design of slender steel structures and it has been widely used in the region of Hong Kong, Macau and Mainland China. This new method to the code of practice for structural uses of steel 2011 used by all structural engineers in Hong Kong (http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/steel/SUOS2005.pdf). Unfortunately, this method put in code is still inadequate when handling ultra-slender scaffold structures with kink imperfections and scissor cross braces. In this project, the important parameters as imperfections are assessed and a more reliable method for design of scaffolds and it aims at reducing the casualty rate of scaffolding systems and thus save human lives. This project identifies causes of scaffold failure and proposes design method for their checking. The outcome design approach will used not only in Hong Kong, but in many cities as scaffolds are widely used as temporary structures. 近年来，因脚手架倒塌造成的工程人员伤亡的事件屡有发生。日前在香港发生的一起脚手架倒塌事件不仅造成了数百万美元的损失，严重拖延了工期，而且对当前急需解决住房问题的香港更是沉重打击。在进行某项目的倒塌原因调查时，申请人重新审视了当前的设计方法并发现当前用于脚手架的分析与设计方法并不适用。现方法忽略了部分重要的结构效应，例如有限节点刚度，套筒节点和剪式节点的误差与扭曲。 脚手架倒塌事故多归咎于施工质量，这虽然也是一个重要因素，但是基于相对粗略的二阶分析方法进行脚手架的分析与设计仍是不恰当的。工程师高估了部分杆件的承载力，导致使用中的脚手架出现超载现象。对于永久性结构来说，在50年的设计周期内一般很少出现荷载达到极限承载力的情况。而对于脚手架来说，在施工过程中其所承受的荷载则容易达到极限承载力，并导致脚手架倒塌。在某些情况下，即使采取了2倍的安全系数，脚手架倒塌的情况仍会出现。 申请人已经提出了可以用来设计细长钢结构的二阶直接分析法。在中国内地、香港和澳门地区，该方法已经被广泛使用并收录在2011年香港钢结构作业守则(http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/steel/SUOS2005.pdf)。但是在处理极细长且具有扭曲缺陷和剪刀撑的脚手架结构时，现行方法仍有不足。 本项目将主要评估脚手架结构的初始缺陷等重要参数并提出更可靠的设计方法，以此减少脚手架的事故率，保障工人安全。本项目也将辨别和总结脚手架失效原因并在设计上提出对应的解决方案。项目成果不仅仅可以运用到香港的脚手架项目中，也可以在更多地区推广这种新的设计方法

15203520.label: Realisation of objectives
15203520.value: To tackle the research objectives, various activities were meticulously planned and executed. The project involved the development of specialized elements for scaffold design, advanced modeling techniques, and comprehensive computer simulations to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the proposed methods. The activities undertaken to achieve the objectives are detailed below. The first objective was to develop a special element for slender members with end offset to cater for kinks due to spigot joints between vertical posts. Conventional modeling by addition of rigid links was impractical for designing a practical scaffold system with thousands of members. The lack-of-fit tolerance for vertical posts at spigot joints was modeled as additional kink imperfections. This approach was essential because too tightly fit spigot joints are difficult to construct in practice, while too loose joints induce excessive imperfections in the post, reducing buckling resistance. Through extensive research and simulations, a novel element formulation was created and validated, accurately representing the mechanical behavior of slender scaffold members with end offsets and kink imperfections. This significantly improved the precision of second-order analysis, ensuring safer and more reliable scaffold designs. The publication "A consistent tapered beam-column element allowing for different variations and initial imperfections" in Structures contributed to this objective by addressing the modeling of imperfections in tapered elements and their impact on structural behavior (Chen et al., 2021). The second objective was to model scissor joints for braces in scaffolds as a scissor element with four nodes, using the concept of static condensation. This involved combining two elements of two nodes each, with internal nodes sharing common displacement but not rotation. This advanced modeling approach captured the unique mechanical behavior of scissor joints, which traditional methods often overlooked. The development of this four-node scissor element successfully represented the complex interactions and load-sharing mechanisms within scissor-braced scaffold systems. Validation against real-world scaffold configurations demonstrated the model's accuracy and reliability in predicting structural responses under various loading conditions. The publication "Co-Rotational Formulations for Geometrically Nonlinear Analysis of Beam-Columns Including Warping and Wagner Effects" in International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics provided crucial insights into the nonlinear behavior of beam-columns, which was essential for modeling scissor joints (Chen et al., 2023). The third objective was to conduct independent computer simulations to verify the proposed computer models, focusing on the impact of kink imperfections on the load capacity of scaffold units. Kink imperfections were meticulously measured and incorporated into the simulations to provide a comprehensive understanding of their effects on scaffold performance. The simulations confirmed the robustness and accuracy of the proposed models, with the measured kink imperfections effectively integrated, allowing for precise calculation of load capacities. These results highlighted the critical role of kink imperfections in scaffold stability and informed the development of safer design guidelines. The publication "Progressive collapse of system scaffolds with accidental removal of bracing members" in Journal of Constructional Steel Research specifically addressed the simulation of scaffold collapse scenarios, providing practical design recommendations to mitigate such failures (Chan et al., 2024). Publications and Dissemination The dissemination of the project's findings was achieved through the publication of six papers in reputable journals, contributing significantly to the body of knowledge in scaffold design and structural engineering. The research conducted under this project has led to the following key publications: 1) Tang, Y.Q., Chen, W.F., Liu, Y.P.*, Chan, S.L. (2021). Consistent co-rotational framework for Euler-Bernoulli and Timoshenko beam-column elements under distributed member loads. Advances in Structural Engineering. DOI: 10.1177/136943322098663. 2) Chen, W.F., Liu, Y.P.*, Du, Z.L., Bai, R., Chan, S.L. (2021). A consistent tapered beam-column element allowing for different variations and initial imperfections. Structures. DOI: 10.1016/j.istruc.2021.06.069. 3) Chen, L., Abdelrahman, A.H.A., Liu, S.W.*, Ziemian, R.D., Chan, S.L. (2021). Gaussian Beam–Column Element Formulation for Large-Deflection Analysis of Steel Members with Open Sections Subjected to Torsion. Journal of Structural Engineering. DOI: 10.1061/(ASCE)ST.1943-541X.000318. 4) Chen, L., Liu, S.W., Bai, R.*, Chan, S.L. (2023). Co-Rotational Formulations for Geometrically Nonlinear Analysis of Beam-Columns Including Warping and Wagner Effects. International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics. DOI: 10.1142/S0219455423500529. 5) He, J.W., Huang, D.H., Liu, Y.P.*, Chen, W.F., Ding, Y.Y., Chan, S.L. (2022). An Innovative Cable Element Allowing for Sliding Effect. Advanced Steel Construction. DOI: 10.18057/IJASC.2022.18.2.7. 6) Chan, J.L.Y., Chan, S.L.*, Liu, Y.P., Liu, S.W. (2024). Progressive collapse of system scaffolds with accidental removal of bracing members. Journal of Constructional Steel Research. DOI: 10.1016/j.jcsr.2024.108720. The final output, as highlighted in the sixth paper, integrates the findings from the project and proposes a reliable design approach to mitigate progressive collapse in scaffolds. The new method emphasizes the importance of considering accidental removal of bracing members, providing a robust framework for scaffold design that can be adopted in Hong Kong and other cities globally. In conclusion, the project has successfully realized its objectives by developing advanced modeling techniques and design guidelines that enhance the safety and reliability of scaffold structures. The innovative methods and findings from this research have significant implications for scaffold design, reducing the risk of failures and improving construction site safety. The project's outcomes have been disseminated through high-impact publications, ensuring that the benefits extend to the broader engineering community and contribute to safer construction practices worldwide.

15203520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203520.value: The project yielded significant findings that contribute to the understanding and improvement of scaffold design and safety. The research outcomes are outlined below: 1. Development of Specialized Elements for Scaffolds: A specialized element was developed for slender members with end offsets to model kinks in spigot joints between vertical posts. This innovation was essential for accurately predicting the buckling behavior and load capacity of scaffold members. Insights from the publication "A consistent tapered beam-column element allowing for different variations and initial imperfections" in Structures were crucial for this development (Chen et al., 2021). 2. Advanced Modeling of Scissor Joints: A four-node scissor element was introduced using static condensation to capture the unique mechanical behavior of scissor braces in scaffolds. This ensured accurate representation of load-sharing mechanisms within the scaffold structure. Findings from the publication "Co-Rotational Formulations for Geometrically Nonlinear Analysis of Beam-Columns Including Warping and Wagner Effects" in International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics supported this development (Chen et al., 2023). 3. Verification through Independent Computer Simulations: Extensive computer simulations were conducted to validate the proposed models, incorporating measured kink imperfections. These simulations demonstrated the models' robustness and accuracy in predicting scaffold performance. The publication "Progressive collapse of system scaffolds with accidental removal of bracing members" in Journal of Constructional Steel Research detailed the impact of accidental removal of braces on scaffold stability and proposed practical design recommendations to mitigate such failures (Chan et al., 2024). 4. Practical Implications for Scaffold Design: The findings have significant implications for scaffold design, particularly in improving safety and reliability. The new design method, validated through simulations and real-world scenarios, provides engineers with a more accurate tool for scaffold analysis, reducing the risk of structural failures on construction sites. The dissemination of these findings through high-impact publications ensures that the benefits extend to the broader engineering community, contributing to safer construction practices globally. In conclusion, the project successfully developed and validated advanced modeling techniques and design guidelines for scaffold structures, addressing critical imperfections previously overlooked. These innovations enhance scaffold safety, offering practical solutions that can be adopted in Hong Kong and other cities worldwide. The research outcomes, supported by six key publications, mark a significant advancement in scaffold design and structural engineering.

15203520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203520.value: The research has significantly advanced scaffold safety, but further development is needed to study the progressive collapse of scaffolding systems in greater detail. Future research should focus on understanding how scaffolds respond to the sudden removal of multiple braces or members, simulating real-world scenarios where accidental damage occurs. We propose developing more sophisticated models to predict the progressive collapse of scaffolds under various conditions, including dynamic loads such as wind and seismic activity. Integrating these models with advanced monitoring systems could provide real-time data on scaffold stability, allowing for immediate corrective actions. Collaboration with construction companies and regulatory bodies is essential to pilot these advanced scaffold designs in actual construction projects. By conducting large-scale experiments and field tests, we can validate our models and refine our design recommendations. Expanding this research to include different types of scaffolding and temporary structures will further enhance safety standards across the construction industry. Our goal is to develop comprehensive guidelines and innovative tools that engineers can use to design safer, more resilient scaffolding systems, ultimately reducing the risk of progressive collapse and improving overall construction site safety.

15203520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203520.value: Scaffolding is essential for construction, but collapses can cause injuries and deaths. This research aimed to make scaffolding safer by developing better design methods that consider key imperfections often ignored. This research focused on two main issues: the tiny bends at the joints where scaffold poles connect and the unique behavior of braces that cross to form an X shape. This research developed new computer models to simulate these imperfections more accurately. These models were tested extensively to ensure they could predict when and how scaffolds might fail. The results showed that our new methods are much better at predicting scaffold behavior under load, helping engineers design safer scaffolds. The findings are published in top engineering journals, making the research available to professionals worldwide. The improved design methods from this project can be used not just in Hong Kong but in construction sites globally, reducing the risk of scaffold collapses and enhancing overall construction safety.

15203620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203620.value: Freeform surfaces are being widely used in a variety of applications such as biomedical, dies and molds manufacturing, optics, aerospace, automotive, etc. Mass production of these kinds of surfaces are much needed to meet the increasing demands. However, the current mass finishing methods can hardly obtain nanometer-scale surface roughness which limits their application in the ultra-precision machining field. Although the magnetic field-assisted polishing method can achieve nanometer-scale surface finishing, it is hard to implement uniform polishing on freeform surfaces due to the variation of material removal rate induced by the variation of curvature and surface shape at different locations of the surfaces. This project aims to develop a novel shape-adaptive magnetic field-assisted mass polishing (SAMAMP) technology to cater for the effect of the variation of materials removal rate due to the surface shape in polishing freeform surfaces. SAMAMP makes use of variation of magnetic field applied outside an annular chamber which drives the magnetic abrasives to impinge on and remove materials from the workpiece mounted inside the chamber. The magnetic field is varied according to the variation of the curvature and the shape of the workpiece. SAMAMP technology is developed for high-efficiency finishing of tens to hundreds of freeform components simultaneously. The effect of the magnetic field on the material removal characteristics will be analyzed by the finite element method. Theoretical modeling and simulation of the magnetic field will be conducted to gain deeper understanding of the SAMAMP method. Modelling and analysis of the material removal characteristics and surface generation in SAMAMP will be undertaken to reveal the material removal and surface generation mechanisms which provide the theoretical basis for the development of shape-adaptive control method. The optimal combination of the polishing parameters will be identified by machine learning method. Moreover, a shape-adaptive control method for controlling the current of the electromagnetic coils and a machine learning-based self-optimization algorithm will be developed for real-time adaptation of the variation of material removal due to the shape and curvature effect during polishing. Hence, a SAMAMP system will be established and experimentally validated for the mass polishing of freeform surfaces with uniform material removal. The success of the project will not only provide a novel massive finishing technology and hence the SAMAMP system for the mass production of high value-added intricate freeform surfaces with nanometer-scale of surface roughness but also generate significant impact for the advancement of manufacturing science and ultra-precision machining technology. 自由曲面已被广泛應用于各种场合，例如生物医学、模具制造、光学、航空航天、汽车等。为满足日益增长的需求，大批量生产此类曲面已成为一个十分緊迫的问题。 然而，当前的批量抛光方法難以获得纳米级的表面粗糙度，这限制了它们在超精密加工领域中的应用。 尽管磁场辅助抛光方法可以实现纳米级的表面粗糙度，但是由于表面的不同位置处曲率和形状的变化會引起的材料去除率的变化，很难在自由曲面上进行均匀抛光。 该项目旨在开发一种新型的形状自适应磁场辅助质量抛光（簡稱“SAMAMP”）技术，以剋服由于抛光自由曲面中的形状變化而引起的材料去除率变化的影响。 SAMAMP利用在环形腔室外部施加的旋轉磁场，该磁场驱动磁性磨料撞击安装在腔室内的工件并从中去除材料。磁场强度可根据曲率和工件形状的变化而变化。 SAMAMP技术是为同时加工数十至数百个自由曲面零件而开发的。将通过有限元方法分析磁场对材料去除特性的影响，进行磁场的理论建模和仿真，以加深对SAMAMP方法的了解。擬在SAMAMP中对材料去除特征和表面生成进行建模和分析，以揭示材料去除和表面生成机制，为形状自适应控制方法的发展提供了理论基础。抛光参数的最佳组合将通过机器学习方法确定。此外，将开发一种用于控制电磁线圈电流的形状自适应控制方法和一种基于机器学习的自优化算法，以实时适应由于抛光过程中的形状和曲率變化而导致的材料去除变化。因此，将建立SAMAMP系统并通过实验验证该方法可对自由曲面进行大批量均匀抛光。 该项目的成功不仅将提供一种新颖的大批量抛光技术，而且開發的SAMAMP系统将为大规模生产具有纳米级表面粗糙度的高附加值复杂自由曲面提供解決方案，还将对先進制造科学和超精密加工技術的发展产生重大影响。

15203620.label: Realisation of objectives
15203620.value: The research project successfully accomplished its original objectives through the development and validation of the Shape-Adaptive Magnetic Field-Assisted Mass Polishing (SAMAMP) system. The working principles of the magnetic field-assisted mass polishing process was studied through a series of experiments and kinematic analysis (Objective 1). The SAMAMP system adopted a rotating magnetic field to form abrasive brushes that continuously impinge on freeform surfaces. High-speed imaging and kinematic analysis were adopted to reveal the impingement dynamics of magnetic brushes, providing critical insights into the impingement dynamics of the magnetic brushes, and establishing a clearer relationship between the process parameters such as rotational speed, multiple workpiece spacing, and the resulting surface finish. The material removal characteristics were observed via groups of systematic experiments on various polishing parameters, including the rotational speed, polishing time, type of abrasive slurry, impingement angle, concentration of abrasive slurry, etc. The optimal polishing parameters for various working materials, including SS304 stainless steel, zirconia oxide ceramics, BK7 glass, and Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy were achieved, providing technical guidance for practical implementation. The optimal design of the SAMAMP system was realized through iterative prototyping and experimental validation (Objective 2). The prototype systems incorporate a rotating annular chamber with two pairs of permanent magnetic poles, allowing for the simultaneous polishing of multiple workpieces. Finite element simulations were employed to model the magnetic field distribution, confirming the magnetic flux density across the workpiece surface (Objective 3). To enhance the magnetic field strength within the working area, different designs and combinations of magnets and yokes were simulated. This design optimization ensured both precision and scalability for industrial applications. Modelling and simulation of the generated magnetic field were conducted using ANSYS Maxwell software and COMSOL Multiphysics software, which accurately predicted the magnetic flux distribution and its influence on material removal. The simulations demonstrated a consistent magnetic flux density range of 0.4 to 0.5 Tesla, validating the system’s ability to maintain stable polishing conditions. These findings were instrumental in refining the process parameters to enhance efficiency and surface quality. A material removal distribution model was developed by integrating magnetic field simulations, kinematic analysis of brush motion, and empirical data to provide a scientific understanding of the polishing mechanism (Objective 4). The magnetic field distribution on the workpiece surface was simulated through FEA simulation, the relationship between the magnetic field and the magnetorheological polishing fluid were examined to correlate the magnetic field and the shear stress induced by the rotating abrasive brushes, and polishing parameters such as rotational speed, polishing time and workpiece material were considered in the model. A series of polishing experiments were conducted on both ferrous and non-ferrous materials to validate the model, and the effect of polishing parameters on material removal distribution and surface quality was examined. The results show that the model achieved a predictive accuracy with less than 15% deviation from the experimental results. This model serves as a foundation for process optimization, enabling precise control over material removal rates and surface finish. The development of a shape-adaptive control method represented a critical breakthrough in addressing the fundamental challenge of polishing freeform surfaces with complex, variable geometries (Objective 5). This approach was realized through a multi-stage development process that combined computational modelling with empirical optimization. The core of the system's adaptability lies in the impingement angle determination algorithm that attempted to adjust the impinging angle of the magnetic brushes by controlling the workpiece rotation, corresponding to the unique topography of each workpiece. The algorithm was developed through extensive finite element analysis of magnetic field distributions and iterative experimental testing, which established optimal angular parameters for different surface curvatures, maximizing brush contact while preventing edge over-polishing. Experimental validation of this method yielded exceptional results, demonstrating its capability to maintain form accuracy with peak-to-valley deviations consistently below 4 micrometres while simultaneously achieving arithmetic surface roughness in the nanometre range. The validation process involved polishing a series of test specimens with deliberately complex geometries, including sinusoidal profiles, hemispherical cavities, and micro-structured surfaces. High-resolution white light interferometry and atomic force microscopy were employed to quantify surface quality, revealing uniform material removal with no detectable tooling marks or subsurface damage, demonstrating the robustness of the shape-adaptive control system. Finally, the effectiveness of the SAMAMP system was rigorously verified across an extensive range of materials and surface geometries (Objective 6), establishing its unparalleled versatility in industrial applications. For medical-grade Ti-6Al-4V alloy, the process not only achieved an average surface roughness of 6.9 nanometres but also preserved the material's essential mechanical properties and biocompatibility. Comprehensive material characterization, including X-ray diffraction analysis and energy-dispersive spectroscopy, confirmed the absence of phase transformations or surface contamination during processing. Similar success was demonstrated with 316L stainless steel surgical instruments, where the system eliminated machining marks while maintaining cutting-edge sharpness, and with zirconia oxide dental implants that required both high gloss surfaces and precise edge retention. The technology's application spectrum was further expanded to include optical-grade materials, where it achieved surface roughness values below 1 nanometre on BK7 glass lenses while maintaining λ/4 form accuracy. In the aerospace sector, the system successfully processed nickel-based superalloy turbine blades with freeform turbine blade geometries. Additional validation on cemented carbide cutting tools demonstrated the system's ability to create uniform, damage-free edges with radii below 5 micrometres, significantly improving tool life in subsequent machining operations. The ability to polish multiple workpieces simultaneously significantly enhanced production efficiency, reducing the processing time and cost compared to conventional single-part polishing methods. Through these comprehensive validation trials, an SAMAMP system has established itself as a transformative solution that bridges the gap between precision and productivity in surface finishing. The system's unique combination of adaptive control, batch processing capability, and material versatility addresses critical limitations in current manufacturing paradigms, offering manufacturers unprecedented flexibility in meeting both quality and throughput requirements. Its successful application across such diverse materials and components demonstrates not only the fulfilment of the original research objectives but also the technology's potential to redefine finishing processes in multiple high-value manufacturing sectors. The integration of theoretical modelling, advanced control algorithms, and robust mechanical design has created a platform technology that can be readily adapted to new materials and geometries as industry requirements evolve, ensuring its long-term relevance in precision manufacturing. Up to present, the research results of the above mentioned objectives have been disseminated in 7 refereed journal papers and presented at 3 refereed international conferences. One PhD student has been trained, and a best presentation award was obtained.

15203620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203620.value: Theoretical modelling, computational simulations and experimental validation of the shape-adaptive magnetic field-assisted mass polishing (SAMAMP) for freeform surfaces were completed in this project. This project has successfully advanced the development of the SAMAMP system and attempted to achieve a better scientific understanding of the fundamental parameters that govern the polishing performance of the process and the material removal characteristics. In this project, the working principles and process parameters were systematically studied, revealing that the distribution of the magnetic field and the flow of abrasives play a critical role in achieving uniform material removal and superior surface finish (Journal paper 1-2). The experimental results demonstrated the system’s capability to produce ultra-smooth surfaces with nanometre-scale roughness (arithmetic roughness Ra < 10 nm) across a diverse range of freeform geometries, including optical components, medical-grade Ti-6Al-4V alloys, and high-precision dental ceramics (Journal paper 4-6). Finite element analysis (FEA) was employed to model the magnetic flux distribution, providing critical insights into the relationship between process parameters and polishing performance, and improving the machine design of the SAMAMP system. Magnetostatic simulation with different patterns of permanent magnet arrangement and sequence was performed to maximize the magnetic field in the working region. The material removal mechanism in SAMAMP was physically modelled based on FEA simulation taking into consideration the working material and the magnetic field strength (Journal paper 3, 7), establishing a scientific foundation for predicting and optimizing material removal rates based on abrasive characteristics, magnetic force, and workpiece material properties. The shape-adaptive strategy which enables an optimal solution to accommodate complex and freeform surfaces while inducing sub-micrometre scale form error was developed based on the working principle and the relationship between magnetic field and material removal. The versatility of the SAMAMP system was rigorously validated through its application to a variety of advanced materials (Journal paper 4-6, conference paper 1-2), including additive-manufactured metals, biomedical alloys, and technical ceramics. The successful development of a functional SAMAMP prototype marks a significant milestone, showcasing the system’s potential for high-throughput, batch-mode polishing of ultra-precision surfaces. On the whole, this project has made substantial contributions to the field of precision surface finishing by establishing SAMAMP as a robust and scalable solution for mass polishing of freeform surfaces. The integration of adaptive control, theoretical modelling, and experimental validation not only deepened the scientific understanding of magnetic field-assisted polishing but also paved the way for its diversified industrial applications.

15203620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203620.value: The SAMAMP system has significant potential for further advancement through the integration of automation control and AI-driven smart polishing. Future research would focus on the development of adaptive learning algorithms to optimize the polishing parameters in real time, enhancing precision while reducing manual intervention. It is also important to expand its applicability to emerging materials and complex geometries, ensuring its continued relevance in next-generation manufacturing processes. Moreover, the development of a variety of SAMAMP series, such as the mechanism of material removal and incorporation of hybrid energy fields (e.g., ultrasonic or electrochemical assistance), could further improve the efficiency, surface quality, and applicability in different industries, so particular attention will be paid to difficult-to-machine materials and high-value-added components. Another critical direction is technology transfer and commercialization, requiring scalability testing, cost-effective manufacturing of polishing tools, and industry collaboration to transition SAMAMP from lab scale to industrial adoption. The development of standardized process guidelines and certification protocols will be essential for widespread acceptance in sectors including aerospace, medical devices, and optics. By pursuing these strategies, SAMAMP will evolve into a next-generation, intelligent polishing platform, bridging the gap between academic research and smart precision manufacturing.

15203620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203620.value: This project developed a novel polishing technology, namely Shape-Adaptive Magnetic Field-Assisted Mass Polishing (SAMAMP), that can smooth out complex, high-precision surfaces with high accuracy. This process applies magnetic fields to control nanoscale polishing particles, allowing it to work on freeform complex shapes, such as medical implants, optical lenses, or aerospace components, without damaging them. Unlike traditional ultra-precision polishing, which produces high-quality surfaces but long production lead times, SAMAMP is efficient and adaptable, and produces ultra-smooth finishes better than most existing industrial mass polishing methods. The scientific value of this technology lies in its versatility and efficiency. It works on a wide range of materials, from metals to ceramics, and polished multiple parts at once, making it ideal for mass production and industrial practices. The theoretical modelling and kinematic analysis provided a deeper understanding of the proposed process, guiding future practical implementation. The proposed SAMAMP could revolutionize industries including medical device or optics manufacturing, where a flawless surface is critical. On the whole, SAMAMP offers a faster and reliable way to polish high-value parts while maintaining high surface quality. Its potential applications could benefit a variety of industries including electronics, optics, biomedical, aerospace, etc., making advanced manufacturing more efficient and accessible.

15203920.label: Realisation of objectives
15203920.value: The project comprehensively addressed its three core objectives through multi-scale investigations spanning global biogeographic analysis and targeted urban hotspot studies, significantly advancing our understanding of airborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance in the context of planetary microbiome dynamics. Objective 1 was fully realised via complementary planetary-scale and targeted urban approaches. The global study of 370 air particulate samples from 63 sites established a groundbreaking atlas of airborne bacteria, cataloging over 27 million nonredundant 16S rRNA sequences. This investigation employed the 16SPIP (16S Pathogenic Identification Process) pipeline specifically designed for clinical samples but adapted here for environmental analysis, overcoming limitations of conventional culture methods. Critically, it demonstrated the urban pathogen paradox where city air harbours lower total bacteria but significantly higher proportions of potential pathogens than rural areas—particularly high-mortality-risk ESKAPE pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter species)—with 22.4% of identified pathogens occurring exclusively in urban environments. Complementing these global insights, targeted urban investigations have been conducted in two potential hotspot sources of airborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance—wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) in Hong Kong and hospitals in Guangzhou. The Hong Kong WWTP study sampled the sewage, sludge, effluent, and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) near the treatment facilities in autumn. PM2.5 in ambient urban environment and in a coastal background site were also collected simultaneously for comparison. All these samples underwent DNA extraction, qPCR quantification of the 16S rRNA gene, and metagenomic sequencing. This approach successfully identified certain kinds of putative antibiotic-resistant pathogens, including World Health Organization (WHO)-priority pathogens and ESKAPE group members, particularly enriched in PM2.5 from WWTP and urban areas. The second study collected PM2.5 samples in a hospital in Guangzhou in summer and winter, with a general urban site for comparison. Metagenomic sequencing was conducted after DNA extraction. By analysing the abundance and diversity of the assembled metagenomes in summer and winter, as well as the functional genes they harboured (e.g., virulence genes), we have demonstrated the seasonal variations of airborne human virulent bacteria and quantified the exposure risks via inhalation. Objective 2 was substantially advanced, though with acknowledged limitations in direct culture of specific viral pathogens in lab environments. The assessment of infectivity and antimicrobial resistance was robustly achieved through metagenomic sequencing, analysis of metabolic activity markers, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), virulence factors (VFs), and mobile genetic elements (MGEs). Potentially virulent antibiotic-resistant bacteria (PARB) were identified in hospital air, with a concentration of around 2.9 genome copies per cubic meter. The occurrence patterns of β-lactam resistance genes and their bacterial hosts in hospital air showed a statistically significant correlation with in-ward β-lactam-resistant infection rates. Besides bacterial pathogens, we have also expanded our research to include airborne phages. We investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of phage-host linkage on airborne resistomes in airborne PM2.5 and their health implications to the human respiratory microbiome in selected cities of China (Beijing, Hangzhou, and Guangzhou). However, attempts to culture viral pathogens from PM2.5 samples were unsuccessful, reflecting the well-documented challenge that the vast majority of environmental microbes resist laboratory cultivation. Consequently, infectivity potential was inferred through sophisticated bioinformatic analyses: the matches of CRISPR (abbreviation for ‘clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats’) between metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and phage contigs that carry ARGs were predicted using CHERRY_crispr with default parameters. The significant enrichment of CRISPR matches in winter and spring indicated a potential increase in infectivity of ARG-carrying phages on hosts during these seasons. By stained with the LIVE/DEAD BacLight™ Bacterial Viability Kit and analysed by a BD FACSVia Flow Cytometer, the viability of airborne microorganisms was also studied, which showed obvious fluctuations across sampling dates which could be due to meteorological influence. Overall, the integration of metagenomics, flow cytometry, and statistical correlation with clinical outcomes provided indirect evidence of airborne transmission and exposure risks of pathogens and antimicrobial resistance. Objective 3 has been addressed by exploring the association between meteorological parameters and atmospheric chemical constituents and the abundance, diversity, and viability of airborne pathogens and infectivity/antimicrobial resistance traits. A unique seasonal pattern in phage-ARG associations was observed in the selected cities, closely resembling China's typical "flu season", with peaks observed in winter and spring. A reduced ratio of the abundance of putative phage-associated ARGs to MGEs was significantly correlated with the increased ratio of bacterially associated ARGs and the increased levels of oxidative gases, e.g., O3 and SO2. The results indicate that under urban atmospheric selective pressures, such as oxidant gases, phage is potentially more susceptible than the associated host. Further analysis quantitatively demonstrated that oxidative gases are comparable to meteorological factors (e.g., temperature and relative humidity) in affecting the percentage of phage-associated ARGs, showing anthropogenic impacts are a critical driver in reducing phage infectivity, repressing phage communities, and shaping the ecological interactions. Our findings highlight that understanding phage-host interactions within airborne antibiotic resistomes, as well as the influence of climate zones and pollution levels, has important and unique implications for human health in urban areas.

15203920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203920.value: This project yielded significant insights into the sources, dynamics, and risks associated with airborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in urban environments. The global microbiome survey revealed that while the total abundance of global airborne bacteria in the troposphere is 1 to 3 orders of magnitude lower than that of other habitats, the number of bacterial taxa (i.e., richness) in the atmosphere is comparable to that in the hydrosphere, and its maximum occurs in midlatitude regions. Critically, compared to the rural counterpart, the urban air harboured lower total bacteria but significantly higher proportions of potential pathogens—particularly high-mortality-risk ESKAPE pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter species)—with 22.4% of identified pathogens occurring exclusively in urban environments (Zhao et al, 2022). Further studies focusing on potential source environments (i.e., WWTPs and hospitals) have revealed their influence on the seasonal patterns and spatial distribution of airborne pathogens and ARGs in urban areas. WWTP-derived sources were responsible for around 13% of the bacteria and over 55% of the airborne ARGs detected in urban PM2.5. Clinically relevant ARGs and priority pathogens, including ESKAPE group members, were significantly enriched in PM2.5 collected near WWTP facilities and in urban areas compared to coastal backgrounds (Xie et al., 2022). Hospital environments were also found to pose a heightened inhalation risk. PM2.5 within the hospital setting harboured nearly double the abundance of ARGs compared to general urban ambient air, irrespective of season. Metagenomic analysis quantified the presence of potentially virulent antibiotic-resistant bacteria (PARB) in hospital PM2.5 at 2.9 genome copies per cubic meter, leading to an estimated daily inhalation exposure of approximately 50 virulent PARB genomes for individuals in these settings – a level ten times greater than exposure via water ingestion. Critically, the profiles of β-lactam resistance genes and their bacterial hosts within hospital air PM2.5 showed a statistically significant correlation with patterns of β-lactam-resistant infections occurring within the hospital wards (Wu et al., 2022). Research into phage-host interactions revealed their substantial role in shaping the airborne resistome and its potential health implications. Airborne phage communities were distinct and showed strong connections to human- and water-associated viromes. Alarmingly, 57% of predicted bacterial hosts for these airborne phages are potential pathogens. For ARG-carrying phages specifically, this proportion rose to over 60%. ARG-carrying phages showed distinct profiles across urban sites, with significant enrichment in abundance, diversity, temperate lifestyle, and CRISPR matches to identified bacterial genomes in winter and spring. They also accounted for 52% of MGE-ARG pairs, displaying a unique "flu season" pattern. The presence of potential CRISPR matches between ARG-carrying phages and pathogenic metagenome-assembled genomes suggested the possible delivery of ARGs from phages to human opportunistic pathogens and potential infectivity of phages. Moreover, climate conditions and pollution levels significantly account for the dynamic distribution of the antibiotic resistome between phage and host. Notably, natural and anthropogenic stressors, particularly wind speed, UV index, and level of ozone, potentially accounted for over 80% of the seasonal dynamics in phage-bacterial pathogen linkages related to antibiotic resistance. Overall, our studies revealed spatiotemporal variations in airborne pathogens and phage-bacteria interactions, highlighted the role of urban hotspots in increasing the abundance and diversity of airborne bacteria and functional traits such as virulence and AMR, and emphasised the influence of environmental factors in shaping these patterns.

15203920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203920.value: Our findings suggest several important directions for future research and practical actions. The evidence identifying WWTPs and hospitals as key emission sources for airborne ARGs and pathogens necessitates the development and testing of targeted mitigation technologies. This includes the development of real-time biosensors for detecting high-risk airborne bacteria, as well as advanced air filtration and disinfection systems specifically designed for the ventilation of these high-risk facilities, to better protect workers and nearby communities. The strong association observed between environmental factors and phage-bacteria interactions further underscores the importance of precisely quantifying how these key drivers—such as particulate matter, wind speed, UV index, and ozone—affect the viability and infectivity of airborne pathogens under real atmospheric conditions. Understanding these cause-effect relationships will be crucial for predicting and managing the spread of airborne pathogens and AMR. Furthermore, establishing direct clinical linkages represents a critical translational step. Future research should continue to actively partner with hospitals to causally correlate quantified levels of airborne pathogens and types of AMR to actual patient infection rates. These efforts should be supported by culture-based experiments to uncover the underlying mechanisms and validate the observed associations. By addressing these research gaps, we can move towards more effective monitoring, prevention, and control strategies to reduce the risks posed by airborne pathogens and AMR in urban environments.

15203920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203920.value: This project explored the hidden dangers in the air we breathe, with a focus on pathogens and antibiotic resistance carried by fine particles in urban environments. The main goal is to understand where these threats come from, how they spread, and the risks they pose to urban populations, especially regarding respiratory infections and the impact of environmental factors. Our research found that, although urban air may contain fewer total bacteria than rural air, it has a much higher proportion of pathogens and antibiotic resistance genes. Notably, urban hotspots such as hospitals and wastewater treatment plants were identified as key emission sources. The research also discovered that phages (viruses that infect bacteria) play an important role in spreading antibiotic resistance between bacteria. The infectivity of airborne phages and their interactions with bacterial hosts can be influenced by environmental conditions like wind speed, UV index, and ozone levels. Overall, our findings provide scientific evidence that both human activities and environmental factors shape the presence and spread of airborne pathogens and antibiotic resistance. This knowledge supports the development of targeted strategies, such as improved emission controls at key sources and pollution reduction, to reduce exposure and better protect public health.

15204320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204320.value: ‘Track-changes’ is a generic concept in many ways: a word processor’s function, a tool of health diagnosis, a change-detection tool in remote sensing. This concept can equally be adopted in diagnosing problems in city underground though it is not commonly perceived. Due to increasing demand of city population requiring water supplies, sewer discharge, energy and telecommunication, city’s underground is getting more complex (more utility types) and congested (higher density). The aging creates problems, like ground subsidence caused by void formation initiated after pipe leak, and thus requires a scientific approach of proper non-invasive imaging and health diagnosis for decision-making about a rehabilitation or replacement. This process is best conducted by Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) because of (1) its 2D and 3D image representations reflecting ground truth, (2) efficiency of data capture, and (3) cm-scale fine resolution. While slicing the underground with GPR images is widely adopted, it is still highly subjective in terms of data collection, processing and imaging. So it is unreliable for ‘track-changes’. A first of its kind, an objective, systematic and bias-free workflow for GPR slice/C-scans has been established by PI’s research team (Luo et al., 2019). Still, health diagnosis cannot rely on one image. It requires ‘track-changes’ with baseline images. So, this proposed project will develop a solution by firstly building an efficient auto-tracking system for GPR imaging in very dense grid. Then, image database of pattern recognized in GPR radargram/B-scans (vertical section’s images parallel to GPR traverses) and classification of two major underground hazards (void of spherical/elliptical shapes and localized pipe leak) will be established. An image-based approach will then be attempted for change-detection diagnosis. The above development will involve lab/field experiments, and simulations. Finally, feasibility of applying the developed solution in city underground’s hazards will be studied by the ratio of success to false alarm through ground truthing. This leads to a decision-making process normally made by analyst but in an objective, systematic and bias-free manner, especially when the most skilled analyst would fall short of handling huge volume of data. Together with colleague Dr. Xiaolin Zhu, a specialist in remote sensing, and Dr. Victor Khoo from the Future Cities Lab (FCL)/Singapore Lands Authority (SLA), this research will develop a solution for urban underground health imaging and diagnosis. It is believed this project will trigger the establishment of a full coverage health-record for underground utilities and associated hazards with GPR in cities. “ 變化檢測”在許多方面是一個通用概念：文字處理器的功能，健康診斷工具，遙感中的變化檢測工具。儘管人們普遍不認識該概念，但它同樣可以用於診斷城市地下的問題。由於城市人口的需求不斷增加，需要供水，下水道排放，能源和電訊，城市的地下設施變得越來越複雜（公用事業種類更多）和交通擁擠（密度更高）。老化會產生問題，例如由於管道洩漏後引發的空洞形成而引起的地面沉降，因此需要科學的方法進行適當的非侵入式成像和健康診斷，以做出有關修復或更換的決策。此過程最好由探地雷達（GPR）進行，因為（1）其2D和3D圖像表示可反映地面真相，（2）數據採集效率和（3）厘米級精細分辨率。雖然廣泛採用GPR圖像對地下切片的方法，但在數據收集，處理和成像方面仍然具有很高的主觀性。因此，在今天“變化檢測” 仍然是不可靠的。 PI的研究團隊已經建立了第一個此類的，用於GPR切片/ C掃描的客觀，系統且無偏差的工作流程（Luo等人2019）。 儘管如此，健康診斷仍不能依靠一張圖像。它要求對基準圖像進行“變化檢測”。因此，此項目將通過首先為非常密集的網格中的GPR成像構建高效的自動跟踪系統。然後，將建立在GPR雷達圖中識別出的模式圖像數據庫，並對兩個主要地下危險（地底空洞和局部管道洩漏）進行分類。然後將嘗試基於圖像的方法進行變化檢測診斷。以上開發將涉及實驗室/現場實驗和正演模擬。最後，將通過地面實測的成功率與誤報率之比，來研究將開發的解決方案應用於診斷城市地下災害的可行性，讓分析人員以客觀，有系統地和無偏見的方式進行決策，尤其是在最熟練的分析人員也無法處理大量數據的情況下。這項研究將為城市地下健康成像和診斷開發解決方案, 建立地下公用事業及城市中危害的全覆蓋健康記錄。

15204320.label: Realisation of objectives
15204320.value: All objectives are 100% achieved, and reflected by the 9 journal papers. For objective 1: To precisely depict the subsurface by GPR, an accurate geo-referencing technique on each GPR scan is essential. Traditional geo-referencing of GPR scans requires a survey wheel to walk along a predetermined grid, or relies on the Global Navigational Satellite Systems (GNSS) to work under open sky environments where enough satellites are available. In this objective, we used a mobile mapping system (MMS) backpack guided by SLAM as the geo-referencing device for synchronizing GPR scans in areas with bad or no GNSS, and is free of control points. A method was developed to synchronise the SLAM positioning and GPR measurements and then validate the proposed method’s precision and accuracy with a site case. It was proved that the integrated time and labour required in the traditional gridding are minimized for improving the GPR survey efficiency, facilitating the large-scale survey in dense urban areas where good GNSS coverage is unavailable. For objective 2: In this objective, we proposed an unsupervised superpixel-based change-detection method using GPR time-lapse slices combining fuzzy c-means and the Markov random field model to investigate an invisible subsurface change due to buried void using time-series measurements. First, simple linear iterative clustering was applied to the difference image, which was generated using paired time-lapse images after intensity registration to create different scales superpixel maps. Then, fuzzy c-means clustering was used to generate superpixel-based change maps. Finally, the Markov random field model was used to integrate the information of adjacent neighbourhoods in three dimensions to iteratively refine the change map. We designed two underground cavities (one representing shallow local voids and the other representing voids near pipeline networks) to verify the capability and adaptability of the proposed method. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of the method, with F1-scores of 0.82, 0.69, 0.69, and 0.65 and kappa coefficients of 0.81, 0.69, 0.68, and 0.64. For objective 3, We reckoned that quality of C-scan images is determined by the spatial resolution and visualisation contrast. Previous studies have standardised the suitable spatial resolution of GPR C-scans; however, their measurement normalisation remains arbitrary. Human bias is inevitable in C-scan interpretation because different visualisation algorithms lead to different interpretation results. Therefore, an objective scheme for mapping GPR signals after standard processing to the visualisation contrast was established. Focusing on two typical scenarios, a reinforced concrete structure and an urban underground, this study illustrated that the essential parameters were greyscale thresholding and transformation mapping. By quantifying the normalisation performance with the integration of image segmentation and structural similarity index measure, a greyscale threshold was developed in which the normalised standard deviation of the unit intensity of any surveyed object was two. A transformation function named “bipolar” was also shown to balance the maintenance of real reflections at the target objects. By providing academia/industry with an object-based approach, the works in this objective contributes to solving the final unresolved issue of 3D GPR imaging (i.e., image contrast) to better eliminate the interfering noise and better mitigate human bias for any one-off/touch-based imaging and temporal change detection. For objective 4, we integrated a generic workflow of time-lapse GPR's applications to image invisible air void and pipe leakage according to the deliverables in objectives 1 to 3.

15204320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204320.value: We built an efficient optical and auto-tracking system of GPR locations for full-scale dense imaging for city underground based on mobile mapping system. A radargram/B-scan and image database of pattern recognition and classification of spherical/elliptical air void and localized pipe leak, based on an unsupervised superpixel-based change-detection method, was established. The associated slice/C-scan and image-based approach for change-detection diagnosis based on the GPR tracking system was established. Finally, we produce a study on the feasibility of applying the system (objective 1), database (objective 2) and approach (objective 3) for time-lapse diagnosis in city underground’s hazards. The deliverables of the four objectives are published in the nine journal papers.

15204320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204320.value: There are lots of potential for research, application and commercial value of the deliverables of this project in the city because time-lapse GPR in city underground, analogous to medical imaging of human bodies, is required due to more congested underground utilities and their derived hazards like voids and leakage.

15204320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204320.value: Ageing and complex underground utility infrastructure present a significant challenge for modern society, requiring long-term monitoring and maintenance to prevent economic and social costs associated with infrastructure degradation and failure. In this study, we proposed an unsupervised superpixel-based change-detection method using ground-penetrating radar time-lapse slices combining fuzzy c-means and the Markov random field model to investigate an invisible subsurface change due to buried void using time-series measurements. Our method represents a significant contribution to the field of GPR-based change detection and shall be able to improve the long-term monitoring and maintenance of complex underground utility infrastructure.

15204820.label: Project Objectives
15204820.value: [Hardware] Objective 1 - acquiring signals in a non-intrusive manner. Achieving a high-precision tracking platform requires considerable efforts in the hardware design. To this end, we propose the triangulation-based tracking solution powered by an antenna array to meet our stringent hardware demands on the platform. Thus, our first objective is to design and build an “K+1”-model RF frontend, which contains K array elements plus 1 additional side antenna. [Middleware] Objective 2 - generating protocol-free spatial spectrums. The main difficulty of generalizing the past indoor localization systems to track different IoT devices is in the diversity and variety of wireless protocols. Thus, at the heart of the platform is the capability that shield device diversity and protocol varieties from tracking algorithms. For this purpose, our second objective is to design and build a middleware between the hardware and the upper layer. By feeding the downconverted RF signals though the two channels, the middleware generates a protocol-free spatial spectrum that indicates the Angle of Arrival of the receiving signal. [Learnware] Objective 3 - developing a deep tracking framework. The traditional triangulation-based localization works well in the relatively stationary environment without the presence of multipath. However, the reality is that the indoor environment is full of reflectors, which produces numerous multipath propagations. As a result, the spatial spectrum may be distorted and the Line-of-Sight (LoS) AoA is severely skewed. To address this challenge, we resort to the deep neural networks. Our third objective is to develop a deep tracking framework over the platform. In addition, a small number of RFID tags are deployed in the region with known locations as anchors and read every few minutes. We take advantage of the transfer learning and the anchor tags to update the neural networks for accommodating the dynamic in the surroundings. [Case Study] Objective 4 - applying the platform to typical applications. The successful implementation of the framework provides research community a novel way and proven experience in practice. Our final objective is to apply the platform to two typical applications, checkout-free supermarket and RFID-assisted warehouse management. We also plan to release the corresponding labels and signal data to the community for building an open and free benchmark library, targeting at building a version of "ImageNet" in the IoT.

15204820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204820.value: Tracking IoT devices inside buildings has become a growing business interest. It prompts a series of key IoT applications such as indoor navigation, augmented reality, location-aware pervasive computing, advertising and social networking. On the other hand, to accommodate the individuation and diversification of user demands, numerous IoT wireless protocols (such as RFID, WSN, LoRa, Sigfox, NB-IoT) have been proposed forward nowadays. Such diversity of wireless protocols has become a serious challenge in the management and tracking of IoT devices. At present, the academia and the industry usually use the divide-and-conquer paradigm to handle this issue, namely, existing tracking solutions have been tailored for specific types of devices. An all-in-one platform for tracking all types of IoT devices does not exist. As a consequence, users must deploy multiple tracking systems in a warehouse where various IoT devices are running or equip multi-radios to a single device. Both impose huge additional costs in installation and maintenance. This proposal aims to build a general-purpose tracking platform for non-intrusively and high-precisely localizing different kinds of IoT devices simultaneously. Specifically, the platform is planned to track five mainstream IoT devices (RFID, Zigbee, LoRa, SigFox and NB-IoT) and be extensible to any other type of IoT devices with minimal effort. The platform provides three main features. First, it is non-intrusive and transparent to tracked devices. The transmitting device is then identified and localized once its packet is intercepted and captured by the platform. Second, the platform is protocol-free due to its capability of shielding the device diversity and protocol variety from the upper-layer tracking algorithms. Third, the platform would also allow for flexibility of deployment and being cost effective. 15204820.label: Realisation of objectives
15204820.value: This project aimed to develop a comprehensive and general-purpose platform capable of non-intrusively tracking diverse IoT devices operating across multiple wireless protocols indoors with high precision. The original objectives addressed four core aspects: hardware design for signal acquisition, middleware development for protocol-agnostic processing, advanced learnware for robust localization under complex propagation conditions, and practical application validation in real-world scenarios. The following details how each objective has been achieved through innovative research and engineering efforts, highlighting the platform’s technical capabilities and performance. Objective 1: Hardware – Non-intrusive K+1 Antenna Array Frontend The first objective focused on creating an antenna array frontend capable of capturing signals from heterogeneous IoT devices without requiring any modification to or cooperation from those devices. This was accomplished by designing a large-scale 8×8 planar antenna array supplemented with a dedicated reference antenna (“+1” side channel). The array elements were carefully engineered to provide wide spatial coverage with fine angular resolution. A novel dual-channel architecture was implemented, where the main channel sequentially sampled signals from each array element using RF switches, while the side channel continuously recorded reference signals. This design enabled stable phase synchronization critical for accurate angle-of-arrival (AoA) measurements. The hardware platform supports all targeted protocols within the ultra high frequency band, including NB-IoT, LoRa, RFID, Sigfox, and ZigBee, thereby achieving true non-intrusiveness and multi-protocol compatibility. The antenna array’s precise calibration and the innovative side channel enabled spatial resolution sufficient to estimate AoA with angular errors as low as 1–2 degrees. This hardware foundation was essential for the subsequent processing and localization stages, fully realizing the first objective. Objective 2: Middleware – Protocol-Free Spatial Spectrum Generation The second objective was to develop middleware that transforms the raw signals acquired by the hardware into a unified, protocol-independent representation suitable for localization. We achieved this by devising a protocol-free phase estimation algorithm that exploits the dual-channel hardware. By dividing the complex signal samples of each antenna element by those of the reference antenna in the side channel, protocol-dependent distortions such as modulation schemes, preambles, carrier frequency offsets, and device-specific phase shifts were effectively canceled. This resulted in a stable relative pseudo-phase that contains only the geometric phase information related to signal direction. Using this clean phase information, the middleware computes spatial spectrums that accurately represent signal power as a function of arrival angles, regardless of protocol. This approach eliminated the need for any prior knowledge or calibration of devices and enabled real-time processing of multiple protocols simultaneously. The protocol-free middleware significantly improved AoA estimation accuracy compared to traditional methods and provided a scalable solution for heterogeneous IoT device tracking, thus fully meeting the second objective. Objective 3: Learnware – Deep Learning for Robust Tracking under Multipath Recognizing the challenges posed by multipath propagation and dynamic indoor environments, the third objective focused on developing a deep learning framework to robustly estimate device locations from the protocol-agnostic spatial spectrums. Inspired by multi-view stereo vision, the large antenna array was subdivided into multiple overlapping sub-arrays, each producing an independent AoA estimate. A two-stage neural network architecture was introduced: the first stage consists of a convolutional neural network trained to extract the true line-of-sight angle from each sub-array’s spatial spectrum, filtering out reflections and noise; the second stage aggregates these AoA estimates via a fully connected network to compute the final three-dimensional device position. This deep learning pipeline demonstrated substantial improvements in localization accuracy under multipath conditions, achieving median positioning errors of approximately 16 cm in realistic indoor scenarios. The approach generalized well across different device types and environments without requiring retraining, fulfilling the third objective of robust, multipath-resilient localization. Objective 4: Case Study – Deployment in Practical Scenarios To validate the platform’s practical applicability, the fourth objective involved deploying the system in representative real-world scenarios such as smart warehouses and checkout-free retail stores. The platform successfully tracked a diverse array of IoT devices—including NB-IoT, LoRa, passive RFID tags, Sigfox, and ZigBee sensors—simultaneously and non-intrusively in an integrated system. Localization accuracy was consistently high across protocols, with median three-dimensional errors below 20 cm for all device types. The system maintained strong robustness under challenging conditions including non-line-of-sight obstructions, with only minor degradation in accuracy. Furthermore, the platform demonstrated scalability to large areas and device populations, confirming its suitability for industrial and commercial applications. These deployments fully realized the final objective by showcasing a unified, cost-effective tracking solution applicable to complex IoT environments. In summary, all four original project objectives have been fully achieved through systematic hardware innovation, middleware algorithm design, advanced deep learning methods, and rigorous practical validation. The resulting general-purpose deep tracking platform non-intrusively acquires heterogeneous IoT signals, generates protocol-free spatial representations, and leverages deep neural networks to deliver robust, high-precision localization under realistic indoor multipath conditions. Real-world case studies confirmed the platform’s effectiveness, scalability, and readiness for deployment in industrial and retail settings. Collectively, these accomplishments mark a significant advancement in unified IoT device tracking technology, providing a scalable and flexible foundation for diverse emerging applications.

15204820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204820.value: Objective 1: Hardware – Non-Intrusive Signal Acquisition We developed a novel K+1 antenna array architecture that integrates an 8×8 planar array with an additional side antenna to provide a stable reference channel, enabling passive, protocol-agnostic capture of signals from heterogeneous IoT devices without modification (MobiSys 2020). The LSAB design further improved spatial and temporal efficiency by dynamically selecting antenna subsets to reduce hardware complexity without sacrificing AoA accuracy (INFOCOM 2022, TOSN 2022). Advances in reconfigurable antenna technologies also enabled cross-medium reception across multiple frequency bands (MobiCom 2024). These innovations collectively reduced cost and enhanced scalability for large-scale IoT tracking deployments. Objective 2: Middleware – Protocol-Free Spatial Spectrum Generation Our middleware algorithms generate unified spatial spectrums by removing protocol-dependent distortions such as modulation and carrier offsets through side-channel referencing (IEEE IoT Journal 2024, MobiSys 2020). Techniques for physical-layer fingerprinting of passive RFID signals (SECON 2023) and cross-technology translation (SenSys 2023) further enhanced protocol agnosticism. Signal enhancement methods enabled robust phase extraction under low-power conditions (INFOCOM 2021). These middleware advances enable a single system to seamlessly process signals from diverse IoT standards, simplifying heterogeneous device tracking. Objective 3: Learnware – Deep Learning for Multipath-Resilient Localization A multi-stage deep neural network framework was designed to extract accurate AoA estimates and fuse them into precise 3D positions despite challenging multipath environments (MobiSys 2020, TOSN 2023). Transfer learning approaches facilitate rapid adaptation to new environments (TMC 2024), while innovations in physical neural networks point to future low-power on-device inference (MobiCom 2024). Explorations into tailored large language models demonstrated promising capabilities for interpreting complex spatial signal data (MobiSys 2024). Combined with physical-layer attribute identification methods (MobiCom 2022), these learnware contributions significantly improved localization accuracy and robustness. Objective 4: Application – Practical Deployments in Warehouse and Retail The platform was validated in real-world settings tracking multi-protocol IoT devices in warehouses and retail stores with decimeter-level accuracy (MobiSys 2020, TOSN 2023). Techniques for spatially controllable RFID interrogation enhanced operational flexibility (NSDI 2024). Cross-technology approaches enabled NFC-enabled barcode scanning on NFC-disabled smartphones, bridging hardware gaps in retail (MobiCom 2023). Applications extended to smart buildings with self-sensing concrete for structural health monitoring (SIGCOMM 2022) and secure voice authentication on wearables (SECON 2022). Security research on inaudible command injection attacks informed platform robustness considerations (SP 2023). These demonstrations confirm the platform’s versatility and readiness for diverse industrial and commercial IoT scenarios.

15204820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204820.value: Building on the successful development of a general-purpose, protocol-free IoT tracking platform, future research can advance in several key directions. First, further miniaturization and integration of the antenna array hardware will enhance deployment flexibility, enabling seamless embedding in smart environments and edge devices. Second, middleware algorithms can be refined with advanced signal processing and domain-adaptive learning techniques to further suppress interference and improve localization under extreme multipath and dense device scenarios. Incorporating real-time anomaly detection and self-calibration will enhance robustness and reduce maintenance overhead. Third, the deep learning framework can be augmented by incorporating unsupervised and reinforcement learning to adapt dynamically to evolving environments and novel device types without extensive retraining. The exploration of lightweight, physically implemented neural networks promises significant gains in on-device inference speed and power consumption. Finally, broader applications can be pursued, such as integration with autonomous robotics, augmented reality, and secure access control, expanding the platform’s impact. Pilot deployments in diverse commercial and industrial settings will guide iterative improvements and accelerate technology transfer to industry. Together, these directions will solidify the platform’s role as a cornerstone technology for pervasive, scalable IoT localization.

15204820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204820.value: This research project developed a new technology to precisely locate many different types of smart devices inside buildings without needing to change those devices. Nowadays, places like warehouses and stores use many kinds of wireless devices that talk in different “languages,” making it hard to track everything at once. Our system listens to the wireless signals these devices naturally send and figures out where they are, no matter what type of device or communication method they use. The technology uses a special antenna setup that captures signals from all directions and a smart computer program that can understand these mixed signals and pinpoint device locations accurately, even when the signals bounce around walls and objects indoors. This helps businesses track their products and equipment more easily and cheaply, without installing many separate systems. The research also tested the system in real warehouses and stores, showing it works well in real life. This technology can improve inventory management, speed up checkout processes, and make indoor navigation smarter. Overall, it makes managing connected devices easier and more efficient, helping businesses save time and reduce costs, while opening doors to new smart building and retail applications.
