15206120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206120.value: The commonly used viscous damper is not effective for damping low-frequency vibration because the damping force is proportional to the vibration frequency and is relatively small at low frequency. A viscous damper with high damper coefficient is required in order to generate a large damping force but that increase its size as well as cost. Friction damper can be a better alternative than the viscous damper because of its low cost and easy maintenance. However, friction damper is not as commonly used as viscous damper because its design involves nonlinear dynamics analysis. In practice, the system parameters and environment of a vibration damper can be easily changed or varied. The amount of damping in the vibration damper requires to be adjusted accordingly for best vibration control performance. However, the most commonly used viscous fluid damper is difficult to provide tunable damping. This project is about researching the design of a hybrid tunable vibration damper using Coulomb damping and electromagnetic shunt damping. The tunable Coulomb damper is used for coarse damping adjustment while the tunable electromagnetic shunt damper (EMSD) can be used for fine tuning in order to provide precise damping tuning with a large adjustment range. By combining friction damping which provide the major amount of damping required, and the EMSD with fine tuning ability for suppressing the nonlinearities of friction damping, a tunable damper with adaptive control of reasonable size and cost can be achieved. 常用的粘性阻尼器對衰減低頻振動無效因為阻尼力與振動頻率成正比，並且相對低頻時較小。 要求使用阻尼係數高的粘性阻尼器為了產生較大的阻尼力，但這會增加其尺寸和成本。 摩擦阻尼器比粘性阻尼器更便宜，因為它的成本低且易於維護。 但是，摩擦阻尼器不像粘性阻尼器那樣常用因為其設計涉及非線性動力學分析。實際上，減振器的系統參數和環境可以輕鬆實現改變或變化。 減振器中的阻尼量要求為進行相應調整以獲得最佳的振動控制性能。 但是，最常用的粘性流體阻尼器很難提供可調阻尼。 這個項目是關於研究混合動力可調振動阻尼器的設計庫侖阻尼和電磁分流阻尼。 可調節的庫侖阻尼器是用於可調電磁分流阻尼器的粗調阻尼,電磁分流阻尼器（EMSD）可用於微調，以獲得大範圍振動阻尼調節。 通過結合摩擦阻尼來提供主要所需的阻尼量，並且具有微調能力的EMSD可抑制摩擦阻尼的非線性，可調阻尼器，具有合理的自適應控制尺寸和成本都可以實現。

15206120.label: Realisation of objectives
15206120.value: A hybrid damper with tunable Coulomb and electromagnetic shunt damping (EMSD) is proposed to cope with applications requiring damping tunability. The proposed hybrid damper is applied to a DVA and H-infinity optimal damping of the absorber is achieved experimentally. The theoretical model of the hybrid damper with tunable damping is also experimentally verified. Coulomb damping can be adjusted by varying the compressive spring force acting on the friction blocks of the damper. The Coulomb damper is used to provide the coarse tuning of the hybrid damper while the EMSD supplements by offering fine-tuning of the damping to the damper. Both theoretical and experimental analyses show that the Coulomb damper is capable of enlarging the tunable range of the EMSD damping without compromising its tuning accuracy. The tunable EMSD adopts a six opposing magnet pair configuration which has been proved sufficiently effective. The damping provided by the EMSD is adjustable by varying the external electrical resistance of the EMSD circuit. Meanwhile, fine adjustment of the external resistance of the EMSD circuit provides sufficient tunability of the damping force of the damper. The measured damping coefficients match well with the calculated results from the theoretical models of the pure EMSD, FD, and the FD-EMSD hybrid damper. As an application example, the damper is implemented in a DVA which requires a precise tuning of the damping to work at its optimum condition. Experiments show that the H-infinity optimal working condition is readily setup owing to the FD-enabled coarse tuning and EMSD-induced fine-tuning abilities. Meanwhile, theoretical prediction, in terms of lowering the tuning sensitivity of the EMSD by its combined usage with the FD, is also confirmed by experiments. A bi-objective optimal design methodology of EMSD is proposed and experimentally validated to achieve maximum amount of energy harvest from the damper and resonant vibration suppression of the vibrating structure simultaneously. To achieve maximum amount of energy harvest by the EMSD, its coil is designed such that its internal impedance equals to the external resistance in the EMSD circuit. By keeping the internal resistance of the EMSD coils constant, the transduction factor of the EMSD is adjusted to its optimum value leading to the optimum damping coefficient of the EMSD as dictated by the fixed-points theory of DVA. The electromechanical transduction factor is tuned by searching the optimal number of opposing magnet pairs numerically. It is found that EMSD with six opposing magnet pairs provides the optimal damping when the coil internal impedance equals external resistance. The proposed EMSD is applied to SDOF and DVA systems for both resonant vibration suppression and energy harvesting. The resonant vibration suppression increases monotonically with the decrease of resistance ratio in the SDOF system. On the other hand, the proposed EMSD provides maximum suppression of vibration amplitude of the primary mass and maximum energy harvested from itself as predicted by the theory. The bi-objective design methodology is applied and achieved in the DVA system as proven by the theoretical and experimental results. Moreover, the harvested energy is higher in the SDOF system than in the DVA, while the useful frequency bandwidth for energy harvesting is much wider in the DVA system. Two enhancement methods of EMSD, namely EMSD with VNIC and EMSD with FD, are analyzed both numerically and experimentally for the ultimate objective of increasing the tunable damping range of an EMSD. EMSDs with VNIC, FD or their combination are designed and tested experimentally for damping enhancement. The tunable range of the damping coefficient of the proposed EMSD is shown to be increased by about 900% after adding both VNIC and FD (EMSD+VNIC+FD) by following the proposed design procedure. The damping force of the proposed hybrid damper is evaluated to maximize the respective advantages of the individual component of the hybrid damper. With the increase of the linear damping from EMSD (high damping ratio α), the nonlinear effect of the damping force of the FD can be significantly attenuated in the proposed hybrid damper. The proposed design procedure leads to an enhanced EMSD, in which the FD and VNIC are tactically added to supplement each other to increase the damping range of the EMSD on one hand, and to avoid the possible instability of the EMSD due to the use of VNIC and the high frequency sensitivity of the FD on the other hand. Moreover, the enhanced EMSD with both hybrid damping and VNIC is applied experimentally to achieve the H∞ optimization in a ground-hooked DVA for the minimization of resonant vibration of a single DOF dynamic system. Meanwhile, the enhanced EMSD proposed here can significantly increase the damping force to mass ratio of the EMSD. Adaptive control system has been tested on the EMSD for adjusting its parameters and behavior in real-time based on changes in the system being controlled or the operating conditions. It is designed to handle uncertainties, variations, and disturbances that can affect the system's performance. The original objective of this project is to design a tunable vibration damper with Coulomb friction damping and electromagnetic shunt damping for steady state vibration control.

15206120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206120.value: Vibration dampers with tunable properties are of practical significance to accommodate the need of vibration control under different circumstances. Among major parameters, tunable damping to deliver required accuracy within a given frequency range is difficult to achieve in practice. This paper proposes a hybrid tunable damper by combining the advantages of both Coulomb friction damping and electromagnetic shunt damping. The tunable friction damper (FD) allows for coarse tuning with a larger tunable range, while the tunable electromagnetic shunt damper (EMSD) functions as a fine tuner with fine precision. The end result is a significantly increased tunable frequency range with high precision. The proposed method allows for simple and low cost adjustment of the damping forces in both dampers. A prototype is fabricated and experimentally tested in a dynamic vibration absorber (DVA) system. The predicted tenability is experimentally verified and Optimal damping of the DVA is readily achieved by using the proposed hybrid damper for suppressing resonant vibration of dynamic structures. Further development of the research may allow the tunable absorber for suppressing random vibrations to protect delicate structure under earthquake and typhoons.

15206620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206620.value: With the resonance of urbanization, global warming and urban heat island effects, people are becoming more dependent on the comfort environment provided by air-conditioning systems, which further exacerbates energy consumption. Radiant cooling is an alternative air-conditioning technology conceived in Europe in the 1990s. It can produce higher comfort level and lower energy consumption since internal heat was directly removed from occupants via thermal radiation by ceiling cooling panels, and the energy consumption for circulating water in replacement of air as heat carrier is much lower. However, its application has been very limited in the hot and humid climates due to condensation risks. The dripping drops formed on panels can cause discomfort to the user, damage paper materials and office device, and result in breeds of fungi and bacteria indoors. To avoid condensation, the current practice is based on the combined use of air de-humidification and control of ceiling surface temperature above the dew-point of room air, but this practice limits the cooling capacity and cripple the energy saving potential of the technology. In recent years, somewhat separately condensation phenomenon on superhydrophobic surfaces has been intensively studied by the Co-Is. It was found that a phenomenon called jumping condensation can occur under some circumstances. The jumping condensation means that micro sized droplets can spontaneously detach from the surface before merging into larger ones, and will re-evaporate into the room air, so no dense large droplets will form on the surface. In this case, the dripping risk can be greatly alleviated. In addition, the Co-I has realized directional migration of droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces by constructing a wettability or charge gradient on the surface. When large droplets can be lead in a controlled manner into drainage pipes, and random dripping will be avoided. In this case, the ceiling panel can work at a temperature well below the dew-point temperature of the room air to have the de-humidification function. Therefore, it is possible to take advantage of either or both of the jumping condensation or directional transportation phenomenon that may occur on an engineered superhydrophobic surface to develop condensation-free and/or dripping-free ceiling panels. The surface temperature of cooling panels can be lower, thus greatly improving its cooling capacity and energy efficiency. The application of radiant cooling systems in hot and humid environments can be greatly promoted, which will assist designers and engineers create more comfortable and efficient buildings. 在城市化，气候变化，及热岛效应的综合影响下，当今社会对高能耗的空调的依赖越来越强。辐射冷却技术做为一种替代式建筑降温技术，90年代初起源于欧洲。 该技术以冷水为传热介质，大幅降低风机能耗； 因与人体有直接的热辐射换热，具有好的热舒适感 。但是， 该技术一直未能在热湿气候得到应用，主要是因为辐射冷板的表面有结露的风险，造成室内滴水及霉菌生长。为了避免结露，辐射冷板的表面温度要高于室内空气的露点温度，因此，该技术的除热强度大大受限，且同时需要另有空气系统来调节室内湿度。 近年来，本研究团队在超疏水界面的研究和制备技术方面取得了新进展， 发现了凝结水珠的跳跃现象。微米尺度的凝结水珠在表面张力的作用下会跳离冷表面，从而再蒸发转变为蒸汽，避免了在表面形成凝水的现象。本团队成员的另一项研究成果是制备了一种表面润湿性有方向性的超疏水表面，从而可以使表面上的水珠朝着既定的方向流动。 次两项技术为新一代的辐射冷板提供了两种可能。 前者可以令辐射冷板运行在空气露点温度以下而不结露，从而提高了辐射冷板的除热强度。后者可令辐射冷板具有除湿功能，而不形成失控的滴水现象。 此两种功能的任何一个均可扩展辐射冷板的应用范围， 从而为建筑节能提供一种新的技术选择。

15206620.label: Realisation of objectives
15206620.value: 1.It has been successfully proved that no large water droplets will be dripping from the panels with superhydrophobic surface materials under typical moist-air conditions through experiments. In a series of eight-hour condensation experiments, large condensation drops are observed in some fixed positions in a large view area in experiments with different conditions. Whereas, in a smaller focused view area the diameter of the largest condensation drop is found to firstly increase over time and then reaches around 80 µm with an occasional size of 152 µm. All these were in contrast with the continuously growing drops simultaneously observed on an ordinary aluminum sheet, which reaches 4 mm. The finding provides experimental evidence that the size of condensation drops formed on the superhydrophobic aluminum surface can be constrained below people’s perceivable range in a long-time condensation in typical indoor air conditions. 2.A scalable wet-etching approach for preparing superhydrophobic surfaces on aluminum substrates have been developed. Aluminum is selected as the substrate to fabricate superhydrophobic surfaces as aluminum is commonly used to assemble radiant cooling panels. The following procedures are used to develop superhydrophobic aluminm surface. The aluminum foil was cleaned by sonication in acetone for 5 min, followed by an equal-time sonication in Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and deionized (DI) water successively. The sample was immersed in 80℃ 0.05M NaOH solution to form microstructures by chemical etching method. Then, after heating in water bath at 90℃ for an hour, the fluorination treatment in 0.5%wt 1H,1H,2H,2H perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane (FAS-17)/hexane solution was conducted after 30 min drying at 120℃. 3.The cooling enhancement potential of no-condensate-forming radiant cooling panels for indoor applications have been studied. With mitigated condensation risks, a superhydrophobic radiant cooling panel can be operated with surface temperature lower than the air dew point. It is found that the condensation mass rate of the superhydrophobic surface can be predicted by the empirical correlation of natural convection heat and mass transfer with a deviation of 12%. The analysis on the heat flux of radiant cooling panels with superhydrophobic surfaces indicates a cooling capacity enhancement of 3% -500% for the latent cooling panel compared with a sensible cooling panel. This is realized by the limited cooling capacity of a sensible cooling panel in humid conditions due to the relatively high panel temperature, and the less limited cooling capacity of a latent cooling panel due to the lower panel temperature.

15206620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206620.value: Through a series of experimental research on the condensation of superhydrophobic surface materials in typical indoor moist conditions, the following findings and research outcome can be concluded. 1.Condensate drop sizes can be limited within the un-perceivable range, namely below the sensory and visual thresholds during a long-time condensation process in typical indoor conditions. Using an optical magnifier, large drops up to the size 802.5 µm were observed in certain fixed positions in the large view area of 4.08 mm x 3.06 mm under different experimental conditions; whereas in a smaller focused view area of 0.96 mm x 0.72 mm the diameters of the largest drops were found to firstly increase over time and then reached around 80 µm with occasional size of 152 µm. All these were in contrast with the continuously growing drops simultaneously observed on the ordinary aluminum sheet, which reached 4 mm. The reason is the droplet jumping mechanism that occurs on the nano-engineered superhydrophobic surface. 2.The condensation rate of the superhydrophobic surface was consistent with that of hydrophilic, hydrophobic and superhydrophilic surfaces, though the condensation regimes of the four surfaces were quite different. The average deviation between the experimental condensation rate and the empirical correlation of natural convection heat and mass transfer was within 12%, which is true for both vertical and horizontal surfaces. The result indicates that vapor transfer induced by diffusion and convection in the boundary layer rather than the heat transfer resistance associated with condensate dominates the condensation heat and mass transfer between the moist air and the superhydrophobic surface. 3. Based on the finding of condensation heat transfer rate of superhydrophobic surfaces in indoor conditions, the heat and mass transfer analogy and traditional empirical methods was employed to predict the total heat flux of radiant cooling panels with latent heat transfer. The results indicated an enhancement of 3% to 500% for the total heat flux compared with only sensible cooling, depending on the panel surface temperature, air temperature and humidity. The total heat flux of RCP with latent heat transfer can be enhanced by firstly the extended sensible heat flux by thermal radiation and convection due to the increased temperature difference between panel surface and indoor space, and secondly the extra condensation heat flux due to the condensation-falling-moving-evaporation behavior of tiny droplets formed on the superhydrophobic panel surface.

15206620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206620.value: 1.The condensation mitigation performance and fabrication method of a large-scale, durable and robust superhydrophobic aluminum surface can be further investigated. 2.The mechanism of droplet formation on superhydrophobic surfaces with nano-structures can be further investigated to analyze the effects of micro- and nano-structures on condensation droplet size. Approaches include localizing the positions where large drops appear in SEM and then analyze the micro-structures at these positions or fabricating a superhydrophobic surface with highly controlled and patterned microstructures to investigate the effects of the uniformity of microstructures on the growth of condensation drops. 3.The effects of droplet jumping condensation on indoor air can be further investigated to see the impact of radiant cooling panels with superhydrophobic surface on indoor environment. CFD methods can be a useful tool to study the motion and evaporation of micro droplets with indoor air flow. 4.The superhydrophobic radiant cooling panel can be operated in a wider range of indoor humidity but without much condensation concern, therefore, some energy-saving in latent cooling can be achieved. However, the low chilled water temperature would also deteriorate the efficiency of chillers. The net energy consumption of radiant cooling panel systems functioned with superhydrophobic surfaces needs further investigation.

15206620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206620.value: Condensation is one of the factors that limit the application of radiant cooling systems. The findings of the research project provide encouraging experimental evidence that the size of condensate droplets on the superhydrophobic surface can be limited below people’s perceptional threshold during a typical eight-hour operation period, thus significantly reducing condensation risks for radiant cooling system indoors. A further heat transfer research revealed that the condensation heat transfer rate of superhydrophobic surfaces in moist air can be predicted by the empirical heat transfer rate. It is also proved through the research that when this happens, a cooled-ceiling panel surface works at a temperature up to 8oC below the room dew-point temperature can provide much higher cooling capacity enhanced with the condensation heat release process compared with conventional sensible cooling panels. In summary, the research project explorers the possibility of using superhydrophobic materials to avoid severe condensation problems of radiant cooling system, and reveals the potential of enhancing the cooling capacity of radiant cooling system by utilizing the controllable condensation process on superhydrophobic surfaces.

15207120.label: Project Objectives
15207120.value: To design a novel mobile mechatronic platform of exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton for the elbow; Mechanical integration between rigid exoskeleton and pneumatic muscle, i.e., exo-musculo-skeleton, may achieve light weights with high torque-to-weight ratios for optimized body-device integration and fast power transmissions at the same time through a balance between the pneumatic muscle and rigid exoskeletal structures for desired mechanical output, e.g., torque applied to a joint. Combining neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) with the exo-musculo-skeleton, i.e., exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton, could further reduce the mechanical scale with low power consumption for mobile systems. However, little is known about the hybrid of NMES, soft pneumatic muscles and rigid exoskeleton, because of difficulties in optimizations on 1) integration between rigid exoskeleton and soft pneumatic muscle for desired mechanical performances, e.g., power transmission, and 2) mechatronic integration between NMES and exo-musculo-skeleton for close-to-normal muscle coordination with maximized voluntary motor effort (VME) involvement. We propose to design a novel exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton driven by continuous VME represented by electromyography (EMG) with the strengths of the team in NMES-robots, exoskeletons, pilot exploration in exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton and VME control designs in robots for stroke rehabilitation. To design the continuous VME-driven control for optimized muscle coordination; A novel control strategy will use EMG to continuously coordinate the NMES and mechanical assistances from the exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton to the elbow for close-to-normal muscular coordinating patterns with minimized compensatory motions, by optimizing the supportive scheme from both the mechanical and NMES parts. To derive the rehabilitation effectiveness and mechanisms of muscular coordination of the exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton-assisted self-help elbow rehabilitation. A novel self-help exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton-assisted training program on elbow extension/flexion will be designed to validate the feasibility and its rehabilitation effectiveness through a randomized controlled trial (RCT) compared with those achieved by the latest EMG-triggered rigid mobile exoskeleton for elbow on the market (MyoPro). We expect the self-help exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton treatment will achieve better motor recovery and muscular coordination in the upper-limb than those by MyoPro with close professional assistance.

15207120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207120.value: Self-help and effective rehabilitation with minimum professional assistance is in urgent need to cope with the expanding stroke populations and insufficiency of professional manpower; nevertheless, the related technology is still lacking. Mobile rigid exoskeleton and soft robots with pneumatic muscles are new trends in robot for potential self-help rehabilitation of the upper limb. However, they are still confined in clinical studies requiring close professional assistance, because of low torque-to-weight ratios with heavy weights in the rigid exoskeleton triggering safety concerns for independent usage and slow power transmission in the pneumatic soft robots associated with uncertain rehabilitative effects. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and robot hybrid system is another new trend in rehabilitative mechatronics with the advantage of more effective in improving muscular coordination than robots without NMES. However, NMES has not been integrated with mobile exoskeletons, or soft robots, because of the challenges in control design 1) to coordinate the respective NMES and mechanical assistances for optimized muscular coactivating patterns, and 2) to maximize the involvement of voluntary motor effort (VME) from the paretic neuromuscular system required for effective rehabilitation, based on the mobile platform with limited mechatronic resources. The goal of this project is to research a novel mobile mechatronic technology, i.e., continuous VME-driven exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton for self-help elbow rehabilitation after stroke. We will optimize the mechanical integration between rigid exoskeleton and pneumatic muscle, i.e., exo-musculo-skeleton, for achieving light weights with high torque-to-weight ratios and fast power transmissions at the same time through a balance between the pneumatic muscle and rigid exoskeletal structures. We will combine NMES with the exo-musculo-skeleton, i.e., exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton, through a novel control design by using electromyography (EMG) as the bio-indicator of VME to continuously promote the voluntary effort from the paretic muscles with close-to-normal muscular coordination in elbow extension and flexion. We will also design a novel exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton assisted self-help elbow rehabilitation program for chronic stroke, whose effectiveness will be evaluated through a randomized clinical trial (RCT) by comparing with those achieved by the latest VME-driven rigid mobile exoskeleton for elbow on the market under close professional assistance. The outcomes of the project will bring technological breakthroughs in mobile mechatronics, with potential application to other body parts. The outcomes of the RCT will provide evidences for the feasibility and effectiveness of the exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton assisted self-help rehabilitation, which may benefit the large stroke populations. 中風人口的急速增加導致用於長期復康的傳統醫療資源不足。在人工協助最小化的前提下，實現患者自助式訓練有望解決中風後長期復康治療的需求。然而，可用於自助式復康的有效技術目前依然匱乏。 移動式外骨骼以及氣動式柔性機器人為復康機器人設計的新方向，於自助式上肢訓練極具應用潛力。但此類系統由於機械傳動效率低、體積/重量大、以及功耗高，用於自助訓練時存安全隱患，仍局限於專業操作下的臨床研究中，基本無法實現患者自助式的獨立操作。神經肌肉電刺激（NMES）與機械傳動結構的混合系統為復康機器人設計的另一新方向。其優點在於NMES可以在機械外力輔助的基礎上改善肌肉協調功能，復康功效較傳統機械機器人更勝一籌；同時利用電刺激誘發的生物肌力輸出可降低整體系統功耗。然而，與NMES相結合的移動式外骨骼或柔性機器人還未被研究，其挑戰在於系統控制如何在移動設計平台上將不同系統集成優化，以及將癱瘓肢體的自主運動輸出（VME）最大化，以實現有效復康。 本項目的主旨在於設計一創新的連續VME驅動的移動式外神經肌骨系統(exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton)，用於中風後自助式肘關節訓練。我們將整合並優化外骨骼與氣動肌肉為肌骨聯合體(musculo-skeleton),使之兼具快速機械傳動、體積/重量小、和低功耗之優點。同時，我們將利用肌電信號（EMG）為生物信號輸入，設計可整合NMES與肌骨聯合體協同工作的新控制方法。之後，我們還將設計基於此系統的自助復康訓練方案，並與現有移動式外骨骼系統相比較，利用隨機對照臨床試驗來驗證其可行性與有效性。由本項目產生的結果將會為復康機器人設計帶來突破性的成果，其原理和方法可應用於其他關節。

15207120.label: Realisation of objectives
15207120.value: The project successfully achieved its three primary objectives, with some objectives expanded in scope to address emerging challenges and opportunities during implementation. 1) Objective 1: Design a novel mobile mechatronic platform of exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton (ENMS) for the elbow The project fully realized this objective by developing a lightweight, mobile exo-neuro-musculo-skeleton (ENMS) platform that integrates rigid exoskeletal structures with soft pneumatic muscles and neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) (Major Finding 1). The hybrid design addressed the original challenge of balancing rigidity and compliance to achieve high torque-to-weight ratios while maintaining low power consumption, critical for home-based rehabilitation. A significant breakthrough was the seamless integration of NMES with the exo-musculo-skeleton through novel control algorithms that synchronize electromyography (EMG)-based voluntary motor effort (VME) with pneumatic actuation. This integration minimized compensatory motions and maximized user involvement in movement coordination. 2) Objective 2: Design continuous VME-driven control for optimized muscle coordination This objective was achieved with an extended scope, advancing beyond initial plans. A continuous VME-driven control framework was developed to dynamically adjust NMES intensity and pneumatic assistance in real time based on EMG signals. This approach enabled "close-to-normal" muscular coordination patterns, as evidenced by EMG and cortico-muscular coherence analysis in clinical trials. The system outperformed commercial EMG-triggered exoskeletons by eliminating abrupt on/off transitions and instead modulating assistance proportionally to the user’s real-time voluntary effort. To address variability in stroke survivors’ EMG signals, a hybrid CMC-EMG control strategy (Major Finding 11) was introduced, combining EEG-EMG coherence to distinguish intentional movements from spasticity or noise. The project also integrated machine learning models, such as support vector machine (SVM)-based classifiers (Major Finding 10), to automatically evaluate tactile and motor deficits, enabling personalized adjustments to the control framework. These innovations not only met the original goal but also laid the groundwork for future adaptive neurorehabilitation technologies. 3) Objective 3: Validate rehabilitation effectiveness and mechanisms of ENMS-assisted self-help training This objective was partially achieved due to unforeseen challenges; therefore, the project expanded its scope to address broader clinical and technological questions. Clinical trials confirmed the feasibility and rehabilitative efficacy of ENMS-assisted self-help training for upper limb motor recovery, with participants demonstrating significant improvements in Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA-UE) scores after 12 weeks of home-based training (Major Findings 1, 4, 6). Mechanistic studies revealed that ENMS training enhanced cortico-muscular interactions (Major Findings 2, 12), promoting neuroplasticity by reinforcing descending motor pathways disrupted by stroke. However, the planned randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing ENMS with the MyoPro exoskeleton was adapted to a single-group design (Major Finding 4) due to recruitment difficulties during the pandemic. The project also explored telerehabilitation readiness (Major Finding 5), post-stroke sensory deficits (Major Findings 3, 9, 10), post-stroke depression (Major Finding 8), and automatic theranostics for long-term neurorehabilitation (Major Finding 7), contributing to a holistic understanding of ENMS’s clinical potential. In summary, all three objectives were met, with objectives 2 and 3 expanded to address evolving clinical needs and technical complexities. The ENMS platform achieved its core aims of lightweight mechatronic integration, continuous VME-driven control, and validated rehabilitative efficacy.

15207120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207120.value: The research establishes a robust framework for advancing neurorehabilitation technologies. However, further development could focus on enhancing the adaptability and accessibility of hybrid ENMS systems by leveraging AI-driven personalization and integrating real-time feedback from EEG-EMG biomarkers. By incorporating AI-driven adaptive algorithms, ENMS systems will be capable of dynamically decoding EEG-EMG biomarkers and movement patterns, continuously adjusting stimulation parameters to tailor therapeutic interventions based on real-time cortical-muscular activity and individual neuroplasticity trajectories. This advancement will expand the applications to include spinal cord injury rehabilitation and cognitive-emotional recovery. Additionally, conducting multicenter trials across diverse populations will provide critical insights into the long-term efficacy of telerehabilitation systems relative to conventional therapies.

15207120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207120.value: Self-help and effective rehabilitation with minimal professional assistance is urgently needed for large stroke populations; however, the relevant technology remains underdeveloped. This project has developed a novel mobile mechatronic platform based on an exo-neuro-musculo-skeletal system with continuous maximized voluntary motor effort (VME) as the control input for upper limb rehabilitation. Restoration of post-stroke limb function relies on repeated and intensive physical practice of the paralyzed limb with VME, promoting close-to-normal muscular coordination. The device features a lightweight mechatronic design for optimal body-device integration, low power consumption, and continuous VME to ensure maximum user involvement in system control. It provides an effective solution for self-help upper limb rehabilitation, which stroke survivors critically demand. Clinical trials were conducted to validate the rehabilitation effectiveness and mechanisms of muscular coordination associated with device-assisted self-help upper limb rehabilitation. Additionally, this project explored related post-stroke rehabilitation technologies, including telerehabilitation, assessment of post-stroke sensory deficiency, robotic motor control via cortico-muscular coherence, and more.

15207220.label: Project Objectives
15207220.value: Develop deep learning-based methods to discover prior structure information for massive connectivity. • For massive connectivity, there exists a sparsity pattern in device activities, i.e., only a small number of devices are active simultaneously. Thus, existing grant-free random access methods apply compressive sensing (CS) techniques, whose performance critically depends on the available prior structure information. The more structure information is available, the better the recovery performance can be achieved. Nevertheless, most existing works on CS-based grant-free random access assumed a simple independent sparsity pattern. Thus, they fail to exploit other types of structures, such as spatial and temporal correlation in the device activity, and structures in the information source. So, these methods cannot obtain the optimal performance. To enhance the performance of activity and data detection, we will apply deep learning methods to discover prior structure information in a data-driven manner. Specifically, we will adopt recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture the temporal correlation in the activities of one device in different transmission blocks, and adopt the graph neural network (GNN) and RNN to further capture the spatial-temporal correlation in activities of different devices across multiple transmission blocks. Moreover, deep generative models will be applied to discover structures in the information sources, which will be critical for multiuser data decoding. We will identify suitable neural network architectures, and train them on simulated and real-life datasets. Develop effective detection algorithms for massive connectivity with prior structure information. • We will leverage the deep learning models that are developed and trained for the previous objective to improve the performance of device activity detection and data decoding. The models will be firstly used to predict the activity pattern in the current transmission block, which will then be exploited via an ensemble method to improve activity detection. Specifically, built upon two existing methods, i.e., weighted Lasso and a sparse support estimation method, we will ensemble their results to provide a more accurate support estimate. The performance of the proposed method will be rigorously analyzed, which will lead to a sharp and non-asymptotic sample complexity characterization that can be used to guide the selection of the pilot length. Then, with the generative models trained to capture the information source structures, effective multiuser detection algorithms will be developed for data decoding. The decoding performance will also be analytically characterized. Thus, the completion of this objective will lead to effective algorithms with theoretical guarantees, which shall demonstrate the advantage of combining analytical methods with deep learning. Design joint activity and data detection algorithms for massive connectivity. • Existing detection algorithms for grant-free random access separately deal with activity detection and data decoding. This objective is to develop effective joint activity and data detection algorithms. A key observation is that the result obtained from the data detection step can serve as a feedback signal for activity detection. We will develop two types of methods, one based on optimization methods and the other based on deep learning. The first method is based on alternating optimization, which alternately optimizes the activity detection step and the data detection step. The result from data detection will serve as a feedback signal for activity detection. The second method is based on deep reinforcement learning. Specifically, a neural network will be applied to approximate the mapping from the estimated signal to the optimal weights for activity detection. The performance of these two types of methods will be extensively tested, and their potential performance gains compared with the separate design will be verified. Apply deep learning methods to develop computationally efficient algorithms for massive connectivity. • Grant-free random access incurs higher computational complexity than conventional random access methods. Given the massive number of IoT devices, the computational efficiency of existing detection algorithms cannot meet the stringent latency requirement of many IoT applications. Inspired by the recent attempts in applying deep learning methods to solve large-scale optimization problems, we will develop deep learning-based algorithms for more efficient detection for massive connectivity. We will develop three different approaches for “learning to optimize”. The first approach is based on deep unfolding, a method recently proposed to speed up signal recovery in compressive sensing. We will develop a high-order accelerated proximal algorithm with a much lower iteration complexity than traditional proximal gradient algorithms. The second approach is based on online learning, which will help to develop an effective coordinate selection policy to improve the convergence rate of the coordinate descent algorithm for activity detection. The third approach is a pure deep learning based method, which will speed up the encoding/decoding computation and also improve the detection performance. It is based on the idea of joint source-channel coding, and we will apply end-to-end learning to design effective encoders and decoders.

15207220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207220.value: Over the past decades, wireless communications technologies have revolutionized every major economic sector and penetrated into everyone’s daily life. The Internet of Things (IoT) represents the next wave of wireless revolution, which will connect billions of devices, objects, and machines. It will in turn enable impactful applications ranging from smart city, healthcare, industrial automation, to logistics and transportation. This trend is driving a paradigm shift in wireless communications, from “connecting humans” to “connecting things”. Compared with other networking technologies, connecting IoT devices via cellular networks enjoys unique advantages, including ubiquitous coverage, unparalleled levels of reliability, security and quality of service. Unfortunately, current 4G LTE networks are incapable of providing scalable connectivity for billions of IoT devices, as their multiple access schemes lead to high contention, long access latency, and large overhead. Recently, an innovative multiple access mechanism, named grant-free random access, has been proposed, which allows a large number of devices to transmit their data without waiting for any permission. It has been regarded as a promising technique for massive IoT connectivity in future wireless networks. Sporadic communication is a key feature of massive connectivity, i.e., only some of the devices are active to transmit messages in each transmission block. Thus, compressive sensing (CS), a sparse signal processing technique, serves as a main design tool by exploiting sparsity in the device activity pattern. Nonetheless, existing studies on CS-based massive connectivity have important limitations. First, they only consider sparsity in the activity pattern, but miss other exploitable prior structure information, including correlation in device activities and structures in the transmitted data. Second, the key tasks of massive connectivity are closely interrelated, including device activity detection, channel estimation, and data decoding, but previous studies treat them separately, leading to sub-optimal performance. Third, existing detection algorithms are not efficient for real-time detection with a massive number of devices. In this project, we propose to leverage deep learning methods to enhance the performance of CS-based grant-free random access. Motivated by their effectiveness in extracting latent representations from complex data, we will apply deep learning methods to discover prior structure information in the device activity pattern and information source, which will then be applied to develop effective algorithms for activity detection and data decoding. To enhance the performance, joint activity and data detection algorithms will be developed. Furthermore, we shall apply “learning to optimize” approaches to develop computationally efficient algorithms for latency-critical IoT applications. 在過去的幾十年中，無線通信技術徹底改變了主要的經濟領域，並滲透到每個人的日常生活中。物聯網（IoT）代表了下一波無線技術革命，將連接數十億個設備，對象和機器。由此，它將賦能智慧城市、醫療保健、工業自動化以及物流和運輸等多個影響廣泛的應用。這種趨勢正在推動無線通信從「連接人」到「連接事物」的範式轉變。與其他網絡技術相比，通過蜂窩網絡連接物聯網設備具有獨特的優勢，包括無處不在的覆蓋範圍，無與倫比的可靠性，安全性和服務質量。不幸的是，當前的4G LTE網絡無法為數十億個物聯網設備提供可擴展的連接，因為它們的多址接入方案會導致高競爭，長接入時延和大開銷。最近，一種新穎的被稱為免授權隨機接入的多址接入機制被提出。該機制允許大量設備無需等待任何許可就可以傳輸其數據。它被認為是未來無線網絡中大規模物聯網連接的很有前途的技術。 零星的通信是大規模接入的獨特特徵，即在每個傳輸塊中，只有少量設備處於活動狀態並能傳輸消息。因此，作為一種稀疏信號處理技術，壓縮傳感通過利用設備激活模式中的稀疏性成為主要的設計工具。然而，基於壓縮感知的大規模接入的現有研究存在一定的局限性。首先，它們只考慮到激活模式中的稀疏性，但忽略了其他可利用的先驗結構信息，包括設備激活之間的相關性和信息源的結構。其次，大規模接入的關鍵任務之間密切相關，包括設備激活檢測，信道估計和數據解碼。但是之前的研究將它們分開考慮，導致性能欠佳。第三，現有的檢測算法對於大量設備的實時檢測效率不高。在此項目中，我們提出利用深度學習方法來提升基於壓縮感知的免授權隨機接入的性能。由於深度學習的方法能有效地從複雜的數據中提取潛在表徵，我們將應用這種方法在設備激活模式和信息源中發現先驗結構信息，然後將其用於開發有效的激活檢測和數據解碼算法。為了提高性能，我們還將開發激活和數據聯合檢測算法。此外，我們將應用「學習優化」方法來開發計算效率高的算法服務於時延敏感的物聯網應用。

15207220.label: Realisation of objectives
15207220.value: This project investigated a key application scenario of 5G networks, namely massive connectivity. It was motivated by the recent shift in wireless communications, from “connecting humans” to “connecting things”. While 4G LTE networks have enjoyed great commercial successes, they are incapable of providing scalable connectivity for serving billions of IoT devices, as their multiple access schemes lead to high contention, long access latency, and large overhead. This project investigated an innovative multiple access mechanism, named grant-free random access, which allows a large number of devices to transmit their data without waiting for any permission. Through the four main research tasks, we have developed deep learning-based algorithms and methods to address the key design challenges of grant-free random access. We started by exploring various kinds of prior structure information and correlations (Research Objective 1), and then developed effective detection algorithms to exploit such information (Research Objectives 2 and 3). To overcome the high computational complexity, we also developed deep learning-based methods to improve efficiency (Research Objective 4). Our investigation closely followed the stated research objectives, which led to fruitful research outcomes. In particular, research results of this project have been reported in 8 journal papers and 9 conference papers. Following is the detailed description of the realization of the objectives. • Research Objective 1 is to explore and discover prior structure information for massive connectivity. Existing works on activity detection of grant-free random access (RA) heavily relies on structured signal recovery techniques, e.g., compressive sensing (CS), which critically depend on the available prior structure information. Nevertheless, most existing works on CS-based grant-free RA assumed a simple sparsity prior: each device is active with certain probability, and the activities are independent across devices and across time. It simplifies the performance analysis and algorithm design but fails to exploit richer structures available in the system. In our investigation, we explored various kinds of structure information in different grant-free RA systems. For synchronous grant-free RA, we investigated the common sparsity pattern in the received pilot and data signal, as well as the channel decoding information; for grant-free RA with retransmission, we investigated the user activity correlation between adjacent transmission blocks; for asynchronous grant-free RA, we investigated the common sparsity among the received pilot signals from multiple base station antennas. Such information is important for the design and analysis of grant-free RA systems. • Research Objective 2 is to develop effective detection algorithms with prior structure information. Leveraging the findings of Research Objective 1, we have developed different detection algorithms for grant-free RA systems. For synchronous grant-free RA, we designed advanced receivers to exploit the common sparsity pattern in pilots and data. To reduce the complexity, a low-cost side information (SI)-aided receiver is proposed, where the channel decoder provides SI to update the estimates on whether a user is active or not. For grant-free RA with retransmission, we developed an activity-correlation-aware receiver based on the correlated approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. We also analyzed the performance of the proposed receiver, including the user activity detection, channel estimation, and data error. For asynchronous grant-free RA, the situation is more challenging as synchronization delay detection is also needed. We applied the framework of orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) to deal with the non-independent and identically distributed pilot matrix. To reduce the computational complexity, a memory AMP (MAMP)-based algorithm is further proposed that eliminates the matrix inversions. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithms validates the importance of exploring prior structure information in grant-free RA systems. • Research Objective 3 is on joint activity detection and data detection algorithms. Most existing works separately design device activity detection and data detection, leading to performance loss, as they failed to exploit the inter-task relationship. We have developed joint detection algorithms for different grant-free RA systems. One approach for joint device activity detection and data decoding is to embed the data symbols in the signature sequences, but it significantly increases the computational complexity. We proposed multiarmed bandit (MAB) approaches for more efficient detection via coordinate descent, which achieves a delicate tradeoff between exploration and exploitation in coordinate selection. For synchronous grant-free RA, we proposed a turbo receiver for joint activity detection, channel estimation, and data decoding, which iterates between a joint estimator and a channel decoder. It is based on the BiG-AMP algorithm. For grant-free RA with retransmission, we developed a novel activity-correlation-aware receiver for joint activity detection and channel estimation, which is based on the correlated AMP algorithm. For asynchronous grant-free RA, we developed novel algorithms for joint user activity detection, synchronization delay detection, and channel estimation. All these algorithms are shown to outperform the separate design. • Research Objective 4 is on deep learning-based methods for faster detection. For latency-critical IoT applications, activity and data detection must be performed in real-time, but traditional algorithms suffer from high complexity, which increases with the number of devices and the number of antennas at the base station. Our research developed innovative deep learning-based methods to significantly improve computation efficiency. Existing learning-based methods have limited capabilities to scale with the problem size and to generalize with varying network settings. We proposed a scalable and generalizable neural calibration framework, where a neural network is adopted to calibrate the input of conventional model-based algorithms. In this way, the backbone of a traditional time-efficient algorithm is integrated with deep neural networks to achieve high computational efficiency, while enjoying enhanced performance. We have also investigated the importance of neural architecture design for “learning to optimize” in wireless networks. Particularly, we found that graph neural network (GNN) based methods can achieve near-optimal performance in large-scale networks and generalize well under different system settings. We theoretically verified the advantages of GNNs over unstructured neural networks in solving graph optimizations in wireless communications, and provided the first generalization analysis for these two neural architectures. Based on the generalization analysis, we also proposed a theory-guided neural architecture design methodology for performance enhancement. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project (Research Objectives 1 to 4), we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area. As a result of this project, a PhD student, Xinyu BIAN, has been trained and graduated. Our investigation has led to innovative ideas and methods that can effectively support massive IoT devices in wireless networks. Moreover, our results have cast new light in designing deep learning-based channel estimation and optimization algorithms for future wireless networks.

15207220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207220.value: Major findings and research outcomes of this project are summarized as follows. For references, [C1] and [J1] represent conference paper #1 and journal paper #1 in Part C, respectively. • Joint Activity and Data Detection for Grant-free Random Access: Existing detection algorithms for grant-free random access separately deal with activity detection and data decoding but have not fully exploited various correlations. Our research developed effective joint activity and data detection algorithms. In [J1], we developed multi-armed bandit (MAB) approaches for joint device activity detection and data decoding, which enjoy faster convergence rates with a lower time complexity compared with the state-of-the-art algorithm. In [C3, C5, J6], to further enhance performance, we developed advanced receivers in a holistic manner by jointly designing activity detection, channel estimation, and data decoding. Algorithms were extended to the case with retransmission in [C8, J7] and to the case with asynchronous random access in [C9]. • Deep Learning Methods for Computationally Efficient Algorithms: Grant-free random access incurs higher computational complexity than conventional random access methods, and we have developed deep learning-based solutions to improve computation efficiency. In [C2, C6, J2], we proposed a scalable and generalizable neural calibration framework for future wireless system design, where a neural network is adopted to calibrate the input of conventional model-based algorithms. In [C1, C4, J4], we developed a unified framework for applying graph neural networks (GNNs) to solve complex optimization problems in wireless networks, with theoretical guarantees and practical design guidelines. • Deep Learning-based Channel Estimation: Accurate channel state information (CSI) plays a critical role in enhancing performance of wireless communication systems, and channel estimation can assist both activity detection and data decoding in random access systems. In [C7, J5], we proposed a general deep learning framework for high-dimension channel estimation, which leverages existing iterative channel estimators and is with provable guarantees. It is implemented by a fixed point network (FPN), consisting of a closed-form linear estimator and a deep learning-based non-linear estimator. Both theoretical analysis and extensive simulation results illustrate the advantages over the state-of-the-art methods in estimation accuracy, convergence rate, complexity, and robustness. • Collaborative Edge Inference of Multiple IoT Devices: In [J3]. [J8], we have also investigated collaborative inference with multiple IoT devices, e.g., multi-camera surveillance. We developed effective communication mechanisms to exploit the correlations between different devices to reduce overall communication overhead, while providing high inference accuracy. Such methods are promising for general IoT applications.

15207220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207220.value: This research holds significant potential for future development across multiple dimensions. As AI and machine learning technologies continue to evolve, the proposed deep learning methods could be enhanced to handle increasingly complex network scenarios and device behaviors, particularly for emerging IoT applications like autonomous vehicles and industrial automation that demand ultra-reliable, low-latency communications. The framework could also be expanded to address critical challenges such as energy efficiency, security concerns, and network resilience, with potential applications extending into next-generation wireless technologies (6G and beyond) where massive connectivity will become even more crucial. The research team proposes a structured approach to realize these possibilities, beginning with the development of sophisticated deep learning models for understanding and predicting device activity patterns, followed by the creation of integrated algorithms that combine activity detection with data decoding. The team will implement "learning to optimize" approaches to achieve real-time performance, and validate solutions through extensive simulations. This systematic progression aims to create a practical, scalable solution that can be seamlessly integrated into future wireless network standards and IoT deployments, ultimately transforming how massive numbers of devices communicate in next-generation networks.

15207220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207220.value: In today's world, billions of devices - from smart home appliances to industrial sensors - need to connect to the internet wirelessly. This massive network of connected devices is called the Internet of Things (IoT). While current cellular networks (4G) work well for connecting phones and computers, they struggle to handle the enormous number of IoT devices efficiently, as each device must "wait its turn" to communicate. This research focuses on developing a smarter way for IoT devices to communicate, similar to how people in a large group conversation might speak when needed without formally asking for permission. The project uses advanced mathematical techniques and artificial intelligence to solve three main challenges: identifying which devices are trying to communicate, establishing reliable connections, and efficiently transmitting data. The value of this research lies in its potential to enable faster, more reliable, and more efficient IoT communications. This could lead to significant improvements in various applications, from smart cities to healthcare systems, making them more responsive and efficient. The project's success could help build better wireless networks that can handle thousands of connected devices simultaneously while using less energy and network resources.

15207320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207320.value: 我们将开发一个整合协同式高速公路入口匝道车辆汇入（InCoMe）管控系统。InCoMe是一个双层交通控制系统。其中，上层控制器负责三个宏观指标的控制：1）匝道车辆汇入点，2）匝道流量，3）主线限速。上述三个控制指标的控制信号将取决于实时交通状态。特别地，第一个控制指标，即匝道车辆汇入点，是一个新的控制概念，由本项目首次提出。下层控制器是一个协同式自动车辆轨迹规划器。车辆轨迹规划将通过状态受限（state constrained）的模型预测控制（MPC）实现。车辆轨迹规划输出的是未来一段时间内主线协助车辆和匝道汇入车辆的时间-速度曲线。我们选择模型预测控制而不是反馈式控制的原因是前者具有优化特性。在模型预测控制中引入状态限制的一个好处是可以阻止主线车辆过分降速以影响主线跟随交通，而这种降速在匝道流量充分大时是可以累积起来的。我们将使用代理模型（surrogate model）对上层控制器的控制指标进行优化，以降低优化所需的计算强度。 车联网下自主驾驶车辆已经证明可以提高安全性，减少污染物排放，以及通过交通控制提高效率。尽管车联网环境下自主驾驶车辆可以不通过人类驾驶员的干涉而自动行驶，但这并不意味着它们做出的决策是系统最优的。因此，InCoMe这样的能够协调自动驾驶车辆的高速公路管理系统就显得有必要了。 本项目将揭示混合交通流和纯粹自主驾驶车辆交通流会给高速公路入口匝道区域带来什么样的收益，以及如何优化该区域的交通而不至产生通行效率的骤降（flow breakdown）和匝道排队车辆的溢出。本项目所开发的理论与优化框架将来可以继续被用来研究混合交通流和纯粹自主驾驶车辆交通流情况下其他形式的高速公路瓶颈（如车道减少和交织段）处的交通运营。 本项目的负责人在高速公路管控和元启发式（meta-heuristic）优化方面有很丰富的研究经验，并于2012年获得过澳大利亚科研委员会（Australian Research Council）的一个项目以开发一种新颖的整合式高速公路管控系统。该项目的科研成果促成了STRC协调式匝道入口流量控制算法。该算法目前正被安装进澳大利亚昆士兰州的STREAMS交通控制系统。这些均证明，本项目负责人是完成本项目的最佳人选。

15207320.label: Realisation of objectives
15207320.value: In this research project, the proposal included integrating merging control, ramp metering, and Variable Speed Limits (VSL) for ramp merging (RM) scenarios in both mixed traffic and completely Connected and Automated Vehicle (CAV) environments. Merging controls tailored for fully CAV environments were developed, resulting in the publication or under-review of three journal papers (refer to entries 1, 3, and 5 in Part C). The research also involved adapting ramp metering using the ALINEA algorithm. Rather than employing a fixed critical density for ALINEA, a dynamic critical density dependent on the CAV penetration rate was devised (Objectives 1, 2, & 5). At the same time, no VSL algorithm was created during this research, leading to underachievement of objectives 3 and 4. The rationale behind this decision will be elaborated in the next section. The project aimed to integrate control mechanisms for both mixed traffic and entirely CAV scenarios (Objectives 1 and 5). The findings from the test results have been submitted to a journal, and the manuscript is currently pending review (refer to entry 4 in Part C). Reasons VSL algorithm was not developed further Ramp metering (RM) alone can achieve near-optimal traffic flow efficiency at on-ramp merging sections. Adding VSL in these scenarios often results in marginal or negligible improvements. Simulation experiments conducted for freeway-to-freeway flow rates of 2800, 3200, and 3600 vehicles per hour, along with ramp flow rates ranging from 800 to 1600 vehicles per hour, indicate that the enhancements in delays range from only 3% to 7.9%. Ramp metering is sufficient to achieve maximum traffic efficiency in on-ramp merging sections because it directly regulates on-ramp vehicle inflow and minimises mainline traffic disruptions. VSL, while useful in broader traffic management scenarios, does not provide significant additional benefits in this specific context, as the merging issue is already effectively addressed by ramp metering. Specifically, the primary bottleneck in merging sections is the imbalance created when too many vehicles enter the highway at once, causing turbulence in the flow. Ramp metering directly mitigates this problem by spacing out vehicles before they merge, maintaining smoother traffic conditions. Since ramp metering already regulates the rate of merging vehicles, adjusting the speed of vehicles on the mainline (via VSL) may not significantly enhance performance. It may complicate the dynamics by introducing unnecessary speed changes for mainline traffic. VSL requires vehicles upstream to adjust their speeds, which takes time to propagate. By the time VSL effects reach the merging section, ramp metering has already optimised the flow. VSL is more effective in situations where congestion is distributed over a larger stretch of highway, such as during incidents, weather-related slowdowns, or recurring bottlenecks (shockwaves) not directly associated with merging. In contrast, ramp metering specifically addresses merging-related congestion, which is a localised issue. Based on the above reasons, the completion rates for Objectives 3 and 4 are assessed at 30% and 90%, respectively. Objective 3 is only 30% complete due to the decision to halt the development of the VSL algorithm after determining that VSL was ineffective. In contrast, Objective 4 is 90% complete because the VSL component was excluded from the upper-level control of cooperative merging. In summary, the choice to omit the creation of a VSL algorithm in this research project was supported by the discovery that ramp metering alone can efficiently enhance traffic flow effectiveness at on-ramp merging areas, and the recognition that integrating VSL could introduce unwarranted complexities.

15207320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207320.value: We conducted in-depth studies on integrating emerging CAV technologies with intelligent transportation control, focusing on the critical traffic bottleneck of freeway on-ramp merging scenarios. Our research yielded significant outcomes: 1) we developed mathematical models tailored to single and multi-mainline merging scenarios for fully CAV traffic scenarios. The proposed models can be employed under different traffic demands, ensuring efficiency and safety in fully autonomous traffic settings. Considering different requirements, such as high solution quality or strict real-time performance, we proposed three algorithms to meet different needs. We explored the state-of-art optimization and deep reinforcement learning methods to solve CAV-based control problems. 2) We further investigated the connection between car-following models and traffic performance. We bridged them by introducing the kinematic wave model with a triangular fundamental diagram and showed that properly modifying the values of the car-following characteristic parameters during congestion resolving can create a recovery wave pattern that can reduce the number of affected vehicles and their total delay. 3) For mixed traffic scenarios, we analyzed the traffic performance under varying CAV penetration rates and proposed a hybrid control strategy that combines existing ramp metering techniques with CAV cooperative control to enhance traffic efficiency. We have submitted five research papers to top-tier transportation journals, of which two have been published, one is under major revision, and two are under review. Our major findings are as follows: 1) We validated the effectiveness of the three proposed freeway merging control strategies, demonstrating their ability to significantly reduce computation time and enhance overall traffic performance across various conditions. Additionally, we highlighted the critical importance of controlling vehicle passing sequences and lane selections in maximizing traffic performance. 2) We demonstrated the feasibility of centralized multi-vehicle control under real-time requirements, achieving superior traffic efficiency by leveraging global optimization techniques to coordinate vehicle movements effectively. Especially in single mainline merging scenarios, centralized coordination of 15 to 20 vehicles can be optimally solved within one second. 3) Our findings underscore the importance of macroscopic traffic flow control strategies for over-capacity conditions. Even in the mixed traffic era, these strategies remain indispensable for managing congestion.

15207320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207320.value: Autonomous driving is one of the most important technological developments today, and it involves a wide range of research directions. Building on the foundation of our work, we propose three future research directions that address key challenges in the field: 1) End-to-end learning framework: Developing an end-to-end framework that seamlessly integrates perception and decision-making is a promising avenue. This approach not only enhances the system’s intelligence but also simplifies the algorithmic workflow, making it more efficient and easier to deploy in real-world scenarios. A notable direction involves leveraging large language models in tandem with learning-based control networks. This integration could enable autonomous systems to interpret complex scenarios and make context-aware decisions, paving the way for fully automated and intuitive driving systems. 2) Centralized Optimization Control: Centralized optimization holds the potential to provide reliable and stable solutions to traffic management. Future research could focus on developing faster algorithms, such as decomposition or approximation methods, to handle real-time decision-making in complex environments. 3) Decentralized Control Strategies: Exploring decentralized control strategies is crucial for addressing the demands of large-scale road networks and high traffic volumes, ensuring scalability and efficiency in complex traffic scenarios.

15207320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207320.value: The research project, titled "Integrated Cooperative on-ramp Merging," explores the integration of emerging Connected and Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) technologies with intelligent transportation control, focusing on freeway on-ramp merging scenarios. The study has produced significant outcomes. Mathematical models tailored to single and multi-mainline merging scenarios for fully CAV traffic were developed, ensuring efficiency and safety under varying traffic demands. Three algorithms were proposed to meet different performance needs. A Hybrid Flow and Trajectory Control (HFTC) strategy was proposed, combining ramp metering and CAV cooperative control to enhance traffic efficiency. This research found that the HFTC strategy demonstrated greater adaptability and effectiveness than ramp metering or cooperative merging independently. It highlighted the importance of considering CAV penetration rates in optimising traffic flow and control strategies, showing that the suitability of macroscopic (ramp metering) and microscopic (cooperative merging) controls varied under different traffic conditions. Furthermore, the research revealed that the benefits of higher CAV penetration rates are more pronounced in congested traffic situations. While ramp metering remains crucial in heavy traffic congestion, cooperative merging is effective and beneficial under low and moderate traffic conditions.

15207420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207420.value: 瞬时激波冲击下，带有初始扰动的两种流体分界面会发生RM不稳定性（RMI）现象。由于激波冲击后压力梯度与流体界面的密度梯度不重合所带来的斜压机制，会诱导扰动振幅的增长，涡结构、尖钉及气泡结构的发展和湍流混合。RMI已经在超燃冲压发动机和惯性约束核聚变等很多工程领域中引起越来越广泛的兴趣。在超燃冲压发动机中，RMI会增大燃料与空气的混合区域从而促进预混和燃烧。然而与此相对的是，在ICF中，RMI会导致内层燃料与外层烧蚀壳和混合，降低了能量增益，甚至最终导致点火失败。可以通过各种典型构型来有效研究RMI。激波与气柱相互作用被认为是其中一种重要的研究手段。在过去的几十年中，由激波气柱相互作用产生了丰富的流动现象，使这一领域的研究非常活跃。值得注意的是，大多数研究仅考虑单层圆柱界面。 但是，实际情况通常涉及激波与多层界面的相互作用，并且相应的RMI机理仍然知之甚少。 在本项目中，打算通过实验，数值和理论方法来研究受到激波冲击的多层气柱的演变。实验部分将进行激波和嵌入空气柱的SF6气柱之间相互作用的激波管实验。 同时，将进行数值模拟以补充流场中详细的流动信息。 之后，将对各个参数进行分析，以研究在界面变形过程中内外气柱相对尺寸和位置，马赫数以及Atwood数的影响。最后，将建立理论模型来评估由RMI诱导的被测气体与周围气体之间的流动和混合速率。该项目的成果预期将为激波与多层界面的相互作用以及界面耦合对流动混合的影响提供流动物理机理上的认识。 可以预计，从该项目中获得的知识将为超燃冲压发动机推进系统的设计和ICF中多层靶丸的设计提供学术基础。

15207420.label: Realisation of objectives
15207420.value: The project has been completed successfully. All the project objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, shock tube experiments have been conducted at University of Science and Technology of China. In the experiments, a double-layer cylinder with air in the inner cylinder and SF6 in the outer ring was generated using a soap film technique. The complete process of shock-induced bubble evolution was recorded using high-speed Schlieren photography. The effects of inner-outer radius ratio and eccentricity on the bubble evolution were investigated. For objective 2, numerical simulations have been performed to provide more detailed flow information. A new flow solver has been developed based on the adaptive mesh refinement technique. The numerical results agreed well with the experiments. For objective 3, the effects of inner-outer radius ratio, the shock Mach number, and the Atwood number on the evolution of a double-layer cylinder were investigated using numerical simulations. For objective 4, theoretical models have been established to predict the evolution of circulation and mixing rate for a double-layer cylinder. The project has successfully developed many theoretical and numerical tools and generated valuable experimental data for the study of Richtmyer–Meshkov instability. The outcomes have advanced the understanding of the underlying physical mechanisms.

15207420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207420.value: 1. For a reactive shock-bubble interaction at Mach 1.34, ignition of the premixed bubble was observed due to the high pressure and temperature near the downstream pole to form deflagration waves, which significantly promotes mixing due to the thermal effects. A new shock focusing mechanism was observed due to the secondary refracted shock, which initiates a new ignition. However, deflagration-to-detonation transition fails. The rich physics in reactive shock-bubble interactions was reported in detail for the first time. 2. For the evolution of a double-layer gas cylinder in A/B/A type, a bulge is generated near the upstream pole of the outer cylinder due to the impingement of a reflected shock wave, which promotes the formation of an upstream jet. The evolution of the jet is suppressed by increasing the Mach number, and increasing the Atwood number promotes mixing. Net circulation can be well predicted by the linear combination of the Picone and Boris model and the Samtaney and Zabusky model. 3. For the evolution of a double-layer gas cylinder in A/B/C type, in scenarios with negative Atwood numbers, secondary vortex pairs emerge at the downstream interface of the outer cylinder, with the distance between them decreasing as the Atwood number is increased. However, a jet is generated at the downstream interface for positive Atwood numbers, supplanting the formation of secondary vortex pairs. 4. For a reactive double-layer gas cylinder at Mach 2.3, a hot spot forms near the downstream interface of the outer cylinder due to high pressure and temperature from the triple point. When the inner-to-outer radius ratio exceeds a critical value, a second hot spot appears near the upstream interface of the inner cylinder.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207420.value: Richtmyer–Meshkov (RM) instability widely exists in various scientific and engineering applications, such as inertial confinement fusion, supernova explosions, and scramjet engines. The study of shock-bubble interaction is crucial for understanding RM instability, which often involves interactions between incident shock waves and multi-layer gas bubbles in engineering contexts. In this project, an extensive study was conducted with a combination of theoretical modeling, numerical simulations, and wind tunnel experiments. High-fidelity numerical and experimental data were provided for nonreactive and reactive interactions between a shock wave and a double-layer gas cylinder for the first time, which provides a baseline for the validation and verification of numerical tools and theoretical models. This study provides a deeper understanding of RM instability.

15207820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207820.value: 通風管道系統是維持現代建築物室內空氣質量的不可或缺的重要組成部分。然而，通風設備噪聲以及管道不連續性（如阻尼器、傳感器、彎道、過渡件、風道轉角、分支點甚至消音器的存在）引起的空氣流動噪聲是不可避免的。管道噪音問題阻礙著以更好空氣質量為目標的通風管道系統的發展。因此，針對通風管道系統中全頻率段噪聲的控制研究是很有必要的。目前常用的阻性消聲裝置對中、高頻寬帶噪聲具有良好的控製作用，但是對低頻噪聲的消聲效果卻非常有限。而亥姆霍茲共鳴器作為一種用於低頻噪聲控制的消聲裝置，在由其幾何尺寸決定的共振頻率處有非常強的吸聲能力，但是吸聲頻帶卻相對較窄。因此，對於大多數工程師而言低頻噪聲的控制目前仍然是一個挑戰。 本申請項目書依據申請人和參與人最近的研究工作提出利用周期性亥姆霍茲共鳴器陣列的布拉格反射和共鳴器共振的耦合效應，為實現寬帶噪聲衰減頻帶的實現提供了新的思路。然而，週期性亥姆霍茲共鳴器陣列會加劇通風管道的不連續性，使得有流條件下存在較強的流體波動。原本用於降低噪聲的亥姆霍茲共鳴器陣列可能變為管道內流體噪聲的聲源，在某些低頻率範圍內產生大於80分貝的噪聲。這些影響從未被申請者或其他研究人員研究過。本申請項目擬採用理論分析方法研究流動效應產生噪聲的基本原理，並通過數值模擬和實驗驗證相結合的研究方法進行驗證。因此，本項目的主要研究目標可分為：從理論上、數值上和實驗上研究不同流速下的流-聲耦合作用對單個共鳴器和周期性共鳴器陣列聲學性能的影響。本項目的研究意義在於基於週期性共鳴器陣列提出一種可靠、有效的低速通風管道中低頻寬帶噪聲控制方法。

15207820.label: Realisation of objectives
15207820.value: In this project, theoretical, numerical, and experimental investigations have been performed to examine the acoustic performance of the single Helmholtz resonator (HR) and the periodic Helmholtz resonators (HRs) array in the presence of grazing flow. 100% of Objective 1 has been achieved. The transfer matrix method and the Bloch wave theory have been used to theoretically calculate the acoustic performance of the single Helmholtz resonator and the periodic Helmholtz resonators array. The Linearized Navier-Stokes, Frequency domain (LNSF) interface of the numerical software COMSOL Multiphysics has been utilized to calculate the acoustic performance of the Helmholtz resonators under background grazing flow. A flow duct system has been designed and built to use the four-microphone method and the particle image velocimetry to measure the flow-acoustic interaction of the side-branch mounted Helmholtz resonators under different grazing flow speeds. We have established a semi-empirical formula to predict the transmission loss (TL) performance of the single HR and the periodic HRs array in the presence of grazing flow. The validity of the semi-empirical formula can be confirmed through numerical and experimental results. The results of Objective 1 have been published in Sensors, titled “An infinity tube with an expansion chamber for noise control in the ductwork system”. 100% of Objective 2 has been achieved. A semi-empirical formula has been proposed to predict the TL performance of the single HR model in the presence of grazing flow. The four-microphone method has been adopted to measure the TL results of a side-branch mounted single HR under different grazing flow speeds in a flow duct. The acoustic pressure of each microphone was recorded and converted to the transfer function. Then the transfer function was used to calculate the non-dimensional TL correction term under different flow speeds. The non-dimensional TL correction term has been fitted from measurement data to predict the TL correction term, and the TL correction term has been added to the theoretical TL calculation equation to predict the TL performance of the side-branch mounted single HR model. The results of Objective 2 have been submitted to Applied Acoustics, titled “Sound transmission performance of the periodic Helmholtz resonator array in the presence of grazing flow”. 100% of Objective 3 has been achieved. A numerical simulation strategy has been performed to investigate the TL performance of the single HR in the presence of grazing flow. The Reynolds Averaged Navier–Stokes model was used to simulate the background flow of the single HR. The flow field results were mapped to an acoustic mesh to calculate the acoustic pressure and the acoustic velocity under different flow speeds. TL results from the numerical simulation fit well with the theoretical prediction in the flow speed range between 0-20 m/s. Besides, The TL results of the single HR have been experimentally measured in the flow duct. The experimental results also fit well with the proposed semi-empirical formula. A particle image velocimetry experiment has been conducted to examine the fluid dynamics of the single HR in the presence of grazing flow. The velocity and vorticity distributions near the neck region of the HR model showed the shear layer increases as grazing flow speed increases. The results of Objective 3 have been published in International Journal of Aeroacoustics, titled “The acoustic performance of a dual Helmholtz resonators system in the presence of a grazing flow”. Preliminary results of Objective 3 have been published in Inter-Noise 2023, titled “Design of an instrumentation system for assessing the acoustic attenuation performance of ducted Helmholtz resonators in the presence of grazing flow”. 100% of Objective 4 has been achieved. A HRs array has been designed by constructing eight single- and double-layer Helmholtz Resonators with Embedded Neck (HREN) in two 2×2 cells. The genetic algorithm was used to optimize the geometry parameters of each cell. A flow correction term has been added to the theoretical formula to modify the acoustic impedance, and the modified theoretical formula has been used to predict the TL performance of the designed array under different grazing flow speeds. 100% of Objective 5 has been achieved. The HREN model was side-branch mounted on the flow duct to measure the TL performance under different grazing flow speeds. The HREN was fabricated using a photopolymer resin that undergoes UV light curing, employing the masked stereo-lithography 3D printing method. The broadband low-frequency sound transmission loss performance of the designed HREN array model has been experimentally investigated under a flow speed range between 0-20 m/s. Experimental results fit well with the theoretical prediction. The proposed theoretical formula can be used to predict the TL performance of the single and the periodic HRs array. The acoustic performance of the periodic HRs array in the presence of grazing flow has been systematically examined. The results of Objective 4 and Objective 5 have been submitted to The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, titled “Broadband low-frequency noise attenuation performance of a Helmholtz resonator array in the presence of grazing flow”. Preliminary results of Objective 4 and Objective 5 have been published in ICA 2022 “A periodic infinity tube array vs a periodic Helmholtz resonator array”.
