15207820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207820.value: A semi-empirical formula has been proposed to predict the transmission loss performance of the Helmholtz resonator (HR) model in the presence of grazing flow. The non-dimensional transmission loss correction term was fitted from measurement data to predict the transmission loss correction term. The proposed semi-empirical formula was applied to the prediction of the transmission loss of the single HR model under the grazing flow speed range of 0-20 m/s. The semi-empirical formula was used to predict the transmission loss performance of the periodic HRs array in the presence of grazing flow. The fluid dynamics of the neck region of the HR model under different flow speeds were investigated experimentally. As the grazing flow speed increases, the transmission loss performance of the HR model decreases due to the increase in the shear layer area [Ref-No.3]. Some modified side-branch mounted HR systems based on the periodic ducted HRs have been proposed for better noise attenuation in constrained spaces of the ventilation ductwork system. An Infinity Tube with Expansion Chamber (ITEC) has been proposed by constructing two curved HRs mounted on the same cross-section of the main duct. The designed ITEC can provide three resonance peaks in the frequency range between 0-1000 Hz. Compared to a parallel straight HR system, the ITEC can reduce the resonance frequencies by 14 Hz and 64 Hz at the first and second resonance peaks, respectively. The curved design of the ITEC can sufficiently utilize the constrained space, making it more suitable for ventilation ductwork systems [Ref-No.1]. The transmission loss performance of a dual HR system in the presence of grazing flow has been investigated. The flow field results showed that air only enters the first neck and cavity. The acoustic pressure field results showed that a secondary acoustic wave source emerges at the downstream side of the neck. The transmission loss results indicated that the flow Mach number has a more significant impact on the first transmission loss peak than on the second transmission loss peak [Ref-No.2]. A sound-absorbing metamaterial composed of the HR array (8 single HRs) has been proposed. It was optimized to increase the noise attenuation band. The transmission loss of the designed array can achieve around 20 dB/m in the prescribed frequency range of 200 to 800 Hz under grazing flow speeds of 0-20 m/s, and the proposed theoretical formula can accurately predict transmission loss performance under different grazing flow speeds [Ref-No.4].

15207820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207820.value: 1. The Helmholtz resonator-based acoustic metamaterial has been proven to be an effective way to attenuate low-frequency noise. The ventilation ductwork systems are often located in constrained spaces, and acoustic metamaterial can achieve perfect absorption with a light and compact geometry. Therefore, acoustic metamaterial can be a promising way for low-frequency noise control of the ventilation ductwork system. However, existing studies seldom consider the noise attenuation performance of acoustic metamaterials in the presence of grazing flow. In the final stage of this project, we conducted both experimental and theoretical investigations into the transmission loss performance of a Helmholtz resonator-based acoustic metamaterial in the presence of grazing flow. More investigations should be performed to design better acoustic metamaterial for low-frequency flow-generated noise control in the ventilation ductwork system. 2. In this project, time-averaged particle image velocimetry has been performed to measure the velocity and vorticity distributions in the neck region of the Helmholtz resonator. Research showed that vortex convection of the side-branch mounted structures is highly related to the acoustic cycles of the shear layer oscillation. The experimental techniques need to be improved to finish a phase-averaged particle image velocimetry to measure the acoustic response of a side-branch mounted Helmholtz resonator in a complete acoustic cycle. The results could help us to understand the sound production mechanisms of the shear layer, and enable us to develop a more accurate theoretical model to predict the sound attenuation of the Helmholtz resonator in the presence of grazing flow.

15207820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207820.value: The ventilation ductwork system has become an essential part of modern buildings as it can provide fresh air to indoor environments. However, the ventilation ductwork system often becomes a significant noise source, as it can propagate low-frequency sound over long distances into the room. The traditional design strategy for duct silencers focused on static, no-flow conditions, overlooking the background grazing flow. Besides, transmitted noise from the fan and flow-generated noise at the duct discontinuities have been identified as the noise sources of the ventilation ductwork system. Therefore, attenuating the low-frequency noise in the ventilation ductwork system is of great importance to improving the indoor acoustic environment. This project aims to use the Helmholtz resonators array to control low-frequency noise in the ventilation ductwork system in the presence of grazing flow. Experimental and numerical investigations have been adopted to investigate the fluid dynamics and acoustic performance of the Helmholtz resonator under different flow speeds. A theoretical model has been proposed to predict the transmission loss performance of the Helmholtz resonators array in the presence of grazing flow. Some modified Helmholtz resonator-based silencers have been proposed for the constrained spaces of the ventilation ductwork system.

15207920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207920.value: Intelligent conversation machines have a wide range of applications such as in customer service, product recommendation and entertainment. It has attracted much attention from research communities to develop conversation models, i.e., the artificial brains used to support machines’ human-like communication behaviors. However, this is unimaginably difficult. Although considerable efforts have been invested and conversation models have been continuously improved over the past few years, current conversation machines still cannot avoid responding with boring, inconsistent or incoherent content. There is a long road ahead for them to become truly intelligent. Humans converse smoothly because we share necessary background and commonsense knowledge. Knowledge benefits listeners to infer other parties’ preferences and focuses. It also contributes to speakers with informative and context-relevant topics for selection. Therefore, it is safe to assert that knowledge-grounded conversation machines can certainly make human-machine conversations more effective and enjoyable. The main objective of this project is to explore how to properly and effectively equip machines with competent knowledge to raise the level of conversational intelligence. We are particularly concerned with what kinds of knowledge are essential, how to logically organize and model knowledge, what mechanisms and strategies facilitate knowledge reasoning given conversation context, and how to incorporate knowledge to understand the conversation flow and generate information-rich and coherent content. Learning from successful experiences in knowledge graph and neural conversation models, we focus on knowledge reasoning and incorporation of knowledge in neural conversation machines. We aim to address the following under-researched key issues. (1) Event and entity are two elements of knowledge. They are interrelated and often applied jointly. Previously, event knowledge is almost completely neglected. It is important to develop novel mechanisms for collaborative reasoning of event and entity. (2) While knowledge is best modeled as a graph, existing conversion models are typically built upon the sequence-to-sequence architecture. This calls for the need to modify sequence-based conversation models in favor of graph-based knowledge reasoning. (3) Knowledge reasoning and incorporation should be dependent on conversation context and individuals’ abilities to understand and use knowledge. It is necessary to explore knowledge-grounded personalized context modeling. Well-organized world knowledge is an effective instrument to boost the level of machine intelligence and enhance the power of machine reasoning. Our research results and findings not only contribute to the development of knowledge-grounded conversation machines, but also provide valuable insights into researches of knowledge-enhanced machines in any applicable area. 智能對話機器在客戶服務、產品推薦和娛樂等方面具有廣泛應用，吸引了研究者的極大關注和大量精力投入智能對話模型（即用於支持機器執行交流行為的人造大腦）的開發。然而困難是難以想象的。儘管在過去幾年中已經投入了大量的精力並且對話模型得到了不斷改進，但是當前的對話機器仍然無法避免以簡單無聊或不一致的內容進行響應。機器要真正變得聰明，還有很長的路要走。 我們可以順利進行對話是因為人擁有必要的背景知識和常識。知識使聽眾能夠推斷出對方的偏好和重點，也有助於講者選擇內容豐富且與上下文相關的主題。因此，可以肯定地說，以知識為基礎的對話機器肯定可以使人機對話更加有效和有趣。該項目的目標在于探索如何正確有效地為機器配備勝任的知識以提高其對話智能的水平。我們特別關注哪些知識必不可少、如何在邏輯上組織和建模知識、在給定的對話上下文下哪些機制和策略可以促進知識推理、以及如何融合知識以理解對話過程並生成信息豐富且連貫的內容。 學習知識圖譜和神經對話模型的成功經驗，我們專注於知識推理和知識在神經對話機器中的結合。我們旨在解決以下尚未充分研究的關鍵問題。（1）事件和實體是知識的兩大要素。它們彼此關聯且經常聯合使用。以前，事件知識幾乎被完全忽略了。開發新穎的事件和實體協作推理機制非常重要。（2）雖然最好將知識建模為圖形，但現有的對話模型通常建立在序列到序列的體系結構上。這就需要修改基於序列的對話模型，以支持基於圖的知識推理。（3）知識推理和知識融合應取決於對話環境和個人理解和使用知識的能力。有必要探索基於知識的個性化上下文建模。 有組織的結構化世界知識是提高機器智能水平和增強機器推理能力的有效工具。我們的研究結果和發現不僅有助於發展以知識為基礎的會話機器，而且還可以為任何適用領域的知識增強型機器的研究提供有價值的經驗和見解。

15208120.label: Project Objectives
15208120.value: To theoretically investigate and optimize plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity structures for spectral-transmissive filtering We will theoretically investigate the gold/silver nanoparticles-on-cavity structures and design plasmonically enhanced optical transmission microfilters. High-index dielectric semiconductor layer will be sandwiched between the metallic nanolayer and gold/silver nanoparticles to form Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity microfilters. Different sized gold/silver nanoparticles are utilized to enhance the spectral differentials between microfilters via Mie resonance. Theoretical analysis based on temporal coupled-mode theory will be carried out to investigate the light resonances, including both FP and Mie resonances, as well as the Fano effects of the structure for response synthesis in filter design. To reduce cross-channel light interference, we will devise microlens-like FP cavities by introduction of spherical surface for the top side of dielectric semiconductor layer. The synthetic influence of such non-flat surface on the optical responses of gold/silver nanoparticles-on-cavity structure will be investigated to excavate the spectral properties of such plasmonically enhanced microfilters. Numerical simulation will be carried out by using commercial software, e.g. COMSOL Multiphysics, to optimize the structural parameters so as to develop large-scale arrayed disparate microfilters whose transmission spectra are with one or more low-loss high-extinction-ratio transmission bands in visible range. To fabricate large-scale plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity microfilter array by using digital ultraviolet (UV) lithography technology We will use our in-house digital UV lithography platform to fabricate the designed large-scale arrayed disparate plasmonic microfilters. Nanoparticles of photocatalyst semiconductor will be dispersed in a solution of the polymer of low decomposition temperature. Then, a dynamic UV projection exposure process will be applied to customize lateral geometry and vertical height. The fabricated microstructures will be sintered in an oxidative atmosphere to eliminate polymer through thermal decomposition to obtain pre-defined FP microcavities of pure dielectric semiconductor. In addition to cavity length, the top surface of FP microcavities will also be tailored toward spherical/nonspherical profiles to obtain optimized FP microcavity array with desired optical response. Using the precision photoreduction technology, we will further print different sized gold or silver nanoparticles upon the FP cavities to achieve plasmonic nanoparticles-enhanced microfilters so as to increase the effective number of microfilters with different transmission spectra. Plasma or chemical etching process will be exploited to modify the surface morphology of the photocatalyst layer at the tens of nanometers scale to optimize the nanoparticles’ nucleation and growing processes for a better control over size and shape. Our objective on microfilter array is to fabricate sub-centimeter sized microfilter array with 1000 ~ 10000 channels whose transmission spectra are diverse from each other. To develop ultracompact optical spectrometers based on microfilter array and spectrum reconstruction algorithm Miniature high-sensitivity low-dark-current CMOS or CCD sensors will be purchased from the market and then integrated with the own-fabricated microfilter array to make ultracompact optical spectrometers. Spectrum reconstruction algorithms will be developed to drive the optical spectrometer. To maximum the performances of the spectrometer, such as spectral resolution and measurement dynamic range, we will design and comparatively test three algorithms: a) lasso and sparse Bayesian regression algorithm; b) least-square based reconstruction algorithm; c) probabilistic convolutional encoder-decoder neural network-based reconstruction algorithm. A machine learning-based method will be established to train these spectrum reconstruction algorithms. Experimental setup with broadband light-source, tunable bandpass filter and commercial optical spectrometer will be built to characterize the performance of the fabricated optical spectrometer. With the tunable filter, the testing light beam will be continuously tailored in spectrum before split and inputted into the commercial and own-fabricated spectrometers. Experimental data measured by the two spectrometers will be used to train the algorithms, and an automated calibration method for the own-fabricated spectrometer will be established. The ultimate goal of this project is to create a new pathway to cost-effectively fabricate large-scale disparate microfilter array with tens of thousands of channels and thereby develop a new generation of high-performance sub-centimeter-sized optical spectrometers with the resolving power of 500 ~ 5000 (i.e. the spectral resolution of 0.06 ~ 0.6 nm) over the whole visible regime.

15208120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208120.value: This project aims to investigate the light resonances and filtering properties of large-scale arrayed plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity microfilters and thereby develop sub-centimeter sized optical spectrometers for high-resolution spectroscopic measurement in applications where miniaturization and portable are critical. Optical spectrometry is an essential tool in the investigation of physical/electronic structures and chemical compositions at the scales of macro, molecular or even atomic levels and thus plays vital roles in nearly all science and engineering fields. Conventional optical spectrometers are bulky laboratory instruments with complex optical systems. One of growing demands is to develop miniaturized optical spectrometers for efficient and user-friendly spectroscopic measurement in pharmaceutical, biochemical and environmental testings as well as industrial and agricultural productions. Various schemes have been proposed to miniaturize optical spectrometers, which can be generally classified into optical fiber/waveguide-type microspectrometers and miniature complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS)/charge-coupled device (CCD)-type spectrometers. Compared with fiber/waveguide-type microspectrometers, miniature CMOS/CCD-type spectrometers can directly measure incident light and have advantages of efficient use of incoming light, ease of operation, and great potential for integration with e.g. smartphone for portable applications. Recently, a miniature CCD-type spectrometer based on a 195-channel microfilter array made from quantum dots attracted wide attention. In addition to its distinct microfilter array, the work illustrated an important concept that the use of good reconstruction algorithm can ease conventional spectral orthogonality requirement on microfilters and improve spectrometer performances. However, as the resolving power of such spectrometers depends mainly on the amount of microfilters and their spectral differentials, the challenge is how to develop cost-effective large-scale disparate microfilter array with much more channels. In this project, we aim to tackle the challenge through the design and fabrication of plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity microfilter array, whose structure can be flexibly fabricated by our in-house digital ultraviolet lithography system. Dynamic optical exposure technology will be used to rapidly fabricate length-varying Fabry-Perot microcavity array. Then different sized gold/silver nanoparticles will be printed upon microcavities by using our recently developed precision photoreduction technology to plasmonically enhance the spectral differentials between microfilters of thousands or even millions of channels. Moreover, convolutional neural network-based spectrum reconstruction and machine learning-based calibration methods will be developed to fully unlock the CMOS/CCD-type spectrometer’s potential. The successful implementation of this project will create a new pathway towards the next generation of high-performance miniature optical spectrometers. Such spectrometers promise to facilitate widespread applications in not only scientific researches but also industrial and agricultural activities. 本項目旨在研究基於等離激元纳米粒子-光學腔結構的大规模微濾光器陣列及其光學共振和濾波特性，開發可在小型化和便攜性至關重要的领域进行高分辨率光譜測量的亞厘米尺寸光譜儀。 光譜测量是研究物理/電子結構和化學組成的宏觀、分子或甚至原子級尺度的重要手段，在幾乎所有科學和工程領域中都發揮著至關重要的作用。傳統光譜儀是具有復雜光學系統的笨重實驗室儀器。近年來，日益增長的需求之一是開發微小型光學光譜儀，用於製藥、生化和環境測試以及工業和農業生產中進行高效且好用的光譜測量。 日前，多種方案已被提出用於实现光譜儀小型化，大致可分為基於光纖/波導的微光譜儀和基於互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）/電荷耦合器件（CCD）的小型光譜儀。與光纖/波導型微光譜儀相比，CMOS / CCD型光譜儀可以直接測量入射光，因此具有利用入射光效率高，易於操作，以及可集成於智能手機并开发便攜式應用等优势。 最近，基於量子點製成的具有195通道微濾光器陣列的CCD型光譜儀引起了廣泛關注。除了其獨特的微濾光器陣列之外，該工作還提出了一個重要的概念，那就是利用良好的重構算法可以緩解光譜仪用微濾光器陣列的光譜正交性要求，並提高光譜儀的性能。但是，這类光譜儀的光譜分辨能力主要取決於微濾光器的數量及其光譜差異性，因此這裡面臨的新挑戰是如何開發具有更多通道的經濟實惠的大規模差異性微濾光器陣列。 在本項目中，我們拟通過設計能用自建數字化紫外光刻系統灵活制备的等離激元納米粒子-光學腔微濾光器陣列來應對该挑戰。我们将采用動態光學曝光技術快速製造腔長可變的法布里-珀罗光學微腔陣列，然後采用自己最近開發的精准光還原技術將不同大小的金或銀納米粒子打印在微腔上，通過等離激元效应增強具有數千個甚至數百萬個通道的陣列式微濾光器的光譜差異性。此外，將開發基於卷積神經網絡的光譜重构和基於機器學習的校準方法，以充分開發CMOS / CCD型光譜儀的潛力。 本項目的成功實施將為下一代高性能微小型光譜儀的研制開闢一條新途徑。该光譜儀不但有利於促進科學研究，而且在工業和農業活動中具有廣泛應用前景。

15208120.label: Realisation of objectives
15208120.value: This project aims to investigate the light resonances and filtering properties of plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilters and develop miniature optical spectrometers for portable spectroscopic measurement applications. In the past several years, many remarkable research outcomes in line with the project objects have been achieved: 1. To theoretically investigate and optimize plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity structures for spectral-transmissive filtering We have theoretically investigated the strong coupling between FP resonance and Mie resonance of plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilters for spectral filtering in miniature computational spectrometers. In these microfilters, size-controlled AgNPs are directly printed within the FP microcavities whose length of microcavities can be precisely tailored, which thus endows such a thin-film microfilter device with high scalability for high-resolution broad-bandwidth computational spectrometers. Numerical simulations have been conducted to reveal the transmission spectra of such plasmonic microfilters. Results revealed that, when the thickness of the photopolymer layer is 320 nm, a typical Rabi splitting of the 3rd FP peak can be observed at a wavelength ranging from 400 to 450 nm with the increase of AgNPs' diameter. In the 400 nm case, when the AgNPs' diameter increases, the 2nd FP peak, and the 3rd FP peak both show a red shift while the 4th FP peak shows a blue shift. Those results show that the introduction of AgNPs not only directly causes Rabi splitting but also causes a Rabi-splitting-like opposite shift to FPMs on two sides of plasmonic resonance mode, even if they are far from the plasmonic resonance frequency near 400 nm. Another typical phenomenon of the strong coupling, anti-crossing, has also been observed with the moving of Rabi splitting peaks with the movement of FP peaks according to the change of cavity length. Simulations have also been conducted to investigate the spectra response of the microfilters when the diameter of the AgNPs changes from 0 nm to 60 nm and the thickness of the photopolymer is 200 nm, 300 nm, and 400 nm, respectively. Results revealed that both changing the thickness of the photopolymer layer and the size of the AgNPs can provide a spectral variety of the plasmonic microfilters. 2. To fabricate large-scale plasmonic nanoparticles-on-cavity microfilter array by using digital UV lithography technology We have fabricated the designed plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilter array and characterized its spectral responses in the experiments. The fabrication of such a plasmonic microfilter array includes mainly five steps: sputtering deposition of silver and SiO2 nanolayers, sol-gel spin coating of TiO2 nanolayer, direct printing of size-controlled AgNPs, grayscale patterning and nanoscale thickness-tuning of polymer FP cavities, and sputtering deposition of silver and SiO2 nanolayers. The two critical steps of the fabrication processes are the direct printing of sized-controlled AgNPs and the nanoscale thickness-tuning of polymer FP cavity, which are the keys to achieving a large-scale spectrum-disparate microfilter array. Notably, the fabrication techniques are based on our in-house digital ultraviolet exposure technology using a digital micromirror array (DMD). The high-speed DMD has a switching time of less than one millisecond, which enables ultra-fast, parallel modulation of UV exposure doses on different target positions. It can thus rapidly and finely tailor the size of AgNPs and the thickness of FP microcavities via the precision photoreduction and grayscale photopolymerization technologies, respectively, to fabricate the designed large-scale disparate microfilter array. The transmission optical spectra of the fabricated large-scale arrayed plasmonic microfilters have been measured. It provides high-density transmission spectral peaks, i.e., 2436 transmission peaks, ranging from 425 nm to 850 nm. The full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs) of those transmission spectral peaks range from 12.2 nm to 88.3 nm with an average value of 23.8 nm. Moreover, Rabi splitting predicted in the numerical simulation was observed in the measured reflection and transmission spectra at short wavelength regions. When the cavity length is short, a broad resonant peak of the 1st-order FPM appears in the wavelength range of visible light. With the size increase of AgNPs, a clear spectral splitting was observed around 400 nm ~ 600 nm in both reflection and transmission spectra. When the cavity length becomes relatively longer, the resonant spectral peaks of the 2nd and 3rd-order FPMs enter the visible light range. 3. To develop ultracompact free-field optical spectrometer based on microfilter array and spectrum reconstruction algorithm We have developed an ultracompact optical spectrometer by using the own-fabricated plasmonic microfilter array. For ease of installation, the fabricated microfilter array was installed on the imaging position of a lens that can clearly project the light pattern passing through the microfilter array onto the CMOS image sensor. The monochrome images measured by the camera, whose dark field and bias response were corrected to enhance signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), were pre-treated with pixel binning and data filtering for noise reduction. Image data after denoising processes were used for spectral reconstruction. A machine-learning-based AI method was established to enable the spectrometer using a large-scale plasmonic microfilter array to reconstruct the spectrum of an input light beam from CMOS image output. Suppose that there are m microfilters and n training data that are the pairs of input light spectrum and CMOS output: (xj, yj), j=1, …, n. An input light spectrum xj(λ) is a function that maps each wavelength λ to the intensity of the light at that wavelength. When a microfilter array of m elements is used, we have a CMOS image output with m effective pixel values yj = [yj,1, ⋯ , y j,m]T for each input light spectrum xj. For a new unknown input light spectrum x ̃(λ), we will reconstruct x ̃(λ) from the CMOS output ỹ = [ỹ1, ⋯, ỹm]T. The performance of the AI-empowered computational optical spectrometer has been evaluated. The spectrum-resolving ability of the spectrometer was tested by using a time-elongated exposure of two quickly generated adjacent single-peak light spectra. Results revealed that the spectrometer can discriminate two adjacent spectral peaks very well. More meticulous testing of the spectrometer’s performance over the whole visible range was conducted by sweeping such single-peak light spectra over the wavelength from 395 nm to 725 nm with a step of 0.2 nm. The spectrometer can measure peak wavelengths accurately over the whole testing wavelength range (i.e., 395 ~ 725 nm) and its error is about 0.03 nm. The measured FWHMs of the peak wavelengths of the measured spectra is 0.65 nm, which is close to the FWHM of the input spectrum, i.e., 0.54 nm. 4. To create a new pathway to cost-effectively fabricate large-scale disparate microfilter array with tens of thousands of channels and thereby develop a new generation of high-performance sub-centimeter-sized optical spectrometers. We have successfully developed a new small-size high-performance computational spectrometer via the creation of a plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilter array. We have designed and fabricated a spectrum-disparate optical microfilter array by directly printing size-controlled silver nanoparticles into cavity-length-varying Fabry‒Perot microcavities. With a machine learning-based training process, a miniature computational spectrometer has been fabricated to measure input spectra at the resolution of about 0.65 nm over the whole visible light range. Such an AI-empowered miniature computational spectrometers may provide a promising solution for many valuable industrial and daily-life applications, such as spectral imaging devices or portable skin health monitoring.

15208120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208120.value: This project proposed to investigate the light resonances and filtering properties of large-scale arrayed plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilters to develop miniaturized optical spectrometers for portable spectroscopic measurement applications. Major findings and research outcomes of the project include: i. A new type of plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilter array has been developed for ultracompact computational spectrometers. The strong coupling between FP resonance and Mie resonance has been harnessed to create large-scale arrayed spectrum-disparate microfilters to meet the requirements of developing high-resolution broad-bandwidth computation spectrometer. Based on our recently developed precision photoreduction technology, the micropatterns of size-controlled AgNPs and the cavity-length-varying FP microcavities were rapidly printed by using a precision photoreduction and grayscale photopolymerization technologies, respectively. A spectrum-disparate plasmonic microfilter array with 1152 elements has been fabricated to integrate with a commercial CMOS image sensor for the construction of a miniature computational spectrometer. (See the paper published in Nature Communications, 2024). ii. With a machine learning-based training process, an AI-empowered miniature computational spectrometer haven been developed for the measurement of input spectra of visible light. The performance of the fabricated AI-empowered computational optical spectrometer has been evaluated. Experimental results revealed that the spectrometer can discriminate two adjacent spectral peaks very well over the whole visible range. The spectrometer can measure peak wavelengths accurately over the whole testing wavelength range at an accuracy of less than 0.03 nm. The measured FWHMs of the peak wavelengths of the measured spectra is 0.65 nm. (See the paper published in Nature Communications, 2024). iii. The fabrication technology established for the direct printing of the micropatterns of size-controlled AgNPs for computational spectrometer has been further developed to directly print the micropatterns of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2). These directly printed micropatterns of MoS₂ can be decorated into gold nanoparticle (AuNP)/MoS₂ heterostructure, in which size-controlled AuNPs can be grown selectively on the surface of MoS₂. Owing to both electromagnetic and chemical enhancements, the directly printed plasmonic AuNP/MoS₂ substrate can greatly enhance Raman spectroscopic signals to detect the footprints of molecules. (See the attached paper under revision in Advanced Materials, 2025). In short, we have developed the proposed ultracompact computational spectrometer based on a specially designed plasmonic microfilter array and machine-learning-based training and spectrum reconstruction algorithms. The technology established for the fabrication of plasmonic microfilter array has been further extended to develop other nanophotonic structures and applications.

15208120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208120.value: We will continue to improve the design and fabrication technologies of plasmonic microfilter array to develop miniature computational spectrometers with higher resolutions and broader bandwidth. In addition to silver nanoparticles, other kinds of plasmonic nanoparticles whose plasmon resonances locate at different wavelengths, will be explored to develop computational spectrometers operating at other wavelengths. We will also further improve the machine learning based training and spectrum reconstruction algorithms. It is expected that better algorithms can not only greatly save response time of the computational spectrometer (which is mainly limited by spectrum reconstruction process) but also further improve the resolution of the spectrometer to meet the demands of high-resolution portable spectroscopic measurement applications.

15208120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208120.value: This project aims to investigate the light resonances and filtering properties of large-scale arrayed plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilters to develop miniaturized optical spectrometers for portable spectroscopic measurement applications. Optical spectrometers are essential tools in many industrial and daily-life applications, but conventional spectrometers are typically bulky and expensive. Recently, great many efforts have been made to develop miniaturized spectrometers. However, it is challenging to overcome the trade-off between small size and high performance. In this project, we have successfully developed a complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor-based miniature computational spectrometer using a plasmonic nanoparticles-in-cavity microfilter array. Based on our in-house digital ultraviolet lithography technology, size-controlled silver nanoparticles are directly printed into cavity-length-varying Fabry‒Perot microcavities to fabricate spectrum-disparate optical microfilter array. A miniature computational spectrometer has been constructed by integrating a plasmonic microfilter array of over a thousand elements with a commercial CMOS image sensor. With a machine learning-based training process, a miniature computational spectrometer has been fabricated to measure input spectra at sub-nanometre resolution over the whole visible light range. Such an AI-empowered high-performance miniature computational spectrometers may find many important applications in both industrial and daily-life applications, such as spectral imaging devices or portable skin health monitoring.

15208420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208420.value: Multifunctional and regenerable N-chlorine based biocidal and detoxifying textiles were designed and developed using a robust zirconium metal–organic framework (MOF), UiO-66-NH2, as a chlorine carrier coated on textiles. The active chlorine loaded MOFs/fiber composite was fast and potent for broad-spectrum inactivation of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as fungi according to ASTM G21. Typically, with a 0.12% chlorine loading, the reductions of 4.7 log (99.998%) and 5.2 log (99.999%) against E. coli and S. aureus after 0.5 min, and 7.7 log (100%) and 7.8 log (100%) after 1 min contact were achieved respectively. In the fungi resistance test, zero growth was observed after a 28-day period at 0.12% chlorine loading indicating a sustained effect for inhibition of fungi growth. The anti-viral activity was tested by measuring the effects on SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. In our experiments, the virus titer was determined using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Both the unmodified cloth and the inactive MOF/fiber composite showed increasing virus titers within 3 days, indicating a rapid infection and virus replication. In contrast, the chlorinated composite showed a significant delay in virus growth for 48 h, after which the virus titer started to increase. The RT-qPCR results indicated that a log 3–5 reduction in virus titer was observed after 48 h in the chlorine loaded composite as compared to that in the controls. For the chlorine stability, the results indicated that after 40 days of storage, the chlorine maintained 77% of its original loading. To evaluate the rechargeability, the active chlorine was quenched by a 0.1% sodium thiosulfate solution and then rechlorinated with a sodium hypochlorite solution. After 5 quenching and rechlorination cycles, the same chlorine loading on the MOF composite was achieved, indicating excellent regenerability of the MOF/fiber composite as well as overall stability of the MOF coating layer. Bio-compatibility of the chlorine loaded MOF/fiber composite was tested using human skin fibroblasts (HSF). Cell bio-compatibility was assessed by MTT assay. Comparing uncoated PET(polyester) fabric, UiO-66-NH2/PET, and chloring loaded UiO-66-NH-Cl/PET, the cell viabilities following a 24-hour treatment are 65.8%, 71.2%, and 85.1%, respectively. The result indicates a very satisfactory bio-compatibility for the chlorine loaded composite. To explore other protective functions, the chlorine loaded MOF/fiber composite selectively and rapidly degraded sulfur mustard and its chemical simulant 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (CEES) with half-lives less than 3 minutes(publication 1).

15208420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208420.value: In the future, it is suggested to study various MOFs that can be applied to textiles and other materials loaded with different active agents to achieve different functionalities. In this regard, we conducted research work by loading persulfate ions, which served as stable active peroxide precursors, into porous zirconium-based MOFs (Zr-MOFs), enabling them to act as regenerable reservoirs for the slow release of biocidal hydrogen peroxide upon hydrolysis by contacting with humid air. The active peroxide precursors within the Zr-MOFs are stable during the storage and easily regenerated once consumed. The persulfate-loaded Zr-MOFs can be integrated onto textiles using a facile aqueous in-situ growth procedure, and these composites demonstrate potent and reusable biocidal activity against both Gram-negative bacteria and Gram-positive bacteria (publication 5). Further extending the research into other materials, such as cellulose nanofibers based aerogel composites loaded with high amount of MOF, can achieve detoxification of air and water (publication 4) and other functions. The synthesis process of the MOF-based composite can also be further optimised, especially using aqueous based media instead of organic solvent for better environmental protection, high-loading efficiency, and better accessibility. This direction was also explored by us (publication 2).

15208420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208420.value: In this project, we designed and developed multifunctional and regenerable biocidal and detoxifying textiles based on a robust zirconium metal–organic framework (MOF) loaded with active chlorine. The release of active chlorine kills a broad-spectrum pathogenetic microorganisms and viruses, including the one responsible for COVID-19, and detoxifies harmful gases such as mustard gas. The active chlorine loaded offers a sustained biocidal and detoxifying functions for a period of over 40 days and can be easily reloaded when it is consumed, which offers a long-term and durable protection. The resulting functional textiles can provide protections against biological and chemical threats in a wide range of applications and in environments such as hospitals, elderly nursing home, as well as chemical warfare. The technologies we developed are scalable and can be adapted by commercial textile processing plants, indicating a high potential for real applications. The results of this research should also encourage the development of other promising MOF-based composites that contribute to the areas of healthcare and human and environment protection.

15208520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208520.value: 空腔氣動聲學共振現象廣泛出現在不同工程應用領域。此現象會引發高度連貫的自我耦合流體運動及自激振蕩流動。持續暴露於此現象會直接導致噪聲污染、持續的共振壓和聲激勵下帶來的結構壽命縮短、以及最終整體工程系統的性能下降。這種共振現象是由其自激流動振蕩和隨之而產生的噪聲之間的連續不斷反饋循環所造成的。此類空腔氣動聲共振問題通常以主動或被動控制技術為解決方案。大多數主動控制方案是通過在指定的腔壁對小擾流最為敏感的位置引入流速擾動來應對流動振蕩。盡管此技術在小規模模擬實驗室測試裡頗有成效，但它仍然未能應用於實際工程中。其主因在於所需要的傳感器和驅動器功能難以按實際工程規模放大，而且在實際應用規模上構建可靠控制架構的成本也過於高昂。預計這些難題在今後短時間內也難以得到解決。而被動控制技術更易於在實際規模中應用，並且成本較低。通常被動控制技術的手段有安裝擾流板、柵欄、小桿、多孔表面，變更腔型幾何形狀，以及為型腔壁提供通風等。這些手段在減少空腔共振噪聲的設計方面非常有效，其效果甚至能比主動控制更好。然而，它們都會遇上壹個重要問題，即被動控制啟動後原來的大尺度基礎流場產生急劇變化，會導致諸如流場總阻力增加等不良後果，而這些不良後果往往需要許多耗時的設計疊代以將其最小化。實際上，這是壹個被動流動控制關鍵技術瓶頸問題。它阻擋了被動控制技術在空腔氣動噪聲共振研究方面的進壹步發展。受此啟發，以及我們在類似氣動聲學研究中的初步成果的鼓舞，該項目旨在開發壹種摒除以上所述缺點的氣動聲學被動控制的新理念。它涉及到運用彈性面板提供的局部表面柔度設計，旨在僅改變流動不穩定性和形成空腔共振反饋的聲波，但同時保持空腔內大尺度基礎流場不變。與此同時，利用面板構型設計來優化降噪技術也壹並得以闡釋。可以預期的是，該項目成果將用於減緩主要由工程流動系統中的氣動噪聲反饋循環所驅動的自激振蕩等不良後果，並為之提供堅實的科學基礎和先進的被動控制技術。

15208520.label: Realisation of objectives
15208520.value: ** For Objective 1 ** The first objective focused on outlining the effects of introducing localized surface compliance, achieved with a thin elastic panel, on the modification of cavity aeroacoustic resonance and its impact on the acoustic radiation. This part of the study utilized a problem from the aeronautical industry, specifically a fundamental unit of a new flow liner design with sub-wavelength absorption capability, which involved an elastic panel placed on a cavity. Unfortunately, the flow supply facility of the open jet used in the anechoic chamber at the Department of Mechanical Engineering at PolyU malfunctioned during this phase, requiring significant funding and time for repairs. Thus, the PI established a collaborative effort for the experiments with research partners at LAUM in Le Mans, France, who had a flow-acoustics facility capable of delivering a subsonic mean flow Mach number of about 0.25. A liner unit composed of a thin stretched elastic latex membrane placed on top of a 3D-printed open cavity was designed and fabricated. The facility dimensions allowed for flow and acoustics testing with shallow cavities, leading to a cavity depth-to-length ratio of 0.5. Extensive experimental results demonstrated that the emergence of panel modes significantly shifted the cavity resonance toward lower frequencies and created several additional acoustic transmission drops, due to substantial modifications of the aeroacoustic-feedback loop associated with the cavity opening. The PI also conducted a study of the experimental observations using his high-fidelity time-domain direct aeroacoustic-structural interaction simulation (DAASIS) code. The numerical results closely matched the experimental findings and indicated that the cavity-panel installation offered greater resistance to acoustic propagation than traditional resonator-based liner designs, along with weaker responses to flow instability and non-linear effects under strong acoustic incidence. These characteristics were well-suited for acoustic absorption requirements in aeronautical applications. Thus, the results confirmed the feasibility of the proposed idea for the project and its potential for expansion to other cavity and flow configurations. ** For Objective 2 ** The second objective focused on examining how the fundamental interaction between an elastic panel and the cavity affected the aeroacoustic-feedback loop, ultimately influencing noise production using DAASIS calculations. To facilitate the investigation, a preliminary problem with similar aeroacoustic-feedback characteristics was addressed first. This problem involved subsonic airfoil flow tonal noise, resulting from the aeroacoustic-feedback between the suction surface boundary layer and its sharp trailing edge. Unlike cavity flow, the absence of an interior volume beneath the elastic panel eliminated the influence of acoustic resonant modes, allowing for a clearer examination of how panel compliance impacted the aeroacoustic-feedback loop and subsequent noise production. Comprehensive analyses indicated that the noise reduction depended on the flow-induced resonant panel modal responses and their influence on convective flow instabilities and interactions with the airfoil trailing edge. The study progressed to the flow past a deep cavity with a length-to-depth ratio of 0.4 at a freestream Mach number of 0.09 and a Reynolds number based on cavity length of 40,000. Similar to the preliminary problem, the aim was to achieve local energy absorption from the aeroacoustic processes that sustain the cavity self-sustained feedback loop for tonal noise. After accurately replicating FIVE key aeroacoustic processes, an elastomeric elastic panel was strategically introduced to modify each process, with its fluid-loaded natural frequency matched to the cavity feedback characteristic frequency to enhance flow-induced resonance for energy absorption. A reduction in cavity noise pressure and power levels of 3.8 and 4.8 dB was achieved, along with an unexpected drag reduction of nearly 19%. Comprehensive wavenumber-frequency analyses showed that while the original aeroacoustic-feedback loop still occurred, its effectiveness was significantly reduced. To verify the DAASIS results regarding cavity noise reduction, an experimental validation study was initiated. Since no suitable aeroacoustic wind tunnel facility was available at PolyU, the PI collaborated with a research partner at Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) in Shenzhen, China. The experimental setup involved a cavity with an elastic panel flush-mounted at the cavity bottom, using same structural and material properties as in the DAASIS calculations. Pressure measurements of cavity flow and far-field noise, along with PIV flow visualization, captured the interactions between flow dynamics and cavity acoustic responses. The results showed that the panel responses effectively altered the aeroacoustic patterns inside the cavity, leading to a significant reduction in tonal noise of 16.1 dB, especially at freestream Mach numbers of 0.06 to 0.09. This study provided a detailed analysis of the modified aeroacoustic-feedback mechanisms due to the elastic panel. A comparison of acoustic spectra with the baseline rigid cavity configuration revealed that the panel reduced peak noise levels and shifted dominant acoustic frequencies, indicating a disruption in aeroacoustic coupling processes. Observations consistent with DAASIS predictions were noted, confirming the proposed concept of using localized surface compliance through an elastic panel. ** For Objective 3 ** The work for the third objective was based on the knowledge and experience gained from the first and second objectives. It involved a unique passive control methodology for suppressing deep cavity noise by employing a distributed surface compliance mechanism through the strategic design and arrangement of multiple elastic panels. The same cavity configuration and flow conditions as in the work for objective two were used. The study focused on the complex dynamics of cavity flows, examining the intricacies of noise generation processes influenced by the placement of one, two, and three panels at various locations on the cavity walls. An extensive analysis included both a rigid cavity and five distinct cavity-panel configurations with a single panel, providing critical insights into flow characteristics. These findings informed the development of five novel cavity-panel arrangements featuring double and triple panel configurations aimed at maximizing cavity noise reduction. The design rationale for these multiple panel configurations is based on two fundamental observations: the predominance of shear layer fluctuations near the cavity's aft wall adjacent to the trailing edge and the dominant acoustic modes operating at the cavity bottom. By targeting these key aspects of the cavity aeroacoustic mechanism with strategically designed elastic panels, the proposed approach was expected to significantly influence and reduce noise generation processes. The cavity aeroacoustics and the structural resonance of various cavity-panel configurations were simulated using the DAASIS code. The numerical results revealed that the flow-induced elastic panels significantly influenced the coupling between developing shear layers and cavity acoustic modes. Each panel dictated its specific bending wave pattern according to its orientation. Vertical panels predominantly exhibited transverse bending wave propagation, while horizontal panels supported standing bending waves. The panels in structural resonance interacted with the flow and acoustic fluctuations in unique ways, leading to significant changes in cavity noise generation characteristics. Notably, the most effective configuration achieved a remarkable noise power reduction of 15 dB, and the panels did not contribute to far-field noise radiation despite their strong vibratory responses. This indicated their primary role in absorbing flow fluctuation energy within the cavity-panel systems. The observation of this new phenomenon of aeroacoustic-structural resonance in multiple panel configurations highlighted the potential of the proposed passive approach for effectively suppressing cavity noise radiation. It was also interesting to note that this passive approach resulted in an unintended advantage of significant drag reduction of up to 15%, enhancing the appeal of the proposed idea in practical engineering applications.

15208520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208520.value: [1] The proposed idea of using localized surface compliance with a thin elastic panel to modify cavity aeroacoustic resonance and its effect on acoustic radiation was fully confirmed both experimentally and numerically. Extensive experimental results showed that the emergence of panel modes significantly shifted the cavity resonance to lower frequencies and created several acoustic transmission drops, due to major changes in the aeroacoustic feedback loop linked to the cavity opening. The numerical results closely matched the experimental findings and indicated that the cavity-panel setup provided greater resistance to acoustic propagation than traditional resonator-based designs. [Outputs 9–1 and 8–1] [2] The fundamental physical mechanisms governing interactions between an elastic panel and a cavity that affect the cavity aeroacoustic feedback loop, thus influencing noise production, were successfully explored through a case study of flow past a deep cavity with a length-to-depth ratio of 0.4 at a freestream Mach number of 0.09 and a Reynolds number based on cavity length of 40,000. This was accomplished using extensive high-fidelity time-domain calculations. Drawing from insights gained from a simpler problem, the goal was to achieve local energy absorption through panel structural resonance from the cavity aeroacoustic processes sustaining self-sustained feedback for tonal noise production. A strategically designed elastomeric panel was introduced to modify five key aeroacoustic processes of the flow. This led to a significant noise power reduction of 4.8 dB and an unexpected drag reduction of nearly 19%. [Outputs 8–1, 8–2, and 9–2] [3] The confirmed idea was successfully extended to attempt more effective deep cavity noise suppression by means of distributed surface compliance through the strategic design and arrangement of multiple elastic panels. The rationale was targeting two key cavity aeroacoustic processes, namely (i) the predominance of shear layer fluctuations near the cavity aft wall adjacent to the trailing edge and (ii) the dominant acoustic modes operating at the cavity bottom, for noise generation. The results of extensive numerical analyses showed that all panel configurations attempted gave less noise with more complicated aeroacoustics-structural interactions. Notably the most effective configurations gave an impressive noise power reduction by 15 dB, together with 15% drag reduction, which is unprecedented in the aeraocoustics community. In these cases, the elastic the panels did not contribute to far-field noise radiation despite their strong vibratory responses. [Outputs 8–3 to 8–5, and 9–3]

15208520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208520.value: The present project establishes a solid foundation for an innovative idea that effectively suppresses noise generated deep cavities while simultaneously reducing drag. The project outcomes highlight opportunities for further research in areas the industry has been exploring to improve technology and operations. Two examples follow. The proposed idea offers a unique advantage over all existing control methods. It is non-invasive, preserving the original flow geometry and its large-scale characteristics. Further development of this idea is recommended to explore turbulent and higher Mach numbers flows. This direction could provide alternative methods for controlling noise and drag for flow-handling systems encountered in green transportation, energy production, and sustainability. Re-designing system geometry is often necessary with current approaches. This innovation may offer a convenient, non-invasive way to modify existing systems, significantly reducing costs. The knowledge gained for the interaction between cavity aeroacoustic processes and resonant panels may foster new ideas of flow acoustic liners for low-frequency noise reduction without sacrificing drag. Such liners are highly demanded for reducing modern aeroengine fan noise and high-speed duct flow applications. Strategic design of panels near silencing elements may enhance noise absorption and flow transmission loss, as indicated in the works for Outputs 8-6 and 9-1.

15208520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208520.value: Cavity noise reduction is an important area of research in aeroacoustics because it affects many mechanical systems. In certain unfavorable conditions, airflow can induced self-sustained flow oscillations and/or structural vibrations that couple with acoustic modes, resulting in intense noise. These vibrations can pose significant challenges in various engineering applications, whether in low-speed or high-speed environments. This study proposes and validates an innovative approach for reducing noise by flow past deep cavities using distributed surface compliance, which is realized with multiple strategically designed elastic panels. By adjusting the natural frequencies of these panels to match the specific flow instabilities that cause cavity aeroacoustic resonance, this approach achieves an impressive overall reduction of 15 dB in noise power levels that surpasses all works in literature, with a concurrent 15% drag reduction. Even just one panel can provide a 4 dB noise power reduction and a 20% decrease in drag. Through comprehensive temporal-spectral analyses, the study elucidates the fundamental aeroacoustic-structural interaction between panel flow-induced vibrations and cavity aeroacoustics and identifies the dominant noise suppression mechanisms. The proposed innovative approach shows great potential for creating quieter and more energy-efficient fluid-moving applications and drones that frequently incorporate cavity configurations.

15208720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208720.value: 太陽/光能已被認為是解決傳染病，能源危機和環境破壞等全球性問題的重要和關鍵因素。收集光能並將其轉換為有用能量正成為科學和工程方面的重要研究。 等離子體激元是一個跨領域，涉及電磁場與金屬中自由電子的集體振蕩之間的相互作用的研究，稱為表面等離子體激元共振（SPR）。在過去的幾十年中，金屬納米結構，例如金屬納米結構。金納米棒和納米殼已通過將光能轉換為多種應用而廣泛用作光學轉換器，包括納米醫學，生物傳感，光伏和光催化。金屬納米結構是優良的光學天線，可以將光波轉換為電子振盪。最近，與等離子體激元有關的研究活動已經過渡到一種新型的等離子體激元材料，即自摻雜半導體納米晶體Cu2-xE（E = S，Se和Te），其中的等離子體激元共振由空穴。這些納米晶體的局部SPR（LSPR）可以在近紅外（NIR）區域進行調整。這種強大的近紅外吸收率使它們成為又一個有希望的光轉換器。 納米雜化結構是一種將兩種類型的納米粒子融合到一個系統中的納米結構，已經作為一種新型材料。納米雜化體的相互作用可以整合各個優勢和新功能的形成。在我們先前的研究中，製備了納米雜化物，即金納米棒-硫化銅（AuNR-Cu2-xS）核-殼結構。與AuNR和Cu2-xS混合物相比，AuNR-Cu2-xS的光熱（光誘導熱）性能非常出色。我們認為，傑出的光熱性能源自兩個納米域之間的協同作用和相互作用，這可能無法通過單個組分的疊加來解釋。 從文獻中也很容易發現，增強性能已在金屬半導體納米雜化物中進行了實驗驗證。在大多數情況下，金屬域直接連接到半導體域。實際上，在這種供體-受體型相互作用中，能量轉移機制強烈地依賴於它們的分離距離。但是，文獻中很少發現相關研究。在此計劃中，我們將合成各種金屬（核）/空間/銅硫族化物（殼）納米結構，並在實驗設置和數值分析中進行全面研究，以使理解能量轉移機理/途徑之間建立聯繫，增強的性能和潛在的應用程序。

15208720.label: Realisation of objectives
15208720.value: Objective 1: Synthesize and characterize structurally well-defined metal (core)/space/copper chalcogenide (shell) nanohybrids (100%) Objective 2: Conduct simulations to elucidate energy transfer mechanisms (100%) Objective 3: Optimize these nanohybrids for applications in solar-to-vapor generation (85%) The synthesis and characterization of structurally well-defined metal (core)/spacer/copper chalcogenide (shell) nanohybrids (Objective 1) have been successfully completed. A two-step fabrication process was developed to create these nanohybrid structures. Initially, gold nanorods (AuNRs) were synthesized using a seed-mediated growth technique. Subsequently, a Cu2O layer was formed around the AuNRs, which was then transformed into a mesoporous hollow Cu2-xS shell through the Kirkendall effect in the presence of sodium sulfide. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) provided detailed structural analysis of the resulting AuNR@Cu2-xS nanohybrids. Uniform rattle structures with a core@shell configuration were observed, as depicted in Figure 1(a) of Ref [1]. Morphological characterization indicated that the gold core measured approximately 40 nm in length with an aspect ratio of ~4, and the Cu2-xS shell had a thickness of about 5 nm. Elemental analysis determined the mass ratio of Cu to Au to be approximately 10%. High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) imaging, as shown in Figure 1(b) of Ref [1], revealed a lattice spacing of 0.197 nm for the outer shell, which corresponds to the (2 0 1) plane of Cu1.96S. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis confirmed the composition of the Cu1.96S outer layer and provided lattice information for both the inner gold nanorod and the outer Cu2-xS shell. Spectroscopic analysis, as shown in Figure 1(c) of Ref [1], identified two distinct absorption peaks, indicative of the interaction between the AuNR cores and the Cu2-xS shells. The successful synthesis and comprehensive characterization of the AuNR@Cu2-xS nanohybrids satisfactorily fulfils the Objective 1, establishing a novel two-step process for the creation of these intricate nanohybrid structures. The Objective 2 has also been achieved with success. The nanohybrid demonstrated enhanced absorption in the NIR-I/II region compared to individual AuNRs and Cu2-xS nanoparticles. This enhancement is attributed to plasmon resonance energy transfer (PRET), a nonradiative energy transfer process facilitated by dipole-dipole interactions. The proximity of the dipoles and the overlap of the plasmonic materials' bandgaps are critical factors influencing the strength of PRET. The unique rattle configuration of the nanohybrid provides an ideal environment for PRET to occur. Additionally, the broadening of the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) peak in the NIR region suggests that electrons from the gold core may diffuse into the Cu2-xS shell, leading to the suppression and broadening of the LSPR peak. Finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) simulations were conducted, revealing that the local electric field intensity distribution, as shown in Figure 1(e) of Ref [1], is significantly enhanced in the nanohybrid structures compared to AuNRs alone. This enhancement suggests stronger coupling and more effective photothermal effects within the nanohybrids. Objective 3 aimed to apply the synthesized nanohybrids for solar-to-vapor generation. To achieve this, we conducted a comparative study of the photothermal responses of various nanoparticles. The results, as illustrated in Figure 1(d) of Ref [1], clearly demonstrated that the nanohybrids exhibit superior photothermal performance compared to individual AuNRs, Cu2-xS nanoparticles, and their physical mixture. This finding revealed the potential of the nanohybrids for efficient solar-to-vapor energy conversion. The initial strategy for Objective 3 involved fabricating various nanohybrid thin films using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) with a molecular weight of 54,000 as a substrate. Unfortunately, the unforeseen COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting lockdowns of local laboratories, including those of our collaborator, Professor Gaixia Xu’s laboratories at Shenzhen University, significantly disrupted our progress. The closure of borders further compounded these challenges, leading to substantial delays in achieving this objective. Efforts to address these setbacks included the attempted recruitment of Dr. Chih-Kuang Chen, an experienced chemist from National Sun Yat-sen University, who would be assigned to synthesize the thin film. However, the visa application process was also delayed due to the pandemic, preventing the utilization of scheduled project funds. Consequently, there remains an unexpected unspent balance, and Objective 3 has been mostly, but not fully, achieved. In response to these challenges, we sought alternative local collaborations and explored new avenues for the application of our nanohybrids. A promising collaboration was initiated with Professor Denvid Lau at CityU. Although the production of the intended thin films was not feasible within the original scope, this partnership led to innovative discoveries. We identified the potential of integrating our nanohybrids into concrete structures for civil engineering applications. These exciting new findings have resulted in the formulation of two collaborative proposals for the Innovation and Technology Support Programme (ITSP) (“Indoor Nanocoating for Clean Building Energy Through a Multiscale Performance-based Approach”) and the Research Impact Fund (RGC Ref No. R1014-23). While Objective 3 has faced significant obstacles due to the global pandemic, the project has adapted to these challenges. The team has redirected its focus towards novel applications of the nanohybrids, which may open up new opportunities for future research and development in the field of sustainable materials and energy conversion technologies. References [1] Z. Xu, R. Aalinkeel, S.D. Mahajan, N. Rao, T. Chen, Y. Jiang, C. Yang, G. Xu, S.A. Schwartz, W.C. Law, Second Near-Infrared Light Triggered Mini Plasmonic Heterostructures for Photothermal-Derived Multimodal Synergistic Cancer Therapy, Advanced Therapeutics 6(6) (2023).

15208720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208720.value: The successful synthesis and characterization of the metal (core)/spacer/copper chalcogenide (shell) nanohybrids, AuNR@Cu2-xS, along with their demonstrated enhanced absorption in the NIR-I/II region and promising photothermal response, opening up several opportunities for further developments and applications beyond this project. 1. Biomedical Applications: The enhanced NIR absorption and photothermal conversion efficiency make these nanohybrids excellent candidates for biomedical applications. They can be served as photothermal therapy (PTT) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI) agents. Their ability to convert NIR light into heat can be used to target and destroy cancer cells with minimal damage to surrounding healthy tissues. The strong NIR absorption could also improve the contrast and depth of photoacoustic imaging, enabling early cancer detection and therapy. 2. Photocatalysis: The presence of Cu2-xS, is good photocatalytic applications. It suggests that these nanohybrids could be effective photocatalysts. They could be used to drive chemical reactions under NIR light. Applications could include degradation of pollutants in water and air, as well as CO2 reduction and hydrogen production through water splitting.

15208720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208720.value: In this project, we explored how to harness the energy from sunlight using advanced materials. Sunlight is a clean and endless energy source that can help solve major global issues like disease, energy shortages, and environmental damage. Our research focuses on plasmonics, which is the study of how light interacts with metals at the nanoscale to create vibrations of surface electrons called surface plasmon resonances. These vibrations can turn light into other forms of energy. We've been working with a core/shell structure that is efficient at capturing light and turning it into heat. This new kind of advanced material made from gold (core) and semiconductor (shell) that can capture light, especially in the near-infrared range, which is a part of sunlight that's not visible to the eye but carries a lot of energy. From our experiments, we have found that the core/shell structure is really good at converting light into heat because they can work together in a “collaborative” way that is better than either of them alone. The project is finished with an understanding of why they work so well and how we can use them in real-world applications such as medical, environmental, and renewable energy.

15209020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209020.value: Integration of conductive materials with functional materials (e.g. photovolatic, pyroelectric, piezoelectric or triboelectric) in a substantial length can lead to a kind of 1D multifunctional fiber-based materials (MFMs) for energy harvesting. However, due to their different physicochemical properties (e.g. elastic modulus, Poisson’s ratio and chemical compatibility), interfacial failure between the constituent components is a common phenomenon for these kinds of MFMs, particularly for triboelectric MFMs where conductive materials (used as electrode, mainly metals with high surface energy) are normally laminated with organic triboelectric materials (mainly silicone and perfluorinated polymers with low surface energy). It inevitably undermines the performance and stability of MFM-based energy harvesters. Currently, fabrication of MFMs as a functional and structural integrity is still a considerably difficult challenge. A survey of literature has shown there are still no effective strategies for general fabrication of MFMs with customizable functionalities and robust interfacial bonding. To address these challenges, this project will design and develop a new kind of MFMs where continuous conductive fiber (CCF) is fully embedded in a composite sheath composed of staple fibers and triboelectric materials, i.e. staple sheath triboelectric-conductive composite yarns (SSTCYs), with customized triboelectric properties and enhanced interfacial bonding. Based on previous work done by the applicant, a special staple sheath-assisted coating strategy combining a spinning method and a surface coating approach will be developed for SSTCYs. Briefly, by introducing a staple sheath wrapped on CCF by physical binding of staple fibers firstly, triboelectric materials will be then firmly introduced on CCF as a fiber-reinforced composite layer where smooth-transition interfacial regions with enhanced bonding are expected to be formed. A series of SSTCYs samples will be designed, prepared and evaluated by adjusting constituent materials, yarn structure, and coating conditions. Both experimental and modeling studies will be carried out to analyze the relationship between system parameters and properties of SSTCYs. As a demonstration of application, SSTCYs will be made into a kind of 3D two-electrode mode energy harvesters for kinetic energy harvesting. It is believed that fundamental study of SSTCYs will provide scientific insights and new knowledge on design, fabrication and evaluation of MFMs with enhanced interfacial bonding and customizable functionalities. Besides triboelectric materials, this study can also be extended to other functional materials (e.g. photovolatic, pyroelectric, piezoelectric, electroactive) to prepare new MFMs with advanced functionalities of sensing, actuating, energy storage and harvesting for a broad range of high-tech applications in wearable technology, smart home and healthcare. 導電材料與功能材料（例如光伏材料，熱電材料，壓電材料或摩擦電材料）在長度方向的集成可以制備一種用於能量收集的一維多功能纖維基材料（MFM）。但是，由於兩者之間的不同物理化學特性（例如彈性模量，泊松比和化學相容性），它們之間的界面容易遭到破壞，這個現象對於摩擦電的MFM尤其明顯。這是因為摩擦電的MFM通常是將導電材料（用作電極，主要是具有高表面能的金屬材料）與有機摩擦電材料（主要是具有低表面能的有機矽和氟化聚合物）層壓在一起。這個問題不可避免地破壞了基於MFM的能量收集器的性能和穩定性。當前，將MFM制備成為功能和結構的完整體仍然具有相當困難和挑戰。文獻調查表明，對於具有可定制功能和牢固界面鍵合的MFM的一般制備方法，目前仍然沒有有效的策略。為了應對這些挑戰，該項目將設計和開发一種新型的MFM，其中連續導電纖維（CCF）完全嵌入到由短纖維和摩擦電材料組成的覆合外層中，即短纖維嵌套摩擦導電覆合紗線（SSTCY），其具有定制的摩擦電性能和增強的界面結合性。在申請人之前所做工作的基礎上，將為SSTCY開发一種結合紡絲和表面塗層方法的特殊嵌套式輔助塗層策略。簡而言之，通過首先通過短纖維的物理纏繞引入包裹在CCF上的短纖外護套，然後將摩擦電材料牢固地引入CCF，作為纖維增強的覆合層，其中有望形成具有增強粘合力的平滑過渡界面區域。通過調整組成材料，紗線結構和包覆條件，可以設計，制備和評估一系列SSTCYs樣品。將進行實驗和建模研究，以分析系統參數與SSTCYs屬性之間的關系。作為應用展示，SSTCYs將被制成一種用於運動能收集的3D雙電極模式能量收集器。據信，對SSTCY的基礎研究將提供具有增強的界面結合和可定制功能的MFM設計，制造和評估的科學機理和新知識。除了摩擦電材料，這項研究還可以擴展到其他功能材料（例如光伏材料，熱電材料，壓電材料，電活性材料），以制備具有傳感，控制，能量存儲和收集等先進功能的新型MFM，從而廣泛應用於可穿戴技術，智能家居和醫療保健等高科技領域。

15209220.value: Peer to Peer環境中的聯邦學習：體系結構，算法和實現

15209220.label: Project Objectives
15209220.value: To develop a tiered architecture and adaptive training algorithms for scalable FL To address the issue of the scalability of the centralized model aggregation of the PS architecture, we propose a tiered architecture, FL-P2P, where peers are organized into clusters, and model aggregation can be offloaded to the peers acting as cluster heads. To construct the clusters of this tiered architecture, we will develop a new algorithm to minimize the communications in model aggregation. To execute the model training in this tiered architecture, we will develop an adaptive algorithm to regulate, in runtime, the interplay of intra-cluster model training and inter-cluster model training. To develop a two-dimensional skip-list structure and algorithms for FL peer management FL model training usually has two swarms of peers, one training swarm and one waiting swarm. For example, in the Gboard application, Google FL selects 500 peers for model training from 500K – 1.5M potential peers. Periodically, low performance peers (stragglers) in the training swarm should be replaced by high performance peers in the waiting swarm. To manage the large number of peers in the waiting swarm, we will develop a novel two-dimensional skip-list structure. This structure has a low management overhead and a high performance in the search operation of the set of peers suitable to be added to model training. To add the peers into appropriate clusters so to minimize the overall model training time, we develop an assignment algorithm based on the weapon target assignment algorithm. To develop algorithms for FL model aggregation with predictable dynamics of peer resources We observe that in certain application scenarios, the dynamics of the peer resources that can contribute to model training are predictable. We thus develop a resource-aware algorithm for model aggregation that can further minimize the model training time. To implement the FL-P2P architecture and algorithms and develop a system to meet the diverse requirements of FL applications We will implement the FL-P2P architecture and algorithms and integrate them as open source modules into existing platforms, i.e., Google TensorFlow Federated. We will evaluate the FL-P2P architecture and algorithms with real world application traces.

15209220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209220.value: 如今，邊緣設備生成了大量可用於學習模型的數據。然而，出於隱私考慮，將數據發送到雲中進行模型訓練應該受到限制。例如，用於觸摸屏移動設備的虛擬鍵盤Google鍵盤（Gboard）必須在客戶端設備上訓練語言模型，以避免將敏感的用戶數據導出到雲中。 Google提出了聯邦學習（FL），一種新的分布式機器學習（ML）範例，以在邊緣設備中進行ML訓練。 聯邦學習的一個重要的特點在於邊緣設備屬於個人。由於邊緣設備（或peers）不一定由FL控制協調者“控制”，而是可以自願“聯邦”，因此可能存在大量peers加入聯邦學習。而且，peers在資源貢獻方面不會像雲中的分布式服務器那樣願意合作。這在ML模型訓練中引入了兩個獨特的挑戰：1）可擴展性：如何大規模管理大量peers節點？和2）peers的動態變化：如何處理peers的動態變化？ 本項目旨在回答如何在對等環境中通過有效利用資源進行聯合學習來最大程度地減少模型訓練時間的問題。模型訓練時間定義為訓練ML模型的收斂時間。資源特別是指計算和通信資源。 在當前的分布式ML體系結構中，如參數服務器（PS）體系結構，盡管分布式服務器要承擔模型訓練的計算工作，但是模型聚合是由集中服務器（參數服務器）處理的。當面對大量peers節點時，集中式模型聚合的通信成為瓶頸，並從根本上限制了系統的可擴展性。而且，PS體系結構沒有機制來處理peers的動態變化。 在本項目中，我們提出了一個分層的模型訓練體系結構FL-P2P，其中peers被組織成集群，以便模型聚合可以由集中服務器卸載給某些peers來承擔。我們提出一系列新算法，包括用於同級管理的新穎的二維跳過列表，以及用於調節，運行時，集群間模型訓練和集群內模型訓練的自適應算法。我們以易於部署的方式實施FL-P2P，以支持具有各種要求的實際應用程序。無論是要解決的問題還是提出的解決方案，我們的項目都是新穎的。我們是第一個在peer to peer環境中研究FL的項目。我們將通過開發教學材料並與行業（例如華為）合作來嘗試FL-P2P架構和算法，從而擴大該項目的影響力。

15209220.label: Realisation of objectives
15209220.value: This project studies the architecture, algorithms and implementation of federated learning, in particular the scalability and dynamics issues in this new collaborative learning paradigm. During the first half of the project, we have (1) carried out a survey on federated optimization and (2) developed algorithms to address the scalability issues by handling the heterogeneity in federated learning and (3) developed algorithms to address the dynamics issues by handling the anomaly aspects in federated learning. In this report period, we further investigated the scalability issues and dynamics issues by a number of studies. We developed system prototypes and evaluated in 251 Amazon EC2 cloud instances. In the education aspect, one Ph.D. student supported by this project has graduated and another Ph.D. student is still on-going. One of the undergraduate students trained by this project, after an MSc study in another university, has decided to join our group to continue his Ph.D. study. To broader the impact of this project, we have conducted tutorials and led special issues. A recent one is a tutorial in IEEE ICC 2023. Summary of deliverables: Knowledge creation: 13 papers 1. 15209220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209220.value: Scalability: Participating peers in the federated learning paradigm can be large. We studied two clustering approaches. First, a clustering approach from a game theoretical viewpoint. Specifically, to address the scalability issue, we propose a Mean-Field-Evolutionary (MFEv) approach that simplifies the interaction between mobile devices as a distribution over their state space, known as the mean-field approximation. Our results were published in IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering. Second, we propose a federated shift invariant dictionary learning clustering approach to enable distributed and computationally efficient user profiling. Our results were published in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. We studied how peers can have incentives and become stable in a large scale federated learning paradigm. We developed our study in a specific HD map application scenario. To motivate social vehicles to contribute data and improve the HD map quality, we formulate an overlapping coalition formation game, OCFUMap, and develop an algorithm to find feasible coalitions. Our results were published in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing. Dynamics: We studied dynamics in computing, where the input video context varies and thus introduce differences in the computing workloads. We studied the sweet spot to split the workloads and our results were published in ACM/IEEE SEC. We studied solution approaches on having different computing resources and our results were published ACM/IEEE SEC. We studied the noisy labels in federated learning and studied a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) approach. DRO can make a decision under uncertainty and dynamics by minimizing the worst-case cost under all possible distributions in the constructed uncertainty set. Our results were published in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing. We studied different types of data since the associated sensor systems have essential pros and cons regarding range, resolution, sensitivity to visibility. We studied such a problem in the application scenario of HD map. In order to quantify the diversity of utilized sensors, we introduced the concept of love of variety. We minimize the HD map updating latency by jointly considering the generation and transmission processes of HD map such that the overall information staleness can be minimized. Our results were published in IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles. System implementation: We developed a system Spread and we developed a Spread prototype on the Amazon EC2 cloud emulating the server and workers using 251 Amazon EC2 instances. Our system was published in IEEE ICPP 2022.

15209220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209220.value: The issues on scalability and dynamics are much broader and richer than what have been studied in this project. They depend on the specifics of applications. There are still many problems to study in the future. A few examples would be how to address various data attackers, how to address energy efficiency issues, to name but a few. With the emergence of video understanding, foundation models, and large language models, collaborative learning in a federated manner will have new meanings.

15209220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209220.value: Nowadays, edge devices generate a wealth of data that can be used for learning models; yet privacy concerns restrict the data to be sent to the cloud for model training. Google has proposed Federated Learning (FL), a new distributed machine learning (ML) paradigm, to enable ML on edge devices. One unique feature of FL is that edge devices belong to individuals. Since edge devices (or peers) are not necessarily “controlled” by the FL coordinator, but can be “federated” instead, there can potentially be a huge number of peers. Moreover, peers will not be as cooperative as the distributed severs in the cloud in their contribution of resources. This introduces two unique challenges in ML model training: 1) scalability: how to manage the large number of peers at scale? and 2) peer dynamics: how to handle the dynamics of peers? In this project, we studied the scalability issue by handling heterogeneity with clustering, game theoretical incentives, etc. We studied a large number of dynamics problems, from communication and computing resources, to sensor types, noisy labels, and anomalies. Our works contribute to the understanding towards an integrated federated learning platform that can mask scalability and dynamics by software.
