15209420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209420.value: Compression textiles/garments can apply pressure onto specific areas of the body for a variety of applications, and have become a cornerstone in treating venous diseases, lymphedema and burn scars. Despite extensive research on compression textiles over the last few decades, controlling and managing applied pressure in an accurate, consistent and controllable way remain challenging with continuous and long-term use because the human body is complex and compression textiles have viscoelastic properties. The absence of real wearable sensing systems for accurate and continuous monitoring of pressure has been an obstacle for treatment purposes. Moreover, the commonly used Laplace’s law for predicting the pressure generated from tensioned fabrics is more suitable for solid objects than a living organism who have a soft-sheath/solid-core and irregular geometry, which has resulted in substantial deviations in the predicted pressure from the actual value. This crucial relationship between the pressure and tension of compression fabric is not fully understood yet and the scientific mechanisms remain unclear. To address the aforementioned problems, this project proposes to systematically perform a theoretical analysis and experimental study on the mechanical and electromechanical properties as well as pressure exerting and sensing mechanisms of pressure fabrics for both applying and monitoring the pressure of compression garments. Inspired by marine mussels, a new yarn strain sensor will be originally developed to achieve not only good weavability but also excellent sensing properties under prolonged tensile and bending stresses with polydopamine as adhesive for effective interface interaction between the elastic core and conductive sheath. Based on the novel designed fabric structures, smart compression fabrics with pressure sensing function will be fabricated by deliberately arranging the yarn sensing elements in a non-binding form within the fabric for good elasticity and sensing properties. Pressure mapping is achieved by placing yarn sensors onto intended positions in the fabric for the first time, which will greatly facilitate pressure monitoring, especially for the gradient pressure exerted. Using such smart fabrics with both pressure exerting and sensing functions, new theoretical understanding will be obtained on the pressure behavior and mechanism of pressure fabrics through experimental and theoretical studies. The project outcomes will address the research gap and contribute to the next generation of compression textiles/garments. The multi-function pressure exerting and sensing fabric can also serve as a universal wearable measurement platform for a scientific understanding of the biomechanics of body-garment interaction, thus facilitating the development of high technology and high-value functional textiles. 壓力紡織品和服裝可以施加壓力於身體特定的區域，已廣泛應用於治療靜脈類疾病、淋巴性水腫和燒傷疤痕。然而，如何使得所施加的壓力準確、保持恒定和可控依然是一項急需解決的問題。為了解決上述問題，該項目將研發壓力施加和傳感織物，並對其壓力性能和機理進行系統的理論和實驗研究。包括研發一種基於多巴胺界面加強的新型紗線傳感器，設計織入紗線傳感元件的特殊織物結構以及由此研制的壓力施加和傳感彈力織物。從長遠來看，該項目將為智能壓力紡織品和服裝的設計和研發提供工程化指引。

15209420.label: Realisation of objectives
15209420.value: Objective 1: The objective 1 has totally been achieved. New yarn piezoresistive strain sensors have been designed based on a co-axial yarn structure, which consists of an elastic core, electrically conductive sheath as well as an outer layer for insulation and packaging of the sensor. In the first trial of sensor development, the polyurethane (PU) yarn and Ag-nanoparticle (AgNP) /graphene nanosheet (GNS) composite were used as the elastic core and conductive sheath, respectively. Based on this, new yarn sensors with enhanced sensitivity, workable strain, durability and lowered initial resistance, particularly the improved processability in weaving, have been developed successfully in the further development of sensors. The carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and AgNPs layers were consecutively deposited on stretchable PU yarn by ultrasonication and polydopamine (PDA) assisted chemical deposition, to achieve a yarn sensor with both high sensitivity and stretchability. In the second trial, by constructing a unique conductive network of dual silver (Ag)/carbon black (CB) layers assisted by PDA and using wet‐spun porous PU fiber as core, a highly stretchable yarn strain sensor was also developed with wider working range as well as ultrahigh sensitivity for detecting very tiny strain of 0.1%. The effects of key factors on the performance of the yarn sensors were investigated, including the linear density of the PU yarn, graphene/carbon nanotubes/carbon black content and plating time of AgNPs as well as PDA concentration; on that basis, the optimized material and fabrication parameters were identified. The yarn strain sensors developed were characterized in terms of their morphological structure, mechanical and electromechanical properties as well as thermal properties, including the surface and cross-section, tensile and bending behaviors and stress relaxation, resistivity, sensitivity, linearity, repeatability as well as durability. Objective 2: The objective 2 has totally been achieved. Various elastic woven, knitted and braided fabric substrates were specially designed for incorporating the sensing yarn into the structure for fabricating the elastic pressure exerting and sensing fabrics for compression textiles, including woven-based single-layer sateen, double-faced sateen and modified Bedford cord structures, knitted-based double-face and single-face jersey as well as triaxial braided structures. Based on these structures, the strain/pressure exerting and sensing fabrics with very good pressure and sensing performance were successful developed through the incorporation of the yarn-based strain sensors developed in Objective 1 into fabric structures using advanced weaving, knitting and braided machines. In addition to the base yarns for the fabric, the developed strain sensing yarn was integrated as a weft yarn, inlay yarn and stuffer yarn into intended positions in the fabric structures, thus retaining a straight configuration for obtaining enhanced linearity and reduced hysteresis of the resultant strain/pressure sensing fabrics. The fabrication trials focused on using this approach of yarn sensor-integration-structure for a better fabric appearance. For the developed braided fabric, the fabric width of fabric produced was limited due to fabric structure and braided machine. Therefore, the fabrication approach was adopted by attaching the strong and narrow braided fabric on the wider elastic fabric substrate, show a more suitable method for fabricating pressure sensing fabrics for the compression textiles. The structure parameters were varied to fabricate sensing fabrics to obtain different electromechanical properties and optimized parameters, including fabric density, linear density of elastic yarn as well as tension applied on the yarn during the fabrication process. Objective 3: The objective 3 has totally been achieved. The experimental investigation on the mechanical and electro-mechanical properties of sensing fabrics was carried out both under unidirectional tension and in a curved form. The performance of sensing fabrics in a planar form were evaluated by using an Instron tester-Keithley’s multimeter combining system. Consequently, the electromechanical properties of the strain sensing fabrics were characterized in terms of gauge factor, linearity, hysteresis, relaxation and durability. The mechanical and electromechanical properties of the strain/pressure sensing fabrics in a curved form were also evaluated by using a newly setup of a test protocol. Consequently, the pressure-displacement and electrical resistance-displacement curves as well as the resultant electrical resistance-pressure were obtained for characterizing the pressure sensing fabric developed. The result is promising, which indicates that the sensing fabrics possess very good sensing performance for pressure exerting and sensing. Particularly, under a fixed amount of extension, the pressure relaxation behavior of the fabric and the electrical resistance changes from applied pressure with time were also evaluated. The effects of yarn linear density, fabric weft density and fabric structure on the mechanical and electromechanical properties of sensing fabrics were investigated for identifying the suitable sensing fabric with desired pressure property for applications of compression textiles. The fabric comfort and washability were also evaluated. Objective 4: The objective 4 has totally been achieved. Based on the response surface methodology (RSM) and by using the Minitab Statistical Software, the effects of the applied fabric extension, curvature of the press head and fabric structure parameters on the pressure performance and electromechanical properties of the sensing fabrics were investigated. Consequently, the statistic model on the relationship between these influential factors and sensing properties of pressure sensing fabric was established. Based on this, the applied fabric extension, yarn count and fabric density were optimized to achieve the desired pressure performance. Besides, geometry models of elastic sateen, double-faced sateen and modified Bedford cord fabrics have been developed. Based on these models, finite element method (FEM) models have been established for the relationship between fabric extension and pressure generated of the sensing fabric through two approached, continuum and discontinue methods, which can be used to predict the pressure behavior of elastic pressure exerting and sensing fabrics. Furthermore, with the above FEM models for the relationship between fabric extension and pressure generated as well as the measured electrical resistance of the sensing fabric, a model for the electrical resistance of the sensing fabric was thus established. A series of numerical simulations were conducted to investigate the effects of the press head diameter, the unit cell crimp factor of fabric and the fabric pretension on the fabric extension and resultant pressure and electrical resistance change. This simulation approach provides a new theoretical understanding on the pressure behavior and mechanism of pressure sensing fabrics for smart compression textiles. Objective 5: The objective 5 has totally been achieved. The comparisons between experimental and simulated fabric pressure as well as resultant electrical resistance subjected to the fabric strains were conducted, showing a good agreement. By using the pressure exerting and sensing fabrics developed, tubular compression bandage protypes have been developed and their pressure behavior were evaluated by using commercial pressure sensors (Kikuhime Subbandage Pressure Measuring Device and FlexiForce Sensor). The measured pressure values using these commercial pressure systems were compared to the testing results in our lab for validation. A data acquisition and processing system was developed to wirelessly transmit the electrical resistance signals of sensing fabrics to computers. Besides, the application of such pressure exerting and sensing fabrics/bandages on for applying and detecting both the pressure and tensile strains on human arm was explored and the sensing performance was also evaluated for fabricating enhanced versions of pressure sensing fabrics/bandages.

15209420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209420.value: The proposed project concerns a systematic investigation of the design, fabrication, pressure mechanisms and properties of fabrics for measuring and monitoring the pressure of compression textiles. New yarn-based sensors are first designed and fabricated based on a tri-coaxial yarn architecture, which can offer good weavability and excellent sensing properties under combined tensile and bending stresses. With the yarn sensor used as the pressure sensing element, smart compression fabrics with pressure sensing function are easily and effectively developed through textile technology. A theoretical analysis and experimental study has been conducted on the pressure behavior and mechanism of pressure fabrics. For the first time, research work on the pressure sensing mechanism of sensing fabrics and determining the effect of yarn sensing elements and fabric structure on the sensing performance can be carried out. Models are finally developed to predict the pressure and electromechanical properties of the compression fabric. The study will provide engineering guidance to the design and fabrication of the next generation of compression textiles. The investigation will promote the new development of textile-based wearable electronics for applications in health care, rehabilitation, and sports and occupational wear and thus increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and electronic industries.

15209520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209520.value: 具有有限空間的部分開放式腔的風扇的低頻噪聲控制仍然很困難。傳統的被動措施，例如多孔吸收材料，通常需要足夠的厚度和較長的衰減路徑，以獲得理想的降噪性能。至為了實現緊湊的配置，已經為開發帶有亞波長尺度吸收劑的超材料，例如帶孔的面板或諧振器不同的內部結構或淺底襯腔中狹窄的空間纏繞通道。這個可以為聲波在背襯腔處提供長的傳播路徑，從而使其聲壓級低頻率吸聲。對於這種帶有穿孔面板的超材料，背襯腔壁 離孔口很近。當穿孔板安裝在局部開放式風扇附近時腔中，空氣流穿過多孔板的孔，並且在孔的邊緣，導致孔中的流與聲學之間的強烈相互作用和淺底襯腔。隨後，孔口的聲學特性將有所不同 從先前所有關於在自由空間或有足夠空間的孔板上的流動影響的發現中得出的結論較大的背襯腔。因此，該項目旨在尋求對流動和聲學的理解放牧條件下多孔板與淺底腔的相互作用表徵其聲學特性，這代表了聲學技術發展的一大進步超材料，帶穿孔面板，控制風扇噪音。為了實現這一目標，將建立一個理論模型建立以便對吸聲機理進行全面分析和理解孔與淺底孔的流-聲相互作用背後的物理和物理學 聲學特性。這有助於設計內部適當尺寸的內部結構。 淺底襯腔可有效控制風扇噪音，尤其是在低頻時。建議 支撐腔內部的內部結構由多層不同的C形環組成 同心取向的尺寸類似於Matryoshka模式，即Matryoshka背襯 腔（MBC），以並行串聯的方式提供多條較長的聲音路徑 傳播。擬議的MBC穿孔板的性能將在 管道和部分開放腔系統，無論是在理論上還是在實驗上。一個成功的 結果將為風扇噪聲控制的超材料設計提供有用的信息

15209520.label: Realisation of objectives
15209520.value: Achievement of Objective 1 The flow and acoustic interactions of an orifice backed by a shallow cavity under grazing flow conditions were investigated using a 3D time-domain Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approach. This study aimed to characterize the acoustic behavior of the orifice influenced by both in-orifice and in-cavity flow dynamics in a compact configuration. To account for the shallow cavity’s effect on reactance, a hybrid Rayleigh end correction model for T-shaped resonators was employed. The simulations solved the compressible Navier–Stokes equations, including the equation of state and conservation laws for mass, momentum, and energy. To model turbulence, the Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) method was used, incorporating the shear stress transport (SST) k–ω turbulence model, which is well-suited for wall-bounded and free shear flows under grazing conditions. Flow patterns and vorticity distributions near the orifice and within the cavity were analyzed at various configurations. Results revealed a vertical shear layer along the hole and cavity, contributing to energy dissipation at the hole. In shallow cavities, vorticity in this shear layer can generate acoustic pulses upon striking the cavity bottom, altering the orifice’s impedance. Moreover, the shallow cavity restricts acoustic wave inflow and outflow, reducing resistance variation caused by shear layer and acoustic wave interactions and significantly modifying the acoustic behavior. Thus, the study successfully achieved the objective 1. Achievement of Objective 2 An acoustic impedance model has been developed to account for the influence of orifice size and the geometry of a compact backing cavity on sound absorption performance under grazing flow. The model expresses impedance as a function of the Strouhal number, the convection velocity of vorticity, and cavity depth (for depths less than 5d). To evaluate the orifice impedance under flow conditions, pressure fluctuations were analyzed at a hypothetical pressure node surface, rather than at the orifice surface itself, as commonly done in previous studies. This approach better captures the flow-induced effects on impedance. A T-shaped cavity was considered for the shallow configuration, as acoustic waves in such geometries propagate laterally from the center to the side branches, rather than vertically. This alters the reactance compared to traditional vertical cavity models. The model’s predictions of transmission loss (TL) for compact micro-perforated panel (MPP) absorbers with single and double cavities were compared with measured results, showing good agreement. This impedance model enhances the prediction accuracy for the acoustic performance of orifices and MPPs with shallow cavity structures, supporting the advancement of acoustic metamaterials in airflow-related applications. The model consists of three components: 1. Baseline impedance without flow, based on Maa’s model [R1]. 2. Viscous boundary layer correction, incorporating two key coefficients to account for flow effects on the end correction. 3. Aeroacoustic interaction terms, represented by non-dimensional resistance and reactance, capturing the dynamic interaction between the unstable shear layer and the incident acoustic wave. The objective 2 was achieved. [R1] Maa D-Y. Theory and design of microperforated panel sound-absorbing constructions. Sci Sin 1975;18:55–71. Achievement of Objective 3 A meta-liner has been developed, consisting of a perforated panel backed by multiple layers of C-shaped enclosures (CSEs), partially embedded with microperforated panels (MPP). This configuration is referred to as a Matryoshka Backing Cavity (MBC). Designed with aerodynamic considerations, this perforated panel with MBC has been studied for its acoustic absorption performance under various structural arrangements. Theoretical and numerical models incorporating acoustic modal decomposition and inter-layer acoustic coupling were developed to evaluate the sound absorption performance of both single-layer and parallel configurations of the proposed absorbers. In addition, the CFD technique was utilized to better understand the fluid dynamics when the flow passes over the proposed compact structure. The flow pattern and vorticity distribution near orifices show that utilizing MPP rather than large holes on the meta-liner surface effectively prevents the fluid from entering the proposed complex structure, which minimizes the flow effects on the acoustic impedance of the internal components of the meta-liner. Thus, the flow effects on the internal component can be neglected. By imposing the impedance model of MPP with flow and shallow cavity effects on the surface MPP, the acoustic performance of the meta-liner can be well-predicted. After that, the acoustic performance of the meta-liner under grazing flow was studied using FEM and validated by experiments. With appropriate structural property, the proposed meta-liner exhibited an average transmission loss (TL) of 10.2 dB in the frequency of 200-1400 Hz without flow. More importantly, the TL of the meta-liner can be accurately predicted and controlled to maintain high levels at flow speeds ranging from 0 to 30 m/s. There is a good agreement between prediction results and experimental data. Therefore, the objective 3 was achieved. Achievement of Objective 4 The acoustic coupling between meta-liner and an open cavity has been investigated using a hybrid method that combines the Finite Element Method (FEM) with the Wiener–Hopf (W-H) technique. The experimental study by measuring sound radiation directivity in an anechoic chamber. Both theoretical and experimental analyses were conducted to evaluate the performance of long enclosures treated with MPP absorbers featuring wavy surfaces under acoustic coupling conditions. The primary advantage of using wavy-shaped MPP absorbers over conventional flat or corrugated MPP designs lies in their ability to suppress sound radiation in the shadow zone across a broad frequency range. This effect is particularly pronounced at non-resonant frequencies, due to the irregular geometry of the wavy-shaped MPP surface and its backing cavity configuration. An experimental study confirmed the accuracy of the hybrid model and demonstrated the effectiveness of wavy-surface MPP absorbers in reducing sound radiation from the portal of a long enclosure. The measured sound pressure levels at the enclosure outlet closely matched the predictions from the hybrid model. With the application of wavy-shaped MPP treatment on the enclosure walls, significant noise reduction was observed, particularly within the 500 Hz to 3000 Hz frequency range, achieving an average insertion loss of approximately 6 dB. The objective of 4 was achieved. Achievement of Objective 5 Fan noise control strategies have been thoroughly investigated. For fan duct noise characterized by complex interactions among flow, sound, and acoustic liners, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were conducted to analyze a scenario where a fan positioned upstream generates grazing flow into the duct. A perforated acoustic liner was installed along one side of the duct to examine the aeroacoustic coupling between the flow, sound field, and liner. The CFD results demonstrated that incorporating microperforated panels (MPPs) on the surface of the meta-liner effectively prevents fluid ingress into the internal structure. This design minimizes the influence of flow on the acoustic impedance of the internal components, allowing the analysis to focus solely on the flow effects at the liner surface. Additionally, the vorticity patterns around each orifice were found to be consistent, indicating that even at a moderately high flow velocity (34 m/s), the orifices are sufficiently spaced to avoid mutual interference. Given the absence of inter-hole coupling, the established impedance model for MPPs under flow conditions can be reliably applied to predict the acoustic performance of the proposed meta-liner under grazing flow. Therefore, the objective 5 was achieved.

15209520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209520.value: The flow and acoustic interactions of an orifice backed by a shallow cavity under grazing flow conditions using a 3D time-domain Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approach was revealed. The acoustic behavior of the orifice influenced by both in-orifice and in-cavity flow dynamics in a compact configuration was understood. The vertical shear layer is present along the hole and cavity and is furthermore responsible for a portion of energy dissipation at the hole. In addition, an acoustic impedance model for an orifice integrated with a shallow cavity under flow effects was proposed. The impedance model is beneficial for predictions for the acoustic performance of an orifice or MPP with shallow cavity structures and further promote the development of metamaterials in airflow applications. [1, 2] A compact acoustic liner featuring perforated panels and layered C-shaped enclosures with microperforated panels (MPPs) was developed for broadband low-frequency noise reduction. Theoretical and numerical models using modal decomposition and inter-layer coupling validated its performance. CFD analysis showed MPPs effectively block fluid intrusion, preserving internal acoustic impedance. The liner achieves an average transmission loss of 10 dB between 200–1400 Hz under grazing flow, making it suitable for fan noise control [3, 4]. A theoretical model was developed to capture acoustic coupling between the long enclosure, absorber (or meta-liner), and the external sound field [1, 2]. Resonator-type absorbers were used to reduce noise from the unbaffled enclosure. The sound peaks and directivity patterns are linked to modal responses at the opening. Properly designed Helmholtz resonators (HRs) significantly suppress dominant modes at peak SPL frequencies, reducing sound field at the top edge and shadow zone of the enclosure [1,6]. The sound absorption performance of a microperforated panel absorber with wavy shaped surface (WMPP) under normal, oblique, and random incidences is investigated numerically and experimentally. The sound absorption performance of the WMPPA and Corrugated MPPA is superior to that of the Flat MPP absorber under oblique plane-wave incidence, especially at large incident angles With the application of wavy-shaped MPP treatment on the enclosure walls, significant noise reduction was observed, particularly within the 500 Hz to 3000 Hz frequency range, achieving an average insertion loss of approximately 6 dB [5, 7]. All the research output are also presented in the conference paper [c1 ,c2, c3].

15209520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209520.value: The proposed impedance model for MPPs incorporating flow effects has been validated through comparisons with published data and experimental results, demonstrating its reliability for developing broadband acoustic liners suitable for flow environments and accurately predicting their performance. This model will be applied to design more efficient, broadband acoustic liners with enhanced absorption characteristics. Beyond grazing flow, bias flow represents another significant flow phenomenon that substantially affects sound absorber performance. We will systematically investigate its impact on shallow cavity meta-structures, aiming to establish a reliable acoustic impedance model incorporating bias flow effects. This research will advance the development of meta-liners for practical airflow applications. Furthermore, the developed C-shaped cavity meta-liner and wavy MPP absorber demonstrate superior performance compared to conventional MPP absorbers, particularly in low-frequency absorption and maintaining stable acoustic performance under various flow conditions. These advantages make them particularly promising for complex aerodynamic noise reduction scenarios in high-speed transportation systems, such as aircraft, high-speed trains, and hyperloop pods. Our ongoing research will further explore their acoustic performance and unique absorption mechanisms under complex flow and noise environments, with particular focus on the underlying physics governing their exceptional performance.

15209520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209520.value: This study explores the acoustic behavior of perforated panels with shallow backing cavities under grazing flow, targeting fan noise control in compact, partially open systems such as hair dryers, computers, and HVAC units. A novel metamaterial design is introduced, featuring concentric C-shaped rings and various microperforated panel (MPP) configurations to enhance low-frequency sound absorption. The proposed compact meta-liner addresses a key challenge in low-frequency noise control where traditional absorbers fail due to space limitations. This research also reveals previously unstudied flow-acoustic interactions in shallow geometries, leading to the development of a new acoustic impedance model for orifices with shallow cavities. This model more accurately captures flow effects in confined spaces compared to existing models. The meta-liner’s flow performance was validated through modeling and experiments, confirming its reliability and practical use. Theoretical modeling and experimental validation confirm that the proposed compact, high-performance meta-liner is highly effective for noise control in both consumer and industrial applications. It offers a scalable solution for integrating metamaterials into existing fan systems without requiring major design changes. Additionally, the newly developed acoustic impedance model accounting for flow effects in shallow cavities provides valuable insights for researchers advancing metamaterial design under aerodynamic conditions.

15209920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209920.value: Road traffic noise has long been a concern for high-density cities like Hong Kong. To address this concern, porous asphalt (PA), an open-graded asphalt mixture with large air void content, has been widely used as a low noise road surfacing material in Hong Kong, which also helps reduce splashing and aquaplaning on rainy days, improve pavement friction, and alleviate urban heat island effect. However, PA road surfaces usually have short service lives due to quick raveling, which refers to the dislodgement of aggregate particles starting from the pavement surface. Recent field trials in Europe have shown that spraying surface-treatment (ST) asphalt emulsions is an effective method to address raveling and extend the service life of PA road surfaces. However, the working mechanism of ST emulsions in PA mixture is still unclear and the scientific evidence of this maintenance method is still missing. To fill this research gap and potentially apply this method in Hong Kong, this study aims to characterize the interaction between ST emulsion and PA mixture using a multiscale approach. At the macroscale, the vertical viscoelastic property gradient of the aged PA samples under different ST conditions (eg: emulsion type, dosage, and curing time and temperature) will be measured to study the short- and long-term ST effects. At the mesoscale, X-ray CT scanning will be performed to monitor the changes in the internal structure of PA samples under different ST conditions. The rheological properties of the aged mortar samples coated with ST emulsions will also be tested to investigate the diffusion of emulsion with time. At the microscale, optical microscopy, nano-indentation, Fourier transfer infrared spectroscopy and gel permeation chromatography will be applied to analyze the micro-crack filling, and binder flexibility, functional group and molecular weight distribution, respectively. Finally, the functional properties, including noise absorption, permeability, and skid resistance, and the mechanical properties, including fatigue, rutting, and raveling resistance of the PA mixtures under selected ST conditions will be tested to ensure the ST can enhance the durability of PA without compromising its functional performance. Based on the revealed working mechanism of ST emulsion, the guidance on applying ST emulsion as a preventive maintenance material for PA road surfaces will be developed. The outcome of this study is expected to significantly improve the durability of PA road surfaces while maintaining their various functional benefits, contributing to the sustainable development of the road network both in Hong Kong and worldwide. 交通噪音一直是困擾像香港這樣的高密度城市的一個環境問題。為解決這一問題，香港廣泛採用了具有開級配的透水瀝青混合料作為一種低噪音路面材料。這種路面材料兼具減少雨天路面濺水與水漂，改善路面抗滑、及緩解城市熱島效應的優點。但是透水瀝青容易產生骨料脫落，因此使用壽命一般較短。對路表噴灑乳化瀝青基材料是一種延緩該病害的潛在方法，但目前該方法的工作機理仍不清楚，且證明該方法有效的科學數據不足。為此，本課題旨在通過多尺度的手段研究表處乳化瀝青與透水瀝青混合料之間的相互作用機理。在宏觀尺度，檢測經過不同乳化瀝青處理的透水瀝青混合料的粘彈性能的縱向分佈；在細觀尺度，通過X光掃面追踪在不同表面處理條件下的透水瀝青的內部結構的變化；此外，測試乳化瀝青表面處理的老化瀝青砂漿的流變性能隨時間的變化。在微觀尺度，通過光學顯微鏡、納米壓痕、紅外光譜及凝膠色譜儀等工具分別分析微裂縫的填充、及瀝青的柔性、化學功能團和分子量分佈。最後，優選最佳表面處理條件，並對該處理條件下的透水瀝青混合料的功能特性（吸音、透水和抗滑）與力學性能（抗疲勞、車轍與鬆散）進行驗證，建立乳化瀝青表處這一透水瀝青路面預防性養護方法的使用指南。該課題的研究成果有望在不影響透水瀝青路面功能特性的前提下，顯著延長其使用壽命，對香港及世界範圍的道路材料的可持續發展做出貢獻。

15209920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209920.value: At the macroscale, both application rate and solid content of surface-treatment (ST) emulsion have significant effects on the ravelling resistance recovery of damaged porous asphalt (PA) mixtures. The optimum application rate of 0.6 kg/m2 and solid content of 60% were recommended. The negative effect of ST emulsion on the functional performance (e.g.: noise reduction, permeability, and skid resistance) of PA was found to be insignificant. Meanwhile, the ST treated PA mixtures achieved superior rutting, fatigue, and cracking resistances. At the mesoscale, the penetration behavior of ST emulsion in damaged PA was investigated by X-ray Computer Tomography (CT). The spatial distribution of ST emulsion in damaged PA presented a gradient characteristic along the depth direction. The ST application reshaped the interconnected pore microstructure, including the size, number, area, interconnectivity, and tortuosity of air voids. The PA specimen treated by the ST emulsion with an application rate of 0.6kg/m2 and a solid content of 60% showed the best coating efficiency and the best ravelling resistance among the three ST conditions. At the microscale, the diffusion phenomena between ST residues and aged asphalt mortars within PA mixtures were observed via the Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) with Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS). TiO2 nano powder was selected as a tracer to tag the ST emulsion. The PA specimen preparation and analysis method for SEM/EDS test were developed. Results showed that the diffusion rate at 60 oC was approximately 5 times faster than that at 25 oC. Thus, it is recommended to spray ST emulsions on old PA pavements in hot weather to accelerate the diffusion efficiency. Due to the nonuniform distribution and slow diffusion efficiency of conventional asphalt emulsion in PA mixture, rejuvenator was added to optimize ST asphalt emulsion. It was suggested to be emulsified first before directly mixing with asphalt emulsion for better compatibility. The optimal dosage of rejuvenator emulsion was determined by balancing the apparent viscosity, wettability, and bonding strength of ST emulsion. The CT images revealed that the rejuvenator-optimized ST emulsion was uniformly distributed in the PA mixture with a higher coating efficiency, which improved the ravelling resistance of PA. The physicochemical analysis implied that the penetrated rejuvenator-optimized ST residues replenished new asphalt and softened aged asphalt binders, decreasing the molecular weight of aged asphalt binder. The rheological results showed the rejuvenator-optimized ST residues improved the stress relaxation property and cracking resistance of aged asphalt binders but might compromise rutting resistance.

15209920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209920.value: Since the application of preventive maintenance material for old PA pavement is a relatively new research topic, further studies are necessary to enhance the ravelling resistance of ST emulsion for PA mixtures. To facilitate the practical implementation of this preventive maintenance technique on aged PA pavements, the following recommendations are proposed: 1. Only one type of ST emulsion was selected in this study to investigate its diffusion characteristic in aged asphalt mortar of PA mixture. Future research should consider various ST emulsions containing different rejuvenators to evaluate their diffusion efficiencies in PA mixtures. 2. The compatibility between different rejuvenators and asphalt emulsions should be further investigated. 3. Field tests should be conducted to assess the actual maintenance effectiveness of ST emulsion on old PA pavements. 4. Life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) should be considered to evaluate the potential economic and environmental effects of using ST emulsions as preventive maintenance materials for old PA pavements.

15209920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209920.value: Porous asphalt (PA) pavement has been widely applied worldwide because of its numerous functional and environmental merits. However, the open-graded structure of PA increases the susceptibility of bitumen to aging, which makes PA more vulnerable to the ravelling distress at the early stage compared to conventional asphalt pavement. Several measures have been applied to alleviate ravelling in road construction period, but the ravelling destress frequently reoccurs after a few years of service. Therefore, an effective preventive maintenance technique is necessary to alleviate ravelling during the road service period. In this study, surface treatment (ST) asphalt emulsion was sprayed to existing PA pavement to mitigate ravelling and extend its service life. The ST treated PA mixtures showed better mechanical performances (e.g.: cracking, rutting and fatigue) and retained most functional properties (e.g.: noise reduction, permeability, and skid resistance). The penetration and diffusion mechanisms of ST emulsion in old PA mixture were comprehensively investigated. Based on its working mechanisms, rejuvenator was proposed to add into ST asphalt emulsion to further improve ravelling resistance of PA by optimizing the penetration status of emulsion in PA and enhancing the diffusion efficiency of emulsion residue in aged asphalt.

15210020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210020.value: 該創新提出的一種創新的FRP（纖維增強聚合物）嵌入基岩中的混凝土樁。這種創新的玻璃鋼管混凝土樁的優點如下：i）玻璃鋼材料的高抗拉強度和復合樁的高整體抗壓強度； ii）FRP耐腐蝕，重量輕且表面光滑； iii）玻璃鋼管利用模板，以保護鑽孔不被土壤塌陷到基岩鑽孔裡； iv）由於省去了鋼管，鋼筋籠和減該項目著重研究創新的FRP管混凝土樁在嵌巖中的變形機理和承載力。將在垂直下方對典型香港土壤的FRP管混凝土嵌巖樁進行大型物理模型測試。在物理模型測試中將考慮上覆壓力，土壤類型，樁類型等的影響。大規模的物理模型將使用基於最新光纖傳感器技術的全壽命監控傳感器進行檢測。該項目的目標是： （a）進行實驗室測試，以了解香港典型土壤（HKMD，沖積層，CDG），玻璃鋼與典型土壤，岩石，混凝土，玻璃鋼管道等的基本特性和行為； （b）優化設置程序，以在PolyU的現有大型物理模型中固結典型土壤，基岩裂縫，下沉FRP管，安裝傳感器以及將混凝土樁注漿到FRP管和預先鑽好的岩石孔裡; （c）進行一系列物理模型測試，其中i）上覆壓力，ii）周圍土壤的類型以及iii）在混凝土樁內部有無鋼筋的情況下，然後對樁進行靜態壓縮到破壞； （d）從以下方面對FRP管混凝土樁的性能進行數據分析：i）樁的應力應變特性； ii）FRP管上的表皮摩擦的發展； iii）FRP管對混凝土的圍壓的發展； iv）岩石孔內部樁的側向摩擦的產生； v）樁端產生的搬運阻力； vi）混凝土內部可能出現的裂縫； （e）以玻璃纖維混凝土管樁在典型土壤中的整體性能作為最終目標，並為香港未來的樁基建設提供新方法； （f）撰寫和發表預期和高影響力的期刊論文。

15210020.label: Realisation of objectives
15210020.value: Objective 1: Detailed laboratory tests for basic properties and behaviours of typical Hong Kong marine soils and FRP pipe concrete pile were carried out and completed. The mechanical behaviours of marine soils included consolidation properties, permeability, volume compressibility, creep/rate effects, friction angle, cohesion, etc. All these indexes and parameters were well calibrated and interpreted using elastic visco-plastic models developed by the research team. The mechanical properties of short columns of FRP tube-confined concrete under different loading conditions are investigated in the laboratory, with calibrated Young’s modulus, possion’s ratio, compressive strength, etc. The pure concrete and FRP sheet were also tested. Objective 2: A large physical model had been built at the beginning of the project. With the model chamber and loading frame, the setup procedures of an FRP-confined model pile in rock socket and soft soils were examined and implemented. This included the pre-consolidation of Hong Kong marine soils in the model chamber, drilling holes in the soils, sinking and fixing the FRP pipe to the rock socket, installation of sensors inside the FRP pipe, grouting and curing concrete through the FRP pipe and into a pre-drilled rock socket at the bottom of the model. After curing for 28 days, the model piles were tested using a hydraulic actuator on the loading frame. Objective 3: A series of physical model tests were conducted on FRP reinforced concrete piles in a rock socket. Different types of pile structures, including the proposed FRP tube-confined concrete, FRP rebar reinforced concrete, FRP stirrup confined concrete, were used for the model tests. Different surrounding conditions (with/without marine soils) were considered. Both static monotonic loadings and cyclic loadings with different cycles and frequencies were applied to the pile head for mechanical tests. Distributed fibre optic system (optical frequency domain reflectometry, OFDR) were implemented in the model tests to monitor the strain profile of the model pile. LVDTs, earth pressure cells, porewater pressure transducers, and multiplexed FBG sensor series were adopted to monitor the piles and soils for comparison and verifications of the OFDR sensing. Objectives 4-5: Test data collected by distributed fibre optic system and other instrumentation techniques were analysed. The pile-load reactions, including displacement accumulation, end bearing pressure, and shaft friction mobilization from soils and rock socket under static monotonic and cyclic loadings were obtained. The test results indicated that the FRP tube–confined model pile showed higher confinement and cyclic capacity and lower stiffness degradation, leading to relatively more stable behavior. A high level of cyclic loading can cause microcracks to form and grow within the pile material, thereby decreasing pile stiffness. Cyclic stiffness showed gains initially when cyclic load conditions were below a certain threshold level but degraded when loading was increased beyond it. The axial strain profiles shows strain concentrations in one third region near the pile head, which led to pile failure at that section. The cracks and failure of the pile were well captured by the sensors. Shaft resistance gradually increased with cycles, causing higher mobilization in the upper portion of the socket, due to the dilation effect of broken-out small particles. The maximum mobilization in the upper one third region of the socket were observed. The analytical solutions of partially embedded piles were adopted to describe the test results, showing good agreement of the test findings. Numerical simulations using Abaqus Finite Element programme were conducted based on the Elastic Visco-Plastic models, which revealed the development of pile skin friction in both marine soils and rock socket. Empirical design formulas were proposed and developed for future rock socketed piles. Objective 6: More than 10 papers closely related to the performance of the proposed piles, the basic mechanical behaviour of soils, and related analytical/numerical solutions were published in high-level international journals and top conferences.

To do data analysis of the performance of FRP pipe concrete pile in terms of (i) stress-strain behaviour of the FRP pile, (ii) development of skin friction on the FRP pipe, (iii) development of confining pressure from FRP pipe to concrete, (iv) development of side friction of pile inside rock socket, (v) development of bearing resistance from the end of socket, and (vi) possible cracks inside the concrete;
To evaluate the overall performance of the FRP pipe concrete pile in typical soils as the final goal and provide a new approach for future pile construction in Hong Kong;
To write and publish high-quality and large-impact journal papers and conference papers.

15210020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210020.value: 1. The test results indicated that the FRP tube–confined model pile showed higher confinement and cyclic capacity and lower stiffness degradation, leading to relatively more stable behavior. A high level of cyclic loading can cause microcracks to form and grow within the pile material, thereby decreasing pile stiffness. Cyclic stiffness showed gains initially when cyclic load conditions were below a certain threshold level but degraded when loading was increased beyond it. The distributed axial strain profiles of all model piles appeared to follow similar trends along the depth with strain concentrations in one third region near the pile head, which led to pile failure at that section. The distributed circumferential strain profiles along the pile length provided reliable information of the localized potential failures around the pile circumference, corresponding well with that from axial strain measurement. 2.Shaft resistance gradually increased with cycles, causing higher mobilization in the upper portion of the socket, due to the dilation effect of broken-out small particles. The magnitude changed less markedly with cycles in the lower section of the rock socket, but increased with an increase in cycle number at the upper portion.The maximum mobilization in the upper one third region of the socket were observed. 3. The analytical solutions of partially embedded piles were adopted to describe the test results, showing good agreement of the test findings. Numerical simulations using Abaqus Finite Element programme were conducted based on the Elastic Visco-Plastic models, which revealed the development of pile skin friction in both marine soils and rock socket. Empirical design formulas were proposed and developed for future rock socketed piles. 4. Distributed fibre optic technology, specifically, optical frequency domain reflectometry, can precisely monitor the complicated deformation behaviour of FRP confined piles, from degradation of stiffness to their cracking and failures.

15210020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210020.value: In the future, cyclic horizontal loading can be considered, by developing a horizontal loading components on the physical model.

15210020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210020.value: This study proposes an innovative pile, by adipting FRP tube as anti-corrosion material, high-strength confinment, and convenient casing, especially for applications in rock-socket piles. To examine the performance of the proposed pile, and to understand its behaviours under external loadings, a large-scale physical model was built in laboratory, with real materials, simulated construction procudures, and advanced monitoring technology using fibre optic sensing. A series of tests were conducted on FRP-confine concrete piles subject to vertical static and cyclic loadings. The characteristics of vertical mechanical behaviours of the pile, including cyclic degradation of pile stiffness, skin friction mobilization, load capacity, and failure modes were investigated through the experiments. Theoretical and numerical studies were performed to deepen the understanding of these mechanical behaviours. The findings from this study can be used to guide and improve the design of FRP-tube rock-socketed piles in Hong Kong and other regions with similar demands.

15210520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210520.value: 火星表面過去被認為是靜態的，但從過去40年從軌道和地表收集的影像中獲得的證據顯示，火星表面某些區域卻是非常動態的。這些動態特徵的包括反復出現的坡地線，“蜘蛛狀”地形，冰塊滑落和滑坡，沙塵暴，新的撞擊坑等。對這些動態變化現象進行研究對火星的動態演化，尋找冰和液態水，以及火星氣象環境和地質特徵等方面的研究具有重要意義。利用過去二十年來積累的來自軌道的米級或亞米級分辨率的影像，可以更好地觀察火星上的動態現象。但是，針對這些在不同時間，不同光照和拍攝條件下獲取的海量的影像數據集，需要更有效，更可靠的方法。本項目將利用在線火星影像數據庫（例如NASA的行星數據系統），開發創新的方法實現更自動化，更可靠地檢測和識別火星上的動態變化現象，研究其科學意義。 項目的主要目標如下： （1）開發一種創新的光照不變匹配方法，並結合一種新穎的大氣感知光度立體策略，實現多時相火星軌道圖像的逐像素匹配； （2）開發新穎的深度學習方法，從匹配的多時相影像中檢測和進一步識別火星上的動態變化現象； （3）開發自動的工作流程，以從在線影像數據庫中進行數據檢索和處理，對火星上的動態變化現象進行系統的調查。 本項目的研究將緩解從海量影像數據中人工識別火星上的動態變化現象所需的大量人力資源，同時還將最大化所有可利用的影像。研究成果將開啟一個火星動態現象科學研究的新窗口。該項目的研究和創新還將促進行星影像處理與行星大數據分析的進步，促進深度學習方法在行星科學研究中的應用。所開發的方法和結果可直接用於2020年啟動的中國首個火星探測任務。項目所開發的方法和技術還具有極好的技術轉移潛力服務於香港的相關工業應用。

15210520.label: Realisation of objectives
15210520.value: (1) For the first objective, we developed an innovative illumination-invariant approach for pixel-wise matching of multi-temporal orbital images, in which a photoclinometry-assisted image matching strategy was developed by integrating photometric stereo analysis into the image matching process to create pixel-wise matches, even for images with large illumination differences (Liu & Wu, 2020, ISPRS J). The developed approach was validated using lunar orbital images acquired under different illumination conditions, and results showed that the proposed approach was robust to severe inconsistencies in illumination and subtle textures in cases where conventional approaches failed. We further extended the approach for pixel-wise matching of Mars orbital images by considering atmospheric influences on Mars. A top-of-the-atmosphere (TOA) photometric model, incorporating the parameters of optical depth and aerosol scattering properties to describe the unique photometric behaviour of the Martian atmosphere, is used to account for the disturbance of surface reflectance due to the atmosphere of Mars (Liu & Wu, 2023, ISPRS J). The atmospheric optical depth can be retrieved using our single-image-based approach of analyzing non-shadowed surfaces (Liu, Wu, et al., 2022, Icarus). The well-established semi-global matching (SGM) method is adopted for the dense matching of multiple Mars orbital images, and a photometric stereo strategy incorporating the atmospheric optical depth was developed to further refine the matching and generate pixel-wise matches. Experimental validations were conducted using Mars orbital images collected by the High Resolution Stereo Camera (HRSC) onboard Mars Express. The results showed that favorable matching results were obtained even for HRSC images with serious atmospheric haze, from which 3D topographic models could be derived, offering subtle topographic details conforming to the original images (Li, Wu, et al., 2022a, IEEE TGRS). The developed approach was also used to process the orbital images collected by the High-Resolution Imaging Camera (HiRIC) onboard China’s Tianwen-1 Mars probe covering its landing site, and the dense and reliable matching results allow the generation of 3D topographic models with subtle topographic details (Li, Wu, et al., 2022b, IEEE TGRS). (2) For the second objective, we developed novel deep-learning approaches for the detection of various types of surface features in Mars images, and for the identification of dynamic surface phenomena on Mars. These include, for instance: (i) A deep-learning approach for rock detection on Mars images: A state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) model for feature detection, namely YOLOv4, was used to detect rocks in high-resolution Mars images. A transfer learning process was developed to fine-tune the YOLOv4 model for better performance by using thousands of rock labels manually identified in the high-resolution images. The fine-tuned YOLOv4 model was used for automatic rock detection at the Tianwen-1 landing region and other regions on Mars, and the results revealed a rock detection rate of approximately 80% (Chen, Wu, et al., 2022, ESS); (ii) An active deep-learning approach for volcanic cone detection on Mars images: The method is based on the YOLOv4 network, with detection performance enhanced by leveraging manual annotation to dynamically add new labels to the training dataset. Unlike fully supervised learning, active learning is semi-supervised, involving specific criteria that prompt human annotators to judge the correctness of network predictions. The manually annotated labels are thus more representative and reliable, enabling enhanced algorithm performance. The developed approach was used to create a global database of volcanic cones on Mars based on a global mosaic of Mars Context Camera (CTX) images, which contains 250,547 pitted cones along with their central coordinates and diameters, facilitating research on the origin and evolution of volcanic cones on Mars (Chen, Wu, et al., 2024, Scientific Data); (iii) A depth-enhanced transformer network for semantic segmentation and recognition of surface features on Mars: The method is based on advanced deep-learning techniques, particularly Transformers, for enhanced semantic segmentation and image interpretation. Unlike regular deep-learning networks that only deal with three bands (red, green, and blue) of images, this approach incorporates the depth information available from stereo images as a fourth band in the network to enable more accurate semantic segmentation and recognition of various surface features. Experimental evaluations and comparisons using actual Mars image datasets reveal that various types of surface features (e.g., soil, sand, rock, crater shadow, sky, rover, and rover wheel tracks) can be successfully segmented and recognized from the images by this approach, achieving an average accuracy of 98%. We systematically studied a representative dynamic surface phenomenon on Mars, i.e., the recurring slope lineae (RSL), in particular. RSL are features presently developing on Mars and have been suggested to result from transient flows of liquid water or dry particles. We conducted a time-series analysis of RSL in Palikir and Raga craters on Mars, using multi-temporal high-resolution images (0.25 m/pixel) collected by the High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) during Mars years (MY) 32 to 36. A deep-learning model based on the backbone of the Siamese network, incorporating a spatial attention module and a balanced evaluation method, was developed for detecting dynamic changes in RSL from the time-series images (Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, ISPRS Archives). Results unveil a significant increase in RSL after the global dust event in MY 34 compared to other years and its dependence on surface temperatures on sun-facing slopes. Further investigation into the relationship between RSL and bedrock outcrops suggests a plausible scenario for RSL formation based on the melting of bedrock aquifers. This outcome is further supported by spectral evidence of the presence of hydrated salts in RSL during the summer and their absence in autumn. Our results provide a possible scenario for RSL formation and support the hypothesis that RSL may be related to contemporary water activity on Mars (Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, Scientific Reports). (3) For the third objective, we developed an automatic workflow powered by a web crawler for data retrieval and processing from online image archives, enabling systematic investigation of dynamic surface phenomena on Mars. The automatic workflow involves several key steps designed to efficiently and systematically collect data from online image archives. First, based on the target area and the required dataset, target product names are generated according to the location and naming conventions for each product. Next, the web crawler generates a list of specific URLs, which serve as the input for the crawler frontier. To address potential issues during the downloading process, a retry mechanism is implemented to ensure that the program can run uninterrupted. Finally, the downloaded data are preprocessed and securely stored in the data repository. The developed method demonstrates the ability to automatically retrieve and process data from online image archives with a 100% success rate, given a relatively stable network connection and retry mechanism (Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, submitted to Space: Science & Technology). The developed automatic workflow for data retrieval and processing from online image archives has been extensively used to retrieve various types of high-quality Mars imagery for the detection of surface features and dynamics in scientific studies. Examples include using CTX imagery to study volcanic cones on Mars (Chen, Wu, et al., 2024, Scientific Data), using HiRISE and HiRIC images to study transverse aeolian ridges on Mars (Lu et al., 2022, EPSL), and using HiRISE imagery to study the time-series dynamic changes of RSL on Mars (Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, Scientific Reports).

15210520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210520.value: (1) An innovative photoclinometry-assisted image matching method was developed for illumination-invariant, pixel-wise matching of multi-temporal orbital images. This approach was further enhanced with a novel atmosphere-aware photometric stereo strategy for Mars orbital images. These methods have been widely used for reliable and dense matching of various Mars orbital images (Liu & Wu, 2023, ISPRS J; Li, Wu, et al., 2022a, IEEE TGRS; Li, Wu, et al., 2022b, IEEE TGRS). (2) The project systematically investigated a representative dynamic surface phenomenon on Mars: recurring slope lineae (RSL). Time-series analysis of RSL in Palikir and Raga craters using multi-temporal HiRISE images from Mars Years (MY) 32 to 36 revealed a significant increase in RSL after the global dust event in MY 34, and a dependence on surface temperatures of sun-facing slopes. Further analysis suggests RSL formation may be linked to melting bedrock aquifers, supported by spectral evidence of hydrated salts in summer but not autumn. These findings support the hypothesis that RSL are related to contemporary water activity on Mars (Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, ISPRS Archives; Scientific Reports). (3) An automatic workflow powered by a web crawler was developed for retrieving and processing data from online image archives, enabling systematic investigation of dynamic surface phenomena on Mars. This workflow has been extensively used to obtain high-quality Mars imagery from online image archives for various scientific studies (Lu et al., 2022, EPSL; Chen, Wu, et al., 2024, Scientific Data; Liu, Wu, et al., 2025, Scientific Reports). (4) Invited by the China Academy of Space Technology, we contributed to landing site mapping and selection for China’s first Mars mission, Tianwen-1. The deep-learning methods for automatic detection and recognition of surface features (craters, rocks, cones) developed in this project were crucial for evaluating and selecting candidate landing regions, ultimately helping to identify the final landing site and contributing to the mission’s successful landing (Wu et al., 2021, ESS; Wu et al., 2022, JGR-Planets; Chen, Wu, et al., 2022, ESS).

15210520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210520.value: The research outputs from this project will facilitate the identification and study of dynamic surface phenomena on Mars using the vast online image archives. The innovative image matching and deep-learning-based feature detection methods developed in this project have broad potential applications. For example, the atmosphere-aware photometric stereo method is essential for high-quality 3D mapping of the Martian surface. Our methods are currently being used to support mapping and analysis of candidate landing sites for the Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission, scheduled for launch around 2029. The deep-learning approaches from this project also have excellent potential for broader intelligent image analysis. For instance, we have applied these methods to study historical aerial images of Hong Kong, acquired 100 years ago, in collaboration with the Survey and Mapping Office of the Lands Department of HKSAR. Further development of this research will advance planetary image processing, planetary big data analytics, and the application of deep learning in various fields.

15210520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210520.value: The Martian surface is dynamic in certain regions, such as the recurring slope lineae (RSL) observed in orbital images. Studying these phenomena is crucial for understanding Mars’ evolution and searching for water. Over the past two decades, high-resolution orbital images have improved our ability to observe such dynamic phenomena, but more efficient analysis methods are needed. This project developed innovative approaches for the detection and recognition of dynamic surface features on Mars using online image archives. Key advancements include: (1) a novel method for pixel-wise matching of multi-temporal images, (2) new deep-learning methods for the detection and recognition of surface features and dynamics, and (3) an automated workflow for retrieving and processing data from online image archives. Systematic analysis of RSL changes on Mars using multi-temporal images over five Martian years revealed a significant increase in RSL after a global dust event, supporting the hypothesis that RSL may form from melting bedrock aquifers. These developments have supported China’s Tianwen-1 Mars mission by enabling detailed mapping and analysis of surface features to identify suitable landing sites. The project’s outcomes will enhance the identification and study of dynamic Martian surface phenomena using the vast online image archives.

15210620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210620.value: Advances in autonomous vehicle technology and the rise of the sharing economy will reshape future mobility. A recent new wave of collaboration between automakers, and billions of dollars of investment for autonomous vehicle innovation, clearly indicate concerted efforts to embrace autonomous and shared mobility in the future. Although the path ahead is unclear, one thing is certain: automakers and suppliers will need to ready their operations for imminent profound and revolutionary changes. Particularly, how to manage a fleet of shared autonomous vehicles effectively will be one of the most pressing challenges faced by shared-and-autonomous-mobility (SAM) service providers. We therefore propose to develop both a static and a dynamic algorithmic framework to support the offline (for reservation-based SAM services) and real-time (for ad hoc SAM services and hybrid schemes) decision making of service providers regarding ride matching and vehicle dispatching, in pursuit of cost minimization while ensuring a required level of service. Within each framework, optimization models and customized efficient algorithms will be developed to make sure that autonomous vehicles are properly dispatched to the right place at the right time, riders are satisfactorily paired, and new request is responded to in a timely manner. Numerical experiments in simulated semi-realistic SAM systems based on the mobility data from the DiDi platform will be conducted to evaluate the proposed decision-making tools, and to explore the impact of the system configuration, demand patterns, and riders’ time flexibility and preferences in matching on the service quality, profitability, and vehicle utilization of SAM services. The obtained managerial insights and operation strategies will be provided to relevant stakeholders. The advancements made in the project are expected to have profound implications for the operation and management of shared autonomous vehicle fleets, in reducing the operational costs and improving the service quality. 自動駕駛汽車技術的發展和共享經濟的興起將重塑未來的交通出行方式。最近幾年汽車製造商之間新一波的合作以及對自動駕駛汽車技術數十億美元的投資，清楚地表明了工業界為實現自動駕駛和共享出行而做出的共同努力。儘管前進的道路尚不清楚，但有一點可以肯定：汽車製造商和供應商將需要為即將發生的深刻而革命性的變化做好準備。特別地，如何有效地管理基於共享運營模式的自動駕駛車隊將是共享自動駕駛乘車服務提供商所面臨的最緊迫的挑戰之一。在此背景下，本項目擬为共享自动驾驶乘车服务提供商开发一套静态和動態決策工具，从而为乘客匹配和车辆调度的离线（针对基于预订的共享自动驾驶乘车服务）和实时（针对即时的共享自动驾驶乘车服务和混合方案）决策提供技术支持。为了确保自动驾驶汽车在正确的时间指派到合适的位置，并根据乘客需求进行配对以响应新的请求，本项目将建立优化模型并针对问题的特点开发相应的高效算法，从而在确保服务质量的同时，将运营成本降到最低。本项目也将基于滴滴平台的交通出行数据模拟共享自动驾驶乘车系统并进行数值实验，對開發的模型和算法進行評估， 並探索系统配置、需求模式以及乘客出行时间的灵活性和偏好对共享自动驾驶乘车服务系统的影响，從而為共享自动驾驶乘车服务提供商的管理和運營提供指導意見。本項目的開展对未来交通出行服务的运营和管理具有深遠的影响，其實現將有力地提高运营商的服务质量并减小其运营成本。

15210620.label: Realisation of objectives
15210620.value: The project objectives to develop models and algorithms for decision-making in shared autonomous mobility (SAM) services, specifically for ride matching and vehicle dispatching in reservation-based and ad hoc systems, have been fully achieved through this study. The team introduces a novel approach to optimizing fleet size, ride-matching patterns, and vehicle routes, focusing on maximizing service operator profits while considering customer satisfaction. By incorporating a nonlinear multivariate customer satisfaction function, we address the complexities of the most commonly seen 'two riders-single vehicle' ride-pooling scenario. The development of a set packing model and a tailored branch-and-cut-and-price approach demonstrates a significant advancement in solving these complex problems. The innovative two-phase method effectively decomposes ride matching and vehicle routing, enhancing the decision-making process for SAM service providers. Phase 1 identifies feasible matching patterns, while Phase 2 employs heuristic and exact methods to solve a new variant of the elementary shortest path problem with time windows. The team further addresses the complexities of real-time ride matching and vehicle dispatching in SAM services by developing an online efficient algorithm aimed at maximizing operator profit while maintaining service quality. We model the dynamic system as a Markov decision process, with each subproblem formulated by a mixed-integer programming model that incorporates constraints on ride-pooling and passenger satisfaction. This approach allows for continual optimization of vehicle dispatching solutions at each decision point, effectively adapting to the dynamic nature of SAM services. The development of a customized hybrid algorithm, which integrates adaptive request assignment into a large neighborhood search heuristic framework, demonstrates a significant advancement in solving these dynamic problems. By decomposing multi-vehicle problems into single-vehicle problems and iteratively optimizing routing solutions, the algorithm efficiently adapts to changing conditions. The performance of the proposed models and algorithms is thoroughly evaluated through numerical experiments using real mobility data, which highlight their effectiveness compared to benchmark approaches. The study also explores the impact of passenger flexibility on system performance, providing valuable managerial insights into the operation and management of SAM services. These achievements indicate a comprehensive fulfillment of the three project objectives.

15210620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210620.value: The project has made significant contribution in optimizing shared mobility services, focusing on critical aspects including fleet size, vehicle routing, ride matching, and vehicle dispatching. We have developed optimization models and efficient algorithms to address the complex decision-making processes faced by shared mobility service providers. These models are designed to enhance operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, we have expanded these models and algorithms to tackle a variant of the vehicle routing problem, which is similar to the vehicle routing problem of shared mobility services. In particular, we have incorporated grouping constraints and simultaneous pickup and delivery. This extension allows for more practical solutions in logistics and transportation problems. In response to feedback from expert panels, we have also explored the realm of vehicle automation, specifically examining vehicle platooning and its implications for space policy, intersection control, and signal setting in the context of autonomous vehicles. We also delve into the development of connected and automated vehicle platoons. These investigations aim to optimize traffic flow at intersections and in transportation networks, proposing innovative solutions such as cooperative signal-free control and optimal intersection design. These advancements are crucial as they pave the way for more efficient urban mobility systems in the era of autonomous vehicles. Moreover, travel safety remains an important concern in autonomous-vehicle-based urban mobility. Our research has investigated the heterogeneity of crash patterns involving autonomous vehicles. By employing latent class analysis coupled with a multinomial logit model, we have identified key factors influencing the severity of damages in autonomous vehicle crashes. This analysis provides valuable insights and guidance for enhancing the safety protocols and design considerations of autonomous vehicles for mobility services.

15210620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210620.value: Building on our current research, there is good potential for further development in several key areas. First, expanding our optimization models to incorporate real-time data analytics and machine learning could enhance decision-making processes for shared mobility services. This would allow for more efficient fleet management and routing strategies based on real-time traffic conditions and user demand patterns. Additionally, further exploration into the integration of autonomous vehicles with other vehicles and existing urban infrastructure is crucial. This includes developing advanced algorithms for autonomous vehicle trajectory planning and control, considering the intricate interaction between autonomous and human-driven vehicles, optimizing mixed traffic flow, and enhancing safety measures. We also propose to investigate the socio-economic impacts of widespread autonomous vehicle adoption, focusing on accessibility, equity, and environmental sustainability. This could involve collaborations with urban planners and policymakers to ensure that technological advancements align with broader societal goals. To achieve these objectives, we plan to establish interdisciplinary partnerships with experts in data science, urban planning, and public policy. Securing funding for pilot projects and field trials will be essential to validate our models and algorithms in real-world settings.

By developing advanced optimization models and algorithms, the project enhances both operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. The extension of these models to address complex transportation and logistics problems, including the vehicle routing problem with grouping constraints and simultaneous pickup and delivery, demonstrates the project’s practical applicability in transportation and logistics. Furthermore, the research explores the integration of vehicle automation, focusing on vehicle platooning and its impact on traffic flow and intersection control. Innovative solutions like cooperative signal-free control, which are crucial for efficient urban mobility in the era of autonomous vehicles, have been proposed. Additionally, the project addresses travel safety by analyzing crash patterns involving autonomous vehicles, providing insights for improving travel safety. Overall, this research outcomes are valuable for its contributions to optimizing shared mobility services and advancing autonomous vehicle integration, ultimately paving the way for safer and more efficient urban transportation systems.

15210720.label: Project Objectives
15210720.value: TO DEVELOP A METHOD FOR DIRECT MONITORING OF PHYSICAL AND MENTAL STRESS BASED ON AN INTEGRATED WEARABLE SENSOR FOR MEASURING CHEMICAL BIOMARKERS Existing methods for measuring physical and mental stress are either based on subjective judgements (e.g. questionnaire surveys) or unable to provide continuous and simultaneous measurement of both types of stress (e.g. EEG sensors). In this research objective, an integrated wearable sensor array (IWSA) will be developed to directly measure lactate level and cortisol level from wrist sweat (or forehead sweat) of workers. Lactate level and cortisol level are biomarkers of physical stress and mental stress, respectively. If successful, the developed IWSA will become a non-invasive tool for continuous and simultaneous monitoring of physical and mental stress. Specifically, the IWSA is to be composed of an organic electrochemical transistor (OET), which can transduce biological ion-based signals into electrical signals with high gain and relatively low voltages. In order to sense the lactate level, lactate oxidase will be used to catalyze lactate and oxygen to produce pyruvate and hydrogen peroxide, which will generate an electrical signal, and the current change amplitude can reflect the concentration lactate in sweat. While to measure the cortisol level in the sweat, the lactate oxidase in the OET sensor will be replaced with cortisol antibodies (Gao et al. 2016) or a molecular imprinted membrane which can recognize the cortisol molecules. Similarly, the cortisol concentration will be reflected by the change of current. Data processing units, wireless data transmission units, as well as power supply units will be integrated with the sensors, so the stress related data can be delivered wirelessly. TO DEVELOP TWO METHODS FOR INDIRECT MONITORING OF PHYSICAL AND MENTAL STRESS USING PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL MEASURES. In this objective, we plan to use two distinct equipment for psychophysiological measures for physical and mental stress monitoring. The first one is an instrumented vest, Equivital EQ02 LifeMonitor (Figure 3). The second equipment is a photoplethysmography (PPG) based wristwatch with skin conductance sensors (E4, Emaptica, Figure 4). Two sets of methods for indirectly measuring physical and mental stress will be developed based on correlating psychophysiological measures with corresponding ground truth values. The reasons for developing two indirect methods are: 1) in case the direct method is not successful, we will still have two indirect methods of measurement; and 2) the two indirect methods can cross-validate the accuracy and users acceptance of all methods. To evaluate the accuracy and reliability of the three methods (1 direct method, 2 indirect methods) for simultaneous physical and mental stress assessment, lab experiments and field tests will be conducted. TO COMPARE AND VALIDATE DIRECT AND INDIRECT METHODS FOR MONITORING PHYSICAL AND MENTAL STRESS USING GROUND TRUTHS AND USERS ACCEPTANCE LEVELS. In this objective, accuracies and users acceptance levels of the direct method and two indirect methods will be cross-validated and compared. Specifically, the measurement accuracy of the methods developed in Task 1 and Task 2 will be compared against blood lactate measurements and values of saliva-based cortisol monitoring as ground truths for physical stress and mental stress, respectively. Further, the R programming software; which is a free software environment for statistical analysis supported by the R Foundation for Statistical Computing; will be used to compare direct and indirect stress assessment methods using accuracy and kappa statistics. In addition, for assessing the user acceptance in wearing these devices, a visual analogue scale for user acceptability will be developed and validated to subjectively evaluate the comfort level and user acceptance (Figure 8). Based on the comparison results, the best tool will be chosen to be used to simultaneously monitor mental and physical stress as the developed stress assessment model. TO EXAMINE THE CAUSAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PHYSICAL AND MENTAL STRESS FOR BETTER UNDERSTANDING AND MANAGING STRESS AMONG CONSTRUCTION WORKERS. In this objective, we will use the identified method to conduct additional experimental studies to examine the causal relationship between physical and mental stress. Specifically, additional laboratory experiments will be conducted with: (1) participants subjected only to mental stress and (2) participants subjected only to physical stress. Data collected during these additional laboratory experiments along with data collected in previous laboratory experiment (Tasks 2 and 3) will be used to evaluate the causal relationship between mental and physical stress making use of the cross-lagged effects model (Cho et al., 2019). Best-fitting model(s) will be obtained using structural equation modelling. Overall, this project will help to develop and validate a feasible non-invasive tool for the combined physical and mental stress monitoring of construction workers. A better understanding of the link between mental and physical stress will provide construction managers with deeper knowledge, enabling better decision-making to reduce physical and mental stress and prevent systemic stress-related illnesses arising.

15210720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210720.value: Construction is considered one of the most hazardous industries around the globe and consequently workers’ health and safety records cast an overly gloomy picture. A major risk factor is the physically and mentally demanding nature of construction tasks. Short and long-term exposure to physical and mental stress could lead to many undesirable consequences such as musculoskeletal disorders, increase in errors and mistakes, elevated chances of accidents, cardiovascular disorders, strokes, and depression. With rapidly ageing construction workforces common in many developed countries, and aged workers are more susceptible to these ill-effects, the need to better comprehend, monitor and manage these stress is unprecedented. While there have been studies on the individual impacts of mental and physical stress, studies of causal relationship between physical and mental stress have been scarce. Given that both types of stress are widely prevalent on construction sites, exploring their causal relationship is essential for better comprehending the needs and ensuring the well-being of workers. Moreover, although there have been attempts to separately measure and quantify mental and physical stress, there is a need for an effective tool to simultaneously monitor mental and physical stress. Importantly, given that construction workers are usually exposed to both mental and physical stress concurrently, and that to counter their detrimental effects is imperative, the monitoring of both mental and physical stress simultaneously will improve our understanding of “stress”. Accordingly, the purpose of this project is four-fold. First, it aims to develop an integrated wearable sensor array (IWSA) to directly measure physical and mental stress by monitoring chemical biomarkers from wrist sweat (or forehead sweat) of workers. Second, it will develop two indirect methods for simultaneous and continuous physical and mental stress monitoring using an instrumented vest and a smart watch, respectively. Third, the direct method and two indirect methods will be compared and validated again ground truths and users' acceptances. The results will enable us to identify the most suitable tool for continuous physical and mental stress monitoring. Fourth, the causal relationship between mental and physical stress will be examined using the cross-lagged effects model. In summary, this project will develop and validate a non-invasive tool for the combined physical and mental stress monitoring. It will assist in gaining a better understanding of the causal relationship between mental and physical stress, which will equip construction managers with deeper knowledge and better decision-making abilities in reducing stress and preventing systemic illnesses resulting from stress. 建築業被認為是全球最危險的產業之一，因此工人的健康和安全記錄給人的印象太陰沉了。一個主要的危險因素是施工任務對身體和精神的要求。短期和長期接觸身體和精神壓力可能導致許多不良後果，例如肌肉骨骼疾病，錯誤和失誤增加，發生事故的機會增加，心血管疾病，中風和抑鬱。隨著許多發達國家普遍出現快速老化的建築工人，而老年工人更容易受到這些不良影響的影響，因此，更好地理解，監測和管理這些壓力的需求是前所未有的。 儘管已經對精神和身體壓力的個體影響進行了研究，但對身體和精神壓力之間因果關係的研究卻很少。考慮到兩種壓力在建築工地上普遍存在，因此探索它們之間的因果關係對於更好地理解需求和確保工人的健康至關重要。而且，儘管已經嘗試分別測量和量化精神和身體壓力，但是仍需要一種有效的工具來同時監測精神和身體壓力。重要的是，鑑於建築工人通常同時承受精神和身體壓力，並且必須應對其不利影響，因此同時監測精神和身體壓力將增進我們對“壓力”的理解。因此，該項目的目的有四個方面。首先，它的目的是開發一種集成的可穿戴傳感器陣列（IWSA），以通過監測工人手腕上汗液中的化學生物標記物來直接測量身體和精神壓力。其次，它將開發兩種間接方法，分別使用儀器背心和智能手錶同時和連續監測身體和精神壓力。第三，將對直接方法和兩種間接方法進行比較並再次驗證真實性和用戶接受度。結果將使我們能夠確定最合適的工具，以進行持續的身心壓力監測。第四，將使用交叉滯後效應模型探討精神壓力與身體壓力之間的因果關係。 總而言之，該項目將幫助開發和驗證一種非侵入性工具，用於身體和精神壓力的綜合監測。它將有助於更好地理解精神壓力和身體壓力之間的因果關係，這將使建築經理在減少壓力和預防其他系統性疾病方面具有更深的知識和更好的決策能力。

The device has been tested among various samples including construction operators at different ages.

15210720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210720.value: Owing to the nature of construction work, equipment operators have to attentively perform their tasks while sitting in equipment-cabins for prolonged periods. Mental fatigue caused by the sustained attention required and passive physical fatigue arising from prolonged sitting are identified as principal risk factors. This study has first developed and validated the feasibility of wrist-sweat based sensors in detecting the fatigue level of construction equipment operators. Secondly, it evaluated the effectiveness of stretching exercises in mitigating fatigue. Taken together, the results of this project provided a comprehensive solution to monitoring and mitigating fatigue of equipment operators (or any workers) exposed to prolonged sitting in seemly intractable environments.
