15210920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210920.value: 本課題主要目的是研發一種寬風速範圍雙轉子對轉風力發電系統。通過先進的繞組切換策略，直流抗飽和技術，該設計有望在有限空間內提升風力發電轉換能力。根據2019年發布的報告，預計到2050年世界人口將達到97億，到2100年左右將達到110億。如何減少化石能源的消耗以及提高住宅和商業建築中的可再生能源轉換效率引起了研究人員的極大興趣。在城市或建築環境中安裝的風力發電機系統，要求風機在較小的空間或有限的橫截面積內充分利用寬速範圍的風能。由於常規的單轉子風力發電機在城市環境中的風能提取能力通常是不理想的，因此使用對轉雙轉子風力發電系統可以將其風能轉換效率提高20％-40％。然而，大多數對轉的風力發電機仍然具有機械行星齒輪箱，電刷/滑環和大容量交流功率轉換器，這增加了系統維護成本並降低了系統的可靠性。如何有效簡化風電轉換系統，提高風能轉換效率成為一個具有挑戰性的課題。 該課題應用繞組切換技術，緩解直流飽和的電機設計理念，開發一種對轉的風力發電。該機器設計在城市風力發電系統中具有巨大的潛力，因為（1）電樞/勵磁繞組可以分開或者組合在一起，以在超寬速度範圍內保持輸出電壓恆定和效率最大化。通過電樞/勵磁繞組切換策略，有效地擴展了風速範圍。在相對較低的風速下，電樞繞組和勵磁繞組串聯連接以提高電壓產生；在相對較高的風速下，為勵磁繞組提供直流電流以調節氣隙磁通，同時通過特殊的方法避免直流飽。 （2）定子槽PM可以減輕直流勵磁引起的直流飽和。通過消除直流飽和的PM設計，可以提高直流勵磁產生的磁阻轉矩。通過定子直流勵磁磁阻電機的直流磁場調節，可以靈活地調節輸出電壓，這使得整個發電系統更簡單，更可靠。設計。 （3）並聯混合勵磁的設計。在課題中，定子直流勵磁磁阻電機中靈活的磁通控制，再加上調磁電機高轉矩密度優點，使新的對轉無刷電機特別適用於超速範圍無刷風力發電發電應用。

15210920.label: Realisation of objectives
15210920.value: The purpose of this proposal is to develop the next generation relieving-DC-saturation contra-rotating wind power generation system with enhanced wind energy harvesting capability over a wide wind speed range in the urban or built environment. Firstly, contra-rotating wind power generator design with extended wind-speed range is the key objective to be achieved in this project. A novel hybrid excitation consequent-pole contra-rotating machine (CRM) with zero-sequence current excitation is successfully investigated for wind power generation, which shows good field regulation capability under an extended wind-speed range. The proposed model has the following merits. 1)The zero-sequence armature winding integrates the dc and ac winding, eliminating the conventional circumferential auxiliary winding and making the structure more compact. 2)The integrated winding enables the ratio of ac and dc current to be freely adjusted, making the slot area further utilized. 3)The flux can be regulated effectively with a wide range by changing the zero-sequence current excitation. A 3-phase 12-coil model with a seven-pole-pair rotor and a five-pole-pair rotor has been designed. The rotor pole pair selection method and the flux controlling method have been illustrated. The winding configuration and the drive circuit have been designed. Three working modes of the proposed machine have been analyzed by the 3-D-FEM. The no-load and on-load statuses have been investigated. The analysis results have proved the model to have field regulation of ±40%. Secondly, relieving-dc-saturation working principle based machine design is one of the main objectives to be achieved. Reluctance machines with dc excitation coils have become a promising solution for wind power generation system because of its robust rotor structure and good field-weakening ability. However, due to both the armature windings and dc excitation are located in the stator side, these machines usually suffer from magnetic saturation, as well as relatively low torque density and efficiency. To solve this problem, we investigated a novel relieving-DC-saturation hybrid reluctance machine with improved torque density and efficiency. The key is to introduce skewed permanent magnets (PMs) in slot openings. The tangential component of skewed PMs can be used to relieve the dc saturation in the stator iron core, so that the B − H working range can be extended and relatively high dc excitation can be applied in the proposed machine. Besides, the radial component of skewed PM provides extra torque component under flux modulation effect. Therefore, the proposed skewed PMs can also achieve torque boost and core utilization improvement simultaneously. Thirdly, winding switching control strategy is successfully developed in this project. A novel winding switching strategy is proposed to improve the flux-weakening capability of a hybrid-excited reluctance machine (HERM). The key is that in low-speed operation, the primary and the secondary windings are connected in series and serve as armature winding to maximize output voltage while in high-speed operation, the secondary winding is switched to dc excitation winding to realize variable speed constant voltage output. The machine configuration, operation principle with dual excitation sources, winding switching concept, and manipulation circuit are comprehensively studied. Then the electromagnetic characteristics of HERM in different operation status are investigated. Finally, the variable speed constant DC voltage output of wind power generation system resorting to winding switching as well as dc excitation regulation is verified with Maxwell/Simplorer cosimulation. The winding switching technology based machine configuration, operation principle of dual excitation sources, winding switching concept as well as winding switching manipulation circuit are studied in detail. The electromagnetic characteristics of HERM are testified by finite-element method. Variable-speed-constant-voltage with both winding switching operation and dc excitation operation is verified by cosimulation with Maxwell/Simplorer software. It demonstrates that, when the machine speed varies with time, winding switching operation and dc excitation operation can keep the output voltage unchanged. Finally, contra rotating machine topology optimization is complicated, especially considering different slot/pole combinations, geometric sizes, PM arrangement and winding distributions. For contra-rotating machines, avoiding the coupling between two sets of winding is very essential, especially when two windings are placed in the same slots. The most effective way of decoupling is to use the winding factor as a filter. When the winding factor of one winding’s PPN is zero for the other winding, two windings are decoupled. In our proposed design, the slot/pole combination of 24/2 for modulation winding and 24/11 for regular winding are chosen. The winding factors of the working harmonics in two sets of winding are calculated. It can be observed that the modulation winding can effectively eliminate the harmonics from the regular winding, and vice versa. Therefore, two sets of winding can work independently without influencing each other. To optimize the design of the contra-rotating machine, a novel design using a high-order harmonic modulation is proposed. The key is that the compound outer rotor is artificially designed to enhance the third harmonic component of airgap flux density in the inner airgap while remaining the fundamental component unchanged in the outer airgap. The presented design is optimized and compared with the conventional design with the same structural dimensions, which shows that the proposed design has 50% higher back EMF in modulation winding and 45.7% larger torque density in the rated conditions. For the complicated topological structure, a novel high-resolution encoding and edge smoothing method is proposed for topology optimization. This method aims to solve complex electromagnetic design problems with time-dependent performance through a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) integrated with a high-resolution encoding and edge smoothing method. The complex structure is represented by a high-resolution image-like matrix and then vectorized by the edge smoothing method. Therefore, the commonly used discrete binary encoded variables related to the finite element (FE) model are replaced with a vectorized topological structure and other control variables. In this sense, high-resolution matrix and edge smoothing methods are used for the first time to represent the rotor topology of AIPMSMs. Numerical results show that a stable convergence is achieved with the avoidance of checkerboards and material overlapping. In summary, all of the objectives have been successfully achieved and published and shared in conferences.

15210920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210920.value: Contra-rotating dual rotor PM machines based on bidirectional flux modulation have been investigated for the standalone DC power supply[4]. This design requires a conventional winding whose pole pair number is equal to the outer rotor, and a modulation winding. Two sets of windings are connected in series as their frequencies are the same. The inner rotor is connected to the servo motor. Therefore, the inner PM flux linkage vector is adjustable and the sum of modulated vector and the outer PM vector, namely the total flux linkage, is controllable. This active-controlled mechanical flux-weakening method suits the machine with a small saliency ratio. Nevertheless, two sets of windings are needed, which have the following shortcomings: First, two pairs of windings have different coil pitches, which are relatively complex to manufacture; second, the turn numbers of two pairs of windings are different for reaching the maximized flux controlling range. Another research outcome is a novel mechanical flux-weakening spoke-type PM generator[5]. In only one set of windings, all three working harmonics have the same frequency, which can be added as vectors based on the flux modulation principle. By adjusting the modulator ring within a certain angle, the flux can be effectively controlled without the risk of PM demagnetization, and the variable-speed constant-amplitude voltage control (VSCAVC) can be achieved. A commercial servo system using the position control mode is sufficient for dynamic performance, which is also cost-efficient, robust, and easy to control. The principles of flux controlling and working harmonic selection are introduced. To investigate the influence of the pole pair number and the performance of the novel design, four cases with different rotor poles and winding configurations, i.e., 12/7, 12/8, 12/10, and 12/11 stator/rotor pole pair combinations, have been designed, optimized, and compared. Finally, the 12/7 design is selected, and its VSCAVC characteristics are analyzed. The winding switching technology based machine configuration, operation principle of dual excitation sources, winding switching concept as well as winding switching manipulation circuit are studied in detail[6-8]. Different typologies have been comprehensively studied[1-3][9-13].

15210920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210920.value: Future work: 1. Pole-changing multiport machine: Based on high-order modulation and utilizing the inherent fundamental and third harmonics of the PMs, a new type of machine can be designed with an extended speed range. For the proposed design, the high-order modulation increases the back EMF at low speeds, while the fundamental modulation allows for a decrease in the inverter frequency at high speeds. 2. Hybrid-excited multiport machine (AC+DC): This design combines zero-sequence DC excitation and consequent-pole PM excitation as the hybrid excitation sources. 3. Multi-set integrated winding (AC*N): The current integrated "AC+AC" winding only allows for the integration of two winding sets. To achieve the integration of more winding sets, such as all three windings for pole-changing multiport machine, the utilization of coil space can be significantly improved, leading to enhanced overall efficiency.

15210920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210920.value: Currently the most popular wind turbines in the market consist of a horizontal axis and one rotor. According to Betz theory, the maximum power extracted from the wind is only 59% of the available energy with single-rotor wind turbine. However, the energy behind the single rotor is not small. Additional rotor can be installed in this wake area to further extract the wind energy. This innovative wind power generation system could effectively extract increased wind energy at low speeds. Key benefit: 1.Integrated and Compact Design: Unlike traditional contra-rotating wind power generators that use two separate units, our design integrates them into a single, compact system. This reduces space requirements and simplifies installation. 2.Brushless Structure: By utilizing a magnetic-geared structure, our system eliminates the wear and tear associated with brushed mechanisms, resulting in a maintenance-free solution. 3.Enhanced Wind Energy Conversion Efficiency: The use of relieving dc saturation contra-rotating turbines and winding switching technology allows for higher energy conversion rates, maximizing the efficiency of wind energy capture. The contra-rotating wind power generator which can efficiently supply electric power with improved wind power extraction efficiency to residential and commercial buildings would be a breakthrough in the development of wind power generation system.

15211120.label: Project Objectives
15211120.value: To design practical lattice-based non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs. We plan to explore ways to construct lattice-based non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs. The main idea is to investigate a new transformation which transforms interactive zero-knowledge proof protocol into its non-interactive form in the quantum random oracle model. To develop lattice-based succinct zero-knowledge proofs. We aim to develop the first lattice-based succinct zero-knowledge proofs with communication cost constant or logarithmic to the size of the statement being proved. We will explore two directions. First, we will examine previous sub-linear lattice-based zero-knowledge proofs and reduce its communication cost to logarithmic. We will also try to build on existing designated-verifier succinct zero-knowledge proofs to achieve public verifiability. To design practical post-quantum zero knowledge from supersingular isogenies. We plan to investigate methods to construct practical post-quantum Zero Knowledge from supersingular isogenies. This involves improving existing zero-knowledge proofs for discrete logarithm friendly language and the design of ZK proofs for other classes of language, such as linear equation etc. In terms of efficiency, we will consider the balance of the communication and computation cost. To analyze the security of our supersingular isogeny based zero knowledge in the quantum random oracle model. We will investigate the security of our supersingular isogeny based ZK in the quantum random oracle model, which provides more reasonable and stronger guarantee of quantum-resistance than the classical random oracle. This involves systematically reconsideration of the design philosophy of existing transformations from Sigma-protocol and the design of new transformation in quantum random oracle model. We will also consider the concrete security under quantum attacks and finally conduct security analysis and complexity analysis.

15211120.label: Realisation of objectives
15211120.value: We have achieved all objectives of this project. Specifically, details of achievements for each objective are listed as follows. For objective 1, we leverage the recent framework for constructing succinct zero-knowledge arguments which involves building an information-theoretic zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) system based on the existence of an idealised object known as polynomial oracle, which provides a compact representation of any polynomial. This ZKP is referred to as polynomial interactive oracle proofs (PIOP). In the actual instantiation, the polynomial oracle is replaced by a cryptographic primitive, namely, polynomial commitment. If the polynomial commitment is quantum safe, the resulting ZKP is also quantum safe. We develop a high-level framework that allows us to build polynomial commitments using any vector commitment (e.g., built from a collision-resistant hash function using a binary tree structure). This enables the construction of post-quantum ZKPs from lattices or any collision-resistant hash functions. By combining these techniques, we construct a succinct zero-knowledge argument for arbitrary fields. For objective 2, we propose and implement a post-quantum succinct zero-knowledge proof system. Specifically, by adding the zero-knowledge property into the post-quantum non-interactive argument of knowledge system, ethSTARK, we developed a highly efficient post-quantum zero-knowledge proof system. This proposed scheme is well-suited for constructing other cryptographic primitives, such as signature of knowledge and linkable ring signature schemes. To examine the efficiency of our post-quantum zero-knowledge proof system, we use it to construct a post-quantum linkable ring signature scheme, which is the first quantum-secure linkable ring signature featuring a signature size of O(log log N) with a ring size of N. In addition to this work, we further improve the lattice-based programmable hash function. This enhanced hash function can serve as an important building block for cryptographic primitives, such as Identity-based encryption schemes, with the resulting scheme benefiting from a shorter key size. For Objective 3, following the discovery of vulnerabilities in Supersingular Isogeny Diffie-Hellman (SIDH) in 2022, we have shifted our focus to Commutative Supersingular Isogeny Diffie-Hellman (CSIDH), which is considered a secure isogeny problem. Our research explores lossy identification, a specialized zero-knowledge proof, within the context of CSIDH and introduces a novel twinning approach for CSIDH by leveraging the properties of zero-knowledge proofs. We further extend these zero-knowledge techniques for isogeny-based cryptography to broader group action problems, generalizing the CSIDH problem. Additionally, our work demonstrates applications of twinned CSIDH in areas such as authenticated key exchange (AKE) and CCA-secure encryption. For Objective 4, building on the work in Objective 3, we analyzed zero-knowledge techniques for isogeny within the quantum random oracle model (QROM). Our findings demonstrate that the twinning approach using isogeny-based zero-knowledge proofs remains valid in QROM, albeit with a square root reduction loss. This is consistent with similar cryptographic primitives in QROM, such as CCA-secure encryption, where such losses are typical. As a byproduct of this work, we also revisited the QROM security of compact authenticated key exchange (AKE) schemes.

15211120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211120.value: Throughout the development of this project, we have made a number valuable findings. Starting with the design philosophy for constructing zero-knowledge proof systems, we identify fundamental building blocks and present new constructions. Specifically, we introduce a new polynomial interactive oracle proof of proximity that operates over any field. It enables the construction of a new post-quantum non-interactive zero-knowledge proof system with fewer restrictions on the choice of the underlying field. Moreover, we also explore practical aspect of post-quantum zero-knowledge proofs. Specifically, we enhance the well-known post-quantum ethSTARK system by incorporating zero-knowledge properties. Based on our new zero-knowledge proof system, we successfully constructed the first quantum-secure linkable ring signature scheme with O(log log N) signature size. Additionally, we introduce a new lattice-based programmable hash function, which can serve as a key building block for constructing other post-quantum cryptographic schemes, such as identity-based encryption protocols with shorter key size. We develop new isogeny-based zero-knowledge proofs, focusing on lossy identification and introducing a novel twinning approach for the Commutative Supersingular Isogeny Diffie-Hellman (CSIDH) problem. We extend this twinned CSIDH to applications such as authenticated key exchange and CCA-secure encryption schemes. Additionally, we analyze zero-knowledge techniques for isogeny in the quantum random oracle model (QROM), showing that the twinning approach remains valid, though with a square root reduction loss. The research outcomes of this project resulted in the publication of two peer-reviewed journal articles in the prestigious journal IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security and four conference papers presented at leading international conferences, including the ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (ACM CCS), the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP), and the European Symposium on Research in Computer Security (ESORICS).

15211120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211120.value: The research project holds significant potential for further development, not only in the realm of post-quantum zero-knowledge proof systems but also in other areas of cryptographic primitives, like post-quantum signature schemes and authenticated key exchange schemes. Specifically, the development of efficient and practical post-quantum zero-knowledge proofs with succinct proof sizes remains a critical direction in this field. The new method introduced in this project paves the way for future work on proposing more practical post-quantum proof systems with fewer limitations. One potential approach is to explore alternative lattice assumptions to help reduce proof sizes. Moreover, since zero-knowledge proof systems can be used to validate the correctness of generated values, they are employed in the construction of other cryptographic primitives, such as signature-of-knowledge and linkable ring signature schemes. Furthermore, building on our finding that the twinning approach using isogeny-based zero-knowledge proofs remains valid in QROM, we extend these zero-knowledge techniques for isogeny-based cryptography to broader group action problems. We demonstrate applications of twinned CSIDH in areas such as AKE and CCA-secure encryption schemes. Our research contributes to the construction of other post-quantum protocols. Future work in this area includes development of additional post-quantum protocols, focusing on enhancing their efficiency and practicality.

15211120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211120.value: In this project, we introduce new constructions of post-quantum non-interactive zero-knowledge proof systems with enhanced efficiency and practicability. We develop new post-quantum proof systems through multiple approaches. To improve efficiency, we incorporate zero-knowledge properties into well-known schemes, resulting in more streamlined constructions. Furthermore, we explore new post-quantum proof systems based on diverse assumptions, such as assumptions from lattices and supersingular isogenies. For the practicability aspect, we propose proof systems capable of generating shorter proofs, which, in turn, lead to signature schemes with reduced key sizes. We also construct a compact AKE scheme within the QROM model by revisiting the QROM model. Moreover, we investigate construction of post-quantum zero-knowledge proof systems based on arbitrary finite field so that it can fit various algebraic settings. In summary, this project makes significant contributions to the development of efficient and practical zero-knowledge proof systems in the domain of post-quantum cryptography. Beyond its immediate scope, the outcomes of this project have a broader impact on other areas of cryptography, including lattice-based cryptography, digital signatures, identity-based encryption and authenticated key exchange protocols.

15211720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15211720.value: 基於多分辨率分析的接縫裁剪圖像和多相機合成圖的相機源識別

15211720.label: Project Objectives
15211720.value: In contrast to the fixed single resolution approach adopted by existing source camera attribution methods on seam-carved images, we will perform a multiresolution study to improve the robustness and reliability of these techniques. We will devise a decision metric for combining the multiresolution features and use a learning-based method for source camera attribution on seam-carved images. We will investigate the effect of image compression on the accuracy of source camera attribution on seam-carved images. We will use the seam carving idea to model the image stitching process of image formation in newly released mobile phones. Hence, the multiresolution study can be extended to the case when the camera array is used to produce the final image.

15211720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211720.value: 在這個信息時代，確定數據的來源是一個非常重要的問題。特別地，在執法程序中，識別非法圖像的來源，有助於確定這些非法圖像是由某些特定的設備所拍攝的，還是由其他方式下載獲取的。目前，最先進的圖像的拍攝設備源識別技術是通過從圖像中提取一種傳感器噪聲，稱為光響應不均勻性噪聲，實現基於相關性的圖像相機源識別。研究學者們已經證明這類基於光響應不均勻性噪聲的方法在對抗不同的圖像增強或圖像處理技具有有效性和魯棒性。然而，當圖像使用“接縫裁剪”技術進行圖像縮放時，這類方法往往無法確定拍攝該圖像的相機來源。這是因為：接縫裁剪技術的主要思想是識別圖像中的最不重要的一些平滑區域，通過移除這些平滑區域，實現圖像縮放，已達到不破壞原圖中重要的圖像結構和內容的目的。這種圖像縮放技術會移除某些特定的圖像區域，使得基於光響應不均性噪聲的方法中位置對應的假設前提無法成立，進而導致該方法失效。 儘管“接縫裁剪”算法已經在流行的圖像編輯軟件中進行應用，但目前，針對使用該技術得到的縮放圖像，僅有兩項研究工作涉及其相機源識別問題。這兩項研究工作都是通過在接縫裁剪後的縮放圖像中，尋找固定大小的未被裁剪過的圖像小塊。這種方法必須尋找到一定數量的未被裁剪過的圖像小塊，才能具有一定的魯棒性。在某些情況下，可能利用超過500個未經裁剪過的圖像小塊都難以準確地識別出圖像的相機源。事實上，未經裁剪過的圖像塊的大小是與圖像內容息息相關的。紋理複雜區域中，未經裁剪的圖像塊的大小會大於平滑區域中的。這是因為：在紋理複雜區域中，使用接縫裁剪技術的可能性要低於在平滑區域中。基於此思想，本項目擬主要研究基於圖像塊大小的多分辨率分析的相機源識別方法，實現比單分辨率分析法更魯棒的性能。我們將根據圖像塊大小，提取相關性變化蘊含的模式。對於同一部相機拍攝的圖像塊，相關性隨著塊大小而增加。然而，如果該圖像塊並非由同一部相機所拍攝，其相關性會隨著塊大小而隨機變化。基於該思想，通過對圖像塊大小相關聯的模式變化進行多分辨率分析，有助於提高相機源識別任務的性能。本項目的特色與創新之處主要體現在基於模式變化的多分辨率分析，各種多分辨率特徵將用於決策函數的設計，或者應用於基於學習型的方法。我們將對這兩類方法進行綜合地對比性研究。 新型的手機產品常配有多相機拍攝功能，使用這些手機產品拍攝的照片，往往是經過多個相機鏡頭拍攝的多張圖像進行拼接優化得到的。這種多相機拍攝功能能夠充分提升圖像質量，但也使得具有位置對應性假設的基於光響應不均勻性噪聲的相機源識別方法失效。因此，本項目擬提出一個新型框架，對使用接縫裁剪思想的圖像拼接過程進行建模。通過這種方式，我們將多分辨率分析法應用在這一難題上，解決使用多相機合成圖的相機源識別問題。 現今，使用接縫裁剪技術進行圖像縮放已經非常普及，大量數字圖像遍布人們的生活中，圖像相機源識別問題不僅在學術界進行了應用研究，更引起了公眾的關注。在許多實際應用中，如犯罪調查，監控成像系統和新聞行業，有效且可靠的圖像相機源識別方法的發展尤為關鍵。我們擬提出的方法將有助於進一步推動數字取證領域的發展。

15211720.label: Realisation of objectives
15211720.value: Source camera identification is a process aimed at determining the specific camera device that has been used to capture a particular photo. Typically, correlation analysis is performed to assess the similarity between a test photo and the camera signature. A high correlation value in a matched case indicates that the test photo originates from the source camera, while a low correlation value in an unmatched case means the test photo is not from the source camera. The objective of this project is to develop effective source attribution methods for photos that have undergone resizing through seam-carving. Previous work relied on finding fixed-size uncarved blocks within the seam-carved resized photos. However, these approaches preset the size of the uncarved blocks. In practice, the optimal block size varies with image content. The size is large in the texture region while it is small in the smooth region. Ideally, the attribution method should make the size to be adaptive according to the image content. The first objective of this project is to devise a multiresolution analysis to explore how the correlation metric varies between the matched and unmatched cases. Our studies found that the multiresolution correlation metric remains more or less unchanged if the seam-carved photos are not taken by the camera under testing. However, the correlation values show an increasing trend if the seam-carved photos are taken by the camera under testing. The multiresolution correlation analysis enhances the accuracy and reliability of source camera identification compared to the existing single-resolution approach. To further improve the robustness of the multiresolution correlation analysis, the position of the alignment blocks is also considered. We found that the matched positions did not change substantially if the seam-carved photo was taken by the camera under testing. However, in the unmatched case, the position changed substantially across scales. By combining both the position and the correlation information, the source device identification can be performed reliably. Multiresolution feature can be obtained from the correlation analysis and positions of the alignment block to characterize the differences between the matched and the unmatched cases. Our second objective is to devise two different methods for using the multiresolution feature in source camera attribution for seam-carved images. The first approach is based on the design of a decision metric while the second approach is based on the use of a learning-based method. In devising the decision metric, features extracted from the multiresolution correlation vectors and matched positions information are obtained which are then combined through a regression function. In the learning-based method, a 1D convolutional neural network is designed. The network is trained to analyze the multiresolution features so that the network can learn the specific pattern in the matched and unmatched cases. The third objective of the project is to perform a detailed analysis of the two approaches for source camera attribution on seam-carved images, especially when images are compressed. The two methods are validated using a dataset containing both smartphones and digital cameras. We have tested different carving ratios at different compression ratios. We considered both seam removal and seam addition cases. We have also considered different ways to perform seam carving, such as the use of different seam carving methods including the forced seam carving approaches. Prior research found that source anonymization is effective, especially if there is at least one seam located in every 25 x 25 image block. Our experimental results confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The accuracy is always over 90%, even for highly compressed photos. Finally, we have tested our methods on newly released mobile phones in which photos can be obtained by combining a number of pictures. Our experimental results demonstrate that a single-resolution analysis cannot be used to reliably identify the source camera in such a case. However, with the use of multiresolution information, the two proposed methods can still achieve reliable results. In summary, all the four objectives have been addressed in this project. Details about the multiresolution analysis (Objective 1), the design of the decision metric (Objective 2), the experimental validation on newly released mobile phones (Objective 4) and the effect of compression (Objective 3) on source camera identification can be found in the following paper: Muhammad Irshad, S.R.C. Liew, N.F. Law, and K.H. 15211720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211720.value: Source camera identification aims to determine the specific camera device that has been used to capture a particular photo. The objective of this project is to develop effective source attribution methods for photos that have been resized by seam-carving. Existing works relied on finding fixed-size uncarved blocks within the seam-carved resized photos. In practice, the size varies with image content. In particular, the size is large in the texture region while it is small in the smooth region. We have devised a multiresolution analysis to explore how the correlation metric varies between the matched and unmatched cases. Our studies found that the correlation metric remains unchanged if the seam-carved photos are not taken by the camera under testing. However, the correlation values show an increasing trend if the seam-carved photos are taken by the camera under testing. In addition to the correlation metric, we found that the matched position of the alignment blocks did not change much in matched cases. In contrast, the position changes substantially in unmatched cases. To improve the robustness of the multiresolution correlation analysis, a decision metric is devised based on the correlation metric as well as the position of the alignment blocks. In addition to the use of decision metric, we have also investigated the use of convolutional neural networks. As the number of seams to be removed varies with the image content and images are compressed in practical applications, we have devised a dataset consisting of different carving ratios at various compression ratios. Our study indicates that the proposed multiresolution correlation analysis is effective in identifying the source camera of seam-carved photos, even at high compression ratios. Recent cameras often contain a number of sensors in which images are formed through an image-stitching process. Our multiresolution analysis has been extended to consider these newly released mobiles. Extensive experimental results have been performed. Our proposed methods are found to be effective for these phones in which the accuracy is over 90%. These results have been published in the following papers: • Muhammad Irshad, S.R.C. Liew, N.F. Law, and K.H. Loo, "CAMID: An Assuasive Approach to Reveal Source Camera through Inconspicuous Evidence", Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation, 46, 301616, Sept 2023. • Muhammad Irshad, N.F. Law, K.H. Loo and S. Haider, "IMG CAT: An Approach to dismantle the anonymity of a source camera using correlative features and an integrated 1D convolutional neural network", Array, 18, p1-13, 100279, July 2023. • Muhammad Irshad, N.F. Law and K.H. Loo, "CamCarv: Expose the Source Camera at the Rear of Seam Insertion", L. Rutkowski Et al. (Eds): ICAISC 2022, LNAI 13589, pp 21-34, Jan 2023. Existing research considered only seam removal cases. In our study, in addition to seam removal, we also considered source camera identification for the case of seam addition. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method works effectively in both seam addition and seam removal cases.

15211720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211720.value: Identifying the source camera of seam-carved images is an important problem. We have proposed two methods to identify the source camera of seam-carved images. Despite the good performance, one major disadvantage of the proposed method is the high computational complexity as multiresolution features have to be extracted from the correlation metrics between the test image and the camera fingerprint. Methods have to be devised to reduce the computational complexities. A potential solution is to perform the analysis adaptively based on the image content. Seams seldom pass through highly textured regions, while are commonly found in smooth regions. Thus, a pre-processing module can be adopted to identify highly textured regions which will undergo multiresolution analysis. In this way, as the number of extracted regions is reduced, the computational time can be reduced. In the future, we will investigate this approach to see if the identification accuracy can remain unchanged while the complexity is reduced.

15211720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211720.value: Determining the source of digital images is an important problem in this information age. In law enforcement applications, identifying the source of illegal images can help determine whether those images are produced by certain devices or downloaded from somewhere else. Existing PRNU (photo response non-uniformity noise) methods are effective in source camera identification. However, they fail when photos are resized through seam-carving. The aim of this project is to investigate methods for identifying the source camera for photos that have been seam-carved. Existing works relied on finding fixed-size uncarved blocks within the seam-carved resized photos. We have performed a multiresolution analysis to achieve a more robust attribution than a single-resolution analysis. We have identified two patterns associated with the change in correlation values. The novelty of this work involves performing a multiresolution analysis of the change in the pattern. These multiresolution features are extracted to design a decision metric and a learning-based method. Experimental results have shown an excellent source camera identification performance for different carving ratios and at different compression ratios. Given the popularity of seam carving for image resizing, the development of robust source camera attribution is critical in many applications such as crime investigation, surveillance imaging systems and journalism.

15212220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212220.value: This project is to study photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) and photoacoustic Raman spectroscopy (PARS) in gas-filled hollow-core negative-curvature fibres (HC-NCFs) and develop highly sensitive gas sensors with these fibres. PAS and PARS measure respectively thermally induced acoustic-pressure-waves due to optical absorption and stimulated Raman scattering, which can be used to detect absorptive and Raman-active gases. In traditional PAS and PARS systems, a free-space optical gas cell and a microphone are used to detect the acoustic-wave over a small region, i.e., the sensitive area of the microphone. HC-NCFs are a novel type of optical fibres that has very broad transmission band from visible to mid-infrared, covering absorption/Raman spectrums of a large variety of gases. A HC-NCF can confine a laser beam, acoustic-pressure-wave and gases simultaneously in the hollow-core, enabling highly efficient interaction between them. Compared with free-space optical systems, the use of HC-NCFs offers several advantages: (i) the optical mode in a HC-NCF has a much smaller mode-field-diameter than a free-space beam, resulting in higher peak-optical-intensity (for the same optical power) and hence a higher pressure change; (ii) the hollow-core acts as a miniature acoustic cavity, which enhances the pressure change in the hollow-core via transverse (radial) acoustic resonance. The small diameter of the hollow-core means high acoustic resonant frequencies (e.g., a few MHz) at which the 1/f noise for detection is smaller; (iii) the acoustic-wave can be measured via propagating a probe laser beam in the same HC-NCF and interferometrically detecting the accumulated phase change, without the need for an additional microphone. The probe beam has negligible effect on the fibre structure, the gas in the hollow-core and the acoustic-wave. This allows the use of a long HC-NCF to detect the overall effect of the acoustic-wave on the phase of probe accumulated over the entire length of the fibre, enabling higher detection sensitivity over the ‘point sampling’ of acoustic-wave with a microphone. Therefore, gas detection with PAS and PARS in HC-NCFs are expected to achieve much higher sensitivity but has not been systematically studied to our knowledge. We plan to model acoustic-wave generation, acoustic resonance and probe phase modulation for both PAS and PARS, for HC-NCFs with different structural parameters and filled with gases at different pressures up to several bars. We will examine the use of different all-fibre interferometers to detect probe phase modulatuion and experimentally evaluate the system performances for detecting absorptive (e.g. C2H2) and Raman-active gases (e.g. H2). 本项目研究气体填充的空芯负曲率光纤（HC-NCF）中的光声光谱（PAS）和光声拉曼（PARS）效应，以及基于这些光纤的高灵敏度气体传感器。PAS 和 PARS 分别测量由于光学吸收和受激拉曼散射而引起的热诱导声压波，可用于检测吸收性气体和拉曼活性气体。在传统的 PAS 和 PARS 系统中，一般采用自由空间气室和麦克风来检测小区域（即麦克风的敏感区域）的声波。 HC-NCF 是一种新型的光纤，其传输带非常宽，可以从可见光到中红外，覆盖了多种气体的吸收或拉曼谱线。HC-NCF 可以将激光束、声压波和气体同时限制在空芯中，从而实现它们之间的高效相互作用。与自由空间光学系统相比，使用HC-NCF具有以下几个优点：（i）HC-NCF 中模式的模场直径比自由空间光束小得多，可以产生更高的峰值光强度，因此更高的声压;（ii） 光纤的空芯是一个微型声学腔，通过横向声学共振可以增强芯内的压力变化。空芯的直径很小，意味着高的声学谐振频率，因此1/f的检测噪声较小;（iii）可以通过在同一HC-NCF中传播的探测激光束来测量声波，应用干涉仪来检测探测光累积的相位变化，而无需使用额外的麦克风。 探测光对光纤结构、空芯中的气体和声波的影响可以忽略不计。因此可以使用较长的HC-NCF来检测声波沿整个光纤长度累积的探测光的相位变化，从而实现比常规"点采样"的带麦克风更高的检测灵敏度。因此，应用HC-NCF进行PAS和PARS气体检测有望获得更高的灵敏度，但至今还没有系统地研究过。 我们计划对HC-NCF声波产生、声学共振和探测光的相位调制进行建模，分析不同的HC-NCF结构参数，不同的气体压力对PAS和PARS系统性能的影响。将采用不同的全光纤干涉仪来检测探测光的相位调制，对吸收性气体的检测进行实验评估。

15212220.label: Realisation of objectives
15212220.value: Objective 1 Gas detection with photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy (PABS) in different types of hollow-core negative-curvature fibres (HC-NCFs, or hollow-core fibres (HCF) for simplicity) are theoretically investigated. The HCFs we studied include anti-resonant hollow-core fibres (AR-HCFs) and nested anti-resonant nodeless hollow-core fibres (NANFs), which can transmit light from near to mid-infrared (up to 4.5 micrometer) with low-loss. Theoretical formulations of PABS are developed, include the optical and acoustic modes supported by the HCFs, the dynamic interaction of the optical and acoustic modes through coupled equations of the pump, Stokes (generated from modulated sideband of the pump) and the acoustic wave, the forcelike and scattering process in absorptive (i.e., including gas absorption of the modulated pump) stimulated Brillouin scattering, and relationship between the phase modulation of the probe beam and the gas concentration, gas pressure, absorption of the gas, interaction length, pump power, and acoustic properties of the microstructure fibre. Numerical simulations with real fibre parameters used in our experiments are performed and reveal that the acoustic modes, including air acoustic mode and capillary elastic modes can be excited efficiently by optical absorption of gas molecules inside the hollow-core via photoacoustic effect, which is two to three orders of magnitude more efficient than previously reported electrostriction and radiation pressure excitation. These findings enable a new approach for high sensitivity photoacoustic spectroscopy named PABS, which can be applied for acoustic spectroscopy of the fibre microstructure as well as optical spectroscopy of gas molecules inside the hollow-core. Objective 2 Experiments are conducted with AR-HCFs, NANFs as well as hollow-core photonic bandgap fibres. It is found that the photonic bandgap fibre support mainly the air acoustic modes while the AR-HCFs and the NANFs support both air acoustic modes and capillary elastic modes. The quality-factors (Q-factor) of the capillary elastic modes are in general higher than that of the air acoustic modes. The measured Q-factor of the capillary elastic mode at low pressure (e.g., 10 mbar) can be as high as 500. The probe phase modulation of the gas-filled NANFs at the resonance of a capillary elastic mode can be an order of magnitude higher than that of the AR-HCFs, meaning higher gas detection sensitivity can be achieved. Different interferometric schemes have been studied to detect the probe phase modulation. The dual-mode interferometer that detects the mode-phase difference has the highest signal-to-noise ratio and used for subsequent gas detection experiments. Both intensity- and wavelength-modulated PABS are studied experimentally. The wavelength-modulated PABS with a NANF demonstrated the best performance. The reasons for the better performance are: First, wavelength modulation obviates the need for external intensity modulation, resulting in a simper system with two or three times lower noise level and better long-term stability. Second, we employ a NANF with capillary tubes of a larger radius than the AR-HCF, which leads to higher acoustic force and larger mode overlapping between the mechanical mode and the optical mode, benefiting the forcelike process and scattering process respectively. The wavelength modulation also eliminates the unwanted phase modulation signals generated by reversible forces unrelated to gas absorption, which is unavoidable in the intensity modulation-based PABS. Gas detection experiments are conducted with both the intensity-modulated and wavelength-modulation based PABS, and with AR-HCFs and NANFs. With the same optical pump power level, the wavelength-modulated PABS with NANF is more sensitive than the intensity-modulated PABS with AR-HCF. The lower detection limit for acetylene detection is 8 ppb for PABS with a 30-cm-long AR-HCF and 0.4 ppb for PABS with a 0.85-m-long NANF. Objective 3 We theoretically evaluate the photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy (PABS) driven by stimulated Raman scattering (SRS), which is referred as stimulated Raman photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy (SRPABS), for hydrogen detection. A pump laser and a wavelength-modulated Stokes laser excite the Raman transition of the hydrogen molecules, which induces periodic heating at the Stokes modulation frequency. The heating inside the hollow-core fiber (HCF) excites the elastic resonance of the inner capillaries through photoacoustic effects, which modulates the phase of a probe beam via forward Brillouin scattering (FBS). A theoretical model describing the PABS process is presented. Numerically simulation on a 0.85-m-long nested anti-resonant nodeless HCF (NANF) with an inner diameter of 48 micrometer shows that that phase modulation is ~10^(-10) rad for 500 mW pump and Stokes power and 1000 ppm hydrogen balanced with nitrogen under 1 bar. With appropriate optimization of the HCF and other parameters, the phase modulation of SRPABS for 1000 ppm hydrogen could potentially reach 10^(-4) rad. Since no paper has been published on this and no manuscript is uploaded as the Research Output, we wish to give some details of our theoretical investigations on the SRPABS below. The theoretical formulation includes three aspects: (a). SRS heat generation. We use wavelength modulation spectroscopy and hence the induced heat source is in the form of harmonics. The frequency of the harmonic heat source is matched to the mechanical resonances of acoustic mode in the HCF. The heat generation is determined by the gain, frequency shift and relaxation time of the selected Raman line. The tight confinement of the pump and Stokes modes in the HCF significantly enhances the SRS heat generation since it is proportional to the product of the pump and the Stokes intensities. (b). Thermodynamic process in HCF. As compared to the Raman induced photothermal effect, SRPABS utilizes the Raman induced photoacoustic effect, which is amplified by capillary resonance inside the HCF. With the harmonic SRS heat source described (a), the thermodynamic process can be studied with the same formulations as those for the conventional PABS. The induced capillary resonance can be numerically calculated and the capillary displacement, gas temperature, pressure, velocity and viscosity change in the HCF can then be obtained. (c) Determining the phase modulation in SRPABS. The resulting phase modulation can be calculated based on results in (b). The phase modulation is primarily determined by the energy transfer efficiency of the capillary's moving boundary and the gas photoelasticity effect, which are related to temperature, pressure, and the compressibility and coefficient of gas thermal expansion. We then numerically studied the process of the SRPABS. The pump and Stokes frequency difference matches the hydrogen Q1(1) vibrational Raman transition 4155 cm^(-1). The NANF is filled with hydrogen balanced with nitrogen under 1 bar pressure. The maximum capillary displacement is found to be nearly eight orders of magnitude smaller than that for acetylene PABS under the same gas concentration and pump power level for the same NANF with 48 micrometer inner diameter. We then numerically evaluated the phase modulation of SRPABS. The phase modulation on the fundamental optical mode is calculated to be ~10^(-10) rad for the NANF with a length of 0.85 m filled with 1000 ppm hydrogen under 1 bar pressure. Such a small phase modulation is difficult to detect with the state-of-the-art fiber interferometer technology. The performance of SRPABS might be enhanced by: (i) down-taper the HCF to reduce the diameter of the hollow-core, (ii) use pulsed high-power laser sources, (iii) use a higher-order mode for phase detection, (iv) use a higher gas pressure, (v) use a longer HCF. With all these measures, the phase modulation could be boosted to the level of 10^(-4) rad for 1000 ppm hydrogen.

15212220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212220.value: We have demonstrated theoretically and experimentally that the acoustic modes, including air acoustic mode and capillary elastic modes in a hollow-core fibre (HCF) can be excited by optical absorption of gas molecules inside the HCF. The excitation is two to three orders of magnitude more efficient than electrostriction and radiation pressure. Based on this, we further demonstrated a new approach for photoacoustic spectroscopy named photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy (PABS). With PABS, acoustic spectroscopy of the microstructures as well as optical spectroscopy of gas molecules inside HCFs are demonstrated. The acoustic resonances detected by PABS reveal the delicate microstructures of the HCFs, which can be used to characterize the inhomogeneity along the fibre. The optical spectral absorption of gas molecules at an acoustic resonance provides a means of photoacoustic gas spectroscopy with enhanced detection sensitivity. (Optica 8(4), 2021) (3/2022/San Diego). The physical mechanisms underlying PABS in HCFs, which have not been investigated previously, are now thoroughly understood. The optical absorption of gas molecules induces forcelike process, which critically determines the efficiency of optical pump power transfer to the mechanical resonances. We have developed an effective theoretical model that can precisely determines the influence of various physical factors on the forcelike process in photoacoustic Brillouin scattering. The result also reveals a unique characteristic of the photoacoustic Brillouin scattering: it can be excited without any optical intensity modulation. Based on the above findings, we optimized the PABS by using wavelength-modulation (instead of intensity modulation) and a nested anti-resonance nodeless HCF (NANF) and achieved improved detection limit from 8 ppb (3/2022/San Diego) to 0.4 ppb (9/2024/Chengdu). The advancement of the wavelength-modulated PABS is primarily due to following factors: First, wavelength modulation obviates the need for external intensity modulation, resulting in a simper system with lower noise level and better long-term stability. Second, we employ the NANF with capillary tubes of larger radius than the anti-resonance HCF (AR-HCF). This leads to higher acoustic force and larger mode overlapping between the capillary elastic mode and the optical mode, which benefits the forcelike and scattering process respectively. The wavelength modulation also eliminates the unwanted modulation signals generated by reversible forces unrelated to gas absorption, which is unavoidable in the intensity modulation scheme. With the same power pump level, the wavelength-modulated PABS based on the NANF is about 20 times more sensitive than the intensity-modulated PABS with the AR-HCF (see the manuscript under preparation, uploaded as research output).

15212220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212220.value: PABS could be applied to other platforms such as dual-nanoweb fibres, integrated photonic waveguides, and opto-mechano-fluidic resonators for developing novel stimulated Brillouin scattering-based devices and sensors. For example, theoretically the dual-nanofibres could achieve much stronger opto-acoustic interaction and potentially enhance PABS signal by orders of magnitude to enable ultra-sensitive gas sensors. The HCF-based PABS could be exploited for distributed gas as well as pressure/force and temperature sensing by examining the influence of the environment on the acoustic resonances of the microstructure along the optical fibres. We may apply research grants to continue research on the above aspects.

15212220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212220.value: Excitations of acoustic modes, i.e., oscillating air acoustic modes and capillary elastic modes, in different types of gas-filled hollow-core optical fibres are demonstrated via photoacoustic effect due to gas absorption of a modulated laser beam. The types of fibres we studied include single-ring anti-resonant nodeless hollow-core fibres, nested anti-resonant nodeless hollow-core fibres and photonic bandgap hollow-core fibres. The photoacoustic excitation is two to three orders of magnitude more efficient than electrostriction and radiation pressure excitation. These findings enable a highly sensitive spectroscopic method named photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy (PABS), which uses a modulated pump beam to excite acoustic resonances in a gas-filled hollow-core fibre and another probe beam to detect the acoustic resonances via optical fibre interferometry. As applications of PABS, we have demonstrated acoustic spectroscopy of the fibre microstructures as well as precision optical spectroscopy of gas molecules inside the hollow-core fibre. Acetylene detection at sub-ppb level has been demonstrated with 0.85-m-long nested anti-resonant nodeless hollow-core fibre. PABS has great potential for high sensitivity gas sensing and non-invasive fibre characterization.

15212720.value: In order to design a lighting system suitable for VLC and VLP, we will characterize indoor VLC multi-path channel by channel measurement and channel modeling. Based on joint optimization algorithms, we will explore a novel LED luminaire deployment to improve VLP/VLC performance while meeting the indoor illumination requirement at the same time. In order to develop a high-accuracy VLP scheme with no need of sending dedicated reference signals, we propose an indoor CSI-based VLP strategy by utilizing VLC channel estimation results. Based on the multi-path channel characteristics, we will try to extract the line-of-sight (LOS) components, conduct indoor VLP, and optimize system parameters, respectively. To evaluate the positioning accuracy of the CSI-based VLP scheme in a 4×4 multiple input multiple output (MIMO) configuration. In order to overcome the VLC multi-path effects caused by multiple LED sources and indoor reflections, we will investigate a location-based equalization (LBE) scheme to equalize the multi-path channel with no need of training symbols. We will also combine LBE with time domain hybrid modulation (TDHM), and investigate the real-time processing of LBE in the form of overlapped frequency domain equalizer (OFDE). To develop LBE algorithm in a VLC MIMO system and make comparisons between ZF and MMSE approaches, respectively. To design novel frame structures and signal formats based on current IEEE standard, which can simultaneously transmit VLP reference signals and VLC data signals in the same system. To develop collaborative strategies to mutually improve VLC performance with LBE, while improving VLP accuracy with CSI at the same time.

15212720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212720.value: Recently, motivated by widespread deployment of LEDs, visible light communication (VLC) has been a potential candidate for indoor wireless access. By encoding data into varying light intensity at a fast speed imperceptible to human eyes, LED luminaires can be used to transmit information. Since radio frequency (RF) spectrum is rapidly exhausted due to data traffic, LEDs can be potential wireless routers to support high-speed transmission via light. Also, VLC signal does not penetrate walls or cause electromagnetic interference, thus can be used in RF sensitive areas with data privacy. Visible light positioning (VLP) is another gift brought by LEDs. In future smart city, cars are automatically guided in basement parking; visitors are recommended the best route to their meeting room; for disabled, smart building may advice the location of barrier-free facilities. Due to attenuation of satellite signal, GPS is not accurate enough in indoor environments. This problem is especially serious in Hong Kong due to extremely crowded high buildings. LEDs are ideal positioning sensors to build indoor VLP systems. With no additional infrastructure, VLP features very high accuracy. For practical applications, achieving simultaneous multi-services of high-speed VLC and high-accuracy VLP is of crucial importance. However, current indoor VLC and VLP systems are designed independently and exclusively. There are quite few investigations to integrate both systems. In addition, multiple LEDs are usually adopted to provide sufficient and uniform illumination indoors. The multi-path signals coming from different LEDs and reflections caused by walls or ceiling tend to interfere with each other. Such multi-path effects will degrade both VLC and VLP system performance. In this work we aim to explore the following questions: • To achieve satisfactory indoor VLC and VLP performance, what is the good LED deployment? • How to achieve accurate indoor VLP with VLC channel state information (CSI)? • How to equalize VLC multi-path channel by utilizing receiver location obtained by VLP? • How to establish a cooperative relationship to benefit VLC and VLP with each other under the same system? To address these questions, we will investigate joint optimization schemes of LED deployment for both VLC and VLP. We will demonstrate an indoor VLP scheme by utilizing optical wireless CSI. We will also experimentally implement a location-based equalization scheme for VLC. Finally, a collaborative framework to achieve simultaneous VLC and VLP will be developed. This research is aligned with Government initiatives. It has both academic impact and practical applications. 近來，由於節能照明LED的廣泛部署，可見光通信（VLC）已成為室內無線接入的重要候選者。將數據編碼調製為人眼無法感知的快速光強變化，照明LED可同時用於傳輸信息。由於射頻（RF）頻譜迅速耗盡， LED可以成為潛在的無線路由器，以支持通過光的高速傳輸。而且，VLC信號不會穿透牆壁或引起電磁干擾，因此具有數據保密性，可用於RF敏感區域。 可見光定位（VLP）是LED帶來的另一項禮物。在未來的智慧城市中，VLP可自動在地下停車場引導汽車；建議參觀者到達會議室的最佳路線；提供殘疾人無障礙設施的位置。由於衛星信號的衰減，GPS在室內環境中不夠準確。香港高樓密集，這個問題尤為嚴重。 LED是構建室內VLP系統的理想定位傳感器，不必增加基礎設施，又具有很高的準確性。 對於實際應用而言，同時實現高速VLC和高精度VLP至關重要。但是，當前的室內VLC和VLP系統是獨立設計的。很少有研究可以集成這兩個系統。另外，通常採用多個LED以在室內提供足夠且均勻的照明。來自不同LED的多徑信號以及牆壁或天花板引起的反射往往會相互干擾。這種多徑效應將降低VLC和VLP系統性能。在這個項目中，我們將研究VLC和VLP的聯合優化部署方案。我們將利用光無線通道狀態信息（CSI）實現室內VLP，並實現基於位置的VLC均衡方案。最終開發一個同時實現VLC和VLP的協作框架。這項研究符合政府關於節能智慧城市的倡議，兼具學術影響和實際應用價值。

15212720.label: Realisation of objectives
15212720.value: Until now, we have successfully achieved the goals of this project. Both experimental and simulation work have been conducted to obtain significant results that align with the defined objectives. The project has progressed according to schedule, and we believe its completion contributes meaningfully to advancing visible light communication and positioning technologies. For Objective 1, we investigated a comprehensive methodology combining empirical channel characterization with theoretical optimization of LED deployment. We refined the transmitter and receiver modules using 3D-printed shields to achieve near-Lambertian radiation patterns. By measuring light intensity at various distances and angles, we applied nonlinear fitting tools to create an accurate channel model, validated through frequency-domain simulations. Based on this model, we used an inverse design approach to optimize LED placement by defining communication and positioning performance requirements first. A convex quadratic objective function was formulated to balance VLC and VLP needs, allowing us to calculate optimal LED number, location, power, and orientation. The design was verified for illumination compliance, inter-symbol interference (ISI) via root mean square delay spread analysis, and robustness against link blockage through spatial diversity evaluation. To overcome the limited modulation bandwidth of commercial phosphor-based LEDs (~10 MHz), which restricts VLC data rates, we fabricated high-bandwidth micro-LEDs. These include parallel mini/micro-LEDs with bandwidths from 85 MHz to 278 MHz, GaN-based single wetting layer micro-LEDs (1.025 GHz), and InGaN-based five-layer quantum dot micro-LEDs (up to 1.22 GHz). These components enabled the development of multiple high-speed VLC systems. For Objectives 2 and 3, we proposed a novel VLP strategy that leverages channel state information (CSI) extracted from VLC signals, eliminating the need for dedicated VLP signals. Each LED transmitter was assigned a unique orthogonal code as a spreading sequence. At the receiver, cross-correlation between received signals and known codes extracted CSI, from which received signal strength (RSS) values were derived. Trilateration was then applied to determine position. This scheme was tested in a multi-user environment with four LED transmitters, achieving 2 cm precision in a room of 1.5 m × 1.5 m × 0.9 m. However, asynchronous transmission in real-world applications can degrade the orthogonality of traditional codes, causing multiple access interference (MAI) that affects RSS accuracy and positioning quality. To mitigate this, we introduced a new OPRC code combining Hadamard codes with m-sequences to enhance orthogonality under asynchronous conditions. Additionally, we implemented a successive interference cancellation decoding (SICD) scheme, iteratively removing stronger signal interference to improve RSS estimation and positioning accuracy. We also proposed a multi-carrier orthogonal coding mechanism (MC-OCM) based on complete complementary (CC) codes. Due to their strong aperiodic correlation properties, CC codes effectively reduce both MAI and ISI caused by asynchronous and multipath transmissions, ensuring robust performance even under complex channel conditions. For Objectives 4 and 5, to overcome multipath effects caused by multiple LED sources and indoor reflections, we implemented a location-based equalization (LBE) scheme that equalizes the multipath channel without the need for training symbols. This method leverages the precise receiver coordinates obtained from the VLP system to achieve LBE. When the coordinates of transmitters and receivers are known, their geometrical relationship can be determined, and the VLC channel can be estimated according to distances and angles. Due to the characteristics of the VLC multipath channel (where real signal components in terms of optical intensity propagate and arrive at the receiver with different gains and time delays, without random coherent superposition as in RF systems), the improvement attributed to localization in LBE is better than that in RF counterparts. Because the VLC channel will change with the receiver's motion, we need to use an optical uplink to send the location information of the receiver to the transmitter to update the equalizer for improving the communication quality. Therefore, we proposed an optical uplink solution for VLC, which adopts a near-infrared vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) array as the transmitter for uplink. The mathematical model based on a modified Monte Carlo ray-tracing (MMCR) algorithm for VCSEL-based optical wireless communication (OWC) is presented, which takes into account both accuracy and time complexity for calculating channel characteristics such as power distribution, impulse response, error analysis, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). For demonstration, we adopted a 940-nm VCSEL array to establish LOS and NLOS systems after measuring the optoelectronic and bandwidth characteristics. Furthermore, multiple multi-carrier schemes are adopted to improve the OWC performance system based on a 940 nm VCSEL array, including uniform-loading orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), channel-coded OFDM, bit-loading/power-allocation OFDM, and OFDM access (OFDMA). Results show that OFDM can effectively decrease the ISI of the indoor channel and increase the data rate, and the bit/power-loading method achieves the highest 7.2 Gbps transmission with the bit error rate (BER) within the forward error correction (FEC). For Objectives 6 and 7, we proposed various integrated visible light communication and positioning (VLCP) schemes. These approaches effectively combine VLC and VLP within a single system, utilizing multiplexing techniques such as time division multiplexing (TDM) or code division multiplexing (CDM) to prevent signal interference between the two functionalities. This integration effectively reduces both deployment costs and system redundancy. In the CDM-based VLCP system, orthogonal spreading codes are assigned to different LED transmitters, with the correlation values between the received signals and the corresponding spreading codes used to recover both user data and positioning information. To ensure robust performance in asynchronous transmission environments, we first introduced an OPRC-based SICD scheme, followed by an MC-OCM based on CC codes. Additionally, we proposed a dual-domain multiplexing (DDM) scheme to enhance the user capacity of the VLCP system. We also developed a single-source VLCP system, where a maximum length sequence (MLS) is embedded within the transmitted data frame to support signal synchronization and extraction. The system utilizes binary phase shift keying (BPSK) modulation to encode data onto the optical intensity. At the receiver side, the RSS is used to simultaneously extract both communication data and positioning information. Experimental results validated the feasibility of this design, achieving error-free communication at a data rate of 1.21 kbps and an average positioning error of 3.40 cm within a 30 cm × 30 cm area. This demonstrates the capability of transmitting both VLP reference signals and VLC data signals simultaneously using a single light source. Furthermore, we proposed an underwater optical wireless communication and positioning (UOWC-UOWP) solution for underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs). A dual-hop architecture was introduced to extend the limited coverage range in UWSNs with mobile nodes. The system consists of a graded-index plastic optical fiber (GI-POF) link and a wireless optical link. Specifically, mini-LEDs provide high-speed and flexible uplink transmission, while high-power LEDs enable downlink communication and positioning. When locating underwater users, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the communication link can be improved by adjusting the illumination angle or focusing the light source. In conclusion, the proposed collaborative indoor visible light communication and positioning schemes have met the objective of this project, which builds a bridge between VLC and VLP. These advancements not only pave the way for future research but also demonstrate practical applications in smart environments, contributing to the development of more efficient and reliable communication and positioning technologies.

15212720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212720.value: The project initiated by developing a comprehensive methodology for LED luminaire deployment, combining empirical channel characterization with theoretical optimization. A pivotal achievement lies in pushing the boundaries of high-speed VLC. The project successfully developed high-bandwidth InGaN quantum dot green Micro-LEDs, a crucial step in overcoming traditional LED bandwidth limitations (as detailed in Journal Paper No. 11). Coupled with advanced artificial neural network equalizers, the research demonstrated impressive data rates, achieving up to 8.75 Gbps with single-pixel blue micro-LEDs (Journal Paper No. 14) and an experimental 16.6 Gbps SDM-WDM visible light communication link using tricolor mini-LEDs (Journal Paper No. 15). These results emphatically prove the immense potential of innovative LED sources and sophisticated equalization methods in drastically increasing VLC data throughput for future high-capacity demands. Addressing multipath effects, a location-based equalization (LBE) scheme was successfully implemented, enabling channel equalization without training symbols by leveraging precise VLP-derived receiver coordinates. Crucially, an optical uplink solution using 940-nm VCSEL arrays and advanced multi-carrier schemes like bit-loading/power-allocation OFDM achieved a 7.2 Gbps transmission, ensuring high-speed feedback for dynamic LBE updates (Journal Paper No. 12). In the realm of high-accuracy VLP, a novel CSI-based strategy was introduced, extracting positioning information directly from VLC signals without dedicated reference signals. Based on a multi-carrier orthogonal coding mechanism, the superior correlation properties of complete complementary (CC) codes are used to achieved interference-free transmission from multiple access interference and inter-symbol interference. Consequently, it delivered sub-3 cm average positioning error even in challenging asynchronous and multipath propagation environments (Journal Paper No. 2). The application of successive interference cancellation decoding in asynchronous code division multiplexing-based networks (Journal Paper No. 3) further enhanced positioning accuracy and overall system performance by effectively mitigating multi-user interference. The project developed various integrated VLCP schemes, employing multiplexing techniques to prevent signal interference and reduce deployment costs. This included a multi-user VLCP system based on dual-domain multiplexing scheme (Journal Paper No. 10) and a single-source VLCP system achieving error-free communication at 1.21 kbps with 3.40 cm positioning accuracy (Journal Paper No. 4). A pioneering underwater optical wireless communication and positioning (UOWC-UOWP) solution extended these capabilities to underwater wireless sensor networks, demonstrating improved SNR by adjusting illumination angles (Journal Paper No. 9). These advancements collectively bridge VLC and VLP, demonstrating practical applications for smart environments and paving the way for more efficient and reliable optical wireless technologies.

15212720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212720.value: The project's strong foundation in high-speed, multi-user VLC/VLP opens several promising avenues for future development. A primary focus will be enhancing adaptability and robustness in dynamic, real-world environments. This includes developing advanced LBE and CSI-based VLP schemes that can dynamically adjust to receiver mobility and varying channel conditions, potentially leveraging deep learning for real-time channel prediction and equalization without constant recalibration. Further research will explore seamless integration with other wireless technologies, such as RF and LiFi, to create hybrid communication and positioning networks, ensuring ubiquitous connectivity and localization accuracy in complex indoor and outdoor settings. Miniaturization of VLC transceivers and development of more energy-efficient components, perhaps incorporating advanced materials, will be crucial for IoT and wearable applications. The proposed course of action involves continued algorithmic innovation, building larger-scale experimental testbeds to simulate diverse deployment scenarios, and actively contributing to standardization efforts to accelerate practical adoption and commercialization of collaborative VLC/VLP systems.

15212720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212720.value: This research project is essentially about making our everyday light bulbs smarter, turning them into invisible, high-speed internet broadcasters and precise indoor navigation tools. Imagine your office or home lights not only illuminating the room but also simultaneously delivering super-fast internet to your devices and telling your phone your exact location, even where GPS signals can't reach. The nature of this research lies in using visible light, which is safe and abundant, to create a new kind of wireless network. Its significance is huge because it offers a solution to the growing demand for data and accurate indoor positioning, especially in crowded spaces like hospitals, malls, or factories. Unlike Wi-Fi, visible light communication (VLC) doesn't interfere with radio signals, making it ideal for sensitive environments. The value of this work is in creating a dual-purpose, energy-efficient, and secure wireless system that could revolutionize how we connect and navigate indoors, paving the way for advanced smart environments and seamless augmented reality experiences.

15213020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15213020.value: 用於鋼橋面鋪裝的高性能瀝青膠砂的開發：從多尺度建模到足尺測試

15213020.label: Project Objectives
15213020.value: Overall Goal. Landmark bridges such as the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, Tsing Ma Bridge, and Stonecutters Bridge are engineering wonders in the world and significant transport assets in the region. These bridges share one common characteristic: They are all paved with an unconventional asphalt material called “mastic asphalt (MA)”. MA is a voidless, self-compacted asphalt mixture that tightly seals steel bridge decks against corrosion, and simultaneously withstands heavy traffic loads and large deformation induced by strong winds and temperature variations. MA mixture currently used on these bridges is based on a fixed recipe design, which specifies the use of a large portion of natural asphalt from a designated single source and specific types and proportions of fine and coarse aggregates. Although 21 years of experience from the Tsing Ma Bridge indicate that the original recipe is generally successful, the recipe design has two problems. (1) Heavy reliance on natural asphalt from a single source may not be sustainable. (2) The physicochemical properties of neat asphalt binder used 21 years ago may not be the same as those of asphalt binders used today. Hence, the overall goal of this study is to identify the working mechanisms of MA and develop alternative MA formula with high performance, excellent durability, and less dependence on natural asphalt. Landmark bridges such as the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, Tsing Ma Bridge, and Stonecutters Bridge are engineering wonders in the world and significant transport assets in the region. These bridges share one common characteristic: They are all paved with an unconventional asphalt material called “mastic asphalt (MA)”. Hence, the overall goal of this study is to identify the working mechanisms of MA and develop alternative MA formula with high performance, excellent durability, and less dependence on natural asphalt.

15213020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213020.value: A special asphalt mixture, “mastic asphalt (MA),” is used on some landmark bridges in Hong Kong and nearby region, including the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, Tsing Ma Bridge, and Stonecutters Bridge. MA is a quite unique material as compared with conventional hot-mix asphalt (HMA). It is voidless and self-compacted, protecting the mega infrastructures against corrosion and simultaneously accommodating large deformation and withstanding heavy traffic loads. In Hong Kong, MA is based on a fixed recipe. The asphaltic cement is made of 70 per cent of natural Trinidad Lake Asphalt (TLA) and 30 per cent of neat asphalt. Although 21 years of experience from the Tsing Ma Bridge indicate that MA has satisfactory performance, several critical questions are raised. Can viable alternatives be found to replace the TLA in MA? Can MA formula with even better performance be developed? Can MA be extended to infrastructures other than bridges? Answers to these questions are meaningful. Following the general success of using MA on the Tsing Ma Bridge, TLA—a non-renewable natural material, has been increasingly used around the world especially in China. Alternatives need to be found to prepare for the eventual depletion of TLA. More severe weather conditions caused by climate change and increasing traffic loads call for more durable MA materials in the future. This study aims to address the three raised questions. It starts with discovering the fundamental working mechanisms of MA. The resurfacing of MA on the Tsing Ma Bridge during the study period offers a precious opportunity to examine the long-term property evolution of MA. Multiscale characterization, modeling and simulation of various MA formula provide additional insights into their working mechanisms, based on which high-performance MA formula less or not dependent on TLA will be developed. Systematic laboratory and full-scale tests will be performed to further assess and verify the performance of developed MA formula. As shown in the methodology part of the proposal, new and innovative methods will be used for multiscale characterization and analysis, accelerated aging treatments, and tests. The research is anticipated to (1) generate valuable data on the long-term behavior and performance of MA, (2) gain scientific insights into MA working mechanisms, (3) develop high-performance MA formula less dependent on natural asphalt, (4) simplify test methods for MA in bridge paving applications, and (5) identify wider applications of MA.
