15213020.label: Realisation of objectives
15213020.value: The proposed research objectives have been fully achieved in this study through comprehensive laboratory tests, numerical analysis, and site trials. Detailed approaches to achieving the objectives are outlines as follows. (1) Overall goal: MA is a voidless, self-compacted asphalt mixture that tightly seals steel bridge decks against corrosion, and simultaneously withstands heavy traffic loads and large deformation induced by strong winds and temperature variations. The overall goal of this study is to identify the working mechanisms of MA and develop alternative MA formula with high performance, excellent durability, and less dependence on natural asphalt. Achievement of the overall goal. In this study, we attempted to use two types of liquid polymers--epoxy and polyurethane--to modify asphalt binder. Such liquid polymers were introduced to SBS polymer-modified asphalt binder. During the material production and construction stage, such liquid polymers act as lubricants to enhance the workability of the asphalt binder. After construction, such liquid polymer reacts into nanoscale particles, which harden the asphalt mixture. The use of liquid polymer was successfully proved through laboratory studies and site trials. (2) Objective: To investigate the long-term behavior and performance of mastic asphalt (MA) used on Tsing Ma Bridge in Hong Kong, which is scheduled to be resurfaced during the study period, and to evaluate the MA performance on other bridges such as the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge and Stonecutters Bridge. Achievement of this objective. With the help of Highways Department in Hong Kong, we have successfully retrieved MA samples from Tsing Ma Bridge in Hong Kong. We found that a critical factor that ensures the success MA pavement on Tsing Ma Bridge is that asphalt binder is little aged, due to negligible void content. (3) Objective: To develop different formula of MA and characterize the developed MA materials of different compositions and different aging states at the nanoscale (< 100 nm), microscale (100 nm to 100 µm), mesoscale (100 µm to 5 mm), and macroscale (>5 mm). Achievement of this objective. We have developed different formula of MA and found that epoxy is better than PU due to its better workability. We have analyzed the asphalt binders and mixtures using the two types of the liquid polymers using a variety of characterization tools, including fluorescent microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and micro-CT. We have also tested the macro properties of the binders and mixtures using dynamic shear rheometer (DSR) and universal test machine (UTM). (4) Objective: To model and simulate the mechanical performance of the characterized MA formula. Achievement of this objective. We have modeled and simulated the mechanical performance of the MA materials. For binders, we used colloidal models. For mixtures, we used discrete element models and finite element models. (5) Objective: To perform laboratory and reduced scale tests on MA of different designs for performance evaluation and improvement. Achievement of this objective. We have performed a large number of laboratory tests (>120) and performed three site trials, with the generous help of the largest asphalt material producer and contractor in Hong Kong--K Wha. Asphalt. The industry partner even specially designed and built an industrial-scale mixer for this project. The industry sponsor believes that this project has high potentials. (6) Objective: The outcomes of this research are insights into the working mechanisms of this unconventional asphalt materials and improved MA designs with better performance and sustainability. The new MA designs are expected to better serve the functional and structural needs of steel bridges, with the potential to be used on non-bridge applications where strong bonding and self-compaction of asphalt mixtures are desired. Achievement of this objective. We found that the fatigue life of this material is more than 10 times of the typical fatigue life of conventional asphalt materials. We performed life-cycle cost analysis of this new materials. With this new material, highway pavements can be built much thinner yet still achieve a remarkable long life. This material has high potential.

15213020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213020.value: We would like to sincerely thank RGC for providing us the opportunity to carry out this study. With the funding support, we have conducted an extensive investigation on this topic and make some significant findings, which are summarized as follows. (1) We developed workable new MA materials that does not rely on high-temperature production yet can achieve remarkable durability. Their fatigue performance is more than 10 times of conventional asphalt materials. (2) We performed life-cycle cost analysis and found that the new MA materials can help the highway agencies significantly reduce life-cycle costs. (3) We found a new mechanism that leads to asphalt pavement fatigue. This finding has significant academic value.

15213020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213020.value: We sincerely believe the new materials developed in this study has high potential to change the practices of road construction. We will try to develop full-scale test and also site trials to prove the workability and cost savings of this materials.

15213020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213020.value: Hong Kong’s iconic bridges, such as the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge and Tsing Ma Bridge, depend on mastic asphalt (MA) for durable, impermeable steel deck paving. However, the current MA formulation—relying heavily on non-renewable Trinidad Lake asphalt (TLA)—faces challenges from changing material properties, climate change, and sustainability concerns. This research focused on developing and evaluating innovative MA materials that reduce reliance on TLA, exploring alternatives such as polymer-modified asphalts and recycled materials. Systematic laboratory and full-scale testing were performed to identify optimal formulations for long-term performance under Hong Kong’s demanding conditions. Scientific investigation was performed to examine MA’s working mechanisms and address causes of premature failures. This was accompanied with industrial-scale production and assessment. This research successfully developed new MA materials that do not rely on high temperature and have remarkable fatigue performance. The fatigue life of such materials is more than 10 times of the fatigue life of conventional materials. Life-cycle cost analysis indicates that this new material has high potential to be widely used.

15213920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213920.value: Fibrous materials that allows liquid flow in one direction, but repels liquid in the opposite direction have many applications including sportswear and protective clothing. In this project, we propose to mimic the directional flow property of the skin of mammals by creating spatially distributed stimuli (i.e. pH and temperature) responsive gradient wettability channels, acting like “sweating glands”, across a predominantly superhydrophobic fabric. As such, moderately acidic and warm sweat can flow easily from its inner side to the outer surface through the responsive gradient wettability channels and the fabric is repellent to external water. If successful, we will be able to fabricate water repellent fabrics with directional liquid water flow rate far exceeding the moisture vapor transmission rate of best commercial breathable fabrics such as Gore-Tex. This concept can be further extended to develop directional flow materials for many other applications such as wound dressing, oil–water separation, geotechnical engineering, flexible microfluidics and fuel cell membranes. The associated theoretical study will improve our understanding on the mechanisms of directional capillary flow and liquid repellency across fibrous materials, which are essential to the optimum design of fibrous materials for different applications. 允许液体沿一个方向流动但排斥另一方向液体的纤维材料在运动服、防护服及其他许多领域都有应用。在该项目中，我们建议通过在超疏水性的织物上创建空间分布的、具刺激（即pH和温度）响应的、梯度可湿性通道来模拟哺乳动物的皮肤汗腺, 从而实現定向流动特性。这样，中等酸性和体温的汗液可以通过具响应性的梯度可湿性通道从织物内侧流到外表面，但织物对外部水具有排斥力。 如果成功的话，我们将能够制造出单向流防水织物, 其液态水透过率远超过最佳商用防水透气性织物（如Gore-Tex）的水蒸气透过率。这个概念可以进一步扩展，以开发用于许多其他应用的定向流动材料，例如伤口敷料，油水分离材料，土工材料，柔性微流体和燃料电池膜。相关的理论研究将增进我们对纤维材料的定向毛细流动和拒液性机理的理解，这对于针对不同应用的纤维材料的最佳设计至关重要。

15213920.label: Realisation of objectives
15213920.value: We have accomplished the following objectives: For the first objective: ∙ A novel polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based fabrication method for skin-like directional liquid flow and water repellent fabric was developed. The method adopted relatively mature technologies such as dip coating and screen printing, which is economical, eco-friendly and can achieve industrial production. ∙ A poly(2-(N-3-Sulfopropyl-N, N-dimethyl ammonium)ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAPS) -based skin-like temperature-responsive fabric was developed. By applying the temperature responsive polymer PDMAPS onto the surface of the skin-like fabric, the fabric exhibited a higher liquid transport rate at higher temperatures and better water repellency at lower temperatures. ∙ A poly(acrylamide-co-acrylonitrile) [poly(AAm-co-AN)]-based non-ionic skin-like temperature-responsive fabric was developed. This is the first successful preparation of a non-ionic upper critical solution temperature (UCST)-type temperature-responsive fabric. Compared with the PDMAPS-based temperature-responsive fabric, this fabric is more difficult to prepare, but the transition temperature is tuneable and exhibited stability against electrolyte concentration. This project proposed a stable fabrication method for poly(AAm-co-AN)-based skin-like temperature-responsive fabric. ∙ Poly(2-(Dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) and poly(N-[3-(Trimethoxysilyl)propyl]ethylenediamine) (PTPED) was grafted to the skin-like fabric for preparing pH-responsive skin-like fabric. These skin-like fabric exhibited pH-responsive wettability that hydrophilic at acidic environments and hydrophobic at alkaline environment. However, their pH-response range was wide and the pH variations on the skin surface is not enough to cause a change in their wettabiliity. For the second objective: ∙ the directional flow phenomena in natural systems were studied, including sweating glands on human skin, water transmission in plants, and substance transporting on biological membranes. ∙ Structures of directional flow systems and their directional water transporting mechanism were explored. Laid a theoretical foundation for further research on directional water transporting fabric. For the third objective: ∙ The mechanisms of directional fluid flow throw the gradient wettability channels spatially distributed across the predominantly superhydrophobic fabric were studied by modeling. The process parameters of preparing the skin-like fabric were improved according to the mechanisms. For the forth objective: ∙ Various properties of the stimuli responsive fabrics were characterized, including the contact angle of different areas, hydrostatic pressure of the fabric, water transmission rate, and air permeability. The results show that this kind of skin-like fabric has an excellent water transmission rate, better than the commercial breathable fabrics such as Gore-Tex. Furthermore, the fabric has high hydrostatic pressure and air permeability, which means the fabric is breathable but water repellent. ∙ The effect of the stimuli responsive polymers on the changes of pore size in the fabric, directional fluid flow rate, reverse liquid repellency and breakthrough pressure were investigated.

15213920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213920.value: ∙ Developed a skin-like fabric directional liquid flow and water repellent fabric using a new Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based fabrication method. In PVA-based fabrication method, the PVA aqueous solution was printed onto the surface of cotton fabric by screen printing before the hydrophobic treatment. The hydrophobic treatment was carried out by dip coating a commercial non-fluorine hydrophobic agent. The printed PVA prevented the covered area from contacting the hydrophobic agent during the hydrophobic treatment. After hot washing, the PVA removed, gradient wettability channels formed on the hydrophobic fabric. Water can be directionally transported through the gradient wettability channels while the outer surface of the fabric is water resistant. This method adopted relatively mature technologies such as dip coating and screen printing, which is economical, eco-friendly and can achieve industrial production. This work has been patented, A Scalable Method for Producing Durable “Skin-like” Directional Flow Moisture Management Fabric, China Patent Application: 202110879048.4. ∙ A PDMAPS-based stimuli responsive skin-like fabric was developed by grafting zwitterionic UCST-type temperature-responsive polymer PDMAPS onto the surface of the gradient wettability channel areas of the skin-like fabric. The effect of the PDMAPS coating on the wettability, water transport property, hydrostatic pressure, and air permeability of the fabric was explored. The mechanism of the temperature-responsive directional liquid flow property was discussed. This work has been published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 16(8), 10960-10968. ∙ A method for preparing poly(AAm-co-AN) stimuli responsive fabric was explored. The non-ionic UCST-type temperature-responsive polymer, poly(AAm-co-AN) was grafted onto the cotton knitted fabric for the first time via a novel site-specific grafting method. The patent of this method is prepared for publication. ∙ A poly(AAm-co-AN)-based stimuli responsive skin-like fabric was prepared. The effect of the mixed silane solution ratio on the wettability of the grafted fabric, the effect of the poly(AAm-co-AN) solution ratio on the transition temperature were explored. The surface morphology, chemical compounds, air permeability, handle, stimuli responsiveness of the fabric were also investigated. The manuscript of this work is prepared for publication.

15213920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213920.value: ∙ To achieve industrial production of skin-like fabric using PVA-based fabrication method, the primary challenge is improving the penetration of PVA solution through the fabric through the mesh printing screen. Further research could focus on optimizing the PVA solution formulation. Using PVA solution with lower molecular weight for printing may improve the penetration of the solution. Additionally, since PVA solution becomes viscous due to self-crosslinking during printing, additives could be introduced to reduce hydrogen bonding, such as urea. Foaming during PVA printing may affect quality, so defoamers could be added to mitigate this issue. ∙ For the stimuli responsive fabric, we can develop a new industrial process for grafting the stimuli responsive polymers. For the grafting process, thermal initiation and crosslinking could be utilized, allowing conventional dip coating and curing processes to graft the polymer onto the fabric surface, enabling large-scale production of the fabrics.

15213920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213920.value: ∙ The skin-like stimuli responsive fabric prepared in this project are novel smart moisture management fabrics. The development of smart moisture management fabrics holds significant potential for improving personal thermal and moisture comfort, particularly in extreme environments where conventional textiles fail to adapt dynamically. This study developed skin-like stimuli responsive fabrics, proposing a novel thermal and moisture management textile that addresses key limitations of traditional moisture management fabrics. ∙ The novel fabrication method proposed in this project provides a general strategy for preparing this class of stimuli responsive textiles, such as PVA-based fabrication method and site-specific grafting approach. The proposed fabrication approaches demonstrate promising scalability for industrial production, thereby facilitating the market translation of this type of smart textiles.

15214320.label: Project Objectives
15214320.value: Demonstrate the resistance ability of suspended circulating tumor cells to fluid shear stress during hematogenous dissemination. Tumor cells metastasize to distant organs mainly through hematogenous dissemination and the frequency of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in vasculature is correlated with patient survival. It is thus important to elucidate the roles of critical factors in the survival of CTCs during hematogenous dissemination. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that mechanical factors play important roles in tumor metastasis. CTCs experience considerable levels of fluid shear stress in suspension during hematogenous dissemination, which could be a key factor of cell survival. However, the resistance of suspended CTCs to fluid shear stress remains less understood. To address this problem, a circulatory system will be developed to explore the influence of fluid shear stress. The distribution of shear stress and tumor cells within the tubing will be simulated. The survival of suspended and adherent breast cancer cells with differential malignancy and shear-resistant cells in fluid shear stress will be compared. The relationship between shear resistance and malignancy will be established. To relate shear resistance to the unique properties of tumor cells, suspended tumor cells will be treated under uniform shear stress. We expect that physiological levels of fluid shear stress eliminate the majority of suspended but not adherent tumor cells. A subpopulation of CTCs survive and resist fluid shear stress. These expected outcomes will highlight the critical roles of fluid shear stress in the survival of suspended tumor cells during hematogenous dissemination and demonstrate the resistance ability of a subpopulation of CTCs to blood shear stress. Elucidate the roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the resistance of suspended CTCs to fluid shear stress. Adherent cells sense mechanical stimulations via mechanosensitive proteins, including Piezo1 and YAP/TAZ. Our preliminary data show that a subpopulation of suspended CTCs persist and exhibit resistance to blood shear stress they experience during hematogenous dissemination. However, it remains unclear how fluid shear stress influences the survival of suspended tumor cells. In particular, the survival mechanisms underlying the resistance to fluid shear stress and the roles of Piezo1 and YAP/TAZ are unknown. To address these questions, the influence of shear stress on Piezo1 and YAP/TAZ will be examined. Their expressions will be compared between breast cancer cells with differential malignancy and shear-resistant cells. The effects of Piezo1 and YAP/TAZ on the resistance of CTCs to shear stress will be elucidated. Further, whether Piezo1 affects shear resistance through YAP/TAZ will be explored. Importantly, the proteins with which activated YAP/TAZ interact in the nucleus will be identified between suspended and adherent tumor cells, including p73 and TEADs. The binding of YAP/TAZ with target proteins will be compared between shear-resistant cells and breast cancer cells. The functional roles of p73 and its interaction with YAP in shear resistance will be examined. We expect that fluid shear stress eliminates the majority of suspended but not adherent tumor cells through Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling, low activation of which underpins the resistance of CTCs to shear stress. These expected outcomes highlight the unique mechanotransduction and resistance mechanism of suspended CTCs in vasculature. Elucidate the therapeutic roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the resistance of CTCs to fluid shear stress and their clinical relevance. It is clinically challenging to eradicate disseminated tumor cells for preventing metastasis. We hypothesize that suspended CTCs sense fluid shear stress through Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling. However, their therapeutic roles in tumor cell resistance to shear flow and their clinical implication remain unclear. To answer the questions, Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling will be activated or inhibited in shear-resistant cells, cancer stem cells, and breast cancer cells. The intravascular survival of these cells will be examined in vivo. The effect on the formation of metastatic tumors will be also tested and compared. Further, the activities of Piezo1, YAP/TAZ, and p73 will be examined in patient-derived CTCs. The correlation between their expressions and patient survival will be established. We expect that the activation of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling significantly overcomes the resistance of CTCs to blood shear stress and suppresses the formation of metastatic tumors. The activity of this signaling in primary CTCs is correlated with patient outcomes. These findings demonstrate the therapeutic roles of the resistance mechanism in eradicating shear-resistant CTCs and the clinical significance.

15214320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214320.value: Tumor cells disseminate to distant organs through blood circulation and the frequency of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is correlated with patient survival. Although many CTCs become apoptotic in vasculature, a subpopulation of them persist and resist the destruction of blood circulation and eventually grow into lethal metastatic tumors. Therefore, unveiling the critical factors underlying the survival of CTCs in vasculature is important to facilitate the development of new therapeutic strategies for eradicating resistant CTCs and preventing metastasis. Except biochemical factors, mechanical cues play important roles in tumor metastasis. Suspended CTCs experience considerable levels of fluid shear stress in blood circulation, which could induce substantial cell apoptosis. It is known that adherent tumor cells sense shear stress via mechanosensitive proteins that influences their functions. However, the effect of blood shear stress on the survival of suspended CTCs remains less understood. In particular, the mechanotransduction mechanism underlying the resistance of suspended tumor cells to fluid shear stress is unknown. The therapeutic roles of the resistance mechanism in eradicating shear-resistant CTCs and the clinical relevance remain elusive. This project will address whether and how suspended tumor cells resist the destruction of fluid shear stress. We will evaluate: 1) the resistance of suspended CTCs to fluid shear stress in vasculature; 2) the roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the shear resistance of suspended CTCs; 3) the therapeutic roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the resistance of CTCs to fluid shear stress and the clinical relevance. We expect that suspended CTCs resist fluid shear stress through Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling, activation of which eradicates shear-resistant CTCs and prevents metastasis. This project studies metastasis from the biomechanical perspective and will demonstrate that suspended but not adherent tumor cells resist shear stress in blood circulation through Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling. Activating this survival mechanism overcomes shear resistance ability and suppresses metastasis, which has promising therapeutic roles and will facilitate the development of novel mechanomedicines against this signaling for eradicating shear-resistant CTCs and preventing metastasis. This research is potentially at the edge of a breakthrough that stresses the unique resistance mechanism of suspended CTCs and may lead the evolution of cancer therapeutics into a new paradigm that eliminates shear-resistant CTCs by targeting the mechanotransduction mechanism, which will benefit cancer patients. The major findings will support the notion that cancer may be not only a genetic but also ‘mechanical’ disease, which will transform our traditional views on cancer and considerably push the boundaries of cancer research. 腫瘤細胞通過血液迴圈擴散到遠端器官，且迴圈腫瘤細胞的出現機率與病人存活率相關。雖然許多迴圈腫瘤細胞在血管中已經凋亡，但是仍然有一小部分腫瘤細胞可以抵抗血液迴圈的破壞並最終產生致命的轉移腫瘤。所以，揭示迴圈腫瘤細胞在血液中的存活機理對於開發新型靶向具有抵抗力的迴圈腫瘤細胞及預防轉移極為重要。 除了生化因素外，力學因素在腫瘤轉移中扮演重要角色。懸浮迴圈腫瘤細胞在血液中承受相當大的流體剪切應力，這種應力可以引起大量的細胞凋亡。眾所周知，貼壁腫瘤細胞可以通過力敏感蛋白感知剪切應力，而這會影響細胞生命活動。然而，血流剪切應力對於懸浮迴圈腫瘤細胞存活的影響還不清楚，對懸浮腫瘤細胞感知並抵抗流體剪切的力學轉導機制一無所知，且這種機制在靶向對於剪切力有抵抗力的迴圈腫瘤細胞中的作用及相關的臨床意義還不清晰。本項目將研究懸浮腫瘤細胞如何抵抗流體剪切應力的破壞，包括1）評估迴圈腫瘤細胞對血流剪切應力的抵抗能力；2）Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73通路在迴圈腫瘤細胞抵抗剪切應力中的作用；3）Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73通路的治療作用及臨床價值。預期懸浮迴圈腫瘤細胞通過Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73信號通路抵制流體剪切應力，而啟動該通路可以靶向並清除抗剪切力的迴圈腫瘤細胞及預防腫瘤轉移。 本項目從生物力學角度研究腫瘤轉移，將證實懸浮而非貼壁腫瘤細胞可以通過Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73通路抵抗血流剪切應力。啟動該存活機制可以克服腫瘤細胞的抗剪切能力並抑制轉移，這將促進開發新型靶向該信號通路及預防腫瘤轉移的力醫學手段。本研究將有可能帶來新的研究突破，強調懸浮迴圈腫瘤細胞抵抗機制的獨特性，引領腫瘤治療進入新的範式，即通過靶向力學轉導機制來清除抗流體剪切的迴圈腫瘤細胞，最終使癌症病人受惠。本項目的主要發現將支持一個突破性的觀點，即癌症不僅是一個基因而且是“力學”疾病，這將極大轉變人們對於癌症的傳統看法並大力推進癌症研究。

15214320.label: Realisation of objectives
15214320.value: Aim 1: Demonstrate the resistance ability of suspended circulating tumor cells to fluid shear stress during hematogenous dissemination. Results achieved: Tumor cells experience considerable levels of fluid shear stress during hematogenous dissemination. We have developed a microfluidic system to simulate blood shear flow in vitro. The average shear stress within venous and arterial circulation is reported to be 0.5-4 dynes/cm² and 4-30 dynes/cm², respectively. The duration of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in the vascular system is within 12 h. Therefore, fluid shear stress within 20 dyne/cm² and the circulation time within 12 h were adopted in this project. The results show that the viability of suspended CTCs gradually decreased under the given shear stress along with the circulating time. Cell survival gradually decreased when the shear stress increased from 0, 2, 8, to 20 dyne/cm2 at the same time points. This finding was further confirmed by PI/Annexin V assay via flow cytometry. Since suspended tumor cells experienced non-uniform fluid shear stress within the microfluidic system, we further circulated these cells in another microplate system that could produce uniform shear stress. The results show that the viability of suspended CTCs decreased along with the increase of shear stress magnitude and circuiting time. Similar phenomena were observed in five types of breast cancer cell lines. Further, fibrin-selected CSCs exhibited survival advantages under the same fluid shear flow condition compared to conventional tumor cells. These results suggest that fluid shear stress eliminates the majority of suspended CTCs. Nevertheless, there are always a minor subpopulation of CTCs that can survive and persist, suggesting that suspended CTCs have the ability to resist fluid shear stress during hematogenous dissemination. These cells could contain the “seeds” that eventually generate metastatic tumors. This objective was fully achieved. Aim 2: Elucidate the roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the resistance of suspended CTCs to fluid shear stress. 1. Elucidate the effects of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ on the survival of shear-resistant CTCs. Results achieved: The results show that the mRNA expression of PIEZO1 was upregulated by 4-40 fold in suspended breast cancer cells after the treatment in 2 and 20 dyne/cm2 fluid shear flow for 12 h, while the expression of PIEZO2 was only upregulated by 2-fold. The western blotting results showed similar findings at the protein level in suspended tumor cells when the cells were subjected to fluid shear flow. Furthermore, we examined the role of Piezo1 in the survival of suspended breast cancer cells under shear stress. In the presence of fluid shear flow, silencing PIEZO1 with siRNA in suspended MCF-7 cells notably improved cell viability, whereas overexpressing Piezo1 with mPiezo1-IRES-eGFP plasmid inhibited cell survival. Using Fluo-4 Ca2+ fluorescent dye, the calcium concentration within MCF-7 cells was gradually upregulated with the increasing magnitude of shear flow. Inhibiting PIEZO1 reduced the calcium entry of suspended breast cancer cells under shear flow. The activation of PIEZO1 in suspended cells facilitated the calcium entry into the cells under fluid shear flow. Activating Piezo1 via Yoda1 inhibits the viability under fluid shear flow. The viability of suspended tumor cells in fluid shear stress was rescued via depleting calcium by chelator EGTA. YAP protein showed a significant nuclear accumulation, which was shear-stress-dependent. The subcellular localization of YAP/TAZ are largely regulated through phosphorylating specific sites, such as Ser127 (Ser89 for TAZ). Our findings showed that YAP Ser127 phosphorylation and TAZ Ser89 decreased in suspended cells under shearing, suggesting that fluid shear stress promotes YAP nuclear translocation in suspended tumor cells. Further, inhibiting YAP enhanced the viability of suspended MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 under fluid shear stress, while activating YAP/TAZ decreased tumor cell survival. These results suggest that YAP/TAZ activation promotes the fluid shear stress induced-apoptosis of suspended CTCs. 2. Examine the interaction of nuclear YAP/TAZ with p73 and the roles in the resistance of suspended CTCs to fluid shear stress. We further investigated how YAP/TAZ mediates shear-induced cell apoptosis and assumed that p73 might play a role. Fluid shear stress upregulated p73 at both mRNA and protein levels in suspended CTCs. p73 was mainly distributed within the nucleus. We next elucidated how shear-induced nuclear YAP promoted the apoptosis of non-adhered tumor cells. Fluid shear stress had no detectable influence on the phosphorylation of YAP at Ser94, which is required for YAP-TEAD interaction. Instead, YAP phosphorylation was reduced at Ser127 but elevated at Tyr357, which could enhance the binding affinity of YAP to p73 and promote YAP nuclear retention. The co-localization between YAP and p73 but not TEADs progressively increased. Further, shear-induced YAP bound to p73 and PUMA but not TEADs. Expressing YAP with mutation of Tyr357 blocked the shear-induced co-localization between YAP and p73. These findings suggest that shear-induced YAP binds to p73 but not TEADs through c-Abl-mediated phosphorylation at Tyr357 in non-adhered tumor cells. Overexpressing YAP with mutation of Tyr357 disrupted the binding of YAP to p73 and significantly elevated the survival of non-adhered tumor cells under fluid shear stress. Inhibiting c-Abl suppressed the phosphorylation of YAP at Tyr357 and YAP-p73 interaction, which further protected non-adhered tumor cells from shear-induced apoptosis. In addition, YAP-p73 interaction co-activated the downstream pro-apoptotic genes, including PUMA. Silencing PUMA or p73 promoted the survival of non-adhered cells under fluid shear stress, while the overexpression reduced cell viability. These results suggest that the interaction of YAP with p73 under fluid shear stress promotes the transcription of pro-apoptotic genes, which further induces the apoptosis of non-adhered tumor cells. This objective was fully achieved. Aim 3: Elucidate the therapeutic roles of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling in the resistance of CTCs to fluid shear stress and their clinical relevance. We further explored whether this previously unappreciated mechanosensing signaling could be utilized to sensitize CTCs to shear-induced apoptosis and thus suppress tumor metastasis. To test this idea, the recently developed Matador assay was used to measure the cytotoxicity of CTCs in circulation. YAP activation reduces the survival of CTCs in vasculature but promotes many other functions after the re-adhesion and arrival at the metastasized organs, including cell proliferation and motility. Therefore, stable modulation of YAP activity could complicate its overall effect on tumor metastasis. To avoid this issue, p-Nluc-labelled breast cancer cells were transfected with doxycycline-inducible YAP plasmid to continuously activate YAP in the consistent presence of doxycycline. After removing the induction medium, YAP expression was restored to the basal level. Therefore, this approach could be utilized to transiently activate YAP in CTCs only within the vasculature. To test this effect, MDA-MB-231 cells with this plasmid were pre-treated with or without doxycycline in vitro and then injected intravenously into mice. After 12-h circulation, the number of viable tumor cells was lower in the cells with doxycycline induction than in those cells without induction. Importantly, tumor cells with doxycycline-induced YAP activation generated notably lower lung metastases at week 7 and 8 post injection. The number of metastases nodules in the lung was reduced when YAP was transiently activated in the vasculature. Further, the expressions of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling were clinically relevant in CTCs. These results suggest that activating YAP temporally in hematogenous dissemination sensitizes CTCs to shear-induced apoptosis, which further suppresses tumor metastasis. This objective was fully achieved.

15214320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214320.value: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) must survive hematogenous dissemination, including fluid shear stress (FSS) within vasculature, in order to generate distant metastases. In contrast to the extensive investigation of mechanotransduction in adherent cells, how CTCs in non-adherent state perceive FSS and survive in blood circulation remains poorly understood. This study reports that FSS elicits substantial apoptosis of non- adherent CTCs but spares the adherent cells, which is mediated by shear-induced YAP nuclear localization and phosphorylation at Tyr357, thereby promoting its binding to p73 that co-activates the pro-apoptotic genes. These mechano-responses of non- adherent tumor cells are orchestrated by shear-activated Piezo1-F-actin-Lamin A/C nuclear mechanotransduction, which is suppressed in adherent tumor cells and can be re-activated by the inhibition of focal adhesion. Transient activation of YAP during hematogenous dissemination reduces the survival of CTCs and suppresses tumor metastasis. This study demonstrates that the adhesion state dictates the mechano-responses of tumor cells and uncovers a previously unappreciated mechanosensing mechanism underlying the shear-induced death of CTCs during hematogenous metastasis, which may be harnessed for mechanotargeting and metastasis prevention. The research findings have been published in 5 journal papers (see Part C).

15214320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214320.value: This project has demonstrated that CTCs sense and respond to fluid shear stress via the activation of Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling, which eventually leads to cell death and the suppression of tumor metastasis. It is important to further investigate 1) whether this mechanism is applicable to multiple types of cancer, which also disseminate to other organs through hematogenous metastasis; 2) how this mechanism can be specifically targeted only in CTCs for efficient eradication and the suppression of tumor metastasis. To address the first question, several other types of cancer, such as colon cancer, liver cancer, and lung cancer, will be tested to examine whether these CTCs perceive fluid shear stress via Piezo1-YAP/TAZ-p73 signaling. To address the second question, we will collaborate with experts in nanotechnologies and test the possibility to utilize nanoparticles to specifically deliver drugs only to CTCs for the transient activation of YAP-p73 signaling, which is expected to kill more CTCs.

15214320.value: Metastatic rather than primary tumors contribute to over 90% of cancer-induced deaths. Tumor cells metastasize to distant organs mainly through hematogenous dissemination, in which circulating tumor cells (CTCs) experience considerable levels of fluid shear stress. It is known that adherent tumor cells sense shear stress via mechanosensitive proteins that influences their functions. However, the effect of blood shear stress on the survival of suspended CTCs remains less understood. This study reports that FSS elicits substantial apoptosis of non- adherent CTCs but spares adherent cells, which is mediated by shear-induced YAP nuclear localization and phosphorylation at Tyr357, thereby promoting its binding to p73 that co-activates the pro-apoptotic genes. These mechano-responses of non- adherent tumor cells are orchestrated by shear-activated Piezo1-F-actin-Lamin A/C nuclear mechanotransduction, which is suppressed in adherent tumor cells and can be re-activated by the inhibition of focal adhesion. Transient activation of YAP during hematogenous dissemination reduces the survival of CTCs and suppresses tumor metastasis. This study demonstrates that the adhesion state dictates the mechano-responses of tumor cells and uncovers a previously unappreciated mechanosensing mechanism underlying the shear-induced death of CTCs during hematogenous metastasis, which may be harnessed for mechanotargeting and metastasis prevention.

15214620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214620.value: 得益於在結構和美觀上的優勢,大跨斜拉索橋在全世界範圍內變得越來越普遍,在現代化的交通網路中發揮著重要作用。 而斜拉索毫無疑問是其中最重要的受力構件之一。 然而由於高柔度低阻尼的特性,斜拉索容易在風荷載、交通荷載、風雨共同作用下發生強烈振動,從而導致在斜拉索中或者斜拉索的錨固端過早的出現疲勞破壞,嚴重影響整座橋的使用性與安全性。 而解決這一問題的常見方法是在斜拉索上安裝各種類型的阻尼器(包括被動式、半主動式、主動式)。 相比之下,被動式阻尼器的應用最為廣泛,但它們對斜拉索的減振性能也相對比較有限。 而主動式控制在理論和試驗中均被證明更為有效,但它們在土木工程中的實用性卻長期遭到詬病。 例如,針對於大型結構的主動控制系統往往需要巨大的能量輸入,而這在實用中常常無法滿足,在極端災害的情況下甚至會出現能量供給中斷的情況。 另外在控制算法異常的情況下,主動控制還有可能帶來系統失穩的情況。 有鑑於此,本項目旨在通過結合結構振動控制、能量收集、電力電子等技術,開發一種自供能的主動控制技術用於斜拉索的減振控制。 它不僅將解除主動控制對電源供應的依賴,也能有效避免控制器對被控結構注入大量能量引起的控制失穩現象。 據申請人所知,這種新型的減振控制策略還未曾被系統的研究過。 本項目將通過系統的理論、數值、試驗研究,對這一問題進行全面的探索,包括作動器的開發、控制系統的設計、斜拉索減振性能的評估。 本項目的預期成果,將為主動控制領域的發展帶來全新的進步。

15215120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15215120.value: 基於先進數據採集和算法的实時甚低頻低頻三維閃電定位網的開發

15215120.label: Project Objectives
15215120.value: General objective: Lightning location network (LLN) is widely used to provide lightning warning and protection services for public utilities like electric power transmission lines, high speed railway systems, airports, and communication tower etc. Lightning emits wide band electromagnetic fields, allowing to develop LLN working in either very-low-frequency (VLF)/low-frequency (LF) or very-high-frequency (VHF) bands. In this project, we are going to build a new VLF/LF LLN over the Great Bay Area around Hong Kong to provide lightning warning services in real-time in 3-dimensional (3D). The LLN will consist of 7 stations separated in 10 to 20 km with one central data server. Each station will include a VLF/LF lightning sensor, a GPS antenna, a PC with advanced data acquisition and processing system, a 4G/5G communication module. There are following six specific issues that need to be addressed. The first issue is the design of a sensitive lightning sensor. Most experimental 3D VLF/LF LLNs use either a magnetic field or an electric field sensor. The electric field measurement has little information on horizontally extended discharging process, while the magnetic field measurement lacks the discharge polarity information unless the source location is determined. In this project, we will develop a VLF/LF lightning sensor that consists of a crossed-loop magnetic field antenna and a flat-plate electric field antenna. The magnetic field signals will be used in finding the source emission time and its 3D location, while the electric field signals will be used to analyze the type of specific discharge process. The second issue is the design of a fast and accurate lightning data acquisition system. In this project, we will use an advanced data acquisition technique to achieve a fully continuous data acquisition and fast data storage and transmission. Analog signals from the two magnetic loops and one electric field antenna will be input into a multi-channel simultaneous data acquisition card controlled with a local PC. A Ping-Pong strategy will be used to handle the high rate data stored in the local PC memory, i.e., the data from the acquisition card is first saved to the PC with a parallel asynchronous thread scanning the PC memory, and then be transferred to the remote server via a 4G/5G network. The third issue is the design of a fast data transfer system to ensure the real-time communications between each sensor and the central server. In this project, we will use the protocol of MQTT and the direct TCP. For the MQTT, the broker will be deployed on the central server side, and the clients will be deployed on both the server and sensor sides. Once the data package is ready, the sensor side publish the data on the broker. The client on the server side subscribe the published data and get it from the broker. The direct TCP will be deployed on the sensor side and has the priority when the communication network condition is fine. The MQTT on the sensor side serves as a backup confronting the poor communication network condition. The fourth issue is is the development of a highly efficient lightning source locating technique to locate as many as possible VLF/LF emission sources in real-time. The time of arrival (TOA) technique is a basic method for finding the location of an emission source. In most VLF/LF LLNs, the time of an electromagnetic pulse peak is used in locating the source, which works well for discrete pulses but doesn’t well for continuous emissions. In a few of VLF/LF LLN, the signal cross-correlation method is used to locate continuous emissions. The signal-cross-correlation method finds the average time difference between each pair of sensors in a short window of a continuous waveform, while it may produce time uncertainty when there are multiple discrete pulses in one short window. Therefore, in this proposed LLN, we will adopt a combined signal-pulse-peak-time and signal-cross-correlation data processing approach, so that both discrete pulses and continuous emissions can be well located. The fifth issue is to accelerate the source locating process with advanced GPU parallel computing technology, which is essential for achieving a real-time 3D LLN. For this purpose, we have recently developed a GPU-based grid traverse TOA algorithm that was nearly 3000 time faster than a transitional CPU-based algorithm, which will be further optimized and applied to this proposed LLN. The last issue is the assembly and testing of the whole network in field based on above 5 key issues. Each station will be powered by a solar power system, so that the whole LLN becomes portable, standalone and easy deployable. With the outputs of above 5 key issues, we believe that a real-time 3D VLF/LF LLN can be successfully built over the Great Bay Area around Hong Kong, which will be beneficial to both the lightning warning and protection community and the lightning research society.

15215120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215120.value: 閃電以其強大的瞬態電流,每年對地球上的生命及各種系統造成巨大的威脅和破壞。 閃電定位網路(LLN)被廣泛應用於電力系統、大型運輸系統和通信系統等公共設施以提供雷電預警和保護。 此外，閃電定位系統也不斷地為雷電研究提供新的數據。雷電會發射覆盖由甚低頻(VLF)、低頻(LF)頻到甚高頻(VHF)的寬頻電磁波， 由此而出現了基於VLF/LF/VHF不同頻段的閃電定位系統。 由新墨西哥礦業科技學院開發的LMA就是一個典型的甚高頻閃電定位陣列, 它可以提供各種雷電過程相關的甚高頻源的三維圖像。 由於雷電產生的甚高頻相比甚低頻/低頻的較弱，甚高頻閃電定位陣列很容易受背景電磁雜訊的干擾， 並且觀測範圍有限， 這很大的限制了其在嘈雜城市環境中的應用。 因此，大多數閃電定位網都是工作在甚低頻/低頻頻段，实時提供每個雷擊的二維地面位置和電流強度等資訊。 二維甚低頻/低頻網可以追蹤大面積的雷電活動，但幾乎無法獲得雷電放電過程讯息， 因此也限制了其在雷電物理研究以及雷暴過程中閃電和氣象環境的關聯方面的應用。 最近，很多研究者開始了三維甚低頻/低頻閃電定位網的實驗，然而這些三維甚低頻閃電定位實驗網無法做到实時工作，主要是因為其數據採集和處理方法耗費時間。本研究将基於高級的數據採集和算法，開發和試験一種实時三維甚低頻/低頻閃電定位網。 這種定位網将由間距在10到20公里的多個雷電觀測站和一個中央數據處理器組成， 覆蓋香港及整個大灣區，实時追蹤雷電活動。每個網站包含一個甚低頻/低頻電磁場感測器、一個GPS時間模組、一台具有高級數據採集系統和快速處理演演演算法的緊湊型電腦、一個4G / 5G數據傳輸模組以及一個太陽能電源模組， 旨在讓定位網便於部署，工作实時高效準確。

15215120.label: Realisation of objectives
15215120.value: The main purpose of this project is to develop a real-time 3D VLF/LF lightning location network using advanced data acquisition and processing algorithms, which is easy-deployable and high-accurate. It includes 5 sub-objectives: 1) Design of new sensitive lightning electric and magnetic field sensor; 2) Design of a portable and fast data acquisition system; 3) Design of a real-time data transfer network; 4) Use of a hybrid signal-pulse-peak-time and signal-cross-correlation data processing technique; 5) Accelerating the locating process with a GPU-based grid traverse TOA algorithm; 6) Assembly and test of the proposed LLN in field. Through the period from August of 2020 (when the project was funded) to June of 2024 (when the project was completed), we have been carried series of in-lab design and in field tests of the network. As the result, all these 6 objectives have been achieved. Specifically, a) In-lab instrumentation and experiment. The lightning sensor at each station of the network is essential for the realization of real-time monitoring of lightning activity. We have started to design and test a LF electro-magnetic field lightning sensor since August 2020 just after the project awarded, and it was successfully designed and lab-calibrated in May of 2021. This newly designed sensor has been in running in Shenzhen City for testing since June of 2021, and then in Beijing area since 2023. The data are now under analysis with a fast lightning locating algorithm to see to what extent that a lightning flashed could be mapped in 3D with VLF/LF signals in real-time. The testing results of the system are summarized in a conference paper [Zilong Ma, Mingli Chen*, Rubin Jiang, Xiushu Qie, A low frequency 3D lightning mapping network in north China, 37th Int. Conf. on Lightning Protection, Sep. 1-7, 2024, Dresden, Germany]. With these works, 100% of Objectives 1), 2), 3) and 6) have been achieved. b) Testing of the lightning mapping technique. Locating a lightning flash in 3D in VLF/LF bands involves complicated physical and mathematical knowledge. To examine the locating technique, starting in August of 2020 just after the project awarded, we have begun to apply our proposed VLF/LF 3D lightning mapping technique firstly to some historical data in literatures. With the data from our collaborator in Duke University, we have successfully got the 3D mapping of two coincident lightning flashes with high accuracy and efficiency. The results were summarized in a paper published on Atmospheric Research. [Fanchao Lyu, Steven A. Cummer, Mingli Chen*, Zilong Qin, Weitao Lyu, Jisong Sun, Three-dimensional mapping of two coincident flashes - An upward positive flash triggered by the in-cloud activity of a downward negative flash. Atmospheric Research, 250 (2021), 105408, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2020.105408]. With these works, 100% of Objectives 4) and 5) have been achieved. c) Study of the impact of rough ground on lightning signal propagation for locating lightning in high accuracy. Lightning location technique is based on the measurement of lightning-produced electromagnetic pulses (LEMPs) that may be distorted over lossy ground. For this sake, we have studied the characteristics of LEMPs propagating over lossy ground and its possible impacts to lightning remote sensing in LF/HF bands with a FDTD-based model. The study mainly consists of two parts: numerical simulation and analytical approximation. For the simulation, firstly, an appropriate RLC model representing a lightning return stroke channel above a lossy ground was developed. The properties of a typical lightning return stroke current wave propagating alone a lightning channel with different RLC settings were evaluated. Then, for a typical setting of the lightning channel, the properties of LEMPs propagating over a lossy ground with different conductivities at different distances. Parts of these works were summarized in a paper published on IEEE Access. [Ge Zhang, Mingli Chen*, Shaoyang Wang, Yan Gao, and Yaping DU, A new FDTD model for lightning return stroke channel above lossy ground and its validation with rocket-triggered lightning data, IEEE Access, August 2023, pp (99):1-1, https://doi.org/10.119/ACCESS.2023.3303478]. With this work, we have further improved the quality of Objectives 1) and 4). d) Lightning attachments interpretation. Besides, supporting by this project, two downward negative flashes with multiple return strokes struck to the 356-m Shenzhen Tower were observed and analyzed in detail. The observations showed that none of the downward negative leader (DNL) completely propagated to the tower tip before the occurrence of the return stroke (RS), so that we inferred that the UCL initiated from the tower tip might exist for each RS of the two flashes. The possible height of the UCL and DNL connecting point above the tower tip for each RS was estimated, which showed a positive correlation to the speed of corresponding DNL. The DNL speed showed a positive correlation to the peak current of corresponding RS. Parts of these work were reported at APL2023. [Yan Gao, Mingli Chen*, Shaoyang Wang, Zilong Qin, Zongxu Qiu, Ge Zhang, Attachment process of a downward negative flash with multiple return strokes struck to a 356-m-tall tower in southern China, at 12th Asia-Pacific Int. Conf. on Lightning Protection (APL2023), 12-15 June 2023, Langkawi, Malaysia, https://doi.org/10.1109/APL57308.2023.10181905]. These works helped us a lot in understanding the lightning attachments to on-ground objects, which is beneficial to the better achievement of Objective 4) and 6).

rows: General objective: Lightning location network (LLN) is widely used to provide lightning warning and protection services for public utilities like electric power transmission lines, high speed railway systems, airports, and communication tower etc. Lightning emits wide band electromagnetic fields, allowing to develop LLN working in either very-low-frequency (VLF)/low-frequency (LF) or very-high-frequency (VHF) bands. In this project, we are going to build a new VLF/LF LLN over the Great Bay Area around Hong Kong to provide lightning warning services in real-time in 3-dimensional (3D). The LLN will consist of 7 stations separated in 10 to 20 km with one central data server. Each station will include a VLF/LF lightning sensor, a GPS antenna, a PC with advanced data acquisition and processing system, a 4G/5G communication module. There are following six specific issues that need to be addressed.

The first issue is the design of a sensitive lightning sensor. Most experimental 3D VLF/LF LLNs use either a magnetic field or an electric field sensor. The electric field measurement has little information on horizontally extended discharging process, while the magnetic field measurement lacks the discharge polarity information unless the source location is determined. In this project, we will develop a VLF/LF lightning sensor that consists of a crossed-loop magnetic field antenna and a flat-plate electric field antenna. The magnetic field signals will be used in finding the source emission time and its 3D location, while the electric field signals will be used to analyze the type of specific discharge process.

The second issue is the design of a fast and accurate lightning data acquisition system. In this project, we will use an advanced data acquisition technique to achieve a fully continuous data acquisition and fast data storage and transmission. Analog signals from the two magnetic loops and one electric field antenna will be input into a multi-channel simultaneous data acquisition card controlled with a local PC. A Ping-Pong strategy will be used to handle the high rate data stored in the local PC memory, i.e., the data from the acquisition card is first saved to the PC with a parallel asynchronous thread scanning the PC memory, and then be transferred to the remote server via a 4G/5G network.

The third issue is the design of a fast data transfer system to ensure the real-time communications between each sensor and the central server. In this project, we will use the protocol of MQTT and the direct TCP. For the MQTT, the broker will be deployed on the central server side, and the clients will be deployed on both the server and sensor sides. Once the data package is ready, the sensor side publish the data on the broker. The client on the server side subscribe the published data and get it from the broker. The direct TCP will be deployed on the sensor side and has the priority when the communication network condition is fine. The MQTT on the sensor side serves as a backup confronting the poor communication network condition.

The fourth issue is is the development of a highly efficient lightning source locating technique to locate as many as possible VLF/LF emission sources in real-time. The time of arrival (TOA) technique is a basic method for finding the location of an emission source. In most VLF/LF LLNs, the time of an electromagnetic pulse peak is used in locating the source, which works well for discrete pulses but doesn’t well for continuous emissions. In a few of VLF/LF LLN, the signal cross-correlation method is used to locate continuous emissions. The signal-cross-correlation method finds the average time difference between each pair of sensors in a short window of a continuous waveform, while it may produce time uncertainty when there are multiple discrete pulses in one short window. Therefore, in this proposed LLN, we will adopt a combined signal-pulse-peak-time and signal-cross-correlation data processing approach.

The fifth issue is to accelerate the source locating process with advanced GPU parallel computing technology, which is essential for achieving a real-time 3D LLN. For this purpose, we have recently developed a GPU-based grid traverse TOA algorithm that was nearly 3000 time faster than a transitional CPU-based algorithm, which will be further optimized and applied to this proposed LLN.

The last issue is the assembly and testing of the whole network in field based on above 5 key issues. Each station will be powered by a solar power system, so that the whole LLN becomes portable, standalone and easy deployable. With the outputs of above 5 key issues, we believe that a real-time 3D VLF/LF LLN can be successfully built over the Great Bay Area around Hong Kong, which will be beneficial to both the lightning warning and protection community and the lightning research society.

15215120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215120.value: Firstly, we succeeded in 3D mapping of lightning flashes in high-accuracy and efficiency with our proposed lightning mapping algorithm. It shows that the mapping algorithm works much faster than existing ones, making the real-time data processing possible. With this new approach for the same set of data, more lightning emission source could be identified and located. As a result, more details of the lightning flash channel development could be reflected in the 3D mapping. Meanwhile, we have succeeded in field testing of our designed lightning low-frequency sensors and the lightning 3D mapping technique by deploying them in a local lightning detection network, proving that our proposed mapping approach is feasible in practice. [Part C: Journal paper No. 1; Conference paper No. 1] Secondly, we have developed a new lightning return stroke model in FDTD code. With this model, we have succeeded in retrieving the current propagation signature along a lightning return stroke channel for rocket-triggered lightning flashes for the first time in the world. Meanwhile, the impact of lossy ground on the propagation of lightning-produced electromagnetic pulses was investigated and formulated. These findings help us a lot in improving the lightning location accuracy at low-frequency bands. [Part C: Journal paper No.2; Conference paper No. 3 and 4]. Lastly, we have succeeded in identifying the attachment process of sub-return strokes to tall structure with our lightning locating and mapping system, which is helpful in the designing of effected lightning protection system for tall buildings. [Part C: Conference paper No. 2].

15215120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215120.value: Due to the limitation of funding and times, the scale of field testing of the system is small. As a result, the volume of the data collected is limited. Towards the application of the system in real world in China, a little bit longer period of field testing and more data are needed to examine the effectiveness of the proposed system. Besides, the system data collecting and processing time are strongly depending on the data transmission and computing techniques. The more advanced the data transmission and processing technique is, the shorter the time delay of the lightning mapping result output. With the deployment of newest data sensing and transmission technology, it is possible that the lightning development can be mapped in 3D with a time delay less than a few seconds.

15215120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215120.value: Lightning location networks (LLNs) are widely used to provide lightning warning and protection services for public utilities like electric power transmission lines, high speed railway systems, airports, and communication tower etc. Lightning emits wideband electromagnetic fields, allowing to develop LLNs working in either very-low-frequency (VLF)/low-frequency (LF) or very-high-frequency (VHF) bands. Nevertheless, most LLNs in services are operating in VLF/LF, providing 2-dimensional (2D) location information of lightning discharges. There are a few of experimental VLF/LF LLN that can work in 3-dimensional (3D) but not in real-time. In this project, we have proposed and tested a new VLF/LF LLN in the Great Bay Area as well as Beijing region, which is proven to be able to provide 3D lightning warning services in almost real-time. The LLN consists of several stations separated in 10 to 20 km with one central data processing server. Each station includes a VLF/LF lightning sensor, a GPS antenna, a compact PC with advanced data acquisition and processing system, a 4G/5G communication module, and a solar power module.

15215620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215620.value: 人工複眼通過模仿節肢動物的天然複眼來獲得較大的視場和快速的運動檢測。但已研發的人工複眼多數只是複制了天然複眼的結構，存在在三個主要缺陷。 （1）非平面結構：微透鏡和光電傳感器單元佈置在彎曲表面上，導致較大的厚度和製造難度。（2）圖像模糊：微透鏡的焦距固定，不能清晰聚焦不同距離的物體，因此圖像一般比較模糊。（3）規格有限，例如尺寸大、視場小。本項目旨在設計及開發一種新型人工複眼，引入微棱鏡陣列來實現全視場成像，並且利用可調液體微透鏡陣列的調焦功能對不同距離的目標實現清新成像，克服當前系統的普遍問題，提供新功能並改善性能。 本項目的人工複眼新設計，並將主要集中在三個任務上：器件設計和理論分析、器件製造和性能表徵、以及原型產品的開發和應用研究。與已有的人工複眼系統相比，本項目在多個方面都具有優勢。（a）新穎且可專利的設計：功能層（包括微棱鏡、微透鏡、圖像傳感器）的平面配置是原創性設計，與大多數報導的人工複眼系統中的彎曲配置完全不同。（b）新功能：可調鏡頭可實現清晰的聚焦功能，並提供物體的距離信息，便於進行三維空間和運動檢測。（c）更好的規格：尺寸將顯著減小，從通常約100毫米減小到約5毫米；能夠進行清晰成像；具有較大的視場，由通常的30度左右提升到約180度。 （d）可批量生產和低成本：微棱鏡和微透鏡可以通過已成熟的微加工技術來批量生產；可以使用商用平面圖像傳感器（例如CCD或CMOS）；每個人工複眼的費用有望從4,000美元降低到20美元。 為準備本項目申請我們已經開展了一些初步研究，嘗試了利用雙光子聚合來加工微棱鏡，並製作和測試了簡單的可調液體透鏡，這些初步結果使我們對該項目的可行性充滿信心。據我們所知，本項目是第一次在人工複眼中實現平面化和可調聚焦這兩項關鍵性功能，如能實現，將對於基於相機的應用如生物醫學成像、機器人視覺、自動駕駛等，具有很大的應用價值。

15215620.label: Realisation of objectives
15215620.value: (1) To develop tunable liquid microlens arrays for variable light focusing In relation to Objective 1, we have successfully designed and fabricated an out-of-plane tunable lens made of isopropylene glycol with a diameter of 500 m. Using interdigitated electrodes, the focal length of the liquid lens can be tuned between 1 mm and 10 mm when the driving potential is adjusted from 0 to 150 V using the electrowetting on dielectric (EWOD) effect. This proves the feasibility of variable light focusing using liquid lenses. In addition, we have applied magnetic force to change the curvature of liquid lens and based on this, we have fabricated a 2 x 2 array of liquid microlenses. (2) To develop microprism arrays for light collection with large field of view In relation to Objective 2, we have tried to use different 3D printers to fabricate microprism arrays with different normal angles and different heights. Experimental studies are undergone but a bit delayed due to the several waves of COVID-19 outbreaks. Most efforts are put on evaluating the influence of surface roughness of microprisms on the imaging quality by using Zemax. It is found that the roughness of Ra 40 nm would reduce the intensity of deflected light by 10%. This result leads to the filing of a Chinese Patent ZL202211263574.9 (see Patent 1). (3) To design and fabricate planar artificial compound eyes by the integration of planar microprism arrays, planar microlens arrays, and flat image sensor units In relation to Objective 3, we have designed the assembly structures of the compound eyes, and have fabricated them using 3D printing. We have also integrated a tunable liquid microlens and a CMOS image sensor for variable-focusing imaging. In addition, we have integrated an artificial compound eye (ACE) setup using the above components and have successfully achieved performances superior to natural compound eyes (NCEs). This leads to 6 journal papers (Journal 1 to Journal 6), including 1 in Light: Science and Applications. It also produces 2 China patents (Patent 2 and Patent 3), and 1 Best Poster Presentation Award and 1 Best Poster Award.

15215620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215620.value: (1) Our integrated artificial compound eye (ACE) setup has performances comparable or superior to natural compound eyes (NCEs), for example, 271 ommatidia versus 272 for bark beetles, 180o field of view (FOV) versus 150–180o FOV for most arthropods. In addition, our ACE outperforms the typical NCEs by ~100 times in dynamic response: 31.3 kHz versus 205 Hz for Glossina morsitans. Compared with other reported ACEs, our ACE enables real-time, 180o panoramic direct imaging and depth estimation within its nearly infinite depth of field. Moreover, our ACE can respond to an angular motion up to 5.6×106 deg/s with the ability to identify translation and rotation, making it suitable for applications to capture high-speed objects, such as surveillance, unmanned aerial/ground vehicles, and virtual reality. This leads to 1 journal paper in Light: Science and Applications (Journal 6). It also produces 2 China patents (Patent 2 and Patent 3), and 1 Best Poster Presentation Award and 1 Best Poster Award. (2) We have conducted systematic studies and theoretical analyses of compound eyes (NCEs), and have categorized them into two groups: fixed focal lengths and tunable focal lengths. We have proposed the main criteria to characterize the ACE performance, such as field of view, acceptance angle of each ommatidium, interommatidial angle, quantitative imaging performance metric, optical sensitivity, and highest angular perception speed, making it easy to compare different ACEs and to apply to practical uses such as surveillance, machine vision and unmanned vehicles. This leads to 1 review article (Journal 5). (3) We have proposed a novel low-temperature fusion bonding method using a standard cleaning recipe assistant with intermediate water, resulting in bonding strength exceeding 10 MPa and optical transmittance surpassing 90 % at 200 °C. In contrast to traditional fusion bonding, this method will not destroy the microstructures in the devices. This method paves the way for the integration of ACEs. This leads to 1 journal paper (Journal 4). Research outcome: (1) Published 6 journal articles and 2 conference papers. (2) Obtained 1 Best Poster Awards. (3) Filed 3 China patents. (4) Established close research collaborations with other institutions, for example, with Abdel El Abed of Université Paris-Saclay (France), Prof. Jia Yanwei of University of Macau, Prof. Liu Detao of South China University of Technology, and Prof. Shui Lingling of South China Normal University. The PI is collaborating with Prof. Abdel El Abed to apply for the ANR/RGC joint project.

15215620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215620.value: Further studies will be conducted in 2 main aspects: (1) Further decrease the acceptance angle of plastic optical fibres to increase the angular resolution. Apertures at the distal end of optical fibres could be used in the future to replace the microlens. By considering the relationship among diameter, thickness, and distance of these apertures from the optical fibre, a further reduction in the acceptance angle could be anticipated. (2) Further improve the resolution. Here are also two specific approaches to improve the resolution. (a) Narrower optical fibres: Plastic optical fibres with smaller diameters (e.g., from currently 250 to 25 mm) can be used to reduce the space occupied by each fibre and thus increase the number of plastic optical fibres. This would allow for a greater number of narrow plastic optical fibres, thereby enhancing the image resolution. (b) Optical fibre bundles: Plastic optical fibres can be replaced with imaging optical fibre bundles to mimic optical and neural superposition in NCEs. Since each imaging optical fibre bundle contains thousands of individual fibres, the resolution can be significantly increased if the relationship between the microlens and the imaging optical fibre bundles is well analysed, similar to the analysis presented in this article.

15215620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215620.value: This project has deveoped a novel design for artificial compound eyes (ACEs) that addresses key limitations of existing systems. Traditional ACEs replicate natural compound eyes but face challenges such as non-planar structures, blurred images, and limited specifications. Our design employs a microprism array and a tunable liquid microlens array, allowing for a full field of view (FOV) and sharp focusing on objects at varying distances. Key improvements include: (1) Planar Configuration: Unlike curved structures in existing ACEs, our original design features a planar arrangement of microprisms, microlenses, and image sensors. (2) Enhanced Functionality: Tunable lenses facilitate sharp focusing and provide distance information for 3D space and motion detection. (3) Superior Specifications: The size is reduced from ~100 mm to ~5 mm, with a clear image and a FOV of about 180°, compared to the typical 30°-150°. (4) Cost-Effectiveness: Utilizing mature microfabrication techniques allows for mass production, decreasing costs from approximately $4,000 to $20 per unit. This ACE system is an original work to realize both functions of planarization and tunable focusing, and holds promise for applications in biomedical imaging, machine vision, and surveillance.

To implement our proposed leader election algorithm in the constructed Hyperledger system and test its performance. The new leader election algorithm can replace current Kafka consensus algorithm in the Hyperledger to improve the DNS system data availability. To provide efficient DNS query services to clients with our Hyperledger-based DNS system and the query delay should be comparable to or shorter than current DNS services. This system should also allow us to trace malicious domains effectively. To build a Hyperledger-based log system. The system can record every event correctly, provide auditing services, ensure authenticity of events even under a new threat model containing untrusted loggers and untrusted auditors. To design flexible storage schemes for the constructed log system. The system performance of space cost and fault tolerance on each node should be investigated with respect to different sizes of log data and different storage schemes. To provide efficient data structure to support the query of a specific event and the whole history tracing, and verify its performance through experiments.

15216220.value: 互聯網依賴於DNS（域名系統）記錄數據來將域名轉換為IP地址轉換，並且還依賴於日誌文件數據進行訪問控制管理。但是，由於設計由於當前DNS和日誌系統存在漏洞，因此Internet不可靠，安全或不可信。在2016年10月21日，發生了著名的Dyn攻擊。一系列DDoS（分佈式拒絕服務）攻擊由DNS註冊表Dyn操作的目標名稱服務器，導致許多網站無法解析和網絡衝浪不可用。在日誌系統中，注入已列為OWASP（OpenWeb應用程序安全性項目）的最大攻擊。如果發生日誌注入攻擊（例如，內部人員），日誌信息被篡改，攻擊行為不可追踪。因此，在此項目中，我們重點研究DNS和日誌系統中的數據安全問題。通過利用區塊鏈技術，確保其數據的真實性，可用性和可追溯性。 我們新的基於區塊鏈的DNS和日誌系統基於Hyperledger架構。數據在新系統是不可變的，防篡改的，並存儲在分佈式節點中。但是，基於區塊鏈DNS /日誌系統無法提供經過身份驗證的數據（例如，緩存中毒中的數據中毒攻擊）。 DDoS可能會攻擊單獨訂購者（在Kafka中）或指定的認可者/訂購者攻擊，導致Hyperledger中的服務終止。而且，Hyperledger中的查詢服務它非常有限，遠非日誌系統中事件歷史記錄跟踪的要求。面對這些挑戰，我們為基於區塊鏈的DNS /日誌系統提出以下新穎設計。 1）改善通過採用新穎的證書機制和註冊表來將數據的真實性提高到更高的安全級別進行DNS記錄認可，並提出新的系統設計以應對更一般的情況日誌系統中的威脅模型； 2）通過提出以下建議，為數據可用性提供更強大的保護：用於Hyperledger訂購服務的新穎領導者選舉協議，以及通過設計鏈上/鏈下/日誌系統中針對不同大小的日誌數據的混合存儲體系結構； 3）更高效通過在DNS中使用高效的查詢界面設計新的交易格式來查詢數據的可追溯性，並通過使用Bloom過濾器和屬性樹構造新穎的數據和交易結構來提高效率日誌系統中的事件和歷史記錄查詢。 提議的新DNS和日誌系統可能會產生重大影響。 1）我們的系統可以提供針對緩存中毒攻擊，DDoS攻擊，Ghost域攻擊和DNS的有效對策劫持攻擊，這在傳統DNS中很難解決。此外，註冊表的功能和低查詢延遲使我們的基於區塊鏈的DNS與當前的DNS兼容，並且可以是一種實用且安全的替代方法。 2）我們基於區塊鏈的日誌系統甚至可以在不受信任的審核員的更惡劣環境中提供可信的審核服務。提出的日誌系統可以容忍客戶端，記錄器之間的合謀攻擊等攻擊和審核員。此外，增強的日誌對象可追溯性顯示出巨大的潛力適用於工業應用，例如數據來源，數字取證和醫療保健審計。

15216220.label: Realisation of objectives
15216220.value: We have fully achieved the above-listed six objectives in this project. 1. Objective 1: To build a Hyperledger-based DNS system. The system should support DNS record registration, update, revocation and deletion operations, with certificates to ensure data authenticity. We propose B-DNS, a secure and efficient blockchain-based DNS system in [1]. We also redesign the transaction format to support registration, update, revocation, and deletion operations for DNS records. Specifically, resource records in legacy DNS are transformed into operation records in B-DNS. We also analyze the security of B-DNS and show that B-DNS can ensure the authenticity of stored DNS records. 2. Objective 2: To implement our proposed leader election algorithm in the constructed Hyperledger system and test its performance. The new leader election algorithm can replace current Kafka consensus algorithm in the Hyperledger to improve the DNS system data availability. We first model and analyze the communication traffic model for permissioned blockchain to summarize the characteristics of blockchain traffic in [2]. Then, we propose a novel Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus protocol in [1]. In our proposed PoS consensus protocol, leaders are elected based on the amount of stake controlled by blockchain participants. The bigger the amount of stake a participant control, the larger the possibility that this participant is elected as the leader to issue new blocks. We demonstrate that our proposed PoS consensus protocol can increase the availability of B-DNS compared with state-of-the-art. 3. Objective 3: To provide efficient DNS query services to clients with our Hyperledger-based DNS system and the query delay should be comparable to or shorter than current DNS services. This system should also allow us to trace malicious domains effectively. We propose a tree-based search algorithm to accelerate the query of DNS records in B-DNS [1]. We also propose a dual-bloom-filter algorithm to enable efficient query of revoked DNS records [1]. Our experiment results demonstrate that B-DNS can provide query service in a comparable performance with commercial DNS implementations. For tracing malicious domains problem, we convert it into a general traceability problem in blockchain and addressed it in VQL [3]. We also design a novel verifiable SSE scheme named Slicer to perform range searches on numerical data in [4]. This approach further enhances the efficiency of tracing malicious domains, and the search results are publicly verifiable. 4. Objective 4: To build a Hyperledger-based log system. The system can record every event correctly, provide auditing services, ensure authenticity of events even under a new threat model containing untrusted loggers and untrusted auditors. We first explore a novel trust paradigm in [5]. The combination of smart contract and TEE allows us to record events and validate event writers (i.e., can be loggers). We have proposed a novel certificate issuance and management system to ensure that only authenticated entity can be issued a certificate. Building upon the aforementioned foundational works, we propose a blockchain-based audit log system that ensures data integrity under a general threat model where a part of the nodes, including loggers and auditors, are untrusted [6]. We also introduce a novel blockchain-based technique to support multi-party authentication, enabling trustworthy group communications and preventing malicious attackers from impersonating legitimate loggers and auditors [7]. 5. Objective 5: To design flexible storage schemes for the constructed log system. The system performance of space cost and fault tolerance on each node should be investigated with respect to different sizes of log data and different storage schemes. To save blockchain storage space, we design an efficient log integrity proof method, which generates a sub-Non-Fungible Token (sub-NFT) for each log file and keeps it on the blockchain as integrity proof in [6]. This idea is also used in [8] for implementing ZKDET, a traceable data exchange scheme. We design an authenticated data structure (ADS) for efficient authenticated queries of graph data in [9]. Our experiment results demonstrate that VQL can significantly reduce the space cost of a blockchain node. To enhance the fault tolerance, we outsource log files to a distributed file system to resolve the single-point failure problem in [6]. We also proposed SolSaviour, a defending framework to address the problem of faulty smart contracts [11]. This framework enables the redeployment of patched contracts and the migration of internal states from old contracts to new ones. 6. Objective 6: To provide efficient data structure to support the query of a specific event and the whole history tracing, and verify its performance through experiments. We explore different storage schemes to enable efficient querying. In [1], we establish two bloom filters, which consist of a revocation list and a valid list, to enable fast domain revocation checking. We evaluate the performance of tree and bloom-filter based query algorithms. In [3], we propose a Verifiable Query Layer (VQL) that can be deployed in the cloud to provide both efficient and verifiable data query services for blockchain systems. We test the performance of blockchain search middleware layer. In [4], we design a novel verifiable SSE scheme named Slicer based on a Succinct Order-Revealing Encryption (SORE) scheme to achieve range search on numerical data. We evaluate the performance of SORE-based range search through rigorous analysis and extensive evaluations respectively. In [5], we evaluate the network traffic of blockchain, which provides network layer data support for designing efficient distributed query algorithms. In [6], we employ a sub-Non-Fungible Token (sub-NFT) for each log file and keeps it on the blockchain as integrity proof. We test the performance of our efficient log integrity proof method. In [9], we test the performance of authenticated data structure (ADS) that supports authenticated queries through theoretical analysis and extensive experiments.
