15216220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216220.value: First, we propose B-DNS, a secure and efficient blockchain-based DNS system, featuring a redesigned transaction format to support DNS record operations and ensure authenticity in [1]. To enhance B-DNS, we introduce a novel Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus protocol, improving availability by electing leaders based on their stake. Additionally, we develop advanced query algorithms, including a tree-based search for DNS records and a dual-bloom-filter algorithm for revoked records, achieving performance comparable to commercial DNS systems in [1]. For tracing malicious domains, we address the problem using VQL [3] for blockchain traceability and enhance efficiency with Slicer [4], a verifiable SSE scheme enabling range searches on numerical data. Then, we propose a blockchain-based audit log system that ensures data integrity under a general threat model in [6]. To optimize storage, we introduce a sub-NFT-based log integrity proof method [6] and a snapshot-based approach [3] for managing growing blockchain data. Our work enhances fault tolerance by outsourcing logs to distributed file systems and introduces a defending framework for faulty smart contracts [11]. We explore various efficient data structure sand evaluate the performance of these data structures, including bloom-filter-based [1], middleware layer [3], SORE-based [4], and sub-NFT-based [6] methods, and authenticated data structure based on the RSA accumulator and completeness set [9]. This project has fruitful research outcomes. The research outcomes of the project have been shown in top journal and top conference papers. Top journal papers include IEEE TNSE-2021 (A Secure and Efficient DNS Based on the Blockchain Technology), IEEE TKDE-2023 (Enabling Privacy-Preserving and Efficient Authenticated Graph Queries on Blockchain-Assisted Clouds), IEEE TITS-2020 (Blockchain-Enabled Trustworthy Group Communications in UAV Networks), and IEEE TPDS-2021 (VQL: Efficient and Verifiable Cloud Query Services for Blockchain Systems). Top conference papers include IEEE IPDPS2022 (Block Validation Mechanism for UTXO-based Blockchains), ACSAC2021 (A Defending Framework for Deployed Defective Smart Contracts), ICDCS2022 (zkDET: A Traceable and Privacy-Preserving Data Exchange Scheme based on Non-Fungible Token and Zero-Knowledge and Slicer: Verifiable, Secure and Fair Search over Encrypted Numerical Data Using Blockchain), IEEE ICC2021 (Communication Traffic Model for Permissioned Blockchain), IEEE ICC2024 (A Secure and Reliable Blockchain-based Audit Log System), IEEE GC2023 (Selfish Mining Attack under the Checkpoint Mechanism), and IEEE IPDPS2020 (A Location-based and Scalable Consensus Protocol for IoT-Blockchain Applications).

15216220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216220.value: Our proposed DNS system can be further extended to other emerging decentralized naming systems, e.g., ENS (Ethereum Name Service) or IPFS-based naming. The leader election algorithm used in our proposed DNS system can be further extended to cross-chain ecosystems or layer-2 solutions, and sharding-based blockchains. Our proposed blockchain-based logging system can be further extended to various areas within the Web3 ecosystem, such as verifying transaction histories in DeFi platforms and enhancing user authentication and history verification within decentralized identity (DID) frameworks. Additionally, our log system can integrate AI-driven analysis to predict and mitigate malicious activities (e.g., mining attacks and front-running attacks) in real time, thereby contributing to a more secure blockchain system.

15216220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216220.value: DNS is one of the most crucial sub-systems of the Internet. The security of DNS is of great significance to the Internet. However, current DNS has many vulnerabilities, which are difficult to handle using traditional methods. For example, the 2011 cache poisoning attack in Brazil and the 2016 Dyn attack in the USA both exploited the vulnerabilities in the current DNS. Facing these challenges, our project proposes a novel blockchain-based DNS, which can provide secure and efficient name services. The project outcome includes new Hyperledger-based DNS system featuring an innovative leader election algorithm, a Hyperledger-based log system employing a unique storage scheme to ensure data availability, and several efficient query methods designed for both systems. Our proposed B-DNS system fills up two shortcomings of current blockchain-based DNS with efficient DNS query services. our proposed system resists collusion attacks by incorporating multiple nodes for system processes and utilizing smart contracts to enforce consensus algorithms. The project research results are published in top journal/conference papers, including IEEE IPDPS 2022, ACSAC 2021, ICDCS 2022, IEEE ICC 2021, 2024, IEEE TNSE 2021, IEEE TKDE 2023, IEEE TITS 2020, and IEEE TPDS 2021.

15216520.label: Project Objectives
15216520.value: Study and quantify, experimentally, the dynamic characteristics of the variable-speed devices (i.e. variable-speed pumps) used in heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems in buildings under frequency regulation control to enable the donation of ancillary services to smart power grids. The main subtasks or challenges to be addressed include: i. identification of the characteristic parameters of HVAC components/systems, which are critical or important to operation performance under frequency regulation control; ii. selection of working conditions corresponding to the needs of frequency regulation control. Study and quantify, experimentally, the quality of ancillary services donated by variable-speed devices of HVAC systems by following the commonly-used test signals which are critical to power grids. Study and quantify, experimentally, the impacts of ancillary services on buildings (i.e., indoor environmental control and control stability) by following the frequency regulation signals critical to buildings, which will be determined based on the frequency regulation signal records. The main challenges to be addressed include: i. selection of the representative frequency regulation signals which are critical to buildings; ii. selection of the proper test conditions in which a large regulation capacity can be provided, so that the impacts of the ancillary services can be observed at critical conditions; iii. selection of the proper evaluation criteria to effectively quantify the impacts, of providing ancillary services, on buildings. Develop a new frequency regulation control strategy, which consists of a frequency regulation control scheme and a frequency disturbance compensation scheme. The frequency regulation control scheme will provide frequency regulation and the novel frequency disturbance compensation scheme reduces/eliminates the impacts of frequency regulation control on indoor environmental control and control stability. The main challenge, for the development of the frequency regulation control scheme, is a proper solution, with optimization, to address the conflict between providing ancillary services to power grids and maintaining satisfactory environmental control in buildings. In the development of the frequency disturbance compensation scheme, the main challenges include: i. establishment of an effective estimator of the level of “disturbance” to the control loop concerned under different working conditions; ii. establishment of a proper means of enhancing the effectiveness of disturbance compensation allowing for the impact of the dynamics of the system on the control process; iii. establishment of a proper means of enhancing the effectiveness of disturbance compensation, taking account of the interaction of components, under frequency regulation control, in multi-zone HVAC systems. Test and validate the frequency regulation control strategy and the frequency disturbance compensation scheme. An experimental test rig will be developed for the quantification of HVAC dynamics characteristics under frequency regulation control, the quality and impacts of the ancillary services as well as the validation of the control strategy/schemes. A dynamic simulation test platform, representing a multi-zone air-conditioning system, will also be developed to test and validate the proposed control strategy/schemes.

15216520.value: 频率调节能够维持电网的瞬时平衡，同时它也是最重要的电网辅助服务类型之一。然而，由于具有间歇性的可再生能源并网速度的快速增加，电网侧的频率调节能力将变得不足。而在用电侧，由于HVAC（供热通风与空气调节）系统在建筑电能消耗中占有很大比重，因此近些年该系统被认为是提供电网频率调节服务的有力候选者。 为了实现及促进HVAC系统提供电网频率调节服务，我们需要解决以下几个主要挑战，包括：一， 由于对频率调节控制下的HVAC系统的动态特性（例如响应速度）了解不足，因此其能提供的服务质量有待确认；二，HVAC系统提供电网频率调节服务时会对建筑内环境控制质量和系统控制稳定性具有影响，而我们对这些影响的了解还不充足； 三，缺乏可以消除这些影响的控制策略。 在这个项目中，我们将开发针对变速HVAC设备的新型频率调节控制策略用以解决以上这些挑战。同时我们将在实验室中构建典型的HVAC系统并对提出的控制策略进行实验验证。该控制策略包括频率调节控制模块和频率干扰补偿模块。频率调节控制模块用以控制HVAC系统提供电网频率调节服务，其包括了用电调节控制器和调节招标控制器。而频率干扰补偿模块的功能是减弱HVAC系统提供电网频率调节服务时对室内环境控制及系统稳定性的影响。该模块是在参考了“基于干扰观测器控制”的基础上进行开发的。 我们首先会对在频率调节控制下的HVAC系统的动态特性进行量化。其次我们会对HVAC系统中变速泵提供的电网频率调节服务质量进行实验评估，这一过程使用的是常用的电网侧提供的频率调节信号。另一方面，我们也会在实验平台上对系统提供电网频率调节服务时对室内环境控制和系统控制稳定性的影响进行评估，这一过程使用的是依据历史信号选取的针对建筑侧的频率调节信号。最后，我们将在实验测试台和动态仿真测试平台上对提出的频率调节控制策略特别是其中的频率干扰补偿模块进行验证。

15216520.label: Realisation of objectives
15216520.value: The project has successfully achieved all its objectives, by developing effective strategies, methods, frameworks, and tools to enhance the integration of building HVAC systems with smart power grids. Through a series of research and testing activities, the project accomplished the following: 1. Conducted a systematic analysis of the dynamic characteristics of variable-speed devices (e.g., variable-speed pumps) in building HVAC systems under frequency regulation control, enabling the provision of ancillary services to smart power grids. 2. Developed a novel frequency regulation control strategy, comprising a frequency regulation control scheme and a frequency disturbance compensation scheme, to balance the provision of ancillary services to power grids with maintaining satisfactory environmental control in buildings. 3. Developed grid-interactive control methods to provide energy flexibility services to power grids, focusing on practical applicability and convenience in real-world applications. 4. Validated the frequency regulation control strategies and grid-interactive control methods through full-scale testing at an existing pharmaceutical building, as well as simulation-based testing on a typical air-conditioning system using a dynamic simulation platform.

15216720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15216720.value: 帶輸入約束的最優仿射隨機控制及其金融應用

15216720.label: Project Objectives
15216720.value: The objective of this project is to address and study three inter-related research problems. While the field of affine nonlinear stochastic control has been well explored, little has been done to address problems with control input constraints. The first problem is a general optimal control problem for affine nonlinear stochastic systems with control input constraints and random coefficients. We shall apply Ekeland's variational principle to derive a Pontryagin-type stochastic maximum principle for this optimal control problem, which is a kind of optimality condition. Furthermore, we shall study the approximations of this problem, which will enable us to implement our theoretical results numerically. The second problem is a stochastic bilinear-quadratic optimal control problem with bilinear dynamic systems and a quadratic cost functional, in which control input constraints follow linear inequalities. We plan to study this problem using coupled backward stochastic differential quasi-Riccati equations as well as the general results established in objective (1). Applying the theoretical findings from the first problem to real financial situations is one of the motivations for this proposed research project. The third problem is a dynamic mean--semi-variance portfolio selection problem involving a non-smooth cost functional with borrowing, upper and lower bound constraints. We plan to extend the results of objectives (1) and (2) to address this research question. This research project aims to fill this gap by investigating issues with practical relevance rooted in portfolio selection models.

15216720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216720.value: 仿射隨機控制問題在科學，工程，經濟學和金融投資等許多領域都有重要的應用。最近，人們對研究這種仿射隨機控制問題以及解決其應用越來越感興趣。在金融投資領域，人們經常會遇到一類有趣且重要的連續時間投資組合選擇問題，其中從財富過程中按比例選擇投資策略和消費成本策略。特別是，相對於標準隨機控制問題，在一些最近的隨機雙線性二次控制問題和均值-方差投資組合選擇問題中，漂移和/或波動率項通常涉及隨機係數。動力系統也就自然遵循具有隨機係數的仿射非線性/雙線性系統。包含具有隨機係數的仿射非線性/雙線性項引入了主要的技術難題，其中包括隨機性的存在，導致確定性的Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman(簡稱HJB)方程法失敗。在這種情況下，動態規劃將導致一些隨機的HJB方程，該方程在技術上相當複雜。然而，在現實生活中，當人們期望在控制輸入約束下更好地管理風險時，情況就更加複雜了。該項目的目的不僅在於其理論意義，而且在於其實際重要性，目的是通過控制輸入約束和隨機係數來解決這一具有挑戰性的問題。在這個擬議的研究項目中，我們計劃開發一些新方法，以解決上述特徵給自然帶來的困難，這些新方法與現有文獻中沒有約束的仿射隨機控制問題大不相同。此外，我們將理論結果應用於具有挑戰性，但又實用且重要的決策模型，該模型具有借貸，金融投資的上限和下限限制。該模型將幫助投資者更好地理解和有效控制風險，從而在有限的投資範圍內獲得更高的回報。

15216720.label: Realisation of objectives
15216720.value: This project mainly investigated a class of affine nonlinear stochastic problems featuring both stochastic control and stochastic affine systems with constraints over a finite/infinite time horizon. We developed new methodologies, which are significantly different from those in the existing literature's standard control theory. In our models, the inclusion of constraints introduces significant technical difficulties, including random coefficients, which lead to its theoretical significance and its practical importance. We considered a class of investment problems such as no-shorting rules, borrowing constraints and consumption constraint, further developed the theory and presented the numerical examples (papers 6, 7 and 10 in Part C). We studied an optimal consumption problem for a loss-averse agent with reference to past consumption maximum. To account for loss aversion on relative consumption, an S-shaped utility is adopted that measures the difference between the nonnegative consumption rate and a fraction of the historical spending peak. In particular, comparing with the existing literature, the utility measures the difference between the control and its running maximum, and a nonnegativity constraint on consumption is imposed. Also, we developed two-person non-homogeneous LQ stochastic differential games (LQ-SDG) in an infinite horizon for a system regulated by a time-invariant Markov chain (paper 1 in Part C). Both non-zero-sum and zero-sum LQ-SDG problems are studied. We showed that the zero-sum LQ-SDG problem can be considered a special non-zero-sum LQ-SDG problem. In particular, the closed-loop representation of open-loop Nash equilibrium point for non-zero-sum (zero-sum, respectively) LQ-SDG is provided by the non-symmetric (symmetric, respectively) solution to coupled algebra Riccati equations. Besides the above works, we studied a reinforcement learning (RL) method to solve infinite horizon continuous-time stochastic LQ problems, where the drift and diffusion terms in the dynamics may depend on both the state and control. Based on the Bellman’s dynamic programming principle, we presented an online RL algorithm to attain optimal LQ stochastic affine control (papers 5 and 12 in Part C). During this project period, we also investigated open-loop and closed-loop solvabilities of optimal LQ stochastic affine control problems with random coefficients and Markovian regime-switching system (papers 3, 4 and 9 in Part C). We provided an alternative characterization of the open-loop solvability of the LQ problem using a perturbation approach. Then we studied the closed-loop solvability of the LQ problem of the Markovian regime-switching system. In particular, we established the equivalence between the open-loop (closed-loop, respectively) solvability and the existence of an adapted solution to the corresponding forward-backward stochastic differential equation with constraint, and applied the theoretical results established in this project to treat a continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with random coefficients and Markovian regime-switching system (paper 9 in Part C). The results obtained from our work are expected to help readers have a better understanding of stochastic LQ control based on the Markov chain model. In paper 13 of Part C, we analyzed control and stabilization problems for continuous-time mean-field systems with input delay, which are the fundamental development of control and stabilization problems for mean-field affine systems. We established the necessary and sufficient solvability condition for this kind of time-inconsistent affine control problem with input delay, and derived the analytical form of an optimal controller through overcoming the obstacle that separation principle no longer holds for multiplicative-noise systems. In paper 2 of Part C, we studied partially-observed control problems for the state governed by affine stochastic differential equation. We investigated weak closed-loop solvability of this problem and prove the equivalence between open-loop and weak closed-loop solvabilities. Besides these, we also studied discrete-time stochastic control problems with random coefficients or unknown uncertainty (papers 8 and 11 in Part C). In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our research has important and practical significance. With the alarm bell's sounding and the ongoing financial crisis, risk hedging has attracted more attention than ever before. We introduced a life-cycle optimal portfolio-consumption problem when the consumption performance is measured by a shortfall aversion preference under an additional drawdown constraint on consumption rate (papers 6 and 10 in Part C). We performed a sensitivity analysis of the value function, the optimal consumption and portfolio on some model parameters, namely the reference degree parameter, the mean return and the volatility of the risky asset, and discussed some quantitative properties and their financial implications. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions.

15216720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216720.value: This project is to deal with stochastic affine control problems with constraints in many fields such as science, engineering, economics, management, and especially financial investment. We mainly revisited some challenging, yet practically important wealth management models over a finite/infinite time investment horizon, reformulated them as stochastic affine control problems with constraints, and derived their optimal analytical strategies. Also, we analyzed stochastic affine differential games over an infinite time horizon using coupled Riccati equations within a game-theoretic framework during this project period. Besides these, we further studied a class of open-loop and weak closed-loop solvabilities for LQ problems with partial observation, and developed this theoretical result to tackle delayed affine control problems. Although we did not project expenses for graduate student training in the original GRF proposal submitted to RGC in October 2019, our university appointed Mr. Zeng Yijie as a Research Assistant to work with us on this GRF-sponsored project in the period of 1 December 2021 – 31 May 2022. In August 2023, he became a PhD student at our university. Also, we supported Miss Yang Yixin to be a Research Assistant. She is studying at Duke University as a Master student now. In the future, I will pay more attention to the training of research postgraduate students. During this project period, I attended at the 10th International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics from 20 to 25 August 2023 in Tokyo. I presented an invited talk at Recent Advances on Quantitative Finance from 27 to 30 August 2023 in Hong Kong. I participated in SIAM Conference on Financial Mathematics and Engineering and introduced our research works in Phildelphia, USA from 6 to 9 June 2023. Also, I attended the 9th International Colloquium on BSDEs and Mean Field in Annecy, France from 26 June to 1 July 2022. This conference invited specialists from various universities, including those from Princeton University, University of California at Berkeley, University of Texas at Austin, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College, ETH Zurich, etc. Also, I served on the organizing committee of the 11th World Congress of Bachelier Finance Society and gave a talk in Hong Kong from 13 to 17 June 2022. 15216720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216720.value: Since it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for non-standard affine stochastic problems within the more general stochastic system framework, such as path-dependent, delayed, and partially-observed stochastic affine differential equations, we will further study these potential research works in the future. [1] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze behavioral portfolio selection, while one encounters investment problem with reference to the historical consumption maximum over his/her investment time horizon. We will further develop those results established in papers 6 and 10 of Part C in the future. [2] Our methods developed in this project can be applied two-person non-homogeneous LQ non-zero sum stochastic affine differential games with random coefficients over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will further study the corresponding techniques in paper 1 of Part C so that we can tackle the above problems. We will present the results in another project report after we complete it. [3] Reinforcement learning method proposed in this project (papers 5 and 12 in Part C) can be further employed to study more general stochastic control problems over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will present the results in another project report after we complete it.

15216720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216720.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as optimal policy and consumption cost in portfolio selection (papers 6 and 10 in Part C), mean-variance portfolio selection, fund management and agency theory (papers 7 and 9 in Part C) within the continuous-time framework. In addition, the methods adopted will improve the optimal control studied and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic affine control constraints (paper 7 in Part C) and under the regime-switching system (papers 1, 3, 4 and 9 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings provides a fundamental tool (paper 13 in Part C) to study a class of delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients. We also studied two-person non-homogeneous LQ non-zero sum stochastic affine differential games with regime-switching over an infinite horizon using open-loop and closed-loop Nash equilibria (paper 1 in Part C). Besides these, introducing reinforcement learning method paves the avenue for analyzing optimal stochastic affine control problems (papers 5 and 12 in Part C). Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance, and it helps provide risk-management advice for policy makers and institutional investors.

15217220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217220.value: Hong Kong has a winding coastline up to 1178 km encircling the main lands and a total of 263 islands. The coastline is rich of marine silty clay (MSC) deposits, whose behavior underpins the design and operation of massive marine infrastructure for Hong Kong. In the construction of these marine infrastructures, steel has traditionally been a predominant construction material for pipe piles, seawalls or caisson foundations. Its corrosion poses a great risk to the service life of relevant infrastructures. A new type of corrosion-resistant material, fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP), has received increasing attention as an alternative of steel in foundations to avoid corrosion and provide sustainability benefits to marine infrastructures. The capacities of FRP piles, seawalls or caisson foundations highly depend on the MSC-FRP interface shear behavior, which needs to be clearly understood. The interface shear behavior (i) is influenced by the applied shear rate due to the coupled effect of the viscosity of MSC and the hydraulic conductivity, known as the rate effect; and (ii) depends on the surface roughness of FRP, which is found to evolve due to the presence of quartz particles in MSC, resulting in strength degradation, termed as the abrasion effect. The combined effects of rate and abrasion are difficult to assess but must be fully considered for better design and analysis of FRP piles, seawalls or caisson foundations in MSC. Therefore, an accurate predictive approach to account for these effects is highly desirable. This project aims at developing an integrated computational model through a thorough study from fundamental theory to practical applications to elevate our predictive capability of the MSC-FRP interface and enhance our understanding of the interface hydro-mechanics. Molecular approach will be employed to simulate interactions between soil particles and FRP at atomic scale, towards a thorough understanding of their fundamental mechanism. The rate and abrasion effects on the interface shear behavior will be investigated using laboratory and discrete approaches. These approaches will be further integrated into a multiscale hydro-mechanical interface finite element for tackling engineering-scale problems. This project will constitute a first-ever systematic multiscale study on MSC-FRP interface. It will offer a novel and reliable hydro-mechanical interface modeling tool with rigorous microstructural characterizations, and provide a theoretical basis to understand rate and abrasion-dependent interface behavior to avoid eventual dysfunction or failure of marine infrastructures. It will contribute significantly to disaster prevention and mitigation for marine infrastructures in Hong Kong and around the world. 香港擁有1178公里的蜿蜒海岸線，圍繞著主島及臨近263個島嶼。近海岸的地基土主要由海相粉質黏土構成，這些土的性質與香港大量的海洋基礎設施的設計和運營安全息息相關。對於這些海洋基礎設施建造，鋼作為一種傳統材料常常被採用於管樁、海堤或沉箱基礎的製作和施工。然而，鋼結構的腐蝕對相關基礎設施的長期服役性能造成了極大風險。近年來，一種抗腐蝕的新型纖維複合材料（FRP）受到了廣泛關注，可作為鋼的替代材料來構築基礎，以抵抗腐蝕並增加海洋基礎設施的耐久性。值得注意的是，用FRP材料構築的樁、海堤或沉箱基礎的服役性能在很大程度上取決於海相粉質黏土和FRP材料界面的相互作用，需要我們有清楚的認識。 界面剪切性能受以下兩方面影響: (i)由於海相粉質黏土的粘性和滲透性耦合效應而產生的界面剪切速率效應；以及(ii)受FRP材料表面粗糙度影響，在剪切過程中FRP結構界面受海相粉質黏土中的石英顆粒磨損而造成的強度衰減，即為磨損效應。目前界面強度的剪切速率效應和磨損效應沒有被同時考慮和評估，但這種耦合影響需要在FRP樁、海堤或沉箱基礎設計分析中被充分考慮。因此，提出一種精確預測這兩種效應對界面特性影響的方法是有很必要的。 本項目通過系統的基礎理論到實際應用研究，旨在提出一個計算模型，來預測和研究海相粉質黏土和FRP材料界面相互作用的其水力學特性。我們首先採用分子動力學方法從原子尺度出發，來模擬土顆粒和FRP材料相互作用的力學規律，從而理解界面特性的基本機理；接著採用離散元方法和室內試驗來研究剪切速率和結構面磨損對界面剪切性能的影響。這些研究方法和結果將最終被整合到多尺度水力耦合有限元界面模型中，來解決工程尺度的問題。 本項目將首次開展對海相粉質黏土和FRP材料界面相互作用的多尺度研究，並提出一種新型可靠的考慮微觀機理的水力耦合界面模型，為界面的剪切速率和磨損影響提供理論依據，以避免海洋基礎設施出現病害或破壞。本項目將會對香港以及全球海洋基礎設施病害的防災與減災作出重要貢獻。

15217220.label: Realisation of objectives
15217220.value: All of the objectives have been achieved through the following activities along with the original plan. (1) We proposed the friction rules of interactions between clay particle (different clay minerals), silt particle (only quartz selected) and epoxy of FRP foundation structure in marine environment (saturated compared to dry state) through MD simulations. The rate effect of interactions and the abrasion effect of quartz-to-epoxy were also considered through simulations. In details, atomic structures of the considered minerals were achieved from the “American Mineralogist Crystal Structure Database”, and the atomic structure of the epoxy was constructed using the commercial MD software “Material Studio” with its structural formula. The interaction between atoms, called “Force Field”, was defined with the potential energy function. The CLAYFF force field was employed in modeling. Then, the interaction of whole atomic structures was modeled in a limited size simulation box. The open source code LAMMPS (an open-source Molecular Dynamics Simulator) was used for calculation. Different sizes of the atomic structure of the considered material were built and applied for simulations in order to find the representative size of the simulation model. For each interaction, under different normal stresses (’n) using three different shear rates were performed, based on which, the rate-dependent friction rules for all interactions were obtained. In addition, for the interaction of quartz-to-epoxy, the abrasion was particularly examined through the contact between the tip of a rectangular pyramid of quartz with a layer of epoxy. All proposed models were integrated into the DEM open source code LIGGGHTS. (2) For the 2nd objective, the experimental tests with microstructural analyses and the numerical tests by CFD-DEM were adopted as two complementary approaches. We set up the interface direct shear box with direct measurement of local PWP with a mini-hole at the interface. The interface shear tests were followed by an in-depth microstructure analysis using Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry (MIP) analyses. Freeze-dried small specimens close to interface were used to minimize the disturbance of soil samples. For numerical simulations, the unresolved coupled CFD-DEM approach based on two open source codes was established and used: the DEM code LIGGGHTS for solid and the CFD code OpenFOAM for fluid. Compared with other materials, the interaction between clay particles is induced by the non-contact short-range van der Waals attraction and long-range electrostatic repulsion. In addition, the rate-dependent inter-particle models were implemented for contacts via user-defined contact models. The clay and silt particles were approximated by clumps with overlapping spheres. In order to analyze the damage of FRP surface, the FRP was modeled with plate made of bonded particles with the size of particle according to the 3D laser-scanning images of FRP, in which the bond breakage representing surface abrasion was modeled. Then, direct interface shear tests were conducted for MSC-FRP interface characterization. Based on all results, (i) the evolutional abrasion of FRP surface roughness was proposed, (ii) the evolution and distribution of pore water pressure was clarified, (iii) the evolution and distribution of soil fabric was plotted and formulated. (3) For the third objective, the phenomenological interface models and the micromechanics-based interface model were developed. These models were designed to describe the influence of shear rate and normal stress on the shear behavior of interfaces between clay and structure plate. The models generally include three key features: (1) the application of overstress theory to account for the viscous behavior of clay-structure interfaces, (2) the transfer of the failure plane from the clay inside to the interface, which captures the softening phenomena in interface shear testing, and (3) the integration of the critical state framework for clay-structure interfaces with an analytical solution of pore pressure dissipation, illustrating the effects of shear rate under drained and partially drained conditions. An explicit numerical scheme was proposed to simulate the coupled mechanical and hydraulic behaviors with the pore pressure generation and dissipation processes. The interface models were implemented via FRIC scheme in ABAQUS, and validated against model tests.

15217220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217220.value: For Objective 1: The research team has focused on the interactions between surface (epoxy) of FRP and some major components of MSC (e.g. Kaolinite, Quartz), which control the performance of foundations, but remain unclear. The rate-dependent friction models of interactions and the abrasion model of quartz-to-epoxy have also been quantified. We proposed these interfacial models through the molecular dynamics (MD) approach and implemented hereafter into DEM code. For Objective 2: The rate-dependent interfacial shear strength and the strength degradation of the MSC-FRP interface are often accompanied by the evolutional abrasion of the FRP surface, and the evolution and distribution of the pore water pressure linked to drainage condition and soil fabric in the interface shear zone and surrounding soil. We focused on these three controlling factors through experimental and numerical studies. We have clarified the physics behind these behaviors through both laboratory and CFD-DEM (Computational Fluid Dynamics - Discrete Element Method) approaches. For Objective 3: We developed CFD-DEM models and phenomenological interface models that faced both theory and practice need of a robust coupled hydro-mechanical interface model considering rate and abrasion effects on the interface shear strength. Due to the prohibitive computational cost using CFD-DEM approach to solve real-scale problems and lack of physics in phenomenological interface models, we also developed the multiscale hydro-mechanical continuous interface finite element based on the knowledge and the quantitative observations drawn from the CFD-DEM modeling for application to engineering-scale foundation problems of marine infrastructures.

15217220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217220.value: The research carried out and the outcomes achieved provide us a good potential for further development of some interesting aspects, which has been preliminarily investigated and can be further investigated in the future: (1) effect of other clay minerals that not considered in this project, (2) effect of OCR for the part of clay, (3) effect of water with different chemicals, (4) effect of silt/clay fraction, and (5) effect of cyclic loading. There is an urgent need to improve the fundamental understanding when using such kind of new sustainable FRP materials in geotechnical structures. One PhD student trained in this project plans to work on these problems as a postdoctoral fellow.

15217220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217220.value: In Hong Kong, the coastline is rich of marine silty clay (MSC) deposits. In the construction of marine infrastructures, a new type of corrosion-resistant material, fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP), has received increasing attention as an alternative of steel in foundations to avoid corrosion and provide sustainability benefits to marine infrastructures. 15217520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15217520.value: 相对拟利普希兹性质及其应用

15217520.label: Project Objectives
15217520.value: We will develop neighborhood necessary condition and sufficient condition for set-valued mappings to have the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed set by virtue of normal cones of a restricted graph. We will introduce a projectional coderivative of set-valued mappings and apply it to establish a verifiable generalized Mordukhovich criterion for the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set. We will apply the obtained results in Research Tasks 1 and 2 to investigate the Lipschitz-like property relative to a set of a level-set mapping and the stationary point set of the l_1-norm convex optimization problem.
rows: We will develop neighborhood necessary condition and sufficient condition for set-valued mappings to have the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed set by virtue of normal cones of a restricted graph.

We will introduce a projectional coderivative of set-valued mappings and apply it to establish a verifiable generalized Mordukhovich criterion for the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set.

We will apply the obtained results in Research Tasks 1 and 2 to investigate the Lipschitz-like property relative to a set of a level-set mapping and the stationary point set of the l_1-norm convex optimization problem.

15217520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217520.value: Stability analysis of set-valued mappings is to determine intuitively verifiable conditions to guarantee that the accuracy of the solutions obtained increases with the degree of approximation of the initial data. The literature on the subject is vast when the study is of global nature. Lipschitz-like property is one of the properties at the center of stability theory. By virtue of coderivative, Mordukhovich criterion provides a necessary and sufficient condition of the Lipschitz-like property and has widely been applied in the study of solution mappings of various linear and nonlinear systems. One important assumption of the Mordukhovich criterion is that the candidate point is in the interior of the domain of set-valued mappings. This is a very restrictive assumption. On one hand, the candidate point under consideration may be at the boundary of the domain of set-valued mappings. On the other hand, in order to guarantee some stationarity conditions one may only need a regular behavior of the constraint systems with respect to one single critical direction, not on the whole space. Thus there is a great demand to study characterizations of Lipschitz-like property relative to a set. This project will investigate characterizations of the Lipschitz-like property relative to a set for set-valued mappings and their applications. We will employ regular normal cone and limiting normal cone of a restricted graph of the set-valued mapping to obtain some neighborhood necessary condition and sufficient condition respectively for set-valued mappings to have the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed set. We will introduce a projectional coderivative of set-valued mappings and apply it to establish a verifiable generalized Mordukhovich criterion for the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set. We will study the representation of the graphical modulus of a set-valued mapping relative to a closed and convex set by using the outer norm of the corresponding projectional coderivative value. We will apply the obtained results to investigate the Lipschitz-like property relative to a set for a level-set mapping and the stationary point set of an l_1-norm convex optimization problem. 集值映射的稳定性分析是为了确立直观可验证的条件，以确保所获得的解的准确性随初始数据的近似程度而增加。基于全局性研究的相关文献非常广泛。在稳定性分析中，拟利普希兹性质尤为关键。凭借上导数，莫尔杜霍维奇准则给出了检验拟利普希兹性质的充分和必要条件，而且被广泛应用于各种线性和非线性系统解集映射的研究。莫尔杜霍维奇准则成立的一个重要的假设：参考点必须位于集值映射有效域的内部。然而这个假设非常有限制性。一方面被考虑的参考点可能在集值映射有效域的边界上。另一方面为了保证一些稳态性条件时，我们只需要考虑约束系统相对于某个临界方向上的正则行为。因此对于相对拟利普希兹性质的研究迫在眉睫。 本项目将研究集值映射的相对拟利普希兹性质的刻画及其应用。运用集值映射限制图集的正则法锥和极限法锥, 我们将获得相对拟利普希兹性质的邻域必要条件和邻域充分条件。我们将引入集值映射的投影上导数以及把它应用到建立相对于闭凸集的拟利普希兹性质的可验证广义莫尔杜霍维奇准则。利用相应投影上导数的外范数, 我们将研究集值映射相对于闭凸集的拟利普希兹性质的图模表达形式。我们将把得到的结果应用于研究水平集映射和一范数凸优化问题的稳定点集的相对拟利普希兹性质。

15217620.label: Project Objectives
15217620.value: Investigate the use for direct modulated laser for high order signal generation and coherent detection. Through optimization of system parameters to maximize overall system capacity. Study DSP algorithm for the systems investigated in 1 and 2 using single sample per symbol to simplify the overall detection algorithm.
rows: Investigate the use for direct modulated laser for high order signal generation and coherent detection. Through optimization of system parameters to maximize overall system capacity.
Study DSP algorithm for the systems investigated in 1 and 2 using single sample per symbol to simplify the overall detection algorithm.

15217620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217620.value: Due to the ever increasing capacity requirement of short reach communication systems, current intensity modulated direct detection(IMDD) based system can no longer meet the system requirement. In the past ten years, coherent detection techniques based on narrow linewidth laser, external IQ modulator and digital signal processing techniques at the receiver have been shown to be an effective technique for realizing very high capacity optical transmission system over tens of thousand kilometer transmission distance. However, use it directly in short reach optical communication systems has not been possible due to the high system cost and high system power consumption. How to realize a simplified coherent detection system using low cost optical components is certainly an important research challenge. In the proposed research, we will explore a few possible approaches to realize this objective. We will study coherent detection based on direct modulated laser(DML). Through optimization of system parameters including bias current and modulation amplitude and through using full field information including amplitude and differential phase, transmission capacity of the system can be maximized. In addition, we will investigate the use of DML to generate complex modulation signals. Through optimization of the realization of the signal detection algorithm, overall system complexity can be reduced. We will also explore the use of coherent detection system using remotely delivered local oscillator(LO). Issues related to singularity in the detection system due to randomly varied polarization state of the LO at the receiver will be analyzed and solutions will be investigated both theoretically and experimentally. It is anticipated that the study shall enable significant reduction of the system complexity for future short reach coherent communication systems and enables its use deeper into the data centre systems. 由于短距光通信容量需求的日益增涨，目前基于强度调制直接监测(IMDD)的光通信技术已经不能满足系统的需求。过去的十多年中，基于窄线宽激光器，IQ外调制器及接受器端数字信号处理的相干检测光通信系统已经被证明可用于上万公里的高容量光通信传输。可是由于价格及功耗的问题，相干系统并没能广泛地用于短距光通信系统。 如何利用低成本光器件实现简化相干光通信系统是一个很好的研究挑战。在拟研究的课题中，我们将研究如何实现这个目标。 我们将研究基于直接调制激光器（DML）的相干光通信系统。通过优化包括偏制电流，调制幅度和包括幅度，相位变化的场信息的系统参数，我们希望能实现系统容量的最大化。同时我们将研究如何利用DML来产生复杂调制信号，通过优化信号检测算法的实现，我们希望能以此减小整体系统的复杂度。

15217620.label: Realisation of objectives
15217620.value: Optical communication technology is essential for providing broadband connectivity in data centres for connecting servers and switches. The rapid advancement of AI technology has also called for high speed connectivities. How to increase transmission speed per data link while keeping cost and energy consumption low is always a challenge. In this project, we have explored various schemes for realizing high speed and low cost data transmission links. In particular, we have studied a iterative pre-EDC algorithm based on the Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) algorithm. Very good results have been obtained. We have also studied various implementation issues of DSP algorithm based on absolute-term nonlinear equaliser. Through collaborating with Sun Yat-sen university, good experimental results have been obtained. By evaluating the characteristics of the direct modulated laser, through using its frequency chirp characteristics, simplified coherent detection has been realised. In addition, simplification in coherent detection algorithm has been realised.

15217820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15217820.value: 探究高鎳層狀材料不同晶面形成SEI膜的各向異性

15217820.label: Project Objectives
15217820.value: To synthesize large single crystalline nickel-rich layered oxide particles with different atomic ratios of Ni:Cr:Mn. To characterize the electrochemical properties and the evolution of solid electrolyte interphase layer on different crystallographic planes of the synthesized NLO single crystalline grains under different cut-off voltages. 15217820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217820.value: Nickel-rich layered oxides (NLO) are gradually coming into the market as attractive cathode materials for advanced high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries due to their very attractive practical capacities (>200 mAh/g) and low cost. However, those NLO materials tend to lose their capacity and show voltage decays upon cycling due to surface structure reconstruction and the formation of unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The current understanding of the SEI formed on the cathode, namely the cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), is much less than the SEI on the anode side. To fully understand the capacity and voltage decays in NLO cathode materials, we propose to conduct a detailed study on CEI under different cut-off voltages. To have a more precise understanding on the evolution of CEI layer on different crystallographic planes of NLO particles, we will use near-field optical spectroscopy to break the diffraction limit and explore the phase evolution in a more precise way than the conventional way of investigation, which is conducted over a bulk scale without the differentiation of crystal anisotropy. Supplemented with in-situ electrochemical strain mapping and in-situ X-ray diffraction techniques, we will be able to figure out the whole picture of detailed phase evolution not only in the CEI layer, but also on the out-most surface layer of NLO itself. The obtained experimental data, together with first-principles calculations, will help deepen our knowledge on the CEI and surface reconstruction of NLO cathode material, leading to the full understanding of the mechanism of capacity fading and voltage decay of NLO. The results obtained will guide us in the control of morphology, design of nanostructure, and optimization of composition for the further enhancement of the electrochemical performance of NLO cathodes, which can be further extended to the case of lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes. The proposed research will be constructive in the searching of an effective method to fabricate high energy density lithium-ion batteries with long cycle life and stable voltage output. 高鎳層狀氧化物由於其具有高比容量（>200 mAh g-1）和低成本等優勢，被認為是極具吸引力的並能逐步實現商業化的先進高能量密度鋰離子電池的正極材料。然而在充/放電過程中，高鎳層狀氧化物表面結構重構和不穩定固態電解質（SEI）膜的形成導致其比容量和電壓的快速衰減。目前人們對正極材料表面形成的SEI膜（即正極/電解液界面相，CEI）了解要遠少於負極材料。針對上述問題，本項目提出通過一系列不同截止電壓下SEI膜形成和演變的研究，闡明高鎳層狀氧化物比容量和電壓的衰減機理。本項目擬采用近場光學光譜技術精確地揭示高鎳層狀氧化物不同晶面CEI膜的演變，該方法有別於傳統的基於塊體對晶體各向異性不加區分的檢測方法，並可打破衍射技術的極限。借助於原位電化學應力譜和原位X射線衍射技術，我們能研究高鎳層狀氧化物近表面結構演變及其CEI膜演化的全貌。上述研究結果結合第一性原理計算可更深入地闡明高鎳層狀氧化物表面重構和CEI膜形成原因，進而揭示其容量和電壓衰減機理。本項目研究結果可指導後續通過形貌調控、納米結構設計和組分優化來進一步提升高鎳層狀氧化物的電化學性能，並可拓展至下一代富鋰正極材料相關改性研究。本項目為長壽命、電壓穩定的高能量密度鋰離子電池的構築提供了一種有效策略。

15218320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15218320.value: 平行網絡班輪聯盟的效率和穩定性

15218320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218320.value: After suffering more than 10 years of low or negative earnings following the 2008 financial crisis, an unprecedented structural change has occurred within the global liner shipping industry. Struggling to stay afloat (sic), all the major liner shipping companies (LSCs) have joined alliances based on Vessel Sharing Agreements (VSA), hoping to limit the active shipping capacity, increase the load factor, and stay profitable. This dominance of alliances on the major trade routes has generated huge concerns from global shippers, container ports, and national and regional competition law regulatory bodies. Their main concerns include potential freight rate increases, reduction in service quality and social welfare. This proposal aims to answer three essential questions for alliances among members serving on the same route: 1) whether social welfare is necessarily lower; 2) whether the alliances are stable when the market recovers; and 3) whether the market freight rate is necessarily higher, considering both the VSA and non-VSA alliances. Both analytical modelling and empirical tests are proposed in this study. For analytical modelling, the following is proposed: a Bertrand game to model the competition behaviour and resulting equilibrium prices; a cooperative game model for that of non-VSA alliances; and a cost minimization model for joint capacity decisions and individual contribution problems. Using empirical tests, this study also attempts to identify whether an alliance is a good strategy if the market recovers, and whether they have already resulted in price increases along the major trade routes. In practice, this research can improve LSC strategies in changing markets by taking into account the possible responses from both other industry stakeholders and the regulations. This is now particularly important, as on one hand many major carriers are still suffering from negative operating margins, and on the other hand joining alliances cannot guarantee positive earnings—it sacrifices flexibility and diminishes service differentiation, especially for smaller solo players. As for public policy, this research can help regulatory bodies in re-assessing Block Exemption (BE) for liner shipping, which is due in 2020 for Hong Kong. The results of this research can also assist in the debate for further BE if the regulatory body considers social welfare as one of the decision factors. The theoretical contributions of this proposal concern the economic efficiency of liner alliances in parallel networks in changing markets, which has been well studied in the aviation industry, but still shows a gap in shipping research.

15218720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218720.value: Recent years have seen an accelerated upsurge in the use of cold-formed steel tubular members in various onshore and offshore structural applications. The advancements in metallurgical science, fabrication techniques and increasing use of highly sophisticated automatic equipment caused a robust change of production from normal strength steel (NSS) with yield strength less than 460 MPa to high strength steel (HSS) with yield strength equal to or greater than 460 MPa, and typically 690 MPa or beyond. Compared to NSS, HSS offers novel architecture and structure design possibilities through the unparalleled merits of high strength, improved toughness, high strength-to-weight ratio and weldability as well as reduced transportation, handling, erection time and costs. Unlike traditional tubular joints, which are fabricated by directly welding the brace member(s) on the flange of the chord member, a novel configuration can be obtained by either rotating the brace, chord or both the members along their respective longitudinal axis by an angle equal to their cross-sectional diagonal plane. With the rotation of only brace member(s), the configuration is referred as brace-rotated joint, when only chord member is rotated then the configuration is referred as square bird-beak joint, and when both the brace and chord members are rotated then the configuration is termed as diamond bird-beak joint. Such novel members-rotated joints were first fabricated for their aesthetic appeal, and afterward, found to be helpful in reducing the wind loads and improving the load capacity. The use of high strength steel is very limited in construction due to the lack of investigation and adequate design rules. However, the construction sector requires high performance materials, thus, the recent trend has been slanted towards steel materials with nominal yield strengths of 460 MPa or beyond. For tubular joints, the applicability of design rules in most of the international codes are limited up to S460 steel grade. The lack of design specifications for HSS tubular joints is an urgent issue and needs an immediate attention to fully utilise the potential merits offered by HSS. Therefore, an investigation, comprising HSS tubular sections of S960 steel grade, is proposed in this project. The objectives of this project are to conduct a series of experiments on cold-formed HSS brace-rotated, square bird-beak and diamond bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints under brace axial compression, perform numerical investigation and comprehensive parametric studies, and finally propose new design rules for HSS tubular joints with these innovative configurations. 近年來，冷彎型鋼管在各種近海和陸上結構的應用急劇上升。由於冶金科學和制造技術的發展，以及高度精密的自動化設備的應用，使得鋼材的生產制造在強度上產生了重大變革，從名義屈服強度小於460MPa的普通強度鋼材跨越到了名義屈服強度不小於460MPa，通常為690MPa甚至更高的高強度鋼材。相對於普通強度鋼材，高強鋼材具有高強度、高韌性、高強重比和可焊性，以及在運輸與搬運和施工周期帶來的降低成本效益，使其為建築和結構的創造性設計提供可能。傳統的鋼管節點是將支管構件直接焊接於主管構件的翼緣上，創新型的鋼管節點形式與傳統節點的構造不同，創新型節點可以將支管構件或者主管構件或者其兩者沿著其縱軸方向旋轉壹定的角度，該轉角等同於其橫截面對角線平面角。若只旋轉支管構件，節點形式稱為支管旋轉式管節點，若只旋轉主管構件，節點形式稱為鳥嘴式方管節點；若同時旋轉主管與支管，則構成了鉆石鳥嘴式管節點。這種新型的節點的應用始於其優美的外觀，而後，研究發現其可以降低結構風荷載以及改善結構承載力。 由於缺少研究以及足夠的設計準則，高強鋼材在建築結構上的應用非常有限。然而，建設部門要求使用高性能材料，因此，近來的趨勢偏向於使用具有名義屈服強度等於460MPa或者更高的鋼材。對於鋼管節點，大多數國際設計規範的設計準則只適用於不大於S460（名義屈服強度等於460MPa）等級的鋼材。缺少高強鋼管節點的設計規範是壹項緊迫問題，這需要引起高度重視以使得高強鋼材所具有的優越性可以得到充分利用。因此，本項目基於S960（名義屈服強度等於960MPa）等級的鋼材對鳥嘴式焊接節點進行研究。本項目的目標是對軸力作用下冷彎高強X型和T型創新型鋼管節點的結構性能進行驗研究和數值模擬研究，X型和T型創新型節點的設計包括支管旋轉式管節點、鳥嘴式方管節點以及鉆石鳥嘴式管節點。最總提出適用於這些創新型高強鋼管節點的設計準則。

15218720.label: Realisation of objectives
15218720.value: The behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel (HSS) bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints has been investigated. The tubular joints were under axial compression at the brace members. Material properties of the HSS tubular members were determined by a series of tensile coupon tests. In addition, a series of cold-formed HSS brace-rotated and square bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints was performed. The joint strengths and failure modes of the HSS bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints were obtained from the test program. The load-deformation curves of the HSS joints were also obtained. Furthermore, finite element (FE) models for cold-formed HSS brace-rotated and square bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints were developed and validated using the test results. The joint strengths, failure modes and load-deformation curves obtained from the test program compared well with the predictions obtained from the finite element analyses. Hence, an extensive parametric study using the calibrated FE models by including a broad range of brace and chord dimensions, ratios of brace-to-chord width, brace-to-chord thickness and chord width-to-thickness was performed. The experimental and numerical results obtained from this project were used to compare with the existing design strength predictions. It is shown that the existing design provisions are not suitable for the design of cold-formed HSS tubular joints. Therefore, new design rules for the ultimate limit state resistance of cold-formed HSS brace-rotated and square bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints have been proposed. Overall, the objectives of this project have been achieved.

15218720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218720.value: The test specimens of cold-formed high strength steel brace-rotated and bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints were carefully designed and fabricated. A series of coupon tests was conducted to determine the material properties of the high strength steel test specimens. Test results of cold-formed high strength steel brace-rotated and bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints under axial compression were obtained from this project. Finite element models of cold-formed high strength steel bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints were carefully developed. The numerical models were verified against the test results obtained from this project. Finite element results were also obtained from an extensive parametric study of the cold-formed high strength steel bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints. It should be noted that new design rules for cold-formed high strength steel bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints have been proposed. Seven high quality international journal papers have been published from this project.

15218720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218720.value: Further development of this research could be focused on cold-formed high strength steel bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints under fire condition and post-fire condition. In addition, other type of joints, such as Y-joint can be investigated.

15218720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218720.value: This research project focused on innovative joint shapes, where steel tubes are connected by rotating them in different ways using high strength steel. High strength steel is much stronger than normal steel, allowing buildings and bridges to be designed more efficiently, using less material and reducing construction and transportation costs. The cold-formed high strength steel bird-beak tubular T- and X-joint designs not only offer improved aesthetics, but also provide greater resistance to heavy loads. However, the lack of guidelines for using these joints in construction has limited their application. In this project, high strength steel joints were tested in the laboratory and analyzed using computer models. As a result, new design rules for cold-formed high strength steel brace-rotated and square bird-beak tubular T- and X-joints have been proposed. These findings could help engineers construct stronger, safer, and more cost-effective structures in the future.

15218820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218820.value: Computer-aided design has become an indispensable tools for optimizing and innovating combustion energy conversion devices in response to the contemporary concerns on climate change and energy security. Developing a quantitatively predictive combustion modeling capability is the critical area that requires advances to support the design. The identified key scientific problems for combustion modelling are combustion chemistry, turbulence/chemistry interaction, and spray, all of which require modelling various physical/chemical processes occurring at length scales being substantially smaller than the device size. The proposed research aims to tackle one of the important sub-problems pertinent to spray modelling: quantitatively predicting the outcomes (e.g. coalescence and bouncing) of droplet collisions in spray. The existing computer simulations are incompetent at quantitatively predicting droplet collision outcomes because they are incapable of simultaneously capturing all the essential flow phenomena of droplet collision, which span over from the sub-millimeter scales of droplet deformation, to the sub-micrometer scales of rarefied gas flow, and eventually to the nanometer scales of the van der Waals force. The proposed research aims to establish the required theoretical models for these physics occurring at below millimeter scales. Computer simulations and experimental validations will be conducted to examine the capability of the models for quantitative predictions. The proposed research will make small but firm steps towards quantitatively predictive spray modelling. 面對氣候變化和能源安全方面的挑战，計算機輔助設計已經成為優化和革新燃燒能源轉化設備不可或缺的工具。發展定量可預測性的燃燒模型能力是支撐這些優化和革新的關鍵。其中公認的重要科學問題包括燃燒化學模型、湍流-化學相互作用模型、和噴霧模型。這些問題的共同難點在於需要對發生在多尺度上的各種物理化學過程進行建模。本項目旨在研究噴霧模型中的壹個重要子問題：定量預測噴霧中液滴的碰撞。 已有的各種計算機模擬方法在定量預測液滴碰撞存在不足。這源於它們無法捕捉到跨越多個尺度的各種物理現象：亞毫米尺度上的液滴變形、亞微米尺度上的稀薄氣體動力學、和納米尺度上的範德華力。本項目旨在對亞毫米尺度以下的液滴碰撞物理建立可靠模型，通過計算機模擬和實驗來驗證模型在定量預測方面的表現。本項目的成功將會是定量預測噴霧方面有意義的壹步。

15220020.value: 傳統AI模型使用從終端設備收集的資料在中央雲上訓練。 這導致較高的通信成本，較長的回應時間和隱私問題。 最近，邊緣智慧支援在靠近數據來源的網路邊緣進行學習和部署AI模型。 邊緣智慧的現有工作包括聯邦學習[7]和參數伺服器。它們採用了分散式機器學習框架。在該框架下，邊緣伺服器使用本地數據分別訓練自己的模型，而位於雲上的集中式主節點則不停對邊緣伺服器的模型參數進行聚合和更新。集中式模型聚合面臨諸如性能瓶頸，可伸縮性差和單點故障等缺點。Gossip學習[8]使用分佈式聚合框架來解決上述問題。 但是，由於模型聚合中未考慮邊緣伺服器上的數據分佈，其收斂速度較慢，推理精度較低。 在該項目中，我們提出了一種新的去中心化模型學習方法，命名為E-Tree學習。E-Tree學習利用邊緣伺服器上優化設計過的樹結構在收斂速度和推理準確性上獲得較好的性能。在該樹結構中，葉子節點表示模型學習的工作者，非葉節點代表模型聚合器。 通過樹結構的優化以及樹上聚合的位置和順序的調度，可以最大程度地提高聚合的並行性，從而加快訓練的收斂性並提高推理的準確性。 本專案中待解決的問題如下。 首先，在構建模型聚合樹時，我們需要根據邊緣伺服器上的數據分佈對邊緣伺服器進行分組，決定聚合樹的層級和結構。 其次，在調度聚合操作時，我們需要根據計算資源，網路拓撲和頻寬來決定在哪個邊緣伺服器以及何時進行聚合。此外，在解決前兩個問題中，我們需要解決E-Tree 學習中數據Non-IID（非獨立同分佈）問題。 總而言之，該專案為推進邊緣計算和AI技術做出貢獻。 它有助於邊緣智慧中的分散式學習和並行聚合，能廣泛應用於各個領域。 為了展示學術價值和實際影響，我們將開發E-Tree學習的原型系統以及基於E-Tree的示範應用。

15220020.label: Realisation of objectives
15220020.value: We have finished all the objectives listed in the proposal. The first objective is to investigate the requirements and the challenges of decentralized model learning and design the E-Tree learning framework. We have systematically investigated and identified the challenging issues of distributed machine learning in edge computing environments, including single node failure, heterogeneous resources, and the Non-IID problem. We have designed and developed a new decentralized model training framework, named E-Tree, to support large-scale model training. E-tree is a configurable collaborative model training paradigm that adopts a generic tree structure, supporting adaptive optimization based on data distribution and network resources. The second objective is to develop the algorithms and mechanisms to address the challenges issues, including aggregation tree design and optimization, model aggregation scheduling and E-Tree specific solution to the Non-IID problem, and conduct both theoretical analyses and/or simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms and mechanisms. We have studied four specific problems. The first problem is to solve the non-IID among edge devices [J2022a]. The second problem is to optimize the aggregation structure and aggregation frequency to improve the learning accuracy and convergence speed in distributed model training [J2023a]. The third problem is to develop a distributed edge intelligence system to support the fast deployment of AI-empowered applications and optimize their performance [J2021a, C2021a, J2022b]. The fourth problem is to develop a mechanism to ensure secure data sharing among edge nodes [J2023b, C2022b]. As follows are the details. First, we study the personalization of ML models in distributed model training to solve the non-IID issue. One popular technique is personalized federated learning, which aims to train each participant with customized model that can fit them well. In existing literature, meta-learning has been regarded as an important technique to achieve personalized federated learning, due to its fast adaptation capability. It first obtains a single global model, and each client achieves a personalized model by fine-tuning the global one with its local data. However, existing meta-learning-based approaches implicitly assume that the data distribution among different clients is similar, which may not be applicable due to the property of data heterogeneity in federated learning. To solve the problem, we propose a group-based federated Meta-learning framework, called G-FML, which adaptively divides the clients into groups based on the similarity of their data distribution, and the personalized models are obtained with meta-learning within each group. Specifically, we develop a simple yet effective grouping mechanism to adaptively partition the clients into multiple groups. Our mechanism ensures that each group is formed by the clients with similar data distribution such that the group-wise meta-model can achieve “personalization” at large. By doing so, our framework can be generalized to a highly heterogeneous environment. The experimental results show that our framework improves the model accuracy by up to 13.15% relative to the state-of-the-art federated meta-learning. Second, we study the joint optimization of the aggregation structure and frequency jointly in dynamic edge computing with the objective to minimize the global loss function. Generally speaking, achieving the desired performance of distributed training on edges requires the aggregation structure and frequency to fit well with the dynamic edge environment. However, existing works either consider the optimization of the aggregation structure or the aggregation frequency. Further, they often assume that the edge environment is stable and deterministic. To jointly determine the appropriate structure and frequencies to accommodate the time-varying edge environment, we propose AutoSF, an automated aggregation structure and frequency optimization approach. The main idea of AutoSF is that when the edge environment changes, the automated machine learning approach, termed AutoControl, is triggered to search out the near-optimal aggregation structure and frequency that fit well with changing edge resources. AutoControl leverages prior knowledge about grouping and frequency optimization to narrow down the search space and is equipped with an adaptive evaluator, which combines analytic models and data-driven ML models to estimate the metrics in time efficiency and grouping effectiveness. Besides, when the environment keeps unchanged, we design a heuristic algorithm termed AdjustCluster, to dynamically tune the aggregation structure and frequency based on the observed training results to further tame the statistical heterogeneity caused by non-IID data. Experimental results show that AutoSF achieves up to 16.3X speedups in convergence speed and 31.0% increase in training accuracy compared to benchmark approaches. Third, we study the collaborative real-time pedestrian re-identification across multiple cameras. The problem is to deploy computing-intensive machine learning (ML) models at resource-constraint edge devices to handle multiple input video streams, with the objective of minimizing the latency. Most works leverage edge-cloud collaboration by offloading inference tasks to the cloud, which leads to long transmission latency. Some works adopt edge-edge collaboration, where each edge device collaborates with others to provide surveillance services. However, they do not jointly optimize the scheduling of camera streams and ML tasks offloading among edge devices, which leads to inferior performance. Fourth, we study the secure data sharing across devices. In distributed machine learning, data may be frequently transmitted among edge nodes, and between edge nodes and servers. How to protect data privacy is an important issue. Traditional methods usually studied from the software aspect, such as encryption and differential privacy. Instead, we present StrongBox, the first GPU TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) for secured general computation on Arm endpoints. During confidential computation on Arm GPUs, StrongBox provides an isolated execution environment by ensuring exclusive access to the GPU. Our approach is based in part on a dynamic, fine-grained memory protection policy as Arm-based GPUs typically share a unified memory with the CPU, a stark contrast with Intel-based platforms. Experiments show that StrongBox successfully ensures the GPU computing security with a low (4.70% -15.26%) overhead across several indicative benchmarks. The third objective is to develop a prototype for E-Tree learning with example applications to demonstrate the effectiveness and performance of our proposed algorithms and mechanisms. We have developed a prototype to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed solutions for distributed machine learning in collaborative edge computing environments. We have developed EdgeTB, a hybrid emulation testbed that can be used to generate a large number of emulated edge nodes and network-flexible test environments while incorporating real physical nodes to guarantee fidelity. We have conducted extensive case studies and experiments to demonstrate the usability of EdgeTB for high-fidelity evaluation of distributed machine learning solutions.

15220020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220020.value: Our research findings and outcomes include four aspects. First, we have developed a personalized federated learning solution to address the Non-IID issues in distributed model training at Edge. We have designed and developed G-FML, a group-based federated Meta-learning framework to solve the problem, which adaptively divides the clients into groups based on the similarity of their data distribution. Specifically, we developed a simple yet effective grouping mechanism to adaptively partition the clients into multiple groups, ensuring that each group is formed by the clients with similar data distribution such that the group-wise meta-model can achieve “personalization” at large. The experimental results show that our framework improves the model accuracy by up to 13.15% relative to the state-of-the-art federated meta-learning. Second, we have designed a joint aggregation structure and frequency optimization mechanism to accelerate model training and improve accuracy in distributed model training. We have proposed AutoSF, an automated aggregation structure and frequency optimization approach, adapting to changing edge environments. We designed AutoControl, leveraging prior knowledge about grouping and frequency optimization to narrow down the search space. We developed AdjustCluster to dynamically tune the aggregation structure and frequency based on the observed training results to further tame the statistical heterogeneity caused by non-IID data. Experimental results show that AutoSF achieves up to 16.3X speedups in convergence speed and 31.0% increase in training accuracy compared to benchmark approaches. Third, we have developed a distributed edge intelligence system to support collaborative real-time video surveillance for across multiple cameras. The proposed solution enables multiple cameras stream the videos to different edge devices, which collaborate with each other to share computation resources and data. Experiments show that our proposed system can achieve near real-time pedestrian tracking and re-identification through efficient task scheduling. This platform has been deployed in PolyU and Beijing Normal University (Zhuhai) for pedestrian counting and safety monitoring, helping improve operation efficiency. Fourth, we present StrongBox, the first GPU TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) for secured general computation on Arm endpoints to facilitate secure data sharing among edge devices and between edge devices and servers. StrongBox provides an isolated execution environment by ensuring exclusive access to the GPU. Experiments show that StrongBox successfully ensures the GPU computing security with a low (4.70% -15.26%) overhead across several indicative benchmarks.

15220020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220020.value: We have conducted a set research to validate the effectiveness of the proposed distributed model training framework in edge computing. We envision that further research can be done in two aspects to extend the impact. One direction is continuous model updating considering the streaming data. Continual learning enables models to adapt incrementally to new data or tasks without requiring retraining from scratch or forgetting previous knowledge. This is essential in dynamic edge environments where data distributions evolve. In collaborative continual learning, edge devices can perform local continual learning to personalize models based on user behavior and environment changes, improving relevance and accuracy over time. Collaborative continual learning frameworks combine continual learning with privacy-preserving distributed training, addressing data heterogeneity and concept drift in edge settings. Another direction is to support large model fine-tuning at Edge. With the explosive growth of large AI models (e.g., LLaMA, GPT variants) and the increasing demand for domain-specific adaptation, fine-tuning large models directly on or near edge devices is becoming critical. This reduces latency, preserves data privacy, and customizes models for local contexts. Edge-based fine-tuning supports injecting private enterprise knowledge, improving instruction-following capabilities, and reducing hallucination in large models, which is vital for vertical AIoT applications.

15220020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220020.value: This research makes a significant contribution to the distributed model training in collaborative edge computing. In particular, this research proposes a novel promising training framework, namely E-Tree, and addresses the key issues of the framework, with the objective to accelerate the distributed model training and improving model accuracy. Several novel problems, including non-IID data, resource-aware model aggregation and structure adjustment, secure data sharing among distributed edge nodes, have been investigated and studied in this project. We have also demonstrated the efficacy of our proposed solution by developing a prototype that enables large-scale testing for distributed machine learning solutions in a collaborative edge computing environment. Based on that, we also developed a collaborative edge intelligence platform to support low-latency and privacy-preserving video analytics. This platform has been deployed in PolyU and Beijing Normal University (Zhuhai) for pedestrian counting and safety monitoring. This research does not only lead to advances in the task scheduling theory in edge computing but also provides significant impact by enabling emerging advanced applications, including autonomous vehicles, video analytics, and smart cities.

15220120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220120.value: Emerging ubiquity of mobile devices, data centers, cloud computing, AR/VR, 5G wireless and Internet of Things(IoT) applications impose insurmountable transmission speed requirements far beyond the capabilities of all types of communication systems. One of the most fundamental physical limitation lies in backbone long-haul optical communications where fiber Kerr nonlinearity induce nonlinear phase shift that depends on the instantaneous signal power, distort and degrade the signal quality and hence limit the achievable transmission speed and distance. Over the past two decades, numerous attempts to mitigate Kerr nonlinear effects were proposed with receiver digital signal processing(DSP) algorithms receiving the most attention. However, all the proposed algorithms are highly complex, not amendable to practical implementation and the intricate interactions between inline amplifier noise, Kerr nonlinearity and fiber chromatic dispersion render them ineffective especially in wavelength division multiplexed(WDM) environments. On the other hand, transmitter-based signal design such as pre-distortion and constellation shaping were proposed but they provide marginal performance improvements compared with receiver DSP in compensating nonlinear effects. In this connection, we note that since optical fibers are dispersive nonlinear systems, the instantaneous power waveform(that is proportional to the Kerr nonlinear phase shift) depends on the overlapping of neighboring pulses and therefore the overall signal-dependent nonlinear distortions actually depend on the symbol sequence and not individual information symbols. Therefore, symbol sequence design, or source coding, for fiber nonlinearity mitigation should be the correct framework to fundamentally address fiber nonlinear effects. This represents a potentially whole new design dimension for nonlinearity mitigation but has been given little attention in the research community. The objectives of the proposed research are to elucidate the fundamental performance gain and lay down concrete steps to realize the aforementioned nonlinearity-tolerant source coding for long-haul optical communications impaired by fiber Kerr nonlinearity. In particular, we will 1)investigate the theoretical gains and tradeoffs in signal-to-noise ratio(SNR)/achievable information rate(AIR) for systems with QAM and general signalling techniques; 2)derive practical algorithms to characterize symbol sequence-dependent nonlinear distortions and enhance other DSP blocks in presence of nonlinearity-tolerant source coding for optimal performance and 3)conduct proof-of-concept single-channel and WDM transmission experiments. The successful completion of the proposed research will open up new avenues in DSP research to addressing the decades-old fundamental issue of fiber nonlinearity. The key experimental demonstrations and unique insights developed will advance transmission capacities to the next level and serve as a key enabler for communication networks Worldwide in the next decade. 移動設備，數據中心，雲計算，AR / VR，5G無線和物聯網（IoT）應用的興起帶來了無與倫比的傳輸速度要求，遠遠超出了所有類型的通信系統的能力。最基本的物理限制之一是骨幹網遠程光通信，其中光纖Kerr非線性會引起非線性相移，該相移取決於瞬時信號功率，使信號質量失真並降低信號質量，從而限制了可實現的傳輸速度和距離。在過去的二十年中，提出了許多減輕Kerr非線性效應的嘗試，其中接收器數字信號處理（DSP）算法引起了人們的極大關注。但是，所有提出的算法都非常複雜，無法實際實施，並且在線放大器噪聲，Kerr非線性和光纖色散之間的複雜相互作用使其無效，尤其是在波分複用（WDM）環境中。另一方面，雖然提出了基於發射機的信號設計，例如預失真和星座圖整形，但與接收機DSP相比，它們在補償非線性影響方面提供了邊際性能改進。在這方面，我們注意到由於光纖是色散非線性系統，因此瞬時功率波形（與Kerr非線性相移成比例）取決於相鄰脈衝的重疊，因此，與信號有關的整體非線性失真實際上取決於噪聲。符號序列，而不是單個信息符號。因此，用於減輕光纖非線性的符號序列設計或源代碼編碼應該是從根本上解決光纖非線性影響的正確框架。這代表了緩解非線性的潛在全新設計維度，但在研究界卻很少受到關注。 這項研究的目的是闡明基本性能增益並製定具體步驟，以實現上述針對光纖Kerr非線性受損的長距離光通信的非線性容忍源編碼。 特別地，我們將：1）研究具有QAM符號序列的非線性容忍系統的信噪比（SNR）/可達到的信息速率（AIR）的理論增益和折衷； 2）推導實用的算法來表徵符號序列相關的非線性失真，以增強接收器信號的處理性能； 3）在耐非線性的源編碼上進行概念驗證的單通道傳輸實驗。 這項提議研究的成功完成，將為DSP研究開闢新的途徑，以解決數十年以來光纖非線性的基本問題。 關鍵的實驗演示和獨到的見解將使傳輸能力提高到一個新水平，並在未來十年內成為全球通信網絡的關鍵推動力。

15220120.label: Realisation of objectives
15220120.value: We proposed to jointly modulate both the eigenvalue 𝝀 and b-coefficients 𝒃(𝝀) of the sequence of 1-soliton pairs in discrete eigenvalue nonlinear transmissions with the mean of 𝝀 alternate between 𝜶+1𝒊 and −𝜶+1𝒊, followed by decoding as composite 2-solitons signals. We extended to dual-polarization(DP) systems and proposed shifting the signal in one polarization by half a symbol period to improve transmission performance. We further proposed to pre-code the b-coefficients of second-order soliton sequences by the analytically tractable offset induced by collisions between 2 solitons to pre-set the relative timing of the pulse sequence for improved detection performance. The effectiveness of the proposed schemes are verified numerically and experimentally in terms of SNR, BER and/or transmission distance. Hence, objective 1 is fully achieved. Regarding digital signal processing(DSP) algorithms development for systems with signal sequence design for nonlinear transmissions, we propose a method to improve the accuracy of calculating b-coefficients, especially for highly nonlinear signals and signal sequences. We also developed a pre-distortion scheme for DP systems to equalize pulse-collision induced distortions and numerical results show a transmission distance extension by a factor of three. We also proposed back rotating the nonlinear spectral phase by half of the transmission distance for discrete eigenvalue transmission systems. Performance improvements of the above schemes are characterized analytically or through simulations. A further extension is to develop the algorithmic framework to optimally combine machine learning and adaptive signal processing for nonlinear compensation and beyond and it has been verified experimentally. Objective 2 is fully achieved. Finally, we conducted single-channel and WDM experimental investigations of the effectiveness of sequence selection techniques with carrier phase noise and polarization effects. Using practical and common nonlinear distortion metrics such as Energy Dispersion Index(EDI) and lowpass-filtered symbol-amplitude sequence(LSAS) with a list-encoding constant composition distribution matcher(L-CCDM) on 4-coding-bits appended to a given symbol sequence (i.e. 16 possible candidate sequences), the SNR gain of sequence selection techniques is around 0.28 dB and 0.18 dB using LSAS for single-channel and 5-WDM-channel transmissions over 800 km respectively. Furthermore, jointly modulating 𝝀 with 16-QAM and 𝒃(𝝀) with 16-APSK experiment was conducted and a record single-polarization discrete eigenvalue transmission of 64 Gb/s (net 54 Gb/s) over 1200km is demonstrated, followed DP record transmission of 81Gb/s DP discrete eigenvalue transmission over 650 km. Experiments in 7 × 288 Gb/s DP-16QAM systems over 1125 km are also conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the joint ML/adaptive DSP framework. With all the aforementioned experimental demonstrations, objective 3 is fully achieved.
