15220120.value: To design signal sequence to improve nonlinear transmission performance, we proposed to jointly modulate both the eigenvalue 𝝀 and b-coefficients 𝒃(𝝀) of the sequence of 1-soliton pairs with mean of 𝝀 alternate between 𝜶+1𝒊 and −𝜶+1𝒊[C8.1], followed by decoding superimposed received waveforms as composite 2-solitons signals. We jointly modulate 𝝀 with 16-QAM and 𝒃(𝝀) with 16-APSK and a record single-polarization discrete eigenvalue transmission of 64 Gb/s (net 54 Gb/s) over 1200km is experimentally demonstrated. We also extended to dual-polarization(DP) transmissions[C8.3] and proposed shifting the signal in one polarization by half a symbol period, which led to record 81Gb/s DP discrete eigenvalue transmission over 650 km. We further proposed in[C8.7] to pre-code the b-coefficients of second-order solitons by the analytically tractable offset induced by collisions between 2 solitons to pre-set the relative timing of the pulse sequence[C8.7] for improved detection performance. For receiver DSP, we proposed a method[C8.4] to improve the accuracy of calculating b-coefficients, especially for highly nonlinear signals and signal sequences. We also analytically derived the distortions to DP signals arising from symbol sequence designed to have pulse collisions along transmissions, revealing that the distortions depends on polarization angle and differential polarization phase[C8.6]. We propose a pre-distortion equalization scheme and achieve three times extension in transmission distance. In [C8.7],[C9.2], we propose back-rotating the nonlinear spectral phase by half of the transmission distance for discrete eigenvalue transmission systems. We analytically and experimentally prove its optimality and show the advantages of lower complexity compared to other algorithms. More generally, we proposed[C8.2] to treat adaptive DSP blocks as extra stateful neural network(NN) layers in a single large NN to optimally incorporate Learning(ML) algorithms to existing DSP for polarization and carrier phase effects mitigation. Experiments in 7×288 Gb/s DP-16QAM systems over 1125km demonstrated its effectiveness. Furthermore, we conducted single-channel and WDM experimental investigations[C8.8] of the effectiveness of sequence selection techniques with practical impairments. Using common and practical nonlinear distortion metrics such as EDI and LSAS with L-CCDM on 4-coding-bits appended to a given symbol sequence (i.e. 16 possible candidate sequences), the SNR gain of sequence selection techniques is around 0.28 dB and 0.18 dB using LSAS for single-channel and 5-WDM-channel transmissions over 800 km respectively. This provide good guidance to its effectiveness and practicability in realistic optical communications systems.

15220120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220120.value: The theoretical gains and associated signal processing algorithms developed in this project are preliminary demonstrations of the potentials of source coding for long-haul transmissions in presence of Kerr nonlinearity. Much remains to explore to reveal the ultimate potentials of source coding and transmitter design, including more efficient sequence selection algorithm with runtime close to linear as supposed to brute-force enumeration. With more advanced source coding methodologies, computational complexity characterizations of the developed efficient encoding algorithms will be the next necessary step to calculate the additional complexity compared to existing signal processing and determine the marginal utility of source coding in practical transceivers chipsets. Furthermore, extensions to joint multi-channel source coding and their benefits in multi-channel and/or multi-band environments are important areas of future research.

15220120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220120.value: Connection speeds and transmission distance of long distance optical communications are fundamentally limited by the nonlinear interactions between signal and noise in the fiber medium (called Kerr effect) which creates distortions to the signal that is difficult to be removed. In this project, we investigated how to design the transmitted signals (also known as source coding) including the transmitted sequence among other aspects, together with appropriate receiver signal processing to improve long-distance transmission performance in presence of Kerr nonlinearity. We characterized the theoretical gains of source coding for long-haul links with different lengths, and derive necessary algorithms at the receiver to recover such specially designed transmitted signals. Experiments are conducted to illustrate the advantages and other challenges of the proposed source coding schemes in a practical environment, thus helping to lay the foundation and pave a new direction to increasing transmission speeds and distance for long-haul communications.

15220220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220220.value: 混凝土是渠道工程結構中使用最廣泛的建築材料。然而，由於微生物代谢引起的腐蝕，大量的渠道混凝土隨著時間的流逝而劣化。渠道系統工程中的這種微生物所引起的腐蝕主要是由微生物代谢產生的生物酸（生物硫酸）所引起的。香港目前利用海水沖洗系統，在當地污水中的硫酸鹽（500- 600 mg / L）濃度很高，這驅使了更多H2S和硫酸的產生，於是這種微生物腐蝕在香港渠道系統工程中尤爲明顯。傳統波特蘭水泥通常應用與混凝土中，但其具有很弱抵抗生物酸侵蝕的能力，在侵蝕中由於石膏和鈣礬石膨脹產物的形成，混凝土表面會腐蝕，這會進一步產生結構損壞甚至失效，從而導致渠道系統工程服務中斷。因此，在許多大型城市中，污水處理基礎設施的微生物腐蝕問題是一個十分緊迫的問題，迫切需要找到一種修復方案。而且，同時也注意到香港正在產生大量的廢玻璃和污泥焚化灰（ISSA），它們目前大多在垃圾填埋場進行處理，尋找合理回收方法也是政府目前必須解決的緊迫任務。 以前實驗研究已表明，ISSA含有大量的鋁矽酸鹽和一定數量的重金屬（鋅和銅）。於是，ISSA可以充當地聚物的前驱体和重金屬殺菌劑的來源。廢玻璃粉 （WGP）由於主要是無定形二氧化矽組成，其可以參加地聚反應過程，並可以用作天然細骨料的替代品，以改善所生產的地聚物砂漿的耐酸性。鑒于此，如果能利用本港目前的兩種固體廢棄物（即ISSA和廢玻璃）用於開發抗菌地聚物複合材料並應用於渠道結構修復，將是非常有發展前途的。 此項目將結合ISSA，廢玻璃粉和廢玻璃碎玻璃，開發一種新型的抗菌和耐酸的地聚物複合材料，並作為污水處理基礎設施的修復材料。該研究項目將評估ISSA和廢玻璃基地聚物的殺菌潛力以及力學和耐久性能。香港理工大學與英屬哥倫比亞大學將進行一起合作，將進行全面的實驗室研究，包括利用一系列先進的微觀結構分析技術來揭示開發的地聚物在惡劣的污水處理環境下的耐腐蝕性能機理，將採用加速的實驗裝置來模擬渠道環境條件以及渠道結構中的微生物腐蝕過程，並對開發的地聚物中重金屬的浸出進行研究，以最大程度地減少對環境的潛在影響。因此，通過該項目進行的創新研究，必將為ISSA和廢玻璃的潛在回收利用提出更好的出路，並能夠開發出一種經濟，耐用且環保的渠道系統結構工程修復材料。

15220220.label: Realisation of objectives
15220220.value: This project has successfully achieved its main objectives through thorough experimental and analytical efforts. The key outcomes, ranging from material development to performance validation under both simulated and real sewage conditions, are outlined below in accordance with each project objective. Objective 1: To develop a novel anti-bacterial and acid-resistant geopolymer as a repair material for sewerage infrastructure rehabilitation using ISSA, WGP, and WGC This objective has been fully achieved. The project has led to the development of an innovative alkali-activated materials (AAMs)/geopolymer binder system utilizing locally available waste resources, including incinerated sewage sludge ash (ISSA), waste glass powder (WGP), and waste glass cullet (WGC). The formulation of AAMs demonstrated that: • Incorporating up to 75% WGP substantially reduced the occurrence and severity of efflorescence, a common durability issue in humid environments, similar to sewerage systems. • Optimal mechanical performance was achieved with 50% WGP, delivering 1.70 MPa bond strength and ~3500 µstrain shrinkage, which meets the requirements for sewerage repair mortars. • The addition of WGC further contributed to shrinkage reduction. Moreover, the use of air pollution control residues (APCR) as a partial activator replacement significantly controlled drying shrinkage. Specifically, 20% APC replacement led to a 30–50% reduction in shrinkage, and the sulfate content contributed to ettringite formation, aiding dimensional stability. Objective 2: To investigate the corrosion-resistant performance of ISSA- and WG-based geopolymers by examining their deterioration in mechanical and durability properties This objective has been fully met through both laboratory and real-environmental assessments. ISSA was integrated into optimized geopolymer formulations and tested under accelerated conditions simulating sewage corrosion and real field exposure. The binder containing 50% WGP, 40% GGBS, and 10% ISSA showed the thinnest biofilm layer, indicating superior performance in mitigating microbial-induced concrete corrosion (MICC). Additionally, calcium aluminate cement (CAC) was trialed as a partial replacement (15%) for ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) in geopolymer mortars. The CAC-containing mixes exhibited improved durability and MICC resistance, attributed to the formation of aluminum-rich phases. These findings confirm the improved corrosion resistance of ISSA- and WG-based alkali-activated composites, validating their use in aggressive sewage environments. Objective 3: To assess the biocidal activities of ISSA- and WG-based geopolymer under the sewerage environment and dissect the underlying mechanisms This objective was also comprehensively realized. The antimicrobial behavior of the developed geopolymer systems was evaluated using DNA sequencing, which revealed: • A significant reduction in corrosive bacteria, including the lower abundance of 16S rRNA gene and dsrB, associated with sulfate-reducing bacteria. • Reduced microbial diversity and biofilm thickness in ISSA-containing mortars, indicating an inhibitory effect on microbial colonization and activity. These results suggest that heavy metals embedded in ISSA likely contribute to the biocidal effect, within environmental safety limits as stipulated by BS EN 12457 guidelines. Optimization and Application Potential The optimal compositional ranges for developing class R4-grade repair mortars (BS EN 1504) were determined to be: • GGBS: 50–100% • WGP: 0–45% • ISSA: 0–25% These optimized formulations provide a strong foundation for full-scale implementation in Hong Kong’s sewerage rehabilitation projects, supporting the city's circular economy goals by valorizing local solid waste streams. Ultimately, all three project objectives were successfully met without encountering any major shortfalls. Challenges such as variability in ISSA/APCR composition were addressed through material pre-treatment and formulation adjustments. The project's outputs, which include ten peer-reviewed articles in SCI journals, emphasize its scientific value and practical significance. The findings offer crucial insights for developing sustainable, durable, and antimicrobial repair materials for infrastructure applications in extreme environments.

15220220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220220.value: As summarized in Part C, this project has resulted in ten publications in SCI journals and one is under review (total = 11). To enhance environmental security and resilience for sustainable development, there is an urgent need to develop effective recycling strategies for ISSA/APCR from T·Park and waste glass in Hong Kong. This project investigated the use of these waste materials in alkali-activated materials (AAMs), with a particular focus on their performance in humid and harsh environments such as sewer systems. Efflorescence, a common issue in alkali-activated materials, was significantly reduced by incorporating waste glass powder (WGP). Specifically, adding 75% WGP to alkali-activated slag (AASG) markedly decreased efflorescence severity. The project also addressed challenges related to poor bond strength and shrinkage, which can cause delamination in AAMs. The optimal WGP content for alkali-activated repair materials (AARMs) was determined to be 50%, achieving a bond strength of 1.70 MPa and shrinkage of approximately 3500 µstrains. The inclusion of glass cullet alongside 50% WGP further reduced shrinkage. Additionally, air pollution control residues (APCR), which contain SO₄²⁻ and Cl⁻ ions, were used as partial activator replacements to control shrinkage in AAMs. Incorporating 20% APCR led to a 30%–50% reduction in drying shrinkage. Sulfate from unwashed APCR acted as an activator and expensive agent, promoting ettringite formation and improving shrinkage performance, while washed APCR contributed aluminosilicates as a precursor. On the other hand, Incinerated sewage sludge ash (ISSA), a Si-Al-rich material containing some heavy metals, was incorporated into optimized mixtures to mitigate microbial-induced concrete corrosion. Under intensified sewage corrosion tests, the mixture containing 50% WGP, 40% GGBS, and 10% ISSA developed a significantly thinner biofilm layer. DNA sequencing further confirmed a substantial reduction in corrosive bacteria (as indicated by 16S rRNA gene and dsrB concentrations) and decreased microbial diversity in the biofilm on ISSA-incorporated binders. Given the superior performance of calcium aluminate cement (CAC) in sewage environments, its effects were evaluated in GGBS/GP-based composites under real sewage conditions. Replacing 15% GGBS with CAC in alkali-activated cement (AAC) mortars enhanced resistance to microbial-induced corrosion, which is attributed to the increased Al content in the AAC gels. Finally, the recommended ranges for producing class R4 repair mortars should be: 50–100% GGBS, 0–45% GP, and 0–25% ISSA. These findings provide valuable guidance for future full-scale applications of these sustainable binders in local wastewater infrastructure.

15220220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220220.value: This research lays a strong foundation for sustainable infrastructure rehabilitation using waste-derived, alkali-activated materials. Future development will focus on upscaling the optimized binder formulations for pilot-scale trials in actual sewerage systems in Hong Kong. Long-term field performance, including durability under dynamic flow conditions and microbial activity, will be monitored. Further studies will also identify minimal inhibitory concentrations of heavy metal ions (Zn/Cu) specifically for sulfur-oxidizing bacteria (e.g., Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans). Advanced characterization techniques will be employed to understand the role of various forms of heavy metal ions in waste, which are crucial for inhibiting microbial growth and promoting biocidal mechanisms. Ultimately, the goal is to facilitate technology transfer through collaboration with municipal authorities and industry stakeholders, thereby supporting large-scale deployment.

15220220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220220.value: Several solid wastes, such as incinerated sewage sludge ash (ISSA) and air pollution control residues (APCR), contain trace heavy metals (Zn and Cu) that can pose health and environmental risks when disposed of in landfills. Although waste glass is chemically stable, it is non-biodegradable and occupies valuable landfill space. Nevertheless, these materials possess unique properties that can be advantageous. This project investigated repurposing these wastes into alkali-activated repairing materials for sewerage systems. The incorporation of ISSA (~10% of the binder) resulted in mixtures that released small but controlled amounts of heavy metals (within environmental regulations), which inhibited bacterial growth (as evidenced by reductions in SRB/SOB through microbiome analysis) in sewage systems and exhibited lesser deterioration depths. Meanwhile, waste glass (in terms of glass powder (~50% of the binder) and glass cullet (~100% as fine aggregate) improved bonding, shrinkage, efflorescence, and chemical compositions of resulting reaction gels, making it more suitable for such conditions. Furthermore, incorporating 20%APCR led to a 30%–50% reduction in drying shrinkage and acted as an expensive agent. These findings provide valuable guidance for the large-scale implementation of this project, addressing minimal reliance on imported raw materials, environmental hazards, and enhancing the performance of wastewater infrastructure.

15220320.value: 傳統集中式機器學習框架要求將所有不同來源用於訓練的數據上傳到遠程數據服務器，這會導致大量的通信開銷和服務延遲，以及用戶隱私的洩漏。為使分佈式計算節點能夠協作訓練模型而不會暴露其自身的數據，Google提出了聯邦學習並對其進行了廣泛的研究，但基於一個不完全符合實際的同質化假設，即參與學習過程的設備具有類似的計算和通訊能力，而且其上的訓練數據是獨立且均勻分佈的（IID）。 本項目將全面研究實際環境異構設置下的聯邦學習，即移動設備擁有非IID數據，並且它們具有獨特的計算和通信能力。我們旨在解決以下挑戰： 1）數據的非IID問題很難克服，因為移動設備不共享其數據，並且我們無法獲取有關數據分佈的信息。同時，設備硬件和網絡的異構性使得移動設備之間的學習過程難以同步，這可能會嚴重降低學習速度。 2）有關不同移動設備上可用資源的超參數很難設置，這對訓練的準確性和效率至關重要。 3）在異構環境下的聯合學習是一個複雜的系統，其性能受許多因素影響，例如數據分佈，訓練批處理大小，以及網絡質量。基於啟發式算法設計或凸優化技術的傳統方法很難有效解決此類大規模複雜系統中的問題。 於本項目我們首先設計一種基於學習的數據選擇方法從非IID數據構建一組IID數據來解決上述挑戰，該方法不依賴於數據內容的知識。然後，我們將應用強化學習聯合優化超參數設置和資源分配來解決設備異質性，從而加快訓練速度。之後，我們將設計計算卸載機制，以實現移動設備上的高效機器學習。最後，我們將實現一個原型系統，以驗證我們的理論研究結果並評估我們提案的效果。 本研究課題將解決實踐中聯邦學習的核心挑戰，以期待聯邦學習可以在更多應用（例如移動醫療，個人理財管理，和自動駕駛）中充分發揮其作用，從而帶來顯著的社會效益。

15220320.label: Realisation of objectives
15220320.value: The proposed project aims to address critical challenges in federated learning, particularly those arising in realistic deployment scenarios involving non-IID data, system heterogeneity, and constrained client resources. Over the first half of the project period, we have made substantial progress toward all the major objectives laid out in the proposal. Below, we elaborate on the realisation status of each objective, major technical approaches, and encountered challenges. Objective 1: Design of Adaptive Federated Learning Algorithms under Non-IID and Resource Constraints. We developed a novel adaptive federated learning framework, in which each client dynamically configures its local training behavior such as batch size, learning rate, local steps, and participation based on local conditions like data distribution and computational capability. This approach effectively addresses performance degradation under non-IID data distributions and diverse resource constraints. The solution is based on deep reinforcement learning, where a controller learns an optimal policy for each client. The design incorporates a well-defined state space, action space, and reward function that reflect local learning dynamics. This adaptive approach significantly improves test accuracy on non-IID image and speech datasets compared to standard methods such as FedAvg. Objective 2: Unified Framework for Joint Optimization of Local Training and Global Aggregation. We proposed a joint optimization strategy that unifies the design space of local training parameters and global aggregation weights. This enables synergy between local adaptation and server-side aggregation, mitigating client drift and improving robustness under heterogeneous settings. Specifically, we developed a gradient similarity-aware weighting scheme in which clients with divergent updates receive lower aggregation weights. This mechanism is integrated with the reinforcement learning-based local adaptation, resulting in improved convergence and generalization performance across tasks with severe data imbalance. Objective 3: Theoretical Analysis of Federated Learning under Adaptive Configuration. We derived theoretical convergence guarantees for federated learning under varying batch sizes and client participation levels. The analysis establishes that the convergence rate is influenced by the interplay of client-side configuration and server aggregation. These theoretical results provide formal justification for our adaptive strategy and were used to design the reward signal in the controller. This contributes to a stronger connection between empirical learning heuristics and optimization theory, offering more principled guidance for practical FL deployments. Objective 4: Real-World Application and System Evaluation. We conducted extensive evaluations on standard datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR-10, as well as on a speech command dataset to simulate on-device learning. The proposed framework outperforms baselines like FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD in both accuracy and efficiency under non-IID conditions. Furthermore, it demonstrates the ability to reduce computational costs on weak clients while maintaining global performance. A large-scale real-world deployment on edge or mobile devices is still in progress. We are preparing a prototype on a federated edge emulator to study end-to-end latency, communication cost, and controller overhead. Challenges Encountered and Mitigation Measures: The first major challenge is the computational overhead introduced by the DRL controller. To address this, we reduced the state and action space, used lightweight models, and trained policies offline for reuse. The second challenge is the difficulty in profiling client heterogeneity in real-time. We mitigated this by using local loss statistics and label entropy as proxies. A third challenge is balancing global model accuracy and fairness among clients. We added fairness-aware terms into the reward design and are now exploring multi-objective reinforcement learning. In conclusion, we have achieved most of the key objectives proposed in the original plan. The developed adaptive federated learning framework effectively addresses practical issues related to data and system heterogeneity. Our methods are theoretically grounded and have shown significant empirical benefits. Ongoing work is extending the system toward more realistic deployments and enhanced fairness. The project is progressing on schedule without significant deviation.

15220320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220320.value: The first major finding of this project is that client-level adaptation, when jointly optimized with server aggregation, can significantly enhance the performance of federated learning under realistic non-IID and resource-constrained settings. We demonstrate that using a deep reinforcement learning controller to guide per-client training configurations leads to faster convergence, higher test accuracy, and better resource efficiency. Our approach dynamically adjusts local steps, learning rate, batch size, and participation frequency in response to client-specific conditions such as label imbalance, compute budget, or energy constraints. Another key outcome is the development of a theoretically grounded framework that connects client adaptation to global convergence properties. By deriving formal convergence bounds under variable local training configurations, we establish theoretical support for our reinforcement learning-based policies. This bridges a critical gap in the literature, where many adaptive approaches are heuristic in nature and lack analytical justification. Our research also shows that incorporating gradient similarity between clients can effectively mitigate the negative impact of model drift and outlier behavior in the aggregation step. This insight led to the design of an adaptive aggregation rule that weights client contributions based on the alignment of their gradients with the global objective. Finally, we have produced many publications based on these findings. One focuses on the adaptive configuration strategy using reinforcement learning, and the other extends this to a unified optimization framework that balances local adaptation and global stability. These results have demonstrated consistent improvements across diverse datasets and FL scenarios, laying the groundwork for more robust and deployable federated learning systems.

15220320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220320.value: The current research lays a strong foundation for several promising extensions. One important direction is to enhance the fairness of the adaptive FL framework by integrating multi-objective optimization. Specifically, we plan to extend the reinforcement learning controller to optimize not only accuracy and resource usage, but also client-level fairness metrics such as participation balance and accuracy parity. This will allow the framework to better support clients with disadvantaged data or limited capacity. Another avenue is to integrate personalization mechanisms into the adaptive strategy. While our current work focuses on a global model, many FL scenarios benefit from partially personalized models tailored to client-specific distributions. We plan to develop adaptive hybrid models that combine global learning with personalized heads, where the controller also decides the degree of personalization. In terms of deployment, we will continue to work toward a system-level prototype. We are currently building a federated edge emulator to evaluate runtime behaviors such as controller latency, client dropout resilience, and communication overhead. This will provide the necessary infrastructure to test the feasibility of deploying the proposed approach on mobile and IoT devices in real-world federated environments. We also intend to generalize the framework to support heterogeneous model architectures across clients and explore its application in vertical federated learning settings, which involve feature-partitioned data. These directions will further increase the applicability and impact of our research across domains such as healthcare, finance, and smart city infrastructure.

15220320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220320.value: Federated learning is a cutting-edge technology that allows mobile phones and smart devices to learn from data without sending it to a central server, protecting user privacy. However, real-world devices often have very different data and limited computing power, making it hard for current methods to work well. Our research focuses on making federated learning smarter and more adaptable. We designed a new system that can learn to automatically adjust how each device trains its part of the model, depending on how much data it has or how fast it can compute. This system uses a technique called "reinforcement learning", similar to how robots learn by trial and error, to make decisions that improve overall learning accuracy and speed. So far, our method has shown much better results than traditional approaches, especially when devices have very different data. This research brings us one step closer to making AI work better and more fairly across all types of devices, paving the way for smarter and more private mobile applications.

15220920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220920.value: This project is to develop novel dual-function transducers for simultaneous micro-particles manipulation and imaging. Micro-particles manipulation technology has been developed for many biophysical applications. Based on the high-resolution optical techniques, optical tweezers are able to offer precise non-contact high-resolution manipulation of micro-particles. However, the heat induced by the tightly focused laser beam limits the use of optical tweezers on the direct manipulation of biological samples. In addition, the high-resolution optical devices are complicated and expensive. Acoustic tweezers are the alternative promising approach to overcome the aforementioned limitations. Besides with the simpler setup at lower cost, the biological samples are less likely to be damaged by the acoustic energy when compared to the same wave intensity in optics. Moreover, the force of acoustic tweezers can be large enough to manipulate relatively large micro-particles. The promising features of acoustic beam have attracted considerable interest to develop acoustic tweezers. In recent years, acoustic tweezers with various operation modes have been investigated. Most studies demonstrate the micro-particles manipulation and potential practical biomedical applications, but most devices are unifunctional and complex. Monitoring is essential during manipulation to locate the trapped micro-particles and the target destination. It also has an on-going role to observe the process and assess the outcome if the manipulation purpose is for therapy delivery or cell-cell interaction study. Optical imaging is the common practice to guide and monitor the manipulation process because it provides real-time imaging with high resolution and contrast. But the bulky and expensive microscope, separated from the acoustic tweezing system, limits the flexibility of setup and further in vivo biomedical applications. Biomedical ultrasound imaging has been developed extensively for real-time guidance in the planning and delivery of therapy, but it is usually used as a standalone technology for diagnostic imaging only without treatment delivery. Here, we propose to develop novel transducers with the integration of acoustic tweezers for micro-particle manipulation and ultrasonic transducers for imaging. Our preliminary studies show that ultrasonic transducers besides traditional circular configurations could effectively perform micro-particles manipulation. To our knowledge, dual-function transducers for simultaneous tweezing and imaging in biomedical applications have not been reported previously. We plan to investigate theoretically and experimentally the synergetic effects of acoustic beams from tweezer and transducer arranged in different configurations, design and develop appropriate dual-function transducers, evaluate the overall performance in different conditions, and optimize the design parameters to achieve simultaneous micro-particles manipulation and monitoring. 本項目旨在開發新穎的可同時進行微粒操控和成像的雙功能換能器。 微粒操控技術已取得許多生物物理方面的應用。基於高分辨率的光學技術，光鑷能夠提供精確的非接觸式高分辨率微粒操控。然而高度聚焦的激光束所引起的熱量限制了光鑷在生物樣品的直接操控上的使用。另外，高分辨率光學裝置都比較複雜和昂貴。相比之下，聲鑷是有望克服上述限制的一種方法。除了以較低的成本搭配相對簡單的設置外，跟相同波強度的光能相比，生物樣品受聲能的破壞較小。此外，聲鑷的力足夠大以操控較大尺寸的微粒。 聲束獨特且有前景的特徵引發了聲鑷研究的熱潮。近年來，各種操作模式的聲鑷得到了廣泛研究。大多研究都証明了聲鑷對微粒的操控能力以及它在生物醫學領域的潛在應用，但是大多數器件都是單功能的并且設計複雜。定位和追踪目標微粒以及靶向位置在操控過程中至關重要。在藥物治療傳輸或細胞相互作用的研究應用中，定位和追踪的監察功能可以持續觀察過程並評估結果。由於可以提供具有高分辨率和對比度的實時成像，光學成像是監察操控過程的常用方法。但是笨重且昂貴的顯微鏡系统是與聲鑷系統分開的，這大大降低了整個系統的靈活性因而限制了聲鑷進一步實現在活體內的生物醫學應用。 生物醫學超聲成像已經得到廣泛的開發，可以在計劃和實施治療時提供實時指導，但通常僅作為獨立的成像診斷技術而不具備治療的功能。 在本項目中，我們提議開發一種集成用於微粒操控的聲鑷和用於成像的超聲傳感器的新型器件。我們的初步研究已表明，不同形狀的超聲換能器都可以有效地進行微粒操控。據我們所知，在生物醫學應用中，能夠同時實現操控和成像的雙功能超聲換能器還沒有被報導過。 我們計劃利用理論和實驗相結合的方法來研究來自聲鑷和成像換能器的聲束在不同配置下的協同效應，從而設計和開發出適當的雙功能換能器。然後通過評估雙功能換能器在不同條件下的整體性能對設計參數進行優化以同時實現微粒操控和成像監察。

It was found that the size of the trapped MBs cluster was directly related to the beam diameter of the focused transducer. With the same peak pressure and duty cycle, 95 the size of the trapped MBs cluster decreased as the excitation frequency increased. In the study of the effect of f-number, the trapping region of the high f-number transducer was bigger than that of the low f-number one at the same driving frequency. MBs manipulation using 12-MHz acoustic vortex-based transducers with different f-numbers. The acoustic vortex-based transducer with higher frequency and lower f-number is expected to trap smaller MB clusters, which means the capability of manipulating the targets in a much more precise approach. The effects of acoustic pressure and duty factor is closely related to the acoustic radiation force that affects the trapping speed and performance significantly. Previous research introduced the relationship between the acoustic radiation forces and acoustic pressure. As the acoustic pressure increases, the generated acoustic radiation force of the focused vortex-based transducer increases, and it would induce the acceleration of MBs trapping. Similarly, the increment of duty cycle would enhance the trapping speed and force so as to make the trapped cluster much more stable. Artificial thrombi have been developed and prepared for the in vitro thrombolysis experiments. The thrombolysis system was designed and modified based on the reported research work. The thrombolysis performance using the 5-MHz acoustic vortex-based transducer was employed and compared with the FUS-assisted thrombolysis. In conclusion, the study of thrombolysis efficiency using different treatments show that the exposure to the VUS combined with r-tPA circulation was the best thrombolysis method. The mechanism of acoustic vortex-based thrombolysis is the total effect of acoustic lateral radiation force combined with shear stress generated by the acoustic vortex, which is different from the traditional focus-mode ultrasound. Micro-streaming effect can be produced by the shear stress, which enhances the thrombolysis performance. To a certain extent, this shows the feasibility of in vivo applications using the acoustic vortex-based tweezing, which has the potential to further improve the efficiency of intravenous r-tPA in acute ischemic stroke. In short, the development of low-frequency acoustic vortex-based transducers for biomedical applications is reported. The experimental findings showed that the developed vortex-based transducers exhibited satisfactory performance, which aligned well with the simulation results. Moreover, both the MBs manipulation and in vitro III thrombolysis performance confirmed the promising potential of vortex-based transducers for various biomedical applications. The simultaneous observation of microbubbles and particle manipulation needs further effort. With dual functions ready, more work can be carried out through collaboration with other institutions. We expect that more data will be collected and published in the near future.

15220920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220920.value: Firstly, low-frequency acoustic vortex-based transducers for biomedical applications are reported. The proposed transducers fabricated using the 1-3 piezoelectric composite materials demonstrated the potential in acoustic vortex tweezing applications. The acoustic properties of 5-12 MHz vortex-based prototypes indicated that the acoustic pressure decreased when the transducer frequency increased. For the micro-bubbles (MBs) manipulation, the effects of transducer specifications (frequency, f-number) and driving conditions (acoustic pressure, duty cycle) on the performance of vortex based transducers were studied. The smaller trapping region or the trapping of smaller MBs cluster size could be induced by increasing the excitation frequency or decreasing the f-number of vortex-based transducer. For the effects of acoustic pressure and duty factor, the aggregation speed of MBs under acoustic vortex accelerated with the increasing output peak pressure and duty cycle. For the study of thrombolysis, the results presented that the efficiency under the exposure to the VUS combined with r-tPA was higher than that under the exposure to FUS with r-tPA circulation, which was also higher than the control group with r-tPA only. With the good performance of the developed acoustic vortex-based transducers, the satisfied results of MBs manipulation and in vitro thrombolysis demonstrated the great potential for various biomedical applications. In addition, high-frequency ultrasound arrays were studied. A 20 MHz phased array transducer targeting at high-resolution biomedical imaging has been successfully developed relying on replacing the active layer with a single crystal ferroelectric material PMN-0.28PT exhibiting high piezoelectric properties. By adopting our developed matching material, the fabricated transducer has achieved 85% yield rate and presented an excellent acoustic performance such as 85% -6 dB bandwidth and -45 dB crosstalk. The transducer shows 40.5 µm and 121.5 µm axial and lateral resolutions, respectively. The in-situ imaging of a fisheye and in-vivo rat cardiac imaging have been demonstrated in which the outline of organ structures can be distinguished.

15220920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220920.value: In this research, low-frequency (20-MHz) vortex-based transducer, a 36° rotated Y-cut LiNbO3 single crystal with a high longitudinal sound speed (~7340 m/s) is a good candidate. As the beam diameter of high-frequency vortex-based transducer will be smaller than that of low-frequency ones, in vitro single particle / cell manipulation may be possible to achieve. In this research work, the developed acoustic vortex-based ultrasonic transducer had only 4 piezoelectric array elements. As the number of array elements is related to the topological charge that is known to affect the beam profile and trapping performance, it is of significance to develop and study the potential performance of vortex-based transducers with more elements in various applications. In the future, vortex-based transducers with more elements, such as 8, will be designed and fabricated.

15221320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221320.value: With our human being’s significant life quality improvement along with the civilization, scientific and technology breakthroughs, access of abundant energy while maintain human friendly environment has become one of the most important challenges for the globe, as our energy supply is dominated by burning fossil fuels – oil, gas and coal. Renewable green energy is therefore of great importance to our world and human being, and solar energy is the most clean and abundant renewable energy. The current dominant crystalline silicon solar cell technology is a great success in human being renewable energy history, with significantly reduced solar electricity cost reaching grid parity through the effort of the past twenty years. However there are other potentially significant solar energy generating scenes the silicon solar cell technology cannot apply, such as flexible/portable PV, building integrated PV, transparent power application. Organic photovoltaic cell (OPV) is an emerging PV technology that has distinct advantages in many of these areas, and the efficiency has reached over 16%, making the real application of OPV technology not just a dream. Aiming at accelerating the OPV technology, we propose to tackle the challenges in OPV from the critical component – the carrier transport layers. We propose a unique class of transport materials for OPV technology – wide bandgap metal halide perovskites, which are another star solar cell materials at low bandgap. The uniqueness of this proposal is that its focus is on the much less studied wide bandgap metal halide perovskite materials, which actually have the potential to be excellent printable transport layers for OPV. These new OPV transport materials share the high mobility, tunable bandgap, excellent printability and tolerance of defects as their low bandgap counterparts, but with much better stability. We believe the thorough materials and device structure investigation of these materials, combined with ternary OPV active layer engineering, will push forward the overall OPV progress in the aspects of high efficiency, stability and being printing friendly. The proposed research represents a new front for OPV research, which integrates chemistry, physics and material science to generate new perspectives in science and come up with solutions to challenging issues in renewable energy. It will also offer a broad spectrum of research and educational opportunities for students and postdocs. 隨著一起顯著改善的人類生活質量，科技突破與文明发展，在保证人类獲取豐富的能源的同時，如何保持人類友好的環境已成為人類面臨的最重要全球挑戰之一。现在我們的能源供應主要是燃燒石油，天然氣和煤炭等化石燃料。因此，可再生綠色能源對我們的世界和人類至關重要。 太陽能是最清潔，最豐富的可再生能源。目前市场主導的晶體矽太陽能電池技術在人類可再生能源的歷史中取得了巨大的成功，大大降低了進入電網的太陽能發電成本，并通過過去二十年的努力實現了平價。但是還有其他潛在的矽太陽能電池技術無法應用的重要太陽能產生場景，例如柔性/便攜式光伏，建築集成光伏，透明電源應用等等。有機光伏電池（OPV）是一種新興的光伏技術，在這些上述許多領域具有獨特的優勢，效率近期已经達到16％以上，這使得OPV技術的真正應用不僅僅是夢想。旨在加速OPV技術，我們建議從關鍵組件來應對OPV的挑戰– 載流子傳輸層。 本研究计划中，我們為OPV技術提出了一類獨特的運輸材料 - 寬帶隙金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料。該提案的獨特之處在於其重點在於研究較少的寬帶隙金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料，實際上具有優異的潛力OPV的可打印傳輸層。這些新的OPV運輸材料具有載流子遷移率高，帶隙可調，出色的可印刷性以及對缺陷的耐受性。相对于用作活性层的低帶隙金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦對應物，寬帶隙金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料具有更好的穩定性。 我們相信，通过對這些材料進行徹底的材料和設備結構研究，結合三元OPV有源層工程，將推動整體OPV在高效，高穩定性和易於打印等方面取得進步。本计划擬議的研究代表了OPV研究的新領域，該領域整合了化學，物理學和材料科學，以產生科學的新觀點並提出解決可再生能源挑戰性問題的解決方案。它還將為學生和博士後提供廣泛的研究和教育機會。

Matter 5, 1-13 (2022) https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matt.2022.04.028 In this work, MAPbBr3 is firstly demonstrated as an effective solution-processed AIL, featuring a 2.3-eV bandgap and high hole and electron mobility. PM6:BO-4Cl based on unannealed device with the MAPbBr3 AIL exhibits an encouraging efficiency of 15.5%. F4TCNQ is further doped into MAPbBr3 to increase work function and passivate defects, boosting the efficiency to 17.3%. The ambipolar ability of MAPbBr3 in OPVs was further proved by inverted devices. Therefore, MAPbBr3 successfully serves multiple functions: a down-conversion layer, an energy donor, and a textured seeding layer influencing bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) morphology. This finding successfully demonstrates the practicability of wide-bandgap perovskite materials as highly promising OPV interfacial materials. Nano Energy, 94, 106923 (2022) doi:10.1016/j.nanoen.2022.106923 In this work, a low cost, methanol processed copper phosphotungstate (Cu003) as AIL is developed for OPVs and OLEDs. The Cu003 film features an optical bandgap of 3.9 eV, a work function of 5.08 eV, high hole mobility, and exhibits superior stability, higher transmittance and carrier extraction capacity than PEDOT:PSS, induces better optoelectronic field intensity distribution, contributing to exciton generation and recombination inhibition. Non-halogenated solvent processed OPVs incorporating Cu003 AIL and PM6:BTPBO-4Cl active layer afford a high efficiency of 17.6%, with an outstanding fill factor of 79.6%, and device based on Cu003/PM6:BTP-eC9:PC71BM affords a remarkable efficiency of 18.2%. The flexible OPVs and OLEDs incorporating Cu003 AIL are also successfully demonstrated. The research shows that the inorganic Cu003 AIL is stable, low-cost, ecologically friendly, and facile-processing for organic electronics. These issues lead to energy loss and device degradation. In this Article, we synthesize acidic magnesium-doped tin oxide quantum dots to modulate the bottom interface contact in wide-bandgap CsPbI2Br perovskite solar cells. This design balances physical, chemical, structural and energetic properties, passivating defects, optimizing energy band alignment, enhancing perovskite film growth and mitigating instability. 15221420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15221420.value: 系統演化網絡的近似算法

15221420.label: Project Objectives
15221420.value: To create and implement a fast, exact algorithm for computing the rooted triplet distance between two unrestricted phylogenetic networks. To invent a new similarity measure between two unrestricted phylogenetic networks that is superior to all the currently existing ones, and to design an algorithm for computing it. The new similarity measure should be efficiently computable as well as informative, and be able to distinguish between more kinds of non-isomorphic networks than the current measures. To develop a framework for approximating a complicated phylogenetic network by a simplified one, having the same leaf label set but smaller level and/or fewer internal nodes, while preserving as much branching information as possible. The two algorithms from points 1. and 2. above will be integrated into this framework, giving two new methods for approximately measuring the similarity between two input phylogenetic networks with no structural restrictions, ideally providing a trade-off between computation speed and accuracy.

15221420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221420.value: Phylogenetic trees are routinely used by scientists and scholars to describe evolutionary relationships. However, phylogenetic trees are unable to represent non-treelike evolutionary events that can create new species such as hybridization among eukaryotes, lateral gene transfer in bacteria, and viral recombination. This has led to the invention of the phylogenetic network model, which is a powerful extension that can describe non-treelike evolutionary events by allowing certain internal nodes to have more than one parent. A phylogenetic network can also be used to visualize conflicts among a collection of two or more phylogenetic trees in a single diagram. The enhanced expressive power of phylogenetic networks comes at a cost: extra complexity. Many combinatorial problems that are efficiently solvable for phylogenetic trees become intractable for phylogenetic networks. The goal of this project is to develop a framework for approximately solving such computationally hard problems for phylogenetic networks by applying exact (but sometimes slow) algorithms to simplified versions of the input networks. If the time complexity of an algorithm depends exponentially on some parameter such as the "level" of the input networks, we will try to find low-level networks that are similar to the input networks before applying the algorithm. We will focus on some fundamental problems related to phylogenetic network comparison. First, we will improve the running times of the fastest known algorithms for computing the so-called rooted triplet distance between two networks. Intuitively, the rooted triplet distance counts the number of small embedded subtrees that are different in the two networks; if they share a lot of branching structure then this number will be small. Next, we will develop a new similarity measure that is better than all the currently existing ones and design an efficient algorithm for computing it. Finally, we will investigate how to find a suitable replacement for a complicated phylogenetic network, having the same leaf label set but smaller level, smaller degree, fewer edges, fewer internal nodes, etc. while preserving as much branching information as possible. 系統演化樹通常被科學家和學者用來描述進化關係。 但是，系統演化樹無法代表非樹狀進化事件，這些事件可以創建新物種，例如真核生物之間的雜交，細菌中的側向基因轉移以及病毒重組。 這導致了系統進化網絡模型的發明，它是一個強大的擴展，可以通過允許某些內部節點具有多個父節點來描述非樹狀進化事件。 系統演化網絡也可以用於在單個圖中可視化兩個或多個系統演化樹的集合之間的衝突。 系統演化網絡的增強表達能力是有代價的： 額外的複雜性。 對於演化樹有效解決的許多組合問題對於系統網絡變得棘手。 該項目的目標是開發一個框架，通過將精確的（但有時是緩慢的）算法應用於輸入網絡的簡化版本，來近似解決系統進化網絡的此類計算難題。 如果算法的時間複雜度指數地取決於某些參數，例如輸入網絡的“級別”，則在應用算法之前，我們將嘗試查找與輸入網絡相似的低級網絡。 我們將關注與系統進化網絡比較有關的一些基本問題。 首先，我們將改善最快的已知算法的運行時間，該算法用於計算兩個網絡之間的所謂三重根距離。 直觀地講，根三聯體距離計算的是兩個網絡中不同的小型嵌入式子樹的數量。如果它們共享很多分支結構，那麼這個數目將很小。 接下來，我們將開發一種新的相似性度量，該度量優於當前所有相似性度量，並設計一種有效的算法來對其進行計算。 最後，我們將研究如何為複雜的系統進化網絡找到合適的替代品，該系統具有相同的葉標籤集，但級別較小，程度較小，邊緣較少，內部節點較少等，同時保留了盡可能多的分支信息。

15221420.label: Realisation of objectives
15221420.value: The project has successfully achieved its primary objectives, resulting in significant algorithmic advances for comparing and simplifying unrestricted phylogenetic networks. The new algorithms and software tools developed provide the first practical solutions for computing rooted triplet distances in general networks, and the theoretical advances lay the groundwork for future development of even more informative similarity measures. The integration of these methods into a simplification framework offers researchers flexible and efficient tools for network comparison, with broad applicability in computational biology and related fields. For Objective 1, we have Developed two new algorithms for computing the rooted triplet distance between two unrestricted phylogenetic networks, with no restrictions on in- or out-degree or network level. Achieved significant improvements in computational efficiency over previous methods. The new algorithms have running times of O(N^2 M+n^3)O(N^2 M+n^3) and O(M+N k^2 d^2+n^3)O(M+N k^2 d^2+n^3), where N, M, k, and d are network parameters as defined in the abstract. Implemented these algorithms and evaluated their performance on both simulated and real datasets. Released the first publicly available software package for computing the rooted triplet distance between unrestricted phylogenetic networks. Identified and discussed practical limitations of the rooted triplet distance, informing future research directions. For Objective 2, we have Investigated the limitations of existing similarity measures, particularly the rooted triplet distance, and explored new approaches for more informative and discriminative measures. Developed a new deterministic algorithm for constructing the frequency difference consensus tree, which retains more information than previous consensus methods and runs in O(k n log n) time. Advanced the theoretical understanding of triplet consistency problems, resolving open complexity questions and providing new algorithmic tools that can be leveraged in the design of improved similarity measures. While the primary focus was on rooted triplet-based measures, the research also contributed to the development of efficient algorithms for related problems, such as consensus tree construction and triplet consistency, which are foundational for defining and computing new similarity measures. For Objective 3, we have Developed a conceptual framework for approximating complex phylogenetic networks by simpler ones, preserving the leaf label set and as much branching information as possible. Integrated the new algorithms for rooted triplet distance (Objective 1) and consensus-based measures (Objective 2) into this framework, enabling two new approaches for approximate similarity measurement between unrestricted networks. The framework supports a trade-off between computational speed and accuracy, allowing users to select the most appropriate method for their data and research needs. The software implementation provides practical tools for the community to apply these methods to real-world phylogenetic network data. Developed two new o(n log⁡ n) algorithms for computing the rooted triplet distance in the special case of caterpillar trees, breaking the previous time complexity barrier for this important class. Provided new insights into the computational complexity of triplet consistency problems for ternary trees, resolving previously open cases and introducing novel algorithmic techniques.

15221420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221420.value: We develop two new algorithms to compute the rooted triplet distance between non-binary phylogenetic trees. We also provide implementations of our algorithms, evaluate their performance on simulated and real datasets, and make some observations on the limitations of the current definition of the rooted triplet distance in practice. Our prototype implementations have been packaged into the first publicly available software for computing the rooted triplet distance between unrestricted networks of arbitrary levels. We present two new algorithms for a special type of phylogenetic trees, in which every node has at most one non-leaf child. Both are significantly better than the best algorithm for the general cases. Our first algorithm makes use of a dynamic rank-select data structure by Raman et al. (WADS 2001) and runs in time O(n log n/log log n). Our second algorithm relies on an efficient orthogonal range counting algorithm invented by Chan and Pǎtraşcu (SODA 2010) and runs in time O(n sqrt(log n)). A consensus tree is a phylogenetic tree that summarizes the evolutionary relationships inferred from a collection of phylogenetic trees with the same set of leaf labels. Among the many types of consensus trees that have been proposed in the last 50 years, the frequency difference consensus tree is one of the more finely resolved types that retains a large amount of information. We presents a new algorithm for constructing the frequency difference consensus tree. Given k phylogenetic trees with identical sets of n leaf labels, it runs in O(knlog{n}) time, improving the best previously known solution. The R+-F+- Consistency problem is a fundamental question in building phylogenetic trees. The input consists of four sets of triplets: R+ and R- (which are resolved triplets) and F+ and F- (which are unresolved, or "fan," triplets). The goal is to find out whether there is a phylogenetic tree that contains all the triplets in R+ and F+, but excludes all those in R- and F-, and to construct such a tree if possible.

15221420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221420.value: Further refinement of similarity measures to address the observed limitations of rooted triplet distance. Extension of the simplification framework to support additional network classes and optimization criteria. Application of the developed methods to large-scale biological datasets to uncover new evolutionary insights.

15221420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221420.value: This project focused on developing new computer methods to compare and simplify complex evolutionary diagrams called phylogenetic networks, which scientists use to study how different species are related. Previous tools could only handle simple cases or required the networks to have a certain structure, limiting their usefulness. We created new algorithms that can quickly and accurately measure how different two networks are, even when the networks are very complex and have no restrictions. We also invented a new way to summarize and compare these networks, making it easier to spot similarities and differences that older methods might miss. Additionally, we built a framework that can simplify a complicated network into a smaller, easier-to-understand version, while keeping as much important information as possible. Our methods have been or can be turned into free software that researchers can use. These advances will help scientists better analyze evolutionary relationships, even when the data is messy or complicated, leading to more accurate and insightful discoveries about the history of life.

15221620.label: Project Objectives
15221620.value: The goal of this research is to investigate a new approach to improve the GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) accuracy by augmenting the PPP with high precision water vapor data from collocated microwave water vapor radiometer (WVR). The aim is to further push the envelope of technical innovation in the PPP area and to enable a wider range of applications of the PPP technique in the GNSS and geodesy communities and beyond. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Investigating the optimal water vapor augmentation schemes for the best PPP accuracy under different observation conditions, depending on GNSS satellite constellation, GNSS satellite elevation cutoff angle, weather condition, and water vapor radiometer operation approach. This will be achieved based on the test and analysis of a large of computational schemes. The result from this research will provide a technical guideline to the GNSS community of optimally using WVR to augment PPP for a higher positioning accuracy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time in the GNSS community to conduct such a study to augment PPP with high accuracy water vapor observations. (2) Identifying the optimal water vapor mapping function based on analyzing a large amount of quality controlled, real-world water vapor data recorded under different weather conditions using two different WVR observation approaches. Such knowledge, derived from big water-vapor data, will be very useful for the whole GNSS community as mapping function is used in almost every GNSS positioning computation/application. (3) For the first time in Hong Kong establishing two WVR and GNSS devices collocated supersites and generating a large, unique database of scientifically valuable, quality controlled water vapor and GNSS observations from three supersites (two at Hong Kong and one at GFZ, Potsdam, Germany). The water vapor datasets will be tremendously useful for Hong Kong Observatory’s local daily weather forecasting and global, long-term climate research. Particularly one Supersite at GFZ and one Supersite in Hong Kong, each to be equipped with two sets of WVR and GNSS devices, will generate quality well controlled water vapor data.
rows: The goal of this research is to investigate a new approach to improve the GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) accuracy by augmenting the PPP with high precision water vapor data from collocated microwave water vapor radiometer (WVR). The aim is to further push the envelope of technical innovation in the PPP area and to enable a wider range of applications of the PPP technique in the GNSS and geodesy communities and beyond. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Investigating the optimal water vapor augmentation schemes for the best PPP accuracy under different observation conditions, depending on GNSS satellite constellation, GNSS satellite elevation cutoff angle, weather condition, and water vapor radiometer operation approach. This will be achieved based on the test and analysis of a large of computational schemes. The result from this research will provide a technical guideline to the GNSS community of optimally using WVR to augment PPP for a higher positioning accuracy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time in the GNSS community to conduct such a study to augment PPP with high accuracy water vapor observations.

(2) Identifying the optimal water vapor mapping function based on analyzing a large amount of quality controlled, real-world water vapor data recorded under different weather conditions using two different WVR observation approaches. Such knowledge, derived from big water-vapor data, will be very useful for the whole GNSS community as mapping function is used in almost every GNSS positioning computation/application.

(3) For the first time in Hong Kong establishing two WVR and GNSS devices collocated supersites and generating a large, unique database of scientifically valuable, quality controlled water vapor and GNSS observations from three supersites (two at Hong Kong and one at GFZ, Potsdam, Germany). The water vapor datasets will be tremendously useful for Hong Kong Observatory’s local daily weather forecasting and global, long-term climate research. Particularly one Supersite at GFZ and one Supersite in Hong Kong, each to be equipped with two sets of WVR and GNSS devices, will generate quality well controlled water vapor data.

15221620.label: Realisation of objectives
15221620.value: Though it was with the impact of COVID-19, great efforts were invested to achieve the objectives. Centering around the objectives of this project, six (6) high quality papers have been published in international journals, including one paper in “Earth and Space Science” of the American Geophysical Union, one paper in “Geophysical Research Letters” of the American Geophysical Union; one paper “Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres” of the American Geophysical Union, one paper in “Atmospheric Research” of Elsevier, and two papers in “GPS Solutions” published by Springer (top journal in the positioning & navigation area). In addition, one journal paper draft is under preparation and the main part has been completed. The research results have been presented at one national conference and one international conference. We have studied the performance of Global Positioning System (GPS) Precise Point Positioning (PPP) under difference weather conditions and the positioning improvement from augmented water vapor data. For instance, we studied the GPS PPP under the impact of real-world water vapor data under different weather conditions, particularly the extreme weather conditions. For the objective one, we have investigated the optimal water vapor augmentation schemes for the best PPP accuracy under different observation conditions, e.g. normal weather conditions with stable water vapor dynamics and extreme weather conditions with high water vapor dynamics (e.g. tropical cyclones). In addition, we have done a series of Lab test and we found that the satellite elevation cutoff angle of 10° is the optimal one to both maximize the use of GNSS data and achieve the best GNSS positioning accuracy. The impacts of two super tropical cyclones i.e., Hato in 2017 and Mangkhut in 2018 were studied. The GPS PPP performance at seven GPS stations over the South China area, where the water vapor concentration is high, were examined. Two schemes, i.e., traditional PPP scheme and water vapor-augmented PPP scheme, were adopted to analyze the PPP results. The traditional PPP results indicate that, affected by the high level of concentration of water vapor in the tropical cyclone, the standard deviation (STD) values of positioning errors in static PPP increased by 33.3%, 6.2%, and 18.8% in the east, north, and up directions, respectively. In the kinematic PPP mode, the positioning STD errors in the east, north, and up directions increased by 11.8%, 13.5%, and 17.8%, respectively. With the augmentation of the water vapor data, the PPP positioning errors in the up direction of static PPP during tropical cyclones was reduced by 4.2%, though the improvements in the east and north directions were very marginal. With the augmentation of the water vapor data, the PPP positioning errors in kinematic PPP during tropical cyclones was reduced by 0.5%, 0.8%, and 5.5%, in the east, north, and up directions, respectively. Under different weather conditions without tropical cyclones, the level of water vapor concentration is lower. With the augmentation of water vapor data, the static PPP positioning errors were reduced by 1.8%, 0.0%, and 11.8% in the east, north, and up directions, respectively, and the kinematic PPP positioning errors were reduced by 5.5% in the up direction. Unfortunately, the kinematic PPP positioning errors in the east and north directions were increased by 1.1% and 1.7%, after augmentation of water vapor data. For the objective two, we have done a series of Lab tests and our publication indicated that the UNB3m tropospheric model is the optimal one to calculate the mapping function of tropospheric zenith wet delay and to correct the hydrostatic component of the tropospheric error in GNSS satellite signals. We also tested the performance of another positioning method, namely precise point positioning real-time kinematic (PPP-RTK) using global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals, under the augmentation of water vapor data. The 10-day positioning results showed that the GNSS three-dimensional (3D, including east, north, and up directions) root-mean squares error (3D-RMS) was reduced by 5.7% from 3.5 cm to 3.3 cm. The average ambiguity-convergence time to achieve such a stable accuracy was reduced by 46% from 10.0 minutes to 5.4 minutes. It clearly shows that the augmentation of water vapor data can significantly reduce the ambiguity-convergence time by nearly half. For the objective three, a large set of water vapor data have been generated and accumulated. This large set of water vapor data can be used to improve the precision of GNSS positioning, to improve the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO)’s weather forecasting, and many other applications such as aerosol modeling. The research team has had a few meetings with senior scientists (e.g. Dr. CHAN Siu Wai, Acting Senior Scientific Office in Forecast Operation and Mr. WONG Wai Kin, Senior Scientific Office in Forecast Development) at the HKO and we are making efforts to assimilate PolyU’s water vapor research dataset into HKO’s local daily weather forecasting and in future global, long-term climate research. This is a long-process and we will continue in this direction though the project is completed. Our collaboration efforts will not stop with the completion of the project. Through the meetings with HKO scientists, the PolyU research team is aware that many types of water vapor data have not been used by HKO, which is exactly the opportunity for PolyU researchers to fill this technical gap for HKO and for the benefit of Hong Kong community. Overall, we think we have achieved the objectives of this project. We have published six (6) high quality papers in international journals and one journal paper is still under preparation. The results have been presented at one national conference and one international conference. More importantly, the research team has had very meaningful meetings with the scientists of the Hong Kong Observatory and we have understood needs of HKO – more high quality water vapor data and the technical gaps existing in HKO’s weather forecasting systems. We are working in a very friendly and collaborative relationship to put this project’s research results into HKO’s weather forecasting models for better forecasting results in Hong Kong.

15221620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221620.value: The major findings produced from this project include several aspects. First, we have clearly shown that accurate water vapor data can significantly improve the accuracy of GNSS positioning, in both static and kinematic modes, in both precise point positioning (PPP) and precise point positioning real-time kinematic (PPP-RTK) approaches, under both stable weather condition and extreme weather conditions. This finding is significant to the GNSS community because the accurate modeling of tropospheric wet delay has long been regarded as a bottleneck that inhibits the further improvement of GNSS positioning accuracy. The results demonstrated in this project have given confidence and guideline to the GNSS community how to further improve the GNSS positioning accuracy. The extensive test results have proved that. The GNSS positioning markets in Mainland China and many other countries in the world are still growing rapidly for various industrial and business applications, including traditional and new ones, such as deformation monitoring, autonomous driving, low-altitude drone navigation, precision agricultural machine navigation, and many others. The further improvement of the GNSS accuracy is critically important. One of the findings from this project exactly serves this purpose. Another major finding from this project is that we have demonstrated that accurate water vapor data can significantly improve the performance of numerical weather prediction. Our extensive test schemes have shown that the equitable threat score (ETS) increases at 37.5% to 54.9% (depending the test schemes) of meteorological stations after the assimilation of water vapor data. After water vapor data assimilation into weather forecasting models, the probability of detection (POD) score of 6-hour rainfall forecasting for the 20 mm or more rainfall category can be improved by 0.074. This improvement represents an improvement of 7.4% when compared to the maximum ideal value (1.0). The improvement of critical success index (CSI) is 0.041, representing an improvement of 4.1% when compared to the maximum ideal value (1.0). The improvement of equitable threat score (ETS) is 0.039, representing an improvement of 3.9% when compared to the maximum ideal value (1.0). It appears that the score increases are just a few percentage. However, we should not underestimate this improvement. In the meteorological community, it is well known that improving a few percent performance is a big challenge. Our research results have clearly demonstrated that the use of high quality water vapor can significantly benefit weather forecasting. This is a very valuable application of high quality water vapor. The finding from this project affirms that the acquisition and generation of more larger amount of high quality water vapor data are crucially important. In the context of climate change, extreme weather forecasting has become more and more important. This project affirms that use of large amount of high quality water vapor data in weather forecasting models can significantly improve the rainstorm forecasting performance.

15221620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221620.value: High quality water vapor datasets have a great deal of importance and have a wide range of applications, e.g. improving GNSS positioning accuracy by augmenting the tropospheric correction models and improving the rainstorm forecasting reliability of weather forecasting models. Therefore, the generation of high quality water vapor datasets becomes a very important task with both scientific and application values. The project team will continue to develop approaches to acquire and generate high quality water vapor data and models to serve multiple scientific and application uses, e.g. GNSS positioning accuracy improvement and rainstorm weather forecasting improvement. Particularly the research team will continue the collaboration with the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). It has been clear that the research team can help fill in the technical and data gaps existing in HKO’s weather forecasting system. This renders the collaboration with the HKO more meaningful and necessary. The research team has had a number of meetings with the senior scientists of HKO and this work is still under development. The close collaboration between research team and HKO will certainly continue after the completion of this project. The research team will provide a large amount of high quality water vapor to HKO scientists for their weather forecasting improvement.

15221620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221620.value: The significance of this project lies in two aspects. First, we have shown through a lot of Lab tests and high quality publications that the GNSS positioning accuracy can be significantly improved via the augmentation of water vapor data. Various GNSS tests have been conducted during different levels of concentration of water vapor, e.g. normal weather conditions with stable water vapor structure and extreme weather conditions (e.g. tropical cyclone) with dynamic water vapor structure. Both static and kinematic GNSS positioning modes have been tested. Both Precise Point Positioning (PPP) and precise point positioning real-time kinematic (PPP-RTK) approaches have been tested. Second, the usefulness of the large amount of water vapor data from this project has been tested in weather forecasting models. The research team is still working with the senior scientists at the HKO to put the water vapor data into use by HKO scientists. The research team is pleased to know that the water vapor data can fill in the HKO’s data gap and we are still working in a friendly and collaborative relationship to put the water vapor data into HKO’s weather forecasting model. This is a long-process and we will continue though the project is completed.
