15222020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222020.value: Biomass wastes have raised critical environmental concerns, especially in densely populated cities. In Hong Kong, food waste contributes to 34% of the municipal solid waste discarded at landfills, whereas forestry wood waste is continuously generated from gardening and extreme weather events (e.g., Super Typhoon Mangkhut in 2018). Biorefinery emerges as a future solution by valorising the biomass wastes into value-added chemical products, which is a vital strategy to achieve a circular bio-economy and meet the Sustainable Development Goals. This project will tailor biochar-supported catalysts derived from wood waste and evaluate engineered biochar’s performance as a sustainable catalyst in the production of bio-based renewable chemicals. Biochar is a promising, economical adsorbent for carbon sequestration and pollutant removal as reported in our previous environmental studies. The modifiable surface functionalities and porous structure make biochar a prospective material to support catalytic sites. Compared to conventional mineral-based supports, biochar derived from biomass wastes enables a more sustainable catalyst manufacturing process at a lower cost. While expensive, noble metal catalysts (e.g., platinum, gold, palladium) are common for industrial redox reactions, we will impregnate transition metal, low-priced copper on biochar support as sustainable catalysts in this project. Mechanisms for the copper-biochar formation will be investigated via high-resolution spectroscopic analyses and computational simulations. This will generate new understanding of the synergy between biochar surface and copper precursor, which will advise controllable nucleation and growth of copper particles to serve as active nanostructures. The catalytic activity of copper-biochar will be examined in the oxidation of hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), as a model reaction representing oxidative biomass conversions. Our recent biorefinery research has revealed successful HMF production from starch-rich food wastes. This project features a continuous effort to upgrade the food waste-derived HMF to FDCA, which is a valuable precursor of bio-based polymers recognised by the US Department of Energy. We will scrutinise the critical properties of copper-biochar (e.g., active site density, chemical potential, pore architecture) that determine its catalytic activity in HMF oxidation. Kinetics and thermodynamics will be studied to elucidate chemistry at the liquid-solid interface. Our hypothesis-driven research plan will generate new scientific insights into the mechanisms for metal-biochar formation and its catalytic function, which will foster biochar materials as the next-generation catalysts for high-throughput biorefineries. The project will deliver broader impact by demonstrating Hong Kong as a leading innovation hub, where pioneering valorisation technologies are incubated for sustainable management of wood and food wastes. 生物質廢物引起了嚴重的環境問題，特別是在密集地區人口稠密的城市。例如在香港，餐廚垃圾占城市固體廢物的34％垃圾被丟棄在垃圾填埋場。通過將生物質廢物轉化為增值化學產品將成為未來的解決方案，這是實現循環生物經濟和發展的重要戰略並達到可持續發展目標。我們的項目將量身定制源自木材廢料的生物炭催化劑，並評估工程生物炭的性能應用為可再生化學品生產中的可持續催化劑。 生物炭是一種經濟的碳固存和污染物吸附劑，可修改的表面功能和多孔結構使生物炭成為支撐的潛在材料催化部位。與傳統的礦物基載體相比，生物炭可在更低的成本下實現更具可持續性的催化劑製造工藝成本。相比貴金屬催化劑（例如鉑，金，鈀），我們將研製過渡金屬，低價銅生物炭作為對於工業氧化還原反應的可持續催化劑。將通過高分辨率光譜分析和計算模擬銅生物炭形成的機理，分析生物炭表面和銅前體兩者之間的協同作用。這將建議可控的形核和銅顆粒的生長以充當活性納米結構。 作為模型反應代表氧化性生物質轉化，將在羥甲基糠醛（HMF）氧化為2,5-呋喃二甲酸（FDCA）的過程中檢查銅-生物炭的催化活性。我們最近的研究表明從富含澱粉的食物垃圾中成功生產HMF，本項目我們將源自食物殘渣的HMF升級為FDCA（高價值的生物基聚合物的前體）。我們會仔細研究銅生物炭的關鍵特性（例如活性位點密度，化學狀態，孔結構），確定其在HMF氧化中的催化活性，並研究動力學和熱力學以闡明液體-固體中的化學反應。 我們的研究計劃將闡繹金屬生物炭形成的機理及其催化功能，促進生物炭材料作為高通量生物精煉的下一代催化劑。我們的項目將發展開拓性的木材和食物垃圾的資源化技術，從而展示香港的創新領先地位以實現可持續發展。

15222020.label: Realisation of objectives
15222020.value: The XPS and XANES analyses suggested Cu species with a lower oxidation state on the N-doped support, indicating the presence of more electron-rich Cu sites on Cu/C-N 800 than on Cu/C 800. Furthermore, the TEM images and FFT analysis revealed Cu(111) facets in Cu/C-N 800 while Cu2O(111) facets were observed in the Cu/C 800 catalyst. A linear correlation can be obtained between the glucose conversion (or gluconic acid yield) and the Cu0-Cu+ to Cu2+ ratio, highlighting the strong dependence of catalytic activity on the Cu valence. The XPS of spent catalysts shows that after reaction, the Cu2+ distribution increased to 56.7% from 35.5% in the pristine Cu/C-N 800 catalyst, suggesting that the low-valence Cu was involved in the glucose reaction by donating electrons and becoming Cu2+. Combining these results, it is believed that the electron-rich, low-valence Cu species (Cu0/Cu+) served as the primary active sites for glucose oxidation. One may expect that the catalytic activity is highly associated with the abundance of Cu0 sites in particular. We emphasize that it is the Cu0/Cu+ sites on well-dispersed nano-sized Cu particles that contribute to the catalysis, considering that Cu/C 800 carries notable metallic Cu in large crystallites (26.2 nm) but was outperformed by Cu/C-N 800. The turnover frequency (TOFs) of glucose oxidation on Cu/C-N 800 at 20 bar air can reach as high as 821 h−1, while maintaining a carbon balance of at least 95%. When the reaction atmosphere was changed from air to N2, only 9.1% conversion of glucose was obtained, indicating the significance of O2 in oxidation reactions. That leads to the next scientific question about the active species derived from molecular O2 activation in the catalytic system. In the aqueous phase, radicals including •OH, 1O2, and O2•− are possibly generated when O2 is activated on the catalyst surface. Starting from the thermodynamic perspective, we calculated the Gibbs free energies (ΔGo) of the formation of different radicals through the redox reactions between O2 and Cu0 using the standard cell potentials. The results showed that the activation of O2 to O2•− reaction is 68 kJ/mol and 50 kJ/mol along with Cu0 oxidation to Cu+ and to Cu2+, respectively (i.e., from initial stage to stage A and to stage B). The positive signs indicate that O2•− formation is not spontaneous. In comparison, the ΔGo of O2 activation to H2O2 (stage D) and then to •OH (stage E) is approximately −4 kJ/mol and −5 kJ/mol, respectively, along with Cu0 oxidation to Cu2+. The negative values suggest thermodynamically favorable processes. Based on the theoretical analysis, we conjecture that •OH radicals, plausibly in the form of *OH adsorbed on active sites of Cu/C-N 800, were the major ROS for glucose oxidation. We note that the four lignin precursors in this study exhibit different characteristics. While the enzymatic lignin and organosolv lignin samples have the lower average molecular weight (Mw) ranging from 899 to 1,581 Da, kraft lignin has much higher Mw (≥10,000 Da) due to the formation of condensed structures under the harsh extraction conditions. Furthermore, both organosolv lignin samples exhibit a broader range of molecular weight than the enzymatic lignin as indicated by the higher polydispersity index (PDI; 1.53 vs. 1.18). The 2D heteronuclear single quantum correlation nuclear magnetic resonance analysis shows that enzymatic and organosolv lignin samples exhibit a high ratio of β-O-4 linkages indicative of the preserved native structures, whereas the kraft lignin has a condensed structure without syringyl units, underscoring compositional differences among various lignin sources. The key highlight of these results is that the structural discrepancies among the lignin precursors exerted only trivial impacts on the catalytic performance. We speculate that the catalyst preparation at 800 °C achieved deep lignin carbonization, to the stage where the carbonized structure may not vary markedly within the category of lignin. This aligns with the TGA results and Raman spectra, showing comparable mass loss% (55 to 67.8%; 900 °C) of the lignin precursors and a narrow range of ID/IG ratio (0.88 to 0.91) for the corresponding Cu catalysts prepared at 800 °C, respectively. While future studies may delve into the carbonization pathways of diverse lignins and their interactions with Cu species, the current results suggest a good chance in securing reproducible catalysis when changing from one type of lignin precursor to another. Our finding supports the evidence-based practice of using lignin, a sustainable biomass-derived material, as a carbon support precursor in wider catalytic applications. DFT calculations elucidated O2 activation over Cu/C-N and Cu/C catalysts, which considered the binding of O2 on the metal sites in both “end-on” (Pauling model) and “side-on” (Yeager model) configurations. It is noted that both Pauling and Yeager adsorption models enable the formation of *OOH—a peroxo intermediate featuring O-O bond—possibly via a proton-coupled electron transfer. This agrees very much with the in situ Raman spectra, where a subtle band was detected at approximately 900 cm−1 on Cu/C-N catalyst, corresponding to the typical peroxo O-O stretching (700 to 900 cm−1). Combining the multifaceted experimental and computational evidence discussed above, we conclude that the Cu/C-N catalysts facilitate the activation of O2 molecules to *OH through a three-electron transfer pathway, which involves *OOH as the intermediate (*O2→*OOH→*OH). The whole process is exothermic and thus thermodynamically favorable. Despite a similar O2 activation pathway, the binding of molecular O2 on Cu/C (i.e., step O2→*O2) tends to be less thermodynamically favored than on Cu/C-N, which may be associated with the difference in the surface electron density of the Cu clusters. We present multifaceted evidence on the catalytic function of low-valence Cu sites and the *OH-involving rate-determining step in air-promoted glucose oxidation. In conclusion, the Cu/C-N catalysts outperformed Cu/C catalysts in the O2-promoted oxidation of glucose to gluconic acid. The former catalysts had a higher proportion of Cu species with zero or low valence (Cu0, Cu+) because the N-doped carbon support favored the formation of electron-rich metal sites. The DFT calculations, in situ Raman analysis, quenching experiments, and KIE studies suggest *OH generated in situ on the catalyst surface as the major radical responsible for glucose oxidation. The evidence also reveal the activation of O2 to *OH through the pathway: *O2→*OOH→*OH, regardless of the O2 adsorption configuration. Furthermore, the localized *OH on the catalyst surface was more selective toward glucose oxidation at C1HO, yielding gluconic acid of higher selectivity, compared to •OHfree radicals in bulk solution that arise from thermal degradation of exogenous H2O2 under noncatalytic conditions. With further kinetic analysis, the addition of *OH to R-C1=O of glucose, instead of C1-H activation, was concluded as the rate-determining step. Another exciting finding is that the performances of catalysts were insensitive to the type of lignin precursor (as catalyst support), of which the reproducibility deserves vigorous verification in the future.

15222020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222020.value: Catalytic oxidation through the transfer of lattice oxygen from metal oxides to reactants, namely the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism, has been widely reported. In this study, we evidence the overlooked oxidation route that features the in situ formation of surface OH species on Cu catalysts and its selective addition to the reactant carbonyl group. We observed that glucose oxidation to gluconic acid in air (21% O2) was favored on low-valence Cu sites according to X-ray spectroscopic analyses. Molecular O2 was activated in situ on Cu0/Cu+ forming localized, adsorbed hydroxyl radicals (*OH) which played the primary reactive oxygen species as confirmed by the kinetic isotope effect (KIE) study in D2O and in situ Raman experiments. Combined with DFT calculations, we proposed a mechanism of O2-to-*OH activation through the *OOH intermediate. The localized *OH exhibited higher selectivity toward glucose oxidation at C1HO to form gluconic acid (up to 91% selectivity), in comparison with free radicals in bulk environment that emerged from thermal, noncatalytic hydrogen peroxide decomposition (40% selectivity). The KIE measurements revealed a lower glucose oxidation rate in D2O than in H2O, highlighting the role of water (H2O/D2O) or its derivatives (e.g., *OH/*OD) in the rate-determining step. After proving the C1-H activation step kinetically irrelevant, we proposed the oxidation mechanism that was characterized by the rate-limiting addition of *OH to C1=O in glucose. Our findings advocate that by maneuvering the coverage and activity of surface *OH, high-performance oxidation of carbonyl compounds beyond biomass molecules can be achieved in water and air using nonprecious metal catalysts.

15222020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222020.value: In situ *OH species can be formed on low-valence Cu active sites when water and air are used as the solvent and oxidant, respectively. Compelling experimental evidence is presented here on the critical roles of the surface *OH species in achieving selective oxidation at the glucose carbonyl group. These findings expand our knowledge base in catalytic oxidation, in which lattice oxygen transfer through the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism has been widely observed. Moreover, the way heterogeneous catalysis impacts product selectivity via the surface *OH inspires a unique perspective to tailor active sites. We also highlight the participation of water in *OH formation and its impact on the kinetics, of which the generic understanding can be transferred to other solvent-assisted oxidation reactions.

15222020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222020.value: Our mechanistic understanding highlights the electron transfer between Cu clusters and N-doped carbon support as well as the participation of *OH in the reaction. We envision that the tuning of *OH coverage and its activity by nanoengineering metal surface is a promising strategy to achieve selective oxidation of bio-based molecules. Our study sheds light on the oxidation mechanisms and characteristics of the key players in the low-cost, green system comprising Cu catalysts and pressurized air. The understanding could assist development in catalytic oxidation of diverse carbonyl compounds and even polysaccharides. The oxidation of starch, pectin, cellulose, etc. to simple organic acids will require systems capable of both breaking glycosidic bonds and oxidizing carbonyl groups. Further advances in catalyst design could foster innovations for effectively utilizing the widely available bioresources, creating circular bioeconomies in broad industries.

15222220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222220.value: 目前，圖捲積神經網絡已經在多個領域基於圖數據的學習任務上取得了先進的效果，包括屬性圖信息網絡上的節點分類和聚類，電子商務中的產品推薦，用於藥物發現的分子圖分類和生成，用於計算機視覺的人體動作識別，用於智能運輸系統的交通流量預測等。這些進步主要歸功於圖捲積，一種以聚合鄰居節點來學習有效節點表示的技術。 但是，當前圖捲積神經網絡方法的一個主要缺陷是它們都采用了一維圖捲積來聚合圖節點特徵。這種方法只利用了圖數據上節點之間的鏈接關係而沒有利用到數據其它維度的有用信息來學習節點的表示，比如説屬性圖中節點特徵屬性之間的關聯。這嚴重限制了這些方法在真實複雜網絡上的建模能力并且會導致它們在噪聲數據上達不到理想的效果。 在本項目中，我們提出用二維圖捲積來聯合建模圖數據多個維度的關聯以學習圖節點的特徵表示。在方法方面，我們將致力於設計計算高效的圖捲積算子來學習有效的圖節點表示并且從方差縮減和圖信號去噪的角度來分析它們的學習性能。在應用方面，我們打算利用二維圖捲積來重新研究和提出對於不同領域的應用問題的新解決方案，例如文本分類聚類，基於知識圖譜的推薦系統以及基於骨架的動作識別。 我們初期的研究表明二維圖捲積能夠有效的結合圖數據不同維度上的信息并且在多個學習任務上取得了明顯好於一維圖捲積的效果。我們相信研究二維圖捲積能顯著推進當前圖神經網絡的研究方法和手段，并且會為很多重要的工業界應用帶來顯著效益。

15222220.label: Realisation of objectives
15222220.value: Graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) have become the preferred model for graph representation learning, primarily due to their effective mechanism of graph convolution, which computes a node's representation by aggregating information from its neighbours. However, existing GCN variants typically employ 1-D graph convolution that operates solely on the object link graph, neglecting the rich relational information among object attributes. This limitation significantly restricts their modelling capability. In this project, we have explored 2-D graph convolution to establish a unified and versatile framework that can jointly model object links and attribute relations for graph representation learning. To reduce computational cost and enhance efficiency, we have proposed a computationally efficient dimensionwise separable 2-D graph convolution (DSGC) for learning node features. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that DSGC can reduce intra-class variance of node features in both the object and attribute dimensions, leading to more effective representations. We have shown that regular 1-D graph convolution on the object link graph can reduce intra-class variance of node features, which helps explain the success of many existing methods. Additionally, we have proven that the same effect can be achieved with graph convolution on a properly constructed attribute affinity graph. Together, these findings provide a robust theoretical justification for DSGC. Consequently, we have successfully addressed the first objective of our project. Building on the proposed convolutional filters and theoretical analysis, we have introduced two learning frameworks: one for unsupervised node clustering and another for semi-supervised node classification. We have conducted extensive experiments on various real-world networks, including email networks, citation networks, and web graphs. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate the advantages of DSGC over the traditional 1-D graph convolution. Furthermore, we have shown that DSGC can be seamlessly integrated into existing strong GCN-based methods, significantly enhancing their performance. Thus, we have successfully addressed the second objective of our project. We further applied our unified framework and convolutional filters to tackle a range of real-world applications, including document classification and clustering, personalized product search, and knowledge-based recommendation systems. Through these applications, we demonstrated the versatility and effectiveness of our approach, thereby successfully addressing the third objective of our project. Our results indicate that the proposed methods not only enhance performance in these specific tasks but also provide a robust foundation for future research and development in graph-based learning.

15222220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222220.value: Existing graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) typically employ 1-D graph convolution, which operates solely on the object (node) link graph and neglects the informative relational information among other dimensions, such as correlations between object attributes. This limitation significantly restricts their modeling capability. In this project, we have addressed the challenge of enhancing the representation capability of GCNs. We established a unified 2-D graph convolution framework that jointly models object links and attribute relations for graph representation learning, encompassing conventional 1-D graph convolution as a special case. Further, we proposed a computationally efficient dimensionwise separable 2-D graph convolutional filter and provided theoretical analysis to demonstrate its effectiveness. Our results show that the proposed framework and filters offer substantial advantages over existing methods across a variety of tasks on real-world attributed graphs. The findings have been published in KDD 2021. We further applied our unified framework and convolutional filters, integrating domain knowledge and designing domain-specific approaches, to tackle a range of real-world applications. These applications include document classification and clustering, personalized product search, and knowledge-based recommender systems. Through these diverse applications, we demonstrated the versatility, potential, and effectiveness of our approach. The results of our work have been published in several top venues, including The ACM Web Conference (TheWebConf) 2022, Pattern Recognition (PR) 2022, IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE) 2023, and the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) 2023.

15222220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222220.value: Graph representational learning has been a central problem and a major focus of research in graph-based learning. While graph neural networks (GNNs) have been the leading models in this area, the node representations (embeddings) they produce are often high-dimensional and lack interpretability. The research method and framework proposed in this project can be extended and enhanced through learning compact, meaningful, and interpretable node representations. Our preliminary research in this direction has shown great promise, and we plan to apply for additional research grants from RGC to further develop and implement this new project.

15222220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222220.value: Graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) have emerged as the leading method for numerous learning tasks involving graph-structured data across various domains. Their success is largely attributed to the implementation of graph convolution, a neighborhood aggregation mechanism that facilitates the learning of effective node representations. In this project, we have explored methods and techniques to enhance the representational capacity of GCNs by designing new graph convolutional filters capable of modelling and integrating relational information from multiple dimensions of data. We have developed computationally efficient graph convolutional filters with theoretical guarantees and validated their effectiveness through comprehensive experiments. These experiments span various applications, including document classification, clustering, product search, and recommendation.

15222320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222320.value: 超過7億智能合約已經被部署到以太坊區塊鏈上以提供各種應用。這些智能合約將被運行在每個以太坊節點上的以太坊虛擬機所執行。由於大量部署的智能合約以及不斷增加的Solidity程序員，以太坊虛擬機被越來越多區塊鏈所支持，例如 Expanse, Wanchain, Tomochain, SmartMesh, CPChain, ThunderCore。因此，以太坊虛擬機上的任何安全問題都將影響大量智能合約，開發者，用戶和區塊鏈平台。為了防止資源被濫用，特別是以消耗資源為目的的DoS攻擊，以太坊採用Gas機制來向智能合約開發者和使用者收取費用。然而，Gas機制裡面的弱點可被利用來發動DoS攻擊病影響區塊鏈平台，智能合約和用戶。被攻擊下，所有節點將被迫執行惡意智能合約從而無法執行合法合約；有缺陷的智能合約的帳號將不能使用其餘額； 合約用戶將無法獲得預期的服務或者被多收費。這種攻擊在近年常被發動。雖然最近一些工作研究了這類問題，但是它們有各種不足。首先，缺乏一個系統性的研究和工具來發現標價偏低的指令。重訪現有的交易無法發現這類指令因為它們不一定包含最差情況的輸入。其次，缺乏有效的運行時保護機制來抵禦現有的和未知的攻擊。第三，缺乏有效的方法來發現和修補與Gas相關的問題。在這個項目中，我們將對利用Gas機制的DoS攻擊開展一個系統性的研究。首先，我們將揭示Gas機制裡面的弱點，包括標價偏低的指令及以太坊虛擬機中可被利用的特性。其次，我們將設計運行時保護框架以抵禦該類攻擊並通過博弈理論來研究防禦機制。第三，我們將提出新的方法來尋找最差情況的輸入及修復Gas效率低的代碼來加固智能合約。

15222320.label: Realisation of objectives
15222320.value: We have achieved the three objectives. 1. Revealing the Weaknesses in Gas Mechanism. We have developed new measurement tool to evaluate and quantify the resource consumption of EVM instructions. In particular, we studied not only the existing EVM instructions but also the instructions in EVM 2.0 and EVM variants used by other blockchain systems. Note that Ethereum community is considering replace EVM with eWASM (Ethereum WebAssembly) runtime whose instructions will be assigned new gas costs. We found that the gas costs were not appropriately set because the designers overlooked the performance variations across different machines and the differences between the original EVM and WASM runtime, leading to underpriced instructions. We identify novel weaknesses in these runtimes and their blockchain systems. Specifically, we found that manipulatable performance bottlenecks in blockchain nodes create new attack surfaces and developed a novel tool named ThreadNeck to identify such vulnerabilities. The corresponding paper appeared ISSTA’24[3], a leading symposium on software testing and analysis. The developers have confirmed the DoS issues identified. Existing DoS vulnerabilities related to the gas mechanism result in only temporary effects, meaning that normal blockchain operations will resume once the attack ceases. We unveiled a novel attack surface in blockchain technology—state storage—through which attackers can launch DoS attacks with persistent effects. This means that even after the attacks cease, the performance of the blockchain platform will still be impaired. We designed NURGLE, the first DoS attack targeting state storage, which forces blockchains to use additional resources for state maintenance and verification, thereby impairing performance. The corresponding paper appeared in IEEE S&P’24[4], a top security conference. We also measured and compared the performance of EVM and eWASM. The corresponding paper appeared in BlockSys’24 and received the best paper award[2]. 2. Defending Blockchain Platforms Against DoS Attacks Exploiting Gas Mechanism. We have developed a framework that replays arbitrary transactions, efficiently collects primitive information, and includes analysis components to profile smart contract behaviors and detect various attacks. The corresponding paper appeared in ACM TOSEM[5]. We also explored using the intent of transactions to detect attacks. Specifically, we propose the Motif-based Transaction Semantics representation method, which can capture the transaction semantic information in the real-time transaction data workflow. The corresponding paper appeared in WWW’23[6]. To defend against novel DoS attacks like NURGLE[4] that exploit inconsistency between the gas consumption and the storage workload, we developed Matt, a novel tool to mitigate such issues (named transaction fee mechanism inconsistency bugs) in Ethereum’s storage [8]. The corresponding paper was recently accepted by USENIX FAST’25[8] (Please note that this paper is not included in the research output list, as the UGC system only permits the listing of published conference papers). Since the attacker may adjust the attack smart contract to escape the detection, we investigated the defense strategy from other aspects. One direction is payment network/channel which allow two parties to perform micropayments privately without broadcasting all of them to the blockchain so that attacker cannot take advantage of smart contracts to launch DoS attacks on Ethereum. We proposed a new off-chain system, which can not only shorten the payment path, but also appropriately avoid problems such as capital dispersion and large deposits. The corresponding paper was published in IEEE TDSC[7]. Existing research on discovering DoS vulnerabilities in blockchain technology and designing defense mechanisms relies heavily on manual analysis. To model the interaction between the attacker exploiting such DoS vulnerabilities and the defender via game theory, we develop a generic and systematic approach to uncover these weaknesses and obtain insights into DoS weaknesses in blockchain resource models [9]. Specifically, we developed DoSVER to reason feasible DoS weaknesses against blockchain resource models by formal verification. The identified DoS weaknesses will be validated by DoSDET, a new framework that automates the attack synthesis in exploiting the identified DoS weaknesses. The corresponding paper appeared in CCS’24[9], a top security conference. We discovered that, due to the design of current blockchain resource models and considerations of performance and utilization, an attacker could always identify DoS vulnerabilities and launch attacks. 3. Hardening Smart Contacts Against DoS Attacks Exploiting Gas Mechanism. We first conducted an in-depth empirical study on contract fuzzing techniques. 15222320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222320.value: We achieved the objectives aimed at identifying vulnerabilities in the gas mechanism of blockchain platforms and developing defenses against related DoS attacks. We created new tools to measure and quantify the resource consumption of EVM instructions. Our analysis showed that gas costs were improperly set due to designers overlooking performance variations across different machines and differences between EVM and WASM. This oversight resulted in underpriced instructions and novel weaknesses in these runtimes and their blockchain systems. We identified manipulatable performance bottlenecks in blockchain nodes that introduce new attack surfaces. Developers acknowledged the DoS issues we identified. Unlike existing DoS vulnerabilities that have temporary effects, we discovered a novel attack surface involving state storage that enables persistent-effect DoS attacks, degrading blockchain performance even after the attacks end. We designed NURGLE, the first DoS attack targeting state storage, and major blockchain platforms have confirmed these issues. We developed a framework that can replay arbitrary transactions, efficiently collect data, and profile smart contract behaviors to detect attacks. To enhance attack detection based on transaction intent, we proposed the Motif-based Transaction Semantics representation method, capturing transaction semantic information in real-time workflows. To counter novel DoS attacks like NURGLE, which exploit inconsistencies between gas consumption and storage workload, we created Matt, a tool to address transaction fee mechanism inconsistency bugs in Ethereum's storage. Anticipating that attackers might adapt, we explored alternative defenses, including a new off-chain payment system that allows two parties to conduct micropayments privately, thus preventing attackers from exploiting smart contracts for DoS attacks. We also developed a systematic approach to uncovering DoS vulnerabilities in blockchain resource models. Our findings reveal that, due to current blockchain resource model designs and considerations of performance and utilization, attackers can consistently identify and exploit DoS vulnerabilities. We conducted an in-depth empirical study on contract fuzzing techniques and, from our insights, designed a new fuzzing approach leveraging LLMs to generate effective seeds. We also developed a new fuzzing method to uncover DoS vulnerabilities arising from transaction fee mechanism inconsistency bugs. To address the time-consuming nature of symbolic detection tools for smart contract vulnerabilities, we introduced Park for parallel-fork symbolic execution in smart contracts. Moreover, we investigated gas-inefficient code patterns and optimization approaches. We discovered that bytecode generated by existing compilers contains gas-inefficient codes that can be optimized using inline assembly. By leveraging LLMs, we facilitated the labor-intensive process of code smell detection, identifying new gas-inefficient code smells.

15222320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222320.value: Potential areas for further development of our research include: 1. Enhance the scope of our measurement tools to cover additional blockchain platforms and newer versions of Ethereum, including those planning to integrate more complex features like sharding and layer 2 solutions. 2. Build on our initial successes with LLM-driven fuzzing by incorporating AI to predict potential new vulnerabilities based on emerging patterns in blockchain development. Also, expand the fuzzing methodology to include more blockchain environments beyond Ethereum. 3. Continue refining the optimization of gas-inefficient code in smart contracts. Develop automated tools that can be integrated into blockchain development environments to help programmers write more efficient and secure code from the outset. 4. Conduct ongoing studies to monitor the effectiveness of implemented defenses against DoS attacks. This will help in adapting strategies in response to evolving attack methods and blockchain technologies. 5. Work with blockchain developers and industry groups to standardize security practices and vulnerability reporting. This collaboration will help ensure that our research findings are rapidly adopted and effectively mitigate risks.

15222320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222320.value: Our research aims to enhance the security and efficiency of blockchain platforms like Ethereum, which are foundational to cryptocurrencies and smart contracts. These systems utilize a "gas mechanism" to levy fees for computational tasks, preventing network overload. However, we identified critical flaws in how gas costs are computed, primarily due to an oversight in accounting for differences in computing environments and updates in system architectures. This results in some operations being underpriced, creating vulnerabilities that attackers exploit through Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. These attacks disrupt operations and, notably, we discovered a new type targeting "state storage" that degrades blockchain performance even post-attack. To combat these threats, we developed analytical tools that replay transactions and monitor smart contracts to detect signs of attacks. We also implemented a systematic approach to proactively identify and address potential vulnerabilities, adapting to evolving attack strategies. Additionally, our study on smart contracts revealed common coding inefficiencies that lead to excessive resource use—increasing transaction costs. By pinpointing these "gas-inefficient" patterns, we proposed optimizations that enhance contract performance. Our use of LLMs helped uncover hidden issues in millions of existing contracts, aiding developers in creating more secure and efficient code.

15223120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223120.value: A rising number of aged buildings in Hong Kong result from deterioration caused by steel corrosion, concrete spalling etc, which has become an increasingly important issue. In addition, the hot weather in Hong Kong requires huge energy consumption to cool the indoor building environment for human comfort. It is said that the air conditioning inside buildings accounts for one-third of the total local electricity consumption in Hong Kong, generating significant energy and environmental burden. The durability and thermal performance of an RC building relies heavily on the performance of the building envelope, which significantly influences the service life, the indoor living environment, and the energy consumption of the building. Therefore, its proper maintenance is of critical importance. Among the many existing maintenance technologies, surface coating is a most cost-effect means which can isolate the building envelope from various external hostile environments such as water, UV radiations, carbon dioxide and chlorides. The surface coating can be also incorporated with heat insulation or reflective functions to reduce the thermal gradient between the indoor and outdoor environment in the building envelope, so that energy needed to maintain the human comfort in the building can be saved. This project aims to develop an innovative multiple functional geopolymer coating for improving the sustainability of concrete building envelope. The system will be featured with the waterproofing, self-cleaning and passive cooling functions. In particular, it is featured with two distinguished characteristics: (1) Ability of sub-ambient daytime radiative cooling (SDRC), which is a breakthrough technology emerging very recently and can reduce the building surface temperature well below the air temperature under direct sunlight. As a result, the amount of energy required for cooling the buildings can be significantly reduced. (2) Use of inorganic geopolymer matrix, which is a cement-free, low-carbon and environmental friendly material and formed by alkali-activation of aluminosilicate sources. Compared to existing polymeric coatings, the geopolymer matrix exhibits superior fire and weathering resistance (e.g., UV resistance), which are important for building applications. The project consists of five research tasks covering design of coating mix-proportion, improvement of optical properties, hydrophobic treatment, durability assessment and cooling effect analysis. Upon the success of the project, a cost-effective method will be established for the service life extension and energy efficiency improvement of existing concrete building, leading to a comprehensive solution for the improvement of building sustainability, in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area and the rest of China. 由於鋼筋腐蝕，混凝土剝落等原因，香港老化建築物的數量日益增加，已成為越來越重要的社會問題。此外，香港炎熱的天氣需要大量的能源消耗來冷卻室內建築環境，以達到舒適的人居環境。據報導建築物內的空調佔香港本地總用電量的三分之一，給能源和環境造成了巨大負擔。 RC建築物的耐久和熱工性能很大程度上取決於建築物圍護結構的性能。因此，對其進行適當的維護至關重要。在許多現有的維護技術中，表面塗層是一種最具成本效益的方法，可將建築圍護結構與各種外部惡劣環境（例如水，紫外線輻射，二氧化碳和氯化物）隔離開來。表面塗層還可結合隔熱或反射功能，以減小建築物室內外環境之間的熱梯度，從而節省維持建築物中人居舒適度所需的能耗。 本項目旨在開發一種創新的多功能地質聚合物塗料體系，以改善混凝土建築圍護結構的可持續性。該系統將具有防水，自清潔和被動製冷功能。特別是，它具有兩個傑出的獨創性：（1）亞環境白天輻射冷卻（SDRC）的能力，可以將建築物的表面溫度降低到遠低於陽光直射下的氣溫，顯著減少冷卻建築物所需的能量。 （2）使用低碳，環保的無機地質聚合物基材，該材料通過對鋁矽酸鹽原料進行鹼激發而形成。與現有的聚合物塗料相比，該地質聚合物基體具有良好的耐火性和耐候性（例如，抗紫外線老化）。 該項目包括五個研究任務，涉及塗層配合比的設計，光學性能的改善，疏水性處理，耐久性評估和冷卻效果分析。項目成功的實施將衛香港以及大灣區建立一種經濟有效的方法，以延長現有混凝土建築物的使用壽命並提高其能效，從而為改善建築物的可持續性提供綜合解決方案。

15223120.label: Realisation of objectives
15223120.value: All the objectives set out for this project have been completely achieved. A geopolymer-based inorganic binder through alkali activation of raw materials was prepared to clarify the film forming mechanisms the binders. Gopolymer binded with different mix proportions (e.g., molar ratios) have been systhesized as the coating matrix to provide coating film formation and adhesion to substrate. The geopolymer matrix was then modified with barium sulphate (BaSO4) and nano-silica (SiO2) particles. The reaction kinetics and reology of geopolymer binders were systematically investigated. The formed geopolymer coating was then used to paint on steel and concrete substrates and was found to have good film forming ability. Furthermore, an inorganic phosphate activated geopolymer-based (PAGP) SDRC coating was also synthesized using nano-silica (SiO2) particles and barium sulfate (BaSO4) sheets as the modiﬁers. The alkali-based and phosphate-based geopolymer coatings can be used for different substrate materials. The optical and physicochemical properties of the formed alkali- and phosphate-based geopolymer coatings were systematically investigated. The chemical composition, functional groups as well as surface morphologies of the raw materials and the formed geopolymer coatings were characterized by XRD, FTIR, SEM and EDS. The developed alkali-activated coating was found to exhibit a high emissivity of 0.95 and solar reflectance of 97.6%. When exposed to direct sunlight, the coating’s surface could cool down up to 8.9 ℃ below the ambient air temperature under Hong Kong’s climate. In addition, the coating could retain its performance well under a variety of harsh environments, including high temperature, water immersion, mechanical wearing, and exposure to sunlight. The synthesized phosphate-based coating was also found to achieve high infrared emissivity of 0.9634 and solar reﬂectance of 0.9471, which also exhibited high-temperature resistance and optical stability up to 1000 ◦C due to its covalently bonded structure and electrically neutral system. The evolution of condensed structures and weight loss analysis during the high- temperature treatment was conducted by TGA and XRD to analyze the dehydration process and phase change during the heat process. The outdoor ﬁeld tests showed a maximum sub-ambient temperature reduction of 3.8 ◦C by the developed coating without any energy input under direct sunlight in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the energy- saving performance of the PAGP-based SDRC coating is analyzed under different climatic conditions in China with the aid of EnergyPlus. Simulation results demonstrated that the PAGP-based SDRC coating can signiﬁcantly save the cooling load in all ﬁve selected cities, which shows great potential in building energy conservation and carbon emission reduction. The linear abrasion test of alkali-activated geopolymer (AAGP) coating was carried out on standard sandpaper (320 mesh) with a 500 g abrading load to compare the solar reflectance performance and microscopic appearance of the geopolymer coating surface before and after the abrasion. The water permeability test of AAGP coating was carried out according to the standard of Japan Society of Civil Engineers JSCE-K571-2004. The pull-off tests of AAGP coatings were carried out with specially designed equipment (PosiTest® AT-M Adhesion Tester) according to ASTM D4541. It was found that the AAGP coating exhibited an approximately the same or even better abrasion resistance than the commercial coating, indicating a better long-term anti-wear property. The results show that the overall reflectance marginally changed after the abrasion (from 0.9758 to 0.9726). Comparing the microscopic surface morphology of the AAGP coating before abrasion and after abrasion indicates that the three-dimensional structure combining the bumps and pores was well retained after the wearing test, i.e., the excellent optical properties of AAGP coating was maintained. The average bonding strength of geopolymer coating to the substrate was approximately 2.48 MPa, indicating a good adhesion property. The longevity of geopolymer-based radiative cooling coatings is questionable due to their hydrophilic nature. The project has used four hydrophobic agents - sodium methyl silicate (SMS), polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), poly-tetraﬂuoroethylene (PTFE), and triethoxyoctylsilane (TEOS) - to modify the surface hydrophobicity of geo-polymer while maintaining its optical properties. The optimal agent contents were determined by optical performance and water contact angle: 5 % for SMS, 10 % for 50 cP viscosity PDMS, and a single-layer thickness for PTFE and TEOS (60 ◦C). The agents’ working mechanisms were analyzed using FTIR and XRD characterization: SMS forms a hydrophobic alkylsilanol layer by reacting with the geopolymer’s silanol group; PDMS lowers the geopolymer’s surface energy with its hydrophobic methyl groups; PTFE’s low electric polarizability is due to its ﬂuorine content; and TEOS replaces the geopolymer surface’s hydroxyl groups with hydrophobic octyl groups. The long-term durability of these modiﬁed coatings was evaluated through outdoor exposure tests, resulting in total solar reﬂectance losses of 0.74 %, 1.9 %, 3.9 %, and 0.05 % respectively. A slight reduction in the water contact angle conﬁrmed their enduring hydrophobic characteristics. These modiﬁcation methods open up possibilities for the practical use of hydrophobic geopolymer radiative cooling coatings.

15223120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223120.value: The key findings from the research project can be summarized in four main aspects: (1) A comprehensive scientific understanding has been achieved regarding the formation mechanisms of geopolymer coating matrices. Extensive research has been conducted on the geopolymer coating mixtures, resulting in optimized formulations for both alkali-activated and phosphate-activated geopolymers. The chemical, physical, and microstructural transformations occurring during the film formation process have been thoroughly examined (refer to papers 3, 4, 5, and 6). Additionally, the use of waste materials in the production of geopolymer coatings has been explored and successfully implemented (refer to papers 7, 8, 9, 10, and 13). (2) The developed geopolymer coatings demonstrate exceptional reflectivity and long-wave emissivity, achieving values of 0.95 and 0.976 for the alkali-activated geopolymer coating, and 0.963 and 0.947 for the phosphate-activated geopolymer coating. Both coatings are capable of achieving sub-ambient cooling effects (refer to papers 2 and 16). Furthermore, they meet industry standards regarding adhesion strength to the substrate and resistance to abrasion. (3) Effective surface treatment methods have been developed for geopolymer coatings to obtain superhydrophobic properties and enhanced durability, resulting in self-cleaning capabilities that require minimal maintenance (refer to paper 12). The incorporation of graphene oxide has also proven successful in enhancing the corrosion resistance of the coatings (refer to paper 1). Additionally, fluorescence-enabled colored coatings have been created (refer to papers 11 and 15). (4) A red mud-based geopolymer coating has been successfully developed, demonstrating significant potential for use in pavements (refer to paper 14).

15223120.value: The performance of a building's envelope is crucial for the durability and thermal efficiency of reinforced concrete structures, affecting service life, indoor conditions, and energy consumption. Maintaining this envelope is essential, and surface coatings offer a cost-effective solution to protect against water, UV radiation, carbon dioxide, and chlorides. These coatings can also be improved with heat insulation or reflective features, reducing the thermal gradient between indoors and outdoors and promoting energy savings for human comfort. This project has developed innovative alkali-based and phosphate-based geopolymer coatings that enhance the sustainability of concrete building envelopes. These coatings provide waterproofing, self-cleaning, and passive cooling features, including sub-ambient daytime radiative cooling (SDRC) technology, which can significantly lower surface temperatures in direct sunlight, reducing energy costs for cooling. Compared to traditional polymeric coatings, geopolymer options offer better fire resistance and weathering capabilities, such as UV resistance, essential for building applications. The success of this project has resulted in a cost-effective approach to extending the service life and improving the energy efficiency of existing concrete buildings, providing a comprehensive solution for enhancing building sustainability in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area, and across China.

15223520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223520.value: 尺寸效应影响的金属材料多尺度变形中各向异性和不对称性的研究

15223520.label: Project Objectives
15223520.value: Unraveling the microscopic mechanisms of anisotropy and asymmetry of deformation: The strongly anisotropic and asymmetric plasticity prevails in deformation of many metallic materials, especially for HCP alloys, where the symbiosis and interaction between directional slip and polar mechanical twining (MT) are the prime culprits. Uncovering the activation of slip and twinning and the competition between dislocation glide and MT of HCP metals under various deformation modes is the first issue to be addressed. The individual and simultaneous effects of various intrinsic and extrinsic factors on the grain- resolved slip and twinning activities of single-, bi- and poly-crystals of α-Ti alloys will be systematically examined by physical tests and material characterization techniques. Particular focuses will be on the interaction between dislocations with twins, and the grain boundaries and misorientations on the nucleation and growth of twin variants. Correlating the grain-level dislocation and twinning activities with microscopic mechanisms of fractures will also be explored. Furthermore, efforts will be provided to explore the influence of deformation heterogeneity like shear localization and bands arising from the strong directional dislocation glide and MT in HCP alloys on fracture mechanisms based on α-Ti polycrystals, as well as the grain-level microstructural features such as twins, twin boundaries, and grain boundaries on initiation of damage. Development of a multi-scaled CP modeling framework: Full-field CP simulation is widely and effectively used to study the anisotropic and asymmetric deformation and fracture by considering microscopic deformation and damage mechanisms. The multimechanisms including different slip and MT and their interactions with GBs will be coupled in the CP model. Various damage sources such as micro-void, shear band, and semi-cleavage will be considered. The inelastic kinematics of single crystals is therefore assumed to be contributed by both plasticity and fracture fields. GBs will be explicitly modeled to accurately predict the strain incompatibility in neighboring grains and the interplay between GBs and dislocation glide. The effects of microstructural grain size and geometrical size will then directly be included from the physical nature. For the largescale simulation, multi-scaled simulation model will be proposed by embedding the fullfield CP model into each integration point of the finite element (FE) model. Identification of the correlations among size effect (SE), anisotropic and asymmetrical deformation and fracture: For multi-scaled forming of HCP metals, the knowledge on the geometrical size and microstructural grain SEs on the anisotropic and asymmetric plastic deformation and under different loading conditions is extremely limited. A major part of this project is to characterize such extrinsic and intrinsic SEs on the slip/twinning activity, interplay between dislocation glide and MT, and the damage evolution mechanism. Overall yield, fracture loci, and forming limit affected by the SEs will also be explored. The SEs affected fracture mode and mechanism in multi-scaled forming of HCP metals with different orientation and strain path will be revealed. Full-field CP simulation under different loading conditions from macroscale to microscale will be conducted to obtain more systematic and in-depth understanding of the size-dependent anisotropy and asymmetry. Development of methods to reduce/avoid the defects induced by anisotropy and asymmetry: The final goal of this project is to serve the manufacturing industry with the developed knowledge for accurately forming part geometries, desirably tailoring the needed properties and assuring the required quality of the fabricated multi-scaled products. With this regard, potential approaches including microstructural and texture design, forming process, workpiece and strain path optimization will be proposed to control the forming defects induced by the anisotropy and asymmetry of deformation via the multi-scaled deep drawing of α-Ti sheets by examining the defects such as earring, wrinkling, and fracture.

15223520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223520.value: The project has conducted extensive research to address the issues related to the four proposed objectives. Upon having addressed those issues, the proposed tasks were completed, and 25 SCI papers arising from this research have been published. The main findings and achievements are : 1: Unravelled the microscopic mechanisms of anisotropy and asymmetry of deformation via extensive physical experiment and FEM modelling and simulation, 2: Developed a multi-scaled crystal plasticity modelling framework and realization of the framework; 3: Determined the correlations among size effect (SE), anisotropic and asymmetrical deformation and fracture based on experiment and FEM simulation results; 4: Explored and studied the methods to reduce/avoid the defects induced by anisotropy and asymmetry.

15223520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223520.value: An in-depth and insightful study of anisotropy and asymmetry-induced heterogeneous deformation behaviour, further resulted in the deformation defects and their prediction and avoidance is a crucial issue to be addressed.

15223520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223520.value: This project employed an integrated experimental and modelling methodology to establish the systematic and fundamental understanding and thorough insight into the microscopic mechanisms of the anisotropy and asymmetry of multi-scaled deformations in terms of the orientation and loading condition dependent activation of slip, damage evolution, as well as the effect of anisotropy and asymmetry on the mechanical response including distorted yield loci, hardening behaviour, fracture of the selected alloys at multi-scaled deformation, interacted with size effects. The project advanced the understanding and generated a systematic knowledge of the size effect affected anisotropy and asymmetry in multi-scaled deformation of metallic materials.

15300020.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15300020.value: Prof Friedlander, Michael Dr Li, Guoyin

15300020.label: Project Objectives
15300020.value: Investigate and develop innovative approaches for solving a class of convex structure-inducing constrained optimization problems, based on gauge duality theory. The developments can be incorporated to enhance some of the state-of-the-art algorithms for compressed sensing and phase retrieval. The techniques developed may also shed light on how new solution methods can be developed for the nonconvex case. Develop new approaches for tackling nonconvex structure-inducing constrained optimization problems. Availability of these new efficient algorithms will likely encourage the proposal and study of new nonconvex structure-inducing constrained optimization models, whose constraints can be designed based on noise models other than Gaussian.

15300020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300020.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will develop innovative approaches for solving a large class of large-scale structure-inducing constrained optimization problems that arise in applications such as compressed sensing and phase retrieval. The investigation will involve both convex and nonconvex models that are commonly used. In the convex setting, the optimization problems involved are typically gauge optimization problems. In this project, based on the recent work by the PI and one of the co-I's on gauge duality and gauge-based smoothing techniques, we will further investigate properties of gauges to devise efficient smoothing-based algorithms for solving the optimization problems. We will also explore the possible use of proximal bundle methods for this class of convex problems and analyze its convergence rate, based on recent findings in Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz exponent by the PI and one of the co-I's. Finally, we will take advantage of our findings in the convex setting to design a new framework of algorithms for solving existing nonconvex models. The outcomes of this project will lead to more efficient algorithms for solving many practical structure-inducing constrained optimization problems, and will likely encourage the proposal and study of new constrained optimization models in contemporary applications. 本項目將針對一系列大規模優化問題設計有效算法。此類問題包括凸或非凸的優化問題，常見於壓縮感知及相位檢索等應用。本項目將循兩方面進行。首先，我們將利用gauge對偶理論及gauge光滑化理論探討gauge的特殊結構以設計凸優化問題的算法，同時亦會探討叢方法的可行性。最後，我們會利用這些凸問題算法設計非凸模型的新算法。成果有望促進帶gauge約束模型的研究與發展。

15300020.label: Realisation of objectives
15300020.value: One of the goals of this project is to investigate and develop innovative approaches for solving a wide class of convex structure inducing constrained optimization problems that involve gauges. In this regard, in the paper “Retraction-based first-order feasible methods for difference-of-convex programs with smooth inequality and simple geometric constraints”, we developed a new algorithmic framework for solving constrained optimization problems with smooth nonlinear constraint functions. A distinctive feature of the proposed algorithm is that it maintains the feasibility of all the iterates by incorporating the idea of retraction from manifold optimization. In particular, feasibility can be maintained without resorting to computing projections onto the feasible set, which can be difficult in applications. In addition, in the case when both the objective and the constraint functions are convex, we established some structural properties (known as the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) exponent) of the extended objective that govern the local convergence rate of the newly proposed algorithm. Particularly, our result covers the case when the objective is the sum of a closed gauge and a (non-overlapping) group LASSO regularizer; this kind of objectives has been widely used in applications such as compressed sensing and variable selections. Next, in the paper “Optimal error bounds in the absence of constraint qualifications with applications to the p-cones and beyond”, we further investigate this KL property for a class of p-norm cone related optimization problems by studying error bounds for conic feasibility problems involving the p-norm cone. We outlined how the new error bound results can be used together with previously obtained results on the calculus of KL exponent to deduce, for the first time, a KL exponent for group p-norm regularized least squares problems. We also presented concrete examples to illustrate the tightness of the error bounds we obtained. In summary, we have developed new approaches for some convex structure inducing constrained optimization problems involving gauges and studied structural properties such as the KL exponent to analyze the efficiency of the solution method. The other goal of the project is to develop new approaches for tackling nonconvex structure-inducing constrained optimization problems. In this regard, in the paper “Retraction-based first-order feasible methods for difference-of-convex programs with smooth inequality and simple geometric constraints”, we specifically discussed how the algorithmic framework can be adapted when the constraint function is the composition of the (nonconvex) Lorentzian norm function with an affine map, and performed numerical experiments to show that our proposed algorithmic framework outperforms some existing algorithms. In addition, in the paper “Doubly iteratively reweighted algorithm for constrained compressed sensing models”, we focused on a specific constrained compressed sensing (CS) model which minimizes a possibly nonconvex sparsity inducing regularizer such as the logarithmic penalty function subject to a bound on a nonconvex loss function such as the Cauchy loss function. We studied the new iterative algorithm as described in objective 2 of the proposal, which leverages existing CS solvers for minimizing a weighted L1 norm subject to a bound on a weighted least squares loss function (e.g., SPGL1 and YALL1) to solve the subproblems in each iteration. Two distinctive features of our approach are: 1. We allow inaccuracy in the approximate solution obtained by the subproblem solvers, meaning that these approximate solutions can be infeasible for the subproblems involved; 2. We incorporate a retraction-like technique to restore feasibility in each iteration. Convergence was established under mild conditions and our numerical experiments illustrate that the proposed approach is competitive with other existing single-loop approaches such as SCP_ls. In summary, we have developed brand new approaches for some nonconvex structure-inducing constrained optimization problems, which maintain feasibility of each iterate.

Availability of these new efficient algorithms will likely encourage the proposal and study of new nonconvex structure-inducing constrained optimization models, whose constraints can be designed based on noise models other than Gaussian.

15300020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300020.value: Three papers were submitted and all of them have already been published (with the second paper published online and the other two papers already published in printed form with page and issue numbers). The first paper is “Retraction-based first-order feasible methods for difference-of-convex programs with smooth inequality and simple geometric constraints”. It was reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in “Advances in Computational Mathematics”. This paper develops a new framework for solving constrained optimization problems with smooth nonlinear constraint functions and difference-of-convex objectives. The second paper is “Optimal error bounds in the absence of constraint qualifications with applications to the p-cones and beyond”. It was also reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint. It was initially rejected and underwent substantial revisions, and is now published in “Mathematics of Operations Research”. This paper studies error bounds for conic feasibility problems involving the p-norm cone, a classical nonsymmetric cone in the literature. The third paper is “Doubly iteratively reweighted algorithm for constrained compressed sensing models”. This paper was under preparation at the time the midterm progress report was submitted, and is now published in “Computational Optimization and Applications”. This paper studies the iterative-reweighting-based method for constrained compressed sensing problems outlined in Objective 2 of the proposal, and discusses how to deal with the inexactly solved subproblems.

15300020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300020.value: There are several avenues for further development. First, among the outcomes of the first goal, it will be interesting to further study the KL property when the objective is the sum of a closed gauge and a possibly overlapping group LASSO regularizer. In addition, it will be interesting to further generalize the algorithm described in Objective 2 of the proposal to cover applications such as matrix completion, whose subproblems will involve the minimization of weighted nuclear norms instead of weighted L1 norms. These are possible venues for future research.

15300020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300020.value: In this project, the PI and his coworkers studied algorithms for tackling structure inducing constrained optimization problems related to gauges. In details, we developed and analyzed new feasible optimization algorithms based on techniques such as retraction from manifold optimization and iteratively reweighting both the objective and constraint functions. The outcomes may lead to more efficient and practical algorithms for contemporary structure inducing constrained optimization problems, and encourage the use of constrained optimization models in emerging applications.

15300120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300120.value: 深度神經網絡的非光滑非凸有限和優化

15300120.label: Project Objectives
15300120.value: We will develop efficient partial penalty methods and stochastic gradient algorithms for solving nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum minimization, by using the special structure of piecewise linear activation functions in the deep neural networks. We will establish comprehensive theoretical results on convergence rate of the proposed algorithms and complexity bounds for solving the structured nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization. We will derive innovative first order and second order necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for local minimizers of the structured nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization. We will explore theoretical properties of smoothing approximation functions such as the gradient consistency and Hessian consistency for the first order directional derivatives and the second order derivatives. We will extensively test the proposed methods and compare them with the existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy, robustness and complexity. Real data from optometry medical images analysis will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms.

15300120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300120.value: Numerous estimation models for training deep neural networks in signal processing and imaging science are nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization where the loss function (empirical risk) measures the error between the model predicated output and the actual output in the data. However, due to the non-differentiability and non-convexity with large amounts of data, their stationarity and optimality are not well understood and finding a second order stationary point efficiently is still an open question. Mathematically, the loss function has the difficulty of non-differentiability and non-convexity. It is known that if each term of the loss function is convex, the subdifferential of their sum equals to the sum of their subdifferentials. However, little is known about the calculation of subdifferentials for the sum of nonsmooth and nonconvex functions. Moreover, in the era with big data where the dimensionality of models increases rapidly, these minimization models usually have another common difficulty of high dimensionality. To bridge the gap, we will study the stationarity and optimality of nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization and develop efficient algorithms for finding strong stationary points and second order stationary points. This project aims to systematically investigate special optimization theory of the structured deep neural networks with nonsmooth activation functions and develop efficient optimization algorithms for these optimization problems. We will establish the theoretical properties of stationary points and the convergence and complexity of these algorithms to stationary points, local minimizers and global minimizers. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate developed algorithms and compare them with existing stochastic gradient algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data from optometry medical images will be used to demonstrate the new theory and methods. The outcomes of this project will have a long term and significant impact, because nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization problems arise naturally from the structured deep neural networks in many real applications and urgently need innovative optimization theory and algorithms. Our new theory and algorithms will attract attention from the international scientific community through collaboration with distinguished researchers and publications in top journals and major international conferences. 在信號處理和成像科學中，眾多用於訓練深層神經網絡的數學模型是非光滑、非凸的有限和優化問題，其中損失函數（經驗風險）用於衡量模型的預測輸出與數據集中真實輸出之間的誤差。然而，由於模型具有非凸性和不可微性並且基於大量數據，模型的穩定性和最優性還沒有得到很好的理解，並且如何有效地找到二階穩定點仍然是壹個懸而未決的問題。在數學上，損失函數的難點在於不可微性和非凸性。眾所周知，對於有限和形式的損失函數，如果每個分量函數都是凸的，那麽和函數的次微分等於分量函數次微分的和。然而，對於非光滑、非凸函數之和的次微分的計算知之甚少。此外，在大數據時代，由於模型的維數迅速增加，這些最小化模型通常還面臨高維數帶來的困難。 我們將研究損失函數的穩定性和最優性，並開發有效的算法來找到非光滑、非凸有限和優化問題的強穩定點和二階穩定點。該項目旨在針對基於非光滑激活函數的結構化深度神經網絡，系統地研究其特殊的優化理論，並對這些優化問題設計有效的優化算法。我們將確立穩定點的理論性質，以及算法收斂到穩定點、局部極小值和全局極小值的收斂性和復雜性。將進行仿真研究以評估已設計的算法，並將它們與現有的隨機梯度算法在算法速度、精確性和魯棒性等進行比較。還將結合來自視光醫學圖像的真實數據以驗證新的理論和方法。由於非光滑、非凸有限和優化問題來源於眾多實際領域中的結構化深度神經網絡，並且迫切需要富於創新的優化理論和算法，該項目的成果將產生長遠而重大的影響。通過與傑出研究人員的合作以及在頂尖期刊和大型重要國際會議上的成果發表，我們的新理論和新算法必將吸引國際科學界的關註。

15300120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300120.value: Nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization for structured deep neural networks has many applications in medical imaging sciences and signal processing. However, the literature of nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization has limited theory and techniques towards developing efficient algorithms for practical applications. The optimization methods developed in this project will make contributions to reduction of radiation dose to the patients and medical staff during medical examination. In particular, we collaborated with Optometry Clinic in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University to propose and implement automatic methods for choroid layer segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography images using deep learning and a series of morphological operations. The choroid layer is a vascular layer in human retina and its main function is to provide oxygen and support to the retina. The thickness of the choroid layer is correlated with the diagnosis of several ophthalmic diseases. Although some automatic methods for choroid layer segmentation have been developed, more effective and accurate automatic methods are required by the clinical sector. We developed new automatic methods to segment the choroid accurately and reduce the error rate. This project made significant contributions to optimization theory and algorithms, and have important short term, medium term and long term impact to the scientific community through publications in top level journals and major conferences, and excellent collaborations with international distinguished researchers.

15300220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300220.value: 過渡金屬催化的交叉偶聯反應通過親電和親核試劑之間的連接來構建碳—碳和碳—雜原子鍵，已成為有機合成中最高效的工具之一。交叉偶聯反應能夠以相對簡單的方式合成高度複雜但多樣的分子，廣泛應用于合成藥物，先進材料和農業化學品。在交叉偶聯反應中，配體扮演著重要的角色。配體能穩定和活化過渡金屬，有效地激活新和具惰性的鍵, 使具挑戰性的底物得以轉化。因此開發和探索簡單、易於製備、結構可調控、催化活性高的配體的需求仍然很大。該項目將會設計合成新型、簡單、可調控的半活性膦配體系列，探索不同的過渡金屬催化反應，研究新的和通用的交叉偶合夥伴，以解決高位阻偶聯反應以及其他具有難度的新型反應, 如C—N鍵斷裂反應。此外亦會進一步開發手性半活性膦配體及應用於不對稱偶聯反應中。

15300220.label: Realisation of objectives
15300220.value: This is the completion report for project 15300220. Regarding the realization of objectives, we have successfully achieved the goals outlined in the proposed work. We designed and developed simple, easily accessible, and highly diversified hemilabile phosphine ligands using straightforward synthetic approaches. The Pd/indolyl-amide-based phosphine ligand catalytic system demonstrated excellent efficiency in the Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of sterically hindered (hetero)aryl chlorides, enabling the synthesis of tri-ortho-substituted biaryls (OBC, 2022, 20, 1373-1378). In this reaction, Pd catalyst loadings as low as 0.05-0.10 mol% were achieved. High functional group tolerance under mild reaction conditions allowed for a broad substrate scope and resulted in good-to-excellent product yields. Notably, an extremely low catalyst loading (0.005 mol% Pd) efficiently facilitated the reaction of sterically hindered aryl chlorides with aryl boroxine. The oxidative addition complex of Pd with the newly developed ligand containing an amide group (InAm-phos) and 2-chlorotoluene was well characterized by single-crystal X-ray crystallography, which revealed the kappa-squared-P, O coordination of the ligand with Pd. This result indicates that the weak O-coordination of the amide group stabilizes the active species during the intervals between reaction cycles, extending the catalyst's longevity. This stabilization may account for the observed need for extremely low catalyst loadings. Furthermore, we developed pyrazolyl-amide phosphine ligands that exhibited high catalytic efficiency in Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions involving (hetero)aryl chlorides and boronate esters. These ligands facilitated the synthesis of tri- and tetra-ortho-substituted biaryls, as well as aryl-alkyl and aryl-alkenyl cross-couplings. These reactions featured a broad substrate scope, with catalyst loadings reduced to as low as 50 ppm. We have been granted a Chinese patent for this type of ligand (ZL202110903637.1). For other selective or unexplored reactions, we achieved palladium-catalyzed chemoselective Suzuki-Miyaura reactions, borylation, direct alpha-arylation of carbonyl compounds, Sonogashira coupling reactions, desulfination, and deuterodehalogenation of polyhalogenated aryl triflates for the first time. These reactions revealed a reactivity order of C-Cl being greater than C-OTf. We designed a new phosphine ligand that demonstrated exceptional chemoselectivity for the C-Cl bond. Experimental and computational results indicated that the methine hydrogen and the steric hindrance provided by SelectPhos are critical factors influencing reactivity and chemoselectivity. DFT calculations showed that Pd-SelectPhos exhibited a more favorable interaction with the C-Cl bond than with the C-OTf bond in the oxidative addition step. We also merged chemoselective Sonogashira and Suzuki-Miyaura coupling reactions to synthesize polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and the natural product analog trimethylselaginellin L. Furthermore, we successfully applied chemoselective alpha-arylation of ester enolates to synthesize flurbiprofen and its derivatives. This work was published in ACS Catalysis (ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 7820-7827), Advanced Synthesis and Catalysis (Adv. Synth. Catal. 2022, 364, 1596-1601), Chemical Science (Chem. Sci. 2022, 13, 4762-4769), Organic Letters (Org. Lett. 2022, 24, 681-685 and 2023, 25, 8429-8433), and the Chinese Journal of Chemistry (Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 909-914). Notably, the publication in Advanced Synthesis and Catalysis (Adv. Synth. Catal. 2022, 364, 1596-1601) was selected as a Very Important Paper and featured on the Front Cover. The articles in Chemical Science (Chem. Sci. 2022, 13, 4762-4769) and Chinese Journal of Chemistry (Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 909-914) were also highlighted on the Front Covers. In addition, we were invited to contribute a review article to Organic Chemistry Frontiers, which provided an overview of the development of palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions and the effects of ligand properties on the chemoselectivity of aryl (pseudo)halides (Org. Chem. Front., 2023, 10, 4408-4436). The review discusses the properties of specific catalysts and their influence on the chemoselectivity of reactions involving these ligand systems. In the area of site-selective cross-coupling reactions, we were invited to contribute a Synfacts article in Synlett (Synlett 2022, 33, 805-814), highlighting the site-selective arylation of alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compounds using a ligand-controlled strategy. Additionally, we accomplished the synthesis of chiral ligands without requiring a tedious resolution step and studied asymmetric cross-coupling reactions. Furthermore, two PhD students were trained during this project period.

15300220.value: The outcomes of this research project offer significant opportunities to advance the development of new catalysts capable of enabling challenging or previously unattainable bond-forming reactions. These advancements hold great potential for further exploration and practical applications, particularly in the fields of pharmaceuticals and functional materials. Moving forward, the proposed course of action involves optimizing these catalytic systems and broadening their scope to address emerging challenges in selective and efficient molecular synthesis.
