15300520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300520.value: Gold catalysis has been developed as a synthetically useful methodology for organic synthesis featuring unique advantages of high reactivity and selectivity, broad functional group compatibility, and insensitivity to open air and aqueous reaction conditions. Gold(I) complexes have been employed to activate alkenes, alkynes, and allenes through π‐bond coordination to achieve diverse organic transformation reactions. In addition, asymmetric gold(I) catalysis has been developed for synthesizing chiral molecules. However, chiral gold(I) complexes having a linear geometry with two coordination sites pose a significant challenge for asymmetric catalysis. During asymmetric gold(I) catalysis, the chiral ligands are far away from the substrates resulting in insufficient chiral induction and hence leading to unsatisfactory enantioselectivity. The use of chiral counter anions and specially designed chiral ligands has been utilized to achieve high enantioselectivity. However, these specific strategies may not be generally applicable. Gold(III) complexes have a square-planar geometry with four coordination sites. Thus, the chiral environment around the gold(III) center can be easily controlled by rational ligand design in a modular approach. In asymmetric catalysis, the active site of the chiral gold(III) catalysts could be positioned in a close proximity to the chiral substituents in order to have effective asymmetric induction and hence to achieve high enantioselectivity. Using a modular approach, it is envisioned that rational design and synthesis of chiral gold(III) complexes would be highly promising for asymmetric catalysis. In this proposal, we will rationally design and synthesize novel chiral bis-cyclometallated phenyloxazoline gold(III) complexes in a modular approach to function as efficient catalysts for asymmetric catalysis. We plan to synthesize chiral bis-cyclometallated phenyloxazoline gold(III) complexes with ligands of tunable steric size and to establish a structure-activity relationship between the chiral environment of the catalysts and enantioselectivity in asymmetric catalysis. The steric size of different parts on the chiral ligand will be adjusted enabling the precise control on the steric effect of the ligands. In addition, we plan to use chiral substituents capable of formation of hydrogen bonding with the substrates so as to improve enantioselectivity. By tethering the two chiral ligands with a linker of different lengths, we propose to tune the dihedral angle in order to afford distorted square planar geometry of the chiral bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes, aiming to improve their catalytic efficiency and enantioselectivity. Finally, we propose to study the use of visible light induced generation of chiral organogold(III) intermediates for the synthesis of chiral oxazoline[3,2-a]pyridinium compounds and studies on their diastereoselective dearomatization reactions.

15300520.label: Realisation of objectives
15300520.value: 1. To rationally design and synthesize novel chiral gold(III) complexes featuring chiral biscyclometallated phenyloxazoline ligand scaffolds in a modular approach for asymmetric induction (a) Modular approaches for the synthesis of novel chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated phenyloxazoline gold(III) complexes We have developed a new modular synthetic route for efficient synthesis of chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes. We used chiral hydroxyl-containing organomercury oxazoline complexes as a key intermediate, allowing further modification into a variety of new chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes with alkyl chain linker connected between the two chiral ligands via SN2 reaction with dibromoalkane of different chain lengths. When dibromoalkane with a short alkyl chain (n = 2) was used, the tethered chiral cyclometallated organomercury complex was not observed. When n = 3, only a trace amount of tethered chiral cyclometallated organomercury complex could be obtained with 8% yield. Notably, as the chain length of the dibromoalkane increased, the yield of the tethered chiral cyclometallated organomercury complexes increased, (n = 4) and (n = 5) in 51% yield and 81% yield, respectively. For alkyl chain length of (n = 6), (n = 7), and (n = 9), the yields are 70%, 40%, and 35%, respectively. Then, the tethered chiral cyclometallated organomercury complexes were converted into the corresponding chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes by transmetallation using KAuCl4 in 7% - 30% yield. This work “Design and Synthesis of Chiral C2-Symmetric Tethered Bis-Cyclometallated Gold(III) Complexes for Asymmetric Catalysis” has been summarized in a manuscript under preparation. (b) Controlled supramolecular assembly of gold(III) amphiphiles in aqueous media Supramolecular assemblies of gold complex-based amphiphiles in aqueous media are highly structural sensitive to external environments, providing an attractive prospect for its application in soft functional materials. In the previous section, we have developed chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes by using a variety of alkyl chains attached to gold(III) complexes. In this section, we have developed a new class of C^N cyclometalated gold(III) amphiphiles (GA), connected to a quaternary ammonium ion with an alkyl-linker to the cyclometalated gold(III) motif. We attached a long alkyl chain with the terminal hydroxyl group onto the ligand by simple SN2 reaction. By converting the hydroxyl group to a hydrophilic charged quaternary ammonium group, the gold(III) complexes exhibited amphiphilic property due to the hydrophilic moiety and the hydrophobic core part. Notably, we are the first to develop the supramolecular co-assembly of the cyclometalated gold(III) amphiphiles in aqueous media. This work “Controlled Supramolecular Assembly of Gold (III) Amphiphiles in Aqueous Media” has been published in Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, e202200281. 2. To explore the applications of the newly developed chiral gold(III) complexes as catalysts for asymmetric organic transformation reactions With the chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes developed, we have conducted asymmetric carboalkoxylation reaction to study the catalytic activity of these newly developed chiral gold(III) catalysts. For the use of chiral non-tethered gold(III) complexes in asymmetric carboalkoxylation reaction, only a trace amount of the products (3 - 6% yield) with poor enantioselectivity (2 - 3% ee) was obtained. When chiral tethered gold(III) complex was used, high catalyst/acid ratio was used, resulting in faster reaction rate in which complete conversion was achieved in 3 h to give relatively high yield (65%); yet no enantioselectivity was observed. The catalyst/acid ratio is possibly the key to control the catalytic activity and the chiral environment for enantioselectivity. If excess acid is added, both of the two metal-ligand (Au-N) bonds would be broken, the gold(III) center is more available to catalyze the reaction to achieve higher product yields. However, according to the proposed transition state of the enantiodetermining step, breaking two metal-ligand bonds would destroy the chiral environment as the chiral bulky groups on the oxazoline ligands would be far away from the bound substrate leading to no enantioselectivity in the products. Thus, the key of success is to fine-tune the catalyst/acid ratio to achieve high product yield but not reducing the enantioselectivity. In our studies, the reaction rate decreased as the catalyst/acid ratio decreased and gave lower yields (35 - 46%). However, the enantioselectivity increased to 17% ee. Having identified the optimal acid to catalyst ratio, we investigated the impact of the alkyl chain length in the tethering linker on enantioselectivity. Using this optimized acid to catalyst ratio as a basis, we studied a series of novel chiral tethered gold(III) complexes featuring alkane chains ranging from 4 to 8 carbons to investigate the influence of the linker structure on catalytic activity and enantioselectivity. Notably, the chiral gold(III) catalyst with a linker of 7 carbons afforded the highest enantiomeric excess (40% ee). We hypothesize that varying the tethering chain length influences the spatial orientation of the oxazoline ligands in the enantiomeric determining step, thus modulating the chiral environment. This modulation likely arises from restricted rotation of the metal-ligand bond and reduced ligand flexibility, which in turn governs the steric interactions between the oxazoline groups and the substrate. This work “Design and Synthesis of Chiral Bis-cyclometallated Phenyloxazoline Gold(III) Complexes for Asymmetric Catalysis” has been summarized in a manuscript under preparation. 3. To study the use of visible light induced generation of chiral organogold(III) intermediates for organic synthesis Oxazolinium cations are useful intermediates in organic transformations, facilitating the synthesis of amides, aldehydes, and ketones. We have synthesized a series of chiral polycyclic oxazolinium compounds from various aryloxazolines with silyl-substituted alkynes and internal alkynes via two synthetic pathways. By using dual photoredox/gold catalysis, coupling of chiral 2-aryloxazoline diazonium compounds with silyl-substituted alkynes afforded chiral silyl-substituted polycyclic oxazoliniums in 20-36% yield. Coupling of 2-aryloxazolines with internal alkynes afforded polycyclic oxazoliniums with up to 81% yield by Rh-catalyzed C‒H bond functionalization. X-ray crystallographic analysis and circular dichroism revealed the successful coupling of chiral (R)-2-aryloxazolines with internal alkynes and afforded the corresponding chiral (R)-oxazoliniums. Cytotoxicity analysis of the polycyclic oxazolinium compounds revealed cytotoxic activity on cancerous HeLa cells in micromolar dosage with the lowest IC50 of 6.4 µM. This work “Synthesis of Polycyclic Oxazolinium Compounds from Aryloxazolines and Alkynes via Dual Photoredox/Gold Catalysis and Rhodium Catalysis” has been accepted by Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis for publication (DOI10.1002/adsc.202500395). Chemoselective reactions are crucial toolboxes for chemical biology to give the multifunctional bioconjugates for fluorescent labelling, cell imaging, and antibody-drug development. Recently, cysteine arylation has drawn attention through the nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) strategy. This approach facilitates simple manipulation of fluorinated aromatic compounds for bioconjugation, providing advantages over metal- or photocatalyzed arylation. Cationic polycyclic heteroaromatic compounds, such as isoquinolinium, quinolizinium, and pyridinium have been developed as fluorophores for applications in catalysis, materials science and biological studies. However, there are only few reports on the synthesis and applications of oxazolinium compounds. We have developed new fluorescent cationic fluorinated oxazolinium compounds for cysteine bioconjugation via SNAr reaction. By using Rh-catalyzed reaction, a series of fluorinated oxazolinium compounds were prepared using a modular approach. We also investigated the photophysical properties of the newly developed oxazolinium compounds and explored the application for cysteine bioconjugation of peptides and proteins. This work “Fluorogenic Cysteine Bioconjugation via SNAr Reaction Using Cationic Fluorinated Oxazolinium Compounds” has been summarized as a manuscript under preparation.

15300520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300520.value: We have developed an efficient strategy for the synthesis of a novel class of chiral C2-symmetric tethered bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complexes and studied asymmetric catalysis. This novel synthetic strategy employs inexpensive and readily available chiral oxazoline derivatives to prepare a key organomercury intermediate. Subsequent reaction of this intermediate with various linkers of different chain-length enables the efficient construction of a series of chiral gold(III) complexes possessing tunable catalytic activity. By adjusting the length of the linkers, asymmetric carboalkoxylation of ortho-alkynylbenzaldehydes can be improved from 0% ee up to 40% ee, clearly indicating the tunable chiral environment of the chiral gold(III) catalysts. We have developed a reversible supramolecular assembly of gold(III) amphiphiles controlled by counterions in aqueous media and their co-assembly with gold nanoparticles. Gold(III) amphiphiles, which respond reversibly to counterion exchange and to co-assemble with AuNP in a controllable manner, were designed and clearly demonstrated. Nanofibres of GAOTs were confirmed by TEM and NRFA. GAOTs can serve as a template for AuNP growth. Reversible supramolecular assembly transformation of GAOTs between nanofibres and micelles was demonstrated. The current approach would open up new prospects to produce stimuli controlled supramolecular assembly of gold amphiphiles. We have developed a series of polycyclic oxazolinium compounds from aryloxazolines and alkynes via dual photoredox/gold catalysis and rhodium catalysis. Expansion of the substrate scope indicated that aryloxazolines were compatible with various alkynes with up to 81% yield of oxazolinium products. Notably, our modular approaches enable convenient preparation of chiral oxazolinium compounds from chiral 2-aryloxazolines, which can be readily prepared from commercially available chiral amino alcohols. Cytotoxicity study revealed the cytotoxic activity of oxazolinium compounds on HeLa cells in micromolar dosage. We envision that this work would facilitate the application of oxaozlinium compounds in different research areas. We have developed a new series of novel fluorescent oxazolinium compounds for cysteine-selective arylation via fluorine SNAr reaction. Under the optimized conditions, selective modifications of cysteine-containing peptides afforded up to 99% conversion. High quantum yield of up to 0.51 was achieved with the oxazolinium bearing electron withdrawing OMe group. Finally, the oxazolinium was successfully employed in the modification of cysteine-containing proteins, allowing a visual indication for successful protein modification.

15300920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300920.value: Willmore 流和表面扩散方程的保结构收敛有限元方法

15300920.label: Project Objectives
15300920.value: We shall reformulate the Willmore flow of closed surfaces into a new system of equations which is theoretically equivalent to the standard formulation but computationally more suitable in approximating the curvature and normal vector of the surface. We shall propose a high-order evolving surface finite element method for the new system, and prove the optimal-order convergence of the proposed semidiscrete finite element method. We shall furthermore develop energy decaying time discretization methods for the equivalently reformulated system of Willmore flow. We shall prove that the resulting fully discrete method has optimal-order convergence in time and space. We shall develop novel fully discrete parametric finite element methods for surface diffusion flow of closed curves and surfaces. For an evolving closed curve, the methods would preserve two properties simultaneously, namely that the area enclosed by the curve is conserved and the length of the curve is decreasing in time. For an evolving closed surface, the volume enclosed by the computed surface will be conserved and the area of the computed surface will decrease in time. Convergence of the proposed methods will be studied through numerical analysis and numerical experiments.

15300920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300920.value: We develop high-order accurate numerical methods for approximating the evolution of surfaces in the Willmore flow and surface diffusion flow. We present rigorous analysis for the stability and accuracy of the proposed methods, and the structure-preserving properties of the methods. Two geometric structures will be preserved for the surface diffusion flow, namely the decay of area of the evolving surface and the conservation of the volume enclosed by the surface. Extensive numerical experiments will be provided to support and complement the theoretical analysis. 本项目拟发展高精确数值方法求解 Willmore 流和表面扩散方程中的曲面演化过程，并对所提出数值方法的稳定性、精确性以及结构保持性质进行严格的分析。表面扩散流将保留两种几何结构，即演化面面积衰减和表面包围体积守恒。在构造方法和分析误差的同时，本项目将提供数值实验结果来支持和补充理论分析。

15300920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300920.value: The outcomes of this project provide a foundation for further exploration and application of highly accurate finite element methods for computing geometric evolution problems. Future research could extend these methodologies to address more complex surface flows, such as anisotropic Willmore flow and geometric flows influenced by external forces or constraints. Additionally, the techniques can be adapted for evolving surfaces in higher dimensions or with topological changes, which are important in material science, biological modeling, and computer graphics. Another promising direction is integrating these methods with machine learning to enhance computational efficiency and predict long-term behavior. The developed energy-decaying and structure-preserving algorithms can also be applied to optimize numerical solutions for diverse shape optimization problems. A key course of action is to collaborate with experts in applied physics and engineering to adapt these methods for practical applications, such as simulating fluid-structure interactions or designing nanostructures.

15300920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300920.value: This research project focuses on developing advanced mathematical methods to study how surfaces and shapes evolve over time, a process that appears in nature (like bubbles forming) and technology (like designing materials). The team created new methods to simulate these changes more accurately and efficiently, ensuring the results follow natural laws, like conserving area or minimizing energy. For example, they can simulate how a liquid droplet changes shape or how an object’s surface adjusts during manufacturing. The project also explored efficient ways to simulate more complex problems, such as how shapes evolve under external forces. The results are not only mathematically rigorous but also provide tools for practical applications. In the future, these methods could be further developed to handle even more challenging problems, like changes in 3D surfaces or predicting long-term behaviors of evolving shapes, and applied to areas like biology, engineering, and materials science.

To demonstrate the potential applications by using the developed MXene compounds, such as electrocatalyst and electrochemical biosensor.

15301020.label: Realisation of objectives
15301020.value: 1. In order to achieve the objective 1, we developed an electrochemical etching (E-etching) technique. Utilizing the highly controllable and selective thermal-assisted E-etching process, we prepared and characterized MXene nanosheets with specific structures and surface functional groups. The molybdenum carbide and molybdenum titanium carbide (Mo2C, Mo3C2, Mo2TiC2 and Mo2Ti2C3) were fabricated by the E-etching method, using purified carbon-fiber cloths (CFCs) treated with ethanol and acetone before immersion in HNO3 for 6 hours under reflux. The NaOH solution neutralized the CFCs, which were rinsed and dried at 60 °C. We fabricated a 3D composite electrode by mixing MAX phase powders (e.g., Cr2AlC for Cr2C and Ti2AlN for Ti2N) with conductive carbon black in a 95:5 mass ratio, using 1 mL of 1 wt.% PVA as a binder. The MAX phase material was drop-casted onto the CFCs substrate, and with a moderate heating temperature of 55 °C and a bias of 0.7 V, the A layer in the MAX phase was dissolved in dilute HCl. The multi-layered MXene was sonicated and rinsed to remove un-etched residue, and the 2D MXene was purified by collecting the supernatant after centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes. This method, which employs diluted HCl, is safer and milder than traditional HF etching, allowing for changes in the structural and surface properties of MXenes based on different E-etching conditions. Additionally, hydrolyzed Nb2AlC was created as a precursor for MXene nanowires. In the standard procedure, KOH solution was added to Nb2AlC, followed by vigorous stirring at 50 °C. The aluminum layer was selectively removed by anodizing the MAX phase precursor for 4 hours at 1 V in a 0.5 m HCl electrolyte. The same process applied for the 2D MXene, but without the hydrolysis step for the precursor. After 4 hours, synthesized MXenes were placed in a test tube, and 80% of the supernatant was collected. The relevant process and results have been published in Adv. Sci. (2021) (Impact Factor ~15.1) and Nano Energy (2022) (Impact Factor~16.8) 2. To achieve objective 2, we utilized various techniques to assess the properties of the synthesized MXene samples. The morphology of the samples was captured using a JEOL 2100F Transmission Electron Microscope (STEM) operating at 200 kV. HAADF-STEM images were obtained using the aberration-corrected Thermofisher Spectra 300. Elemental analysis and catalyst morphologies were examined with a JEOL JSM-6490 Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) equipped with an energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) system. Raman spectra were collected using a Witec Confocal Raman system with a 532 nm diode laser. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was conducted with a Thermo Scientific Nexsa X-ray photoelectron spectrometer, featuring a monochromatic microfocus Al Kα X-ray source (1486.2 eV). All samples were freshly prepared and washed prior to XPS analysis. Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of MXene were recorded using a Rigaku Smart Lab 9 kW system with a 2D detector and Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.154 nm). For electrochemical characterization, we employed a Solartron electrochemical workstation. A polished glassy carbon (GC) electrode acted as the working electrode, with a carbon rod as the counter and a standard calomel electrode as the reference. The MXene catalysts were dispersed in deionized water and drop-casted onto the GC electrode. We performed cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge/discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at the workstation. 3. To achieve objective 3, we optimized the electrochemical etching synthesis process, adjusting factors such as E-etching temperature, time, voltage, electrolyte concentration, electrode setup, surface treatment, purification, product yield, and testing conditions like charge/discharge cycles, DC/AC fields, measurement temperature, and duration. We identified that a 3D composite electrode made from carbon black (CB) additive and CFCs porous substrate is crucial for our design. Additionally, we discovered that mild heating enhances etching of MAX materials when using a diluted hydrochloric acid etchant. Electrochemical characterizations in 0.5 M H2SO4 (aq) electrolytes were carried out using a Solartron electrochemical workstation with a typical three-electrode configuration. The working electrode was a glassy carbon (GC) electrode, while the counter and reference electrodes were a carbon rod and a standard calomel electrode (SCE) filled with saturated KCl solution, respectively. The catalysts were dispersed in 0.5 mL of deionized water and drop-cast onto the GC electrode without additional additives, achieving a mass loading of 0.1 mg cm-2 at a thickness of 80 μm, while the platinum plate was 100 μm thick. The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) was conducted at a scan rate of 5 mV s-1 without external gas purging, and the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) curve was measured from 1 MHz to 10 mHz with a 4 mV voltage amplitude versus SCE. We found that the E-etching process effectively modifies the structural properties of MXenes, including material phase, crystallinity, defects, thickness, spacing, lateral size, and surface morphology. 4. To fulfill objective 4, we integrated porous carbon fiber with self-assembled MXene compounds as electrocatalysts, achieving impressive catalytic activities of 33.3 mV in acidic and 65.1 mV in alkaline solutions. Our research reveals a feasible approach to reactive metal–support interaction (RMSI) at lower temperatures without reduction gas, enhancing potential electrocatalyst applications. Additionally, we explored the phase-controlled growth of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) on MXene substrates, directly growing 1 T’-MoS₂ and 1 T-MoSe₂, which exhibited strong electrochemical activity with a low overpotential of 167 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², highlighting the distinct chemical characteristics of various MXenes. We also developed a label-free FRET-based biosensor using Nb₂CTx nanosheets. This multiplexed sensor enhances detection efficiency. Furthermore, we created a rapid, one-step, seedless, and surfactant-free method for synthesizing noble metal nanostructures with tunable anisotropy on MXene, regulated by single-DNA molecules, enhancing the nanoplatform's capabilities for molecular biosensing. The relevant experiments and demonstrations have been published in ACS Applied Mater. Interfaces (2021 and 2022) (Impact Factor ~8.3), Mater. Des. (Impact Factor ~7.6) and Small Struct. (Impact Factor ~15.9). 5. In summary, several research staff and one postgraduate student working on the GRF project have been recruited and participated in related studies during this period. 6 journal articles acknowledging this project have been published in prestigious international journals, including Advanced Science (IF ~15.1), ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces (IF ~8.3), Nano Energy (IF~16.8), and Materials & Design (IF~7.6) with the PI serving as the sole or co-corresponding author for these papers. To share our findings, the PI delivered 3 plenary or invited presentations on electrochemical MXenes at recognized international conferences focused on MXenes and materials. All research outputs have credited this GRF project. Additionally, our research titled “HF-free facile and rapid synthesis of MXenes related materials and their efficient energy conversion and storage applications,” by HAO Jianhua and PANG Sin-Yi, received a TechConnect 2021 Global Innovation Award (October 2021, Washington, DC, USA), with acknowledgment of this funding. Please refer to https://www.techconnectworld.com/World2021, the list of awardees at https://www.techconnectworld.com/World2021/participate/innovation/awards.html, https://www.polyu.edu.hk/en/media/media-releases/2021/1018_polyu-innovations-win- techconnect-awards/. Furthermore, this project involved supporting work on a U.S. Patent (Pub. No. US20200399771A1), entitled “Method for HF-free Facile and Rapid Synthesis of MXenes and Related Compounds”.

15301020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301020.value: 1. We found that thermal-assisted electrochemical etching (E-etching) method enjoys advantages of highly controllable and selective etching process. Specific structures and surface groups of MXene can be prepared by E-etching. The synthesis strategy is ideal for construction of heterostructures. We developed a novel one-step method to modulate the growth of Pt quantum dots on HF-free MXene, leveraging low-temperature metal-support interactions. We demonstrated that the catalytic activity of the heterostructure catalyst can be significantly enhanced, achieving a specific current density of 10 mA cm². The overpotential needed to reach this current density is 33.3 mV, reflecting superior efficiency and low Tafel slope. (See: Part C Journal 1,2,3, Conference 2,3,4) 2. We developed a surfactant-free method for synthesizing anisotropic noble metal nanoparticles on MXene using a molecular regulator. This approach enables rapid formation of diverse nanostructures, enhancing photothermal effects and surface-enhanced Raman scattering. Simultaneously, we created a multiplexed biodetection using Nb2CTx MXene. This label-free biosensor allows identification of multiple gene fragments with detection limits as low as 15 pM. (See: Part C Journal 2 and 5) 3. We found that specific crystal phase modulations in metastable transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) can be significantly influenced by tunable surface properties of HF-free MXene substrates. The direct growth of 1T′-MoS2 and 1T-MoSe2 on electrochemically synthesized MXene reveals that the phase characteristics can be tailored effectively. The resulting heterostructure catalysts exhibit enhanced electrochemical activity, achieving a low overpotential of 167 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm-2. This research highlights the surface engineering capabilities of various MXenes, showcasing their superior electrochemical performance. (See: Part C Journal 1,3,6, Conference 1,2,4) 4. We explored memristors made from 2D MXene Ti3C2 nanosheets as artificial synapses for neuromorphic computing. Our study revealed that these memristors exhibit both digital and analog resistive switching behaviors, contingent on the applied voltage. We demonstrated essential synaptic functions, including long-term potentiation, and successfully emulated “learning-forgetting.” These findings highlight the potential for integrating memristors into artificial neural networks for image recognition. (See: Part C Journal 4, Conference 3) 5. We investigated the potential of MXene macrostructures as a reinforcing agent in polymer-based nanocomposites, highlighting their superior mechanical robustness and environmental stability. We observed significant enhancements in thermal and electrical properties of the resulting composites. The manipulation of MMs' structure and their interactions with polymers was found to critically influence performance outcomes. (See: Part C Journal 6, Conference 2)

15301020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301020.value: Firstly, we have primarily focused on the synthesis of HF-free MXene through a thermal-assisted electrochemical fluoride-free strategy. Recently, the application of MXene in electrocatalysis, biosensing, and neuromorphic computing has gained much attraction. Therefore, there is a new opportunity to explore the integration of HF-free MXene developed in this project into information technology devices, which offers innovative designs for 2D MXene heterostructures aimed at advancing device development. Specifically, the direct growth of 2D materials on MXene surfaces is anticipated to enhance capabilities in 2D information devices. Secondly, our findings indicate that the potential for MXene heterostructures can be extended to a wider range of promising materials beyond conventional 2D options, paving the way for the development of high-performance nanoelectronic devices and catalysts. Compared to bulk materials, the surface characteristics of 2D materials play a crucial role during fabrication due to their atomically thin nature. Although we have made progress with heterostructure-based MXene compound in our research, further theoretical exploration and application development regarding interfacial engineering and performance are required. Additional studies on the MXene-based heterostructure design and 2D phenomena are necessary before these innovative catalysts and devices can be effectively utilized in practical applications in the future.

15301020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301020.value: MXenes have become an important family of nanomaterials, which exhibit versatile properties leading to numerous promising applications. However, the acute toxicity of HF acid impedes the large scale fabrication of MXenes and their wide utilization in applications. In this project, we have developed electrochemical etching (E-etching) method. Taking advantage of the highly controllable and selective thermal-assisted E-etching process, we have prepared and characterized the MXene nanosheets with specific structures and surface groups. As a much safer and milder method than the conventional HF-etching, the E-etching method is developed to prepare commonly used MXene compound. Furthermore, this method has been successfully extended to produce some novel MXenes. Thanks to the high degree of controllable variances in the thermal-assisted electrochemical fluoride-free synthesis strategy, we developed a one-step method to grow platinum quantum dots on MXene. We also demonstrated the direct growth of transition metal dichalcogenides on the HF-free synthesized MXene, resulting in highly active electrochemical catalysts. Furthermore, we designed a multiplexed biosensor utilizing MXene for rapid and sensitive detection of biomarker. Our research paves a non-toxic and HF free route to prepare various MXenes and demonstrates various applications in sustainable energy and biochemical sensing using MXene compounds and MXene-based heterostructures.

15301120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301120.value: Self-assembling and targeted delivery of supramolecular compounds /nanoparticles have received much attention over the past decade, as they can offer high-loading as carriers for free drug delivery to a specific target, providing an alternative strategy to address prevalent challenges of inferior water solubility, premature bio-degradation, rapid renal clearance, cancer non-selectivity and real-time trafficking of hydrophobic drug molecules. However, monitoring their function in deep tissue has always been a problem. Responsive fluorescence is seen to be one of the possible solutions, however, even with near infrared excitation/emission, limitations to a few nm of penetration power is insufficient to be of practical use. The advantage of fluorescence signals is to help with evaluating the drug performance, such as toxicity, uptake profile in vitro. For deep penetration imaging, MRI is the more conventional method. The simple and similar isostructural coordination properties of lanthanide ions is an advantage for developing fluorescence / MRI probes. For example, gadolinium is used based on its paramagnetic properties for MRI, whereas the photophysical properties of europium (visible), ytterbium (NIR) ions is useful for optical imaging. The change of the metal ion allows the same ligand to be used for different imaging modalities, giving rise to versatility. In this regard, developing a single-component multifunctional self-assembling theranostic prodrugs, which combines selective cancer targeting as well as real-time imaging/ diagnosis is an ideal “all-round” strategy. In this proposal we focus on this area to synergistically design lanthanide probes to combine different imaging modalities with specific disease targeting vectors to overcome some of the current inherent disadvantages of commercial imaging probes and to open up the field for precision medicine. The use and design of dual functional optical imaging probes for sensing and inhibition of certain diseases such as cancer are very important to elucidate information concerning the pathology of diseases that are constantly evolving, hence our work will be targeting specific oncogene proteins which plays a critical role in malignant tumours. eg. epithelia cancers. Based on our recent work, our key goals are to develop a self-assembling lanthanide nanoparticle delivering vehicle by utilizing a pro-drug approach for specific imaging and inhibition of some of our oncoprotein of interest such as LMP1. We hope to directly allow real-time trafficking of the drug as well as to study its binding/inhibition functions. Direct visualization of the action and location of specific molecules within complex living systems is a key to understanding their functions and potential as drugs. 超分子化合物/納米粒子的自組裝和靶向遞送具有 在過去的十年中受到了很多關注，因為它們可以提供高承載力 為特定目標免費提供藥物，提供替代策略來解決 低水溶性，過早生物降解，快速腎髒病的普遍挑戰 清除率，癌症的非選擇性和疏水性藥物的實時販運 分子。然而，監測它們在深層組織中的功能一直是一個問題。 響應式熒光被認為是可能的解決方案之一，即使 近紅外激發/發射，穿透功率限制在幾納米 不足以實際使用。熒光信號的優點是可以幫助 評估藥物性能，例如毒性，體外吸收情況。對於深 穿透成像，MRI是更常規的方法。簡單而相似 鑭系元素離子的同構配位性質是開發的優勢 熒光/ MRI探針。例如，基於順磁性使用g MRI的特性，而euro（可見），的光物理特性 （NIR）離子可用於光學成像。金屬離子的變化允許相同 配體可用於不同的成像方式，從而提高了多功能性。在這 方面，開發單組分多功能自組裝理論 前藥，結合了選擇性的癌症靶向以及實時成像/ 診斷是一種理想的“全方位”策略。 在本提案中，我們專注於這一領域，以協同設計鑭系元素探針， 將不同的成像方式與特定的疾病靶向載體相結合，以克服 商業成像探頭的一些當前固有的弊端和開放 精密醫學領域。

15301120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301120.value: In this project period, a few systems have been developed Firstly, we have devised a molecular-to-micellar strategy to incorporate a lanthanide nanoplatform for the delivery of an anticancer drug that simultaneously offers hybrid near-infrared (NIR) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capabilities with ratiometric variations of lanthanide metals to afford ratio metric control. These nano composites have cancer selective properties due to the methodology of the self-assembled nanocomposite with a small drug molecule. The selection of the lanthanide nanocomposites was prepared using hybrid nanoparticles (Gd/YbNPs) which can give rise to NIR and MR imaging properties. Our study shows that the enhanced stability at ultralow critical aggregation concentrations shows simultaneous optical and MR imaging, and can improved delivery/chemotherapeutic efficiency, and cancer cell selectivity . This shows potentials of such nanomicellar theranostic prodrugs for use in vitro and in vivo imaging , offering a stimuli-activated NIR luminescence and real-time MR imaging biocompatible nanoplatform for selective cancer treatment. Secondly, we also developed a few improved DOTA based analogies with both chiral and non chiral derivatives for enhancing the contrast images in MR and also in improving the stability as well as evaluated the importance of coordination geometic isomers. In this work two chiral DOTA chelators was optimised to display higher stability and relaxivity than Gd-DOTA, rendering them as potential CAs in terms of safety and efficiency. Both coordination geometric isomers of (TSAP)/ (SAP) of our two Gd complexes were studied and found to have prominent relaxivity compared to the commercial contrast agent , Gd-DOTA. Our work here, reflects the importance of the control in coordination isomer formation and also the use of specific isomers in both chiral and achiral DOTA complexes for particular applications. We also looked at the limitations in reaction-progress monitoring for bioorthogonal chemistry and successfully utilised some of the intrinsic luminescence or magnetic relaxivity properties of our lathanide compounds affording it as a strategy to monitor specific bioorthogonal reactions. In this work, a Eu(III)-based complex is reported as a small-molecule optical imaging agent which shows off-on luminescence and provides quantitative analysis for the progression of the bioorthogonal reaction. The characteristic signal is achieved through efficient energy harvesting and transferring to the Eu(III) from the expansion of the conjugated system of the antenna. Moreover, the gadolinium(III) counterpart significantly enhances relaxivity in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after the bioorthogonal reaction since the rotational correlation time is shortened with increased molecular sizes and weights.

15301120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301120.value: In our future work, some of these systems will be optimised and investigated with other types of oncoproteins. Also, more biological and pharmacokinetics studies will be performed to assess the suitability of these developed contrast agents/ imaging probes. We believed by developing more multifunctional and smart imaging agents as well as creating more interactive and selective systems , this will open the door for the use and application of theranostics

15301120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301120.value: In our project , we developed a nanocomposite system using mix lanthanide ratios which shows prodrug potential and can be used for multimodal imaging. We also developed improved methodologies for synthesising and engineering more advanced imaging chelators for different MRI/ PET imaging modalities. For example, we show that chiral functional group, geometric coordination isomers are also important in affecting the properties of the macrocyclic chelators and can be manipulated to help enhance the stability and chemical inertness to provide safer contrast agents. Simultaneously, we also developed a luminescent lanthanide based complex which can be used as an optical imaging probe , as it shows off-on luminescence which can give quantitative analysis in monitoring specific bioorthogonal reactions.

15301220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301220.value: The efficient utilization of clean energy requires low-cost and high-performance energy storage devices. Li-ion batteries have gained giant success in portable electronics due to their superior energy density. The extension to large-scale applications such as stationary energy storage is partly restricted by the limited lithium reserves. In view of sustainability, potassium-based batteries would be an alternative considering the natural abundance of potassium resources. Nevertheless, the large radius of K ion renders difficulty in designing appropriate electrode materials for potassium-based batteries. Having a high theoretical capacity of 685 mAh/g, potassium metal anode is receiving increasing attention. The practical application will not only provide a high-capacity anode for K-ion batteries but also enable the use of potassium-free cathodes such as sulfur and oxygen, which are under intensive exploration. The primary two factors afflicting potassium metal anode are the severe safety issue arising from the dendrite growth and the short service life due to the low Coulombic efficiency. Non-uniform plating-stripping leads to the preferential growth of metallic potassium, which may induce short-circuit of the cells and isolation of active potassium. A freestanding carbon nanofiber (CNF) film produced by electrospinning will be employed as a host electrode. It will function as several roles including i) a fast charge transfer path for running at high rates; ii) nucleation sites for uniform potassium growth, and iii) a buffer layer to accommodate the volume change. To achieve these objectives, the microstructure of CNFs will be tailored to provide diverse nucleation sites with a low energy barrier. An alloy-based potassiophilic interphase will be fabricated to increase the affinity between carbon host and potassium. Furthermore, the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) will be regulated to increase the electrochemical stability and mechanical properties with remarkable homogeneity at nanoscale. A robust and homogeneous SEI will further inhibit the sporadic deposition and prevent the fracture during cycling. Alkali-metal batteries suffer from similar issues. The fundamental understanding and design principles developed in this project will also benefit the lithium and sodium metal anodes. 低成本高性能儲存系統對於清潔能源的使用至關重要。鋰離子電池在便攜式電子器件中取得了巨大成功，但是由於鋰資源有限，它在大規模能源儲存中的應用受到了部分限制。自然界中鉀資源比較充足，鉀基電池可以作為鋰離子電池的有效補充。鉀離子半徑較大，對於開發合適的電極材料帶來了挑戰。鉀金屬電極具有685mAh/g的理論容量，它的實用化不僅可以為鉀離子電池提供高性能負極，也將推動鉀-硫和鉀-空氣電池的發展。目前鉀金屬負極開發的難點在於解決枝晶生長帶來的安全問題和庫倫效率低導致的容量衰減。本項目將利用靜電紡絲製備的納米碳纖維作為鉀金屬沉積的載體，碳纖維將發揮以下三個功能: i) 提供電子快速輸運通道，提高倍率性能；ii) 充當鉀金屬成核位點，引導其均勻生長；iii) 為電極膨脹提供自由空間，保持電極結構穩定。為實現以上目標，將通過微觀結構調控在碳纖維中創造豐富的活性位點，並利用合金修飾碳表面增加碳和鉀之間的親和力。此外，將調控固態電解質界面膜來提高其電化學和機械穩定性，有效抑制鉀金屬非均勻沉積和界面破裂。鹼金屬負極具有較多共性，本項目所提出的結構設計和原理探索也將會為鋰金屬和鈉金屬的開髮帶來有益的借鑒。

15301220.label: Realisation of objectives
15301220.value: The objectives of the project have been realized, which are summarized as follows: (1) Carbon nanofibers (CNFs) have been prepared by electrospinning using polyacrylonitrile as a precursor, followed by stabilization in air and carbonization under a constant flow of Ar gas. We have systematically tailored the heteroatom contents and graphitization degree of CNFs by carbonization at a wide temperature range from 800 to 2800 oC. The CNFs with varied microstructures are adopted as the host for potassium metal anodes to explore the correlation with potassium deposition behavior, including the nucleation overpotential and morphology evolution under different deposited potassium amounts. We have also assembled asymmetric cells to evaluate the long-term stability of potassium anodes and their rate capability. In addition, the effect of CNF surface functionality on the formation of solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) has also been investigated, which plays a vital role in achieving high Coulombic efficiency and long lifespan. The composition and mechanical properties of SEIs on different CNFs have been probed through X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and atomic-force microscopy-based nanoindentation, respectively. (2) Apart from the host materials, the electrolytes also have a great impact on the nanostructure of SEIs. SEIs mainly consist of electrolyte decomposition products; thus, modifying the electrolyte formulations could directly affect the SEIs composition. A series of potassium metal anodes with regular variations in the physicochemical properties of electrolytes were constructed by varying the concentration of KFSI in ethylene carbonate (EC)-diethyl carbonate (DEC). The Young’s modulus and yielding strain of SEIs under different electrolytes have been examined to investigate the mechanical stability of SEI upon electrode swelling/contraction. The homogeneity of SEIs could be detected by collecting the mechanical properties at diverse positions. The electrolyte with a medium concentration demonstrates the highest stability. We reveal that, through experimental and finite element simulation, such an unusual stability root in the alternation of SEI’s nanostructure and the resulting mechanical properties of the SEIs. (3) To test the performance of potassium metal anode in critical conditions, we have assembled full cells by coupling with high-voltage manganese hexacyanoferrate cathodes. A new electrolyte is designed to satisfy the stability at a high voltage while maintaining the superior Coulombic efficiency of potassium metal anode. The cells deliver decent cyclic stability at a challenging anode/cathode capacity ratio of four. Furthermore, we have developed a cycling protocol with a high pulse current density at the initial stage for eliminating the potential dendrite formation and inducing abundant nuclei, which could greatly extend the cyclic life.

15301220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301220.value: We have developed CNF hosts and modified the electrolyte formulations to improve the stability of potassium metal anodes. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows. (1) We found that, compared to the Cu current collector, the CNFs could significantly reduce the nucleation overpotential from over 200 mV to around 50 mV. Improving the carbonization temperature promotes the graphitization degree and reduces the defects of CNFs, which positively impacts the Coulombic efficiency and extends the cyclic life. Moreover, we reported the surface functionality of CNFs could alter the amount of organic and inorganic species in the SEIs, thus offering a potential way to optimize the SEIs besides electrolyte regulation. Under classical carbonate electrolytes, the CNFs carbonized at 2800 oC exhibit a decent Coulombic efficiency and stable long-term cycling for over 2000 h (C: Research Output No. 1). (2) We reported that the mechanical properties of SEIs greatly impact the stability of potassium metal anodes, which could be tuned by simply changing the electrolyte concentration (C: Research Output No. 2). The high concentration increases the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte and the resulting SEIs, both of which are beneficial to decreasing the overpotential during K plating/stripping. Despite these, increasing the concentration does not benefit the Coulombic efficiency and cyclic life. A smooth potassium plating morphology is observed in the electrolyte with a medium concentration of 0.5 M KFSI/EC-DEC, giving rise to the highest efficiency and longest cycle time. The reason lies in the largest maximum elastic deformation energy of SEIs formed in the 0.5 M electrolytes, which has a balanced Young’s modulus, elastic strain limit and ionic conductivity. We also reviewed the recent progress in probing the mechanical properties of SEIs and provided a perspective toward future development (C: Research Output No. 4). (3) We developed an initial high-current discharging protocol to promote potassium nucleation (C: Research Output No. 3). It was generally thought the high current density would deteriorate the stability due to the fast depletion of potassium ions at the interface. Our studies show that a pulse-high current at the beginning of each discharging is beneficial because of the increased nucleation sites, which guide the subsequent potassium deposition at normal current rates in the following discharging process. (4) We developed a novel electrolyte formulation based on non-fluorinated ether with extended alkyl groups to enable high-voltage potassium metal anodes (C: Research Output No. 5). Extending the terminal groups of ether expands the electrochemical window to realize the stable cycling of High-energy Mn-based Prussian blue cathodes. The performance is further enhanced through S-containing additives to promote the kinetics. Consequently, the potassium metal full cells with a limited anode excess deliver promising stability.

15301220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301220.value: In this project, we have shown that developing CNFs host and functional electrolytes could greatly improve cyclic stability. While this project focuses primarily on the anodes, the stability of cathodes cannot be ignored. Particularly, high-voltage cathodes are essential to realize a competitive energy density, posing a challenge to the cathode-electrolyte interphases (CEIs). Thus, the designed electrolytes should benefit both the SEIs on the potassium metal anodes and the CEIs. Furthermore, the performance at a wide temperature is necessary for the practical application. Again, this requires building stable interphases to boost the kinetics at low temperatures and inhibit the parasite reactions at high temperatures. The correlation between the interphase composition and mechanical/electrochemical stability established in the project could provide insights into the rational SEI/CEI design.

15301220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301220.value: Considering the resource abundance and reasonable energy densities, potassium metal batteries could complement current energy storage systems to facilitate clean energy utilization. The dendrite formation and deteriorated interfaces are the primary two factors afflicting the potassium metal anodes. In this project, we addressed the challenges through host electrode design and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction. We first prepared carbon nanofibers (CNFs) through an electrospinning technique and tailored the surface functionality and graphitization degree to explore the effect on the potassium nucleation and growth behavior. Such a three-dimensional CNF host enables the stable cycling of potassium metal anode for over 2000 h in classical carbonate electrolytes. We then optimized the electrolyte formation to tune the composition of SEI. In particular, a novel ether-based electrolyte has been developed through solvent molecular engineering, which benefits not only the anode stability but also the high-voltage cathode for full-cell construction. Besides these, this project was also devoted to the fundamental understanding of potassium nucleation and SEI stability. A customized cycling protocol has been established to manipulate the potassium nucleation/growth, while nanoindentation tests have been conducted to thoroughly investigate SEI's mechanical stability. These findings would guide further development of potassium metal batteries.

15302120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302120.value: 近年來，關於電磁場與兩種不可壓縮，不互溶和導電流體的相互作用的研究在工程中具有重要意義，例如鋁電解槽，冶金工業，泵加速器，MHD發電機和聚變反應堆。兩相MHD問題的一個基本問題是兩種不同的不可壓縮流體之間的界面動力學。在本項目中，我們考慮一個Cahn-Hilliard-MHD模型，該模型由Cahn-Hilliard方程（自由界面），Navier-Stokes方程（流體力學）和Maxwell方程（磁場）組成。這些方程通過對流非線性耦合，壓力和洛倫茲力。 為了解決耦合非線性系統，我們建議開發一種無條件穩定且滿足離散能量定律的時間離散化方案。這絕非易事，因為我們必須克服一些重大挑戰，其中包括：（i）通過不可壓縮性約束來耦合速度和壓力； （ii）與界面寬度有關的相位方程的剛度； （iii）將密度作為變量係數的昂貴壓力求解器，以及（iv）通過非線性對流和應力將相場變量，流場變量和磁場變量耦合在一起。我們開發的方案基於以下方法：（1）線性穩定方法來處理Cahn-Hilliard方程中的三次項； （2）速度和相位函數的穩定解耦； （3）速度和壓力的有效解耦。 進行Cahn-Hilliard-MHD模型分析的一個簡單主意是將Cahn-Hilliard和MHD方程的可用方法結合起來。然而，事實是這種組合思想僅部分起作用，因為強大的耦合，非線性和剛度引起了巨大的困難和技術問題。為了直接基於弱公式證明Cahn-Hilliard-MHD模型的適定性，我們計劃利用非奇異解分支的框架。為了證明模型的能量定律，我們計劃在工作中利用通用框架：[J. Shen和X. Yang，兩相不可壓縮流相場模型的能量耦合解耦方案，SIAM數值分析，53（1）：279-296，2015]。本質上線性解耦方案的穩定性分析遵循上述思想進行模型的穩定性分析。但是，完全離散的線性解耦方案涉及不同時間步長的數量，特別是由於對線性化和去耦進行了明確處理。由於引入了用於處理耦合項和非線性項的輔助中間函數，因此對於解耦，線性和完全離散方案的誤差分析存在重大挑戰

15302320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302320.value: Spin-orbitronics, which exploits the interplay between the spin and charge degrees of freedom via the spin-to-momentum coupling, has become a heated topic of investigation in the field of spintronics, with the prospects for practical spin current generation schemes and associated applications in data storage and logic operations. Among various device structures investigated for spin-orbitronics, heavy metal (HM)/ferromagnet bilayers have demonstrated spin-Hall magnetoresistance (SMR) and spin-Hall anomalous Hall effects (SHAHE). In particular, rare-earth iron garnets (REIG) are frequently used as the ferromagnetic layer due to its insulator property. Typically YIG is used as the REIG, while recent years there is also a surge in other REIG systems (such as TbIG, GdIG) which demonstrate perpendicular anisotropy and compensation temperatures (Tcomp, at which overall magnetic moment of the material momentarily vanishes). Studies of Pt/REIG with Tcomp have shown a rich variety of phenomena. On the other hand, there is always debate on whether the spin-Hall related effects are interfacial or bulk in nature. There are a few studies on inserting spacers at the HM/REIG interfaces, and virtually all investigations used REIG layers with homogenous composition. Well-designed REIG heterostructures that provides a stable HM/REIG interface and adjustable bulk magnetism, we argue, would bring new prospects in the studies of spin-orbitronics, and should be of fundamental interest. In this proposal, two types of REIG heterostructures will be prepared, with the purpose of keeping a constant Pt/REIG interface while the bulk of the garnet layer is modulated. Based on garnets of different RE (Tb and Y) we will prepare: (1) TbIG/YIG/TbIG trilayers, with varying distance of YIG from Pt inner-face, to investigate the variation of spin-Hall magnetotransport properties. (2) YIG/(Y,Tb)IG, where (Y,Tb)IG is the mixed iron garnet of Y and Tb that shows gradual variation of magnetism (such as Ms and Tcomp), such that the impact of varying REIG bulk can be directly probed. Epitaxial REIG multilayers will be grown on lattice-matching substrates, before they are covered with Pt and patterned into Hall-bar structures. Magnetoresistance and anomalous Hall effect measurements on those samples will be conducted as functions of temperature and layer thicknesses. Results will be compared with polarized neutron reflectivity and first-principle density functional theory calculations, in order to obtain a holistic picture on the SMR behaviour and provide experimental bases for building better models to explain the SMR-related phenomena. 自旋-軌道電子學是有關載流子的自旋及角動量的耦合之研究，現已成為自旋電子學領域中一個熱門課題。它有望能提供自旋電子流產生的具體方案，並帶動相關的數據存儲和邏輯運算之發展。在各種自旋軌道電子器件結構中，重金屬(HM)/鐵磁體器件結構已被證明能夠展示自旋霍爾磁阻(SMR)和自旋霍爾異常霍爾效應(SHAHE)。 在這類器件結構中，稀土鐵石榴石(REIG, 特別是 YIG)因其電絕緣性而被廣泛用作鐵磁層材料。近年來，其他REIG系統如TbIG，GdIG也因其表徵垂直磁各向異性和補償溫度(Tcomp，即材料於該溫度時其磁矩會被壓抑)而受到關注。不同的 Pt/REIG的研究已顯示出多種自旋霍爾效應和Tcomp有關的現象。 另一方面，究竟自旋霍爾效應是源自介面還是材料本身，也一直存在爭議。其中一些研究嘗試於HM/REIG介面中插入其他材料，但幾乎所有研究均使用均質磁性的REIG層。我們認為，如果能夠利用設計良好的REIG異質結構，即可提供穩定的HM/REIG界面而同時調節REIG層的體磁，而這將會為自旋電子學的研究帶來新的方向。 在本研究中，我們將準備兩類REIG異質結構，目的是保持Pt/REIG介面不變而同時調節石榴石層的磁性。基於不同RE (Tb和Y)的石榴石，我們將準備：(1) TbIG/YIG/TbIG三層薄膜，並逐漸改變YIG與Pt層的距離，以研究其自旋霍爾磁傳輸性質。(2) YIG/(Y,Tb)IG，其中(Y,Tb)IG是混合Y和Tb的鐵石榴石，會因應Y及Tb 的比例展示出磁性的逐漸變化(如 Ms 和 Tcomp)，以便直接探測REIG材料變化的影響。 我們會在晶格匹配基板上生長外延REIG多層薄膜將，並蓋上Pt以製作霍爾器件結構。這些樣品於不同溫度和層厚度的磁阻和霍爾效應測量將被檢測，並與極化中子反射實驗和DFT理論計算結果比較，以求全面了解SMR行為，並為構建更佳的SMR模型提供實驗數據支持。

Sample notation of e.g. TbIG(30)|EuIG(t) refers to a 30-nm TbIG layer covered with a top EuIG layer of thickness t nm). Objective 1: 100% completed. Three set of garnet-type heterostructures were prepared in this project: (1) GGG(111) substrate|TbIG(30)|YAG(t1); (2) GGG(111)|TbIG(30)|EuIG(t2); (3) GGG(111)|TbIG(t3)|EuIG(5)|TbIG(30-t3). Set (1) targets to investigate the impact of a non-magnetic interfacial barrier on the spin-Hall magnetotransport (SHM) of TbIG|Pt. While this set of samples is not mentioned in the objective, it serves as a starting point for the investigation of REIG|Pt interface dependence of SHM. Set (2) is an alternative for the co-doped REIG system. It was observed that by preparing bilayers of TbIG(30)|EuIG(t2), a decrease in Tcomp with rising t2 was obtained from temperature-dependent anomalous Hall effect resistance (RAHE). We postulated the effect to originate from the strong coupling between the TbIG and EuIG across the interface given their close crystal structure. Tcomp regulation by deposition of bilayers has practical advantage over co-doped system for easy variation of Tcomp by simply changing the thickness ratio of the constituent REIG layers. To this end, we considered the deposition of this sample set a more pragmatic approach in achieving bulk Tcomp modulation, as compared to the preparation of co-doped REIG targets as originally proposed in Objective 1. Finally, the sandwich structure of sample Set (3) was prepared by varying the insertion location of EuIG(5) within the bulk of TbIG(30) during the film growth process. Given the same total EuIG and TbIG thicknesses in various samples of the set, they basically demonstrated identical Tcomp (refer to sample Set (2) above). Meanwhile, the change from EuIG|Pt to TbIG|Pt interface did have an impact on the SHM behaviour as reported below. Objective 2: 100% achieved Subsequent to the PLD deposition of REIG heterostructures, Pt Hall bars were prepared by dc magnetron sputtering; the Hall-bar geometry was defined either by a stainless steel shadow mask, or by optical lithography followed by standard ion beam etching processes. Temperature-dependent SHM behaviour was investigated in three types of samples prepared under Objective 1. Primarily, RAHE resistances were measured from the samples. Temperature-dependent SHM were performed in a physical property measurement system (PPMS) up to 9 T. All sample Sets (1) to (3) mentioned above have been subjected to the measurements, results of which are listed as follows. We therefore regard the Objective to be fulfilled completely. Objective 3: 100% For sample Set (1), we observed hysteretic RAHE loops at low magnetic fields but with reducing magnitude as the YAG thickness t1 increases. A crossover of the RAHE sign was observed at temperatures below Tcomp, which decreased sharply from 135 to 34 K as t1 increased from 0 to 1 nm. Alternatively, when the YAG layer was replaced by GGG, no RAHE signal was observed even when the GGG spacer thickness was 0.5nm, which could be linked to the strong magnetic contribution of Gd ions. This work highlights the tunability of interfacial transport in REIG|heavy metal systems through ultrathin spacers. For Set (2), RAHE measurements of TbIG (30)|EuIG(t2) bilayers illustrated that tuneable Tcomp (which was observed from an abrupt sign reversal in RAHE sign, and accompanied by the divergence of coercivity (Hc)) could be achieved by changing t2. We a ascribed this to the strong ferromagnetic coupling of Fe sublattices between the two REIG layers. Very often, REIG|heavy metal heterostructures such as TbIG|Pt display two RAHE sign crossovers with varying temperatures, one being attributed to the Tcomp of REIG, and the other to the competition between the magnetic proximity effect and the spin Hall effect (often called T1 point). For sample Set (3) we modulated the layer stacking of the TbIG|EuIG(10)|TbIG sandwiches with a fixed total thickness of the two TbIG layers (30 nm) and explore the contributions of REIG bulk and REIG|Pt interfaces on Tcomp and T1. As TbIG gradually moved away from Pt, Tcomp showed some fluctuations. However, when TbIG is entirely out of contact with Pt, the second crossover point undergoes a change that shows REIG|Pt interface dependency. The results highlight the dominance of REIG bulk on the compensation behaviour, and the interface determines both the magnitude and T1 cross-over of the REIG|Pt structure. In summary, all the tasks detailed in the Objectives of the project have been accomplished.

15302320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302320.value: (references refer to outputs listed in journal publications in Section C). 1. Interlayer coupling in REIG multilayers We observed antiferromagnetic coupling at low temperatures in YIG|TbIG bilayers epitaxially grown on YAG [2]. Detailed study [8] was performed on the impacts of temperature, crystallographic orientation, and layer thickness, on the coupling and magnetization reversal behaviour of such bilayers. The interlayer coupling strength was calculated by measuring the minor hysteresis loops. 2. Modulation of Tcomp Tcomp of TbIG is around 220 K in bulk, but TbIG films grown on GGG indicate a rise of Tcomp along with decreasing film thickness [4]. We postulated this arises from interfacial element diffusion [3] and strain between TbIG and GGG [1]. Meanwhile, Tcomp modulation was achieved by controlling the EuIG thickness in TbIG(30)|EuIG bilayers, which was ascribed to the ferromagnetic coupling of Fe3+sublattices in the two REIG layers. These studies provides alternative strategies for regulating Tcomp in REIG thin films. 3. Impact of interface on SHM [6] TbIG (30)|YAG(t) were grown on(GGG) (111) substrates. YAG thickness-dependence of RAHE indicated no Tcomp change, but with reducing RAHE magnitude as t increases. The T1 point, decreased sharply from 135 to 34 K as t varied from 0 to 1 nm, due to the strong dependence of the magnetic proximity effect at the TbIG|Pt interface. Replacement of YAG spacer with GGG strongly suppressed RAHE, and no RAHE-H loops were observed for GGG spacer of 0.5 nm, which could be linked to the strong magnetic contribution of Gd ions. 4. Effect of modulated REIG bulk and REIG|Pt interface on SHM [7] The relative contributions of modulated REIG bulk and REIG|Pt interfaces on the SHM were studied in the TbIG|EuIG|TbIG|Pt system. RAHE–T plots indicated two events of RAHE sign reversal, one at Tcomp and the other at T1 which arise from the competing MPE and SHE at REIG|Pt interface. The results indicated that Tcomp changes need to consider the contribution of the whole REIG stack. The T1 point exhibited strong REIG|Pt interface sensitivity. Different stacking orders can alter the interface quality, including interface exchange coupling energy and roughness, thereby affecting spin transport. The projected yielded 8 journal publications, 3 conference presentations, trained 1 PhD student. It has also led to extended collaborations on related directions (PNR beamtime in Australia for studying REIG|topological insulator structures).

15302320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302320.value: 1. The current work has not touched upon co-doped REIG, and it would be of interest to understand the physical difference between co-doped REIG and REIG heterostructures. While on a whole both structures demonstrate similar Tcomp modulation, the impact of the two different systems on the SHM is unknown. 2. An exciting prospect is the possible regulation of SHM with the solid state control of magnetism in garnets. While there are abundant studies on the magnetism modulation of perovskites and ferrites, its realization in garnets is less reported by should be of great potential. 3. The current work focused on the SHM behaviour of the samples. Related studies of such samples using other techniques (such as spin Seebeck effect, FMR measurements) would provide a holistic picture on the relative contributions of REIG bulk and REIG|Pt interface various phenomena.

15302320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302320.value: In this project, various rare-earth (RE) iron garnet (IG) heterostructures were prepared, with the purpose of elucidating the impact of REIG bulk modulation and REIG|Pt interface modification on the spin-Hall magnetotransport (SHM) behaviour. Based on REIG of different RE (Tb and Eu) we prepared: (1) TbIG|Pt with non-magnetic garnets as spacers, (2) TbIG|EuIG bilayers, and (3) TbIG|EuIG|TbIG trilayers, with varying distance of EuIG from Pt inner-face, to investigate the variation of temperature-dependent SHM properties. Epitaxial REIG multilayers were grown on lattice-matching substrates, before they were covered with Pt and patterned into Hall-bar structures. Temperature-dependent anomalous Hall effect measurements on those samples were conducted as functions of temperature and layer thicknesses. Our results indicated a strong dependence of the SHM with the REIG|Pt interface (as revealed from the variation of the T1 temperature), as well as the bulk of the REIG (with the REIG|Pt interface kept constant), as shown by the impact of compensation temperature variations on the SHM changes. Our study has indicated potential strategies in regulating Tcomp in REIG thin films, and highlights the impact of various part of REIG|Pt system on the magnetotransport behaviour.

15303020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303020.value: 有機催化劑在制藥業和藥物相關研究的不對稱催化反應中具有極其重要的作用。這是因爲有機催化的不對稱反應可以避免金屬催化劑的使用，並排除由其造成的金屬雜質在藥物中的殘留問題。除此之外，有機催化劑易於合成及便於修飾的特性也增加了其在研究應用中的便捷性。具有軸手性的聯二萘酚及其衍生物是一種得到廣汎應用和認可的有機催化劑。手性聯二萘催化劑的剛性骨架結構和分子内的活性官能團，確保了催化劑可以通過特定構象和底物綜合作用，以確保反應中高度手性誘導催化作用的產生。相較之下，對於構象不穩定的骨架結構，例如旋轉未受阻的聯苯結構，作為有機催化劑的基本結構設計的研究較少。由於可能同時存在Ra和Sa的轉阻異構體，因此通常認為，基於聯苯骨架的有機催化劑會對反應催化過程中的對映選擇性產生不利影響。但是，如果可以預測聯苯化合物的轉動性，並以此爲基礎選擇性合成具有特定結構的Ra或者Sa轉阻異構體，那麼開發新型有效的有機催化劑將成爲可能。這一方案或許可以為不對稱催化反應中的軸手性催化劑設計提供新的思路。 在該方案中，我們將圍繞一系列在合成上或者生物學中具有重要作用的反應，展開對手性聯苯基有機催化劑的研究。我們的催化劑設計主要通過結合以下方法控制聯苯結構的軸手性旋轉自由度：(1)通過引入不同的空間位阻取代基；和/或(2)通過引入酸度可調控基團來形成單一異構體，或可分離的非對映異構體有機催化劑。我們建議可以通過引入不同的取代基來合理地調節催化劑的氫鍵形成能力，並以此通過經驗研究他們在不同反應中的催化能力。為探究軸手性聯苯骨架的應用，我們希望在聯苯骨架中引入不同的功能活性位點，如-OH，-NH2，-POOH，-NHTf和-NH(thiourea)等。具有不同活性的催化劑將會被分別應用到其對應的化學反應研究中，如Strecker反應，氫氰化反應，Diels-Alder反應，Mukaiyama Aldol反應，環氧化反應，Mortia-Baylis-Hillman(MBH)反應和傅-克反應等。如果可以得到較好的反應產率和對映選擇性，那麽反應的機理研究將會進一步展開。

15303020.label: Realisation of objectives
15303020.value: We proposed to synthesize a number of new chiral atropisomeric organocatalysts that are based on rotationally unrestricted biphenyl scaffold. In addition, we proposed to synthesize a number of new chiral atropisomeric organocatalysts that can easily undergo further functional group modifications. In this project, three biphenyl diamines 1, 2 and 3 with additional stereogenic centers to control biphenyl atropisomeric selectivity were successfully synthesized. The syntheses of these diamines were not easy. A number of difficulties have to be overcome. Our original synthetic plan for direct two-step diazidation of chiral biphenyl dialcohol 1-OH and then reduction to obtain diamine 1 failed, and the 1-OH remained unreactive. Another prolonged synthetic strategy has to be applied instead. The chiral intermediate chiral bromo-azide (S)-b was synthesized by direct azidation of chiral bromo-alcohol (R)-a first. Then, another chiral intermediate bromo-NH2 (S)-c was synthesized by reduction of bromo-azide (S)-b, and the enantiopurity of (S)-c has to be high enough to proceed to the next steps. Then, this chiral bromo-NH2 (S)-c intermediate has undergone general protection with Boc-group before undergoing the next homocoupling step. However, the yields of the desired diamine product 1 from the homocoupling were found to be extremely low (< 5%) even after a number of modifications to the reaction conditions. Other protecting groups were tried but resulted in poor yields. 1 was finally synthesized by direct coupling without the need of prior NH2 protection and the yield of the desired product was found to be impressive (85%). After obtaining the biphenyl diamine compound 1, further modification to the diamino group was tried by reacting with isothiocyanate or isocyanate. The corresponding diamino-based thiourea derivative 1a and urea derivatives 1b were then successfully synthesized. Apart from the diamine 1 with methyl substituents, other diamines 2 with phenyl and diamine 3 with t-butyl substituents were synthesized with the above method. However, for the synthesis of sterically bulkier diamine 3, the first azidation step of its chiral bromo-alcohol intermediate failed. A more reactive Bose-Mitsunobu method was applied. These diamines possess sterically very different substituents: methyl, phenyl, and t-butyl. The series of steric variation is important to demonstrate how steric bulkiness affect the biphenyl atropisomerically selectivity, and hence affect catalytic behaviour. For the characterization, apart from general 1H NMR, 13C NMR and MS analyses, the diamines 1 and 2 was successfully structural characterized with X-ray crystallography. The structure of diamine 1 reveals that it is a Ra atropisomer when two stereogenic centers (C2 and C15) are in (S)-configuration (figure 2). For diamine 2, it is confirmed to be an Sa atropisomer when equipped with two (R)-stereogenic centers (C24 and C25). Functionalization of the diamines 2-3 were also performed. For the diamino-based thioureas 2a (phenyl), 3a (t-butyl) and urea derivatives 2b (phenyl), 3b (t-butyl), the synthetic method was similar to that for 1a and 1b. The atropisomeric stability for all biphenyl compounds (1-3, 1a-b, 2a-b, 3a-b) were investigated with 1H NMR studies. Only the most sterically hindered tert-butyl 3, 3a, 3b and 2 are atropisomeric stable and no obvious atrop-isomerization can be found. However, atropisomerizations were found for the less bulky 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b. The thioureas and ureas 1a-b, 2a-b and 3a-b have been explored as organocatalysts using the MBH reaction of benzaldehyde and 2-cyclohexen-1-one as a test reaction. One equivalent of benzaldehyde, three equivalents of 2-cyclohexen-1-one, 20 mol% of catalyst and 1,4-diazabicyclo [2.2.2]octane (DABCO) were used. The results showed that all the thioureas and ureas are active catalysts that gave the allylic alcoholic product (41–69% yields) but all the products have low enantioselectivities (<10 %ee).

15303020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303020.value: The major finding in this project is the successful demonstration of the synthetic path for chiral atropisomeric diamines (1, 2 and 3) that are based on rotationally unrestricted biphenyl scaffold. Our synthetic method seems to be a general method to achieve atropisomeric diamines which can be equipped with different substituents other than methyl (1), phenyl (2) and t-butyl (3) groups. The atropisomeric stability was found to be dependent on the bulkiness of these different substituents. Furthermore, another major finding is to demonstrate the possibility of easy modification of these atropisomeric diamines (1, 2 and 3). By utilization of the reactive diamino functional group, their corresponding thiourea derivatives (1a, 2a, 3a) and urea derivatives (1b, 2b, 3b) can be easily obtained. In this project, the utilization of these chiral atropisomeric compounds as organocatalysts was successfully demonstrated with the asymmetric Baylis–Hillman reaction. Although the enantioselectivities were not ideal, they showed to be active organocatalysts.

15303020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303020.value: In this project, the results showed that sterically bulkier substituents (t-butyl > phenyl > methyl) can result in more atropisomerically selectivity. So, other sterically bulkier biphenyl, such as the methyl substituents replacing with triphenylene, pyrene, perylene, corannulene etc and their corresponding derivatives, are worth further investigation. More active chiral-induction pockets may be formed and may result in better enantioselectivity in asymmetric reaction. In addition, these kinds of chiral diamines can be further developed to be bifunctional organocatalysts. Since NH2- is a very useful functional group for further modification, by using suitable ratio of diamine and functional group precursors, potential bifunctional organocatalysts can be easily developed. Thanks to the usefulness of the NH2-, these chiral diamines can be developed as building units in other fields of research such as supramolecular structure synthesis.

15303020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303020.value: Many natural occurring substances are chiral. So, the syntheses of chiral compounds are very important because it can help us to understand nature. The synthesis of new chiral compounds is also essential to continue the development of new functional materials that may help us to build a better world. In this project, we tried to develop a new synthetic pathway to obtain one kind of very important chiral compound called atropisomeric compound. Other than that, we also developed a method to incorporate a kind of chemically and biologically very important functionality, the NH2- group, into our newly develop atropisomeric compounds. We also demonstrated how to control/maintain good atropisomeric selectivity in order to maintain a chemically purer form. We found that further incorporating other larger groups can increase our newly developed atropisomeric NH2-compounds’ purity. This concept is beneficial to develop chiral functional materials. We also demonstrated the ease of further modification of our NH2- group to other catalytic active groups-urea and thiourea groups. This is important and other active reactive groups can be incorporated.

15303220.label: Project Objectives
15303220.value: To study the importance of interaction energy disorder as opposed to particle positional disorder in glasses: A main character of structural glasses is the spatially disordered particle arrangements. The positional disorder also induces a particle interaction free energy disorder since particle interactions depend strongly on inter-particle distances. An interesting question is whether spatial disorder, energy disorder or both of them are essential pre-conditions of glassy dynamics. In another word, can a crystalline system with only an energy disorder exhibit most or all relaxation characteristics of structure glasses? The success of the construction of such a system will have the long-term impact of focusing further research of glassy dynamics on the energy disordered nature of model systems. The spatial disorder, which is very challenging to handle analytically, is then relevant to glassy dynamics only via the generation of an energy disorder. We hypothesize that the answer is affirmative. To this end, we propose to study computationally a new meta-material which is a glassy crystal with an energy disorder but a spatial crystalline order. We will examine to what extent it exhibits typical glassy dynamics and what we can learn from it about structural glasses in general. To construct glassy crystals with dynamics dominated by a density of mono-vacancies: The proposed glassy crystal is a system in which each pair of particles admits a pair-interaction with a random strength selected at the start of a molecular dynamics simulation. The random interactions model the impacts of random particle separations in glasses. In the glassy crystal, the bond length is however chosen to be uniform for all particle pairs leading to uniform particle separations. We thus expect to obtain a stable crystalline structure, while the random pairings of particles give rise to an interaction energy disorder. Particle diffusive dynamics is enabled by introducing a density of vacancies. An additional many-body interaction will be imposed to generate an effective repulsion between vacancies so as to attain mono-vacancy dominated dynamics. To quantitatively characterize the glassy relaxation properties of glassy crystals: Vacancy motions are energetically affected by random particle interactions in the proposed glassy crystals. They may be described by random walks in random energy landscapes. This motivates the expectation of possible glassy dynamics. We propose to perform extensive simulations to study the expected glassy properties of the glassy crystal. Besides heat capacitive studies and microscopic particle dynamics measurements, calorimetric spectroscopy will be investigated in attempt to observe alpha, beta, and Boson peaks. It is possible that the glassy crystal will exhibit almost all typical relaxation properties of structural glasses. To study enhanced surface mobility in glassy crystal thin films: We will study glassy crystal thin films with free surfaces and check for surface enhanced mobility. This is motivated by experimental findings of the existence of a non-glassy mobile layer on top of glassy polymer and small molecular films. The focus is to understand the mechanism by which surface enhanced mobility propagates from the surfaces to the inner regions of the films, which is a controversial problem attracting great research interest. To study perturbations to glassy dynamics upon confinement down to one and two dimensions: Besides three-dimensional bulk properties, gradual confinement to quasi-two or even one dimensional systems with periodic boundary conditions will be computationally investigated. We hope to obtain simpler quantitative characterization of confinement effects than those from usual spatially disordered glasses, which should facilitate further theoretical studies.
