To construct glassy crystals with dynamics dominated by a density of mono-vacancies: The proposed glassy crystal is a system in which each pair of particles admits a pair-interaction with a random strength selected at the start of a molecular dynamics simulation. The random interactions model the impacts of random particle separations in glasses. In the glassy crystal, the bond length is however chosen to be uniform for all particle pairs leading to uniform particle separations. We thus expect to obtain a stable crystalline structure, while the random pairings of particles give rise to an interaction energy disorder. Particle diffusive dynamics is enabled by introducing a density of vacancies. An additional many-body interaction will be imposed to generate an effective repulsion between vacancies so as to attain mono-vacancy dominated dynamics.

To quantitatively characterize the glassy relaxation properties of glassy crystals: Vacancy motions are energetically affected by random particle interactions in the proposed glassy crystals. They may be described by random walks in random energy landscapes. This motivates the expectation of possible glassy dynamics. We propose to perform extensive simulations to study the expected glassy properties of the glassy crystal. Besides heat capacitive studies and microscopic particle dynamics measurements, calorimetric spectroscopy will be investigated in attempt to observe alpha, beta, and Boson peaks. It is possible that the glassy crystal will exhibit almost all typical relaxation properties of structural glasses.

To study enhanced surface mobility in glassy crystal thin films: We will study glassy crystal thin films with free surfaces and check for surface enhanced mobility. This is motivated by experimental findings of the existence of a non-glassy mobile layer on top of glassy polymer and small molecular films. The focus is to understand the mechanism by which surface enhanced mobility propagates from the surfaces to the inner regions of the films, which is a controversial problem attracting great research interest.

To study perturbations to glassy dynamics upon confinement down to one and two dimensions: Besides three-dimensional bulk properties, gradual confinement to quasi-two or even one dimensional systems with periodic boundary conditions will be computationally investigated. We hope to obtain simpler quantitative characterization of confinement effects than those from usual spatially disordered glasses, which should facilitate further theoretical studies.

15303220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303220.value: Structural glasses and glassy thin films of nano-meter thickness are important and very active fields in condensed matter physics. A main characteristic of structural glasses is the spatially disordered particle arrangement, which also induces an energy disorder in the particle interactions. We propose to study whether it is the energy disorder rather than the positional disorder of the particles which is directly responsible to the main characteristic relaxation behaviors of glasses. Our approach is to propose and study a glassy crystal which is a meta-material with a crystalline structure but a random interactions between each particle pairs. Particle motions will be induced by a density of mono-vacancies. Detailed forms of the interactions enabling the stability of the crystalline structure and discouraging the aggregation of the vacancies will be workout out. Vacancy motions are energetically affected by random particle interactions. They may be described by random walks in random energy landscapes which dictate the motions of the vacancies and thus also of the particles. We will examine to what extent our glassy crystal exhibits typical glassy dynamics and what we can learn from it about structural glasses in general. We will conduct quantitative characterization of glassy crystals concerning standard thermodynamic and microscopic particle dynamics measurements. We will also simulate calorimetric spectroscopy measurements in attempt to access alpha, beta, and Boson peaks. Besides bulk measurements, we will also study glassy crystal thin films with free surfaces and check for surface enhanced mobility analogous to those observed in polymer and small molecular thin film experiments. The focus is to understand the mechanism by which surface enhanced mobility propagates from the surfaces to the inner regions of the films. Free surfaces may alter the dynamics drastically and overshadow bulk properties. We will in addition study confinement to quasi-one or two dimensional systems with periodic boundary conditions without any free surface, repulsive wall, or stationary bounding particles. We expect to obtain simpler quantitative characterization of confinement effects than those from traditional approaches. In all these studies, due to the spatial regularity, we expect more straightforwardly understandable results. Insight obtained will then be applied to better understand structural glasses. 结构玻璃和纳米玻璃薄膜是凝聚态物理中重要而又非常活跃的领域。结构玻璃的一个主要特征是粒子的空间排列无序性，这也导致粒子相互作用中的能量无序。我们提出是否由于能量无序而非粒子的位置无序直接导致玻璃的弛豫行为。我们的方法是提出一种玻璃化晶体，具有晶体结构但粒子对之间相互作用随机分布。我们将给出使晶体结构稳定和阻止空位聚集的相互作用的详细形式。粒子的运动是由单空位密度引起。空位运动受粒子随机相互作用的能量影响，可以在随机的能量图景中随机游走。随机能量图景决定空位的运动，也决定粒子的运动。我们将观察玻璃化晶体在何种条件下展现典型的玻璃动力学行为，并学习和理解结构玻璃。 此外，我们将根据热力学和微观粒子动力学测量对玻璃态晶体进行定量表征。通过模拟量热光谱测量，获得α-峰、β-峰和玻色子峰。除了块体测量外，我们还将研究具有自由表面的玻璃晶体薄膜，分析表面迁移率增强是否类似于在聚合物和小分子薄膜实验中观察到的结果，并理解表面增强迁移率从表面传播到薄膜内部区域的机制。自由表面可能会对动力学行为影响很大，甚至掩盖块体性质。我们将进一步研究具有周期边界条件的无自由表面、无排斥壁或无固定边界粒子的一或二维系统的约束效应，并获得比传统方法更简单的约束效应的定量表征。在所有这些研究中，由于空间的规律性，我们期望得到更直观易懂的结果，能更好地理解结构玻璃。

15303220.label: Realisation of objectives
15303220.value: We have shown that characteristic dynamical features of glassy materials can be reproduced in systems with only energetic disorder but no structural disorder, under void-induced particle motions. Our main approach is the development of a distinguishable-particle glassy crystal (DPGC) in which particles are ordered in a face-centered cubic lattice and follow particle-dependent random interactions, leading to an energetic disorder in the particle configuration space. Molecular dynamics simulations in the presence of vacancy-induced particle diffusion show typical glassy behaviours. A unique feature of this molecular model is the knowledge of the complete set of inherent structures with easily calculable free energies, implying a well-understood potential energy landscape (see objectives 1, 2 & publication 8). The unique importance of energetic disorder is also supported by studying a lattice model variant of the glassy crystal we have developed and named the distinguishable-particle lattice model (DPLM). We demonstrate that the DPLM without any structural disorder can reproduce the specific-heat capacity cv of glass formers undergoing a hysteresis when subjected to a cooling-heating cycle, with a larger cv and a more pronounced hysteresis for fragile glasses than for strong ones. We have shown that these experimental features, including the unusually large magnitude of cv of fragile glasses, are well reproduced by the DPLM after incorporating a two-state picture of particle interactions. The large cv in fragile glasses is caused by a dramatic transfer of probabilistic weight from high-energy particle interactions to low-energy ones as temperature decreases (see objectives 1,3 & publication 1). To understand the role of vacancies or analogous voids in glasses, we have studied a swap algorithm of much recent interest. We argue that swapping particles are analogous to vacancies or voids in glass. Particle swaps can drastically accelerate dynamics in glass. The mechanism is expected to be vital for a fundamental understanding of glassy dynamics. To extract defining features, we propose a partial swappability with a fraction of swap-initiating particles, which can only swap locally with each other or with regular particles. We focus on the swap-dominating regime. At all temperatures studied, particle diffusion coefficients scale with the swap-initiator density in unexpected power laws with temperature-dependent exponents, consistent with the kinetic picture of glass transition. At small density, swap-initiators, becoming defect particles, induce remarkably typical glassy dynamics of regular particles. This supports defect models of glass. In addition, we experimentally manipulate the structural relaxation of colloidal glass at an atomistically controlled position. We focus a laser beam to eject a particle from the colloidal system. This creates a void that transforms rapidly into a mobile soft spot (quasivoid) composed of a few neighbouring free-volume fragments. The transformation and subsequent motions of the quasivoid trigger a sequence of well-connected stringlike motions emanating precisely from the point of laser action with free volumes flowing along the string. Furthermore, the sequence can be terminated by the annihilation of the quasivoid (see objective 2 & publications 2,4). Confining glassy materials into films can substantially modify their local and film-averaged properties. We have applied the DPLM to simulate in thin film geometry with void-mediated facilitation behaviours but free from any elasticity effect. We analyse the spatially varying viscosity to delineate the transport properties of glassy films. The film mobility measurements reported in previous experiments are successfully reproduced. The flow exhibits a crossover from a simple viscous flow to a surface-dominated regime as the temperature decreases. The propagation of a highly mobile front induced by the free surface can be visualized in real space. Our approach provides a microscopic treatment of the observed glassy phenomena. We also determine the glass transition temperature versus film thickness from the heat capacity during heating as well as from the local relaxation time. The results based on both approaches are in good agreement with experiments. The thus demonstrated interplay between calorimetric properties and structural relaxation is further corroborated by successfully reconstructing the simulated heat capacity during heat and cooling from the local relaxation times. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the thickness of the surface mobile layer depends on temperature differently under different definitions, although all are based on local structural relaxation rate. The rate can be fitted to a double exponential form with an exponential-of-power-law tail. Our approach and results exclude elasticity as the unique mechanism for the tail. Layer-resolved particle hopping rate, potentially a key measure for activated hopping, is also studied but it exhibits much shallower surface effects (see objective 4 & publications 3, 4,7). To study confinement effects in low dimensions, we have further simplified our lattice model to a one-dimensional highly coarse-grained version called the facilitated random walk (FRW). Each particle performs a continuous time random walk in the presence of its own random local kinetic constraints. The particles do not interact energetically. Instead, they interact kinetically with a hopping rate resampling rule under which motions of a particle can randomly perturb the local kinetic constraints of other particles. This dynamic interaction is reversible, following a rate restoration rule. A step-by-step reversal of the particle motions exactly restores the previous constraints, modelling randomness quenched in the configuration space of glass. The model exhibits stretched exponential relaxation and dynamical heterogeneity typical of glasses. Despite the lack of an explicit facilitation rule, the FRW shows facilitation behaviours closely analogous to those of the kinetically constrained models (KCM). The FRW is a coarse-grained version of the distinguishable particle lattice model (DPLM) and this exemplifies that compatible defect and atomistic models can complement each other in the study of glass. Introducing a free surface at one end of the lattice, surface enhanced mobility is also studied using the FRW (see objective 5 & publication 6).

15303220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303220.value: We have proposed the possibility that the most important role of disordered structures is to induce associated energetic disorder in the presence of randomly quenched separations of neighboring particle pairs. Apart from this, the structural disorder may play little qualitative role in glassy dynamics. To achieve this, we have proposed a distinguishable-particle glassy crystal model defined on an ordered lattice. We directly incorporate energetic disorder by introducing random particle pair interactions, which in principle should result from structural disorder in realistic glasses. From our molecular dynamic simulations, major thermodynamic and kinetic properties of glasses are successfully reproduced. This should motivate further studies focusing directly on energetic disorder rather than structural disorder in order to solve the problem of glass. Our glassy crystal model adopts vacancy induced glassy dynamics. In this ordered system, the counterpart of vacancy is void, or more precisely a fragmented form of void called quasivoid. Using molecular dynamics simulation and colloidal glass experiments with laser tweezer manipulation, we have provided support of the physical relevance of quasivoid in disordered systems and have justified assumptions in the grassy crystal model. Furthermore, systems with energetic disorder are also simulated based on our DPLM and FRW lattice models. In particular, our lattice models have shown that surface-enhanced mobilities in film geometries found in experiments can be successfully reproduced. Characteristic thermal dynamic properties of glass in bulk geometry are also obtained. These results show that energetic disorder is the key feature for understanding glass.

15303220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303220.value: We believe the importance of energetic disorder in glassy systems proposed and supported in this project is a promising direction for further theoretical research. We are continuing related projects in this direction with our collaborators, including Prof. Cho-Tung Yip of Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen), Prof. Haiyao Deng of Cardiff University and Prof. Takeshi Kawasaki of Osaka University, based on molecular dynamics and lattice model simulation techniques related to this project.

15303220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303220.value: The nature of glassy dynamics and glass transition is one of the most long-standing puzzles in condensed matter physics. The major defining feature of glass is the disordered structures. However, it is not clear what the main mechanism under which the disordered structures impact glassy dynamics. We have proposed the possibility that the most important role of disordered structures is to induce associated energetic disorder due to random particle separations. Apart from this, the structural disorder can be playing little qualitative role in glassy dynamics. By proposing and simulating a distinguishable-particle glassy crystal (DPGC) model in which particles are ordered in a face-centered cubic lattice with random pair interactions leading to an energetic disorder, we have shown that typical glassy behaviours can already be reproduced. Another important assumption in the model, namely void-induced particle dynamics, is also evidenced in our simulations and experiments. Thermodynamic and kinetic properties of lattice models, which are simplified variants of the glassy crystal, are studied with characteristic glassy features in film and bulk geometries successfully reproduced. All these results contribute to support the key importance of energetic disorder, as opposed to merely structural disorder, in glassy materials.

15303420.label: Project Objectives
15303420.value: To develop ligand sets for facile reversible redox changes of the ruthenium-metalloenolate complexes: We will prepare some defined ruthenium-metalloenolate complexes coordinating with chelating nitrogen ligands bearing electron-donating and -withdrawing substituents. Their activity in modulating the reversible Ru(II)/Ru(III) changes will be examined. Our goal is to identify the optimal ligand scaffolds that favor the catalytic alkylation of the metalloenolates. To determine the structure-activity relationship of some defined ruthenium-metalloenolate complexes toward alkylations: We aims to develop a mechanistic model for the alkylation reaction and delineate the desirable steric and electronic properties of the ligands and the enolates for selective transformations. Stoichiometric reactions of alkenes and alkyl radicals with the metalloenolates will be investigated. It is expected that a three-component catalytic carbenoid coupling system with predictable chemo- and regioselectivity would be developed. To develop enantioselective alkyl-alkyl coupling reactions based on the ruthenium-metalloenolates: Having developed a working model for metalloenolates alkylations, we would pursue the more challenging enantioselective C-C bond coupling reactions. Chiral ligands with appropriate donor sets will be examined for favorable electronic and steric properties. A challenging goal is to achieve C-C bond formation with contiguous stereocenters.

15303420.value: 卡宾插入到M-C(SP2)键（M=过渡金属）是C-C键形成的有效策略。在此之前，我们选择有机硼酸，卡宾和NFSI试剂（苯磺酰亚胺）三组分芳基氟化反应。该反应利用卡宾插入到芳基-Rh(III)配合物，形成金属环烯中间体，并与NFSI反应生成C-F键。结合实验和计算研究表明，HOMO位于C(alpha)位置利于亲电氟化反应。在这一结果的启发下，我们设想在C()位点的自由基烷基化应该是实现烷基与烷基交叉偶联反应的有效策略。 在本计划中，我们旨在开发一锅法使卡宾的插入实现自由基烷基化反应。我们先前的研究Ru(II)配合物与有机硼酸和重氮试剂(卡宾插入)自发反应生成相应的Ru(II)烯烃配合物。我们假设Ru(II)烯烃配合物的单电子氧化得到相应的Ru(III)配合物。Ru(III)中心的自旋离域与烯烃片段作用赋予C()自由基特征。因此，Ru(III)烯烃类配合物可以使烯烃和烷基发生自由基反应形成C(SP3)-C(SP3)键。显然，手性配体的引入将直接影响烷基对映选择性。 我们重点探究一些已知螯合含氮配体对Ru(III)/Ru(II)氧化还原对的影响，并研究它们的烯烃配合物的自由基烷基化反应。通过循环伏安法可以研究配体对Ru(III)/Ru(II) 可逆氧化还原对的影响。我们推测简单的Ru(III)-Ru(II)相互转化应该是有效的催化自由基烷基化的基础。此外，类似的-芳基配合物的也是令人感兴趣的。Ru(III)--烯丙基配合物有望在烯丙基配体的取代位点实现亲核自由基反应。所提出的自由基-烯丙基烷基化反应该补充钯催化反应，因为它是亲核进攻取代反应的首选。 另一个挑战是利用地球丰富金属催化剂实现三组分卡宾类偶联反应。在适当的自由基前体下，我们计划探索一些Cu(I)-酰胺配合物的单电子氧化，形成Cu(II)-酰胺和卡宾自由基。自由基随后与重氮类化合物生成结构比较复杂的二次自由基，与Cu(II)-酰胺配合物偶联，最后实现烷基-氮键的形成。该反应为合成功能多样的烷基胺提供一个良好的策略。发展类似的对映选择性烷基胺的合成是可以实现的。 过渡金属催化烷基-烷基交叉偶联反应为构建有机分子的C-C骨架提供了一种简单直接的方法。有利于我们通过三组分卡宾类偶联反应开发功能化烷烃和胺的合成。不对称烷基交叉偶联催化方法的发展为药物和材料设计提供了良好的平台。

15303420.label: Realisation of objectives
15303420.value: This project aims to develop efficient regiocontrolled C–C bond formation technology based on carboradical cross-coupling reactions. Based on the initial success of the Pd-catalyzed direct alkylation of arenes, we are keen to explore a broader application of the radical chemistry C–C and C–X bond formation. In this respect, our initial attempt is to explore the metalacyclic ruthenium-enolate complexes for radical coupling reactions. While the reactions were successful at a stoichiometric scale based on ESI-MS and crude NMR product analysis, the ruthenium system failed to turnover for catalysis. After some investigation, we found that the radical reaction did not took place at the C(enolate) center, instead a C–O bond coupling product was later confirmed to be the product of the radical coupling reaction with the metalacyclic Ru-enolate complex. The preferred C–O over C–C bond formation is attributed to the 6pi-electronic stabilization of the metalacyclic ruthenium-enolate structure, and the nucleophilic nature of the enolate is polarity-mismatched with the alkyl radicals tested. To realize the project objectives, we focused on radical coupling with Cu-enolate complexes. We recently established that Cu-H complexes, generated in situ by hydride transfer reagents such as PMHS, can undergo facile coupling with diazoacetate to afford Cu-enolate complexes in good yields. Based on this finding, we have developed a hydroamination of diazoesters using O-benzoyl hydroxylamines as aminating reagents. The hydroamination reaction delivers the unnatural alpha-amino acid derivatives in good yields and functional group tolerance (including cyano, alkene and esters). The Cu-catalyzed protocol operates under mild conditions and is applicable to several classes of diazoesters and amino benzoates, affording the desired amino acids. Mechanistic experiments revealed the intermediacy of a nitrogen radical, suggesting that radical amination of the Cu(II) enolate complex generated by the hydrocupration of the diazoesters may be critical for the C–N bond formation. This work has been published in Organic Letters. Diazo compounds have been extensively used as precursors of reactive transition metal-carbene species to mediate many synthetically valuable transformations such as alkene cyclopropanation, C–H/X–H (X = N, B, Si) insertion, and ylide-type reactions. Recently, we developed the metal-free photoredox decarboxylative C(sp3)–N coupling of alpha-diazoacetates with alkyl N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) esters to access structurally and functionally diverse N-alkyl hydrazones. In this project, we developed a highly efficient coupling reaction of alpha-diazoacetates with amino acid-derived alkyl N-hydroxy phthalimide esters to synthesize 1,2,4-triazoles. Under metal-free conditions involving 1,8-diazabicyclo(5.4.0)undec-7-ene (DBU) as the base, highly functionalized 1,2,4-triazoles can be obtained in excellent yield with remarkable functional group tolerance. 1,2,4-Triazoles belong to a privileged class of five-membered aromatic heterocycles containing three nitrogen atoms that exhibit a broad spectrum of biological activities. Some notable examples are ribavirin (antiviral), letrozole (anticancer), and itraconazole (antifungal). With the optimized conditions, a series of aryldiazoacetates bearing a variety of electron-donating and -withdrawing groups are effective substrates for the cycloaddition reaction. As anticipated, structural variation on the ester group of the diazo esters is also tolerated. Apart from donor-acceptor diazo compounds, acceptor-acceptor diazo compounds such as malonates and phosphonates were effective coupling partners. Yet, the NHPI scope was limited by the synthetic accessibility of the reagents. For instance, those NHPI esters derived from amino acids bearing simple alkyl side chains can be prepared in good yields and react successfully with the diazo esters under optimized conditions. However, despite multiple attempts, the synthesis of the NHPI esters from more functionalized amino acids was unsuccessful. NHPI esters are known to undergo thermal and photochemical decomposition to form reactive carboradicals. However, the cycloaddition reaction was completely tolerant to radical traps such as TEMPO and BHT. This finding is not compatible with radical mechanism. NMR studies on the reaction of NHPI esters with DBU revealed the facile decomposition reaction of the NHPI esters as the key step to initiate the cycloaddition reaction. While we could not characterize the immediate products of the NHPI esters decomposition, a preliminary mechanism involving carbanion derived from the NHPI esters was proposed. This work has been published in Organic Letters. Our next project concerns the development of structurally and functionally diverse synthesis of gem-difluoroalkenes by cross-coupling reactions. gem-Difluoroalkene is recognized as a bioisostere of the carbonyl group in drug design. Unlike carbonyl groups, which are prone to reduction by NAD(P)H-dependent reductases, replacing them with gem-difluoro alkene has been shown to exhibit prolonged in vivo bioactivities and pharmacokinetic profile. Furthermore, gem-difluoroalkenes can be converted into a range of organofluorine structures, including trifluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, monofluoroalkenyl, and difluoromethylenyl groups, facilitating late-stage functionalization. However, the diverse synthesis of gem-difluoro alkenes was limited by the coupling scope of conventional Wittig, Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons-type olefinations. Recent advancements have occurred through transition metal-catalyzed defluorinative cross-coupling reactions involving SN2' reactions involving vinyl trifluoromethyl compounds. Yet, synthesizing the trifluorovinyl precursors can be costly due to the limited availability of the trifluoromethyl precursors. In 2021, we developed a straightforward and modular approach for the synthesis of gem-difluoroenol ethers and gem-difluoroalkenes by the Ni-catalyzed coupling of some structurally diverse 2,2-difluorovinyl benzoates (BzO-DFs) with a variety of nucleophiles such as arylboronic acids, arylmagnesium bromides, alkylzinc bromides, potassium alkyltrifluoroborates. Building on this foundation, we have expanded the catalytic cross-coupling of BzO-DF with alkenes. Compared to main-group organometallic nucleophiles, alkenes are more abundant feedstocks. Indeed, Fu and co-workers have already established that alkenes can act as effective surrogates for main-group organometallics reagents. To begin, we tested some simple alkenes such as 1-decene, and they are ineffective coupling partners with all the starting materials being recovered. Assuming Ni-H intermediate, the observed failure is somewhat unusual, and hydrometallation of alkene is known to be spontaneous in general. Notwithstanding, we turned to search for effective alkene coupling partners by hypothesizing that a preinstalled coordinating group on the alkene substrates may facilitate the metalation process. After extensive screening of alkenes with various coordinating groups, we found that treating N-(but-3-en-1-yl)picolinamide (0.1 mmol) and 1-ethoxy-2,2-difluorovinyl benzoate (BzO-DF) (0.2 mmol) with Ni(COD)₂ (10 mol%), 4-methoxypyridine (15 mol%), Ph2SiH2, and K₂CO₃ (2.0 equiv) in THF at 60 °C for 16 hours afforded the desired product in 85% yield. An optimization study revealed that picolinamide is the best directing group for the coupling reaction, while other groups such as 8-aminoquinoline gave less optimized results. Employing bidentate phenathroline and bipyridine as ligands yielded <40% product formation; simple pyridines gave far better results (>60% yield). Yet, 2,6-dimethoxypyridine ligand is not as efficient as the 4-methoxypyridine ligand for the coupling reaction. The observed high regioselectivity of the coupling reaction is noteworthy. While adding alkenes commonly afforded two regioisomeric addition products, our reaction exclusively afforded a single regioisomer with the difluorovinyl group connected to the carbon at the delta position to the amino group. Assuming the vinyl-Ni complex rather than a Ni-H intermediate, the regioselectivity can be understood by the favorable 5-membered metallacycle formation after the vinyl addition to the C=C bond. Furthermore, the BzO-DF coupling reactions with alkenes do not proceed via a carboradical pathway since the addition of TEMPO failed to interfere the coupling reaction, and the desired product was formed in 85% yield under standard conditions. Employing deuterated silane reagent for the coupling reaction afforded that deuterated product in which the deuterium was specifically labeled at the gamma-carbon.

15303420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303420.value: (1) We developed a Cu-catalyzed cross-electrophilic coupling reaction for synthesizing α-amino acid derivatives from α-diazoesters with O-benzoyl hydroxylamines with Cu(OAc)2 as the catalyst and polymethylhydrosilane (PMHS) as the hydride reagent. Excellent functional group compatibilities were demonstrated. With ethyl 2-diazo-3-oxobutanoate as precursor, a Cu-acetoacetate complex has been characterized by ESI-MS analysis. Results from the radical trap experiments are consistent with the intermediacy of nitrogen-centered radicals. This strategy offers a simple and inexpensive synthesis of α-amino acid derivatives. This work has been published in Organic Letters. (2) 1,2,4-Triazoles are privileged scaffolds for many pharmaceuticals, and methods leading to structurally diverse compound libraries are of current interest. In this project, we developed a highly efficient coupling reaction of alpha-diazoacetates with amino acid-derived alkyl N-hydroxy phthalimide esters for the synthesis of 1,2,4-triazoles. Under metal-free conditions involving 1,8-diazabicyclo(5.4.0)undec-7-ene (DBU) as the base, highly functionalized 1,2,4-triazoles can be obtained in excellent yield with remarkable functional group tolerance. Preliminary studies revealed that 1,2,4-triazole 3a exhibits potent inhibition of tyrosinase activities in melanoma B16F10 cell lines. This result demonstrates that 1,2,4-triazoles such as 3a can be promising skin-whitening agents. This work has been published in Organic Letters. A patent has been filed for possible application development and technology transfer. (3) gem-Difluorovinyl moiety is considered a bioisostere of carbonyl groups. Reports showed that drug candidates having the carbonyl group replaced by gem-difluorovinyl group displayed better bioactivity and pharmacokinetic properties. In this project, we developed a Ni-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction of alkenes with our difluorovinyl benzoate (BzO-DF) building block. The high degree of regioselectivity of the vinylation reaction is likely controlled by the directing group mediated by the five-membered metallacycle formation. A preliminary mechanistic study supports the vinyl-Ni(II) intermediate, and its reaction with alkenes should proceed by a non-radical pathway as supported by the insensitivity of the product yields with radical trap reagents such as TEMPO. A manuscript summarizing the project results is in preparation.

15303420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303420.value: This project has developed highly efficient cross-coupling reactions for the synthesis of structurally and functionally diverse unnatural alpha-amino acids, 1,2,4-triazoles, and gem-difluorovinyl compounds. These compounds serve as valuable building blocks for synthesizing potential drug candidates through late-stage functionalization or downstream coupling reactions with various medicinally active molecules. For example, one of our triazole compounds has demonstrated enhanced inhibition of melanin formation. We are collaborating with Nanjing Normal University to investigate further the inhibitory activity of these compounds. It appears possible to develop a new class of anti-melanoma drugs. A patent for the catalytic synthesis of 1,2,4-triazoles has been filed. We will continue to develop catalytic processes for the synthesis of diverse gem-difluorovinyl compounds. Despite some initial successes, the knowledge regarding the basic reactivity of difluorovinyl metal complexes is limited. We are attempting to isolate and characterize the putative vinyl metal complexes, and we will survey their reactivity toward various organic building blocks. We hope to formulate a more comprehensive understanding of our BzO-DF building block design to devise more efficient coupling reactions

15303420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303420.value: This project established metal-catalyzed conditions for C–N and C–C bond formation, involving metal-carbene and radical coupling pathways. We demonstrated that migratory hydride insertion into metal-carbene is highly versatile for generating diverse metal-enolate complexes. Electrophilic nitrogen radicals can selectively functionalize these metal-enolate complexes to form C–N bonds. The successful development of catalytic C–N bond coupling reactions via metal-carbene and nitrogen radicals provides straightforward access to a range of unnatural alpha-amino acids for potential applications in drug research. Recognizing the significance of triazole in drug research, we developed a simple and versatile metal-free cycloaddition method to prepare diverse triazole compounds using NHPI esters and diazoacetates. Notably, the compound library created by our metal-free reactions is not easily accessible through conventional synthesis. Some of our compounds have been favorably tested for anti-tyrosinase activities, which may serve as a lead in designing first-in-class anti-melanoma drugs. Further testing of the compounds is underway in collaboration with Nanjing Normal University. We successfully developed a route for the diverse synthesis of gem-difluoroalkenes for drug development research. Our research has created a valuable platform for efficiently synthesizing potentially bioactive compounds. This capability is essential to prepare Hong Kong as a world-leading bioscience research hub.

15303720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303720.value: From its origins in the work by Monge and Kantorovich in the eighteenth and the twentieth centuries, respectively, and through to the present day, the optimal transport (OT) has been a well-developed mathematical theory that defines robust metrics between probability distributions. In recent years, optimal transport theory has gained much attention for its numerous applications in machine learning, including unsupervised learning, semi-supervised learning, optimization models for clustering and text classification, as well as in statistics, and other applications. In the big data era, the large-scale models from these applications have placed significant new demands on the efficiency of algorithms for solving the OT problem. As a consequence, much research is needed, for dealing with the burgeoning appeals of solving the OT problem, especially for large-scale (often nondifferentiable) problems with realistic data. Specifically, novel theories and algorithms should be elaborately developed to explore the rich structures, in particular the sparsity and the nondifferentiability, exhibited in the corresponding OT problem. In this proposal, we focus on the Wasserstein barycenter problem (WBP), which is essentially a multi-marginal OT problem. In the discrete setting, the computation of the WBP with the support to be known can be formulated as a large-scale linear programming (LP) problem. Thus, we propose to study the LP model of the WBP and its nonconvex counterpart with unknown supports. Specifically, we will develop in-depth theoretical results and powerful solvers for solving the WBP. For large-scale LP model of the WBP, primal-dual interior point methods or the semismooth Newton inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian methods may fail to solve them efficiently while the first-order methods based numerical packages are often not robust enough and in general may only be able to deliver solutions of low to medium accuracy. This indicates that one needs new approaches to solve these large-scale LP models that are always highly degenerate with many basic variables to be zeros. In this proposal, exploiting the solution sparsity in addition to data sparsity, we shall design an efficient sparse smoothing Newton algorithm with low complexities for solving the LP model of the WBP, and establish the superlinear convergence of the proposed method. Moreover, for the nonconvex WBP, we shall design an efficient proximal alternating minimization method for the outer iterations. Hence, once the outer loops and the subproblems are settled, we will further extend the sparse smoothing Newton algorithms to deal with the subproblems arising from solving the nonconvex WBP. 從最早起源於18世紀Monge的工作和20世紀 Kantorovich的工作，一直發展到今天，最優傳輸（OT）已經具備完善的數學理論，它可以用來定義概率分佈之間的魯棒度量。近年來，最優傳輸理論因其在機器學習中的眾多應用而受到廣泛關注，包括無監督學習，半監督學習，用於聚類和文本分類的優化模型以及統計和其他應用。在大數據時代，來自這些實際應的大規模問題對求解OT問題的演算法效率提出了的新要求。因此，需要大量的研究來解決求解OT問題的新興需求，特別是對於具有實際數據的大規模問題（通常是不可微的）。具體而言，我們應該開發新穎的理論和演算法，以探索相應OT問題內在的豐富結構，尤其是稀疏性和不可微性。 在本項目中，我們將主要關注Wasserstein重心問題（WBP），該問題本質上是一種多分佈的OT問題。在離散意義下，在支撐已知的情況下，我們可以將WBP的計算轉化為大規模線性規劃（LP）問題。因此，在本專案中我們將研究WBP的LP模型及其在支撐未知下的非凸模型。具體來說，我們將為WBP建立深入的理論結果和高效的求解器。對於WBP的大型LP模型，高階方法，例如原對偶內點法或基於半光滑牛頓法的不精確鄰近點增廣拉格朗日方法，可能無法有效地求解；同時基於一階方法的數值軟體包通常不夠魯棒，並且一般情況下只能夠求解到中低精度的解。目前這些已存在的方法的缺點正好給我們的研究提供了機遇和挑戰，因此我們需要提出一種新的算法來解決這些WBP中高度退化的大規模LP模型。在本項目中，充分利用數據稀疏性以及解的稀疏性，我們將設計一種複雜度較低的高效稀疏光滑化牛頓算法來求解WBP的LP模型，並分析該方法的超線性收斂性。此外，對於非凸WBP，我們將為外部迭代設計一種有效的鄰近交替極小化方法。這樣，當外部迭代和子問題確定後，我們將利用我們提出的稀疏光滑化牛頓算法來求解相應的子問題。這些有效策略的結合，使得我們有理由預期我們提出的方法在求解WBP上將表現地非常高效和魯棒。

15303720.label: Realisation of objectives
15303720.value: We have designed a smoothing Newton algorithm for solving the optimal transport problem. Leveraging the sparsity of the solution and the data, we use the Huber smoothing function and implement a dimension reduction technique to reduce the dimension of the Newton system in our algorithm. Thus, the computational cost is relatively low despite the large scale of data. As a by-product, we propose an efficient HPR algorithm for solving the Wasserstein barycenter problem (an important application of the optimal transport problem), for which we prove the computational complexity is linear to the dimension of data. We have designed an alternating minimization method for the nonconvex optimal transport problem, where the subproblem can be solved efficiently by the smoothing Newton method. We develop software based on the smoothing Newton method for solving the optimal transport problems in MATLAB and another software HOT in Python for solving the optimal transport problems based on the HPR method. All objectives have been achieved, supported by the necessary exploration and detailed analysis.

15303720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303720.value: We have designed a smoothing Newton algorithm for solving the optimal transport problem. The global convergence of the algorithm is established. We prove this algorithm is locally superlinear convergence under the strict complementarity condition. To enhance the efficiency of the algorithm, we use the Huber smoothing function and implement a dimension reduction technique to leverage the sparsity of the optimal transport problem. Consequently, we only need to solve a much smaller Newton system compared to the original one, which means the computational cost for the proposed algorithm is relatively low even for large-scale data. During the research, we also come up with another idea to simultaneously have good complexity results and a low computational cost. We propose HPR algorithm, as a by-product, for solving the Wasserstein barycenter problem, which is an important application of the optimal transport problem. The sparsity is fully utilized that the computational complexity of the HPR algorithm is linear to the dimension of the problem. We have designed an alternating minimization method for solving the nonconvex optimal transport problem. The main subproblem of this method is a convex optimal transport problem that can be solved by the proposed smoothing Newton method. The numerical results show that the proposed method is 2-4 times faster than Gurobi's interior point method. We develop software based on the smoothing Newton method for solving the optimal transport problems in MATLAB, which is around 1-6 times faster than Gurobi's interior point method. We develop another software HOT in Python for solving the optimal transport problems based on the HPR algorithm. It can be used in various applications like color transfer, texture synthesis, and mixing. The numerical results show that HOT (on GPU) is 15 times faster than Gurobi (on CPU) and 20 times faster than the convolutional Sinkhorn method (on GPU).

15303720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303720.value: We aim to further refine the smoothing Newton algorithm by exploring alternative smoothing functions that could enhance convergence rates and stability. Additionally, we plan to investigate the potential of relaxing the strict complementarity condition while maintaining the algorithm's superlinear convergence properties. Our alternating minimization method has shown significant speed advantages over existing methods like Gurobi's interior point method. We intend to delve deeper into optimizing this method, potentially integrating advanced machine learning techniques to adaptively guide the optimization process and further reduce computational time. Finally, we are eager to apply our algorithms to a wider range of real-world applications. By collaborating with industry partners, we hope to address practical challenges and gather valuable feedback that will inform future improvements of our designed algorithm and software. Through these efforts, we aspire to push the boundaries of optimal transport solutions and contribute to advancements in fields such as logistics, image processing, and beyond.

15303720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303720.value: The optimal transport (OT) problem has many important real applications. As an example, when one needs to figure out the most efficient way to move goods from warehouses to stores in various locations, solving the OT problem will help to find the best solution. We have designed a smoothing Newton based algorithm to solve the OT problem with or without fixed supports. We further designed a highly efficient HOT algorithm for solving OT problems with discrete supports in 2D, which can substantially outperform the popular Sinkhorn algorithm. We developed optimization software based on the designed algorithms for solving the OT problems in both CPU and GPU, which is demonstrated to be much faster than the state-of-the-art solvers, such as Gurobi, and POT. The research outcomes of this project significantly contribute to a wide class of important applications in industries like logistics, supply chain management, and so on.

Different types of isomers were selected for the investigation, including amino acid isomers Leu, Ile and allo-Ile, their homo di-, tri-, tetrapeptides, their analogue isomers with similar alkyl side chains, such as amino alcohols (S)-isoleucinol, (R)-isoleucinol and (S)-leucinol, keto acids (S)-3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid, (R)-3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid and 4-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid, fatty acids (S)-3-methyl-pentanoic acid, (R)-3-methyl-pentanoic acid, 4-methylvaleric acid and 2-methylvaleric acid; saccharide isomers with different compositions, connectivity and configurations, e.g., monosaccharide isomers glucose, fructose, mannose and galactose, and disaccharide isomers maltose, cellobiose, isomaltose, lactose and sucrose; chiral drugs (S) and (R)-propranolol. It was found that the difference of the isomer assemblies in drift time and collision cross sections (CCSs) in IM-MS generally became larger with the increased number (n) of the assembled analytes. 3. Investigation of the assembly-driven differentiation of isomers with multiple mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry. Multiple MS/MS of assembly ions of amino acids: It was found that larger assembly ions of Leu, Ile and allo-Ile, typically with an even number of M and more than 4 copper ions, consistently lost a M2Cu during the multiple MS/MS. The dissociation spectra of [M2CuII-H]+ of Leu, Ile and allo-Ile exhibited loss of only H2O and CO2 even at very high collision energy, indicating the high stability of the complex ions. Taken together, these suggested M2Cu as a predominant dissociation/building block. Interestingly, different degrees of isomeric discrimination were observed during the multiple MS/MS. For example, the intensity ratios of product ion to precursor ion for the complex ions of Ile and allo-Ile were 0.4155 and 0.2137, respectively at MS2 (I679/I841), and became 0.2346 and 0.1951, respectively at MS4 (I388/I518), showing a new dimension for isomeric differentiation. Combination of two chiral selectors for chiral recognition by MS/MS: For the first time, combination of two chiral selectors (CS1 and CS2) was used for chiral recognition by MS, and chiral recognition was evaluated based on chiral-recognition ratio (CR) values, i.e., the intensity ratios between product ions and precursor ions of copper-bounded trimeric complex ions [CuII(M)(CS1)(CS2)-H]+. Chiral selector pairs such as Pro/Phe, Pro/Trp, Pro/Tyr, Pro/His, Pro/Ser and combinations of Pro with amino acids with other side chains have been attempted for chiral recognition of 19 chiral amino acids were successfully differentiated. Significant chiral discrimination was observed. Particularly, chiral selector pairs Pro/Phe and Pro/Trp enabled successful chiral differentiation of all 19 amino acids. In general, amino acids with aromatic rings showed better chiral discrimination as either chiral selectors or analytes. An interesting finding is the different roles of the two chiral selectors. Both of them could contribute to the chiral discrimination degree, but one of them might specifically play an anchoring role in determining the chiral discrimination tendency. Differentiation of chiral drugs by MS/MS: Chiral drugs with different structural properties have been investigated for chiral differentiation by MS/MS typically with the use of amino acids as the chiral selectors. For the ofloxacin enantiomers, dissociation of [ofloxacin+2Tyr+Cu-H]+ into [ofloxacin+Tyr+Cu-H ]+ resulted into a CR value of 0.85±0.02. For the clopidogrel enantiomers, a CR value of 2.16+/-0.04 was obtained when the timers [clopidogrel+2Trp+Cu-H]+ dissociated into [clopidogrel+Trp+Cu-H]+. For the omeprazole enantiomers, a very significant CR value of 0.27+/-0.15 was obtained by dissociating [omeprazole+2Phe+K+H]2+ into [omeprazole+Phe+K]+ without use of copper ions. Very interestingly, for the bupivacaine enantiomers, without use of chiral selectors, a CR value of 2.50+/-0.12 was achieved with the self-assembly trimers [3M+H]+ dissociated into dimers [2M+H]+. Chiral selectors for omeprazole were investigated by introducing one amino acid, combinations of two amino acids, and dipeptides as CSs, each with and without copper-bound. When using one amino acid, only Trp was found to result in the chiral differentiation of omeprazole. Combinations of two amino acids performed better, with four sets of amino acids (His/Ala, His/Leu, His/Thr and Phe/Trp) resulting in CR values ranging from 1.17+/-0.01 to 1.53+/-0.07. Dipeptides even outperformed the combinations of two amino acids, and all dipeptides investigated could lead to the chiral recognition of omeprazole with significant CR values. To explore the versatility of peptides in chiral discrimination, the MS/MS-based method using peptides was extended to another chiral drug, clopidogrel, which also led to outstanding results, e.g., a CR value of 0.50+/-0.05 obtained for [clopidogrel+Trp/Ala+K]+ with loss of an analyte. 4. Investigation of assembly and structures by combining the experimental data from IM-MS and tandem MS with the computational modelling. The general features of the assemblies were studied with computational modeling by using density functional theory (DFT) and evaluating the theoretical CCSs of assemblies using exact hard-sphere scattering (EHSS). For Leu and Ile, it was revealed that in the assemblies, an amino and a carboxyl group with lone pair of electrons are attracted to the transition metal ions in the centre, with the alkyl chains protruded outwards as a hydrophobic shell. The typical loss of large assembly ions and the remarkable stability under high energy suggested the role of the copper-bound dimer M2Cu as the predominant building block for the assembly, and all the observed assembly ions could be aligned well based on the proposed building block and bases, with good correlations between the CCSs and the assembly numbers. In the structures of the assemblies, the differences between the isomers, which are mainly the alkyl side chains, could be projected onto the exterior of the assemblies, and the ∆CCSs could be accumulated with the growing number of assembled units, leading to more significant discrimination of the isomers by IM-MS. The geometries of copper-coordinated dimers and trimers for chiral recognition of amino acids by MS/MS were also explored. It was revealed that in the dimers, two amino acids coordinated with copper as a square planar base and showed a trans arrangement of N and O atoms. For the trimers, over 100 initial geometries of [CuII(Pro)(Phe)(Tyr)-H]+ were calculated and optimized, including the number of coordination sites (4: square planar; 5: square pyramidal; 6: octahedral). Complexes of 5-coordination resulted in the lowest energy geometry, with two amino acids coordinated with copper in a square planar base, and the other amino acid had only one elongated axial coordination bonding. Such geometries enabled consistent results from the experimental and modelling studies.

15304020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304020.value: Higher assembly of isomers tends to enable larger CCS differences and thus more significant discrimination of isomers in IM-MS. This result indicates an interesting phenomenon that assembly could allow accumulation and enlargement of differences between molecules, which could be explained by the proposed structures of the higher assemblies, and suggests a new approach for differentiation of isomers. Our investigation revealed the copper bound dimer of amino acids, M₂Cu, as the predominant building block, as well as the assembly bases and assembly pathways for copper-coordinated assemblies of amino acids, providing new insights into relevant biological processes and manufacture of material assemblies. The combination of two chiral selectors revealed the potential different roles of the two chiral selectors, with the anchoring role for one of them in determining the chiral discrimination tendency. This allowed a better understanding of the chiral recognition mechanism and a new strategy for designing of chiral selectors for better chiral recognition. Dipeptides were proven to be ideal chiral selectors for both omeprazole and clopidogrel, outperforming one amino acid and combinations of two amino acids. Peptides, which are short chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds, may utilize the chiral environment caused by amino acid residues while provide more stable and tightly bound structures for chiral recognition.

15304020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304020.value: Our study demonstrated that the combinations of two chiral selectors could create new possibilities for chiral recognition by MS. More combinations of chiral selectors can be studied in order to figure out the conditions of playing specific roles. Computational modelling can be further applied to elucidate the structures and energies of the complex ions formed from various amino acids and their fragment ions and to understand the chiral recognition mechanism. The binary chiral selector system established for chiral recognition of amino acids can be further applied to various other compounds, such as amino acid analogues, saccharides and drugs, to develop general strategies for chiral recognition and provide hints for the origins of the homochiralities in biological systems. Our finding that dipeptides had better chiral recognition performance than single amino acids and combination of two individual amino acids opens a new source of chiral selectors. Peptides with various combinations of chiral amino acids can be attempted for the chiral recognition of various compounds, and the results obtained by the MS-based method can be utilized as a chiral stationary phase to HPLC columns. Many studies can be further planned to this end.

15304020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304020.value: Differentiation of isomers is an important task in research fields such as chemistry, biology and pharmaceutical science, and mass spectrometry (MS) is the method of choice for differentiation of isomers due to its advantages in speed, sensitivity and specificity, and ability to study molecular assembly and recognition in the gas phase. In this project, various isomeric compounds have been investigated with ion mobility MS (IM-MS), MS/MS and computational modeling. The results showed that higher assembly of isomers tended to enable larger collision cross section differences and thus more significant discrimination of isomers in IM-MS. Multiple MS/MS and modeling studies revealed the predominant building block and the assembly pathways of the assemblies. Furthermore, combination of two chiral selectors and use of dipeptides as the chiral selectors showed interesting results and new possibilities for isomeric differentiation by MS. Overall, the results of this project proposed new approaches for differentiation of isomers and provided new insights into molecular assembly mechanism and fundamental chemistry.

15304420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15304420.value: 反常扩散模型的反问题研究：数值方法与分析

15304420.label: Project Objectives
15304420.value: First of all, we plan to study the numerical method for solving the backward problem of the subdiffusion equation, which involves a fractional derivative in the time variable. The goal of this part is to provide rigorous error analysis of the discretized problem of a quasi-boundary type method. With a fully discrete scheme, the discretization errors are introduced into the problem. Then it is important to derive a priori error estimates, to provide guidelines to balance crucial algorithmic parameters: discretization error and regularization parameter with the noise level. However, such an analysis remains unavailable (even for normal diffusion), and it is precisely this gap that the first part of the project aims to fill in. The analysis relies heavily on refined properties of (discrete) solution operators, and nonstandard error estimate for the direct problem in terms of problem data regularity. Moreover, the argument will be further extended to the more complicated case of weak problem data and semilinear problems. Second, we shall investigate the inverse source problem of the subdiffusion with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. Due to the nonlocality of the “fractional” derivative, many powerful tools from PDE theory and classical numerical analysis, e.g., energy argument and integration by parts formula, are not directly applicable. Therefore, in most existing works of inverse subdiffusion problems, the analysis is mostly based on the analytic properties of Mittag-Leffler functions (or equivalently the Laplace transform), which are not available for the case of time-dependent diffusion coefficients. In this research programme, we shall develop a rigorous approach to tackle the challenge, which relies on certain a priori estimates of the problem established by a novel perturbation argument proposed in our prior work. Further, we shall propose and analyze a fully discrete scheme for the inverse source problem with rigorous error analysis. Such an estimate seems still unavailable even if the diffusion operator is independent of time or spatially / temporally dependent only source functions, in the context of normal diffusion, due to the low regularity of the recovered source term. The analysis is expected to rely on smoothing property of subdiffusion, nonsmooth data error estimate, and some technical tools like discrete L^p-maximum regularity and discrete fractional Gronwall’s inequality. Third and last, we focus on the inverse problem of superdiffusion, which is generally described by a space-nonlocal diffusion equation. The distinct nonlocality of the operator in superdiffusion and the low regularity of the forward solution render the mathematical and numerical analysis of related inverse problems very challenging and radically different from the traditional inverse problem. We shall study the identification of a diffusion coefficient from distributed observations. To show the stability of the reconstruction, the classical choice of test functions generally does not work for the superdiffusion model. The first task in this part is to propose novel test functions and to provide suitable estimates on the residual term so as to develop some useful weighted L^2 stability. Moreover, we shall develop numerical schemes for solving the inverse problem, based on the output least-square formulation with a Sobolev H^s penalty. Numerically, the computation is far more expensive, due to the nonlocal nature of the operator, which leads to dense stiffness matrices. Thus, the repeated forward evaluation can be hugely expensive, which calls for novel model order reduction techniques, e.g., reduced basis methods. Theoretically, we aim at deriving some a priori weighted L^2 error estimates for the discrete approximation under a mild regularity assumption on the exact diffusion coefficient. The obtained estimates should depend on the spatial mesh size, the noise level, and the regularization parameter. The following tools are needed in the analysis: proper test functions (for the stability estimate), Sobolev regularity estimate, and the finite element approximation for the forward problem.

15304420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304420.value: Anomalous diffusion, due to their wide range of applications in physics and biology, has attracts a lot of attention in recent years. Most mathematical models for anomalous diffusion involve “fractional” differential operators (or some other types of nonlocal operators), which may significantly change both diffusive dynamics and solution regularity. In the last two decades, the related direct problems have been extensively studied both mathematically and numerically. However, in-depth studies of numerical methods for solving related inverse problems remain fairly scarce. In this project, we aim to develop and analyze stable and efficient numerical methods for several exemplary inverse problems in anomalous diffusion with rigorous error analysis. This project will consist of three parts. First, we shall investigate the numerical method for solving the backward problem of the time-fractional subdiffusion equation. The aim in this part is to establish a systematical framework to derive a priori error estimates for the discretized problem, indicating the way to balance discretization error, regularization parameter and noise level. The analysis relies heavily on refined properties of (discrete) solution operators, and nonstandard error estimate for the direct problem in terms of problem data regularity. Second, we shall study the inverse source problem of subdiffusion with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. In most existing works of inverse subdiffusion problems, the analysis is based on the analytic property of Mittag-Leffler functions, which is inapplicable in this case. We shall present a rigorous stability and error analysis, whose proof is based on novel technical tools, e.g., perturbation argument, discrete L^p-maximum regularity and discrete fractional Gronwall’s inequality developed in our prior work. Third and finally, we shall study stability and numerical analysis for identifying diffusion coefficient in the space-nonlocal superdiffusion problem from distributed observations. The following tools are needed in the study: proper test functions (for the stability estimate), Sobolev regularity estimate, and the finite element approximation for the forward problem. 反常扩散现象因其在物理与生物学的应用，近年来得到了人们的广泛关注。大部分的反常扩散模型中含有分数阶微分算子（或者其他类型的非局部算子），这些算子的出现显著的改变的扩散的动力学过程以及方程解的正则性。在过去的三十年间，相关正问题无论是哎理论和数值方面z已经得到了很多研究。然而，反问题数值方法的深入研究还很缺乏。本项目的目标是建立并分析稳定有效的数值方法去求解一些典型的反常扩散模型的反问题。 首先我们计划研究时间分数阶亚扩散模型的倒向问题。我们将建立一套系统的架构去分析数值格式，指明如何平衡离散误差、正则化参数以及数据噪声。分析依赖于离散解算子的光滑性以及正问题的一些非常规的依赖于数据正则性的误差分析方法。其次，我们将研究具有时间相关扩散系数的亚扩散方程的反源问题。现有的证明技巧大多依赖于Mittag-Leffler函数的性质，将不适用于该情况。我们将利用扰动分析、离散极大Lp正则性，构造一个新的稳定性分析方法。 最后，我们将研究空间非局部超扩散模型的扩散系数反演问题。研究的关键是构造合适的试探函数去证明稳定性，分析在sobolev空间的正则性，以及研究正问题的有效数值方法。

15304420.label: Realisation of objectives
15304420.value: We have made significant progress and successfully achieved the objectives of this project. Objective 1: Backward Problem for Subdiffusion We developed numerical methods for solving the backward problem of the subdiffusion equation, and derived a rigorous error analysis for the fully discrete scheme. The analysis relied heavily on refined properties of discrete solution operators and nonstandard error estimates for the direct problem in terms of the regularity of the problem data. Furthermore, we extended the analysis to the more challenging case of time-dependent diffusion coefficients. In this case, the proof utilized a perturbation argument to handle the time dependence of the coefficients, combined with advanced error estimates for the direct problem. Objective 2: Inverse Source and Conductivity Problems We investigated the inverse source problem for subdiffusion with time-dependent diffusion coefficients, addressing challenges where existing works, relying on the analytic properties of Mittag-Leffler functions, were not applicable. To overcome these limitations, we developed a novel perturbation argument that enabled us to derive several conditional stability results. Additionally, we extended our study to the inverse conductivity problem, characterized by the high degree of nonlinearity in the forward map that links the unknown diffusion coefficient to the distributed observations. Using a novel test function, we established conditional stability bounds in the $L^2$ norm under a suitable positivity condition. On the numerical side, we proposed a numerical scheme and conducted a comprehensive error analysis by leveraging new analytical tools, including optimal error estimates for the direct problem, a discrete version of fractional maximal $L^p$ regularity, and a nonstandard energy argument. Objective 3: Space-Nonlocal Models We focused on space-nonlocal models, particularly the generalized bathtub model, a nonlocal transport equation describing network trip flows served by privately operated vehicles within a road network. First, we established the well-posedness of the model for both classical and weak solutions. Next, we addressed an inverse source problem with model parameters reflecting specific traffic scenarios. By employing a Volterra integral formulation, we established conditional Lipschitz stability of the inverse problem under suitable a priori regularity assumptions on the data. Based on our analysis, we developed an easy-to-implement numerical method for reconstructing flow rates and provided a rigorous error analysis of the method.

15304420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304420.value: This project focused on numerical analysis of inverse problems of time- or space-nonlocal models, with significant contributions in three main areas: 1. Backward Problem for Subdiffusion: We studied numerical methods for solving the backward problem of the subdiffusion equation. The primary goal of this work was to provide a rigorous error analysis for the discretized problem using a quasi-boundary type method. The analysis relied heavily on refined properties of discrete solution operators and nonstandard error estimates for the direct problem in terms of the regularity of the problem data. Additionally, we extended the analysis to the more challenging case where the diffusion coefficients are time-dependent. The proof in this case relied heavily on a perturbation argument to handle the time dependence of the coefficients, as well as on nonstandard error estimates for the direct problem. These findings were published in SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing and Inverse Problems ([4], [7]). 2. Inverse Source and Conductivity Problems: In the second part, we investigated the inverse source problem for subdiffusion with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. Unlike most existing studies rely on the analytic properties of Mittag-Leffler functions, we developed a novel perturbation argument to derive several useful conditional stability results. We also extended our analysis to the inverse conductivity problem, where the primary challenge arises from the high nonlinearity of the forward map, which links the unknown diffusion coefficient to the distributed observations. By employing a novel weighted energy estimate, we derived stability bounds under a suitable positivity condition. On the numerical side, we proposed a numerical scheme and conducted a complete error analysis using new analytical tools, including optimal error estimates for the direct problem, discrete maximal $L^p$ regularity, and a nonstandard energy argument. Results from this part were published in SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis and IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis ([2], [6]). 3. Space-Nonlocal Models: In the third part, we focused on space-nonlocal models, particularly the generalized bathtub model, which involves a nonlocal-in-space operator and arises in network traffic flow modeling. We addressed an inverse source problem, establishing conditional Lipschitz stability under suitable a priori regularity assumptions on the problem data. Building on this analysis, we developed an easy-to-implement numerical method for reconstructing flow rates and provided a rigorous error analysis. These findings were submitted to the SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics ([13]) and are currently under review.

15304420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304420.value: 1. In this project, we addressed the backward problem for the linear subdiffusion model, where the diffusion coefficient may be time-dependent. However, the backward nonlinear time-fractional diffusion model remains an ongoing research topic. By combining the proposed framework for linear problems with refined analytical techniques for nonlinear models, it is possible to develop an efficient solver and derive a rigorous error analysis. 2. It is feasible to study the recovery of the source term in the subdiffusion model using a posteriori measurements taken within a small time window. Unlike local diffusion models, the nonlocality in time inherent in subdiffusion models allows for the unique determination of the source term from such observations. However, achieving this requires more refined and detailed analysis. 3. We have investigated the generalized bathtub model, which involves a nonlocal-in-space operator and arises in network traffic flow modeling. In the future, we aim to study other inverse problems associated with the generalized bathtub model, such as calibrating both inflow rates and inflow distributions using more comprehensive measurement data. Moreover, we intend to study the more challenging problems to recover the kernel function of the nonlocal operators in the nonlocal traffic flow or superdiffusion models.

15304420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304420.value: Anomalous diffusion models, which involve “fractional” differential operators or other types of nonlocal operators, have garnered significant attention in recent years. Over the past two decades, the related direct problems have been extensively studied both mathematically and numerically. However, in-depth studies of numerical methods for solving the associated inverse problems remain relatively scarce. In this project, we developed and analyzed stable and efficient numerical methods for several exemplary inverse problems in nonlocal models, such as anomalous diffusion, complemented by rigorous error analysis. First, we investigated numerical methods for solving the backward problem of the time-fractional subdiffusion equation. To address this, we established a systematic framework for deriving a priori error estimates for the discretized problem. Second, we studied the inverse source problem for subdiffusion with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. Using a novel perturbation argument proposed in our prior work, we applied certain a priori estimates to analyze the problem. Furthermore, we developed and rigorously analyzed a fully discrete scheme for the inverse source problem. Third, we focused on the numerical treatment and analysis of inverse problems for nonlocal-in-space models. Specifically, we investigated the nonlocal transport equation, which models network trip flows served by privately operated vehicles within a road network.

15304720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304720.value: Blood vessel network formation in vitro demonstrates that endothelial cells randomly dispersing on a gel substrate (matrix) can spontaneously organize into connected capillary networks with phase transitions. This phenomenon has been called in vitro angiogenesis - a major factor of tumor growth. How endothelial cells self-organize geometrically into capillary networks and how individual cells cooperate to form the coherent patterns remain poorly understand biologically up to date. These coherent network patterns cannot be explained by the macroscopic chemotaxis models that lead to point-wise blowup or rounded aggregates, nor by the microscopic chemotaxis models that describe single cell behaviors. Surprisingly the damped hydrodynamic (hyperbolic-parabolic) chemotaxis model can numerically reproduce many key features of the remarkable networking patterns. Compared to the microscopic kinetic equations and macroscopic parabolic chemotaxis models for which an enormous number of results have been available, the hydrodynamic chemotaxis model remains poorly understood due to the complicated interaction of parabolic dissipation and hyperbolic anti-dissipation and only few preliminary results are obtained so far. The existing results assume the initial datum is a small perturbation of some constant background states and assert that the solution will asymptotically approach these constants, which are clearly unable to decipher the experiment patterns that are essentially of non-constant profiles. The primary goal of this proposal is to exploit the distinctive structure of the hydrodynamic chemotaxis model, find non-constant profile solutions relevant to the patterns observed in the experiment, and hence to provide some qualitative understanding of the mechanism underlying the experimental patterns. We show that depending the boundary conditions at far fields, the asymptotic profile of solutions to the hydrodynamic chemotaxis model may be of vacuum stationary solutions with phase transitions or the nonlinear diffusion waves determined by the porous medium equations. We further show that, as the damping force is sufficiently large, the damped hydrodynamic chemotaxis model indeed strongly converges to the well-known Keller-Segel chemotaxis models. To prove the above results, we develop various news ideas/approaches in this proposed research, including the derivation of an exponentially weighted Hardy type inequality in the half space, delicate weighted energy estimates with various inequalities, Darcy law to derive the time asymptotic profile of solutions, sophisticated coupling estimates techniques, and so on. 血管网络形成的实验验证了随机分布在培养基上的表皮细胞能够自发形成相互联通的毛细血管网络， 这种过程是肿瘤生长的主要机制。到目前位置， 对于表皮细胞之间如何合作自发形成这些毛细血管网络的机制的理解非常有限。这些联通的网络图既不能用产生逐点爆破的宏观趋化模型解释， 也不能用描述单个细胞行为的微观趋化模型来解释。反而带有阻尼的流体动力学（双曲-抛物）趋化模型能在数值上模拟产生出实验中观测到网络图的许多关键特征。宏观和微观趋化模型已经有了大量的数学结果，然而流体动力学趋化模型的数学结果相对就很少，仅仅有一些初步的结果。已知的数学研究都假设初始值是一个常数稳态解附近的小扰动，然后证明系统有整体解并且解渐进收敛到常数稳态解。 因为实验里面观测到的是非均匀（非常数）的网状图，所以这些结果都不能解释实验现象。 本研究项目的主要目的就是挖掘流体动力学趋化模型的特殊结构， 找出与实验现象相关联的非常数数学解，为血管网络形成提供一些定性的理解。依据所给定的边界条件， 我们证明流体动力学趋化模型的渐进解是一个带有相变的真空稳态解或者是渗流模型的非线性扩散波。并且我们证明当阻尼系数足够大的时候， 流体动力学趋化模型收敛到著名的 Keller-Segel趋化模型。为了证明上述结果，我们发展了一些新的数学工技术具， 包括半空间中指数权的 Hardy不等式，精细的带权能量估计，Darcy律， 以及耦合估计等等。

15304720.label: Realisation of objectives
15304720.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives listed above, as specified below. In the research output [1], we derive the large-time profile of solutions to the Cauchy problem of a hyperbolic-parabolic system modeling the vasculogenesis in three dimensional whole space. When the initial data are prescribed in the vicinity of a constant ground state, by constructing a time-frequency Lyapunov functional and employing the Fourier energy method and delicate spectral analysis, we show that solutions of the Cauchy problem tend time-asymptotically to linear diffusion waves around the constant ground state. This fully achieves the goals set in the Objective 3. In the research output [2], we prove that the hydrodynamic chemotaxis model admits stable nonlinear diffusion waves that connect two different end states at far fields which are referred to as the phase transition solutions. This fully achieves the Objective 1. In the research output [3], we rigorously derive the relaxation limit of a three-dimensional quasi-linear hyperbolic-parabolic (i.e. hydrodynamic) chemotaxis system modeling vasculogenesis when the initial data are prescribed around a constant ground state. When the relaxation time tends to zero (i.e. the damping is strong), we show that the strong-weak limit of the cell density and chemoattractant concentration satisfies a parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel type chemotaxis system in the sense of distribution. The Objective 2 is fully achieved in this work.

15304720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304720.value: In the project, we initiated new ideas to exploit the non-constant solution profiles/structures relevant to the main features of the observed experimental patterns, in particular the phase transition profiles. These new ideas will stimulate mathematicians in PDEs to pursue more interesting analytical results on the hydrodynamic chemotaxis model. Though hydrodynamic chemotaxis model considered in the proposal has some exclusive features, it also shares many similarities with the Euler or Euler-Poisson equations. Therefore the methods and results developed in the proposed research not only can help understand the mechanisms underlying the chemotactic network pattern formations observed in the experiment, but also shed lights on the analytical studies of open questions of the Euler or Euler-Poisson equations such as the stability of vacuum (stationary) solutions vanishing on the boundary. In this proposed research, we shall take the full advantage of the special structure of the hydrodynamic chemotaxis models to develop some novel ideas to establish the stability of vacuum stationary solutions which vanish on the boundary only (at far field). We anticipate that the research scholars in PDEs can solve (at least partially) or make some substantial progress towards some open questions of the Euler-Poisson equations inspired by the ideas and methods developed in this project
