15305020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305020.value: Organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites have become exciting candidates for next-generation solar cells, owing to their extraordinary performance and low-cost, scalable fabrication routes. Despite the encouraging progress, however, little is known about the intragrain defects in hybrid perovskites. This is primarily due to their vulnerable structure that can be easily modified by probes such as electron beams, making it extremely challenging to obtain pristine structural information. In addition, the superior performance of hybrid perovskites has led to a belief that any intragrain defects must be electronically benign with little detrimental effect. On the other hand, the experimental evidence to support this belief is still lacking. More critically, hybrid perovskites still face other challenges hindering their applications, such as hysteresis and instability, which could be defect-dependent as suggested by studies on conventional photovoltaic materials. A better understanding on the intragrain defects is thus needed to clarify their roles in hybrid perovskites, which holds the promise for further enhancing the solar-cell performance via defect engineering. The aim of this project is to address this immediate need, by unravelling the nature of the intragrain defects in hybrid perovskites, especially their influence on solar-cell properties, as well as developing defect-engineering approaches to inhibit the detrimental defects for optimized performance. The recently-developed ultralow-dose cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) grants us a unique tool to probe the intrinsic defect structure in the vulnerable hybrid perovskites without damage. Our expertise in perovskite oxides further allows us to borrow the established approach of defect engineering, such as tuning the tolerance factor through chemical doping to control the structure instability and the underpinned defect type and density. The “engineered” samples will then be examined using the ultralow-dose cryo-TEM to reveal the characteristic structure and density of defects, followed by property measurements to illustrate their effects on solar-cell performance. Our strategy combining defect engineering and ultralow-dose cryo-TEM characterization offers an unprecedented opportunity to clarify the roles of defects in hybrid perovskites. We plan to apply this strategy on archetypal MA1-xFAxPbI3 perovskites, focusing on their intrinsic defects such as twinning and hexagonal-phase intergrowth, the latter of which may represent the major degradation pathway in FAPbI3-based solar cells. The exclusive information achieved from this work will significantly advance the understanding of intrinsic defects and physical properties of hybrid perovskites. The demonstrated defect engineering approach may open up an entirely new avenue for further optimizing perovskite solar-cell performance to meet the requirement of real-life applications.

15305020.label: Realisation of objectives
15305020.value: The objectives have all been achieved as stated below: Firstly, we have synthesized a series of hybrid perovskite MA1-xFAxPbI3 with x varying from 0 (MAPbI3) to 1 (FAPbI3), and using ultralow-dose TEM to examine their characteristic intragrain defects, such as intrinsic twinning in MA-rich MA1-xFAxPbI3 (with x < 0.2) and stacking faults in FA-rich MA1-xFAxPbI3 (with x > 0.5). We revealed the defect morphology using TEM imaging and derived their structure based on selected-area electron diffraction (SAED). We also measured the density of defects which exhibit a clear trend as a function of x (or FA content), and can be well explained using the Goldschmidt’s tolerance factor, which confirms our defect engineering approach on hybrid perovskites (Objective 1). Furthermore, a correlation between the identified defect type/density and the solar cell properties (PCE, VOC, life time) has been established. It unambiguously demonstrates that both twinning and stacking faults degrade solar cell performance, while the stacking faults in FA-rich MA1-xFAxPbI3 are more detrimental than the twinning (Objective 2). The best performance is achieved in MA0.8FA0.2PbI3 (x = 0.2) sample which shows the least amount of intragrain defects. This result disproves the widely-accepted belief that intragrain defects in hybrid perovskites should be electronically benign and have only a minimal influence on solar-cell performance. It also points out the way to further improve the solar cell performance, by inhibiting intragrain defects in hybrid perovskites using defect engineering. Secondly, we have further combined the ultralow-dose TEM with in situ heating capability to unravel the anisotropic δ-to-α transition in epitaxial FAPbI3 thin films. We adopted polarized light microscopy (PLM) that offers enhanced contrast to distinguish isotropic α-FAPbI3 from anisotropic δ-FAPbI3. Facilitated by in situ heating, it allowed us to identify heterogeneous nucleation of α-FAPbI3 and the subsequent diffusional phase transition preferentially occurring along <0001>, which is underpinned by the smaller activation energy along the face-sharing direction of PbI6 octahedra. We further revealed the morphology and orientation relationship at the δ-to-α transition front using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM), evincing the surface energy dominated orientation rather than the interfacial energy. The presence of high-density planar defects is also discovered at the transition front, which can be considered as an intermediate state facilitating δ-to-α structure transformation (Objective 2). Moreover, using the ultrafast ultrasensitive camera (K3 from Gatan Inc.), we further pushed the ultralow-dose TEM technique to atomic scale and imaged the atomic structure of α-FAPbI3 with negligible beam effect. It can detect the nanoscale defects such as intergrowth of PbI2 in α-FAPbI3 lattice (Objective 3). Thirdly, based on our understanding on the δ-to-α transition above, we have developed an effective approach using ex situ XRD to detect the formation of inactive δ phase in FAPbI3, which is identified as its major degradation mechanism. To introduce degradation in FAPbI3, we put sample in the humid atmosphere (88%Rh) and also apply UV illumination (50 mW/cm2) to simulate the solar cell operation condition. Ex situ XRD on the degraded FAPbI3 clearly shows the signal of the δ-FAPbI3, which starts to develop after 1 hour degradation and appears to saturate after ~2 hours. It is accompanied with the decrease of active -FAPbI3 diffraction intensity, clearly indicating the -to-δ conversion process as the degradation process. Interestingly, the formed δ-FAPbI3 can be converted back to the active -phase through annealing at 150 ⁰C, as revealed by the decrease of δ-FAPbI3 signal and the increase of -FAPbI3 signal with extended annealing time. This established approach provides a reliable tool to identify the formation of δ-FAPbI3 and to track its development process. Combined with ex situ TEM and PL measurements, it which will shed light on the degradation mechanism in FAPbI3 (Objective 4). Finally, with the significant research interest on 2D hybrid perovskites recently, we have also fabricated such novel materials and revealed their degradation behavior under both light and electron irradiation (Objective 4). In particular, we systematically investigated the photostability of 2D perovskite (BA)2(MA)n−1PbnBr3n+1 with n = 1, 2, and 3 under UV illumination. Using multimodal characterization approaches including XRD, ultraviolet–visible (UV-vis) absorption, photoluminescence (PL) emission, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), and ultralow-dose TEM, we have identified similar photodegradation mechanism for all three types of materials, with higher photostability observed in higher n samples. Furthermore, we demonstrate FTIR as an effective technique to track the loss of organic molecules driven by light illumination on 2D perovskites. Quantitative FTIR peak modelling further enables us to distinguish the escape kinetics of BA and MA molecules, which reveals the faster escape rate of BA than MA. The organic molecules preferentially escape from sample edges and surface cracks, leading to the collapse of the BA layers with the reduced sample thickness and intrinsic PL emission. The final degradation product is the transparent PbBr2 with an amorphous structure, which propagates gradually from sample edges and surface cracks to the inside. Interestingly, this transformation process does not alter the 2D shape of the original flakes.

To identify the degradation pathways in hybrid perovskites, through a combination of in situ degradation, utilizing the in situ gas holder that can convey water vapor during TEM observation, and ex situ degradation that can exclude potential beam effects.

15305020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305020.value: We tuned the structure and density of intragrain planar defects in MA1-xFAxPbI3 using x and then characterize and correlate these defects with device performance. We showed that the charge carrier lifetime, open-circuit voltage deficit and current-voltage hysteresis depend critically on the density and structure of twin planes; {111}c (for x=0.5-1) and {112}t (for x=0-0.1). Furthermore, the best electronic properties and device performance, by far, are found when no planar defects are present (x=0.2). Intragrain defect control can thus provide an important additional route for improving solar cell performance. The result has been published on Nature Energy with PI Zhu as a co-first author and Collaborator Chen as the corresponding author. We combined multiscale microscopy with in situ heating to directly observe the anisotropic δ-to-α phase transition in FAPbI₃ films. We showed that α-FAPbI3 nucleates heterogeneously, followed by a diffusional transformation preferentially propagating along <0001>, which is underpinned by the lower activation energy along the face-sharing direction of PbI6 octahedra. 4D-STEM further unveils the morphology and orientation relationship at the δ-to-α transition front, indicating the incoherent δ/α interfaces with potentially lower interface energy. We have also identified high-density planar defects in newly formed α-FAPbI3 near the transition front, which appears to be an intermediate state promoting the δ-to-α transition. Besides filling the knowledge gap on the phase transition behavior in FAPbI3, our work also demonstrate a multiscale microscopy approach to interrogate phase transition mechanism in hybrid perovskites. The result has been recently accepted by ACS Nano [doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.5c00037] with PI Zhu as the corresponding author. We have systematically investigated the photostability in (BA)2(MA)n−1PbnBr3n+1 sample series via multimodal characterizations combining both microscopy and spectroscopy. Samples with all three compositions exhibit similar photodegradation mechanism, with higher photostability observed in higher n samples. By explicitly detecting the loss of BA and MA molecules driven by light illumination and quantitatively measuring their loss rates, we identified faster loss of BA molecules compared with MA, both occurring preferentially at the sample edges and surface cracks and leading to the collapse of the BA layers with the reduced sample thickness and intrinsic emission. Eventually all samples degrade into the transparent PbBr2 with an amorphous structure, which propagates gradually to the inside without altering the 2D shape of sample flakes. The result has been published on Materials Chemistry Frontiers with PI Zhu as the corresponding author.

15305020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305020.value: By demonstrating that intragrain planar defects can also play an important role, it provides further scope for optimization of this exciting photovoltaic technology through the control of intragrain planar defects. Moreover, our study on phase transition indicates that planar defects may originate during the structure transformation, which could be minimized by optimizing the synthesis condition. We are currently experimenting along this direction to further limit the intragrain defects for better photovoltaic performance. We have demonstrated a multiscale microscopy approach to interrogate phase transition and degradation mechanism in hybrid perovskites. In particular, we developed a quantitative approach to measure the loss of organic molecules in hybrid perovskites, which can be used to understand the performance degradation in perovskite solar cells and to be extended to emerging 2D perovskite materials.

15305020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305020.value: Perovskite solar cells show excellent properties, which encourages a view that intragrain defects are electronically benign with little impact on device performance. In this study, we systematically studied the impact of intragrain defects in hybrid perovskites. This was achieved through a combination of (1) defect engineering by changing the chemical composition to tune the tolerance factor, while otherwise keeping the device materials and configuration nominally the same, (2) ultralow-dose electron microscopy to characterize reliably the nature of these defects, and (3) correlation of the measured intragrain defect structures with the measured solar-cell performance. It enabled us to identify the detrimental role of intragrain planar defects, with the best performance found when essentially no such defects. Our findings thus indicate that the control of intragrain planar defects can provide an additional avenue for device optimization. Further studies revealed that the planar defects could originate from phase transition during material synthesis, which might be minimized by optimizing the synthesis condition. In addition to the above insight, the project also demonstrated an effective multiscale microscopy approach to interrogate phase transition and degradation mechanism in hybrid perovskites.

15305320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305320.value: Luminescent materials that convert certain kinds of energy into light emission have become an essential part of our daily lives for their widespread use in displays and lighting. Various types of energy, including electromagnetic radiation, electric field and mechanical action, have been utilized to generate light energies via photoluminescence (PL), electroluminescence (EL) and triboluminescence (TL) processes, respectively. Metallophosphors including iridium(III) and platinum(II) heavy metal complexes have been widely used in many areas such as EL for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, high-performance OLEDs are mainly achieved by incorporating the noble metal-based phosphors, which often suffer from the low abundance, high cost and potential risks in environmental pollution. Thus, the utilization of relatively abundant, low-cost and environmental-friendly phosphorescent manganese(II) coordination complexes possessing many unique properties, such as the high PL quantum efficiency, ease of triboluminescence and reversible emission response behavior to solvent, could be the solution to this problem. In contrast to the noble metal-based phosphors with the well-established structure-property relationships, the study of phosphorescent Mn(II) coordination compound is still in its infancy and much remains unknown for these materials. To date, there is also a lack of the deeper understanding of their structure-property relationships. In this project, we plan to develop a series of phosphorescent Mn(II) coordination complexes and polymers to establish the relationships between their structures and photophysical properties by investigating the intramolecular or intermolecular packing arrangements and interactions of Mn(II) complexes. With our strengths in synthetic, polymer and coordination chemistry, the photophysical and triboluminescent properties of these Mn(II) complexes can be fine-tuned through chemical modifications of the organic counterion and phosphine ligand with appropriate triplet energy level and charge transport characteristics for ensuring efficient energy transfer between the organic cation/phosphine ligand and Mn(II) ion, and this can result in improved luminescence efficiency, tunable lifetime, bipolar charge transport, controllable TL property, reversible emission response behavior to solvent and excellent solution processability. On this basis, applications such as organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), information recording and security protection will be further developed. The present work will also open a new research era for the design of TL materials. One important motivation in developing TL materials is the search for smart stress and crack sensors. It is anticipated that those highly efficient and durable Mn(II) complexes can be utilized for fabricating TL devices. Clearly, this project will establish a solid foundation in the development of low-cost multifunctional phosphorescent Mn(II) coordination compounds. 將某種能量轉換成光能的發光材料已廣泛用於照明和顯示器中，成為日常生活的重要組成部分。目前，可利用各種類型的能量，包括電磁輻射、電場和機械能，分別通過光致發光（PL）、電致發光（EL）和摩擦發光（TL）過程來產生光能。 重金屬磷光體（如銥(III)和鉑(II)金屬配合物）已廣泛用於許多領域，例如用於有機發光二極管（OLED）。然而，高性能OLED主要是通過摻雜貴金屬磷光材料來實現，貴金屬通常具有低豐度、高成本以及潛在環境污染等缺點。因此，可利用相對豐富高、低成本和環境友好的磷光錳(II)配合物實現這一目標。這類配合物具有許多獨特的性質，例如高的光致發光量子效率和對某些溶劑的可逆發光回應。與構效關係較為成熟的貴金屬磷光材料相反，磷光錳(II)配合物的研究仍處於起步階段，目前，對它們的構效關係仍然缺乏深入理解。在本專案中，我們擬發展一系列磷光錳(II)配合物和聚合物，通過研究分子內/分子間的排列方式和相互作用來建立分子結構與光物理性質之間的關係。憑藉我們在聚合物合成和配位元化學方面的優勢，將通過對有機抗衡離子和配體進行化學修飾，實現調控有機抗衡離子和配體的三重態能級與電荷傳輸性質，以確保有機陽離子/配體和錳(II)離子之間實現有效的能量傳遞，實現對這類錳(II)配合物的光物理性質調控，例如提高發光效率、可調控的發光壽命與雙極性電荷傳輸、可調節的摩擦發光特性、對溶劑的可逆發射回應以及優異的可溶液加工性。在此基礎上，進一步將其應用于有機發光二極管、信息記錄和安全保護以及應力/裂紋感測器。本項目擬開展的研究工作將為摩擦發光材料的設計與應用開闢新的研究時代。發展摩擦發光材料的一個重要動機是將其應用于智慧應力/裂縫感測器。預期這些高效發光且穩定的錳(II)配合物可用於製備與摩擦發光相關的新型光功能器件。因此，本項目將為發展低成本多功能磷光錳(II)配合物材料奠定堅實的基礎。

15305320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305320.value: Phosphorescent manganese(II) complexes with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) and low cost exhibit great potential in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), information security, and X-ray imaging. However, it is still a challenge to tune their emission colors. An effective strategy for engineering the phosphorescence colors of tetrahedral Mn(II) complexes through steric hindrance-driven bond angle distortion has been proposed. Modulating the steric hindrance between phosphine and benzofuran and varying the O─Mn─O bond angles allows these Mn(II) complexes to emit from 498 to 548 nm. Interestingly, these achiral single crystals of Mn(II) complexes exhibit signiﬁcant circularly polarized luminescence signals due to symmetry breaking. Furthermore, high-performance green OLEDs are achieved by using these Mn(II) complexes as dopants, providing a record-high external quantum eﬃciency of 15.7%. The work was published in Adv. Optical Mater. (2024, 12, 2302132). An aromatic moiety-free strategy has also been proposed for the effective excited state manipulation of the neutral luminescent manganese(II) halide. Interestingly, compared to the traditional monodentate ligand-based manganese(II) complexes, a dramatic enhancement of photoluminescent quantum yield of 0.413 is achieved by incorporating tri(pyrrolidin-1-yl)phosphine oxide (TPPO) as a new ligand without any aromatic moiety into the manganese(II) complex. The designed aromatic moiety-free neutral luminescent manganese(II) bromide (TPPOMnBr2) featuring an intense green emission (512 nm) and a short emission lifetime (0.564 ms) is employed to realize efficient X-ray imaging with a high spatial resolution value of 11.3 lp mm-1 and a low detection limit of 34.95 nGy s-1, making it a promising candidate for high performance X-ray detection. The work was published in J. Mater. Chem. C (2024, 12, 8296). Next, we recently proposed an isomer engineering strategy for designing three new photofunctional ionic manganese(II) bromide complexes by introducing methyl groups into the ortho (o)-, meta (m)-, or para (p)-position of the phenyl groups in ethyl triphenylphosphonium cation. The work will be published in J. Inorg. Organomet. Polym. Mater.. In order get ready for the architectures of the OLED structures to test for the as-prepared manganese(II) emitters in the next stage of development, we also attempted to study various device structures using known and other new materials (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.; Adv. Optical Mater.; Org. Electron.) and did many literature searches which ended up in a number of review articles (ACS Mater. Lett.; Sci. China Chem.) and chapters in monographs (Comprehensive Inorganic Chemistry III and RSC Polymer Chemistry series).

15305320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305320.value: Many important data emanated from this project which will make a good impact on the OLED, anti-counterfeiting and X-ray imaging technologies. We believe that the results will pave the way to the future design and development of low-cost luminescent manganese(II) complex materials. The field is expected to remain exciting and stimulating for the foreseeable future. The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other manganese(II) complexes and ionic manganese(II) coordination polymers exhibiting high photoluminescence quantum yield, circularly polarized luminescence and narrowband emission. (2) Development of other optoelectronic applications (e.g. high-quality white light-emitting diodes and X-ray imaging) based on new phosphorescent manganese(II) materials.

15305320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305320.value: Phosphorescent manganese(II) complexes are emerging as a new generation of luminescent materials. In this project, the molecular design, synthesis and photophysical properties of a series of phosphorescent neutral and ionic manganese(II) complexes were investigated in detail. We have successfully designed an efficient approach to tune the emission color of neutral tetrahedral manganese(II) complexes. Steric hindrance-driven bond angle distortion strategy can effectively tune the emission colors of tetrahedral neutral manganese(II) complexes from blue-green to yellow-green. Our work provides a design map for constructing multi-color luminescent manganese(II) complexes, shedding light on the discovery of the relationship between steric hindrance and energy splitting, which facilitates the fast development of manganese(II) complexes for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). We also explored the influences of various length of alkyl groups attached on the phosphine atoms and how the functional groups on the phenyl ring may pose impact on their luminescent properties by changing the position of a methyl group on different positions (i.e. ortho-, meta-, para-) on the phenyl ring. The applications of these complexes were evaluated as emitters in high-efficiency OLEDs (with record-breaking external quantum efficiency up to 15.7%) and X-ray scintillators with high spatial resolution and low detection limit for efficient X-ray imaging.

15305420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305420.value: Derivative information is not available in problems arising from industrial and engineering applications. A typical example is the so-called black-box optimization, where the objective function is evaluated by a computer simulations or physical processes without explicit formulations. This happens, for example, in integrated circuit design, aircraft design, and hyperparameter tuning in artificial intelligence. In such scenarios, problems need to be solved by algorithms that do not need derivative information, also known as derivative-free optimization algorithms. Currently, a major challenge for the derivative-free optimization community is large-scale problems. It is commonly believed that derivative-free optimization algorithms are not able to solve problems with more than several hundreds of variables. However, recent applications from machine learning challenges us with problems of much larger scale. Although subspace-based algorithms l can deal with problems with up to thousands of variables, even larger problems have always been insurmountable in general. Based on our works on derivative-free optimization, we will provide systematic methodologies for tackling large-scale optimization problems without using derivatives. Very often, the development of derivative-free optimization algorithms follows a paradigm of imitating the mature techniques in derivative-based optimization. However, we will take a completely different approach: our techniques are novel even in the case where derivatives are available. They do not originate from the optimization community but from numerical methods for PDEs, especially Domain Decomposition. This include particularly Restricted Additive Schwarz and coarse space correction techniques. Being highly successful in Domain Decomposition, they have not been fully explored in nonlinear optimization, let alone in a derivative-free context. With these techniques, our objective is to develop parallel derivative-free optimization algorithms that are well adapted to modern High Performance Computing architecture, enjoying good scalability as Domain Decomposition methods. We will also investigate randomized versions of these algorithms as well as the fault-tolerance behavior of such algorithms in parallel computation. For these algorithms, we will establish global convergence and non-asymptotic complexity bounds, which will provide us with insights that guiding us to the optimal implementations of these algorithms. 導數信息在傳統優化算法的設計和分析中佔據至關重要的地位。但是，在工業和工程應用中，諸多優化問題的導數信息並不能有效地獲取。一個典型的例子是所謂 “黑箱優化”。此類問題中目標函數往往由複雜模擬給出而沒有顯式表達，它們廣泛出現在集成電路設計、飛行器設計、人工智能超參數調節等應用中。这类问题要求我們設計無需導數信息的優化算法，即無導數方法。 目前，高維問題是無導數方法研究中面臨的一個重大挑戰。一般認為，無導數方法無法处理大規模問題，幾百維的問題已属困難。然而，最近機器學習中出現的應用問題迫切要求我們求解更高規模的問題。本項目將為大規模無導數優化提供系統的方法。在傳統研究中，無導數優化方法框架往往來源於已有的基於導數的方法。本項目將採取截然不同的研究範式：我們的研究並不基於已有的優化方法，而是藉鑑數值偏微分方程中處理大規模問題的成熟思路，主要是區域分解方法，特別是其中的限制加性施瓦茲 (Restricted Additive Schwarz) 和粗網格矯正技術。作為區域分解方法賴以成功的關鍵，限制加性施瓦茲和粗網格矯正並未在優化算法的設計中被充分挖掘。我們將把此類技術發展成適合一般的非線性優化的空間分解和粗空間矯正技術，並應用到無導數優化算法的設計中，構建求解大規模問題的並行無導數方法。正如區域分解方法一樣，這些方法將適應現代高性能計算機體系結構，且具有良好的可擴展性。除此之外，我們還將探索此類方法的隨機化版本，以及它們在並行計算環境下的容錯性 (fault tolerance)。我們將建立這些方法的全局收斂性和收斂率估計，此種分析將為這些方法的最優實現提供指導和理論依據。

15305420.label: Realisation of objectives
15305420.value: 1. Develop a Derivative-Free Parallel Schwarz (DFPS) space decomposition framework. We have developed a unified framework under the name “optimization by space transformation”. At each iteration of the framework, the gradient of the objective function is mapped by a forward transformation to an auxiliary (possibly lifted) space, in which a model is established based on the transformed gradient and a step is obtained by minimizing this model. A backward transformation then maps the step back to the original space, where the iterate is updated accordingly. The space transformation framework can be directly specialized to a parallel space decomposition framework for nonlinear optimization, which can be regarded as an extension of the parallel Schwarz domain decomposition method for PDEs and linear systems; here, the transformation is defined by an ensemble of the decomposition operators. Meanwhile, the space transformation framework can be specialized to analyze trust-region methods when the gradient is inaccurate (e.g., obtained from sampling or surrogate models), the key idea being to regard the inaccuracy as a transformation rather than an error. 2. Incorporate coarse spaces into the Derivative-Free Parallel Schwarz space decomposition framework. Our space transformation framework can incorporate coarse space easily, as the coarse space can be regarded as a subspace in addition to the subspaces obtained by decomposition, and it can covered by properly designing the forward and backward transformations, and hence covered by our global convergence and convergence rate results. 3. Analyze the fault tolerance behavior and randomization of the Derivative-Free Parallel Schwarz space decomposition framework. We prove that our framework still converges if the subspaces can still cover a sufficient proportion of the full space with a certain probability determined by the expanding and shrinking parameters of the trust-region radius. In addition, the convergence rate is essentially the same as the deterministic case.

With properly chosen transformations, it covers optimization by space decomposition and optimization based on inaccurate gradients. The results are summarized in the 116-page paper "Optimization by Space Transformation and Decomposition". 2. A software package named PDFO. This package provides five solvers for solving general nonlinear optimization problems without using derivatives. It is available at https://www.pdfo.net It has been downloaded for more than 300,000 times. It is included in the industrial software GEMSEO (https://gemseo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/, co-developed by Airbus and other companies) as an optimization engine. 3. A software package named COBYQA. It is available at https://www.cobyqa.com It is included in SciPy 1.4.0 as a highlight of the release. See https://scipy.github.io/devdocs/release/1.14.0-notes.html#highlights-of-this-release

15305420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305420.value: An important output of this project is the software packages PDFO and COBYQA. They have taken huge efforts to develop, and their impacts in the industry are significant. Many ways exist to improve them. For example, the current version of PDFO contains a considerable amount of legacy Fortran 77 code. Such old-style code poses an essential obstacle to the usability, maintainability, and extensibility of our package. We have continuously received demands from the community for a modernized implementation of the legacy code. To address the problem we are currently reimplementing the Fortran 77 code in modern languages including Fortran 2008, Python, and MATLAB, which again demands a large amount of computing resources and developing time. Nevertheless, given the feedback received from the industrial users of our software, we believe that all the efforts are worthwhile, because our work will make real impacts to industry and society.

15305420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305420.value: Most optimization algorithms utilize the gradients (or more generally, first-order information) of the objective function. However, such information is not available or costly to obtain in many industrial and engineering optimization problems. Derivative-Free Optimization (DFO) algorithms are designed to solve such problems based on only function evaluations. This project provides systematic methodologies for tackling large-scale optimization problems without using derivatives. Our techniques do not originate from the optimization community but from numerical methods for PDEs, especially Domain Decomposition. This includes particularly Restricted Additive Schwarz and coarse space correction techniques. We establish the convergence theory of the framework by studying a unified framework for optimization by space transformation, which covers optimization by space decomposition and optimization based on inaccurate gradients. Even though our study has led to a rich and intriguing theory, we do not want to confine our work to theoretical analysis. There is a huge and often overlooked gap between theoretical development of algorithms and practical implementations of them. To bridge this gap, we have endeavored to develop DFO solvers based on our theory. This has led to two packages, namely PDFO (https://www.pdfo.net) and COBYQA (https://www.cobyqa.com). Our packages have been applied by industrial players including Airbus, and COBYQA is included in SciPy 1.14.0 as a highlight of the release.

15305720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305720.value: Classification is a big branch of machine learning and contemporary data science. Many applications of data science in the industry are designed based on efficient and accurate training of classification predicted functions. However, a lot of classification training algorithms are not able to efficiently process unbalanced data, large-sized data, and / or semi-supervised data. Although AUC (Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve) has long been used in statistics as a criterion to evaluate classification algorithms for unbalanced data or unbalanced distribution, there is no efficient algorithm that trains nonlinear classifiers for AUC maximization. We propose to use recently developed pairwise reproducing kernels designed based on pointwise kernels for classification learning with AUC maximization. Computationally, the obtained scheme has the same complexity as pointwise learning algorithms. Theoretically, we propose to analyze the convergence of the kernel-based AUC maximization scheme based on our existing research on pairwise learning. We propose to design and analyze kernel-based online AUC maximization schemes, distributed AUC maximization schemes, and kernel-based AUC maximization with semi-supervised data. The proposed research program will significantly advance the research and application of AUC maximization for classification. 分類是機器學習和當代數據科學的一大分支。數據科學在工業中的許多應用都是基於對分類預測函數的有效且準確的訓練而設計的。但是，許多分類訓練算法不能有效地處理不平衡數據，大數據和/或半監督數據。儘管AUC（接收器工作特性曲線下的面積）長期以來一直在統計中用作評估不平衡數據或不平衡分佈的分類算法的標準，但仍沒有有效的算法來訓練用於AUC最大化的非線性分類器。我們計劃使用新近發展的基於單點核設計的成對再生核，於AUC最大化分類學習。在計算方面，得到的算法具有與逐點學習算法相同的複雜度。在理論方面，我們計劃基於我們現有的成對學習的研究來分析基於再生核的AUC最大化算法的收斂性。我們計劃設計和分析基於再生核的在線AUC最大化算法，分佈式AUC最大化算法以及使用半監督數據的基於再生核的AUC最大化算法。我們計劃的研究將大大促進AUC最大化用於分類的研究和應用。

15500020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500020.value: The increased pollution arising from production activities highlights the need to balance the environment with economic development. Indeed, responsible production is one of the sustainable development goals (Goal 12) advocated by the United Nations. It is a viable way for manufacturers to alleviate the environmental damages caused by their pollution and resources consumption. These problems will become more serious when they internationalize their production and market activities across countries. In achieving this Goal 12, the objective for manufacturers is to “do more and better with less”. The need for responsible production is salient among Chinese manufacturers considering the environmental degradation caused by industrial activities in the country. Yet, many Chinese manufacturers are hesitant on adopting responsible production to improve their operations. One reason is that not much is known about the scope and characteristics of adopting responsible production among Chinese manufacturers as well as their disclosure, hindering its diffusion. Another reason is that they are uninformed regarding how and when responsible production shall be adopted to gain financial benefits while preserving the environment. Particularly, there are different operating environment conditions (i.e., munificence, complexity, and uncertainty) influencing their operations and performance outcomes. They find no clue whether these conditions are beneficial or adversarial for them to adopt responsible production. This study will respond to their doubt on the financial value of responsible production by employing a multi-method approach involving topic modeling with machine learning, event study, simulation, and company interviews to address the above issues. In doing so, we will analyze publicly available data of manufacturers listed in China’s stock markets with a focus on their disclosed responsible production practices and financial performance outcomes under these different operating environment conditions. The results will show 1) the characteristics of responsible production disclosure among Chinese manufacturers, 2) the financial value of adopting responsible production, 3) how the responsible production-performance relationship is affected by these operating environment conditions as well as the relationship evolution in simulated environment, and 4) managerial and policy insights to improve and diffuse responsible production in the Chinese manufacturing industry. 生產活動導致了日益增加的污染，這一現象凸顯了平衡環境和經濟發展的必要性。實際上，責任生產是聯合國提倡的可持續發展目標之一（目標12）。這是製造商減輕其污染和資源消費對環境造成損害的一種可行方法。當製造商跨國家地使生產和市場活動國際化時, 這些問題將變得愈發嚴重。為了實現負責任消費和生產這一目標，製造商的目標是用較少的資源輸出更多且品質更佳的產品。考慮到工業活動在中國造成的環境惡化，對中國製造商責任生產的要求是尤為突出的。然而，許多中國製造商對於採用責任生產方式來改善其經營狀況是猶豫不決的。一個原因是中國製造商不瞭解採用責任生產的範圍和特徵以及披露方式，從而阻礙了責任生產的傳播。另一個原因是他們不知悉如何採用和何時採用責任生產的方式在保護環境同時，也可以獲得經濟利益。特別是在不同的運營環境條件下 (如敏捷性，複雜性和不確定性)，這些因素會影響製造商的運營和績效結果。他們不知道這些條件對他們採取責任的生產方式是有利還是不利的。本研究將通過採用涉及機器學習進行主題建模，事件研究法，模擬模擬以及企業訪談的多方法融合方式來解決他們對責任生產帶來財務價值的疑惑，並解決上述問題。在此過程中，我們將分析中國股票市場上市公司的公開資料，重點觀察這些企業在不同的運營環境條件下其披露的責任生產措施和財務績效。結果將顯示 1）中國製造商責任生產披露的特徵；2）採用責任生產的財務價值；3）不同的運營環境是如何影響責任生產和金融績效之間的關係以及在模擬環境下的關係演化；4）對改善和傳播責任生產在中國製造業的重要性提出相應的管理性和政策性的啟示。

15500020.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500020.value: First, this study significantly contributes to the field by examining the research evolution of responsible production for sustainability. Using the concept analysis approach, we first summarize four underlying attributes: the change to sustainability, preventive initiatives, process management, and company-specific context. We also identify that contextual factors and firm characteristics are antecedents of responsible production, which consequently affects customer attitude, employee behavior, and firm performance. A bibliometric review of 518 most relevant articles reveals a noteworthy research boom in responsible production for sustainability, particularly in developing countries, with China emerging as one of the most prominent contributors. Secondly, this study ventures into the realm of market responses to the adoption of responsible production practices, shedding light on the boundary conditions of firm size and financial slack that influence the performance link. Drawing from a dataset of 392 manufacturers that embraced responsible production practices between 2016 and 2023, this study employs a short-term event study approach to reveal the significant positive market value of such adoption. Through cross-sectional regression analysis, we uncover that firm size and financial slack can bolster the market value of adopting responsible production practices, particularly in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, offering a ray of hope in these challenging times. Lastly, we establish a robust positive correlation between resource responsibility and financial performance, leveraging propensity score matching and difference-in-differences analysis on a substantial 3,022 firm-year observations. Our findings also unveil that digital transformation and political connections amplify the positive impact of resource responsibility on financial performance, further strengthening the arguments of our research.

15500020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500020.value: To promote research development on responsible production for sustainability, the link of responsible production with financial performance can be further elaborated in different contexts of manufacturing and service operations.

15500020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500020.value: This study answers the following questions: 1) How to evaluate responsible production practices; 2) Does responsible production pay? 3) What contingencies influence the relationship between responsible production and financial performance? This project undertakes a comprehensive examination of the attributes, antecedents, and consequences of responsible production. It reveals that responsible production can indeed benefit the financial performance of manufacturing enterprises. However, its performance value is not a straightforward matter, but rather a complex interplay of factors such as firm size, financial slack, digital transformation, and political connections, presenting a stimulating challenge for further exploration.

15500320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500320.value: Although recent studies have examined the negative consequences of cybersecurity risk on shareholder wealth and firm policies, little is known about the source of shareholder wealth loss and its effect on a firm’s long-term growth. In this project, we focus on cyberattacks in which firms’ intellectual property (e.g., trade secrets, research output, and proprietary know-how) is stolen via hacking or malware-electronic entry by an outside party (hereafter, “cyber theft of IP”) to investigate how cyber risk affects firms’ innovation activities. More specifically, we investigate whether cyber theft of IP affects the scale and novelty of firms’ innovation output and their strategy toward acquiring innovation externally versus producing it in-house. Cyber risk is different from other conventional types of operation risks (e.g., piracy and counterfeiting of IP-protected products). Due to the emerging and evolving nature of the risk, firms and their stakeholders tend to have limited understanding about the nature of a cyberattack and the likelihood of its occurrence. It is almost impossible to entirely prevent cyber theft of IP, even if firms allocate unlimited resources to risk-mitigating actions (Kamiya et al., (2019)). Since the real culprits of cyberattacks (e.g., state actors, hackers) are often unknown, it is also difficult for affected firms to restitute damages caused. In contrast, in the case of patent infringement by a firm’s competitors, affected firms can take legal actions to ensure an effective remedy or even compensation for damages caused. Cyber theft of IP could adversely affect firms’ innovation output for three main reasons. First, it would increase the risk of unintended disclosure of a firm’s confidential information to external parties. Second, the increased uncertainty in a firm’s operation and its future prospects would reduce managers’ risk-taking incentives and discourage a culture of experimentation. Third, attacked firms must allocate more resources to remedy the event, which in turn reduces cash flow available for innovation activities. Thus, we expect that firms experiencing cyber theft of IP to reduce their innovation activity, particularly in-house innovation output and to focus on innovation via M&As or strategic alliances. The results of this project will provide new insights about how cyber risk affects economic growth by deterring corporate innovation and the extent to which it imposes indirect costs on firms. As cybersecurity is becoming an increasingly important concern for firms’ daily operations, the findings will also provide implications for industry practitioners and regulators in Hong Kong and around the world. 尽管最近的研究已经研究了网络安全风险对股东财富和公司政策的负面影响，但对于股东财富损失的根源及其对公司长期增长的影响知之甚少。 在此项目中，我们重点研究网络攻击，其中公司的知识产权通过外部黑客或恶意软件电子入侵被盗，以调查网络风险如何影响公司的创新活动。 更具体地说，我们调查知识产权的网络盗窃是否会影响企业创新产出的规模和新颖性，以及它们从外部获取创新与内部产生创新的战略。

15500320.value: The primary objectives of our project have been successfully achieved, and we have made significant strides in advancing our research on insider trading and cybersecurity incidents. Our paper has been presented at several prestigious international conferences and global institutions, garnering valuable feedback from experts in the field. This exposure has not only enhanced the visibility of our research but also facilitated critical discussions that have enriched our findings. Following these presentations, we received constructive comments and suggestions from peers and reviewers, which have been instrumental in refining our paper. Based on this feedback, we have undertaken substantial revisions to address the critiques and enhance the robustness of our analysis. These revisions have been critical in preparing our manuscript for submission to a top-tier finance journal, demonstrating our commitment to achieving high standards of academic excellence. Our revised paper will make a significant contribution to the literature on insider trading and cybersecurity and provide valuable insights for both academics and practitioners in the field.

15500320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500320.value: Our study provides significant insights into the trading profitability of both target and peer insiders in the context of cybersecurity incidents. We find that target insiders earn higher abnormal returns by trading their firms’ shares before the disclosure of a cyberattack compared to after the disclosure, but only if their firms do not face higher litigation risk. Peer insiders who trade their own firms' shares before the target firm’s cyberattack disclosure earn 4.5% higher market-adjusted abnormal buy-and-hold returns over 180 days than those who trade after the disclosure. This profitability is robust when measured using industry-adjusted abnormal buy-and-hold returns and Carhart’s (1997) four-factor model. High litigation risk in target firms discourages insiders from leaking private information. Peer insiders with nonworkplace or nonboard ties earn greater trading profits when target firms have lower litigation risk. This is particularly evident in firms with low institutional blockholder ownership, those operating in low-litigation industries, and those in regions with lower liberal court scores. The SEC's guidance issued on October 13, 2011, regarding cybersecurity risk disclosure, aimed to curb opportunistic trading by increasing regulatory scrutiny. Post-guidance, peer insiders' trading profits significantly decreased compared to the pre-guidance period, especially for those with nonworkplace or nonboard ties to target insiders. However, peer insiders with nonboard ties continue to earn abnormal profits even during the post-guidance period. Peer insiders leverage their information advantage before the market becomes aware of target firms’ cyberattacks, highlighting a gap in market fairness and the efficacy of current regulatory measures. The research confirms that insider trading related to cybersecurity incidents provides significant abnormal returns, exploiting the lack of material classification and regulatory scrutiny of such events. Despite efforts to curb such behavior through litigation risk and regulatory oversight, insiders with specific social ties continue to profit from early information about cyberattacks. Our findings underscore the need for stronger regulatory frameworks and more rigorous enforcement to address these gaps. The study suggests potential policy adjustments, such as broadening the definition of material information to explicitly include cybersecurity incidents and enhancing the monitoring of insider trading activities connected to such events. This research not only contributes to the literature on insider trading and cybersecurity but also provides practical insights for policymakers aiming to improve market integrity and corporate governance.

15500320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500320.value: As cybersecurity risks grow, many firms still do not recognize these threats as material events. Former SEC Commissioner Kara M. Stein noted that companies often view cyber threats as technical issues rather than significant business risks (Stein, 2018). This leads to weak cybersecurity measures and inadequate disclosure about data loss risks. Although the SEC issued detailed guidelines in 2018 regarding disclosure controls and insider trading prohibitions related to cybersecurity, many firms still do not treat cyberattacks as involving “material, nonpublic” information. Our study addresses this gap by examining the risks associated with cyber-related information and its impact on insider trading. We explore how insider trading is influenced during cybersecurity incidents at both target firms and their industry peers, providing new insights into the dynamics of information dissemination in cybersecurity, a relatively underexplored area. For further development, we propose analyzing the post-SEC guideline periods to assess changes in corporate behavior and regulatory compliance. Additionally, exploring international regulatory frameworks and their effectiveness in managing cybersecurity risks could offer valuable comparative insights. This will deepen our understanding of how cyber-related information affects market behavior and inform more robust regulatory policies and corporate governance practices.

15500320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500320.value: Our research explores how cyberattacks impact insider trading within industries. Unlike traditional events like earnings reports or mergers, cyberattacks are not always labeled as critical, confidential information. We investigate if insiders at rival firms benefit from early knowledge of these attacks. Our findings reveal that insiders often profit by trading their own company's stock before the public announcement of an attack on a competitor, particularly when they have social connections with insiders at the attacked firm. The severity of the attack, the rival's cyber risk exposure, and their location affect these profits. These practices declined after the SEC's 2011 cybersecurity guidelines. Our study makes significant contributions. First, it expands the understanding of insider trading by focusing on cyberattacks, a less regulated area. We highlight how these attacks lead to information sharing between competitors, resulting in abnormal profits. Second, we show the role of social networks in information transmission, especially through personal and less regulated connections, enhancing trading performance. Lastly, we address the broader economic impact of cybersecurity risks. Our research demonstrates how cyberattacks provide insights into both firm-specific and industry-wide risks, influencing insider trading activities and highlighting the negative effects of cyber threats.

15500820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500820.value: Critical components are crucial to the survival of an original equipment manufacturer (OEM). To ensure the stable supply of critical components and mitigate the potential for supply disruption, some OEMs invest in R&D activities to develop their own abilities to make such critical components. When a critical component supplier is the sole supplier of that component, it faces a critical decision: should it sell its components exclusively to certain manufacturer(s), or inclusively to all manufacturers? Note that exclusive selling may be forced by government intervention (as when Huawei was placed on a US trade blacklist). When a manufacturer faces the potential for (mandatory) exclusion of component suppliers, how does its component-making ability affect its optimal strategic response? In what ways does government intervention affect the performance of supply chain parties? Our proposed research project will investigate these questions. Specifically, we aim to examine how the OEM’s component-making ability affects its supplier’s selling strategy and its own production incentives. First, we will consider a supply chain consisting of a critical component supplier, an independent OEM with the component-making ability, and a dependent OEM without that ability. The supplier can sell either inclusively to both OEMs or exclusively to one OEM. We will determine the optimal wholesale prices, order quantities, and production decisions under these two selling strategies, and then compare the associated equilibrium outcomes. This comparison will help us to answer the following questions: When should a supplier sell exclusively? When should an OEM develop the capability to make crucial components in-house, and when should it outsource those components from a supplier? How does the OEM’s ability to make its own components affect the supplier’s selling strategy choice, market competition, and its own profitability? Next, we will extend our analysis to a situation where the mandatory exclusion of manufacturers is enforced by government intervention. We will re-examine the supplier’s optimal pricing decisions and the OEMs’ corresponding ordering/production decisions. We will then compare the equilibrium outcomes under this situation with those when mandatory supplier exclusion is absent. The results will help us identify conditions under which mandatory exclusion is effective for expelling the concerned manufacturer from the market. Throughout this analysis, we can answer the following question: To what extent can the OEM’s component-making ability mitigate its dependency on the supplier? Finally, we plan to investigate when and to what extent an OEM should invest in developing its own critical-component-making ability. 关键组件对于原始设备制造商的生存至关重要。为了确保关键组件的稳定供应并减少潜在的供应中断，一些原始设备制造商在研发活动上进行了投资，以开发自己制造此类组件的能力。当关键组件供应商是该组件的唯一供应商时，它将面临一个关键决策：它是将组件卖给某些制造商，还是卖给所有制造商？有时候，独家销售可能来源于政府干预。当制造商面临（强制性）不能从零部件供应商购买的风险时，其零部件制造能力如何影响其的战略响应？政府的强制干预如何影响供应链各方的绩效？我们的项目将研究这些问题。 具体来说，我们旨在研究原始设备制造商的组件制造能力如何影响其供应商的销售策略和自身的生产决策。首先，我们将考虑一个由关键组件供应商，具有组件制造能力的独立型原始设备制造商和没有该组件制造能力的依赖型原始设备制造商组成的供应链。供应商既可以分销给两个原始设备制造商，也可以只分销给其中一个原始设备制造商。我们将求解这两种销售策略下的最佳批发价格，采购决策及生产决策，然后比较相关的均衡结果。这种比较将帮助我们回答以下问题：供应商什么时候应该独家销售？ 原始设备制造商何时应开发自身的关键组件制造能力，何时应从供应商外包这些组件？原始设备制造商自己制造组件的能力如何影响供应商的销售策略选择，市场竞争以及自身的盈利能力？ 接下来，我们将把分析扩展到政府干预迫使制造商被强制排除在外的情况。我们将重新检查供应商的最佳定价决策和原始设备制造商的相应采购/生产决策。然后，我们将对这种情况下和没有强制性排除供应商情况下的均衡结果进行比较。结果将帮助我们确定何时强制性排除能有效地将有关制造商从市场上驱逐出的条件。然后，我们可以回答以下问题：原始设备制造商的组件制造能力可以在多大程度上减轻其对供应商的依赖？我们还计划讨论原始设备制造商应该在何时以及在多大程度上投资发展自己的关键组件制造能力。

15500820.label: Realisation of objectives
15500820.value: All the objectives have been achieved. In this study, we aim to examine how the manufacturer’s component making capability affects the critical component supplier’s pricing and distribution strategy (whether to sell exclusively) and the manufacturer’s own ordering and capability investment decisions. We also explore the effects of mandatory exclusion imposed by government regulations. Specifically, we have considered a technology-product supply chain with two representative manufacturers: an independent manufacturer that has the capability to produce components internally and a dependent manufacturer that does not have the ability to produce internally and has to rely on an external supplier for the production of the component. Without government regulation, the supplier decides whether to sell its product exclusively to one manufacturer or to both manufacturers. If the supplier engages in an exclusive agreement with a manufacturer, then the contract involves a profit sharing rate, a fixed exclusion/licensing fee, and a per-unit wholesale price (royalty fee) charged to the manufacturer. If instead the supplier opens its component production to both manufacturers, then the independent manufacturer determines the quantity to be sourced from the supplier and the quantity to produce in-house, contingent upon the contractual terms offered by the supplier and the manufacturer's own internal sourcing capability. The manufacturers engage in Cournot competition by choosing their respective selling quantities, while the independent manufacturer determines its capability level. We first consider a scenario where the supplier endogenously decides whether to sell exclusively. In this scenario, the supplier is better off selling only to the dependent manufacturer when the profit sharing rate is high and the quality of the independent manufacturer's in-house component production is low. Conversely, it is optimal for the supplier to engage in exclusive selling with the independent manufacturer when this manufacturer produces a high-quality component or when the profit sharing rate is low. From the perspective of consumer welfare, either a dual selling strategy or exclusive selling to the dependent manufacturer can yield the highest surplus, as these distribution strategies intensify competition in the downstream market. Taking into account the supplier's decision regarding its distribution strategy and the cost of investment in quality of in-house component production, the independent manufacturer determines its optimal investment in quality. When the profit sharing rate is low, the supplier is better off selling exclusively to the independent manufacturer. As such, the independent manufacturer chooses a relatively lower level of investment in quality. In contrast, when the profit sharing rate is high, the supplier may be better off engaging in dual selling or in exclusive partnership with the dependent manufacturer. Anticipating this, if the investment cost is low, the independent manufacturer chooses a high level of investment in quality to strategically deter the supplier from establishing exclusive selling with the dependent manufacturer. If the investment cost is high, then the independent manufacturer chooses a relatively low quality level. Our findings highlight the interaction between the supplier's distribution strategy and the independent manufacturer's investment in internal sourcing capability. We further examine a setting with mandatory exclusion. Our analysis reveals that blocking trade between the supplier and the independent manufacturer can lead to either under- or over-investment in quality, relative to the level of investment that emerges under voluntary exclusion. Specifically, when the profit sharing rate is high and the investment cost is moderate, the independent manufacturer has a stronger incentive to invest in quality under voluntary exclusion as a deterrent against the supplier's potential decision to pursue an exclusive selling agreement with the dependent manufacturer. In all other scenarios, mandatory exclusion leads to over-investment in quality due to the heightened competitive pressure faced by the independent manufacturer. As expected, we also find that mandatory exclusion hurts the supplier, as it diminishes its ability to dictate the terms of its distribution strategy and it restricts the supplier from selling to both manufacturers. However, mandatory exclusion may benefit or hurt either manufacturer, depending on the contract terms and on the investment cost. In particular, the dependent manufacturer tends to benefit from mandatory exclusion for a broad set of parameter values. Indeed, mandatory exclusion allows the dependent manufacturer to operate under an exclusive partnership with the supplier without incurring the costs associated with exclusion and it leads to relatively weaker downstream competition. On the other hand, the independent manufacturer benefits from mandatory exclusion under a much more restricted set of parameter values that correspond to instances in which the supplier would charge a relatively high wholesale price under mandatory exclusion. We also find that consumers can benefit from or be hurt by mandatory exclusion. In particular, consumers may benefit from mandatory exclusion as it can induce the independent manufacturer to invest more aggressively in quality, leading to intensified market competition and therefore lower market prices. Overall, our findings on mandatory exclusion provide a cautionary note on the potential implications of such government-imposed regulations. We further consider a situation where the government imposes the tariff to impact the trade, ordering and pricing decisions of multinational firms (MNFs) that compete in domestic and overseas markets. We build a game-theoretical model to examine how tariff policies affect the competition of MNFs in a global trading environment. Specifically, the MNFs sell substitutable products and compete in two countries where the governments may adopt a welfare-maximizing tariff or a trade-surplus-maximizing tariff. We then derive the equilibrium outcomes under different tariff policies. We find that the MNF will solely serve the domestic market if the foreign country’s tariff rate exceeds a threshold. We show that the tariff rate is higher under the trade-surplus-maximizing tariff than under the welfare-maximizing tariff. Under the welfare-maximizing tariff, the government may set a modest tariff rate to incentivize the product sales by the foreign MNF if its product’s value-added level is high relative to the domestic MNF’s. However, under a trade-surplus-maximizing tariff policy, the government always sets a high tariff rate to block imports. Moreover, we find that if one government deviates from the welfare-maximizing tariff to the trade-surplus-maximizing tariff, this always hurts social welfare and also harms the domestic MNF’s profit if its product value-added level is low relative to the foreign MNF’s. We also notice that the supplier can even encroach into the market to sell directly. We then examine the interplay between the supplier’s potential entry and its downstream retailer’s information sharing incentive. Two leadership scenarios—the supplier-leads and the e-tailer-leads—are examined. We then characterize the equilibrium information sharing and encroachment decision and the system performance. Interestingly, we show that supplier encroachment always improves consumer surplus, but it is not necessarily welfare-improving. Based on the findings in this research project, we have completed three academic papers which are listed as follows: M. Yuan, F. Bernstein, X. Guan and Y. Wang. 15500820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500820.value: The PI has trained one visiting PhD student, and the research results have been presented at four conferences and several universities. Our main findings are as follows: Consider a supply chain consisting of a supplier with a key technology to produce a critical component, an independent manufacturer that also has the capability of producing the component in-house, and a dependent manufacturer without such capability. We show that exclusion with either the dependent manufacturer or the independent manufacturer can arise in equilibrium. We identify conditions under which the independent manufacturer invests in a high quality level to deter the supplier from engaging in exclusion with the dependent manufacturer. We show that mandatory exclusion imposed by government regulations can increase the independent manufacturer’s incentive to invest in quality compared to that emerges under free trade. Mandatory exclusion always hurts the supplier and in general hurts the independent manufacturer, but it tends to benefit the dependent manufacturer. Moreover, mandatory exclusion can benefit consumers if it leads to a higher investment in quality by the independent manufacturer. Related results are published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 1. Government tariff greatly affects the global product distribution. We show that if the import tariffs are low, there are bilateral exports. However, if one government imposes a high import tariff but the other imposes a modest import tariff, only unilateral exports occur. There is no cross-border trade if import tariffs of both countries are sufficiently large. Under the welfare-maximizing tariff, the government will set a high tariff rate to block imports when the domestic multinational firm (MNF) cannot export products and its product value-added level is low relative to the foreign MNF’s. Under the trade-surplus-maximizing tariff, the government will always set a high tariff rate to block imports. Moreover, if one government unilaterally deviates from the welfare-maximizing tariff to the trade-surplus-maximizing tariff, both MNFs’ profits and both nations’ social welfare may decrease. Related results are published on International Journal of Production Economics; See Part C (8) Item 2. Suppliers can even encroach into the consumer market to sell directly. We show that the substitution rate of the products sold by the e-tailer and the supplier and the commission rate under the agency scheme are crucial factors determining the equilibrium strategy. Related results are published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 3.

15500820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500820.value: There are some related research topics that are worth exploring. For example, conducting some empirical analysis to verify our analytical results could be an interesting direction for further study. Also, we notice that many Chinese firms now invest more in R&D to avoid the potential supply blockade. Meanwhile, more and more USA firms now shift their supply chains to other regions and countries. Follow-up research can investigate the impact of mandatory exclusion on the firms’ global supply chain network design.

15500820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500820.value: We show that the independent manufacturer may invest in a high capability level (leading to a high-quality component) as a strategic deterrent against the supplier’s decision to engage in an exclusive selling agreement with the dependent manufacturer. Mandatory exclusion imposed by government regulations affects free trade among parties, It can exacerbate or mitigate the independent manufacturer’s incentive to invest in internal sourcing capability, relative to a setting in which the supplier determines its distribution strategy in the absence of such government regulations. Moreover, we show that mandatory exclusion always hurts the supplier, but it can benefit or hurt the manufacturers as well as the consumers, depending on the independent manufacturer’s investment cost and the conditions leading to an exclusionary contract under free trade. We find that the multinational firms will solely serve the domestic market if the foreign country’s tariff rate exceeds a threshold. Under the welfare-maximizing tariff, the government may set a modest tariff rate to incentivize the product sales by the foreign multinational firms. However, under a trade-surplus-maximizing tariff policy, the government always sets a high tariff rate to block imports.

15501220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501220.value: 為應對快速變化的商業環境，企業持續強調員工互助行為的重要性並積極塑造團隊助人規範。然而，理論及實證研究並未能指出團隊助人規範對新員工的影響。具體而言，團隊助人規範是否能激發新員工的助人行為，並鼓勵他們在較長一段時期內維持此行為。基於社會資訊處理理論（Salancik & Pfeffer, 1978），組織公民行為的時間動態模型（Methot, Lepak, Shipp, & Boswell, 2017），以及自我概念的相關研究（Lord, Brown, & Freiberg, 1999），我們提出，新員工對團隊助人規範會有不同的心理及行為反應，取決於其自我概念。當新員工擁有一個更高的關係自我概念，團隊助人規範更容易激發他們的親社會動力。而當新員工擁有較低的關係自我概念，團隊助人規範則更容易形成一種助人壓力。而這兩種不同的心理反應，對新員工在團隊中提供助人行為有不同的影響。為檢驗我們的研究模型，我們計劃對100個團隊中的100位新員工及其400位現有員工進行六個月追踪的問卷調查。

15501220.label: Realisation of objectives
15501220.value: We examined whether and how an existing helping norm shapes newcomers' helping behavior during the onboarding stage using two major longitudinal studies. These two studies involved a total of 570 newcomers and 1,149 veterans who completed weekly or biweekly surveys for a period of up to 6 months. Across these two studies, we progressively found support for our hypotheses. First, in achieving Objective #1, our results showed a quadratic trend characterized by an increase followed by a decrease in helping behaviors over the study period. That is, during the onboarding stage, on average, newcomers adapt to the work teams by increasingly providing more help to their veteran coworkers. However, newcomers start to withhold or even reduce their helping behavior after reaching a peak level of help. Second, our results also showed that the existing veteran helping norms influenced newcomers' psychological perceptions related to helping. In Study 1, we found that newcomers' perception of helping norms resulted in a higher level of perceived pressure to help coworkers at work. In Study 2, we replicated this finding and further showed that helping pressure was related to a higher impression management motive but a lower prosocial value motive. Therefore, Objective #2 is fully achieved. Lastly, we found that the impression management motive, but not the prosocial value motive, predicted the trajectory of newcomer helping behavior. More specifically, the impression management motive was positively related to the linear slope of helping behaviors and negatively related to the quadratic slope of helping behaviors. That is, for newcomers with higher levels of the impression management motive to help coworkers, their helping behaviors increased substantially once they joined the work teams, but the level of helping behaviors did not sustain and started to decline after a certain period of time. Thus, we have realized Objective #3.

15501220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501220.value: Grounded in the temporal model of citizenship behavior, as well as research on social norms, citizenship pressure, and citizenship motives, we examine whether, how, and why newcomers react to existing helping norms by providing varying levels of helping behavior to veterans. We propose that overall, newcomers' helping behavior demonstrates a curvilinear pattern characterized by an initial increase and subsequent decrease after reaching a peak. In addition, the helping norms in the existing work teams, shaped by veteran team members, influence newcomers' psychological reactions and thus change the pattern of the trajectory. To test our theoretical model, we conducted two major longitudinal studies. First, as an initial study, we collected data from newly graduated individuals in mainland China and asked them to report their perceptions of helping norms, perceived helping pressure, as well as helping behavior towards coworkers once per week for twelve to thirteen weeks. In Study 1, we found initial support for the trajectory of self-reported helping behavior, as well as the influence of helping norms and helping pressure. However, the self-reported data used in this study may raise concerns regarding potential biases. Thus, we conducted Study 2 using a more complex design by involving both veterans and newcomers in our research and collected data from one major real estate company in Beijing. In this study, veterans reported helping norms before the newcomers joined the team, allowing an accurate reflection of the norms without the influence of the newcomers. Subsequently, two weeks after newcomers joined the team, newcomers reported their perceptions of helping pressure in their respective teams, as well as the motives behind their helping behaviors. Lastly, veterans rated newcomers' helping behavior once biweekly for close to 6 months. These two studies involved a total of 570 newcomers and 1,149 veterans who completed weekly or biweekly surveys for a period of up to 6 months. We have successfully completed this project despite the difficulties due to COVID-19 and the constraints resulting from the economic situation and company downsizing. Overall, our findings underscore the dynamics of helping behavior demonstrated by newcomers during the onboarding stage and the influences caused by the existing helping norms. We presented the initial conceptual framework at the 80th Annual Meeting of the Academy of Management. We are currently in the stage of writing the manuscript, and we plan to submit it to the Journal of Applied Psychology by the end of 2024.

15501220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501220.value: Our research opens doors to new areas of inquiry regarding the positive and negative consequences of cultivating helping norms in organizations. Through our study, we have challenged existing literature by identifying potential negative effects on newcomers, such as increased perceptions of helping pressure and impression management motives, as well as unsustainable helping behavior. One area worthy of exploration is comparing whether the effects found in our research are unique to newcomers or could also apply to veterans. Answering this question would further emphasize the importance of our research for newcomers. Another crucial aspect of future research is identifying organizational factors or interventions that can foster sustainable helping behavior without creating pressure among newcomers. Conducting field experiments will help address this question.

15501220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501220.value: In a Harvard Business Review article, Amabile and colleagues emphasized the significance of fostering a culture of collaborative assistance and highlighted the case of design firm IDEO as an example. While previous research has shown a positive connection between helping norms and helping behaviors among experienced employees, our study aimed to understand how newcomers respond to these norms and whether they provide sustained help. Surprisingly, our findings revealed a potential downside of helping norms for newcomers. We discovered that when newcomers are exposed to strong helping norms, they tend to feel more pressured to provide assistance and are driven by a desire to make a good impression. Unfortunately, this led to unsustainable helping behavior. While we acknowledge the importance of cultivating a helping culture in organizations, we caution companies to be mindful of the pressure it may create for newcomers and the potential for short-term and unsustainable help.
