15502820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15502820.value: In the original proposal, we mainly consider the quality-information signaling problem of a service provider whose quality is fixed. As our research progresses, we expand our study to another setting where the service quality level is random. In the first setting where the service provider's quality level is fixed, we consider two information scenarios: 1). customers are uninformed of service quality and 2). some are informed and others are uninformed. In scenario 1, the equilibrium is always a pooling one, which means that the service provider cannot signal its quality information through queue revelation/concealment. In scenario 2, we find that a separating equilibrium can occur only when the market size is moderate. Our study also reveals that the signaling effect of queue disclosure increases (decreases) the effective arrival rate of the high-quality (low-quality) server and also increases the customers' total utility when the server is of low quality. In the second setting, we investigate a server's best queue disclosure strategy with an uncertain quality level (which is assumed to be binary). We model this problem as a Bayesian persuasion game. The server ﬁrst commits to a possibly mixed strategy stating the probability that the queue length will be revealed to customers on their arrival given a realized quality level. The service quality level is then realized, and the server’s corresponding queue-disclosure action is observed by customers, who then update their beliefs regarding service quality and decide whether to join the service system. We find that when the market size is sufﬁciently small (large), the server always conceals (reveals) the queue, regardless of the realized service quality. Numerically, we ﬁnd that in a medium-sized market, the server's optimal commitment strategy is often hybrid or mixed, that is, randomizing queue concealment and revelation. We also extend our analysis to a situation in which the server aims to maximize social welfare. We show that under certain conditions, it is always beneﬁcial for the social planner to randomize queue concealment and revelation, regardless of the market size. In our third work, we consider the information service in a bus station. We find that providing more information on bus schedule might not benefit the customers as a whole. The result depends on the curvature of customer demand distribution.

15502820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15502820.value: In our current project, we mainly consider the service provider's information providing strategy in a monopoly market, that is, the market with only one service provider. It remains to be an interesting research question to consider a duopoly market with two competing service providers. I am thinking over such questions and possibly qill conduct another research project to investigate them.

15502820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15502820.value: Customers often are unclear about service quality and sometimes can infer such information through observing the queue length. For example, customers can infer the food quality if observing a long queue in front of a restaurant. For the profit-maximizing service provider, how shall it convince customers to join its queue? And how is the optimal strategy for a service provide being a welfare maximizer? My research outcome contributes to people's understanding about the service provider's queue disclosure strategy. In the setting where the server's service quality is fixed, I find that a server can only signal its quality information via queue disclosure when some customers are old customers, and some are new. If all customers are new, it does not work. In another setting where the server's quality is random, I find that the server can persuade more customers to join its system via randomization over queue disclosure and concealment. These research outcomes help managers to better control the service system via providing information on queues, to achieve either profit maximization or welfare maximization.

15503220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15503220.value: 與高管薪酬相關的成本分類轉移，以及對盈餘性質的影響

15503220.label: Project Objectives
15503220.value: To provide evidence on compensation-driven classification shifting
rows: To provide evidence on compensation-driven classification shifting

15503220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503220.value: The 2006 Securities and Exchange Commission rule 33-8732A requires expanded disclosure of information related to executive compensation in proxy statements, thus allowing researchers to directly observe the earnings numbers that are used by the board in determining compensation payout. Exploiting this newly disclosed information, recent studies document that firms frequently (but do not always) remove transitory earnings components in arriving at the realized earnings in performance measurement for compensation purposes. We argue that when managers expect transitory earnings components to be removed for compensation performance measurement, they will find it beneficial to shift expenses from core expenses to special items, as it results in higher core earnings and consequently higher compensation payout. In this project, we propose the following research questions. First, does the expectation of the removal of transitory earnings components for compensation performance measurement motivate managers to engage in classification shifting? Second, when do we expect more compensation-driven classification shifting? Third, how does the compensation-driven classification shifting affect the properties of earnings components? Using a large sample of manually collected data on firms’ treatment of transitory earnings components in compensation performance measurement, this project will provide empirical answers to these questions. In addition to contributing to the research on executive compensation contracting and financial disclosure, our study will be of interest to financial market regulators and other users of reported accounting information. 2006年SEC監管條例33-8732A要求公司披露更多的高管薪酬信息，這讓研究人員能夠直接觀測到董事會決定高管薪酬是使用的盈餘信息。現有的研究發現公司有的時候（但不是所有時候）會在覺得實現的盈餘數字時排除一次性的盈餘部分。我們認為高管在預期一次性盈餘部分被排除的時候把一些成本從核心盈餘移動到一次性盈餘，以此來獲得更高薪酬。在這個研究項目中，我們有以下研究問題。是不是高管在預期一次性盈餘部分被排除的時候把一些成本從核心盈餘移動到一次性盈餘？什麼時候高管會更多的移動成本？這會怎樣影響盈餘的性質？我們將會收集數據進行相應的分析。我們的研究會增進對高管薪酬和公司財務信息披露的理解，同時也會對金融市場監管機構和其他財務信息使用者有幫助。

15503920.value: 降低去中心化供应链中的供给风险：推迟定价还是推迟付款？

15503920.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15503920.value: Prof GENG, Xin Prof YANG, Nan

15503920.label: Project Objectives
15503920.value: First, we start by solving our multi-stage Stackelberg game as building block, and derive the channel firms' equilibrium decisions and the corresponding optimal profits for every possible combination of payment and price postponement strategies. Such analysis is helpful in revealing the fundamental impact of timing issues on channel members' equilibrium decisions. We also intend to conduct sensitivity analysis to investigate how various model parameters affect the equilibrium decisions and the corresponding profits. Second, building upon the analysis of the aforementioned individual scenarios, we aim to understand the isolated impact of price postponement and payment scheme separately. To achieve this, we analyze channel members' preference for each individual strategy. That is, given a preset pricing [payment] scheme, we investigate channel members' preferences over the alternative payment [pricing] scheme. This singles out the disjoint effect of price and payment postponement strategies, and provides us clear understanding on how each strategy may affect supply risk allocation and mitigation within the channel. Third, the central theme of the proposal is to investigate the strategic interplay between payment scheme and price postponement in combating yield shortage. We mainly investigate such interplay from the downstream buyer's perspective to see if the two strategies are substitute or complement, and how to effectively combine them to mitigate upstream supply yield risk. Meanwhile, we also aim to identify the supplier's preference and investigate if there exists a strategy combination that could align incentives along the channel and improve both firms' profits. Finally, the deployment of postponement strategies affects not only the risk allocation within the channel, but also the determination of the endogenous wholesale price and market price, which may have a profound impact on end market consumers' surplus. As such, we would like to further our analysis by studying the impacts of channel strategies on consumers' surplus. Particularly, we would like to investigate whether there exists a combination of strategies that not only align channel incentives but also benefit consumers, i.e., leading to a win-win-win outcome within the entire value chain.

15503920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503920.value: Nowadays, outsourcing becomes a trending and prevailing strategy for many firms to reduce cost and ensure competitiveness in the global market. However, such a strategy also exposes firms to various kinds of risks, out of which supply risk is a significant one. Among others, production yield risk is considered as a major supply risk, and is common in many industries, e.g., semiconductor industry, agribusiness, etc. When sourcing from a supplier with production yield risk, how to properly deploy effective mechanisms to mitigate the adverse impact of yield shortage becomes a primary concern for the buying firms. Among various risk mitigation strategies, two are commonly adopted in practice. On the one hand, the buyer could postpone the payment to make it contingent upon the final delivered quantity, rather than the production input quantity. This provides the supplier with strong incentive to inflate the production quantity and enhance the delivery performance. On the other hand, the buyer could also postpone the decision of the market price after the yield realization, which better controls the demand to consume the available supply in a more profitable way. Intuition suggests that these strategies would allow the buyer to manipulate the allocation of the yield risk among the channel members, thereby managing the supply uncertainty to its advantage. However, potential issues may arise to offset the effectiveness of the two strategies, especially in a decentralized environment where the supplier is able to make strategic decisions and counteract the buyer's intention. Such an interplay between firms may worsen the double marginalization problem and in turn weaken the buyer’s incentive to adopt these postponement strategies. The central theme of the proposal is to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the strategic interaction between different payment and pricing schemes, which are used by a buying firm to mitigate supply yield risk in the presence of potential channel conflicts due to decentralization. We aim to investigate the buying firm’s strategy selection and to identify the conditions under which a strategy or strategies could combat the supply yield risk in the most effective way; moreover, we attempt to uncover the corresponding implications on the channel members’ profitability/welfare. As both postponement strategies are commonly observed in practice, our proposal, upon its successful completion, can provide rich managerial insights on how to effectively deploy them to mitigate supply yield risk and induce Pareto improvement for every member along the value chain. 如今，外包生产已成为许多公司降低成本，确保在全球市场上竞争力的一种流行趋势和主流策略。但是，这种策略也使公司面临各种风险，这其中供应风险是非常重要的一类。生产良品率风险被认为是主要的供应风险，在许多行业中很常见，例如半导体行业，农业等。 当从具有生产良品率风险的供应商那里采购时，如何适当地部署有效的机制来减轻供给短缺的不利影响成为采购公司的首要问题。对于各种风险缓解策略，实践中通常采用两种。一方面，买方可以推迟付款，以使付款取决于最终交付的数量，而不是生产投入的数量。这为供应商提供了极大的动力来增加产量并提高交货性能。另一方面，购买者也可以在得知供给量后再决定市场价格，这可以更好地控制需求，从而以更有利可图的方式消耗可用供应。直觉表明，这些策略将允许购买者操纵渠道成员之间的收益风险分配，从而将供应不确定性管理到有利的位置。 但是，潜在的问题可能会抵消这两种策略的有效性，特别是在去中心化的环境中，供应商能够做出战略决策并抵消买方的意图。企业之间的这种相互作用可能会使双重边缘化问题恶化，进而削弱买方采取这些推迟策略的动机。 该提案的中心主题是提供一个理论框架，以了解不同支付和定价方案之间的战略互动，在去中心化导致潜在的渠道冲突的情况下，购买公司可以使用这些框架来减轻供应收益风险。我们的目的是调查购买公司的策略选择，并确定使得一种或多种策略得以有效地应对供应收益风险的条件；此外，我们尝试揭示各种策略对渠道成员的获利能力/福利的相应影响。 由于这两种延迟策略在实践中通常都会被观察到，因此在成功完成后，我们的提案可以为如何有效地为去中心化供应链减轻供应风险提供丰富的管理见解。

15503920.label: Realisation of objectives
15503920.value: All the four objectives have been fully achieved. The proposal outlines four key objectives centered on developing a theoretical framework to analyze the strategic interplay between payment schemes and price postponement in mitigating supply yield risk. This risk arises in decentralized supply chain settings, where channel conflicts often emerge due to misaligned incentives among members. Specifically, the study aims to: (1) Identify the conditions under which specific strategies (e.g., payment schemes, price postponement, or their combination) most effectively address supply yield risk, and (2) Evaluate the implications of these strategies for the profitability and coordination of supply chain stakeholders. By clarifying the mechanisms through which these strategies interact, the framework seeks to provide actionable insights for optimizing risk management in decentralized supply chains. To this end, we have built a game theoretical model including one upstream reliable supplier suffering from production random yield and one downstream retailer who can decide whether to price the product before or after the yield realization to the market. We have proposed the following four research objectives to be investigated. First, we start by solving our multi-stage Stackelberg game as building block and derive the channel firms' equilibrium decisions and the corresponding optimal profits for every possible combination of payment and price postponement strategies. Second, building upon the analysis of the aforementioned individual scenarios, we aim to understand the isolated impact of price postponement and payment scheme separately. Third, the central theme of the proposal is to investigate the strategic interplay between payment scheme and price postponement in combating yield shortage. Finally, we would like to further our analysis by studying the impacts of channel strategies on consumers' surplus. We have thoroughly analysed the above supply chain game model and achieved all four objectives. The main findings have been summarized in the paper titled “Supply Risk Mitigation in a Decentralized Supply Chain: Pricing Postponement or Payment Postponement?”, which has been published in UTD journal Manufacturing & Service Operations Management. Please see the attached paper in part C for details. In what follows, we will elaborate on how and to what extent the four project objectives have been achieved: Objective 1: We fully solve each of the four different strategy combinations (i.e., no postponement, postponing pricing, postponing payment, postponing both) to derive the optimal pricing and production decisions as well as the associated optimal profits. From such analysis, we can see how decision timing would create different incentives to affect the channel member’s optimal decisions. Objective 2: Starting with the benchmark scenario where no postponement is present, we compare the retailer's optimal profit among the scenarios where the retailer deploys different combinations of the payment and pricing schemes. On the one hand, we find that, when the supplier's production cost is low and the likelihood of yield loss is relatively high, the benchmark scenario is already optimal; i.e., the retailer will not strictly benefit from either postponement strategy. If the production cost is high, however, the retailer's profit will be strictly improved if pricing postponement is used. On the other hand, we establish the retailer's preference order over various postponement strategy combinations. Specifically, with low production cost, the retailer is more likely to postpone payment rather than pricing; however, the retailer prefers the pricing postponement strategy when the supplier's production cost increases. Overall, we find that the benefit of pricing postponement for the retailer is growing as the production cost increases, because the contingent market price accompanied with low production cost would worsen the double marginalization problem. Furthermore, the retailer benefits less from postponing payment when the cost increases, because the supplier simply will not inflate production even under a pay-by-delivery contract if doing so is too costly. Objective 3: In addition to the direct comparison among the combinations of strategies, we also investigate the interplay of the payment and pricing schemes, i.e., whether the presence of one strategy would enhance or reduce the value of adopting the other strategy. Since they are both potential tools for the retailer to mitigate the supply yield risk, intuition suggests that the two postponement strategies may be substitutes. Nevertheless, our analysis uncovers the opposite: When the potential yield loss is not too severe and the production cost is in the medium range, payment postponement and pricing postponement are strategic complements. In such a situation, the use of one strategy can enhance the positive effect of the other for the retailer. Objective 4: We take the channel's perspective, and study the respective impacts of the payment and pricing schemes on firms' profits as well as the consumer surplus. We find that payment postponement can be a Pareto optimal choice for the entire supply chain, especially when the supplier's production cost is low. However, with relatively high cost, either the consumers (without pricing postponement) or the supplier (with pricing postponement), but not both, will be negatively affected by the payment postponement. As for the impact of the pricing postponement, we show that it can be positive for the entire channel, but the benefit is largely enhanced when accompanied by payment postponement. In fact, the retailer's pricing postponement strategy may hurt the supplier if payment is not postponed. Rather, once the retailer shifts the yield risk back to the upstream and lets the supplier make inflation decision, postponing the pricing decision will never hurt anyone in the supply chain. Under each payment scheme, pricing postponement is more likely to benefit the supply chain with relatively high production cost. Others: Inspired by the above research, we also conduct another related research to investigate the strategic interplay between price postponement and supply diversification in mitigating production yield risk. Using a similar modeling framework, we find that although the firm is better off with responsive pricing, the effect of price postponement on the optimal sourcing decision and the firm's need for supply diversification varies and is influenced by factors such as unit procurement cost, supply portfolio, and supply reliability. For the case of one unreliable supplier, we show that responsive pricing mitigates the overage and underage risks imposed by yield uncertainty, and results in a lower optimal order quantity than that under ex ante pricing when the procurement cost is low, and a higher quantity otherwise. For the case of two unreliable suppliers, we show that responsive pricing promotes supply diversification when the sole-sourced supplier's reliability is low, and discourages when it is high. By contrast, when the sole-sourced supplier's reliability is moderate, responsive pricing promotes supply diversification when its unit procurement cost is low and discourages otherwise. The composition of supply portfolio also has a fundamental impact on such strategic interplay: When the supply portfolio consists of one unreliable and one reliable supplier, diversified sourcing is never optimal under ex ante pricing, but may be optimal under responsive pricing. Thus, responsive pricing promotes dual sourcing in this setting. The finding is summarized in a paper “Supply diversification under random yield: The impact of price postponement”, published in UTD journal Production and Operations Management. Please refer to part C for details.

15503920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503920.value: In this project, we have obtained fruitful results and interesting managerial insights. To summarize those findings, we have published two papers in UTD journal, one in MSOM and one in POM. We briefly summarize the main findings below: Objectives 1-2: We compare the retailer’s optimal profit across different combinations of payment and pricing schemes. We find that when the supplier’s production cost is low and yield risk is high, the benchmark scenario is already optimal, and postponement strategies offer no additional benefit. However, if production cost is high, pricing postponement strictly improves the retailer’s profit. Our analysis shows that with low production cost, the retailer prefers payment postponement, but as production cost rises, pricing postponement becomes more advantageous. Overall, the benefit of pricing postponement increases with production cost, while the advantage of payment postponement diminishes, since high costs discourage the supplier from increasing production even under favorable payment terms. Objective 3: We examine how payment and pricing schemes interact—specifically, whether adopting one enhances or reduces the value of the other. While intuition suggests these postponement strategies might be substitutes, our analysis reveals that, when yield loss is moderate and production cost is in the medium range, payment and pricing postponement actually act as strategic complements, with each enhancing the effectiveness of the other for the retailer. Objective 4: From the channel’s perspective, we analyze how payment and pricing schemes affect both firms’ profits and consumer surplus. We find that payment postponement can be Pareto optimal for the supply chain, especially when production costs are low. However, with higher costs, payment postponement may harm either consumers (without pricing postponement) or the supplier (with pricing postponement), but not both. Pricing postponement can benefit the entire channel, particularly when combined with payment postponement; otherwise, it may hurt the supplier. Overall, pricing postponement is more likely to benefit the supply chain when production costs are high, especially if payment is also postponed. Others: Building on this research, we also examine the interplay between price postponement and supply diversification in mitigating production yield risk. Using a similar model, we find that while responsive pricing benefits the firm, its impact on optimal sourcing and the need for supply diversification depends on factors like procurement cost, supply portfolio, and supply reliability.

15503920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503920.value: Building upon these two research papers, we will further investigate risk mitigation strategies in global supply chain context to fight against both supply risk and tariff risk. The insights from this project would be helpful for us to develop follow up works in this direction.

15503920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503920.value: In this project, we explored how firms can use different payment and pricing strategies to manage risk in production. We found that if it’s cheap for suppliers to produce goods and there’s a high chance of production problems, sticking to traditional payment and pricing methods works best. However, when production costs are higher, allowing retailers to set prices later (pricing postponement) helps them earn more. Surprisingly, while it might seem that payment and pricing postponement would replace each other, our research shows they can actually work better together under certain conditions, making both strategies more effective. For managers, this means that combining payment and pricing flexibility can be a powerful tool, especially when facing moderate risks and costs. From a broader supply chain perspective, postponing payments can benefit everyone when costs are low, but with higher costs, it may hurt either the supplier or the consumer unless combined with pricing postponement. We also found that the best way to handle production risks—such as choosing multiple suppliers or delaying pricing—depends on costs, supplier options, and reliability. These insights can help managers design smarter contracts and supply strategies to better handle uncertainty and improve overall profitability.

15504820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504820.value: Improving upon previous hotel efficiency studies largely lacking consideration on either internal or external non-homogeneity of hotel properties under evaluation, this project proposes a non-homogeneous data envelopment analysis (DEA) model to examine the performance of hotels in the Greater Bay Area (GBA). In particular, our study will, first, from an output perspective estimate and validate a DEA model considering variable output sets for Hong Kong hotels with different combinations of service provisions. Second, from a competitive regional perspective, a three-stage DEA model will be carried out to evaluate the performance of hotels in the wider GBA, where hotels in Hong Kong, Macau, Shenzhen and Guangzhou operate and compete under a non-homogeneous external competitive environment. The three-stage DEA model incorporates environmental effects and statistical noise into a producer performance evaluation so as to realistically measure the performance of hotels on a relatively fair basis without the bias of environmental factors. Third, a new approach considering simultaneously internal and external non-homogeneity of hotels is devised to evaluate the performance of hotels. Finally, suggestions for efficiency improvement and resource saving could be provided for the hotels operating in the GBA. 針對過去酒店效率研究中很大程度上缺乏對被評估酒店屬性的內部或外部非均質性給予考慮，本項目提出了一種非均質數據包絡分析（DEA）模型來評估大灣區（GBA）酒店的績效。特別是，我們的研究將首先從產出的角度給香港酒店業估計並驗證一個考慮了具有不同服務產品組合且有可變產出集合的DEA模型。第二，從區域競爭角度出發，我們將採用三階段DEA模型來評估大灣區包括香港，澳門，深圳和廣州在非同質的外部競爭環境下運營和競爭的酒店績效。三階段DEA模型將環境影響和統計噪聲納入生產者績效評估中，以便在不受到環境因素的影響下及相對公平的基礎上更現實地衡量酒店的績效。第三，我們構建一種同時考慮酒店內部和外部非同質性的新方法來評估酒店的績效。最後，本項目可以為在大灣區運營的酒店提供效率提升和節省資源的建議。

15504820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504820.value: Improving upon previous studies on hotel performance evaluation in terms of efficiency, which usually treat different hotels as homogeneous in their product provision, this study examines the performance of 53 hotels in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area (GBA) during 2015-2019 by employing data envelopment analysis with a non-homogeneous decision making units (DMUs) model. The results show that the hotels in the GBA were generally inefficient, and those with high product diversification were able to achieve higher efficiency scores. Specifically, the hotels providing rooms, food and beverage, meeting services, and spa services had relatively higher efficiency scores, while those providing only rooms had relatively the worst performance. Among the GBA cities included in this study, the non-homogeneous efficiency scores of the hotels in Guangzhou outperformed those of hotels in the other cities, and the overall hotel efficiency score of the core cities was better than that of the key node cities. The research outcome has been submitted to potential journals for publication consideration; however, the most recent submission is still pending review. The research outcome is prepared in a manuscript titled "Hotel performance in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area: A product heterogeneity perspective " and was first submitted to International Journal of Hospitality Management, however with a lengthy revision and review process and unfortunate rejection outcome. The manuscript retitled "Hotel performance in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area: A non-homogeneous perspective" was then submitted to the Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research and is now under a 2nd-round review. The submission history is as follows: To International Journal of Hospitality Management: First submission: 13 July 2022 (Manuscript ID: HOSMAN-D-22-00828) First decision received: 24 Sep 2022 Second submission: 18 Nov 2022 (Manuscript ID: HOSMAN-D-22-00828R1) Second decision received: 17 Jan 2023 Third submission: 9 Apr 2023 (Manuscript ID: HOSMAN-D-22-00828R2) Rejection notice: 22 July 2023 To Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research: First submission: 27 July 2023 (Manuscript ID: JHTR-23-07-668) First decision received: 27 Sep 2023 Second submission: 20 Nov 2023 (Manuscript ID: JHTR-23-07-668.R1) Status: Awaiting review result During the course of the project, with collected data and literature for the project, we were able to publish a paper in Tourism Economics titled "Spatial spillover and determinants of tourism efficiency: A low carbon emission perspective" and we acknowledged the funding support of the project. The doi of the paper is DOI: 10.1177/13548166231167045.

15504820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504820.value: Since our research findings were derived from data on 53 hotels in the GBA during 2015-2019 collected from STR Global, the key conclusions of this study are specifically based on a sample of hotels within the GBA. Therefore, future studies can, first, validate the results of this study by using data from a larger sample of hotels. Second, the diversity of more products provided by hotels, such as golfing and online retail, among others, could be studied so as to assess the non-homogeneous efficiency of hotels more comprehensively. Besides, since the project focused on the heterogeneity of product categories, in the next step we can consider the heterogeneity of product quality in the same category. That is, future research can extend to define and measure the heterogeneity of service quality and how this heterogeneity affects efficiency evaluation.

15504820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504820.value: This study measured hotel performance in terms of efficiency by considering the diversity of products provided by the sample hotels in seven cities in the GBA during 2015-2019. The results show that, first, considering product diversification, the hotels in the GBA were not efficient, with at least one type of their products causing this inefficiency. Second, the hotels providing rooms, F&B, meeting services, and spa services had higher non-homogeneous efficiency, followed by those providing rooms, F&B, and meeting services, those providing rooms, F&B, and spa services, and, lastly, those providing only rooms. F&B had the greatest impact on the non-homogeneous efficiency of hotels in the GBA. Third, among the seven GBA cities, the non-homogeneous efficiency of the hotels in the core cities was better than that of those in key node cities. In particular, Guangzhou in general outperformed the others, with the highest non-homogeneous efficiency, followed by Shenzhen and Hong Kong, while Macau had the worst efficiency. Considering the efficiency of products of hotels in each city, on the other hand, Zhongshan had the best performance in terms of rooms, Macau in terms of F&B, Hong Kong in terms of meeting services, and Shenzhen in terms of spa services.

15505320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505320.value: We have met the objectives of the project and come up with results in four journal papers. (Due to COVID-19, we could not attend conferences overseas.) The details of the four journal papers are as follows. (1) In the paper “Effects of imperfect IoT-enabled diagnostics on maintenance services: A system design perspective” published in Computers and Industrial Engineering, we developed a strategic queuing model to investigate a maintenance service provider’s optimal capacity allocation and pricing decisions in the presence of imperfect IoT-based diagnostics. In addition, we considered the heterogeneous service rates resulting from the accelerating effect of IoT-based diagnostics. The results of the study revealed that, on the one hand, the optimal service rate always increases with the diagnostic quality; on the other hand, if customer error cost is higher than that of the service provider, the optimal price increases with the diagnostic quality; otherwise, it decreases with the diagnostic quality. For details, please refer to the paper. (2) In the paper “Optimization of after-sales services with spare parts consumption and repairman travel” published in International Journal of Production Economics, we studied the optimization of discretionary after-sales maintenance services with spare parts consumption and repairman travel. Discretionary service means that the service quality (which depends on the use of imperfect IoT technology or not, and the repairman) and spare parts consumption are determined by the service provider. For details, please refer to the paper. (3) In the paper “Optimal after-sales service offering strategy: Additive manufacturing, traditional manufacturing, or hybrid?” published in International Journal of Production Economics, we investigated the effects of additive manufacturing (also known as 3D printing) on the optimal after-sales maintenance service offering strategy. A service offering strategy should be selected on the basis of not only its characteristics but also customers’ decisions influenced by the associated costs of each strategy. Two supply chain structures are examined in this study: one in which the service provider is vertically integrated and the other in which an outside agent is involved to adopt additive manufacturing. For details, please refer to the paper. (4) In the paper “Maintenance services offering strategies with imperfect IoT-enabled diagnostics: Monopoly and duopoly scenarios” submitted to Production and Operations Management, we analyzed the optimal capacity allocation and pricing decisions of service providers by taking account the imperfect nature of IoT-enabled diagnostics. The optimal service offering strategies are presented. Monopoly and duopoly scenarios are discussed separately. For details, please refer to the paper.

However, the monitoring results may produce inaccurate outcomes due to inaccurate information or inappropriate predictive methods. We have developed advanced analytical and mathematical tools for optimizing operational strategies to tackle the problem.

15505720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505720.value: The banking industry practice of hiring former regulators has drawn intensive public attention. Critics believe that this so-called “revolving door” practice could create conflicts of interests, and undermines the fairness and enforcement of regulations, thereby eroding public trust in the regulator. As a recent US congressional report points out, the “revolving door” has been one of the most important factors threatening bank regulators’ independence (Government Accountability Office, 2017). The revolving door phenomenon in bank regulation has become prevalent over the recent decade and is considered “an important cause of the global financial crisis” (OCED, 2009). In the US, around 30% of banks have at least one ex-regulator. The number of ex-regulators working in banks has increased by 24% from 2001 to 2015 (Shive and Forster, 2017). Despite the prevalence of this phenomenon, academic research on this issue is relatively scarce (Lucca, Seru, and Trebbi, 2014). Motivated by the gap between this common practice and the scarcity of relevant research, this project plans to investigate the economic consequences of the revolving door in a bank setting. The impact of the revolving door could be twofold. On the one hand, hiring ex-regulators can help the bank to establish connections with current regulators and consequently receive preferential treatment, leading to poor accounting quality (quid-pro-quo hypothesis). On the other hand, hiring ex-regulators can help the bank if the ex-regulators leverage their skills and expertise to improve the bank’s accounting quality (schooling hypothesis). Thus, the net effects of this practice are an empirical question. Specifically, by employing a propensity score matching difference in differences (PSM-DID) method, we will first examine the impact of hiring former regulators on abnormal loan loss provision. Second, we will study the impact of hiring former regulators on accounting conservatism. Third, we will consider the impact of such hires on bank restatements. Fourth, we will test whether these effects are more pronounced when an ex-regulator is hired as the CFO or as an audit committee member and when the ex-regulator has accounting expertise. Last, using the 2016 U.S. Federal Reserve’s policy shock on the revolving door, we will re-examine the revolving door’s impact on bank accounting quality. This project will shed light on the role of the revolving door in bank behaviors. It will also contribute to the growing literature about banking regulators and as such, it will have policy and practical implications for worldwide governments, bank regulators, and practitioners. 银行业中雇佣前任监管者的行为广泛存在并引起了公众的极大关注。批评者将之成为“旋转门”。这一现象可能带来利益冲突，并削弱监管的公平与执行力，从而损害公众对于监管者的信任。根据美国审计署（Government Accountability Office, 2017）的报告，“旋转门”现象已经成为了最为损害银行监管的因素之一。 在过去的十年间，“旋转门”现象变得越来越普遍，并被认为是“金融危机的起因之一”（OCED, 2009）。在美国，大约30%的银行至少有一个前任监管者。前任监管者在银行中工作的数量从2001年到2015年间增长了24%(Shive and Forster, 2017)。尽管这一现象广泛存在，但是相关的学术研究却屈指可数(Lucca, Seru, and Trebbi, 2014)。 基于该现象的普遍性和相关研究的缺乏性，本研究将尝试调查银行监管旋转门的经济后果。银行监管中“旋转门”的影响可能是两个方面的。第一，雇佣前任监管者可以帮助银行建立与现任监管者的关系网络，从而受到更有利于银行的特殊对待，导致银行的会计质量更低（利益交换假说）。另一方面，雇佣前任监管者可以帮助银行利用其专业知识和背景来改善银行的会计质量（教育假说）。所以，这一现象的最终效应还有待检验。 利用倾向性打分的双重差分法（PSM-DID），本研究将首先考察雇佣前任监管者对于银行可操控贷款损失的影响。其次，本项目将考察雇佣前任监管者对于银行会计稳健性的影响。再次，本项目将考察雇佣前任监管者对于银行财务重述的影响。第四，本项目将考察前任监管者担任CFO或者审计委员会职务或前任监管者的会计专长能否放大上述效应。最后，本研究将考察2016年美联储关于旋转门的监管政策对于上述问题的影响。 本项目有助于厘清旋转门在银行行为中的作用。本项目将丰富现有的关于银行监管者的研究，并对政府、银行监管者及从业者具有政策启示意义。

15505720.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505720.value: We examine the effect of the revolving door practice (i.e., hiring former regulators) on banks’ accounting quality. Conceptually, the revolving door practice could lead to inferior accounting quality by helping banks avoid punishment from regulatory institutions, or alternatively bring about improved accounting quality due to ex-regulators’ expertise. Using a sample of U.S. bank holding companies during 1999–2020, our evidence shows that the practice of the revolving door significantly decreases income-increasing abnormal loan loss provision, suggesting an accounting quality-improving effect. Our result holds even when we implement a difference-in-difference test and exploit the Fed’s regulation change as an exogenous shock to the revolving door practice. The documented effect is more pronounced for former regulators with accounting experience or in financially influential positions and for banks with weak internal control. Further investigations show that the revolving door practice reduces the number of restatements of banks’ financial reports and enhances accounting conservatism. Overall, our findings support the notion that hiring ex-regulators for banking operations is helpful in banking governance.

15505720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505720.value: The paper is under review of a top journal in accounting.

15505720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505720.value: The revolving door practice in the banking industry has been a subject of debate. We analyze the impact of hiring ex-regulators on banks’ accounting quality. Our baseline results show that these employees are associated with reduced income-increasing ALLP but not with reduced total or income-decreasing ALLP. By implementing a staggered DID design and a PSM approach as robustness checks, we provide further evidence corroborating our baseline finding that the revolving door practice leads to lowered income-increasing accounting accruals and thus improved reporting quality. Our empirical evidence may be useful to regulatory agents because it shows how the revolving door benefits banks’ accounting practices in that ex-regulators can efficiently leverage their experience and expertise to improve accounting quality. However, we acknowledge that the intensified relationship between governments and private sectors might introduce corruption to public regulations, which may harm financial stability (OECD 2009). Hence, it is important to set appropriate rules and procedures to control conflicts of interest generated by this phenomenon.

15505820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505820.value: Exploring a recent change in fund reporting requirements in the U.S. (Investment Reporting Modernization rules), we propose a study to examine the effect of disclosed information on the regulators’ role in disciplining fund managers’ opportunism. Investors and regulators are concerned that periodically (e.g., quarterly in the U.S. up to April 2019) disclosed portfolio holdings do not fully capture fund managers’ stock selection abilities. It is often alleged that fund managers upwardly manipulate their reported performance by placing large orders of existing holdings (i.e., portfolio pumping) or buying winner stocks while selling loser stocks in advance of disclosure dates (i.e., window dressing). In turn, misled investors could reward the fund manager with new fund inflow. Cognizant of such an agency problem between fund managers and investors, regulators impose a fine or raise litigation against fund managers for market manipulation once a suspicious trading pattern is detected. While it is argued that mandatorily disclosed portfolio information is one primary source needed for regulators to monitor fund trading, it is ex ante unclear to what extent fund managers’ opportunism can be effectively suppressed by well-informed regulators as compared to by market investors. When a certain type of portfolio information is released equally to regulators and investors, it is difficult to tell which party becomes more equipped with that information. Even if researchers find an interesting observation following such an information event, it often remains inconclusive who is the primary cause of their finding-the regulators or the investors. It is essential for regulators to know how distinctive their disciplinary role in the finance market is from that of investors so that they can better predict the consequences of policy changes. In studying the disciplinary role of regulators, we plan to examine to what extent fund managers’ self-motivated trading behavior is alleviated after the introduction of new reporting requirements that substantially enhances the quality and the quantity of information available to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The completion of our proposed research will significantly further our understanding on 1) the role of portfolio information disclosure in mitigating agency problems between fund managers and investors, and 2) the role of regulators, as distinctive from that of investors, in disciplining fund managers’ opportunism. Considering its significance as a financial hub, this study will be of particular interest to the Hong Kong's regulation body who fights to protect fair, orderly, and efficient finance market. 在这一研究课题中，我们计划探索一项基金报告规则的最新变化 （《投资报告现代化规则》），以检验披露的信息对监管机构在约束基金经理机会主义中的作用。 当某种特定类型的投资组合信息被同等程度地披露给监管者和投资者时, 我们通常很难分辨哪一方更好地掌握了该信息. 即便研究者有了关于这一信息事件的有趣发现, 我们也通常不能确定究竟监管者还是投资者是导致这一现象的主要原因。 在研究监管者的约束作用中， 我们计划检验在引入这一能从实质上提升美国证券交易委员会（SEC）可获得的信息质量和数量的新报告规则后， 从何种程度上， 基金经理自我逐利的交易行为被减弱了。

15505820.label: Realisation of objectives
15505820.value: This study provides novel evidence on the regulatory effect of fund disclosure on fund mangers’ opportunism. Since fund managers’ behaviors are only partially observable from quarterly disclosure of fund holdings, regulators and investors concerned about fund managers disguising their true performance through portfolio pumping or window dressing. In turn, misled investors could reward the fund manager with new fund inflow. Cognizant of this agency problem between fund managers and investors, regulators impose a fine or raise litigation against fund managers for market manipulation once a suspicious trading pattern is detected. Although it is argued that mandatorily disclosed portfolio information is essential for regulator to monitor fund trading, it is ex ante unclear to what extent fund managers’ opportunism can be effectively suppressed by well-informed regulators as compared to by market investors. Exploring a recent change in fund reporting requirements in the U.S. (Investment Reporting Modernization rules), we examine the effect of disclosed information on the regulators’ disciplinary role in deterring fund managers’ opportunism. This setting is particularly interesting since the newly reported information is only viewable to the SEC, but not the public, which allows us to better distinguish the regulators’ role in deterring managerial opportunism from that of investors. This study successfully achieves the proposed objects by investigating the role of disclosed information in regulatory oversight over fund activities. Our finding shows that while the new filing rule potentially increases the information value of fund disclosure, there is no evidence that Investment Reporting Modernization rules substantially lower fund managers’ opportunistic motivation; we find no significant pre- vs post-adoption change in portfolio pumping and window dressing. This finding thus provides valuable insight to the current debates on regulation design about to what degree fund information should be shared with investors. Without investors properly being informed, regulators’ role in monitoring fund managers would be limited. We admit that our analysis could be non-trivially affected by the high market fluctuation during the pandemic period, which coincides with the post-event period in our study. Such high market volatility in a short period is likely to make it more difficult for us to attribute our finding to the event of interest (i.e., the adoption of Form N-PORT). As such, our results should be interpreted with caution.

15505820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505820.value: Exploring a recent change in fund reporting requirements in the U.S. (Investment Reporting Modernization rules), we examine the effect of information disclosure on regulators’ disciplinary role in deterring fund managers’ opportunism (as distinguished from that of investors). Investors and regulators are concerned that periodically (e.g., quarterly in the U.S. up to April 2019) disclosed portfolio holdings do not fully capture fund managers’ stock selection abilities even though they remain as an important monitoring device over fund managers. It is often alleged that fund managers upwardly manipulate their reported performance by placing large orders of existing holdings (i.e., portfolio pumping) or buying winner stocks while selling loser stocks in advance of disclosure dates (i.e., window dressing). Fund disclosure is believed to be essential to keep those fund managers from behaving opportunistically. We investigate the information value of Form N-PORT on which fund managers are required to report monthly holdings, in addition to quarterly holdings that have been available by Form N-Q and Form N-CSR previously. To the extent that Form N-PORT helps the SEC become better equipped to monitor fund managers, we predict to observe the reduction in portfolio pumping and window dressing in the post-adoption period. Our analysis, however, documents no such empirical evidence supporting the post-adoption decrease in fund managers' opportunism; we detect no significant difference-in-differences changes in portfolio pumping and window dressing, as opposed to our hypotheses. This finding is robust to alternative event study designs. Since the newly reported monthly holdings information remain hidden from the public, our results thus highlight the critical role of investors in disciplining fund managers.

15505820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505820.value: We find two future research ideas arising from this study. First, it would be interesting to examine the relation between reporting frequency of fund holdings and mutual fund management fees. Regulators and investors call for more transparency in the determination of mutual fund pricing. A future study could test whether the enhanced portfolio disclosure lowers mutual fund fees. Second, some funds are disclosing their holdings information more actively than required (e.g., Cathie Wood). Why do some fund managers want to use holdings disclosure as a marketing tool while others want to keep their strategy secretly? We have little understanding on their different voluntary disclosure choices. A future research project examines the benefits and costs of fund managers’ voluntary disclosure of fund management.

15505820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505820.value: While a substantial amount of investors’ money is managed by mutual fund managers, most of general investors are only able to track the components of their mutual fund holdings only periodically, such as quarterly in the U.S. As such, since fund mangers’ activities are not fully observable, they are often believed to engage in opportunistic trading activities to disguise their true performance. Utilizing the recent portfolio disclosure rule change in the U.S. (Investment Reporting Modernization rules), we examine whether shortening the reporting interval of fund holdings (from quarterly to monthly) deters fund mangers’ opportunistic behavior. Furthermore, this setting is particularly interesting, in that the newly reported monthly holdings information will be only viewable to the SEC, not to the public, which makes it easier for a researcher to distinguish the disciplinary role of regulators from that of investors. Our empirical analysis finds that there is no significant change in portfolio pumping and window dressing following the adoption of Investment Reporting Modernization rules. This suggests that in spite of the new information available, the regulators alone might not be effectively monitoring fund managers.

15506520.label: Realisation of objectives
15506520.value: Addressing Objective 1, we find that the implied skewness obtained from options that cover the FOMC (Federal Reserve Open Market Committee) announcement day tend to be higher than the implied skewness of similar options that mature just before and do not cover the announcement day. This result is consistent with the market anticipating the Fed to take accommodative actions if market stress arises—removing some of the tail risks from the return distribution ex ante. We also find that this pre-announcement increase in option-implied skewness exhibits a significant difference across firms, and is related to a firm’s announcement-day return premium. Addressing Objective 2, we interpret a firm’s pre-announcement increase in option-implied skewness as the firm’s Fed put exposure (FPE) anticipated by the market ex ante. We find that the FPE premium cannot be explained by a stock’s market beta, co-skewness beta, or co-kurtosis beta. These results suggest that a stock’s exposure to higher-order market risks cannot explain its FPE premium on FOMC announcement days. Addressing Objectives 3 and 4, we find that FPE commands a positive price of risk: firms with higher FPE earn a higher announcement-day return premium. This finding suggests that the Fed put is viewed as a source of risk by option market participants. Although the Fed put refers to Fed actions that aim at stabilizing market stress, such actions are neither guaranteed nor explicitly spelled out—causing the Fed put itself to be a source of risk to the financial market. In a similar analysis on a cross section of country-level stock index options, we also detect a positive price of risk for a country's exposure to US monetary policy. In the case of Hong Kong, we detect no significant change in its exposure to US monetary policy and the price of FPE over time. In the foreign exchange market, we examine how currency returns vary over the FOMC cycle. We find that a currency's reaction to US monetary policy is moderated by anchoring biases. A surprise US interest rate hike (cut) leads to a strengthening of the USD (foreign currency) relative to the foreign currency (USD) - but this adjustment process is delayed when the currencies in question are near their 52-week extremes. Consistent with investors suffering from anchoring bias, they become reluctant to further bid up the value of high-interest-rate currencies that are already near their 52-week high, or to further bid down the value of low-interest-rate currencies that are already near their 52-week low. This delay in the exchange rate adjustment process causes high-interest-rate (low-interest-rate) foreign currencies to continue to appreciate (depreciate) following a surprise US rate cut (hike). To obtain more precise estimates of the price of US monetary policy exposure of non-US economies, we have moved beyond using only stock and option prices at the country index level. We now examine non-US, firm-level data, estimate the beta of a foreign firm’s stock return to unexpected US interest rate changes, and link the cross-sectional variation in this exposure to different firm characteristics.

15506520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15506520.value: We find that the FOMC-announcement-day return premium earned by a firm is positively related to the increase in its ex ante, option-implied skewness prior to the announcement. This finding is consistent with: (1) the existence of an announcement-day Fed put that is partially anticipated by the financial market; (2) the pre-announcement increase in a firm’s option-implied skewness being a proxy for its Fed put exposure (FPE); and (3) FPE commanding a positive price of risk. High (low) FPE firms are those firms whose preannouncement increase in option-implied skewness is the largest (smallest). We find that high (low) FPE firms indeed experience a larger (smaller) increase in their realized skewness and 5% conditional value at risk (CVaR) on announcement days. Using aggregate implied skewness measured right after the FOMC announcement as a proxy for the strength of the realized announcement-day Fed put, we verify that the announcement-day returns of high FPE firms indeed exhibit greater sensitivities to the Fed put. We also find that the announcement premium earned by high relative to low FPE firms tend to increase when the level of VIX is high or when one-month-lagged market return is low, consistent with the Fed put being more valuable to market participants during these times. These results are reported in the paper titled, "Stock Return Skewness and the Cross Section of Monetary Policy Announcement Premiums". We find that a currency's reaction to US monetary policy is moderated by investors’ anchoring biases. A surprise US interest rate hike (cut) leads to a strengthening of the USD (foreign currency) relative to the foreign currency (USD) - but this adjustment process is delayed when the currencies in question are near their 52-week extremes. Consistent with investors suffering from anchoring bias, they become reluctant to further bid up the value of high-interest-rate currencies that are already near their 52-week high, or to further bid down the value of low-interest-rate currencies that are already near their 52-week low. This delay in the exchange rate adjustment process causes high-interest-rate (low-interest-rate) foreign currencies to continue to appreciate (depreciate) following a surprise US rate cut (hike). Motivated by this finding, the paper titled "Anchoring Bias and Predictable Returns in the Foreign Exchange Market" evaluates the economic significance of such biases and constructs trading strategies to profit from them.

15506520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15506520.value: To obtain more precise estimates of the price of US monetary policy exposure of non-US economies, we propose to move beyond using only stock and option prices at the country index level. We now examine non-US, firm-level data, estimate the beta of a foreign firm’s stock return to unexpected US interest rate changes, and link the cross-sectional variation in this exposure to different firm characteristics. In addition to characteristics that previous studies have identified to affect a domestic firm’s monetary policy exposure, such as cashflow duration, cashflow volatility, financial constraints, cash holdings, and operating profitability, we also examine the possible impact from a foreign firm’s reliance of USD-denominated loans. The cost of capital of firms with greater dependence on USD debt may be more affected by US monetary policy.

15506520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15506520.value: Although there is a long literature that examines the effect of monetary policy on the stock market, studies on the relationship between monetary policy and stock return skewness are relatively scarce. We find supportive evidence for the existence of the “Fed put”—the Federal Reserve undertakes accommodative actions in response to economic and financial stress. Even though the Fed is expected by the market to act when needed, such actions are neither guaranteed nor explicitly spelled out—the Fed put is not a formal contract after all. As such, the Fed put itself can be a source of risks. These expectations and risks affect both stock and option prices prior to the FOMC (Federal Reserve Open Market Committee) announcement. We find that US monetary policy affects exchange rates, but the impact is moderated by investors’ anchoring biases. A surprise US interest rate hike (cut) leads to a strengthening of the USD (foreign currency) relative to the foreign currency (USD) - but this adjustment process is delayed when the currencies in question are near their 52-week extremes. Our results show that, even in the foreign exchange market, which is dominated by professional investors, behavioral biases are still prevalent.

15507320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507320.value: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced tremendous growth in the past decade. At the end of 2018, worldwide ETF total net assets reach US$4.7 trillion. ETFs are a convenient way for retail and institutional investors seeking to gain from the exposures to broad markets, sectors, or factors. The advantages of ETFs include easy diversification, low expense ratio, low trading cost, and tax efficiency. Although ETFs have attracted a lot of attention from media, investors, and regulators and become one of the retail investors’ preferred choices for long-term investment, academic research is still at its infant stage. Most academic studies focus on the impacts of equity ETF ownership on the underlying stocks’ price efficiency, return volatility, liquidity, and mispricing. Several new factor models have been recently developed. However, many of these new factors are motivated by anomaly variables, which are pronounced mostly among small growth stocks. All studies use characteristic-sorted (long only or long-short) portfolios to compare the performance of these new models and find that these new models, especially behavioral models, clearly outperform the Fama-French three-factor model. However, these portfolios, especially long-short portfolios, are costly and difficult for investors to replicate or implement. Moreover, whether the outperformance of these new models and their relative ranking extend to ETFs is still unknown. ETFs by nature are well diversified, so what matter the most are probably systematic risks. The first objective of this proposal is to use ETFs to assess the performance of these new factor models. The benefit of using ETFs is that it not only serves as an out-of-sample test, but we can also use fund flows to assess which is the best model investors use (Berk and van Binsbergen 2016). The second objective is to explore whether price, return, volume, and short interest related anomalies discovered in stocks extend to ETFs. This also serves as an out-of-sample test and if the answer is yes, we can alleviate the criticism of p-hacking by Harvey (2017). Moreover, these ETF anomalies may motivate the foundation for the construction of new factors based on technical analysis, which in contrast to the practice that almost all new factors are constructed from fundamental variables. The results from this project will not only contribute to the literature on empirical asset pricing tests using ETFs as out-of-sample test assets, but also offer valuable guidance to global and domestic ETF investors, especially retail investors. 交易所交易基金（ETF）在過去十年中經歷了巨大的增長。截至2018年底，全球ETF總淨資產達到4.7萬億美元。ETF是尋求從廣闊的市場，部門或因素中獲利的散戶和機構投資者的便捷方式。ETF的優點包括易於分散，費用率低，交易成本低和稅收效率高。儘管ETF吸引了媒體，投資者和監管機構的廣泛關注，並成為散戶投資者長期投資的首選之一，但學術研究仍處於起步階段。大多數學術研究都集中於股票ETF所有權對標的股票的價格效率，收益波動率，流動性和定價錯誤的影響。 最近開發了幾種新的因子模型。但是，許多這些新因子是由股票收益表現異常變量激發的，這些股票收益表現異常變量在小型成長型股票中尤為明顯。所有研究都使用特徵分類的投資組合（僅做多或做空）來比較這些新模型的性能，發現這些新模型（尤其是行為模型）明顯優於Fama-French三因子模型。但是，這些投資組合，特別是多空投資組合，成本高昂，並且投資者難以復製或實施。此外，這些新模型的出色表現及其相對排名是否擴展到ETF尚不清楚。ETF本質上具有很好的多樣性，因此最重要的可能是系統性風險。本提案的第一個目標是使用ETF來評估這些新因子模型的性能。使用ETF的好處在於，它不僅可以作為樣本外測試，而且我們還可以利用資金流來評估哪種模型是投資者使用的最佳模型（Berk and van Binsbergen 2016）。 第二個目標是探討在股票中發現的與價格，回報，交易量和與空頭量相關的股票收益表現異常變量是否擴展到ETF。這也可以作為樣本外測試，如果答案是肯定的，我們可以減輕Harvey（2017）對p-hacking的批評。此外，這些ETF收益表現異常現象可能會為基於技術分析的新因素的構建提供動力，而這與幾乎所有新因素都是由基本變量構成的實踐形成對比。 本項目的結果不僅會為使用ETF作為樣本外測試資產定價模型測試提供文獻資料，而且還將為全球和國內ETF投資者（尤其是散戶投資者）提供有價值的指導。

15507320.label: Realisation of objectives
15507320.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to assess the performance of newly developed asset pricing models using the flows of global equity ETFs; and (ii) to explore whether the market-based anomalies discovered in stocks extend to equity ETFs. Our results in general have clearly achieved the objectives of the proposal. First, using a large sample of global stock returns, we find that several market-based characteristic variables including historical fund returns, past fund flow, fund size, and salience bias are strong predictors of future returns on ETFs. However, the predictability of fund characteristics is not consistent across different regions. A conditional latent risk factor model (i.e., instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA)) performs much better in capturing variation in ETF returns both in sample and out of sample than conventional models with pre-specified factors. Expected returns according to the IPCA model give more precise prediction for realized ETF returns. A large fraction of the long-term momentum effect in developed ETF markets can be explained by the IPCA model, whereas it is puzzling by other prominent asset pricing models. However, the short-term reversal effect in the ex-U.S. developed regions is difficult to be reconciled by any models. Overall, our results shed light on the importance of introducing dynamic factor loadings and latent risk factors to better understand the risk and return properties of the passively managed portfolios. It is clearly that we have achieved the second objective of the project (ii). Second, we use the response of ETF flows to various factor model-adjusted returns to infer how ETF investors evaluate risk by taking into account the special features of EFTs. We find that the market-adjusted return (MAR) is the best predictor for subsequent ETF flows. The relative performance is related to the features and trading activities unique to ETFs. The superior performance of the MAR over the CAPM is mainly concentrated among ETFs with active short selling, high tax efficiency, and high tracking errors, and is robust to controlling for Morningstar Ratings. It is clearly that we have achieved the first objective of the project (i). In another paper, I also completed a paper partially related to this GRF project, which is also associated with the risk and return trade-off in the Chinese A-share market. Our research questions are: (i) are the anomalies discovered in the U.S. market replicable in the Chinese A-share market and (ii) which model performs the best in explaining the significant anomalies in the Chinese market. We find that 83.4% of the anomaly variables do not generate significant high-minus-low quintile raw return spreads in China. We show that the conventional procedure using all A-share breakpoints with equal-weighted returns for the anomaly test is indeed problematic, as it assigns too much weight to microcaps and has a very limited investment capacity. Finally, we find that the Chinese version of the three-factor model (Liu, Stambaugh, and Yuan, 2019) and the q-factor model show the best performance over the whole sample period. The q-factor model is the best performer in the post-2007 subsample period, after significant improvements occurred in China’s financial market environment, such as the completion of the split-share structure reform and the implementation of new accounting standards conforming to the IFRS. It is clearly that we have enhanced the achievement of the second objective of the project (ii) using the Chinese stock market data. The results are summarized in three papers. The paper on “What drives exchange-traded fund flows? The role of ETFs’ special features” has been presented in many international academic conferences, including the 2022 Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) held at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsinchu, Taiwan on May 13~14, 2022, the 2022 Asian Finance Association (Asian FA) conference in Hong Kong on June 27~29, 2022, and the 2022 China International Conference in Finance (CICF), Virtual, on July 6-9, 2022. We plan to submit the paper to Management Science. The paper on “Modelling equity exchange-traded funds: International evidence” is ready for submission to a top-tier finance journal. We plan to submit it to Review of Financial Studies. The paper on “Replicating and digesting anomalies in the Chinese A-share market” has been accepted for publication at Management Science (2023). Overall, the outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

15507320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507320.value: Our major findings are as follows: (1) Using the response of ETF flows to past risk-adjusted returns as a measure of investor preference to a particular asset pricing model, we find that the market-adjusted return (MAR) is the best performer. Moreover, the superior performance of the MAR over the CAPM is mainly concentrated among ETFs with active short selling, high tax efficiency, and high tracking errors, and is robust to controlling for Morningstar Ratings. The results suggest that because ETFs are passive funds, investors in general appear not to care about risk, especially for those with special features unique to EFTs. (2) Using a large sample of global stock returns, we find that a few market-based characteristic variables are strong predictors of future returns on ETFs. We also find that a conditional latent risk factor model based on IPCA outperforms other existing asset pricing models in capturing variation in ETF returns. The results suggest that it is very important to incorporate dynamic factor loadings and latent risk factors to understand the risk and return properties of the passively managed portfolios. (3) We find that a majority of anomaly variables documented in the U.S. do not generate significant high-minus-low raw return spreads in China. The Chinese version of the three-factor model (i.e., market, size, and value factors) and the q-factor model are the best performers over the whole sample period, whereas the q-factor model is the best in the post-2007 subsample period when China’s financial market environment has improved significantly, including the completion of the split-share structure reform and the implementation of new accounting standards conforming to the IFRS. The above major findings are detailed in the following three papers (updated): 1. K.C. John Wei,* and Linti Zhang, 2024, “What drives exchange-traded fund flows? The role of ETFs’ special features?” ready for submission to Management Science. 2. K.C. John Wei,* and Linti Zhang, 2024, “Modelling equity exchange-traded fund returns: International evidence” ready for submission to Review of Financial Studies. 3. Zhibing Li, Laura Xiaolei Liu,* Xiaoyu Liu, and K.C. John Wei, 2023, Replicating and digesting anomalies in the Chinese A-shares market, Management Science, forthcoming,

15507320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507320.value: We find that investors’ flows in and flows out of equity EFTs in general respond to the EFT past market-adjusted return, especially for those with special features unique to equity ETFs. In contrast, for other EFTs, investors’ trading tend to respond to the past fund performance based on the CAPM. We also find anomalies in the equity ETF market and these anomalies are associated with ETF market-based characteristic variables. Importantly, these anomalies are better explained by an IPCA factor model and not the existing prominent factor models. The potential for further development of the research centers on whether these findings in the equity ETFs extend to the bond ETFs. While most corporate bonds are not very liquid, bond ETFs are in general much more liquid than the underlying bonds. Therefore, the empirical findings of the bond ETFs would be more interesting and meaningful from the practical application point of view than equity ETFs.

15507320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507320.value: What drives equity exchange-traded fund flows? Do there exist any profitable trading strategies in the equity ETF market? If yes, which is the best asset pricing model to explain these anomies in the ETF market? In this project, we explore these interesting and important research questions. We find that investors in general trade in and out of an ETF based on its past performance measured by the market-adjusted returns, especially for those funds with special features unique to ETFs such as active short selling, high tax efficiency, and high tracking errors. We also find that historical fund returns, past fund flow, fund size, and salience bias are strong predictors of future returns on ETFs. These ETF anomalies can be best explained by a dynamic factor model based on instrumented principal component analysis.

15507720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15507720.value: 做中學習：金融分析師團隊的啟示

15507720.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15507720.value: Prof Yu, Fang Frank Prof Yu, Xiaoyun

15507720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507720.value: As an important type of financial intermediary, financial analysts publish their research to express their opinions on the future earnings, valuation, and corporate events of the firms under coverage. Extensive research effort has been spent on understanding the forecasting behaviour of analysts and how it is driven by the their personal traits. While the majority of analyst forecasts are provided by a team of analysts, the existing research provides little evidence on the role of teams in shaping the forecasting behaviour and career development of individual analysts. In this proposal, we try to understand whether the characteristics of a lead analyst in the team have any impact on the career development and reporting behaviour of non-lead analysts (also known as associate or junior analysts). Based on the analyst reports, we can identify the lead analyst, shown first on the list of authors, and the associate analysts, shown after the lead. An analyst report should reflect the opinions of the lead analyst, who is ultimately responsible for the quality of the report and the performance of the team. The associate analysts take responsibilities of preparing for analytical models and reports, under the guidance of the lead analyst. Which lead analysts provide more learning opportunities that eventually benefit the junior analysts’ career? We will focus on two dimensions of the characteristics of lead analysts: professional quality and personal traits. We will then examine whether these two dimensions affect the career of associate analysts, specifically, the likelihood of being promoted to a lead position in a team, the first milestone in their career development. We believe our research can make multiple contributions to the literature. First, our research examines a fundamental question of how analysts build their human capital. Different from prior work which attributes analysts’ human capital to their own characteristics, we study how analysts learn from a leader in a team environment. Second, when examining an analyst’s career development, most research relies on the less frequent move made by analysts across different financial institutions. Based on our hand-collected data, we can directly identify the first milestone in their career advancement, that is, whether an analyst is promoted from associate to lead analyst in a team. Lastly, we hope to contribute additional evidence to the literature of learning which has been found extensively in firms, financial intermediaries, and mergers and acquisitions.

To investigate which of the two plausible explanations, overreaction or the liquidity effect, is more relevant to reversal profitability across countries. 15507920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507920.value: Short-term reversal refers to the observation that stocks performing the worse (best) in the prior month tend to perform well in the coming month. This phenomenon is found in equity markets worldwide (Griffin, Kelly, and Nardari, 2010). There are two plausible explanations for short-term reversal. The first is overreaction. Investors may overreact to news because their beliefs are affected by cognitive errors. Hence, stock prices may be momentary deviated from their fundamental values and these pricing errors are corrected in the near future (Cooper, 1999; Mase, 1999; Subrahmanyam, 2005). The second is the liquidity effect. When liquidity providers have positive excess inventory, they tend to quote prices below the fundamental value so as to encourage buy orders and discourage sell orders. Stock prices return to their intrinsic values when these inventory imbalances vanish (Jegadeesh and Titman, 1995; Campbell, Grossman, and Wang, 1993; Avramov, Chordia, and Goyal, 2006; Cheng, Hameed, Subrahmanyam, and Titman, 2017). Prior studies use US data to disentangle overreaction from the liquidity effect and the evidences are mixed. To the best of our knowledge, the determinants for the cross-country variation of short-term reversal remain unexplored. This study aims at filling this gap. Furthermore, this study also attempt to find out which of the two explanations is more relevant to the cross-country variation of short-term reversal. Hence, findings of this study shed light on which of the two prominent explanations underpins short-term reversal. We classify possible determinants into three categories. First, institutions enhance information flow. Second, factors facilitate arbitrage activities. Third, cultural values relates to cognitive biases. Since short-term reversal arises from persistent mispricing of assets, we expect short-term reversal is weaker in markets with faster information flow and a lower cost of arbitrage. Cultural value individualism is a measure for overconfidence and we expect a positive relation between individualism and short-term reversal. However, the theoretical relation between short-term reversal and uncertainty avoidance, another cultural value, is uncertain. To untangle overreaction and the liquidity effect, we calculate short-term reversal using residual returns. According to Da, Liu, and Schaumburg (2014), if a determinant is related to the returns on the long (short) side of residual return reversal strategy, then this determinant is more likely related to the liquidity effect (overreaction). Besides, motivated by Cheng et al. (2017), we use active institutions as a measure for the liquidity effect and reexamine cross-country variation of short-term reversal while controlling for active institutions. 當月股票股價做好(差)的股票往往在下一個月的表現會較差(好)。這現象稱為股票收益反轉現象。這現象現時有兩個普遍接受的解釋。一. 反應過度理論: 投資者對好(壞)消息反應過度，導致股價高於(低於)應有價值，股票價格在下個月回復到原本應有價值因而導致股價反轉。二. 流動性理論:當大量沽盤(買盤)出現，買家(賣家)為了減少存貨風險故調低買入價格(調高賣出價格)。股價在下個月反回應有價值而導致股價反轉。雖然這股票收益反轉現象在不同國家都被發現但其強度在不同國家有著顯著的分別。到目前為止還沒有任何研究去解釋為何股票收益反轉現象在不同國家會有不同表現。本研究透過檢視不同國家的制度及文化背景去解釋股票收益反轉現象。國家制度影響資訊質量及其流通速度，亦影響市場對沖效率。資訊質量越好、流通速度越快、市場對沖效率越高、則股票收益反轉現象越弱。此外，文化影響到投資者的認知。過往研究發現在個人主義文化薰陶下的投資者往往對資訊反應過度，故此個人主義越強的國家這股票收益反轉現象則越明顯。本研究除了對跨國股票收益現象的成因作出探討也嘗試利用不同的制度及文化去探究這一股票收益反轉現象的主要成因是投資者反應過度還是因為市場流動性不足導致。

15507920.label: Realisation of objectives
15507920.value: The main objective of this research is to understand the drivers of short-term reversal around the world. This main objective is completely achieved using firm-level data. We document that firm characteristics are the main drivers of short-term reversal across world regions. Among the characteristics examined, return volatility and momentum provide the most robust predictions on short-term reversal worldwide. Short-term reversal in Asia Pacific is more significant than in Europe because stock returns in Asia Pacific are more volatile than in Europe and momentum in Asia Pacific is weaker than in Europe. There are three auxiliary objectives. First, to investigate which two explanations, investor sentiment or liquidity provision is more relevant to short-term reversal worldwide. This objective is completely achieved. We find that short-term reversal is more affected by pessimistic investor sentiment than limited liquidity provision. Second, to investigate if liquidity provision by institutional investors is a major determinant of short-term reversal. This objective is completely achieved. We find that an increase in the number of active institutions attenuates short-term reversal. This finding is consistent with the conjecture that institutional investors provide more liquidity for stocks which in turn reduces short-term momentum on these stocks. Third, to examine how formal and informal institutions affect short-term reversal across countries. Only 50% of this objective is achieved. Evidence from our analysis is mixed and not conclusive. Further analysis is required to complete this objective.
