15507920.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507920.value: 1. Short-term reversals are pervasive worldwide. The Asia Pacific countries have the largest short-term reversal, while European countries have the least. 2. We find that short-term reversal worldwide is more related to pessimistic investor sentiment than limited liquidity provision. 3. In contrast to the common belief, the relationship between firm size and short-term reversal is weak. Book-to-market ratio, share illiquidity, return volatility, and residual analyst coverage strengthen short-term reversal, while share turnover, analyst coverage, predicted analyst coverage, and momentum weaken it. 4. Predicted analyst coverage attenuates short-term reversal, while residual analyst coverage strengthens it. This finding is consistent with the roles played by analysts. 5. Excess analyst coverage is likely concentrated in undervalued stocks rather than in overvalued stocks. Moreover, analysts are more able to find out undervalued stocks in developed countries instead of in developing countries. These findings are consistent with the prediction of Lee and So (2017) while they are inconsistent with the prediction of Doukas et al. (2005). 6. Momentum has a significant negative effect on short-term reversal. This finding provides support to the theory proposed by Jegedeesh et al. (2023). 7. Among all the firm characteristics, return volatility and momentum give the most robust predictions on short-term reversal. The above findings are discussed in the working paper titled “What drives short-term reversal around the world?”. 8. Short-term reversals become more profound in the current month when economic policy uncertainty is larger in the prior month. There is evidence that economic policy uncertainty influences return reversals through the liquidity channel. This finding is discussed in the paper titled “Economic Policy Uncertainty and short-term reversals”. It is forthcoming in the Handbook of Investment Analysis, Portfolio Management, and Financial Derivatives, World Scientific. 9. The predictability of economic policy uncertainty on short-term reversals is stronger among stocks exposed more to the volatility index (VIX) and economic policy uncertainty index (EPU). This finding is discussed in the paper titled “Economic Policy Uncertainty, short-term reversals, and investor sentiment”. It is published in Review of Pacific Basin Financial Markets and Policies 26 (2023). 10. Short-term reversal is substantial among the most illiquid stocks in India. This finding is discussed in the paper titled “Momentum, reversals, and liquidity: Indian evidence”. It is published in Pacific Basin Finance Journal 82 (2023). 11. An increase in the number of active institutions attenuates short-term reversal. This finding will be incorporated into the working paper mentioned above.

15507920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507920.value: Short-term reversal is pervasive and economically significant worldwide. The reversal strategy generates an average monthly return of 1.6% in a sample consisting of all countries. The Asia Pacific countries have the largest short-term reversal of 1.9% per month, while European countries have the least short-term reversal of 1.1% per month. In contrast to the common belief, the firm size on short-term reversal is weak. Book-to-market ratio, share illiquidity, return volatility, and residual analyst coverage strengthen short-term reversal, while share turnover, analyst coverage, predicted analyst coverage, momentum, and change in active institutional investors weaken it. Overall, return volatility and momentum are the most robust predictors for short-term reversal. Our findings are consistent with investor sentiment and liquidity provision explanations of short-term reversal. However, short-term reversal is more significant following negative returns than positive returns. This evidence indicates that pessimistic investor sentiment exerts a larger effect on short-term reversal than limited liquidity provision.

15508320.label: Project Objectives
15508320.value: Construct a tractable dynamic principal-agent model in which agents have perfect information about their own periodical outputs but are uninformed about their rival's periodical outputs. Derive best responses in terms of efforts and use them to identify the Nash equilibrium solutions. Reveal insights about the relationship between tournament durations and the agents' incentives for effort investments. The basic model involves discretized decision and random variables. 15508320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508320.value: Principals often have problems in monitoring their agents' efforts. Tournaments provide an efficient way of dealing with such situations by rewarding winner prizes to agents with the highest outputs. The competition for promotion among executives and academics is a classic example. Consider the one-day competitions initiated by Citadel, a hedge fund, as another example. In these competitions, students can win job interviews and the permission to join a yearly final event in which they can win 100,000 USD. The proposed study analyzes whether one-day competitions with relatively low winner prizes or less frequent, for instance, two-day competitions with increased winner prizes could produce stronger incentives for effort investments. This study belongs to a strand of the literature which deals with dynamic tournaments. An innovative feature of the proposed model is that agents observe their own periodical outputs but not their rivals’ periodical outputs. This is a realistic feature for salespersons, insurance broker and consultants etc.. The analysis will reveal insights about the optimal duration of tournaments. To our knowledge, optimal durations have not been studied in the context of tournaments until now. We therefore consider this analysis as the main literature contribution of the proposed study. Preliminary results indicate that longer tournaments can indeed provide stronger incentives to invest in efforts than a corresponding number of short tournaments. The proposed analysis consists of two main modules and each main module consists of several submodules. The first main module is considering a discretized basic model version with two periods, two identical agents, stochastic first-period outputs and deterministic second-period outputs. This error term structure is rich enough to study agents who can observe their own periodical outputs but not their rival’s periodical output. However, it is also complicated enough to justify, for tractability reasons, the consideration of discrete decision and noise variables. Extensions of the discretized basic model version consider asymmetric agents and periods. The second main module considers continuous decision variables and noise variables to test the robustness of the results derived based on the discretized model version and to develop new insights on the fundamental sources driving optimal tournament durations. 由于委托人常常很难监控其代理人的努力程度，锦标赛通过奖励产出最高的代理人，为此提供了一种有效的应对方式。企业职业管理人和科研院校研究人员的晋升竞争就是一个范例。另一个例子是对冲基金Citadel发起的一日竞赛。通过这些竞赛，学生可以赢得求职面试的机会，同时可获得参加年度决赛的许可，并在决赛中可能赢得100,000美元的奖金。拟议的研究旨在分析奖励相对较低的一日竞赛或是，比如说，奖励增加但频率较低的两日竞赛，哪种激励机制更有效。 本项目属于动态锦标赛文献研究的范畴。其创新点在于代理人只能观察自己的在各个时段内的产出，而不能观察竞争对手的产出。对于销售人员，保险经纪人和咨询顾问等而言，这是一个现实的设定。这一分析将揭示关于锦标赛最佳时长的见解。据我们所知，现有文献尚未研究锦标赛的最佳时长。因此，我们认为对最佳锦标赛时长的分析是本研究的主要贡献。初步结果表明，与相应数量的短期锦标赛相比，更长的锦标赛可以更好地激励代理人投入更多的努力。 拟议的分析包括两个主要模块。第一个主要模块考虑离散的基本模型。该模型包括两个时段，两个相同的代理人，随机的第一时段产出和确定的第二时段产出。此随机结构足以研究代理人可以观察到自己的产出但不能观察其竞争对手产出的情况。然而，从易处理性的角度，它也足够复杂，证实了考虑离散的决策和产出的合理性。离散化的基本模型将进一步扩展到考虑不对称的代理人和时段的情况。第二个主要模块将考虑连续的决策和产出，以测试离散模型结果的稳健性，并对最佳锦标赛时长的根本驱动因素提供新见解。

15508320.label: Realisation of objectives
15508320.value: Objectives 1 and 2: Our problem involves agents who choose effort over two periods. As an example, think of a football game in which the players play two half times. The football game example is useful because it can serve us as a contrasting example for what we do. More specifically, when football players go into half time, they know their own team’s score as well as the other team’s score. This is different in the problem we analyze. We assume that agents know their own output after “halftime” but not(!) their rival’s “halftime” output. We believe that this better reflects the reality of, for example, data science competitions. We distinguish between a long tournament that goes over two periods versus two short tournaments each going over only one period. The problematic case is the long tournament. This is because our modelling choice regarding the information structure has strong implications for tractability. For illustration, consider the scenario in which the second-period outputs are deterministic for both agents and “halftime” outputs are public information. In this case, the rival agent’s second-period output depends on its half-time output and second-period efforts. Deriving the best responses requires optimizing own efforts for each feasible second-period effort level of the rival conditional on the halftime difference in scores. This resembles the football game example. By contrast, consider our case in which the rival agent’s “halftime” output is private information in the sense that the exact value is only known by the rival. In this case, deriving the best responses requires optimizing own efforts for each feasible second-period effort level of the rival conditional on the halftime difference in scores which now is stochastic. This creates an optimization problem which poses great challenges for the analysis. For the sake of tractability, our study focuses on situations where both the efforts and random terms are discrete. We solve various versions of such a discrete framework by deriving best responses and identify equilibrium solutions proving the tractability. Objectives 3 and 4: We have solved discrete framework for four scenarios by distinguishing between symmetric and asymmetric periods as well as symmetric and asymmetric agents. Symmetry versus asymmetry is always modelled in terms of the number of noise terms involved. The case of asymmetric agents involves one agent with stochastic and one agent with deterministic outcomes. The case of asymmetric periods involves a first period with stochastic outputs and a second period with deterministic outputs. Altogether, the scenarios involve one (asymmetric and asymmetry), two (asymmetry combined with symmetry), or four (symmetry and symmetry) noise terms. The results show that equilibrium efforts and the relative performance of the long tournament versus two short tournaments depend very much on agent asymmetry. For the case of agent symmetry, we found that the long tournament creates stronger incentives to invest in effort than two short tournaments although the tournaments are getting closer to each other in terms of incentives when periods are asymmetric. For the case of agent asymmetry, we found the opposite result, that is, that the long tournament creates weaker incentives to invest in effort than two short tournaments which is especially true in the case of period asymmetry. We looked beyond the discrete framework and developed a model involving continuous variables. We use this part to illustrate the difficulties associated with the consideration of continuous variables justifying the importance of the discrete framework in terms of tractability.

15508320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15508320.value: The project has supported five studies. One is already published in Transportation Research Part A (TRA). Another is in the second round of the review process in Economics of Transportation (EoT). A third is in the first round of the review process in Journal of Air Transport Management (JATM). According to our assessment, the other two papers still need some further work before they will be ready for submission. Especially, this is true for the study related to tournament durations; the detailed explanations on our ideas for additional efforts help to further improve the contribution of this study are described in “6.2 Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action extensions.” Finally, the project has led to one PhD thesis (Zhang, H., 2023) and five presentations (four conferences, one research seminar). The corresponding studies involve theoretical and empirical contributions. These contributions are related to tournament durations and information structures (Czerny, Song, work in progress). They are further related to other transport problems involving congestion management (Lang and Czerny, 2023, TRA), resilient airline schedules (Brueckner, Czerny and Gaggero, JATM), the effect of airline competition on intertemporal price dispersion (Zhang (PhD student), Czerny, van Ommeren, Niemeier, 2021, 2nd round EoT), and the emerging role of Gulf carriers for competition in long-distance markets (Zhang (PhD student), Chen, Czerny, van Ommeren, Porta, Zheng; work in progress).

15508320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15508320.value: We have identified the following avenues for future research: 1) We have compared the incentives created by two short tournaments versus one long tournament. Moving from two short tournaments to one lone tournament changes, first, the tournament duration. Second, it changes the information structure because only in the case of one long tournament it matters that agents cannot observe their rival’s performance at the end of the first period. To clearly attribute the change in the incentives to the tournament duration and information structure, an additional scenario in which agents have information about their own and(!) their rival’s outcomes at the end of the first period even during the long tournament will be considered. The outcomes will serve as a new benchmark. 2) Our analysis concentrated on positive productivity shocks. In this sense, stochasticity does two things at once. It increases uncertainty and it increases agent productivity because, for given efforts, expected outcomes are higher in the case of stochastic outcomes. To disentangle the effect of uncertainty and productivity on incentives, we will look at noise terms with zero expected values. 3) Most importantly, we consider employing an experimental setting to empirically test our theoretical results.

15508320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15508320.value: In production, principals rely on their agents’ efforts in producing outputs. The problem is that efforts cannot be measured directly. Therefore, writing a contract on efforts is not a practical approach. Instead, principals incentivize agents by relying on tournaments in which agents are awarded when they stand out in terms of performance. Our study is concerned about the duration of tournaments. We consider two periods which is like many sports games such as football including a half time break. In football, teams know their own scores and those of their opponents during breaks and the game finishes when the two halftimes are over. Using the soccer example, we ask two questions. First, what if the long game with half time would be changed into two short games? Second, what if, in the long game, teams would only know their own scores but not their opponent team’s scores during half time? The second feature resembles data science competitions in which teams know their own progress but not their rival’s progress. We demonstrate that one long game can create stronger incentives to invest in efforts than two short games when teams are equally able.

15600320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600320.value: 手勢是說話者思考過程的一種表徵方式，但手勢卻常常被我們忽略。手勢的研究在二語及外語（FL）學習領域至關重要，因為語言學習者將手勢用於與語言學習有關的溝通和心理功能。然而，手勢研究在該領域和語言學上均未有代表性成果，語言學習者的手勢與其語言能力發展之間的關係仍然缺乏綜合理論基礎。 這項研究的申請書提出了首個長期的、多研究對象的、縱向的手勢與語言水平的研究。通過對外語學習中手勢的定量和定性分析，該項目將設計一個手勢與話語處理的機制模型，重點關注手勢這一動作所表達的語用和語義意義。儘管針對母語人士手勢與話語的處理機制模型（圖1）已存在，但手勢在外語學習中並未得到足夠的學術關注。此外，外語學習者手勢中的某些細節無法通過適用於母語使用者的模型來解釋。 過往的手勢研究傾向於以參照手勢為重點的語義方法（圖3），並對話語內容進行解讀；本項研究獨一無二之處，是透過手勢相對於話語內容（類型）的‘形式’ ，結合手勢的語義與語用意義（功能），對手勢進行系統地分類。研究人員將在未來三年內，收集至少40名以廣東話為母語的英語學習者的數據，並分三步分析他們的手勢。第一步、識別每個被研究者在不同外語水平下某些類型手勢的頻率；第二步、根據外語學習者的口語水平，判別被研究者的手勢與同步的話語之間，在時間及意義上的共現關係；基於前兩步的實驗數據以及分析結果，第三步、開發第一個將手勢的發展變化與口語能力發展相關聯的動態模型。 基於語言水平的手勢模型將為有效的語言教學提供一個堅實而有理據的框架，並支持在不同語言水平的情況下使用不同種類的教學方法，例如顯性教學與隱性教學。該手勢模型亦將證明現有語言學習理論的有效性，如印證學習過程的動態性或非線性。這項手勢研究的結果有潛質令香港處於外語手勢研究的領導位置，通過開發新的動態模型為手勢研究領域做出貢獻，並為外語教育者提供參考。

15600320.label: Realisation of objectives
15600320.value: The project aimed to explore the relationship between gestures and oral proficiency among Cantonese speakers learning English as a second language. The project recruited 125 participants to account for an estimated attrition rate of 40%. The project had been designed as a face-to-face study but due to the COVID pandemic sessions were carried out online. Participants joined our sessions every six months and completed various tasks, including: a brief chat about their progress in English learning over the last few months; describing a photo; discussing a topic (with someone else); watching and narrating a cartoon. This study was based on the data from the cartoon narrations only. Other data collected will be used in future studies. Not all participants were able to complete all of the sessions, therefore the number of participants varies from session to session. The last session included 50 participants online. Participants narrated the same cartoon they had narrated during session 1 (all the other sessions had used different cartoon) in English and then a second one in Cantonese. A Cantonese-English comparison study will be carried out in the future. At the end of the last session, we also carried out debriefing interviews to understand how participants perceived gestures and their functions. They also completed an online questionnaire. Between the first and second years, participants also completed a personality test. Objective 1: Correlation Between Gesture Type and Oral Proficiency The first objective was achieved through a longitudinal study with data from 44 participants. Analysis of the data on how gesture changes with proficiency did not reveal any consistent patterns, contradicting previous findings that suggest that gesture rates and type of gesture vary by proficiency. It was possible to divide our participants into those who had improved their English proficiency and those who had not improved. Among the first group there were non-significant decreases in the frequency of most types of gestures except beats (marking prosody) which increased. Among the second group there were statistically significantly fewer discursive gestures (those with a discursive pragmatic function) and more beats. We speculate that an increase in beats with proficiency might be related to a better command of prosody in English (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2022). Analysis of the data session by session, correlating it to the proficiency of the participants during that session, led to contradictory results without a clear pattern. This raises concerns about the reliability of previous gesture and proficiency studies. These results suggest that variables other than proficiency are also affecting how L2 speakers gestures. Additional research was carried out to find what those other factors might be. In particular we focused on gender, age and personality. Our sample for this sub-study was 61 Cantonese speakers who had completed the 44 question Big-Five inventory personality test. Correlations and a series of generalized linear models were developed to explore the interplay between variables. Proficiency and gender had little effect on gestures. In terms of personality, agreeableness was found to be positively correlated with semantic gestures. Contrary to the findings from previous studies, no significant relationships were found between neuroticism and adaptors or semantic gestures, nor between extraversion or openness and semantic gestures. As personality has been shown to be an important factor in gesture production in mother tongue speakers, we expected to also see a similar result with foreign language speakers, this not being so suggests that other variables, aside from those tested, should be considered. In particular, the results suggest that emotion and emotional constructs, such as anxiety, self-confidence or empathy, might have a greater impact on gesture production than proficiency or personality (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2024). To explore this possibility, we carried out debriefing interviews at the end of the project. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between language, culture, and emotional responses in gesture production, suggesting that emotional perceptions of languages/cultures modulate the gestural behaviour of bilingual speakers(Lopez-Ozieblo, under review). Objective 2: Synchronization of Gestures with Speech The second objective focused on understanding how oral proficiency influences the timing and meaning of gestures in relation to speech. The study's results indicated that proficient speakers were better at synchronizing their gestures with their speech, using gestures that matched the emotional tone and prosody, especially with beats. In less proficient speakers, beats are more likely to be used to stress each word, often positioning them in space as if visually constructing the utterance. More proficient speakers focus the stress on more salient information (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2022). We confirmed that most gestures occur with speech, including adaptors -- hand movements that traditionally had been thought not to carry meaning. However, we observed that adaptors tend to occur with disfluencies or expressions that indicate to the interlocutor that the speaker is thinking or is unsure about something. Adaptors, contrary to what we expected, increased with proficiency. Another use of adaptors seems to be to mark utterance boundaries. However, there is another factor that needs to be taken into consideration, and that is the level of engagement of the participants and their willingness to make their narrations as accurate as possible, more likely to be the case in the later sessions (in this study), which might impose a higher cognitive load on speakers leading to more adaptors. Additional work on adaptors is ongoing, after receiving departmental funding to study them. An article on adaptors is due for a special issue on non-representational gestures for the journal Language (Lopez-Ozieblo, in preparation, abstract accepted). Objective 3: Comparison with Existing Gesture-Speech Models Existing Gesture-Speech Models Traditional gesture-speech models, such as those proposed by McNeill, emphasize the integration of gestures with spoken language, suggesting that gestures serve to enhance communication by complementing or supplementing verbal messages. These models primarily focus on the cognitive aspects of gesture production, asserting that gestures are closely tied to the speaker's linguistic processes. However, our research highlights that this perspective may be too narrow, as it does not fully account for the emotional and cultural dimensions that influence gesture use among bilingual speakers. Our results indicate that while proficiency is an important factor in gesture production, it is not the only determinant. Higher proficiency speakers are likely to have developed a better speech-gesture link allowing them to focus their gestures at more salient lexical units (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2022). However, participants' emotional states significantly influenced their gestures. For example, during high-stress situations or when experiencing anxiety, even proficient speakers resorted to what seem to be inhibited gestures, we have termed these flutters (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2024). This observation aligns with the notion that emotional factors can modulate communicative effectiveness, a concept that is not adequately addressed in traditional gesture-speech models (Lopez-Ozieblo, under review). Proposal for an Integrated Dynamic Model Based on our findings, we propose an integrated dynamic model of gesture-speech interaction that incorporates changes related to language proficiency and emotional factors. Key components of this model include: Proficiency Level, Emotional Context, Cultural Influence, Dynamic Interaction.

15600320.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600320.value: Major findings derived from the three-year longitudinal research: 1. Variability in Gesture Production The study revealed that a number of internal and external factors affect gesture production. Proficiency was just one of these variables, and not the main one, others include age, personality and external factors that affect emotional responses. Participants' self-reported personality traits, such as agreeableness, correlated with their willingness to use gestures in communication (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2024). Additionally, external factors like social norms and situational contexts influenced how participants approached gesture use, indicating that both internal and external factors play a role in gestural behavior (Lopez-Ozieblo, under review). 2. Influence of Emotional Factors Emotional perceptions significantly modulate gestural behavior among bilingual speakers. Participants expressed that their feelings about using English, such as anxiety or confidence, directly influenced how they gestured during communication. For example, higher anxiety levels often led to less effective gesturing (Lopez-Ozieblo, under preparation, see above). This underscores the importance of considering emotional factors in understanding gesture production in L2 contexts, an area which has not been studied. 3. Cognitive vs. Social Functions of Gestures The study found that the cognitive function of gestures was more closely associated with the first language (L1), Cantonese, whereas the social and emotional functions were more prominent in the second language (L2), English. This indicates that as learners engage with a new language, their gestural expressions evolve to reflect not only their linguistic abilities but also their emotional engagement and social interactions within that language context. As proficiency increases, speakers' control of prosody also increases, as well as the link speech-gesture, allowing them to produce more meaning gestures (Lopez-Ozieblo, 2022). 4. Challenges in Gesture and Proficiency Studies The research raises a number of flags as the results often contradict previous findings of gesture and proficiency studies. Only a handful of longitudinal studies have been carried out to date and all with small groups of participants. In addition, gesture classifications are not always transparent, making it very difficult to duplicate or compare results across studies. We believe ours might have been one of the few studies with a larger sample and including all hand movements, such as adaptors and inhibited gestures, classifying them from a functional perspective. We expect future studies to replicate our methodology.

15600320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600320.value: The project is rich in data and will allow for additional research to be carried out. The following studies are already underway or have been approved: -In-depth analysis of the functions of adaptors gestures both in English and Cantonese. -Exploration of interactive gestures in dyadic discussions in English comparing online with face-to-face contexts (collaboration with Dr. Kosmala, University Paris-Est Creteil, France). In future, we expect to develop the following studies, using the existing corpus: -In-depth comparison of English and Cantonese narrations -In-depth comparison of English online and face-to-face narrations -In depth comparison of English narrations vs. others tasks (narrations and interviews)

15600320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600320.value: The research set out to explore how Cantonese speakers of English as a second language (L2) use gestures and how these change with proficiency. Over three years, the study involved over 100 participants who narrated stories in English based on a previously viewed video. The findings reveal that gestures are not only tied to language proficiency but are also shaped by emotions, personality, and cultural background. Aside from narrating stories, participants also completed various surveys related to the study and were recoded speaking in Cantonese as well as to an interlocutor. Participants reported that they perceived gestures as more significant in English interactions compared to Cantonese, indicating that emotional context plays a crucial role in gesture production. This highlights the complex relationship between language, culture, and emotions, suggesting that bilingual speakers adapt their gestural behavior based on their feelings about each language. The value of this research lies in its potential to enhance teaching methods for language learners by emphasizing the importance of gestures in communication. Understanding how emotional perceptions affect gesture use can lead to improved educational strategies, making language learning more effective and engaging.

15601520.value: Dr Jeong, Hyeonjeong Prof Klippel, Alexander

15601520.label: Project Objectives
15601520.value: To examine the impacts of immersive VR contexts and how learners use the rich visuo-spatial features in these contexts for acquiring perception-action based, embodied, representations. We propose to compare degree of immersiveness (VR high-immersive, VR low-immersive, and non-VR contexts) and interactivity in the VR to identify the degree to which analyses of the learning environments can lead to optimal learning conditions for second language, particularly through visual-spatial-kinesthetic rich experiences. To understand how effects of L2 learning under 3D VR contexts are modulated by individual differences in non-linguistic cognitive skills, specifically spatial abilities. We examine how individuals differing in their spatial analysis and cognitive executive function show different patterns of learning performance and behavioral response, and how VR learning may especially help individuals who have lower abilities to succeed. To identify patterns of learning behavior through interaction and movements in VR-enabled embodied contexts versus traditional learning contexts. We aim at studying how the perception-action enabled context and the corresponding visuo-spatial analyses may drive more native-like linguistic representations in the new language, as compared with paired association/translation learning methods in the traditional instructional context. To use advanced data-analytic methods including network-based analyses to tackle large-scale motion and eye-movement data from the VR learning environments. We propose to collect multimodal, continuous large-scale data and use the relevant advanced data analytics to measure the cognitive and behavioral changes across time as a result of different learning contexts and cognitive abilities. Together, our research objectives allow us to address key questions and hypotheses regarding mechanisms of language learning, spatial cognition, and individual differences. Our research will also be an important step toward linking language and cognition with digital education in a society that is increasingly dependent on cyber-enabled technology.

15601520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15601520.value: This project is designed to investigate the role of sensorimotor integration for second language (L2) learning through immersive Virtual Reality (VR) technology. The project allows us to address key scientific questions about theories of language acquisition, while building a bridge to connect language learning, spatial cognition, and digital education. Specifically, the project is aimed at identifying the role of embodied perception-action (enabled by the use of immersive VR environments) for second language learning. We develop the VR environments to promote the analysis of visuo-spatial cues, bodily interactions, and consequently sensorimotor integration in the representation of learned L2 material. In the proposed study, VR features (degree of immersiveness and interactivity) are systematically examined and compared with desktop 3D learning and traditional paired-association learning. To the extent that immersive VR can enhance learning success and cognitive representation, the proposed work will provide evidence for the utility of embodied and simulated interactions in adult L2 learning, contrasting to the lack of them in traditional L2 learning. VR-based L2 learning with rich visuo-spatial features may also lead to changes in performance patterns that can be captured by large-scale behavioral and eye-movement data collected during the learning process. Given this rich set of data, our project will further study individual differences in spatial abilities by analyzing the learner movement patterns in VR, and identifying how such differences impact language outcome and learning performance in terms of attention, memory and retention. Advanced data analytic methods including network-based analyses will be used to tackle the large-scale continuous motion and eye-movement data. Our approach to connect perception, action and cognition in a technology-driven perspective will provide crucial scientific evidence on the utility of immersive VR for second language, and at the same time will also have practical implications for future innovative technological designs for education. By exploring VR’s use for language learning, we seize a unique opportunity to connect basic research in language and cognition with practical educational outcomes. Because an ever-increasing globalized workforce has led to growing cross-cultural communications and a growing need to learn foreign languages in adulthood, findings from our project have significant implications for not just the language-learning students but also the general public and the society as a whole. 該項目旨在研究沉浸式虛擬現實（VR）技術在第二語言（L2）學習中感知覺運動整合的作用。該項目使我們能夠解決有關語言習得理論的關鍵科學問題，同時搭建連接語言學習，空間認知和網絡教育的橋樑。具體來說，該項目旨在確定第二語言學習中體現的感知行為（通過使用沉浸式VR環境實現）的作用。我們開發VR環境，以促進對視覺空間線索，身體相互作用的分析，並因此促進對L2學習材料的感覺運動整合。在提出的研究中，系統地研究VR功能（沉浸度和交互性），並將與桌面3D學習和傳統的聯想學習進行比較。就沉浸式VR可以增強學習成功和認知表示的程度而言，該課題的工作將為成人L2學習提供模擬交互效用的實證。 基於VR的L2學習具有豐富的視覺空間功能，也可能導致腦功能及結構發生變化，這些變化可以通過在學習過程中收集的大規模行為和眼動數據來捕獲。有了這些豐富的數據，我們的項目將通過分析VR中學習者的運動模式，並從注意，記憶和空間能力方面識別這種差異如何影響語言學習，來進一步研究個體差異。基於網絡分析的高級數據分析方法將用於處理大規模連續性運動和眼動的數據。 此項目以技術驅動的觀點將感知，行動和認知聯繫起來的方法，將為沈浸式VR在第二語言中的應用提供重要的科學證據，同時還將對未來的創新教育科技產生實際意義。通過探索VR在語言學習中的用途，我們抓住一個獨特的機會，將語言和認知方面的基礎研究與實際的教育成果聯繫起來。越來越多的跨文化交流導致成人學習外語的需求不斷增加，因此我們項目不僅對學習語言的學生而且對公眾和社會都具有重大意義。

15601920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15601920.value: “正常”／“異常”以及“具能”／“失能”之解構、重構或同存：在香港與英國之間建立“異”的對話

15601920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15601920.value: This proposed comparative qualitative research investigates two rigid, potent and hegemonic yet nevertheless taken-for-granted and seemingly “natural” dualisms circulating in contemporary societies. These are “normalcy”/“abnormalcy” and “ability”/“disability”; terms I introduce with quotation marks to register they are socially constructed and therefore partly contrived notions that persons and societies nevertheless live by. Although this proposed project is primarily inductive, or data-led, it begins with a sense of a problem, namely that these violent hierarchical dualisms not only obfuscate the fluidity and blurriness of, within and between, these concepts but also invalidate ways of being that deviate from a largely mythical, and relatively recent, sociocultural and discursive creation: that of the norm, or normal. While it is tempting to try to overturn binaries of normalcy/abnormalcy and ability/disability, this project instead strives to dwell with, and alongside, such terms and the experiences to which they refer, while also contriving dialogue between them, in ways that might register the fluidity that exists between them. In phase one, the project explores how normalcy/abnormalcy and ability/disability are constructed in extant cultural forms (e.g. print media, filmic representations, government documents, etc.), paying particular attention to similarities and differences in the forms they take in and between Hong Kong (hereafter, HK) and the United Kingdom (hereafter, UK) thereby contriving conceptual dialogue between these locations and the symbolic cultures therein. In phase two, the project will listen to, and document, the experiences of persons who are either labelled abnormal, or different, or who self-identify as such. The focus of this phase is on participants’ experiences and narratives of discrimination, or the identification of difference, and the ways in which such practices act as means through which persons, and identities, are validated/invalidated. Understandings of participants’ everyday lives will be derived in order to reveal how dis/ability is constituted at the mundane level of the everyday. Emerging from this part of the research will be participant-produced texts that will speak to, and perhaps against, those extant narratives explored in the first phase of the project, thereby creating further potential for conceptual dialogue. In the third phase of the project the participant-produced texts will be shared with schoolchildren, university students and the “general public” thereby opening up, or contriving, actual dialogue about abnormalcy/normalcy and ability/disability. It is intended this might produce flickers of the conscientizing potential of dialogue and novel conceptualizations of dis/ability: in contrast to the debilitating, reductive, ability/disability dichotomy. 本研究屬於質性比較研究，考察當代社會的兩個二元論：“正常”與“異常”以及“具能”與“失能”。這兩個二元論界定嚴密、廣為接受、頗具影響力，但卻常被視為理所當然。筆者在此處使用引號，意在強調這些術語是由社會性建構而來，因而在一定程度上屬於人為創造的概念，但卻是人類與社會賴以生存的概念。雖然屬於歸納／資料驅動的研究類型，本研究從具體問題入手：那些極端的等級性二元論不僅僅加劇了概念內部以及概念之間的易變性和模糊性，而且還否定了那些偏離近年來虛構式社會文化話語性創造的生存方式：那些規範的或正常的生存方式。本研究不是為了顛覆正常／異常以及具能／失能之間的二元化，而是力求詳述這些術語及其所指經歷，並通過闡釋其間的易變性為其建立對話。 在第一階段，本研究探討正常／異常以及具能／失能如何在現有的文化形式（如印刷媒體、電影、政府文檔等）中得以建構，聚焦於其在香港和英國呈現方式的異同，從而在地理位置和象徵性文化之間建立概念性對話。 在第二階段，本研究將聽取並記錄那些被認作或自認為反常或異常之人的經歷。該階段的焦點在於（1）參與者的受歧經歷和敘述，或者參與者對於異常的識別，（2）具體實踐如何使得個人和身份得到肯定或否定。此外，本研究也將解讀參與者的日常生活，從而揭露具能／失能在日常生活中的構成元素。因此，本研究將聚焦於參與者產出的文本，這些文本可能支援／反對第一階段所探討的現有敘述方式，從而進一步為建立概念性對話提供可能。 在第三階段，參與者產出的文本將分發至中小學生、大學生和“公眾”，從而展開，或者更深層地探討，關於正常／異常以及具能／失能的實際對話。這可能會使得人們認識到對話的可能並產生新的關於具能／失能的概念化方式：這些方式將異於削弱性的、簡化式的具能／失能二分法。

15602920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602920.value: Ethnic minority older adults are often an ‘invisible’ group due to a lack of attention to their unique needs, linked to systemic inequities and barriers in health and social care systems, and assumptions that they are cared for by families or will return to their home country as they age. Studies in Hong Kong have identified disparities in health outcomes and access to health information and health services in ethnic minority communities. Health and wellbeing are affected by numerous factors, including social capital. Knowledge on these correlates of health can inform the development of services and policies to reduce health disparities and promote more equitable health outcomes. South Asians are one of the largest ethnic minority populations in Hong Kong. This study seeks to identify differences in health and wellbeing and social capital within and between South Asian and Chinese older adult populations. A hypothesized conceptual framework that outlines the associations between ethnic minority status, social capital and health and wellbeing along psychosocial and material pathways will guide this study. Data collection will involve a quantitative questionnaire survey with 210 South Asian adults (including Indians, Pakistanis, and Nepalese) and 210 local Chinese adults aged 55 years and older. Qualitative in-depth narrative interviews will be conducted with 45 South Asian older adults, 45 Chinese older adults, and 15 service providers, to contextualize and triangulate the quantitative findings. Purposive samples will be recruited in five District Council areas with assistance from collaborating agencies and local NGOs. The study results will help to identify the types of social capital assets that should be targeted in developing effective community health and support programs for ethnic minority older adults in Hong Kong. A better understanding of social capital and health and wellbeing disparities among South Asian and Chinese older adults can allow community support and allied health professionals to design interventions to address and reduce these disparities. This study will lay the foundation for future research with larger samples of older ethnic minority groups in Hong Kong, building a knowledge base for the development of culturally sensitive and equitable community health and social care strategies and services. 由於少數族裔長者尋求醫療保健及社會護理服務屢遭系統性不平等的狀況和障礙，以及社會認為他們會被家庭照顧或隨著年紀漸長會回歸祖國的臆斷，少數族裔長者的特殊需求缺少社會關注，使他們成為一個經常被 「忽視 」的群體。香港的研究已發現少數族裔社羣的健康與其獲取健康資訊及衛生服務方面存在差異。健康及福祉與多重因素息息相關，這當中也包括社會資本的因素。有了對這些健康相關知識的瞭解，可以為社會服務和政策的發展提供資訊，亦可以減少健康差異並促進更公平的健康結果。 南亞裔人士是香港其中一個最大的少數族裔社羣。本次研究旨在鑒別南亞裔人士與華人之間的健康， 福祉及社會資本的差異。 本研究將以一個假設的概念框架為指導。該框架概述了少數族裔地位、社會資本、醫療健康在社會心理以及物質途徑方面的聯繫。 本研究將會採用問卷調查方法收集資料。問卷調查的對象包括210名年齡為55歲或以上的南亞裔人士（當中包括印度裔，巴基斯坦裔及尼泊爾裔人士）及210名55歲以上的本地華裔人。此外，我們還將會與45名南亞裔長者、45名華裔長者15位服務提供者進行深度訪談。所收集的資料將會與問卷調查結果作情景化及多重檢核分析。研究對象將會在機構以及本地非盈利組織的協助下，在5個區議會分區中以立意抽樣的形式招募。 本研究結果將有助於辨別在發展有效社區健康及支援專案時， 對香港少數族裔長者有利的社會資產種類， 讓社區支援和衛生專業人員更好地瞭解南亞和中國老年人之間的社會資本、健康和福祉差異，制定干預措施去解決和減少這些因素的差距。這項研究將為日後香港少數族裔長者群體研究奠定基礎，為發展跨文化敏感度、公平的社區衛生及社會護理策略服務建立知識根基。

15603420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603420.value: Research on face-to-face communication to date takes place principally in two modalities: speech between ‘normal’ speaking/hearing persons, and (tactile) sign language between hearing- and/or sight-impaired persons. Can writing serve that function? This project investigates a historically salient lingua-cultural practice in Sinographic East Asia. For hundreds of years until 1900s, East Asian literati of Literary Sinitic (wényánwén, 文言文) from today’s China, North and South Korea, Japan and Vietnam could engage in ‘silent conversation’ interactively using brush, ink and paper in cross-border communication face-to-face in the absence of a shared spoken language. Such an interactive communication pattern, called ‘Sinitic brushtalk’ or ‘brush conversation’ (筆談), remains little understood beyond or even within East Asia, despite a sizable body of historiographic documentation and detailed descriptions published in Japanese and Korean, less so in Chinese and Vietnamese. By contrast, in the vast literature of ancient civilizations elsewhere, writing as a modality of interactional cross-border communication seems unparalleled. Why was writing a viable option for literati of Sinitic, which is written with a logographic script, but not their literate counterparts well versed in other languages written with a phonographic script (e.g., Latin or Cyrillic alphabet, abjad in Arabic)? What were the material conditions that made ‘silent conversation’ possible for literati of logographic Sinitic but not other phonographic languages? Using a well-documented, contextually rich, and rigorously edited and transcribed brushtalk data source (He et al. 2010), this project addresses the above research questions by digitizing the above-mentioned transcript (ca. 8,000+ sinograms), conducting content analysis qualitatively and quantitatively, and analyzing the linguistic and sociopragmatic features of 39 dyadic interactions between three prominent brushtalkers (Sun Yat-sen 孫逸仙; Miyazaki Toten 宫崎滔天; He Shuling 何樹齡) during the 1900s. This will enable us to establish a baseline model of writing-based brush conversation in Sinitic, which to our knowledge is the third known modality of interactive communication between humans, albeit forgotten following gradual decline in sinogram-based literacy in East Asian nations. The analysis of the brushtalk dataset will address two other objectives: (i) to extract all kanji-based words that form part of the core of the ‘Meiji lexicon of modernism’, and examine their uptake trajectory in modern Chinese – the reverse flow of kanji-based ‘returned loanwords’ from Japanese to Chinese as evidenced in Chinese dictionaries and online databases; and (ii) to assess the possible impact of phonetic adaptation and semantic adaptation for disambiguation purposes when such words were coined or created in Japanese (Handel 2019). 長久以來，針對人類面對面溝通的研究，主要體現在兩個溝通模式：其一，能說話的正常人之間以言語互動溝通；其二，聾啞或弱視﹑弱聽人士之間以(觸覺)手語傳意。問題是，人類是否能以書寫方式，面對面以筆代舌或手來互動傳意呢？這研究項目旨在深入調查歷史上在東亞漢字文化圈內這廣爲人知的語言文化現象。 数百年來，直至1900年代，來自現今中﹑日﹑韓﹑越等地區，能讀能寫的東亞文人雅士可以面對面，通過筆﹑墨﹑紙，用漢文 (尤指以文言爲主要文體) 進行互動交流，達致 “無言交談” 或 “無言對話” 的效果，皆因他們沒有共同的口語。 因爲書寫的關係，歷史上留下了不少漢文筆談 (簡稱筆談) 的墨寶及相關的文獻，尤以日﹑韓居多，中﹑日較少。儘管如此，我們對筆談這溝通現象所知甚少。而與此相比，在其他古代文明社會，在跨境及跨文化交際中以書寫作爲互動溝通的媒介，則幾乎聞所未聞。 人們不敢要問，爲何以書寫爲手段進行面對面溝通互動的模式，在運用表意文字 (即漢字) 的古﹑近現代東亞社會如斯流行，而在表音文字 (如拉丁或阿拉伯語) 的文明社會則鮮有所聞。 究竟是甚麼物質條件，讓運用表意文字 (尤指以文言爲文體) 的人可達致無言對話，而表音文字的人，又是何種物質條件，令他們無意或無法以筆代舌進行互動溝通的呢？ 針對以上的研究目標，我們將以一項質素與知名度俱高，且編撰嚴謹的筆談文獻 (何大章等 2010) 爲基礎，先加以數碼化，然後進行細緻的篇章分析及量化梳理。 全文約八千字，含39篇筆談對話。筆談人士乃三位歷史人物，身份顯赫：孫逸仙 (中)， 宫崎滔天 (日)， 與何樹齡 (中)。 通過細緻的篇章分析，我們期待可重構以漢文爲書寫工具的筆談方式，讓已被遺忘的，以書寫作爲互動的第三種人類溝通模式重現，並重溫二十世紀之前在漢字文化圈內的東亞各國仍然積極學習運用漢字的年代，漢文是如何擔起跨文化交際的橋樑作用並體現其人際傳意交流的功能。 上述筆談材料的篇章分析完成後，我們便具備條件去探討另外兩個研究目標： (i) 列出所有在語料庫中出現的明治維新時期以漢字建構的現代日語詞彙，並對照它們如何通過借詞的方式直接用在漢語語境之中，從而了解日語 “回流” 到漢語的軌跡。“日語回流借詞” 的傳播軌跡可通過檢視歷時的漢語詞典與在線資料庫得以確認。 (ii) 我們亦可了解，在建構現代日語詞彙的過程中，以調整日語語音或語意作爲創造新詞的手段之比例 (Handel 2019; 對 Handel 2019 的書評, 見 Li 2000)。 References cited: • Hé, Dàzhāng 何大章, Shào, Qún 邵群, Lĭ, Péng 李朋, Táng, Quán 唐詮, and Zhào, Bō 趙波 (eds). 2010. 宮崎滔天家藏：來自日本的中國革命文獻 [Miyazaki Toten’s family collection: Documents on Chinese October Revolution from Japan]. Peking: People's Fine Arts Publishing House. • Handel, Zev. (2019). Sinography: The borrowing and adaptation of the Chinese script. Leiden: Brill. • Li, David C.S. (2020). 15603420.label: Realisation of objectives
15603420.value: 1. Digitalization, transcription of brushtalk dataset, and construction of online searchable website have been completed (A corpus of Miyazaki Touten’s family collection – see the link: sinitic-brush-talk-hk.github.io). The ‘Sun Yat-sen – Miyazaki Tōten’ database contains 7,904 characters (5,970 words; 2,061 word types). A database of all content keywords (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) that make up the ‘Meiji lexicon of modernity’ has also been created (see the link: 1897-8)Miyasaki220718_horizontal.xls). In terms of language contact dynamics, four trajectories of lexical borrowing involving 58 word types were identified (all disyllabic): (a) Japanese coinage not used in Chinese (n = 15); (b) Loanwords: Chinese --> Japanese (n = 9); (c) Loanwords: Japanese --> Chinese (n = 11); (d) ‘Returned loans’: Chinese --> Japanese --> Chinese (n = 16); and (e) Idiosyncratic (n = 7). 2. Completed. The website facilitates fine-grained analysis of baseline contextual details of and material conditions for conducting brush-talk. • Surviving brush-talk records and images accessible and downloadable from several museums afforded in-depth understanding of the actual setting of Sinitic brush-talk between literati of Sinitic from China and Japan, including how the brush-talkers were seated and the most likely turn-taking routine regarding how they exchanged writing-mediated information by turning the paper 180 degrees to facilitate the fellow brush-talker’s turn, as evidenced in the re-enacted display of brush conversation setting between 孫逸仙 Sun Yat-sen and 宮崎滔天 Miyazaki Tōten dated around 1900 (source: Miyazaki Brothers Museum 宮崎兄弟資料館, Arao 荒尾市, Kyushu: https://www.city.arao.lg.jp/kurashi/shisetsu/miyazaki-kyodai/). • The prevailing Japanese etiquette suggests that the face-to-face seating arrangement could be the norm in brush conversations between Chinese and Japanese literati of Sinitic hosted by the Japanese side. • Additional clues include responses to questions and commentaries written next to the brush-talker’s input (see photocopies of well-preserved brush conversation manuscripts in He et al. 1990) showing different calligraphic styles and dissimilar ink marks. • The test-run of the system shows that the website is sufficiently robust and smooth, and will be made publicly and freely accessible for online search when ready (see A corpus of Miyazaki Touten’s family collection (sinitic-brush-talk-hk.github.io). 3. Tabulation of the ‘Meiji lexicon of revolution’ completed (see Brushtalk_task2_findings_Harry_20231230.xls (sharepoint.com). Their contextualized use in specific brush-talk interactions helps assess the semantic or pragmatic affordance of sinograms, and the extent to which they are script-specific (i.e., Chinese characters and Japanese kanji). • A careful review of the relevant literature shows the following material conditions: o Importation of literary canons and other Classical Chinese texts from China through trade, but also personal collections purchased by individual East Asian visitors to China (Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese), notably monks and students. o The learning of Sinitic as evidenced by careful annotation of primers of Sinitic such as Three-character Classic and Thousand Characters Classic. o Acquisition of Sinitic, a major investment in terms of time and material resources, was widely regarded as a privilege of the social elite in East Asian polities – the rich and powerful in society. o Knowledge of Sinitic helped literati of Sinitic to get around the problem of no shared spoken language in cross-border encounters – to make meaning by engaging in brush conversation, hence the ‘scripta franca’ function of Sinitic. 4. No comparable writing-mediated communication in other ancient civilizations that have a full-blown literate culture such as the Latin-, Arabic- and Malay-speaking world was found. While we acknowledge “the absence of evidence is no evidence of its absence”, our postulation – that writing-mediated Sinitic brush-talk was script-specific – remains valid. As such, we believe the ‘morphographic hypothesis’ will continue to be upheld – until any counter-evidence is unearthed. • Reassurance was obtained at KT event on 18/12/2023 featuring three 30-minute presentations (Part 1), premiere of a 22-minute video documentary (animation), and launch of a 90+ page multilingual manga: The narrative of the documentary comes in different language versions: Cantonese, Korean, and English (see the links below), but also Mandarin, Japanese and Vietnamese as well as other Sinitic languages (the latter three are still under construction): • Cantonese: https://youtu.be/7hbkHqKcwoM • Korean: https://youtu.be/36RuvH6l6Y0 • English: https://youtu.be/Nv7tXMRxjd8 (McCune-Reischauer Romanization); https://youtu.be/cWUCCJxVUqA (Revised Romanization) • The manga is likewise multilingual, accessible in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese and English: https://sinitic-brush-talk-hk.github.io/polyu-text-corpus/images/the-brush-is-mightier-than-the-sword-v14.pdf. During the Q & A session, one question was raised regarding whether similar writing-mediated interactive, face-to-face communication had been reported in other ancient civilizations such as the Latin-, Arabic-, or Malay-speaking world. According to the feedback (speakers Prof. Ross King of University of British Columbia, Canada, and Dr Ivana Gubić of University of Zagreb, Croatia, and the international audience), the answer was ‘no’, suggesting that the morphographic hypothesis is valid. 5. Completed. A 5,907-word database (7,904 characters) of all the brush conversations in He et al. (2020) was constructed, with the following tags for each word: Part-of-speech, Syntactic note, Mandarin pronunciation, Cantonese pronunciation, Sino-Korean pronunciation, Sino-Japanese pronunciation, Japanese gloss, Korean gloss, English gloss, and Stratum: o Classical Chinese / loanword imported from Japanese into Chinese / words coined until the late Qing period / proper name / Cantonese / Japanese usage not found in Chinese • Translations of each sentence into English, Japanese, Korean and modern Chinese are also provided. See https://polyuit-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/personal/hkmncc_polyu_edu_hk/Documents/video-documentary/(1897-8)Miyasaki220718_horizontal.xls?d=w24e38dd4c0ee41e7a1589c11c82123cd&csf=1&web=1&e=5z23iW. • An online search interface of this database was constructed. The digitalized 7904-character database is used to identify kanji-based Japanese coinages. Fine-grained analysis will inform us of the relative significance of phonetic adaptation and semantic adaptation (or any combination of these) in the process of borrowing first from Chinese into Japanese before the Meiji period, and from Japanese into Chinese (and Korean) during the 100 years beginning from the Meiji era. This helps ascertain the extent to which Handel’s theory of script borrowing (2019) is valid. This database allows interested researchers to scrutinize various cross-linguistic processes of adaptation of the kanji-based Japanese coinages – phonetic or semantic, or some combination of these in accordance with Zev Handel’s (2019) theory of lexical borrowing and adaptation (see (1897-8)Miyasaki220718_horizontal.xls). 6. In progress. While the database has been thoroughly digitized, work toward addressing this objective is behind, largely because objectives 1–4 has been a higher priority. The groundwork has been laid by starting a dialogue with leaders in this area of research in Japan, namely, Prof. SHEN Guowei沈国威 教授 of Kansai University, Japan. He is a leading authority in the transfer or adaptation of kanji-based vocabulary into Chinese and Korean. His profile may be viewed here: 沈国威研究室|関西大学 (kansai-u.ac.jp). • The words from the partial list constituting the kanji-based ‘Meiji lexicon of revolution’ will be used to examine the degree of uptake in modern Chinese. This will be analyzed vis-à-vis the attitudes of the Chinese intelligentsia at large over an extended period for nearly a century until the 1980s, to what extent the Japanese coinages and ‘returned Sinitic loanwords’ should be adopted or discarded.

15603420.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603420.value: 1. For several hundred years until 1900s, Sinitic brush-talk (漢文筆談) was a widely practiced writing-mediated communication practice – interactively face-to-face – in cross-border contexts between literati in today’s Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and China. Research outputs abound in England East Asian languages, but publications in English are scarce. One important outcome is the publication of the first monograph in English, contributing a comprehensive overview of the range of contexts, regional and topical, in which Sinitic brush-talk took place across Sinographic East Asia during the Ming and Qing dynasties. 2. The classification of brush conversation datasets (diplomatic envoys 外交官筆談; boat drifters 漂流民筆談; traveling literati 遊歷者筆談) has proved to be heuristically very productive for analysis. 3. On knowledge transfer, dissemination and impact in society, we produced two artistic works featuring a 20-minute video documentary (animation) accessible in 5 languages: Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, English and Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin in the case of the video documentary; see A corpus of Miyazaki Touten’s family collection (sinitic-brush-talk-hk.github.io)), and a 90+ page penta-lingual manga, the latter featuring narratives and dialogues in 5 written languages: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, and English. Both animation and manga tell the story of a five-month drifting ordeal of Chosŏn (Korean) scholar-official, Ch’oe Pu 崔溥 (1454–1504), whose boat with 42 other Koreans on board was blown off course and stranded off the coast of Zhejiang in Ming China in 1488. Despite no shared spoken language, Ch’oe Pu’s excellent command of Classical Chinese allowed him to dispel allegations of disguised Japanese pirates, but more importantly to ascertain their Korean identity culminating in a meeting with the Ming Emperor before being repatriated to Korea. A KT event was organized (18/12/2023) featuring premiere of the video documentary, launch of the manga, and three 30-minute academic presentations respectively by Prof. Ross King of University of British Columbia, Canada; Dr. Ivana Gubić of University of Zagreb, Croatia; and the PolyU research team. This hybrid KT seminar attracted 115 registered participants online. Both multilingual artistic works have been made accessible freely online. Complimentary copies of the printed manga were sent to local university and public libraries; email acknowledgment of receipt were received from CityU, HKBU, EdUHK, and Saint Francis University in mid-March 2024.

15603420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603420.value: 1. There exist several other bodies of manuscripts (e.g. carefully preserved, high-resolution 8-volume《大河内文書》, The Ōkōchi Documents, 3000+ pages edited by Wang Baoping). Digitization of Sinitic brush-talk manuscripts is definitely worth supporting to facilitate research in Sinitic brush-talk as a possibly script-specific but forgotten cross-border communication practice (e.g., between Sun Yat-sen and his Japanese sympathizers such as Miyazaki Tōten and his brothers). 2. In terms of significance toward knowledge production, there is good prospect of writing-mediated communication – interactively face-to-face – being recognized as the 4th modality of communication between humans after (i) speech between talking humans, (ii) gesture-based sign language between hearing-impaired humans, and (iii) tactile communication through touch between hearing- and sight-impaired humans. A deeper understanding of the interactional dynamics of Sinitic brush-talk will have much to inform the broadly defined field of Linguistics, notably cross-cultural pragmatics in Sinographic East Asia. 3. To what extent is writing-mediated brush conversation a script-specific communication phenomenon? The search for comparable writing-mediated communication practice in other literate cultures, ancient or modern, will help ascertain the validity of the ‘morphographic hypothesis’ – an important outcome of this project.

15603420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603420.value: In China and Japan, thousands of hànzì/kanji (漢字) are taught and learned in school. In Chinese-Japanese communication, 漢字 may be improvised for disambiguation or clarification, e.g., to solicit travel information or service. For hundreds of years until 1900s, Sinitic-based brush-talk (漢文筆談) was a salient communication practice between literati of Classical Chinese from today’s Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and China. While regional 漢字texts were comprehensible throughout Sinographic East Asia, their respective spoken languages were mutually unintelligible. Brush conversation in Sinitic has left behind sizable historical data, allowing us to identify who communicated with whom, where and when, and for what particular purposes. Similar to speech-based ‘lingua francas’ like Latin, Arabic, French and English, 漢字 and its regional incarnations during the pre- and early modern periods functioned effectively as a writing-mediated ‘scripta franca’ (shared writing-based language). Deep and sometimes aesthetically rich intellectual exchange in cross-border encounters are reminiscent of an East Asian ‘world without translation’ – thanks to the improvisation mediated by a resourceful brush in the hands of well-educated literati of Sinitic from different parts of Sinographic East Asia.

15603520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603520.value: Background: The future practice of our graduates is no longer stable and predictable. Graduates are required to be not only knowledgeable and skillful, but also adaptive to the changing demands of work . The increasing use of simulation-based education (SBE) is to prepare nursing students for their practice. However, the standardized approaches with pre-determined outcomes only allow students to learn what is planned and delivered. The individualist and cognitive perspectives adopted in simulation are also insufficient to understand the process of how learning takes place in the complex professional practice. This understanding has an important implication for fidelity/realness in simulation since such scenarios cannot capture the full range of behaviours and interactions, most significantly within the embodied and material world of the nurse, notably the interface with physical tools, monitoring equipment, protocols, which shape and engineer practice. Hence emphasizing only the human or the social and the intended learning over the material and the unintended learning in SBE will undoubtedly limit our understanding of how knowledge is developed through SBE. Purpose: The purpose of this study is to explore an innovative approach to student learning on palliative care communication through SBE, based on the sociomaterial perspective. Globally, palliative care is becoming increasingly complex, with ever more sophisticated treatment options and education needs for advanced care planning. This reality, combined with the tension and high emotions of patients, families, and nurses, is a clarion call to the importance of preparing nursing students through SBE to develop better communication with this population and their families prior to their clinical practice. Method: An ethnographic approach will be adopted to examine SBE for nursing students' palliative care communication based on sociomaterial perspectives. In addition to a document review, data will be collected from field observations before simulations, video-recordings during simulations, focus group interviews through debriefings, and interviews with students after their subsequent clinical practice. There will be a collaborative analysis of data from field notes and videotapes; a content analysis of the focus group debriefings and follow-ups of students in practice, and a document and artifact analysis to determine how nurse-patient palliative care communication can be enhanced using the sociomaterial approach. Relevance to simulation/clinical practice: The sociomaterial approach in SBE will reorient us into taking into account the multiple ways in which human and non-human elements relate, that might otherwise go unnoticed during the simulation learning of palliative care communication. 背景：護理實踐多變並難以預測。現今僱主要求畢業生有知識和技能並能適應不斷改變的工作需求。為預備學生實踐護理，模擬教學越來越普遍。不過，標準化的模擬學習方法成效預設，往往使學生只按計劃學習。護士的物質世界，例如：所用的工具、監測儀器，護理程序可塑造不同的護理情境並影響護理實踐。模擬教學著重仿真/真實程度，但模擬情境無法捕捉護士全部的行為和互動。在模擬學習過程中，學生的個人和認知觀點不足以理解在複雜的專業實踐中學習是怎樣發生的。 在模擬教學過程中如何令學生明白學習是怎樣發生，這十分重要。若模擬教學只強調人或社會因素及預期學習目標，而略忽物質和非預期學習目標，這無疑限制我們理解在模擬教學過程中知識是如何産生。 目的：探討以創新的取向，即社會物質觀點來推行模擬教學，協助學生學習紓緩護理的溝通技巧。 全球的紓緩護理服務日益複雜，治療選擇越來越精細。為幫助患者制訂預設臨終照顧計劃，要求護士的教育水平越來越高。面對末期疾病，患者，其家屬和護士之間關係緊張並有強烈情緒。護理學生在臨床實踐前接受模擬教學十分重要，它可預備學生與患者及其家人良好溝通。 方法：採用民族誌研究法，從社會物質角度出發，探討如何以模擬教學方法培育護理學生的紓緩護理溝通技巧。 研究員審閱文檔。模擬教學前在現場觀察並搜集資料。錄影模擬教學過程，在學生匯報會進行焦點小組訪談，並在學生護理實踐後訪問他們。合作分析現場觀察筆記和錄像，內容分析焦點小組訪談，跟進學生的護理實踐和教學文件，並從社會物質角度及以器物分析法，找出改善紓緩護理服務的護患溝通方法。 與模擬/臨床實踐的相關性：以社會物質取向來推行模擬教學有助我們從新的角度來考慮人與物質 (非人) 之間的多種聯繫，使學生模擬學習紓緩護理的溝通技巧時，不會忽略這些聯繫。

15603520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603520.value: Twenty-seven final-year nursing students in six groups participated in two simulated scenarios, followed by a debriefing and post-clinical focus groups to capture their reflections and learning. Fourteen of them joined the post-clinical focus groups after completing their clinical placements. Video recordings of the simulation, debriefing, and post-clinical focus groups were transcribed and coded based on the human and non-human elements that were observed. These were triangulated with data collected through team participant observations, an analysis of the existing syllabi and curriculum, and a participant mapping exercise after the simulation. These various data sources illustrate how student learning and reflections took place. Results: The three themes of student learning derived from the results and analysis were: 1) students’ expanded learning of healthcare communication through a socio-material approach in the context of palliative care; 2) students’ discovery of the diverse and complex relations and interactions between humans and materials and 3) students’ new perspectives on healthcare communication and the transfer of knowledge and skills through a socio-material approach in clinical practice. Conclusions: This study showed how nursing students learned about palliative care communication through simulation-based education under a sociomaterial perspective, and illustrated the importance of sociomaterial interactions and emergent learning in the complex and uncertain context of palliative care communication. The approach enabled students to describe the connections between their prior learning, the moment of care during the simulation and their future learning and performance in new ways. Theory-based simulation-based education and an unplanned attunement in learning are crucial to equip health professionals and educators to address student practices in new ways that may enhance the care that they provide, and to transfer their knowledge and skills to uncertainties and complexities of clinical practice.

15603520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603520.value: This study highlights how simulation-based education can be further expanded using a socio-material approach to prepare students to learn beyond standardized and cognitively-driven approaches and procedures. Student learning demonstrates that simulation-based education may develop beyond high fidelity and standardization to leave room for emergent learning and increased awareness in learning for students and teachers to optimize learning outcomes and competence. This approach can be further adopted in different clinical/nursing contexts to allow students' emergent understanding through diverse approaches and to develop a continuous level of comfort in dealing with uncertainties.

15603520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603520.value: Simulation-based education (SBE) is crucial to prepare nursing students prior to their clinical learning experience. This study describes and analyzes how nursing students learn through simulation in the context of palliative care communication through networks and interactions of human and non-human factors, and explores the transfer of their knowledge and skills from simulation to clinical practice. Final-year nursing students participated in two simulated authentic scenarios, followed by debriefings and post-clinical focus group interviews. The findings included students’ discovery of the diverse and complex relations and interactions between humans and materials and students’ new perspectives on palliative care communication and the transfer of their learning to clinical practice. This study is significant in being the first to address palliative care communication beyond the cognitive and social aspects. In particular, the reference is to non-human factors in the environment that allow students to learn about their decision to act in certain ways from working with the uncertainties and their discomfort, by acting in the moment. The value of this study lies in its contribution to SBE through adopting a theoretical structure, yet allowing students to relate their ah ha moments. This enables healthcare educators/students to analyze how students learn.

15603920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603920.value: IPCC在第五次評估報告中表示，氣候變化將成為21世紀下半葉影響人類健康的重要因素。其中，城市熱島強度的增加對人類健康的影響顯著加劇。近年來，許多學者針對城市熱島強度變化進行了一系列探討，但依然缺少對其動態模式與行為的深入探究。因此，本項目以香港為研究對象，設計了顧及城市環境的動態熱模擬模型。該研究將支持香港政府最近制定的“香港2030+”計劃的政策框架，以緩解香港居民對日益增強的熱環境不適應的問題。 研究團隊在基於太陽同步衛星圖像和氣象站數據的早期研究的基礎上，提出一整套估算香港地區熱島效應的動態模型。該研究旨在利用遙感技術，設計一種面向地表溫度估算的知識整合動態模型，並構建基於GIS建模的城市熱島效應生命週期，具體包含以下四方面：（i）利用時空自適應算法，從太陽同步影響（即ASTER，Landsat）和對地靜止衛星影像（即Himawari-8 AHI）中，提取每小時的高空間分辨率的熱輻射影響；（ii）提出了基於有效發射率和地理幾何因素的地表溫度估算方法；（iii）研究基於面向對象動態模型的城市熱島生命週期及行為特徵；（iv）利用輔助數據，實現地表溫度與太陽輻射，綠化和建築幾何效應進的分析比較。 這項研究將填補缺乏基於高時空分辨率的城市熱島現象演變方法的研究空白。其研究方法和成果將會輔助解決Manoli等（2019）於《自然》期刊中提出的全球尺度熱島效應研究問題。 這項研究將為“香港氣候行動藍圖2030+” 計劃提供城市熱島效應動態模式研究的科學依據。該計劃旨在通過市區重建計劃下的一系列城市規劃策略，緩解城市效應並改善城市氣候。本研究團隊在熱遙感、GIS建模、城市景觀和規劃分析方面具有扎實的研究基礎。

15604220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604220.value: In Hong Kong, nearly 2 million people among total population are living with disabilities or chronic diseases. About 30% of them receive informal care solely from adult children or children in-law rather than from domestic helpers. Many family caregivers experience role and family conflicts. Studies have consistently showed that compared with adults without such caregiving responsibilities, informal caregivers have worse health, more medical consultations, anxiety and depression, and lower quality of life than those who do not provide such care. A significant number of international and local studies have reported positive outcomes of psychoeducation interventions and mindfulness-based interventions in reducing caregiver burden and depression. However, two major limitations have been identified in these studies. Firstly, caregiver intervention studies should be theory-driven but previous programme have not studied variables that explain such positive outcomes adequately. Secondly, some intervention programmes were relatively long in duration, making it less cost-effective in implementation. Further studies should base on brief and clear in programme structure that facilitate routine implementation in community care. There is an emerging evidence base for the utility of mindfulness-based interventions, and this study investigate the feasibility and efficacy of a brief 10-hour intervention for caregivers of frail elderly. The proposed study is a multi-site, three-arm randomized controlled trial of a mindfulness-based intervention for Chinese family caregivers in Hong Kong. Effects of the intervention will be compared with those of an evidence-based psychoducation programme, and treatment-as-usual. 240 caregivers of frail elderly with a score of 6 on the Clinical Frailty Scale, indicating moderate to severe levels of frailty, will be recruited and randomly assigned to mindfulness-based intervention, psychoeducation, and treatment-as-usual experimental conditions. Overall programme effectiveness will be analyzed on measures of caregiver burden, depression, anxiety, positive caregiving experience, spirituality, family conflict, and the biomarker of heart rate variability. Measures on coping styles, experiential avoidance, and self-efficacy will be explored to see if they mediate the changes to participant improvements in outcomes. 6-month follow-up will be included to investigate the maintenance effects. This study will provide comparative effectiveness data on outcome variables for mindfulness-based interventions and psychoeducation on caregivers of frail elderly. It may also help to expand the existing models of intergenerational caregiving in Chinese culture, and to improve the overall quality of life of informal caregivers. 在香港, 約二百萬人口生活在殘疾或長期病中, 當中三成依賴成年子女或媳婦等非正規照顧者。不少家庭照顧者經歷角色及家庭衝突。非正規照顧者與沒有照顧責任的同齡對照組比較, 健康狀況更差, 更常看病, 更常出現抑鬱焦慮癥狀, 生活質素較低。 研究顯示心理教育課程及靜觀介入能有效減低照顧者負擔及抑鬱。其主要限制包括: 介入的研究理論基礎不足, 而且介入時間較長, 推行的成本效益低。進深研究需建基於精要的清晰的程序結構, 以便在社區推行。當靜觀介入的成效續漸建立, 本研究將探討一個為體弱長者照顧者而設的十小時精要靜觀介入課程的可行性的成效。 本研究採用多地點, 三臂隨機對照試驗設計, 招募240名華人家庭照顧者, 隨機編配入靜觀介入, 心理教育課程, 及照常治療控制組。研究對象為臨床體弱量表 6 分或以上中度至嚴重體弱長者照顧者。活動成效將以照顧負擔, 抑鬱, 焦慮, 正向照顧經驗, 靈性生活, 家庭衝突量表及心率變異作比較。應對方式, 經驗性迴避, 及自我效能感則為中介變項, 探討照顧課程的理論。研究同時包括六個月跟進探討介入效果的持久性。

15604220.label: Realisation of objectives
15604220.value: Objectives 1 and 2 investigate the effects of a brief mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) in reducing the burden and depressive symptoms of family caregivers of Chinese frail elderly and compare the effects of the mindfulness-based intervention with that of an evidence-based psychoeducation (PSY) programme, and treatment-as-usual (TAU) In the Group x Time interaction analysis, caregivers in the MBI showed a significant reduction in depressive symptoms (η2 = 0.072, p = 0.043) and experiential avoidance (η2 = 0.101, p = 0.016) at T1 compared to the TAU group, with medium effect sizes. They also exhibited significant improvements in family functioning (η2 = 0.127, p = 0.006), self-efficacy (η2 = 0.113, p = 0.011), and problem-solving coping style (η2 = 0.126, p = 0.007) at T1 compared to the TAU group, all with medium effect sizes. Self-efficacy in the MBI group also demonstrated a medium effect size at T2 (η2 = 0.070, p = 0.046) and a small effect size across three time points (η2 = 0.058, p = 0.043) compared to the TAU group, indicating a maintenance effect on self-efficacy of the MBI. A significant small maintenance effect was also reported on problem-solving coping style across three time points (η2 = 0.054, p = 0.048). Compared to the PSY group, the MBI group reported a significant reduction in experiential avoidance (η2 = 0.085, p = 0.018) at T1, with a medium effect size. A larger improvement in problem-solving coping style was observed at T1 in the MBI group compared to the PSY group, with a medium effect size (η2 = 0.079, p = 0.022). The outcomes of caregiving burden were significantly reduced at T1 in both of two groups (η2 = 0.076, p = 0.025), but returned to their pre-test levels at T2 (η2 = 0.073, p = 0.028). The marginally significant difference across three time points indicated a similar immediate effects on caregiving burden (η2 = 0.049, p = 0.054) between the MBI and the PSY. Moreover, significant improvements of self-efficacy at T1 (η2 = 0.154, p = 0.001), T2 (η2 = 0.093, p = 0.013) and across three time points (η2 = 0.086, p = 0.005) also showed similar immediate and maintenance effects of both the MBI and the PSY. Additionally, a delay improvement with a medium effect size was reported for the MBI group in terms of denial as a coping style at T2 (η2 = 0.063, p = 0.042) and a small effect size was reported across three time points (η2 = 0.047, p = 0.046). The MBI showcasing greater reductions in depressive symptoms and experiential avoidance compared to usual care. Additionally, the mindfulness group exhibited significant greater improvements in family functioning, self-efficacy, and problem-solving coping style at posttest, when compared to the usual care group. The results indicated that the outcomes of the brief MBI were akin to those of a standard 8-week MBI at posttest, significantly ameliorating caregiver depression, and caregivers’ coping skills relating to problem-solving and self-efficacy. However, the study did not observe significant improvements in caregiver burden. Recent reviews suggested that caregiver burden, being a multi-component variable encompassing both objective and subjective dimensions of caregiving, may be less responsive to change. Contrary to the majority of reviews, this study did not demonstrate significant improvements in anxiety and stress. This discrepancy might indicate varying effects on mental health outcomes post a low intensity MBI, with the possibility that heightened awareness of internal experiences and reduced avoidance could potentially elevate anxiety and perceived stress levels in some participants. At the six-month follow-up, the effects of MBI on self-efficacy persisted, remaining superior to usual care, with a medium effect size, and the effects of MBI on problem-solving coping style maintained across three time points with a small effect size. However, apart from self-efficacy and problem-solving coping style, most outcomes did not sustain at the six-month follow-up. Continued mindfulness practice would be a key factor that contribute to sustainability of program effects. This study echoes with their findings, suggesting the need for a shorter follow-up period or the integration of booster sessions to maintain the effects of the brief MBI. The study provides further evidence that a brief MBI can enhance family functioning and reduce experiential avoidance. This study revealed no significant differences between the outcomes of the mindfulness group and psychoeducation group in terms of their effects at in the Group x Time interactions, with all effect sizes (η2) being less than or equal to 0.06. Both the MBI and the PSY showed their significant effects on reducing caregiving burden across three time points. It suggests that the effects of MBI are similar to psychoeducation across all outcome measures, further reinforcing the feasibility and effectiveness of this unique approach in promoting caregiver mental health and well-being. Objective 3 test the factors that contribute to positive improvements in both caregiver programmes, and develop a preliminary model for understanding and reducing caregiver burden and depressive symptoms The mediation analysis controlled for the caregiver’s gender and age, frailty scores, and baseline depression levels as a covariables, with changes in the outcomes assessed at T1. Upon consolidation, changes in self-efficacy, experiential avoidance, and problem-solving coping style were considered as potential mediators for the effects of MBI. The indices of the model demonstrated its goodness of fit: χ2 = 11.427, df = 10, p = 0.325, CFI = 0.986, RMSEA = 0.050, TLI = 0.925, SRMR = 0.045. Enhanced self-efficacy significantly mediated the MBI effects on reducing depression caregiving burden (indirect effect = -0.129, 95% CI = -0.295 to -0.014) and anxiety (indirect effect = -0.174, 95% CI = -0.269 to -0.014). Change in experiential avoidance significantly mediated the MBI effects on reduction of depressive symptoms (indirect effect = -0.120 (95% CI = -0.235 to -0.005). Improvements in problem-solving coping style marginally mediated the relationships between the MBI and the reductions in depressive symptoms (indirect effect = -0.149, 95% CI = -0.300 to -0.003), and showed its significant mediating role in anxiety (indirect effect = -0.372, 95% CI = -0.669 to -0.075). When compared to psychoeducation, the mindfulness group demonstrated larger improvements in experiential avoidance at T1, and unexpectedly, a similar pattern was observed in problem-solving. The effect of MBI in experiential avoidance appears to be treatment specific, potentially indicating that caregivers are learning to accept the aging and declining health of their family members. In addition, caregivers in the mindfulness group may enhance in cognitive flexibility and they are more willing to initiate practical and positive actions in daily caregiving routines. MBI had effects on all three mediators. Further analysis revealed indirect effects of self-efficacy on depressive symptoms and caregiving burden and anxiety within the multiple-mediation model. Experiential avoidance had indirect effects on depressive symptoms, while problem solving coping had a marginal indirect effects on depressive symptoms and an indirect effect on anxiety. Although the mediating analysis did not support all outcome variables, it highlighted an intervention-specific pattern in predicting different outcomes for caregivers.
