15604220.label: Major findings and research outcome
15604220.value: A multi-site, three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted to assess the impact of a mindfulness-based intervention for Chinese family caregivers. Intervention effects were compared with those of an evidence-based psychoeducation program and treatment-as-usual. One hundred and fifty-one caregivers initially expressed interest in participating, with ninety-three eligible caregivers ultimately being randomly assigned to brief mindfulness-based program, psychoeducation, or treatment-as-usual. Caregivers in the mindfulness group showed greater improvements in depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, family functioning, self-efficacy, and problem-solving in coping style at posttest, compared with those receiving usual care. When compared to the psychoeducation group, caregivers in mindfulness group showed greater improvements in experiential avoidance, and problem-solving coping. The improvement in self-efficacy was sustained at the six-month follow-up.

15604220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15604220.value: The findings suggest that a brief mindfulness-based intervention can significantly enhance caregiver mental health and overall well-being. This study provides further evidence that a low intensity mindfulness intervention could be better suited to address the challenges faced by caregivers with limited time due to their demanding schedule.

15604220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15604220.value: Caregivers in the mindfulness group showed greater improvements in depression, family functioning, self-efficacy, and problem-solving in coping style after the programme, compared with those receiving usual care. When compared to the psychoeducation group, caregivers in mindfulness group showed greater improvements in experiential avoidance, and problem-solving coping. The improvement in self-efficacy was maintained at the six-month follow-up. The findings suggest that a ten-hour mindfulness-based intervention can significantly enhance caregiver mental health and overall well-being. This study provides further evidence that a brief mindfulness intervention could be better suited to address the challenges faced by caregivers with limited time due to their demanding schedule.

15605520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605520.value: The rising prominence of corpus-based approaches in translation studies has greatly informed the research into the nature of translation process and act. While most research efforts have focused on uncovering the translational language as a "third code" (Frawley 1984) that is perceptibly different from both native source and target languages from the perspective of "translation universals"(Baker 1993), little progress has been made as to the linguistic and grammatical features of translations done by student translators and a gap clearly remains between corpus-based translation studies and learner translation corpus research. The present project intends to systematically examine the lexical, syntactic and textual features of student translations (Chinese-English) using the enhanced multidimensional analysis (eMDA) proposed by Hu, Xiao and Hardie(2016). It is hoped that by drawing on the insights from corpus-based multidimensional analysis methodology, we are able to uncover the core features and patterns of student translations and examine the extent to which student translations are (dis)similar to professional translations and/or English second language writing. It is hypothesized in the current research that the translation universals identfied in professional translation can also be found in learner translation. Major research questions include: 1) In what ways, if any, are the different registers of learner translation different or similar from the same registers of professional translation along the dimensions established in this study? 2) In what ways, if any, are the different registers of learner translation different or similar from the same registers of second-language variety along the dimensions established in this study? 3) Can the similarities or differences, if identified, be explained using translation or mediation universals to characterize learner translation? The major corpus resources to be used include International Corpus of English in Hong Kong(ICE-HK) as well as two corpora, i.e. the Corpus of Professional Translational English(CPTE) and the Parallel Learner Translation Corpus(PLTC), to be constructed under the current project. Both corpora to be compiled will match the printed written component of ICE-HK in text categories. The proposed research will conduct a systematic analysis on the lexical, syntactic and textual features with an aim of identifying (dis)similarities between the three corpora and seeking a possibility of identifying learner translation as under the influence of translation-specific (translation) or L2-specific (interlanguage) factors. The research will not only analyse systematically the unique features of Chinese-to-English learner translation, but will also help uncover the relation between learner translation, professional translation and the second language variety of English. 基於語料庫研究方法在翻譯研究中的地位日益提高，極大地推動了翻譯過程和行爲本質的研究。目前，許多研究從「翻譯共性」的角度出發，側重於研究翻譯語言爲「第三代碼」（Frawley 1984），即翻譯既不同于源語，亦有別于目標語（Baker 1993）。然而，對學生譯者的譯文作語言及語法特徵的研究甚少。基於語料庫的翻譯研究與翻譯學習者語料庫研究之間顯然存在一定差距。本研究旨在通過增强型多維分析法（eMDA）（Hu，Xiao & Hardie 2016）系統地考察學生譯文（漢英翻譯）的詞彙、句法和文本特徵，以期借鑒基于語料庫的多維分析方法的視角，挖掘學生譯文的核心特徵和模式，幷探究學生譯文與專業譯文和英語二語寫作的异同。本研究假設翻譯共性不僅存在於專業譯文，也同樣存在於學生譯文，主要的研究問題包括：1）在確立的維度上，學習者譯文的不同語域與專業譯文的對應語域存在哪些异同之處？2）在確立的維度上，學習者譯文的不同語域與二語寫作的對應語域有哪些异同之處？3）若异同之處被識別，是否可以使用翻譯共性或調和共性來解釋學習者譯文的特徵？本研究使用的主要語料庫資源包括國際英語語料庫香港子庫（ICE-HK）以及兩個自建語料庫，即專業譯文英語語料庫（CPTE）和平行學習者譯文語料庫（PLTC）。兩個自建語料庫將在文本類別上與ICE-HK的書面語部分相匹配。本研究將對三個語料庫從詞彙、句法和文本特徵作系統分析，以闡明其異同點，幷嘗試探討識別學習者譯文受到翻譯特定（翻譯）或二語特定（中介語）因素影響的可能性。本研究將有望系統地分析漢英學習者譯文的獨特特徵，有助於揭示學習者譯文，專業譯文與英語二語寫作之間的關係。

15605620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605620.value: The mismatch negativity (MMN) brain signal is a widely used tool for investigating the neural processing of language. It remains uncertain, however, whether this component of brain activity reflects the processing of abstract linguistic features (i.e., those with no reliable physical correlates), or only that of low-level physical features. While MMN experiments have often been used to argue for the psychological reality of theoretically-motivated but abstract linguistic structures, there are often other explanations available that do not rely on abstract linguistic knowledge. The present project will more deeply investigate the mechanisms underlying the MMN, by testing whether MMN can be elicited for contrasts which are not cued by any physical correlate. MMN can be elicited by a putatively abstract contrast, e.g., between a random sequence of unaspirated sounds (e.g., "ba", "da", and "ga") and aspirated sounds (e.g., "pa", "ta", and "ka"). It is assumed that the standards only form monolithic categories (required for the elicitation of MMNs) at a level of formal linguistic features (i.e., unaspirated vs. aspirated). However, this contrast could be explained without recourse to linguistic features: "pa", "ta", and "ka" all include a brief puff of air (aspiration) whereas "ba", "da", and "ga" do not. The present experiments will test, for the first time, whether the MMN can be elicited in contrasts that truly have no physical correlate. Experiments 1a-b will examine whether the MMN is observed for a contrast between English irregular past and present verbs (e.g., {"shake", "run", "sit"} and {"gave", "won", "lit"}), where there is no single physical cue that signals the difference. Experiments 2a-b will examine whether the MMN is observed for another contrast which has no physical cue: a contrast words from different semantic categories. If MMN can be elicited by contrasts without a single acoustic cue, this will be the strongest evidence to date that the MMN reflects automatic activation of abstract linguistic representations. This research will also help narrow down what kinds of categorization can occur pre-attentively in the brain. The findings will have relevance for theories and models in cognitive neuroscience, as they will either strongly reaffirm or challenge current assumptions about what the MMN reflects. The MMN is also gaining traction as a diagnostic tool in individuals with some neurodevelopmental disorders, and a deeper understanding of its mechanisms may improve its efficacy in clinical contexts or broaden its application to different clinical populations and other translational applications. 不匹配負向波（MMN）是一個經常用於研究語言加工的腦電波。可是，到目前為止，這個腦電波到底反應抽象語言特征（也就是說沒有任何可靠的聲學實現）還是隻反應底層的聲學特征還不明確。多項先前MMN實驗的結果被認為是前者的証據（也就是說，有學者主張那些實驗的結果說明抽象的語言學結構有心理真實 [psychological reality]），但是不依靠抽象語言學知識的理論也能夠解釋這些結果。所以，本次研究將會試驗完全沒有任何聲學實現的對照會不會導致MMN波，來更深的探查MMN的心理基礎。 所謂的抽象對照會導致MMN：比如說，如果一系列隨機的不送氣音（如ba, da, ga）對照一系列隨機的送氣音（如pa, ta, ka），MMN就會出現。為了導致MMN，一組因必須做一個范疇；有學者認為 {ba, da, ga} 或者 {pa, ta, ka} 隻有在抽象的層次才成為兩組來自不用犯愁的音（不送氣音和送氣音）。但是，這個對照不需要抽象語言學概念來解釋：{pa, ta, ka} 中的送氣是明顯可以聽得出來的。本次實驗會實驗會試驗完全沒有任何聲學實現的對照會不會導致MMN波。實驗1A-1B會試驗英語的不規則動詞的過去時和現在時（如{gave, won, lit}和{shake, run, sit}）會不會導致MMN波；在這種情況下，兩組單詞之間沒有任何明確的聲學差別，差別卻在抽象層次（第一組為過去時動詞，第二組為現在時動詞）。試驗2A-2B會試驗另外個沒有聲學暗示的對照——來自不同語義范疇的單詞——同樣會不會導致MMN。如果沒有任何聲學暗示的對照能夠導致MMN波，這就會証明MMN真的反映了抽象的語言學結構。這項研究也會更詳細地確定大腦能夠自動地分別出哪幾種范疇。 本次研究的結果對認知腦科學的理論和模型會有含義，因為結果要麼會強有力地支持目前有關MMN的設想，要麼是徹底駁斥那些設想。最近，有很多學者也開始用MMN來診斷各種神經發展障礙；如果想這麼做，我們先必須明確地理解MMN的基礎。所以，通過這項研究來更深地理解MMN就將會提高我們用MMN治療各種神經障礙的能力。

We set out to determine whether abstract morphological contrasts can elicit the MMN, and we found that they could. Objective 3 was fully realized.

15605620.label: Major findings and research outcome
15605620.value: We carried out a high-powered experiment in which we found that the mismatch negativity can be elicited by an abstract, purely linguistic contrast with no physical correlate. While extant theories of the MMN predict that this should be possible, no experiment to date had ever shown it. This research thus provides the strongest evidence yet available that the MMN is elicited by a contrast between categories. Our findings were published in a registered report in the journal Neurobiology of Language (IF=3.6, JCR Q1 journal). While the above study was the major focus of this project, the grant also enabled other impactful research. Part of the grant money funded a post-doc position, and the holder of this position (Dr. Bernard Jap) carried out several more studies examining cleft structures, wh-questions, passive voice, and thematic role assignment inIndonesian. This project also inspired a undergraduate project funded by the Undergraduate Research and Innovation Scheme (URIS), which examined long-lag morphological priming from the perspective of Mandarin third tone sandhi. Additionally, the research has generated some media interest, as it was covered by the local media SCMP (link provided below). https://www.scmp.com/news/people-culture/article/3198433/its-not-scam-hong-kong-university-offers-paid-netflix-viewing-all-name-science

15605620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605620.value: The research team is in the process of extending this research to other sorts of linguistic contrasts. We have carried out a similar study examining whether visual MMN can be elicited by an abstract contrast between verbs and nouns in Indonesian. In that experiment (a paper of which is currently under review at another journal), we found a visual MMN for an abstract contrast between words and pseudowords, but not for the abstract contrast between nouns and verbs. Now further experiments are needed to determine why certain abstract contrasts yield MMNs and certain ones don't. The project team also extended the question about abstract linguistic representations to examine the processing of the abstract tonal category and the context-specific tonal variant of Mandarin Third Tone (T3) sandhi in word production using EEG and the formation of abstract linguistic representations in the context of foreign language learning.

15605620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15605620.value: In this project, we found out what causes a certain pattern of brain activity to happen. Specifically, we focused on the Mismatch Negativity, which is a brainwave that occurs when a person hears a sound that doesn't fit a pattern they had gotten used to. For example, when hearing "pa pa pa pa pa pa pa da", a person's brain would show a Mismatch Negativity wave when they hear the "da". While this brainwave has been studied since the1970s, it remained uncertain how abstract the "pattern" needed to be to elicit it. In this project, we demonstrated -- for the first time ever -- that the Mismatch Negativity can be triggered by a completely abstract pattern, based not on the physical sounds heard but on the linguistic categories that the sounds belong to. Specifically, we had people listen to series of past-tense verbs with occasional present-tense verbs (e.g.,"gave swore clung bled grew PAVE"), and we found that they showed a Mismatch Negavitity brainwave when hearing the unexpected present-tense verb.

15606320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606320.value: Relationship science has thus far been dominated by research on Western couples, and has overlooked how culture shapes the relationship processes. This project applies the cultural theory of naïve dialecticism to provide a culturally informed understanding of intimate relationship and marriage. Cross-cultural research using the theory of dialectical thinking has revealed important differences in how East Asians and Westerners think about contradiction and change (see Spencer-Rodgers & Peng, 2018). Whereas East Asians tend to tolerate both positive and negative aspects of things and find a middle way, Westerners are motivated to resolve seeming contradictions by synthesis or adopting extreme positions. Further, East Asians tend to view the world as constantly changing and in flux, whereas Westerners see stability and continuation. Although this theory has provided insight into cultural differences in cognition, emotion, and behaviors between the East and the West, it has received relatively less attention in the study of close relationships. In the present project, we propose to examine the role of dialectical thinking in the relationship process, including the evaluation of romantic partners and relationships, the organization of partner knowledge, and the perception of change in a relationship across four cultural groups, including two Eastern cultures (Hong Kong and Mainland China) and two Western cultures (United States and Australia). A series of studies will be conducted using cross-sectional, experimental, and longitudinal designs, explicit and implicit measures, as well as self- and partner-evaluation to assess romantic partners’ perceptions and cognitions in the development and maintenance of close relationships. We will compare attitudes toward romantic partners and relationships, the organization structure of partner knowledge, and relationship adjustment between Chinese and Westerners and test the mediating role of dialectical relationship beliefs to explain these cultural differences. This research will contribute to the limited literature on relationship theories and models that take account of Chinese people’s assumptions about and expectations for intimate relationships. The findings from this research can also inform practitioners regarding the assessment and interpretation of East Asian beliefs about relationships as well as the underlying psychological mechanisms. This project will contribute to the identification of ways to maintain more meaningful relationships and foster better relational well-being in diverse cultures. 迄今為止，關係科學主要集中在對西方情侶的研究，而忽略了文化如何塑造關係的過程。本項目運用通俗辯證法這個文化理論，從文化角度去了解親密關係和婚姻。使用辯證思維理論的跨文化研究揭示，東亞人和西方人在思考矛盾和變化方面有著重要的差異（參見Spencer-Rodgers & Peng, 2018）。東亞人傾向於容忍事物的正反兩立，並從中尋找中庸之道；相反，西方人則積極地通過綜合或採取極端立場，以解決表面上的矛盾。此外，東亞人傾向認為世界是常變和動態的；而西方人則視世界為穩定和延續的。縱使這理論為東西方的認知、情感、及行為方面的文化差異提出了獨到的觀點，它在研究親密關係方面所受到的關注卻相對較少。在本項目中，我們通過研究辯證思維在關係過程中的角色，探討四個文化群體之間，包括兩個東方文化（香港和中國內地）及兩個西方文化（美國和澳洲）對伴侶和戀愛關係的評估、關於伴侶的認知結構、以及對於關係變化的感知。此項目內的一系列研究將採用橫斷法、實驗、及縱貫法，以外顯和內隱測量及自我和伴侶評價，來評估伴侶對發展和維持親密關係的看法和認知。我們將比較中國人和西方人對伴侶和戀愛關係的態度、伴侶認知的組織結構、以及關係調整，並測試辯證關係的中介角色，以解釋這些文化差異。這項研究將融入中國人對親密關係的看法，在現今有限的關係理論和模型文獻作出貢獻。研究成果還可以為在這方面工作的從業者提供有關東亞人的信念如何影響他們對關係的評估與詮釋，及了解其潛在心理機制。

15606520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606520.value: Background: Family violence often co-occurs and multiple exposures might impose more threats to the health of family members. Family polyvictimization (FP) is a new concept that takes family as the basic unit of the victim to address the co-occurrence of multiple types of family violence and to promote integrated approaches encompassing effective prevention, detection, and interventions, in order to combat family violence. Little is known about FP and its correlates and underlying mechanisms, especially under the influences of Chinese cultural practices in Chinese families in Hong Kong. Objectives: This study extends existing knowledge about FP by examining the problem in a Chinese cultural context. Specifically, it (a) provides a reliable estimate of family polyvictimization among Chinese families in Hong Kong; (b) examines the effects of family hierarchy and Chinese cultural practices on family polyvictimization; and (c) tests the moderating effects of father and grandparent involvement in childcare on the associations between family hierarchy, Chinese cultural practices, and family polyvictimization. Study design: This study consists of two phases: a population-based household survey and a qualitative focus group study. In the household survey study, a population-based probability sample of 1,100 Chinese families with at least one child aged under 18 years will be recruited. Both parents, and capable grandparents if present, will be asked to report their experiences of family violence. Parent respondents will be asked to provide a proxy report for all children and grandparents who are not functionally capable of reporting on their own violence experiences. Parents will also answer questions about other Chinese cultural practices, father and grandparent involvement in childcare, and the family’s demographic information. Six types of family violence will be measured with the 11-item Family Polyvictimization Screen. Families with exposure to three or more types of violence will be regarded as experiencing polyvictimization. In the qualitative study, a purposive sample of 20 victims of family violence and 30 stakeholders working on family violence will be recruited to participate in focus group discussions. Contributions of the study: With the population-representative data of the Chinese families, this study will make significant academic and practical contributions to the field of violence by extending the current limited knowledge on FP and its underlying mechanisms. In particular, the findings will shed light on the development of effective early detection mechanisms for family violence, integrated preventions, and multi-disciplinary collaborated interventions of FP in the Chinese context. 背景： 家庭暴力往往同時發生，家庭多重傷害可能對家庭成員的健康構成更多威脅。家庭多重傷害是一個新概念，以家庭為單位，定位多種類型家庭暴力的共同發生，並促進有效的綜合預防，發現和介入的方法，以打擊家庭暴力。現時對家庭多重傷害及其相關性和潛在機制知之甚少，尤其是在中國文化習俗對香港華人家庭的影響下。 目標： 這項研究通過在中國文化背景下探討相關問題。具體而言，項目將（a）提供一個可靠的估計，說明香港華人家庭的多重傷害行為； （b）研究家庭等級制度和中國文化習俗對家庭多重傷害的影響； （c）檢驗父親和祖父母參與育兒對家庭等級，中國文化習俗和家庭多重傷害之間的聯繫的調節作用。 研究方法： 這項研究包括兩個階段：基於人口的家庭調查和定性焦點小組研究。在住戶調查研究中，將收集一個基於人口的概率樣本，該樣本來自1,100個至少有一個18歲以下兒童的華人家庭。父母和祖父母將被邀請報告他們的家庭暴力經歷。父母將回答有關其他中國文化習俗，父親和祖父母參與育兒以及家庭信息的問題。將通過11個項目的“家庭多重傷害” 量表测度六種家庭暴力。遭受三種或以上暴力侵害的家庭將被定義為經歷多重傷害。在定性研究中，將招募20位家庭暴力受害者和30位從事預防家庭暴力工作的專業人士，參加焦點小組討論。 研究貢獻： 借助香港華人家庭的代表性數據，本研究將通過擴展當前對家庭多重傷害及其基本機制的知識，為預防家庭暴力做出重要的學術和實踐貢獻。研究成果將開發有效的家庭暴力早期檢測機制，綜合預防措施以及多學科協作干預措施提供啟示。

15606520.label: Major findings and research outcome
15606520.value: Although the data collection schedule had been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, the research team completed data collection before the end of the project period. This study consists of a population-based household survey and a qualitative focus group study. In the household survey study, a population-based probability sample of 1,400 Chinese families with at least one child under 18 years was successfully recruited, with a successful % response rate of 65%. It exceeded the original plan aimed at 1,100 families because the response rate was better than expected during the post-pandemic period. The data provides a reliable estimate of the prevalence of family polyvictimization among Chinese families in Hong Kong, ranging from 2% to 17%, covering child maltreatment, partner violence, elder abuse, in-law violence, etc. We examine the effect of family hierarchy and Chinese cultural practices on family polyvictimization and identify the protective effect of father and grandparent involvement in childcare on the associations between family hierarchy, Chinese cultural practices, and family polyvictimization. In the qualitative study, the research team recruited a purposive sample of 20 victims of family violence and 30 stakeholders working on family violence in focus group discussions. They shared their experiences and shed light on the improvement of child protective services as well as family violence prevention measures. The manuscripts have been under review by peer-reviewed academic journals. We have published a meta-analysis study and a secondary data analysis to consolidate the research work and provide a systematic literature review for the project. The RGC support has been acknowledged in the two published papers.

15606520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606520.value: The goal of this project is to make an impact on the services and policy related to the handling of family violence by filling the current knowledge and service gap caused by the focus on only one single type of violence in each identified case. This project will deliver findings, including the effect of family hierarchy and other Chinese cultural practices on family polyvictimization and protective factors. The findings will inform the strategies of violence prevention and enhance multi-disciplinary collaboration using an integrated family approach. The beneficiaries of the study will be frontline refuge services and providers of protective services for children and families, as well as their clients (i.e., victims of family violence) in Hong Kong. The findings of this project will extend existing knowledge regarding the complexity of family violence and the importance of considering family hierarchy and other family cultural practices when providing effective services, thus giving evidence for the need to make changes to enhance the current handling procedures of relevant cases.

To develop the weaving technology and system, and create the weaving loom model for fabricating four-warp leno. The mechanism involves (1) an innovative synchronized vertical and horizontal lifting system to alter the current rigid (vertical only) lifting system; (2) an effective distance controlling technology to achieve flexible yet accurate placement of warps for leno formation without limitation on leno pattern and structures; and (3) an automatically method for securing the clearance of the shed to eliminate undesirable twine. 15607920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607920.value: China is hailed as a country with a long history of producing silk and is known for the development and evolution of various weaving structures. China’s textiles not only exemplify the country’s historical wisdom and culture but also provide valuable resources for human consumption and references for the development of highly functional textiles. Nevertheless, not all of China’s intricate weaving techniques have been handed down, and thus, production methods have faded into extinction. The four-warp leno is an ancient textile craft that is well known for its soft, thin, airy texture and high quality. Unfortunately, the production method and apparatus have been lost. This study thus aims to investigate the traditional leno and create the weaving technology, system and apparatus for fabricating this treasure of the past – the four-warp leno. The research and methodology involve four stages: (1) investigation of historical four-warp leno textiles in terms of design, structure and techniques; (2) creation and modelling of weaving technology and a system for fabricating a four-warp leno; (3) evaluation and validation of the properties of produced four-warp leno by objective testing; and (4) development of a new leno weaving structure. The proposed study is unique and challenging because it involves the development of a weaving system and the creation of weaving machinery to reproduce intricate ancient weaving techniques. This study will thus contribute to a breakthrough in textile design and weaving technology and push the boundaries of fashion and textile design. This study is expected to lead to the development of not only various leno patterns but also functional protective textile development, which may be inspired by the special properties of the four-warp leno. Realizing machine weaving means enabling mass production and mass dissemination, which will eventually contribute to the inheritance of special techniques and the sustainable development of high-value added textile products. Additionally, by re-creating the traditional four-warp leno, archaeological and historical studies on textiles will benefit from actual samples, and relics may be preserved. It is hoped that this ancient handicraft will not be sacrificed and that China’s traditional techniques can be shared with the public. 中國被譽為絲綢之國，有著悠久的絲綢生產歷史，以各種織物結構的發展和演變而聞名。中國的紡織品不僅體現了中國的歷史智慧和文化，更為現今人類的織物消費提供了寶貴的資源，並為功能性紡織品的發展提供了參考。然而，並非所有複雜的織造技術都被流傳下來，部分生產方法已逐漸消失。四經絞羅是一種古老的紡織工藝，以其柔軟、輕薄、透氣的質地和高品質而聞名。不幸的是，生產方法和設備已經失傳。 因此，本研究旨在研究傳統的羅，並創造出相關織造技術、系統和設備以製造歷史上的寶藏--四經絞羅。研究和方法論包括四個階段：（1）從設計、結構和技術上對歷史四經絞羅紡織品進行調查；（2）織造技術的創造和建模，以及用於製造四經絞羅的系統設計；（3）對所生產的四經紗羅的性能作客觀測試評估和驗證； 擬議的研究是獨特且具有挑戰性的，因為它涉及織造系統的開發和織造機械的製造，以再現複雜的古織造技術。因此，這項研究將有助於突破現今紡織品的設計和編織技術，並打破時裝和紡織品的設計界限。預期該研究不僅會帶來各種羅結構和圖案的發展，而且受到四經絞羅的特殊性能的啟發，還可能會帶來具功能性及保護性的紡織品的發展。實現機器織造意味著能夠進行大規模生產和大規模普及，這最終將有助於傳承特殊織造技術，並實現高附加值紡織產品的可持續發展。此外，通過重新創建傳統的四經絞羅，紡織品的考古和歷史研究將從受益於實際樣品，並且可以幫助保存文物。希望這種古老的手工藝品不再犧牲於歷史時間發展，並希望中國的傳統技術可以與公眾分享。

15608120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608120.value: The question of how words are mentally represented and retrieved during the writing process has been investigated for decades. Previous studies involving writing-to-dictation of alphabetic languages found that the task is strongly influenced by the non-lexical pathway (assembling letters according to the sounds of words) of writing. Whether such strong effect of non-lexical pathway is due to the transparent sound-to-script nature of alphabetic languages or the task nature which requires converting sound into written words remains unknown. The Chinese writing system differs from other alphabetic writing systems in that the subcomponents in characters do not map onto sub-syllabic units as in words of alphabetic languages. This characteristic of Chinese indicated that non-lexical pathway of writing is impossible. Therefore, testing the significance of phonological effects using Chinese writing-to-dictation will help to verify if the strong non-lexical pathway effect previously observed in writing-to-dictation in alphabetic scripts is due to the sound-to-script transparency of the languages concerned or due to the task requirements. In this study, writing-to-dictation norm performance of 3128 Chinese characters will be obtained. The accuracies, response time and total writing time of each trial will be collected over a total of 50 healthy participants. Each of them will participate in eight sessions of data collection, each containing 391 stimuli randomly selected from all the targets. Linear mixed effect models will be constructed to investigate the significance of different lexical, sublexical and psycholinguistic variables, including lexical frequency, age-of-acquisition, homophone density, homophone frequency, imageability, concreteness, familiarity in predicting the three different dependent variables of writing-to-dictation. Moreover, there exist sublexical units in Chinese characters (e.g. semantic radical 木 [wood] and phonetic radical支/zi1/ in the character 枝/zi1/[twig]) which give clues to meaning and sound, implying the possibility of sublexical processing in writing. Although previous observations of brain-damaged patients supported this sublexical processing in writing Chinese (Law et al., 2005; Lau & Ma, 2018), whether they can be generalized to healthy individuals warrants further investigation. Hence, phonetic regularity and transparency of semantic radicals will also be entered into the model. The results obtained will extend current theories on the lexical processes in both alphabetic and non-alphabetic languages writing. Clinically, it will also facilitate future investigations of how individuals with writing difficulties differ from the norm. Finally, the handwriting data obtained will be used to establish a databank that document writing performance in Chinese. The databank will serve as important resources for future studies on Chinese handwriting processes. 數十年來，研究員一直在探討人們如何在書寫過程中檢索單詞。過去關於書寫的研究發現，書寫任務受「非詞彙途徑」（透過詞的聲音組裝字母）的強烈影響。其原因可能是：（一）由於書寫任務通常需要將聲音轉換成書面單詞、（二）由於這些研究通常都涉及印歐語言，而印歐語言的聲音和字母轉換性質通常比較透明，因此透過詞的聲音組裝字母較易達到書寫任務的要求。漢字書寫系統與印歐語言書寫系統的不同之處，在於字符中的子組件不會像印歐語言中的單詞那樣映射到子音節單位上，即「非詞彙途徑」並不適用於漢語書寫。因此，研究漢字書寫將有助於分辨過去研究所指書寫任務受「非詞彙途徑」的強烈影響，到底是由於聲音和字母轉換性質的透明度，還是單純由於書寫任務要求將聲音轉換成書面單詞所致。 是項研究將會招募50名健康參與者，收集他們對3128個漢字的書寫任務時的準確性，反應時間和總寫作時間。每個參與者將參加八次數據收集小節，每個小節包含從所有目標漢字中隨機選出的391個。透過大數據研究，將分析出詞彙頻率、習得年齡、同音詞密度、同音詞頻率、可成像性、具體性和熟悉度等變量如何預測漢字書寫任務時的準確性、響應時間和總寫作時間。此外，過去曾有研究就著對腦部受損患者的觀察，指出漢字中的聲旁和形旁（如「枝」字的形旁「木」和聲旁「支」）對漢字書寫加工有影響。因此是項研究亦會分析聲旁和形旁的透明度如何影響漢字的書寫。 是項研究的結果將有助擴展有關印歐語和非印歐語書寫加工的最新理論。此外，結果亦將應用在書寫困難的臨床研究。最後，是項研究將會建立一個龐大的筆跡數據庫，以記錄漢字書寫的每一個過程。此數據庫將成為今後研究漢字書寫和手寫過程的重要資源。

15608120.label: Realisation of objectives
15608120.value: To begin with, the PI would like to expressed that one major difficulties encountered when conducting this project concerns the difficulties of data collection during COVID days. This project kicked off in early 2021. Since then, multiple lockdowns were announced by the Hong Kong Government due to the COVID pandemic. In response, universities in Hong Kong also announced online or hybrid teaching. These have made participants recruitment and data collection very difficult, particularly because the experiments targeted universal students and required them to attend 10 sessions of data collection. That handwriting responses have to be collected using standardized digitizers and styli in this project also made online data collection impossible at that time. This was one of the major reasons why the PI had to apply for extension of this project. Fortunately, data collection went smoothly after the social distancing measures were relaxed. However, the delayed data collection inevitably delayed the scoring and analyses, as well as the compiling of the online databased procedures. The project aimed at achieving the following objectives: 1. To construct a comprehensive writing-to-dictation norm of Cantonese-Traditional Chinese This project collected the writing-to-dictation performances from 25 male and 25 female participants using 3126 Cantonese-Traditional Chinese characters. The results indicated that the overall average accuracy achieved by the participants was 0.61 (SD = 0.30; range = 0.00 to 1.00). Preliminary findings of this norm were reported in Publication #1. The PI is currently working on another manuscript introducing these findings and the online database of handwriting data to-be-submitted to the Behavior Research Methods. 2. To investigate the significance of various lexical and psycholinguistic variables in predicting writing-to-dictation accuracy, RT and total writing time The results of the psycholinguistic norms of ratings of age-of-acquisition, familiarity, imageability, concreteness, and semantic-radical-transparency, as well as their association with writing-to-dictation accuracy were reported in Publication #1. In addition, the results of the significance of different lexical and psycholinguistic variables in predicting writing-to-dictation accuracy, RT and total writing time were reported in Conference Presentations #1 and #2. They will be further discussed in Publication #3 as well. 3. To validate the potential interaction between lexical non-semantic and semantic pathways in writing-to-dictation of Chinese The results of linear mixed effect models calculated indicated no significance in the interaction effect between semantic-radical-transparency (or imageability) and character frequency. Instead, the interaction between phonetic regularity and character frequency significantly predicted both accuracy and RT of writing-to-dictation. Given that the phonetic regularity captures the script-to-sound mappings while writing-to-dictation is a sound-to-script process instead, the results supported the notion of feedback consistency in the lexical process. Hence, information flow in the lexical retrieval process should be bi-directional instead of unidirectional. This theoretical implications was discussed in Conference Presentation #2 and will be elaborated in Publication #3. 4. To find out whether the different significance of lexical and non-lexical pathways in writing-to-dictation can be better explained by (a) the sound-to-script transparency of the language concerned, and/or (b) the requirements of conversion of sound to script of the task Results of both multiple regression analysis (reported in Conference Presentation #1) and linear mixed effect models (reported in Conference Presentation #2) indicated that in contrast with a previous large scale study by Han et al. (2012), the operation of the non-lexical pathway of Chinese writing-to-dictation was only partially driven by the mapping consistency from phonology to orthography. The difference between the results was attributed to the adjustment of the task requirement of the current study which did not give extra favor to items with consistent phonology-to-orthography mappings. Overall, it is concluded that the significance of lexical and non-lexical pathways in writing-to-dictation should be related to the inter-relationship between the phonological and orthographic systems of the language concerned. This was discussed in Conference Presentations #1 and #2 and will be elaborated further in Publication #3. 5. To elucidate current theories of writing-to-dictation of Chinese Overall, the results of the current study supported the dual route model, encompassing the lexical-semantic and non-semantic pathways, of Chinese writing-to-dictation. The dual route model was reported in Conference Presentation #2, which will be further elaborated in Publication #3. The central and peripheral processes of writing-to-dictation of Chinese in the dual route model was also illustrated in Publication #2. 6. To construct a database of writing-to-dictation of Chinese One minor hiccup experienced by the PI while conducting this project was that the research assistant, who received training during the employment period to convert the handwriting data into HTML codes, suddenly resigned several months before the revised completion date. At that time, most university graduates have already found jobs, which made recruitment difficult. For the available candidates, none of them demonstrated their willingness to learn to write HTML codes. Therefore, despite not being very competent webpage scripting, the PI has to take up the duties of converting the handwriting data into HTML codes on his own. The online database will be published online in the PI’s homepage hosted in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University’s server. A demo version is available here: https://mst-cbs.polyu.edu.hk/Resources/HandwritingDatabase/Demo.html The PI is working on the manuscript introducing this online database of handwriting data to-be-submitted to the Behavior Research Methods. The complete version of the online database will go live once the manuscript is accepted.

15608120.label: Major findings and research outcome
15608120.value: The results indicated significance of word frequency, character frequency, age-of-acquisition (AoA), imageability, semantic-radical-transparency (SRT), phonetic regularity and the interaction between phonetic regularity and character frequency in predicting both accuracy and RT of Chinese writing-to-dictation. Homophone density was found significant only in predicting RT but not accuracy. Total writing time was significantly predicted by AoA and character frequency. In a previous study (Han et al., 2012), it was suggested that the non-lexical pathway of Chinese writing-to-dictation operates primarily based on the mapping consistency from phonology to orthography. However, it was unclear whether this was driven by their task requirement which favored items with consistent phonology-to-orthography mappings. In this study, targeted characters were specified in the instruction by offering word contexts, e.g. 「背包嘅背字」 [“back” in the word “backpack”], to avoid the confounding. Results showed less robust effect of homophone density. Instead, larger proportions of the non-lexical operation should be driven by SRT, the phonetic regularity and its interaction with character frequency. Finally, results also indicated that both character and word frequencies significantly predicted writing-to-dictation performance. This can be explained by the unique hierarchical multi-level representations in the Chinese lexicon. Theoretically, the significance of lexical and non-lexical pathways in writing-to-dictation should be related to both feedforward and feedback relationship between phonology and orthography of the language. These were reported in Conference Presentations #1 and #2. They will be elaborated in Publication #3. The implied central and peripheral processes of Chinese character writing was illustrated in Publication #2. The online database of handwriting data will be published in the PI’s homepage (Other research output #3). The complete version of the database will be made publicly available once the corresponding manuscript, to-be-submitted to Behavior Research Methods (BRM) (Publication #3), is accepted. Finally, the PI created a 6-hour online learning module titled “Writing disorders and its intervention” accordingly (Other research output #2), which was made compulsory to all speech therapy students in HKPolyU. Empirical and theoretical findings were also shared with practicing speech therapists in invited seminars by the Hong Kong Association of Speech Therapists and the Education Bureau. Overall, the planned publications, including a journal article in BRM and two conference presentations were all achieved. Together with the published book chapter (Publication #2), and the upcoming journal article (Publication #3), the total dissemination outputs will exceed the planned targets.

15608120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15608120.value: The database will allow the investigation of peripheral processing of writing Chinese characters. Previous studies emphasized the importance of using prescribed stroke sequence in writing instructions. A quick look at the stroke sequence of the radical 扌 from the database indicated that only two third of the participants used prescribed stroke sequence (i.e. 一 to 亅 to ㇀) in their handwriting. The remaining tend to use another stroke sequence (i.e. 一 to ㇀to 亅). Further investigation will verify whether prescribed stroke sequence or simply consistent stroke sequence in handwriting should be emphasized in handwriting instructions. Next, in collaboration with colleagues, the PI identified 64 characters that can differentiate between good and poor writers and collected the corresponding writing-to-dictation performances from 120 secondary school students in Hong Kong. A writing-to-dictation screening test available to practicing speech therapists will be published soon to fulfil the service need. Finally, given the significance of both character and word frequencies observed, future studies that vary the word contexts of the stimuli can be conducted to investigate the possible interaction effect between word and character frequencies. Theoretically, the results will imply on the unique operation of the lexical pathway of writing-to-dictation in Chinese.

15608120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15608120.value: This study obtained the performance in a writing-to-dictation experiment involving 3126 Chinese characters from 50 native Cantonese speakers (gender-balanced). The results showed that while Chinese character writing shares similar cognitive mechanism as English word writing reported in the literature, distinct features have to be added to universal theories explaining word writing to accommodate the unique characteristics of Chinese. The results were reported in two international conference presentations, one publication in a high-impact journal and one peer-reviewed book chapter. One more high-impact journal publication is under preparation. The corresponding online database documenting the handwriting results obtained in the experiment will be made available to public once the publication is accepted. Student speech therapists studying in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University will have to complete a 6-hour online learning module before they graduate. Practicing speech therapists in Hong Kong also received training on theories of Chinese writing disorders and the corresponding intervention accordingly. It is expected that more speech therapists in Hong Kong will assume the responsibilities to delivery service to individuals with written language disorders. Finally, the results of the current study also created future directions for researchers to develop intervention tools readily made for Cantonese traditional Chinese.

15608820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15608820.value: 桃源的繼承人：中國鄉村文化的道教架構

15608820.label: Project Objectives
15608820.value: The project will enrich the prevalent textual study of Chinese cultural classics like Tao Qian’s Record of Peach Blossom Spring by adding perspectives gained from the living, ritual lore that refers itself to the same subject. Daoist manuscripts containing originary myths (genyin) of Peach Spring all articulate it as a sacred site, and situate it within discourses of ritual, divinity, local immortals’ cults, and efficacy. Thus, the project will first of all produce a detailed study of the largely unknown immortals’ cult of Peach Spring that has strong ties to both the local religious landscape (villages, caves, mountains) and to a classic, literary tradition. As a most basic contribution to the fields of Chinese Religious Studies, Cultural History, and perhaps Anthropology, the project will accumulate a wealth of data through collection of manuscripts circulating among Daoist priests. These data will be collected in a clearly delimited area of Hunan province where the PI has worked before and built up excellent connections to local priests, mostly in villages of Taoyuan County and around two towns in regions adjacent to it (Anhua 安化 and Xinhua 新化). All relevant materials will be made available for the larger public by digitizing the manuals’ contents and establishing an open-access, searchable database (see Research Plan). The use of a Daoist ritual perspective will open up new directions in itself, but also broadens the scope for existing methodologies. Although in the small field of Daoist studies scholars frequently take their cue from ritual materials, even they do not generally relate them to more mainstream Chinese topics as exemplified by the literary tradition of Peach Spring. What ritual has to offer beyond Daoist studies is its widespread role as a mediating force in the dissemination of culture. This should be fruitful for analyzing the dynamic of interaction between perceived spheres like “mainstream” and “local,” or other cultural spheres, like “vernacular” and “classical” Chinese, with implications for classifications of high or popular culture. Another objective pertains to academic disciplines themselves, as the scope of ritual may pose a challenge to overdetermined modern categories like “literature,” “history,” or “religion.” In the proposed project, the category of “ritual” has the potential to become a useful unit of assessment for scholars other than those working on religious topics. By examining ritual manuscripts and their ritual contexts for analyzing Peach Spring lore, the project will open up ritual as a new perspective in the study of Chinese cultural history, reconsidering its role as a constitutive element of traditional culture and the society that produces it. In sum, by combining textual analysis with fieldwork, literature and ritual, the disciplines of Religious Studies, Literature, and Cultural History can become conversation partners. In related vein, the project should have impact for the way in which Daoism is stereotypically viewed, especially when it comes to the seemingly esoteric practice of Daoist ritual. Debunking assumptions about Daoists as outsiders to society, the project will illustrate the specific contributions of Daoism in mediating the mongrel world of local lore with the more established institutions of traditional Chinese culture. This project will result in three tangible outcomes, in addition to the database mentioned in point 2 above: two research articles in well respected international journals (one top journal has already invited me to submit), and a chapter in my forthcoming monograph.

15608820.value: 本研究將從儀式角度切入，通過研究中國湖南省鄉村的壹系列道家古籍，探究當地傳統和普遍中國文化傳統的共同文化領域。研究的核心是著名詩人陶潛 (365? - 427)的經典作品《桃花源記》，在這故事中漁夫無意間發現了庇護著桃花源居民和平生活的壹片石窟。在陶潛的敘述中，桃花源的故事發生在武陵，即今天的常德。湖南北部的桃源縣毗鄰常德，它的名字讓傳說壹代代流傳了下去。在這片廣袤的土地上，人們認為石窟中的居民是靈驗的（女）神仙，而豐富的道家儀式傳統也圍繞著桃源仙境代代相傳。 由於這種地方傳說只記載於道教的儀式手冊之中，中國文化或文化史領域的學者迄今仍無法從中探究關於桃源仙境的觀念，而民俗學家往往卻又忽略了文學傳統。幸好，湖南諸多鄉間道士家庭世代相傳的斑駁古籍中有許多記載了對桃花源的描述，筆者因而能夠將它作為獨特的地方傳統來研究。重要的是，在地方上，它是解釋不同村落宗教崇拜的敘事框架，而每壹處村落都有獨特的道觀和踐禮。 本研究著眼於記敘了傳說根因的手稿，研究者將分析桃花源傳說的不同方面與片段：（1）. 如果桃花源是地方傳說的框架，有哪些傳統（儀式、本土宗教）被保留了下來？（2）.經典傳說與地方版本有何共同之處，這對於我們探究地方傳統和更主流中國文化間共同的文化領域又有何啟示？（3）.這種不朽的仙境又有什麽靈力？ 最後，研究者希望能夠將道教儀式研究發展為對其他學術學科有用的分析範，哪怕是在可能有儀式表現、卻對“宗教”內容毫無先驗興趣的研究中也是如此。

15608820.label: Realisation of objectives
15608820.value: Objective [1] has been fully achieved. I have produced exactly what I set out to do in this objective, namely to produce a detailed study of the cult of Peach Spring's transcendent beings (for details, see below, Objective #6, and the long abstract of my forthcoming monograph, in the section on Research Output). Objective [2], also, has been fully achieved. I have collected many manuscripts from Daoist priests (and vernacular masters), both in northern Hunan (Taoyuan County) and central Hunan (Anhua, Xinhua), exactly in the way I set out to do in this objective (also see below, Objective #6). A database has been established, currently containing 21 digitized, properly formatted, and searchable ritual manuscripts. The work will continue. Objective [3] is also fully achieved. My relevant publications, presentations, and conversations with peers over the past few years have – without exception – aimed to reveal the incontrovertible relevance (often: the clear centrality) of insights gained from fieldwork on Daoist ritual in Hunan province for understanding a wide variety of other topics within the traditional cultural mainstream and beyond Hunan. My article on the long history of Peach Spring as a sacred site (see below, Objective 6) has been able to relate the topic of Tao Qian’s famous story to various, hitherto unexplored, dimensions: Daoist institutions with clerics who performed Daoist ritual on site; sacrificial cults to local Daoist saints; and, importantly, the original inhabitants of the region that Tao Qian indicated as the area where his record was set. My forthcoming monograph fills in the blanks, and goes beyond it: the topic of Peach Spring is fully situated within an environment of Daoist ritual, allowing for a longue durée narrative on Peach Spring’s historical circumstances from the fourth century to the present. Objective [4], even more than objective [3], is very ambitious in its scope and remains an ongoing project – but I am confident that I have achieved exactly what I set out to do. My monograph quite powerfully presents ritual as a useful perspective in the study of Chinese cultural history, reconsidering its role as a constitutive element of traditional culture and the society that produces it. Key chapters in the monograph (Introduction; Chapter 1, Chapter 2, and Chapter 7) combine textual analysis with fieldwork, literature and ritual. I have built a forceful case for the argument that the disciplines of Religious Studies, Literature, and Cultural History can become conversation partners. Objective [5], again, is fully achieved. In relevant publications and presentations I have been able to show that Daoist clerics occupied key positions in traditional society, and that they contributed to local flourishing in quite a broad variety of ways: communal organization, ecological preservation, and dissemination of culture. Objective [6] has had several tangible outcomes. First and foremost, I would like to mention my forthcoming monograph, The Presence of Peach Spring: Ritual, Locality, Daoism, currently in press with Harvard University Asia Center (scheduled for publication in early 2026). This voluminous work is a detailed elaboration of all the Objectives listed above for this project. Beyond the items already mentioned, I would like to add that it the book is a serious attempt to engage “sinological” topics like Peach Spring in a comprehensive dialogue with entirely different fields, especially the History of Religion, Ritual Studies, Comparative Literature, Anthropology, and Art History. A long summary of the book is provided in section (C) on Research Output. Secondly, I have published an article that provided groundwork for the monograph, based on preliminary research done within the framework of this GRF project: “The Peach Blossom Spring’s Long History as a Sacred Site in Northern Hunan.” T’oung Pao 107, Issue 1-2 (2021): 1 – 39. The following relevant talks were presented by me: “The Presence of Female Immortals inside the Peach Flower Spring.” Keynote lecture, International Conference on “Historiography and Hagiography in Buddhism and Beyond.” Cambridge University (UK), July 8 – 10, 2024. “Peach Spring Abbey during the Ming Dynasty.” Paper presented at the AAR, panel A19-309 (Chinese Religions Unit and Daoist Studies Unit), San Antonio, November 2023 “Peach Spring: An Ancient Sacred Site and its Rituals.” NUS (Singapore), Department of Chinese Studies, Nov. 2022 “Peach Spring: Studying the History of a Sacred Site from the Perspective of Daoist Beliefs and Rituals” 桃源：由道教信仰與儀式來研究一個聖地的歷史. Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Feb. 2022 Finally, I have developed a database with ritual manuscripts in digitized, searchable format, hosted by the Data Repository of HKU Library: https://datahub.hku.hk/. The set of manuscripts is here:https://doi.org/10.25442/hku.c.7630964

rows: The project will enrich the prevalent textual study of Chinese cultural classics like Tao Qian’s Record of Peach Blossom Spring by adding perspectives gained from the living, ritual lore that refers itself to the same subject. Daoist manuscripts containing originary myths (genyin) of Peach Spring all articulate it as a sacred site, and situate it within discourses of ritual, divinity, local immortals’ cults, and efficacy. Thus, the project will first of all produce a detailed study of the largely unknown immortals’ cult of Peach Spring that has strong ties to both the local religious landscape (villages, caves, mountains) and to a classic, literary tradition.

As a most basic contribution to the fields of Chinese Religious Studies, Cultural History, and perhaps Anthropology, the project will accumulate a wealth of data through collection of manuscripts circulating among Daoist priests. These data will be collected in a clearly delimited area of Hunan province where the PI has worked before and built up excellent connections to local priests, mostly in villages of Taoyuan County and around two towns in regions adjacent to it (Anhua 安化 and Xinhua 新化). All relevant materials will be made available for the larger public by digitizing the manuals’ contents and establishing an open-access, searchable database (see Research Plan).

The use of a Daoist ritual perspective will open up new directions in itself, but also broadens the scope for existing methodologies. Although in the small field of Daoist studies scholars frequently take their cue from ritual materials, even they do not generally relate them to more mainstream Chinese topics as exemplified by the literary tradition of Peach Spring. What ritual has to offer beyond Daoist studies is its widespread role as a mediating force in the dissemination of culture. This should be fruitful for analyzing the dynamic of interaction between perceived spheres like “mainstream” and “local,” or other cultural spheres, like “vernacular” and “classical” Chinese, with implications for classifications of high or popular culture.

Another objective pertains to academic disciplines themselves, as the scope of ritual may pose a challenge to overdetermined modern categories like “literature,” “history,” or “religion.” In the proposed project, the category of “ritual” has the potential to become a useful unit of assessment for scholars other than those working on religious topics. By examining ritual manuscripts and their ritual contexts for analyzing Peach Spring lore, the project will open up ritual as a new perspective in the study of Chinese cultural history, reconsidering its role as a constitutive element of traditional culture and the society that produces it. In sum, by combining textual analysis with fieldwork, literature and ritual, the disciplines of Religious Studies, Literature, and Cultural History can become conversation partners.

In related vein, the project should have impact for the way in which Daoism is stereotypically viewed, especially when it comes to the seemingly esoteric practice of Daoist ritual. Debunking assumptions about Daoists as outsiders to society, the project will illustrate the specific contributions of Daoism in mediating the mongrel world of local lore with the more established institutions of traditional Chinese culture.

This project will result in three tangible outcomes, in addition to the database mentioned in point 2 above: two research articles in well respected international journals (one top journal has already invited me to submit), and a chapter in my forthcoming monograph.

15608820.label: Major findings and research outcome
15608820.value: The project has collected several dozens of ritual manuscripts used by Daoist (and other kinds of) priests in the region of Central Hunan. Using the data contained in these manuscripts, the PI has found that the topic of Peach Blossom Spring, hitherto mainly studied from literary perspectives, is not only not merely a lifeless literary fiction, but instead constitutes a vibrant tradition of local ritual traditions that perpetuate the lively presence of Peach Spring in several concrete ways: [1] Peach Spring is an ancient sacred site, exactly located in the region (Wuling) indicated by Tao Qian in his medieval tale, nowadays under the administrative region of Changde (northern Hunan province). Daoist abbeys and saints already mentioned in eighth-century sources continue to be renovated and otherwise patronized by pilgrims and other visitors. A long trail of historical records reveals the details of a local history with many ups and downs. [2] Peach Spring is alive in the same region, beyond the ancient Daoist institution, namely in the form of earthenware jars or bamboo tubes that are placed on domestic altars and consecrated as embodiments of the ancient site of Peach Spring. These objects have a beneficent effect on the flourishing of family, household, and livestock. [3] Peach Spring is alive, also in northern and central Hunan, through the spirit-possession of female mediums, who channel the presences and powers of Peach Spring's female transcendent beings (who dwell in the sacred space of Peach Spring). [4] Peach Spring is alive as a ritual tradition not only in majority Han ethnic communities, but also among ethnic minorities who have a long history in this region, especially the various Yao groups. For them, Peach Spring is a realm where the souls of the dead await reincarnation. Points [2] and [3], moreover, are closely intertwined with the ways in which villages organize their domestic business around the presence of Peach Spring's sacred beings, organizing frequent ritual occasions to maintain prosperity, inaugurate new life phases, and stabilize various physical and mental disturbances.

15608820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15608820.value: There is so much potential for further development of the research, especially in relation to the vernacular ritual traditions of the Plum Mountain region, which is one main topic in my ongoing GRF project. Furthermore, the ritual manuals already collected (and the thousands still remaining to be collected among the region's ritualists) will allow for fine-grained understanding of various topics: 1 - local pantheons 2 - relationship between local ritualists and more institutionalized traditions such as Daoism, Buddhism, and Confucianism 3 - ecological dynamics inherent in sacrificial traditions in honor of local, natural landmarks

15608820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15608820.value: This project has shown that Tao Yuanming's famous "Record of the Peach Blossom Spring" is best understood side by side with local traditions that belong to the same region mentioned in the opening line of the classical tale: northern Hunan province. The PI has identified a historically verifiable complex of living rituals centering on the tradition of Peach Spring, widespread throughout Hunan province, that circulated in Hunan at least since the eighth century. The ritual manuscripts collected in this region show that Peach Spring continues to be an important element in the communal life of Hunan villagers.

15609420.value: 重探非詞複誦測試對診斷患有發展性語言障礙的粵語兒童之準確性

15609420.label: Co - Investigator(s)

15609420.label: Project Objectives
15609420.value: Revisit and improve the diagnostic accuracy of nonword repetition for the identiﬁcation of Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) in L1 Cantonese-speaking children, by testing the hypotheses that NWR tasks which incorporate abilities in phonological processing, storage capacity, statistical learning, and lexical knowledge would better differentiate typically developing children and children with DLD. Specify the underlying abilities assessed by NWR in Cantonese-speaking children with and without DLD, by testing whether and how independent measures of these abilities would predict individual differences in NWR performance, which would advance our understanding of the nature of deficits in Cantonese-speaking children with DLD.

15609420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609420.value: Nonword Repetition (NWR) tasks are used cross-linguistically to discriminate between children with Specific Language Impairment (SLI; more recently “Developmental Language Disorder (DLD)”, Bishop et al., 2016) and their typically-developing peers. NWR has been described as a clinical marker of SLI/DLD, and is one of the most sensitive measures in identifying bilingual children with SLI/DLD (Armon-Lotem, de Jong & Meir, 2015). NWR has been shown to not discriminate between Cantonese-speaking children with and without DLD (Stokes, Wong, Fletcher & Leonard, 2006), making Cantonese an interesting exception cross-linguistically. However, little published research has revisited this line of investigation in child Cantonese. This project re-examines the diagnostic accuracy of NWR in identifying DLD in child Cantonese. The project addresses these important issues: first, are there ways to improve the diagnostic strength of NWR in identifying DLD in Cantonese? Second, what abilities underlie the ability of Cantonese-speaking children with and without DLD to repeat nonwords? Our project adapts the quasi-universal NWR task from the European COST Action IS0804 “Language Impairment in a Multilingual Society: Linguistic Pattern and the Road to Assessment” into Cantonese to assess Hong Kong children with and without DLD. This task has been shown to be better at disentangling language impairment and language disadvantage due to less language experience than more language-specific measures in some languages. We will compare it with two other NWR tasks with more and less Cantonese word-like stimuli respectively, to evaluate their differentiation of Cantonese children with and without DLD. A corpus study and an adult rating study will be conducted to determine what stimuli are more/less Cantonese-like. A number of predictor variables are included to evaluate the underlying abilities assessed by our NWR tasks, to shed light on the nature and source of difficulty of NWR tasks for Cantonese children with DLD. To delimit the project scope, this project focuses on children acquiring Cantonese as their first language without extensive/intensive exposure to other languages. This application will bring Cantonese research in line with current international trends and standards, and add an important cross-linguistic perspective on using NWR to identify DLD. The findings allow us to better understand the nature of difficulties in NWR in children with and without DLD. The project also has important societal impact as it will lay necessary groundwork for further research on using NWR measures to improve the identification of DLD in Cantonese-speaking bilingual children, an important area largely lacking assessment tools. 重探非詞複誦測試對診斷患有發展性語言障礙的粵語兒童之準確性 研究顯示，非詞複誦測試（Nonword Repetition）能在不同語言中辨別患有「特殊語言障礙」 (Specific Language Impairment; 最近稱為「發展性語言障礙」（Developmental Language Disorder）的兒童及發展正常的同齡兒童。在非詞複誦測試中表現明顯困難，曾被認為是「特殊語言障礙」或「發展性語言障礙」 的一個臨床標記。在文獻中，也是其中一個最敏感的方法來識別一些患有「特殊語言障礙」或「發展性語言障礙」 的雙語兒童。然而 ，也曾有研究顯示，非詞複誦測試不能辨別患有及沒有「發展性語言障礙」的的粵語兒童，使粵語在跨語言中看似為一個例外。但是，很少再有已發表的研究以粵語兒童為對象重探這一研究議題。 此研究項目會重新探討非詞複誦測試對診斷患有「發展性語言障礙」的粵語兒童之準確性。主要研究議題為：如何提高非詞複誦測試，在粵語中識別「發展性語言障礙」的診斷強度？對於患有及沒有「發展性語言障礙」的粵語兒童，非詞複誦涉及什麽基礎能力？ 此研究把歐洲重點研究項目《COST Action IS0804》「多語言社會中的語言障礙：語言模式與評估之路」 的非詞複誦測試改編為粵語，來測試患有或者沒有「發展性語言障礙」的香港兒童。有其他語言研究顯示，這測試與一些較接近特定語言的非詞複誦測試相比，較適合用於區分患有語言障礙的兒童與因較少語言經驗而語言表現遜色的兒童。我們將這測試與其他兩個分別以比較近似粵語單詞和比較不近似粵語單詞組成的非詞複誦測試進行比較，以評估這些非詞複誦測試對患有或者沒有「發展性語言障礙」的粵語兒童之區分能力。我們將進行語料庫研究和成人評級研究，以確定哪些非詞音節比較近似或不近似粵語單詞。我們亦會加入多項預測變量，以評估這些非詞複誦測試所涉及的基礎能力，以闡明患有「發展性語言障礙」的粵語兒童在非詞複誦測試中，表現的困難之性質和根源。為了劃定研究範圍，此項目著重研究以粵語為母語及家庭語言，同時沒有恆常大量接觸其他語言的兒童。 此研究項目令粵語研究與當前的國際趨勢和標準接軌，並為使用非詞複誦測試來識別「發展性語言障礙」添加重要的跨語言觀點。所得結果能使我們更了解患有「發展性語言障礙」的兒童在非詞複誦測試中，表現的困難之性質。此項目還具有重要的社會應用價值，能為未來研究，探討非詞複誦測試能否在粵語雙語兒童中，識別「發展性語言障礙」奠定必要的基礎 。如何為粵語雙語兒童識別「發展性語言障礙」，此重要的研究議題現時一直缺乏有效的診斷工具。

15609620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15609620.value: 社會企業的正當性與顧客惠顧意願

15609620.label: Project Objectives
15609620.value: To develop a new research direction in social entrepreneurship and policy research using an organization-customer-policy perspective. To develop a process model to better understand the factors and mechanisms underlying customer patronage behavior towards social enterprises’ products and services. To empirically test how different types of social enterprise legitimacy and policy design jointly affect customer patronage behavior. To provide insights for policy interventions that better support social enterprises and better educate the public about the roles of social enterprises in the society. To contribute to policy debates on the necessity for certification, government financial incentives for social enterprises and mechanisms that enhance sustainable (i.e., long-term) customer patronage for social enterprises’ products and services. To develop a more resilient social enterprise sector by providing advice on how to better attract customers to patronize and support social enterprises’ product and services. To introduce and popularize the use of (field and lab) experimental paradigm in research, teaching and learning in social entrepreneurship and social enterprise. 15609620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609620.value: In recent years, social entrepreneurship has emerged as an important approach to creating public value (Teasdale & Dey, 2019). Social enterprises are a key partner of nonprofits and the government in solving many of the public problems (e.g., inequality) that none of the sectors can do alone (Defourny et al., 2014). The fast-growing interest in social entrepreneurship research (Terjesen et al., 2016) suggests that research in this field needs to go beyond studying the “supply side” of social entrepreneurship – the organizations – (e.g., Tracey & Phillips, 2016). Much research is needed to understand the “demand side”, especially the role of customers as the engine of revenue and value creation for social enterprises. Studying the demand side is important because customer patronization (i.e., purchase behavior) is a key driver of social enterprise’s economic survival. Importantly, an understanding of customer patronage behavior will enable more effective policy interventions (Tummers, 2019). As a relatively new sector and organizational form that combines social and commercial goals (Battilana & Lee, 2014), social enterprises are susceptible to external legitimacy issues as they need to convince external constituents (e.g., customers) of their “good citizenship” while demonstrating commercial viability. Legitimacy is a key determinant of survival and success for all organizations (Hannan & Freeman, 1984) and is crucial to attracting customers and resources (Shepherd & Zacharakis, 2003). Despite the centrality of legitimacy and policy for social enterprise (Dart, 2004; Teasdale & Dey, 2019), very little research investigates the roles and consequences of legitimacy for social enterprise, the effects of policy design and how they influence customers patronization in terms of purchase intention and behavior towards social enterprises. Given the importance of legitimacy, customers and policy for social enterprises, it is valuable to investigate the social enterprise-customer-policy nexus and how relevant factors and mechanisms play out in this nexus. This proposal aims to examine how social enterprise’s economic, moral, and origin legitimacy will interact with policy design (i.e., government financial support) to jointly affect customer patronization (e.g., purchase intention and behavior) towards social enterprises. We propose three complimentary studies to explore and test the relationships among these factors. The first study will be a qualitative, theory building research. The second and the third studies will use field and lab experiments to manipulate different kinds of legitimacy to test how legitimacy and government financial support jointly affect real consumers’ perceptions and purchase behavior in Hong Kong. 近年來，社會企業家精神已成為創造公共價值的重要途徑（Teasdale & Dey, 2019）。 社會企業是非營利組織和政府在解決許多公共部門無法獨立解決的公共問題（例如不平等）方面的重要合作夥伴（Defourny et al., 2014）。 對社會企業家精神研究快速增長的興趣（Terjesen et al., 2016）表明，該領域不僅要研究社會企業家精神的“供給方”，即組織（例如，Tracey & Phillips, 2016），更加需要進行大量研究才能理解“需求方”，尤其是顧客在社會企業中作為收入來源和價值創造的角色。 研究需求方很重要，因為顧客的光顧（即購買行為）是社會企業經濟生存的關鍵驅動力。 重要的是，了解顧客惠顧行為將使政策干預更加有效（Tummers, 2019）。 作為結合了社會和商業目標的相對較新的部門和組織形式（Battilana & Lee, 2014），社會企業容易受到外部正當性問題的影響，因為它們需要向外部成員（例如顧客）證明自己“良好公民身份”的同時，也要證明自己的商業可行性。 正當性是所有組織生存與成功的關鍵性決定因素（Hannan & Freeman, 1984），對於吸引顧客和資源至關重要（Shepherd & Zacharakis, 2003）。 儘管正當性和社會企業政策十分重要 (Dart, 2004; Teasdale & Dey, 2019），很少有研究從正當性的角度研究正當性對社會企業的作用和後果，對政策設計的影響，以及在購買意圖和行為方面如何影響顧客光顧社會企業。 考慮到正當性，顧客和社會企業政策的重要性，研究社會企業-顧客-政策關係以及相關因素和機制如何在這關係中發揮作用很有價值。 該研究計劃旨在研究社會企業的經濟，道德和出身的正當性如何與政策設計（即政府財政支持）相互作用，共同影響對社會企業的顧客惠顧（例如購買意圖和行為）。 我們提出了三個互補的研究來探索和檢測這些因素之間的關係。 第一項研究將是定性的理論構建研究。 第二和第三項研究將使用現場實驗和實驗室實驗來控制不同類型的正當性，以探索正當性和政府的財政支持如何共同影響香港實際消費者的觀念和購買行為。

16100820.label: Project Objectives
16100820.value: To characterize CDK5RAP2-CM1 autoinhibition We found that the conserved segment 96–117 in CDK5RAP2 CM1 possesses binding and inhibitory activities toward the γTuNA and thus, we named this conserved region the γTuNA-inhibitor (γTuNA-In) domain. The direct interaction between the γTuNA and the γTuNA-In domain will be validated in binding assays of purified recombinant proteins. Reconstitution of the γTuNA with isolated γTuRCs in the presence of the γTuNA-In protein will be performed to evaluate the inhibitory function of the γTuNA-In. Next, we will investigate the following potential mechanisms by which the γTuNA-In inhibits the γTuNA. First, the binding of the γTuNA-In may mask the γTuRC-binding site on the γTuNA. Second, the γTuRC interaction may require the γTuNA to undergo dimerization or oligomerization, and the interaction with the γTuNA-In may disrupt γTuNA dimerization/oligomerization, resulting in γTuNA inhibition. In addition, we plan to solve the solution structure of the γTuNA and CM1 by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. This will allow us to gain a better understanding of the autoinhibitory mechanism. To reveal the role of CDK5RAP2-CM1 autoinhibition in microtubule organization We created the double mutation I104A/E105A, which is located within the γTuNA-In domain, thereby generating a CDK5RAP2 mutant that harbors constitutively active CM1. We will generate cell lines that stably express the CDK5RAP2 mutant I104A/E105A by using the CRISPR/Cas9 system to edit the cdk5rap2 gene. As an alternative approach, we can perform rescue experiments of cdk5rap2 knockdown or knockout by inducible expression of the mutant and wild-type CDK5RAP2. The following functional assays will be conducted on I104A/E105A- and the wild type-expressing cells: (1) Microtubule nucleation at subcellular sites, such as centrosomes and the Golgi complex, will be evaluated in microtubule regrowth assays or by time-lapse microscopy of microtubule growth in an EB1-GFP stable line, (2) microtubule organization in interphase and mitosis will be visualized by immunofluorescence microscopy or by time-lapse microscopy of living cells, and (3) we will analyze the cellular activities that require Golgi-derived microtubules, and these activities include Golgi assembly and structural organization, protein trafficking, and cell polarization and directional migration. To further explore the function of CM1 autoinhibition, we will test the effect of the I104A/E105A mutant on the formation of epithelial structures by using three-dimensional (3D) culture systems, such as acinar formation of breast epithelial MCF10A cells in 3D Matrigel culture. The assays of 3D culture together with those of 2D culture will provide information on the cellular function of CM1 autoinhibition. To identify mechanisms that counteract CDK5RAP2-CM1 autoinhibition We will investigate whether CDK5RAP2-CM1 autoinhibition is disrupted by CDK5RAP2 phosphorylation and by CM1 association with other proteins. CDK5RAP2 is phosphorylated at Ser112 and Ser140 and moreover, phosphomimetic mutation of either of them enhanced the γTuRC-binding activity of CM1. Reconstitution assays will be performed with the phosphomimetic and non-phosphorylatable mutants of CM1 constructs that contain the phosphorylation sites to validate the phosphorylation effects. In addition, the recombinant proteins of wild-type CM1 will be phosphorylated by respective kinases, such as Nek2 for Ser112, to assess the effects on the autoinhibition. The cellular impact of the phosphorylation will be assessed by using the phosphomimetic and non-phosphorylatable mutants in the complementation experiments of cdk5rap2 knockdown or knockout. To examine the spatiotemporal patterns of CDK5RAP2 phosphorylation, we will generate phosphorylation site- and state-specific antibodies of CDK5RAP2. Alternatively, we will apply targeted mass spectrometry, which is based on methods such as selected reaction monitoring, in conjunction with subcellular fractionation to analyze the distribution of phosphorylated CDK5RAP2. We will also search for cellular proteins that interact with CM1 by using the tandem affinity purification approach, and the subsequently identified interactions will be functionally characterized to reveal their physiological consequences. The phosphorylation and the protein-protein interaction analyses will inform how CM1 autoinhibition is disrupted in specific cellular events.
