16201220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201220.value: This research project has generated significant outcomes in advancing MEMS-based thermal flow sensor technology, particularly in achieving ultra-low flow detection capabilities. The key research outcomes are documented in several high-impact publications: Technical Breakthroughs: Our most significant achievement was the development of an integrated CMOS-MEMS thermal flow sensor with unprecedented detection limits, as reported in IEEE MEMS 2020 (Xu et al.). The sensor achieved a remarkable minimum detectable flow velocity (MDFV) of 30μm/s and resolution of 60μm/s at zero flow conditions, representing a significant advancement in the field. The sensor demonstrated excellent normalized sensitivity of 533μV/(m/s)/mW while maintaining low power consumption (<13.1mW). Key Publications: The research outcomes were documented in several peer-reviewed publications: "CMOS Compatible MEMS Air Velocity Sensor With Improved Sensitivity and Linearity for Human Thermal Comfort Sensing Applications" (IEEE Sensors Journal, 2021) detailed the sensor's design optimization and practical applications. "Integrated Predicted Mean Vote Sensing System Using MEMS Multi-Sensors for Smart HVAC Systems" (IEEE Sensors Journal, 2021) demonstrated system-level integration capabilities. "Bidirectional CMOS-MEMS Airflow Sensor With Sub-mW Power Consumption and High Sensitivity" (2022) showcased power optimization achievements. "A Real-Time Wireless Calorimetric Flow Sensor System with a Wide Linear Range for Low-Cost Respiratory Monitoring" (2023) illustrated practical applications in healthcare monitoring. Theoretical Contributions: We developed a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding mixed convection effects in microscale devices, particularly in the crucial regime where Gr/Re²>1. This included a novel semi-empirical model for predicting sensor performance and noise characteristics, providing valuable design guidelines for future developments in the field. Technological Impact: The research has established new benchmarks for MEMS flow sensor performance, particularly in: Ultra-low flow detection capabilities Power efficiency Integration density System-level implementation These achievements have attracted international attention, leading to collaboration with Delft University of Technology and potential commercial applications in micro/nanofluidics and biomedical devices. The research has also contributed to human capital development through the successful completion of a PhD thesis focusing on micro thermal comfort sensing systems for indoor HVAC applications. The project's outcomes have significantly advanced the field of MEMS flow sensors and established a strong foundation for future developments in ultra-sensitive flow detection technologies.

16201220.value: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action The successful development of ultra-sensitive CMOS MEMS thermal flow sensors opens several promising avenues for further research and development: 1 Power Optimization: Development of new low-power readout circuits using advanced CMOS technology Implementation of intelligent power management schemes for wireless applications Integration of energy harvesting capabilities for self-powered operation 2 System Integration: Development of multi-sensor arrays for distributed flow field mapping Integration with wireless communication modules for IoT applications Implementation of advanced signal processing algorithms for noise reduction 3 Application Extensions: Adaptation for biomedical applications, particularly in respiratory monitoring Integration into smart building HVAC systems for improved thermal comfort Development of specialized versions for industrial process monitoring 4 Performance Enhancement: Investigation of alternative materials and structures for improved sensitivity Development of compensation techniques for environmental variations Implementation of machine learning algorithms for smart calibration Proposed course of action includes: Collaboration with industry partners for commercialization Development of application-specific prototypes Further investigation of noise reduction techniques Integration with emerging IoT platforms These developments will be pursued through new research proposals and industrial collaborations, building upon the current project's successful outcomes.

16201220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201220.value: Imagine being able to detect the slightest movement of air, even slower than a falling snowflake. This project has developed a tiny electronic sensor that can do exactly that, measuring air movement as slow as 30 micrometers per second - about 1,000 times slower than a gentle breeze. Our sensor, called a CMOS MEMS thermal flow sensor, is smaller than a fingernail and uses advanced microchip technology to detect incredibly small air movements by measuring tiny temperature differences. Think of it as a highly sensitive electronic thermometer that can feel which way the air is moving. The sensor is extremely energy-efficient, using less power than a typical LED. This breakthrough is particularly exciting for developing next-generation smart buildings. When integrated into building automation systems, these sensors can create "intelligent" environments that precisely control air flow and temperature. This leads to significantly improved energy efficiency - buildings with our sensors could reduce their energy consumption and carbon footprint by optimizing heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. Given that buildings account for about 40% of global energy consumption, this technology could make a substantial contribution to global carbon reduction efforts. The technology is cost-effective for mass production as it uses standard computer chip manufacturing processes. This makes it ideal for widespread deployment in smart building systems, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and artificial intelligence-powered building management systems, paving the way for more sustainable and comfortable living environments while fighting climate change.

16201320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201320.value: Deep learning has received considerable empirical successes in recent years. However, while many ad hoc tricks have been discovered by practitioners, there has been a severe lack of theoretical foundations for tricks invented in the deep learning literature. This lack of theoretical understanding has hindered the further development of deep learning. It was known by practitioners that over-parameterized neural networks (NNs) are easy to learn. In the past two years, there have been important theoretical developments in the analysis of over-parameterized NNs. In particular, it was shown that such systems behave like convex systems under various restricted settings, such as for two-level NNs, and when learning is restricted locally in the so-called neural tangent kernel space around specialized initializations. However, no theoretical techniques have been discovered that can analyze fully trained deep neural networks (DNNs) encountered in practice. The objective of this proposal is to solve this fundamental and challenging problem by investigating such overparameterized DNNs when fully trained. We will develop the following fundamental theoretical results: (i) A new technique called neural feature repopulation, which can be used to reformulate NNs. It is shown that under such reformulation, overparameterized DNNs are inherently convex globally, and when fully optimized, the system can learn effective feature representations suitable for the underlying learning task. (ii) With the new formulation, we will further investigate the convergence of the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm, and will design new optimization algorithms to accelerate training. (iii) With the new formulation, we will investigate the benefit of DNNs over shallow networks in terms of representation power, and design better network structures. Our highly unexpected theoretical result is a breakthrough in developing a better understanding of deep learning. It can satisfactorily explain the empirical success of DNNs that are fully trained using standard optimization methods. It establishes a solid theoretical foundation for deep learning, and can be used to guide the design of better learning algorithms in the future. 近年来，深度学习在实践上获得巨大成功。 尽管研究人员发现了许多特殊的技巧，这些基于实践的技巧仍然缺乏理论基础。 这个问题已经阻碍了深度学习的进一步发展。 研究人员从机器学习实践中发现超参数化神经网络易于学习。基于这个现象，在过去两年中，对超参数化神经网络的分析取得了重要的理论进展。 可以证明在各种受限设置下，过参数化两层神经网络类似于凸系统。 但是目前没有可以分析深度神经网络的理论框架。 这个研究目的是建立过参数化深度神经网络理论。我们专注以下几点：建立一个新的理论框架，证明过度参数化的深度神经网络在全局有凸性。使用新的方法研究随机梯度下降算法的收敛性，并设计新的优化算法以加快训练速度。我们将研究深度网络相对浅层网络在表示能力方面的优势，并设计更好的网络结构。

16201420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201420.value: 從2D圖像學習3D外觀具有挑戰性，因為圖像是相應3D世界的2D投影，其中對象可能會經歷複雜的變形和遮擋。該項目著重於人類的圖像，其不同的姿勢引入了複雜的非剛性變形和自閉塞。計算機視覺中的現有相關工作 機器學習要使用某種形式的3D模型來產生高質量的結果，或在只允許使用圖像的情況下產生分辨率較低的輸出圖像沒有使用3D信息。 具體來說，給一個人的參考圖像，我們提出的方法可以無縫轉移在保持高質量的同時對目標姿勢的人的參考外觀參考人的服裝質地，同時真實地產生幻覺它們在目標姿勢下的複雜外觀。請注意網絡不僅應移動相應的身體部位以匹配目標姿勢，而且還可以現實地將看不見的身體/服裝零件上漆或幻化在輸入中由於遮擋。 由於3D人體的非剛性特性，這對於人體圖像而言尤其具有挑戰性身體以及人類穿著的3D服裝上複雜的紋理和幾何變形。 為了應對這些挑戰，我們建議 1.新穎的姿勢指導的外觀轉移網絡，以前所未有的方式將給定的參考外觀轉換為目標姿勢圖像分辨率，分別給出參考人物和目標人物的圖像。 2.新穎的局部描述詞（漸進的局部感知損失+局部區分詞以最高分辨率）以增強局部細節和生成質量； 3.我們對自動編碼器體系結構進行漸進式訓練以實現輸出前所未有的高分辨率。 據我們所知，這種提議的方法是第一個漸進式深度編碼器-解碼器傳輸網絡可以在目標上如此高分辨率地產生幻覺穿著的衣服的外觀，包括先前被遮擋的部分參考圖片。

16201420.label: Realisation of objectives
16201420.value: The four project objectives have been achieved with a journal paper published. See "Research Outputs". Based on the research findings and results on pose transfer on videos in this project, we investigate deep video matting and sematic image matting for extracting humans in complex poses as well as other non-rigid objects from a video/image, and published two CVPR'21 papers (see "Research Output"). Despite the significant progress made by deep learning in natural image matting, there has been so far no representative work on deep learning for video matting due to the inherent technical challenges in reasoning temporal domain and lack of large-scale video matting datasets. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based video matting framework which employs a novel and effective spatio-temporal feature aggregation module (ST-FAM). As optical flow estimation can be very unreliable within matting regions, ST-FAM is designed to effectively align and aggregate information across different spatial scales and temporal frames within the network decoder. To eliminate frame-by-frame trimap annotations, a lightweight interactive trimap propagation network is also introduced. The other contribution consists of a large-scale video matting dataset with groundtruth alpha mattes for quantitative evaluation and real-world high-resolution videos with trimaps for qualitative evaluation. Quantitative and qualitative experimental results show that our framework significantly outperforms conventional video matting and deep image matting methods applied to video in presence of multi-frame temporal information. Our dataset is available at https://github.com/nowsyn/DVM. The other CVPR'21 paper (see "Research Output") is related to matting humans in different poses: natural image matting separates the foreground from background in fractional occupancy which can be caused by highly transparent objects, complex foreground (e.g., net or tree), and/or objects containing very fine details (e.g., hairs). Although conventional matting formulation can be applied to all of the above cases, no previous work has attempted to reason the underlying causes of matting due to various foreground semantics. We show how to obtain better alpha mattes by incorporating into our framework semantic classification of matting regions. Specifically, we consider and learn 20 classes of matting patterns, and propose to extend the conventional trimap to semantic trimap. The proposed semantic trimap can be obtained automatically through patch structure analysis within trimap regions. Meanwhile, we learn a multi-class discriminator to regularize the alpha prediction at semantic level, and content-sensitive weights to balance different regularization losses. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our method outperforms other methods and has achieved the most competitive state-of-the-art performance. Finally, we contribute a large-scale Semantic Image Matting Dataset with careful consideration of data balancing across different semantic classes. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/nowsyn/SIM. Pose transfer in the presence of occlusion is an important issue to address to produce realistic transfer results. In this ICCV'21 paper (see "Research Output"), we investigate occlusion-aware video object inpainting. Conventional video inpainting is neither object-oriented nor occlusion-aware, making it liable to obvious artifacts when large occluded object regions are inpainted. This paper presents occlusion-aware video object inpainting, which recovers both the complete shape and appearance for occluded objects in videos given their visible mask segmentation. To facilitate this new research, we construct the first large scale video object inpainting benchmark YouTube-VOI to provide realistic occlusion scenarios with both occluded and visible object masks available. Our technical contribution VOIN jointly performs video object shape completion and occluded texture generation. In particular, the shape completion module models long-range object coherence while the flow completion module recovers accurate flow with sharp motion boundary, for propagating temporally-consistent texture to the same moving object across frames. For more realistic results, VOIN is optimized using both TPatchGAN and a new spatio-temporal attention-based multi-class discriminator. Finally, we compare VOIN and strong baselines on YouTube VOI. Experimental results clearly demonstrate the efficacy of our method including inpainting complex and dynamic objects. VOIN degrades gracefully with inaccurate input visible mask. Progressive training in autoencoder architecture was applied in this project. Combining this and furthering research on occlusion-awareness, we developed new architecture for deep occlusion-aware instance segmentation with overlapping bilayers, which was published in CVPR'21 (see "Research Output"). Segmenting highly-overlapping objects is challenging, because typically no distinction is made between real object contours and occlusion boundaries. Unlike previous two-stage instance segmentation methods, we model image formation as composition of two overlapping layers, and propose Bilayer Convolutional Network (BCNet), where the top GCN layer detects the occluding objects (occluder) and the bottom GCN layer infers partially occluded instance (occludee). The explicit modeling of occlusion relationship with bilayer structure naturally decouples the boundaries of both the occluding and occluded instances, and considers the interaction between them during mask regression. We validate the efficacy of bilayer decoupling on both one-stage and two-stage object detectors with different back-bones and network layer choices. Despite its simplicity, extensive experiments on COCO and KINS show that our occlusion-aware BCNet achieves large and consistent performance gain especially for heavy occlusion cases. Code is available at https://github.com/lkeab/BCNet. Identifying multiple humans and objects for pose transfer are necessary. In this CVPR'21 paper (see "Research Output"), We present a novel group collaborative learning framework (GCoNet) capable of detecting co-salient objects in real time (16ms), by simultaneously mining consensus representations at group level based on the two necessary criteria: 1) intra-group compactness to better formulate the consistency among co-salient objects by capturing their inherent shared attributes using our novel group affinity module; 2) inter-group separability to effectively suppress the influence of noisy objects on the output by introducing our new group collaborating module conditioning the inconsistent consensus. To learn a better embedding space without extra computational overhead, we explicitly employ auxiliary classification supervision. Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks, i.e., CoCA, CoSOD3k, and Cosal2015, demonstrate that our simple GCoNet outperforms 10 cutting-edge models and achieves the new state-of-the-art. We demonstrate this paper’s new technical contributions on a number of important downstream computer vision applications including content aware co-segmentation, co localization based automatic thumbnails, etc. Code has been made publicly available: https://github.com/fanq15/GCoNet. Finally, interactive segmentation is fundamental to human pose transfer in the presence of very complex poses. In this CVPR'21 paper (see "Research Output"), we present Modular interactive VOS (MiVOS) framework which decouples interaction-to-mask and mask propagation, allowing for higher generalizability and better performance. Trained separately, the interaction module converts user interactions to an object mask, which is then temporally propagated by our propagation module using a novel top-k filtering strategy in reading the space-time memory. To effectively take the user’s intent into account, a novel difference-aware module is proposed to learn how to properly fuse the masks before and after each interaction, which are aligned with the target frames by employing the space-time memory. We evaluate our method both qualitatively and quantitatively with different forms of user interactions (e.g., scribbles, clicks) on DAVIS to show that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art algorithms while requiring fewer frame interactions, with the additional advantage in generalizing to different types of user interactions. We contribute a large-scale synthetic VOS dataset with pixel-accurate segmentation of 4.8M frames to accompany our source codes to facilitate future research.

16201420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201420.value: Humans are interactive animals and thus closely related to human pose depicted on videos, the main research topic in this project. We investigate interactive humans and the relevant findings are reported in CVPR'22 "Interactiveness Field in Human-Object Interactions", ICCV'23 "EgoPCA: A New Framework for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Understanding" and CVPR'24 "Gear-NeRF: Free-Viewpoint Rendering and Tracking with Motion-aware Spatio-Temporal Sampling" (see Research Outputs). While 2D human poses and transfer were investigated in this project, detecting and recognizing 3D human poses are instrumental in computer vision and robotics applications. Capitalizing on the findings against the objectives (section 5.3 above), we developed 3D detection and segmentation algorithms for neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and published the findings in NeurIPS'22 "Unsupervised Multi-View Object Segmentation Using Radiance Field Propagation", CVPR'23 "NeRF-RPN: A general framework for object detection in NeRFs", ICCV'23 "Instance Neural Radiance Field", and CVPR'24 "SANeRF-HQ: Segment Anything for NeRF in High Quality" (see Research Outputs). With these fundamental contributions on static NeRFs, 3D spatio-temporal poses and motion can be detected and tracked, as in the aforementioned CVPR'24 paper. Unlike 2D humans poses, 3D data is scarcer and more difficult to acquire. Thus research in few shot learning is underway, where less reliance on local descriptors and progressive training can be achieved given the rapid development of stable diffusion models and multimodal language model, best exemplified by the recent breakthrough in OpenAI's SORA. In this regard, our findings in few shot learning are reported in three papers at ECCV'22 (see Research Outputs), namely, "Few-Shot Video Object Detection", "Few-Shot Object Detection with Model Calibration" and "Self-Support Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation".

16201420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201420.value: Poses can be regarded as a modality different from image for visual understanding. With the recent emergence of multimodal large language model, we started a preliminary investigation on multimodal content generation and reported preliminary findings in CVPR'24 (see Research Outputs), where we present Compound Conditioned ControlNet, C3Net, a novel generative neural architecture taking conditions from multiple modalities and synthesizing multimodal contents simultaneously (e.g., image, text, audio, and poses in the future). C3Net adapts the ControlNet architecture to jointly train and make inferences on a production-ready diffusion model and its trainable copies. Specifically, C3Net first aligns the conditions from multi-modalities to the same semantic latent space using modality-specific encoders based on contrastive training. Then, it generates multimodal outputs based on the aligned latent space. Our model offers an improved solution for joint modality generation through learning and explaining multimodal conditions, involving more than just linear interpolation within the latent space. Meanwhile, as we align conditions to a unified latent space, C3Net only requires one trainable Control C3-UNet to work on multimodal semantic information. We contribute the first high-quality tri-modal validation set to validate quantitatively that C3Net outperforms or is on par with the first and contemporary state-of-the-art multimodal generation.

16201420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201420.value: We propose a novel pose-guided appearance transfer network for transferring a given reference appearance to a target pose in unprecedented image resolution (1024 * 1024), given respectively an image of the reference and target person. No 3D model is used. Instead, our network utilizes dense local descriptors including local perceptual loss and local discriminators to refine details, which is trained progressively in a coarse-to-fine manner to produce the high-resolution output to faithfully preserve complex appearance of garment textures and geometry, while hallucinating seamlessly the transferred appearances including those with dis-occlusion. Our progressive encoder-decoder architecture can learn the reference appearance inherent in the input image at multiple scales. Extensive experimental results on the Human3.6M dataset, the DeepFashion dataset, and our dataset collected from YouTube show that our model produces high-quality images, which can be further utilized in useful applications such as garment transfer between people and pose-guided human video generation.

16201620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201620.value: 流感病毒带来了严重的全球公共卫生问题。仅在香港，流感病毒造成每年400多人死亡，12000人住院，高达数百万美元的经济损失。预防或减少流感流行的一个关键因素是必须定期更新的季节性疫苗。 该项目将运用前沿的机器学习算法来解决与疫苗研发和更新过程相关中的关键问题。在基础水平上，它将通过提出能够预测流感病毒毒株对之间“抗原距离”的自动化智能模型，来解决流感疫苗开发中的核心问题，即是否需要更新当前的流感疫苗。“抗原距离”是一个生物学的量化指标，用于量化由一种毒株所产生的抗体中和另一种毒株的能力。它被世界卫生组织用于量化现有流感疫苗的效力，并据此判断是否需要更新疫苗和新疫苗的组成成分。目前测量抗原距离的方法主要包括需要专业知识的血清学实验，此类方法需要耗费大量的时间和财力。 该项目的主要创新点是提出一种无需新的血清学实验就能预测毒株对间抗原距离的新方法。我们将引入一个基于深层神经网络（deep neural network, DNN）的模型，来根据病毒毒株对之间遗传序列的差异预测它们之间的抗原距离。该模型可使用病毒序列的大数据信息进行训练来获得，这些序列信息可相对容易地从常规的流感监测和之前进行过的血清学实验中获得。DNN是一种很适合解决这个问题的框架，因为一对病毒毒株间遗传序列的差异和它们的抗原距离之间的映射关系是非常复杂和高度非线性的，并且这种映射关系很难用传统的机器学习方法解出。能准确预测病毒毒株间抗原距离的模型能够对关于是否更新疫苗的决策提出非常有意义的参考，目前关于是否更新疫苗的决策主要是根据对来自多个不同实验室的流感病毒样本进行血清学实验获得。 本项目中我们将应用DNN框架研发出能提供在给定的流感季节下是否需要更新疫苗和哪些毒株应该被纳入用于疫苗更新的建议的自动化智能模型。该模型还将提供一种理解流感病毒抗原基因变异的方法，从而启发对流感生物学和流感病毒进化的研究。

16201620.label: Realisation of objectives
16201620.value: All key objectives have been successfully met, resulting in significant contributions. The project has led to three publications in high-impact journals, including two in the Nature family. Additionally, it has supported one Ph.D. and one MPhil student who have successfully defended their theses. [*Please note that in 2021 approval was granted by RGC to switch the original PI (McKay) to a Co-Investigator status, and to assign the original Co-Investigator (Palomar) as the new PI. This was necessary as Dr. McKay was leaving Hong Kong to join the University of Melbourne in Australia (Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering and the Department of Microbiology and Immunology). He retained an Adjunct Professor position at HKUST. Dr. Palomar served as the PI and led the research activities for the remainder of the project.] Objective 1: Develop deep learning models for predicting antigenic distances between influenza strains This first objective was addressed thoroughly, with the main results reported in Journal Paper 1 published in Nature Communications. This was a collaborative work with influenza experts, Prof. Ian Barr from the WHO Collaborating Centre for Reference and Research on Influenza, Australia, and Prof. Leo Poon from the School of Public Health, LKS Faculty of Medicine, The University of Hong Kong. We developed a machine learning (ML) model that predicts antigenic properties of influenza A virus (IAV) H3N2 isolates circulating in a season using their hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1) sequences and associated metadata while being trained on data from past seasons only. The model is designed and evaluated for predicting, on a season-by-season basis, HI titers of virus-antiserum pairs involving viruses sequenced globally as part of WHO’s seasonal influenza surveillance. Unlike previous methods that randomly selected virus-antiserum pairs over time, our approach focuses on predicting HI titers of virus-antiserum pairs sequenced globally as part of the WHO's seasonal influenza surveillance program. We trained and tested our model using IAV H3N2 antigenic data from influenza seasons spanning 2003 to 2021, sourced from the Worldwide Influenza Center at the Francis Crick Institute. We also incorporated genetic data from multiple influenza sequence databases and their associated metadata. Our model achieves a high level of accuracy, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.702 antigenic units per season. Additionally, it demonstrates excellent discriminatory ability in differentiating antigenic variants across seasons. Our developed model is based on adaptive boosting method (AdaBoost) consisting of an ensemble of decision trees. This model was selected after thorough comparison with different ML and deep learning neural network models (e.g., multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and residual neural network (ResNet)). When evaluated under the seasonal prediction framework over 14 test seasons, the AdaBoost model achieved the best performance (MAE of 0.702) while the neural network models achieved the worst performance. Consequently, we did not adopt these neural network models for our specific application. This research builds upon Journal Paper 2, which appeared in Molecular Biology and Evolution. In Journal Paper 2, we expanded upon our initial framework (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0737-3) published in Nature Biotechnology, by incorporating the impact of interaction between mutations, which enhanced our understanding of the evolutionary processes at play. Additionally, we have made further advancements in our research in Working Paper 1 (listed as Journal Paper 3). This paper, currently in the revision stage, presents an extension of our framework that enables the analysis of short-read data as input. We anticipate resubmitting it for publication soon. Objective 2: Apply the models to reveal the genetic determinants of antigenic changes in influenza This objective was completely addressed. The model that we developed in Journal Paper 1 enables the identification of the specific HA1 sites that have the greatest effect on antigenic changes during a given season, providing insights into the seasonal dynamics of these sites. By analyzing the feature importance scores from our model, we predicted the top sites that contribute significantly to antigenic changes. When examining the seasons from 2014NH to 2020SH, a total of 30 important sites were identified by aggregating the top 20 sites across these seasons. Notably, 25 of these sites were located within well-established HA1 epitopes. It is widely recognized that substitutions occurring within these epitope regions have a dominant effect on the antigenic evolution of influenza virus. Our analysis revealed that epitopes A and B exhibited statistically significant enrichment among the identified 30 sites, which aligns with previous research that epitopes A and B are the most immunodominant regions. Additionally, we identified nine sites that consistently and significantly affect the antigenicity of HA1 in each of the studied seasons. Objective 3: Explore the use of the models for guiding seasonal vaccine selection This objective was completely addressed. Our proposed approach in Journal Paper 1 predicts accurate antigenic properties (HI titers) for influenza viruses circulating in a given season, based on their sequence data only. This prediction can therefore be done rapidly (since viruses can be sequenced quickly and easily) and could be helpful for enhancing antigenic surveillance of influenza. The HI titres that the method predicts are typically generated via experiments conducted with ferrets. Results from these experiments are crucial for informing decisions about whether newly observed flu viruses are likely to evade antibodies elicited by vaccines, whether a vaccine update is required, and if so, what the best vaccine virus would be from the available choices. Since only a subset of circulating viruses in an influenza season are tested with antigenic (HI) assays due to practical constraints (e.g., animal availability, resources, cost, time), our approach can provide antigenicity estimates for all sequenced circulating viruses in that season. This comprehensive assessment can offer a more complete understanding of the antigenic landscape and can provide complementary input to existing surveillance protocols and methods for vaccine strain selection. As mentioned earlier, this work was done in collaboration with Prof. Ian Barr from the WHO Collaborating Centre for Reference and Research on Influenza. Prof. Barr is directly involved with WHO’s influenza seasonal vaccine selection process each year. In future, we will further explore ways in which the developed models can aid WHO protocols and procedures for flu vaccine strain selection. Objective 4: Develop software to facilitate widespread use of the results of the project This objective was completely addressed. The web server running the web application for seasonal antigenic prediction of IAV H3N2 using the AdaBoost model proposed in Journal Paper 1 can be accessed from Hugging Face Spaces (https://huggingface.co/spaces/sawshah/SAP_H3N2). This web application was developed using streamlit, that provides an easy-to-use GUI for applying our model to perform seasonal antigenic prediction for IAV H3N2. With this web application, users can directly input full-length (329 amino acids) HA1 sequences of test virus-antiserum pairs and corresponding (optional) metadata information, or they may choose to upload the same data for multiple virus-antiserum pairs using a CSV file. Based on the season of the virus isolates being tested, the web application allows the user to select the appropriate model trained up to (but excluding) the test season.

16201620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201620.value: Below is a brief summary of some the major contributions in this project: [Journal Paper 1]: This paper, published in Nature Communications (IF: 16.6), developed a machine learning model to predict the outcomes of HI assays, specifically for H3N2 viruses of human influenza A. The model utilized the genetic sequences of the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1) and associated metadata. It learned a nonlinear mapping of genetic changes to antigenic changes using past data from previous seasons. The model demonstrated high accuracy in distinguishing between antigenic variants and non-variants. It also dynamically identifies the HA1 sites that have the most significant impact on antigenic changes throughout the seasons. These antigenic predictions generated by the model have practical applications in influenza surveillance, public health management, and the selection of vaccine strains. [Journal Paper 2]: This paper, published in Molecular Biology and Evolution (IF: 10.7), extended the approach in Journal Paper 2 to incorporate epistasis, where mutations' effects depend on genetic background. Epistasis is prevalent in viruses, impacting drug resistance and immune evasion. Estimating epistatic effects from population data is challenging. Our proposed method inferred epistasis and mutation fitness from observed evolutionary histories, accurately identifying pairwise interactions given sufficient genetic diversity. It quantified uncertainty and allows for complex selection models, enhancing our understanding of evolution.

16201620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201620.value: There are various avenues for further development. Here we briefly list a few such directions. 1. Exploring amino acid substitutions as features in the model to determine the specific importance of individual sites, enhancing the understanding of antigenic changes. 2. Investigating the collective effects of sites (epistasis) on antigenicity using interpretable artificial intelligence techniques like Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). 3. Augmenting the model with genetic information from the HA2 subunit and the neuraminidase (NA) protein to improve prediction accuracy and study their roles in driving antigenic changes in H3N2 influenza viruses. 4. Extending the study to track the antigenic evolution of other influenza subtypes, such as IAV (H1N1) pdm09 or influenza B viruses, if sufficient antigenic data becomes available. 5. Exploring the prediction of neutralization titers, complementing the traditional HI assays, to address issues with certain H3N2 clades that do not react in HI assays. These future directions aim to enhance the model's predictive capabilities, improve understanding of antigenic changes, and expand its applicability to other influenza subtypes and alternative assay methodologies.

16201620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201620.value: The project has provided new statistical models and a web-based platform for predicting accurate antigenic properties (HI titers) for influenza viruses circulating in a given season, based on their sequence data. Our developed method enables identification of specific sites within influenza that have the greatest effect on antigenic changes during a given season, informing targets for intelligent vaccine design. Antigenic predictions produced by the model can aid influenza surveillance, public health management, and vaccine strain selection activities.

16201820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201820.value: 迫切需要开发一种具有最低CO2排放量的高效能量转换系统。固态氧化物燃料电池（SOFCs）由于比其他直接的燃料-电能转换系统更高的效率和更低的排放而特别适合于此。但是，SOFCs的广泛使用受到其较高的工作温度（通常高于800°C）的阻碍，这使得系统复杂化并增加了成本。这个问题可以通过使用质子传导陶瓷电解质代替氧传导膜来解决。由于质子的传输比氧离子更快，因此质子陶瓷燃料电池（PCFCs）可以在较低的温度（400°C-600°C）下工作。另外，PCFCs在阴极侧产生水，从而避免了SOFCs中遇到的燃料稀释问题。尽管有很大的希望，但常规PCFC阴极的活性部位仅限于阴极、电解质和气体汇合的三相界面（TPB）。在拟议的项目中，我们将研究三重导电氧化物（TCOs）的使用，它们可以同时传导质子、电子和氧离子。由于这种特性，TCOs可以大大扩展电化学活性区域，使其超出TPB，从而进一步降低温度。 在有关TCOs的文献中，已经提出了一些高性能材料，例如BaCo0.4Fe0.4Zr0.1Y0.1O3-δ（BCFZY）。然而，这些研究主要集中在燃料电池的制备和构造上，仅进行了一些基础研究。正是由于这个原因，BCFZY的许多特性仍然是未知的，许多与它的稳定性和活性有关的问题尚未得到解答。在拟议的项目中，我们将通过实验和计算研究BCFZY。在该项目的实验部分，我们将使用良好控制的薄膜来研究材料的表面稳定性和组成。实验结果将与第一性原理计算紧密联系。特别地，将探索支撑BCFZY高电化学活性和稳定性的机理。在针对实验验证了计算模型之后，我们将设计描述符以使阴极活性与易于计算的特性相关。然后，我们将使用机器学习和描述符来选择几种有前途的材料，以在实验室规模的PCFCs中进行测试。 总体而言，拟议的项目将寻求揭示BCFZY高性能的基本原理。我们的发现将为设计新材料提供基础，该项目的成功完成将促进PCFC技术的发展。

16201820.label: Realisation of objectives
16201820.value: The project "From material study to design: A fundamental investigation of triple conducting oxides for proton ceramic fuel cells using thin films and first-principles calculations" set out with four primary objectives. These objectives have been comprehensively addressed and successfully achieved through a synergistic combination of extensive experimental investigations and in-depth computational modelling. The research explored a range of triple conducting oxides (TCOs), advanced synthesis techniques, and novel material concepts, leading to significant contributions to the PCFC field. Objective 1: To determine the characteristics of the triple conducting oxide surface using flat thin films of BaCo0.4Fe0.4Zr0.1Y0.1O3-δ (BCFZY) created using pulsed laser deposition. The surface stability, composition, and electrochemical activity will be analyzed as a function of the atmosphere, temperature, and lattice strain. Achievement: This objective was fully realized through systematic studies on BCFZY and other relevant TCOs using various thin film and coating preparation methods, including pulsed laser deposition (through collaborations) and the innovative ultrafast high-temperature sintering (UHS). The surface stability, composition (XPS), and electrochemical activity (EIS) of materials like BCFZY (Journal Paper #28), SrTi0.5Fe0.5O3-δ-based perovskites (STF, Journal Paper #1), and BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ, Journal Paper #10) were thoroughly analyzed. The influence of atmosphere (e.g., redox conditions, humidity) and temperature on surface properties, including nanoparticle exsolution/dissolution in BCFZY and F-retention in BFZ-F (Journal Paper #30), was extensively investigated. The project successfully established methodologies to correlate surface characteristics with electrochemical performance, for instance, demonstrating how controlled surface modifications (e.g., via UHS or in-situ exsolution) can significantly impact catalytic activity and stability. The development of self-assembled nanocomposites like SCFN and BCF also provided crucial insights into the role of surface-enriched phases. Objective 2: To develop first-principles models to calculate the formation energy of defects, their transport properties, and the stability of both the surface and bulk of the materials. Achievement: This objective was comprehensively met. First-principles (DFT) calculations served as a vital tool throughout the project, providing predictive power and mechanistic understanding. DFT was employed to calculate formation energies of defects (e.g., oxygen vacancies, hydroxyl ions in BCFZY, as detailed in Journal Paper #10 and Journal Paper #28), hydration energies, and proton/ion transport barriers for various TCOs. This was critical in understanding, for example, the ORR mechanism on D-BFZ and the enhanced HER kinetics in modified fuel electrodes. The stability of bulk phases (e.g., in HEPs) and surfaces, including the energetics of cation segregation (e.g., Sr in STF) and nanoparticle exsolution (Co-Fe in BCFZY), was extensively modelled. Molecular orbital theory was also applied to understand TM-O bond strengths and their influence on catalytic activity (Journal Paper #10; Journal Paper #28). These computational insights were consistently validated against experimental findings. Objective 3: To develop guidelines for designing new high-performance cathodes based on the experimental and computational findings. Achievement: This objective was successfully achieved, resulting in several key design guidelines for advanced PCFC cathodes. A major guideline emerged from the BCFZY work (Journal Paper #28), demonstrating that designing TCOs with tailored defect chemistry for reversible nanoparticle exsolution/dissolution can lead to highly durable and fuel-flexible symmetric electrodes. The exploration of high-entropy perovskites (Journal Paper #18; Journal Paper #20) established that leveraging configurational entropy is a viable strategy to enhance the stability and tailor the functional properties of perovskite electrodes. Work on SCFN, BCF, and PNCO-LSCF (Journal Paper #11) highlighted the importance of multiphase nanocomposites and controlled interfaces for optimizing ORR/OER activities by synergistically combining functionalities. The UHS method (Journal Paper #12; Journal Paper #30) provided a guideline for synthesizing phase-pure and functional TCOs, especially anion-doped materials, by minimizing unwanted reactions and volatile element loss. The integration of DFT, molecular orbital theory, and advanced EIS deconvolution (deep-DRT, fGP-DRT) provided robust tools for rational material design and performance prediction. Objective 4: To document the electrochemical performance of both BCFZY and other promising candidate materials in a laboratory-scale proton ceramic fuel cell. Achievement: This objective was extensively fulfilled and significantly expanded upon. The bifunctional performance of BCFZY in symmetric PCFCs was thoroughly documented (Journal Paper #28), showcasing high PPDs with H2 (≈350 mW cm-2 at 600°C), methanol, and methane, alongside its unique self-recovery features. The D-BFZ variant, designed through computational guidance, achieved exceptional PPDs of 0.67 W cm-2 at 500°C (Journal Paper #10). A wide array of other promising materials, including HEPs (Journal Paper #18), nanocomposites like SCFN and BCF, PNCO-LSCF (Journal Paper #11, PPD 1.358 W/cm2), UHS-synthesized BFZ-F, and exsolution-based electrodes (Journal Paper #21; Journal Paper #28), demonstrated excellent performance in PCFC/RePCC test configurations, often surpassing benchmarks. For instance, the BCFZYN nanocomposite showed high electrolysis currents (-1267 mA cm-2 at 1.3V, 600°C) and durability (Journal Paper #22). The project has comprehensively achieved its stated objectives by systematically investigating TCOs from fundamental principles to device-level demonstration. It has pioneered work on self-recoverable electrodes and HEPs for PCFC applications, developed advanced synthesis and characterization tools, and delivered a portfolio of high-performance electrode materials, significantly advancing the field.

16201820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201820.value: This project has delivered transformative findings and established new paradigms in the design and understanding of triple conducting oxides (TCOs) for proton ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) and reversible PCFCs (RePCCs). A cornerstone achievement is the development and elucidation of self-recoverable symmetric PCFCs based on BCFZY (Journal Paper #28). Through integrated DFT, molecular orbital theory, and experimental validation, the project demonstrated BCFZY's unique ability for reversible exsolution/dissolution of Co-Fe nanoparticles. This "smart" electrode design imparts exceptional durability, high bifunctional HOR/ORR activity, and remarkable fuel flexibility (H2, methanol, methane; PPD ≈350 mW cm-2 at 600°C with H2), marking a significant step towards commercially viable PCFCs. The rational design of A- and B-site co-substituted BaFeO3−δ, specifically D-BFZ (Ba0.875Fe0.875Zr0.125O3−δ), guided by DFT, led to cathodes with exceptional PPDs (0.67 W cm-2 at 500°C, Journal Paper #10). The project ventured into the pioneering exploration of high-entropy perovskites (HEPs) for PCFCs and broader energy applications (Journal Paper #18; Journal Paper #20). This research established that high configurational entropy can be harnessed to create exceptionally stable TCOs with highly tunable electrochemical properties, opening a new materials design space. Significant advancements were made in novel TCO nanocomposites and advanced synthesis techniques. In-situ assembled electrodes, such as PNCO-LSCF (Journal Paper #11, PPD 1.358 W/cm2 at 750°C) and BCFZYN (Journal Paper #22, electrolysis current -1267 mA cm-2 at 1.3V, 600°C), demonstrated superior ORR/OER activities and stability. The ultrafast high-temperature sintering (UHS) method was successfully applied to synthesize fluorinated air electrodes (BFZ-F, Journal Paper #30) and other NTE-composite cathodes (U-BFZ-NM, Journal Paper #27) with enhanced performance and thermal compatibility, effectively mitigating issues like fluorine volatility or phase degradation. The comprehensive integration of first-principles calculations with advanced experimental characterization (including in-situ studies of exsolution, Journal Paper #21) provided deep mechanistic insights into defect chemistry, ion transport, surface catalysis, and the role of extended defects across a wide range of TCOs. This was further augmented by the development of sophisticated EIS deconvolution tools (deep-DRT, fGP-DRT), enhancing the ability to diagnose and optimize electrochemical systems. These outcomes have been widely disseminated through numerous high-impact publications.

16201820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201820.value: The successful outcomes of this project unlock significant potential for future research and development. A key direction is the further optimization and long-term durability assessment of self-recoverable BCFZY electrodes and the exploration of this "smart exsolution/dissolution" concept in other TCO systems, potentially guided by high-throughput computational screening. The emerging field of high-entropy perovskites (HEPs) for PCFCs/electrolyzers warrants extensive investigation. This includes synthesizing and characterizing a broader library of HEP compositions to establish clear structure-property-performance relationships, focusing on maximizing proton conductivity, catalytic activity, and chemo-mechanical stability under diverse operating conditions. Machine learning integrated with DFT will accelerate this discovery. The UHS synthesis technique should be further developed for scalability and applied to a wider range of complex oxides, including HEPs and NTE-composites, to precisely control microstructure and phase purity. Fundamental understanding of dynamic processes at TCO interfaces, including exsolution dynamics, surface reconstruction, and the role of extended defects, will be pursued through advanced in-situ/operando characterization techniques coupled with multi-scale modeling. The ultimate goal is to translate these advanced materials and concepts into practical PCFC/RePCC devices, necessitating collaboration for stack development and testing under industrially relevant conditions.

16201820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201820.value: Our research has focused on creating new and improved materials for advanced fuel cells, which are clean energy devices that efficiently convert fuels like hydrogen directly into electricity. A major goal was to make these fuel cells more durable, versatile, and powerful. We made several exciting breakthroughs. We developed a "smart" electrode material (called BCFZY) that can actually "heal" itself if it gets damaged during use. It does this by re-growing tiny active particles on its surface, which keeps the fuel cell working well for longer and allows it to use different fuels like hydrogen, methanol, or even methane. We also explored a brand-new class of materials called "high-entropy perovskites." Think of these as a complex cocktail of many different elements mixed together. This complexity can make them incredibly stable and efficient for energy applications. Additionally, our team invented ultra-fast ways to make these advanced materials, cutting down manufacturing time from days to just minutes. Using powerful computer simulations, we also gained a much deeper understanding of how these materials work at the tiniest atomic level. The significance of this work is that it provides new and better building blocks for future clean energy technologies, helping to create fuel cells that are more reliable, efficient, and adaptable.

16202120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202120.value: Rapid economic development and urbanization in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area (GBA) have caused major air pollution issues, including severe nitrogen dioxide (NO2) pollution. Nitrogen dioxides are an essential precursor in the formation of tropospheric ozone, acid rain and nitrate particles, and they significantly exert adverse impacts on human health. However, research on NO2 pollution is less than that on particulate matter pollution. Enhanced ground-based monitoring of NO2 concentration has been available since only 2013. Knowledge about the long-term spatiotemporal variation, causes, and environmental impacts of NO2 pollution is far from complete because of the lack of long-term measurements. The proposed study will develop an integrated approach by using a variety of advanced methods to investigate the decadal NO2 pollution in this region. These methods include but are not limited to polar-orbiting and newly developed geostationary satellite remote sensing, chemical transport model (CTM), drone-based sensor measurement, and ground-based LIDAR and radiosonde measurements. Satellite remote sensing technique measures the vertical column density of NO2 with an extensive spatial and temporal coverage. Recent developments in geostationary satellites offer new opportunities to observe the atmosphere with a high resolution of 1 hour. The emission-based CTM is capable of demonstrating three-dimensional NO2 pollution variation and the tracking the emission sources. Given the model’s uncertainty in simulating NO2 variation, a systematic evaluation is needed. Most previous model’s evaluations relied on ground measurements only. Observations of the NO2 vertical variation are still limited. This study uses the newly developed drone-based system equipped with miniaturized NO2 sensor to measure the NO2 vertical profile across the GBA for the model’s evaluation and improvement. The LIDAR and radiosonde measurements provide critical information on the planetary boundary layer height, which determines the convection and dispersion of NO2 pollution. In summary, the proposed study will take advantage of a variety of advanced measurements and modeling techniques to deduce and investigate the decadal NO2 pollution variation; to better understand the vertical variation of NO2 and its impact on surface NO2 pollution; to improve the chemical transport model’s ability in simulating the NO2 variation; and to investigate the effects of different emission sources and meteorological factors on the decadal NO2 pollution variation. We envision that enhanced understanding about long-term NO2 pollution can provide scientific evidence for the development of appropriate strategies for NO2 pollution control and serve the green development objective of the GBA. 粵港澳大灣區經濟的高速發展和快速城市化已引起嚴重的空氣污染問題，其中包括二氧化氮（NO2）污染。二氧化氮是形成對流層臭氧，酸雨和硝酸鹽顆粒物必不可少的前體物，並對人體健康產生重大不利影響。然而目前對NO2污染的研究遠少於對顆粒物污染的研究。地面NO2濃度的廣泛監測僅始於2013年。由於缺乏長期監測，有關NO2污染的長期時空變化，成因和環境影響的了解還遠遠不夠。本研究將集合使用多種先進技術來研究大灣區長期的NO2污染。這些技術方法包括極軌衛星和新開發的靜止衛星遙感，化學傳輸模型，基於無人機的傳感器測量，以及基於地面的激光雷達和探空測量。衛星遙感技術可測量NO2的垂直柱密度，並具有廣泛的時空覆蓋範圍。新開發的靜止衛星以每小時的高分辨率觀測大氣。化學傳輸模型能夠刻畫NO2污染三維變化並識踪排放源。考慮到模型在模擬NO2變化方面的不確定性，模擬結果需要進行系統的評估。以往大多數模型的評估僅依賴於地面測量，對NO2垂直變化的測量仍然十分有限。本研究使用新開發的基於無人機的觀測系統，該系統配備了微型NO2傳感器，可用於測量大灣區上空NO2的垂直分佈，以評估和改進化學傳輸模型。激光雷達和探空儀的測量結果提供了有關大氣邊界層高度的關鍵信息，這些信息決定了NO2污染的對流和擴散。綜上，本研究將利用多種先進的測量和建模技術研究大灣區十年期NO2污染變化趨勢，同時更好地了解NO2的垂直變化及其對地面NO2污染的影響，提高化學傳輸模型模擬NO2變化的能力，並研究不同排放源和氣象因素對十年期NO2污染變化的影響。本研究將加深對大灣區長期NO2污染的了解，為製定適當的NO2污染控制策略提供科學依據，並服務於大灣區的綠色發展目標。

16202120.label: Realisation of objectives
16202120.value: In this project, we developed an integrated approach using a variety of advanced methods to investigate decadal nitrogen dioxide (NO2) pollution in China and its Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area (GBA). These methods include polar-orbiting and newly developed geostationary satellite remote sensing, chemical transport models, and various vertical measurements. In particular, we employed measurements from the Geostationary Environmental Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS), the world’s first geostationary environmental satellite, to monitor NO2 levels in China and the GBA region. The geostationary Earth orbit significantly enhanced the temporal resolution of observations from daily to hourly. These advanced measurements and modeling techniques were employed to (1) investigate the decadal variation of NO2 pollution; (2) better understand the vertical variation of NO2 and its impact on surface NO2 pollution; (3) improve the capability of chemical transport model (CTM) to simulate NO2 variation; and (4) examine the effects of emission controls and meteorological factors on decadal NO2 pollution variation. Through multiple analyses conducted during the project period, we successfully achieved all objectives and published six papers. To achieve objective 1, we developed an ensemble backpropagation neural network method to estimate surface NO2 concentrations in East Asia from 2001 to 2016 by combining satellite vertical column densities (VCDs) of NO2 with reanalysis data (Hu et al., 2022). The estimated monthly and annual mean NO2 concentrations showed strong correlations with observations, with correlation coefficients of 0.89 and 0.91, respectively. Our results indicate that NO2 concentrations in most areas of East Asia peaked during 2011–2013. In autumn and winter, especially in the eastern and northern parts of China, NO2 concentrations were significantly higher than in summer. Based on our estimations, NO2-related asthma cases in East Asia increased by 1.37% annually from 2001 to 2015, reaching 139,000 cases in 2015. Although GEMS has revolutionized air quality monitoring with hourly resolution, satellite-derived air quality data often face limitations and biases due to missing data. Using GEMS measurements, we assessed the potential for improving data availability and mitigating bias in monitoring ground-level NO2 concentrations in China through a machine learning framework that integrates gap-filling and column-to-ground conversion processes (Ahmad et al., 2025). The results indicate that the gap-filling process significantly enhanced data availability from 10-50% to full coverage across China. Furthermore, the seamless data substantially reduced bias in estimating the annual mean of ground-level NO2 concentrations, eliminating a significant underestimation of over 3.0 μg/m³ in 36.3%, 47.2%, and 63.6% of the area for 8 AM, 2 PM, and 3 PM, respectively. To achieve objective 2, we used a DJI Matrice 350 drone equipped with an air quality sensor (Sirius-E2V2) to measure vertical profiles of NO2 concentration in the GBA area. The flight experiment consisted of vertical soundings and horizontal flight observations. Multiple flight experiments were conducted daily to cover morning, noon, and evening times. Using the information on NO2 vertical distribution, we conducted a thorough examination of spatiotemporal variations in the mixing height of NO2 (NMH) using data from both GEMS and ground-based air quality monitoring networks (Ahmad et al., 2024a). A random forest model was employed to assess how meteorological parameters affect the NMH. The results of our study reveal notable seasonal fluctuations in the NMH, with the highest values observed during the summer and the lowest values during the winter. Additionally, there was an increasing diurnal trend from early morning to mid-afternoon. The results also indicated a positive correlation between the NMH and both temperature and wind speed, while negative associations were identified with relative humidity and air pressure. Additionally, an analysis was conducted to understand the impacts of the vertical distribution of NO2 on ground-level NO2 concentration (Ahmad et al., 2024b). We developed a nested XGBoost machine learning model to convert VCDs of NO2 into ground-level NO2 concentrations across China using GEMS measurements. This nested model was designed to directly incorporate NMH into the methodological framework for estimating satellite-derived ground-level NO2 concentrations. The inner machine learning model predicted the NMH from meteorological parameters, which were then input into the main XGBoost machine learning model to predict ground-level NO2 concentrations from its VCDs. The inclusion of NMH significantly enhanced the accuracy of ground-level NO2 concentration estimates. Specifically, the R² values improved from 0.73 to 0.93 in 10-fold cross-validation and from 0.88 to 0.99 in the fully trained model. Furthermore, NMH was identified as the second most important predictor variable, following the VCDs of NO2. Subsequently, the satellite-derived ground-level NO2 data were analyzed across subregions (e.g., the GBA region) with varying geographic locations and urbanization levels. Highly populated areas typically experienced peak NO2 concentrations during the early morning rush hour, while lightly populated areas observed a slight increase in NO2 levels 1 or 2 hours later due to regional pollutant dispersion from urban sources. To achieve Objective 3, we improved a CTM modeling system to enhance our understanding of the spatio-temporal variation of NO2 in Hong Kong (Che et al., 2023). By combining urban morphology, dynamic traffic emissions, regional and local meteorology, and physicochemical transformations in air quality models using big data fusion technology, we developed an ultra-fine resolution CTM system that provides air quality data down to the street level. We then investigated the effects of pollution heterogeneity on individual and population exposure to various air pollutants, including NO2, in Hong Kong. Sharp fine-scale variabilities in air pollution were revealed within individual city blocks. Using a traditional 1 km average to represent individual exposure resulted in a positively skewed deviation of up to 200% for individuals with high exposure levels. Citizens were disproportionately affected by air pollution, with annual pollutant concentrations varying by factors of 2 to 5 among 452 District Council Constituency Areas (DCCAs) in Hong Kong, indicating significant environmental inequities within the population. Unfavorable city planning resulted in a positive spatial correlation between pollution and population density, which increased public exposure to air pollutants by as much as 46% among districts in Hong Kong. To achieve Objective 4, we developed an observation-based decomposition model to investigate the effects of emission controls and meteorological factors on the variations in NO2 and its photochemical product (e.g., O3) concentrations in China from 2013 to 2020 (Lin et al., 2021). Ground measurements showed that both NO2 and O3 concentrations decreased in eastern, central, and southeastern China (e.g., NO2 and O3 concentrations in Wuhan reduced by 4.3 and 6.2 ppb, respectively), which was unexpected. Analyses of meteorological effects revealed that reduced wind strength, decreased temperature, and increased relative humidity significantly lowered O3 concentrations in eastern and central China (e.g., by 10.5 ppb in Wuhan). After accounting for the major meteorological effects, the O3 trends reversed in eastern and central China (e.g., increasing by 4.9 ppb in Wuhan). The contrasting trends in NO2 and O3 concentrations suggest that O3 formation was sensitive to volatile organic compounds (VOC-limited regime). In the GBA region, both NO2 and O3 concentrations decreased, indicating that the O3 formation regimes shifted to mixed sensitivity or nitrogen oxide-limited (NOx-limited) regimes. The meteorological effects varied by region and may play a dominant role in controlling long-term O3 variation.

16202120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202120.value: With the support of this project, we published six papers. Firstly, we developed an ensemble backpropagation neural network method to estimate ground-level NO2 from satellite VCDs (Hu et al., 2022). Our investigation of decadal NO2 variation showed that NO2 concentrations in most areas of East Asia peaked during 2011–2013. Based on GEMS measurements, we improved data availability and mitigated bias in monitoring ground-level NO2 concentrations through a machine learning framework that integrates gap-filling and column-to-ground conversion processes (Ahmad et al., 2025). The results indicate that this seamless data significantly reduced bias in estimating ground-level NO2 concentrations. Secondly, we used a drone equipped with an air quality sensor to measure vertical profiles of NO2 concentration in the GBA area. With information on NO2 vertical distribution, we conducted a thorough examination of the spatiotemporal variations in the mixing height of NO2 (Ahmad et al., 2024a). The results revealed a positive correlation between the mixing height of NO2 and both temperature and wind speed, while negative associations were found with relative humidity and air pressure. Next, we developed a nested XGBoost machine learning model to convert VCDs into ground-level NO2 concentrations using GEMS measurements (Ahmad et al., 2024b). Our analyses of NO2 variation found that highly populated areas typically experienced peak NO2 concentrations during the early morning rush hour, whereas lightly populated areas observed a slight increase in NO2 levels 1 to 2 hours later due to regional pollutant dispersion from urban sources. Thirdly, we developed an ultra-fine resolution CTM modeling system to enhance our understanding of the spatiotemporal variation of NO2 in Hong Kong (Che et al., 2023). This revealed sharp fine-scale variabilities in air pollution within individual city blocks. Using a traditional 1 km average to represent individual exposure resulted in a positively skewed deviation of up to 200% for individuals with high-end exposure. Lastly, we developed an observation-based decomposition model to investigate the effects of emission controls and meteorological factors on variations in NO2 and its photochemical product concentrations in China from 2013 to 2020 (Lin et al., 2021). Our analyses of meteorological effects showed that reduced wind strength, decreased temperature, and increased relative humidity significantly affected NO2 concentrations in eastern and central China. In the GBA region, both NO2 and O3 concentrations decreased, suggesting that the O3 formation regimes shifted to mixed sensitive or NOx-limited regimes.

16202120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202120.value: The research conducted under this project has laid a solid foundation for further development in understanding and managing air quality in East Asia. Building on our success in publishing six papers, we propose several avenues for future exploration. First, we aim to refine our ensemble backpropagation neural network method and nested XGBoost model to enhance the accuracy of ground-level NO2 estimations by integrating additional variables such as land use and traffic patterns. Additionally, expanding our vertical measurements to other urban areas will provide a comprehensive dataset for analyzing vertical profiles of air pollutants, further elucidating its spatiotemporal variations. We also plan to enhance our ultra-fine resolution CTM modeling system to include real-time data assimilation, which could improve predictive capabilities for air quality management. Lastly, we will investigate the interactions between meteorological factors and other pollutants, such as particulate matter, to develop a holistic understanding of air quality dynamics. By pursuing these initiatives, we hope to contribute valuable insights that can inform policy decisions and improve public health outcomes in urban environments.

16202120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202120.value: This research project focused on understanding air pollution, specifically nitrogen dioxide (NO2), in China and the Greater Bay Area (GBA). By employing advanced technology such as satellite remote sensing and machine learning, we were able to measure air quality with greater accuracy and identify patterns in pollution levels over time. One finding was that NO2 levels peaked between 2011 and 2013 in many areas, which helps us understand past pollution trends and their potential drivers. We also discovered that pollution levels vary significantly within small city blocks, meaning that some neighborhoods may be more affected than others. This information is crucial because it highlights environmental inequalities, drawing attention to areas that need urgent intervention and targeted policies to mitigate exposure. Additionally, we examined how weather conditions, such as temperature, wind speed, and humidity, influence pollution levels. By understanding these relationships, we can better predict air quality fluctuations and implement timely measures to protect public health. Overall, this research is significant because it provides valuable insights that can help policymakers create effective strategies to improve air quality, safeguard public health, and reduce the harmful effects of pollution on communities.

16202220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202220.value: 药品和个人护理产品 (PPCPs) 的过度生产和使用严重影响了水生环境。由于其难降解的性质，传统的污水处理方法 (WWTPs) 无法有效降解药品和个人护理产品，因此它们经常出现在水体中。 一般来说, 药品和个人护理产品在水生环境中的浓度范围在在ng/L和µg/L之间，这些物质会通过内分泌紊乱和增加抗生素的耐药性，对人类健康和水生环境构成威胁。高级氧化法 (AOPs) 已被用于去除废水中的药品和个人护理产品。根据已有报道，芬顿 (Fenton) 反应和光催化技术可以有效氧化去除药品和个人护理产品。但是，Fenton反应和光催化产生的主要活性物质是羟基自由基 (•OH) 其氧化性能不足以完全氧化去除具有更复杂化学结构的PPCPs。近年来，基于硫酸根自由基 (SO¬4•-)的高级氧化技术 (SR-AOP) 因其较强的氧化能力和较高的矿化效率在难降解有机物领域成为研究热点。在SR-AOP中，催化剂活化后可生成氧化能力较高的SO¬4•-自由基和寿命较长的非自由基1O2，其去除有机物效果较好，并且有机物的矿化率较高。虽然光催化剂已被广泛用于去除药品和个人护理产品，但由于光产生电子和空穴的快速复合阻碍了其在环境领域的进一步发展。 因此，我们构建了一个可见光驱动的SR-AOP系统，协同使用过硫酸氢钾 (PMS)活化和有效的电荷分离光催化技术，作为一种有效且实用的处理PPCPs的一种手段。在这个方案中，我们提出三种具有可见光响应的光催化剂，亦即在SR-AOP系统也可以作为催化剂激活PMS，例如硒化钼、磷化钴负载的氮掺杂碳化氮纳米片CoP/N-g-C3N4和中空结构的Pt@CeO2@MoS2。金属价态的变化协同光生电子的高利用效率作用将极大地促进PPCPs的催化降解。本项目包括: (1) 三种可见光驱动(光)催化剂的合成与表征； (2) 探索其在各种条件下的降解动力学和性能，并利用密度泛函理论 (DFT) 确定金属活性位点和光生电子和空穴消耗机制；(3) 研究PPCPs的降解机理以了解自由基产生途径以及光生电子在SR-AOP中的作用。本项新技术有望极大地推动高级氧化技术催化去除药品和个人护理产品。

16202220.label: Realisation of objectives
16202220.value: The project progressed smoothly, as evidenced by achieving the as-proposed three objectives. Three nanomaterials, including MoSe2, CoP/g-N-C3N4, and Pt@CeO2@MoS2, were applied in photocatalytic (PC) or photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) system for visible-light-driven activation of PMS to efficiently degrade pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) from wastewater. Based on the proposed objectives, the nanomaterials were purchased or synthesized and comprehensively characterized to understand their physical, chemical, and photocatalytic properties. Then, they were applied to the PC/PMS and PEC/PMS processes to verify their effectiveness in removing various PPCPs, and their active sites for PMS activation were investigated using density functional theory. Finally, the mechanisms of PPCP degradation were revealed using different approaches. The detailed investigation using different nanomaterials is shown as follows. In the first study, commercial MoSe2 was used in visible-light-driven PMS activation for PPCP degradation. This nanomaterial was found to have a nanosheet structure with a large surface area using the scanning electron microscope (SEM). It has a narrow bandgap that can produce sufficient charge carriers under visible light illumination to activate PMS. In this study, three PPCPs, including ibuprofen (IBU), benzophenone-3 (BZP), and carbamazepine (CBZ), are used as the target pollutants. MoSe2 exhibited excellent performance in activating PMS under visible light, as evidenced by achieving 100% removal of BZP and CBZ (conditions: 1.2 mmol/L PMS, 0.3 g/L MoSe2), and removing 94.5% of IBU with the presence of Fe(II) ions. Moreover, the PC/PMS process using MoSe2 shows a high rate constant of 0.222 min-1, which was 57 times faster than the PC process without PMS (0.00389 min-1), indicating that the combination of PC and PMS activation achieves a synergistic effect on PPCP degradation. As for the mechanism investigation, the reactive species scavenging experiments showed that superoxide radical (O2•-) was the dominant reactive species in CBZ degradation, while sulfate radical (SO4•-), singlet oxygen (1O2), and hydroxyl radical (•OH), played minor roles. Further, the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurements also confirmed the coexistence of these reactive species. The XPS spectra of fresh and used MoSe2 demonstrated that the Mo4+ ions engaged in PMS activation and were oxidized to be Mo5+ and Mo6+, while the photogenerated electrons reduced Mo5+ and Mo6+ back to Mo4+, facilitating the valance cycling of Mo. The results of density functional theory (DFT) calculation exhibited that the O-O bond in the molecule of PMS is favored to be adsorbed on the MoSe2 surface, facilitating PMS activation for ROS generation. Importantly, the PC/PMS system using MoSe2 was proven to be efficient in treating real sewage, showing its potential for real-world applications. In the second study, the CoP-modified N-doped C3N4, namely CoP/N-g-C3N4, was synthesized through a thermal decomposition method for the PC/PMS process to degrade IBU, BZP, and CBZ. The SEM and EDS-mapping measurements revealed that CoP/N-g-C3N4 has a uniform nanosheet structure with a large surface area. The X-ray diffraction spectrometer (XRD) patterns demonstrated the well crystallization of the synthesized material and XPS spectra confirmed the coexistence of all the involved elements in the as-prepared nanomaterial. The CoP-N-g-C3N4 exhibited good performance in PMS activation, achieving 100% removal of CBZ and BZP within 30 minutes of treatment. This is attributed to the N doping and CoP loading benefiting the transfer of photogenerated electrons from the N-g-C3N4 nanosheets to the CoP particles, allowing more electrons to participate in PMS activation for efficient PPCP degradation. Moreover, different water matrices, such as pH value, anions, and cations, were found to insignificantly influence the PC/PMS process. In terms of mechanism, the reactive species scavenging tests and EPR measurement demonstrated that singlet oxygen (1O2) plays an important role in CBZ removal. The electrochemical measurement showed that the doping of N atoms can modify the electronic characteristics of g-C3N4 nanosheets to regulate PMS activation. Subsequently, DFT calculation revealed that CoP nanoparticles prefer to bond with the N=N bond formed by the doping of N atoms, resulting in the formation of a Co-N bond that can significantly enhance the charge of photogenerated elections by N-g-C3N4. In addition, the PMS molecules were also adsorbed on the electron-deficient surface of N-g-C3N4 caused by the formation of N=N bonds during N doping, which enabled the separated electrons engaging in PMS activation to improve the degradation efficiency of CBZ and BZP. In the third study, we synthesized the hollow-structured Pt@CeO2@MoS2 nanomaterials on the conductive substrate as the photoanode for the PEC/PMS system. The SEM images were obtained to confirm the successful synthesis of the hollow-structure material. Moreover, Pt@CeO2@MoS2 exhibited significantly enhanced photoelectrocatalytic performance due to the construction of CeO2@MoS2 heterojunction and the doping of Pt significantly improved the light adsorption ability and charge transfer ability. As a result, the Pt@CeO2@MoS2 photoanode achieved excellent performance in CBZ degradation in the PEC/PMS system with a high-rate constant of 0.13202 min−1. Then, the effects of the hollow structure on the performance of the material were investigated, which was found to increase the active sites on the material for PMS activation as well as suppress the recombination of photogenerated charge carriers. As for the mechanism study, reactive species scavenging tests and EPR measurement showed that 1O2, O2•−, SO4•−, and •OH were generated in the PEC/PMS system for contaminant removal and the 1O2 contributed the most to CBZ degradation. Afterwards, the XPS spectra revealed that both the Ce and Mo participated in PMS activation, and the PEC/PMS can promote the separation of charge carriers to produce sufficient electrons for the valence cycling of Ce3+/Ce4+ and Mo4+/Mo6+, thus promoting PMS activation. Furthermore, the applicability of the PEC/PMS process using Pt@CeO2@MoS2 was comprehensively investigated, including testing the performance of the system in treating real wastewater, evaluating the stability of the material, and measuring the mineralization efficiency of the pollutant. The three objectives have been realized through the aforementioned studies and the findings were published in Applied Catalysis B: Environmental, Journal of Hazardous, and Environmental International. The research group further dipped into the related research areas and obtained some promising findings. We developed a magnetic S-scheme ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 heterojunction for PMS activation to achieve PPCP degradation. This novel photocatalyst showed significantly improved photocatalytic reactivity due to the construction of S-scheme heterojunction and the ammoniated modification of MoS2. The mechanism investigation revealed that the directional transfer of reductive electrons to ZnFe2O4 can facilitate the valence cycling of Fe2+/Fe3+ for PMS activation, generating sufficient reactive species for PPCP degradation. The ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 heterojunction also exhibited excellent stability and reusability in treating real sewage and can be easily recovered using its magnetic property after sewage treatment. The study provides a novel strategy and fundamental theory for the development of S-scheme heterojunction in environmental remediation. In addition, a 1T/2H MoS2 was embedded in the flexible carbon cloth (1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC) as the photoanode for the PEC/PMS process to remove PPCPs. By regulating the molecular structure of MoS2, the 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC achieved significantly enhanced PEC reactivity and performed efficiently in removing antibiotics. The developed PEC/PMS system using 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC showcased the synergistic effect of PMS activation and photoelectrocatalysis, demonstrating high degradation efficiency and high stability and reusability. Overall, we successfully achieved the three as-proposed objectives and extended the research to different aspects, as evidenced by the development of ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 S-scheme heterojunction and 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC photoanode for efficient PPCP degradation.
