16202220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202220.value: In this project, the novel visible-light-driven photocatalytic and photoelectrocatalytic peroxymonosulfate activation (PC/PMS and PEC/PMS) processes were developed for PPCP removal. Several nanomaterials, including MoSe2, CoP/g-N-C3N4, and ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2, were developed as photocatalysts for PC/PMS process. MoSe2 achieved efficient PPCP degradation because the metallic Mo ions and photo-generated electrons enhanced PMS activation, producing superoxide radicals (O2•−) as primary reactive species for pollutant removal. The density functional theory (DFT) calculation revealed the preferred adsorption dynamics of PMS molecules on MoSe2, leading to PMS decomposition for reactive species generation. Moreover, the process was also effective in treating actual wastewater, demonstrating promise in practical application. For the CoP/g-N-C3N4 nanosheets, the N doping and CoP loading can significantly improve the photocatalytic reactivity of the material due to the promoted charge separation. Mechanism investigation showed that the singlet oxygen (1O2) contributed the most to pollutant removal. Based on DFT calculation, N doping on C3N4 facilitated PMS adsorption and enhanced the charge transfer, promoting PMS activation to produce 1O2. The study highlights the huge potential of CoP/g-N-C3N4 in real sewage treatment and emphasizes the advancement of non-radical pathways for pollutant degradation. The magnetic S-scheme ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 was also developed for the visible-light-driven PMS activation. ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 demonstrated enhanced photocatalytic reactivity because the construction of S-scheme heterojunction facilitated the separation of highly reductive electrons to the ZnFe2O4. The material achieved efficient PPCP removal because ZnFe2O4 reactive center offers sufficient Fe2+ active sites for PMS activation and the enhanced separation of electrons promotes Fe2+/Fe3+ recycling. The ZnFe2O4/A-MoS2 also exhibited excellent stability and reusability in different sewages and can be easily recovered after sewage treatment. The Pt@CeO2@MoS2 and 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC photoanodes were synthesized for the PEC/PMS process. Both Pt@CeO2@MoS2 and 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC were synthesized on the conductive substrates, which can be easily recovered and reused after sewage treatment without producing secondary pollution from the use of nanomaterials, enabling the process to be scaled up for practical applications. Moreover, the externally applied voltage can enhance the separation of photogenerated electrons in the PEC/PMS system, promoting PMS activation to produce 1O2 as the dominant species for PPCP removal. Importantly, the PEC/PMS processes using Pt@CeO2@MoS2 and 1T/2H-MoS2@C/CC also exhibited excellent stability and reusability, and high applicability to remove various PPCPs from different water sources. All the above-mentioned studies were successfully completed and the findings were published in top journals, including Environmental Science & Technology, Applied Catalysis B: Environmental, Chemical Engineering Journal, etc.

16202220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202220.value: The developed PC/PMS and PEC/PMS processes showed excellent performance in PPCP removal. Nonetheless, all experiments were conducted at a laboratory scale, and the research is pending to scale up for the application in real-world scenarios. The above-mentioned studies were investigated using batch reactors, which are not suitable for practical applications in treating a large amount of real wastewater. Therefore, the scale-up continuous flow reactor should be designed and fabricated to meet the requirement of treating real wastewater with a huge amount. Meanwhile, the scale-up synthesis of material in a large production amount is also a crucial issue, and the current material preparation methods should be modified for large production of nanomaterials with cost-effectiveness. In addition, the solar light simulator was applied in the lab-scale experiment, which is energy-intensive. Future studies should be performed under natural sunlight to verify the feasibility of the PC/PMS and PEC/PMS processes using sustainable and renewable solar energy. We will cooperate with the Drainage Services Department of Hong Kong to facilitate the practical application of the developed techniques of this project and integrate the developed techniques into a local wastewater treatment for the removal of PPCPs from real sewage.

16202220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202220.value: PPCPs are a group of emerging micropollutants that cannot be effectively removed by wastewater treatment plants. As a result, PPCPs are frequently detected in aquatic environments due to the continuous discharge, which adversely affects the ecosystem and human health even at low concentrations. The sulfate radical-based (SO4•-) advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs) have attracted extensive attention for PPCP degradation due to their high oxidation capacity and high mineralization efficiency. In this project, we developed novel photocatalysis (PC) and photoelectrocatalysis (PMS) processes for visible-light-driven peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation to remove PPCPs. Three nanomaterials, including MoSe2, CoP/g-N-C3N4 nanosheets, and Pt@CeO2@MoS2 hollow nanoparticles, were synthesized for the PC/PMS and PEC/PMS processes. The synthesized materials achieved excellent performance for PPCP removal in the developed PC/PMS and PEC/PMS systems because they can provide sufficient transition metals as active sites and produce sufficient photogenerated electrons for the efficient activation of PMS. Moreover, the materials also showed excellent stability and reusability and maintained high performance in real wastewater, demonstrating their outstanding practicability. The project produces in-depth insights and fundamental theories into the development of novel PC/PMS and PEC/PMS processes for the efficient removal of PPCPs, providing guidance for the future industrialization of the developed technologies.

The incident sound will be determined by the prediction of both the tonal and broadband noise of the rotors.

16202520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202520.value: The proposed project will focus on the aerodynamic noise of multi-rotors, which are a common power lift configuration on now ubiquitous unmanned aerial vehicles and will on future electrically powered aircraft. Many studies on the flow generated noise from isolated rotor blades have been conducted. Methods to predict rotor noise are now available, but most are only suitable for a single rigid rotor blade, and thus the blade oscillations and the rich physics raising from the multi-rotor interactions are not considered. In practical multi-rotor configurations, the aerodynamic interaction between the rotors can change the near-field flows of turbulent wakes and tip vortices, alter the sound generation physics and lead to new sources of sound. There is a distinct lack of studies of the relevant physics. A systematic study of the aeroacoustics and aerodynamics of multi-rotors is needed to identify these new sources of sound and enhance prediction capability. Of note is that rotor blades made of light materials may oscillate at high rotation speeds due to the unsteady loading. For accurate noise prediction, it is necessary to quantify the blade displacement and deflection and to understand the impact of these parameters on noise. The far-field sound directivity can be affected by sound scattering off solid surfaces such as fuselages and rotor blades, and thus an efficient means to compute of the scattering is needed. This proposed study will aim to provide answers and solutions to these problems. First, systematic measurements of aerodynamics and noise will be conducted for dual-rotor interaction in anechoic chambers. A phased microphone array will be used for acoustic source imaging, and particle image velocimetry will be used to study the turbulent flow field. Numerical simulations using computational aeroacoustics will be undertaken to analyze the aerodynamic interaction and sound generation. Second, the blade-tip displacements due to the blade oscillation, which could be included in sound predictions, will be quantified with a high-speed camera. Wind tunnel tests will be conducted to study the aeroacoustics of oscillating semi-infinite blades. Finally, an efficient, reduced-order boundary element method will be developed to calculate broadband rotor noise scattering and radiation. This research will enhance our understanding of aeroacoustics and aerodynamics of multi-rotor interaction and blade oscillation. It will also provide us with an efficient method to assess the environmental noise impact of multi-rotor. The outcome of the proposed study will aid the design of the low noise flying vehicles powered by multi-rotors. 該項目將着重於目前應用廣泛的多旋翼飛行器的空氣動力噪聲。目前，單個轉子葉片產生的氣動噪聲方面，人們已經進行了許多研究。對於已經發展的轉子噪聲預測方法，存在的問題是僅適用於單個而且剛性的轉子葉片，而沒有考慮實際情況中存在的葉片振動和和可能的多轉子相互作用所引起的複雜物理過程。對於實際飛行器來說，旋翼之間的空氣動力相互作用可以改變湍流尾流和尖端渦流的近場流動，從而可能改變聲音的產生物理原理、並可能產生新的聲源。目前來說這方面的相關研究相對稀缺。為此，我們需要對多旋翼的空氣聲學和空氣動力學進行系統的研究，識別新的可能的聲源並且增強噪聲和氣動預測能力。值得注意的是，由於葉片表面存在非定常的載荷，輕質材料製成的轉子葉片在高速轉動的情況下可能會發生振盪。為了進行準確的噪聲預測，必須量化葉片的位移和形變，並了解這些參數對噪聲產生和輻射的影響。另外，實際旋翼飛行器的遠場噪聲指向性特性也會由於機身和轉子葉片等固體表面散射的作用發生變化。為了考慮這些作用，我們需要發展更為有效的方法來對之進行計算。本研究將針對上述實際問題進行深入研究。首先，我們將對消聲室內的雙轉子相互作用進行空氣動力學和噪聲的系統測量。相控麥克風陣列將用於聲源成像，而粒子圖像測速儀將用於研究湍流場。同時我們將進行使用計算氣動聲學(CAA)的數值模擬，以分析空氣動力相互作用和噪聲產生過程和特性。其次，我們將採用高速攝像機對由于于葉片振動而產生的葉片尖端位移（可以包括在聲音預測中）將進行量化。同時我們還將開展靜音風洞測試以研究振盪的半無限葉片的空氣聲學特性，研究相關物理過程。最後，將開發一種有效的降階邊界元方法來計算寬帶轉子噪聲的散射和輻射。這項研究將增進我們對多轉子相互作用和葉片振動的空氣聲學和空氣動力學的理解。它還將為我們提供一種評估多轉子環境噪聲影響的有效方法。擬議研究的結果將有助於設計由多旋翼驅動的低噪聲飛行器。

16202520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202520.value: Through the project study, we have conducted theoretical, experimental, and numerical studies of the aeroacoustics of multi-rotors. The theoretical study shows that even slight blade vibration and rotation speed fluctuation can lead to significant noise generation due to their high efficiency in converting to the acoustic mode. The prediction accuracy of the theoretical study is also validated by the numerical simulation based on computational aeroacoustics and wind tunnel tests. We also developed the acoustic scaling law about the dependence of noise due to different unsteady modes on the influential factors including the rotating speeds, the radius, and blade number, etc. Acoustic imaging studies were conducted based on conventional and advanced wavelet-based beamforming methods, and the distribution of sound sources at different frequencies was studied. As for the scattering effect, the study based on the efficient boundary element method shows that the shielding effect is more significant at high frequency, as expected. Moreover, for the rotor noise that propagates in a spinning pattern, the scattering effect tends to be more important than that of the simplified point sources at the same frequency. The research outcome of the project includes the flow and acoustic data for muti-rotors in different working conditions by both experimental tests and high-fidelity computational aeroacoustic simulations. Moreover, a noise prediction model was proposed, which employs the blade-element and moment theory for the aerodynamic flow calculation and Goldstein's acoustic analogy for noise assessment. We also conducted the wing aeroacoustics measurement in the wind tunnel as a simplification of the rotor blades. A boundary element method with the technique to remove the ill-pose issue is implemented and employed for the scattering evaluation of the fuselage. The database and proposed method can support the continuing studies regarding the aeroacoustics of the emerging multi-rotor unmanned flying vehicles.

16202520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202520.value: With the rapid development of unmanned aircraft systems for low-altitude aviation, which causes worldwide attention and huge investment, continuing research and development activities can be conducted. Based on the developed prediction and numerical tools and the experimental capability, more relevant studies can be conducted. Recently, the PI was funded by RGC for another project focusing on the installation effect of unmanned aircraft systems on rotor noise. There are other topics in that project including the identification of the near-field patterns in complex aerodynamic flows, the development of the fast prediction method considering the installation effect, and the development of effective long-distance propagation. With the accumulated experience and enhanced understanding, studies related to rotor aeroacoustics can contain the investigation of the ground effect, considering the atmospheric condition and the psychoacoustic impact. Also, the research outcome can also lead to advanced technologies, e.g., the low-noise blade design, low-noise flight operation, etc., that can be used by the industry.

16202520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202520.value: This project studied the noise properties of multi-rotors used for unmanned flying vehicles. The interaction effect was studied by both the prediction method and tests in wind tunnels. The noise source distribution was studied by an advanced source imaging method and the characteristics were obtained using microphones. We also studied the airflow and noise properties in cases where the rotor blades are vibrating and experience speed fluctuation, which is common for plastic blades driven by practical motors. It is shown that the noise emission is very significant because these unsteady motions have very high efficiency in converting aerodynamic energy into sound. Moreover, by using an advanced numerical computation method, we revealed that the noise emitting from multi-rotors can be shielded by the fuselage of drones. Because of the employment of the POD-based method, the boundary element method can be completed within a short time, enhancing the efficiency in assessing the influence of key parameters. Within the project period, we also conducted the tests for wings in wind tunnels as a simplification of the rotor blades. The study enhances our understanding of the flow and acoustic physics of multi-rotors. Together with the comprehensive database obtained in this study, and the developed theoretical prediction models and numerical simulation tool, continuing research studies on more complex configurations of the multi-rotors for unmanned aircraft systems can be conducted to support the rapidly blooming low-altitude aviation.

16202720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202720.value: Soil bioengineering using plants is recognised as an aesthetically pleasing, ecologically sound and environmentally friendly technique to stabilise shallow soil against rainfall. Over the last four decades, many studies have been conducted on two root reinforcement mechanisms: the mechanical effects of root reinforcement and the hydrological effects of the increase of soil shear strength by transpiration. These two mechanisms have often been studied separately. Although plant roots are well-known to change their water content diurnally through repeated desiccation and rehydration cycles, the effect of root hydraulic status on their mechanical properties has received little attention. The coupling between the mechanical and hydrological effects of root reinforcement to unsaturated soil is unclear. Direct shear tests have been widely used to quantify the soil reinforcement effects of plant roots. However, accurately interpreting the root-induced changes in shear strength parameters remains challenging, since shearing along a pre-defined plane in these tests leads to undesirable non-uniform stress concentrations in the soil. In the proposed project, new experimental evidence and insights into root hydromechanical behaviour and their role on unsaturated soil reinforcement will be presented. This project will explore and quantify for the first time whether plant roots would experience hydraulic hysteresis when subjected to repeated dehydration/rehydration cycles and the effect of different hydraulic statuses on the root mechanical properties. This project will also pioneer the use of the Environmental Scanning Electron Microscopy (ESEM) on plant roots to estimate root volume changes during dehydration/rehydration cycles in the scales of millimetre to microns. When the root hydromechanical behaviour is identified, a new simple shear column apparatus will be developed and used to determine the shearing behaviour of unsaturated soil with roots. This new apparatus will eliminate the need to predefine a shear plane and, therefore, avoid any over-strengthening of soil with roots caused by non-uniform stress concentrations. The resulting original and unique data about the interaction between soil, roots and water will be used to evaluate existing root reinforcement theories. This new understanding on the coupled hydromechanical reinforcement mechanisms of roots to soil will enhance the ability of engineers to estimate the effects of root reinforcement on soil and assess the effects of vegetation on soil stabilisation. 利用植物加固斜坡一直被認為是一種美觀且對生態環境友好的方法，用以提高淺層土壤在降雨作用下的穩定性。在過去四十年中，已經有大量文獻研究根系加固的兩種機理，即根系加固的力學作用和蒸騰誘導土壤抗剪強度提高的水文學作用。這兩種機理通常被分開獨立研究。儘管植物根系每天會由於重複的乾燥和增濕循環而改變其含水量已經眾所周知，但是根系水力學狀態的改變怎樣影響根系的力學性質卻很少受到關注。根系加固中力學作用和水文學作用的耦合對非飽和土壤的是否存在影響也不清楚。直剪試驗通常被用於測量根係對土壤的加固作用，然而這種方法在準確解釋根系引起的剪切強度參數改變方面依然存在挑戰，這是由於在這一類實驗中土樣沿著預先確定的平面剪切從而導致土壤不均勻的應力集中。本項目會對根系的水-力行為以及它們在非飽和土加固中所起的作用提供新的實驗證據和深刻的見解。本項目將首次揭示植物根系在乾燥和增濕循環中的滯後行為，以及根係不同的水力學狀態怎樣影響根系的力學性質。本項目同時也將開創性地使用環境掃描電子顯微技術觀察根係並且估算根系在乾燥-增濕循環中的體積改變。在刻畫根系的水-力學行為後，將會開發一個單剪裝置用於確定非飽和根系土的剪切行為。這種高度創新和獨特的土壤-根系-水相互作用數據將被用於評價現存的根系加固理論。憑藉這種根係對土壤的耦合水-力加固機理的新發現，工程師們將會在根係對土壤加固作用的預測以及在植物對邊坡穩定性評價方面獲得新的知識及認知。

16202720.label: Realisation of objectives
16202720.value: Objective 1: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings have been disseminated in two top-tier cross-disciplinary international journals (see the published journal article, J8, and the accepted article, A1, in Part C). Hysteresis of root water potential and root moisture content (the so-called root water retention curve) were investigated and the phenomena were explained through the comprehensive monitoring of plant physiological responses and soil water potential (or suction) changes. An apparent decline in root water potential (psi_R) was observed as the available soil water depleted and correspondingly soil water potential (psi_S) decreased. As the plants progressed towards the permanent wilting point, the value of psi_R approached an asymptote of -4 MPa. Our results acquired psi_R measurements in excised roots from field capacity to near wilting moisture status, and marked a logarithmic psi_S-psi_R correlations, regardless of the plant growth periods. The nonlinearity of psi_S-psi_R response was observed to originate at the psi_S ranged between -0.3 and -0.5 MPa. The psi_R variation at these two soil depths, however showed no significant difference. The psi_R turned nonlinear faster at greater plant growth period, causing earlier wilting. Specific leaf area (SLA) showed an apparent decline with psi_S and displayed a similarly significant logarithmic correlation. The onset of the nonlinearity of SLA was also observed at the values of psi_S ranged between -0.3 and -0.5 MPa, consistent with the range obtained for the onset of the nonlinearity of psi_R. This consistency confirms the continuity between the root and leaf hydraulics during soil drying. SLA did not show any significant difference among different plant growth periods. We further observed SLA reducing with reducing psi_R, meaning that the dry matter in the leaves was increasing as psi_R progressed to drop. The linearity was found between SLA and psi_R was well perceived from the onset of the nonlinearity of psi_R. A correlation between root diameter and psi_R was obtained. The diameter measured in all our pots ranged between 0.3 mm and 0.6 mm and showed no significant difference among the plant growth periods. Objective 2: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings have been disseminated in several top-tier cross-disciplinary international journals (see publications J1-4 and J5-7 in Part C). We have conducted an experimental campaign to comprehensively and systematically investigate the effects of root decay (J1, J6), species variate (J2), growth media (J3), inter-species variability (J4), arbuscular mycorrhiza (AM) fungi (J6) and loading pattern (J7) on the biomechanical properties of roots with due consideration of the hysteretic root hydraulics identified in objective 1. Our root tensile test results showed that the variability of the tensile strength of the fine roots (diameter less than 1 mm) of vetiver grass was more significant than that of the coarse roots. Root water content primarily introduced variability to the tensile strength of the fine roots, whereas growth conditions (i.e., grass grown in pots versus in open field) and the rate of tensile loading (16 and 200 mm/min) played a smaller role. We identified variability of other root biomechanical traits, including Young's modulus and breakage strain, because of root water content (from oven dried to hydrated). Dried roots had higher tensile strength and higher Young's modulus but smaller breakage strain than hydrated fine roots. Strength and modulus had a negative power law relationship with root diameter (R^2 = 0.54 and 0.69, respectively), whereas strain was positively and linearly related with diameter but with a relatively low R^2 of 0.21 for all data with n =344. Considering that slope normally failed during rainfall, testing hydrated roots (compared with dried roots) was relevant, which would give a conservative (i.e., lower) strength for slope stability design. However, assuming roots to be hydrated might overestimate the ductility of roots and root-reinforced soil, leading to a less conservative estimation on the time-of-slope failure. We have also explored how changes in root moisture due to growth duration, decay duration by burning or herbicides affected the root biomechanical properties. All the tensile strength-diameter relations of the vetiver roots followed a negative power law relation (R^2 higher than 0.6) regardless of the treatment applied. Growth effects had minimal influences on root diameter during the 180-day growth period but had significant effects on the increase in median tensile strength. The tensile strength gain was consistent with the increase in cellulose and lignin contents. Root decay due to burning or herbicide application caused significant reductions in cellulose and lignin contents, accompanied by a drop in root tensile strength (i.e. root weakening). The root decay effects did not change the shape but shifted the tensile strength–diameter relations downwards. Objective 3: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings have been disseminated in a top-tier geotechnical journal (see the published article, J4, and article under preparation, P1, in Part C). We have designed, manufactured and used a newly-improved simple-shear apparatus to investigate the shearing behaviour and stress-dilatancy relationships of rooted soils. Identical rooted soil specimens were tested under direct-shear test (DST) and simple-shear test (SST) conditions, aiming to explore any difference in the root reinforcement effects to the soil due to the shear modes adopted. Results show that the soil strength was always overestimated when tested by DST at any confinement, when compared to the case of SST. For the bare soils, the effective peak friction angle and dilation angle obtained from the DST were overestimated by approximately 10% and 30%, respectively, because of the forced shearing on a predefined failure plane that did not coincide with the soil's natural plane of weakness. For the rooted soils, the shear strength parameters were also remarkably overestimated by the DST mode, especially the effective cohesion (by more than 100%). This phenomenon was because of the much greater principal stress rotation in the DSTs due to the undesirable stress concentration near the forced horizontal shear plane, making the direction of the major principal stress more perpendicular to that of the roots (which were mainly vertical in the tests) and thus causing virtual increases in root reinforcement. In terms of volumetric responses, the rooted soils exhibited greater dilatancy than the bare soils, irrespective to the shear modes adopted. Unlike the bare soils, the shear strain levels where the maximum dilatancy of the rooted soils was attained were lower than those corresponding to the peak shear strength. This phenomenon suggests that the roots progressively mobilised more of their tensile strength even after beyond the peak strength, continually contributing to the shear strength of the rooted soil specimens. Based on the new phenomena observed from the SST, a new stress-dilatancy relationship for the cohesive-frictional rooted soils was derived to explain and capture the root-induced changes in soil dilatancy under plane-strain condition. Existing Rowe stress-dilatancy equation was modified by incorporating the Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion and the shift of the Mohrs circle of strain accompanying root reinforcement and mobilisation of root tensile properties. The predicted results by the new equation showed good matches with the experimental data of both bare and rooted soils. It is the first root reinforcement model that is capable of quantifying the changes in peak friction angle due to the additional dilatancy contributed by the soil-root interaction during plane-strain shearing.

16202720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202720.value: For objective 1, we have provided new experimental evident that hydraulic properties of plant roots can be remarkably hysteretic (see published journal article, J8, and accepted articla, A1 in Part C). Gradients in water potential of soil and plant system drives the water movement in soil-plant-atmospheric continuum. Root water potential could significantly change the soil water potential during drying-wetting cycles. We have sought a logarithmic increase in gradient between soil and root water potentials. Specific leaf area reduced with root water potential, indicating the hydraulic continuity between roots and leaves. A new power law correlation between root diameter and root water potential established a trait-based understanding of root water uptake. For objective 2, we have conducted extensive experimental campaign to reveal the influences of various factors on the biomechanical properties of vetiver roots of varying water potential, including root decay (J1, J6), species variate (J2), growth media (J3), inter-species variability (J4), arbuscular mycorrhiza fungi (J7) and loading pattern (J8). Changes in root water potential enlarged the variability of root tensile properties. Gains in root water potential due to drought, wildfire or root hydraulic interaction with soils of different water retention abilities, made the roots significantly stronger and stiffer but less ductile under monotonic and cyclic loading conditions. The new findings highlight the needs to consider the dependency of root water potential on root tensile properties following the soil-plant-atmosphere interaction (objective 1) because such dependency would directly affect the root reinforcement effects to soils (objective 3). For objective 3, we are the first to demonstrate that root reinforcement mobilised under simple-shear conditions could be remarkably different from that under direct-shear condition (P1). The stress nonuniformities in rooted soil samples tested under direct-shear condition affected the soil shear strength. The cohesion, friction angle and dilation angle of rooted soils obtained from the direct-shear condition were all overestimated. Thus, we cautioned the use of direct-shear method to quantify the root reinforcement effects as the overestimation of rooted soil shear strength could lead to unsafe design of vegetated slopes. We have derived a new anisotropic failure criterion of rooted soils to explain the effects of root reinforcement (J5). The model can predict the amount the shear strength of rooted soils by considering the major principle stress rotation with respect to the root orientation under different loading paths including the direct- or simple-shear condition.

16202720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202720.value: The development of the simple shear apparatus through objective 3 has made the project team possible to investigate unsaturated soil-root hydromechanical interaction at more correct stress states. Because the new simple-shear apparatus was designed to have the capabilities in studying soil cyclic behaviour, future work will extend the test program to assess the liquefaction potential of unsaturated rooted soils, which is lacking in the literature. Moreover, the new test data generated from this project will be used to derive and formulate new root reinforcement models that take into account the effects of density, matric suction and dilatancy. The new discoveries of the detailed plant-water relation from the research through objectives 1 and 2 have provided new insights into the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) modelling, understanding how soil water potential varies with root and leaf water potentials. These findings have formed a solid basis for the project team to explore the possible use of plants as a type of moisture sensor in unsaturated soils for the purpose of evaluating slope stability; by remotely sensing the leaf water potential changes, it may be possible to estimate the soil water potential (i.e. soil suction) through SPAC modelling.

16202720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202720.value: The project has advanced our fundamental understanding of root reinforcement in soils at more correct stress states, providing necessary evidence to support the beneficial use of vegetation as a nature-based solution for slope stabilisation. We have discovered new mechanisms of how the measurements of the above-ground plant physiological responses such as leaf water potential could help assess the variation in not only the root water potential but also the soil’s. The latter (i.e. also known as soil suction) is a crucial stress-state variable that governs the hydromechanical behaviour of rooted soils. This finding provides engineers a new means to assess the effects of plant transpiration and root-water uptake on changes in soil suction, and hence soil stability. We have also designed and manufactured an improved large-size simple-shear apparatus to effectively quantify the effects of root reinforcement to soils. Based on the new data generated from this project, we are the first to highlight the remarkable overestimation root reinforcement effects, should the stress and strain nonuniformities of soil samples due to the use of existing direct-shear apparatus be ignored. We caution the use of direct-shear apparatus when quantifying the beneficial effects of root reinforcement, avoiding unsafe engineering design.

16202920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202920.value: Field Effect Transistors (FET) has been the most basic unit of today's nano-electronic circuits. Traditional FETs have a top-gate structure where the gate terminal is placed on the top of the transistors. The applied gate voltage modulates the conductance of channel of the FETs to control the terminal currents. In many other applications such as Thin-Film-Transistors (TFT) in display and flexible electronics, the gate is usually placed at the bottom of the FETs due to the limitation of the fabrication process. The source and drain regions of the bottom-gate FETs are contacted by metal from the top and the metal contact usually overlaps with the gate terminal at the bottom of the active layer. Due to the source-gate overlap region, the source-to-channel injection is usually achieved by carrier tunnelling instead of thermionic emission in the case of top-gate FETs. The gates of such transistors are thus modulating the supply of the carriers from the source instead of the channel conductance. This kind of transistors have many names such as Tunneling contact transistors, Schottky barrier TFTs or source-gated transistors (SGT) that we will use in this proposal. While some SGT has been used in production, a clear understanding of the operation principle, conduction mechanism, effects or geometry and design strategy are all missing. With the scaling of FETs following the Moore’s law is reaching its limit, researchers are searching for alternatives to the traditional FETs. 2-D FETs formed by layered materials have been considered as an attractive technology to extend the Moore’s law as well as adding new functionalities. Due to the thin-film nature of 2-D FETs, the bottom-gate structure is the more natural choice and most of the reported 2-D transistors are fabricated with low temperature bottom-gate technology. When applying the SGT structure to 2-D FETs, there are more complications coming from the 2-D material properties, Van deer Waal contact with metal and interface properties with the dielectric. Without a clear understanding of the device physics of 2-D SGT transistors, it is difficult to bring the 2-D SGT into applications. With an urgent need to have a unified understanding of the operation of 2-D SGTs, we will develop a compact model for it in this project. The model will be verified by atomic level ab-initio simulation, published experimental data as well as in-house fabricated test structures. After calibration, the model will be implemented in Verilog-A and released to the research community. 場效應晶體管（FET）一直是當今納米電子技術中最基本的單元電路。傳統FET具有頂部柵極結構，柵極端子放置在該結構中在晶體管的頂部。施加的柵極電壓調製了FET的通道以控制端子電流。在許多其他應用中，例如作為顯示器和柔性電子產品中的薄膜晶體管（TFT），門通常是由於製造工藝的限制，將其放置在FET的底部。的底部柵極FET的源極和漏極區域從頂部開始與金屬接觸而且金屬觸點通常與有源器件底部的柵極端子重疊層。由於源極-柵極重疊區域，源極至通道注入通常是在頂柵情況下，通過載流子隧穿而不是熱電子發射實現場效應管。因此，這種晶體管的柵極正在調製來自源端而不是通道電導。這種晶體管有很多諸如隧道接觸晶體管，肖特基勢壘TFT或源極門控之類的名稱我們將在本提案中使用的晶體管（SGT）。雖然某些SGT已用於生產，對操作原理，傳導機理，效果，幾何形狀和設計策略都丟失了。 隨著遵循摩爾定律的FET的規模達到極限，研究人員正在尋找傳統FET的替代品。分層形成的二維FET材料被認為是將摩爾定律擴展為以及添加新功能。由於二維FET的薄膜特性，底柵結構是更自然的選擇，並且大多數已報導的二維晶體管採用低溫底柵技術製造。什麼時候如果將SGT結構應用於二維FET，則二維材料的特性，范德華與金屬的接觸以及界面的特性會帶來更多的複雜性。對2-D SGT的器件物理認識不清，很難將2D SGT投入應用。迫切需要對二維SGT的操作有統一的了解，我們將開發一個緊湊的在此項目中為其建模。該模型將通過原子級ab-initio進行驗證模擬，發布的實驗數據以及內部製造的測試結構。校准後，該模型將在Verilog-A中實施並發佈到研究社區。

16202920.label: Realisation of objectives
16202920.value: The research project aimed to explore the intricate dynamics of Source-Gated Transistors (SGTs) and has successfully achieved its objectives with significant outcomes. The following section elaborates on how each objective has been realized, demonstrating the project's comprehensive impact. 1) Studying the Contact Structure The first objective focused on examining the contact structure between metal electrodes and common 2-D materials, such as MoS2 and WSe2. This objective has been achieved through extensive experimental and theoretical analyses. The research established how various factors, including material work function, doping levels, and interface characteristics, influence the contact properties. Notably, the study revealed that metals like scandium form effective ohmic contacts with niobium-doped MoS2, facilitating both thermionic emission and tunneling. These findings have contributed to understanding the contact mechanics in 2-D materials. 2) Designing Test Structures and Measurement Methodology The second objective aimed to design test structures and measurement methodologies to extract structural parameters and their effects on gate-source current-voltage characteristics. This objective was accomplished as the research team fabricated n-channel and p-channel SGTs with precise geometrical control. The meticulous design allowed for the detailed characterization of electrical properties, providing experimental data crucial for model calibration. 3) Studying Physical Conduction Mechanisms The third objective involved investigating the physical conduction mechanisms between metal electrodes and 2-D materials through atomistic ab initio simulations. This objective has been fully achieved as the research provided valuable insights into the unique operational mechanisms of SGTs, particularly the role of carrier tunneling from the source metal into the active 2-D material layer. The findings elucidated how gate voltage modulates carrier injection in the gate/source overlap region, rather than merely affecting channel conductance. 4) Analyzing Geometric Effects The fourth objective sought to study the effects of geometry, including active region thickness and gate-source overlap length, on source carrier injection efficiency and output current-voltage characteristics. This objective has been realized through systematic experimentation and analysis, which demonstrated how variations in geometry impact device performance. The results have been used to calibrate the model published as a result of this work. 5) Constructing a Compact Model The final objective was to construct a compact model to provide design guidelines for generic source-gated transistors with emphasis on 2D transistors. This objective has been achieved with the development of a comprehensive physical model that accurately represents the current-voltage characteristics of both thick body and 2-D SGTs. The model integrates various physical parameters, including effective doping levels and Fermi-level pinning, and has been successfully implemented in Verilog-A code for circuit simulation. The model's accuracy in simulating flexible electronic circuits and display circuits further confirms the accuracy of the model. In conclusion, the project has successfully achieved its objectives, leading to significant advancements in the understanding and application of Source-Gated Transistors. The comprehensive insights gained and the robust model developed will serve as a valuable resource for future research and practical implementations in the field of electronics. The groundwork laid by this project promises to inspire further exploration and innovation in the realm of source-gated transistors and their applications.

16202920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202920.value: A significant outcome of this project is the enhanced understanding of the device physics governing 2-D Source-Gated Transistors (SGTs). Unlike traditional top-gate transistors, the operational mechanism of source-gated transistors is predominantly characterized by carrier tunneling from the source metal into the active 2-D material layer. This research has established that the gate voltage modulates carrier injection in the gate/source overlap region, rather than solely influencing channel conductance. The insights gained into SGT operation have facilitated the development of a comprehensive physical model that accounts for the unique characteristics of 2-D SGTs. This model integrates various physical parameters, such as effective doping levels in the active layer and the degree of Fermi-level pinning, thereby providing an accurate representation of the current-voltage characteristics of these devices. These findings have been summarized in the second journal paper reported in Part C. To provide experimental data for model calibration and validation, we successfully fabricated n-channel and p-channel source-gated 2-D transistors. These test structures were designed with precise geometrical control, enabling detailed characterization of their electrical properties. In addition to provide experimental data for model calibration, our work has yielded valuable insights into the contact properties between metals and 2-D materials. Our research demonstrated that metals such as scandium can form ohmic contacts for holes in niobium-doped MoS2 films, facilitating both thermionic emission and tunneling contacts. These results have been documented in the first journal paper reported in Part C. The model developed in this project has been implemented in Verilog-A code and integrated into a circuit simulator. To assess the model's utility in circuit simulation, it necessitates application to large-scale circuits. Unfortunately, to date, the fabrication of circuits utilizing 2-D SGTs has been limited to a few transistors. However, the principles governing SGTs are also applicable to a broader class of oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs) used in flexible electronics and display technology. These devices share the SGT structure, and their operational principles are similarly dependent on gate-modulated metal-semiconductor contacts. Given the absence of models capturing SGT behavior, the model developed in this work holds significant value for large-scale circuits in oxide-TFT applications. To validate the functionality of our model in larger-scale circuits, it has been utilized to design flexible electronic circuits and display circuits, demonstrating high accuracy. The research has culminated in two journal publications and two conference papers, as detailed in Part C.

16202920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202920.value: The research on 2-D Source-Gated Transistors (SGTs) has laid a strong foundation for further development in both theoretical modeling and practical applications. The enhanced understanding of the device physics, particularly the tunneling mechanisms and the influence of gate voltage on carrier injection, presents opportunities to refine the existing model further. Future work could focus on exploring different 2-D materials and their interfaces with various metals to optimize performance across diverse conditions. A proposed course of action includes expanding the experimental fabrication of larger-scale circuits using 2-D SGTs, which would allow for comprehensive testing of the model in real-world applications. Collaborations with industry partners could facilitate the integration of these transistors into flexible electronics and display technologies, capitalizing on the model’s applicability to design circuits with both 2-D transistors and oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs). Additionally, further investigations into the geometric effects and interface properties could yield insights into improving device efficiency. Exploring advanced fabrication techniques and materials could also enhance the performance of SGTs. Overall, this research not only contributes to the fundamental understanding of 2-D SGTs but also opens pathways for innovative applications in next-generation electronic devices.

16202920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202920.value: This research project focuses on an emerging type of transistor called a Source-Gated Transistor (SGT), which uses two-dimensional materials. Unlike traditional transistors, SGTs work by allowing electrical charges to tunnel from a metal source into the active material, making them potentially more efficient. The significance of this research lies in its ability to improve how we understand and design these devices. By identifying key factors that affect their performance, such as the materials used and their thickness, the researchers have created a detailed model that helps predict how these transistors will behave. The findings could also help industries create more advanced technologies, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in electronics. Overall, this project not only enhances our knowledge of SGTs but also opens the door for exciting innovations in the electronics world.

16203720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203720.value: Landslide prevention is an important issue in Hong Kong and many parts of the world. More than 120,000 landslides, including 89,000 relict landslides, 21,000 recent natural terrain landslides, and over 10,000 man-made slope failures, have been identified in Hong Kong. In a changing climate, a large rainstorm can trigger more than 1,000 landslides. Therefore, landslide forecasting is an essential task for devising engineering risk mitigation strategies and achieving early warning and evacuation. Recently, machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool in real-time information fusion and prediction. Machine learning builds up a model by using a training dataset and applies the trained algorithm for prediction. Out of numerous options, landslide forecasting using machine learning is very appealing because of the huge amount of historical landslide data available in Hong Kong, including reliable records on 414 major rainstorms in Hong Kong from 1984 to 2016, the distribution of landslides caused by each rainstorm, and the high-resolution (0.1–0.3 m) LiDAR-based digital elevation model of Hong Kong. Such rich data can be used to train suitable machine learning algorithms to revolutionize the forecasting of rain-induced landslides. The primary objective of this research project is to use the aforementioned rich landslide and triggering rainfall data to train machine learning algorithms and apply the trained algorithms in forecasting real-time landslides. To achieve this project goal, three closely related research tasks will be carried out. First, various sources of topographic and geological data, historical landslide data, and corresponding triggering rainfall data will be organised into geographic information system (GIS)-based geo-databases in machine-readable forms. Second, the geo-databases will be used to train and validate several deep learning algorithms. Special machine learning technical issues associated with landslide forecasting, such as highly imbalanced data samples and uncertainty in training data, will be tackled. Finally, a protocol for using the trained deep learning algorithms to forecast real-time landslides will be established. A significant innovation of this project will be the ability to forecast the occurrence times and locations of landslides using over 200 geo-information layers. This ability goes beyond the prediction of landslide density–rainfall intensity relations via statistical methods, which predict the number or probability of landslides but not the likely locations and times of landslides. This pilot study on real-time landslide forecasting will promote the application of machine learning in landslide science and pose many technical issues for further study. 滑坡防治是香港和世界許多地區的重要問題。香港已記錄有超過12萬個滑坡，包括8.9萬個歷史天然滑坡、2.1萬個近期天然滑坡、以及1萬多個建築邊坡滑坡。在氣候變環境下，一場大暴雨可能引發數以千計的滑坡，滑坡預測是製定減災策略、實施滑坡預警和疏散的基礎工作。近年來蓬勃發展的機器學習方法已成為資訊融合和實時預測的強大工具，通過歷史數據訓練建立模型，再將訓練好的演算法應用於滑坡預測。採用機器學習進行滑坡預測與其它諸多方法相比尤為可行，因為香港擁有完備的歷史滑坡數據，包括1984至2016年間414場大暴雨的可靠記錄、每場暴雨誘發的滑坡分佈、以及基於光學雷達LiDAR的高解析度（0.1-0.3米）數字高程模型。如此豐富的數據非常適合訓練和實施機器學習演算法，提升降雨誘發滑坡的預測水準。 本項目的主要目的是基於上述豐富的香港滑坡及其觸發降雨數據來訓練機器學習演算法，並將訓練好的演算法應用於實時滑坡預測。為了實現該目標，將開展三項緊密相關的研究任務。首先，將多種來源的地形地質數據、歷史滑坡數據、以及相應的觸發降雨數據以機器可讀的形式整合到地理資訊系統GIS數據庫中。其次，基於該地理數據庫訓練並驗證多種深度學習演算法，重點解決與滑坡預測相關的特殊機器學習難題，例如訓練數據的高度不均衡性及不確定性等。最後，建立通過深度學習進行實時滑坡預測的方法。 本項目的重大創新之一是通過200多個地理資訊層來預測滑坡的時間和位置。這種能力遠遠超出了現有的基於滑坡密度與降雨強度統計關係的方法。統計方法僅能預測滑坡的數量或概率，無法預測其可能的位置和時間。此項實時滑坡預測的初步研究將促進機器學習在滑坡科學中的應用，並提出許多技術問題供進一步的深入研究。

16203720.label: Realisation of objectives
16203720.value: (1) To integrate multi-source spatio-temporal geo-databases for landslide learning. A comprehensive database named READHK has been compiled in a geographic information system, composed of three sub-databases: rainstorm sub-database (RSD), multi-source sub-database (MSD) and landslide sub-database (LSD). RSD is based on hourly rainfall data from 141 rain gauges, consisting of maximum rolling rainfall indices of 419 rainstorms in the period of 1984-2017. MSD covers twenty geo-environmental data layers related to terrain, geology and ground cover. LSD contains 109,333 natural terrain landslide records and 10,000 man-made slope failure cases. To further enhance the landslide inventory from point-based to polygon-based, a deep learning method is proposed to interpret landslide surface information from satellite images, including landslide areas and traces. It consists of three steps, namely image enhancement using pan-sharpening, landslide identification using deep learning, and landslide segmentation using morphological image processing. A case study of East Sai Kung is investigated to demonstrate the capacity of the proposed framework. The pan-sharpening techniques improve the accuracy of deep learning-based landslide identification. The proposed method provides an efficient and objective paradigm to identify numerous landslides in a large area. Additionally, two high-resolution LiDAR-derived digital terrain models taken in 2010 and 2020 are leveraged to interpret the volumes of 1326 shallow landslides that occurred in Hong Kong during the same period. The newly interpreted volume information, which can reflect landslide subsurface characteristics, further enriches the created landslide database. Power-law models relating landslide volume to landslide surface characteristics (i.e., source area, width and length) are constructed to estimate the landslide volume. These power laws are associated with high coefficients of determination of more than 0.8, providing more accurate estimations of source area and volume than the conventional elliptic assumption. The method is also applied to detect co-seismic landslides. Representative outputs: [1] Ju, L.Y., Xiao, T., Zhang, L.M. (2022a). Automatic landslide inventory generation using deep learning. Proceedings of the 8th International Symposium on Geotechnical Safety and Risk, 673-678. Conference Paper #2. [2] Ju, L.Y., Zhang, L.M., Xiao, T. (2023). Power laws for accurate determination of landslide volume based on high-resolution LiDAR data. Engineering Geology, 312, 106935. Journal Paper #5. [3] Wang, H.J., Zhang, L.M., Wang, L., Fan, R.L., Zhou, S.Y., Qiang, Y.J., Peng, M. (2023). Machine learning powered high-resolution co-seismic landslide detection. Gondwana Research, 123, 217-237. Journal Paper #6. (2) To develop machine learning methods for predicting event-based spatio-temporal landslides A novel AI-powered object-based landslide susceptibility assessment method has been proposed to predict the spatial distribution of landslides. The landslide and non-landslide objects and samples are first extracted based on an optimal object size. Then, several deep learning techniques, such as convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM), are applied to learn susceptibility prediction. The proposed models outperform conventional cell-based models. The new models have been used to produce the ﬁrst set of AI-based territory-wide landslide susceptibility maps for Hong Kong and extended to assess earthquake landslide susceptibility. A transfer learning-based landslide susceptibility assessment approach is further developed, aiming at substantially improving prediction for specific regions with limited landslide data using the knowledge from similar regions. A case study in Hong Kong has demonstrated that this method is an intelligent and promising way to improve landslide susceptibility assessment for data-limited regions. Regarding the spatio-temporal forecasting of rain-induced landslides, a landslide forecasting model has been developed within a unified machine learning framework. With a storm-based data integration strategy and multiclass classification on landslide scales, the framework incorporates landslide time and consequences into landslide susceptibility mapping to successfully achieve spatiotemporal landslide forecasting. For those time-incomplete landslides, a probabilistic landslide modelling strategy based on ‘at least one failure’ is proposed to link the storm-based failure probabilities and the period-based landslide observations. The machine learning-based landslide forecasting model is validated against historical landslide incidents both temporally and spatially. The model can predict the real-time evolution of probabilities, scales, and spatial distribution of landslides during the progression of a rainstorm, which can never be achieved by statistical methods. (3) To forecast real-time rain-induced landslides and possible landslides under extreme rainstorms The developed machine learning models are applied to forecast the spatio-temporal landslide distributions during an extreme rainstorm on 6-9 June 2008, with a recurrence period of 1100 years. Results show that hardly any landslides occur before 30 h. The western Lantau Island is the first area to witness many landslides at 32 h. Afterwards, there is a rapid outbreak of landslides on the north-western Hong Kong Island and western Kowloon for man-made slopes. The final predicted landslide distribution at 96 h is consistent with the observations, with a total of 191 man-made slope failures and 2033 natural terrain landslides. Moreover, a novel terrain matching-targeted machine learning model is proposed for predicting landslide runout paths under extreme rainfall. The model first forward predicts multiple travel distances based on geographic characteristics of all cells along a possible runout path, and then determines the termination cell whose predicted travel distance fits the terrain features best to backward estimate model parameters. It is applied to forecast the landslide spatial impact extent during an extreme rainstorm on 16-21 August 2005. A total of 2238 landslide travel paths are predicted in Mid-Levels, among which 1268 landslides rush into the urban area. The model can provide guidelines for designing landslide prevention and mitigation measures and has also been extended to analyze the landslide dam formation. A prompt quantitative landslide risk assessment framework has been proposed using the predictions of both landslide initiation and mobility. The developed models have been applied to assist emergency management during the century black storms in June 2008, Sept 2023 and the severe storm in May 2024. 16203720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203720.value: (1) A comprehensive spatio-temporal geo-database including rainfall, geo-environmental data and landslides has been compiled for landslide machine learning. The database is further enriched to cover full information on landslide geometric characteristics with multi-source satellite images and LiDAR data. A deep learning method is proposed to interpret landslide surface information from satellite images, including landslide areas and traces (Ju et al., 2022a (Conference Paper #2)). High-resolution LiDAR-derived digital terrain models are leveraged to interpret landslide volumes, based on which power law models relating landslide source volume to landslide area are developed (Ju et al., 2023 (Journal Paper #5)). (2) A novel AI-powered object-based landslide susceptibility assessment method has been developed. Based on this advanced tool, we have produced the ﬁrst set of AI-based territory-wide landslide susceptibility maps for Hong Kong (Wang et al., 2021 (Journal Paper #4)). A transfer learning-based landslide susceptibility assessment approach is further developed to improve prediction for specific regions with limited landslide data using the knowledge from similar regions (Wang et al., 2023 (Journal Paper #3)). With a storm-based data integration strategy and multiclass classification on landslide scales, a machine learning framework incorporating landslide time and consequences is proposed to achieve spatiotemporal forecasting (Xiao and Zhang, 2023a (Journal Paper #2)). It can predict the real-time evolution of probabilities, scales and spatial distribution of landslides and serves as an essential tool for landslide risk assessment and early warning. (3) The spatio-temporal evolution of landslides under extreme rainstorms can be successfully predicted with the developed machine learning models (Xiao and Zhang, 2023b (Conference Paper #3)). A storm transposition method is developed to generate more extreme rainstorms (e.g., 85% PMP) for stress testing of the existing slope safety system. A novel terrain matching-targeted machine learning model is proposed for predicting landslide runout paths (Ju et al., 2022b (Journal Paper #1)). With the obtained spatial impact map, the model can provide guidelines for designing landslide prevention and mitigation measures. A prompt quantitative landslide risk assessment framework has been proposed using the predictions of both landslide initiation and mobility (He et al., 2023 (Journal Paper #8)). (4) The outcomes have played a key role in assisting emergency management of landslides caused by the Sept 2023 black storm. The outcomes also form the basis for several major research awards: National Outstanding Engineer Medal (國家卓越工程師獎) from the State Council of China (2023), Ralph B. Peck Award from ASCE (2023), ISSMGE Bright Spark Lecture Award (2023), HKIE Geotechnical Paper Award (2024), 75th Géotechnique Anniversary Early Career Award (2023), Engineering Geology Best Paper Award (2024), FOMLIG Excellent Paper Award (2023), and ISGSR Best Student Paper Award (2022).

16203720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203720.value: It is challenging to automatically compile landslide inventory and predict the landslide full process timely for landslide management, warning and engineering design. The emerging machine learning techniques are an attractive solution to rapid landslide prediction due to their powerful ability to model complex systems and high computational efficiency after training. A course of action for landslide prediction with machine learning techniques is proposed as follows: (1) Automated landslide mapping: Machine learning methods need to be developed to automatically delineate landslide sources and trails from aerial photos and satellite images. This will greatly enhance the update frequency of the existing landslide inventory in Hong Kong. (2) Full-process landslide prediction: More advanced machine learning models are required to predict landslide locations, sizes, runout paths, and impact areas simultaneously. Several issues such as incomplete landslide data needs to be addressed.

16203720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203720.value: Landslide prevention is an important issue in Hong Kong owing to the region’s steep terrain and subtropical climate. On average, 380 natural terrain landslides and 230 man-made slope failures occurred in Hong Kong annually. In a changing climate, rainstorms of large magnitude may occur more frequently in the future, and thus the slope safety will be more challenging. With the rich landslide data and triggering rainfall data in Hong Kong, this research project has developed novel machine learning models for forecasting event-based spatio-temporal rain-induced landslides. Various sources of geo-environmental, landslide and rainfall data, as well as satellite images and LiDAR data, are integrated in machine-readable forms. Several deep learning models are developed for landslide susceptibility assessment and spatio-temporal forecasting. Transfer learning is applied to improve landslide prediction for data-limited regions. The machine learning-powered spatio-temporal forecasting model can predict the real-time evolution of probabilities, scales, spatial distribution and runout paths of landslides. The machine learning models are applied to extreme rainstorms to identify high-risk and landslide-prone areas. The outcomes lay a solid basis for managing landslide hazards, forecasting the slope safety under extreme storm conditions, and developing effective engineering techniques for improving community resilience.

16203820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203820.value: Safeguarding public health from drinking water consumption is one of the 17 sustainable development goals of the United Nations (UN). Achieving this goal is complicated by the need to control micropollutants of health concern, such as pharmaceuticals and personal care product residues, on top of pathogen transmission. These micropollutants, with increasing concentrations in source water, are well documented in developed countries. Many of these micropollutants cannot be well removed by conventional drinking water treatment processes and thus require advanced treatment. Advanced treatment processes, such as ozonation, carbon adsorption, advanced oxidation, and photocatalytic oxidation, have been proposed and proven effective in controlling micropollutants in laboratory settings. Although some of these processes have already been used in practice, their implementation is very much limited even in developed countries because of the high cost and/or intensive energy demand incurred. The problem of micropollutants in drinking water is more serious in developing countries, where their uses in agriculture, aquaculture, animal farming and human health/medical care are poorly controlled and advanced drinking treatment is unaffordable. Among the advanced oxidation and photocatalytic oxidation processes for micropollutant abatement, UV light at 254 nm (UV254) is commonly used as an energy source to produce reactive species and degrade micropollutants. However, any UV254-driven process is energy intensive and unsustainable. This energy issue is being solved by adopting solar irradiation to activate chlorine or visible-light photocatalysts. However, solar-driven processes are less effective in generating highly reactive species than their UV254-driven counterparts. In our recent trials, we have observed that combining chlorine, which is available in drinking water, with near-UV-to-visible light photocatalysts and light at 365/450 nm can much enhance (over 10 times) the degradation of carbamazepine, a micropollutant, compared with a similar setting but without photocatalysts. In this proposed project, based on the observation, we will develop a novel near-UV-to-visible light photocatalytic chlorine activation process for micropollutant degradation. We propose and will verify a few hypotheses that explain the fast but different degradation rates of micropollutants by this process using different photocatalysts and lights at different wavelengths. We will also apply this process to develop a novel reactor using photocatalyst-coated optical fibers. We will examine the matrix effects and long-term performance of the process in treating real water. The development of the process/reactor and the improved understanding of the fundamentals will facilitate the practical implementation of the process to achieve the UN’s sustainable development goal in developed and developing countries. 保障公眾飲用水安全是聯合國的17個可持續發展目標之一。由於需要在控制病原體傳播的基礎上控制水中可能威脅公眾健康的微污染物，例如殘留的藥品和個人護理品，實現此目標變得愈發複雜。已有很多報道指出，這些微污染物在發達國家的水源中的濃度不斷增加。由於常規的飲用水處理工藝對大部分微污染物的去除效果不佳，因此需要對飲用水進行更深度的處理。目前，已經有很多高級處理工藝，如臭氧氧化，碳吸附，高級氧化和光催化氧化，被提出並已在實驗室條件下證明可有效去除微污染物。儘管其中一些工藝已在實踐中使用，但鑒於其相對高的成本和/或能耗，即便是在發達國家，這些工藝的實施也受到很大限制。飲用水的微污染物問題在發展中國家更加嚴重。因為微污染物在這些國家的農業、水產養殖、畜牧業和醫療保健行業中的使用處於失控狀態，而這些國家更是負擔不起高級處理工藝。 254 nm的紫外線（UV254）通常作為產生反應活性物質和降解微污染物的能量來源，被應用在去除微污染物的高級氧化和光催化氧化工藝中。然而，由UV254驅動的工藝大多數都是高能耗和不可持續的。通過利用太陽光輻射來活化氯或可見光催化劑可以解決這一問題。但是，太陽光驅動的工藝在產生高反應活性物質方面遠不及UV254驅動的工藝高效。在我們最近的試驗中，我們發現當結合飲用水中存在的餘氯，近紫外至可見光的光催化劑，以及365或450 nm的光相時，卡馬西平（一種微污染物）的降解速率會比沒有光催化劑時高十倍。在本研究項目中，我們將基於上述的發現開發壹種新型近紫外線至可見光光催化氯活化工藝用於降解水中的微污染物。我們提出並將驗證一些假設，用以解釋使用不同催化劑和不同波長的光對於提高該工藝中微污染物降解速率的原因。我們還會利用此工藝來開發一種使用了光催化鍍膜光纖的新型反應器。另外，我們會評估常見水參數對於該工藝在處理真實水體中的微污染物時的影響以及該工藝長期運行時的性能。該工藝和反應器的開發以及對工藝涉及的基本原理的更深層次的了解將促進此工藝的實際實施，從而促進在發達和發展中國家實現聯合國的可持續發展目標。

16203820.label: Realisation of objectives
16203820.value: Objective 1 is completed. The chlorine activation mechanisms in enhancing radical production in the near-UV-to-visible light photocatalytic chlorine activation process were investigated using near UV-activated TiO2 and visible light-activated g-C3N4. Photolysis of free chlorine (HOCl/ClO-) is an advanced oxidation process (AOP) to produce hydroxyl (HO radical) and other radicals for refractory micropollutant degradation. However, HOCl/ClO- is only conducive to activation and production of radicals by UVC or UVB light. For the first time we show the use of near-UV-to-visible light to produce HO and ClO radicals, through use of g-C3N4 and TiO2 and photogenerated h_vb^+, e_cb^- and O2- radical in the presence of HOCl/ClO-, which is termed Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine and nUV/TiO2/chlorine processes, respectively. Both Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine and nUV/TiO2/chlorine processes show enhanced HO and ClO radical yield and achieve 16/34.2 and 7/3.5 times higher pseudo-first order degradation rate constant of a model micropollutant, CBZ, than those without g-C3N4/TiO2 and HOCl/ClO-, respectively. In the nUV/TiO2/chlorine process, chlorine serves a more important role as a catalyst to enhance the yield of HO radicals without being consumed, in addition to its role as a radical precursor to produce HO radicals and reactive chlorine species. The findings about the Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine process that were obtained from our preliminary investigation (stipulated in the proposal) and the following mechanistic investigation, following the task plan stipulated in the proposal, before project commencement, were published in Environmental Science and Technology in 2020 (Journal paper #1). The findings about nUV/TiO2/chlorine process were published in ACS EST Water in 2022 (Journal paper #2). Two more manuscripts to differentiate the detailed roles of h_vb^+ and e_cb^- in two light-activated systems are submitted (Journal paper #3) and in preparation to be submitted in 2025 (Journal paper #4), respectively. The content is also included in the thesis of the MPhil student trained from the project. One paper was given in a leading conference (Conference paper #1). Objective 2 is completed. Five emerging contaminants, including BA, CAF, DEET, DMOB and NB, with different physicochemical properties were selected as model emerging contaminants to investigate the effects of their affinity to g-C3N4 and TiO2 on their photocatalytic degradation by the nUV/TiO2/chlorine and Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine processes. The degradation rate constants for both processes followed the same order as DMOB, CAF, DEET, BA and NB. The degradation rate constants of DMOB and CAF in both processes are all at least 10 times higher than those of DEET, BA, and NB, which is due to the much higher second order rate constants of DMOB and CAF with ClO radical and both ClO and Cl2- radicals, respectively. For the first time, affinities of emerging contaminants, including BA, CAF, DEET, DMOB and NB, towards g-C3N4 and TiO2 were studied by measuring the differential capacitance variation of the three-electrode systems due to the presence of each emerging contaminants. The obtained apparent first-order degradation rate constants of BA, CAF, DEET, DMOB and NB were then correlated with the differential capacitance variation. A model, considering the affinities of emerging contaminants to g-C3N4 and TiO2 and reactivity of the micropollutant with radicals formed in both processes, was established. With this model, the degradation rate constants of other emerging contaminants by the Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine and nUV/TiO2/chlorine processes can be predicted based on their affinities to the g-C3N4 and TiO2 and reactivities with radicals formed in both processes. A manuscript reported the above finding is in preparation for the submission to Water Research in 2025 (Journal paper #5). The content is also included in the thesis of the PhD student trained from the project. Objective 3 is completed. The impacts of various water parameters, including bicarbonate, NOM, ammonia and chloride, on the CBZ degradation were evaluated. Some results were included in the manuscripts published in ACS EST Water in 2022 (Journal paper #2). Another manuscript evaluating the impact of ammonia was published in Water Research in 2024 (Journal paper #6) and presented in a conference (Conference paper #2). It reveals the production of active chlorine species (RCS), reactive nitrogen species (RNS) and HO radical in the presence of NH3. Photocatalyst-coated side-emitting polymeric optical fiber (POFs) with high photocatalyst loading and a porous coated layer were fabricated by a facile dip-coating using acetone without affecting the PMMA core of the POFs. The high mass-loading TiO2-POFs were used to activate ambient chlorine under UV-A light irradiation for emerging contaminant removal in decentralized water supply treatment system. CBZ was selected as a model organic pollutant, whose degradation rate constants reached 0.0304 min-1 using a bundle of 150 individual TiO2-POFs with 5.0 mgCl2/L chlorine, which was 8.4 times higher than that without of chlorine. The hydrophobic PVDF-constructed TiO2 metamaterial porous structures on TiO2-POFs repulse hydropholic aqueous components, thus they possess less impacts from aqueous components on their photocatalytic performance compared with that of TiO2 in slurry reactors or on quartz optical fibers. The photocatalytic activity of TiO2-POFs decreased by 40% by treating model drinking water containing high levels of Fe3+ and Cu2+ over 60 cycles, due to excessive copper ion deposition. However, the activity could be easily restored via simple acid-washing. More importantly, the virgin, aged and regenerated TiO2-POFs treated solutions are compatible with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, indicating its safe-use for decentralized drinking water treatment. In the presence of aqueous chlorine, the TiO2-POFs with an UV-A light source produced lower yields or cyto- and geno- toxicity disinfection by-products (DBPs) than comparative UV-C/chlorine AOP at similar CBZ removal during both short- and longer-term operation. A manuscript reported the findings related to Objective 3 is submitted to Environmental Science and Technology (Journal paper #7). One conference presentation about the topic was given in a leading conference (Conference paper #3).

16203820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203820.value: The major findings obtained from this study have formulated 3 prestigious journal papers (#1‒2, and 6) and 3 conference presentations (#1‒3) in three leading conferences in the field. We are also working on four other journal papers (#3‒4, 5 and 7). This study provided training of 2 postgraduate student who obtained his PhD degree and her MPhil degree in Jan 2022 and August 2022, respectively. Details can be found in Section 5.3 above. The specific major findings are: A novel strategy for advance oxidation was developed through the use of near-UV-to-visible light activated photocatalyst and chlorine as well as another commonly used oxidant, i.e., NH2Cl , to achieve enhanced emerging contaminants degradation, which was mainly attributed to the generation of RCS, RNS, and HO radical from chlorine and NH2Cl activation by photoinduced h_vb^+, e_cb^- and O2- radical (Journal papers #1-4 and Conference paper #1). Affinities of BA, CAF, DEET, DMOB and NB to TiO2 and g-C3N4 were quantified by measuring the differential capacitance variation induced by the addition of each micropollutant to the three-electrode systems using TiO2 and g-C3N4 coated FTO as working electrodes. A diffusion-mediated degradation model was then established to successfully correlate the affinities of the selected emerging contaminants to TiO2 and g-C3N4 with their apparent first-order degradation rate constants by the nUV/TiO2/chlorine and Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine processes. The performances of the Vis/g-C3N4/chlorine and UV/TiO2/chlorine processes in degrading other emerging contaminants thus can be predicted based on their affinities to the g-C3N4 and TiO2 and reactivity towards radicals formed in both processes using the developed model (Journal paper #5). The impacts of aqueous components on the processes were evaluated (Journal papers #2-3 and #6, Conference paper #2). A facile dip-coating method using acetone was developed for the fabrication of TiO2-coated side-emitting POFs with high photocatalyst loading and a porous polymeric outer layer. The use of TiO2-POFs can eliminate the energy consumption for photocatalyst recovery and minimize light irradiation loss due to light scattering or occlusion without sacrificing the mass transfer efficiency as those photocatalyst coated fibers fabricated by conventional methods (Journal paper #7, Conference paper #3).

16203820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203820.value: The fundamentals revealed by this research enables the design of different photocatalysts that are effective in activating chlorine to produce higher concentrations of radicals. Photocatalysts including modified TiO2 and g-C3N4 can be developed to further improve the hole-electron separation under solar irradiation to enhance the chlorine activation efficiency. It also enables the future development of activation of oxidants. For example, dissolved organic matters under solar irradiation may also activate HOCl/NH2Cl in water to produce radicals that degrade organic pollutants. Or photocatalysts can be used to activate hydrogen peroxide and permanganate. The photocatalytic chlorine activation processes may also be used to produce radicals for chemical and polymer synthesis. Future research may also focus on developing better photocatalyst coated optical fibers (P-OFs) for effective activation of chlorine for the application in groundwater treatment and water disinfection.

16203820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203820.value: Elevated levels of emerging contaminants found in source water poses great threat to drinking water safety and human health. The novel near-UV-to-visible light photocatalytic chlorine activation process provides a greener, low-carbon and low-cost strategy to produce significant amounts of radicals on needs to tackle the challenges of emerging contaminants by taking the advantage of residual chlorine in drinking water. With the help of the diffusion-mediated degradation model, performance of process in eliminating concerned impurities can be predicted to make sure the treated water safe for drinking. Of great importance is the use of the TiO2-coated polymer optical fibers that greatly facilitates the practical implementation of the near-UV-to-visible light photocatalytic oxidant activation process. The efficient emerging contaminant degradation and excellent stability and reusability of the coated optical fibers well demonstrated that such a AOP is a promising assembly treatment module in both centralized and decentralized water systems for emerging contaminants abatement.
