16204220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204220.value: The urban heat island effect, in which temperatures are higher in urban areas than in their rural counterparts, has significant implications on sustainable development of cities. In China, the percentage of urban population rose from 18% in 1978 to 59% in 2017, and the resultant warming of annual air temperature reaches about 2 oC over the Yangtze River Delta megalopolis. The spatiotemporal variation in air temperature at the intra-urban scale (i.e., neighborhood heat island) plays a critical role in determining the vulnerability of urban residents and infrastructures under future environmental changes. Accurate characterizations of neighborhood heat islands remain challenging due to sparsely distributed meteorological stations within cities. In the absence of sufficient observational data, mesoscale urban climate modeling represents the state-of-the-art tool to study neighborhood heat islands under the changing climate. Despite the implementation of complex features in mesoscale climate models in previous years, the physical-based model does not function equally well over different neighborhoods due to their heterogeneous landscape and social-economic conditions. This limitation leads to the following questions: how large is the spatiotemporal variability of neighborhood heat islands, to what degree can latest approaches predict neighborhood heat islands, and how can we improve in future numerical and observational studies? These questions have been addressed for a few cities with site-specific investigations, yet a general framework applicable for most cities is missing in the literature. The proposed project will be the first attempt to answer the above questions at a large spatial extent. We will quantify the spatiotemporal variability of air temperature in different urban neighborhoods across Chinese cities between 2011 and 2017. Adopting the Local Climate Zone classification system, we will divide the cities into neighborhoods with distinct temperature regimes and conduct cross-city comparisons over various local climate zones. The next step will be to evaluate the performance of the urban climate model and advanced regression algorithm in predicting neighborhood heat islands. The comparison results can reveal constraints of current modeling methods and provide directions for future work. Last, we will utilize the knowledge gained from the first two steps to explore the optimal design of urban meteorological networks, which are under rapid growth in China. Research outcomes will help address challenges related to resident health and energy consumption in the urban environment. In the long term, the proposed project sheds new light on neighborhood heat island studies and provides an important basis for fine-resolution urban weather forecast. 城市熱島效應是指城市氣溫普遍高於其周邊郊區的現象，此效應對城市可持續發展有著顯著影響。1978年以來，中國進入快速城市化進程，城市人口占總人口比例從18%增長至2017年的59%。伴隨著城市化進程，城市區域氣溫逐漸上升，如長三角地區年均氣溫已上漲約2℃。在未來氣候變化的背景下，城市內街區尺度上空氣溫度的時空差異將決定城市居民健康和基礎設施的脆弱性。現有氣象觀測站一般零星分佈在城市個別區域，因此準確表徵高分辨率的街區熱島效應受到限制。在缺少足夠觀測資料條件下，研究氣候變化背景下街區熱島效應最有效的方法是運用微尺度城市氣候模型。隨著近年來的不斷發展，城市氣候模型已具備複雜的結構和功能，但由於異質性的城市土地利用和社會經濟因子，基於物理機制的模型並不能準確地模擬不同條件下的街區尺度微氣候。這些限制條件引發我們對以下問題的思考：街區熱島效應的時空變異性有多大？運用最前沿的方法是否可以準確地預測街區熱島情況？未來我們該如何推進基於數值模擬和觀測資料的城市熱環境研究？針對以上問題，先前的工作對一些特定城市進行了研究，然而迄今始終缺少適用於多數城市的街區熱島效應的研究框架。 此項目計畫首次嘗試從大尺度而非特定城市來解決上述問題。該研究將量化2011至2017年間全中國城市內的街區氣溫時空差異性。通過採用城市局地氣候分區系統，我們將城市分為具有不同熱環境特徵的街區，並且針對不同局地氣候分區進行跨城市對比研究。下一步，我們將評估城市氣候模型和統計回歸方法對街區熱島效應的預測性能。對比此兩種方法的預測結果，揭示現有模型的缺陷，為未來模型研究發展指出方向。最後，基於以上兩步的結果，我們將探索適用於中國城市的最優化城市氣候觀測網路設計。此研究成果將為未來城市的居民健康，能源消耗等相關挑戰提供有效建議和解決方案。從長期學術發展角度上看，此項目將成為街區熱島效應研究的新起點，並為高精度的城市天氣預測奠定重要基礎。

16204220.label: Realisation of objectives
16204220.value: The proposed project objectives have been achieved. As a result, the project team has published 4 top journal articles and 4 conference presentations. Two PhD students have developed part of their PhD thesis from this project. One has already graduated in 2023, and one will graduate in August 2025. Objective 1. Quantify the spatiotemporal variability of neighborhood heat islands over different local climate zones across Chinese cities. We have successfully estimated the variability of neighborhood heat islands over different local climate zones (LCZs) across Chinese cities based on meteorological measurement data from 2131 stations in year 2016. Measured air temperatures over studied LCZs are found to have strong relations with latitude, altitude, and the distance to coastline. After removing the signal of background mean air temperature, thermal contrasts among various LCZs are found to reduce to less than 1 °C in all seasons. Our results reveal consistent characteristic air temperature regimes of LCZs exist at a continental scale. The warmth of built type LCZs is more evident at night, with an annual mean air temperature difference of 0.51 °C compared to the low plant LCZ. Among the studied LCZs, compact mid-rise neighborhoods have consistently high air temperatures throughout the year. Comparative analysis suggests that open high-rise neighborhoods are preferred over compact mid-rise and low-rise neighborhoods for sustainable city development. Objective 2. Compare the performance of the urban climate model and regression algorithm in predicting air temperature over various local climate zones, and identify the deficiency of current methods in studying neighborhood heat islands. First, we have successfully evaluated the performance of the urban climate model in predicting air temperature over various local climate zones. By using 294 meteorological stations in Beijing, we found systematic biases in current models over low-density urban areas. The temperature biases fall in the range of 0.5–3.0 °C, which suggests that existing models tend to overestimate air temperatures. Inclusion of refined canopy parameters has a limited impact on air temperature simulations. In terms of wind speed simulations, consistent overestimations are found, which can be reduced significantly after incorporating canopy parameters, especially on windy days in winter. The accuracy of wind speed simulations increases with urban fraction and building surface ratio. This indicates poor model performances over low-density urban areas, which requires enhanced aerodynamic parameterizations. Second, we have reviewed 45 articles that use machine learning for urban air temperature prediction between 2011 and 2022. We find that tree-based models fit for spatial prediction and neural network models work for temporal prediction. For spatial prediction, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) varies from 0.10 to 2.60 °C, and there is no clear relationship between RMSE and spatial resolution. Prediction errors of temporal studies tend to increase with the time horizon, with an RMSE of 1.35 ± 0.60 °C (4.02 ± 0.93 °C) for 4-h (5-days) ahead prediction. Based on the review study, we have explored the usage of long short-term memory (LSTM) for urban air temperature prediction. Our work has involved an extensive hyperparameter search with 21,600 trails and evaluated the spatiotemporal performance of LSTM in forecasting air temperature at pedestrian level up to 120-hour ahead, based on data from six urban weather stations in Hong Kong. Two broad categories of data input strategies were assessed, including adding auxiliary timestamp predictors and integrating external decomposition models. Both strategies significantly enhance performance, achieving over 5% reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE) compared to only using Ta series. Findings from our study offer detailed guidance on configuring LSTMs and deepen our understanding of both the capacities and limitations of data-driven air temperature forecasting. Objective 3. Examine the efficiency of different urban meteorological networks in measuring neighborhood heat islands, and find optimal network designs applicable to most cities. We have successfully developed a novel design strategy for urban meteorological networks, whose efficiency in measuring neighborhood heat islands are tested in Beijing and Hong Kong. This design has overcome three major issues in the literature: 1) focusing on summertime and lack of seasonal variation, 2) overlooking meteorological variables other than air temperature, 3) not incorporating the current network into the future design. Utilizing a cluster-based design strategy, we optimize the current network by rearranging sensor locations. For the study period, the sampling error of meteorological variables by the rearranged network is 22.7% smaller in Beijing and 10.7% smaller in Hong Kong than that by the current network. With a sampling ratio of 6.3%, the expanded monitoring network has a mean bias of 0.58 °C (0.44 °C) for representing the air temperature variability across Beijing (Hong Kong). The proposed method is not sensitive to the cluster models, background climate, and resolution of the weather simulation data. The design strategy thus can be applied to other cities for establishing dense urban climate monitoring networks.

16204220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204220.value: We first investigated the thermal contrast of air temperatures over different local climate zones (LCZs) at the continental scale (Journal Paper#1). Based on measurement data from 2131 stations over mainland China, we found that the warmth of built type LCZs is more evident at night. Among the studied LCZs, compact mid-rise neighborhoods have consistently high air temperatures throughout the year. Then we evaluated the performance of urban climate models and machine learning approaches in predicting air temperature over various local climate zones. We found that urban climate models have a bias of 0.5–3.0 °C in predicting 2-m air temperature, and a bias of 0.5 – 6.0 m/s in predicting 10-m wind speed. The consistent bias indicates poor model performances over low-density urban areas, which requires enhanced aerodynamic parameterizations to overcome current model limitations. For machine learning approaches, we found that tree-based models fit for spatial prediction and neural network models work for temporal prediction (Journal Paper#3). The root-mean-square error (RMSE) of spatial prediction varies from 0.10 to 2.60 °C, while RMSE of temporal studies fall in the range of 1.35 ± 0.60 °C for 4-h ahead prediction. With an extensive hyperparameter search with 21,600 trails, we investigated the performance of LSTM in forecasting air temperature at pedestrian level with various data input strategies (Journal Paper#4). We found a RMSE of 2.02 °C for six weather stations in Hong Kong after integrating external decomposition models. Our study offers detailed guidance on configuring LSTMs and deepens our understanding of the capacities and limitations of data-driven air temperature forecasting. Finally, we proposed a cluster-based network design for monitoring urban meteorological variables, and examined its applications in Beijing and Hong Kong (Journal Paper#2). The clustering method separates the city into groups with similar urban climate characteristics, and consequently one sensor is sufficient to collect representative meteorological information for each group. Results show the sampling error of meteorological variables by the new design strategy is 22.7% smaller in Beijing and 10.7% smaller in Hong Kong than that by the current network. Our proposed method is not sensitive to the cluster models, background climate, and resolution of the weather simulation data. All research output is listed in Part C.

16204220.value: The scientific knowledge and modelling techniques obtained from this project have infused new insights into the machine learning applications on urban microclimate and extreme weather forecast. The findings have contributed to the development of a new project that focuses on urban microclimate modelling, which is funded by the excellent young scientist scheme (Hong Kong & Macau) of NSFC. In addition, a young collaboration research fund project focused on urban renewable energy is inspired by this work and is currently under reviewed.

16204220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204220.value: Elevated air temperatures in cities, a phenomenon named urban heat island, has adverse impacts on building energy consumption and public health during hot periods across global cities. However, the spatiotemporal variation of neighbourhood heat island and the capacity of state-of-the-art modelling tool to capture such variation is unclear. This project reveals the seasonal thermal contrast among different urban neighbourhoods at the continental scale with ground-based weather stations. It is found that open high-rise neighbourhoods are preferred for sustainable city development due to its lower temperature. When simulating the neighbourhood heat island, this project shows that physics-based models have relatively poor model performances over low-density urban areas. On the other hand, machine learning approaches are found to have comparable performances with traditional weather simulations that require high computational resources. Cluster-based machine learning algorithm can also be applied to design urban microclimate monitoring network. The sampling error of existing urban sensor network can be reduced by more than 10% with the new strategy. This project reveals the limitation of current urban climate simulations, deepens our understanding of neighbourhood heat island, and provides guidance for future model developments.

16204420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204420.value: 機器人在未來將會廣泛的存在於我們的社會生活中，在家、學校、工作場所等地方和人並肩工作。設計師和工程師無法預先估計並編寫好機器人在各項應用中所需的全部技能，因此需要讓機器人具備學習新技能的能力以應對多變的環境和具體的用戶需求。因為通過示例來展示一項技能比形成公式化的表達要容易，一個自然的將人類知識遷移到機器人身上的方法是讓其根據人類給予的技能演示進行學習。這個過程並不需要演示者具備編程的能力。比如想要教一個機器人如何扛箱子上樓在其面前示範幾遍供其觀察學習就行，不必請機器人公司的專家來幫忙編寫新程序。 雖然有這樣的便利性，目前提出的技能示範學習方法普遍關注於如何模仿還原一個直接的人類技能展示。當新的任務到來時，機器人需要獲取新的示範數據。舉例來說，在傳統的技能示範學習定義中，空手上樓、雙手抬箱子上樓和把箱子扛在肩上上樓是三種完全不同的技能，因此機器人需要用戶分別進行展示。這極大的降低了示範學習在任務空間大小和復雜性增加時的可擴展性。相比之下，人類可以通過先掌握通用知識然後轉化為具體問題下的執行流程來學習多樣化的技能。 本項目目標是根據人類技能學習中的基本原理來提升機器人技能示範學習的可擴展性。基於我們在人和機器人交互研究上的豐富經驗，本項目可分為四個四個相關聯的任務： 1. 通過技能映射表述說明性知識。我們將提出一個框架來增加對元技能的說明性示範可覆蓋的任務場景數量。 2. 根據觀察人類技能分解方法提取說明性知識。我們將對人類如何將一個組合技能分解為元技能進行建模分析，並將得到的知識遷移到機器人。 3. 在用戶參與下指導說明性技能的獲取。我們將設計一個實時交互系統，幫助人類用戶通過特殊的示範技巧輔助機器人更好的觀察學習技能分解。 4. 構建模擬平台以進行實地測試。

16204420.label: Realisation of objectives
16204420.value: Upon the completion of this project, we realized the four key objectives. The research outcomes were demonstrated in two journal articles and eight conference publications. Our progress report explained how we achieved the first two objectives. In particular, we framed skill retargeting as a form of learning from multiple training tasks and applying the acquired skill to a target task (Objective 1, RQ1.1), which led to the development of a meta-learning-based approach. We tested this method in a text game ALFWorld that requires robots to reproduce manipulation and navigation (declarative) skills under textual instructions in a simulated household environment. Our experimental results showed that this method with adaptation may reach marginal improvement of success rate in both seen and unseen testing environments, suggesting that more guidance would be needed in such situations with very sparse rewards. To enable procedural control adaptation (RQ1.2), we further extended our approach to meta-reinforcement learning to train the robots. Through learning-to-explore, the robots are able to gather information about the new environment and subsequently adapt the skills learned from humans in the previous tasks. This method was shown to achieve better generalization in a wide range of skills and scenarios. To meet Objective 2, we first tried to close the perception gap between human teachers and ML researchers (RQ2.1). We employed computational NLP models on textual descriptions to dissect how humans break a complex task plan into solvable subproblems, and we further externalized such knowledge as structured schema (e.g., trees or rule sets). To provide insights into how humans decompose and decontextualize skills (RQ2.2), we compiled the resulting schema into interactive mindmaps and procedural trees for exploration. With the schema, human teachers can easily inspect if the steps within a skill match their mental model. We addressed Object 3 by first answering RQ3.1 through a large-scale literature survey to understand the possible interfaces for humans to label critical information during teaching. The findings were used to inform our design of the human-in-the-loop interactive LfD system. We identified two popular forms of feedback-providing mechanisms: information visualization and conversational user interfaces. The former provides a good overview of the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and Zone of Actual Development (ZAD) of a given skill with details on demand. The latter enables scaffolding in teaching, interactively guiding learners to interpret and acquire the demonstrated steps. To address the last objective, we investigated the performance of our proposed methods and the quality of experience in various simulation platforms that are accessible to the lay public, including but not limited virtual reality simulations, text games, interactive web apps, and real-world tasks with conversational agents. Our quantitative and qualitative results suggested that with our designs, human teachers could better articulate their skills and intelligent agents (robots) could better transfer their acquired knowledge to unseen task instances. We also released relevant project page(s) online for open access.

16204420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204420.value: In the realization of Task 1 (Objective 1), Conference Paper #2 showed that our proposed meta-learning-based approach for robots to learn from multiple training tasks could have marginal improvement of success rate in both seen and unseen testing environments. Conference Paper #1 further extended our approach to meta-reinforcement learning to train the robots through learning-to-explore. As a result, the learned knowledge is no longer applied blindly, and our method is shown to achieve better generalization results in a wide range of skills and scenarios. Furthermore, to improve training data quality, we developed a visual analytical system that combines projection and ranking to identify similarities between observed demonstrations expressed as multi-attribute data (Journal Paper #1). To accomplish Task 2 (Objective 2), we observed how humans perform skill decomposition and then computationally modeled their mental model. Journal Paper #2 and Conference Paper #5 tried to dissect and decontextualize human decisions into unit steps from demonstrations and then formulate them into a modular structure, such as a tree or a rule set, for easy expansion and customization. In our exploration of Task 3, to answer RQ3.1, we carried out a large-scale literature synthesis to review the possible (hybrid) interfaces for humans to annotate information during teaching (Conference Paper #3). To address RQ3.2 and 3.3, we experimented with different feedback-providing mechanisms, including but not limited to visualization (Conference Paper #7) and conversational agent (Conference Paper #6 and #8). In Task 4, we investigated the quality of experience of possible simulation platforms that are accessible to the lay public, including virtual reality (Conference Paper #4), text games (Conference Paper #1 and Conference Paper #2), online communities (Conference Paper #7), crowdsourcing (Conference Paper #5), and real-world tasks (Conference Paper #6). Besides, we have made the experimental site of our gesture demonstration dataset and exploratory interface (https://sunzhida.github.io/Metaphoraction/) open to the research community, to meet our Object 4.

16204420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204420.value: This research can be extended in several directions. 1) Exploring Skill Decomposition with LLMs and VLMs. Besides the meta(-reinforcement) learning frameworks we have studied, we can leverage the abilities of large language models (LLMs) and vision language models (VLMs) to dissect a skill. We can fine-tune the models to align with humans’ mental model of actionable steps obtained from demonstrations and feedback. 2) Enhancing Transparency in Skill Transfer. A robot must realize a skill with respect to its physical capabilities and environmental constraints. We can deliver such information to human teachers in real time and study how humans may adjust their exercise of skills accordingly. 3) Extending to Multimodal Human-AI Collaboration. We can study how other means of communication between humans and robots such as speech and non-verbal cues may support the collaborative learning process, balancing the trade-offs (e.g., informativeness, accuracy, speed, etc.) of different modalities.

16204420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204420.value: Future robots will be commonplace in our society, working alongside humans in homes, schools, and workplaces. One intuitive way to transfer human knowledge to robots to cope with varying environments and specific user demands is through learning from demonstration (LfD). It models a skill from examples rather than formulating it into computer codes. Even laymen who are knowledgeable about a task but do not know how the program can teach a robot through LfD. However, existing LfD methods primarily focus on direct imitation of human actions, impairing the scalability of LfD as the task space and complexity increases. This project aims to address the issue of scaling up robot learning skills through LfD by following the set of basic principles posited in the theory of skill acquisition in human learning. We proposed a meta-learning-based approach for robots to learn from multiple training tasks and apply the acquired skill to a target task and then extended our approach to meta-reinforcement learning to train the robots through learning-to-explore. We designed several methods for human users to elicit their views critically in the process and evaluated the effects of our proposed methods in simulated environments as well as on experimental platforms.

16204520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204520.value: 微型飛行器，尤其是四軸 飛行器 被廣泛應用於勘測，搜救和航拍等多個領域。在這些應用中， 四軸飛行器 需要在復雜的 環境中 快速，準確，安全地飛行 。這要求反饋控制器可以在有限的時間內準確實現所規劃的運動軌跡。否則， 四軸 飛行器 可能會偏離 所 規劃的軌跡甚至墜毀。傳統的軌跡規劃和反饋控制的設計是分開的。因為軌跡規劃不考慮動力學中不確定項和外部 擾動 ，所以無法保證系統可以產生所需的加速度。在某些場景中， 例 如 不確定性被低估或者執行器出現飽和 時 ，實際的加速度 便 不能達到期望 值。因此，傳統 的 系统 策略 無法保證飛行器的控制精度。 本項目旨 在 開發一種可 行 的 技術 該技術可以提高自動 四軸 飛行器 在遇到干擾時的精度和效率。本項目提出建立一 個 同步規劃與執行的系統。該系統包含執行，運動規劃和環境感知 等 模塊。其中，執行部分將設計一種基於可達性的控制器。 與傳統的穩定性控制器不同，所提出的可達性控制器不但能使狀態誤差在有限時間內趨近於零，而且還能有效地估計未知的動力學信息和外界的 擾動 。 為了在給定的 轨迹 幾何和執行器功率約束下 ，實現飛行器的最短飛行時間，本項目提出一種基於梯形加速度的運動規劃策略。 由於所規劃的理想軌跡可以根據執行器的功率和對未知動力學擾動的估計進行在線調 整 所提出的同步規劃與執行 系統 能保證規劃的軌跡是嚴格可執行的。 初步的 模擬 結果顯示 ，當飛行器 在有外部 擾動 的環境中飛行時，同步規劃與執行的 系統 能顯著改善 自動 飛行器的控制精度和效率。 然而，本項目 還 有待進一步的探索。如果所提出的同步規劃與執行系統能經過理論和實驗 的驗證，該系統將有利於改進飛行器在各個應用領域的安全性，效率和精度。

16204520.label: Realisation of objectives
16204520.value: All the four research objectives were achieved in this project. Objective 1 focuses on the development of a minimum time trajectory planning algorithm aimed at achieving aggressive flight maneuvers. This algorithm utilizes a piecewise cubic function to generate time-efficient third-order trajectories, decoupling the coupled maximum thrust into three independent axes. By doing so, each axis can generate trajectories that satisfy arbitrary state constraints, thus ensuring dynamic feasibility. The algorithm was implemented on the STM32 embedded platform, demonstrating an average computing time of less than 150 µs. This computational efficiency makes it suitable for quadrotors with limited onboard computing capability. Furthermore, a strategy called simultaneous planning and execution (SPAE) is proposed to address the challenge of navigating narrow gaps with six degrees of freedom for quadrotor flight. In the SPAE strategy, disturbance estimation is performed online during system execution. The estimated disturbance, combined with the quadrotor's attitude angle and maximum thrust, is used to constrain the trajectory's acceleration. This approach enables the quadrotor to navigate through narrow gaps successfully. The results obtained from implementing the minimum time trajectory planning algorithm and the SPAE strategy have been published in Journal paper No. 1. Objective 2 of the research project focuses on developing reachability control strategies for three different practical systems: quadrotors, unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), and interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs). For quadrotors, a constraint model is introduced to address their underactuation, meaning they have fewer control inputs than the degrees of freedom. The developed reachability control strategy enables quadrotors to achieve precise trajectory tracking even in challenging scenarios with large angles and high speeds. The results of this work have been published in the conference paper (listed in Part C) and a journal version is under review in paper No. 6. To improve the safety of damaged systems experiencing a complete loss of one rotor, an emergency control strategy is proposed. The solution of Euler angles at equilibrium states is analyzed to ensure that control inputs remain within feasible ranges despite disturbances. An attitude control strategy based on reachability is then developed to handle the under-actuation caused by the missing rotor and achieve desired angles. The findings of this research have been published in journal paper No. 3. In the case of underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), a control strategy based on reachability is developed. A novel model transformation is proposed to address the specific underactuation challenges faced by USVs. This transformation simplifies the derivation of trajectory tracking control models for different types of trajectories, such as radius-track, yaw-track, and sway-track, within a newly defined PMPCS (position and motion parameter control system). The results of this research have been published in journal paper No. 4. Furthermore, an approach for calculating reference currents based on the IPMSM model is introduced. This approach aims to simplify computation by utilizing the maximal torque per ampere (MTPA) and maximal torque per voltage (MTPV) points. The proposed method linearly combines the MTPA and MTPV points on the same torque contour with respect to speed, resulting in reduced computational costs. The results of this work have been published in journal paper No. 5. Overall, objective 2 of the research project focuses on developing reachability control strategies for quadrotors, USVs, and IPMSMs. These strategies aim to improve trajectory tracking, handle under-actuation, enhance safety in emergency situations, and simplify computation for efficient control. The findings of this research have been published in conference and journal papers, contributing to the advancement of knowledge in the respective fields. For objective 3, a time delay filter method is developed to enhance the accuracy of the visual-inertial estimator. The proposed approach incorporates a delay compensation strategy based on Taylor expansion to mitigate the impact of noise on the measured signal. This compensation step effectively addresses the inherent time delay within the system and provides an initial estimation of the filtered signal. Based on the output of the time delay compensation, an iterative filter with angular constraint is employed to ensure the smoothness of the filtered result. The filter iteratively refines the estimate based on the previous estimate and the current input, incorporating angular constraint to maintain a smooth trajectory. To prevent potential instability in the iterative filter, boundary constraints are introduced. These constraints are based on the output of the time delay compensation and serve as limits for the filtered result. If the iterative filter output exceeds the boundaries, a mechanism is triggered to bring the result back within the boundaries and continue the filtering process. The results are to be published soon. Objective 4 involves the development of a hardware platform for quadrotors to validate the performance of the proposed SPAE approach. The platform is composed of key components such as a Pixhawk flight controller, four 2212 brushless motors, four 20 A electronic speed controllers (ESC), and four 9015 propellers. In terms of the sensing system, two MPU6000 inertial measurement units (IMUs) are integrated into the Pixhawk to measure acceleration, angles, and angular rate. The quadrotor's altitude is measured using a low-cost HC-SR04 sonar sensor. Additionally, an M8N Global Positioning System (GPS) with decimeter-level accuracy was employed to obtain horizontal position and velocity information. This hardware platform serves as the experimental setup for verifying the performance of the developed SPAE approach. The results obtained from this validation process have been published in papers No. 1, 2, 3.

16204520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204520.value: The emphasis of this project is on trajectory planning, control system design, and filtering design. The major findings and research outcomes can be summarized as follows: The project developed a trajectory planning approach for quadrotors that incorporates disturbances during the planning stage, ensuring feasible trajectories. The approach considers position constraints and inclined angles simultaneously, providing a comprehensive strategy. A computationally efficient algorithm is proposed, minimizing flight time and generating smooth piecewise cubic trajectories in real-time. The algorithm solves thrust allocation and trajectory planning numerically, optimizing memory usage and eliminating the need for storing multiple trajectory profiles. The improved approach allows for arbitrary final velocity and acceleration requirements, enhancing smoothness and flexibility. For a more detailed analysis, please refer to Journal paper No. 1. A reachability-based controller was proposed for quadrotors to achieve position and angular tracking. Performance verification included circular trajectory tracking at 5m/s flight speed and flip tasks. The controller demonstrated the ability to handle disturbances and accurately track the planned position and attitude. The conference paper (listed in Part C) provide additional information. The project also developed an SPAE strategy to address safety concerns in quadrotors, considering the loss of one rotor and disturbances. The strategy includes an emergency controller and an online time adjustment mechanism. The SPAE strategy achieved significant improvements in position tracking error, with two orders of magnitude improvement in the z-axis and a 50% improvement in the y-axis. Actuator saturation was also mitigated. Journal paper No. 3 provides further details on the SPAE strategy. A new model transformation was developed for USVs, allowing for the derivation of radius-track, yaw track, and sway-track control models in a newly defined PMPCS. The proposed trajectory tracking control framework demonstrated steady and precise tracking performance in comparison to conventional controllers. It is also designed to be easily understandable for non-control experts. For more information, refer to Journal paper No. 4. The project introduced an approach for calculating the working point of the torque contour and voltage-limit ellipse in IPMSMs with reduced computational cost. The calculated point, along with the remaining voltage margin, successfully addressed challenges related to parameter inaccuracy, modeling uncertainty, and disturbances. The reachability control method employed in IPMSMs exhibited good transient performance without the need for complex control coefficient design, while meeting torque and speed requirements. For more information, please refer to Journal paper No. 5. A filtering method was developed for the visual-inertial estimator. The proposed filter ensures smoothness, low delay, and accurate trajectory estimation. Comparative evaluations show superior performance compared to existing filters. The proposed filter effectively reduces signal distortion, resulting in smoother and more accurate results. Publication of the results is forthcoming.

16204520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204520.value: The research presented in this project has great potential for further development and exploration in several areas. Here are some potential directions for future research: Safety and Fault-Tolerance: The SPAE strategy developed in this project addresses safety concerns in attitude control of quadrotors. Further research will focus on expanding the strategy to handle position control in additional fault scenarios and disturbances, ensuring the safe operation of quadrotors in real-world applications. Cooperative Control: The integrated framework can facilitate the collaboration and coordination of multiple quadrotors or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in performing complex tasks. Algorithms and protocols can be developed to enable cooperative control, allowing the quadrotors to work together to achieve common objectives, such as formation flying, area coverage, or object manipulation. Sensor Fusion and State Estimation: Incorporating advanced sensor fusion techniques, such as visual-inertial fusion or multi-sensor fusion, can improve the accuracy and reliability of the state estimation process for quadrotors. Investigating the integration of additional sensors, such as LiDAR or radar, can further enhance situational awareness. The proposed course of action involves pursuing these research directions, collaborating with experts in the field, and seeking funding opportunities to support further development and validation of the proposed methods. Additionally, publishing the research findings in relevant conferences and journals will contribute to knowledge dissemination and facilitate knowledge exchange with the wider research community.

16204520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204520.value: The researchers have developed new techniques that make quadrotors smarter and more reliable. These advancements enable quadrotors to better understand their surroundings, plan efficient flight trajectories, accurately estimate their states and unknown disturbance, and execute those flight trajectories effectively. These developments have practical applications in various fields. For instance, in delivery services, quadrotors equipped with improved trajectory planning and execution abilities can navigate around obstacles, reducing the likelihood of accidents and making deliveries more efficient. In search and rescue missions, quadrotors with enhanced flight efficiency can quickly locate individuals in need of help or maneuver through confined spaces. The research also has broader implications for the field of robotics. By integrating controllers and planning components, the researchers are paving the way for more advanced robots that can interact effectively in unknown environments. This has potential applications in industrial automation, high-precision manufacturing, and even space exploration. Overall, this research project brings us closer to a future where robots can operate autonomously and intelligently. By improving their decision-making, estimation, and execution abilities, these technologies have the potential to make our lives easier, safer, and more efficient.

16204720.value: 在過去的十年中，我們目睹了機器學習在越來越多的現實應用中發揮核心作用。隨著通用機器學習軟件工具的普及，這趨勢持續增長。當機器學習接觸到對它沒太多經驗的普通用戶時，一個常見的誤解是，人們只需要為眼前的問題收集原始數據，機器學習算法將自動處理其餘的問題。事實是，在許多實際應用中，機器學習的流程中多達90％的時間仍然是手動完成的，且通常是單調乏味的。具體來說，數據收集和預處理仍遠未實現自動化。 此項目旨在自動化數據收集和預處理中的一重要組件，稱為數據擴充。該組件通過生成新的訓練示例來擴展原始數據集，以便在以擴充了的數據來訓練模型時可以提高模型的準確性。我們稱此問題為自動數據擴充（AutoDA），到目前為止，它是一種很少被研究的自動機器學習（AutoML）問題。我們相信，研究AutoDA將在幫助使機器學習技術民主化方面發揮重要作用。 在這個項目中，我們旨在通過研究四個主要的研究主題來推進最新技術。我們將首先嘗試通過探索可直接生成合成數據的生成模型的使用，並考慮結合兩種數據擴充方法，來改進主要為圖像數據設計的現有AutoDA算法。接下來，我們將使用貝葉斯優化方法，通過為AutoDA設計搜索算法來進一步提高性能，該算法有望勝過基於強化學習和進化算法的現有方法。此外，我們將考慮將這些AutoDA方法擴展到圖像數據之外，以用於與圖像數據有一些主要差異的文本數據。最後，為了使我們用於多模式數據的AutoDA工具能夠使其他機器學習研究人員和從業人員以及更多的普通用戶受益，我們計劃使其首先公開在GitHub上，然後作為基於雲端服務公開提供，可無縫地用於流行的機器學習平台，例如scikit-learn、TensorFlow和PyTorch。我們還將與半導體和電子行業的領先集成解決方案提供商合作，評估我們的AutoDA工具。

16204720.label: Realisation of objectives
16204720.value: We have achieved all four project objectives that we set out to achieve as stated in the project proposal. In what follows, some highlights will be listed to summarize the major achievements in accordance with the objectives: • For the first time in the machine learning research community, a comprehensive framework for categorizing different automated data augmentation methods (including both existing and potentially possible ones) was proposed by us (Cheung and Yeung, TNNLS 2024). • Based on our framework, we proposed methods for all three categories of automated data augmentation. Among these methods, we proposed a generative model that can learn to augment data adaptively under challenging scenarios with highly imbalanced data distributions that often occur in practical applications. • We formulated optimization problems to learn data augmentation policies that can adapt to specific classes or even instances (Cheung and Yeung, ICLR 2022). The resulting method outperforms previous methods based on reinforcement learning, evolutionary and other algorithms significantly in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. • In order to develop automated data augmentation methods for modalities beyond image data, we proposed a novel modality-agnostic method that works in the latent space to which data of various modalities can be mapped, including text, tabular, time-series, and image data modalities (Cheung and Yeung, ICLR 2021). • For all the published papers with research software implementations, we have made them publicly available on cloud-based platforms such as GitHub to facilitate others to pursue further research. • As of April 2025, the research publications resulted from this project have been cited more than 150 times. Some of them also show an increasing trend.

16204720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204720.value: As summarized in Section 5.3 above, we have demonstrated through extensive empirical studies that integrating ideas from multiple approaches to automated data augmentation helps. In particular, we found that the generative model proposed by us has appealing properties that are not possessed by other approaches. Moreover, we have succeeded in extending beyond the image data modality in a comprehensive way to handle a wide range of data modalities through performing data augmentation in the latent space. During the second half of the project period, we also attempted to go beyond the usual classification problems that most of the existing automated data augmentation methods aim to help. One of them is related to the role of data augmentation in the context of adversarial attacks (Yan et al., ICLR 2023; Wu et al., ICASSP 2024). Another direction is more about evaluating the performance and robustness of several natural language processing tasks, which involve text-based data augmentation (Zhao et al., ACL 2023; Wu et al., EMNLP 2023).

16204720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204720.value: Automated data augmentation was a popular research topic a few years back at the time when the proposal for this project was written. Early works were done and published by leading research groups such as that from Google Research. However, in the last few years, the ground-breaking advancements made by large language models, such as ChatGPT, seem to give people the impression that massive datasets are available to train very large models, undermining the need for (automated) data augmentation. Nevertheless, it should be noted that almost all large language models in use today are pre-trained in a self-supervised (i.e., unsupervised) manner without using labeled datasets. For applications in which labeled datasets are necessary for model training, having massive unlabeled datasets alone does not help. Moreover, imbalanced class distributions are often encountered in many real-world applications. One challenge is the scarcity of labeled data for the long-tailed minority classes. Moreover, for some application domains such as healthcare, a major ethical concern is data privacy. Data augmentation methods capable of generating synthetic data that appear realistic can be used instead for model training to alleviate the data privacy concerns. As such, we anticipate that further development of this direction of research can focus on scenarios such as these that can benefit more from automated data augmentation techniques.

16204720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204720.value: Data-centric machine learning methods that play a central role in many of today’s artificial intelligence systems rely heavily on high-quality and often massive datasets for model training. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the data privacy concerns in some application domains, among other challenges, make it necessary to develop data augmentation techniques to generate synthetic data that mimic real data. Automated data augmentation aims to automate this augmentation process by learning how to augment data optimally based on various practical scenarios. This project has led to new methods for automated data augmentation based on different approaches that are complementary to each other. In addition, they can be applied to a wider range of data modalities beyond image data that most existing automated data augmentation methods focus exclusively on. The software implementations of our new methods have been made publicly available to facilitate further development.

16204820.label: Project Objectives
16204820.value: RF sensing capability has added more of a burden to the over-crowded RF environment, as the number of smart devices in smart homes increasing. To ease RF spectral congestion, in this project we would like to investigate whether we can develop a joint RF sensing and communication design to improve spectrum efficiency. Explore two directions to address the joint RF sensing and communication design. Specifically, we will first try to empower a customized RF sensing device with a data communication capability. We will also try to enhance the sensing capability of the existing communication signals, e.g., Wi-Fi (i.e., IEEE 802.11). To verify the feasibility of whether a traditional RF sensing device (i.e., RF radar) can have a communication capability. We will design dual-function signals for the radar, which will not only preserve the sensing capability but will also carry information that can be decoded by legacy devices. We will also design the receiving chain for the radar so that it can understand reflected signals from objects and decode uplink transmissions simultaneously. To implement the dual-function radar using signal helpers/software-defined radios and demonstrate that it can communicate with legacy devices in a bi-directional way. We will evaluate the performance of the proposed implementation from three aspects: downlink transmission, uplink transmission, and sensing accuracy. We want to demonstrate that we can achieve home-level coverage while preserving the sensing resolution of the RF radar. To analyze the sensing capability of existing pilot patterns in Wi-Fi signals. Align the direction, to explore the potential of pilot subcarriers to enhance the sensing capability of Wi-Fi signals. We will further design pilot patterns/waveforms that can enhance the sensing capability of Wi-Fi signals without degrading its communication performance. To build a prototype system to demonstrate that our design can serve both the sensing and communication aspects well.

16204820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204820.value: Smart home technologies could significantly support people and allow them to have a better life quality. With the recent advances in technologies, smart homes are becoming a reality. In 2019, the household penetration rate in the smart home market is 16.4%, and it is estimated that this will rise to 30.9% by 2023. It is essential for a smart home to understand its residents by monitoring their behaviours and providing personalized healthcare services. Radio frequency (RF)-based sensing, due to its contactless nature, is a promising approach. Researchers have demonstrated that using the RF radio signals that bounce off people’s bodies can enable behavioural sensing at home. Researchers have demonstrated the great potential of RF sensing in smart homes, including understanding the residents’ gesture commands and monitoring the residents’ vital signs, including but not limited to heart rate, breathing rate, gait patterns, and sleep cycles and quality. Compared with other approaches, RF sensing is totally unobtrusive, requires no on-body instrumentation, and can even work in non-line-of-sight scenarios. In other words, radio signals – traditionally used for data communication – are now emerging as sensing media. Although RF sensing has appealing properties, since radio waves are transmitted from time to time for sensing purposes, it brings congestion to wireless networks. To make the situation worse, there is an unprecedented amount of wireless traffic in smart homes, as there are numerous intelligent devices that exchange data and control messages through the air. In this project, we will investigate the joint design of sensing and communication systems to alleviate the strain on wireless resources. Instead of designing sensing and communication systems as separate objectives, we will address them jointly. In this project, we plan to address this issue from two directions. The first is to empower the traditional sensing device with communication capability, so that the sensing device will become a dual-function apparatus. The second is to enhance the sensing capability of existing signals by redesigning the packet format so that the current communication infrastructure can also act as a sensing device. We will evaluate our design through prototype implementation and extensive simulations to demonstrate the effectiveness of the design. The proposed project will enable the sensing and communication system to work harmoniously in smart homes, providing both unobtrusive sensing and ubiquitous connectivity. 16204920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204920.value: Clustering is a fundamental topic in unsupervised learning. Its objective is to group objects into clusters such that objects in the same cluster are in some sense more similar to each other than to those in other clusters. Clustering is used in many fields such as biology, medicine, business, social sciences, and computer science (pattern recognition, image analysis, information retrieval, etc.). Well-known clustering algorithms include K-means and Gaussian mixture models. Traditional clustering algorithms do not perform well on high-dimensional data. One reason is that points in high dimensional spaces are essentially equidistant from each other. In the past, this difficulty was tackled using feature transformation such as principal component analysis and kernel methods. Recently, deep learning methods have become popular. The idea is to first map high-dimensional data points to a low-dimensional feature space using a neural network and then conduct clustering in the feature space. For deep clustering to be effective, the feature transformation must preserve the key distributional and geometric characteristics of the data, and the data distribution in the feature space must be clustering-friendly. Several frameworks for deep clustering have been proposed. Clustering algorithms such as K-means and Gaussian mixture models are unidimensional in the sense that they yield one partition of data. However, complex data often have multiple natural facets and can be meaningfully clustered in more than one way. For example, students in a high school can be clustered in terms of (1) academic performance based on their scores in various subjects, and (2) personality based on their social behaviours. Therefore, there is a need to consider multidimensional clustering, which refers to the task of finding multiple meaningful ways to partition data. In the past decade, we have developed several algorithms for multidimensional clustering, and have used them to, among others, identify patient clusters with various symptom patterns, customer clusters with various tastes, and document clusters with various word patterns. In this project, we plan to develop deep learning algorithms for multidimensional clustering in several deep clustering frameworks, and evaluate/compare them on benchmark text and image datasets. The work is meaningful because it can benefit data organization, data labelling, and information retrieval. In addition, it expands the realm of deep learning to cover a new and interesting types of problems.We also plan to set up a platform to facilitate further research on deep multidimensional clustering, which will include benchmark datasets, pre-processing routines, evaluation protocols, and baselines. 深度学习在图像分类方面的能力已经达到了人类水平。本项目研究深度聚类分析，目的是开发出与人类类似能从多个维度对图像进行聚类的算法。 在本项目以前，已有学者提出多种用于聚类的深度学习算法，其主要思想是首先使用神经网络来将高维数据映射到低维特征空间，然后在特征空间中进行聚类分析。但是，以往所有的深度聚类算法都是单维的，它们综合考虑所有特征，从整体角度对数据做一种划分。 但是，复杂的数据通常具有多个侧面，可以从多角度进行有意义的聚类。例如，高中生群体即可以按照各科成绩进行聚类，也可以基于人际交往能力进行聚类。 如果把单维聚类与单标签分类对应，那么多维聚类就对应多标签分类。本项目研究多维深度聚类，从无标签数据出发，构造和确定出一些意义明显的特征子集，并且基于每个特征子集对数据进行聚类，从而获得多种划分。

16204920.label: Realisation of objectives
16204920.value: The first objective of the project is to develop deep learning algorithms for multidimensional clustering within various deep clustering frameworks and evaluate/compare them on benchmark text and image datasets. Here is a summary of our work on text clustering: In Conference Paper #1, we cluster sentences of different styles in the latent space (Figure 4) and use the results to improve text style transfer. In Conference Paper #2, we employ a reverse-order language model to form tight clusters of rhyming sentences in the latent space (Figure 4), facilitating better rap generation. In Zhao et al. Conference Paper #3, we introduce a memory module to cluster support-set examples in meta-learning (Figure 1), alleviating the memorization overfitting problem. In Conference Paper #8, we address the problem of generating clusters of herbs (prescriptions) for symptom descriptions. Here is a summary of our work on image clustering: In Conference Paper #4, we create a hierarchical clustering of image labels (Figure 5) and use it for a two-stage contrastive explanation of image classification. In Xie et al. Conference Paper #5, we cluster ViT masks (Section 3.2) and use the clusters in a causal explanation of vision transformers. In Gao et al. Conference Paper #6 and in Conference Paper #7 we study methods to extract core features from images, implicitly clustering semantically similar content, and use these features to build classifiers with better cross-domain generalization. The first authors of all these papers are the PI’s PhD students. The second objective of the project is to establish a platform for deep multidimensional clustering research, including benchmark datasets, preprocessing routines, evaluation protocols, and baselines. For this purpose, we have set up a GitHub repository: https://github.com/XingzhiZhou/DMC.

16204920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204920.value: Our research has achieved significant progress in deep multidimensional clustering, with key contributions in both text and image domains, as well as the development of essential research infrastructure. In text clustering, we successfully developed deep learning approaches that cluster sentences by style to enhance text style transfer, formed tight latent space clusters of rhyming sentences to improve rap generation, and introduced memory-based clustering of support-set examples to address memorization overfitting in meta-learning. Additionally, we pioneered methods for clustering herbal prescriptions based on symptom descriptions, demonstrating practical applications in traditional medicine. For image clustering, our work established hierarchical clustering of image labels to enable explainable classification, developed ViT mask clustering techniques for causal interpretation of vision transformers, and introduced core feature extraction methods that implicitly group semantically similar images while improving cross-domain generalization in classifier performance. Beyond algorithmic advances, we created an open research platform for deep multidimensional clustering, providing standardized datasets, preprocessing tools, evaluation protocols, and baseline implementations to support future work in this field. These outcomes, published in premier venues including NeurIPS, IJCAI, ACL and UAI, represent both theoretical advances and practical solutions with applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare domains.

16204920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204920.value: This research lays the groundwork for several promising directions: (1) Expanding applications to video and multimodal data (combining text, images, and audio), (2) Adapting the methods for real-world domains like personalized education and precision medicine, and (3) Enhancing interpretability to make the clustering results more actionable for end-users. The proposed course of action involves collaborating with domain experts to refine applications and optimizing computational efficiency for large-scale deployment. Near-term focus will be on healthcare applications, leveraging the herb clustering work as a starting point.

16204920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204920.value: Our research focused on teaching AI systems to automatically organize information by finding natural patterns in data. For text applications, we developed methods that group sentences by their writing style to improve tools that rewrite or translate text, discovered ways to structure rap lyrics so they rhyme more effectively, and created systems that analyze medical texts to connect symptoms with relevant herbal treatments. On the image side, we built techniques that help computers sort image into more meaningful categories while explaining their decisions in understandable ways, uncovered how AI vision systems actually process what they see, and improved their ability to focus on the most important elements of pictures so they perform better across different situations. Essentially, our work helps computers make better sense of language and visual information, with applications ranging from creative arts to healthcare.

16205420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205420.value: Suppose that a data analyst writes the following query, possibly in SQL, against a database at of e-commerce website: find the top-10 best-selling products, where the buyer and seller are from the same city and the rating of the seller is at least 4. This is a typical analytical query, featured in many industrial benchmarks, and it can be evaluated efficiently using mature techniques by most database systems. Next, suppose that the database is not static, but undergoes a series of updates. For example, new orders will be continuously added, old orders expire (assuming the query is only interested in recent orders), the rating of a seller may fluctuate over time, and buyers/sellers may relocate to a different city. When these updates are received by the database, the query results must also be refreshed in time. This is commonly known as the problem of "query answering under updates" or "incremental view maintenance" in the literature. However, in spite of many years of research, existing solutions for this problem are far from satisfactory. In fact, strong negative results are known showing that recomputing the query from scratch after each update is basically the best one can do, at least theoretically, except for some very restricted query types (the example query above is definitely not one of them). In view of these negative results, in practice people can only settle for heuristics without any guarantees. These heuristics may perform very badly under certain update sequences. In this project, we explore what the power of approximation can do for this difficult problem. On the one hand, most analytical queries report aggregates (such as the example query above), where 100% accuracy is not always required. This is particularly the case when the database is under high volumes of updates: by the time the query results are refreshed using an exact but slow method, new data may have already arrived, rendering the "accurate" results inaccurate anyway. On the other hand, allowing approximation has proved to be extremely helpful for a variety of hard computational problems in lowering their complexity. We believe this problem also falls into this category, and we will try to explore how much efficiency we can obtain by allowing small errors in the query results. 假设一个数据分析师对电子商务网站的数据库写了以下SQL查询：找到前10名最畅销的产品，其中买家和卖家来自同一个城市，且卖家的评分至少是4分。 这是一个典型的在许多工业基准中都有的分析式查询，而大多数数据库系统可以使用成熟的技术对其进行有效执行。现在假设数据库不是静态的，而是不断被更新。例如，新的订单会不断增加，旧的订单会过期（假设查询只对最近的订单感兴趣），卖家的评级可能会随着时间的推移而波动，买家/卖家可能会搬迁到不同的城市。当数据库接收到这些更新时，查询结果也必须及时刷新。这就是文献中通常所说的 "更新下的查询应答 "或 "增量视图维护 "问题。然而，尽管经过多年的研究，现有的解决该问题的方案还远远不能令人满意。事实上，已知的理论负面结果表明，每次更新后从头开始重新计算查询基本上是最好的办法。鉴于这些负面的结果，在实践中人们只能满足于没有任何保证的启发式方法，而这些启发式方法在某些更新序列下可能表现得非常糟糕。 在这个项目中，我们将探索如果允许近似结果的话，这个困难的问题有无更好解法。一方面，大多数分析性查询报告的都是汇总结果（比如上面的例子），在这种情况下，并不总是要求100%的准确性。当数据库处于大量更新的情况下，情况尤其如此：当使用精确但缓慢的方法刷新查询结果时，新的数据可能已经到达，使得 "精确 "的结果无论如何都不准确。另一方面，大量事实证明，允许近似结果对于各种难于计算的问题都有极大的帮助，降低其复杂度。我们认为这个问题也属于这个类别，将尝试探索通过降低精度而大大提升查询效率。

16205420.label: Realisation of objectives
16205420.value: In this project, we have successfully realized the original objectives of designing and evaluating efficient algorithms for approximate query evaluation under updates: 1. We have designed efficient algorithms for approximate query evaluation under updates specifically tailored for counting queries. These algorithms provide robust theoretical guarantees on both the approximation error and the update costs. Our approach ensures that the solutions are not only theoretically sound but also practical for dynamic data environments. The foundational work on exact query evaluation paved the way for these advancements, with detailed theoretical analysis and initial implementations published in paper [2]. Building on this, we developed optimized reservoir sampling algorithms that achieve theoretical optimality in running time while delivering approximate answers to counting queries, with results detailed in paper [3]. 2. We have extended these algorithms to effectively handle group-by queries. This extension broadens the applicability of our solutions to a wider range of SQL queries, including those with joins, selections, and group-by aggregations, supporting various aggregation functions such as counting, sum, average, and max/min. The theoretical properties of these algorithms have been thoroughly analyzed, ensuring efficient performance under updates. These developments, including their adaptation to multi-party settings, have been documented in papers [3] and [5]. 3. We have implemented the designed algorithms and conducted comprehensive experimental studies to investigate their practical performance. These studies utilized both benchmark and real-world datasets to validate the algorithms' effectiveness. Our system prototypes, built on the Flink distributed streaming processing engine, demonstrate significant performance improvements over exact methods. Additionally, we extended our work to differentially private query processing for private data and streaming contexts, implementing the DP-SQL prototype to support diverse SQL queries under differential privacy. The practical performance of these implementations has been rigorously evaluated, with findings published in papers [1], [3], and [4]. These realized objectives collectively advance the field of approximate query evaluation, offering efficient, theoretically grounded, and practically validated solutions for dynamic and privacy-sensitive data processing scenarios. Justification for overspending the conference budget by $47,000: Due to COVID, many conferences were suspended, canceled, or transitioned to online formats. As a result, we spent more on Conferences in this project as the PI and the students attended more conferences to make up the lost interaction with researchers globally.

16205420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205420.value: In this project, we aim at designing efficient algorithms for approximate query evaluation under updates, study their theoretical properties, and build system prototypes to evaluate their practical performance. Towards this goal, we have achieved the following outcomes: 1. We have first studied the problem of how to evaluate queries exactly under updates. We have successfully designed efficient algorithms that can handle a variety of SQL queries that are composed of relational operators including joins, selections, and group-by aggregations, where the aggregation function can be counting, sum, average, or max/min. We have analyzed the running times of these algorithms theoretically, and also implemented them in a system prototype based on Flink, a widely used distributed streaming processing engine. These results have been published in paper [2]. 2. We observe that the performance of these exact algorithms are not satisfactory enough. Thus, we have further studied if some approximation can further improve the performance. In particular, we have designed efficient reservoir sampling algorithms over SQL queries. The reservoir sample can thus be used to answer various analytical queries approximately. We have shown that the sampling algorithm's running time achieves theoretical optimality, and also evaluated their practical performance over many real and benchmark datasets. These results have been published in paper [3]. We have further extended these algorithm to the multi-party setting, and the results have been published in paper [5]. 3. Finally, we have extended our approximate query processing algorithms to analyzing private data, using the well established privacy standard of differential privacy. We have shown that our algorithms achieve a strong instance-optimality in terms of utility. We have also built a prototype system DP-SQL to support a variety of SQL queries under differential privacy. These results have been published in paper [1]. Furthermore, we have extended these algorithms to streaming data to provide differentially private query answers under the continual observation setting. The paper has been published as [4].

Complex Queries: Extend algorithms to nested, recursive, or spatio-temporal queries for broader applications (e.g., GIS, graph data). Adapt sampling and test on specialized datasets. 2. Hardware Optimization: Leverage GPUs or serverless systems to boost performance for large-scale streaming. Refactor algorithms and compare across setups. 3. Industry Deployment: Apply algorithms to real-time use cases like fraud detection. Partner with industry to build production systems and test with live feeds.

16205420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205420.value: This research project is about making databases faster and smarter when handling constantly changing information, like social media updates or sales data. Normally, databases take time to give exact answers to questions (queries), but we’ve created quick methods that give close-enough answers instead. These methods work for common tasks like counting, grouping, or averaging data, even when it’s private or streaming in real-time. Why does this matter? In today’s world, businesses and scientists need fast answers from huge, shifting datasets --- think spotting trends on Twitter or protecting health records. Our work cuts the wait time, saves computing power, and keeps private info safe using a privacy trick called differential privacy. We’ve tested these ideas on real and standard datasets, proving they work well in practice, not just on paper. The value? It’s like upgrading from a slow calculator to a speedy app—cheaper, faster, and secure. This could help companies make quicker decisions, researchers analyze data on the fly, and even keep your personal info safer online. Plus, we’ve built working prototypes to show it’s ready for the real world.

16206020.label: Project Objectives
16206020.value: To develop and study solid-state lithium-ion electrolytes with giant ionic Seebeck effects (S > 2 mV/K) and high ionic conductivity (>10^-5 S/cm). We will start with PVDF-HFP based polymer electrolytes and experimentally investigate the effects of various factors, including the ion concentration, different types of anions, polymer hosts, ion transfer number, inorganic nanofillers, and temperature, on the ionic Seebeck coefficient, ionic conductivity and thermal conductivity. These systematic investigations will guide the development and optimization of solid polymer electrolytes for ionic thermoelectric applications. Unlike ionic thermoelectric phenomena in liquid electrolyte, the understanding of ionic thermoelectric behaviors in solids is still in the infancy stage due to different ion transport mechanisms. Through comparative study, we will reveal whether the fundamentally different ion transport mechanisms in solids can result in different ionic thermoelectric behaviors from those in liquids. The experimental results will be used to develop the correlations between ionic thermoelectric effects in solid-state electrolytes and the ion transport behaviors in the electrolytes. To develop and characterize an efficient phonon-polariton-enhanced absorber that has strong selective absorption within 8-13 microns. The absorber will be fabricated using a facile solution process near room temperature and SiO2 nanoparticles will be used to improve the absorption. We will adopt the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method to understand and utilize the coupling between the PHPS-induced SiONx film and SiO2 nanoparticles to optimize the design. The absorption spectrum of the optimized absorber structures will be characterized using the Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). To develop a comprehensive theoretical model that can predict the behaviors of thermal radiation sensors based on the ionic thermoelectric effects in solid polymer electrolytes. The sensor performance is influenced by many factors except the ionic thermoelectric properties of the electrolyte. The effects of various factors such as the geometry of thermoelectric pillars, electrolyte/electrode contact resistance, absorber area and the heat loss caused by the ambient air will be explored using numerical simulation and theoretical modeling. The developed model can be used to predict the responsivity, response time and signal-to-noise ratio of ionic thermoelectric sensors based on solid electrolytes and provide the guidelines for the design and optimization of these novel sensors. Finite element simulations will also be used to simulate the sensor performance and the results will be used to improve the theoretical model. With the developed model, an optimized design will be developed.

16206020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206020.value: Thermal radiation sensing is a key component for many applications including green building, gas detection, and environment monitoring. Inexpensive solutions of low power and high performance are thus in high demand in numerous fields. Among various thermal radiation detection techniques, thermoelectric (TE) sensors can operate over a broad spectrum without current input or active temperature control, thus offering low cost, high stability, compact structure and low power consumption. However, the wide applications of thermoelectric sensors are hindered by their low responsivities and low spatial and temporal resolutions, which are mainly due to unsatisfactory thermoelectric material properties and large device sizes. To overcome these issues, we propose to develop a low-cost high-performance thermal radiation sensor based on the giant ionic thermoelectric effects in solid-state polymer electrolytes and the corresponding polymer-compatible absorber. We will first explore the ionic Seebeck effects in solid-state polymer electrolyte and investigate the effects of various factors on the ionic thermoelectric behaviors. The knowledge attained will be used to develop a solid-state polymer electrolyte with a giant Seebeck coefficient. We will then integrate the solid-state electrolyte into a novel single pillar design, which can significantly improve the responsivity while minimizing the device size and response time relative to the conventional planar structure. Meanwhile, we will develop an efficient phonon-polariton-enhanced absorber that has strong selective absorption within 8-13 microns and can be fabricated using a facile solution process near room temperature to provide compatibility with the polymer sensing unit. Preliminary analysis shows that the proposed design could achieve both a high responsivity (up to ~ 1000V/W) and fast thermal response (<10 ms), which makes it very competitive in thermal radiation detection. It is expected that this new design will find many potential applications in areas that require low-cost thermal radiation or temperature sensing, such as thermal imaging, night vision and bio-sensing. 熱輻射傳感在綠色建築，氣體檢測和環境監控等諸多應用至為關鍵。各個領域都急需低成本，低功耗和高性能的熱輻射傳感解決方案。在各種熱輻射傳感技術中，熱電感測器無需電流輸入或者主動溫度控制就能在寬頻譜上運作，從而具備尺寸小，低成本，高穩定性和低能耗等特點。但是，由於熱電材料的熱電性能不足以及較大的器件尺寸， 熱點感測器的回應率較低，空間和時間解析度不高，這些缺點限制了熱電感測器的廣泛應用。為解決這些問題，我們提出基於固態樹脂電解質中的巨離子熱電效應以及相容的吸收層來發展一種低成本高性能的熱輻射感測器。我們將首先探究固態樹脂電解質中的離子熱電效應，研究各種因素對離子熱電效應的影響。所得到的知識將用來發展一種具有巨離子熱電效應的固態電解質。我們將採用一種新穎的單柱設計來集成該固態電解質，該設計可以在降低器件尺寸和回應時間的同時顯著提升回應率。同時，我們將發展一種有效的通過聲子極化選擇性增強8-13微米吸收率的吸收層，該吸收層將通過室溫附近的簡捷溶液法來製造以與傳感單元相容。初步分析表明該設計可以同時實現高的回應率（高達~ 1000V/W）和低熱回應時間（<10 ms）, 從而在紅外傳感方面具備很強的競爭力。這種新設計有望在需要低成本熱輻射或者溫度傳感的領域得到應用，例如紅外熱成像，夜視，以及生物檢測。

16206020.label: Realisation of objectives
16206020.value: Mr. Gongze Liu and Miss Sijing Liu were admitted as PhD students to work on the project. Dr. Cheng Chi was also involved in the infrared sensor materials fabrication and characterization as a postdoc and he left HKUST in September 2021.Thereafter, Mr. Gongze Liu and Miss Sijing Liu continued to work on the project. Miss Sijing Liu received her PhD degree at HKUST in August 2023. During the reporting period, we built the platform for the characterization of ionic thermoelectric materials and developed both flexible p- and n-type ionic thermoelectric materials with giant thermopowers (S=17 and -4 mV/K, respectively) and high ionic conductivity (>4 mS/cm). We also further endowed the materials with superior mechanical properties, such as stretchability. We focused on the numerical simulation of infrared sensors based on ionic thermoelectric materials, the fabrication process of the designed microsensors as well as the characterization of the fabricated device. An efficient phonon-polariton-enhanced absorber is developed during the reporting period. The main function of the absorption layer is to absorb the infrared radiation from the target being detected. The preparation of the absorption layer is carried out using a solution method, where silica nanoparticles with ST3 are selected as the absorbing material due to their strong absorption capabilities in the 8–14-micron infrared region. By dispersing silica nanoparticles into the ST3 solution, it is possible to reduce the thickness of the absorption layer while maintaining the same absorption rate. The absorption layer is applied using an ultrasonic nozzle at a frequency of 45 kHz to achieve optimized thickness and concentration. ST3 belongs to polysilazane, where silicon and nitrogen atoms are alternately arranged to form the basic backbone. It is liquid at room temperature and reacts with oxygen and moisture to form a layer of SiO2. The absorbance of the ST3 film was measured using a Fourier transform infrared spectrometer (FTIR). ST3 films containing silica nanoparticles exhibit good selectivity, with low absorbance in the 4-to-8-micron and 13-to-16-micron ranges, and higher absorbance in the 8-to-13-micron range. This high absorbance and selectivity make it an ideal material for the absorption layer of an ion thermoelectric sensor. The fabrication flow process for ionic-thermoelectric-based sensors was developed. Process recipes for each step were tested. Two key steps are filling ionic thermoelectric materials, and the top metal connection, which determines the yield of the device. Most of the i-TE materials behave like liquids or gels, the materials are soft and make it a great challenge to precisely control the shape and size of the sensing units. An SU-8 template is introduced to precisely control the sensor unit size. Based on the optimized design, we successfully fabricated sensors with i-TE materials of diameters ranging from 50 microns to 1000 microns. According to the international standards for infrared sensor characterization, we have developed an infrared measurement platform, which comprises a blackbody radiation source, a vacuum chamber, an optical chopper, and a set of data acquisition systems. This platform was calibrated using commercial infrared sensors and can be used to characterize the responsivity, internal resistance, and response time of an infrared sensor. The other parameters could then be calculated based on these two measured parameters. With the optimized device design and absorber structure, the first ionic thermoelectric infrared sensor is developed. The efficient phonon-polariton-enhanced absorber is applied to achieve good selectivity. An SU-8 template is introduced to solve the fabrication issues in i-TE materials. Laser and blackbody radiation measurements were conducted to characterize the performance of the fabricated TE infrared sensors. The measured performance of devices with 10-micron thick sensors is very close to the theoretical prediction, with a responsivity reaching 42V/W and a response time of around 300ms. Increased sensor thickness could enhance responsivity to 1000V/W, and a single-pixel infrared sensor could generate an mV level signal under a 100℃ black body, while the response time increased to several seconds.

16206020.value: High-performance low-power uncooled infrared sensors are widely demanded in many emerging markets including smartphones, automobiles, gas sensing, and monitoring systems. Compared to traditional bolometers, uncooled thermoelectric sensors are the most suitable solution for low-power applications due to their passive nature, high stability, high dynamic range and low cost. However, their low responsivity, slow response, and large size hinder the wide applications of thermoelectric sensors. In this project, we developed ionic thermoelectric(i-TE) materials, The thermopower of p- and n-type ionic thermoelectric materials could reach +17 mV K-1 and-4 mV K-1 respectively which is about 100 times the value of conventional semiconductor-based thermoelectric materials. We developed the infrared sensor based on ionic thermoelectric materials together with the fabrication process for i-TE materials. Compared with the commercial infrared sensor, the i-TE materials could enhance the responsivity of infrared sensors and show great potential for those applications requiring low power consumption and low cost.
