16206220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206220.value: Multidimensional partitioning is the task of dividing some input multidimensional space into regions, called buckets. It is a well-studied problem within a variety of applications in databases and computer vision. Existing techniques partition the space or the data in a predetermined way, with the objective of optimizing measures such as load balancing (i.e., each bucket should have the same number of objects), bucket area, data uniformity within buckets etc. On the other hand, multidimensional partitioning can be viewed as a type of pattern discovery, since intuitively, buckets constitute groups of neighboring objects that have some desirable properties. Machine learning (ML) techniques are very successful at identifying patterns, and have become increasingly important due to the exponential increase of data from various sources such as mobile devices and sensors. In the proposed project, we will investigate the application of ML techniques for the partitioning of spatial and multidimensional data. Specifically, we plan to utilize artificial neural networks and reinforcement learning. For the first approach, we will train a deep neural network to mimic a combination of existing partitioning algorithms, with the aim of outperforming each individual method. For reinforcement learning, we will focus on deep Q-learning, in which operations (e.g., bucket splits) are performed according to some reward, or punishment, that depends on the measures of choice. We expect ML techniques to yield substantial benefits both in solution quality and efficiency, compared to conventional algorithms. Finally, we intend to extend our methods to related problems, including dynamic partitioning for moving object databases, and geosocial partitioning, which should also take into account the social connections. 多維分區是將輸入的多維空間劃分為區域(稱為存儲桶)的任務。 在數據庫和計算機視覺的各種應用中，這是一個被廣泛研究的問題。 多維分區的目標是對數據存儲進行優化，現有技術以預先確定的方式對空間或數據進行分區，如負載平衡(每個存儲桶內具有相同數量的對象)、存儲桶大小一致、存儲桶內數據量一致等。 另一方面，多維分區可以看作是模式發現的一種類型，因為直觀上，存儲桶構成了具有某些特殊屬性的鄰近對象的組合。 機器學習(ML)技術在模式識別方面非常成功。 而由於多種來源(如行動裝置和感測器)的數據呈指數級增長，機器學習正變得越來越重要。 在本擬議計劃中，我們將研究機器學習技術在空間和多維數據分區中的應用。 具體來說，我們計劃利用人工神經網絡和強化學習這2種技術。 針對第一種方法，我們將訓練一個深度神經網絡來模仿現有劃分算法的組合，目的是使其優於任何單一的算法。 針對強化學習，我們將關注深度Q-learning方法，其中的操作(如存儲桶分割)，根據選擇的方式，算法會給予獎勵或者懲罰。 與傳統算法相比，我們期望機器學習技術在解決方案質量和效率方面都能帶來實質性的進步。 最後，我們計劃將我們的方法擴展到其他相關問題，包括移動對象數據庫的動態分區和需要考慮社會聯繫的地理社會分區(geosocial partitioning)。

16206220.label: Realisation of objectives
16206220.value: In this project we focused on multidimensional partitioning and its application to spatial indexing. Our initial approach based on machine learning techniques failed to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, partitioning based on neural networks is very sensitive to the training data and fails to capture distributions that deviate significantly from the training set. Partitioning based on reinforcement and deep Q-learning is prohibitively expensive for large real datasets, common in practical applications. Moreover, neither approach adapts to dynamic data, where the distribution changes over time. Thus, we shifted our direction towards conventional approaches. The focus of multidimensional partitioning, as applied in spatial indexing, is to group objects into nodes so that the resulting index exhibits several, sometimes conflicting, characteristics. (1) It should be fast to build and update. (2) It should be space efficient, packing nodes close to their maximum capacity because half empty nodes have a negative effect on queries with large output. (3) It should minimize the total node area per level. (4) It should have shapely (i.e., square-like) node extents, avoiding nodes that are elongated on some dimension. Such nodes are likely to be accessed by many queries, even though they may not contain results. (5) It should minimize overlapping nodes at the same level because all such nodes are visited by queries that intersect the overlapping area. As a first contribution we propose Waffle, a novel disk-based spatial index, which delivers excellent performance and can accommodate both update- and query-intensive workloads. Waffle constitutes a complete indexing solution that includes: (i) a novel bulk loading method that guarantees optimal disk page utilization on static data, and emphasizes square-like nodes; (ii) algorithms for dynamic updates that create non-overlapping nodes and, (iii) a maintenance mechanism that monitors the query workload and distribution, continuously optimizing the index. Extensive experiments with real datasets verify that Waffle outperforms all its competitors on update and query performance. The bulk-loading algorithm of Waffle involves two-step partitioning. A first step creates the leaf level by recursively sorting and splitting the data points on the longest dimension, until each resulting subspace contains a single page. The split point corresponds to the entry that is nearest to the median and at the boundary of one of the pages. After the termination of the first step, the index contains the leaf nodes and an overflowing root. Each round of the second step splits the root to create a new root at the next (higher) level, until all levels are formed. This process yields almost full nodes with zero overlap between nodes at the same level. For dynamic data, Waffle delays index optimizations until required by the query workload. Specifically, Waffle book-keeps (i) the fat for each directory node, which is the ratio of the data nodes it contains compared to the optimal number, and (ii) the tolerance, which is a limit for the deterioration based on the update/query ratio. Intuitively, the existence of fat implies that the directory contains more nodes than necessary to accommodate the entries in its subtree. When the fat exceeds the tolerance, the directory is repacked by locally bulk loading its subtree. In this way, frequently queried directories, are timely repacked to preserve the low I/O cost of queries. On the other hand, nodes that have relatively more updates, compared to queries, provide leeway to postpone repacking, thereby enabling faster update operations. Our second contribution regards adaptive partitioning and index building. As opposed to previous methods (including Waffle) that build the index only based on the data, in adaptive indexing the data are partitioned on-demand, according to the query workload. Consequently, only parts of the data space that contribute query results are indexed, avoiding unnecessary work. The resulting AMBI (Adaptive Multidimensional Bulk-loaded Index) has a huge advantage compared to non-adaptive competitors, when the queries cover a small part of the data space, in which case only a partial index is generated. AMBI index building and refinement involves the following four steps. In the absence of an index, each query necessitates a sequential scan of the data file. Thus, when the first query is received, Step 1 reads M pages of data points in memory, where M does not exceed the available buffer. Then it uses a major split tree (MST) to recursively partition these points into a set of root entries/subspaces. Specifically, the first split sorts all the points of the M pages on the longest dimension, and assigns the first half of the M pages to the first subspace (of MST) and the rest to second. The new subspaces are recursive partitioned in the same way, always on the longest dimension. If the split dimension changes (between a split point and its parent), sorting on the new dimension is required, but it is always performed in main memory. Step 2 distributes the points of the remaining pages into the subspaces of Step 1. Initially, each subspace is deemed to be active, and its full pages are kept in main memory. At the first insertion in some subspace, we allocate it a new buffer page. A search on MST determines the subspace covering each data point. If the buffer reaches its limit when allocating a new page, we need to free space by flushing an active subspace to the disk. AMBI maintains a max-heap of active subspaces based on their Euclidean distance from the query, and flushes the top of the heap. Consequently, subspaces that are unqualified (i.e., those not containing query results) are deactivated first, whereas those that are qualified are kept in main memory. Step 3 creates the AMBI subtree for active subspaces (already in-memory). The procedure recursively partitions each subspace, until leaf nodes are generated. Then leaf nodes are merged together bottom-up to generate directory nodes. This may lead to directory nodes that are not fully packed. Consequently, Step 4, invokes a bottom-up strategy that merges them conceptually. Concretely, we perform a post-order traversal of MST, where for each underflowed branch, we find the subspace with the lowest common ancestor, such that the total number of their entries is within the node capacity. The aggregated contents of both nodes are stored on the same disk page, but the root of AMBI maintains two separate entries. This process does not introduce additional I/O during query processing since merged pages are only accessed if some of their nodes potentially contain query results.

16206220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206220.value: Although several spatial indexes achieve fast query processing, they are ineffective for highly dynamic data sets because of costly updates. On the other hand, simple structures that enable efficient updates are slow for spatial queries. In publication J1, we propose Waffle, a workload-aware, query-sensitive spatial index, that effectively accommodates both update- and query-intensive workloads. Waffle combines concepts of the space and data partitioning frameworks, and constitutes a complete indexing solution. In addition to query processing algorithms, it includes: (i) a novel bulk loading method that guarantees optimal disk page utilization on static data, (ii) algorithms for dynamic updates that guarantee zero overlapping of nodes, and (iii) a maintenance mechanism that adjusts the trade-off between query and update speed, based on the workload and query distribution. Whereas competitive spatial indexes, such as the KDB-Tree and the R*-Tree, fail in some settings, our experimental evaluation reveals that Waffle delivers excellent query and update performance in all settings, and for both static and dynamic data. Existing bulk loading methods (including Waffle) partition a set of multidimensional points into index nodes using external sorting. In publication C1, we propose techniques that apply linear scan, and are therefore significantly faster. The resulting FMBI index possesses several desirable properties, including almost full and square nodes with zero overlap, and has excellent query performance. As a second contribution, we develop an adaptive version AMBI, which utilizes the query workload to build a partial index only for parts of the data space that contain query results, i.e., the index is built on-demand as a response to the input queries. A comprehensive experimental evaluation with real datasets compares FMBI and AMBI with a multitude of existing indexes under a unified framework. They both outperform all competitors in terms of combined index construction and query processing speed, often by orders of magnitude.

16206220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206220.value: We are currently working on adaptive partitioning algorithms to support dynamic updates. Existing algorithms can be expensive and unsuitable for update intensive workloads. To alleviate this problem, Waffle determines the update frequency of nodes based on their ratio of queries over updates, using the fat and tolerance parameters. Our adaptive techniques, developed in the context of AMBI, provide a natural way to handle workload-based dynamic updates. Specifically, when a new point causes a leaf node to overflow, a new page is allocated to the node to accommodate that point as well as future insertions. Eventually, the node will be processed and refined, when it is accessed by some query. Similarly, underflows are only handled when the node is queried. Unlike Waffle, this lazy approach does not require the maintenance of statistical information per node (the counter of queries and updates), or the introduction of additional parameters (fat and tolerance). Compared to existing algorithms for dynamic multidimensional indexes, this is expected to drop the cost significantly for update intensive workloads, especially when updates arrive in bursts.

16206220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206220.value: In the context of this project, we developed novel techniques for the effective partitioning, indexing and querying of multidimensional objects. Our methods cover a wide variety of application scenarios, including static data, workload-aware updates, and adaptive indexing. Thorough experimental evaluations, with numerous datasets and under diverse settings, reveal that they outperform their state-of-the-art competitors, by large margins. The importance of the proposed methods is only expected to grow with the fast accumulation of multidimensional data from various sources (e.g., sensors, satellites) and emergence of novel applications that utilize them.

16206320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206320.value: Computer-aided design powered by advanced design methods is playing an increasingly important role in a variety of industrial sectors. A relatively new application of computer-aided design is in the field of architected materials in which specific properties of the materials are achieved by carefully controlling the topological distribution of different phases. The demand for materials with high performance and multiple functionalities amplifies the need to search for novel materials. Topology optimization (TO) is a design method that determine the connectivity, shape and size of an optimal structure by distributing the materials wisely inside a given design domain, and hence is an ideal method for designing novel architected materials. Compared to the conventional shape/size optimization, TO operates on a broader design space, and therefore results in much better designs. In the automotive industry, the use of TO to design structural parts typically results in a weight saving of 20%-40%. However a major limitation of TO methods is the need for repetitive evaluations of design objective functions and constraints, which are carried out using high-dimensional numerical simulations that require a large amount of computational power. This greatly limits the application scope of TO methods, despite the potential economic and social benefits that they can bring. The goal of the proposed project is to develop efficient topology optimization methods that can be applied to large-scale design problems. We will first develop model order reduction methods for large-scale mechanical analysis. Then the reduced models will be used in the analysis required in each design iteration. For the design of architected materials, neural-network-based surrogate models will be developed using training datasets generated from the reduced models. These efficient surrogate models will then be embedded into the TO framework to replace the costly finite element analysis. The developed methods will be evaluated by applying them to two design problems: the design of a 3D load bearing wing-like structure with a minimum weight and the design of broadband elastic metasurfaces for vibration isolation. The successful completion of the proposed project will result in a set of efficient design methods and related software tools that enable large-scale structure designs to be carried out with a reasonable amount of computing power. It will also produce, for the first time, broadband elastic metasurfaces that are able to simultaneously block both P and SV waves, paving the way for the design of passive anti-earthquake systems for the protection of buildings. 基于先进的设计方法的计算机辅助设计对推动各种工业领域的发展起着重要的作用，目前计算机辅助设计已应用到材料领域，是设计新颖材料，比如超材料，的一个有效工具。 拓扑优化（TO）是一种通过在给定的设计域内明智地分配材料来确定最佳结构的连通性，形状和大小的设计方法，因此是设计超材料的理想方法。与传统的形状/尺寸优化相比，TO可以在更广阔的设计空间中运行，因此可以提供更好的设计。在汽车工业中，使用TO设计结构零件通常可减轻20％-40％的重量。但是，TO方法的主要局限性是需要对设计目标函数和约束进行重复评估，这需要使用需要非常耗时的高维数值模拟来进行，从而极大地限制了TO方法的应用范围。 本项目的目标是开发可应用于大规模设计问题的高效拓扑优化方法。我们将首先开发用于大型力学分析的模型降阶方法， 用于每次设计迭代所需的分析中。对于超材料的设计，将使用从简化模型生成的训练数据集来开发基于神经网络的替代模型。这些有效的替代模型随后将被嵌入到TO框架中，以取代昂贵的有限元分析。 我们将用以下两个设计问题对提出的方法进行评估：最小重量的3D承重翼状结构的设计以及用于隔振的宽带弹性超表面的设计。本项目的成功完成将产生一套有效的设计方法和相关的软件工具，可应用于大规模的结构设计。它还将首次产生能够同时阻挡P波和SV波的宽带弹性超表面，从而为保护建筑物的抗震系统的设计铺平了道路。

16206320.label: Realisation of objectives
16206320.value: There are four project objectives proposed in this project. The following is the description of the achievement of each objective. To develop model-order reduction methods for large-scale structural analysis suitable for topology optimization Currently, nearly all existing machine learning-based methods for accelerating structural analysis are supervised, requiring a large set of labeled training data. For structural analysis, labeled training data is typically generated through high-dimensional numerical simulations or experimental measurements, both of which can be time-consuming and costly. As a result, generating a substantial amount of training data for large-scale analysis is often infeasible. This research focuses on developing model-order reduction methods to accelerate large-scale analysis using machine learning. We have created two approaches to reduce the size of the simulation system and design problems. The first approach employs artificial neural network models to map coarse mesh solutions to their corresponding fine mesh solutions. During inference, only the coarse mesh solution is needed, significantly reducing the size of the analysis system. To minimize the amount of full-order training data, we utilize domain decomposition. The analysis domain is divided into smaller subdomains, allowing the neural network models to operate on each small domain rather than the entire domain. This approach offers two main advantages: first, the number of training data points is greatly increased by a factor of N, where N is the number of decomposed subdomains. Second, both the complexity and size of the network model are significantly reduced, making it easier to train and requiring much less training data. The second approach is specifically designed for structural design using the topology optimization (TO) method. To reduce the size of the design problem, TO is initially performed to create low-resolution designs. Artificial neural network models are then constructed to map these low-resolution designs to fine-resolution ones. Similar to the previous approach, domain decomposition is employed to augment the training data and reduce the complexity of the network, thereby decreasing the number of high-resolution designs required for training. Both approaches have been successfully validated through a series of 2D and 3D benchmark problems in structural analysis and design. For detailed information please refer to journal articles No. 3-4 and No. 5. To develop neural network-based surrogate models for metamaterial/metasurface design We have developed efficient machine learning-based surrogate models for both architectured metamaterials (also known as mechanical metamaterials) and wave-manipulating metamaterials/metasurfaces, including acoustic and elastic metamaterials During the design of acoustic and elastic metamaterials, the most time-consuming part occurs during the repetitive wave analysis for the evolving metamaterial structure at each design iteration. We have developed efficient surrogate modeling techniques based on the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to facilitate fast wave analysis for varying wave frequencies and structures in both interior and exterior domains. The FNO is a neural network model that maps one function space to another, making it suitable for constructing surrogate models for wave analysis across a wide range of parameter spaces. However, the current FNO has two shortcomings. First, it was originally developed for interior problems only, and extending it to exterior problems poses challenges due to the need for domain integration, which is infeasible for infinite domains. Second, the original FNO requires substantial memory and has slow computation speeds during both training and inference phases. Although several variants of the FNO have been proposed, improvements for large-scale problems are still necessary. To address these shortcomings, we have developed two novel techniques. First, by combining the boundary element method with the FNO, we propose a Boundary Fourier Neural Operator (B-FNO) for handling exterior wave analysis. This approach reduces the problem dimension by one and transforms the integration over infinite domains into finite domains, thus enabling analysis for exterior problems. Regarding the second issue, the main contributors to the large memory consumption and slow calculations are the full-order kernel used in domain integration and the 3D convolution integral calculations. By integrating proper generalization decomposition, a model-order reduction technique, with the FNO, we introduce a Decomposed FNO (D-FNO) approach. This method significantly reduces the computational time required for the 3D convolution integral. Additionally, we propose a reduced-order kernel that greatly diminishes memory consumption for storing this kernel. Various acoustic and elastic wave analysis problems have been employed to validate the performance of the proposed approaches. For detailed information please refer to journal articles No. 7 and 8. For the design of architectured metamaterials, we have developed an adaptive artificial neural network-based generative design approach that rapidly produces a variety of metamaterials with desired mechanical properties. By combining generative models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), ANN-based regression models, and genetic algorithms, we have designed a range of novel composite materials, including those with stiffness reaching the theoretical upper bound, for the first time. For detailed information please refer to journal articles No. 1 and 2. To evaluate the performance of the developed methods through the design of a load bearing 2D wing-like structure with high resolution Several load-bearing structures, including a 2D wing-like structure and various 3D load-bearing designs, have been developed using the proposed methods. Detailed information can be found in the journal papers mentioned above. To design a broadband elastic metasurface for vibration isolation and validate its performance A variety of broadband acoustic and elastic metasurfaces for wave manipulation, including efficient beam steering and wave focusing, have been designed. These metasurfaces effectively mitigate wave propagation paths and isolate specific vibration ranges. Their performance has been numerically validated through full-order finite element simulations. Although not part of the original objectives, experimental measurements have been conducted to validate the performance of several designed acoustic metasurfaces, with the results documented in a journal paper. Measurements for the designed elastic metasurfaces are currently ongoing. For detailed information please refer to journal articles No.6.

16206320.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206320.value: Several machine learning-based model-order reduction methods and surrogate modeling techniques have been proposed for large-scale structural analysis and metamaterial design. These approaches enhance the state of the art in computational methods and facilitate the design of a diverse array of high-performance structures and materials. In total, eight journal papers have been published or accepted.

16206320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206320.value: The performance of the proposed approaches can be further improved by incorporating multigrid simulation techniques, which have the potential to reduce further memory consumption, improving computational speed and enable parallel computation. Preliminary studies have been conducted, yielding promising results. In terms of applications, several key problems have been identified, including the simulation of noise propagation in urban environments and the design of underwater sound absorbers. These concepts have been compiled into a GRF proposal submitted in November 2024.

16206320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206320.value: Computer-aided design is becoming increasingly vital across various industries, especially in developing metamaterials. These materials achieve specific properties through careful control of their structure. As the demand for high-performance, multifunctional materials grows, innovative solutions are needed. One promising design method is topology optimization (TO), which optimally shapes and sizes structures by smartly distributing materials within a defined space. However, traditional TO methods require extensive computational resources due to repeated evaluations of complex design simulations, limiting their wider application. The proposed project aims to develop more efficient TO methods for large-scale design challenges. We have created machine learning-based model-order reduction techniques for large-scale structural analysis, significantly reducing analysis time and enabling the design of high-resolution 3D structures and materials. Additionally, we have developed efficient surrogate modeling techniques based on the Fourier Neural Operator to facilitate rapid wave analysis across varying frequencies and structures in both interior and exterior domains. These approaches have been successfully employed to design several high-performance, multifunctional acoustic and elastic metamaterials for a variety of applications.

16206620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206620.value: A networked control system is a closed-loop system that utilizes wireless networks to communicate between its key subsystems. The development of communication technology has brought enormous convenience and reduced the cost of installment, diagnosis, debugging and maintenance. However, if the participating agents do not belong to the same organization, the flow of information and data may cause privacy issues. The different purposes of the involved agents may cause conflicts of interest. One participant's data may be collected and even explored and analyzed by another, resulting in then unintentional disclosure of private information. For example, details of household life can be inferred from data on household energy consumption collected by smart meters, and personal lifestyles may be learned from driving records collected by navigation softwares. In conventional communication, encryption techniques work by encoding data so that data packets are unreadable by unauthorized parties. However, even without a malicious external attacker or eavesdropper, an agent's private information may be fully accessed by other legitimate users (e.g., servers) whom they may not completely trust. For example, agents provide private data to obtain certain services yet they hope to protect sensitive private information from being exposed. Traditional encryption techniques cannot solve such privacy concerns. Strategic information transmission (SIT) originated from the economics field. It provides a communication model between two agents-a transmitter (e.g., strategic sensor) and a receiver (e.g., remote estimator)-with different objectives. The transmitter designs its encoder, and the receiver designs the decoder accordingly. The mismatch between the transmitter and the receiver is modeled using different costs, where the transmitter's cost is additionally affected by a single parameter, e.g., the private information. Our preliminary study showed that SIT is a powerful tool that can be applied in a number of application scenarios in networked control systems where privacy issues arise. The aim of this proposed project will be to comprehensively explore the use of SIT to tackle the mismatching objectives between different agents and to further investigate the trade-off between system performance and individual privacy. We will develop a set of methodologies for privacy-aware decision-making problems in networked control systems. 網絡化控制系統是一個通過無線通信網絡連結子系統的閉環迴路。通信技術的發展帶來極大便利的同時也降低了部署、診斷、調試和維護的成本。不過，當其中的多個智能體分屬不同利益團體時，信息的流動將引發關於隱私的憂慮。同時，智能體之間不同的目標也將引發利益衝突。其中任一參與者的數據將被系統中其他智能體所收集並利用，造成對隱私的無意洩露，例如：日常生活的細節可從用電數據推斷，個人的生活習慣亦能由GPS導航歷史所反映。傳統通信的加密可通過數據編碼來實現，未授權的用戶無法對信息進行解碼。然而，即便系統中不存在攻擊者和竊聽者，用戶的隱私也將被合法用戶們（例如：服務器）所掌握，而合法用戶之間亦難確保完全信任。舉例來說，用戶們提供個人信息來獲取相應服務，同時他們也希望保護隱私免於洩露。傳統加密技術已無法解決人們對隱私的憂慮。作為一個可行的方案，策略化信息傳輸（SIT）源於經濟領域。它描述了追求不同利益的發送端（如策略化的傳感器）和接收端（如遠程狀態估計器）之間的通信。發送端決定了編碼器，並由接收端相應的設計解碼器。兩端間的利益衝突由不同的成本函數來建模，其中發送端的成本函數會額外將隱私納入考量。 我們的初步研究表明，策略化信息傳輸是一項功能強大的技術，可以在網絡化控制系統的許多存在隱私顧慮的應用場景中使用。該擬議項目的目的是全面探索策略化信息傳輸，以實現智能體的不同利益目標，並進一步研究系統性能與個體隱私之間的權衡。我們將為網絡化控制系統中的隱私保護決策類問題制定方法： 1. 為存在策略化傳感器的隱私保護決策問題推導最優編碼器和解碼器； 2. 將事件觸發機制引入保護隱私的策略化信息傳輸中，以保持通信與性能之間的平衡； 3. 使用平均場博弈論分析具有大規模策略化傳感器的應用場景，並為其找到最優的編碼器和解碼器。

16206620.label: Realisation of objectives
16206620.value: We have made excellent progress under the support of this funding. Following the objectives of the project, we have obtained many interesting and important results published in leading international journals including Automatica and IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control. These journal publications can be found in Section 8 of this report. In these research results, we used a wide range of tools including differential privacy, game theory, event-triggered control and optimization theory to address some typical sensor design/allocation and the associated state estimation problems in a cyber-physical system. We study the trade-off between the system performance and the limited resources. We further improve the system performance by constructing effective and efficient sensor schedules. Along the original objectives, we have also successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as distributed optimization, neuromorphic sensor, power allocation in a smart sensor, etc. The results are fruitful which are summarized and published in 8 leading prestigious international journals and 1 leading international conference (We submitted more papers to international journals instead of conferences because of the pandemic). In addition to the above theoretical development, we have provided rigorous training to two PhD students (Huiwen Yang and Nachuan Yang).

16207120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207120.value: 軟件系統通過不斷的錯誤修正，引入新功能，軟件重構等的代碼更改而持續演化。不幸的是，由於演化過程的固有複雜性，現實生活中的軟件系統在實踐中無可避免地附有錯誤。研究發現這些錯誤經常由演化過程中的代碼提交所導致。由於測試不足，通常不會在代碼提交時檢測到這些錯誤。我們稱此類提交為導致錯誤的代碼提交。我們最近的研究發現，開發人員在診斷軟件故障時常常先找出引起錯誤的提交。一旦找出了此信息，開發人員可以利用與之關聯的上下文信息（例如，代碼更改的類型以及進行這些更改的開發人員）來幫助理解引起故障的原因，從而找到錯誤的代碼並相應地對其進行修復。此問題引發了各種研究以理解這些代碼提交的特性用以預測代碼在提交時是否可能出錯。這些研究還提出了從已知的代碼修復中識別出導致故障的相關代碼提交的技術。但是，這些技術不能幫助開發人員在製定代碼修復前識別出導致故障的代碼提交。儘管導致故障的提交對於診斷錯誤非常重要，但我們發現現有研究並未從揭示故障的測試中有效地識別此類提交。此外，現有的研究很少將引起故障的提交信息用於故障定位和代碼修復。本項目旨在彌合這些差距。 儘管引起故障的提交為故障定位和代碼修復提供了有價值的信息，但是如何識別它們卻具有挑戰性。為了理解這些挑戰，我們最近對從大型開源項目的故障中收集的基準數據集進行了實證研究。我們的研究發現，現有方法只能準確地識別出25.5％引發故障的提交。導致識別不精確的原因有多樣。主要的原因是無法在那些測試所依賴的某些API或類丟失或不兼容的那些舊軟件版本上運行那些能夠揭示故障的測試。它導致使用那些測試來從過去提交歷史中搜索錯誤的版本，從而重複需要診斷的故障。我們建議通過兩種自動化機制來解決此問題：減少測試腳本和模擬測試腳本中引發的依賴關係。前者是從測試腳本中刪除與所關注的故障診斷無關的那些依賴關係，而後者是模擬依賴的API。我們將進一步開發機制，以利用已確定的引起故障的提交來增強故障定位和代碼修復。我們建議的工作將為軟件質量保證和維護帶來巨大的幫助。我們將為提出的新技術提供工具支援，並將其與我們的數據集一起發布給公眾。正如華為，騰訊和微軟亞洲研究院的合作夥伴所指出，本項目引起了業界的極大興趣。

16207120.label: Realisation of objectives
16207120.value: The following activities were carried out to realize the project objectives. Objective 1: Our research activities focused on collecting and characterizing subjects to investigate bug-inducing program commits (BICs), offering significant contributions to the software engineering community. We gathered a diverse set of datasets, including open-source software projects and their historical commit data, projects from the Defects4J dataset with real bugs and triggering test cases, 2,007 MR-encoded test cases (MTCs) from high-quality Java projects on GitHub, 196 configuration compatibility (CC) issues from 43 open-source Android apps, four Java projects from programming assignments, and 58 faulty Deep Learning (DL) programs from Stack Overflow and GitHub. By analyzing commit histories and failing test cases in Defect4J projects, we identified bug-inducing commits (BICs) and revealed compilation errors tied to incompatible commits. This comprehensive data collection enhances the understanding of failing tests and BICs across varied software contexts, aiding the community in tackling software maintenance challenges. We further characterized these subjects to uncover patterns and impacts of BICs, providing actionable insights for software engineers. The collected subjects were analyzed based on attributes like project domain, programming language, size, and complexity, specifically focusing on BIC characteristics such as the types of changes introduced and their behavioral effects. Build failures were classified into four categories—changes to the Java language, standard library, unsupported character encoding, and build tools—illuminating how software evolution triggers bugs. For MTCs, we filtered 180 cases to study metamorphic relations for fault detection. At the same time, CC issues in Android apps revealed patching strategies for XML configuration inconsistencies across API levels. In Java projects, we characterized OOP features and linked errors committed by junior programmers to bug patterns. In DL programs, we identified five prevalent fault types (e.g., activation function, optimizer). These efforts contribute by detailing how faults manifest and persist, informing better debugging and prevention strategies for DL applications. Our methodological advancements and exploration of new domains further bolster the study of BICs and fault manifestation in recent software development paradigms. Using GitHub Bisect, we manually identified BICs, encountering challenges like inconsistent failure messages and oscillating failures across versions, which prompted the exploration of static analysis solutions. We noted that many bugs from BICs were detected years later—some over twelve years—highlighting difficulties in reproducing old versions due to test dependencies and obsolete APIs, a critical insight for improving long-term software maintenance. Additionally, we ventured into blockchain smart contracts as a new domain, leveraging their evolutionary nature and fewer dependencies to locate buggy evolutions, such as transaction-related bugs. Objective 2: Our research has significantly advanced test dependency resolution and maintenance, directly enhancing the software engineering community's ability to address bug-inducing program commits (BICs). We conducted dependency analysis to examine how bug-revealing tests rely on various software components and versions, followed by the development of automated dependency resolution techniques to ensure these tests can execute on historical commits, including those with BICs. To support long-term test suite usability, we implemented dependency maintenance strategies that keep resolved dependencies current as software evolves. Additionally, we introduced a test dependency minimization technique, removing unused classes and methods, and implemented it at the source level to fix compilation errors. Supported by reachability analysis and methods for handling dynamic method calls, this approach retains only essential code while maintaining test validity. These efforts, evaluated using real-world projects, improve regression testing and fault localization by enabling efficient testing of BICs. We extended our core techniques to specialized applications, such as metamorphic testing and Android compatibility, further contributing to robust testing practices. For metamorphic relations (MRs), we proposed MR-Adopt, an LLM-based method for input transformation generation, using a two-phase pipeline to create and refine transformation functions. This process, supported by dependency management via data-flow analysis, ensures alignment with encoded MRs, aiding in the maintenance of tests sensitive to BICs. In parallel, we addressed Android compatibility by diagnosing CC issues and analyzing dependencies between XML attributes and the Android framework to understand how framework changes (and related commits) cause issues. Using UI test scripts to reproduce problems and validate fixes, we ensure test scripts remain effective amidst framework evolution. These contributions enhance testing resilience in dynamic software environments. Objective 3: Our research activities have significantly advanced fault localization and repair, with a strong emphasis on leveraging bug-inducing commits (BICs) to enhance software engineering practices. We have utilized BICs to improve fault localization techniques by analyzing the changes they introduce, allowing us to suggest potential fault locations within codebases. This approach is complemented by the development and enhancement of algorithms that integrate BICs with contextual information to pinpoint bug locations with greater accuracy and efficiency. We evaluated these techniques using benchmarks of real-world bugs and conducted case studies to demonstrate their practical application, providing the software engineering community with reliable tools to streamline debugging. Additionally, our automated repair efforts include a minimization technique that resolves compilation errors by removing unused code, restoring compilability in all evaluated cases and replicating test results in over 80% of instances. This technique supports automated bug bisection, directly aiding in the identification of BICs, thus offering developers a robust method to maintain software quality. In the domain of testing and fault detection, we have pioneered the use of metamorphic testing with generated input transformations to uncover faults across a wider range of inputs. By applying metamorphic relations (MRs) and using developer-written assertions as oracles, we enhance fault localization and improve test adequacy, as evidenced by higher line coverage and mutation scores. This comprehensive testing indirectly supports the identification of BICs by revealing faults that might otherwise go unnoticed. Furthermore, our ConfFix tool addresses compatibility (CC) issues by identifying problematic XML elements and attributes and generating automated patches to resolve them. Evaluated for effectiveness and validated through developer feedback, ConfFix ensures software integrity without introducing new faults. Our ongoing exploration of abstract interpretation to locate BICs further promises to narrow down bug-inducing commit candidates, enhancing fault localization capabilities. Objective 4: We developed benchmarks and evaluation frameworks to support further BIC management that advance research and improve software quality. JavaBench, a project-level Java benchmark, assesses large language models' code generation capabilities, focusing on object-oriented programming features. With a robust evaluation pipeline, it identifies potential bug sources in generated code, indirectly contributing to BIC prevention by promoting higher-quality code generation. Compared to existing benchmarks and continuously improved based on feedback, JavaBench was publicly released to foster further study. Additionally, we built a benchmark for DeepFD, featuring 58 faulty DL programs with patches and faulty statement locations, enabling standardized evaluation of fault localization tools. This benchmark and DeepFD’s evaluation pipeline and public release support ongoing research into BIC-related faults in DL programs. Together, these resources provide the software engineering community with valuable tools and data to mitigate bug-inducing commits effectively. The datasets and tools developed are publicly available at: - https://zenodo.org/records/15205931 (bug-inducing commits) - https://mr-adopt.github.io/ (synthesized metamorphic tests) - https://mr-scout.github.io/ (collection of metamorphic tests) - https://github.com/java-bench/JavaBench (Java benchmarks) - https://github.com/ArabelaTso/DeepFD (faulty deep learning programs)

16207120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207120.value: This project led to the training and graduation of 3 research students, and the publication of multiple top-tier research articles. 1. Data Collection and Characterization of BICs - Diverse Datasets: The research collected varied datasets, including open-source projects, 2,007 metamorphic test cases (MTCs) [J2, C3], 196 Android configuration compatibility (CC) issues [C5], Java student projects [C4], 58 faulty deep learning (DL) programs [C6], and ecosystem vulnerabilities [C7]. Commit histories and bug reports identified BICs [J4], while recompiling with JDK8 and JDK17 exposed compilation errors from incompatible commits [J1]. - BIC Characterization: Projects were analyzed by domain, language, size, and complexity, with BICs classified by change types and effects [J4]. Build failures were grouped into Java language changes, standard library issues, encoding problems, and build tool errors [J1]. Android CC issues showed XML inconsistencies, and DL programs revealed five fault types [C6, J3]. 2. Challenges and New Domains: Challenges included inconsistent failure messages and reproducing old versions due to obsolete APIs, with some bugs detected over 12 years later [J1, J4]. Blockchain smart contracts emerged as a new domain for studying synchronization and transaction reverting faults [C1, C2], facilitating future studies of BICs. 3. Test Dependency Resolution and Maintenance - Dependency Techniques: Automated dependency resolution ensured bug-revealing tests ran on historical commits, keeping maintenance strategies current [J1, J4]. A minimization technique removed unused code to fix compilation errors, which was validated via reachability analysis [J1]. - Specialized Applications: MR-Adopt, an LLM-based tool, generated input transformations for metamorphic testing [J2, C3], while Android CC issues were addressed using UI test scripts and XML-framework dependency analysis [C5]. 4. Fault Localization and Repair - Fault Localization: BICs improved fault localization by analyzing introduced changes, with algorithms integrating contextual data [J4]. Evaluations used real-world bugs, and a minimization technique aided automated bug bisection [J1]. - Repair Tools: DeepFD diagnosed DL faults, both showing superior performance [C6]. LLMs were assessed for code generation risks [C4].

16207120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207120.value: The research offers several areas for further development. - Data Expansion: Broadening data collection to encompass diverse programming languages and domains, such as web development or embedded systems, could reveal unique BIC patterns, enhancing generalizability. - Root Cause Analysis: Investigating deeper causes of BICs, like developer behavior or team dynamics, could inform more effective prevention strategies. - Scalability Improvements: Enhancing automated test dependency resolution techniques to handle large, complex codebases would boost their practical applicability. - Predictive Modeling: Integrating machine learning to predict potential BICs based on code patterns or developer history could preemptively reduce bugs. Tool Enhancement: Refining tools like ConfFix and DeepFD for better usability and integrating them into popular IDEs would encourage wider adoption. - Benchmark Construction: Expanding benchmarks like JavaBench and the DeepFD benchmark to include varied scenarios would strengthen evaluation standards. - Standardization: Creating standardized protocols to tackle challenges like inconsistent failure messages or reproducing old versions would improve BIC identification reliability. - Education: Developing educational tools or curricula, leveraging insights from Java student projects, could train new developers to avoid BICs. - Industry Collaboration: Partnering with industry to test findings in real-world projects would refine tools and techniques, amplifying impact.

16207120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207120.value: Software developers add new features and fix bugs as software evolves. Their changes can accidentally mess things up—creating "bugs" in the code update. These mistakes are called bug-inducing commits (BICs). This research explored how to spot and fix them to keep software reliable. First, the project gathered various examples, like open-source projects, student code, and even AI programs, to determine how BICs happen. It found patterns—like updates to coding tools causing unexpected glitches—and learned some bugs hidden for over 12 years! Next, the project tackled testing, such as running safety checks on the software. The project developed tools to ensure these tests work on older code versions where BICs lurk, fixing issues that block the checks so bugs get caught early. It also built tools to automatically fix certain bugs, especially in Android apps and AI systems, saving developers time. Finally, the project shares tools and datasets with the public, helping the software community catch and facilitate reliable software evolution.

16207420.label: Project Objectives
16207420.value: To design, fabricate and characterize (on the heterogeneously integrated III-V-on-Si photonic platform) four-port nonlinear optical processing nodes based on optical injection to electrically pumped microcavity-oscillators, with a relaxation oscillation frequency of a few GHz, which are vertically coupled with an input-waveguide carrying optical signals and with an output-waveguide in the conventional add-drop filter configuration. To develop a photonic reservoir using the four-port microcavity-oscillator node, with optical injection from the input-port and coherently feedback-coupled over a waveguide delay line, with delay line losses of < 2 dB/cm, a time delay of ~500 ps, to serve as a simple single-node photonic reservoir. To test the data processing performance for this using a Boolean XOR operation and 5-bit header recognition tasks at 2 Gbit/s, with an error rate of ~1% and < 10%, respectively. To develop a photonic reservoir in a 1x2 coupled-oscillator network comprising two four-port microcavity-oscillator processing nodes, connected by a ring waveguide-loop delay line, with an XOR operation at 2 Gbit/s with an error rate of < 1%, and to demonstrate an 8-bit header recognition task at 2 Gbit/s, with an error rate of < 10%.

16207420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207420.value: 受人腦的功能與結構啟發，現代人工智能利用人工神經網絡來訓練機器，以在不輸入具體領域知識的情況下解決問題。範例應用有語言識別、物體探測、國際象棋等。循環神經網絡是一種專門處理連續資料輸入（例如口語）的變體人工神經網絡。為了減少訓練循環神經網路的計算成本，研究人員發展出了儲蓄池計算。這是一種利用固定的儲蓄池內連接來避免對高度非線性及動態的網絡進行訓練的循環神經網絡構架。 在過去的二十年裡，研究人員在機械、生物、電子及光學物理系統內實現了儲蓄池計算。耦合振盪器網絡作為一種有前景的儲蓄池計算的物理實施途徑被提出並驗證。振盪器的非線性動態響應把連續的資料輸入映射到高維的狀態輸出空間，這是進一步處理資料的關鍵。與此同時，網絡中振盪器間的耦合確保了資料在儲蓄池中循環連接，這提供了一種短期記憶。 在本研究計畫中，我們將致力於在硅基芯片上實現集成的用於儲蓄池計算的光子耦合振盪器網絡。與其他物理系統相比，光學儲蓄池計算具有光通信的高並行性、極快的模擬計算速度以及信號光速連接的特點。與分立的的光子器件平臺相比，用於儲蓄池計算的集成硅基光子平臺有機械穩定性高、可拓展性強和與標準納米製造工藝及光纖通信網絡相兼容的突出優點。基於異質集成的有源增益材料與諧振腔的耦合，我們可以在硅基光子芯片上集成光學振盪器（例如激光器）。通過在芯片上利用集成的光學延遲線自耦合一個或互耦合多個振盪器，我們希望能驗證芯片上儲蓄池計算的功能。 特別的，我們會研究用於儲蓄池計算的基於硅上三五族光子學平臺的耦合微腔振盪器網絡。我們將利用硅波導來形成微環結構，與異質集成的銦鎵砷磷基的增益介質一起構成光學振盪器，同時用光延遲線來形成光子儲蓄池中處理節點間的連接。我們將利用振盪器在光學輸入信號及其循環的相干光學反饋信號影響下的非線性動態過程。我們將級聯這樣的光子處理節點以形成雙耦合振盪器網絡，並研究擴展至更大規模網絡的可行性。我們將在2 Gbit/s的資料速率下表徵我們的光子儲蓄池。

16207420.label: Realisation of objectives
16207420.value: Objective 1: Achievements: We successfully increased the yield of bonding the patterned silicon-on-insulator (SOI) dies with III-V semiconductor gain dies from ~60% to >90% with an improved fabrication robustness. We fabricated the designed devices by tuning the atomic layer deposition (ALD)-assisted molecular bonding (as planned in the extension request) and exploited the III-V dummy dies to test and to tune the etching recipe of III-V medium to achieve a smooth sidewall. We developed a CH4-based etching recipe for the inductively coupled plasma (ICP) RIE process of the III-V gain medium. We demonstrated continuous wave (cw) lasing output from the vertically coupled silicon waveguides at room temperature. We measured multi-mode lasing spectra in the telecommunications bands from 1500 nm to 1620 nm wavelengths (refer to Other Impact). We characterized our III-V-on-Si waveguide-coupled microring lasers upon an external optical injection at various optical powers and wavelengths. Our experiments revealed both external-optical-injection-dependent time series of the diode currents and of the light output from the vertically coupled silicon waveguides. Under-achievements: The fabrication process took much longer than planned due to the ultra-high pm-level cleanliness and smoothness requirements for the molecular bonding process. We have characterized all our 20 fabricated devices, yet we have not observed a relaxation oscillation frequency. Attempts to overcome problems: We will continue to fabricate new devices using our improved fabrication process and characterize the on-chip lasers for relaxation oscillation frequency. Objective 2: Achievements: We successfully designed and fabricated III-V-on-Si microring lasers coupled with (i) integrated spiral delay lines and (ii) integrated feedback mirrors. We measured the light-emission spectra collected from the silicon waveguides of external-feedback-coupled III-V-on-Si microring cavities (refer to Other Impact). We characterized the time series of the oscillated light output from the coupled silicon waveguides of devices with optical injection from the input-port. We completed the characterizations of our fabricated III-V-on-Si tapered waveguide as a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) and an on-chip photomonitor, which are building-block components required to be integrated into external-coupled feedback loops (as originally proposed in Objective 2). We tested our fabricated passive silicon devices including 2 to 4 cm-long spiral delay lines with a waveguide loss of 4 dB/cm comparable to the typical commercial foundry values of 2.5 dB/cm. We constructed a numerical modelling based on the coupled-mode theory of the nonlinear dynamics in semiconductor waveguide-coupled microring injection lasers (as mentioned in our extension request). We explored numerically that under which perturbations from optical feedback can induce the microring lasers to desirable time-dependent oscillations while not entering into a chaotic state. Our modelling results suggested that upon certain external feedback strength realizable on a chip the microring lasers can function as a workable reservoir (refer to conference paper #1). Based on the theoretical models, we completed an optimized layout design. We numerically demonstrated a Boolean XOR operation at 2 Gbit/s, with an error rate of ~1% using our designed microcavity oscillator externally coupled with feedback delay lines. Under-achievements: We have not been able to experimentally test the data processing of 2 Gb/s using a Boolean XOR operation or 5-bit header recognition tasks at 2 Gbit/s with the required error rates. There are three major problems that we encountered as follows: First, our microring lasers turned out to fall short on vertically coupled power from the III-V gain layer to the silicon passive layer. We measured in our fabricated devices a thicker bonding layer of ~50 nm thickness than a designed thickness of 30 nm, which potentially leads to a weaker vertical coupling than designed. Thus, our microring lasers see an insufficient gain with a short round-trip cavity length of 38 μm to 177 μm. The III-V microring sidewalls were also aligned with those of the silicon waveguides underneath, exposing the light to the sidewall roughness from the heterogeneous integrated waveguide. Second, our fabricated silicon spiral delay lines were characterized with a ~4 dB/cm propagation loss, which is larger than the original target value in Objective 2. We attribute the extra propagation loss to water vapors generated in the molecular bonding were not completely released and trapped around the silicon waveguides. Our plasma-enhanced chemical-vapor oxide cladding is not conformal, which is unable to fully fill the air trenches (for releasing the water vapors) surrounding the silicon waveguides. Third, the device yield is low despite the high wafer bond yield. Some of our fabricated devices were measured with a large contact resistance or short-circuited contacts. Some of the fabricated silicon spiral delay lines were destroyed due to exposure to a chlorine-based III-V dry etching process. Attempts to overcome problems: First, we have adopted a new ALD process (in our on-going fabrication) with a measured thinner bonding layer of ~20 nm thickness. We have optimized our current designs and completed a new layout design (as planned in the extension request). We have designed a reduced silicon waveguide height with a better phase-matched coupling with the III-V layer on the top. We have designed a 300 nm-wide offset from the III-V waveguide sidewalls outside the silicon waveguide sidewalls to reduce the light scattering losses due to the former. We will adopt Tetraethoxysilane (TEOS) oxide to serve as a conformal cladding layer for surface passivation of the III-V waveguides. Second, we have adopted an optimized bending radius of silicon spiral delay lines in our new layout to achieve a reduced propagation loss of 2 dB/cm (as originally proposed in Objective 2). We will also adopt TEOS oxide with better conformity as an insulated cladding layer for the silicon waveguides. Third, we have optimized the metal layer design with an enlarged P/N contact gap spacing to avoid short circuiting. We optimized the device layout with a compact structure to increase the device yield given a limited bonding area of 1 cm × 1 cm. We will adopt Titanium (enhanced adhesion) and Copper (reduced resistivity and improved thermal stability) with a lift-off process for the device metallization, to achieve reduced contact resistance. Objective 3: Achievements: We successfully designed and fabricated waveguide-interconnected dual-microring lasers as a 1×2 coupled oscillator network. We measured the time series of the oscillated light output from the coupled silicon waveguides of the devices with optical injection from the waveguide input-port. We constructed theoretical modellings based on the coupled-mode theory of the nonlinear dynamics in two interconnected semiconductor waveguide-coupled microring injection lasers as microcavity-oscillator processing nodes for reservoir computing. Based on our theoretical modellings, we completed a new layout design (as planned in the extension request). We numerically demonstrated a Boolean XOR operation at 2 Gbit/s, with an error rate of <1% using our designed waveguide-interconnected dual-microring lasers. Under-achievements: We have not been able to experimentally test the data processing of 2 Gb/s in a Boolean XOR operation or 8-bit header recognition tasks at 2 Gbit/s with the required error rates. The major problems that we encountered can be referred to those listed for Objective 2. Attempts to overcome problems: Refer to the descriptions for Objective 2.

16207420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207420.value: 1. We theoretically modeled (See conference paper #1, conference paper #2) the nonlinear dynamics in external-feedback-coupled semiconductor waveguide-coupled microring injection lasers upon external optical injection for reservoir computing. Based on our theoretical modeling, we numerically simulated, designed, and fabricated III-V-on-Si waveguide-coupled microring lasers externally coupled with 2 to 4 cm silicon spiral delay lines (See conference paper #1). We plan to submit a journal manuscript over the next 6 months reporting our experimental results on nonlinear dynamics from such microring lasers based on our device fabrication along with an updated theoretical modeling. 2. We developed die-to-die ALD-assisted molecular bonding process with pm-level chip cleanliness (See Other Impact) and achieved a >90% bonding yield within a 1 cm × 1 cm die size (See conference paper #2). We developed an III-V inductively coupled plasma (ICP) reactive ion etching (RIE) recipe, achieving a smooth waveguide sidewall of 6 μm-radius III-V microrings and III-V-on-Si SOA waveguide tapers (See Other Impact). 3. We demonstrated in our fabricated waveguide-coupled III-V-on-Si microring laser multi-mode cw lasing (See Other Impact) in the telecommunications bands from 1500 nm to 1620 nm wavelengths at room temperature, with a threshold current density of ~0.12 kA/cm2 (upon a turn-on voltage of ~0.9 V), emitted in both clockwise and counter-clockwise directions. 4. We demonstrated in our fabricated III-V-on-Si SOA (See MPhil. thesis #1) a maximum on-chip gain of 13 dB upon an injection current of 18 mA at an optical injection of 30 dBm, at a wavelength of 1556 nm. We demonstrated in our designed and fabricated III-V-on-Si in-line photodetector (PD) a responsivity of 1.501 A/W (See MPhil. Thesis #1) at 1550 nm wavelength upon a reverse bias of −2 V, and an estimated bandwidth of 1.19 Gb/s. These lay down a solid foundation towards achieving coupled microcavity-oscillator networks integrated with SOAs and PDs.

16207420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207420.value: The major difficulties of the research are the low yield of devices and the long iteration time of the complex 7-mask device fabrications for heterogeneous integration. Multiple factors that are difficult to control or systematically repeat in a university cleanroom (e.g., quality of metallization, quality of etched III-V waveguide sidewalls, fabrication tolerance, etc.) turn out to significantly compromise the device yield and the performance of our fabricated III-V-on-Si devices. For further developments, we will keep optimizing our device designs for more tolerant to inevitable fabrication imperfections (e.g., adopting an enlarged cavity length, a more compact configuration of the feedback-coupled microcavity oscillator network, and an optimized metal contact design), and keep optimizing our fabrication process to achieve an improved yield of robust devices.

16207420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207420.value: Reservoir computing (RC) is a formidable analog computing scheme specifically tailored to process the vast amount of sequential input data in application tasks such as speech recognition. The research community has been extensively investigating optical implementations of RC given its potentially low power consumption and high data rate. Among the various optical reservoir implementations, silicon-based photonic integrated circuits have gained traction in the community. While heterogeneously integrated III-V multi-quantum-well structures can provide optical gain under an electrical injection. In this project, we designed and fabricated the III-V-on-Si microcavity oscillators externally coupled with silicon waveguides and feedback mirrors or feedback delay lines. We developed the fabrication process of a heterogeneously integrated III-V-on-Si photonic platform. Based on the coupled-mode theoretical modelling, we studied the fundamental mechanisms of nonlinear dynamics in semiconductor microcavity oscillators when perturbed with external optical injection and with coherent optical feedback as a single processing node of a photonic reservoir. We characterized the time-series of the nonlinearly oscillated light outputs and diode currents of our fabricated devices.

16207620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207620.value: 在健康、環境、製造和基礎設施監控以及提升性能，效率和服務的方式上，物聯網（IoT）將為我們帶來一場革命。在本質上，傳感器，執行器，機器，可穿戴設備，車輛，機械人等將能夠連接到互聯網，從而成為我們信息網絡的一部分。但在物聯網實現的同時，我們亦面對許多挑戰，其中一個關鍵是如何為這些數量越來越多和體積越來越小的設備供電。電池也增加了重量，尺寸和成本，並且需要定時充電或更換，增加了維護的工作，這在數十億個物聯網設備上是很難實現的。 其中一個可為物聯網設備供電的解決方案是利用環境背向散射通信（AmBC）。AmBC與常規無線通信相比的優勢在於，它不需要電池，因為它在射頻環境中向後散射，重新利用和收集能量。此外，AmBC不需要任何頻率分配，因為它將現有的環境通信信號（如電視和無線網路）反向散射。 此外，AmBC亦不需要諸如閱讀器之類的任何基礎設備。但是，AmBC的設計存在不少挑戰，其中最關鍵的是其在AmBC 標籤的低強度反向散射信號和低採集能量。 在本研究計劃中，我們將對可重構的多天線技術和可重構的智能表面（RIS）進行研究，以此作為AmBC的低功率反向散射信號和低採集功率的解決方案。我們將特別研究使用可重構多天線的可能性，以增加來自AmBC標籤的反向散射，從而幫助解決低功率反向散射信號的挑戰。 另外，可重構的多個天線還可以增加AmBC標籤收集的能量。此外，我們可將可重構的多天線能量收集與AmBC通信整合在一起產生新的速率能量折衷。同時，我們亦研究將可重構的多個天線推廣到RIS，以增加AmBC標籤上可用的環境射頻功率。特別地，我們將提供可提升AmBC標籤接收功率的RIS。在所有擬議的研究中，該方法的重點將是同時應對天線和系統挑戰。這項研究的長期意義在於它可導致新的可實現無電池物聯網設備。

16207620.label: Realisation of objectives
16207620.value: The three objectives in this project have all been completed. The results for meeting objective 1 have provided two novel techniques based on multiple antenna systems to overcome the very low received power from ambient backscatter (AmBC) Tags and the high surrounding ambient interference [J1,J2]. Previous researchers have overcome the very low power and interference by averaging the received symbols over long time periods and subsequently using non-linear processing techniques based on averaging. The non-linear processing prevented the use of conventional detection techniques that need to be based on linear channels. To overcome this issue we developed a simplified, but accurate, AmBC channel linearization. This was achieved by removing second order terms (resulting from the non-linear processing) which were small in comparison to the linear terms in realistic AmBC operating regimes. With our channel linearization we could increase AmBC performance and help address the challenge of low power in these systems. In particular in output [J2] we describe the linear channel approach and investigate it through the perspective of multiple antennas and reconfigurable beamforming. We have obtained general results that provide bounds on the capacity, diversity and beamforming capability of multiple input multiple output (MIMO) based Tags. The work is different from conventional MIMO in that the power constraint is per antenna (instead of per system) and that effective channel is real [J2]. After completing this work we developed a very novel ratio AmBC receiver that avoided the averaging-based approach altogether. This receiver is based on a ratio approach where the ratio between multiple antennas at the receiver is utilised. This allows interference to be removed without requiring averaging and therefore performance can be greatly enhanced. It is shown in [J1] that a reduction in BER of 100x is achieved compared to the conventional averaging-based energy detectors. This is one of the first works to explore an alternative approach to averaging in AmBC detectors. To address objective 2 we looked into utilizing multiple antennas at the AmBC Tag where some of the antennas were used for energy harvesting and some are used for backscatter [C1]. This work is important as it further opens up the possibility of using multiple antennas at the AmBC Tag. In particular we developed an optimal antenna selection and time-sharing approach. This allows energy harvesting and backscatter to be allocated flexibly. In addition the optimal allocation of the Tag multiple antennas between harvesting and transmitting was also investigated using a block-coordinate descent guided exhaustive search. This was the first available work that looked into multiple antenna harvesting tradeoffs at the Tag and has been published in [C1]. To address objective 3 we investigated reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS). The use of RIS for AmBC performance enhancement is limited by the need for training the large number of RIS elements. This is a significant overhead, even in conventional RIS based communication systems. We have therefore focused on approaches that can reduce RIS training. Leveraging multiple antenna concepts we looked into results concerning mutual coupling between RIS elements to understand whether this can be used to reduce training. We have considered the grouping of elements together to understand the tradeoffs in RIS performance and have shown that a reduction in training without a large reduction in performance is possible. This technique can be applied to AmBC Tags by leveraging the channel state information at the detector to enhance the signals backscattered by the AmBC tags. The reduction in RIS training required can allow tradeoffs between the possible data throughput of the AmBC system and the training precision.

16207620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207620.value: Three significant research findings have arisen from this work and they are reported in [J1,J2,C1]. The first was the development of a linearised channel model for the analysis of AmBC systems as described in [J2]. This allows the application of conventional detection and signalling techniques to AmBC and therefore opens a whole new range of designs, tradeoffs and performance possibilities for AmBC. These possible designs have been explored with simulation results provided in [J2]. In addition we have explored numerically the capacity-diversity tradeoff in this work. Utilizing a linear channel approximation opens up AmBC systems to a whole new range of approaches and techniques and is therefore a significant contribution. The second significant finding was the application of the ratio detector to AmBC as described in [J1]. This is a novel contribution to AmBC and has not been previously considered by others. The technique allows removal of the standard averaging approach used in AmBC. The approach is to utilize at least two antennas at the receiver. The complex ratio of the two antennas is taken so that interference is removed while allowing maximum likelihood detection to deduce the AmBC Tag symbols. With more than 2 receive antennas various antenna combinations can also be taken to enhance performance further. The advantage is that bit rates can be increased because averaging over a large number of symbols is no longer required [J1]. Error performance is also improved. This is a significant contribution because the use of averaging is no longer needed and therefore opens up AmBC to new receiver designs. The third significant finding was the use of multiple antennas at the Tag and utilizing some of the antennas for energy harvesting and the remainder for backscatter in an optimal configuration as described in [C1]. The energy harvesting tradeoff increases the throughput possible in AmBC by adaptively selecting the optimum antenna configuration. The technique is useful because it considers ambient energy harvesting from additional antennas as an additional part of the AmBC system.

16207620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207620.value: Our techniques have opened the door to new approaches to meet the challenge of the low ambient energy and significant ambient interference in AmBC systems. The first area which could be explored further is our novel ratio detector [J1]. This is a new technique that promises significant performance improvement. Because the technique is new, we recommend that the circuit and system requirements for the detector be considered further with the ultimate aim of proving that a prototype could be developed for it. Another area for further investigation is the use of AmBC with RIS. While we have suggested techniques for overcoming the challenge of the RIS training overhead, tradeoffs between our techniques proposed [J1,J2,C1] and the use of RIS need to be explored. Finally, the multiple antenna energy harvesting techniques suggested in [C1] could also be considered further by integrating them with our novel detection approaches suggested in [J1,J2].

16207620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207620.value: Ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) promises battery free sensing and monitoring systems. However one major limitation of these techniques is the extremely low power that is available from the ambient RF signals in the environment and the high ambient interference from teh surrounding systems. To overcome this challenge we have developed new techniques to enhance the performance of AmBC systems. This has included the development of new receiver techniques, multiple antenna harvesting techniques and also a simplified but accurate method to analysis these systems. The approaches represent a promising step forward in AmBC systems that could be further explored by developing prototypes to verify the results.

16207820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207820.value: 网络表示可以构建实体之间的关系，并已经广泛应用在各个领域之中，比如生物学，金融，社会学，工程学和运筹学。在很多情形中，实体之间的关系是简单直接的。比如，两个人在社交网络中是朋友吗？两个学者在一篇文献中是合著者吗？两个节点在传感器网络中是相邻节点吗？这些关系在一个系统中是可以直接观察得到的。但是，在其它很多情况中，实体间的关系是无法直接清晰确定的，因而需要推理出来。比如，一个基因是否调控其它基因的表达？一个公司的交易方式是否影响另一个公司的股票价格？哪个药物改变了另一种药物的药理作用？ 从数据中推理网络的各种方法已经在很多领域中被广泛探索。这些方法在特定任务中使用了专业知识来推断和测量推理网络的质量。但是，当今的数据多样性以及日益增长的数据规模，对现有方法的有效性提出了严峻挑战。比如，现有算法的高计算复杂度在处理大规模且时变的数据时碰到了瓶颈。另外，很多算法要求数据同质性，这限制了从异构数据信息中推理网络的可能性。在实际中，用于构建实体关系的网络类型和推理算法的计算效率是决定这些方法适用性的关键因素。传统的数据表征网络的方法已经不足以应对从现代应用中带来的挑战。总而言之，为了利用当今前所未有的数据无处不在的机会，有必要开发新颖的数据驱动、数据自适应方法来从数据中推理网络表示。 该拟议的项目将开发一套基于数据驱动的优化框架和算法技术，以解决几个关键的网络推理问题。拟开发的技术包括： 1. 将网络表示建模成规范化的拉普拉斯矩阵估计问题以应用于深度学习中；2. 寻找适用于大规模时变网络推理的低计算复杂度的在线优化方法；3. 确定对于具有异构数据的一组实体的网络推理和恢复。相关的初步工作已经得到了令人鼓舞的结果。

16207820.label: Realisation of objectives
16207820.value: The realization of objectives in this project focused on advancing data-driven methods for large-scale network inference. The primary aim was to develop novel optimization frameworks and algorithmic techniques to address key challenges in network inference, particularly when dealing with large-scale and heterogeneous data. The project successfully achieved its main objectives, which were: - Normalized Laplacian Estimation for Machine Learning Applications: This objective involved proposing formulations for learning structured normalized Laplacian network models by leveraging the spectral properties of graphs. The development of optimization methods based on a block coordinate descent approach was crucial, offering low computational complexity and fast convergence. - Stochastic Optimization for Large-Scale Time-Varying Network Inference: A stochastic framework was designed to handle large-scale, time-varying networks. This involved developing stochastic online optimization methods capable of efficiently solving the underlying optimization problems. - Sparse Network Completion and Inference with Heterogeneous Attributes: This objective aimed at developing a semi-supervised learning and optimization framework to infer networks with heterogeneous attributes and partially known connections, focusing on sparse graph learning. In addition to these primary objectives, the project also accomplished several supplementary goals: - Learning Graphs Under Heavy Tails: Algorithms were developed for graph learning in heavy-tailed settings, overcoming challenges posed by nonconvexities in such environments. - Optimization Methods Incorporating High-Order Statistics: New methods were devised to incorporate high-order statistics into optimization formulations, enhancing applications such as portfolio design. - Characterization and Imputation of Missing Values: Techniques were developed for characterizing and imputing missing values in datasets with heavy-tailed distributions, improving the robustness of network inference methods. These achievements not only fulfilled the project's original goals but also expanded its scope, contributing significantly to the field of network inference through innovative methodologies and practical algorithmic solutions.

16207820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207820.value: The project achieved significant advancements in network inference methodologies, focusing on data-driven optimization frameworks. Key outcomes include the development of novel algorithms for estimating network representations as normalized Laplacians, particularly useful for deep learning applications. These algorithms addressed challenges associated with large-scale and time-varying networks by introducing low-cost online optimization methods. Additionally, the project tackled network inference and completion for entities with heterogeneous data, providing robust solutions for real-world applications where data homogeneity cannot be assumed. The publication output is substantial, comprising several high impact works: 1 book chapter in a Springer book, 5 IEEE journal papers, and 12 conference papers (including 4 NeurIPS papers, 1 ICML paper, and 1 AAAI paper, all of which are commonly considered in the machine learning community at the same level, if not higher, than journal publications). In addition, several open-source software packages (spectralGraphTopology, mtp2, sparseGraph, and fingraph) under the programming language R (commonly used in statistics, machine learning, and finance). See https://github.com/convexfi for the group software webpage. The algorithms demonstrated superior performance compared to state-of-the-art benchmarks in extensive experimental evaluations. Overall, the project contributed significantly to the literature by providing scalable solutions for graph learning under heavy-tailed data distributions and sparse network structures. These innovations have broad implications across domains such as finance, biology, and engineering, where network inference plays a critical role.

16207820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207820.value: The project's outcomes highlight promising avenues for future research. One key direction is the learning of time-varying graphs under more robust consistency metrics. This involves developing methodologies that can accurately capture the dynamic nature of networks over time, ensuring that the learned graphs are consistent with observed data patterns. Such advancements could significantly improve the understanding and prediction of complex systems where time-variability is a critical factor. Another important direction is the learning of sparse clustered graphs while controlling the balance of cluster sizes. This research aims to refine clustering techniques by ensuring that identified clusters are not only sparse but also balanced in size, which is crucial for applications requiring equitable partitioning of data, such as resource allocation and community detection in large networks.

16207820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207820.value: Network representations are crucial for understanding relationships between entities across various domains, such as biology, finance, and engineering. While some relationships are straightforward, like friendships in social networks or collaborations in research, others require inference, such as gene regulation or financial market interactions. This project has focused on developing data-driven methods for inferring large-scale network structures where direct observations are not possible. By employing techniques like normalized Laplacian estimation and stochastic optimization, the project has achieved to develop efficient algorithms that can handle the complexity and scale of modern data. These methods are particularly useful for networks with heterogeneous attributes and time-varying characteristics. The project's innovations include frameworks for sparse network completion and inference, which are essential for managing large datasets with incomplete information. The outcomes promise to enhance our ability to model complex systems accurately and efficiently, providing valuable insights into the underlying structures of diverse datasets.
