16208920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208920.value: The potential for further development of this research is vast and promising. Future studies can be expanded to include more variables and scenarios, such as the impact of emerging technologies like autonomous shared vehicle driving and its integration with public transit systems. Additionally, exploring dual-services of ride-sourcing platforms, such as combining goods and passenger transport, or incorporating public roles like emergency ambulance services or security, can significantly enhance the versatility and appeal of ride-sourcing services. To achieve these advancements, it is essential to establish partnerships with academic institutions, industry stakeholders, and government agencies to foster collaborative research efforts. Seeking funding from government grants, private sector investments, and international research programs will support further research and pilot projects, ensuring sustainability and scalability. By following this proposed course of action, the research can continue to contribute to the advancement of sustainable and efficient multi-modal transportation systems.

16208920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208920.value: This research delves into the intricate relationship between ride-sourcing services like Uber and public transportation systems, exploring how they can complement or substitute each other. The goal is to understand how these services interact, what strategies can enhance their operation, and ultimately improve urban mobility. By using mathematical models and data analysis, the research examines the effects of ride-sourcing on public transit usage, proposes strategies to optimize operations, and investigates cooperation between service providers and governments. The significance lies in the potential to create a more efficient, user-friendly, and sustainable transportation network. The research aims to reduce traffic congestion, increase accessibility, and improve service quality for passengers. Practical strategies derived from this study can help transportation companies maximize profits while benefiting public welfare, making urban travel smoother and more reliable. This work's value is enormous for city planners, policymakers, and transportation providers who seek to leverage modern mobility solutions to enhance urban living standards, reduce environmental impact, and offer better services to residents. It bridges the gap between traditional public transit and innovative ride-sourcing services, creating a harmonious, multi-modal transportation ecosystem.

16209120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209120.value: 基于边缘的可扩展和隐私保护的联邦学习

16209120.label: Project Objectives
16209120.value: Improving the efficiency of federated learning on non-IID data. Federated learning has been shown to perform poorly in terms of the speed of convergence and model accuracy due to the presence of non-IID (independent and identically distributed) data across devices given the different user preferences and device usage patterns. We seek to significantly improve the performance of federated learning by using deep reinforcement learning techniques to strategically select an optimal set of participating devices in each round of training; Scheduling resources for federated learning across a large collection of edge devices. We propose to select a large number of participating devices by reducing the amount of time taken in each iteration of training, and reducing the number of iterations at the same time. In particular, we propose to offload some of the computation to emerging serverless cloud computing platforms, such as AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Functions; Preserving data privacy and model robustness in federated learning. As edge devices are inherently more vulnerable to malicious attacks and leaks, it is critically important to guarantee both the privacy of user data and the model robustness against malicious attacks. In term of user privacy, we will propose new local differential privacy mechanisms to safeguard federated learning systems from typical white-box and black-box attacks such as member inference attacks. In terms of model robustness, we will study how model compression — as well as other communication-efficient techniques — affects model robustness, and how model robustness interacts with local differential privacy mechanisms; Creating real-world implementations and open-source releases. We will develop and evaluate a new open-source implementation of our proposed techniques based on TensorFlow Federated. To guarantee reproducibility, we will release the dataset and all the scripts used in our performance evaluations, so that all our results can be scientifically reproduced by other researchers.

16209120.label: Realisation of objectives
16209120.value: In the era of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), numerous smart devices from cameras, smartphones to sensing devices, have been designed to collaborate autonomously with one another. With the increasing concerns and regulatory requirements on data privacy, Federated Learning (FL) paradigm becomes a promising approach to train machine learning (ML) models in a collaborative manner without exposing client private data. The current FL frameworks, however, have largely adopted a two-layer client-server architecture that utilizes only a single centralized FL server, which needs to deal with a potentially large number of clients in the context of AIoT. This raises serious scaling problem as well as privacy vulnerability issues. Moreover, this is further challenged in that a shared global model presented by the existing FL framework may not satisfy the individual needs of different clients. This project improves the scalability of FL by utilizing data from numerous participating clients in training workloads. The realization builds upon our proposed three-layer hierarchical architecture with the inclusion of edge servers. The inclusion of edge servers brings three fundamental benefits, (1) it substantially reduces the amount of model update traffic needed to be sent to the central FL server, (2) it improves the scalability of FL systems, and (3) it mitigates the privacy leakage problem by keeping the model updates within the boundaries of edge servers, i.e., for instance within an institution. The three-layer hierarchical architecture we proposed consists of a central server, edge servers, often at the boundary of an institution, and a large number of smart devices. Each client device, upon receiving the current global model from its institution, i.e., a corresponding edge server passed from the central server, the client conducts local training utilizing only its local dataset to update the model and sends its updated model to the edge server. Each edge server aggregates models from its clients and transfers the aggregated model to the central server. The central server then generates an updated global model by aggregating all institutions’ aggregated models. There are several technical challenges in this new architecture. First, there are frequent exchanges of model weights throughout the training process that may easily lead to massive communication overhead. The limited and unstable network connections of clients, typical in the federated learning environment, further exacerbate the problem and result in a long training time. Moreover, it is common in real world applications that clients’ local datasets are non-IID (not independent and identically distributed). We design and implement a novel mechanism based on pruning technique, which is shown to be able to significantly reduce the communication overhead with negligible degradation in global model accuracy. Specifically, our rigorous analysis indicates that the weight difference between each institution’s aggregated model and the current global model is directly related to the global model performance. Based on this result, with proper adjustment, the pruning method we proposed opts to prune local model updates instead of local model weights, and the results demonstrate that the global model trained with pruning can converge to higher accuracy only with fewer training iterations, even in the situation when clients have highly skewed non-IID local datasets. In addition, we implement our proposed pruning technique on PLATO, our open-source research framework for scalable federated learning and conduct extensive experiments. The empirical investigations confirm the promising potential of pruning on boosting communication efficiency with an insignificant reduction on global model accuracy. To train a high-quality global model, it has been widely recognized that the aggregation on the central server plays a critical role. In our proposed architecture, it is important to notice that the quality of contributions from local training on different edge devices can be substantially different. Existing mechanisms for quantifying the model quality are intuitively based on training loss or model parameters, which fail to capture the effect of highly variable data and heterogeneous resources available on participating client devices. We propose a new aggregation mechanism that utilizes deep reinforcement learning to dynamically evaluate the quality of model updates. By dynamically mapping the quality of local models to their importance during model aggregation, the training process can converge towards the direction of better effectiveness and generalization. We show this outperforms its state-of-the-art counterparts that employ different aggregation strategies on a suite of federated learning applications with faster convergence and more stable learning progress even in extreme heterogeneity. “The right to be forgotten” in recent privacy legislation, such as the GDPR, grants users a right to request their private data be deleted. This allows trained machine learning models to forget the data to be removed. Federated unlearning, which erases a client’s entire or part of data from the global model, can help improve the flexibility and reliability of FL systems. There are several unique challenges in federated unlearning. For example, there are many cases in federated learning where only a portion of a client’s data is requested to be removed in contrast to the scenario that a client completely opts out of the current FL session. Different clients may have similar, or to some extent, shared training samples. In this case, removing all or part of the data of a client from the global model will affect the performance of the unlearned model on the remaining data of other clients. We are the first to notice and investigate the information leakage risk problem induced by the discrepancy between the models before and after unlearning in the context of federated unlearning. We study the inherent vulnerability of the federated unlearning paradigm under membership inference attacks. We also examine the potential of widely used defense against membership inference attacks and provide insights for improving the privacy-preserving nature of federated unlearning mechanisms Finally, we have designed and fully implemented an open-source federated learning (FL) platform – Plato (https://github.com/TL-System/plato). Since the completion of the previous report, we have added support for a large collection of FL algorithms, most of them have no prior open-source implementations including: (1) our proposed server aggregation mechanisms, which the server runs to adjust its weights when aggregating client updates to produce a shared global model; (2) client training loop customization mechanisms, designed to calibrate local updates on the clients during local training, so to help contribute to improving the global model; (3) client selection mechanisms, designed for the server to improve its training performance by selecting clients with higher data quality in each round; (4) personalized federated learning mechanisms, designed to train models that are personalized to produce high validation accuracies on the specific dataset at each client device, while still being able to benefit from collaborative training over a shared global model; (5) communication-efficient federated learning mechanisms, designed to mitigate the communication overhead during the training process, by pruning, compressing, or quantizing the model at each client before sending updates to the server; (6) attack and defence mechanisms: attacks are launched by adversaries to reconstruct the raw private data on the clients, and defence mechanisms are designed to guard against or detect such attacks.

16209120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209120.value: The proposed three-layer hierarchical FL architecture presents a promising solution to accommodate a potentially enormous number of clients in coping with the scaling issue, while considerably reducing the model update communication overhead that need to be routed to the central server for aggregation. We start by implementing PLATO, an open-source framework for scalable federated learning from scratch and use that to conduct extensive experiments of applying a popular compression technique in machine learning, pruning methods, to compress models and investigate how to improve the communication efficiency. The results of our empirical study suggest that even a simple pruning method, L1-norm unstructured pruning, can significantly reduce the communication overhead with negligible degradation in model accuracy. We design a new pruning mechanism, which prunes local model updates instead of local model weights, and we demonstrate that the global model trained with this method can converge to higher accuracy with fewer training iterations, especially when clients have highly skewed non-IID local datasets. We proceed to conduct mathematical analysis of the impact on the shared global model, and we find that the epoch numbers of clients’ local training can significantly affect the global model performance. Based on the analysis, we devise a new framework to adaptively tune clients’ epoch numbers based on the differences between their institutions’ aggregated models and the current global model. The evaluation under real network environments indicates this can increase the global model accuracy while reducing the number of required training iterations and the elapsed training time. We investigate the problem of machine unlearning in FL environment, where data holders are collaboratively performing training and unlearning without sharing raw data. Erasing data samples from a trained FL model turns out to be particularly challenging for two reasons, (1) the interactive nature of the FL training, in which clients continuously share the knowledge learned from their local dataset with other clients via model aggregation; (2) FL training is an incremental procedure in which any given local update reflects all past updates that occurred at the client. We believe that the best approach for data erasure in FL is to perform retraining among all data holders, so as to completely eliminate the contributions of data samples to be removed. We propose an efficient and effective retraining algorithm and conduct extensive evaluations on four real-world datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of our proposed realization.

16209120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209120.value: The proposed hierarchical FL architecture should be considered as a work in progress towards the realization of the full potential of FL paradigm. One detriment is that it is practically difficult to collect trace data and performance in real world FL setting, which are largely unavailable publicly. One aspect worth further exploration is a fair and comprehensive investigation on the FL convergence performance, as existing methods are exclusively evaluated in their own proprietary simulation or emulation testbed, which are usually biased. Our open-source PLATO framework fills this gap in providing a reproducible FL framework under a consistent set of performance metrics, especially two most relevant metrics, model convergence time and accuracy. Another avenue for the future work is that we believe the potential of information leakage in federated unlearning still remains as a critical challenge, as it defeats the purpose of performing the unlearning process in the first place. There is a pressing need for improving resilience against enhanced membership inference attacks and other privacy attacks. In addition, it would be theoretically interesting to study how resilient this category of unlearning mechanisms perform against privacy attacks.

16209120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209120.value: Federated Learning (FL) promises to train machine learning (ML) models in a collaborative manner across different client devices without exposing their private data. The current FL frameworks largely adopt a two-layer client-server architecture that engages only a single centralized FL server for model aggregation, which needs to deal with a potentially large number of clients in the context of AIoT. This raises serious scaling problems as well as privacy vulnerability issues. Moreover, this is further challenged by the fact that a shared global model presented by the existing FL framework may not satisfy the individual needs of different clients. The significance of this project and its outcomes are mainly two-folded: (1) we introduce a novel three-layer hierarchical FL architecture with the inclusion of edge servers, which effectively enhances the scalability by reducing the volume of model updates to the central FL server through new aggregation algorithms, while at the time mitigating the privacy leakage issue; (2) we successfully build and implement an open-source FL framework - PLATO, which is not only scalable to support numerous clients, but also extensible to accommodate different datasets, models, and learning algorithms.

16209220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209220.value: 毫米波雷達已經成為許多應用的有前途的解決方案，包括目標檢測，天氣特徵和人類生命體徵，並且具有極高的分辨率和準確性。其中，汽車雷達由於其出色的檢測能力和對環境條件的魯棒性，作為高級駕駛員輔助系統（ADAS）和自動駕駛汽車中的一項關鍵技術，變得越來越有吸引力。將來，將在車輛中安裝許多此類雷達，以提供高分辨率的4D信息，以實現更多的安全功能，例如防撞，盲點檢測，自適應巡航控制和交叉交通警報。 同時，隨著互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）技術的最新進展和大規模擴展，在CMOS工藝中以高集成度和低成本實現緊湊的完全集成高性能毫米波雷達變得更加可行。頻率合成器是至關重要的組成部分，它最終決定了此類雷達系統的性能，並且需要在寬頻率範圍內產生快速而線性的頻率調製。 在此項目中，我們建議開發一種用於77 GHz汽車雷達的調頻連續波（FMCW）頻率合成器，該器在大帶寬，高線性和快速線性調頻方面具有高性能。該合成器將以標準的數字CMOS工藝進行設計和製造，以實現最高集成度和最低成本。將選擇合適的合成器體系結構，對於該體系結構，將根據77 GHz汽車雷達的實際要求確定一些裕度的系統規格。因此，將得出每個構件的規格。將開發新穎的電路設計技術，並將設計，佈置，製造和測試關鍵的構建模塊。最後，完整的FMCW合成器將以最先進的性能進行集成，製造和演示。

16209220.label: Realisation of objectives
16209220.value: All the proposed objectives for the project have been fully achieved, including the original Objective #5 to integrate and demonstrate complete FMCW synthesizer systems that had been removed in the revised version Specifically, two novel system architectures have been proposed and demonstrated for FMCW synthesizers. In addition, many advanced design techniques have been proposed, designed, and some were successfully integrated and demonstrated in the synthesizers: • Magnetic tuning techniques were proposed for both coarse tuning or fine tuning for high-performance oscillators. • Automatic successive phase calibration and automatic frequency-domain duty-cycle calibration for multiple-phase non-50%-duty-cycle nonoverlapping LO generator. • An on-chip transformer-based six-port balanced-to-unbalanced quadrature hybrid coupler (QHBC). • A Type-II digital PLL with zero chirp-rate-independent TDC offset, TDC-gain-independent loop bandwidth, a high-resolution glitch-free wideband linear digitally controlled oscillator (DCO). • Bandwidth-extension and phase-noise cancellation techniques. The project has not only contributed to advancement of the field but also resulted in many good publications in the flagship journals and conferences in the research area as further described and detailed in Section 6.

16209220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209220.value: • Magnetic tuning techniques were proposed for both coarse tuning or fine tuning for high-performance oscillators to achieve ultra-wide frequency tuning range and low phase noise without a need for varactors with low quality factor Q at high frequencies. The techniques were demonstrated and published in several journals, including TVSLI May 22 (Journal Paper #1), TCAS II June 22 (Journal Paper #2), and TTST Jan 23 (Journal Paper #3). • A 10.8–14.5-GHz eight-phase 12.5%-duty-cycle nonoverlapping LO generator is proposed. A four-stage ring oscillator (RO) is followed by reconfigurable injection-locked-oscillator NOR gates to generate eight-phase 12.5%-duty-cycle signals featuring automatic successive phase calibration and automatic frequency domain duty-cycle calibration. The work was published in RFIC June 21 (Conference Paper #1), RFIC June 23 (Conference Paper #2) and JSSC May 2024 (Journal Paper #5). • The first on-chip transformer-based six-port balanced-to-unbalanced quadrature hybrid coupler (QHBC) was proposed and demonstrated. The proposed six-port QHBC employs three transformers to replace eight-inductor design in conventional LC-based couplers for miniaturization. The work was published in SSCL July 24 (Journal Paper #4). • Finally, two FMCW synthesizers were successfully proposed, integrated, and demonstrated with state-of-the-art performance, in terms of bandwidth, phase noise, and linearity. In addition to novel system architectures, the two synthesizers also featured many design techniques for building blocks. The designs were published in RFIC June 2024 (Conference Papers #3 and #4).

16209220.value: It would be interesting and useful although challenging to follow up the project to integrate the proposed frequency synthesizers with the other building blocks, including low-noise amplifiers, mixers, power amplifiers, to realize high-performance transceiver systems for high-resolution high-bandwidth FMCW radars.

16209220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209220.value: • The research project has contributed significantly to the advancement of the state-of-the-art performance in the field of high-performance frequency synthesizers and their building blocks for FMCW radars. Frequency synthesizers suitable for FMCW radars with state-of-the-art performance in terms of frequency, bandwidth, phase noise, linearity, and/or power consumption were demonstrated and paved the way to realize high-resolution low-phase-noise low-power FMCW radar systems.

16209320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209320.value: Firms are increasingly shifting their focus from products to product-service system, as the ancillary service is able to facilitate the consumption of base products. During the transformation to servitization, the product market competition is complicated by asymmetric service capability among firms. In current business practice, the firm with service capability might design specific pricing policy for the ancillary service or even choose to prohibit the competitor's consumers from using its service. This research proposal aims to understand the implication of designing optimal service policy by the focal firm with service capability. We identify the trade-off between efficient service provision and competition intensity when designing the optimal service policy. Based on our preliminary results, we plan to build a general model to study the endogenous product design, to investigate the hidden price and compatibility issues in implementing the service policy, to explore the policy impacts on supply chain performance and market entry, and to discuss some potential regulations to enhance social welfare. Moreover, these theoretical results would be backed by an empirical study using the transaction-level data, to maintain the external validity of the research project. 产品附加服务可以提高人们对实体产品的消费，基于此， 越来越多的企业从单纯的实体产品设计发展到产品和附加服务一体化设计。在向产品附加服务转化的过程中, 各个企业受限于不同的附加服务能力，这种不对称性给产品市场竞争带来挑战。在目前的实践中，有的企业针对产品附加服务制定专有的定价策略，有的甚至选择禁止竞争对手的消费者使用其增值服务。 这项研究旨在帮助企业更好的了解如何设计最优产品附加服务策略。我们首先明确了在制定最优产品附件服务策略时，必须要权衡有效服务和竞争强度二者之间的矛盾。 我们计划建立一个通用模型来研究产品附加服务，以分析增值服务带来的隐形价格和服务兼容性的问题，从而进一步探讨产品附加服务对供需链和市场准入策略的影响，并且讨论可行的规范以提高社会福利。基于这些理论研究的成果，我们还计划用企业销售交易的具体数据，开展实证研究。

16209820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209820.value: It has recently become possible to culture cells such that they can grow into a 3D cell mass that resembles an organ with microanatomical structure and consisting of multiple organ-specific cell types. These so-called organoids are usually derived from a few embryonic stem cells (ESCs) or induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) that are grown in culture and can self-renew and differentiate in culture to form the organ-like structures. Today there are many approaches for creating organoids representing a myriad of organs, including the intestines, brain, kidney, heart, stomach, and many more. Most intriguingly, organoids not only recapitulate features of the normal organ, they can also capture disease-associated features; thus increasingly they are used to understand biological mechanisms in disease, and for drug screening and therapeutic target discovery. Many disease model organoids are being developed; currently, these organoids are largely grown in liquid culture. However, it is difficult to deliberately organize or guide developmental anatomy during their formation, and to control the microenvironment of the organoids such as vascularization, specific 3D geometry and structure. One of the critical tissue complexities that need to be addressed first is the vasculature of the tissue constructs. Integration of the vasculature is essential if the organoid is to grow larger, in which case it becomes difficult for nutrients and oxygen to reach the center of the tissue mass. Without vasculature, the core of the organoids cannot survive. This eventually leads to the short lifespan of tissue constructs. Multiple studies have shown that in-vivo, microenvironments and niches can greatly impact the growth and vascularization of organs, which begs the question: if we could more closely replicate the in-vivo microenvironment, could we also direct vascular growth to more closely resemble primary human tissue? Efforts are ongoing to incorporate the vasculature into the organoids using microfluidic platforms, containing miniature chambers that can be controlled independently. In this project, we will design a microfluidic platform for organoid culture, creating a tunable microenvironment that promotes controllable vasculature formation. We will incorporate novel functionalized synthetic hydrogels into the microfluidic platform to better control the distribution and patterning of signaling molecules to enable a truly customizable microenvironment. Then, we will determine the effect of these microenvironmental cues such as on vasculature growth by measuring features such as size/diameter, permeability, perfusability, and interconnectedness, as well as by profiling and comparing their gene expression. 研究摘要 培養細胞以使其生長成類似微解剖結構的器官，並由多種器官的特異性細胞組成3D細胞團，在近年來逐漸成為可能。生成這些類器官通常可以通過誘導胚胎幹細胞（ESC）或多能幹細胞（iPSC）的體外發育，使它們能在培養基中生長和自我更新，進而分化形成像器官一樣的結構。如今，人們可以通過許多方法來產生多種含有器官關鍵特性的類器官，成功被培植出的類器官包括腸，腦，腎，心臟，胃等。最有趣的是，這些類器官不僅涵蓋正常器官的特徵，還擁有與疾病相關的特徵。因此，類器官越來越多地被應用到研究疾病的生物學機制、藥物篩選和靶標治療領域。許多疾病模型的類器官也正在被研發。目前，這些類器官主要生長在液體培養基中。但是，在類器官形成過程中，有意地組織和誘導細胞發育成具有像體內的生理組織結構是非常困難的。要形成這樣的組織結構需要去調控類器官的微環境，例如保持類器官內的血管形成和灌注，還有塑造組織特定的3D幾何形狀與結構。 這其中一個極待解決的關鍵性問題就是類器官內血管系統的組織構造與灌注。如果類器官要生長，那麼血管系統的整合必不可少，在這種情況下，營養素和氧氣很難到達組織塊的中心。如果沒有血管系統，類器官的核心將無法生存，最終導致組織構建物的壽命很短。經多項體內研究表明，體內的微環境和生態位會極大地影響器官的生長和血管灌注，由此引申出了另一個問題：如果我們能更精密在體外培植時複製體內微環境，我們是否能使血管的生長更接近原本的人體組織呢？我們正致力於使用擁有獨立控制微腔室的微流體平臺裝置，將血管系統整合到類器官中。在該研究項目中，我們將設計用於類器官培養的微流體平臺，以創建可調控的微環境，從而促進可控血管系統的形成。同時，我們將新型功能合成水凝膠導入微流體平臺，以更好地控制生物信號分子的分佈，從而真正實現可控制的微環境。然後，我們通過測量尺寸/直徑，通透性，灌注性和互聯性等特徵，以及分析和比較基因的表達，確定微環境誘導對血管系統生長的影響。

16210020.label: Project Objectives
16210020.value: To develop a general framework of using pricing to stabilize the grand coalition in cooperative games with empty core. In our preliminary study, we have formulated the problem into inverse optimization, and proposed two possible approaches to solve the basic problem. However, there are still some open questions, such as the feasibility issue, integration with other instruments, and the possibility of adjusting other parameters in the game. Answering such questions will substantially extend the scope of the applicability of the framework. To design pricing mechanisms for collaborative logistics coordinated by 4PL. In particular, we will study the problem of last mile delivery by multiple 3PLs where each 3PL has a set of orders to deliver. The collaboration of 3PLs can be formulated into vehicle routing game which known to have an empty core. 4PL has access to full information of the involved shippers, carriers, and customers. Therefore, 4PL can make centralized decisions at a reduced cost. 4PL collaborative logistics game features a more complicated relationship among the players. To ensure the sustainable development of collaborative logistics, all stakeholders shall share the benefits of reduced cost fairly. For this, incentive mechanism design is necessary. We propose to stabilize the game through pricing the demands, as well as other extended decisions. To provide sharing mechanisms to vehicle platooning games. Although vehicle platooning has demonstrated its technological readiness, not enough operational models are available to stimulate the sustainable participation of vehicles. Our work will fill this gap by providing appropriate mechanisms for participating vehicles to fairly share the benefits of platooning. This will foster the sustainable development of vehicle platooning. Our preliminary results show that the vehicle platooning game exhibits a structure that is different from the general framework, thereby requiring specific mechanisms to stabilize the game.

16210020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210020.value: Cooperative game theory involves the collaboration of multiple decision makers. If all decision makers collaborate to form a grand coalition, then a centralized optimal decision can be made. Furthermore, the payoff of the centralized optimal decision needs to be reasonably allocated to each of the individual decision makers. This issue is addressed by the concept of the core which, roughly speaking, is the set of allocations under which no subset of players can be better off by leaving the grand coalition. Many cooperative games have an empty core, and their grand coalitions are unstable. For such games, certain external instruments can be designed to stabilize the grand coalition in the literature, such as subsidizing the grand coalition and penalizing any subcoalition that deviates from the grand coalition. In this project, we propose a new instrument for a class of games in which players need certain services provided by a service provider. This service provider can decide the price of the service, which in turn determines the cost structure of the coalition. When the game has an empty core, the service provider can use pricing to adjust the cost structure to make the core nonempty. A stable grand coalition benefits not only the players but also the service provider by making the service more competitive. The pricing-based instrument can be used in different applications, e.g., collaborative logistics and vehicle platooning. In collaborative logistics, different models have been proposed for shippers and 3PLs to collaborate. In the particular situation where multiple 3PLs are used for last mile delivery, it often leads to TSP/VRP games with empty cores. We will address this issue by a new model in which a 4PL may use delivery order pricing to stabilize the grand coalition. Vehicle platooning is a type of collaborative driving for multiple vehicles, where a major incentive to vehicles is to save on fuel. Since the level of fuel saved for each vehicle depends on its position in the platoon, it raises the issue of cost sharing. We study a particular problem of platooning on a tollway, where the tollway operator may adjust toll fees to stabilize vehicle platooning. In our preliminary study, we formally defined the problem in its general form, formulated the problem as inverse optimization, and proposed two solutions. In the current project, we will continue studying the general problem, but our main effort will be on the abovementioned applications. 合作博弈理論研究多個決策者的協作問題。如果所有決策者一起組成一個大聯盟，則可以做出全局最佳決策。基本問題在於如何把全局最佳收益合理地分配給每個決策者，保證任何子聯盟得到的收益不低於其離開大聯盟得到的收益。這樣的分配方案稱為核心分配。許多合作博弈不存在核心分配，意味著大聯盟不能穩定存在。對於此類問題，我們可以設計某些外部機制來確保大聯盟穩定，例如，補貼大聯盟，並對不參加大聯盟的任何子聯盟徵收費用。 本研究項目將針對一類合作博弈問題提供一種新的穩定大聯盟的機制。具體地講，所有決策者的問題都基於一個服務提供商提供的某些服務。該服務提供者可以決定服務的價格，從而影響聯盟的成本結構。當博弈不存在核心分配時，該服務提供商可以使用定價來調整成本結構，以形成核心分配， 從而穩定大聯盟，使服務更具競爭力，從而使博弈參與者及服務提供商均受益。 基於定價的機制可以用於不同的場合，例如協作物流和車輛編隊。協作物流有不同模式。在第三方物流的最後一公里配送問題中，通常核心分配不存在。我們將通過一種新模型來解決此問題，在該模型中，一個第四方物流可以使用交貨單定價來穩定大聯盟。車輛編隊行駛可以節省燃料。但每輛車節省的燃油量取決於其在編隊中的位置，這帶來了成本分攤的問題。我們將研究在收費公路上的編隊行駛，公路運營商可以通過調整通行費以穩定車輛編隊。 在我們的初步研究中，我們已經定義了問題一般形式，將問題表述為逆優化，並提出了兩種解決方案。在此研究項目中，我們將繼續繼續研究一般形式的解， 並在此基礎上給出上述兩個應用的方案。

16210020.label: Realisation of objectives
16210020.value: The project aims to design mechanisms to stabilize the grand collaboration for cooperative games with empty cores. There are three objectives in the project, one focusing on developing a general theoretic model, and the other two studying the application and extensions in two specific areas. All objectives have been achieved with details elaborated as follows. The first objective is to develop a general framework of adjusting existing cost coefficients of an unbalanced game under which the game becomes balanced, and the total cost to be shared by the grand coalition is within a prescribed range. We formulate the problem on how to optimize the cost adjustment as a constrained inverse optimization problem. Based on linear programming reformulations, we develop two solution algorithms running on polynomial time under certain conditions. The first one is a cutting-plane algorithm for the case where the corresponding separation problem is polynomial time solvable; and the other one for the case when the linear program contains only a polynomial number of inequalities. The second objective is to study the collaborations in the last-mile delivery. We have investigated several applications that benefit from cooperation. One is the classic facility location game where we show it possible to modify the cost terms to ensure that the games become balanced. Another one is the sharing of deposit lockers for different third-party delivery companies, where we show how competing delivers can share the lockers which are provided by an independent locker company. We have further extended the research to the adoption of drones in the last mile delivery, in particular, how to coordinate the drones schedule and the existing delivery modes to improve the delivery punctuality, in both general package delivery and meal delivery. The third objective is to study the stability of vehicle platooning, a new driving mode that allows for multiple vehicles to be driven cooperatively. We consider the platooning formation process of teams among stochastic arrivals, whose collaborative stability and cooperative structure are critical to both the system efficiency and the profitability of the service provider. We establish stability conditions for cooperation among stochastically arriving individuals, based on which we characterize the structure of the optimal strategy for the service provider to maximize long-term reward while stabilizing cooperation through managing the service charge. We prove that for a representative class of reward functions, the service provider's optimization problem reduces to selecting a target team size, which can be solved in polynomial time. Overall, the project generates four papers, one published in INFORMS Journal on Computing, one published in European Journal of Operational Research, one under major revision with Naval Research Logistics, and one under review with Operations Research.

16210020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210020.value: Many cooperative games have an empty core, indicating that a grand collaboration is not stable. This project aims to design models and algorithms to stabilize grand collaboration in cooperative games with empty cores. Below are the major results we have achieved. First, we consider the class of integer optimization games, which includes many cooperative games defined based on operations research problems. We propose a new approach that allows us to adjust existing cost coefficients of the game, ensuring (i) the game becomes balanced, stabilizing the grand coalition, (ii) a desired mode of cooperation is optimal for the grand coalition to adopt, and (iii) the total cost to be shared by the grand coalition remains within a prescribed range. Our main contributions include formulating the problem of optimizing cost adjustments as a constrained inverse optimization problem, discussing the complexity of these problems, and developing polynomial-time algorithms to solve the problem under certain conditions. These results are documented in a paper published in the INFORMS Journal on Computing [RO-Item-8.1]. We have also investigated collaborations in last-mile delivery across various applications. For the classic routing-based problem, we study a facility location game, demonstrating it as a typical case of the inverse optimization approach [RO-Item-8.1]. Additionally, we address the sharing of lockers among different third-party delivery companies, showing how an independent locker operator can coordinate, by setting the rental price, the usage of lockers [RO-Item-10.2]. Our research further extends to the adoption of drones in last-mile delivery, where we are interested in the concept of drone resupply in the implementation of coordinating drones with existing delivery modes, both for on-time general package delivery [RO-Items-8.2, 9.1] and real-time meal delivery [RO-Items-8.3, 9.2]. Lastly, we have studied the stability of vehicle platooning, a new driving mode that leads to lower fuel consumption, shorter vehicle-to-vehicle distances, and higher speeds. Typically, the benefit of each individual vehicle depends on the position in the platoon, and thus the fairness issue is raised. As such, the formation of platooning aligns with the principles of cooperative game theory; however, its dynamic nature extends beyond the standard cooperative game model. To address this challenge, we define an extended cooperative game with new concepts of stability. Our research indicates that, on a toll way, a toll collector can design pricing schedules to incentivize stable platooning, benefiting both vehicles and toll collectors [RO-Item-8.4, 9.3].

16210020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210020.value: This research project focuses on improving cooperation among groups in situations where working together is difficult or unstable. Cooperative game theory shows that many operations management problems, when involving multiple stakeholders in the decision making process, can end up with no stable agreement, making collaboration challenging. Our project aims to create methods and tools that help these groups find stable solutions, ensuring everyone benefits. We specifically looked at problems in areas like delivery services and vehicle platooning (where cars drive closely together to save fuel). By adjusting costs and finding optimal ways to share resources and the resulted benefit, we can help these groups work together more effectively. The significance of this research lies in both theoretical research and practical relevance. Specifically, it enhances the scope of cooperative game theory with its potential to enhance efficiency in real-world applications, such as last-mile delivery and traffic management. This could lead to lower costs, faster deliveries, and reduced environmental impact. Overall, our work provides valuable insights and practical solutions for improving collaboration in various industries, making it easier for people and organizations to work together successfully.

16210420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210420.value: With the increasing demand for energy resources worldwide and the gradual depletion of oil and gas reserves in shallow waters, oil and gas have been extracted from waters (with depths over 1,000m). For economic reasons, the oil and gas extracted from deep waters are commonly transported through a steel pipe (i.e., steel catenary riser, or SCR), that rests on the seabed at one end and is connected to a floating production platform (i.e., a vessel) at the other end. The riser is repeatedly loaded by the motions of the floating platform including heave, surge and sway, and the vortex-induced vibrations (VIVs) in the sea. However, the potential fatigue damage to an SCR in the critical region where the riser pipe touches the seabed, also known as the “touchdown zone (TDZ)” has not been well investigated and understood. Assessing both the fatigue safety margin and fatigue life poses a major challenge to designers. For instance, fatigue failure was reported to destroy risers in the Eastern China Sea in 2000. The main objectives of this proposed project are (a) to investigate the fundamental fatigue mechanism in the TDZ on a clayey seabed of an as-laid SCR subjected to highly realistic combined three-dimensional (3D) cyclic motions, including platform motions (swaying, surging and heaving) and the vortex-induced “butterfly-wing” locus; and (b) to develop improved calculation methods that allow engineers to predict the fatigue life of as-laid SCRs. These objectives will be met (i) by developing a novel in-flight control technique to simulate an SCR that accounts for the complex motions of a production platform and VIVs at the state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge facility at HKUST; (ii) by performing systematic centrifuge model tests; (iii) by conducting 3D numerical simulations by the state-of-the-art bounding surface plasticity cyclic soil model to improve our fundamental understanding of the phenomenon and gain new insights. Simplified calculation methods will also be developed for practising engineers. The results and findings of this project will, without doubt, benefit the global oil and gas industry by alleviating the risk, environmental damage and costs of extracting fuels from deep waters.

16210420.label: Realisation of objectives
16210420.value: One of the key objectives of the project was to develop a novel in-flight control technique to simulate an in-flight steel catenary riser (SCR) container that accounts for the complex motions (swaying, surging and heaving) of a production platform and vortex-induced vibrations (VIVs) in centrifuge. Due to COVID-19, this project was delayed during the period between January 2021 and June 2022 as many parts and instrumentation needed to manufacture the novel SCR container were not available because of the closure of Hong Kong boarders. Under this circumstance, some existing actuators and traducers were loaned from another laboratory in the university to test our new design and control concept of the novel SCR container to save project’s time. After the opening of the boarders, all loaned actuators and traducers were returned to their original owner.

16210420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210420.value: A novel in-flight three-dimensional (3D) servo-actuator system and the corresponding model package was developed at the state-of-the-art 400 g-ton beam centrifuge at HKUST. This 3D servo-actuator control system allows researchers to investigate the fundamental fatigue mechanism of an as-laid steel catenary riser (SCR) subjected to combined vertical, horizontal, and axial cyclic motions. The unique feature of the novel servo-actuator system is capable of controlling three independent and mutually orthogonal motions, namely vertical, horizontal, and axial motions while the centrifuge is spinning or so-called in-flight simulation. This physical modelling capability is the first of its kind in the world. More details are published in the following paper (see Part C): Ng, C.W.W., Le, Y., Baghbanrezvan, S. & Van Laak, P. (2024). A novel three-dimensional SCR motion simulator for modelling the catenary riser-seabed interaction in a centrifuge. Canadian Geotechnical Journal 61, 1266-1274. It is well-known that SCR is prone to fatigue failure due to the cyclic motion of the host floating platform. While previous studies have primarily focused on one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) motions of SCRs, real-world scenarios often involve complex three-dimensional (3D) motions that can significantly affect SCR-seabed interactions and SCR fatigue. Based on centrifuge model tests carried out in this project, cyclic SCR-seabed interactions under episodic 3D motions are understood. It is found that 3D motions produce the highest cyclic stress in the SCR, approximately 20% higher than that from 2D motions at the end of the fifth motion packet. This highlights a critical design concern regarding SCR fatigue under episodic 3D motions. Additionally, the steady cyclic stress increases with the number of motion packets and stabilises by the seventh motion packet in the 3D motion scenario, suggesting that the cyclic stress at the seventh episodic motion packet can serve as a reference for evaluating the SCR’s fatigue. Contrary to conventional understanding that lower seabed stiffness reduces cyclic stress, this study reveals that increased SCR embedment depth in a softer seabed can lead to higher cyclic stress and hence unsafe design. More findings are given in the following paper (see Part C): Ng, C.W.W., Le, Y., Zhang, S. & Zhang, Q. (2025). Centrifuge modelling of steel catenary riser-seabed interactions under three-dimensional cyclic motions. Submitted to Géotechnique.

16210420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210420.value: A novel in-flight three-dimensional servo-actuator system was developed to simulate a steel catenary riser undergoing complex motions (swaying, surging and heaving) and vortex-induced vibrations (VIVs) in centrifuge. This three-dimensional (3D) system allows researchers and engineers to investigate the fundamental fatigue mechanism of an as-laid steel catenary riser (SCR) subjected to combined vertical, horizontal, and axial cyclic motions as those happen in the field. This physical modelling capability is the first of its kind in the world. By using this novel system, unique centrifuge model tests were carried out. High quality of test data was obtained for calibrating a newly developed state-of-the-art soil model and numerical modelling procedures. It is found that current design guidelines do not seem to be on the safe side as they are based on simplified one and two-dimensional test results. Based on numerical parametric analyses, the probability of fatigue failure of an SCR in the critical region has been investigated and understood. Calculation charts for assessing both realistic fatigue safety margin and the fatigue life are developed for engineers to improve the safe and economical design of SCRs.

16210520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210520.value: Passengers’ travel choice and behavior are the fundament components in transportation analysis and modeling. With the fast development of mobile technology-based e-hailing systems (e.g., Uber, DiDi) that provide timely and convenient on-demand ride services to anyone, anywhere, and anytime, urban mobility has witnessed drastic changes in recent years. Particularly, the availability of a massive amount of mobility data collected via the online platform provides excellent opportunities to tackle some new and intriguing travel behavioral issues encountered in the era of new smart mobility. Of particular interest among the various emerging issues in ride-sourcing markets are passengers’ willingness to wait (WTW) in queuing systems with sunk waiting time and their choice of service modes with bundled options. When demand exceeds supply, passengers need to wait for the platform to answer their ride request for vehicle dispatch. The online platform displays and updates the real-time queuing information (queuing length and estimated waiting time) and passengers decide whether and when to abandon the service in the face of sunk waiting time and newly updated additional waiting time in a dynamic environment. Moreover, in addition to the normal non-ride-splitting service (to assign one driver to serve one passenger/request) and ride-splitting (sharing) service (to assign one driver to serve two or more passengers/requests), ride-sourcing platforms such as DiDi are now providing a bundled option that combines the two types of services. A passenger opting for the bundled option waits on the queues of both normal non-ride-splitting and ride-splitting services, and the platform assigns the passenger to either one of the services or queues. In this way, the platform has more flexibility in both supply resource allocation and demand assignment to further improve system efficiency and reduce passenger waiting time. In collaboration with DiDi Chuxing, this research project is proposed to investigate passengers’ WTW with sunk waiting time and to develop an equilibrium model to characterize individual passengers’ choice of ride-splitting and non-ride-splitting services and a bundled option of these two services in a ride-sourcing market. The model is then used to develop optimal platform operating strategies for demand assignment and resource allocation to increase platform profit and social welfare. In addition, the actual mobility data, which are collected on DiDi’s platform, will be used to calibrate the distribution of passengers’ WTW with sunk waiting time and evaluate the impacts of the bundled options. 乘客的出行選擇和行為是交通出行分析和建模的基本組成部分。網約車系統（如Uber，滴滴）隨著移動互聯網技術的普及而快速發展，該系統可為任何人，在任何地點，任何時間提供實時便捷的按需乘車服務。在此影響下，近年來城市交通發生了翻天覆地的變化。特別地，通過在線平台收集的大量移動數據，為解決在智能出行新時代下遇到的一些新的，有趣的出行行為問題，提供了絕佳的契機。 隨著網約車市場出現的各種新問題中，尤其令人感興趣的是，在網上叫車排隊時，乘客繼續等待的願意（WTW）隨著已經等待的時間的變化規律，以及網約車平台提供同時呼叫拼車與不拼車服務時，對乘客出行方式選擇的影響。當乘客需求超過車輛供應時，乘客需要等待平台響應其乘車請求以進行車輛調度。在線平台顯示並更新實時排隊信息（排隊人數和估計的等待時間），面對已經等待的實際時間和平台動態顯示更新的額外等待時間，乘客可以決定是否以及何時放棄叫車服務。此外，除了普通的不拼車服務（指派一名駕駛員為一名乘客/請求服務）和拼車服務（指派一名駕駛員為兩個或更多乘客/請求服務）之外，像滴滴這樣的網約車平台現在提供了同時服務的選項，即將兩種類型的服務結合在一起。選擇同時服務的乘客，可在常規不拼車和拼車服務的隊列中等待，最終平台將分配乘客到兩種服務或隊列之一。這樣，該平台在車輛供應調節和乘客需求分配方面都將具有更大的靈活性，以進一步提高系統效率並減少乘客的等待時間。 與滴滴公司合作，我們提出了此研究項目，研究調查乘客WTW與沉沒等待時間之間的變化，並提出一個平衡模型來描述乘客對拼車和非拼車服務的選擇行為，以及網約車市場中同時呼叫服務的影響。該模型可為平台的需求分配和供應調節提供最佳運營策略，以增加平台利潤和社會福利。此外，在滴滴平台上收集的實際出行數據，將用於校準乘客WTW隨著沉沒等待時間的分佈，並評估同時呼叫服務的影響。

16210520.label: Realisation of objectives
16210520.value: Throughout the three and half years of the research period, we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of analyzing passengers’ willingness to wait, resource allocation and demand assignment in the ride-sourcing market in the original proposal were addressed and the objectives were fully achieved. For objective 1: We analyzed real-life queuing data to identify key factors influencing passenger behavior, providing insights into ride service queuing and responses. Using these findings, we built an initial survival model with constant coefficients to study these factors. We applied the Cox proportional hazard model to examine service abandonment or willingness to wait (WTW), estimating coefficients for passenger and queue-related factors using a maximum likelihood function. We then developed an extended survival model with time-varying coefficients to explore how WTW changes over time, capturing decisions to abandon the service based on sunk waiting time and updated expected wait times. We derived the maximum likelihood function to estimate the extended model’s parameters. The results provided valuable theoretical insights into queuing behavior and practical guidance for ride-sourcing services. For objective 2: Ride-sourcing platforms typically provide two service queues: one for ride-pooling (shared ride) and another for non-ride-pooling (solo ride). Passengers who choose a bundled option combining both services are assigned to either queue by the platform. The platform allocates vacant vehicles to serve both queues. Waiting times, passenger demand for the three service options (ride-pooling, non-ride-pooling, and bundled), and the pool-matching probability for those in the ride-pooling queue interact in a complex, endogenous way. To capture these relationships, we developed a system of simultaneous nonlinear equations. The model was calibrated using real mobility data from DiDi across multiple Chinese cities. For objective 3: We developed a bi-level mathematical framework to optimize ride-sourcing platforms. The upper-level problem aims to maximize platform profit or social welfare by allocating vacant vehicles and assigning passengers who select the bundled service option to either the ride-splitting or non-ride-splitting queues. The lower-level problem incorporates models that account for passengers’ willingness to wait (WTW) and their service preferences based on the upper-level decisions. We explored how optimal resource allocation and passenger assignment shift depending on external factors, particularly the demand-to-supply ratio. When supply far exceeds demand (a low ratio), the platform’s best approach is to direct all bundled option passengers to the non-ride-pooling queue, enhancing service quality, minimizing detours, and boosting revenue. On the other hand, when demand greatly outstrips supply (a high ratio), the optimal strategy shifts to assigning these passengers to the ride-pooling queue, increasing vehicle occupancy and reducing waiting times. A key focus was identifying specific ranges of the demand-to-supply ratio where distinct allocation strategies perform best. To validate our approach, we tested and implemented these optimal strategies in simulation platform, assessing the framework’s effectiveness and efficiency.

16210520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210520.value: During the investigation of the project, several important findings related to emerging on-demand mobility services were notified. The market penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) has surged in recent years and is projected to grow rapidly in the coming decades. Soon, a significant portion—if not all—of ride-sourcing services may shift from conventional gas-powered cars to EVs. This transition is likely to reshape key aspects of the industry, including driver behavior, passenger pricing, and the operational strategies of ride-sourcing platforms. For example, factors like charging infrastructure and battery range could influence how drivers operate and how platforms function compared to gas-powered markets. Exploring the impact of EVs on ride-sourcing markets offers an exciting avenue for future research, potentially uncovering new challenges and opportunities for platforms, drivers, and passengers alike. Looking ahead, the arrival of fully autonomous vehicles is imminent. Self-driving cars, capable of operating without human input, will require a complete reimagining of ride-sourcing—from operational strategies and pricing to the role of drivers—opening the door to innovative models tailored to this technology. To address these issues, new research proposals are being prepared for funding applications to carry out further research in these areas.

16210520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210520.value: Figuring out how people get around cities is important for improving transportation. With apps like Uber and DiDi, booking a ride is as easy as tapping your phone. These apps have changed the way we travel—and they also collect a ton of data, helping researchers study how people make decisions in today’s tech-savvy world. In this project, we focused on two big questions: 1) How Long Will People Wait for a Ride? When demand is high, passengers may have to wait in a virtual "line." The app tells them how long the wait might be or how many people are ahead of them. But here’s the catch: if you’ve already waited 5 minutes and the app says it’ll take even longer, do you keep waiting or give up? 2) How Do People Choose Between Ride Options? Some apps, like DiDi, now offer a "bundled" choice. Normally, you pick either a solo ride (just you) or a shared ride (splitting with others). The bundled option puts you in both lines at once—whichever ride becomes available first. This helps the app match drivers and riders faster, reducing wait times. Partnering with DiDi, we studied how passengers react to waiting times and how they choose between ride options. We built a model to predict these decisions and tested it using real DiDi ride data. The goal is to help ride-hailing apps work smarter—like assigning drivers more efficiently or balancing ride types—to improve service, cut wait times, and make things better for both passengers and the company. By studying real ride patterns, this research helps make ride-hailing systems smoother and more user-friendly in the future.

16210720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210720.value: Last-mile delivery incurs more than 50% of the overall logistics cost in e-commerce. It plays important roles in today’s business world. Many innovations in last-mile delivery have emerged recently. One of the most popular is crowdshipping, which refers to using individual drivers for the last-mile delivery. Big retailers such as Amazon and Alibaba, as well as startups such as Deliv and PiggyBee have been using crowdshipping. Recently mergers and acquisitions involving last-mile delivery companies are also becoming increasingly common. For example, in 2018, SF Express acquired DHL’s China operations, and Alibaba acquired a crowdshipping startup Ele.me, integrating it with Alibaba’s own crowdshipping operations. Despite being popular among firms, mergers often raise antitrust concerns because they may lessen competition and harm consumers. Antitrust agencies rely on existing research to evaluate potential mergers, but as the last-mile delivery evolves rapidly, current merger research findings may be insufficient for analyzing the increasingly-common mergers in the field. A last-mile delivery company’s decisions are heavily influenced by the spatial distribution of demand. However, current merger research has not considered this spatial aspect. Second, if firms rely on crowdshipping, then they compete both in the consumer and labor markets. It is not clear how the additional competition in the labor market interacts with merging firms’ combined delivery and price competition in the consumer market. To bridge this gap, we propose to adopt a game-theoretical approach to study a merger of two last-mile delivery companies in an oligopolistic market. The firms first engage in price competition for consumers, and then they decide their shipping plans. We study two scenarios for shipping: Firms either use their own trucks, or crowdsource drivers. If a merger takes place, two firms become a single firm and they make decisions in a centralized manner. We will analyze operational details of last-mile delivery and the role of crowdshipping in mergers. We hope to understand how they interact with competition in the consumer and labor markets. Using these findings, we can provide clear guidelines firms can apply to make optimal decisions after a merger. These findings will also help antitrust agencies to understand mergers in last-mile delivery better, especially in the new crowdshipping operations. As a result, new policy implications can be generated to better regulate mergers and benefit consumers in China and around the world. 最後一公里配送在電子商務的成本中佔比50%以上，在當今的商業運營中發揮著重要作用。近年來最後一公里有了很多的革新。其中應用最廣的就是利用第三方個人進行最後一公里配送的眾包物流。大型零售商如亞馬遜和阿里巴巴以及一些小型初創企業都在使用眾包物流。 近年來最後一公里物流公司的兼併與收購也越來越頻繁。在2018年順豐快遞併購了DHL快遞的中國運營部，阿里巴巴併購了一個眾包物流初創公司餓了麼並將其整合入阿里巴巴自己的眾包物流運營。雖然公司常常利用兼併與重組，反壟斷機構對於併購常常有很大的擔憂，因為兼併常常會降低競爭和傷害消費者。反壟斷機構倚靠已有的研究來評估併購提議。但是最後一公里物流的快速發展讓已有的併購研究難以全面地評估最後一公里物流公司的併購。 最後一公里物流公司的決策深受市場需求的空間分佈影響。但是，當前的併購研究尚未考慮此空間方面。其次，如果公司依靠眾包，那麼他們在消費者和勞動力市場上都會競爭。目前尚不清楚合併企業在勞動力市場上的額外競爭與消費者市場上的價格競爭如何相互作用。 為了彌合這一差距，我們計劃採用博弈論的方法來研究寡頭市場中兩家最後一公里的物流公司的合併。這些公司首先在消費者市場進行價格競爭，然後決定他們的運輸計劃。我們研究了兩種運輸場景：企業使用自己的卡車或眾包物流。如果發生合併，則兩家公司將成為一家公司，並以集中方式進行決策。 我們將分析最後一公里物流的運營細節以及眾包在合併中的作用。我們希望了解它們如何與消費者和勞動力市場中的競爭相互作用。利用這些發現，我們可以為公司提供合併後的最佳決策的明確指導。這些發現還將幫助反壟斷機構更好地理解最後一公里物流公司的合併，尤其是涉及到新的眾包業務的公司。可以產生新的政策指導，以更好地規範合併並惠及中國乃至全球的消費者。

16210720.label: Realisation of objectives
16210720.value: This research project studies the mergers in last-mile delivery. Mergers and acquisitions have emerged as a vital business strategy for firms seeking market expansion, enhanced competitiveness, and cost reduction. Among the various merger types, horizontal mergers, involving two competing firms in the same market, often raise concerns among antitrust agencies due to their potential to significantly reduce competition and harm consumers. While existing research has extensively studied horizontal mergers in traditional industries, there is a notable gap in analyzing the increasingly mergers within the rapidly evolving sharing economies. We focus on two categories of last-mile delivery service operators, including (i) on-demand service platforms, a prominent segment of the sharing economy that facilitates the connection between customers in need of services and self-scheduled independent service providers; and (ii) logistics service providers, who offer parcel delivery services to end customers in the last mile segment. Next, we illustrate how we accomplish our outlined research objectives. (1) Insights for Last-Mile Delivery Service Operators on Profitable Mergers and Post-Merger Decisions This project provides actionable insights for last-mile delivery firms by modeling how mergers affect profitability and operational dynamics. For on-demand service platforms, mergers enable firms to pool delivery agents (e.g., drivers or couriers) across platforms, amplifying cross-side network effects. For instance, a merged platform can reduce delivery times by assigning agents from both pre-merger networks to serve a unified customer base, enhancing customer satisfaction and order volume. We show that firms should prioritize mergers in less saturated markets (where customer demand is moderate or low). In such markets, post-merger resource pooling expands service coverage and agent utilization rates, creating a “win-win-win” outcome (higher profits, consumer surplus, and labor welfare). Additionally, while post-merger prices increase due to reduced competition, firms must balance this with improved service quality (e.g., faster deliveries from a larger agent pool). In unsaturated markets, higher wages attract more agents, further boosting network effects. In saturated markets, wages may decline, necessitating regulatory safeguards (e.g., minimum wage floors). For logistics service providers (LSPs), we study the mergers problem from the perspective of joint design of last mile delivery facilities, such as the parcel lockers. Our research highlights that merging firms can achieve delivery cost savings by optimizing shared infrastructure. Specifically, our study explores two operational modes: the two-trip mode, where home and locker deliveries are managed separately; and the mixed-trip mode, which consolidates both into one route. For both delivery modes, we show that locker networks optimized for larger LSPs can be “nested” to serve smaller LSPs effectively, i.e., the optimal locker network is contained in the optimal network of the larger one. Merging firms could adopt this principle to consolidate delivery routes and facilities, reducing redundant infrastructure. For instance, merging carriers into a single mixed-trip system reduces travel distance, especially with high customer adoption of lockers. Furthermore, our work emphasizes that locker adoption rates critically impact efficiency. Post-merger, firms should incentivize customer shifts to locker pickups (e.g., via discounts) to maximize cost savings. (2) Policy Implications for Antitrust Agencies and Customers The project equips regulators with criteria to evaluate mergers in last-mile delivery markets. For on-demand service platforms, it is recommended to Target mergers with geographically or demographically complementary platforms (e.g., a urban-focused firm merging with a suburban-focused competitor) to maximize resource synergy. Post-merger, use dynamic pricing algorithms to reflect real-time demand-supply imbalances and incentivize agent retention through loyalty programs. On the other hand, it is beneficial to adopt a tiered review process -- fast-tracking mergers in underserved areas while imposing stricter conditions (e.g., price caps) in concentrated markets. For logistics service providers (LSPs), our analysis highlights the important role played by the larger LSPs in the operations of the interoperable system. We notice that “the current private-sector driven market for parcel lockers is largely fragmented, with competing players deploying their proprietary networks which are accessible only by selected delivery service providers. This has given rise to deep inefficiencies for local operators. The lockers are duplicated at high-traffic commercial locations and e-commerce marketplaces and delivery service providers are unable to access all lockers which may be available.” Our analysis explains why there is so much duplication (i.e., nested) in the locker networks set up by competing players, but also underscore the challenges ahead -- the network set up to maximize delivery efficiency for all the LSPs will necessarily be the one that suit the largest LSP the most, and efforts need to be made to encourage the larger commercial players into the program, to avoid the head-to-head competition between the government and these players. (3) Contribution to the Literature on Last-mile Delivery Mergers This project contributes to the literature on last-mile delivery mergers in the following ways. Endogenous Cost Synergies: Unlike traditional models assuming exogenous cost reductions (e.g., economies of scale), our work introduces resource pooling as an endogenous synergy. For example, merging platforms reduce delivery costs by eliminating duplicate agent recruitment efforts and optimizing route assignments. Two-Sided Market Dynamics: Our model captures interdependencies between demand (customer orders) and supply (agent availability). Post-merger, higher agent utilization lowers delivery costs, which in turn attracts more customers. This feedback loop is often ignored in single-sided merger analyses. Labor-Consumer Trade-offs: Prior literature often neglects labor welfare. Our work shows that mergers can raise wages in unsaturated markets (by expanding order volume) but suppress them in saturated ones (via reduced competition for agents). Multi-stage Network Design: Our research contributing to the multi-stage facility location problem. We establish that the optimal network solution is nested as the demand volume increases. This property is often overlooked in the network design problem. (4) Framework for Future Research on Last-Mile Delivery Mergers This project lays the groundwork for future studies through extending existing models and exploring emerging contexts in the field of on-demand service platform mergers. Model extensions include incorporating spatial competition by analyzing geographic parameters like agent density per ZIP code and investigating algorithmic collusion effects where AI-driven pricing tools may inadvertently coordinate post-merger price increases across platforms. In emerging contexts, the research suggests examining how mergers impact investments in autonomous delivery technologies such as drones and self-driving vehicles, focusing on fleet optimization, as well as evaluating sustainability factors, like reduced emissions from consolidated delivery routes post-merger. Furthermore, the research roadmap highlights the potential integration of behavioral elements and regulatory constraints into future analyses to refine predictions, leveraging the adaptable game-theoretic structure of the study as a foundational framework for these investigations. For logistics service providers (LSPs), our research proposes a framework for merging the facility networks of different LSPs into an integrated network, with the aim to ensure efficiency for each LSP. By combining the BHH theorem for optimizing delivery routes and logit choice models for estimating demand, we provide a structured approach to analyzing post-merger operational and demand shifts. It recommends incorporating variables such as locker density, customer adoption rates, and TSP tour lengths in future research to measure the consequences of mergers accurately. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the significance of government-led infrastructure, like the locker alliance network, as a focal point for evaluating public-private partnerships within merger scenarios, including mandatory resource-sharing agreements to prevent market fragmentation and incentive mechanisms (e.g., subsidies) to boost infrastructure adoption.

16210720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210720.value: In response to the surge of horizontal mergers within the on-demand economy, our study constructs a game-theoretical model to scrutinize the ramifications of a merger between two on-demand service platforms on consumer surplus and labor welfare. In a published work, titled “Mergers Between On-Demand Service Platforms: The Impact on Consumer Surplus and Labor Welfare”, we find that while a merger diminishes competition, it can potentially benefit customers and agents through enhanced pooling advantages facilitated by the merger and positive cross-side network effects. These outcomes hold vital implications for management strategies. Notably, our research unearths two opposing dynamics -- a reduction in competition and a pooling benefit stemming from a merger -- that collectively shape the welfare outcomes of such mergers. Furthermore, we delineate the circumstances under which a merger is likely to bolster consumer surplus and labor welfare, offering practical benchmarks for antitrust bodies to assess platform mergers. Our findings suggest that mergers are more inclined to be beneficial if initiated in less saturated markets, as exemplified by the Postmates-Uber Eats merger during a period of burgeoning food delivery demand. In such scenarios, where market demand is expanding, mergers possess the potential to bolster consumer surplus, labor welfare, and platform profitability simultaneously. Additionally, the likelihood of a triple-win scenario increases when the customer and agent markets exhibit greater differentiation, urging antitrust authorities to consider a more lenient stance towards mergers in evolving or distinctive markets. Contrary to common assumptions, our study reveals that the impact of a merger on customers in highly time-sensitive service sectors is nuanced. While resource pooling may suggest customer benefits, congestion effects introduce uncertainties, i.e., optimal outcomes are most probable when customers display moderate sensitivity to congestion. In the context of last-mile parcel delivery, we focus on the Locker Alliance Network (LAN) initiative in Singapore, and evaluate how locker network design impacts last-mile delivery efficiency. We extend the network design model for a Logistics Service Provider (LSP) to broaden our analysis to encompass the design challenge for multiple LSPs (mergers) within the context of the LAN's interoperable structure. The research emphasizes the vital role of larger LSPs in the interoperable system and the challenges posed by fragmented private-sector-driven locker networks, stressing the need for collaboration to enhance delivery efficiency and avoid duplication. We present our findings in an accepted work titled “Does Locker Alliance Network Improve Last Mile Delivery Efficiency?”.

16210720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210720.value: The research on the impacts of mergers between on-demand service platforms provides significant insights into how these mergers affect consumers, workers, and the overall market dynamics. We also address the network design problem when multiple LSPs intend to share their service facilities. The findings suggest that while mergers can reduce competition, they can also bring benefits through improved resource utilization and network effects. The study highlights the importance of considering factors like market saturation and differentiation between customer and agent bases when evaluating the outcomes of mergers. Additionally, we show that the optimal locker network solutions exhibit a near-nested structure in terms of delivery volume. Therefore, a well-constructed network should incentivize different LSPs, especially the larger ones, to join the LAN to improve their delivery service. Moving forward, future research could explore incorporating spatial features into the analysis to better understand how these factors influence the pooling effect and overall outcomes. Additionally, studying how mergers impact pricing schemes and competition in scenarios where multiple platforms continue to coexist post-merger could offer valuable insights. Finally, it will be interesting to understand how this mergers solution concept can help to reduce carbon emissions in the last-mile delivery segment.

16210720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210720.value: This research explores what happens when companies like Uber or DoorDash merge or when multiple Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) want to merger their facility networks. Imagine two food delivery apps joining forces: the study asks whether this hurts customers (higher prices) and workers (lower pay) or actually helps everyone. Using rigorous models, it shows that mergers can sometimes create a “triple win” by pooling drivers and customers, leading to faster service, more jobs for workers, and higher profits for companies, even if prices rise a bit. Additionally, our analysis for last-mile parcel delivery shows that the optimal locker network design tends to expand in a “nested” manner relative to the market share of an LSP. This finding suggests that operator could design locker networks based on the profiles of the largest LSP, ensuring that the expansion of these networks aligns with the existing logistics infrastructure. Our findings help regulators decide when to allow mergers. Instead of just blocking them for reducing competition, they can now check if the merger improves efficiency or worker opportunities. The research offers a roadmap for fairer rules in the gig economy, where millions rely on these services for income and convenience.

16211220.label: Project Objectives
16211220.value: Objective 1: Developing A Unified Framework of Optimal Competitive Algorithms for Online Admission Control Online admission control (OAC) is a classic network resource allocation problem. While there already exist many works addressing OAC, most of the proposed online algorithms are strictly application-dependent, and thus provide somewhat limited guidance for other OAC problems in emerging applications. The first objective of this project will thus be to develop a unified framework that can guide the systematic design of competitive algorithms for OAC. Our framework will first build the connection between a competitive algorithm for OAC and a solution of a set of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). It will then show that the solution can be used to design a posted price algorithm with a constant competitive ratio. Based on this framework, we will reproduce the well-known online algorithm for the basic online 0/1 knapsack problem, and establish the optimality of this algorithm, in the sense that no other online algorithms can achieve a better competitive ratio. Furthermore, we will extend this framework to a more general online admission control and routing problem with multiple links over multiple time slots and multiple paths. Objective 2: Designing Competitive Algorithms for Online Network Utility Maximization Network utility maximization (NUM), which studies rate control of network users, is another classic network resource allocation problem, and has been similarly well-addressed in the literature. Online NUM (ONUM), however, in which users arrive for rate allocation in a sequential and arbitrary manner, is less well understood. The second objective of this project will thus be to design competitive algorithms for ONUM by extending the framework for OAC from binary admission control to continuous rate control. We will tailor the posted price algorithm to continuous rate control and re-establish the connection between competitive algorithms and the solutions of ODEs. We will first derive the results for the basic one-way trading problem with a linear utility function and a single link. We will then extend the utility function to general concave functions in a network based on Fenchel's duality theorem. Extensive numerical experiments will be conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed online algorithms with practical utility functions, and under realistic network and user arrival instances. Objective 3: Integrating Congestion Costs to Competitive Algorithm Design for Online Network Resource Allocation Classic network resource allocation problems treat network links as "pipes" with fixed transmission capacities. However, as the throughput of links approaches the capacity, congestion occurs, which may lead to long queueing delays or packet loss for data transmission. This is not taken into account in network resource allocation but is of great importance for the quality-of-service (QoS) of network users. The third objective of this project will thus be to integrate the congestion costs of links into the competitive algorithm design frameworks for OAC and ONUM. We will begin with the framework for OAC, based on our previous experience in online combinatorial auctions with production costs. Since the form of congestion cost function can greatly impact upon the design of the online algorithm, we will utilize different congestion measurements (e.g., delay and packet loss probability) to design the corresponding competitive algorithms, and compare their performances via extensive simulations. Based on these results as well as our proposed framework for ONUM, we will integrate congestion costs to the competitive algorithm design for ONUM, making use of specific and practical forms of utility and congestion cost functions. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithms will be numerically validated under realistic network and user instances.
