16211220.value: 競爭算法旨在解決只能利用因果信息進行實時決策的在線優化問題。現有的關於在線算法的設計框架通常是針對特定應用開發的。因此，這些框架針對具有相似的離線優化公式的問題會提出不同的設計原則。此外，已有的在線算法通常只是基於對具體應用的理解而設計。因此對於研究其他應用的科研人員而言，這些算法似乎“不知從何而來”。事實上，人們對如何系統地設計競爭算法這個基本問題了解甚少。競爭算法只是被不同的研究者從不同角度進行了研究。這阻礙了不同領域的研究人員合作解決在線算法的核心困難以及有效地擴展現有結果的努力。該項目旨在開發一個可以統一指導在線優化問題中的競爭算法的設計框架。我們將主要研究預算受限的在線優化問題（OBO）並將其應用於在線網絡資源分配問題上。我們的目標是在OBO的競爭算法與一組常微分方程的解之間建立聯繫，並使用常微分方程的解設計具有確定競爭比的定價算法。隨後，我們希望通過研究相應的常微分方程來建立OBO的競爭算法的最優性，存在性和唯一性。 更具體地說，我們的項目將解決以下三個方面上的關鍵技術挑戰。首先，我們將開發一個統一的框架用於設計在線准入控制的最佳競爭算法。從最基本的在線0/1背包問題入手，我們先為這個問題構造常微分方程，然後使用可保證最小競爭比的可行解來設計定價算法，最後證明這個算法的最優性。基於此基本模型的結果，我們會將這個設計框架擴展到一個更通用的在線准入控制和路徑規劃問題。其次，通過把在線准入控制問題中的0/1變量擴展到連續變量，我們將為在線網絡效用最大化問題設計競爭算法。這是一個非常具有挑戰性的問題，因為在構造相應的常微分方程時，連續變量會帶來額外的困難。另外，在線網絡效用最大化問題的效用函數是凹函數，這要求我們將設計框架從在線線性規劃擴展到在線凸優化。這是一項非常困難的工作。我們將通過改進定價算法以及 Fenchel對偶定理來解決連續變量和凹效用函數帶來的技術困難。第三，我們將把網絡鏈路的擁塞成本整合到在線准入控制和在線網絡效用最大化問題的競爭算法框架中。這是因為隨著網絡鏈路的吞吐量接近容量，鏈路會發生擁塞，而這將極大地降低網絡用戶的端到端的服務質量（例如，延遲或丟包概率）。又由於效用和擁塞成本函數的特定形式會極大地影響算法設計，我們將研究可以確保不同程度的公平性的效用函數和可能導致不同服務質量的擁塞成本函數。最後，我們將通過在實際網絡和用戶實例下的大量仿真來驗證基於我們提出的框架設計的競爭算法的高效性。

16211220.label: Realisation of objectives
16211220.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: The first objective of this project was to develop a unified framework of competitive algorithms for online admission control (OAC). We modeled OAC as an online knapsack problem (OKP). The basic 0/1 knapsack problem considers a single knapsack and aims to irrevocably decide whether to admit each online-arriving item/user with the objective of maximizing the total value of admitted items while respecting the capacity of the knapsack. We studied a general version of the problem with three important extensions: (i) the online multiple knapsack problem, where there are multiple knapsacks and the decision becomes whether to admit each item, and which knapsack the item should be assigned to if admitted; (ii) the online multi-dimensional knapsack problem, where each item has a multi-dimensional weight, and the decision is whether to admit each item while simultaneously respecting the multi-dimensional capacity limits; and (iii) the online knapsack with departures problem, where arriving items depart after finite time duration. This general version is most applicable to practical problems such as the routing problem with multiple links over multiple time slots and multiple paths, and the online cloud job scheduling problem. To make the admission decision, we designed a class of online threshold-based algorithms (OTAs), which use threshold functions to estimate the cost of admitting users and determine the admission decisions by maximizing a pseudo-utility (i.e., user’s value minus estimated cost). Our core work was to provide a systematic method to design the threshold function so that OTAs can ensure bounded competitive ratios. In particular, we proposed an instance-dependent online primal-dual framework that connects the design of the threshold function to the solution of a set of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Furthermore, we showed that the designed threshold function can achieve optimal competitive ratios when the ODEs are constructed based on the worst-case instance. (2) Realization of Objective 2: The second objective of this project was to design competitive algorithms for online network utility maximization (ONUM), by extending the framework for online admission control from binary decision to continuous rate control. We first investigated a simplified ONUM with a single resource constraint and linear utility functions, which is also known as the one-way trading problem (OTP). We established the connection between OTP and its corresponding binary control problem, online 0/1 knapsack problem (OKP), under a mild infinitesimal assumption. Both OTP and OKP can be solved by a unified online threshold-based algorithm (OTA) that achieves the optimal competitive ratio. In each step of OTA, the continuous decision is determined by solving a pseudo-utility maximization problem, which is constructed based on the carefully-designed threshold function. We then studied the general ONUM with multiple resource constraints and general concave utility functions, based on the general Fenchel’s duality theorem. The coupling between different resources is the main hurdle for designing a competitive algorithm for the general ONUM. We proposed a novel extension of OTA that can determine the continuous rate of each user as a solution of a convex optimization problem. We rigorously proved that the proposed algorithm achieves a competitive ratio that is logarithmic in the maximum number of links requested by a user. This competitive performance matches the lower bound of ONUM problem and thus is order-optimal. To validate the performance of the proposed algorithm for ONUM problem, we applied the algorithm to the online bandwidth allocation problem based on real-world traces from Abilene network. Extensive simulations demonstrated the performance advantages of our proposed algorithm in comparison to two state-of-the-art algorithms (i.e., online primal-dual algorithm and posted-pricing algorithm). In addition, we devised an adaptive implementation of the algorithm by using an online learning approach to estimate the algorithm parameters. The average cumulative performance of this adaptive algorithm quickly converges to that of the algorithm with the best possible parameters selected offline. Thus, the adaptive algorithm can learn parameters online and can be applied in a wider range of application scenarios. (3) Realization of Objective 3: The third objective of this project was to further address the congestion costs induced in the online network resource allocation problem. First, under the adversarial input model, we extended the online threshold-based algorithm to address the online knapsack problem and online network utility maximization problem with congestion costs. These costs model the performance degradation of users as the throughput of network links approaches capacity. We derived the sufficient and necessary conditions for designing the threshold function to ensure a bounded competitive ratio. To move beyond worst-case analysis, we further considered a stochastic input model where all arrivals are drawn from the same distribution. In this setting, we formulated a regularized online allocation problem with additive non-linear utility function and non-separable regularizer that captures the congestion cost. We proposed a dual-based adaptive resolving algorithm for this problem. Each iteration of the algorithm consists of two subroutines: periodical dual optimization and primal decision-making. Specifically, in each dual optimization, we adaptively update the average remaining resources in the dual problem and (approximately) solve the dual solution. The adaptive update of the resources plays an essential role in attaining a good performance guarantee. Given the solution from the dual optimization problem, we then solve a primal pseudo-utility maximization problem using the dual solution as pseudo prices of resources. We evaluated the performance of our algorithm under the regret analysis framework with the offline optimum as the benchmark. We proved that our adaptive resolving algorithm achieves a logarithmic regret in the number of steps, which matches the best lower bound results in the constraint-free and non-regularized online convex optimization literature. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first theoretical guarantee of an exact logarithmic regret bound for online non-linear allocation with hard constraints and a non-separable regularizer. In addition, the performance of the proposed algorithm is guaranteed for general regularizers under a mild assumption. Besides congestion cost, the regularizer can also be designed for other objectives in network resource allocation such as the max-min fairness in online bandwidth allocation and load balancing.

16211220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211220.value: First, we introduce and study a general version of online knapsack problem that considers multiple knapsacks, multi-dimensional capacity limits, and item departures. This general model has a wide range of applications in networking and operations research areas. We propose a novel online threshold-based algorithm for this problem and rigorously prove that it attains the order-optimal competitive ratio among all online algorithms. From the technical perspective, we develop an instance-dependent online primal-dual approach for designing and analyzing the online threshold-based algorithm in a systematic way. Specifically, we find that the threshold function is the solution to a system of ordinary differential equations that are crafted based on worst-case analysis. The research outcomes of this part have been published in the journal papers [J1] and the conference papers [C2][C4] listed in Part C. Second, we study an online version of the well-known network utility maximization problem, which extends the online knapsack problem from binary decisions to continuous decisions, and from linear objectives to general concave objectives. We propose a modified online threshold-based algorithm for this problem, and prove that it attains an optimal competitive ratio that is logarithmic in the maximum number of links requested by a user. Through extensive simulations based on real-world traces, we demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms two state-of-the-art online algorithms. These results are published in [C1][J2]. In addition to worst-case analysis, we also explore how to leverage predictions from modern machine learning tools to improve the algorithm's average-case performance when the predictions are accurate while still providing a worst-case guarantee regardless of prediction accuracy. A preliminary work has been published in [C3]. Third, we integrate link congestion costs into the previously studied online knapsack problem and online network utility maximization problem, extending the design and analysis of the online threshold-based algorithm under the adversarial input model. The corresponding results are published in [J3]. We further consider the problem under the stochastic input model and formulate it as a regularized online allocation problem. We propose a dual-based adaptive resolving algorithm and prove this algorithm achieves the optimal regret bound that is logarithmic in the time horizon. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first theoretical guarantee of an exact logarithmic regret bound for online non-linear allocation with hard constraints and a non-separable regularizer. The research outcomes of this part have been published in [J4].

16211220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211220.value: We believe that developing learning-augmented algorithms for online network resource allocation is a promising direction. This project focuses primarily on developing competitive algorithms that provide performance guarantees even in worst-case scenarios. However, real-world conditions often differ from these worst-case scenarios, leading algorithms to sometimes be overly pessimistic. Furthermore, our algorithm designs do not assume any knowledge of future events. In practical scenarios, however, it is possible to predict future conditions using advanced machine learning tools and historical data. Therefore, further research is necessary to explore how to integrate machine learning predictions into our algorithm design and analysis, potentially improving performance beyond worst-case scenarios. Our preliminary study has shown promising results in the context of the one-way trading problem, which is a simplified case of general online resource allocation. Moving forward, it is important to investigate how these findings can be extended to more complex scenarios, such as online network resource allocation involving multiple resources, multi-dimensional capacity limits, and resource reusability. This exploration could pave the way for more effective and adaptive resource allocation strategies in practical network settings.

16211220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211220.value: Our project focused on enhancing real-time management of network resources by developing algorithms that efficiently allocate resources like bandwidth. These algorithms were designed to dynamically adjust as network demands change, ensuring optimal resource utilization. We also addressed congestion issues that arise as resources near capacity, which can degrade network performance. Through rigorous testing and simulations using real-world data, our algorithms demonstrated their effectiveness in maintaining efficient and resilient network operations, even under challenging worst-case scenarios. Overall, our research provides practical solutions that enable network operators to optimize resource allocation in real-time, effectively manage congestion, and consistently deliver reliable network performance. These advancements are crucial for enhancing user experience across diverse network environments.

16211520.label: Project Objectives
16211520.value: Pronoun and entity linking in an eventuality-centric knowledge graph. We will perform pronoun resolution and entity linking in our existing eventuality-centric knowledge graph, ASER (Activities, States, Events, and their Relations). The new links, in addition to existing links between activities, states, and events, will provide more information for commonsense reasoning. Conceptualization and higher-order selectional preference construction. We will develop our commonsense reasoning module using a linguistic phenomenon called selectional preference, based on which we will develop a contextualization and conceptualization approach to automatically aggregate more abstract information to further densify the relationships in ASER. Development of transferability from linguistic knowledge to commonsense knowledge. We will use experiments to demonstrate that the linguistic knowledge extracted in ASER can be transferred easily to commonsense knowledge, proving that the augmented ASER is essentially a commonsense knowledge graph. Evaluation based on human annotation and downstream tasks. We will perform evaluation based on both human annotations, other existing knowledge graphs, and downstream natural language processing tasks.

16211520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211520.value: 常識知識的獲取和推理一直是人工智能的核心問題。但是，長期以來缺乏有效收集常識知識的方法。在本項目中，我們提出基於選擇偏好收集常識知識的方法。首先，該方法基於人類語言中的選擇偏好的這一普遍現象，將選擇偏好的定義從一階依存關係擴展為高階關係。我們同時使用實體鏈接和指代消解等技術增強抽取過程，以向知識圖譜添加更多鏈接。第二，我們提出了一種事件上下文概念化的方法，用來自動聚合知識圖譜中更多的抽象概念，從而建立更高階的選擇偏好知識。第三，我們提出了可行的方法來證明基於語言知識提取的知識圖譜可以自動遷移到常識知識上，從而構成常識知識圖譜。最後，我們同時使用內部和外部數據集以及相應的指標來評估我們的知識，並將其與當前的最新技術進行比較。

16211520.label: Realisation of objectives
16211520.value: The project successfully achieved its objectives, with detailed outcomes for each: Objective 1: Pronoun and Entity Linking in an Eventuality-centric Knowledge Graph Achievement: The project enhanced ASER with pronoun and entity linking, improving commonsense reasoning. The conference papers like "Exophoric Pronoun Resolution" (EMNLP 2021) and "PCR4ALL" (LREC 2022) developed robust pronoun resolution methods for ASER. Extent: Fully achieved. These methods densified ASER’s relational structure, enabling better eventuality-centric reasoning. Evidence: Publications and conference papers demonstrate improved coreference resolution, with benchmarks like PCR4ALL providing evaluation standards. Challenges: Handling ambiguous pronouns in complex dialogs was challenging. The team mitigated this through topic regularization (EMNLP 2021) and comprehensive benchmarks (LREC 2022). Objective 2: Conceptualization and Higher-order Selectional Preference Construction Achievement: The project developed higher-order selectional preference frameworks, with ASER (Zhang et al., 2022) as a core contribution. The publication "Acquiring and modeling abstract commonsense knowledge via conceptualization" (He et al., 2024) proposed a contextualized conceptualization approach. Conference papers like "CAT" (ACL 2023) and "CAR" (EMNLP 2023) advanced conceptualization for commonsense reasoning. Extent: Fully achieved. These methods aggregated abstract information, enhancing ASER’s density and reasoning capabilities. Evidence: ASER’s scalability and conceptualization frameworks were validated through publications and presentations at ACL, EMNLP, and LREC/COLING. Challenges: Modeling abstract commonsense knowledge was complex. The team addressed this through iterative framework development, as seen in "CAT" and "CAR." Objective 3: Development of Transferability from Linguistic Knowledge to Commonsense Knowledge Achievement: The project demonstrated that linguistic knowledge in ASER could be transferred to commonsense knowledge. Publications like "Logical Queries on Knowledge Graphs" (Wang et al., 2022) and "Sequential Query Encoding" (Bai et al., 2023) showed how ASER’s linguistic structures support commonsense inference. Conference paper "FolkScope" (ACL 2023) validated transferability in tasks like question answering and e-commerce commonsense discovery. Extent: Fully achieved. ASER was established as a commonsense knowledge graph through these experiments. Evidence: Multiple publications and conference papers, with applications in diverse domains, confirm transferability. Challenges: Ensuring generalizability across tasks was difficult. The team used diverse downstream tasks (e.g., NAACL 2024’s "AbsPyramid") to validate transferability. Objective 4: Evaluation Based on Human Annotation and Downstream Tasks Achievement: The project conducted evaluations using human annotations and downstream tasks. Benchmarks like "PCR4ALL" (LREC 2022), "Benchmarking Commonsense Knowledge Base Population" (EMNLP 2020), and "AbsPyramid" (NAACL 2024) provided robust evaluation frameworks. Conference papers like "CIKQA" (EACL 2023) and "QADYNAMICS" (EMNLP 2023) evaluated commonsense question answering, while "EventGround" (LREC/COLING 2024) assessed narrative reasoning. Extent: Fully achieved. Evaluations confirmed ASER’s effectiveness and provided community resources. Evidence: Benchmarks and downstream task results in high-impact venues demonstrate rigorous evaluation. Challenges: Obtaining high-quality human annotations was resource-intensive. The team mitigated this by leveraging existing knowledge graphs (e.g., EMNLP 2023’s "Gold") and synthetic data (EMNLP 2023’s "QADYNAMICS").

16211520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211520.value: The project "Higher-order Selectional Preference Inference for Commonsense Knowledge Acquisition" significantly advanced commonsense knowledge acquisition through the ASER knowledge graph, achieving all four objectives outlined in the original application. Major findings and outcomes are summarized below. Objective 1: Pronoun and Entity Linking: The project enhanced ASER with robust pronoun and entity linking, improving eventuality-centric commonsense reasoning. The conference papers like "PCR4ALL" (LREC 2022) and "Exophoric Pronoun Resolution" (EMNLP 2021) developed scalable pronoun coreference methods, densifying ASER’s relational structure. These advancements enabled better contextual understanding in dialogs and narratives, validated through benchmarks like PCR4ALL. Objective 2: Conceptualization and Higher-order Selectional Preference: The publication "Acquiring and modeling abstract commonsense knowledge via conceptualization" (He et al., 2024) and papers like "CAT" (ACL 2023) and "CAR" (EMNLP 2023) proposed contextualized conceptualization approaches. These methods aggregated abstract information, enhancing ASER’s ability to model complex commonsense relationships, as demonstrated in tasks like zero-shot question answering. Objective 3: Transferability from Linguistic to Commonsense Knowledge: The project proved ASER’s linguistic knowledge transfers effectively to commonsense knowledge. Publications like "Logical Queries on Knowledge Graphs" (Wang et al., 2022) and "Sequential Query Encoding" (Bai et al., 2023), alongside conference paper "FolkScope" (ACL 2023), showed ASER’s applicability in diverse domains, including e-commerce and causal reasoning, establishing it as a commonsense knowledge graph. Objective 4: Evaluation: Rigorous evaluations were conducted using human annotations, existing knowledge graphs, and downstream tasks. Benchmarks like "Benchmarking Commonsense Knowledge Base Population" (EMNLP 2020), "AbsPyramid" (NAACL 2024), and "CIKQA" (EACL 2023) validated ASER’s effectiveness. Papers like "EventGround" (LREC/COLING 2024) and "QADYNAMICS" (EMNLP 2023) demonstrated superior performance in narrative reasoning and question answering. The project produced five publications, tens of conference papers, and trained seven PhD students, whose theses contributed to the outcomes.

16211520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211520.value: The project’s advancements in ASER, pronoun resolution, conceptualization, and commonsense knowledge transfer offer significant potential for further development. The ASER framework’s scalability and robust benchmarks (e.g., PCR4ALL, AbsPyramid) provide a foundation for extending commonsense reasoning to new domains like multimodal AI, real-time dialog systems, and automated narrative generation. The conceptualization approaches (e.g., CAT, CAR) can be refined to handle more abstract and culturally diverse commonsense knowledge, enhancing global applicability. Additionally, integrating ASER with large language models, as explored in “ConstraintChecker” (EACL 2024), could improve reasoning accuracy and efficiency. Proposed Course of Action: (1) Develop hybrid models combining ASER with multimodal data (e.g., images, videos) to support tasks like visual commonsense reasoning. (2) Expand ASER’s knowledge base with multilingual and domain-specific eventualities, leveraging transfer learning. (3) Enhance evaluation benchmarks with real-world downstream tasks, such as autonomous agent decision-making. (4) Collaborate with industry to apply ASER in practical applications like e-commerce recommendation systems (e.g., FolkScope, ACL 2023). (5) Secure funding to train additional researchers, building on the seven PhD graduates, to sustain innovation in commonsense knowledge acquisition.

16211520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211520.value: This research project aimed to teach computers to understand everyday human knowledge. We improved a system called ASER, a digital map of activities, states, and events, to make it smarter about how things connect in real life. First, we helped ASER understand pronouns (like "he" or "it") and link them to the right people or objects, making conversations clearer. Second, we developed ways to group similar ideas together, creating a deeper understanding of abstract concepts. Third, we showed that the language patterns in ASER can be used to solve practical problems, like answering questions or making recommendations. Finally, we tested ASER with human feedback and real-world tasks to ensure it works well. The project led to five major publications, many conference presentations, and trained seven PhD students. Its value lies in making AI systems more human-like in understanding the world, with applications in chatbots, recommendation systems, and storytelling. This work lays the groundwork for smarter, more helpful AI in daily life.

16211620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16211620.value: 响应联合国可持续发展目标的模因框架机器学习：走向热门社会文化模因的大规模自动获取

16211620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211620.value: Even as we explore the many exciting short-term applications of data-hungry deep learning techniques, serious limitations on understanding situations and grasping their meaning continue to daunt even our latest machine learning approaches to natural language processing. Much of “meaning” rests not on literal logic but rather on our large interrelated inventories of often arbitrary, cultural conventions about how to frame abstract situations. How do we understand the world? The challenge is not just modeling extensional “real world knowledge”, but modeling our socioculturally shaped intentional perspectives on abstract real world situations. For decades, various AI sub-communities have struggled with aspects of such difficulties under slogans like “commonsense”, “humanlike”, “intuitive”, and so on. But while our neural and statistical approaches have come quite far in modeling contextual associations and probabilistic implications, they still fail to exhibit a grasp of “meaning" that even children have little difficulty with. We aim to create new machine learning approaches explicitly targeting the specific challenge of massive scale automatic acquisition of the kind of lexical semantics that are conventionally used to frame socioculturally relevant current topics. We directly address stated needs of the United Nations Secretary General’s data science and AI-focused research and innovation initiative, UN Global Pulse, who, like us, believe the social impact of this new research direction has become critical to many of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) articulated and adopted by the UN. The biggest obstacle is not a lack of economic or technological resources, but rather the way misleading framings undermine social will to reallocate those resources to tackling SDGs. The world is suffering the tremendous influence of viral memetic framings spreading unchecked over social networks and the internet, with serious consequences to public policy. To avoid the philosophical morass of defining “meme”, we restrict this groundwork laying stage to shallow memetic frames: semantic frames in the style of PropBank, consisting of a set of alternations of roughly equivalent lexical frames that have become conventionally adopted to shape perspectives on socioculturally current topics. Being able to machine learn lexical memes on a large scale will be the key to enabling a new generation of more relevant, practical models for deeper natural language understanding. At the same time, in extracting explicit symbolic knowledge while developing and applying new probabilistic and neural learning techniques, we aim to advance the state of the art in explainable AI, thus making machine learning less of an opaque black box. 虽然我们在数据饥渴型机器学习方面有很多激动人心的短期进展，然而即使是这些最新的机器学习自然语言处理算法依然在分析现状和理解语义方面有着诸多限制。大多数语句的“意思”并非存在于表面的逻辑层面，而是依附在大量互相关联而又通常形式随意的描述抽象情景的文化习俗上。该如何理解这个世界？这并非一个仅需要对具体“客观知识”建模便能解决的问题，而是一个需要对由社会文化塑造的现实情境主观认知建模才能解决的问题。几十年来，许多AI亚社区打着“常识”、“类人”、“直观”等旗号，尝试从各种方面解决该问题而困难重重。虽然我们的方法，不论基于神经网络还是统计学的，在描述上下文关联和概率影响上有着长足进步，但是这些方法依然无法匹敌即便是儿童都具有的理解“意思”的能力。 为此，我们致力于开发一个新的机器学习方法，专一地解决如下挑战：如何大量自动获取用于描述社会文化相关话题的词义。我们直接响应“UN Global Pulse”，即联合国秘书长的数据科学和AI的研究创新的号召。该号召和我们一样，都相信这个研究方向对于联合国研讨并采纳的多项可持续发展目标（SDGs）有着至关重要的影响。现今最大的障碍并非我们的社会缺乏经济和科技资源，而是各种误导性的言论降低了整个社会对于实现SDGs的意向。不经审查的模因框架在媒体和社交网络上病毒式传播，公共的政策被此严重影响，世界的进展因此受到阻碍。 为避免如何定义“模因”这个哲学陷阱，我们这一项基础层面的研究将限制在浅层模因框架中：浅层模因框架类似于PropBank，是一个大体相近但更改过的词框架的集合，这些词框架是已经被接纳并用于塑造社会文化当前话题的词框架。能够对这些词的模因进行大规模机器学习，是孕育新一代更加关联实际，切合实际的深度自然语言理解模型的钥匙。在提取规范的符号性知识的同时，新的基于概率学和基于神经网络的机器学习方法亦得到了开发和应用，这将产生可解释AI的前沿进展，推进机器学习去黑盒化的进程。

16212120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212120.value: 隨著第5代（5G）移動網絡的出現，無線通信技術正處於萬眾矚目的輝煌時期，並正以前所未有的的轉變以及革命性的飛躍，有望在2030年將人類帶入6G時代。與此同時，具有重大變革的後5G(Beyond 5G)網絡將通過發展人工智能和大數據分析技術將 “互聯萬物”轉變為“互聯智能”。這壹轉變將會使未來的無線和移動網絡極大程度區別於現有網絡，從而徹底釋放無線通信對海量應用支持的潛力，包括物聯網、觸感網以及無縫虛擬\增強現實等。另壹方面，這類應用也會進壹步驅動革命性的技術進步，從而使網絡能夠適用更加嚴苛和挑戰的網絡環境及需求，諸如無限制的無線連接（1 Tbps速率下）、海量機器類型通信、泛在持續在線式全球寬帶接入、人工智能層級化組網、海量低時延控制（低於1毫秒端到端時延）等。 無蜂窩大規模天線陣列技術是壹種顛覆性的新興技術，其可以看作是對未來5G++乃至6G網絡具有決定性的核心技術。該技術可以為移動網絡帶來極為廣泛的性能優勢，包括極大的數據吞吐量、超低時延、超高可靠性、巨大的移動能效提升以及泛在的網絡均勻覆蓋等。在無蜂窩大規模天線陣列技術中，大量的分布式接入點通過前傳網絡連接到壹個中心處理單元，從而可以在廣泛覆蓋區域內采用相同的時間或頻率資源協作式地服務壹定數量的用戶。與傳統的蜂窩系統相反，在無蜂窩天線陣列網絡中通常是無蜂窩或無蜂窩界限。因此，作為壹項重大變革，該技術無疑能夠突破現有無線網絡的壹項主要瓶頸，即小區間強干擾。 本項目研究主要致力於解決能夠推動大規模無蜂窩天線陣列技術部署應用的基礎研究問題。特別地，項目中將聯合功率控制、導頻分配、接入點選擇等方法研究有效的信道估計和獲取技術，從而平衡網絡吞吐量、網絡覆蓋範圍、時延、公平性等多項性能指標。特別值得關註的是項目中采用基於機器學習的優化方法並且研究高計算效率的信號處理技術，來減少前傳網絡的開銷，從而實現傳輸預編碼、功率控制、信道估計多種技術高效協作。

16212120.label: Realisation of objectives
16212120.value: The advent of 6G heralds a transformative era of connectivity. At the forefront of this transformation is cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), recognized as a pivotal enabler for enhancing both spectral and energy efficiency. This approach addresses critical challenges faced by existing wireless systems, particularly in high-density environments where user demands continue to escalate. This project focuses on the development of cell-free massive MIMO technology, which is increasingly recognized as a crucial component for future 6G wireless communication networks. As a disruptive technology, cell-free massive MIMO is poised to be a key enabler for enhancing both wireless spectrum efficiency and energy efficiency. It addresses the numerous challenges posed by existing wireless systems, particularly in terms of increasing user demands and the complexity of network management in high-density environments. In our efforts, we endeavored to make substantial contributions to the broader field of wireless communication by concentrating on the design and optimization of distributed detection schemes specifically tailored for cell-free massive MIMO systems. This includes addressing the scalability of signal processing tasks as the number of users increases, which is vital for maintaining system performance and reliability in real-world scenarios. Additionally, we focused on improving the acquisition of channel state information (CSI) through the development of methods designed for efficient CSI acquisition in distributed systems. This enhancement is essential for enabling better performance under real-world conditions and ensuring the overall viability and effectiveness of cell-free massive MIMO systems. We are excited to report substantial progress toward achieving the project's goals, resulting in several noteworthy publications. These publications not only reflect our commitment to advancing knowledge in this dynamic field but also signify our dedication to pushing the boundaries of current wireless technologies. During the first reporting period, our research focused on several core areas that yielded promising results: • Development of Efficient Detection Algorithms: The project prioritized creating scalable and effective algorithms for distributed MIMO detection. We proposed a non-linear detector based on the expectation propagation (EP) principle. This iterative method enables the recovery of transmitted data from received signals and is applicable across both sub-6GHz and mmWave frequency spectrums. The flexibility of this detector is crucial as it allows for adaptability in various operational environments, enhancing the overall functionality of cell-free massive MIMO systems. • Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection: A distributed joint channel estimation and data detection (JCD) algorithm was developed to tackle the significant challenge of dealing with noisy or unavailable CSI. This algorithm cleverly integrates linear minimum mean square error (MMSE) channel estimation with distributed EP detection, leading to a marked improvement in detection accuracy. Furthermore, it enables the use of non-orthogonal pilots, which helps to reduce pilot overhead—an essential factor in optimizing system resources and maintaining high levels of performance. • Performance Evaluation: To ensure the robustness of our solutions, we established an analytical framework for evaluating the performance of the developed algorithms. This framework utilizes state evolution equations, allowing precise performance predictions without the need for time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations. Key performance metrics, such as mean square error (MSE) and average bit error rate (BER), were analytically determined and optimized, significantly enhancing the reliability and efficiency of the proposed solutions. This rigorous performance evaluation is critical for validating our research and ensuring that the developed algorithms meet the high standards required for practical implementation in future wireless networks. In the second reporting period, and due to the latest advances in the field, our efforts shifted towards developing innovative solutions for cell-free massive MIMO technologies, which have the potential to contribute to theoretical advancements and practical implications for the future of wireless communications. Our major contributions include: • Optimizing Cluster Formation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO: We developed a novel Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based clustering technique for access points (APs) in cell-free massive MIMO (CFMM) systems. This approach addresses the challenges of optimizing cluster formation to enhance user data rates. Unlike traditional methods that rely on multiple iterations to determine the optimal number of clusters, our method formulates an optimization problem that simultaneously maximizes the average downlink rate per user and the number of clusters. This results in a more efficient clustering process with significantly reduced computational complexity, allowing for faster convergence and better scalability in practical applications. • RIS-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G Networks: We explored reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided CF massive MIMO systems, addressing their architectural designs, operational principles, and application scenarios. Key issues studied include system models, channel models, communication protocols, and multilayer signal processing frameworks that differentiate RIS-aided CF MIMO from traditional systems. We also considered practical challenges such as hardware impairments and electromagnetic interference, offering insights into solutions that facilitate the implementation of RIS-aided CF MIMO systems. Additionally, we explored the synergy between these systems and emerging 6G technologies, such as millimeter-wave communications and unmanned aerial vehicles. • Spatial Correlation and Mutual Coupling on Cell-Free Massive MIMO: We undertook a comprehensive analysis of cell-free massive MIMO systems, focusing on the effects of spatial correlation and mutual coupling among multi-antenna access points (APs) and users. We derived closed-form expressions for downlink achievable spectral efficiency (SE) and investigated how reducing inter-antenna distances impacts performance. By incorporating a practical power consumption model, we assessed the energy efficiency (EE) of the system while considering power control coefficients, providing a holistic understanding of the trade-offs between SE and EE. • Mobile Cell-Free Massive MIMO: Our research included a comprehensive study of mobile cell-free massive MIMO communication systems, outlining key deployment architectures and application scenarios. We identified four key structures—star, chain, ring, and tree—tailored to environments such as transportation, UAVs, and satellite communications. We also proposed solutions to mobility issues, channel calibration, and scalable networking, enhancing performance and reliability in mobile settings. • SWIPT-Enabled Cell-Free Massive MIMO-NOMA Networks: We developed a novel approach to optimizing simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) in CF-mMIMO networks utilizing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We derived closed-form expressions for signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and harvested power, formulating a sum rate maximization problem while considering user equipment (UE) clustering and power control. Our machine learning-based solution combines K-means clustering for UE optimization with a multi-agent deep Q-network (MA-DQN) for joint optimization of power control and splitting ratios. In conclusion, the advancements made in this project have not only met but exceeded our initial objectives, significantly enriching the theoretical and practical foundations of cell-free massive MIMO technology. The innovative solutions developed, ranging from efficient detection algorithms to optimized cluster formation techniques, represent a paradigm shift in addressing challenges within next-generation networks. Our research responds to the increasing demands for higher efficiency and reliability in wireless communication as we move into the 6G era. By enhancing spectral efficiency and improving energy consumption, our work lays a solid foundation for future exploration and refinement of cell-free massive MIMO technologies. The practical implications ensure that these solutions are not only theoretically sound but also ready for real-world application, making them adaptable to the complexities of modern communication systems. Ultimately, our contributions reinforce the significance of cell-free massive MIMO as a transformative technology with the potential to redefine the future of wireless communications. Further details about the results can be found in our published work listed in the Research Output Section.

16212120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212120.value: Our project on cell-free massive MIMO technology has yielded significant findings and research outcomes that advance the field of wireless communication, particularly in the context of 6G networks. Central to our efforts was the development of innovative algorithms and methodologies aimed at enhancing system performance in high-density environments. One of the major outcomes was the creation of efficient detection algorithms, specifically a non-linear detector based on the expectation propagation (EP) principle. This iterative method significantly improves the recovery of transmitted data across both sub-6GHz and mmWave frequency spectrums. Its adaptability allows it to perform effectively in diverse operational conditions, enhancing the overall functionality of cell-free massive MIMO systems. Additionally, the development of a distributed joint channel estimation and data detection (JCD) algorithm marked a critical advancement. This algorithm integrates linear MMSE channel estimation with distributed EP detection, addressing the challenges posed by noisy or unavailable CSI. Importantly, it allows the use of non-orthogonal pilots, thereby reducing pilot overhead and optimizing system resources, which is essential for maintaining high performance in real-world applications. Performance evaluation was another key focus area, leading to the establishment of an analytical framework that predicts algorithm performance using state evolution equations. This innovative approach enables precise assessments of key metrics such as MSE and average BER, which are critical for validating the robustness and reliability of the developed solutions. Our research has also included optimizing cluster formation techniques through a novel Gaussian mixture model (GMM). This method efficiently addresses the challenges of cluster optimization, simultaneously maximizing average downlink rates and reducing computational complexity. Our findings indicated that unbalanced clustering strategies consistently yield higher spectral efficiency per user. Furthermore, we explored the integration of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) within cell-free massive MIMO systems, addressing architectural designs and practical challenges. This work highlights the synergy between RIS and emerging 6G technologies, paving the way for innovative applications. The study of spatial correlation and mutual coupling effects led to insights into balancing spectral and energy efficiency, while our research on mobile cell-free massive MIMO explored deployment architectures and solutions for mobility challenges. Finally, our work on SWIPT-enabled networks utilizing non-orthogonal multiple access showcased the potential for optimizing simultaneous wireless information and power transfer. Overall, these findings not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of cell-free massive MIMO but also provide practical solutions for future wireless communication systems.

16212120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212120.value: The research on cell-free massive MIMO technology presents significant potential for further development, particularly as we approach the rollout of 6G networks. Key areas for exploration include enhancing algorithm efficiency and robustness, particularly in dynamic and diverse environments. Future work could focus on refining the detection algorithms and improving the joint channel estimation techniques to support a broader range of user scenarios and mobility patterns. Additionally, the integration of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) offers exciting prospects for optimizing signal propagation and enhancing network performance. Further research could investigate adaptive clustering techniques and machine learning approaches to enable real-time optimization of resource allocation and user management. A proposed course of action includes establishing collaborative partnerships with industry stakeholders to pilot these technologies in real-world environments. This would provide valuable feedback for iterative improvements. Moreover, expanding the scope of simulation studies to include various deployment scenarios—such as urban, rural, and vehicular networks—will enhance the applicability of our findings. Finally, pursuing interdisciplinary research that combines wireless communication with emerging fields like AI and IoT will be crucial in addressing the complexities of future communication systems, ensuring that cell-free massive MIMO technology remains at the forefront of wireless innovation.

16212120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212120.value: The arrival of 6G wireless networks represents a transformative leap in connectivity, offering unprecedented speeds, greater capacity, and ultra-reliable low-latency communication. This research project focuses on a game-changing technology known as cell-free massive MIMO, which is essential for the future of 6G. Envision a system where numerous distributed access points (APs) connect to a central processing unit via a front-haul network, collaboratively serving multiple users with shared time and frequency resources. Unlike traditional systems that depend on a single tower, this method provides a consistently strong and reliable wireless connection while addressing a significant challenge: inter-cell interference, a common limitation in wireless networks. Cell-free massive MIMO excels in managing a high volume of users, ensuring faster speeds. As our world becomes increasingly interconnected, this technology meets the growing demand for robust and uninterrupted service, paving the way for innovations in smart cities, autonomous vehicles, and advanced healthcare. Beyond just enhancing internet and wireless speeds, this project facilitates a future where everyday devices and critical infrastructure communicate seamlessly. By laying the groundwork for 6G, this research contributes to a connected world that enhances daily life and drives technological advancements across various sectors, ultimately shaping a more efficient and connected society.

16212720.label: Realisation of objectives
16212720.value: We have conducted holistic study of ocean circulation over the continental shelf in the northern South China Sea, by investigating (1) the spatiotemporal characteristics and dynamics of the circulation intrinsically (Obj 1); (2) linkages of the intrinsic dynamics of the continental shelf with the extrinsic dynamics in the adjacent broad South China Sea and western Pacific Ocean (Obj 2) through (3) downscaling couplings of physical and numerical connections (Obj 3). We published total 11 papers with additional one under revision and one resubmitting. All are in international top journal in our field. We outline the details in these three respects (objectives). Objective 1 Intrinsic Characteristics and Dynamics 1.1. Responses of Coastal Upwelling to Tidally Induced Bottom Friction Dynamics and Plume-Modulated Geostrophy. We used a high-resolution cross-shelf two-dimensional numerical model to investigate the response of coastal wind-driven upwelling circulation to barotropic tidal forcing and lateral buoyant discharge over a broad continental shelf. We found that the tidally amplified asymmetric friction effect arising from the interaction between tidal and subtidal currents modulated the upwelling structure across the shelf. The responses of upwelling circulation to tidal and lateral buoyancy forcing highlighted in this process-oriented study are fundamental for interpreting more complex wind-driven shelf circulation. 1.2. Dynamics paradigm of geostrophic cross-isobath transport (GCT) over highly variable shelf topographies. Flow-topography interaction is the key dynamics that governs the circulation over highly variable continental shelf, and its underlying dynamics remains as an active research topic. Based on results of observations and 3D process-oriented numerical modeling, we illustrated the 3D upwelling circulation and variability over the characteristic steep, concave, uniform (2D) and widened shelf topographic regimes in Northern South China Sea (NSCS). We presented the geostrophic cross-isobath transport (GCT) dynamics associated with the formation of the along-isobath pressure gradient force (PGFy*) to interpret the unique circulation and variability of wind-driven upwelling circulation over these shelf topographic regimes. This study provides holistic analyses based on the framework of GCT dynamics to enrich the wind-driven shelf circulation dynamics over highly variable topographic regimes. 1.3. Variability of the Bottom Boundary Layer Induced by the Dynamics of the Cross‐Isobath Transport Over a Variable Shelf. This study investigated the dynamics impact of wind‐driven upslope transport on the bottom boundary layer (BBL). We found that the current‐induced instability (determined by current intensity) and the upslope buoyancy transport‐induced stabilizing process (determined by current direction) jointly balance the BBL dynamics. Objective 2. Extrinsic Dynamics 2.1 Hotspots of the stokes rotating circulation in a large marginal sea. Our study demonstrates that the rotating circulation in the South China is structured by energetic hotspots with large vorticity arising from unique dynamics in the marginal sea and is identifiable by the constraints of Stokes Theorem. Our findings provide new insights on the dis tinguishing features of the rotating circulation and the dominant physics with the objectives of advancing our knowledge and improving modeling of marginal seas 2.2 Dynamics of the Layered Circulation Inferred from Kinetic Energy Pathway in the South China Sea. We investigated the mean kinetic energy (MKE) and eddy kinetic energy (EKE) in the South China Sea to illustrate the dynamics of the vertically rotating cyclonic–anticyclonic–cyclonic (CAC) circulation in the upper, middle, and deep layers. This study provides a new interpretation to the maintenance of CAC circulation from energy prospect. 2.3. On the north equatorial current spatiotemporal modes and responses in the western boundary currents. We utilized the validated three-dimensional and time-dependent China Sea Multi-scale Ocean Modeling System to investigate the variability of the WBCs and the physical processes linked with the upstream NEC and associated with the circulation.The latitude-dependent KC and MC strengthen downstream from the NEC bifurcation (NB) and are maintained by the northern and southern parts of the NEC, respectively. By resolving spatiotemporal modes in NEC-KC-MC, the study provides a new understanding to the WBCs in the NEC-WBCs current system. 2.4. Parameterization of the Vertical Mixing for the Luzon Undercurrent in the Northern Western Pacific Ocean. We found that a. Baroclinic pressure gradient force due to strong isopycnal tilting in the thermocline is crucial to the formation and maintenance of the Luzon Undercurrent (LUC) b. The strong isopycnal tilting is induced by locally enhanced vertical mixing. Nonlinearity and submesoscales also benefit the LUC formation, c A Munk‐like adaptive mixing scheme is designed to capture the LUC, providing significant improvement over previous results. 2.5. Characteristics and Formation of the Luzon Undercurrent in the Western North Pacific: Observational Study. We found a. The Luzon Undercurrent (LUC) is contributed to and characterized by waters from the Deep North Equatorial Current and Luzon Strait middle-layer outflow, and is locally sustained by baroclinic forcing. b Temporally, the LUC intensity has weak seasonality and significant intra-seasonal variation, with two peaks in May/June and October. c Spatially, the LUC shifts from in-shore to off-shore from early summer to late fall, originating from the interior North Pacific and South China Sea middle layer, respectively. Objective 3. Downscaling Couplings 3.1. Impacts of high-resolution atmospheric forcing and air-sea coupling on coastal ocean circulation off the Pearl River Estuary. We investigated the impacts of high-resolution atmospheric forcing and ocean-atmosphere coupling on the estuary-shelf ocean simulation off the Pearl River Estuary. We conducted process and dynamics analyses of the wind-driven coastal ocean circulation under atmospheric flux forcing from (1) global reanalysis data, (2) a high resolution regional atmospheric model, and (3) an air-sea coupled model during an upwelling-favorable wind. The results revealed that the high-resolution atmospheric model significantly improved the representations of the near-surface wind field and air temperature. 3.2 Variability in coastal downwelling circulation in response to high-resolution regional atmospheric forcing off the Pearl River estuary. We investigated the variabilities in coastal circulation and dynamics in response to spatiotemporally variable high-resolution atmospheric forcing off the Pearl River estuary during the downwelling wind. Our investigation focused on the dynamics of coastal downwelling circulation in response to variable atmospheric forcing of (1) single station observation, (2) global reanalysis data, and (3) a high resolution regional atmospheric model. We found that the high-resolution atmospheric model significantly improved the representations of the near-surface wind and air temperature, and the ocean model driven by the high-resolution and spatially variable atmospheric forcing improved the circulation and associated hydrographic properties in the coastal ocean.

16212720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212720.value: We investigation intrinsic win-driven ocean circulation dynamics over the variable shelf topography in the northern South China Sea (NSCS) and identified key dynamics theorem of Geostrophic Cross-isobath Transport or GCT (outputs 3, 4, 10, 11 and 12). GCT unveils the underlying governing physics of shelf circulation, which, for the first time, outlines the flow-topography interaction. We found the local topographic controls on the circulation and quantitatively assessed its interaction with the remote forcing. Based on the GCT, we further develop the boundary layer dynamics by providing new dynamics through integrating GCT with classic boundary layer dynamics. We then further investigate external forcing to the circulation in NSCS from adjacent South China Sea (SCS) and western Pacific Ocean. We found the characteristic 3-layer circulation in the SCS and, for the first time, pointed out that the dynamics of slope topography (outputs 1, 2) is the ‘hotspot’ that shapes the 3-layer circulation. Based on this framework, we outline the momentum, vorticity and energy balances in the SCS circulation and identify its 3D circulation, particularly over the hotspot slope that connects with the NSCS shelf. We further investigated the SCS circulation under the forcing from the western Pacific Ocean through western boundary surface and under currents (outputs 6, 7, 8). In this part, we made important progresses on the understanding the western Pacific ocean. This undercurrent is linked with the middle layer circulation in the SCS and thus the cross-slope water exchange with the NSCS. We, for the first time, provides the formation mechanism of the western boundary current, and develops a physics-based parameterization scheme to overcome the failure enrapturing this undercurrent in all previous numerical models. To better understand the important terrestrial buoyancy forcing to the coastal circulation, we also investigate the characteristics of the streamflow in the adjacent Pearl River Basin to quantify the freshwater discharge onto the NSCS shelf (output 9). Based on the both intrinsic and extrinsic study of dynamics to the wind-driven circulation in the NSCS, we have downscaled forcing to numerically investigate the shelf circulation over the continental shelf under multiple forcings of wind and variable shelf topography locally and current intrusion from the SCS remotely.

16212720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212720.value: Potential development includes (1) integration of waves and Langmuir turbulence dynamics into the shelf circulation in the NSCS; (2) development of the biogeochemical response to new findings of holistic ocean circulation in the continental shelf of NSCS from this project.

16212720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212720.value: The ocean circulation over the coastal ocean of the northern South China Sea (NSCS) is internally regulated by wind forcing and variation of bathymetry of the ocean. This wind-driven flow-topography is physically complex itself, yet the coastal circulation is also externally controlled by current intrusion from the adjacent South China Sea (SCS). Similarly, SCS circulation is also governed by both SCS circulation physics and forcing from the adjacent western Pacific Ocean (WPO), and unclear to us. This study conducted fundamental study of wind-driven circulation dynamics and proposed a dynamics theorem of Geostrophic Cross-isobath Transport (GCT), which, for the first time, provides a new framework to relate coastal upwelling and downwelling with the formation of pressure gradient forcing (PGF) along the isobath of topography. We further provided the physical processes that lead to PGF formation. This finding provides not only new understanding to the coastal ocean circulation, but also improves our capability to predict the 3D ocean circulation and transport of biogeochemical substances. Meanwhile, our new findings of hotspot circulation in the SCS and the related western boundary undercurrent in WPO provide completed internal and external forcing spectrum for the understanding and predicting the coastal ocean circulation in the NSCS.

16213120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213120.value: 大規模雲計算平台上運行著大量的在線雲服務應用。這些應用不斷接受用戶提交的動態請求並予以即時處理。在線應用通常以容器形式部署，且會運行相當長的時間（數天至數月），故而也被稱為常駐應用。這些常駐應用佔據了雲平台的大多數計算資源。如何以最優方式對常駐容器進行智能化調度是雲平台運維必須要解決的主要問題。然而，常駐應用的調度問題非常困難。應用容器的性能通常會受到彼此的影響。例如，將多個容器調度到同一台服務器上會導致資源競爭，從而造成性能下降。應用容器之間往往也具有數據流依賴，即一個容器的輸出會被導入為另一個應用容器的輸入。將具有數據流依賴的多個容器部署在同一台服務器上可以避免它們之間的網絡通信開銷，從而帶來顯著的性能提升。 現有的容器調度系統需要運維人員將容器之間的性能影響總結為一系列的調度約束規則，諸如親和（兩個容器盡量部署在一起）及反親和（兩個容器盡量分開放置）。根據這些調度要求，調度系統使用人工設計的啟發式算法進行調度，盡可能滿足最多的約束。然而，我們的實驗證明這一業界常用的調度方法往往會帶來非常低效的調度結果並導致嚴重的性能損失。 在這一研究項目裡，我們將設計一種新穎的基於機器學習的智能化容器調度策略，從而取代現有的人工調度方案。我們將使用強化學習，利用雲平台已積累的海量歷史數據訓練調度器自動學習最優調度策略。但是，這一方法的主要技術難點在於問題的規模所帶來的超高複雜度。訓練強化學習的深度神經網絡通常需要消耗大量的計算資源，且問題越複雜效率就越低下。考慮到雲平台上部署的海量常駐容器，直接使用常規強化學習方法所帶來的複雜度將不可接受。我們將提出一系列新穎的強化學習優化方法來解決這一難題。 我們的核心想法是使用分層強化學習技術來大幅降低訓練複雜度。具體來說，我們會將一個複雜的調度問題分解為一系列的子問題。這些子問題分別處於不同的決策層，並且具有較小的狀態和決策空間。所有的子問題均具有相似的結構，從而可以使用一個通用的強化學習訓練模型來左出決策。我們將會實現這一解決方案，並據此開發出一套基於強化學習的自動化常駐應用調度系統。我們會在真實的雲平台上利用生產集群的數據集對我們的調度系統進行深入、細緻、全面的測試。我們的系統最終將會以開源軟件的方式發布。

16213120.label: Realisation of objectives
16213120.value: In this project, we have developed an intelligent long-running application (LRA) scheduler by utilizing state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. We refer to our research output stated in Sections 8 and 9, where conference paper #n is denoted as Cn and journal paper #m is denoted as Jn. - Realisation of Objective-1 Training a neural network using policy gradient requires the RL agent to frequently interact with the environment, which is extremely time-consuming for LRA scheduling. In real systems, it takes at least minutes to deploy containers and measure their performance. As RL training typically requires tens of thousands of iterations to complete, having the scheduler directly interacting with a real cluster is too slow to be practical. We have developed a high-fidelity cluster environment simulator that can faithfully predict container performance given a placement [C1]. This allows the learning to be performed with simulated experiments without deploying containers in a real cluster. Particularly, instead of modeling low-level resource interference based on contentions on CPU caches or memory bandwidth, which may not be available in production traces, we turn to high-level performance metrics such as container throughput and request latency. We then predict how those metrics may change under varying container placements. In particular, we log the machine-level container co-location vectors along with the observed RPS/latency of each resident container, and use them as the training samples for the simulator. Our simulator uses multivariate Random Forests (RF) as the main regressor to characterize container interactions. RF method uses a combination of decision trees to perform the regression task, and can make accurate predictions with a small number of training data. It is also resilient to overfitting when supplied with a large number of repetitive samples. Both properties make the RF regressor an ideal choice for our simulator. We have also extended our performance prediction algorithm and simulator to long-running machine learning inference services [C5], GPU-sharing containers [C9], data-flow computation services [C3], and large-scale production trace analysis in Alibaba clusters [C6, C7]. - Realisation of Objective-2 We have designed an efficient deep reinforcement learning algorithm for LRA scheduling that scales to large clusters where tens of thousands of containers run on thousands of machines [C1]. Our solution employs three novel designs. The first is the hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) techniques. The main idea is to decompose an initially complex learning task into multiple layers of simpler subtasks, following a divide-and-conquer approach. Each subtask is independently modeled as a single MDP (Markov Decision Process) with its own state, action, and reward. Specifically, given a container, we learn to place it following a decision tree. At the root level, we divide the cluster into K partitions and learn to determine which sub-cluster provides the optimal placement. Following our choice, we descend to a lower level of the tree, where we subdivide the selected sub-cluster into K partitions, and learn to choose the one that contains the optimal placement. As we traverse down the decision tree, we recursively narrow our search for the container placement, until it pinpoints a single machine. In the end, the scheduler makes a sequence of K-choose-1 decisions that can be individually learned at each level by training simple RL models. Note that at one level all the decision-making tasks have the same learning structure, enabling a shared model to be reused by all tasks. Second, to accelerate the learning process, we have also pretrained a sub-scheduler for general workloads in a small sub-cluster. This allows the traverse down the decision tree to stop at a high level when reaching that sub-cluster, where the pretrained sub-scheduler is used to decide the container placement. In addition, we have designed a transfer learning mechanism that further reduces the training time to tens of minutes. Our trace analysis shows that LRA scheduling events in clusters are similar in a long period of time, which implies that a well-trained LRA scheduler can be possibly reused. Therefore, upon a scheduling event, we opt to train a scheduler based on the results from prior scheduling events. In our evaluation, using these techniques leads to over 100× training speedup. The third novel contribution in our design is a projection-based proximal policy optimization (PPPO) algorithm, which schedules LRA containers under the operation constraints. Operation constraints are usually specified by cluster operators to meet various deployment requirements. For example, a business-critical LRA may require its multiple instance replicas to run on different machines in order to provide high availability against node failures; when launching a new cloud service, phased deployment is commonly used, where container placements are confined to a small set of machines in the initial phase before committed in the entire cluster. Operation constraints can be hard or soft: hard constraints must be strictly enforced, whereas soft constraints can be violated within a pre-defined threshold at the expense of performance degradation, e.g., reduced fault tolerance. We integrated PPPO with Integer Linear optimization techniques to handle the hard constraints. Compared with the traditional constrained policy optimization algorithms using RL techniques, our policy can satisfy all operation constraints and obtain high-quality LRA placement performance with significantly less training time. Built on our LRA scheduling algorithm, we have developed efficient schedulers for machine learning workloads [C6, C8, C9, J2], serverless inference [C2], and auto-configuration systems for cloud-native inference serving [C5]. - Realisation of Objective-3 We have implemented the proposed learning-based LRA scheduler as a pluggable scheduling service in Docker Swarm. Our scheduler first collects abundant container co-location data samples by an Performance Profiler, using direct benchmarking or trace analysis. It logs the machine-level container co-location vectors along with the observed throughput/latency of each resident container. The collected data is fed to a Cluster Environment Simulator. The Simulator builds a random forest regressor with scikit-learn, taking an ensemble of 100 classifying decision trees with a maximum depth of 20. Utilizing the Simulator, the scheduler initializes the RL model training for each group of container launching requests, which is an iterative interaction process between the Simulator and the RL agent. We implemented the proposed PPPO algorithm in the RL agent in TensorFlow. The trained model then produces optimized container placement decision. The scheduler also batches episodes of agent-environment interactions and trains the policy network in a mini-batch manner. To speed up the batching process, it distributes the agent-environment interaction tasks to processes with Ray and execute them in a synchronous parallel manner, substantially reducing the data sampling time. We have evaluated our LRA scheduler on EC2 clusters with 9 to 729 nodes using container workloads of seven real applications, covering machine learning, stream processing, I/O and storage services. Compared with the state-of-the-art LRA schedulers, our solution meets all the operation constraints and achieves 25% higher request throughput. In particular, our proposed PPPO algorithm reduces the RL model update time by up to 40%. When combined with transfer learning, the model training process is further accelerated by 6×. - Realisation of Objective-4 We have released our scheduler and cluster simulator as open-source software in GitHub [C1, C9], with 84 stars as of November 2024. Our work [C5, C9] has been adopted by Alibaba.

16213120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213120.value: This project studied the optimal container placement problem for long-running applications (LRAs) in large clusters, where LRA containers demonstrate sophisticated performance interactions. Current LRA schedulers define placement constraints to manage these interactions, such as affinity and anti-affinity, and attempt to satisfy as many constraints as possible using human-generated heuristics. We started to identify three fundamental drawbacks of constraint-based scheduling. First, it requires operators to painstakingly identify complex container interactions and manually specify them as constraints, which can be labor-intensive and error-prone. Second, these constraints offer qualitative guidelines without quantifying their actual performance impacts, leading to sub-optimal scheduling quality. Third, the complexity of these constraints can create intractable optimization problems, forcing schedulers to rely on simplistic heuristics that compromise performance. To address these inefficiencies, we proposed an intelligent LRA scheduler that learns to make optimal container placement decisions using the state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning techniques. Our solution employs three novel designs: (1) a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) algorithm that decomposes an initially complex learning task into multiple layers of simpler subtasks, following a divide-and-conquer approach, (2) pretraining a sub-scheduler for general workloads in a small sub-cluster together with a transfer learning mechanism that reduces the training time to tens of minutes, and (3) a projection-based proximal policy optimization (PPPO) algorithm that optimally schedules LRA containers under the operation constraints. We showed through extensive evaluations that these algorithms together optimize various performance objectives, including maximizing query throughput, improving cluster utilization, minimizing SLO violations, and ensuring fair sharing. We have implemented the proposed algorithms as a pluggable LRA scheduler in Docker Swarm and evaluated its performance through real cloud deployment on AWS EC2 and trace-driven experiments. The results conclusively demonstrated that our scheduler optimizes various performance objectives, including maximizing query throughput, improving cluster utilization, minimizing SLO violations, and ensuring fair sharing. The project has led to fruitful results published in various top-tier conferences and journals (listed in the research output), including NSDI, ATC, SoCC, and TPDS. The scheduler and simulator we developed in this project has been released as open-source software at https://github.com/hkust-adsl/kubernetes-scheduler-simulator, with 84 stars in GitHub as of November 2024. The systems and algorithms have been adopted by Alibaba.

16213120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213120.value: The cluster scheduler is a vital component in large-scale production clouds. This project focuses on designing a reinforcement-learning-based container orchestrator to optimize the performance of long-running applications while meeting operational constraints like failure isolation and incremental deployment. However, the effectiveness of RL-based scheduling heavily relies on the accuracy of the cluster environment simulator. Our current simulator is primarily designed for CPU clusters, but with the rise of machine learning (ML), high-performance GPU clusters are becoming more prevalent in the cloud. To accurately predict ML application performance on GPU clusters, a comprehensive monitoring system is needed to collect performance data such as GPU utilization, memory footprint, I/O and network bandwidth, and kernel metrics. Additionally, the computation and communication semantics of ML jobs should be incorporated into the simulator for high-fidelity simulation. We plan to extend our simulator to GPU clusters running AI tasks, enabling our RL-based scheduling approach to manage GPU containers effectively. Another critical aspect is the explainability of RL scheduling decisions. Operators need to understand the rationale behind scheduling decisions and identify root causes in case of incidents. We aim to explore new theories and approaches, like explainable AI, to address these explainability and accountability challenges.

16213120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213120.value: Production datacenters manage two main types of workloads: long-running applications (LRAs) for online services and batch jobs for offline processing. Unlike batch jobs, LRAs operate in long-lived containers, facilitating real-time query servicing without the overhead of launching new instances. LRAs are crucial for business-critical, user-facing services with strict service-level objectives (SLOs) and thus receive priority scheduling with substantial dedicated resources. Scheduling LRAs is challenging due to their complex performance interactions and data dependencies. Current schedulers use placement constraints to manage these interactions, relying on human-generated heuristics. However, this approach demands extensive manual effort, provides only qualitative guidelines without quantifying performance impacts, and often results in intractable optimization problems. This research proposes utilizing deep reinforcement learning (RL) as a viable alternative for LRA scheduling. By formulating LRA scheduling as an RL problem, an intelligent scheduler can learn optimal placements autonomously. The scheduler optimizes various performance objectives, inferring container interactions from past data. To address scalability, hierarchical learning techniques have been developed, breaking down scheduling into simpler sub-problems, together with novel transfer learning mechanisms. The new RL-based scheduler has been implemented on real clusters and has demonstrated substantial improvements over existing constraint-based scheduling solutions across various settings.

16213420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213420.value: 基於矽的集成電路（IC）是最強大和最成熟的微/納米電子技術，可實現現代生活中無處不在的信號處理，存儲和人工智能。然而，由於其固有的晶體和能帶結構的限制，Si不能與光子有效地相互作用並且不能緩慢地傳輸電子。諸如高頻和光子器件之類的利基應用已經被化合物半導體所佔據，該化合物半導體具有固有的波長調諧靈活性，並且可以促進電子的超高速傳輸。近幾十年來，對射頻（RF），發光和光通信設備的需求不斷增長，推動了化合物半導體（主要來自元素週期表的第III和V列）的發展。這些材料現在廣泛用於顯示，照明和電信光纖網絡。用化合物半導體製成的光子集成電路價格昂貴並且受到限制。但是，還沒有一個通用的公式可以將兩全其美的技術相結合-化合物半導體的高性能和特定功能性與Si可製造性的效率和成本效益。 矽光子學是一個擴展領域，旨在通過採用非常成功的Si IC基礎架構來擴展集成光子學，以用於電信，數據通信和傳感。數十年來，利用光子技術在遠距離傳輸大量數據的有效性已廣為人知。除了速度和帶寬優勢外，通過光子而不是電子發送數據可能會更加節能。因此，實現高效的設備和電路是下一代信息技術和計算的集成光子學領域的重中之重。最終目標是將光子學與電子設備集成在同一矽平台上，以便可以在單個微型矽芯片上以節能，高速和最小延遲的方式進行數據通信和處理。多年來，人們一直致力於將高性能的III-V有源器件集成到矽上，以與無源元件和Si光子學的波導集成在一起。為此，已經開發了諸如晶片鍵合和管芯鍵合的異構集成技術。在我們的實驗室中，我們採用了另一種方法，並在用於晶體管和激光器的矽模板上開發了非常高質量的III-V。 這些模板的晶體質量已通過各種材料表徵得到驗證，並成功用於激光生長。然而，使激光缺陷最小化所需的緩衝層（至少幾微米厚）使得與基於矽的組件的集成困難且效率低下。 在此程序中，我們建議通過選擇性III-V / Si異質外延在Si-光子絕緣體上矽（SOI）平台上開發橫向集成的III-V激光器。我們提出了一種獨特的生長方案，稱為 “橫向ART（長寬比陷阱）” ，以使無位錯的III-V材料的橫向外延恰好位於掩埋氧化物層的頂部。與常規的選擇性生長方法相比，我們提出的技術在調節外延III-V合金尺寸方面具有更大的靈活性，從用於光泵浦激光器的納米級晶體到用於電驅動設備的微米級晶體。更重要的是，外延III-V合金與Si器件層的緊密和平面內定位將允許III-V有源器件和基於Si的無源器件之間的有效連接。我們旨在通過金屬有機化學氣相沉積（MOCVD）的直接異質外延性，在工業標準SOI平台上實現緊湊型III-V光源的單片集成。

16213420.label: Realisation of objectives
16213420.value: We investigated the effects of InxGa1-xAs/InP strain-compensated superlattices inserted as dislocation filter layers into InP films grown on planar (001) Si substrates by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition. Smooth InP films were achieved on (001) Si substrates, showing potential compatibility with CMOS technology. To evaluate the material quality of the compliant InP grown on Si, we fabricated optically pumped microdisk lasers (MDLs) on the InP/Si templates and achieved continuous-wave (CW) lasing above room temperature (RT). The 4 μm MDLs exhibit lasing thresholds ranging from 300 to 400 μW at RT by CW optical pumping. We report room temperature (RT) continuous-wave (CW) lasing of quantum well (QW) lasers grown on (001) Si substrates emitting at 980 nm. Two different QW structures, including conventional compressively-strained InGaAs/GaAs QWs and strain-compensated InGaAs/GaAs/GaAsP QWs were investigated. Photoluminescence properties and device performance of both structures on native GaAs and (001) Si substrates are discussed. By adding GaAsP barriers to the InGaAs/GaAs QWs, the lowest threshold current density of ridge waveguide edge-emitting QW lasers obtained on Si is 550 A/cm2, measured on a 10 μm ×2 mm device at RT. The working temperature of the InGaAs/GaAs/GaAsP QW lasers grown on Si can be over 95 ℃ in CW mode. This work suggests a feasible approach to improve the 980 nm laser performance on Si for monolithic optoelectronic integration. Our project has been so successful that we reported our achievements and results at many conferences. The PI has been invited to give plenary and invited talks on this new breakthrough and participating students presented their results at many conferences. This results in major spending of conference expenses.

16213420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213420.value: The deployment of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) necessitates an integration platform that is scalable, high throughput, cost-effective, and power-efficient. Here we present a monolithic InP on SOI platform to synergize the advantages of two mainstream photonic integration platforms: Si photonics and InP photonics. This monolithic InP/SOI platform is realized through the selective growth of both InP sub-micron wires and large dimension InP membranes on industry-standard (001)-oriented silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafers. The epitaxial InP is in-plane, dislocation-free, site-controlled, intimately positioned with the Si device layer, and placed right on top of the buried oxide layer to form “InP-on-insulator”. These attributes allow for the realization of various photonic functionalities using the epitaxial InP, with efficient light interfacing between the III–V devices and the Si-based waveguides. We exemplify the potential of this InP/SOI platform for integrated photonics through the demonstration of lasers with different cavity designs including subwavelength wires, square cavities, and micro-disks. Our results here mark a critical step forward towards fully-integrated Si-based PICs. Based on our previously demonstrated InP-on-SOI platform, we incorporated 28 periods of InGaAs/InP QWs as the active region sandwiched in the InP crystals by the LART technique. Uniform QWs with high crystal quality were obtained as evidenced by the PL and TEM characterization. RT telecom band lasing was achieved with a low threshold of 20 μJ/cm2 through fabricating MRLs on the as-grown in-plane structure. These promising results provide a possible solution of electrically pumped lasers at the telecom band, paving the way toward fully integrated Si-photonics. Seamlessly integrating III-V active devices with Si passive components in a monolithic manner is the key for fully integrated Si photonics. In this project, we demonstrate high performance III-V photodetectors directly grown on industry-standard (001)-oriented silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafers and intimately coupled with Si waveguides.

16213420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213420.value: Si-based integrated circuit (IC) is recognized as the most powerful and mature micro/nano-electronic technology enabling signal processing, memory, and artificial intelligence that are ubiquitous in modern day life. Because of the nature of indirect bandgap of the Si crystal, making light sources with Si and other group IV elements that do not interact efficiently with photons has been challenging. Since the 1970s, niche applications such as ultra-high-frequency and photonic devices have been dominated by III-V compound semiconductors, which have an innate wavelength-tuning flexibility with various alloys and quantum well/dot structures. In addition to the speed and bandwidth advantages, sending data via photons instead of electrons can be much more energy efficient. Consequently, achieving highly efficient devices and circuits is one of the top priorities in the field of integrated photonics for the next generation of information technology and computing. The eventual goal is to integrate photonics with electronic circuitry on the same silicon platform, so that data communication and processing can be performed on a single tiny silicon chip with energy-efficiency, high speed and minimal delay. Over the years, intense efforts have been made to incorporate high-performance III-V active devices on silicon, to be integrated with passive components and waveguides of Si photonics. Heterogeneous integration techniques such as wafer bonding and die bonding (transfer printing) have been developed for this purpose. In our laboratory, we have taken an alternate approach and developed extremely high-quality III-V on silicon templates for transistors and lasers. The crystalline quality of these templates has been verified by various material characterization and successfully adopted for laser growth. However, the buffer layer (at least a few microns thick) required to minimize the heteroepitaxy-induced defects for lasers makes integration with the Si-based components difficult and inefficient.
