16213620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213620.value: 區塊鍊是由一組不完全信任對方但是對包含多個事務的一組有序塊達成一致的節點維護的分佈式追加賬本。 基本上，區塊鏈可以分為UTXO模型和帳戶模型。在一個基於UTXO模型的區塊鏈上，鏈上記錄的數據是一組交易，每個交易只能使用一次。在基於帳戶模型的區塊鏈中，鏈上記錄的數據是一組賬戶餘額和作為賬戶的定製智能合約在鏈上記錄和運營。與UTXO模型鏈相比，帳戶模型鏈可以在處理交易同時並支持更多類型的智能合約，交易和智能合約對於供應鏈，醫療保健和金融等工業應用是非常需要的。與UTXO模型一樣，帳戶模型也具有許多有價值的特性，例如透明，可溯源，容錯和可靠。但是，帳戶模型的透明特性也導致了很多隱私保護問題。在許多實際應用中，用戶可能不想公開其交易金額或交易夥伴。但是，現有的區塊鏈框架還不能夠解決賬戶模型區塊鏈所麵臨的隱私保護挑戰：1）原生的環簽名方案容易受到可追溯性分析的攻擊，並且不能保護用戶隱私如果對手擁有額外的輔助信息，例如了解某些資產在交易中被消費的概率； 2）帳戶模型中的不同數據結構與當前UTXO模型上的隱私保護方法不兼容； 3）儘管生成的過程非常複雜, 區塊鏈框架應能夠有效而且快速地生成最優化環簽名的同時又能保護隱私；和4）儘管該框架的事務分配成本很高，但框架仍應能夠根據用戶要求有效地進行子事務分配。 在這個項目中，為了解決賬戶型區塊鏈在保護隱私方麵的挑戰，我們計劃開發一個新穎且高效的隱私保護框架來隱藏原始交易金額，接收方和發送方同時能夠處理大量交易(TPS每秒的交易）。該框架將能夠抵抗可追溯性分析並且確保隱私保護即使對手了解其他附帶信息。 除此之外，我們將為用戶設計有效的方法高效的生成合格的環簽名。 最後，我們將開發新穎的遷移策略以滿足不同的需求。該項目的實施不僅為保護帳戶模型區塊鏈的隱私提供堅實的理論基礎，也將為整個行業提供隱私保護的實用指南。

16213620.label: Realisation of objectives
16213620.value: The objectives set forth at the inception of our research project aimed to advance the field of privacy-preserving technologies within blockchain systems. Below, we detail how and to what extent each objective has been achieved. 1. Defining a Measure of Privacy-Preserving Effect and Proposing a Novel Effect-Aware Ring Signature Scheme We successfully defined a quantifiable measure for assessing the privacy-preserving effect of ring signatures. This measure allows for a theoretical analysis of the privacy protection offered by various ring signature schemes. Our work in this area has been published at the SIGMOD conference, demonstrating the academic rigor and relevance of our approach. Furthermore, we proposed a novel effect-aware ring signature scheme that incorporates this measure, ensuring that the privacy-preserving effect can be explicitly evaluated and optimized. 2. Proposing a General Privacy-Preserving Framework for Account-Model Blockchain We have developed a comprehensive privacy-preserving framework specifically tailored for account-model blockchains. This framework hides the original transaction amount, receiver, and sender while guaranteeing privacy preservation. Our framework effectively defends against de-anonymization attacks such as chain-reaction analysis, enhancing the overall security of blockchain transactions. The work on this framework has also been published at the SIGMOD conference, validating its contribution to the field. 3. Designing Effective and Efficient Methods for Generating Eligible Effect-Aware Ring Signatures We designed and implemented an efficient algorithm for selecting optimal ring signature confusion sets. This algorithm helps users generate ring signatures with minimized size, thereby reducing transaction fees. The algorithm's efficacy has been demonstrated through extensive testing and has been published in the SIGMOD conference proceedings. This achievement not only meets the project objective but also contributes to making privacy-preserving transactions more economically viable. 4. Developing Novel Transfer Strategies to Satisfy Different Requirements In addition to minimizing the size of ring signatures, we also developed a transaction generation algorithm that optimizes for various other requirements, including maximizing the privacy-preserving effect, minimizing transaction cost, minimizing transaction processing delay, and minimizing transaction communication cost. This work has been published at the ICDE conference, highlighting its significance in advancing the practicality of privacy-preserving blockchain transactions. 5. Creating Demo Prototypes Utilizing the Proposed Technologies We have leveraged our proposed technologies to develop two demo prototypes: an anonymous and verifiable questionnaire system and an anonymous transaction system. These prototypes showcase the practical applications of our research and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating privacy-preserving technologies into real-world blockchain systems. The development and evaluation of these prototypes have been published in the VLDB conference, further establishing the practical relevance of our work. 6. Collecting and Studying Real Cryptocurrency Privacy Transaction Data To gain insights into the real-world performance and challenges of privacy-preserving blockchain transactions, we collected and analyzed extensive data from actual cryptocurrency privacy transactions. This data analysis has provided valuable insights into the practical implementation and potential improvements of our proposed technologies. Although this work has not been published in a conference or journal as a standalone contribution, it has significantly influenced our research direction and the refinement of our proposed methods. Conclusion In summary, we have achieved all the objectives set out for our research project. We have defined a quantifiable measure for privacy-preserving effect, proposed a novel effect-aware ring signature scheme, developed a comprehensive privacy-preserving framework, designed efficient methods for generating ring signatures, created demo prototypes, and analyzed real cryptocurrency privacy transaction data. Our work has been published in prestigious conferences such as SIGMOD, ICDE, and VLDB, attesting to the academic and practical significance of our contributions.

16213620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213620.value: Our research project has achieved significant findings and outcomes in the domain of privacy-preserving blockchain technologies. Firstly, we have defined a quantifiable measure for the privacy-preserving effect and theoretically analyzed the corresponding privacy protection efficacy of our proposed effect-aware ring signature scheme. This work has been published at the SIGMOD conference [No.2 in Part C.9], demonstrating the robustness and applicability of our approach. Secondly, we have developed a general privacy-preserving framework for account-model blockchains that can effectively conceal the original transaction amount, receiver, and sender while guaranteeing privacy preservation. This framework includes a ring signature generation mechanism that defends against de-anonymization attacks such as chain-reaction analysis. The efficacy of our framework has also been validated through publication at the SIGMOD conference [No.2 in Part C.9]. To further enhance the practicality of our research, we have designed an efficient ring signature obfuscation set selection algorithm. This algorithm aids users in generating minimal-sized ring signatures, significantly reducing transaction fees. Additionally, we have crafted a transaction generation algorithm that optimizes transaction size, thereby saving users considerable expenses. Both algorithms have been recognized through publication at the SIGMOD conference [No.2 in Part C.9] and the ICDE conference [No.4 in Part C.9]. Beyond theoretical advancements, we have also translated our research into tangible prototypes. Leveraging our proposed technologies, we have developed two demo prototypes: an anonymous and verifiable questionnaire system and an anonymous transaction system. These prototypes showcase the real-world applicability of our research and have been presented at the VLDB conference [No.7 and No.9 in Part C.9]. Lastly, we have conducted extensive empirical research by collecting and analyzing real-world cryptocurrency privacy transaction data [No.1 - 6, No. 8, and No. 10 in Part C.9]. This analysis has provided insights into the practical challenges and opportunities for privacy-preserving blockchain technologies, further enriching our understanding of this complex domain. In summary, our research project has not only contributed novel theoretical frameworks and algorithms but also demonstrated their practical implementations and applications, making substantial strides in advancing the field of privacy-preserving blockchain technologies.

16213620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213620.value: The current research holds significant potential for further development. Firstly, the proposed privacy-preserving measures and effect-aware ring signatures can be extended to other blockchain models, such as the UTXO model, to broaden their applicability. Additionally, the privacy-preserving framework can be enhanced by incorporating advanced cryptographic techniques to further strengthen the resistance against sophisticated attacks. Future work should also focus on optimizing the transaction generation algorithm to minimize not only transaction fees but also processing and communication costs. Exploring the integration of our techniques with existing blockchain platforms could facilitate real-world adoption. We propose to conduct extensive experiments with various blockchain networks to validate the scalability and robustness of our methods. Collaboration with industry partners would enable the development of practical applications based on our research, such as secure voting systems or privacy-preserving financial transactions. Moreover, analyzing real-world privacy transaction data in-depth could lead to new insights and improvements in our privacy-preserving mechanisms. Ultimately, our goal is to establish a comprehensive and versatile privacy-preserving blockchain ecosystem.

16213620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213620.value: Our research project aimed to enhance privacy protection in blockchain transactions. We defined a way to measure how well privacy is preserved and proposed a new ring signature scheme that is aware of this effect. Ring signatures allow transactions to be verified without revealing the identities of the sender or receiver. We developed a framework that hides the original transaction amount, sender, and receiver, ensuring privacy. Additionally, we created methods to help users generate smaller and more efficient ring signatures, which can save on transaction fees. Our transaction generation algorithm further minimizes costs by creating smaller transactions. Our work has been published in top conferences like SIGMOD, ICDE and VLDB. We also built two demo prototypes: an anonymous and verifiable survey system, and an anonymous transaction system. These prototypes showcase our techniques in real-world applications. Furthermore, we studied real-world cryptocurrency privacy transaction data to gain insights. Our research is significant because it provides new ways to protect user privacy in blockchain transactions, which is becoming increasingly important as blockchain technology grows.

16214220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214220.value: During earthquake shaking, granular soils may liquefy and completely loss its strength, which is termed as “liquefaction”. During past earthquakes, liquefaction has caused tremendous infrastructural and ground damage. Considerable effects have been devoted in the past 50 years to study liquefaction resistance of soils. Recent earthquake case histories in Japan and New Zealand also revealed that, a site can experience liquefaction multiple times under a sequence of earthquake shaking. Laboratory and field study showed that liquefaction resistance of once liquefied soils can be vastly different, depending on the loading history and resulted soil structures. However, only some specific devices can be used to simulate the multiple liquefaction process, that includes liquefaction, reconsolidation and reliquefaction of the sample for multiple times. Existing laboratory equipment suffers from limitations that the stress field inside the sample is not uniform. There is also a lack of direct measurement of soil structure during the test. Therefore, it is an urgent need to develop an innovative laboratory device to simulate multiple liquefaction process, and develop scientific understanding that connect the soil structure to reliquefacton resistance, with an overarching goal to develop criteria and guidelines for engineering application. This proposal aims at improving fundamental understating of reliquefaction resistance of granular soils through the state-of-the-art laboratory testing and 3D discrete element modeling. In the proposed project, an innovative staked ring torsional shear apparatus will be developed by combining the advantage of the hollow cylinder torsional shear with those of a ring shear test (Task 1). The new device will produce much more uniform stress field within the sample and suitable for large deformation test. It can also be used measure the anisotropy of small strain modulus of the test sample directly. The innovative device will be used to provide high quality data on reliquefaction resistance of a wide spectrum of sandy/silty sandy soils (Task 2), which will be used to provide evidence to formulate criteria for reliquefaction resistance. To validate various hypotheses, 3D discrete element modeling will be conducted to trace microstructure evolution of the soil in the multiple liquefaction process (Task 3). A salient feature of the DEM simulation is that realistic particle shapes of the granular packing will be faithfully simulated using clumped particles, which enables realistic soil fabric to be quantified during liquefaction-consolidation-reliquefaction process for a thorough micromechanical investigation. 地震时颗粒土可能會像液体一样，完全喪失強度，這种现象被稱為“液化”。在以往的地震中，液化造成了基礎設施和场地的极大破壞。近五十年来，针对土体液化已有大量研究。最近日本和新西蘭的地震实例表明，一個场地会在一系列地震作用下經歷多次液化。實驗室和现场研究显示，曾经液化过的土体抵抗再次液化的性能会有极大不同，這取決於加載歷史和所產生的土体結構。 然而，只有一些特殊的试验設備可以用來模擬多次液化過程，包括初始液化、再固結和再液化。現有的试验設備在樣品內部会产生不均匀的應力場，具有很大的局限性，在測試過程中也不能對土体結構进行直接測量。因此，迫切需要開發一種新型的實驗設備來模擬砂土反复液化過程，將土体結構與反复液化性能聯繫起來以增强科學認識，从而达到提出工程应用准则和指引的总体目标。 該项目旨在通過最先进的實驗室測試技术和三维離散元模拟來提高对土体再液化的基本认识。在本項目中，任務一：結合空心圓柱扭剪仪與環剪仪的優點，開發一種新型的叠环扭剪裝置。新設備將在樣品內產生更均勻的應力場，適用於大變形測試。它也可以直接測量試樣的各向異性小應變模量。任務二：該新型設備將用於提供各種砂土、粉砂土再液化性能的高質量试验數據，為製定土体再液化性能准则提供科学依据。任务三：為了驗證各種假設，將進行三维離散元模拟，以追踪多次液化過程中土体的微觀結構演變。本研究中三维離散元模擬有一個顯著特点，它将采用颗粒团簇模拟土体颗粒的真实形状，以便对液化-固結-再液化過程中土体的真实结构开展微观力学研究。

16214220.label: Realisation of objectives
16214220.value: Project Objective 1: “Develop an innovative staked ring torsional apparatus to obtain high quality laboratory data on reliquefaction behavior of sandy, silty sandy soils”. Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI and his coworkers have successfully developed a new stacked ring torsional shear apparatus at HKUST. We have finished manufacturing all components of the apparatus, including (1) the pedestal; (2) inner rings; (3) outer rings; (4) bearing system; (5) restraining poles etc. The soil sample is fully saturated within membranes, and the inner/outer fluid pressure can be independently controlled. The staked ring is built upon existing torsional shear device, so it can perform cyclic simple shearing to liquefaction (undrained), volumetric compression/dissipation of pore pressure (drained), and cyclic simple shearing to liquefaction again. Pressure compensation technique is devised to reduce the fiction between sample membrane and the ring, in order achieve more uniform distribution of vertical stress in the sample, which is a key feature of this device. A Chinese National Patent (No. 202011233820.7) entitled “A stacked ring torsional shear apparatus and pressure compensation technique”, jointly filed with Tsinghua University, has been granted by China National Intellectual Property Administration on Feb. 9, 2022. Pressure transducers were installed on the base of the device to directly measure the effective stress transmitted to the base. The bottom stress is approximately 75% of that applied at the top of the sample [C1], which is much better than 50% achieved by another device developed by University of Tokyo, showing the pressure compensation technique is successful. The staked ring device was calibrated in various aspects, and is fully functional. We have conducted 42 sets of reliquefaction (liquefaction twice) tests, and the results are published in top journals Géotechnique and Géotechnique Letters [J1, J2]. The laboratory tests provide new data for a deeper understanding of reliquefaction. Based on the test data, we are able to investigate effects of inherent and induced anisotropy on reliquefaction resistance and proposed an energy-based method to quantify it [J1]; we studied the properties of shear modulus reduction and damping of reliquefied Toyoura sand under the integrated effects of strain history and induced anisotropy [J2]. In addition, 18 sets of multiple liquefaction (liquefaction up to 8~10 times) tests on sandy and silty sandy soils were also conducted by this device, showing how reliquefaction resistance increases or decreases with prescribed strain histories. Project Objective 2: Characterize fabric evolution using 3D discrete element simulation, and seek a linkage between soil fabric anisotropy with reliquefaction resistance. Project objective 2 has been fully achieved. For objective 2, the PI and his coworkers at Tsinghua University have developed 3D Discrete Element Method (DEM) to investigate fabric change in reliquefaction process [J3, J4, J5]. A salient feature of the DEM simulation is that realistic particle shapes of the granular packing were faithfully simulated using clumped particles, which enables realistic soil fabric to be quantified during for a thorough micromechanical investigation. The DEM models have been carefully calibrated such that the DEM simulations are “quantitatively” similar to the experimental results, see benchmark tests in [J4, J5]. In addition, new indices were also proposed to quantify the anisotropy of the void space, which is very complicated in irregularly shaped particle assemblage [J4] Through DEM simulation, we quantified particle-void structure and fabrics evolution in multiple liquefaction process. Several important correlations were proposed, including: degree of fabric anisotropy (ac) vs. reliquefaction resistance; averaged number of interparticle contact (Z) vs. reliquefaction resistance [J4, J5]; void fabrics vs. volumetric compression [J3]; volumetric compression at different strain levels [J4]. The research identified that Z is the most effective fabric index correlating to reliquefaction resistance. Once it can be measured in situ through wave-based method, reliquefaction resistance can be assessed [J4]. These results were published in Journal of Engineering Mechanics ASCE, Acta Geotechnica, Computers and Geotechnics. In addition, we have actively developed discrete element methods to model soil-water interaction via CFD-DEM coupling scheme considering irregular shaped particles [J6] and multiphysics phenomenon in granular materials by finite-discrete element method [J7]. In summary, to date, the research findings have been published as 7 SCI journal papers in top international journals, including Géotechnique, Acta Geotechnica, Computers and Geotechnics, ASCE Journal of Engineering Mechanics, Journal of Computational Physics, Géotechnique Letters etc. The results were also presented as Invited Theme Lecture in the 4th International Conference on Performance-based Design in Earthquake Geotechnical Engineering (PBD IV), July 15-17, 2022, Beijing, China, and Distinguished Lecture in the 43th Distinguished Lecture Series at University of California, Berkeley on May 9, 2025. The project findings have been shared and discussed with graduate students in the PI’s graduate-level course “CIVL5750 Earthquake Engineering and Soil Dynamics” at HKUST. 16214220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214220.value: 1. The project successfully developed a staked ring torsional shear apparatus at HKUST to study multiple liquefaction behaviour of sands and silty sands. The device is unique of its kind, using an innovative pressure compensation technology to achieve more uniform stress distribution in soils [C1-C4]. 2. The device generated high-quality data to reveal the fundamental behavior of reliquefaction. More than 60 sets of multiple liquefaction tests were conducted on sandy and silty sandy soils to investigate the stress-strain-strength characteristics, coupled effects of inherent and induced anisotropy on reliquefaction resistance of soils under different sample preparation methods, relative densities, reconsolidation states, loading intensity and strain histories [J1, J2]. Based on laboratory tests, we developed an energy-based criterion to evaluate reliquefaction resistance. The paper was published in top journal Géotechnique [J1]. 3. Advanced Discrete Element Method (DEM) was successfully developed to trace fabric evolution and reveal the fundamental mechanism of the reliquefaction process [J3-J7]. By using irregular particle shapes, the DEM captures individual particle movement, realistic particle-void structure and fabrics evolution during liquefaction-consolidation-reliquefaction process. We observed that the significant increase or decrease of reliquefaction resistance can be attributed to fabric changes under different strain histories. We discovered strong correlations between reliquefaction resistance and soil fabric indices, in particular, the average number of contacts per particle (Z) and fabric anisotropy index (ac). Once these fabrics can be measured, reliquefaction resistance can be assessed [J4]. The research findings have been published as 7 SCI journal papers in top international journals, including Géotechnique, Acta Geotechnica, Computers and Geotechnics, ASCE Journal of Engineering Mechanics, Journal of Computational Physics, Géotechnique Letters etc. The research findings also have been actively disseminated in important local, national and international conferences, as Invited Theme Lecture at PBD-IV (2022) in Beijing [C2, C3], 8ICEGE (2024) in Japan [C1], HKSTAM Annual Conference in Hong Kong (2022) [C4], and distinguished lecture at the 43rd Annual Geosystems Engineering Distinguished Lecture Series at University of California, Berkeley, USA (2025). Two PhD students at HKUST (Dr. FARDAD AMINI Pedram, graduated, and Mr. YUAN Zhengxin, in final year), and a visiting PhD student, Mr. YANG Siyuan, from Tsinghua University (Jan - May 2024) were trained. Five MSc students have completed their MSc theses on laboratory testing of soil liquefaction/reliquefaction using the developed stacked ring torsional shear apparatus. They are HU Bing (2021-2022), ZHANG Yuewen (2021-2022), CHAN Long Yee (2022-2023), KWAN Tim Chung (2023-2024) and MA Chen Kei (2023-2024).

16214220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214220.value: (1) This project revealed that reliquefaction resistance is strongly correlated to the soil’s fabric, in particular, the average number of contacts per particle and the anisotropy of contact distribution. However, these fabrics are mostly obtained from numerical simulation, instead of being directly observed in laboratory tests and in-situ state. Direct observation of fabric evolution is urgently needed for real engineering application. However, direct measurement of contact fabric from X-ray tomographic images still remains a challenge in terms of both imaging resolution and data interpretation. Particle contact may be quantified through small-strain modulus or wave velocity. It is an opportunity for the future to develop wave-based measurement to directly quantify these fabrics in situ. (2) Most of this study focus on reliquefaction behaviour of clean Toyoura sands. Tests on silty sands are limited. We need to further research on how fines content influence reliquefaction resistance and compare these test results with clean sands. (3) Existing constitutive models of soils are not adequate for simulating reliquefaction. Based on findings from this project, there is a great opportunity to develop a unified constitutive framework to model multiple liquefaction by incorporating laws of soil fabric evolution to improve the model prediction.

16214220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214220.value: Reliquefaction is a phenomenon that a soil ground can experience liquefaction multiple times under a sequence of earthquakes. Limited laboratory and field study showed that reliquefaction resistance of once liquefied soils can be vastly different from initial liquefaction. Yet, the fundamental mechanism remains unclear. This project aims at improving fundamental understating of reliquefaction resistance of granular soils through the state-of-the-art laboratory testing and advanced 3D discrete element modeling (DEM). In this project, an innovative staked ring torsional shear apparatus was developed for multiple liquefaction testing. By using pressure-compensation technique, the device produces more uniform stress field within the soil sample, and generates 60 sets of high-quality multiple liquefaction data on clean sands and silty sands. The advanced 3D DEM traces evolution of soil structure (fabric) in the multiple liquefaction process, which provides direct evidence to link soil fabric with reqlieufaction behaviour. Based on laboratory tests and numerical simulation, we developed an energy-based criterion and discovered strong correlations between soil fabric change and its reliquefaction resistance. The project has significantly advanced scientific understanding of reliquefaction phenomenon, and paves the way for developing practical methods to evaluate and mitigate reliquefaction hazards and associated engineering problems.

16215620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215620.value: Solid-state lighting (SSL), renewable energy and smart power grids are among the major initiatives being deployed worldwide for building a more sustainable environment. In particular, the SSL revolution of replacing conventional lighting by LEDs is projected to cut global electricity consumption by 15% beyond 2023. The ubiquitous deployment of LED lights also provides an opportunity for innovative optical applications other than just simply for lighting. An emerging technology under intense research is the use of LED lights for wireless communication known as visible light communication (VLC). The operating principle is to modulate the LED driver with a data stream at high speed. Since human eyes have “low-pass filter” characteristics, they will not sense the high-speed “flickering” of the light. Compared with traditional radio-frequency (RF) wireless communications, VLC is advantageous in terms of high security, no RF radiation, wide available spectrum and transceiver simplicity. Currently, VLC is being regarded as an effective form of wireless communication supplementing conventional RF communication as well as providing some new wireless applications uniquely achievable with this technology. In particular, the Li-Fi (Light Fidelity) market based on VLC is projected to have a compound annual growth rate of 82% and reach over $2 billion per year by 2025. With great efforts from both academia and industry, the VLC technology has achieved significant progress. As an example, a single VLC link achieving over 100 Mb/s has been demonstrated using commercial LED lamps. However, the power consumption is prohibitively high due to the usage of discrete components. In addition, the estimated energy efficiency of a discrete VLC system is about 20-100 nJ/bit, which is about 100 times lower than the state-of-the-art Wi-Fi's efficiency of 0.2-1 nJ/bit depending on the range. System-on-a-chip (SoC) will be a promising solution to achieving better power efficiency, high reliability, smaller system form factors and lower costs to enable practical Li-Fi applications. Unfortunately, the relevant research is still in the very early stage and no example is available. This project aims to design, implement, test, and characterize a fully integrated VLC transceiver SoC in CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) technology for Li-Fi networks, targeting at a data rate of 500Mb/s over 5 meters. The energy efficiency is expected to reach 10x better than discrete VLC systems. The VLC SoC will enable high-speed location-based secured wireless data communication and reliable high-accuracy indoor positioning. 固態照明（SSL），可再生能源和智能電網都是為建立可持續環境而在全球被採用的主要方案。其中,用LED取代傳統照明的SSL革命有望在2023年削減全球電力消耗15％。LED燈的普及除了用於照明之外，還為創新的光學應用提供了新的機會。一個受到廣泛研究的新興技術是使用LED燈進行無線通信,被稱為可見光通信（VLC）。工作原理是調節LED具有高速數據流的驅動程序。由於人眼具有“低通濾波器”的特性，因此人們不會察覺到高速的燈光“閃爍”。相比與傳統的射頻無線通信，VLC具有更高安全性及更大的可用頻譜， 同時不產生任何RF輻射。目前，VLC被視為一種有效的無線通信可以補充傳統的射頻無線通信，這項技術並可以提供一些無線通信的獨特應用。特別是基於VLC的Li-Fi網絡，市場預計將以82％的複合年增長率增長到2025年，每年將超過20億美元。在學術界和工業界的共同努力下，VLC技術已實現重大進展。使用商用LED燈，單通道VLC鏈路的速度已經超過100 Mb/s了。但是，由於使用了分立元件，所以用電量消耗很高。此外，預計分立VLC系統約為20-100 nJ/bit，比最新的Wi-Fi技術(0.2-1 nJ/bit)效率低約100倍。集成芯片系統(SoC)將有望成為解決方案以實現更低的用電量，更高的可靠性，更小的系統體積和更低的成本，來推動Li-Fi網絡的應用。不幸的是，相關研究仍處於早期階段，尚無可用實例。本項目旨在CMOS中實施設計和測試針對Li-Fi網絡應用的全集成的VLC收發器芯片系統，數據速率超過500Mb/s。通訊距離超過5米。能源效率有望達到10倍以上離散VLC系統。 VLC SoC芯片系統將能夠實現高速安全無線數據通訊和可靠的高精度室內定位。

16215620.label: Realisation of objectives
16215620.value: For the first objective, we designed a 4-level pulse-amplitude-modulation (PAM-4) VLC transmitter with both digital and analog equalizations. It consists of a clock unit, digital baseband and analog front-end. The clock unit will generate proper clock sequences from external clock source to support the synchronization of different circuits. The PRBS generator in digital baseband aims to generate original signal and the encoder will encode it to PAM-4 sequence. Delay unit adds a 0.5 UI delay time to the original signal for 3 taps to compose the compensating signals for digital equalizer. These signals together with the main signal will control the states of multiplex (MUX) and choose corresponding data from look-up table (LUT). Data stored in LUT are the feed-forward equalization (FFE) signals with pre-calculated coefficients and will be utilized to compensate high-frequency loss. The analog front-end is a digital to analog converter (DAC) with current mode logic (CML) structure and converts digital input signal to analog output driving current signal. A D flip-flop (DFF) will synchronize the input signal of each slice of DAC and guarantee correct sample time. Then, this signal drives the LEDs in current mode to the desired working states. Except from the on-chip digital equalization method, a passive analog equalizer is also adopted off-chip to assist with further signal improvement. In this proposed transmitter, two kinds of equalization will be applied to achieve a better performance of extending modulation bandwidth and improving signal quality. FFE is commonly used in high-speed optical communication PAM-4 transmitter systems. A 4-tap FFE is utilized here to fully cancel the rising and falling tails in transmitted signal caused by LED bandwidth limitation as well as decrease low-frequency components for better extend the transmitter bandwidth. The input data from encoder will be inverted and delayed properly then set as the pre-tap and post-tap FFE signals. These signals will combine with main-tap signal and perform as select signal of MUX to choose appropriate data stored in LUT. These data are the calculated coefficient to adjust weights of different taps for exact cancellation of tails. Therefore, the loss of high-frequency components will be compensated, and the quality of PAM-4 eye diagram at receiver side can be improved. To verify and assess the improvement of 4-tap FFE and passive equalizer to high-speed data transmission, we simulated the transmitted results with 1 Gbps PAM-4 data by using a 50 MHz LED model. Then we compare the eye diagrams of output signal with and without equalization. The FFE tap number and weights are calculated and 1 pre-tap with 2 post-taps are applied to compensate transmission loss. The delay time of each tap is 0.5-UI, and the main driving current is 60 mA. The quality of eye diagram under PRBS-7 1Gbps PAM-4 data transmission has been improved significantly. The eye width of top, middle and bottom eyes are same with value of 57.5% to 1-UI while the height percentage of each eye are 77%, 80% and 77%. With the proposed cooperation of 4-tap FFE and passive equalizer, a 50 MHz LED model can support 1 Gbps PAM-4 data in schematic-level simulation.

16215620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215620.value: To address the practical deployment problem of VLC, we present the design of a 10-W AC-powered LED light bulb as VLC transmitter with standard E27 socket, which converts AC input voltage to DC output for supporting the Bluetooth control block and generating VLC signals. The light bulb achieves a VLC link distance of 3.4 m while maintaining illumination of over 300 lx at 1.5 m. It can be utilized as location beacon in a smart-home system with smartphone as receiver. In addition, this light bulb can be used to calculate the 3D position and orientation of the smartphone with accuracy of an average PER less than 7 %. For more details, see Part C/8/Paper 4 and 9/Paper 1. To further increase the speed of VLC system, we have designed and evaluated high-speed VLC systems. A 4-level pulse-amplitude-modulation (PAM-4) VLC transmitter with both digital and analog equalizations is designed to realize 1 Gbps VLC. A look-up table (LUT) and multiplexes (MUXs) with DAC-based driver are utilized to generate feed-forward equalization (FFE) signals with following passive equalizers. A cascode TIA with cross-coupled pairs and a scaled dummy side is proposed, realizing an IRN current of 0.21 uArms over a -3dB BW of 2.3 GHz. A VLC transceiver based on the proposed TIA is designed and evaluated through the ISEE with modulation schemes of NRZ, PAM-4, and DCO-OFDM. At 1.5 m, a maximum data rate of 5 Gb/s is achieved using the receiver with a scaled dummy side whereas the maximum data rate is 3 Gb/s for the receiver with a replica dummy side. For more details, see Part C/8/Paper 3 and 9/Paper 2. Visible light positioning (VLP) is one important application of designed VLC system, and we propose and implement several methods to increase its accuracy. Firstly, a VLC-assisted pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR)-based indoor navigation system is proposed, which can realize a precision of < 0.7 m in case of one light every 15 m. Secondly, we propose a loosely-coupled VLP-inertial fusion method for robotics localization with single or even without LED through single LED VLP with odometer (SLO-VLP) algorithm with an average accuracy of 2.1 cm and computational time around 33 ms. Thirdly, we propose a tilted receiver camera correction and partially blocked LED image compensation method for VLP systems, which can eliminate the positioning errors caused by tilted cameras. For more details, see Part C/8/Paper 2.

16215620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215620.value: For the PD-based VLC system design, a highly integrated system is critical since it contributes to reducing the parasitic components, decreasing system scale, and improving energy efficiency. An integrated PD-based VLC system typically consists of digital baseband, analog front-end, LED as light source, and PD as light signal detector. In the digital baseband, various digital pre- and post-equalization schemes such as FFE, DFE, NN-based equalization, and advanced modulation schemes such as PAM, OFDM, CAP, and WDM are important for extending the limited modulation bandwidth. Implementing these schemes in the integrated digital baseband through the real-time method is the future direction since most of the digital basebands for PD-based VLC systems are designed in MATLAB with an offline process. In the analog front-end, the energy-efficient LED driver, high impedance gain and low noise receiver amplifier, and multiple-stage equalizer are essential research directions for improving system performance. For the light source, high modulation bandwidth white LED is one significant research focus for VLC device development due to its severe limitation effect on the communication data rate. Therefore, from digital design through analog circuit design to VLC device development, there are quite a lot of research topics pending for subsequent work.

16215620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215620.value: Light-Fidelity (Li-Fi), based on visible light communication (VLC) technology, is not limited by conventional radio spectrum congestion issue and any existing LED light sources, such as room illumination, display or signage, can be used for optical wireless communication. The huge bandwidth available can allow high-data-rate indoor wireless links, which will help relieve the increasing need in radio spectrum for next generation internet infrastructure. In addition, VLC is especially compelling because it is inherently line-of-sight providing high-security data communication while there is no RF radiation. On the other hand, no special installation is required, and the associated cost is hence minimal, considering the VLC?s backhaul connectivity to the internet can be provided by power-line communication, which is a mature commercialized technology. As a result, VLC is expected to be widely deployed not only for high-speed connectivity but also for enabling wireless communication in some particular settings where RF interference is a concern such as hospitals. This project has designed integrated circuits in CMOS technology to implement a VLC transceiver SoC for Li-Fi networks. The enabling technologies should significantly reduce the form factors, increase the reliability, lower the cost and improve the energy efficiency of Li-Fi systems.

16215720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215720.value: Compared to the eye of a vertebrate with single-chamber lens, the compound eyes of insects have lower resolution but larger angular field-of-view (FoV), negligible spherical distortion and aberration, high angular sensitivity and temporal resolution. These attributes have motivated research on the implementation of artificial compound eyes (ACE) for potential applications in areas such as surveillance, endoscopy, motion detection, visually controlled navigation or optomotor. Reported implementations of ACE utilize light sensors and rigid silicon-based integrated circuits; both are readily realized on conventional planar substrates but subsequently diced and packaged on a flexible substrate - a tedious operation offering limited FoV and resolution. By far the widest FoV achieved is still no more than 115°. Though there are techniques to enlarge the horizontal FoV to 180°, the vertical FoV is still less than 60°. Instead of using rigid “chip-based” circuits and photo-detectors, an alternative approach to further improve the capability of an ACE is to monolithically integrate the various components of an ACE on a flexible substrate which is subsequently bent into a curved or a hemispherical surface. It should be noted that the glass-transition temperature of a flexible substrate is typically less than 400 °C, which is significantly lower than the 1000 °C needed for the realization of a silicon-based transistor. Overcoming this fundamental contradiction demands the selection of suitable flexible substrate materials; the development of low-temperature technologies for realizing the active devices; and the resolution of potential incompatibility between the technologies when monolithically integrating the devices. The goal of the present proposal is to use the implementation of an ACE as a vehicle to drive the development of the component technologies for fabricating active devices such as transistors and photodiodes on a flexible substrate. 與脊椎動物的單腔眼睛相比，昆蟲的複眼具有較低的分辨率，但具有較大的視場角（FoV），可忽略的球面畸變和像差，較高的角靈敏度和時間分辨率。這些屬性可應用在監視，內窺鏡，運動檢測或視控導航等領域，促使人們對人工複眼（ACE）的實現進行研究。已報導的ACE實現方案均使用光傳感器和基於矽的剛性集成電路。兩者都可以很容易地在傳統的平面基板上實現。但其需要被切成小塊後才能封裝在柔性基板上，經過一個繁瑣又復雜操作後也只能提供有限的FoV和分辨率。到目前為止，獲得的最寬視距仍不超過115°。儘管有將水平FoV擴大到180°的技術，但垂直FoV仍然小於60°。替代使用異性集成剛性“基於芯片”的電路和光電檢測器，進一步提高ACE能力的另一種方法是將ACE的各個組件整體集成在柔性基板上，然後將其彎曲成形。應當注意，柔性基板的玻璃化轉變溫度通常小於400℃，這大大低於實現矽基晶體管所需的1000℃。為了克服這一基本矛盾，需要選擇合適的柔性基板材料。開髮用於實現有源器件的低溫技術；以及解決單片集成時技術之間潛在的不兼容問題。本研究的目的是使用ACE的實現作為媒介來驅動用於在諸如柔性襯底上的晶體管和光電二極管之類的製造有源器件的組件技術的發展。

16215720.label: Realisation of objectives
16215720.value: A technology has been developed for the monolithic integration of hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) photo-diodes (PDs) and metal-oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs) based on indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO). The most critical issues to be resolved are the sequence of device integration and the potential cross-contamination posted by H. Related to the order of fabricating the PDs or the TFTs, the first issue is mainly a thermal stability problem. This is resolved by constructing first the TFTs and lowering the deposition temperature of the active a-Si:H layers of the PDs to no higher than 250 degC. This temperature is low enough to prevent thermally-induced drift of the parameters of the TFTs that are fabricated before the construction of the PDs. Related to the presence of H, which is needed for the functionality of the PDs but is a killer defect for the TFTs, the second issue is the prevention of H from ingressing into the underlying TFTs. This was accomplished by strengthening the TFTs by plasma-fluorination treatment and the insertion of an aluminum oxide as a H diffusion barrier between the PDs and the TFTs. For the construction of an artificial compound-eye (ACE) system on a polyimide flexible substrate, a low-temperature process with a peak temperature of no higher than 300-degC has been developed. Curved ACEs with a resolution of 200 pixels per inch have been constructed and their functionality demonstrated.

16215720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215720.value: Constructed by heterogeneous integration of electronic and optical units, current ACEs have limited resolution and high construction complexity on a curvy surface. Though both can be alleviated using monolithic integration, hitherto the lack of progress can be attributed to the difficulty in resolving incompatibility issues when integrating the photo-sensors and the transistors. Constructed as an array of pixels with each consisting of metal-oxide (MO) TFTs, a hydrogenated a-Si:H PD, and a structured optical path, this work contributes to the resolution of all major integration issues and concludes with the construction of a monolithic integrated ACE system. The entire engineering chain covering ACE design, process and characterization, and application have been explored. Applying a customed developed physico-mathematical model, ACE optical units are designed with specified angular field of view, inter-ommatidial angle, resolution, and cross-talk prevention. Motion-tracking on the planar and cylindrical ACE surfaces has been accomplished. ACE in-pixel circuit consisting of an a-Si:H PD, a one-stage amplifier, and scan TFT is proposed for PD signal amplification and active-matrix addressing. The monolithic integration processes of each pixel component on the planar and flexible ACE arrays are developed. When integrated with PD, a protection layer is incorporated to protect the TFTs from H diffusion and radiation damage. The performances of the optical and electrical units on planar and flexible ACEs are characterized. With the proposed circuit, the signal strength can be boosted by around 6.7 times. Visualized patterns and light source tracing are demonstrated using a planar ACE array and a 200 ppi flexible ACE array, respectively. The planar ACE system is applied in motion detection and proximity pattern recognition. The motion tracing along the x-, y-, and z-axis and on the x-y plane are demonstrated based on the designed resolution. For proximity pattern recognition, three finger patterns are identified with 95% predicting accuracy by constructed neural networks and fabricated ACE.

16215720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215720.value: The technology could be practically applied to a range of sensor arrays other than PDs. This is being actively pursued for tactile sensing in robotics by the principal investigator.

16215720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215720.value: A technology has been developed for the light detectors and transistors. The low-temperature technology is compatible with the construction of an artificial compound eye on a flexible substrate. The compound eye could be applied to motion-detection. As a demonstration a compound eye with a resolution of 200 pixels per inch has been fabricated and characterized, demonstrating good functionality.

16215820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215820.value: 针对资源有限的社会最优政策，并应用于运输和水管理

16215820.label: Project Objectives
16215820.value: To extend our preliminary work on congestion pricing and cross-subsidies for transportation into the context of water resource management. This parts adds two interesting dimensions to the problem, including randomness in the supply side in terms of the rainfall provided by nature, and the difficulty of solving the problem through the supply side. To extend our work into supply side solutions by studying ways to increase capacity in a way that is socially optimal possibly in combination with demand side solutions through prices and subsidies. We plan to look, in particular, to private-public-partnerships (PPP) and the conflicting goals between private companies and governments in terms of pricing. Our third area is more tentative and will look, if possible, at dynamic models where prices and subsidies can change over time.

16215820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215820.value: 当需求远远超过供给时就会发生拥堵，这在许多领域都是不可避免的现象。需求和供给之间的这种不平衡将导致效率损失并造成额外的社会成本。我们在交通拥堵定价方面的初步工作表明，在对驾驶员收取拥堵费的同时对公交乘客提供交叉补贴这一政策对于驾驶员、乘客、环境和政府可以实现共赢。基于这一结果，本项目仍旨在解决在资源有限的拥堵缓解问题，并计划从以下三个方面开展。 首先是将交通拥堵的研究扩展到水资源管理的情景下，研究如何通过定价和交叉补贴在农民和居民之间分配水库水。当水资源短缺时，政府需要执行一些政策使用水量降低到社会最优水平。本部分旨在研究政府应如何设定水价和交叉补贴，以激励居民减少用水量并防止农民空置土地，从而实现对当前政策的帕累托改进。 本研究的第二个方向是研究政府如何通过增加容量来从供应的角度解决交通拥堵问题。在交通项目中，修建新道路需要政府大量支出。因此，当政府本身没有足够的资金承担此类项目时，它可以采用公私合营（PPP）的方式来实现这一目标。在该模式下，首先由企业投资修建新道路，然后企业通过在特许运营期内收取通行费来收回前期投资。由于政府与企业之间存在目标不一致的问题，因此本研究旨在探讨在什么情况下采用PPP模式修建一条新的道路可以实现社会最优，进而研究在该情形下的社会最优道路容量。 本研究的第三个目标是探索动态定价如何缓解拥堵。我们已经完成的初步工作旨在激励消费者从驾车转向乘坐公交以减少道路车辆，这可以看作空间维度上的需求转移。由于交通需求通常在高峰时段和非高峰时段有着显著的差异，因此动态拥堵定价可以进一步将消费者从高峰时段转移到非高峰时段，这可以看作是时间维度上的需求转移。

16300220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300220.value: 基于局域测量的量子态重构

16300220.label: Project Objectives
16300220.value: Long-Term Objective 1 (over 10 years): Understand the correlation hierarchy of many-body quantum states for systems with local Hamiltonians, and its relationship with the quantum phase of matter. Correlation/entanglement in many-body wave functions plays a key role in determining the physical properties of quantum systems. Thus far, we have only acquired very limited knowledge of these phenomena in the interdisciplinary field of quantum information and quantum matter. In the proposed project, we will study the different types of correlations and their relationships with the quantum phase of matter, with the aim of generating a new basis for a fundamental microscopic theory of quantum matter. This will lead to the discovery of new quantum phases of matter, and new types of quantum materials. Long-Term Objective 2 (over 10 years): Understand many-body correlation/entanglement as a fundamental resource for quantum information processing, including quantum tomography, quantum error correction, and quantum computing. Correlation and entanglement hold the key to deciphering the ultimate power of quantum information processing. Different types of correlations correspond to different complexities of quantum states and hence different information processing capabilities. Understanding these types of correlations will lead to more effective methods of performing quantum tomography and quantum error correction, and of building large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. Short-Term Objective 1: Find convergent algorithms that determine the uniqueness of multipartite quantum wave functions based on their local parts, among all of the density matrices. As physical interactions are local, it is reasonable to enquire whether a “natural” quantum states are determined by their local parts. Although some algorithms are known to calculate compatible states with the given measurement results, none are known to be convergent. To achieve this objective, we will explore the convergence of the existing algorithms and develop new algorithms. Short-Term Objective 2: Find symmetry groups that lead to degenerate ground states, which are uniquely determined by their local measurements. The first set of examples of this phenomenon was only found very recently. These examples show that many-body quantum states exist that are uniquely determined by their local parts, but cannot be unique ground states of local Hamiltonians. Symmetry seems to play an essential role in building these examples. Thus, we will explore the role that symmetry plays in the ground states with the hope of finding a general theory that can describe the relationship between the correlation types and ground state degeneracy of local Hamiltonians. Short-Term Objective 3: Find an algorithm that can determine the uniqueness of multipartite wave functions based on their local parts, among all of the wave functions. It was only until recently discovered that the set of wave functions uniquely determined by their local parts (called UDA) is different from the set of wave functions uniquely determined by their local parts among all of the wave functions (called UDP). However, the nature of the difference between UDA and UDP remains largely unknown. Thus, we will develop algorithms that can determine UDP to further study this UDA-UDP gap. Short-Term Objective 4: Understand the correlations of the eigenstates of local Hamiltonians, and determine whether these eigenstate wave functions are uniquely determined among all of the wave functions by local measurements. Some recent studies have shown that in generic cases, the eigenstates of local Hamiltonians can be determined by their local parts. How to characterize these kinds of eigenstate correlations among the known types of the correlation hierarchy remains to be determined. Thus, we will explore the relationship between the eigenstate correlation and UDP, which may add a new type of correlation to the known correlation hierarchy. Short-Term Objective 5: Understand the correlation of the low-energy states of local Hamiltonians, and determine whether these wave functions are uniquely determined among all of the wave functions by local measurements. Low-energy states are not uniquely determined by their local parts, because states with the same local parts can be obtained by mixing states with different energy. However they may be natural candidates for UDP. Thus, we will further examine these states with the hope of developing a better understanding of the UDA-UDP gap.

16300220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300220.value: Quantum correlation and entanglement hold the key to deciphering the ultimate power of quantum information processing. Although the interactions in natural quantum systems are local, even the ground states of these systems exhibit exotic behaviours such as topological order. In recent years, the correlations of the eigenstates of local Hamiltonians have become a central topic in the interdisciplinary field of quantum information and quantum matter. It has long been assumed that unique ground states of gapped local Hamiltonians are “trivial”, in the sense that they can be connected to the product states by a simple transformation using only a small number of layers of local quantum gates. However, recent developments suggest that the correlations in these seemingly simple systems are more complicated. Studies have also examined problems related to the correlations of many-body eigenstates in the field of quantum chemistry and quantum information theory. These studies have revealed that correlations of many-body quantum states exhibit a hierarchical structure, with the trivial states being at the very bottom level. The underlying theory behind this hierarchy remains largely unknown. In some cases, only a handful of examples illustrate that one layer of hierarchy indeed represents a different kind of correlation from another nearby layer. The proposed three-year project will examine three kinds of correlations in the hierarchy. The first type, called UGS, are the set of unique ground states of local Hamiltonians. The second type, called UDA, are many-body wave functions that are uniquely determined by their local parts. The third type, called UDP, are many-body wave functions that are uniquely determined by their local parts among all of the wave functions. Only very recently, examples were found showing that UGS and UGA, and UDA and UDP, are not the same sets of states. This proposed project will systematically examine the differences between UGS and UGA, and between UDA and UDP. Due to the lack of general methods for studying these problems and the few known examples, we will develop new theoretical and numerical methods, to address these issues. Overall, the results of this project will deepen our understanding of the correlation hierarchy, provide more insight into the correlation properties of many-body quantum states, shed light on the related problems of quantum tomography and quantum error correction in quantum information theory, and lead to the generation of new perspectives on the theory of joint numerical range in applied mathematics. 量子信息处理对比于传统信息处理的优势高度依赖量子关联和量子纠缠的性质。实际量子物理系统中，相互作用是局域的。尽管如此，量子系统的基态依然可能具有长程纠缠。许多奇特的物理特性与这种长程关联有关，比如拓扑序。近年来，研究多体量子体系本征态的关联特性是量子信息与量子物质这一交叉领域的热点之一。 直觉上，没有简并的量子系统的基态应当是平凡的，也就是说不具有长程纠缠。但是，近期的研究表明，哪怕是这类看似平凡的量子态，也具有相当复杂的关联结构。我们注意到，在早前量子化学和量子信息学的研究中，已经有一些相关研究结果。现在，人们把多体量子体系的关联性质总结为一种层级结构。具有平凡关联的量子态处于这个层级的最底端。尽管如此，我们对这些层级结构之间的区别和联系还知之甚少。 本研究项目将致力于系统研究这一量子多体关联的层级结构。我们主要关注其中三种层级。第一种称做UGS，指的是具有局域相互作用的量子体系的非简并基态。第二种称做UDA，指的是在所有的量子态的集合里（包括混合态）可以被局域约化密度矩阵完全确定的多体量子波函数。第三种称做UDP，是在所有的量子波函数的集合里可以被局域约化密度矩阵完全确定的多体量子波函数。直到最近，研究工作才揭示出UGS和UDA并不是相同的集合，UDA和UDP也不是相同的集合。 本项目将系统的研究UGS和UDA两个层级之间的区别，以及UDA和UDP两个层级之间的区别。到目前为止，关于这些层级间的区别，我们只知道有限的几个具体例子。由于不存在现成的，系统的方法来研究这些层级的性质，我们需要发展新的方法，包括理论方法和数值算法。项目的研究成过将会加深我们对多体系统量子关联层级的理解，特别是对于UGS，UDA和UDP这几个重要层级的性质的理解。这些理解将对相关学科的研究，包括多体量子体系关联，量子态层析，量子纠错，量子信息理论，以及数值域研究的相关数学理论，提供新的观点和方法。

16300220.label: Realisation of objectives
16300220.value: In this project, we aimed to deepen our understanding of many-body quantum states and their correlations, focusing on implications for quantum information processing. Our objectives included long-term goals for the next decade and immediate short-term aims. Below, we detail how our research outputs align with and contribute to these objectives. Long-Term Objective 1: Understand the correlation hierarchy of many-body quantum states for systems with local Hamiltonians, and its relationship with the quantum phase of matter. Realisation: Significant progress was made through Paper 3: ''Theory of Quasi-Exact Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing and Valence-Bond-Solid Codes.'' We developed the theory of quasi-exact fault-tolerant quantum (QEQ) computation using ''quasi codes,'' which are parametric, approximate quantum error-correcting codes that become exact upon parameter tuning. By introducing valence-bond-solid (VBS) codes as examples, we explored the correlation hierarchy in many-body quantum states. VBS codes exhibit unique entanglement patterns arising from local Hamiltonians. Adjusting parameters allowed us to study how correlations evolve and relate to different quantum phases of matter. Contributions: -Development of Quasi Codes: Established a new class of codes to explore a continuum of correlation structures. - Analysis of Correlations: Gained insights into how local interactions create complex correlations indicative of quantum phases. - Connection to Quantum Phases: Clarified the relationship between correlation hierarchies and quantum phases, providing a foundation for discovering new phases and materials. This work directly advances our understanding of the interplay between local interactions, many-body correlations, and quantum phases, aligning with our long-term goal. Long-Term Objective 2: Understand many-body correlation/entanglement as a fundamental resource for quantum information processing, including quantum tomography, quantum error correction, and quantum computing. Realisation: Papers 1, 2, and 4 collectively advance this objective: Paper 1: We presented a method where deep reinforcement learning steers quantum imaginary time evolution, minimizing algorithmic errors. By managing entanglement and correlations, we enhanced fidelity in preparing ground and thermal states on near-term devices. Contributions: - Error Mitigation through Learning: Leveraged many-body correlations to enhance fidelity. -Practical Implementation: Verified efficacy through simulations and experiments. -Advancement in State Preparation: Improved essential methods for quantum computations. Paper 2: Introduced a scalable extrapolation approach to mitigate algorithmic errors in quantum optimization algorithms like quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolvers. Contributions: - Energy Extrapolation Technique: Improved ground state energy estimates using annealing time and variance. - Analytic Derivations: Provided convergence proofs emphasizing the role of correlations. - Robustness Against Noise: Demonstrated suitability for near-term devices. Paper 4: Built an optical neural network (ONN) for quantum state tomography of photonic polarization qubits, using optical nonlinear activation functions. Contributions: - Innovative ONN Design: Enabled efficient quantum state tomography. - Accurate State Determination: Showed potential in quantum information processing. - Integration of Optics and AI: Paved the way for optical quantum networks. These works demonstrate that understanding and leveraging many-body correlations are essential for advancing quantum information processing technologies. Short-Term Objective 1: Find convergent algorithms that determine the uniqueness of multipartite quantum wave functions based on their local parts, among all density matrices. Realisation: Methods in Papers 1 and 2 offer insights: Paper 1: The reinforcement learning approach suggests machine learning can navigate complex quantum systems, indicating potential for algorithms determining state uniqueness via efficient exploration of local measurements. Paper 2: The energy extrapolation method informs algorithm development by examining convergence properties related to measurement variances. These advancements lay groundwork for creating convergent algorithms determining uniqueness from local information. Short-Term Objective 2: Find symmetry groups that lead to degenerate ground states uniquely determined by their local measurements. Realisation: Paper 3 contributes significantly by constructing VBS codes with specific symmetries, identifying groups resulting in degenerate ground states uniquely determined by local measurements. Contributions: - Symmetry Analysis: Investigated roles of symmetries in ground state degeneracy. - Uniqueness from Local Measurements: Demonstrated certain symmetries yield unique determination. - General Framework: Connected symmetry properties with ground state degeneracy and uniqueness. This enhances understanding of using symmetry to control quantum systems, fulfilling the objective. Short-Term Objective 3: Find an algorithm that can determine the uniqueness of multipartite wave functions based on their local parts, among all wave functions. Realisation: Paper 4 provides a promising direction: Demonstrated optical neural networks can learn mappings from local measurements to global state properties. Contributions: - Learning-Based Approach: Showed neural networks infer global information from local measurements. - Scalability: Indicated potential for handling complex systems, aiding uniqueness determination. This suggests advanced computational techniques can effectively solve quantum state determination problems. Short-Term Objective 4: Understand the correlations of eigenstates of local Hamiltonians and determine whether they are uniquely determined by local measurements. Realisation: Paper 3 offers insights: Eigenstate correlations indicates how local Hamiltonians produce specific correlation structures in quasi codes. Achievements: - Quasi-Exact Framework: Studied evolving correlations between exact and approximate eigenstates. - Uniqueness Determination: Explored conditions for unique determination by local measurements. Additionally, Papers 1 and 2 improved preparation and characterization of eigenstates, aiding correlation studies. Short-Term Objective 5: Understand the correlation of low-energy states of local Hamiltonians and determine whether they are uniquely determined by local measurements. Realisation: Our work in Papers 1 and 2 addresses this: Paper 1: Used reinforcement learning to prepare ground and thermal states, probing low-energy state correlations and uniqueness. Paper 2: Mitigated algorithmic errors, enhancing accuracy in low-energy state determination and understanding of correlations. These contributions deepen understanding of low-energy state correlations and their determinability from local measurements. Conclusion: The project has made substantial progress toward achieving all objectives: - Advancement in Correlation Hierarchies: Deepened understanding through quasi-exact and VBS codes. - Innovations in Quantum Information Processing: Contributions highlight the practical importance of many-body correlations. - Development of Algorithms and Methods: Advanced methods leveraging correlations and local measurements to determine quantum state properties. - Foundations for Future Research: Provided a solid foundation for further advancements. Our accomplishments bring us closer to a comprehensive understanding of many-body quantum systems and their applications, aligning with both our short-term and long-term objectives.

Correlation/entanglement in many-body wave functions plays a key role in determining the physical properties of quantum systems. Thus far, we have only acquired very limited knowledge of these phenomena in the interdisciplinary field of quantum information and quantum matter. In the proposed project, we will study the different types of correlations and their relationships with the quantum phase of matter, with the aim of generating a new basis for a fundamental microscopic theory of quantum matter. This will lead to the discovery of new quantum phases of matter, and new types of quantum materials.

Long-Term Objective 2 (over 10 years): Understand many-body correlation/entanglement as a fundamental resource for quantum information processing, including quantum tomography, quantum error correction, and quantum computing. Correlation and entanglement hold the key to deciphering the ultimate power of quantum information processing. Different types of correlations correspond to different complexities of quantum states and hence different information processing capabilities. Understanding these types of correlations will lead to more effective methods of performing quantum tomography and quantum error correction, and of building large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers.

Short-Term Objective 1: Find convergent algorithms that determine the uniqueness of multipartite quantum wave functions based on their local parts, among all of the density matrices. As physical interactions are local, it is reasonable to enquire whether a “natural” quantum states are determined by their local parts. Although some algorithms are known to calculate compatible states with the given measurement results, none are known to be convergent. To achieve this objective, we will explore the convergence of the existing algorithms and develop new algorithms.

Short-Term Objective 2: Find symmetry groups that lead to degenerate ground states, which are uniquely determined by their local measurements. The first set of examples of this phenomenon was only found very recently. These examples show that many-body quantum states exist that are uniquely determined by their local parts, but cannot be unique ground states of local Hamiltonians. Symmetry seems to play an essential role in building these examples. Thus, we will explore the role that symmetry plays in the ground states with the hope of finding a general theory that can describe the relationship between the correlation types and ground state degeneracy of local Hamiltonians.

Short-Term Objective 3: Find an algorithm that can determine the uniqueness of multipartite wave functions based on their local parts, among all of the wave functions. It was only until recently discovered that the set of wave functions uniquely determined by their local parts (called UDA) is different from the set of wave functions uniquely determined by their local parts among all of the wave functions (called UDP). However, the nature of the difference between UDA and UDP remains largely unknown. Thus, we will develop algorithms that can determine UDP to further study this UDA-UDP gap

Short-Term Objective 4: Understand the correlations of the eigenstates of local Hamiltonians, and determine whether these eigenstate wave functions are uniquely determined among all of the wave functions by local measurements. Some recent studies have shown that in generic cases, the eigenstates of local Hamiltonians can be determined by their local parts. How to characterize these kinds of eigenstate correlations among the known types of the correlation hierarchy remains to be determined. Thus, we will explore the relationship between the eigenstate correlation and UDP, which may add a new type of correlation to the known correlation hierarchy.

Short-Term Objective 5: Understand the correlation of the low-energy states of local Hamiltonians, and determine whether these wave functions are uniquely determined among all of the wave functions by local measurements. Low-energy states are not uniquely determined by their local parts, because states with the same local parts can be obtained by mixing states with different energy. However they may be natural candidates for UDP. Thus, we will further examine these states with the hope of developing a better understanding of the UDA-UDP gap.

16300220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300220.value: Our project achieved significant advancements in understanding many-body quantum states, their correlations, and applications in quantum information processing, aligning with our objectives in Part C. 1. Quasi-Exact Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (Paper 3): We introduced the theory of quasi-exact fault-tolerant quantum (QEQ) computation using ''quasi codes,'' parametric approximate quantum error-correction codes that become exact upon parameter tuning. By analyzing valence-bond-solid (VBS) codes, we demonstrated QEQ computation. This advances our understanding of the correlation hierarchy in many-body quantum states with local Hamiltonians and connects to different quantum phases of matter, fulfilling Long-Term Objective 1. 2. Error Mitigation via Reinforcement Learning (Paper 1): We developed a deep reinforcement learning method to steer quantum imaginary time evolution, mitigating algorithmic errors from Trotterization and local approximations. The agent finds evolution paths where errors cancel out, enhancing fidelity in preparing ground and thermal states on near-term quantum devices. This demonstrates the utility of managing many-body correlations and entanglement, contributing to Long-Term Objective 2 and Short-Term Objectives 1 and 5. 3. Energy Extrapolation for Quantum Optimization (Paper 2): We presented a scalable extrapolation method to mitigate algorithmic errors in quantum optimization algorithms like quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolvers. By extrapolating annealing time to infinity or measurement variance to zero, we improved ground state energy estimates. Analytical derivations and experiments confirmed the method's validity, enhancing our ability to exploit correlations for improved computation, aligning with Long-Term Objective 2 and Short-Term Objectives 1 and 5. 4. Optical Neural Network Quantum State Tomography (Paper 4): We built an optical neural network (ONN) with optical nonlinear activation functions based on electromagnetically induced transparency. The ONN accurately determined the phase parameter of photonic polarization qubit states, showcasing the potential of integrating optics with neural networks for quantum state tomography. This harnesses entanglement and correlations in practical applications, contributing to Short-Term Objective 3 and advancing Long-Term Objective 2. Overall Outcome: Our findings meet the project's objectives. We deepened understanding of many-body correlations and developed novel quantum error-correction codes through QEQ computation and VBS codes (Paper 3). We introduced innovative error mitigation strategies via reinforcement learning (Paper 1) and energy extrapolation (Paper 2), enhancing fidelity and accuracy in quantum computations. We pioneered an optical neural network for quantum state tomography (Paper 4), integrating optical technologies with artificial intelligence.

16300220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300220.value: Building on our significant findings, the research has substantial potential for further advancement in both theoretical understanding and practical applications. For further development, - We plan to explore new classes of quasi-exact quantum error-correcting codes beyond valence-bond-solid (VBS) codes. Investigating their properties could lead to the discovery of novel quantum phases and materials. - Extending the reinforcement learning approach to steer other quantum algorithms and handle larger, more complex quantum systems is a priority. This includes integrating machine learning with quantum control techniques to optimize state preparation and error mitigation across various quantum platforms. - Further development of extrapolation methods aims to improve accuracy and efficiency in quantum optimization algorithms. Applying these techniques to a broader class of Hamiltonians and quantum devices will enhance their robustness and practical utility. Proposed Course of Action: We will pursue interdisciplinary collaborations, secure additional funding and resources will enable us to accelerate the translation of theoretical insights into practical quantum technologies.

16300220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300220.value: Our research aims to improve quantum computing, a technology that can solve complex problems much faster than today's computers. Quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which can exist in multiple states at once due to quantum phenomena like entanglement and superposition. We developed new methods to enhance the reliability and efficiency of quantum computers: Reducing Errors with Artificial Intelligence: We applied reinforcement learning, a type of artificial intelligence, to better control quantum systems. Improving Optimization Algorithms: We created techniques to correct errors in quantum optimization algorithms, essential for solving complex tasks in fields like logistics and material design. Innovative Error-Correcting Codes: We introduced new error-correcting codes called ''quasi-exact codes'' and ''valence-bond-solid codes'' that protect quantum information from errors, which is crucial for building reliable, large-scale quantum computers. Optical Neural Networks for Quantum States: We built an optical neural network using light to accurately determine the state of a quantum system. This combines artificial intelligence with quantum physics and could lead to advances in quantum communication and sensing. Overall, our work brings us closer to practical and reliable quantum computing, potentially revolutionizing technology by solving problems currently impossible for classical computers.

16300320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300320.value: A central task of synthetic chemistry is finding new ways to control bond formation and selectivity. In the proposed project, we will develop a novel donor/acceptor carbene mimetic for asymmetric sigmatropic rearrangement reactions. Carbene is a central species and an indispensable reaction intermediate for molecular synthesis. Due to carbene’s kinetic and transient nature, chemistry involving carbene is executed via diazo precursors or carbenoid intermediates using transition-metal catalysts. However, the vast majority of diazo compounds are shock sensitive, which excludes usage of related carbene chemistry in large-scale industrial operations. In the proposed project, we will explore a new strategy that uses a chemically benign, non-diazo, formylcarbene mimetic to unlock an asymmetric sigmatropic rearrangement reaction. This transformation will accomplish direct C–H difunctionalization of aldehydes, leading to products of utmost importance. The chemical versatility of the formyl group with a neighboring quaternary chiral center will be explored to generate a compound library possessing unique three-dimensional (3D) conformation. Detailed analysis of asymmetric control will be discussed and telescoped organocatalysis will be proposed to address the challenging issue of enantioselectivity. Preliminary results support the proposed mode of action, wherein a moderate level of enantioselectivity was accomplished. This project is expected to greatly expand carbene chemistry to access chiral compounds with tremendous synthetic diversity. 合成化學的核心任務是發現新方法來控制化學鍵的選擇性構建。本申請書計劃發展一類新的供體/受體卡賓模擬體來進行不對稱sigmatropic重排反應。卡賓是分子合成中不可替代的重要中間體。由於卡賓的高活性和短暫的壽命，卡賓化學通常是通過重氮化合物前提經由過渡金屬催化來執行的。然而，絕大多數重氮化合物是易爆物質，無法在大規模工業生產使用。本申請計劃探索一類新的化學穩定的非重氮醛基卡賓模擬體來解鎖不對稱sigmatropic重排反應。該反應將一步實現醛類化合物的碳氫雙官能團化，在合成中具有重要的價值。所獲得的產物含有一個四級碳手性中心和一個鄰近的衍生能力很強的醛基官能團，可以產生具有獨特三維分子結構的化合物庫。在本申請書中，我們詳細討論了不對稱選擇性的控制思路，並提出利用遠程協同的有機催化來解決對映選擇性這一科學難點。在初步試驗中，我們獲得了中等的對映選擇性，驗證了所提出的作用機制。本課題具有廣闊的合成多樣性，將大大拓寬卡賓化學在手性化合物合成中的應用。

16300320.label: Realisation of objectives
16300320.value: This project has successfully achieved all the outlined objectives, establishing a novel and safe approach to sigmatropic rearrangement reactions, achieving high enantioselectivity, developing a straightforward synthesis strategy for valuable heterocycles, generalizing the concept of a carbene mimetic, and obtaining a diverse library of chiral spiro scaffolds. The results have significant implications for the field of organic chemistry, particularly in the synthesis of complex molecular architectures and the development of new pharmaceutical agents. Below is a summary of the completion status for each of the objectives. Objective 1: Establish a Novel Protocol for Sigmatropic Rearrangements via a Non-Diazo, Non-Carbene Intermediate - We successfully developed a novel protocol for sigmatropic rearrangement that avoids the use of diazo compounds, addressing safety and reactivity concerns. - The protocol utilizes α-iodo-imine as a formylcarbene equivalent, generated through amine-catalyzed electrophilic iodination of aldehydes. Objective 2: Accomplish a High Level of Enantioselectivity for Sigmatropic Rearrangements Using Organocatalysis - We achieved high levels of enantioselectivity in sigmatropic rearrangements (up to 99% ee) through the use of synergistic organocatalysis. - We identified a combination of chiral trans-1,2-cyclohexanediamine and a chiral phosphoric acid as a remarkable catalyst system for the intramolecular asymmetric [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement reaction. - We systematically optimized reaction parameters and the substrate scope to demonstrate the generality of this protocols in the synthesis of sulfur-containing quaternary chiral centers. Objective 3: Develop a Straightforward Strategy for Synthesis of Valuable Saturated Sulfur-Containing Heterocycles - We established a straightforward strategy for the synthesis of valuable saturated sulfur-containing heterocycles from simple aldehydes tethered with sulfide. - This method employed a single-step [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of aldehyde substrates, resulting in the formation of chiral tetrahydrothiophene and tetrahydro-2H-thiopyran frameworks, both featuring a chemically versatile bridgehead formal group. - We explored the chemical versatility of the formal group under various reaction conditions, successfully achieving a straightforward synthesis of a number of chiral sulfur-containing spiro compounds. Objective 4: Generalize the Concept of a Donor-Acceptor Carbene Mimetic to a Series of Transformations - We established σ-iodo iminium as a donor-acceptor carbene mimetics for insertion and [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement to perform double functionalization of the σ-carbon of aldehydes. - We demonstrate that σ-iodo iminium can also function as a carbene equivalent in organocatalytic cross-coupling reactions. - We developed a novel carbene precursor, I,S-ylide, and demonstrated its capabilities in generating donor-acceptor carbenes and carbene cascades in various insertion reactions. Objective 5: Obtain a Compound Library of Intriguing Structures, Such as Chiral Spiro Scaffolds - We successfully established a compound library featuring novel chiral spiro scaffolds by leveraging the reactivity of the α-chiral center in cyclic sulfides. - We synthesized a series of 1,2-dicarbonyl alkenes with high stereoselectivity (E/Z ratio) through α-iodo-imine mediated cross-coupling reactions, expanding the library with structurally diverse compounds. - We prepared a diverse library of complex structures, including tetrasubstituted allenes, carboxylates with bulky β-sidechains, and carboxylates containing a chiral selenium center, through N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalyzed multicomponent reactions. - We utilized our newly developed donor-acceptor carbene precursor (I,S-ylide) to execute a range of cycloaddition and double/triple functionalization reactions, resulting in a library of synthetically challenging structures that are not easily accessible by conventional methods.
