16300320.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300320.value: (1) We developed the first organocatalytic enantioselective [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement using a diazo-free donor-acceptor carbene mimetic, σ-iodo iminium. (2) We developed an organocatalytic protocol that enables the direct coupling of aliphatic aldehydes with sulfonium ylides via a key carbene mimetic, α-iodoenamine/enol. (3) We developed an NHC-catalyzed four-component reactions via radical relay. (4) We accomplished NHC-catalyzed 1,4-alkylacylation of 1,3-enynes. (5) We accomplished the first highly enantioselective seleno-Michael addition using a designer chiral bifunctional NHC catalyst. (6) We developed a novel non-diazo donor-acceptor carbene precursor, I,S-ylide, and demonstrate its carbene reactivity in photoinduced cycloaddition to unsaturated bonds. (7) We accomplished cascade insertion reactions using a carbene relay strategy, including intermolecular [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement.

16300320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300320.value: Our project has designed a novel, stable non-diazo carbene precursor with remarkable domino reactivity, surpassing existing carbene species in multifunctionalization reactions. Looking ahead, we aim to further explore this reagent across diverse chemical contexts, thereby pushing the frontiers of carbene chemistry and unlocking new synthetic pathways.

16300320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300320.value: In our project, we have developed innovative reaction intermediates that can carry out a series of reactions in sequence, all without relying on shock-sensitive diazo compounds. This is a significant advance in carbene chemistry. Carbenes, which are highly reactive molecules capable of forming new chemical bonds, play a vital role in the creation of complex molecules used in pharmaceuticals and materials science. Our new intermediate can selectively form multiple bonds in a single, stereoselective process. This advancement promises to streamline the synthesis of complex chemicals, making it more efficient and eco-friendly. It could also pave the way for the development of new medications and cutting-edge materials.

16300620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300620.value: Direct C-H bond functionalization is emerging as one of the most valuable synthetic methods, allowing the incorporation of functional groups into organic molecules and facilitating the improved synthesis of useful pharmaceuticals, agrichemicals and organic materials. Despite challenges, great advances have been made in research areas associated with C-H bond functionalization. Among the advances made, copper-catalyzed radical relay reactions have attracted considerable interest and attention recently. Over the past few years, copper-catalyzed radical relay reactions have been shown to efficiently catalyze the difunctionalization of alkenes and regioselective C-H bond functionalization. Collaborating with experimentalists, we have carried out theoretical (density functional theory, DFT) studies of these catalytic reactions to gain a deeper understanding of their outcomes. All these work have placed us at the forefront of this research area. This proposal builds on our very recent work (jointly published in Nature by an experimental group and ourselves) regarding site-specific allylic hydrogen atom transfer by a Cu(II)-bound N-centered radical. In this just published work, our theoretical calculations showed that a Cu(II)-bound N-centered radical was able to amplify the site-selectivity of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) among similar allylic C–H bonds in a complex molecule. As a continuation of this important work, in the proposed project we intend to perform DFT calculations to systematically explore the mechanisms underlying these HAT reactions, as well as the effect of ligands and reagents on their site-selectivity. We hope that this research will provide guidance to experimental work dedicated to the development of new or improved processes for targeted organic synthesis. 16300720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300720.value: String theory was designed to combine quantumn field theory with gravity. It suggests that our universe has a hidden freedom called Calabi-Yau(CY) threefold, and particles are states of a vibrating string whose trace of movement in the CY threefold is the origin of particle interactions observed in the lab. A special measurement of such traces is the enumeration of the numbers of surfaces or worldsheets in a CY threefold. Denoting g to be the number of loops in the worldsheet, usually called the genus, the whole enumeration is encoded in a series Fg, which provides important ingredients in type IIA string theory, and have been known to be very difficult to calculate for almost three decades. Recently, for a special CY threefold, the quintic threefold, a "Feynman structure" among its Fgs is established by Mixed-Spin-P(MSP) field moduli, and this determines the Fgs up to finite data effectively. In this project, we aim to search for N-Mixed-Spin-P theory for a more general class of CY threefolds, namely those smooth complete intersections in weighted projective spaces or toric varieties. If such can be found with properties analogous to those in the quintic MSP example, the task if evaluating all Fgs for all these CY threefolds will be largely reduced to the problem of determining finite many data. We will look for a package of them that can lead to a 'Feynman structure" for such CY threefolds. This would then verify the the prediction of Bershadsky-Cecotti-Ooguri-Vafa)in 1993 for such CY's. The result will enhance our understanding of type IIA string theory in mathematics. 弦理論的目的是統合量子場論和相對論. 在弦論中我們的宇宙 有一隱藏的維度, 被稱之為 卡拉比-丘 流形, 而且粒子是 一根弦的震動態. 該弦在 卡拉比-丘 流形 中運動的軌跡的量度 給出了實驗室觀察到的粒子交互作用的常數. 在各種量度中有一種特殊的量度等同於在卡拉比-丘 流形裡面數 黎曼曲面(也被稱為世界面）的個數. 用 g 代表 該世界面的圈數(也被稱為虧格). 則這個計數的結果 是冪級數 Fg, 成為了 type 2A 弦理論中很重要的一個部分. 最近 對於特殊的 卡拉比-丘 流形: 五次三維流行, 人們發現了其 Fg (各種g) 必須滿足的一種一種``費曼結構”, 給出了數學的嚴格證明. 這套理論是為 混合P旋場 理論 (MSP). 這些結果可以決定 無限多個 Fg, 只要知道有限個 (3g-3那麼多的）起始條件(數字). 在這個計畫中, 我們的目的是對更一般的 卡拉比-丘 流形, 也就是那寫可以寫成 加權射影空間或是toric簇裡面的全相交的 卡拉比-丘 流形, 來加以尋找 混合P旋場 理論. 如果成功的話 那麼對於非常大量的卡拉比-丘 流形(至少五億多種）我們都能獲得其憲論不變量Fg的有效決定法. 這決定法理應也是某 ``費曼結構”. 如果此結果完成, 一個主要推論即能證實 1993年 Bershadsky-Cecotti-Ooguri-Vafa 的預測這些結果將會使我們對於type 2A弦論之數學有更深刻的了解.

16300720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300720.value: Once objectives 5,6,7 are fully finished for general cases, a full BCOV type structural theorem for Gromov Witten invariants would be established for a general class of Calabi Yau manifold. This would be a milestone of the enumerative algebraic geometry.

16300720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300720.value: This work has further consolidated the mathematical rigor of string theory and laid the geometric foundation for infinite-dimensional path integrals. It enables expanding dimensions beyond the intrinsic Calabi-Yau spaces and unifying their high-genus theoretical structures, thus underscoring the significance of the hybrid P-spin field theory established through this research.

16300920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300920.value: Stick-slip motion is often observed in out-of-equilibrium disordered systems as a yield response to a smoothly-varying external forcing. It is characterized by intermittent bursts of irregular signals of different amplitudes, durations, and separations that result from the spontaneous depinning of mechanical contacts or fracture of materials. Earthquakes on faults and the mechanical failure of materials are two extreme examples of stick-slip events. While the incidence of these events is rare, their impact on our living conditions is often catastrophic. A common feature of stick-slip events is their broad range of slip sizes, manifest as power-law distributions of many orders of magnitude. The fact that very different systems behave in a similar manner has prompted extensive investigations for a common mechanism or universal law underpinning these phenomena. However, despite these experimental and theoretical efforts, it remains unclear whether the stick-slip dynamics arising from different systems are indeed determined by a common physical mechanism. Is the scaling behavior uniquely determined by a sequence of stick-slip instabilities, with no a priori dependence on the microscopic material properties and inhomogeneities? To answer this question, fundamental studies with well-characterized model systems are needed. In this project, we will conduct a systematic study of the stick-slip dynamics in two unique model systems, namely the moving contact line between a liquid-air interface and a micro-sized fiber and the friction between two mesoscale solid surfaces. In the experiment, we will use newly-developed force apparatuses based on atomic force microscopy to measure the capillary and frictional force fluctuations resulting from stick-slip motion. Micro-assembly, focused ion-beam milling, advanced surface patterning and coating techniques will be used to precisely control the solid-liquid and solid-solid interactions, as well as system dimensions, symmetry, and size, to enable study of the collective behavior of multiple slip events at the mesoscale in a well-characterized landscape of spatial disorder with single-slip resolution. The proposed research will establish quantitative methods and statistical laws that are essential to bridging the knowledge gap between the microscopic behavior of individual slips and the macroscopic laws of stick-slip motion. This will involve the exploration of new physics in out-of-equilibrium systems and the investigation of rare extreme events, both of which are of practical importance. New knowledge gained from this research will assist scientists in the development of reliable models for the physical prediction and early detection of precursors of catastrophic events, such as earthquakes and the stick-slip instability-based mechanical failure of materials. 黏滑运动作为一种在平稳变化的外力下的屈服反应，常见于一些非平衡态无序系统中。其特征表现即是由物体间力学接触的自发性脱落或者材料断裂引发的一系列强度，持续时间和间隔均不相同的信号的间歇性爆发。发生在地壳断层处的地震和力学材料的损伤便是黏滑运动的两个典型例子。尽管此类事件少见，但它给人类的生存环境带来的影响却是灾难性的。黏滑运动的一个常见特点是其每次滑动的幅度跨度很大并且呈现为多个数量级之广的幂次率分布。由于差异巨大的物理系统在发生黏滑运动时表现相似，这引起了对黏滑运动共有机理甚至其后所隐藏的普遍性定律的广泛研究。然而，这些实验和理论层面的研究努力依旧未能清晰揭示不同系统中的黏滑运动是否由一种普遍性物理机理来决定。滑动幅度的分布律是否唯一地由不稳定黏滑过程决定，而非先验性地和材料的微观性质和内部缺陷关联？为了回答这个问题，对特征明确的相关系统进行基础透彻的研究就非常必要。 在这份研究方案中，我们将会在两个独特的模型系统中对黏滑运动进行系统性的研究分析，一个是固-液-气三相接触线在一根微米粗细的玻璃棒表面的运动，另一个是介观尺度大小的两个固体表面之间的摩擦。实验中，我们将利用新设计的基于原子力显微镜的力学测量装置来测量在两个系统中发生黏滑运动时分别引起的毛细力和摩擦力的波动。我们将用到微组装，聚焦离子束，先进表面刻图和涂层处理技术来精细控制固-液和固-固相互作用力以及系统维度，对称性，尺寸，以便使我们在拥有检测单个滑动的精度条件下对介观尺度下发生在空间无序性可表的系统中对多处滑动的集体行为进行研究。这个研究方案将会确定一套可量化的方法以及统计规律，来联系关于微观尺度单滑动和宏观黏滑动已有的知识。研究将包含关于非平衡态系统在外力驱动下的新物理规律的探索以及对于稀有事件发生规律的探查，而这两者在实用性的角度都有重大意义。基于这项研究所获得的新知识将帮助科学家发展应用于物理预测和灾难性事件的早期预断方面的可靠模型，比如地震和不稳定黏滑引发的力学材料失效问题。

16300920.label: Realisation of objectives
16300920.value: Since Prof. Penger Tong’s contract as Chair Professor of Physics at HKUST expired in June 2022, the PI of this project has been Prof. Qin Xu in the Department of Physics for over six months. In 2023, Prof. Tong renewed his contract as Chair Professor of Physics at HKUST for an additional five years. RGC approved him to lead this research project continuously as the PI, and he is fully responsible for completing the report. To fulfill this project’s two research objectives, we conducted two sets of experiments to investigate avalanches and extreme statistics in the stick-slip motion of moving contact lines and solid friction. In the first set of experiments, we systematically studied the stick-slip friction of a mesoscale contact area sliding against an ultrafine sandpaper. Stick-slip is a common phenomenon both in nature and in many engineering applications. It is often observed in out-of-equilibrium disordered systems as a yield response to a smoothly varying external force. Stick-slip is characterized by intermittent bursts of irregular signals of varying amplitudes, durations, and separations, resulting from the spontaneous depinning of mechanical contacts or the local rearrangement of material bonds. Among the stick-slip phenomena explored thus far, friction between two rough solid surfaces in contact has attracted special attention, partly due to its connection with earthquakes, whose impact on our daily lives is often catastrophic. Earthquakes on faults are believed to result from frictional stick-slip instabilities along pre-existing faults. Our current understanding of stick-slip friction is often limited to two spatial regimes. One involves macroscopic solid interfaces containing many asperities; thus, fluctuations resulting from individual slip events are averaged out. The other involves systems with a nanoscopically sharp tip sliding against a (rough) solid surface, and thus, only single-asperity dynamics are at play. In the experiments, we designed a novel lateral hanging-beam atomic-force microscope (AFM) to measure frictional force fluctuations over a mesoscale contact area. This setup can record the collective response of many slip events at the single-slip resolution. We conducted systematic experiments on a rough silicon carbide sandpaper surface to observe stick-slip behavior under varying normal loads. The AFM probes, designed in quasi-1D and 2D geometries, were used to measure the frictional force as a function of lateral displacement. We recorded a large dataset of frictional force measurements, focusing on the probability density functions (PDFs) of slip lengths, the maximum forces required to trigger slips, and the local force gradients of the asperity-induced pinning force field. These measurements provided a comprehensive statistical description of stick-slip friction, which is often associated with avalanche dynamics at a critical state. In particular, the measured PDF of slip lengths follows a power-law distribution. We developed a coarse-grained theoretical model for the under-damped spring-block motion under a Brownian-correlated pinning force field. This model predicts the power-law exponent for under-damped avalanche dynamics, which agrees well with the experimental result. Our model provides a long-sought physical mechanism for the avalanche dynamics in stick-slip friction at the mesoscale. In the second set of experiments, we investigated the pinning-depinning dynamics of a circular moving contact line (CL) on the rough surface of a micron-sized vertical hanging glass fiber that intersects a liquid-air interface. When a CL is pulled at a constant speed, the CL motion is accomplished by a continuous series of local pinning-depinning events from a finite number of defect sites (a few hundred) on the solid surface. It is commonly believed that the dynamics of CL-depinning involve avalanches of slip length, resulting in a power-law distribution of slip lengths. Experimental studies of the CL dynamics are often conducted in two spatial regimes. One is at the macroscopic level, in which a CL of macroscopic length interacts with many surface defects simultaneously, and thus, fluctuations resulting from individual slip events are averaged out. The other is at the nanoscopic level, where a nanoscale tip is in contact with a liquid interface. What is lacking in the study of CL dynamics is an experimental framework at the mesoscale that is small enough to resolve individual slip events but is also large enough to examine a broad range of slip lengths in a well-characterized defect landscape with a single-slip resolution. In the experiment, we developed a mesoscale experimental framework consisting of a micron-sized long-needle atomic force microscope (AFM) probe, which measures the capillary force acting on the circular moving CT formed on the hanging glass fiber. With this framework, we measured capillary force fluctuations, which exhibit sawtooth-like patterns, with a linear force accumulation of slope k (stick) followed by a sharp release of force f, proportional to the CL slip length x = f/k_0, where k_0 is the static spring constant of the CL. We collected a large number of stick-slip events under various experimental conditions, including different liquid interfaces and fiber surface roughness. The measurements enabled us to observe the hysteresis loops and force profiles associated with the CL motion. We applied extreme value statistics to analyze the local maximal force required for CL depinning. Additionally, we examined the power-law distribution of slip lengths, which characterizes the avalanche dynamics of the moving CL. Our experimental results were compared with the prediction of the Alessandro-Beatrice-Bertotti-Montorsi (ABBM) model to validate the observed scaling behavior and statistical properties of the stick-slip motion. Our experiment provided a comprehensive statistical description of the collective pinning-depinning dynamics at a critical state, bridging the gap between the microscopic behavior of individual slips and the macroscopic laws of contact angle hysteresis. The above two experimental investigations fully accomplished the project's two objectives. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic from 2021 to 2023 in Hong Kong, the PI and his team members were unable to attend in-person international and regional conferences. The research activities reported here were primarily conducted using existing equipment, and no major equipment purchases were made during this period. The funds obtained for this project were used mainly to support the research staff.

16300920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300920.value: Statistical Laws of Stick-Slip Friction at the Mesoscale. The study investigated stick-slip friction at the mesoscale contact using a lateral hanging-beam atomic force microscope, revealing significant insights into the statistical properties of this phenomenon. The measured probability density functions (PDFs) of slip lengths, the maximum force required to trigger local slips, and the local force gradient of the pinning force field provide a comprehensive statistical description of stick-slip friction, which is often associated with avalanche dynamics at a critical state. In particular, the measured PDF of slip lengths obeys a power-law distribution indicative of avalanche dynamics. The power-law exponent varies with probe geometry, emphasizing the role of multiple asperities in the stick-slip process. The experimental findings suggest that the stick-slip behavior operates at a critical point, with the measured quantities showing universal statistical properties. Furthermore, we introduced a coarse-grained theoretical model, which provides a physical mechanism for the observed avalanche dynamics. The research establishes a comprehensive statistical framework for understanding stick-slip friction, bridging the gap between microscopic slip events and macroscopic friction laws. This work was published in Nature Communications in 2023. Avalanches and Extreme Value Statistics of a Mesoscale Moving Contact Line. Our experiments revealed key insights into the scaling behavior and statistical properties of the stick-slip motion of moving contact lines. The capillary force exhibited saw-tooth-like fluctuations, characterized by linear accumulations followed by sharp releases, indicative of mesoscale stick-slip dynamics. The local maximal force required for contact line depinning conformed to extreme value statistics, represented by a generalized extreme value distribution. Additionally, the measured slip lengths followed a power-law distribution, confirming the presence of avalanche dynamics and the absence of a characteristic slip length. The dynamic spring constant exhibited significant fluctuations and was characterized by an exponential distribution, indicating the influence of surface roughness on local force gradients. The experimental findings are in good agreement with the prediction of the Alessandro-Beatrice-Bertotti-Montorsi (ABBM) model, highlighting the collective stick-slip events among multiple defects on the glass fiber. The experiment provides an accurate statistical description of the contact line dynamics at the mesoscale, which has important implications for a common class of problems involving stick-slip motion in a random defect or roughness landscape. This work was published in Physical Review Letters in 2024.

16300920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300920.value: The research activities successfully addressed the project objectives by providing a comprehensive statistical description of stick-slip dynamics at the mesoscale. The experimental findings contribute to a deeper understanding of frictional behavior at solid interfaces, with potential applications in materials science and geophysics. The experimental framework developed during this study lays the groundwork for future investigations into complex frictional phenomena. Up to now, we have only measured the frictional force fluctuations using a long-beam atomic force microscope (AFM), and no information is available about what happens at the micro-contacts between the two rough surfaces. We aim to leverage our new analytical capabilities to systematically investigate the correlation between the frictional force releases to be measured by AFM and the corresponding micro-contact evolution, which can be visualized simultaneously using total internal reflection microscopy. This spatial-temporal correlation is crucial for bridging the gap between the microscopic behavior of individual slips and the macroscopic laws of friction at solid interfaces. We plan to seek additional funding to support this initiative.

16300920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300920.value: Stick-slip motion is a common phenomenon observed in nature and various engineering applications. An example of stick-slip events is the earthquake along fault lines. Although these events happen infrequently, their effects can be devastating. This research project investigated the statistical behavior of stick-slip dynamics in two well-characterized systems: a moving contact line between a liquid interface and a rough solid substrate and solid friction between two rough surfaces. This topic is of concern in many engineering applications, ranging from reducing frictional loss between sliding solid surfaces to the early detection and prevention of mechanical material failure and earthquakes. Using a specially designed atomic force microscope, we measured the statistical distribution of slip lengths and the forces required to trigger them, which follows extreme value statistics, much like the way avalanches occur in nature. The experimental findings suggest that stick-slip operates at a critical point, where even small changes can have significant effects. By providing a clearer understanding of how these stick-slip events work, our research not only advances scientific knowledge but also has practical implications for improving materials and technologies that rely on friction. The results were published in high-impact journals, underscoring their significance within the scientific community.

16301020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16301020.value: 有限域上的短化線性碼

16301020.label: Project Objectives
16301020.value: Develop a general theory for shortened linear codes over finite fields. Construct linear codes over finite fields with desirable parameters by shortening known families of linear codes over finite fields. Study applications and properties of shortened linear codes.
rows: Develop a general theory for shortened linear codes over finite fields.
Construct linear codes over finite fields with desirable parameters by shortening known families of linear codes over finite fields.
Study applications and properties of shortened linear codes.

16301020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301020.value: Linear codes have important applications in communication systems, computer systems, data storage systems, and consumer electronics. They are related to many areas of mathematics, such as algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic function fields, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorics, finite fields, finite geometry, graph theory, and group theory. An important but challenging problem in the theory and applications of coding theory is the construction of optimal linear codes and linear codes with desirable parameters. One way of obtaining such codes is by shortening certain families of linear codes. This technique has been known for a long time, but has been overlooked by the community of coding theory from the very beginning. By now, only a handful of references on shortened linear codes exist in the literature. The first objective of this project is to develop general theory for shortened linear codes over finite fields. Specifically, it will be shown that every linear code over a finite field with minimum distance two can be shortened from a linear code in a special family of linear code. Relations between a shortened code and its original code will be developed. The second objective is to construct linear codes with optimal or desirable parameters by shortening certain known families of linear codes. The third objective is to study applications and properties of the shortened codes obtained in this project. The outputs of this project would enhance coding theory and would also have applications in engineering. 線性碼在通信系統，計算機系統，數據存儲系統和電子消費品中有廣泛的應用。線性碼與數學的許多分支有密切的關系， 例如，代數，代數幾何，代數函數域，代數數論，結合方案，組合設計，有限域，有限集合，圖論和群論。 構造好參數的或者最優的線性碼是編碼學理論及其應用的一個很重要但具有挑戰性的問題。短化一些已有的線性碼類是構造好參數的或者最優的線性碼的一個途徑。短化線性碼這個技術有很久的歷史，但是一直沒有受到編碼學界的重視。到目前為止，短化碼的文獻不超過12篇。 本項目的第一個目標是建立短化碼的一般理論。第一個目標內的第一個任務是証明任何一個線性碼（假定它的對偶距離至少為2）都能通過短化一類特殊線性碼中的某個碼得到。第一個目標內的第二個任務是找到各種短化碼與原碼之間的聯系。本項目的第二個目標是通過短化一些特殊的線性碼來得到好參數的或者最優的線性碼。本項目的第三個目標是研究本項目所得到的短化碼的性能和應用。 預期本項目的成果會加強編碼學的理論和應用。

16301020.label: Realisation of objectives
16301020.value: All the three objectives have been fully achieved. A general theory for shortened linear codes over finite fields has been developed. It has been proved that every projective linear code is a shortened Hamming code. Linear codes over finite fields with variable parameters have been constructed by shortening several known families of linear codes over finite fields. Specifically, some shortened codes of the Hamming codes, Simplex codes, some Reed-Muller codes, and ovoid codes have been studied. Eleven families of optimal shortened codes over finite fields have been obtained. Applications of shortened linear codes in combinatorics and locally recoverable codes have been given.

16301020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301020.value: 1) Some general theory for shortened linear codes was developed. For example, it is proved that every projective linear code is a shortened Hamming code. 2) Some shortened codes of the Hamming codes, Simplex codes, some Reed-Muller codes, and ovoid codes were studied. Eleven families of optimal shortened codes over finite fields were obtained. As applications of some shortened codes, five infinite families of 2-designs were also constructed. 3) Some punctured codes of several families of binary linear codes were studied. Several families of binary linear codes with few weights and new parameters were obtained. Several families of distance-optimal binary linear codes with new parameters were also produced. 4) Linear codes generated by component functions of perfect nonlinear (PN for short) and almost perfect nonlinear (APN for short) functions and the first-order Reed-Muller codes have been an object of intensive study in coding theory. Some binary shortened codes of two families of linear codes from APN functions and some p-ary shortened codes associated with PN functions were investigated. The weight distributions of these shortened codes and the parameters of their duals were determined. The parameters of these binary codes and p-ary codes are flexible. Many of the codes obtained are optimal or almost optimal. Our results show that the shortening technique is very promising for constructing good codes. 5) Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) were proposed for the recovery of data in distributed and cloud storage systems. The minimum locality of several families of shortened linear codes were settled. Our results mentioned above were published as three papers in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, the best journal in the area of information and coding theory, and one paper in another reputable journal.

16301020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301020.value: We may look for other applications of shortened linear codes. For example, we may investigate applications of some shortened linear codes in cryptography. We may study some shortened codes of the Simplex codes.

16301020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301020.value: The shortening technique is one of the several methods for constructing new linear codes from known linear codes. It is proved in this project that every projective linear code over a finite field is a shortened code of a Hamming code. This general result demonstrates the importance of the shortening technique and the Hamming codes. Many families of shortened linear codes with optimal parameters have been constructed in this project. Parameters and the weight distributions of some shortened linear codes have been determined. Applications of some shortened linear codes in combinatorics have been demonstrated. Applications of some shortened codes in LRCs have also been investigated.

16301120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301120.value: 由於高價鐵(Fe)化合物作為中間體參與到鐵介導的有機合成和生物學上相關的酶氧化反應而引起了近期的廣泛關注。這些化合物也與關鍵的鐵基廢水處理工藝有關。在這些化合物中，高價鐵氧化物已引起了特別的注意，由於它們已被預測作為某些血紅素和非血紅素酶的活性氧化劑。由於這個原因，人們已經花費大量的努力來理解氧化鐵/羥基鐵配合物的合成和反應性。大多數報導的鐵(IV)化合物在室溫條件下非常不穩定，因此通常在低溫下在有機溶劑中進行分離和表徵。 相反，具有氮橋聯配體的雙核鐵(IV)化合物已顯示易於製備且相對穩定。因此，這些化合物提供了獨特的機會來研究複雜的高價鐵化學。以前，Sorokin及其同事報導說，氮橋聯的雙核鐵酞菁配合物催化過氧化物與碳氫化合物的氧化，推測是通過活性雙核鐵(IV)-氧代活性物質。儘管已經證明了Fe-N-Fe配合物（N = 構成氮橋的氮原子）對C-H的催化活性，但尚未探索相關雜金屬M-N-Fe (M = 過渡金屬）化合物的氧化化學。我們在以前的工作中證明，可以通過Fe(II)配合物與Ru(VI)氮化物的反應方便地合成異金屬 Ru-N-Fe(IV)(Ru = 釕)配合物。這種成功的合成策略使我們能夠製備一系列Ru-N-Fe(mac)(mac =大環/螯合配體）配合物，然後闡明影響其氧化還原化學的因素。 在擬議的項目中，我們將通過合成帶有卟啉，酞菁和席夫鹼配體的水溶性 M-N-Fe (M = Ru，Os)水配合物來獲得成功。這些配合物在水中的酸鹼，氧化還原和氧化化學也將被研究。此外，將通過氧化M-N-Fe水配合物或光解M-N-Fe氧陰離子配合物來合成高價雜金屬鐵的羥基/氧雜物，並將研究其對烴類底物的反應性。此外，將闡明控制這些鐵羥基/氧代物種的氫原子提取和氧原子轉移反應性的因素。最後，將嘗試開發基於水溶性M-N-Fe絡合物的非均相催化劑，用於在環境友好的水性介質中氧化有機底物。

16301120.label: Realisation of objectives
16301120.value: The objectives of this research project are: (1) To synthesize water-soluble heterometallic M-N-Fe complexes (2) To study the redox chemistry of water-soluble M-N-Fe complexes (3) To generate higher-valent heterometallic iron hydroxo/oxo complexes and explore their hydrogen atom abstraction and oxygen atom transfer chemistries. (4) To develop M-N-Fe-based catalysts for green oxidation of organic substrates We have developed a method to synthesize water-soluble heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes to achieve the first objective. A series of iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) nitrido complexes containing water-soluble porphyrins, such as tetrakis(sulfonatopoprhyrin) (TPPS) and tetrakis(carboxyphenyl)porphyrins (TCPP), have been synthesized from iron(II) porphyrins and ruthenium(VI) nitride starting materials, such as [(LOEt)Ru(N)Cl2] (LOEt- = [CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3]-) and [Ru(N)(salen)(MeOH)](PF6) (salen2- = tetradentate Schiff base ligand). These complexes have been fully characterized spectroscopically, and their bonding has been analyzed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies. Spectroscopic and X-ray diffraction studies have confirmed the iron(IV)-ruthenium(VI) formulation. We have shown that the binding of the ruthenium nitride to the iron porphyrin not only enhances the solubility of the water-soluble heterometallic nitrido complexes in organic solvents, facilitating their isolation and crystallization, but also inhibit their aggregation in water. In addition, using charge-neutral or cationic ruthenium(VI) nitrides as starting materials, we were able to tune the redox and catalytic property of the heterometallic iron/ruthenium nitrido complexes. Apart from iron, we have shown that high-valent iridium can also be stabilized by binding with ruthenium(VI) nitrides. For example, an iridium-ruthenium nitrido complex, [(H2O)Cl(C^N^C)Ir-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2], supported by a dianionic C^N^C ligand has been synthesized. NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction study have confirmed the iridium(V)-ruthenium(IV) formulation of the complex. To address the second objective, we have investigated the electrochemistry of the water-soluble iron(IV) nitrido porphyrin complex Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] in aqueous solution. The two redox couples observed in the cyclic voltammogram of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] in acidic solution have been unambiguously identified as metal-centered and porphyrin centered couples, respectively. A formally iron(V)-ruthenium(IV) nitrido complex has been synthesized via chemical oxidation of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] and characterized spectroscopically. The reactivity of this iron(V) complexes toward phosphines, thioethers, and alcohols has been studied. In addition, we have synthesized an iridium(VI)-ruthenium(IV) nitrido complex bearing a chlorinated C^N^C ligand via the oxidation of [(H2O)Cl(C^N^C)Ir-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] with PhICl2, demonstrating the ability of the ruthenium nitride to stabilize high-valent iridium. As for the third objective, we have generated high-valent heterometallic iron peroxo and oxo species that have been characterized by high-resolution mass spectrometry via the oxidation of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] with hydrogen peroxide in water. The iron oxo species can undergo oxo transfer to organic substrates such as phosphines and thioethers. In addition, it can oxidize alcohols and thiols in aqueous media via H-atom transfer. The factors affecting the reactivity of this transient iron oxo species have been investigated. It was found that the aqueous media and tetra-anionic nature of the TPPS ligand play important roles in stabilizing the high-valent iron oxo and peroxo species. To address the fourth objective, catalytic systems for oxidation of organic substrates using environmentally benign hydrogen peroxide have been developed. We have found that Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] is an efficient catalyst for the oxidation of thioethers with hydrogen peroxide in alcohols or aqueous media. The factors affecting the catalytic activity of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] have been elucidated. It has been found that the tetra-anionic nature of the complex and the aqueous reaction media are beneficial to the catalytic oxidations. On the basis of UV-visible spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, a mechanism involving an iron peroxo intermediate that undergoes heterolytic O-O cleavage to give a reactive iron-oxo species has been proposed for the catalytic oxidation with Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2]. In conclusion, in this research project, we have developed a synthetic route to water-soluble heterometallic iron nitrido porphyrin complexes, which enabled us to systematically elucidate the factors that control the stability and redox reactivity of high-valent heterometallic iron nitrido complexes in aqueous media. High-valent heterometallic iron(V)/ruthenium(IV) nitrido complexes have been synthesized by chemical oxidation of the iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) precursors and characterized spectroscopically. Notably, high-valent heterometallic iron peroxo and oxo species, which are able to undergo oxygen-atom and hydrogen-atom transfer with organic substrates, have been generated by oxidation of heterometallic iron nitrido complexes with hydrogen peroxide. We have for the first time characterized the heterometallic iron peroxo and oxo species by high-resolution mass spectrometry. The water-soluble iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) complex Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] has been shown to be an efficient catalyst for the oxidation of thioethers with hydrogen peroxide in water. The results of this project showcase the potential application of heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes in catalytic oxidations in environmentally friendly aqueous media.

16301120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301120.value: (i) A synthetic route to water-soluble heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes involving the reaction between iron(II) tetrakis(4-sulfonatophenyl)porphyrin (TPPS) and ruthenium(VI) nitrides has been developed. These iron(IV) complexes have been fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and X-ray diffraction. The crystal structure of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] (LOEt- = [CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3-] has been determined, providing new insights into the nature of the water-soluble porphyrin complex in solution. (ii) Cyclic voltametric studies have shown that the Fe(V/IV) potential of the Fe-N-Ru nitrido porphyrin complexes can be tuned by the porphyrin ligands and the ruthenium nitride moiety. Formally Fe(V) species have been generated by chemical oxidation of the heterometallic Fe(IV) nitrido precursors and characterized by UV/visible spectroscopy and spectroelectrochemistry. (iii) Catalytic systems for oxygen-atom transfer using heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes have been developed. Notably, Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] has been shown to be an efficient catalyst for the oxidation of thioethers by hydrogen peroxide in aqueous media. (iv) The reactive intermediates of the iron-catalyzed oxidation with hydrogen peroxide have been characterized. Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry indicated that the reaction of Na4[(TPPS)Fe-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2] with hydrogen peroxide generated a heterometallic peroxo species that was then converted into an oxo species, which is the active oxidant of catalytic oxidation. The oxygen-atom transfer reactions of the iron oxo species with substrates such as phosphines have been followed by mass spectrometry. (v) The first heterometallic iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) and ruthenium(IV)/ruthenium(IV) nitrido complexes bearing a polyvalent porphyrin, tetrakis(3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-hydroxyphenyl)porphyrin (TDBHPP), have been synthesized and structurally characterized. Oxidation of the iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) TDBHP complex with m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid led to isolation of a novel heterometallic nitrido complex containing a bis(quinone) porphyrin ligand. (vi) A series of heterometallic iron(IV)/ruthenium(IV) nitrido complexes derived from iron(II) Schiff base (salen) precursors have been synthesized. Unlike the porphyrin analogues, the iron center in these iron/ruthenium nitrido complexes can bind to a ligand, such as oxo. Trimetallic oxo- and nitrido-bridged complexes including [(ReO4)(salen)Fe-N-RuCl(py)(LOEt)] (py = pyridine) and a mixed valence Fe/Ru/Tl complex have been synthesized and structurally characterized. (vii) An Ir(V)-N-Ru(IV) complex, [Cl(H2O)(C^N^C)Ir-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2], supported by a dianionic tripodal C^N^C ligand has been synthesized. Oxidation of the Ir-N-Ru complex with PhICl2 yielded a mixed valence nitrido complex, [Cl2(Cl-C^N^C)Ir-N-Ru(LOEt)Cl2], containing a chlorinated C^N^C ligand. Density functional density calculations revealed that the unpaired spin of this mixed valence complex is mostly delocalized on iridium, indicative of the Ir(VI)-Ru(IV) resonance form. To our knowledge, this is the first heterometallic Ir(VI) nitrido complex, demonstrating the ability of the bridged nitrido ligand and the dianionic C^N^C ligand to stabilize high-valent iridium.

16301120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301120.value: In this project, we have demonstrated that heterometallic peroxo and oxo species generated by hydrogen peroxide oxidation iron(IV)/ruthenium nitrido complexes can be identified by mass spectrometry. In the future, effort should be made to study the kinetics and mechanism of the oxygen-atom transfer reactions of heterometallic peroxo and oxo species with organic substrates by high-resolution mass spectrometry. Understanding the mechanism and the factors that control the oxygen-atom transfer reactivity of heterometallic iron oxo species can help us develop efficient catalysts for organic oxidations in aqueous media. Furthermore, we have shown that the ruthenium center in the heterometallic iron-ruthenium nitrido complexes derived from the ruthenium(VI) Schiff base (salen) precursor, [Ru(N)(salen)]+, contains a vacant coordination site that is potentially useful in catalytic reactions. For example, [(TPP)Fe-N-Ru(salen)L] (L is an amine or anionic ligand) have been synthesized. In the future, efforts should be made to explore the catalytic activity of Fe-N-Ru(salen) complexes.

16301120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301120.value: High-valent iron species are of importance due to their involvement as reactive intermediates in iron-catalyzed oxidation and enzymatic processes. Although iron complexes in +IV or high oxidation states are well documented, these complexes are generally very reactive and unstable with respect to reduction, and therefore they are mostly isolated or characterized at low temperature. In this project, we have synthesized a new class of room-temperature stable iron(IV) complexes via the reaction between iron(II) precursors and ruthenium(VI) nitrides. This synthetic strategy has enabled us to synthesize a series of heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes with tuneable redox properties. Heterometallic iron(V) nitrido complexes have been synthesized via one-electron oxidation of the iron(IV) starting materials. Importantly, water-soluble heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido porphyrin complexes that can catalyze oxidation of organic substrates in aqueous media have been isolated and structurally characterized. We have for the first time characterized heterometallic iron peroxo and oxo species, which are active intermediate in the iron-catalyzed oxidation, using high-resolution mass spectrometry at room temperature. The results of this project showcase the potential application of heterometallic iron(IV) nitrido complexes as catalysts for green oxidations in environmentally benign aqueous media.

16301220.value: To synthesize and purify the major DNA and protein adducts of formaldehyde and their corresponding heavy isotope-labeled derivatives for use as standards and internal standards in the analysis. To identify and rigorously quantify the DNA and protein adducts of formaldehyde in serum protein and DNA samples isolated from patients suffering from leukemia, with the goals of identifying their potential causative roles and evaluating their possible use as biomarkers in human leukemia development. Matching healthy negative control (non-diseased) subjects and subjects who do not have leukemia but are exposed to benzene and formaldehyde as positive controls, i.e. smokers will also be recruited to the study. To identify novel DNA adducts, and thus the etiological agents, associated with leukemia development using an LC-MS/MS-based adductomics approach. It is anticipated that the results of this study will provide a better understanding of the roles played by other chemicals in causing leukemia. The identification of these DNA damaging agents can aid in formulating policy to prevent/minimize chemical exposure. Furthermore, it is hoped that the identified DNA adducts may act as biomarkers for clinical diagnosis and disease risk assessment.

16301220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301220.value: Leukemia is a group of blood cancers that produces large numbers of abnormal blood cells unable to perform the usual functions of oxygen transport and defense against invading pathogens. As a result, patients suffer from multiple symptoms including fatigue and increased risk of infections. Despite being one of the most devastating group of human cancers, the etiology of leukemia remains poorly understood. However, some epidemiological studies have revealed a cause-and-effect relationship between chemical exposure, e.g. occupational exposure to benzene, and leukemia. The goal of this study is to use a combination of targeted and non-targeted adductomics approaches to identify the carcinogen-induced DNA/protein adducts associated with genotoxicity, disease development and progression. Through these analyses, it is anticipated that the etiology of chemically-induced leukemia can be better understood, and biomarkers associated with the disease can be identified and used to predict the exposure level and disease risk. We will first synthesize and purify major chemical-DNA and -protein adducts associated with leukemia, and then develop the highly sensitive and selective liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometric (LC-MS/MS) methods needed to characterize the adducts in human blood samples. In this study, we will initially focus on benzene and formaldehyde, both implicated as potential human leukemogens, and identify and quantify the associated DNA and protein adducts formed between their reactive intermediates in hepatic metabolism and the DNA and protein molecules in cultured human blood cells. It is expected that the adduct levels will correlate to the degree of exposure. After completing the targeted adductomics analysis, we will proceed to a non-targeted DNA adductomics approach using blood samples isolated from leukemia-suffering patients, and identify DNA adducts that may be associated with disease development. In collaboration with medical practitioners and experts of the field, we will analyze the DNA hydrolysate using a non-targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometric (LC-MS) method, and then complement this with analysis of DNA samples isolated from healthy volunteers. From these crucial pieces, we will develop chemometric algorithms to identify the DNA adduct markers, thus the etiological agents of leukemia. We anticipate that the proposed adductomics platform will also be applicable in identifying the etiological agents of many other chemically induced human diseases, including liver, kidney, and lung cancers, by their unique adductomics profile signatures, useful in early disease diagnosis. 白血病是一类造血系统的恶性肿瘤性疾病，由于克隆性白血病细胞大量增殖累积，正常血细胞供氧、免疫等功能被抑制。因此，患者会出现疲劳、感染等多种症状。尽管白血病是最致命的癌症之一，但其致病源并不十分明确。一些流行病学研究显示，化学接触（如职业性接触苯）与白血病之间存在因果关系。本研究的目的是结合靶向分析和非靶向加合物组学来识别表征与基因毒性和疾病发生发展相关的DNA/蛋白质加合物。通过这些分析，可以更好地了解化学因素导致的白血病，开发与疾病相关的生物标志物检测方法，并将其用于预测暴露水平和疾病风险。 在靶向分析中，我们将主要研究有潜在致白血病作用的甲醛。在合成并纯化与白血病相关的主要DNA/蛋白质加合物后，我们将开发高灵敏度和高选择性的液相色谱-串联质谱（LC-MS/MS）方法用于检测血液样品中的加合物。通过在培养的血细胞中进行化学物质暴露、分离和检测定量，我们检验细胞中的加合物水平与暴露程度的相关性。 在完成靶向加合物分析后，我们将与该领域的医生和专家合作，使用非靶向液相色谱-质谱（LC-MS）方法分析DNA水解产物。通过对白血病患者的血液样本进行非靶向DNA加合物分析，并与来自健康志愿者的样本进行比较，确定可能与疾病发展相关的DNA加合物。通过开发化学计量学算法识别DNA加合物标记物，从而确定白血病的病因。本研究的加合物组学方法也可以应用于其它化学因素导致的人类疾病的早期诊断，如肝癌、肾癌和肺癌。

16301220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301220.value: Our study, which combined our developed sample preparation and cleanup methods, synthesized standards, heavy isotope-labeled internal standards, and LC-MS/MS techniques, discovered that cultured human cells and urine from volunteers subjected to high formaldehyde scenarios produced conjugated metabolites formed by the reaction of formaldehyde with glutathione (GSH) and associated amino acids, such as cysteine and cysteinyl-glycine, in high abundance. These metabolites were excreted in urine and can serve as biomarkers and dosimeters for quantifying human exposure to this leukemia-associated carcinogen, which is ubiquitous in both indoor and outdoor air. The results of this research were published in leading toxicology and environmental research journals (Chem. Res. Toxicol. 2022, 35, 858; Environ. Sci. Technol. 2024, 58, 16368). By combining the use of face masks as a novel air sampling method with LC-MS/MS analysis, we also explored their potential to identify airborne etiological agents, such as formaldehyde, associated with leukemia development. We anticipate that the results of this study will provide a user-friendly method for identifying and better understanding the roles played by formaldehyde and other chemicals in causing leukemia. Identifying these airborne toxicants can aid in formulating policies to prevent or minimize chemical exposure. Furthermore, we hope that the developed method will facilitate the identification of toxicants for disease risk assessment.

16301220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301220.value: There is accumulating evidence that many human diseases, including leukemia, are environmental diseases caused by a combination of multiple environmental factors. However, most current studies investigating the etiological agents involved in leukemia development focus on the targeted analysis of specific families of chemicals. Therefore, the breathing-through-face-mask method developed for air sampling could be expanded to simultaneously and non-targetedly investigate personal exposure to various families of etiological agents associated with leukemia. Additionally, using glutathione (GSH) conjugated metabolites, including thioproline and thiopronylglycine developed in this study, as biomarkers of exposure may facilitate human risk assessment through a non-invasive approach for indiviaually who are working in environments know to be associated with higher risk of leukemia development.

16301220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301220.value: Prolonged exposure to airborne volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (VOCs/SVOCs), such as formaldehyde, is associated with the development of various human diseases, including lung cancer and leukemia. This study developed four face-mask-based methods to collect and measure exposure to VOCs and SVOCs, which can be used to assess the risk of related diseases. Specifically, we introduced a novel and user-friendly sampling method that involves breathing through face masks to assess personal exposure to a variety of airborne VOCs and SVOCs, including the carcinogenic formaldehyde, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and tobacco-specific nitrosamines such as N′-nitrosonornicotine and 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone, along with a range of common indoor air pollutants. Additionally, given the crucial role of glutathione (GSH) in detoxifying various xenobiotics, including formaldehyde, we rigorously quantified the conjugates formed when formaldehyde reacted with GSH in human cells and urine. This was achieved using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) coupled with an isotope dilution method, with the goal of identifying potential biomarkers of formaldehyde exposure. The results of these studies have been published in international peer-reviewed journals.

16301520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301520.value: In this proposed project, we will study two goodness-of-fit statistics for the spectral distribution of random matrices. They are the Cramer-von Mises statistic and Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, which characterize the distance between the empirical spectral distribution and the limiting one in l^2 and l^infty norm, respectively. Specifically, we aim at deriving the precise limiting behaviour such as the first-order deterministic limit and the second-order fluctuation, for these two statistics. 在這個項目中，我們將研究兩個隨機矩陣譜分布的擬合度統計量. 它們是Cramer-von Mises統計量以及Kolmogorov-Smirnov統計量，分別描述了經驗譜分布和極限譜分布之間的2範數距離和無窮範數距離. 特別地，我們將研究這兩類統計量的一階和二階極限性質.

16301520.label: Realisation of objectives
16301520.value: This project focuses on investigating the limiting behavior of the Cramér-von Mises (CvM) statistic and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic for the empirical spectral distributions of random matrix models. Unlike the classical study of i.i.d. samples from a distribution function, the eigenvalues of random matrices exhibit strong correlations. It is known that, in the bulk, the spectrum behaves somewhat like a log-correlated field. However, the current precision of such approximations remains inadequate for capturing the fine limiting behavior of goodness-of-fit statistics, such as the CvM and KS statistics, making this a theoretically challenging problem. From a practical perspective, while hypothesis testing in the i.i.d. case generally focuses on the limiting distribution of a random variable, goodness-of-fit statistics for spectral distributions enable the evaluation of more general parameters of matrix ensembles, rather than just the limiting spectral distribution. In this project, we explored both the theoretical properties of these statistics and their application to statistical inference problems. First, we derived the limiting distribution of a mesoscopic approximation of the CvM statistic for Wigner matrices, as well as the limiting distribution of the original CvM statistic for the Circular Unitary Ensemble. These limiting distributions are expressed as a series of chi-square random variables, thereby addressing Objective 1. Second, we established a near-optimal order for the KS statistic measuring the distance between the law of the linear spectral statistics and the limiting Gaussian law for Wigner matrices. Additionally, in a separate work, we derived a sharp bound on the KS distance between the spectral distribution of the log-concave ensemble and the limiting Marchenko-Pastur law. These two results jointly address Objective 2. Third, we applied our findings on the KS statistic to a statistical application. Specifically, we developed, for the first time, Neyman-Pearson classifiers for the LDA model without splitting the training sample. In this context, we applied quantitative control over the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the distribution of quadratic forms of sample covariance matrices and the limiting Gaussian laws. This work addresses Objective 3.

16301520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301520.value: We first derived the limiting distribution for the CvM statistic for the spectral distributions of Wigner matrices and the Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE) and found that both limiting distributions are novel. This result was published in the Annals of Applied Probability (2022). Next, we obtained the optimal bound for the KS distance for the distribution of the linear spectral statistics of Wigner matrices as well as the spectral distribution of the log-concave ensemble. Both bounds are nearly optimal. These results were published in the Annals of Applied Probability (2022) and the Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré (2025+), respectively. We then applied a result on the KS distance for the distribution of the quadratic forms of random matrices to Neyman-Pearson classification. This work was published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research (2024). Finally, we established the limiting spectral distribution of sample block correlation matrices and derived the CLT for the linear spectral statistics. This result was published in the Annals of Statistics (2024).

16301520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301520.value: In the work on the KS statistics of the linear spectral statistics of Wigner matrices, we required the test function of the linear spectral statistic to belong to C^5(R). Future work will focus on optimizing the regularity condition of the test function and extending the results to other random matrix models.

16301520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301520.value: In this project, we focused on two goodness-of-fit statistics for various objects in random matrix theory: the Cramér-von Mises (CvM) statistic and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic. We derived the limiting distributions and established tight bounds for these statistics across various random matrix models. Additionally, we applied one of these results to Neyman-Pearson classification. The findings of this project are significant in the fields of Random Matrix Theory, Free Probability Theory, and High-Dimensional Statistics.

16301620.value: 该项目将提出基于修剪的最小二乘估计（LSE）的CUSUM程序以检验与估计重尾G-GARCH噪音线性过程均值中 的单个变点。 在原假设下, 预计将给出检验统计量将依分布收敛到标准布朗运动的函数 。在替代假设下, 该检验统计量的功效将依概率收敛到1。我们将研究变点的修剪LSE的一致, 然后探索其收敛速度。估计的变点预期会依分布收敛到双边随机游动的最大值的位置，并且估计的均值应该是渐近正态的。我们将进一步扩展从单个变点到基于修剪LSE的CUSUM检验与估计带有重尾G-GARCH噪声的线性过程均值中的多个变点, 以及建立他们的极限理论。将进行广泛的模拟研究以评估有限样本中检验与估计程序的性能。这个项目将应用新的理论和方法来分析各种经济和金融数据，特别是那些与香港有关的。我们希望为未来的研究重尾时间序列分析领域开辟新的方向。

16301620.label: Realisation of objectives
16301620.value: To understand the heavy-tailed time series, we first studied the Whittle estimation for vector autoregressive and moving average (ARMA) models with heavy-tailed noises. It is shown that the Whittle estimator is consistent with the rate of convergence $n^{1/alpha}$L(n) and its limiting distribution is a function of two stable random vectors, where L(n) is a slowly varying function and $alpha in (0,2)$ is the tail index of heavy-tailed vector noise. A simulation study is carried out to assess the performance of this estimator in finite samples and a real example is given. We then investigated two test statistics for testing structural changes and thresholds in predictive regression models. The generalized likelihood ratio (GLR) test was proposed for the stationary predictor. Under the null hypothesis of no structural change and threshold, I we showed that the GLR test statistic converges to a function of a centered Gaussian process, and the generalized F test statistic converges to a function of Brownian motions. We next studies the supremum-type score test for the single-index model against a threshold single-index model. It is shown that the test weakly converges a maxima of a Gaussian process under the null hypothesis. The bootstrap method is used to tackle the bias problem and provide the p-values of our test statistic. Simulations are carried out to assess the performance of our procedure and real data examples are given for its illustration. We finally proposed a winsorized CUSUM approach to solve this problem. We begin by investigating the winsorized CUSUM process and deriving the limiting distributions of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and the Self-normalized test under the null hy-pothesis. Our tests are shown to exhibit a power approaching to one for both fixed and local alternatives. Furthermore, we study the winsorized-mean-based least squares estimator (WLSE) for the change point and demonstrate that its limiting distribution is exactly the minimizer of a random walk. Additionally, the LSE of both means before and after change-point are shown to be asymptotically normal. Our framework is quite general and its assumption is very weak. This enables the application of our tests and estimation theory not only to linear time series but also to nonlinear time series, such as TAR and G-GARCH processes. To evaluate the performance of our procedures, we conduct simulation stud- ies and provide two real examples from financial markets. The empirical evidence supports the effectiveness of our proposed procedures for testing and dating change-points in heavy-tailed time series. To explore the possibility of extending our approach to the vector non-stationary heavy-tailed time series and the time functional variance (TFV) noises, we carried out the following research: (1). We then showed that he rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters in vector error correction (VEC) model is n (sample size) and its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when the tail index α ∈ (0, 2). Furthermore, we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n1/α ̃L(n) and its limiting distribution is a functional of two stable processes when α ∈ (1, 2). Simulation study is carried out to demonstrate the performance of both estimators. A real example with application to 3-month Treasury Bill rate, 1-year Treasury Bill rate and Federal Fund rate is given. (2) We next studied the full rank least squares estimator (FLSE) and reduced rank least squares estimator (RLSE) of the heavy-tailed and partially nonstationary ARMA model with the tail index $alpha in (0,2)$. It is shown that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters is $n$ (sample size) and that related to the short-term parameters are $n^{1/alpha} ilde{L}(n)$ and $n$, respectively, when $alpha in (1,2)$ and $ in (0,1)$.Its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when $alpha in (0,2)$ for the long-run parameters and is a functional of some stable processes when $alpha in (1,2)$ for the short-run parameters. Based on FLSE, we derive the asymptotic properties of the RLSE. The finite-sample properties of the estimation are examined through a simulation study and an application to three U.S. interest rate series is given. (3) We studied the autoregressive and moving average (ARMA) model with time functional variance (TFV) noises, called the ARMA-TFV model. We first establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of its least squares estimator (LSE). The Wald tests and portmanteau tests are constructed based on the theory for variable selection and model checking. A simulation study is carried out to assess the performance of our approach in finite samples, and two real examples are given. It should be mentioned that the process generated from the ARMA-TFV model is not stationary, and the technique in this paper is nonstandard and may provide insights for future research in this area.

16301620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301620.value: This project has proposed the trimmed / winsorized-mean-based least squares estimator (WLSE) -based CUSUM tests and estimation procedures for a single change-point in the mean of linear processes with heavy-tailed G-GARCH noises. We have showed that test statistics converge weakly to a functional of standard Brownian motions under the null hypothesis and have a power converging to 1 in probability under the alternative hypothesis. We have studied the consistency of the WLSE of change-point and then explore its rate of convergence. The estimated change-point is shown to converge weakly to the location of maxima of a double-sided random walk and the estimated means are asymptotically normal. We further extended the WLSE-based CUSUM tests and estimation procedures from a single change-point to the multiple change-points in the mean of linear processes with heavy-tailed G-GARCH noises. A novel limiting theory has be developed for testing and estimating multiple change-points under this general setting.

16301720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301720.value: Grain boundaries are interfaces between grains with different orientations in polycrystalline materials, and junctions are meeting points of grain boundaries. Dynamic properties of grain boundaries and triple junctions play essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors of materials. Recent experiments and atomistic simulations have shown that these properties of grain boundaries and triple junctions strongly depend on their underlying microscopic structures, whereas continuum dynamics models that account for these novel microscopic mechanisms are still limited. In this project, we will systematically develop continuum models for the dynamics of grain boundaries and triple junctions incorporating underlying microstructures of line defects (dislocations/disconnections) and the constraints associated them. Recently, the PI and collaborators have developed a continuum model for the motion of low-angle grain boundaries with dislocation structures, in which the long-range elastic interaction is critical to maintain stable dislocation structures on grain boundaries. Despite its success in the incorporation of microscopic mechanism of the coupling effect, calculation of the long-range force is quite time-consuming due to its form of integrals over all the grain boundaries. In this project, we will address this limitation by developing a new continuum dynamics model, in which the long-range driving force in its strong limit will be replaced by constraints that governs the stable, equilibrium dislocation structure during the evolution. We will also develop continuum models of high-angle grain boundaries whose dynamics are controlled by motion of disconnections. The previously developed models by the PI and collaborators focus on the dynamics of individual high-angle grain boundaries or individual triple junctions. However, in polycrystalline materials, the motion of grain boundaries is inevitably constrained by other grains and triple junctions, and this essentially influences the materials properties. We will incorporate these important microscopic constraints to continuum dynamics models of high-angle grain boundaries. We will also develop continuum models for the motion of triple junctions of both low-angle and high-angle grain boundaries incorporating these microscopic constraints. The continuum models will provide a basis for large scale simulations of polycrystalline networks. The obtained continuum grain boundary dynamics models will take the form of systems of evolution equations with constraints due to the microscopic structures, which is a novel class of mathematical models compared with the classical model of motion by mean curvature. We will further develop efficient numerical methods to solve these constrained evolution problems. The obtained continuum models will be validated by comparisons with results of atomistic simulations. 晶界是多晶材料中不同取向晶粒之间的界面，不同晶界的交汇点称为结点。晶界和三结点的动力学性质在材料的机械和塑性行为中起着至关重要的作用。最近的实验和原子模拟表明晶界和三结点的这些性质很大程度上取决于它们微观结构上的线性缺陷（位错/台阶位错），而用来解释这些新颖的微观机制的连续性动力学模型仍很有限。在这个项目中，我们将系统地建立基于线性缺陷(位错/台阶位错)的微观结构和相关约束的晶界和三结点的连续性动力学模型。 在PI和合作者的近期工作中，我们建立了基于位错结构的小角度晶界的连续性动力学模型，其中长程的弹性相互作用在维持晶界上稳定的位错结构起到了关键作用。尽管其成功地融入了耦合效应的微观机制，长程作用力在计算上是通过在整个晶界上的积分得到的，其计算相当耗时。在这个项目中，我们将通过建立一个新的晶界运动的连续模型来解决这个问题，在其演化过程中，长程力由于其强作用可以被控制晶界上稳定的平衡位错结构的约束条件来代替。我们还将建立大角度晶界的连续模型，其动力学是由台阶位错的运动控制的。PI和合作者之前建立的模型集中在单个的大角度晶界或三结点的运动模型。然而，在多晶材料中，晶界的运动不可避免的受到其他晶粒和三结点的约束影响，这会从本质上影响到材料的性能。我们将把这些重要的微观约束包含到大角度晶界运动的连续模型中。同时，我们也将建立包含这些微观约束的小角度和大角度晶界三结点运动的连续模型。这些连续性模型将为建立多晶网络的大规模模拟奠定基础。 这些建立的晶界动力学的连续性模型将采用带有微观结构约束条件的演化方程组形式。相较于经典的平均曲率运动，这是一类新型的数学模型。我们将进一步建立有效的数值方法来解决这类受约束的演化问题，并将得到的连续模型对比原子模拟结果来进行验证。

16301720.label: Realisation of objectives
16301720.value: For the first objective, (i) We have developed a new continuum model for the coupling and sliding motions of grain boundaries that avoids the time-consuming calculation of the long-range elastic interaction. In this model, the long-range elastic interaction is replaced by a constraint of Frank's formula. The constrained evolution problem in our new continuum model is further solved by using the projection method. Effects of the coupling and sliding motions in our new continuum model and relationship with the classical motion by curvature model are discussed. The continuum model is validated by comparisons with discrete dislocation dynamics model and the early continuum model [L. Zhang and Y. Xiang, J. Mech. Phys. Solids, 117 (2018), pp. 157-178] in which the long-range dislocation interaction is explicitly calculated. These results are summarized in [1]. (ii) We develop a continuum model for the dynamics of grain boundaries in three dimensions that incorporates the motion and reaction of the constituent dislocations. The continuum model is based on a simple representation of densities of curved dislocations on the grain boundary. Illposedness due to nonconvexity of the total energy is fixed by a numerical treatment based on a projection method that maintains the connectivity of the constituent dislocations. An efficient simulation method is developed, in which the critical but computationally expensive long-range interaction of dislocations is replaced by another projection formulation that maintains the constraint of equilibrium of the dislocation structure described by the Frank's formula. This continuum model is able to describe the grain boundary motion and grain rotation due to both coupling and sliding effects, to which the classical motion by mean curvature model does not apply. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions of evolutions of low angle grain boundaries and their dislocation structures. These results are summarized in [2]. (iii) We have developed a continuum model to determine the dislocation structure and energy of low angle grain boundaries in three dimensions. The equilibrium dislocation structure is obtained by minimizing the grain boundary energy that is associated with the constituent dislocations subject to the constraint of Frank's formula. The energy of a grain boundary is the total energy of the constituent dislocations derived from discrete dislocation dynamics model, incorporating both the dislocation line energy and reactions of dislocations. The constrained energy minimization problem is solved by the augmented Lagrangian method and projection method. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions of the energy and dislocation densities of both planar and curved low angle grain boundaries. These results are summarized in [3]. We have also proposed a convergent ADMM algorithm for this constrained grain boundary energy minimization process [4]. Different continuum models have been developed by upscaling from discrete line defect dynamics models under different settings (dislocations or disconnections, low angle grain boundaries or high angle grain boundaries, etc.), to account for the specific detailed natures of the microscopic dynamics mechanisms observed in experiments and atomistic simulations, but these continuum models are not in the variational form. We have proposed a unified variational framework to account for all the underlying line defect mechanisms for the dynamics of both low and high angle grain boundaries and the associated grain rotations. The variational formulation is based on the developed constraints of the dynamic Frank-Bilby equations that govern the microscopic line defect structures. The proposed variational framework is able to recover the available models for different motions under different conditions. The unified variational framework is more efficient to describe the collective behaviors of grain boundary networks at larger length scales. It also provides a mathematically tractable basis for rigorous analysis of these partial differential equation models and for the development of efficient numerical methods. These results are summarized in [5]. For the second objective, we have presented continuum equations of motion for grain boundaries that are based upon the underlying disconnection dynamics and accounts for the mechanical constraint in polycrystals. This leads to a reduced-order (zero-shear constrained) model for GB motion that is easily implemented in a computationally efficient framework, appropriate for the large-scale simulation of the evolution of polycrystalline microstructures. These results are summarized in [6]. As described in the realization of the first objective, we have proposed a unified variational framework to account for all the underlying line defect mechanisms (dislocations or disconnections) for the dynamics of both low and high angle grain boundaries and the associated grain rotations. The variational formulation is based on the developed constraints of the dynamic Frank-Bilby equations that govern the microscopic line defect structures. The proposed variational framework is able to recover the available models for different motions under different conditions. These results are summarized in [5]. Nanoscopic cross-grain cation homogenization mechanism in Perovskite solar cells has been discussed and the role played by triple junctions has been identified in [7]. The background is that although multiscale cation inhomogeneity has been a major hurdle in state-of-the-art formamidinium-cesium (FA-Cs) mixed-cation perovskites for achieving perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with optimal power conversion efficiencies and durability, the understanding and tailoring of grain-to-grain cation inhomogeneity remains elusive. We revealed that the grooves at the grain triple-junction geometrically create nanoscale trap-like morphologies onto the perovskite film surface, detrimentally influence the solid-state cation exchange between adjacent grains. For the third and fourth objective, the reduced-order dynamic model obtained in [6] provides a leading order approximation for the interaction between grain boundaries and triple junctions in a polycystalline network. Grain boundary dynamics are largely controlled by the formation and motion of disconnections (with step and dislocation characters) along with the grain boundary. The dislocation character gives rise to shear coupling; i.e. the relative tangential motion of two grains meeting at the grain boundary during grain boundary migration. In a polycrystal, the shear coupling is constrained by the presence of other grains and grain boundary junctions, which prevents large-scale sliding of one grain relative to the other. Our continuum model of motion for grain boundaries is based upon the underlying disconnection dynamics and accounts for this mechanical constraint in polycrystals. As already described in the realization of the second objective, the reduced-order model for grain boundary motion is easily implemented in a computationally efficient framework, appropriate for the large-scale simulation of the evolution of polycrystalline microstructures. We validated the proposed reduced order model with direct comparisons to full multi-disconnection mode simulations. A continuum model for grain rotation and translation in polycrystals has been developed [8], in which dislocation reactions at the triple junctions are incorporated and the associated dynamics of triple junctions is established.

16301720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301720.value: Grain boundaries are interfaces between grains with different orientations in polycrystalline materials, and junctions are meeting points of grain boundaries. Dynamic properties of grain boundaries and triple junctions play essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors of materials. Recent experiments and atomistic simulations have shown that these properties of grain boundaries and triple junctions strongly depend on their underlying microscopic structures, whereas continuum dynamics models that account for these novel microscopic mechanisms are still limited. In this project, we have systematically developed continuum models for the dynamics of grain boundaries and triple junctions incorporating underlying microstructures of line defects (dislocations/disconnections) and the constraints associated them. We have developed a new continuum model for the motion of low-angle grain boundaries that addresses the limitation of time-consuming calculation in our previously continuum model, in which the long-range driving force in its strong limit will be replaced by constraints that governs the stable, equilibrium dislocation structure during the evolution. We have further developed continuum models for the dynamics incorporating the motion and reaction of the constituent dislocations and equilibrium dislocation structure and energy of grain boundaries in three dimensions. We have presented continuum equations of motion for high-angle grain boundaries that are based upon the underlying disconnection dynamics and accounts for the mechanical constraint due to triple junctions and other grains in polycrystals. This leads to a reduced-order (zero-shear constrained) model for GB motion that is easily implemented in a computationally efficient framework, appropriate for the large-scale simulation of the evolution of polycrystalline microstructures. We have also proposed a unified variational framework to account for all the underlying line defect mechanisms for the dynamics of both low and high angle grain boundaries and the associated grain rotations. The variational formulation is based on the developed constraints of the dynamic Frank-Bilby equations that govern the microscopic line defect structures. The proposed variational framework is able to recover the available models for different motions under different conditions. The unified variational framework is more efficient to describe the collective behaviors of grain boundary networks at larger length scales. It also provides a mathematically tractable basis for rigorous analysis of these partial differential equation models and for the development of efficient numerical methods. All the obtained continuum models have been validated by numerical simulations and comparisons with results of experiments and atomistic simulations.

16301720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301720.value: The obtained continuum grain boundary dynamics models take the form of systems of evolution equations with constraints due to the microscopic structures, which is a novel class of mathematical models compared with the classical model of motion by mean curvature. Further research can be conducted to develop efficient numerical methods to solve these constrained evolution problems and to analysis the solution properties of these PDE systems. This project is a theoretical study of grain boundary dynamics which plays essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors in polycrystalline materials. The obtained models and numerical simulation results will provide theoretical guidance to the usage and designs of polycrystalline materials.

16301720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301720.value: Dynamic properties of grain boundaries and triple junctions play essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors of crystalline materials. Traditional continuum grain boundary dynamics models are not able to account for the novel microscopic mechanisms associated with the recent development of advanced materials. In this project, we have systematically developed continuum models for the dynamics of grain boundaries and triple junctions incorporating underlying microstructures of line defects (dislocations/disconnections). Specifically, we have developed new continuum models for the motion of low-angle grain boundaries that address the limitation of time-consuming calculation in the available continuum models; we have developed continuum models for the dynamics of high-angle grain boundaries based on the underlying disconnection mechanism, incorporating the microscopic constraints of grain boundary triple junctions and other grains and enabling large-scale simulations of the evolution of polycrystalline microstructures; we have also proposed a unified variational framework to account for all the underlying line defect mechanisms for the dynamics of grain boundaries and the associated grain rotations. Further research can be conducted to develop efficient numerical methods to solve these constrained evolution problems and to analysis the solution properties of these PDE systems, and to provide guidance of the design of advanced materials.
