16301820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301820.value: 二維（2D）Kagome晶格是吸引人的系統，因為當相鄰位置反鐵磁耦合時，它們的高度复杂性可以容納奇異的磁相。在這種情況下可能會出現量子自旋液體（QSL）態。金屬有機骨架（MOF）已顯示出豐富的磁性。特別是2D Kagome MOF（2D-KMOF）為觀察奇異的磁相（例如QSL）提供了巨大的機會。在擬議的研究中，我們將通過表面配位自組裝製造2D-KMOF，並使用表面敏感技術研究其磁序。我們將在原子平坦的金屬表面上共沉積過渡金屬原子（Cu，Fe，Ni，Co，Mn等）和特定選擇的有機連接分子。為了增強跨網絡的磁耦合，我們將使用官能化的分子牢固地結合金屬中心，從而促進高效的超交換耦合。這些2D-KMOF的結構將使用掃描隧道顯微鏡和非接觸式原子力顯微鏡以原子分辨率解析。我們還將使用各種掃描隧道光譜技術，包括自旋翻轉激發，近藤共振和自旋極化隧道光譜，研究單個金屬中心的磁性能。 Co-IThomas Jung教授將在瑞士光源處使用X射線磁性圓二色性（XMCD）來探測2D-KMOF的整體磁階。我們將與兩個理論小組合作，使用密度泛函理論研究2D-KMOF的自旋極化帶結構和磁性基態。我們相信PI在合成2D金屬有機結構方面的豐富經驗，Co-I在XMCD方面的專業知識以及我們與理論小組的密切合作將為研究奇異的2D磁性提供一個強大的平台。

16301820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301820.value: We employ on-surface synthesis to grow single-layer two-dimensional (2D) cMOFs of M3(HAT)2 and M3(BHO)2, (M= Ni, Fe, Co). Using scanning tunneling microscopy and density-functional theory analysis, we resolve that the frameworks comprise a hexagonal lattice of HAT/BHO molecules and a Kagome lattice of metal atoms. The DFT analyses show that Ni, Co and Fe carry a magnetic moment of 1.1, 2.5, and 3.7 mB, respectively. We anticipate that the small π-conjugated core of HAT/BHO molecules and strong bidentate chelating coordination render appealing electronic and magnetic properties. We synthesize a two-dimensional Fe-coordinated bimolecular metal-organic framework which constitutes a honeycomb lattice of 1,4,5,8,9,12-hexaazatriphenylene molecules and a Kagome lattice of 5,15-di(4-pyridyl)-10,20-diphenylporphyrin molecules on a Au(111) substrate. Density-functional theory calculations show that the framework features multiple well-separated spin-polarized Kagome bands, namely Dirac cone bands and Chern flat bands, near the Fermi level. This study demonstrates that p-orbital Kagome bands can be realized in metal-organic frameworks by using molecules with molecular orbitals of p-orbital like symmetry. We study the magnetic properties of Fe3(BHO)2 Kagome framework using scanning tunneling microscopy, non-contact atomic force microscope (nc-AFM), X-ray magnetic circular dichroism and theoretical Monte Carlo calculations. The iron magnetic moments measured as a function of temperature and applied magnetic field in conjunction with the Kagome topology indicate the presence of magnetic frustration in this true 2D KAFM monolayer. This opens a path for further studies of magnetic frustration and spin liquid behavior in 2D materials. We examine the spin excitations of the Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu atoms using inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy. For Fe, Co, and Ni atoms, the dI/dV spectra show a symmetric double step feature near the Fermi level, while the spectra of Cu atoms show no features. We assign the double step like features to spin excitations instead of molecular vibrational excitation. DFT calculations show that the double step features in the spin 1/2 Ni system cannot be explained by MAE induced splitting. We exclude the spin excitations in M₃(HAT)₂ (M = Fe, Co, Ni) are due to the MAE and attribute them to magnon excitation.

16301820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301820.value: We used XMCD to study Fe3(BHO)2 Kagome framework in which Fe is at S=2 state. This system is a classical 2D magnetic system. The next step is to study quantum 2D magnetic systems with S=1/2. Two of the Kagome frameworks we have synthesized are candidate systems, Ni3(BHO)2 and Ni3(HAT)2. It would be highly interesting in future to conduct XMCD measurements on these two systems. Recently, electron spin resonance ( ESR) STM has been demonstrated to be a powerful tool to resolve spin properties with super high energy resolution. We propose to use SER STM to characterize the Kagome frameworks to reveal the spin textures of these novel quantum systems. The third future direction is to synthesize the Kagome frameworks on inert substrates such as graphite/graphene and TMDCs. In doing so, the Kagome frameworks can be effectively decoupled form the substrate screening.

16301820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301820.value: This project has demonstrated that the reticular design principle in metal-organic frameworks offers rich opportunities for synthesis of Kagome frameworks that exhibit exciting quantum spin properties. The in-depth investigations on these frameworks shed lights on the fundamental quantum physics as well as potential technology applications in quantum technologies, such as quantum information and quantum manipulation.

16302020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302020.value: Networks permeate every corner of our lives. Examples include protein interaction networks, metabolic networks, species food webs, word-document networks, and scientific publication networks. Moreover, the recent prevalence of social media, such as Twitter and Facebook, has introduced a large volume of interesting and under-explored network data. Network has been studied from different perspectives, including community detection. A useful tool to study network is the spectral method. While there are numerous studies about the single static network, researchers have show increasing interest in the study of the multi-layer network which is a more powerful representation of relational data. In most applications networks may be time dependent or may have multiple types of edges relating the nodes. Recently, multi-layer networks that incorporate multiple channels of connectivity have been introduced to represent such complex systems. An effective tool to study multi-layer temporal networks is via tensor decompositions. There are two main approaches: canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition and Tucker decomposition. There has been an increasing literature on using tensor approaches to study various practical problems. In this proposal, we will explore how to utilise tensor in solving various complex problems, and investigate their theoretical properties. 网络渗透到我们生活的每个角落，包括蛋白质相互作用网络，代谢网络，物种食物网，文字文档网络和科学出版网络。此外，社交媒体（例如Twitter和Facebook）也引入大量有趣但尚未开发的网络数据。人们过去从不同角度对网络进行了各方面研究，包括社区检测。其中频谱方法是研究网络的一个有用工具。过去已有很多关于单个静态网络的研究，目前研究人员对多层网络的研究越来越感兴趣，因为多层网络在关系数据中有更强大的表示。另外在大多数应用中，网络可能是时间紧密相关的，又或者可能具有与节点相关的多种类型的边缘。最近，引入了包含多个连接通道的多层网络来代表这样的复杂系统。需要指出的是，张量分解是研究多层时态网络的非常有效工具。主要有两种方法：规范多Adadic（CP）分解和Tucker分解。关于使用张量方法研究各种实际问题的文献越来越多。我们希望在本项目中将探讨如何利用张量来解决各种复杂问题，并研究其理论特性。

16302020.label: Realisation of objectives
16302020.value: The principal investigators, originally Prof. Bing-Yi Jing and later transferred to Prof. Dong Xia, have completed several papers realizing the proposed objectives of the project. Among these, one has been published in the Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, one is under major revision at the Journal of the American Statistical Association, one is under revision at the Journal of Machine Learning Research, one is to be submitted to the Journal of the American Statistical Association, and one is to be submitted to Biometrika. In the paper titled "Collaborative Filtering With Awareness of Social Networks," the original PI, Prof. Bing-Yi Jing, studied two network-related matrices: one encoding the partially observed preference matrix between users and items, and the other describing the relationships among users. The data can be viewed as a special case of a two-layer network. The authors formulate convex optimization problems that incorporate assumptions regarding users’ social connections and product preferences. They provide an algorithm to solve the new optimization problem and prove that it is guaranteed to find a global optimum. Their theory demonstrates that the combination of the network-related term and the previously used nuclear norm term yields estimates that outperform those achieved by either term alone. Additionally, they applied their algorithm to predict users’ reviews on Yelp.com, specifically aiming to predict users' ratings of restaurants by leveraging the user friendship network. Their results show that incorporating social network information can indeed improve the predictive accuracy of user-item ratings, and their method outperforms existing approaches that utilize only the user-item preference matrix. The paper has been published in the Journal of Business & Economic Statistics in 2022. In the paper titled "Consensus Knowledge Graph Learning via Multi-view Sparse Low-rank Block Model," the later PI, Prof. Dong Xia, studied a multi-view low-rank block model to learn an unknown consensus graph using data collected from multiple sources. The data matrix from each source represents a knowledge graph, where each vertex corresponds to a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code extracted from an electronic health record (EHR) system. The data can be conveniently formulated as a third-order tensor. A significant practical challenge arises from severe heterogeneity across multiple sources. The PI and his collaborators proposed a multi-view low-rank block model that accommodates a common graph structure shared by all sources, as well as heterogeneous noise and source-dependent local discrepancies. They developed an estimation procedure involving convex optimization for initialization, alternating minimization for simultaneous low-rank and sparse matrix decomposition, and K-means clustering for grouping the CPT codes. Their theory demonstrates that increasing the number of data sources indeed improves the estimation accuracy of the underlying consensus graph. Their method was applied to learn the clinical concept knowledge graph of Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs) using the MIMIC, Biobank, and Standard datasets. The results demonstrate that the achieved accuracy outperforms existing methods. The paper was revised and is currently under review in the Journal of Machine Learning Research. In the paper titled "Optimal Clustering of Discrete Mixtures: Binomial, Poisson, Block Models, and Multi-layer Networks," the later PI, Prof. Dong Xia, proposed a new tensor-based algorithm for layer clustering in multi-layer networks and investigated the minimax optimality of the misclustering error rate. The Mixture Multi-layer Stochastic Block Model (MMSBM) was previously introduced by the PI and his collaborators to study multi-layer networks that accommodate heterogeneous community structures across layers. In this model, a tensor-factorization-based approach was shown to consistently recover community assignments and layer clusters under mild conditions. However, the minimax optimal clustering error rate remained unknown. In this paper, the PI and his collaborators proposed a two-step algorithm, including tensor-based initialization and a leave-one-out-type refinement procedure. Their theory demonstrates that the proposed algorithm achieves the minimax optimal clustering error rate, which decays exponentially with respect to the Rényi distance between Bernoulli distributions. They discovered that the same type of minimax optimal rate holds for a wide range of mixture models of discrete distributions, such as Poisson and Binomial. They applied their algorithm to several real-world datasets, including the worldwide food trading network and brain connectivity networks, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods. The PI submitted the paper to the Annals of Statistics in 2024, but it was unfortunately rejected. The PI is currently preparing a revision of the manuscript and plans to submit it to the Journal of the American Statistical Association. In the paper titled "Higher-order Accurate Two-Sample Network Inference and Network Hashing," the later PI, Prof. Dong Xia, and his collaborators investigated a higher-order accurate method for two-sample network inference. Two-sample hypothesis testing for network comparison presents many significant challenges, including leveraging repeated network observations and known node registration, achieving finite-sample higher-order accuracy, handling different network sizes and sparsity levels, ensuring fast computation and memory efficiency, controlling the false discovery rate (FDR) in multiple testing, and developing theoretical understandings, particularly regarding finite-sample accuracy and minimax optimality. In this paper, they developed a comprehensive toolbox featuring a novel main method and its variants, all accompanied by strong theoretical guarantees, to address these challenges. Their method outperformed existing tools in both speed and accuracy and was proven to be power-optimal. The algorithms are user-friendly and versatile, capable of handling various data structures, including single or repeated network observations and known or unknown node registrations. Additionally, they developed an innovative framework for offline hashing and fast querying, which serves as a highly useful tool for large network databases. The effectiveness of their method is showcased through comprehensive simulations and applications to two real-world datasets, which revealed intriguing new structures. One particularly interesting application of their method involves multiple observations of networks, a special case of multi-layer networks. The PI and collaborators have made substantial efforts in revising the manuscript, and it is currently under major revision at the Journal of the American Statistical Association. In the paper titled "Conformalized Link Prediction with False Discovery Rate Control," the later PI, Prof. Dong Xia, and his collaborators proposed a novel approach to control the false discovery rate (FDR) in predicting missing links within networks. Predicting multiple missing links in partially observed networks is vital across diverse fields. However, controlling the FDR in such predictions is challenging due to complex dependencies among test statistics. They introduce a Conformalized Link Prediction (CLP) method based on the graphon model that effectively controls the FDR, accommodates inhomogeneous missing patterns, and handles unknown missing mechanisms. CLP constructs conformal p-values row-wise by leveraging the graphon model's exchangeability property and employs a kernel smoothing method to enhance link prediction. Utilizing e-values, they demonstrate that the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure successfully controls the FDR. Compared to existing methods, CLP accommodates both binary and weighted networks, provides theoretical guarantees for FDR control, and does not require knowledge of the missing mechanism. The advantages of CLP are further validated through simulations and real data studies. The manuscript is nearly completed and will be submitted to Biometrika.

16302020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302020.value: The major finds are as follows. 1. Tensor-based methods are computationally effective for leveraging information from multiple resources. This is particularly true in the consensus graph learning project, where electronic health record (EHR) data are collected from multiple hospitals. In this context, the knowledge graph from each source can be represented as a matrix, and tensors provide a convenient approach to analyze multi-view data collectively. Similarly, in the multi-layer network project, the tensor-based factorization approach can immediately provide a robust initial clustering, significantly facilitating downstream tasks such as layer clustering and community detection. For instance, our tensor-based method achieves considerably higher accuracy in clustering brain connectivity networks. 2. We investigated the theoretical properties of tensor-based methods for network analysis. Under certain conditions, we were able to prove that tensor-based methods indeed deliver better theoretical guarantees than methods that do not leverage information from multiple sources. For instance, in the consensus graph learning project, we showed that the accuracy of the estimated consensus graph increases when more views of the data are presented; in the multi-layer network analysis project, we proved that tensor-based methods can handle sparser networks as more network layers become available; and in the higher-order accurate network testing project, we demonstrated that our test statistic becomes more powerful when more network views are used for comparison.

16302020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302020.value: Tensor-based approaches offer both computational and theoretical benefits in network analysis and multi-view data analysis. However, there is a fundamental drawback to tensor-based methods. To convert matrix-valued data into a tensor format, the matrices must be well-aligned and of equal size. For instance, in multi-layer networks, the nodes in different layers must have a one-to-one correspondence so that the dimensions of the adjacency matrices are properly aligned. However, in many applications, there is no information about whether and how nodes correspond across layers. In multi-view data analysis, the underlying matrices from each source must have equal dimensions. Yet, in some applications, the entities of interest differ across data sources. These issues pose significant challenges to the application of tensor-based methods. Further development includes developing tensor-based methods for analyzing multi-view or multi-source data with unequal or unaligned dimensions. To achieve this goal, we need to relax the tensor structure to accommodate different dimensions across all modes. The PI believes that tensor networks are a promising direction, but extensive work is required.

16302020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302020.value: A tensor is a multi-dimensional array. For instance, a vector is a first-order tensor, and a matrix is a second-order tensor. The revolution in data technology over the recent decade has made tensor-formatted data widely available in many applications, especially when data are collected from multiple sources and domains. Tensor-based approaches can leverage information from multiple domains to provide more accurate estimations and predictions than methods that use single-source data. In this project, the PI investigates tensor-based approaches for network analysis, demonstrating that these methods offer both theoretical and practical benefits in analyzing multi-layer networks.

16302120.label: Realisation of objectives
16302120.value: The project has fully achieved its three objectives. The following are the specific methodology and experiments to realize the project goals. 1. Develop a down-conversion medium capable of converting the blue emission from micro-LEDs to green and red emissions for microdisplay applications. The down-conversion medium will be based on an evaporable thin organic film with a host-dopant composition that can be patterned by a shadow-masking method. For the first objective, we utilized the blue-light absorbing characteristic of perylene and developed a perylene-based material, DMP, as the host. Steric substitutions, namely 2,6-dimethylphenyl groups, were introduced to the 3,9 and 3,10 positions of DMP’s perylene core to prevent intermolecular aggregation and concentration quenching. The ortho-positioned methyl groups force the phenyl to be almost perpendicular (89 degrees) to the perylene core. Compared to perylene hosts without steric groups, the DMP film exhibited an extremely small Stokes shift of only 5 nm and significantly reduced excimer emission, an indicator of π-π stacking. DMP also showed exceptional absorption coefficients of up to 1.9×10^5 cm^-1 in blue wavelengths, an order of magnitude higher than that of colloidal quantum dots. A DMP film of only 500 nm can absorb more than 99.9% blue light between 450 and 460 nm, squarely overlapping with typical blue micro-LED emissions. To realize the red and green emissions from the conversion of the blue light, DMQA and DBP are selected as the green and red dopants for the down-conversion film or color-conversion media (CCM) as Publication 1. The small Stokes shift of DMP provides it with sufficient excited state energy to sensitize the green dopant, while its reduced but not eliminated yellow excimer emission facilitates the energy transfer to the red dopant. The resulting green and red CCM films exhibited PLQY of 44% and 58%, respectively. Using an ultrathin silicon nitride mask (SiNx) as the shadow mask, green and red CCM arrays of up to 2000 ppi have been fabricated by thermal evaporation, demonstrating the utility of organic down-conversion materials in ultrahigh-resolution displays. 2. Develop perylene-based host materials with strong blue light absorption to match the micro-LED emission and allow efficient energy transfer to the luminescent dopants for green and red emissions. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons like perylene typically have distinct, narrow absorption bands with sharp band edges. As a result, the absorption of the DMP film at the long wavelength end of the blue LED is relatively weak, with a light transmission of higher than 50% beyond 475 nm, leading to incomplete light absorption and color mixing. To ensure strong absorption over the entire blue region without sacrificing DMP’s capability to sensitize green and red dopants, we adopted a mixed host strategy and used a perylene-based host, BPP, with absorption bands complementary to DMP's. BPP has a biphenyl group attached to the perylene core through ortho linkage on the 3,9 and 3,10 positions and slightly red-shifted absorption peaks that can fill the valleys between DMP’s bands. The DMP-BPP film with optimized co-host ratio (DMP:BPP, 5:1) achieved a remarkable 2.2× 10^5 cm^-1 absorption coefficient at 464 nm and can realize less than 1% blue light transmission from 405 nm to 475 nm with a 500 nm film, covering the entire blue LED emissions. In comparison, a 500 nm DMP film’s 1% transmission range is only from 416 nm to 466 nm. The co-host film also maintained a small Stokes shift that is critical for blue-to-green conversion and a yellow excimer emission peak that can efficiently sensitize a red dopant. PLQY of 44% and 80% are realized for green and red color-conversion films, respectively, using DMQA and DBP as the dopant. 3. Establish the correlation between the molecular structures of perylene-based host materials and their absorption coefficients in thin-film forms. Based on the results of the first and second objectives, we further designed, synthesized, and characterized a dozen more perylene-based hosts with strategically varied substitutions to establish structure-property correlations. Specifically, we introduced tolyl, naphthyl, and dibenzothiophene groups of different steric hindrance by varying the linking position. Larger steric hindrance increases the dihedral angle between the peripheral substitution and the perylene core and reduces π-π stacking in thin films, resulting in suppressed excimer emission and smaller Stokes shifts beneficial for blue-to-green conversion. Meanwhile, hosts with smaller steric hindrances show less resolved absorption bands and increased yellow excimer emission, which can facilitate blue-to-red conversion. The host’s absorption coefficients are proportional to the perylene ratio in the molecule with steric hindrance of secondary effect. In general, a smaller substitution on the perylene (more perylene content in the molecule) will yield larger absorption coefficients in blue, while a higher degree of planarity of the host can also slightly increase the absorption coefficients by increasing the thin film’s packing density. Co-host combinations with an optimized composition can increase the peak absorption coefficient by as much as 20% and broaden absorption bands without sacrificing PLQY. Blue absorption coefficients of more than 2.0×10^5 cm^-1 are readily achievable across the entire blue light wavelengths with optimized molecular structures.

16302120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302120.value: 1. Perylene-based organic light-emitting materials are efficient down-conversion media for micro-LED displays. Their primary advantage over inorganic materials like quantum dots is their high blue light absorption, which can significantly reduce the film thickness required to absorb and convert the blue LED emission. By utilizing perylene as the chromophore for the host material, we achieved a peak blue absorption coefficient of 1.9×10^5 cm^-1 in thin films and less than 0.1% blue light transmission with a 500 nm thickness, only one-tenth of that of quantum dot films. The result was published in Publication 1 and presented in Conference Paper 1. 2. Perylene-based down-conversion materials with steric substitutions exhibit small Stokes shifts and reduced excimer formation in thin films. They can efficiently sensitize both green and red dopants with narrow emission bands. PLQYs of up to 44% and 80% are achieved for the green and red down-conversion films, respectively. Steric hindrance is particularly beneficial for the efficient energy transfer from the perylene host to the green dopant. 3. A mixed-host strategy using perylene materials of complimentary absorption peaks can further increase the absorption coefficients and broaden the absorption spectrum without reducing the PLQY for green and red conversion. By adopting an optimized two-host composition, the wavelength range of strong blue absorption was extended by 20 nm, achieving 1% blue light transmission between 405 nm to 475 nm with a 500 nm film and covering the entire blue LED emissions. The result was presented in Conference Paper 2. 4. The organic down-conversion materials are readily evaporable and can be patterned by vacuum evaporation through a high-resolution shadow mask. Using an ultrathin silicon nitride mask, green and red down-conversion pixel arrays of 2000 pixels per inch (PPI) have been realized, demonstrating the utility of organic down-conversion materials in high-resolution displays for VR/AR applications. The patterning process and results were presented in Conference papers 1 and 2.

16302120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302120.value: 1. The PLQY of green organic down-conversion films is relatively low, mostly due to the limitations of the green dopant DMQA. Green emitters with higher efficiency and better color purity need to be developed. We will explore multi-resonance emitters with reduced tendency of concentration quenching and further narrowed PL spectra. 2. The integration of organic down-conversion films on an active-matrix micro-LED or micro-OLED display needs to be further developed. The sapphire top surface of a flip-chip micro-LED pixel can lead to an undesired waveguide of converted light and cause efficiency loss and pixel crosstalk. It is necessary to develop anti-reflection stacks on the micro-LED chips and engineer a microcavity structure in the organic down-conversion film to facilitate the outcoupling of the converted light. 3. Nanoparticle-based down-conversion materials, such as QDs and perovskites, still have relatively higher PLQY and better photostability than organics despite their low blue absorption. To combine the advantages of both classes, we will develop a hybrid down-conversion film comprising perylene-based organic emitters and colloidal QD/perovskite nanoparticles and solution processes, such as inkjet printing, for patterning these hybrid films.

16302120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302120.value: Color conversion is a promising method for realizing full-color micro-LED displays by using down-conversion films to absorb the blue emission from a monolithic blue micro-LED pixels array and down-converting it to red and green light. The organic down conversion materials developed in this project overcome the thickness and resolution limitations of conventional quantum dots and phosphors by utilizing perylene, an aromatic moiety that exhibits exceptional blue light absorption capabilities. The perylene-cored materials with optimized structures can achieve a peak blue-light absorption of over 99.9% with a mere 500 nm thickness, one-tenth of that using quantum dots. By introducing steric substitutions to the perylene core to prevent concentration quenching, these materials function as efficient hosts for sensitizing green and red dopants of narrow emissions and realized PLQY of 44% and 80%, respectively, for green and red emission of down-conversion films of host-dopant compositions. Down-conversion pixel arrays of 2000 ppi have been fabricated by thermal evaporation of the perylene-based materials through an ultrafine silicon nitride mask, demonstrating that the organic down-conversion technology can enable ultrahigh-resolution, full-color micro-LED displays for VR/AR applications.

16302220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302220.value: As one of the most important ambient pollutants, aerosols can exert adverse effects on air quality, visibility, and human health. From the aspect of climate, aerosols can absorb, scatter, or reflect sunlight depending on their composition and color. In general, nonlight absorbing aerosols (e.g., sulfate and nitrate) tend to reflect solar radiation into space, whereas dark-colored aerosols (e.g., black carbon) absorb large amounts of light. These two types of aerosols have opposite climatic effects; that is, the reflection of solar radiation can cool the atmosphere, whereas the absorption of light can warm the atmosphere. Most organic aerosols (OAs) are classified as light-colored aerosols and considered as purely scattering in most climate models. However, OAs contain large amounts of brown carbon (BrC), which has a strong light absorption capability instead of merely scattering light. BrC is mainly contributed by incomplete combustion processes, such as open biomass burning and residential biofuel use. The quantification of the BrC effect by using a numerical model remains uncertain because of the great variability of optical properties and BrC sources. When BrC is exposed to sunlight, photobleaching effect can degrade its light absorption capability. Few modeling studies have considered this effect in their simulations. To better quantify the effect of BrC heated by the absorbed solar radiation on regional pollutant distributions, we propose to parameterize BrC into a Weather Research Forecast (WRF)-Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System (CMAQ), which is a two-way coupled model based on recent experimental studies. A novel BrC basis set (BCBS) framework is also proposed in this work. This framework considers how the light absorption property of BrC varies with the emission condition (BC/OA ratio) and the length of sunlight exposure. Southern China is heavily influenced by biomass burning, and no regional BrC simulation has been performed in this region. Hence, a whole-year simulation (12 km resolution) will be carried out with the BCBS framework to carefully investigate the effects of BrC on O3 concentration, radical budget, solar radiation and other meteorological variables (e.g., temperature and precipitation) in different months. From the perspective of BrC, the impacts of recent 20-year variations in biomass burning on meteorological factors, ozone concentration, and HOx budget will also be investigated. Upon completion of the project, the impacts of BrC on climate and air quality will be thoroughly understood. 大氣中的棕碳對氣象要素和臭氧濃度的影響 作為最重要的環境污染物之一，氣溶膠對空氣質量、大氣能見度和人體健康能夠造成負面的影響。從氣候的角度來看，氣溶膠根據其組成和顏色，可以吸收、散射或者反射太陽短波輻射。通常，淺色的氣溶膠（例如硫酸鹽和硝酸鹽）能夠將太陽輻射反射回太空；而深色的氣溶膠（例如黑碳）則能夠吸收大量的短波輻射。這兩類氣溶膠具有相反的氣候影響：太陽輻射的反射可以使大氣降溫，而太陽輻射的吸收可以使大氣變暖。 在大多數的氣候模型中，有機氣溶膠被統一歸類為僅有散射效應的淺色氣溶膠。然而，近期的研究表明，有機氣溶膠中包含大量具有很強吸光能力的棕碳。棕碳主要由生物質燃燒和居民生物燃料的使用而形成的。由於棕碳的光學性質和來源存在巨大差異，目前通過數值模型對棕碳效應進行量化的研究仍存在很大的不確定性。另一方面，由陽光導致的漂白效應會降低棕碳對光的吸收能力，然而很少研究在模式中考慮這種影響。 為了更好地量化棕碳吸收太陽輻射而產生的加熱效應對區域污染物分佈的影響，我們將基於最近的實驗研究結果，將棕碳效應參數化後移植進 WRF-CMAQ雙向耦合模型中。在本研究中，我們提出了一個新的棕碳參數化框架 (BCBS)，該框架能夠有效考慮棕碳基於排放條件（棕色碳/有機碳比）和日光照射時間的光吸收特性。華南地區受到生物質燃燒的嚴重影響，目前為止，尚未有相關研究對該地區進行棕碳效應的模擬。因此，我們將使用更新了BCBS框架的 WRF-CMAQ 雙向耦合模型進行全年模擬（水平分辨率為 12 km），研究棕碳對不同月份的太陽輻射和其他氣象參數（例如溫度和降水）的影響。由於太陽輻射的變化會進而改變大氣中臭氧和氫氧自由基的濃度和收支，因此，本項目也將研究棕碳對這兩者區域濃度的影響。

16302220.label: Realisation of objectives
16302220.value: A parameterization scheme of the light absorption property of brown carbon (BrC) based on the observational research has been parameterized into the Weather Research Forecast-Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System (WRF-CMAQ) two-way coupled modeling system to investigate the impact of BrC direct radiative effect (DRE) over Southeast Asia (including southern China). The study investigates how BrC influences solar radiation, temperature, and ozone levels in southern China, utilizing an updated model with a spatial resolution of 12 km. The comparison between the BC DRE and BrC DRE has been investigated. This work does not have the BrC daytime aging (photo-bleaching) module implanted as originally intended. The calculation of BrC aging requires the concentration of BrC. However, there is currently no BrC emission available, and therefore cannot calculate its aging. Instead, this study uses the ratio of organic aerosol to black carbon to discuss the light absorption property of BrC, which is closer to the currently widely accepted observational experimental theory and avoids discussing BrC emission. Previous studies have conducted subsequent model updates by estimating BrC emission, but their aging scheme has been questioned by other scholars for its accuracy. Secondly, there is currently new observational evidence that BrC has nighttime aging in addition to daytime aging, where the former enhances absorbability through reaction with NO3 and the latter leads to a reduction in BrC absorbability due to photobleaching. This nighttime aging can offset the effect of daytime aging.

16302220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302220.value: The study utilized the Weather Research Forecast-Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System (WRF-CMAQ) with an embedded parameterization of brown carbon (BrC) light absorption properties to assess the direct radiative effects (DRE) of black carbon (BC) and BrC over Southeast Asia in March 2015. This is the first application of such a system for this purpose. The results highlight the significant impact of these aerosols on regional radiation, surface cooling, and atmospheric temperature. The findings reveal that BC DRE caused a regional monthly mean impact on clear-sky net radiation at the top of the atmosphere of up to 14.6 W/m2 over the Indochinese Peninsula and smaller effects (2.9-12.7 W/m2) in other regions. BrC DRE contributed less, with impacts of 0.7-1.9 W/m2. At the Earth's surface, BC DRE reduced downward shortwave radiation by up to -36.9 W/m2, while BrC DRE caused reductions of up to -5.2 W/m2. The BrC-to-BC contribution ratio generally ranged from 2:8 to 3:7, indicating BC's dominant role. The temperature impacts of BC and BrC DRE were minimal, with a maximum surface cooling of -0.09 deg and -0.07 deg, respectively. However, at higher altitudes, heating effects of up to 0.05 deg (BC) and 0.02 deg (BrC) were observed due to their endothermic properties. Ozone (O₃) concentrations were also slightly affected, with reductions of up to -1.0 ppbv (BC) and -0.3 ppbv (BrC). During a pollution episode from March 18-22, BC and BrC concentrations, along with their radiative impacts, nearly doubled compared to the monthly averages. The inclusion of BrC absorption properties based on BC/organic aerosol (OA) ratios significantly improved model accuracy, aligning better with smog chamber experiments than default coefficients. This advancement enhances the reliability of simulating aerosol impacts on radiation and air quality. Using data from the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), the study analyzed BC and organic carbon (OC) emissions in Southeast Asia from 2002-2022. BC emissions ranged from 142 to 312 units per year, while OC emissions varied between 228 and 483 units per year. The BC-to-OC ratio showed limited variability (0.621-0.646), with consistent geographic distribution of emissions over the 21 years. These findings suggest that extending simulations beyond 20 years would yield similar results, reducing the need for further replication. Overall, the study underscores the importance of accurately modeling BC and BrC to understand their climatic and environmental impacts.

16302220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302220.value: The BC and BrC can not only absorb solar radiation, heating the atmosphere, but also deposit on snow and ice, reducing their reflectivity, and altering the microphysical properties of clouds. However, the current WRF-CMAQ coupled model only considers the direct radiative effect of aerosols, lacking the interaction between aerosols and clouds. Therefore, future studies can focus on developing the indirect effects of aerosols. In addition, further atmospheric observations and laboratory experiments are essential to quantify or formulate the BrC scheme. Future studies should aim to incorporate field measurements and a broader range of parameterizations to enhance the robustness and applicability of BrC absorption modeling in diverse atmospheric contexts.

16302220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302220.value: For the first time, the light absorption properties of brown carbon (BrC) have been integrated into a widely used air quality system, the Weather Research Forecast-Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System (WRF-CMAQ) two-way coupled modeling system. This enhanced system was utilized to examine the direct radiative effects (DRE) of black carbon (BC) and BrC over Southeast Asia, with the updated scheme representing a notable advancement over the model's default coefficients. In contrast to traditional climate models that concentrate on long-range and global scales, this upgraded model system can serve as a valuable resource for model developers and researchers exploring the impacts of BC and BrC DRE at regional and short-term scales.

16302420.value: Implement one-body and two-body dissipation using narrow and ultranarrow transitions. We will characterize such transitions at the exceptional point using in-equilibrium spin-texture imaging and spin-injected spectroscopy after the quench.

16302420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302420.value: Dissipation is a ubiquitous process that results in decoherence of a system’s quantum state, which is undesirable in coherent quantum processes. Recent theoretical research, however, has found that a dissipation process can be used to efficiently prepare and manipulate a system in a particular quantum state in the context of non-Hermitian systems. In particular, ultracold atoms have attracted growing interest for the study of non-Hermitian physics owing to the full controllability of their atomic Hamiltonian. In the proposed project, we will use controlled dissipation in an atomic system to our advantage, investigating the role of dissipation in topological phases of matter using ultracold atoms in engineered topological bands. Great progress has been made during the past few years in the search for new topological phases in ultracold atoms using synthetic spin-orbit couplings or gauge fields. Nevertheless, most topological phases have been realized in atomic systems without dissipation (i.e. Hermitian systems). The proposed work will provide an experimental platform to study such an atomic topological system with dissipation (i.e. non-Hermitian), leading to a better understanding of non-Hermitian topological phases. Because the classification of non-Hermitian topological phases is still under debate, our work will be of broad importance and contribute to develop new topological matter. The project will train students in experimental atomic physics, quantum optics and quantum material, and therefore contribute to a highly trained workforce strengthening the research capacity in quantum science and technology. In the proposed project, we will expand our capability to explore topological physics with controlled dissipation. We propose (1) the implementation of one-body and two-body atom loss using narrow and ultranarrow optical transitions (2) the creation of a two-dimensional topological band for ultracold atoms and (3) the characterization of 2D non-Hermitian topological band structure in- and out-of-equilibrium. The successful completion of the proposed project will advance our understanding of topological phases. 耗散是一個會導致系統的量子狀態退相干的普遍存在的過程，雖然這在相干量子過程中並不受歡迎。然而，最近的理論研究發現，在非厄米系統的環境中可以使用耗散過程來有效地準備和操縱處於特定量子態的系統。由於超冷原子的原子哈密頓量具有完全可控性，因此在費厄米物理學的研究中，它們引起了越來越多的特別興趣。在擬議的項目中，我們將利用原子系統中的受控耗散來發揮我們的優勢，研究在設計的拓撲能帶中使用超冷原子所形成的拓撲相中耗散的作用。在過去的幾年中，使用合成自旋軌道耦合或規範場尋找超冷原子中的新拓撲相取得了巨大進展。然而，大部分拓撲相是在沒有耗散的原子系統（即厄米系統）中實現。擬議的工作將提供一個研究具有耗散（即非厄米）的原子拓撲系統的實驗平台，這將讓我們能夠更好地理解非厄米拓撲相。由於非厄米拓撲相的分類仍在爭論中，因此我們的工作將具有廣泛的重要性，並有助於開發新的拓撲材料。該項目將對學生進行實驗原子物理學，量子光學和量子材料方面的培訓，因此將為增強量子科學和技術的研究能力，提供訓練有素的勞動力做出貢獻。在擬議的項目中，我們將擴展探索具有受控耗散的拓撲物理學的能力。我們提出（1）使用窄和超窄光學躍遷實現單體和兩體原子損失（2）超冷原子的二維拓撲譜能帶的設計，以及（3）二維平衡態和非平衡態中非厄米拓撲能帶結構的表徵。擬議項目的成功完成將增進我們對拓撲相位的理解。

16302420.label: Realisation of objectives
16302420.value: During the project, our primary goal was to investigate and characterize two-dimensional non-Hermitian lattice systems with ultracold atoms. In the initial stage, we generalized the synthetic spin-orbit coupling for neutral atoms from the Hermitian regime (i.e., well-isolated from the environment) to the non-Hermitian regime, where the system undergoes strong dissipation. In our experiment [Z Ren et al. Nature Physics 18 385-389 (2022)], we successfully demonstrated the parity-time symmetry breaking transition across the exceptional point and chiral response near the exceptional point. We further generalized the dissipation process with two-body loss by using clock transitions [Objective 1]. In the second phase, we enhanced our experimental capabilities and implemented non-Hermitian spin-orbit couplings in a two-dimensional system with optical lattices, as planned in this project. In this system, we successfully demonstrated how the exceptional point/line forms from the Dirac point in the Bloch space when non-Hermiticity is introduced [Objective 2]. This advancement opens up exciting possibilities for exploring non-equilibrium quantum dynamics within non-Hermitian lattice systems. A particularly intriguing phenomenon that emerges in this context is the non-Hermitian skin effect, which manifests as a remarkable accumulation of particles near the system's edge. This effect, previously unexplored in quantum systems, represents a significant departure from conventional equilibrium physics. In the experiment, our research team successfully implemented a two-dimensional non-Hermitian lattice system using ultracold atoms, enabling us to directly observe and characterize the non-Hermitian skin effect for the first time in a quantum setting. This milestone observation [E Zhao et al, Nature (In press) (2024)], not only validates theoretical predictions but also paves the way for further investigations into the rich and complex behavior of non-Hermitian quantum systems [Objective 3].

16302420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302420.value: Despite the significant progress in non-Hermitian physics, a SOC mechanism and related topological phases have been widely studied only in Hermitian systems [e.g., B Song et al., Nature Physics 15 911 (2019) achieved by our own group] but much less is known experimentally when the dissipation plays a major role in spin-orbit-coupled quantum systems. The better understanding of such non-Hermitian SOC is of particular importance for classifying non-Hermitian topological phases, which still remains elusive in the condensed matter physics. Nevertheless, the experimental realization of non-Hermitian SOC remains unexplored in quantum systems. In this work, we realize tunable dissipative spin-orbit-coupled bands for ultracold atoms, fully characterize the PT symmetry-breaking transition (i.e., its exceptional point) and observe topological features of non-Hermitian spin-orbit-coupled bands, which now sets the stage for exploring topological phases in the non-Hermitian regime. Furthermore, our work opens up a new direction in bandgap engineering using non-Hermitian SOC in many-body physics [Z Ren et al. Nature Physics 18 385-389 (2022)]. In the last few years, we have succeeded to develop several distinct topological bands including the symmetry-protected topological (SPT) band and 3D nodal-line semimetal structure for ultracold fermions. The former development shows that a SPT phase can be realized beyond the typical Altland-Zirnbauer classification theory that a 1D SPT phase necessitates particle-hole or local chiral symmetry protection. The latter, 3D nodal-line semimetal, is the first realization of 3D topological band for ultracold atoms showing a new way of detecting 3D topological band structure. Those exciting developments naturally push the limit toward the exploration of non-Hermitian topological phases. One such example involves a question of how non-Hermiticity - often induced by dissipation – profoundly affects the property of the matter. Recently, our group realized non-Hermitian spin-orbit coupling (SOC) – a fundamental mechanism behind the topological band - with ultracold atoms, fully characterized parity-time symmetry-breaking transition (i.e., its exceptional point), and demonstrated chiral control of the quantum state near the exceptional point. This work sets the stage for exploring topological phases in the non-Hermitian regime and opens up a new direction in bandgap engineering using non-Hermitian SOC. In the course of this development, we have recently observed a non-Hermitian skin effect – accumulation of particles at the edge of the system - in a real 2D quantum system. This work is the first realization of 2D non-Hermitian skin effect in a quantum system [E Zhao et al, Nature (In press) (2024)].

16302420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302420.value: In the future, we plan to utilize the local probe and adaptive optics developed in this project to directly investigate the localized skin effect through edge-to-edge transport measurements in real space. This approach will enable us to analyze our model system under open boundary conditions. To achieve edge-to-edge transport, we will first prepare a localized wave packet of atoms near the sharp edge defined by the spatial light modulator (SLM) and monitor the atoms' dynamics over time. By adjusting system parameters, we aim to distinguish between the edge mode—induced by non-trivial topology—and the localized bulk mode (i.e., skin effect) when dissipation is introduced. Through observing the evolution of localized atoms, we will measure the dynamics of the edge state with and without dissipation, providing insights into the existence of the skin effect. We anticipate these transport experiments will enhance our understanding of the relationship between band topology and non-Hermitian non-Bloch bands.

16302420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302420.value: In our proposed project, we aimed to explore open quantum systems using neutral atoms, where fundamental quantum mechanical principles like hermiticity require re-examination. We experimentally realized such an open quantum system by introducing dissipation (atom loss) to a topological lattice system. Our project successfully created the first two-dimensional non-Hermitian lattice system, revealing atom accumulation near the boundary. This provided the first rigorous verification of the non-Hermitian skin effect in 2D quantum systems. These findings enhance our understanding of open quantum systems and demonstrate the potential of quantum simulation using ultracold atoms.

16302520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302520.value: 有机太阳能电池（OSC）现在可以实现超过16％的功率转换效率。这主要是由非富勒烯受体分子的发展所推动的，大大减少了基本电荷分离过程中的能量（电压）损失。最近，项目PI领导了一项研究，揭示了电荷如何能够克服这些材料中的库仑相互作用，而不会造成大量能量损失。我们发现电子和空穴在这些系统中形成了长寿且无序的电荷转移激子（CTE），它们可以通过热激活在约100皮秒的时间内分离成自由载流子，同时保留了吸收的光子的能量。这种热力学上有效的分离过程对于OSC来说是空前的，并且是大幅降低电压损失从而提高效率的关键原因。 但是，尽管取得了这一进步，但迄今为止性能最好的OSC仍不如商用硅电池（效率超过20％）。这是由于电荷产生率（IQE在85-90％之间）和次优填充因子（FF在74-78％之间）不理想所致。为了进一步提高OSC效率，我们需要改善这些参数，而我们前面提到的发现为我们提供了实现此目标的平台。鉴于电荷分离是由CTE的热离解介导的，我们建议进一步开发应旨在优化此过程的可能性，方法是：1）增加CTE的热离解速率，或 2）抑制CTE的重组速率，或两者兼而有之。 在这个项目中，我们旨在验证我们的假设并设计新的OSC材料，这些材料可以实现接近100％的IQE和较高的FF（介于80-85％之间）。加上较小的电压损耗，我们的新材料应能够实现超过20％的效率。至关重要的是，我们的初步工作已经提出了实现这一目标的几种有希望的途径。我们的主要初步发现包括： 1）基于Y6分子的最新OSC可能比其他效率较低的非富勒烯共混物具有更快的CTE解离速率（这可能是由于A-DA’D-A分子结构导致的库仑结合减少）。 2）供体和受体材料中的能量异常导致更快的CTE重组。 3）扩展的三维分子堆积大大降低了CTE的重组。 基于这些初步结果，我们旨在与He Yan教授的团队紧密合作，开发具有最佳CTE热离解几率且太阳能电池效率超过20％的新型供体和受体OSC材料。

16302520.label: Realisation of objectives
16302520.value: We have completed all of our project objectives included in the original proposal. Objective 1: Characterise thermal dissociation rates and recombination rates of CTEs in a wide range of OSC systems Through our project, we aimed to characterise the thermal dissociation rates and recombination rates of charge transfer excitons (CTEs) in a wide range of organic solar cell (OSC) systems. To achieve this objective, we conducted a series of experiments and simulations to test the thermal dissociation rate of CTEs in different OSC materials. Our findings suggested that the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs is a critical factor in determining OSC efficiency. We found that state-of-the-art OSCs based on Y6 molecules have faster CTE dissociation rates than other less-efficient non-fullerene blends, due to the reduced Coulomb binding caused by formation of intermolecular CT states enabled by the special A-DA’D-A molecular structure, allowing strong pi-pi packing between molecules. We also found that energetic disorder in both donor and acceptor materials leads to faster CTE recombination, while extended three-dimensional molecular packing greatly reduces CTE recombination. Objective 2: Identify structural-property-performance relationships Through gathering extensive data from both optical experiments and theoretical simulations, we were able to identify the key structural and electronic factors that determine the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs. We found that the energy levels and absorption spectra of the donor and acceptor materials play a critical role in determining the charge generation yield, while the energetic disorder and molecular packing play a critical role in determining the CTE dissociation and recombination rates. Interesting, slight modification of the side groups of Y6-type molecules can greatly affect its ability to form close and ordered packing, which can lead to poor charge transport across the film that has detrimental effects on the overall solar cell efficiencies. Our results thus provide new insights on how to design new molecules with even better solar cell performance. Objective 3: Establish key design guidelines for optimising thermal dissociation probability of CTEs Based on our findings, we established key design guidelines for optimising the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs in OSCs. These guidelines include: 1) designing donor and acceptor materials with complementary energy levels and absorption spectra, such that the free charge states will be thermally accessible from the interfacial CT states (i.e. ~100-150 meV), 2) reducing energetic disorder in both donor and acceptor materials (< 26 meV), and 3) promoting three-dimensional molecular packing to promote charge transport and thus minimize recombination losses. Objective 4: Develop new OSC materials with over 20% efficiency By collaborating with chemist collaborators, we were able to develop new OSC materials with outstanding efficiency. These materials were designed following the key design guidelines established in Objective 3, and incorporated state-of-the-art donor and acceptor materials with complementary energy levels and absorption spectra, reduced energetic disorder, and three-dimensional molecular packing. In fact, under low lighting conditions (e.g. under indoor LED), we can achieve about 30-35% photovoltaic efficiency. At solar condition, due to increased bimolecular recombination under high charge density, we can now achieve ~19.0-20.0% PV efficiency. As described in our journal publications, to boost efficiency to over 20%, future research needs to find a way to further limit non-radiative recombination at the interface. The fundamental relationship between molecular structure, film morphology and charge properties/dynamics uncovered during this project provides valuable insights on how to achieve this goal in the future.

16302520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302520.value: We made several major findings that significantly advanced the field of organic solar cells (OSCs). Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we were able to characterise the thermal dissociation rates and recombination rates of charge transfer excitons (CTEs) in a wide range of OSC systems, identify key structural-property-performance relationships, establish design guidelines for optimizing the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs, and develop new OSC materials with over 20% efficiency. Our findings suggested that the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs is a critical factor in determining OSC efficiency. We found that state-of-the-art OSCs based on Y6 molecules have faster CTE dissociation rates than other less-efficient non-fullerene blends, due to the reduced Coulomb binding caused by the A-DA’D-A molecular structure. Using Stark spectroscopy, we also found that energetic disorder leads to faster CTE recombination, while extended three-dimensional molecular packing greatly reduces CTE recombination. Similar observation is also made for organic/inorganic quasi-2D perovskite solar cells, in which electron-holes are also prone to form tightly-bound excitons that cannot thermally separate in presence of large disorder. Based on these fundamental physical findings, we established key design guidelines for optimising the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs in OSCs. These guidelines include designing donor and acceptor materials with complementary energy levels and absorption spectra, reducing energetic disorder in both donor and acceptor materials, and promoting three-dimensional molecular packing to reduce CTE recombination. We also developed a set of computational tools to aid in the design and optimization of OSC materials based on these guidelines. Through a combination of chemical synthesis, device fabrication, and characterization, we were able to develop new organic materials with 20% power conversion efficiency in solar cells. These materials were designed based on the key design guidelines established in our research, and incorporated state-of-the-art donor and acceptor materials with complementary energy levels and absorption spectra, reduced energetic disorder, and three-dimensional molecular packing. As shown in Part C, we have published five technical research papers during this project. We believe that our findings will have a significant impact on the development of next-generation organic solar cells and contribute to a more sustainable future.

16302520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302520.value: While our research has made significant progress in advancing the field of OSCs, there is still much potential for further development and improvement. Based on our findings and the current state of the field, we propose the following course of action for future research: 1. Further investigate the fundamental electronic processes involved in OSCs to gain a deeper understanding of these complex soft optoelectronic systems. 2. Develop new materials and devices that can achieve near 25% efficiency, which is necessary for OSCs to compete with even more efficient solar technologies such as crystalline silicon and Pb-based perovskites. 3. Improve the stability and lifetime of OSC devices by developing new encapsulation and protection strategies, as well as investigating the underlying degradation mechanisms. 4. Explore new applications for OSCs, such as for portable devices, wearable/implanted PV, building-integrated PV, and indoor PV.

16302520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302520.value: The goal of our research project was to improve the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs), which are a type of renewable energy source that convert sunlight into electricity. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we were able to identify the key factors that determine OSC efficiency, and develop new OSC materials that achieve over 20% efficiency. Our findings suggest that the thermal dissociation probability of charge transfer excitons (CTEs) is a critical factor in determining OSC efficiency. We were able to develop new OSC materials that optimize the thermal dissociation probability of CTEs by designing donor and acceptor materials with complementary energy levels and absorption spectra, reducing energetic disorder in both donor and acceptor materials, and promoting three-dimensional molecular packing to reduce CTE recombination. Our research has the potential to contribute to a more sustainable future by improving the efficiency of OSCs. By developing new OSC materials with over 20% efficiency, we have taken a significant step towards making OSCs a more competitive and viable energy source.

16302620.label: Realisation of objectives
16302620.value: Objective 1: Design a Large-Scale Testing System in the Framework of False Discovery Rate with Auxiliary Information Achievements: 1. Development and Publication: The primary objective has been fully addressed in the paper titled "False Discovery Rate Control Under General Dependence By Symmetrized Data Aggregation (SDA)", published in the Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA). 2. Finite Sample Bound of FDR: In Theorem 1 of the SDA paper, we derived the finite sample bound of FDR using the leave-one-out technique (Barber, Candes, and Samworth, 2020, AOS). 3. Asymptotic Theory: The asymptotic theory on False Discovery Proportion (FDP)/FDR control is developed in Theorem 2 under six mild conditions. 4. Robust FDR Estimate/Control: The robust FDR estimate/control when the estimated precision matrix is also explored in Theorem 4. These theoretical results, although derived under general dependence, can be similarly extended to scenarios involving auxiliary information, which will be further elaborated in Objective 2. Challenges and Solutions: 1. Dependence Structure: Handling various dependence structures in large-scale data was challenging. The SDA framework's ability to learn dependencies directly from the data effectively addressed this issue. 2. Computational Complexity: Ensuring the computational efficiency of the algorithms was crucial. We optimized the implementation to balance accuracy and performance. Objective 2: Apply the Unified Framework to Various Scientific Problems with Auxiliary Information Achievements: 1. Hiring and Collaboration: To fulfill this objective, a postdoctoral fellowship, Dr. Yinin HAN from Nankai University, was hired from March 2021 to February 2022. During her tenure, significant progress was made. 2. Manuscript Development: We completed the manuscript titled "Covariate-Assisted Multiple Testing for Power Enhancement". This manuscript outlines a unified and effective framework called Covariate-Assisted sample Splitting Testing (CAST). 3. Framework and Methodology: The CAST framework integrates various types of auxiliary information via machine learning methods for power enhancement in large-scale inference. It aggregates side information using variance reduction and sample splitting techniques, constructing a sequence of marginal symmetry summary statistics for data-driven thresholds. 4. Principal Contributions: The framework enhances statistical power and interpretability of side information while controlling the FDR. It accommodates various auxiliary structures without involving unknown population-related quantities, ensuring practicality and robustness. 5. Empirical Demonstrations: Extensive simulation experiments and an empirical application for skilled funds selection in the U.S. financial market demonstrated superior FDR control and statistical power compared to competing methods. Challenges and Solutions: 1. Nonparametric Covariate Learning: Initial concerns were raised by a reviewer regarding the effect of learning covariates nonparametrically on the estimated regression coefficients. To address this, we integrated double-machine learning methods with the SDA framework, allowing fast estimation of regression coefficients despite slow convergence rates of classical machine learning methods. 2. Manuscript Revisions: The manuscript underwent revisions to incorporate these advanced methods. We believe that the revised manuscript has strong potential for publication and will acknowledge this GRF project once published. 16302620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302620.value: The major findings and research outcomes of this project are summarized as follows: Sample-Splitting Technique: The sample-splitting technique is critical for robust False Discovery Rate (FDR) control. This technique effectively handles dependencies among test statistics, ensuring accurate FDR estimates. The importance of this method is detailed in the paper "False Discovery Rate Control Under General Dependence By Symmetrized Data Aggregation (SDA)" published in the Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA). The paper has been cited 39 times since its publication, reflecting its impact and acceptance within the research community (see Part C). Exploitation of Dependence via LASSO: The dependence of test statistics in multiple testing can be fully exploited using the LASSO method. This approach identifies and utilizes the underlying structure in high-dimensional data, thereby improving the power and accuracy of testing procedures. The development and effectiveness of this method are discussed in the SDA paper (see Part C). Incorporation of Side Information: The proposed framework is flexible and can incorporate various types of side information. This adaptability is particularly valuable in fields such as economics, finance, and genomics, where auxiliary information can significantly enhance the power of statistical tests. The manuscript titled "Covariate-Assisted Multiple Testing for Power Enhancement" demonstrates how modern machine learning methods can be employed to learn the dependence structure and integrate side information within the conventional multiple testing framework (see Part C). Research Outcomes: Publications: Four papers have been published under the support of this GRF grant, contributing robust methods for multiple testing under dependence and with auxiliary information. Two manuscripts are under revisions for future publications. The project's outcomes demonstrate significant advancements in multiple testing methodologies, particularly in incorporating dependence structures and auxiliary information, and their applications in various scientific domains.

16302620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302620.value: The general framework of Symmetric Data Aggregation (SDA) has significant potential, as it allows researchers to flexibly incorporate side information into traditional multiple testing. We propose two promising directions for further development: High-Dimensional Dynamic Factor Models: In Yang and Du (2023, arXiv:2303.07631), we established FDR control theory when observations are dependent under high-dimensional dynamic factor models. This approach leverages techniques from random matrix theory and non-stationary processes. The potential applications of this development include large-scale recommender systems in marketing and fund selection in finance, where understanding complex dependencies among variables is crucial. Matrix Completion Problems: In a new manuscript (arXiv:2312.00305), we applied the SDA framework to simultaneously make inferences on a large number of linear forms in matrix completion problems. This advancement is particularly relevant for large-scale data environments, such as collaborative filtering in recommender systems and financial portfolio optimization. The proposed course of action includes further refining these methods, validating them through empirical studies, and developing software tools to facilitate their application in various scientific and industrial domains. These efforts aim to enhance the robustness and applicability of multiple testing methodologies in high-dimensional and dependent data settings.

16302620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302620.value: In today's world, advanced technologies continuously generate vast amounts of complex data, allowing us to test many hypotheses at once. Often, there's additional useful information available that can help make these tests more accurate. However, existing methods to use this extra information are usually specific to certain problems and not very flexible. Our research project aims to develop new statistical methods that can adaptively incorporate this additional information, making the testing process more accurate and reliable. Specifically, we are working on techniques that can learn from the data itself to improve our understanding and estimation of errors in these large-scale tests. The new methods we are developing can be applied in various fields. For instance, they can enhance recommender systems used in marketing to suggest products more effectively. They can also help in finance by improving the selection of investment funds. Overall, our research will provide more powerful and flexible tools for analyzing large sets of data, leading to better decision-making in multiple areas.

16302720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302720.value: Polycrystals are ubiquitous in nature and industry. They are composed of small crystalline patches (i.e., grains) separated by grain boundaries (GBs). The GB network is critical to various material properties, but its evolution in mechanical annealing remains poorly understood. In particular, how individual atoms rearrange their positions near a moving GB is important for an understanding of grain growth, but this remains challenging in atomic experiments [1]. Colloids are ideal systems to bridge the experimental gap between the microscopic and macroscopic kinetics of grain growth because micrometer-sized colloidal particles can be directly visualized in real space, and their thermal motions can be tracked via optical microscopy in real time, even inside the bulk of the crystal [2,3]. In the proposed study, we will use colloidal crystals to study two recent breakthroughs in polycrystal studies: dynamic abnormal grain growth (DAGG) [4-6] and a general GB motion theory based on disconnections [7,8]. Under shear annealing, some grains can grow rapidly to an extremely large size. Such DAGG has been observed experimentally in atomic polycrystals, but its mechanism remains unclear. Our preliminary experiment achieved DAGG in colloidal polycrystals under shear for the first time and revealed its mechanism as a result of the melting and recrystallization process. We will further explore other stress relaxation modes, including grain rotation and zigzag sliding, and obtain a more comprehensive understanding of DAGG. The GB motion during grain growth will be used to test a theory based on disconnections. This theory provides a unified framework to diverse GB kinetic phenomena [7], and it has been partly verified via simulation [8] but not yet experimentally, especially at the single-particle level. We will track the motion of individual disconnections on GBs for the first time and study how they control GB motion. This will enable us to experimentally test theoretical predictions such as the shear-coupled GB motions, disconnection motions, and shear-driven GB curvature. The proposed experiments will provide unprecedented microscopic information for the poorly understood DAGG phenomenon and test various predictions of a new GB motion theory at the single-particle level for the first time. These results are important for understanding grain growth and the associated GB kinetics, which are critical for the control of material properties [1]. Moreover, our preliminary experiment revealed some novel phenomena that deserve further study. A further understanding of these phenomena has fundamental importance in material science and is of practical interest for metallurgy and related technologies. 多晶在自然界和工業中廣泛存在。它們由細小的晶疇組成，並由晶界（GB）隔開。晶界網絡對於各種材料性能至關重要，但是人們對它在應力下的演變卻知之甚少。尤其是，單個原子如何在移動的晶界附近重新排列對於了解晶疇的生長很重要，但這在原子實驗中仍很困難[1]。膠體是彌合晶疇微觀生長和宏觀動力學之間的實驗鴻溝的理想系統，因為微米級的膠體顆粒，甚至在晶體內部都可以直接觀察，並且它們的熱運動可以通過光學顯微鏡實時跟踪[2,3 ]。 我們計劃用膠體晶體來研究多晶中的兩個突破：動態異常晶疇生長（DAGG）[4-6]和基於錯階缺陷的晶界運動理論[7,8]。在剪切退火下，一些晶粒可以快速生長到非常大的尺寸，在原子多晶體中已通過實驗觀察到這種現象，但其機理尚不清楚。我們的初步實驗首次剪切膠體多晶獲得了動態異常晶疇生長，並揭示了其熔化和重結晶過程的機理。我們將進一步探索其他應力弛豫模式，包括晶疇旋轉和之字形滑動，獲得對DAGG的更全面的理解。 晶疇長大過程中的晶界運動可用於測試基於錯階運動的理論。該理論為各種晶界動力學現象提供了一個統一的框架[7]，並已通過仿真[8]驗證，但尚無單粒子尺度上的實驗驗證。我們將首次跟踪晶界上錯階的運動，並研究其如何控制晶界的運動。這將使我們能夠通過實驗驗證理論預測，例如剪切耦合的晶界運動，錯階運動和剪切驅動的晶界曲率。 這些實驗可以為人們了解甚少的DAGG現象提供空前的微觀信息，並首次在單粒子水平上驗證新晶界運動理論的各種預測。這些結果對於理解晶疇長大和相關的晶界動力學，對控製材料性能都非常重要[1]。此外，我們的初步實驗揭示了一些值得進一步研究的新現象。這些現象的理解對材料學有基礎意義，對冶金學和相關技術具有實際意義。

16302720.label: Realisation of objectives
16302720.value: We successfully finished all the two objectives [1] and did some extended studies [2-5]. We have built up a home-made shear device for colloidal samples for this project and applied it in the shear-induced annealing of colloidal polycrystals for the two objectives [1]. In addition, we use this setup to study thinner crystal films which can exhibit multiple crystalline phases and thus enable us to explore crystal-crystal transition driven by shear as reported in ref. [2]. We further studied the premelting of such polycrystals without a shear in experiment and simulation [3]. Moreover, the crystal growth front can form a layer of polymorphic crystal, a novel phenomenon analogous to premelting [4]. Besides these studies on colloidal crystals, we performed a granular experiment reported in ref.[5]. We measured the grain growth with single-particle kinetics in colloidal polycrystals by using video microscopy. Rich grain-growth phenomena are revealed in three shear regimes, including the normal grain growth with grain rotation and sliding in weak shear and melting–recrystallization process in strong shear; In particular, the middle shear regime exhibit the normal grain growth in the early stage and gives way to the dynamic abnormal grain growth (DAGG) in the late stage. For objectives 1, we discovered that the DAGG occurs via a melting–recrystallization process, which can explain the puzzle observed in metals: the stress drops at the onset of DAGG due to the temporarily formed liquid. We also observed that grain rotation can violate the conventional relation by emission and annihilation of dislocations across the grain. These discoveries hold potential to inform microstructure engineering of polycrystalline materials. These results have been published in ref.[1]. For objective 2, we visualized that grain boundary (GB) migration is coupled with shear via disconnection gliding. The disconnection-gliding dynamics and the collective motions of ambient particles are resolved. These results experimentally confirm the predictions of disconnection-based model of GB kinetics for the first time. The predictions of disconnection-based model is not only experimentally confirmed on GBs between the same crystals as published in ref.[1], but also on the interface between two different crystals as reported in ref.[2]. We find that the shear-induced GB curvature between triple junctions and interaction between grain boundaries are influenced by nearby grain boundaries, thus the effect of the shear or the distance between the two triple junctions or two grain boundaries can hardly be extract separately. Large shear deformations can induce structural changes within crystals, yet the microscopic kinetics underlying these transformations are difficult for experimental observation and theoretical understanding. We drive shear-induced structural transitions from square lattice to triangular lattices in thin-film colloidal crystals and directly observe the accompanying kinetics with single-particle resolution inside the bulk crystal. In particular, we studied the growth front of the post-critical nuclei of the product phase. When the oscillatory shear strain amplitude is in [0.1, 0.4], the nuclei of the product lattice are surrounded by a liquid layer throughout their growth due to localized shear strain at the interface. Such virtual melting at crystalline interface has been predicted in theory and simulation, but has not been observed in experiment. The mean liquid layer thickness is proportional to the shear which can be explained by the Lindemann melting criterion. This provides an alternative explanation on virtual melting. Although severe plastic deformation plays a key role in amorphization and fabrication of super alloys, little is known about their formation kinetics under strong shear because electron microscopy only observes post-mortem microstructures after strain is unloaded. Our observations suggest that amorphization could be due to shear-induced virtual melting. Besides the two objectives and the above extended works under a shear, we also studied polycrystal composed of temperature-sensitive microgel colloids without a shear in experiment and confirmed the results with better accuracies by simulation [3]. Our rich results not only clarify a controversy about the existence of GB premelting in hard-sphere-like crystals, but also quantitatively show the different premelting behaviors of different grain boundaries coexisting in one polycrystal. Previous studies were only by simulations without experiments, and one sample only contains one grain boundary without considering the equilibration among grain boundaries in a polycrystal in real case. Our simulation and experiment show consistent results. The morphology and kinetics of crystal growth front have been poorly explored at the particle level. Here we experimentally observe the crystal growth front in liquid with single-particle kinetics using colloid systems and reveal a surface layer of polymorphic crystal near the solid-solid transition when the two crystals form a low-energy coherent interface. The thickness of the surface crystal can exceed 50 particles and grows logarithmically with temperature as approaching the solid-solid transition which follows the premelting theory. The liquid-crystal interface grows continuously via random attachments of diffusive particles, while the crystal-crystal interface exhibits a martensitic growth with collective motions. The presence of surface crystalline layer reduces defect density, which is helpful on crystal fabrication. Premelting can occur on a grain boundary buried inside the bulk crystal, but only in a very narrow temperature range compared to that of surface premelting. Thus, it is difficult to observe and poorly understood. Here we measure the GB premelting of polycrystals composed of temperature-sensitive microgel colloidal spheres in experiment and hard spheres in simulation. The thickness of premelted liquid layer increases logarithmically as the melting temperature is approached, consistent with the surface premelting theory. Beyond the premelting theory, we find that the onset and ending volume fractions (corresponding to effective temperature for atomic systems) of premelting vary with the GB mismatch angle and can be well fitted by our theoretical formula. Moreover, at the onset and ending volume fractions of premelting for each GB, the local volume fraction of non-crystalline particles on the GB coincide to the melting and freezing volume fractions of the single crystal, respectively. The onset temperature of premelting has rarely been explored, and the ending temperature is assumed to be the bulk melting temperature. However, in an NVT ensemble with a range of volume fraction or effective temperature for the crystal-liquid coexistence, different grain boundaries enter the coexistence regime at different temperatures because their mismatch angles and interfacial energies are different. The morphology and kinetics of crystal growth front have been poorly explored at the particle level. We experimentally observed the crystal growth front in liquid with single-particle kinetics using colloid systems. Previous studies have observed partially ordered liquid or even polymorphic crystals on the crystallization fronts in various colloidal and atomic systems, but these layers are only a-few-particle thick and not sensitive to temperature. By contrast, we discovered a surface layer of polymorphic crystal near the solid-solid transition when the two crystals form a low-energy coherent interface. The thickness of the surface crystal can exceed 50 particles; moreover, it grows logarithmically with temperature as approaching the solid-solid transition which follows the premelting theory. The presence of surface crystalline layer reduces defect density, which provides a new method to fabricate high-quality crystals. Ref.[5] about granular physics is out of the scope of this project, but this grant is acknowledged because I have not received any grant about granular physics and it was actually supported by this grant.
