16302720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302720.value: We studied the shear-induced annealing of polycrystals [1]. The mechanism of DAGG in polycrystal annealing is not clear. We discovered that the DAGG occurs via a melting–recrystallization process, which can explain the puzzle observed in metals. We tested the predictions of disconnection-based model of GB kinetics including the shear-coupled GB migration not only in grain boundaries [1], but also on interfaces between different lattices [2]. We studied the shear-induced crystal-to-crystal transition, especially on its late stage of nucleus growth [2]. We observed a novel liquid band on the growth front, which confirms the theoretical prediction of virtual melting on propagating crystal-crystal interfaces for the first time. Our observation reveals an alternative mechanism based on the the Lindemann melting criterion which holds under non-equilibrium shear. GB premelting occurs in a very narrow range, leading to a controversial of its existence in hard-sphere crystals. We not only clarified this controversy and confirmed its existence, but also explored premelting of various GBs in one crystal [3]. We obtained novel results about the onset and ending points of GBs with different mismatch angles, and their relations to the crystal-liquid coexistence regime. We find that the crystallization front of a post-critical nucleus in liquid can exhibit a layer of polymorphic crystal which may exceed 50 particles thick and change with temperature logarithmically [4]. By contrast, previous studies show thin ordered liquid or crystalline layer with a few particles thick at the crystallization growth front. We further showed that its mechanism is analogous to premelting and suggested some atomic and molecular polymorphic crystals which should exhibit this phenomenon. We further studied the kinetics of the growth front, the surface orientation effect and achieved novel double-layer of crystals on the surface under certain conditions. 16302720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302720.value: Colloids are excellent model systems to study the microscopic kinetics in crystals and related phase transitions because micrometer-sized colloidal particles and their thermal motions can be directly visualized by optical microscopy even inside 3D bulk. By using colloids, we experimentally studied polycrystal annealing under a shear and shear-induced a crystal-crystal transition at the single-particle level for the first time. We further clarify the existence of premelting of grain boundary and discovered a novel polymorphic crystalline layer on the surface of the crystal growth front. We observed a shear-induced abnormal grain growth. It occurs via a melting–recrystallization process which can hardly be resolved in atomic systems because electron microscopy can only observe the interior of solid samples by cutting the samples after the shear is removed. This melting–recrystallization process can explain the puzzle observed in metals. A recent theory explains the shear-coupled grain-boundary migration which experimental test needs the observation of single-particle kinetics. Our experiment confirmed this theoretical picture for the first time [1]. Moreover, we observed that the growth front of crystalline nucleus forms a layer of liquid in the crystal-crystal transition, which confirmed the theoretical prediction of virtual melting at crystal-crystal interface for the first time [2].

16303320.label: Project Objectives
16303320.value: The PI aims to investigate the statistical inference for noisy tensor SVD by higher-order orthogonal iteration (HOOI) algorithm. Noisy tensor SVD is a fundamental model for evaluating statistical performances of tensor algorithms. HOOI, as a special version of AM, is particularly efficient for noisy tensor SVD. Characterizing the distributions of HOOI estimators not only enables uncertainty quantification of HOOI but also reveals fundamental differences between matrix and tensor models. The PI will extend exclusive spectral tools to establish the limiting distributions of HOOI estimators under near-optimal signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. The outcomes enable the statistical inferences of singular subspaces for noisy tensor SVD The PI and collaborators will investigate the statistical optimality of a restricted AM algorithm on Grassmannians for noisy tensor completion (NTC). NTC refers to the recovery of missing entries in noisy tensorial datasets. It has wide applications in multi-dimensional recommender systems and signal processing. AM algorithms are practically outperforming, whose statistical performances are largely unknown. Designing an AM algorithm with guaranteed statistical efficiency can greatly promote tensor algorithms for multi-way data analysis. Under near-optimal sample size and sharp SNR conditions, the team will prove that statistically optimal convergence rates, proportional to the noise level, are attainable by an AM algorithm. Several techniques from the team's prior works will help achieve the goal. The PI and collaborators aim to investigate a tensor method for estimating mixed memberships of nodes in hypergraph networks. Hypergraph networks consist of higher-order interactions of network nodes which bring new insights for network analysis. Estimating mixed memberships in complex hypergraph networks is important. By integrating tensor algorithms and community detection, the team could further advocate tensor methods for analyzing complex networks. The proposed method is a combination of the regularized HOOI and the collaborator's vertex hunting (VH) algorithm. The regularized HOOI is for spectral estimation and VH is for mixed membership estimation. The team shall study the statistical limitations of the proposed algorithm and conduct real data analysis. The PI will propose an AM algorithm for robust tensor SVD, aiming to exactly recover a low-rank tensor when it is corrupted by sparse noise. Robustness is always a benchmark of effectiveness for statistical methods. Developing robust tensor AM algorithms is meaningful for various applications such as video denoising. The algorithm is a combination of hard thresholding and alternating minimization on Grassmannians. The PI shall investigate its statistical performances.

16303320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303320.value: In an era of big data, large datasets with complex structures routinely arise from diverse fields. One particularly fascinating type of data often derived with multi-dimensional features or from multiple information sources, is a tensor or multilinear array. These tensorial datasets pose unprecedented challenges to the statistics, machine learning, and data science communities. Tremendous efforts were made to innovate efficient algorithms and statistical methods to analyze tensorial datasets. As a key ingredient, noisy tensor decompositions often show exceptional performances in practice. Unlike matrix decompositions, the statistical theory of noisy tensor decomposition is more delicate since the computation feasibility is usually a decisive factor of the statistical optimality. The alternating minimization algorithm is a class of non-convex methods for noisy tensor decomposition. While being computationally efficient and practically outperforming, the statistical understanding of alternating minimization algorithms for noisy tensor decomposition is still in its infancy. The goal of this project is to study statistical theory, convergence behavior, and applications of alternating minimization (AM) algorithms for noisy tensor decomposition. The PI and collaborators aim to investigate: (1) the statistical inference of noisy tensor SVD by higher-order orthogonal iteration (HOOI) which is a special AM algorithm; (2) the statistically optimal convergence rates of noisy tensor completion by a restricted AM algorithm; (3) the estimation of mixed memberships in hypergraph networks by a regularized HOOI algorithm and its statistical limitations; (4) the estimation of robust tensor SVD by hard thresholding and alternating minimization. 在大数据时代，复杂结构的数据出现在各种领域里。张量(多维矩阵)数据是其中一种独特结构的数据。它往往来自于多维度的特征或者多信息采集源头。这些张量数据给统计和数据科学带来了前所未有的挑战。近些年来，研究者花费了很多经历去创造统计方法去分析张量数据。然而张量模型的统计理论比矩阵更加复杂， 尤其在统计最优化和计算可行性之间的相变。目前为止，很多经典的张量方法的计算和统计分析仍处于不完整的阶段。

16303320.label: Realisation of objectives
16303320.value: 1. The PI and collaborators successfully achieved Objective 1. They investigated the higher-order orthogonal iteration (HOOI) algorithm for noisy tensor SVD. By leveraging a spectral tool developed in the PI's previous work, they established a central limit theorem for the singular vectors estimated with the HOOI algorithm. Moreover, they extended these methods to the tensor regression model, thereby enabling statistical inference for the singular vectors within that framework. The results can be found in the paper titled "Inference for low-rank tensors" published in The Annals of Statistics. 2. Objective 2 has been accomplished as expected. The PI and the student studied the restricted alternating minimization (AM) algorithm on Grassmannians for noisy tensor completion (NTC). Notably, they investigated low-rank tensors in the tensor-train format, which have attracted considerable attention due to their popularity in tensor networks. They demonstrated that the algorithm converges linearly when the step size is carefully chosen, and statistically optimal estimators can be achieved in the presence of noise. These results are detailed in the paper titled "Provable Tensor-Train Format Tensor Completion by Riemannian Optimization", published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research. 3. The PI and collaborators successfully achieved Objective 3, which led to the publication of two papers: "Community Detection on Mixture Multilayer Networks via Regularised Tensor Decomposition" in The Annals of Statistics and "Latent Space Model for Higher-Order Networks and Generalized Tensor Decomposition" in the Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics. In these works, they investigated tensor-based approaches for higher-order network analysis, including community detection and nodal embedding. Hypergraph networks and multilayer networks are special cases of higher-order networks, and their results demonstrate that tensor-based methods can effectively handle extremely sparse higher-order networks. 4. The PI and collaborators studied robust methods for network inference. Their approach is based on counting the number of motifs in one or multiple networks, which are referred to as network moments. In an observed network, the moment associated with cyclic motifs is given by the trace of an appropriate power of the adjacency matrix. We derived higher-order accurate methods for testing network moments and comparing networks. These results led to the publication of two papers: "Edgeworth Expansion for Network Moments", published in The Annals of Statistics, and "U-Statistic Reduction: Higher-Order Accurate Risk Control and Statistical-Computational Trade-Off", published in the Journal of the American Statistical Association.

16303320.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303320.value: The major findings are as follows: 1. The alternating minimization algorithm is computationally efficient and statistically optimal for both tensor SVD and tensor regression. Moreover, with appropriate debiasing treatment, the derived estimators can be used for statistical inference. These results are presented in the paper "Inference for Low-Rank Tensors", published in The Annals of Statistics. 2. The alternating minimization algorithm is powerful for noisy tensor completion, whether the tensor is in Tucker format or tensor-train format. These results are detailed in the paper "Provable Tensor-Train Format Tensor Completion by Riemannian Optimization", published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research. 3. Tensor-based methods, including alternating minimization algorithms, can be effectively used for higher-order network analysis, such as community detection and nodal embedding. These methods can handle extremely sparse higher-order networks. The findings are presented in two papers: "Community Detection on Mixture Multilayer Networks via Regularised Tensor Decomposition" in The Annals of Statistics and "Latent Space Model for Higher-Order Networks and Generalized Tensor Decomposition" in the Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics. 4. Higher-order accurate methods have been derived for network inference based on the Edgeworth expansion of network moments. These methods are more robust than approaches that rely solely on tensor decomposition. The results are detailed in two papers: "Edgeworth Expansion for Network Moments", published in The Annals of Statistics, and "U-Statistic Reduction: Higher-Order Accurate Risk Control and Statistical-Computational Trade-Off", published in the Journal of the American Statistical Association.

16303320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303320.value: Rapidly evolving data processing and collection technologies have made massive tensor datasets prevalent across diverse fields, imposing significant demands for advanced methodologies to analyze and uncover hidden information in high-dimensional tensor-format data. Alternating minimization is a computationally efficient algorithm for obtaining effective tensor decompositions and has found many successful applications. In this project, the PI investigated this powerful algorithm for various tensor-related problems, demonstrating its theoretical properties. The results not only provide practical guidelines for implementing these algorithms tailored to different problems but also showcase their usefulness for statistical inference in low-rank tensors and higher-order network analysis. Overall, this research represents a systematic study of the computational aspects, theoretical properties, statistical inference, and network-driven applications of alternating minimization algorithms.

16303420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303420.value: Human life is full of chirality. For example, cells, proteins, carbohydrates and many pharmaceuticals are all made of chiral molecules. Therefore, the ability to synthesize chiral molecules and understand their properties reflect our ability to control and improve human life. Today, many of these useful chiral molecules are made by organic synthesis, more specifically, asymmetric synthesis. Among different strategies for asymmetric synthesis, asymmetric catalysis that employ chiral catalyst for the introduction of chirality is the most efficient. In the past few decades, various new tools and concepts have been developed to achieve better catalysis. Particular noteworthy is the rapid improvement in organocatalysis, which provides an excellent alternative to metal catalysis. In the new context, numerous new opportunities and challenges emerge for the development of previously underdeveloped asymmetric reactions in chiral building block synthesis. Here we propose to further advance asymmetric synthesis by means of organocatalysis. Specifically, we propose to developed three types of new reactions employing Brønsted acid as catalyst. They include (a) direct catalytic asymmetric oxidative rearrangement of indoles for the synthesis of chiral pyrrolidinyl-spirooxindoles, (b) formal N‒H insertion of sulfur ylides for the synthesis of chiral α-amino carbonyl compounds, and (c) design, synthesis, and application of a new family of chiral structures, tetraarylmethanes, that lack general and efficient access before. The development of these asymmetric reactions will not only provide fundamental understanding of new reactivity and stereocontrol methods, but also provide rapid access to a range of useful chiral building blocks with potential applications in medicines, materials, other aspects of daily life. 人類的生活充滿手性，例如細胞、蛋白質、碳水化合物和許多藥物都是由手性分子構成的。因此，合成手性分子並了解其性質在一定程度上與人類生活密切相關。今天，許多改變人類生活的手性分子是通過有機不對稱合成的手段獲得的。在不對稱合成的策略中，採用手性催化劑引入手性的不對稱催化是最有效的方法。在過去的幾十年中，已經出現各種新的策略和概念來實現更好的催化作用。特別值得注意的是有機小分子催化得到了快速改進，對金屬催化是一個重要的補充。在新的背景下，手性結構單元合成中仍然存在很多挑戰，同時也是不對稱催化領域的機遇。本研究將通過有機小分子催化進一步推進不對稱合成。具體而言，我們將使用布朗斯特德酸作為催化劑研究三類反應。其中包括（a）吲哚的直接催化不對稱氧化重排，用於合成螺環手性吲哚酮；（b）硫葉立德的不對稱N‒H插入反應用於合成手性α-氨基羰基化合物；以及（c）設計合成新的手性結構家族。這些反應的發展，不僅可以對反應性和立體控制方法有新的拓展，而且可以快速獲得一系列有用的手性結構單元，並在藥物、材料和日常生活的其他方面有潛在的應用。

16303420.label: Realisation of objectives
16303420.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a range of asymmetric reactions employing Brønsted acid as catalyst. They include N‒H insertion of sulfur ylides for the synthesis of chiral α-amino carbonyl compounds and the further development using different precursors and nucleophiles, direct catalytic asymmetric oxidative rearrangement of indoles for the synthesis of chiral pyrrolidinyl-spirooxindoles and the use of electrochemistry for the development of chiral indoline compounds; the design, synthesis, and application of a range of previously less-explored chiral tetraarylmethanes. The objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. We have developed the first catalytic enantioselective oxidative rearrangement of indoles to oxindoles. With NIS as the superior oxidant and a suitable CPA as the catalyst, high efficiency and excellent enantioselectivity have been achieved under mild conditions. Mechanistically, this process involves rapid and reversible halogenation followed by water addition and rearrangement. This work has been published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. Regarding the challenging task of making chiral tetraarylmethanes, we have achieved the first example of asymmetric nucleophilic attack of m-hydroxyl benzylic carbocations providing access to highly enantioenriched tetraarylmethanes, a chemical space with limited access previously. Preliminary biological studies indicated that these products not only exhibit impressive anticancer activities, but also have the potential to improve the efficacy of chemotherapeutics in cancer stem cells through a distinct mechanism, thus providing opportunities for the development of anticancer chemotherapy. This work has been published in Nat. Synth. We have developed the first organocatalytic asymmetric N−H insertion reaction of α-carbonyl sulfoxonium ylides, a safe and stable surrogate of diazocarbonyl compounds (published in J. Am. Chem. Soc.) Recently we have further developed a series of asymmetric reactions involving sulfur ylides, including the C-N bond formation using sulfoxonium ylides, which has been published in Chemical Science. More recently, we have developed a catalytic asymmetric azidation that provides efficient access to enantioenriched α-azido carbonyl compounds, also published in Chem. Sci. Then, we further advanced this topic to a photo-induced metal-free enantioselective X−H insertion reaction of diazo compounds under mild conditions. By employing visible light as promoter, a chiral phosphoric acid as catalyst, and most importantly, DMSO as additive, the reaction of a range of α-diazoesters and arylamines successfully proceeded in one-pot asymmetric N−H insertion to form the desired enantioenriched α-aminoesters with high efficiency and good enantioselectivity. This work has been published in Chem. Sci.

16303420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303420.value: (1) We have developed a catalytic enantioselective oxidative rearrangement of indoles to oxindoles (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.). (2) We developed the first organocatalytic asymmetric N−H insertion reaction of α-carbonyl sulfoxonium ylides (Chem. Sci.). (3) We developed the first catalytic asymmetric formal cross dehydrogenative coupling for the efficient synthesis of chiral tetraarylmethanes (Chem. Sci.). (4) We developed a new process for the convenient access to the cyclopropane-incorporated polycyclic structures from isobenzopyryliums (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.). (5) We have introduced a new chiral backbone (SPHENOL) of chiral catalyst for asymmetric synthesis (J. Am. Chem. Soc.). (6) We have developed a Sc-based catalytic asymmetric oxetane opening by carbon nucleophiles (Org. Lett.). (7) We have developed two new protocols for the efficient asymmetric synthesis of chiral pyrrolidines based on oxetane desymmetrization (Org. Lett.). (8) We have achieved the first asymmetric nucleophilic attack of m-hydroxyl benzylic carbocations, providing access to enantioenriched tetraarylmethanes. These compounds have the potential to improve the efficacy of chemotherapeutics in cancer stem cells through a distinct mechanism (Nat. Synth.). (9) We have developed the first electricity-driven catalytic asymmetric process employing weak ion-pairing interaction for asymmetric induction. Two representative asymmetric bromocyclization processes have been developed to showcase this powerful system (Nat. Commun.). (10) We have developed a catalytic asymmetric azidation to access enantioenriched α-azido carbonyl compounds by formal asymmetric H-N3 insertion of the versatile α-carbonyl sulfoxonium ylides (Chem. Sci.). (11) We have developed a catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution/isomerization process with central chirality transposition (Org. Lett.). (12) We have developed a photo-induced metal-free enantioselective N−H insertion reaction of diazo compounds under mild conditions using a suitable amount of DMSO as additive (Chem. Sci.). (13) We have developed the first deracemization approach for efficient access to enantioenriched triarylmethanes (Chem. Synth.). (14) We have achieved the first asymmetric addition to naphthoquinone methides with methide and carbonyl located in different rings, allowing a wide range of previously less accessible remotely chiral naphthols and naphthylamines to be efficiently synthesized from readily available racemic alcohols with excellent enantioselectivity (J. Am. Chem. Soc.). (15) We have developed the first catalytic asymmetric reactions of indole imine 5-methides to synthesize indole-containing triaryl alkanes bearing a remote stereogenic center. This work has been published in Org. Lett. (16) We have developed the first catalytic enantioselective nucleophilic α-chlorination of ketones to generate α-chloro ketones bearing a tertiary stereogenic center from racemic α-keto sulfonium salts and NaCl (J. Am. Chem. Soc.).

16303420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303420.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful catalytic asymmetric organocatalytic reactions involving indoles and sulfur ylides will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will continue to explore and push the boundary of the synthesis of alpha-chiral carbonyls using the sulfur ylide precursors as well as the more general synthesis of chiral tetraarylmethanes. We will spend more efforts to explore mechanistically different processes to achieve these goals. In the meanwhile we are developing new catalysts that can enable previously challenging reactions to proceed more efficiently.

16303420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303420.value: Human life is full of chirality. For example, cells, proteins, carbohydrates and many pharmaceuticals are all made of chiral molecules. Therefore, the ability to synthesize chiral molecules and understand their properties reflect our ability to control and improve human life. In this project, we have developed a range of methods that can provide access to chiral molecules through control of catalyst, conditions, and design of starting materials. These processes provided access to important structures, such as indole derviatives and topologically novel but synthetically challenging molecules chiral tetraarylmethanes can be thus synthesized with ease. They can serve as potential drug candidates or intermediates. Some of these reactions represent unprecedented reaction modes. They also use metal-free catalysts, which have the potential to protect the environment in modern synthesis. These findings will contribute to the advances in materials industry, drug discovery and environmental protection.

16303720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303720.value: 在转角石墨烯中发现的超导和绝缘态为研究二维系统的平带开辟了新途径。人工叠加两片石墨烯，当转角在奇异角度时，此系统的低能态电子被改变，从而产生平带，绝缘态，超导态和磁性。用转角或晶体点阵差异构造二维稳定摩尔晶体已经成为调控材料性能的新方法。最近我们报道了过渡金属二硫化物的摩尔晶体的结构应力状态和平带特性，不同于石墨烯，过渡金属二硫化物的摩尔晶体没有奇异角度。1-4度转角内都可以观察到平带特性，而且超导转变温度比石墨烯中高。但是由于其中的界面态在应力和再构影响，或反演对称性的破缺和强轨道自旋的电子交互作用，平带特性变得比较复杂。 我们研究表明，在较小转角度下WSe2的摩尔晶体偏离理想结构。其界面原子结构和对称性破缺成为产生特殊平带特性的重要因素。我们计划系统地研究摩尔晶体界面结构，应变以及对称性变化与奇异的电子输运特性的关联，特别是超导态，非线性霍尔效应以及磁性的产生。此项目的成功将提供关键的技术信息用以精确调整不同摩尔超晶格的结构和特性，同时这些信息可以用来调节电学特性和设计功能器件。

16303720.label: Realisation of objectives
16303720.value: This project started in January 2021. Due to the influence of the Covid-19 period, the research central facility in HKUST campus was often partially opened and closed from time to time. We therefore faced difficulties of using some of the equipment in the campus. Because of the Covid-19, we were not able to attend international conference outside Hong Kong. We have made some changes on the conference budget. We spent more money to purchase small equipment so that our students could conduct some experiments in our labs. The cost for purchasing materials is increased in the past three years and therefore there is significant expenditure changes on the General Expenses budget. In the first year of study, we have mainly carried out research on the first objective of fabricate and characterize moiré interface structures of twisted atomically thin transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). We finally identified that the quality of twisted WSe2 superlattice device structure was suitable for our study by investigating the electronic transport and scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). Then, we have focused on the STM study of the flat-band-induced unconventional transport properties., which is the second objective of this project. We published the first paper in 2021, “Lattice reconstruction induced multiple ultra-flat bands in twisted bilayer WSe2”. We uncovered the interface reconstruction of twisted WSe2, which exhibits a strong dependence on the constituent layer number and twist angles. The competition between the interlayer interaction leads to rich superlattice motifs and strain modulation. The number of ultra-ﬂat bands and spatial distribution of the wavefunctions match well with the theoretical predictions, providing a foundation for further study of correlated electronic phases (Nature Comm. 12, 5601 (2021). Our further study has resulted in our second discovery, the unconventional ferroelectricity in half-filling states of antiparallel stacking of twisted WSe2. We observed an abnormal electronic polarization in twisted double bilayer WSe2 in antiparallel interface stacking geometry, where local centrosymmetry of atomic registries at the twist interface does not favor the spontaneous electronic polarizations. The ferroelectric behaviors occur at half-filling insulating states at cryogenic temperatures. Our work highlights the prominent role of many-body electronic interaction in fostering novel electronic states in moire supperlattices (see National Science Open 2 (2023)20220033). Another unconventional phenomenon we discovered is the giant nonlinear Hall effect in twisted bilayer WSe2. We observed that twisted WSe2 shows highly tunable giant nonlinear Hall effects (NHE). No specific twist angles for generating such a NHE. The extracted Berry curvature dipole in twisted WSe2 is among the highest of all materials ever explored. The electron correlation effects may play a significant role in generating the record high responsivity (see our paper published in National Science Review 10 (2023) nwac232). Through deep collaboration with research groups in Shanghai University of Science and Technology and Oxford University in UK, we first observed a new effect of twist-induced modification in the electronic structure of bilayer WSe2 (Nano Letters 2023 23 (15), 7008-7013), and another important effect of the Γ-Valley Moir´e bands and emergent hexagonal lattice in twisted transition metal dichalcogenides (PHYSICAL REVIEW X 12, 021065 (2022)). We performed a systematic investigation on the electronic structure of 5.1° twisted bilayer WSe2 that hosts correlated insulating and zero-resistance states. Interestingly, contrary to one’s expectation, moir´ e bands were observed only at Γ valley but not K valley in μ-ARPES measurements, and correspondingly, our STM measurements clearly identified the realspace honeycomb- and kagome-shaped charge distributions at the moir´ e length scale associated with the Γ-valley moir´ e bands. These results not only reveal the unusual valley-dependent moir´e-modified electronic structure in twisted transition metal dichalcogenides, but also highlight the Γ-valley moir´ e bands as a promising platform for exploring strongly correlated physics in emergent honeycomb and kagome lattices at different energy scales. Trough collaboration with theoretical groups, we have elucidated the relationships between moiré interface structures, stacking orders, symmetry breaking effects, and unconventional transport properties in twisted TMDC heterostructures. This is a successful project which has achieved all objectives we proposed in the project.

16303720.value: We have established close collaboration with colleagues working in the area of 2D quantum materials and twisted Moiré superlattice structures through this project in HKUST and international research groups. 16303720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303720.value: Artificially stacking one atomic layer on another flake of single atomic layer with a small, specified rotation angle generates moiré unit-cells, which reshape the low energy electronic states. This results in new flat bands and many exotic quantum phenomena such as Mott-insulator transitions, unconventional superconductivity and ferromagnetism. In this project, we build 2D structures through staking, twisting or lattice mismatching to form stable moiré crystals. The main achievements in this project are: (1) we uncovered the interface reconstruction of twisted WSe2, which exhibits a strong dependence on the constituent layer number and twist angles. (2) we observed an abnormal electronic polarization in twisted double bilayer WSe2 in antiparallel interface stacking geometry, and (3) we achieved the highest efficiency of the nonlinear Hall effects in twisted WSe2 devices. The success of this project has provided critical knowledge and technical information needed to precisely control different moiré superlattice structures in twisted structures and modulate their electronic properties for further development of functional devices.

16303820.label: Project Objectives
16303820.value: To construct a highly detailed phase diagram of the low temperature and high magnetic field region of bulk NbS2. To conduct a detailed examination of the unusual superconducting state we observed in preliminary experiments above the Pauli-limiting field in NbS2. To classify the unusual high magnetic field phase by searching for characteristic fingerprints of the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov(FFLO) phase or of Ising superconductivity. To conduct detailed experiments (e.g., field angle-resolved experiments and directional point contact spectroscopy) in high magnetic fields to investigate the nature of the superconducting order parameter, and to probe for the presence of the possible topological phases predicted for the Ising superconducting state in 2D materials. To search for similar phases above the Pauli limit in other superconducting bulk transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and if found, determine if these TMDs exhibit Ising superconductivity in their 2D form.

16303820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303820.value: A novel electronic state with so-called strong Ising spin-orbit coupling of the conduction electrons has recently been observed in 2D monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), in which the electrons spins are firmly pinned to an out-of-plane orientation [1]. Under superconducting conditions, this spin-confinement leads to the formation of a very unusual material state highly robust to magnetic fields applied parallel to TMD layers, and consequently to extremely enhanced critical fields far beyond the Pauli limit (i.e., the magnetic field limit, beyond which superconductivity is normally suppressed. In addition, the Ising spin-orbit coupling combined with the absence of inversion symmetry of the crystal lattice may give rise to an unconventional Ising superconducting state [2] comprising admixtures of spin-triplet superconductivity, nodal superconducting order parameters and even topological superconductivity [3]. The latter is a special superconducting state of great interest, which hosts so-called Majorana states at its edge. These special quasiparticle electronic states formed by the electronic wave functions are topologically protected by the bulk electrons. They posited to be important for future applications in topological quantum computation [4]. Topological qubits are more robust against decoherence and can take advantage of the exotic anionic exchange statistics of Majorana quasiparticles. Ising superconductivity is only known from 2D TMD materials, with this requirement for 2D geometry greatly limiting the experimental tools that can be used, and excluding the use of bulk thermodynamic probes. In a preliminary magnetic torque experiment, we found that the upper critical field for bulk 2H-NbS2 single crystals extends far beyond the Pauli limit, and displays a characteristic upturn of the upper critical field line at low temperatures. In the proposed research, we will investigate whether this unusual high-field superconducting state is associated with Ising superconductivity. An alternative explanation could be the equally interesting Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, in which Cooper pairs attain a finite center-off mass momentum [5,6], thereby leading to a pair-density wave state. We will use our sensitive specific heat, thermal expansion and magnetic torque techniques to study the high magnetic field phase diagram for field orientations exactly parallel to the layer structure, which will allow us to identify the nature of the unusual state. Field angle resolved experiments in combination with directional point contact spectroscopy will allow us to map the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter and identify topological superconducting phases. We will then extend the study to other bulk TMD superconductors, including 2H-NbSe2 and 2H-TaS2. 最近的研究在二維單層過渡金屬硫族化合物(transition metal dichalcogenides,TMDs) 中發現了一種嶄新的電子態──該態在強Ising自旋-軌道作用下電子的自旋被牢牢固定於與平面垂直的方向。由於電子的自旋被固定了，該特殊的超導態能抵抗與材料平面平行的強磁場，因而擁有遠高於Pauli極限（普通超導體的臨界磁場）的臨界磁場。此外，在Ising自旋-軌道作用與空間反演對稱性的破缺下，可能產生一種混合自旋三重態超導現象、nodal superconducting order parameters甚至拓樸超導現象的特殊Ising超導態。其中拓樸超導現象更為炙手可熱的研究課題。拓樸超導現象能產生馬約拉納態──該態為一種被塊體電子以拓樸保護的準粒子，並被預測將成為未來拓樸量子計算的基石：以馬約拉納準粒子建構的拓樸量子位元較非拓樸量子位元更能避免退相干現象；其非比尋常的 anionic exchange statistics亦能被運用於拓樸量子計算。理論上Ising超導現象只存在於二維TMD物料，其二維的要求硬性限制了我們能使用的實驗儀器，例如排除了使用大型熱動力探針的可能。在初步的磁矩實驗中，我們發現了2H-NbS2 單晶體塊體的上限臨界磁場遠高於Pauli極限，且顯示了低溫下上限臨界磁場線翻轉的特徵。在計劃的實驗中，我們會研究這特強磁場下的特殊超導態是否和Ising超導現象相關。 如非相關，該態可能為Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) 態──即庫柏對得到質心動量，因而成為一種pair-density wave state。我們會使用高敏感度的比熱、熱膨脹和磁矩技術來研究在與材料平面完全平行的強磁場下的相圖，從而判定這特殊超導態的本質。我們亦會利用拆解磁場方向的實驗，並結合指向性點接觸光譜學，找出超導序參數的對稱性以及判定拓樸超導相。其後我們會拓展研究至其他塊體TMD超導體，包括2H-NbSe2 和 2H-TaS2。

16303820.label: Realisation of objectives
16303820.value: Objectives 1 - 3: Unusual Superconducting Phase in NbS2 These objectives have been achieved and are detailed in our publication in Nature Communications [Nat Commun 12, 3676 (2021)]. Background: NbS2 is a layered transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) superconductor. Our preliminary experiments indicated that its upper critical field exceeds the Pauli limit for superconductivity when the magnetic field is applied parallel to the layers. Methods: We conducted a detailed investigation of its magnetic phase diagram using magnetic torque measurements at fixed temperatures as a function of applied field, and at constant fields as a function of temperature. We also performed specific heat and thermal expansion/magnetostriction experiments. For specific heat, we used an AC modulated temperature measurement with temperature modulation amplitudes of less than 1 mK, allowing measurements at a fixed base temperature of the thermal bath as a function of magnetic field. Findings: We focused on thermodynamic probes to provide bulk evidence for phase transformations in the superconducting phase and possible FFLO states. Precise field orientation with respect to the basal plane was required, so all measurement sensors were mounted on a low-temperature piezo rotating stage. We identified characteristic signatures of the FFLO phase: • Initial saturation of the upper critical field line near the Pauli limit at 10 T. • A characteristic upturn of the upper critical field line above the Pauli limit. • A phase transition line within the superconducting phase separating the low-field superconducting phase from the high-field FFLO phase at low temperatures. Results: We observed all these signatures. The upper critical field became almost flat near 10 T, indicating the approach of the Pauli limit. At lower temperatures, the upper critical field line rose again, forming the characteristic upturn known from other FFLO superconductors. This superconductivity above the Pauli limit suggests the formation of an exotic superconducting phase, likely the FFLO state rather than Ising superconductivity, which is typically found in ultrathin 2D samples but not in bulk 3D samples. Thermodynamic probes revealed a sharp spike-like phase transition anomaly near the Pauli limit at 10 T, reversible upon increasing and decreasing the field. This first-order phase transition confirmed the formation of an unusual superconducting phase above the Pauli limit. The anomaly was further confirmed by the field derivative of the magnetic torque and specific heat, thanks to the high resolution of our experimental techniques. The phase transition anomaly within the superconducting phase is expected for the FFLO scenario but not for the Ising scenario. Theoretical models for FFLO and Ising phases allowed us to fit the expected upper critical field lines. Only the FFLO phase formation could explain the pronounced upturn beyond the Pauli limit. A 1-degree misalignment of the magnetic field suppressed the FFLO phase entirely. Conclusion: Our experimental observations and theoretical modeling ruled out the Ising superconducting scenario in favor of the FFLO scenario. A peculiarity observed was a relatively small initial slope of the upper critical field lines in low fields near the critical temperature, indicating a strong orbital effect in this superconductor. Objectives 4: FFLO Phase in NbSe2 This objective has been achieved. After publishing our results on NbS2, we focused on another FFLO phase in 3D bulk samples of NbSe2. Detailed experiments, including field angle-resolved and directional point contact experiments, revealed the characteristic 6-fold rotational symmetry expected for the orbital FFLO state, which vanished in the low-field ordinary superconducting phase. These results are under review in Nature Communications [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2312.03215]. We also performed point contact spectroscopy in the FFLO state of NbS2 and NbSe2 to look for changes in the Andreev reflection spectra when entering the FFLO phase. This required a dedicated scanning probe, which became available towards the end of the reporting period. Promising results have been achieved, and this work is ongoing. Objectives 5: Identification of New FFLO Superconductors This objective has been achieved in detail. We identified three new FFLO superconductors in this research project, significantly increasing the number of known FFLO superconducting compounds. Summary: We investigated three different TMD superconductors (NbS2, NbSe2, and TaS2) and found FFLO states in two of them. Detailed magnetic torque experiments on NbSe2 revealed that the upper critical field approached but did not reach the Pauli limit. We compared NbS2 and NbSe2, publishing an article in New Journal of Physics [https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/ac8114] explaining the differences through the weaker out-of-plane anisotropy of NbSe2. A publication by another group reported an orbital FFLO state in very thin NbSe2 layers, stimulating us to reinvestigate our data. We found similar anomalies in DC magnetization experiments, indicating the formation of an unusual superconducting phase in perfectly parallel fields. Collaboration with theorist Noah F. Q. Yuan confirmed the existence of an orbital FFLO phase in bulk NbSe2, currently under review in Nature Communications [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2312.03215]. Additionally, we extended our investigation to Ti4Ir2O, discovering an FFLO state in an isotropic 3D superconductor, with the report under review in Cell Reports Physical Sciences [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2312.01914]. Conclusion: We successfully identified three new FFLO superconductors, demonstrating the success of this research project.

16303820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303820.value: This research project focused on investigating the unusual superconducting phases in NbS2 and NbSe2, two layered transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) superconductors, and led to the identification of a total of three new FFLO superconductors. Our investigation into NbS2 revealed that its upper critical field exceeds the Pauli limit for superconductivity when the magnetic field is applied strictly parallel to the layers. Using magnetic torque, specific heat, and thermal expansion/magnetostriction measurements, we constructed a detailed magnetic phase diagram. We observed characteristic signatures of the FFLO phase, including the initial saturation and subsequent upturn of the upper critical field line above the Pauli limit, and a phase transition line within the superconducting phase. These findings were confirmed through high-resolution thermodynamic probes, which provided bulk evidence for the phase transformations. Theoretical modeling ruled out the Ising superconducting scenario, supporting the formation of the FFLO phase in NbS2. Following our publication on NbS2, we focused on NbSe2 and discovered another FFLO phase. Detailed experiments, including field angle-resolved and directional point contact spectroscopy, revealed the characteristic 6-fold rotational symmetry of the orbital FFLO state in 3D bulk samples. These results, currently under review in Nature Communications, highlight the presence of an orbital FFLO phase in NbSe2. Additionally, point contact spectroscopy in the FFLO state of NbS2 and NbSe2 showed promising results, with ongoing work to further explore these findings. We identified three new FFLO superconductors: NbS2, NbSe2, and Ti4Ir2O. Our comparative study of NbS2 and NbSe2, published in New Journal of Physics, explained the differences in their superconducting behavior through the weaker out-of-plane anisotropy of NbSe2. Collaboration with theorist Noah F. Q. Yuan confirmed the existence of an orbital FFLO phase in bulk NbSe2, with findings under review in Nature Communications. Additionally, our investigation of Ti4Ir2O led to the discovery of an FFLO state in an isotropic 3D superconductor, with the report under review in Cell Reports Physical Sciences. This research project successfully identified three new FFLO superconductors, significantly contributing to the understanding of superconducting phases in TMD materials. The findings demonstrate the project's success and provide a foundation for future research into exotic superconducting states.

16303820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303820.value: To further substantiate the existence of the FFLO state in NbSe2, NbS2 and Ti4Ir2O, we propose conducting experiments sensitive to the spatial modulation of the order parameter. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) has been successfully employed to demonstrate the inhomogeneity of the superconducting state in the FFLO phase. Additionally, anisotropic sound velocity and attenuation experiments have shown the stripe-like spatial modulation of the order parameter in real space. Implementing these techniques on NbSe2, NbS2 and Ti4Ir2O will provide more robust evidence for the FFLO state by confirming the spatial modulation of the order parameter. Moreover, we plan to complete more detailed experiments using our newly developed scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) setup. This setup is specifically designed to visualize the FFLO state by scanning the tip across the surface perpendicular to the field applied parallel to the basal plane. We anticipate observing a periodic opening and closing of the superconducting gap, which is not possible with conventional STM setups where the tip is parallel to the applied field. This innovative approach will allow us to directly observe the spatial modulation of the superconducting order parameter, providing critical insights into the FFLO state.

16303820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303820.value: Our research focused on understanding a special type of superconductivity called the FFLO (Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov) state. This state is technologically significant because it can exist in high magnetic fields, useful for developing advanced magnetic and electronic devices, such as high-field electromagnets in magnetic resonance imaging machines, particle accelerators, and future nuclear fusion reactors. We studied two materials, NbS2 and NbSe2, which are layered transition metal dichalcogenides. These materials can become superconductors, meaning they conduct electricity without resistance under certain conditions. Our experiments showed that when a magnetic field is applied in a specific way, these materials exhibit unusual superconducting behavior beyond known limits. In NbS2, we discovered that its superconducting state remains stable even in very strong magnetic fields, which is uncommon for most superconductors. We used various techniques to confirm this behavior, providing strong evidence for the FFLO state. In NbSe2, we found a similar FFLO state and used advanced imaging techniques to visualize it. Additionally, we observed an FFLO state in an isotropic material, Ti4Ir2O, which can conduct stronger electrical currents, crucial for superconducting high-field electromagnets. Overall, our research identified three new FFLO superconductors, significantly advancing our understanding of these exotic states and their potential applications.

16304020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304020.value: Light has internal degrees of freedom, including polarization and orbital angular momentum in addition to propagating direction. There is currently a great deal of interest in exploiting these internal degrees of freedom to increase data capacity in optical fiber and free-space communication, and we expect the same benefits to apply to information processing. In the proposed project, we will combine the capability of wavefront control and coherent control from a single layer of nanostructures, termed as a metasurface, to perform an arbitrary unitary transformation, which is the natural framework in carrying out information processing using interference as the driving mechanism. Such a framework will be useful for both classical and quantum optical fields. In both cases, the scaling up of the complexity of the unitary transformation is usually based on the theorem that any large but finite unitary matrices can be factorized into 2x2 matrices, giving rise to implementation by cascading small optical elements, such as beam splitters and mirrors. Recently, metasurfaces have been proved and demonstrated to generate complex wavefronts with the finest detail. Distinct wavefronts can even be multiplexed with the different internal degrees of freedom of the excitation light. We envision that metasurfaces can be a very generic and compact platform to carry out unitary transformations with all of the previous complexity of scaling up using smaller elements now replaced by a single interface. In pursuing such a compact and unitary approach, we will use dielectric or low-loss metasurfaces, the scattering matrices of which are unitary. The unitarity of the scattering matrix also suggests that the beam does not need to come from a single direction. Rather, the excitation can come coherently from different directions and with different polarizations or orbital angular momenta. Specifically, we will design metasurfaces that can be tailor-made to cover different possible SU(n) matrices using the metasurface as an interference medium. The designed metasurfaces will be fabricated and their unitary matrix elements will be experimentally characterized through transmission and reflection measurements. We will also investigate new kinds of Hong-Ou-Mandel (quantum interference) effects supported by more than one qubit in such metasurfaces in the quantum optical regime, in which only a few photons are allowed to interact with the metasurface. All of these investigations will further expand the applications of metasurfaces in the broader context of information processing. 光具有內部自由度，除了傳播方向外，還包括偏振和軌道角動量。目前，利用這些內部自由度來增加光纖和自由空間通信中的數據容量引起了極大的研究興趣，我們希望將這些內部自由度同樣應用於信息處理上。在本項目中，我們將單層納米結構（超表面）的波前控制能力和相干控制能力相結合，從而執行任意形式的么正變換，以構建一個利用相干性進行信息處理的自然框架。該框架對於經典光學和量子光學領域都同樣有效。一般而言，么正變換的複雜度的增加通常遵從以下定理：任意有限大的么正矩陣都可以分解為多個2x2的矩陣，這些矩陣可以通過串聯多個小型光學元件（如分束器、反射鏡）來實現。這樣並不利於擴大系統規模。最近幾年，關於超表面的經典光學實驗已經證明了超表面能夠儲存大量有意義的信息並產生極其精細的波前控制。不同偏振和軌道角動量的入射光作用在超表面上甚至可以激發出不同的波前或全息圖。這使得超表面可以作為一個非常通用且小巧的平台，因此那些用多個光學原件串聯才可以實現的複雜的么正變換就可以用一個超表面代替。在追求這種小巧統一的方法時，我們將使用介電或低損耗的超表面，從而使得其散射矩陣接近么正變換。同時我們也將研究用不同方向、不同偏振和不同軌道角動量的光束來激發超表面，這種不同自由度的相干性可以增加么正變換的複雜程度。我們將設計和製造合適的超表面作為相干介質，量身定制以覆蓋不同的SU(n)矩陣，並通過測量透射和反射譜來對它們所代表的么正變換進行實驗表徵。我們還將研究在量子光學狀態下這種擁有多重自由度的超表面能否支持更為廣義的Hong-Ou-Mandel（量子干涉）效應，其中多於一個或者數個光子與超表面相互作用。這些研究將進一步擴展超表面在信息處理更廣泛範圍內的應用。

16304020.label: Realisation of objectives
16304020.value: 1. We have developed a theory using path degrees of freedom to carry out SU(2) transformations with two input and two output paths, employing appropriately designed metasurfaces to control transmission and reflection from both forward and backward normal incidence. Metasurfaces are therefore, in principle, capable of implementing unitary transformations. We begin with 2x2 matrix transformations for simplicity. In the later part of the project, we further extend the concept of using metasurfaces to implement more general unitary matrix transformations with higher dimensions. Objective 1 is fully implemented as the foundation for other objectives, from design to theory development and experimental realizations. 2. By considering only the transmission of metasurfaces but generalizing the input paths to a meta-lens array and the output paths to multiple diffraction directions in transmission, we have formulated how such a meta-lens array can implement a unitary transmission with a unitary matrix larger than 2x2. In particular, we have considered unitary transformations for two qubits, corresponding to implementing SU(4) transformations. Some notable 4x4 unitary matrices considered include those corresponding to the quantum Fourier transform and Grover's search algorithm for two qubits. Objective 2 is fully implemented. 3. Based on the design of the last objective, Focused Ion Beam lithography has been used to fabricate the metasurfaces, a meta-lens array made of nano-slots with varying orientation profiles on a silver-coated glass substrate. An experimental setup has been established to carry out the unitary transformation through the metasurface. We have adopted single-photon cameras to record the results using single photons. Objective 3 is fully implemented. 4. Based on the setup and design principles of metasurfaces in the last objective, we have used entangled photon source pairs to construct a hybrid entangled state between polarization and orbital angular momentum, proving that one photon in the heralding arm can be used to control the orbital angular momentum in the signal arm. Objective 4 is largely implemented, though more general transformations of the orbital angular momentum are still possible. 5. We have developed a method for using metasurfaces as a general medium to control two-photon interference, with the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) effect being a special case of destructive interference. This is achievable through model development linking the Jones matrix at each location of the metasurface with two-photon interference. Objective 5 is fully implemented. In carrying out the experiments to prove the designed unitary transformations and the two-photon interference, we found that it would be appropriate to work in the low light regime where photons can be counted one by one. To achieve this, in addition to the single-photon camera we have, we need two additional single-photon detectors and the associated correlator to help conduct the experiments, resulting in an overbudget on the equipment expenditure.

16304020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304020.value: 1. We have developed a framework for implementing SU(2) transformations using metasurfaces, Opt. Exp. 29 (2021), as preliminary work, to unitary transformations of larger dimensions, e.g., 4x4, using a meta-lens array that transforms an input state falling on different meta-lenses to an output state scattering in different directions. With this design scheme for using metasurfaces to carry out unitary transformations, we have demonstrated quantum algorithms for up to two qubits, corresponding to SU(4) transformations. The work is now published in Nanophotonics (2024). It constitutes an early experimental demonstration of using metasurfaces to perform quantum algorithms. Our metasurface has totally 9 lenses, while a spatial light modulator can choose different sets of four lenses to have programmable control in carrying out different two-qubit operations. 2. Quantum interference is a new resource for metasurface applications. We formulated a theoretical framework for quantum optical scattering from a lossy metasurface and proved that with appropriate design, two-photon quantum interference can occur for the single-photon output state on only one side of the metasurface (with one photon absorbed) when two photons arrive at the metasurface simultaneously. These are published in Physical Review A. We used forward and backward propagation as the path degrees of freedom. Next, we considered a more practical implementation of realizing two-photon interference by using different locations as the input path degrees of freedom and different polarizations as the output degrees of freedom for transmission across the metasurface. We have experimentally demonstrated polarization HOM-type interference using metasurfaces, either to create tailor-made coincidence images or to reveal information about the Jones matrix profile of the metasurface. These works are published in iScience (2022) and Nanophotonics (2023) and can be useful for developing quantum imaging schemes based on photon coincidence signals. 3. Using polarization-entangled photon pairs, we can send one photon through the metasurface while directing the other photon of the pair to a polarization analyzer to construct a hybrid-entangled state between polarization and the transmitted wavefront of the metasurface. This allows us to construct a hybrid entangled state between polarization and orbital angular momentum (OAM) generated by the metasurface. We have demonstrated a continuous heralding effect, using polarization in one arm to control the OAM in the other arm, indicating possible applications of metasurfaces for quantum information transformation (Communications Physics, 2023). Some initial attempts to generalize the heralding control from polarization to more sophisticated wavefronts, such as holograms (Advanced Photonics Nexus, 2024).

16304020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304020.value: While we have demonstrated small-scale unitary transformations of optical states using metasurfaces, further optimization of the metasurface designs is necessary to scale up the implementation to larger matrices. This is crucial for bridging to practical applications. Optimizations can include a smarter choice of the permutation of the lenses, the design of nanostructures, and the adoption of dielectric metasurfaces. Our metasurface implementation is not limited to unitary transformations but extends to more general types of matrix-vector multiplication. For example, this platform can be used for more general optical computations, such as implementing neural networks. The parallel fashion of calculation can also be used as a simulation device, for instance, to simulate a quantum open system. These lead to new application scenarios of our results.

16304020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304020.value: Recent advancements in metasurfaces point to new applications for information processing in the quantum optical realm. Our project targets the use of metasurfaces as a compact platform for unitary transformations, which are essential for quantum operations, from computation to more general state transformations. By exploiting the different path and polarization degrees of freedom for waves interacting with a metasurface, we have successfully demonstrated how metasurfaces can implement SU(2) to SU(4) operations, equating to single and two-qubit operations using both classical and quantum light. In the quantum optical regime, quantum interference becomes a new resource for computation. We have experimentally demonstrated two-photon polarization interference using metasurfaces to create tailor-made coincidence images and reveal information about the Jones matrix profile of the metasurface, leading to novel quantum imaging schemes. Metasurfaces add a new candidate for developing larger-scale quantum computation, as they effectively replace several conventional bulky optical elements with a single surface. Additionally, they can be used for generating quantum optical states and enhancing quantum imaging applications. This compact, versatile platform opens up new possibilities for more efficient and scalable quantum technologies.

16304220.label: Project Objectives
16304220.value: Further strengthen the convergence regularity results of the Kahler-Ricci flow on compact Kahler manifolds with semi-ample canonical line bundle. Extend the existing singularity analysis results about the Kahler-Ricci flow on projective bundles to a wider class of holomorphic fibrations and with less restrictive symmetry assumptions.
rows: Further strengthen the convergence regularity results of the Kahler-Ricci flow on compact Kahler manifolds with semi-ample canonical line bundle.
Extend the existing singularity analysis results about the Kahler-Ricci flow on projective bundles to a wider class of holomorphic fibrations and with less restrictive symmetry assumptions.

16304220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304220.value: The project aims at refining and strengthening the higher-order regularity results of convergence of the Kahler-Ricci flow when the fibration structure collapses. When the canonical bundle is semi-ample, the Kahler-Ricci flow has long-time solutions. Over the years, steady progress has been made by many authors including the PI to understand better the convergence regularity of the flow. It has been a conjecture that the flow would converge in smooth topology away from singular fibers to its limit, which is obtained by collapsing of fibers. As of today, the conjecture is proven only when the generic fibers are complex tori. One major goal of this project is to further strengthen this result to other types of holomorphic fibrations. Another focus of the project is the study of Kahler-Ricci flow with finite-time singularity on some specific holomorphic fibrations, such as a holomorphic submersion which is horizontally conformal. It includes the case of CP^1 bundles over CP^{n-1} studied by the PI and other authors when the metric has U(n) symmetry. The PI aims at generalizing these results to those holomorphic submersions which are horizontally conformal. 這個項目旨在研習凱勒-瑞奇流在體積極限為零時的高階估算作更深入和強化的分析。當一個凱勒流形的基本束 (canonical bundle) 為非負 (semi-ample)的時候，該流形富有纖維結構。在瑞奇流下，這些纖維結構會塌成一個基流形 (base manifold)。在這個情況下，専家猜想凱勒-瑞奇流會光滑的收斂至基流形。這個猜想除了在纖維為環面的特例之外，至今仍未解決。這個項目我們會針對這個猜想作深入研究。

16304220.label: Realisation of objectives
16304220.value: Objective 1 has been successfully addressed in the paper "Higher-order estimates of long-time solutions to the Kähler-Ricci flow" published in J. Funct. Anal, in which we proved the higher-order regularity problem in the proposal when the regular fibers are biholomorphic. It is worthwhile to note that the full generality of the problem has been recently announced by Hein, Lee, and Tosatti. I have guided my former undergraduate advisee Nguyen The Hoan (now studying PhD in U of Chicago) to think about problems related to Objective 2. He was able to come up with some fruitful results (announced in https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.13065) that address Objective 2 stated in the proposal. The work provided another proof of my former work published in Tran. Amer. Math. Soc. which proves the Type I singularity of the Kahler-Ricci flow under Calabi's symmetry. His results prompted the PI to consider further questions about the proposed problem under Dancer-Wang's cohomogenity-1 ansatz. In the study of Dancer-Wang's cohomogenity-1 ansatz which involves the understanding of homogeneous spaces, the PI was able to generalize some former works on self-similar solutions, leading to a new preprint (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08198).

16304220.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304220.value: We proved that the Kahler-Ricci flow on manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle and biholomorphic fibers converges smoothly away from singularity. The PI also guided an undergraduate to prove that my former work on Kahler-Ricci flow on projective bundles can be reformulated and reproved using conformal submersion setting, leading to further investigation on the Kahler-Ricci flow under Dancer-Wang cohomogeneity-one ansatz. The study of the former work also allows the PI to generalize former works about self-similar solutions to non-Euclidean wrapped product spaces.

16304220.value: Based on the experience gained from addressing Objective 2, the PI will launch a new project studying the Kahler-Ricci flow under Dancer-Wang cohomogeneity-one ansatz.

16304220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304220.value: In this completed project, the PI and his collaborators substantially improve the convergence regularity of the long-time solutions of the Kahler-Ricci flow. The methodology used is in the interface of differential geometry and partial differential equations. We believe the work is of interest by experts in both areas. The study of Kahler-Ricci flow on conformal submersions also prompt the PI to launch another project on the Ricci flow on Dancer-Wang's ansatz in the near future.

16304520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304520.value: Over the past decade, the field of non-Hermitian photonics based on parity-time (PT) symmetry has led to many innovative techniques for creating, manipulating, and detecting light, such as PT-symmetric lasers and absorbers, optical isolators, and etc. Non-Hermitian optics not only contributes to the design of new photonics devices, it also deepens our understanding of fundamental quantum physics due to their mathematical equivalence. Existing photonic systems realize PT by engineering material loss and gain. In the proposed project, we will experimentally investigate non-Hermitian nonlinear optics based on four-wave mixing (FWM) process in cold atoms. The proposed new system will not only allow gain and loss manipulation, but will also examine how phase mismatching provides a method for manipulating non-Hermitian properties. We will demonstrate PT and anti-PT symmetric FWMs in both classical and quantum regimes. Specifically, we will realize anti-PT symmetric quantum optics without gain and loss by manipulating the phase mismatching condition in the forward-wave configuration. In the backward-wave configuration, the system will switch to PT symmetry and we will study the phase transition. The proposed project will lead to a new type of non-Hermitian optics, which will have new applications in nonlinear optics. 在過去的十年中，基於宇稱-時間（PT）對稱性的非厄密光子學在製備，調控和測量光學上帶來了許多技術創新，例如PT對稱性激光和吸收體，光學隔離器等。非厄密光學不僅有助於發展設計新型光學器件，而且由於其數學形式的等價性，也加深了我們對基本量子物理學的理解。現有的光學系統是通過控制材料的損耗和增益來實現PT對稱性的。在本項目中，我們將通過實驗研究冷原子中基於四波混頻（FWM）的非厄密非線性光學。我們的新系統不僅將允許進行增益和損耗控制，還將提供利用相位失配來操縱非厄米特性的新方法。我們將在系統的經典和量子區間分別演示PT和反PT對稱四波混頻。具體來說，我們將通過控制前向波配置中的相位失配條件，實現無增益和無損耗的反PT對稱量子光學。在背向波配置中，系統將切換為PT對稱性，我們將研究其中的相變問題。本項目所研究的新型非厄密光學將在非線性光學中有新的應用。

16304520.label: Realisation of objectives
16304520.value: 1. Our preliminary work shows four-wave mixing in the forward wave propagation can be used to construct non-Hermitian exceptional point, in which the anti-PT-phase transition has been demonstrated by scanning across one system parameter for a cold-atom system. This has brought us to the next step to explore non-Hermitian physics when there are two system parameters we can tune for a cold-atom system. Still using a 2x2 Hamiltonian picture, we have then demonstrated chiral spin transfer of the quantum state when the system parameters encircle the exceptional point in a parameter space consisting of two tunable parameters. We have further developed a quantum state control scheme based on such exceptional point. Objective 1 is accomplished by exploring non-Hermitian exceptional point for a cold-atom system. 2. Regarding Objective 2, we are interested in the further usage of a non-Hermitian exceptional point for quantum sensing at the phase-matching condition for the nonlinear wave-mixing process. In this case, two nonlinear media with wave-mixing replace two beam splitters in a conventional Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Specifically, we have investigated how such quantum interferometer, being called a SU(1,1) interferometer, can be used as a quantum sensor at an exceptional point and being perturbed by an additional propagation phase to sense. This broadens the operational regime of the quantum interferometer. The exceptional point is about the input-output relationship matrix for a finite system, generalizing from the bulk Hamiltonian in Objective 1. Objective 2 is fully implemented. 3. We have investigated how quantum photon states interact with an optical system equipped with a non-Hermitian exceptional point. By using a metasurface as example, we have shown that two-photon interference can be designed to occur only for the single-photon output state towards one side but not the other when two identical photons (generated from spontaneous wave-mixing) enter both sides of the metasurface. Such consideration of non-Hermitian metasurface provides more degrees of freedom in entangled or quantum photon states generation. Objective 3 is accomplished.

16304520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304520.value: 1. We have demonstrated non-Hermitian exceptional point (EP) using cold-atom systems. It started with the discovery of the anti-PT symmetry possibly embedded in a well-designed nonlinear system with four-wave mixing [Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 193604 (2019)]. The 2x2 Hamiltonian associated to the Stokes and anti-Stokes field along the forward propagation direction can exhibit an EP, degeneracy in both eigenvalue (propagation constant) and eigenvector, in which the phase mismatch Δk is in the same order of the nonlinear coupling coefficient. A phase transition occurs when the nonlinear coupling coefficient is scanned through such threshold by varying the atomic density of the laser-cooled 85Rb atoms. Furthermore, based on laser-cooled 173Yb atoms, we have extended the number of tunable system parameters to two, including tuning the quasimomentum and the atom loss. We have demonstrated the EP, eigenvalue and eigenvector degeneracy for the complex energy band diagram. In addition to phase transition, as the EP is in a two-parameter space, a chiral behavior of spin transfer is further demonstrated. The resultant spin of the system depends on the encircling direction around the EP [Nature Physics (2022)]. We have then developed these phenomena into a quantum state control scheme [Phys. Rev. A 109 (2024)]. 2. From above, since the wave mixing in nonlinear medium can now be used to establish an EP, we further demonstrate its usage for wave mixing by two cascaded parametric amplifiers (nonlinear media), as an extension of a quantum SU(1,1) interferometer, that can previously work around a diabolical point (only eigenvalue being degenerate), but now to an EP of the input-output relationship matrix. We have shown that such an EP is linked to both high signal and low noise, hence also applicable for achieving quantum sensing applications. The result is published in New Journal of Physics (2023). 3. We have investigated how quantum optical states interact with a metasurface equipped with an EP. We start from setting up the theoretical and design schemes to obtain unitary operation [Optics Express in 2021] to metasurface with non-unitary action to capture an EP in its scattering matrix so that when two indistinguishable photons shining on the metasurface from both sides, quantum interference only occurs for the single-photon output state towards one side but not the other [Phys. Rev. A 104 (2021); Phys. Rev. A 106 (2022)]. These results are potential for entangled state and quantum optical states generation.

16304520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304520.value: The project mainly observes non-Hermitian physics related to exceptional points in nonlinear optics and quantum systems. All the above are actually investigating exceptional point of the semi-classical response matrix of the system, although the system itself can be quantum in nature. We now know there is an interesting class of quantum exceptional point, called purely quantum Liouvillian exceptional point which only exists in the quantum mechanical level but not the semi-classical level of the response matrix (Hamiltonian/propagation matrix/scattering matrix). We have recently some preliminary results in realizing such purely quantum Liouvillian exceptional point (qLEP) in a quantum computer (SPINQ) based on nuclear magnetic resonance. It is based on performing a simulation of quantum open systems through both signal and ancilla qubits. We are designing metasurface that can perform such simulation of quantum open systems to capture qLEP as well. These directions will be potential for us to explore non-Hermitian physics of quantum systems and to develop a new project for developing schemes in simulating quantum open systems.

16304520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304520.value: The recent realizations of parity-time (PT) symmetric systems in the realm of non-Hermitian photonics in the last decade has enabled many counter-intuitive applications such as PT-symmetric lasers and absorbers, exceptional point (EP) sensing and non-reciprocal wave control. As PT symmetry consideration was originally proposed as extension to conventional quantum mechanics, an interesting question is whether these non-Hermitian physics can be brought to the quantum mechanical systems. In this project, we have used laser-cooled atoms in a magnetic-optical trap to construct non-Hermitian EP by two routes: wave-mixing in lossless nonlinear media through anti-PT symmetry and adding atom loss in cold-atoms with Raman-coupling through PT-symmetry. We have also extended to using metasurfaces to construct the EPs. We have demonstrated PT/anti-PT phase transition across and also chiral transfer encircling an EP as experimental evidence of the non-Hermitian physics of both classical nonlinear optics and quantum state manipulation. While EP is a mathematical entity in which both eigenvalues and eigenvectors become degenerate with a defective system response matrix, the theory and experimental results in quantum systems investigated in this project will lead to new schemes in quantum sensing, quantum photon states or entangled states generation, and quantum state manipulation as applications.
