16304620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304620.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study time-symmetry breaking in coupled parametric micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators in science and technology applications ranging from inertial sensing to high stability frequency standards. When system parameters such as the mass or spring constant are strongly modulated near twice the resonant frequency, vibrations are excited at half the frequency of modulation. The phase of oscillation can take on either one of two values that differ by pi. This bistable nature of parametric oscillators has been exploited for classical and quantum computation. They have also been considered as Ising spins, with the two vibrational phases corresponding to up and down states respectively. Systems of coupled Ising spins can be constructed to solve complex optimization problems. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the imperfect mapping of the bistable vibrational states in parametric oscillators to Ising spins. In particular, the rate of fluctuation-induced phase switch cannot be obtained from a simple extension of the Kramers approach that is based on free energy for systems in equilibrium. Coupling of the two parametric oscillators modifies the switching rate of each unit. Preliminary calculations and measurements indicate that the change of the switching rates of two resonators are not identical. Such non-reciprocal behavior and the lack of detailed balance have no counterpart in conventional Ising spin systems. Proposed experiments will seek to elucidate the origin of this difference and explore how it affects the use of parametric oscillators for computation. In addition, the project will explore geometrical frustration by placing three coupled parametric oscillators in a triangular lattice. Successful implementation of the proposed project will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but will also lead to new ways of using parametric oscillators for computation and sensing. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. His group performed an extensive investigation of the scaling behavior of the rate for phase switching in a micromechanical resonator driven into parametric resonance. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors in the phase switching when multiple parametric oscillators are coupled together. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究耦合參數微機械諧振器中的時間對稱破壞。微機電諧振器被廣泛應用於從慣性傳感到高穩定度頻率標準的科學技術應用上。當質量或彈簧常數等系統參數在共振頻率的兩倍附近被強烈調製時，諧振器就會產生頻率為調製頻率一半的振動。振蕩的相位是相差pi的兩個值之一。參數振盪器的這種雙穩態性質已被用於經典和量子計算。這種現像也可以被認為類似於伊辛自旋，其中的兩個振動相位分別對應於向上和向下方向的自旋。耦合的伊辛自旋系統可以用來解決複雜的優化問題。 提案中研究的重點在於揭示參量振盪器中雙穩定振動態到伊辛自旋的不完美映射。具體來說，由波動引起的相位切換速率不能由基于平衡態中自由能的克莱默斯方法進行簡單延申而獲得。兩個參數諧振器的耦合改變了每個單元的切換速率。初步的計算和測量表明兩個諧振器的切換速率改變並不完全相同。這樣非交互的行為和缺乏細緻平衡性是與傳統的伊辛系統沒有相對應的。計劃的實驗將尋求並解釋這種差異的來源並且探索這樣的差異如何影響參數諧振器在計算中的應用。此外，本課題會通過將三個耦合的參數諧振器放置為三角形陣列，進而研究這樣的幾何不穩定性。該計劃課題的成功實施將不僅能夠推動新的理論研究和驗證多種理論方法的合理性，而且會引領運用參數振盪器來計算和傳感的新方法。 主要研究者在微機械器件的波動現象這一領域有豐富的經驗。他的團隊對驅動到參數諧振的微機械諧振器中相位切換速率的比例行為進行了廣泛的研究。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的理論物理學家Mark Dykman教授緊密合作，揭示出參數振盪器耦合時的相位切換的新現象。

16304620.label: Realisation of objectives
16304620.value: During the reporting period, we carried out an investigation of time-symmetry breaking in two coupled parametric micromechanical oscillators. We achieved the project objectives of demonstrating tunable coupling between two micromechanical parametric oscillators that leads to anti-correlated vibration phases, revealing the non-reciprocal change in the rates of fluctuation-induced phase switching due to coupling, and exploring the breaking of detailed balance in the fluctuation-induced switching in weakly coupled parametric oscillators. The outcome of our research includes one paper and four invited presentations at international conferences. A PG student was trained. The student has completed his PhD degree and is now a faculty member in a university. To achieve the project objectives, we designed and fabricated two micromechanical torsional resonators with tunable coupling between them. Each unit consists of a 200 um-square movable silicon plate supported by two torsional springs. There are electrodes located underneath the silicon plate, so that the spring constant can be electrostatically modulated by ac voltages near twice the resonance frequency. Oscillations emerge at half the drive frequency when the modulation is sufficiently strong. The phase of these oscillations takes on one of two values differing by pi, breaking the time symmetry imposed by the modulation. Such bistability of parametric oscillators has been used in both classical and quantum computation. They have also been proposed to serve as building blocks of Ising machines that can solve complex optimization problems, where the two out-of-phase oscillation states represent the up and down spins states in the Ising model. We demonstrate tunable coupling between the oscillators by applying a dc potential difference between the two movable plates so that they attract each other electrostatically. Noise is applied so that each resonator can occasionally overcome the activation barrier and switch between the coexisting stable states. When coupling between the two units is turned off, we verify that the switching rates out of the two states are identical in each resonator, which is a consequence of the symmetry. After we turn on the coupling, the switching rate of one resonator is enhanced or diminished if the phase of the other unit is identical or opposite, respectively. We find that if the eigenfrequencies of the two resonators are almost identical, the switching rates of the two units are changed due to the coupling by almost the same factor, similar to symmetric Ising spins in thermal equilibrium. The system shows detailed balance. In contrast, if the eigenfrequencies are tuned to be different, the switching rates of the two units change by different factors, resembling two Ising spins with asymmetric interactions. The difference of the eigenfrequencies is a simple and important example of disorder in the oscillator system. We show that the disorder leads to the onset of a probability current that circulates in the stationary state. Detailed balance is broken. The probability flux of a switching process and the reverse process is no longer equal to each other. There is a preferred direction for the system to evolve. We find that the probability current depends on the mismatch in frequency of the two oscillators. The main problem encountered and solved include the necessity for close loop control of the resonance frequencies of the two oscillators to compensate for long term drifts. The measurement of switching rates requires continuous measurement over months. We developed a scheme to control the resonance frequencies via the electrostatic spring effect of the dc voltages to keep the amplitude of the parametric resonance constant.

16304620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304620.value: 1. We find that when two micromechanical parametric oscillators with different eigenfrequencies are weakly coupled, the effect of the coupling on the rate of switching out of an oscillation state is asymmetric. The change of the activation barrier of the first oscillator is not equal to that of the second oscillator. As a result, the two oscillators map onto two asymmetric Ising spins. Such asymmetry cannot be achieved in equilibrium systems characterized by a Hamiltonian. If the two eigenfrequencies are tuned to be identical, the change of the activation barriers due to coupling are identical and the system maps to the conventional symmetric Ising model. 2. We show that the asymmetric changes in the switching rates can be understood in terms of the change of the activation barrier of a single, isolated oscillator subjected to an additive periodic drive at half the frequency of parametric modulation. The extra drive plays the role of an external magnetic field on an Ising spin. We characterize the dependence of the change of the switching rate on the amplitude of the symmetry breaking drive by the concept of logarithmic susceptibility. When an oscillator is coupled to another oscillator, vibrations of the latter generate a period force at half the frequency of parametric modulation in a manner similar to the extra drive. 3. We find that the asymmetric changes of the switching rates break the detail balance in fluctuation induced switching. For a system with detailed balance, the probability flux of a process and the reverse process should be equal to each other. Such symmetry is broken in our system, giving rise to a persistent probability current that circulates in state space. Remarkably, there is a preferred direction for the system to evolve. The probability current is found to be proportional to the frequency mismatch between the two oscillators. The outcome of our research includes one paper published in Physics Review Research and 4 invited presentations at conferences. A PG student was trained. The student has completed his PhD degree and is now a faculty member in a university.

16304620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304620.value: While this project demonstrated the mapping of two coupled parametric oscillators onto two asymmetric Ising spins, the concept can be extended to three or more oscillators to implement complex asymmetric Ising networks that play a crucial role in neural networks. Parametric oscillators represent the simplest non-equilibrium bistable system that can act as a building block for both symmetric and asymmetric Ising models. To make further progress, it is necessary to fabricate the oscillator arrays and scale up the measurement apparatus so that individual units can be excited and detected simultaneously.

16304620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304620.value: In this research project, a micromechanical parametric oscillator with two coexisting vibration states of opposite phase is regarded as an Ising spin which, in simplified terms, can be used to model a neuron firing or not firing. So far, neural networks are only implemented using computer. To our knowledge, neural networks have not been built using inorganic physical components aside from computer simulations. The main hurdle is that the interactions between neurons in the brain are believed to be asymmetric: the effect of a first neuron on the second neuron is different from that of the second on the first. While symmetric Ising models can be implemented using bistable components in thermal equilibrium, asymmetric Ising models require special bistable components that are out of equilibrium. We have demonstrated, for the first time, that two parametric oscillators can be designed to exhibit asymmetric interactions and can therefore serve as a component to fulfil this requirement.

16305320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305320.value: Conjugated polyelectrolytes (CPEs) are an emerging class of advanced functional polymers with π-conjugated backbones and ionizable moieties. These polymers have many intrinsic advantages including high conductivity, excellent charge-transporting ability, water solubility and processability, amphiphilic aggregation characteristics and ionic interactions with chemo/bio-analytes. Due to these unique features, CPEs provide an extensive platform for numerous practical applications, ranging from chemo/bio-sensing and biological imaging and therapy, to light-emitting diodes and photovoltaic devices. CPEs with ionic side chains, synthesized mainly by post-polymerization processes, have been developed and widely studied. These studies have been limited, however, by the difficulties associated with the synthesis of these polymers and by their lack of structural variation. In this context, the development of new and effective strategies for the simple synthesis of conjugated polyelectrolytes CPEs with well-defined structures is of great significance. Our research group has been exploring novel alkyne-based polymerization routes for many years. In contrast to traditional olefinic polymerizations, these acetylenic polymerizations yield a variety of polymers with various unsaturated units populating their backbones, including double and triple bonds, fused rings and heterocycles. Due to their π-conjugated electronic structures, these synthesized acetylenic polymers have been endowed with distinctive photophysical and optoelectronic properties. The migration of delocalized electrons along acetylenic polymer backbones has been shown to result in the amplification of fluorescence signals, enabling these polymers to perform extremely well in organic electro-/photoluminescence devices. Despite this, only a few acetylenic polymerizations capable of generating charged polymer backbones have been reported. Considering the diverse and fascinating properties of CPEs, the development of simple and efficient methods to synthesize charged acetylenic polymers is highly desirable. In the proposed research project, we will aim to develop new alkyne-based polymerization routes for the in-situ synthesis of CPEs from uncharged monomers. Our research will be elaborated through monomer design, polymer synthesis, structural characterization and polymer properties and applications. To achieve the aims of this project, a series of new monomers with different functional groups will be designed and synthesized. Polymerization conditions will be systematically optimized to attempt to acquire the target high molecular weight CPEs in high yields. Polymer structural diversity will be examined and explored to advance the functionalities of our targets. The properties of the CPEs synthesized in the proposed project will be investigated and the materials will be used in high-tech applications. 共軛聚電解質（CPE）是一類新型的具有π共軛骨架和可電離部分的高級功能聚合物。這些聚合物具有許多特有的性質，包括高電導率，出色的電荷傳輸能力，水溶性和可加工性，兩親性聚集特性並可用作化學/生物感測器。由於這些獨特的功能，CPE具有廣泛的應用前景，從化學/生物傳感，生物成像、治療到發光二極體和光伏設備。具有離子性側鏈的CPE主要由聚合物後修飾得到，並且前人已作了充分研究。然而，這些研究受制于聚電解質複雜的合成步驟難以實現產物結構的多樣性。鑒於此，開發可簡單有效合成具有明確結構的共軛聚電解質的新型策略具有重要意義。 我們的研究小組多年來一直在探索基於炔烴的聚合新方法。與傳統的烯烴聚合反應不同，這些炔烴聚合反應生成的聚合物具有許多遍佈主鏈的不飽和單元，包括雙鍵、三鍵，及各類稠環和雜環等。由於其獨特的π共軛電子結構，這些合成的炔烴聚合物具有獨特的光物理和光電性質。研究表明，離域電子沿著乙炔聚合物主鏈的遷移會導致螢光信號的放大，因此這些聚合物在有機電/光致發光器件中表現出色。儘管如此，只有極少數基於炔烴聚合原位合成聚電解質的反應被報導。考慮到CPE結構和功能多樣性，開發簡單而有效的聚電解質合成方法具有重要意義。 在擬議的研究項目中，我們將致力於開發新的基於炔烴的聚合路線，用於從不帶電荷的單體原位合成共軛聚電解質。我們的提案將從單體設計、聚合物合成、結構表徵以及聚合物應用的角度進行闡述。為了實現該研究目的，我們將設計和合成一系列具有不同官能團的新單體。系統地優化聚合條件，以得到高產率和高分子量的聚電解質。我們還會對所得的聚電解質的性能進行研究，並將這些材料用於高科技應用。

16305320.label: Realisation of objectives
16305320.value: The purpose of this proposed project is to synthesize conjugated polyelectrolytes with multifunctionalities through simple and efficient acetylenic polymerizations. We believe through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goal, a one-pot polymerization route to in-situ generate functional azonia-containing polyelectrolytes was developed from allylamines, internal diynes and sodium hexafluorophosphate. Compared with traditional methods, this new strategy does not require a post-modiﬁcation step or expensive ionic monomers. The polymerization proceeds eﬃciently in air, generating polyelectrolytes in excellent yields (up to 99%) with high molecular weights (up to 28700) in high atom economy. Due to the presence of electron-deﬁcient azonia rings in the polymer main chain, the emission colour of the polyelectrolytes can be easily tuned by changing the electron donor. Thanks to the high luminescence in the solid state, good processability, and high refractive indices, these polymers are excellent materials for fabricating ﬂuorescent photo-patterns and promising for optical applications. The azonia-containing polyelectrolytes can generate reactive oxygen species upon white light irradiation to kill the drug-resistant superbug such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus both in vitro and in vivo. One of the polymers was demonstrated to eﬀectively kill MRSA both in vitro and in vivo. We further developed an efficient multicomponent polymerization route for in-situ generation of functional heteroaromatic hyperbranched polyelectrolytes using readily accessible internal diynes, low-cost, commercially available arylnitriles, NaSbF6 and AcOH/H2O in a one-pot manner. The polymerization works efficiently with a broad spectrum of monomers to afford functional polymers in excellent yields and high molecular weights. All the obtained polymers are soluble in common organic solvents and show tunable emission because of their donor-acceptor structures. The compact hyperbranched architectures of the polymers efficiently restrict the intramolecular motions, which block the nonradiative decay channel to result in high fluorescence quantum yields in the solid state. The light-emissive polymers can fabricate highly ordered fluorescent photopatterns at different scales. Upon white-light irradiation, they can produce considerate reactive oxygen species for the efficient inactivation of bacteria. Furthermore, for the first time, the possibility of using the hyperbranched polyelectrolytes for the creation of customizable living bacterial patterns via photodynamic therapy was demonstrated. Additionally, a catalyst-free, atom-economical interfacial amino-yne click polymerization to in-situ synthesize new free-standing porous organic polymer (POP) films with aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) at room temperature was developed. The crystalline properties of POP films are confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. Their good porosity was proved by their N2 uptake experiments, and their thickness can be easily regulated by adjusting the monomer concentration. More importantly, these AIEgen-based POP films show bright luminescence with high absolute photoluminescence quantum yields of up to 37.8 % and good chemical and thermal stability. They can encapsulate organic dyes such as Nile red to further form an artificial light-harvesting system with a large red-shift, highly efficient energy-transfer ability and high antenna effect. A powerful multicomponent polymerization of activated alkyne, isocyanide and electrophilic was also developed to prepare functional poly(cyclopentadiene)s under metal-free conditions. The present method shows several advantages including the use of simple starting materials, easy operation and great atom economy efficiency. Under optimized conditions, high-molecular- weight polymers with cyclic moieties can be generated in-situ from linear starting materials in very high yields. The obtained polymers show good thermal properties and impressive aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics. They are photosensitive and can be applied in generating fluorescent photopatterns. Some polymers can be used as visualizing agents for selective imaging of lipid droplet in live cells. A MCP of internal diynes, disulfonyl azides and Schiff bases was further developed for the facile access to functional polymers with multi-substituted four-membered heterocycles. As all the monomers can be difunctionalized, all the possible monomer combination ways (A 2 + B2 + C1, A2 + B1 + C2, and A1 + B2 + C2) can be realized. This enables the polymer chain to extend in all possible directions, which greatly enhances the product diversity. All polymerizations perform eﬃciently under mild conditions with good tolerance to diﬀerent functional groups. The resulting polymers exhibit distinguished properties such as high chemical stability after acid and base treatment. Furthermore, they show typical AIE characteristics and can function as promising ﬂuorescent chemosensors in response to Pd2+ and Cr2O72− ions. A simple and efficient polyannulation of dual-activated alkyne and pyridines to construct novel N-heterocyclic poly(quinolizine)s was developed. This polymerization can proceed smoothly under catalyst-free conditions with 100% atom utilization to furnish poly(quinolizine)s with high molecular weights) and well-defined structures in satisfactory yields. The obtained polymers show good solubility, high thermal stability, and strong red aggregation-induced emission. They also exhibit low cytotoxicity and can selectively label lysosomes in live cells. Because of the remarkable advantages of readily available monomers, mild polymerization conditions, atom economy, and excellent properties of the resulting polymers, the present polymerization tool is expected to open large opportunities for preparing functional heterocyclic polymers. Last, a facile and metal-free polymerization route with a coloration effect is demonstrated. By using 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (DABCO) as catalyst, the polymerizations of difunctional or trifunctional activated alkynes proceed quickly at 0 °C in air to generate a series of polymers with stereoregular enyne structure and divinyl ether structure. While both the catalyst and monomers are colorless, the obtained polymers are deep-colored. Such color change can be applied for the damage visualization of polymers using the micro-encapsulation technique. Thus, microcapsules containing the reactive alkyne monomer are prepared and mixed in a DABCO-dispersed polymer film. Both the external and internal damage regions of the composite film can be readily visualized once the microcapsules are ruptured to initiate the polymerization. Additionally, the newly formed polymer automatically seals the cracks to provide an additional protection function. Thus, the present polymerization may be useful in the preparation of smart coatings with dual functions of self-reporting and self-healing.

16305320.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305320.value: Polyelectrolytes play an important role in both biological systems and human society. Their synthesis, functional exploration and profound applications are thus essential for biomimicry and new material design. The progress of research dedicated to polyelectrolytes especially with conjugated backbones has been unsatisfactory because of their difficult syntheses. Thus, new synthetic methodologies capable of efficiently assembling polyelectrolytes are required to address these problems. In this investigation, we have developed new methodologies to functional conjugated polyelectrolytes. They are (i) Rh(III)-catalyzed multi-component polymerizations of allylamines, internal diynes and sodium hexafluorophosphate to azonia-containing polyelectrolytes, (ii) Rh(III)-catalyzed polyannulations of arylnitriles, internal diynes, NaSbF6, and AcOH/H2O to functional heteroaromatic hyperbranched polyelectrolytes, (iii) multicomponent polymerizations of activated diynes, isocyanides and electrophilic styrenes to functional poly(cyclopentadiene)s, (v) multicomponent polymerizations of internal diynes, disulfonyl azides and Schiff bases to functional polymers with multi-substituted four-membered heterocycles, and (vi) catalyst-free polyannulations of dual-activated internal diynes and pyridines to N-heterocyclic poly(quinolizine)s. These developed methods enjoy several advantages such as readily available monomers, wide monomer scope, simple operation, high efficiency, mild polymerization conditions in the absence of catalyst or metal complex, high atom economy, high tolerance to functional groups, etc. Different monomer combinations can be utilized to generate polymers with diverse structures, functionalities and applications. Most of the polymers are produced in high yields. They are soluble in common organic solvents and thus possess good processability. Additionally, they show high thermal stability and good-filming ability. Those containing tetraphenylethene moieties show aggregation-induced emission characteristics and emit strong light emission in the solid state upon photoexcitation. Due to such properties, they show potential applications such as fluorescent chemosensors, fluorescent photopatterning, visualizing agents for bioimaging, bacteria imaging and killing, etc. As you can see in part C of this report, 11 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful results.

16305320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305320.value: Development of new methodologies for the construction of functional polymers is always a hot research topic in polymer research. Recently, conjugated polyelectrolytes have attracted considerable academic and industrial interest because of their distinctive optical, electronic and material properties that are suitable for high-tech application in analytical chemistry, biological science, and optoelectronic devices. However, they are hard to synthesize. In this investigation, we developed new polymerization routes for their syntheses using alkyne monomers. These methods show several advantages such as commercially available monomers, wide monomer scope, simple operation, high efficiency, mild polymerization conditions, high atom economy, functional group tolerance, etc. Polymers with different structures and functionalities are obtained by using different monomer combinations. The obtained polymers are soluble, thermally stable and can form free-standing film by simple solution spin-coating film-forming. They show unique materials properties that are not found in commodity polymers with non-conjugated backbones, making them to find potential high-tech applications. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the exploration of new systems. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore more applications and commercialize our results.

16305320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305320.value: Polyelectrolytes show unique properties and have found potential high-tech applications in many fields. However, they are difficult to prepare. Thus, the development of efficient methodologies for their synthesis has both academic importance and application implication. In this investigation, we developed new polymerization routes to conjugated polyelectrolytes. These methods show many advantages such as readily available monomers, wide monomer scope, simple operation, high efficiency, mild polymerization conditions, etc. All polymers are generated in high yields with good solubility and film-forming ability. They show unique properties that enable them to find potential applications as fluorescent chemosensors, visualizing agents for bioimaging, bacteria imaging and killing, etc. Thus, the polymerizations developed in this project provide facile strategies for the synthesis of polyelectrolytes to enlarge their family members. On the other hand, the unique properties of the present polymers offer great opportunities for the exploration of their practical applications such as photoelectronic materials and phototheranostics.

16305920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305920.value: 球面的五邊及四邊形拼貼

16305920.label: Project Objectives
16305920.value: To classify edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent almost equilateral pentagons. To explore edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent quadrilaterals.
rows: To classify edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent almost equilateral pentagons.
To explore edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent quadrilaterals.

16305920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305920.value: Tilings appear in many natural structures such as honeycombs, crystals, and molecular structures, which have inspired many man-made engineering structures. Tiling is also an integral part of human civilization. It is, for example, an essential part of Islamic art and is also a recurring theme in the paintings of Maurits Cornelis Escher. Adding to the beauty of the subject and its broad application in chemistry, biology, crystallography, architecture, and many other scientific and engineering fields, tiling is also an ancient and fruitful subject of mathematical research. Among the major mathematical achievements is the solution to Hilbert’s 18th problem, the classification of wallpaper groups and crystallographic groups, and the classification of isohedral tilings of the plane, and the very recent classification of convex pentagons that can tile the plane. All of these achievements are on the plane or Euclidean spaces, and the tiling literature is dominated by the study of such spaces. In contrast, little research has been done on the tilings of the sphere. The only major work in this field is the classification of tilings of the 2-sphere by congruent triangles, which began in 1923 and was completed in 2002. In an earlier project, we have completed the classification of tilings of the sphere by congruent pentagons in many cases. The remaining and the most difficult case is that the pentagon is almost equilateral. The primary aim of this project will be to classify edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent almost equilateral pentagons. Our earlier experience for the easier cases gave us the confidence to pursue this most difficult case. The secondary goal is to apply our experience about pentagonal tilings to quadrilateral tilings, which is considered even more difficult. Although we do not expect to completely classify quadrilateral tilings, we will have a good understanding of the problem and build a solid foundation for studying the problem. 自人類文明以來，拼貼就出現在日常生活的各個方面。在藝術，設計，工程，數學等領域，都可以看到拼貼。拼貼作為數學研究的對象，已經有一百多年的歷史。關於拼貼的主要數學成就包括希爾伯特第十八問題的解決，牆紙群和晶體群的分類，平面的等面拼貼的分類，以及球面的全等三邊形的對頂拼貼的分類。拼貼的數學研究已被廣泛應用於許多科技領域，也被應用於其它數學領域。 全等多邊形的平面拼貼一定是由三邊，四邊，五邊或六邊形做成的，這些平面的拼貼問題已有大量的研究文獻。在球面上，類似拼貼一定是由三邊，四邊或五邊形做成的。全等三邊形的球面對頂拼貼問題已經完全解決，剩下的是四邊或五邊形的拼貼問題，然而這方面的研究文獻卻是屈指可數。我們最近完成的十二個全等五邊形的對頂拼貼問題的分類，是這個研究方向的最簡單例子。儘管最簡單，這個例子的研究展示了五邊形拼貼的許多獨特複雜的結構。我們的分類也引進了一些新的方法和技巧，應該可以在全等五邊形的對頂球面拼貼的進一步研究中發揮作用。 目前看來，全等四邊或五邊形的球面拼貼的分類還是比較遙遠的事情，這方面的研究才剛剛起步。我們試圖將簡單的全等多邊形的對頂拼貼進行分類，以建立對問題的理解和研究經驗。在此過程中，我們也試圖設計一些電腦程序，以便處理一些繁複的計算，當全等多邊形的個數越來越多，問題越來越複雜時，這些程序將會相當有用。我們也希望通過總結這些理解和經驗而得到一些一般的結果，並將這些結果應用到其它問題。

16305920.label: Realisation of objectives
16305920.value: Both objectives are completely achieved. Therefore we completed the century long classification program. Moreover, we worked on the related problem of angle congruent tilings, torus tilings, and the moduli space of deformable tilings. The whole classification work is written in five papers of more than 500 pages. The first three have been published, and the other two longer ones are submitted and still under review. In order to complete the whole classification program, I need to hire RA for longer period than expected. Therefore I used the budget in general expenses for hiring research staff. This explains the devotion of the budget and actual expenditure in 4.2.

16305920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305920.value: The two objectives are the final and most difficult part of the century long program of the classification of edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent polygons. The amount of work is much more than all the previous work in the program combined. Here is the complete classification: [1] Platonic type: Five Platonic solids, and six subdivisions of the Platonic solids. [2] Earth map type: Three triangular tilings, two quadrilateral tilings, and two pentagonal tilings. [3] Sporadic type: Simple triangular subdivision of the cube, and eight sporadic quadrilateral tilings. [4] Modifications of [1], [2], [3]: Mostly flip modifications, together with some shiftings. Also one rotation modification, and one rearrangement modification. Moreover, tilings by almost equilateral quadrilaterals or pentagons are the most difficult. We developed some special tools that may become useful for other research. We also developed two methods for finding the classifications.

16305920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305920.value: We are conducting lots of follow up research. The following are some directions. [1] Non-edge-to-edge tilings on the sphere. [2] Tiling by congruent polygons with non-straight edges, on all surfaces, not just the sphere. [3] Angle congruent tilings. [4] Bihedral tilings.

16305920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305920.value: The objective of this project is to complete the century long program of completely classify edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent polygons. The cases covered in this project are the most difficult part of the program, and the amount of work is more than all the previous work combined. We have successfully completed all our objectives. This means the century long program is finally completed. We also developed various geometrical and combinatorial tools for the classification work. In fact, we found two different ways to deal with the almost equilateral case. All these tools will be very useful for the subsequent works such as non-edge-to-edge tilings, tilings by polygons with non-straight edges, etc. Overall, we now have much better understanding of tilings, and such understanding allow us to pursue many more interesting and important problems about tilings.

16306020.value: 交流驱动白光和RGB透明显示器用的卤化铯铜钙钛矿纳米晶体

16306020.label: Project Objectives
16306020.value: Synthesize high PLQY lead-free perovskites using Cs3Cu2X5 (X=Cl, Br, I) using improved ligands for higher QY, shape-control and size-tuning, emission tuning via size, composition and doping of R, G, B copper perovskite NCs with phosphors. Investigate the ultrafast optical properties of these NCs, including size-effects and excited states both in solution and thin films, and in operating AC driven devices and contrast these to charge injection LEDs. Construct transparent AC-driven LEDs, for white light transparent panels (mixed films), and transparent displays (single color).

16306020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306020.value: 金属卤化物钙钛矿对发光器件（LED）具有优异的性能，具有明亮的发射，高的光致发光量子产率和可在可见光谱范围内调节的颜色范围。不幸的是，基于铅的钙钛矿LED具有相对较差的稳定性和较短的设备寿命，并且铅是有毒金属，这可能会阻碍钙钛矿显示器的发展。 在这里，我们将使用Cs3Cu2X5胶态纳米晶体（X = Cl，Br，I）作为无铅钙钛矿，以生产纳米晶体薄膜作为蓝色，绿色和红色橙色发光LED中的活性层。我们小组的初步尝试已成功地使用卤化铯铜生产出了高度单分散的喷墨可印刷胶体纳米晶体样品，其中绿色的量子产率超过90％，蓝色的量子产率超过35％，橙红色的量子产率超过30％。通过进一步的合成工作，可以将颜色范围扩大到红色，并且可以提高发射蓝色和绿色发光的钙钛矿的量子产率。此外，从这些材料中发射的确切机理尚待充分探索。我们建议与我们的合作伙伴合作，通过理论建模，超快速光致发光（PL）和瞬态吸收（TA）探索这些动力学。超快方法将使我们能够查看辐射寿命，陷阱填充效应，激发态动力学，并确定发射态的性质以及它是由陷阱，缺陷，激子还是掺杂剂驱动的。 迄今为止，尚未报道具有任何无铅钙钛矿的高效LED，这主要是由于难以以这种方式实现电荷注入。取而代之的是，我们将使用交流驱动设备，其中有源层的高电阻有利于有效激励设备。 AC场驱动的LED通过碰撞电离过程发挥作用，其中，在场中以高动能振荡的电荷能够激发嵌入在电阻介电材料中的纳米晶体。交流驱动设备与已经安装在外壳中的电气系统配合使用效果更好，因此可以使其效率更高。最后，摆脱电荷注入作为激发源，可以轻松构建透明的LED，这些基于铜的钙钛矿因其非常宽的带隙和可见光发射而特别适合。 因此，这项建议为香港提供了一个机会，以新颖的材料为生机勃勃的研究界做出贡献，并为香港成为消费技术中心奠定牢固的地位。

16306020.label: Realisation of objectives
16306020.value: This project was highly successful, in that it achieved the first two objectives completely and most of the third objective, while also completing more than 17 papers on these and closely related topics. We also achieved further funding through ITF for further exploration of topics related to copper based LEDs. Not bad for a 440K grant! Objective 1: This objective was completed to 100%. We have synthesized lead-free perovskites of the Cs3Cu2X5 crystal structure where X is Cl, Br or I, or mixed I/Br and mixed Br/Cl. We have also synthesized related crystal structures where Cs is replaced by Rb, K and Na. We have also synthesized materials with varying shapes, sizes and explored their optical effects. Finally we have altered the crystal structure by doping/alloying with organic A groups, allowing us to discover, somewhat serendipitously, a new family of hybrid organic/inorganic copper halides with unique phosphorescence emission mechanisms. Objective 2: This objective was completed to 100%. We have used ultrafast spectroscopy to investigate the optical properties of the single Cs3Cu2Br5 and Cs3Cu2I5 crystals, as well as the hybrid crystals found in the course of completing Obj. 1 and nanocrystals in solution. The inorganic materials are found to have very long lived excited states, in agreement with the “self-trapped excitonic” state decay theory, while the hybrid materials are found to possess long-lived phosphor states that decay via well-studied spin-frustrated phosphoresence pathways. In opero, we have studied the time-resolved PL decay of AC driven LEDs using cesium copper iodide thin films. Charge injection devices were used in the AC study (currently under review), as these showed the best emission efficiency. Objective 3: This objective was completed to 100%. Pixels of white light and pure color displays were achieved using down-conversion and AC driven, charge-injection LEDs. Down-conversion devices using mixed films of inorganic and hybrid organic copper halides were found to have high down-conversion efficiency and white light with CIE points close to (0.33, 0.33) and CRI of >97 (max is 100 i.e. perfect blackbody emitter). AC devices using ion impact excitation were not observed to function well, possibly due to breakdowns in the thin films achievable with our in-house sputterer. Early stage problems with this aspect of the project were exacerbated by COVID restrictions from 2021-2022 (as noted in previous report). Instead we focused on charge-injection copper based perovskite-likes and were able to fabricate functional AC driven cesium copper iodide, yellow and orange emitters, as well as down-conversion blue, green, red and white emitting LEDs using the range of materials discovered as part of this project. For the AC driven copper based LEDs, we observed severe shifts in color of the electroluminescence were correlated strongly with the mobility of the injection layer, effects of which could be temporally resolved via AC excitation of the device.

16306020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306020.value: We have synthesized a wide range of lead-free, copper based perovskite-like nanocrystals, crystals and thin films, for use in white light and display applications, with wide range of optical features, including high PLQY and bright emission in the UV to visible to NIR range. [Ref 1, 2, 3, 4, 7] We have found that we can make inorganic crystals with varying properties replacing the A and X groups, but also hybrid organic-inorganic crystals with a wide range of crystal structures. [8, 10, 15] We have studied the emission mechanisms for these materials, finding they generally emit by the STE (self trapped excitonic) or by a range of well known phosphorescence mechanisms. [1, 2, 3, 8, 10, 15, 18, 19] We have fabricated a wide range of white light LEDs, via down-conversion as proof of concept for white light emission. We have fabricated orange and yellow emitting AC LEDs using cesium copper iodides. AC charge injection was used to study time-resolved emission to better understand the phenomenon of shifting electroluminescence peak. This was correlated to charge mobility in the electron injection layer.[1, 2, 3, 7, 18] Additionally, general improvements in our understanding of surface and defect chemistry, developed as part of this project, has fed into other projects within our group and students trained under this project have gone on to contribute strongly to papers on other related topics (see publication list).[5, 6, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14]. In particular, ligand manipulation that we began on copper based materials yielded fantastic results with a related system, AgBiS2. [17]. Students trained on this project also contributed their findings to a review.[ 4]

16306020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306020.value: From our work on CsCuX perovskite-like materials, we have found a massive class of related materials using organic hybrid crystal structures. We have investigated some of these already, but are working on more, including other transition metal and metalloid B groups, including Mn, Zn, Sb and As. We expect to publish more shortly. Additionally, we are now further funded to fabricate finished displays using CsCuX, via a deep UV backlight unit as part of an ITF Midstream project, for which we have now received funding. The materials designed in this project have allowed us to design brighter, higher PLQY emitters for display applications. LEDs made using lead-free perovskite-like nanocrystals are still an area of great research interest and we have found several promising materials as part of this project.

16306020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306020.value: Copper halide "perovskite-like" crystals have several properties that make them interesting for light emission applications. Here we have synthesized a wide range of nanocrystalline and crystalline materials using lead-free copper halides, with significant improvements in their optical properties. These include inorganic "perovskite-like" emissive materials with very bright emission across the visible spectrum, ranging from the UV to the near-infrared. From these we can construct light emitting devices (LEDs) for lighting, including white lights, and displays. In this project, we focused on AC driven LEDs using copper halides, because these have several advantages in heating and efficiency, but mainly here we studied how time varying charge injection affects the time varying light emission, and what this can tell us about the emission mechanism in these devices.

16306120.label: Project Objectives
16306120.value: Find an efficient algebraic method of computing all orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. Find a way of expressing these polynomials as of generating function over combinatorial objects related to the reduced words of their permutation indices. Prove, geometrically or algebraically, that each orthogonal Grothendieck polynomial is a finite linear combination of ordinary Grothendieck polynomials. Explicitly describe the summands appearing in this expansion. Determine whether the corresponding coefficients are always positive and find an explanation for this positivity. Prove that the limits defining the stable orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials always exist. Prove that the resulting power series are symmetric functions that expand positively in terms of Ikeda and Naruse's K-theoretic Schur Q-functions. Prove Ikeda and Naruse's conjecture that the K-theoretic Schur Q-functions generate a ring. Prove Lewis and Marberg's conjecture describing the finite expansion of the K-theoretic Schur Q-functions in terms of the K-theoretic Schur P-functions. Initiate the study of crystal structures on clan words. Describe a natural crystal structure on increasing factorizations of clan words. Determine if this structure is normal in an appropriate crystal category. Find a clan word version of Edeman-Greene insertion that classifies the full subcrystals of each clan word crystal and gives a morphism to a crystal of tableaux of an appropriate type. Identify a natural crystal structure on semistandard set-valued shifted tableaux. Formulate a good heuristic definition of "queer K-crystals" and describe such a structure on appropriate supersets of the crystals of factorizations of involution words, fpf-involution words, and clan words.

16306120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306120.value: Flag varieties are certain well-behaved spaces attached to semisimple Lie groups. Symmetric varieties are interesting analogues of flag varieties with many similar properties. The K-theory ring of an algebraic variety is a fundamental topological invariant with many applications. On the other hand, crystals are combinatorial structures derived from representations of quantum groups. The first part of this proposal is centered around open questions about the K-theory rings of type A symmetric varieties. The second part is concerned with problems related to the construction of certain crystals associated to these rings. The type A flag variety is a space of fundamental interest in algebraic geometry and representation theory. The K-theory ring of this variety arises concretely as a quotient of a polynomial ring, so it is sensible algebraic problem to try to find polynomials that represent the K-classes of interesting closed subvarieties. Type A symmetric varieties belong to one of three different families, derived either from the orthogonal group, the symplectic group, or a product of general linear groups. To each such variety, there is an associated finite set of orbit closures in the flag variety that serve as an interesting test case for many geometric problems. There has been great progress in the last decade in providing polynomial K-theory representatives for these orbit closures. However, few explicit formulas are known for K-theory representatives in the orthogonal family. We intend to further study these representatives. Conjecturally, there is a well-defined way of taking "stable limits" of the orthogonal K-theory representatives to obtain a family of symmetric functions indexed by self-inverse permutations. These symmetric functions appear to be closely related to Ikeda and Naruse's K-theoretic Schur Q-functions. Many questions about these power series merit further study. Hiroshima has recently identified natural crystal structures on the sets of maximal chains in certain weak orders associated to the families of orthogonal and symplectic symmetric varieties. The remaining family of type A symmetric varieties also has an associated weak order, and one expects that similar crystal structures should exist in this context. There are several natural open problems related to finding a relevant construction for this crystal. Such crystals have characters that give cohomology representatives for associated orbit closures. Another interesting open problem, motivated by recent work of Hawkes, Monical, Pechenik, and Scrimshaw, is to find a way to upgrade these constructions to "K-crystals" whose characters give K-theory representatives. 旗簇是一类性质优异的的与半单李群有关联的空间。与旗簇类似，对称簇也有很多相似的性质。代数簇的K-理论环是一个基本的拓扑不变量，有很多应用。另外，晶体是一个从量子群的表示中衍生出的组合结构。 这篇申请的第一部分将探讨一些关于A型对称簇的K-理论环的未解决问题。第二部分是会讲如何构造与这些环对应的晶体。在代数几何与表示论中，A型旗簇是至关重要的空间。这类簇的K-理论环具体作为一个多项式环的商环出现，所以其中的某些多项式会代表一些有趣的闭子簇的K-类。因此，尝试找到这些多项式是一个明智的代数问题。 A型对称簇一共有三族，它们分别衍生于正交群、辛群和一般线性群的乘积。对于每一个A型对称簇，有一个对应的有限集。这个集合包含一些该旗簇中的轨道闭包，它们在许多几何问题中是有趣的测试用例。过去十年，人们试图给出在K-理论中代表这些轨道闭包的多项式，并取得了丰富的进展。但是，在正交族对称簇的情形下，我们对这些K-理论代表元的明确公式所知甚少。我们试图继续研究这些代表元。 我们猜想存在一种定义良好的方法，通过取正交K-理论代表元的“稳定极限”来获得一族对称函数，这些函数由自逆的置换来索引。这些函数正好与池田(Ikeda)和Naruse的K-理论Schur Q-函数密切相关。很多与之有关的问题值得继续研究。 广岛(Hiroshima)最近确定了某些特定弱序中极大链的集合上有自然的晶体结构。这些弱序与正交族和辛族的对称簇有关。剩下的一族A型对称簇也有相关的弱序。人们预测这个弱序中极大链的集合上也有类似的晶体结构。很多未解的问题都与构造它的尝试有关。这些晶体的特征标给出了相应轨道闭包的上同调代表元。另一个有趣的未解问题以Hawkes, Monical, Pechenik, 与 Scrimshaw最近的论文为动机：试图将这些结构升级成“K-晶体”，其特征标给出K-理论代表元。

16306120.label: Realisation of objectives
16306120.value: Objectives #1 and #2 have been largely achieved in a collaborative project with the PI's former MPhil student Jiayi Wen. The preprint "On some Grothendieck expansions" associated to this collaboration has recently been finished and submitted to the arXiv. It uses a variety of algebraic and combinatorial techniques (such as several transition formulas of Lenart and Sottile) to give new formulas for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials, and for the coefficients in the expansion of an orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials into ordinary Grothendieck polyomials. Objective #3 has not yet been fully achieved, but there has been substantial progress. The joint preprint with Wen mentioned above derives some new formulas for the stable limits of orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. Another joint paper of the PI and Brendan Pawlowski ("Ideal transition systems", posted recently on the arXiv) establishes the convergence of these stable limits in general modulo a separate conjecture about Gröbner bases for the ideals of symmetric matrix Schubert varieties. So the final obstacle to achieving this objective is to prove this subsequent conjecture, which the PI intends to study more in the future. The positivity question in Objective #2 has been resolved affirmatively for the vexillary case in a joint preprint of the PI with Travis Scrimshaw. In that work, a general geometric theorem of Brion was used to derive the expected positivity property. Objective #4 has been fully resolved through separate joint papers of the PI with Yu-Cheng Chiu and with Joel Lewis. The first of these papers uses algebraic techniques to derive the GP-expansion of each GQ-fucntion. The second paper combines some elaborate bijective combinatorics and algebraic methods to prove the conjectured ring property. Objective #7 is accomplished in a joint preprint of the PI with his former PhD student Kam Hung Tong. This paper generalizes a construction of Yu to give a natural crystal structure to set-valued shifted decomposition tableaux. Objectives #5 and #6 have not yet been substantially addressed. The reason for this under-achievement is primarily because the questions in objectives #1, #2, and #3 turned out to be harder than expected, and to require more time to fully address. Objectives #5 and #6 are still interesting open problems which the PI intends to study in the future.

16306120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306120.value: The major findings of the proposal are contained in the published papers "Expanding K-theoretic Schur Q-functions" (by the PI and Yu-Cheng Chiu, appearing in the journal Algebraic Combinatorics) and "Combinatorial formulas for shifted dual stable Grothendieck polynomials" (by the PI and Joel Lewis, appearing in the journal Forum of Mathematics, Sigma), along with the submitted preprints "Key and Lascoux polynomials for symmetric orbit closures" (by the PI and Travis Scrimshaw) and "Crystals for set-valued decomposition tableaux" (by the PI and Kam Hung Tong). The first paper proves Lewis and Marberg's conjecture describing the finite expansion of the K-theoretic Schur Q-functions in terms of the K-theoretic Schur P-functions. The second paper proves Ikeda and Naruse's conjecture that the K-theoretic Schur Q-functions generate a ring. The first preprint proves that orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials indexed by vexillary involutions are finite linear combinations of ordinary Grothendieck polynomials. The last preprint identifies a natural crystal structure on certain set-valued shifted tableaux and defines a K-theoretic analogue of queer crystals. A number of other papers were completed by PI with support from the proposal, but these have less direct ties to the major objectives.

16306120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306120.value: Objective #3 is still not completely resolved and is the subject of continuing collaborative projects by the PI and coauthors. While an interesting definition of queer K-crystals has been found, resolving objective #7, these crystals have some mysterious properties and merit further study. In particular, the characters of these crystals appear to satisfy a nontrivial positivity result. The PI is currently collaborating with Kam Hung Tong and Tianyi Yu to try to prove conjectures related to this phenomenon. Finally, the questions in objectives #5 and #6 are still largely open and unresolved, but remain interesting and worth studying in the future.

16306120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306120.value: The main contributions of this research project were to prove some conjectural properties of certain polynomials that record geometric invariants of interesting spaces called the orthogonal Grassmannian and Lagrangian Grassmannian. The polynomials in the first case are called GP-functions and in the second case are called GQ-functions. The first major result of the proposal was to find an explicit expansion of GQ-functions into GP-functions. The second major result of the proposal shows that products of GQ-functions are equal to sums of other GQ-functions. Other contributions of the project include identifying crystal structures on sets of objects that appear in summation formulas for GP- and GQ-functions, and deriving propreties of non-symmetric generalizations of GP- and GQ-functions that arise when studying the geometry of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrix spaces.

16306220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306220.value: 儘管量子力學經過了大約100年的發展已經可以非常準確地描述最小到原子和亞原子粒子尺度上的自然性質，然而我們並不能很好地理解周圍許多材料的特性。原因之一是計算這些特性的復雜性隨系統大小而急劇增加。 例如，對於具有N個自旋的最簡單的依辛模型，構型空間的大小為2N。對於量子系統，計算成本甚至更高。 因此，通常不可能給出解析解。 為了研究這些多體系統，許多數值方法已經被開發。 其中，蒙特卡羅（MC）模擬是最強大的數值方法之一。蒙特卡羅模擬的核心思想是通過構型空間中的隨機遊走對系統進行采樣，但是這樣生成的構型之間不可避免地存在相關性。具有小相關性的有效更新方法的缺乏已成為阻礙探索許多有趣的性質和新的物質態的瓶頸之一。 受最近機器學習技術突破的啟發，申請人開發了一種新型的蒙特卡羅方法，稱為自學習蒙特卡羅方法，該方法可以實現相關性小得多的有效更新，從而顯著加快了模擬速度。基於“先學習後獲得”的理念，我們首先學習有效的模型，並用它來指導我們全局更新構型。 自學習蒙特卡羅方法方法已被證明在各種自旋費米模型中非常有效，但還沒有在純費米子晶格模型中被證明，而後者更接近於實際材料，並且有望具有更有趣的未探索物理性質。 在本項目中，我們擬在自學習蒙特卡羅的框架下，為大尺寸的純費米子晶格模型開發新方法。 我們將首先將自學習蒙特卡羅擴展到量子蒙特卡羅算法，以開發適用於費米子晶格模型的新方法。然後，我們將探索如何用深度神經網絡替換有效模型。由於深度神經網絡具有強大的表達能力，從而可以提高自學習蒙特卡羅的通用性。同時，基於已得出的物理學規律，我們還將設計更適於物理問題的新型深度神經網絡，以進一步提高計算效率。

16306320.label: Project Objectives
16306320.value: Study the asymptotic behavior of solutions to fast diffusion equations. These equations arise from models of natural phenomena including plasma, gas-kinetics, and thin liquid film dynamics driven by Van der Waals forces. It is of physical interests and desires to study their asymptotic behavior as the time evolves. Study qualitative and quantitative properties of solutions to fractional diffusion equations. The fractional diffusion is the diffusion driven by the fractional Laplacian operator, which is a long range diffusion and arises in many contexts such as probability, geometry, physics, and ecology. It is natural and important to investigate their properties, explore the similarities as well as differences compared with the standard diffusion, and seek unified mathematical approaches.

16306320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306320.value: A wide variety of natural phenomena, such as sound, heat and fluid dynamics, can be well described by partial differential equations (PDEs). They also interact decisively with other branches of mathematics such as geometry and probability, as well as other scientific fields such as engineering and economics. This proposed project will analyze a family of nonlinear evolution equations, which describe processes involving fluid flow, heat transfer, or diffusion. Depending on the parameter of the nonlinearity, this family of nonlinear evolution equations can describe either the flow of an isotropic gas through a porous medium (the porous medium equation or slow diffusion equation), or fast diffusions arising in models of plasma, gas-kinetics, thin liquid film dynamics driven by Van der Waals forces, as well as geometry. Different nonlinearities correspond to different models of various phenomena. It would be ideal if one could find explicit solutions of such equations. But this is only possible for very few special cases. The existence of solutions then becomes the next question. It is common nowadays to establish the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions by variational or viscosity methods first, and study the regularity of the weak solutions afterwards, that is, whether the weak solutions are smooth enough to evaluate the equations classically. For these nonlinear diffusion equations, most physical settings lead to the default restriction of the non-negativity of the solutions, and key physical interests include the regularity of the weak solutions, and their asymptotic behavior as the time evolves. In this proposal, we focus on fast diffusion equations. In a classical paper by Berryman and Holland, asymptotic behavior of these solutions in the Sobolev subcritical regime was obtained along a sequence of times, assuming the global smoothness of the solutions. This convergence was later verified without the smoothness assumption, and the convergence rate was strengthened. In two joint works with Jingang Xiong, the PI proved optimal global regularity of these solutions, and obtained the asymptotic behavior of the solutions with a class of singular initial data, respectively. Here, we propose to study the asymptotic behavior of solutions to fast diffusion equations in the Sobolev critical regime, and also investigate singular asymptotic behavior when the diffusion is of long range. 在这里我们主要研究一系列快速扩散方程的正解的渐进行为。快速扩散方程是一个来自等离子体物理学中的非线性抛物型方程。只有在极端特殊的情况下，我们才能显示地写出它们的解。因此，在数学上，我们一般是关心它的解的存在唯一性，正则性，以及当时间趋于无穷大时的渐进行为。Berryman和Holland在解的正则性假设下，最先得到了次临界快速扩散方程的解在沿着一串时间序列上的渐进行为。这个结果后来被人改进，并且去掉了正则性假设。后来我们证明了正解的全局正则性，以及得到了一些初始值不光滑的情况下的解的渐进行为。在此，我们想要研究临界快速扩散方程的解的渐进行为，以及当初始条件不光滑时的分数阶快速扩散方程的解的渐进行为。

16306320.label: Realisation of objectives
16306320.value: Fast diffusion equations arise from models of natural phenomena including plasma behavior, gas kinetics, and thin liquid film dynamics driven by Van der Waals forces. It is of significant physical interest to study their asymptotic behavior as time evolves and to investigate the stability of the limit behavior. While fast diffusion equations with subcritical exponents have been well studied, our research in outputs 1 and 3 focused on fast diffusion equations with critical exponents, where blow-up phenomena occur. In research output 1, we examined critical fast diffusion equations with the Brezis-Nirenberg effect. Using blow-up analysis, we demonstrated the convergence of solutions and established the stability of the limiting stationary state. In research output 3, we investigated critical fast diffusion equations for initial data below the two-bubble energy threshold. We proved a dichotomy showing that every solution converges uniformly, in terms of relative error, to either a steady state or a blowing-up bubble. These studies achieved our first objective. The study of diffusion equations has been extended to those involving the fractional Laplacian, which represents long-range diffusion. In research output 2, we examined a nonlinear boundary diffusion equation of porous medium type arising from a boundary control problem. This essentially corresponds to the porous medium equation with the one-half fractional Laplacian, including some lower-order terms. We provided a complete and sharp characterization of the asymptotic behavior of its solutions, showing that the solution may become extinct in finite time, blow up in finite time, or exist for all time. We determined the asymptotic behavior of all solutions and proved the stability of its separable solutions. Notably, we established a quantitative Hopf's lemma, which played a critical role in the entire proof. The stability proof we developed is robust and can be applied to other diffusion problems. These findings achieved our second objective.

16306320.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306320.value: In our first study, we examined a Sobolev critical fast diffusion equation in bounded domains, incorporating the Brezis-Nirenberg effect. Our research yielded significant insights into the extinction profiles of positive solutions, demonstrating that the convergence rates of the relative error in regular norms are at least polynomial. For generic domains satisfying a non-degeneracy condition, we established exponential decay rates. Our methodology employed a combination of regularity estimates, curvature-type evolution equations, and blow-up analysis. This approach not only provided a deeper understanding of the critical case but also allowed us to extend our findings to Sobolev subcritical fast diffusion equations in bounded domains, where we similarly obtained polynomial convergence rates. Our second investigation focused on a nonlinear boundary diffusion equation of porous medium type, originating from a boundary control problem. This equation essentially corresponds to the porous medium equation with a one-half fractional Laplacian, complemented by lower-order terms. We achieved a comprehensive and precise characterization of the asymptotic behavior of its solutions, revealing three possible outcomes: extinction in finite time, blow-up in finite time, or existence for all time. Our analysis provided detailed insights into the asymptotic behavior of all solutions and demonstrated the stability of separable solutions. In our third study, we delved into the extinction behavior of nonnegative solutions to the Sobolev critical fast diffusion equation in bounded smooth domains with Dirichlet zero boundary conditions, without the Brezis-Nirenberg effect. By imposing a two-bubble energy threshold assumption on the initial data, we proved a striking dichotomy: every solution converges uniformly, in terms of relative error, to either a steady state or a blowing-up bubble. This result provides a clear characterization of the long-term behavior of solutions under specific initial conditions, offering valuable insights into the dynamics of critical fast diffusion processes. These three studies collectively advance our understanding of fast diffusion equations, providing novel insights into their behavior under various conditions and boundary effects.

16306320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306320.value: Future research directions could include investigating the extinction behavior of nonnegative solutions to the Sobolev critical fast diffusion equation in bounded smooth domains with Dirichlet zero boundary conditions for arbitrary initial data. This presents a significant challenge, as solutions may exhibit blow-up at multiple points. In such cases, a meticulous analysis of bubble interactions becomes crucial. A potential starting point for this complex problem would be to focus on the case within a spherical domain. This approach could help determine whether it is possible to exclude the formation of bubble towers. By beginning with this simplified geometry, researchers may gain insights that could later be extended to more general domains. The complexity of this problem stems from the need to understand and characterize the intricate interplay between multiple blow-up points, the geometry of the domain, and the initial conditions. Overcoming these challenges could lead to a more comprehensive understanding of the behavior of critical fast diffusion equations, potentially opening new avenues for both theoretical advancements and practical applications.

16306320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306320.value: Our research focused on understanding how certain processes change over time, specifically through what are known as fast diffusion equations. These equations help describe how things like heat or substances spread in a confined space. By studying these equations with special mathematical properties, we discovered important patterns in how solutions behave as time progresses. We also explored equations related to controlling systems at their boundaries, similar to adjusting the temperature on the surface of a material. Our findings provide a clear and precise description of how these systems evolve, which is crucial for improving control methods. This research is significant because it enhances our understanding of diffusion processes, which are fundamental in fields like physics, engineering, and even finance. By providing new insights into these equations, our work can help improve technologies and systems that rely on efficient spreading or mixing, contributing to advancements in various scientific and industrial applications.

16306520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306520.value: In the paper Maosheng Xiong, Decoding error probability in the erasure channel and the $r$-th support weight distribution (in Chinese), Sci Sin Math, 2021, 51: 1--14, doi: 10.1360/SSM-2021-0019, we find that the decoding error probability in the erasure channel under the three important decoding principles are all closely related to the $r$-th support weight distribution, and we also compute the error exponent for the linear code ensemble of fixed rate with the length going to infinity. In the paper Chin Hei Chan, Maosheng Xiong, Spectral distribution of random matrices from mutually unbiased bases, Advances in Mathematics of Communications Vol. 16, No. 4, 2022, 721--732, we study a different problem related to the $r$-th support weight distribution distribution of linear codes, that is the spectral distribution of matrices from mutually unbiased bases arising from special linear codes. In the preprint Chin Hei Chan, Fang-Wei Fu and Maosheng Xiong, Decoding Error Probability of the Random Parity-Check Matrix Ensemble over the Erasure Channel, at arXiv 2108.09989.pdf, which is still under review, we studied the decoding error probability of the random parity-check matrix ensemble over the erasure channel and computed the error exponent under the three decoding principles. The last paper was submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory and was rejected after three rounds of major revision. During the process, the editor asked for additional referees. Because of the technical nature of the paper, each review and revision took a long time. We finally decided to submit the paper to another journal.

16306520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306520.value: As we find out, the result of the decoding error probability of random linear code ensemble under list decoding principle is the most surprising as it was shown to be different from that of random non-linear code which showed that non-linear code is superior than linear code in this respect. There has been a lot of interest on list decoding and this seems a major finding. We shall look at other code ensembles and see if this is the case in general.

16306520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306520.value: In this project, we studied the decoding error probability of linear codes in the erasure channel under three decoding principles, namely, the maximum likelihood decoding and list decoding, and found that these decoding error probability functions are all directly related to the $r$-th support weight distribution of the linear code. We also studied the decoding error probability of random linear codes ensemble in the erasure channel and computed the error exponent. In particular we found that under the list decoding, non-linear codes seem to perform better than linear codes. It will be interesting to know if this is true for other linear code ensembles and for other communication channels. We also studied the spectral distribution of matrices of mutually unbiased bases arising from linear codes and were related to $r$-th support weight distribution and showed that as the length of the code goes to infinity, the spectral distribution converges to the Marchenco-Paster law.

16306620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306620.value: Precise medicine is a frontier in healthcare that utilizes accurate and noninvasive early diagnosis to formulate personalized treatment. Phototheranostics, which simultaneously combines photodynamic and/or photothermal therapy with real-time diagnostic imaging, is an emerging technology for precise medicine to enable exact disease localization and efficient therapy. Materials that absorb light in the first window of near-infrared spectrum (NIR-I) and emit luminescence in the second window (NIR-II) are highly sought after in phototheranostics because they allow deep penetration of NIR light and high-resolution imaging. Despite great recent success in developing inorganic materials for such applications, organic materials, with the merits of strong NIR absorbance, high photothermal conversion efficiency, excellent biocompatibility, readily fine-tuned chemical structures and easy metabolism, are still the most suitable candidates. According to the Jablonski diagram, excited molecules can decay energy via both radiative (luminescence) and nonradiative (heat) channels, and these two channels are in competition. Thus, it is usually difficult to maximize both processes simultaneously in one system. Although some attempts have been conducted in planar conjugated molecules by tuning the π-π stacking, little success was obtained due to the strong intramolecular interaction. This challenge can be addressed by adjusting the “excited-state molecular motion” through combining twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) and aggregation-induced emission (AIE) effects in one system. The activation of the TICT effect and hence the molecular motion in nanoparticles promotes the nonradiative decay of excited states to generate heat, which is conducive to applications in photoacoustic (PA) imaging and photothermal therapy (PTT). Conversely, restriction of molecular motion results in radiative decay, leading to emission for fluorescent (FL) bioimaging. Therefore, by manipulating the excited-state molecular motion in nanoparticles, phototheranostic systems with NIR-I absorption and NIR-II emission can be developed simultaneously, affording strong performance in terms of both imaging (FL and PA) and therapy (PTT). In this proposal, new phototheranostic systems based on molecular motion in nanoparticles will be designed and developed. Molecular rotor-like AIE luminogens will be built, whose donor-π-acceptor-π-donor core structures will cause the absorption and emission to be shifted to the NIR region. The effects of the donors, acceptors and conjugated bridges on their photophysical properties will be systematically investigated. AIE phototheranostic systems with great potential will be identified for both in vitro and in vivo FL and PA dual-mode imaging and image-guided PTT. Their performance and toxicity will be evaluated to fine-tune the design strategy and obtain molecules with the desired imaging and therapeutic capabilities. 精確醫學是現代醫學的前沿方向，它利用準確和無創的診斷技術，實現疾病早期診斷並制定個性化治療方案。光診療劑，同時結合光動力和/或光熱療法與實時診斷成像技術，是壹種用於精確醫學的新興技術，可實現疾病的精確定位和有效的治療。為了實現更高的組織穿透深度和分辨率，通常需要光診療劑具有近紅外一區吸收和近紅外二區發射的性質。無機納米材料在近紅外光診療劑領域取得了巨大成功，但是具有強近紅外吸收，高光熱轉換效率，出色的生物相容性，易於調控的化學結構和快速代謝的有機材料仍然是作為臨床轉化最佳選擇。 根據Jablonski示意圖，激發態分子可以通過相互競爭的輻射躍遷（發光）和非輻射躍遷（熱）兩種通道回到基態。因此，通常很難在一個系統中同時實現兩個過程都達到最大化程度。儘管有報道通過調整平面共軛分子的π-π堆積，但由於分子內的強相互作用而鮮有成效。為了解決該難題，我們提出通過在一個系統中同時調控分子內扭曲電荷轉移（TICT）和聚集誘導發光（AIE）效應來調節“激發態分子運動”。 TICT效應的激活以及納米粒子中的分子運動促進了激發態的非輻躍遷以產生熱量，這有利於光聲（PA）成像和光熱治療（PTT）的應用。相反，限制分子運動會導致啟動輻射躍遷，從而產生熒光（FL）信號，用於生物成像應用。因此，通過調控納米粒子激發態分子運動，可以同時開發具有NIR-I吸收和NIR-II發射的光診療劑，從而在成像（FL和PA）和治療（PTT）方面均具有強大的性能。 在此項目中，我們將致力於設計和開發基於納米粒子分子運動的新光診療體系。具有分子轉子的AIE發光劑，同時具有供體-π-受體-π-供體的核心結構，這將有利於使分子吸收和發射移至近紅外區域。我們將系統地研究供體，受體和共軛橋對其光物理性質的影響。我們還會評估這種具有巨大潛力的AIE光診療劑的體外和體內FL和PA雙模成像以及成像指導的PTT的性質。最後，將評估它們的性能和毒性，以微調設計策略並獲得具有所需成像和治療能力的分子。

16306620.label: Realisation of objectives
16306620.value: The primary goal of this GRF project is to design and develop novel phototheranostic systems using near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics. We aim to investigate their photophysical properties and explore applications in fields such as fluorescent and photoacoustic imaging, photodynamic therapy (PDT), and photothermal therapy (PTT) for tumors. Over the past three years, we have made significant advancements in achieving these goals. We have successfully synthesized and characterized novel NIR-emissive AIE materials, demonstrating their efficacy in enhancing imaging contrast and therapeutic outcomes. Additionally, our research has shown promising results in applying these phototheranostic systems for precise tumor targeting and treatment, underscoring their potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy. Despite many design strategies for bright NIR-II fluorophores, the lack of solid structural identification, particularly through single-crystal analysis, has hindered further progress. To address this, we employed molecular single-crystal engineering to better understand the structure-function relationship of NIR-II dyes. We developed TBP-b-DFA, a well-defined fluorophore designed by fine-tuning donor-acceptor distances, achieving an absolute quantum yield of 0.4% and an emission wavelength reaching 1400 nm. This enables effective NIR-II brain imaging and quantification of cerebrovascular functions, such as cerebral blood flow and reactivity. We also devised a strategy for integrating AIE luminogens with metal–phenolic networks to create stable, tunable, and bright AIE dots, labeled 2TPEA-AQ@AIE-T. These dots are versatile, incorporating various metal ions to tailor their optical properties. They enable dual-modality in vivo imaging, visualizing blood flow in zebrafish and supporting magnetic resonance and fluorescence imaging in tumor-bearing mice. In addition to their role in fluorescence imaging, AIE materials have shown promise as photothermal agents for precise tumor targeting and treatment. By optimizing molecular design, AIE materials can efficiently convert absorbed light into heat, enabling PTT. Building on this, we developed an agarose-based thermosensitive hydrogel incorporating the mild photothermal AIE agent TPE-BBT and the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 to enhance FLASH radiotherapy and prevent tumor recurrence. Upon 660-nm laser irradiation, the hydrogel releases TPE-BBT and CB-839 into the tumor site, enabling concurrent mild PTT and chemotherapy. This approach inhibits DNA repair pathways, enhancing FLASH radiotherapy effects and preventing tumor recurrence, while minimizing systemic toxicity. In a related study, we introduced TPA-NDTA nanoparticles (NPs) to enhance the immunogenicity and therapeutic efficacy of ferroptosis in cancer treatment. These NPs, equipped with a molecular rotor to promote efficient excited-state intramolecular motion, exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency, stability, and broad absorption. When combined with the ferroptosis inducer RSL3, TPA-NDTA NPs significantly enhance the immunogenicity of ferroptotic cell death. In poorly immunogenic 4T1 tumor models, this combination improved therapeutic outcomes both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, it triggered a CD8+ T cell-mediated immune response, effectively inhibiting untreated tumor growth, and holds promise for systemic antitumor effects through immunogenic ferroptosis. We also developed two photothermal upconversion nanoparticles (PT-UCNP-B/G) for bidirectional modulation of neural activity via both photostimulation and thermostimulation. These nanoparticles combine photothermal and luminescent properties, enabling neural control through heat at 808 nm and visible light emission at 980 nm. PT-UCNP-B/G modulates neuronal activity by activating sodium currents in neuro2a cells expressing channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2) under 980-nm light, and inhibiting potassium currents in cells expressing KCNQ1 under 808-nm light. In vivo, PT-UCNP-B enabled deep-brain stimulation in mice, modulating feeding behavior without invasive brain implants. PDT is another promising noninvasive treatment for cancers and other diseases, utilizing photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light activation to induce cell death. AIE materials represent a new class of photosensitizers for image-guided PDT. In this project, we reported IQ-Cm, an AIE-active cationic diphenyl luminogen with isoquinolinium and coumarin units, for treating bacterial keratitis. IQ-Cm selectively binds to bacteria, exhibits low cytotoxicity, and functions as a self-reporting probe, distinguishing live and dead bacteria by emission color changes. IQ-Cm also shows antibacterial activity in the dark and generates ROS upon light irradiation, making it highly effective for PDT. In vitro and rabbit models of bacterial keratitis infected with S. aureus demonstrated significant antibacterial efficacy under both dark and light-activated conditions. We expanded this approach to a mitochondria-targeted PDT strategy using AIE luminogens to selectively kill fungi while minimizing damage to mammalian cells. Three AIEgens—IQTPE-2O, IQ-Cm, and IQ-TPA—were designed to accumulate in fungal mitochondria by exploiting differences in surface charge and mitochondrial membrane potential. Upon white light irradiation, these AIEgens generate ROS (¹O₂), damaging mitochondria and leading to fungal cell death. Among them, IQ-TPA showed the highest PDT efficiency with minimal cytotoxicity to mammalian cells. In a fungal keratitis rabbit model, IQ-TPA demonstrated superior therapeutic effects compared to the clinically used Rose Bengal, highlighting its potential for treating fungal infections. Manipulating electron donor/acceptor (D/A) interactions is crucial for advancing fluorescent materials; however, acceptor engineering is often overlooked. Inspired by the "more is different" concept, we developed two systems—D′−D−A−D−D′ (1A) and D′−D−A−A−D−D′ (2A). The 1A system exhibited an AIE-to-ACQ shift, while the 2A system displayed a reverse ACQ-to-AIE change due to enhanced electron deficiency. The 2A system also demonstrated higher molar absorptivity (ε), superior NIR-II emission, greater ROS generation, and improved photothermal conversion efficiency. A representative 2A fluorophore (2TT-2BBTD) excelled in multimodal imaging-guided phototherapy for tumor elimination and NIR-II fluorescence imaging in mice. AIE materials are ideal theranostic agents due to their ease of construction, modification, and biocompatibility. However, integrating multiple functions (imaging and therapy) into a single component remains challenging due to competitive energy relaxation pathways and fluorescence quenching. To address this, we designed two AIE-active molecules, TPA-TBT and TPE-TBT, with a donor–acceptor–donor (D–A–D) structure. While TPE-TBT favored radiative decay, limiting its PTT and PDT efficiency, TPA-TBT achieved a balanced energy decay, resulting in bright NIR emission, 44% photothermal conversion efficiency, and robust ROS generation. The TPA-TBT nanoaggregates demonstrated exceptional performance in NIR fluorescence imaging and multimodal therapy (PDT/PTT) for tumor ablation in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice. Though multifunctional nanoaggregates are promising for cancer phototheranostics, constructing them efficiently remains challenging. As a continuation, we designed a NIR-absorbing small molecule, TBT-2(TP-DPA), as a one-for-all phototheranostic agent. Its nanoaggregates, encapsulated by DSPE-PEG, demonstrated a photothermal conversion efficiency of 51% while maintaining a high photoluminescence quantum yield in the NIR region. These nanoaggregates can be delivered to solid tumors within 40 minutes using an 808 nm pulse laser, faster than the traditional enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, which takes over 24 hours. This rapid delivery process, termed the photoinduced thermoacoustic (PTA) process, offers a new approach for drug delivery. Additionally, TBT-2(TP-DPA) nanoaggregates exhibited strong NIR-II fluorescence, photothermal imaging, and photoacoustic imaging capabilities, enabling multimodal cancer imaging and effective tumor ablation in a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model. This PTA-driven strategy enhances tumor accumulation and improves PTT efficiency. These studies introduce practical designs for multifunctional nanoaggregates, boosting the potential for efficient, biosafe cancer treatments and broader clinical applications.
