16306620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306620.value: The key outcomes of the research are as follows: 1) Synthesis of novel NIR AIE materials: we successfully synthesized and characterized new NIR-emissive AIE materials, demonstrating their effectiveness in enhancing imaging contrast and therapeutic outcomes. 2) AIE materials for bioimaging: we developed TBP-b-DFA, a well-defined NIR-II fluorophore with 0.4% quantum yield and 1400 nm emission, enabling effective brain imaging and cerebrovascular function quantification. Additionally, 2TPEA-AQ@AIE-T dots, which integrate AIE luminogens with metal–phenolic networks, demonstrated dual-modality imaging in zebrafish and tumor-bearing mice. 3) AIE materials for photothermal therapy, ferroptosis-based immunotherapy and neural modulation: we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel incorporating TPE-BBT and CB-839 for mild photothermal therapy and chemotherapy, enhancing FLASH radiotherapy and reducing tumor recurrence. Additionally, TPA-NDTA nanoparticles enhanced ferroptosis-based immunotherapy, triggering a CD8+ T cell response in 4T1 tumor models, effectively improving therapeutic efficacy in poorly immunogenic tumors. Moreover, PT-UCNP-B/G nanoparticles enabled non-invasive, bidirectional neural modulation and deep-brain stimulation in mice, highlighting their potential in tether-free neural control. 4) AIE materials for photodynamic therapy: we developed IQ-Cm, an AIE-active photosensitizer for bacterial keratitis,exhibiting selective bacterial binding, low cytotoxicity, and effective ROS generation upon light activation. Additionally, IQ-TPA exhibited high PDT efficiency and minimal mammalian cell toxicity, demonstrating superior therapeutic effects in a fungal keratitis model compared to Rose Bengal. 5) AIE materials for multimodal cancer theranostics: two fluorescent systems, 1A and 2A, were developed to explore donor/acceptor (D/A) interactions. The 1A system exhibited an AIE-to-ACQ shift, while the 2A system demonstrated a reverse ACQ-to-AIE transformation, with superior NIR-II emission, increased ROS generation, and improved photothermal efficiency. A representative 2A fluorophore, 2TT-2BBTD, excelled in multimodal imaging-guided phototherapy and tumor elimination in mice models. Furthermore, TPA-TBT nanoaggregates, with 44% photothermal conversion efficiency, achieved bright NIR emission and robust ROS generation, enabling NIR fluorescence imaging and multimodal therapy (PDT/PTT). Additionally, the TBT-2(TP-DPA) nanoaggregates, with 51% photothermal efficiency, allowed rapid tumor targeting via a photoinduced thermoacoustic process, enhancing drug delivery and cancer treatment efficacy These findings underscore the potential of AIE materials in creating multifunctional, biocompatible theranostic platforms for efficient cancer treatment, bioimaging, and broader clinical applications, offering innovative solutions for multimodal imaging and therapeutic strategies in modern medicine. In Part C of this report, we have listed the publications that have emerged from this research project. Most of these papers have been published in high-impact journals, reflecting the significance of our findings.

16306620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306620.value: The development of multifunctional phototheranostic systems has shown promise in improving imaging contrast, therapeutic outcomes, and precise tumor targeting. Moving forward, the next steps should focus on: 1) Optimization of molecular design: further refinement of donor-acceptor (D/A) interactions and single-crystal engineering will enhance the structure-function relationship of NIR-II fluorophores, improving their brightness, stability, and targeting capabilities. 2) Expanding applications: additional investigation into the use of these AIE materials for dual- or multi-modal imaging (e.g., combining fluorescence, photoacoustic, and magnetic resonance imaging) could open up new avenues in diagnostics and theranostics. 3) Enhancing delivery efficiency: further exploration of the photoinduced thermoacoustic process for rapid and targeted drug delivery could revolutionize approaches to cancer treatment, reducing side effects and improving therapeutic precision. 4) Preclinical translation: the next phase of research should focus on in vivo studies to evaluate long-term biocompatibility, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy in larger animal models. This would help pave the way for clinical trials and applications.

16306620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306620.value: This research focuses on developing innovative fluorescent materials known as "aggregation-induced emission" (AIE). Unlike conventional fluorescent materials which often lose brightness when they accumulate, AIE materials become brighter as they aggregate. This unique property makes them highly effective for both medical imaging and cancer therapy. We have successfully developed several near-infrared emitting AIE materials, specifically designed to enhance the visibility of tumors during advanced imaging techniques such as fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging. These materials enable high-contrast imaging, enabling more accurate tumor detection and improving diagnostic precision. Beyond imaging, some of these AIE materials also serve as therapeutic agents. By absorbing light, they can convert it into heat or generate reactive oxidants, both of which can selectively destroy cancer cells. This dual functionality—combining imaging and therapy—enables simultaneous tumor detection and treatment, significantly enhancing the precision of cancer therapies while minimizing damage to healthy tissues. Overall, this research holds the potential to transform diagnostic and therapeutic practices, particularly in cancer treatment, by integrating imaging and therapy into a single, highly efficient platform. This approach could lead to safer, more targeted treatments for a variety of diseases, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing side effects.

16306720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306720.value: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLED) have been widely adopted in consumer electronics, such as smartphones and TVs, due to its superior display quality and unique form factor. However, the relatively short device lifetime for the current blue OLED devices remains a serious drawback that could ultimately limit the application of OLED displays. Fundamentally, the lifetime of a blue OLED device is related to the photochemical and electrochemical stability of the emissive materials and adjacent charge-transport materials. The degradation mechanisms identified in our research and that of others strongly suggest that free radical byproducts and their subsequent free radical chain reactions play a significant role in the operational decay of blue devices. These radical species are primarily produced by exciton-induced C-N dissociations of amine-based materials and the oxidation of OLED materials by residual O2/H2O. As the C-N bond dissociation energies overlap with the bandgap of blue materials, it is extremely difficult to develop amine-based blue materials that experience absolutely no degradation. It is also impractical to completely eliminate O2/H2O from the deposition chambers during manufacturing processes. A viable solution to mitigate the radical related degradation is using radical scavengers as additives to convert the minute but detrimental radical intermediates into unreactive and non-quenching molecules. This method can be used to stop the propagation of radical chain reactions and contain the chemical degradation of blue materials. In this study, we will develop phenolic scavengers based on blue OLED materials and fully establish their photophysical and photochemical processes in devices. We will investigate the efficacy of these materials in extending the lifetime of blue devices and establish the chemical pathways of their radical scavenging process via in-situ chemical analyses of faded samples, optimize the molecular structure of radical scavengers, and improve the life time of blue OLED devices without degrading the light emission efficiency. Ultimately, we aim to chemically stabilize blue materials against free radical reactions and substantially extend the lifetime of blue devices.

16306720.label: Realisation of objectives
16306720.value: After three years of research, all three project objectives have been achieved. The specific methodology and experiments to meet these goals are outlined below. 1. Extend the lifetime of blue OLED devices using deuterated materials to suppress detrimental radical chain reactions during device operation. The high-energy state excitons in blue OLEDs destroy the chemical bonds in molecules and then generate radicals with high reaction activity that significantly reduce the longevity of blue OLEDs. The hole transporting layer (HTL)/emitting layer (EML) and electron transporting layer (ETL)/emitting layer (EML) interfaces are most prone to degradation in blue OLEDs as the radicals are mainly generated by the chemical degradation of transport materials, resulting in detrimental radical chain reactions in the whole devices. Using deuterated organic materials is a promising method to strengthen the molecular structure because the deuteration effect reduces the internal vibrational energy by replacing C-H bonds with C-D bonds and suppresses the harmful radical chain reactions in blue OLEDs during operation. Focused on a model blue fluorescent device, we designed and synthesized a series of deuterated blue materials and then proved that deuteration indeed improves the lifetime of blue OLEDs by suppressing the harmful radical reactions, an effect known as the isotope kinetic effect (KIE). By replacing the HTL and host materials in the device with their perdeuterated counterparts, we have extended the device lifetime by as much as eightfold. 2. Develop deuterated materials for use as the host, dopant, and transport materials in blue OLED devices to maximize the deuteration substitution in the light-emitting and the adjacent transport layers. In the project, we have developed 18 deuterated blue materials, including the host, dopant, and transport materials, and investigated their lifetime-enhancing capabilities in correlation with their molecular structures, overall deuteration degree, and deuterated positions. We chose two blue host materials, 9-phenyl-10-(4-phenylnaphthalen-1-yl) anthracene (PNA) and 3,4-diphenyl-1-(10-phenylanthracen-9-yl) dibenzo[b,d]furan (DPAF), as the model compounds to study the effect of deuteration degree. Deuterated hosts with various degree of deuterium substitution are synthesized: PNA-d5 (-dx represent the number of deuterated atoms), PNA-d18, PNA-d22, DPAF-d5, DPAF-d15, and DPAF-d26 (Publication 1 and 2 in Part C). These materials were used as the host in a blue OLED device with N,N,N′,N′-tetraphenylpyrene-1,6-diamine (TPPDA), N,N′-Di(1-naphthyl)-N,N′-diphenyl-(1,1′-biphenyl)-4,4′-diamine (NPB), and LG201 as the blue dopant, HTL, and ETL, respectively. Both PNA and DPAF exhibited a positive relationship between deuteration degree and device lifetime (T90). The deuteration of a single phenyl group in the host (PNA-d5 and DPAF-d5) can result in a twofold increase in lifetime, while perdeuteration (PNA-d22 and DPAF-d26) leads to over 4 times longer lifetime. To study the deuteration effect of the HTL, we synthesized deuterated NPB-d19. Replacing HTL with NPB-d19 in the device with a perdeuterated host (PNA-d22) further improved the device lifetime by eightfold compared to the device without deuterium. These results showed that deuteration on both host and transport materials has a cumulative enhancement effect on the device lifetime of the blue OLEDs, as device degradation typically originates from the HTL/ETL interfaces. To study the deuteration effect on the dopant in the blue OLEDs, we compared the device lifetimes of the fluorescent dopant (TPPDA) and partially deuterated TPPDA-d3 and TTPDA-d10 (Publication 3 in Part C). The dopant still exhibited a positive relationship between deuteration degree and device lifetime, but the device lifetime only increased by 32% using TTPDA-d10 as the emitter. When TTPDA-d10 was used as a host material for a red dopant, we obtained a more than twofold increase in device lifetime. These results indicate that the overall deuterium concentration in the EML, not the deuteration degree of a specific material, is responsible for the lifetime enhancement effect. We further investigated the effect of the deuterium positioning within the host molecule on the device lifetime, as radical reactions occur at different rates in different locations in the molecule. We strategically introduced a deuterated phenyl group at different positions of two host materials, PNA and PADF (Publication 4 in Part C). The deuterated phenyl was positioned adjacent to or separated from the anthracene chromophore core. PNA-based devices with deuterated phenyl adjacent to anthracene exhibited larger lifetime enhancement. In contrast, the PADF-based devices demonstrated more enhanced operational stability when the deuterated phenyl was separate from the anthracene core. Although there is no definitive conclusion on the cause for such different results, we speculate that the molecular orientation of these hosts in devices plays a key role. Our research offers a practical strategy for developing partially and fully deuterated materials to achieve longer-lasting blue OLEDs. 3. Identify the molecular structure of byproducts generated in the radical reactions during device degradation using in-situ chemical analysis. We used an analytical technique called laser desorption/ionization-time-of-flight (LDI-TOF) to identify the byproducts produced in radical reactions during device degradation. Samples for LDI-TOF analysis were prepared by depositing organic thin films on an ITO glass substrate, similar to how the devices were made. The sample was irradiated by a UV laser in situ to induce photochemical degradations. The laser was operated at a specific intensity below the film desorption and ionization threshold to avoid material ablation. After irradiation, we analyzed the sample using LDI-TOF on the same spot to get a mass spectrum of the degraded film. The results showed that the degradation of blue OLED is linked to adduct species formation at the devices' interfaces. When the transport material NPB was excited, its C-N bonds dissociated to form radical fragments. These radicals reacted with nearby NPB or host molecules to create various chemical species, including quencher adducts. When NPB or the host was deuterated, the adduct byproducts were generated at a reduced rate. An isotope kinetic effect value of 2 was observed for PNA and PNA-d5, meaning PNA-d5 reacts with radicals at only half the rate of PNA. This is in direct correlation with the twice longer lifetime of PNA-d5, compared to PNA. The in-situ chemical analysis revealed the degradation pathways of the blue host. It correlated the identified kinetic isotope effect of byproduct reactions with the lifetime enhancement of deuterated materials observed in OLED devices.

16306720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306720.value: 1. Progressive deuteration of blue host materials has a cumulative enhancement effect on their device lifetime, with highly deuterated hosts improving T90 lifetime by more than fourfold through KIE (Publication 2 in Part C). Through experiments with different transport materials and various EML configurations, we determined that device degradation occurred predominantly at the EML interfaces, and the KIE value is specific to the material set responsible for degradation. We also found that deuterated devices could withstand stress tests under higher temperatures and current densities. 2. Degradation analysis using LDI-TOF identified host-transport material adduct species as the main byproducts in photo-degraded films with a mixed host and transport material composition, indicating that similar species could be produced in the device using these functional materials under operation. Deuteration, in effect, mediated the formation of these adduct species, presumably quenchers, thus improving the device lifetime. An approximate agreement was obtained between the kinetic isotope effect of the photo-degradation reactions and the enhancement in device lifetime with deuteration. Based on this finding, additional lifetime increases were realized in devices using a deuterated HTL in combination with a deuterated host, extending the device lifetime by eightfold over the device without any deuterium (Publication 1 in Part C). 3. The dopant plays a minor role in blue device degradation. Deuterated blue dopant materials only improve device lifetime by up to 32%, indicating that the overall deuterium concentration in the EML, not the deuteration degree of a specific material, is responsible for the lifetime enhancement effect (Publication 3 in Part C). 4. Deuteration of different moieties of the blue materials produces different lifetime enhancement effects. Yet the reason for this phenomenon is not fully understood. Changes in reactivity towards radicals and different molecular orientations at the EML interfaces are speculated as the two leading causes (Publication 4 in Part C). 5. The deuteration of materials at the recombination interface generally applies to all OLED devices to prolong their lifetime.

16306720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306720.value: 1. The project used fluorescent OLED materials, which only utilize singlet excitons, as model compounds. Future research could expand the deuteration strategy to other blue materials, such as phosphorescent materials and thermally activated delayed fluorescent materials, which utilize both the singlet and triplet excitons. Currently, the device lifetime of these blue materials is still too short for practical applications. According to our results, deuteration could help these materials achieve the longevity required for commercialization. 2. The project only investigated deuterated hole transport materials. In future research, it is only logical to apply deuteration to electron transport materials such as LG201. It is anticipated that deuterated ETL will further extend the device lifetime by minimizing the reaction rate of chemical degradations at the EML/ETL interface. 3. The effect of deuteration position within a specific molecule is still not fully understood. A more detailed study should be conducted using materials with deuterium substituted at different molecule moieties. Potential energy surface mapping of radical reactions will help us elucidate the significance of deuteration at each hydrogen atom and the corresponding KIE factor, providing a more precise deuteration strategy for blue materials.

16306720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306720.value: Over several decades since its discovery, the lifetime of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) has been dramatically improved, leading to the widespread adoption of OLED displays in consumer electronics. One effective technology for achieving longevity is using deuterated compounds in the EML, which can slow down detrimental chemical reactions and increase the device lifetime. However, the exact relationship between the degree of deuteration and device lifetime and the degradation mechanisms involved remains unclear. In this project, we systematically investigated the effects of deuteration on the host, dopant, and transport materials in a conventional blue OLED device, establishing a quantitative correlation between lifetime enhancement and deuterium substitution. In addition, we identified possible chemical degradation pathways in the deuterated OLED devices using laser desorption/ionization-time-of-flight (LDI-TOF) analysis and elucidated a degradation mechanism consistent with deuteration enhancement. Our results demonstrate that deuterated materials can significantly improve device lifetime and provide a general deuteration strategy for developing more stable blue OLED materials and devices.

16306920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306920.value: The central theme of this proposal is the development of a new synthetic methodology for total synthesis of several indole alkaloids. Many of this class of secondary metabolites possess potent yet highly specific bioactivities (therapeutic effects) and have attracted extensive research interest including chemical synthesis. Indole alkaloids are structurally complex and diverse and thus present significant challenges to the chemical synthesis. Although tremendous advances on synthetic methods for indole alkaloids have been made in the past decades, the continued development of new and efficient methodology to facilitate or simplify the total synthesis of indole alkaloids remains of the paramount importance. The specific methodology proposed herein involves intermolecular aza-Friedel-Crafts (AFC) reaction of Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) products with indoles. In light of many limitations of direct transformations for AAR products that are unstable and tend to aromatized to 3-hydroxypyridines, we carried out preliminary study that verify this new methodology (2 examples with up to 80% yield). Full studies on this new methodology will employ a comprehensive examination of various promoters (Lewis acids or Bronsted acids) and substitution effects of indoles on the regioselectivity and efficiency. To develop an asymmetric version of this new approach, we propose to employ chiral ion-pairing catalysis strategy by exploiting chiral counteranion-iminium interaction to achieve enantioselectivity. Four classes of chiral counteranions: phosphorate, borate, thiourea-halide/acetate, and pentacarboxycyclopentadiene anion will be evaluated for the enantioselective AFC reaction of AAR with indoles. Our preliminary results showed that the enantioselectivity of AFC could be achieved using chiral BINOL-based phosphoric acid (ca. 20% ee). This finding is encouraging as a proof-of-concept and considerable efforts are entailed to improve the enantioselectivity. To showcase the synthetic utility, four representative bioactive indole alkaloids; tacamonine, hirsutine, aspidospermidine and tabersonine are chosen as targets for total synthesis that features our innovative AFC reaction of AAR products with indoles. Once our AFC methodology is established, the synthetic route for these alkaloids are very short (6-10 steps), which allows for a rapid access to a library of alkaloid natural products and analogues for evaluation of their biological activity that has considerable therapeutic implications. In summary, we propose a new synthetic method: AFC reaction of AAR products with indoles, and apply it in total synthesis of four indole alkaloids. 本提案的中心主題是開發一種新的合成方法,以應用於幾種吲哚生物鹼的全合成。許多此類二次代謝物具有強效但高度特異性的生物活性(治療效果),並吸引了廣泛的研究興趣,包括化學合成。吲哚生物鹼結構複雜多樣,因此對化學合成構成重大挑戰。雖然過去幾十年吲哚生物鹼的合成方法方面取得了巨大進展,但繼續發展新的和有效的方法,以促進或簡化對吲哚生物鹼的全合成仍然至關重要。本文提出的具體方法主要涉及氮雜-Achmatowicz重排產品與吲哚之間的氮雜-Friedel-Crafts反應研究。鑒於對不穩定且傾向於芳香化為 3-羥基二丁的 AAR 產品的直接轉化有許多限制,我們進行了初步研究,驗證了這種新方法(2 個示例,產量高達 80%)。對新方法的全面研究將採用對各種促進劑(劉易斯酸或勃朗酸)的全面研究,以及吲哚取代基對區域選擇性和效率的影響。為了開發這種新方法的不對稱版本,我們建議採用手性離子對催化策略,利用手性抗離子-二分體相互作用來實現選擇性。我們將仔細研究四類手性抗離子:磷酸鹽、硼酸鹽、硫尿-鹵化物/醋酸酯和五羰基環戊二烯陰離子對AAR與英吲哚間的不對稱選擇性AFC反應。初步結果表明,使用基於手性BINOL的磷酸,可實現AFC的不對稱選擇性(約ca.20%ee)。這一發現令人鼓舞,也是證明了我们的设计方案,然而仍然需要作出相當大的努力以提高選擇性。為了展示這方法在合成中的應用,四種具有代表性的生物活性生物鹼; tacamonine, hirsutine, aspidospermidine and tabersonine 被選為全合成的目標, 其中關鍵的反應是我們創新的AAR 產品與 吲哚的 AFC 反應。 一旦我們成功的建立AFC方法,這些生物鹼的合成路線是非常短的(6-10步), 它允許快速獲得這些生物鹼天然產品和類似物庫,以評估其生物活性,這會具有相當大的意義。總之,我們提出了一種新的合成方法:AAR產品與吲哚的AFC反應,並將其應用於四種內多生物鹼的全合成中。

16306920.label: Realisation of objectives
16306920.value: Objective 1: To develop the first intermolecular Aza-Friedel-Crafts reaction of Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement with indoles. This objective has been achieved and the results have been published in Chemical Science (Chem. Sci. 2024, 15, 5730-5737). Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) represents one of the most facile entries into functionalized piperidines, and our research group has great interest in exploiting AAR for total syntheses of bioactive alkaloids. To extend the synthetic utility of rather unstable AAR products in total synthesis, we envisioned that the freshly prepared AAR products (functionalized 2-hydroxypiperidines) might react with indoles to enable a direct C3–C20 coupling (iAFC) for aspidosperma and uleine alkaloids. We began our study with aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement of N-Boc-furfurylamine under our oxone/KBr (cat.) conditions to provide functionalized 2-hydroxypiperidine (AAR product), which was unstable for storage and should be used immediately for the subsequent reaction with indoles. Two indoles were chosen to evaluate the reaction efficiency and functional group tolerance. Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) was used first as the catalyst (5 mol%) for the iAFC reaction of indole and AAR product under various solvents and the results were excellent with 78% to 88% yields derived from selective C3–C2’ coupling. Notably, the C2–C2’ coupling product was not observed. It was noteworthy that the widely used Lewis acid BF3–Et2O gave a lower yield (60%), while the unusual organic Brønsted acid pentacarbomethoxycyclopentadiene (PCCP) in toluene delivered slightly higher yield (90%). It was noted that the tert-butyldimethylsilyl (TBS) ether survived under these conditions. Extensive experiments revealed that PCCP was the optimal protic acid as the catalyst with high reproducibility and best efficiency at 0.05–0.2 M concentration (58% yield). Under the optimal conditions (PCCP or TFA in toluene), the scope of the iAFC reaction of indoles with AAR products was evaluated and 37 examples were successfully achieved with good to excellent yields and regioselectivity. Objective 2: To develop enantioselective Aza-Friedel-Crafts reaction of Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement with indoles. This objective has been addressed and parts of the preliminary results have been published in Chemical Science (Chem. Sci. 2024, 15, 5730-5737). The asymmetric version of this aza-Friedel-Crafts reaction of aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement was attempted with variety of different chiral protic acid as the promoters including chiral PCCP derived from methanol, camphor, and chiral amines, chiral phosphoric acids, and chiral ureas. The best enantioselectivity was 36% ee, which is not synthetically useful. The major problem is the instability of aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement products under acidic conditions due to the ready aromatization into pyridine derivatives. We also examined different N-protecting group on the aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement products but they did not afford the expected enantioselectivity or stability. While the modification of both substrates seems necessary to identify the appropriate reactivity and stability, the future efforts are made on evaluating the effect of C2-substituted (i.e., ester) aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement products for enhancing the stability and providing the chelating functional group that induces the chirality. Objective 3: To accomplish the total synthesis of tacamonine and hirsutine. This objective has been addressed and more data and results are collected for publication in due course (expected in 2025). Our preliminary results suggested that the aza-Friedel-Crafts reaction of aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement products could proceed in a highly regioselective way. When indole C3 is substituted, the reaction occurs at indole C2, which provide an expedite access to tacmonine and hirsutines where indoles and piperidines are linked at C2-C2’. A protic acid was identified for the AAR-AFC reaction at C2-C2’ and optimization for a gram-scale is undergoing. The total synthesis of tacamoinine, hirsutine, and structurally related alkaloids is expected to be completed by 2025. Objective 4: To accomplish the total synthesis of aspidospermidine and tabersonine This objective has been achieved and the results have been published in Chemical Science (Chem. Sci. 2024, 15, 5730-5737). The iAFC reaction of indoles with AAR products not only greatly expanded the synthetic utility of AAR but also allowed access to the structural skeleton that could not be constructed by the intramolecular AFC reaction. To demonstrate such advantage of iAFC as compared to the intramolecular version, we undertook the total syntheses of uleine and aspidosperma alkaloids. The AAR-iAFC product was elaborated in 9-11 steps to furnish (+)-3-epi-N-nor-dasycarpidone, (+)-3-epi-dasycarpidone, and (+)-3-epi-uleine. Next, we focused our efforts on the total synthesis of aspidosperma alkaloids by exploiting iAFC of indoles with AAR products. The iAFC product was obtained in >26 g and used as the starting material for the synthesis of all aspidosperma alkaloids. The 6-exo-trig cyclization of failed to occur with samarium iodide (SmI2) or palladium catalysis (Heck) but could be realized via a radical mechanism by treatment with 1,10-azobis(cyclohexane-1-carbonitrile) (V-40) and tributyltin hydride under refluxed toluene to provide the tetracyclic core, which was common to all aspidosperma alkaloids. We have accomplished the collective total synthesis of six aspidosperma alkaloids: 1,2-didehydropseudoaspidospermidine, 1,2-dehydroaspidospermidine, vincadifformine, winchinine B, aspidospermidine, N-acetylaspidospermidine, within 9 steps.

16306920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306920.value: With the financial support of this project, we have made three major findings as follows. 1) Have developed a powerful method/strategy for chemical synthesis of indole alkaloids, leading to publication of three research articles in top journals (paspalinines, sarpagines, and aspidospermines, etc). 2) Have established five green and efficient oxidation/halogenation protocols in organic synthesis (electrochemistry, semipinacol, alcohol oxidation, desulfurization, and Hofmann/Curtius rearrangements, etc). 3) Have expanded the synthetic utility of furans and Achmatowicz rearrangements in organic synthesis and drug discovery.

16306920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306920.value: While the main aims have been achieved with the establishment of a new efficient methodology for assembly of indoles and furans into structurally complex indole alkaloids, the enantioselectivity of AFC remains poor and needs to be further improved, which might be attained by evaluating different furan substrates for aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement with handle to coordinate with chiral catalysts. The C2-C2’ coupling has been validated in this project, however, the synthetic utility has not been illustrated with total synthesis of indole alkaloids, which are targeted currently and might be achieved in the near future.

16306920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306920.value: The central theme of this project is to develop a new synthetic methodology for total synthesis of several indole alkaloids. Many secondary metabolites of this class possess potent yet highly specific bioactivities (therapeutic effects) and have attracted extensive research interest including chemical synthesis. The specific developed methodology herein involves intermolecular aza-Friedel-Crafts (AFC) reaction of Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) products with indoles. Full studies on this new methodology will employ a comprehensive examination of various promoters (Lewis acids or Bronsted acids) and substitution effects of indoles on the regioselectivity and efficiency. Our preliminary results showed that the enantioselectivity of AFC could be achieved using chiral BINOL-based phosphoric acid (ca. 20% ee). This finding is encouraging as a proof-of-concept and considerable efforts are entailed to improve enantioselectivity. To showcase the synthetic utility, four representative bioactive indole alkaloids; tacamonine, hirsutine, aspidospermidine and tabersonine are chosen as targets for total synthesis that features our innovative AFC reaction of AAR products with indoles. Our AFC methodology is established, and the total synthesis of these alkaloid natural products has been accomplished. The new methodology and strategy will greatly advance the chemical synthesis of indole alkaloids.

16307020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307020.value: Long persistent luminescent (LPL) materials possess fantastic potential for a wide range of applications because they can store excitation energy for extended periods of time, and slowly release energy as light. Use of these materials in in vivo imaging, anti-counterfeiting measures, and enhancing photovoltaic device efficiency has generated strong research interest. Unfortunately, currently the best LPL materials are inorganic in nature and accessible only via harsh synthetic conditions using heavy/rare-earth metals. In addition, the inorganic materials required can be difficult to mass produce and process, which hinders widespread adoption. Our group has been investigating organic materials with long-lived excited states, and we have recently observed that host-guest interactions can produce organic systems with LPL properties. This was achieved by incorporating a small number of molecules (guest) into a bulk matrix of another molecule (host). The combination of the host and guest was able to generate LPL. However, due to the limited number of examples of systems exhibiting organic LPL (OLPL), there are no clear design guidelines for their synthesis. Thus, in this proposed project, we aim to develop new organic materials exhibiting LPL. We will investigate the structure-property relationships of these materials to aid in the design of future systems. The practical applications of the materials will also be explored for the fields of biological sciences, anti-counterfeiting measures, and renewable energy technologies. Our previous work showed that host-guest interactions can drastically enhance LPL durations in organic systems, and thus we aim to systematically investigate which hosts and guests are most suitable for such properties. By carefully examining the energy differences between hosts and guests, and how the addition of electron-donating or -withdrawing groups affect the LPL properties, it will become possible to draw general mechanistic conclusions to aid in the generation of improved OLPL materials. In this proposed project we will examine how to best control the emission wavelengths of the OLPL materials, their LPL duration, and their emission efficiency. With additional theoretical analyses of their host-guest interactions, it will become possible to rationally design new OLPL materials for use in a variety of high-technology applications. It is expected that the proposed project will generate a large variety of new organic systems with LPL properties, which can be used for in vivo imaging without constant excitation, advanced anti-counterfeiting measures, and enhancing the efficiency of photovoltaic devices to increase the utility of solar energy. 超長持續發光材料能長時間儲存激發光源的能量並緩慢以光的形式發射出來，因而具有廣泛應用潛能。這類材料在生物成像、防偽以及光伏器件領域的應用引起學界濃厚研究興趣。然而，目前性能最佳的超長持續發光材料都是無機材料，它們需要利用到重/稀土金屬且合成條件苛刻，難以量產和加工，因而應用受限。 我們課題組長期從事長壽命激發態有機材料研究，近期已觀測到主客體相互作用可以產生超長持續發光現象。然而，目前觀測的實例有限，尚缺乏明確的超長持續發光有機材料設計原則。因此，在該項目中，我們旨在開發更多新型有機超長持續發光材料，系統研究結構-性能關係，提出普適性設計策略，並且探索它們在生物科學、防偽和可再生能源技術領域的應用。 我們的前期工作表明主客體作用可以大幅增加有機體系的持續發光時間，在此我們將系統研究何種主體和客體分子最適合實現這一性能。通過詳細研究主客體能級差、相對給/吸電子能力對發光性能的影響，有望得到普適性的機理與結論來指導獲取性能更佳的有機超長持續發光材料。在該項目中，我們將研究如何調控這類材料的發光波長、發光時間和發光效率，結合理論計算分析主客體相互作用，有望合理設計出適用於不同高科技應用領域的超長持續發光材料。預期本項目的執行將能獲得多種新型超長持續發光材料，並將它們成功應用於長余輝無背景生物成像和高級防偽技術領域，以及用來增強光伏器件效率和太陽能利用率。

16307020.label: Realisation of objectives
16307020.value: The purpose of this proposed project is to synthesize new organic materials showing long persistent luminescence characteristics. We believe through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goal, a novel system exhibiting room temperature phosphorescence (RTP) in the near infrared (NIR) region in both crystalline state and host-guest system was developed. Dithienopyrrole (DTP) with a high electron density was used as a core to lower the triplet state energy. Heteroatoms, including oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur are further incorporated to balance n-pi* and pi-pi* transitions to promote the inter-system crossing eﬃciency and stabilizing the triplet exciton. Halogen atoms are introduced to fine tune the RTP through diﬀerent chalcogen-halogen interactions and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) constants. The resulting DTP derivatives exhibit persistent NIR RTP at wavelengths of 645-702 nm with phosphorescence eﬃciencies of 0.5-2.4% and lifetimes of 0.24-3.68 ms in the crystalline state. Notably, DTP-Cl shows the longest lifetime of 3.68 ms compared to reported single-component organic RTP materials in the NIR region. By lowering the temperature to 77 K, the pi-pi interactions are strengthened due to the restriction of molecular motions. This stabilizes the triplet excimer, preventing its dissociation and nonradiative decay. Consequently, the emission shifts from 630 to 746 nm. The RTP performances of DTP derivatives can be further enhanced by doping them into a host matrix called BP-Br. Most of the current materials exhibiting long persistent luminescence (LPL) are multicomponent inorganic systems obtained by harsh synthetic procedures and often involve the use of expensive rare-earth metals. Thus, metal-free organic LPL (OLPL) systems have gained much interest recently because they can overcome most of the disadvantages of inorganic systems. Herein, a novel OLPL system exhibiting a detectable duration of up to 12 min under ambient conditions was developed. Unlike the previously developed OLPL systems, the present one is single component, which shows better reproducibility and enables large-scale production. The molecular design of this system was based on the current binary OLPL systems. By incorporating both electron-accepting and electron-donating moieties into a single molecule, the resulting system is able to generate both electrons and holes. The photophysical properties of the targeted compounds are carefully investigated to reveal their OLPL natures under different conditions, from which a mechanistic understanding of the underlying process was gained. Improving RTP efficiency and lifetime simultaneously in metal-free systems remains the biggest challenge for realizing their applications. In this report, a simple guest/host system with efficient RTP built from commercial sources based on an unconventional cluster exciton mechanism was disclosed. The guest (NL) was a traditional and illegal component for widespread mothballs, while the host (DCB) was a less flammable alternative to NL for manufacturing mothballs. Such a system shows a RTP efficiency of >20% with a ultralong lifetime, which is much better than those of metal-free RTP materials reported previously. In addition to the paramagnetic role from halogens, the strong RTP of NL/DCB was proposed to mainly arise from a cluster exciton, where electrons and holes are delocalized to promote strong ISC. The energy of the transient excited state quickly decays to the localized excited triplet state of the guest to give rise to efficient and ultralong RTP. The synergistic interaction between the guest and host in the excited state is different from the classical energy transfer model where only one species exists in the excited state at any time. This interpretation was based on detailed experimental and theoretical evidence and should advance the understanding in purely organic RTP systems. On the other hand, since the naked eye is more sensitive to green light, the RTP of NL/DCB is indeed recognizable by common people, even under soft room lighting. It was demonstrated in a safe manner in sealed containers that the initial ‘‘dark’’ DCB solid can show notable green afterglow emission at ambient temperature upon mixing with a trace amount of NL vapor. Development of room-temperature phosphorescent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with free heavy metal atoms, high quantum yields, and long lifetime has been the focus of this research area. However, it is rare to develop methods to tune the intrinsic RTP of MOFs. Herein, it is demonstrated that colour-, lifetime-, and intensity-tunable intrinsic RTP can be achieved in simple and classical heavy-atom-free CAU-10 MOFs by ligand functionalization. Through the introduction of electron-donating groups on the IPA ligand, materials with multicolours visible fluorescence and phosphorescence with different lifetimes at room temperature are successfully achieved. Compared with the crystals of pure organic ligand crystals, the MOFs present superior performance, tunability, and stability of RTP due to the immobilization of the ligand molecules by the strong metal−organic coordination bonds in the MOF structures. TD-DFT calculations describe the ISC process and illustrate that the electron-donating substituents influence the composition and electron density of the frontier orbitals to produce a colour-tunable emission. Diverse luminescence patterns are fabricated from these MOFs, making them promise to find applications in display, anticounterfeiting, and information encryption.

16307020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307020.value: Materials showing long persistent luminescence (LPL) are potential candidates for a wide range applications such as in vivo imaging anti-counterfeiting measures. Unfortunately, currently the best LPL materials are inorganic in nature and accessible only via harsh synthetic conditions using heavy/rare-earth metals. In addition, the inorganic materials required can be difficult to mass produce and process, which hinders widespread adoption. In this project, several purely organic LPL systems have been designed and synthesized. Through detailed investigations, we found that the introduction of electron-donating moiety helps reduce the triplet state energy. Heteroatoms, on the other hand, work to balance n-pi* and pi-pi* transitions to promote the intersystem crossing eﬃciency and stabilizing the triplet exciton. Halogen atoms help to tune the emission. Unprecedentedly, the dynamic transition process between the emission of monomer and excimer with temperature variations is captured. The results show that the dissociation and non-radiative decay of triplet excimer can quench the RTP in pi-stacked crystals. In addition to being abused globally as insect repellents, naphthalene (NL) is also a major product of coal tar. Furthermore, NL is a characteristic substance found in certain interstellar medium, which can indicate the evolution of galaxies and also a compound synthesized by some fungi to protect their host plants. The bright RTP observed in NL/dichlorobenzene systems should be of vital significance for sensing applications, not only in identifying illegal mothballs, but also in the fields of chemical industry, air quality monitoring, astronomy, and biosciences. As you can see in part C of this report, 15 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16307020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307020.value: Materials with long persistent luminescence can store excitation energy for extended periods of time, and slowly release energy as light. Use of these materials in in vivo imaging, anti-counterfeiting measures, and enhancing photovoltaic device efficiency has generated strong research interest. Particularly, the organic ones have received much attention because they are synthetically accessible by a diverse range of simpler approaches. They also feature much better processability and can be biologically inert. In this investigation, we have developed several LPL systems such as dithienopyrrole derivatives/BP-Br, [Zn(IPA)(4,4’-bpy)], [Zn(IPA)(3,3’-bpy)], diphenyl-4-(dimethylamino)phenylphosphorium salt and naphthalene/dichlorobenzene, and examine their photophysical properties and structure-property relationships by experimental methods and theoretical calculations. However, what we have done is just a beginning and there are many ways awaiting us to explore to guide the further design of LPL materials with improved performances. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the exploration of new systems and new strategies to obtain efficient and ultralong LPL materials. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to get further detail study on the LLP mechanism and meanwhile explore their high-technological applications.

16307020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307020.value: Materials showing long persistent luminescence (LPL) is the next generation of functional materials with wide potential applications. Particularly, the purely organic ones have received special attention because of their easier preparation, excellent processability and better biocompatibility. In this investigation, several such systems are designed and synthesized. They show high emission efficiencies and ultralong lifetimes, making them promise to be used in anti-counterfeiting, information encryption, luminescent sensors, etc.

16307420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307420.value: The electromagnetic wave is the main carrier of information in modern technology and in the real world, imperfections are inevitable. We aim to explore whether electromagnetic energy can be transported in an environment full of disorder and defects. Can disorder promote transmission, rather than suppressing it? Can artificial materials be designed whose signal transport functionality is immune to imperfections? When a wave encounters disorder or imperfections, it will be scattered to other directions. Anderson showed in 1958 (Nobel Prize in Physics 1977) that if the scattering is strong enough, the wave can be pinned by the imperfections (become "localized") and cannot propagate forward. Such an absence of wave transport is now called Anderson localization and it is a general wave interference phenomenon that applies to all kinds of waves, including electromagnetic waves. In this project, we seek to understand how disorder may affect the transmission of electromagnetic waves in photonic band gap materials that have topological protection. The idea of a photonic band gap was first introduced in 1987, by both Yablonovitch and John. Optical materials possessing photonic band gaps are generally called photonic crystals. John’s pioneering 1987 paper showed that strong disorder can localize light, thus prohibiting energy transmission in photonic crystals. However, recent breakthroughs in condensed matter physics and optics show that the transport on the boundary of a material can become robust against disorder if the material is “topological”, and if the disorder is not too strong. Our aim is to explore whether waves can propagate in the bulk and on the edge of strongly disordered topological photonic band gap systems. We will first use a network photonic band gap system which can configured to have different symmetries and dimensions. The electromagnetic waves travelling in the network can be measured point by point, giving a direct indication whether edge modes exist and whether the bulk modes are localized or delocalized. The network can be connected in a way that the waves travelling inside feels an artificial magnetic field (without the need of putting in any real magnet), and it is useful as some topological characteristics of topological material originates from magnetic flux that breaks the time-reversal symmetry. We will also study the disorder-induced localization and delocalization of a special type of photonic crystals that are optical counterparts of “quantum spin Hall” systems, which have topological characteristics even in the absence of an external field. 在该项目中，我们希望理解无序性会如何影响拓扑保护光子晶体中的电磁波传输行为。自从1987年Yablonovitch和John分别独立引入光子晶体的概念，光子晶体作为一种类新型人工材料已实现了以前所未有的方式对光场进行操控。John在其1987年的开创性文章中发现强的无序性可以局域化光场进而阻止光在光子晶体中的传输。由于现实世界中缺陷与无序无处不在，无序导致的局域化现象在技术应用上显然有着极其重要的价值。近期，凝聚态物理中突破性的发现表明在拓扑材料中电子的输运对无序有着极强的抗扰性，其中拓扑的含义是系统的能带和能隙可由一系列量子化的拓扑不变量表征。 我们将探究在具有强无序性的拓扑光子带隙系统中电磁波是否可以在其体内和边界上稳定的传播。我们将首先研究一类电缆网络系统。这种电缆网络系统在实验上有着特有的优势，因为这种系统由同轴电缆相连而成，构造一个新网络只需要重新以不同的方式连接电缆，因此这种系统是完全可循环利用的。电缆网络既可以是周期的也可以是非周期的。它也可以具有不同的维度和满足不同的对称性。通过特殊的连接，信号在网络中传播可感受到一个有效人工磁场（并非由真正的磁铁产生）。系统的本征态可以划分入几个不同的子系统，其中一些子系统是拓扑的而另一些是非拓扑的。当引入无序和缺陷时，我们可以同时对具有不同对称性的不同子系统进行探测。通过控制缺陷的类型，我们可以实现让具有不同对称性子系统间交叉耦合现象。我们还将研究光子Z2拓扑绝缘体中的局域化效应。光子Z2拓扑绝缘体是量子自旋霍尔系统的光学对应，我们将设计具有特殊对称性的光子晶体，使其可以在时间反演下具有类似费米子系统的性质，进而可以严格地模拟量子自旋霍尔系统。我们将通过设计结构引入人工非阿贝尔规范势来混合不同的自旋态，并由此构造类似于量子自旋霍尔系统中各种不同类型的自旋轨道耦合。我们的设计方案可以自由控制人工规范场的分布和自由控制自旋轨道耦合，因而可以实现观测不同类型的缺陷导致的无序效应。

16307420.label: Realisation of objectives
16307420.value: Objective 1: We proposed a method to create a rainbow concentrator for topological photonic states in 2D photonic crystals using the concept of synthetic dimensions. The synthetic dimension is formed by the translational degree of freedom of nanostructures within the unit cell of a 2D photonic crystal. By inducing translational deformation, we create a nontrivial topology in the synthetic dimension, resulting in Chern numbers. This deformation induced Chern number occurs without the need for an actual magnetic field; instead, it can be interpreted as a synthetic gauge field. As a consequence of this topological configuration, we observed the emergence of robust interface states at various frequencies. The topological rainbow effect enables the trapping of states with distinct frequencies, which can be controlled by adjusting the spatial modulation of the group velocities of the interface states. Moreover, the operating frequency and bandwidth of the topological rainbow can be easily tuned by manipulating the band gap of the photonic crystal. This configuration exhibit robustness against disorder, thanks to the inherent topological protection. It is worth noting that the topological principles we have employed can be applied to photonic crystals of any symmetry and arbitrary material composition, as long as a complete band gap exists [Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 113902 (2021)]. We then realized the system in a nano-photonics platform, with the aim to achieve robustness and insensitivity to disorder. We realized an on-chip nanophotonic topological rainbow achieved through the utilization of translational deformation as a synthetic dimension. To directly observe and measure the topological rainbow effect on a silicon-based photonic chip, we employed a high-resolution scattering scanning near-field optical microscope. The implementation of the topological rainbow using synthetic dimensions offers several advantages. It is not limited by optical lattice types, symmetries, materials, or wavelength bands, making it highly versatile and easily integrated on-chip and is robust against the usual fabrication error and disorder encountered in nano-fabrication processes [Nat. Commun. 13, 2586 (2022)]. Objective 1 and 2: We explored the localization/delocalization phenomena of bulk modes in a network system. This system can be configured to possess big photonic band gaps, even when subjected to disorder. Additionally, we explored the persistence of topological invariants, such as local Chern numbers, and topological boundary modes when different types of randomness were imposed on the network system. The chiral connectivity of the network induces non-zero Chern numbers within the non-zero angular momentum subspace. To characterize the topological features of the transmission line network in the presence of disorder, we employed the concept of local Chern numbers. We showed that both the local Chern numbers and the edge states exhibit remarkable robustness against onsite disorder. However, the quantization of local Chern numbers can be compromised by breaking the parity symmetry, leading to the absence of edge modes. We also observed non-integer peaks in the local Chern numbers within the bulk bands. However, we found that these non-zero, non-integral local Chern numbers are trivial and not associated with the existence of robust edge states [EPJ Appl. Metamat. 9, 4 (2022)]. We investigated the robustness of chiral zeroth Landau levels, which are bulk states that are topologically protected. We propose an experimental approach to realize these chiral Landau levels in a two-dimensional photonic system. Our method involves introducing an position dependent effective mass which interacts with the Dirac quasi-particles. As a result, the zeroth-order chiral Landau levels can be induced, and we have experimentally observed their one-way propagation characteristics. Furthermore, we have also conducted experimental tests to demonstrate the robustness of the chiral zeroth mode against defects and disorder in the system [Light: Science & Applications 12, 165 (July 4, 2023)]. We introduced a new concept of photonic alloys as disordered 2D topological materials. By combining non-magnetized and magnetized rods in a random configuration, we successfully realize photonic alloys in the microwave regime. This is a new concept and has attracted the attention of media [https://phys.org/news/2024-06-photonic-alloy-topological-properties.html] and highlighted by Phys. Rev. Lett. Our experimental investigation demonstrates that even at very low concentrations of magnetized rods, the photonic alloy supports non-reciprocal chiral edge states. Remarkably, our results indicate that the threshold concentrations required for the investigated system to exhibit topological behavior within the first non-trivial band gap approach zero in the thermodynamic limit for substitutional alloys. Photonic alloys represent a new category of disordered topological materials [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 223802 (2024), selected for editor’s suggestion]. We have expanded our investigation to include disordered non-Hermitian systems. In such systems that exhibit the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), the bulk spectrum under open boundary conditions deviates significantly from that of the periodic counterpart. This discrepancy poses a challenge to the conventional bulk-boundary correspondence and renders it inapplicable. To address this issue, we introduced a new approach called "doubling and swapping" to restore the bulk-boundary correspondence. As an illustrative example, we have employed the non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By extending our study to disordered systems, wherein the asymmetric hoppings are randomly swapped, we demonstrate that two distinct types of winding numbers can be defined. These winding numbers account for both the NHSE and the topological edge states in the system [Commun. Phys. 7: 140 (2024)]. When the skin effect arises, eigenstates within the bulk continuum can exhibit localization at the edges, making it difficult to differentiate between edge and bulk states. We established the bulk-boundary correspondence for a Chern insulator model featuring a non-Hermitian skin effect. We combined two approaches: the "non-Bloch" approach and the "biorthogonal" approach. Both of these approaches offer methods to suppress the skin effect, albeit relying on different mathematical tools. Additionally, we used a non-Bloch Chern number to characterize the system's topology and predict the number of topological edge bands. We delve into the localization and delocalization behavior exhibited by the edge states. This analysis contributes to a comprehensive understanding of the intricate properties of systems with a non-Hermitian skin effect [Phys. Rev. B 105, 075128 (2022)]. We conducted an experimental exploration of the eigenvalue splitting rules and the corresponding topological characterization near defective points in a prototypical non-Hermitian system using an electrical network circuit system. Additionally, we presented a mathematical analysis demonstrating that the exponent of phase rigidity and the discriminant number can jointly serve as topological invariants to fully characterize the system. [Phys. Rev. 108, 115427 (2023)]. Objective 3: We explored the effect of disorder in photonic Z2 topological insulators. That disorder can induce nontrivial topology is a surprising discovery in topological physics. By taking transverse magnetic and transverse electric polarizations as pseudospin degrees of freedom, we proposed a scheme to realize disorder-induced symmetry-protected topological phase transitions in two-dimensional photonic crystals with a combined time-reversal, mirror, and duality symmetry. We demonstrated that the disorder-induced symmetry-protected topological phase persists even without pseudospin conservation, thereby realizing a photonic Z2 topological Anderson insulators, in contrast to a Z-classified quantum spin Hall (QSH) topological Anderson insulator (TAI) with decoupled spins. By formulating a new scattering approach, we show that the topology of both the QSH and Z2 TAIs can be manifested by the accumulated spin rotations of the reflected waves. Such systems can be implemented as 2D photonic crystals comprising of bi-anisotropic materials [Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 043902 (2022)].

16307420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307420.value: In this project, we seek to understand how disorder may affect the transmission of electromagnetic waves in photonic crystals that have topological protection. We want to explore whether wave can propagate in the bulk and on the edge of strongly disordered photonic band gap systems that are “topological". Instead of repeating the details given in section 5.3, we highlight some interesting aspects here. We employed different systems to explore the effect. We used network systems that have some unique advantages. Experimentally, it is as simple as coaxial cables connected together and the system is completely “recyclable” because building a new network simply means reconnecting the cables in a different manner. The network can be periodic or aperiodic or disordered. It can have different symmetries and dimensionalities. It can be configured so that the signals travelling in the network feels a synthetic magnetic field (but without the need of adding a real magnet). The eigenstates can be classified into different sectors, some are topological and some are not. When disorder is introduced, we have probe the disorder effects simultaneously for different sectors belonging to different symmetry classes. We used circuits, which can model tight-binding models. The advantage of circuit is that we can employ current-inversion negative impedance converters (INICs) to achieve non-reciprocal hoppings. this allows use to realize Hatano-Nelson models, which is the standard and most popular class of models to study the interplay of disorder, localization and the effect of non-Hermiticity such as skin effect. Another interesting advance is the achievement of topology without a real field. This is very useful for photonic cystals if we want to apply to photonics. For example, in the work concerning "topological rainbow", the topology is characterized by Chern numbers, which are achieved by using a "deformation dimension". This makes the system feasible to implement in photonics regime, as demonstrated experimentally. A rainbow concentrator can collect weak signals and route different frequency components to different spatial locations. Another interesting way to impose synthetic gauge field is using the concept of position dependent effective mass, which is applicable to photonic crystals that have Dirac points. We introduced the new notion of disordered topological photonic alloy, which is a new way to induce topological transport without order and the work has been highlighted by Phys. Rev. Lett. and reported in media.

16307420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307420.value: Our immediate future plan is to demonstrate photonic Z2 topological insulators experimentally in the microwave regime. There are several approaches to designing bi-anisotropic metamaterials that can realize Z2 topological insulators. One approach involves starting with materials that exhibit high double Dirac cones at the K/K' point due to duality symmetry. Another possible direction is to explore the implementation of these ideas in optical frequencies. Extending our study on the effect of disorder to photonic band gap systems can also be expanded to non-Hermitian systems. We have already made some progress in this area. However, these systems are indeed very complex, especially when considering the intricate interplay between disorder, gain/loss, non-reciprocity, and external fields. It is important to note that disorder can lead to localization, but a magnetic field can induce delocalization due to disruption of interference. Additionally, non-reciprocity and asymmetric hopping can also induce localization in the form of the skin effect. These effects become more complex in higher dimensions than 1D, whether symmetry mismatch can induce skin effect. The concept of a photonic alloy is intriguing, and we plan to investigate its implementation at higher frequencies.

16307420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307420.value: Topological photonic materials offer a significant advantage due to their inherent robustness against defects, disorder, and imperfections. They possess topological protection, which prevents scattering or backscattering of certain modes or states by defects. This robustness enables efficient transmission of electromagnetic waves without notable loss or distortion, making them highly desirable for transportation applications. However, the presence of very strong disorder can lead to disorder-induced localization, which compromises transport in topological photonic materials. This project aims to investigate how strong disorder affects the transmission of electromagnetic waves in photonic crystals with topological protection. By studying various prototypical systems such as network systems, network circuit systems, and photonic crystals, we achieved a deeper understanding of the limitations and constraints of topological photonic systems in the presence of disorder. Encouragingly, certain topological materials can withstand strong disorder and provide robust transport. The good news is that disorder can in fact transform a non-topological photonic material into a topological one under specific conditions. This transformation gives rise to protected edge states that are highly resistant to disorder-induced scattering. Consequently, these materials exhibit robust electromagnetic transport properties along their edges, even in the presence of strong disorder.

16307620.label: Project Objectives
16307620.value: Our first objective is to develop and optimize an indexing method that enables one to retrieve, in a reasonable amount of time, the most similar matches to any given query tandem mass spectrum among billions of existing spectra in a spectral archive. To handle the enormous and rapidly growing amount of proteomic data, the retrieval time must not scale with archive size. Our second objective is to develop the first spectral archive search engine for proteomics, bypassing the need to predict peptide fragmentation patterns or to build spectral libraries. To take advantage of the additional information provided by a spectral archive, the scoring function of this search engine should incorporate spectral similarities and the multiplicity of matches to the same peptide ion. The search engine should also allow mass-shifted matches to support open modification searching.

16307620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307620.value: Proteomics aims at the complete characterization of the proteome, the set of all proteins in a biological system, in a high-throughput manner. In contrast to reductionist approaches, proteomics allows one to observe the entire cellular machinery, and is particularly helpful in generating useful hypotheses or screening for molecular targets of interest. However, compared to sequencing, this powerful technology has been underutilized by life scientists, which can be partly attributed to challenges in data analysis. In the most common “shotgun proteomics” work-flow based upon the liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS) platform, proteins are identified and quantified indirectly by experimental observations of their constituent peptides in the form of tandem mass (MS/MS) spectra, which are typically identified by sequence database searching. Since this process is memoryless and makes no reference to the mountain of publicly available data, it is error-prone and computationally costly, and often a burden to the less computationally inclined researchers. To address this challenge, this proposed research will deliver a novel MS/MS identification method that compares a query spectrum to all previously observed spectra, analogous to sequence alignments routinely performed in genomics. This method, which we call “spectral archive search,” demands a new way of organizing proteomic data to cope with the rapidly growing data volume. Instead of storing spectra in flat files or grouping them by peptides, we must organize them by similarity in so-called spectral archives, such that similar spectra are clustered in the same “neighborhood” and can be retrieved in a short time that does not scale with archive size. This will be achieved by an indexing scheme that can not only retrieve approximate nearest neighbors of a query spectrum, but also sort them by similarity. With this ability, peptide identification can be accomplished by an instance-based classifier that incorporates cluster structure information. The search is done by the central data repository as the archive is simultaneously updated, effectively coupling the tedious peptide identification step with data deposition. This should also be more accurate and robust than existing methods, since it bypasses the need to construct a model (a predicted or representative spectrum) for a candidate peptide. We plan to deploy our new search engine in a real proteomic data repository, to ensure wide adoption by the community and to evaluate its performance dynamically over time. If successful, this project will greatly simplify proteomic data analysis and bring proteomics one step closer to genomics in terms of accessibility. 蛋白質組學旨在以高通量的方式完整表徵蛋白質組（生物系統中所有蛋白質的集合）。與還原論方法相反，蛋白質組學技術允許人們觀察整個細胞機制，有助於生成假設或者篩選感興趣的分子靶標。然而相比基因測序，蛋白質組學技術尚未被生命科學家充分利用。這可以部分歸結於數據分析的挑戰。在基於液相色譜-質譜（LC-MS）平臺的最常見的“鳥槍法蛋白質組學”工作流程中，蛋白質的定性和定量分析是間接地通過實驗觀察構成它們的肽完成的。這些肽被采集為串聯質譜圖的形式，並由序列庫搜索方法 鑑定。由於數據分析過程是無記憶的，並且不參考公開數據，因此它容易出錯，計算成本很高，也常常給非計算型的研究人員帶來困難。 為了應對這一挑戰，這項擬議的研究將開發一種新穎的MS / MS鑑定方法。這種方法將查詢的譜圖和所有之前觀察到的譜圖做對比，類似於基因組學中常規的序列比對，我們稱之為“質譜檔案搜索”。這種方法需要一種全新方式來組織蛋白質組數據以應對快速增長的數據量。我們不再將譜圖存儲在許多文本文件中或按肽進行分組，而是將譜圖按照彼此的相似度組織在所謂的譜圖檔案中，使得相似的譜圖聚集在同一個“鄰域”，並且能快速讀取，其讀取時間不隨檔案容量線性增長。這些目標將通過索引方案來實現，該方案可以讀取所查詢譜圖的近似最近鄰居，並且按照相似度對鄰居譜圖排序。憑藉這種能力，肽的鑑定可以通過一個采用了聚類結構信息的分類算法來實現。搜索的過程可以在中心數據倉庫更新譜圖檔案的時候同時完成，這樣有效地把冗長的肽段鑑定和數據存儲約簡為同一個步驟。這也應該比現有方法更加準確和可靠，因為它不需要為候選肽構建（理論預測的或選擇代表的）譜圖模型。我們計劃將新的搜索引擎部署在真實的蛋白質組數據存儲庫中，以確保被社區廣泛採用，並隨著時間的推移動態評估其性能。如果成功，該項目將極大簡化蛋白質組學數據分析，並使蛋白質組學在可及性方面更接近基因組學。

16307620.label: Realisation of objectives
16307620.value: The captioned project has been completed with full realization of the objectives. Objective 1 Our first objective is to develop and optimize an indexing method that enables one to retrieve, in a reasonable amount of time, the most similar matches to any given query tandem mass spectrum among billions of existing spectra in a spectral archive. To handle the enormous and rapidly growing amount of proteomic data, the retrieval time must not scale with archive size. This objective has been completed through the work of Long WU during and after his Ph. D., resulting in a publication in Nature Communications (Wu et al., Nature Communications 14, 6267, 2023, journal paper #3 in the list of research outcomes). More details of the algorithm have been described in the progress report and in the paper. Briefly, the outline of the algorithm described in the proposal was implemented and tested on a spectral archive of up to 100 million spectra, and the speed of approximate nearest neighbor retrieval was shown to be unaffected by the archive size. Since the progress report, more optimization was performed to find the best hyper-parameters, and the graphical user interface was vastly improved. The resulting software was named “Spectroscape” and deployed on our own server, which houses about 100 million spectra of human data in our possession. Objective 2 Our second objective is to develop the first spectral archive search engine for proteomics, bypassing the need to predict peptide fragmentation patterns or to build spectral libraries. To take advantage of the additional information provided by a spectral archive, the scoring function of this search engine should incorporate spectral similarities and the multiplicity of matches to the same peptide ion. The search engine should also allow mass-shifted matches to support open modification searching. This objective has been completed, which is to be disseminated in a manuscript in preparation. Spectroscape has a function to perform a spectral archive search of a batch of query spectra, which will simply return the list of true nearest neighbors. To take advantage of the likely multiplicity of matches to the correct identification, as well as the connectivity information in the “neighborhood,” we decided to recast the problem as one of spectrum clustering. Using Spectroscape to build an adjacency matrix efficiently, and then the established density-based clustering non-parametric algorithm (DBSCAN) to partition the neighborhood into tightly-connected clusters while removing outliers and bridges, the putative identification of any query spectrum is determined to be the majority identification of the cluster it belongs to. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we ran this algorithm for all existing spectra in the archive (which can be thought of as an “internal” spectral archive search) and managed to re-annotate millions of previously unidentified or mis-identified spectra. To validate the search results rigorously, we adopted two different approaches. First, we developed a spectrum prediction model using deep learning (Chan et al., Journal of Proteome Research 22, 3672-3702, 2023, journal paper #4 in the list of research outcomes), which enables us to produce a high-quality reference spectrum for any unmodified peptide ion. (The method does not work as well for modified peptide ion due to insufficient training data, which remains ongoing work.) We can then validate the search result independently by comparing the query spectrum to the predicted spectrum of the putative identification, without relying on the annotations of the retrieved spectra from the spectral archive. Second, we developed a method to properly model the score distribution of lower hits (i.e., non-highest scoring peptide-spectrum matches) without using decoys, which is necessary for spectral archive search (Madej and Lam, Journal of Proteome Research 22, 1159-1171, 2023, journal paper #2 in the list of research outcomes). The parametric distributions of the lower hits can be used to calculate p-values, and in case of multiple lower hits identified to the same peptide ion, the p-values can be combined by Fisher’s method to produce a statistically meaningful score at the peptide level for each query spectrum. This method still needs more thorough validation to confirm that the scores are well-calibrated, but this would require a ground-truth dataset which is difficult to generate for spectral archives. Objective 3 (removed due to partial funding) Our originally proposed Objective 3 was to deploy the spectral archive search engine in a real proteomic data repository with a user-friendly web interface, in order to maximize its usage by the community, as well as to collect real-time data to evaluate the effectiveness of the method over time. Additional software tools for query data submission, result visualization and automated validation will be developed. Due to partial funding, we decided not to pursue the originally proposed Objective 3 within the project period. However, for full disclosure, we are working with the PeptideAtlas data repository (www.peptideatlas.org) to integrate Spectroscape into their user interface. There are considerable technical challenges due to software compatibility and cybersecurity issues, which we hope to resolve in the near future in collaboration with the PeptideAtlas team.

16307620.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307620.value: The major research outcome of this project was an efficient indexing scheme that enables real-time visualization of a spectral archive, and the first spectral archive search engine for proteomics. The software Spectroscape was released as open-source software and deployed on a server for the community to use. The project also led to the development of several other enabling advances that can be employed in the scoring and validation of spectral archive search results, and more generally for other search engines as well. Another outcome of the project was the training of two Ph. D. students Ayman Hoque (expected graduation in 2025) and Dominik Madej (graduated in 2024), one M. Phil. Student, Chak Ming Jerry Chan, and several undergraduate students in their final-year projects.

16307620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307620.value: We believe we have taken a crucial first step in the ultimate goal of reusing the massive amounts of proteomics data collected by the community. The vision of organizing spectra by similarity in an efficient manner was largely realized by an indexing scheme that facilitate the searching of a spectral archive. While we have a preliminary method for scoring spectral archive search results and validating them using predicted spectra, we continue to refine those methods for wider applicability (e.g. modified peptides) and more statistical rigor. Efforts are also ongoing to bring bigger impact to the community by integrating the software tools with the existing data repositories (the originally proposed Objective 3).

16307620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307620.value: Proteomics, the high-throughput identification of all proteins in a biological system, is now widely employed in life science research. As one of the “omics” fields, however, proteomics is both blessed and burdened by the enormous amount of data generated. Such data, though made publicly available, is currently poorly organized and reused. To take advantage of this data, the best way is to organize the peptide mass spectra by similarity in a structure called a spectral archive. The challenge is in overcoming the computational cost as the archive size increases over time. This research project overcame this challenge by developing an indexing scheme to vastly speed up the retrieval of approximate nearest neighbors, which enables real-time visualization and efficient searching of a spectral archive, consisting of potentially billions of spectra.
