16307820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307820.value: 氮質氣溶膠是環境大氣氣溶膠的重要組成部分，對大氣能見度及區域乃至全球氣候變化有顯著影響，其沉降過程是生態系統重要的氮素輸入途徑之一。氮質氣溶膠可分為無機氮和有機氮氣溶膠。無機氮氣溶膠主要包括銨鹽和硝酸鹽，其大氣濃度水平和行為已得到廣泛認識。然而，有機氮氣溶膠是一類組成極其複雜的混合物，目前人們對有機氮總量的認識仍非常有限。現有的有限的測量數據表明全球尺度上氣溶膠中水溶性有機氮約占到水溶性總氮的30%。然而，由於分析技術限制，當前十分缺乏對水不溶性有機氮的定量。因此，大氣氣溶膠中總有機氮處於什麼濃度水平、有何種環境影響及生態意義很大程度上仍不得而知。 本研究將致力於開發一台可以同時測定以濾膜採集的氣溶膠樣品中碳含量以及無機和有機氮含量的儀器。濾膜上的碳質氣溶膠和氮質氣溶膠在特定溫控程序下同步熱解析，而後被氧化轉化成二氧化碳和氮氧化物進而被測定。由於無機氮組分只產生氮信號而有機氮組分同時產生氮信號和碳信號，因此對特定溫控條件下碳信號和氮信號的同步測定可幫助區分無機和有機氮氣溶膠。該分析儀將可能實現對濾膜氣溶膠中無機氮和有機氮的快速測定（每30分鐘分析一個樣品），進而可在實現在本項目之內分析數百個樣品。我們計劃分析在中國珠三角地區五個站點已採集的共約300個PM2.5樣品，從而獲得該地區有機氮氣溶膠的大氣濃度水平和來源情況，並結合區域大氣化學模式來評估有機氮氣溶膠幹濕沉降的環境影響。

16307820.label: Realisation of objectives
16307820.value: Objective 1: Development of an aerosol C & N analyzer for joint determination of carbon and nitrogen content and simultaneous determination of organic nitrogen (ON), and inorganic nitrogen (IN) in filter-based aerosol samples. We have assembled an aerosol C&N analyzer for offline analysis. A novel approach to achieve simultaneous quantification of inorganic nitrogen (IN) and organic nitrogen (ON) is realized through using programmed thermo-evolution of carbonaceous and nitrogenous aerosols and chemiluminescent detection coupled with multivariate curve resolution (MCR) data treatment. We characterized thermograms of individual IN standards, aerosol ON mixture, and ambient aerosol sample under a 6-step temperature program (150 ℃, 180 ℃, 300 ℃, 400 ℃, 500 ℃, and 800 ℃). The aerosol ON mixture is a sample of humic-like substances isolated from water extract of an aerosol sample and rid of water-soluble IN through a solid-phase extraction procedure. Thermal program characteristics of identification utility include: (1) NH4NO3 produces a major fraction of N signal at 150 ℃ and a minor fraction at higher temperature steps; (2) (NH4)2SO4 evolves mostly at the 180 ℃ and 300 ℃ steps, consistent with a previous mechanistic study reporting its decomposition and releasing NH3 at 170 ℃ to form (NH4)3H(SO4)229; (3) NH4HSO4 produces nearly all N signal at 300 ℃ step; and (4) Over half of the aerosol C contents evolves at the last three temperature steps (400 ℃, 500 ℃, and 800 ℃), while minor C signal evolves at the 150 ℃ and 180 ℃ temperature steps. These results qualitatively suggest that N signals at the 150 ℃ and 180 ℃ steps are mostly ascribed to the evolution of aerosol IN, while aerosol organics evolve dominantly at temperatures higher than 180 ℃. The low C/N ratios of PM sample at the 150 ℃ and 180 ℃ steps (0.37 and 0.63) indicate dominant presence of IN while the significantly higher C/N ratios (6.2-21.7) at the last three temperature steps clearly signal the predominance of ON. We have tested our methodology using 36 synthetic mixtures of (NH4)2SO4-NH4NO3-HULIS.Additionally, we tested our method using 60 ambient samples. The MCR-modelled IN concentrations and those independently measured IN (i.e., the sum of NO3--N and NH4+-N) using IC method are in excellent agreement (R2: 0.99, slope: 0.99). We further compare the MCA-modelled NO3--N and NH4+-N masses with those measured by the IC method. High correlations (R2: 0.98 and 0.99) and slope close to unity (1.14 and 0.95) are obtained for both IN species. By successfully resolving the IN portions from the joint thermograms, the MCR method is able to achieve simultaneous determination of IN and ON in the aerosol samples. Objective 2: Source investigation of ON through analyzing seasonal and spatial variation of ON and other chemical components using archived filter-based aerosol samples collected in the past. We used the laboratory Aerosol N Analyzer to quantify ON in ca. six hundred aerosol filter samples collected from twelve sites under varying urban influences in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) and other locations in China and spanning a year at most sites. A north-south concentration gradient is recorded for ON, with the average ON at 1.4 µgN/m3 in northern China, 0.7 µgN/m3 over the urban sites, and 0.5 µgN/m3 over suburban/rural PRD in southern China. The north-south contrast and the urban-suburban/rural contrast suggest broad association of ON sources with urban emissions. The site-average of the fraction of ON in total N is in the range of 17-31%, indicating ON represents a significant fraction of aerosol N. Utilizing ON and other major aerosol chemical constituents, and source-specific elements and organic molecules, available for only three of the sites (one urban, one suburban, and one rural site), we carried our positive matrix factorization (PMF) analysis of sources. The three sites are (1) Tsuen Wan (TW), an urban site in Hong Kong, (2) Nansha (NS), a rural site in south China, and (3) a suburban site of Beijing (BJ) in north China. The resolved factors consist of 7 primary sources (i.e, mixed industrial emissions and coal combustion, vehicular emissions, ship emissions, biomass burning, primary biological particles (PBA), dust, and sea salt) and two secondary factors (i.e., sulfate-rich and nitrate-rich factors). Each resolved factor (source) can be clearly identified according to the source-specific tracers. The source analysis identifies biomass burning (27-38%) and secondary formation (~30%) as common major ON sources, with primary biological particle emission a prominent ON source in non-urban environments and vehicle emission a significant source of aerosol ON at the urban site. While these results based on samples of daily resolution provide some preliminary quantitative understanding of ON sources, such source analysis is only a first step, and the results are coarse in time-resolution. Objective 3: Development of a semi-continuous aerosol C, ON and IN analyzer and field test-deployment for evaluating its use in identifying ON sources. With the experience learned from the offline aerosol C&N analyzer, we have also put together a prototype online version of the aerosol C&N analyzer. Difficulties were met in using a different model of NOx detector and in maintaining a proper flow split between C and N detector channels. These issues are now solved, and we are able to collect one data every 2 hour cycle. The online instruments were tested and validated by comparison with off-line analysis results obtained from filter-based samples at our HKUST air quality research supersite. A second online aerosol N analyzer was assembled and successfully deployed in Shanghai. Objective 4: Model assessment of environment impacts of aerosol ON via dry and wet deposition in our study region Prof. Tzung-May Fu, the co-I of this project, led the effort to simulate aerosol ON using Weather Research and Forecasting-Geos-Chem (WRF-GC) model. We constructed a comprehensive global model of atmospheric gaseous and particulate organic nitrogen, including the latest knowledge on emissions and secondary formations. Using this model, we simulated global atmospheric particulate ON abundances consistent with observations. Our estimated global atmospheric ON deposition was 26 Tg N yr −1 , predominantly in the form of particulate ON (23 Tg N yr −1 ) and mostly from wildfires (37%), oceans (22%) and aqueous productions (17%). Globally, ON p contributed as much as 40% to 80% of the total N deposition downwind of biomass-burning regions. In carrying out work to achieve Objectives 1 and 3, two post-doctoral fellows were deployed in developing the two versions of aerosol N analyzers- an offline version and an online version. Initially, our plan was to involve two PG students for the tasks. However, at the time of the project kick-off, we could not find suitable PG students who possess sufficient familiarity with instrument development. This deviation has caused significant overspending in the research staff category.

16307820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307820.value: Inorganic nitrogen (IN) and organic nitrogen (ON) molecules constitute a significant part of atmospheric aerosol. Unlike IN, the total ON quantity remained largely unquantified due to a lack of a simple and direct measurement method. In this project we have effectively addressed this analytical deficiency by developing an aerosol nitrogen analyzer. The major achievement and findings include: 1. We developed an analyzer system that utilizes programmed thermal evolution of carbonaceous and nitrogenous aerosols and chemiluminescence detection coupled with the multivariate curve resolution data treatment to achieve simultaneous quantification of IN and ON in filter samples (Yu X. et al., 2021). The system is capable of detecting IN and ON as low as 96 ng N per sample on a small filter aliquot (1 cm2) without any pretreatment and applicable to both PM2.5 and PM10 samples (Yu X et al., 2023a). 2. We determined aerosol ON in 600+ aerosol filter samples collected from sites of varying urban influence in the Pearl River Delta and other sites in China using our recently developed aerosol N analyzer (Yu X et al., 2024). Annual average ON concentration was in the range of 0.4–1.4 μgNm−3, representing 17–31% of aerosol total nitrogen. Monte Carlo simulations constrained by paired ON and organic carbon measurements suggest N-containing organic molecules contributed typically 37–50% to ambient organic aerosols. Source apportionment analysis reveals that biomass burning and secondary formation, and primary biological aerosol are dominant ON sources. 3. We built a prototype of semi-continuous aerosol nitrogen analyzer that provides bihourly time resolution of IN and ON monitoring (Li JJ et al., 2022). The online instrument was field-tested at a site in Hong Kong and measurements were validated through comparing with IN measured by ion chromatography analysis of offline filters (Li JJ et al., 2022). A second unit of online aerosol N analyzer was assembled and successfully deployed in an urban location in Shanghai (Yu X et al., 2023b). 4. We constructed a comprehensive global model of atmospheric gaseous and particulate ON, including the latest knowledge on emissions and secondary formations (Li YM et al., 2023). Using this model, we simulated global atmospheric ON p abundances consistent with observations. Model results indicate that aerosol ON deposition constituted the dominant external N supply to the N-limited boreal forests, tundras, and the Arctic Ocean, and its importance may be amplified in a future warming climate.

16307820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307820.value: We have built on the success of this project and secured funding for a subsequent GRF project titled "Investigating sources of nitrogenous organic aerosols". The prototype semi-continuous aerosol N analyzer built during this project is being further developed to improve robustness in its field deployment. Additionally, we are also collaborating with researchers from different provinces of China to map aerosol inorganic nitrogen and organic nitrogen across the country.

16307820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307820.value: Nitrogen (N) is a significant element that constitutes ambient organic aerosol, serving as an important source of supplementary nutrition for ecosystems after deposition. Chemically, they fall into two groups, i.e, inorganic N and organic nitrogen (ON). While abundance and chemistry of inorganic N are largely established, aerosol ON is hugely complex in its molecular composition and the total ON quantity had been almost un-characterized until this project. In this work, we have successfully developed an aerosol N analyzer that enables direct and simultaneous measurements of organic and inorganic N in aerosol samples. The analyzer utilizes programmed thermal evolution of carbonaceous and nitrogenous aerosols and chemiluminescence detection coupled with the multivariate curve resolution data treatment to achieve simultaneous quantification of inorganic N and ON. This method breakthrough has enabled the quantitative survey of 600+ aerosol samples collected from sites of varying urban influence in the Pearl River Delta and other places in China, thus revealing a large contribution of nitrogenous molecules to ambient organic aerosols. The new instrument and the new data generated will bring forth a breakthrough in our ability to describe and model organic aerosols and to assess their environmental impacts, such as atmospheric nitrogen nutrient inputs to ecosystems.

16308020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308020.value: 近年來，使用馬約拉納費米子進行拓撲量子計算的實用設備的開發吸引了越來越多的關注，因為這種方法比傳統的量子計算具有容錯的優勢。近期的理論研究預測，準一維拓撲超導體可用於在其扭結或末端位點捕獲馬約拉納費米子，因此它們被高度視為展示拓撲量子計算的潛在材料平台。但是,到目前為止，由於馬約拉納費米子的產生，檢測和編織仍處於起步階段，因此該領域的可行設備尚未實現。 由於其引人入勝的能帶結構, 拓撲絕緣體被認為在多種應用中具有很好的前景。最近鉍-雙層已經被確認是具有拓撲邊緣態的二維拓撲絕緣體，而碲化鉍和類似化合物是具有拓撲表面/界面態的三維拓撲絕緣體。我們的研究小組最近通過分子束外延技術演示了高質量外延碲化鉍/碲化鐵的製備，並在其界面處發現了一種罕見的二維超導性。我們的進一步研究證實了該異質結構的碲化鉍頂層也具有超導能隙，其與二維超導界面的超導能隙不同，這歸因於超導性的鄰近效應。最近，我們還發現了另一種拓撲絕緣體/碲化鐵系統, 那就是碲化銻/碲化鐵異質結,也具有二維超導特性，並發現了拓撲絕緣體層的拓撲界面態可能是誘發觀察到的二維超導性的本源。如果可以研製鉍-雙層/碲化鐵異質結,這個結構可能會產生邊緣超導，因為鉍-雙層的拓撲邊緣態很可能會在此異質結構的界面邊緣處誘發超導。因此，三維和二維拓撲絕緣體/碲化鐵異質結構或可形成理想的拓撲超導體，可用於實現可行的拓撲量子計算設備。 我們建議生長鉍-雙層/碲化鐵和碲化銻/碲化鐵異質結構，然後通過采用合適的樣品幾何形狀或納米線製造技術進行研究它們可能具有的準一維拓撲超導。我們的研究旨在在擬定的有望實現拓撲量子計算單元的準一維材料系統中形成和檢測馬約拉納費米子。 我們團隊在拓撲量子材料的分子束外延生長,納米加工工藝,化學成分和電子傳輸特性的表徵均具有廣泛專業知識和經驗,為我們實施擬定的研究項目提供了強而有力的支持。

16308020.label: Realisation of objectives
16308020.value: Regarding the first objective, we had tried to fabricate a Bi(111) thin film on GaAs(111)B substrate, Al2O3(0001) substrate, ZnSe (111)B buffer, Bi2Te3(0011) buffer and Mica(001) substrate. However, the resulting Bi(111) layers are not continuous, instead they contain separated islands and sharp rods, which seems to be an intrinsic obstacle for the growth of Bi(111) thin film. Recently, we conducted a series of FeTe growth on Bi2Te3 by the MBE technique through varying the substrate temperatures alongside modifications to the source cell temperatures, resulting in three typical FT-BT samples grown under different growth conditions. The structures of the three samples were analysed via RHEED observation, HRXRD profiling, and HR-STEM imaging. Our analysis reveals that specific growth conditions of the top FeTe layer could lead to the extraction of Te atoms from the Bi2Te3 layer, facilitating the transformation of Bi2Te3 into Bi4Te3, and with a higher Fe/Te ratio, even into Bi6Te3. Moreover, a lower growth temperature of FeTe could avoid Te extraction from Bi2Te3 and form a FeTe/Bi2Te3 heterostructure. Among these results, it is interesting to point out that at the interface of the FeTe/Bi4Te3 heterostructure, a Bi-bilayer (see Figure 4(b) of [Part C: 8(3)] Thus indeed a FeTe/Bi-bilayer structure has been realized in a special way. Our electrical transport measurements reveal that all three FT-BT samples display superconductivity with the FeTe/Bi2Te3 sample enjoying the highest superconductivity quality. Magneto-transport studies reveal that the induced superconductivity seems to have a 3D nature though its underlying mechanism is unclear at the moment. Some related research works were also performed, such as the realization of a new structural phase of tetragonal FeTe consisting of c-axis-aligned nanocrystals and a superconducting FeTe/layered-MnTe heterostructure, which will be further addressed in Section 6.1. Regarding objectives 2 and 3, our group has reported previously that both Bi2Te3/FeTe [Nature Communications, 5, Article number: 4247 (2014)] and Sb2Te3/FeTe [PNAS, 117 (1) 221-227 (2019)] heterostructures display 2D superconductivity. However, these studies also revealed that the Sb2Te3 layer suffers from a much higher conductivity than that of the Bi2Te3 layer, thus the former heterostructure may be more favorable to trap the Majorana fermions for the quasi-1D nanostructure proposed in this project. Thus we decided to devote our effort to the fabrication and characterization of Bi2Te3/FeTe quasi-1D nanostructures. We have demonstrated a fabrication process for Bi2Te3/FeTe nanowire devices for electrical transport and Andreev reflection point contact spectroscopy experiments at one end of the nanowire. Atomic force microscopy was used to determine the surface morphology of the Bi2Te3/FeTe nanowire, demonstrating that the heterostructure remains intact in the nanowire. Electrical transport and Andreev reflection point contact spectroscopy show that the interfacial superconductivity is preserved and exhibits similar characteristics to 2D Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructures with a twin-gap structure and a zero-bias conductance anomaly. While the overall gap structures appear rather smeared due to enhanced fluctuations in the reduced dimensionality, the ZBCP (zero-bias conductance peak) is sharper than in 2D samples and we have discussed possible links to unconventional superconductivity, Andreev bound states from the excess iron in FeTe or Majorana zero modes. With the present experiment, we are only at the beginning and cannot provide a conclusive explanation for the ZBCP. The search for Majorana zero modes has been proven to be far more difficult than originally assumed, with the most spectacular reports on its observation all been retracted. The aim of this work is to promote a new potential platform, which can be easily realized in a simple top-down approach, and as we demonstrated with another device, a Bi2Te3/FeTe nanoribbon, with a particularly clean tunneling interface formed within the epitaxially-grown material without the need for an external tunneling lead, thus avoiding the so-called “soft-gap” problem, which is considered as the main obstacle in approaches based on free-standing nanowires. It is worth mentioning that objective 3, “detecting Majorana fermions at the two ends of the proposed nanostructure”, has not been explored detailed enough, which indeed is quite challenging to everyone in the relevant community since its predicted signature could also be caused by some other mechanisms. Further studies along this direction will be addressed in Section 6.2. This project's general expenses have largely exceeded the approved budget due to the necessity of conducting more trial runs than initially anticipated for the development of the new material systems under investigation, As a result, additional FIB and TEM imaging experiments were required, which entail rather high costs.

16308020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308020.value: 1) We discovered that FeTe grown on Bi2Te3 under different growth conditions could result in three typical FT-BT samples. Our analysis reveals that specific growth conditions of the top FeTe layer could lead to the extraction of Te atoms from the Bi2Te3 layer, facilitating the transformation of Bi2Te3 into Bi4Te3, and with a higher Fe/Te ratio, even into Bi6Te3. Moreover, a lower growth temperature of FeTe could avoid Te extraction from Bi2Te3 and form a FeTe/ Bi2Te3 heterostructure. It was found that all three FT-BT samples display superconductivity, however, with a 3D nature. [Part C: 8(3)] 2) A new structural phase of FeTe is resulted when it is grown on a c-plane sapphire substrate, consisting of c-axis-aligned nanocrystals of tetragonal FeTe. Further growth involves a cannibalism process resulting in nanocrystal pillars. Depending on the nominal thickness, the temperature-dependent resistance of these thin films show various characteristics attributed to the thermal responses of the nanocrystals during cooling and heating processes. These findings provide an approach to fabricate a heterostructure in which one layer could generate all possible twisted angles relative to the other layer, for example. [Part C: 8(2)] 3) Growth of FeTe on ZB-MnTe could induce a transformation from ZB-MnTe to layered-MnTe (l-MnTe), resulting in the formation of an FeTe/l-MnTe heterostructure. The Fe/Te flux ratio is crucial to the phase transformation occurring in the MnTe layer, a higher ratio will lead to localized transformation into l-Mn4Te3 among the dominating l-MnTe lattice, while lower ratio minimizes the conversion from ZB-MnTe to l-MnTe. Furthermore, by lowering the growth temperature the original ZB-MnTe layer will go through transformation to dZB-MnTe and then WZ-MnTe as the Fe/Te flux ratio decreases. The as-grown FeTe/l-MnTe heterostructures display a superconducting transition around 12 K with a 3D nature. [Part C: 8(4)] 4) We achieved a top-down approach starting from two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures to fabricate one-dimensional (1D) Bi2Te3/FeTe nanowires or narrow nanoribbons. We demonstrate that the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure remains intact in nanostructures of widths on the order of 100 nm and the interfacial superconductivity is preserved. The differential conductance shows a similar superconducting twin-gap structure as in two-dimensional heterostructures, but with enhanced fluctuation effects due to the lower dimensionality. A zero-bias conductance peak indicates the presence of an Andreev bound state and given the involvement of the topological Bi2Te3 surface state, we discuss a possible topological nature of the superconductivity. [Part C: 8(1)]

16308020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308020.value: To reveal if the observed ZBCP in the Bi2Te3/FeTe quasi-1D nanostructure is related to Majorana fermions, further experiments should ideally be performed on heterostructures with higher Tc and at lower temperatures in a dilution refrigerator so that lower reduced temperatures T/Tc are accessible to reduce fluctuations and obtain sharper features. An interesting tool would be microscopic experiments, e.g. with a scanning tunneling probe, to see if there is a connection between the ZBCP and the excess iron. Furthermore, it would be interesting to deposit some nanoscale Fe clusters near the interface to study the effect of the exchange field in a more controlled way. The 3D nature of the FeTe/Bi2Te3 and FeTe/l-MnTe heterostructures could be related to the more stoichiometric FeTe layer of these systems, which could be revealed by HRTEM studies. On the other hand, the layered MnTe phase discovered by us is a previously unreported phase, it may have an unusual magnetic property that could offer a non-local or long-distance effect that may suppress the AFM state of the entire FeTe layer. These further studies are on-going via the collaboration with the colleagues in HKUST and collaborators in SUStech.

16308020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308020.value: This project aims to investigate various quasi-1D heterostructures and evaluate whether they can achieve the generation and manipulation of quasi-particles, known as Majorana fermions, which serve as suitable qubits for an innovative quantum computing approach. The key aspects of this project can be outlined as follows: 1) a methodical strategy is developed to create an FeTe/Bi-bilayer heterostructure through the growth of the FeTe/Bi4Te3 heterostructure; 2) we have discovered a unique tetragonal FeTe phase that may serve as a foundation for constructing heterostructures with any possible twisted angles; 3) we demonstrated a novel FeTe/layered MnTe superconducting heterostructure system; 4) we showed that Bi2Te3/FeTe quasi-1D nanostructures could potentially provide a viable means to trap and manipulate Majorana fermions. These achievements allow the relevant community to gain better insight into the essential mechanisms and properties of various superconducting heterostructures that show potential as an excellent basis for realizing innovative quantum computation.

16308120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308120.value: 在生物醫學研究中，推斷風險因子與結果變量之間的因果關係至關重要。因果關係問題的例子包括：高密度脂蛋白膽固醇是冠狀動脈疾病的保護因子嗎？產前吸煙是兒童破壞性行為障礙的危險因素嗎？回答這些因果問題的一個重大挑戰是：即使沒有因果關係，混雜因素也可以引起風險因子和結果變量之間的關聯。為解決因果推理方面的挑戰，隨機對照試驗通常被視為黃金標準。但是，隨機對照試驗非常昂貴，有時甚至是不可行和不道德的（例如，隨機分配給產前吸煙）。為克服隨機對照試驗的局限性，引入孟德爾隨機化來模擬隨機對照試驗，從而進行因果推理。根據孟德爾遺傳定律，基因型是從一代到下一代隨機分配的，並且不受混雜因素的影響。因此，基因型可以用作工具變量，以消除混雜因素的影響。但是，由於人類遺傳學的複雜性，孟德爾隨機化面臨一些獨特的挑戰，包括多基因性，基因多效性，以及數據預處理過程中引起的潛在偏差。在這個課題中，我們致力於研發一個統一的框架MR-SSH，以完善地解決孟德爾隨機化中的獨特挑戰。在我們的前期研究中，我們提出的貝葉斯加權孟德爾隨機方法已經取得初步成效。在此基础上，我們進一步提出MR-SSH，更加全面地回應來自實踐中的遺傳學數據的挑戰。

16308120.label: Realisation of objectives
16308120.value: 1. Develop statistical methods for Mendelian randomization using genome-wide summary statistics Mendelian randomization (MR) is an instrumental variable (IV) method used to infer causal relationships between an exposure and an outcome, utilizing genetic variants, such as single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), as IVs for the exposure. Conventional MR methods rely on three key assumptions: (A-I) IVs must be associated with the exposure, (A-II) IVs should be independent of confounding factors, and (A-III) IVs should affect the outcome solely through the exposure. However, assumptions (A-II) and (A-III) are frequently violated in practice due to hidden confounding factors in genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, leading to false-positive findings. Two major confounding factors that complicate causal inference with genetic data are pleiotropy and sample structure. Pleiotropy occurs when a genetic variant influence both exposure and outcome traits directly or indirectly via an intermediate phenotype. This phenomenon can create associations between traits without implying causality, particularly due to the polygenic nature of complex traits and linkage disequilibrium (LD) within the human genome. As a result, many SNPs may exhibit pleiotropic effects, violating assumptions (A-II) and (A-III) in traditional MR. Sample structure also contributes to bias in SNP effect-size estimates and can introduce spurious trait associations. Sample structure includes factors such as population stratification, cryptic relatedness, and sample overlap in GWASs of exposure and outcome traits. When population stratification or cryptic relatedness is present, SNPs may affect the outcome through these structural biases, violating the aforementioned assumptions. Without correcting for sample structure, SNP effect-size estimates can be significantly skewed, leading to misinterpretations of trait associations and numerous false-positive discoveries. To address these issues, we developed MR-APSS [1], a unified approach that simultaneously accounts for pleiotropy and sample structure in MR analysis. MR-APSS uses a foreground-background model to decompose observed SNP effect sizes. The background model addresses confounding factors hidden in GWAS summary statistics, including correlated pleiotropy and sample structure, while the foreground model focuses on causal inference, accounting for uncorrelated pleiotropy. By using the pre-estimated background model, MR-APSS can determine whether an SNP is part of the background or foreground component. Importantly, even with many invalid IVs, type I error rates remain controlled, as only foreground signals are used for causal inference. As more SNPs are incorporated, the increasing number of foreground signals enhances statistical power, improving causal inference outcomes. 2. Implementation of the proposed algorithms and statistical inference We proposed a novel variational expectation-maximization algorithm to fit the background-foreground model in our MR-APSS method. To make sure the background and foreground model identifiable, we first fit the background model using the background model using genome-wide summary statistics, under the assumptions of LD score regression (LDSC). In such a way, pleiotropy and sample structure hidden in the GWAS summary statistics have been appropriately accounted for. Then we fit the entire MR-APSS model using a variational expectation-maximization algorithm, where the selection bias of IV has been properly adjusted. Through the variational expectation-maximization algorithm, we can accurately estimate the model parameters and then perform likelihood-based statistical inference for the causal effects. 3. Evaluate model performance using comprehensive simulation studies and compare analysis results with other related methods. To evaluate MR-APSS in various scenarios and compare it with nine MR methods (three groups based on their assumptions, including IVW from group 1; Egger, RAPS, and dIVW from group 2; and Weighted-median, Weighted-mode, MRMix, CML-MA, and CAUSE from group 3). We first performed simulation studies under the MR-APSS model. After that, we investigated the robustness of MR-APSS in the presence of model misspecification. For exposure and outcome traits, we used 47,049 SNPs on chromosomes 1 and 2 of 20,000 individuals of White British ancestry randomly drawn from the UK BioBank (UKBB). The simulation studies and results have been presented in [1]. 4. Apply the proposed methods to real data. To have a comprehensive study of the influence of the assumptions in MR methods (A-I, II, and III), we further designed a systematic benchmarking study [2], where 16 two-sample summary-level MR methods using real-world genetic datasets. To assess the performance of these MR methods, we utilized real-world datasets and focused on three key aspects: type I error control, the accuracy of causal effect estimates, and replicability. Particularly, in evaluating type I error control, we used GWAS summary-level datasets for more than 1,000 exposure-outcome trait pairs of no causal effect from multiple sources, serving as negative controls. These trait pairs were carefully selected to represent scenarios involving confounding factors, such as population stratification and pleiotropy. We conducted a comparison between population-based MR and family-based MR to evaluate the influence of family-level confounders. Through our comprehensive experiments using real-world datasets, we found that the performance of MR methods is heavily influenced by confounding factors that arise from various sources in practical scenarios. Our study offers practical guidelines for researchers in choosing appropriate MR methods and improving the reliability of causal inference in MR analyses. 5. Investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed methods. As our MR-APSS model is built upon the normal distribution of GWAS summary statistics, it is necessary to rigorously establish the asymptotic normality of GWAS summary statistics. The main challenge comes from the principal component adjustment for population stratification in GWAS data analysis. To our best knowledge, the distribution of summary statistics after PC adjustment has not been rigorously established in the literature. By using the random matrix theory, we provide a justification on the asymptotic normality of GWAS summary statistics after PC adjustment. The detailed proof is given in [1]. In addition to the asymptotic normality of GWAS summary statistics, based on the Berry-Essen theorem, we also show that the uniformity of the approximated distribution of the summary statistics can be guaranteed when the third absolute moment of phenotype and the genotype variables are bounded by finite values. This theoretical result provides a reasonable justification to our MR-APSS model. We also established theoretical understanding of several existing MR methods, such as IVW and dIVW. These theoretical results can explain why these existing MR methods do not perform very well in the presence of confounding bias from sample structure and pleiotropy. 6. Release open-source software to disseminate the results from this research. We provide an open-source software for easy usage of MR-APSS at https://github.com/YangLabHKUST/MR-APSS. The Software can be installed as #install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("YangLabHKUST/MR-APSS") In addition, we provide a step-by-step tutorial document for MR-APSS. https://github.com/YangLabHKUST/MR-APSS/blob/master/MRAPSS_Rpackage_Tutorial.pdf In addition to the software of our developed methods, we also provide a website which collects all the real datasets we used in our benchmarking study. https://github.com/YangLabHKUST/MRbenchmarking References [1]. 16308120.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308120.value: Mendelian randomization (MR) is a powerful tool for inferring causal relationships among various traits using summary statistics from genome-wide association studies (GWASs). However, existing summary-level MR methods often rely on strong assumptions, leading to a high rate of false-positive findings. To address these limitations, ongoing research has primarily focused on mitigating confounding due to pleiotropy. In this study, we highlight that sample structure—encompassing population stratification, cryptic relatedness, and sample overlap—is another significant confounding factor. We introduce a unified MR approach, MR-APSS, which: 1) simultaneously accounts for pleiotropy and sample structure by leveraging genome-wide information, and 2) permits the inclusion of additional genetic variants with moderate effects as instrumental variables (IVs) to enhance statistical power without increasing type I errors. We first validated MR-APSS through comprehensive simulations and negative controls, then applied it to explore causal relationships among a diverse array of complex traits. Our results indicate that MR-APSS reliably identifies plausible causal relationships, particularly for highly polygenic traits, where IV strengths are typically weak and existing summary-level MR methods are susceptible to confounding effects. In addition to developing this new statistical method, we conducted a benchmark study evaluating 16 two-sample summary-level MR methods using real-world genetic datasets, aiming to establish best practices. Our study focused on critical aspects such as type I error control in various confounding scenarios (e.g., population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounders like assortative mating), accuracy of causal effect estimates, replicability, and statistical power. By thoroughly assessing the performance of these methods across over one thousand exposure-outcome trait pairs, our study provides valuable insights into their strengths and limitations, offering practical guidance for researchers selecting appropriate MR methods for causal inference.

16308120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308120.value: The process of aging encompasses intricate biological changes, with epigenetic modifications playing a vital role. Epigenetic clocks, which are machine learning algorithms that predict biological age based on DNA methylation patterns, have gained popularity as computational tools in aging research. These clocks can effectively estimate chronological age and have been linked to various health outcomes, including age-related diseases and mortality. However, since these clocks are founded on correlations, it becomes challenging to differentiate causal factors from mere associations in the aging process. Epigenome-wide Mendelian randomization (EWMR) is a robust approach that can bridge this gap, enabling researchers to infer causal relationships between epigenetic changes and aging-related traits. The EWMR method utilizes methylation quantitative trait loci as genetic instruments, which are genetic variants associated with DNA methylation levels at specific CpG sites. By investigating the connection between these methylation quantitative trait loci and aging-related outcomes, researchers can estimate the causal impact of DNA methylation on aging phenotypes. This approach is based on the principle that genetic variants are randomly distributed at conception, making them less prone to the confounding factors that often affect observational studies. The methods developed in our research hold significant promise for addressing the challenges associated with EWMR, facilitating reliable causal inferences regarding the aging process.

16308120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308120.value: This research project focuses on a method called Mendelian randomization (MR), which helps scientists understand the cause-and-effect relationships between genetic traits and health outcomes. Traditional MR methods often make strong assumptions that can lead to incorrect conclusions, so this study aims to improve the accuracy of these methods. We introduced a new approach, MR-APSS, that takes into account not only genetic influences but also the structure of the study samples, such as differences in populations and relatedness among individuals. This is important because it helps reduce errors and provides more reliable results. By testing MR-APSS through simulations and real-world data, we found that it can effectively identify true causal relationships, especially in complex traits influenced by many genes. Additionally, we benchmarked 16 existing MR methods to understand their strengths and weaknesses, offering valuable guidance for researchers.

16308420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308420.value: Hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions (HER/HOR) in alkaline conditions are several orders of magnitude more sluggish than those in acidic conditions, which significantly increases the overpotential and consequently lowers the overall energy efficiency of alkaline fuel cells and electrolyzers. Despite great efforts, researchers have not been able to fully understand these pH-dependent reaction kinetics. In the proposed research, we will use two powerful in situ vibrational spectroscopic techniques, namely surface-enhanced infrared absorption and shell-isolated nanoparticle-enhanced Raman spectroscopies, to directly obtain molecule-level data on the electrochemical interface, including the vibration wavenumber and potential-dependent band position shift of both adsorbed *H intermediate and water molecules, in solutions with different pH values. The in situ spectra on a series of metal surfaces (e.g., Pt, Pd, Ru, Ir, Rh, and Pt-Ru) will be recorded. The HER/HOR reaction rates will be correlated with the wavenumbers of the Pt-H stretching bands, which are directly associated with the binding energy of *H. The hydrogen binding energy derived from the Pt-H vibration wavenumber is the net consequence at the electrochemical interface, including the intrinsic hydrogen binding energy, double layer electric field, *H and water interaction, etc. As a result, this parameter more accurately reflects the real situation than those derived from calculations in a vacuum. The results will lead to more accurate assessments of the activity of HER/HOR in different electrolytes. More importantly, we will develop and optimize a novel theoretical model to explain the basic physical data obtained from the in situ spectroscopies. For the first time, we will create a complex model of the real interfacial reaction environment; it will include metal surfaces, water molecules, adsorbed *H, and ions at various concentrations. We will calculate the hydrogen binding energies and Pt-H vibration wavenumbers of these models with or without applied potentials and compare the results with the experimental data. Reaction pathways will be determined using this more realistic model. The combination of theoretical simulations and spectroscopic data will clarify the pH- and surface-sensitive HER/HOR reaction rates, and provide guidelines for the rational development of more advanced electrocatalysts. The approaches and findings can also be applied to other electrocatalytic reactions. 氫氣氧化和析出反應在鹼性電解液裡比在酸裡慢幾個數量級，從而降低了鹼性燃料電池和電解池的效率。這種反應速率和pH值相關的現象還沒有得到很好的解釋。 在這個項目裡，我們將利用現場紅外增強吸收光譜和殼絕緣的拉曼增強光譜來研究Pt, Pd, Ru, Ir, Rh, Pt-Ru等金屬的電化學界面，以得到更全面的分子水平信息，包括反應中間產物氫原子和水分子的吸附、振動波數等隨pH值的變化等，得到氫氣氧化和析出反應速率和鉑-氫鍵波數的關係，從而直接和氫原子的吸附能量關聯。氫原子吸附能量和眾多因素相關，從本實驗得到的值將比常規計算出來的值更接近於實際。 更重要的是，我們還將根據現場光譜的數據建立一套新穎的理論模型，作為聯繫實驗和理論計算的橋樑。在這個複雜的模型中，我們將首次嘗試把金屬表面、水分子、吸附的氫原子、及離子等放在一起，得到一個更接近於雙電層的系統。計算出來的氫吸附能和振動波數將和實驗得到的數據比較。我們將結合現場光譜數據和理論結果提出新的電化學反應路徑和機理，全面揭示氫氣氧化和析出反應和電解液pH值的關係，為設計更高效的催化劑提高指導。本項目的研究思路和結果也可以拓展應用到其它的點催化體系。

16308420.label: Realisation of objectives
16308420.value: Objective 1: To obtain molecule-level data on electrochemical interfaces during hydrogen oxidation and evolution reactions using in situ spectroscopic techniques and to correlate the reaction rates with measured hydrogen binding energies on various metal surfaces with different pH. We developed a two-step wet method to deposit a series of metal thin films including Pt, Ir, Rh, and Ru on an Au thin film on a hemispherical Si prism as model catalysts. Interfacial vibrational features including *H and interfacial water layers on different surfaces during hydrogen oxidation and evolution reactions (HOR/HER) in solutions with different pHs (1.1, 3.1, 7.0, 10.9, and 12.9) were successfully investigated by surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (SEIRAS). We found that the metal-hydrogen bonding energy decreased with pH suggesting that the lower reaction rates at high pH related with their weaker *H and metal interaction. This result is opposite with the previous theory. Part of these results were published in Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2020, 142, 19, 8748-8754 and Catalysis Science & Technology 2022, 12, 3228-3233. By applying the SEIRAS, we also investigated the role of Ru decoration on improving the kineties of HOR/HER on Pt surfaces. We demonstrated that Ru is the main active sites instead of Pt. This result provided new insights in understanding the electrocatalytic at the atomic level and was published in Nature Catalysis, 2021, 4, 711-718. 2. To construct a novel theoretical model that is closer to the real environment by considering solvent, electric fields, and pH effects. We develop a new model based on VASP by including both explicit and implicit water molecules to construct the hybrid model, which is critical to explore the interfacial reaction mechanisms at the solid-liquid interface. Fractional charge is introduced to tune the applied potential and pH. the linear relationship is observed between the potential applied potential and the fractional charge , as well as between pH and the fractional charge. Pt-H vibrational wavenumbers obtained from our model are consistent with those measured by SEIRAS at different pHs, demonstrating the efficacy of our theoretical models in reproducing the Pt-water electrochemical interfacial behaviors under HER/HOR conditions. These results were published in Electrochimica Acta , 2022, 425, 140709. 3. To reveal the origins of pH- and surface-dependent hydrogen reaction kinetics through a combination of spectroscopic and theoretical data. To investigate the pH-dependent HER activity thoroughly at Pt(111)/water electrochemical interfaces, all elementary reaction steps including Volmer, Heyrovsky and Tafel steps are simulated to search the transition state and minimum energy path (MEP) in both acid and alkaline solutions. The reaction pathway is explored by using the climbing image nudged elastic band method and the reaction barrier was calculated to be the energy difference between the reactant and transition state. HER mechanism is found to be strongly affected by both pH and surface properties (*H coverage). On Pt(111) surface with pre-adsorbed *Hatop, HER in acid followed the Volmer-Tafel/Heyrovsky pathway with the second step being the rate-determining step (RDS), and alkaline HER proceeded via the Volmer-Tafel pathway where the Volmer step serves as the RDS. The pH-dependent HER kinetics can be well explained by the correlated proton sources and different surface properties in acid and alkaline solutions. This work was published in Electrochimica Acta , 2022, 425, 140709. The faster reaction kinetics on Ru/Pt(111) might originate from the change of the electronic structures of Ru by the Pt substrate. The positively-shifted d-band for Ru skin contributed to an enhanced interaction between adsorbates and substrate. Therefore, both experimental and theoretical results suggest that the improved hydrogen reaction kinetics in alkaline media on surface Ru-modified Pt was mainly originated from the tuned structural and electronic properties of Ru overlayer, enhanced *H/*OH adsorptions and consequently improved kinetics of rate-determining Volmer step. This result was published in Nature Catalysis, 2021, 4, 711-718.

16308420.value: 1. Proposed a new understanding of the role of Ru on improving the HER/HOR activity of Pt. This result rules out the commonly accepted bifunctional mechanism. This work not only deepens our understanding of hydrogen electrocatalysis mechanisms, but also provides guidelines for the rational design of advanced electrocatalysts. Some of the results were published in Nature Catalysis, 2021, 4, 711-718. 2. By using this powerful model, new understandings on the pH effects and surface modifications are proposed. Some of the results were published in Nature Catalysis, 2021, 4, 711-718 and Electrochimica Acta , 2022, 425, 140709.

16308720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308720.value: The proposed project will focus on the long-time behaviors and approximations of the invariant measures of two frequently used stochastic phase field models. These two equations, the stochastic Allen--Cahn and the stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equations, are driven by general multiplicative infinite dimensional Wiener processes which would be degenerate. The proposed study will also derive the associated optimal time-independent weak error analysis for a family of Galerkin-type fully discrete numerical schemes and error estimates between the invariant measures and their approximations. Phase field models have become very common in physical and chemical applications that involve the phase separation of multicomponent mixtures, especially when there are multiple sources of noise. Therefore, it is necessary and significant to consider stochastic effects and to study the impact of noise on the long-term behaviors of the solutions. More and more researchers are conducting mathematical and numerical analyses of the Allen--Cahn and the Cahn--Hilliard equations perturbed by white and colored noises. Most previous studies have concentrated on investigating the long-term behavior of the solutions and on designing efficient numerical schemes with strong and weak convergence rates in the mean and probability distribution senses, respectively, to complement the stochastic equations. Due to the non-Lipschitz continuity of the potential term and the degeneracy of the noise, there are difficulties in obtaining the ergodicity and weak convergence with time-independent optimal rates for reasonable numerical approximations of the stochastic Allen--Cahn and stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equations. To overcome this difficulty, the main tool in the proposed project will be to combine various coupling methods and tools from Malliavin calculus with variational and mild solution theories. We will discretize the spatial variable using Galerkin-type approximations, to take advantage of the high accuracy and established theory for error estimates of the Galerkin methods; we will discretize the temporal variable using Euler or Milstein schemes. The main goal of the proposed approach is to obtain optimal time-independent weak error estimates of these schemes as applied to approximate the invariant measures of the stochastic Allen--Cahn and stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equations driven by multiplicative degenerate white or colored noises. We also intend to examine the ergodicity of these schemes and derive sharp error estimates between the invariant measures and numerical ones. We will generalize the developed methods to study other types of stochastic phase field equations, such as the coupling of the stochastic Allen--Cahn and stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equations, and solve them numerically in material sciences to verify our theoretical results. 16308820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308820.value: This proposal focuses on the analysis of the inertial nematic liquid crystal flow. Liquid crystal is an intermediate phase between the isotropic fluid state and the crystalline solid state. It displays an orientational order, and in the meantime, possesses none or partial positional order. Many cell membranes, proteins, soap solutions, detergents, the tobacco mosaic virus, etc. are liquid crystals. Many contemporary electronic displays use liquid crystals. Hence it is necessary to study the liquid crystal both in mathematical theory and in physical application. The nematic liquid crystals are composed of rodlike molecules with the long axes of neighboring molecules approximately aligned to one another. It is one of the most common phases in liquid crystals. This project focuses on the hydrodynamic theory for the inertial nematic liquid crystal first established by Ericksen and Leslie sixty years ago. The inertial nematic liquid crystal is interesting both in physics and in mathematics. On one hand, it is physically relevant and has important applications. On the other hand, inspired by the global regularity results on wave maps, it is natural to conjecture that the threshold theorem also holds for the two-dimensional inertial nematic liquid crystal flow. This conjecture is completely open. Our proposed project can be regarded as the first step towards proving the threshold conjecture. The inertial Ericksen-Leslie system for the nematic liquid crystal is a system coupling the Navier-Stokes equation with the wave map. If the space dimension is one, the full Ericksen-Leslie system with inertial effect reduces to a variational wave system for general Oseen-Frank energy, and some progress has been made along this direction. For the case when space dimension is higher than one, the nontrivial result of the global well-posedness of the classical solution in three dimensions near equilibrium was recently established by the PI and his collaborators. This opens the door to the future study of the problem. The PI will continue the research of the nematic liquid crystal flow. Specifically, we will address the well-posedness problem including the global existence of classical solutions, finite-time singularity and the low regularity problem. The research methods will mainly come from the study of wave maps, and include vector field theory, the ghost weight method, the construction of type I and type II blow-up solutions, Bourgain spaces techniques, Strichatz estimates, and renormalization techniques. The results will provide new insights for both mathematics and physics. 液晶是各向同性流体状态和晶体固态之间的中间相，它表现出特定的指向顺序，与此同时，不具有或仅具有部分位置顺序。许多细胞膜，蛋白质，肥皂溶液，洗涤剂，烟草花叶病毒等都是液晶，电子显示器等设备也使用液晶。液晶最常见的类别之一是向列型，向列型液晶是由棒状分子组成的，相邻分子的长轴相互近似排列。本项目将研究Ericksen与Leslie于1961年提出的惯性向列型液晶的适定性问题。 惯性向列型液晶的Ericksen-Leslie系统是一个Navier-Stokes方程与波映照耦合的系统。我们计划研究经典解的全局存在性、有限时间的奇性和低正则性问题。研究方法主要来源于波映照方程的研究，包括向量场方法、ghost权方法、I型和II型爆破解的构造、Bourgain空间技术、Strichatz估计和重整化技巧。

16309020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309020.value: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is an engineered system with one graphene layer stacked on top of the other and rotated by a twist angle. As a result of the twist, the carbon atoms form moiré patterns in real space. Around the "magic angles", the low energy electronic structures of TBG are characterized by four nearly flat bands. These low-energy flat bands are believed to be responsible for the recently observed correlated insulating states, superconductivity and orbital ferromagnetic state in TBG. These experimental observations have stimulated numerous theoretical studies, but the physical mechanisms behind these phenomena remain unclear. Recently several researchers, including the PI and Co-I, have found that the low-energy flat bands in TBG possess nontrivial topological properties. In particular, the PI and Co-I have established important connections between the flat bands in TBG and the zeroth Landau levels of Dirac fermions under some pseudo magnetic fields, which provides a natural explanation for the intrinsic topological nature of these flat bands. In previous studies, we have revealed that various of topological band structures are commonly exist in all kinds of twisted graphene systems. At the same time, the interaction among the electrons in graphene system is generally strong due to the under-screened Coulomb interaction in 2D systems. Therefore, the twisted graphene system provides a good platform to study the interplay between the band topology and correlation effect, which will lead to new exotic phases as already seen by many experiments in TBG and TMG. In the present proposal, we plan to systematically study the correlation effects and transport properties in twisted graphene systems. We are going to focus on the following two aspects. 1) what are the nature of the correlated insulating states observed in these twisted graphene systems? Are they from spontaneous symmetry breaking? If yes, what kind of symmetry has been broken? Up to now, different insulating states have been discovered at 1/4,1/2 and 3/4 filling. We will apply both the first principle Hatree Fock, random phase approximation (RPA) and exact diagonalisation methods to reveal the physical nature of these insulating states, based on which we can explain the full phase diagram. 2) given such correlated insulating states and/or spontaneous symmetry breaking states, what would be the corresponding transport and optical properties? What is the response of such a state to external magnetic fields and electric fields? We will study these problems using the linear response theory. 摘要 轉角雙層石墨烯 (TBG) 是一種工程化系統，其中壹層石墨烯堆疊在另一層石墨烯上，並旋轉了一個角度。由於扭轉，碳原子在真實空間中形成莫爾圖案。在“魔角”的情形下，TBG的低能電子結構的特徵是四個幾乎平坦的帶。這些低能平帶被認為是TBG中最近觀察到的關聯絕緣態，超導性和軌道鐵磁態的原因。這些實驗觀察引發了許多理論研究，但是這些現象背後的物理機制仍不清楚。最近，包括PI和Co-I在內的幾位研究人員發現TBG中的低能平帶具有非平凡的拓撲特性。特別地，PI和Co-I將TBG平帶和在贗磁場下的狄拉克費米子的第零Landau能級之間建立了重要的聯繫，為這些平帶的固有拓撲性質提供了自然的解釋。 在以前的研究中，我們發現各種扭轉的石墨烯系統中普遍存在各種拓撲帶結構。同時，由於2D系統中未屏蔽的庫侖相互作用，石墨烯系統中電子之間的相互作用通常很強。因此，扭轉的石墨烯系統為研究能帶拓撲和關聯效應之間的相互作用提供了壹個很好的平臺。這種相互作用所導致的新奇異相已經被研究人員在TBG和TMG中所進行的許多實驗觀測獲得。 在本提案中，我們計劃系統地研究轉角石墨烯系統中的關聯效應和輸運性質。我們將集中在以下兩個方面。 1. 在這些轉角石墨烯系統中觀察到的關聯絕緣態的性質是什麼？它們是自發對稱性破壞的嗎？如果是，則打破了哪種對稱性？到目前為止，在1/4、1/2和3/4填充時發現了不同的絕緣狀態。我們將應用第一原理Hatree Fock，無規相近似(RPA)和精確對角化方法 (ED) 來揭示這些絕緣態的物理性質，在此基礎上我們可以解釋整個相圖。 2. 考慮到這種關聯絕緣態和/或自發對稱斷裂態，相應的輸運和光學性質是什麼？這種狀態對外部磁場和電場有什麼響應？我們將使用線性響應理論研究這些問題。

16309020.label: Realisation of objectives
16309020.value: Completion Report Objective 1: Development of First-Principles Hartree-Fock Method for Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Phases in Twisted Graphene Systems Progress and Outcomes: The first-principles Hartree-Fock approach was developed to study symmetry-breaking phases in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG). Building upon foundational work in orbital magnetic states and moiré graphene systems, this method leverages the orbital magnetic properties unique to TBG as outlined in recent studies ￼ ￼. Utilizing insights from the truncated atomic plane wave (TAPW) method, an accurate basis was established for analyzing local orbital contributions, enabling us to investigate symmetry-breaking phases at the atomic level ￼. This methodological framework sets the stage for probing spontaneous symmetry breaking in TBG under various configurations and strain conditions, capturing nuances in phase behaviors that align with experimental results. Objective 2: Analysis of Transport and Optical Properties in Symmetry-Breaking Phases of Moiré Graphene Systems Progress and Outcomes: Through analysis of the transport and optical properties of symmetry-breaking states, this study examined how quasiparticles and collective modes contribute within moiré graphene systems. Key findings indicate that transport phenomena in such systems are deeply influenced by topological and orbital magnetic features, as highlighted by studies on orbital magnetism and the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAH) observed in aligned moiré graphene systems ￼ ￼. The investigation revealed that both the quasiparticles and exotic collective modes in TBG significantly impact carrier dynamics, influencing electrical conductivity and magneto-optical responses. Objective 3: Stabilization Conditions for Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall States Using Exact Diagonalization Progress and Outcomes: Exact diagonalization techniques were employed to determine the conditions for fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) state stabilization in twisted bilayer graphene. Utilizing heavy-fermion models in TBG and leveraging insights from exact subband calculations via the TAPW method, the study defined stability criteria for fractionalized quantum states at specific filling factors ￼ ￼. Additionally, research into orbital magnetic states emphasized the critical role of Coulomb interactions and symmetry breaking in establishing fractional quantum Hall effects, thereby enriching our understanding of stability thresholds and the conditions necessary for realizing FQAH in TBG.

16309020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309020.value: 1. Possible Quantization and Half-Quantization in the Anomalous Hall Effect Caused by In-Plane Magnetic Field. In this study, we explore the conditions under which a quantized or nearly half-quantized anomalous Hall effect (AHE) can occur in nonmagnetic two-dimensional systems subjected to an in-plane magnetic field. We show that, through the Zeeman effect, an in-plane magnetic field can induce intrinsic AHE in systems with strong spin-orbit coupling and broken rotational symmetry. 2. ''Electrical Breakdown of Excitonic Insulators'' This work introduces a novel breakdown mechanism in excitonic insulators, termed ''many-body breakdown,'' which occurs when the electric field destabilizes the condensate of electron-hole pairs, differing from traditional Zener breakdown observed in band insulators. Through a BCS-type wave function under electric fields, we investigate how the excitonic insulator transitions to a metallic state once a critical field strength is reached, either directly or following an intermediate tunneling phase. 3. ''Heavy-Fermion Representation for Twisted Bilayer Graphene Systems'' In this work, we present a heavy-fermion model for twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) by constructing localized and itinerant states using the orthogonalized plane wave method. We show that the electronic states of TBG near the magic angle can be viewed as a hybridization of zeroth pseudo-Landau level (ZLL) orbitals and itinerant states, reflecting a balance between localization and itinerancy in the moiré flat bands. 4. ''Orbital Magnetic States in Moiré Graphene Systems'' We examine the orbital magnetic properties and topological effects in moiré graphene systems, particularly focusing on twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) aligned with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The study highlights the spontaneous symmetry breaking and resulting orbital magnetism at partial fillings, characterized by current-loop patterns at the moiré scale, which lead to quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) states. 5. ''Truncated Atomic Plane Wave Method for Subband Structure Calculations of Moiré Systems'' In this work, we propose the truncated atomic plane wave (TAPW) method to efficiently calculate the subband structure of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) and similar moiré systems. By combining elements from the tight-binding and Bistritzer-MacDonald models, the TAPW approach enables detailed analysis of band structures across a wide range of twist angles, including the magic angle. This method preserves high computational accuracy while significantly reducing complexity, making it ideal for examining low-energy physics in TBG and understanding the interplay of moiré phonons and screened Coulomb interactions.

16309020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309020.value: Potential developments in this research direction could focus on experimental verification and material innovation in twisted graphene and related moiré systems. For instance, further exploration of quantized anomalous Hall effects (AHE) in nonmagnetic 2D materials could lead to new spintronic devices, particularly by manipulating in-plane magnetic fields to control AHE. Developing materials that stabilize the excitonic insulator phase under various field strengths might reveal unique switching mechanisms for future electronics, leveraging the ''many-body breakdown'' phenomenon. Additionally, the heavy-fermion model of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) could be applied to other low-angle twisted multilayers, enhancing our understanding of strong electron correlations and superconductivity across different moiré configurations. On the computational side, the truncated atomic plane wave (TAPW) method could be refined for larger systems or adapted to study twisted multilayer structures, providing precise insights into subband structures and interactions. Finally, investigating orbital magnetism and spontaneous symmetry breaking at partial fillings could uncover new types of topological states or fractional quantum phases in twisted systems. Together, these developments would deepen insights into tunable quantum phenomena and could drive applications in quantum information processing, low-power electronics, and novel magnetic materials.

16309020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309020.value: The research outputs explore diverse physical phenomena in twisted graphene and related systems, particularly focusing on anomalous Hall effects, excitonic insulators, heavy-fermion models, orbital magnetism, and efficient computational methods. One study investigates the quantized anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by in-plane magnetic fields in nonmagnetic systems, identifying unique Hall behaviors in Sb₂Te₃ films under specific conditions. Another introduces the concept of ''many-body breakdown'' in excitonic insulators, where an electric field destabilizes electron-hole pairs, distinct from conventional breakdown in band insulators. A third study models twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) as a heavy-fermion system, describing its electronic states as hybridized localized and itinerant modes near the magic angle, essential for understanding its strong correlation effects. Further research examines orbital magnetic states in TBG, showing that spontaneous symmetry breaking leads to topological and quantum anomalous Hall states. Finally, a novel computational method, the truncated atomic plane wave (TAPW) approach, accurately calculates subband structures in TBG while managing computational demands, aiding in the analysis of moiré patterns and Coulomb interactions. Together, these studies advance our understanding of topological, magnetic, and transport properties in twisted graphene systems and offer powerful tools for future explorations.

16309920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309920.value: Heterogeneity exists among all cells. In recent decades, great strides have been made in single-cell analysis, representing a group of technologies that examine cells one by one, to improve our understanding of cells and various diseases. Traditionally, flow cytometry has a high throughput in examining cells, but it is expensive and needs significant expertise. Microfluidics offers more versatility. Microwell array and single-cell droplets by flow focusing are the two most popular microfluidic single-cell approaches. However, they share severe common limitations. For example, the number of cells per microwell or droplet is governed by a Poisson distribution, making it difficult to obtain high single-cell capture efficiencies. It is also difficult to exchange solutions once cells are isolated. Moreover, in all current single-cell technologies, harsh cell isolation processes are normally required, which are likely to change the cell states, damage or even kill cells. Existing single-cell techniques are still not robust enough to provide a firm foundation for real applications and markets. Here we propose a conceptually new and reliable single-cell analysis method that can avoid the disadvantages above. Our microchip is a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) micropillar array with hydrophilic top surfaces. Cell suspensions will be directly applied onto the micropillar array without pretreatments. An oil phase will be added to wet the micropillars except the top surface. The oil/water interphase is tuned to curve toward the aqueous phase such that, under gravity, all cells will sediment towards the micropillars. Because each micropillar has a similar size to the cells, only one cell can have direct contact with each micropillar and subsequently attach to it. Flushing away all non-attached cells will leave a single-cell array; furthermore, we can raise the oil level to form droplets on the micropillars with each droplet containing only one cell. We also propose simple strategies to exchange solutions in the droplets, facilitating downstream multi-omics analysis. Our proposed method has distinct advantages: (1) it is simple to operate; (2) the gentlest force, i.e., gravity, is exerted on cells, and surfactants are avoided, so that damage to the cells is avoided and the cell state is retained; (3) the distribution of cells is inherently one cell per droplet; and (4) it is easy to exchange droplet solutions. Moreover, it can achieve high cell densities up to 1 million cells per chip. These unique features make our proposed method potentially much better than existing methods for single-cell analysis and closer to real applications. 異質性存在於所有細胞之間。近幾十年來，單細胞分析取得了長足的進步並增進了我們對細胞和各種疾病的了解，最具代表性的是可以逐一檢查細胞的一组技術。傳統上，流式細胞術在檢查細胞方面具有很高的通量，但是它很昂貴並且需要大量的專業知識。微流體技術提供了更多的多功能性。通過流體聚焦的微孔陣列和單細胞液滴是目前兩種最流行的微流體單細胞方法。但是，它們具有嚴重的共同局限性。例如，每個微孔或液滴的細胞數遵從泊松分佈，這使得難以獲得高的單細胞捕獲效率。一旦單個細胞被隔離，細胞外溶液便很難交換了。此外，所有當前的單細胞技術通常都需要苛刻的細胞隔離過程，這很可能會改變細胞狀態，損壞甚至殺死細胞。現有的單細胞技術仍然不夠強大，無法為實際應用和市場化提供堅實的基礎。這裡，我們提出了一種概念上新穎且技術可靠的單細胞分析方法，可以避免上述缺點。我們的微芯片是具有親水頂表面的聚二甲基矽氧烷（PDMS）微柱陣列。細胞懸浮液無需預處理即可直接應用於微柱陣列。除頂部表面外，將添加油相以浸潤微柱。調整油/水界面，使其向水相彎曲，這樣，在重力作用下，所有細胞都會向微柱沉澱。因為每個微柱的大小都被設計成與細胞尺寸相似，所以只有一個細胞可以直接與每個微柱直接接觸並隨後附著在其上。沖洗掉所有未附著的細胞會留下一個單細胞陣列。此外，我們可以提高油位以在微柱上形成液滴，這樣每個液滴僅包含一個細胞。我們還提出了交換液滴中溶液的簡單策略，以利於下游多組學分析。我們提出的方法具有明顯的優點：（1）操作簡單；（2）只對細胞施加最輕柔的力，即重力，避免使用表面活性劑，從而避免了對細胞的損害並保持了細胞原有狀態。（3）細胞的分佈本質上是每個液滴一個細胞；（4）易於交換液滴溶液。此外，它可以實現每個芯片高達一百萬個單元的高單元密度。這些獨特的功能使我們的方法可能比現有的單細胞分析方法更好，並且更接近於實際應用。

16309920.label: Realisation of objectives
16309920.value: Let me show the realization of the objectives below: Objectives 1&2: to fabricate well-functionalized micropillar arrays with proper size ranges; & to generate single-cell arrays with the functionalized micropillar arrays. We have successfully fabricated a single cell pipette device as designed, two pieces of master molds were fabricated by photolithography and different ratios of PDMS prepolymers were cast into both molds and then thermally bonded together. In our work, Quake valves and a simple mild negative pressure system controlled by Arduino were employed to precisely control the flow of cell suspension in the device. We tested more than thirty geometric designs to confirm the best one that trap cells. Using HepG2 cells as model, we found that when the width and length of bypass area were set at 900 um and 20 um, respectively, an trapping efficiency of almost 100% was reached. Moreover, we were able to release only one single cell per droplet after replacing the cell suspension with phosphate-buffered saline. We also explored alternative strategies for arraying single cells and addressable cell release on demand by exploiting controlled electrolysis of water to form microbubbles in desired microchambers. The Objectives are completed Objectives 3&4: to demonstrate a general method for performing a proteomic study on the single-cell arrays; & to demonstrate a general method for performing a genomic study on the single-cell arrays. In our work (mainly from Qiaoyi Wang’s and Xingyang Yan’s PhD thesis work, part of which is published so far), we constructed a microfluidic single-cell array chip that can realize addressable cell release at low cost. With rational geometric designs, we realized high cell capture efficiency (~90%) and release of a single cell in a 10 x 10 array. Asymmetric microelectrode pairs were devised to produce addressable electrolytic bubbles in the 10 x 10 microelectrode array (MEA). This platform combines both passive and active manipulation techniques to control the motion of a single cell. This device will be coupled with a downstream single-cell module and form a cost-economical single-cell analysis platform. In addition, we constructed a high-throughput, open-space and reusable microfluidic chip for combinational drug screening on tumor spheroids. This microchip is straightforward to fabricate, compatible with standard spheroid cultures, and friendly for end-users. In order to sort single particles such as cells and organoids based on their desired properties, we developed an integrated microfluidic device for particle sorting sing image recognition. Tumor organoids present a challenge in drug screening due to their considerable heterogeneity in morphology and size. To address this issue, we proposed a portable microfluidic device that employs image processing algorithms for specific target organoid recognition and microvalve-controlled deflection for sorting and collection. This morphology-activated organoid sorting system offers numerous advantages, such as automated classification, portability, low cost, label-free sample preparation, and gentle handling of organoids. We conducted classification experiments using polystyrene beads, F9 tumoroids and patient-derived tumor organoids, achieving organoid separation efficiency exceeding 88%, purity surpassing 91%, viability exceeding 97% and classification throughput of 800 per hour, thereby meeting the demands of clinical organoid medicine. Furthermore, a current PG student, Yiwen Huang, has been working on the 2D gel electrophoretic separation of single-cell proteins and nucleic acids, where we obtained some good results; we will try to wrap up and publish the results in the future. The Objectives are completed. Objective 5: To explore the analysis of the multi-omics data on the single-cell arrays above. We have explored possible applications of our single cells/organoids microchip technology in different bio-applications. In the first example, we developed a high-throughput and logarithm-serial-dilution microfluidic chip for combinational drug screening on an array of single tumor organoids. Tumor organoids are biological models for studying precision medicine. Microfluidic technology offers significant benefits for high throughput drug screening using tumor organoids. However, the range of concentrations achievable with traditional linear gradient generators in microfluidics is restricted, generating logarithmic drug concentration gradients by adjusting the channel ratio in the chip is confined to single-drug dilution chips, significantly restricting the application of microfluidics in drug screening. Here, we presented a microfluidic chip featuring continuous dilution capabilities, which generates logarithmic stepwise drug concentration gradients. We have devised a “mathematical-circuit-chip” model for designing such chips, and based on this model, we have developed and fabricated a device capable of providing 36 distinct drug concentration conditions for two types of drugs. The chip is composed of two structurally identical yet orthogonally arranged layers, each containing a dilution network capable of forming a 5-fold gradient and a tumor organoid culture module. Drug and culture medium delivery to the open culture chamber array is driven by syringe pumps. We have conducted drug screening experiments on patient-derived tumor organoids. This device facilitates high-throughput drug screening for patient-derived organoids, representing a significant stride toward the realization of precision medicine. In the second example, we developed a novel technique for the fabrication of whole-Teflon microfluidic chips on a film. Current materials for film-based microfluidics suffer from limitations such as low compatibility with organic solvents and significant adsorption of molecules. Teflon materials seem a perfect solution, yet the fabrication of Teflon microchips remains challenging. This study presents a convenient and cost-effective technology for fabricating flexible and integrative thin-film whole-Teflon microfluidic chips. By employing a micro embossing technique, we created micropatterns on a thin fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) film (~50 µm), which were then sealed with another flat FEP thin film (~200 µm) to form microchannels. This approach enables rapid and economical prototyping of FEP film chips, without the need for expensive equipment or precise control of bonding parameters. The developed microfluidic chip stands out due to the inherent properties of Teflon material and the advantages of the entire chip being a thin film. These factors provide distinct benefits, including exceptional chemical resistance, high transparency, flexibility, and efficient heat transfer. We developed an adhesive-free, tight-fit, and solvent-resistant interconnector to interface FEP microfluidic film chips with external components for stable fluid delivery. Additionally, microvalves can be easily integrated into our Teflon microfluidic film chips, offering convenient fluid manipulation due to the flexibility of the FEP thin film. We demonstrated the applications of FEP film chips through an on-chip photochemical reaction that exhibited a high yield from the improved illumination efficiency. These FEP microfluidic film chips offer powerful features that expand the capabilities of microfluidics, making them an attractive option for many applications such as flow chemistry, biosensing, portable detection, and wearable electronics. The Objectives are successfully completed.

16309920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309920.value: Our major findings and research outcome are the following: 1. We have successfully implemented the fabrication of well-functionalized micropillar arrays with proper size ranges, which can be used to generate single-cell arrays. 2. We have successfully developed an integrated and individually addressable microfluidic single cell array chip. 3. We have successfully developed an integrated microfluidic device for the sorting of tumor organoids using image recognition, which can also be used for sorting of single particles including biological cells. 4. We have successfully developed a high-throughput, open-space and reusable microfluidic chip for combinational drug screening on arrays of tumor spheroids and/or cells. 5. We have successfully developed a high-throughput and logarithm-serial-dilution microfluidic chip for combinational drug screening on arrays of tumor organoids and/or cells. 6. We have successfully developed a novel technology for the fabrication of whole-Teflon microfluidic chips in a flexible film. The Teflon materials of the microfluidic chips, which show super cleanness and no fouling of contaminants, are important for the accurate analysis of cell contents. Furthermore, we also developed a directly moldable, highly compact, and easy-for-integration 3D micromixer with extraordinary mixing performance, which can play an important role in various cell analysis processes.

16309920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309920.value: The potential for further development of this research focuses on optimizing the technology and exploring suitable applications in bioengineering and biological studies. A critical challenge related to this proposal is the accurate and quantitative analysis of rare proteins present in minute amounts within cells, for which no existing solutions currently exist. The following steps are suggested for further advancement: Optimize cell trapping and release mechanisms in the device. Increase the throughput of the single-cell array. Apply this technology for single-cell-based drug screening and cell-cell interaction studies in practical settings. Develop a novel technology for the precise and quantitative analysis of rare proteins in low concentrations. My research group is actively pursuing these directions with the aim of creating a user-friendly microfluidic chip for single-cell analysis.

16309920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309920.value: Heterogeneity among cells has led to significant advancements in single-cell analysis technologies, which examine cells individually to enhance our understanding of various diseases. Traditional methods like flow cytometry are high-throughput but costly and require expertise. Microfluidics offers versatility, with microwell arrays and single-cell droplets being popular approaches; however, both face challenges, such as low single-cell capture efficiencies and harsh isolation processes that can harm cells. Here a novel single-cell analysis method using a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) micropillar array. Cell suspensions are applied directly to the array, with an oil phase added to wet the micropillars, allowing cells to sediment under gravity. Each micropillar, sized to fit a single cell, enables direct attachment while non-attached cells are flushed away. This process creates a single-cell array, with droplets formed on the micropillars, each containing one cell. Our method allows for easy solution exchange, retains cell integrity, and achieves high densities of up to 1 million cells per chip. These advantages position our approach as a superior alternative to existing single-cell technologies, making it more suitable for practical applications. This microchip has also been extended to organoids in drug screening.

16310020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310020.value: 有机光伏（OPV）是一种太阳能应用技术，其柔性、轻质、可卷对卷印刷等特点，以及器件在加工过程不含有毒金属的优势，使OPV器件表现出很好的发展和应用前景。最近，单节OPV电池器件的认证效率已迅速提升至16.4％。 近年来，OPV的快速发展主要归功于非富勒烯受体（NFA）的研究。在OPV发展的早期，其器件的制备普遍以富勒烯衍生物（例如PCBM）为受体。 但是，富勒烯基OPV具有多种难于克服的缺点：受体能级的可调节性差、富勒烯衍生物自身吸收较弱、器件能损较大（通常为0.8-0.9 V）等。 在2016年，我们课题组（HKUST）首次报道了基于非富勒烯受体的有机太阳能电池以较小给受体能级差（从而实现较小的电压损耗），实现高效电荷分离的研究，其中器件的电压损耗为0.55V，而这一工作发表在Nature Energy。 那么，如果可以实现在如此小的电压损耗下，OPV器件的其他参数的更优化，那么非富勒烯基有机太阳能电池则在理论上可以实现接近20％的光电转换效率。 最近，研究者们开发了一类新的NFA分子（例如Y6和N3），这类分子快速推动OPV的发展，使非富勒烯基OPV的效率超过16％。尽管如此，目前我们还不清楚这类材料优异性能的内在原因。 在此研究项目中，我们将设计和合成一系列与Y6结构类似的 NFA分子，以了解Y6类受体材料优异光伏性能的内在原因以及该系列材料的结构与性能关系。具体来说，我们将通过对分子中具体结构的修饰来设计和合成一系列与Y6具有类似结构的分子：1）修饰中心“A”结构单元；2）通过调节结构中并噻吩单元实现对分子形状的改变，3）调节以及替换结构单元中的烷基链等。以此为基础，通过一系列分子设计，我们希望可以揭示Y6类分子结构与性能间的本质原因。此外，我们还将设计可以与NFA在能级、相容性以及形貌等方面相匹配的聚合物给体材料。通过对传统具有温度诱导聚集特性的聚合物给体的修饰，我们希望合成一系列可以与不同能级小分子非富勒烯受体实现良好匹配的高性能聚合物材料。基于以上一系列的策略，我们的初步研究已使OPV实现了接近17.2％的光伏效率，这表明我们提出的研究方法的可行性和前瞻性。而我们的目标则是使OPV器件的光电转化效率达到20%。
