16505720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505720.value: Prior Research argues that the well-known analyst optimism is driven by analysts’ incentives to generate more trading commissions with buy than sell recommendations (e.g., Irvine, 2004; Hayes, 1998; Jackson 2005, and Cowen et al. 2006). Our proposed project questions the validity of this view, as well as the evidence in these prior studies. There are several reasons why we cast doubt on this conclusion: First, these prior studies draw their conclusion based on quantitative research outputs issued by analysts—earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. However, survey evidence show that the institutional investors who pay for equity research with their trading commissions do not use these quantitative research outputs (see annual survey conducted by Institutional Investor and the survey paper by Brown, Call, Clement and Sharp 2016). These survey evidence indicates that institutional investors consider phone calls and written reports much more useful than earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. In other words, prior research might focus on the wrong analyst research outputs in concluding the relation between analyst optimism and trading commission. Second, institutional investors are informed and sophisticated investors equipped with financial expertise and the resources to conducted their own independent research and analyses for the companies they invest. It is naïve and counterintuitive to assume they execute trades according to earnings forecasts and recommendations that are clearly optimistically biased. Third, analyst report text (i.e., the soft research output) is expensive and only accessible to institutional investors who pay for it (buy-side industry in the United States allocates around 60% of commissions, roughly $6 billion, to purchase research and advisory services from the sell side according to Greenwich Associates 2015; 2016), while earnings forecasts and recommendations are “free” and released to general public. Last, analysts spend much of their time on verbal and written communication with institutional clients rather than producing quantitative outputs, according to the weights in their compensation (Bradshaw, Ertimur and O’Brien 2016). Prior research shows that analyst report text provides incremental information beyond the hard outputs (Huang, Zang and Zheng 2014; Huang, Lehavy, Zang and Zheng 2018). Our proposal will revisit the relation between analyst optimism and trading commission by focusing on analyst report text. In addition, we will use a unique dataset that links institutional investors’ trades to analyst reports issued from the brokerage where they execute their trades to establish a more credible relation between trading commission and analyst optimism. 早前研究認為，賣方分析員意圖通過"買入"評級獲得比"賣出"評級更為豐厚的交易佣金，從而招致了其知名的樂觀傾向 (e.g., Irvine, 2004; Hayes, 1998; Jackson 2005, and Cowen et al. 2006)。我們提出一項研究計劃，置疑該觀點的效力與相關證據。理由如下: 第一，早前研究聚焦於分析員的量化研究產出，包括盈餘預測和股票評級，然而調查證據卻顯示通過交易佣金支付股票研究的機構投資者並非使用這些量化研究產出 (請參閱 Institutional Investor 期刊的年度調查和Brown, Call, Clement and Sharp 2016 的調查文章)。調查證據指出，機構投資者認為比起盈餘預測和股票評級，分析員的電話溝通和書面報告更為有用。換言之，早前研究或許使用了不正確的研究產出來推斷分析員樂觀傾向與交易佣金之間的關係。 第二，機構投資者是成熟且有見識的投資者。他們擁有財務專長和豐富資源對被投資公司進行獨立研究。因此，簡單地假設他們依賴於過度樂觀的盈餘預測和股票評級進行交易有違常理。 第三，分析員的書面報告售價高昂，因而只有為之付款的機構投資者可以閱讀其文字內容 (根據 Greenwich Associates 2015; 2016 的資料，全美國的買方機構每年分配百分之六十的交易佣金，約六十億美元來購買賣方分析員的研究與咨詢服務)。相反，盈餘預測和股票評級通常"免費"向公眾發放。 最後，分析員的薪酬構成表明，她們投入大量時間與機構客戶口頭與書面溝通，而非進行盈餘預測和股票評級 (Bradshaw, Ertimur and O’Brien 2016)。早前研究亦顯示，分析員報告的文字內容向市場提供了超越量化研究產出的額外資訊 (Huang, Zang and Zheng 2014; Huang, Lehavy, Zang and Zheng 2018)。 因此，我們的研究計劃將聚焦分析員報告的文字內容，再次探討分析員樂觀傾向與交易佣金之間的關係。另外，我們將使用一個獨特的數據以查看機構投資者與提供分析員報告的經紀公司之關聯，即該經紀公司是否以及以何種程度為機構投資者執行股票交易。這種設計有助於我們證實一個分析員樂觀傾向與交易佣金之間更為可信的關係。

16505720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505720.value: First, soft information produced by sell-side analysts is non-public information, based on which institutional investors trade stocks whereas retail investors do not. Second, among all buy-side institutions, a few top clients are better served with the soft information, as their trading responds to the soft content of the analyst's report. Third, the incremental trading responses of top clients to the soft information in the analyst's report are more pronounced when the information is more scarce and the competition for information is greater. Last, the trades based on soft information, primarily initiated by the top clients, are profitable. Overall, these findings are consistent with our prediction that important clients of the analyst follow the analyst's soft research output closely and profit from it. We are in the process of organizing the results, structuring the tests, and writing up the first draft of the working paper.

16505720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505720.value: We plan to finish various tests in the summer and start the formal writing process in the fall semester and finish the first draft in the fall. We target to submit the first draft for conferences or different schools' seminars for presentation early next year. After we collect feedback for several presentations, we will revise the paper and submit it for journal publication in the spring semester next year.

16505720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505720.value: We open the black box of the value provided by analysts, as the important information intermediary of the capital market. We show that there is a relationship between an analyst and the important clients he/she is serving. Specifically, an "important client" follows an analyst's soft research output closely, and makes profit from it by taking action (i.e., trading) earlier than other investors. These clients reward the analyst with commission revenue by trading at the brokerage house of the analyst.

16506020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506020.value: Anthropogenic climate change from the use of fossil fuels has become one of the major concerns of the 21st century. There has been increasing awareness in both the academia and industry to transit to clean technology in controlling and reducing fossil fuel emissions and potentially limiting climate change. Recent finance research recognizes the importance of financial constraints on firms' environmental policy and firms' corporate social responsibility. Meanwhile, there is empirical evidence showing that firms' environmental policies affect cost of capital. We plan to develop a tractable dynamic general equilibrium model with financial constraints and heterogeneous firms, which explicitly make optimal decisions between clean and dirty technologies. The clean technology is more expensive to install currently, but its production is not subject to the carbon tax in the future. In contrast, the dirty technology is less expensive to install to begin with, however, it products carbon emissions in its production, and is subject to an optimal carbon tax, the variations of which depend on the climate change risks. Our theory predicts that financial constraint is an important determinant for firms' optimal choice between clean and dirty technologies. Due to the fact that dirty technology is more exposed to climate risks through the optimal carbon tax, our model also predicts that firms with more dirty technology capital have more emission intensity and higher cost of capital. These model predictions are consistent with the above-mentioned motivating evidence. We will carefully calibrate and compute the model, study the quantitative model implications and empirically test the model implications using firm level data. This paper is a first attempt in the literature to provide a coherent and comprehensive theoretical framework to study the financing of clean technology and its asset pricing implications. For industry professionals, it will help increase their awareness of ESG factor and climate change risks. It will also motive them incorporate the ESG factor into account in their long-term investment decisions. 使用化石燃料造成的人為氣候變化已成為21世紀的主要關注之一。學術界和業界都已逐漸意識到使用清潔技術來控制和減少化石燃料的排放，並緩解氣候變化。最近的金融實證研究發現融資約束對公司的環保政策和公司社會責任的重要性。同時，有經驗證據表明企業的環保政策會影響資本成本。我們計劃構建一個具有融資約束和異質公司的動態一般均衡模型。在模型中，我們引入公司在清潔技術和污染技術之間做出最優決策。清潔技術的當期安裝成本較高，但其生產不產生碳排放，所以將來無需繳納碳排放稅收。相反，污染技術一開始安裝起來較便宜，但是，它會在生產過程中產生碳排放，並且要繳納最佳碳排放稅，而碳排放稅收的變化取決於氣候變化的風險。我們的理論預測，融資約束是企業在清潔技術和污染技術之間進行最佳選擇的重要決定因素。由於最佳的碳排放稅是隨氣候變化而變動的，污染技術更容易受到氣候風險的影響。我們的模型還預測，具有污染技術的公司有更高的污染排放強度，同時資金成本也更高。這些模型預測與上述啟發我們開展這項研究的實證證據一致。我們將仔細校準和計算模型，定量研究模型的含義，並使用公司層面的微觀數據對模型的含義進行實證驗證。本文是文獻中首次嘗試提供一個全面的理論框架來研究清潔技術的融資及其資產定價的含義。對於金融行業專業人士來說，這將有助於提高他們對ESG因素和氣候變化風險的認識。這也將促使他們將ESG因素納入其長期投資決策中。

16506020.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506020.value: Main findings and research outcome of the paper: Financing the Clean Technology and the Unintended Redistributive Implications, by Yan Ji, Kai Li, Yicheng Wang and Chenjie Xu 1. The paper develops a general equilibrium model that incorporates financial constraints and heterogeneous firms to analyze their optimal choice between clean and dirty technologies. 2. The study reveals a novel insight: the implementation of a carbon tax in such an economy can have unintended distributional consequences, specifically benefiting financially constrained firms. Key intuition: By examining firms' production processes, including investments in dirty and green capital, along with financial frictions, the paper finds that increased carbon taxes prompt financially unconstrained firms to shift towards green capital. This shift results in a lower price for dirty capital, which ultimately benefits financially constrained firms. 3. The findings are supported by various theoretical and quantitative examples, enhancing the credibility of the results. 4. Policy Implications: The study provides significant policy implications for designing carbon tax policies. In particular, the paper considers a social planner's approach to improving the decentralized market equilibrium by addressing climate externality and financial frictions. Points 1-2 are corresponding to objectives 1-2. Points 3 is corresponding to objective 3. The paper is presented at PHBS and Sargent Institute of Quantitative Economics and Finance. Main findings of the working paper: A Machine Learning-based Anatomy of Firm-level Climate Change Exposure, Weiwei Hu, Kai Li and Tingyu Yu 1. Developed firm-level climate change exposure measures using natural language processing on earnings call transcripts. 2. Measures cover both physical and transition perspectives of climate change. 3. Identified diverse strategies adopted by firms aligned with the greenhouse gas emission mitigation hierarchy. 4. These measures carry significant impacts on firm valuations: First, firms effectively reducing their own carbon emissions and those of their customers experience higher valuations and lower expected returns. Second, firms exposed to physical risks of climate change face profit losses and higher costs of equity. This paper is consistent with objective 4. The paper is presented at various conferences and seminars: HKIMR Webinar, FutFinInfo Webinar of Stockholm Business School, The 19th Chinese Finance Annual Meeting 2022 and The Second China Finance Advancement Forum 2023 Besides these two working papers. The Pollution Premium, by Po-hsuan Hsu, Kai Li and Chi-Yang Tsou, is forthcoming at Journal of Finance, the top international finance journal.

16506020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16506020.value: Overall, future research in this area should focus on leveraging the new insights provided by the study to inform and refine the design of carbon tax policies, taking into account the specific challenges faced by financially constrained firms. 1. Further investigation of the distributional consequences of implementing a carbon tax in an economy with financial constraints and heterogeneous firms. 2. Exploring the specific mechanisms and strategies through which financially unconstrained firms shift towards green capital in response to increased carbon taxes. 3. Examining the long-term implications of the lower price for dirty capital on financially constrained firms and their ability to benefit from the transition to clean technologies. 4. Evaluating the effectiveness of different policy interventions in addressing the unintended distributional consequences and financial frictions associated with carbon taxes. 5. Assessing the policy implications and potential trade-offs of optimal carbon tax design, considering both the climate externality and financial constraints faced by firms. 6. Conducting empirical research to validate the theoretical and quantitative findings presented in the study. 7. Investigating the broader implications of the study's insights for sustainable economic growth and the transition to a low-carbon economy. 8. Considering additional factors, such as regulatory frameworks and technological advancements, that could further enhance the optimal design of carbon tax policies.

16506020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506020.value: This research paper looks at how different companies choose between clean and dirty technologies. We found something interesting: when a carbon tax is introduced, it can have surprising effects on companies, especially those with financial struggles. Here's why: we studied how companies invest in both dirty and green technologies and the financial difficulties they face. When the carbon tax goes up, companies that aren't struggling financially tend to invest more in greener technologies. This reduces the demand for dirty technologies, which makes them cheaper. Surprisingly, this actually helps struggling companies because they can afford the cheaper dirty technologies. We looked at different examples, both theoretical and real-world, to support our findings. We also explored how a social planner could make things even better by considering the environmental impact of carbon emissions and the financial difficulties that companies face. Our study has important implications for policymakers. It can help them design better carbon tax policies that consider the challenges faced by struggling companies. In the end, we want to contribute to a more sustainable and fair transition to cleaner technologies.

16506720.label: Project Objectives
16506720.value: The first objective of the project is to examine the implications of various behavioral assumptions in terms of decisions about investment in financial products with features of derivative warrants. I plan to start with the basic model of Allen and Gale (1994) in which investors are fully rational. I will then add various behavioral assumptions, such as skewness preference, loss aversion, over-confidence, etc., individually and jointly. I will parameterize the behavioral models using state variables that can be mapped to the actual state variables to be used in the empirical work. The second objective is to use price and volume data on derivative warrants to construct test statistics for the hypotheses developed in the first objective for various behavioral models. These test statistics are based on unconditional distributions of the sample period, and conditional on state variables to generate more powerful tests. I will conduct a welfare analysis based on the results of the empirical tests.

16506720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506720.value: Hong Kong has an active market for derivative warrants which are issued by investment banks and traded mostly by individuals. Unlike many other financial innovations, derivative warrants are not initiated in the United States and they are not even traded there. While they are traded in several European countries, as well as in Australia, Singapore, and Korea, the trading volume and turnover ratio in Hong Kong in recent years has exceed those in all other parts of world combined. It is well documented that derivative warrants traders as a whole lose to the issuers and the returns to the traders are negative on average. The question is why the traders trade. A popular view is that these traders are unsophisticated, uninformed and behaviorally biased. Investment bankers simply pander to the biased behavior of the individual investors. This project aims to investigate the role various derivative warrants play in the financial market. It addresses the issues of whether these instruments help improve the performance of the traders' overall investment portfolios and what the pros and cons of participating the derivative warrants market are for individuals. The results of the project will shed light on the important question of whether and how derivatives can enhance investor welfare and how the financial market can function better to serve average investors. 香港有活跃的衍生权证市场，该权证是由投资银行机构发行，而 主要由散户进行交易的。与许多其他金融创新不同，衍生权证不 在美国发行，也不在那里交易。尽管它们在多个欧洲国家，澳大 利亚， 新加坡和韩国进行了交易，香港的交易量和周转率最近几 年已超过世界上所有其他地区的总和。有证据显示衍生权证交易 者整体上输给发行人，交易者获得收益平均为负。问题是为什么 交易者还要进行交易呢？ 一个流行的观点是这些交易者不老练， 没有信息，且行为偏颇。投资银行家只是在利用个人投资者的偏 颇行为。本研究项目旨在调查各种衍生权证在金融市场中的作用。 它探讨诸如衍生工具是否有助于改善投资者的投资组合的整体表 现， 参与衍生权证市场交易对个人有何利弊等问题。该研究项目 的结果有助于理解衍生品能否与如何提高投资者福利，以及金融 市场如何更好地为普通投资者服务的重要问题。

16506720.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506720.value: In this project, I teamed with a coauthor to study the relationship of expected asset returns with their skewness, besides variance. Most authors in the behavioral finance refer to the preference for skewness and associate behavioral bias as gambling or lottery preference, which pertains to the right tail of the return distribution. A heavier mass on the right tail, however, is not the only reason for the return skewness to be (perceived) larger. A lighter mass on the left tail can also increase the skewness. We examine how overpriced protection/insurance on assets can induce a negative relationship between expected asset returns and return skewness. We study this question in the market of callable bull/bear contracts (CBBCs) in Hong Kong. Li, Subrahmanyam and Yang (2018) also study the same market and find that these contracts have negative average returns with high return standard deviation and skewness, which they attribute this to the preference for lottery-type payoffs. We focus on the effect of downside insurance provided by most of the CBBCs. The insurance embedded in CBBCs increases skewness by cutting the left tail of the return distribution. We show that the expected return of CBBCs is negatively related to the skewness of the return, but more because of the perceived insurance on the left tail than the lottery feature on the right tail of the CBBC returns. By decomposing skewness into left skewness and right skewness, we find the expected CBBC return is more related to the left skewness of the return than the right skewness of the return, suggesting a stronger effect of overpaid insurance than that of overpaid lottery. The intended contribution of the project is to offer fresh evidence of the effect of behavioral biases on asset pricing. Most behavioral studies focus on lottery effect, and relatively little attention is paid to and less evidence has been documented on the insurance and loss aversion part of the prospect theory. Our contribution in addition to that of Li, Subrahmanyam, and Yang (2018) is that we make use of the insurance feature and contrast it with the proxy of lottery feature. We are able to show that in the case of Hong Kong CBBCs, the overpaid insurance effect actually dominates the overpaid lottery effect. The results are written in a paper titled "Overpaid Lottery and Overpaid Insurance: Evidence from Retail Structured Products." It has been accepted for presentation in several conferences. Afterwards, the paper will be submitted to journals for consideration of publication.

16506720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16506720.value: While the work is conducted in the Hong Kong derivative markets, the principles can be applied to a broader range of markets in the world. We plan to extend the work to other markets in which similar patterns exist.

16506720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506720.value: In this project we examine the returns on callable bull/bear contracts (CBBCs) listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Focusing on the residual value that these products typically possess, we show that CBBCs attract individual investors who are willing to pay relatively higher prices and to endure lower expected returns. We find that the CBBC expected return is negatively related to the skewness of the return, but this is more due to the overpriced insurance on the left tail (with less negative left skewness) than to the overpriced lottery payoff on the right tail (more positive right skewness). Our findings contribute to the literature of behavioral finance by offering evidence of loss aversion and overpriced insurance effect on asset pricing. The results in this project fill the gap by pinpointing this less noticed behavioral bias and the corresponding implication for asset pricing.

16506820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506820.value: 中国致力于人民币国际化已经有一段时间了。一般而言，国际货币具有三个功能：记帐单位，交换媒介和价值存储。一种货币在国际支付中的使用程度，是其在国际上的“交换媒介”功能的重要指标。国际支付可能基于不同原因，例如贸易结算，金融交易结算或国外直接投资结算。我们这项研究的目的，是希望建立一个定量分析模型来解释以人民币计价的国与国间的双边支付流量。为此，我们建议首先建立一个定量模型，来解释以某一特定货币计价的双边支付流量。然后，根据这个计量出来的模型，我们建立另一个模型，来解释国与 国间以人民币计价的双边支付流量。然后，我们将使用该模型进行一些推理实验。第一组推 理实验是使用模型来预测人民币的全球支付份额，如何随着各国的GDP、金融发展程度、以及资本账开放程度的变化而改变。第二组推理实验是评估 “一带一路” 倡议（BRI）对人民币支付流量的影响。我们推测 “一带一路” 倡议可以帮助扩大中国与 “一带一路” 沿线国家的贸易和对外直接投资，从而增强人民币作为 “一带一路” 项目的融资货币角色。根据这种观点，一带一路将增强人民币作为贸易结算和对外直接投资的结算货币的角色，以及增强其为“一带一路”相关基础设施项目的融资货币的角色。研究的策略是，首先，我们将建立一个定量的实证模型，来解释国与 国间以某一特定货币计价的双边支付流量。第二，根据这个计量出来的模型，我们建立另一个模型，来解释国与 国间以人民币计价的双边支付流量。第三，根据以上第二点计量出来的模型，我们将尝试预测人民币在全球支付中所占的份额，及其在中期与长期将如何随各国的经济发展而变化。第四，根据以上第二点计量出来的模型，我们将估计“一带一路” 如何影响各国间以人民币计价的双边支付流量，以及人民币的全球支付份额。在实务的层面上，我们相信我们的研究，能帮助了解和预测 “一带一路” 如何影响人民币计价的国际支付流量和人民币作为国际融资货币的程度，从而帮助政策制定者设计政策，和在诸如香港、新加坡和伦敦等离岸人民币中心的金融机构，计划未来。

16506820.label: Realisation of objectives
16506820.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved. First, the gravity model performs well in explaining inter-country bilateral payments flows by currency. Due to the gravity effect, the value of the bilateral payment flow by currency is negatively affected by distance but positively affected by: the GDP of the origin (destination) country, the relative development and openness of the financial market of the issuing country, and a set of other minor variables that affect the choice of a payment currency. In the book titled _One Currency, Two Markets: China’s Attempt to Internationalize the Renminbi_ (single-authored by Edwin L.-C. Lai) published by Cambridge University Press in September of 2021, in detail why capital account openness, financial development, as well as the GDP of the country, are the three most important economic factors that determine the international use of the country’s currency as a medium of exchange in trade and investment. In Chapter 8 of the book, I explain how to use a gravity model to explain quantitatively the global pattern of bilateral inter-country payments flows by currency. Then I explain how a counterfactual thought experiment can be carried out to estimate the payment share of any currency (such as the RMB) in global payments. In the working paper listed in Part C, I explain how the payment shares of different currencies evolve over time as the capital account openness, financial development, and the GDP of different countries change over time. To do that, I built a gravity model to explain quantitatively the global pattern of bilateral inter-country payments flows by currency. I made use of the data obtained from SWIFT for the bilateral inter-country payments flows by currency. First, I found that the gravity model works very well in explaining bilateral inter-country payments flows when aggregated over all currencies. Second, I found that gravity model works very well in explaining bilateral inter-country payments flows by currency. The regression results are shown in the table in Appendix A of the mid-term progress report, with the preferred result being column (7). One important right hand side variable in the regression equation for bilateral inter-country payments flows by currency above is “share ratio” (which is equal to the ratio of FX turnover share of the currency to the GDP share of the issuing country). I found that when I run a regression of “share ratio” on “capital account openness” and “financial development”, I obtain significant and positive coefficients, and the R^2 is also quite high, indicating that “capital account openness” and “financial development” are important determinants of “share ratio”. I argue that share ratio stands for the market thickness of the currency after controlling for the GDP of the issuing country. Thus, I conclude that the market thickness of a currency after controlling for the GDP of the issuing country is mostly determined by the “capital account openness” and “financial development” of the country. I found that there are no endogeneity issues with my regressions. From the above analysis, I conclude that the relative development and openness of the financial market of China are much more important than the economic size of China in determining the payment share of the RMB. I also found that the RMB’s payment share can be as high as 7% by 2030 if China’s growth rate maintains at 5.5% per year from 2016 to 2030 and its financial development and openness in 2030 reaches the level of Thailand’s in 2016. Second, the gravity model can explain bilateral RMB payments flows very well when applied to the top 30 RMB payment countries. The following regression result is based on SWIFT payments data for RMB payments for 2011-2016. As can be seen, almost all the relevant variables are significant to 1% level. sample size: union of top 30 total inbound and top 30 total outbound RMB payments countries Left hand side VARIABLE: RMB payment (converted into USD amount) Right hand side variables: t_year_2012 (fixed effect) 0.632*** t_year_2013 (fixed effect) 1.441*** t_year_2014 (fixed effect) 2.214*** t_year_2015 (fixed effect) 2.381*** t_year_2016 (fixed effect) 2.221*** lngdp_o 0.641*** lngdp_d 0.361*** lndistw -0.270** lnTradeShare_o -0.0165 lnTradeShare_d 0.385*** UK_o (fixed effect) 2.512*** UK_d (fixed effect) 1.026*** CHN_o (fixed effect) 4.475*** CHN_d (fixed effect) 5.052*** SGP_o (fixed effect) 2.743*** SGP_d (fixed effect) 2.620*** Constant -0.243 Observations 2330 R-squared 0.902 Robust standard errors in parentheses *** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1 UK = UK, CHN = China, SGP = Singapore. Definition of variables: gdp_o = GDP of origin (in trillions of USD) gdp_d = GDP of destination (in trillions of USD) TradeShare_o = share of trade with China in total trade of the origin country TradeShare_d = share of trade with China in total trade of the destination country distw = weighted distance (pop-wt, km) gdpShare = GDP share of China to the world shareratio = ratio of RMB turnover share and GDP share of China Third, I have used the above gravity model as a basis for estimating how the BRI can enhance the use of RMB as a payment currency through the increases in trade flows among B&R countries and the reduction of investment barriers between China and the B&R countries. I have carried out two counterfactual thought experiments to estimate the above two effects of BRI mentioned on global total RMB payments in 2016. My finding is that, to the extent that the BRI increases the trade shares of all B&R countries with China by 50% due to the increase in outward direct investments of China into these countries, the BRI will increase total global RMB-denominated payments by about 14%. To the extent that BRI reduces the trade costs of the two major corridors, namely the China‐Mongolia‐Russia Economic Corridor and the China–Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor, it will increase total global RMB-denominated payments by 6%. Fourth, the BRI should lead to RMB-denominated financing of the infrastructure projects in these BR countries, which requires financing from the offshore RMB centers such as HK, London and Singapore. Assuming that there is an amount of USD 0.6 trillion per year to be invested in infrastructure in the B&R in the ten years after 2016, and making the assumption that 50% of the financing is to be in RMB, it only amounts to an increase in 1.4% over the actual amount of RMB payment flow in 2016. Summing up the third and fourth results, the total effect of the BRI on RMB payment flows is equal to an increase of 14+6+1.4 = 21.4% of its payment share in 2016. The payment share of the RMB in 2016 is 1.62%, making it the 8th largest. Thus, BRI would increase the RMB’s payment share to 2.0%, and it will still be the 8th largest. Thus, we conclude that the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) does not significantly enhance the use of RMB as a global payment currency.

16506820.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506820.value: The major findings can be found in Chapter 8 of my book as well as the working paper listed in Part C. The first major finding is that the gravity model performs well in explaining inter-country bilateral payments flows by currency. Due to the gravity effect, the value of the bilateral payment flow by currency is negatively affected by distance but positively affected by: the GDP of the origin (destination) country, the relative development and openness of the financial market of the issuing country, and a set of other minor variables that affect the choice of a payment currency. The second major finding is that the gravity model can explain bilateral RMB payments flows very well. The relative development and openness of the financial market of China are much more important than the economic size of China in determining the payment share of the RMB. The third major finding is that the RMB’s payment share can be as high as 7% by 2030 if China’s growth rate maintains at 5.5% per year and its financial development and openness reached the level of Thailand’s in 2016. The fourth major finding is that the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) does not significantly enhance the use of RMB as a global payment currency, as explained below. To the extent that the BRI increases the trade shares of all B&R countries with China by 50%, the BRI will increase total global RMB-denominated payments by only 14%. To the extent that BRI reduces by 50% the inter-country bilateral trade costs for any pair of countries along the two major B&R corridors, it will increase total global RMB-denominated payments by only 6%. Assuming that there is an amount of USD 0.6 trillion per year to be invested in infrastructure in the B&R in the ten years after 2016, and making the assumption that 50% of the financing is to be in RMB, it only amounts to an increase in 1.4% over the actual amount of RMB payment flow in 2016. In sum, the total effect of the BRI on RMB payment flows is equal to an increase of 21.4% of its payment share in 2016. The payment share of the RMB in 2016 is 1.62%, making it the 8th largest. Thus, BRI would increase the RMB’s payment share to 2.0%, and it will still be the 8th largest.

16506820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16506820.value: Although the gravity model performs well in explaining the inter-country bilateral payments flows by currency, it is not satisfactory to mix the gravity effect with the currency choice effect in one single regression. Ideally, one would want to split the single-regression model into a two-layered model. In this two-layered model, the first layer is a gravity model that explains the bilateral payments flows (aggregated over all currencies). The second layer is a currency choice model that explains determinants of the share of each currency used to denominate the payment estimated in the first layer. One possible currency choice model is a discrete choice model. In the currency choice model, we should explain the share of a currency “cur” used to denominate the payment flow from sender country “s” to receiver country “r”. The payment share of “cur” is conjectured to be a function of a set of “first-nature” variables, such as capital account openness, financial development, and GDP of the issuing country of “cur”. It is also conjectured to be a function of the market thickness of “cur” (proxied by, for example, the foreign exchange turnover of “cur”), which I call a “second-nature” variable. The above is my work-in-progress.

16506820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506820.value: The current international monetary system is dominated by the US dollar (USD). For example, the USD is by far the most popular currency used to denominate trade, loans and bonds. Other countries have to use the USD when they trade, lend and borrow internationally. China, however, wants its international trade and finances to be independent of foreign currencies and foreign countries. Thus, China tries to internationalize the renminbi (RMB), i.e. to use RMB for denomination of trade, loans and debts. My research tries to explain what factors determine the extent to which a currency is used in international payments. I found that freer capital mobility, higher degree of financial development and higher GDP are the most important factors. In fact, I found that the first two factors are much more important than the third one. Thus, China has to greatly reduce its capital controls and liberalize its financial markets to make it much broader, deeper and more liquid if it wants to internationalize the RMB. Economic size alone cannot catapult the RMB into the league of major currencies used in international payments. I also found that the Belt and Road Initiative has very limited impact on RMB internationalization.

16601020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601020.value: 在學術界（Garfield，1955; Hirsch，2005）和高科技行業（Gittleman＆Kogut，2003; Moser，Ohmstedt和Rhode，2018年）, 引文數量已廣泛用作表示研究的影響力。多個表示研究影響力的指標（例如h指標，影響因子）, 正是從引文頻率得出的（Garfield，1999； Hirsch，2005年）。但是，以往的研究發現，引文受與研究影響無關的因素，例如數學方程式的多寡（Fawcett＆Higginson，2012）以及論文標題的長短（Letchford，Moat和Preis，2015）等，所左右。最近，我們發現了引文的新偏差，表明論文與第一作者姓氏的字母順序有負的關係（即姓氏順序）。這個偏差出現在兩個主要使用字母排序引文系統的學科（管理學和心理學），但沒有出現在另兩個主要使用數字引文系統的學科（生物學和化學）。 我們認為這種偏見很可能是由於人的認知限度導致對信息的選擇性關注（Baddeley，1992，2012; Kahneman，1973; Simon，1972，1991）。較早（相對於較晚）遇到的信息更可能儲在人的認知系統中（Deese＆Kaufman，1957; Ebbinghaus，1913; Murdock, 1962）, 所以更容易被引用。同時，我們的初步發現選擇性記憶檢索似乎不能解釋因姓氏排序引致的偏差。 儘管我們較早的發現與選擇性關注的說法相符，但該研究在概括性，因果關係和實際含義方面存在局限性（詳請參見建議書）。在這項提案中，我們提出了三組研究來解決這些問題。在第一組中，我們將包括更多學科以提升研究結果的概括性。在第二組中，我們將實驗性地操弄姓氏順序來建立因果關係。第三組將擴大這種偏見對職業發展的影響，以加強實際意義。 我們的研究將在理論和實踐上都有貢獻。從理論上講，它將揭示了引文偏見的心理機制（即選擇性關注）。實際上，我們的發現將引導我們建立一個更公平，準確的系統，表明研究的影響。

16601820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601820.value: 本研究的目的是检测香港民意调查中受访者是否如实回答政治敏感性问题，而不是由于外部政治社会环境的压力而隐瞒其真实想法。政治敏感性对民意调查的干扰是影响民意调查准确性的普遍问题，在世界各国都存在。例如，在美国，白人受访者会隐藏他们对少数族裔的种族偏见，在中国，人们通常不愿意在接受访问中承认他们的行贿行为。 本研究的第一步是确定在香港社会什么样的问题属于敏感问题，其中包括港人对中国的认同，是否参与反送中的示威游行，对示威游行中的暴力所持态度，或者对社会上少数群体的态度，例如同性恋、菲佣等等。 检测政治敏感性的方法叫做列表实验，这个方法是由美国政治学者在１９９０年代首先发明的，目的是检测美国白人在接受面对面问卷调查时是否会隐瞒他们对黑人的种族偏见。列表实验目前正在被广泛应用于各个国家的民意调查中，用来检测不同社会中社会政治敏感问题为民意调查结果所带来的偏差。 本研究的具体步骤是，首先以１６岁以上的香港居民为基础，抽取一个２０００人的随机样本，然后将２０００人的样本随机分为５组，每组４００人。五组中的一组设为控制组，其它４组为实验组，每一个实验组中将嵌入一个列表实验，每一个列表实验将包括一个敏感问题，例如１）对中国的认同感；２）返送中游行参与行为；３）对游行中的暴力行为的支持度；以及４）对港独的支持度。 列表实验的好处是，它可以比较准确地估计出有百分之多少的受访人在回答上述问题时，出于香港社会当下的社会政治压力而隐瞒了自己的真实想法，如果这个方法在香港的民意调查中成功得到应用，将为香港今后的民意调查提供一个方法，有效避免因为政治社会敏感问题所产生的误差。 最后，本调查将对列表实验方法进行进一步完善，也就是在列表实验结果的基础上建立一个加权变量，再通过加权变量来分析政治敏感性的个人特征，例如年龄，教育，性别，社会经济地位，政治倾向，家庭环境等因素对政治敏感性的影响。

16601920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601920.value: As American writer J. D. Salinger famously claimed, “love is a touch yet not a touch.” Touch, as the most private and fleeting of the senses, plays a vital role in bodily experiences of intimacy, love, and sexuality. Amidst the transformations of the first half of the twentieth century in Republican China, intimate touch assumed a new significance and intensity in modern Chinese literature and culture under the powerful influence of western Romanticism, classical Hollywood films, advertising and publicity, and a variety of other modern stimuli. Through selected examples from poetry (written in both the classical and vernacular styles), fictional and non-fictional narratives, and visual images, this project explores intimacy as a tactile experience and sensation as well as a representation and discourse that shape collective sensibilities and feelings. The critical issues examined include: how the immediate, fleeting interaction and electrifying sensations are represented in different literary genres; how bodily self-awareness and sensation in touching hands and lips link to the formation of modern selfhood as well as the self’s relationship with others through corporeal copresence; how the notion of intimacy as private and personal intervenes in the mapping of social, public, and gendered spaces; in which ways the sensory experience interconnects with feelings, emotions, and memories in the tumultuous journey of modern China. Not only has Chinese emotional life experienced substantial transformations, but also both the conceptualization and practice of romantic intimacy have been significantly reconfigured as the corporeal basis of language and modern subjectivity. Exploring the previously unexamined sensuous realm and embodied experience of Chinese modernity in the twentieth century, this project will elucidate a range of critical issues concerning the intertwined relationship between tactility and vision, touch and bodily feeling, tactile experience and its relationship with the formation of the individual voice, desire and subjectivity, and the subject’s chiasmic relationship with the other and the world. Through exploration of the distinctiveness of touch as a sense and as a topic of literary-historical inquiry, this project will illuminate the intertwined relationship between sense experience, emotion, and representation in these eras of radical cultural transformations. 現代文化的變革並非僅僅是思想、技術的變革，同時亦是感知、感覺的革命。學界多年來關注視覺的審美效果，強調視覺在現代文化建構中的突出意義。本課題嘗試突破此類視覺至上的感官秩序，探討親密的觸碰、撫摸、接吻、握手等觸覺行為在文學與文化中的意義。討論議題包括，感知感覺的經驗，如何構成現代自我主體性的基石，如何與集體、公共、家國的大場域相聯繫，如何與情感、記憶互動，如何與革命、啟蒙、抒情話語相呼應等。

16601920.label: Realisation of objectives
16601920.value: The project commenced in January 2021 and has been recently completed. Over the past four years, I have surveyed many primary materials concerning touch, kissing, and intimacy from late imperial China and contemporary China. Primary materials for this project have covered: (1) the translation of Western poetry and literature relating to intimacy and romantic love in the early twentieth century; (2) a significant number of stories and poems on touch and intimacy; (3) essays, memoirs, and descriptions of viewing and reading experiences of romantic intimacy; (4) visual materials such as Hollywood and Chinese films and photographs that present kisses and touch. After working through many primary sources, I have completed the writing outlined in the project proposal, published two research articles, and co-edited one volume on modern China’s sensory revolution. Five chapters that I have drafted focus on the five topics of “Kiss as Translated Intimacy,” “Kiss and Caress as Intercorporeal Dialogue,” “Kiss and Touch as Sensible Ideas,” “Handshaking in Memory and Cultural Politics,” and “Being Touched and Feeling-With.” All five topics that were in the original proposal have been written in a chapter format. As mentioned in my mid-term report, I have further adjusted the project’s thematic focus by adding a number of critical focuses to interrogate issues such as how the human body works as a multisensory register of material reality and how Western psychoanalytic discourses (e.g., Freudian theory) and Japanese literary/popular aesthetics (notably ero guro nansensu) influenced Republican-era culture. I have analyzed how emerging media forms—such as cartoons—functioned as conduits for affective engagement, leveraging visual and narrative strategies to stimulate reader-viewers’ sensory and imaginative faculties directly. This new set of materials and critical inquiries have been realized in my forthcoming article “Theatre of Emotion” (proof attached in Section 8), but will not be included in the final book manuscript, since this topic goes beyond the original framework for a thematically coherent book. Developing from the original proposal, I have expanded the manuscript to include two additional chapters. Chapter One reconstructs the “prehistory” of kissing and sensuous touch by analyzing traditional literary and visual materials. By tracing these historical representations, this chapter establishes a critical foundation for interrogating how modern intimacy ruptured from earlier practices. In response to the rapidly evolving socio-technological landscape, the final chapter shifts focus to the intersection of tactility and machinic interfaces in contemporary culture. This addition explores themes such as disembodied kissing (e.g., digital or virtual encounters) and the erotics of human-machine relationships in science fiction and film. By synthesizing these threads, this revised framework enables a more rigorous, historically grounded analysis of how affect, materiality, and sensory experience collectively shape the contested terrain of Chinese literary and sensory modernity. The General Research Grant has greatly assisted me in my research, providing additional time for teaching relief and writing, and supporting the hiring of research assistants in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan, while I was unable to take research trips to conduct archival research during the pandemic era. These supports have been essential for the successful completion of the project. I am tremendously grateful for the support that I have received. The RGC’s support has been acknowledged in the publication of two research articles (attached in section 8) and will be prominently acknowledged in the book on the making of intimacy in modern China upon its publication. Outlines for the monograph in final preparation The Introduction offers etymological studies of the keywords such as wen (kissing), lian’ai (romantic love), and chujue (the sense of touch), illuminating their translingual trajectories with the West and Meiji Japan. It also provides discussions of phenomenological interpretations of tactility and critical understanding of mutually imbricated tactility, vision, and flesh, and their metaphorical and ethical implications. Chapter One briefly depicts the “prehistory” of kissing and sensuous touch in traditional literature and visual materials, the Republican era’s unprecedented kissing fad, and the debates surrounding the morality, hygiene, danger, scientific discourse, and proper techniques for engaging in kissing. Chapter Two focuses on the circulation of classical Hollywood stars’ images in pictorial magazines and Republican moviegoers’ experiences of visual intimacy. Evoking Laura Marks’s formulation of “haptic visuality,” it analyzes the reconfiguration of viewers’ relationships with the image of touching and kissing, and how the affect-charged image functions as the representation of haptic experience. This chapter is revised from my article in Sensing China: Modern Transformation of Sensory Culture, coedited by Xuelei Huang and myself (Routledge, 2023). Chapter Three explores the thematic interlocking of love, beauty, and death, drawing a range of influences of Western romanticism, the aesthetic movement, and fin de siècle aesthetics. Through discussing different sets of literary materials (including Zhou Shoujuan’s fixation on death after kissing and Tian Han’s translation of Oscar Wilde’s Salomé), the chapter investigates the role literary translation played in the formation of the modern sensorium, as well as the pervading romantic dichotomy between love and death, art and life, carnality and spirituality in love. Chapter Four describes the intimate scenes as “sensible ideas” (in Merleau-Ponty’s term) and extraordinary, fraught “events.” Focusing on the aspects of kissing during intoxication, kissing as a lyrical pause, and the kiss in memory by offering re-readings of well-known stories by Lin Shuhua, Eileen Chang, Shi Tuo, and others, this chapter studies narrative desire, gender politics, and embodied experience in the development of the genre of modern short stories. Chapter Five examines sensual touch, sensations, and their relationship to flesh by investigating image-text practices and modernism in Republican Shanghai. Exploring the eruption of multisensory experience and the heightened attention to tactility from neo-sensationalist writers, it then analyzes one recurring literary theme, i.e., caressing the female body, or more specifically, a machine-like female body, offering reflections on the entangled relationship between consumerism, technology, and embodied experience. Chapter Six reads the handshake and its precariousness as a central plot device featured in a number of socialist stories such as Zhang Yang’s The Second Handshake and Zhang Jie’s “Love Must Not Be Forgotten”. Handshaking (an adopted modern custom) as a substitute for kissing or other forms of bodily contact registers the coded expressions of erotic desires in socialist literature. The chapter also considers the reading and viewing experience of forbidden “underground” novels such as The Heart of a Maiden and foreign films like The Waves of the Danube in the restrictive political climate of the Cultural Revolution, along with the suppression of sexuality, and erotic impulses sublimated through reading, viewing, and imagining. Then exploring various topics such as the kissing app, kissing without a body, and the amorous relationship between humans and machines in contemporary film and science fiction (e.g., The Kiss Addict and Membranes), Chapter Seven offers insights into the affective intimacy of touching and mediality in the hyper-media environment of the present and the collective dystopian future.

16601920.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601920.value: This project has explored romantic intimacy’s connection to and rupture with the traditional emotional discourse of love, with a distinct focus on the role of the tactile and carnal. In conjunction with the four objectives that were set up in the proposal, some major findings include: 1) Through re-examining the historical developments on emotions and senses, this project argues that historical experiences have significantly contributed to the formation of modern senses and emotional life; 2) the project has illustrated the interplay between sensory perception, affective states, and subject formation and their relationship with literary form, rhetorics and images; 3) through charting the historical trajectories, the project has offered a new understanding of the transformation of sensory practices and intimate bonds, as well as the modern sensorium and emotional landscapes; 4) this project has brought critical attention to the larger issues in modern Chinese literary studies and literary modernity, and their enduring influence in contemporary cultural production. 16601920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601920.value: I am currently preparing the book manuscript in English, which has been significantly expanded from the original proposal in terms of its material bases and critical issues. In order to reach a broader readership, I am planning to publish a Chinese edition in a style accessible to general readers, soon after the publication of the English monograph, through recognized presses in mainland China and Taiwan. This will further disseminate and share my research findings with a Chinese audience, and help educate readers to gain a better understanding of Chinese emotional life. I plan to continue to give public lectures at a variety of venues such as universities, museums, libraries, and local communities, as well as podcasting and web posting, catering to the general public’s fascination with Republican-era culture and modern love stories.

16601920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601920.value: This study cuts across the disciplines of literature, visual studies, sensory research and cultural studies. By looking at literary magazines, stories, poetry, love letters and images, the project explores acts of romantic touching, kissing and handshakes, and how they functioned in twentieth-century China. It shows that the Chinese emotional life experienced substantial transformations during this time, and also illuminates the intertwined relationships among sensory experience, emotion, and literary representation. It examines how sensuous touch and kisses are represented in literary genres in different historical eras; how bodily self-awareness and sensation link to the formation of modern self as well as the self’s intimate relationships; how the idea of intimacy as private and personal interacts with social, public, and gendered spaces; and the ways sensory experience interconnects with feelings, emotions, and memories in the tumultuous journey of modern China. These intimate social gestures, etiquette, and expressive behaviors changed the language and narrative forms of the time, and can help us understand the relationship of embodied experience and Chinese literary modernity. Like the popular song ‘As Time Goes By” from Casablanca has it, “a kiss is never just a kiss.”

16602420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16602420.value: 消费者异质性和冲击的国际分配效应

16602420.label: Project Objectives
16602420.value: The first objective of this project is to document empirical facts on the impact of US monetary policy shocks and productivity shocks on consumption inequality in foreign countries. There have been a number of research on the distributional effect of monetary policies, both empirically and theoretically. But few of them focus on the spillover effect of US monetary policies on inequality in foreign countries. So in this project we intend to fill this gap. The second objective is to introduce heterogeneous agent into a standard two country New Keynesian model to study the international distributional effect of monetary policy shock and productivity shocks theoretically. We also want to check if the theoretical predication of shocks on domestic and foreign consumption inequality is consistence with the empirical evidence. The third objective is to explore how the distributional factors affect the international transmission mechanism of shocks. In particular, we are interested in finding out if the exchange rate regime choice and the export price setting behaviour will affect the distributional effects of shocks or channels through which heterogeneity affect international transmission of shocks.

16602420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602420.value: The income and wealth inequality have increased in developing countries as well as OECD countries during the last few decades. With persistent inequality, how economic policies affect the inequality, or the distributional effect of policies has attracted attentions and heated discussion among policy makers and academic researchers. Meanwhile, with the substantive deepening of trade and financial integration of the global economy, the spillover effect from shocks in other economies, especially those from large developed economies such as the US and the Euro zone, has attracted academics, policy makers, and investors to put more efforts in understanding the relevant transmission mechanisms of international shocks. However, few papers connect these two literatures and study the international distributional effect of shocks and policies in foreign countries or explore how inequality affect the international transmission of shocks. So in this project, we will explore how foreign productivity shocks and monetary shocks, especially that of the large economies such as the US and the Eurozone, affect the domestic consumption inequality empirically and theoretically. We will also explore the channel through with heterogeneity affect the transmission mechanism of shocks in an open economy. Using the data on consumption inequality from Canada and US, and US monetary and productivity shocks, we will first estimate VAR models and construct impulse responses of consumption inequality to policy or productivity shock. Then we will develop a theoretical model which introduces heterogeneous agents and incomplete domestic financial market into a standard two-country open economy New Keynesian model. This model will help us to explore if the theoretical prediction of international distributional effect is consistent with the empirical evidence. With the theoretical model, we will also be able to analyze how the heterogeneity affect the international transmission of shocks qualitatively and quantitatively. In particular, it is will be interesting to see how the exchange rate regime choice and export pricing behavior will affect the channels through which the real economy is affected by inequality in an open economy. Research output from the project will help the academics and policy makers understand more the impact of household heterogeneity on international transmission mechanism and the impact of monetary policy on inequality. It will also provide a framework for policy analysis for governments, international companies and institutions such as IMF and World Bank. 在过去几个世纪里，发展中国家和经合组织国家等发达国家的收入和财富不均问题都日益严重。面对持续的贫富不均，经济政策对收入以及消费不平等的影响及其分配效应引起了政策制定者和学术研究者的广泛兴趣和热烈讨论。 与此同时，随着全球经济在贸易和金融领域的整合不断深化，来自外国的冲击，特别是来自大的发达国家（比如美国和欧元区）的冲击之溢出效应，也吸引了学术界，政策制定者，和投资者更加努力去了解国际冲击对本国经济的传导机制。 但是，很少有研究把两个研究领域和文献联系起来；研究外国政策或者冲击带来的分配效应，或者说，研究外国冲击如何影响本国的贫富差距。 所以，在这个项目中我们打算从理论和实证上研究外国的生产率冲击和货币冲击，尤其是来自美国和欧元区的这些大国的冲击，如何影响本国的消费不均。与此同时，我们也希望探索消费者异质性将如何影响开放经济下外部冲击的传导机制。 首先，本文将利用加拿大以及美国的消费数据，货币政策冲击和生产率冲击等数据，使用VAR方法，来估计消费不平等对货币冲击和生产率冲击的脉冲反应。 然后我们会将消费者异质性和不完美的国内金融市场引入标准的凯恩斯两国开放经济模型，从而为本文的分析为构建理论基础。模型拟合将帮助我们检验理论预测的分配效应是否和实证证据吻合。在理论模型的帮助下，我们也能够定性和定量地分析消费者异质性是如何影响这些冲击的国际传导机制。特别值得一提的是，我们可以研究汇率制度选择以及出口定价行为会如何在开放经济下改变贫富差距对实体经济的影响。 这个项目的研究成果将帮助学术界和政策制定者了解消费者的差异性对国际冲击传导机制的影响，以及大国的货币政策对发展中国家贫富不均的影响。同时，项目也会给政府和国际组织，比如世界银行，货币基金，提供一个政策分析框架。

16602420.label: Realisation of objectives
16602420.value: In Objective 1, we intend to document empirical facts on the relationship between US monetary policy shocks and productivity shocks and consumption inequality in foreign countries. This objective is almost complete. To explore this relationship, my initial plan is to use the Canadian micro-level household expenditure survey data to empirically explore the impact of US monetary policy shocks and productivity shocks on consumption inequality in foreign countries. The two datasets are the Survey of Household Spending (SHS) and the Survey of Family Expenditures (SFE), which can be combined to document features of the distribution of income, consumption and wealth in Canada. However, since both data set are confidential, I need to file an application to Statistics Canada to get access to these datasets and process them in a Research Data Centres (RDC) located in Canada. As explained in the midterm report, due to the travel restrictions and quarantine requirement caused by Cov-19 pandemic, I am not able to collect and process these datasets in Canada until mid-2023. Now I have already got the approval for these datasets, and I will go to Canada to process these data in the summer 2025. Meanwhile, I have also collected some data from several household survey dataset discussed in earlier progress reports, such as Peruvian household survey, Encuesta Nacional de Hogares (ENAHO), South African National Income Dynamics Study (NIDS), the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS). These micro datasets include both the income and expenditure of households, so we can derive key information about consumption heterogeneity and income inequality. My RA has already collected data on income inequality, as well as data on US monetary shocks and productivity shocks. He is now working on processing and organizing data to get information on consumption inequality. Empirical analysis using income equality data and US monetary policy shocks indicates that the response of consumption to productivity shocks varies significantly between low-inequality and high-inequality countries. This suggests that income inequality affects the transmission of technology shocks to output and consumption, which aligns with the predictions of our theoretical model. Additionally, we find that the spillover effects of U.S. monetary policies are greater in countries with higher income inequality. These findings are also consistent with the results presented in our JME paper. I will keep working on using the two Canadian datasets and household survey data to explore how consumption inequality will affect the US monetary shocks spillover. Our JME paper predicts that demand spillovers from monetary shocks are increasing in heterogeneity in the source and receiving country. Our empirical finding already proves this prediction using income inequality. An interesting follow-up from our results would be to explore if the spillover of US monetary policy shocks depends on the degree of consumption heterogeneity within and across countries and how the exchange rate regime and capital flow will affect this relationship. We are working on that. For Objective 2, we plan to introduce heterogeneous agent into a standard two country New Keynesian model to study the international distributional effect of monetary policy shock and productivity shocks theoretically. In Objective 3, we will explore how the distributional factors affect the international transmission mechanism of shocks. In particular, we want to understand how this impact will depend on the currency of pricing Objectives 2 and 3 have been completely realized. In the paper entitled “Consumption heterogeneity and monetary policy in an open economy” which is published in Journal of Monetary Economics in November 2023, we extend Debortoli and Gali (2018)’s TANK (Two Agents New Keynesian model) to a two-country model to explore how consumption heterogeneity affects the transmission mechanism of monetary policy in open economy. We incorporate two types of agents (Ricardian versus Keynesian) into a standard open economy macro model. We find that consumption heterogeneity has major implications for the impact of monetary policy shocks, the international transmission mechanism, and the design of optimal monetary policy. With sticky prices, the existence of Keynesian agents causes a spillover of shocks across countries, and leads to the interdependence of optimal monetary targeting rules. In the case of local currency pricing, consumer heterogeneity leads an optimal monetary policy to generate currency misalignment and deviations from the law of one price. Theoretically, there are ranges of household heterogeneity in which monetary policy becomes ineffective, but this depends sensitively on the interaction of aggregate demand and relative price effects. There has been an extensive debate about the question of whether central banks should be concerned with distributional effects of monetary policy. We extend this debate into the open economy in a simple but tractable model in which there is consumer heterogeneity due to the inability of a group of consumers to access financial markets. Consumer heterogeneity has important effects on the outcome of monetary policy shocks and the transmission of monetary shocks across countries. Optimal monetary policy rule should take account of consumer heterogeneity, and with heterogeneity, optimal monetary targeting rules become interdependent. In the situation of local currency pricing, an optimal monetary policy actively allows for deviations from the law of one price as a second best policy in face of consumer heterogeneity. During the entire reporting period, I attended five conferences, two of which were regional and the other two were international. Unfortunately, due to travel restrictions and lockdown measures imposed during the Covid-19 pandemic, I was unable to present my paper at many international conferences, nor can I interact with international scholars about this project. Therefore, I made the most of my trip to the United States last summer by attending conferences and visiting esteemed scholars in the field, including Dr. Nan Li and Dr. Dong He from the IMF, as well as Prof. Ruixue Jia from UCSD. Their valuable insights and suggestions greatly contributed to the development of my project, and I gained significant knowledge from our discussions. It is important to note that the expenses for attending conferences have significantly increased after the Covid-19 pandemic. For instance, the airfare from Hong Kong to Washington DC, and then to San Diego, alone cost approximately HKD $20,000. The hotel expenses in the US have also increased significantly. Since I stayed in Washington DC and San Diego for attending conferences and discussing the paper with scholars in the field for some time, the costs related to accommodation and daily expenses were also quite high. Furthermore, I also attended the EEA-EMES conference in Barcelona last August. It lasted for five days, and the airfare and hotel/subsistence added approximately another $30,000 to the conference expenses. At the conference, I had the opportunity to meet scholars like Dr Zheng Liu from the San Francisco Fed and Dr. Sergio Villalvazo from Federal Reserve Board, and Philippe Bacchetta from University of Lausanne. Our discussion of the paper and future research on the second paper from this project greatly benefited me. Overall, after the Covid-19 pandemic, I have actively taken the chances to interact with international scholars and participate in international conferences. Meanwhile, it is important to note that conference expenses have increased due to factors such as rising airfare and accommodation/daily expenses during the post-Covid period.

16602420.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602420.value: 1. A paper titled 'Consumption Heterogeneity and Monetary Policy in an Open Economy' was published in the Journal of Monetary Economics in November 2023. This paper incorporates two types of agents---Ricardian and Keynesian---into a standard open economy macro model. Our findings reveal that consumption heterogeneity has significant implications for the impact of monetary policy shocks, the international transmission mechanism, and the design of optimal monetary policy. 2. A working paper entitled 'A Tractable Heterogeneous Agent Framework for International Monetary Policy Analysis', which we recently presented at the 8th International Macroeconomics and Finance Conference at HKUST in June 2024. In our JME paper, while the TANK model maintains tractability, it sacrifices some mechanisms through which household heterogeneity influences optimal consumer decisions, such as precautionary saving. In this project, following Bilbiie (2024), we introduce the possibility of type-switching between savers and hand-to-mouth agents to develop a tradable heterogeneous agent New Keynesian two-country model. This introduction of type-switching allows for uninsurable income risk and precautionary saving. Our findings indicate that, in this context, the dynamics of the terms of trade will influence the likelihood of switching and the degree of heterogeneity. This suggests that the real income channel and precautionary saving effects may interact in the open economy, impacting both the domestic and spillover effects of domestic monetary shocks, as well as the design of optimal monetary policy and the coordination gains from international monetary policy cooperation.

16602420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602420.value: 1.Continue investigating whether the spillover effects of U.S. monetary policy shocks depend on the degree of consumption heterogeneity both within and across countries, and how the exchange rate regime and capital flows influence this relationship. Additionally, we aim to examine how the responses of terms of trade and real exchange rates to monetary and productivity shocks vary with income and consumption inequality. 2.Continue working on the project titled 'A Tractable Heterogeneous Agent Framework for International Monetary Policy Analysis.' Preliminary findings indicate that this paper will significantly enhance our understanding of how income inequality affects the transmission mechanisms of monetary policy and the formulation of optimal monetary policy in open economies.

16602420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602420.value: It is well observed that income inequality and heterogeneous financial inclusion rise worldwide. In the United States, for example, the Gini coefficient increased from 0.4 in 1980 to 0.49 in 2021, according to the US Census Bureau. Similar trend is also observed in other OECD countries. With persistent and increasing inequality, there has been an extensive debate about the question of whether central banks should be concerned with distributional effects of monetary policy. We extend this debate into the open economy in a simple but tractable model in which there is consumer heterogeneity due to the inability of a group of consumers to access financial markets. Consumer heterogeneity has important effects on the outcome of monetary policy shocks and the transmission of monetary shocks across countries. Optimal monetary policy rules should take account of consumer heterogeneity, and with heterogeneity, optimal monetary targeting rules become interdependent. Findings from this project will help the academics, policy makers, and international organizations such as IMF or World Bank to understand how inequality affects international transmission mechanism of shocks. It also provides a framework for policy analysis that incorporates international distributional effects into the design of stabilization policies and coordination among monetary authorities across economies.

16602520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16602520.value: 選擇中立國的韓戰戰俘：從中國、朝鮮到印度與拉丁美洲

16602520.label: Project Objectives
16602520.value: To narrate the global odysseys of the 88 Korean War prisoners who chose neutral nations, tracking their journeys from China and Korea to India and finally to Latin America from the late 1940s to the present. To examine the concept of neutrality, its contested meanings, and grassroots experiences of “neutrality.” What did “neutrality” mean to the prisoners and to the governments of India, Argentina, and Brazil? How did its meaning evolve at different historical junctures? To broaden our understanding of the origins, processes, and aftermaths of the Korean War in temporal, spatial, conceptual, and human dimensions. To make historical writing on the Korean War truly transnational and comparative by bringing in both Chinese and Korean prisoners’ voices and using archival sources from the PRC, Taiwan, South Korea, India, the United States, and the United Nations.

16602520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602520.value: Using both Chinese and North Korean POWs’ oral histories and multinational archival documents, this project examines the global odysseys of the 88 POWs who refused repatriation and sought asylum in neutral countries at the end of the Korean War. Their unusual choices and life histories in three continents allow the authors to transcend the nationalist paradigm. With an eye for the human experience in all its complexity, this project examines the experiences of these ordinary men who made extraordinary decisions. Compelling us to rethink Cold War "neutrality" through grassroots diaspora experience, this bottom-up history will broaden our understanding of the origins, processes, and aftermaths of the Korean War in temporal, spatial, and human dimensions. 本研究利用中國和朝鮮戰俘的口述歷史與多國檔案，聚焦於在韓戰結束後拒絕遣返而尋求中立國庇護的88名中國和朝鮮籍戰俘，重建他們在三大洲不尋常經歷。本研究試圖超越民族主義範式，著眼於個人經歷的複雜性，分析考察這些底層人物的決定與選擇，以此重新思考冷戰時期「中立」的複雜意涵，拓寬我們對韓戰的起源、過程及其後果的理解。

16602520.label: Realisation of objectives
16602520.value: The project aimed to explore the journeys of 88 Korean War prisoners who chose neutral nations, examine the concept of neutrality, and broaden our understanding of the Korean War's origins, processes, and aftermaths. The project was conducted from 1 November 2020 to 31 October 2023. Unfortunately, a significant portion of the project coincided with the global COVID-19 pandemic, resulting in various challenges. The pandemic had a severe impact on regions crucial to the project, such as Hong Kong, South Korea, and India, which served as the planned archival research site. Travel restrictions imposed during this period prevented the team from participating in conferences or workshops until 2023. The long-planned visits to archives in India, especially the Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Museum and Library (NMML) in New Delhi, were not materialized. However, the project team quickly adapted to the challenging circumstances and found alternative avenues to advance their research. Significant progress has been made, and the project has or is on track to achieve its various objectives by 2025. Paper #5 entitled "Jawaharlal Nehru and India's Role in Resolving the POW Controversy in the Korean War" is expected to be published in an edited volume by a top university press in 2025. OVERCOMING COVID-CAUSED DISRUPTIONS In a fortunate turn of events, in 2021, the PI was invited by Tansen Sen of New York University, Arunabh Ghosh of Harvard University, and Gal Gvili of McGill University to join the collaborative project entitled "China and India in an Age of Decolonization: An Analysis of the Nehru Papers, 1947–1964." As a member of a team of fifteen scholars from North America and Asia, the PI took on the task of examining the Nehru papers during the Korean War era (1950 to 1953) and contributing a book chapter in an open-access edited volume on Indian-Chinese relations during the Cold War based on the Nehru papers. After an unsuccessful application for funding from the US National Endowment of the Humanities in 2021–2022, the project team was finally awarded a substantial NEH grant of U$244,624 in August 2023. Only then was the project formally launched, and the PI gained access to more than 30,000 pages of archival documents from the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library. OBJECTIVE ACHIEVEMENTS: Throughout the grant period, the project team made significant progress in achieving the project's objectives: 1. Narrating Korean War Prisoner’s Global Odysseys: The team successfully traced the journeys of the 88 Korean War prisoners from China and Korea to India and ultimately to Argentina and Brazil. Through extensive research and analysis of archival sources, including documents from Argentina, Brazil, China, Taiwan, South Korea, Switzerland, the United States, and the United Nations, the project shed light on the experiences of these prisoners. 2. Examining the Concept of Neutrality: The project delved into the contested meanings of neutrality and explored how it was perceived by the prisoners themselves and the governments of India, Argentina, and Brazil. The evolving interpretations of neutrality at different historical junctures were examined, deepening our understanding of this concept. 3. Broadening Understanding of the Korean War: By incorporating the voices of Chinese and Korean prisoners and employing a transnational and comparative approach, the project expanded our understanding of the Korean War in temporal, spatial, conceptual, and human dimensions. 4. Writing a transnational history of the Korean War: The research brought together diverse perspectives and highlighted the interconnectedness of global events during this period.

16602520.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602520.value: PUBLICATIONS This project was a resubmission of a previous unsuccessful GRF application. The PI and Co-Is have been actively working on the project since early 2019. In the 2019 Proposal, the PI declared having organized an AAS panel in 2019 and being commissioned to guest edit a theme issue of The Journal of American-East Asian Relations (JAEAR). The special issue, which includes Outputs #1, 2, and 3, was published in late 2020, coinciding with the official start of the current project. Regrettably, acknowledgment of RGC funding was omitted, due to the chaos and confusion in the early months of the pandemic. Nevertheless, these outputs were the direct outcome of the project, despite the official project start date being one year after actual work began. The JAEAR theme issue entitled “The Korean War Prisoners Who Chose Neutral Nations” received wide attention. It resonates strongly with scholars interested in transnational histories, human rights, political refugees, and the Chinese and Korean diaspora. These publications have garnered frequent citations from researchers and journalists, solidifying the PI's and Co-Is' reputation as leading authorities on the topic of Korean War prisoners who chose neutral nations and India’s role in the Korean War. H-Diplo, a prominent online journal specializing in diplomatic history, organized a roundtable in 2021 to review the publication. William Stueck from the University of Georgia, Charles S. Young from Southern Arkansas University, and the PI's MPhil student Leonardo Barbosa, participated as reviewers. The PI thoroughly responded to their reviews in Output #4. CONFERENCES/WORKSHOP: COVID-era travel restrictions prevented the team from participating in conferences or workshops until 2023. The research team held their first in-person workshop in Hong Kong in May 2023 and their second workshop in Seoul in December 2023. The PI, Co-Is, and two other Japanese and Korean scholars presented papers on their latest research findings (Output #5). In addition, the PI and Co-Is examined the transcripts of the interviews they conducted with surviving Chinese and Korean POWs in Argentina and Brazil in 2016–2017. They made plans to publish a book in Korean in 2025 (Output #7) that includes the oral history accounts and the JAEAR articles.

16602520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602520.value: Due to COVID-caused disruptions, conferences were not held between 2020 to early 2023. In May 2024, the PI will present Output #5, "Jawaharlal Nehru and India's Role in Resolving the POW Controversy in the Korean War," in a conference in Beijing funded by the US National Endowment for the Humanities. The article will be published in 2025 in an edited volume on India-China relations during the Cold War, probably by Columbia University Press. Output #6 "韓戰戰俘程立人的環球移動：從中國西南到韓國、印度，再到阿根廷" will be published in an edited volume in Taiwan in 2025. The PI and Co-Is plan to publish a book in Korean in 2025 (Output #7) that includes the POWs’ oral history accounts and the four research articles published in the JAEAR special issue. This book will serve as a comprehensive and authoritative resource, shedding light on the experiences of these POWs and the broader context of the Korean War. In the longer term, the PI plans to co-author a monograph in English that weaves together the global journeys of these prisoners.

16602520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602520.value: The project aimed to study the experiences of the 88 Korean War prisoners who chose neutral nations, expand our understanding of the war, and explore the concept of neutrality. Despite COVID-caused setbacks, the project team adapted to the circumstances and made progress in their research. They successfully traced the journeys of the prisoners through extensive archival research and analyzed documents from various countries. The project delved into the concept of neutrality, examining how it was perceived by the prisoners and the governments of India, Argentina, and Brazil. By incorporating the voices of Chinese and Korean prisoners and adopting a transnational approach, the project expanded our understanding of the Korean War and its human dimensions. The team achieved its objective of publishing a special issue of The Journal of American-East Asian Relations (JAEAR), which received significant recognition and citations from scholars. They also plan to publish a book in Korean that includes the oral history accounts and the research articles from the JAEAR special issue. Output #5 entitled "Jawaharlal Nehru and India's Role in Resolving the POW Controversy in the Korean War" is expected to be published in an edited volume by a top university press in 2025.

16603120.label: Project Objectives

To understand the effect of the government’s crackdown on social organizations before the famine. 16603120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16603120.value: The Great Famine in China that occurred between 1959 and 1961 reportedly claimed the lives of 16 to 36 million people, most of whom were peasants. Severe famines are suggested as being unlikely in functional democracies because the democratic government can neither hide information about the famine nor afford to ignore it. In authoritarian regimes severe famines might still be avoided if the victims are able to signal the shortage of food by staging protests or if they can migrate to other places to secure food. However, neither large-scale collective action nor large-scale migration occurred during China’s Great Famine. This proposed study aims to explore why the vast number of Chinese peasants who faced starvation failed to stage collective actions to avoid the tragedy. The study will focus on the mobilization infrastructure in rural China at that time. In traditional Chinese society, social organizations such as civil organizations, religious groups, and secret societies served as important channels for mobilizing collective action. Such organizations still played an important role in mobilizing “riots” after the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) came to power. For this reason, the CCP launched campaigns to suppress such organizations. Despite the crackdown, some social organizations were able to survive, and some of the collective actions by Chinese peasants during the famine were orchestrated by those surviving social organizations. This proposed study will examine why some organizations survived longer than others. And why were they still able to orchestrate peasant resistance? Answers to these question promise to shed light on why so many of the peasants remained silent and why the famine lasted for three years. This study will contribute to understanding social control in a Leninist polity by defining the effects of weakened mobilization infrastructure. 本計劃旨在研究中國1959-1960年大饑荒期間中國農民的反應。在信息不暢通的社會，民眾的抗議有信號作用。換言之，如果決策者了解到民眾的抗議及其抗議的原因，就有可能調整政策，避免不當的政策後果。然而，在中國大饑荒期間，盡管眾多的農民面臨饑荒，但他們卻很少進行大規模抗議。本研究試圖解釋為什麽農民沒有進行抗議從而避免悲劇。本研究的重點是考察中國農村的動員結構在饑荒期間的運作。在傳統的中國社會，社會組織是重要的集體行動動員機制。這些組織包括民間組織，宗教組織，宗族組織等等。這些組織和國民政府的剩餘勢力在社會主義中國建國初期依然是集體行動動員的重要機制。為此，中國政府對它們進行了大規模的清除。然而，政府的清洗並沒有讓所有的社會組織消失，有一些社會組織依然存在並成為農民集體行動的動員機制。本研究將探討為什麽有些組織能繼續存在並起到動員作用而其他組織卻消失。這壹問題的答案能夠幫我們理解為什麽眾多的農民在饑荒中選擇沈默，使得饑荒能夠持續長達三年。本研究有助於理解列寧式制度是如何通過削弱社會動員機制來管理社會的。
