16604120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16604120.value: It is well known that returns on assets demonstrate strong comovement, and that such systematic comovement can be captured well by a few common factors. However, researchers have found that distinct sets of factors can explain asset returns equally well. In this proposed research, we want to form a robust test of the factor asset pricing models that is robust to model misspecification. The misspecification could be due to omitted factors in the asset pricing model. It could also be due to the presence of spurious factors in the model setup. The spurious factors could have significant factor loadings in the conventional test due to potential omitted-variable problem. 資本市場的一個普遍現象是資產回報呈現強聯動性，這種系統性的聯動通常能夠被幾個共同因子較好地刻畫。然而研究表明存在不同組別的因子對於資產回報有幾乎相同的解釋能力。此項目希望通過穩健性的檢驗方法來研究含模型誤差設計的資產定價模型。誤差設計可能有不同的起因，比如建模時使用了偽因子或者遺漏了一些重要的因子。在傳統的檢驗中，缺失變量的存在會導致偽因子也有統計顯著的回歸系數。

17100220.value: 調查顯示，在香港一半以上的5歲兒童都有蛀牙，而90%以上已蛀的乳牙都沒有進行治療。沒治療的蛀牙會導致疼痛和感染，甚至對兒童營養，生長，發育，健康，及生活質量都有深遠的負面影響。儘管香港的學齡前兒童的蛀牙很普遍而且嚴重，現時還沒有有組織的牙科保健計劃提供給學齡前兒童。 從2008年開始，香港大學牙醫學院已經進行一項幼兒園牙科保健的外展服務。這服務的一項主要成就是多年來參與兒童的蛀牙患病率顯著下降。評估這項服務是否對兒童上小學後的蛀牙經歷，治療需要以及生活質量有長期效用是非常重要的，因爲這將對制定學齡前兒童的口腔保健政策產生影響。 這項研究基金申請提議對曾經參加過幼兒園牙科保健外展服務，現在就讀小學並參加政府衛生署提供的牙科保健項目（SDCS）的兒童（及其父母）進行回顧性研究。對照組則是已加入SDCS但未參加過幼兒園牙科保健服務的小學生。我們會聯繫參與牙科保健外展服務的幼兒園有接連的小學，邀請小學3年級的兒童及他們的父母參加這項研究。在收集數據之前，會給家長簽署參加研究的同意書。 我們會從衛生署的電子記錄中檢索出參與研究兒童的的蛀牙經歷和治療情況，並使用問卷調查方式評估他們口腔健康相關的生活質量參數。對比兩組的結果，並根據節省的牙科治療費用來衡量外展牙科服務的成本效益。 在香港，這是第一個評估幼兒園牙科保健外展服務項目的影響和經濟效益的研究。本研究預計接受過幼兒園牙科保健外展服務的兒童的患蛀牙的情況將減少，需要治療的情況更少，及有更好的口腔健康的生活質量。本研究可以為政府在制定為學齡前兒童口腔保健政策方面提供重要依據。

17100220.label: Realisation of objectives
17100220.value: 1. Study design To achieve the three proposed objectives, an observational retrospective study was designed and performed. The data of this study were mainly collected from two sources: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of children and their parents and real-world electronic oral health clinical records by the School Dental Care Service (SDCS). 2. Study population and data collection The study sample consisted of Grade 3 and 4 (P3 and P4) primary school students who enrolled in the SDCS. These children were selected because the three- and four-year intervals following primary school entry provided an adequate timeframe for evaluating the long-term impact of the outreach service. In addition, P3 and P4 students typically retain most of their primary canines and molars, as these teeth have not yet undergone exfoliation. However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic and class suspensions, the protocol was modified, and participants were mainly recruited from four school dental clinics in Hong Kong (Tuen Mun, Fanling, 1/F Argyle Street, and 3/F Argyle Street) between July and November 2022. These school dental clinics were selected because it was expected that these clinics would cover more children who have attended kindergartens that received the kindergarten dental outreach service provided by the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Hong Kong (hereafter 'the outreach service'). After the recruitment of children and obtaining informed consent from their parents, a questionnaire survey consisting of a parent questionnaire and a child questionnaire was conducted to collect children's personal identification information, sociodemographic background, oral hygiene practices of children, and oral health-related quality of life (OHQoL). To acquire children's caries and treatment records, children's name, date of birth, and ID No./SDCS No. were securely transmitted to the Department of Health in an encrypted format. For mismatched cases, every effort was made to verify these values with their parents. Final data were obtained following three rounds of data validation and data transmission. The retrieved data contains examination and treatment records. In examination records, children's caries status records at all consultations after their enrollment of SDCS were listed, along with consultation date and children's primary school grade. The caries status was documented as the number of untreated decayed teeth (dt, DT), the number of missing teeth due to caries (mt, MT), and filled teeth (ft, FT) for both primary and permanent teeth. In the treatment records, all treatments administered by SDCS since the enrollment of children, along with their corresponding treatment dates, were provided. Additionally, for certain types of treatments, information regarding tooth numbers and surfaces was also provided. The OHQoL was measured by two short forms of the Child Perceptions Questionnaire (CPQ-ISF:8 and CPQ-RSF:8), which were included in the child questionnaire. 3. Definition of exposure Children were classified into the exposure group if they reported attending kindergartens that had received the outreach service from 2015 to 2019; otherwise, they were classified into the non-exposure group. 4. Definition of outcome measures Caries experience in primary teeth was measured by mean and prevalence of dmft and its components (dt, mt, and ft) from P1 to P3. Treatment performed was measured using the mean number of treatment items provided to each child. The treatment items were also classified into 'prevention' and 'caries-related treatment' categories to evaluate the outreach service's impact on specific kinds of treatments. 5. Statistical methods The observational study design of this study posed challenges for establishing causal relationships between exposure and outcomes. To address potential confounding between the outreach service and study outcomes, statistical methods based on the potential outcome causal framework were applied to mitigate the influence of confounding. The stabilized inverse probability weighting (SIPW) method was applied to adjust for confounding. SIPW offers better confounding control by creating a pseudo-population where exposure is independent of measured confounders, allowing for more robust causal inference compared to traditional regression which may be limited by model misspecification and residual confounding. To address missing caries-related outcomes, stabilized inverse probability of censoring weight was applied to help mitigate potential selection bias caused by loss-to-follow up under the missing at random assumption.

17100220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100220.value: Of 1,095 parent questionnaires that were collected, a total of 964 children's examination and treatment records were matched and retrieved. Among these children, 180 (18.7%) and 784 (81.3%) were classified as the exposure and non-exposure groups, respectively. From P1 to P3, the mean dmft (SD) of these children were 2.5 (3.1), 2.4 (2.8). and 2.0 (2.4), respectively. The prevalence of caries experience was 54.6%, 60.7%, and 57.6%, respectively. Children who were exposed to the outreach service were significantly associated with an approximate 10% lower prevalence of dt in P3 and a decrease of 0.4 dt in P2, compared with those unexposed. Overall, study children received a mean (SD) of 6.6 (5.7) total treatment items from P1 to P3. Specifically, they received a mean (SD) of 2.7 (3.3), 2.0 (3.0), and 1.9 (2.2) overall treatment items in P1, P2, and P3, respectively. However, no significant association was found between the outreach service and treatments administered by the SDCS. A total of 883 children with complete parent and child questionnaires were included in the analysis of OHQoL. Of these, 716 (80.0%) were classified as the non-exposure group and 177 (20.0%) as the exposure group. The median (Q1, Q3) total scores of CPQ11-14-ISF:8 and CPQ11-14-RSF:8 in the study sample were 3.0 (2.0, 5.0) and 2.0 (1.0, 4.0), respectively. These relatively low scores (possible range: 0 to 32) indicated favorable OHQoL among study children. Although the outreach service was not associated with lower total CPQ scores, children exposed to the outreach service demonstrated better OHQoL in the oral symptoms domain and mouth sores item, which were of the primary factors compromising overall CPQ score. The associations were notably stronger among children whose caries were likely arrested through SDF therapy.

17100220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100220.value: Besides addressing the proposed research questions, the collected data offers an opportunity to explore the association between caries in primary and permanent teeth among primary school students. Among 825 children (mean age in Grade 1: 5.7 [0.5]; boys 54.8%) without caries in permanent teeth in Grade 1, the prevalence of caries in permanent teeth increased to 5.7% in Grade 2 and 10.5% in Grade 3. Among those with caries in primary teeth (n=443), 15.4% had caries experience in permanent teeth in Grade 3, compared to 4.9% among those without (n=382, adjusted risk ratio 2.8 [95% CI:1.7 to 4.8; P<0.001]). Sex and being an only child were identified as significant effect modifiers, with the association stronger in boys and children with siblings. The presence of caries in primary teeth increases the risk of developing caries in permanent teeth among primary school students. Oral health promotion programs targeting susceptible subpopulations can be explored to maximize benefits. Future research grant applications will be submitted to evaluate the effectiveness of these programs on susceptible subpopulations. Experience gained in this research can be applied to evaluate the long-term effects of our research team members' territory-wide Jockey Club Children Oral Health Project (https://www.jccohp.hku.hk/).

17100220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100220.value: This study shows that the kindergarten dental outreach service provided by the Faculty of Dentistry at the University of Hong Kong is effective in reducing dental cavities in young children and improving their oral health quality of life as they grow. It is a cost-effective program that can be easily implemented to improve dental health for kindergarten children, providing long-lasting benefits. This study provides a valuable example of using real-world dental check-up and treatment records to assess the long-term effects of a specific dental service. Prospective studies on dental cavities usually require experienced dentists to conduct multiple check-ups, which can be difficult and expensive. However, using real-world data from regular dental practices, along with modern statistical analysis methods, allows researchers to evaluate potential exposures and their long-term effects more efficiently. This approach reduces study costs and makes better use of existing clinical data, which is especially important given the current shortage of pediatric dentists.

17100520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100520.value: DNA損傷反應(DDR)是保護基因組完整性的重要機制。基因突變能擾亂DDR並損害基因組穩定性，從而引發不同疾病包括發育缺陷和癌症等。 為了解細胞對DNA損傷的反應，我們最近成功發現一種新型的DNA修復因子-DYRK1A激酶，而且透過初步解構DYRK1A蛋白質複合物的組成部分ARIP 4也使我們發現了解旋酶在DSB上的作用。 我們將研究ARIP4累積在DNA損傷上的因素，以及DYRK1A-ARIP4軸如何協調受損染色質的DNA轉錄。最後，我們將表徵ARIP4解旋酶的活性，以及其在DNA損傷上的作用。 上述的研究方向除了加強我們對DDR的認知外，透過了解DYRK1A-ARIP4複合物的作用更有望發展個人化治療方案。

17100520.label: Realisation of objectives
17100520.value: The study aimed to study the DYRK1A-ARIP4 complex in DNA double-strand break (DSB) responses and its role on genome integrity protection. To this end we have delineated the DYRK1A-ARIP4 interaction, and have carried out a series of experimentations to thoroughly dissect how ARIP4 supports cellular responses to DSBs. Intriguingly, we found that ARIP4 is pivotal in driving DSB formation following hormone-induced transcription, and is important in fueling androgen-stimulated AR gene expression. These findings were recently published in Science Advances (see below). Ng RR, Lin Z, Zhang Y, Ti SC, Javed A, Wong JW, Fang Q, Leung JW, Tang AH, Huen MS. R-loop resolution by ARIP4 helicase promotes androgen-mediated transcription induction. Sci Adv 2024; 10(29):eadm9577.

17100820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100820.value: 研究背景： 牙齒酸蝕是牙齒磨耗的主要原因之一。唾液與牙齒接觸後，唾液蛋白附著在牙齒表面形成獲得性膜。該膜具有防止牙齒酸蝕的功能。局部應用氟化氨銀於牙齒表面會影響獲得性膜的結構，並可能增强其對牙齒酸蝕的預防作用。 目的：研究氟化氨銀 i)對獲得性膜預防牙齒酸蝕作用的影響；和 ii)預防牙釉質和牙本質酸蝕的作用。 方法： 1 氟化氨銀對有/無獲得性膜覆蓋的牙齒表面酸蝕的預防作用 將氟化氨銀分別塗布於有/無獲得性膜覆蓋的牙釉質和牙本質樣本表面後，樣本在電腦控制的人工口腔中受到酸蝕衝擊。分別採用顯微硬度測試、光學輪廓科技和X射線衍射法對樣品表面硬度、損失和沉澱物特性進行分析。 2 氟化氨銀對牙齒酸蝕的預防作用 在原位試驗中，將氟化氨銀處理過的牙釉質和牙本質樣本嵌入實驗對象佩戴的牙科器具中。牙釉質和牙本質樣本表面分別塗布氟化鈉、氟化氨銀和氯化亞錫的漱口液作為陽性對照，塗布水作為陰性對照。標本將受到口外的酸蝕衝擊。分別採用顯微硬度測試、光學輪廓科技、X射線衍射法和分光光度法對樣品表面硬度、損失、沉澱物特性和顏色參數進行評估。 3 氟化氨銀對獲得性膜的改性 在原位模型中，使用橫向電子顯微鏡分析氟化氨銀對獲得行膜形態的改變。並使用液相色譜-質譜法對其蛋白質組學進行分析。 預期結果：氟化氨銀增强獲得性膜防止牙齒酸蝕的作用，和體內外實驗證實氟化氨銀有效預防牙齒酸蝕。 結論與臨床意義： 該項目證實氟化氨銀有效預防牙齒酸蝕。這將有助於建立一個使用氟化氨銀管理牙齒酸蝕的臨床方案。使用氟化氨銀無痛，簡單且價格合理，可廣泛推薦其用於臨床中牙齒酸蝕的管理。

17100920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100920.value: Cancers arise through the malignant transformation of somatic cells in the body. The study of how a cell becomes malignant is a major objective in cancer research as it allows us to better understand the behaviour of specific cancer samples. One of the major determinants of a cancer cell’s phenotype is its cell of origin. The cellular origin of cancers has been shown to be important in dictating the cancer’s aggressiveness, response to therapy and patient outcomes. In chemical-induced mouse models of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), it has been shown that these cancers likely arise from mature hepatocytes. Even so, a limitation of these mouse model is that it may not be representative of all subtypes of HCC. Importantly, whether these models recapitulate the clinical scenario in human HCC remains unclear. In recent years, our research group along with others have established that chromatin structure has a major influence on the density and distribution of somatic mutations across cancer genomes. As somatic mutations are generally acquired by a cell prior to its malignant transformation, it was shown that the distribution of somatic mutations from a given cancer is sufficient to infer its cell type of origin. We have further extended this idea to examine cancer cell of origin at the single cell level. Using whole genome sequenced HCC and single cell transcriptomic data from normal human liver, we found that human HCC mutational landscape may be derived from dedifferentiated mature hepatocytes. In this application, we propose to refine our understanding of the cell of origin of HCC. We will apply established mouse models of HCC to validate and improve our methodology for cell of origin inference from cancer somatic mutations. We will optimise and identify features that underlie associations between mutational landscape, chromatin profiles and the transcriptome. Finally, we will apply our improved methodology to examine the cell of origin in over 400 whole genome sequenced liver cancer samples and identify molecular and clinical features associated with the inferred cancer cell type of origin at the single cell level. This research is expected to further our understanding of the origin of HCC. It has the potential uncover clinically relevant cell of origin-based subtypes that can be validated in future studies. Furthermore, the methods developed in this project should be broadly applicable and can be applied to study the cellular origin of other cancer types in the future. 腫瘤起源於人體內體細胞的惡性轉變。研究細胞的惡性轉變在腫瘤研究中意義重大，因為其能加深我們對特定腫瘤演化的理解。腫瘤細胞表型主要取決於腫瘤細胞的起源。腫瘤細胞起源在腫瘤發生髮展，藥物治療反應和腫瘤預後方面起著重要的作用。肝癌小鼠模型的研究表明肝癌很可能起源於成熟的肝細胞，然而小鼠模型的不足之處在於其並不能代表所有肝癌的亞型，同時，是否存在更容易發生惡性轉變的肝細胞亞群也有待研究。幾年來，我們研究團隊及別的研究者已闡明染色質結構對體細胞突變在整個基因組上的分佈有著深遠的影響。基於體細胞突變在細胞惡性轉變之前已發生的事實，有研究表明特定腫瘤的體細胞突變的分佈特徵能夠很好的推斷細胞的類型。因此，我們進一步將此方法擴展至單細胞水平的研究。通過關聯肝癌的全基因組測序數據及正常肝組織的單細胞轉錄組測序數據，我們發現去分化成熟的肝細胞是肝癌突變的主要來源。因此，此課題的研究將加深我們對肝癌細胞起源的理解。我們將通過已建立的肝癌小鼠模型對基於體細胞突變推斷細胞起源的方法進行驗證和完善，優化並鑑定能準確反映腫瘤突變，染色質及轉錄組圖譜之間內在關聯的基因組特徵。最後，我們將在超過400例肝癌全基因組樣本中驗證我們的方法，在單細胞水平上鑑定出肝癌細胞來源，並探索其於臨床及分子特徵之間的關係。因此，此項研究將有助於對肝癌細胞起源的理解。同時，其有助於揭示與臨床緊密關聯的基於肝癌細胞起源的肝癌亞型。最後，該項研究中的方法能廣泛的運用於其他腫瘤類型的細胞起源的研究中。

17100920.label: Realisation of objectives
17100920.value: In the proposed project, all proposed objectives were successfully achieved. Specific details for each objective are provided below. Objective 1: Validation of computational method using established chemically induced HCC mouse models A key aspect of our project is to demonstrate that the cell type of origin can be predicted by the correlation between somatic mutation landscape of a tumour and the epigenetic profile for its cell type of origin. Objective 1 is focused on generating a mouse HCC model for the validation of our algorithm. This involved two key tasks: lineage tracing to confirm hepatocyte origins of HCC and generation, plus analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and whole genome sequencing (WGS) data from these models. Achievement of Objective 1a: Lineage Tracing Lineage tracing was conducted using AAV‐TBG‐Cre;RosatdTomato mice treated with DEN and CCl4 to label hepatocytes specifically. This allowed for tracking the cellular origin of tumors, at least those that can activate the TBG promoter, which is hepatocyte-specific. Lineage tracing confirmed that the majority of HCC tumours expressed the hepatocyte-specific tdTomato reporter, as demonstrated by fluorescence imaging, which is consistent with prior studies. We found that the order of DEN+CCl4 treatment did not affect the tdTomato positivity of HCC, but CCl4+DEN treatment did not generate tumours as frequently and with later onset. Establishment of these models allowed us to proceed to the generation of single-cell transcriptomic and WGS data. Achievement of Objective 1b: Generation and Analysis of scRNA-seq and WGS Data High-quality scRNA-seq was generated from the liver harvested from control AAV‐TBG‐Cre;RosatdTomato treated mice before and after DEN or CCl4 treatment (in triplicates). The scRNA-seq data allowed us to further refine the identity of tdTomato-expressing cells but was equally abundant in progenitor markers from mature hepatocytes. Equip with single cell profiles, we performed WGS on HCC in DEN+CCl4 or CCl4+DEN mice. DEN+CCl4 mice had a median mutational burden of 15.8 mutations/Mb, consistent with previous studies and were higher than CCl4+DEN mice with a median mutation burden of just 3.7 mutations/Mb. Mutational landscapes of the tumours, revealing DNA damage signatures characteristic of chemical carcinogenesis with a predominance of T>A and T>C mutations. Correlation of mutational profiles with scRNA-seq derived mutational landscape confirmed hepatocytes as the cell type of origin with the highest similarly confirming the observation from lineage tracing. In summary, Objective 1 was successfully realised by confirming hepatocyte origins of HCC through lineage tracing and generating integrated scRNA-seq and WGS datasets from chemically induced mouse models. Objective 2: Optimise computational approach to maximise correlation between mutation landscape and scRNA-seq data Objective 2 aimed to refine the computational methodology to enhance the correlation between the mutation landscape derived from WGS and transcriptional profiles from scRNA-seq data. Achievement of Objective 2a: Implementation of Improvement Methods The baseline method for comparing mutational profiles with the epigenetic landscape is based on uniform binning of the genome into 1 Mb windows. We sought to improve this using a range of statistical and computational methods. First, we introduced a dynamic window sizing strategy that adapts bin lengths based on local genomic features such as mutation density and chromatin signal variability, allowing for more precise regional comparisons. Second, we redefined the similarity metrics by incorporating advanced statistical measures beyond simple correlation, to better capture complex relationships between mutation patterns and epigenetic landscapes. Third, we enhanced the model’s robustness by explicitly accounting for epigenetic-independent factors that influence mutation distribution, such as replication timing and nucleotide composition, through covariate adjustment and normalisation procedures. Achievement of Objective 2b: Evaluation of Methods The implemented methods were rigorously evaluated by comparing mutation calls from scRNA-seq with those from WGS across both our data from Objective 1 as well as publicly available scRNA-seq data from the human cell atlas and WGS data from PCAWG. Ultimately, we found that optimal parameters can vary depending on the tumour type and mutational burden. Nevertheless, we have developed a robust framework for statistical evaluation and normalisation of mutations to maximise similarity detection. As our study was focused on HCC, we have defined an optimal method for processing HCC tumours and using this to match scRNA-seq data from healthy liver tissue. We have evaluated this in human HCC samples through cross-validation, achieving over 90% accuracy in identifying hepatocytes as the cell type of origin. The samples that did not match HCC generally had low mutational burden or other DNA repair mutations that altered the mutational landscape. Overall, Objective 2 was achieved by successfully implementing and validating computational improvements that maximised the correlation between mutation landscapes and scRNA-seq data. Furthermore, through the method development, two studies were published [1, 2] directly as a result of our efforts in method development that allowed us to identify new relationships between mutational landscape and epigenetic profiles based on background somatic mutations in DNA repair genes. Objective 3: Analysis and applications of cell type of origin in human HCC The third objective extended the computational framework to human HCC, focusing on inferring tumour cell origins and exploring associations with molecular and clinical features. Achievement of Objective 3a: Inferring Origins of Human HCC Using scRNA-seq data from normal and cirrhotic human liver tissues as references, the computational method was applied to human HCC samples to infer their cellular origins. By comparing tumour single-cell transcriptomes with annotated normal liver cell types, the analysis identified hepatocytes as the predominant cell of origin in human HCC in ~90% of samples, as mentioned in Objective 2, and is consistent with findings from mouse models. We further examined and sought to detect subpopulations of single cells that were more strongly correlated with the HCC mutational data. There is evidence that progenitor-like transcriptional signatures from DLK1-expressing cells are enriched. Achievement of Objective 3b: Identifying Associations with Molecular and Clinical Features After adjusting for tumour burden, mutational signature, and driver mutations, we performed a cluster analysis to determine whether the inferred cell-type of origin was associated with molecular characteristics, such as mutation profiles, gene expression signatures, and clinical parameters, including tumour stage and patient outcomes. The study identified potential links between specific cell-of-origin patterns poorer prognosis, however the significance was diminished when accounting for the tumour stage. We also found cell-of-origin clusters were enriched in inflammatory signalling gene expression pathways, which may imply that cell-type-of-origin expression signatures may also be carried through to some tumours. In conclusion, all objectives of the project have been carried out and successfully completed. The project has yielded two publications [1,2], both of which are direct results of the methods developed in Objective 2. We will sought to publish one further paper to report the findings from our mouse model and in human HCC. 1. Fang H, Zhu X, Yang H, Oh J, Barbour JA, Wong JWH. 17100920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100920.value: The major findings and research outcomes from this project provide significant advances in understanding the cell of origin of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and improving computational approaches to study cancer mutational landscapes. First, our chemically induced mouse models of HCC—using DEN and CCl4 treatments in AAV‐TBG‐Cre;RosatdTomato mice—confirmed that hepatocytes are the predominant cell type of origin for HCC in these models. This conclusion was supported by lineage tracing experiments showing tumour cells derived from hepatocytes, consistent with prior literature indicating mature hepatocytes give rise to toxin-induced liver tumours. Importantly, whole genome sequencing (WGS) of mouse tumours revealed mutational landscapes that, when integrated with the transcriptomic profiles from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), recapitulated these lineage findings. This validated the capability of our computational algorithm to accurately identify the cell type of origin by correlating mutational signatures with transcriptional states. Second, we developed and optimised novel computational algorithms that correlate the mutational landscape of tumours with the epigenetic and transcriptional status of their putative cells of origin. In particular, our methods to associate changes in mutational distribution based on epigenetic features have been published in Science Advances and Cell Genomics. They have been successfully applied beyond HCC to other cancer contexts, demonstrating their broad utility. Third, applying these approaches to human HCC samples revealed that hepatocytes are also likely the primary cell type of origin in patients. At single-cell resolution, we identified a subset of hepatocytes expressing higher levels of DLK1, a known progenitor cell marker linked to cancer stem-like properties and aggressive tumour behaviour. These DLK1-high hepatocytes showed the strongest correlation with the mutational landscape of human HCC, suggesting that hepatocytes with progenitor-like features may be particularly prone to malignant transformation. In summary, our major findings confirm that hepatocytes, especially those exhibiting progenitor-like transcriptional profiles, serve as the cell of origin for HCC. We have also established advanced computational methods that enhance the study of cancer mutational landscapes by linking them to the epigenetic state of the originating cell type. These methods further enable the identification of potential DNA repair deficiencies, offering insights into tumour biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Collectively, these outcomes represent a substantial contribution to the molecular understanding of HCC and provide powerful tools for cancer research.

17100920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100920.value: The potential for further development of this research includes expanding sample size, increasing sequencing depth, and leveraging large language models (LLMs) to enhance mutation data analysis. Obtaining a larger cohort of both mouse and human HCC samples will improve the statistical power and generalisability of our computational models, allowing more robust inference of cell-of-origin patterns across diverse genetic backgrounds and clinical contexts. Increasing sequencing depth, particularly for whole genome and single-cell RNA sequencing, will enhance sensitivity and specificity in detecting low-frequency and subclonal mutations. Deeper coverage reduces noise and improves the resolution of mutational landscapes, which is critical for accurate mutation-expression correlation and subclone reconstruction. Deeper scRNA-seq profiling will also enable more accurate detection of rare cell types, which may have the potential to be the cell-type of origin for HCC. Finally, with the recent emergence of LLMs, we are also exploring the use of LLMs to learn complex dependencies between somatic mutations and the epigenetic landscape that might not be immediately obvious based on current knowledge-driven analyses. LLMs have the ability to capture sequence context and long-range interactions between genomic regions, and we believe that this is a promising novel approach to defining epigenetic-somatic mutation relationships.

17100920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100920.value: This research project explored the origins of liver cancer (specifically hepatocellular carcinoma, or HCC) and developed new computer tools to study the genetic changes that cause it. We wanted to know which type of liver cell is most likely to turn cancerous. Using laboratory mice, we confirmed that most liver cancers start in regular liver cells called hepatocytes, especially when those cells have some characteristics of younger, more primitive liver cells. These findings were also confirmed in human liver cancer. We also built advanced computer programs that connect the genetic mutations found in tumours with the specific features of the cells where the cancer began. These computational tools have the potential to help scientists better understand how and why certain cells become cancerous. By better understanding the source of cells from which cancers develop\, we can work towards earlier detection, more effective treatments that target the right cells, and personalised medicine tailored to each patient's unique cancer.

17101020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101020.value: Obesity has rapidly become a global concern as the number of individuals with a body mass index exceeding 30 continues to rise. Commensurately the number of surgical procedures performed in this population continues to grow at a rapid pace. Sevoflurane is a widely used inhalational anesthetic agent and its interaction with central nervous system is still being elucidated. Previous studies suggested that animals with diabetes and/or metabolic syndrome - in which obesity is a hallmark trail, have higher risk of developing cognitive dysfunction under general anesthetics like sevoflurane. This implies brains from these animals have a greater sensitivity to the adverse effect of sevoflurane and surgery but mechanisms accounting for the potential sensitivity observed in these studies are yet to be determined. Adiponectin is an adipocyte derived molecule that regulates important anti-inflammatory and neurotrophic actions. It is associated with a neuroprotective effect on the central nervous system. Moreover, hypoadiponectinaemia is measured in different models of cognitive dysfunction, including aged and metabolic frailty models. Obese patients have decreased levels of adiponectin leading to an increased vulnerability to cognitive dysfunction. Therefore, we speculated that adiponectin dysregulation may contribute to the increased susceptibility of brains from obese subjects to sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction. Our preliminary data demonstrated significant cognitive dysfunction, neuroinflammation and adiponectin reduction in high fat diet induced obese mice after sevoflurane exposure. Pretreatment with adiponectin reduced the differences in performance between the groups. Our current proposal aims to examine, in detail, the molecular mechanism of sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in obese compared with lean mice. In particular, we will assess whether adiponectin is critical in this process and examine its downstream pro-inflammatory JNK signaling pathways, which may lead to consequent neuronal dysfunction and neuropathologies. The prevalence of obesity has doubled in since 1980, the global burden of surgery was estimated at 234.2 million major procedures per year in 2008. Sevoflurane is likely to capture 70% market share of the inhalational agent market by 2022, as such the number of obese patients with the potential to develop postoperative cognitive impairment escalates. Therefore, our proposal to identify a molecular target for clinical evaluation thus mitigating the detrimental effects of general anesthesia for this sizable patient group is of utmost importance. 隨著身體質量指數(BMI)超過30的人數日漸增長，肥胖已發展成為全球關注的重要問題之一。同時，肥胖人群的手術需求量也極速增長。2022年，作為目前廣泛運用的吸入麻醉藥，七氟醚的預期市場份額將佔據吸入麻醉藥市場的70%。然而其與中樞神經系統的相互作用尚未明確。前期研究發現，七氟醚會增加在糖尿病或肥胖的動物模型患上認知功能障礙的風險，但該作用機制尚未明確，有待進一步研究。 脂聯素是由脂肪細胞分泌的蛋白質，具有抗炎及神經營養作用，與中樞神經系統的神經保護作用相關。此外，老年與代謝綜合症等不同的認知功能障礙模型中常伴有低脂聯素血症。肥胖患者的低脂聯素水平降低導致其更易罹患認知功能障礙。因此，我們推測脂聯素失衡是導致肥胖動物或患者對七氟醚誘導的認知功能障礙的原因。 我們的前期研究表明，高脂飲食誘導的肥胖小鼠在七氟醚麻醉後出現了明顯的認知功能障礙，神經炎症以及脂聯素水平降低。在七氟醚麻醉前予以脂聯素干預能夠緩解其在肥胖小鼠誘導的認知功能障礙表現。本研究計劃的目的為充分研究在肥胖與正常小鼠中七氟醚誘導的認知功能障礙機制的差異，尤其是探究脂聯素是否在這一過程中發揮重要作用，以及脂聯素是否通過下游JNK信號通路進一步導致神經功能障礙以及神經病變。

17101020.label: Realisation of objectives
17101020.value: For the three objectives, we have successfully accomplished them near entirety as indicated by our published reports and yet to be published findings (manuscript is under review and attached in part C). For objective 1, our study confirmed that high fat diet induced obese mice are more vulnerable to the neurotoxicity of sevoflurane while lean mice are more resilient. In the obese mice, cognitive dysfunction, synaptic loss and apoptotic pathway activation are observed after sevoflurane exposure. Significant increase in tau pathologies and neuroinflammation were also found in the hippocampus of obese mice. In contrast, no significant modulation of these phenomena was observed in lean mice. Part of the results in lean mice were included in our previous publication and the grant was acknowledged (Huang et al, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2022; Chen et al, Journal of Neuroinflammation, 2023; Chen et al, Journal of Neuroimmune Pharmacology, 2024). For objective 2, a similar strategy of sevoflurane exposure was carried out in adiponectin knockout lean mice and we demonstrated that sevoflurane induced neurotoxicity and triggered cognitive dysfunction in a similar fashion to obese mice. Given both obese and adiponectin knockout lean mice are deficient in adiponectin, our results supports the hypothesis that adiponectin deficiency is the potential mechanism underlying the sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in obese animals. In the final objective, we demonstrated the neuroprotective effects of pretreating animals with adiponectin receptor agonist adipoRon against sevoflurane induced neurotoxicity in both obese and knockout mice. AdipoRon is a synthetic analog that mimics the actions of adiponectin. AdipoRon was orally fed to the animals before and after sevoflurane exposure. It was shown that adipoRon could alleviate sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction and mitigated the neuroinflammatory response in both obese and knockout mice post anesthesia. Taken together, our results indicated the detrimental effects of sevoflurane in animals with obese background and adiponectin deficiency is the predisposing factor contributed to the vulnerability of the obese animals towards the neurotoxicity of sevoflurane. By reactivating the adiponectin receptor signaling, it can minimize the neurotoxicity of sevoflurane in obese subjects.

17101020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101020.value: For objective 1, we first successfully established the high fat diet induced obese animal model. In obese animals, sevoflurane induces cognitive decline, including the memory function (from novel object recognition test and puzzle box test) and problem solving ability (from puzzle box test). It was associated with the significant increase of dendritic spine loss (Golgi staining) and apoptotic signaling (TUNEL assay and Bax/Bcl2 ratio) in the hippocampus. By confocal microscopy, we found that sevoflurane induced a notable increase of IBA1 (microglial activation) and GFAP (GFAP activation) immunofluorescence activities, indicating the neuroinflammatory response in the obese mice. In addition, , increase of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and MCP-1 were observed. Western blot results indicated that sevoflurane inhibited the phosphorylation of AMPK and up-regulated phosphorylated JNK/c-jun expressions. Furthermore, significant increase of phosphorylated tau expressions were observed. For adiponectin level, reduction of mRNA expression of adiponectin was found in the visceral adipose tissue and muscle of obese mice after sevoflurane exposure. These data suggesting that sevoflurane triggered neuroinflammatory response and aggravated tau pathologies in the obese animals. Meanwhile, no significant adverse impact of sevoflurane was observed in lean mice. For objective 2, we elucidated the impact of sevoflurane in the transgenic mice of adiponectin knockout (APN-KO). We first confirm that no significant alteration of body weight was found in APN-KO mice compared with the wild type C57 mice at the same age of 3-month and 4-month-old, indicating that no significant obesity was developed. After sevoflurane exposure, cognitive impairment was observed in APN-KO mice which is similar to obese mice. Moreover, increase in dendritic loss, glial activation, JNK/c-jun activation, IL-1beta, tau phosphorylation and apoptosis were found in the hippocampus of APN-KO mice. These data confirm adiponectin deficiency is a crucial event in sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in obese mice. For objective 3, our study demonstrated the neuroprotective effect of an adiponectin receptor agonist, AdipoRon which mimic the biological activities of adiponectin, in both obese and APN-KO mice. In novel object recognition test, oral administration of AdipoRon could alleviate sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in both. Furthermore, we found that AdipoRon administration ameliorated sevoflurane induced microglial activation, dendritic spine loss, apoptotic signaling and tau phosphorylation in those mice. These data suggested the therapeutic potential of targeting adiponectin receptor against sevoflurane induced neurotoxicity and subsequent cognitive dysfunction in obese subjects.

17101020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101020.value: Adiponectin deficiency has been implicated in a number of metabolic disorders including obesity, diabetes and fatty liver disease. Results from this study suggests that the relative lack of this factor in obese animals may also contribute to post anesthetic neurotoxicity and cognitive decline. The adiponectin receptor agonist AdipoRon is actively being investigated for a its therapeutic potential but has not been investigated clinically to date. However, a phase 2b/3 clinical trial of ophthalmic solutions containing ALY688, another small peptide of adiponectin receptor agonist, has just been completed. Given the range of conditions for which it is potentially beneficial and its promising preclinical results, it is hoped that the clinical safety and efficacy of AdipoRon will be evaluated in the near future. Once that is available for clinical use, its efficacy minimizing the occurrence of post operative cognitive decline can be evaluated.

17101020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101020.value: Obesity has been linked to cognitive decline and inflammation, Obese individuals have a reduced level of a brain protective substance called adiponectin. We suspected this deficiency renders them more vulnerable to potential cerebral side effects from anesthesia. After administering sevoflurane, a commonly used anesthetic drug, to mice that are genetically engineered not to produce adiponectin and obese mice we showed these animals developed more side effects when compared with their lean counterparts who were not adiponectin deficient. They had worse cognitive performance, more inflammation of the brain, reduced number of connections between neurons and more attrition of these cells. On the other hand, by pre-treating them with a synthetic substitute (AdipoRon) that mimics the biological actions of adiponectin before anesthesia, we were able to reduce the severity of these side effects in adiponectin deficient animals. These results may explain why some obese individuals may be more prone to develop post operative cognitive decline. As AdipoRon shows promise in preclinical research for its potential therapeutic effects in various metabolic disorders such as diabetes, and fatty liver disease, its use maybe expanded to perioperative brain protection for obese patients should it become clinically available.

17101120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101120.value: We aim to uncover how SOX17 acts as a dual-purpose molecular switch that directs discordant cell fate decision in the early embryo. We seek to invent re-engineered SOX17 variants that can serve as tool to faithfully manipulate stem cells in a dish – a pre-requisite to model human diseases and to eventually treat diseases such infertility with synthetic gametes. The barrier between soma and germ line was deemed impermeable and both types of cellular lineages were thought to be characterised and regulated by unique sets of molecules. SOX17 holds the key which of the two cell types are formed. Overexpression of SOX17 in cultured pluripotent cells allows for the generation of early stages of human germ cell lineages. However, at roughly the same time and from similar starting cells, SOX17 also specifies somatic endoderm, the precursor of gut, liver and lung. How can a single gene have dual and seemingly conflicting roles to direct cellular switches in early human development? To answer this question, we will use a protein engineering method termed directed molecular evolution to modify the SOX17 gene. In mouse cells, we have previously shown that SOX17 teams up with OCT4 to regulate genes in early embryos. We could demonstrate that the rational manipulation of this partnership can profoundly change its function and were able to re-engineer SOX17 into an inducer of pluripotent stem cells. Therefore, we hypothesise that we can also re-engineer co-factor association, target gene selection and cell fate specification of SOX17 in human germ cell and endoderm specification. We will use a sensitive model for early human development in a dish and differentiate pluripotent cells towards a developmental crossroad where a precursor cell population can be coaxed to either become somatic endoderm or to form germ cells. We aim to identify mutated SOX17 variants that are modified in a way such that they are exclusive in their ability to specify these two lineages. Analysis of the effects of the mutations on gene expression and binding to target genes and their interactors will untangle the SOX17-centred molecular network that separates the germ line from somatic lineages. The discovery of engineered versions of SOX17 that uniquely specify endoderm or germ cells, respectively, will allow for the more controlled and homogenous command of cell fate decisions without unwanted by-products. This will be a critical step towards the robust generation of synthetic gametes in a dish. 本項研究旨在重塑細胞命運決定關鍵分子開關SOX17，探討為何SOX17於人類早期胚胎發育持有雙重功能，並利用成品引導幹細胞在試管內分化為目標細胞系。 生殖細胞之所以擁有「不朽」之稱，是因為生殖細胞能將其遺傳物質一代一代傳下去，從而建立代與代之間的聯繫。鑑於生殖細胞與其他體細胞的特質截然有異，人們一直視生殖細胞和別的體細胞之間的屏障為不可滲透，並認為兩種細胞譜系必定受不同獨特的分子表徵及調節。然而，最近研究指出SOX17可能是控制胚胎幹細胞最終到底成為生殖細胞或其他體細胞的決定因素。來源及發育時間點大致相同的起始細胞，在過度表達SOX17的情況下能分化為人類生殖細胞譜系的前體細胞；與此同時，SOX17亦能推動起始細胞進行體細胞內胚層規範，最終形成腸、肝、肺等器官。到底是什麼促使SOX17這個基因擔當雙重且看似矛盾的角色，指令細胞命運規範？ 本團隊欲運用蛋白質工程技術「定向分子進化」，透過修改SOX17基因，跡察驅使SOX17擔任細胞命運規範這角色的因素。本團隊近年已證明SOX17會跟OCT4合作調節小鼠早期胚胎細胞的基因。通過理性操縱兩者的合作關係，SOX17的功能會隨着改變。本團隊更發現經歷修改的SOX17能成為多能幹細胞的誘導劑。因此，本團隊冀望重新設計SOX17，改變其輔助因子關聯、靶基因選擇和細胞命運規範的特徵；並利用敏感的體外模型模擬人類早期發育，將前體多能細胞群分化為內胚層或生殖細胞。由此，本團隊盼望鑒定專屬於生殖細胞或內胚層譜系規範的SOX17基因工程變體。只要分析突變對SOX17基因表達以及SOX17與靶基因及其相互作用物關係的影響，便能梳理以SOX17為中心的分子網絡之間的纏結，從而理解SOX17如何有效隔開內胚層或生殖細胞譜系。 倘若能將SOX17不同功能解耦，成功設計專於特定譜系規範的SOX17工程變體，SOX17工程變體便能更有效控制細胞命運決定，避免產生所不希望的副產物。透過進化SOX17此蛋白質，更可促進於體外生產細胞技術發展，製造各種細胞（如合成配子）。

17101120.label: Realisation of objectives
17101120.value: Objective 1: To establish a cell fate programming system to evaluate the capacity of SOX17 mutants to promote selective specification of somatic and germ cell lineages. Recent progress made in human somatic cell differentiation and primordial germ cell specification provided instrumental tools to delve deeper into early human embryonic development. We adopted and optimized a two-dimensional induction method from the Sebastiano lab of Stanford University to generate human primordial germ cell-like cells (hPGCLCs) and definitive endoderm (DE) from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). The 2D method is substantially simpler and faster than methods-based on embryonic bodies. The latter is difficult to establish and reproduce. In our protocol, transient WNT activation for 12 hours followed by WNT inhibition and BMP activation, specifies hPGCLCs. Sustained WNT exposure for 24 hours followed by BMP inhibition induced primitive streak and followed by DE induction. We evaluated the induction efficiency of hPGCLCs and DE with primed PSCs representing a post-implantation epiblast and hPSCs representative of an earlier pre-implantation state. Our immunocytochemistry staining results show an average of roughly 20% hPGCLCs (hPGC markers: SOX17, TFAP2C, NANOS3, BLIMP1, OCT4, NANOG) in classical primed hPSCs differentiation. We also used human expanded potential stem cell (hEPSC) lines EM3 and EM4 stem cells with an expanded potential to generate extraembryonic lineages. With these cell lines, we can achieve a 40% - 60% hPGCLCs induction efficiency. However, there is no significant difference in DE induction efficiency for EPSCs and primed PSCs. More than 80% of the cells are positive for DE markers SOX17 and FOXA2. Hence, somatic cells (forming the primitive streak) and PGCLCs, while stemming from the same precursor cells, can be differentiated through a time-dependent modulation of signaling pathways. Pluripotency factors including NANOG are continuously expressed during the transition from pluripotency to posterior epiblast to PGCs, thus bridging pluripotent and germline states. Collectively, we succeeded in establishing a robust, fast, and efficient protocol to obtain PGCLC and DE from a diverse set of human stem cell lines. Objective 2: To identify and verify re-engineered SOX17 variants that efficiently and selectively induce either definitive endoderm or specify primordial germ cells. The high mobility group transcription factor SOX17 holds the key to which of the two cell types are formed. Overexpression of SOX17 in cultured pluripotent cells allows for the generation of early stages of human germ cell lineages. In this project, we used CRISPR-Cas9 based gene editing to knock out SOX17 in one human embryonic stem cell line, WIS1. Without SOX17, PSC cannot be maintained in a pluripotent statet but no longer differentiate into PGCLCs. We purchased deep mutational scanning (DMS) libraries and cloned focused hotspot libraries for a key position: SOX17E57, a hSOX2-E46L-K57E, and homologs of SOX17 from diverse species including the comb jelly Mnemiopsis leidyi. All plasmids were introduced into the doxycycline-inducible lentiviral vector pHAGE2-TetO. Then we packaged lentivirus for these SOX genes and transduced SOX17 knock-out cells. We used our monolayer method to differentiate these hPSCs into hPGCLCs within five days by adding doxycycline overexpressing SOX genes. Surprisingly, we found all of hSOX17E57 mutants can rescue hPGCLCs specification in a SOX17 knock-out scenario. However, wild-type SOX2, SOX2-E46L-K57E and SOX17 from non-bilaterian animals are incapable achieve this. Results for this objectives revealed important insights on sequence requirement of SOX17 to direct PGCLC induction and its evolutionary conservation. Objective 3: To define how changes in DNA binding, partner factor association and gene regulation determine how wild-type SOX17 and engineered SOX17 direct lineage choices. We previously used combinatorial libraries that probed all 8000 amino acid combinations at positions 46, 53 and 57 of the HMG boxes of SOX2 or SOX17. These amino acids are positioned at the heterodimer interface with OCT4 and can influence OCT4/SOX cooperativity. In this project, we systematically interrogated how mutations at this critical position affect the cellular reprogramming activity of SOX17. We found that most mutations turn SOX17 into a pluripotency factor regardless of their biophysical properties except for acidic residues and proline. The mutation to an aspartate allows the SOX17E57D protein to maintain a self-renewing endodermal state as the heterodimer of SOX17E57D and OCT4 is preferred to bind canonical DNA motifs. We showed that the glutamate in the wild-type protein blocks the formation of a SOX17/OCT4 dimer bound to composite DNA elements in pluripotency enhancers. A SOX17 variant with an L46F, V53N and E57V triple mutation (henceforth termed SOX17FNV) had more effective reprogramming efficiency than SOX2 in mouse and human cells. We discovered that SOX17 and SOX17FNV bound OCT4 more tightly than SOX2 and formed larger and more liquid condensates.

17101120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101120.value: In one project published in Nucleic Acids Research, we showed that full-length SOX17 variants associate more tightly with OCT4 and have extraordinarily potent transactivation domain. Our findings reveal that engineered SOX17 has a competitive edge over SOX2 in partnering with OCT4, as SOX17FNV/OCT4 heterodimers are predominantly formed over SOX2/OCT4 dimers when both proteins are present. Transcription factors with structural similarities often form both homo- and heterodimers within the scope of palindromic DNA elements. However, strong associations between heterotypic, or evolutionarily unrelated factors, are uncommon, which distinguishes the SOX-OCT dimerization as a singular instance. The intrinsically disordered C-terminus of SOX17 contains several elements that collectively operate as a multivalent entity, bolstering transactivation and other essential functions for reprogramming. In summary, we have highlighted the crucial sequence-function relationships that underpin the distinctive roles of SOX2 and SOX17 in transcriptional regulation, and the foundation of their capacity to guide cell fate decisions in the early embryo. Furthermore, we have identified key characteristics for high-performance reprogramming factors that convert somatic cells into pluripotent stem cells in both mice and humans. In another study that just got pro forma accepted by the ISSCR journal Stem Cell Reports, we discovered that most substitution of the Glu57 of SOX17 turn it into a highly potent inducer of pluripotency. Only SOX17 Glu57Asp or Glu57Pro Pro resulted in reprogramming-incompetent SOX17 variants. SOX17E57D could induce the expression of endoderm-associated genes under pluripotency induction and maintenance conditions. In the case of pluripotency maintenance, we found an upregulation of XEN-specific genes without significant loss of pluripotency-associated genes. Consistently, SOX17E57D concurrently binds the pluripotency-associated canonical motif and the XEN-associated compressed motif. The ability of SOX17E57D to induce a self-renewing endodermal state could be harnessed. Besides, we systematically interrogated how mutations at this critical position affect the hPGCLC specification of SOX17. The heterodimer of SOX17WT and OCT4 has tightly bound affinity to compressed DNA motif but heterodimers of SOX17E57 mutants and OCT4 prefer to bind canonical DNA motif which may impair hPGCLCs specification by overexpressing SOX17E57 mutants.

17101120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101120.value: The variant findings in our studies present a promising avenue for enhancing not only germline specification but also for directing stem cells into extraembryonic lineages such as the hypoblast. A point of particular interest would be to thoroughly assess the potential of SOX17E57D in in vitro differentiation protocols. Currently, some protocols employ the overexpression of wild-type SOX17 to generate the challenging XEN component of human embryo models. A significant limitation of existing in vitro embryo models is the incomplete portrayal of the XEN component, which seldom resembles the cellular composition of natural embryos. Testing the use of SOX17E57D to enhance embryo models presents an intriguing prospect for future research. Moreover, we foresee that the integration of genome editing techniques with this robust in vitro model for hPGCLC specification, in tandem with patient-specific human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), will catalyze significant breakthroughs in human germ cell biology. This includes insights into the unique germline-specific epigenetic program with potential implications for subsequent generations and genetic infertility.

17101120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101120.value: Stem cells offer a lot of potential to help us understand how human embryos develop and could be used to study and possibly treat infertility. One important element in this process is the transcription factor SOX17, which acts as a molecular switch to turn genes on and off. SOX17 is like a traffic controller in the early stages of a human embryo. First, it helps create cell types that feed the embryo and provide oxygen. Then, it acts as a guide, steering some embryonal cells to become early forms of the gut, liver, and lung, and others to become the germline, which can later turn into sperm and egg cells. In this project, we discovered more about how SOX17 can control the genes needed for these different types of cells. We found how it works with other factors to bind DNA and which parts of it are most important to activate genes. This helped us design new versions of SOX17 that allowed us to more accurately and efficiently turn stem cells into the cells we need to study the development of germ cells in a lab setting. This could lead to a way to study infertility and look for potential treatments.

17101320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101320.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is characterized by the absence of nerve cells in the colon, caused by the defects of enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), leading to intestinal obstruction. We have successfully established a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-based disease model to elucidate the disease mechanisms underlying HSCR. Recently, we have performed a high-resolution single-cell analysis of iPSC-derived ENCCs from 7 HSCR patients and 2 controls and identified 19 core genes implicated in the disease initiation and/or progression. They included the Hedgehog (GLI3) and Notch (HEY2) pathway genes and that are implicated in the differentiation of ENCCs and HSCR pathogenesis. Through a pathway-based analysis, we further identified a histone deacetylase, HDAC1, as the overarching regulator of the core gene set and mislocalization of HDAC1 to nucleus was frequently found in HSCR ENCCs, highlighting the potential implications of this histone modifying enzyme in HSCR phenotypes. In line with these observations, our genome-wide chromatin mapping also suggested that chromatin remodeling has a key role in regulating human ENCC-specific gene expression and determining how the non-coding common variants contribute to the HSCR pathogenesis. With the mouse model, we further demonstrated that the interplay between histone modifier and GLI is critical for the neurogenesis of ENCCs. All these observations therefore raise an important possibility that modulation of the histone modifying enzyme may rescue the differentiation defects of the patient ENCCs, representing a new therapeutic strategy for HSCR. Here, we hypothesize that HDAC1 acts epigenetically and/or non-epigenetically causes aberrant activation of Hedgehog and Notch pathways, interrupting the formation of the enteric neurons. We will test our hypothesis by 1) defining the key roles of HDAC1 in the human ENCC development and HSCR pathogenesis; 2) elucidating how HDAC1 interplay with Hedgehog and Notch pathways in the neurogenic and gliogenic lineage differentiation of human ENCCs; and 3) deciphering the key regulomes underlying the disease risk and severity through integrating the transcriptome and epigenome of human ENCCs. Defining the key regulomes underlying the pathogenic pathways which are shared across the entire (or the majority of) spectrum of HSCR disease will allow the identification of the therapeutic targets and evaluation of the potential side effects of various HDAC inhibitors, with a long-term goal of developing effective and affordable treatments. 巨結腸病（HSCR）的特徵是結腸缺乏神經細胞，這是由於腸神經原細胞（ENCC）的缺陷引起，可導致腸梗阻。我們已經成功建立了基於人類誘導的多能幹細胞（hiPSC）的疾病模型，以闡明HSCR的疾病機制。最近，我們從7位HSCR患者和2位對照的iPSC分化出ENCCs，進行了高分辨率單細胞分析，並鑑定出19種與疾病的發生和/或進展有關的核心基因。他們包括了Hedgehog（GLI3）和Notch（HEY2）通路基因，它們與ENCC的分化和HSCR發病機制有關。通過基於路徑的分析，我們進一步確定了組蛋白脫乙酰基酶HDAC1，作為核心基因集的總體調節劑，並且在HSCR ENCC中經常發現HDAC1到核的定位錯誤，突出表明了這種組蛋白修飾酶在HSCR表型中的潛在影響。 。與這些觀察結果一致，我們的全基因組染色質圖譜還表明，染色質重塑在調節人類ENCC特異性基因表達和確定非編碼常見變體如何促進HSCR發病機理中具有關鍵作用。使用小鼠模型，我們進一步證明了組蛋白修飾劑和GLI之間的相互作用對於ENCC的神經發生至關重要。因此，所有這些觀察結果提出了重要的可能性，即組蛋白修飾酶的調節可以挽救患者ENCC的分化缺陷，代表了HSCR的新治療策略。在這裡，我們假設HDAC1在表觀遺傳和/或非表觀遺傳上起作用，從而導致Hedgehog和Notch通路異常激活，從而中斷了腸神經元的形成。我們將通過以下方法檢驗我們的假設：1）定義HDAC1在人類ENCC發育和HSCR發病機理中的關鍵作用； 2）闡明HDAC1在人類ENCC的神經和膠質發生譜系分化中如何與Hedgehog和Notch通路相互作用； 3）通過整合人類ENCC的轉錄組和表觀基因組，破譯疾病風險和嚴重程度的關鍵規律。定義在整個HSCR疾病譜中（或大部分）共有的致病途徑的關鍵調控因素，將有助於確定治療目標並評估各種HDAC抑製劑的潛在副作用，從而實現長期目標開發有效和負擔得起的治療方法。

17101320.label: Realisation of objectives
17101320.value: Followings are the key findings under each objective: 1. To define the key roles of HDAC1 underlying the human ENCC development. Using induced pluripotent stem cell-based models of Hirschsprung and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, we identified a gene set of 118 genes commonly dysregulated in all patient enteric neural crest cells, and suggested HDAC1 may be a key regulator of these genes. In particular, the HDAC1 transcript levels were elevated in ENCCs derived from 2 S-HSCR and 2 L-HSCR lines. Therefore, we performed additional biological assays to delineate how HDAC1 may influence the development of hENCCs and determine how the aberrant HDAC1 activity may cause HSCR disease. Western blot analysis revealed that the total protein expression of HDAC1 in control- and all HSCR-ENCCs are highly comparable. We also examined the repressor function of HDAC1 based on its ability to catalyze the removal of acetyl groups from core histones (H3), but no obvious deacetylation of the H3 was found in HSCR-ENCCs based on the levels of H3K27Ac. HDAC1 forms Sin3, NuRD and CoREST complexes to repress gene expression through promoting histone deacetylation. Therefore, we also examined the potential repressor function of HDAC1 based on the combined expression levels of various subunits in the Sin3, NuRD and CoREST complexes, the inferred Sin3, NuRD and CoREST complex activities were highly comparable between control and HSCR-ENCCs. All these data imply that the aberrant HDAC1 activity as seen in HSCR-ENCCs is unlikely due to the enhanced expression of HDAC1 itself nor its repressor function. On the other hand, expression of HDAC1 was mainly found in the nuclei of HSCR-ENCCs, while both cytoplasmic and nuclear expression of HDAC1 were observed in control-ENCCs. Given the overall expression levels of HDAC1 was comparable between the control- and HSCR-ENCCs, the enhanced nuclear localization of HDAC1 may increase the transactivation activity of HDAC1 in HSCR-ENCCs, leading to the aberrant expressions of HDAC1 target genes. To directly demonstrate the impact of the elevated HDAC1 activity in the neuronal differentiation defects of HSCR-ENCCs, we performed the in vitro differentiation assays using HSCR-ENCCs with specific knock-down of HDAC1, where the HSCR-ENCCs were directed to neuronal lineage to generate enteric neuronal progenitors (NPs) in presence of Control-MO or HDAC1-MO. Consistently, down-regulation of HDAC1 expression level by addition of morpholinos (HDAC1-MO), favored the neuronal lineage differentiation of all HSCR-ENCCs, and significantly more NF expressing NPs were found at the day 5 of differentiation. Similar observations were found when HDAC1 was blocked by two different HDAC inhibitors (pan-HDAC inhibitor: VPA and HDAC1 class I inhibitor: CI994). In summary, aberrantly high HDAC1 transactivation activity is likely associated with the neuronal differentiation defect as observed in HSCR-ENCCs. 2. To delineate elucidating the interplay between HDAC1, Hedgehog and Notch pathways in the neurogenic and gliogenic lineage differentiation of hiPSC-derived ENCCs We have examined the potential interplay between HDAC1 and Hedgehog pathway. Based on our data from the mouse studies, the canonical (Gli-dependent) Hedgehog pathway is associated with HSCR pathogenesis. HDAC1 can bind to Gli3 to repress enhancers and prevent premature activation of hedgehog target genes, while the aberrant Gli3 activator function and premature activation of Hedgehog are associated with HSCR pathogenesis. Overexpression of GLI3 repressor in hiPSC-derived ENCCs abolished their neurogenic lineage differentiation, but did not actively promote the glial lineage differentiation. We have cross-referenced the transcriptomic data obtained from mouse and human ENCCs with mutated Hedgehog components, we found that there are significant overlap in the enriched pathways, suggesting the potential interactions among these two pathways. On the other hand, the non-canonical (Gli-independent pathway) Hedgehog pathway favors the neuronal differentiation of hENCCs and rescues the differentiation defects of HSCR cells, via enhancing the OXPHOS (not through HDAC1). Thus, the two arms of Hedgehog pathway possess different biological roles during ENS development. As for the NOTCH pathway, we also identified that 16 out of 118 hub genes associated with HSCR pathogenesis are the direct targets of NOTCH pathways and they show direct interaction with HDAC1. Nevertheless, unlike HDAC1, inhibition of NOTCH signaling did not affect the neuronal lineage differentiation of hiPSC-derived ENCCs. 3. To decipher the key regulomes underlying the disease risk and severity through integrating the transcriptome and epigenome of human ENCCs We sequenced the transcriptomes of ENCCs derived from 2 control and 7 HSCR-iPSC lines at high resolution. Using these scRNA-seq data, we identified the pathways that commonly affected across various patient bases and identify the corresponding “potential driver genes”. A total of 118 DEGs are shared between the S- and L-HSCR groups, including 49 downregulated and 69 upregulated genes. Then, we built a statistical model to assess how these 118 DEGs change along the disease severity axis. From this analysis, we identified 20 genes that were significantly perturbed along the disease severity axis and functionally enriched in biological pathways. We then used a local linear regression model to identify the rate of expression changes of these core genes across severity axis. We found that 14 and 6 core genes were consistently upregulated and downregulated, respectively, in HSCR. Based on the STRING database, these genes encode proteins that show strong interactions and involvement in neurogenesis and NC development. Specifically, HDAC1 was identified as a hub gene in the PPI network that bridging multiple crucial biological processes. Since most of the core genes were upregulated in the HSCR-ENCCs and showed similar expression pattern with HDAC1, we performed motif enrichment analysis to explore the potential transcriptional coactivator effects of HDAC1 on their expression using the ChIPseq data. We found that 13 of the 20 core genes had at least two sites enriched with the HDAC1 DNA-binding motif. Furthermore, 6 of them were predicted to be “high-confidence” direct target genes of HDAC1. Particularly, we deliberately used the non-DEGs as background genes to perform HDAC1 motif enrichment analysis and observed significantly more enrichment in the DEGs compared to the non-DEGs. This suggested the binding of HDAC1 to the human genome was neither universal nor random and it was associated with the disease state. Using SCENIC analysis, we established a GRN of HDAC1. HDAC1 exhibited transcript enrichment paired with concomitant activation of downstream regulatory networks in various disease states. Intriguingly, the HDAC1 GRN was slightly activated in cells of low severity state but highly activated in severe disease state. This implies that the upregulation of HDAC1 and activation of its GRN are highly associated with disease severity, highlighting its role in different forms of HSCR. Please also refer to our paper (Li, et al, Nat Com, 2023) for the details.

17101320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101320.value: HDAC1 possesses dual regulatory roles in gene transcription and mediates a large number of genes and control various cellular processes. HDAC inhibitor, such as Valproic acid (VPA), possesses neuroprotective and has been commonly used to treat epilepsy and bipolar disorder, while it also downregulates many genes that are essential for dendritic morphogenesis and synapse maturation during early neurodevelopment. This has greatly hampered their therapeutic applications in neurogenic disorders. The next important step is to further delineate how HDAC1 regulates the neuronal differentiation of ENS progenitors for identifying the more specific targets for ENS recovery.

17101320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101320.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is characterized by the absence of enteric neurons caused by the defects of enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), leading to intestinal obstruction. In this project, using induced pluripotent stem cell-based models of Hirschsprung and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, we identified a gene set of 118 genes commonly dysregulated in all patient enteric neural crest cells, and suggested HDAC1 may be a key regulator of these genes. Aberrant activation of HDAC1 was associated with the differentiation defect of HSCR ENCCs and inhibition of HDAC1 recused this defect. Furthermore, aberrant activation of HDAC1 is also associated upregulation of RNA splicing mediators and enhanced alternative splicing events as observed in the severe form of HSCR. In particular, the higher inclusion rate of exon 9 in PTBP1 and the perturbed expression of a PTBP1-target, PKM, are significantly enriched in these patient cells, and associated with the defective oxidative phosphorylation and impaired neurogenesis. In sum, we have defined HDAC1 as a core gene associated with Hirschsprung pathogenesis and suggested that HDAC1 may represent a therapeutic target of HSCR disease.

17101520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101520.value: 固醇是控制細胞膜流動性與通透性的重要中性脂質，它們亦調控包括受體、轉運體及酶等跨膜蛋白的活性。膽固醇（最常見固醇的一種）的生物合成在動物中受到嚴格反饋機制的調節。然而，固醇生成的調節在植物中的相關研究則甚少。從環阿屯醇（前驅物）轉化成具活性的植物固醇須經兩次C4脱甲基化過程，第一步是固醇甲基氧化酶（SMO1）的催化作用。早期的固醇生成路徑共六個步驟，其中的五個曾被利用反向遺傳學技術在模式植物擬南芥的突變體中做研究。我們最近也針對擬南芥的兩個SMO1酶（SMO1-1及SMO1-2）發表研究報告，揭示它們跟擬南芥酰基輔酶A結合蛋白（AtACBP1）相互作用以組織特異性的方式調節固醇的生成。本課題旨在探討最後一個SMO1酶（SMO1-3）的功能，以完成對整個擬南芥SMO1家族的研究。我們已從基本的亞細胞定位及基因空間表達模式推演SMO1-3在植物發育中可能扮演的角色。擬南芥雙突變體和三突變體將被構建，以準確闡述三個SMO1酶的協同功能。固醇類含量分析將揭示其生成過程中的瓶頸及時空調控，而反向遺傳學將有助說明SMO1-3與AtACBP之間的功能關係。我們也會對AtACBP在固醇調節機制所扮演的角色作進一步探究。本計劃的研究成果不僅會增加我們對固醇生成調節機制的知識，也將開拓提高植物固醇產量的應用方法。由於植物固醇的功效在於有效阻擋人類攝取膽固醇，大眾對來自天然食材的植物固醇也漸感興趣，因此增加植物固醇的含量將提高食物營養保健的價值。

17101720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17101720.value: DDK在複製起始過程中功能的冷凍電鏡研究

17101720.label: Project Objectives
17101720.value: Elucidate the mechanisms by which yeast DDK is docked onto the MCM DH to act on distinct substrates. It is known that the MCM DH is the only essential substrate for DDK to trigger replication initiation. However, how DDK is recruited onto the DH to phosphorylate three MCM subunits remains elusive at a molecular level. In this study, we plan to determine the cryo-EM structures of yDDK bound to the DH at atomic resolution, aiming to reveal most of the structural features of yDDK. Determine the cryo-EM structures of human DDK in complex with the MCM DH isolated from human cultured cells. Although the function of DDK in DNA replication is conserved from yeast to human, the protein sequences of Dbf4 orthologs only show limited homology. It is not clear how Dbf4 engages with Cdc7 to recognize and bind to their substrates on the DH in different organisms. To have a better understanding of the function of human DDK in helicase activation, we plan to determine the cryo-EM structures of the hDDK bound to the MCM DH from human cells. The solved structures in this objective will provide valuable information for us to understand the regulation of replication initiation in human cells and also lay a solid foundation for anti-cancer drug development with both Mcm2-7 and DDK as targets.

17101720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101720.value: 在真核生物細胞中，DNA複製開始於染色體上成百上千的起始位點。每一個起始的過程都受到嚴格調控，從而確保基因組可以被準確複製。這個調控的關鍵在於在複製原點上按次序組裝並激活Mcm2-7解旋酶雙六聚體（DH）。雖然這個過程已經被廣泛地研究，其具體調控的分子機制仍然不清楚。自2013年開始，冷凍電子顯微鏡技術迅猛發展，使得DNA複製相關的蛋白複合物結構不斷被解析。這些結構信息，幫助我們對DNA複製調控有全新的認識。 DDK是解旋酶激活當中必須的蛋白激酶複合物。釀酒酵母DDK可以特異結合MCM DH而磷酸化其中三個MCM亞基；其結果得以促進Sld3和Cdc45被招募到DH上。這一個過程是產生Cdc45-GINS-Mcm2-7(CMG)有活性解旋酶的先決條件。DDK的功能在真核生物中非常保守。DDK有兩個亞基：Cdc7和Dbf4。Cdc7激酶亞基的活性受制於其調控亞基Dbf4。其中，Dbf4的蛋白序列保守性較低。目前，Cdc7激酶被Dbf4激活，以及其作用于DH的機理非常不清楚。 之前，我們利用冷凍電鏡解析了MCM DH的高分辨率結構。在此基礎上，我們最近得到了一個3.2埃分辨率的DDK-DH複合物的電鏡結構。在此項目中，我們計劃進一步研究DDK磷酸化激活解旋酶MCM DH的機制。同時，我們也會純化人源DDK以及MCM DH，並解析其結構。本研究，將會揭示複製起始調控的新機制。人源DDK-DH的結構信息，將有助于以DDK以及Mcm2-7作為靶標抗癌藥物的研發。

17101720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101720.value: The Dbf4-dependent kinase Cdc7 (DDK) plays a crucial role in regulating the initiation of DNA replication by phosphorylating the MCM double hexamer (MCM-DH) to promote helicase activation. In our project, we utilized both structural and functional approaches to investigate how DDK controls MCM-DH during origin firing. Through a series of cryo-electron microscopy structures of the DDK-DH assembly, we observed that DDK recruitment to the MCM-DH is primarily facilitated by Dbf4 interacting with the three N-terminal domains (NTDs) of Mcm2/6/4 at the hexamer interface. This specific arrangement positions the core of the Cdc7 kinase in close proximity to its essential substrate, the N-terminal serine/threonine-rich domain (NSD) of Mcm4. Notably, we found that the conformation of NSD is altered by a Dbf4 loop, leading to its immediate capture by nearby Cdc7. Furthermore, a unique Dbf4 inhibitory loop occupies the active center of Cdc7, which is released when the kinase core assumes flexible conformations, establishing a hierarchy for phosphorylating substrates within the MCM complex. Removal of the relevant Dbf4 loops/MCM-binding motifs disrupts the sequential targeting of DDK substrates. In conclusion, our findings highlight the role of Dbf4 in mediating DDK binding to the DH and coordinating a series of phosphorylation events, starting with Mcm4-NSD and extending to other substrates like Mcm2 and Mcm6, ultimately leading to helicase activation.

17101720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101720.value: To achieve selective killing of only cancer cells for chemotherapy, it is important to develop highly specific Cdc7 inhibitors that are capable of antagonizing unique features of the kinase. The information derived from our structures provides crucial insights into the detailed molecular mechanisms of Cdc7 activation by its regulatory subunit Dbf4 and how DDK is targeted to its essential substrate. It would be invaluable for developing anti-cancer drugs that target the unique features of DDK.

17101720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101720.value: In order to create better cancer treatments, we need to find drugs that can specifically target cancer cells without harming healthy cells. By studying the structure of a kinase called DDK and how it works with its substrate, a replicative helicase called MCM, we can better understand how to develop drugs that only affect cancer cells. This information is important for figuring out how to stop DDK from working properly and targeting the specific parts of cancer cells that rely on it.
