17101820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101820.value: The CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing system is flexible due to the ease of changing its target loci, contributing to its widespread use for editing the genome. While various improvements to the Cas9 protein and spacer region of the guide RNA (gRNA) have been made to enhance the target specificity of the CRISPR/Cas9 system, little has been done to the scaffold region of gRNA. This project focuses on studying possible gRNA scaffold variants to optimize the genome editing activity of SpCas9, the most widely used Cas9 protein from Streptococcus pyogenes, for creating gene knockout and precise base edit. We shall generate and characterize a panel of gRNA scaffold variants to enhance the on-target editing and minimize the off-target editing efficiencies of the SpCas9 system. We shall evaluate and confirm the usefulness of the scaffold variants in single-locus gene editing, as well as in multiplexed gene editing. The development of efficient scaffold variants would help improve multiplexed gene editing systems, which would therefore enhance the discovery power of combinatorial CRISPR screens. Here, we also aim to identify scaffold variants that are compatible with the ribonucleoprotein (RNP) delivery system, such that high on-target and low off-target genome editing can be achieved in therapeutically-relevant cells, such as stem cells and primary cells. Overall, this proposed work aims to improve the system functionality of CRISPR/Cas9 for efficient and accurate genome editing. CRISPR / Cas9基因組編輯系統的靈活性，主要源於靶向位点易於更改，這有利於其廣泛應用於編輯基因。雖然針對Cas9蛋白和嚮導RNA間隔區，已有不少的改良設計，以提升Cas9系統的靶向特异性，但對於嚮導RNA支架區域的研究卻不多。 因此，本研究將致力於研究及改良嚮導gRNA支架，以新改良的支架變體，從而優化化膿性鏈球菌Cas9蛋白的基因組編輯活性，提升基因敲除和鹼基編輯的精確度。我們將製造不同嚮導RNA支架的變體，篩選出可提升Cas9系統的中靶率及降低脱靶率的支架變體。我們將評估與鑒定支架變體，於進行單基因與多基因的編輯時，是否具同樣效能 。由於支架變體可降低序列的相似性，避免嚮導RNA表达载体于慢病毒转导期间重组，因此有助發展高效多點基因編輯系統，加強我們篩選基因組合的能力。除此以外，我們同時亦可鑑定與核糖核蛋白（RNP）兼容的支架變體，透過直接輸入核糖核蛋白到乾細胞和原代細胞中，進行高精確的基因組編輯作治療用途。總括而言，這研究計劃旨在優化CRISPR / Cas9系統，以進行高效且準確的多點基因編輯。

17101820.label: Realisation of objectives
17101820.value: This project aims to identify and characterize sgRNA scaffold variants to enhance the on-target editing and minimize the off-target editing efficiencies of SpCas9. For part of Aim 1, we have characterized the candidate sgRNA scaffold variants (v3.11, v3.12, and v3.13) that we have identified in our experiments. To characterize their on-target activities of sgRNA scaffold variants, we have performed T7 endonuclease assay to measure the DNA cleavage activity of the variants at 5 endogenous loci. Our results showed that using the three sgRNA scaffold variants increased the editing activity of SpCas9 by about 10-15%. To evaluate the genome-wide off-target activity of these variants, we have performed GUIDE-Seq (Genome-wide Unbiased Identification of Double strand breaks Enabled by Sequencing) to detect oligo tag integration into the on-/off- target sites of nuclease-induced double strand breaks in live human cells using three sets of sgRNAs targeting the EMX1, FANCF, and PD1 loci. Our results indicated that v3.11, v3.12 and the previously published sgRNA scaffold variant from Chen et al., Cell, 2013 all generated low on-to-off targeting ratio (i.e., more off-target edits and in some cases new off-target sites) than wild type scaffold, while v3.13 variant resulted in comparable on-to-off target editing to wild type. Therefore, our engineered v3.13 variant has a distinct advantage of increasing SpCas9’s on-target activity while maintaining high editing specificity, which has not been previously achieved with other existing scaffold variants. We have further showed that the v3.13 variant is compatible with the lentiviral combinatorial sgRNA expression system for multiplexed editing of two and three genes. For the other part of Aim 1, we sought to broaden our search to systematically identify additional sgRNA scaffold variants that show robust on-target activity and low off-target activity via constructing a variant library with other extensions and mutations introduced onto the lower stem, upper stem, and hairpin structures of the scaffold sequence. While we were designing the library, another research group published a paper (Jost et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2020) and the group screened through a large library of 995 sgRNA scaffold variants comprising single-nucleotide substitutions, base-pair substitution, and a combination of both. However, the substitution-function relationship of the sgRNA scaffold was not thoroughly analysed in that study. We have thus set out to perform a more extensive computational analysis to look at the sgRNA scaffold activity data to help us pinpoint 1) high activity mutations, 2) positions that tolerate engineering, and 3) preserved positions for sgRNA functions, and thus we have modified our original sgRNA library design to focus on the above pinpointed mutations/sites. Briefly, our computational analysis has identified sets of single-nucleotide/base-pair mutations that confer high/low sgRNA activity (beneficial mutations/deleterious mutations) from the Jost et. al. dataset. We also found that mutations at stem-loop 2 and 3 of the sgRNA scaffold appears to be highly tolerated. We have then moved on to design a sgRNA scaffold library with specific base-pair mutations and stem-length combinations at stem loop 2 (which is also the site at which mutations are introduced onto v3.13). We applied ModeRNA to model all the mutation combinations to generate target-template alignment fasta, focusing on changes on nucleotides 58-69 and stack 58-69, 60-67, 61-66 plus stem-length and loop extensions. We designed optimized stem-length extension using RNA designer with parameters: temperature: 37oC, target GC % of 50%, etc. We selected top designs with the minimum free energy and designs that fit with the beneficial mutations including U61G-A66C. We also re-designed loop extension distal from the tetraloop. Then, we have successfully constructed our designed sgRNA library and delivered it into human cells for profiling the scaffold variants’ activity with SpCas9. We have completed the large-scale profiling experiments and identified two candidate sgRNA scaffold variants, named SV1 and SV48, that exhibit high editing activity with SpCas9. We have validated their editing activities using non-pooled assays. The above bioinformatics analysis and experimental profiling work achieve Aim 1’s objectives, which forms the larger part (over 50% of work) of the entire study. We moved on to characterize engineered sgRNA scaffold under the settings of ribonucleoprotein (Aim 2). Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) delivery, in which recombinant Cas9 protein is pre-complexed with sgRNA and directly delivered to cells, is a method that is more preferred than DNA- and RNA- based expression methods in translating CRISPR/Cas9 tools for therapeutic applications. Here we have demonstrated the compatibility of our engineered gRNA scaffolds SV48 and SV240 with the RNP system for genome editing. We have built a library of ~100 sgRNA spacers to broadly evaluate the editing efficiencies of SV48 and SV240 when paired up with WT SpCas9. We used deep sequencing to characterize the on- and off- target activities and successfully confirmed their efficacy and compatibility, thus achieving Aim 2’s objective. For Aim 3, we have successfully characterized the engineered gRNA scaffolds for enhancing efficiency of CRISPR-mediated base editing. We performed individual validation experiments using deep sequencing and confirmed that using SV48 and SV240 generated more base edits than using a WT scaffold across five endogenous loci. In particular, at the CXCR4 loci, substituting the WT scaffold with SV240 increased base edits from 21.3% to 47.7%. Using SV48 and SV240 resulted in largely comparable editing purity, indel generation rate, and noncanonical G-to-H conversion rate, compared with those using a WT scaffold. We also looked into how SV48 and SV240 could increase base editing activity. Both SV48 and SV240 carry a GGUG tetraloop sequence replacement at upper stem loop 2. Our molecular modelling indicates that a GGUG tetraloop, along with the other substitutions in the stem loop 2 regions of SV48, leads to a different loop conformation. The backbone of G65 and C66 is brought closer to His721 (at distances of 3 A°) of SpCas9 and forms two points of contacts for stronger interactions. With WT scaffold, A64 and A65 at the tetraloop of stem loop 2 interact with His721 of SpCas9 at distances of 4–5 A°. The SV240 scaffold is also modelled to strengthen existing interactions with His721 of SpCas9 and create new interactions with K1176 of the PI domain in SpCas9. These models indicate that strengthening the scaffold’s interaction with SpCas9 via His721 and the PI domain of SpCas9 represents a viable approach to enhance base editor activity. The objective of Aim 3 is also achieved.

17101820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101820.value: We have successfully engineered several sgRNA scaffolds that boost with genome editing efficiency and specificity across a broad range of endogenous targets in human cells in vitro. These scaffolds are useful for achieving both gene knockouts and base edits. The design principle (including rational structure-based design and bioinformatics modelling) can be readily applied to build more engineered sgRNA scaffold variants to broaden the search for even more enhanced variants. Our identified variants will be further applied in editing therapeutically relevant loci and in vivo models in future to demonstrate its translational utility.

17101820.value: We have created new engineered sgRNA scaffolds useful for enhancing the efficiency of CRISPR-based genome editing in human cells. Our design methods are validated and can be extended to engineer even more variants with superior efficiency and specificity for diverse genome editing applications.

17102120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102120.value: The process of memory storage is not a random event. Emerging evidence supports the view that a given memory is stored in specific neurons and synapses in the neural network. Our previous study found that auditory-cued fear conditioning and fear extinction induced dendritic spine elimination and formation on the same dendrites in a location- and cue-specific manner in mouse frontal association cortex. The activity-dependent dendritic spine modifications involve different mechanisms at multiple levels in spatiotemporal manners, including synaptic input patterns, signal transduction, local protein translation via mRNA transport and translation, and protein synthesis and delivery. These processes all play roles in memory allocation within the complex neural network. However, little is known about the mechanisms and components that enable memory allocation for efficient memory storage and recall. Local protein synthesis in dendrites is thought to be essential for synapse-specific plasticity. Kinesin-1 (KIF5) is one of the kinesin motor proteins that have been found to transport fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP) and messenger ribonucleoprotein (mRNP) complexes in dendrites. Three kinesin-1 heavy chain isoforms including KIF5B have been identified in mammals. Our preliminary data showed specific knockdown of KIF5B in hippocampal neurons led to reduced dendritic spine density, frequency of miniature excitatory synaptic current (mEPSC), and FMRP granule density. In addition, KIF5B postnatal conditional knockout (cKO) mice showed significant deficits in fear conditioning and heightened dendritic spine plasticity. Based on these findings and the previously identified KIF5B cargoes, we hypothesise that KIF5B plays a role in dendritic spine plasticity and dendritic localization of FMRP, which are crucial for fear learning-induced cue- and location-specific dendritic spine plasticity. To test this hypothesis, we will utilize the Cre-Lox P system to create a conditional knockout model of KIF5B in CaMKIIα-expressing excitatory neurons. First, we will study the baseline dendritic spine plasticity of layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons in KIF5B cKO mice in vivo by using two-photon microscopy. Second, we will examine cue- and location-specific dendritic spine modifications in auditory-cued fear conditioning and extinction in KIF5B cKO mice. Third, we will investigate the dendritic localization of FMRP and dendritic spine plasticity in awake and head-fixed behaving mice in response to fear learning and recall. In summary, our findings will reveal the fundamental and novel role of KIF5B in learning-induced spatiotemporal dynamics of dendritic spine and dendritic FMRP localization in vivo. 記憶存儲過程不是隨機事件, 越來越多的證據支持記憶存儲在特定的神經元和神經網絡的突觸中。然而我們對於啟用內存分配以進行有效的內存存儲和調用的機制和組件知之甚少。樹突中的局部蛋白質合成被認為對於突觸特異性可塑性至關重要。 Kinesin-1（KIF5）是一種驅動蛋白運動蛋白，已發現可在樹突中轉運Fragile X Mental Retardation protein （FMRP）和信使核糖核蛋白（mRNP）複合物。在哺乳動物中已鑑定出包括KIF5B在內的三種kinesin-1亞型。KIF5B條件性基因敲除（cKO）小鼠表現出恐懼調節方面的明顯缺陷，並增強了樹突棘的可塑性。基於這些發現和先前確定的KIF5B貨物，我們假設KIF5B在樹突棘可塑性和FMRP的樹突局部化中起作用，這對於恐懼學習誘發的提示和特定位置的樹突棘可塑性至關重要。我們將利用Cre-Lox P系統在表達CaMKIIα的興奮性神經元中創建KIF5B的條件敲除模型。首先，我們將使用雙光子顯微鏡研究KIF5B cKO小鼠體內第2/3層錐體神經元的基線樹突棘可塑性。其次，我們將在KIF5B cKO小鼠中檢查提示性和特定位置的樹突棘修飾在聽覺提示的恐懼學習中的作用。第三，我們將研究恐懼學習和回憶對FMRP的樹突定位和樹突棘的可塑性。我們的發現將揭示KIF5B在學習誘導的樹突棘可塑性和樹突FMRP轉運和定位中的基礎作用。

17102120.label: Realisation of objectives
17102120.value: Objective 1: To first investigate the role of KIF5B in baseline dendritic spine plasticity of L2/3 pyramidal neurons, we used GFP construct to label dendritic spines by in utero electroporation targeting the frontal region on E15.5 embryos of CamkII-Cre (as control) or CamkII-Cre; Kif5bfl/fl (KIF5B cKO) mice. Mice were imaged by transcranial in vivo two-photon imaging in the frontal association cortex (FrA) at 1-month old. We found that fewer persisted spines throughout entire imaging period from day 0 to day 7 in KIF5B cKO compared to control. Further looking into the dynamics of dendritic spines revealed that KIF5B cKO had significant higher spine elimination rate both from day 0-2 and day 2-7 when compared to control. Although spine formation rate was not significant different between control and KIF5B cKO from day 0-2, there was significant higher spine formation rate in KIF5B cKO from day 2-7. We next investigated the mechanism underlying the reduced spine stability in KIF5B cKO mice by examining the dendritic spine plasticity and excitatory and inhibitory synaptic markers and scaffolding proteins, PSD95 and gephyrin, respectively. To visualize these two synaptic markers and dendritic spine plasticity simultaneously, we co-electroporated constructs that express the cre-recombinase, and three other cre-depending expression of structural fill eYFP, PSD-95-mCherry, and gephyrin-teal into E15.5 mouse embryos to enable co-expression and sparse labeling. Mice were reared to postnatal day (P) 27 for cranial window implantation. At P38, mice were subjected to two-photon imaging for 6 imaging sessions between day 0-12. Consistent with the previous experiment, there was a higher proportion of eliminated spine that re-formed on the third time point (at day 5). However, percentage of these recurrence spines that persisted in all imaging sessions was lowered in KIF5B cKO mice. In addition, we also observed more highly recurrent spines (with 4 dynamic events, including elimination and formation) over 6 imaging sessions in KIF5B cKO mice. These data showed that KIF5B deletion led to a reduction of dendritic spine maintenance with spines eliminated and re-formed more frequently. Here we found that the spine type composition was different between control and KIF5B cKO mice. There were fewer PSD-95 positive spines, but there were significantly more double negative spines in KIF5B cKO when compared to control, while the proportion of double positive and gephyrin positive spine was not different between two groups. While around 80% of PSD-95 puncta were found in spine in both control and KIF5B cKO, the density of PSD-95 on shaft was significantly lower in KIF5B cKO. For highly recurrent spines, we found that PSD-95 negative proportion was higher than those that are PSD-95 positive in both control and KIF5B cKO, although there is no statistical significance between two groups. Consistent with previous reports, gephyrin is highly dynamic on dendritic spines and thus not likely to contribute to dendritic spine structural maintenance. Although all KIF5s were reported to transport gephyrin in dendrites, our findings show that KIF5B deletion did not affect gephyrin dynamics in dendrites. Therefore, KIF5B deletion specifically led to reduction of PSD-95 puncta in dendrites, which resulted in more PSD-95 negative spines that were less stable. Objective 2: Previously we have shown that KIF5B deletion impaired fear memory in fear conditioning (FC), so here we then asked whether the learning induced spine plasticity was altered. Mice were separated into 3 groups: WT unpaired, WT paired and KIF5B cKO paired groups. WT unpaired served as a control to delineate the learning specific effect of FC instead of experience. As previous studies have reported that FC induced spine plasticity in layer 5 pyramidal neurons could be observed as soon as 4 hours after FC, we adopted head-fixed awake imaging at 1 hour, 4 hours and 8 hours after FC to minimize impact of anaesthesia on learning induced spine changes, and a recall test was carried out 24 hours after FC. Fear extinction was also carried out. Similar to previous behaviour results with recall test 2 days after FC, cKO paired groups also had lower freezing response than WT paired group 24 hours after FC, which was comparable to WT unpaired control. Fear extinction protocol could successfully reduce freezing response in all groups. When we examined the FC and extinction induced spine plasticity, we found FC increased spine elimination but not formation rate in WT paired group. Extinction induced higher spine formation rate in WT paired group. On the contrary, for cKO paired group, FC did not induce spine elimination but higher spine formation rate. Extinction had no effect on spine formation for cKO paired group. The degree of freezing response was correlated with the degree of learning induced spine plasticity, indicating these spine changes are relevant to behavioural changes. Taken together, KIF5B deletion impaired both fear memory and learning related location-specific spine plasticity in layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons of FrA. Objective 3: To investigate whether KIF5B also regulates the FMRP dendritic localization and FMRP associated spine plasticity, L2/3 pyramidal neurons were transfected with constructs to label spines (DsRed) and FMRP (FMRP-GFP). We quantified the spine plasticity and FMRP dynamics in basal dendrites, since FMRP is more localized in proximal dendrites. We examined the association between FMRP and spine plasticity by measuring the relative distance of the closest shaft FMRP puncta to different spine types: stable, eliminated, and newly formed spines in hour-interval. On average, the closest shaft FMRP distance to stable spines was similar between control and KIF5B cKO. For the spine plastic events that occurred at H4, FMRP was found to be localized closer to the sites of spine formation 4 hours prior to their formation and remained close at H4, compared to stable spines in both control and KIF5B cKO. This suggests that FMRP localization is associated with spine formation. We next asked if FMRP localization is associated with fear conditioning- and extinction-induced spine plasticity. We quantified the relative distance between shaft FMRP puncta and the closest eliminated spines or newly formed spines induced by fear learning. In control, FC induced no significant difference in the FMRP relative distance to both eliminated spines or newly formed spines when comparing paired and unpaired control groups. For fear extinction, while the rate of spine formation was significantly higher in control paired group than unpaired group, we found more FMRP localized closer to newly formed spines in control paired group, but not to sites of spine elimination. Therefore, FMRP dendritic localization is associated with spine formation but not spine elimination, which is consistent with our findings in baseline FMRP localization. Interestingly, Kif5b deletion led to abnormal FMRP puncta proximity to plastic spines: 1) after FC, FMRP puncta population shifted further away from eliminated spines, but shifted closer to newly formed spines in KIF5B cKO paired group when compared to control paired group; 2) after fear extinction, FMRP puncta population shifted closer to eliminated spines and further away from newly-formed spines in KIF5B cKO paired group. In summary, there is specific fear learning-dependent FMRP localization towards newly formed spines but not eliminated spines after fear extinction in control. Notably, Kif5b deletion not only abolished fear learning-induced spine plasticity, but also altered this learning-dependent FMRP dendritic localization, underscoring the specific roles of KIF5B in experience-dependent spine plasticity by regulating the FMRP localization.

17102120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102120.value: Kinesin 1 (KIF5) is one of the major types of motor proteins that transport synaptic proteins and mRNAs to dendrites, but their function in dendritic transport of neurons in vivo remains undefined. Using in vivo two-photon longitudinal imaging, we found that mice with conditional knockout of kif5b (KIF5B cKO) in CaMKIIα-Cre expressing neurons showed heightened turnover and lower stability of dendritic spines in L2/3 pyramidal neurons in the frontal association cortex. The increase of dendritic spine instability was accompanied with less postsynaptic density 95 (PSD95) acquisition in dendritic spines without affecting the inhibitory synaptic scaffolding protein gephyrin. Notably, the RNA-binding protein Fragile X Mental Retardation protein (FMRP), a KIF5 cargo that regulates PSD95 translation and degradation, was translocated to the proximity of newly formed spines several hours before the spine formation events in vivo in control mice. However, this preceding transport of FMRP towards new spines was abolished in KIF5B cKO and the FMRP puncta became less dynamic in dendritic spines. We further found that FMRP was localized closer to newly formed spines after fear extinction, and this learning-dependent localization of FMRP was disrupted in KIF5B cKO. This is the first report showing FMRP translocation in cerebral cortex in vivo. Together, these results indicate that KIF5B is a crucial motor protein for the dendritic targeting of synaptic proteins that underlies dendritic spine plasticity.

17102120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102120.value: This study found that RNA binding protein, FMRP, translation is related to dendritic spine formation. However, it is not known if it is general properties for RNA binding proteins or specific to FMRP. Therefore, it would be interesting to further investigate other RNA binding proteins distribution in relation to dendritic spine plasticity. In addition to RNA binding protein localization, it would be interesting to further study mRNA localization upon learning and dendritic plasticity in the cerebral cortex in vivo.

17102120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102120.value: In the present study, we performed intravital imaging to track the translocation of synaptic proteins (PSD95 and Gephyrin) and FMRP in dendrites in the mouse frontal cortex. KIF5B, a type of motor protein, is discovered to regulate synaptic protein composition and turnover of dendritic spines. KIF5B promotes PSD95 gain and maintenance in dendritic spines. In addition, KIF5B also plays an important role in regulating spine plasticity-related FMRP localization in baseline condition. Conditional knockout of KIF5B impairs spine plasticity-related FMRP localization and activity-dependent dendritic spine plasticity in fear learning.

17102420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102420.value: 神經板邊界內神經嵴細胞（NCC）的命運是由涉及多個信號和轉錄因子的基因調控網絡（GRN）協調控制的，其賦予神經嵴不同於神經祖細胞和非神經外胚層的調控狀態。時空表達、基因擾動和順式調控研究表明，信號分子和神經板邊界特化因子協同控制神經嵴特化因子的表達，從而決定神經嵴細胞的命運。但是，目前尚不清楚這些順式作用因子如何與基礎轉錄機制相互作用來調節神經嵴特化因子基因的轉錄起始和維持。解決該問題將進一步揭示神經嵴特化因子的轉錄調控機理，從而能夠將真正的神經嵴細胞及時從其他譜系中分離出來。 我們在雞胚胎中的初步研究數據表明Rho GTP酶激活蛋白(RhoGAP) Deleted in Liver Cancer 1 (DLC1) 能夠獨立於RhoGAP介導的RHOA活性抑制，在細胞核中調節神經嵴特化因子基因的維持。我們從機理上發現了一個神經板邊界特化因子,PAX7, 能夠調節DLC1的表達，而且它們的相互作用是PAX7與神經嵴特化因子增強子結合所必需的。質譜分析進一步確定了DLC1和TCEB1之間的特定關聯，這是延長RNA聚合酶II與DNA結合所必需的，以維持神經嵴特化因子基因的高效轉錄。基於這些數據，我們假定核DLC1以RhoGAP獨立的方式將神經板邊界特化因子連接到基礎轉錄機制中來調節神經嵴特化因子的轉錄。在本課題中，我們提議以雛雞胚胎為模型研究核DLC1在神經嵴特化過程中的功能，主要通過以下方式實現：(1）闡明核DLC1的功能獨立於其RhoGAP在調節神經嵴細胞命運過程中的催化活性；(2）研究核DLC1-PAX7複合物在調控神經嵴特化因子基因表達中的作用，以及（3）闡明DLC1如何調控神經嵴特化因子基因的轉錄機制。該研究將通過探究核DLC1與控制神經嵴特化因子基因轉錄相關的轉錄因子和轉錄體系成分的關係來揭示核DLC1的新功能（獨立於其RhoGAP活性。這將是第一個揭示在基因調控網絡中將神經板邊界建立過程與神經嵴特化過程聯繫起來的非DNA結合因子的研究。

17102420.label: Realisation of objectives
17102420.value: Objective 1: 1.1 Assessing the role of nuclear DLC1 in NCC fate maintenance We first examined whether cells overexpressing WT DLC1 or RhoGAP acquire neural or non-neural ectoderm lineage by staining for SOX2 and E-Cadherin as representative markers respectively. Immunofluorescence staining showed that both WT DLC1 or RhoGAP overexpression led to upregulation of SOX2 expression in the NC territory where expression of NC specifier genes SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3 were lost. In contrast, ectodermal expression of E-Cadherin remained unchanged in all treatments. These results indicate switching of cell fate from NC to neural progenitors. Despite the presence of NLS motif in the RhoGAP domain, we also found more NLS sequences in START domain. Since mutating each single residue and in different combinations may modify DLC1 protein function and the outcome may not be informative, we adopted another approach by overexpressing DLC1 truncated constructs in DLC1 knockdown environment to determine which domain(s) are able to restore NCC fate. The results obtained so far indicate that WT DLC1 and the RhoGAP-deficient mutant (DLC1 R712A) but not RhoGAP alone or the dominant negative DLC1 (DNDLC1, without RhoGAP and START domains), can restore SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3 expression while restricting SOX2 expression in the neural progenitors in DLC1 MO expressing cells. Altogether, these results suggest that both RhoGAP and START domains determine the nuclear localization of DLC1 which regulates NCC fate determination independent of its RhoGAP catalytic activity. 1.2 Functional studies of nuclear DLC1 in regulating NC specification independent of its RhoGAP catalytic activity To address this issue, we have generated a DLC1 RhoGAP deficient construct (DLC1 R712A) which caused increase level of RhoA-GTP (active form) compared to reduced expression of RhoA-GTP by WT DLC1. This could be due to the dominant-negative effect of DLC1 R712A on endogenous DLC1 function in inhibiting RhoA activity. In addition, electroporation of constitutive active form of RhoA (Q63L) or dominant-negative form of RhoA (T19N) did not affect SOX9 expression. These results further consolidate that DLC1 regulates NC specification independent of RhoGAP catalytic activity or alteration RhoA activity. Objective 2: 2.1- Evaluating a direct transcriptional activation of DLC1 expression by PAX7 To determine whether PAX7 directly regulates DLC1 expression through binding to tis motif within the DLC1 promoter region, we have performed ChIP-qPCR to quantify the binding efficiency of PAX7 on DLC1 promoter in st 7-8 chick embryos, when both genes are expressed in the dorsal neural tube. The results showed that PAX7 antibody was able to enrich its consensus motif in the DLC1 promoter region compared to no enrichment by IgG control, indicating that PAX7 can bind to the DLC1 promoter region. In addition, we also generated a DLC1 promoter-driven luciferase construct and demonstrated that PAX7 is able to transactivate the reporter activity. These results indicate that PAX7 directly transactivates DLC1 expression through binding to its promoter region. 2.2- Investigating the association of nuclear DLC1 with PAX7 at the chromatin level Our co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) experiments in chick embryonic lysates showed that endogenous DLC1 was able to associate with PAX7. To map the interacting domain, we found ectopic expression of WT DLC1 or RhoGAP domain alone is able to immunoprecipitate with endogenous PAX7, suggesting that DLC1 interacts with PAX7 via its RhoGAP domain. ChIP-qPCR showed that PAX7 could bind to the enhancer regions of SOX9, FOXD3 and SNAI2. Although DLC1 was not able to bind to the enhancer regions of NC specifier genes, it is required for PAX7 binding to these regulatory regions. To examine the potential mechanisms by which DLC1 regulates PAX7 occupancy at enhancer elements of NC specifier genes, we performed ChIP-qPCR for H3K27ac which marks active enhancer, in DLC1 MO treated cells. We repeated the experiments three times, however, only the first trial showed a reduction in H3K27ac enrichment at the enhancer regions of SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3 in DLC1 MO cells compared to control (Ctrl) MO. The other replicates did not show any differences between DLC1 MO and Ctrl MO. The inconsistency across replicates may be attributed to low knockdown efficiency or suboptimal transfection efficiency of DLC1 MO in the neural crest cells. Objective 3: (i) Mapping of DLC1 domain(s) responsible for interacting with TCEB1 Our previous mass spectrometry analysis of immunoprecipitated proteins associated with ectopic DLC1 in chick neural tube lysates identified transcription elongation factor B polypeptide (TCEB1) which has been shown to interact with RNA polymerase II (PolII) for promoting transcriptional elongation (PolII-Ser2P) through suppression of RNA polymerase pausing. We confirmed the ability of endogenous DLC1 to associate with TCEB1 whereas PAX7 did not interact with TCEB1. Domain mapping analysis showed that TCEB1 can interact with the RhoGAP domain of DLC1. Like WT DLC1, overexpression of RhoGAP domain alone and DLC1 R712A can reduce the binding affinity of PolII-Ser2P to the SOX9 genomic DNA, leading to decreased SOX9 transcription, likely to due to TCEB1 sequestration. To further investigate the possibility of TCEB1 sequestration, we conducted rescue experiments by overexpressing TCEB1 full-length cDNA in embryos treated with WT DLC1, the RhoGAP domain alone or DLC1 R712A using TCEB1 MO as a control to determine whether any of these constructs could restore PolII-Ser2P binding on the SOX9 genomic DNA and consequently rescue SOX9 transcription. However, the results showed variability in the enrichment of PolII-Ser2P along the SOX9 gene bodies. This variability may be due an insufficient high amount of TCEB1 to counteract the dominative effect of the other constructs or may involve other factors beyond TCEB1 that regulate PolII-Ser2P occupancy on the SOX9 genomic regions. (ii) Assessing the impact of DLC1 MO on PolII-Ser2P-SOX9 genomic DNA association To determine whether DLC1 regulates the binding efficiency of PolII-Ser2P within the SOX9 genomic locus, we carried out ChIP-qPCR for PolIII-Ser-2P in embryos treated with DLC1 MO and control MO. The results showed that DLC1 MO reduced the binding of PolII-Ser2P to the SOX9 locus compared to control MO, suggesting that DLC1 is required for efficient association of PolII-Ser2P along the SOX9 genomic DNA during transcription. Moreover, ChIP-qPCR further revealed a decrease in TCEB1 occupancy at the SOX9 promoter region in DLC1 MO cells. These findings indicate that DLC1 is required for TCEB1 association at the SOX9 promoter to facilitate efficiency transcription elongation of PolII-Ser2P along SOX9 gene body. (iii) Examine how PAX7-DLC1-TCEB1 complex directs transcription of NC specifier genes Our previous results showed that TCEB1 MO resulted in loss of mRNAs encoding NC specifiers without disrupting the expression and association of DLC1 and PAX7, suggesting that DLC1-PAX7 complex is not sufficient to maintain transcription of NC specifier genes in the absence of TCEB1. In agreement with this, ChIP-qPCR analysis showed that PAX7 remained associated with the enhancer regions of SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3 in TCEB1 MO cells. Altogether, these results indicate that nuclear DLC1 serves as a “bridge” connecting PAX7 on enhancers with the transcriptional machinery at the promoter region of NC specifiers to regulate NC specification. Due to funding constraints, we were unable to perform mass spectrometry to identify factors associated with TCEB1 involved in the regulation of PolII phosphorylation. This experiment aims to reveal the components of transcriptional machinery responsible for directing neural crest specification.

17102420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102420.value: Major findings: Our study reveals a nuclear role of RhoGAP Deleted in Liver Cancer 1 (DLC1) in specifying neural crest cell fate in a RhoGAP independent manner. Mechanistically, the neural plate border specifier PAX7 associates with DLC1 and their interaction is required for PAX7 binding to the enhancers of neural crest specifiers, SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3. In addition, DLC1 further recruits TCEB1, which is essential for DNA binding of elongating RNA polymerase II to maintain transcription of neural cest specifiers. In summary, our results indicate that nuclear DLC1 serves as a “bridge” connecting PAX7 on enhancers with the transcriptional machinery at the promoter region of neural crest specifiers to regulate neural crest specification. Research Outcome: Due to COVID-19, I delivered a Zoom seminar on this project at the 6th International Anatomical Sciences and Cell Biology Conference on 22 Feb 2022. A PhD student was trained and recently graduated. Due to COVID-19 and funding constraints, the findings of this project were presented on posters at several local scientific conferences. A manuscript is currently in preparation for submission to Nature Communications.

17102420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102420.value: Based on the results obtained in chick embryos, we also examined whether DLC1 plays a conserved role in regulating human neural crest (NC) specification. Based on the protocol from the literature, we generated human NC cells (NCCs) from induced pluripotent stem cells via the neural plate border (NPB) stage. Human express five DLC1 isoforms, and our analysis revealed that DLC1 isoform 2 (equivalent to chick DLC1 isoform 3) is specifically expressed in NPB-like cells and maintained in NCCs. In contrast, DLC1 isoform 1 (DLC1-i1) expression coincides with the initiation of NC specifiers expression. Functional studies showed that knockdown of both isoforms significantly reduced the expression of NPB and NC markers. Conversely, overexpression of DLC1 isoform 2 maintain cells in an NPB state, while overexpression of isoform 1 promotes NC specification. These results demonstrate a conserved role for DLC1 in NC development between human and chick and establish that isoform switching of human DLC1 is essential for the transition from NPB-to-NCC. We have applied for internal funding to further investigate the molecular mechanisms by which distinct DLC1 isoforms regulate NPB formation and NC specification.

17102420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102420.value: The process of neural crest cell (NCC) formation begins at the border of the neural plate, regulated by a network of genes that control this fate. A key gene, PAX7, activates crucial genes (SOX9, SNAI2 and FOXD3) that define NCC identity. However, we do not fully understand how these genes are turned on and kept active. Our research found that a protein called DLC1, located in the cell nucleus, acts as a connector which links PAX7 at the gene’s enhancer regions to the machinery that turns genes on at the gene’s promoter, helping to initiate and maintain NCC development. These findings reveal a new and crucial role for DLC1, a RhoGAP protein, in controlling neural crest formation at the transcriptional level. This adds a new piece to the puzzle of how neural crest cells are formed during development.

17102620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102620.value: 研究背景：人臉是變異程度最大的外在可見的人體結構特徵。人臉形態特徵主要受到遺傳因素影響。既往對人臉遺傳因素的了解多來源於對唐氏綜合症、唇腭裂等影響顱面部發育的遺傳性疾病的研究。然而，影響正常人臉結構變異的遺傳結構尚不明確。 研究重點：人類已發現眾多影響身高、體重指數等複雜性狀的遺傳結構變異，卻僅發現了有限的影響正常人臉結構的遺傳變異。這是由於既往研究僅基於坐標點間的線性距離定義面部形態特徵，並且選取的面部坐標點稀疏，因此無法捕捉人臉豐富的形態細節特徵。此外，既往基於幾何形態學的人臉遺傳結構研究僅分析了面部整體特征，並且局限於歐洲、非洲、及拉丁美洲人群。目前尚無探討中國漢族人面部遺傳結構的大樣本全基因組關聯分析。 研究目的：運用有效方法識別影響中國漢族人群人臉形態特征的遺傳位點。 研究方案：本項研究擬招募7200名18歲研究對象。本項目將採用立體攝影系統採集研究對象3D面部影像。運用緻密標誌點高保真重建人臉結構特徵，採用多元統計算法方法提取面部形態信息，運用非監督學習算法將人臉拆分為多層次聚類模塊。運用全基因組關聯分析對基因型及表型數據進行分析，明確影響中國漢族人面部結構的遺傳變異。 研究意義：本項目將建立中國漢族人面部形態數據庫，其研究結果將準確量化遺傳因素對人臉形態的影響程度並識別相應的遺傳變異位點。本項目有助於闡明面部發育異常的分子機制，並為基於人工智能算法的遺傳疾病快速診斷提供重要參考。在精準醫學的時代背景下，本項目有助於基於患者遺傳背景制定個體化顱頜面整形手術方案。

17102620.label: Realisation of objectives
17102620.value: # How the project objectives have been achieved: 1. Preparation for realization of the objectives Ethical approval was obtained for this survey (UW 19-591). Invitation letters were sent to 7500 students and their parents prior to data extraction from the extant database and data collection in the secondary schools. Written consent has been obtained from 7256 (3656 females and 3600 males) participants. 2. Clinical data collection The participant’s oral cavity was cleaned with gauze and dental floss. All types of malocclusion, the presence of dental anomalies, and oral health status were evaluated using the same criteria. One trained and calibrated examiner performed the clinical examination using a disposable plane intra-oral mirror with a built-in LED light source. Participants’ body height was measured using a portable height measure (Seca 213, Hamburg, Germany) and body weight measured using a calibrated weighing scale (WB-8000RW, Tanita, Japan). Their BMI was then calculated. One trained and calibrated examiner (intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) = 0.96 - 0.99 for intra-examiner reliabilities of assessing body height and body weight) performed all of the anthropometric measurements following standardised assessment procedures. The 3D facial images of the participants were captured using a stereophotogrammetric technique. The participants were seated at a fixed distance from the cameras, facing at a mirror placed in front of him/her. A surgical cap was used to allow for sufficient exposure of the face. The 3D facial images were captured using the 3dMDface stereophotogrammetric optical system (3dMD, Atlanta, GA, USA). This system contains three pairs of synchronised cameras, which allows for the capture of six images within 2 milliseconds. These images were merged by a triangulation algorithm to generate life-like facial images with natural surface textures. 3. Data processing Standardised facial landmarks were digitised on the 3D facial images to include all important facial features. Curve and surface sliding semilandmarks were also be digitised to capture the shape information of the face where there was a lack of distinct landmarks. Digitisation were performed using the Checkpoint software (Stratovan, Davis, USA) twice, separated by a minimum of two weeks, to determine the measurement error. Coordinates of landmarks and semilandmarks were submitted for Generalised Procrustes Analysis (GPA) which is a registration technique that removes information on location, orientation, and size of an object through iterative cycles of translation, rotation, and scaling. After GPA, non-shape information in the raw landmark data were eliminated and the resulting Procrustes shape coordinates captured the pure shape information. Facial shape data were then fully preserved using a revolutionary analytical package i.e. geometric morphometrics. The MeshMonk toolbox in MATLAB was used to ensure homology (i.e., point-to-point correspondence) for facial landmarks among all target faces. The method rapidly captured high-dimensional facial configurations while avoiding manual digitisation errors to realise “high-throughput phenotyping” as in the study title. After rigid and non-rigid registration, each target face was represented by a spatially dense point cloud consisting of 7,160 3D facial landmarks. 3D facial images, Height, weight and BMI z-scores of 2874 Bantu Africans (1630 females and 1244 males) aged 6 - 18 years were further obtained and Gaussian kernel-weighted partial least squares regression was applied to establish non-linear trajectories of facial centroid size (CS). Bandwidth of the Gaussian kernel determined the weights of observations when predicting CS. Larger bandwidth allowed distant observations to have larger modelling weights, and as a result the model became more linear. Repeated grid search suggested an optimal bandwidth of 1.15 for females and 0.50 for males. Bandwidth of 1.15 was chosen for modelling of both sexes to be conservative about the non-linear trends and to ensure comparability of both sexes. To ensure stable predictions of facial CS, predictions were restricted to 8 to 15 years of age so that the summed weights for individuals aged above and below any age at prediction are comparable (ratio not less than 0.4). The multivariate linear regression model Shape was applied to establish facial shape developmental trajectories. Original genotypic data in the format of .ped and .map files were extracted from the extant database and converted into .bim, .bed, and .fam files using PLINK for further analyses. 4. Data analysis The pairwise Covariance Ratio (CR) coefficient was computed for all landmarks, resulting in a squared similarity matrix that reflected the strength of association among facial landmarks. The modularity.test function of the geomorph package in R was used for CR coefficient estimation. Hierarchical spectral clustering was then performed to partition the face into global-to-local modules. This clustering was performed hierarchically such that each of the two clusters are further bifurcated stepwise up to five levels of hierarchy. (Objective 1) ANCOVA was performed to investigate statistical significance involving the interaction effect based on Procrustes distances among observations through 10,000 permutation iterations of residual randomisation. Sex differences in the rate of facial shape development, a high-dimensional vector characterised by magnitude and direction, were investigated using the Procrustes ANCOVA model. The analysis was performed using the lm.rrpp and pairwise function in RRPP (version 1.3.1) in R. The developmental trajectory of the magnitude of sex difference in model-predicted facial shape, quantified through Procrustes distance, was modelled using a generalized additive model with penalised thin plate regression splines. Procrustes variance, the sum of squared Procrustes distance of individuals from the model-predicted mean shape divided by group size, was used to quantify the magnitude of facial shape variation. Individuals were binned into 1-year age groups of from 6 to 18 years of age for estimation and pairwise comparison of Procrustes variance. The pairwise function in RRPP was used for analysis with 10,000 permutations for statistical evaluation. GAM was used to model the developmental trajectories of Procrustes variance. Developmental trajectories of facial phenotypic covariance matrix were established in order to investigate changes in facial shape covariance structure. Individuals were categorised into age-by-sex groups based on age intervals. The matrix of pairwise squared Riemannian distance of covariance matrices across groups was ordinated using principal coordinate analysis to establish developmental facial phenotypic covariance matrix trajectories. Relative PCA was performed based on the phenotypic covariance matrix in order to identify developmentally constrained and diversified facial features. The vcvComp R package (version 1.0.2) was used for analysis. The RElative STrength of Relative Eigenvectors (RESTORE) was developed to evaluate the proportion of shape variation described by relative eigenvectors. Low RESTORE score indicates that relative eigenvectors trivially explain shape variation. For visualisations in this study, colour mesh of local deformations and superimposed facial meshes illustrating relative landmark displacement are used to denote the magnitude of local deformations and their morphological effects. Local deformations were calculated using the localmeshdiff function in the Arothron package in R. (Objectives 2 and 3) For annotation of genes associated with identified loci, genes 500 kb upstream and downstream of the replicated SNPs were identified using the UCSC Genome Browser. Literature-based annotation of these genes was performed based on articles retrieved from PubMed. The OMIM database was searched for syndromes associated with the annotated genes. Gene Ontology term enrichment analysis was performed with Genomic Regions Enrichment of Annotations Analysis to interrogate the biological processes, cellular components, and molecular functions associated with the annotated genes. (Objective 4) # To what extent the project objectives have been achieved: The project objectives have been completely achieved.

17102620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102620.value: A total of 63 facial modules covering stepwise focused facial regions were generated to enable us to explore the genetic effects of SNPs from global to local facial regions. (Conference Abstract 1; Objective 1) Facial growth and development trajectories were developed with particular focus on identifying morphogenetic processes that lead to observed developmental shape changes. Procrustes ANCOVA suggested sexually dimorphic patterns of facial shape development (p = 0.0036). The forehead was relatively contracted during development in both sexes. The glabella region was more anteriorly displaced in females due to expansion in the region laterosuperior to the eyes. Nasal protrusion increased with development, which was found to arise from local expansion in the nasal alae and columella. Local expansion in the upper and lower labial regions resulted in forward displaced lips in both sexes, with the effect more pronounced in males. The lateral facial region corresponding to the underlying body of the mandible were developmentally expanded but were posteriorly positioned due to protrusive growth of surrounding structures. Generalised additive modelling of Procrustes variance suggested that facial variation decreased non-linearly with age (p < 0.05). Relative principal component analysis suggested that variations in facial outline shape were developmentally constrained, whereas nasolabial and mental regions, where developmental changes were significant, became morphologically diversified with development. In contrast to simple descriptive illustration of facial shape development, we gained transformative insights into patterns of facial shape development by analysing morphogenetic processes and variational properties. Our analytical framework is broadly applicable to morphometric studies on ontogenetic shape changes. (Paper 1, Conference Abstract 2, and PhD Thesis 1; Objectives 2 and 3) A novel measure of local shape that incorporates the magnitude and direction of local deformation was proposed. Correlation matrix constructed from this novel measure provided a solution to the conundrum of quantification of correlations of local shape in geometric morphometric. Hierarchical consensus clustering based on this correlation matrix yielded clusters with desirable morphometric and topological properties. An atlas of hierarchical structural organisation of the human face was established, which provided a reference facial atlas for multi-scale analysis of the morphology and genetics of human face. Genes 500 kb upstream and downstream of the replicated SNPs were identified. Gene Ontology term enrichment analysis performed with Genomic Regions Enrichment of Annotations Analysis identified no genetic variants associated with global-to-local facial feature. (Conference Abstract 3 and Patent 1; Objective 4)

17102620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102620.value: Our work approached geometric morphometrics through a deformation perspective. Our methods and findings shed light on future morphometric research on craniofacial structures and have implications more generally for the field of geometric morphometrics: (1) Patterns of craniofacial growth and development of multiple ethnic groups could be examined with reference to our methods. This would facilitate a comprehensive understanding of facial growth patterns of global human populations; (2) The proposed measure of local shape and the resulting topographic perspective of shape analysis pave the way for a new generation of research in geometric morphometrics. In the context of craniofacial morphological research, it is of interest to investigate developmental changes of topographic properties of craniofacial morphology. It is also of interest to gain deeper understanding of the morphological characteristics of craniofacial anomalies by comparing patients’ facial topographic properties with those of individuals without facial anomalies. (3) Genetic information could be leveraged to obtain genetically informed hierarchical facial clusters to provide insights into the genetic architecture of the human face. Genome-wide association analysis based on the identified facial clusters can be further investigated for novel genetic variants associated with facial shape.

17102620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102620.value: This study addressed three key limitations of previous studies on human facial growth and development: lack of detailed analysis of local morphological changes, a mere focus on changes in mean facial shape, and a restriction of analysis largely to European populations. By quantifying localised facial changes through deformation, this study provides a series of transformative insights into detailed patterns of facial development. This allows the present study to move beyond simple description of the observed changes to unveil the underlying morphogenetic processes shaping such differences. In addition, this study exploits state-of-the-art morphometric methods to comprehensively characterise changes in mean, variation and sexual dimorphism of facial shape. The analytical framework of this study is broadly applicable to morphometric investigations of ontogenies of shape in general. Finally, we leveraged a uniquely large sample to characterise facial development in an important population with distinct facial developmental patterns that may have important implications for various disciplines but which remains largely absent in facial growth studies.

17102920.label: Project Objectives
17102920.value: To validate that TRIF regulates circulating PCSK9 in gender-specific manner using tissue-specific knockout mice: We observed an increase in LDL levels and aortic lesions in female but not male TRIF-deficient atherogenic mice. In addition, a higher hepatic PCSK expression was detected in female global TRIF-knockout mice compared with wild type, and no difference was observed in male. We will first validate that the gender-specific effect on PCSK9 is mediated by the TRIF in liver. To explore the molecular mechanism of how TRIF regulates estrogen-inhibited PCSK9 secretion in hepatocytes: Although PCSK monoclonal antibody is available in the market for treating hypercholesterolemia, the molecular regulation of PCSK9 secretion remains unclear. We demonstrated that estrogen treatment inhibited extracellular but not intracellular PSCK9 expressions in wild type hepatocytes, and the extracellular PCSK9 level was oppositely induced by estrogen in TRIF-deficient cells. In this part of study, we will investigate the underlying mechanism. To investigate whether poly-I:C treatment inhibits PCSK9 secretion in ovariectomized female and male mice: Our in vitro data showed that polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid (poly-I:C) treatment can inhibit PCSK9 secretion in female hepatocytes in TRIF-dependent manner. We will examine the feasibility of using such small molecule to inhibit PCSK9 and eventually upregulate LDL receptor and decrease LDL level in vivo. The current anti-PCSK9 therapy using monoclonal antibody is expensive, and the use of small molecule targeting PCSK9 is noteworthy to investigate.

17102920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102920.value: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the number one killer worldwide. Difference in awareness on the prevention of CVD between genders is substantial. Women often pay less attention because of the belief of lower incidence of CVD in women before menopause. Physicians also initiate less aggressive treatments for female patients compared with male. However, since CVD is also an aging-related disease, the emphasis on the protective effect in younger population would be misleading. In fact, CVD is the leading killer for both male and female in population older than 65. Moreover, several large clinical trials have reported that estrogen replacement therapy does not show any benefits towards CVD in postmenopausal women. Estrogen was even shown to exert harmful effect for older menopausal women. These suggest that some critical factors are obligatory for estrogen-associated cardiovascular protection in young women. Thus, the current prevention and treatment for CVD may not be sufficient for women in older age. Understanding the gender-specific pathophysiology of CVD is key to develop effective therapeutic strategies for postmenopausal women. Our preliminary data show that knocking out one of the branches of Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling pathway, namely TIR-domain-containing adapter-inducing interferon-β (TRIF) aggravated atherosclerosis in female but not male mice. Such gender-specific aggravation was associated with increased LDL and circulating proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) levels. PCSK9 regulates LDL receptor degradation, and PCSK9 inhibitor, in the form of monoclonal antibody, has been approved for treating hypercholesterolemia which is the major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Estrogen treatment in hepatocytes inhibited PCSK9 secretion, but oppositely led to induction under TRIF-deficiency. Moreover, activation of TRIF pathway by using TLR3 ligand, polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid, also inhibited PCSK9 secretion in female hepatocytes. Taken together, we hypothesis that TRIF serves as a mediator of estrogen-regulated PSCK9 secretion. In this project, we are going to investigate the underlying mechanism of how TRIF facilitates such effect of estrogen, and to explore the feasibility of using small molecule to activate TRIF pathway to inhibit PCSK9 secretion. The findings of our study will help to understand the gender-specific regulation of PCSK9 secretion, thus to explore other alternatives to inhibit circulating PCSK9 thus decrease LDL level. It will provide additional insight of how female-specific physiology affect disease development. 心血管疾病是全球的頭號死亡殺手，但心血管疾病的預防意識在不同性別群體之間卻存在較大差異。絕經前，女性心血管疾病發病率低於男性，這一現象使得很多女性減少了對心血管疾病發生的警惕。另一方面，臨床醫生對女性患者的治療較男性患者更趨保守。由於心血管疾病屬於老齡化相關疾病，是65歲以上老年男性和女性死亡的主要原因，故而強調年輕群體預防心血管疾病的發生容易產生誤導。此外，一些大型臨床試驗顯示雌激素替代治療對預防更年期女性心血管疾病的發生沒有獲益，甚至有些研究認為雌激素對更年期女性反而有害。這表明，在年輕女性中，雌激素相關的心血管保護作用存在一些關鍵因素。鑑於當前老年女性心血管疾病的預防與治療方法尚不夠充分，開展對性別相關心血管疾病的病理生理機制的研究，對於拓展罹患心血管疾病的更年期女性患者的治療方法至關重要。我們的前期研究發現， Toll樣受體（TLR）信號通路上的一個分子，含TIR結構域的銜接子誘導干擾素-β（TRIF），在動物模型上敲除後加劇了雌鼠動脈粥樣硬化損傷，同時，低密度脂蛋白（LDL）和外周血中前蛋白轉化酶枯草桿菌蛋白酶Kexin-9型（PCSK9）水平升高，但雄鼠不受影響。 PCSK9參與調節LDL受體的降解，作為PCSK9抑製劑的一種單克隆抗體，已被批准上市用於治療高膽固醇血症，高膽固醇血症是心血管疾病發生的主要風險因素。我們的前期研究還發現使用雌激素干預肝細胞能抑制PCSK9 的分泌，但在TRIF敲除之後則會誘導肝臟分泌PCSK9。此外，通過TLR3的配體（聚肌胞苷酸，Poly I:C）激活TRIF通路亦可抑制雌鼠肝臟分泌PCSK9。綜上，我們推測TRIF可介導雌激素調控PCSK9的分泌。在這項研究中，我們將深入研究TRIF介導雌激素產生這種保護作用的潛在機制及通過小分子激活TRIF通路從而抑制PCSK9分泌的可行性。這一研究結果將有助於理解肝臟分泌PCSK9的性別特異性調控，以尋找其它替代製劑減少外周血PCSK9，進而降低LDL水平，為探究女性這一性別因素如何影響心血管疾病的發展提供一些新的見解。

17102920.label: Realisation of objectives
17102920.value: Objective 1: To validate that TRIF regulates circulating PCSK9 in gender-specific manner using tissue-specific knockout mice. As mentioned in the mid-term report, we successfully generated hepatocyte-specific TRIF knockout (Hep-TrKO) mice. Triffl/f and Trif fl/Abcre (Hep-TrKO) mice were fed either a normal chow diet (NCD) or a Western diet (WD) for 20 weeks. Physiological parameters, including body weight, fat mass, lean mass, fasting blood glucose, and various organ weights, were similar across different genders and genotypes. Under the NCD for 8 weeks, we observed significantly lower serum PCSK9 levels in male Hep-TrKO mice compared to Triffl/fl mice, while no such difference was observed in females. However, this subtle difference did not lead to a significant increase in LDL-C levels. In contrast, after 20 weeks on the WD, female Hep-TrKO mice exhibited significantly higher serum PCSK9 levels compared to Triffl/f controls (97.2 ± 21.3 ng/ml vs 47.2 ± 28.9 ng/ml, p = 0.006), whereas this difference was not observed in male mice. Additionally, females, in general, had lower serum PCSK9 levels compared to males. When evaluating the corresponding lipid profiles, no differences were found in total cholesterol, total triglycerides, or HDL-C levels between Triffl/f and Hep-TrKO mice of either gender. However, as expected, female Hep-TrKO mice had higher LDL-C levels compared to Triffl/f mice, while no such increase was observed in the male mice. Overall, these results validate that TRIF in hepatocytes regulates circulating PCSK9 in a gender-specific manner. Objective 2: To explore the molecular mechanism of how TRIF regulates estrogen-inhibited PCSK9 secretion in hepatocytes Next, we examined the mRNA and protein levels of PCSK9 in Triffl/fl and Hep-TrKO mice. We observed a significantly higher hepatic Pcsk9 mRNA level in female Hep-TrKO mice, but not in males. However, we only noted a trend toward higher PCSK9 protein levels in the female liver, which did not reach statistical significance. This may be due to the fact that PCSK9 is a secreted protein, and the in vivo measurements may not have captured transient increases in liver expression. In our preliminary data, we demonstrated that neither estrogen nor poly-I:C (a dsRNA mimetic used to stimulate the TLR3/TRIF pathway) alone stimulated PCSK9 mRNA expression in female murine hepatocytes. However, when combined, these factors showed a synergistic effect, leading to upregulation of PCSK9. This synergistic effect was found to be TRIF-dependent. To improve the clinical translatability of our findings, we used human hepatocytes (HepG2) to further investigate the underlying mechanism. While poly-I:C treatment alone decreased PCSK9 mRNA levels in a dose-dependent manner, 17β-estradiol, the active form of estrogen, had the opposite effect, increasing PCSK9 mRNA levels. Pre-treatment with poly-I:C in HepG2 cells significantly blocked the 17β-estradiol-induced increase in PCSK9 mRNA levels. Although this result differs from what we initially proposed in the grant application, it is consistent with the findings in the mouse model, where TRIF is necessary for suppressing PCSK9 levels. Since the estrogen receptor (ER) is a transcription factor, it is possible that ER acts as a co-activator of PCSK9 transcription. Additionally, the downstream signaling of TLR3/TRIF involves activation of transcription factors, which may act as co-suppressors of PCSK9 transcription. Objective 3: To investigate whether poly-I:C treatment inhibits PCSK9 secretion in ovariectomized female and male mice In this objective, we aim to explore the clinical translatability of poly-I:C as a potential treatment to reduce atherosclerotic lesion development by decreasing PCSK9 levels. To investigate this, we designed an experiment to treat both male and female mice, with or without ovariectomy, using oral poly-I:C in conjunction with a Western diet. However, we have encountered challenges in establishing the ovariectomy model in mice and are currently seeking collaboration to assist with this (see collaboration via research output #4). While awaiting the establishment of the ovariectomy model, we successfully obtained human liver tissues from both genders (see research output #1). These tissues will undergo confocal microscopy to examine the localization of TLR3, TRIF, and estrogen receptors. We anticipate that these results will provide valuable insights into the interactions between these three proteins and their role in PCSK9 transcription. Additionally, we have analyzed the proteomics and transcriptomes of liver tissues from male and female mice (samples from the control group of research output #2), which will serve as a comparison to data obtained from human liver samples. Furthermore, we have explored various strategies for achieving liver-specific delivery of poly-I:C via oral administration, drawing on current knowledge of gut microbial constituent entry (research output #3). Once the ovariectomy model is established, we plan to test different approaches for liver-targeted delivery of poly-I:C.

17102920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102920.value: Our study demonstrated that TRIF plays a protective role in atherosclerotic lesion development by reducing PCSK9 production, with this effect being sex-specific in females. After 20 weeks on a Western diet, female hepatocyte-specific TRIF knockout (Hep-TrKO) mice exhibited significantly higher serum PCSK9 levels compared to controls, while no such difference was observed in males. These elevated serum PCSK9 levels were accompanied by increased LDL-C levels in the female mice, while other lipid profiles remained unchanged. The increased PCSK9 levels were linked to higher PCSK9 transcription in the liver of female Hep-TrKO mice. In the human hepatocyte model (HepG2), poly-I:C treatment alone reduced PCSK9 mRNA levels, while 17β-estradiol increased these levels. Notably, poly-I:C treatment blocked the 17β-estradiol-induced increase in PCSK9 mRNA, aligning with the findings in the mouse model and suggesting that poly-I:C could be a potential therapeutic approach to suppress PCSK9 levels.

17102920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102920.value: There are several future developments based on the current findings: Molecular mechanism: • Identifying sex-specific cofactors or transcriptional regulators that modulate PCSK9 expression in response to TRIF signaling. • Examine the broader role of TRIF-mediated immune signaling in atherosclerosis development, particularly in relation to other inflammatory mediators. Human studies: • Validate the findings in human subjects to assess whether TRIF’s protective role and its interaction with PCSK9 are conserved across species. (The human samples used in Research Output#1 and #4 can be used for further studies.) Therapeutic explorations: • Investigate the broader impact of poly-I:C treatment on lipid metabolism and atherosclerosis progression, • Evaluate the therapeutic potential of poly-I:C or similar compounds in reducing PCSK9 levels in both preclinical and clinical settings. Sex-specific studies: • Investigate whether hormone replacement therapies in postmenopausal females influence TRIF-PCSK9 pathways and lipid metabolism. • Examine the relationship between serum PCSK9 levels, TRIF expression, and sex hormone levels in humans with atherosclerosis • Study how sex-specific immune responses influence the development of atherosclerosis and interact with lipid metabolism pathways.

17102920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102920.value: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading global cause of death, yet awareness of its prevention varies significantly between genders. Many women overlook prevention, mistakenly believing that CVD affects them less before menopause, while physicians also tend to provide less aggressive treatment for women. However, CVD becomes a major cause of death in both genders after the age of 65, and estrogen replacement therapy has shown no benefit for postmenopausal women. This underscores the importance of understanding gender-specific factors in CVD, particularly in older women. Our research indicates that disrupting the TRIF pathway in the liver of female mice leads to increased levels of LDL and PCSK9. PCSK9 regulates the degradation of LDL receptors, and its inhibition with monoclonal antibodies is an established treatment for hypercholesterolemia. Estrogen stimulates PCSK9 secretion in hepatocytes, but activation of the TRIF pathway by poly-I:C reverses this effect. We propose that small molecules structurally similar to poly-I:C, which activate the TRIF pathway, could be a promising therapeutic strategy to reduce LDL levels in women. These findings will contribute to a better understanding of gender-specific cardiovascular disease mechanisms and aid in the development of more effective treatments for women.

17103020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103020.value: Major depressive episode is associated with significant distress, suicidality, and functional impairment. Delayed, incomplete, and nonresponse to pharmacotherapy are common. Chronotherapeutics, based on the principles of circadian rhythm organization, are proven to be safe and have a rapid onset of antidepressant action. Combination of total sleep deprivation, sleep phase advance, and bright light therapy (known as triple chronotherapy) is advantageous in term of sustained effectiveness. In view of the methodological limitations in previous studies and a paucity of circadian and genetic data, we propose to conduct a randomized, sham-controlled study to examine the efficacy, safety, and clinical, circadian, and genetic markers of triple chronotherapy for non-seasonal depression. Ninety-six patients will be recruited from a regional teaching hospital and block-randomized at a ratio of 2:1 to triple chronotherapy or sham chronotherapy. The estimated effect size is 0.7 and the use of 2:1 allocation ratio aims at increasing statistical power. Early sleep deprivation for 2 hours (bedtime between 12 am to 5 am), regular sleep schedule, and dim light (50 lux) will be used as sham controls for total sleep deprivation, 3-day sleep phase advance, and bright light (10,000 lux). Major inclusion criteria are current major depressive episode according to the DSM-5, absence of hypomanic or mixed symptoms, and ≥ 22 points on Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS). For safety purposes, severe agitation, marked psychotic symptoms, high suicidality, history of epilepsy and chronic eye diseases, and using photosensitizing drugs are the exclusion criteria. To reduce the influence of concomitant pharmacological treatment, subjects’ medications will be kept unchanged for at least 2 weeks prior to baseline (Day 0) until Day 7. To ensure treatment fidelity, inpatient monitoring during the treatment period (Day 0 to Day 4) will be arranged. Assessments will be conducted at screening and Day 0, 1, 2, 4, and 7. Primary outcome is the total MADRS score as MADRS is sensitive to change and can be administered for a recall period of 24 hours. Secondary outcomes (e.g., suicidality) and safety assessments (e.g., manic switch) will be included. Clinical, circadian, and genetic markers, such as chronotype, sleep-wake pattern (3-week sleep diary and actigraphy), diurnal mood variation, dim light melatonin onset (using salivary samples), circadian clock gene expression (using hair follicle cells) and genotype (using Infinium Asian Screening Array BeadChip), will be assessed. 17103320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103320.value: Spexin (SPX）是一種由GalR2/3受體介導的多功能神經肽，也是魚類新發現的飽食因子。在金魚肝臟中SPX的表達可以由胰島素誘導，從而引起於進食後的飽食反應。在我們利用金魚進行的前期研究中，我們發現（i）食物攝入後可提升金魚血漿中胰島素，SPX，生長激素（GH）和胰島素樣生長因子I（IGF-I）的水平，同時也引起垂體GH和肝臟SPX以及IGF-I轉錄本的增加，（ii）胰島素處理可降低金魚腦細胞中生長激素抑制素的轉錄本水平，同時亦上調金魚垂體細胞中GH分泌以及肝臟中SPX和IGF-I mRNA表達，（iii）在金魚肝細胞中GH的誘導可以提高SPX，IGF-I和GalR2 mRNA的水平，但這些反應可以被抑制JAK2和STAT5而阻斷，（iv）IGF-I可以有效地刺激金魚肝細胞中的SPX基因表達/轉錄并且快速磷酸化ERK1/2和Akt激酶，以及（v）SPX可以通過GalR2偶聯激發的PKA，PKC和Ca2+信號誘導金魚肝細胞中的胰島素mRNA表達。總的而言，我們的發現意味著胰島素除了在金魚肝臟中直接誘發SPX表達外，還可以通過在中樞和垂體水平發揮對GH/IGF軸的間接調控以提升SPX信號。同時，於肝臟中GH對GalR2的上調連同SPX誘導的胰島素表達可能會形成一個能在肝臟水平放大由進食引起的SPX信號的正反饋迴路。為測試上述假設，動物活體實驗與相應細胞的體外培養將用以：（i）揭示參與胰島素對肝臟SPX調節的GH/IGF控軸各組成部分的功能作用和信號轉導，（ii）探查GH和IGF誘導的SPX表達/轉錄的機制以及肝臟中產生的胰島素信號對SPX的正反饋效應，特別是通過GH對GalR2的上調來增強SPX敏感性，並通過SPX激活胰島素在肝臟中表達以增加刺激強度。我們的研究不僅將闡明胰島素對SPX調節的新機制，還將為魚類模型中的攝食與生長激素調控軸之間的功能交聯提供一個新的研究方向。

17103320.label: Realisation of objectives
17103320.value: (1) In goldfish, spexin (SPX) can act as a satiety factor and its expression in the liver can be induced by insulin signal triggered by glucose uptake after feeding. Since insulin & insulin-like growth factor (IGF-I) are structurally related and exhibit cross-reactivity at the receptor level, growth hormone (GH) & IGF-I signals from the somatotropic axis are predicted to play a role in SPX regulation in fish model. In our study, food intake in goldfish induced postprandial rises in plasma glucose, insulin, SPX, GH & IGF-I with parallel increases of GH mRNA in the pituitary and SPX & IGF-I transcripts in the liver. In goldfish with IP injection of insulin, transient rises of plasma GH & SPX were noted with concurrent elevations of pituitary GH and hepatic SPX & IGF-I mRNA. Transcript expression of IGF-I induced by insulin were also observed in goldfish liver cell culture and insulin co-treatment could enhance GH stimulation of SPX & IGF-I expression at the hepatic level. In goldfish pituitary cells, insulin-induced GH release but not GH gene expression. In goldfish brain cells prepared from the hypothalamus, insulin could stimulate gene expression of the GH-releasing factors in goldfish including sGnRH, cGnRH-II & PACAP with a concurrent drop of the GH-release inhibitor SRIF and the opposite was true with removal of insulin from the serum substitute used in the culture medium. As a whole, our findings reveal that, besides the direct effect of insulin on SPX expression in goldfish liver, insulin can also induce hepatic expression of SPX indirectly by recruiting GH & IGF-I signals via modulations occurring at multiple levels in the somatotropic axis. The combined effect of GH & IGF-I with subsequent enhancement of the stimulatory effect by insulin is believed to play a key role in hepatic expression of SPX in fish model. (2) To shed light on the role of somatotropic axis on SPX regulation at hepatic level, goldfish liver cells were used to examine the effects of GH & IGF-I on SPX expression. In our cell model, similar to insulin, IGF-I could increase SPX mRNA & this stimulatory effect was mediated by insulin receptor (InsR) and to a lower extent via IGF-I receptor (IGF1R). IGF-I was also effective in causing MEK, ERK, P38 MAPK, PI3K & Akt phosphorylation and blockade of PI3K/Akt pathway and P38 MAPK, but not MEK/ERK pathway, could inhibit IGF-I induced SPX gene expression. Using RNA POL-II ChIP coupled to qPCR of SPX promoter, insulin & IGF-I were both effective in recruiting RNA POL-II to goldfish SPX promoter. In goldfish liver cells, insulin & IGF-I could also elevate both the mature RNA & primary transcript of SPX and the stimulatory effects caused by insulin & IGF-I were not additive. Using HEK293 cells transfected with LUC reporter carrying the 5’ promoter of goldfish SPX gene, insulin & IGF-I were effective in activating SPX promoter mainly through InsR coupled to MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Using 5’ deletion analysis, the responsive region sensitive to insulin & IGF-I induction could be mapped to position -860 to -700 of the SPX promoter. Our findings imply that IGF-I & insulin exhibit cross-activation at the receptor level, which can lead to transcriptional activation of SPX expression in goldfish liver via MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Similar to IGF-I, GH treatment could also increase SPX mRNA in goldfish liver cells via JAK/STAT, MARK & PI3K/Akt pathways and this stimulatory effect was partially reduced by InsR/IGF1R inactivation. These results suggest that, besides its direct action, GH can induce SPX expression in goldfish liver cells via local production of IGF-I. (3) Using 5’/3’RACE, goldfish GalR2, the cognate receptor for SPX, was cloned & notable signals of SPX & GalR2 were detected in the liver, suggesting the role of SPX as an autocrine/paracrine factor at the hepatic level. Of note, the liver was also found to have a high level of insulin expression, which is consistent with the idea of hepatopancreas in fish models. In goldfish liver cells, GH could elevate GalR2 transcript level along with its stimulation on SPX & IGF-I signals and parallel treatment with SPX could also up-regulate SPX & insulin gene expression at the hepatic level. Similar to the responses of SPX & IGF-I, GH-induced GalR2 expression in the liver was mediated by activation of JAK/STAT, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Furthermore, parallel treatment with insulin & IGF-I could also mimic GH-induced GalR2 expression & these stimulatory effects were sensitive to InsR/IGF1R inactivation or inactivation of MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. These findings suggest that GH & IGF-I from the somatotropic axis together with insulin signal caused by food intake can enhance the hepatic responsiveness to SPX, which may play a role on SPX-induced SPX gene expression observed in goldfish liver cells. Since GalR2 expression induced by GH was partially reduced but not totally negated by InsR/IGF1R inactivation, it would be logical to assume that GH-induced GalR2 expression in goldfish liver cells is partly mediated by local production of IGF-I. (4) In our study, goldfish insulin was cloned and its expression in the liver could be induced by food intake. IP injection of insulin was also effective in reducing foraging behaviors & food consumption in goldfish. In the same study, down-regulation of NPY & AgRP with parallel rises of POMC, CART, CCK, MCH & leptin expression were noted in the telencephalon, hypothalamus & optic tectum, which are the brain areas for appetite control in fish models. These results provide evidence that insulin can serve as a satiety factor similar to SPX in our fish model. For SPX-induced SPX & insulin expression at the hepatic level, these stimulatory effects were sensitive to GalR2 antagonism & mediated by AC/cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades in goldfish liver cells. Interestingly, GH co-treatment did not alter the insulin response triggered by SPX but notably enhanced SPX-induced SPX transcript expression in our cell model. In parallel experiment with removal of endogenous SPX in liver cells culture using immunoneutralization with SPX antiserum, basal levels of SPX & insulin transcripts could be suppressed while the stimulatory effect of GH on SPX expression as well as its potentiation on SPX-induced SPX expression was totally abolished. Our findings, as a whole, have revealed that (i) similar to SPX, insulin can also act as a satiety factor in goldfish in addition to its role in glucose homeostasis & as a functional link between food intake & SPX expression, (ii) a positive feedback loop is involved in SPX autoregulation in goldfish liver with SPX-induced insulin expression at the hepatic level followed by subsequent SPX induction by local signal of insulin, and (iii) SPX autoregulation in goldfish liver cells via reciprocal interaction of SPX & insulin signals can be enhanced/potentiated by GH & IGF-I signals from the somatotropic axis via up-regulation of GalR2 expression at the hepatic level.
