17103320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103320.value: The major findings based on our research using goldfish as an animal model can be listed as follows: (1) The postprandial rise of insulin can act on multiple levels to recruit GH & IGF-I signals from the somatotropic axis, which can then exert a direct stimulation on SPX expression at the hepatic level via JAK/STAT, MAPK and/or PI3K/Akt pathways and contribute to the satiation response mediated by SPX observed in fish model. (2) In goldfish, similar to the role of SPX as a satiety factor, hepatic expression of insulin can be induced by food intake and may contribute to insulin inhibition of foraging behaviors & food consumption mediated by differential regulation of orexigenic and anorexigenic signals expressed in brain areas involved in appetite control. (3) In goldfish liver cells, SPX can stimulate SPX expression along with a parallel rise in insulin signal and these stimulatory actions are mediated by GalR2 coupled with cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Together with insulin induction of SPX expression reported in our previous study, it would be logical to assume that a positive feedforward loop for SPX autoregulation may exist in goldfish liver and contributes to the satiation response after a meal in fish model. (4) In goldfish liver cells, GH can induce GalR2 expression via JAK/STAT, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways and this stimulatory effect is partly mediated by local production of IGF-I. The combined effect of GH & IGF-I signals can further enhance SPX-induced SPX expression at the hepatic level, suggesting that the positive feedforward loop for SPX autoregulation in goldfish liver is under the control of somatotropic axis.

17103320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103320.value: In our study, we only focused on IGF-I signal working downstream of the GH response triggered by insulin activation of somatotropic axis. Unlike mammals with IGF-I as the dominant form of IGFs, high levels of IGF-II are expressed in the liver of fish species and IGF-I & -II expression in fish liver cells can be up-regulated by GH from the pituitary. Therefore, it would be of interest to follow up our study by examining the functional role of IGF-II in SPX regulation by insulin & GH in our cell model. In our study with SPX promoter activity using HEK293 cells as the host cells, 5’ deletion analysis with goldfish SPX promoter has revealed that the responsive region for insulin & IGF-I induction can be located to position -860 to -700 of goldfish SPX promoter. Within this region, the binding sites for transcription factors including c-Fos, SP-1, HNF3, SRY, Oct-2, c-Myb & POU3 can be identified. To further investigate the role of these cis-acting elements in SPX promoter activation induced by insulin & IGF-I signals, additional studies with site-directed mutagenesis of respective binding sites (alone/in combination) coupled to parallel experiments with over-expression of target transcription factors are clearly warranted.

17103320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103320.value: Using goldfish as an animal model, we have unveiled the mechanisms underlying the postprandial rise of hepatic SPX caused by insulin signal after a meal, which constitutes a key component of the satiation response in fish species. In goldfish, besides insulin-induced SPX expression in liver cells, postprandial rise of insulin can also recruit GH & IGF-I signals via actions at multiple levels of the somatotopic axis, which can then trigger hepatic expression of SPX via JAK/STAT, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Interestingly, a positive feedback loop with local interaction of SPX & insulin is also involved. In this case, SPX can induce insulin production at the hepatic level followed by reciprocal stimulation of SPX expression via local insulin signal. These stimulatory effects are mediated by GalR2 coupled to cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. The “SPX autoregulation” observed in goldfish liver cells can be further enhanced by increasing GalR2 expression at the hepatic level via GH & IGF-I signals. These findings, as a whole, provide novel insights on the functional crosstalk between insulin & somatotropic axis in feeding control via SPX signal in fish model.

17103620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103620.value: 癌症是世界上最嚴重的公共衛生負擔之一。癌症患者除了身體上的不適外，通常還有很多嚴重的健康問題。近期，癌症患者的自殺問題引起了公眾的關注。眾所周知，癌症患者的自殺風險明顯高於一般人群，並且許多因素會影響他們自殺的決策過程。儘管有越來越多的證據支持癌症診斷與較高自殺率之間的潛在關係，但學術界對已自殺的癌症患者的獨特特徵了解甚少。此外，有關自殺的理論試圖通過討論絕望，社會孤立，感到自己是負擔等概念來解釋這種行為。這些概念或可應用於癌症患者，但尚無定論，并且其背後的機制尚不清楚。一些研究人員認為，癌症患者的自殺行為可能是理性的，因為他們仔細權衡了自殺帶來的收益和損失，並且決策過程不受情緒困擾的影響。癌症是香港的頭號殺手。近年來，罹患癌症的人數一直在增加。但是，目前尚無全面的研究來調查香港癌症患者的自殺行為。我们尚不知道香港癌症患者的自殺風險是否可以與其鄰近的亞洲國家比較，以及西方有關自殺的理論是否可以解釋香港癌症患者的自殺行為。同樣重要的是，我們要知道哪些因素會影響癌症患者的決策過程，例如醫療狀況，身體疼痛或情緒困擾等。這將會是首個針對香港癌症患者自殺行為的綜合研究。我們將會使用患者的醫療診斷記錄，死因裁判法庭的報告以及對癌症患者的採訪來了解患者的自殺問題，找出其動機，並了解其思想和行為背後的原因和機制。我們將同时使用定性和定量的分析方法来鞏固我們的發現。癌症患者的自殺行為是可以預防的。此研究的結果將對香港癌症患者的自殺行為帶來更深入及全面的了解。這些發現將為未來的教育，預防計劃和政策制定提供證據和見解。醫療及護理人員亦可以參考研究中找到的風險因素和機制，進一步預防癌症患者的自殺行為。資源也可以相應地分配去改善患者的生活質量。

17103620.label: Realisation of objectives
17103620.value: In this project, we aimed to comprehensively investigate suicide issues among cancer patients in Hong Kong. Five detailed objectives have been identified: (1) exploring the characteristics of the cancer patients who killed themselves; (2) investigating into the association between cancer and suicide among patients in Hong Kong; (3) examining the sociodemographic, environmental, physical and psychiatric factors, and disease comorbidities that contribute to suicide behaviors; (4) identifying the critical period of suicide among cancer patients; and (5) understanding the decision-making process and the reasoning of the suicidality among the cancer patients. We achieved all five objectives during the study period, resulting in four peer-reviewed articles, two presentations at international conferences, and one newspaper article. For objective one, we analyzed 15 years of Hong Kong Coroner’s Court reports on suicide (2003-2017), comparing the characteristics of cancer patients who died by suicide with those without cancer. We identified the differences between cancer patient who died by suicide and noncancer suicide cases. The study results was published in Psycho-Oncology in 2021. Objectives two, three and four were accomplished by collaborating with oncologists from Queen Mary Hospital and analyzing electronic medical records from the Hong Kong Hospital Authority (HA) Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS). We used a cohort design to follow cancer patients after their first inpatient admission, identifying potential suicidal or self-harm behaviors, and a case-control design to compare the medical histories of cancer patients who died by suicide with those who did not. We also conducted stratification analysis to identify potential differences by age group, gender and metastasis status. The research findings were published in Psychological Medicine in 2020 and the Lancet Regional Health-Western Pacific in 2021. For objective five, we initially planned face-to-face semi-structured interviews with cancer patients in Hong Kong to explore their decision making process regarding suicide. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we instead conducted a semantic analysis of suicide notes from the Hong Kong Coroner’s Court written by individuals with a cancer diagnosis. This analysis summarized significant reasons for suicide among cancer patients, and the results were published in Psycho-Oncology in 2022. We also disseminate our research findings on the importance of emotional and social support for cancer patients during the pandemic through a Chinese newspaper article in Ming Pao. 17103620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103620.value: This project resulted in four peer-reviewed research articles. Study one explored the characteristics of cancer patients who died by suicide. The results indicated that cancer patients who died by suicide, compared to those without cancer, tended to be older and less likely to live alone. They were more likely to use violent methods for suicide, less likely to have histories of physical and psychiatric problems, and more likely to express their suicidal intention before dying. Age also played a significant role in these differences between cancer and noncancer patients. Study two investigated whether clinical profiles and hospital utilization patterns are associated with suicide among cancer patients. It showed that overall, younger age, having metastatic or recurrent cancer, suffering from head and neck cancer, having psychiatric conditions, using opioid painkillers, and frequently visiting the emergency room or being admitted to the hospital increased the risk of suicide among cancer patients. In contrast, being diagnosed with liver cancer, having many outpatient visits, and spending a lot of days as an inpatient decreased the risk of suicide. Further analysis confirmed that young age and metastatic or recurrent cancer status significantly influenced the risk of suicide. Study three examined the risk of suicidal or self-harm behaviors among cancer patients within the first year of their inpatient admission. It found that the severity of cancer, a history of suicidal or self-harm behaviors, diabetes, and hypertension increased the risk of suicidal or self-harm in cancer patients. Age also played a role, with the highest risk around age 58, showing a U-shaped relationship. Interestingly, having previous psychiatric conditions did not affect the risk of suicidal or self-harm behaviors. The impact of these factors differed based on the patient's age and gender. The last study utilized suicide notes to understand the patterns in expressed reasons for suicide among cancer patients. This qualitative study found that suffering from physical disease was a major theme identified among cancer note-leavers across all age groups.

17103620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103620.value: This project highlights potential opportunities for further research and actionable steps to mitigate suicide risk among cancer patients in Hong Kong. Future research should explore the underlying mechanisms driving the higher suicide risk in younger cancer patients and those with metastatic or recurrent disease. Investigating the physical and psychological impact of head and neck cancers, opioid use, and frequent hospitalizations could provide deeper insights into tailored interventions. Additionally, qualitative interviews with cancer patients about their experiences and difficulties are required to identify potential risk factors for suicide. A proposed course of action includes developing targeted suicide prevention programs that address the unique needs of high-risk groups, such as younger patients and those with advanced cancer. Enhancing training for healthcare providers to recognize and respond to suicidal ideation, particularly in emergency and inpatient settings, is crucial. Implementing routine mental health screenings and integrating psychiatric support into oncology care can ensure early identification and intervention. Moreover, creating support systems for cancer patients that focus on managing physical pain, improving communication about mental health, and providing comprehensive palliative care could reduce the burden leading to suicidal thoughts.

17103620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103620.value: This project explored the risk of suicide among cancer patients in Hong Kong. It is the first detailed study of its kind in this area in Hong Kong. The study identified specific characteristics of cancer patients who died by suicide and examined various factors, such as social, physical, and mental health aspects, that might contribute to suicidal thoughts and behaviors. It also looked at why and how these patients decide to end their lives. The findings have led to the creation of a suicide prevention guideline tailored for cancer patients in Hong Kong. This project also provides valuable information that can shape future education and intervention programs, influence policy changes, and improve communication between medical professionals and patients. It highlights the need for better mental health support for cancer patients, helping families, healthcare workers, and society to understand and address their needs. By raising awareness about the mental challenges faced by cancer patients, the study helps ensure resources are directed to where they are most needed to enhance the well-being of these patients.

17103920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103920.value: In contrast to other tissues, the uterine endometrium undergoes dramatic remodeling and regeneration on a repeated basis during menstruation, pregnancy and parturition. For instances, the endometrium undergoes extensive morphological and physiological changes during embryo implantation in the uterus, involving attachment and invasion through the epithelium into the underlying stromal compartment. During pregnancy, the luminal endometrial epithelial cells undergo a epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), but mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) for endometrial stromal cells. Both EMT and MET have been under intensive study in the context of malignancy. These malignancy-related processes may lead to tumorigenesis if dysregulated during the remodeling and regeneration of endometrium. This proposal will provide insight how gene ZNF555, a recent evolution invention, modulates these malignancy-related processes in human endometrium. 與其他組織相比，子宮內膜經歷了劇烈的重塑，並在月經，懷孕和分娩期間反復進行再生。例如胚胎著床過程中，子宮內膜經歷了廣泛的形態和生理變化，包括附著和侵襲通過上皮進入下面的基質腔室。在懷孕期間，腔內膜上皮細胞經歷上皮-間質轉化（EMT），但子宮內膜基質細胞經歷間充質-上皮轉化（MET）。EMT和MET兩者與惡性腫瘤的相關性已得到深入研究。在子宮內膜的重塑和再生過程中，這兩者的失調可能導致腫瘤發生。該提案將探索ZNF555基因， 作為人類最近的壹項進化發明，如何調控子宮內膜惡性腫瘤的發生。

17103920.label: Realisation of objectives
17103920.value: We have successfully achieved the three objectives. 1. To characterize the tumor suppressive role of ZNF555 in endometrial tumorigenesis and the transcriptional repression of oncogenic CLDN9 by ZNF555 Focal deletion of ZNF555 in TCGA UCEC cohort We detected focal somatic copy number alterations (SCNA) on chromosome region 19p13.3 of 539 UCEC samples from TCGA dataset by GISTIC method. ZNF555 mRNA expression level was highly correlated with its copy number variation. The average expression of ZNF555 with copy number loss was significantly lower than its expression in SCNA neutral samples (p-value=5e-16, t-test). Patients with lower expression of ZNF555 expression (bottom 1/3) were associated with poor prognosis compared with those with higher expression of ZNF555 (top 1/3) (Log-rank p=0.009). CLDN9 was the downstream transcriptional target of ZNF555 We used both bioinformatics and experimental methods to identify ZNF555 targets. CLDN9 was identified as the top candidate of ZNF555 transcriptional targets. The cis-acting regulatory elements recognized by the multiple ZFs of ZNFs can be predicted with high specificity. We predicted the position weighted matrix (PWM) motif of ZNF555 by modeling the amino acids composition of the ZF domains of ZNF555 [32] (Figure 2a, b). Then we searched the putative ZNF555 binding sites on the human genome (hg19) with the PWM motif by using the MEME Suite 5.0.2 (cutoff p-value < 0.005). Totally, 270,788 ZNF555 binding regions overlapping with gene promoters were kept for the next step of analysis. Integrated analysis conducted here included ZNF555 regulon analysis, simple repeat mapping, master regulator rank, survival significance, and anti-correlation with ZNF555. All of the predicted ZNF555 targets were ranked by their anti-correlation coefficients with ZNF555 along with other aforementioned analyses. The top target CLDN9, a member of ZNF555 regulon, displayed a very strong oncogenic signature (Master-Regulator Analysis adjusted-p-value=1e-5). Higher expression of CLDN9 (top 1/3) was found to be associated with worse survival of the UCEC patients (HR=0.38, CI95=0.22~0.65, Log-rank-p-value=2e-4). The anti-correlation between ZNF555 and CLDN9 mRNA expression was further confirmed by 19 EC cell lines, and TCGA UCEC cohort (Pearson-cor=-0.355, P-value<1e-19). ZNF555 attenuated cell migration and proliferation through CLDN9 repression We hypothesize that ZNF555 may function as a tumor suppressor by repressing CLDN9 in EC. To test this hypothesis, we conducted transwell migration and colony formation assay upon ZNF555 overexpression or depletion by shRNA. Among the EC cell lines used in this study, qPCR test indicated that Ishikawa had the modest expression level of ZNF555 while MFE296 had higher expression level of ZNF555, whereas both cell lines showed comparable protein expression level by Western blot. And there were no ZNF555 mutations identified for these cell lines. Subsequently, Ishikawa cells were transduced with lentiviruses carrying cDNA of ZNF555 and/or CLDN9, and MFE296 cells were transduced with lentiviruses carrying inducible shRNA-ZNF555 and/or shRNA-CLDN9. The knockdown efficiency of both shRNAs were confirmed by Western blot. Overexpression of ZNF555 decreased the colony formation numbers and migration potential. Conversely, depletion of ZNF555 had opposite effect. Moreover, the repressive effect of ZNF555 overexpression on colony formation or migration potential was counteracted by CLDN9 co-overexpression. Similarly, co-knockdown of CLDN9 abolished the effect induced by ZNF555 knockdown. It is known that EMT is associated with greater metastatic potential. We tested whether ZNF555/CLDN9 regulates the EMT process in EC cells. The results indicated that the overexpression of ZNF555 led to induction of epithelial markers, E-cadherin, and reduction of mesenchymal markers, such as N-cadherin, Vimentin, and Fibronectin, and overexpression of CLDN9 counteracted the effect of ZNF555. Conversely, depletion of ZNF555 resulted in the reduction of epithelial markers and induction of mesenchymal markers, which were abolished by co-knockdown of CLDN9. Taken together, these experiments supported that the tumor-suppressive role of ZNF555 was mediated by CLDN9 in EC. 2. To characterize the role of ZNF555 in suppressing cancer stemness ZNF555 inhibits cancer stemness properties through CLDN9 repression The recurrence and heterogeneity of endometrial cancer can be attributed to the existence of a small population of cancer stem cells (CSCs). Firstly, we explored whether ZNF555 affected the stemness properties of CSCs of EC. EC cells overexpressing ZNF555 were cultured in serum-free (stem cell) media, and used in low-attachment sphere formation assay in vitro to test the role of ZNF555 in self-renewal of CSCs and maintenance of stemness-like properties. ZNF555 overexpression inhibited the sphere formation capability with reduced sphere size and number. On the contrary, CLDN9 overexpression augmented the sphere formation with increased size and number. Consistently, the expression of stemness-related genes were downregulated by ZNF555 overexpression or upregulated by CLDN9 overexpression. The NANOG promoter-driven GFP reporter system has been validated in isolation of endometrioid CSCs. Here, we used the reporter system to isolate the CSCs of Ishikawa cells. We compared the expression level of ZNF555 and CLDN9 in NANOG-positive versus negative cells by qPCR. ZNF555 exhibited lower expression in NANOG-positive cells, whereas the expression of CLDN9 was higher in NANOG-positive cells. Next, we overexpressed ZNF555 in NANOG-positive cells, which led to the decrease of CSCs population. However, the decrease of CSCs was blocked by co-overexpression of CLDN9, the downstream target of ZNF555. Moreover, the repressive effect of ZNF555 overexpression on the sphere formation was counteracted by overexpression of CLDN9. Together, all of these results demonstrated that ZNF555 negatively regulated the stemness properties through the downstream target, CLDN9, in EC. 3. To characterize the interaction between ZNF555 and corepressor CTBP1 and the effect on CLDN9 expression ZNF555 is physically associated with CTBP1 to repress CLDN9 expression CTBP1 generally interacts with ZNF protein to act as a transcription co-repressor. Here, we investigated whether ZNF555 interacts with CTBP1 to repress the expression of CLDN9. First, we tested the direct interaction between ZNF555 and CTBP1. Total protein extracts from Ishikawa cells overexpressing FLAG-ZNF555 (FLAG-epitope tagged ZNF555) and HA-CTBP1 (HA-epitope tagged CTBP1) were immune-precipitated with anti-HA, followed by immunoblotting with antibodies against FLAG. FLAG-ZNF555 was successfully detected. Reciprocally, HA-CTBP1 was readily detected after immune-precipitation with antibodies against FLAG followed by immunoblotting with antibodies against HA. These results supported the physical interaction between ZNF555 and CTBP1. To further test whether the transcription repression of ZNF555 on CLDN9 is mediated by CTBP1, ChIP-qPCR experiments were performed on CLDN9 promoter in Ishikawa cells. Soluble chromatins were immuno-precipitated with antibodies against ZNF555 or CTBP1. The result validated the binding of ZNF555 and CTBP1 at the promoter of CLDN9. Moreover, the repression of ZNF555 on CLDN9 expression was abolished when CTBP1 was depleted. The depletion efficiency of CTBP1 by shRNA-CTBP1 was also confirmed here. Similarly, the effect of ZNF555 overexpression on EMT markers was reversed by CTBP1 depletion. Similar results were also observed in other cellular assays, such as the luciferase reporter activity of CLDN9 promoter, cell migration, colony formation and sphere formation, in which the depletion of CTBP1 reversed the effect of ZNF555 overexpression. Collectively, these data supported our hypothesis that ZNF555 recruited CTBP1 to CLDN9 promoter to repress CLDN9 transcription, and the tumor suppressor activity of ZNF555 was dependent on CTBP1.

17103920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103920.value: Zinc-finger protein 555 (ZNF555) is a poorly characterized protein coding gene. Here, we reported that ZNF555 functioned as a tumor suppressor with focal deletion in endometrial cancer, affecting about 28.7% endometrial cancer samples of TCGA. CLDN9 was identified as the downstream target of ZNF555, which physically associated with the corepressor CTBP1 to repress CLDN9 expression. ZNF555 inhibited cell migration, proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, sphere formation, and the expression of stemness-related genes mediated by oncogenic CLDN9. ZNF555 played a critical role in maintenance of the apical-basal polarity in endometrial glandular epithelium, which was disrupted by ZNF555 knockdown or CLDN9 overexpression. Furthermore, the reduced expression of ZNF555 resulted in the increased cisplatin resistance, tumor overgrowth in xenograft tumor mouse model, and poor prognosis in endometrial cancer patients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of the involvement of ZNF555 in tumorigenesis and self-renewal of cancer stem cells.

17103920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103920.value: The aberrant expression of ZNF555 may make a significant contribution to chemo-resistance to cisplatin treatment. We found that ZNF555 reduction associated with alterations of cellular polarity, cisplatin resistance, and tumor growth in xenograft model. EC cells, such as Ishikawa, derived from glandular epithelium, can be induced to grow 3D-spheroids (organoids) reminiscent of endometrial gland in vitro. After staining of F-actin (a marker of apical polarity), the apical-basal polarity can be observed in these endometrial 3D-spheroids with F-actin enriched in central lumen side, and the disappearance of the polarity is an important morphological change during epithelial cancer development. Here, we found that the 3D-spheroids generated from Ishikawa cells with ZNF555 knockdown or CLDN9 overexpression displayed a decreased proportion of spheroids with apical/central F-actin staining, compared with control cells. This result demonstrated the opposite role of ZNF555 and CLDN9 in endometrial cell polarity. Next, we explored the effect of ZNF555 knockdown on cisplatin sensitivity in EC cells. As flow cytometry analysis shown, knockdown of ZNF555 increased the survival rate of Ishikawa or MFE296 cells upon the treatment of cisplatin, a commonly used chemotherapy drug. Moreover, subcutaneous murine xenograft model indicated that ZNF555 knockdown promoted tumor growth in vivo.

17103920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103920.value: Zinc-finger containing DNA binding protein (ZNF) is the largest transcriptional factor family in mammals with roughly 700 members. ZNF is tetrapod specific, and evolved recently in veterbrate lineage after genome duplication and diversification. The dramatic expansion of ZNFs in mammals is driven by positive selection, pivotal for mammals to establish its unique structure and better fitness to the environment. Recent studies have revealed that ZNFs are critically involved in many physiological and pathological processes, such as development, differentiation, and cancer. In this study, we found that the frequent loss of ZNF555 was significantly associated with human endometrial tumorigenesis. Patients with lower expression of ZNF555 expression were associated with poor prognosis. It is critical for us to understand the downstream targets of ZNF555, and the associated signaling pathways deregulated in patients with loss of ZNF555. We have identified CLDN9 as one of the downstream targets. However, it is not celar if there are other downstream gene targets of ZNF555 involved. The high-throughout sequencing technologies, e.g., ChIP-Seq and RNA-Seq, will be instrumental to explore these posibilties. Detailed characterization of the downstream targets and signalling pathways of ZNF555 will not only shed light into the gene regulatory network underlying human endometrial evolution and EC development, but also enable the identification of novel biomarkers and drug targets for prognosis and therapeutic intervention.

17104120.label: Project Objectives
17104120.value: To analyze the structural and biochemical basis of bromodomains as Kcr readers. To develop and validate structure-based inhibitors for the BPTF bromodomain.
rows: To analyze the structural and biochemical basis of bromodomains as Kcr readers.

17104120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104120.value: Posttranslational modifications (PTMs) of proteins are indispensable for regulating many biological processes. Recognition of histone PTMs by chromatin-binding protein modules ("readers") is a major mechanism for epigenetic regulation, typified by bromodomains that bind acetyllysine. Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is a distinct PTM on histones. So far, no research has been reported to support that bromodomain is a significant crotonyl-lysine “reader” due to lack of further essential characterization. Our preliminary investigation by means of integrative approaches demonstrated that the bromodomain of NURF complex subunit BPTF, a transcriptional factor, is an important crotonyl lysine reader on histones. This is the first time that a bromodomain is identified as a “reader” of endogenous histone crotonylation in cells. We plan to investigate other bromodomains for their potential Kcr readout capabilities by using structural and biochemical approaches. This investigation will broaden the scope of currently known Kcr readers. We will also develop and validate structure-based inhibitors targeting the BPTF bromodomain. As BPTF has been reported to promote tumor growth, the results may have potential therapeutic impact. 蛋白質的翻譯後修飾（PTM）對於許多生物學過程的調節是必不可少的。染色質結合蛋白對組蛋白PTM的識別 模塊（“閱讀器”）是表觀遺傳調控的主要機制，以結合乙酰賴氨酸的溴結構域为典型。賴氨酸巴豆酰化（Kcr）是一種獨特的組蛋白PTM。由於缺少進一步的表徵，到目前為止，尚無任何研究支持溴結構域是一種 重要的巴豆酰賴氨酸“閱讀器”。我們通過綜合方法進行的初步調查表明， 轉錄因子NURF複雜亞基BPTF的溴結構域是重要的組蛋白巴豆酰賴氨酸閱讀器。這是第一次識別溴結構域作為細胞內源性組蛋白巴豆酰化的“閱讀器”。我們計劃使用結構和生化方法調查其他溴結構域潛在的Kcr讀出功能。這項研究將擴大目前已知Kcr閱讀器的範圍。我們還將開發和驗證針對 BPTF溴結構域的抑製劑。由於據報導BPTF可以促進腫瘤生長，因此研究結果可能具有潛在的治療效果。

17104120.label: Realisation of objectives
17104120.value: Objective 1: To analyze the structural and biochemical basis of bromodomains as Kcr readers. Bromodomain-containing proteins have been reported as readers of acetyl lysine (Kac) on histones. Our preliminary data have demonstrated the BPTF bromodomain can act as a “reader” of crotonyl lysine (Kcr) on histones. Based on our microarray data, we have shown not only BPTF, but also other bromodomain-containing proteins such as PB1brd6 and BRD4brd2 could bind towards Kcr on histones. Thus, we planned to elucidate the molecular mechanism of how other bromodomains read the epigenetic code Kcr. We further screened and optimized conditions to co-crystallize PB1brd6 or BRD4brd2 with Kcr peptides to examine the interactions between the Kcr and the bromodomain binding pocket. Various lengths of proteins, different tags fused to the proteins and different digestion enzymes to remove different tags from the target proteins were attempted. Crystals were flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen before being carried to Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF) for X-ray diffraction and data analysis. However, the Kcr peptides could not be seen in the co-crystal structures. These results have negatively affected our understanding of the molecular basis of bromodomains as Kcr readers. Objective 2: To develop and validate structure-based inhibitors for the BPTF bromodomain. By utilizing a CRBN-based E3 ligase recruiting system, proteolysis-targeting chimeric (PROTAC) technology, we have successfully designed the first PROTAC degrader with high specificity and low toxicity targeting BPTF, which is named 8d. Inhibition of BPTF via 8d leads to an increase in the abundance of natural cytotoxicity receptors (NCR) ligands in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells, thereby triggering NK cell activation and effector function. Furthermore, our newly developed 8d has demonstrated its ability to enhance the antitumor activity of NK cells against HCC cells isolated from HCC patients' tumor tissues. A manuscript based on our findings is currently under revision at Molecular Therapy. The GRF fund has led to two publications, which are included in this report. (i) Liu et al., 2023 Nature Communication (ii) Fan et al., 2023 iScience

17104120.value: 1) We solved the crystal structure of a SbSOMT-resveratrol-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (β-NAD) ternary complex, a SbSOMT-resveratrol binary complex, and two ternary complexes reproduced with pinostilbene or pterostilbene (Nature Communications, 2023) 2) We performed crystallographic studies to gain insight into the molecular basis of SIRT3’s interaction with lactyl peptides by solving the co-crystal structures of H3K23la-SIRT3 and H4K16la-SIRT3 complexes (iScience, 2023).

17104120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104120.value: As a transcription factor and epigenetic regulator, BPTF has captured our attention as an attractive candidate for immunotherapy in breast cancer. Specifically, BPTF has been shown to upregulate HPA-1 expression while downregulating NCR ligand abundance on breast cancer cells, thereby modulating NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Our BPTF-degrading PROTAC reported here has been shown to enhance NK cell antitumor activity against HCC, further supporting our finding that BPTF may be a novel immunotherapeutic target for treating HCC. This work opens an avenue for using PROTAC degraders as a potential strategy to improve the efficacy of NK-mediated cancer immunotherapy.

17104120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104120.value: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) discovered on histones provide another layer of gene transcription regulation complementing cis-regulatory elements in our genes. As a transcription factor and epigenetic regulator, BPTF is an attractive candidate for immunotherapy, particularly in breast cancer. We have developed a BPTF-degrading proteolysis-targeting chimeric (PROTAC) that effectively activates and enhances the effector function of natural killer (NK) cells against primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells isolated from tumor tissues of HCC patients. Therefore, our findings provide a chemical/biological approach using PROTAC to enhance the efficacy of NK cell-mediated immunotherapy and ultimately offer potential clinical benefits to patients with advanced cancers.

17104220.label: Project Objectives
17104220.value: To estimate the infectiousness of asymptomatic infections from a household cohort study. To estimate and optimize the population-level effectiveness of household-based isolation and quarantine accounting for asymptomatic transmission.
rows: To estimate the infectiousness of asymptomatic infections from a household cohort study.
To develop a transmission model of a network of connected households in a population to quantify the impact of asymptomatic transmission in influenza epidemics.
To estimate and optimize the population-level effectiveness of household-based isolation and quarantine accounting for asymptomatic transmission.

17104220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104220.value: Background: Influenza virus infections cause considerable morbidity and mortality every year in Hong Kong and across the world. It is well established that a fraction of infections is asymptomatic, possibly even more than half of all infections, but their infectiousness is still unknown. If these cases are somewhat infectious, there are important implications for public health control measures, particularly for those aim to reduce transmission such as isolation of symptomatic cases. Purpose: We propose to conduct a comprehensive study using mathematical and statistical modeling to determine the impact of asymptomatic transmission on influenza epidemiology and control measures. We aim to estimate the infectiousness of asymptomatic infections from a household cohort study, in which test results of blood samples can be used to identify influenza virus infections in persons who were asymptomatic. Then, we will construct a model for the transmission dynamics within households incorporating the asymptomatic cases. Our transmission model will then be used to quantify the population-level effectiveness of household-based interventions, from a network of connected households with household size distributions based on census data. Methods: We will develop a household transmission model to reconstruct transmission pathways in households, to estimate the infectiousness of asymptomatic infections. Then, we will develop a population transmission model to reconstruct epidemic curves of asymptomatic and symptomatic infections, and estimate the risk of asymptomatic and household transmissions. Finally, we will apply the fitted population transmission model to estimate and optimize the population-level effectiveness of household-based isolation and quarantine, accounting for asymptomatic transmission. Data from eight influenza epidemics in 2009-2013 will be analyzed with these approaches to validate our approach and ensure our results are robust. Potential implications: This study proposes a novel methodology to estimate the infectiousness of asymptomatic infection, which fill an important gap on influenza epidemiology and control strategy, particularly for those interventions only targeting symptomatic infections. Rigorous modeling of the impact of infectiousness of asymptomatic infections on population transmission dynamics allows estimating and optimizing the population-level effectiveness of household-based isolation and quarantine. Public health policy for influenza control may need to be more aggressive and focus on reducing susceptibility, if infectiousness of asymptomatic infection is even a fraction of the infectiousness of symptomatic cases. This framework can also be extended to explore and optimize the impact of other public health interventions in the future. 背景：流感病毒每年都會在香港和全球導致相當多的感染和死亡。當中，有一半以上的病例可能是無症狀的，但它們的傳染性仍然未知。如果這些病例具有一定的傳染性，這對公共衛生控制措施病有重要意義。特別是對那些旨在減少傳播的控制措施，例如隔離有症狀的病例。 目的：我們採用數學和統計模型方法進行全面研究，以確定無症狀傳播對流感流行病學和控制措施的影響。我們的目標是利用一項家庭隊列研究的數據，以其中血液測試結果來識別無症狀的流感病毒感染。然後，我們將會建立一個家庭傳染模型來評估無症狀病例對家庭傳播的影響。基於 人口普查數據和家庭規模分佈，我們會利用傳染網絡模型來量化基於家庭的干預措施在群體層面的有效性。 方法：我們將建立家庭傳播模型以重建傳播路徑，以評估無症狀感染的傳染性。然後，我們將建立一個群體傳播模型同時重建無症狀和有症狀病例的流行病學曲線，和估計無症狀和有症狀病例的家庭傳播風險。最後，我們將應用在2009-2013的8個流感季節的數據去擬合的人口傳播模型，以評估和優化基於家庭隔離和檢疫的有效性，以驗證我們的方法並確保我們的結果可靠。 潛在影響：本研究提出了一種新穎的方法來估算無症狀感染的傳染性，填補了流感流行病學和控制策略的未知，尤其是那些僅針對目標人群的干預措施有症狀的感染。嚴格建模去估計無症狀病例的 傳染性對估計和優化基於家庭的公共衛生措施有重要影響。如果無症狀病例的傳染性不低，流感控制的公共衛生政策可能需要更加積極並著重於降低易感性。這個框架可以擴展以探索和優化其他公共衛生措施。

17104220.label: Realisation of objectives
17104220.value: All three objectives were realized. To achieve Aim 1, we analyzed the data from an influenza cohort study. In this study, sera were collected from all participants so that asymptomatic influenza virus infections could be identified. Additionally, home visits were triggered when participants reported symptoms, thereby enabling the identification of household transmission. We developed a statistical model to estimate the relative transmissibility of asymptomatic verses symptomatic influenza virus infection. In the model, both the force of infection from the community and infected household members were accounted for, using the surveillance data of influenza in Hong Kong. We also developed a data-augmentation Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach to infer unobserved infection times for asymptomatic infections, along with an additional reversible jump step to infer the infection status for individuals with missing information. As a result, all participants, including those with missing infection status, could be included in the analysis to retain the transmission dynamics within households. The model also adjusted for age group (children and adults). Our analysis included 727 households with at least one household member whose infection status was known, totaling 2515 participants. We aimed to estimate the relative infectiousness of cases with no symptoms versus those with at least one symptom (main analysis) and cases without acute respiratory illness (ARI) versus those with ARI, as these are two commonly used definitions of 'asymptomatic cases' in the literature. ARI is defined as having at least two of the following symptoms: fever (temperature ≥37.8°C), cough, runny nose, sore throat, headache, phlegm, and myalgia. The proportion of cases with at least one symptom is 68% in children, 60% in adults, and 64% overall. The proportion of cases with ARI is 52% in children, 40% in adults, and 46% overall. Almost all participants had a pre-season HAI titer <10 before the community spread of H1N1pdm09. The estimated probability of infection from the community during the entire pandemic is 33% (95% credible interval (CrI): 30%, 36%) for children and 12% (95% CrI: 10%, 13%) for adults. The estimated probability of transmission from a symptomatic case to another household member is 15% (95% CrI: 11%, 20%) for children and 5% (95% CrI: 4%, 7%) for adults. We estimate that children are 3.2 (95% CrI: 2.8, 3.7) times more susceptible than adults. The posterior probability that asymptomatic cases are less infectious than symptomatic cases is 0.82, with an estimated relative infectiousness of 0.57 (95% CrI: 0.11, 1.54). In an alternative analysis, the estimated relative infectiousness of cases meeting the ARI definition compared with cases without ARI is 0.41 (95% CrI: 0.07, 1.09), with similar estimates for other parameters. To achieve objectives 2 and 3, we analyzed the collected surveillance data, along with the results from aim 1. We used a stochastic agent-based model implemented in the Covasim framework, which is well-suited for simulating the transmission of infectious diseases among populations. We adjusted the transmission model and disease progression parameters to align with the specifics of influenza transmission. We used the characteristics of the Hong Kong population, including age structure and household size, in the preloaded data in Covasim. In Covasim, four distinct contact networks are generated, including households, schools, workplaces, and community environments. The probability of transmission of the virus from an infected individual to a susceptible individual depended on the contact network and the age of the individuals involved. To simulate the population size of Hong Kong with 7.2 million individuals, we used a rescaled approach that allowed us to simulate 72,000 individuals but estimate the transmission dynamics of 7.2 million individuals. To estimate the population transmission dynamics over six influenza A seasons in our study, we extracted the epidemiological parameters, including incubation period (1.5 days), infectious period (5 days), symptomatic probability (0.7), and probability of testing symptomatic cases (0.05 or 0.1). To fit the observed epidemic curve, we performed an automatic search for the optimal value of transmission probability under baseline conditions, assuming no interventions such as testing. We calibrated the model using the daily count of new cases during each of the six seasons. The curve count was constructed using the influenza proxy activity times the observed attack rate estimated by serology data in our cohort. Then, we applied the calibrated model to simulate the following test-isolate-quarantine strategy to determine the impact.  Strategy 0: Baseline, no intervention.  Strategy 1: Only symptomatic cases are isolated.  Strategy 2: symptomatic cases are isolated and all household contacts are quarantine. For each scenario, we estimated the daily and cumulative numbers of infections. To account for uncertainty, we conducted 50 replications in each simulation. We present the median estimates along with ranges across the 50 replications. We fitted the model to six epidemics, which are: 1) A(H1N1)pdm09 from July 5, 2009 to January 16, 2010 2) A(H3N2) from August 1 to October 16, 2010 3) A(H1N1)pdm09 from January 9 to February 26, 2011 4) A(H3N2) from March 11 to June 23, 2012 5) A(H1N1) pdm09 from February 17 to April 20, 2013 6) A(H3N2) from July 14 to October 12, 2013 The attack rate ranged from 6.9% to 24.3%, and the model estimates of the new number of infections and cumulative infections among the Hong Kong population in six influenza seasons showed a good fit with the surveillance data. We first assumed that asymptomatic cases are 50% less infectious than symptomatic cases. Compared to the baseline without interventions, when the test probability of symptomatic cases is 5%, implementing isolation of symptomatic cases (S1) can result in a reduction in the attack rate ranging from 0%-10% over the six seasons, when the effectiveness and compliance are the lowest (40% and 30%, respectively). When the effectiveness and compliance are the highest (80% and 90%, respectively), the reduction in the attack rate ranges from 23%-60% over the six seasons. Compared to S1, when isolation of symptomatic cases and quarantine of household contacts were conducted (S2), there are reductions in the attack rate ranging from 6%-17% over the six seasons, when the effectiveness and compliance are the lowest (40% and 30%, respectively). When the effectiveness and compliance are the highest (80% and 90%, respectively), the reduction in attack rate ranges from 37%-79% over the six seasons. The reductions in attack rate at different levels of compliance and effectiveness are in between the corresponding extreme cases. When the test probability of symptomatic cases is 10%, the reduction in the attack rate is higher compared to the corresponding scenario when the test probability is 5%. The results under the assumption of equal infectiousness of asymptomatic and symptomatic cases are similar to the main analysis.

17104220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104220.value: Our results are exciting in developing a novel method to estimate the relative infectiousness of asymptomatic versus symptomatic cases. The results regarding the Bayesian method to estimate relative infectiousness (Aim 1) have been submitted to PNAS and are currently in the first round of review. Manuscripts for publication about the results of agent-based modeling (Aim 2 and 3) are currently in preparation and should be of interest to high-impact general scientific journals. Further exploration should include developing a method to handle the potential misclassification of self-reported symptoms in estimations, in order to obtain more accurate estimates. In the agent-based modeling, additional strategies, such as age-dependent strategies, may also be tested. The modeling could be further improved by incorporating workplaces and schools, making the results even more realistic. Given that the sample size may not be large enough to yield significant results for the estimation of relative infectiousness, we plan to seek funding to conduct a similar cohort study. We are also considering collaborating with researchers who have similar datasets, in order to apply our developed approach to perform estimations.

17104220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104220.value: The infectiousness of asymptomatic influenza virus infection is important for informing control policy. The challenge is that asymptomatic infection could not be observed directly. This study has examined the relative infectiousness of asymptomatic verses symptomatic cases based on a large cohort with 700 households and 2500 individuals. We developed a novel statistical approach to overcome the challenge to estimate the household transmission dynamics. The results from our study demonstrated that asymptomatic cases are around half infectious compared to symptomatic cases. Based on this results, we further used an agent-based modelling approach to compare the strategy that only symptomatic cases are isolated (strategy 1), or additionally their household contacts are quarantined to prevent asymptomatic transmission (strategy 2). The effectiveness would depend on the compliance and effectiveness of isolation and quarantine. Compared to strategy 1, strategy 2 could further reduced the attack rate for influenza season by 6-17%, and 37-79% when the compliance and effectiveness are low and high respectively. Overall, we estimated that the relative infectiousness of asymptomatic verse symptom cases is 0.57, and suggested that further quarantine household contacts could reduce the attack rate, when the compliance and effectiveness of isolation and quarantine are large.

17104420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104420.value: Staphylococcus aureus, especially methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), is a life-threatening pathogen in hospital- and community-acquired infections. The golden-colored carotenoid pigment of S. aureus, staphyloxanthin, contributes substantially to pathogenesis by interfering with host immune clearance mechanisms but has a negligible impact on ex vivo survival of the bacteria. Agents blocking staphyloxanthin production may discourage the establishment and maintenance of bacterial infection without exerting selective pressure for antimicrobial resistance. Our recently discovered small molecule compound NP16 shows inhibition against CrtN, a key enzyme in staphyloxanthin biosynthesis pathway. NP16 treated S. aureus has increased the susceptibility of the bacteria to H2O2 and to human neutrophil killing. In acute mouse infection models, NP16 significantly decreased the staphylococcal loads in the spleens, livers, and kidneys. These findings have illustrated that CrtN plays a pivotal role in S. aureus infections. To further investigate the potential involvement of CrtN in chronic infections, we have conducted pilot in vivo mice experiments for preliminary assessment. We found that the deletion of CrtN severely affected the establishment of S. aureus chronic infection in animals. In the same pilot study, we have also verified that the deletion of a global regulator sigB could downregulate pigment production in S. aureus and slightly reduce the establishment of chronic infection, while the deletion of CrtN could substantially reduce the establishment chronic infection. Thus, understand the cross-talks between SigB and CrtN in sigB mediated chronic infection seem to be important for addressing the issue of S. aureus persistent infection. Our pilot study has demonstrated that the importance of newer chronic infection models to study and novel treatment strategies to control S. aureus persistent infection. Chronic infection models will be established in different cell lines and in mice, and the role of CrtN will be evaluated using deletion mutants. Cross-talks between CrtN and sigB in chronic infections will be studied using sigB mutants and CrtN inducible promoters. The inhibitory effects of NP16 and in combination of other antibiotics will be assessed in the chronic infection models. The proposed project is an attempt to investigate the role of CrtN in S. aureus chronic infections, and an approach to develop novel treatment strategies to combat this important human pathogen. 金黃色葡萄球菌，尤其是耐甲氧西林的金黃色葡萄球菌（MRSA）是一種可以在醫院內和社區傳播的，威脅生命的致病菌。金黃色葡萄球菌利用其金黃色的胡羅蔔素類的色素，葡萄球菌黃素，干擾宿主免疫清除機制而在發病中起重要作用。然而葡萄球菌黃素對與金黃葡萄球菌的體外生存沒有影響。抑制葡萄球菌黃素的產生可能阻斷細菌感染的建立和維持，同時並不會對耐藥性的出現產生選擇壓力。我們最近發現了一個小分子化合物，NP16，可以有效抑制葡萄球菌素合成過程的關鍵酶，CrtN。經NP16處理的金黃色葡萄球菌增加了對雙氧水和人中性粒細胞殺傷的敏感性。在一個小鼠的急性感染模型中，NP16顯著的降低了葡萄球菌在關鍵臟器，脾，肝和腎細菌載量。這些發現意味著CrtN在金黃色葡萄球菌感染中起到了至關重要的作用。為了進一步研究CrtN在慢性感染過程中的潛在作用，我們進行了一些預實驗表明，CrtN敲除菌株極大程度的影響金黃色葡萄球菌在小鼠體內建立慢性感染。同時，我們也驗證了SigB敲除之後，可以減少葡萄球菌色素的產生並降低慢性感染的發生。因此，探究SigB和CrtN的相互作用對於研究SigB對慢性感染和金黃色葡萄球菌持留性感染的過程的影響非常重要。我們預實驗的結果證明建立的慢性感染模型和全新的治療慢性感染的策略的重要性。我們將會在細胞和動物水平上建立慢性感染模型，同時我們會評估CrtN敲除對於慢性感染的影響。在慢性感染過程中，我們將在SigB敲除菌株中建立誘導表達的CrtN來研究CrtN和SigB的相互作用。然後，我們會對單獨使用NP16和抗生素聯合使用對於慢性感染的治療作用進行探究。本項目是對於探究CrtN在金黃色葡萄球菌慢性感染的作用的一個嘗試，也是針對這個人類的重要致病菌的開發全新治療策略的一個方法。

17104420.label: Realisation of objectives
17104420.value: For objective 1, Evaluating the contribution of CrtN in S. aureus chronic infections. 1. Both SigB and CrtN contribute to the persister infection in epithelial cells We have successfully created mutant strains for sigB and crtN, USA300-ΔsigB and USA300-ΔcrtN. Using A549 cells, we tested different bacterial strains' ability to cause persister infections. At first, we faced challenges replicating published results since we couldn't keep the cells alive during the 7-day culture with bacteria. We tried to eliminate extracellular bacteria using gentamicin, but the culture became turbid due to bacterial growth even with a concentration of 50-100 µg/ml. We tried different methods to optimize the conditions, such as using different bacterial strains, different growth phase of bacteria, different multiplicity of infection (MOI), gentamicin concentrations, media (gentamicin in HBSS), and replacing the media every 1-2 days. Despite our attempts, we could not keep the cells alive until we added lysostaphin and gentamicin. Additionally, we discovered that THP-1 cells couldn't be cultured long after induction with PMA, so we used Raw264.7 to test intracellular survival. 2. We have successfully established chronic infection in mice We observed that both crtN and sigB deletion significantly reduced bacterial load in A549 cells after 7 days, with a difference of around 1 log from the wildtype strain (9.02×10^4) to USA300-ΔsigB (3.24×10^3) and USA300-ΔcrtN (8.13×10^3) at the same MOI. The differences were significant, with a p-value of less than 0.0001 for wild type and USA300-ΔsigB and a p-value of 0.0009 for wild type and USA300-ΔcrtN. 3. S. aureus tends to form chronic infections in kidney We conducted multiple infections and obtained kidneys from mice at different time points, including day 1, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, and 42, for bacterial load and histology analyses. We observed bacterial load increased from approximately 10^5 per kidney on day 1 to 10^6 per kidney on day 7. It remained stable from day 7 to day 21 and gradually decreased to 10^4-10^5 from day 28 to day 35 before stabilizing until day 42. Histological data revealed inflammation in the kidney, with obvious abscess formation from day 7. The abscesses consisted of bacterial communities in the middle, surrounded by neutrophils. We observed bacterial budding out to the kidney surface from day 21, reducing bacterial load on day 28. Afterwards, a balance was established between the bacterial and immune systems in the kidney, resulting in stable bacterial loads. For objective 2, Investigating the role of CrtN in SigB mediated chronic infections. 1. we have successfully replaced the crtOPQMN promoter with tetO promoter in wildtype strain and sigB deletion strain Initially, we intended to use a hemin-induced promoter to replace the crtO promoter. However, hemin can have a systemic impact on gene expression, so we changed our strategy and opted for a constitutive promoter, tetO, to replace the crtOPQMN promoter. This promoter ensures that crtOPQMN is expressed continuously without being affected by SigB. We successfully constructed the plasmid pKOR1 with a 1 kb upstream - tetO promoter and a 1 kb downstream sequence, which we transformed into RN4220 before transforming it into USA300 and USA300-ΔsigB after sequencing. After a temperature shift, we selected colonies that turned orange on aTc plates and subjected them to PCR and sequencing. We observed that the promoter-replaced strain turned orange, while the wild type strain remained yellow, and the sigB or crtN deletion strains were white. We also tested the CrtN inhibitor LM32 against various strains, with an IC50 of approximately 30nM against USA300 and 5µM against USA300-terO-crtO and USA300-ΔsigB- terO-crtO, indicating that the promoter-replaced strains with overexpressed crtOPQMN. 2. SigB’s effect on persister is partially due to crtN Next, we investigated bacterial persistence in A549 cells. Using the same MOI for USA300, USA300-ΔsigB, USA300-ΔcrtN, USA300-terO-crtO, and USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO, we monitored bacterial load at various time points, including inoculation, 3 hours post-infection, 1 day post-infection, and 7 days post-infection. We observed that all groups had similar bacterial loads from 3 hours post-infection to 1 day post-infection. However, on day 7, we observed clear differences in bacterial load among the five groups: USA300 (9.02×10^4), USA300-ΔsigB (3.24×10^3), USA300-ΔcrtN (8.13×10^3), USA300-terO-crtO (9.48×10^4), and USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO (3.34×10^4). A comparison of USA300 and USA300-terO-crtO showed no significant difference, indicating that enhanced pigment production due to overexpression of crtOPQMN does not increase bacterial virulence or survival ability in epithelial cells. A significant difference was observed between USA300-ΔsigB and USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO (p=0.0003), indicating that the effect of SigB on bacterial persistence depends on pigment production controlled by SigB. While there was no significant difference between USA300 and USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO (p=0.39), bacterial load in USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO was relatively lower than in USA300. There was also no significant difference between USA300-ΔsigB and USA300-ΔcrtN, but bacterial load for USA300-ΔcrtN was higher than for USA300-ΔsigB. These results suggest that the effect of SigB on persister infection may be partially due to pigment production. 3. overexpression of crtN did not enhance the virulence of S. aureus We conducted a chronic infection experiment using a similar procedure described in the first objective. We infected mice with different strains, including USA300, USA300-ΔsigB, USA300-ΔcrtN, USA300-terO-crtO, and USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO, using the same inoculum as previously mentioned. After 28 days, we collected the kidneys for data analysis. We found significant differences between USA300 and USA300-ΔcrtN. While promoter-replaced groups showed increased bacterial load compared to USA300-ΔcrtN and USA300-ΔsigB, there were no significant differences between either USA300-terO-crtO or USA300-ΔsigB-terO-crtO and USA300. This further supports that pigment production does not enhance bacterial virulence but can complement the deletion of the SigB gene. For objective 3, Assessing the inhibitory effects of NP16 (CrtN inhibitor) in combination of antibiotics on S. aureus chronic infection models 1. LM32 showed moderate effect on intracellular survival of S. aures Our intracellular persister experiment on A549 cells revealed that the CrtN inhibitor LM32 showed a moderate effect on the intracellular survival of S. aureus. We tested LM32 in combination with gentamicin and rifampicin but found no synergistic effect in killing intracellular bacteria for gentamicin, while a slight synergistic effect between LM32 and rifampicin on day 3. 2. combination of LM32 and antibiotic in vivo To investigate the potential of LM32 in combination with antibiotics in vivo, we combined LM32 with gentamicin, rifampicin, or vancomycin. Similar to the in vitro experiment, there was no combinational effect between LM32 and gentamicin during acute infection model. However, LM32 combined with rifampicin or vancomycin showed an enhanced bacterial killing effect in the kidneys during the seven-day treatment course in the acute infection model. Since vancomycin is a suggested antibiotic in clinical use for MRSA infection, we tested multiple combinations in vivo, including lethal infections in mice and rats. We found the combination of LM32 and vancomycin showed a significant difference compared with LM32 or vancomycin mono-therapy in a bacteremia mice model. The combination of LM32 and vancomycin in chronic infection models led to a decreased bacterial load.

17104420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104420.value: 1. Prior to establishing a chronic infection model, we needed to set up an adherence and invasion assay, which we achieved using A549 cells. In our investigation into the impact of ampicillin on bacterial virulence, we discovered that ampicillin could increase bacterial attachment and internalization in A549 cells. Our findings were published in the journals called Antibiotics and microbiology spectrum. 2. We developed a chronic infection animal model and discovered that the type of bacterial inoculum used affected the infection's state. Using overnight cultured bacteria resulted in a more chronic infection, while using log phase bacteria led to acute infection formation. We discovered a compound SA558 specifically targeting bacterial chronic infection. Our findings were published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 3. Our study also established an intracellular survival model in macrophages, which we used to analyze changes in lipidomics during infection. In this study we found linoleic acid could enhance intracellular bacterial killing. Our results were published in Chemical Science. 4. In addition to the kidney chronic infection model, we developed a subcutaneous chronic infection model. Using this model, we determined that SaeRS is a crucial regulator of bacterial infection. After a 14-day infection, the nodule size of wildtype strain-infected mice remained at least 0.2 cm²; however, SigB had no effect in this type of chronic infection. SaeRS deletion significantly reduced nodule sizes and bacterial load. Our findings were published in Emerging Microbes and Infection. 5. We developed the pigment production inhibitor LM32, which had an improved anti-pigmentation effect and in vivo efficacy. When combined with vancomycin, LM32 showed a synergistic effect on S. aureus in both acute and chronic infection models in mice and rats, leading to a significant increase in mice survival. Our data were used to file a patent application, which has already been submitted.

17104420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104420.value: 1. In our animal experiment, we discovered that the use of LM32 to treat chronic infections led to earlier bacterial budding from kidneys compared to the vehicle group. This suggests that combining LM32 with antibiotics earlier in the infection course could enhance the combinational effectiveness and reduce the possibility of chronic infections. 2. Further research is needed to confirm and investigate the impact of LM32 on bacterial budding in the kidney through histology study. 3. In vitro cell assays cannot accurately replicate in vivo abscess conditions, since there are no immune cells to restrict bacterial growth. Establishing an organoid with immune cells to mimic kidney abscess conditions would provide a more reliable model for research purposes and yield more insights. 4. In previous research, SigB was identified as a key regulator for persister infections. Our study further demonstrated that SigB regulates pigment production, which is an essential aspect of SigB regulation. This discovery indicates that pigment inhibitors may be effective in controlling persister infections. Future research will concentrate on this aspect to promote the development of LM32 and its analogs for market use.

17104420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104420.value: The study aimed to understand how a type of bacteria called S. aureus causes long-term infections in the body. The researchers found that the pigment produced by the bacteria plays a key role in this process. They also discovered that SigB previously proved important key factor, modulate chronic infection through controling the production of pigment. By testing a pigment production inhibitor called LM32, they found that it could be used to prevent chronic infections caused by S. aureus and the combination of LM32 with vancomycin can be used to treat S. aureus infection. The significance of this study lies in its potential to pave the way for the development of new strategies to prevent and treat chronic infections caused by S. aureus. Chronic infections can be challenging to treat and can lead to severe complications. Therefore, finding new ways to prevent and treat them is crucial to improve patient outcomes. The study's findings could also lead to the development of new drugs that target the production of the pigment to prevent chronic infections caused by S. aureus. Overall, this study has significant value in advancing our understanding of bacterial infections and developing new treatments for chronic infections.

17104720.label: Project Objectives
17104720.value: Functional characterization of a positive regulator (a MYB protein) Mutant analyses have identified a MYB protein (LL304) as a putative positive transcription factor for tricin biosynthesis. DNA-binding, ChIP-PCR, and transactivation assays will be done to investigate its binding and activation of the promoters of tricin biosynthesis genes. ChIP-seq and RNA-seq will be conducted to identify more LL304-directly regulated targets which may be tricin transcription factors in lower hierarchical layers or structural genes in other metabolic pathways. Transgenic over-expression and CRISPR-Cas9 mutant lines will generated for selected genes, which are both LL304-bound and LL304-regulated, to conduct tricin metabolite and gene expression analyses. Functional characterization of a negative regulator (a RING E3 ligase) Mutant analyses have identified a RING E3 ligase (F26) as a putative negative regulator for tricin biosynthesis. Protein interaction, ubiquitination, degradation, and immunoblot experiments will be conducted to investigate whether LL304 is a direct target of F26-mediated degradation. An on-going yeast 2-hybrid screening effort is expected to be completed before the start of this project to provide more candidates for these protein experiments with F26. Transgenic over-expression and CRISPR-Cas9 mutant lines will be generated for selected F26-regulated/degraded proteins to conduct tricin metabolite and gene expression analyses.

17104720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104720.value: Flavonoids are an abundant major group of phytochemicals with important functional roles in plant growth, physiology, and development. In addition, food products containing high amounts of flavonoids are associated with a number of health benefits, such as anti-oxidation and anti-cancer properties. Tricin and related metabolites belong to a major class of flavonoids called flavones. They have been widely reported as healthy constituents in rice hull and bran. Meanwhile, accumulation of soluble tricin-derived metabolites in plant biomass is ubiquitous in the grass family which includes the economically important cereal crops. Recently, tricin was discovered to be a natural co-monomer with other polyphenolic monomers (monolignols) for cell wall lignin formation in grass species. Lignin is a complex polymer interspersed extensively with polysaccharides (cellulose and hemicellulose) in cell wall, forming a major barrier for biomass utilization. Our laboratory has been using rice as a model system to investigate flavonoid biosynthesis in monocot. Previously, we have successfully elucidated the key reaction steps for the formation of tricin, representing significant advances in understanding the evolution of this unique biosynthetic pathway which is widespread in grass species. Our recent work further demonstrated that disruption of tricin biosynthesis could alter lignin content and composition, resulting in improved yield of fermentable sugars from cellulose digestion. Importantly, neither biomass productivity nor grain yield was compromised. This proposed study aims to investigate the molecular regulation of tricin biosynthesis in rice. Preliminary studies have identified one positive regulator (a MYB protein) and one negative regulator (a E3 ligase) for detailed characterizations in this proposal work. The hypothesis is that the E3 ligase is involved in degradation of positive transcriptional factors such as MYB proteins during regulation of tricin biosynthesis. Results from this study will provide new insights into the largely unknown molecular regulatory mechanism of tricin production in the grass family. The identified and validated molecular components can represent novel targets to manipulate tricin biosynthesis in cereals and other grass species for different applications. For example, they can be utilized for metabolic engineering of edible tissues (e.g. endosperm) that do not normally produce the highly health-beneficial tricin-derived metabolites. In addition, they can be exploited for improving cell wall digestibility of grass biomass for bioethanol production through the modulation of cell wall lignin content and composition. 黃酮類化合物是豐富的植物天然產物，在植物生長、生理和發育中具有重要的功能。此外，高黃酮含量的食品對人類健康具有諸多好處，如抗氧化和抗癌特性。苜蓿素以及其相關代謝物屬於黃酮的一大類，它們作為稻殼和米糠中的健康成分被廣泛報導。同時，在包括重要經濟作物的禾本科植物, 其生物質普遍存在著可溶性苜蓿素衍生代謝物。近年的研究進一步表明，苜蓿素是可以與其它多酚類單體結合的共單體，一起聚合成木質素, 存在於禾本科植物細胞壁中。木質素是一種複雜的聚合物，散佈在於細胞壁的多糖（纖維素和半纖維素）中間，是生物質能利用極需解決的主要障礙。 本實驗室以水稻為系統模型，研究單子葉植物黃酮的生物合成。目前，我們已成功闡明了形成苜蓿素的關鍵反應步驟，這代表這我們在瞭解苜蓿素這一獨特生物合成途徑的進化過程方面取得了重大進展。最近的研究進一步證明，透過中斷苜蓿素的生物合成過程，能改變木質素的含量和組分，從而提高可發酵糖的產量，並且此過程對於生物量生產力和種子產量均沒有影響。 本研究的目的是探究水稻中苜蓿素生物合成的分子調控機制。我們初步發現一個正調節因子（MYB蛋白）與一個負調節因子（E3連接酶）， 當中的假設是E3連接酶參與了苜蓿素生物合成中相關正轉錄因子（如MYB蛋白）的降解過程。這項研究的結果將進一步揭示禾本科植物中苜蓿素的分子調控機制。經鑒定和驗證的分子組分可以用於調控穀類和其他禾本科植物的苜蓿素生物合成，例如，在不產生苜蓿素代謝物的食用組織（例如胚乳）中進行代謝工程，也可使用它們通過調節細胞壁木質素含量和組分來提高禾本科植物的細胞壁消化率，從而生產生物乙醇。

17104720.label: Realisation of objectives
17104720.value: Objective 1 To elucidate the molecular regulation of tricin biosynthesis in rice, we started on the characterization of R2R3-MYB genes showing co-expression pattern with the genes encoding CYP93G1, CYP75B4, and ROMT9 for tricin biosynthesis pathway as well as CYP93G2 and CYP75B3 for the competing flavone C-glycoside biosynthesis pathway. In silico analyses revealed a number of putative MYB-binding motifs in the promoter regions of these genes. A total of seven R2R3-MYBs were selected: LL303, LL304, M14, JX2, JX6, JX7, and JX8. They were subject to yeast 1-hybrid (Y1H) analysis and dual luciferase report (DLR) assay using tobacco leaves. Pairwise testings of each MYB candidate with 2-kb promoter region of each gene were performed. We demonstrated that both M14 and JX8 interacts physically with promoters of CYP75B4 and ROMT9 (Y1H data) while also activating their activities in DLR tobacco leaf assays. Meanwhile, some MYBs showed negative results in Y1H assays but positive results in some DLR assays, for example, JX7 activated the promoters of CYP93G2, CYP75B3, and CHI; LL303 activate the promoters of CHI and ROMT9; JX6 and LL304 both activate the promoter of ROMT9. These activations were likely due to participation of plant-specific partners which are not present in the yeast cells. Meanwhile, JX2 did not produce positive results in Y1H and DLR assays. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) were performed for M14, JX8, and JX7 with promoters of flavonoid genes which showed positive DLR results. M14 directly bound to the promoters of OsCYP75B4 and OsROMT9 through recognition of the AC elements (AC-I and AC-II) and SMRE motifs (SMRE2, SMRE3, SMRE5, SMRE 6); Jx8 recognized AC-I and AC-II for direct binding on OsCYP75B4 promoter whereas it recognized the AC-II motif on OsROMT9 promoter for binding. Meanwhile, Jx7 recognized the "AGTGGTAGGTAAC" motif in OsCYP93G2 promoter and the GATA motif ("AAGATAACA") in OsCYP75B3 promoter for binding. Together with the DLR data, these MYBs transactivate the respective gene promoters by direct binding to MYB-specific cis-regulatory elements. Simultaneously, transgenic rice plants were generated to mutate the individual MYB genes by CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis (2 different mutations per gene) or over-express the individual MYB genes. Transgenic lines were propagated up to T2/T3 generation for characterizations including metabolite profiling and gene expression analysis. Experimental characterizations were primarily focused on M14, JX8, and JX7. For M14, rice mutant plants showed significantly down-regulated gene expression of CYP75B4 and ROMT9 in vegetative tissues where substantially reduced levels of extractable tricin and tricin-lignans were recorded. Meanwhile, rice over-expression lines showed significantly up-regulated gene expression of CYP75B4 and ROMT9 in vegetative tissues. However, the levels of extractable tricin-derived metabolites remained similar to wild-type plants. It is likely that there is a maximum storage capacity for these soluble metabolites in rice leaves and shoots. Alternatively, tricin may be channelled to secondary cell wall to form tricin-lignin which is not extractable by soluble solvents. Consistently, the expression of levels of other lignin biosynthesis genes (i.e. monolignol genes including PAL, 4CL3, C4H, and C3H) were also up-regulated in the M14 over-expression lines. For JX8, rice mutant plants showed significantly down-regulated gene expression of CYP75B4 and ROMT9 in vegetative tissues but no metabolite changes were detected. For JX7, rice over-expression lines showed significantly up-regulated gene expression of CYP93G2, CYP75B3, CHS. As the metabolite and gene expression analyses for JX8 and JX7 are incomplete at this stage, their regulatory roles on flavonoid biosynthesis in rice remain inconclusive. Meanwhile, M14 and JX7 were selected for DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) to further understand their regulatory functions and network in rice. For M14, DAP-seq data analysis revealed that the top 3 bound motifs shared a consensus sequence “GGT[A/T]GGTG” or “CACC[T/A]ACC” (reverse complement) which is the AC-II motif, suggesting that M14 recognized the AC-II motif at the target promoters. Using the core motifs, 102 genes under Gene Ontology “secondary metabolic processes” were found to be the putative targets of M14 including Os4CL3, OsCYP75B4, OsROMT9, OsCYP93G2 and OsCYP75B3. OsCHI and OsCHIL1 were found under the GO “Response to abiotic stimulus”. The occurrences of CYP75B4 and ROMT9 in the dataset validated the reliability of the DAP-seq strategy to identify new regulatory targets of M14. 4CL3, an enzyme along the phenylpropanoid pathway upstream of flavonoid biosynthesis, was selected for further characterization. M14 transactivates 4CL3 promoter (DLR assay) and recognizes AC-I, AC-II, SMRE2, and SMRE3 motifs for direct binding. Consistently, 4CL3 gene expression is significantly up-regulated in M14 over-expression lines but down-regulated in mutant lines, hence confirming 4CL3 as an additional target under transcriptional activation by M14. For JX7, DAP-seq data analysis revealed that the 4 most enriched motifs were found in the binding region of potential target promoters. Using the core motifs, 110 genes under the GO:0019748, secondary metabolic processes, were found to be the putative targets of Jx7 including OsCYP75B4, OsROMT9, CYP93G2 and OsCYP75B3. OsCHI was found under GO:0009628 (Response to abiotic stimulus). Subsequent DLR assays suggested that Jx7 probably be the transcriptional activator in regulating the expression of OsCHI, OsROMT9, OsCYP93G2 and OsCYP75B3. Further characterizations will be performed with transgenic OE and mutant lines to validate the in planta regulatory roles of JX7 on these genes Furthermore, there are a number of target promoters with enriched M14- or JX7-binding motifs in other GO term categories, hence presenting a wealth of information for future investigations of these two rice R2R3-MYB transcription factors. Lastly, we established a rice protoplast system for DLR and transient expression analysis, providing a time-efficient platform to analyze a large number of transcription factors. M14 was used to validate this approach. In addition to B4 and ROMT9 mentioned above, M14 was shown to transactivate the promoter of CYP93G1 and up-regulate its gene expression in rice protoplasts. Since Y1H and DLR-tobacco assays were negative for M14 with CYP93G1 promoter, it is likely that there are rice-specific downstream components that activate CYP93G1. To test this hypothesis, we engineered a M14-GR fusion protein that translocates to the nucleus only upon DEX induction. After protoplast transformation of M14-GR fusion gene, CHX was added to inhibit protein synthesis, followed by DEX addition, and CYP93G1 gene activation was largely reduced, suggesting that M14-induced CYP93G1 activation is mediated by de novo synthesis of downstream proteins (presumably some other transcription factors). Objective 2 Objective 2 aimed to characterize a potential negative regulator (F26: a ring E3 ligase) of tricin biosynthesis. The investigations were undertaken by a PhD student during the first 15 months of the project. Unfortunately, the F26 data generated by this student were non-reproducible and all related biological materials (e.g. transgenic and mutant seeds) were unusable/non-trackable. When requested to rectify the irregularities, the student disappeared immediately and quitted the study without proper handover of materials and experimental records. As this happened during the prolonged COVID-19 pandemics, we took a long period of time to get back on track. Subsequently, we decided to focus our efforts on Objective 1 with a newly-recruited PhD student working tirelessly on the different tasks as detailed above. Overall, we have performed expanded investigations for Objective 1 together with generation of valuable information and biological resources for future work, thereby compensating the shortfall in Objective 2 due to unanticipated and unfortunate events with the initial student during the period of COVID pandemics.
