17104720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104720.value: The identification and demonstration of M14 as a new R2R3-MYB transcription factor that regulates tricin biosynthesis in rice is the major finding in this study. M14 positively regulates the expression of genes encoding CYP75B4 and ROMT9 through direct binding of MYB-specific recognition motifs. This discovery has been supported by molecular assays (Y1H, DLR, and EMSA) as well as gene expression and metabolite characterization of transgenic over-expression and mutant rice plants. The majority of these tasks were completed by a postgraduate student (GAN Yiming, PhD 2021-2025) who has been supported by this funding. He had presented these findings at an international conference (Plant Canada 2024) and is expected to submit his PhD thesis in August 2025. A manuscript is now in preparation regarding the regulatory role of M14 on tricin biosynthesis in rice tissues. In addition, an undergraduate student (Wu Peilin BSc 2021-2025) has been working on his final year research project on the molecular validation of target genes identified by DAP-seq analysis of M14. Finally, we have published a few review articles on biosynthesis, applications, and characterizations of flavonoids and tricin-lignin involving the tricin biosynthesis genes which are regulated by M14 as shown in this study. These publications are achieved through collaborations with international scientists in Japan (Kyoto University and Akita University), USA (Cornell University and Washington State University), and Mainland (South China University of Technology and Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences).

17104720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104720.value: This GRF project has generated useful resources and information which open up springboards for future investigations. For example, the CRISPR-Cas9 rice mutants and transgenic over-expression rice lines for the six different R2R3-MYBs represent valuable biological materials for in planta investigations. While some of them do not seem to be involved in regulation of flavonoid biosynthesis genes, detailed phenotypic analyses will be conducted to reveal potential functional roles during growth and development or under different environment and stress conditions. New collaborators specialized in the respective disciplines will be invited to work together and submit new funding applications. Furthermore, DAP-sequencing analyses of M14 and JX7 presented a list of candidates for further analysis of the regulatory network downstream of these two R2R3-MYBs. New postgraduate students are now working on DLR and rice protoplast assays to validate the physical binding and transactivation activities of M14 and JX7 on their respective target gene promoters. The above tasks will generate strong supporting data for our future GRF applications.

17104720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104720.value: Flavonoids are phytochemicals with diverse functions in plants and valuable health benefits for humans. Rice, as an important staple crop, produces an abundant level of tricin as the major flavonoid in leaves and shoots (vegetative tissues). Previously we established the biosynthetic pathway for tricin in grasses using rice as a model system. Results from this study has offered new insights into the previously unknown molecular regulatory mechanism of tricin biosynthesis. Specifically, the R2R3-MYB transcription factor M14 was shown conclusively to modulate expression of genes encoding enzymes which catalyze the key reaction steps leading to tricin formation. In particular, M14 binds to promoter regions of these genes by recognition of specific binding motifs, thereby upregulating their expression levels. Meanwhile, genetic manipulations of M14 in transgenic rice led to altered profiles of tricin and tricin-derived metabolites in vegetative tissues. Hence, M14 may be utilized to improve cell wall digestibility of grass biomass for bioethanol production through manipulation of tricin levels in lignin which normally impacts cellulose digestion negatively. In addition, M14 may be exploited for metabolic engineering of edible tissues (e.g. endosperm in seeds) to synthesize the health-beneficial tricin and tricin-metabolites which are not naturally in these tissues.

17104820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104820.value: 癌症的轉移佔癌症總死亡人數的90％，因此了解其潛在機制顯然很重要。在所有類型的癌症中，腫瘤內的異質性(ITH)，即腫瘤中不同癌細胞亞群的共存，對癌症進展和治療的耐藥性有深遠影響。然而，儘管腫瘤的遺傳異質性已經得到了很好的定義，但其表型異質性在驅動臨床發展中的功能卻知之甚少。 最近，我們課題組超越了現有方法缺乏嚴格控制和代表性細胞模型的局限性，建立了一個穩健的框架來解開介導轉移的關鍵分子。我們已經成功開發了一種具有不同轉移特性的同基因卵巢癌模型。利用此模型，我們發現β-catenin是轉移表型的關鍵調控因子。在此，我課題組第一次展現了，β-catenin高表達和β-catenin低表達卵巢癌細胞作為一個整體，在腫瘤內的相互作用顯著增強了腫瘤的轉移行為。同時，與衰老相關的分泌型β-catenin低表達細胞是促進β-catenin高表達細胞傳播轉移的主要因素。這種協同作用是通過β-catenin和Hippo信號通路之間的獨特串擾實現的。與之連貫的是，體內基因組學和病理學研究也明顯地證實了這種調節。令人興奮的是，這種異型腫瘤對鎮靜藥物達沙替尼和槲皮素高度敏感。雖然β-catenin ITH在多種癌組織中有據可查，但其功能性作用尚未見報導。更重要的是，β-catenin抑制Hippo信號傳導的機制尚不清楚。細胞衰老是很多癌症的基礎標誌，我們也將第一個揭示細胞衰老和ITH之間的聯繫。我們的猜想是，在異型腫瘤中β-catenin ITH通過積極增強β-catenin高表達細胞的促進行為來驅動腫瘤的轉移，其中衰老相的關分泌型β-catenin低表達細胞則是這一現象的關鍵因素。 應用體外和體內實驗方法，我們將徹底:(1)闡明β-catenin ITH在腫瘤發展不同階段的功能性作用;(2)破譯β-catenin-Hippo信號軸的分子機制;(3)描繪β- catenin低表達細胞，特別是與細胞衰老的β-catenin低表達細胞在驅動β-catenin高表達細胞轉移中的作用基本機制。 這項研究不僅將發現一個在腫瘤轉移中起至關重要作用的合作互動機制，也為β-catenin ITH在設計新穎有效的抗腫瘤治療方法的應用提出了科學依據。

17104820.label: Realisation of objectives
17104820.value: Objective 1: To date, there is no direct evidence for the functional relevance of beta-catenin in driving tumor aggressiveness. Using the well-controlled isogenic metastasis-competent beta-catenin-high (HM) and metastasis-incompetent beta-catenin-low (NM) model, we showed for the first time that the cooperative interactions of these two subclones significantly enhanced the metastatic behavior of the tumor, resulting in substantially higher metastatic burden in vivo. Heterogeneous beta-catenin was also observed in tumor spheroids derived from patients malignant ascites, supporting the clinical relevance of our findings. HM and NM exhibited distinct responses within the tumor microenvironment and displayed a selective advantage for therapy resistance characteristic of metastasis. Coculture assays reveal that NM supported HM migration and invasion. The conditioned media from NM cells was sufficient for enhancing HM migration/invasion, suggesting that these effects were mediated through secreted factors from NM. Conditioned media from HM-beta-catenin shRNA cells produced similar effects in promoting HM migration. We have also successfully established HM-beta-catenin knockout cells using CRISPR-Cas9 and found that beta-catenin plays an important role in the HM aggressive phenotypes of HM mediated by NM. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: Mechanistically, we found that beta-catenin could suppress Hippo signaling to promote the activation of nuclear translocation of YAP and upregulation of YAP target genes (CTGF, CYRB1, GOT1 and TXN), whereas YAP silencing has no effects on beta-catenin expression. Consistently, NM cells showed active Hippo signaling as compared to HM. Moreover, Hippo pathway factors MST2 and LATS2 were found to downregulate YAP activation. Immunohistochemistry staining of the orthotopic tumors further showed that tumor cells with high beta-catenin also have higher expression of nuclear YAP, and high expression of beta-catenin and YAP was also associated with poor overall survival in ovarian cancer patients. We further showed the involvement of O-GlcNAcylation, a posttranslational modification that can antagonize phosphorylation by competing for the same serine and threonine sites on target proteins, in beta-catenin regulation of YAP. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: To understand how NM promotes HM migration, we performed phenotypic characterization and showed that NM exhibit various senescence-like features as compared to HM: slower growth rate, larger and more flattened morphology, positivity for senescence-associated beta-galactosidase staining, and higher expression of markers for cellular senescence (p21, HMGB1, and gamma H2A.x) and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors (IL-6, TNF-alpha, and PAI-1) and cytokines (IL-6, G-CSF, IL-12p70, and IL-27). We found that SASP were suppressed by beta-catenin/YAP signaling in HM. Furthermore, senolytic drugs e.g. quercetin, fisetin and senomorphic agent e.g. anti-IL-6 suppressed SASP of NM cells, while SASP-induced HM migration could also be enhanced by YAP inhibition through siRNA or verteporfin. These data suggest the potential use of YAP inhibitors and/or senolytics as anti-metastatic therapeutics. Percentage achieved: 100% These findings not only reveal a previously unrecognized role for beta-catenin ITH in metastatic progression, but also unveil a novel role for beta-catenin ITH mediated cooperative interaction as a key regulator of cellular senescence, which has been recognized as the prime driving event in almost all hallmarks of cancer. As such, our findings introduce a new dimension to our existing knowledge on the oncogenic roles of beta-catenin ITH in tumor progression and that the targeting of beta-catenin signaling components and senescent-associated secretome may represent more precise targets with potential therapeutic advantage for metastatic ovarian cancer. 17104820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104820.value: Objective 1: Here, using isogenic ovarian cancer cell models with opposite metastatic abilities, whose growth and metastasis patterns were similar to those observed in human ovarian cancer, we provide the first evidence that beta-catenin plays a crucial role in tumor aggressiveness, as demonstrated by enhanced metastatic behavior in the metastasis-competent beta-catenin-high HM cells. Cooperative interactions between subclones contribute significantly to metastatic burden, supported by heterogeneous beta-catenin presence in patient-derived tumor spheroids. Our in vivo experiments together with patient samples, strongly support the clinical importance of our proposed mechanisms in ovarian cancer. Journal article: #1, 2, 3 Conference proceeding: #5 Objective 2: Using an omics-guided approach, we discovered beta-catenin functions as an upstream regulator of YAP, leading to the induction of senescent-like phenotypes in beta-catenin depleted cells when YAP is inhibited. Hippo was found to downregulate YAP activation. In addition, our findings highlight the role of a widespread posttranslational modification O-GlcNAcylation in the regulation of YAP by beta-catenin showcasing its ability to compete with phosphorylation at the same serine and threonine sites. Notably, high expression of both beta-catenin and YAP is associated with poor overall survival in ovarian cancer patients, highlighting their potential roles in patient outcomes. Journal article: #1, 3 Conference proceeding: #4 Objective 3: To explore the molecular mechanism of beta-catenin ITH in promoting metastatic progression, we identified NM exhibited senescence-like characteristics compared to HM cells. SASP factors are regulated by beta-catenin/YAP signaling in HM, and the SASP of NM cells can be suppressed by senolytic drugs like fisetin. In addition, inhibiting YAP enhanced HM migration induced by SASP. These findings suggest the potential therapeutic benefit of YAP inhibitors and senolytics in combating metastasis. Journal article: #1 Conference proceedings: #4 Beta-catenin, not previously studied in the context of ITH, exhibits varied expression in ovarian and other tumors. This project systematically investigated beta-catenin ITH and uncovered not only its previously unrecognized role in metastatic progression, but also its novel and significant role in cooperative interactions as a key regulator of cellular senescence, a pivotal driving event in almost all hallmarks of cancer. In contrast to that beta-catenin and Hippo/YAP pathways operate independently, our research highlights their interconnectedness. Cellular senescence may provide potential vulnerabilities to target. Our findings introduce a new dimension to our understanding of beta-catenin ITH oncogenic roles in tumor progression, suggesting that targeting beta-catenin signaling components and senescent-associated secretome for enhanced therapeutic outcomes in metastatic ovarian cancer.

17104820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104820.value: We reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic role of beta-catenin ITH in ovarian cancer metastasis and implicate that beta-catenincould be a promising therapeutic target. To identify novel signaling paths, we have compared the differential interacting partners of beta-catenin in metastatic competent CSCs using LC-MS/MS. We have identified several novel and tumor-specific targets of this area. Given their high expression levels and correlation with poor clinical outcomes in ovarian cancer, targeting these factors may offer a safe and promising strategy for treating metastatic ovarian cancer. Our research will further develop in this area to enhance the robustness of the study and potential clinical applications. We have developed nanostructures based on dendrimers as effective carriers for beta-catenin siRNA in novel RNAi therapeutic applications. We will cotreat with senolytic drugs or YAP inhibitors and unravel the underlying mechanisms of action as scientific basis for its development as rationally designed drug combinations. Beta-catenin ITH is also observed in uterine, pancreatic and colon cancer. We will expand our findings by exploring these other tumor types. These findings should highlight the functional importance of beta-catenin ITH in impacting aggressive malignant cell behavior and implies important clinical implications.

17104820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104820.value: One of the most critical challenges in effectively treating cancer is metastasis. Currently, there is a lack of effective therapies, resulting in a poor 5-year survival rate (less than 25%). This underscores the urgent need for new therapeutic targets and a deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms driving cancer progression. Tumor heterogeneity significantly impacts cancer relapse and metastasis, yet understanding interactions among cell subclones and the microenvironment is limited. Cellular senescence, a hallmark of cancer, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target. This study makes significant advancements to the field: (i) by showing for the first time a new role of beta-catenin in driving tumor aggressiveness and promoting metastasis through interactions between different subclones; (ii) identifying YAP, a master regulator of the cell state, as a novel target of beta-catenin, linking it to tumor progression, metastasis, and poor outcomes in ovarian cancer; and (iii) presenting evidence suggesting that targeting YAP or using sinolytic drugs could effectively suppress metastasis. (iii). These findings offer a new perspectives on the oncogenic roles of beta-catenin and emphasize its importance as a potential therapeutic target. Targeting beta-catenin signaling components and senescent-associated factors holds promise of enhancing treatment outcomes in metastatic ovarian cancer.

17105220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105220.value: 腦卒中是高致殘率和高死亡率的疾病。組織型纖溶酶原啟動劑（t-PA）是唯一FDA批准的治療急性缺血性腦卒中藥物，但其4.5小時治療時間窗限制了其臨床應用。延遲t-PA治療增加出血轉化(HT)併發症。t-PA促進中性粒細胞向腦組織聚集，中性粒細胞表達髓過氧化物酶（MPO），催化氯離子（Cl-）和過氧化氫（H2O2）生成次氯酸（HOCl），加重腦缺血再灌注損傷。 氧化HMGB1半胱氨酸殘基形成二硫化HMGB1可引發炎症反應，二硫化HMGB1是否參與血腦屏障（BBB）損傷和HT尚不清楚；HOCl能否二硫化HMGB1不清楚。為此, 我們發展了新的螢光探針檢測HOCl，預實驗顯示：（1）血漿HOCl水準與腦梗死面積和神經功能缺損呈正相關；（2）在延遲t-PA治療大鼠腦缺血模型中，MPO抑制劑4-ABAH和HOCl清除劑牛磺酸減少HOCl，減輕血腦屏障損傷、HT和神經功能缺損;（3）Acteoside減少HOCl活性，減輕HT；（4）HOCl促進BV2細胞表達和分泌HMGB1。因此，我們提出假說：HOCl誘導二硫化HMGB1引發BBB損傷和HT。我們將重點研究以下問題：（1）HOCl是否介導BBB損傷和HT；（2）HOCl能否二硫化HMGB1, 引起血腦屏障損傷和HT；（3）Acteoside是否清除HOCl，減輕血腦屏障損傷，HT和神經功能缺損。我們期望本研究為減少腦卒中溶栓出血轉化提供新的治療靶標。

17105220.label: Realisation of objectives
17105220.value: With the support of the GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments to test the objectives and demonstrated the roles of MPO/HOCl in mediating the formation of disulfide HMGB1 and facilitating the translocation and secretion of disulfide HMGB1, subsequently aggravating the BBB disruption and inducing hemorrhagic transformation in post-ischemic brains with the t-PA treatment beyond the golden therapeutic window. We have reached the goals as expected in the original RGC GRF proposal. Objective 1. We first performed a series of experiments to explore complex interactions of different cell types in the neurovascular unit (NVU) and their impacts on brain damage and BBB disruption by using a co-culture system with BV2 microglial cells and PC12 cells explored to oxygen and glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) conditions that mimicked cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in vitro. Co-cultured with the BV2 microglial cells and explored to OGD/R condition, the PC12 cells had significantly increased MPO expression and HOCl level, leading to the release of LDH and aggravating apoptotic cell death. Treatment of 4-aminobenzoic acid hydrazide (4-ABAH, an MPO inhibitor) significantly reduced LDH release and apoptotic cell death. Knockdown of MPO expression in BV2 cells down-regulated the expression of MPO, decreased HOCl production, and inhibited apoptosis in the co-cultured PC12 cells under OGD/R conditions. Furthermore, we demonstrated the release of MPO-containing exosomes from microglial cells played crucial roles in mediating the production of HOCl in the neighboring neuronal cells under OGD/R conditions. Isolation of exosomes from the supernatant of OGD/R-stimulated BV2 cells confirmed the presence of MPO. Incubating with these exosomes significantly increased the HOCl production in the PC12 cells. Treatment of taurine, an HOCl scavenger, alleviated apoptotic cell death in PC12 cells under OGD/R conditions. We then investigated the dynamic changes in MPO expression and HOCl production, as well as their cellular sources, in rat brains after subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) with or without delayed tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) treatment in vivo. After the rats were subjected to 2 ischemia plus different reperfusion periods (0, 2, 4, 6, 24 hours), the expression of MPO and the production of HOCl in the ischemic brain were significantly enhanced, and they were further increased in the ischemic brain tissues with delayed t-PA infusion at 5 hours after cerebral ischemia. MPO inhibitor 4-ABAH and HOCl scavenger taurine decreased the expression of MPO/HOCl, protected the blood-brain barrier integrity, reserved the expression of tight junction proteins including occludin and claudin-5, and prevented HT, and eventually improved the neurological outcomes and survival rates. Those results provide direct evidence to support the hypothesis in Objective 1. Objective 2. To test the role of HOCl in aggravating apoptotic cell death and facilitating HMGB1 release in vitro, we treated the PC12 cells with HOCl (25, 50, and 100 μM) under normoxic condition (NC) or OGD/R conditions. The apoptotic cell death and cell viability were detected by Annexin V-FITC/PI assay and MTT assay, respectively. Nuclear and cytosolic extractions were collected by using the Nuclear and Cytoplasmic Protein Extraction Kit. The results showed that excessive HOCl production induced apoptotic cell death in the PC12 cells under OGD/R conditions. The apoptosis was alleviated by taurine, an HOCl scavenger. Western blot analysis revealed that HOCl induced the formation of disulfide HMGB1 in the cytoplasm and supernatant. ELISA assay showed that the elevation of HMGB1 in the supernatant was reversed by treatment of taurine. These results suggest that HOCl could induce the formation of disulfide HMGB1 and facilitate its translocation and secretion, subsequently aggravating apoptotic cell death in the PC12 cells. Consistently, in vivo study also revealed the colocalization of HOCl and HMGB1 in the cytoplasm rather than in the nuclear of the neuronal cells in the ischemic brains. The delayed t-PA infusion further enhanced HMGB1 translocation and release in the ischemic brains. With the treatment of 4-ABAH or taurine, the expression of MPO and the level of HOCl were decreased, respectively, in the post-ischemic brains. They effectively inhibited the translocation of HMGB1 to the cytoplasm and its release. Those results indicate that MPO/HOCl could mediate HMGB1 translocation and secretion, aggravate neuroinflammation, and induce BBB damage as well as HT in rat ischemic brains with or without delayed t-PA treatment. Objective 3. We identified Acteoside, an active compound identified from Chinese medicinal herb Radix Rehmanniae, had scavenging effects on HOCl through direct reaction and neutralization in chemical systems. Acteoside also directly scavenged HOCl and inhibited its production in the ischemic brains with delayed t-PA treatment. Moreover, acteoside treatment reduced the rates of mortality in the MCAO rats with delayed t-PA treatment. Acteoside treatment significantly improved neurological outcomes, attenuated the BBB damage, and decreased HT. Acteoside treatment reserved the expression of occludin and claudin-5 levels in ischemic brains. Finally, we investigated the effects of Acteoside on inhibiting HMGB1 translocation and release in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in the MCAO rats with delayed t-PA treatment. MCAO ischemia induced the cytoplasmic translocation and plasma release of HMGB1. The delayed t-PA treatment further enhanced HMGB1 translocation and release. Acteoside treatment significantly reduced HOCl level and inhibited HMGB1 translocation and release in the MCAO rats with delayed t-PA treatment. Taken together, we conclude that Acteoside could inhibit the HOCl-mediated HMGB1 release, protect the BBB integrity, and attenuate HT in ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment, subsequently extending the therapeutic window for thrombolytic treatment.

17105220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105220.value: This project yields three original articles and one review article published in peer-reviewed international journals. There are two manuscripts in preparation. The major discoveries are summarized as below: (1) Microglia-derived MPO/HOCl production plays crucial roles in mediating HMGB1 translocation and secretion, and aggravating brain damage and the BBB disruption in cerebral I/R injury: Exposure to OGD/R and co-cultured with microglia BV cells, PC12 cells significantly increased MPO/HOCl expression. MPO-containing exosomes derived from BV2 cells were released and transferred to PC12 cells, increasing MPO/HOCl in the PC12 cells. HOCl mediated disulfide HMGB1 translocation and secretion and aggravated apoptosis. In cerebral ischemia and reperfusion rats, there were increased MPO/HOCl at the reperfusion stage, accomplished with enlarged infarct volume, aggravated BBB disruption and neurological dysfunctions. MPO inhibitor 4-ABAH and HOCl scavenger taurine reversed those changes. HOCl was colocalized with cytoplasm transferred HMGB1, which was blocked by taurine. Clinical investigation revealed that plasma HOCl concentration was positively correlated with infarct volume and neurological deficit scores in ischemic stroke patients. These results have been published in Journal of Neuroinflammation. (2024. 21(1): p.70). (2) MPO/HOCl-mediated HMGB1 release could be a crucial pathological process in delayed t-PA infusion mediated the BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke: This is a novel cellular signaling pathway discovered with both in vivo and in vitro experimental evidences. A manuscript is preparing to report the roles of MPO/HOCl in mediating the BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. Meanwhile, we demonstrated that peroxynitrite-activated NLRP3 inflammasome contributed to HT and poor outcome in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. This work has been published in Free Radical Biology & Medicine (2021;165:171-183). (3) Acteoside could be a promising adjunct with delayed t-PA treatment to reducing HT via inhibiting HOCl/HMGB1/NLRP3 pathway: Acteoside is an active compound isolated from Radix Rehmannia. Acteoside significantly reduced mortality, improved the neurological outcomes, and attenuated BBB disruption and HT in MCAO rats with delayed t-PA treatment. Acteoside scavenged HOCl, inhibited HMGB1 release, and deactivated NLRP3 inflammasome in the ischemic stroke rats with delayed t-PA treatment. The manuscript has been prepared for publication. In addition, we investigated the neuroprotective effects of Danggui-Shayao-San (DSS), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. DSS attenuated oxidative/nitrosative stress and inhibited neuronal apoptosis in brains subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury via SIRT1-dependent manner. This paper has been published in Frontiers in Pharmacology (2021:12:653795).

17105220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105220.value: Based on the achievement of our studies, we expect following potential directions for further studies: (1) To investigate the impact of the MPO/HOCl/HMGB1 signaling cascades in neurovascular unit on hemorrhage transformation and other complications in both ischemic stroke patients and animal models with thrombolytic treatment or thrombectomy. (2) To develop Acteoside as a novel drug candidate as adjunct therapy with t-PA to improve the outcome of thrombolytic treatment for ischemic stroke. (3) To use the MPO/HOCl/HMGB1 signaling cascades as novel therapeutic targets for drug discovery from Chinese Medicinal plants. We plan to seek for new fund sources to develop frontier and translational studies in future.

17105220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105220.value: Stroke is a major disease burden with high mortality and disability rates worldwide. Currently, t-PA is the only FDA-approved thrombolytic drug for ischemic stroke, but it has been limited within 4.5 hours of golden therapeutic time. Delayed t-PA treatment would increase the risk of brain bleeding named hemorrhage transformation (HT) that contributes to increased mortality. This project aims to explore underlying mechanisms related to oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in mediating the blood-brain barrier disruption and HT in ischemic stroke with t-PA treatment beyond 4.5 hours post-stroke. By performing a series of experiments including cell culture, animal experiments and clinical trials, we have demonstrated that MPO/HOCl/HMGB1 signaling cascades and peroxynitrite-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome play crucial roles in the BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. They are also important therapeutic targets for drug discovery. Acteoside, an active compound from medicinal plants, has been identified as a potential drug candidate to reduce t-PA-induced brain bleeding and increase the survival rates of ischemic stroke. The study brings novel insight into understanding the pathological mechanisms of thrombolysis-induced brain bleeding and develops novel therapeutic targets and drug candidates for ischemic stroke treatment.

17105420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105420.value: Influenza virus infections pose a major threat to public health worldwide. The genetic plasticity and adaptation in various animal and human hosts continue to fuel the emergence of novel strains that can infect humans with increasing efficiency. Currently, there is no robust model to evaluate and predict which strain or subtype of emerging virus will infect humans and how virulent/pathogenic a virus will be. We recently established protocol to derive long-term expandable human lung organoids from the adult stem cells in normal lung tissue. We induced proximal differentiation in lung organoids and developed airway organoids which can faithfully simulate human airway (the upper respiratory) epithelium. We proceeded to induce distal differentiation and generated alveolar organoids mimicking the lower respiratory epithelium as demonstrated in the preliminary data. We propose, firstly, to characterize the maturation status of alveolar organoids by single cell RNA sequencing. Apart from being a comprehensive characterization, single cell RNA sequencing analysis may inform us potential mechanism for further alveolar differentiation. we may incorporate the related molecules to improve maturation status of current alveolar organoids. In addition, we will evaluate the functionality of alveolar epithelial cells in the alveolar organoids. Secondly, the capability of a given virus causing human influenza, i.e., viral infectivity largely depends on its competence to propagate in the upper respiratory epithelium. Since airway organoids can morphologically and functionally simulate human airway epithelium, we will use two strains of virus, human seasonal virus H3N2 and avian virus H5N1, as a proof-of-principle, to demonstrate that airway organoids can model higher infectivity of H3N2 virus than H5N1 virus in humans. Thirdly, the high pathogenicity of avian virus H5N1 is largely attributed to its ability to establish productive infection in the lower respiratory tract and cause pneumonia. Together with the airway organoids we reported previously, we have established the first long-term expandable organoid culture system of human upper and lower respiratory epithelium. 17105420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105420.value: We have developed a robust protocol to establish alveolar organoids from undifferentiated organoids. We have characterized the alveolar organoids by RNA sequencing and various assays and demonstrated that alveolar organoids can adequately phenocopy the native alveolar epithelium in terms of cellular composition, morphology and functionality. The alveolar organoids, airway organoids and nasal organoids were leveraged to study SARS-COV-2 and emerging variants (Cell Discovery 2022, mBio 2022, viruses 2023). The results indicate that human airway and nasal organoids are more susceptible to BA.5 than the prior variants B.1.1.529 and WT; BA.5 acquired an adequate fitness in human airway and nasal organoids to a level comparable to a seasonal influenza virus strain. BA.5 spike pseudovirus showed a significantly higher entry efficiency than that carrying WT or B.1.1.529 spike. Notably, we observed prominent syncytium formation in BA.5-infected nasal and airway organoids, albeit elusive in WT- and B.1.1.529- infected organoids. BA.5 spike-triggered syncytium formation was verified by lentiviral overexpression of spike in nasal organoids. influenza virus infection in the organoids elicited an intensive upregulation of antiviral and proinflammatory genes. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 infection in these organoids with similar replication efficiency exhibited a dysregulated pattern, including the strong induction of proinflammatory chemokines (IP10) and dampened antiviral response of IFNs and ISGs. The viral titer of BA.5 was consistently and significantly lower than that in WT and BA.1, suggesting the lower propensity of BA.5 to cause pneumonia, a severe complication of COVID-19 (PNAS 2023). 17105920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105920.value: 代謝綜合症是一項嚴重的公共衛生問題。在患有代謝綜合症的病人群體惡化至疾病階段前，及時介入能夠通過降低糖尿病及心血管疾病的發病率帶來可觀的健康益處。高強度間歇性訓練是一項新興，受歡迎，低成本並且省時的運動模式，並且可作為介入手段改善代謝綜合症。較低的高強度間歇性訓練頻率有助於提高介入的依附性，但將高強度間歇性訓練用於改善代謝綜合症的最佳運動頻率尚不清楚。 本項目研究目標在於確定不同運動頻率（每週一次對比三次）的高強度間歇性訓練改善中央肥胖成年人代謝綜合症的治療效果。本研究計畫的假說是根據流行病學的發現：週末勇士型的運動模式（每週一到兩次的運動）的運動效果和每週規律運動在改善代謝綜合症心血管代謝風險因素，降低心血管疾病發生以及全因死亡率風險的效果相似。 我們的初步數據也闡明在肥胖成年人群中，每週一次的高強度間歇性訓練可以改善最大攝氧量，身體成分以及血壓。然而我們之前的研究缺少每週的總運動量一致的對照組，限制了我們無法直接比較不同運動頻率的高強度間歇性訓練的益處。本項三臂隨機對照試驗會進一步延伸我們之前的研究，從而探索運動頻率在高強度間歇性訓練處方中的角色。 患有中央肥胖的成年人士會被隨機分入三組：通常介入組，每週一次以及每週三次的高強度間歇性訓練組。高強度間歇性訓練組參加人士會接受由運動教練授課，為期16週，每週一次或者三次的訓練（兩組每週運動總量一致）。不清楚受試者組別分配的測試員會在第16週（介入後）以及第32週（跟蹤觀察後）對受試者進行身體成分（由雙能量X光吸收儀測定），內臟脂肪（由核磁共振測定），身體指標（身體質量指數以及腰圍），代謝綜合症的心血管代謝風險因子（血壓，血糖，三酸甘油脂以及高密度膽固醇），介入依附度，心理學問卷，健康相關的生活質量，心理健康，藥物使用，不良事件，基準身體活動及飲食習慣進行測定。 此項研究將會闡明較低頻率高強度間歇性訓練的健康益處。本研究伴有的跟蹤隨訪可評估低頻率高強度間歇性訓練的有效性，安全性，依附性以及可以持續性。我們預計該介入模式可以加強高強度間歇性訓練在不活躍肥胖人士中的可鍛鍊性，並且為將低頻率高強度間歇性訓練作為一項可替代性的運動模式納入管理代謝綜合症的管理提供證據。

17105920.label: Realisation of objectives
17105920.value: This project aimed to examine the effectiveness of 16 weeks of once-weekly HIIT and thrice-weekly HIIT on improving cardiometabolic risk factors in centrally obese adults. Through rigorous implementation, this project produced robust findings that both HIIT frequencies are safe and therapeutic for improving cardiorespiratory fitness and alleviating excess adiposity and waist circumference. Thus, fully achieving its objective. The project was managed by the principal investigator and his supervised research postgraduate students. The breakdown of how the project’s objective was achieved is provided below. Participant enrollment began on September 1, 2021 and concluded on November 23, 2023. During the enrollment period, adults with central obesity were recruited from the local communities through a poster and leaflet mailing campaign. Responding individuals were invited to the laboratory at the Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine, The University of Hong Kong for a preliminary screening based on the following inclusion criteria: (1) aged 18 years or above, (2) ethnic Chinese, (3) overweight (body mass index ≥23, classification adopted by the Department of Health of the Hong Kong SAR Government), and (4) centrally obese (waist circumference ≥90 cm for men and ≥80 cm for women, classification adopted by the International Diabetes Federation for Chinese ethnic group). In total, 315 eligible participants provided written informed consent and were included in this project. This fulfilled the estimated sample size pre-specified in the original application. After enrollment, participants underwent baseline assessments using standardized procedures conducted by blinded assessors. The cardiometabolic risk factors assessed included fat mass, body weight, body mass index, waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, low-density lipoprotein, triglyceride, and cardiorespiratory fitness. The primary outcome was body fat mass which was assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). To ensure validity and reliability, a standardized preparation and scanning procedure was adopted. Briefly, participants were told to fast for 4 hours before the scan but could drink water and take their usual medication. Minimal and loose-fitting clothing with no metallic materials was worn for the scan. Participants were then positioned on the DXA scanner according to the recommended positioning and alignment of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) method. Furthermore, the daily physical activity and dietary intake of the participants were also monitored as potential confounding factors to ensure that the findings were robust. Following baseline assessments, participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to the once-weekly HIIT (n = 105), thrice-weekly HIIT (n = 105), or usual care control group (n = 105) by an independent study statistician. Participants were randomized in batches, resulting in 14 batches. Participants randomized to the usual care control group attended a 150-minute health education class every 2 weeks for 16 weeks. The contents of the health education program were based on obesity-related health information from the Hong Kong SAR Government. Participants randomized to the HIIT groups were prescribed 75 minutes of supervised HIIT per week for 16 weeks. The once-weekly and thrice-weekly HIIT groups accumulated 75 minutes of HIIT weekly in one and three training sessions, respectively. The exercise volume between the once-weekly and thrice-weekly HIIT groups was matched. Each HIIT session totaled 25 minutes of exercise and consisted of four 4-minute high-intensity intervals at 85%-95% peak heart rate (HRpeak), interspersed with 3-minute active recovery intervals at 50%-70% HRpeak. Participants randomized to the once-weekly HIIT group performed the 25-minute HIIT session three times in one training session, with a 15 to 30-minute break in between each HIIT session. After 16 weeks of intervention, post-intervention assessments were performed to assess the differences in the measured cardiometabolic risk factors. Overall, the project had a very good completion rate with minimal dropout and no serious adverse events reported. Of note, 297 (94%) participants completed the 16-week follow-up. Dropouts were balanced across groups. Encouragingly, the high completion rate is coupled with a high attendance rate, with the usual care control, once-weekly HIIT, and thrice-weekly HIIT groups reporting 88%, 86%, and 83% attendance, respectively. Collectively, the large sample size, high completion and attendance rate combined with the rigorous conduct of the research process has resulted in the full achievement of the project’s objective. Despite the full achievement of its objective, the project experienced difficulties, primarily stemming from COVID-19. A frequent problem was that the participants would be infected with COVID-19 which affected their respiratory system, thus making compliance with the HIIT intervention difficult. The project resolved this challenge by implementing a standardized training protocol for COVID-19 recovered participants. The COVID-19 training protocol consisted of the following two steps: (1) provide proof of two consecutive days of negative rapid antigen test results, and (2) initiate 4 weeks of gradual resumption of HIIT beginning at 50% of the initial volume with an intensity of ~70% HRpeak for the high-intensity intervals and progressing to 100% of the prescribed intensity and volume by the fourth week. Additional minor problems caused by COVID-19 included the exclusion of eligible and willing participants due to their non-compliance with Hong Kong SAR Government vaccination requirements. Moreover, COVID-19 did impose significant difficulties, particularly concerning the delivery of the interventions. In February 2022, a COVID-19 outbreak occurred in Hong Kong resulting in tightened social distancing measures. Consequently, the HIIT intervention for batch 1 and 2 participants was modified from group training to 1-on-1 training (1 participant with 1 trainer) per training time slot. In March 2022 when COVID-19 cases exponentially increased, the intervention was further adjusted to HIIT conducted at home via bodyweight exercises. The research team adapted to this challenge by mailing heart rate monitors to the participants, combined with guiding and supervising their home-based training via Zoom. Participants in the usual care control group also switched from group-based face-to-face lessons to group-based online sessions via Zoom.

17105920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105920.value: This project demonstrates that 75 minutes of HIIT per week performed in a once-weekly and thrice-weekly frequency is safe and efficacious for improving cardiometabolic risk factors in adults with central obesity. After 16 weeks of HIIT intervention, the once-weekly HIIT group induced a 0.7 kg within-group reduction in fat mass (relative change: –2.6%) while the thrice-weekly HIIT group induced a 1.3 kg within-group reduction in fat mass (relative change: –3.5%). In contrast, the control group had a 0.2 kg within-group increase in fat mass (relative change: +0.2%). The fat mass reduction observed in the once-weekly HIIT (H1) and thrice-weekly HIIT (H3) groups was statistically significant when compared with the control group (H1 vs CON: P = 0.0098; H3 vs CON: P = 0.0003). Importantly, there was no significant difference in fat mass reduction between the once-weekly HIIT and thrice-weekly HIIT groups (H1 vs H3: P = 0.3613). This suggests that once-weekly HIIT, a more time-efficient exercise modality, is of comparable effectiveness to thrice-weekly HIIT in managing excess adiposity. Although there is currently no consensus on what constitutes a clinically meaningful reduction in fat mass, the magnitude of fat mass reduced in the HIIT groups is encouraging as they are consistent with the clinical criteria of 3% weight reduction established by the joint clinical guideline on obesity management from the American Heart Association (AHA), American College of Cardiology (ACC), and The Obesity Society (TOS). This guideline states that even modest reductions in weight can confer meaningful cardiometabolic health benefits to patients with obesity. Indeed, aligned with this statement, we observed that once-weekly HIIT and thrice-weekly HIIT achieved statistically significant reductions in waist circumference compared to the control group (H1 vs CON: P = 0.0007; H3 vs CON: P = 0.0065). Furthermore, both frequencies of HIIT (once-weekly and thrice-weekly) also exhibited a statistically significant improvement in cardiorespiratory fitness compared to the control group (H1 vs CON: P = 0.0029; H3 vs CON: P = <0.0001). The improvements in waist circumference and cardiorespiratory fitness induced by both once-weekly HIIT and thrice-weekly HIIT are important, as both are independent predictors of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality. Collectively, robust findings based on 315 participants, with 94% retention at post-intervention and an average exercise attendance rate of 85% demonstrate that condensing 75 minutes of HIIT into one day of the week is safe, adherable and produces similar benefits on adiposity and cardiometabolic parameters as thrice-weekly HIIT in adults with central obesity. In adults with central obesity, 75 minutes of HIIT performed once-a-week is safe and confers improvements in excess adiposity (fat mass), central adiposity (waist circumference), and cardiorespiratory fitness.

17105920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105920.value: This project elucidated the effects of once-weekly HIIT and thrice-weekly HIIT on improving adiposity and cardiometabolic risk factors in adults with central obesity. Nonetheless, patients with obesity are at an increased risk of a variety of co-occurring physical and mental health conditions. This merits further investigation into the role of these exercise modalities in managing comorbid conditions. Further scrutiny of the feasibility and effectiveness of once-weekly HIIT in the context of managing obesity-related comorbidities (e.g., obesity and diabetes) is warranted. Furthermore, research is needed to examine whether modest reductions in adiposity induced by low-frequency HIIT can result in clinically important health benefits (e.g., reduced risk of all-cause mortality, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and site-specific cancers) for patients with obesity in the long term. Finally, future research should investigate the feasibility of low-frequency HIIT in real-world settings to enhance its public health implications. In particular, interventions employing differing levels of supervision are needed to determine the effectiveness and applicability of this exercise modality in more practical settings and patient populations. Accordingly, the encouraging result of this project provides the basis and motivation for continued exploration in the application of low-frequency HIIT for managing different critical public health issues.

17105920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105920.value: This research project investigated the effectiveness of once-a-week and thrice-a-week high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on adiposity and cardiometabolic risk factors in adults with central obesity. Participants were randomly assigned to the once-weekly HIIT, thrice-weekly HIIT, or control group. Body fat mass and cardiometabolic risk factors were assessed before and after the 16-week intervention. Findings demonstrate that 75 minutes of HIIT per week performed in a once-a-week (H1) and thrice-a-week (H3) frequency can produce modest yet meaningful reductions in body fat (relative reduction from baseline: H1 = –2.6%; H3 = –3.5%). Moreover, significant improvements in waist circumference and cardiorespiratory fitness were exhibited by both frequencies of HIIT compared to the control group. Importantly, no significant difference was observed for any measure of adiposity between the once-weekly and thrice-weekly HIIT groups. This suggests that once-weekly HIIT, a more time-efficient exercise modality, is of comparable effectiveness to thrice-weekly HIIT in managing excess adiposity. The project reported no adverse events and a high completion rate of 94% at post-intervention. This study provides robust evidence that 75 minutes of HIIT performed once-a-week is safe and effective and confers improvements in excess adiposity (fat mass), central adiposity (waist circumference), and cardiorespiratory fitness in centrally obese adults.

17106320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106320.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a prototype autoimmune disease that mainly affects women of child-bearing age, characterized by autoantibody production and multi-organ damage. Genetic factors play a vital role in the etiology of the disease, and there is a significant difference between major ethnicities on the prevalence and manifestations of SLE. We are among the first to conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) on SLE, and a recent effort identified 38 novel loci for the disease. A number of associated loci showed clear population differences between European and East Asian populations. Many of the population different susceptibility loci are involved in B cell development and function, raising an intriguing possibility that differences in humoral immunity might at least partially explain ethnic differences in SLE and other autoimmune diseases. In this study, we are going to study the impact of genetic factors as categorized in three levels. 1). the role of the TACI mutation that is associated with SLE susceptibility only in Asians but not in Europeans, 2). a selected subset of associated genetic variants that mainly affect B cell survival, development and function, and 3). A genome-wide polygenic risk core reflecting the overall genetic susceptibility to SLE. For these three levels of genetic factors, we will study their effect on clinical subphenotypes, disease activities, onset age and disease outcomes to detect the role of genetics on clinical manifestations. We will also study healthy controls stratified by highest risk and lowest risk groups for these genetic factors to study their roles on B cell-focused endophenotypes, such as B cell subsets, relevant cytokines, immunoglobulin levels and autoantibody production. This study promises to help us understand the roles of genetics in stratifying patients to understand the heterogeneity of the disease and in risk prediction for healthy individuals. 17106520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106520.value: This proposal will investigate the mechanism underlying flavivirus transmission from infected host cells in specialized secretory organelles, generated by viral manipulation of the host secretory pathway. We will therefore address a longstanding debate on how Dengue and Zika viruses exit from infected cells and determine whether their mode of transmission dictates tropism and pathogenesis. Dengue infects approximately 400 million people annually, often causing severe pathologies such as vascular endothelial leakage. ZIKV too has emerged as a global threat with recent outbreaks linked to serious neuro-developmental complications in children and Guillain Barré syndrome in adults. No effective vaccines or therapeutics are currently available, along with scant information on mechanisms of tissue tropism and viral pathogenesis. Secretion of progeny virions from infected cells is the final stage in the intracellular virus lifecycle. We previously determined that Dengue progeny virions hijacked KDEL receptor carrying transport vesicles to arrive at the Golgi from the ER, accompanied by activation of the Src-family kinases (SFKs). We therefore performed systematic analyses of SFK-activation to establish that anterograde transport from the Golgi compartments required membrane targeting and Lyn kinase activity to trigger biogenesis of secretory organelles resembling autophagosomes. In the absence of Lyn, these organelles are redirected for lysosomal degradation. Building on our results, we have hypothesized that Dengue/Zika virus co-opts Lyn kinase to generate specialized secretory autophagosomes for exiting infected cells. These organelles emerge from the Golgi compartments, are secreted more efficiently than conventional exocytosis, and likely enable immune evasion from circulating antibodies. In this proposal we aim to define this process of secretion triggered during infection in three specific aims: (1) characterise virus-containing secretory autophagosomes using biochemical and imaging analyses, (2) functionally validate host genes in this pathway using: (a) CRISPR/Cas-mediated gene-editing and (b) pharmacological inhibitors against specific genes, (3) determine how viral structural proteins trigger biogenesis of secretory autophagosomes and its implications on tissue tropism and pathogenesis. 17106620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106620.value: 脊椎動物的發育是一個複雜的過程，其中多輪細胞分裂，再加上細胞命運的指定和細胞運動，導致建立體軸和模式。在估計包含40萬億個細胞的成年人體內，有230多種分化的細胞類型形成了各種組織/器官。這種複雜的發展過程是由多種信號通路協調的。Hedgehog（HH）信號以信號分子（Sonic HH，Indian HH和Desert HH）命名，代表了一種需要適當調節的途徑。已經表明，HH信號缺乏會導致與腦部和麵部特徵畸形相關的發育障礙，而已知HH信號增加會增強幹細胞增殖，從而導致諸如基底細胞癌的癌症。 包含多個PDZ域的蛋白質2（PDZD2）在多個成人組織/細胞中普遍表達。我們以前證明全長PDZD2蛋白可以被蛋白水解切割，以產生分泌形式sPDZD2作為信號分子。與其在小鼠早期發育過程中緊靠HHs的表達相一致，最近發現sPDZD2對雛雞神經管和瞬時報告基因檢測中的HH信號傳導具有負調節作用。我們懷疑sPDZD2通過與G蛋白偶聯受體（GPR）結合而信號傳遞，因為重組sPDZD2給予胰島素瘤細胞系INS-1E刺激了cAMP水平，並且使用蛋白激酶A抑製劑可以抑制所產生的下游效應。有趣的是，還發現孤兒受體GPR161（具有未知配體）通過促進GLI3的蛋白水解過程以通過PKA依賴性機制產生阻遏物GLI3R來抑制HH信號傳導。重要的是，我們最近證明了sPDZD2在雛雞神經管測定中增強了GPR161對HH信號的負面作用。此外，RNA原位雜交分析表明，Gpr161和Pdzd2在小鼠神經管，肢芽和晶狀體中緊密表達，並且sPDZD2和GPR161可以在體外相互免疫沉澱。 基於這些最新發現，我們假設sPDZD2是孤兒受體GPR161的配體，並且sPDZD2的負HH調節作用是通過PPR依賴性機制中的GPR161介導的。在這裡，我們提出了兩行實驗來研究sPDZD2和GPR161在HH信號負調控中的潛在串擾。首先，將在小鼠胚胎成纖維細胞（MEF）進行GPR161敲除/敲除或GPR161瞬時過表達後（不論是否使用sPDZD2處理），研究sPDZD2-GPR161相互作用的功能相關性，以研究cAMP，GLI3和GLIR水平的變化和使用Hli熒光素酶報導基因監測HH信號活性。此外，我們將定義GPR161胞外域內的關鍵相互作用區域/氨基酸，該區域通過缺失和定點誘變介導其與sPDZD2的相互作用。 sPDZD2-GPR161相互作用有缺陷的突變體將在雛雞神經管試驗中研究其對HH信號的影響。第二，Pdzd2 +/-；與Pdzd2和Gpr161單突變同窩仔相比，將產生從E9.5到E18.5的Gpr161 +/-雙雜合突變突變體胚，以檢測對神經管，肢芽和晶狀體發育的加重作用。 HH信號和模式缺陷將通過免疫印跡，免疫染色和RNA原位雜交進行分析。綜上所述，擬議的研究將揭示sPDZD2與GPR161在HH信號的負調節中的假定夥伴關係，這是人們普遍關心的問題，也是設計更好的在疾病條件下擾動HH信號傳導策略的前提。

17106620.label: Realisation of objectives
17106620.value: Objective 1: To study the interaction of sPDZD2 and GPR161 in vitro using MEFs and chick neural tube as model systems (100% realized) We previously demonstrated that overexpression of sPDZD2 in chick neural tube by electroporation led to suppression of Hh signaling. In this project, we further studied the mechanism of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling using the MEF cell line C3H10T1/2. Although addition of recombinant sPDZD2 at 10-7 to 10-12 M did not affect basal Hh signaling as reflected by GLI3R processing and expression of Hh direct targets (Gli1 and Ptc transcripts), sPDZD2 at 10-10 and 10-11 M could counteract ectopic Hh signaling induced by Purmorphamine (Pur). Pur is a Hh agonist that directly acts on SMO and activates downstream intracellular signaling. sPDZD2 at 10-10 M was also shown to counteract Gli1 expression induced by recombinant SHH. This negative effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling could also be demonstrated by transient transfection and is reminiscent of the negative effect of GPR161 and PATCHED (PTC) similarly tested. Besides gain-of-function study, we depleted PDZD2/sPDZD2 expression using both shRNAs and gRNAs in C3H10T1/2 cells and studied the effect on Hh signaling. Interestingly, suppression of endogenous PDZD2/sPDZD2 expression led to induction of basal Hh signaling as reflected by reduced GLI3R level but increased Gli1 and Ptc expression, consistent with sPDZD2 being a negative regulator of Hh signaling. We hypothesize that GPR161 might be the GPCR that mediates the negative effect of sPDZD2, which was previously shown to stimulate PKA/cAMP signaling in pancreatic beta-like cells. As a first test, we performed whole mount RNA in situ hybridization analysis to show that Gpr161, similar to Pdzd2, is expressed in the somites and distal limb bud mesenchyme in E9.5 and E11.5 mouse embryos, respectively. To investigate whether sPDZD2 interacts with GPR161 physically, epitope-tagged sPDZD2 and GPR161 were co-transfected into HEK293 cells followed by pull-down assay. We detected reciprocal pull-down of the two proteins which was lost when both PDZ domain 5 and 6 were deleted from sPDZD2 (in construct sPDZD2-DelC), suggesting that the PDZ domains are critical for the sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction. The sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction was also validated using Nano-Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer (Nano-Bret) assay. Interestingly, in both pull-down and Nano-Bret assays, sPDZD2 also interacted with PTC but not with SMO. To test the functional relevance of the sPDZD2/GPR161 interaction, sPDZD2 and GPR161 were overexpressed individually or in combination by in ovo electroporation. Overexpression of sPDZD2 and GPR161 individually resulted in decreased expression of the Hh target NKX2.2 by 50% and 30%, respectively. Importantly, co-expression of sPDZD2, but not the truncated form (sPDZD2-DelC), and GPR161 showed more than 60% reduction of NKX2.2-expressing cells, suggestive of additive effect in the negative modulation of Hh signaling. We wondered whether sPDZD2 exerts its negative effect on Hh signaling exclusively via GPR161. To test this notion, we generated MEFs from Gpr161-/- mice and tested whether the ability of sPDZD2 to suppress Hh signaling induced by Pur would be lost. To our surprise, 10-10 M sPDZD2 could still counteract the induced Hh signaling in Gpr161-/- MEFs, indicating that the negative modulation was not abrogated in the absence of GPR161. We believe that the action of sPDZD2 was not entirely GPR161-dependent as sPDZD2 was also shown to interact with PTC. These findings reflect the complexity of sPDZD2 signaling which might be mediated by multiple receptors. These findings were included in a manuscript ready for submission to Dev. Biol. We did not pursue RNA-seq analysis using MEFs due to the fact that these cells are not equivalent to the somites and limb buds in which we detected the sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction and also due to the paucity of funding and resource. Instead, we devoted more of our effort to characterize the functional relevance of the sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction in vivo (see Objective 2 below). Besides studying the developmental role of PDZD2/sPDZD2, we addressed its relevance in the regulation of eye function due to the statistically significant association of a PDZD2 SNP with primary open angle glaucoma, a major cause of blindness worldwide. Using the human neuronal progenitor cell line NT2 as model, we showed that depletion of PDZD2/sPDZD2 expression by RNA interference led to dysregulation of Hh signaling, consistent with the MEF and chick neural tube studies (PhD thesis work of Ms Lam Yan Yi who was supported by this grant). In fact, further animal study revealed interesting glaucoma-like phenotypes in Pdzd2-deficient mice. These findings together with our analysis of the PDZD2 SNP are being prepared into a manuscript for submission to Heliyon. Objective 2: To study the functional relevance of the sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction in vivo using double heterozygous Pdzd2+/-; Gpr161+/- embryos (100% realized) We generated a floxed Pdzd2 allele using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to allow deletion of mouse exon 19 (the largest and most conserved exon carrying the caspase-3 cleavage site critical for sPDZD2 synthesis) after crossing with beta-actin-cre mice. Whole mount RNA in situ hybridisation of Pdzd2-/- embryos showed loss of Pdzd2 expression at E11.5. Pdzd-/- mice could survive and showed no observable phenotypes comparing to wild type littermates, suggesting that there might be compensatory effects to bypass embryonic lethality. To investigate the possible genetic interaction of Pdzd2 and Gpr161 in vivo, Pdzd2+/- mice were crossed with Gpr161+/- mice to generate the double mutant Pdzd2+/-: Gpr161+/- to study whether deleting one copy of Pdzd2 will lead to aggravation of phenotypes in Gpr161 heterozygous background. Homozygous Gpr161 mutant mice was previously shown to be embryonic lethal at around E10 due to cardiac defects and open fore/mid brain regions whereas Gpr161+/- mice survived and exhibited no observable phenotype. Interestingly, qPCR analysis of trunk tissues (consisting of mainly neural tube and paraxial mesoderm) harvested from E9.5 mice revealed that Gli1 levels were increased by 6-fold in double heterozygotes when compared against the single heterozygotes, supporting up-regulation of Hh signaling. During limb patterning, Shh was known to develop a Hh gradient from posterior to anterior of the limb bud to positively regulate expression of the direct Hh target Hoxd13. Importantly, Hoxd13 expression was shown to be stimulated in E11.5 limb buds harvested from the Pdzd2+/-: Gpr161+/- double mutant but not in the single mutants by RNA in situ hybridisation analysis. As control, Fgf8 similarly analysed did not show any observable change. qPCR analysis of the limb buds also revealed that both Gli1 and Hoxd13 transcripts were increased by 10-fold in the double mutants comparing to the single mutant littermates. Taken together, our studies indicate a novel negative regulatory role of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling mediated via GPR161, which was confirmed in both cell and animal models.

17106620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106620.value: Using the MEF cell line C3H10T1/2 as model, we characterised the negative modulatory effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling after its upregulation by Pur and SHH treatment. The suppressive effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling could also be shown by shRNA-mediated knockdown and gRNA-medated gene knockout. Interestingly, we could detect physical interaction of sPDZD2 with GPR161 and PTC, but not SMO by immunoprecipitation and Nano-Bret assays. The sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction could be abrogated by deletion of the C-terminus of sPDZD2 which carries two PDZ domains, hinting that the C-terminus is the critical interaction interface with GPR161. Importantly, sPDZD2 and GPR161 were demonstrated to show additive effect on the negative regulation of Hh signaling after overexpression by ovo electroporation into chick neural tube. The additive effect was lost with the deletion of the putative interacting C-terminus of sPDZD2. However, The negative effect of sPDZD2 was not suppressed in MEFs generated from Gpr161-/- embryos, indicating that the modulatory effect was not solely mediated via GPR161 and there might be compensatory regulation of downstream mediators of sPDZD2 regulation. This finding is also consistent with the interaction of sPDZD2 and PTC we could detect in vitro. We went on to demonstrate the physiological relevance of the sPDZD2-GPR161 interaction using double heterozygous Pdzd2+/-; Gpr161+/- embryos. Project funds were spent in the generation of the Floxed Pdzd2 allele, breeding of the founder mice against a beta-actin cre line and then Gpr 161 knockout mice to generate double mutants at E9.5 and E11.5. Suppression of Pdzd2 expression was shown to exhibit additive effect with Gpr161 deficiency in the regulation of Hh signaling by qPCR and immunostaining analyses in both developmental stages. However, the functional effect detected was found to be transient as there was no overt phenotypes, suggestive of compensatory changes in gene expression during early development. In summary, we provided both in vitro and in vivo data to support a novel negative regulatory role of sPDZD2 in the regulation of Hh signaling via interaction with GPR161. These findings were included in a manuscript ready for submission to Development Biology (see Part C Research Output). In addition, a PhD student was trained and supported by this GRF grant to study the role of sPDZD2 in the regulation of Hh signaling in the eyes using both NT2 cells and our Floxed Pdzd2 mice. Novel findings about the eye regulation are being prepared into a manuscript for submission to Heliyon.

17106620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106620.value: Our findings pave the way for further exploring the involvement of sPDZD2 in diseases and future therapeutic strategies to tune down Hh signaling. First, PDZD2/sPDZD2 have been implicated in diseases like cancer and primary open-angle glaucoma. ELISA assay and/or mass spectrometry can be designed to monitor sPDZD2 levels for diagnostic purpose. Second, since sPDZD2 mediates its effect via both GPR161 and PTC (Patched), it is worthwhile to explore the relative importance of these receptors in mediating sPDZD2 action. Double Pdzd2+/-; Ptc +/- and triple Pdzd2+/-; Gpr161 +/-; Ptc +/- mutant embryos/mice would need to generated for expression and phenotypic analyses. It remains to be analysed whether the Gpr161 and Ptc genes cross-regulate each other transcriptionally and post-transcriptionally. These studies are prerequisite for further drug screening of sPDZD2 analogs for tuning down Hh signaling in different cells/tissues. Third, sPDZD2 was recently shown to regulate hematopoiesis in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. We have established research link with Prof Figueroa at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine to further pursue the role of sPDZD2 as tumor suppressor in AML. We have shared with them our antibodies/serum and recombinant protein to support their analysis of both mouse and human samples.

17106620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106620.value: Precise communication among cells via signal transduction pathways is crucial during development. Deregulation of the Hedgehog (Hh) signaling pathway is known to cause developmental diseases and cancer. Recently, we discovered that secreted PDZD2 (sPDZD2) acts as a novel negative modulator of Hh signaling. Understanding the underlying mechanism of action of PDZD2, including its receptor, would reveal how Hh signaling can be tuned down to treat developmental disorders and cancer. In this project, we compared sPDZD2 to other known negative regulators like GPR161 and PTC (both receptors) in Hh regulation. Interestingly, we detected a specific interaction of sPDZD2, through its two PDZ domains, with GPR161. When over-expressed in the chick neural tube, sPDZD2 and GPR161 were shown to additively affect negative regulation of Hh signaling. The physiological relevance of this interaction was confirmed by expression analysis of early embryos missing one copy of each of the Pdzd2 and Gpr161 genes. However, GPR161 is not the sole mediator of sPDZD2 action, as the sPDZD2 effect was not abolished in GPR161 deficient cells, and sPDZD2 was also shown to interact specifically with PTC. Taken together, these novel findings reveal a complicated regulatory network mediated by sPDZD2 and Hhs and their downstream receptors.

17106720.label: Realisation of objectives
17106720.value: 1) Successful reprogramming of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from patients with tricuspid atresia (TA): We recruited three patients with TA and reprogrammed iPSCs from the peripheral CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells. Immunofluorescence staining of iPSCs markers, SSEA-4; OCT3/4; TRA-1-81 and SOX2 indicated the successful cell line establishment. Cardiomyocytes (CMs) were generated from these three TA-iPSC lines and three healthy control-iPSC lines through embryoid body differentiation. 2) Gene expression in early stage of cardiac differentiation: Animal models of TA suggest the involvement of second heart field (SHF) progenitors and endocardial cells. Therefore, we aimed to capture the corresponding population in the early in vitro cardiac differentiation and performed single-cell RNA sequencing at 24 and 120 hours post-WNT inhibition (Day 5 and Day 9). On Day5, 37757 cells from 3 TA-iPSC and control-iPSC in vitro cardiac differentiation were retained for analysis after pre-processing and filtering. Similar to our previous publication, three lineages, endoderm (SOX17+/FOXA2+), mesoderm (MESP1+/MESP2+) and ectoderm (POU5F1+/SOX2+), were identified. Re-clustering of the mesodermal lineage (16549 cells) identified two main populations, lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) (CFC1+/HAND1+) and endothelial progenitors (EPs) (ETV2+/KDR+/FLT1+). Within the LPM population, it was further divided into two populations characterized by LEFTY2 and CDH11 expressions. In vivo LPM gives rise to SHF and subsequently contribute to the tricuspid valve formation. Yet, we did not identify significant differences in the distribution of the LPM population between TA and control groups. In addition to the comparable distribution, the transcriptome was largely comparable between TA-iPSC-LPM and control-iPSC-LPM with less than 20 DEGs identified in each TA lines. Therefore, our TA-iPSCs were comparable to the control-iPSCs in the early stages of cardiac differentiation. 3) Differential gene expression in later stage of differentiation: On Day 9, we identified multiple cardiac lineage descendants (21330 cells), including early differentiated ventricular (v) CMs (TNNT2+/MYL3+), SHF (ISL1+/NKX2-5+) and SHF-derived cardiac mesenchyme (ISL1+/S100A11+). For the endothelial cells (ECs), we also identified three distinct populations (2449 cells), deriving from the endodermal lineage (EPCAM+/TTR+) or cardiac lineage (NKX2-5+/TNNT2+) and the endothelial progenitors (PLVAP+/PECAM1+ without endodermal or cardiac expression). We compared the TA cells with the control cells in each population and found that they were largely comparable, except those derived from TA2. We found significant downregulation of TOP2A, in both iPSC-SHF and iPSC-vCMs, from TA2 compared to the counterparts from the control. In addition to the cell cycle gene, we found significant downregulation of both HAPLN1 and COL1A1, in TA2 iPSC-SHF and iPSC-ECs from cardiac lineage. TA2-iPSC mesenchyme also showed significant downregulation of HAPLN1. In short, the transcriptomic analysis on Day 9 in vitro cardiac differentiation suggested a lower proliferation rate in the TA-iPSC-SHF/CMs and an impaired extracellular matrix remodeling in the TA-iPSC cardiac lineage (SHF/mesenchyme/cardiac derived-ECs). 4) Functional assessment of TA-iPSC-CMs: To examine the electrophysiology and the contractility of the TA-iPSC-CMs, we engineered the iPSC-CMs into cardiac tissue strips, cardiac anisotropic sheet, and cardiac organoid chambers. Cardiac progenitors were sorted out from other lineages (ectoderm and endoderm) on Day 5, differentiation with cTNT% > 80% were fabricated into cardiac engineered tissues. In line with the lack of differential expressing genes (DEGs) related to sarcomeric structure and ion channel/handling in the transcriptomic analysis, the contractility and the action potential duration 50 and 90 (APD 50 and APD90) were comparable between the TA and controls. In summary, the project objectives have been completely achieved.

17106720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106720.value: 1. This is the first successful attempt to differentiate tricuspid atresia patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. 2) Single cell RNA sequencing revealed similar trajectory of the early stage of cardiac differentiation between patients with tricuspid atresia and healthy control subjects. 3) Significant downregulation of TOP2A in iPSC-secondary heart field mesenchyme and ventricular cardiomyocytes and downregulation in HAPLN1 and COL1A1 in iPSC-secondary heart field mesenchyme and endothelial cells suggest impaired proliferation and extracellular matrix remodeling in tricuspid atresia. 4) There is absence of functional abnormalities of iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from patients with tricuspid atresia.

17106720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106720.value: Our findings implicate that the endocardium and extracellular matrix is crucial to the pathogenesis of tricuspid atresia as these might contribute to the endocardial cushion for the valve formation and regulates the growth of ventricular cardiomyocytes. Future studies to differentiate endocardial cells directly and to explore the interaction between endocardial cells and ventricular cardiomyocytes and even model the endocardial cushion formation would shed more light on the pathogenesis of congenital malformation of tricuspid atresia.

17106720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106720.value: Congenital heart disease is the most common congenital defect that affects about 1 in 100 live births. Tricuspid atresia belongs to the important category of hypoplastic right heart syndrome and accounts for 1% to 3% of congenital heart defects. It is characterized by obstruction of the inflow into and outflow from the right heart. The emergence of the human induced pluripotent stem cell technology provides unique opportunities to understand possible pathogenetic mechanisms. This is the first successful attempt to differentiate tricuspid atresia patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. We found that that function of the human induced pluripotent stem cell iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from patients with tricuspid atresia is similar to that of healthy subjects and that the early developmental trajectory of cardiac progenitor cells is similar between patients and healthy subjects. However, we found significant downregulation of genes (TOP2A, HAPLN1 and COL1A1) that are related impaired of proliferation and modeling of the extracellular matrix in the heart. This is the first study to shed potential light on developmental abnormalities of the complex cardiac malformation and pave way for future studies to explore the exact pathogenetic mechanisms and strategies that may reduce the prevalence of complex congenital cardiac malformations.

17106820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106820.value: 擴散磁力共振影像能夠以不具侵入性的方式來描繪人類大腦神經纖維走向，因此也開啟了基於醫學影像技術的神經科學研究。過去十年，世界上眾多神經科學中心均安裝了磁力共振掃描儀，作為研究大腦聯結的一個重要影像工具。然而， 商品化的二維擴散磁力共振影技術只能夠提供有限度的資料品質和低空間解像度 （例如大於 1.5毫米以上的體素大小），推動空間解像度到達毫米等級以下的等向體素大小是幾乎不能實現的。因此，研究人員希望可透過高資料品質和高空間解像度的擴散磁力共振影像來改善追蹤神經纖維的準確性，以及描繪各神經纖維的細節。 有見及此，科學家提出了各種不同設計的三維擴散磁力共振影像技術，來達到1毫米等向體素大小的高解像度擴散磁力共振影像。然而，三維擴散磁力共振影像技術需要較長的掃描時間，因此在資料採集的過程中十分容易受到頭部運動影響，尤其對挑戰性族群採集資料（例如兒童、年長或柏金遜症患者）。而且由三維擴散磁力共振影像取得的三維腦部體積資料，是由多個三維厚切資料所組成，會遭受在切面方向的不均勻訊號影響。所以三維擴散磁力共振影像需要高階的影像重建方法以及額外資料（需要額外採集時間），來修正在切面方向的不均勻訊號問題。目前，三維擴散磁力共振影像是獨特的影像技術，能取得高解像度的大腦神經纖維圖譜，所提供的精細神經纖維圖譜能潛在地提供更多資訊，有助於更進一步了解大腦的發展和疾病。 因此，此研究計劃總體的目標是開發一個能達到高解像度的三維擴散磁力共振影像技術，並具有合理的掃描時間、較少的假影以及免除於頭部運動的影響。首先，我們將會實行一個新型的假性隨機取樣方法，此方法可以使得壓縮感知能應用於單一厚塊的三維擴散磁力共振影像資料採集，因此能夠在不犧牲品質下進行資料採集的加速。然後，我們將開發一個相容於磁力共振的頭部追蹤系統，可應用於三維擴散磁力共振影像的資料採集。此追蹤系統是基於細小無線式的半主動標記，此半主動標記較先前的設計更細小且更輕量。最後，我們將會整合上述頭部追蹤系統和新型的假性隨機取樣方法，建立實時回饋系統，在三維擴散磁力共振影像掃描過程同時進行前瞻性的頭部運動修正。 在成功開發和整合高取樣加速的三維擴散磁力共振影像技術、輕量化的及磁力共振相容的追蹤系統和在臨床掃描儀下的實時回饋系統，將會提供一個穩健和運動免疫的三維擴散磁力共振影像技術，並可用於建立挑戰性族群的高解像度大腦聯結圖譜。

17106820.label: Realisation of objectives
17106820.value: 1. Brief background: 3D diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) enables non-invasive high-resolution mapping of brain fiber pathway at the submillimeter-voxel level, serving as an advanced imaging tool for many neuroscience studies. However, The relatively long scantime of 3D dMRI still limits its applications in both clinical and neuroscience fields. In addition, head motion is a significant problem during 3D dMRI data acquisition because acquiring a complete dataset requires anywhere from a few minutes to half an hour. Although head motion is relatively easy to control, this challenge remains for several healthy and patient populations, such as children, old adults, stroke patients, and Parkinson’s patients. Head motion is a significant problem not only in routine clinical scan but also in neuroscience research. Therefore, there is a need to urge the development of a 3D dMRI technique with more acceptable scan time and immunity to head motion. 2. Goal: The ultimate goal of this project was to enhance 3D dMRI by addressing the two key issues mentioned above (scantime and head motion), thereby improving its feasibility and robustness. 3. Research activities and outputs: Over the 48-month project duration, we have achieved the three objectives proposed in the original project proposal and successfully extended the technical developments to benefit other MRI studies related to the applications of dMRI. Below is a brief summary of the research activities and achievements of each objective. Objective 1: We have successfully developed a highly accelerated 3D dMRI technique based on multi-shot EPI (msEPI) acquisition. To enable this, we developed a pseudo-random data sampling scheme that overcomes the incompatibility between compressed sensing (CS) and 3D msEPI acquisition. This scheme was implemented on the 3D-MUSER pulse sequence by adding blipped gradients on the z-axis concurrent with phase-encoding blips. For the reconstruction of this data, we developed a CS pipeline where the acquired data is first pre-processed to remove ghosting artifacts and measure 3D inter-shot phase variations. By concatenating all segment data from all coils, we composed an encoding matrix to successfully solve the artifact-free image data using a conjugate gradient method. During this development, we discovered that the reconstruction performance is highly affected by the sampling density (the sampling pattern distribution in k-space). By considering the hardware constraints and EPI sampling requirement (maintaining consistent off-resonance effect across data sampling), we further designed a variable density sampling pattern with CAIPI optimization for 3D dMRI acquisitions with either single-thick slab or multi-thick slabs to cover the whole brain, achieving 3- to 4-fold acceleration using only a 12-channel head coil. In addition, we also successfully integrated the developed reconstruction method with our previously proposed sliding slab profile encoding (SLIPEN) for simultaneously suppressing slab-boundary artifact in multi-slab data and recovering fully-sampled data from the accelerated slab acquisition with variable-density sampling. In summary, we have completely achieved the goals of Aim #1 by developing a novel pseudo-random sampling scheme with variable sampling density and a corresponding CS reconstruction pipeline, thereby achieving significant scan acceleration for 3D dMRI. Objective 2: We have successfully developed an effective head motion tracking system for 3D dMRI, consisting of a novel omnidirectional marker based on three tiny wireless coils, a fast tracking sequence, and an evaluation platform. Our design showed insignificant tracking error and temperature increase, with a full 6-DoF tracking capability inside the MRI scanner. For motion extraction, we successfully implemented a fast tracking MRI sequence that can obtain projection signals along three orthogonal dimensions with an approximate tracking rate of 25ms under an MRI scanner with moderate hardware performance. This sequence uses a non-selective RF pulse to trigger the wireless coils, amplifying the signal of the MRI contrast agent solution (i.e., Gd) inside the markers to localize the marker location along arbitrary orientation within the MRI scanner. To reduce interference between the signals arising from the subject and the markers, we applied a phase-field dithering method with a spoiler gradient. We successfully extracted the position of each marker from the acquired signals by transforming them into 1D projection profiles and using a sub-pixel localization method to improve localization accuracy. The physical 3D translation and rotation due to head motion were then successfully resolved from these positions using a rigid-body transformation. To rigorously evaluate the precision and accuracy of our tracking system, we built an MRI-compatible robot capable of generating linear motion. Furthermore, to address potential off-resonance effects that could cause position shifts in the projection profile, we implemented a bipolar readout for the tracking sequence, using the reversed gradient method to compensate for the local off-resonance effect without external calibration. This off-resonance effect can cause significant scan-parameter dependent error in localization, which can be significantly reduced by using the proposed method. This development has also led to the filing of a patent application. In summary, we have completely achieved the objectives of Aim #2 by developing a novel lightweight omnidirectional wireless marker, an efficient motion extraction sequence, thereby enabling a robust head motion tracking system suitable for 3D dMRI, even in challenging populations. Objective 3: We have successfully developed and validated a real-time feedback system on the MRI scanner for prospective motion correction in 3D dMRI data acquisition. In the initial stage of this objective, we encountered an issue regarding the software compatibility between HeartVista® research software (RTHwak® and SpinBench®) and the operation software version for our research MRI scanner. We then tested a potential development platform offered by the MRI vendor and decided to switch to this vendor-specific platform by purchasing software licenses with an upgrade supported by the project budget. This vendor-specific platform allows the programming of internal software and the modification of pulse sequence code to enable real-time data streaming and the transfer of data messages between the host computer and the hardware acquisition component. We have successfully developed a tracking module that streamed the raw projection data to the geometric estimation/update module, where a rigid-body transformation extracted the 6-DoF motion. We then successfully used this information to generate an updated rotation matrix and receiver settings, which were applied to the imaging module for a dynamic scan plane update. We successfully established the program architecture and preliminarily validated the data streaming and processing pipeline for real-time motion tracking and compensation. To ensure the feasibility of dynamic scan plane updates, we optimized the sequence parameters to reduce EPI-related artifacts by considering the limit of gradient coil performance, ensuring the scan plane update did not exceed hardware constraints. To address the varying eddy current effects caused by scan plane changes, we developed a robust self-reference 2D phase correction method for both 2D and 3D multi-shot EPI, effectively suppressing Nyquist ghost artifacts. Finally, we conducted an in-vivo evaluation to validate the efficacy of the prospective motion tracking system during different head motion conditions. In summary, we have completely achieved the objectives of Aim #3 by developing an integrated real-time feedback system, optimizing the sequence for dynamic updates, and validating the effectiveness of motion tracking through in-vivo testing.
