17113720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113720.value: Rationale: An ageing population is a global public health issue, as it is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. In particular, it represents the most important risk factor for morbidities such as hypertension and dementia. Hypertension is also associated with risk of incident dementia. The exposure to antihypertensive drugs seems to have a class-dependent protective or harmful effect in development of dementia. Objectives: The primary objective is to compare the incidence of dementia in patients exposed to different classes of antihypertensive drugs. The secondary objectives are 1) to compare incidence of different subtypes of dementia (including Alzheimer’s Disease, vascular dementia, and other dementia subtypes) in patients exposed to different classes of antihypertensive drugs; 2) to compare the incidence of dementia in patients exposed to centrally-acting vs non-centrally acting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors; and 3) to compare the incidence of Alzheimer’s disease in patients exposed to centrally-acting vs non-centrally acting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. Hypothesis: Antihypertensive use will lower the risk of dementia depending on the drug class, however, the use of centrally-acting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors may increase the risk of Alzheimer’s disease when compared to non-centrally acting ones. Design and subjects: Population-based cohort study. People aged 40 or older who received antihypertensive drugs prescriptions. Study instruments: Multi-database individual level data collected from electronic health records from four different databases across Asia and European countries with a cohort size of over 36 million individuals. Intervention: The exposure to antihypertensive drugs. Main outcome measures: The hazard ratio of incident dementia and their subtypes. Data analysis and expected results: Cox regression will be used. We expect that the risk of incident dementia varies among the certain antihypertensive exposed groups when compared to other antihypertensive classes. Centrally-acting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors may demonstrate an increased risk for incident Alzheimer’s disease when compared to non-centrally acting ones. 研究背景：人口老化帶來的高死亡率和高發病率導致其成為一項全球關注的公共衛生問題。¬¬作為高危險因素的高血壓和認知障礙症問題尤為突出。高血壓也與認知障礙症的發生率有關。使用不同類型降血壓藥可能對認知障礙症的發生具有保護或有害作用。 研究目的：本研究的主要研究目的是比較不同降血壓藥使用者認知障礙症發病率的不同。次要目的是: 1) 比較認知障礙症不同類型（包括阿氏痴呆症，血管性癡呆症，和其他痴呆症）在不同降血壓藥使用者中的發病率；2）比較作用於中樞神經與非中樞神經的血管緊張素轉換酶抑制藥（ACEI）使用者的認知障礙症發病率；3）比較作用於中樞神經與非中樞神經的ACEI阿氏痴呆症的發病率。 研究假設：不同降血壓藥可以不同程度的降低認知障礙症發病的風險。與非中樞神經性ACEI相比，作用於中樞神經的ACEI阿氏痴呆症發生的風險。 研究設計：本課題為基於人群的隊列研究，納入樣本為40歲及以上有降血壓藥處方的患者。 研究工具：課題從來自於亞洲和歐洲的四個電子數據庫中採集樣本數據建立多人群數據庫。該數據來源包含超過3600萬人的健康信息。 干預指標：使用降血壓藥 主要結局變量：認知障礙症及分型發生的危險比 數據分析及預期結果：課題將採用Cox回歸進行數據分析。課題組預期使用不同的降血壓藥的人群有不同的認知障礙症發生率。相比於非中樞神經的ACEI的降血壓藥，作用於中樞的ACEI可能會提高阿氏痴呆症發生的風險。

17113720.label: Realisation of objectives
17113720.value: To achieve the primary objective, a large multinational population-based cohort study was conducted comparing the use of different classes of antihypertensive drugs and the risk of incident dementia. Data was extracted from electronic health databases in Hong Kong, United Kingdom, Sweden, and Australia to conduct this study. Six drug class comparison groups were included, defined as angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI), angiotensin-II receptor blockers (ARB), beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, diuretics, and two or more concurrent antihypertensive classes used concurrently (Combination). The incidence of all-cause dementia was estimated by following up patients in the longitudinal retrospective data who initiated different antihypertensive drug classes and were compared with ACEI users as the reference group. ACEI was chosen as the reference group as it is a common first-line antihypertensive and because of the emerging angiotensin hypothesis in dementia pathology. A common protocol approach was used to execute the multinational study to harmonise the study design and ensure high scientific standards. Study analysis was conducted in each individual study site to keep patient confidentiality and the results were pooled together for interpretation. The secondary objective of comparing the incidence of subtypes of dementia including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD) was also achieved in this study by breaking down the primary outcome of all-cause dementia to its subtypes. For secondary objectives 2 and 3, a cohort study using the data from Hong Kong was conducted to compare the use of centrally-acting and non-centrally acting ACEI and the incidence of dementia and Alzheimer’s disease. This study could not be conducted in all study sites in the multinational collaboration as not all the included databases could differentiate between centrally-acting and non-centrally acting ACEI or dementia subtypes.

17113720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113720.value: In the multinational cohort study, 1,982,839 individuals were included across the four databases with a median follow-up time ranging from 5.6 to 8.4 years. The pooled results showed that when compared with ACEI, ARB had a reduced risk of all-cause dementia (Hazard ratio (HR): 0.92, 95% Confidence interval (CI): 0.89-0.94) and VaD (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.78-0.96) but not AD. The findings suggest that ARB may be a safer alternative for antihypertensive initiation compared with ACEI in terms of dementia risk. Clinicians and patients should consider the reduced risk of dementia with ARB compared with ACEI in their risk-benefit assessment when initiating antihypertensives. This is the largest multinational cohort study conducted to date investigating the use of different antihypertensive drug classes and the risk of incident dementia. The publication is currently under review in European Heart Journal (Impact factor 37.6; Rank 2 out of 220 in CARDIAC & CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEMS), which has been sent out to peer reviewers for comments. The manuscript under review is enclosed in section 8 item 1. The preliminary results have also been presented in a conference. The abstract is enclosed in section 9 item 3. In the study investigating the risk of dementia and AD between centrally-acting and non-centrally acting ACEI, initiation with centrally-acting ACEI had a reduced risk of AD (HR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.59-0.98) but no evidence of a difference in risk of all-cause dementia. The findings from this study suggest that the differentiation between centrally-acting and non-centrally acting ACEI may be important when considering the risk of AD in patients as this difference in mechanism of action is not a factor that clinicians consider when prescribing ACEI in current guidelines. The final results are presented in an oral presentation. The abstract and presentation slides are enclosed in section 9 item 4. In addition to the output relevant to the stated objectives, we also drafted a manuscript to describe the different prescribing trends of antihypertensive among people with dementia across the 4 databases. The time series analysis results suggested that there was increased vigilance of blood pressure control shortly after dementia diagnosis. Also demonstrating the differences in healthcare systems in disease management among ageing population. The manuscript in preparation is enclosed in section 8 item 2. The results were also presented in conferences. The abstracts are enclosed in section 9 item 1 and 2.

17113720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113720.value: The research undertaken in this project found differences in the risk of incident dementia in users of different antihypertensive drug classes, highlighting the reduced risk of ARB initiation compared with ACEI. In further research of this topic, studies investigating the mechanism of these differences in dementia risk between antihypertensive drug classes are warranted, for example, the role of blood pressure control following antihypertensive initiation. Such studies will require greater data richness to continuously track changes in blood pressure over patient follow-up. Studies in specific subgroups of patients such as those heart failure or other indications of antihypertensives given a greater sample size of patients in these subgroups would also provide evidence to support clinician decision-making when offered a choice of antihypertensive drug classes in different prescribing scenarios. Similar studies comparing the risk of dementia and AD between centrally-acting and non-centrally acting ACEI initiation in other countries would help validate the findings in this project.

17113720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113720.value: In this project, the main research objective was to compare the risk of dementia between patients who started different classes of blood pressure-lowering medication, also known as antihypertensive drugs. This was achieved by conducting a large study following up users of antihypertensives using databases of electronic health records. Almost two million patients were included in this study across four countries/regions, which included Hong Kong, United Kingdom, Sweden, and Australia. The results of this study found that angiotensin-II receptor blockers (ARB) had an approximate 8% reduced risk of dementia compared with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI), which are two common first-line medication classes for treating high blood pressure. When breaking down dementia into its subtypes, ARB also had a reduced risk of vascular dementia compared with ACEI but not Alzheimer’s disease. This is the largest multinational study on this topic conducted to date and the findings of this research project provide evidence on the differences in dementia risk between the use of different antihypertensive classes, aiding clinician decision-making when prescribing medications for patients.

17114520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114520.value: Biliary atresia (BA) is a devastating obstructive bile duct disease affecting 5-20:100,000 newborns, with the highest frequency in Asians, poorly understood, incurable and frequently requires liver transplantation. Kasai surgery is the first line treatment but bile drainage is only re-established in 50% of patients. Moreover, Kasai surgery only replaces the extra-hepatic bile duct, and the intra-hepatic cholangiopathy (bile duct disease) is un-remedied. Hence patients often develop biliary infection and sclerosis, leading to liver failure requiring liver transplantation which presents challenges from organ shortage and long-term immunosuppression. BA thus represents a huge medico-societal problem. There is currently no functional therapy for BA beyond Kasai surgery, and new therapies would be urgently needed. The major pathobiology of non-syndromic BA (the common form) presents peri-natally, hence there are post-natal windows for therapeutic intervention to attempt to slow the progression of disease post-natally for BA. Using liver organoids studies in human and mice, we unexpectedly identified beta-amyloid deposition, the main pathological feature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA), around BA bile ducts uncovers a previously unsuspected disease mechanism, opening the door to innovative treatment strategies for BA. Beta-amyloid blocking or inhibiting approaches are currently evaluated for AD and CAA including lithium salts. We preliminarily showed that lithium mitigates the morphological aberrations of organoids from BA patients. We hypothesized that tackling beta-amyloid accumulation in the liver of BA patients could (i) prevent the disease onset and obviate the need for the relatively ineffective Kasai surgery, and (ii) to ameliorate, prevent or reverse the progression to unrelenting liver fibrosis and obviate the need for liver transplantation. In this proposed study, we will (i) elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which lithium mitigate the morphological aberrations of BA liver organoids; (ii) elucidate if RRA-infection induces aberrant growth/morphologies of liver organoids and its underlying molecular mechanisms; and (iii) evaluate if long-term lithium treatment alleviates BA phenotypes of RRA-infected experimental model for BA and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Our proposed “proof of principle” study will open a completely new avenue to be explored for therapy development in BA, "take out" the disease based on tackling beta-amyloid accumulation. Furthermore, newly identified molecular pathways underlying lithium treatment could be novel therapeutic targets for future drug screening/development for the treatment of BA.

17114920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114920.value: About 10-15% of couples at their reproductive ages experience different types of infertility. Among them, many types of infertility originate from defects in germ cell development caused by dysregulation of meiosis, which produces gametes containing only half of the chromosome number. Starting from 2015, my laboratory has identified around 1,000 novel genes that are up-regulated during prophase I stage of meiosis in mice through RNA sequencing of germ cells. Among these candidate genes, we have identified genes that are essential for meiosis prophase I, such as our recently reported SCRE and Zcwpw1 genes. In this proposal, as ongoing efforts to identify novel molecules controlling germ cell development in mammals, we will systematically study the regulation of another newly identified meiosis-specific gene 4930432K21rik (432K, in short) in meiosis prophase I. This will be achieved by using 432K knockout mouse model together with various cell and molecular biology approaches. The goal is to find out more molecular controls of meiosis and germ cell development. We have generated a 432K knockout mouse model, and our preliminary results show that the development of male germ cells in these mutant mice is defective. We are very interested in studying the mechanisms of how 432K regulates germ cell development, especially its roles in meiosis prophase I in mice. We plan to analyze the reproductive phenotypes observed in the 432K knockout mice, and further investigate the functional roles of 432K in regulating meiosis prophase I. By using our well-established research platform at the University of Hong Kong, we hope to obtain a better understanding of molecular mechanisms underneath meiosis, germ cell development, and controls of fertility and infertility. We hope to find ways to open up new prospects for developing novel treatment of both male and female infertility. The proposed research is therefore of significance for both basic research and for clinical reproductive research. 不孕不育在育龄夫妇中约占10-15%。其中,由减数分裂错误导致生殖细胞发育缺陷是不孕不育的重要病因。本实验室自2015年起一直致力于通过生殖细胞的RNA测序筛选揭示候选基因在第一次减数分裂中的作用，目前已鉴定了约1000个在小鼠第一次减数分裂时期表达上调的新基因。在这些候选基因中，我们团队已经鉴定出多个参与减数分裂过程调控的重要蛋白，包括最近发表的SCRE 和 Zcwpw1 基因。在本项目中，我们将系统的研究另一个全新的减数分裂特异性基因4930432K21rik（简称，432K），拟通过432K敲除小鼠模型以及各种细胞和分子生物学方法阐明432K在减数分裂中的作用机制，并尝试揭示更多调控减数分裂和生殖细胞发育的分子。通过432K敲除小鼠模型，初步结果表明，这些突变小鼠雄性生殖细胞的发育存在缺陷，但是对于432K如何调节生殖细胞发育的机制，特别是它在小鼠第一次减数分裂中的作用机制还有待阐明。因此，我们下一步将重点研究432K在调节第一次减数分裂中的功能。通过香港大学成熟的研究平台，对432K作用的分子机理的揭示将进一步加深我们对减数分裂调控的机制、生殖细胞的发育以及控制生育和不育的分子机理的理解，而且对于开发新的治疗男性和女性不孕症提供了新的可能途径，因此，本项目的开展对于基础研究和临床生殖研究都具有重要意义。

17114920.label: Realisation of objectives
17114920.value: The project “Studies of a novel meiosis-specific protein 432K in meiosis cell cycle and germ cell development in mice” have been completed very well with 100% completion of all goals. In this project, we have independently identified a novel meiosis protein 4930432K21Rik and named it MAMERR (Male Meiosis Recombination Regulator), and showed that it is indispensable for meiosis prophase I progression in male mice. Using super resolution structured illumination microscopy, we found that MAMERR functions at the same double strand breaks as the RPA and MEIOB/SPATA22 complex. We generated a Mamerr-deficient mouse model by deleting exons 3-6 and found that most of Mamerr−/− spermatocytes were arrested at pachynema and failed to progress to diplonema, although they exhibited almost intact synapsis and progression to the pachytene stage along with XY body formation. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the recruitment of DMC1/RAD51 and HSF2BP in Mamerr−/− spermatocytes was only mildly impaired with a partial reduction in DSB repair, whereas a substantial reduction in ubiquitination on the autosomal axes and on the XY body appeared as a major phenotype in Mamerr−/− spermatocytes. We propose that MAMERR may participate in meiotic prophase I progression by regulating the ubiquitination of key meiotic proteins on autosomes and XY chromosomes, and in the absence of MAMERR the repressed ubiquitination of key meiotic proteins leads to pachytene arrest and cell death. The above results were published (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1673852720301272?via%3Dihub) We performed further work to study the functioning mechanisms of MAMERR. We have precisely identified the localization and expression of MAMERR. We also identified that only the isoform 202 of Mamerr is expressed in male germ cells in mice. Additionally, we characterized the changes in MAMERR from leptotene spermatocytes to spermatids, and found that MAMERR gradually translocates from nuclei to cytoplasm in spermatids. This suggests that MAMERR may play a role in spermiogenesis. Gene transcription is strictly regulated during meiosis. Defective meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI) is closely associated with complete meiotic arrest and germ cell apoptosis. Through RNA sequencing analysis of isolated pachytene spermatocytes, we found that MSCI is defective in Mamerr-/- pachytene cells. Moreover, a large number of differentially expressed (DE) genes were observed on autosomes. These results indicate that gene transcription in Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes is globally dysregulated, suggesting that MAMERR is involved in regulating gene transcription during the pachytene stage. Ubiquitination is a common post-translational modification process that plays indispensable roles in key processes such as homologous recombination and sex chromosome silencing during meiosis. We further showed that MAMERR is involved in regulating ubiquitination in the pachytene spermatocytes. Analysis of ubiquitination in Mamerr+/+ and Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes revealed increased ubiquitination, which was confirmed by ubiquitination modification mass spectrometry (Ub-MS) analysis of testes and isolated pachytene spermatocytes. Notably, ubiquitinated sites of meiosis associated proteins, such as ATR, HORMAD1, TOPBP1, SETX, RAD18, and MDC1, were significantly increased in Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes, which may be associated with the failure of MSCI establishment. Furthermore, we generated a mouse model overexpressing MAMERR and found that overexpression of MAMERR in mice resulted in decreased ubiquitination in spermatocytes. Taken together, our results indicate that MAMERR is involved in regulating ubiquitination during pachynema in mouse spermatocytes. We further investigated the potential mechanism of MAMERR in regulating ubiquitination using HEK293T cells. We found that overexpression of MAMERR suppresses ubiquitination. However, in vitro deubiquitinase assays with purified recombinant MAMERR protein showed that MAMERR is not a deubiquitinating enzyme. Considering the intimate structural and functional interplay among MAMERR, HSF2BP, and BRCA2, we speculate that HSF2BP and BRCA2 may also be involved in the ubiquitination regulation process of MAMERR. Remarkably, our experiments showed that overexpression of HSF2BP or truncated BRCA2 significantly enhanced ubiquitination levels. Intriguingly, these increased ubiquitination was reduced upon co-transfection with MAMERR, suggesting that MAMERR's ubiquitination-suppression function may be achieved through its interaction with HSF2BP and BRCA2. In conclusion, we identified new functions of MAMERR in prophase I of meiosis in mice. It is not only a regulatory factor of meiotic recombination but is also involved in the regulation of gene transcription and ubiquitination in mouse pachytene spermatocytes. Although, overexpression of MAMERR in mice can significantly suppress ubiquitination both in vivo and in vitro, and it is not a deubiquitinating enzyme. Its ubiquitination-suppression function may be achieved through its combination with HSF2BP and BRCA2. In Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes, gene transcription are globally dysregulated, MSCI fails to establish, ubiquitination levels are significantly increased, eventually leading to cell apoptosis occurring at the early pachytene stage. Further studies identifying MAMERR’s ubiquitination regulated substrates during meiosis prophase I and how MAMERR regulates ubiquitination at the protein levels will be interesting.

17114920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114920.value: Meiosis is a specialized cell division for producing haploid gametes from diploid germ cells. In this project, we have independently identified a novel meiosis protein 4930432K21Rik and named it MAMERR (Male Meiosis Recombination Regulator), and showed that it is indispensable for meiosis prophase I progression in male mice. Using super resolution structured illumination microscopy, we found that MAMERR functions at the same double strand breaks as the RPA and MEIOB/SPATA22 complex. We generated a Mamerr-deficient mouse model by deleting exons 3-6 and found that most of Mamerr−/− spermatocytes were arrested at pachynema and failed to progress to diplonema, although they exhibited almost intact synapsis and progression to the pachytene stage along with XY body formation. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the recruitment of DMC1/RAD51 and HSF2BP in Mamerr−/− spermatocytes was only mildly impaired with a partial reduction in DSB repair, whereas a substantial reduction in ubiquitination on the autosomal axes and on the XY body appeared as a major phenotype in Mamerr−/− spermatocytes. We propose that MAMERR may participate in meiotic prophase I progression by regulating the ubiquitination of key meiotic proteins on autosomes and XY chromosomes, and in the absence of MAMERR the repressed ubiquitination of key meiotic proteins leads to pachytene arrest and cell death. The above results were published (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1673852720301272?via%3Dihub) Moreover, we identified new functions of MAMERR in meiosis. It is not only a regulatory factor of meiotic recombination but is also involved in the regulation of gene transcription and ubiquitination in pachytene spermatocytes in mice. Although overexpression of MAMERR can significantly suppress ubiquitination both in vivo and in vitro, it is not a deubiquitinating enzyme. Its ubiquitination-suppression function may be achieved through its binding with HSF2BP and BRCA2. In Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes, gene transcription are globally dysregulated, MSCI fails to establish, and ubiquitination levels significantly increase, eventually leading to cell apoptosis occurring at the early pachytene stage. Further studies identifying how MAMERR regulated substrates and how MAMERR regulates ubiquitination at the protein levels will be interesting. We are working to summarize this part of the study into a manuscript, and it also constitutes the major part of the Ph.D. thesis of Mr. Binjie Jiang, who will defend his thesis in August 2024.

17114920.value: In this study, we found that MAMERR can significantly suppress ubiquitination both in vivo and in vitro, but it is not a deubiquitinating enzyme. Its ubiquitination-suppression function may be achieved through its interaction with HSF2BP and BRCA2. Further studies identifying how MAMERR regulate ubiquitination at the protein levels will be interesting. We had already performed Ub-MS analysis and identified differential levels and amino acids of ubiquitination in Mamerr-/- pachytene spermatocytes, and these results will serve as a solid basis for the next efforts in identifying protein targets that MAMERR regulates during meiosis in mice.

17114920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114920.value: Meiosis is a complex and highly ordered physiological process that is crucial for spermatogenesis. During this process, diploid progenitor cells transform into haploid gametes. Meiotic prophase I can be divided into five stages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis. The pachytene stage is the longest stage of meiotic prophase I, during which autosomes undergo complete synapsis, accompanied by DSB repair, crossover formation, and the establishment of meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI). In this project, we have independently identified a novel meiosis protein 4930432K21Rik and named it MAMERR (Male Meiosis Recombination Regulator), and showed that it is indispensable for meiosis prophase I progression in male mice. We further showed that it is not only a regulatory factor of meiotic recombination but is also involved in the regulation of gene transcription and ubiquitination in pachytene spermatocytes in mice. Our findings indicate that MAMERR is an important protein that regulates fertility, whose dysfunction can be the causations of male infertility. Further analyses with clinical samples will reveal how this protein may be involved in patients’ infertility and how it may be used as a gene maker to diagnose male infertility.

17115320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115320.value: During pregnancy, the decidualized endometrium undergoes physiological changes to establish the fetal-maternal interface. A key step to successful pregnancy is transformation of the high-resistance muscular maternal arteries to a low-resistance, high-flow vessels capable of providing sufficient placental perfusion to support the growing fetus throughout the pregnancy. This step is termed remodeling of the spiral arteries and occurs in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. It involves invasion of a special type of trophoblasts, extravillous cytotrophoblast (EVTs) into and subsequent replacement of the lining of the spiral arteries. Failure in remodeling gives rise to pregnancy-associated diseases such as preeclampsia (PE) and fetal growth restriction. Despite research advances in the pathogenesis of PE, up to date, there is no reliable diagnostic test for early prediction of PE. The placental origin of PE is well recognized. Recent studies reveal that impaired endometrial gland function is another cause of PE, though its pathogenesis is unknown. Apart from invading the spiral arteries, EVTs invade the uterine glands from around Day 10 after conception. It has been proposed that the invaded EVT will be transformed into endoglandular trophoblast, which modify uterine gland secretion and indirectly modulates the vascular remodeling functions of other EVT in the deciduas in the first trimester of pregnancy. No proof of the proposal is available yet. This project hypothesizes that dysregulation of endoglandular trophoblast is a cause of PE via affecting EVT invasion and vascular remodeling. A new technique of culturing endometrial glands (endometrial organoid) and co-culture with EVTs will be used to delineate the function of endoglandular trophoblast and their role in PE. The hypothesis is supported by (1) EVTs invaded and modified the cellular composition and secretion of organoids, which regulate functions of EVTs; and (2) Compared to normal pregnancy, the spent media of organoid culture from PE pregnancy induces less EVT invasion. PE is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality affecting 4.6% of pregnancies worldwide. PE is associated with a high incidence of fetal growth restriction and long-term maternal and perinatal complications, and therefore, is a substantial burden to the healthcare system. It is probably the first study on the biological role of endoglandular trophoblast. The outcome of this project will provide confirmatory evidence on the maternal regulation of spiral artery remodeling indirectly via the endometrial glandular secretion. 17115320.label: Realisation of objectives
17115320.value: During pregnancy, the decidualized endometrium undergoes physiological changes to establish a connection between the fetus and the mother. A critical step for a successful pregnancy involves remodeling the maternal spiral arteries. These arteries, initially high-resistance muscular vessels, transform into low-resistance, high-flow vessels capable of supplying sufficient blood to the placenta to support fetal growth. This remodeling process occurs within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy and involves the invasion of specialized placental cells called extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). If vascular remodeling fails, the vessels remain unmodified and may lead to preeclampsia (PE). Recent studies have indicated that impaired endometrial gland function is another contributing factor to PE development, although the exact mechanisms remain unknown. In addition to invading the spiral arteries, EVTs differentiate from the cytotrophoblast in the placental villi and invade the uterine glands, typically starting around Day 10 after conception. This interaction between EVTs and uterine glands is believed to be a two-way communication process. The invaded trophoblasts transform into a unique subset called endoglandular trophoblasts, which then alter the secretion of the uterine glands. This project aims to investigate the roles of endoglandular trophoblasts in mediating EVT invasion and vascular remodeling and explore the potential dysregulation of their differentiation as a possible cause of PE. Human first-trimester placenta and endometrial tissue samples were obtained with written consent from women undergoing surgical abortion and hysterectomy during the mid-luteal phase, respectively. Primary EVTs were isolated through immunomagnetic separation using HLAG antibodies. To form endometrial organoids, endometrial tissues were digested using collagenase and DNase, and endometrial gland fragments were isolated using a 40µm filter. They were then cultured in a chemically defined medium. These organoids were co-cultured with and without EVTs for seven days for subsequent experiments. Confocal microscopy confirmed the EVT invasion towards the organoids. The invaded EVTs were attached to the organoids and transformed from mesenchyme to epithelial morphology. The invasion of EVT towards the endometrial gland was also confirmed by the ex vivo uterine gland invasion model using full-thickness endometrium. The organoids were recovered using a recovery solution and disintegrated by digestion with trypsin, DNase, and collagenase. Endoglandular trophoblasts were then isolated for gene expression analysis. This analysis revealed that the endoglandular trophoblasts co-expressed high levels of trophoblast markers CD9, HLAG, KRT7, and KRT8, as well as endometrial epithelial markers EPCAM, KRT18, and CLDN3. They also expressed secretory endometrial epithelium marker SCGB2A1 and ciliated endometrial epithelium marker TUBA1A/TUBA1B. The data suggested that endoglandular trophoblasts possess features of both EVT and secretory endometrial glands. Gene ontology analysis indicated that the genes expressed by endoglandular trophoblasts positively regulate epithelial cell migration, endothelial cell migration, and myeloid cell differentiation. The expression of trophoblast markers was also confirmed in frozen endometrial tissue sections from non-pregnant endometrium and decidual tissue. The vascular remodeling activity of trophoblasts was determined by their ability to migrate, invade, and subsequently integrate into the endothelial cell network. Spent medium derived from endometrial organoids containing endoglandular trophoblasts induced invasion and migration of primary EVT in transwell assays, without affecting EVT proliferation. This induction of invasion was also supported by the upregulation of matrix metalloproteinase and urokinase activities in the treated EVT. However, the medium did not affect the integration of trophoblasts into endothelial cell networks during EVT-endothelial cell co-culture. In the EVT-mediated spiral artery remodeling process, spent medium derived from endometrial organoids containing endoglandular trophoblasts induced endothelial cell angiogenesis through tube formation assays and permeability through vascular permeability assays. The expression of tight junction proteins, such as occludin, claudin-5, and zonula occludens-1, was reduced as indicated by immunostaining, which is associated with decreased permeability. On the other hand, the medium did not further induce vascular apoptosis through caspase-3 activity assays or endovascular differentiation of EVT by exhibiting any change in the expression of endothelial and epithelial markers. The effect of NFκB signaling on endoglandular trophoblast modulation of organoid secretion was examined. The activation of NFκB in endometrial organoids with endoglandular trophoblasts was confirmed by the NFκB p65 transcription factor assay. Using NFκB inhibitors, BAY-117085 and CAPE, the effects of organoid secretome on trophoblast invasion and endothelial cell functions were studied. Endometrial organoids with endoglandular trophoblasts treated with NFκB inhibitors showed diminished activation of EVT invasion and migration, as well as endothelial cell angiogenesis and permeability. Decidua tissue was obtained from normotensive and early-onset PE and recurrent early-onset PE pregnant women with written consent. The tissue was initially digested with trypsin and the gland tissues were isolated by a 40um filter. The glands were further disintegrated, and dead cells were removed by an immunomagnetic separation kit. The cells were then subjected to 10X genomics analysis. Unexpectedly, the phenotype of the endoglandular trophoblast isolated in this tissue was similar, suggesting that other factors such as the number of endoglandular trophoblasts per endometrial gland would mediate the biological functions in normal and PE pregnancies, which remains to be further investigated. On the other hand, Normotensive/PE/recurrent PE organoids will be produced. Their conditioned media will be collected for proteomics analysis, which identified a total of 447 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between the organoid groups. The DEPs were associated with extracellular structure/matrix organization, humoral immune response, acute inflammatory response, glycosaminoglycan binding, integrin binding, IL-17 signaling pathway, proteasome, complement and coagulation cascades, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis between PE organoid and NT organoid secretion. Among the organoid DEGs, six genes namely Apolipoprotein D (APOD), S100 Calcium Binding Protein P (S100P), LIF Receptor Subunit Alpha (LIFR), Atonal BHLH Transcription Factor 8 (ATOH8), Carbonic Anhydrase 8 (CA8), and KIT Proto- Oncogene, Receptor Tyrosine Kinase (KIT), were selected for further validation based on the set criteria. qPCR analysis suggested that S100P, LIFR, ATOH8, CA8, and KIT mRNA levels were significantly decreased in PE organoids compared with the NT organoids, while APOD increased. The relative expression level of APOD and S100P in the organoid condition medium was measured by ELISA. The abundance of APOD/S100P was significantly higher/lower in the conditioned medium collected from PE organoid than those obtained from NT organoid. The secretome of PE organoid impedes angiogenesis, primary EVTs invasion, and integration, which were evaluated. The secretome of PE organoid impeded capability in endothelial cells to form a tube-like endothelial network compared to the secretion of NT organoid. The secretome of PE organoid also hindered EVTs invasion and integration into the HUVEC network. Such effects were abolished when APOD were suppressed PE organoids via lentivirus or the PE organoids secretome were treated with APOD function-blocking antibody. To validate the results obtained from the analysis of secretome, we selected APOD and S100P (based on proteomics analysis) for further investigation using clinical samples. The levels of these proteins were measured in maternal serum from women who experienced the onset of PE in late pregnancy. The data suggests that APOD levels were up-regulated, while S100P levels were reduced in these pregnant women compared to those with normal pregnancies.

17115320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115320.value: - The endometrium is composed of glandular and luminal epithelia that are supported by stromal connective tissue and various other cell types. The secretion of endometrial glands plays a crucial role in the communication between the human fetus and mother (Li J et al., 2022; Li X et al, 2022; Zhong et al., 2023). In this study, a 3D organoid model was established to investigate the development and functions of endometrial glands. This model accurately replicates the structural and functional characteristics of the glands (Li X et al, 2022; Liu et al, 2022). - Our data suggests that human primary extravillous trophoblasts invade the endometrial organoids, mimicking uterine glands, and differentiate into endoglandular trophoblasts with glandular epithelial phenotypes and functions. Additionally, our spatial transcriptome analysis of placental villi indicates that the genes expressed by the trophoblasts in the placental villi play a role in mediating glandular development, epithelial cell differentiation, and epithelial cell development (Liu et al., 2022). - Endometrial gland secretion during the early stages of pregnancy has been found to enhance the migration and invasion of extravillous trophoblasts, as well as improve endothelial cell functions, compared to those obtained from proliferative/secretory phase organoids (Dong et al, 2023). Additionally, endometrial gland secretion plays a role in mediating the differentiation and functions of decidual macrophages (Lin et al., 2023; Bai et al., 2022, Bai et al., 2023). The glycosylation of the glandular secretory product and the glycan receptor on trophoblasts may contribute to these biological functions (Zhong et al., 2023). - Impaired differentiation of endoglandular trophoblasts leads to abnormal secretion from endometrial glands, resulting in inadequate invasion of extravillous trophoblasts (EVT) and insufficient remodeling of spiral arteries, contributing to the development of preeclampsia (PE) (Dong et al., under preparation). In order to compare the secretome of normal and PE endometrial organoids, our data indicates dysregulation of three endometrial gland secretory factors known as APOD, S100P, and glycodelin-A in the PE organoids. The levels of these proteins were measured in maternal serum from women who experienced the onset of PE in late pregnancy. The data suggests that APOD levels were up-regulated, while S100P and glycodelin-A levels were reduced in these pregnant women compared to those with normal pregnancies (Dong et al., under preparation).

17115320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115320.value: This study provides valuable insights into the role of endoglandular trophoblasts in the development of preeclampsia and the regulation of spiral artery remodeling. However, there are still several areas that could be explored to deepen our understanding and translate the findings into practical applications. Firstly, further studies could investigate the specific mechanisms of how endoglandular trophoblasts differentiate into glandular trophoblasts. By delving deeper into these mechanisms at a molecular level, we could advance our understanding by identifying key targets for interventions and therapeutic strategies to prevent or mitigate preeclampsia. Secondly, based on the important role of glandular secretion in regulating placental development, it is reasonable to speculate that deficiency in normal glandular functions may contribute to the pathophysiology of various pregnancy-associated diseases. We plan to submit a grant application for a clinical study to determine the expression of glandular secretion investigated in this study, in early maternal serum from women who suffer from preeclampsia at term pregnancy. Our aim is to measure the serum levels of these identified proteins from pregnant women at different gestational ages and to determine the expression level and characteristics of these proteins in early maternal blood from women who develop preeclampsia at term pregnancy.

17115320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115320.value: This study aimed to understand the causes of pregnancy-related complications known as preeclampsia, which can be harmful to both the mother and the baby. It is hypothesized that a specific type of placental cells called endoglandular trophoblasts may be responsible for preeclampsia by affecting the remodeling of spiral arteries in the uterus. To test the hypothesis, the endometrial gland organoids were co-cultured with extravillous trophoblasts and observing changes in the secretion of the endometrial gland. Our data provided evidence supporting the idea that the secretion of the endometrial gland plays a role in regulating spiral artery remodeling. The extravillous trophoblasts invade the endometrial gland and change their characteristics, which then influences the secretion of the gland. This impaired differentiation of the endoglandular trophoblasts is associated with inadequate invasion of the spiral arteries and contributes to the development of preeclampsia. The findings of this study provide direct evidence of how the placental cells mediates maternal blood vessel remodeling in the uterus. Additionally, this research could lead to the development of tests that allowing for early detection of preeclampsia, which can help healthcare professionals provide better advice and monitoring for high-risk pregnant women, ultimately reducing the risk of complications.

17115420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115420.value: 早期功能性血管和神經的形成是實現牙髓再生組織血液循環和神經支配的關鍵環節。然而，根管系統的特殊解剖結構使得工程化牙髓組織植入根管後迅速面臨缺氧環境，遠離根尖孔的組織會發生缺氧性壞死，限制了功能性血管和神經的快速建立。因此，要獲得全根管的牙髓組織再生，迫切需要新的方法來提高細胞的存活率以及形成完善的血管和神經網絡。近期研究發現，通過金屬鈷穩定微環境中的缺氧誘導因子-1α是提高移植細胞存活率、促進血管形成的有效途徑。另外，適當的電刺激可促進神經再生。因此，我們提出假設，製備一種新型的鈷摻雜明膠-甲基丙烯酰(GelMA)水凝膠將有效地促進血管新生，且聯合電刺激可以加速神經形成，從而促進牙髓再生。本課題擬通過體內外實驗，系統研究新型導電GelMA水凝膠支架在牙髓再生中對血管生成和神經發生的重要作用。本項目的成功實施有望為獲得全根管的牙髓組織再生以及為複雜組織/器官的治療提供新思路和新策略。

17115420.label: Realisation of objectives
17115420.value: 1. Objective 1 has been fully achieved through in vitro study. In our study, a novel hypoxia-mimicking, multi-walled carbon nanotubes/cobalt (MWCNTs/Co) nanocomposite was prepared using the metal–organic framework (MOF) route for the in situ insertion of MWCNTs into Co3O4 polyhedra. Our results proved that the synthesized MWCNTs/Co nanocomposites possessed a well-designed connecting structure and could release cobalt ions in a sustained way. The MWCNTs/Co nanocomposites at 50 μg/mL significantly upregulated hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) protein expression in SCAP, with no apparent cellular cytotoxicity. The conditioned medium collected from SCAP treated with MWCNTs/Co markedly promoted endothelial cells vessel formation. In conclusion, hypoxia-mimicking MWCNTs/Co nanocomposites exhibit promising angiogenic potential for dental tissue engineering and might provide an alternative solution for translational applications. 2. Objective 2 has been fully achieved through in vitro study. In this study, a three-dimensional (3D) electroconductive gelatin methacryloyl–multi-walled carbon nanotube/cobalt (GelMA–MWCNTs/Co) hydrogel scaffold was fabricated by incorporating MWCNTs/Co composites into a GelMA hydrogel matrix. Our results showed that GelMA–MWCNTs/Co exhibited higher electrical conductivity than GelMA–MWCNTs. Live/dead and CCK8 assays demonstrated the good biocompatibility of the hydrogel for stem cells from apical papilla (SCAP) growth and differentiation. The cells encapsulated in the GelMA–MWCNTs and GelMA–MWCNTs/ Co hydrogel scaffolds exhibited significant neuronal cell-like changes and a notable level of neuronal-specific marker expression after the electrical stimulation (ES) for 7 days, compared to that in the hydrogels without ES. Notably, the neurite spreading and Tuj1 fluorescent intensity of the SCAP in the electrically conductive GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel were more prominent compared to those of the other two groups. In addition, the 3D conductive hydrogel scaffolds advanced the neural differentiation of SCAP to an earlier time point. Considering these aspects, the novel electroconductive GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel provides an ES platform for driving the SCAP towards neural differentiation and a new perspective for the development of neural tissue engineering scaffolds for stem cell-based neural regeneration. 3. Objective 3 has been fully achieved through in vitro and in vivo studies. A controlled release of Co ions from the GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel was successfully achieved, which is well-suited for early-stage vasculogenesis during tissue regeneration. This hydrogel demonstrated excellent biocompatibility for the coculture and growth of HUVECs and SCAP. Notably, SCAP encapsulated in GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel exhibited significantly higher expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) proteins compare to the cells in bare GelMA hydrogel. Immunofluorescence results revealed that significantly longer vessels and increased junctions were formed in GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel compared to the vessels formed in bare GelMA hydrogel. Moreover, the vessels formed within the hydrogel showed the presence of SM22α-expressing SCAP wrapping around the vessel walls. This finding indicates the differentiation of SCAP into pericyte-like cells, which play a crucial role in vascular stability and regulation. Additionally, the 3D GelMA–MWCNTs/Co hydrogel exhibits neurovascular characteristics that facilitated interactions between electrically stimulated induced-SCAP (ES-SCAP) spheres and HUVECs, enhancing vasculogenesis and neurogenesis. Furthermore, in vivo studies demonstrated that the in vitro maturation of microvascular networks within the GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel led to improved blood perfusion and cell survival within the construct. Histological analysis revealed that the GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel containing the coculture of ES-SCAP Sphere and HUVECs exhibited the highest number of both perfused and total blood vessels. Immunohistochemistry results indicated positive staining for human CD31 in the majority of blood vessel lumens, indicating the involvement of implanted HUVECs in the formation of blood vessels in vivo. Moreover, the GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel with ES group exhibited a significantly higher percentage of Tuj1-positive cells, indicating its remarkable ability to enhance the vascular formation of HUVECs and neurogenic differentiation of SCAP after implantation in nude mice. In summary, this novel hydrogel demonstrates promising therapeutic potential as a desirable Co-ion controlled release system and a powerful in vitro platform for generating mature neurovascular structures, thereby enhancing cell-based therapies.

17115420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115420.value: In our study, we developed and characterized a novel hypoxia-mimicking nanocomposite and an electroconductive hydrogel scaffold for dental tissue engineering. The hypoxia-mimicking nanocomposite, MWCNTs/Co, demonstrated a well-designed structure and sustained release of cobalt ions. It significantly upregulated the expression of HIF-1α and VEGF proteins in stem cells from apical papilla (SCAP), thereby promoting vessel formation in endothelial cells. This indicates that the MWCNTs/Co nanocomposites have the ability to enhance the angiogenic potential of SCAP, rendering them well-suited for applications in dental tissue engineering. Regarding the electroconductive hydrogel scaffold, GelMA-MWCNTs/Co, exhibited superior electrical conductivity when compared to GelMA-MWCNTs. When SCAP were encapsulated within this hydrogel scaffold and subjected to electrical stimulation, they showed significant neuronal cell-like changes and expressed neuronal-specific markers. The hydrogel scaffold also facilitated the spreading of neurites and promoted neuronal differentiation of SCAP, making it a promising platform for neural tissue engineering and neural regeneration. Additionally, the GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold achieved a controlled release of cobalt ions, which is suitable for early-stage vasculogenesis during tissue regeneration. It displayed excellent biocompatibility, supporting the growth and coculture of HUVECs and SCAP. SCAP encapsulated in the hydrogel exhibited increased expression of HIF-1α and VEGF proteins, promoting the formation of longer vessels. Moreover, the results also showed the differentiation of SCAP into pericyte-like cells, which play a crucial role in vascular stability and regulation. The hydrogel displayed neurovascular characteristics, enhancing interactions between electrically stimulated SCAP and HUVECs, thereby facilitating vasculogenesis and neurogenesis. In vivo studies showed improved blood perfusion and cell survival within the hydrogel, indicating its potential as a promising platform for cell-based therapies and tissue regeneration. In summary, the hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold holds great potential in the field of dental tissue engineering and cell-based therapies. This innovative scaffold possesses controlled release capabilities, promotes vasculogenesis and neurogenesis, and facilitates the formation of mature neurovascular structures. These findings provide promising potential for future translational applications in regenerative medicine.

17115420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115420.value: Our study held promising prospects for dental tissue engineering and cell-based therapies. This hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold, with its well-designed structure and sustained release of cobalt ions, demonstrates the ability to enhance the angiogenic potential of SCAP. Moreover, it promotes vessel formation in endothelial cells and supports the growth and coculture of HUVECs and SCAP. Encouragingly, this hydrogel scaffold also exhibits neurovascular characteristics, facilitating interactions between electrically stimulated SCAP and HUVECs, thereby promoting vasculogenesis and neurogenesis. Based on these promising findings, further research and development efforts should focus on optimizing and upgrading the production of the hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold, including refining the fabrication techniques and promoting stability and biocompatibility. Additionally, more in vivo studies are necessary to evaluate the scaffold's efficacy and safety in dental tissue engineering applications. By addressing these aspects, the hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold has the potential for cell-based therapies and contributes to translational applications in regenerative medicine.

17115420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115420.value: Our study developed a new hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold for dental tissue engineering. This hydrogel scaffold has the property to release cobalt ions over time and mimics the hypoxic conditions in the body. When stem cells from apical papilla (SCAP) are cultured in the hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold, it has a significant positive effect on the cells by increasing the production of proteins that promote the formation of blood vessels. This suggests that the scaffold can enhance the growth of blood vessels, making it suitable for dental tissue engineering. Additionally, when SCAP were cultured in the hydrogel scaffold and exposed to electrical stimulation, they showed changes similar to nerve cells and expressed specific markers for neurons. The scaffold also helped the growth of nerve-like structures. This makes it a promising platform for engineering neural tissues and promoting nerve regeneration. In summary, the hypoxia-mimicking GelMA-MWCNTs/Co hydrogel scaffold has great potential for dental tissue engineering and cell-based therapies. It can mimics the hypoxic conditions that promote blood vessel growth and support the development of nerve-like structures. These findings offer exciting possibilities for future applications in regenerative medicine.

17115520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115520.value: Iroquois (Irx)基因與許多發育過程密切相關。Irx3和Irx5基因在IrxB基因簇中緊密相聯，並且廣泛表達於發育中的哺乳動物內耳。目前已知，擁有Irx5基因突變的病人患有感覺神經性耳聾。然而，Irx3和Irx5在耳蝸上皮細胞命運決定以及下游基因表達調控中的作用並不清楚。這項研究旨在闡明Irx3和Irx5基因在哺乳動物耳蝸非感覺上皮發育過程中轉錄調控機理。 為了進一步瞭解Irx基因在耳蝸發育和功能中的作用，我們研究了Irx突變小鼠的表型。我們發現Irx5-/-突變小鼠有嚴重的聽力喪失問題。Irx3/5-/-突變小鼠表現出非感覺上皮細胞的異常排列模式，包括大上皮嵴區域的喪失，Sox2+/Jag1+感覺域的擴大，小上皮嵴區域的部分缺失，以及耳蝸和球囊感覺區域之間的由非感覺細胞構成的邊界的缺失。因此，Irx3和Irx5基因在發育中的耳蝸非感覺上皮細胞的命運決定過程中至關重要。 基於我們對Irx5-/-突變細胞的轉錄組分析，以及其它相關的轉錄組和開放染色質測序數據的生物信息學分析，我們推斷Irx3和Irx5可以在非感覺上皮細胞中與Lmx1a和其它因子相互作用來共同調節下游基因的表達。Irx3/5 可能直接或者間接調控非感覺上皮細胞排列和分化相關的基因，從而維持耳蝸的聽覺功能。 在這項研究中，通過分析一系列Irx3和Irx5單突變或雙突變小鼠的表型和單細胞轉錄組，我們會闡明這兩個基因在小鼠耳蝸發育中的轉錄調控以及它們的下游靶點。具體的目標有：（1）檢驗Irx3-/-，Irx5-/-，Irx3/5-/-突變小鼠耳蝸的非感覺上皮細胞表型；（2）分析Irx3/5-/-突變小鼠耳蝸上皮的單細胞轉錄組從而鑒定差異表達的基因以及鑒別感覺/非感覺細胞命運的轉變；（3）探究Irx3/5下游基因的轉錄調控並破譯耳蝸上皮細胞功能的基因調控網絡。 在這項研究中，通過整合小鼠遺傳學，轉錄組，生物信息分析以及分子實驗，我們將解碼Irx3和Irx5基因在哺乳動物耳蝸非感覺上皮細胞的發育與功能中轉錄調控機理。

17115520.label: Realisation of objectives
17115520.value: Objective 1. To examine the non-sensory cochlear epithelium phenotypes of Irx3-/-, Irx5-/- and Irx3/5-/- double knockout mutants A. Irx3 and Irx5 define the cochlear GER and regulate LER and other non-sensory regions The Irx3/5-/- DKO mutants displayed significant phenotypes including: 1) the absence of non-sensory boundary between the saccule and the organ of Corti; 2) the replacement of non-sensory GER (greater epithelial ridge) cells with sensory hair cells. We found that Crabp1, a specific marker for differentiating GER cells, was absent in E16.5 DKO cochlea, suggesting the loss of GER identity. Instead, the GER domain expressed vestibular genes Aldh1a3 and Tnfaip2, and differentiated into sensory hair cells with vestibular stereocilia features. Irx3-/- and Irx5-/- cochlea did not show these phenotypes, indicating functional compensation between Irx3 and Irx5. In E14.5 DKO cochlea, the LER displayed abnormal gene expression profiles characterized by low Bmp4 expression, medially expanded patterns of Fst, Fgfr2 and Etv5, failed downregulation of Msx1, and absence of Lmo3. Furthermore, expression of Cd44 in LER-derived Claudius cells was only detected at E18.5, suggesting a delayed LER differentiation. We generated Emx2-cre Irx3/5-/- to study neonatal root cells. By immunostaining of Aqp5 and Kcnj10, we found that the conditional mutants lacked root processes at P7. Irx3-/- and Irx5-/- also exhibited notably shorter root processes at P7, indicating the essential roles of Irx3 and Irx5 in root cells differentiation. B. The roles of Irx genes in maintaining non-sensory cell differentiation and functions The DKO mutants displayed reduced Gsc+ marginal cell progenitors from E12.5 to E14.5, followed by diminished Kcnq1+ marginal cells and expanded Otx2+ Reissner’s membrane region from E16.5 to E18.5. We examined the expression of ion channels, transporters, and gap junction proteins in the non-sensory regions of DKO cochlea. From E14.5 to E16.5, Irx3/5-/- mutants displayed medially expanded expression patterns of Slc26a4 (transmembrane ion transporter) and Cxn26 (gap junction) in the outer sulcus. In the DKO mutant, the stria vascularis (SV) structure was disrupted, characterized by the reduced Kcnq1+Esrrb+ marginal layer, expanded cMet+Cd44+ intermediate cell layer and restricted Cxn26+ basal cell layer. At P7, the Cd44+ Claudius cells and Aqp5+ root cells were disconnected in the Irx3-/-, Irx5-/- and Emx2-cre Irx3/5-/-, which would affect ion transportation functions. Our results demonstrated disordered patterning and abnormal cellular functions of Claudius cells, outer sulcus cells and SV in the Irx3/5-/- mutants. In summary, we showed that Irx3 and Irx5 function cooperatively to regulate the development and function of multiple non-sensory cell types in the cochlear epithelium. We have fully completed Objective 1. Objective 2. To analyze single cell transcriptomes of Irx3/5 mutant cochlear epithelial cells to identify differentially regulated genes and sensory/non-sensory cell fate changes A. Generation and analysis of scRNA-seq data for normal and mutant cochlea We generated and analysed single-cell RNA-transcriptome data from wildtype and Irx3/5-/- inner ears at E14.5, a crucial time point when the cochlear epithelial cell fates are established. For each genotype, two inner ears were dissected and used for RNA extraction. In total, 11940 cells with 23215 gene features were profiled. Specific markers were used to annotate different groups of cells. Epcam+Krt18+ epithelial cells were isolated in silico, comprising 1877 cells (751 cells from the wildtype and 1126 cells from the Irx3/5-/- group). UMAP plots revealed distinct heterogeneity in Irx3/5-/- inner ears, including the absence of the GER cluster and an increase in vestibular sensory cells. We examined the differentially expression genes (DEGs) in the wildtype and mutant scRNA-seq datasets and characterized the up- and down-regulated transcription profiles. Notably, the expression levels of two vestibular genes Aldh1a3 and Dlx5 were elevated, while cochlear specific genes Clu and Thrb were down-regulated in the DKO mutants. Whole mount in situ hybridization confirmed that the expression patterns of Aldh1a3 and Dlx5 were expanded from vestibule to cochlea, whereas Clu expression declined from basal cochlea, and persisted in the medial turn to apex. Our DEGs analysis also depicted that Msx1 and Slc26a4 were upregulated while Lmo3 were decreased in mutant LER, supported by in vivo validations of expression. Other LER-specific genes such as Tac1 and Fbln2 were also identified, allowing us to identify transcriptome signatures for various non-sensory cell types. B. Identification of Irx3 and Irx5 target genes and gene regulatory network for cochlear epithelium development To systematically study the functions of Irx3 and Irx5 in cochlear epithelium, we predicted the gene regulatory networks (GRNs) of E14.5 cochlear epithelium using single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC). Genes co-expressed with all transcriptional factors were characterized using the GENIE3 algorithm, followed by cis-regulatory motif analysis with RcisTarget to identify the downstream regulons. The result was visualized using Cytoscape. In total, 152 downstream candidates of Irx3/5 were identified. Mycn (N-Myc), Ebf1, Prdm16 and Hes1 could be potential direct targets of Irx3 and Irx5. Notably, Mycn null mutants exhibited similar phenotypes of fused saccular and cochlear sensory epithelium. In addition, Rbpj, Hes6 and Zbtb20 were identified as the targets of Irx5 rather than Irx3. Intriguingly, Notch signaling was affected in the absence of Irx3/5 genes (see Objective 3). Furthermore, Zbtb20 null mutants also represented similar phenotypes of the retarded root cells, supporting a possible regulation between Zbtb20 and Irx3/5 genes in regulating the outer sulcus epithelium development. We have completed Objective 2 satisfactorily. Objective 3. To investigate the transcriptional regulation of Irx3/5 downstream candidate genes to decipher the gene regulatory network for cochlear epithelial cell function Our preliminary data suggested that Irx3 and Irx5 may regulate downstream targets Aqp5 and Fst through binding with Lmx1a. However, our further experiments revealed largely normal expression domains of Lmx1a, Fst and Aqp5 in Irx3/5-/- cochlea. The reduced expression of Aqp5 was likely resulted from defective root processes rather than direct dys-regulation of Aqp5 expression. Interestingly, from our single-cell transcriptome analysis, by construction of GRNs we found that Notch signaling factors Hes1, Hes6, and Rbpj were potential downstream candidates of Irx3 and/or Irx5. Remarkably, we found that the expression patterns of Notch signaling genes were significantly affected in Irx3/5-/- mutant cochlea. By wholemount in situ hybridization, we showed that deletions of both Irx3 and Irx5 in DKO led to an expanded and fused expression domains of Notch ligand Dll1, effector gene Hey1, and modulator Lfng in saccule and cochlea; overflowed expression domains of Hey1, Jag2 and Mfng from saccule to cochlea were also observed. The altered expression profiles of multiple Notch signaling factor genes in the DKO mutant cochlea strongly suggest that the Irx3/5 mutant phenotypes could be mediated by Notch signaling functions. To investigate the potential involvement of Notch signaling, we used the Emx2Cre;Rosa26N1-IC mutant which over-expressed the Notch1 receptor (NICD) in the cochlear epithelium. We found that at E14.5, the NICD mutant cochlea displayed the absence of non-sensory GER region and fusion of saccule and cochlear sensory domains, recapitulating the phenotypes displayed by the Irx3/5 DKO mutants. It has been previously reported that supernumerary inner hair cells and ectopic hair cells in GER could be found in Jag1, Jag2, Hes1, or Hes5 null mutants, suggesting Notch signaling functions in sensory/non-sensory cell fate commitment. Taken together, our results so far provided evidence for the regulatory relationship between the Notch signaling pathway and Irx3/5 genes. Through our single-cell transcriptome and mutant analysis, we have completed Objective 3 satisfactorily.

17115520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115520.value: Our analyses of DKO mutant phenotypes and single-cell transcriptomes show that one major role of Irx3/5 is to suppress vestibular sensory cell fate in the cochlea. In the absence of Irx3/5, ectopic vestibular hair cells replaced the cochlear non-sensory structure, the Greater Epithelial Ridge (GER). Crabp1, a specific marker for differentiating GER cells, was lost in DKO cochlea. The vestibular genes Aldh1a3 and Tnfaip2 were ectopically expressed in the GER, which differentiated into sensory hair cells with vestibular stereocilia features. Investigation of the innervation in the Irx3/5 DKO cochlear nucleus provided further evidence for the evolutionary significance of Irx3/5 gene functions in defining the cochlear cell fates (Fritszch et al 2024). The results of this part of our study are summarized as a preprint (Liu et at 2024) in BioRxiv, we plan to submit the manuscript to Nature series journal for publication. In this project, we obtained wildtype and Irx3/5-/- DKO single-cell transcriptome data from E14.5 inner ears. Analysis of our data together with other wildtype datasets covering E16.5 to neonatal stages available in the public domain, we have been able to examine the transcriptomes and gene regulatory networks for the saccule and cochlear sensory and non-sensory cell types (Liu et al. 2024). By lineage reconstruction analysis, we predicted that the LER cells are progenitors of non-sensory cells including the outer sulcus cells, Hensen’s cells, Claudius cells, root cells, and spiral prominence cells. We found that the cochlear roof epithelium is already specified into discrete domains with distinctive gene expression profiles at E14.5, and discovered that Gsc is a marker gene of the marginal cell lineage. Analysis of our E14.5 dataset generated in this project has provided crucial information for the study of marginal cell and stria vascularis development (Qin et al 2024). By differential gene expression analysis of wildtype and Irx3/5-/- DKO mutant scRNA-seq data, we found that Notch signaling factors Hes1, Hes6, and Rbpj were potential downstream targets of Irx3/Irx5. Our in vivo validation of gene expression patterns confirmed that Notch signaling genes Dll1, Jag2, Hey1, Lfng, Mfng were altered in DKO mutant cochlea. Over-expression of NICD in mouse inner ear also led to fusion of saccule and cochlear sensory domains. Our discovery of interactions between Irx3/5 genes with Notch signaling has opened up a new direction for further studies of vestibular and cochlear sensory development.

17115520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115520.value: 1. Based on the results obtained from this study, it is clear that Irx3/5 are essential to maintain several non-sensory regions in the developing cochlea, which will in turn affect the hearing functions. From our transcriptome-based lineage reconstruction analysis, the LER is likely contributing to several outer sulcus derived cell types, including the root cells. We have submitted a RGC GRF proposal to further investigate the roles of Irx3/5 in the differentiation and functions of these outer sulcus derived non-sensory cells. 2. Our discovery of interactions between Irx3/5 and Notch signaling genes will require further studies. In the short term we could perform cell based experiments to validate whether the predicted targets Hes1, Hes6, and Rbpj are indeed directly regulated by the Irx3/5 genes. In the longer term, we will design mutant mouse studies by manipulating Notch regulators or effectors such as Notch1, Jag2 and Rbpj in Irx3/5 compound mutant studies. These experiments will provide valuable insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying the interplay between Irx3/5 genes and Notch signaling pathway during the cochlear epithelium development.

17115520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115520.value: During inner ear development, an interplay of transcription and signaling mechanisms define the cochlear epithelial sensory and non-sensory cell fates. In this study, by mouse mutants and single cell transcriptomic analyses, we investigated the phenotypes of non-sensory cell types in Irx3-/-, Irx5-/-, Irx3/5-/- double knockout, and Emx2-cre Irx3/5-/- conditional double knockout mutant cochlea. We showed that Irx3/5 genes could suppress vestibular sensory cell fate in the cochlea. In the absence of Irx3/5, ectopic vestibular sensory hair cells replaced the cochlear non-sensory structure, the Greater Epithelial Ridge (GER). We found that Irx3/5 genes could define the GER cell fate, promote LER (lesser epithelial ridge) development, regulate dorsal cochlear epithelial patterning, modulate root cells differentiation and contribute to the formation of stria vascularis. Our results highlighted the multiple functions of Irx3 and Irx5 during cochlear non-sensory epithelium differentiation. Furthermore, our transcriptomic analysis has identified Notch signaling genes as potential downstream candidates of Irx3 and Irx5, suggesting that Irx3/5 genes may interact with Notch signaling pathway in regulating the specification of sensory and non-sensory cell types in the cochlear epithelium. In summary, we showed that Irx3 and Irx5 cooperatively contribute to define the sensory and non-sensory regions in the cochlea.

17116520.label: Realisation of objectives
17116520.value: 1. Determine the effect of CSR-1 on HCP-3 localization We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of the effects of CSR-1 depletion. We assessed the functionality of kinetochore–microtubule attachment in the embryonic divisions in the absence of CSR-1. In two-cell embryos with CSR-1 depletion, both early and late mitosis were prolonged. To test whether there are additional effects caused by CSR-1 depletion on chromosome dynamics independent of merotelic attachment, we generated a scenario devoid of tension caused by pulling forces from opposite poles. Without ZYG-1, centrosomes fail to duplicate after the first division. Cells with depletion of both ZYG-1 and CSR-1 [zyg-1 csr-1(RNAi)] cells had a shorter average chromatin-to-pole distance of 3.349 μm, which was 68.5% of that observed for the zyg-1(RNAi) cells. The metaphase plate appeared bulkier in csr-1(RNAi) embryos, likely due to imperfect chromosome alignment. We quantified an increase in centromere and kinetochore protein localization on chromatin after CSR-1 depletion. The metaphase plate intensities of the centromere protein HCP-3 and the kinetochore proteins MIS-12, KNL-1, KNL-3 and HCP-1 were increased significantly in csr-1(RNAi) embryos. In prometaphase, the localization of centromeric and kinetochore proteins remained concentrated on the poleward faces of the chromosomes in csr-1(RNAi) embryos. The levels of the centromeric protein HCP-3 and the kinetochore proteins HCP-4 and NDC-80, but not of the centromere licensing factor Mis18BP1 homolog KNL-2, increased at the poleward faces of the chromosomes in csr-1(RNAi) embryos. Through chromatin fiber assay, HCP-3 has increased chromatin occupancy as distinct foci with higher density in csr-1(RNAi) embryos. These increased kinetochore proteins can act as additional anchor points for microtubules binding, thereby changing how chromosomes dynamically move, align and segregate. 2. Decipher the mechanisms used by CSR-1 in restricting HCP-3 localization We evaluated the HCP-3 expression upon CSR-1 depletion at the transcript and protein levels. Interestingly, although the total HCP-3 protein level and the chromatin HCP-3 turnover rate was unchanged, more HCP-3 was deposited onto the chromatin. HCP-3 localization requires KNL-2 and LIN-53. To determine whether the additional deposition of HCP-3 after CSR-1 knockdown occurs through KNL-2 or LIN-53, we depleted CSR-1 in embryos with RNAi-mediated depletion of KNL-2 [knl-2(RNAi)] or LIN-53 [lin-53(RNAi)]. In csr-1(RNAi) embryos, some HCP-3 can be loaded onto the chromatin by mechanisms that are independent of KNL-2 or LIN-53. Thus, the increased deposition of HCP-3 in csr-1(RNAi) embryos is not completely hindered by the depletion of KNL-2 or LIN-53. We further screened for requirements important for CSR-1 to control the HCP-3 level on chromatin. We found that upstream components of the CSR-1 RNAi pathway and the PIWI domain activity of CSR-1 were essential for this elevation of chromatin-localized HCP-3. Our work unravels details of the mechanism by which CSR-1 is required to regulate the proper amount of centromere protein deposited on holocentromeres, which has significant implications for our understanding of holocentromere function and organization. Our study has shed light on how the deposition of centromeric proteins is regulated in C. elegans and has exemplified how an RNAi pathway can be involved in the determination of centromere regions in organisms containing non-regional centromeres. 3. Decipher the relationship between embryonic transcription and HCP-3 localization by low input genomic approaches We have performed HCP-3 DNA adenine methyltransferase identification (DamID) and RNA-sequencing in wildtype and csr-1(RNAi) embryos and germline. The results of HCP-3 wildtype DamID and chIP-seq are being compared. We will then compare the localizations of HCP-3 in csr-1(RNAi) and wildtype embryos, and examine whether the increased number of locations of HCP-3 in csr-1(RNAi) embryos is related to changes in embryonic or germline RNA expression. The results of this part is under preparation in another manuscript.

17116520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116520.value: (Abstract of https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.261895) Chromosome segregation errors caused by centromere malfunction can lead to chromosome instability and aneuploidy. In Caenorhabditis elegans, the Argonaute protein CSR-1 is essential for proper chromosome segregation, although the specific mechanisms are not fully understood. Here, we investigated how CSR-1 regulates centromere and kinetochore function in C. elegans embryos. We found that depletion of CSR-1 results in defects in mitotic progression and chromosome positioning relative to the spindle pole. Knockdown of CSR-1 does not affect mRNA and protein levels of the centromeric histone H3 variant and CENP-A homolog HCP-3 but does increase the localization of HCP-3 and some kinetochore proteins to the mitotic chromosomes. Such elevation of HCP-3 chromatin localization depends on EGO-1, which is an upstream factor in the CSR-1 RNA interference (RNAi) pathway, and PIWI domain activity of CSR-1. Our results suggest that CSR-1 restricts the level of HCP-3 at the holocentromeres, prevents erroneous kinetochore assembly and thereby promotes accurate chromosome segregation. Our work sheds light on the role of CSR-1 in regulating deposition of HCP-3 on chromatin and centromere function in embryos.

17116520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116520.value: Our work on C. elegans holocentroemre suggests a regulatory function of Argonaute CSR-1 in CENP-A/HCP-3 deposition and localization on chromatin. It will be important to explore the potential contribution of epigenetic modifications and CSR-1-genome interactions in restricting HCP-3 localization. Consistently, in humans, the AGO2 RNAi pathway is also required for proper chromosome segregation, with depletion of AGO2 or a slicer-inactive AGO2 mutant leading to abnormal α-satellite RNA levels and CENPC1 mislocalization to the chromosome arms. Even though humans and C. elegans have different centromere architectures and DNA sequences, the epigenetic regulation, including histone modifications, RNAi pathways, transcription and non-coding RNAs, might be conserved. It will be interesting to investigate whether Argonautes and RNAi pathways have conserved functions in maintaining centromeres or controlling CENP-A loading across species.

17116520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116520.value: Accurate chromosome segregation during cell division is crucial for organism survival and is moderated by the microtubules, which attach to chromosomes through the kinetochores. The kinetochore complex is assembled on the centromere region of each chromosome. Erroneous microtubule attachment is prone to result in uneven chromosome segregation. We have found that an important protein in the RNA interference pathway, CSR-1, negatively regulates the level of the first assembled centromeric protein CENP-A on the chromatin. The misregulated HCP-3 chromatin level in turns changes the kinetochore–microtubule interface and potentially increases the frequency of erroneous mcirotubule attachment, leading to chromosome missegregation.

17116820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116820.value: Cardiopulmonary toxicities following thoracic radiotherapy or PD-1 blocking immunotherapy have a major impact on quality of life and survival. Thus we propose to investigate autoimmune mechanisms that modulate cardiopulmonary toxicities in this clinical setting. Our preclinical findings demonstrated: 1) excessive mortality in mice exposed to Thoracic Radiotherapy and anti-PD-1, 2) cardiac fatality is dependent on the cytokine IL-17A and B-cells, 3) Rise of autoantibodies against heart or lung tissues in mice with combined treatments. IL-17A is produced by both release from neutrophils as part of the innate immune response, and by T lymphocytes following adaptive Th17 response. Our central hypothesis is that toxicities result from the unchecked adaptive Th17 response due to PD-1 blockade, combined with autoantibodies against heart and lung tissues generated by the pro-inflammatory B-lymphocytes. We will employ knockout mouse models and pharmacological inhibitors to dissect the underlying autoimmune mechanisms. Aim 1: To determine whether IL-17A/Th17 responses mediate toxicities from TRT+/-aPD-1. We hypothesize that both innate and adaptive immunity contributes to the toxicities through the link of IL-17A. Since both neutrophils and Th17 cells contribute to the IL-17A pool, we will generate KO mice unable to produce IL-17A through either neutrophils or CD4 T cells. We expect that the toxicities are attenuated when Th17/IL-17A are blunted in these mouse models. We expect that these results will reveal the extent to which innate and adaptive immune response contribute to the toxicities through the IL-17A cytokine. Aim 2: To determine whether humoral response mediates toxicities from TRT+/-aPD-1. We hypothesize that pro-inflammatory Tbet+ B-lymphocytes drive autoantibody production, leading to the toxicities. We will use Tbetflox/flox CD19cre mice in which mature Tbet+ B cells are absent. This approach will be complemented by pharmacological depletion of B cells (anti-CD20) or by neutralizing autoantibodies (IVIg). We expect the toxicities attenuated in both cases. We will then determine whether Tbet+ B cells and autoantibodies are dependent upon the Th17/IL-17A, using pharmacological inhibitors of Th17/IL-17A. We expect that the inhibitors will attenuate the toxicities in both wild-type and MRL/MpJ autoimmune mice. N/A
