17119120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119120.value: The extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by tumor cells have emerged as a critical mediator for creating a tumor-supportive microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma (Seminars in Cancer Biology 2022). The current project elucidated how the EV-NID1/TNFR1-mediated pathway elevates OXCT2 levels, thereby enhancing the utilization of ketone bodies to generate energy that drives the growth and motility of disseminating cells during HCC metastasis. The findings revealed that the upregulation of TNFR1 induced by EV-NID1 is mediated by the NF-κB pathway. Additionally, the study demonstrated that increased OXCT2 levels elevate cellular ATP, highlighting the pivotal role of OXCT2 in providing energy to sustain HCC metastasis. NID1, a protein with multiple functional domains, plays a crucial role in these processes. By utilizing an EV-targeting vector to engineer HCC EVs expressing full-length and mutant forms of NID1, our study identified the C-terminus (671-1247 aa) of NID1 as essential for inducing TNFR1 secretion and driving the oncogenic properties of NID1, including promoting cell growth, motility, tumorigenesis, and metastasis (The Liver Week 2020 and APASL 2021). Given the crucial role of C-terminus region of NID1 in its oncogenic ability, interacting partners of NID1 via the C-terminus was identified using mass spectrometry, and revealed TGM3 as a critical interacting partner of NID1. Our findings revealed that loss in TGM3 level hindered the aggressiveness of HCC cells and responsiveness to EV-NID1 treatment, underscoring its role in oncogenesis. Subsequent investigation revealed that TGM3’s ability in activating the integrin-YAP/TAZ signaling cascade, contributing to tumorigenesis (Manuscript in preparation). Our findings suggest the potential of NID1 as a therapeutic target for HCC. Immunogold labeling of EVs obtained from MHCC97L cells and late-stage HCC patients revealed the presence of NID1 on the EV surface, suggesting that neutralizing NID1 with an anti-NID1 antibody could be a viable therapeutic approach to target NID1. Evidence from various mouse models of HCC, including orthotopic liver implantation, HCC induction by hydrodynamic injection, and patient-derived xenograft models, demonstrated that anti-NID1 antibody effectively counteracted the tumorigenic and metastatic effects of NID1-enriched EVs in promoting HCC progression (The 6th International Summit on Innovative Drug Discovery 2024). Moreover, NID1 is found to be upregulated in other cancer types such as breast cancer, lung cancer, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Demonstrated by both the in vitro and in vivo assays, anti-NID1 antibody was shown to significantly inhibit the aggressiveness of these cancer cells that express NID1 (Journal of Translational Internal Medicine 2024).

17119120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119120.value: EVs are regarded as a molecular signature of the parental cells. Recent advancement in liquid biopsies holds the promise of implementing EV content for clinical diagnostics. Much of the current research is aimed at finding promising biomarkers of diseases through validation and better molecular candidates to maximize the potentials of targeted therapies. The identification of upregulated NID1 in circulating EVs of HCC patients compared to that of healthy individuals, suggesting the potential of NID1 as a biomarker and therapeutic target of HCC. The study also delineated the role of EV-NID1 in driving HCC via different signaling pathways. NID1 is found to localize on the surface of EVs which enables the blockage of EV-NID1 by neutralizing antibody. A custom-made mouse monoclonal anti-NID1 neutralizing antibody was developed that could effectively reduce HCC cell growth and motility in vitro and dampen liver tumor formation and metastasis in mice. The anti-NID1 antibody did not exert cytotoxicity to normal liver cell line and cause adverse effect to mice. These findings suggest the feasibility of translating the blockade of NID1 into targeted therapy of cancer patients with high blood level of EV-NID1 or tumorous tissues with elevated NID1 expression.

17119120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119120.value: The research project revealed that EV-NID1 stimulates pulmonary fibroblasts to release TNFR1, which in turn upregulates OXCT2 in liver cancer cells. The increased OXCT2 levels facilitate the utilization of ketone bodies for energy production, thereby supporting cell growth and movement during the metastasis of liver cancer. The study elucidated the mechanism through which NID1 facilitates communication between primary liver cancer cells and pulmonary fibroblasts via the delivery by extracellular vesicle, thereby creating a pre-metastatic niche that enhances the growth and motility of HCC cells. Additionally, it uncovered a novel function of OXCT2 induced by TNFR1 in HCC, highlighting its role in regulating ketolysis. In terms of clinical implications, these findings suggest a promising strategy for liver cancer treatment by targeting oncogenic EV-NID1 with neutralizing antibodies to mitigate the aggressive characteristics of cancer cells. Notably, this research has resulted in a patent being granted for the use of anti-NID1 antibody in liver cancer treatment, as well as for the application of NID1 as a diagnostic marker and therapeutic target in liver cancer.

17119420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119420.value: 重症抑郁是一种严重的神经精神疾病，是导致全球疾病负担的主要原因之一。抑郁症可以通过针对血清素能系统的药物和/或心理疗法进行有效治疗。然而，大约20％的患者对这些标准疗法无效，而近60％的患者无法获得足够的疗效。考虑到尝试药物和心理疗法仍然严重抑郁的患者，我们提出了一种非侵入性神经调节方法的新概念。该方法采用经角膜电刺激法（transcorneal electrical stimulation, TES）减轻抑郁症的临床前动物模型中的抑郁类行为。 我们的主要目标是检验TES可以在经慢性不可预测的压力模式的抑郁症动物模型中诱导类抗抑郁作用的假设。 我们将评估一系列类抗抑郁行为的影响，包括焦虑样反应，运动行为，享乐行为，社交互动行为和强迫游泳模型。我们的目标是探明与传统抗抑郁药疗法如使用依西酞普兰相比较下，TES会成为在动物模型中治疗抑郁类行为的最有效治疗措施。 我们的前期实验表明，TES诱导了与海马体神经发生相关的基因和蛋白质表达增强的类抗抑郁活性。TES的这些深远影响促使我们进一步研究其潜在机制，我们的第二目标是重点关注TES诱导的抗抑郁类反应的神经发生（或BDNF / TrkB）依赖性和非依赖性作用。在这方面，我们将在给予替莫唑胺或TrkB拮抗剂的动物中进行实验，已知该药物可阻断海马体神经发生或BDNF / TrkB功能。 我们的第三个目标是使用组织化学和生化方法研究TES诱导的类抗抑郁作用的细胞和分子机制。 在机制上我们优先考虑BDNF / TrkB-ERK-CREB的特定途径。在TES对神经发生的影响方面，我们预期随着神经元核、双皮质素和巢蛋白阳性细胞数量的增加，存活的BrdU标记细胞会增加。TES动物中与神经发生和BDNF / TrkB功能特定相关的蛋白质标记物的过量表达会进一步支持上述结果，从而支持TES在挽救应激诱导的抑郁类行为方面的神经保护作用。 总体而言，我们预计TES通过BDNF / TrkB的特定途径增强神经保护作用，这将有助于提高抑郁症动物模型海马体中的神经增殖、细胞存活和神经可塑性。 最后，我们希望将这有力的机制研究和结果转化为治疗抑郁症患者的临床应用。

17119420.label: Realisation of objectives
17119420.value: We have completed all the experiments stated in the objectives. Our primary objective was to test the hypothesis that TES induced antidepressant-like effects in an animal model of depression using a chronic unpredictable stress paradigm. The behavioral effects of anxiety-like response, locomotion, hedonia, social interaction and forced-swim immobility for antidepressant-like activities were assessed. We have identified that TES will ascertain the most effective therapeutic measures for treating depressive-like behaviors that is comparable (or more superior) to the classical antidepressant drug by escitalopram treatment in animal model. Our preliminary experiments have demonstrated that TES induced remarkable antidepressant-like activities with enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis-related gene and protein expression. These profound effects of TES have prompted us to further examine its underlying mechanisms that focus on the neurogenesis-dependent and -independent effects of TES-induced antidepressant-like responses in Objective 2. In this respect, experiments have performed in animals with administration of temozolomide, which are known to block the hippocampal neurogenesis. Our third objective was to investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms of TES-induced antidepressant-like effects using histochemical and biochemical methods. For mechanisms, we prioritize on the specific pathway of BDNF/TrkB-ERK-CREB. For effects of TES on neurogenesis, we demonstrated an increase in surviving BrdU-labeled cells with increase in the numbers of neuronal nuclei-, doublecortin- and nestin-positive cells. These results are further supported by the overexpression of protein markers specifically related to neurogenesis in TES animals, thereby supporting the neuroprotective effects of TES to rescue the stress-induced depressive-like behaviors.

17119420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119420.value: Given that visual impairment is bi-directionally associated with depression, we decided to examine whether transcorneal electrical stimulation (TES), a non-invasive treatment for visual disorders, can ameliorate depressive symptoms. The putative antidepressant-like effects of TES and the underlying mechanisms were investigated in an S334ter-line-3 rat model of retinal degeneration and a rat model of chronic unpredictable stress (CUS). TES was administered daily for 1 week in S334ter-line-3 and CUS rats. The effects of TES on behavioral parameters, plasma corticosterone levels, and different aspects of neuroplasticity, including neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, and apoptosis, were examined. In the S334ter-line-3 rats, TES induced anxiolytic and antidepressant-like behaviors in the cylinder, open field, home cage emergence, and forced swim tests. In the CUS rat model, TES induced hedonic-like behavior and decreased behavioral despair, which were accompanied by reduced plasma corticosterone levels and upregulated expression of neurogenesis-related genes. Treatment with the neurogenesis blocker TMZ only inhibited the hedonic-like effects of TES, suggesting the antidepressant-like effects of TES were mediated through both neurogenesis-dependent and -independent mechanisms. Furthermore, TES was found to normalize the protein expression of synaptic markers and apoptotic Bcl-2-associated protein in the hippocampus and amygdala in the CUS rat model. The improvements in neuroplasticity may involve protein kinase B (AKT) and protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathways in the hippocampus and amygdala, respectively, as demonstrated by the altered pAKT/AKT and pPKA/PKA ratios. The overall findings suggest a possible neuroplasticity mechanism of the antidepressant-like effects of TES.

17119420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119420.value: We have further investigated the effects of TES in an animal model of Alzheimer's disease. Dementia is a major burden on global health for which there are no effective treatments. In this study, we investigated the effects of TES on memory enhancement using two mouse models, in aged mice and in the 5XFAD model of Alzheimer's disease. After 3 weeks of TES treatment, mice were subjected to Y‐maze and Morris water maze tests to assess hippocampal‐dependent learning and memory. Immunostaining of the hippocampus of 5XFAD mice was also performed to examine the effects of TES on amyloid plaque pathology. The results showed that TES improved the performance of both aged and 5XFAD mice in memory tests. TES also reduced hippocampal plaque deposition in male, but not female, 5XFAD mice. Moreover, TES significantly reversed the downregulated level of postsynaptic protein 95 in the hippocampus of male 5XFAD mice, suggesting the effects of TES involve a postsynaptic mechanism. Overall, these findings support further investigation of TES as a potential treatment for cognitive dysfunction and mechanistic studies of TES effects in other dementia models.

17119520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119520.value: 下頜第三磨牙（智慧齒）阻生在人類中很常見，並經常引起口腔健康問題，如感染和蛀牙。相鄰的第二磨牙通常由於下頜第三磨牙引起的局部牙周病而受到影響。移除整隻下頜第三磨牙是治療的傳統方法。然而，即使除去引起毛病的下頜第三磨牙之後，支撐第二磨牙的牙周附著組織和骨骼也可能永久減少,導致持續的慢性牙周炎。牙冠切除術是治療下頜第三磨牙的一種新手術方法，該方法僅除去牙冠並保留牙根。研究證明，這是一種安全的方法，而術後神經缺損和疼痛的風險亦較小。術後兩年大多數牙根會停止向前移動。我們的初步結果顯示，牙冠切除術後相鄰的第二磨牙有明顯的牙周附著組織和骨再生。因此，我們假設牙冠切除術在相鄰第二磨牙牙周附著組織和骨的再生優於移除整隻下頜第三磨牙。 此研究旨在比較牙冠切除術與移除整隻下頜第三磨牙術後第一年內相鄰第二磨牙的牙周附著組織和骨的再生的關係。此研究設計是一項隨機臨床試驗。將招募有雙側下頜第三磨牙的患者，一側進行牙冠切除術，另一側移除整隻下頜第三磨牙。臨床檢查和錐束電腦斷層掃描將用於評估術後的牙周附著組織和骨的再生。研究亦評估了兩種技術的手術風險。該隨機臨床試驗需要60名受試者。術後第2週，第3，第6和第12個月對患者進行複查。 此研究的結果將提供一個重要的證據，證明採用牙冠切除術或移除整隻下頜第三磨牙對相鄰的第二磨牙的牙周和骨骼再生方面更好。此研究將在計劃移除下頜第三磨牙時幫助牙醫和患者做出決策，並可以減少相鄰的第二磨牙患上牙周病的機會。

17119520.label: Realisation of objectives
17119520.value: Objective 1. A blinded assessor unaware of the interventions performed pre-operative and post-operative assessments at specific time-points. Periodontal attachment measurements were performed pre-operatively and at the post-operative 2nd week and in the 3rd, 6th and 12th post-operative months. Periodontal attachment were measured - Periodontal probing depth (PPD): measurement from the gingival margin to the bottom of the defect - Clinical attachment level (CAL): measurement from the cemento-enamel junction to the bottom of the defect Objective 2. A cone beam computer tomography (CBCT) scan with a small field of view (FOV) of the region of interest were taken pre-operatively and at post-operative 6th and 12th month. For the assessment of bone level (BL) changes, first, the second molar were set into an upright position in coronal and sagittal views. Then, the axial view were adjusted to the level of the pulpal floor, with the alveolar ridge set into vertical. In the sagittal view, a vertical line was drawn from the cemento-enamel junction (CEJ) down to the alveolar crest level. The measurement was done in three sites, i.e. disto-buccal, mid-distal and disto-lingual, by shifting the image via the sagittal view. By comparing the measurement taken in the pre-operative and post-operative images, the BL changes in the surgical site were calculated. Objective 3. Clinical examinations were performed in the 2nd post-operative week and in the 3rd, 6th and 12th post-operative months to detect pain score on the visual analog scale (VAS) (0-10), infection rate (determined by the presence of pus formation), inferior alveolar nerve and lingual nerve deficit rate in both groups, the root exposure rate and the need of re-operation to remove the retained root in the coronectomy group.

17119520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119520.value: A total of 62 patients recruited with a predicted 20% dropout rate. There were 2 patients who did not receive the interventions. There were 50 patients who were reviewed for 6 months. There were 59 patients who received the interventions. There were 46 patients (27 males, 10 females) with a mean age of 27.9 years (S.D. 6.6 years) were reviewed for 12 months and completed the follow-up protocol. Majority (81.7%) of the lower third molars were horizontally impacted, with 18.3% were mesially impacted. For the periodontal attachment changes of the adjacent second molar, both coronectomy group and control group brought improvement in PPD and CAL when compared to pre-operatively. The mean PPD reduction in the control group was 1.04mm, whereas PPD reduction in coronectomy was 1.24mm, which was significantly better (p=0.007). CAL improvement was also better in the coronectomy group than the control group (1.18mm vs 0.71mm, p=0.003). The finding showed coronectomy had better periodontal attachment improvement than total removal of lower third molar. For the bone regeneration of adjacent second molar, both coronectomy group and control group showed significant bone regeneration when compared to pre-operatively (p<0.001). For the control group, the bone level from CEJ improved from 5.5mm (S.D. 1.7mm) to 3.6mm (S.D.1.1mm). For the coronectomy group, the bone level from CEJ improved from 5.42mm (S.D. 1.6mm) to 3.4mm (S.D.1.1mm). There were no difference between the two groups p=0.258). No patients from either group presented with pain, swelling, infection, neurosensory deficit at post-operative reviews. No patients from the coronectomy group presented with root exposure during the study period.

17119520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119520.value: A longer follow-up will be indicated to compare the long-term benefit of coronectomy on the periodontal attachment and bone level of the adjacent second molars. The longevity of the adjacent second molars and how the prevention of localized periodontal disease by coronectomy may be useful indicators of outcomes and it will require a long-term study.

17119520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119520.value: Lower third molar impaction is common in the population and often causes oral health problems like infection and dental decay. The functional adjacent second molar is often affected as a consequence of the localized periodontal disease causes by the lower third molar. This project showed coronectomy, i.e. removing the crown of the third molar and keeping the tooth root in situ, is able to improve the periodontal conditions in terms of attachment gain and bone regeneration when compared to tradition total removal of lower third molars. There is no surgical morbidities relating to coronectomy during the study period. This study gives evidence to help in the decision making of the dentists and the patients when a lower third molar is planned to be removed, and may avoid the occurrence of residual periodontal disease at the adjacent second molar.

17119820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119820.value: Influenza poses a heavy burden to our health service. The World Health Organization estimates that seasonal influenza causes 250,000-500,000 deaths worldwide each year. Elderly and patients with chronic illness are most at risk and often required hospitalization for treatment of complications, with even higher morbidity and mortality during an antigenically drifted A(H3N2) season. In the recent 2018 season, more than 80,000 patients died from influenza infection and its complication, likely secondary to vaccine mismatch of a drifted H3N2 influenza strain. Treatment and prophylaxis of influenza is currently limited to neuraminidase inhibitors including the oseltamivir, zanamivir, peramivir and laninamivir. Nevertheless, patients with severe influenza and pneumonia often presented beyond 48 hours from symptoms onset, rendering neuraminidase treatment less effective. Besides, severe cases of influenza virus infection were characterised by delayed clearance of viral load and marked cytokine activation. Most recently a new anti-influenza antiviral agent baloxavir marboxil, a selective inhibitor of influenza cap-dependent endonuclease was shown to be superior to both oseltamivir and placebo in reducing the viral load 1 day after initiation of treatment in patients with uncomplicated influenza. Further trial in hospitalized patients with severe influenza infection is underway. Antiviral and immunomodulators combinations with different modes of action were used for treating severe influenza infection. Recently, a macrolide antibiotic, clarithromycin in combination with naproxen, was shown by our team to inhibit human influenza A virus production in in vivo. Clarithromycin also suppressed tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and augmented interleukin-12 (IL-12) production in influenza virus infected mice. Flufenamic acid (FFA) and naproxen a non-selective cyclooxygenase inhibitor, were shown to protect susceptible cell line and mice against influenza A viral challenge by inhibiting influenza nucleoprotein-RNA association. Treatment with this FFA-clarithromycin-zanamivir triple combination in mouse model resulted in significantly better survival than either with the clarithromycin-zanamivir or the zanamivir alone. Therefore, we hypothesize that the treatment with baloxavir-FFA antiviral and immunomodulator combination will result in better clinical efficacy, virological suppression and immunomodulation than baloxavir alone. 臨床醫生一直在使用具有不同作用方式的抗病毒和免疫調節劑組合治療嚴重的流感感染。 最近，我們的研究小組證明了大環內酯類抗生素克拉黴素與萘普生合用可在體內抑制人類甲型流感病毒的產生。 氟苯胺酸和萘普生是一種非選擇性環氧化酶抑製劑，已顯示可通過抑制流感病毒核蛋白-核糖核酸結合而保護易感細胞系和小鼠模型免受甲型流感病毒攻擊。 因此，我們假設與單獨使用巴洛沙韋相比，使用巴洛沙韋和氟苯那酸抗病毒藥治療將產生更好的臨床療效，病毒學抑製作用和免疫調節作用。 我們將進行一項雙盲隨機對照試驗，比較在嚴重流感感染住院的患者的病毒學，免疫學和臨床結局中，將巴洛沙韋與氟苯那酸與單獨使用巴洛沙韋作比較

17119820.label: Realisation of objectives
17119820.value: Patient Characteristics Between January 2023 and September 2025, 50 patients were screened, and 47 met eligibility criteria and were enrolled. Twenty-five patients were randomized to the baloxavir-FFA combination group and 22 to the baloxavir-placebo (control) group. All enrolled patients completed the 5-day study drug regimen and were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. The median age of the cohort was 79 years (interquartile range [IQR], 67-84), and 34 (72%) were male. Forty-five (96%) patients had influenza A infection (predominantly H3N2), and 2 had influenza B. The median time from symptom onset to treatment initiation was 48 hours (IQR 36-60). Baseline characteristics, including age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, proportion requiring oxygen support, and baseline NEWS, were well-balanced between the two groups. Primary and Secondary Clinical Outcomes The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was low overall. One patient in the control group died (4.5%), compared to zero deaths in the combination group (p=0.462). One patient in the combination group died (4%) during the 90-day follow-up period (p=1.0). Length of hospital stay was significantly shorter in the combination therapy group. The median hospitalization was 7 days (IQR 5-7) compared to 8 days (IQR 6.75-10.25) in the control group (p=0.003). Clinical improvement, as measured by the NEWS, occurred more rapidly in the combination group. While baseline scores were similar, NEWS from day 3 through day 6 post-treatment were significantly lower in the baloxavir-FFA group (p<0.001). Virological Outcomes Both treatment groups demonstrated a rapid and significant decline in viral load as measured by both RT-PCR and TCID₅₀. There was no statistically significant difference in the rate or magnitude of viral load reduction between the two groups over the 7-day sampling period. No neuraminidase inhibitor-resistant (NIRV) quasi-species were detected in any serial sample from either group by deep sequencing analysis. Immunological Outcomes Plasma cytokine analysis revealed a distinct immunomodulatory effect of FFA. Patients in the combination group exhibited significantly lower levels of both the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6 from day 2 through day 5 and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 from day 3 through day 5 post-treatment initiation, compared to the control group (p<0.05 for each time point comparison). Safety The study interventions were well-tolerated. No serious adverse events attributable to either baloxavir or FFA were reported. There were no instances of significant gastrointestinal bleeding, renal impairment, or hypersensitivity reactions. Our study has limitations. Its single-center design may limit generalizability, though the patient population is representative of severe influenza burden. The sample size, while adequate to detect a significant difference in the secondary clinical and immunological outcomes, it was far below the initial power calculation. This was due to the very low influenza infection rate during the COVID-19 pandemic. The open-label use of baloxavir in both arms means we cannot assess FFA's effect compared to standard care (e.g., oseltamivir), only its additive effect to a potent backbone. Finally, while the cytokine data is suggestive, the precise molecular mechanisms by which FFA exerts its immunomodulatory effects in this context warrant further investigation.

17119820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119820.value: Background Severe influenza infection remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, particularly during seasons with antigenically drifted strains. While neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) are standard-of-care, their efficacy diminishes when initiated late. Baloxavir marboxil, a novel cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor, offers a new mechanism of action. Preclinical evidence suggests that combining antivirals with immunomodulators like flufenamic acid (FFA) may improve outcomes by simultaneously suppressing viral replication and mitigating deleterious hyperinflammatory responses. Methods We conducted a prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial at Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong. Adults hospitalized with severe, virologically confirmed influenza (symptom onset ≤72 hours) were randomized 1:1 to receive either two doses of weight-based baloxavir (days 1 & 4) plus oral FFA (200mg twice daily for 5 days) or baloxavir plus placebo. All patients received empirical antibiotics and gastroprotection. Primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, viral kinetics (TCID₅₀, RT-PCR), emergence of resistant quasi-species, cytokine/chemokine profiles, clinical improvement (National Early Warning Score, NEWS), length of hospitalization, and adverse events. Results From January 2023 to September 2025, 47 patients were enrolled (25 combination, 22 control). The median age was 79 years, with 45 influenza A and 2 influenza B infections. Groups were balanced at baseline. Thirty-day mortality was low (1 death in control group, 0 in treatment group; p=0.462). Ninety-day mortality was zero. The combination therapy group experienced a significantly shorter median length of hospitalization [7 days (IQR 5-7) vs. 8 days (IQR 6.75-10.25); p=0.003], faster clinical improvement as measured by NEWS from days 3-6 (p<0.001), and significant attenuation of pro-inflammatory (IL-6) and anti-inflammatory (IL-10) cytokine levels from days 2-5. No significant difference in viral load reduction was observed. No antiviral-resistant quasi-species were detected, and no treatment-related adverse events were reported. Conclusions The addition of the immunomodulator flufenamic acid to baloxavir marboxil in hospitalized patients with severe influenza was safe and associated with accelerated clinical recovery and reduced hospitalization duration, likely mediated by modulation of the host inflammatory response rather than enhanced direct antiviral activity. This combination represents a promising therapeutic strategy for severe influenza.

17119820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119820.value: The combination of baloxavir marboxil and FFA for the treatment of severe hospitalized influenza infection was safe and well-tolerated. While it did not further enhance the potent antiviral effect of baloxavir, it significantly accelerated clinical recovery and shortened hospital length of stay. This clinical benefit was associated with a favorable modulation of the host cytokine response, specifically a reduction in IL-6 and IL-10 levels. These findings support the therapeutic concept of combining direct antiviral agents with immunomodulators to improve outcomes in severe influenza. Further research is warranted to validate these findings in larger, diverse populations and to explore the potential of this strategy in other settings, including outpatient management of high-risk patients with influenza.

17119820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119820.value: This study tested a new two-part treatment for severe flu in hospitalized older patients with multiple comorbidity. Everyone received a strong new antiviral drug called baloxavir. Half the patients also received an additional drug, flufenamic acid (FFA), which is thought to calm the body's harmful overreaction to the virus, not just fight the virus itself. The goal was to see if adding FFA would help patients get better faster. The results were promising. While both groups cleared the virus equally well and had very low death rates, the patients who received the extra FFA got out of the hospital about a day sooner. They also showed faster improvement in their vital signs and had lower levels of key inflammatory markers in their blood, meaning their immune response was less extreme. In short, adding FFA to the antiviral treatment did not kill the flu virus any better, but it did help patients' bodies recover from the illness more quickly and safely. This suggests that treating the body's dangerous inflammatory response is just as important as fighting the virus for helping very sick flu patients heal.

17120120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120120.value: 由于人为CO2引起的海水碳酸盐离子浓度和pH值的降低, 这一过程被称为"海洋酸化 (OA), 预计食用牡蛎的尺寸将变小, 并且在壳受损的情况下生长更慢. 世界各地的水产养殖业担心牡蛎产量可能受到OA的影响, OA的发生速度空前. 中国是全球80%以上的牡蛎生产国, 特别关注这一新出现的问题. 许多短期（天）实验涉及一代人内的单一生命阶段帮助我们预测哪些牡蛎物种有能力适应环境或可塑性耐受OA通过基因, 蛋白质和代谢产物的差异表达. 与此同时，环境压力源能够通过DNA甲基化过程在DNA上添加或删除甲基，这也可以将基因表达"打开或关闭". 重要的是, 这种表观遗传DNA修饰可以由后续几代人继承, 以允许在几代人内快速适应。 基于这些假设和最近对牡蛎基因组DNA甲基化模式的分析, 人们可以假设生活在高度紧张和多变环境中的物种, 如具有高遗传变异状态的河口, 可以在几代内适应未来50-100年预测的OA的影响. 如果这个假设是正确的, 那么它可能对牡蛎产业来说是一个好兆头. 几个长期（个月）OA研究看转代（内和跨代）表观遗传遗传遗传, 包括我们的初步数据, 表明存在积极结转效应和 "非遗传" 适应机制牡蛎, 即通过DNA甲基化介导的 但是, 我们不了解这种TGP变化的动态, 包括它们在多代（例如F0，F1和F2）上的"持久性和继承". 此外, OA 适应F2个人获取TGP的最终" 命运"仍是未知的自然环境, 体验多种压力源. 因此, 目前海洋气候变化研究中的热点课题就不足为奇了. 最近，我们调查了来自华南地区的"香港牡蛎"（Crassostrea hongkongensis）人口. 我们观察到, F1代的父母接触到OA的幼虫增加了生长和变态下OA相比那些父母没有接触到OA. 在此建议中, 我们将继续研究这项工作是否表现出积极的结转效应和TGP进一步推进到下一代的F2, 以及确定底层的跨代继承机制。 我们假设父母暴露于OA可以通过差异甲基化基因, 如结转的几个商业和生理重要性状（即肉质和数量, 在牡蛎多代生成有利的持久性和遗传性状. 同样重要的是要知道OA适应的个体如何在自然界的多重压力条件下相互作用和生存. 这项建议的主要目标是(1)通过分析一组有针对性的性状相关的生理适应性和商业价值在个人从我们正在进行的多代实验中, (2)比较差异表达的基因 DNA甲基化数据还将与表型和转录组学数据一起使用, 以确定表观遗传修饰和可继承的分子和表型特征, 这些特征对于该领域多代商业物种的生存至关重要. 所有这些数据都是迫切需要和及时的，以协助水产养殖业实施其分子育种计划，并准确预测具有商业重要性的贝类物种应对气候变化的能力.

17120120.label: Realisation of objectives
17120120.value: This is one of the most productive GRF projects in our research group. We are super excited to report on the outstanding outputs of this project. As proposed, we have successfully completed our multi-generational, long-term ocean acidification exposure experiment in our oyster hatchery located in mainland (Zhanjiang, China). As a result, we have collected almost all necessary samples and data to accomplish and address all three objectives of this project. In this project, the ecologically and commercially important estuarine oyster species, Hong Kong oyster was used as the model to study epigenetic adaptation and molecular plasticity to ocean acidification (OA) stress in the context of aquaculture. We have exposed oysters to OA-induced low pH 7.4 against control pH 8.0 condition at larval stage in the hatchery to identify and study the epigenetic mechanism, i.e., DNA methylation pattern and its molecular pathways, to explain the physiological and developmental traits of the oyster over multiple generations. As follow-up experiment, the adults and/or larvae exposed to OA stress were outplanted as post-metamorphic juveniles at three different aquaculture sites with contrasting environmental stressors for over years. Thus, we have examined how DNA methylation altered gene expression to account for the trans-generational and within-generational carry-over OA effects on the phenotypic traits of the species in the aquaculture environment. During this whole experiment, we have managed to examine gene expression and associated methylation pattern dynamics, as proposed. This success was possible because of the recruitment of the highly talented THREE graduate students from interdisciplinary background (Dr James Lim, Dr Xin Dang and Mr David Lee), and great cooperation from both mainland (Prof Zinu Yu) and USA (Prof Steven Roberts). Our team has also brought in a few other collaborators from both mainland, USA and UK to make sure we have made use of all the data collected from this project to make an impact in the field (see our last publication of this project in end of 2024: Dang etal 2023). The students who have accomplished this project successfully defended their PhD thesis and proceeded to become Professors and post docs. This we would consider an one of the outstanding achievements of this project. As a result of this interdisciplinary international collaborative teamwork, we have achieved more than what was promised to deliver for this project – e.g. published 13 high quality papers (all attached with this report), three more high quality manuscripts are under early stage of preparation. As most of our results have been published, here we briefly summarize how we have achieved those findings (all these published papers are attached with this report). Before, we proceed with this project, we have successfully established ocean acidification and oyster culture experiments and published those results (see Pub1). Basic experiment for the project (Published in Science and Total Environment: Pub2): In recent years, OA is known to influence carryover effects, i.e. exposure of larvae to OA exhibits either positive or negative effects after metamorphosis. Our study examined those hidden effects of OA exposure from parental to larval stage on post-metamorphic traits in one of the commercially important oyster species, Crassostrea hongkongensis. Adults were exposed to control) and OA-induced low pH conditions. Their offspring larvae were also exposed to the aquarium conditions and then out-planted as post-metamorphic juveniles for 10 months at a mariculture site. The out-planted juveniles with parental exposure had improved survival and growth than juveniles without parental exposure, regardless of their larval exposure history. This implies that transgenerational effect from parental exposure not only persisted but also had a greater influence than within-generation effect from larval exposure. Our results shed light on the importance of linking various life history stages in assessing OA-induced carry-over capacity of C. hongkongensis in the natural environment. Understanding the linked relationships helps in facilitating better prediction in species rapid adaptive response in the face of changing coastal condition due to OA. Biomineralization is a seriously impacted biological process under OA (Published in Global Change Biology and Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology – Pub3 and 4): Understanding molecular changes in the biomineralisation process under OA and its heritability, is key to developing conservation strategies for protecting ecologically and economically important oyster species. To do this, in this study we have explicitly chosen the tissue involved in biomineralisation (mantle) of Crassostrea hongkongensis. The primary aim of this study is to understand the influence of DNA methylation over gene expression of mantle tissue under decreased ~ pH 7.4, a proxy of OA, and to extrapolate if these molecular changes can be observed in the product of biomineralisation – the shell. The population of oysters used in this study was found to be moderately resilient to OA at the end of the experiment. The expression of key biomineralisation related genes such as carbonic anhydrase and alkaline phosphatase remained unaffected, thus, mechanical properties of the shell (shell growth rate, hardness and crystal orientation) were also maintained without any significant difference between control and OA conditions with signs of severe dissolution. In addition, this study makes three major conclusions: 1) higher expression of Ca2+ binding/signalling related genes in the mantle play a key role in maintaining biomineralisation under OA, 2) DNA methylation changes occur in response to OA, however, these methylation changes do not directly control gene expression, 3) OA would be more of a ‘dissolution problem’ rather than a ‘biomineralisation problem’ for resilient species that maintain calcification rate with normal shell growth and mechanical properties. Winter Mass Mortality of Oysters and Ocean acidification (Molecular Ecology and Environmental Pollution: Pub5 and 6): As shown in our previous study, carry-over effects have a potential to alter several phenotypic traits including survival under mass mortality of oysters in winter. However, molecular mechanisms that mediate “OA” triggered carry-over and winter mortality effects have not been explicitly explored, especially from adaptation perspective, such information is key to improve species fitness and develop management strategies for aquafarming. In this study, we specifically, examined how one of the environmentally induced epigenetic modifications on DNA alter gene expression that is associated with the carry-over impacts of OA on phenotypic traits of the ecologically and commercially important oyster species Crassostrea hongkongensis under natural field conditions. The methylome and transcriptome of the species were site- and OA exposure-dependent, with genes related to signal transduction and endocrine system being the most common and highly enriched functions across treatments. Intron, a non-coding region was highly associated to the overall expression of the genes with DNA methylation, but the higher methylated exon to intron ratio prevailed in the key genes that linked to general metabolic and endocytic responses. These suggest that oysters with prior larval exposure history to OA had the capability to trigger rapid adaptive responses via epigenetic modification to cope with multiple stressors in the mariculture area. PhD Thesis Related Research Work and Publication of their Results (Pub7 to 12): The whole project objectives was finally realized via publishing thesis research reports of three PhD students who directly worked for the project and another two PhD students who have partially involved in this project. Those publications are attached with this report.

17120120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120120.value: Pleased to publish 12 research papers in high impact factor journals with this project funding support. Besides, three PhD thesis report have been completed and those graduated doctoral students are now continuing their research as professor and post-docs in various institutions. The result has been used to develop hypothesis for a new RGC-GRF proposal to study transgenerational effects of multiple stressors on bioactive peptide synthesis in oysters – which has been funded and now ongoing. The project has been effectively used to strengthen our established and ongoing interdisciplinary interinstitutional collaborations, e.g. authors listed in almost all the 13 papers published from this project are showing such collaboration. Impact Case Study: Oysters are protein- and nutrient-rich carbon neutral seafood delicacy for growing middle-class population around the world, particularly in Asia. Therefore, its expansion to new culture areas is critically important for securing global food security. However, aquaculture production of oysters in estuarine areas is now seriously threatened by climate change (acidification, salinity stress and warming) and unsustainable practices that are imposed on growers to meet the increasing demand – together causing mass mortality and impacting food safety and quality. Our research in this project have identified a high-stress and disease resilient mechanisms and genotypes to thrive at highly stressful areas in the face of multiple-stressors imposed by climate change. This project leads to the development of a comprehensive integrated molecular and digital toolkit, named “HKU’s breeder SNP Chip” for identification of broodstocks for producing stress-tolerant triploid” seeds. Together with established knowledge exchange network with growers, industry and government agencies, our decade-long research has (1) improved grower’s confidence of producing seeds from the so-called stress-resilient parents to ensure their expansion to new coastal areas (impact 1), (2) helped growers associations, industry and governments in Hong Kong and South China to develop policy guidelines for regulating oyster farming in their favored estuarine areas and also to expand their culture in coastal areas that are currently unsuitable for farming (impact 2) and (3) made an impact on hatchery managers, entrepreneurs and growers with industrial mindset and various government officers who are involved in setting up hatchery and oyster farming regulations in the region and greater China through empowering them to identify wild-population rich in commercial traits for breeding in their hatchery and to use them for subsequent breeding of their own super oysters (impact 3).

17120120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120120.value: Proposed “Impact Case Study” for RGC’s Research Assessment Exercise 2030: As we have developed one the highly rated (internal HKU reviews) 4* impact proposal for 2026 round of RAE, our faculty team encouraging us to continue the effort to make even better impact in the oyster farming industry through research. This is our focus. Specifically, our collaboration with various genomics scientists in mainland and overseas led to the development of Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) array, named as HKU’s breeder SNP Chip” (R5). Specialties of HKU’s breeder array is 1) it covers the entire genome of HK species at regular intervals with highly polymorphic SNPs, 2) composed of multiple stress and high salt tolerant SNPs and markers as identified in our research, 3) have many polymorphic SNPs and they are evenly spaced them, and 4) include markers from pathogens and other oyster species for application in entire south China and beyond. This holistic and inclusive “grower and hatchery focused” SNP-chip with various detection methods and machine leaning classification tools will be interactively used for identification of the best brood stock of HK oysters from wild populations.

17120120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120120.value: The anthropogenic activities-driven excessive emission of carbon-di-oxide is absorbed in coastal ocean, leading to declining pH of seawater. This alteration is known as ocean acidification (OA), which appears with other factors, such as bacterial infection, concomitantly threatening the physiology, immunity and survival of oysters. China, as the main producer of oyster aquaculture, contributing more than 80% of global production, is particularly concerned about this emerging issue– because oysters are experiencing mass mortality. This research project addressed this critically important socio-economic issue and found solutions. In this project, we have systematically and comparatively examine Hong Kong oyster response to the effects of long-term OA through three generations under OA exposure. It was found that Hong Kong oyster showed high immune resistance to OA in the first generation, but this resistance gradually decreased in the following generations. Interestingly, the negative effects on oyster immune system and gene expression profiles were irreversible after two generations of OA. These results made us to submit “impact case study” for the upcoming round of RGC’s RAE – which is titled as “Integrated omics and hatchery technologies for fast-forward breeding of multiple stress resilient Hong Kong oysters for China”.

17120220.label: Project Objectives
17120220.value: To automate the CAD process by fine-tuning the fatigue model, which is the core information of the new algorithm. Based on our previous studies, we have developed a mathematical model that can generalize and predict the fatigue of different dental CAD/CAM crown materials on human tooth according to various preparations. Now, this research study is going to focus on fine-tuning this FE-fatigue model by obtaining the mechanical properties (static and fatigue biaxial flexural strength (BFS), fracture toughness and microhardness) of CAD/CAM materials. These will generate the core dataset in the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) which will be used as the shape-optimization parameters in the automated CAD algorithm that is based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) (Project Objective 2). To develop a new computation algorithm based on the fatigue model using the Artificial Intelligence approach. This AI-enabled CAD algorithm will use Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), which is a subclause of supervised learning under machine learning, to “generate” the missing crown on the abutment tooth. 500 sets of single missing crown case from the Faculty and Prince Philip Dental Hospital datasets containing the jaw relationship with prepared tooth and adjacent teeth, the opposing jaw, and the designed crown in digital STL format have been identified and collected (400 sets for training and 100 sets for evaluation). Then, the “generated” crown will be fed into FEA based on the fine-tuned fatigue test (Project Objective 1) to optimize the crown shape based on the CAD/CAM material properties. To improve the CAM process that can mill and polish the CAD/CAM materials directly into a dental crown. The machining involves milling and the criterial part is the tooling, i.e. milling bits/burs. We have pilot studied and developed a set of milling burs with a new nano-diamond coating (crystalline grain size: 30-50nm) using Hot Filament Chemical Vapor Deposition (HFCVD) technique. The burs have shown an extended life (i.e. less wear), and leaves a glossy finishing surface on the materials after milling. So, using the new nano-diamond coated milling burs is a good approach to fabricate the CAD/CAM crown by one shot (milling and polishing together), and we are going to investigate the optimal tools and conditions in this project with respect to different materials. Besides, this study will compare the fatigue performance on the CAD/CAM crown materials (with the crown designed by the automated CAD algorithm) milling with non-coated burs and coated ones in our previously published model on human pre-molars. This is essential before putting this automated CAD and improved CAM into clinical trial and market.

17120220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120220.value: 背景 隨著數字牙科的迅速發展，牙科治療中的製作流程和所使用的材料得以改變。現在，牙醫和牙科技工人員可以使用各種數字化設備和處理軟件（即計算機輔助設計，CAD）進行牙冠的設計，同時又可以應用新型的具有高強度及美學性質的材料進行牙冠製造（例如計算機輔助加工，CAM）。可是，當前的CAD和CAM仍然很大程度上取決於「人」；除此以外，製作中的更多時間被使用在牙冠的設計和拋光製作上。為解決以上問題，本項目提出通過使用人工智能（AI）技術作為一種新穎及自動化的牙科CAD / CAM解決方案。 目的 該項目旨在（1）通過人工智能（AI）算法，跟據我們的研究數據開發自動CAD工藝，以及（2）開發具有納米鑽石塗層的CAM工具，使牙冠的生產，包括研磨和拋光一起完成的。 材料和方法 本項目將使用牙科CAD / CAM材料，包括燒結的矽酸鋰，氧化鋯增強的矽酸鋰，聚合物滲透的陶瓷網絡和3種樹脂複合材料塊。 在第一項研究中，將確定這些材料的機械性能（彎曲強度，斷裂韌性和微硬度）。然後，這些材料將由牙科技工人員進行牙冠設計。所有牙齒和牙冠都會在進行疲勞測試之前以MicroCT掃描，然後在我們先前建立的前臼牙疲勞模型中測試，這些數據將用於有限元（FE）分析中。 在第二項研究中，利用支持AI的CAD算法，進行（1）監督機器學習方法，即使用生成對抗網絡（GAN），對我們收集的500組牙齒數據，設計牙冠形狀。（2）牙冠將通過FE（有限元分析），根據材料的機械性能，進行牙冠形狀優化。通過此AI 的CAD算法設計的牙冠將銑削出來，以及在前臼牙模型上進行疲勞測試。 在第三項研究中，會使用熱絲化學氣相沉積（HFCVD）法，將我們已初步研究的納米鑽石塗在牙科銑刀上。這些銑刀將利用於制備材料樣本，銑削和拋光一體化，再將牙冠進行機械測試、表面分析以及疲勞測試。 預期結果 這項目預計能夠開發出自動化牙科CAD / CAM牙冠生成的核心AI技術。最終，牙醫可以簡單地掃描患者的牙齒，然後利用AI自動設計出牙冠，並同時使用一體化銑削和拋光的銑刀製備牙冠，直接放在患者身上。

17120420.value: 引言 如果可以使用較小的肝移植物進行成人到成人的活體供體肝移植（LDLT），則將大大提高供體安全性。但是，如果肝移植物太小而不能滿足患者的代謝需求，則會導致肝衰竭和死亡。 我們為LDLT提出了一種新穎的方法：將非常小的移植肝以輔助性肝移植的方法到受體豬中（即不去除部分天然受體肝）。通過將血流轉移至新的肝移植物，可以維持並加速肝移植物的生長。一周後，剩餘的天然肝臟被完全清除。 目的 為了研究在豬模型中，門靜脈結紮和分期肝切除術輔助LDLT的結果 研究設計 實驗動物將分成 4 組： 1. 對照組 1 SHAM 2. 對照組 2 肝功能衰竭 3. 實驗組 1 （0.2% 肝重量比LDLT及沒有門靜脈結紮） 4. 實驗組 2 （0.2% 肝重量比LDLT及門靜脈結紮） 在兩個實驗組中，操作步驟如下： 1） 輔助移植：從接受者的豬中取出80％受體的天然肝臟，並移植一小塊肝臟。 2） 門靜脈結紮：切斷流向接受者天然肝臟的血液 3） 分階段肝切除術：1週後，將接受者的天然肝臟作為輔助肝臟 主要目標：移植後1個月的豬的存活率。我們假設實驗組的豬將存活，而肝衰竭組的豬將無法生存。 次要目標包括技術成功率，肝功能恢復和肝移植物生長。

17120420.label: Realisation of objectives
17120420.value: SECTION 1: OUTCOMES OF DONOR AND RECIPIENT PROCEDURES 1.1 Donor Operation: Initial attempts at liver procurement demonstrated variable success rates, with 3 animals died due to bleeding from parenchyma transection or from IVC. Implementation of advanced energy device (Thunderbeat, Olympus, Japan) combined with vascular staplers (Johnson & Johnson, USA) identical to those used in clinical practice, enabled us to procure left lateral grafts safely in 23/26 (88.5%) experiments. Regarding technical success rate, it was 100% (26/26) for all donor operative steps including: midline incision and exploratory laparotomy, hilar dissection and isolation of left hepatic artery, left portal vein, main portal vein, and common bile duct. Also, isolation of IVC was achieved in 25/26 (96.2%) after learning curve optimization and left lateral section graft procurement rate: 100% after technical refinement (3 early failures completely resolved). Successful donor operation protocol established the technical foundation necessary for recipient operation. 1.2 Recipient Operation: The primary challenge was hemodynamic instability during IVC and portal vein clamping. Pigs tolerated vascular occlusion poorly, exhibiting rapid hemodynamic deterioration during the critical recipient hepatectomy and implantation phases. This accounted for the majority of procedural failures. In recipient operation, we were able to achieve successful liver parenchyma transection in 22/26 (84.6%) but 5 animals died due to bleeding from IVC. The critical bottleneck was graft implantation. The overall technical success at this stage was 12/26 (46.2%) with the leading cause of failure as hemodynamic collapse after IVC clamping, bleeding and reperfusion injury after vascular anastomosis. Explored rescue strategies: 1) Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) assisted approach might provide hemodynamic support during critical vascular clamping. Commercial availability ECMO systems in HK are mainly for clinical training purposes and no expertise including perfusionist/ anesthetic support is available. 2) Alternative animal model evaluation: Transition to mouse model to bypass hemodynamic constraints. It was deemed scientifically unsound. Hemodynamic parameters in mouse/ mice are incompatible with the proposed complex surgery. The translational validity of findings depends on physiological similarity to human recipients; mouse model physiology would invalidate the applicability to clinical LDLT. 1.3 Impact of COVID-19 pandemic disruption: Mar 2020 – Sep 2022 (overlap with study period) Research activity was interrupted including animal facility operations severely restricted and surgical team reassigned to clinical COVID-19 frontline duties. Our project was reactivated in Sep 2022, leading to the extended timeline for completion. SECTION 2: PRIMARY OUTCOME ASSESSMENT 1-month survival after auxiliary LDLT with portal vein ligation and staged hepatectomy was zero as all successfully implanted animals only survived for a few hours after auxiliary LDLT. Of 26 trials initiated: 12 animals (46.2%) achieved successful graft implantation with reperfusion and only survived a few hours (0.5-5.4 hours) after operation but all with significant hemodynamic compromise. Graft implantation and/or reperfusion failed in the remaining 14 animals (53.8%). Therefore, none of the animal reach the time point required for primary outcome assessment. The failure to achieve the projected outcome was directly attributable to technical barriers during the recipient operation, specifically: 1. Inability to complete vascular anastomosis without lethal hemorrhage (primary cause) 2. Hemodynamic collapse during IVC and portal vein clamping (secondary cause) These were fundamental physiological limitations of the porcine model, not deficiencies in surgical technique. Our team demonstrated surgical/ procedural competency with highly successful donor operation. Graft implantation was limited by hemodynamic factors, not surgical skill. Our experience clearly indicated that successful advancement of this model requires hemodynamic support technology (ECMO or equivalent), which proved unavailable within the project constraints. SECONDARY OUTCOMES 3.1 Portal hemodynamic measurement was carried out in those who had graft successfully implanted, i.e. 12/26 (46.2%). The median portal pressure was 5 (4-9) mmHg. It was lower than our target pressure and flow, as our target parameters were based on human LDLT experience. Pigs were smaller and hemodynamic-wise different to human. Another contributing factor was all the animals were in hemodynamic compromise, therefore the recorded portal flow and pressure were lower. 3.2 Graft regeneration assessment: None of the 12 animals achieving successful implantation survived to reach the planned for day 7 second-stage hepatectomy required for regeneration assessment. The actual graft weight after donor procedure was available in 23 donor left lateral section grafts (110-134 gram) and actual GRWR was 0.38-0.44%, with the proposed target was GRWR <0.6%. 3.3 Biochemical liver function assessment: All animals were in significant hemodynamic compromise and only survived for a few hours (0.5-5.4 hours) after operation, therefore no blood tests were performed. Although we did not achieve the primary survival endpoint and regeneration assessment, we exhausted all feasible approaches and deployed substantial technical expertise in this complex surgical protocol. The barrier was inherent porcine hemodynamic physiology, not deficiency in our surgical or research approach. We respectfully submit for consideration these significant achievements in donor and recipient operations, which will pave the way for our future clinical applications.

17120420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120420.value: Over the study period, our team conducted 26 porcine trials to establish a novel surgical model combining auxiliary LDLT with portal vein ligation and staged hepatectomy. While the intended completion of the study protocol was not fully achieved, substantial technical, procedural, and scientific progress was accomplished. The project identified critical technical challenges related to hemodynamic management during the recipient operation and generated valuable data contributing to our ongoing clinical research on portal flow modulation in LDLT. Technical Achievements: The donor operative protocol demonstrated 100% technical success across all procedural steps (n=26), including hilar dissection, vascular isolation, and left lateral section procurement. Recipient operations achieved 46.2% (12/26) successful graft implantation with reperfusion, validating vascular anastomotic techniques. These findings established reproducible surgical protocols directly applicable to clinical LDLT practice. Portal pressure was successfully obtained in all successful implantations, providing physiological validation for selective portal flow modulation strategies. Identified Limitations: The project identified that porcine hemodynamic intolerance to IVC and portal vein clamping represents the critical barrier to achieving survival endpoints. This fundamental physiological constraint—not surgical competency—indicates that successful implementation of this model requires hemodynamic support technology such as ECMO or veno-venous bypass, which proved unavailable within project constraints. Despite the ultimate inability to achieve primary endpoints, our team exhausted all feasible approaches and deployed substantial technical expertise, surgical skill, and institutional resources in attempting to establish this extraordinarily complex porcine model; the failure was attributable to fundamental physiological constraints of the porcine species during prolonged vascular clamping, not to insufficient effort or surgical competency. Clinical Research Output: One MRes thesis and 2 conference abstracts described the utilization and implication of portal flow modulation in LDLT.

17120420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120420.value: - Should this porcine model be revisited, explore collaboration with institutions having dedicated ECMO support programs for research applications - Our findings provided invaluable experience in overcoming a technical complex operations, that would benefit in human LDLT. Our team is planning to start a prospective pilot study on the use of auxiliary LDLT with small graft followed by staged hepatectomy based on our experience in the porcine model and LDLT. - To further evaluate the change in portal flow and pressure, not only in transplant surgery, but also postoperative period using percutaneous doppler USG in human LDLT will be crucial.

17120420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120420.value: What We Did: Our team investigated a new surgical technique to help patients who need liver transplants from living donors. The challenge is that doctors currently use fairly large pieces of liver, which is safer but harder to find donors for. We wanted to test if smaller liver pieces could work if we used a special surgical approach based in a pig model. What We Tried: We performed 26 surgical experiments on pigs to test this new technique. First, we removed part of a donor pig's liver—this worked around 90% of the time. Then we transplanted it into another pig and left part of the pig's own liver in place temporarily, planning to remove it later once the new liver had grown. What We Found: The first part went very well. However, pigs don't handle the blood vessel clamping needed during transplant surgery as well as humans do. Without special heart-lung support machines, we couldn't keep the animals stable long enough to complete the operation safely. The Good News: We learned important things and have developed excellent surgical techniques that would enable the team to perform such operation in human in the future.

17120720.label: Realisation of objectives
17120720.value: Embryo implantation begins direct interaction between the fetus and the mother. However, the underlying mechanism that regulates this biological process is poorly defined. About 15% of couples have difficulty conceiving and need to seek fertility treatment. However, even if good-quality embryos are transferred, about 75% of women fail to conceive or give birth, partly due to implantation failure. It is believed that the maternal reproductive tract changes its microenvironment to provide the best environment for embryo implantation and maintenance of pregnancy. Currently, there are no known molecules/compounds that can increase the embryo implantation rate. Small molecules are chemical compounds with therapeutic activity that can easily bind to or enter cells. Library of Pharmacologically Active Compounds (LOPAC) is a collection of 1,280 pharmacologically active compounds with known structures and biological functions. In this GRF-funded project, we established a high-throughput screening method by using a spheroid-endometrial co-culture assay with receptive and non-receptive human endometrial epithelial cells and screened the 1280 small molecules, and identified over 100 small molecules that significantly (p<0.05) suppress or stimulate spheroid attachment onto human endometrial Ishikawa cells. We further screened the top 20 molecules that significantly suppress spheroid attachment for their cytotoxic effect on endometrial epithelial cells. Eight small molecules were further selected for spheroid attachment at lower concentrations (<10uM) and confirmed five of them have low toxicity (large LC50 value) on spheroid attachment. We further hypothesized that the LOPAC modulates could be used to suppress and/or stimulate spheroid (embryo surrogate) attachment through modulating endometrial receptivity in vitro and in vivo. We tested our hypothesis with the following objectives: (1) The use of receptive and non-receptive endometrial epithelial cells to validate putative small molecules from the Library of Pharmacologically Active Compounds (LOPAC) that modulate endometrial receptivity, (2) Investigate the synergistic effect of LOPAC on endometrial epithelial and stromal cell functions, and (3) Perform comparative proteomic and metabolomics analysis of endometrial protein expression and secretion: in vitro and in vivo studies. (1) The use of receptive and non-receptive endometrial epithelial cells to validate putative small molecules from the Library of Pharmacologically Active Compounds (LOPAC) that modulate endometrial receptivity LOPAC is a collection of 1,280 pharmacologically active compounds arrayed in a 96-well format. We have performed a high-throughput screening assay using BeWo Spheroid-Endometrial Ishikawa cell co-culture assay and identified 174 small molecules that suppressed spheroid attachment (Chen et al., 2022b; 2022c), and the selected top 20 molecules that modulate spheroid attachment were further studied. We carried out cytotoxicity assay and cell proliferation studies of these molecules and tested the minimal effective doses of these molecules on human endometrial epithelial cells. Then, we tested these compounds on other receptive endometrial RL95-2 cells, as well as two non-receptive endometrial cell lines (HEC1-B and AN3-CA), and validated their efficacy on spheroid attachment. We identified dihydroouabain (P5D6), JS-K (P8F6) and Nemadipine-A (P11B5) significantly suppressed spheroid attachment (Chen et al., 2022a; Chen, PhD thesis), whereas loxapine succinate (P9H11), perphenazine (P12E11), and N-oleoylethanolamine (P12G3) were found to significantly improved spheroids attachment in endometrial epithelial HEC1-B cells and primary cell lines (Sun, PhD thesis). (2) Investigate the synergistic effect of LOPAC on endometrial epithelial and stromal cell functions We investigated the combined effects of dihydroouabain (P5D6), JS-K (P8F6), and Nemadipine-A on the attachment of BeWo spheroid attachment onto Ishikawa and RL95-2 cells. We tested small molecules in combination and found no significant change in the attachment rate when compared to a single concentration at 3 or 10uM. Moreover, triple compound treatment did not significantly suppress spheroid attachment. The cytotoxicity of the combined small molecules was investigated to exclude the cytotoxic effect of the drug on spheroid attachment (Chen et al., 2022a). We also investigate the effect of small molecules on stromal cell functions including migration (via wound healing assay) and invasion (transwell migration assay) with or without decidualization process (e.g. PRL and IGFBP-1 expression via qPCR analysis; Jiang et al., 2024). We observed all the small molecules did not have a significant effect on stromal cell functions including invasion, migration, and decidualization process. (3) Perform comparative proteomic and metabolomics analysis of endometrial protein expression and secretion: in vitro and in vivo studies. Our preliminary study using the conditioned media from the treated samples detected various macro-molecules that were differentially expressed in the secretome of treated samples. Yet, data analysis failed to find reproducible secretome profiles for detailed molecular analysis partly due to large batch-to-batch variation during sample collection. Alternatively, we used the RNA-seq to investigate if the molecular changes could be seen at the transcript level. For mRNA sequencing, total RNA was extracted from non-receptive cells treated with or without LOPAC for 48 hours and sequenced using an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform and used the PE150 paired-end strategy to ensure adequate sequencing depth and coverage. We performed bioinformatics analysis through CPOS/HKU and several differentially regulated pathways were identified in different small molecules (Sun, PhD thesis). The transcervical transfer device was used for drug delivery into the uterus of ICR mice (n=6-8). At 1.5 dpc, a 5-µL solution containing the selected small molecule was transcervically delivered to one uterine horn and the contralateral side with vehicle control. The implantation sites in both uterine horns were assessed at 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc. We confirmed that dihydroouabain (P5D6), and Nemadipine-A (P11B5) decreased the number of implantation sites in the treated animals (Chen et al., 2022b; Chen, PhD thesis) and increased implantation sites for loxapine succinate (P9H11), perphenazine (P12E11), and N-oleoylethanolamine (P12G3) for the treated animals on the contralateral side (control) (Sun, PhD thesis) both on 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc. We also investigated the molecular changes of JS-K-regulated spheroid attachment in non-receptive endometrial epithelial (HEC1-B and AN3-CA) cells and demonstrated that JS-K enhances embryo implantation in vivo on 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc, through modulating key pathways involved in immune regulation, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Quantitative PCR analyses confirmed differentially regulated genes involved markers for endometrial receptivity (Chen et al., 2022b; Chen, PhD thesis). References Chen X. 17120720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120720.value: We screened 1,280 pharmacologically active compounds and identified identified dihydroouabain (P5D6), JS-K (P8F6) and Nemadipine-A (P11B5) significantly suppressed spheroid attachment (Chen et al., 2022a; Chen, PhD thesis), whereas loxapine succinate (P9H11), perphenazine (P12E11), and N-oleoylethanolamine (P12G3) were found to significantly improved spheroids attachment in endometrial epithelial HEC1-B cells and primary cell lines (Sun, PhD thesis). The combined effects of dihydroouabain (P5D6), JS-K (P8F6), and Nemadipine-A on the attachment of BeWo spheroid attachment onto Ishikawa and RL95-2 cells were not significant when compared with single doses. Moreover, all small molecules did not have a significant effect on stromal cell functions including invasion, migration, and decidualization process. RNA-sequencing followed by bioinformatics analysis identified several differentially regulated pathways involved in modulating immune regulation, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling (Sun, PhD thesis). Transcervical drug delivery into the uterus of ICR mice (n=6-8) at 1.5 dpc was used. The implantation sites in both uterine horns were assessed at 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc. We confirmed that dihydroouabain (P5D6), and Nemadipine-A (P11B5) decreased the number of implantation sites in the treated animals (Chen et al., 2022b; Chen, PhD thesis) and increased implantation sites for loxapine succinate (P9H11), perphenazine (P12E11), and N-oleoylethanolamine (P12G3) of the treated animals when compared to the contralateral side (control) (Sun, PhD thesis) both on 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc. Finally, the molecular changes of JS-K regulated spheroid attachment in non-receptive endometrial epithelial (HEC1-B and AN3-CA) cells and embryo implantation in vivo on 5.5 dpc and 18.5 dpc were studied. Results from this study will provide fundamental information on the selected small molecules in regulating the implantation process, delineating the underlying signaling mechanism modifying the expression of transcripts and/or secretome profiles for embryo attachment, and providing fundamental information for potential pre-clinical application of these small molecules.

17120720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120720.value: In sum, this work provides a foundation for developing new therapeutic strategies to improve endometrial receptivity and implantation success, ultimately contributing to better fertility outcomes for patients undergoing assisted reproductive treatments. Our findings suggest that these compounds, including JS-K, could be potential therapeutic agents to enhance endometrial receptivity and improve implantation outcomes. However, challenges remain in translating these findings from in vitro and animal models to human applications. Future research should focus on validating these results in human models, optimizing dosing strategies, and exploring the potential synergistic effects of drugs on fertility treatments.

17120720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120720.value: We screened 1,280 pharmacologically active compounds and identified a few molecules that significantly suppressed or stimulated spheroid (embryo surrogate) attachment onto uterus epithelial cells and primary cell lines. The combined effects of these molecules on the spheroid attachment were also investigated, but no synergistic drug effect was found. These small molecules also did not change the stromal cells' decidualization process which are important process in preparing uteri cells to accept embryos for implantation. Gene expression analysis identified several differentially regulated pathways involved in modulating immune regulation, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling of the treated uteri cells. The small molecules were found to increase the number of embryos found on day 5.5 and 18.5 in the treated uteri horn suggesting a stimulatory effect on embryo attachment, potentially useful for clinical IVF treatment. Results from this study provided fundamental information about the selected small molecules in regulating the implantation process and provided fundamental information for potential pre-clinical application.

17120920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120920.value: The flight prowess of modern birds is linked to their anatomy. From the size, outline and cross-section of the wing, to finer-scale details like the shape of individual feathers. Non-avialan paravian theropod dinosaurs are the closest relatives of birds. They inherited much of the same anatomy from their paravian common ancestor, including small size, hollow bones, vanned feathered wings and a laterally-facing shoulder joint. However, the flight potential among non-avialan paravians remains highly contentious. The microraptorine dromaeosaurid paravian Microraptor stands out as the best-studied candidate for flight potential outside of birds and has been found capable of gliding flight by disparate research groups. Microraptor had asymmetrically-feathered wings and a tail frond whose feathering has been studied in some detail. Circumstantial evidence even delimits the presence of a muscular propatagium of the wing. However, beyond this, finer-scale details of Microraptor flight anatomy are elusive, especially those that must be derived from preserved non-feather soft tissues. This project proposes to use Laser-Stimulated Fluorescence (LSF), synchrotron and neutron imaging to reveal and interpret otherwise unseen flight-related anatomy in Microraptor. On the basis of our experience in other contemporaneous non-avialan paravians as well as early short-tailed birds, we focus on the flight-essential propatagial region of the wing, particularly its never-before-seen feather arrangement (pteryology) and internal muscular anatomy. As a so-called ‘four-winged’ taxon, we also seek to document the pteryology of the ‘hindwing’ so its orientation in space can be directly observed for the first time. This project will enable crucial never-seen flight-related aspects to be directly compared to other early-diverging paravians (including early birds) and to later-diverging birds. This will help to narrow down our understanding of flight in this iconic raptor and give us much needed insight into what was novel or inherited anatomy during the early history of theropod flight. 現代鳥類的飛行技能與牠們的解剖學息息相關。由翼的大小、輪廓和切面，以至更細緻的特徵例如每條羽毛的形態。非鳥近鳥類獸腳類恐龍是鳥類關係最密切的近親。牠們從近鳥類的共同祖先遺傳了近乎一樣的解剖特徵，包括小體型、中空的骨頭、帶有正羽的翼和橫向的肩關節。但是，非鳥近鳥類恐龍的飛行潛能依然非常不確定。小盜龍是一種近鳥類馳龍科小盜龍類恐龍，牠是鳥類以外，飛行潛能被研究得最詳盡的物種，過去曾有多個研究團隊分別證明牠有滑翔能力。小盜龍帶有不對稱羽毛的翼和扇狀尾羽都曾被研究過。偶然發現的證據更顯示牠的翼帶有由肌肉組成的前翅膜。然而，除此以外，小盜龍其他與飛行相關的解剖特徵依然存疑，尤其是羽毛以外的軟組織。此研究利用激光誘導熒光技術、同步加速器和中子成像來揭示和研究其他未知的小盜龍飛行相關的解剖特徵。建基在同期的非鳥近鳥類恐龍和早期短尾鳥的認知上，我們集中於對飛行至為重要的翼膜區域，尤其是一直未知的羽毛排列和內部肌肉結構。小盜龍一般被稱為‘四翼’物種，因此我們也會研究‘後翼’的羽毛排列，以首次了解它們的空間分佈。這個研究將首次允許我們比較基幹近鳥類（包括早期鳥類）和較進步鳥類在飛行方面的差異。它會加深我們對這種標誌性的盜龍飛行能力的認識，以及讓我們辨別在獸腳類早期的飛行進化史上，有哪些特徵是創新或是遺傳得到的。

17120920.label: Realisation of objectives
17120920.value: Objective 1 was achieved successfully in full (100% complete). Our team was able to use Laser-Stimulated Fluorescence (LSF) to rapidly survey Shandong Tianyu Museum Microraptor specimens (n = 100) to identify the best soft-tissue preserving specimens (13 specimens). Macro- and microphotography of these 13 best specimens was completed under LSF and white light. The LSF images were post-processed uniformly across the images for sharpness, colour balance and saturation. The images were then interpreted to produce anatomical reconstructions of the forewing and hindwing. Objective 2 was not achieved. The pandemic prevented travel to and from HK. In the mid-term report, we stated that we would make best efforts to re-arrange synchrotron and neutron imaging in the remainder of the project despite the huge uncertainties coming out of the pandemic. Unfortunately, this was not possible despite our best efforts: it was not possible to visit and export the specimens from the Shandong Tianyu Museum to Australia because of museum staff shortages (loss of staff) associated with the pandemic. However, determined to make the project a success, the project collaborators stepped up to collect and interpret additional data to make up for the shortfall from Objective 2, including a computer-based wind tunnel experiment. This required the funding portion originally assigned to cover the overseas trips. Objective 3 was achieved successfully in full (100% complete). The LSF-based wing and 'hindwing' anatomical reconstructions of Microraptor were compared with existing ones of other early-diverging paravians (including early birds) as well as later-diverging birds. The synchrontron and neutron data was not collectable due to factors beyond our control (see Objective 2 above), but to make the most of the situation, the functional significance of the LSF-based reconstruction was analysed and interpretated im much more detail that originally planned. Our revised four-winged body plan of Microraptor was instead evaluated in a computer-based wind tunnel to understand how airflow interacted with the body during flight, showing the types of aerodyanmic features that Microraptor could utilise to fly in life. This expanded work identified aerodynamic features that appear to be shared by early four-winged paravians but also identified specialised utilisation of certain aerodynamic features by Microraptor alone. Our project results have been published in the reputable peer-reviewed journals PNAS and Nature Communications so far with a third and final paper due to submitted to Nature in March 2024 (the paper should be published in some form of high-impact journal, but Nature is our first journal of submission). Thus, with the extended work for Objective 3 and at least 2 high impact papers published from the project, we are very proud to have delivered so very successfully under unexpectedly challenging circumstances beyond our control.

17120920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120920.value: Our revised forewing reconstruction of Microraptor shows a more extended wing (larger humerus-forearm and forearm-manus angles). It maintains the long and extended wing tip of previous reconstructions created by the long primary remiges, but unlike previous work, our reconstructed wing tip has a slenderer V-shape. Unlike previous work, the length transition between primary and secondary feathers is sharper, creating a deep and narrow notch between them. The secondary feathers also gradually decrease in size proximally along the forearm, creating a relatively straight trailing edge, that is at the same level as the trailing edge of the primary feathers. Our revised hindwing reconstruction of Microraptor has a more distally shifted subtriangular trailing edge shape with its apex at the approximate level of the ankle joint. The proximal edge of this subtriangular shape is formed by the tips of the primary remiges closest to the apex; the edge is then indented and formed by the tips of the crural feathers furthest from the apex. The distal edge is formed by the tips of the primary remiges only. These revised wing plans confirmed the distal expansion of the hindwing was a genuine feature, raising questions about its aerodynamic function. To evaluate this, a 3D computer model of the body plan of Microraptor was created from our new data in the industry software Ansys to evaluate its interaction with an airflow at a flight speed. We found that the distal expansion of the hindwings maintained a lower pressure tip vortex above them that enhanced lift generation. This suggests that this hindwing expansion was an adaption for improved flight performance -- the earliest record of this phenomenon in animal flight evolution. The pronounced size of this expansion compared to other early-diverging paravians suggests that Microraptor specialised to utilise this aerodynamic feature, underscoring its refined flight anatomy and performance. The revised reconstruction permitted interaction between the wings to be studied for the first time. This was found to be beneficial, with forewing airflow passing over the hindwings to reduce drag, allowing Microraptor to accelerate more easily. This study used new data to better understand how the four-winged body plan of Microraptor worked and made important headway in understanding why four-winged body plans were prevalent in early theropod flight evolution.

17120920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120920.value: This research demonstrates that it is possible to undercover the aerodynamic features utilised by four-winged early flyers to achieve flight. Expanding this new frontier will allow us to better understand why the four-winged body plan became extinct and how birds transitioned to from dual-wing to single-wing flight. Expanding this project approach to other four-winged early flyers (easier now with the model template created here) will allow us to compare their use of vortices and wing interactions in flight (and potentially other aerodynamic features) to comment on the detailed performance differences between lineages of early flyers; ultimately informing us about how animals evolve flight.

17120920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120920.value: Early birds and their close relatives used their arms and legs to fly, but why this body plan arose and became extinct has puzzled palaeontologists. To address this, this project revised the wing reconstruction of the early four-winged flyer Microraptor. We found that the forewing had a slenderer V-shaped wing tip and a sharper transition between primary and secondary feathers. We found that the hindwing had a more distally shifted triangular trailing edge shape with its apex level with the ankle joint. We evaluate the function of this revised body plan in a computer-based wind tunnel. We found that the distinct distal expansion of the hindwings maintained a low region above them, enhancing lift generation. This unique flight specialisation is the earliest record of its type in the evolutionary history of flying animals. The revised reconstruction also permitted the study of wing interaction which was beneficial: air flowing from the forewings to hindwings reduced the body's drag, allowing Microraptor to accelerate more easily. This study used new data to provide key insights into the mechanics of the four-winged body plan of Microraptor and made important headway into understanding why four-wing body plans were prevalent during early flight evolution.
