17121120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121120.value: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) play significant roles in the regulation of a variety of cellular processes, including DNA replication, gene expression, cell cycle control, metabolism, and signal transduction. In humans, given the numerous links between PPIs and normal cell physiology, dysregulation of PPIs can often lead to severe developmental abnormity and diseases. Therefore, the profiling of PPIs not only is important for fully understanding the regulatory mechanisms of cellular processes, but also likely to provide novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of various human diseases. Most of the current methods for identifying PPIs focus on an overview of all the possible physical contacts between proteins, which can only provide limited insight into protein interaction networks in a biological context. Considering the differential expression levels and functions of proteins across tissues, cell types, and diseases in multicellular organisms such as humans, it is crucial to develop a method that can identify cell-type-specific interactions in physiological context. The proposed research aims to develop novel bifunctional amino acids that can be incorporated into proteins of specific cell type, which then undergo photo-induced crosslinking and bio-orthogonal reactions to identify context-dependent PPIs. Our study has two main objectives. First, we will design and synthesize a series of bifunctional amino acids that contain i) a photo-reactive group (diazirine group) to capture the weak and transient PPIs by converting non-covalent interactions into irreversible covalent linkages, and ii) a bio-orthogonal handle (alkyne or azido group) to further conjugate the captured proteins to affinity tags for purification. The feasibility of using such amino acids for detecting and identifying PPIs will be validated in vitro using peptide-based probes targeting known interacting partners at both the single protein and proteome-wide levels. Second, we will apply the bifunctional amino acids into living systems to demonstrate their cell-type-specific proteome labeling and interactome profiling in physiological context. The completion of this project will provide novel chemical tools for comprehensive and large-scale analysis of protein-protein interactions in the context of distinct cell types or tissues. In the long-term, the methods developed in this proposed research may help to identify PPIs of pathophysiological relevance, and may potentiate the treatment of human diseases associated with dysregulation of PPIs. 蛋白相互作用在諸如DNA複製、基因表達、細胞代謝及信號傳導等多種細胞進程中發揮著關鍵作用，其調節的紊亂經常會造成生物體的發育異常以及引發相關的人類疾病。因此，鑑定細胞內的蛋白相互作用不僅對於理解細胞活動的調節機制非常重要，也有利於開發針對多種人類疾病的新型療法。大多數現有的方法著眼於不同蛋白之間所有可能的相互作用，這使得獲得的蛋白相互作用網絡未必能反映在生物學環境下的真實情況。考慮到在人類等多細胞生物體中，即便同一蛋白在不同的組織、細胞類型以及疾病中的表達量和功能都不盡相同，我們認為開發一種可以在生理條件下鑑定細胞類型特異的蛋白相互作用的方法十分必要。 在本研究中，我們旨在開發一種新型的多功能非天然氨基酸。此氨基酸可以被插入到特定種類的細胞的蛋白質中，繼而介導光交聯反應并通過生物正交反應来鑑定特定細胞中的蛋白相互作用。本研究有兩個主要的研究目標。首先，我們會設計並合成一系列包含以下兩種化學基團的非天然氨基酸：（1）光敏基團（雙吖丙啶基團），用以介導紫外誘發的光交聯反應將非共價的相互作用轉化成穩定的共價連接，從而捕獲一些微弱的和瞬時的蛋白相互作用；（2）生物正交基團（炔官能團或者疊氮官能團），用以通過生物正交反應連接親和標籤以實現蛋白質的純化。我們將利用含有該非天然氨基酸的多肽探針在體外環境捕獲和鑑定其已知的相互作用蛋白，從而證明這種方法的可行性。其次，我們會將此氨基酸應用於細胞內，從而證明其在生理條件下鑑定蛋白相互作用組的能力。我們相信，該項目的完成會為探究和分析細胞或組織特異的蛋白相互作用網絡提供強有力的工具。長遠而言，此項目開發的方法或可幫助研究人類疾病中的蛋白相互作用，並為治療相關疾病提供新的思路。

17121120.label: Realisation of objectives
17121120.value: Objective I: To devise bifunctional (photo-cross-linkable and bio-orthogonal) noncanonical amino acids for the detection and identification of protein-protein interactions in vitro. We developed and synthesize a bifunctional methionine analog, 2-amino-5-diazirinylnonynoic acid (photo-ANA). The alkyne group of photo-ANA enables profiling of the labeled proteins, while its diazirine group mediates covalent linkages of interacting proteins upon photoactivation, allowing the capture of transient or weak PPIs. We successfully incorporate photo-ANA into peptides through standard Fmoc-based solid-phase peptide synthesis strategy to obtain peptide probes bearing various PTMs including H3K4me3, H3K4cr, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, and H3K9mal. We showed that these photo-ANA-incorporated probes could efficiently and specifically capture the ‘erasers’ and ‘readers’ of these histone PTMs, demonstrating the capability and potential of photo-ANA to identify the protein-protein interactions mediated by protein PTMs. Furthermore, using photo-ANA-incorporated H3K4me3 probe and corresponding control probe, we performed a quantitative chemical proteomic analysis to identify the H3K4me3-interacting proteins from human proteome. The photo-ANA probe robustly identified most know H3K4me3-mediated protein interactions, showing comparable performance to a previously developed H3K4me3 probe with separated photo-crosslinker and bioorthogonal handle. In conclusion, we designed a bifunctional noncanonical amino acid photo-ANA, which is equipped with photo-crosslinker and bioorthogonal handle and is capable of identifying protein-protein interactions in vitro as well as in complicated proteome. Objective II: To develop a method for selective labeling of bacterial proteome and identification of host-bacteria PPIs during infection in living cells. We first screened the active MetRS for photo-ANA by mutating Escherichia coli MetRS (EcMetRS) at leucine 13 (L13), tyrosine 260 (Y260), and histidine 301 (H301) residues that are located in the methionine binding pocket of MetRS. We identified that a single residue substitution (L13G) had the highest efficiency for incorporating photo-ANA into E. coli proteins. The addition of methionine outcompeted photo-ANA for incorporation, confirming that both amino acids followed the same route to be incorporated into synthesized proteins. To further increase the efficiency of photo-ANA incorporation, we generated a methionine auxotroph (ΔmetB) by knocking out the metB gene, which is essential for endogenous methionine biosynthesis, and we demonstrated the high efficiency and specificity of photo-ANA labeling in Salmonella proteome without sequence bias. Next, using Salmonella-infected HeLa cells as a model and with a series of optimization on the labeling timing, duration, and concentration, we showed that photo-ANA can selectively labeling Salmonella proteome while not HeLa proteome during infection. Therefore, we explored the proteome dynamics of Salmonella during infection using photo-ANA-based chemical proteomics approach, and identify an extensive metabolism reprogramming during different stages of infection. More importantly, utilizing the cell-type-specific and photo-reactive features of photo-ANA, we are able to identify the host-pathogen protein-protein interactions during infection. We found and validated two new host targets FLOT1/2 of Salmonella virulence factor PipB2. Then we established a quantitative chemical proteomics platform and discovered the host global protein targets of Salmonella during infection. We unraveled that various and different host cellular processes are targeted and disturbed by Salmonella in different infection stages. Furthermore, we also expanded the scope of photo-ANA-based approach to profile the cell-type-specific protein-protein interactions in multicellular animals using C. elegans. We first modified a SILAC (stable isotope labeling by amino acid in cell culture) method for the use in C. elegans and applied it to profile proteins from body wall muscles. We prepared triply labeled ΔmetB E. coli expressing EcMetRS L13G in photo-ANA-containing medium supplemented with either “heavy” or “light” isotope-labeled amino acids. Transgenic C. elegans expressing the CeMetRS L43G mutant in body wall muscle were fed with bacteria grown in either heavy medium containing photo-ANA or light medium containing methionine. Tissues were lysed and pooled for conjugation with biotin via click chemistry, followed by enrichment via streptavidin beads and in-gel tryptic digestion. The digested peptide mixture was then subjected to liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry. Proteins with a high ratio of heavy to light isotopes (H/L) were considered to be from body wall muscles. Among the 498 proteins with H/L values greater than 1.5, 94.8% of them had mRNA transcription in body wall muscles based on transcriptomic data. Among them, 52 proteins were highly enriched in muscles with expression level >100 times higher than the average expression across other tissues (neuron, hypodermis, and intestine), and 16 proteins had mRNA expression exclusively (e.g., UNC-22, SET-18, and OST-1) in the muscle. To further validate our results, we selected a few hits in our dataset whose expression patterns had not yet been studied by fluorescent reporters. We generated transcriptional reporters expressing GFP under their respective promoters and confirmed that the candidates from the muscle proteome (e.g., INOS-1 and TTR-16). These results not only validated our proteomic data but also suggested that our approach can effectively identify different tissue-specific proteins. We next used this method to profile tissue-specific PPIs using HSP90 as an example. We performed SILAC experiments to profile tissue-specific HSP90 interactors. C. elegans strains were fed with E. coli grown in either heavy or light medium containing photo-ANA. The heavy isotope-labeled C. elegans were subjected to photoactivation, but not the light C. elegans. Cell lysates extracted from heavy and light C. elegans were then pooled together for two rounds of enrichment followed by mass spectrometry analysis. Using this approach, we identified 142 and 125 candidate HSP90 interactors from body wall muscles and neurons, respectively, with 16 proteins shared between the two tissues. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that the HSP90 interactors were enriched in pathways related to protein translation, unfolded protein binding, and protein transport, which is in line with the roles of HSP90 in the folding, intracellular transport, maintenance, and degradation of proteins. The above results show that this method can profile PPIs with tissue selectivity in intact animals.

17121120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121120.value: This project developed a novel ‘photo-crosslinkable and clickable’ amino acid, Photo-ANA, to identify novel host proteins which are targeted by Salmonella during its invasion. In this study, we demonstrated that Photo-ANA selectively label S. Typhimurium during infection by in-gel and in-cell click chemistry experiments. We also determined that the background signal of photo-ANA labeling caused by nonspecific labeling or click-chemistry reaction maintained at low level (~1%). Then used photo-ANA, we studied protein synthesis dynamics of S. Typhimurium through different infection stages. Further, we used photo-ANA to capture the host binding partners of PipB2, a virulence effector which is essential for the extension of Salmonella-induced filaments (SIFs) and is actively synthesized in the late stage of infection. Using photo-ANA, we identified 48 potential PipB2-interacting host proteins, including four known PipB2-interactors KLC1, KLC2, KIF5B, and KIF5C, which demonstrated the reliability the photo-ANA-based approach. We also identified and validated FLOT1/2 as the novel host interactors of PipB2 in late stage of infection. Finally, we proteome-widely identified the host proteins that were targeted by S. Typhimurium during infection. They discovered extensive host-bacterial protein interactions including those known ones and many uncharacterized interactions (Nat. Chem. Biol., 2023, doi: 10.1038/s41589-022-01245-7). In addition, by using Photo-ANA, we further developed a localized proteomics approach called Methionine Analog-based Cell-Specific Proteomics and Interactomics (MACSPI). This method uses the tissue-specific expression of an engineered methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MetRS) to label proteins with a bifunctional amino acid photo-ANA in selected cells. We applied MACSPI in Caenorhabditis elegans, a model multicellular organism, to selectively label, capture, and profile the proteomes of the body wall muscle and the nervous system, which led to the identification of new tissue-specific proteins. Using photo-ANA, we successfully profiled HSP90 interactors in muscles and neurons and identified tissue-specific interactors and stress-related interactors. The study demonstrates that MACSPI can be used to profile tissue-specific proteomes and interactomes in intact multicellular organisms (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A, 2024, doi: 10.1073/pnas.2319060121).

17121120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121120.value: The incorporation of photo-ANA in tissues can be easily controlled by the expression of tissue-specific MetRS mutants capable of attaching photo-ANA to methionyl-tRNA. For example, by expressing tissue-specific MetRS mutants in body wall muscles and all neurons, we showed that MACSPI can profile muscle-and neuron-specific proteomes and interactomes. Future efforts will focus on profiling proteomes and interactomes in specific neuron types in intact animals, such as the six touch receptor neurons. In fact, our method was able to label these cells out of ~1,000 somatic cells. We are currently working on improving the efficiency of protein isolation and the sensitivity of mass spectrometry detection to achieve higher cellular resolution. Furthermore, the photo-ANA-based approach should be readily extended to study other pathogenic bacteria or even fungi or parasites, as long as a corresponding MetRS can be expressed. In addition to C. elegans and host–pathogen interplay, we envision that the utilization of photo-ANA can also be applied to other multicellular systems wherever the investigation of intercellular protein–protein interactions is desired.

17121120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121120.value: In this project, we created a new way to study proteins and their interactions within different tissues of whole living organisms. We used a special molecule called photo-ANA, which can be added to proteins in certain tissues. This molecule has two parts: one helps us identify the proteins, while the other helps us see how they interact with each other, even if these interactions are weak or temporary. Photo-ANA can be used to study proteins and their interactions in all kinds of organisms. We showed that it's a great tool for looking at how bacteria like S. Typhimurium work during infections, as well as studying muscle and nerve cells in C. elegans, a tiny worm often used in scientific research. Since C. elegans is used to study many different areas of biology, we think our method will be helpful in lots of different situations, like understanding how proteins and their interactions change during development, or in different health and disease conditions.

17121220.value: 上皮性卵巢癌（EOC）是全球最致命的女性惡性腫瘤之一。 儘管癌症治療取得了進步，但在過去的幾十年中，卵巢癌的治愈率僅得到了適度的提高。 該癌症的高死亡率是由於晚期卵巢癌的轉移性進展。最近的證據表明，轉移性卵巢癌細胞對腫瘤微環境壓力的適應對於轉移性進展至關重要。 但是，相關的分子機制仍然不清楚。越來越多的證據表明，低氧在控制卵巢癌的跨腔傳播中起著至關重要的作用。 缺氧誘導因子激活許多基因，促進腫瘤血管形成，細胞外基質重編程，轉移前小生境發展，癌細胞存活，細胞遷移/侵襲以及轉移部位的外滲等。因此，靶向低氧似乎是阻止癌症轉移的一種有前途的方法 。我們的先導研究使用cDNA微陣列分析技術鑑定了在缺氧性卵巢癌細胞中顯著誘導的BCL2A1。 進一步的研究表明，應激會立即誘導BCL2A1，隨後表達逐漸降低，這表明卵巢癌細胞中存在針對BCL2A1表達的自動調節系統。 由於NF-κB是感染和壓力後的早期反應信號，因此我們的發現證實了NF-κB信號是缺氧誘導BCL2A1所必需的。功能研究表明，BCL2A1在脅迫條件下增強了灶形成能力，表明BCL2A1參與卵巢癌細胞的細胞存活。細胞色素c的檢測表明，此過程是由對固有凋亡途徑的干預所介導的，在該途徑中，BCL2A1與僅BH3蛋白Bid / Bad / HRK相互作用並抑制其生長。另一方面，BCL2A1的延長表達抑制了正常培養中卵巢癌細胞中滯留的G1的細胞週期進程，而BCL2A1的耗竭則通過誘導p27和p18促進了G1 / S過渡。這些結果表明高水平的BCL2A1抑制了在正常條件下培養的細胞增殖。值得注意的是，BCL2A1在缺氧區高表達，但在鼠肝表面形成的腫瘤結節的血管區域低表達。因此，我們假設BCL2A1在卵巢癌腹膜轉移過程中，在控制細胞存活和細胞生長中起著雙重協調作用。 在這項研究中，我們將深入研究BCL2A1在保護卵巢癌細胞免受壓力和促進腫瘤生長方面的分子機制。 我們還將剖析BCL2A1在卵巢癌腹膜轉移中的臨床相關性。 基於已驗證的分子機制，我們將嘗試測試藥物抑製劑干擾BCL2A1致癌特性的可行性。 我們堅信，我們的擬議工作可能會為探索BCL2A1作為治療靶標來阻止卵巢癌的經結腸擴散而提供科學依據。

17121220.label: Realisation of objectives
17121220.value: Objective 1: To completely decipher the molecular mechanisms of BCL2A1 in regulating ovarian cancer cell survival and growth. 1) The role of NF-kB signaling as the upstream regulators of BCL2A1 induction in various physiological stresses. In ovarian cancer cells (OVCA433, ES-2, RMG-1), BCL2A1 expression was stimulated under physiological stress conditions, including hypoxia, glucose deprivation, anoikis, ascitic fluid, and OCM (patient-derived omental conditional medium) (Fig.1A, as shown in Section 8, No. 2). NF-kB signaling is an early response to tumor environment stresses. Given that BCL2A1 is a direct transcriptional target of NF-kB, it is crucial to determine whether the activation of NF-kB plays a role in the induction of BCL2A1 expression under these physiological stresses. Hence, the expression of BCL2A1 and p-IkB was assessed following stress stimulation at various time points. It revealed a positive correlation between p-IkB and BCL2A1 expression (Fig.1B). Furthermore, upon inhibiting NF-kB signaling with siRNA targeting NF-kB p65 (RELA), BCL2A1 induction was delayed and diminished compared to parental cells subjected to stress conditions (Fig.1C). These findings underscored the involvement of activated NF-kB signaling in the upregulation of BCL2A1 expression in response to physiological stresses in ovarian cancer cells. 2) HIF1a is involved in BCL2A1 expression upon stress treatments? BCL2A1 was characterized as an inducible factor by Affymetrix GeneChip 3' Expression Array, which aimed to profile hypoxic vs. normoxic ovarian cancer cells (Fig.2A). It is questioned whether the induction of BCL2A1 by hypoxia is induced through HIF1a signaling. Hence, we evaluated the expression of BCL2A1 in HIF1a transiently transfected ovarian cancer cells using qPCR and western blot analyses. Overexpression of HIF1a resulted in a significant increase in BCL2A1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels (Fig.2B). Conversely, knockdown of HIF1a resulted in downregulation of BCL2A1 expression (Fig.3B), suggesting that the upregulation of BCL2A1 in response to hypoxia in ovarian cancer cells is likely driven by HIF1a signaling. 3) The crosstalk between NF-kB and HIF1a signaling on the induction of BCL2A1. We co-transfected NF-kB luciferase reporter plasmid into HIF1a knockdown ovarian cancer cells. The changes of NF-kB luciferase signals were evaluated in response to hypoxia treatment (Fig.3A). In HIF1a knockdown ovarian cancer cells, NF-kB luciferase activity was reduced significantly. Consistently, p-IkB and BCL2A1 stimulation was also attenuated in HIF1a knockdown cells (Fig.3B). In contrast, overexpression of HIF1a collectively induced both p-IkB and BCL2A1 expression (Fig.2B). As a consequence of HIF1 expression alteration due to the tumor environment, particularly hypoxia, both NF-kB signaling and BCL2A1 activity were impacted, alluding that HIF1a was conceivably served as a potential upstream regulator of BCL2A1 induction via NF-kB signaling. 4) The regulation mechanism of BCL2A1 on P18 and P27. We propose that BCL2A1 per se has a dichotomous role in ovarian cancer cell growth. To further study the functional roles of BCL2A1 in ovarian cancer progression, BCL2A1 stable cell lines with overexpression or gene knockdown were established by lentiviral expression of BCL2A1 cDNA or shRNAs. Overexpression of BCL2A1 in ovarian cancer cells resulted in a decrease in cell viability rather than an increase under normal culture conditions (Fig.4A). Conversely, knockdown of BCL2A1 led to enhanced cell proliferation in the same culture medium (Fig.4A). Flow cytometric analysis revealed that overexpressed BCL2A1 induced G1-phase cell cycle arrest in ovarian cancer cells when cultured without stress (Fig.4B). Western blot analysis using the Cell Cycle Regulation Antibody Sampler Kit (Cell Signaling) confirmed that BCL2A1 upregulated the expression levels of P18 and P27 in ovarian cancer cells, further supporting its impact on G1/S cell cycle transition (Fig.4C). 5) The role of BCL2A1 in autophagic cell death. Emerging evidence shows that several members of BCL2 family proteins interact with Beclin1 to block caspase-independent autophagic cell death during cellular stress. To examine the correlation between BCL2A1 and autophagy, we assessed the expression of the autophagy marker light chain 3B (LC3B) in ovarian cancer cells subjected to various stress conditions. Autophagosome membrane formation by converting LC3B-I to lipidated LC3B-II is an established indicator of autophagy. Treatment of ovarian cancer cells with diverse conditions resulted in a marked accumulation in BCL2A1 expression, accompanied by a rise in LC3B-II conversion (Fig.5A). Our findings validated that induced BCL2A1 triggered autophagy progress by facilitating the turnover of LC3B, as evidenced by the accumulation of LC3B-II. Notably, the enhanced expression of both LC3B and BCL2A1 was in a time-dependent manner. To gain insight into the mechanism of BCL2A1 in the autophagy process, we assessed the interaction of BCL2A1 and Beclin-1 by proximity ligation assay (PLA) in ovarian cancer cell lines and primary cells derived from ascitic fluid (Fig.5B). Positive signals were detected in both cell types, while primary cells exhibited much stronger interaction. Objective 2: To dissect the clinical relevance of BCL2A1 in ovarian cancer metastatic progression. 1）The clinical significance of BCL2A1 in metastatic ovarian cancer cells in peritoneal cavity. In vitro, overexpression of BCL2A1 promoted cell invasion and migration upon stressed conditions (Fig.6A). In an ex vivo experiment, we co-cultured BCL2A1 knockdown ovarian cancer cells on the surface of patient-derived omentum samples. The knockdown cells demonstrated a reduced rate of movement on the omentum and primarily formed smaller colonies (Fig.6B). To address the importance of BCL2A1 and NF-kB to ovarian cancer biological behavior, tissue microarray of 40 pairs matched ovarian primary cancer samples with metastatic cancer samples (OV812) were analyzed to evaluate the expressions of BCL2A1 and p-IkB by immunohistochemistry staining. We identified a strong correlation between BCL2A1 and p-IkB expression, with elevated levels of both proteins observed in metastatic cancer samples (Fig.6C). Our findings were further supported by the analysis of another tissue array (OV483a) with normal ovary tissue and ovarian cancer samples characterized by clinical stage, which revealed concurrent upregulation of BCL2A1 and p-IkB in stage III ovarian cancer samples (Fig.6D). Note, in line with our primary results, as expected, higher levels of BCL2A1 and p-IkB in stressed zones in ovarian tumor samples. These results provided substantial evidence for the crucial involvement of the NF-kB/BCL2A1 axis in ovarian cancer metastasis progression. Objective 3: To test the feasibility of using NF-kB inhibitors or BCL2A1 targeting approach in impeding metastatic colonization of ovarian cancer cells. 1）Targeting NF-kB signaling to impede metastatic dissemination of ovarian cancer cells. Due to the limited availability of commercial small molecules for BCL2A1 inhibition, we evaluated the metastatic dissemination effect of RELA/NF-kB p65 inhibitors, including RELA/NF-kB p65 [p-Ser529, p-Ser536] inhibitor peptide set and commercial inhibitor BAY11-7082 in SCID mice (Fig.7A). We generated ES-2 cells labeled with LV-CMV-Rluc-IRES-GFP pre-made lentiviral particles containing luciferase and GFP reporters (ES-2-GFP-Luc). Then, we inoculated 5 x 106 ES-2-GFP-Luc cells in 200 µL of PBS into SCID mice intraperitoneally. Once palpable tumors formed after one week, we administered various doses (as follows) of RELA/NF-kB p65 inhibitor peptides and BAY11-7082 intraperitoneally every two days for a total of six injections to the tumor-bearing mice. Saline was injected intraperitoneally as a negative control. Group-1:ES-2-GFP-Luc+NF-kB peptide inhibitors(5 mg/kg/i.p.) Group-2:ES-2-GFP-Luc+NF-kB peptide control(5 mg/kg/i.p.) Group-3:ES-2-GFP-Luc+BAY11-7082(10 mg/kg/i.p.) Group-4:ES-2-GFP-Luc+Control(saline). IVIS Spectrum in vivo Imaging system was used to assess cancer cell metastasis within the mice's intraperitoneal cavity on a weekly basis after two weeks post-injection (Fig.7B). There was a trend of inhibition on tumor growth and metastasis upon treatment of NF-kB P65 inhibitor peptide set.

17121220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121220.value: Major findings: 1. BCL2A1 was induced not only by hypoxia but also other physiological stresses through NFkB signaling and then was gradually reduced by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway in ascites-derived ovarian cancer cells. 2. The upregulated BCL2A1 was frequently found in advanced metastatic ovarian cancer cells, suggesting its clinical relevance in ovarian cancer metastatic progression. Furthermore, IHC analysis additionally proved the clinical relevance that BCL2A1 and p-IκB was frequently upregulated in metastatic ovarian cancers, inferring the NF-κB /BCL2A1 axis is required for ovarian cancer metastatic progression. 3. BCL2A1 enhanced the foci formation ability, cell migration and invasion capabilities of ovarian cancer cells in a stress-conditioned medium, colony formation in an ex vivo omental tumor model, and tumor dissemination in vivo. Under stress conditions, BCL2A1 accumulated and colocalized with mitochondria to suppress intrinsic cell apoptosis by interacting with the BH3-only subfamily BCL2 members HRK/BAD/BID in ovarian cancer cells. 4. The stresses-induced BCL2A1 expression in ovarian cancer cells was attributed to the crosstalk between NF-κB and HIF-1α signaling. Overexpression of HIF-1α in ovarian canceer cells led to the concomitant increase in p-IκB and BCL2A1 expressions. Meanwhile, BCL2A1 expression in hypoxic ovarian cancer cells with HIF-1α induction and siRNA-mediated knockdown of NF-κB p65 (RELA) was not apparently activated as before, alluding that HIF-1α signaling is conceivably involved as the upstream regulator of BCL2A1 induction via NF-κB signaling. 5. Stresses-induced BCL2A1 was able to trigger autophagy in ovarian cancer cells by interacting with Beclin1 and facilitating the turnover of LC3, leading to cell survival of ovarian cancer cells in stressed conditions. 6. The significance of NF-κB/BCL2A1 signaling cascade in promoting intraperitoneal metastatic colonization of ovarian cancer cells was examined using an intraperitoneal tumor xenograft mouse model and results showed there was a trend of inhibition on tumor growth and metastasis upon treatment of NF-κB P65 inhibitor peptide set. 17121220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121220.value: Our findings suggest NF-κB signaling is crucially in upregulation of BCL2A1 upon stress stimulation. The upregulation of BCL2A1, which in turns, blocks the effects of HRK, Bad and Bid in releasing cytochrome C from mitochondria and subsequent cell apoptosis in the stressed conditions. This is equivalent to the early stages of metastatic dissemination of ovarian cancer cells when the tumor nodules have developed well vascularized system. Indeed, data here consistently indicated that there was a trend of inhibition on tumor growth and metastasis upon treatment of NF-κB P65 inhibitor peptide set, suggesting that targeting NF-κB/BCL2A1 signaling could impede metastatic dissemination of ovarian cancer cells. Thus, subsequent testing of optimal inhibitor peptide doses can be conducted and if significant outcomes are achieved, there is potential for translating these findings into targeted therapeutic approaches for women with transcoelomic metastasis of ovarian cancers.

17121220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121220.value: Ovarian cancer mortality is mainly due to metastasis. Micrometastases in the peritoneal cavity pose a challenge in treating ovarian cancer, requiring effective targeted interventions for good management. Hypoxia is commonly found in solid tumors like ovarian cancer and plays a significant role in the spread of cancer cells. Recent research has identified that BCL2A1 helps ovarian cancer cells survive under stressful conditions, including low oxygen levels. Our initial findings suggest that BCL2A1 is more active in the hypoxic regions of tumor nodules compared to areas with better blood supply. This research project aims to further understand the molecular mechanisms by which BCL2A1 protects ovarian cancer cells from stress and promotes tumor growth through regulation with HIF1a and NF-κB crosstalk, p18/p27 cascade and autophagic cell death. Additionally, we had examined the clinical relevance of BCL2A1 in peritoneal metastasis and explored the potential of targeting NFkB signaling using a peptide inhibitor to interfere with the cancer-promoting properties of BCL2A1. The ultimate goal is to establish BCL2A1 as a therapeutic target for preventing the spread of ovarian cancer within the abdomen.

17121420.value: 人類免疫缺陷1型病毒（HIV-1）感染會導致獲得性免疫缺陷病綜合症（AIDS）。儘管正致力普及昂貴的抗逆轉錄病毒聯合療法 (cART)，但HIV-1仍主要通過無保護的性接觸在香港和世界各地傳播。為了有效阻止AIDS的傳播，現階段必須研發新的治療方法及其相關的分子機制來治療HIV-1感染。最近，我們發現雙特異性中和抗體BiIA-SG對所有測試的HIV-1亞型和測試菌株均表現出明顯的廣度和效力（JCI 2018）。使用第三代HIV-1 / 人源化小鼠模型，我們證明了在體內延長表達 AAV載體BiIA-SG有助於消除脾臟中受感染的T細胞。我們也證明了在停止cART聯合可溶性BiIA-SG治療，或cART聯合 47抗體治療後，仍無法有效地持續控制HIV-I（AIDS 2019)。這些結果顯示了消除人源化小鼠內的潛伏病毒對治療是十分重要的。 與我們合作的研究團隊發現，細胞膜金屬蛋白酶TRABD2A能透過降解質膜上病毒體的多蛋白Gag結構前體去抑制靜止CD4 + T細胞中HIV-1的製造(Nat. Immunol.2019 ）。此外，在靜止CD4 + T細胞中消除或抑制TRABD2A金屬蛋白酶活性能顯著提高HIV-1的生產。這些結果均顯示TRABD2A能有效地遏止靜止CD4 + T細胞中HIV-1的組裝和複製。HIV-1主要潛伏在患者的靜止CD4 + T細胞中。因此，我們計畫研究BiIA-SG和TRABD2A的聯合使用能否成為治療HIV-1潛伏感染的有效免疫治療方案。我們會在HIV-1 /人源化小鼠中進行一項針對性的GRF研究，其目的有兩個：1） 評估BiIA-SG和TRABD2A抗體或藥物聯合治療對HIV-1潛伏感染的功效並與單一療法作比較（1-1.5年）和 2）確定聯合使用cART和TRABD2A抗體或藥物治療HIV-1潛伏感染的療效（1.5-3年）。通過進行上述提議的研究，我們將揭示TRBD2A抗體或藥物和BiIA-SG在治療HIV-1感染中的作用，特別是在促進消除潛伏感染的靜止CD4 + T細胞以達至HIV-1功能性治療。

17121520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121520.value: Adipose tissue is a highly plastic endocrine organ. (1) Functionally, it can be converted from energy storing white adipose tissue to thermogenic brown adipose tissue to potentiate weight loss. (2) During onset of obesity, adipose tissue becomes fibrotic which contributes to adipose dysfunction and systemic metabolic disorders. (3) Anatomically, adipose tissues in different locations have distinct clinical implications. Abdominal obesity is more strongly associated with metabolic abnormalities. Currently the key regulator and physiological cue that dictate adipose remodelling still remain incompletely understood. PRDM16 (PR domain containing 16) is a master regulator for brown fat development. Recently several studies demonstrate that PRDM16 exerts metabolic-protective functions beyond its role in adipose browning, including repression of adipose fibrosis. But how PRDM16 is transcriptionally regulated at physiological conditions remains elusive. Androgen plays an important role in regulation of body fat distribution and function via activation of androgen receptor (AR). Androgen excess is significantly correlated with and contributes to higher body mass index (BMI), abdominal obesity, and metabolic derangements. But the mechanism linking androgen-AR activation to adipocyte dysfunction is poorly understood. By using our unique PRDM16-reporter system to search for potential factors that regulate PRDM16 expression, we found that AR expression is negatively associated with PRDM16 in adipocytes. Further analysis revealed that activation of AR downregulates PRDM16 expression, in accompany with reduced browning in adipocytes and in animal models. Mice deficient of AR display elevated PRDM16 expression, higher browning and reduced fibrosis. Based on these findings, we hypothesise that androgen/AR complex serves as an endogenous suppressor of PRDM16 expression. By suppressing PRDM16 expression, hyperandrogenism impairs browning and increases fibrosis especially in omental white adipose tissue, which in turn leads to central obesity, adipose dysfunction and systemic metabolic disorders. To prove this hypothesis, drug inducible adipocyte-specific Ar KO mice and supplementation of AR agonist will be employed to clarify the function of androgen in adipose tissue. Moreover, we will also use Ar/Prdm16 double KO mice and strategy to overexpress PRDM16 to address whether PRDM16 is required for the actions of androgen in adipocytes. The detailed molecular events downstream of AR activation will also be elucidated. The study will facilitate a better understanding on physiological function of androgen in adipose remodelling. Additionally, a new connection between androgen-PRDM16 will be established, which will shed light on development of novel strategies for anti-obesity and other related diseases. 背景：脂肪組織是壹個高度活躍且可塑的內分泌器官。從功能上它能夠從作為能量儲存態的白色脂肪組織(WAT)轉變為以產熱為主要生理活動的棕色脂肪組織(BAT)。臨床以及動物實驗方面的研究均證實脂肪褐變具有壹系列的有益功能。在肥胖的發展過程中，脂肪組織的纖維化在脂肪組織肥大以及其並發的全身性代謝功能障礙中起重要作用。在解剖學上，存在於不同部位的脂肪組織擁有截然不同的臨床意義。與皮下脂肪的聚集相比，腹型肥胖與代謝異常有更加緊密的聯系。目前，引導脂肪重塑的關鍵調控因子以及其生理學意義仍未得到充分的了解。 PRDM16 (PR domain-containing 16) 是棕色和米色脂肪發育的重要轉錄調控因子。近期的幾項研究表明PRDM16在代謝性疾病中具有保護作用，除了其在脂肪褐變中的作用還可抑制脂肪纖維化。然而在生理條件下，PRDM16的轉錄調控機制仍然未得到闡明。 雄性激素通過激活雄激素受體(AR)，在調節體內脂肪的分布及功能中起重要作用。雄性激素過多與體重指數(BMI)，腹部肥胖以及代謝功能紊亂均有密切的聯系。然而對於雄激素受體激活與脂肪細胞功能障礙之間的聯系仍未有充分的理解。 利用我們所建立的獨特的PRDM16追蹤表達系統，我們分析了PRDM16表達的潛在調控因子，並發現AR的表達與脂肪細胞中PRDM16的表達呈負相關關系。進壹步的分析表明，AR的激活能夠下調PRDM16的表達，同時在離體脂肪細胞以及動物模型中，脂肪褐變均受到抑制。缺乏AR的小鼠表型為PRDM16表達升高，脂肪褐變增強以及脂肪纖維化減少。 假設：雄激素/AR復合體是PRDM16的內源性抑制劑。通過抑制PRDM16，雄激素過多能夠抑制脂肪褐變並且增加尤其是在網膜脂肪組織中的纖維化，從而引起中樞性肥胖以及胰島素抵抗癥狀。 方法：局部AR敲除以及AR/PRDM16雙敲除小鼠，AAV介導的PRDM16過表達，以及AR激動劑補充將被用於體內以及體外的研究。ChIP-seq以及熒光素酶報告基因檢測將被用於數據分析。 預期結果：該研究將揭示雄激素在脂肪組織重塑中的生理功能。同時，雄激素與PRDM16的關聯將被進壹步闡明。其結果能夠為抗肥胖以及代謝綜合癥的研究策略提供新的啟示。

17121520.label: Realisation of objectives
17121520.value: All the objectives have been realized. The major findings are summarized below. Objective (1) determine the age-dependent function of androgen/AR in adipose tissue using inducible adipocyte Ar KO mice; In order to address the age-dependent function of androgen/AR, we firstly compared the effect of AR agonist, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), on young and adult female mice. To this end, we implanted the silicone tube containing DHT to establish the chronic, sustained release model of DHT. The success of the model establishment was validated by serum level of DHT, and elevation of AR downstream genes in the animals. We found that chronic activation of AR signalling enhances the expansion of the adipose tissue in visceral part, but not in subcutaneous counterpart, while this effect was not prominent in adult mice. In accompany, the whole body insulin resistance was exacerbated by DHT administration in young-aged female mice. However, we unexpectedly found that albeit increased adiposity in the omentum and more severe whole body insulin resistance, the insulin sensitivity in visceral adipose tissue was improved by chronic administration of DHT, as determined by insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of AKT. (2) To investigate whether the detrimental effects of androgen on adipose tissue browning is mediated through suppression of PRDM16; We firstly established the inducible PRDM16 expression stromal vascular cell line by using the Tet-on system. The inducible expression was confirmed. After that, we differentiated the stromal vascular cell line to mature adipocytes and treated the adipocytes with DHT. Meanwhile, doxycycline was added to the cell medium to induce the expression of PRDM16. The results showed that the inhibitory effect of DHT on adipocyte browning was overcome upon overexpression of PRDM16, as evidenced by oxygen consumption rate, expression of browning markers. (3) To interrogate whether androgen enhances adipose fibrosis and insulin resistance via PRDM16; To approach this question, we managed to mate the AR adipocyte-selective knockout mice with Prdm16 transgenic mice. We found that overexpression of PRDM16 in adipocytes protected against HFD and aging-associated adipose fibrosis in both WT and AR adipocyte-overexpression mice. These results demonstrate that PRDM16 acts downstream of AR signaling to regulate the tissue fibrosis in adipose tissue. (4) To elucidate the mechanism by which androgen suppresses Prdm16 transcription. To address this question, we performed the Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) experiment, which is a new and alternative method to chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) technology to investigate genomic localization of certain protein in cells. We have found that AR protein indeed bound at the promoter region of Prdm16, but not at the Ucp1 and several other beige adipocyte marker gene locus. According to the CUT&Tag result, the specific binding site of AR on PRDM16 gene locus was identified, which was further validated by ChIP. These observations demonstrate that AR directly interferes with the transactivation of Prdm16, which in turn alters the reprogramming of downstream browning in beige adipocytes.

17121520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121520.value: This project aims to reveal the unrecognized physiological function of androgen in control of adipose remodelling, and to elucidate the underpinning mechanism. We found that in adipocytes, androgen acts through AR to suppress adipocyte browning in a depot- and age-selective manner. Mechanistically the action of androgen/AR complex is mediated via direct inhibition of PRDM16, a key transcriptional co-regulator in adipose tissue. The findings shed light on development of new strategies for anti-obese and anti-metabolic syndromes. The major findings and research outcome are described as follows: In order to address the age-dependent function of androgen/AR, we compared the effect of AR agonist, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), on young and adult female mice. We found that chronic activation of AR signalling enhances the expansion of the adipose tissue in visceral part, but not in subcutaneous counterpart, while this effect was not prominent in adult mice. In accompany, the whole body insulin resistance was exacerbated by DHT administration in young-aged female mice. More importantly, we found that DHT infusion or adipocyte-selective overexpression of AR inhibited the remodeling of white adipose tissue browning. To investigate the mechanism, we further found that DHT infusion or adipocyte-selective overexpression of AR significantly inhibited the transcription of Prdm16, which encodes a transcriptional master regulator of adipose tissue remodelling, including browning. Furthermore overexpression of PRDM16 rectified the compromised browning and metabolic disorders in adipocyte selective AR KO mice, and in AR KO adipocytes in vitro. These results suggest that androgen and AR act via PRDM16 in adipose tissue (Zhao et al. Advanced Science. 2023). To elucidate the mechanism by which androgen suppresses Prdm16 transcription, we performed the Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) experiment to map the AR binding sites in a genome-wide manner. We have found that AR protein bound at the promoter region of Prdm16, but not at the Ucp1 and several other beige adipocyte marker gene locus, demonstrating that AR directly interferes with the transactivation of Prdm16, which in turn alters the reprogramming of downstream browning in beige adipocytes (Zhao et al. Advanced Science. 2023).

17121520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121520.value: In this project, we have uncovered that androgen receptor is the strongest negative regulator of PRDM16, which is a key master regulator of adipose browning and fibrosis. Our findings demonstrated that in adipocytes, androgen acts through AR to suppress adipocyte browning in a depot- and age-selective manner. Mechanistically the action of androgen/AR complex is mediated via direct inhibition of PRDM16, a key transcriptional co-regulator in adipose tissue. The findings shed light on development of new strategies for anti-obese and anti-metabolic syndromes. Furthermore, these findings expands the understanding on the action of sex hormones on adipose tissue remodeling, and highlight the heterogeneous mechanism of action for androgen and androgen receptors, which work in age, and adipose depot selective manner. In future, the differential mode of action for androgen is worthy to be examined in further, to facilitate precision medicine. Moreover, the crosstalk between the white adipose tissue with other organs/tissues, under the action of androgen, will be an intriguing direction to explore. For example, whether and how the adipose tissue contributes to prostate cancer in response to androgen stimulation, will be a question of interest and translation value.

17121520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121520.value: Obesity is now becoming a global epidemic. During the onset of obesity and its associated metabolic disorders, the remodeling of adipose tissue from a healthy one to the unhealthy dysfunctional status. PRDM16 is a key transcriptional regulator of adipose tissue remodeling. Multiple studies have highlighted the essential function of PRDM16 in maintaining the metabolic health of the adipose tissue. However the knowledge regarding how PRDM16 is regulated at the physiological and pathological conditions is unclear. In the current project, we uncovered that androgen acts as a negative regulator of PRDM16 expression, and the mechanism is investigated as well. We have also discovered a sex dimorphic difference of PRDM16 in human, which is consistent with our finding that androgen is a negative regulator of PRDM16. Therefore these findings provide new explanation on sex hormone-induced metabolic disorders. In future strategies aiming to alleviate androgen excess or AR hyperactivation may serve as a new therapy to treat obesity and metabolic diseases.

17121620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121620.value: Human enterovirus EV-A71 is one of several Enterovirus serotypes that cause hand-foot-and-mouth disease, which can produce life-threatening neurological complications. Severe outbreaks caused by different enteroviruses, including EV-A71 and CV-A16, have been reported periodically throughout the world. Nevertheless, neither an effective vaccine nor an anti-enteroviral drug is available. Our recent work has identified a novel interferon gamma (IFNg) inducible EV-A71 entry factor, a host-produced tryptophanyl tRNA synthetase (hWARS), which is not only essential for translation but also upregulated for effective enterovirus infection. In addition to hWARS, several other cellular factors have been reported to interact with EV-A71 on the cell surface. However, the key biological pathway regulating receptor/entry factor-mediated EV-A71 endocytosis remains elusive. In this proposed study, we would like to investigate cell entry pathway of enterovirus by studying the interaction between the hWARS and the EV-A71. We will first investigate the protein interactome of hWARS by using liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry analysis (LC-MS/MS). Our preliminary protein interactome analysis suggests that hWARS could be involved in a receptor-trafficking pathway regulated by BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis. We hypothesize that hWARS could be excreted extracellularly through BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis as a form of microvesicle. The hWARS-decorated extracellular microvesicles can then interact with the EV-A71; hence facilitating enteroviral infection through BBSome-mediated retrieval. To prove, we have first established a protocol for purification of microvesicle. Preliminarily, we have successfully isolated microvesicles from cell culture conditioned media which can be positively stained with anti-hWARS. We have further demonstrated the interaction between the hWARS-decorated microvesicles and the EV-A71 by using immunogold electron microscopy and co-immunoprecipitation analyses. The uptake of hWARS-decorated extracellular microvesicles will be further investigated through production of artificially generated hWARS-decorated fluorescent microvesicles followed by confocal microscopy analysis. Lastly, we will test the inhibitory effect of BBSome-targeting drugs on EV-A71 infectivity. As a proof-of-concept, three drugs, cytochalasin D, jasplakinolide and latrunculin A, which have been known to modulate the actin dynamics critically important for vesicular trafficking of BBSome-mediated retrieval, have been administrated to cells before their challenge with EV-A71. Our pilot data have shown initial promise to control EV-A71 replication through targeting the BBSome pathway. Drugs targeting other biological molecules that are important in regulating BBSome-mediated retrieval and ectocytosis will also be tested. Overall, our proposed work may shed new light on the mechanism of enterovirus cell entry. The information obtained from this study could also be beneficial for the future development of anti-enterovirus therapy. 人类肠道病毒EV-A71是导致手足口病的肠道病毒血清型之一，严重者可诱发致命性的神经系统并发症。全球范围内时常爆发不同血清型肠道病毒感染的疫情，包括EV-A71和CV-A16型，然而目前尚无任何有效的疫苗以及抗肠道病毒药物。我们近期研究发现宿主体内的色氨酸tRNA合成酶（hWARS）是干扰素γ诱导的EV-A71入侵因子。hWARS不仅在蛋白质翻译过程中必不可少，其表达量在肠道病毒感染过程中也显著上调。除hWARS之外，其他几个细胞因子与EV-A71在细胞表面相互作用已被报道，然而调节受体或细胞因子介导EV-A71内吞的关键生理途径仍未得到阐述。在此项拟议研究中，我们将通过hWARS和EV-A71的相互作用研究以阐明肠道病毒入侵细胞的途径与机制。我们将首先利用液相色谱串联质谱（LC-MS/MS）研究hWARS的蛋白交互作用。我们初步蛋白交互作用结果表明hWARS有可能参与到BBSome介导的纤毛形成所调节的受体转运途径。我们假设hWARS可以通过BBSome介导的纤毛生成以微囊泡的形式分泌出胞，hWARS修饰的胞外微囊泡可以与EV-A71相作用并且通过BBSome介导的入胞方式促进肠道病毒感染。为了论证上述假设，我们首先建立了胞外微囊泡的纯化实验方案并初步成功的从细胞外培养基中分离出微囊泡，并且发现了抗-hWARS染色阳性的微囊泡。我们通过免疫金电镜技术和免疫共沉淀研究进一步发现hWARS修饰的微囊泡可与EV-A71相互作用。hWARS修饰的微囊泡入胞方式将通过人工构建hWARS修饰的荧光微囊泡与共聚焦显微镜术深入研究。最后我们将测试微囊泡靶向性药物对EV-A71感染的抑制性。作为概念验证，三个可以调控肌动蛋白动力学以干扰囊泡转运的药物（细胞松弛素D/Jasplakinolide/红海海绵素A ）将在EV-A71感染前预处理细胞。我们的实验数据初步显示BBSome通路的靶向性药物可以控制EV-A71的复制。与此同时，其他参与调控BBSome介导的回收/入胞的生物分子靶向性药物将进一步检测。综上所述，我们所提议课题研究将进一步阐释肠道病毒感染的入胞机制，此项研究中所获得相关信息也将有利于未来抗肠道病毒治疗的研发。

17121620.label: Realisation of objectives
17121620.value: We are pleased to report that we have successfully achieved all the objectives outlined in our grant proposal. Through meticulous planning and execution, we have completed the investigation of receptor/entry factors-decorated microvesicles production from different cell types under both IFNγ-stimulated and unstimulated conditions. Additionally, we have thoroughly examined the interaction between EV-A71 and hWARS-decorated microvesicles. Our research also delved into the role of vesicular trafficking of BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis during enterovirus infection. Finally, we explored the feasibility of using BBSome-targeting drugs as potential anti-enterovirus therapeutic options. Each of these objectives was met with rigorous scientific inquiry and the results have significantly advanced our understanding in these areas. Below are sections providing a detailed account of the work accomplished for each objective. Objective 1. To investigate the production of receptor/entry factors-decorated microvesicles from different cell types under IFNγ-stimulated and unstimulated conditions We have thoroughly characterized the production of hWARS-decorated microvesicles across 12 distinct human cell lines derived from kidney, muscle, liver, nerve, lung, cervical, and immune cells, both in the presence and absence of IFNγ. Our findings have indicated that seven of the tested cell lines (293T, RD, NT2, Calu-3, HeLa, U-937, and H9) were capable of producing hWARS-decorated microvesicles under IFNγ-stimulating conditions. In the absence of IFNγ, only 293T, HeLa, and U-937 cell lines were able to produce hWARS-decorated microvesicles, albeit at lower levels. These results have been validated through the repetition of independent experiments. Our data concluded that hWARS could be secreted from cells via the process of ciliogenesis in response to IFNγ stimulation. Objective 2. To investigate the interaction between EV-A71 and hWARS-decorated microvesicles To investigate the interaction between EV-A71 and hWARS-decorated microvesicles, we purified the conditioned culture supernatant from 293T cells, which produced the highest quantity of hWARS-decorated extracellular microvesicles. We then performed immunogold electron microscopy and pull-down experiments in the presence of EV-A71. Our results demonstrated that EV-A71 could directly interact with hWARS-decorated microvesicles. Using gradient centrifugation, we successfully co-purified naturally produced microvesicles with EV-A71 from permissive cell lines RD and Vero-E6. Our analysis revealed a high proportion of EV-A71-bound microvesicles. These findings suggest that EV-A71 infection may be influenced by the abundance of microvesicles produced by the host cells. Given that the surface proteins on microvesicles are specific to the cell type, we demonstrated that EV-A71 infectivity could be modulated by these cell type-specific microvesicles. This modulation could play a significant role in BBSome-mediated cell entry. These results form a crucial part of a manuscript we are currently preparing (attached). Furthermore, we confirmed the involvement of hWARS in this interaction by producing artificially generated microvesicles that presented hWARS as the sole surface protein. Our findings confirmed that EV-A71 could specifically bind to these hWARS-decorated microvesicles. No interaction was observed in the control group, where EV-A71 was inoculated with artificially generated microvesicles lacking hWARS. Objective 3. To investigate the role of vesicular trafficking of BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis during enterovirus infection The role of vesicular trafficking in BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis during enterovirus infection has been delineated. We observed a consistent, dose-dependent decrease in EV-A71 replication in supernatants of cells treated with the BBSome pathway inhibitors YM-58483, LaCl3, and CK-636 as assayed by Western blot, qPCR, and infection assay analyses. Interestingly, the levels of EV-A71 detected in cell lysates remained similar between the BBSome inhibitor-treated and mock-treated controls. Transmission electron microscopy further revealed that, in drug-treated cells, EV-A71 and microvesicles were sequestered within large vesicles associated with ciliary structures. This suggests that BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis is critical for the release of enterovirus from infected cells, as the inhibition of this pathway leads to viral entrapment within the cells. Objective 4. To explore the feasibility of using BBSome-targeting drugs as anti-enterovirus therapeutic options We have successfully identified BBSome-targeting drugs that can significantly inhibit the replication of EV-A71. Additionally, we have explored the anti-EV-A71 effects of less well-characterized drugs that may impact BBSome function. For instance, cytoskeletal protein-targeting drugs, including cytochalasin D, jasplakinolide, and latrunculin A, inhibit vesicular trafficking events involving the retrieval of extracellular microvesicles, which require an intact cytoskeletal network. Moreover, we tested vemurafenib, a known inhibitor of the MAPK signaling pathway. Vemurafenib disrupts the MAPK signaling cascade, potentially impacting Rab5-mediated endocytosis, a process essential for the internalization and trafficking of EV-A71 within host cells, and regulated by the BBSome-mediated DLK-MAPK signaling pathway. The anti-EV-A71 effects of vemurafenib have been fully characterized, with an EC50 (half-maximal effective concentration) of 0.34 ± 0.01 µM and a CC50 (half-maximal cytotoxic concentration) of 17.71 ± 0.58 µM. This work has been published (doi.org/10.3390/ph15091067).

17121620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121620.value: Our study has demonstrated that EV-A71 infection can be regulated by BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis, a cellular process crucial for the virus's release and infectivity. This was evidenced by experiments that specifically targeted the BBSome pathway. Using inhibitors such as YM-58483, LaCl3, and CK-636, we observed a dose-dependent reduction in EV-A71 replication. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed that, in drug-treated cells, EV-A71 and microvesicles were sequestered within large vesicles associated with ciliary structures, highlighting the importance of BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis in the release of enterovirus from infected cells. We further investigated the production and role of hWARS-decorated microvesicles in the context of EV-A71 infection. Across 12 human cell lines from various tissues, seven cell lines (293T, RD, NT2, Calu-3, HeLa, U-937, and H9) produced hWARS-decorated microvesicles when stimulated with IFNγ, while only 293T, HeLa, and U-937 cell lines did so under unstimulated conditions, albeit at lower levels. These findings partially explained the tissue tropism of EV-A71 by modulating the uptake of the virus-extracellular vesicle complex via BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis. Direct interaction between EV-A71 and hWARS-decorated microvesicles was demonstrated by immunogold electron microscopy and pull-down assays using the microvesicles naturally produced by cells. We further confirmed this by gradient centrifugation of permissive cell lines RD and Vero-E6 co-purified produced microvesicles with EV-A71. Comparative study of EV-A71 produced from cells producing different types of microvesicles suggested that the cell type-specific extracellular vesicles could modulate EV-A71 infectivity which could be regulated by BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis. Lastly, we produced artificially generated microvesicles presenting hWARS as the sole surface protein confirmed that EV-A71 specifically binds to these hWARS-decorated microvesicles, with no interaction observed in control microvesicles lacking hWARS. The results further confirmed the regulated roles of receptor-decorated microvesicles on EV-A71 infection. Given the important regulatory roles of BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis in EV-A71 infection, we explored the potential anti-EV-A71 strategies by targeting the BBSome pathway using several drugs. Importantly, we characterized a MAPK pathway inhibitor, vemurafenib, which could inhibit the BBSome-mediated DLK-MAPK pathway. We showed that cells treated with vemurafenib exhibited potent inhibition of Rab5-mediated endocytosis. Inhibition of this process resulted in the abolishment of EV-A71 internalization and hence reduced in infectivity. The pharmacokinetics, including the half-maximal effective concentration and half-maximal cytotoxic concentration have been characterized which could be useful for future clinical use.

17121620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121620.value: Our study has revealed the crucial role of BBSome-mediated ciliogenesis in regulating EV-A71 infection, highlighting potential therapeutic targets within this pathway. Our study has laid the groundwork for exploring new therapeutic strategies targeting the BBSome pathway to combat EV-A71 and potentially other enteroviruses. Future research can focus on optimizing the efficacy and specificity of identified inhibitors like YM-58483, LaCl3, and CK-636, as well as cytoskeletal protein-targeting drugs and vemurafenib. Moreover, deeper investigation into the molecular mechanisms governing the interaction between EV-A71 and hWARS-decorated microvesicles could uncover novel drug targets and biomarkers for early detection and intervention. Developing high-throughput screening methods to identify additional compounds that disrupt BBSome function or enhance the secretion of inhibitory microvesicles could accelerate the discovery of effective antiviral agents. Furthermore, the therapeutic potential of engineered microvesicles presenting specific receptor/entry factors can be explored for targeted delivery of antiviral agents. Understanding the broader implications of BBSome-mediated pathways in other viral infections and their role in immune response modulation could pave the way for broad-spectrum antiviral therapies. Overall, our findings open new avenues for innovative treatments and a deeper understanding of viral pathogenesis and host-pathogen interactions.

17121620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121620.value: Our research focuses on understanding how certain cells in the body produce tiny particles called microvesicles, which are decorated with different proteins, including an enterovirus receptor, hWARS. We found that the production of hWARS-decorated microvesicles can be significantly boosted when the cells are stimulated by a substance called IFNγ. These hWARS-decorated microvesicles can interact with an enterovirus, EV-A71, which can cause serious diseases in humans, particularly in children. By studying how these microvesicles and the virus interact, we discovered that certain drugs can disrupt this interaction and prevent the virus from spreading. Specifically, we identified drugs that can block a cellular pathway called the BBSome pathway, which is crucial for the virus to replicate and exit infected cells. One of the drugs we tested, vemurafenib, showed promising results in stopping the virus. The significance of our research lies in its potential to lead to new treatments for EV-A71 and possibly other viruses. By targeting the pathways that viruses use to spread, we can develop more effective antiviral therapies. This research could pave the way for innovative treatments that enhance our ability to combat viral infections and improve public health outcomes.

17121820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121820.value: Periodontitis is an infectious-inflammatory disease that affects more than 1 billion people worldwide. It is the leading cause of tooth loss in adults. Periodontitis results from a chronic build-up of bacterial communities in the shallow gum crevice around the base of the tooth. Its etiology is complex and multifactorial. Capnocytophaga gingivalis is one species of bacteria associated with periodontitis, especially within diabetic individuals. Unlike other Capnocytophaga species, C. gingivalis cells have potent ‘trypsin-like’ activities, i.e. they digest polypeptide chains after Arginine or Lysine residues. Trypsin-like activities are possessed by several other oral pathogens (e.g. Porphyromonas gingivalis), and are considered to be key drivers of periodontal disease. The trypsin-like activities of C. gingivalis have been attributed to the oligopeptidase B (OpdB) protein. Our preliminary bioinformatic analysis indicates that C. gingivalis actually encodes two oligopeptidase B (OpdB) proteins, as well as two prolyl oligopeptidase (POP) proteins. This is an extremely unusual (possibly unique) arrangement within bacteria. OpdB and POP both belong to the large S9 family of serine peptidases, and share significant sequence similarity, but have very different activities. POP proteins cleave peptide chains after Proline residues, and are pivotally-important for the hydrolysis of collagen fragments derived from host tissues. Here, we will dissect the activities of the C. gingivalis OpdB (OpdB1/OpdB2) and POP (POP1/POP2) proteins. We will establish their respective substrates and potential biological targets. We will use protein structure modelling to identify the key structural factors underpinning OpdB and POP activities. Structure activity-relationships for C. gingivalis OpdB1/OpdB2 and POP1/POP2 will be compared and contrasted with OpdB/POP proteins from related disease-causing bacteria. We will perform pop/opdB gene inactivation experiments in C. gingivalis and selected other Capnocytophaga species, and establish the phenotypes of the respective mutant strains to identify their biological roles. In particular, we will determine their peptide-degrading, cell-binding and biofilm formation activities. As OpdB proteins are cell-surface associated, we hypothesize that these proteins play key roles in cellular adhesion and multispecies biofilm formation. Notably, we will investigate whether S9 peptidase inhibitors (e.g. sitagliptin) inhibit OpdB/POP activities of C. gingivalis and related oral bacteria. We hypothesize such inhibitors may be used to significantly reduce the ‘disease-promoting’ peptide-degrading activities of dental plaque biofilms, to restore a healthy balance to the oral microbiome. In summary, this research proposal is aimed at identifying fundamentally-important biological mechanisms employed by bacteria that promote periodontal disease; with the future goal of inhibiting these specific processes promote the restoration of oral health. 牙周炎是一種感染性炎症疾病，影響全球超過10億人口，它是導致成人缺牙的首要原因。牙周炎由環繞牙齿頸部浅齦溝間隙中细菌菌群长期积累所致，它的病因複雜且包含多種因素。牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌是一種與牙周炎相關的細菌，它與伴有糖尿病的牙周炎患者關係密切。牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌與二氧化碳噬纖維菌屬其他菌種不同，它具有較強的“胰蛋白酶樣”活性，即它可以消化連接在精氨酸或賴氨酸殘基後的多肽鏈。胰蛋白酶樣活性也存在於其他牙周炎致病菌如牙齦卟啉單胞菌等，它被認為是牙周病的主要驅動因素。牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌的胰蛋白酶樣活性是由寡肽酶B (oligopeptidase B, OpdB)產生。 我們的前期生物信息學研究結果顯示，牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌編碼兩種寡肽酶B和兩種脯氨酰寡肽酶 (prolyl oligopeptidase, POP)，這在細菌中可能是一個獨一無二的發現。OpdB 和 POP均屬於絲氨酸蛋白酶家族中的S9家族，他們的蛋白序列相似但活性不同。POP切割脯氨酸殘基後的多肽鏈，它對來源於宿主的膠原蛋白片段的水解至關重要。 本項目將研究牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌寡肽酶B (OpdB1/OpdB2)和脯氨酰寡肽酶 (POP1/POP2)的蛋白活性，探究他們各自的作用底物和潛在生物靶點，同時使用蛋白質結構建模尋找支撐OpdB 和 POP活性的關鍵結構因素，對比二氧化碳噬纖維菌OpdB1/OpdB2和POP1/POP2和其他疾病致病菌OpdB/POP蛋白的結構活性關係。 本研究將在牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌和同種屬其他菌類中實施pop/opdB基因失活實驗，建立各自基因失活表型，以確定其在肽降解、細胞結合及生物膜形成中的生物學作用。因OpdB蛋白與細胞表面相關，推測這些蛋白在細胞粘附和多物種生物膜形成中發揮重要作用。 同時，我們將探究S9肽酶抑制劑如西格列汀是否可以抑制牙齦二氧化碳噬纖維菌和相關口腔細菌的OpdB/POP活性，推測這些抑制劑可以顯著降低與疾病進展相關的牙菌斑生物膜肽降解活性，以恢復口腔微生物菌群平衡。 綜上所述，本研究旨在探究牙周病細菌致病的基本生物學機制，未來的目標是抑制致病過程，促進口腔健康恢復。

17122320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122320.value: Associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) is a new surgical procedure that induces rapid liver regeneration in patients with small liver remnant planning for major liver resection. It is a two-staged operation with stage I including portal vein ligation and splitting the right liver away from the left liver. After stage I, the left liver will undergo rapid liver regeneration and the stage II operation can be performed at 7-10 days after stage I operation when the liver remnant reaches an adequate size. In stage II operation, the right liver that contains the tumor is then removed. This surgical procedure was incepted in Germany in 2013 and was later started in Queen Mary Hospital in Hong Kong for the first time in December 2015. The initial indication was mainly for colorectal liver metastasis but due to the relatively high incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in Hong Kong, we have transferred this procedure to be applied for hepatitis-related hepatocellular carcinoma and so far, we have cumulated one of the largest single-center experience in the literature. Nonetheless, the usual approach for ALPPS involved open surgery and induced substantial surgical stress to the patient, especially after stage I operation. With the advent of minimally invasive liver surgery in recent years, we have successfully applied laparoscopic surgery to ALPPS in 2019. Despite the advancement in laparoscopic surgical skills that rendered laparoscopic ALPPS feasible, there is scarcity of data in the literature to evaluate its outcome in comparison with open ALPPS with regard to perioperative recovery and liver regeneration. Hence, the aim of this project is to evaluate the short-term clinical outcomes of laparoscopic ALPPS and the impact of laparoscopy on liver remnant regeneration after ALPPS in a prospective randomised clinical trial setting. 肝分割和門靜脈結紮相關聯的分期肝切除術（ALPPS）是一種新的外科手術方法，可在計劃進行大面積肝切除的肝小殘留患者中誘導快速的肝再生。這是一個分為兩個階段的手術，第一階段包括門靜脈結紮和將右肝與左肝分開。在第一階段之後，左肝將迅速進行肝再生，並且當肝臟殘餘物達到適當大小時，第二階段手術可以在第一階段手術後的7-10天進行。在II期手術中，然後取出包含腫瘤的右肝。該手術方法於2013年在德國接受，後來於2015年12月在香港瑪麗醫院首次開始。最初的適應症主要是結直腸肝轉移，但由於香港肝細胞癌的發病率較高，我們已經將該方法轉移到了與肝炎相關的肝細胞癌中，到目前為止，我們已經積累了文獻中最大的單中心經驗之一。儘管如此，ALPPS的常規治療方法包括開放手術，並給患者帶來巨大的手術壓力，尤其是在I期手術後。近年來，隨著微創肝手術的出現，我們已在2019年成功地將腹腔鏡手術應用於ALPPS。儘管腹腔鏡手術技術的進步使腹腔鏡ALPPS可行，但文獻中尚缺乏用於評估的數據，因此，本項目的目的是前瞻性隨機臨床試驗中評估腹腔鏡ALPPS的短期臨床療效以及腹腔鏡對肝殘餘再生的影響。

17122420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122420.value: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) 編碼microRNA調節葡萄糖代謝及促進鼻咽癌細胞耐藥性 未分化鼻咽癌臨床樣本中近乎100%腫瘤細胞為EB病毒感染陽性。EB病毒BamH I-A區右向轉錄產物 (BARTs) 基因家族是EBV潛伏感染時表達最為廣泛的基因家族之一，其表達量可高達鼻咽癌細胞中總微小RNAs (microRNAs) 總量的45%。BARTs基因高豐度表達提示其在鼻咽癌疾病發生中起重要作用。越來越多證據表明BARTs基因參與多種細胞生理活動， 比如促進細胞存活以及腫瘤細胞免疫逃逸。目前BARTs基因參與調節葡萄糖代謝重編程引起研究學者關注。有報導指出，BARTs家族基因BART1-5p可靶向AMPK基因從而上調mTOR以及重編程細胞葡萄糖代謝。然而，BARTs家族其他基因成員是否參與葡萄糖代謝調節以及在鼻咽癌發病過程中的作用尚未清楚研究。 EB病毒感染在鼻咽癌發生發展中的機理尚未清楚闡明，主要原因是缺乏真正具有代表性的鼻咽癌細胞模型。本實驗室早先成功建立鼻咽癌細胞系NPC43 (包含EBV陽性以及陰性細胞亞群)，並成功分離其中EBV陰性NPC43細胞克隆，為研究EB病毒的致病機理提供重要實驗模型基礎。前期免疫缺陷小鼠腫瘤注射實驗表明EBV陰性NPC43細胞克隆不具有成瘤能力，然而穩定感染M81-WT (M81為NPC來源EB病毒株，克隆並惠贈來自Prof. HJ Delecluse, 癌症研究所，漢堡，德國) 病毒株的EBV陰性NPC43細胞克隆具有顯著成瘤能力，值得注意的是穩定感染M81-缺失BART (BART基因缺失突變體) 的EBV陰性NPC43細胞克隆未呈現腫瘤成瘤能力。與此同時，我們發現穩定感染M81-WT病毒株可以提高葡萄糖攝取及乳酸產生 (細胞糖酵解水平增加標誌)，然而M81-缺失BART突變體未能明顯提高细胞糖酵解水平。以上實驗結果充分錶明EB病毒BARTs基因參與調節鼻咽癌腫瘤細胞葡萄糖代謝重編程。此外，我們發現EB病毒感染細胞的葡萄糖代謝改變與腫瘤細胞的順鉑 (一種臨床腫瘤治療中廣泛應用的化療藥物) 耐藥性密切相關。此外，前期實驗結果表明EB感染細胞中上調糖酵解代謝水平可以抑制DNA損傷，提示BARTs基因可能參與DNA損傷修復。上述實驗結果與先前BARTs基因促進EB病毒感染的腫瘤細胞存活報導高度一致。 在此項研究中，我們將深入探究EB病毒BARTs基因是否以通過調節葡萄糖代謝重編程以促進DNA損傷修復來剖析BARTs基因在順鉑耐藥中的作用。我們會評價並闡明BARTs基因簇(C1和C2) 以及單獨的BART基因在順鉑耐藥中的作用。此研究旨在鼻咽癌體外以及臨床前模型中探索靶向葡萄糖代謝從而增加EB病毒感染的鼻咽癌細胞對順鉑及其他DNA損傷劑敏感性的治療意義。

17123420.value: According to the comments from the panel and two external reviewers, PTBP1 is involved in fundamental cellular mRNA processing and this may complicate its use as a therapeutic target. In addition, Akt inhibitors may also have serious side effects during the treatment. It is recommended that the efforts should be focused on the study of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2. Summary (part 1): Therefore, during the first year of this two-year project, we applied the genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout method and proteomic approach to study the virus-host interaction. Besides PTBP1 identified by the CRISPR-Cas9 KO library, we have identified several host dependency factors by the MERS-CoV-host protein-protein interactome. They are USP13, SIRT1, GSK3B, PTGES2, TTK and TPP2. We have examined the importance of these factors for both MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 using the specific small molecule inhibitors. Some of the inhibitors that potently suppressed the SARS-CoV-2 and/or MERS-CoV were further characterized. We further selected two FDA-approved small molecule inhibitors (celecoxib and pyrvinium) for both in-vitro and in-vivo characterization. During the early pandemic, we showed that celecoxib could potently suppress SARS-CoV-2 in-vitro but had no significant effect on the SARS-CoV-2 infected hamster model. Although celecoxib is an FDA-approved NSAID, it also has a side-effect on the cardiovascular system. Therefore, we had not yet published the data to minimize the chance of misuse of celecoxib during the early pandemic. In addition, we examined the anti-viral effect of pyrvinium (both orally and intraperitoneally) in MERS-CoV-infected DPP4-knockin mice and SARS-CoV-2-infected ACE2 transgenic mice. Intraperitoneal injection of pyrvinium slightly protects the MERS-CoV- infected mice, while the oral administration of pyrvinium was unable to suppress the intestinal infection of SARS-CoV-2. Based on our interactome data, we focused on two host factors, USP13 and VPS34. We examined the antiviral effects of spautin-1 (USP13 inhibitor) and VPS34-IN1 (VPS34 inhibitor) against SARS-CoV-2 infection. Both specific inhibitors have potent suppressive effect in SARS-CoV-2 infected lung cell-line and ex-vivo lung tissues. For the VPS34 study, we immediately published the data in the Journal of Medical Virology during early pandemic (Yuen CK, Wong WM, Mak LF, Wang X, Chu H, Yuen KY, Kok KH. Suppression of SARS-CoV-2 infection in ex-vivo human lung tissues by targeting class III phosphoinositide 3-kinase. J Med Virol. 2021 93:2076-2083). At that time, it is unclear whether any components of autophagy or virophagy can be therapeutic targets for COVID-19 treatment. In that report, we examined the antiviral effect of four well-characterized small molecule inhibitors that target the key cellular factors involved in key steps of the autophagy pathway. They include small molecules targeting the ULK1/Atg1 complex involved in the induction stage of autophagy (ULK1 inhibitor SBI0206965), the ATG14/Beclin1/VPS34 complex involved in the nucleation step of autophagy (class III PI3-kinase inhibitor VPS34-IN1), and a widely-used autophagy inhibitor that persistently inhibits class I and temporary inhibits class III PI3-kinase (3-MA) and a clinically approved autophagy inhibitor that suppresses autophagy by inhibiting lysosomal acidification and prevents the formation of autophagolysosome. Surprisingly, not all the tested autophagy inhibitors suppressed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We showed that inhibition of class III PI3-kinase involved in the initiation step of both canonical and noncanonical autophagy potently suppressed SARS-CoV-2 at a nano-molar level. In addition, this specific kinase inhibitor VPS34-IN1, and its bioavailable analogue VVPS34-IN1, potently inhibited SARS-CoV-2 infection in ex vivo human lung tissues. Taken together, class III PI3-kinase may be a possible host target for COVID-19 therapeutic development. Summary (part 2): Although the project was proposed to be finished within two years, with this GRF funding support, we continued to focus on the study of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2, as the reviewers suggested. Other than host targeting drug study, we focused on the novel vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 infection. We have developed two novel vaccines: 1) a live-attenuated universal Sarbecovirus vaccine and 2) an RNA-scaffold protein subunit vaccine. Regarding to the 1) live-attenuated mucosal universal Sarbecovirus vaccine, the manuscript has been accepted by Nature Communications, IF: 16.6. (Yuen CT, Wong WM, Mak LF, Lam JY, Cheung LY, Cheung DT, Ng YY, Lee AC, Yuen KY, Kok KH An interferon-integrated mucosal vaccine provides pan-sarbecovirus protection in small animal models. Nature Communications; accepted: 9 October 2023) A pan-sarbecovirus or pan-betacoronavirus vaccine that can prevent current and potential future beta-coronavirus infections is important for fighting possible future pandemics. We reported a mucosal vaccine that cross- protects small animal models from sarbecoviruses including SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2 and its variants. This vaccine comprises a live-but-defective SARS- CoV-2 virus that is envelope deficient and has the orf8 segment replaced by interferon-beta, hence named Interferon Beta Integrated SARS-CoV-2 (IBIS) vaccine. Nasal vaccination with IBIS protected mice from lethal homotypic SARS-CoV-2 infection and hamsters from co-housing-mediated transmission of homotypic virus. Moreover, IBIS provided complete protection against heterotypic sarbecoviruses, including SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants, and SARS-CoV-1 in both mice and hamsters. Besides inducing a strong lung CD8 + T cell response, IBIS specifically heightened the activation of mucosal virus-specific CD4 + T cells compared to the interferon-null vaccine. The direct production of interferon by IBIS also suppressed virus co-infection of SARS- CoV-2 in human cells, reducing the risk of genetic recombination when using as live vaccines. Altogether, IBIS is a next-generation pan-sarbecovirus vaccine and warrants further clinical investigations. Regarding to the 2) an RNA-scaffold protein subunit vaccine, this novel mucosal vaccine design has been published in Vaccines, IF: 7.8 (Lam JY, Wong WM, Yuen CK, Ng YY, San CH, Yuen KY, Kok KH An RNA-Scaffold Protein Subunit Vaccine for Nasal Immunization. Vaccines 2023 11,1550 doi.org/10.3390/vaccines11101550). Developing recombinant proteins as nasal vaccines for inducing systemic and mucosal immunity against respiratory viruses is promising. However, additional adjuvants are required to overcome the low immunogenicity of protein antigens. Here, a self-adjuvanted protein-RNA ribonucleoprotein vaccine was developed and found to be an effective nasal vaccine in mice and the SARS-CoV-2 infection model. The vaccine consisted of spike RBD (as an antigen), nucleoprotein (as an adaptor), and ssRNA (as an adjuvant and RNA scaffold). This combination robustly induced mucosal IgA, neutralizing antibodies and activated multifunctional T-cells, while also providing sterilizing immunity against live virus challenge. In addition, high-resolution scRNA-seq analysis highlighted airway-resident immune cells profile during prime-boost immunization. The vaccine also possesses modularity (antigen/adaptor/RNA scaffold) and can be made to target other viruses. This protein-RNA ribonucleoprotein vaccine is a novel and promising approach for developing safe and potent nasal vaccines to combat respiratory virus infections.

17123420.value: Small molecule drugs, including host-targeting and virus-targeting, may be useful for therapeutic treatment against SARS-CoV-2 infections. 17123920.label: Project Objectives
17123920.value: Objective 1: To understand the fundamental biology of TMPRSS13 in the context of ZIKV infection. Extending from our pilot studies on the identification of TMPRSS13 as a novel host dependency factor for efficient ZIKV replication, we aim to thoroughly dissect the role of TMPRSS13 on ZIKV infection in this proposal. In Objective 1, we first seek to understand the basic biology of TMPRSS13 in the context of ZIKV infection. Objective 1 (A) First, we will characterize the baseline expression of TMPRSS13 in un-infected cells. Objective 1 (B) Second, we will investigate the cellular localization of TMPRSS13. Objective 1 (C) Third, we will evaluate the expression pattern of TMPRSS13 upon ZIKV infection. Objective 2: To thoroughly investigate the impact of TMPRSS13 on ZIKV infection. Based on the knowledge obtained from Objective 1, we will have a more systemic grasp on the basic biology of TMPRSS13 that is relevant to ZIKV infection. In Objective 2, we will thoroughly investigate the modulatory effect of TMPRSS13 on ZIKV infection on multiple dimensions. Objective 2 (A) First, we will extent our line of investigation on loss of function studies. Objective 2 (B) Second, we will study the outcome of TMPRSS13 overexpression in more details. Objective 2 (C) Third, we will investigate if TMPRSS13 can also modulate the replication of other flaviviruses. Objective 3: To dissect the mechanism of how TMPRSS13 modulate ZIKV replication. Extending from our findings from Objective 1 and 2, we next plan to investigate the mechanism of how TMPRSS13 facilitates ZIKV replication in Objective 3. Objective 3 (A) First, we will examine the role of TMPRSS13 during ZIKV entry. Objective 3 (B) Second, we will investigate if TMPRSS13 mediates cleavage of ZIKV proteins. Objective 3 (C) Third, we will directly assess the association of the cleavage activity of TMPRSS13 with TMPRSS13-facilitated ZIKV replication. Objective 3 (D) Forth, the relative effect of furin and TMPRSS13 on prM cleavage will be assessed. Objective 3 (E) Fifth, the potential effect of additional TMPRSS on prM proteins of flaviviruses will be examined.

17123920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123920.value: 寨卡病毒是一種新興的蚊媒黃病毒，在近期導致了前所未有的大規模流行，並引起嚴重的神經系統併發症，包括小頭畸形和格林-巴利綜合徵等。迄今為止，寨卡病毒已在超過80多個美洲，非洲，和東南亞國家/地區中導致了感染或暴發。因此，寨卡病毒流行成為了國際關注的突發公共衛生事件。 寨卡病毒的發病機理仍不完全清楚。鑑定在寨卡病毒的複制和發病中起重要作用的宿主因子仍然是關鍵的研究重點。通過比較寨卡病毒感染的巨噬細胞和樹突狀細胞的轉錄組，我們的研究指出跨膜絲氨酸蛋白酶13(TMPRSS13)是一個有利寨卡病毒複製的潛在宿主依賴性因子。 在本提案中，我們旨在進一步闡明TMPRSS13的作用，並研究TMPRSS13介導的寨卡病毒複製的潛在機制。有趣的是，TMPRSS13可識別與furin蛋白酶向似的剪切基序，這是黃病毒通過切割prM蛋白成熟所需的步驟。在這方面，TMPRSS13的作用可能可以被廣泛運用到跨多種黃病毒的多種細胞類型。因此，通過研究TMPRSS13在寨卡病毒成熟和復制中的作用，我們的研究將大大擴展我們目前對黃病毒所利用的宿主蛋白酶範圍的了解，這有機會成為對抗黃病毒感染的新型干預目標。

17124220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124220.value: Background: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) causes severe respiratory disease and extrapulmonary complications with an exceptionally high mortality rate (~35%). The molecular mechanisms underlying the severe and unique clinical manifestations of MERS remain incompletely understood. Phosphoproteomics identifies and characterizes proteins containing a phosphate group as a post-translational modification, and allows rapid analysis of entire phosphorylation-based signaling networks. It has been increasingly used to study virus-host interactions and identify potential host-targeting treatments. In our preliminary works, we successfully utilized quantitative phosphoproteomics to newly identify casein kinase 1 alpha (CSNK1A, a ubiquitously expressed protein kinase with important regulatory functions in many cellular processes) as the most activated kinase upon MERS-CoV infection of lung epithelial cells. Hypothesis: We postulate that CSNK1A plays an important role in MERS pathogenesis and is a potential anti-CoV therapeutic target. Preliminary findings: Label-free quantitative phosphoproteomics on MERS-CoV-infected Calu-3 cells identified 409 phosphopeptides (322 proteins) that showed a change in phosphorylation status. This markedly perturbed host protein phosphorylation profile included many proteins that were involved in various cellular processes. A comprehensive siRNA library knockdown screen of all 262 upregulated phosphoproteins followed by in-silico prediction with Group-based Prediction System 3.0 identified the 5 top-ranked kinases for further investigations. Both siRNA knockdown of CSNK1A and kinase inhibitor treatment resulted in the most significant MERS-CoV load reduction among these top-ranked kinases. Treatment of hDPP4-knockin mice with CSNK1A inhibitor (D4476) resulted in significantly ↑survival, ↓viral load, and ↓viral antigen expression. Research plan: Based on these exciting findings, we now propose to comprehensively investigate the mechanism of how CSNK1A modulates MERS-CoV replication and assess the treatment effects of CSNK1A inhibitor in additional physiologically relevant models. Objective 1 focuses on understanding the biology of CSNK1A upon MERS-CoV infection. First, we will study how CSNK1A’s expression is modulated by MERS-CoV infection. Next, we will characterize the function of CSNK1A in CoV infections by investigating its effects on different CoVs and in different cells types. Then, we will dissect the mechanism of how CSNK1A affects MERS-CoV replication by determining the steps of the virus replication cycle that CSNK1A is involved in. Objective 2 aims to thoroughly investigate CSNK1A inhibitor’s anti-CoV effects. We will evaluate the in-vitro anti-CoV effects of CSNK1A inhibitor against MERS-CoV and other human-pathogenic CoVs, followed by thorough evaluation of the inhibitor’s anti-MERS-CoV effects in ex-vivo human tissue cultures, and intestinal organoids.
