17124220.label: Realisation of objectives
17124220.value: Objective 1: To investigate the role of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV infection Objective 1.1: To understand the biology of CSNK1A upon MERS-CoV infection. - To understand how the expression/activation of CSNK1A is modulated by MERS-CoV, we investigated the cellular distribution of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV-infected cells, and the effect of CSNK1A overexpression on MERS-CoV replication. - We investigated if the expression/activation of CSNK1A is modulated by MERS-CoV infection. We detected CSNK1A expression in MERS-CoV- and mock-infected cells with Western blot. - We examined the cellular distribution of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV-infected cells. CSNK1A has been reported to be localized at various cellular compartments. This broad tissue distribution corroborates with the notion that CSNK1A is involved in multiple physiological processes. - To evaluate if the cellular distribution of CSNK1A is altered upon MERS-CoV infection, we infected different cells with MERS-CoV and fixed the infected cells at different time-points post-infection. The differential cellular distribution patterns of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV- vs mock-infected cells were determined together with cellular organelle markers. - As many cells contain high basal levels of CSNK1A, our attempt to overexpress CSNK1A did not yield dramatic changes in the cellular levels of CSNK1A and MERS-CoV replication. Objective 1.2: To characterize the function of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV infection. - We evaluated whether CSNK1A’s effect on MERS-CoV replication is virus-specific. We depleted CSNK1A in Calu-3 cells with siRNA and infected the cells with SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2. We found that the depletion of CSNK1A led to reduced viral load of all 3 viruses. - We evaluated whether CSNK1A’s effect on MERS-CoV infection is cell type-dependent. To this end, we knock-downed CSNK1A in a broad range of cell lines originating from different tissues, including Calu-3, HEK, Huh-7, and Caco-2 cells. We found that CSNK1A’s effect on MERS-CoV infection was consistently in these cell lines. - To assess CSNK1A’s effect on MERS-CoV infection in a more physiologically-relevant system, we evaluated the effect of CSNK1A inhibition on MERS-CoV replication in ex vivo human lung explant culture model. We found that CSNK1A inhibition resulted in significant reduction in MERS-CoV viral load in human lung tissues. Objective 1.3: To dissect the mechanism of how CSNK1A affects MERS-CoV replication. - We investigated the step(s) of the MERS-CoV replication cycle CSNK1A is involved in and the activating role of CSNK1A on substrate proteins that are involved in MERS-CoV replication. - We utilized multiple assays to evaluate the exact step(s) of the MERS-CoV replication cycle that CSNK1A is involved in. - We evaluated whether CSNK1A is involved in MERS-CoV entry. Our time-of-drug-addition assay by treating the cells with siRNA at different time intervals post-infection showed that CSNK1A modulated MERS-CoV viral load at a post-entry event. - To further determine whether CSNK1A affects the trafficking and/or assembly of MERS-CoV, in the next study period, we used co-immunostaining of different cellular markers together with viral markers to visualize whether CSNK1A depletion alters the cellular distribution or trafficking of the viral genome or gene products; as well as to assess if CSNK1A knockdown would affect virus release. We showed that CSNK1A depletion affected multiple steps of the viral replication cycle. Objective 2: To evaluate the effects of CSNK1A inhibitor as a novel treatment strategy for MERS-CoV infection Objective 2.1: To investigate the in-vitro antiviral activity of CSNK1A inhibitor against MERS-CoV and other human-pathogenic CoVs to determine if CSNK1A inhibitor may be a potentially “pan-CoV” antiviral. - To establish a suitable in vitro platform for assessing the anti-MERS-CoV activity of CSNK1A and other kinase inhibitors, we set up various antiviral evaluation assays, including cell viability assay, viral load reduction assay, and viral antigen expression assay (research output #1: Chu et al., Sci Adv 2021). - Our data showed that CSNK1A inhibitors significantly reduced the MERS-CoV and other coronaviruses’ viral load in vitro. Objective 2.2: To assess the anti-MERS-CoV activity of CSNK1A inhibitor in physiologically relevant ex-vivo culture systems, including ex-vivo human lung and kidney tissue cultures, and human intestinal organoids. - To establish a suitable ex vivo platform for assessing the anti-MERS-CoV activity of CSNK1A and other kinase inhibitors, we set up an ex vivo human lung explant culture model to assess MERS-CoV-induced signaling changes (research output #1: Chu et al., Sci Adv 2021). Objective 2.3: To evaluate the in-vivo activity and identify the optimal dosing regimen of CSNK1A inhibitor against MERS-CoV in a lethal hDPP4-knockin mouse model. - To establish an animal model for evaluation of the effects of CSNK1A and other kinase inhibitors, we set up an in vivo model using human DPP4-transgenic mice for thorough evaluation of the effects of treatment on MERS-CoV infection (research output #1: Chu et al., Sci Adv 2021). - Using this animal model, we showed that treatment of the mice with the CSNK1A inhibitors D4476 significantly improved the outcome of MERS-CoV-infected mice. The D4476-treated mice had lower viral burden in tissues and a higher survival rate than the control mock-treated mice. Please refer to Research Output #3 (under preparation) for details.

17124220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124220.value: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) causes severe respiratory disease and extrapulmonary complications with an exceptionally high mortality rate (~35%). The molecular mechanisms underlying the severe and unique clinical manifestations of MERS remain incompletely understood. In this study, quantitative phosphoproteomics was used to identify casein kinase 1 alpha (CSNK1A), a ubiquitously expressed protein kinase with important regulatory functions in many cellular processes, as the most activated kinase upon MERS-CoV infection of human lung epithelial cells (Calu-3 adenocarcinoma cells). Analysis of the integrated MERS-CoV responsive kinase-phospho-peptide network identified 14 kinases and 102 phospho-peptides, and a total of 467 interactions defined by phopshoprylation modification were mapped in the network. Bioinformatic analysis showed that the identified MERS-CoV-perturbed proteins are involved in various cellular processes. The CSNK1A inhibitor D4476 exhibited significant antiviral activity against MERS-CoV in vitro and in ex vivo human lung explant culture model. Moreover, D4476 demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity against other human-pathogenic coronaviruses, as well as human-pathogenic RNA viruses. Importantly, D4476 significantly improved survival of MERS-CoV-infected human dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (hDPP4) knock-in mice (45.5% in D4476-treated vs mock-treated mice, P<0.05). Mechanistically, CSNK1A modulates MERS-CoV infection trhgouh phosphorylation modification. Taken together, these results demonstrated the important biological role and of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV replication. CSNK1A-targeting drugs should be further evaluated as potential anti-MERS-CoV therapeutics. Please refer to Research Output Publication #3 (research article under preparation) for details.

17124220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124220.value: In addition to the identification of CSNK1A as an important host dependency factor in MERS-CoV infection with potential antiviral importance, the current project has also facilitated the establishment of ex vivo human lung explant culture model and in vivo mouse model for evaluation of MERS-CoV-induced signalling perturbations (Research Output Publication #1) for further mechanistic and antiviral evaluation studies. We also identified a number of host-targeting drug compounds, including the CSNK1 inhibitor D4476, with antiviral activity against MERS-CoV. We plan to utilize these important MERS-CoV infection models to evaluate additional potential anti-MERS-CoV drugs and conduct further pathogenesis studies using various omics platforms such as additional phosphoproteomics analysis in different cell types / organ tissues in the future.

17124220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124220.value: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) causes severe disease with an exceptionally high mortality rate (~35%) in human. How MERS-CoV causes these unique changes in human is incompletely understood. In this study, quantitative phosphoproteomics was used to identify a host enzyme called casein kinase 1 alpha (CSNK1A) which has important regulatory functions in various cellular processes to be highly activated in MERS-CoV-infected human lung cells. Experimental results indicated that MERS-CoV markedly changes the host protein phosphorylation profile and that these changes involve various cellular processes. D4476 is an inhibitor of CSNK1A which demonstrated the ability to inhibit MERS-CoV replication in cell culture and human lung explant organ culture models. Importantly, D4476 treatment increased the survival rate of MERS-CoV-infected mice. The inhibition of CSNK1A likely inhibits MERS-CoV replication via phosphorylation modification. Taken together, the results in this study demonstrated the important biological role and of CSNK1A in MERS-CoV replication. The potential role of drugs targeting CSNK1A in treating MERS-CoV infection should be further investigated.

17124420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124420.value: Regulatory T-cells (Treg) maintain the immune homeostasis by facilitating self-tolerance, in turn preventing autoimmune as well as chronic inflammatory diseases. The majority of Treg in the body are originated from thymus. Under obese conditions, the subpopulations of Treg are significantly altered in peripheral organs, such as adipose tissue and liver. Treg-based therapy is considered as a promising approach to treat metabolic disorders, including obesity, insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. However, the optimal application of Treg relies on our further understanding of the origin, specificity and function of their different subsets. Adiponectin is a well-known insulin sensitizer and anti-inflammatory molecule, with therapeutic potentials in obesity-related cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. It was originally discovered in adipocyte and considered as an abundant adipokine. The circulating levels of adiponectin are paradoxically decreased in obese animals and human subjects. Replenishment of adiponectin potently restores metabolic function and energy homeostasis in mice challenged with either dietary or genetic obesity. Our results demonstrated that adiponectin is expressed in the thymus, by a population of Treg precursors. After tail vein injection, these cells rapidly resided within the thymic nurse cell complexes (TNCs) and differentiated into thymic Treg (tTreg) cells. Adoptive transfer of adiponectin-expressing thymocytes prevented the development of obesity, insulin resistance and non-alcoholic fatty liver injuries in wild type (WT) mice fed with high fat diet. By contrast, the same treatment did not protect adiponectin-deficient (AKO) mice against high fat diet-induced metabolic abnormalities. The microenvironment of TNCs is involved in the establishment of central tolerance. Here, we hypothesize that adiponectin plays a cell-autonomous role in tTreg maturation and formation in the niche of TNCs. In particular, adiponectin facilitates the interactions between T- and B-cells, thus the Treg development in TNCs and their subsequent distribution in peripheral organs to control the immunological self-tolerance and homeostasis. This proposal is thus designed to investigate how adiponectin promotes energy homeostasis by regulating central (thymus) and peripheral (adipose tissue and liver) Treg populations, in turn eliciting the anti-obesity, insulin-sensitizing and anti-inflammatory activities. The results are expected to pave the way for utilizing adiponectin-expressing tTreg for the development of novel immunotherapies. 調節性T細胞（Treg）通過促進自我耐受來維持免疫穩態，進而預防自身免疫以及慢性炎症性疾病。體內大部分Treg來自胸腺。在肥胖條件下，Treg的亞群在周圍器官（例如脂肪組織和肝臟）中顯著改變。基於Treg的療法被認為是治療包括肥胖，胰島素抵抗和2型糖尿病在內的代謝疾病的有前途的方法。但是，Treg的最佳應用取決於我們對它們不同子集的起源，特異性和功能的進一步了解。 脂聯素是胰島素增敏劑和抗炎分子，具有肥胖相關的心血管和代謝疾病的治療潛力。它最初在脂肪細胞中發現，被認為是豐富的脂肪因子。在肥胖動物和人類受試者中脂聯素的循環水平反常降低。補充脂聯素可有效恢復飲食或遺傳性肥胖症小鼠的代謝功能和能量穩態。我們的結果表明，脂聯素在人群的胸腺中表達。尾靜脈注射表達脂聯素前體後，這些細胞迅速駐留在胸腺護士細胞複合體（TNC）中，並分化為胸腺調節性T細胞（tTreg）。過表達脂聯素的胸腺細胞的過繼轉移阻止了高脂飲食餵養的野生型（WT）小鼠的肥胖，胰島素抵抗和非酒精性脂肪肝損傷的發展。相比之下，相同的治療不能保護脂聯素缺乏症（AKO）小鼠免受高脂飲食誘導的代謝異常的影響。 在這裡，我們假設脂聯素在tTreg成熟和TNC的形成中發揮細胞自主作用。脂聯素促進T細胞和B細胞之間的相互作用，從而促進TNC中的Treg發育以及它們隨後在周圍器官中的分佈，以促進免疫自耐受和體內平衡。因此，該項目旨在研究脂聯素如何通過調節中樞（胸腺）和外周（脂肪組織和肝臟）Treg種群來促進能量穩態，進而引發抗肥胖，胰島素敏感性和抗炎活性。預期結果有望為表達脂聯素的tTreg的發展鋪平道路，以開發新的免疫療法。

17124420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124420.value: Adiponectin plays an important role in T-cell development by modulating the cellular interactions within the thymic nurse complexes (TNC). In particular, it modulates the surface glycoprotein interactions between T-cells, epithelial cells and B cells in the micro-environment of TNC, which leads to differential activation/inactivation of subsets of T and B cells. Further investigations of the detailed cellular composition and their functions are warranted. The results will uncover pomising cellular targets for therapeutic development.

17124420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124420.value: We have performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of TNC samples under different pathophysiological conditions. The results demonstrated that under different pathophysiological conditions, the B cell receptor (BCR) profiles are significantly different. As B cells have been implicated in chronic inflammation associated with obesity and related cardiometabolic diseases, to characterize the precise subsets of these B cells and their distribution as well as function will reveal the underlying pathogenesis of these medical complications. Another grant application will be prepared to obtain further fundings to support the subsequent study.

17124420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124420.value: Adiponectin is a protein in our body that helps the development of T lymphocytes. Adiponectin does this by regulating the interactions between different types of cells in the thymus. These interactions leads to activating or deactivating certain subsets of T and B cells, dysfunction of which plays critical roles in causing obesity and related medical complications. More research is needed to understand the specific roles of the different subsets of T and B cells during the disease progression.

17125720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125720.value: Medical care services are mainly provided for patients only. End-of-life care is an exception extending care to the patient’s entire family and beyond the patient’s death. Bereavement care, as an integral part of end-of-life care, supports family members before and after the patient’s death. Audits of end-of-life care often highlight bereavement care as requiring further improvement. Fundamentally, bereavement care, in particular pre-death bereavement care, is a vague term, although in the past decade a few studies have attempted to provide elucidation. However, their findings only refer to the types and means of bereavement care but not its content and no studies have been undertaken in Asia. Current evidence provides little help for clinical utility or globally applicability. Moreover, the UK’s Medical Research Council drew attention to the need to understand not only the content of care but also its implementation, underpinning change mechanism and contextual factors. The proposed study aims to fill these gaps in order to address this inevitable life event in a preventive way. The study will adopt a mixed-methods design that consists of two stages, a survey with health and social care providers of end-of-life care in Hong Kong and a key stakeholder workshop. The survey will invite all health and social care professionals in hospital, community, residential care and private end-of-life care settings in Hong Kong to participate. A list of components of pre-death bereavement care (“what”) will be generated. The multi-disciplinary research team will invite experienced bereavement care professionals in Hong Kong, academics, representatives of professional organizations related to bereavement care and former service users to participate in a key stakeholder co-creating workshop. In the workshop, the “what” components of pre-bereavement care will be refined, with further discussion on the change mechanisms (“how”) and risk factors (“to whom”). This study is expected to inform researchers about the black-box of pre-death bereavement care. It will further contribute to clinical utility and benefit not only health and social care professionals and service organizations but also enhance the well-being of bereaved-to-be families. 醫療護理服務主要是提供給病人。晚期照顧卻是一個例外，它將關懷延伸到病人的整個家庭，甚至在病人死亡之後，繼續照顧喪親家屬。善別照顧是晚期照顧的一個部分，在病人死亡之前和之後為家庭成員提供支援。晚期照顧的審計往往強調善別服務有改進空間。善別照顧是一個模糊的概念，特別是死亡前的善別照顧，更是鮮為討論。儘管在過去的十年中，有一些研究試圖闡明善別照顧的內容。但是，他們的研究結果只涉及善別照顧的類型和方式，而沒有涉及其內容，而且在亞洲也沒有進行過研究。目前的證據對臨床實用性和全球適用性提供的幫助不大。此外，英國醫學研究委員會呼籲，研究不僅要瞭解照顧的內容，還要瞭解其實施情況、基礎變化機制和背景因素。本研究旨在填補這些空白，以預防的方式解決這一不可避免的生命事件。 研究會採用混合方法，分兩個階段進行。首先會向香港提供晚期照顧的醫療和社會護理機構人員進行調查，調查將邀請香港所有在醫院、社區、院舍和私人晚期照顧中的醫療和社會護理專業人員參與。調查結果將列出死前喪親照顧的組成部分。繼而，會舉辦主要持份者工作坊。跨學科研究小組會邀請香港資深的善別照顧專業人員、學者、與善別照顧有關的專業團體代表及前服務使用者，參與一個主要持份者共同創造的工作坊。在工作坊中，研究人員會細化死亡前善別照顧的內容（"什麼"），並進一步討論改變機制（"如何"）和風險因素（"對誰"）。本研究有望為研究者提供關於死亡前善別照顧的黑匣子。它將進一步促進臨床實用性，不僅使醫療和社會護理專業人員和服務機構受益，還將提升喪親准家庭的福祉。

17125720.label: Realisation of objectives
17125720.value: The study consisted of two stages of data collection. Stage 1 is a survey with health and social care providers mainly for objective 1 and 4, whereas stage 2 is a key stakeholder cocreation workshop which is for objective 2 and 3. Due to the covid-19 pandemic, the co-creation workshop had to be held via zoom. Additionally, the health and social care professionals were all torn during that period due to the lack of manpower. The workshop was postponed as well. Eventually, we secured 30 participants joining the workshop, discussions were carried out in 4 small groups and then big group. Generally speaking, the objectives are all achieved. 1. To understand the implementation and core components of pre-death bereavement care offered by end-of-life care services in Hong Kong; In the survey with 111 health and social care professionals, 15 core components were identified. These components were also compared between the three time points: at the point of referral, major care period and last moment. The pre-death bereavement need with the highest occurrence was the respect of preference of patients and family members during the trajectory of care. Being listened to, communication and information were the key care needs. The proportion with emotional needs increased over the trajectory of care. From referral time to the major caring period, physical needs, practical needs, opportunities to care and capture memorable moments increased. The group with required listening ears and reconciliation increased significantly at the death moment 2. To identify different pathways of the mechanism of change induced by pre-death bereavement care As the identified components of the pre-death bereavement care included 15 factors, possible number of pathways were expected to be large. Yet in the stakeholders co-create workshop, two major mechanisms were spelt out. The first one is via quality holistic care towards the patients. They considered the care to patients as more important than that to the bereaved person-to-be. The dyadic relationship between the wellbeing of the patient and the carers was evidence and was postulated to apply in the pre-death bereavement context. The second major pathway was the trustful relationship between the health care professionals with the bereaved person-to-be. The bereaved person-to-be, acknowledged that the death was inevitable and understood the limitations of the staff. They did not have unrealistic expectations on the staff in solving their problems. Instead, the sincere attitude and willingness to listen were considered to be important factors. 3. To distinguish moderators which affect the relationship of pre-death bereavement care and bereavement outcome; and The group further proposed moderators of “providing the chance for carer to be by the deathbed”, “offering adequate time to stay with the patients”, and “remind the carers about the signs of approaching death”. As it was a qualitative study, these moderators have to be further tested via quantitative study in future. 4. To suggest locally relevant pre-death risk factors of complicated post-death grief. The survey identified 21 risk factors which further confirmed by the stakeholders. The findings were actually used in a local validation study in 2024.

17125720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125720.value: Contrary to the intuitive thinking, the top three of the pre-death bereavement care needs were not about the bereaved person-to-be, but related to the patients. Specifically, the quality of holistic care to patient, the information of the patient, and the involvement in the decision-making process for the patient were the leading aspects. Particularly, the information need, rather than the emotional or physical needs, is considered to be most important in the early stage. Additionally, the needs were not stable over time. Differences with statistical differences were found between point of referral, major care period and around death moment. Interdisciplinary differences were identified between nurses, doctors and social workers in the perceived needs.

17125720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125720.value: The current study was carried out when bereavement care was not a popular topic. After the Covid-19 pandemic, both health and social care professionals and the general public are more open to examine and discuss bereavement care. Further research with public is carried out by the team on both bereavement care and risk factors for bereavement outcomes.

17125720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125720.value: In facing the taboo topic of death and bereavement, this study unfolds the mystery of pre-death bereavement care, identified crucial risk and protective factors of bereavement outcomes that fits the local Chinese context. The finding will inform the clinicians the way to support people facing the death of their loved one at the pre-death stage.

17125820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125820.value: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) are severe mental disorders causing enormous burdens to patients and society. Despite advance in neuroscience, neurobiological mechanisms underpinning the disorders remain elusive. Significant clinical and genetic overlap between two disorders also challenge the long-held assumption that they constitute two discrete diagnostic entities, and indicates a paradigm shift towards psychosis spectrum. It is suggested that direct comparison between SZ and BD using neurobiological assessments helps delineate shared and distinct biomarkers across two disorders, and facilitate development of neuroscience-based diagnostic classification and individualized treatments. Neuroimaging and cognitive assessments represent key strategies in elucidating differential neurobiological signatures across psychosis spectrum, and are increasingly applied in SZ-BD comparison research. Literature reveals that both disorders are associated with widespread cognitive impairment and share common patterns of brain structural/functional abnormalities, but to a greater extent in SZ than BD. However, previous studies are hampered by several important methodological limitations. First, the majority of prior SZ-BD comparison studies examined chronically-ill patients with longstanding medication treatment which may confound study results. There is a paucity of research directly contrasting neuroimaging and cognitive measures in first-episode SZ (FES) and first-episode BD (FEB). Second, most studies were of small sample size, compromising the power to detect subtle between-group differences. Third, although multimodal neuroimaging is a powerful approach to capture altered patterns of brain structures and functions, most published reports focused on a single neuroimaging modality. Until now, multimodal neuroimaging has not been employed to concurrently compare between FES and FEB. Fourth, longitudinal investigation is scarce, but is critical to clarifying differential courses of cognitive functions and brain structural/functional abnormalities across disorders, as well as dynamic relationship between cognitive trajectories, neuroimaging changes and clinical progression. We will conduct a prospective 1-year follow-up study in FES and FEB patients using multimodal neuroimaging approach which measures brain volumes, structural and functional connectivity, and resting-state cerebral-blood-flow, as well as standardized cognitive assessment. Neuroimaging and cognitive assessment will be performed at baseline and 1 year to track longitudinal changes. This study will facilitate identification of trans-diagnostic and disorder-specific neurobiological markers between two disorders in the early illness stage. Our data will clarify potential differential neurobiological trajectories between disorders and their relationships with clinical and functional outcomes. Additionally, exploratory analysis of integrating neuroimaging and cognitive data with clinical variables are performed to further enhance outcome prediction, which will then facilitate development of targeted intervention for early psychosis in the future. 精神分裂症和躁鬱症皆是對患者及社會帶來沉重負擔的嚴重精神病。儘管近年神經科學發展迅速，但學界至今對造成這兩種精神病的神經生物學機制仍未有透切的了解。兩種疾病在臨床症狀和遺傳因子上的重疊，亦挑戰了人們長期以來認為它們構成兩個獨立診斷種類的假設，並向兩種疾病同處思覺失調病譜的理論方面邁進。學界相信使用神經生物學評估對精神分裂症和躁鬱症進行直接比較分析，可能有助於識辨兩種疾病之間共享的和獨特的生物標記，並促進以神經科學為本的診斷分類和個人化治療的發展。 磁力共震掃描和認知評估是闡明思覺失調病譜中不同疾病的神經生物學特徵的關鍵策略，更是越來越多地應用於精神分裂症和躁鬱症的比較研究中。文獻顯示，兩種精神病患者均表現出廣泛的認知障礙，並在大腦結構及功能上存在共同的異常模式，只是這些異常在精神分裂症病人中程度比較嚴重。然而，以往的研究方式存在一些重要的限制。首先， 先前的精神分裂症和躁鬱症比較研究，大多數都是針對累年接受藥物治療的長期精神病患者而進行的，這可能會混淆研究結果。而在首發性精神分裂症和躁鬱症的研究中，則缺乏直接對比磁力共震掃描和認知指標的研究。其次，大多數研究的樣本量較小，因而削弱了檢測兩種疾病間細微差異的能力。第三，儘管多模式磁力共震掃描是了解大腦結構和功能改變的有效方法，但大多數已發表的研究報告都只採用了單模式磁力共震掃描。到目前為止，還沒有研究採用多模式磁力共震掃描對精神分裂症和躁鬱症進行比較。第四，雖然目前在精神分裂症和躁鬱症方面的縱向調查很少，然而要釐清不同精神疾病在認知功能障礙和異常大腦結構或功能方面的異同，並了解認知功能軌跡、磁力共震掃描影像變化和臨床病症演變之間的動態關係，縱向調查是至關重要的。 在這個項目中，我們將進行為期一年的跟進性磁力共振掃描研究，對首發性精神分裂症和躁鬱症病人進行關於腦容量、腦部結構及功能連通性、靜息狀態的腦血流量，以及標準認知功能的評估。為了更準確地捕捉腦結構變化及認知功能的演變，病人會在首次參與時及第12個月進行此評估。這項研究將有助於在早期階段識別兩種疾病之間的相通和獨特的神經生物學標記。我們的數據將闡明疾病之間潛在的神經生物學軌跡差異，及其與臨床和功能結果的關係。此外，我們亦會結合磁力共振掃描影像、認知數據及臨床變數進行探索性分析，以進一步增強對疾病結果的預測，這將有助於思覺失調的針對性早期介入治療的發展。

17125820.label: Realisation of objectives
17125820.value: 1. Objective 1 This was successfully achieved. We have recruited 82 patients with first-episode schizophrenia (FES), 78 patients with first-episode bipolar disorder (FEB), and 80 demographically-matched healthy controls (HCs), resulting in a final sample of 240 subjects. All of the participants completed clinical, functional and cognitive assessments as well as MRI scans. Baseline cognitive impairment in FES and FEB was compared using standardized z-scores derived from HC performance for each cognitive test. At baseline, general cognition and performance on individual tests differed significantly across the three groups, with both FES and FEB scoring lower than HC on all measures. FES patients demonstrated higher level of cognitive impairment than those with FEB across tasks, consistent with the findings from a previous meta-analysis (Li et al. 2020). FES patients were significantly more impaired compared to FEB patients in digit symbol and Trail Making test–part B (TMT-B). Impairments were not significant between two groups in Letter Number Span, TMT–part A, and Verbal Fluency. These findings aligned with previous studies reporting more quantitative (i.e., difference in severity of impairments) than qualitative (i.e., similarity in cognitive domains that are impaired) cognitive differences between FES and FEB (Bora et al. 2015, 2017). Furthermore, recent evidence has suggested more pronounced deficits in digit symbol performance in FES relative to FEB, with more subtle differences observed on other cognitive measures (Zanelli et al. 2022) 2. Objective 2 This was successfully achieved. Brain abnormalities were observed in FES and FEB patients as compared to HCs. Both patient groups exhibited increased subcortical lateral ventricle volume, and reduced cortical volume and thickness, in particular in frontal and temporal regions, relative to HCs. This generally accorded with past meta-analysis (De Peri et al. 2012). Both FES and FEB patients showed reduced fractional anisotropy in corpus callosum, cingulum and frontal white matter regions relative to HCs, which was consistent to the majority of studies. Hypoconnectivity was observed in default mode, salience and central executive network in both FES and FEB patients compared to HCs, with FEB showing intermediate connectivity levels that differed from both groups, which broadly aligned with previous findings (Birur et al., 2017; O’Neill et al. 2019). Patients with FES and FEB had reduced resting cerebral blood flow (rCBF) than HCs in several regions, in particularly reduction in frontal areas, middle occipital gyrus and cingulate gyrus, which was similar to earlier studies (Selvaggi et al. 2023; Toma et al. 2018). More severe psychotic symptoms and cognitive impairment were associated with structural, white matter integrity, network connectivity and rCBF abnormalities in FES patients. Associations between brain abnormalities and various cognitive domains were observed in FEB patients. No association was observed between brain abnormalities and clinical variables in FEB patients. Past evidence suggested that reduced global functional connectivity is linked to poorer neuropsychological outcomes in patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. 3. Objective 3 This was successfully achieved. At 1-year follow-up, 17 patients with FES, 16 patients with FEM, and 20 HCs discontinued participation. The overall drop-out rate for the study sample was 22.1%, resulting in 187 participants as the final sample for follow-up analysis. Our findings showed that both patient groups performed worse than HCs at baseline and at one year. However, FEB patients consistently outperformed FES patients across all cognitive tasks. This aligned with previous research, which reported that both FEB and FES patients showed widespread cognitive impairment, albeit the severity of impairment was lower in FEB than in FES (Bora et al. 2015). Moreover, we observed significant improvement from baseline to one year in both FES and FEB groups in the digit symbol, letter-number span, TMT-part A, and TMT-part B. These results further supported previous findings that there was no conclusive evidence for progressive cognitive deterioration in either FEB or FES, and that the cognitive impairment profiles are relatively similar between the two groups (Bortolato et al. 2015). In addition, we observed no significant difference on verbal fluency from baseline to one year in both group, which was consistent with previous evidence that verbal fluency deficits are state independent in these two groups. We observed no significant difference between HC vs FEB vs FES over time across the cognitive domains. These findings indicated a lack of difference in neuropsychological profiles between FEB and FES patients, which generally aligned with previous meta-analysis (Bora et al. 2017). 4. Objective 4 This was successfully achieved. The drop-out rate of study sample for MRI scanning was 24.2% (19 patients with FES, 17 patients with FEM, 22 HCs), resulting in 182 participants as the final sample for analysis. At 1-year follow-up, FES and FEB groups showed cortical volume reductions in frontal and temporal regions, and ventricular enlargement, compared to HCs, with no significant changes from baseline. These findings generally align with studies of treated FES and FEB patients over short follow-up periods. Although earlier studies examining longitudinal changes in functional connectivity before and after treatment initiation reported significant differences (Cui et al. 2025; Gonzalez-Vivas et al. 2019), our findings revealed that alterations in functional connectivity were relatively stable in both patient groups over the 1-year period, which is likely due to the relatively short time interval and all patients receiving treatment from baseline. No changes in diffusion indices and rCBF were observed in FEB and FES patients. Of note, mixed findings regarding longitudinal changes in FES and FEB were found. More studies would be needed to verify our current findings. 5. Objective 5 This was successfully achieved. Baseline cognitive and MRI measures independently predicted symptom and functional outcomes at the 1-year follow-up in patient groups, after adjusting for age, sex, education level, diagnostic group, and baseline symptom and functional levels. Our results found that digit symbol at baseline predicted positive symptom outcome at 1 year follow-up while TMT-part B at baseline predicted functional outcome at 1 year follow-up. Processing speed, measured by the digit symbol task, constitutes a core and robust cognitive impairment in psychosis. Accumulating evidence highlighted processing speed as a robust predictor of better clinical outcome, making it a crucial target for intervention. Moreover, psychotic features in bipolar disorder have been linked to impaired processing speed performance. Our results further supported the predictability of processing speed for clinical outcomes in patients in their early course of bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. As for TMT-part B, a task that primarily assesses executive function, was associated with poorer social and occupational functioning in both bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. These findings further supplemented existing literature by demonstrating that these relationships are evident early in the course of illness. Our findings showed that subcortical structural abnormalities significantly predicted greater severity of positive symptoms at 1-year follow-up. Consistent with previous research, subcortical structural abnormalities have been linked to the presence of psychotic features in bipolar disorder and were associated with poorer clinical outcomes in schizophrenia. Furthermore, poorer social and occupational functioning was predicted by reduced cortical thickness and volume in frontal area. Previous review suggested cortical abnormalities in the frontal lobes was linked to impaired executive function in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Impaired executive functioning, which comprised difficulties in planning, problem-solving, and goal-directed behaviour, would in turn contribute to the decline in social and occupational capabilities in patients with FEB and FES.

17125820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125820.value: Both FES and FEB patients exhibited significant cognitive impairments relative to HCs, with FES patients showing more severe deficits, especially in processing speed and executive functions (e.g., digit symbol, Trail Making test–part B). The cognitive profiles of the two patient groups differed mainly in severity rather than type of impairment, consistent with recent meta-analyses that reported quantitative rather than qualitative differences in cognitive impairment between schizophrenia and bipolar disorder at the first episode. The cognitive impairments in FEB patients generally fall intermediate between those in FES and HCs. Both patient groups had increased lateral ventricle volumes and reduced cortical volumes and thickness in frontal and temporal regions. Fractional anisotropy was reduced in corpus callosum, cingulum and frontal white matter regions in patients with FES and FEB relative to HC. Hypoconnectivity was observed in default mode, salience and central executive network in both FES and FEB patients compared to HCs, with FEB showing intermediate connectivity levels that differed from both groups. Reduced resting cerebral blood flow, particularly in frontal regions, was also observed. More severe symptoms in FES correlated with wider brain abnormalities, whereas in FEB, brain changes correlated mainly with cognitive functioning but not clinical symptoms. At 1-year follow-up, cognitive impairment persisted, with FEB patients consistently performing better than FES across cognitive tests. Cognitive improvement was observed over time in all cognitive domains except verbal fluency, which remained relatively stable over time in both FES and FEB patients. Both patient groups exhibited persistent structural brain abnormalities and stable functional connectivity alterations at the 1-year follow-up. No significant changes were seen in diffusion or cerebral blood flow measures longitudinally. Baseline cognitive domains (processing speed, executive function) and brain structural abnormalities predicted one-year clinical and functional outcomes. Processing speed and subcortical abnormalities predicted more severe positive symptoms while executive function and frontal cortical abnormalities predicted poorer social and occupational functioning.

17125820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125820.value: First, due to the complex inter-relationship among psychopathological, cognitive and functional measures in FES and FEB patients, future analysis will employ data-driven network model to investigate the cross-domain associations. This approach will identify central symptom hubs, bridge nodes between domains, and characterize dynamic interactions, offering transdiagnostic insights into illness mechanisms. Second, we plan to extend our neuroimaging analyses using advanced analysis approach like graph theory-based analysis. Utilizing network metrics, such betweenness centrality, local efficiency, and hub scores, we could characterize both the anatomical and functional brain connectivity patterns in FES and FEB. This approach will provide powerful insight into the topological organization of brain networks, revealing key network properties that may relate to cognitive function. Third, the current study was limited to a 1-year follow-up. Extended reassessments of this cohort (e.g., at 5 years) would track longer-term cognitive and neuroimaging trajectories, clarifying any potential differential longitudinal courses of cognitive impairment and neuroimaging abnormalities between FES and FEB. In addition, reassessment at later follow-ups would also capture relapse/recurrence, sustained remission, functional recovery, and enable predictive modelling for extended clinical and functional outcomes, which would ultimately support the development of individualized outcome prediction and early intervention for these disorders.

17125820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125820.value: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) are severe mental disorders causing enormous burdens to patients and society. Neuroimaging and cognitive assessments represent key strategies in elucidating differential neurobiological signatures between SZ and BD. Nonetheless, most SZ-BD comparison research examined chronic patients with long-term medications. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) study in first-episode schizophrenia (FES) and first-episode bipolar disorder (FEB) with longitudinal follow-up is scarce. We conducted a prospective 1-year follow-up study in FES and FEB patients using a multimodal neuroimaging approach and standardized cognitive assessment. Assessments were performed at baseline and 1 year to track longitudinal changes. Both FES and FEB patients demonstrated cognitive impairment and brain abnormalities as compared to healthy controls (HCs), with FES patients showing more severe and widespread abnormalities relative to FEB patients. Longitudinal changes were observed in some cognitive domains in both groups of patients. Cognitive impairment and brain abnormalities were associated with clinical and functional outcomes. This study helped delineate shared and distinct biomarkers across two disorders, clarify relationships of cognitive and MRI measures with clinical and functional outcomes in the early illness stage, improve outcome prediction, and facilitate development of neuroscience-based diagnostic classification and individualized early intervention.

17125920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125920.value: DNA鹼基配對中可編程的特性，使其外形及生物醫學上的功能可被完全控制。DNA納米結構在用於治療、影像或編程上有顯著的成效，特別是針對性傳遞及控制載體運送分子到細胞中。目前研究領域中的挑戰，是在維持簡單結構和臨床實用性的前提下，開發出有效攜帶及傳送分子到特定細胞的可變式DNA納米結構。十五世紀中，達文西以環狀幾何圖形描繪出「Mazzocchio」。當這個結構投放在分子層面上，mazzocchio擁有數個在可用於分子傳遞中的特性，包括可控的大小、不常見的分子價、承載能力及展示分子的特性。我們的初步結果顯示，我們能夠利用僅十二條單鍵DNA製造出這個環狀結構，而這個結構同時能夠有效地傳遞抗癌藥物艾黴素。在此，我們提議全面研究、鑒定並將mazzocchio應用於細胞及活體內的抗癌藥物傳遞。為此，我們整合研究團隊內已建立的核酸適體技術，用作引導藥物傳遞至細胞所展示的獨特癌症生物標記。我們會將mazzocchio與另一種不常見的、呈現蛇皮狀的磚塊型的DNA納米管進行比較。我們的蛇皮狀納米管由平面的磚塊型表面捲曲而成，且擁有與mazzocchio相似，使用少量單鍵DNA製造的特性。我們的提議有五個階段，第一︰我們將研究及鑒定控制蛇皮狀DNA納米管結構的各項因素。第二︰我們將會利用蛇皮狀DNA納米管傳遞藥物分子到癌細胞。第三︰我們將研究及鑒定控制DNA mazzocchio結構和功用的各項因素。第四︰我們將研究DNA mazzocchio結構上的變化與其針對性運送及傳遞藥物分子到細胞之間的關係。第五︰我們將會在活體老鼠進行運送抗癌藥物的異體移殖，以此判斷蛇皮狀DNA納米管及DNA mazzocchio之間的優劣。這項研究將會為利用由達文西啟發的DNA納米結構，在臨床上作引導性治療定下基礎。

17126720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126720.value: TRIM28 is an epigenetic master regulator that plays an essential role in early development. Over the past two decades, numerous studies have extensively investigated the role of TRIM28 in embryonic stem cell pluripotency and differentiation, cell senescence, innate immune response, apoptosis, autophagy epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and etc. Misregulation or de novo mutation of TRIM28 has been linked to a broad range of diseases from obesity, diabetes, neurological disorders to cancers. TRIM28 has been shown to interact with a variety of factors implicated in transcriptional repression and activation. TRIM28-associated transcription complexes primarily regulate transcription of transposable elements that account for almost half of human genome. TRIM28 is recruited to transposable elements mainly through the physical interaction with hundreds of KRAB domain-containing zinc finger proteins (KRAB-ZNFs). At the same time, TRIM28 acts as a scaffold protein that tethers a variety of epigenetic silencers including the heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1), histone H3K9 methyltransferse SETDB1, DNA methyltransferases and nucleosome remodelling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex to induce chromatin compaction for silencing of TEs. Recently we identified an uncharacterized protein POGK (pogo transposable element with KRAB domain) that is a bona fide binding partner of TRIM28. Our preliminary data showed that POGK is colocalized with TRIM28 but does not localize at pericentric or centromeric heterochromatin, which is unexpected. In this project we will develop a new structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of human TRIM28/POGK complex including the following aims: (1) To provide the molecular basis for the interaction between TRIM28 and POGK. The crystal structure of TRIM28/POGK complex will be determined. (2) To determine DNA-binding specificity of POGK, which will help understand where POGK binds in the genome and its related functions. (3) To determine the functional consequence of the interaction between TRIM28 and POGK. The completed study should help to understand the molecular mechanism by which POGK targets TRIM28 to specific genomic regions, and the effect of POGK knockout on cell growth, proliferation and transformation as well as on early development. The completed study will likely broaden our pool of possible targets for cancer therapeutics given that both TRIM28 and POGK are dysregulated in various types of cancers. TRIM28是表觀遺傳的主要調節因子，在早期發育中起著至關重要的作用。在過去的二十年中，許多工作已經廣泛研究了TRIM28在胚胎幹細胞多能性和分化，細胞衰老，先天免疫應答，細胞凋亡，自噬,上皮向間充質轉化等方面的作用。TRIM28的失調或從頭突變具有與肥胖，糖尿病，神經系統疾病和癌症等多種疾病有關。 TRIM28已被顯示與一系列轉錄抑制和激活相關的因子有相互作用。 含有TRIM28的轉錄複合物參與調節了佔人類基因組近一半的轉座因子的轉錄。TRIM28主要通過與數百種含KRAB結構域的鋅指蛋白（KRAB-ZNFs）的物理相互作用而募集到轉座因子。同時，TRIM28充當支架蛋白，可束縛多種表觀遺傳沉默子，包括異染色質蛋白1（HP1），組蛋白H3K9甲基轉移酶SETDB1，DNA甲基轉移酶和核小體重塑和脫乙酰酶（NuRD）複合物，從而誘導染色質緊縮以沉默轉座因子。最近，我們鑑定了一個未曾表徵的蛋白POGK（具有KRAB域的Pogo轉座因子），並發現它是TRIM28的一個結合蛋白。我們的初步數據顯示，POGK與TRIM28共定位，但未定位於周邊或著絲粒異染色質，這是意料之外的。在這個項目中，我們將系統分析TRIM28 / POGK複合體的結構 與功能，包括以下目標： （1）將確定TRIM28 / POGK複合物的晶體結構，為TRIM28與POGK之間的相互作用提供分子機理。 （2）確定POGK的DNA結合特異性，這將有助於理解POGK在基因組中的結合位置及其相關功能。 完成這項研究應有助於了解TRIM28 / POGK複合物靶向特定基因組區域的分子機制，以及POGK基因敲除對細胞生長，增殖和轉化以及早期發育的影響。鑑於TRIM28和POGK在各種類型的癌症中均失調，因此完成的研究可能會拓寬我們治療癌症的目標範圍。

17126820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126820.value: Lumbar intervertebral discs (IVD) undergo age- and non-age-related degeneration, causing low back pain and neurological deficits. Mouse models are widely used in dissecting physiology and pathobiology due to versatile molecular tools available and other benefits. However, the mouse spine is considered to have limited relevance to IVD degeneration because of distinct IVD anatomy and cellular composition from the human counterpart. To this end, mouse models that exhibit features of human IVD, in particular in the lumbar levels, are therefore much desired to further advance our understanding of IVD degeneration and its associated morbidity. Our recent study in a notochord-specific N-cadherin deficient mouse model revealed accelerated lumbar IVD remodelling with features resembling human IVD degeneration. Moreover, exogenous loading of the tail IVD in this mutant could trigger the remodelling and degeneration. This indicates a unique opportunity of establishing a mouse model relevant to human lumbar IVD degeneration. In this proposal, we hypothesize that that N-cadherin inactivation can induce human disc degeneration-like features in mouse lumbar IVD. We aim to investigate the IVD phenotype of transgenic mouse models that have inducible loss of N-cadherin function specifically in the notochord and its descendent nucleus pulposus. By crossing the mutants with a specific mouse strain, we will also test whether intrinsic cartilage regeneration capacity can further modify the phenotype. IVD remodelling and degeneration will be assessed by a spectrum of histological, molecular, and imaging methodologies. This investigation will establish a novel mouse model with relevance to human IVD degeneration. Such model has advantages of being inducible, surgery-free, and relatively short onset time. This will provide an important tool to better understand IVD degeneration mechanism. Moreover, it may enable cost-effective pilot evaluation of disc regeneration strategies prior to trials in large animals and humans, contributing to spine health care. 腰椎間盤會出現年齡和非年齡相關的退化，導致腰痛和神經功能障礙。基於多功能的分子工具和其他好處，小鼠模型被廣泛用於解剖生理學和病理學。然而，因為椎間盤結構和細胞組成不同，小鼠脊柱被認為跟人類椎間盤退化的相關性有限。為此，具有人類椎間盤特徵的小鼠模型，特別是腰椎，對推進我們對椎間盤退化及其相關的病狀的理解十分重要。 我們最近在一個脊索特定的N-鈣黏著蛋白 (N-cadherin) 缺陷小鼠模型中, 發現腰椎間盤出現加速重塑及具有類似於人類椎間盤退化的特徵。此外，外源性加載該小鼠模型尾部椎間盤能觸發重塑和變性。這些發現對建立與人類腰椎間盤退化有關的小鼠模型提供了獨特機會。 在這項提案中，我們假設滅活N-鈣黏著蛋白功能可以誘導小鼠腰椎間盤出現人類椎間盤退變特徵。我們旨在研究可誘導的脊索及其後髓核中N-鈣粘蛋白功能喪失的轉基因小鼠模型中的椎間盤表型。並且通過這小鼠模型與特定的小鼠品種雜交，我們將測試軟骨再生能力與椎間盤表型的關係。我們將通過一系列組織學，分子和成像方法對椎間盤重塑和退化進行評估。 這項研究將建立與人類椎間盤退化有關的新小鼠模型。這種模型的優點是可誘導，無需手術並且發展時間相對較短。這將為了解椎間盤退化機理提供重要的工具。此外，在大型動物和人類試驗之前，此模型對椎間盤再生策略提供具成本效益的先導評估，從而有助於提升脊柱醫療。

17200320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200320.value: Recent advances in soft electronic materials have created a wealth of opportunities for building skin-conformal sensors for healthcare monitoring in wearable form. Although many devices have been demonstrated for the measurement of bioelectricity, temperature and strain, characterization of biochemical markers in a continuous and non-irritating manner remains challenging. As exemplified by glucose monitoring, traditional methods rely on invasive components that disrupt the skin barrier for the sampling of blood, causing pain or discomfort to the patient. Non-invasive analyses of sweat, saliva or tears can generate useful data, but provide only limited information for clinical decisions. Recent approaches have exploited wearable, needle-based devices for the analyses of dermal interstitial fluid, which are particularly helpful for continuous glucose monitoring in the management of diabetes. However, their stiff structures may cause unwanted tissue responses that compromise their performance. An ideal wearable system for monitoring biochemical markers may require new materials and structures that can naturally integrate with the skin tissues, providing a permeable and tissue-compliant interface for biochemical sampling. We recently developed a class of biomimetic materials based on aramid nanofibers (ANFs). The ANF composites can emulate the structures and properties of natural skin, combining high porosity (>90%) with tissue-like mechanics and biocompatibility. Their solution-based fabrication methods allow for integration with electronic sensors and 3D microstructures to form organ-conformal devices. In addition, we have extensive experience in the development of soft electronics for bio-interfacing, including epidermal systems for electrophysiological and thermal mapping, organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) for biomolecule sensing, 3D electronic membranes for cardiac sensing and stimulation, and many other devices for biomedical applications. In this proposed research, we aim to explore ANF-based biomaterials and develop multifunctional soft devices as a “lab-on-skin” for biochemical analyses. We will fabricate ANF-based microneedles that penetrate the stratum corneum barrier and integrate with the shallow layer of the epidermis. Their tissue-like mechanics and miniaturized structures could enable a biotic/abiotic interface with long-term stability. The hydrophilic and microporous nature of the ANF composites could facilitate capillary transport of the interstitial fluid to the skin-mounted sensors. We will incorporate high-performance semiconductor electronics in the skin patches for real-time measurement of glucose, C-reactive protein or other important biomarkers. Animal experiments will help to evaluate their performance and biocompatibility in clinically-relevant settings. This fundamental research into materials properties, device design and biological evaluation could pave the way for the development of next-generation wearable health sensors for clinical medicine. 近來，柔性電子材料的發展為構建可穿戴式生物醫學傳感器創造了機會。雖然一些新型的柔性可穿戴設備已經可以應用於生物電信號、溫度和應力的測量，但是實現生化指標的連續無刺激的監測依然具有挑戰性。以葡萄糖檢測為例，傳統方法依靠的是可以穿破皮膚屏障進行血液分析的侵入式設備。這種方式會給患者造成疼痛和不適。基於汗液、唾液或者眼淚的非侵入式分析可以獲得有用的數據，但是對臨床診斷僅能提供有限的信息。最近的一些方法利用可穿戴的微針式設備對皮膚組織液進行分析，為糖尿病管理所需的連續葡萄糖監測提供了途徑。但是，它們的剛性結構可能會產生一些不良的組織反應並影響設備的性能。理想的可穿戴式生化監測系統需要一些能與皮膚組織自然集成的新材料和新結構，從而為生化採樣提供一個可滲透的且與組織器官兼容的界面。 我們最近研發了一種基於芳綸納米纖維（ANFs）的仿生材料。芳綸納米纖維複合材料可以模擬天然皮膚的結構和特性，它將高孔隙率（> 90％）與類組織的力學性能和生物相容性相結合。它們基於溶液的製備方法能夠與電子傳感器和三維微結構的加工工藝兼容，使得製造與器官共形的電子設備成為可能。此外，我們在開發用於生物生物集成的柔性電子器件方面擁有豐富的經驗。我們的代表性工作包括用於電生理信號和溫度測繪的表皮電子系統，用於生物分子檢測的有機場效應晶體管，用於心臟生理檢測和刺激的三維電子膜以及其他的一些生物醫學設備。 在這個研究中，我們致力於探索以芳綸納米纖維為基礎的仿生材料，並由此開發用於生化分析的多功能可穿戴柔性器件，即一種“皮膚上的生化實驗室”。我們將製備基於芳綸納米纖維的微針陣列。它們可以穿透角質層屏障並與表皮的淺層相結合。它們的與組織相似的力學性能和小型化的結構可以使生物/非生物界面保持長期穩定。芳綸納米纖維的親水性和微孔性質有利於組織液向安裝在皮膚上的傳感器進行毛細傳輸。我們將在器件中集成高性能半導體電子傳感器，對葡萄糖，C反應蛋白或其他重要的生理指標進行實時測量。動物實驗將有助於評估它們在臨床相關環境中的性能和生物相容性。這些對材料特性，設備設計和生物學評估的基礎研究可以為下一代可穿戴式的健康監測傳感器及其在臨床醫學中的應用鋪平道路。

17200320.label: Realisation of objectives
17200320.value: The ANF-based nanocomposites were synthesized with solution-based processes. With added hydrophilic polymers and multifunctional molecules added in to the composites, pore size was actively tuned. The water transport properties were further characterized with experiments and FEA simulation, demonstrating the roles of nanoscale building blocks. We developed micro-molding process for the fabrication of microneedles and use transfer printing techniques to integrate wafer-fabricated electronics onto the hydrogel membranes, forming hybrid devices. Sampling and analysis of biofluids were carried out using these soft and skin-conformal bioelectronic system. Organic electrochemical transistors (OECT) based on conducting polymers were fabricated on the hydrogel devices, allowing for precise measurement of biomarkers based on the specific binding chemistry at the electrodes. This method can be extended for potential diagnoses and monitoring of many medical conditions. We thoroughly characterized the biocompatibility of the materials using both cell culture and animal experiments. The study shows no observable toxicity to living cells. The good biocompatibility also originates from the tissue-like mechanical behavior of the hydrogels, which minimized tissue irritation and unwanted immune responses.

17200320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200320.value: We find the ANF-based porous composites, when integrated with soft hydrophilic macromolecules, exhibit excellent water-transport properties. They can be manufactured into soft skin-integrated electronics and microneedle devices for the analysis of physiological properties and biochemical markers. Advanced wafer-fabricated electronics, such as OECT, can be integrated in this platform to provide precise sensing capabilities. The excellent biocompatibility and functionality of this system indicate potential applications in medical technologies.

17200320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200320.value: Further development include integration with wireless modules for long-term application on human subjects, AI-based data analysis and active stimulation in a closed-loop manner, and development of manufacturing processes for low-cost production of devices, and many others. These works will help to unleash the potential of the device technology for clinical translation.

17200320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200320.value: In this project, we successfully developed ANF-based porous composites as a key component for wearable biochemical sensors. Their fluid transport characteristics were engineered with self-assembled fibrillar network with tunable topology and dimensions. 3D molding of microneedle devices were realized by the solution-based processing of the materials. Various bioelectronic sensors, including those based on wafer-fabricated organic transistors, were integrated with the device platform for sampling and analysis of biofluids and biomarkers. This device platform demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and functionality during animal experiment, and it may facilitate the development of next generation wearable devices for medical diagnosis and disease management.

17200820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200820.value: This research project is motivated by the PI's experience of developing workforce optimization tools for transportation and logistics organizations. While a schedule planner (called an agent in this research) has the knowledge of the criteria and work rules for staff scheduling, a typical challenge is that she produces schedules based on her implicit preferences and is uncertain about the relative importances of the multiple objectives. Moreover, due to the limited human capability of achieving optimality, the observed schedules produced manually may not reflect the agent's actual preferences. Another challenge is that the agent occasionally allows violation of certain work rules. A common practice is that the model developer and the agent refine the objective weights and constraints iteratively through continuous discussions. Nevertheless, the staff schedule produced by the mathematical model may not fully satisfy the agent's preferences so that the agent often still needs to put considerable efforts into adjusting the schedule. We formalize the above challenges by three main properties of the problem: model uncertainty, bounded rationality, and compromised infeasibility. The PI will leverage his experience of staff scheduling and inference of latent variables to develop a data-driven inverse optimization framework to determine the agent's implicit preferences in staff scheduling. Instead of the common practice which asks the agent to guesstimate the objective weights and degree of allowed infeasibility, the agent is given sample staff schedules to rank according to her realized preferences. The ranked staff schedules will be fed into the inverse optimization model for inferring the problem parameters. The novelty of this proposed research is threefold. First, we address the agent's self-unconsciousness of relative importances of objectives and constraint violations simultaneously in staff scheduling. Second, we propose a novel data-driven inference framework that interacts with the agent to learn her implicit preferences and improve the effectiveness of staff scheduling models. Third, our computational study is original; it mimics the procedure of our proposed preference inference framework. Known staff scheduling problem structures will be used in the computational experiments and compared with the solutions found by the inverse optimization approach. The performance of the proposed methodology will be evaluated. Non-trivial insights into the inference of human preferences will be derived. To translate research into practice, the solution methodology will be applied for real-world staff scheduling problems from major parties in the industry, through the PI's existing collaboration network and a key logistics organization in the region for practical assessment and implementation. 本研究項目受啟發於項目主持人為運輸和物流組織開發人力優化工具之經驗。調度員（在此研究中稱為代理人）大多了解員工編排的標準和工作規則，但常見編更的困難是代理人根據自己的隱性內在個人偏好來製定員工編排計劃，代理人並不確定多個編排目標的相對重要性。此外，由於人手達到最佳化的能力有限，現實所觀察到的工作編排可能無法反映代理人的實際偏好。另一個挑戰是代理人有時會允許違反某些工作規則。現實中常見的解決方法是數學模型開發人和代理人通過不斷的討論來以迭代方式優化目標權重和約束。然而，由數學模型產生的編排計劃可能無法完全滿足代理人的偏好，因此代理人經常仍然需要花費大量的時間及精力調整編排計劃。 我們考慮三個主要問題屬性以正式規範上述挑戰：模型不確定性、有限理性及不可行折衷。 項目主持人將利用其在人員調度方面的經驗和潛在變量推論作研究數據驅動逆向優化框架，以尋找代理在人員調度中的個人偏好。有別於要求代理人猜測客觀權重和允許折衷程度的一般做法，此研究提出給代理人提供參考之編排計劃，以根據其實現的偏好進行排序。以分排名的編排計劃將被放進逆向優化模型中，以推斷問題參數。 這項提議的研究之創新性是三方面的。首先，我們在工作人員調度中同時解決代理人對目標相對重要性和約束違反之潛意識。其次，我們提出了一種新穎的數據驅動推理框架，該框架與代理進行交互以了解其隱式偏好並提高人員調度模型的有效性。第三，我們的計算實驗是原創的；實驗模仿了此研究提出的偏好推理框架的過程。已知的人員調度問題結構將用於計算實驗中，並與通過逆向優化方法找到的解決方案進行比較。擬議方法的性能將得到評估，並得出關於人類偏好推理的非平凡見解。 為了將研究轉化為實踐，本解決方案方法將通過項目主持人現有合作伙伴網絡以及本地域的主要物流組織，針對行業中主要的實際員工調度問題應用，以進行實際評估和實行。

17200820.label: Realisation of objectives
17200820.value: For Objective 1 (To tackle the challenge of inferring non-observable human preferences in staff scheduling problems): Under this objective, we first reviewed the literature on staff scheduling problems (Kuo and Han, 2025) and human preference estimation (Yan et al., 2022). In Kuo and Han (2025), we discuss that traditional staff scheduling methods primarily rely on model-based approaches, such as mixed-integer linear programming and queuing models, where machine learning (ML) approaches have gained popularity in recent years. In Yan et al. (2022), we discuss inverse reinforcement learning (IRL), an approach in which human experts specify actions for specific situations, allowing us to infer the underlying reward function from their behavior. While ML and IRL aim to imitate expert decisions, these decisions may not always be optimal—experts can make errors due to the complexity of the problems, as we note in our project. Therefore, our work addresses the challenge of inferring non-observable human preferences in staff scheduling problems, which we explore through Objectives 2 and 3. For Objective 2 (To develop a novel inverse optimization framework that interacts with the agent to learn her preferences for constructing more effective staff schedules), Objective 3 (To conduct computational experiments with the proposed inverse optimization approach on known staff scheduling structures for the assessment of the performance of the methodology), and Objective 4 (To derive non-trivial insights into the inference of human preferences in staff scheduling): Under these three objectives, the PI's PhD student (who completed her PhD in 2025) conducted her PhD research on this topic (Han, 2025). Objectives 2, 3, and 4 are addressed in Sections 3, 4, and 5 of Han (2025). Specifically, to tackle the challenges related to these objectives, we first identify soft constraints within staff scheduling problems and allow for their violation to address potential infeasibility issues. To infer the agent's implicit preferences, we develop a data-driven inverse-optimization framework that minimizes estimation errors. The agent is provided with sample staff schedules, which she ranks according to her realized preferences. These ranked schedules serve as input to the inverse model, which infers the weights assigned to various goals. We establish theoretical results demonstrating the existence of solutions to the inverse problem—regardless of the agent’s rationality level—and the conditions for the uniqueness of solutions when the agent is fully rational. Additionally, we analyze properties such as the sign of the coefficients, the number of samples needed, and the criteria for sample selection. To determine whether minimizing total ranking errors or maximal individual errors yields better results, we formulate the inverse optimization problem using the L_1 (sum of errors) and L_\infty (maximum error) norms, respectively. Extensive computational experiments examine how factors such as sample size, agent rationality, solution similarity, and signal changes affect the performance of the inverse models. Our findings indicate that minimizing the maximum error (L_\infty norm) is more effective than minimizing the total error (L_1 norm) for accurately capturing the agent's preferences during ranking. For Objective 5 (To apply the proposed solution methodology for real-life staff scheduling problems) and Objective 6 (To promote the proposed solution methodology and benefit the transportation and logistics industry): Under these two objectives, we conducted a real-world case study focused on a student helper assignment problem for the 27th International Conference of the Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies (please refer to Section 5 of Han (2025)). The methodology was applied to a scenario involving ten human agents. The results indicated that estimation accuracy improves when agents exhibit rational behavior. Specifically, for rational agents, the model was effective in accurately estimating their true preference weights, even when the agents were uncertain about their actual weights. Experimental findings demonstrated that our proposed approach effectively infers the preferences of rational human schedulers. However, for agents showing high levels of irrationality, the effectiveness is not guaranteed. The project also explored a dynamic assignment problem for service agents responsible for on-site service delivery, such as maintenance tasks or emergency response (Yan et al., 2023), as well as a machine scheduling problem (Li et al., 2022). As part of an effort to advance optimization frameworks for staff scheduling, one MSc dissertation and three undergraduate final-year projects were completed, which they focused on a collaborative project on emergency department physician scheduling (please refer to Part C). 17200820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200820.value: First, we developed a novel linear inverse optimization model that minimizes ranking errors to infer human preferences in staff scheduling. The model effectively accounts for model uncertainty, bounded rationality, and infeasibility, enabling the inference of non-observable human preferences with high efficiency. Second, we proved the existence and uniqueness conditions of the inverse model solutions, providing foundational insights into preference inference. We analyzed properties such as coefficient signs, sample requirements, and criteria for sample selection, enhancing the understanding of the model's behavior. Third, we demonstrated that the model that utilizes the L_\infty norm consistently outperforms the model that utilizes L_1 norm in estimating true preferences, especially for bounded rational agents. We found that the models effectively estimate preferences for rational agents, with estimation accuracy improving as the number of samples increases. We showed that schedule similarity influences convergence speed but not the final estimated weights, and that signal changes do not significantly impact model performance. Fourth, we applied the methodology to a real student helper assignment problem at an international conference, validating the practical applicability of the approach. We found that estimation accuracy improves with rational behavior, and the model can effectively infer true preferences even when agents are uncertain about their weights. We identified limitations where high irrationality levels reduce the effectiveness of the inference method. Finally, we extended the research to dynamic assignment problems for on-site service agents and machine scheduling, broadening the scope of the inverse optimization framework. In summary, the project provides an inverse optimization methodology capable of inferring human preferences in complex scheduling environments. It offers a quantitative measure of bounded rationality via objective values, enabling a better understanding and modeling of human decision-making behavior. The findings support practical deployment of preference inference models in real-world staff scheduling, with potential for adaptation to various service and operational contexts. The research advances theoretical knowledge in inverse optimization, preference modeling, and human-in-the-loop decision-making, serving as a foundation for future developments in intelligent scheduling systems. The research resulted in several publications, including an HKU PhD dissertation and papers in Transportation Research Part B/E, International Journal of Production Research, and a book chapter in the Encyclopedia in Operations Management. The journal version of the HKU PhD dissertation is also under preparation for submission to Production and Operations Management.

17200820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200820.value: In this project, we evaluated the computational performance of our proposed inverse optimization framework through a case study involving student helper scheduling at the 27th International Conference of the Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies. The results demonstrated the effectiveness of the approach in inferring scheduler preferences in this context. Furthermore, the methodology holds potential for broader applications in real-world staff scheduling problems that require understanding and modeling human preferences, such as scheduling for international conference helpers, public transit drivers, and airline staff. Initial research has also been initiated on related problems, including service agent scheduling and machine scheduling. As previously noted, an MSc dissertation and three undergraduate final-year projects have been completed, focusing on emergency department physician scheduling. Collaborations have been established with several prominent institutions to advance this line of research: - HKU Department of Emergency Medicine and HKU-Shenzhen Hospital - CUHK Accident and Emergency Medicine Academic Unit and Prince of Wales Hospital - Tseung Kwan O Hospital, Accident and Emergency Department

17200820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200820.value: In staff scheduling, a scheduler (called an agent) knows the rules and goals but often makes schedules based on their own preferences, which are not always clear. They may not realize how important different goals are, and because human decisions are not perfect, their schedules might not always match their true preferences. Sometimes, they even break rules intentionally or unintentionally. We refer to these issues as model uncertainty, bounded rationality, and compromised infeasibility. To address these challenges, we propose a data-driven method that considers past schedules the agent has chosen. These schedules are ranked according to the agent's preferences. Our inverse optimization approach then identifies the hidden priorities behind these schedules by minimizing estimation errors. We show that, regardless of the agent's rationality, our solution exists, and if the agent is fully rational, it is unique. We also compare two ways of minimizing errors: one that minimizes the largest difference between schedules, and another that minimizes the total errors. Computational experiments show that minimizing the largest error performs better. We also applied our proposed method to a real-world case involving 10 schedulers. We find that the more rational the agent, the more accurately we can estimate their true preferences, even if they are unsure about them.

17201020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201020.value: When phase information is lost in measurements, the recovery of the underlying object from the magnitudes of its Fourier transform is called phase retrieval problem. Phase retrieval is one of important problem in imaging science. There are many scientific and engineering applications involving phase retrieval problems, for example, astronomical imaging, microscopy imaging and optics. There are theoretical and computational challenges in phase retrieval problem. They include questions of uniqueness, regularization, optimization, efficient reconstruction algorithms and convergence analysis. The main aim of this proposal is to study and analyze phase retrieval of color images. It is interesting to note that there a strong correlation among red, green and blue channels of color images and such correlation can be used for solving phase retrieval problems more efficiently. Our main focus will be proposing new mathematical analysis and developing efficient solution methods for phase retrieval of color images. Our contributions are to propose new mathematical models and algorithms, and analyze their theoretical and convergence properties. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to make use of correlated color channels to study and analyze phase retrieval problems. Our idea is to study phase retrieval of color images under the quaternion framework by encoding red, green and blue color pixel values on the three imaginary parts of a quaternion. Because of non-commutative nature of quaternion, we propose to use real-structure preserving tool to study and analyze the corresponding phase retrieval problem. Moreover, we develop and analyze algorithms for phase retrieval of color images by using transform-based regularization, and also study sparsity effect and support information in phase retrieval problem. The recovery guarantee and convergence properties of the proposed methods will be investigated. On the other hand, we propose to apply our theoretical results and develop numerical algorithms in the application of wide-field, high-resolution Fourier ptychographic microscopy imaging. The main issue is to study high-to-low resolution matrix and the spectral multiplexing and coherent-state decomposition in the our mathematical models and optimization algorithms. We will develop iterative algorithms for solving such ptychographic microscopy setting. We can make use of experimental data sets to verify the proposed mathematical models for phase retrieval of color images and demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithms for color image recovery. 當相位信息在測量中丟失時, 基礎對象的恢復從其傅立葉變換的幅度來看, 稱為相位檢索問題. 相位檢索是成像科學中的重要問題之一, 如天文學, 顯微鏡和光學中的工程應用. 相位檢索在理論和計算中的挑戰, 包括唯一性問題, 正則化, 優化, 高效的重建算法和收斂等. 項目的主要目的是研究和分析色彩的相位恢復圖片. 因為紅色, 綠色和藍色之間存在很強的相關性, 可更有效地求解相位檢索問題. 我們的主要重點是提出新的數學分析和開發有效的彩色圖像相位檢索的解決方法. 我們的貢獻是要提出新的數學模型和算法, 並分析它們的理論和收斂性屬性. 據我們所知, 這是首次嘗試利用相關的顏色通道, 以研究和分析相位檢索問題. 我們的想法是研究在四元數框架下通過編碼對彩色圖像進行相位檢索.因為關於四元數的非交換性質, 我們建議使用實結構保留研究和分析相應相位檢索問題的工具. 而且, 我們通過使用基於變換的正則化開發和分析用於彩色圖像相位檢索的算法, 並研究稀疏效應和相位支持信息檢索問題. 擬議方案的恢復保證和收斂性方法將進行調查。 另一方面, 我們建議應用我們的理論結果並發展數值算法在寬域高分辨率傅里葉指紋圖譜分析中的應用顯微鏡成像. 主要問題是研究從高到低的分辨率矩陣和數學模型中的頻譜多路復用和相干態分解和優化算法. 我們將開發迭代算法來解決這種問題. 我們可以利用實驗數據集來驗證提出的用於彩色圖像相位檢索的數學模型並演示提出的彩色圖像恢復算法的性能.

17201020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201020.value: In the research output [3,7], we proposed and studied theoretical problems of phase retrieval for color image under the quaternion framework. In [3], we showed that n-dimensional quaternion signals can be reconstructed up to a global right quaternion phase factor from O(n) phaseless measurements. In the research output [3,7], basic theoretical results about quaternion vectors/matrices were established for analysis and development. In the research output [2,5], some properties of structured quaternion matrices were also provided. We have investigated low rank pure quaternion approximation for pure quaternion matrices (color images), and studied block diagonalization of quaternion circulant matrices. These properties are different from the case of real or complex matrices, and are important for color imaging applications. In the research output [1,3], we developed and analyzed algorithms for phase retrieval of color images by using transform-based regularization, and also studied sparsity effect and support information in phase retrieval problem. The scalable algorithm quaternion Wirtinger flow for solving quaternion phase retrieval problems was established and its convergence guarantee was provided. Compared with the analysis of complex Wirtinger flow, a series of mathematical treatments were employed to overcome the difﬁculties of the non-commutativity of quaternion multiplication. In the research output [3,4,6], numerical results on color images and Fourier imaging examples are considered to validate our theoretical results. In particular, for pure quaternion signal recovery, our quaternion method often succeeds with notably fewer measurements compared to real-valued methods based on monochromatic model or concatenation model.

17201020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201020.value: Color image restoration methods typically represent images as vectors in Euclidean space or combinations of three monochrome channels. However, they often overlook the correlation between these channels, leading to color distortion and artifacts in the reconstructed image. To address this issue, we will investigate into quaternion-based norm minimization methods for color image reconstruction. We would like to explore and utilize quaternion algebra to capture the relationships among RGB channels comprehensively. Our idea is to employ quaternion-based techniques to approximate the underlying low-rank structure of quaternion-encoded color images. We will study both theoretical proofs and numerical results to validate and demonstrate the versatility and efficacy of the proposed idea in various color low-level imaging tasks.

17201020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201020.value: The quaternion phase retrieval problem is formulated as the reconstruction of the underlying signal from its sensed magnitudes with known sensing matrix. The problem attracted much attention because there are many color imaging applications. In this project, we confirmed that the global right quaternion phase factor is the only trivial ambiguity which is different from real or complex case. The main contribution is to demonstrate that a scalable and practical algorithm is developed for solving quaternion phase retrieval problem.

17201120.label: Project Objectives
17201120.value: To develop multi-level models to estimate the cradle-to-end of construction embodied carbon emissions of high-rise staff quarters in Hong Kong that adopt the innovative three-dimensional modular integrated construction (MiC) method, which will enable effective systematic comparison with the embodied carbon of the same type of buildings adopting the traditional two-dimensional panelized system as the baseline. To use the estimation models developed to quantify the cradle-to-end of construction embodied carbon emissions of modular high-rise staff quarters buildings and, via systematic comparison with the baseline, identify and examine embodied carbon-sensitive structural design parameters and variables aligned with the design, production, transport, and construction stages of the buildings. To develop and validate low-carbon structural design solutions using uni-, bi-, and multi-variate sensitivity and scenario analyses and, via application of an artificial neural network and genetic algorithm, systematically optimize MiC to achieve maximum embodied carbon reduction in Hong Kong’s high-rise staff quarters buildings while meeting structural stability and safety performance requirements.
