17201120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201120.value: Buildings contribute significantly to carbon emissions over their life cycle. Hong Kong has the highest population density in the world, with high-rise residential blocks the norm. The Hong Kong government has adopted a prefabrication strategy involving the use of two-dimensional (2D) panelized systems for all public housing developments, and recently began promoting three-dimensional (3D) modular integrated construction (MiC) to enhance productivity and competitiveness. In theory, the use of MiC should lead to a reduction in buildings’ life cycle carbon emissions. However, there is a lack of systematic understanding of modular buildings’ embodied carbon. Also, although structural design has been identified as a major factor influencing buildings’ embodied carbon, low-carbon structural design still receives marginal consideration in design decision-making. The aims of the proposed project are to examine the extent to which the use of innovative 3D MiC can reduce the embodied carbon emissions of high-rise residential buildings in Hong Kong compared with the traditional 2D panelized system and to optimize the modular method to achieve maximum embodied carbon emission reduction. The project will be carried out over a 36-month period in three interrelated stages. The first is the development of emission estimation models for 3D modular buildings in spatial and temporal comparison with the 2D baseline using real-life high-rise staff quarters buildings, which will involve five levels of analysis: material, component, module, apartment, and building. Cradle-to-gate embodied carbon emissions will be calculated using SimaPro software, and transport and construction-related carbon emissions will be measured using the process analysis method. The second stage is the examination of embodied carbon-sensitive structural design parameters and variables, and the third is the optimization of the modular method by applying an artificial neural network (ANN) and genetic algorithm (GA) to achieve maximum embodied carbon reduction. The low-carbon structural design solutions developed will be validated, and the optimal modular method verified. The project outcomes will be: (1) multi-level models for estimating the cradle-to-end of construction embodied carbon emissions of high-rise staff quarters in Hong Kong that adopt innovative 3D MiC; (2) the quantified embodied carbon of such modular high-rise residential buildings and embodied carbon-sensitive structural design parameters and variables aligned with the design, production, transport, and construction stages of buildings; and (3) validated low-carbon structural design solutions and optimized MiC via an ANN-GA-integrated process which achieves maximum embodied carbon reduction in high-rise residential buildings while meeting structural stability and safety performance requirements. 建築在全生命週期中的碳排放顯著。香港擁有最密集的人口，高層住宅建築成為常態。香港政府已採取預製策略，即在所有公共住房開發中使用二維（2D）預製板系統，並且最近開始推廣三維（3D）組裝合成建築法（MiC），以提高生產力和競爭力。理論上，使用MiC可以減少建築物生命週期碳排放。但是，目前對於模塊化建築的隱含碳排放缺乏系統性理解。并且，儘管結構設計已被認為是影響建築隐含碳排放的主要因素，但在設計決策中仍少考慮低碳結構設計。 此項目旨在研究與傳統的二維系統相比，使用創新的組裝合成建築法可以在多大程度上減少香港高層住宅建築的隱含碳排放，並通過模塊優化實現最大化的隱含碳減排。該項目將分三個階段進行，為期36個月。第一階段是建立三維模塊化建築的排放估算模型，並與現有的二維高層員工宿舍在時間和空間維度進行比較。這將涉及五個層次的分析：材料，組件，模塊，建築單元和整棟建築。原材料生產到預製件生產的碳排放是基於SimaPro軟件進行計算，而運輸和現場安裝相關的碳排放則使用過程分析方法計算。第二階段是識別及研究對隱含碳排放影響較大的結構設計參數和變量。第三階段是通過應用人工神經網絡（ANN）和遺傳算法（GA）來實現最大化的隱含碳減排。最終，將對這些低碳結構設計方案以及優化的組裝合成建築法進行驗證。 該項目的成果將是：（1）針對採用三維組裝合成建築法的香港高層員宿舍的多層次隱含碳排放估算模型，該模型將考慮從原材料生產到建築施工階段。（2）此類模塊化高層住宅建築的隱含碳排量以及與建築的設計，生產，運輸和施工階段有關的碳敏感結構設計參數和變量。（3）經過驗證的基於人工神經網絡（ANN）和遺傳算法（GA）的低碳結構設計方案以及優化組裝合成建築法，該過程在滿足結構穩定性和安全性能要求的同時，實現高層住宅建築最大化的隱含碳減排。

17201120.label: Realisation of objectives
17201120.value: All three objectives have been successfully achieved. More good quality research outputs have been delivered and a solid foundation has been paved for future research on life cycle carbon assessment and reduction of concrete MiC high-rise buildings. For achieving Objective 1: First, we have defined the system boundary as cradle-to-end-of-construction for the life cycle embodied carbon (EC) assessment of concrete MiC high-rise buildings in this project. The study scope included EC emissions generated from materials, components, and modules, as well as the process of excavation, prefabrication, transport, and construction for concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings. We have also examined the differences of the construction process and EC emission sources in the process of MiC compared with conventional prefabricated buildings. Second, based on the defined system boundaries and study scope, we have established the multi-level EC assessment model for concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings in both temporal and spatial dimensions. In the temporal dimension, the cradle-to-gate (including raw material production, transportation to factory, and manufacturing), prefabrication (in factory), transportation to site, and construction stages were examined. In the spatial dimension, the EC was examined at the five levels of material, component, module, flat and building. Third, we have selected one block of a pilot concrete MiC staff quarters project for detailed case study. In comparison, we have selected another concrete MiC high-rise public housing project and two additional conventional prefabricated concrete building projects for cross-case benchmarking. Regarding the project data collection and processing methods for the EC assessment, we have also investigated the integration of BIM models of the building or modules and LCA tool (e.g., SimaPro software) to achieve a high-efficiency EC analysis. The established multi-level EC assessment model facilitated the comparison among different MiC and conventional prefabricated buildings. It also enhanced the understanding of EC emissions of concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings in a systematic approach, and provided a solid foundation for identifying EC-intensive lifecycle stages in the temporal dimension and building elements in the spatial dimension. The findings have been published in Building and Environment (IF=7.4) (Teng et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2024), CIB World Building Congress 2022 (Pan et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022) and CRIOCM Conference (Chen et al., 2023). For achieving Objective 2: First, we have conducted a thorough data collection of the two concrete MiC projects as well as the baseline case of conventional prefabricated building projects for their cradle-to-end-of-construction EC quantification and cross-case comparisons. Multiple data collection channels and methods were used, including desk study of the project documents and records, data collection from the contractor and module supplier, personal interviews, and site and factory visits. A detailed list of data or project information was summarized, collected and verified. Second, we have conducted the multi-level EC assessment of the MiC case building. We have carefully input and double-checked the EC-relevant data for the EC quantification using the process-LCA method and SimaPro software. The results revealed that the cradle-to-gate stage contributed the most EC emissions during the cradle-to-end-of-construction stage. The material production alone generated around 80% of the total cradle-to-end-of-construction EC emissions of the building. Particularly, structural materials and corresponding building elements were identified as major EC sources in the case building. The EC from transportation and construction only accounted for a marginal percentage of the total EC emissions. The EC of the other examined concrete MiC high-rise residential building projects was also assessed. Third, we have conducted a detailed cross-case EC comparison among the examined two case MiC buildings and two conventional prefabricated residential buildings. Comparing with the baseline case (staff quarters), both case MiC buildings generated less cradle-to-site EC emissions from structural materials (i.e., concrete and rebar) by 15% and 19% respectively. By examining the consumed quantity of structural materials, the EC reduction was identified to be mainly caused by the less use of rebar in the two MiC case buildings. While comparing with the other baseline case (a public housing project with a different layout design and story height), the two MiC case buildings generated more EC emissions from structural materials’ production and transportation as this baseline case was identified to use much less structural materials than the two MiC case buildings. These results indicated that different building designs also made significant impact on the EC emissions apart from different construction approaches. Nevertheless, the cross-case comparisons revealed fewer EC emissions of MiC during the construction stage. The case building achieved 30% and 49% less EC emissions than the two baseline cases during construction, respectively, owing to less onsite material consumption and onsite activities that are commonly acknowledged as advantages of MiC. The findings have been published in Building and Environment (IF=7.4) (Pan and Wang, 2023; Zhang et al., 2024), Resources, Conservation and Recycling (IF=11.2) (Chen et al., 2023), CIB World Building Congress 2022 (Zhang et al., 2022) and CRIOCM Conference (Chen et al., 2023). For achieving Objective 3: First, we have conducted a thorough review on low carbon concrete materials and low carbon structural design (LCSD) methods to identify the feasible low carbon design solutions for concrete MiC high-rise buildings. Regarding the low carbon concrete materials, we have identified the use of supplementary cementitious materials, i.e., fly ash and ground granulated blast-furnace slag, could lead to averaged 27.4% EC reductions while maintaining the concrete strength and other properties. Other materials, such as low carbon cementitious binders, recycled concrete aggregates, and high-strength concretes, have been identified to effectively reduce the EC. In terms of LCSD, we have identified seven detailed optimization measures at three structural levels, i.e., 1) enhancing material strength, optimizing the external size and internal section design of components at the component scale, 2) changing the structural layout and building shape at the layout scale, and 3) optimizing the structural system and types at the system scale. Second, based on the findings of Objective 2 and the review, we have developed a guiding framework for LCSD of concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings through a 3-step optimization, i.e. 1) module optimization; 2) structural design optimization; and 3) low-carbon material optimization. We have used the visual programming in Dynamo of Revit software to investigate different designs by changing concrete grade, module component size, rebar ratio and using low carbon concrete. We have also developed a LCSD tool by integrating parametric structural modeling using Grasshopper/Python and structural software (ETABS) to achieve a more efficient EC reduction analysis. Third, we have developed an AI-based optimization and prediction model based on machine-learning. We applied it to the case building, which presented 500 structural design scenarios suitable for creating a robust dataset to train the model. We employed four machine learning (ML) models to predict the EC of the case building under different design scenarios. We have also examined some other factors that affect the EC reduction potential in Hong Kong’s building sector in a long term. The findings have been published in Building and Environment (IF=7.4) (Pan and Wang, 2023; Zhang et al., 2024; Wang and Pan, 2024a,b), Resources, Conservation and Recycling (IF=11.2) (Chen et al., 2023), npj Urban Sustainability (IF=9.1) (Wang and Pan, 2024), CIB World Building Congress 2022 (Zhang et al., 2022) and CRIOCM Conference (Chen et al., 2023).

17201120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201120.value: The major findings have been reported in 7 journal articles (5 in BaE, IF 7.4; 1 in RCR, IF 11.2; 1 in npj Urban Sustainability, IF 9.1), and 4 conference papers. Regarding EC assessment model and BIM-aided LCA, the major findings/outcomes include: (1) Systematic EC analysis of MiC buildings can be conducted in temporal and spatial dimensions; and (2) BIM-integrated LCA methods cover three typical types: integrating data into a third-party application/tool, importing a bills of quantities generated from the BIM model into a dedicated LCA tool, and using plug-ins with LCA data for BIM software (Zhang et al., 2024; Teng et al., 2022). Regarding EC assessment, the major findings/outcomes include: (1) For MiC staff quarters project, intensive EC was from producing materials, especially structural; (2) The cradle-to-end-of-construction EC of the building was quantified as 569.3 kgCO2e/m2, of which 81.7% was from material production; (3) The concrete and reinforcement production generated over 65% of the cradle-to-end-of-construction EC; (4) The EC of the modules ranged from 3418.6 to 7730.8 kgCO2e, and structural modules generated more EC than nonstructural modules; (5) The residential area on a typical floor had significantly higher EC (626.4 kgCO2e/m2) than the communal area (410.1 kgCO2e/m2) (Zhang et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2023). Regarding cross-case comparisons, the major findings/outcomes include: (1) Concrete MiC reduces the EC at the construction stage but not necessarily achieves a lower initial EC, which is further affected by different building designs; (2) Comparing with the baseline case, both MiC case buildings generated less cradle-to-site EC emissions from structural materials; (3) Compared with the other baseline case, the two MiC case buildings generated more EC from structural materials’ production and transportation but fewer during construction. The increased material use due to the double-panel issue is a major cause for additional EC (Zhang et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2023). Regarding EC reduction measures, the major findings/outcomes include: (1) Three major approaches were identified; (2) By using both low-carbon concrete (using PFA and GGBS replacement) and structural optimization, the case MiC building could achieve the EC reduction potentials ranging from several to more than 135 kgCO2e/m2 (around 35%); (3) Addressing the “double panel” issues could reduce the cradle-to-end-of-construction EC by 47.5 kgCO2e/m2 by eliminating the nonstructural module floor and by 95.1 kgCO2e/m2 by further reducing the nonstructural walls (Zhang et al., 2022, 2024; Chen et al., 2023; Wang and Pan, 2024).

17201120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201120.value: The developed multi-level EC assessment model and proposed EC reduction measures can facilitate a more systematic EC evaluation and guide EC reduction practices for concrete MiC high-rise buildings. However, further development should be made as below: - To conduct data collection and EC assessment of more MiC building projects for cross-case EC comparison and benchmarking in HK and worldwide. The analyzed results will help identify the attributes of EC and provide more specific and meaningful suggestions for the EC reduction of different MiC building types. They will also help establish an EC database for simple and efficient EC auditing in future MiC products and projects. - To improve low-carbon structural design (LCSD) by addressing its complex and time-consuming process. The EC reduction performance by LCSD is closely related to the considered design parameters, while also constrained by many practical design issues. Therefore, LCSD of concrete MiC buildings should be further examined with more advanced structural design theories and principles. - To develop more innovative and reliable AI algorithms or models to conduct the LCSD and EC estimation. Future development can also consider other variables than structural design perspective for more accurate EC estimation and prediction of concrete MiC high-rise buildings.

17201120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201120.value: This research focused on the estimation and reduction of embodied carbon (EC) emissions of concrete high-rise residential buildings in Hong Kong built using modular integrated construction (MiC). Theoretically, it proposed a multi-level EC assessment model in a systematic approach for concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings, addressing the EC emissions at different lifecycle stages in the temporal dimension and at five different levels (i.e., material, component, module, flat, and building) in the spatial dimension. Based on the developed model, the EC emissions among concrete high-rise residential buildings that adopted MiC and conventional panelized prefabrication were cross-compared and benchmarked systematically. By reducing the EC of structural materials, design optimization of modules, structural design optimization of the global MiC building structure, and addressing the double-panel issues, the EC of concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings can be effectively decreased. Practically, the examined EC-intensive building elements and sources, the developed low-carbon structural design methods that integrate parametric structural modeling and life cycle carbon assessment, and the machine-learning based EC prediction model, altogether, extend the knowledge of EC generation, reduction and structural design of concrete MiC high-rise residential buildings. This research should help MiC professionals form effective EC reduction strategies in early project stage.

17201220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201220.value: This project will investigate distributed protocols that preserve security and privacy even when the participants or the communication network behave adversarially. We will consider various distributed settings, in which the common theme is to achieve security and privacy, while maintaining communication efficiency at the same time. The most relaxed setting that we will consider is when all parties are honest, and the adversary can observe but not corrupt data. The massively parallel computation (MPC) model is proposed to capture parallel frameworks such as MapReduce and Hadoop that handle massive data. In this model, data needs to be distributed among many machines that can process their portions locally during each round, after which they can communicate with one another. Since communication between machines is often the bottleneck for performance, communication and round complexity are the metrics to be optimized in the MPC model. In addition to developing algorithms in the MPC model, a major goal is to investigate the notion of differentially oblivious MPC algorithms, whose communication patterns between machines do not reveal sensitive information about the input data. Under the Byzantine model, each user can behave arbitrarily, which is often the case in smart contract and blockchain applications. In a distributed protocol, often users need to commit their data on the blockchain in some phase, before the next phase can proceed. As each phase can be modeled as one round of communication, the performance of such protocols is measured by their round complexity. Using our preliminary results on Byzantine agreement, each phase of such protocols can be modeled by our commit-reveal paradigm. Using cryptographic tools and concepts in game theory, we will consider protocols in which an honest player’s utility will not be harmed, even if all other players collude against that player. In a noisy communication network, transmitted bits might be corrupted. The goal here is to design a correcting mechanism whose communication overhead degrades gracefully with respect to the corruption rate. In oblivious storage applications, the servers are honest but curious about the data stored on them by the clients. The additional challenge in these scenarios is that corrupted instructions from clients in previous rounds should not compromise data privacy in subsequent rounds. In conclusion, this project will develop theoretical tools that bring insights on achieving both privacy and communication efficiency for distributed protocols, which have practical impacts on blockchain protocols and oblivious storage systems. 本課題將研究在參與者或通信網絡本身具有對抗性行為時仍能保證安全性與隱私性的分布式協議。我們將考慮多種分布式的情形，其中共同的核心目標是在保持通信效率的同時實現安全性和隱私性。條件最為寬鬆的一種情形是各通信方都是誠實的，而對手可以觀察到但不能破壞數據。人們提出大規模並行計算（massively parallel computation，MPC）模型以刻畫諸如MapReduce和Hadoop的處理大量數據的並行框架。在此模型中，數據需要在許多計算機之間分發，這些計算機可以在各輪通信間於本地處理各自的部分，然後彼此通信。由於機器之間的通信通常是性能的瓶頸，所以通信複雜度和輪次複雜度是MPC模型中要優化的指標。除了在MPC模型中設計算法外，我們的另一主要目標是研究差分無記憶的MPC算法這一概念，在這類算法中，機器之間的通信模式不會洩露有關輸入數據的敏感信息。在拜占庭模型下，每位用戶的行為可以是任意的；在智能合約和區塊鏈應用場景中通常是這種情況。在分布式協議中，用戶通常需要在某個階段將其數據提交到區塊鏈上，然後才能執行後續步驟。每個階段都可以被看作是一輪通信，因此協議的性能由其輪次複雜度來衡量。應用我們關於拜占庭協議的初步結果，此類協議的每個階段可以使用我們的提交展示範式來描述。使用密碼學工具和博弈論中的概念，我們將考慮那種即使除一位誠實玩家外的所有玩家串通起來與之對抗，該誠實玩家的利益也不會受到損害的協議。在含有噪聲的通信網絡中，傳輸的比特可能被損壞。我們的目標是設計一種糾錯機制，該機制的通信開銷隨損壞率的下降而適當降低。在無記憶存儲的應用中，服務器雖然誠實，但會希望獲取客戶端存儲在其上的數據。在該場景下的另一個難題則是在前幾輪中來自客戶端的被識破的指令不應損害後幾輪中的數據隱私。總之，本課題將開發理論工具，為在分布式協議上實現隱私性和通信效率提供深刻見解；這將對區塊鏈協議和無記憶存儲系統的實際應用產生深遠影響。

17201220.label: Realisation of objectives
17201220.value: This project aimed to advance the state of the art in secure and efficient distributed computing through three main research objectives. These objectives were as follows: first, to develop communication-efficient algorithms under the Multi-Party Computation (MPC) model that maintain privacy, even with regard to the patterns of communication between parties; second, to design distributed protocols that are resilient to Byzantine faults and fair in terms of round complexity, such that honest participants are not disadvantaged even if all others collude; and third, to construct interactive coding protocols for noisy communication networks that degrade gracefully in performance and maintain privacy even in the presence of corrupted or lost messages. The following outlines how and to what extent these objectives have been accomplished. Objective 1: Privacy-Preserving Communication-Efficient Algorithms under MPC The first objective addressed a critical challenge in secure computation. While techniques like encryption and secure multi-party computation protect the values of data, they may still leak sensitive information through access patterns and communication behaviour. To mitigate this, our work focused on the concept of differential obliviousness, which is inspired by differential privacy but designed to protect access patterns. Our starting point was the database join operation, a foundational operation in data processing. We showed that by applying the notion of differential obliviousness, it is possible to construct join algorithms that achieve near-optimal performance specific to each instance, without falling back on worst-case padding used in traditional Oblivious RAM techniques. These findings were first presented at ITC 2021. We further extended the theory in subsequent work published in the Journal of the ACM in 2022, where we provided formal definitions and analysis of differentially oblivious algorithms across various tasks, including sorting and range queries. In addition to presenting efficient algorithms, we established lower bounds that clarify the limitations of this new framework. These results create a solid foundation for practical and privacy-preserving multi-party computation protocols. Extent of achievement: This objective has been fully achieved. We introduced a new privacy framework, provided both upper and lower bounds, and demonstrated the approach’s practical viability in key computational settings. Objective 2: Fair Distributed Byzantine Protocols with Small Round Complexity The second objective focused on achieving fairness in distributed systems where some participants may act maliciously. Specifically, our goal was to ensure that the utility of honest participants remains protected even if all other participants collude. We pursued this objective through two related lines of work. First, we studied the problem of opinion dynamics in networks, where an adversary aims to bias average opinions by selectively altering agents’ resistance to persuasion. This reflects real-world scenarios where agents may be more or less stubborn in accepting influence. We examined both unbudgeted and budgeted versions of the problem, including a variant with L1-budget constraints. We showed that optimizing opinion under the L1 constraint is computationally hard. These results, presented at COCOON 2021, help illuminate the potential for adversarial manipulation and suggest how systems might defend against it. Second, we turned to the problem of leader election in distributed systems, where fairness is essential. Traditional methods achieve fairness but require many rounds of communication. In CRYPTO 2021, we proposed a class of protocols that achieve approximate game-theoretic fairness in fewer rounds. Under standard cryptographic assumptions, we demonstrated that it is possible to obtain fairness guarantees similar to those of the standard tournament-tree approach using as few as logarithmic-logarithmic rounds. This significantly improves efficiency while retaining fairness. We also contributed to the broader understanding of Byzantine Agreement, a key problem in distributed systems. In our 2023 work published in Distributed Computation, we developed protocols with subquadratic communication complexity and expected constant rounds. These protocols are resilient to adaptive adversaries, as long as certain realistic limitations are in place, such as no after-the-fact message removal. These results directly support our goal of designing protocols that remain fair and efficient even under adverse conditions. Extent of achievement: This objective has been substantially achieved. We introduced new fairness concepts, improved round efficiency, and deepened understanding of how adversaries may manipulate distributed protocols. While complete protection from collusion remains theoretically challenging, our work represents significant progress in this direction. Objective 3: Multi-Party Coding Protocols in Noisy Networks with Privacy Preservation The third objective addressed the problem of designing protocols that continue to function and maintain privacy in the presence of noise or adversarial communication disruptions. These issues are particularly relevant to large-scale systems such as federated learning and blockchain networks. First, we revisited the design of Oblivious Parallel RAM systems. These systems ensure that data access patterns do not leak sensitive information, even when executed in parallel. Our work, presented at ITC 2021, improved the expected communication overhead from previous constructions and provided an alternative with deterministic guarantees. This advancement makes perfectly oblivious computation more efficient and feasible in practical settings. Second, we tackled vector mean estimation under local differential privacy, a fundamental problem in federated analytics. We proposed algorithms tailored for sparse data, where each user contributes a vector with relatively few non-zero entries. Our algorithms achieved optimal error rates while keeping communication efficient and preserving user privacy. These contributions are particularly valuable for scalable and private data analysis. Third, we explored robust consensus protocols for permissioned blockchains, where denial-of-service and network partition attacks pose serious threats. We introduced Eges, a new consensus protocol that uses a stealth committee approach to hide the identity of actual decision-makers. This method prevents attackers from targeting key nodes and allows the system to maintain performance even under attack. Though not a classical interactive coding protocol, Eges reflects similar principles by tolerating disruptions and degrading performance gracefully. Finally, we addressed clustering in dynamic and adversarial settings. Our algorithm for k-center clustering with outliers is designed to remain effective even when points are inserted or deleted arbitrarily. This setting mimics noisy communication environments where data may be incomplete, corrupted, or frequently changing. The algorithm maintains strong approximation guarantees and low amortized update cost, aligning with the goal of graceful degradation. Extent of achievement: This objective has been fully achieved. We developed several novel constructions that ensure protocol functionality and privacy in hostile environments, spanning theoretical and applied domains. In summary, the project has successfully met its stated goals. Objective 1 was fully accomplished through the development and analysis of differentially oblivious algorithms. Objective 2 was substantially fulfilled by designing efficient and fair Byzantine protocols and exploring adversarial influence in networks. Objective 3 was fully realized through the design of robust algorithms and protocols for noisy and adversarial communication settings. The work has been supported and enriched by collaborations with leading institutions, resulting in high-impact publications and broad contributions to secure distributed computing.

17201220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201220.value: This project produced several significant contributions at the intersection of secure computation, distributed systems, and privacy-preserving communication. One major finding is the development of the differentially oblivious (DO) framework, a new notion of privacy for algorithmic access patterns. Unlike traditional Oblivious RAM (ORAM), DO allows for efficient algorithms that offer meaningful privacy without worst-case overhead. Our work showed that key primitives, such as database joins, can achieve near-optimal performance while still protecting access patterns under differential obliviousness. This result was published in ITC 2021 ("Differentially Oblivious Database Joins") and extended in JACM 2022 ("Foundations of Differentially Oblivious Algorithms"), where we formally defined the DO model and proved tight upper and lower bounds for fundamental algorithmic tasks. In the context of fair distributed protocols, we advanced the theory of game-theoretically fair leader election. Our protocol achieves approximate fairness in as few as O(log log n) rounds, a significant improvement over classical logarithmic-round solutions. These results, published in CRYPTO 2021 ("Game-Theoretic Fairness Meets Multi-party Protocols"), are the first to show that strong fairness guarantees can be preserved even under majority collusion, while maintaining low round complexity. Additionally, we explored adversarial opinion dynamics. We demonstrated the NP-hardness of optimizing susceptibility parameters under L1 budget constraints, showing the computational limits of such adversarial strategies (COCOON 2021). Further work in ACM TKDD 2022 revealed that although the objective function is non-convex, local optima coincide with global optima, enabling efficient optimization algorithms for large-scale networks. In addressing noisy and adversarial communication environments, we presented improved constructions for perfectly oblivious parallel RAM (OPRAM). Our scheme, published in ITC 2021, achieves better asymptotic overheads in both expected and deterministic settings, making OPRAM more practical for real-world use. We also introduced Eges, a consensus protocol for permissioned blockchains resilient to denial-of-service and network partition attacks. Eges ensures robust consensus via stealth committees and maintains high performance under attack conditions (Performance Evaluation 2022). Finally, our work on fully dynamic k-center clustering with outliers provides the first constant bi-criteria approximation with low amortized update costs, even under adversarial insertions and deletions (Algorithmica 2024). Collectively, these outcomes contribute novel theory, efficient algorithms, and resilient system designs, advancing secure and fair distributed computing.

17201220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201220.value: The research outcomes from this project lay a strong foundation for further exploration in privacy-preserving and resilient distributed systems. One promising direction is to extend the differentially oblivious framework to broader classes of algorithms, including graph processing and streaming, where communication patterns can still leak information. This could lead to practical tools for secure data analytics in multi-party and cloud settings. Building on our work in game-theoretic fairness, future efforts will focus on real-world deployment of fair protocols in decentralized platforms, such as blockchain governance and federated learning, where strategic manipulation is a tangible risk. Integrating cryptographic fairness with incentives and auditability remains an open and impactful challenge. The resilience of consensus protocols under real-world network threats also warrants continued development. We aim to enhance the scalability and energy-efficiency of protocols like Eges, making them suitable for IoT and edge computing environments. Lastly, our clustering and opinion dynamics results suggest broader applications in robust machine learning, where adversarial robustness, efficiency, and fairness must coexist. The proposed course of action includes strengthening interdisciplinary collaborations and pursuing targeted prototypes to validate these methods in operational systems, such as secure data platforms and collaborative AI frameworks.

17201220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201220.value: This research project aimed to enhance the security, fairness, and reliability of modern digital systems, particularly those involving multiple participants who may not all be trustworthy. In many computing environments today, sensitive data is processed and transmitted across multiple machines. Even when the data itself is encrypted, the patterns of communication can unintentionally reveal private information. Our research developed new methods to conceal these patterns, offering strong privacy protection with minimal performance cost. We also addressed the challenge of fairness in group decision-making, such as selecting a leader in a distributed system. We designed protocols that ensure honest participants are not disadvantaged, even if a majority of others attempt to cheat. These protocols are also efficient, requiring fewer communication steps than traditional methods. In addition, we created tools to maintain accurate results and system agreement even in the presence of network disruptions, attacks, or corrupted messages. This ensures that systems can function correctly and securely under real-world conditions. The outcomes of this project have broad relevance for technologies such as secure cloud computing, online collaboration, federated learning, and blockchain. They contribute to building digital infrastructure that protects individual privacy, promotes fairness, and remains robust against adversarial threats.

17201520.value: 決策過程通常涉及從一組備選方案中選擇最佳方案，但其績效尚不確定，只能通過昂貴的抽樣或仿真評估。旨在促進這種決策過程的抽樣程序的設計和分析叫做排序擇優（R＆S），它是仿真領域一個的研究重點。 在此提案中，我們將研究一類新的R＆S問題，它們由於情景決策在諸如醫療保健、電子商務和財富管理等各個領域的日益普及而廣受關注。在情境決策中，決策是根據有關所涉個人的情境或狀態的知識而定制的，這樣得出的決策通常更加有效。例如，由於認識到患者的異質性，個性化醫療旨在開出針對個體患者特徵定制的治療方案，以大幅度地提高治療效果。又例如，電子商務公司可以根據每個消費者的個人購買行為和人口統計學意義上的特點去定制產品推薦或促銷，從而增加銷售額並提高客戶滿意度。 我們將這類新的R＆S問題稱為帶協變量的排序擇優（R＆S-C)。協變量（covariates）也稱為情景信息或輔助信息。在存在協變量的條件下，每個替代方案的平均表現都隨協變量的變化而變化。因此，R＆S-C的目標是設計有效的抽樣程序，以識別為給定的協變量值指定最佳替代方案的策略（policy）。 在此提案中，我們為R＆S-C開發了一個新研究框架並提出了一個仿真模型。它的特點是協變量通過一個低維變量來影響模型的輸入。這將允許高維協變量被直接使用，無需另外構建將所有協變量作為輸入一部分的複雜仿真模型，從而大大擴展了我們方法的應用範圍。假設協變量是從一個外生過程中隨機生成的，我們將在不同條件下設計抽樣程序，包括具有高維協變量的線性模型和非參數模型。抽樣程序的形式可以是階段性的，也可以是完全序列式的。除了對價值函數（value function）進行建模外，我們還將研究另一種針對R＆S-C的方法，該方法旨在對策略函數（policy function）進行建模。新方法自然地將R＆S-C與隨機優化和梯度估計聯繫起來，將來可以為仿真領域提供許多研究機會。

17201520.label: Realisation of objectives
17201520.value: Regarding Objective (i): Ranking and selection (R&S) in stochastic simulation selects alternatives with best mean performance, assuming constant performance across alternatives. However, this approach falls short in personalized decision-making, where outcomes vary with individual characteristics, such as cancer treatments depending on patient-specific biomarkers and genetic profiles. While conventional R&S could be applied after observing individual characteristics, this approach faces limitations: decision-makers may lack access to complex simulation models, and repeated application for each individual is less efficient than developing a unified selection policy. Additionally, with high-dimensional covariates, discretizing the covariate space for simulation becomes computationally prohibitive. To address these challenges, we developed a framework for ranking and selection with covariates (R&S-C), treating mean performances as functions of covariates. This enables offline learning of performance functions followed by efficient online application, making it valuable for widespread deployment in medical decision support systems or autonomous vehicles. Our R&S-C framework examines k competing alternatives through simulation. For each alternative u (u = 1, ..., k), the performance function g(u, ξ) incorporates model uncertainty ξ, decomposed into two components: Y, which depends probabilistically on observable covariate vector X, and Z, which remains independent of X. This decomposition enables a low-dimensional variable Y to serve as input to a simplified simulation model while capturing the influence of high-dimensional covariates X on alternative performance. The framework accommodates various scenarios, such as inventory management where order quantity u represents the alternative, demand Y is influenced by covariates X (like historical sales and seasonal patterns), and Z encompasses independent factors like replenishment lead times. This approach broadens the methodology's applicability by avoiding complex simulation models that would otherwise need to directly incorporate covariates. The ultimate objective is to construct an optimal policy mapping covariate vector X to decisions that maximize the conditional expected performance E[g(u, ξ)|X]. Regarding Objective (ii): Under the assumption that the conditional expected performance E[g(u, ξ)|X] follows a linear relationship with X (or with specific basis functions of X) for each alternative u = 1, ..., k, the R&S-C problem reduces to estimating unknown linear coefficients for each alternative, as ranking k linear functions effectively determines the optimal policy. While fixed designs for covariate observations are common in computer experiment design and linear regression literature, they present limitations in our context. Fixed designs require modeling the conditional distribution of Y given X to enable simulation at arbitrary X values — a challenging task when both X and Y are multi-dimensional. Therefore, we adopt random designs, utilizing real-world observations of (X, Y) pairs. The linear assumption, however, may oversimplify the relationship between conditional expected performance and covariates. In sequential data collection and simulation experiments, model misspecification introduces an estimation bias that exacerbates over time rather than diminishing with additional data. This occurs because biased selections in a dynamic environment influence future data generation, creating a feedback loop where misspecification errors propagate through the estimation process. Without external corrective information, this cascading effect can lead to severely suboptimal policies. To address the estimation bias, we examine model misspecification through the lens of endogeneity issues in econometrics literature and employ instrumental variable (IV) regression for bias correction. By integrating IV regression techniques with standard online learning algorithms such as greedy and UCB (Upper Confidence Bound), we develop sequential selection algorithms that overcome the endogeneity problem. These IV-based algorithms achieve dual objectives: they successfully identify the optimal policy while maintaining low regret bounds. Regarding Objective (iii): We have conducted two studies for R&S-C under nonparametric models. In our first study, we assume each alternative's conditional expected performance lies in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), allowing for complex performance-covariate relationships without specific parametric forms. When the covariates are high-dimensional, this approach naturally encounters the curse of dimensionality, where sample requirements for accurate function estimation and policy identification grow exponentially with covariate dimensionality. To mitigate this challenge, we adopt a sparse additive model for each performance function, comprising a small number of nonzero components relative to dimensionality, with each component being a general function in certain RKHS. For sequentially arriving independent covariate observations, we develop a selection procedure that combines nonparametric estimation via doubly penalized methods with a novel sequential screening mechanism balancing exploration and exploitation. The procedure achieves sublinear cumulative regret over time horizon while maintaining logarithmic scaling with covariate dimensionality. Our second study extends to general contextual stochastic optimization problems, encompassing continuous decision variables and R&S-C problems as special cases. We analyze weighted sample average approximation (wSAA), examining its statistical properties in solving contextual stochastic optimization through nonparametric estimation of conditional expected performance functions. The analysis proceeds in two stages. First, we establish central limit theorems for wSAA estimates of optimal values under exact solution conditions, quantifying how estimation uncertainty scales with covariate sample size. Second, we examine scenarios with computational budget constraints, revealing a fundamental tradeoff between statistical accuracy and computational cost as samples increase. Through central limit theorems for budget-constrained wSAA estimates, we characterize this statistical-computational tradeoff precisely and develop “over-optimizing” strategies that ensure valid statistical inference. Regarding Objective (iv): When the optimal policy belongs to a parametric function class u(x; θ), the R&S-C problem reduces to maximizing the unconditional expected cost E[g(u(X; θ), ξ)] with respect to θ, where the expectation considers the joint distribution of (X, ξ). This stochastic optimization can be solved using stochastic approximation (SA) schemes, including stochastic gradient descent and Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithms. To handle temporally correlated data observations of (X, ξ), we analyze SA's finite-sample performance in a general framework permitting adaptive data collection. Our analysis yields two key results: a finite-sample bound on the SA iterate's mean squared error, and a concentration bound guaranteeing that SA iterates' sample paths remain within a polynomially shrinking ball with probability approaching one at a polynomial rate. We prove this polynomial rate is optimal, as it cannot be improved in general. These results emerge from novel proof techniques combining backward recursive coupling and polynomial chaining. Note regarding PhD student training: My student Ms Wang Yanyuan is expected to complete her PhD in Spring 2026. She began her doctoral studies in 2020 at University of Hong Kong, where I worked at the time, and transferred to HKUST in 2023 to continue her research under my supervision. Despite facing challenges from both the Covid pandemic and the inter-university transfer, she has demonstrated exceptional scholarly abilities. Her strong intellectual capabilities, sense of responsibility, and excellent interpersonal skills position her well for a successful academic career.

17201520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201520.value: First, when the conditional expected performance is misspecified as a linear model, sequential data collection and simulation experiments introduce an estimation bias that compounds rather than diminishes over time. Drawing from econometrics, we address this bias through instrumental variable (IV) regression and develop algorithms that integrate IV techniques with standard online learning approaches like greedy and UCB methods. These IV-based algorithms both identify optimal policies and maintain low regret bounds, effectively solving the endogeneity problem. The working paper "Dynamic Selection in Algorithmic Decision-making" is currently under review. Second, we assume each alternative's conditional expected performance lies in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). To address the curse of dimensionality arising from high-dimensional covariates while retaining the modeling capability to capture complex performance-covariate relationships, we consider sparse additive models with few nonzero components for the performance function. Our selection procedure combines doubly penalized estimation with sequential screening, achieving sublinear regret while scaling logarithmically with dimensionality. The working paper “Sparse Additive Contextual Bandits: A Nonparametric Approach for Online Decision-making with High-dimensional Covariates” is currently under review. Third, we examine weighted sample average approximation (wSAA) in general contextual stochastic optimization which include R&S-C as special cases. We establish central limit theorems for optimal value estimation and analyze the tradeoff between statistical accuracy and computational cost under budget constraints, developing “over-optimizing” strategies for valid statistical inference. The working paper “Statistical Inference for Weighted Sample Average Approximation in Contextual Stochastic Optimization,” currently under review. Fourth, assuming the performance function belongs to a parametric function class, we reduce R&S-C to stochastic optimization solvable via stochastic approximation (SA). Our analysis of SA under temporally correlated, adaptively collected data yields two optimal bounds: a finite-sample bound on mean squared error and a sharp concentration bound showing SA iterates remain within a polynomially shrinking ball with probability approaching one at an unimprovable polynomial rate. These results derive from novel proof techniques combining backward recursive coupling and polynomial chaining. The working paper “Finite-time Analysis of Adaptive Markovian Stochastic Approximation: Mean Squared Errors and Sharp Concentration Bounds” is currently under review. Lastly, our methods developed for R&S-C problems proved applicable to broader simulation-optimization challenges beyond finite solution sets. This led to our tutorial paper "Surrogate-based Simulation Optimization," which explores the integration of machine learning models in simulation optimization over continuous domains. The work gained recognition as a one-hour tutorial at the 2021 INFORMS Annual Meeting and was subsequently published as a book chapter in "Emerging Optimization Methods and Modeling Techniques with Applications," part of the INFORMS TuTorials in Operations Research series.

17201520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201520.value: The project's findings in personalized decision-making can be extended by incorporating risk considerations, moving beyond mean performance to more sophisticated risk measures such as quantiles and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). This extension would be particularly valuable in domains where extreme outcomes are critical, such as healthcare and financial decisions. The research would require several key developments. First, the existing methodological framework must be adapted to handle risk measures, necessitating new theoretical advances in sequential learning. Second, efficient computational methods for risk-aware decision-making must be developed, addressing the inherent challenges of non-linear risk measures. Third, the instrumental variable approach needs extension to handle risk measures under sequential data collection. Fourth, the statistical-computational tradeoffs specific to risk-based optimization require careful study. Finally, investigation of sparse structures in risk measures for high-dimensional problems would maintain computational efficiency. The research could proceed sequentially: establishing theoretical foundations for risk-aware sequential learning, developing computational algorithms, applying to specific domains like healthcare and finance, and ultimately integrating into existing decision support systems. This extension would significantly enhance the practical impact of the research, particularly in risk-sensitive applications.

17201520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201520.value: This research project advances personalized decision-making in complex systems where outcomes depend on individual characteristics. Imagine selecting the best treatment for each patient or optimizing delivery routes based on traffic conditions — these decisions require understanding how different factors affect outcomes. The project tackles several key challenges in making such decisions. First, it develops methods to correct biases that occur when collecting data adaptively over time but under a misspecified model, similar to how economists handle market data. Second, it creates efficient ways to learn from past experiences with minimal model assumptions while keeping computational costs manageable, especially when dealing with high-dimensional individual characteristics (like multiple patient symptoms or various traffic factors). The research also addresses practical concerns about computational resources and accuracy. When computing power is limited, we developed strategies to balance calculation speed with decision quality. They proved their methods work reliably and efficiently, even in challenging situations where data points are correlated rather than independent. The results have broad applications in healthcare, logistics, and other fields requiring automated decision-making. The methods are particularly valuable when decisions must be made quickly using complex data, ensuring both accuracy and computational efficiency.

17201620.label: Project Objectives
17201620.value: The first objective of the project is to achieve high-speed digital holography with the use of a neuromorphic imager. This involves setting up the phase-shifting digital holographic imaging, reading the data asynchronously from the sensor, and processing them for image reconstruction. We aim at demonstrating a bandwidth equivalent to a 10-fold increase in frame rate from a conventional CMOS sensor. The image reconstruction can be model-based and does not have to be real time, but should allow a user to specify the desired sectional image that corresponds to a particular axial distance and time. The second objective of the project is to enhance the image quality and speed through computational advances. The first part is to develop efficient denoising algorithms to suppress the artifacts of unwanted event triggering. The second part is to develop machine learning techniques, such as spiking neural network, for end-to-end holographic image reconstruction. This should significantly speed up the image sectioning, and we aim to achieve close to real-time processing. The third part is to further improve the image quality through combining model-based reconstruction with deep learning for the image prior. The aim is to show a reconstruction quality that is indistinguishable from that using a traditional electronic sensor, while operating at an equivalent of 10 times higher frame rate. The third objective of the project is to demonstrate the use of the high-speed holographic imaging in biomedical applications. We aim to combine it with a microfluidics channel, and showcase cell imaging in the flow. We will investigate two main tasks: pattern analysis on the cell images, which aims as phenotype classification, and tracking. Our goal is to show the unique capabilities of our neuromorphic holography system in high-speed 3D imaging, and make it a viable tool for further scientific explorations.

17201620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201620.value: Conventional cameras can be extremely slow when it comes to capturing many chemical processes and biological phenomena. A bottleneck has been with the electronic sensors. Whether they are based on CCD or CMOS technology, the typical frame rate does not exceed hundreds of frames per second. Faster video cameras exist, but at a much higher cost. Others achieve ultrafast imaging through customized designs of the optical system, and the data are captured with dedicated devices such as high-sampling-rate electronic digitizers or streak cameras. However, the complex setups generally limit their portability and integration with other imaging techniques. In this proposal, we pursue an alternative path, and set our sights on high-speed holographic imaging that can deliver three-dimensional information of the object under study. Neuromorphic imagers, or silicon retinas, are event sensors that capture brightness change asynchronously and independently on a pixel-by-pixel basis. They represent a paradigm shift from traditional frame-based sensors, and can deliver the equivalent of megahertz readout rates. The burden, however, is on computation, demanding innovation in algorithms to convert the collection of events into images. We push this further by coupling the neuromorphic sensor with a holographic imaging setup, in order to capture the optical wavefront at a high temporal resolution. We then design novel computational algorithms to recover sectional images of high spatial resolution, both laterally and axially. The challenges are threefold: first is the low-level data processing, specifically the suppression of noise that is a prevalent issue with event sensors. As sectional image reconstruction in digital holography is an ill-posed inverse imaging problem, guarding against noise amplification is non-trivial and requires customized techniques. Second, speed of the computational reconstruction must be commensurate with the fast data capture. Learning-based techniques, often involving heavy computation in training but relatively fast execution, represent a suitable approach for this purpose. In essence, this is neuromorphic computing for neuromorphic sensing. Third, in certain applications, the ultimate goal is not to have high spatial and temporal images, but pattern analysis on such images. The uncharted territory is to demonstrate, as a proof-of-concept, the feasibility to do so from the raw sensor output. We aim to apply our novel neuromorphic holography system for flow imaging, with biological cells moving through microfluidic channels. We believe that achieving high-speed, high-resolution volumetric imaging and classification of the cells will bring new biological insights and lead to further uses of this technology in various applications. 傳統相機在捕獲許多化學過程和生物現象時非常慢。影響其速度的瓶頸在於電子傳感器。無論它們是基於CCD還是CMOS技術，一般幀速率都不會超過每秒數百幀。可以使用更快的攝像機，但它們的成本要高得多。還有的通過定制光學系統來實現超快成像，並使用專用設備，如高采樣率電子數字轉換器或條紋相機，來採集數據。但是，複雜的裝置通常也限制其便攜性以及與其他成像技術的可集成性。 在此份研究計劃中，我們尋求另一種途徑，着眼於研究物體的三維的高速全息成像。神經形態成像儀，或矽視網膜是能夠異步且獨立地逐像素捕獲亮度變化的事件傳感器。它們體現了從傳統的基於幀的傳感器的範式轉變，並且能夠達到兆赫茲級的讀出速率。然而這對計算帶來了負擔，要求對捕捉事件轉換為圖像的算法進行創新。我們進一步將神經形態傳感器與全息成像裝置結合，以便在高時間分辨率下捕獲光波前。然後，我們設計了一種新的算法，來恢復橫向和軸向上的高空間分辨率的截面圖像。挑戰有三個方面：首先是底層數據處理，特別是抑制事件傳感器普遍存在噪聲問題。由於數字全息中的截面圖像重建是一個不適定的逆成像問題，防止噪聲放大並不容易並且需要特定技術。第二，計算重建的速度必須與快速的數據捕獲相匹配。基於學習的技術通常會在訓練階段涉及大量計算，但在執行階段速度相對較快，是一種合適的方法。本質上，這是用於神經形態感應的神經形態計算。第三，在某些應用中，最終目標不是獲得高空間和時間圖像，而是對此類圖像進行模式分析。從原始傳感器輸出達到此目標的可行性仍然未被驗證。我們的目標是將新型神經形態全息系統應用於生物細胞通過微流體通道的流動成像。我們相信，通過實現對細胞的高速高分辨率體積成像和分類，能夠帶來新的生物學見解，並使該技術在各種應用中有進一步的應用。

17201620.label: Realisation of objectives
17201620.value: This project consists of 3 objectives: achieving high-speed digital holography with the use of a neuromorphic imager, enhancing image quality with denoising algorithms and machine learning techniques, and demonstrating the use of the high-speed holographic imaging in biomedical applications. These objectives have been realized with the conclusion of this project. Regarding the first objective, we reported a 40% completion in the mid-term progress report. As explained in that report, we developed event-based laser speckle imaging with low latency and high temporal resolution, and computational methods that made use of speckle correlation for micro motion estimation. Continuing this momentum, we further broke ground in achieving millisecond autofocusing microscopy using neuromorphic sensing. Our approach could detect the sparse brightness changes asynchronously and respond to the specimen displacement efficiently. With an effective autofocusing algorithm to process the event data, we demonstrated autofocusing in only tens of milliseconds, which was substantially faster than existing technologies. The work was first presented in the Optica Computational Optical Sensing and Imaging as part of the Imaging Congress in July 2022, where we focused on photon-limited conditions, and later expanded into a journal paper published in the Optics and Lasers in Engineering in 2023 (see the list of publications in the section below). Regarding the second objective, we also reported a 40% completion in the mid-term progress report. A major challenge with neuromorphic imaging is that the event data captured are very noisy. Because events are generated in accordance with changes in intensity, environmental causes such as illumination flickering can trigger unwanted event data. Their presence, particularly if such noise was abundant, could affect the subsequent processing, such as autofocusing accuracy as developed above. Thus, we devoted substantial efforts in this reporting period to develop effective denoising algorithms. They cumulated into two major methods. First was a method using density-based spatiotemporal denoising. The basic premise was that real event data and noise had different spatiotemporal profiles or statistics, in the sense that the former tended to be clustered in space-time, while the latter was more scattered. To differentiate them, we developed a sub-quadratic clustering algorithm that coupled event priors with density estimation for noise removal on raw event streams, with strongly correlated signals taken to be denser in space-time. The work was published in IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging in May 2023. Second, we took advantage of the fact that some existing event cameras captured both frame and event data simultaneously. Noting their complementarity, we pioneered a scheme with joint image deblurring and event denoising. An event-regularized prior offered precise high-frequency structures and dynamic features for blind deblurring, while image gradients served as reliable supervision in regulating neuromorphic noise removal. The resulting method showed greater robustness to challenging realistic scenarios such as varying levels of illumination, contrast and motion magnitude. It was published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing in March 2024. Regarding the third objective, we reported a 25% completion in the mid-term progress report. As explained in the proposal, we aimed to combine high-speed imaging enabled by event camera with a microfluidic channel, where cells flowed through in the field of view of the imaging system. For this, we developed a computational scheme to deal with the high turbulence commonly found in fluidic flow. The result was an angle-based neuromorphic wave normal sensing, where we incorporated adaptive optics to achieve imaging and tracking under fast-changing turbulence. The full paper was recently accepted to a journal as early view; furthermore, we discussed this in an invited presentation in SPIE Photonics West, under the conference track of Computational Optical Imaging and Artificial Intelligence in Biomedical Sciences, in January 2024.

rows: The first objective of the project is to achieve high-speed digital holography with the use of a neuromorphic imager. This involves setting up the phase-shifting digital holographic imaging, reading the data asynchronously from the sensor, and processing them for image reconstruction. We aim at demonstrating a bandwidth equivalent to a 10-fold increase in frame rate from a conventional CMOS sensor. The image reconstruction can be model-based and does not have to be real time, but should allow a user to specify the desired sectional image that corresponds to a particular axial distance and time.

The second objective of the project is to enhance the image quality and speed through computational advances. The first part is to develop efficient denoising algorithms to suppress the artifacts of unwanted event triggering. The second part is to develop machine learning techniques, such as spiking neural network, for end-to-end holographic image reconstruction. This should significantly speed up the image sectioning, and we aim to achieve close to real-time processing. The third part is to further improve the image quality through combining model-based reconstruction with deep learning for the image prior. The aim is to show a reconstruction quality that is indistinguishable from that using a traditional electronic sensor, while operating at an equivalent of 10 times higher frame rate.

The third objective of the project is to demonstrate the use of the high-speed holographic imaging in biomedical applications. We aim to combine it with a microfluidics channel, and showcase cell imaging in the flow. We will investigate two main tasks: pattern analysis on the cell images, which aims as phenotype classification, and tracking. Our goal is to show the unique capabilities of our neuromorphic holography system in high-speed 3D imaging, and make it a viable tool for further scientific explorations.

17201620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201620.value: In this project, the major findings and research outcome center on achieving high-speed holographic imaging through computational neuromorphic imaging, i.e., the use of an event sensor combined with computational algorithms. In recent years, event sensors have shown to be a powerful addition to various emerging electronic sensors, known in particular for its capability to capture fast dynamics. However, while the event signals contain useful information, extracting such information is not trivial, in part due to a very different nature or statistics of such signals, and in part due to extensive noise. As such, our work is significant because we developed effective and efficient event denoising algorithms in order to highlight the event signals. (Details of these denoising methods are given in the relevant research publications in Part C, entitled Neuromorphic imaging with density-based spatiotemporal denoising and Neuromorphic imaging with joint image deblurring and event denoising, respectively.) Moreover, we also demonstrated important uses of such event data in optical microscopy, namely, in micro motion estimation and in millisecond autofocusing microscopy. (See the publications entitled Event-based laser speckle correlation for micro motion estimation and Millisecond autofocusing microscopy using neuromorphic event sensing, in Part C.) In addition, such technological advancement was tied to 3D imaging through holographic capture and reconstruction, in order to enable imaging with microfluidic flow. Early on, we demonstrated holographic 3D particle reconstruction (Holographic 3D particle reconstruction using a one-stage network, in Part C), and more recently, we summarized the development in flow imaging and microfluidics in an invited conference presentation (Computational neuromorphic imaging: principles and applications, in Part C) as well as further journal manuscripts.

17201620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201620.value: The research has room for further development on a couple of directions. In terms of algorithmic developments, the speed of denoising has room for improvement, particularly because newer event sensors have higher spatial and potentially higher temporal resolutions as well, leading to a greater amount of event data in a shorter period of time. In terms of applications, flow imaging with microfluidics has a lot of uses, from imaging cells in biomedicine to environmental monitoring through inspecting pollutants in water. Each presents different challenges, such as scattering and density of the objects of interest, and leveraging advances in event sensing technology for such applications require continuous development of innovative computational algorithms. We aim to foster further collaborations with researchers both in the electronic sensor community and in the targeted application areas to continue to amplify the impact we have made with this project.

17201620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201620.value: Conventional cameras have significant limitations in capturing fast dynamics, primarily because of the nature of the sensors where the scene is recorded frame by frame. Unfortunately, that can be a significant hurdle in optical microscopy, particularly when imaging flow. In this project, we successfully demonstrated high-speed holographic imaging through a technology called computational neuromorphic imaging, where an emerging form of electronic sensor called event sensor was combined with computational algorithms we developed, in order to record 3D signals in a holographic manner. We overcame challenges in dealing with very noisy event sensors, and showed how such technology can lead to micro motion detection and fast autofocusing, which enabled imaging and tracking in microfluid flow.

17201820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201820.value: Many practical systems, such as biological systems and transportation networks, possess the property that the input, internal state and output are all nonnegative. Such systems are often referred to as positive systems, and their applications have been found in modeling compartmental networks, population evolution, chemical reactors, and gene regulation. Conventional analysis and synthesis techniques of positive systems usually ignore the saturation effects arising from the hard limit of actuators/sensors in the physical systems. Existing semi-definite programming based approaches dealing with positivity-preserving control under saturating input are often handicapped when large-scale networked systems are encountered. Therefore, it is imperative to propose a new framework for the control design of positive systems subject to input saturation. In this project, the analysis and synthesis problems of interconnected positive systems with constrained inputs will be tackled. The concept of ``local'' positivity, describing the situation where the invariant set is merely part of the nonnegative orthant, will be first put forward. The global and local stability of positive systems in the presence of saturating inputs will then be studied. Specifically, the domain of attraction with the aid of novel invariant sets will be estimated, and linear-programming-based optimal control algorithms with low conservatism will be established. Building on this, we will further investigate the distributed control of interconnected positive systems with actuator saturation. The small gain theorem based on an operator-theoretic approach in nonlinear systems will be established, and scalable algorithms for both controller synthesis and network topology design, using only local information of the subsystems, will be developed. Besides the stability issue of interconnected positive systems, the consensus problem of positive multi-agent systems will also be investigated. To tackle the consensus problem of directed networks, a modified algebraic Riccati inequality approach and a new system augmentation framework will be proposed for positive multi-agent networks. Then by generalizing the saturation results for a single dynamic system to multiple dynamic systems, the positive consensus problem of multi-agent systems with input saturation will be addressed. Finally, the newly established distributed control algorithms will be applied to vehicle platooning and formation control of multiple quadrotors. There is a strong prospect that this project will not only develop control techniques with improved solvability and lower cost for large-scale positive delay systems, but also provide new insights into the modeling and analysis of other related areas, including cooperative control of multi-agent systems, coordination of multiple robots, and power control of wireless sensor networks. 許多實際系統具有輸入、內部狀態和輸出均非負的性質，如生物系統和交通網絡。這類系統通常被稱作正系統，在房室網絡，人口演化，化學反應和基因調控等領域的建模中有著廣泛的應用。傳統的正系統的分析與綜合技術往往忽略了物理系統中執行器或傳感器的硬件限制所產生的飽和效應。現有的正性約束下的飽和控制方法通常基於半定規劃，不適用於大規模網絡。因此，針對具有輸入飽和的正系統提出新的控制系統設計架構是一個亟待解決的問題。本項目擬研究輸入受限情形下的互聯正系統分析與綜合問題。首先，項目將提出局部正性的概念，用以描述不變集只是第一象限一部分的情形，進而研究具有飽和輸入的正系統的全域穩定性和局部穩定性問題。具體地，我們將借助新的不變集類型估計吸引域，建立基於線性規劃的低保守性優化控制算法。基於此，我們將研究執行器飽和情形下互聯正系統的分布式控制問題。我們將建立基於算子理論的非線性系統小增益定理，並且僅利用子系統的局部信息建立可尺度化的控制器和網絡拓撲結構設計算法。除了考慮互聯正系統的穩定性問題之外，我們還將研究具有正性約束的多智能體系統一致性問題。為了研究有向網絡的一致性問題，我們將針對正多智能體網絡提出一種改進的代數黎卡提不等式方法和一個新的系統增廣框架。然後，我們將具有飽和約束的單個系統的結論推廣到大規模系統，研究具有輸入飽和的多智能體系統的正一致性問題。最後，我們將新建立的分布式控制算法應用於車輛編隊和多旋翼飛行器的編隊控制。本項目具有廣闊的應用前景，不僅對大規模時滯正系統建立了可解性高且成本低的控制技術，而且為相關應用領域的建模和分析提供了新穎的見解，如多智能體協同控制，多機器人協作以及無線網絡功率控制。

17201820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201820.value: Systematic methodologies have been developed for the stability and synthesis of diverse positive systems with or without input saturation. These methodologies cover attraction domain estimation, stability analysis, input-output gain characterization, controller design, and consensus of positive multi-agent systems (MASs). A major contribution is the development of advanced techniques for attraction domain estimation of positive systems under saturation constraints. For positive linear mixed fractional-order systems under time-varying delays, the problem has been treated within the asymptotic Lyapunov stability framework [1]. Novel bounding methods and geometric-shape invariants have been applied to reduce conservativeness and enhance performance [2, 6]. Input-output gains have been characterized for discrete-time and continuous-time positive periodic systems, revealing a dual relationship between these gains [3]. These findings have been extended to periodic piecewise positive systems [5] and cone-preserving systems, a generalization of positive systems [15, 20]. Geometric programming-based algorithms have been developed for optimizing multi-input-multi-output gains [13, 16]. Controllers have been designed for single positive systems, guaranteeing desired performance. Proportional-derivative (PD) controllers have been proposed for continuous and discrete-time positive systems [4, 10, 19]. Interval observers and state-estimate feedback controllers have been co-designed for Markov jump systems with interval uncertainties [7]. For periodic piecewise positive systems, a state-feedback controller has been designed using a time-scheduled copositive Lyapunov function [14], which has been extended to the interconnected case, with a primal-dual iterative algorithm developed for the solution [18]. The consensus problem has been studied for positive MASs under undirected and directed graphs. Edge consensus criteria have been improved for the undirected case using slack matrix variables [11]. Output-feedback and state-feedback controllers have been devised to handle consensus in undirected graphs [12] and directed graphs with spanning trees [8, 9], respectively. These methods have been extended to fractional-order MASs [17].

17201820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201820.value: The project has yielded several significant outcomes, offering promising avenues for future exploration and enhancement. 1. Developing robust reliability for positive systems subject to uncertainties or component faults. Challenges can arise from environmental changes or equipment ageing, which critically influence the stability and performance of positive systems. Consequently, a robust control design ensures dependable operation and functionality. 2. Investigating the positive finite-time consensus problem for positive multiagent systems. This problem ensures that the agents can agree on a desired value within a specific finite time. This is crucial for timely decisions in applications such as autonomous vehicle coordination, sensor networks and robotic swarms. Further exploration of this topic can advance consensus technologies in real-world scenarios. 3. Exploring the analysis and controller design for complex positive systems with nonlinearity or fractional order. Nonlinearity complicates analysis, as conventional linear control methods are often inapplicable. Fractional-order systems leverage non-integer-order derivatives for a refined dynamic representation. The unique traits of nonlinear fractional-order positive systems present stability determination challenges. Thus, advancing control methodologies for general positive systems can significantly expand their applicability. Ongoing research in positive systems continues to yield valuable insights and practical solutions applicable across diverse domains.

17201820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201820.value: The increasing recognition of positive systems, characterized by nonnegative inputs, internal states, and outputs, has highlighted their significance in practical applications. Since traditional analysis methods often fail to account for the saturation effects caused by actuator and sensor limitations, this project seeks to establish a new framework for the control design of positive systems subject to input saturation. Key achievements include studying positive systems' global and local stability under saturating inputs, estimating the domain of attraction using novel invariant sets, and developing linear programming-based optimal control algorithms with minimal conservatism. Building on these advancements, distributed control strategies have been explored for interconnected positive systems, leveraging a small gain theorem derived from operator-theoretic approaches. Furthermore, the consensus problem in positive multi-agent systems has been tackled using a modified algebraic Riccati inequality approach and a new system augmentation framework. By extending saturation results from single to multiple dynamic systems, the input saturation in multi-agent consensus scenarios has been addressed, with these approaches further applied to vehicle platooning and formation control of quadrotors. This project’s outcomes are intended to offer fresh perspectives on the modelling and analysis of various related fields, promising enhanced solvability and cost-effectiveness for large-scale positive delay systems.
