17202020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202020.value: Urbanisation dramatically changes natural catchment characteristics by increasing impervious areas and creating drainage systems. These anthropogenic activities, therefore, result in significant adverse hydro-bio-ecological effects, such as flash runoff, reduced natural stormwater storage, and deteriorated stormwater quality. To mitigate these adverse effects, stormwater management techniques such as Blue-Green Infrastructures (BGIs), including stormwater ponds, bio-retention cells etc., have been increasingly considered as effective options. In past decades, a variety of studies have been conducted on the local-scale effects of BGIs via monitoring or simplified hydrological modelling. However, the benefits of BGIs vary not only by their different forms, but also at spatial and temporal scales. Systems within a system may interact with each other, and a measure may lose its effectiveness after a period of usage. This suggests there is a need to upscale local-scale evaluations to broader catchment-scale effects and to explore the benefits from the short-term to the lifespan of BGIs. The aim of the proposed research is to develop an evidence-based understanding for BGIs’ performances on stormwater management at multiple spatio-temporal scales by using bottom-up dynamic modelling supported by field data. The overarching research question is how BGIs work individually and interact with grey infrastructures to influence stormwater runoff management at the catchment scale. This will be achieved by developing a robust dynamic model, which is capable of modelling BGI performance at the local level and upscaled to the broader catchment scale, as well as making systematic multi-scale evaluations. We will first develop a reliable dynamic modelling tool to reproduce the physical processes of rainfall, runoff, and associated transport over urban areas and BGIs in there. By overcoming the identified challenges, our developed in-house modelling tool will then be applied to a catchment study with the support of good-quality field data. Evaluation of the multi-scale performance of BGIs will be conducted by building up detailed simulations of a variety of defined scenarios. We will then test the developed approaches in a case study (Anderson Road Quarry Site) in Hong Kong where a variety of BGIs are being used. Building on these results, we will finally draw key conclusions regarding the usage and performance of BGIs under different climate conditions, as well as systematically develop a better understanding of stormwater runoff management using BGIs at the multi-scale. The research findings will lead to generic approaches for sustainable urban stormwater management that can be applied anywhere around the world. 城市化通過增加不透水面積和建立排水系統，極大地改變了自然流域的特徵。這些人為活動會導致水文生態不利影響，例如洪水的發生、減少天然雨水蓄積的減少和雨水水質的惡化。為了減輕這些不利影響，諸如藍綠色基礎設施（BGI）之類的雨水管理技術，包括雨水池塘，生物保留池等，已被視為有效的城市雨洪管理選擇。在過去的幾十年中，已經通過監測或簡化的水文模型對BGI的局部規模效應進行了各種研究。但是，BGI的表現不僅因其形式不同而異，而且在空間和時間尺度上也不同。城市系統中的子系統可能會彼此交互，並且在使用一段時間後，一種措施可能會失去其有效性。這表明有必要對當地規模的評估進行升級，以擴大集水區規模的影響，並探討短期，長期使用BGI的益處。 本項目的研究目的是通過使用現場數據支持的動態模型，對BGI在多個時空尺度上的雨水管理績效進行循證理解。首要的研究問題是BGI如何單獨工作以及如何與灰色基礎設施交互以影響集水區規模的雨水徑流管理。這將通過開發穩健的水動力模型來實現，該模型能夠在BGI的局部性能進行建模，並擴大到更廣泛的流域規模，並進行系統的多尺度評估。我們將首先開發一種可靠的水動力建模工具，以模擬降雨、徑流以及相關污染物輸移的物理過程。開發的模型將應用於流域尺度的研究。 BGI的多尺度性能評估將通過建立各種已定義場景的詳細模擬來進行。然後，我們將在香港BGI的案例研究中測試開發出的方法。研究結果可用於指導世界各地的可持續城市雨水管理。

17202020.label: Realisation of objectives
17202020.value: The project identified four objectives, all of which have been fully achieved. Specifically: To achieve Objective 1, we developed a grid-based hydrodynamic model for rainfall-induced stormwater flows over complex surfaces, including various infrastructures such as flood retention lakes and urban streets with manholes. The model has been validated and tested through a variety of case studies. Using the model in a set of hypothetical scenarios, we investigated how the spatial distribution of urban drainage inlets affects stormwater flow dynamics and discharge. This research has resulted in a publication in a top-tier journal, the Journal of Hydrology (JCR Q1). Furthermore, we developed a novel meshless model based on Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics coupled with the Two-Component Pressure Approach (SPH-TPA) to simulate transient mixed flows of stormwater within urban drainage systems. This model offers improved accuracy and stability compared to the traditional Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) and provides an alternative tool for investigating transient mixed stormwater flows in urban drainage networks. This work has been published in another JCR Q1 journal, Water Resources Management. To achieve Objectives 2 and 3, we conducted multiple parallel studies. First, we used the developed model to build a detailed flood hydrodynamic model for a case study in the upper catchment of the Shenzhen River Stage V, where a blue–green infrastructure (BGI) flood retention lake has been implemented for river flood regulation. By performing catchment-scale simulations and assessments of a series of rainfall-induced stormwater flood scenarios, we demonstrated how catchment-scale rainfall–flood modelling with BGIs is sensitive to model parameters and how the performance of flood retention lakes is affected by their configuration and climatic conditions. These findings have been published in a top journal, Water Resources Research (JCR Q1). Second, we evaluated stormwater system performance incorporating integrated BGIs, in-sewer storage capacity, and real-time control (RTC) strategies at a pilot study site. The results showed that BGIs play a major role in mitigating peak flows and high runoff volumes, whereas adding RTC to storage units and in-sewer flow control mainly improves performance under relatively small rainfall events. This study has been published in a reputable journal, the Journal of Hydrologic Engineering (ASCE). To achieve Objective 4, we conducted several studies on stormwater flow quantity and quality. Using an urban basin in southern Finland as an example, we examined the hydrological response of an urban catchment to climate change and urbanization through process-based urban hydrological modelling and statistical analysis under Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP) 4.5 and 8.5. Focusing on Hong Kong, we also investigated the relationship between urban construction activities and stormwater quality in the Anderson Quarry Site Development, providing insights into the assessment, temporal variations, and key variables associated with the impact of construction works on streamflow water quality. In addition, we studied how urbanization affects downstream urban river water quality in Hong Kong, thereby advancing understanding of the relationship between urbanization and stormwater quality in a subtropical climate. These studies have resulted in four journal articles in the Journal of Hydrology (JCR Q1) and Science of the Total Environment.

17202020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202020.value: 1. To develop a grid-based hydrodynamic modelling tool for rainfall-induced stormwater flows over complex surfaces, including various infrastructures such as flood retention lakes and urban streets with manholes. 2. To develop a novel meshless model based on Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics coupled with the Two-Component Pressure Approach (SPH-TPA) to simulate transient mixed stormwater flows within urban drainage systems. 3. The performance of flood retention lakes (RLs) exhibits an L-shaped band of satisfactory performance in the frequency–duration diagram. When operating jointly, RLs in series configurations are more effective in reducing mainstream flood peaks, whereas parallel configurations provide a greater spatial extent of flood hazard mitigation. For both series and parallel layouts, upstream-weighted configurations tend to outperform downstream-weighted ones under more extreme events. In addition, decentralized arrangements within urban areas yield greater benefits for spatial flood hazard mitigation than centralized configurations. 4. Blue–green infrastructures (BGIs) play a major role in mitigating peak flows and high runoff volumes, whereas adding real-time control (RTC) to storage units and in-sewer flow control mainly improves performance under relatively small rainfall events. 5. To propose a novel approach to correlate water quality with construction works, improving the strength of inferred causality by 45% compared to existing methods. Construction works impact stream water quality via dissolved and suspended solids, and key construction signatures increase stormwater temperature and pH. 6. It is also found that the dominant portion of urban streamflow shifts from summer to autumn in the future under both RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Urbanization has a direct impact on hydrological response through changes in imperviousness, but climate change has a more significant influence on the seasonal distribution of urban streamflow. Additionally, urbanization, together with climate change, reduces the magnitude of monthly streamflow differences.

17202020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202020.value: Urbanisation dramatically alters natural catchment characteristics by increasing impervious areas and introducing drainage systems, resulting in significant adverse hydro-bio-ecological effects on stormwater quality and quantity. Blue–Green Infrastructures (BGIs) are increasingly recognised as effective options for stormwater management. Through this project, we have systematically developed evidence-based understanding of the impacts of urbanisation and climate change on urban stormwater, as well as how BGIs can help mitigate these adverse effects at various spatiotemporal scales and under different climate scenarios. The research findings have led to generic models and approaches, as well as first-hand datasets for sustainable urban stormwater management that can be transferred and applied worldwide.

17203020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203020.value: Efficient and reliable building facilities are vital to a society and citizens’ well-being. Of various emerging technologies, digital twin is regarded as a promising concept to revolutionize the manufacturing, planning and operation of a product, system or city. While NASA, General Electric and Singapore have been promoting digital twin as a disruptive paradigm to implement smart city, industrial 4.0 and digital business, it is imperative to explore how digital twin can be utilized to manage the built environment to enhance the performance, reliability, efficiency, cost saving and occupant experience. Increasing the operational intelligence of building facilities through digital twin pose grand challenges in data collection and integration, modeling and simulation, real-time analytics and collaborative operations. Idiosyncratic digital twins would result in information silos, and this could render information integration and analytics difficult and human-system interactions more complicated. Advances in internet of things, artificial intelligence, building information modeling, asset management system and building automation system may open up new ways for improving the operational intelligence of digital twins of facilities and workspaces. This research aims to develop a holistic smart digital twin enabled framework to improve the operational intelligence of building facilities. The framework consists of a mechanism to construct discrete twins, assemble and orchestrate composite twins of building facilities and occupants that captures real time data related to operational efficiency and reliability; a strategy for digital twin data aggregation and integration fitting for edge and cloud computing architecture; a social physics and data driven model for deriving the interaction patterns between facility and human twins; a reference software architecture; and a prototype system for creating, sharing, monitoring, analyzing and orchestrating facility twins. The research begins with a series of interviews, case studies and focus group meetings and a Delphi study to unveil the potentials, obstacles and requirements of applying digital twin to deriving building facilities management solutions and identify feasible algorithms and systems for simulating and optimizing facility operation decisions. A workshop will be convened to design a cloud-based digital twin framework for improving the operation intelligence of building facilities. Finally, case studies will be conducted to validate the developed framework and prototype system. The novelty of this investigation lies in the innovative use of digital twin, data science and social physics approaches to delineate the problems, capacities and solutions associated with building facilities management and decision making. This investigation should help foster harmonious human-cyber-physical communities for smart, sustainable and resilient built environment development. 高效可靠的建築設施對於社會和市民福祉至關重要。在各種新興技術中，數字孿生被視為前途無限的概念，因它能用於革新產品、系統、以致城市之建造、規劃、和運營。正當美國太空總署、通用電氣、和新加坡大力推廣數字孿生，將其作為實現智慧城市、工業化4.0、和數字業務的顛覆性典範，我們有需要探索如何利用數字孿生技術來管理建築環境，以提高其性能、可靠性、 效率、節省成本、和用戶的體驗。 然而，通過數字孿生來提高建築設施的運營智能存在嚴峻挑戰，尤其在數據收集與集成、建模及模擬、實時分析、和協作運營方面。而分散的數字孿生模組不僅加劇信息孤島化，引致信息集成和分析變得更加困難，亦會使系統與人之交互變得加倍複雜。隨着現今物聯網、人工智能、建築物信息模型、資產管理系統、和建築物自動化系統的進步，這一切都可為數字孿生開闢新方向從而改善設施和工作空間的操作智能。 這項研究旨在開發一個整體智能數字孿生框架，以改善建築設施運營智能。該框架包括建造、組合和編排獨自建築設施和用戶的雙胞胎成為一個整體合成雙胞胎，用以收集實時之運營效率和可靠性數據；建立以邊緣及雲計算架構的數字孿生數據聚合和集成策略；利用社會物理和數據驅動模型推斷設施與人雙胞胎之間的相互作樣式；及發展用於創建、分享、監測、分析、和編排建築設施雙胞胎的原型系統。

17203020.label: Realisation of objectives
17203020.value: Objective 1: A thorough desktop study was conducted and the results show that certain international data model standards for storing and managing diverse data can be made referenced to when modeling the indoor environment in the digital world. A case study on a university campus was carried out to depict the facilities management service components, the interaction between the facilities of a building and its users, and how digital twin can be applied to support users and facility managers in improving the user experience and service quality respectively. Interviews were carried out with facility managers, users, operators, planners, etc., and it was found that planners and users would rely on the digital information for service involving indoor space, like indoor navigation in unfamiliar buildings, evacuation in case of fire outbreak or other emergency events, spatial analysis for complex buildings, space management of large buildings, etc. Experts were engaged to understand their perspectives on digital transformation of facilities management and clarify their diverse and real needs for digital facilities management services. Through which, a multi-criteria decision model was developed to elucidate the relationships among the barriers and propose an optimal strategy to accelerate the adoption of digital technologies in built facilities [Journal Paper 4]. Objective 2: Before devising a mechanism for constructing a digital twin model, a literature review was carried out to gain a better insight of how digital twin was applied to improve the operational intelligence of built facilities throughout their lifecycle stages [Journal Paper 3]. The research team then adopted and developed a three-pronged approach, i.e. developing a common platform as an information sharing environment to integrated data from several different interacting systems; establishing uniform data exchange standards or uniform data format specification so as to facilitate information exchange and sharing across different information systems; and linking the data using Semantic Web technologies [Journal Paper 1]. Case study was carried out based on the proposed three-pronged approach, and an information integration and decision support framework was proposed according to the Semantic Web technologies, whereby cross domain linkage of various twins is made possible by means of ontology development; multiple-source heterogeneous data collected from the twins is integrated through automated ontology instantiation and resource description framework (RDF) schema; the twin information is retrieved by the RDF query language; and local inferencing is supported by rule language and logic engines [Journal Paper 1]. As a result, the research team developed a semantic pedestrian networks to improve the operational intelligence within a building in terms of navigation, evacuation and spatial analysis [Journal Paper 2]. With the fundamental ontology being confirmed, a data converter was established to convert diverse digital model data with various formats into a common data format to achieve semantic interoperability for the digital twin model development. Objective 3: At this stage, an industry foundation class (IFC) based data aggregation and integration digital twin data strategy was first developed. To organize the three aspects of data, i.e. semantic, topological and geometric information, under a united data model, an ontology-based indoor spatial information model was built using building topology ontology (BOT) as our reference. Here, the research team applied the sensor, observation, sample and actuator (SOSA) ontology to examine how BOT can work with other ontologies to provide more rich information relevant to the decision making process. The open library IfcOpenShell embedded in the Python program was used to capture the building information presented in the IFC files according to the internal organizational structure of the IFC specification. Subsequently, a python-based package RDFlib was adopted as the ontology instantiation tool to translate different data formats into the target RDF format. The RDF files resulting from converting different proprietary formats into a common data format would allow the information from various platforms including the building information model (BIM) and geographic information system (GIS) models to be shared in a common environment [Conference Paper 1]. Objective 4: A SPARQL query language for RDF, which closely reassembles a natural searching language, was adopted to facilitate easy and effective searching. An intelligent indoor path planning analytical platform was designed according to the human wayfinding behaviors, optimal route planning, evacuation patterns, and indoor space through the information captured by the digital twins. While human being would prefer finding feasible routes that would best meet their special needs and preference, human knowledge was integrated into the analytical platform to support intelligent indoor navigation. The development of a digital twin based semantic pedestrian network involves a four-step process. The first step was to analyze the standard data schema of digital models and determine the scope of data conversion. In the second step, domain ontologies were developed to define the terms and relationships of the data sources. The third step involved the creation of a mapping mechanism that establishes correspondences between the terms defined in the ontologies and the entities expressed in origin datasets. A program was designed in the fourth step to automatically parse and extract data in heterogeneous structures and serializations to RDF data models structured according to ontology and storing it in appropriate RDF triplestores. Objective 5: The digital twin model was developed according to the generic implementation process, which requires the solicitation of real-time data from physical entities; the creation of a visual model based on data derived from the digital twins; and the realization of a range of evaluation and prediction functions through both digital models and real-time updated data [Journal Paper 3]. With that, a software architecture was developed based on the findings of the preceding stages. The software architecture consists of the digital twin modeling engine, internet-of-things (IoT) middleware for integrating sensors and video cameras, data repository, analytics engine, visualization tools, etc. [Conference Paper 2]. To support the system architecture, a multi-source data conversion and integration regime was designed [Journal Paper 2]. Finally, a digital twin model for a combined indoor and outdoor pedestrian network was developed to improve the operational intelligence of building in terms of navigation and evacuation based on the physical, personal and environmental conditions. The digital twin model integrates multi-source data by linking IoT data (i.e. video camera, environmental sensors, etc.) with the BIM and GIS datasets to create a unified and interoperable knowledge representation for the SPN, effectively integrating both static and dynamic information [PhD Thesis]. Through which, real-time people movement, crowdedness as well as indoor and outdoor environmental parameters can be fed into the decision-model to perform instantaneous decision support according to the identified constraints and requirements. Objective 6: A case study was conducted in a university campus to validate the proposed digital twin model and the outcomes of the preceding stages. Specifically, the research team obtained the example data from related studies using Info Works ICM and PyroSim to get flooding and fire data, respectively to simulate the evacuation in case of flooding and fire outbreak. Besides, pedestrian data was obtained through time object detection algorithm – You Only Look Once (YOLO). Consequently, this study employs software tool of Pathfinder to capture data on variables such as the remaining number of individuals in a room in order to validate the reliability of the digital twin pedestrian network model in case of emergencies and/or abnormalities like flooding and fire [PhD Thesis].

17203020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203020.value: A systematic framework using Semantic Web technologies has been proposed to overcome the interdependent infrastructure decisions. The results show that the proposed framework can facilitate meaningful data integration and interoperability between diverse interdependent infrastructure systems. Moreover, existing open data standards can be used as common domain knowledge and international concept library, which can serve as a potential solution for ontology development for efficient data sharing and seamless data interpretation between different infrastructure domains. Moreover, the proposed semantic query and logical reasoning strategies can assist decision-makers acquire information and explore the interdependency of intertwined infrastructure systems from fragmented and heterogeneous data resources. [Journal Paper 1] Novel perspectives on interlinking BIM and GIS data have been developed for a semantic pedestrian network. The proposed approach consists of converting BIM and GIS data into linked data, interlinking across-domain ontologies and RDF instances, establishing a semantic pedestrian network, and designing the potential applications. The interlinkages between ontologies from BIM and GIS domains bind the diverse domain knowledge together. The interlinkages between instances from BIM and GIS datasets provide seamless representation of the physical built environment in the virtual world. The final integrated RDF graphs form a knowledge base covering diverse indoor and outdoor pedestrian infrastructure information. The findings play a crucial role in the development of data infrastructure for smart cities and digital twins. [Journal Paper 2] The prevalent research scenarios for digital twin application in the building construction industry and its role in improving operational intelligence have been identified. The results have led to three key categories of digital facilitating technologies for digital twin, namely: data-related technologies, high-fidelity modeling technologies, and model-based simulation technologies. The lack of universal standards for digital twin has been found to be the major research gap, which leads to numerous outstanding issues, such as loss of valuable information, system fragmentation across building projects due to the abundance of information, and difficulties in real-time data access and integration for users. The paper calls for a universal standard for digital twin implementation. [Journal Paper 3] The optimal strategy for the adoption of digital technologies in the construction industry has been analyzed. The results show that the lack of clear policy, legal framework, as well as certification and industry-specific standards are the major barriers hindering digital technologies adoption. To improve the adoption of digital technologies in built facilities, digital systems should be effective, impactful, feasible and cost effective. [Journal Paper 4]

17203020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203020.value: While the data quality of the experimental digital twin model and IoT database is based on an experimental model, its semantic richness needs to be improved. The data quality with enough comprehensive information plays a critical role in knowledge inference and more intelligent digital twin applications support. Future work shall explore more complicated and high-quality data sources. More research effort should be directed to delineate the ontologies of the digital twin model. The current study only has a simple representation of property values and names to minimize the data size and ensure good data readability. Using unit and property ontologies for a more detailed property modeling shall be considered in future research. As this study did not provide a detailed comparison and validation of the digital twin models, to fully explore the range of complex applications enabled by the SPN, further case studies using different datasets should be carried out to provide valuable insights and contribute to a thorough examination of the potential value of this approach. Utilizing linked data and semantic web technologies to enhance seamless data integration between heterogeneous information systems and ensure information accessibility for all stakeholders is highly desirable for the future development of smart cities.

17203020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203020.value: Built facilities support various human, social and economic activities, and their operational efficiency and reliability are, therefore, of paramount importance. In this project, a digital twin model was developed to improve the operational intelligence of built facilities. Of various issues related to the operation of a building, indoor navigation and emergency evacuation can severely affect the efficiency, safety and wellbeing of occupants. Through Semantic Web technologies, a common platform was first built to enable information sharing and integration across various systems. An indoor spatial information model was developed to combine data with building information model and geographic information system. An intelligent indoor path planning analytical platform was then designed according to the human wayfinding behaviors, optimal route planning, evacuation patterns, and indoor space through the information captured by the digital twins. Finally, a digital twin model for a combined indoor and outdoor pedestrian network was developed to improve the operational intelligence of building in terms of navigation and evacuation based on the physical, personal and environmental conditions. Through data captured by internet-of-things, real-time physical condition, people movement, and indoor and outdoor environmental parameters are fed into the digital twin model for instantaneous decision support according to the constraints and requirements.

The effects of surface roughness, vibrational frequency and amplitude, and generation of turbulent eddies on the resuspension process will be studied. 17203220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203220.value: Previous theoretical research studies on particle resuspension from stationary surfaces may not accurately describe the real phenomenon, as reflected by the opposite findings compared with field measurements. Laboratory studies based on ideal surfaces found that unrealistic vigorous conditions in terms of airflow and force field are required to initiate resuspension, but resuspension does occur in various indoor environments, especially when the room has many interior surfaces and furnishings. Indeed, surfaces composed of twisted tufts may easily become breeding grounds for microorganisms that spread bacteria and viruses through the resuspended aerosols. Addressing this issue properly is crucial to more accurate assessment of risks to occupants. Recent studies have investigated the influence of the airflow generated by human activities, but the possible contribution of induced surface vibration has been overlooked. Particularly, flexible materials oscillate when subjected to airflow and/or an external force, which may lead to the higher resuspension rate found for carpets compared with wooden surfaces. This proposed project aims to reveal the particle dynamics during the resuspension process taking into consideration the interaction between the external force, airflow and the flexible structures on surfaces. Our preliminary results suggest that this interaction would substantially enhance resuspension rates from 2.6% to 87%, which cannot be explained by the existing theories in the literature. We hypothesize that the surface vibration creates vortices which initiate the rolling of particles on the surface, detach the particles from the surface and carry away the detached particles downstream, thereby enhancing the resuspension rate. To elucidate the exact mechanism, the proposed study will first experimentally determine the particle resuspension rate from the surface materials that are commonly found in indoor environments, characterized by their geometry, rigidity and roughness. We will conduct a parametric study to investigate the effects of flow-induced and/or forced surface motion of different materials under various airflow rates, classified in terms of vibration frequency and amplitude, on particle resuspension. Particles in spherical and irregular shapes of different sizes will be tested as analogy to the shape of real bioaerosols. Then, numerical simulation tools will be employed to study the vortex generation process in the near wall flow regime. The ultimate goal is to develop a generalized mathematical model describing the particle resuspension behavior through theoretical analysis. Not only will this project clarify the discrepancy between field studies and laboratory measurements, it will also provide important and helpful information on the design of healthier indoor environments. 以往對靜止表面的顆粒再懸浮的理論研究可能無法準確地描述真實現象，與實地測量相悖的結果則反映了這一問題。基於理想表面的實驗室研究發現，再懸浮需要在流場和力場極其劇烈的非現實條件下才能進行，然而，再懸浮確實會發生在各種日常的室內環境中，尤其是當室內有許多內表面和傢俱時。事實上，彎曲的絨毛組成的表面很容易成為微生物的繁殖地，並通過再懸浮的氣溶膠傳播細菌和病毒。因此，為了更準確地評估居住者所面臨的風險，妥善解決上述問題顯得至關重要。最近的研究已經調查了人類活動所產生的氣流的影響，但忽略了其引起表面振動的潛在作用。特別是，柔性材料在受到氣流和/或外力的影響時會發生振盪，這可能導致地毯的再懸浮率高於木質表面。本項目旨在揭示氣溶膠再懸浮過程中的粒子動力學，同時考慮外力、氣流和表面柔性結構之間的相互作用。我們的初步結果表明，這種相互作用將極大地提高再懸浮率，從2.6%提高到87%，這是現有文獻理論無法解釋的。我們假設表面振動產生漩渦，引發顆粒在表面上的滾動，使顆粒從表面上分離，並順著氣流帶走分離的顆粒，從而提高了再懸浮率。為了闡明其確切的機理，本研究將首先通過實驗確定室內環境中常見的表面材料上的顆粒再懸浮率，以其幾何形狀、剛度和粗糙度等特徵來選取表面材料。我們將進行一項參數研究，以探究不同材料在按振動頻率和振幅分類的不同氣流速度下，由氣流和/或外力引起的表面運動對顆粒再懸浮的影響，並將不同大小的球狀和不規則形狀的顆粒作為真實生物氣溶膠形狀的類比物進行測試。然後，利用數值模擬的方法研究了近壁區流態下漩渦的形成過程。最終目的是通過理論分析建立顆粒再懸浮行為的廣義數學模型。本項目不僅將闡明實地研究和實驗室測量之間的差異，還將為設計更健康的室內環境提供重要和有幫助的資訊。

17203220.label: Realisation of objectives
17203220.value: The overall objectives have been achieved. The effects of force-induced, flow-induced, and combined vibrational motions of flexible materials on aerosol resuspension were investigated. The effects of particle shape and size on resuspension behavior were investigated. A mathematical model to describe the resuspension process from surface motion to detachment to airborne release was developed. The model covered both force-induced vibration and flow-induced vibration of flexible materials, which was verified by a series of experiments. Some key results are shown below. We report the resuspension results of dust (with different shapes and sizes) from fabrics (with varying contamination levels) subjected to force-induced low-frequency vibrations, originally inspired by daily human activities (e.g., shaking clothes). The flexible fabric motion and the multilayer dust motion have been experimentally demonstrated as major contributors to the resuspension in this scenario. The acceleration amplification effect along the fabric and the various particle-particle interactions are key experimental observations. Some reasonable assumptions based on these observations have been used to describe the scenario mathematically. A set of semi-empirical correlations has thus been developed. Our semi-empirical correlations incorporating surface acceleration, surface size, vibration frequency, dust load, and vibration duration are proposed to provide comprehensive and effective predictions for scenarios involving moving flexible surfaces. Multiple essential factors have been identified and included, making our findings generally applicable, for example, to real-life cases with different surfaces, different dust loads, and even local or global contamination (i.e., different area sizes). On the basis of the above conclusions, some of the enhancement factors, e.g., the acceleration amplification effect, are instructive for the future development of resuspension-related products. Moreover, our proposed mathematical description form supported by our experimental observations can facilitate future parametric studies and modeling in multiple contexts. To sum up, these findings can propose dust resuspension guidelines for some real-world scenarios or practical applications and can provide new insights into interpreting particle resuspension. We also report the resuspension results of dust (with different shapes and sizes) from four typical fabrics (cotton, linen, silk, and polyester) exposed to airflow with common velocities within 0 ~ 10 m/s. This scenario points out another typical example of moving flexible surfaces related to particle resuspension, inspired by natural phenomena (e.g., flags and leaves fluttering in the wind). Following our semi-empirical mathematical form, the development of semi-empirical correlations for the flow-induced moving fabric case offers a feasible solution for describing and predicting this complex resuspension phenomenon under the different conditions of air velocity, fabric motion mode, fabric type, and airflow duration. In particular, this set of semi-empirical correlations makes it possible to use the target air velocity to effectively estimate the stronger-than-expected resuspension during the inevitable airflow acceleration period, proposing that the time-segmented approach based on this period in this work deserves to be applied in similar theoretical work in the future. This finding also demonstrates a significant contribution of short-term accelerating airflow to dust resuspension from fabrics, as the fabrics are moved by the airflow, suggesting the potential for wind gusts in real-world scenarios to trigger high levels of air pollutants even in a short time. Not only the superior overall resuspension enhancement of the moving fabrics, but also their resuspension-promoting effect by the accelerating airflow, are confirmed in this work compared to the fixed fabrics. These findings can shed light on evaluating and controlling the particulate matter exceedances in daily life as well as the design and optimization of decontamination applications. In the fluttering case, the airflow and the surface motion were found to work in combination, giving us the best of both worlds. Thus, we further report a single-particle dynamics analysis for the resuspension of polystyrene (PS) spherical particles (with different diameters) from a flow-induced fluttering flexible oriented polypropylene (OPP) substrate at air velocities of 0 ~ 8 m/s with a comparative fixed substrate experiment under the same conditions. The fluttering motion of the substrate was quantified by a high-speed camera, and the particle resuspension was assessed by a microscope. There was almost no particle resuspension in the fixed substrate case with a remaining fraction of 1 ~ 0.9786, while the local remaining fraction could be reduced from 1 to 0 in the fluttering substrate case, showing a remarkable particle resuspension enhancement and a great reduction in the threshold velocity, which were dependent on the particle diameter and position. For a single particle in the fluttering substrate case, the force caused by the fluttering acceleration of the substrate, which exceeded its gravity by several orders of magnitude, was identified as an important factor enhancing the particle resuspension. Another necessary factor was the significant flutter-induced aerodynamic force/moment enhancement acting on the particle, illustrated by the static force and moment balance analysis. This theoretical work suggests an interesting research focus for future particle resuspension studies, i.e., flutter-induced fluid dynamics. It can have practical implications in several fields. In the industrial field, fluttering dynamics is expected to inform applications that require particle resuspension, e.g., aerosolization of powders, drug delivery, spray systems and surface contaminant cleaning, due to its strong resuspension capacity. Our parametric studies also benefit the optimization of related products. In the environmental field, our experimental results indicate that substrate flutter can cause significant particle resuspension in low-air-velocity scenarios (e.g., indoors), which may easily degrade air quality. Besides, liquid aerosol resuspension from the fluttering surfaces warrants further investigation. Although liquid aerosols tend to be more difficult to resuspend than solid particles, it can be speculated from this project that the surface flutter may achieve appreciable liquid aerosol resuspension. Its in-depth understanding may help reduce the transmission of pathogens via respiratory droplets. Moreover, a proportional relationship (i.e., fluttering frequency ∝ air velocity) obtained in this work connects the physical meanings of the semi-empirical correlations developed in our previous studies. This connection implies that although the parameters used as independent variables in our semi-empirical correlations are different in the previous cases, they follow the same mathematical form under the assumptions in this project. Therefore, the model is proposed to be applicable in a wide range of scenarios involving moving flexible surfaces. In summary, we conducted a series of studies corresponding to the project objectives. All our studies are interconnected and progressive, so that the project objectives have been fully achieved. This project not only systematically studies particle resuspension from moving flexible materials but also helps enrich the understanding of aerosol dynamics.

17203220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203220.value: For force-induced vibrations, it was found that different settings of vibration duration, vibration frequency, and initial dust load can lead to significant differences in the resuspension results. Flexible fabric motion and multilayer dust motion were demonstrated as major contributors through visualization experiments. The observed phenomena of acceleration amplification effect along the fabric and various particle-particle interactions provided a crucial basis for our reasonable assumptions in our mathematical description. A set of semi-empirical correlations was thus developed. For flow-induced surface motions, following the above modeling configuration, a set of semi-empirical correlations, involving air velocity, fabric motion mode, fabric type, and airflow duration was developed for the moving fabric case. It was found that a stronger-than-expected resuspension was triggered by short-term accelerating airflow. The resuspension enhancement of over 90% was reported for the moving fabrics compared with the fixed ones. Fabric motion induced by airflow was proposed to account for these resuspension findings. Fabric acceleration was then demonstrated to be a key factor in evaluating the resuspension for such a scenario. In the fluttering case, the airflow and the surface motion were found to work in combination, giving us the best of both worlds. The comparison results show that the case of flow-induced fluttering flexible surfaces was recognized as the one with greater resuspension potential, which deserved further theoretical development. A single-particle dynamics analysis for spherical particles on a flow-induced fluttering flexible substrate was therefore performed. The effects of the flow-induced flutter on the resuspension, and the underlying mechanisms initiating the resuspension in the fluttering substrate case, were quantitatively illustrated by comparing with the fixed substrate case. A force caused by the fluttering acceleration was identified as an important factor enhancing the resuspension. The existence of a significant flutter-induced aerodynamic force/moment enhancement acting on the particles was demonstrated as another necessary factor, charting a new course for future studies. Moreover, a proportional relationship (i.e., fluttering frequency ∝ air velocity) connected the physical meanings of our semi-empirical correlations in this project, implying that our model is proposed to be applicable in a wide range of scenarios involving moving flexible materials.

17203220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203220.value: A series of recommendations for future work are put forward here. First, due to the complexity caused by moving flexible materials, more accurate real-time microscopic studies are urgently needed. Next, we call for more tests to further refine our model. Then, more real-life scenario investigations are required to overcome the discrepancies between experimental and real-world conditions. After that, in the theoretical framework developed in this project, further fluid dynamics data encompassing the stochastic nature of the resuspension problem are believed to be the last piece of the puzzle. Last but not least, the flutter-driven resuspension technology proposed in this project, inspired by natural phenomena, is a non-contact self-driven innovative technology. However, replacing rigid surfaces with flexible ones is not always feasible in product development. For some products, the material must be rigid while in use. Thus, we may need surfaces that are rigid while working but can switch to be flexible when particle resuspension is desired. A forward-looking idea could be to develop smart materials that meet these requirements. Furthermore, if artificial intelligence (AI) is involved in the proposed product development, our so-called “self-resuspension” technology may become “more self-reliant” in the future.

17203220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203220.value: Understanding particle resuspension contributes to building healthy living environments and improving industrial operations. Previous theoretical studies on resuspension from stationary surfaces may not accurately describe the real phenomena, as reflected by the opposite findings compared with field measurements. Laboratory studies based on ideal surfaces found that unrealistic vigorous conditions (e.g., extremely strong forces and winds) are required to initiate resuspension, but field surveys suggested that resuspension does occur in various environments, especially when many flexible surfaces are involved. It may act as an obstacle to achieving a truly unified picture of resuspension. Therefore, this project strives to overcome this obstacle by focusing on moving flexible materials, inspired by human activities (e.g., shaking clothes) and natural phenomena (e.g., flags and leaves fluttering in the wind). We systematically report the effects of flexible materials on resuspension and the underlying mechanisms in multiple cases, including both flow-induced and forced surface motion and classified in terms of vibration frequency and amplitude. We also develop a mathematical model covering a wide range of scenarios. Not only will this project clarify the discrepancy between field studies and laboratory measurements; it will also provide important and helpful information on the design of healthier indoor environments.

17203320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203320.value: Federated Learning (FL) is a new paradigm that enables mobile phones to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model while keeping all the training data on the devices. Although federated learning is a promising idea, training by a massive network of mobile devices introduces new challenges. First, device heterogeneity is a fundamental issue considering different resources and capabilities of the mobile devices. Second, local data of the mobile devices may have different data quality and statistical distribution. Third, mobile devices may suffer from hardware, software and network failures, and malicious attacks. Despite existing federated learning paradigm can accommodate heterogeneous mobile phones, the problem of poor data quality, imbalanced data distribution, reliability and security issues remain to be further explored. To tackle the above challenges, this project will design a robust federated learning framework, called RobustFL, which can handle poor data quality, imbalanced data distribution, failures and malicious attacks. First, we will study how data quality, imbalanced data distribution, and reliability of mobile clients affect the accuracy and convergence of the global model through both theoretical and empirical analysis. Then, we will develop a RobustFL framework with three objectives: (1) We will provide mechanisms to monitor reliability and evaluate local training quality of the mobile clients; (2) We will propose quality aware client selection algorithms to maximize the accuracy of the global model; (3) We will develop methods to detect malicious clients and improve the robustness in global aggregation. Finally, we will verify the framework by implementing real applications on mobile phones and conduct both simulations and experiments for performance evaluation. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to study robust federated learning considering data quality, imbalanced data distribution, reliability and malicious behaviors of heterogeneous mobile clients in an integrated framework. At the moment, existing federated learning schemes are not designed to handle poor data quality or training performance of the participating mobile clients. There is no mechanism to evaluate and select reliable mobile clients in FL, so the mobile clients may suffer from poor data quality, failures and malicious attacks. This project advances the state-of-the-art in FL by providing robustness and resilience against poor local training quality, failures and malicious attacks. The project will have a direct impact on existing mobile applications relying upon FL and significantly improve the robustness and resiliences of future mobile and IoT applications, such as autonomous vehicles, city surveillance, and medical applications. 聯邦學習是一種新的機器學習架構框架，它使移動設備可以協作學習共享的預測模型，同時將所有訓練數據保留在設備上。與此同時，通過龐大的移動設備網絡進行培訓也帶來新的挑戰。首先，考慮到移動設備的不同計算資源和功能，設備異構性是一個基本問題。其次，移動設備的本地數據可能具有不同的數據質量和統計分佈。第三，移動設備可能會遭受硬件，軟件和網絡故障以及惡意攻擊。儘管現有的聯邦學習範例可以適應異構移動電話，但數據質量差、數據分佈不平衡、可靠性和安全性問題仍然有待進一步探討。為了解決上述挑戰，這項目將設計一個可靠的聯合學習框架，稱為RobustFL，該框架可以處理數據質量差、數據分佈不均、故障和惡意攻擊。首先，我們將通過理論和經驗分析研究數據質量，不平衡的數據分佈和移動客戶端的可靠性如何影響全局模型的準確性和收斂性。然後，我們將開發一個具有三個目標的RobustFL框架：（1）我們將提供機制來監控可靠性並評估移動客戶端的本地培訓質量； （2）我們將提出以數據質量為基礎的客戶選擇算法，以提高全局模型的準確性； （3）我們將開發檢測惡意客戶端並提高模型聚合準確性的方法。最後，我們將通過在手機上實現實際應用程序來驗證框架，並進行仿真和實驗以評估性能。據我們所知，我們是第一個在集成框架中考慮數據質量、不平衡數據分佈、可靠性和異構移動客戶端惡意行為的聯合學習方法。目前，現有的聯合學習方案的設計尚未能處理參與方移動客戶端的不良數據質量。 聯邦學習中沒有評估和選擇可靠的移動客戶端的機制，因此移動客戶端可能會遭受數據質量差、故障和惡意攻擊的困擾。這項目通過提供抵禦數據質量差、故障和惡意攻擊的能力，從而提高聯邦學習的準確性。這項目將對依賴聯邦學習的現有移動應用產生直接影響，並顯著提高未來移動和物聯網應用（如自動駕駛汽車，城市監控和醫療應用）的可靠性。

17203320.label: Realisation of objectives
17203320.value: We realized the above objectives by completing the primary works below. 1. We have comprehensively investigated the requirements and challenges of designing a robust Federated Learning framework, called RobustFL, which can handle failures and malicious attacks, and accommodate mobile clients with heterogeneous resources, data quality, and imbalanced data distribution. Byzantine-robust federated learning aims at mitigating Byzantine failures during the federated training process, where malicious participants (known as Byzantine clients) may upload arbitrary local updates to the central server in order to degrade the performance of the global model. In recent years, several robust aggregation schemes have been proposed to defend against malicious updates from Byzantine clients and improve the robustness of federated learning. These solutions were claimed to be Byzantine-robust, under certain assumptions. Other than that, new attack strategies are emerging, striving to circumvent the defense schemes. However, there is a lack of systematical comparison and empirical study thereof. 2. We have conducted an experimental study of Byzantine-robust aggregation schemes under different attacks using two popular algorithms in federated learning, FedSGD and FedAvg. We surveyed existing Byzantine attack strategies, as well as Byzantine-robust aggregation schemes that aim to defend against Byzantine attacks. We also proposed a new scheme, ClippedClustering, to enhance the robustness of a clustering-based scheme by automatically clipping the updates. Then, we provided an experimental evaluation of eight aggregation schemes in the scenario of five different Byzantine attacks. Our experimental results showed that these aggregation schemes sustain relatively high accuracy in some cases, but they are not effective in all cases. In particular, our proposed ClippedClustering successfully defends against most attacks under independent and identically distributed (IID) local datasets. However, when the local datasets are Non-IID, the performance of all the aggregation schemes significantly decreases. With Non-IID data, some of these aggregation schemes fail even in the complete absence of Byzantine clients. Based on our experimental study, we concluded that the robustness of all the aggregation schemes is limited, highlighting the need for new defense strategies, in particular for non-IID datasets. 3. Federated learning provides a communication-efficient and privacy-preserving training process by enabling learning statistical models with massive participants without accessing their local data. Standard federated learning techniques that naively minimize an average loss function are vulnerable to data corruption from outliers, systematic mislabeling, or even adversaries. In this project, we addressed this challenge by proposing Auto-weighted Robust Federated Learning (ARFL), a novel approach that jointly learns the global model and the weights of local updates to provide robustness against corrupted data sources. We proved learning bound on the expected loss with respect to the predictor and the weights of clients, which guides the definition of the objective for robust federated learning. We presented an objective that minimizes the weighted sum of the empirical risk of clients with a regularization term, where the weights can be allocated by comparing the empirical risk of each client with the average empirical risk of the best p clients. This method can downweight the clients with significantly higher losses, thereby lowering their contributions to the global model. We showed that this approach achieves robustness when the data of corrupted clients is distributed differently from the benign ones. To optimize the objective function, we proposed a communication-efficient algorithm based on the blockwise minimization paradigm. We conducted extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, FEMNIST, and Shakespeare, considering different neural network models. The results show that our solution is robust against different scenarios, including label shuffling, label flipping, and noisy features, and outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in most scenarios. 4. Federated learning (FL) facilitates distributed training across different IoT and edge devices, safeguarding the privacy of their data. The inherent distributed structure of FL introduces vulnerabilities, especially from adversarial devices aiming to skew local updates to their advantage. Despite the plethora of research focusing on Byzantine-resilient FL, the academic community has yet to establish a comprehensive benchmark suite, pivotal for impartial assessment and comparison of different techniques. This project implemented Blades, a scalable, extensible, and easily configurable benchmark suite that supports researchers and developers in efficiently implementing and validating novel strategies against baseline algorithms in Byzantine-resilient FL. Blades contains built-in implementations of representative attack and defense strategies and offers a user-friendly interface that seamlessly integrates new ideas. Using Blades, we re-evaluated representative attacks and defenses on wide-ranging experimental configurations (approximately 1,500 trials in total). Through our extensive experiments, we gained new insights into FL robustness and highlighted previously overlooked limitations due to the absence of thorough evaluations and comparisons of baselines under various attack settings.

17203420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203420.value: Contaminated environmental surfaces (known as fomites) can spread enteric and respiratory infections by means of human touch. For example, norovirus infections spread by fomites can affect a large number of people in environments such as cruise ships, hospitals, and nursing homes. Crowded, semi-enclosed spaces are the commonly cited explanation for the cruise ship phenomenon, but the exact mechanisms remain unknown. In addition, conclusions from previous studies on the effects of hand hygiene and surface hygiene for controlling infections have often been contradictory, which may be because hand and surface hygiene are usually studied separately. A poor understanding of surface contamination dynamics has hindered the analysis and implementation of intervention methods. We hypothesise that environmental surface cleaning (including disinfection) and hand hygiene (including disinfection) are both necessary to control the spread of contamination between surfaces and should not be considered separately; however, their exact relationship remains undetermined for realistic conditions. This is supported by our recent development of surface hygiene criteria through the analysis of microbe spread on contaminated surfaces in an idealised environment. In the proposed project, we will develop a generalised system of mass balance equations for contamination spread on surfaces. This will allow us to analyse, for the first time, the dynamics of surface contamination in a general system instead of in specific systems as in the literature. The new model will enable us to characterise the transit life, age, and residual life of microbes on surfaces in occupied environments, thus providing a theoretical basis for environmental and hand hygiene. Contact transfer rates of microbes vary significantly according to the characteristics of touch, that is, with or without twisting or rubbing. Here, we define a new concept of ‘complete touch’ that will provide a measurable microbe transfer rate. Our recently developed concept of a ‘surface touch network’ will be used to characterise surface touch behaviour; in particular, heterogeneous surface touch networks. Our multi-disciplinary work will be carried out through laboratory studies of surface contamination in ideal networks, by mathematical analyses, and by in-depth examination of our new concept of surface touch network using contamination data derived from observations in a graduate student office and multi-route transmission analyses of norovirus outbreaks on a cruise ship. The findings will shed light on the timescales of microbes in the surface touch network and will provide guidance for pairing hand and surface hygiene for infection control. 受污染的環境表面（稱為“污染表面”）可通過人為接觸傳播腸道和呼吸道疾病。例如，由污染表面傳播的諾如病毒传播可能感染遊輪，醫院和療養院等環境中的許多人。人們普遍引用擁擠，半封閉的空間來解釋遊輪大爆发現象，但是確切的機理仍然未知。此外，先前關於人手衛生和表面衛生對控制感染影響的研究結論常常是矛盾的，這可能是因為手和表面衛生通常是分開研究的。對表面污染動力學的了解不足，阻礙了有效乾預方法的分析和實施。 我們假設環境表面清潔和手部衛生（包括消毒）两者都是控製表面之間污染物擴散的必要條件，因此不應單獨考慮；但是它們的確切關係對於许多實際情況仍然不確定。通過在理想環境中分析受污染表面上的微生物擴散情況，我們最近制定的表面衛生標準為解决這一問題提供了可能性。 在擬議的項目中，我們將開發一種用於表面污染物擴散質量平衡的通用方程。這將使我們能夠首次在一般系統中而不是特定係統中分析表面污染的動力學。新模型將使我們能夠表徵在人们居住環境中表面上微生物的传输时间，当时时间和剩餘时间，從而為環境和手部衛生实施提供理論依據。微生物的接觸轉移速率會根據觸摸的特性（即是否帶有扭曲或摩擦）而發生變化。在這裡，我們定義了一个“完全接觸”的新概念，它將提供可測量的微生物轉移率。我們最近開發的“表面觸摸網絡”概念將用於表徵表面觸摸行為；特別是異構表面觸摸網絡。 我们將通過實驗室研究上面理想網絡中的表面污染，和通過數學分析以及使用最近從研究生办公室中觀察到的污染數據和多路徑傳輸對我們的表面接觸網絡的新概念進行深入研究，開展跨學科分析遊輪上的諾如病毒暴發。我们的發現將闡明表面接觸網絡中微生物的時間尺度，並為配對手和表面同时衛生以控制感染提供指導。

17203420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203420.value: Microbe contamination on surfaces and hands can lead to enteric and respiratory infections when hands also touch noses, mouths and eyes. In this project we explore the dynamics of contamination and cleaning using a novel concept of surface touch network. Our theoretical analysis first extended our findings that hand hygiene and environmental surface hygiene (including disinfection in both cases) should be coupled to control contamination spread between surfaces. A coupled hygiene Criterion was established for realistic heterogenous networks, which underscores the importance of integrated hand and surface hygiene practices. The cleaning threshold increases as the numbers of surfaces and hands increase, illustrating the limitations of random cleaning strategies, particularly in large-scale and complex environments such as cruise ships. A generalised system of mass (number) balance equations is suggested for contamination spread on surfaces. The equilibration time (time to reach the equilibrium time) and mean residence time (time between entry and exit of particles on a surface network) are found to be dependent on the network structure, transfer rates of particles during surface touch and removal rates on surfaces and hands (surface and hand hygiene). A new parameter E is defined to measure the contaminant spreading efficiency in different networks. The spreading efficiency was found to be highly related to some network parameters, such as the source node’s average path length and degree, and considerably varied with the transfer rate per inter-node interaction. The contaminant spreading was particularly efficient in the fractal network when the transfer rate was ~0.5. Touching public (door handles) and hidden public (desks, chair seatbacks) surfaces, sparse hand-to-hand contact, and active carriers contributed significantly to contamination spread, which was also correlated with the size of the social group containing carriers. The contamination degree of known and hidden public surfaces can indicate fomite exposure risk. Our theoretical study is supported by the development of surface contamination tracer microbes. The non-toxic, non-human-origin and gram-positive bacterium Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. Bulgaricus was shown to be applicable for studying bacterial contamination spread on environmental surfaces was investigated in an office setting. The pepIP gene is used as a unique marker of externally introduced contamination. A surface touch network is established using surface touch data from two independent experiments conducted in office spaces. Using the microbe tracer method, the extent of surface contamination was assessed using qPCR. The touch data were analyzed using an agent-based model that predicted the observed contamination.

17203420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203420.value: Our theoretical and experimental exploration of surface contamination and hygiene probably established a new existing area of indoor surface environment. During the COVID-19 pandemic, our theory was found to be useful in evaluating exposure risk and ruling-out the role of fomite route, contributing to the establishment of airborne transmission as the predominant transmission route of SARS-CoV-2. Our work also provides a possibility for identifying general transmission mechanisms, i.e. reconciling airborne and surface touch routes. Our vision is that the future COVID-similar pandemic or even enteric infection pandemics can be controlled. Both respiratory and enteric infections remain the top five killers in the world. Most transmission occurs indoors. We have explored both airborne and surface touch (fomite) transmission mechanisms in the past 20 years. There is a need to eventual reconciliation of the two routes in terms of virus spread both in a room before exposure and virus entry into cells after exposure. Members in PI’s extended team (former students) have already started to develop automatic surface touch detection for applications in hospitals, schools and nursing homes. The PI plans to apply further funding to develop the possibly ultimate reconciliation of the fomite and airborne transmission routes of infection.

17203420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203420.value: Surace touch by hands can transport fine particles, microbes or microbe-containing particles between surfaces, or between a surface and a hand. This is the fundamental physical process behand the transmission of infection by the so-called fomite route. Surfaces are connected by hands, and hands are connected by surfaces, which is a surface touch network. If some surfaces/hands are contaminated, the time to spread to all surfaces (equilibrium), and how long microbes can reside on the surfaces/hands are found to depend on predominantly on the features of surface touch network. Some surfaces are touched more frequently than others (high touch surfaces), and some people touch more than others (high touch people). We found that hand hygiene and environmental surface hygiene (including disinfection in both cases) should be coupled to control contamination spread between surfaces. The cleaning efforts should increase as the numbers of surfaces and hands increase, illustrating the limitations of random cleaning strategies, particularly in large-scale and complex environments such as cruise ships. Our theoretical study is supported by the development of surface contamination tracer microbes. A non-toxic, non-human-origin and gram-positive bacterium was shown to be applicable for studying bacterial contamination spread on environmental surfaces.

17203520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203520.value: With the support of this funding, we have developed a DTCC using a GO cathode and a NiHCFeII anode for low-grade heat recovery. Utilizing NiHCFeII as the anode enhances the discharge capacity and allows for device recycling. We have systematically studied the fundamental thermodynamics and kinetics process of K+ extraction from the NiHCFeII electrode at different temperatures. The DTCCNCF (DTCC with NiHCFeII and GO) achieves a high heat-to-electricity conversion efficiency of 3.59% (equivalent to 26.2% of Carnot efficiency), positioning it at the forefront of existing technologies in the low-grade heat regime. Through thermal charging and electrical discharging cycles, an areal power density of 10 μW/cm2 can be reached for over 100 cycles. After long-term cycling, the DTCCNCF can be disassembled and reassembled for the next life cycle, as GO and NiHCFeII electrodes can be regenerated through simple chemical treatments. This realization embodies green technology and the circular economy. Additionally, this work demonstrates the wide applicability of DTCCNCF, providing an alternative approach for effectively harvesting low-grade heat in various applications.

17203520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203520.value: The developed system has the advantages of green technology, flexibility, cost-effectiveness, and scalability, making it promising in practical applications for direct energy conversion from low-grade heat sources.

17203520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203520.value: The research project focuses on converting low-grade heat, which is typically wasted, into electricity. By developing a device called a Direct Thermal Charging Cell (DTCC) using special materials like graphene oxide and nickel-hindered carbene, the researchers aim to efficiently capture and convert this heat. This technology has the potential to significantly improve energy efficiency and sustainability. It can be applied in various areas such as HVAC systems and self-powered smart windows and electronics. The research is valuable because it addresses the untapped potential of low-grade heat and offers a solution to reduce energy waste and greenhouse gas emissions. The DTCC achieves a high heat-to-electricity conversion efficiency, surpassing existing technologies. This breakthrough opens up opportunities to make energy production more sustainable and minimize our environmental impact. Overall, this research project offers a promising pathway to utilize wasted heat, enhance energy efficiency, and contribute to a greener future.

17203620.value: 使用多模態深度學習框架研究虛擬環境中的人體機能

17203620.label: Project Objectives
17203620.value: To build up a multimodal dataset of human performance of representative tasks in virtual environment (VE). The dataset is collected through large-scale trials of human users subjected to different VR cues in VE. The dataset contains human factors data including real-time electroencephalogram, eye and body movement, heart and breath rates, etc. The dataset represents a valuable resource for understanding human reactions when exposed to various situations in VE and as a standard reference for VR system design. To develop a multimodal deep learning framework with data representation of the different modalities that model the corresponding human factors data associated to human performance. The framework shall provide a means to characterize VR systems implemented by a VE, and to predict the effect to human users when interacting with these VR systems. To apply the multimodal deep learning framework to build a prototype VR system that is implemented using VR devices in the imseCAVE VR lab at HKU. The VR system should have desirable functionality including adaptive presentation and early discomfort warning to users. The resulting VR system should deliver optimal performance driven by the multimodal deep learning framework developed in the project through parameter refinement and fine tuning.

17203620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203620.value: While virtual reality or VR has become a jargon in our everyday life where a large number of disciplines including education, entertainment, healthcare, finance, real estate, retail, manufacturing, public services, etc. are associating their business and operations with, there are fundamental issues of mismatch between technology and human users to be addressed since VR is categorically created for human beings. Yet over the past decades, these very issues of human-VR system interactions have not been systematically and holistically studied. The novelty of the research fills this knowledge gap through finding answers to three very important questions of (a) how to quantify human factors including performance of human beings in a virtual environment, (b) the correlations between human behavior and VR scenarios, and (c) the psychological and/or physiological effects to the human body when working with VR and living in virtual environment (VE) over a significant period of time. The undertaking of this research involves investigation of human behavior in virtual environment, behavior modeling of human behavior, collection of human performance data through extensive trials with subjects using different VR devices experiencing different virtual scenarios, big data modeling and data analytics. A multimodal deep learning framework based on the artificial intelligence (AI) method of specially designed neural network is used to relate various human factors dataset such as electroencephalogram (EEG), bodily and eye movement, blood pressure, heart rate, etc. so that high-order human performance in VE can be predicted. While the research outcome helps to define the underlying theory of human behavior and performance in a virtual environment, the knowledge obtained will provide definitive answers to these research questions. Through extensive human trials, the analysis on the data collected and the deep learning framework developed shall facilitate the creation of directives for VR systems qualification not only in system performance, but also health and safety impacts to users, as well as industrial standards for future VR system design and deployment that will make VR a pervasive technology for our daily life. 虛擬實景（VR）在日常生活中應用廣泛，為不同行業帶來高質素的業務和運作應用，在教育、娛樂、醫療保健、金融、房地產、零售、製造業、公共服務等眾多範疇均不難發現它的蹤影。雖然虛擬實景能為人類帶來便利，但是現有的虛擬實景科技和原有的使用概念還有一段距離，成為了目前發展虛擬實景的根本問題。 然而，過去幾十年間，鮮有人全面且有系統地研究人類與虛擬實景系統交互時所衍生的問題。有見及此，此項新研究希望能透過解答以下三方面的問題，填補目前的研究缺口：（一）如何在虛擬環境（VE）中量化人體機能等的人為因素；（二）人類行為與虛擬環境之間的關聯性；以及（三）長時間使用虛擬實景科技或在虛擬環境生活對人的心理及生理影響。 此項研究內容包括：建立識別人類在虛擬環境中的行為模型、收集受試者使用虛擬實景設備經歷各種場景時的人體機能數據、建立大數據模型以及數據分析。此研究建立的多模態深度學習框架建基於經特殊設計的人工神經網絡，能夠關聯各種人體機能數據，例如腦電圖（EEG）、身體及眼球運動、血壓、心率變異等，因此可以預測虛擬實景中的高層次人為表現。 研究成果將有助探討虛擬環境中人類行為及機能的基礎理論，從中獲取的知識亦能為上述的研究問題提供肯定的答案。透過進行一連串的實驗，分析所收集的數據並開發深度學習框架，此項研究能為虛擬實景系統認證創立新的方向，尤其針對虛擬實景的系統性能表現及對使用者的健康及安全影響，並定立未來虛擬實景的行業標準，令虛擬實景成為日常生活中更為廣泛應用的技術。

17203620.label: Realisation of objectives
17203620.value: This project compares and examines the perceptual mechanism of the hypotheses related to cybersickness in detail with the objective to develop a theoretical model to explain cybersickness for VR users. Three major studies are undertaken to achieve these objectives: Study 1 examined the sensory conflict hypothesis using a seated motion-coupled VR system. It was found that a synchronised visual-physical signal in VR could reduce visual-vestibular sensory conflict and mitigate cybersickness symptoms. Results suggest that the absence of multisensory synchronisation, visual-vestibular at least, plays a key role in the mechanism of cybersickness elicitation. Study 2 examined the sensory conflict hypothesis and the postural instability hypothesis using a standing motion-coupled VR system. While previous research found that postural instability is the prerequisite of cybersickness, it was found that postural instability induced by external horizontal physical oscillation may not necessarily lead to the onset of cybersickness. Study 3 examined the eye movement hypothesis and the differences between central and peripheral visual field. It was found that manipulating involuntary eye movements via viewpoint fixation may be more effective in reducing cybersickness discomfort than a peripheral field of view restriction.

17203620.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203620.value: The major research outcomes from this awarded project include 5 published journal papers and 3 conference articles. Some key findings are as follows: (1) A hierarchical spatial attention-based cross-scale detection network is designed to address these challenges and provide accurate on-site information for the DWSS [Journal paper 1]. (2) Sleep quality, spatial ability, and pain sensitivity had been suggested to affect cybersickness discomfort. This study evaluated various human factors on the cybersickness symptoms and tolerance duration in a nausegenic virtual environment. It is found that participants with better sleep quality had better cybersickness tolerance. Further, participants with lower pain threshold had slightly lower cybersickness tolerance and reported more cybersickness symptoms. [Conference paper 3].

17203620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203620.value: It is not fully validated psychophysically and neurologically and would require future research efforts to modify and improve our understanding of this malady that hinder the development of VR technologies. For example, the sensory conflict hypothesis is often criticised for not being able to be falsified and not being able to account for gender differences; the postural instability hypothesis is often criticised for incompatible data from a number of experimental studies; and the eye movement hypothesis is found to be complicated by other factors. These are some of the unresolved issues in the aetiology of cybersickness that are not fully addressed or validated by these hypotheses or the current model. In addition, other factors such as age-related difference or observers with the absence of visual or vestibular function could also be examined in detail. Future work may also investigate cybersickness in other VR equipments such as different brands of commercially available HMD, LED or projector based VRsystems to validate the results across different systems.

The second topic examines the sensory conflict and the postural instability hypothesis using a standing motion-couple VR system. The third topic examines the eye movement hypothesis and the differences between central and peripheral visual fields. There are some interesting and significant findings and observations.
