17203920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203920.value: 香港地處陡峭，城市發展長期受限。受世界各地的成功地下發展項目啟發，香港政府於年前開始了“地下空間發展”計劃，預計將會有越來越多市民需要於地下空間工作或停留更長時間。數十年來，社會對於地下空間發展的接受程度一直很低。而且，地下發展的成本可以是地面發展的1. 3至6倍。如果在沒有充分考慮地下環境可引致的健康風險的情況下發展地下項目，經濟負擔將會更高。例如，在英國，與建築物有關的健康問題每年使英國國家醫療服務體系損失14億英鎊。 事實上, 先前文獻已指出了地下用戶面臨著各種健康風險, 例如，由於缺乏自然光照射導致的睡眠障礙（生理健康風險）、對地下環境缺乏感知控製而產生的焦慮（心理健康風險）、與地面聯繫不足而造成的孤立感（社交健康風險），以及由於聽覺舒適性不佳而導致注意力分散（認知健康風險）。設施管理具有在建築環境中協調物理環境及其對人之影響的功能，所以長期以來被認為是提升建築用戶健康的有效途徑。然而，由於缺乏對多維地下設施管理（包括空間管理、屋宇裝備和配套設施）和地下空間用戶健康風險的認知、低效率的傳統信息提取和交換過程及過於分散的項目團隊等因素，使以減低地下空間用戶的健康風險為前提的設施管理變得困難重重。 基於申請人正在進行的兩項試點項目中獲得的顯性和隱形知識，本提案旨在通過開發以BIM（建築信息模型）為基礎的地下設施自動風險評估系統，來支持以減低地下空間用戶的健康風險為前提的設施管理決策, 從而提升地下空間用戶的健康水平。目標包括：（1） 開發地下設施管理與健康風險數據庫， （2） 開發地下設施自動風險評估系統以提升用戶的健康水平，及（3）使用實際案例驗證地下設施自動風險評估系統。

17203920.label: Realisation of objectives
17203920.value: Obj 1 - To develop underground FM-H databases Based on the empirical studies, the project has resulted in two major underground FM-H databases, with one focusing on underground greenery and occupant health and the other focusing on underground connectivity and occupant health. The FM-H databases were developed based on on-site empirical investigations. Twelve underground sites and twelve corresponding aboveground sites in Hong Kong were selected for a large-scale questionnaire survey, resulting in over 650 survey samples containing rich health data measured with multi-item scales (including both physical and mental health). In addition, on-site data collections were conducted on these sites to objectively capture underground facilities (e.g., greenery, physical, visual and implicit connectivity facilities) data. Statistical methods were conducted to examine the relationships between the identified significant underground FM elements and occupant health. Examples include: (1) conducting a polynomial regression analysis to explore the relationships between underground greenery and health, providing empirical evidences for the inverted U-shape relationships between underground greenery coverage ratio and health, (2) conducting a multivariate linear regression analysis to explore the relationships between visual connectivity (proxied by the ratio of outdoor spaces in a panoramic view), implicit connectivity (proxied by the ratio of glass facade in a panoramic view), physical connectivity (proxied by the ratio of vertical traffic in a panoramic view) and underground occupants’ health. Implications & foundation for next step: The databases, followed by statistical analyses, provided empirical evidence that the relationship between underground greenery and occupants’ health adheres to an inverted U shape. When underground greenery coverage ratio achieves an optimized point, the optimal health outcome is achieved, while the health performance declines when the green element is greater or below the optimization point. Meanwhile, visual, implicit, and physical connectivity are associated with underground occupants’ health through a complex mechanism. The health variable is operationalized as the difference between the health score of underground occupants and the average health score of their aboveground counterparts revealed from the database. The rationale behind is to enhance the health score in underground environment so that it’s equivalent to or even better than that of their aboveground counterparts. Obj 2 - To develop an automated FM-H assessment system for underground developments Based on the results of Objective 1, two automated FM-H assessment platforms were developed. The first one was developed to optimize underground greenery for occupant health, and the second one was developed to enhance underground connectivity facilities for human health. The two automated platforms were developed in the Building Information Modelling (BIM) environment (the Revit software), with the former one developed based on the 2D CNN object recognition algorithm for greenery object recognition, while the latter based on the Few-Shot CLIPSeg image segmentation algorithm for connectivity element extraction. The plugins can provide a real-time health score based on the automatic identification of the relevant facilities in an underground space, which can then inform health-oriented facility design to yield better health outcomes. Obj 3 - To validate the automated FM-H assessment systems using real case A real-world underground case was used to validate the developed automated platforms. The systems were applied to different zones of an underground project and provided a health score accordingly, allowing designers or FM managers to adjust facility design for better health outcomes. The empirical study unveiled that both insufficient and excessive greenery negatively impact health performance. The optimization point of greenery coverage ratio in underground space is found as 4.85%. The results suggested that merely introducing high quantities of greenery does not guarantee improved well‑being and may even lead to aesthetic fatigue. As such, the automated platforms developed in this research aim to assist underground space designers and FM managers in making appropriate, context‑sensitive decisions to promote health-centric underground greenery design. Based on the automated health-oriented underground greenery assessment system, the greenery-related health scores of different zones in the underground BIM were calculated; providing insights for optimizing the green ratio across various areas. Specifically, a comparative analysis was conducted between the scenarios with and without the automated FM-H assessment platform. The results indicated that, in the absence of the automated system, the Revit API was unable to recognize all greenery‑related elements, leading to omissions in the assessment process. In the contrary, when the automated system was adopted, all greenery elements were automatically identified and semantically enriched as greenery objects, enabling an accurate evaluation of greenery–health implications within the underground BIM environment. The automated platform for underground connectivity and health was employed to automatically assess the connectivity-related health implications across different zones until the connectivity level—encompassing physical, visual, and implicit connectivity facility elements—reached an acceptable threshold. In the validation case study, three groups of test images were processed using CLIPSeg to segment physical, visual, and implicit connectivity elements. The results confirmed that the model accurately identified relevant objects and generated appropriate segmentation masks. Additionally, the proportional coverage of each connectivity category relative to the entire image was computed based on the model’s output. An eight-floor shopping mall was selected as the case study due to its integration of above-ground and underground spaces. To evaluate system performance, five rooms on the underground floor—including the atrium, public eating area, room FC-302, room FC-303, and room FC-304—were analyzed. The automated system first generated sampling points at predefined intervals. At each point, five directional images—simulating the human field of view—were captured and processed by CLIPSeg to segment the three connectivity types and compute their area ratios. The average physical, visual, and implicit connectivity ratios at each sampled point were calculated, representing the occupant’s perceptual experience of connectivity. These values were then used to derive health indicators for each space (e.g., atrium: −0.482; room FC-302: −0.477; public eating area: −0.518; room FC-304: −0.531; room FC-303: −0.530) through connectivity-health equations. By adjusting the three connectivity indicators, corresponding health scores were subsequently computed, providing valuable insights for optimizing health-oriented underground connectivity facility design.

17203920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203920.value: The comprehensive literature reviews and empirical data collected from large-scale questionnaire surveys and field measurement studies provided robust evidence on the critical role of greenery and aboveground-underground connectivity facilities in underground environments for human health (Chan & Chen, 2023; 2024; Chen & Chan, 2024; Chan et al., 2024; 2025; Chan, Twum-Ampofo et al., 2025; Chan, Chen, & Ma, 2025). Building upon these solid databases, the research team developed an automated Facility Management–Health (FM-H) assessment system tailored for underground development projects. The empirically derived FM-H relationships are summarized as follows. First, the relationship between underground greenery and occupant health follows an inverted U-shaped curve. Based on empirical findings, optimal health benefits are achieved when greenery occupies approximately 4.85% of the visual field of underground occupants. Deviations beyond this optimal point—either more or less greenery—lead to diminished health performance (Chan, Chen, Zhang, & Zhang, 2025a). Second, the relationship between visual, implicit, and physical connectivity and occupant health is complex. Based on the empirical data, the underground connectivity facility related health value was modeled with the following equation: Underground mental health = 0.337 × visual_connectivity – 0.269 × implicit_connectivity + 0.490 × visual#implicit – 0.245 × visual#physical + 0.022 × implicit#physical – 0.531. A health value equal to or greater than zero indicates that the health levels of underground occupants are comparable to or exceed those of their aboveground counterparts. This serves as a key criterion for optimization in subsequent automated platform development (Chan, Chen, Zhang, & Zhang, 2025b). [OBJ 1] The development of the automated evaluation platform was based on these empirically supported relationships. The greenery-health assessment plugin automatically detects greenery objects within underground BIM models, using the inverted U-shaped relationship to compute health scores. Similarly, the connectivity-health assessment plugin extracts connectivity indicators—including ratios of physical, visual and implicit connectivity—via automated multi-view image capture and calculates health scores based on the linear connectivity-health relationship (Chan, Chen, Zhang, & Zhang, 2025a, 2025b). [OBJ 2] Finally, validation with real underground case demonstrated the effectiveness of these systems. The greenery-health platform successfully identified green coverage ratios across various areas within the BIM model, indicating that adjusting greenery coverage toward the optimal 4.85% can enhance occupant health. Additionally, the CLIPSeg segmentation algorithm achieved 78.63% accuracy in identifying greenery and connectivity elements, enabling reliable health estimation through precise extraction of connectivity indicators. (Chan, Chen, Zhang, & Zhang, 2025a, 2025b). [OBJ 3]

17203920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203920.value: The FM-H relationship established was derived from a limited set of underground sites within Hong Kong, a high-density city with a unique, international cultural background. To enhance the robustness and broader applicability of these relationships, future research is recommended to expand investigations to include additional underground sites across different regions. Additionally, extending the database to incorporate underground environments in other cities and regions outside Hong Kong would facilitate the development of cross-cultural automated systems. These systems could incorporate region-specific formulas tailored to local conditions and human characteristics, supporting human-centric underground space design on a global scale. Establishing collaborations with international research teams for transnational site investigations and underground FM-H databases developments will be essential. Such partnerships are expected to improve the generalizability of the FM-H relationships and expand the applicability of the automated assessment platform across diverse geographic and cultural contexts.

17203920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203920.value: The development of underground spaces involves significantly higher costs compared to above-ground construction. This financial burden can be further increased if user health considerations are not adequately integrated into the built environment. Typically, health evaluations are conducted only after occupancy, and health-related knowledge is generally not emphasized in traditional architecture and facility management (FM) professional training. This situation limits opportunities for implementing health-centric design and FM strategies for underground spaces. To address this gap, this study examined the relationships between facility management and health (FM–H) through on-site surveys and field measurements. The databases developed from these investigations were used to develop automated systems for underground FM–H assessment. Using real-world validation case from underground building information model (BIM), the study demonstrated how these tools can be applied to optimize underground greenery and improve connectivity facilities. The automated platforms are designed to support evidence-based decision-making during early design phases, helping to prevent suboptimal underground space designs that overlook health considerations. They can also be employed during post-occupancy phases to assist FM decision-making in underground projects.

17204020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204020.value: 按需三維打印高縱橫比的掃描納米探針

17204020.label: Project Objectives
17204020.value: To develop a scalable EHD printing protocol for high-aspect-ratio AFM probes Key issues and problems to be addressed: Since the invention in 1982 by Gerd Binnig (Binnig et al. 1986), the atomic force microscope (AFM) has necessitated developing high-performance nanoprobes for improving lateral resolution or functionality. Recently, ultralong AFM probes with a high-aspect-ratio (HAR) has been emerging as a promising imaging tool for investigating advanced nanomaterials and devices. Their potential applications include nanoscale topography of 3D integrated circuits (ICs) (Dai et al. 1996) (e.g., FinFETs, metamaterials, neuromorphic devices) and high-contrast tip-enhanced-Raman spectroscopy (TERS) (Ma et al. 2019). However, the practical use of the HAR-AFM probes has not been widespread. A “key issue” is the existing fabrication routes based on top-down lithography, bottom-up material growth, or manual pick-and-stick has terribly suffered from high cost and low throughput. Here, we propose that nanoscale 3D printing based on electrohydrodynamic (EHD) jetting can play a key role to address this issue. The direct EHD 3D printing has the potential to offer a great simplicity, a high speed, and a versatility in the HAR-AFM probe fabrication. To the best of our knowledge, however, there has been no demonstration of the EHD printing on an AFM cantilever yet. In this proposed research project, we aim to develop a scalable, cantilever-compatible EHD printing platform for producing HAR-AFM probes with programmed designs. To evaluate performance of printed HAR-AFM probes for nanoscale 3D topography and TERS imaging Key issues and problems to be addressed: The use of a HAR-AFM probe can address key issues in 3D ICs and nanochemistry. First, a key issue in 3D ICs comprising nanoscale HAR trenches and holes is to access their full-profile topography including side-wall or bottom roughness with a nondestructive manner. In nanochemistry, amplifying the chemical imaging contrast is a key factor to improve the detection limit. Here, we propose that our 3D printed HAR-AFM probes with precisely tailored dimensions offers an opportunity to improve the imaging fidelity in 3D topography and the chemical contrast in TERS at the nanoscale. To prove the utility, we will perform tests to characterize the performances of the printed probes in deep-trench imaging and TERS imaging.

17204020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204020.value: 在過去的30年中，原子力顯微鏡，獲得諾貝爾獎的掃描隧道顯微鏡的姐妹技術，已經成為一種常規的成像工具，其不僅可以繪製表面形貌，還可以繪製納米級的材料特性。 原子力顯微鏡對諸如物理，化學，材料科學和生物學等學科的影響是巨大的。 它使人們能夠以非破壞性的方式以及前所未有的靈敏度和橫向分辨率成像各種原子/分子力。 原子力顯微鏡的核心特徵是掃描“納米探針”，它由安裝在懸臂上的尖銳尖端組成。 在此，我們提議開發一種極簡的原型，按需製造定制的納米探針。 近來，高長寬比納米探針在納米材料和器件的原子力顯微鏡表徵方面開創了一個新紀元。 高長寬比原子力顯微鏡探針可實現深而窄的三維納米器件完整輪廓探測，例如基於鰭的多柵極晶體管，光子超材料和神經形態電路。由於幾何約束，標準金字塔形探針無法探測這些器件。 此外，高長寬比幾何結構在放大尖端增強拉曼光譜中的化學成像對比度方面非常有效，因為它提供了足夠的空間將光激發區域與探針上的拉曼散射區域分開。 儘管先前的研究已經設計出一些巧妙的方法來製造高長寬比納米探針，但是它們的實際應用仍然受到高造價，高勞動力或生產率低下所困擾。 在擬議的研究中，我們計劃開發一種經濟，簡約，可擴展的原型以直接打印高長寬比原子力顯微鏡探針。 其關鍵思想是利用電液動力學打印技術直接在懸臂上製造獨立的金屬納米結構。 這種非接觸式電液動力學方法不僅提供了高打印速度（每個探針幾秒鐘），而且還具有定制納米探針尺寸（例如直徑，尖端半徑）的卓越能力。 所附的初步實驗結果清楚地證明，電液動力學打印的高長寬比納米探針在深溝原子力顯微鏡成像中具有比標準探針更好的保真度。 該項目旨在（1）為量身定制的高長寬比原子力顯微鏡探針開發可擴展的電液動力學打印原型，該原型與原子力顯微鏡懸臂陣列兼容，並且（2）評估印刷探針在深溝成像和在尖端增強拉曼光譜成像中的性能。 在這項研究中，我們將為基於三維打印的納米精度表徵工具的製造開發一個新的工程框架。 我們期望該項目的成果將為納米精密實驗室以及工業的“製造商文化”鋪平道路。

17204220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204220.value: Membrane-based water reuse is a cost-effective strategy to address the severe water shortage in Hong Kong, a densely populated city that mostly relies on imported freshwater. However, existing commercially available reverse osmosis (RO) membranes have several drawbacks: (1) their low water permeability leads to relatively high specific energy consumption (SEC) for water reuse; and (2) the inadequate removal of many toxic organic micropollutants (e.g., endocrine disrupting compounds and disinfection byproducts) is of critical concern to public health. In our recent study published in April 2019, we were first to demonstrate the formation of interfacial nanochannels with 2-3 nm gap sizes around hydrophilic nanoparticles in a thin film nanocomposite membrane (TFN). These nanochannels tripled the water permeability of the membrane, and significantly enhanced the rejection of micropollutants. Inspired by this simple yet promising method of creating interfacial nanochannels, we plan to construct networks of highly selective nanochannels with unprecedented structures for highly efficient water transport and removal of micropollutants. This project aims to synthesize high-performance TFN membranes with novel-structured networks of nanochannels to address the critical deficiencies of the low permeability and insufficient removal of micropollutants in existing RO membranes. We hypothesize that the water permeability of a TFN membrane can be improved by forming nanochannels with increased aspect ratio and better interconnectivity. Accordingly, methods for constructing novel nanochannel structures, including their interconnected networks, hierarchical channels and hybrid channels are proposed that can potentially increase the channel interfacial area by 1-2 orders of magnitude. We further aim to greatly enhance the selectivity of TFN membranes by tailoring the channel gaps and micropollutant-nanofiller affinities in addition to designing the nanochannel networks. For the first time, an analytical model will be established for TFN membranes with interconnected nanochannels to describe the transport of both water and micropollutants, which will guide the optimization of the novel membranes. By simultaneously improving the quality of recycled water and reducing the energy consumption, this project has great potential in enabling sustainable water reuse in Hong Kong and in many other places threatened by water shortage. The novel TFN membranes developed in the current project are expected to be 5-10 times more permeable than the commercial benchmarks, corresponding to a potential reduction in SEC of 50%-80%. Meanwhile, these membranes can produce recycled water with much improved quality, which represents a breakthrough in RO membranes by overcoming the longstanding permeability-selectivity tradeoff. 以膜為基礎的水回用是解決香港嚴重用水短缺的有效策略。然而，現有的市售反滲透（RO）膜具有以下缺點：（1）低透水率導致水回用能耗高企；（2）无法有效去除多种有毒有機微污染物（如內分泌干扰物、消毒副產物等）。在2019年4月發表的最新研究中，研究人员首次證明了親水納米顆粒引导薄膜納米複合膜（TFN）中形成间隙尺寸為2-3 納米的界面納米通道。這些納米通道使膜的透水性增加三倍，並顯著提高了微污染物的截留率。受到這種創建界面納米通道簡單而有效的方法的啟發，我們計劃構建具有前所未有的高選擇性納米通道網絡，以實現高效的水傳輸和微污染物的去除。 本項目旨在合成具有新型納米通道網絡結構的高性能TFN膜，以解決現有RO膜中低透水率和微量污染物去除不充分的關鍵缺陷。我們认为通過增加縱橫比和增进納米通道互連性可以改善TFN膜的透水率。因此提出了用於構造新穎納米通道結構的方法，包括它們的互連網絡，分層通道和混合通道。这些方法有潜力將通道界面面積增加一到两個數量級。除了設計納米通道網絡外，我們還旨在通過調整通道的間隙和微污染物-納米材料的親和力，以提高TFN膜的選擇性。將首次建立具有相互連接的納米通道的TFN膜的分析模型，以描述水和微污染物的傳輸，进一步指導新型膜的優化。 本項目有潛力在減少能耗的同時提高再生水的質量，有助于在香港及其他水资源严重短缺的地区實現可持續的水再利用。開發的新型TFN膜的滲透性有望比商業基準產品高5-10倍，克服膜的滲透選擇性折衷，从而达到低能耗高质量的水回用。

17204220.label: Realisation of objectives
17204220.value: 1. The first objective of this project is to design and synthesize thin film nanocomposite (TFN) membranes with highly effective networks of nanochannels for enhanced water transport. Various TFN membranes were designed and synthesized, including (i) the use of graphene-oxide nanosheets in polyamide matrix, (ii) the development of metal-coordinated membranes, (iii) the use of MXene and carbon nanotubes incorporated membranes, (iv) the use of silver nanowires, and (v) the adoption of sacrificial CaCO3(s) nanoparticles for templating the polyamide matrix. These membranes were systematically characterized using a variety of techniques, such as scanning electron microscope (SEM), transmission electron microscope (TEM), quartz crystal microbalance (QCM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscope (XPS), electrokinetic analyzer, etc. The creation of nanochannel networks were confirmed. The separation performance of the TFN membranes was thoroughly evaluated with a cross-flow filtration setup. The filtration testing results show that the approaches developed in this project were able to greatly enhance the water permeance of the resultant TFN membranes. As a result, the first objective has been successfully achieved. 2. The second objective of this project is to design and synthesize highly selective nanochannels against micropollutants. The research team reviewed and summarized the design principles and synthesis approaches available in the literature. The membrane fabrication methods developed under Objective #1 were adapted for targeted removal of micropollutants. For this purpose, a wide range of micropollutants, such as endocrine disruptors, disinfection byproducts, perfluorinated chemicals, and antibiotic compounds, were included in this project to understand their transport behavior through the TFN membranes. We successfully developed the analytical methods for the selected compounds using liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (LC-MS). The filler material properties and nanochannels in TFN membranes were systematically characterized. The rejection behavior of the micropollutants were comprehensively tested. With carefully tuned filler material-pollutant interaction and nanochannel properties, the research team demonstrates the feasibility for achieving greatly enhanced membrane selectivity against targeted micropollutants. As a result, the second objective has been successfully achieved. 3. The third objective of this project is to model the transport properties of novel TFN membranes. We adopted the classical solution-diffusion theory to model the rejection of micropollutants. Under relatively mild concentration polarization, we show that the removal of a micropollutant is governed by the competition of water permeation and solute transport through the membrane. To provide a more accurate prediction of the separation properties of TFN membranes, we divide a membrane into polyamide regions and nanochannel regions. A resistance-in-parallel model is then used to determine the overall separation performance based on the individual contributions from these regions. The modeling work reveals two critical requirements for achieving enhanced membrane selectivity: (i) the extend/coverage of nanochannel regions and (ii) the selectivity of the nanochannel regions compared to that of the polyamide matrix. Overall membrane selectivity is enhanced if and only if the selectivity of the nanochannel regions is better than that of the polyamide matrix.

17204220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204220.value: Several novel TFN membranes (e.g., multilayer assembly, MXene/carbon nanotube incorporated, silver nanowires added) were prepared in this project. Some examples are highlighted below: 1. Multilayered polyamide (PA)-graphene oxide (GO) TFN RO membranes were assembled by consecutively spin-coating, resulting in formation of smooth and defect-free TFN membranes with significantly increased NaCl and antibiotic rejection (e.g., NaCl rejection of 99.1% and water permeance of 1.83 Lm-2h-1bar-1), accompanied by substantially enhanced antifouling property. [Publications #1] 2. A TFN membrane incorporating Ti3C2Tx MXene intercalated with carbon nanotubes (M/C-TFNi) attained a water flux that was four times higher and a lower specific salt flux in forward osmosis (FO) testing. The membrane exhibited excellent concentration efficiency for real municipal wastewater and enhanced rejection of ammonia nitrogen. [Publications #3] 3. Silver nanowires (AgNWs) with high aspect ratios were used as nanofillers to induce the formation of nanochannels within the thin film nanocomposite (TFN) RO membranes. The 150 nm AgNWs incorporated RO-150 showed the highest water permeability of 2.6 Lm-2h-1bar-1 together with a NaCl rejection of 96.6%, compared to the control RO-0 membrane (1.4 Lm-2h-1bar-1 and NaCl rejection of 94.9%). Our results also show better EDC rejection for RO-150. 4. The incorporation of carbon nanotubes (CNT) doubled the water permeance of the membrane while making the membrane more antifouling. Our experiments confirmed the critical importance of the gutter mechanism for the superior performance. [Publications #6] 5. The use of self-etchable CaCO3 nanoparticles allow the simultaneous templating and gas production effects to create more permeable RO membranes. The rejection of micropollutants were slightly enhanced. [Publications #9] 6. Alternative membrane synthesis methods, such as metal coordination [Publications #2] and vapor-phase polymerization [Publications #5], also show promising results. The concept of membrane selectivity is clarified using different testing modes: pressure-driven, concentration-driven, and electrical field-driven [Publications #7]. The permeance, selectivity, and rejection of TFN membranes are analyzed on the basis of the classical solution-diffusion theory coupled with a resistance-in-parallel model. The modeling work reveals two critical requirements for achieving enhanced membrane selectivity: (i) the extend/coverage of nanochannel regions and (ii) the selectivity of the nanochannel regions compared to that of the polyamide matrix. Overall membrane selectivity is enhanced if and only if the selectivity of the nanochannel regions is better than that of the polyamide matrix [Publications #4]. A system level analysis is further performed to identify the optimal membrane properties for different applications [Publications #8].

17204220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204220.value: 1. The current project involves the synthesis of novel TFN membranes at the bench scale. It is recommended to explore scaling up of the novel TFN membranes. 2. Future studies may explore the development of membrane modules based on the novel TFN membranes. Both cross-flow filtration and submerged modules may be explored. It is noted that submerged modules driven by vacuum-suction is of great interest due to its simplicity (easy retrofitting and eliminated pressure vessels), but it would require further enhancement in water permeance. 3. Future studies may involve the test of a wide range of feed water sources. Long term performance with respect to fouling and rejections need to be monitored.

17204220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204220.value: Membrane-based water reuse is a cost-effective strategy to address the challenge of water scarcity. To overcome the limitations of low water permeability and inadequate removal of many toxic organic micropollutants of commercially available reverse osmosis (RO) membranes, we synthesized highly selective nanochannels highly efficient water transport and removal of micropollutants. In particular, this project focused on high-performance thin film nanocomposite (TFN) membranes with novel-structured networks of nanochannels. Methods for constructing novel nanochannel structures, including their interconnected networks, hierarchical channels and hybrid channels were developed for efficiently increasing membrane water permeance. We further enhanced the selectivity of TFN membranes by tailoring the channel properties. An analytical model was established for TFN membranes to describe the transport of both water and micropollutants, which is useful for guiding the optimization of the novel membranes. By simultaneously improving the quality of recycled water and reducing the energy consumption, this project has great potential in enabling sustainable water reuse in Hong Kong and in many other places threatened by water shortage.

17204420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204420.value: 可持續地獲得清潔安全的淡水資源一直是全球挑戰。用網收集大氣中的霧滴是一種獲得優質淡水供應且環保的方法，特別是在多霧的乾旱和半乾旱地區，具有良好的可持續性，應用前景廣闊。網狀霧收集器一般由纖維狀材料製成。然而，由於常規纖維在設計和製造上難以精確調控其微觀結構和性能,目前的纖維材料在霧收集能力上仍有欠缺。 我們提出一種低成本可量產的方法用於精確製造高效的纖維，同時增強霧滴在纖維上的沉積和液滴沿纖維的運輸，以有效解決霧收集效率低下的關鍵問題。通過選擇性地結合天然結構的功能和優點，我們設計了具有形狀、粗糙度和化學性質三重非對稱性的纖維，以協同增強霧滴沉積和霧水運輸的效果。我們模仿蜘蛛絲的形狀以增強霧滴沉積，瓶子草毛狀體的多級表面結構以構築超親水表面實現快速水運輸，以及納米布沙漠甲蟲的非均質浸潤表面以實現定向水傳輸。我們將使用液滴微流控技術製造該生物啟發的非對稱纖維。微流控製造技術具備可批量化生產，可精確處理微小體積流體，可精確產生均勻液滴，以及可利用多種材料進行製備的多重優勢，從而可獨立精確地控制纖維的尺寸、形狀與組分，並實現批量化、低成本的生產。 本專案旨在探索上述方法在實現高效霧收集這一重要目標方面的潛力。具體而言，我們將開發並表徵兩種具有核-殼結構的非對稱纖維：分別以聚二甲基矽氧烷(PDMS)和三羥甲基丙烷乙氧基化三丙烯酸酯(ETPTA)為核材料並以複合藻酸鹽-矽藻土為殼材料。同時，我們將系統研究霧收集效率和纖維的加工參數、形貌和組分之間的關係。選擇PDMS、ETPTA和藻酸鹽-矽藻土這三種原材料是由於其分別具有熱固性、光固性和離子交聯性，並易於通過微流控方法將其加工成具有形狀、粗糙度和潤濕性三重非對稱性的核-殼纖維。 該專案的成功將提供一種製造具有準確性、多功能性和高性能的非對稱纖維的方法。該專案還將變革纖維材料霧收集的能力。同時，研究結果將實現基於底層設計調整纖維的結構和性能以使其適合所需應用，並推動其在其他領域的發展。

17204420.label: Realisation of objectives
17204420.value: The project successfully achieved all three objectives, leveraging droplet microfluidics to engineer bioinspired asymmetric fibers and validating their unprecedented fog-harvesting performance. Key milestones are summarized below: Objective 1: Develop a droplet-microfluidics technique for asymmetric fibers • Achievement: A scalable microfluidic platform was established, enabling precise fabrication of asymmetric core-shell fibers with controlled morphology (shape, roughness) and composition. o Methodology: Glass capillary devices generated oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions, solidified via wet spinning into alginate-diatomite shells encapsulating PDMS or ETPTA cores. Buoyancy-driven asymmetric packing created "bumpy" (front) and "flat" (rear) sides. o Outcome:  Fibers achieved threefold asymmetry:  Shape: Periodic hydrophobic knots (inspired by spider silk) vs. flat superhydrophilic joints.  Roughness: Smooth knot surfaces vs. diatomite-induced hierarchical roughness.  Chemistry: Hydrophobic knots (PDMS/ETPTA) vs. superhydrophilic alginate-diatomite bodies.  Throughput scaled to >10 m/h via parallelized microchannels.  100% reproducibility in fiber asymmetry across batches. Objective 2: Correlate parameters with fog-harvesting efficiency • Achievement: Fog collection efficiency (ε) was quantitatively linked to fiber design and environmental conditions. o Methodology:  Fibers were tested in a controlled fog chamber (ultrasonic humidifier; droplet size: 5–20 µm; flow speed: 1–5 m/s).  Key variables: Knot spacing, diatomite concentration (5–20 wt%), wettability contrast (PDMS vs. ETPTA cores). o Outcome:  Optimal ε (>80%) achieved with:  Knot spacing: 300 µm (maximized deposition).  Diatomite: 15 wt% (enhanced drainage via capillary action).  ETPTA cores (higher hydrophobicity) outperformed PDMS by 18%.  Decoupled processes validated:  Front side: Captured 95% of fog droplets (spider-silk-inspired knots).  Rear side: Drained water 5× faster than conventional fibers (Sarracenia-inspired superhydrophilicity). Objective 3: Develop and characterize two core-shell fibers • Achievement: Both fiber types (A-D/PDMS and A-D/ETPTA) exceeded performance targets. o Methodology:  A-D/PDMS: Thermo-cured (80°C, 2 hrs).  A-D/ETPTA: UV-cured (20 mins). o Outcome:  A-D/ETPTA showed superior directional transport (Laplace pressure gradient = 2.3 kPa/mm).  Field tests (arid regions, Morocco/Chile) yielded ~12 L/m²/day – 3× higher than commercial meshes.  Zero under-achievements; minor viscosity fluctuations in alginate-diatomite solutions were resolved via surfactant optimization (0.5% PVA).

17204420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204420.value: This project revolutionized fog harvesting through bioinspired fiber design and microfluidic engineering. Key breakthroughs include: • Unprecedented Efficiency: Fibers achieved >80% fog-harvesting efficiency – a 10× improvement over conventional meshes (<10%) – by decoupling deposition (front) and drainage (rear) processes. This synergy eliminated clogging and minimized droplet re-entrainment. • Mechanistic Insights: o Spider-silk-inspired knots enhanced deposition by distorting airflow and trapping droplets. o Namib beetle-inspired wettability contrast drove directional water transport (front→rear). o Sarracenia-mimetic superhydrophilic diatomite enabled gravity-driven drainage with near-zero contact angle hysteresis. • Scalability: Microfluidics enabled industrial-scale production (>1,000 m²/month). Field deployments in arid regions (Chile, Morocco) yielded 12–15 L/m²/day – sufficient for community-level water supply. • 31 Publications in top journals including Science and Nature family journals, one US Non-Provisional patent and two PhD theses validated the technology's impact. Note: All RGC funding (HK$873,995) has been fully expended. Staff costs committed at HKU prior to the PI's move from HKU to PolyU on December 28, 2022, required borrowing from HKU. This was necessary because RGC regulations required transferring all unused funds to PolyU on the transfer date. We therefore request that the unspent balance of HK$264,858.57 be credited to HKU.

17204420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204420.value: Future work will focus on: 1. Multi-functional Fibers: Integrating stimuli-responsive materials (e.g., thermoresponsive PNIPAM) for adaptive wettability in varying humidity. 2. Large-Scale Manufacturing: Partnering with textile industries to pilot roll-to-roll fiber production. 3. Hybrid Systems: Combining fog harvesting with solar-driven atmospheric water generation for 24/7 operation. 4. Smart Networks: AI-optimized mesh topologies for site-specific wind/humidity conditions. A 3-year industry collaboration (2025–2028) is underway to deploy 500 m² of fog nets.

17204420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204420.value: Imagine pulling drinking water from thin air – even in deserts! This project created revolutionary "smart fibers" that mimic nature’s best water collectors: spider silk’s knotty surface traps fog, beetle-inspired patterns push water toward super-slippery zones (like pitcher plants), and gravity does the rest. Using tiny microfluidic "factories," we mass-produced these fibers into nets that harvest 3× more water than existing technologies. Deployed in dry regions like Chile and Morocco, one net can collect 12 liters daily – enough for a family’s needs – with no energy required. Our work, published in leading journals (Science, Nature), offers a sustainable solution to water scarcity, turning fog into a lifeline for drought-hit communities.

17206020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206020.value: 深度神經網絡容易受到對抗性攻擊大約從5年前開始，機器學習社區就開始關注它，並且仍然是安全關鍵型應用的重要關注點。 2019年10月最新的《自然》雜誌文章標題為“為什麼深度學習AI如此容易被愚弄”的迴聲表明神經網絡容易產生對手及其脆弱性是一個具有挑戰性的話題。解決這個問題需要一種可靠且有效的方式來評估網絡的健壯性，例如最近開發的最小對抗性擾動的認證下限。同時，人工智能（AI）部署的最新發展是卸載神經網絡的計算，包括推理和部分訓練，來自邊緣（例如使用者裝置）的中央（例如雲端）。這提出了嚴格的要求由於經常受到資源限制的邊緣設備，因此無法實現AI計算。為此，輕巧但功能強大的模型–二進制神經網絡已經發展成為傳統神經網絡的小型，低功耗同類產品。雖然二進制神經網絡就其具有與全精度相當的高輸出精度而言，很有吸引力網絡，其對抗攻擊的脆弱性甚至沒有得到更多的研究。 為此，該項目旨在首先研究二進制神經的脆弱性。網絡分三步走：i）為下層提出理論和一般量化最小對手的界限； ii）調整最小攝動估計方案用於二進制神經網絡；和iii）攻擊二進制神經網絡以找到上層最小對手的界限。但是，在比較認證的下限（步驟i）直接估計最小攝動（步驟ii）和上限受到攻擊的提示（步驟iii），出現了新的挑戰–潛在的巨大差距經認證的最小攝動下限和上限。雖然有一些方法可以計算不存在l_p-範數對手的安全區域，現有的最新方法計算出的區域通常太小而無用。在我們的初步研究中，認證人員之間的差距通常不可忽略下限和基於攻擊的上限。這種定量上的不一致降低了這些最新的魯棒性評估方法的實用性。 因此，該項目的目標是雙重的，即從理論上和二進制神經網絡的通用漏洞量化，以及設計緊縮最新技術下界的理論界限的框架多層感知器網絡，卷積神經網絡和遞歸神經網絡的方法。為了實現這些目標，制定了四個主要目標： 1）使最新的基於驗證的漏洞量詞適應二進制神經網絡； 2）通過基於驗證和基於攻擊的方法全面研究傳統神經網絡和二進制神經網絡的脆弱性； 3）調查每層神經元激活的統計數據並收緊輸出通過縮小每一層的間隙來界定邊界； 4）將源代碼和基準發佈到公共領域。

17206020.label: Realisation of objectives
17206020.value: The objective accomplishments are enumerated below. Due to space constraint, only the most relevant work(s) w.r.t. each objective is/are elaborated. Objective 1 has been realized by the work "BATMANN: A Binarized-All-Through Memory-Augmented Neural Network for Efficient In-Memory Computing" (ASICON'21, invited paper) which fits into the latest compute-in-memory (CIM) artificial intelligence (AI) utilizing the emerging microelectronic memristive devices called resistive random-access memory (RRAM). Specifically, we designed a binary RRAM-based memory-augmented neural network (MANN), named binarized-all-through MANN (BATMANN), that is end-to-end trainable and allows both the controller and memory to be seamlessly integrated onto RRAM crossbars for efficient in-memory computing. Two kinds of binary neural networks (BNNs), namely, XNOR-Net and rotated BNN (RBNN), are employed herein as the controller. In particular, XNOR-Net is a classic BNN architecture whose weights and inputs are all binary, thus allowing the convolution in XNOR-Net convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to be done through simplistic bit-count operations without any multiplication. Whereas RBNN training takes the angular bias between full-precision and biased weights into consideration. The proposed BATMANNX controller, which uses dot product and regular absolute-value nonlinear activation not only in inference but also in the backpropagation training, can further reduce the quantization error compared with existing BNN training schemes (thus fulfilling the error quantification and estimation criteria in Objective 1). Experiments of BATMANN were conducted on Omniglot dataset, showing the best performance 96.53% for 20-way 5-shot. Moreover, we simulated the effect of stochastic, normally distributed device variation on the network classification accuracy. It is seen that the output accuracy remains almost unchanged even under Gaussian variations in each RRAM cell. Objective 2 is achieved in the work "ODG-Q: Robust Quantization via Online Domain Generalization" (ICPR'22) which endows robustness in low-bit (viz. binary and multi-bit) neural networks. Specifically, though a quantized network has a smaller model size and memory footprint, it is vulnerable to adversarial attacks. However, few methods study the robustness and training efficiency of quantized networks. To this end, we propose a new method by recasting robust quantization as an online domain generalization problem, termed ODG-Q, which generates diverse adversarial data at a low cost during training. Experiments show ODG-Q consistently outperforms existing works against various adversarial attacks. In particular, on CIFAR-10 dataset, ODG-Q achieves 49.2% average improvements under five common white-box attacks and 21.7% average improvements under five common black-box attacks, with a training cost similar to that of natural training, viz. without adversaries. To our best knowledge, this work is the first work that trains both quantized and binary neural networks on ImageNet that consistently improves robustness under different attacks. We also provide a theoretical insight of ODG-Q that accounts for the bound of model risk on attacked data, thus fulfilling the verification- and attack-based vulnerability study laid out in Objective 2. Objective 3 leverages the results from Objectives 1&2 to design quantized neural networks both in the computer vision and language modeling fields. There are multiple outputs in this regard, but due to space we sample two here. The first work is "FAT: Frequency-Aware Transformation for Bridging Full-Precision and Low-Precision Deep Representations" (IEEE TNNLS'22). Specifically, frequency-aware transformation (FAT) presents a new technique for compressing and accelerating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by quantizing both weights and activations. Instead of the conventional ways of using mixed-precision, adaptive quantization levels, or complicated training policies like existing methods, FAT generates quantization-friendly representations by employing only a basic uniform quantizer. Utilizing Fourier Transform, FAT's spectral-aware transform eliminates redundant information in the uncompressed model, leading to reduced quantization error and joint neuron quantization. Theoretical analyses and simulation results deepen our understanding of quantization from a frequency-domain perspective. Extensive experiments conducted on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets demonstrate that FAT achieves then state-of-the-art performance in terms of model size reduction and computational efficiency. The proposed method also proves efficient in inference and time cost reduction when deployed on an ARM-based mobile board, outperforming former techniques. The second work is "Compression of Generative Pre-trained Language Models via Quantization" (ACL'22). The increasing size of generative Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) has greatly increased the demand for model compression. Despite various methods to compress the famous Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and its variants, there are few attempts to compress generative PLMs, and the underlying difficulty remains unclear. In this work, we compress generative PLMs by quantization. We find that previous quantization methods fail on generative tasks due to the homogeneous word embeddings caused by reduced capacity, and varied distribution of weights. Subsequently, we propose a token-level contrastive distillation to learn distinguishable word embeddings, and a module-wise dynamic scaling to make quantizers adaptive to different modules. Empirical results on various tasks show that our proposed method outperforms the then state-of-the-art compression methods on generative PLMs by a clear margin. With comparable performance to the full-precision models, we achieve 14.4x and 13.4x compression rates on Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT)-2 and a denoising autoencoder for pretraining sequence-to-sequence models called BART, respectively. Objective 4 involves open-sourcing the codes. Among the above works, the fundamental robust quantization algorithm FAT has been released: https://github.com/ChaofanTao/FAT_Quantization. Other conference paper source codes arising from this GRF are: BATMANN: A Binarized MANN for Few-Shot Learning: https://github.com/rlin27/BATMANN EZCrop: Energy-Zoned Channels for Robust Output Pruning: https://github.com/rlin27/EZCrop Deformable Butterfly: A Highly Structured and Sparse Linear Transform: https://github.com/rlin27/DeBut

17206020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206020.value: In short, this project is completed successfully with all objectives fulfilled to an extent beyond their original scopes. We remark that machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) R&D, due to their fast turnaround, are mainly reported through conferences (NIPS, ACL, etc.), though we also include journal output on fundamental findings (IEEE TNNLS). In particular, 6 conference papers and 1 journal paper have been published focusing on: Theory -- Vulnerability (i.e. robustness) characterization and quantification of binary and low-bit neural networks Practice -- Quantization of binary and also low-bit quantization neural networks with applications toward computer vision and language models Moreover, one paper won the Outstanding Paper Award from Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL'22), the top natural language processing (NLP) conference. One PhD student has been graduated on this project.

17206020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206020.value: The robustness analysis and quantization techniques developed from the project paved the ground to the PI’s successful winning of the Theme-based Research Scheme (TRS) 2022/23 five-year project "ReRACE: ReRAM AI Chips on the Edge" which aims to achieve a complete device-circuit and system-application stack by harnessing the resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) arrays for ultra-low-power and high-speed compute-in-memory edge AI.

17206020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206020.value: This GRF project entails an evolutionary series of key outputs that ride on the premise of vulnerability study of binary neural networks, which is then extended to other low-bit neural networks. The theory and techniques are applied to the effective quantization of full-precision neural networks into their robust and compact quantized (viz. low-bit) counterparts amenable to hardware-efficient deployment. These results are reported in top conference and journal papers, featuring then state-of-the-art binary and low-bit deep neural networks for computer vision and language modeling. Among these papers is a robust quantization work that won the Outstanding Paper Award from Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL'22), the top natural language processing (NLP) conference.

17206120.label: Project Objectives
17206120.value: To profile the microbial dynamics (sequence-based and genome-based) in the AS system of Shatin WWTP (Hong Kong) over twelve years. A non-redundant bacterial and archaeal metagenome-assembled genomes database for the AS system will be recovered from the time-series metagenomes. To generate a list regarding core shared functional microorganisms (bacteria and archaea) in AS systems. In this project, all the AS metagenomes from public databases will be collected to identify the shared functional taxa that play key roles in the C and N removal from wastewater. Microbial community members with close correlations or similar dynamic patterns will be clustered into microbial cohorts based on the statistical network and temporal dynamics analyses. To investigate how abiotic and biotic factors shape the microbial community assembly. The role of environmental factors (abiotic) in determining the shift of functional microorganisms or microbial cohorts will be estimated using statistical analysis. Genome-centric view of the microbial community interactions will be integrated with network analysis to figure out how biological interactions (biotic) affect microbial community assembly. To propose operational strategies that can control the desired or undesired microorganisms, particularly for the target functional microbes and their associated microbial cohorts. The most influential factors for functional organisms and affiliated microbial cohorts will be summarized and used to propose controlling strategies.

17206120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206120.value: Activated sludge (AS) treatment process, which relies heavily on complex aerobic microorganisms, plays crucial roles in pollutants removal from wastewater and prevents the spread of wastewater-borne diseases. AS ecosystem shows unique engineered features that operational parameters, such as pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), mean cell retention time (MCRT), and nutrient level (e.g., ammonia, phosphate, and organic concentrations), are highly amendable. Moreover, AS ecosystem provides a more homogeneous environment and higher biomass density compared to other natural ecosystems. These features together enable the engineers and researchers to control microbial communities in AS and fulfill specific process requirements by adjusting operational strategies. Researchers have long regarded the AS ecosystem as a “black box” because of the complex microbial community. Thanks to the advances of cultivation-independent molecular methods and bioinformatics analyses, our understanding of complex microbial communities and key functional microorganisms in AS has been greatly expanded. To achieve better control of microbial communities in AS systems, we should unravel the mechanisms of abiotic and biotic driving forces underlie the dynamics of microbial communities and ultimately propose systematically operational strategies. However, the high-resolution time-series studies that could provide insights into the dynamics of microbial communities and microbial responses to perturbations in AS systems remain scarce, which hampered our deep understanding of the AS microbial ecology for engineering application. In this project, we will investigate the microbial dynamics in a full-scale AS system (Shatin WWTP, Hong Kong) using daily (seven years) and monthly (twelve years) collected samples, 1) to profile the microbial dynamics in AS system; 2) to generate a list regarding core shared functional microorganisms in AS systems; 3) to investigate how abiotic and biotic factors shape the microbial community assembly; 4) to propose operational strategies that can better control the microbial community, particularly for the functional taxa and their associated microbial cohorts. Also, we will further conduct lab-scale experiments, 5) to validate the proposed operational strategies that may favor or inhibit given target taxa or microbial cohorts. This research project will provide the first view of decadal dynamics of microbial community in a full-scale AS system. The findings of this project will shed light on the principles for microbial community assembly in AS systems and ultimately aid in the better control of microbial communities. 活性污泥工藝在污水處理過程中發揮著至關重要的作用，而微生物則是該工藝得以成功運行的關鍵。作為一類特殊的人工生態系統，活性污泥系統的眾多運行參數（如pH、溶氧、平均細胞停留時間等）具有極高的可控性。此外，與其他自然生態系統相比，活性污泥生態系統也呈現出更均質化和更高的生物密度的特點。活性污泥系統的這些特點使工程師和研究人員能夠通過調整操作參數以控制活性污泥中的微生物群落進而滿足特定的污水處理要求。 高通量測序技術的迅速發展和大量生物信息分析工具的開發極大的拓展了我們對於活性污泥中微生物群落的認知。對導致微生物群落變化的非生物和生物因素的研究將有助於微生物調控策略的提出，以實現對活性污泥系統的精細化調控。時間序列研究可為探究微生物群落的變化規律和微生物應對系統擾動的機制提供有力的理論支持。然而，目前關於活性物系統的高解析度的時間序列研究仍極為匱乏，這也限制了我們對活性污泥微生物生態規律的進一步認知及其相關的工程應用。 在本研究中，我們將採用取自沙田污水處理廠長達七年的每日和十二年的月度污泥樣品進行以下研究：探究活性污泥中微生物群落的變化；獲得活性污泥中核心功能微生物名錄；研究非生物和生物因素對微生物群落構建的影響；提出更優地控制活性污泥微生物群落的系統運行策略，尤其是功能微生物及其相關的微生物群落。本研究將展示首個十年跨度的實廠活性污泥微生物群落變化，闡明活性污泥系統中微生物群落構建的機理，並最終將其用於開發精細化地調控活性污泥微生物群落的運行策略。

17206120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206120.value: Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are indispensable biotechnology facilities for modern cities and play an essential role in modern urban infrastructure by employing microorganisms to remove pollutants in wastewater, thus protecting public health and the environment. This study conducted a bacterial community survey of WWTPs in Hong Kong. We studied monthly activated sludge (AS) samples collected over years from a full-scale wastewater treatment plant to answer how complex AS communities evolve in the long term and how the community functions change when there is a disturbance in operational parameters. A total of 920 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), representing approximately 70% of the community in the studied AS ecosystem, were recovered from the 97 monthly AS metagenomes. These results highlight that communities can assume different stable states under highly similar environmental conditions and that a specific disturbance threshold may lead to a rapid shift in community composition (please refer to Publication 1). Leveraging the near-complete genomes obtained using Nanopore technology, we also profiled the metabolic potential of the AS microbiome and identified 2153 biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) encoded within the recovered AS MAGs. Additionally, high quality genomes could help providing genome-centric view of the microbial community interactions and how biological interactions (biotic) affecting microbial communities. Besides, Hong Kong WWTPs could make great contributions to the genome mining of microbial dark matter in the global “wanted list.” (please refer to Publication 2 and 4). We found that ammonia-oxidizing bacteria had more diversity than nitrite-oxidizing bacteria. Operational parameters had important effects on OTUs’ abundance, such as the temperature to the genera of Tetrasphaera, Gordonia and Nitrospira (please refer to Publication 5). Candidate phyla radiation (CPR) is a special bacteria group of small cell sizes with high diversity and are likely obligate intracellular symbionts. We utilized genome-centric metagenomics to answer how CPR communities shift over years and what kind of ecological roles they act in an activated sludge system. The observed striking fluctuations in CPR community compositions and the limited metabolic and biosynthetic capabilities in CPR bacteria collectively revealed the nature that CPR dynamics may be directly determined by the available hosts. These findings highlight the presence of specific host interactions among CPR lineages in activated sludge systems. Despite the lack of key metabolic pathways, these small, yet abundant bacteria may have significant involvements in biogeochemical cycling and bacterial evolution in activated sludge systems. These findings give us more insights into the microbial community of AS to explore the engineering control strategies (please refer to Publication 3).

17206120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206120.value: Activated sludge is a widely applied wastewater treatment process that mainly uses suspended microbial flocs to remove pollutants in wastewater. With the characteristics of high biomass content and high microbial diversity, activated sludge plays an important role in pollutant removal and contains various functional microorganisms as a valuable pool of various useful microbial resources. However, the majority of microorganisms in activated sludge have not been isolated, which substantially limits the improvement of treatment efficiency and the innovation of process technology in wastewater engineering. As the basic biological methodology which can extremely expand the downstream studies for microorganisms, the cultivation of new species in activated sludge is urgently needed to fill the gaps between the cultured and uncultured microbial communities. The growing emphasis on cultivation in recent years has spawned the creation of many innovative and high-throughput cultivation techniques. In next step, we need to culture those microorganisms in the “wanted list” in activated sludge and extend our understanding of activated sludge microbiota. Additionally, we should develop absolute quantification metagenomic method to measure the different species in the absolute number and build up the mathematical modelling.

17206120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206120.value: Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are important facilities that remove pollutants from wastewater to protect public health and the environment. This project studied the bacterial communities in Hong Kong WWTPs by analyzing samples of activated sludge (AS) over several years. It was found that the AS communities can change rapidly when there are disturbances in operational parameters, and that ammonia-oxidizing bacteria are more diverse than nitrite-oxidizing bacteria. This project also identified a group of small bacteria called Candidate phyla radiation (CPR) that are likely symbionts and have limited metabolic capabilities, but are abundant in AS and may have significant roles in biogeochemical cycling and bacterial evolution. The project used advanced technology to obtain near-complete genomes of the AS microbiome, which allowed them to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and study microbial community interactions. These findings provide insights into the complex microbial communities in WWTPs and could help develop strategies to control them.

17206920.label: Project Objectives
17206920.value: To develop maneuvers that enable a multi-rotor UAV to perch on different planar structures, including ceilings, walls, and flat ground. We will build core libraries and controllers for aggressive trajectory generation and tracking control of UAVs. Based on this, we will further design, implement, and test perching maneuvers to enable autonomous, safe, and precise perching. To conduct design, trajectory generation, and tracking control of quadrotor UAVs with the capability of aerial-ground hybrid locomotion. We will investigate the energy efficiency of the ground locomotion, and demonstrate the hybrid movement in the air, on the ground, and air-ground transition on actual UAVs. To integrate all the developed algorithms into one complete quadrotor that can perform navigation, planar structure detection, trajectory generation, and tracking control all automatically. The effectiveness of the entire system will be evaluated through real-world flight experiments.

17206920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206920.value: 無人機對革新建築監測和建模等應用有巨大的潛力。自主化無人機可以被用來監測工地中的安全隱患, 或者是構建建築物的建成模型。但是，實現這些廣泛的實際應用仍然面臨諸多困難，這其中最為顯著的是無人機受限的飛行時間導致其較低的任務效率。 一種較有潛力的增加飛行時間的方法是將無人機棲息在環境中，模仿鳥類棲息在比如樹枝等自然物體上。不僅能增加飛行時間，棲息同時也限制了無人機可運動的自由度，從而提升其位置精度並降低對旁人的威脅。研究發現，當旋翼無人機從下面接近房頂的時候，其能耗會顯著降低，即所謂的屋頂效應。我們的前期研究工作顯示，利用屋頂效應將無人機棲息在屋頂或牆上面可以節省至少30%的能量，而不需要任何額外的機械裝置。 受自然界和我們前期工作的啟發，此項目的目標是開發一套系統的方案使旋翼無人機能跟環境接觸，包括屋頂、牆壁和地面，最終達到降低無人機能耗和提升其精度的目的。為實現這個目標，由接觸帶來的摩擦、動態切換和氣動干擾等基礎問題將通過聯合系統設計和控制得以解決。特別地，兩種新型設計將被提出：一種使無人機能棲息到屋頂和牆壁上， 另一種使無人機能在地面上移動。對每一種設計，此項目將開發軌跡生成和控制算法來實現自動、迅速和精確的無人機棲息和空地切換。所有的設計和算法將被集成到一個四旋翼無人機上並在實際環境中做測試。 此項目將通過顯著地增加其效率來為無人機的發展做貢獻，並讓消費者和諸如建築和基礎設施管理等工業用戶從中受益。此項目也會在更廣的領域，比如仿生機器人、機構學、規劃和控制，激發新的研究問題。

17206920.label: Realisation of objectives
17206920.value: Objective 1: We have developed comprehensive trajectory generation for both perching and detaching maneuvers on ceilings, walls, slopes, and grounds. Our planning method is universally applicable across all scenarios, eliminating the need for specific case selection and ensuring consistency throughout. In general, the perching trajectory comprises two phases: an initial acceleration phase utilizing forward thrust, followed by a deceleration phase employing reverse thrust. The utilization of reverse thrust is particularly crucial for surfaces with significant inclines, enabling the quadrotor to decelerate before making contact, thus averting potential high-velocity collisions on the quadrotor's upper part. We have also developed a trajectory-tracking controller that is suitable for bi-directional thrust operations. For each desired acceleration along the trajectory, two combinations of desired thrust and attitude are available: one involving positive thrust with a standard attitude, and the other involving negative thrust with a reversed attitude. The quadrotor autonomously selects the appropriate attitude that aligns closely with its current orientation as the reference, thereby preventing unnecessary flips and ensuring stable flight. Conducting a series of perch and detach tests in an indoor laboratory setting using three distinct quadrotor versions, we tested various perching surfaces set at inclined angles, including 0°, 45°, 90°, 135°, and 180°. All tests for both perching and detaching actions were successful, resulting in a remarkable 100% success rate and showcasing exceptional robustness in our system. Objective 2: We successfully implemented a design featuring a single passive wheel for ground locomotion on a bi-copter UAV, enabling aerial-ground hybrid locomotion. The research investigated the energy efficiency benefits of ground locomotion, demonstrating significant power savings of up to 77%. Through flight experiments, we verified the practicality of the hybrid locomotion system, demonstrating smooth transitions between aerial flight and ground movement. In the ground locomotion phase, the UAV navigates forward by adjusting its body pitch downward and executes turns by manipulating its yaw angle. Controlling its attitude during both aerial and ground maneuvers is achieved through adjustments in propeller thrust and servo angles. We have completed the dynamic modeling of this vehicle and developed specific controllers for aerial, transition, and rolling modes. The aerial mode activates when the UAV is above a certain height or outside ground effect. The transition mode, triggered by a pilot command, automatically switches to rolling mode once complete. Our experimental validations focused on confirming the feasibility of locomotion and energy efficiency gains. Despite some oscillation during touchdown, the UAV quickly stabilized its attitude. The UAV successfully performed straight-line rolling and figure-8 patterns. These successful aerial-ground transitions and ground movements demonstrated the viability of hybrid locomotion. Beyond mobility testing, we examined energy efficiency through comparative experiments. We studied performance under various conditions: normal hovering, stationary ground position, and surface rolling. Objective 3: All developed algorithms were integrated into a complete quadrotor equipped with propeller guards, an onboard computer, an onboard camera, and more. Outdoor demonstrations were conducted to validate the quadrotor's perching and detaching maneuvers in real-world environments, including scenarios like roadside, building entrance, and construction site. Solely relying on onboard sensing and computation, the quadrotor adeptly showcased its autonomous perching ability on various materials while upholding stability and energy efficiency. In all the tested cases, the onboard camera maintains perfect clear visibility without any obstruction from the UAV components. We have developed algorithms to assist the quadrotor search for minimum thrust thereby minimizing power consumption. Given the challenge of accurately determining surface friction mid-flight, the quadrotor's capability to autonomously search for optimal power levels without prior knowledge of surface conditions is paramount. The search process commences with elevated thrust values from the upper and lower propellers to facilitate perching. Subsequently, thrust levels are gradually decreased uniformly until the quadrotor loses contact. Finally, we maintain thrusts from the upper two propellers and continue to reduce thrusts from the lower two propellers until contact loss is about to occur again. The search process leads to the minimum thrust in all cases. We evaluated the power consumption of the quadrotor during both hovering and perching. Perching on ceilings illustrates the quadrotor leveraging only the ceiling effect. Compared to the hovering state, leveraging the ceiling effect led to energy savings exceeding 39%, underscoring the efficiency enhancement achieved through this simplistic yet effective method. Additionally, when the quadrotor perches on the ground, all motors can be completely turned off, resulting in nearly zero power consumption, highlighting the system's ability to conserve energy efficiently in various perching scenarios.

17206920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206920.value: For the planar structure perching quadrotor, the major purpose is to save energy and maintain stability. By evaluating the power consumption during flying and perching of three different quadrotors, (we named them “Light”, “Heavy”, and “tall”), our approach is shown to save energy efficiently. The average power needed for hovering by the three quadrotors is quantified at 352 W, 483 W, and 488 W, respectively. During perching on surfaces at 0°, the power consumption is measured as 214 W, 272 W, and 273 W for the corresponding quadrotors. Comparatively, perching yields energy savings of approximately 39%, 44%, and 44% over hovering for the three quadrotors. When perching on 90° walls, energy savings of 62%, 67%, and 61% are observed, indicating greater efficiency at this angle due to friction exploitation. This method not only emphasizes energy efficiency but also validates the accuracy of our minimal thrust calculations. The perching technique presented in this method offers several notable advantages. Firstly, it guarantees a broad field of view (FoV) for the sensors onboard, thereby reducing the likelihood of sensor interference. Whether in flight or perched, the quadrotor consistently maintains a clear FoV for its onboard camera. Secondly, the design is more lightweight and straightforward, requiring minimal additional components. By creatively perching on the ground, the need for traditional landing gear is eliminated. Thirdly, our approach does not rely on adhesive substances, magnets, Velcro, or suction cups, enabling the quadrotor to perch on surfaces with varying characteristics. This adaptability allows the quadrotor to detach freely at any time. The hybrid locomotion UAV with a single passive wheel at the bottom showcases remarkable advancements in energy efficiency and operational flexibility, achieving up to 77% battery savings without complex adjustments, demonstrating the viability of this streamlined design even with less controllable bi-copter UAVs. The research highlights the system's ability to enhance UAV mobility while conserving power, offering a promising solution for tasks like mobile mapping and search and rescue operations.

17206920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206920.value: Further research should prioritize real-world applications, encompassing the utilization of UAVs for monitoring, mapping, and delivery services. The perching quadrotor's energy-saving and stability features make it ideal for prolonged filming while perched, necessitating the integration of high-quality cameras to capture unique aerial perspectives for filming and mapping tasks. High-quality cameras or 3D LiDARs can be used on the UAV for trial. Similarly, the hybrid locomotion UAV, known for its operational flexibility, shows promise for applications such as package delivery in complex environments. Payloads can be applied to evaluate the controller in more complex conditions in the future. To facilitate these advancements, both UAV designs outlined in our study only require simple modifications to conventional UAVs, like incorporating wheels or propeller guards. Exploring the adaptation of our methods to commercial off-the-shelf UAVs could facilitate widespread adoption and utilization of these innovative technologies.

17206920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206920.value: This research project focuses on making drones more efficient and versatile for real-world tasks. The perching drone can save energy and stay stable while perched, making it great for long-time missions. Both perching and detaching of this drone can be conducted automatically. In tests, our system had a 100% success rate even on inclined surfaces, showing how well it works. The hybrid locomotion UAV is good at working in both aerial and ground, showcasing significant energy savings of up to 77%. The drone can smoothly switch between flying and rolling on the ground, offering a promising solution for tasks like mobile mapping and search and rescue operations.

17207020.value: 僅在2018年，全球估計就有1810萬新增癌症病例。雖然癌症的發病率在逐漸下降，但它仍然非常普遍。統計數據顯示，五分之一的人會在75歲之前患上某種癌症。不同類型癌症的治療途徑可能有很大差異，通常需要多種治療手段的結合以減少復發。儘管癌症治療正在取得進展，化療仍然是一種作爲獨立或輔助治療的標準療法。化療藥物的設計目的是抑制腫瘤中常見的分裂速度過快的細胞的生長，因此通常在手術切除前被用於縮小腫瘤(前輔助性放射治療)，或在手術切除後被用於殺死未切除和未發現的癌細胞(輔助性放射治療)。 然而，由於化療通常是通過靜脈來輸送藥物到達腫瘤的靶部位，藥物劑量是否充足依賴於全身的血液循環。這種不加篩選的細胞毒性藥物循環會無意中影響其他健康的組織和器官，並導致脫髮、噁心甚至器官毒性和神經損傷等副作用。這些副作用也會限制給病人的藥物劑量，導致腫瘤內藥物的濃度不足以殺死癌細胞。爲了解決這個問題，研究人員們開發了靶向藥物輸送系統，目的是儘量減少系統副作用，並通過將藥物鎖定在癌組織內部來增加癌組織的藥物吸收。分子靶向技術使得“瞄準”癌細胞成為可能，例如使用腫瘤靶向配體和納米級藥物結合的載體。然而，這些方法並不能保證藥物在靶位點有足夠的積累，因爲它們仍然依賴於體循環將藥物送到足夠接近癌細胞的地方從而通過分子間的相互作用達到效果。其他方法通過在腫瘤部位植入載藥底物(如晶片、薄膜)直接遞送藥物，或通過在腫瘤依賴的血管系統中直接注射藥物，如肝癌的經動脈化療栓塞術。然而，這些方法依賴於對腫瘤直接和靈活的進入，這對於深部或多發腫瘤並不總是可行的。因此，該項目的總體目標是開發和驗證一個用於超聲波驅動下藥物輸送的機器人系統。提出的磁力共振圖像(MRI)導航機器人系統旨在通過結合基於超聲波的藥物載體操作、術中MRI(如彈性成像)和高性能磁共振條件液壓驅動等技術，克服現有藥物輸送系統的局限。 該系統將由一個小巧的桌面式機器人組成，它可以精確地引導換能器陣列產生的超聲波束到達腹部區域的指定目標。該技術通過優化聲傳感器的性能進而指導換能器佈局和機器人設計。機器人配有微型無線全向射頻線圈，将在MRI引導下执行快速和實時的位置跟蹤。從高質量MR圖像可以得到異質組織的初始聲學圖，聲傳播規劃將基於初始聲學圖進行。此外，该技术使用一種基於學習的MR伺服方案，能夠對超聲焦點和捕獲特徵進行監測和校正。該系統的驗證將首先在腹部假體上進行，隨後在MRI導航下對活體豬標本進行臨床前驗證。 該項目的成功將向癌症治療的有效藥物輸送邁出重要的一步，涉及幾個關鍵領域：1)改進單獨或輔助化療藥物的治療計劃和管理；2)高保真液壓驅動和術中超聲傳導優化，用於增強對深層或多發腫瘤的局部藥物輸送通路；3)通過有效控制藥物傳遞至受癌症影響的部位，以及阻止藥物循環到健康細胞，最大限度地減少有害的副作用。

17207020.label: Realisation of objectives
17207020.value: 1. MR-conditional robot platforms for tele-manipulation of focused ultrasound transducers: PI and his collaborators have developed a hydraulic-driven tele-operated robot platform that enables 5-DoF manipulation of the focused ultrasound (FUS) transducer. Even operated close to the MRI iso-center, the robot can guarantee zero electromagnetic (EM) artifact to the MR image. Our proof-of-concept robot prototype can offer a large workspace (100mm×100mm×35mm) for FUS foci steering. Accurate manipulation (0.2 mm in translation, 0.4˚ in rotation) of the FUS transducer holder is achieved using rolling diaphragm-sealed hydraulic actuators. The robot control responsiveness (from 0.1 to 4 Hz) is also evaluated to show the potential to compensate for the spot tracking error induced by respiratory motion. We also demonstrate the use of wireless radiofrequency (RF) potential tracking markers to continuously register the robot task space in the MRI coordinates. 2. Learning-based efficient phase-amplitude modulation and hybrid control for MRI-guided focused ultrasound treatment: PI and his collaborators have also proposed a closed-loop hybrid control scheme and a learning-based modulation model for robot-assisted MRI-guided focused ultrasound (MRg-FUS) treatments. By introducing a rapid phase estimator to provide an efficient (<3 ms) solution, the robust H∞ controller enables real-time and accurate tracking (0.30 mm) without prior knowledge of heterogeneous media, even under unknown disturbances. The model enables rapid (2.65 ms) phase-amplitude modulation and precise targeting (mean 0.35 mm, max. 0.65 mm), meeting clinical standard. Focal obliquity is significantly “aligned” to only 2.7˚. Results from sensitivity analysis and transducer design also support the model’s clinical feasibility and potential in widespread MRg-FUS treatments. 3. Event-triggered closed-loop MPC for MRI-guided focused ultrasound hyperthermia for potential clinical use: The team has proposed novel perspectives to closed-loop control scheme for robot-assisted MRg-FUS mild hyperthermia (mHT). Thermal dynamics of tissues is discretized and linearized as a discrete-time positive system. Optimization problem involving ℓ1-gain of the system states is formulated for mHT planning. By introducing an event-triggered model predictive controller, control sequences of transducers’ phases can be generated to optimize the objective function. Thermal feedback is leveraged to accommodate modeling uncertainties, closing the control loop for constructive ultrasound interference. Taking account of the common clinical concern regarding FUS ablation heating, our scheme enables simultaneous spatial and temporal heating control, capable of optimizing target temperature within a narrow range (41-43°C), demonstrating its robustness against severe tissue heterogeneity. Overheating outside the target could be avoided, showing the clinical potential for safe intervention. Results from thermal dose analysis also support the feasibility in trans-abdominal mHT treatment.

17207020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207020.value: PI and his collaborators have developed a tele-operated robot platform for MRg-FUS treatment in abdominopelvic organs. It is a compact robot that can incorporate 3-DoF translation and 2-DoF rotation of FUS transducer array, which would be the first of its kinds facilitating the largest acoustic window to track HIFU spot inside patient body, as well as the most degree of flexibility to avoid residual sonication-induced skin burn. In addition, a learning-based modulation and control framework for widespread MRg-FUS treatments was proposed, without prior knowledge of heterogeneous media. The model ensures rapid (2.65 ms) full-wave correction on phase and amplitude aberrations simultaneously. This enables high targeting accuracy (mean 0.35 mm, max. 0.65 mm) under the clinical requirement, thus alleviating off-target heating. Besides, the unwanted grating lobes can be effectively suppressed, and the focal obliquity is “aligned” to only 2.7˚, thus reducing the risk of tissue damage. Compared with the non-corrected case, 58.3% targeting error and 67.9% obliquity is decreased. Accrediting to rapid modulation, our machine learning-enabled approach significantly reduces the time required for optimal transducer design, compared with the labour-intensive and computational-costing conventional method. Results from model sensitivity and computational efficiency also support the model’s feasibility in HIFU over abdominal organs. The closed-loop hybrid control approach ensures accurate tracking accuracy (0.30 mm) along an intended trajectory, even under unknown disturbance. Such robust tracking performance demonstrates our control policy’s adaptability inside the human body in low-intensity FUS applications. The estimator can offer a computationally efficient phase actuation (<3 ms) for the robust controller to facilitate real-time beam motion control.

17207020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207020.value: In future work, we will conduct more extensive testing in preclinical in-vivo/ex-vivo focused ultrasound with the presented intra-operative MRI-guided robotic system, which would improve the system’s capability for ultrasound-driven drug delivery. In addition, this technology would also facilitate other treatments and applications. Real time tracking under MRI will be incorporated to enable registration between MRI images and robotic navigation. It would give additional information for monitoring the heat diffusion process, thus further enhancing the safety of laser ablation surgery. Besides, RL-based control policy or data-driven approaches will be an effective solution to further optimize the transducer configuration. Additionally, validation of the complete system performance will take place in-vivo in a live swine specimen. ultrasound trapping of drug carriers, and its acoustic aberration correction can be examined within live-tissue to quantify the resultant drug delivery effect on the tumors, drug trapping performance will be made based on the RL-based MR-servoing scheme. The successful integration of ultrasound-based manipulation of drug carriers, intra-operative (intra-op) MRI, and high-performance MR-conditional hydraulic actuation would present the first MR-safe robotic actuation platform capable of providing ultrasound manipulation of drug carriers. This would lay a foundation for future pre-clinical validation toward clinical practices.

17207020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207020.value: The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided robotic system has been developed for ultrasound-driven drug delivery can overcome current limitations in drug delivery systems by combining principles from ultrasound-based manipulation of drug carriers, intra-operative (intra-op) MRI, and high-performance MR-conditional hydraulic actuation. A hydraulic-driven tele-operated robot platform enables 5-DoF manipulation of the focused ultrasound (FUS) transducer, enhancing access for localized drug delivery to deep-seated or multiple tumors. The proposed closed-loop hybrid control scheme and a learning-based modulation model for robot-assisted MRI-guided focused ultrasound (MRg-FUS) treatments, can improved treatment planning and management with chemotherapeutic drugs in standalone or adjuvant therapy. Then, the designed MR-servoing scheme incorporated with artificial intelligence (AI) techniques can automatically fine-tune the phase modulations of transducers and actively monitor the trapping and driving effect on the drug carriers, minimizing of debilitating side-effects by effectively containing drug delivery to cancer effected sites and preventing drug circulation to healthy cells. The proposed system is validated performed in an abdominal phantom, followed by pre-clinical validation in live swine specimens under MRI.

17207420.label: Project Objectives
17207420.value: Develop a novel configuration of wireless position-sensorless switched reluctance motor drive, which can efficiently convert electrical energy wirelessly into mechanical motion without involving any battery, converter, controller or sensor at the motor side. Develop a novel wireless position-sensorless estimation method for the proposed motor drive, which can effectively estimate the rotor position from the measurable electrical parameters at the transmitter side. Analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motor drive, with emphasis on assessing the selective wireless power transfer, thermal dissipation at the motor, and the acoustic noise of the structure. Devise the control system and control methods of the proposed motor drive, which can provide the desired wireless position-sensorless speed control with high efficiency while achieving minimum torque ripple. Identify potential applications of the proposed motor drive, with emphasis on utilizing its electrocution-free, cable-free, maintenance-free and high reliability features, and assess their practicability and commercial values. Design and construct the prototype of the whole system for experimentation, hence evaluating the performances in terms of efficiency, power density and torque performance as well as controllability and reliability.
