17207420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207420.value: Electric motors are the main energy conversion device from electrical energy to mechanical motion. However, their risk of electrocution has been a long-term problem because of the damage of electric cables. In the presence of physical cables, their portability is another long-term problem. Although the use of batteries to temporarily store electrical energy can reduce the risk of electrocution and improve the portability, it suffers from high cost, heavy weight, bulky size, limited energy storage and limited cycle life. In recent years, the wireless power transfer technology has been actively developed. By combining the wireless battery charger and the battery-powered motor drive, the resulting wireless motor drive can readily be derived so that the risk of electrocution and portability problem can readily be solved. Wait a minute! It is not a real wireless motor drive. This pseudo-wireless motor drive not only suffers from the aforementioned problems on using the battery, but also desires the additional converter, controller and sensor at the motor side. Most importantly, it cannot be utilized to work at isolated or inaccessible environment because the battery, converter, controller and sensor have much shorter lifespan than the motor. In order to eliminate the risk of electrocution and solve the portability problem, a real wireless motor drive is highly desirable. Since the switched reluctance motor (SRM) takes the definite advantages of low cost, rugged structure and high efficiency over a wide speed range, it is our natural choice for this wireless motor drive. Nevertheless, the use of rotor position sensor not only adds complexity and cost but also reduce the reliability and restrict its application. So, our aim is to develop a wireless position-sensorless SRM drive, which can operate wirelessly without involving any battery, converter, controller or sensor at the motor side, and can be controlled solely at the transmitter side. The purpose of this proposal is to develop a novel wireless position-sensorless SRM drive, and to explore its practical applications. The corresponding objectives are: (1) develop a novel configuration of wireless position-sensorless SRM drive; (2) develop a novel wireless position-sensorless method for the proposed motor drive; (3) analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motor drive; (4) devise the control system and control methods of the proposed motor drive; (5) identify potential applications of the proposed motor drive; (6) design and construct a prototype of the whole system for experimentation. 電動機是從電能到機械運動的主要能量轉換設備。然而，由於電纜的損壞，它們的觸電危險已成為長期問題。在存在電纜的情況下，它們的可攜性是另一個長期的問題。儘管使用電池暫時存儲電能可以降低觸電死亡的風險並提高可攜性，但電池成本高﹑重量大﹑體積大﹑能量存儲受限和循環壽命受限。 近年來，無線電力傳輸技術已得到積極發展。通過將無線電池充電器和電池驅動的電動機驅動組合在一起，可以輕鬆地得出最終的無線電動機驅動，從而可以輕鬆解決觸電和可攜性問題的風險。等一下！它不是真正的無線電動機驅動。這種偽無線電動機驅動不僅在使用電池時遇到上述問題，而且在電動機側還需要附加轉換器﹑控制器和傳感器。最重要的是，由於電池﹑轉換器﹑控制器和傳感器的壽命比電動機要短得多，因此不能用於隔離或不可接近的環境。 為了消除觸電的風險並解決可攜性問題，非常需要真正的無線電動機驅動。由於開關磁阻電機（SRM）在很寬的速度範圍內具有低成本﹑堅固耐用和高效率的明顯優勢，因此，我們選擇這種無線電機驅動。然而，轉子位置傳感器的使用不僅增加了複雜性和成本，而且降低了可靠性，並限制了其應用。因此，我們的目標是開發一種無線無位置傳感器SRM驅動，該驅動可以無線運行，而無需在電動機側安裝任何電池﹑轉換器﹑控制器或傳感器，並且可以僅在發送器側進行控制。 這個項目目的是開發一種新穎的無線無位置傳感器SRM驅動，並探索其實際應用。相應的目標是：（1）開發一種新穎的無線無位置傳感器SRM驅動的配置；（2）開發一種新穎的無線無位置傳感器方法； （3）分析電動機驅動的電磁場﹑熱場和結構性能；（4）設計電動機驅動的控制系統和控制方法；（5）建議電動機驅動的潛在應用；（6）設計並構建整個實驗系統的原型。

17207420.label: Realisation of objectives
17207420.value: The 1st objective has been fully completed. Firstly, a novel wireless switched reluctance motor (SRM) has been proposed, which employs the single-transmitter single-receiver configuration to achieve a very compact structure for wireless power transfer (WPT). This system can eliminate any battery or controller at the motor side, leading to maintenance-free operation. Then, a hybrid-frequency pacing technique has been proposed for high-order transformed WPT. It can efficiently tune the innate constant-frequency resonances of WPT to eliminate the high-frequency hard-switching problem while reducing the switching frequency with zero-voltage switching. Meanwhile, a multi-topological low-frequency-switching high-frequency-resonating WPT system has been proposed, which can significantly improve the system efficiency for specific equal-power applications. Also, a multi-coil omnidirectional WPT system has been proposed, which can provide more homogenous output power with high efficiency under arbitrary transmission directions. Consequently, a unique WPT system using the laminated magnetic coupler has been proposed to directly drive the wireless SRM over an extendable distance with all controls centralizing in the transmitter. By extending the concept of wireless SRM, a novel wireless universal motor has been proposed, which can achieve bidirectional movement while retaining the unique advantages of small size, universal input and large starting torque. Then, a novel wireless shaded-pole induction motor has been proposed, which can achieve single-phase operation without involving any controller at the motor side. Furthermore, a novel permanent-magnet brushless DC motor has been proposed, which can offer higher efficiency and torque density, while retaining the wireless and maintenance-free features. The 2nd objective has been fully completed. Firstly, a novel position-sensorless estimation method has been developed for the wireless SRM. Differing from the sensorless techniques developed for the conventional or wired SRM, the motor voltage and current cannot be directly measured at the primary side. The key is to online measure the transmitter current at the primary side, which is highly related to the phase inductance of the SRM, while the phase inductance contains information of the rotor position. On the other hand, the concept of a wireless resolver has been proposed for the wireless SRM, which can detect the rotor position and transfer the information to the primary side without involving any battery storage or active components at the secondary side. The key is to integrate WPT into a variable reluctance resolver, namely incorporating the excitation, sine, and cosine windings into the reluctance structure, to detect and transmit the rotor position. Compared with other wireless feedback techniques such as adopting the Hall effect position encoder with Bluetooth communication, this wireless resolver takes the definite advantage that it is much more robust and exhibits no communication delay, hence very attractive for high-speed wireless motor applications. The 3rd objective has been fully completed. A new analytical solution for mutual inductance calculation in the WPT system with multiple coils has been derived. The influence of mutual inductance under different angular inclinations on the magnetic flux leakage and transmission efficiency can be analyzed accordingly. Meanwhile, the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed wireless SRM have been conducted by finite element analysis, with emphasis on assessing the selective WPT, thermal dissipation and acoustic noise. Particularly, the magnetic flux densities before and after magnetic field editing are critically compared by electromagnetic field analysis, which confirms that the magnetic field distribution can be arbitrarily edited through the selective WPT. Then, a compact magnetic coupler consisting of two orthogonally integrated bipolar coils has been analyzed, which takes the definite advantage that they can be separately energized without cross-couplings. Moreover, a wireless shaded-pole induction motor has been analyzed. By performing the system analysis between the single-stator-winding full-bridge-inverter system and the dual-stator-winding half-bridge-inverter system, the wireless motor with the half-bridge inverter and dual-frequency resonant network can significantly improve the system robustness and efficiency. The 4th objective has been fully completed. A new frequency-modulated wireless direct-drive motor control has been proposed, which can offer direct wireless motoring with high robustness, mobility and flexibility. Also, a pulse-frequency modulation is developed for this wireless motor speed control. Meanwhile, a selective WPT control based on magnetic field editing has been proposed to deliver wireless power with higher safety, flexibility and selectivity. The algorithms for current calculation and synchronized control strategies are also developed to construct the desired magnetic field effectively, hence realizing the selectivity of the powering area. Also, a low-frequency-switching phase-shift control is developed for the multi-topological high-frequency-resonating WPT system, which can effectively control the wireless power while suppressing the switching frequency. Moreover, commutative-resonant control has been developed to directly drive the wireless SRM, which takes the definite advantages of balanced phase currents and flexible WPT distance while achieving high efficiency and minimum torque ripple. After incorporating the position estimation algorithm, the position sensorless control of the wireless SRM has been realized, which confirms that this system can work well in the absence of sensor, controller and converter at the secondary side. The 5th objective has been fully completed. Firstly, the underground in-pipe pump has been identified as a potential application. An energy-carrying electric vehicle can park above the underground in-pipe pump and wirelessly drive the motor inside the pump to control the water flow rate under severe weather hazards such as heavy rainfall. Also, the robotic arm has been identified as another potential application. By independently controlling bipolar coils in the transmitter, the wireless motors of robotic arms can be separately excited by bipolar coils in the receiver via the shared power-transfer channel at a single resonant frequency. Hence, it can significantly shrink the system volume and reduce the system complexity. Moreover, the pipeline pigging in isolated environments has been identified to be promising because of the cable-free, maintenance-free and high reliability features. For those applications desiring unique features such as low-speed motion, high starting torque and smooth speed control, the wireless motors can readily be modified to adopt relevant motor types. On the other hand, the wireless motors have been compared with relevant wired motors in terms of their practicability and commercial values, which confirms that the wireless motors can outperform the wired ones for specific applications. The 6th objective has been fully completed. The proposed wireless motor systems have been designed and constructed for experimentation. Their key performances are evaluated in terms of efficiency, power density and torque performance as well as controllability and reliability. The hybrid-frequency pacing WPT system can achieve the system efficiency of over 91.5%, the multi-topological high-frequency-resonating WPT system can reach the system efficiency of 91.6%, and the multi-coil omnidirectional WPT system can offer 0-360 degree transmission directions with the system efficiency of over 85% and output power fluctuation within 5%. The proposed wireless SRM has been prototyped, which can offer the system efficiency of 89.1% at 1500 rpm. Meanwhile, the wireless resolver has been built for the wireless SRM, which works well for rotor position detection with power consumption of only 1.1 W. By extending the wireless SRM, the wireless shaded-pole induction motor can achieve variable-voltage variable-frequency speed control from 486 to 1330 rpm with the system efficiency of 86.2%, the wireless universal motor prototype can offer bidirectional movement with the system efficiency of 86%, and the wireless permanent-magnet brushless DC motor can operate from 400 rpm to 4000 rpm with the efficiency of 80.2%.

17207420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207420.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 12 international journal papers [J1]-[J12] and 4 international conference papers [C1]-[C4]. Meanwhile, 2 PhD students have been trained. Concerning the system design and configuration for this project, two novel wireless power transfer (WPT) systems have been proposed, namely the hybrid frequency pacing technique [J1] and the multi-topological low-frequency-switching high-frequency-resonating WPT system [J2]. Instead of using multiple receivers, a novel wireless switched reluctance motor (SRM) adopting the single-transmitter single-receiver WPT has been proposed to achieve a compact structure [C2]. Then, a unique WPT system using the laminated magnetic coupler has been proposed to directly drive the wireless SRM with all controls centralizing in the transmitter [J9]. By extending the concept of wireless SRM, a novel wireless universal motor has been proposed to achieve bidirectional movement while retaining the small size and large starting torque [C4], [J11]. Furthermore, a novel permanent-magnet brushless DC motor has been proposed to offer high efficiency and torque density while retaining the wireless and maintenance-free features [J12]. Concerning the system modeling and analysis for this project, an omnidirectional energy harvester with a multi-coil structure for WPT has been modeled and analyzed, which can provide more homogenous output power with high efficiency under arbitrary directions [J3]. Instead of adopting the one-to-many coil structure, a compact magnetic coupler consisting of orthogonal bipolar coils has been modelled and analyzed, which can suppress unnecessary cross-couplings [C1], [J8]. Consequently, a wireless shaded-pole induction motor has been modelled and analyzed [J6]. By performing system analysis to compare its two topologies, the dual-stator-winding half-bridge-inverter one can offer better robustness and higher efficiency [J7]. Concerning the system estimation and control for this project, a novel frequency-modulated wireless direct-drive motor control has been proposed for underground in-pipe pumping [J4]. Meanwhile, a novel current control strategy has been proposed to arbitrarily edit the magnetic field distribution, which can deliver wireless power with higher safety, flexibility and selectivity [J5]. Then, a wireless resolver has been proposed for the wireless SRM, which can detect the rotor position and transfer the information to the primary side without involving any battery or active components at the secondary side [J10]. Moreover, a position sensorless control strategy has been proposed to achieve the first sensorless wireless SRM, where the transmitter current is measured to online estimate the phase inductance and hence the rotor position [C3].

17207420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207420.value: The project has been focused on developing wireless motors using electromagnetic motors and inductive power transfer techniques. Although the wireless switched reluctance motor has been further extended to wireless shaded pole induction motor and wireless universal motor while the inductive power transfer techniques have been expanded to involve orthogonal multi-coils and omnidirectional coils, the wireless non-magnetic motors using capacitive power transfer is an important area that needs further development. In particular, the wireless ultrasonic motor using capacitive power transfer is highly desirable for operation in the vicinity of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machine where magnetic materials are prohibited. Another important area that needs further development is the development of fault-tolerant control for the proposed wireless motors. This is highly desirable for operation in an isolated or inaccessible environment where maintenance is nearly impossible or very expensive.

17207420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207420.value: Electric motors are the main energy conversion device from electrical energy to mechanical motion. Their risk of electrocution and difficulty in moving around have been long-term challenges. By combining the wireless battery charger and the battery-powered motor, the resulting pseudo-wireless motor can readily solve the electrocution risk and portability problem but still suffers from the reliance on batteries and the desire of additional converter, controller and sensor at the motor side. Also, the use of rotor position sensors for closed-loop control not only adds complexity and cost but also reduces reliability. Particularly, it cannot be utilized to work in an isolated or inaccessible environment. The project has successfully developed a novel wireless position-sensorless switched reluctance motor, which can operate wirelessly without involving any battery, converter, controller or sensor at the motor side while retaining the inherent merits of high robustness and high controllability of the motor. The motor can be totally sealed and wirelessly operated in an isolated environment, while all controls are realized at the primary side. This opens up a new direction for research and development of electric motors and exerts a long-term impact on our society.

17207920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207920.value: After four decades’ rapid growth, China’s economy is entering a consolidation phase in which industrial restructuring activities are intensified. Enormous capital flows between cities have created an inter-urban network that becomes intriguing and significant to understand China’s urban dynamics in the new development era. The primary question this research seeks to answer is whether urban growth is driven by a networked economy underpinned by inter-city capital flows. This research will use Castells’ (1996) space of flow theory and Huggins’ (2010) calculative network capital discourse as the theoretical foundation to examine urban network capital and its impact on urban growth. Urban network capital refers to the connections a city has with other cities that enable virtual, rather than physical, exchange of information, thoughts, knowledge and capital. It serves to bridge the gap between mobile capital flows and immobile local market. In other words, urban development is not only contingent on locational factors but also affected by how a city is positioned in a networked economy. However, the actual effect of network capital on urban growth has yet to be identified empirically. This research will utilize Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) of firms in China as a proxy of capital flows to construct an inter-urban capital network. M&A, as an important source of capital flows, have grown considerably during China’s consolidation phase, providing enough observations and dynamic changes for this study. They also reflect the underlying long-term interactions between cities and reshape the pattern of business networks (Lee and Lieberman, 2010). This facilitates us to design more rigorous tests to examine urban network capital and its effect on urban growth. The results of this research will help urban planners and enterprises clarify their cities’ strategic positions and formulate policies to strengthen urban competitiveness. 在經歷了四十年經濟快速成長之後，中國的經濟進入一個相對穩定的鞏固和升級階段。而這一階段以產業的重組和優化升級為代表。隨著中國資本管制的放鬆，大量的跨地域資本流動創造出一個複雜的多維資本網絡，城市的發展逐漸嵌入在此網絡的發展中，形成自身獨特的發展路徑。因此，我們認為城市經濟發展已經不是一個孤立的區域經濟問題，而取決於城市與其他城市間的關係即其所在資本網絡中的位置。此研究項目所要解決的主要問題就是檢驗現今中國城市的經濟發展是否已經受到城市間資本流網絡的顯著影響？此研究將會建立在Castell (1996)的流空間理論以及Huggins（2010）的可計算網絡資本論述下，結合中國城市發展的獨特路徑，利用實證方法檢測中國城市的網絡資本以及其對城市經濟的影響。城市網絡資本強調城市之間的‘不可見’經濟聯繫，比如知識、信息、以及金融資本的交換。此外，城市網絡資本把可移動要素稟賦研究和不可移動的本地要素稟賦研究結合起來，彌補了雙方之間的研究缺口。換言之，城市的經濟成長不單取決於本地要素稟賦的貢獻，同時也會受到城市在無形資本網絡中的嵌入位置的影響。然而目前學界對於此種城市網絡資本缺乏足夠的關注和實證研究。因此，本研究將會利用公司間的投資兼併事件作為城市間資本流的指標，組建中國的城市間資本網絡進行分析。投資兼併事件作為一項重要的資本流來源，近些年來在中國大陸發展極為迅速，成為中國經濟轉型升級的重要手段，為本研究提供了豐富的動態數據。跨區域投資兼併事件可以反映城市間長期潛在的經濟聯繫以及商業網絡的變化（Lee and Lieberman，2010）。這有助於我們設計嚴謹的檢測來衡量城市網絡資本對於城市經濟成長的作用。研究結果將會有助於城市經濟規劃和相關企業更深入的認識城市所在的戰略位置從而制定更有效的政策以提高競爭力。

17207920.label: Realisation of objectives
17207920.value: To realize the first objective, we collected and processed over 17,000 M&A transactions and city-level location factors to construct a city-level panel dataset covering 279 Chinese cities from 2003 to 2017. Based on the dataset, we employed the Social Network Analysis approach to unveil the spatial pattern of China’s intercity capital flow network. We identified the simultaneous process of megacity prominence and city region clustering in China’s capital flow network. To realize the second objective, we extracted the individual network performance of Chinese cities from the spatial analysis above and established an urban growth model that allows inter-city spillovers through capital flows. The model was then used to test hypotheses about the relationship between network capital and urban economic growth. To estimate the effect of network capital on urban economic growth, we controlled for other growth drivers like human capital and knowledge, while using a cross-lagged panel model to account for the reverse causality between capital mobility and urban development. We found that cities’ network positions play a vital role in urban development, and the M&A-induced network capital is intertwined with conventional location factors, indicating the rise of networked agglomeration economy. To realize the third objective, we borrowed the theoretical insights above to investigate the role of network factors in other urban development scenarios. One study applied the urban network approach to construct a regional travel network with 6,000 nodes in Wuhan and showed that the relatively high Covid-19 infection rates in secondary cities could be explained by their strong network positions. A place-based policy is then suggested to recognize the dual role of these secondary cities in generating positive and negative externalities. The other study constructed an inter-urban capital flow network by classifying M&A within the manufacturing industry into horizontal, vertical, and conglomerate types, and found that only vertical M&A activity is conducive to urban economic growth. This suggests differential policy measures to promote vertical integration of businesses across cities while keeping an eye on horizontal or conglomerate integration that could reduce urban competitiveness.

17207920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207920.value: Research output #1 of Part C is the major paper arising from this project. It is published in Regional Studies, which has an impact factor of 4.6 in 2022 and is ranked Q1 in the fields of economics, geography, and regional & urban planning. The paper was presented in two academic conferences. The major findings are: 1) an uneven geography of M&A network capital is revealed, indicating regional disparity; 2) a positive impact of outward- and gateway-network capital on urban economic growth is identified; 3) the impact of the emergent network capital is moderated by local human capital and knowledge stock, indicating a networked agglomeration economy. The findings support a coordinative and place-based policy for fostering urban and regional development. Research output #2 of Part C is a second paper arising from this project. It is published in Cities, which has an impact factor of 6.7 in 2022 and is ranked Q1 in the field of urban studies. The major findings are: 1) secondary cities could be highly exposed to contagion risk; 2) these cities have enhanced transmission capacity in a balanced, well-connected travel flow network, whereas a locally clustered network would be more spread resilient; 3) both hierarchical position and horizontal flows are found relevant for explaining Covid-19 uneven spread. The findings shed light on improving mobility interventions if there is another outbreak. Research output #3 of Part C is a third paper arising from this project. It is being reviewed by Papers in Regional Science, which has an impact factor of 2.1 and is ranked Q2 in the fields of Economics and Geography. The paper was presented in one academic conference. The major findings are: 1) there is no significant effect of horizontal M&As on the urban economy; 2) vertical M&As are positively associated with urban economic growth in all directions; 3) conglomerate M&As dampen the local economy in all directions. The findings demonstrate that whether ownership transfer is beneficial to local economies depends on M&A typology, flow directions, and regional contexts. The network ideas from this project have also inspired our PhD student, Ziwei Lin, to adopt a similar analytical framework as part of her PhD thesis. A summary of her working paper is attached in Part C. In addition, the project also led to international collaboration with Dr. Zheng of University of Bath. We are currently extending the network ideas to information technology development.

17207920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207920.value: We will continue guiding our PhD student, Ziwei Lin, to further extend the network ideas in this project to study corporate action and carbon emissions as part of her PhD thesis. We will also continue collaborating with Dr. Zheng, associate professor of finance at University of Bath, to link M&A activity with information technology development in China.

17207920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207920.value: After four decades’ rapid growth, China’s economy is entering a consolidation phase in which industrial restructuring activities are intensified. Enormous capital flows between cities have created an inter-urban network that becomes intriguing and significant to understand China’s urban dynamics in the new development era. This project investigates the role of network capital in urban development by utilizing mergers and acquisitions (M&A) as a flow metric to construct China’s inter-urban capital flow network. It is shown that network capital, in general, has a positive impact on urban economic growth. In the process of industrial restructuring, the impact is heterogeneous, depending on M&A typology, flow directions, and regional contexts. During the pandemic, network capital, in terms of travel flows, could even have a negative impact as a result of contagion risk. The results of this research will help urban planners and enterprises clarify their cities’ strategic positions and formulate policies to strengthen urban competitiveness.

17208120.label: Project Objectives
17208120.value: A comprehensive waste characterization work will be conducted to understand the detailed chemical compositions of the waste electric and electronic equipment (WEEE) components, such as waste fluorescent powder, computer hard disks, and neodymium magnets in mobile phones. The focus will be on the search and quantification of the rare-earth elements (REE) of neodymium (Nd), yttrium (Y), and lanthanum (La) metals. The project work will then carry out extensive thermal treatments to observe the interactions of REEs with various component matrices under various thermal processing schemes (temperature profile, treatment time, and reduction/oxidation atmosphere). The crystal phases in which metals are hosted largely determine the material reactivity and the mobility of metals, and the identification of REE-hosted phases in the thermally treated samples also critically indicates the REE reaction mechanisms at various thermal transformation stages. X-ray diffraction analysis can be used to probe the signals of various crystal phases in the samples, and thus this proposed project will first use X-ray diffraction analysis to identify REE-hosted phases in the thermally reacted samples. Moreover, our unique quantitative X-ray diffraction (QXRD) analysis method (the Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through internal standards) will then report the quantities of REE-hosting phases in products via high-resolution X-ray diffraction data. The Rietveld structural refinement technique and the electron diffraction pattern analysis can provide lattice parameters, cation distributions, and crystal sizes of the thermally treated samples. After identifying the reaction mechanisms of the REE with the associated component matrices, sintering additives may often be incorporated into the thermal treatment processes to induce or enhance preferred reaction pathways. For this reason, the roles of sintering additives will also be explored by observing their influences on the crystal structural parameters of the REE-hosting phases and their effects on promoting the metal speciation behavior. The separability and extractability of REE from the thermally processed WEEE components will be evaluated by electron microscopic microstructure analyses and solution leaching experiments. To quantify the metal extractability and reaction selectivity, various levels of leaching experiments will be implemented to observe the metal release efficiencies under various chemical extraction conditions. After leaching experiments, the leached samples will be subjected to the characterizations of surface-sensitive analytical tools, including atomic force microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, to elucidate the reaction pathways and release behavior of REE. Optimized pyrometallurgical processes will be generated to achieve the desired nano- and micro-structural features for the intermediate and final products in REE recovery. Our precise controls of REE speciation and grain boundary features will be based on the unambiguous understanding of the reaction mechanisms, phase compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics obtained in the above procedures. The overall benefits of reducing the use of extraction chemicals, shortening the processing time, and reducing energy consumption will be evaluated and compared with the conventional hydrometallurgical approaches. The material properties and stabilization strategies for the processing residues will also be provided to eliminate secondary pollution.

17208120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208120.value: Rapid technological development resulting in the upgrade and adoption of electrical and electronic equipment has generated tremendous waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) problems on a global scale. Such development quickly depletes valuable natural resources, such as rare-earth elements (REE), that are critical for the function and performance of electric and electronic components. A new and effective waste-to-resource strategy is desperately needed to overcome these challenges of waste management and resource exploitation and create new material resources. WEEE is enriched with REE such as neodymium (Nd), yttrium (Y), and lanthanum (La). Current methods used to extract metals from the waste are primarily hydrometallurgical-based processes. They achieve metal extraction via aqueous chemistry but generally suffer from low metal recovery rates, high chemical consumption, long processing times, and secondary pollution. This proposed project aims to develop a new pyrometallurgical technology to physically and chemically transformation the metals in WEEE components and to enhance the recovery of valuable REE. However, the knowledge gap on metal speciation and their quantities at various transformation stages presents the major hurdle to the development of this new resource recovery technology. Metal speciation is directly related to the mobility of metals in crystalline (ceramic) and amorphous (glass) phases at the atomic and nano scales. Combined with the understanding of structural configurations, the metal reaction behavior and extractability can be well-controlled in the designed thermal treatment schemes. Conventional hydrometallurgical methods mainly rely on heterogeneous surface-limited reactions, but the pyrometallurgical treatments are able to further immobilize the metals incorporated inside the crystal structures via thermal transformation. This unique advantage eliminates the need for many repeating cycles of grinding and leaching processes often designed in the hydrometallurgical processing and reduces the overall energy consumption in the operation. This project will reveal the phase transformation mechanisms that control Nd, Y and La speciation at various thermal conditions and WEEE component matrices (e.g., waste fluorescent powder, computer hard disks, and neodymium magnets in cell phones). The high-resolution X-ray diffraction technique will then be performed on the thermally treated samples, and state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification will be implemented to quantify the various metal phases and crystalline parameters of the REE-hosting phases. By identifying the grain boundary features and evaluating the metal mobility, a variety of nano- and micro-structural features in the products will be explored to further facilitate REE recovery for a sustainable WEEE management strategy. 科技進步所致的快速電子產品更新造成了嚴重的電子廢棄物問題，這同時也快速地消耗全球稀土金屬的資源量。稀土金屬是許多電子元件中不可或缺的一部分，因此一個可化廢棄物為再生資源的技術，正是現階段電子廢棄物管理策略急需突破的挑戰。稀土金屬如釹、釔、鑭等常被使用於電子元件中，而它們目前的提取方法常依賴濕式溶鍊法。濕式溶鍊法的優點為操作簡單，但其缺點為有限的表面提取效率、大量化學溶液之使用、過程需時及可能產生的二次污染風險。本研究計畫開發相應的熱冶處理法，以解決上述的問題，但主要突破點的需求將在對金屬於熱冶過程中的相變分化行為，有正確的了解及量化成果的指引。金屬的相變分化行為常導致金屬於在結晶相(陶瓷)與非結晶相(玻璃)中的賦存型態。根據不同金屬相的結構特徵、反應性與金屬可萃取程度，金屬熱冶的過程可相互設計配合以達最佳的金屬提取策略。本研究將先針對可能含釹、釔、鑭的廢棄電子產品零件，如燈管瑩光粉、電腦硬碟、行動電話中所用的磁性元件，進行相關的探測與分析。其後將觀察金屬於陶瓷玻璃基質中熱冶過程的分化行為，並利用高解析X射線衍射技術與最新的Rietveld結構分析方法，進一步量化金屬存於各結晶相與非結晶相的結果。以此訊息配合晶界特徵之觀察，一系列納米及微米級結構的設計將更有助於稀土金屬提取的目地，並藉此邁向一個更具可持續性的電子廢棄物管理策略。

17208120.label: Realisation of objectives
17208120.value: Rare-earth elements (REEs) are valuable natural resources critical for the function and performance of electric and electronic components. This demand is intensified by the rapid technological development resulting in the upgrade and adoption of electrical and electronic equipment and generated tremendous waste electrical and electronic equipment problems on a global scale. The objectives of this project were realized by metal incorporation experiments to target REEs and the other heavy metals as the components contained in WEEE for the targeted stabilization or extraction strategies. High-resolution X-ray diffraction data were collected to observe the partitioning of metals in the product phases, assisted by the confirmation with the electron diffraction technique. The thermal reactions of these targeted metals were found to be largely affected by the component matrices due to the competing crystallization processes. Our Rietveld refinement analysis technique has uniquely quantified the metal distributions in the systems, and the results also provided the lattice parameters, cation distributions, crystal sizes, and impurities of the thermally treated products. We have established structure models for the metal hosting phases of Nd, Pb, Ni, and Co using our Rietveld refinement analysis technique (fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification). Information from transmission electron microscopy was used to confirm the findings, and we observed the structure and texture variabilities in the final products when using different compositions and additives in the sintering systems. The metal occupancy ratios in the samples with different raw material compositions were obtained. This developed skill was further applied to the synthesis of the zeolitic imidazolate framework-8, a new metal-organic framework (MOF), to assist the recovery of cerium (Cs), a REE used for cylinder head alloys in the automobile industry, with the discovery of a unique Ce transformation process. The X-ray diffraction has resolved the framework’s crystal plane information in detail when incorporated with Nd, La and Y, and their relationships with the synthesis reaction mechanisms were discussed in this task. The use of Rietveld structural refinement on diffraction data also assisted reporting the lattice parameters, cation distributions, crystal sizes, and impurities of the thermally formed REE hosting phases. The structure and texture variabilities observed in the final products also revealed the reaction pathways and product properties resulting from the thermally treating e-waste with different sintering additives. The task also extended the observation of formation mechanisms of layered metal sulfides by revealing their crystalline features and cation distributions at different crystal growth stages. The experimental and simulated powder XRD patterns were compared with the packing arrangement of the layers resolved by the quantitative XRD method. The zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 hosting phase was further investigated using the synchrotron-based EXAFS to obtain its K-edge spectra to understand the coordination environment and behavior of the produced sample framework. Acid leaching schemes were used to distinguish the metal stability and extractability in the produced samples. Surface characterizations are used to confirm the preferred interfacial reactions, and the grain boundary features further indicated the metal leaching behavior. The electron microscopic microstructure analyses were carried out for grain boundary characterization. Results of leaching experiments further reflected the beneficial outcome of achieving the targeted REE hosting phases to facilitate the phase separation. The atomic coordinates and isotropic displacement parameters were also reported. Surface characterizations by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed the designed interfacial reactions, and the atomic force microscopy verified the nanoscale surface topological features of the resulting samples. The selected area electron diffraction carried out in the electron microscopic analyses provided the patterns of the Mg-doped zirconolite samples with their corresponding Miller indices and d-spacings to advance our understanding of the REE-hosting phase coordination behavior. The metal leaching behavior and reaction pathways further reflected such grain boundary and coordination features. With the nano- and micro-structural features identified in this study, we have proposed the metal incorporation mechanisms in the investigated reaction systems. The optimization of the product designs includes the control of the precursor compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics in the treated WEEE. The nano- and micro-structural features of the generated metal hosting products and their raw waste residues were compared. The reaction mechanisms for the observed intermediates were proposed with optimized processing parameters to control and minimize their growth. The product designs through compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics were realized by the obtained nano- and micro-structural features found in this project. This goal was achieved by our in-depth understanding of the reaction mechanisms, phase compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics reported in this project. Compared to the conventional hydrometallurgical recovery process, the proposed pyrometallurgical processes using deep eutectic solvent systems reduce processing energy and shorten processing time to achieve a greener metal recovery approach.

17208120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208120.value: Metal incorporation experiments of rare-earth elements representing the components in WEEE and/or its treatment residues were conducted in this project. The metals in the waste electronics were also investigated together with the other concerned metals to maximize the metal recovery potential. We have established structure models for the metal hosting phases of Nd, Pb, Ni, and Co using our Rietveld refinement analysis technique to quantify the metal distributions in the systems. This developed skill was further applied to the synthesis of the zeolitic imidazolate framework-8, a new metal-organic framework (MOF), to assist the recovery of cerium (Cs), a REE used for cylinder head alloys in the automobile industry, with the discovery of a unique Ce transformation process. Through this project, the phase transformation from monoclinic zirconolite-2M to orthorhombic zirconolite-3O occurred in the designed system when x is larger than 0.35. The results of Rietveld refinement revealed Nd dominated over Ca in the 8-fold coordinated site, and Mg preferred occupying the TiO5 site in zirconolite-2M structure. The results from XAS analysis further confirmed the substitution mechanism of Mg in the target system and indicated that higher Mg incorporation resulted in less distortion in the zirconolite-2M lattice. The task also extended the observation of formation mechanisms of layered metal sulfides by revealing their crystalline features and cation distributions at different crystal growth stages. The stacking of the layers and the cation vacancies were found to be relevant to the appearance of different monovalent and divalent cations in the systems. The zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 hosting phase was further investigated using the synchrotron-based EXAFS to obtain its K-edge spectra to understand the coordination environment and behavior of the produced sample framework. Results of leaching experiments further reflected the beneficial outcome of achieving the targeted REE hosting phases to facilitate the phase separation. The atomic coordinates and isotropic displacement parameters were reported, and the selected area electron diffraction was carried out in the electron microscopic analyses to provide the patterns of the Mg-doped zirconolite samples with their corresponding Miller indices and d-spacings. The nano- and micro-structural features of the generated metal hosting products and their raw waste residues were compared. The reaction mechanisms for the observed intermediates were proposed with optimized processing parameters to control and minimize their growth. A new REE-end zirconolite phase approach was developed, with its perovskite formation largely inhibited in the sample preparation procedure.

17208120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208120.value: The implementation of this project has sufficiently used the experimental resources in a laboratory-scale facility. Further scientific research development can be planned with more synchrotron-based characterization techniques to further understand the changes of atomic coordination and occupancy when the targeted metals are going through different leaching processes. Additional development direction can be additional theoretical thermodynamic calculations to model the behavior of REEs when subjected to different acidic attack conditions and verified by the experimental outcomes. Both future developments can further confirm the product phase stability results presented in the current project outcomes. Another direction of development is to refine the parameters and processing procedures generated from our laboratory-scale experiments through industrial-scale operations to fully realize the treatment process for e-waste treatment facilities.

17208120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208120.value: The soaring manufacture and use of electrical and electronic devices have generated a significant amount of electronic waste (e-waste), and the associated consumption of rare-earth elements poses both waste and resource management challenges. The research project aimed to treat the rare-earth elements commonly found in e-waste, and the research work has successfully incorporated the targeted elements into the crystal phases, facilitating easier separation operations to achieve the resource recovery goal. The project results identified a few promising metal-hosting phases and utilized leaching experiments, coupled with surface characterization techniques, to investigate the metal leaching behavior. The resulting metal speciation and grain boundary features from different reaction matrices were found to be most crucial in the metal reactivity and recovery efficiency. Such know-how generated from this project further assisted the design of nano- and micro-structural features of the metal-incorporated products to achieve the control of metal mobility and to realize the elemental separation, as the key technology toward the feasible metal recovery goal from e-waste. Compared to the conventional hydrometallurgical recovery process, the developed pyrometallurgical processes using deep eutectic solvent systems can reduce processing energy and shorten processing time, which provides a much greener rare-earth elements recovery technique.

17208920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208920.value: 本項目設計用於深度學習作業中通信和計算操作的設備放置和執行順序安排的高效算法，以最大程度地利用可用部分的機器學習（ML）集群資源來最快速地完成訓練作業。 深度神經網絡（DNN）已廣泛用於計算機視覺、自然語言處理等領域。由於輸入數據量大和DNN模型規模不斷增長，訓練DNN通常非常耗時。流行的訓練模式是在分佈式環境中使用配備有多個GPU的工作結點進行並行培訓，該訓練模式由最新的ML框架（例如TensorFlow，PyTorch等）所支持。 迄今為止，仍然不清楚的是，給定DNN模型和不同物理服務器上的一組可用設備（例如GPU），將模型訓練運算部署到設備上並優化其執行順序的最好策略是什麼。現今有不同的分佈式訓練模式可供選擇，它們具有不同的硬件/訓練效率：數據或模型並行、用於參數同步的PS或All-Reduce構架、是否進行流水線化等等。訓練DNN時，計算和通信運算符都涉及到，其執行時間需仔細安排，以最大程度地保證操作的並行性。 現有的工作均單獨研究計算符部署和通信調度。對於通信調度，現有工作提出了DNN層分區/合併和無等待反向傳播，以更好地隱藏計算時間內的通信開銷。對於計算符放置，現有的工作已經設計了手動優化並行性的專家策略以及更通用的、基於搜索/深度學習的方法。這些策略要么需要人類專家的紮實領域知識，要么就需要花費大量資源和時間來尋找好的策略。有效、系統的共同優化DNN訓練中的通信和計算放置以及執行順序的策略仍然缺乏，來實現在給定資源下最快速地完成訓練的目的。 本項目旨在研究這套策略。我們從研究更好的通信調度策略開始，基於最佳計算調度假設，設計允許先佔和合併張量傳輸的方法。在給定參數同步構架和通信調度策略的情況下，我們接下來研究接近最佳的計算操作符的放置和調度。其後，我們一並考慮計算同通信放置和調度，並在決策空間中包括參數同步構架選擇。我們追求具有紮實理論基礎的、可高效計算出來的策略。我們將在AI雲中最先進的集群調度器上部署我們設計的策略，並將其與其他代表性策略在真實的作業負載下進行比較。

17208920.label: Realisation of objectives
17208920.value: We have achieved all Objectives 1-4 in this project. [Objective 1] Regarding Task a), we design communication schedulers that schedule detailed tensor transmissions to maximize network bandwidth utilisation and expedite job training progress, and adapt the communication strategies according to device and network heterogeneity. The results are reported in publication 1 in part C-8 and publications 4 and 10 in part C-9. In addition, in DNN training optimizer frameworks that we have designed, tensor fusion/partition passes are included to optimize training performance, with search or DNN-based methods. The results are reported in publications 1 and 9 in part C-9. For Task b), we propose optimal scheduling of operator execution orders, together with communication scheduling and computation and communication resource constraints. The results have been reported in publications 5, 6, 13 in part C-9. For Task c), in the context of pipeline scheduling of model parallelism, we have designed efficient, near-optimal algorithms for data transfer scheduling over arbitrary inter-GPU connectivity, together with pipeline partition and device mapping, and microbatches processing ordering over the partitions, to minimize the per-iteration training time. The results have been reported in publication 2 of part C-9. In the context of SPMD-based DNN training, in publications 8, 12 of part C-9, we maximize computation-communication overlap with strategical tensor sharding and communication scheduling. In the context of diffusion model training, we have designed efficient pipeline mechanism in publication 6 of part C-9. For Task d), in a multi-tenant AI cloud running many DNN training jobs, we have designed a flow scheduler (deployed per server) that dynamically tunes the sending rates of outgoing tensor flows from each server, for cooperative scheduling of communication. The results are reported in publication 3 in part C-8. [Objective 2] For Task a), in publication 5 in part C-9, we deal with computation scheduling as well, and propose cost models. In the context of pipeline-parallel training in publication 2 of part C-9, we discuss how to linearize a non-chain DNN model by ignoring shortcut connections (as in ResNet152) and aggregating parallel branches (as in Inception-V3). In publication 7 of Part C-9, we build detailed cost models for synchronous distributed training across hybrid devices. For Task b), in publications 1, 9 in part C-9, we have enabled memory usage estimation using a carefully designed DNN training replayer, and designed memory-optimization passes to reduce the memory footprint. Besides, in publication 5 in part C-8, we use a simulator to effectively estimate peak memory consumption and avoid OOM error for device placements of ops. For Task c), in publication 5 in part C-8 and publications 2, 5 in part C-9, we consider operator placement and execution scheduling among multiple workers, with efficient cost modeling and tensor transmission across machines. Regarding Task d), in publication 2 of part C-9, we have designed efficient, near-optimal algorithms for expediting synchronous pipeline-parallel training of large DNNs, including: a pipeline partition and device mapping algorithm, and a pipeline scheduler that decides processing order of microbatches over the partitions, which together minimize the per-iteration training time. [Objective 3] For Task a), in publication 5 in part C-8, we derive optimized DNN training graph and its deployment onto any device topology, for expedited training in device- and topology- heterogeneous ML clusters. We novelly combine both the DNN computation graph and the device topology graph as input to a GNN, and join the GNN with a search-based method to quickly identify optimized distributed training strategies (to resolve the very large action space issue). Besides, in publication 4 of part C-9, we construct optimized parameter synchronization topologies in heterogeneous ML clusters, to maximize network resource utilization, expedite training, and ensure training convergence. For Task b), in publications 4 and 10 in part C-9, we address communication tensor partition and preemptive scheduling, and design efficient algorithms. Computation pipelining with proven efficiency has been addressed in publication 2 of part C-9. Regarding Task c), we have designed a multi-scheduler system for large-scale multi-tenant AI clusters, and proposed a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) scheduling framework to cooperatively learn fine-grained job scheduling policies, towards the objective of minimizing job completion time. The results have been reported in publication 1 of part C-8. In an edge-cloud setting, we devise task placement and resource allocation strategies with a GNN-based multi-agent reinforcement learning paradigm in publication 4 of part C-8 and publication 11 of part C-9. In case of multiple DNN training jobs using ring all-reduce for parameter synchronization, we have designed resource scheduling models, which cover a wide range of objectives in training performance optimization (e.g., excessive training avoidance, energy efficiency, fairness), with provable performance guarantee. The results have been reported in publication 3 of part C-9. Furthermore, in case of PS-based DNN training jobs, we have designed efficient scheduling algorithms to allocate workers and parameter servers across different machines to minimize the overall training time, as in publication 2 of part C-8. In publication 6 of part C-8, we present a deep learning-driven ML cluster scheduler that places heterogeneous training jobs (either with parameter server architecture or all-reduce architecture) to minimize interference and maximize performance. In publication 7 of part C-8, we propose optimized, joint computation operator and communication tensor fusion strategies to enable highly efficient distributed training with a GNN-based simulator to effectively estimate per-iteration training time. [Objective 4] We have evaluated our algorithms and systems in Publications 1, 3, 6 in Part C-8 and publications 2, 4 in Part C-9 using our testbed system. We reported evaluation results in terms of DNN training speed, model accuracy, algorithm overhead, etc, when various DNN training jobs are run with different configurations. We have carefully compared our designs with state-of-the-art representative designs in the respective work. For example, in publication 2 of Part C-9, we compared with GPipe, PipeDream and HetPipe, which are state-of-the-art pipeline-parallel training designs. For tensor flow scheduling in publication 3 of part C-8, we compare with various flow/congestion control protocols, including TCP variants, PCC, Aurora, DeepCC, etc. In publication 1 in Part C-9, our designs were evaluated in ByteDance's production ML cluster with 16 servers (128 Tesla V100 32GB GPUs), and compared with Horovod's default tensor fusion and Autotune (which automatically tunes the interval and upper bound for tensor fusion), as well as BytePS's default tensor partition. In publications 7 and 9 in Part C-9, our evaluations were conducted in ByteDance's production ML cluster as well. For publications 5, 6, 10 in Part C-9, our evaluation was done on Amazon AWS cloud; we compared with representation scheduling algorithms including Tetris, load balancing, Least Interference First, LIF, etc. Experiments in publications 5, 7 in Part C-8 and publications 8 and 12 in part C-9 were conducted in Alibaba PAI cloud platform, and evaluated against state-of-the-art designs.

17208920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208920.value: In publication 3 of Part C-8 and publication 4 of Part C-9, we propose flow scheduler and communication library that dynamically tune the sending rates of outgoing tensor flows from each server, optimize inter-node communication topology in heterogeneous clusters, and maximize network bandwidth utilization and expedite job training progress. In publication 1 of Part C-8, we adopt multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for ML job scheduling in large-scale ML clusters, that makes distributed scheduling decisions under realistic datacenter topologies; we design a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) with edge information encoded to capture the cluster/data center topology, server architectures and link status. In publication 5 of Part C-8, we novelly combine both the DNN computation graph and the device topology graph as input to a GNN, and join the GNN with a search- based method to quickly identify optimized distributed training strategies and its deployment onto any device topology, for expedited training in device- and topology- heterogeneous ML clusters. In publication 7 of Part C-8, we generate optimized, joint computation operator and communication tensor fusion strategies to enable highly efficient distributed training; a GNN-based simulator is built to effectively estimate per-iteration training time achieved by operator/tensor fusion candidates. In publications 1 and 9 of part C-9, we design efficient tool kits to predict DNN execution latency, diagnose performance bottlenecks and explore optimization strategies (from computation, communication, and memory aspects) for training acceleration on different hardware. In publication 2 of part C-9, we devise a pipeline partition and device mapping algorithm, and a pipeline scheduler that decides processing order of microbatches over the partitions, which together minimize the per-iteration training time. In publications 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 in part C-9, we design fine-grained tensor/operation partition, computation and communication overlap strategies for training expedition of MoE models, diffusion models, and SPMD-parallel models.

17208920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208920.value: Nowadays very large-scale deep learning models have been fast evolving. This project mostly focuses on fine-grained operator and communication scheduling of the earlier generation of large models. Though we have investigated the techniques for more recent models as in a couple of publications reported above, more computation and communication scheduling designs can be investigated on the newer, more complex NN architectures.

17208920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208920.value: This project focuses on automatic model deployment and execution strategies to fully exploit resources scattered across physical servers in a ML cluster. Efficient auto ML strategies, which optimize utilization of the very expensive hardware and maximize performance of the ML models, are vital for cost saving of the relevant industry sectors, more efficient datacenter energy consumption, and less carbon footprint for carrying out the enormous computation. Our designed methodologies can significantly benefit industries and institutions which invest significantly in building and operating a large-scale ML/AI cloud, on performance improvement and cost reduction of their infrastructure.

17209220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209220.value: 火災是香港最為常見的事故之一，它不但會導致嚴重身體傷害甚至死亡，亦可能造成財產損失。根據香港政府資料，在2016年一共發生了5836場火災，當中26人喪生，290人受傷以及9196人獲救。為了最大程度地減少對住戶以及相關設備和設施的損害，及時地向先遣急救人員提供事故相關的信息，例如事故的潛在原因和涉及的設備、住戶位置、以及容易受事故影響的設備和設施等尤其重要的，因為這些信息可以方便他們儘早制定應對計劃並有效地在現場執行救援行動。而不同持份者(即先遣急救人員、設施管理人員/工程人員、和住戶)之間的協作和溝通亦是不可或缺。因為，這可大大減少相關持份者從各渠道收集必要信息並進行分析的時間，使其儘早了解現場情況以便更有效地在先遣急救人員進行決策的過程中提供幫助。 此研究旨在開發一個建築信息模型和人工智慧驅動的智能系統，該系統可以輔助先遣急救人員收集必要的數據(例如建築信息、建築性能數據和維修相關數據)，分析各項設備和設施的易受損性，展視收集到並經分析後的信息，制定協作應對計劃，以及在發生火災緊急情況時共同協作地執行現場行動。這項研究將開發的關鍵模塊包括一個用於存儲和檢索各種類型信息的數據結構，一個經過建築物信息模型訓練使其可以最準確地了解目標建築物的人工智慧模塊，一個分析易受損部位的模塊，和一個基於增強現實/虛擬實境技術的模塊，藉此有效地透視住戶與易受損設備及設施的位置，以及先遣急救人員與易受損害的對象之間的最短可行路徑。 此研究最大的影響力在於讓先遣急救人員能實時探索各種數據來源並收集所有相關信息，以便在緊急情況下準確地對現場情況作出判斷，從而制定最有效的現場應對計劃並提高拯救住戶和保存易受損設備及設施的可能性。此研究亦將可用作為可靠的科學基礎來研究和開發新的機制以提高先遣急救人員的現場行動，並可將其應用領域擴展到其他類型的緊急事故，以致日常運營與維修，及施工期間與安全相關的現場活動中。

17209320.value: To develop an innovative two-beam interference lithography with structured light exposure to deterministically fabricate centimeter-large spatially varying metasurfaces with continuously changing gradient dimension and geometry To investigate the position-dependent optical properties on large-area gradient metasurfaces through numerical modeling to establish a comprehensive modeling framework for evaluating the performance and elucidate the guidelines of metasurface design for molecule detection To experimentally demonstrate and evaluate the molecule detection performance of the gradient metasurface sensors for imaging-based refractometric sensing and space-multiplexed broadband surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopic sensing

17209320.label: Realisation of objectives
17209320.value: The project outlined three key objectives, each of which has been successfully accomplished as detailed below. Objective 1: Develop Two-Beam Interference Lithography for Gradient Metasurface Fabrication (100% completed) Towards this object, the Team has established a customized two-beam interference lithography setup in the lab, utilizing single-mode polarization-maintaining fibers to emit spatially varying Gaussian beams for deterministic nanostructuring. Using this setup, we demonstrated the capability to fabricate centimeter-scale metasurfaces with gradient geometries, as published in Advanced Materials. The technology developed in this task has been partially translated into a commercial nanopatterning product through a spin-off company, supported by the University of Hong Kong and the ITF Technology Start-up Support Scheme. In the second half of the project period, the Team further extended the two-beam interference lithography patterning using a secondary grayscale-patterned exposure for modulating the nanostructure sizes, offering a new innovative approach to create gradient metasurface. This work has led to a publication in Light: Sciance & Applications, a top journal in Optics area. Objective 2: Investigate Optical Properties via Numerical Modeling (100% completed) To use the gradient metasurface fabricated in Objective 1 for sensing applications, the Team developed a comprehensive simulation framework to predict metasurface morphology, position-dependent optical properties (e.g., reflection/transmission spectra), and resonance behaviors for optimizing the sensing performance and exploring diverse materials (metallic/dielectric), gradient profiles, and nanostructure geometries. Such simulation framework has been integrated with our gradient plasmonic sensor demonstration and published in top-tier journals. In the future, the Team will further refine this design framework for broader applications, including multi-physics coupling (e.g., thermal/mechanical effects). Objective 3: Demonstrate Molecular Detection Performance (100% completed) Based on the fabrication platform established in Objective 1 and the design and optimization framework developed in Objective 2, the Team successfully demonstrated and tested ultrasensitive gradient metasurface sensors capable of detecting single-molecule layers via imaging-based refractometry, which was published in Advanced Materials. The Team has also advanced the technology by integrating sensors into microfluidic devices and exploring applications in early disease diagnostics (e.g., biomarker detection). For example, the Team used this gradient plasmonic sensor to demonstrate the detection of exomers and SARS-CoV-2 sequence. As an extension of this work, based on the innovative fabrication method developed in the later stage of this project for modulating the nanostructure size using interference lithography and grayscale-patterned secondary exposure, we fabricated gradient plasmonic metausrfaces with linearly varying geometry profiles and also demonstrated its application in imaging-based sensing applications. This work has also been published in leading academic journals.

17209320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209320.value: This research project successfully achieved its three key objectives, leading to significant advancements in gradient metasurface fabrication, optical modeling, and molecular sensing applications. For Objective 1, the team developed a customized two-beam interference lithography system using polarization-maintaining fibers to fabricate centimeter-scale gradient metasurfaces with precise nanostructuring (item 7 in Part C-8). An innovative extension combining grayscale-patterned secondary exposure enabled modulation of nanostructure sizes, enhancing design flexibility (Light: Science & Applications, item 5 in Part C-8). This technology was partially commercialized through a university spin-off (item 2 in Part C-11). Under Objective 2, a numerical modeling framework was established to predict metasurface optical properties (e.g., resonance behaviors, reflection/transmission spectra) for optimizing sensing performance. This framework supported the design of gradient plasmonic sensors and was validated in high-impact publications (item 7 in Part C-8). Future refinements will explore multi-physics coupling (e.g., thermal/mechanical effects). For Objective 3, the team demonstrated ultrasensitive molecular detection using gradient metasurfaces, achieving single-molecule-layer sensitivity via imaging-based refractometry (item 7 in Part C-8). Integration with microfluidics enabled applications in disease diagnostics, including SARS-CoV-2 sequence detection and biomarker analysis (item 2 and 4, in Part C-8). Further work exploited grayscale-patterned exposure to create linearly varying plasmonic metasurfaces for imaging-based sensing, published in leading journals. In summary, the project established a robust platform for large-scale, high-precision metasurface fabrication, advanced computational design tools, and high-sensitivity biosensing, with translational potential in diagnostics and nanotechnology.

17209320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209320.value: Our research presents strong potential for expansion in three key directions: 1. Scalable manufacturing & commercialization – the interference lithography technique can be optimized for high-throughput, cost-effective production of metasurfaces, facilitating industrial adoption. Collaboration with semiconductor and photonics industries could accelerate commercialization. 2. Expanding the applications of the spatially-varying gradient metasurfaces and also extending the numerical framework to incorporate thermal, mechanical, or quantum effects could enable metasurfaces for energy harvesting, optomechanics, or quantum sensing. 3. Innovative biomedical sensing applications by integrating the gradient metasurface platform with AI-driven imaging analysis and portable microfluidics could enhance point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders. These future potential directions can be explored through industrial partnerships for scalable fabrication, pursuing interdisciplinary grants to explore applications, validating biosensing performance in clinical trials through collaboration with partner groups, and expanding machine learning integration for real-time analyte detection.

17209320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209320.value: This research explored new methods for creating specialized optical surfaces at a very small scale. Using an improved laser-based fabrication technique, the team developed a way to produce nanometer-scale structures over wafer-scale area, with their sizes modulated spatially. These spatially-varying nanostructures over large area enable high-sensitivity detection of tiny amount of molecules, which are essential particularly in biomedical sensing applications. The research outcome in this project can bring new capability of scalable nanomanufacturing and plays an important role in broader applications beyond biomedical sensing.

17209520.label: Project Objectives
17209520.value: Mechanizing local type inference for polymorphic languages with OO style subtyping: This objective aims at providing, for the first time, a fully mechanized account of local type-inference for polymorphic languages with OO style subtyping. Mechanizing local type inference for simple dependent types: The second objective is to investigate local type inference in the presence of simple forms of dependent types. Languages like Scala already support simple forms of dependent types, and dependent types are becoming more and more prominent in programming languages. They are therefore an important feature for programming languages in the near future. This objective will investigate the algorithms and metatheory for local type-inference with dependent types. Mechanizing local type inference for type systems with intersection and union types: The final objective is to extend the results in the first objective with two important and non-trivial features: intersection and union types. Intersection and union types are employed currently in various languages (such as Scala, RedHat Ceylon, Facebook Flow or Microsoft Typescript). This goal will investigate the algorithms and metatheory for local type-inference with those features.

This goal will investigate the algorithms and metatheory for local type-inference with those features.

17209520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209520.value: 靜態類型的編程語言（例如Java，C＃，C ++，Swift或Scala）用於實現我們社會使用的許多軟件。此類軟件的範圍可能從簡單的移動應用程序到醫療設備，金融服務，飛機或汽車中使用的關鍵軟件。因此，最重要的是那些編程語言的實現中使用的各種算法都是正確的。換句話說，編程語言實現是關鍵軟件，因為它們最終可以用於實現其他關鍵軟件。編程語言實現中的錯誤可能會帶來災難性的後果。此外，它還可以擊敗其他用於驗證軟件正確性的驗證技術（通常假定編程語言實現本身是正確的）。 類型推斷算法是編程語言實現的重要方面。所有上述靜態類型化的編程語言都具有結合了各種功能的複雜類型系統。這些功能包括子類型化和泛型（具有子類型化的參數多態性的一種形式）。這樣的類型系統表現力很強，但是通常它們可能需要沉重的（類型）註釋負擔。為了緩解類型註釋過多的問題，許多語言都支持某種形式的類型推斷，該類型推斷用於自動推斷程序中使用的類型。類型推斷使註釋負擔減輕，使程序員能夠專注於程序邏輯，並使程序更簡短，更易讀。類型推斷算法具有一些理想的屬性。首先，類型推斷算法應該是正確的。在這種情況下，正確性意味著如果為表達式或變量推斷出一個類型，則這種推斷出的類型確實應該是有效（正確）的類型。可用於類型推斷算法的第二個屬性是可預測性：程序員應該容易確定需要註釋的位置。最終的理想屬性是可判定性：類型推斷算法應終止並推斷類型，或因類型錯誤而拒絕程序。 該項目的目的是研究和開髮用於豐富類型系統的類型推斷算法，其中包括子類型，泛型和從屬類型形式等功能。我們專注於本地類型推斷技術，Pierce和Turner（2000）對本地類型推斷技術進行了研究和推廣，從而為具有子類型和多態性的簡單語言提供了一種實用的類型推斷形式。不幸的是，儘管他們進行了開創性的工作，但本地類型推斷技術仍未得到充分研究，文獻中研究的本地類型推斷的形式與諸如Scala，Java或C＃等語言的類型推斷的實現之間還存在很大的差距。儘管這些實現大致基於Pierce和Turner的思想，但它們具有各種局限性，目前尚不清楚它們是否正確以及是否具有其他期望的屬性。一個問題是，與Pierce和Turner研究的語言相比，Java和Scala之類的語言類型系統功能強大且功能豐富，因此，新功能的處理是臨時性的。另一個問題是很難擴展局部類型推斷的元理論來說明新功能。這是因為這樣的元理論是手工完成的（即使用手寫的證明和定理），並且需要大量的專業知識作為起點。因此，主流語言中幾乎所有類型推論的實現都沒有得到正式研究，從而導致了臨時性和未經驗證的設計。關於類型推斷算法的現有實現中有許多錯誤的報告，對於許多語言來說，當需要註釋時，這是不可預測的。

17209520.label: Realisation of objectives
17209520.value: Objective 1: Mechanizing local type inference for polymorphic languages with OO style subtyping We have developed a basic algorithm for type inference in the presence of subtyping in our ECOOP 2022 paper entitled "Elementary Type Inference". In addition we have successfully developed and published a new algorithm for addressing the challenges introduced by object-oriented (OO) subtyping, including bounded quantification, in polymorphic languages. Our type inference algorithm, which builds on the foundational work by Pierce and Turner for local type inference, incorporates recent advancements in higher-ranked type inference algorithms. This work is detailed in the paper "Greedy Implicit Bounded Quantification" by Chen Cui, Shengyi Jiang, and Bruno C. d. S. Oliveira, presented at the 37th ACM International Conference on Object-Oriented Programming, Systems, Languages, and Applications (OOPSLA 2023). Our algorithms significantly differ from previous approaches by employing novel techniques that enhance its efficiency and scalability, making it suitable for modern programming languages that support OO subtyping. The key contributions of our work include the development of robust type inference algorithms that can handle the complexities of OO subtyping in polymorphic languages. This algorithm not only improves the accuracy of type inference but also reduces the need for manual type annotations, thereby simplifying the programming process. Our approach ensures that the type inference system remains both expressive and practical for real-world applications. The successful implementation and validation of our algorithms in prototype systems demonstrate their effectiveness and potential for integration into existing programming languages and development tools. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of type systems and programming languages, providing a solid foundation for future research and development in this area. Objective 2: Mechanizing local type inference for simple dependent types We have made significant progress in mechanizing local type inference for simple dependent types, focusing on investigating local type inference in the presence of simple forms of dependent types, which are increasingly prominent in modern programming languages like Scala. Our work began with the design of a new declarative type system for a dependently typed language, capable of handling polymorphic subtyping. This foundational work was published in the journal Science of Computer Programming (SCP) in April 2021 and presented at ECOOP 2021 in the paper "A Dependently Typed Calculus with Polymorphic Subtyping" by Mingqi Xue and Bruno C. d. S. Oliveira. Our approach leverages recent advancements in type inference algorithms to ensure that the system remains both expressive and practical for real-world use. The key contributions of our work include enhanced type inference capabilities that handle dependent types, which are crucial for expressing more precise and flexible type relationships in programming languages. Moving forward, we plan to refine our algorithms further, explore additional optimizations, and extend our type system to support more complex forms of dependent types. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of programming languages and type systems, addressing important challenges and providing a solid foundation for future research and development. Objective 3: Mechanizing local type inference for type systems with intersection and union types We have made significant progress in mechanizing local type inference for type systems that include intersection and union types. This objective addresses the technical challenges necessary for developing inference algorithms capable of handling these complex type features. Our work is presented in the paper "Bidirectional Higher-Ranked Polymorphism with Intersection and Union Types" by Shengyi Jiang, Chen Cui, and Bruno C. d. S. Oliveira, which will be presented at the 52nd Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages (POPL 2025). Additionally, we have an ICFP 2021 paper that deals with related technical issues. The key contributions of our work include the development of algorithms that can efficiently infer types in the presence of intersection and union types, which are used in various modern programming languages such as Scala, RedHat Ceylon, Facebook Flow, and Microsoft TypeScript. Our approach leverages recent advancements in type inference to ensure that the system remains both expressive and practical for real-world use. We have implemented these algorithms in a prototype system, demonstrating their practicality and effectiveness in handling complex type relationships. Additional Relevant Work In addition to the main papers mentioned above, we have also published other relevant papers that were started after the beginning of this project. These papers further explore and expand on the objectives outlined above, contributing to the overall success and advancement of our research. "Distributing Intersection and Union Types with Splits and Duality" by Xuejing Huang and Bruno C. d. S. Oliveira, presented at ICFP 2021. This paper discusses the distribution of intersection and union types, which is directly relevant to our work on type systems with intersection and union types, and Objective 3. The paper called "Contextual Typing" by Xu Xue and Bruno C. d. S. Oliveira, presented at ICFP 2024 introduces a generalization of bidirectional typing called contextual typing. Contextual typing propagates not only known type information during typing but also other known information about the surrounding context of a term. This richer notion of contextual information reduces the need for annotations while remaining lightweight and scalable. This work is highly relevant to our objectives as it enhances the expressiveness and efficiency of type inference algorithms. These additional papers provide a broader context for our research and demonstrate the ongoing contributions we are making to the field of programming languages and type systems.
