Mechanizing local type inference for simple dependent types: The second objective is to investigate local type inference in the presence of simple forms of dependent types. Languages like Scala already support simple forms of dependent types, and dependent types are becoming more and more prominent in programming languages. They are therefore an important feature for programming languages in the near future. This objective will investigate the algorithms and metatheory for local type-inference with dependent types.

Mechanizing local type inference for type systems with intersection and union types: The final objective is to extend the results in the first objective with two important and non-trivial features: intersection and union types. Intersection and union types are employed currently in various languages (such as Scala, RedHat Ceylon, Facebook Flow or Microsoft Typescript). This goal will investigate the algorithms and metatheory for local type-inference with those features.

17209520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209520.value: For each of the objectives we had the following major findings: Objective 1: We developed novel algorithms for local type inference in polymorphic languages with object-oriented (OO) style subtyping. These algorithms have all desirable properties including soundness, completeness and decidability. Our approach enhances the accuracy and efficiency of type inference, reducing the need for manual type annotations and simplifying the programming process. The successful implementation of these algorithms in a prototype system demonstrates its practicality and potential for integration into existing programming languages and development tools. Objective 2: We designed a new declarative type system for a dependently typed language, capable of handling polymorphic subtyping. This type system has been show to be type sound and important properties of subtyping, including transitivity have been proved. Objective 3: We addressed the technical challenges necessary for developing inference algorithms capable of handling intersection and union types. Our work is sufficient to express a large and practical subset of languages like TypeScript or Flow, which are of high practical relevance. The type systems and algorithms have been proved to be sound, complete and decidable. All the metatheory for all the work above has been proved in the Coq theorem prover and we have simple prototype implementations. NOTE ABOUT PUBLICATIONS: Please note that in the area of Programming Languages, like in most other areas in Computer Science, the most prestigious venues for publication are conferences. However, major conferences (POPL, ICFP, OOPSLA, PLDI) now publish their proceedings in the Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages journal. My publication list includes only journals because most of my publications were presented in major conferences in the field, whose proceedings are published at the Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages journal. Thus, every publication in that journal has been physically presented in a conference.

17209520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209520.value: The research conducted in this project has laid a strong foundation for further advancements in type inference algorithms and type systems. Moving forward, there are several promising directions for further development. Firstly, we plan to refine and optimize the algorithms developed for local type inference, particularly focusing on enhancing their scalability and efficiency. This includes exploring new techniques and optimizations that can further reduce the computational overhead and improve the performance of the type inference process. Secondly, we aim to extend our type systems to support more complex forms of dependent types, intersection types, and union types. This involves not only theoretical advancements but also practical implementations and integrations with existing programming languages and development tools. Additionally, we see significant potential in applying our research to real-world programming languages and software development environments. By collaborating with industry partners and open-source communities, we can ensure that our algorithms and type systems are adopted and utilized in practical applications, thereby maximizing their impact. Finally, we plan to continue publishing our findings in leading conferences and journals, contributing to the academic discourse and fostering further research in this area. This ongoing dissemination of knowledge will help drive innovation and inspire new approaches to type inference and type systems. These proposed actions will ensure that our research continues to evolve and address the emerging challenges and opportunities in the field of programming languages and type systems.

17209520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209520.value: Our research project focuses on improving how computer programs understand and manage different types of data. We developed new methods to help programming languages automatically figure out the types of data being used, which makes writing and maintaining software easier and less error-prone. One part of our work dealt with making these methods work better with object-oriented programming, which is a common way to write software. Another part focused on handling more complex types of data that are becoming popular in modern programming languages. Finally, we worked on combining different types of data in ways that make programs more flexible and powerful. The significance of our research lies in its potential to make software development more efficient and reliable. By reducing the need for programmers to manually specify data types, our methods can save time and reduce mistakes. This can lead to better software that is easier to develop and maintain, benefiting both developers and users. Our findings provide a strong foundation for future advancements in programming languages and software development tools.

17210420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210420.value: 感應功率傳輸（IPT）技術已嵌入許多移動電子設備中，以取代傳統的有線功率連接和電池充電。這些設備涵蓋了社交通信，個人管理和娛樂，物聯網，醫療保健，環境和基礎設施監視與防禦系統的廣泛應用。耦合線圈是IPT系統中的關鍵組件。它們提供電能的非接觸式傳輸。 製作一對耦合線圈很容易。但是設計一個好的方案可能很困難。磁場是看不見的。因此，工程師使用有限元分析（FEA）和有限元磁模型來分析磁問題並開發更有效的解決方案。FEA是一種非常高的計算成本方法。在過去的幾十年中，研究致力於開髮用於設計分析的快速數值求解器。經驗豐富的磁性設計工程師使用FEA來研究磁場模式並優化其磁性設計。 在過去的幾年中，機器學習（ML）在解決複雜問題方面受到了極大的關注。最先進的機器學習模型已部署在圖像分析，自動駕駛汽車，醫療診斷，語言處理等各種應用中。有了新的機器智能，據報導機器學習是一種用於模式識別，預測分析和推薦生成的有前途的技術。在這個項目中，我們嘗試研究機器學習方法在感應功率傳輸應用的耦合線圈設計中的使用。具體來說，我們將製定適用於此應用程序的框架和方法。 這個為期兩年的項目的成功完成將拉近電磁仿真和ML之間的差距。該項目的結果有三方面： 1) 它為電磁設計開闢了一個新的研究場所。學生和工作人員將獲得新的知識和技能，從而使無線電力領域煥然一新。 2) 即將開發的新設計方法將提供新的見識和知識。無疑刺激了IPT技術的發展，激發了技術創新 3) 該項目中開發的ML方法和推薦系統將展示一種新解決方案，並促進行業適應新技術。 IPT技術的不斷發展必將使各行各業受益，從而改善人們的生活。

17210420.label: Realisation of objectives
17210420.value: The project started on 01 Jan 2021. One PhD student Mr. He Liangxi was working on this project. The Principal Investigator (PI) taught him the principles and latest development of wireless power transfer technologies. Unfortunately, the Co-Investigator (Co-I) Dr Yuen C.H., who is an expert in computer science quit HKU in May 2021. PI and Mr. He collaborated on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods to identify the system parameters of inductive power transfer systems from measured terminal voltage and current. A journal paper has been published based on this new proposal [1]. In this paper, ML method simplified the calculation for mutual inductance by transforming the measuring targets. The effectiveness of the ML method has been verified through experiments, which determined a maximum error of 2.9% in mutual inductance estimation and a maximum error of 7.4% in load resistance estimation. In summary, this study established the foundation for further research and addressed project objective 1. In the design of wireless power transfer (WPT) system, predicting the magnetic field distribution during the early design process is essential. However, traditional methods of predicting WPT magnetic field distribution have several drawbacks, including time-consuming computations, inaccurate models, and imprecise results. PI proposed the use of AI and ML methods to predict the magnetic field distribution of WPT system. By comparing the results obtained from COMSOL and ML, it was observed that ML offers faster calculation speeds, resulting in time savings for computing the WPT magnetic field distribution. The computation time for the magnetic field distribution using COMSOL increases with the number of turns in the coil, whereas the ML method’s computation time remains unaffected by the number of turns. Therefore, the ML model trained can perform fast computations to obtain magnetic field distribution maps. This work addressed the project objective 1, and has been accepted to publish in an IEEE conference [2]. Insights were gained regarding the use of ML methods for predicting the magnetic field distribution of a WPT system. PI proposed a ML-based method for optimizing WPT parameters. A convolutional neural network was adapted for training and predicting the performance of a pair of coupled coils based on a set of input parameters. The performance parameters included the spatial magnetic field distribution map, quality factor, inductance value, and mutual inductance value, all of which are critical in determining the efficiency and selecting optimal coil parameters such as the number of turns and wire diameter. The proposed ML method was successfully validated through experiments, demonstrating minimal discrepancies between the hardware measurement and predicted results. After training on 30,000 sets of data, the proposed method achieved an error value of 0.0034 for the obtained normalized image predictions. In comparison to commercial tool like COMSOL, ML exhibited significantly faster calculation times, regardless of the number of turns in the coupled coils. This accelerated the design and optimization process considerably. The predicted outcome using ML closely aligned with those from COMSOL, confirming the accuracy of the proposed ML method. This work directly addressed project objective 3 and has been accepted for publication in an international journal [3]. While exploring a recommender system that combines collected data and machine learning techniques, it has been categorized as product development, perceived to have limited innovation and research value. However, it has been confirmed that ML can serve as a reliable tool for the rapid design and optimization of WPT systems. A novel WPT system for capsule endoscope (CE) applications is developed to address the problem of insufficient energy during high-speed and high definition image acquisition or complex tasks. The structural design of a 3-dimensional transmitting coil (3DTC) and 1-dimensioinal receiving coil (1DRC) reduces the volume of the CE occupied by the receiving coil within the CE. The designed 3DTC is capable of generating a magnetic field in any spatial direction. When combined with attitude data feedback from the inertial measurement unit (IMU), real-time adjustments to the magnetic field direction can be made to facilitate WPT in any orientation. By collecting current information from each coil of 3DTC, closed-loop control can be achieved. In experimental examination, the CE demonstrated a relatively stable receiving wireless power, with an average current of 123 mA and an average power of 1512.9 mW. These values are sufficient to meet the power requirements of CEs. This research work successfully fulfilled the project objective 2 and has been accepted for publication in an IEEE conference [4].

17210520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210520.value: Living cells need to undergo significant shape changes during processes such as cell spreading, migration and endocytosis. Therefore, it is commonly believed that the deformability of cells is intimately related to their capability in executing different biological duties as well as the progression of diseases like cancer. Interestingly, recent evidence has indicated that a cell cannot fully recover to its original shape after being stretched locally. However, a robust method allowing us to precisely characterize the plasticity exhibited by the entire cell, which is more relevant in analyzing most cellular activities, is still lacking. In addition, our preliminary study suggested that the plastic response of breast cancer cells is correlated with their invasiveness. Nevertheless, whether this is also true for other carcinoma cell lines and, more importantly, tumor cells extracted from real cancer patients remains unclear. This issue is not only important for our basic understanding of tumor development but could also be critical for potentially using cell plasticity as a novel metastatic potential marker in future clinical applications. Finally, although it is conceivable that the observed irreversible deformation inside the cell is induced by cytoskeletal damage, the fundamental question of how microscopic details of the cytoskeleton dictate the bulk plastic response of cells remains largely unanswered. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address these outstanding issues. Specifically, on the basis of our pilot studies, a novel microfluidic system for quantitatively characterizing the plasticity of cells will be developed. The plastic response of different cancer cell lines and circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from lung cancer patients will then be systematically measured. At the same time, the cytoskeletal structures of these cells will also be closely monitored via fluorescence and confocal imaging. Data to be generated here in conjunction with subsequent theoretical modeling, taking into account important features that were neglected in previous investigations, will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that the plastic response of cancer cells is regulated by cytoskeleton integrity and correlated with metastatic potential. If successful, this project will greatly enhance our basic understanding of how processes like tumor invasion and metastasis take place as well as provide critical clues for the design of new strategies for cancer diagnosis and prognosis. In addition, the comprehensive data to be generated by this study are also expected to be extremely useful in guiding/assisting the development of future theories. 細胞在擴散，遷移和胞吞等過程中需要經歷明顯的形狀變化。因此，研究人员普遍認為細胞的可變形性與其執行不同生命任務的能力以及諸如癌症等疾病的發展密切相關。有趣的是，最近的證據表明，細胞在受局部拉伸後并不能完全恢復其原始形狀。然而，我们仍然缺乏一種能精確表徵細胞塑性響應的方法。此外，我們的初步研究表明乳腺癌細胞的塑性反應與其侵襲性有關。然而，这一關聯是否也存在於其它癌細胞系或從癌症患者中提取的腫瘤細胞中尚不清楚。這個問題不僅對於我們對腫瘤發展的基本理解很关键，而且對於是否在將來的臨床應用中可以使用細胞塑性響應作為新的標記物也至關重要。 在這個項目中，我們計劃進行實驗和模拟相结合的研究來解決這些懸而未決的問題。具體而言，在我們的前期研究的基礎上，一種定量表徵細胞塑性響應的微流系統將会被開發出来。然後此系統将被用来系统測量來自肺癌患者的不同癌細胞系和循環腫瘤細胞（CTC）的塑性变形能力。同時，這些細胞的細胞骨架結構也將通過熒光和共聚焦成像進行密切監測。将建立的理論模型和得到的數據將明確確認或駁斥我們的主要假設，即癌細胞的塑性響應受細胞骨架完整性調節並與其轉移潛力相關。如获成功，該項目將極大地增強我們對腫瘤侵襲和轉移等過程發生机理的理解，並為設計新的癌症診斷和监控策略提供關鍵線索。此外，該研究將得到的大量數據也能极大的協助/指導未來细胞力学理論的發展。

17210520.label: Realisation of objectives
17210520.value: 1. A microfluidic system capable of imposing precisely controlled cyclic deformation on cells and therefore probing their plastic characteristics has been developed. In addition, robust methods for introducing damages to the cell membrane and cortex-membrane attachment have also been established. 2. The plastic responses of tumor cell lines with distinct invasiveness, as well as circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from lung cancer patients, were carefully examined using different setups developed. 3. By considering the breakage and re-bundling/re-crosslinking of cytoskeletal biopolymers, models were proposed to elucidate the physical origins of the plastic response of cells. In addition, a mechanism-based theory was also developed to explain how plastic/permanent constriction of cells can be induced by active internal contraction.

17210520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210520.value: 1. A microfluidic system capable of imposing cyclic deformation, with precisely controlled duration and amplitude, on cells and therefore probing their plastic characteristics has been developed (refer to item 8-1 in Part C). In addition, methods for introducing membrane damages through mechanical puncturing (see item 8-3 in Part C) or cell blebbing via mechanical compression (refer to item 8-4 in Part C) have also been established. 2. Under imposed deformation, it was found that significant plastic strain can accumulate rapidly in highly invasive cancer cell lines and circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from late-stage lung cancer patients with a characteristic time of a few seconds. In contrast, very little irreversible deformation is observed in the less invasive cell lines and CTCs from early-stage lung cancer patients (refer to item 8-1 in Part C). Furthermore, the membrane self-repairing capability (item 8-3 in Part C) and blebbing response (item 8-4 in Part C) of different cancer cells were found to depend on their drug-resistivity and annexin-6 levels. 3. By considering the breakage and re-bundling of F-actin under loading, we have developed a physical model to show how cellular plasticity can be triggered (refer to item 8-2 in Part C). We also demonstrated the dissociation and re-binding of crosslinks within the biopolymer network could lead to its irreversible deformation (see item 8-5 in Part C). Finally, a mechanism-based theory was proposed to show that, in response to optical or mechanical stimuli, the myosin contraction and thermal fluctuation–assisted formation and pinching of endocytic vesicles could lead to permanent shortening of cell junctions and that such plastic constriction can stretch neighboring cells and trigger their active contraction through mechanochemical feedbacks and eventually their plastic deformations as well (item 8-6 in Part C).

17210520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210520.value: We have developed novel setups to systematically characterize the plastic response of cells under different loading and stimulation conditions. Utilizing these methods, it was found that significant irreversible deformation can accumulate rapidly in highly invasive cancer cell lines and circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from late-stage lung cancer patients with a characteristic time of a few seconds. In contrast, very little irreversible deformation is observed in the less invasive cell lines and CTCs from early-stage lung cancer patients. Furthermore, the membrane self-repairing capability and blebbing response of different cancer cells were found to depend on their drug-resistivity and annexin-6 levels. Findings from this study shed lights on the development of new strategies for cancer monitoring and treatment.

17210720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210720.value: There are numerous engineering problems where noise is carried by flow through a duct. Examples include aircraft engines, gas turbines, exhaust stacks in power plants, building ventilation systems, etc. In most cases, noise control by sound absorbers is hampered by the penalty of flow energy loss due to the drag on the absorbers. Without drag consideration, there would be no problem of duct noise! This naturally leads us to the airfoil shape to minimize the drag. A closer look at the traditional, rectangular absorbers in grazing sound incidence reveals that they work well only for a limited band in the noise absorption spectrum, much narrower than the range frequently found in practical applications, such as from 50 Hz to 5000 Hz. As the peak frequency roughly scales with the absorber thickness, a broadband absorber should have a suitable thickness distribution along its length. That may well look like an airfoil designed to reduce the aircraft drag! Initial experimental results for a new silencer with a modest degree of streamlining and other new acoustic features demonstrate an extra noise reduction of 8.5dB, or a sevenfold reduction in sound energy, compared with the traditional design subject to the same drag. Whether or not a minimum-drag airfoil is exactly the best-performing sound absorber is an open question. To satisfy this curiosity is our first motivation but our goal is to go further to explore how an acoustic sink far better than existing technology is possible when drag is imposed as a stringent constraint. More specifically, we will embark on three tasks. (a) For a simple cascade of absorbers, we examine the relationship between the drag minimization and the broadband sound absorption design. The expected outcome is what we call a “sound-foil” with a specified drag allowance. (b) We explore new smart structures inside such sound-foils to broaden the sound absorption spectrum towards the difficult regime of low frequencies. (c) We explore new patterns of sound-foils which may perform better than a simple cascade, a thought inspired by fish schooling. Through this project we hope to find a new path towards a comprehensive solution for the broadband duct noise pollution. 有許多工程問題中，管道流動會攜帶噪聲，常見的例子包括飛機發動機，燃氣輪機，發電廠中的排氣煙囪，建築物通風系統等。許多時候吸聲器本身造成的阻力會妨礙系統性能。如果這個自身阻力不需要考慮，那噪聲問題就不是個問題了！本課題探討採用翼型設計以最大程度地減小這個阻力。我們發現在傳統的矩形吸聲器在掠入射情況下，吸聲僅在頻譜中的有限頻帶上有效，而該頻帶比實際應用的範圍（例如50 Hz至5000 Hz）要窄得多。由於吸聲峰值頻率與吸聲器的厚度大致成比例，因此寬帶吸聲器應沿其長度方向應該具有合適的厚度分佈。這看起來很像是旨在減少飛機阻力的機翼了！與具有相同阻力的傳統設計相比，具有適度流線型和其他新聲學功能的新型消音器的初步實驗結果表明，這樣的消聲器可將總噪音進一步降低8.5dB、也就是聲能再降低七倍。最小阻力的機翼是否正好也是性能最佳的吸聲器呢？這可是一個懸而未決的科學問題。回答這個問題以滿足科學好奇心是本課題的首要動機，但我們進一步的目標是探索在以阻力作為一個優化約束的條件下，如何實現比現有技術更好的聲吸收。更具體地說，我們將執行三個任務。 （a）對於簡單的吸聲器排列，我們研究阻力最小化與寬帶吸聲設計之間的關係。我們預期得到一個具有指定阻力許可量的設計，稱為“聲翼”。 （b）我們拓展此類聲翼內部的新結構設計，以期將吸聲譜擴大到技術上困難的低頻範圍。 （c）我們還將探索聲翼的空間排列模式以達到類似魚群效應的最佳結果。通過該項目，我們希望找到一條解決寬帶管道噪聲污染問題的新途徑。

17210720.label: Realisation of objectives
17210720.value: This project was awarded upon re-submission, and so a considerable amount of preparatory work was carried out. All anticipated outcomes and effects were found to be true in the actual project implementation. However, such validation is only qualitative, while quantitative findings suggest adaptation of specific research plan which has led to many new and important research discoveries outlined below. Objective 1 on spectral imbalance. It is true that all existing silencer designs only cover the mid-high frequency range and the focus of the current project is therefore the low and very high frequencies. When these two extremes are covered, we achieve improved spectral matching (or balance) for engineering noise problems. The major finding of the project is that the coverage of the high frequency range can be achieved through our airfoil-shaped absorber, or equivalent, but the space cost for the low-frequency part is still far too high for practical purposes. This firm conclusion has led to the adaptation of the search towards new approaches which do not involve excessive space requirement. What we did was to use the loudspeaker diaphragm with electrical shunt-circuit. This is so because any modification in shunt circuit involves only electrical component whose physical volume is negligible. The reason why such addition still keeps the study within the scope of the original project is that the effect of the shunt circuit is acoustically equivalent to modifying mechanical components and the acousto-electric coupling is mathematically represented by a simple scalar. Papers listed as [2] and [4] in Part C represent the output in this adapted direction where shunt circuit is a direct substitute of mechanical components. Paper [3] differs slightly in its use of piezoelectric patch to replace the diaphragm but with similar acoustic goal. Paper [2] also extended the goal to vibration isolation which is fundamentally related to noise isolation. However, none of these have addressed the fundamental problem of impractical requirement of device space at low frequencies, which is central to the current project. Paper [1] does offer a very different prospect of tackling low-frequency problem by partially converting low-frequency sound energy to higher frequencies which can then be absorbed easily. Objective 2 on smart interior design. The outcome of this part of study closely follows the original proposal and the result is very encouraging. The most important discovery is the following. The fluid mechanics constraint, which dictates the total noise reduction, is a local (near field) effect which is sensitive to the shape of the interface between the air passage and the bulk silencer material. However, the interior of the silencer has a “long-range” impact on the acoustic field. Because of this, what happens inside the silencer affects the acoustic result but is decoupled from fluid mechanics constraints. By working on interior structure design, one is better able to match the silencer spectrum with that of the incident sound. To tackle low-frequency noise, an embedded perforated panel with very low porosity is used such that the unit response brings a broad peak in the low-frequency region. However, for high-frequency noise, one can simply adjust the location of the above embedded panel beneath the surface exposed to airflow. A very shallow porous layer causes absorption peak towards higher frequencies. Together with the gain in the low-frequency region, an optimized silencer unit with embedded panel achieves the widest bandwidth in terms of silencer performance. Major results in this step form the submission of paper [6] which is being extensively revised at the time of writing this report. The reason why this publication has been rather late in the making is due to two factors. One is the scale of experiments involved goes beyond normal university laboratory (we needed the help an external certified testing centre in the mainland), and the second reason is that the main PhD student undertaking the task suffered from health problems for an extensive period of time during the pandemic. Albeit with some delay in publication, we are still rather pleased with the research outcome. For example, the frequency range examined in the final results is one octave wider than what was proposed and is thus closer to practical engineering applications. With the help of optimized interior structure, the typical gain in the silencer performance is 5dB, which is very significant for industrial applications. Objective 3 on external silencer shape. Aerodynamically, we found that the most critical factor for the total pressure loss is the avoidance of narrow cross section in the entire flow passage. Under this condition, the use of airfoil shape will be beneficial for the further reduction of pressure loss caused by flow separation. Descent result can be obtained by a simple diffusor design, but more streamlined shape like airfoil can further minimize the loss. For reasons of keeping the total length under a certain limit, use of the combination of flat diffusor and partial airfoil shape can also be considered. In terms of acoustics, any change of flow passage will benefit the high-frequency noise control by acoustic scattering. The question is whether such benefit is accompanied by corresponding pressure loss. When silencer made of homogeneous porous material is used, whatever the external shape, the contribution of scattering is rather limited. The use of the interior structure as described under Objective 2 is important. If the cost of manufacturing is not a critical consideration, optimization of interior structure under the airfoil shape will definitely maximize the overall performance. Paper [6] does not go as far as to achieve such optimal performance as the focus is on development of designs most likely to find practical engineering applications. With such guideline, the use of interior structure under simple diffusor geometry is adopted. The answer to the question posed in the original proposal is clear: what is best for fluid mechanics differs from what is best for acoustics. Acoustics can be better taken care of by interior structure design as described above and the fluid mechanics problem in silencer also differs from traditional aerodynamics problem for aircraft wings. We are rather satisfied by this clear-cut conclusion despite the fact that we were rather curious about the possibility of the reverse conclusion at the proposal stage. Objective 4 on multiple sound-foils and acoustic scattering effects. Yes, multiple segments are definitely required for design optimization. However, having conducted extensive parametric studies, it is realized that the gain in acoustic scattering by eccentric placement of central segment will not outweigh the increase in production cost for most typical industrial applications. However, when the frequency band is further extended beyond 4kHz or 8kHz, the gain in scattering effect will outweigh the cost through complicating the structural design. Detailed discussions and essential conclusions in this regard are included in paper [6].

17210720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210720.value: Broadband duct noise control requires a huge volume for the silencer accompanied by a high pressure-loss (or energy consumption) for the flow conduit. The project seeks the best design when the total pressure loss is given as a design constraint. Low-loss airfoil is examined for its potential use and the following findings are made. (1) Direct deployment of classic airfoil shape for an array of silencers is not feasible, and the most critical issue is the avoidance of local narrow flow passage. When this issue is resolved, the airfoil shape can indeed help control flow separation and minimize fluid dynamic losses, which can be translated directly into acoustic gains. Details are given in paper [6] listed in Sec. C. (2) For a given total pressure loss, there is an obvious upper limit of sound absorption by pure mechanical designs. Electrically shunted diaphragm has been introduced to see if the electro-acoustic coupling can offer acoustic gains without the strict geometric limitation since circuit components are usually small. Results in papers [2-5] indicate that the shunt circuit offers a very convenient approach of achieving the best design. When incident sound changes its spectrum and is rather mismatched with the silencer performance (cf. objective 1), the silencer can be adapted by passive electronic means without changing its mechanical design. In addition, paper [1] points to the possibility that part of the incident sound energy can be transformed from low frequency to high frequency to be effectively absorbed. This is a new exciting prospect totally out of the “box”, but the realization of a complete electroacoustic silencer is left to future studies. (3) In the pure mechanical design, it is concluded that what is best for fluid mechanics differs from what is best for acoustics. Fluid mechanics depends on local shapes of the silencer, while acoustic performance of a silencer depends on both interior structures (cf. objective 2) and external shapes. Placement of simple embedded perforated panel can significantly broaden the silencer performance and a typical improvement by such design, plus the diffusor design, amounts to at least 5dB for a generic noise spectrum spanning the huge range of 80-8000 Hz, cf. Paper [6]. Even more broadband phenomenon is observed when shunt circuit is used in the related problem of vibration problem, cf. paper [2].

17210720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210720.value: Out of the typical 5dB gain in silencer performance described in paper [6] for the typical silencer used in industry with 15-20dB total noise reduction, about half of the gain is derived from the acoustic structure design and half from the fluid dynamic improvements. Both have the potential to go a step further. For acoustic structure, we merely explored the use of embedded perforated panel with uniform properties. Gradient parameter design and optimized panel curvature can be further explored. For fluid dynamics, more aggressive diffusor design with more specialized airfoil segments will be tested. A diffusor with straight walls can compromise acoustic gains and so a more advanced design like a diffusor with multiple exit flow passages can be explored. With such consolidation, we shall endeavour to see it through in real silencer products. We are in contact with local acoustic manufacturers for this development and shall seek ITF funding support. We shall also further develop the electro-acoustic approach of matching the changing incident wave spectrum with a silencer of fixed geometry. These will form the content of next research proposals [1,4].

17210720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210720.value: The problem of noise carried by flow in ducts exists in numerous industrial and daily-life applications, such as aircraft engines and ventilation duct systems. The difficulty of reducing such noise lies in the wide range of sound frequencies and that low frequency requires a large volume of absorber that will cause high energy loss in flow. This project began by examining the use of aircraft wing shape to reduce the flow drag and hence the flow energy loss. It was found that, while the anticipated airfoil effects exist in the duct, it has to be carefully deployed inside a duct since the airfoil is not meant for use in ducts. It was also found that the acoustic performance mainly depends on the structural design inside the absorber contrasting with aerodynamics. A simplified version of the optimized design was actually implemented in an urban renewal project of power plant noise control in preparation for the Asian Games Hangzhou 2023. Through the studies we also recognized that the optimized design has its limits, so the project went beyond pure mechanical means by introducing electro-mechanical coupling, and reached many useful conclusions that will be further developed in future projects.

17211220.label: Project Objectives
17211220.value: Coordinating the primary color light for an efficient polychromatic EL In order to achieve efficient polychromatic EL in PeLEDs for various target applications, the coordination of the primary color light is very important but has not been clearly studied. In this proposal, we propose the unique combination of q-2D perovskite (as the front short-wavelength light emitter) and NC perovskite (as the back long-wavelength emitter) to establish the novel polychromatic EL structure. The structure can also prevent the long-wavelength light absorption in the front emitter and take the advantage of the solvent compatibility between the two perovskites. As a case study, we will investigate white light emission to show the ways for achieving efficient polychromatic EL. (1) We will coordinate the primary colors by experimentally adjusting the stacking number of blue q-2D perovskites and the mixed halides ratio of red NC perovskites, and by conducting colorimetry calculation with CIE chromaticity plots. (2) We will enhance the primary color intensity by minimizing perovskite defects through introducing ionic liquids and metal dopants into the q-2D and NC perovskites respectively. (3) While the device-structure design for manipulating the carrier distribution in the emitters is crucial for realizing the white polychromatic EL, this issue is not thoroughly studied. We will conduct multi-physical (electrical and optical) studies for whole PC-PeLED device structures together with the measured material parameters. The theoretical results will be combined with experimental demonstration to finalize the design of PC-PeLEDs. Designing an effective ICL for PC-PeLEDs For PC-PeLEDs constructed from the new polychromatic EL structure, such as PC-PeLED with an architecture of anode/ hole transport layer (HTL)/ q-2D perovskite/ ICL/ NC perovskite/ electron transport layer (ETL)/ cathode, the carrier transport mechanisms of ICLs which are important for understanding and optimizing device performances are yet to reach conclusive understanding. We will formulate targeted models based on our previous work and unveil the carrier transport mechanisms of different ICLs through rigorous simulations. Together with the theoretical results, PC-PeLEDs with different ICLs including layered and mixed material structures will be characterized and analyzed for ICLs optimization. To achieve effective ICLs, we will simultaneously address the ion-exchange and solvent incompatibility issues among perovskites and ICL materials by designing properly layered structures and selecting appropriate materials and solvents. Meanwhile, the electrical properties and band-alignment of the carrier transport materials of ICLs are very important to achieve the efficient and appropriate carrier transportation for suitable carrier distributions in the perovskite emitters. Besides studying commercially available materials, we propose to use our home-synthesized metal-oxide nanomaterials particularly ternary metal oxides featured with their adjustable bandgap and conductivity, low-temperature processes (for avoiding thermal damage of perovskites), and the use of perovskite and organic materials compatible solvents. 3. Achieving high-performance PC-PeLEDs To obtain high-performance PC-PeLEDs, we will focus on their EQE, spectral stability, and operational stability. For EQE, we will theoretically and experimentally analyze the EQE loss mechanisms and evaluate their effects on device performances, including non-radiative recombination loss, interfacial loss, optical loss, and the loss from detrimental carrier distribution. For the spectral stability, since the changes of carrier transportation governed by various mechanisms (as stated in Part II-2(b)2(1)) with external voltage biases and temperatures will be different, we will simulate PC-PeLED performances taking into account effects of various voltage biases and temperatures with different mechanisms. The corresponding PC-PeLED characterizations will be made and compared with theoretical results. Finally, we will establish a guideline for achieving spectrally stable PC-PeLEDs . *** To show our capability to manage the project, we have started to work on the project. The preliminary results show that, in Objective 1, by using a new ionic liquid and adjusting the q-2D perovskite, we enhance the blue PeLED intensity to 5737 cd m-2 luminance. In Objective 3, by forming a new co-ligand quasi-core/shell structure in NC perovskite, we enhance the red PeLED lifetime to 316.5 hrs. They are the best results in the correspondingly reported PeLEDs from our best knowledge as detailed in “Research Plan and Methodology”.

17211220.value: 作為有前景的溶液處理光源之一，鈣鈦礦發光二極管由於具有寬波長可調性，高量子效率和良好的色純度等優異特性而引起了社會的廣泛關注。已經從基於鈣鈦礦的薄膜，納米晶體和準2維結構中證明了具有綠色，藍色和紅色基色的電致發光。多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管提供了超越原色發光二極管極限的實現多峰甚至白電致發光的獨特自由度，從而擴展了鈣鈦礦發光二極管在生物醫學光譜/成像和照明等不同領域的潛在應用。 雖然堆疊不同的原色發光體是在發光二極管中實現多色電致發光的公認方法，但是對通過堆疊不同鈣鈦礦發光體構造的多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管進行的研究有限，並且面臨幾個主要挑戰：（1）離子交換 鈣鈦礦與固溶體材料之間的溶劑不相容性會導致意外的發光並損壞鈣鈦礦。（2）差的外部量子效率，缺乏對該發光二極管器件物理的了解。（3）低光譜穩定性，這在不同的電壓偏置和溫度下，受到鈣鈦礦發射體中載流子分佈穩定性的嚴重影響。（4）差的操作穩定性主要受鈣鈦礦發射器的穩定性和熱降解的影響，在有限的理解下，尤其是在器件操作過程中產生的熱量的負面影響。 受益於我們最近在多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管方面的工作，我們提出了一種新穎的準2維鈣鈦礦-互連層-納米晶體鈣鈦礦多色電致發光結構，以同時解決上述挑戰。在這個項目中，我們的目標是（1）從戰略上將準2維鈣鈦礦與納米晶體鈣鈦礦匹配，以最大程度地減少鈣鈦礦之間溶劑誘導的改性，並插入互連層以解決離子交換和溶劑不相容性問題。（2）有效地協調原色鈣鈦礦的顏色，強度和光譜穩定性，以實現有效的多色電致發光；（3）揭示不同互連層的基本載流子傳輸機制，並給出了光譜穩定的多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管的互連層設計指南；（4）通過對損耗機理和電流產生的熱效應進行全面的理論和實驗分析，對材料和器件進行設計和優化，從而獲得較高的外部量子效率和操作穩定性。因此，這項工作對於實現高效的多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管具有根本和實際的重要性。提高多色鈣鈦礦發光二極管和其他串聯/堆疊設備的理論理解，實驗材料的進步和設備結構設計，以實現高性能以促進其應用。

17211220.label: Realisation of objectives
17211220.value: For objective 1, we incorporated 1-cyclohexene-1-ethanamine cation (CEA+) into the host 1-phenylbutylamine cation (PBA+) and fabricating mixed-cations nano-perovskites, a homogeneous phase distribution in nano-perovskite films is achieved through precise tuning of the phase formation energy. The resulting perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) exhibit remarkable performance with an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 5.8% at 467 nm, which is one of the highest EQEs among the pure-blue PeLED devices with emission wavelengths below 470 nm. Additionally, the device demonstrates a half-lifetime of 25 mins. Furthermore, the PeLEDs utilizing mixed-cation perovskite exhibit a stable electroluminescence (EL) spectrum under varying voltage biases, even when the chlorine content in the halogen sites reaches as high as 30%. Overall, this work offers a novel and promising avenue to achieve both high EQE and a stable EL spectrum in blue-light PeLEDs. [Adv. Opti. Mater., 2302273, 2024]. We also reported a facile ionic liquid (IL, 1,3-dimethyl-3-imidazolium hexafluorophosphate) post-treatment on the as-fabricated perovskite film to passivate the uncoordinated Pb through the strong interaction with IL. The IL-assisted perovskite film demonstrates a great enhancement of radiative recombination efficiency, and the photoluminescence quantum yield of the film increases from 35.7% to 74.6%. IL post-treatment also adjusts the energy level of perovskite film and enhances the hole injection in PeLEDs. As a result, the peak EQE of the blue PeLED is improved from 4.0% to 9.0%, and the turn-on voltage is reduced from 3.3 to 3.0 V. This work contributes to a feasible and effective approach for improving the quality of blue perovskites and enhancing the efficiency of blue PeLEDs.[Adv. Opt. Mater., 202202721, 2023] We further reported that the introduction of multifunctional side-chain-promoted polymer architectures in the synthesis of I/Br-mixed perovskite nanocrystals (PeNCs) to suppress halide segregation and enable electroluminescent stability of the PeLEDs up to ~2500 min, which is the longest to our knowledge. Meanwhile, the PeLEDs exhibit the pure-red electroluminescence spectrum with Commission Internationale de l’Eclairage coordinates (0.705, 0.292) at one of the highest external quantum efficiencies reported to date, 23.6%. Fundamentally, the as-proposed polymer ligand architecture simultaneously offers long-term nanocrystal dispersion, good charge transport, defect elimination, and phase segregation suppression. Overall, the work demonstrates the potential of the multifunctionalized polymer ligands for developing high-performance PeLEDs toward practical applications. [ACS Energy Lett., 9, 2118, 2024] For objective 2, we established a capacitance-voltage (C-V) model for PeLEDs to describe carrier behaviors. Four different regions in this typical C-V model, including a neutrality region, a barrier region, a carrier diffusion region, and a carrier recombination region, were analyzed. Importantly, the C-V model is implemented to improve the EL emission. By studying the measured C-V characteristics of a typical PeLED, issues of a high hole injection barrier and insufficient recombination are revealed. To address them, one MoO3 interface layer with a deep conduction band minimum is designed between a hole transport layer and a hole injection layer to enhance the hole injection. The C-V characteristics for the optimized PeLED confirm the reduced injection barrier and strengthened recombination rate. The optimized PeLED shows an improved external quantum efficiency from 8.34% to 15.82%. The C-V model helps us to quantitatively understand the essential carrier behaviors in PeLEDs and can serve as an efficient method to improve the EL performance of PeLEDs.[Appl. Phys. Lett., 120, 243501, 2022] We also applied 2D chiral perovskites as the spin injection layer and CdSe/ZnS quantum dots (QDs) as the active layer to construct a spin-QLED. The chiral perovskite is inserted into the classic QLED device between TFB and QDs. The Chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect of chiral perovskites endows spin polarization to the injected holes. The spin-polarized holes recombine with related electrons based on the optical selection rules, resulting in circularly polarized electroluminescence (CP-EL) emission. By modifying the chiral perovskite layer, the spin-QLED devices achieve a CP-EL asymmetric factor (gCP-EL) of 1.6 × 10-2. From the simulation of the device, we can see that the recombination center is close to the chiral perovskites/QDs interface, which benefits the gCP-EL of the spin-QLED device. [Adv. Mater., 2305604, 2023] For objective 3, we dedicated to the p-type inorganic semiconductor material of cuprous sulfide (Cu2S). We demonstrate the solution-based formation of Cu2S with almost perfect lattice matching with a measured value of 99.71% on the perovskite Cs3Cu2I5 to establish core/shell Cs3Cu2I5/Cu2S nanocrystals. This is achieved by carefully controlling the reactivity of the precursors used for the shell layer synthesis. The photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of the core/shell structures dramatically increased from 26.8% to 70.6%. With these advancements, we further design and construct an architecture of Cs3Cu2I5/Cu2S NCs- hole injection layer of Cs1Cu2I3 for efficient white PeLEDs (W-PeLEDs). The EQE reached 3.45% and a color-rendering index (CRI) showed a very high value of 91. This represents the highest reported electroluminescent performance for lead-free copper-based W-PeLEDs. Our findings provide a straightforward and efficient strategy for highly efficient W-PeLEDs, offering promising prospects for advancing the lighting technologies [Adavnced Materials Under review]. We also introduced an electron attractor of phenethylammonium (PEA+) to the surface of PeNCs. The PEA+ conjugated ligands can reversibly store and release electrons driven by the electron local density of states redistribution, which enhances the delocalization of electrons in PeNCs, and thus suppresses PeNCs charging at high carrier concentrations, as evidenced by the excitation energy-dependent photoluminescence. Besides, PEA+ down-shifts the Fermi level of perovskite PeNCs, consequently increasing the hole concentration, and thus greatly improving hole conduction. The halogen-rich synthesis environment also reduces the number of halogen vacancies, consequently narrowing the distribution of electronic states at the band edges, leading to slightly improved electron conduction. By leveraging the enhanced electron delocalization and improved charge transportation, the CsPbI3 PeNCs LEDs demonstrate a maximum EQE of 15.6% with low-efficiency roll-off and a maximum luminance of 1634 cd m-2. [Adv. Optical Mater., 10, 2200189, 2022] We also systematically investigated the effect of microcavity on the efficiency of PeLEDs and demonstrated that an extremely high efficiency of over 50% is achievable. To explain the high efficiency, we demonstrated that the high ratio of the horizontal dipole with high efficiency is obtained in the strong-microcavity PeLED. Furthermore, we present that the efficiency can increase with increasing EML refractive index, which contradicts classical ray optics. The phenomenon is attributed to the attenuated near-field coupling and the selective enhancement of dipole emission. In the microcavity PeLED, the horizontal dipole shows three times the Purcell factor of the vertical dipole, indicating that the horizontal dipole emits 86% of light. We think that microcavity turns the disadvantage of high-index EML into an advantage and provides an opportunity for PeLEDs to surpass OLEDs in terms of efficiency. Accordingly, the experiment verified the optical performance improvement by microcavity optimization. [Adv. Opt. Mater., 11, 2300912, 2023].

17211220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211220.value: In the whole project, 29 research articles have been published in international peer-reviewed journals partially supported by the project. We successfully developed ligand-modified blue and red nano-perovskites by the Rec.2100 standard, and the resulting monochromatic color devices exhibited high EQE and demonstrated significantly improved operational stability. Specifically, the introduction of ligands effectively eliminated defects, enhanced the spectral stability of perovskite, and achieved high PLQY of perovskite film. Furthermore, the ligands modified the band structure of perovskite, facilitating charge transport within the device. In summary, research on the primary colors is expected to advance the study and practical applications of W-PeLEDs. To improve the EL performance of PeLEDs, analyzing and optimizing carrier behaviors (e.g., enhancing the rate of carrier injection, transporting, and recombination) are widely implemented strategies. A C-V model for PeLEDs is established to analyze carrier behaviors, including carrier injection, transportation, and recombination. By studying the measured C–V characteristics of a typical PeLED, issues of a high hole injection barrier and insufficient recombination are revealed. To address these issues, a MoO3 interface layer is inserted between the hole transport layer (HTL) and hole injection layer (HIL) to enhance the hole injection. Consequently, the optimized PeLED shows an improved EQE from 8.34% to 15.82%. The C–V model helps us to quantitatively understand the essential carrier behaviors in PeLEDs and can serve as an efficient method to improve the EL performance of PeLEDs. The research presented in these studies highlights significant advancements in the field of PeLEDs with various innovative approaches. Firstly, the development of core/shell Cs3Cu2I5/Cu2S nanocrystals demonstrated a substantial increase in PLQY, leading to the successful fabrication of efficient W-PeLEDs. Secondly, the introduction of PEA+ ligands to PeNCs improved electron delocalization and charge transportation, resulting in reduced joule heat in PeLEDs. Lastly, the investigation into the impact of microcavity on PeLED efficiency revealed the potential for achieving over 50% efficiency by optimizing the dipole orientation and refractive index within the device. These findings collectively contribute to advancing PeLED technologies with improved performances.

17211220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17211220.value: Perovskite materials have garnered significant attention for their wide wavelength tunability, high quantum efficiency, and excellent light color purity. EL with the primary colors of green, blue, and red has been demonstrated from perovskite-based thin films, NCs, and perovskite structures. The development of highly efficient red and blue nano-perovskites enables the realization of multiple-peak and white EL emission, expanding the potential applications of PeLEDs in fields such as lighting, display, etc. Meanwhile, stacking different primary color emitters is a well-recognized approach for realizing polychromatic EL in LEDs. The development of ICL is very important for achieving efficient and appropriate carrier transport for suitable carrier distributions in the perovskite emitters. Besides, effective ICLs can simultaneously address the ion exchange and solvent incompatibility issues among perovskites. With the achievement of the above research projects, the light extraction technique is an effective strategy to further enhance energy utilization, especially toward light loss caused by wave-guided modes and surface plasmon polariton modes in W-PeLEDs. Various light outcoupling techniques, such as micro-lens arrays and nanoimprint patterns, have been introduced into the PeLEDs to enhance light emission. In the future, the development of convenient, high-performance, and low-cost integrated technology for W-PeLEDs is an important direction.

17211220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211220.value: In this project, significant improvement of the emission properties has been demonstrated in the advanced PeLEDs using various original approaches. By developing new emission materials integrated with carrier transport materials, we have achieved high efficiency and stability in primary light and white light emission. We then analyzed and optimized carrier behaviors to further enhance the light emission performance. Additionally, we designed the device structures and introduced optical structures to improve the light emission properties and thus obtain both optical and electrical enhancement, resulting in improved overall efficiency. These advancements in PeLED technology hold great promise for future applications in lighting and displays, showcasing the continuous evolution of energy-efficient and high-performance lighting solutions.

17211320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211320.value: Nonlinear estimation is frequently encountered in cyber-physical and complex systems which range from power system state estimation, data analytics in smart city to identification of gene regulatory networks, etc. Such information is crucial to efficient control, data driven modeling and detection of anomalies and faults for reliable operations. In applications such as smart grid, large number of measurements and variables located at distant geographical areas will be involved say in system state estimation and power flow, etc This makes distributed estimation a problem of fundamental importance. An efficient and scalable approach for large-scale distributed estimation which is robust to outlying measurements, signal non-stationarity, and various uncertainties, represents a major challenge in these applications. The alternating direction method of multipliers is a promising framework as it decomposes the entire problem into local subproblems, which can be solved locally with limited information exchange between each others. Its reduced communication overhead and local computational complexity make it extremely scalable. A limitation of this conventional approach is that it is rather sensitive to the selection of the penalty parameters and generally does not include nonlinear equality/inequality constraints. This affects its convergence speed and applicability to problems with physical constraints in the optimization variables. Moreover, for online applications, an effective recursive algorithm for solving the local subproblems is essential to deal with possibly streaming incoming measurements/data. This proposal aims to develop a novel framework for large-scale online distributed estimation with both equality and inequality constraints. More specifically, we shall 1) incorporate physical or other desirable inequality constraints via the augmented Lagrangian method into our previously developed framework, 2) develop new approaches for solving the subproblems online for streaming data, and 3) investigate its application to distributed power system state estimation, optimal power flow, and other related problems such as fault/anomaly detection under various physical constraints. Since promising preliminary results have already been obtained, we expect that the methods developed will be valuable to the research and engineering communities in solving such important problems. Our long-term goal is to develop a comprehensive framework and set of tools for researchers/practitioners in the field. 非線性估計是復雜工程系統中經常遇到的問題。 它在電力系統狀態估計，智能城市的數據分析到基因網絡識別等都有着重要的應用。此類信息對於系統有效控制及可靠運行，數據建模及故障檢測至為重要。 在智能電網中，系統狀態估計都涉及大量遙遠地區的測量數據和變量及其處理。這使分佈式估計方法猶為關鍵。要確保其在 非平穩性信號, 測量錯誤及 各種不確定性中的 穩定 及 魯棒 表現 乃目前一項嚴峻挑戰。 其中, 交替方向法 是一個很有前途的框架。 因為它能將整個問題分解為局部的 子問題，並通過相互之間有限的信息交換來解決整個問題, 從而減少大量的 通信和計算要求, 具有極大的可擴展性。 不過, 這傳統方法對 目標函數參數的選擇相當敏感，並且通常不支援 變量的非線性等式 或不等式的物理限制。因此。其收斂速度及對物理約束的適用性亦受影響。 此外，在實時應用中，如何快速解决在不停串流測量數據下 的子問題, 亦是有待解决的關鍵問題。 本項目旨在開發一個創新及具創等式和不等式的大規模分佈式估計框架 。 我們將 1）通過 增廣拉格朗日懲罰函數法 將物理或相關式 納入我們先前開發的框架， 2）開發 快速解决在串流數據下的子問題 的新方法，以及 3）研究其在分佈式電力系統狀態估計，最佳功率流 以及其他相關問題（例如各種物理約束下的故障/異常檢測）中的應用。 由於我們已經獲得了令人鼓舞的初步結果，我們希望所開發的方法有助 業界/研究員對解決此問題提供一個有效的方案。更長期的目標是為業界/研究員提供一個全面的框架和工具庫。

17211320.label: Realisation of objectives
17211320.value: Realization of research objectives as per each project objectives performed are summarized below: 1. Develop a novel methodology for robust distributed nonlinear estimation with equality and inequality constraints via the augmented Lagrangian method -------------------------------------------------------------------------- We have completed the proposed framework for distributed nonlinear estimation with equality and inequality. We have utilized this approach to decompose the identification of large-scale time-varying gene regulatory network into small subproblems so that they can be run in parallel with much less storage requirement as in the original problem. We are polishing the draft and will submit this work soon. We have also developed a distributed framework for optimal power flow (OPF) using the augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) framework, which demonstrates its usefulness in incorporating equality and inequality constraints. We also proposed to select the regularization parameter, a key problem in the ADMM framework, using LANCELOT. We further propose to simplify the unconstrained subproblems under the ALM framework to a quadratic programming problem, which can be effectively solved using Cholesky factorization algorithm. Experimental shows that the proposed method can solve reliably the nonconvex OPF problem and achieve superior speedup over classical ADMM-based methods and other alternatives using L-BFGS-based method and sequential quadratic programming (SQP). The work was submitted to IEEE Access [R5]. 2. Develop a framework for solving the local subproblems involved for streaming data. In particular, we shall develop two approaches, one based on Kalman filtering and the other based on stochastic optimization. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ We have developed a robust distributed state estimation (DSE) algorithm for power systems using our previous proposed adaptive fading Unscented transform Kalman filter (AFUKF). Simulations show that it can better adapt to uncertainty in measurement and state noises of the generators and is robust to non-Gaussian measurements having impulsive behavior. Preliminary version of the work appeared in IEEE ISCAS 2023 [R4]. The above robust AFUKF has also been applied to Vector Tracking for Mitigating GNSS under non-line-of-sight reception [R1]. Based on [R4], we have extended the our AFUKF-based DSE algorithm to the estimation of unknown system inputs for say fault detection. We have also conducted a performance of the mismatched KF/EKF/UKF and established their condition for stability, which is shown to be rather mild. It is also shown theoretically that adaptive fading can improve the overall performance by better approximating the correct Kalman gain matrix. The findings were submitted to IEEE Trans. on Power Systems [R6]. We shall further extend the robust KF in [R1] to other robust localization and the more general setting of distributed localization and synchronization in sensor networks using the distributed framework developed. Preliminary version of this work appears in IEEE VTC 2024-Spring [R7] and the journal version is currently under polishing. 3. Investigate its application to power system state estimation, distributed optimal power flow, and other related problems -------------------------------------------------------------------------- As mentioned earlier, we have completed the investigation of the proposed ALM in distributed optimal power flow (OPF) and the full paper has been submitted to IEEE Access. It will be very valuable to OPF involving microgrid and battery storage. This will be left for future work. We have also incorporated the robust framework to dynamic factor analysis [R2] and frequency estimation [R3]. In particular, we have extended the subspace-based approaches to distributed spatial-temporal estimation and fault detection for sensor networks. The full manuscript is under preparation. The approach is applicable to wide range of spatial-temporal estimation problems in environmental modeling. 17211320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211320.value: There are several major findings in this research 1. The ALM method allows equality and inequality constraints to be reformulated as unconstrained problem which greatly simplify distributed solution of large scale optimization problem. Moreover, the resultant unconstrained problem can be solved using a wide variety of methods. In our OPF problem, the subproblems are solved by exploring the inherent structure and solved using Cholesky factorization method. It significantly outperforms L-BFGS method and SQP because the subproblems are now much small and there is not need to exactly solve the subproblem during the iterations. The LANCELOT is also shown to be effective in selecting the important regularization problem leading to better accuracy and convergence speed. The results are reported in [R5] 2. In distributed dynamic state estimation, we focus on using Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) for solution under bad data and unknown inputs. One important problem is the selection of the state and measurement covariance which are generally unknown. A novel adaptive fading (AF) algorithm is used to update the nominal covariance matrices for better performance. Substantially improved performance and reliability are achieved. Moreover, the stability of the proposed AFUKF is established under mild conditions and the improved performance of AF in mismatched situations can be theoretically explained. The results are reported in [R4] and [R6]. 3. The AF-UKF has been applied to several localization problems including GNSS-IMU tracking in vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) using UWB-IMU and object tracking using angle of arrivals (AOA). Good performance has been achieved. A distributed version of the AOA tracking has also been developed. Parts of these results are reported in [R1], [R7]. 4. We have also extended our subspace-based algorithms

17211320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17211320.value: The proposal research can be developed in the following directions: 1. With increased penetration of renewables and power electronic devices, optimal power flow has to be performed more often and subject to large uncertainties. Battery storage, fuel cells, microgrids and demand response are important techniques that can mitigate such fluctuation. As our distributed framework is both scalable and reliable, they can potentially be used to solve the large scale optimization arising from incorporation of these mechanism. Preliminary results show very encouraging results and more findings will be reported in the future. 2. During the course of the research, we found that the OPF framework can also be used to handle nonlinear load model such as ZIP load. This can be used to lower the operating voltage for energy saving. We are currently working on recursive load estimation algorithm which will work together with our distributed OPF to address such problem. 3. As mentioned, we are still polishing the distributed localization work and distributed spatial-temporal estimation arising from [R7] and [R2]. The full manuscript will be available later this year. Due to time limitation, the problem of distributed synchronization/frequency estimation is not covered addressed in this work and will be a good future direction.

17211320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211320.value: Large scale constrained optimization problems are frequently encountered in science and engineering. This project aims to develop a convenient framework for performing such large-scale optimization in a distributed or collaborative manner to improve scalability, reliability and extensive communications in the centralized approach. Moreover, we aim to develop online algorithm for solving the resultant subproblems for handling streaming data frequently occurred in real-time systems. A novel methodology based on augmented Lagrangian method is developed in this project together with novel adaptive estimation methods based on unscented Kalman filters. They are shown to achieve better performance under noise covariance matrices uncertainties and are stable under mild condition. We have applied the developed methodology to address several important problems encountered in smart cities such as distributed optimal power flow and decentralized state estimation, which are important operations in more power systems with high penetration of renewables. Other applications include localization of unmanned vehicles, IoT, etc based on GPS and ultrawideband technologies. The research will facilitate the further development of distributed and online estimation and optimization algorithms as well as several emerging applications such as UWB localization, autonomous vehicle positioning, and energy management in future power systems.

17211720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211720.value: With the Information Age entering the wireless broadband stage, the amount of data bombarding us is increasing at an enormous rate. Consequently, today's computer and communication equipment have to operate at very high speed so as to cope with this data deluge, and often under low-voltage circumstances. In order to meet all these stringent requirements, worldwide research interest in using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) for semiconductor applications has greatly increased over the past few years. This interest has been stimulated by many unique and outstanding electrical and physical properties of MoS2 when compared with the most commonly used semiconductors (silicon and gallium arsenide). These features make MoS2 an ideal material for making high-speed and low-voltage electronic devices in many high-impact military and industrial applications (compact radar, wireless network, low-power system). But before all these benefits could be realized, it is of utmost importance to develop appropriate materials for the devices to facilitate the flow of electrons inside them. Therefore, the main goal of this project is to develop new materials which have high potential in ushering the MoS2 devices into future-generation electronic components and systems. 隨著資訊時代進入無線寬頻階段,轟炸我們的數據量正在以巨大的速度增長。因此,當今的計算機和通信設備必須以非常高速運行,以應付這種數據泛濫,而且往往在低壓情況下。為了滿足所有這些嚴格的要求,全球對在半導體應用中使用二硫化鈾(MOS2)的研究興趣在過去幾年中大大增加。與最常用的半導體(矽和亞硫酸二鈣)相比,MOS2的許多獨特和出色的電氣和物理特性激發了這種興趣。這些功能使MOS2成為許多高衝擊軍事和工業應用(緊湊型雷達、無線網路、低功耗系統)中製造高速低壓電子設備的理想材料。但是,在實現所有這些好處之前,為器件開發適當的材料以方便設備內部的電子流動至關重要。因此,這專案的主要目標是開發具有很大潛力的新材料,將MOS2器件引入下一代電子元件和系統。

17211720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211720.value: 1. CF4/O2-plasma is used to treat the interfaces of gate stacks (MoS2/Al2O3/ ZrO2/p+-Si). Experimental results show that excellent electrical properties have been achieved for the MoS2 transistors with CF4/O2-plasma treated stacked gate dielectric, especially for the F-treated ZrO2 device: high mobility of 53.7 cm2/Vs, and high on/off ratio of 2.7 × 107. The involved main mechanisms lie in the facts that: (i) the MoS2/dielectric interface is improved through the F- passivation on the oxygen vacancies in the dielectric, decreasing the dangling bonds and surface roughness of the dielectric; (ii) the dielectric constant (k) of the gate stack dielectric is increased because of suppressed growth of low-k Zr-silicate interlayer and improved dielectric quality by forming Zr single bond F and Al single bond F bonds; (iii) CF4/O2-plasma treatment on the ZrO2 surface can result in F incorporation in both ZrO2 and Al2O3, giving the best passivation on oxygen vacancies and oxide traps near/at the MoS2/dielectric interface. 2. The ferroelectricity of HfZrO (Hf0.5Zr0.5O2, HZO) is enhanced by fluorine (F)-plasma treatment, which is used to fabricate MoS2 negative-capacitance fieldeffect transistor. Measurements show that the subthreshold swing of the transistor is significantly reduced to 17.8 mV dec−1, as compared to its counterpart without the F-plasma treatment (37.4 mV dec−1). The involved mechanism is that during the F-plasma treatment, F atoms can be incorporated into the HZO bulk to passive its oxygen vacancies and interface traps, thus forming robust Zr–F and Hf–F bonds. 3. The influence of transferred S/D electrodes on the performance of MoS2 FET is investigated. The experimental results demonstrate that the transferred S/D electrodes exhibit superior electrical performance compared to their PVD counterparts for 3 kinds of metals (Ag, Au, and Pt). Specifically, by utilizing Ag S/D electrodes via the wet transfer method (instead of the conventional thermal evaporation), the device has the highest carrier mobility and lowest S/D contact resistance. 4. A hybrid wet transfer method for the fabrication of MoS2 FET array is demonstrated by using PMMA support and HF assistance, which significantly reduces the fabrication complexity and cost. The MoS2 FET array is fabricated with amorphous HfO2 as gate dielectric, undoped CVD monolayer MoS2 as conduction channel, and Ag as source/drain electrodes. The FET exhibits a low VT of 0.72 V, a high mobility of 69.9 cm2V-1s-1, and a low contact resistance of 1.49 kΩ·μm, together with good electrical uniformity.

17211720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211720.value: With the Information Age entering the wireless broadband stage, the amount of data bombarding us is increasing at an enormous rate. Consequently, today's computer and communication equipment have to operate at very high speed so as to cope with this data deluge, and often under low-voltage circumstances. In order to meet all these stringent requirements, worldwide research interest in using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) for semiconductor applications has greatly increased over the past few years. This interest has been stimulated by many unique and outstanding electrical and physical properties of MoS2 when compared with the most commonly used semiconductors (silicon and gallium arsenide). These features make MoS2 an ideal material for making high-speed and low-voltage electronic devices in many highimpact military and industrial applications (compact radar, wireless network, low-power system). But before all these benefits could be realized, it is of utmost importance to develop appropriate materials for the devices to facilitate the flow of electrons inside them. Therefore, the main goal of this project is to develop new materials which have high potential in ushering the MoS2 devices into future-generation electronic components and systems.

17212120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212120.value: We propose to develop efficient solutions to unique computer vision problems that find important applications in orthodontics, a branch of dentistry concerned with rectifying tooth alignment to restore proper masticatory function or improve smile and facial appearance. Orthodontic treatment is a complex and lengthy process, with its success depending highly on the patient's commitment and cooperation, and continual adjustments based on effective monitoring of treatment progress. While many digital technologies have been developed for improving diagnosis and treatment planning, we study in this project two key technologies for orthodontic treatment: 1) developing an augmented reality (AR) system to facilitate the communication between doctors and patients, in which the patient may view and better appreciate the potential benefit of the treatment beforehand; 2) developing an image-based high-precision 3D measurement system that uses a smartphone camera to monitor treatment progress. This light-weight system can be used by either the doctor or the patient to conveniently and effectively monitor tooth movement during treatment. Our research will focus on a challenging computer vision issue underpinning these two technologies, i.e., how to use cameras on smartphones to perform fast and accurate 3D tracking and reconstruction of the patient's teeth in the presence of large head movements and varying facial expressions. For the AR system, we will develop methods for tracking the patient's teeth and determine their 3D positions in a fast and stable manner so that the properly aligned and simulated 3D virtual teeth can be rendered to replace the current teeth on smartphones at the rate of 30 frames per second. For treatment monitoring, we will develop methods for estimating the poses of the teeth at sub-millimeter precision from the multiple input images, and then measure the distances between the actual and the planned tooth to report the status of tooth movement progress. Furthermore, we will extend these works to handle significant changes in face appearance as the result of orthodontic or orthognathic treatment. We will present research methodology and research tasks, show preliminary studies to demonstrate the feasibility and potential superiority of our proposed methods, and discuss validation plans with lab tests and user studies. We will also discuss the extension of the proposed methods for dealing with changes to facial tissues as the result of orthodontic treatment as well as orthognathic surgery. The outcome of this project will be of significant contributions to improving the accessibility and quality of orthodontic treatment. 17212120.label: Realisation of objectives
17212120.value: The projects achieve the objectives. To test our algorithm under the protocol, we captured an evaluation dataset under our IRB approval, including 8 subjects from the patients of the Faculty of Dentistry requiring orthodontic treatment at the Prince Philip Dental Hospital. As multidisciplinary research, the computer science team collaborates closely with the Faculty of Dentistry and has established long-term collaboration with teams in mainland China and overseas. Objective 1: We have developed a prototype system for tracking teeth efficiently and robustly. The system takes intra-oral scanned models and selfie monocular video clips captured by mobile phones as input. We trained a UNet to detect the inner mouth mask and used an edge detector to extract the edge maps of the teeth. By matching the contours between the projected contour of the 3D tooth model and the edge map, we solve an optimization problem to estimate the 6DoF pose parameters for both upper and lower teeth. To ensure stability, we use optical flow to reduce the jittery effect caused by per-frame optimization. The algorithm for this objective has been realized. Significant effort was invested in method evaluation, using both real captured videos of our subjects and synthetic data to quantitatively assess accuracy. The integrated systems represent a major breakthrough in video applications, outperforming all related methods. Objective 2: We integrated a photo-realistic renderer into the video. This renderer renders the 3D tooth model with the estimated poses in each frame and blends the results seamlessly with the input video. Compared to recent generative AI techniques, our method is faster and less computationally intensive, and ensuring the consistency of the 3D model. We also conducted a formal user study with our subjects, who reported that the visualization helps them understand the effects of the orthodontic treatment and improves patient-doctor communication. Objective 3: We proposed a novel and practical mobile device-based framework for precisely measuring tooth movement during treatment, simplifying and enhancing the traditional tooth monitoring process. We formulate the tooth movement monitoring task as a multi-view multi-object pose estimation problem using different views that capture multiple texture-less and severely occluded objects (i.e., teeth). Specifically, we use a pre-scanned 3D tooth model and a sparse set of multi-view tooth images as inputs for our proposed framework. By extracting tooth contours and localizing the initial camera pose of each view from the initial configuration, we propose a joint pose estimation scheme to precisely estimate the 3D pose of each individual tooth and infer their relative offsets during treatment. Our approach demonstrates high accuracy and efficiency, meeting the practical requirements of orthodontic treatment monitoring.

17212120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17212120.value: Our major findings and research outcomes include the methodology, evaluation methods, and the feasibility of using consumer-level cameras in digital orthodontics. Methodology: Given that teeth are textureless, reflective, and highly self-occluded objects, reconstructing or tracking them in general computer vision tasks is challenging. Our research validates two major findings: 1) optimizing a contour-matching-based objective function can solve individual tooth pose estimation; 2) deep learning-based rough pose estimators can provide good initialization, which is not accurate but can be further refined by the optimization. Evaluation Methods: Quantitatively evaluating orthodontic research outputs is challenging. We proposed multiple methods to synthesize dental data virtually or physically: 1) using photo-realistic rendering techniques, we generate images and videos with ground-truth 3D models to simulate real scenarios and validate algorithms quantitatively using various accuracy metrics; 2) using a typodont with irregularly arranged teeth, we simulate orthodontic treatment by moving the teeth to planned treatment poses and scanning the before and after 3D models to obtain ground-truth data. These methods address the difficulties and ethical concerns of capturing large amounts of data from patients. Validity of Applications in Digital Orthodontics: We thoroughly validated the feasibility of using consumer-level cameras to improve patient-doctor communication by visualizing treatment effects and monitoring orthodontic tooth motion using multi-view images.
