17303220.label: Realisation of objectives
17303220.value: This project has five objectives. We have successfully completed all of them. We have achieved 100% of Objective 1. We have developed a novel DNA-encoded library method capable of synthesizing large-scale linear precursor libraries with high chemical diversity. Two macrocycle precursor libraries have been prepared with a total of >500 million compounds. Notably, the method features new DNA-compatible chemistry that can construct peptides conjugated with DNA codes through thioester linkage, thereby enabling cyclative cleavage upon macrocyclization. More specifically, Nvoc-protected amino acid building blocks were conjugated to the thioate-modified DNA strands with their respective sequence codes. After conjugation, the Nvoc-protecting group can be removed under brief non-damaging UV irradiation (365 nm, 1 min.) without cleaving the thioester linkage. The library was synthesized through three to four rounds of split-and-pool procedure. Finally, the last Nov-protecting group was maintained in the library to prevent the linear compounds from auto-cyclization in the absence of the target protein. The libraries have been subjected to thorough characterization and QC, including mass spectrometry confirm the addition of the building blocks in each step and DNA sequencing to validate the encoding fidelity. Overall, the libraries were prepared at a scale enough for ~500-1,000 selections, which is sufficient not only for the proposed targets, but also many others beyond this project. We have completed 100% of Objective 2. Frist, we prepared two model libraries and validated the selection methods by using two protein targets, Insulin-Degradation Enzyme (IDE) and Src kinase. Each model library contains a linearized macrocyclic ligand for the respective protein target. It should be noted that, since these known macrocycles were not developed with the same cyclative cleavage chemistry as in this project, their cyclized structures are slightly different from the reported ones. Nevertheless, the model selections have clearly shown the specific enrichment of the positive controls. Moreover, we have also examined different types of cyclative cleavage reactions besides thioester cleavage mediated by primary amines. For example, we tested library cyclization by using native chemical ligation (NCL); however, although NCL indeed facilitated the protein-templated cyclization, it also increased target-independent, non-specific cyclization in the background. Thus, we have decided to use the simple thioester-primary amine cyclization in actual selections. We have completed 100% of Objective 3. We have applied the ~500-million DNA-encoded linear precursor library against 13 targets of high biological and therapeutic importance, which includes enzymes, protein-protein interactions (PPIs), and membrane proteins that can be interrogated both in a purified form and directly on live cells. The list of the protein targets is as follows: IDE (Insulin degrading enzyme), Src kinase (Proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src), PD-1 (Programmed cell death protein 1), PD-L1 (Programmed cell death ligand 1), EP300 (Histone acetyltransferase), AGP (α-globulin glycoprotein), TRKA (Tropomyosin receptor kinase A), Mcl-1 (Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein), IDO (Indoleamine-pyrrole 2,3-dioxygenase), NKp46 (triggering receptor involved in the natural cytotoxicity of human NK cells), BIR2 domain of XIAP, Sirt family proteins, and TIGIT (T cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and ITIM domain). A large amount of sequencing data was obtained from these selection campaigns. In order to accurately identify the true hit compounds, we have also developed a machine-learning (ML)-based approach to process large-scale DEL selection datasets by using a Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation loss function, a probabilistic framework that can account for and quantify uncertainties of noisy data. The Extended-Connectivity Fingerprint (ECFP)-based regression model using the MAP loss function was able to identify the true binders and reliable structure-activity relationship (SAR) from the noisy DEL selection datasets. Our data analysis has identified and rank-ordered 3-10 hit compounds for each target. These compounds were synthesized in both the linear and cyclized form. Next, the compounds were tested for the binding affinity to the target protein via biophysical methods such as SPR and MST. In particular, we compared the binding affinities of the linear precursor and the macrocyclic compounds. In most cases, the macrocyclic hit compounds showed higher affinity than the linear precursors. Furthermore, to validate that the macrocyclization is indeed promoted by the protein template, kinetic target-guided synthesis (KTGS) experiments were performed in the presence of the target protein, with an unrelated non-target protein, and in buffer, respectively. We have observed significantly higher level of macrocyclization with the target protein but not in other cases, proving the cyclization is target-specific. For example, for Src kinase, the linear precursor’s binding affinities are in the range of 30~50 μM as determined by SPR; in contrast, their corresponding macrocycles have shown significantly stronger affinity in the single-digit μM to nanomolar range. Moreover, in KTGS studies, the presence of Scr kinase template increased the macrocyclization rate for >100 fold than with buffer only or with a non-target protein (carbonic anhydrase 2 or glutathione S-transferase). Similar results were obtained for other protein targets. We have completed 100% of Objective 4. We have applied the DNA-encoded linear precursor library against two PPI targets: SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (S-protein) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1). Novel ligands with binding affinity in the low μM range have been identified. We also performed the library selections against several membrane protein targets directly on live cells: epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), thrombopoietin receptor (TPOR), and insulin receptor (INSR), all are important drug targets in human diseases. INSR is the primary target for anti-diabetes drugs; however, small molecule INSR agonists are extremely rare. Nearly all clinical INSR agonist drugs are peptides that can only be administered by injection, resulting in prolonged morbidity and poor compliance in patients. Our selections have identified a series of novel allosteric INSR agonists with novel chemical structures and they exhibited strong synergistic effects with insulin in activating INSR and the glucose uptake pathway. Importantly, the agonists are not competitive with insulin and have no lateral activation of IGF-1R, which is a major concern in insulin replacement therapy as IGF-1R activation leads to tumorigenesis. The absence of the off-target effect renders these allosteric agonists highly promising candidates for anti-diabetes drug development. The selections with EGFR and TPOR also identified several agonists with modest activities. For Objective #5, we have summarized the research findings in this report. The hit compounds discovered in this project have potential to be further developed as novel drug candidates in the more downstream development pipeline, and related patent applications have already been filed. 17303220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303220.value: Macrocycles have recently attracted significant interest in biomedical research and drug discovery, largely owing to their unique structural features that allow them to efficiently interrogate challenging biological targets such as PPIs. The large cyclic structures of macrocycles allow key functional groups to reach extended binding sites on protein surfaces without significant entropic loss, leading to high binding affinity and specificity; also, the conformationally restricted structures of macrocycles have favorable pharmacokinetic properties. However, the development of macrocycle drugs still remains a challenging task, and there is a great need to develop effective strategies to not only access diverse macrocyclic structures, but also efficiently screen them against biological targets to identify and develop novel macrocyclic compounds with high therapeutic value. In this project, we have developed a novel method capable of performing high-throughput screening of macrocycle ligands against protein targets without the need to prepare a macrocycle library, which is the primary aim in the original proposal. This method employs a target-guided synthesis approach where the target protein directs the formation of macrocycle ligands from large-scale DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) of linear precursors. Moreover, a cyclative cleavage strategy coupled with DNA encoding was used to decode the specific cyclized binders after the selection. This method circumvented the challenge of global macrocyclization in large chemical libraries; instead, the target protein promotes the cyclization of its binders. Since the linear precursors can adopt more diverse conformations, this method may enable more efficient sampling of conformations of the macrocycle ligands. In addition, here, the DNA tag encodes not only the chemical structures but also the cyclization events, and only the cyclized molecules can be enriched after the library selection. Finally, this method is compatible with non-immobilized proteins and the selection can be performed with membrane proteins directly on live cells. The selection campaigns have discovered many novel macrocyclic ligands against challenging protein targets. For example, the Src kinase selection identified a nanomolar macrocyclic binder that turned out to be extremely difficult to synthesize due to its constrained cyclic structure; thus, it could not be discovered with traditional chemical libraries and would become a false negative. However, the template effect from Src kinase promotes the cyclization in the linear precursor library. These results have demonstrated the power of the developed method in discovering novel macrocyclic ligands that are intractable to traditional approaches. The importance of macrocycles in drug discovery has been demonstrated by the many approved macrocycle drugs. The macrocyclic hit compounds identified in this project may be subject to medicinal chemistry optimization for further drug development. The research findings of this project contributed to a number of publications including two published articles on Nature Chemistry, one J. Am. Chem. Soc. article just accepted, and two preprints (formal manuscripts will be submitted soon) as well as two patent applications. We expect more impactful research outputs will continue to arise following the work of this project.

17303220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303220.value: 1) The DNA-encoded linear precursor libraries were prepared at a scale enough for ~500-1,000 selections. These libraries have been integrated into our general DEL collection and will be used in other drug discovery programs beyond the ones described in this project. Moreover, future research efforts will also be dedicated to intracellular selections and selections against large protein complexes. 2) The libraries synthesized in this project all have peptide structures, and the thioester-amine reaction is the only cyclization chemistry used. In future, other types of cyclization chemistry, such as Click reaction, disulfide formation, thio-ene/yne reactions, may be exploited to build libraries with more diverse structures. However, these reactions only cyclize the structure but are unable to release the DNA tag for hit identification; therefore, the selection strategy needs to be modified to distinguish the linear and cyclic binders. 3) We also intend to perform medicinal chemistry optimizations of the identified macrocycles to refine their binding affinities and activities. The more downstream drug development would require collaborations and funding support from external agencies and/or companies. We plan to apply ITF seed funding to conduct drug development on some of the most promising agonists. We also envision this method to be extended to more types of membrane proteins, protein complexes, and perhaps even the whole cancer cells as the target.

17303220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303220.value: Macrocycles, broadly defined as cyclic molecules of 12 atoms or more, have attracted significant interest in drug discovery, largely owing to their unique structural features that allow them to efficiently interrogate challenging drug targets in many human diseases. However, despite the significance, the complex structure of macrocycles significantly hampers the synthesis, testing, and development of macrocycle-based drugs. In this project, a novel high throughput screening method has been developed to enable the simultaneous selection of hundreds of million of compounds to rapidly identify macrocyclic ligands. Notably, the target protein acts as a template to pick its “favorite” macrocycles from a large pool of linear precursors. The selections in this project have discovered potent macrocycle ligands with potential therapeutic value against several high-value drug targets, such Src kinase and Bcl-2.

rows: Prove the wall crossing formula of DT invariants under mutation of quivers with analytic potentials.
Study the rigidity of the cluster categories of contractible rational curves on Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

17303420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303420.value: Cluster algebra was invented by Fomin and Zelevinksy in early 2000 as a combinatorial tool to understand Lusztig’s canonical basis on quantum group. Donaldson-Thomas theory is a theory on enumeration of semistable coherent sheaves on projective Calabi-Yau 3-folds. The relation between these apparently disjoint subjects were first discovered by Kontsevich and Soibelman. Their observation is that the Donaldson-Thomas invariants satisfy the wall crossing formula when the stability condition changes, while the formula looks very similar to the mutation rule of cluster variables. The revolutionary work of Kontsevich and Soibelman builds a deep link between algebraic geometry and representation theory. The aim of the project is to study the calculus of quiver with potential and its application to DT theory and cluster algebra. Quiver with potential is a noncommutative geometric object that appears naturally in both cluster algebra and in DT theory. In DT theory, there is a quiver with potential associate to deformation of a coherent sheaf. They also appear naturally in categori- fication of cluster algebra. Instead of formal potentials, our focus is on analytic potentials, i.e. those potentials whose coefficients are bounded by geometric series. Compared with their formal counterparts, the calculus and the DT theory of analytic potentials are technically more involved due to the difficulties on convergence issue. However, numerous evidence show that various open problems in cluster algebra and DT theory might be solved by analyzing the convergence properties of analytic potentials. On the other hand, if the potential is assumed to be analytic we will get an additional geometric structure on the moduli space of representations which is significant in the study of cluster algebra. Fomin和Zelevinsky在20世紀初期發明了叢代數作為一種研究Lusztig典範基的組合方法。Donaldson-Thomas理論則是一種研究投射Calabi-Yau三維流形上半穩定凝聚層的計數幾何理論。Kontsevich和Soibelman觀察到DT不變量滿足的穿牆公式類似於FM理論中叢變量所滿足的置換關係，並進一步建立了代數幾何和表示倫間的深刻聯繫。 我們的目標是研究帶勢箭圖的微積分以及在DT理論和叢代數上的應用。作為一個非交換幾何的對象，帶勢箭圖自然地出現在叢代數理論和DT理論。在後者當中，一個凝聚層的形變對應一個帶勢箭圖。在前者中，帶勢箭圖用來範疇化叢代數。我們聚焦於解析勢函數。 相比於一般的勢函數，解析勢的微積分更加困難。這主要來自於證明係數收斂性的困難。但有很多跡象顯示叢代數理論和DT理論中的一些問題可能跟收斂性有關。另外如果我們考慮解析勢，那麼帶勢箭圖的表示模空間會具備一些額外的幾何結構，而這一結構都叢代數的研究有重要作用。

17303420.label: Realisation of objectives
17303420.value: 1 Goal of research This project is partially a continuation of the joint project with Gui-song Zhou on noncommutative Mather- Yau theorem. Let Q be a finite quiver and W be a formal potential on Q with finite dimensional Jacobi algebra Λb(Q,W). In [4], we prove that the formal equivalence class of (Λb(Q,W),W) determines the formal right equivalence class of W . As an intermediate result, we prove that a formal potential with finite dimensional Jacobi algebra is formally right equivalent to an algebraic potential. A natural question is whether this equivalence can be chosen to be analytic? The notion of analytic potential was first introduced by Toda in [7] to establish a local categorical model for DT theory. The analyticity condition is posed in order to define the weighted euler number of the moduli stack of objects. Mutation of algebraic potentials are in general not algebraic [1]. If one can prove that mutation of algebraic potentials have analytic representatives then the weighted euler number of the moduli spaces are well defined after mutation. This will enable us to generalize the result of Nagao [6] from topological euler number to weighted euler number. Another place where analytic condition becomes important is in the construction of the noncommutative space which is locally modeled by quiver with potential. 2 Realisation of objectives We have made some progress on the differential calculus of quiver with potentials and obtain several interesting applications for the Jacobi-finite cases. However, for potentials with infinite dimensional Jacobi algebras we have encounter a significant amount of difficulties. For the cluster category of contractible rational curves on Calabi-Yau threefolds, we are able to generalize our results in [2] to the case when the exceptional locus has more than one irreducible components. 2.1 Foundation of differential calculus of quivers with potentials (Objective 1) We have established several foundational results on noncommutative differential calculus. As an application, we prove a noncommutative version of Saito’s theorem which links the quasi-homogeneity of potential and the vanishing of the equivalence class of the potential in Hochschild homology of Jacobi algebra. For analytic theory, we prove an inverse function theorem for quiver with analytic potential and a noncommutative version of a Moser’s trick. Then we use them to prove (1) an analytic version noncommutative Mather-Yau theorem, (2) mutation of analytic potential is analytic. We are not able to prove any significant results for potentials with infinite dimensional Jacobi algebras. For example, if W is an algebraic potential then the mutation of W is formally right equivalent to an analytic one. When the Jacobi algebra of W is finite then one can choose the right equivalence to be analytic. However, we could not prove such a result for general W. This is the main obstacle to generalize Nagao’s theorem. In commutative algebraic geometry, we have a twisted de Rham complex associate to a holomorphic function whose hypercohomology computes cohomology of perverse sheaf of vanishing cycles. When the function has isolated singularity the twisted de Rham complex has sheaf cohomology concentrating in one degree. One possible approach is to define a noncommutative analogue of twisted de Rham complex associate to quiver with an analytic potential. We are currently working along this direction. 2.2 Cluster categories for contractible rational curves on Calabi-Yau 3-folds (Objective 2) Let f : Y → X be a 3-dimensional flopping contraction. If the exceptional locus of f is irreducible then we can construct a potential W on a d-loop quiver for d = 0, 1, 2, which models the deformation theory of the structure sheaf of the reduce fiber of f. In [2], we prove that the (dg) cluster category associate to the d-loop quiver and potential W determines the isomorphism type of X. Later we generalize the result to f whose exceptional locus has multiple components. In this case the quiver has multiple nodes. Differential resolutions of X are related by the silting theory of the cluster category. Our theorem together with a recent result of Jasso, Muro and Keller [5] lead to a complete proof of the Donovan-Wemyss conjecture.

17303920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303920.value: Cyclic peptides represent a class of structural motifs with diverse potential applications in both fundamental research and drug discovery. The chemical space of cyclic peptides lies between small molecules and large biologics (e.g., antibodies), rendering them with new therapeutic properties of potency, target selectivity, metabolic stability, binding interaction size, oral bioavailability, and toxicity. Thus, the exploration of methods and strategies for the chemical preparation of cyclic peptides with diverse structures provides chemists with new opportunities to develop new chemistry for peptide cyclization. In this proposal, we aim to develop chemoselective reactions for peptide cyclization on native (unprotected) peptides. Towards this goal, we recently discovered that ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) can react with the thiol of cysteine and the amine of lysine or the N-terminal amine to form the isoindole moiety-linked side chain-to-side chain or head-to-side chain cyclic peptides. The features of this method include its unique chemoselectivity, operational simplicity, no catalyst requirement, broad substrate scope, fast reaction kinetics, post-cyclization modification, and mutual compatibility with biomolecules under aqueous buffer conditions. In this project, we aim to systemically study the parameters for optimizing the cyclization conditions, establish its structure-activity relationship, and explore its potential applications for constructing cyclic peptides, stapled peptides, and super-diverse phage-displayed cyclic peptide libraries. 環肽是一類在基礎研究和藥物發現方面具有潛在應用價值的結構基序。環肽的化學空間介於小分子藥物和大分子生物製劑（例如抗體）之間，這就賦予了環肽在效力、靶標選擇性、代謝穩定性、口服生物利用度和毒性等方面上有了新的療效特性。因此，探索新的合成方法和策略來製備具有不同結構的環肽為化學家提供了新的機會來開發合成環肽的新化學。在這項目中，我們旨在開發針對天然（未保護的）肽段的具有化學選擇性的環化方法。為了實現這一目標，我們最近發現鄰苯二甲醛（OPA）可以與多肽上半胱氨酸的硫醇和賴氨酸的胺或N端胺形成異吲哚連接的側鏈至側鍊或頭對側鏈環狀肽。這種方法的特點包括高度化學選擇性、操作簡便、無需催化劑、底物範圍廣、快速的反應動力學、環化後可修飾等等。在這個項目中，我們旨在系統地研究優化環化條件的參數、確定其結構活性關係、並探討其在構建環肽文庫中的潛在應用。

17303920.label: Realisation of objectives
17303920.value: Cyclic peptides are a unique group of compounds that offer an intriguing chemical structure, which can be utilized against difficult targets such as protein-protein and protein-nucleic acid interactions, both involving extensive binding areas. They reside in the chemical space between small molecules (MW < 500) and larger biologics like antibodies. Cyclic peptides potentially possess numerous therapeutic characteristics, including potency, specific target selection, metabolic stability, oral bioavailability, and toxicity. Their production costs are estimated to fall between those of small molecules and large biologics. These peptides are more resistant to enzymatic breakdown and exhibit better cellular absorption than linear peptides. Furthermore, their rigid structure decreases entropy loss upon binding to a target. Therefore, they are actively being explored in pharmaceutical industries for drug discovery. However, developing chemoselective peptide cyclization is difficult due to the diverse nucleophilic side chain functionalities in unprotected peptides, like thiol, hydroxyl, indole, guanidine, etc., which can interfere with coupling reactions. Therefore, these reactions need to tolerate various functional side chains present in the peptides, and the reaction conditions should be mild and compatible with the complexity of biomolecules. This proposed project aims to develop new chemoselective peptide cyclization to create various cyclic peptides and explore their application. We have previous developed a chemoselective peptide cyclization on unprotected peptides, where ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) interacts with the thiol of cysteine and the amine of lysine or N-terminal amine. This forms an isoindole moiety-linked side chain-to-side chain or head-to-side chain cyclic peptides. The reaction is efficient in creating cyclic peptides, completing in 10-15 minutes at sub-mM concentration. This OPA-peptide cyclization method's advantages include using unprotected peptide side chains as cyclization precursors, which are easier to manage than side chain protected peptides; it's operationally simple with common reagents and doesn't require any catalyst; and the resultant isoindole moiety can be further modified post-cyclization, such as introducing fluorescence or other tags. In this proposed project, our goal is to further refine this OPA-thiol-amine peptide cyclization method, optimize the cyclization conditions, establish its structure-activity relationship, and explore its potential uses in constructing stapled peptides and studying the behavior of these stapled α-helical peptides. We also aim to investigate its application in creating cyclic peptides in highly diverse libraries with phage display. We have carried out and completed the following studies: 1) Structure-activity relationship of OPA-mediated peptide cyclization; 2) Explore OPA-cyclic peptides mimicking disulfide cyclic peptides; 3) OPA-thiol-amine cyclization for synthesizing stapled peptides; 4) Application OPA peptide cyclization for phage display. Firstly, we now have a good understanding of the structure-activity of OPA analogues. For instance, we found TDA had a much lower reactivity for which TDA could be used for peptide cyclization for phage display (objective 4). We also synthesized a symmetrical OPA moiety with an alkyne tail that would only afford homogeneous product. Based on the model study on thiol-amine cyclization, the reactivity of this OPA derivative was perfectly retained. Moreover, the alkyne tail could serve as an additional functionality. We hypothesize that once a peptide was cyclized, the alkyne tail could be subjected to the click reaction. Diverse functionalities of interest, such as fluorophores, could be readily introduced to the resultant cyclic peptide. Secondly, we have successfully applied the OPA-based cyclization for mimicking disulfide cyclic peptides. For example, we explored the use of Fmoc as a transient N-terminal amine protecting group and have successfully carried out one-pot Fmoc deprotection after cyclization. Three oxytoxin analogues bearing the isoindole linkage and free N-terminal were synthesized. Apart from oxytocin, we have also applied the same strategy to its related pituitary neuropeptide, vasopressin. Thirdly, apart from the disulfide bond mimetics, we have also applied the OPA-cyclization strategy to synthesize a wide range of stapled peptides analogues. We first focused on the p53/MDM2 inhibitor. P53 is a tumor suppressor and MDM2 is a negative regulator of p53, blocking their interaction would liberate p53 and restore its tumor suppressing function. Based on the reported bioactive thio-ene stapled peptides, we have designed and synthesized several i, i+7 isoindole stapled peptide analogues. Besides, to demonstrate that our method could well-tolerate the varied unit spacing, we have also synthesized a range of i, i+4 analogues. In addition to the conventional 8-atom linker formed between Cys and Lys, we have further explored the cyclization between Cys and Orn, or homoCys and Lys. We were pleased to find that the reaction was adaptable to these unnatural residues and formed isoindole linkers with varying lengths. In view of the better stability of the Pen analogues, cyclic peptides utilizing Pen and Lys were also synthesized. Our next target was the estrogen receptor (ER). Due to its critical role in regulating reproduction, it has been a point of intervention in breast and endometrial cancers. Based on the reported bioactive 11-mer peptide, we have designed and synthesized two i, i+4 OPA-stapled ERα peptide inhibitors, cyclized between Lys and Cys, as well as Lys and Pen. In addition, we focused on the postsynaptic density 95 protein guanylate kinase domain (PSD95GK). As this protein associates with neuronal diseases, the development of PSD95 inhibitor constitutes a promising therapeutic strategy. Based on our previous study on the PSD95 lactam-stapled peptides, we have modified the peptide sequence to include Lys and Pen, without interfering with the recognition motif. A i, i+4 PSD95 isoindole-stapled peptide inhibitor was achieved. Overall, these results have evidenced that our method could accommodate varying unit spacing between staples, length of linkers and residues composition. Moreover, this reaction is simple, rapid and chemoselective, hence it represents a potent approach for peptide stapling. Finally, from all the OPA analogues tested, we found that the thiophene-2,3-dicarboxaldehyde (TDA) could react specifically with the primary amine (from Lys side chain or peptide N-terminus) and thiol (from Cys side chain) within unprotected peptides to generate a highly stable thieno[2,3-c]pyrrole-bridged cyclic structure, while it did not react with primary amine alone. This reaction is carried out in the aqueous buffer and features tolerance of diverse functionalities, rapid and clean transformation, and operational simplicity. We therefore explored the feasibility of TDA-assisted cyclization strategy on constructing phage-displayed cyclic libraries. A model sequence SKGSCGENLYFQS containing the TEV protease cleavage site was displayed by phage pIII and subjected to the TDA cyclization. Thanks to the high selectivity for the S-N cyclization over the N-modification and the low abundance of Cys residue, we found that the phage’s infectivity has minimal change even after treatment with up to 50 μM of TDA. Of note, the superb biocompatibility (low toxicity) of TDA further highlights the site-specificity of TDA cyclization. After successful cleavage of the displayed peptide at the Gln-Ser juncture by TEV protease, the released peptide with the sequence SKGSCGENLYFQ was concentrated and detected by high-resolution LC/MS. Together with large scale phage production, this method allowed us to directly analyze the reaction on displayed peptide by LC/MS to our knowledge for the first time. The results clearly showed the TDA-assisted cyclization reaction occurred on the displayed peptide efficiently, demonstrating that TDA cyclization may offer a promising approach to develop macrocyclic compounds for inhibitor screening.

17303920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303920.value: Cyclic peptides, compounds with intriguing chemical structures, are being explored for their potential in targeting challenging protein-protein and protein-nucleic acid interactions. They possess several therapeutic properties, such as target selectivity, potency, metabolic stability, and oral bioavailability. Despite the challenges in developing chemoselective peptide cyclization due to the diverse nucleophilic side chain functionalities in unprotected peptides, we have successfully developed a method involving ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) that forms an isoindole moiety-linked cyclic peptide. This method has several advantages including its simplicity and the absence of the need for a catalyst. We have conducted and concluded several studies in this project, leading to key findings. First, we now understand the structure-activity relationship of OPA analogues and have successfully used OPA-based cyclization to mimic disulfide cyclic peptides. Second, we have applied the OPA-cyclization strategy to synthesize a wide range of cyclic peptides and stapled peptides analogues, demonstrating its adaptability to unnatural residues and varied unit spacing. Third, we discovered that thiophene-2,3-dicarboxaldehyde (TDA) reacts specifically with the primary amine and thiol within unprotected peptides, generating a stable thieno[2,3-c]pyrrole-bridged cyclic structure. Moreover, we successfully explored the feasibility of the TDA-assisted cyclization strategy in constructing phage-displayed cyclic libraries. We found that the TDA-assisted cyclization reaction occurred efficiently on the displayed peptide, indicating that TDA cyclization could be a promising approach for developing a super diverse macrocyclic peptide compounds for inhibitor screening. In conclusion, our research on cyclic peptides has led to significant advancements in their development and understanding, providing a solid foundation for future drug discovery efforts.

17303920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303920.value: The research on cyclic peptides and the development of chemoselective peptide cyclization has significant potential for further progression. The next phase of research could focus on improving the efficiency and selectivity of the cyclization reaction. This might involve fine-tuning the reaction conditions or exploring new catalysts or reagents. Another promising avenue for exploration is the development of new cyclic peptide structures with enhanced therapeutic properties or target specificity. The cyclization method could also be applied to a broader range of peptides, potentially expanding its utility in drug discovery. Additionally, the use of TDA-assisted cyclization in constructing phage-displayed cyclic libraries could be further optimized and applied to high-throughput screening of bioactive cyclic peptides. The ultimate goal would be the translation of these research findings into practical applications in pharmaceutical development, such as the creation of new drugs for challenging targets. This will require collaboration with pharmaceutical industries and rigorous preclinical and clinical testing. The research has laid a strong foundation, and the future course of action should focus on building upon these findings, optimizing methods, and moving towards practical applications.

17303920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303920.value: Our research focuses on developing new ways to create compounds called cyclic peptides. These are ring-shaped molecules that have shown potential in treating various diseases because they can interact with biological targets in our bodies that are hard to reach with traditional drugs. However, making these compounds can be challenging due to their complex structures. We've developed a new method that makes it simpler and faster to produce cyclic peptides. We've also found a way to make these compounds more stable and resistant to breakdown in the body, which could potentially increase their effectiveness as drugs. Additionally, we've applied our method to create a large library of these compounds, which can be screened to find new potential drugs. Overall, our research could pave the way for the development of new treatments for a wide range of diseases.

17304320.value: Development of a method for rearranging intracellular signal transduction pathways, which is unprecedented up to date, leads to deeper understanding of cell mechanism in molecular level and precise, tailor-made treatment of diseases. In this project, a new method that enables such synchronous inhibition/activation of 2 proteins will be developed using 'molecular glue'. For proving the concept, the followings are key issues. 17304320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304320.value: Intracellular signal transduction plays essential roles in cell functions, behaviors, and destiny. If a specific signaling pathway can be manipulated as intended, it leads to not only a big progress in understanding biological mechanisms but also a strong method for curing diseases. Genetic engineering such as genome editing is a solid strategy to manipulate signal transduction in live cells. By knocking-in and knocking-out genes that encode proteins mediating a signal transduction of interest, incorporation and elimination of a signaling pathway can be achieved respectively. Genetic engineering is, therefore, powerful. However, it is still unprecedented to “rearrange” the existing signal transduction pathways. For rearranging one signaling pathway to another, (i) inhibition of the former signal and (ii) activation of the latter signal should be accomplished synchronously. In this research project, a novel methodology for rearranging intracellular signal transduction will be established based on ‘molecular glue’. 'Molecular glue' is a series of water-soluble polymers bearing multiple guanidinium ion pendants. Through multivalent salt-bridges with oxyanionic groups, molecular glue can tightly adhere to the surface of proteins. Previously, we found that, when a ligand unit for a target protein is conjugated to molecular glue, its adhesion can be guided to the target even under the existence of non-target proteins. Taking advantage of this nature, we will employ a protein as a trigger for detaching molecular glue from the other protein. By choosing proteins involving in 2 different signaling pathways, one of them can be activated by the detachment of molecular glue, whereas the other can be inhibited by the adhesion. As a proof of concept, we will try to rearrange the following signal transduction pathways: (1) cancer signals (survivin) to apoptosis signals (caspase); (2) inflammatory signals (NF-kB) to cell differentiation signals (JNK). 细胞内信号的转导对于细胞的功能与表达有着重要的作用。如果单一的信号可以被可控地转导，对于生物机理的研究和疾病的治愈都是一个巨大的进步。基因工程是活细胞内操控信号转导的一种可行的措施。通过键入和移除可作为信号转导媒介的编码蛋白上的基因，可以有效地建立与消除信号转导通道，从而实现可控地细胞内信号转导。但是重排现有的信号转导路径依旧是一个空白的研究领域。将一个信号路径重排到另一条路径可以通过（1）抑制原有的信号并且（2）激活新的信号来共同实现。 这个研究项目提出一种以“分子胶水”为基础，可以重排细胞内转导信号的新思路。“分子胶水”是一种带有多个胍盐的水溶性高分子化合物。通过与氧阴离子的多重价键的桥连作用，“分子胶水”可以紧密地贴合在蛋白表面。之前的研究结果显示，即使有非目标蛋白存在，“分子胶水”可以有导向性地与目标蛋白的配体相结合。基于这个优势与特性，我们使用一种蛋白作为触发点使得“分子胶水”可以从其他蛋白解离出来。因此，我们将选用两个带有不用的信号路径的蛋白，一个通过与“分子胶水”的分离而被激活，另一个可以通过粘合的方式被抑制。为了验证这个这种方法的可行性，我们将尝试重排如下几种信号转导路径：（1）从癌细胞信号（survivin）到凋亡信号（胱天蛋白酶）；（2）炎症信号（NFkB）到细胞分化信号（JNK）。

17304320.label: Realisation of objectives
17304320.value: [Achieved Objectives] We have successfully synthesized a molecular glue precursor that allows for the introduction of diverse ligands through click chemistry and used it to create a molecular glue with an inhibitor (Objective 2). Using this molecule, we achieved the inhibition of the 'output-signal' protein (Objective 3) and confirmed the recovery of its activity upon the addition of the 'input-signal' protein in vitro (namely, signal: OFF -> ON; Objective 4). Besides, we confirmed that molecular glue/protein complexes can be introduced into cells (Objective 5). Regarding the caspase/survivin system, preliminary results have been obtained that actually promote the apoptosis signal in cells (Objective 6). However, the differentiation between the apoptosis-inducing effect of the delivered exogenous caspase into the cell and the inhibition of intracellular survivin has not yet been completed. Therefore, we plan to conduct additional control experiments to demonstrate that the expected mechanism is at work. [Under-achieved Objectives] Objective 1: Since this Objective encompasses the overall goals of the research project, please refer to the details below. Objective 6: It was confirmed that the intracellular introduction of molecular glue/caspase complexes induces apoptosis. The unresolved issue, as mentioned earlier, is verifying the mechanism. To address this issue, we plan to conduct control experiments using molecular glue without the survivin inhibitor and a mock protein other than caspase (e.g., bovine serum albumin). Objective 7: We have been focusing on validating the caspase/survivin system first, which is more easily handled, and plan to conduct experiments based on the findings obtained (such as optimal conditions). Therefore, we have not yet started working on the intracellular signal conversion of JNK/NF-κB.

17304320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304320.value: While investigating the combination of dendritic molecular glue and DNA aptamers, we discovered that molecular glue with specific functional groups has a significantly high affinity for DNA aptamers. This led us to further develop a technology to enhance the binding of DNA aptamers with molecular glue (Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2021). In addition, in an effort to expand the conversion of biological signals beyond those involving protein mediators, we developed a covalent organic framework (COF)-based molecular glue. This novel approach successfully facilitated the release of small molecules in response to elevated calcium ion levels (Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2021). In addition, to establish a prototype system for converting mechanical force into biological signals, we designed a mechanotransducing hydrogel embedded with molecular glue that effectively induced enzymatic reactions (Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2024).

17304320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304320.value: By experimentally validating the conversion of protein-mediated intracellular signals and advancing the development of biological signal conversion systems, described above, that employ small molecules or mechanical stimuli as input signals, we plan to create molecular tools for the treatment of diseases such as cancer and inflammation.

17304320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304320.value: In living organisms, various biological processes are controlled by the transmission of information using different signaling molecules. When there are problems with these signaling pathways, it can lead to serious diseases. Compounds that can either boost or reduce these biological signals are often used as drugs. While genetically engineering these signaling pathways is possible, using such techniques in humans raises significant safety and ethical concerns. This research focuses on developing a flexible chemical tool that can 'temporarily' modify signaling pathways. This approach aims to provide a way to reprogram biological signals without the challenges associated with genetic engineering techniques when applied to humans. The key idea is to create a versatile chemical system that can be used to control signaling processes in the body, potentially leading to new treatment options for diseases caused by disruptions in biological communication networks. By developing this chemical tool, we hope, in the future, to overcome the barriers that limit the use of genetic engineering for directly altering signaling pathways in human patients.

17304520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304520.value: Planetary Nebulae (PNe) are the beautiful, ionised manifestations of the ejected outer envelopes of intermediate to low-mass stars. This occurs towards the end of their long lives due to the radiation field of their residual, hot and contracting stellar cores as they evolve to the "white dwarf" phase. This phenomena lasts for only a few thousand years. In contrast the PNe progenitor star mass range is 1-8 times that of our Sun, resulting in stellar ages of 1 - 10 billion years. Despite the PNe phase brevity their study is essential for improving understanding of the evolution of intermediate and low mass stars in their later stages. PNe are visible to great distances compared to their main-sequence counterparts because nearly all their energy is radiated via strong emission lines. These also permit the determination of abundances, expansion and radial velocities and, via photo-ionisation modelling, estimates of their central star temperatures. The study of PNe yields information on the nuclear burning, dredge up, and mass loss in their stellar progenitors so they are extremely powerful Galactic probes. They provide us with vital clues on the chemical enrichment of our entire Galaxy as their host stars dominate the Galactic mass-loss budget over billions of years. Here we propose the first extensive study of an extremely rare class of PNe: those that reside in Galactic open star clusters. After careful investigation over many years using our extensive accumulated samples of carefully vetted PNe and associated data we have discovered 8 excellent candidates. These rare jewels are rosetta stones for stellar evolution. This is because the accurate cluster distances allows us to obtain precise determinations of the physical parameters of any cluster associated Planetary Nebula (PN) and of its central star. These are rarely known otherwise but are key to understanding mass loss and ISM feedback. Theoretical cluster isochrones can then used to determine the PN progenitor's properties, while photometry of their central stars will constrain their intrinsic luminosity and mass given the known distances. The progenitor star's mass will be related to the PN's chemical characteristics, determined from spectroscopy, and will provide valuable additional data points for the important white dwarf initial-to-final mass relation over currently very poorly sampled mass-ranges. We have already proven two of our PN to reside in Galactic open clusters and have added 6 more promising candidates to this exceptionally rare sample. 17304520.value: As for other projects this project was affected by the impact of Covid but nevertheless some notable project achievements were made. 17304520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304520.value: Our major research findings are of course detailed in the related publications including one in ApJ Letters. Here we report confirmation of a large, evolved, bipolar planetary nebula and its blue, white dwarf central star as a member of the ~500 Myr old Galactic open star cluster M37 (NGC 2099). This is only the third known example of a planetary nebula in a Galactic open cluster and was found via our ongoing program of identifying and studying planetary nebulae-open cluster associations. High confidence in the association comes from the consistent radial velocities and proper motions for the confirmed central star and cluster stars from Gaia, reddening agreement, and location of the planetary nebula well within the tidal cluster boundary. Interestingly, all three Galactic examples have bipolar morphology and likely Type-I chemistry, both characteristics of higher mass progenitors. In this case the progenitor star mass is in the midrange of ~2.8 Msun. It provides a valuable, additional point on the key stellar initial-to-final mass relation independent of cluster white dwarf estimates and also falls in a gap in the poorly sampled mass region. This planetary nebula also appears to have the largest kinematical age ever determined and implies increased visibility lifetimes when they are located in clusters.

17304520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304520.value: The original project still has further to go due to the delays and disruption caused by Covid and because several new promising PN-Open Cluster candidates have also been found by our team in the interim. Our new telescope time awards on 8-m class telescopes also promise to deliver high quality data to enable determination of Cluster and PNe chemical signatures and to further constrain stellar evolutionary models under original objective 4. These new data could also help provide independent verification of the latest accelerated evolutionary models and lead to additional impactful science publications.

After careful investigation over many years using our extensive accumulated samples of carefully vetted PNe and associated data we discovered 8 excellent candidates. The progenitor star's mass will be related to the PN's chemical characteristics, determined from spectroscopy, and will provide valuable additional data points for the important white dwarf initial-to-final mass relation over currently very poorly sampled mass-ranges. 17304720.label: Realisation of objectives
17304720.value: This project conducted precise measurements of β-decay spectroscopy near the sd-shell proton drip line at the end of the radioactive beamline RIBLL1 terminal at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) of Institute of Modern Physics (IMP) for systematic studies on isospin symmetry breaking and β-delayed multi-particle emission mechanisms. We have successfully developed a detector array consisting of double-sided silicon strips and ion-implanted quadruple silicon detectors. This detector array can efficiently record the energy, time, and spatial information of light particles produced by exotic decays of nuclei near the proton drip line. It possesses high position resolution and large spatial coverage. Using this new generation of double-sided silicon strip detector arrays and high-purity germanium detectors, we carried out high-precision β decay measurements of exotic atomic nuclei 22Si, 22Al, 23Si, 26P and 27S near the proton drip line in the RIBLL1 terminal of the Lanzhou Radioactive Beam Line. We recorded all the information of the emitted particles in exotic decays, fully reproducing the physical process of exotic decay. We achieved coincident measurements of light and heavy ions, β particles, and γ rays, and strictly selected rare decay events based on positional, temporal, and energy information. With high-precision decay measurements, we have deeply explored the symmetry-breaking of exotic nuclear symmetry, isospin mixing phenomena, double-proton decay emission mechanisms, and nuclear astrophysical processes. The entire experimental setup is the following. A primary beam 28Si was accelerated to 75.8 MeV/u by HIRFL cyclotrons and then fragmented on a 1500 μm 9Be target. Secondary ions were separated by the first Radioactive Ion Beam Line (RIBLL1) and identified by the combination of energy loss and time of flight. The ions of interest (22Si,23Si and 27S) were finally implanted into a silicon array surrounded by clover-type high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors. The schematic layout of the detection setup can be found in our paper [PRL 125, 192503(2019)]. The silicon array we constructed was composed of two thin double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) and several quadrant silicon detectors (QSDs). DSSD1 of 149 μm thickness and DSSD2 of 66 μm served to measure energy-time-position correlations between the implantation of 22Si, 22Al, 23Si, 26P and 27S and their decay. The 314 μm thick QSD1 placed behind DSSD2 was used for anticoincidence of the penetrating fragments and measurement of high-energy protons escaping from DSSD2, while the 1546 μm thick QSD2 was employed for β measurements. Another two QSDs were installed at the end to veto the possible disturbances from the penetrating light particles coming along with the beam. The implanted ions were identified on an event-by-event basis, and the accurate number of the implanted 22Si, 22Al, 23Si, 26P and 27S and the subsequent decay, as well as the absolute proton and γ-ray intensities, were determined accordingly. We successfully analysed all the data. We carried out detailed investigation on mirror-nuclei systems including 22Si-22O, 23Si-23F and 27S-27Na for the first systematic study of isospin symmetry breaking in sd-shell nuclear region. To interpret the physics, we established collaboration with theorists in Japan and China who made efforts to improve the calculation program for the large shell model. A unique quadrupole moment + pairing force Hamiltonian, in which the INC nuclear force has been introduced. This successfully incorporates isospin-breaking nuclear forces in shell model calculations. The theorist collaborators have also solved numerical calculation challenges and conducted systematic theoretical research on this issue. Using the theoretical results, we have explored and comprehensively explained the experimental data. We also investigated on a new probe to halo nuclei in mirror-nuclei systems using beta-decay measurements and shell model interpretation. It led to the publications of two Physical Review Letters under this GRF grant. In addition, we have also developed another more power silicon array under this GRF grant - large-scale silicon strip detector array coupled with digital acquisition system based on application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) technology. The entire ASIC system can support data acquisition for up to 30,720 channels, breaking through the development bottleneck of traditional nuclear electronics. We have utilized the ASIC system to achieve signal acquisition from the TTT series double-sided silicon strips by the UK-based Micron Semiconductor company. The energy resolution of the 5.157 MeV α peak is around 1%. So far, we have purchased eight TTT double-sided silicon strip detectors and ASIC electronic instruments, and designed a detector array support system based on printed circuit boards (PCB). After assembling the silicon strip detector array, its detection efficiency, time resolution, and other performance parameters will reach to world’s leading standard. The large solid-angle and high-granularity silicon strip array possesses excellent detection efficiency, high energy resolution, and strong discrimination capabilities, enabling higher precision measurements of β decay properties. The assembly of the silicon strip detector array has been completed, and comprehensive testing of the array has been carried out at both HKU laboratory and IMP laboratory.

17304720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304720.value: The study of exotic nuclei far from the β stability line would greatly contribute information to the knowledge of fundamental forces and nuclear structure. Using a state-of-the-art silicon detection array with five HPGe detectors, β-decay experiments of 22Si、23Si, 22Al、26P and 27S near the proton drip-line were performed at HIRIFL-RIBLL1 in Institute of Modern Physics, aiming to investigate the isospin-symmetry breaking, the mechanism of β-delayed two-proton emission and other exotic decay modes. As a result, the largest value of mirror asymmetry in low-lying states by far, with δ=206(96), is found in the transition to the first 1+ excited state, revealing a proton halo structure in 22Al [Phys. Rev. Lett 125,192503]. In additional, by investigating the β decay of 26P to 26Si at Ex = 5929.4(8) keV, the 25Al(p, γ) 26Si reaction rate in explosive hydrogen burning environments was studied, providing a high-precision data for 26Al nucleosynthesis in stellar environment [Phys. Rev. C 101, 024305, and HKU Ph.D. thesis]. Another important achievement is the T= 2 isobaric analog state (IAS) at 13 055 keV and two new high-lying states at 13 380 and 11 912 keV in 26Si being unambiguously identified through β-delayed two-proton emission. The isospin mixing matrix element between the 26Si IAS and the nearby 13 380-keV state is determined to be 130(21) keV, and this result represents the strongest mixing, highest excitation energy, and largest level spacing of a doublet ever observed in β-decay experiments [Phys. Rev. Lett 129, 242502 (Editor's suggestion)]. For the detection system, we have successfully constructed the Silicon detector array coupled with the readout of front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC). This array with high granularity and large solid-angle coverage achieves high detection efficiency, superior energy and angular resolutions as well as excellent particle-identification, The entire ASIC system can support readout of 30720 channels, which could realize high precision beta-decay measurements. Publication is under prepared.

17304720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304720.value: In 1932, Nobel laureate Werner Karl Heisenberg introduced the concept of isospin to explain the symmetry of atomic nuclei resulting from the similarities between protons and neutrons. Isospin symmetry is still widely accepted concept today. However, due to the differences in mass between protons and neutrons, Coulomb interaction, and charge-related aspects of nuclear forces, isospin symmetry is not strictly conserved. We conducted beta decay experiments on the proton-rich nuclei at the Radioactive Ion Beam Line in Lanzhou, located within the Heavy Ion Research Facility of Lanzhou to provide new data on isospin asymmetry. Surprisingly, we observed the largest value of mirror asymmetry in low-lying states by far with δ=206(96) in 22Al and the strongest isospin mixing doublet in 26Si. The unexpected experimental results cannot be well explained by nuclear models which may be related to weak binding (or continuum) effects or nuclear deformation, posing a direct challenge to our understanding of nuclear forces.

17304820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304820.value: The study of transport phenomena in many-body physics is one of the most important branches of modern condensed matter physics. Transport measurements offer crucial insight into the microscopic interactions and scattering mechanism in the system and reveal important information about the many-body quantum state. For example, the linear-temperature dependence of electric resistivity in the strange metal phase of high-temperature cuprate suggests that the usual Landau quasi-particles do not exist. In the past decades, due to advances in the manipulation of cold atoms in a harmonic trap or in optical lattices, cold atom systems have emerged as ideal platforms for the investigation of certain transport phenomena in strongly interacting systems. One of the most interesting systems in this regard is the unitary Fermi gas where inter-atomic scattering reaches maximal strength allowed by quantum mechanics. Spin diffusion experiments, which are typically quite difficult in solid state materials, can be done relatively easily in a unitary Fermi gas where it is demonstrated that spin diffusivity reaches a minimum. In addition, unitary Fermi gas also possesses scaling invariance which leads to the vanishing of bulk viscosity. Investigating the effects of breaking scale invariance (by either a finite scattering length or effective range) on the transport phenomena thus becomes a very important question. In this proposal, we will investigate two related systems where effective range breaks the scale invariance. The first is a two-component Fermi gas with s-wave interactions. In this case, it is known that a finite scattering length will break the scale invariance and give rise to a finite bulk viscosity. We will investigate the how a finite effective range at unitarity leads to the appearance of a non-zero viscosity and obtain analytic expressions in limiting cases. We will also determine the dependences of ground state energy on effective range at resonance. The second example is a single-component Fermi gas with p-wave interactions. In this situation, it is already known that even for equilibrium properties, it is important to include the effect range correction. In this proposal, we will investigate its transport properties, in particular, bulk and shear viscosities. Due to energy dependent scattering in the p-wave case, it is expected that the effects of effective range will be more prominent. We will try to compare the s-wave and p-wave calculations wherever appropriate. 对多体体系输运性质的研究是凝聚态物理研究很重要的一个方面。输运测量可以提供体系相互作用，粒子散射以及量子态的重要信息。例如高温超导态正常态电阻对温度的线性依赖说明传统意义上的朗道准粒子是不存在的。由于实验技术的进步，冷原子体系在过去的几年里成为模拟多体体系的一个重要平台。这其中，所谓的幺正费米气体是其中最为有趣的一个体系。在幺正费米气体中，粒子之间的相互作用达到量子力学所允许的最强情况，一个直接的结果就是自旋输运达到量子允许的最小值。另外，幺正费米气体还具有所谓的尺度变换不变性。研究破坏尺度变化不变性的微扰对其性质的影响就成为了一个很有意义的问题。在这个项目中，我们将研究两类体系。一是具有s-波相互作用的两份量费米子。我们将研究有限大小散射长度以及有效力程对体系粘滞系数的影响。另外一个是单份量的p-波气体。我们早就知道有效力程对p-波气体的影响尤为重要，我们将着重研究其对体系粘滞系数的影响。

To compare with possible experiments, we shall derive frequency dependences of the bulk and shear viscosities for the p-wave Fermi gas, and relate them to experimentally measurable quantities such as the damping of breathing mode.

17304820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304820.value: The major findings of the proposal is the explicit calculation and comparison between bulk viscosities for s-wave and p-wave Fermi gases. We showed that the effective range correction plays very different roles in the s-wave and p-wave cases. In the s-wave case, it is perturbative while in the p-wave case, it is non-perturbative. In particular, the bulk viscosity spectral function is divergent in both zero frequency and high frequency limit when the p-wave effective range goes to zero, in contradistinction to s-wave case. We have also made investigation of the bulk viscosity in the damping of breathing mode, showed that how it can be extracted from the current experiments by using the equation of motion technique for the monopole operator and exploit the conformal dynamical symmetry of the problem. There are a few other papers that are partially supported by the current GRF grant. Namely, we have explored, together with the experimentalist the correlation properties of the 1D Fermi gas and the emergence of s-wave scattering. We have also explored the scaling symmetry in 3D unitary Fermi gas.

17304820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304820.value: In three-dimensions, it is may be useful to investigate the associated the structure of two-body density matrix and explore how the effective range effects appears in other dynamical processes, as was investigated in another publication of ours, exploring the consequence of conformal symmetry in s-wave case. In 1D, it is important to explore the effects of large effective range as this is related to current experiments.

17304820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304820.value: We are all familiar with the viscosity of water or honey, for which the later is obviously very viscose and the former is not. Viscosity measures the ability of the liquid to transfer momentum (or for momentum gradient to relax) and is a fundamental quantity that characterise different fluid. In quantum fluid where strong interaction is present, the calculation of viscosity turned out to be very complicated and so far no well defined methods that can be applied to different situations exits. In this project, we have made use of a particular symmetry and its breaking to explore the viscosity in a unitary Fermi gas with either s- or p-wave interaction and has found profound difference as to the role of scattering effective range.

17304920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304920.value: Over 50 years after their discovery, pulsars continue to fascinate and surprise in equal measure. Their extreme properties (e.g. density, magnetic field), combined with their precise timing signature, make them useful tools to probe fundamental questions in physics and astronomy (e.g. General Relativity), while their broad emission across the electromagnetic spectrum (from radio to gamma rays) make them attractive targets to a large fraction of the astronomical community. Recent advances in gamma-ray detectors (in space and on the ground) have led to a revolution in pulsar astronomy. In just over a decade, we have witnessed the number of gamma-ray pulsars balloon from a handful in 2008, to over 250 today. Furthermore, the energy up to which pulsars are detected has increased from a few GeV up to TeV energies. Below 100 GeV, the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT), in orbit since 2008, has detected most of the gamma-ray pulsars, uncovering new populations (many radio-quiet). Above 100 GeV, ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) are more sensitive, making important detections, sometimes up to unprecedented energies. Indeed, in the case of the Crab and Vela pulsars, pulsed emission has been detected beyond 1 TeV, something which challenges conventional emission models developed over the past 50 years. Whether this represents a new emission component or an extrapolation of the GeV component is an open question with important implications, both for our understanding of pulsars themselves, and for their potential as tools in the study of fundamental physics (e.g. Lorentz Invariance Violation). Unfortunately, IACTs have small fields of view (few degrees) and limited duty cycles (typically fewer than 1000 hr per year), making the deep study of a large number of pulsars with these telescopes impossible. The High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) observatory, inaugurated in 2015, uses a radically different technique enabling it to observe a wide field of view (several steradians) uninterruptedly (24 hours a day, 365 days a year). HAWC is currently carrying out the deepest wide-field survey of the Northern Hemisphere sky at TeV energies. We propose to develop and apply a set of specific tools and techniques for the study of pulsars with HAWC, providing the best observational constraints on pulsar emission above 100 GeV. Our survey will produce scientific insights and answer key questions on pulsars (e.g. is there a TeV emission component) and guide future very high energy observations of pulsars (e.g. with LHAASO and CTA). 脈衝星自從50多年前首次被發現以來，它們的特性一直使人著迷和驚奇。它們的極端密度和磁場，與精確的時計，使其成為探索物理學和天文學的基本問題（例如廣義相對論）的有效工具。它們發出的幅射包括整個電磁頻譜（從無線電波到伽瑪射線），使其成為很有趣的研究對象。地面和空間伽馬射線探測器的最新進展導致了脈衝星天文學的一場革命。在短短的十年中，我們目睹了伽瑪射線脈衝星的數量從2008年的少數增加到今天的250多個。此外，脈衝星被探測到的能量已經從幾個GeV上升到TeV能量。在100 GeV以下的波段，費米大面積望遠鏡（LAT）自2008年以來一直在軌道上運行，它已探測到大量伽馬射線脈衝星，包括許多無線電安靜的。在100 GeV以上， Cherenkov望遠鏡（IACT）則比較更靈敏，有時甚至可以探測到前所未有的能量。事實上Crab和Vela脈衝星已探測到超過1 TeV的訊號，對過去50年來沿用的幅射模型作出挑戰。究竟TeV以上的幅射代表新的發射機制還是GeV的伸延，至今仍未有定論，但這對脈衝星本身的理解以及它們作為研究基礎物理學的工具（例如，違返洛倫茲不變性）均有重要意義。可惜IACT的視野很小只有幾度，觀測時間有限（通常每年少於1000小時），這使得用這些望遠鏡進行大量脈衝星的深入研究成為不可能。HAWC觀測站於2015年啟用，它使用了一種截然不同的技術，使它可以不間斷地（365天，24小時）觀察廣闊的視野。 HAWC目前正在對北半球的天空進行最深的TeV觀測。我們建議開發一套工具和技術來研究脈衝星，從而觀測脈衝星100 GeV以上的幅射。我們的研究將回答有關脈衝星的關鍵問題（例如是否存在TeV幅射成分），並指導未來對脈衝星的超高能量觀測（例如使用LHAASO和CTA）。

17304920.label: Realisation of objectives
17304920.value: Our first objective, to devise a tool that could serve to assign pulsar phases to HAWC data was achieved (100%). Using pulsar software PINT, in conjunction with dedicated scripts we are now able to set up a pipeline that will enable us to take HAWC data, along with a timing model (.par) file for a pulsar, and assign a pulsar phase to each individual event. Our second objective mostly completed. We have a preliminary list of candidate sources from the Third HAWC Catalog (3HWC) that we will apply our analysis to. Our selection of candidates is based on both the properties in the very high energy (VHE) range, as detected by HAWC, and the pulsar properties as measured by the Fermi Large Area Telescope. However, we are still waiting for the most recent HAWC catalog, which is still in preparation. We will perform our final analysis on pulsation searches once our list of candidates is finalized. Our third objective is fully completed. We have carried out extensive studies using simulated HAWC data, and models for possible expected pulsar spectra to determine the sensitivity of HAWC to discriminate between a pulsar and Pulsar Wind Nebula (or other background) emission. In addition, we have demonstrated the effect of using the pulsed signal to improve the sensitivity of our search technique, over a simple spectral discrimination. Our fourth objective (the search for TeV pulsations) is still on-going. Due to the fact that we have not finalized our search pipeline or candidate list, we have been unable to complete the final search which will form one of the main results of our investigation. Our fifth objective was completed. By carrying out a detailed investigation of simulated data, we determined the possible improvement in the sensitivity of HAWC using neural network techniques. This result was presented at an international conference (ICRC) and published. The sixth objective has only partially been completed (70%). Searches for sub-TeV pulsations were completed using Fermi LAT data, and published as part of the Fermi LAT Third Pulsar Catalog (3PC). However, the complementary searches for pulsations using HAWC data are still pending and will be carried out once we have finalized the list of HAWC candidates described above. The seventh objective is in process. A publication detailing our simulation studies, as well as our candidate selection and description of the sensitivity of our search techniqes is in preparation for submission to the Astrophysical Journal. The journal article is in its final phases and has gone through one round of internal reviewing within the HAWC Collaboration. It will be submitted to the journal later this year.

17304920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304920.value: The main findings of our studies, based on a series of HAWC simulations, include the determination of the sensitivity of HAWC to the detection of two coincident point sources with different spectral characteristics: a pulsar-like source, with a power law spectrum, and a different component (pulsar wind nebula – PWN) with a Log Parabola spectrum. Our study indicates that to detect the pulsar component, the cross-over energy between these two components plays a vital role, as does the flux ratios between the two components. This result highlights that spectral separation becomes feasible when each component dominates in distinct energy regimes. We also carried out preliminary pulsed analysis, an initial exploration of the added sensitivity that a pulsed analysis might provide, by assuming that all the pulsed signal is contained in a single bin, while the PWN signal is spread out evenly over all bins. During pulsed analysis of HAWC data, the PWN flux value is reduced, keeping the Pulsar component fixed, resulting in an increase in the flux ratio of the two components, thus enhancing the pulsar detection likelihood. Thus, a phased analysis is significantly more sensitive than a simple, unpulsed analysis.

17304920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304920.value: Future directions for this project include the application of the techniques described in our studies to the latest catalog of HAWC sources (4HWC), and the use of pulsar phases to distinguish between pulsed and unpulsed emission. A detailed phased analysis using this future HAWC dataset is a logical next step.

17304920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304920.value: HAWC is a wide field gamma-ray telescope which has been observing the Northern Hemisphere sky for the last ten years. Among the numerous sources that HAWC is detecting are bright TeV-emitting Galactic sources coincident with pulsars. HAWC has the potential for detecting pulsed emission from dozens of these sources. This work demonstrates that, under the right conditions, such a potential can be realized, raising questions about the possible pulsar mechanism.

17305220.label: Project Objectives
17305220.value: To characterize digraphs with the min-max relation on packing and covering cycles (arc version), and find a structural description of all such digraphs. The possible outcome is a structural chacterization and description of all such digraphs. If successful, we shall get not only a beautiful mathematical theorem (in the same spirit as the celebrated Strong Perfect Graph Theorem) but also a polynomial-time algorithm for the feedback arc set (FAS) problem on these digraphs. Since the FAS problem arises in a rich variety of applications, the algorithm devised in our proof can be employed or further developed to solve many important real-world problems. To characterize digraphs with the min-max relation on packing and covering feedback arc sets, and find a structural description of all such digraphs. The PI believes that he can make significant contributions to this proposed problem. For example, he is very confident that the min-max relation on strongly planar digraphs is within reach. In his investigation of the general case, the PI needs to exhibit a wealth of structural properties enjoyed by the feedback arc set packing problem, and to develop various new proof techniques. They can certainly be used to tackle some other well-known problems in combinatorics, such as Woodall's conjecture on packing dijoins. To resolve the problem of recognizing Grillet graphs proposed by Chvatal in 1995. The PI has investigated this problem for several years; he is inclined to believe that this problem is solvable in polynomial time. He will make arduous effort to obtain a good characterization of all Grillet graphs. If obtained, it can dispel the long-standing controversy over Chvatal's problem. This deep result will also have interesting applications in game theory.

17305220.label: Realisation of objectives
17305220.value: I have carried out Objectives 1 and 2 completely, and have also been making steady progress towards recognizing Grillet graphs. In particular, I wish to state that packing feedback arc sets is a notoriously hard problem in combinatorial optimization; several of the finest unclaimed prizes in this field involve the packing of feedback arc sets (or dijoins, which are dual concepts). With the support of this General Research Fund, I have successfully characterized all tournaments with the min-max relation on packing and covering feedback arc sets.

17305220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305220.value: (1) In the paper entitled A Min-Max Relation on Packing Cycles in Digraphs (in preparation; with G. Ding and R. Tao), we have successfully characterized all digraphs, such that the minimum total weight of a feedback arc set is equal to the maximum size of a cycle packing for every nonnegative integral weight function defined on the arc set, which yields a beautiful and deep theorem in combinatorial optimization. Our proof is highly sophisticated and difficult, taking more than 80 pages in total. (2) A celebrated conjecture made by Woodall in 1978 asserts that in any planar digraph the length of a shortest cycle is equal to the maximum number of disjoint feedback arc sets. Despite tremendous research effort, little progress has been made towards its resolution. In the paper entitled Packing Feedback Arc Sets in Tournaments Exactly (Math. Oper. Res. 49 (2024), 151-170; with X. Chen, G. Ding and Q. Zhao), we have successfully described all tournaments, such that the minimum total weight of a cycle is equal to the maximum size of a feedback arc set packing for every nonnegative integral weight function defined on the arc set. This result represents a significant contribution to combinatorial optimization. (Math. Oper. Res. is a flagship international journal in operations research.) (3) Our paper entitled On Gupta's Codensity Conjecture (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 37 (2023), 1666-1673; with Y. Cao et al.) is devoted to the study of the codensity conjecture proposed by Gupta in 1978, which is the dual version of the famous Goldberg-Seymour conjecture we proved a few years ago. In this paper we have successfully established the best existing bound on the cover index of a multigraph, which differs from the bound conjectured by Gupta only by at most one. A preliminary version of this paper (manuscript) was contained in the completion report of my GRF project entitled Edge-Colorings of Multigraphs. This published article is a revised version.

17305220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305220.value: A complete solution to Chvatal's problem on recognizing Grillet graphs. I also believe that a complete proof of Gupta's condensity conjecture can be obtained by further developing techniques created in our proof of the Goldberg-Seymour conjecture and in our paper published in SIAM J. Discrete Math., with hard work.

17305220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305220.value: The present project has both great theoretical interest and practical value. First, the proposed problems are all fundamental and attractive; solution to any of them will yield not only a beautiful mathematical theorem but also a polynomial-time algorithm for the corresponding feedback arc set problem, cycle packing problem, feedback arc set packing problem, and recognition problem of Grillet graphs. Second, since our research covers a wide spectrum of combinatorics and optimization, in our investigation we have to develop various new solution techniques and exhibit a wealth of new structural properties. As feedback arc set and dijoin are dual concepts when restricted to plane digraphs and Grillet graphs have important applications in game theory, the techniques and structural properties obtained in this project can certainly be further employed or developed to tackle the well-known Woodall conjecture on dijoins and some interesting game problems. Finally, both the optimization and recognition problems investigated in this project arise in a rich variety of applications, the results obtained can be applied to solve many important real-world problems.

17305420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305420.value: In the last decade, ozone air quality in Southern China/Hong Kong has significantly deteriorated due to the increase in the number of tropical cyclones (TCs) entering the Luzon/Taiwan Strait from the Western North Pacific (WNP). The effect of the more frequent occurrence of TCs in the Luzon/Taiwan Strait not only enhances the transport of airborne pollutants from inland China resulting in high ozone concentration, but also induces strong subsidence airflow in their outer periphery. These subsidence airflows carry rich ozone air mass originated from the stratosphere and magnify the ground-level ozone pollution in the outer TC regions (>800km from the TC center). It is important to quantify the effect of this Upper Troposphere-Lower Stratosphere (UTLS) ozone transport for the sake of ozone air pollution management in Southern China. In this proposal, the WRF-CMAQ air quality modeling system will be applied to better understand the transport pathway of TC induced UTLS ozone transport, and its relationship with surface ozone enhancement in the outer TC regions. The study will first use observational data (both air quality and meteorology) from multiple historical TC cases to better understand the environmental conditions that cause such ozone transport. Secondly, air quality simulations using WRF-CMAQ will be used to decipher whether TC intensity influences the UTLS ozone transport and trigger higher ground- level ozone pollution. We are hypothesizing that the increase in TC intensity expected in the future climate would induce stronger peripheral subsidence airflow and potentially cause more UTLS ozone transport. The success of the proposed research will improve our understanding of the TC induced ozone episodes. 過去十年中，從北太平洋西部進入呂宋/台灣海峽的熱帶氣旋有增加的趨勢，也令中國南部及香港的臭氧污染日益嚴重。頻繁的熱帶氣旋，不但增強了來自中國內陸的污染物傳輸，導致臭氧濃度增强。其外圍所引起的沉降氣流，也引来了來自平流層的臭氧，影响區域性的臭氧濃度。管理對華南地區的臭氧污染，量化對來自平流層的臭氧傳輸是非常重要。在此研究，我們將使用WRF-CMAQ空氣質量建模系統去了解熱帶氣旋所引發的平流層臭氧傳輸。這研究將使用多個歷史案例的觀測數據（空氣質量和氣象學），來了解導致此類臭氧傳輸的環境條件。我們也會使用WRF-CMAQ進行空氣質量模擬，以判斷熱帶氣旋的強度是否影響平流層臭氧傳輸。
