17500420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500420.value: I-deals are individualized and non-standard employment and work agreements that are mutually agreed by, and are beneficial to, employees and employers. We draw on career resourcing theory to conceptualize the relationship between i-deals and career success. Career resourcing theory describes the process of conducting career actions to generate career resources, thereby enhancing career outcomes. This theory also highlights the importance of schema, that is, cultural and cognitive framework that guides the interpretation, mobilization and utilization of resources to attain career outcomes. We suggest that securing i-deals is a career action that brings career resources that, in turn, enhance career success. While i-deals can have positive effects on employee careers, these effects can be even more positive or not so positive as a function of organizational and employee schema. We propose an organizational and an employee schema that would jointly affect the effectiveness of i-deals in generating career resources and enhancing career success. Organizational schema is represented by organizational career management and employee schema by boundaryless career orientation. I-deals in organizations with a schema of long-term orientation towards development and retention of employees in their career management are more likely to bring career resources and career success. Employees with a schema of boundaryless career orientation that centers on ease of movement across employment situations would be less likely to generate career resources from i-deals. These employees are even less likely to generate career resources from i-deals if their organizations have this long-term orientation towards development and retention of employees in their career management. Career resources is a key construct in career resourcing theory and career research but there is no established measure for it. We propose to develop a measure of career resources. We propose a qualitative, a scale development and two field studies to test our model. The constructs we examine, i-deals, career resources, boundaryless career orientation, organizational career management and career success are all prevalent and important to employees and employers. Establish the basic model of a monopolistic seller, and then solve and fully characterize the profit-maximizing mechanism, based on which policy implications will be derived. The reneging cost is assumed to be positive and increasing as the buyer’s payoff reduces due to deceptive tactics. For a given function of reneging cost, we study whether the seller finds it profitable to renege on any contract, the contracts offered in the first stage as well as the contracts offered in the second stage, if any. We will then conduct comparative statics to see how equilibrium changes in the reneging cost function. Based on the results obtained, we will derive policy implications on the optimal level of regulatory penalty. Our intuition suggests that a moderate penalty is optimal. Moreover, we need to find the optimal amount of fixed penalty and variable penalty that increases as buyer’s payoff reduces.

Extend the basic model to a dynamic model of information transmission. Instead of paying explicit reneging costs, the seller in this extended model suffers loss in future profit once future buyers learn about the past reneging behavior. The results can shed some light on how word of mouth can affect the monopolistic seller’s reneging behavior as well as contracts offered. We would like to see whether more transparent information is better for consumers and for society.

Extend the model to consider competing sellers, each of which cannot commit on their initial offers. It is a non-trivial extension because now each seller needs to design the initial offers to attract buyers from other sellers while not being able to commit on those initial offers. In this competing environment, the initial offers can be naturally interpreted as advertisements. This extension can thus help us gain better understanding about how competing sellers advertise. Moreover, with this extension we can also look into how competition affects the equilibrium mechanism and social welfare by varying the degree of competition in the market.

17500620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500620.value: Sellers advertising something that is not actually what they intend to sell is not unusual. This is a common feature of business tactics such as bait-and-switch and deceptive advertising. These tactics are frequently used by both small-size sellers (such as real estate agencies, and car dealerships) and large companies (such as major chain retailers and airlines). On the other hand, using these tactics can be costly in the form of, for example, regulatory penalties, law suits or reputation loss. The possibility of reneging brings a new challenge to sellers when they want to profit from non-linear pricing, because customers are more reluctant to reveal how much they like high quality products, as they worry that they will be exploited afterwards for revealing this private information. Canonical works on non-linear pricing such as Mussa and Rosen (1978) show that a monopolistic seller can separate consumers of different preferences by providing a spectrum of quality-differentiated products. A crucial assumption in these works is that the seller can commit to the offers. In the proposed study, we seek to explore how a seller’s profit-maximizing mechanism would change when sellers can only partially commit. Through this research, we aim to completely characterize the profit-maximizing mechanism and derive policy implications. To list some of the expected results, with a moderate reneging cost, the seller needs to adjust the optimal mechanism in Mussa and Rosen (1978) so that the seller can self-commit. In some cases, this adjustment actually favors the buyers and yields a higher social welfare compared with the scenario when the seller can fully commit. In general, we expect that the buyer’s expected payoff and social welfare are non-monotonic in the reneging cost and they are maximized at a moderate level of reneging cost. When the reneging cost is low, the seller does renege on some contracts in equilibrium and we can deduce which contract(s) the seller chooses. We plan to extend the basic model to a dynamic model of information transmission to endogenize the reneging cost. By characterizing how intertemporal information transmission affects the optimal mechanism, we can derive policy implications on the regulation of information transparency. As another extension, we plan to investigate the model of competing sellers, where we can establish how sellers design initial offers (which can be interpreted as advertisements) to attract buyers when they cannot commit to these offers. 在日常生活中，賣家为一些並不打算出售的商品打广告并不鮮見。我们可以在包括誘導轉向法和誤導性廣告在內的商業策略中看到这一特征。不仅是小商戶（比如地產中介和汽车销售），大公司（比如大型连锁零售商和航空公司）也有使用这些商业策略。但与此同时，使用这些策略通常会付出例如监管处罚、法律诉讼或商誉损失等的成本。 这样撤回已提供的合约的可能性给希望从非线性定价中牟利的卖家带来了新的挑战，因为买家担心在透露私有信息之后被完全剥削，从而更加不愿意表露他们对购买高质量产品的真实意愿。传统的非线性定价模型假设卖家可以对提供的合约做出完全承诺。我们希望在计划的研究中探索卖家的利润最大化机制会如何因为他们只能做出部分承诺而发生改变。我们的目标是完全刻画利润最大化的机制并导出它的政策含义。

17500620.label: Realisation of objectives
17500620.value: The project is motivated by the observation that sellers frequently do not fully adhere to their initial offers. In real-world scenarios, it is not uncommon to witness some sellers honoring their initial offers while others unilaterally modify the contract terms through tactics such as add-on pricing, bait-and-switch, and deceptive advertising, often incurring certain costs. Contrarily, seminal works on nonlinear pricing, such as those by Mussa and Rosen (1978) and Maskin and Riley (1984), have presupposed that the seller is committed to the offered contract terms. This project delves into a dynamic mechanism design problem that permits the seller to renege on initial offers at a cost and present an entirely new set of options. We have developed a dynamic nonlinear pricing model that incorporates the cost of reneging. The model is structured as a two-stage game. In the first stage, a monopolistic seller (referred to as the principal) presents a selection of price-quality contracts, from which a buyer (referred to as the agent), who has private preference information, selects one. Following the buyer's selection, the seller has the option to finalize the transaction, thereby concluding the game. Alternatively, the seller may incur some cost to retract the initial offer and propose a new set of contracts to the buyer. In the second stage, the seller is able to fully commit to the new contracts. In our model, a scenario of full commitment corresponds to a sufficiently high reneging cost. Conversely, when the cost is negligible, the initial contracts lack any commitment power, resulting in no information disclosure by the buyer. The objective is to delineate the optimal dynamic mechanism for intermediate levels of the reneging cost. We first explore "reneging-proof" mechanisms, encompassing both separating and pooling mechanisms, and discover that in both instances, welfare can be enhanced relative to the full-commitment benchmark. Subsequently, we define the "partial-revelation" mechanism and demonstrate that it can lead to a more favorable outcome for consumers compared to the full-commitment scenario. The model's predictions align with various market phenomena. For instance, depending on market conditions, sellers may opt to renege on contracts offered to different consumer segments. Our model also elucidates why sellers might prefer a pooling mechanism even with the knowledge that consumers have diverse types. We provide a comprehensive analysis of how a profit-maximizing mechanism changes in the reneging cost. Additionally, the findings have significant policy implications, as regulatory measures can influence the costs associated with reneging. In a working paper, we expand upon the basic model by incorporating a dynamic model of information transmission and word-of-mouth communication. In this extended model, if a seller chooses to renege on an offer, the news of this action propagates through the interconnected web of consumers' social networks. This dissemination of information can tarnish the seller's reputation, leading to detrimental effects on future profits. The impact of such reputational damage is not uniform; it is intricately linked to the structure of the social network through which the information travels. Our findings establish a connection between the selling mechanism and the structure of the social network. We explore how the nature of these networks—whether they are tightly-knit communities or more dispersed networks—can influence the seller's decision-making process and the resulting market dynamics. Building on this, we delve into the competitive landscape by examining scenarios with two competing sellers. This competitive angle introduces a new layer of complexity, as sellers must now consider not only the potential reputational damage from reneging but also the strategic moves of their competitors. We investigate how the presence of competition influences the equilibrium outcomes. Through this extended analysis, we aim to provide a more comprehensive understanding of how information transmission and market competition interplay to shape the behaviors of sellers and the experiences of consumers in the marketplace. The insights gleaned from this study have the potential to inform both business strategies and policy regulations in the context of consumer protection and fair trading practices.

17500620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500620.value: The theoretical predictions of our dynamic nonlinear pricing model can be empirically tested by examining real-world market data and seller behavior. One approach is to collect and analyze data from industries where contract modification is prevalent, such as telecommunications or travel. Additionally, the model's implications regarding consumer welfare under "reneging-proof" and "partial-revelation" mechanisms can be assessed by comparing consumer satisfaction and market efficiency in scenarios with varying levels of contract commitment. Regulatory changes that affect the cost of reneging, such as increased penalties for deceptive advertising, provide a natural experiment setting to observe how such costs influence seller behavior and market outcomes. By employing these empirical methods, the validity of the model's predictions can be tested against observed market behaviors, providing valuable feedback for refining the theoretical framework and informing policy decisions.

17500620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500620.value: Have you ever noticed how some companies change the deal after you've already agreed to it? They might add extra fees or change the terms of service. We have been studying this problem and have come up with a way to predict when companies might do this. Our study looks at how companies decide whether to stick to their original offer or change it, which can sometimes cost them money. We created a game-like model where a seller offers a deal, and then can choose to either keep their promise or offer something different, which might be better or worse for the buyer. This could help us understand why some companies seem to always be changing their offers and how new rules or laws might affect their decisions. It's important because it can help make things fairer for customers and help policymakers create better regulations.

Empirical applications will be performed to assess the impact of these modifications in practical work with real data.

17501420.value: 由于认识到经济关系的潜在变化，阈值模型在最近的计量经济学文献中变得越来越流行。阈值是重要的实证度量，因为它们为决策者可以量化和使用的经济行为转变提供了触发点。这些阈值触发点的计量经济学估计将为决策提供有用的参考点。为此，有必要提供阈值估计值并评估这些估计值的不确定性，以协助政策实施。这正是置信区间和置信集合的用途。阈值回归中的置信区间构建提出了许多挑战，这是该项目要解决的目标。 根据Hansen（2000）的工作，阈值的似然比置信区间（LR-CI）和回归参数的Bonferroni型置信区间在文献中最受欢迎。但是这些方法有缺点。模拟实验表明，当阈效应较小时，LR-CI通常会过低覆盖，而当阈效应较大时，LR-CI会过度覆盖。此外，在前一种情况下，回归参数的通常置信区间会过低覆盖，而在后一种情况下，Bonferroni型置信区间会过度覆盖。该项目试图解决这些缺陷，使得无论阈效应的大小如何，阈值和回归参数的置信区间都能尽可能地接近预设的覆盖值。 我们将采用的方法是，首先通过检查阈效应检验的p值是大于还是小于一个缓慢缩小到零的显著性水平，将阈效应分为“小”或“大”。当阈效应较大时，我们将表明，如果用Hansen的临界值，则真实阈值点落入反转LR统计量的集合的凸包（cov-LR-CI）中的概率大于预设水平，因此应使用较小的临界值。至于回归参数，可以使用通常置信区间，因为它具有完美的覆盖值。当阈效应较小时，无法一致地估计阈值点。我们将推导出cov-LR-CI的覆盖值，并表明它可以为有限样本下的真实覆盖值提供更好的近似。由于不能一致地估计阈效应的局部参数，因此我们将对最不利的LR统计量进行模拟，以找到每个假设阈值下的临界值。最终的cov-LR-CI将被构造为所有接受的阈值的凸包。至于回归参数，我们将使用具有理论上合理性的覆盖值的Bonferroni程序来构建置信区间。 我们计划用两个实证应用（一个关于经济增长，另一个关于劳动经济）来验证我们的新方法在实际工作中的表现，特别是评估当阈效应大/小的情况下我们方法的特征。

17501720.label: Project Objectives
17501720.value: Using accounting restatements as an empirical setting, we examine the appropriateness of using the ESG framework to measure Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) of firms. We want to see if it is justifiable for the Environment and Social (ES) dimensions to be grouped with the Governance (G) dimension to form composite ESG scores. While most researchers recognize that ES and G are distinct constructs that should not be combined, reputed agencies like Bloomberg and Sustainalytics continue to compile such composite ESG scores, and many investment managers use them to make important asset allocation decisions. Specifically, we investigate if the ES aspect and G aspect of CSR have the opposite effects on the market reaction to restatement announcements. We also examine if the ES aspect and G aspect of CSR continue to show opposite effects on the long-term financial performance of the restating firm in the post-restatement period. Essentially, we propose to build strong theoretical arguments explaining why the ES dimensions capture a completely different aspect of CSR than the G dimension. Our empirical results showing how ES and G dimensions can have completely opposite effects on firm performance would support our arguments. This would bring in much needed clarity in the ESG space for both academics and practitioners. We examine whether a firm experiences negative market reaction and greater analyst forecast dispersion in response to an accounting restatement announced by the firm's alliance partner (contagion effect of restatement). Prior research in accounting restatement literature has documented a contagion effect of restatements spreading to peer firms that operate in the same industry, share the same auditor, share the same board member, or share the same home country with the restating firm (Gleason, Jenkins, & Johnson, 2008; Jia & Zhao, 2017; Kang, 2008). If we find our predicted results, we will discover a new conduit (strategic alliance link) of the contagion effects of accounting restatement. We examine whether market participants downgrade their expectations of a firm's future financial performance following a restatement announcement by its alliance partner (the economic outlook revision channel of contagion). Theoretically, if a restatement significantly alters the economic outlook of the restating firm, then it can also affect the expected future profitability of firms that have close economic ties to the restating firm. However, the economic outlook revision channel of restatement contagion has not been well explored by prior research. Since alliance partners have well defined economic ties with considerable variation in the strength of these economic bonds, we will be able to fully explore the economic outlook revision channel of the contagion effect of restatements in our setting. We investigate whether market participants become more uncertain about a firm's disclosure credibility following a restatement announcement by its alliance partner (the accounting quality concern channel of contagion). We also examine the characteristics of alliances as well as possible corporate actions non-restating firms may take with regards to their alliance formations to insulate themselves from potential negative contagion effects.

17501720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501720.value: The first two research objectives have led to the completion of the academic paper titled "ESG Should Be ES+G: Reassessing the Effect of Corporate Social Responsibility on Firm Performance after Negative Financial Events." The paper can be summarised as follows: We investigate the relationship between corporate social responsibility (henceforth, CSR) and short- and long-term firm performance after corporate scandals. Drawing on strategic CSR, relational contract, and psychological contract theories, we hypothesize that corporate citizenship and corporate governance aspects of CSR have opposite effects on the market reaction to financial restatements. Our empirical analysis reveals that firms with a strong reputation for corporate citizenship experience a smaller negative market response to restatements. Conversely, a firm’s reputation for corporate governance exacerbates the negative surprise triggered by restatements. Our analysis also shows that firms experience a long-term decrease in financial performance following restatements. It appears that a strong reputation for citizenship ameliorates the damaging effects of a corporate scandal, while governance reputation ranges between unrelated to damaging in different models. A key takeaway from our study is that mixing ES and G ratings to operationalize CSR obfuscates the role of corporate citizenship, which could lead to misleading estimates of the corporate “returns” to CSR. The last four research objectives have led to the completion of the academic paper titled "The Contagion Effect of Accounting Restatements on Strategic Alliance Partners." The paper can be summarised as follows: We investigate restatement contagion to strategic alliance partners, and we document a negative stock price reaction for non-restating firms whose alliance partners announce an accounting restatement. We find that a non-restating alliance partner can mitigate this contagion effect by having a diverse network of alliances and/or having termination clauses in their alliance contracts. However, in contrast to the findings of Boone and Ivanov (2012), we find that forming joint ventures instead of contractual alliances does not offer protection from negative spillover effects from alliance partners’ restatements. We also find empirical support for both the accounting quality concern (information risk) and the economic outlook revision (information updating) mechanisms of restatement contagion. Taken together, our findings indicate that, despite the limited quantitative disclosure about alliances and a decrease in information about production decisions for alliance participants (Kepler 2021), markets infer significant information about the contagion effects of restatements.

17501720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501720.value: A firm’s corporate social responsibility (CSR) is measured in terms of its activities in the environment, social, and governance (ESG) dimensions. Investment institutions often use a single all-encompassing ESG score to make investment decisions. Our first paper argues that the corporate citizenship (ES) aspect of CSR generates ‘relational reputation capital’ for the firm, while the corporate governance (G) aspect of CSR generates ‘transactional reputation capital’ for the firm. We find that these two types of reputation capital behave differently. Firms with higher levels of citizenship reputation experience a significantly less negative market reaction to restatement announcements, while the firm’s pre-restatement reputation of corporate governance exacerbates the negative surprise triggered by restatements. The value-saving (value-destroying) effect of corporate citizenship (corporate governance) is more prominent for fraudulent restatements. We advise practitioners to not combine the ES and G scores. Our second paper investigates restatement contagion to strategic alliance partners, and document a negative stock price reaction for non-restating firms whose alliance partners announce an accounting restatement. We find that a non-restating alliance partner can mitigate this contagion effect by having a diverse network of alliances and/or having termination clauses in their alliance contracts.

17501820.value: To present stylized facts on risk-free procyclicality, positive sovereign risk premium, and positive comovement between sovereign risk premium and term premium. To prove theoretically that a procyclical risk-free rate leads to a negative sovereign risk premium in the absence of any correlation in economic fundamentals, which is in inconsistent with the data. 17501820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501820.value: Default risk in emerging markets is one of the most fundamental risks in the international financial market. We summarize four stylized facts that pose challenges to the existing literature: (i) Sovereign spreads are higher than the realized default frequency; (ii) The US risk-free rate is procyclical with respect to output and consumption growth; (iii) Sovereign spreads have higher correlation than the economic fundamentals; and (iv) Sovereign spreads are high when the real term premium in the US is high. We show that stylized facts (i) and (ii) constitute a a problem for a large class of models. We prove theoretically that the procyclical risk-free rate implies a negative sovereign risk premium. The sovereign bond payoff increases in low risk-free rate states because it is easier to roll over the debt. In these states, investors' marginal value of wealth is high, as suggested by fact (ii). Therefore, the emerging market sovereign bond provides insurance to the US investors. They are willing to hold these sovereign bonds at a lower return. We term this mechanism the ``risk-free rate channel". This implication is inconsistent with fact (i). Moreover, fact (iii) rules out a simple solution to the problem that the economic fundamentals are highly correlated. Analogously, a similar logic also applies to long-term bonds. Long-term bond prices increases in low risk-free rate states, which the long-term bond a hedge. Fact (iv) further validates the risk-free rate channel in both sovereign bond and long-term bond markets. The goal of our study is to quantify the risk-free rate channel. We examine the importance of this channel in two models of sovereign risk premia: consumption habit formation and long-run risk. We show that the risk-free rate channel generates a sizable negative risk premium and thus reduces the quantitative power of these models. Finally, we propose two resolutions---taste shock and convenience yield--- to accommodate the our four stylized facts. We provide additional evidence in support of each of these resolutions.

17501820.label: Realisation of objectives
17501820.value: We show that interest rate cyclicality is an important factor that should be accounted for when examining the relation between world interest rate and sovereign spread. In additional to the original objectives, we use structural VAR to identify two shocks that drive world interest rate, one is countercyclical and one is procyclical. We show that these two shocks have distinct effects on EM sovereign spread. We use a canonical structural sovereign default model to quantify these relations and study the contribution of default probability, risk premia and convenience yield in sovereign spread. As for the research objectives, we move beyond only showing stylized facts about interest rate cyclicality, as stated in objective 1. We utilize more sophisticated econometric method of structural VAR to construct two structural shocks with different cyclicalities. Objective 2 is achieved through a theoretical proof (see the midterm report) but we do not include it in the paper as it does not fit the flow of the paper very well. Objective 3 is achieved by examining the different response of sovereign spread to the two procyclical and countercyclical world interest rate shocks. Objective 4 is achieved through a quantitative model. For Objective 5, we include the convenience yield into the model and shows it does account for a significant fraction of spread change in the model. Taste shock is not included because it does not help the model fit the data. For Objective 6, we use the bond-CDS basis as a model-free measure of convenience yield and discipline the model with such additional evidence.

17501820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501820.value: We study the world interest rate drivers of sovereign spreads in emerging markets. With a structural VAR, we identify the procyclical and countercyclical shocks that differentially impact world interest rate, US output, emerging market output, sovereign spread, and sovereign bond wedge. These shocks suggest substantial risk premia for sovereign bonds, which vary with world interest rates and exhibit considerable cross-country dispersion. A model with structural shocks quantitatively explains the effect of interest rates on sovereign default. The model indicates a higher correlation between spreads than between outputs. Our findings highlight the importance of distinguishing the various drivers of world interest rates that impact sovereign spreads in distinct ways.

17501820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501820.value: 1. There is still room for improvement in terms of finding quantitative models of sovereign debt that can further account for how world interest rate affects sovereign spread. 2. It will be interesting to study how world interest rate or global financial factors affect the creditor composition of EM sovereign debt.

17501820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501820.value: The world interest rate is considered as an important factor for the debt issued by emerging market economies (EMEs). A higher interest rate means higher debt burden and thus increases the likelihood of default, raising the cost of borrowing for EMEs. We show that the source of world interest rate fluctuations matter. If a world interest rate rise is associated with good news in the US economy, it is also likely that it brings good news to the EME. On the contrary, if a world interest rate rise is associated with bad news in the US economy, the EME is hurt as well. In terms of default incentive, two forces are at play: higher debt burden and bad economic conditions. In this paper we empirically prove the hypothesis and study the different implications of these two different types of interest rate shocks in a quantitative model. Particularly, we disentangle the impact of world interest rate shocks on default probability, sovereign risk premia and a sovereign bond wedge that may likely reflect the constraint faced by global investors.

17502020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502020.value: Foreign exchange (FX) markets are the largest asset markets with an average daily trading volume of more than USD 5 trillion. This exceeds tenfold the trading volume of US stocks. FX investors earn high expected returns and the currency carry trade significantly outperforms stock markets. At the same time, it is common practice among international firms to hedge exchange rate risk exposures. Moreover, central banks’ decisions to intervene in FX markets have far-reaching consequences. During the Asian financial crisis in 1997 several currencies were under attack which led to significant devaluations after central banks were no longer able to sustain currency pegs to the USD. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority undertook costly interventions to keep the HKD pegged to the USD. More recently in 2013 investors were worried when Bernanke announced the end of the Federal Reserve’s quantitative easing program, which led to a sell-off in emerging markets. Thus, it is important to understand the economic forces in FX markets. Unfortunately, FX market risks are not well understood, and traditional asset pricing models cannot capture many important empirical facts (Fama, 1984; Backus and Smith, 1993; Brandt et al., 2006). Many international finance puzzles arise because pricing is determined by aggregate consumption growth in traditional models. We use a model with cohort-specific endowment shocks and limited inter-cohort risk sharing (Garleanu and Panageas, 2019). Pricing is determined by cohort-specific consumption growth, which differs from aggregate consumption growth per capita. This allows us to resolve many puzzles. Our insight is that cohort-specific risks are important for pricing, but these risks are absent in traditional models due to too much aggregation. Although long run risk (and other) models also address the same puzzles (Colacito and Croce, 2011), the challenge in these models is that the state variables are latent. The difficulty in quantifying the main economic force is a major problem. For instance, unobservable state variables limit the ability to forecast economic quantities and guide policy decisions. In contrast, the state variables in our model can be estimated in the data (Garleanu and Panageas, 2019). Our objective is to demonstrate the theoretical and empirical importance of cohort-specific endowment shocks to explain FX market risks. Moreover, we test whether shocks in certain countries are more relevant than in other countries. This has important implications for future research and provides guidance for policy, investment, and hedging decisions. 外匯（FX）市場是最大的資產市場，平均每日交易量超過5萬億美元，是美國股票交易量的十倍以上。外匯投資者獲得很高的預期回報，而且貨幣套利交易的表現明顯優於股票市場。同時，國際公司普遍會為匯率風險進行對沖。再者，中央銀行干預外匯市場的決定具有深遠的影響。在1997年的亞洲金融危機期間，由於一些中央銀行無法再維持與美元掛鈎機制，幾種貨幣受到了攻擊，導致貨幣大幅貶值。香港金融管理局採取了成本高昂的干預措施，以保持港元與美元掛鈎。較近期的例子發生於2013年，當伯南克宣布結束美國聯邦儲備局的量化寬鬆計劃，導致新興市場遭到拋售，投資者對此感到擔憂。因此，了解外匯市場的經濟力量很重要。 可惜，外匯市場風險尚未得到很好的理解，還有傳統資產定價模型無法反映許多重要的經驗事實 (Fama, 1984; Backus and Smith, 1993; Brandt et al., 2006)。因定價由傳統模型中的總消費增長決定，於是衍生了許多國際金融難題。本研究使用具有特定群組的稟賦衝擊和有限跨群組風險分擔的模型 (Garleanu and Panageas, 2019)。 定價取決於特定群組的消費增長，這與人均總消費增長不同。 這模型為我們解決了許多難題。 我們認為針對特定群組的風險對於定價很重要，但是由於匯總過多，傳統模型無法計算這些風險。 儘管長期風險(及其他)模型也解決了同樣的難題 (Colacito and Croce, 2011)，然而這些模型面臨的挑戰為狀態變數是潛在的， 因此難以量化主要經濟推動力是這類模型的一個重要問題。 例如，不可觀察的狀態變限制了預測經濟量和指引決定政策的能力。然而相較之下，我們的模型可以由數據估算狀態變數 (Garleanu and Panageas, 2019)。 我們旨在證明特定群組的稟賦衝擊在理論上和經驗上對解釋外匯市場風險的重要性。 此外，我們測試了某些國家的這些衝擊是否比起其他國家更重要。這對未來的研究具有重要參考作用，並為政策、投資和對沖決策提供指引。

17502020.label: Realisation of objectives
17502020.value: Please note that the original objectives have been revised, and this change was approved. In the following I will only refer to the revised objectives. Objectives 1 & 2: We have set up a model and have obtained solutions up to a system of PDEs. We have numerically solved the model, and came to the realization that the extended version of our model (which includes endogenous migration) has counter-factual implications. Specifically, in our two country model we can only match the price-earnings ratio of one economy to the data, while the endogenous migration results in a counter-factual price-earnings ratio in the other economy. We found this problem can only be overcome in a simpler version of our model where there is no endogenous migration, and instead the population composition is specified exogenously. In addition, we noticed that numerical solutions can be unstable depending on the parameterization of the model. We are now using the approach introduced by Garleanu and Panageas (2019) to reverse engineer the PDEs. . Objectives 3: We have collected the relevant data as outlined in the original proposal. We have explored the data and the relevant international asset pricing puzzles. This analysis led to interesting and novel empirical findings. In particular, we were studying the time-series variation in conditional currency return moments. This led to a somewhat new paper (but still related to the original proposal). The title of the finished paper is “Dollar and Carry Redux” and it is co-authored with Sining Liu, Andrea Vedolin and Yaoyuan Zhang. Contrary to existing literature, in this paper we establish that two factors, dollar and carry, suffice to explain a large cross-section of currency returns with R-squares exceeding 80%. Our paper highlights the importance of accounting for time-series variation in conditional risk loadings and premia. Unconditional estimations that ignore this time-series variation mistakenly reject the two-factor model. We propose a parsimonious framework to estimate conditional currency factor models and provide testable restrictions. Other risk factors (than the Dollar and Carry) proposed in the literature do not span new dimensions in the risk space but they are useful to describe the time-series variation in dollar and carry factor risk loadings and premia. This is related and relevant for the originally proposed research project as this new empirical insights inform macro-finance models that (i) it suffices to identify two macro-risks that resemble the Dollar and Carry, but (ii) it is crucial that risk exposures are time-varying. We think it is important to address these features in macro-finance models since current models in the literature focus on unconditional moments and are not designed to match the novel time-series patterns.

17502020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502020.value: The contribution of our model to the literature is a novel economic channel to explain international finance puzzles. Due to intergenerational market incompleteness displacement risk is an important driver for pricing. Since the exchange rate is the ratio of country-specific stochastic discount factors (SDFs), then displacement risks across countries have important implications for FX markets. Intuitively, a country with more displacement risk has a more volatile SDF, leading to a lower interest rate (due to precautionary savings), a higher equity premium, and its currency appreciates in times of large disruptions. In addition, since displacement risk is not instantly affecting aggregate consumption growth (but rather affects the distribution of consumption within the economy), our channel naturally breaks the tight link between pricing and aggregate consumption growth. This means our model provides a potential resolution of the famous Backus-Smith puzzle. This is a novel economic channel that has not been studied in international finance. The recent advances in artificial intelligence is a particularly nice showcase. AI affects economies across the world, displacing certain groups in the economy, and arguably has a large impact on SDFs. This leads to interesting effects on the exchange rate between economies that differ with respect to the size of the technology sector and the potential disruption of AI on the overall economy. This is an interesting contribution to the literature, and in addition provides novel insights to understand the effects of the recent AI revolution on FX markets. Using the angle of AI further help to increase the visibility of our model. During the data exploration we have further identified novel empirical findings in the data and have written an empirical paper. The insights of this empirical paper are that expected returns in FX markets are described by only two factors, the Dollar and the Carry. However, contrary to the literature we show that the time-series variation in risk loadings and premia is crucial. Unconditional estimations that ignore this time-series variation (i.e., imposing constant factor loadings and premia) mistakenly reject the two-factor model. In contrast, a conditional estimation reveals that the two factor model explains the data very well. Accordingly, macro-finance models should focus on macro-risks that (i) are associated with the Dollar and Carry, and (ii) risk exposures have to be time-varying.

17502020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502020.value: The model provides novel theoretical insights. However, we have not done a serious estimation of the model implications in the data. It is worth to do so in future research. Second, it is promising to follow up on the empirical finding that currency returns are explained by the dollar and carry but that it is crucial to account for time-series variation in risk loadings and premia. In particular, macro-finance models in the literature are designed to match unconditional moments and properties of conditional moments are by and large ignored. A promising direction is to dig into the macro-finance literature and check which models can potentially match the time-series variation in conditional moments. If this is a major challenge for current models, then it would be interesting to explore how we can adjust these models to better explain the data.

17502020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502020.value: The main insight of the model is that new technologies lead to displacement of certain groups in the economy. This displacement risk differs across countries depending on the potential disruption of new technologies in each country. Given the differential effect across countries, there are important implications on the exchange rate between countries. A country with more exposure to technological disruptions and displacement risk features a lower interest rate (due to precautionary savings), a higher equity premium, and its currency appreciates in times of large disruptions. This is a novel economic channel that has not been studied in international finance. Finally, we show in an empirical analysis that we only need two risk factors, the Dollar and Carry, to explain risks and expected returns in FX markets. That is, these two risk sources subsume other factors that were introduced in the literature. We further document that there is a strong time-series variation in risks and premia. It is important to correctly account for this time-series variation to understand the trade-off between expected returns and risks. This is important to guide macro-finance models (such as the originally proposed project), inform central banks in monetary policy decisions, and investors.

17502320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502320.value: Many cities/communities across the globe operate online websites and/or billboards announcing the current waiting time at emergency departments (EDs) to see a doctor. This practice is carried out to help both potential ED patients and the EDs. If patients who are sensitive to waiting time and want quicker access to treatment are informed of the latest crowding situation at the potential destination facilities, they can make a better decision for themselves regarding which facility to go to. Meanwhile, this strategic behavior by waiting time sensitive patients can help EDs in the vicinity to balance their patient loads since patients will gravitate towards a less crowded ED, hence, reduce the patient load at more crowded ones. The motivation of announcing delay at EDs is based on a fundamental operations management principle of capacity pooling which can help service providers, EDs, facing uncertain demand, patient arrivals, to balance their load. However, the effectiveness of ED delay announcements in practice has not been studied much in both operations and emergency medicine literature. Even the few existing studies are limited to aggregate facility level analysis. In this proposal, we aim to empirically quantify the effectiveness of the ED waiting time announcement system in a representative community, Hong Kong. We will study whether and how individual ED patients incorporate the announced ED waiting times into their decision of choosing which ED to attend for emergent medical treatment. We will first compile a comprehensive patient level dataset which merges detailed patient level ED visit data with patient survey responses collected during their ED visit and ED waiting time data announced publicly via the website operated by Hospital Authority, Hong Kong’s healthcare governing body. The data will be collected from the three and only public hospital EDs on Hong Kong Island which can be considered as a closed ED network. Using a structural model of patients’ ED choice decision, we will estimate ED patients’ sensitivity to waiting time at the ED and travel time to the ED, then directly compare their magnitudes to understand the patients’ ED choice behavior. We will provide further policy implications for ED delay announcement systems in general by performing counterfactual analyses on the effectiveness of such systems under various system parameters. Our study contributes to the literature of queueing networks and customer behaviors in queues as well as emergency medicine. 全球許多城市或社區都會通過網站或公告牌預告當前在急診室（ED）的就診等待時間。這樣可以同時幫助潛在的急診室患者以及急診室本身的運作。如果患者對等待時間敏感並希望更快地就醫，他們知道可選的急診室的最新擁擠情況后就可以自行決定去哪個急診室就診是更好的選擇。與此同時，對等待時間敏感的患者的這種策略性行為可以幫助急診室平衡他們的患者負荷，因為患者將趨向於選擇相對不擁擠的急診室，從而減少了更擁擠的急診室的患者負荷。 急診室等待時間預告的研究動機是基本運營管理原則中對容量的合并管理。該原則可以幫助服務提供方（急診室）在面對不確定的需求（患者到達）時平衡他們的負荷。但是在運營和急診醫學文獻中，對急診室等待時間預告在實踐中的有效性並未進行太多研究。即使是少數的現有研究也僅限於對總體設施水平的分析。在這項研究中，我們旨在以實證研究的方式量化急診室等待時間預告系統在香港的有效性。我們將研究急診室患者個體是否以及如何將已預告的急診室等待時間納入他們選擇要接受急診治療的急診室的決定中。 我們將首先收集一個綜合的患者層面的數據庫，該數據庫將整合詳細的患者層面的急診室訪問數據，在其急診室訪問期間收集的患者調查回復以及通過香港醫療保健管理機構醫院管理局運營的網站公佈的急診室等待時間數據。數據將從香港島僅有的三個公立醫院急診室收集，這可以被視為一個封閉的急診室網絡。 通過使用患者急診室選擇決策的結構模型，我們將估算急診室患者對急診室等待時間和到急診室的行程時間的敏感性，然後直接比較其量級以理解患者的急診室選擇行為。我們將在各種系統參數下對此類系統的有效性進行虛擬事實分析，從而對急診室延時預告系統提供更多的策略支持。這項研究將會對排隊網絡、排隊顧客行為以及急診醫學領域做出貢獻。

17502420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17502420.value: 在采购商与供应商产品共创中的能力不对称与创新绩效：一个双边及动态的视角

17502420.label: Project Objectives
17502420.value: To develop a dyadic view of technological capability in buyer-supplier product co-development. Reasons: In buyer-supplier exchanges, product co-development refers to the involvement of the supplier in the buyer’s innovation development (Wang, Li, and Chang 2016). As the supplier provides important and complementary resources and technologies, product co-development becomes a critical way to foster innovation (Rindfleisch and Moorman 2003; Ulaga and Eggert 2006; Wang et al. 2017). Despite the emerging interest in the role of buyer-supplier collaboration in new product development, prior studies predominately adopt a single-sided view from either the buyers (e.g., Fang 2008) or the suppliers (e.g., Yan, Ribbink, and Pun 2018). Because both buyers and suppliers provide valuable and diverse insights and know-how that can inform novel products, they act as interdependent agents that stimulate value co-creation (Dong and Sivakumar 2017; Vargo and Lusch 2004; Wang et al. 2017). However, because buyers and suppliers often differ in their resources and capabilities, it is crucial to take a dyadic approach to examine such asymmetric effects in buyer-supplier collaboration (Lumineau and Oliveira 2018; McEvily, Zaheer, and Kamal 2017; Villena and Craighead 2017). Solutions: This project takes a dyadic view to investigate the role of partner capabilities in buyer-supplier product co-development. We focus on technological capability (TC) because of its pivotal role in innovation development. To better capture dyadic capability, we use the absolute value of buyer TC minus supplier TC to indicate asymmetric TC, and use the sum of buyer TC and supplier TC to reflect joint TC, the total TC intensity in the relationship. To develop a dynamic view to understand how joint TC and asymmetric TC affect innovation performance in buyer-supplier product co-development. Reasons: Exchange relationships are dynamic. As business relationships evolve and performance changes over time, capability likely has dynamic implications on innovation since it takes time for business parties to develop the cooperation process and respond accordingly (Narayandas and Rangan 2004; Palmatier et al. 2013; Zhang et al. 2016). However, prior studies are mostly cross-sectional and examine the immediate association of capability and innovation performance (e.g., Wang, Jin, and Zhou 2019; Zhou and Wu 2010), which limits our understanding of the underlying mechanisms through which asymmetric capability affects the consequent innovation and the change in innovation performance over time. Solutions: We will examine how joint TC and asymmetric TC differentially influence knowledge co-creation and cooperation continuity, and in turn, subsequent innovation performance and the change in innovation performance. To understand the contingent values of joint TC and asymmetric TC in product co-development. Reasons: Prior studies have well recognized that the value of capabilities is contingent on external environments such as industry types as well as firm-level features such as business type and firm size (see Krasnikov and Jayachandran 2008 for a review), yet we know little about what factors moderate the effect of asymmetric capability. For example, in emerging markets such as China, firms face strong challenges from institutional voids, such as the lack of intellectual property right (IPR) protection (Zhou, Gao, and Zhao 2017). Such environmental factors, as well as exchange-related features, are potential moderators that deserve further investigation. Solutions: We will assess the moderating roles of environmental factors (i.e., IPR protection and technological turbulence) and exchange features (i.e., goal compatibility and task complexity) on the relationships between joint/asymmetric TC and knowledge co-creation/cooperation continuity. We plan to test our propositions using a longitudinal survey of manufacturers (buyers) and their suppliers in China.

17502420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502420.value: With the rise of open innovation, buyer (manufacturer)-supplier collaboration becomes an increasingly important source of innovation. For example, Huawei cooperates with its screen supplier, Boe Technology, to develop the flexible display for its foldable smartphone Mate X. Geely, a Chinese automobile company, with the help of its global supplier Siemens, developed a new mid-end brand for the global market. However, the product co-development process is also full of dispute and conflict between partners, making two questions salient in this context: (1) With whom is it beneficial to cooperate? (2) How can better innovation performance be achieved in product co-development? Despite the emerging interest in this topic, prior studies predominately adopt a single-sided view from the focal firm. Whereas both buyers and suppliers provide valuable and diverse insights and know-how that can inform novel products, they differ significantly in their capabilities. Therefore, it is crucial to take a dyadic approach to examine the effects of capability asymmetry on innovation outcomes. Moreover, exchange relationships are dynamic. As business relationships evolve and performance changes over time, capability likely has dynamic implications on innovation performance since it takes time for partners to form the cooperation process and respond accordingly. However, prior studies are mostly cross-sectional and examine the immediate association of capability and innovation. To address these research gaps, our project take a dyadic and dynamic view to investigate the relationships between capability asymmetry and innovation performance in buyer-supplier exchanges in China. We focus on technological capability (TC) because of its pivotal role in innovation development. To better capture dyadic capability, we use the absolute value of buyer TC minus supplier TC to indicate asymmetric TC, and use the sum of buyer TC and supplier TC to reflect joint TC, the total TC intensity in the relationship. We examine three research questions: 1. How do joint TC and asymmetric TC differentially affect knowledge co-creation and cooperation continuity, and in turn innovation performance? 2. How do environmental factors such as intellectual property right (IPR) protection and technological turbulence moderate the effects of joint TC and asymmetric TC? 3. How do exchange features such as goal compatibility and task complexity moderate the effects of joint TC and asymmetric TC? By addressing these questions, our results will enrich the product co-development literature and provide important managerial implications on whom to partner with and how to deal with capability asymmetry and achieve better innovation performance in China. 随着开放式创新的发展，采购商与供应商之合作日益成为创新之重要源泉。例如，华为与其屏幕供应商，博尔科技，为其可折叠智能手机共同开发了柔性屏。汽车制造商吉利与其供应商西门子为全球市场共同开发了中端品牌。但是，产品共创过程亦充满了争议与冲突，导致了两大问题：（1）与谁合作最有益？（2）如何在产品共创中取得更好创新绩效？ 尽管对此问题的兴趣日益增加，以往研究皆是采用焦点公司的单边视角。但是，采购商与供应商在其能力上区别甚大，所以我们必须从双边视角来研究能力不对称对创新绩效的影响。此外，合作关系不断变化，合作伙伴之能力对创新绩效有动态的影响。 但以往文献大多用截面数据来研究能力对创新的作用。 为解决这些问题，我们将采用一个双边及动态的视角来研究在采购商与供应商产品共创中的能力不对称与创新绩效的关系。我们将聚焦在科技能力，并以采购商与供应商的科技能力差额的绝对值来代表能力不对称，并以采购商与供应商的科技能力之和来代表能力总额。研究问题如下： （1） 能力总额与能力不对称如何影响知识共创及持续合作，进而影响创新绩效？ （2） 环境要素(产权保护与科技变化)如何调节能力总额与能力不对称的影响？ （3） 交易要素(目标一致性与任务复杂性)如何调节能力总额与能力不对称的影响？ 本项目的研究结果将丰富产品共创之文献，并对在华企业如何挑选合作伙伴及应对能力不对称以提高创新绩效提供重要的指导。

17502420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502420.value: Major findings: 1) Our study develops a dyadic CBV by conceptualizing collaboration partners’ capability as technology capability (TC) strength and TC asymmetry and empirically confirming their differential impacts on supply chain process innovation. 2) We find that TC strength can become a liability in the context of buyer–supplier process innovation and TC asymmetry can actually foster supply chain process innovation. 3) We further reveal the contingent roles of macro-level institutional factors. We find that, when they encounter government intervention, buyer-supplier partners need to recognize related challenges and adapt their practices, thus counteracting the liability associated with TC strength and diminishing the facilitative role of TC asymmetry on supply chain process innovation. 4) We also find that as guanxi importance strengthens attachment and social obligations between partners, it amplifies the roles of TC strength and asymmetry on supply chain process innovation.. Outcome: four papers published in peer-reviewed journals. 1) Wang L, JL Jin, KZ Zhou (2023), “Technological Capability Strength/Asymmetry and Supply Chain Process Innovation: The Contingent Roles of Institutional Environments,” Research Policy, 52 (4): 104724. 2) Lumineau F, JL Jin, S Sheng, KZ Zhou (2022), “Asset Specificity Asymmetry and Supplier Opportunism in Buyer–Supplier Exchanges,” Journal of Business Research, 149: 85-100. 3) Wang M, S Sheng, KZ Zhou (2022), “Fairness asymmetry, changes in mutual trust, and supplier performance in buyer–supplier exchanges in China: A dyadic view,” Industrial Marketing Management, 106: 14-30. 4) Wang M, KZ Zhou, X Bai, J Li (2024), "Trust asymmetry and changes in supplier opportunism: An institutional contingency view," Journal of Business Research, 174: 114537

17502420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502420.value: Although we highlight the distinctiveness between supply chain process innovation and product innovation, we empirically examine only the former. One potential way is to simultaneously examine supply chain product and process innovation so as to fully identify their differences.

17502420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502420.value: This project examines how technology capability (TC) strength and asymmetry between buyers and suppliers affects supply chain process innovation in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) While TC strength reduces supply chain process innovation, TC asymmetry actually improves supply chain process innovation. Thus, exchange partners should fully utilize the positive impact of TC asymmetry on supply chain process innovation. 2) Supply chain partners should pay special attention to salient institutional factors, which vary significantly across regions in China. In particular, when they experience extensive or intrusive government intervention, supply chain partners should know that TC strength becomes less of a liability while TC asymmetry also becomes less useful for promoting supply chain process innovation. 3) When guanxi is important, TC strength may erect even higher barriers against supply chain process innovation. To facilitate process innovation, partners may need to address the inertia and inaction caused by TC strength by keeping their minds open to external information and avoiding relational over-embeddedness. Meanwhile, partners need to fully utilize TC asymmetry to stimulate supply chain process innovation.

17502820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502820.value: Social network analysis has been widely applied in business and economics research. One of the important and growing applications in organizational studies is to quantify the social proximity between two firms. Prior studies in the literature have adopted and defined a variety of social proximity measures depending on research context and data availability. These measures often focus on one type of personal or social relations only (e.g., alumni, friends, colleagues, ethnic origins) and do not fully utilize the abundant information available in the broad network of firms and individuals. This research proposes a new and generalizable social proximity measure that is multi-dimensional and can take into account different types of network relationships at the same time. The construction of the proposed measure is achieved through knowledge graph embedding, which is to model the entities and relations of a knowledge graph in continuous vector spaces. To validate the new measure, we investigate whether and how it is associated with prior social proximity measures in the context of corporate venture capital investment. We also demonstrate its value in the task of recommending potential portfolio companies for different corporate venture capitalists and conduct experiments to evaluate whether the new social proximity measure contains additional information that helps improve the recommendation accuracy. This research will make an important methodology contribution to the social network literature and introduce a new social proximity measure that can be easily adopted by future organizational studies in business and economics. 社交網絡分析已廣泛應用於商業和經濟學研究中。組織行為學研究中一個重要且越來越普遍的應用是量化兩家公司之間的社交接近度。先前的研究根據研究背景和數據可用性已經採用並定義了多種社交接近度的量化方法。這些方法通常只關註一種類型的社交關係（例如，校友，朋友，同事，民族血統等），而沒有充分利用廣泛的公司和個人網絡中存在的大數據信息。這項研究提出一種新的並可以廣泛應用的社交接近度的量化方法，它可以同時考慮到不同類型的多維網絡關係。新的量值的構建是通過知識圖譜嵌入實現的，該方法將知識圖譜中的實體和關係放在連續向量空間中進行建模。為了驗證這個新量值，我們在企業風險資本投資這個應用背景下，調查研究該量值與先前研究提出的社交接近度是否以及如何相關聯。我們還在為不同的企業風險資本家推薦潛在投資標的這個任務中衡量新方法的價值，並進行實驗以評估新的社交接近度指標是否包含有助於提高推薦準確性的額外信息。這項研究將對社交網絡文獻做出重要的方法論貢獻。它提出了一種新的社交接近度的量化方法，可以很容易地被未來的商業和經濟學研究所採用。

17502820.label: Realisation of objectives
17502820.value: We conducted two studies to achieve the four objectives outlined in the research proposal. In the first study, we developed a novel social proximity measure called "entity proximity," which is more powerful and flexible as it can consider multiple types of entities and relations simultaneously. This measure was constructed using a knowledge graph embedding approach, specifically the advanced TransR method. The social proximity measure was defined as the cosine similarity between the entity embeddings of two entities. A key advantage of TransR is its ability to represent an entity in different roles by projecting it onto various relational spaces, which aligns with the idea that a focal entity should have distinct identities in different social contexts. Consequently, "entity proximity" can capture similarities between two entities across diverse social relations simultaneously. To validate this social proximity measure, we designed a series of empirical analyses to examine its characteristics and effectiveness in real-world applications, specifically venture capital investment. The venture capital industry, which has garnered significant academic interest, serves as an ideal testbed for network-based measures due to its wide range of social interactions among individuals and organizations. We constructed a heterogeneous network representing social interactions and attributes among venture capitalists, start-ups, individuals, ethnic origins, and educational institutions. Through correlation and regression analyses, we demonstrated that entity proximity can effectively capture social closeness between entities across different relations. In the second study, we leveraged information on various relationships among players in the venture capital industry, particularly individuals' social connections, to develop a novel start-up recommendation framework called SocioLink. We constructed a venture capital knowledge graph (KG) depicting connections among venture capitalists, start-ups, individuals, ethnicities, educational institutions, cities, and industries. To model the multi-relational data in the graph for recommendations, we adopted two different approaches: the graph embedding approach and the meta-path-based approach. We defined a social proximity score between a venture capitalist and a start-up, indicating the probability of one entity having a specific type of relation with another given the observed connectivity patterns in the KG. To showcase the practical value of relation-based models, we conducted experiments demonstrating that our SocioLink method identifies more successful actual investment targets than benchmark methods. This suggests that investors can save time and effort in searching for start-ups while also achieving greater financial gains using our approach. Furthermore, we developed a web-based prototype for start-up recommendations based on the SocioLink framework, which generates a list of promising start-up candidates for a venture capitalist after they input their name. These visualizations aim to help investors better understand the underlying logic behind each recommendation and their connections with other entities.

17502820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502820.value: Our proposed social proximity measure, entity proximity, is distinct from existing measures as it can simultaneously consider heterogeneous relationships when assessing the social closeness between two entities. Validated within the context of the U.S. venture capital industry, entity proximity not only offers a more accurate and comprehensive assessment of social closeness by considering various relations, but also exhibits the highest predictive power in determining the likelihood of forming a business partnership between a venture capitalist and a startup, compared to existing measures. As a powerful tool for assessing social proximity, entity proximity can facilitate future research across various disciplines. This first study was published in the International Conference on Information Systems in 2020. Utilizing data from CrunchBase, we found that the performance of the SocioLink framework surpasses that of several state-of-the-art startup recommendation models. Our research is among the first to propose and validate the value of relational information, particularly individuals' social relations, which are often publicly available across numerous industries, in designing a two-sided recommendation model. This second study was published in the Journal of Management Information Systems in 2023.

17502820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502820.value: The successful development of the entity proximity measure and the SocioLink framework presents significant potential for further research and practical applications. As entity proximity effectively assesses social closeness considering heterogeneous relationships, it can be extended to various disciplines, enhancing the understanding of complex social structures and interactions. Future work could explore the application of this measure in other industries and contexts to study the impact of social closeness on decision-making processes. Moreover, the promising results of the SocioLink framework in venture capital investment demonstrate the value of relational information in designing two-sided recommendation models. This study opens the door for further development of recommendation systems that incorporate social relations in other sectors where such information is publicly available. It is also worth investigating how to integrate other data sources and types to refine the recommendations. In addition, researchers could explore the potential of machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to advance the capabilities of the SocioLink framework and related models. To capitalize on these research opportunities, the proposed course of action involves collaboration with industry partners, data collection from diverse sources, and continuous refinement of the proposed measures and models, ensuring their relevance and applicability in real-world scenarios.

17502820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502820.value: This research project focuses on improving the way we measure social closeness between two entities in various business contexts, such as venture capital investment. Current methods are limited and cannot effectively support applications in complex networks. To address this issue, the researchers developed a new measure called "Entity Proximity," which uses a knowledge graph embedding approach to consider different types of relationships and entities at the same time. This allows for a more accurate and comprehensive assessment of social closeness, ultimately helping businesses make better decisions. To test the effectiveness of Entity Proximity, the researchers applied it to the US venture capital context and found that it outperformed existing measures in predicting the likelihood of forming a business partnership between a venture capital firm and a startup. Additionally, they developed a framework called SocioLink, which uses machine learning to analyze various relations in a knowledge graph. This framework showed significant improvements in accuracy and quality compared to other startup recommendation methods. Overall, this research contributes to the development of better tools for assessing social proximity and decision support in business contexts, particularly in the venture capital industry.

17502920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502920.value: Recently, the possibility of increasing monopoly power in the United States and other countries has been a heated topic in policy debates. A wave of new research using both micro and macro data shows that industry concentration, firm profits and markups have been rising, at least in the United States. However, researchers still do not have a complete picture of the underlying causes of the phenomenon and the explanations for the differential trends across industries. At the same time, there has been rapid globalization in the past few decades. Large firms are more likely to export to foreign markets and to import cheaper intermediate inputs. This project investigates the role of globalization in the rise of industry concentration and markups, with a special focus on the sourcing of foreign inputs. For researchers and policymakers, it is crucial to understand the underlying causes of these trends. As discussed in Syverson (2019), higher concentration, profits and markups do not necessarily indicate higher market power. On the contrary, higher concentration sometimes suggests stronger competition or more efficient production. In the case of foreign input sourcing, large firms overcome the fixed costs of sourcing and get access to cheap inputs. Therefore, globalization benefits the large firms more and may increase industry concentration. However, it may lead to higher welfare because it improves the production efficiency of a group of firms. The current project aims at understanding the mechanisms connecting input sourcing and industry concentration. It will contribute to policy making on regulating large firms, which indirectly affects individuals, firms, and the overall equitable growth of the society. 在美国和其他国家，近来政策讨论中的一个热门话题是企业垄断力量的增强。一系列运用微观和宏观数据的新研究表明，至少在美国，行业集中度、公司利润和加价幅度都有所上升。但是，研究人员仍然完全了解这一现象的根本原因，也未能完全解释各行业的差异趋势。与此同时，过去几十年全球化进程十分迅速。在全球化的趋势下，大公司更有可能向国外出口以及进口便宜的中间投入品。本项目旨在研究行业集中度和价格上涨与全球化的内在联系，特别关注进口中间投入品这一机制。 对于研究人员和政策制定者来说，了解导致行业集中度上升的根本原因至关重要。正如Syverson（2019）所述，更高的集中度，利润和加价幅度不一定表示更高的市场支配力。相反，集中度更高有时表明竞争加剧或更有效的生产。以购买国外中间投入品为例，大公司可以克服采购的固定成本并获得廉价的投入。全球化会使大公司受益更多，并且增加行业集中度。但是，它也可能同时提高福利，因为它可以改善一部分企业的生产效率。当前项目旨在了解进口中间投入品和行业集中度的联系机制。它将有助于制定大公司的监管政策。这间接影响到个人，公司和社会的整体公平增长。

17503420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17503420.value: 视频广告中动画移动速度如何影响消费者的回应：一个情感反应的视角

17503420.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17503420.value: Prof Wan, Echo Wen Prof Yang, Sha

17503420.label: Project Objectives
17503420.value: Due to advances in telecommunication technologies, video advertising plays an increasingly crucial role in marketing communications (Teixeira, Wedel, and Pieters 2012). Vivid product animations and brand logo animations are commonly employed on websites to attract consumers’ attention. In-stream video ads and in-app video ads frequently appear before, during, or after consumers watch videos, use apps, or play games. On Instagram, more ads are featured with videos than static images (Vrountas 2018). Undoubtedly, videos have become an important medium through which consumers learn about the outside world (Kim and Lakshmanan 2015; Roggeveen, Grewal, Townsend, and Krishnan 2015), as evidenced by the fact that YouTube now serves as the second-largest search engine (Wagner 2017). In response to these trends, spending on digital video advertising among major global brands has increased by more than 50 percent in recent years (Marvin 2018). Nevertheless, compared with the increasing prevalence of video ads in daily life, our understanding of how dynamic visual components of video ads can shape consumer responses is still limited. In video ads, various entities (e.g., products, brand logos, and other visual elements in the background) can be animated to move in a dynamic manner. The main objective of the proposed project is to develop a comprehensive theoretical framework to better understand how the speed of animated movements as a major, salient, and unique dynamic visual cue can systematically impact consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity. Theoretically, the proposed project aims to contribute to the visual marketing literature broadly and generate more insights into research on product display in particular. Over the past two decades, product display research has mainly focused on how “static” features influence product evaluation (Patrick 2016). Yet, none of these “static” factors, such as display location and position (Chae and Hoegg 2013; Chae, Li, and Zhu 2013; Cian, Krishna, and Schwarz 2015; Deng and Kahn 2009; Janiszewski 1990; Sundar and Noseworthy 2014), display orientation (Deng, Kahn, Unnava, and Lee 2016; Elder and Krishna 2012; Peracchio and Meyers-Levy 2005), camera angle (Meyers-Levy and Peracchio 1992; Yang, Zhang, and Peracchio 2010), and color (Hagtvedt and Brasel 2017; Lee, Deng, Unnava, and Fujita 2014; Lee, Fujita, Deng, and Unnava 2017), is uniquely related to movements of products and brand logos in video ads. More recently, product display research has started to shift focus from “static” visual cues to “dynamic” visual cues. We join this endeavor to advance our understanding of the effects of dynamic visual cues. All movements, regardless of their specific natures, occur at a certain speed. Whereas recent studies have explored several factors related to the specific natures of movements, such as direction (Hsee, Tu, Lu, and Ruan 2014), pattern (Kim and Lakshmanan 2015), and animacy (Brasel and Hagtvedt 2016), research on movement speed has been scant. One exception is the work of Morewedge, Preston, and Wegner (2007) who examine how the movement speed of robots affects observers’ perception. Unlike Morewedge, Preston, and Wegner (2007) who focus on entities that are able to move on their own power sources in reality and thus for which movement speed is an inherently relevant and objectively informative attribute, in the proposed project we focus on entities that are not able to move spontaneously in reality but animated to move freely and lively in video ads (e.g., audio speakers and brand logos). For these immobile entities, animated movement speed is merely a visual effect and thus actually does not carry substantive meanings. Yet, we will demonstrate that animated movement speed as an objectively irrelevant visual cue can produce a systematic and substantial impact on consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity. With this unique focus, the proposed project will further broaden the scope of the emerging research on dynamic visual cues. Managerially, the proposed project aims to provide highly actionable implications for marketers and graphic designers on increasing the effectiveness of video ads. Specifically, we propose that a fast animated movement speed will enhance consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity when the entity is moving in a predictable pattern, whereas consumers’ evaluation of a fast-moving entity will become unfavorable when the entity is moving in an unpredictable manner. Marketers and graphic designers can directly apply our findings to the practice of video ad creation by setting an either fast or slow animated movement speed according to whether they would like to present the animated movement in a predictable or a less predictable manner. We further enrich our theoretical framework by proposing that the aforementioned speed × predictability interaction effect on consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity will be even stronger when consumers watch video ads on touch devices, when products involve a high level of utility uncertainty, and when consumers watch video ads in crowded environments. The identification of these facilitating conditions further strengthens the managerial implications of the proposed project.

17503420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503420.value: Digital ads, such as pop-up, in-stream, and in-app ads, often display video content. Despite the increasing prevalence of video ads, research on how dynamic visual factors can shape consumer responses has been scant until recently. In video ads, various entities, including products, brand logos, and other visual components in the background, can be animated to move spontaneously. We examine how an entity’s animated movement speed can exert a systematic impact on consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity presented in video ads. We propose that the speed of the animated movement will interact with the predictability of the movement pattern in influencing consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity. Specifically, we expect that a fast animated movement speed will lead to a favorable evaluation of the focal moving entity due to an induced feeling of fluency when the entity is moving in a predictable pattern, whereas the same fast animated movement speed will elicit an unfavorable evaluation of the focal moving entity due to an induced feeling of anxiety when the entity is moving in an unpredictable manner. We further predict that our proposed speed × predictability interaction effect on consumers’ evaluation of the focal moving entity will be even stronger when consumers watch video ads on touch devices, when products involve a high level of utility uncertainty, and when consumers watch video ads in crowded environments. The proposed research aims to make theoretical contributions to the visual marketing and product display literatures. Whereas prior research has focused on how displayed movement speed may affect consumers’ perception from an inference-making perspective, we examine the impacts of animated movement speed from an affective reaction perspective and identify feelings of fluency and anxiety as two opposing speed-driven affective reactions that jointly explain consumers’ evaluation of a fast-moving entity. We further develop a comprehensive theoretical framework to gain a more nuanced understanding of the proposed animated speed effects. The proposed research will also provide highly actionable implications for marketers by examining marketing-relevant consequences of the speed of animated movements, which can be easily controlled by marketers. We offer suggestions regarding how marketers should tailor the speed of animated movements according to specific movement patterns during the video ad creation stage in order to elicit positive consumer responses. In terms of the scopes of dynamic visual cues, our findings cover not only animated movement speeds but also other dynamic visual cues, such as moving directions. In terms of domains of moving entities, our research not only examines traditional contexts (e.g., advertising) for which dynamic visual cues are prevalent, but also extends the investigations into novel contexts of price discounts and online review ratings, in which dynamic visual cues have played increasingly important roles. Animated movements are merely visual effects for brand logos, price discounts, and online review ratings. Thus, movements are objectively irrelevant visual cues for these entities.
