17503420.value: Supported by the GRF, the PI and collaborators have completed two projects and worked on two projects in progress, which examine various ways in which dynamic visual cues impact consumers’ responses. --The first project has been published in the Journal of Consumer Research (one of the top four journals in the field of marketing) in 2023: Jia, He (Michael), Echo Wen Wan, and Wanyi Zheng (2023), “Stars versus Bars: How the Aesthetics of Product Ratings ‘Shape’ Product Preference,” Journal of Consumer Research, 50 (1), 142–66. This paper shows that dynamic visual displays of online review ratings can effectively mitigate the perpetual bias that the shape of visual rating units (e.g., stars) induces in the process of preference formation when consumers examine online review ratings. --The second project has been prepared for journal submission: Jia, He (Michael), B. Kyu Kim, Wanyi Zheng, and Huachao Gao, "Seeing Sound from Silence: Enhancing the Effectiveness of Soundless Animated Product Images Through Triggering Auditory Imagery," working paper. This paper demonstrates that animated product images, though soundless, can trigger stronger auditory imagery and consequently lead to more favorable product evaluations than static product images when the motions displayed in the soundless images produce sounds in reality. --The third project is in progress of data collection: Jia, He (Michael), "Animated Movement Speed, Controllability, and Consumer Responses," research in progress. This project demonstrates that fast (vs. slow) animated movement speeds induce positive responses when the movements seem predictable and controllable, whereas fast (vs. slow) animated movement speeds induce negative responses when the movements seem unpredictable and uncontrollable. --The fourth project is in progress of data collection: Jia, He (Michael) and Zhengyu Shi, "Animated Movement Directions and Powerfulness Perceptions," research in progress. This project demonstrates that when a product is animated to move in a direction against (vs. along with) viewers’ dominant hand, the viewers perceive the product as more powerful. Such an effect manifests for male viewers only, who are more sensitive to the concept of power. Furthermore, the animated moving direction against one’s dominant hand improves product evaluation when the product is positioned as a powerful product. --In addition, the PI presented the major findings in the seminars at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Singapore Management University, Peking University, and Shanghai Jiaotong University and in leading international conferences, such as the Association for Consumer Research Annual Conference.

17503420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503420.value: First, the current GRF-supported projects have compared dynamic displays with static displays and examined speed and direction as two unique dynamic visual cues. Our future research will further expand the scope of dynamic visual cues to examine other variables (e.g., acceleration vs. deceleration, zooming in vs. zooming out) and investigate how the interplays between different dynamic visual cues affect consumers’ responses. Second, the current GRF-supported projects have examined how dynamic visual cues influence consumers’ evaluations of products, brand logos, and online review ratings. Serving as an important channel for consumers to receive information, digital platforms have become more heavily featured with various dynamic visual cues. Our future studies will expand the scope of research on dynamic displays across various digital platforms, for instance, examining how various dynamic displays of numerical information affect consumers’ perceptions and preferences. Third, the current GRF-supported projects have examined how several demographic variables, such as gender and age, influence consumers’ responses to dynamic visual cues. Our future research will further explore more managerially actionable variables that determine consumers’ responses to dynamic visual cues, which can facilitate targeting decisions and the design of the marketing mix to improve marketing effectiveness.

17503420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503420.value: The modern media channels and digital platforms are heavily featured with various types of dynamic visual cues—visual information related to actual or animated movements of products, brand logos, celebrities, and different forms of information. This GRF contributes to a deeper understanding of how various dynamic visual cues influence consumers’ responses. Theoretically, this GRF contributes to the growing visual marketing literature by examining the impacts of various types of dynamic visual cues (e.g., animated movement speeds, animated movement directions) and comparing the effectiveness of dynamic displays versus static displays of visual information. These impacts extend to various domains of marketing communications related to brand logos, foods, technological products, and online review ratings. The research findings generate novel theoretical insights and demonstrate that subtle and objectively irrelevant dynamic visual information can substantially affect consumers. Managerially, the findings from this GRF provide actionable implications for marketers and graphic designers. For instance, our findings suggest that when animating a product to move in a predictable manner, increasing the animated movement speed can lead to more favorable consumers’ responses. The findings of this GRF contribute to an effective guiding framework for managing and optimizing various dynamic visual cues in marketing communications.

17503520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503520.value: This research project attempts to provide an economic-based analysis to study the determinants of the optimal composition of a board and its impact on a CEO retention decision by the board. The proposed model emphasizes the board’s dual role of advising and monitoring a CEO as well as its decision to retain or replace the CEO so as to enhance the long-term shareholder value. In the model, the shareholders’ interests are well protected by the board in that the board contracts with a CEO to motivate him/her to generate a non-contractible short-term output and decides to keep or fire the incumbent CEO at an interim date based on a public accounting report about the short-term output and a private signal about the CEO’s ability, which is unknown and affects both the expected short-term output of the firm and its long-term prospect. The CEO also exerts an unobservable productive effort that affects the expected output and an unobservable manipulative effort that affects a contractible accounting outcome reflecting the firm’s output to be realized later. There are two types of board members — advisory and monitoring — and the composition of the board is chosen by the shareholders. While board advising assists the CEO to increase the expected output of the firm, board monitoring uncovers the earnings manipulation by the CEO. We want to show how the optimal composition of the board that maximizes shareholder value is determined and discuss its impact on the efficiency of the board’s CEO retention decision, which is measured by the expected total cost of undue CEO replacement and retention. We will also provide testable implications on how the optimal board composition, probabilities of accounting misstatements and CEO replacement (retention) despite having a good (bad) accounting report are related to firm, industry and market characteristics. We hope that this project will enhance our understanding about the determinants of the optimal composition of a board and provide novel empirical predictions that have yet been tested in literature. 本研究項目嘗試從經濟學的角度分析董事會最優組成的決定因素及其對董事會保留首席執行官決策的影響。我們提議的經濟模型強調了董事會在建議和監督首席執行官方面的雙重作用，以及其保留或更換首席執行官的決策對提高股東長期價值的影響。在該模型中，股東的利益受到董事會的良好保護。通過股東的授權，董事會與首席執行官簽約以激勵他/她產生不可合約的短期產出，並基於有關短期產出的公開會計報告和有關首席執行官能力的私人信息，作出中期保留或解僱現任首席執行官的決定，從而影響公司的長期前景。首席執行官一方面可施加無法觀察到的生產性努力，從而影響了預期的短期產出，另一方面可施加無法觀察到的操縱性工作，從而影響了有關短期產出的會計結果。董事會的組成由股東選擇，其成員分為兩種：諮詢和監督。董事會諮詢可以幫助首席執行官增加公司的預期產出，而董事會監督則可以防止首席執行官對會計結果的操縱。我們想透過此經濟模型展示股東價值最大化的董事會最優組成，並討論其對董事會首席執行官保留決策效率的影響，該影響可以通過過度更換和保留首席執行官的預期總成本來衡量。我們還將就最佳董事會組成，會計錯報和首席執行官更換的概率，與其行業和市場特徵之間的關係提供可驗證的假設。我們希望這個研究項目將增進我們對董事會最佳組成的決定因素的理解，並提供尚未在文獻中得到檢驗的新穎預測。

On November 16, 2022, we received the decision letter and one review report from the Journal of Accounting and Economics, inviting for revision and re-submission. After going through a substantial revision of the paper that addresses the comments and incorporates the suggestions from the editor and the reviewer, we resubmitted the paper to Journal of Accounting and Economics on October 22, 2023. On January 3, 2024, we received the final decision letter from the Journal of Accounting and Economics. While the reviewer still liked the main ideas of our paper, s/he still has concerns about whether contribution of our paper is substantial for publication in the Journal of Accounting and Economics. Unfortunately, the editor agreed and decided to reject the paper. Since the editor and the reviewer did not deny the importance of the research questions nor showed any serious concerns about any of the assumptions or results in the paper, we believe that the rejection decision was mostly based on personal preference. Incorporating some of the more positive and constructive suggestions from the reviewer and having the help from a professional copy editor to improve the readability of the paper, we have recently (June 24, 2024) submitted the paper to the Journal of Accounting Research, which is considered one of the top-tier journals in accounting. In term of the use of research funding, we had only used 2% of the fund during the whole project period, mainly for journal submission and copy editing fees. We did not use the research fund to attend overseas international conferences in the earlier period of the project because of the then travel restrictions. 17503520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503520.value: The results obtained in this paper titled “Board’s Dual Role of Advising and Monitoring CEOs, Earnings Management, and CEO Turnover Decisions” are summarized as follows: Abstract: We study the determinants of the optimal board composition and its relation to the CEO’s compensation, the quality of financial statements, and the CEO turnover decision from a lens of boards’ dual role of advising and monitoring CEOs. We find that the board composition affects the overall informativeness of accounting information as an assessment tool and the efficiency of related decisions. The central mechanism is that board advising makes a firm’s output more informative about the CEO’s effort and fit, whereas board monitoring plays an important role in enhancing the quality of financial reporting that reflects the firm’s output by mitigating manipulation. Our analyses shed light on cross sectional variation of board composition and its equilibrium association with the CEO’s compensation, the quality of financial statements, and the board’s CEO turnover decision across firms and industries (e.g., startups vs. established corporations, growth vs. value firms, CEO characteristics, etc.). Such findings provide novel empirical predictions.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503520.value: This paper contributes to the emerging literature on board structures by providing a theory of optimal board composition from a lens of boards’ dual role of advising and monitoring CEOs. Our model shows that the board composition affects the overall informativeness of accounting information that the board’s decisions on CEO compensation and turnover hinge on. While board advising renders a firm’s output more informative about the CEO’s effort and fit by complementing his effort and fit in improving firm productivity, board monitoring enhances financial reporting quality by mitigating misstatement. We first study how the board composition influences the informativeness of accounting information, the CEO’s compensation, and the CEO turnover. Then, we examine the optimal board composition and conduct comparative static analyses. We show that firms in early (mature) stages of development are more likely to have an adviser-heavy (monitor-heavy) board. Nevertheless, for early-stage (mature-stage) firms, the optimal level of the fraction of advisory board members decreases (increases) with the long-term benefit of having a CEO with a good fit relative to a bad fit and increases (decreases) with the quality of private information about the CEO’s fit.

17503720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503720.value: In the practice of procuring goods and services in the modern economy, sealed tenders are a widespread mechanism. A robust and well-documented feature in procurement auctions has received a lot of attention from empirical economists: barriers-to-entry. That is, not all eligible bidders choose to submit a bid, even though they have shown their potential interest in the auctioned object. This stylized observation suggests that entry into the auctions could be costly. But such a cost may further imply the entrants to the auctions are selective. Understanding the entry and selective effects in such a large and important market itself is a topic of general interest. The proposed project aims to investigate the impact of entrant selectivity in procurement practices. Economic models theoretically interpret the entry cost either as to information acquisition or as to bid submission. The key difference is whether at all the bidders already know their valuations at the entry stage. Accordingly, the equilibrium conditions for these stylized models vary. However, neither of these conditions is easy to justify in applications. For example, in highway procurement auctions in US, contractors usually have already acquired a fair amount of information on the auctioned object through the bidding plans. Assumption of completely uninformed or informed entry seems hard to swallow. This project will use a general selective entry framework that we proposed in the literature. The bidders observe informative, but imperfect signals at entry in our model. The focus of this project is on the correlation between signals and valuations, which in turn improves our understanding of the selectivity from entry. We will also look into the feasibility of optimal policy on entry. In particular, we will assess how change of signal informativeness can substitute for regular policy tools such as entry fees and reserve prices. We use a structural approach to study patterns of entry and bidding in the procurement markets. Our study will make its methodological contribution to the literature through the investigation on the issues of empirical identification, estimation and inference strategy, and policy evaluations in procurement markets. In particular, the project intends to address the following questions: (1) If the key model primitive is not identifiable nonparametrically, what is the best alternative then? (2) How to efficiently estimate the model primitives and conduct inferences? (3) How to evaluate the impact of policies aiming at improving selectivity? 在现代经济中采购商品和服务的实践中，招投标是一种普遍的机制。 经验丰富的经济学家对采购拍卖中的一项普遍现象给予了极大的关注：进入壁垒。 也就是说，即使所有合格的投标人都对拍卖对象表现出了潜在的兴趣，也并非所有投标人都选择投标。 这种观察表明，参与招投标的过程可能是昂贵的。 但是这样的成本可能进一步暗示拍卖的参与者是有选择性的。 了解在如此大而重要的市场本身中的进入和选择效果是一个普遍感兴趣的话题。 拟议的项目旨在调查进入者选择性对采购实践的影响。 经济模型从理论上解释了参与成本是信息获取还是投标预备成本。 关键区别在于，投标人在进入阶段是否已经知道他们的估值。 因此，这些理论模型的平衡条件会有所不同。 但是，这些条件都不容易在应用中证明。 例如，在美国的公路采购拍卖中，承包商通常已经通过招标计划获取了有关拍卖对象的大量信息。 完全不知情或完全知情进入的假设似乎难以接受。 该项目将使用我们在文献中提出的最具通用性的选择性参与理论框架。 投标人在进入模型时观察到了信息丰富但不完善的信号。 该项目的重点是信号与估值之间的相关性，这反过来又加深了我们对入场选择性的理解。 我们还将研究最佳准入政策的可行性。 特别是，我们将评估信号信息性的变化如何替代常规政策工具，例如入场费和竞标底价。 我们使用结构化方法来研究采购市场中的参与和招标模式。 我们的研究将通过对经验鉴定，估计和推论策略以及采购市场中的政策评估问题进行研究，从而对文献做出方法上的贡献。 特别是，该项目打算解决以下问题：（1）如果无法通过非参数识别关键模型要素，那么最佳选择是什么？ （2）如何有效地估计模型要素并进行推理？ （3）如何评估旨在提高选择性的政策的影响？

17503720.label: Realisation of objectives
17503720.value: We develop a complete theory for the identification and estimation of the semipara- metric model discussed in the conclusion section of Gentry and Li (2014), which has not been studied in the literature, to the best of our knowledge. The econometric theory part of this paper fills the void. We derive testable sufficient conditions that ensure (semi- parametric) local and global identification in the sense of Lewbel (2019). We propose a convenient and practical generalized method of moments (GMM) estimator and develop its first-order asymptotic theory. Some intermediate results in the econometric part are of independent interest. Our semiparametric GMM estimation uses the empirical CDF of pseudo values based on a nonparametrically estimated inverse bidding strategy. GPV pro- poses kernel density estimation using these pseudo values. Ma, Marmer, and Shneyerov (2019) derives the first order asymptotic theory of the GPV-type value density estimator. The asymptotic properties of the GPV-type value CDF estimator have not been studied in the literature to the best of our knowledge. The econometric part complements Ma, Marmer, and Shneyerov (2019) and fills the void by providing the first-order asymptotic properties for such an estimator in an intermediate result. The optimal weight matrix of the semiparametric GMM estimator depends on the as- ymptotic variance of the GPV-type value CDF estimator, which takes a nonstandard form and necessitates bootstrap estimation. Ma, Marmer, and Shneyerov (2019) shows con- sistency of the bootstrap distribution for the GPV-type density estimator. However, con- sistency of the bootstrap distribution does not guarantee consistency of the bootstrap variance estimator, which may overestimate the asymptotic variance asymptotically. See Hahn and Liao (2021) for examples and general theory. Fortunately, the bootstrap vari- ance estimator consistently estimates the asymptotic variance. Our bootstrap (variance) consistency result complements that of Ma, Marmer, and Shneyerov (2019) and requires an entirely different proof. The following intermediate results used in its proof are of independent interest. Estimating the inverse bidding strategy requires plugging in a nonparametric estimator of the compactly supported bid density. Standard kernel density estimator suffers from boundary bias. Either trimming (GPV) or boundary bias correction (see, e.g., Hickman and Hubbard, 2015 or Ma, Marmer, Shneyerov, and Xu, 2021) has been used to address the issue. In this paper, we follow Ma, Marmer, Shneyerov, and Xu (2021) to use the boundary adaptive local linear density estimator (Lejeune and Sarda, 1992). We de- rive concentration bounds for the more general local polynomial (LP) density estimators (Bickel and Doksum, 2015, Chapter 11.3), and also its first and second derivatives, which extend the classical concentration results for kernel density estimators (Gin´e and Guil- lou, 2002). These results are also novel and useful in other semiparametric estimation problems in which a compactly supported density is a nuisance parameter.

17503720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503720.value: One of our main findings is an unusual discontinuous entry behavior under the bid requirement format. The equilibrium entry cutoff is determined by the zero profit con- dition for the marginal bidder (entrant). That is, in the equilibrium the bidder whose signal is equal to the entry cutoff is indifferent between entering and not entering. We find that the expected profit from the entry of the marginal bidder is non-monotone in the entry probability, leading to multiple equilibria. In particular, zero entry is always an equilibrium. This is in contrast to the reserve price format, where the expected profit of the marginal bidder decreases in the entry probability, leading to a unique equilibrium (Marmer, Shneyerov, and Xu, 2013). This is an intuitive result for the reserve price for- mat: the marginal bidder faces less competition under smaller entry probabilities and is more likely to be the only bidder, which increases her expected revenue. On the other hand, under the bid requirement format, the contract is canceled if there are no addi- tional bidders, which wipes out the potential benefits of small probabilities of entry. The important consequence is that there may be zero entry under the bid requirement for- mat, while positive entry under the reserve price format. Such a scenario is more likely to occur in auctions with high entry costs. It is plausible that the level of signal informativeness varies in practice. We use the structural model and our estimates to investigate the relative performance of the two formats under different levels of signal informativeness. Theoretically, the effect of signal informativeness is ambiguous as changing the level of signal informativeness induces two effects, which we refer to as the “information” and “cutoff” effect. The information effect is the direct effect of the informativeness of signals on the expected procurement cost, while the cutoff effect is the indirect effect through the equilibrium entry probability. Without changing the equilibrium entry probability, more informative signals from the information effect reduce the expected cost of procurement. This is because with more informative signals, entering bidders tend to have lower private costs. On the other hand, the cutoff effect may increase or decrease the entry cutoff and the probability of entry. Thus, the overall effect of signal informativeness on the expected procurement cost is ambiguous.

17503720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503720.value: We examined bid requirements in this project, where the government may cancel a procurement contract unless two or more bids are received. Using a first-price auction model with endogenous entry, we analyze the effects on auction failure and procurement costs. Bidders face imperfect signals about private costs at the entry stage, influencing their decision to enter. Comparing bid requirements to a reserve price format, we find the latter is more effective, especially with high entry costs and informative signals. Bid requirements can lead to zero entry and certain auction failure, while reserve prices sustain positive entry under broader conditions.

17503820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503820.value: 长期以来，金融经济学中关于公司价值创造的观念是：公司价值源自对现有投资的运营，以及根据外部机会调整投资规模。因此，在动态的商业环境中，如何通过调整公司的投资运营从而为投资者创造价值，是公司经理层的核心任务。对公司投资规模的调整也被称为公司的实物期权。这意味着公司需要在组织经营活动时保持灵活性。 先前的多数研究已经在没有经济摩擦的理想情况下，检验了公司实物期权的重要性。在理想情况下，企业可以根据情况外部环境的变化无成本地调整经营规模。其他一些研究探索外部经济环境（例如，一国的经济自由度）如何影响公司执行实物期权的能力。然而，先前的研究没有考虑的是，公司内部产生的经营摩擦对执行实物期权的影响（比如，公司不同的组织和进行商业活动方式，会带有不同特征经营摩擦）。实践中，公司在开展商业活动时会伴随多种类型的经营摩擦（交易成本），这会降低公司投资的灵活性，从而限制了其利用投资机会的能力。例如，一些公司的业务需要投入较大的前期固定成本，因而投资规模无法低成本地向上或向下调整；一些公司可能被锁定在特定的客户和供应商的关系中，无法灵活地转向新的交易伙伴；公司的高管也可能会采取机会主义行为，而不是选择最优投资规模来增加公司价值。 本项目旨在系统地探索公司的经营摩擦对公司投资灵活性的影响，并且最终如何影响公司通过执行实物期权创造价值的能力。我们以现有的估值模型为起点，为投资灵活性与公司价值之间建立更一般性的联系。进一步，我们考虑公司日常运作中各种类型的经营摩擦，并探索这些经营摩擦如何阻碍价值创造。具体来说，我们考虑公司多个层面的经营摩擦:（a）销售特征（例如客户集中度），（b）成本结构，以及（c）其他经营特征。我们同时运用理论分析与实证检验，探索公司经营活动的特征（交易成本）如何影响公司根据不断变化的投资机会进行增加或收缩投资规模的能力，以及最终如何影响公司价值。 现有学术研究较少探索公司组织经营活动的方式与创造价值能力之间的联系。本项研究将有助于深入理解，公司如何通过保持经营灵活性以更好地执行实物期权，进而作用于价值创造。本项研究对于在实体经济以及金融市场上进行公司估值并做出投资决策的经理层与投资者均具有借鉴意义。

17503820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503820.value: We hypothesize that because of potential holdup concerns, customer-base concentration (CC) is a source of operational inflexibility that impedes firms’ capital investment and reduces their ability to exploit growth options. Supporting this hypothesis, we find a negative relation between CC and the responsiveness of capital investment to profitability signals. Along with reduced investment responsiveness, firm value as a function of profitability becomes less convex, suggesting a diminished ability to utilize growth options. We use instrumental variables to address endogeneity concerns and conclude that the CC effect is likely causal. Cross-sectional analyses indicate that the documented CC effect is stronger when firms have low bargaining power vis-à-vis their customers, and becomes muted where firms’ major customers are governments (which should be less opportunistic). Finally, the CC effect is stronger in industries with high (versus low) capital asset reusability, suggesting that inflexibilities stemming from sales and production activities have a substitutive relation.

17503820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503820.value: We will conduct further tests to strengthen causal evidence. And we will revise the working paper for submission to a top accounting journal.

17503820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503820.value: We use firms’ customer base concentration (CC) to capture their operational inflexibility and explore how CC affects firms’ investment efficiency and their ability to exploit growth options. We find that CC makes firms’ capital investment less responsiveness to profitability signals and consequently reduces their ability to utilize growth options. The negative effects of CC are stronger for supplier firms with low bargaining power in relation to customers but are muted where firms’ major customers are governments. The negative effects of CC are also stronger in industries with higher capital asset reusability.

17504120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504120.value: 开放式共同基金的流动性错配问题引发了越来越多的关注：一方面共同基金的投资者可以每天赎回持有的基金份额，另一方面共同基金通常持有流动性差的资产，例如小市值股票和公司债。这一流动性错配问题导致共同基金容易受到基金投资者的赎回挤兑，进而影响金融市场的稳定（Coval and Stafford, 2007；Chen, Goldstein and Jiang, 2010；Goldstein，Jiang and Ng，2017； Zeng，2017）。 近年来涌现了一批文献研究共同基金如何进行流动性管理以避免遭受挤兑。这一系列的文献通过分析基金的季度持股数据（例如，Morningstar的数据）发现共同基金持有大量的现金或者现金等价物作为流动性的缓冲工具（Chernenko and Sunderam, 2016）。但是，由于缺少了详细的交易数据，我们仍然不清楚开放式基金是否以及如何动态地使用衍生品进行流动性管理。从稳定金融市场的角度出发，这一研究上的空白引发我们去关注使用衍生品是否可以促进金融市场稳定性的问题。而目前的学术研究尚未触及流动性管理如何影响金融市场稳定性的问题。 本项目将利用英国金融行为监管局（FCA）提供的独有的数据来研究上述问题。本项研究中将主要关注信用违约互换（CDS）这一衍生品。具体而言，FCA提供的ZEN数据库和DTCC提供的trade repository（TR）数据库包含了所有二级市场上受到FCA监管的公司和英国公司下属分公司的公司债以及CDS的交易数据（Czech， Huang，Lou and Wang, 2019；Czech，2018）。相比于已有文献中使用的数据，ZEN数据库具有三大独特优势。第一，它提供了每笔交易详细的信息，包括时间、交易价格和数量、以及交易对手方的信息。第二，它覆盖了英国市场上的所有投资者和交易。第三，我们可以通过它识别出投资者在公司债以及CDS上同时进行的交易。ZEN数据库的微观性和完整性使得我们可以实证研究共同基金如何动态地使用CDS进行流动性管理，并进一步探索其对于金融市场稳定性的意义。 衍生品在流动性管理中具有重要的作用。衍生品相比于其基础证券有两点特征：高流动性以及内嵌杠杆。一方面，衍生品的高流动性和低交易成本使得基金可以更低成本地应对投资者的买入和赎回。但是另一方面，使用衍生品令基金面临追加保证金的风险，这会令部分基金不愿意使用衍生品作为流动性缓冲工具。这两点特征可能会使得衍生品和其基础证券的交易产生有趣的动态变化。例如，当一个债券基金面对大量的投资者赎回需求时，它会首先卖出CDS违约保护权从而避免在债券市场中抛售资产产生大量的价格冲击和交易成本。但是卖出CDS违约保护权同时会增加基金的杠杆率，并使得基金随后需要通过逐渐买入该CDS对应的基础债券来逐渐对该CDS平仓。 基于我们数据完整性上的优势，我们也将研究流动性管理对于资产价格和金融稳定性的意义。具体而言，我们将主要研究赎回需求以及追加保证金风险两点共同作用下导致的资产抛售的外部性。我们在研究中将参照Czech（2019）使用CDS以市值计价的损失作为追加保证金的工具变量，因为大量的以市值计价的损失不可避免地导致受到追加保证金通知的概率增大。基于此，我们将分析市场总体面对赎回需求以及追加保证金的风险敞口是否会导致金融市场上资产抛售的概率上升并产生价格下行压力。

17504220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17504220.value: 企業政治策略的前置因素：政治網絡觀點

17504220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504220.value: 企業通常大量投資于政治策略以營造有利的營商環境。學者發現企業在政治策略上的決策取決於企業層面、行業層面以及制度層面的因素（Hillman et al., 2004）。而越來越多研究開始強調政府政治行為者之間的關係在分析企業政治策略中的重要性（Yan and Chang, 2018）。然而，我們對於企業跟不同政治行為者在政治網絡中的關聯是否影響以及如何影響企業進行政治策略的傾向性的理解十分局限。缺少一個從政治網絡觀點對於政治政策前置因素的完整認知，我們便無法全面理解政治策略影響企業的機制。 此項研究試圖填補這一空白，並透過政治網絡觀點分析企業跟不同政府機構之間合作與競爭的關係。政治網絡理論起源於政治社會學文獻，並透過聚焦於公共與私人行為者的權利網絡以分析政策制定過程（Knoke, 1990）。我進而將動競爭觀點同政治網絡框架結合以研究政治網絡中同盟之間的競爭強度。 具體而言，本文視企業招待政府官員訪問作為一種重要的政治策略並加以研究。近年來一些研究已經分析招待政府官員對企業業績的影響（Green et al., 2016; Jia et al., 2018; Li et al., 2016; Schuler et al., 2017）。我提出當一間企業跟一間政府機構結成同盟並與其他同盟競爭時，這間企業就可能會在競爭同盟內的企業招待競爭同盟的政府官員之後，也招待其自身同盟的政府官員訪問，以作出競爭性的回應。此外，伴隨企業動員其同盟內的權力資源，在招待較低層級的政府官員後，企業更有可能招待與這些官員相關聯的更高層級的官員。最後，我分析同盟間競爭強度以及企業政治聯繫對以上影響的調節作用。 由此，本研究聯結過往強調政府結構對對於政治策略影響的研究，並拓展政治策略前置因素的文獻。此外，本研究也聯結近年來強調需要同時考慮政策供應者與需求者的動機的研究（Wang et al., 2018）。

17504320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17504320.value: 小企业主个人金融健康对企业的影响

17504320.label: Project Objectives
17504320.value: The project is expected to have three main objectives. First, it aims at helping existing and potential small business owners (the entrepreneurs) to better understand how their financial and behavioral characteristics can influence the performance of their businesses. This could help the entrepreneurs to better discipline and train themselves and ultimately achieve more satisfying business outcomes, which would ultimately drive the growth of our overall economy. Second, the project will help financial institutions to better understand the informational value of personal finance and behavioral traits to small business financial performance, which could largely affect their asset allocation and risk management activities especially during periods after adverse economic or financial shocks. This would then further help improve financial inclusion and increase credit availability to small businesses. Third, this project could also help policy makers evaluate the risk in the SME credit sector in a more comprehensive way, and also to design better supporting policies and programs to help train entrepreneurs and to develop small businesses.

17504320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504320.value: Given the important role of small businesses in driving our economic growth and creating jobs, many efforts have been made to understand what affect the development of small businesses especially in the aftermath of adverse shocks to our economy, eras that small businesses are performing much more poorly that their larger peers. So far most studies focus on external factors such as credit supply from financial institutions, but not very much is known from inside the businesses. In this proposed project, I would like to investigate how the performance of small businesses could be affected by their owners’ personal financial wellbeing, which has been found one of the most important factors that determine the finance of small businesses according to survey evidence. More specifically, the project will use micro-level data to investigate how small business owners’ personal debt overhang during the last financial crisis affect the performance of their businesses, and whether policy interventions that facilitate personal debt relief help alleviating the potential negative effects through owner financial problems. The identification will be based on the eligibility criteria of the U.S. government bailout program that is set up to help underwater or near-underwater households to relief their debt burden. By comparing otherwise similar small business owners who were (the treatment group) or were not (the control group) eligible to the program, I can test whether and how owners’ personal debt relief affect the financial and real activities of the small businesses. I will also explore the potential mechanisms that are driving the results. Related theories suggest that owners’ personal financial wellbeing could affect their businesses by influencing funding availability or by influencing owner incentives. Since these different channels have different implications on the businesses’ financial activities, I can empirically identify the dominating mechanism under different situations. 小微企业对推动经济增长和创造就业岗位中的重要作用。为此，各界均一直致力于了解影响小微企业发展的主要因素。 这一问题在经济受到负面冲击之后的时期尤为重要。目前已有研究主要集中在外部金融机构信贷供给对小企业的影响，而对于企业内部的相关探讨还相对空白。此前有调查显示，企业主个人因素对企业的金融活动具有重要的作用。基于这一发现，本课题将深入研究企业主个人的金融健康状况对企业经营的影响。 本课题将采用微观数据研究金融危机期间企业主个人债务积压对其企业的影响， 以及相关政策措施是否能有效缓解相应问题。课题的实证分析方法将基于美国政府的救济政策对不同人群的适用标准及范围， 并对比能否获得救济对其他方面相似的企业主带来的不同后果。 课题还将探寻企业主个人因素通过哪些机制来影响企业的发展。相关理论认为企业主的金融财务状况可以影响企业的融资能力，也可以影响企业决策者的决策动机。由于这些不同的机制对企业金融活动会产生不同角度的影响，本课题可以通过实证分析找到最主要的影响机制。

17504320.label: Realisation of objectives
17504320.value: The high-level objective of this project is to better understand the role of small business owners’ personal characteristics in affecting banks’ lending decisions and credit resource allocations across those small businesses. We achieve this goal by producing two pieces of research works that provide granular empirical evidence on this question. The first piece of research work is “Attention Constraints and Financial Inclusion” by Huang, B., Li, J., Lin, T., Tai, M., and Zhou, Y., (2024), which is recently accepted by the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis (JFQA). The second is “What Matters in FinTech Credit Assessment – Behavioral Traits or Algorithms?” by Lin, C., Luo, Y., and Tai, M., (2022), which has been included in the Hong Kong monetary Authority (HKMA)’s HKIMR Applied Research Paper Series. Specifically, to achieve the first major objective, Huang, Li, Lin, Tai and Zhou (2024) use proprietary bank administrative records to show that certain socioeconomic labels of small business owners (the entrepreneurs), e.g., whether one is a local resident or migrant, can be important factors that lead to differential bank lending decisions to borrowers with comparable credit quality. As a consequence, small businesses with owners from certain socioeconomic backgrounds face less favorable credit access, which can ultimately influence the real performance of their businesses. In addition, Lin, Luo, and Tai (2022) realize the first objective by merging high-dimensional data from multiple bank business sectors and utilizing state-of-art machine learning techniques to show that small business owners’ personal behavioral traits have strong predictive power on the future business performance. This further stresses the importance of the relation between small business owners’ personal characteristics and the businesses’ real activities. For the second major objective, Huang, Li, Lin, Tai and Zhou (2024) track the step-by-step bank loan screening process to show that bank loan officers make their lending decisions based on simple signals about the borrowers’ personal socioeconomic characteristics. Such a lending decision-making criteria can impact the outcomes on financial inclusion and credit resource allocation across small businesses. Moreover, Lin, Luo, and Tai (2022) show that banks can substantially enhance their credit risk management by utilizing information revealed from entrepreneurs’ personal behaviors. This unconventional information source can be particularly valuable for the screening of small businesses that lack traditional credit history, thus improving the overall financial inclusion for young and micro businesses in our economy. For the third major objective, both research works generate relevant policy implications regarding how to enhance the efficiency of financial resource allocation across small businesses and better support their contributions to our real economy. In particular, both works suggest that by incorporating advanced algorithms that enable lenders to make more efficient use of small business owners’ personal information can improve both the efficiency of financial risk management and the equality in credit resource distribution.

This could help the entrepreneurs to better discipline and train themselves and ultimately achieve more satisfying business outcomes, which would ultimately drive the growth of our overall economy.

17504320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17504320.value: In the first research paper, “Attention Constraints and Financial Inclusion” by Huang, B., Li, J., Lin, T., Tai, M., and Zhou, Y., (2024), which is recently accepted by the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis (JFQA), we use detailed bank administrative records to provide empirical evidence that small business owners’ personal socioeconomic labels, such as status of residence and ownership of properties, can influence bank lending decisions. As a result, even small businesses with comparable credit quality may face differential credit resource allocations and thus end up having differential real economic performance. In the second research paper, “What Matters in FinTech Credit Assessment – Behavioral Traits or Algorithms?” by Lin, C., Luo, Y., and Tai, M., (2022), which has been included in the Hong Kong monetary Authority (HKMA)’s HKIMR Applied Research Paper Series, we show that the latest development of big-data techniques could enhance large financial institutions’ credit risk management for small businesses. Specifically, large financial institutions can leverage their data advantages by merging granular information on small business owners’ personal behaviors with the business credit records. As business owners’ personal characteristics have strong predictive power on their business performance, this new data-driven methods can improve financial inclusion for small businesses that lack traditional credit records.

17504320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17504320.value: The project corroborates the importance of small business owners’ personal information on the credit access and financial inclusion of their businesses. This suggest that novel information sources on entrepreneurs’ personal behaviors can be utilized to improve credit provision to small businesses, especially to those that lack traditional credit histories. For example, information from mobile location data on business owners’ footfalls, and their personality and ideology revealed from public speeches and social media can all be potentially incorporated in lenders’ risk management systems. This idea can also be extended to examine how personal behaviors of firms’ lower-level employees impact the business and financial performance.

17504320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17504320.value: This project helps lenders and borrowers to better understand the importance of small business owners’ personal characteristics in affecting the firm’s access to credit. For example, one research work under this project shows that if a small business’s owner is an immigrant rather than a local residence, the firm is less likely to be granted a business loan even when it is qualified. Another research work further shows that if banks can observe a small business owner’s personal consumption, investment and credit activities, it can help the bank to better assess the default risk of the business and make better credit risk management.

17504920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504920.value: 2012年4月金正恩上台後，朝鮮政府宣布了一系列市場改革政策，包括農業去集體化和公司私有化，讓人聯想到中國1970年代後期的經濟改革。2012年至2018年期間，朝鮮進行的導彈和核試驗數量是過去三十年的兩倍以上。目前，該國受到聯合國安理會實施的各種經濟制裁（Davenport，2016）。然而令人驚訝的是，在該國與國際社會的關系日益惡化的情況下，越來越多的軼事和非正式報告描述了被稱為“Jangmadang”的商業市場對人們日常生活和行為方式日益增長的影響。這些信息使我們產生了兩個問題：朝鮮的真實經濟狀況是怎樣的，以及市場改革在多大程度上影響了朝鮮的发展。 該項目旨在利用機器學習和高分辨率的白天衛星圖像，開发一種收集經濟數據的新方法來回答這些問題。在過去十年中，高分辨率的衛星圖像的廣泛使用和圖像識別技術的发展為研究人員更準確和詳細地衡量重要的經濟发展指征提供了新的道路。有了更好的數據，政府和其他組織可以有效改善有關資源分配、消除貧困和基礎設施建設的政策。然而朝鮮經濟的數據缺口尤為嚴重：世界銀行的數據庫中，沒有該國的國內生產總值（GDP）和收入水平等可以衡量該國貧困狀況的數據。家庭調查可能彌補這些數據缺口，但代價高得令人望而卻步—不僅成本極高，在朝鮮這樣一個世界上最隱秘的國家中也幾乎不可行。 作為一個跨學科項目，我們正在與計算機科學和地理領域的研究人員合作開发一個深度學習網絡。該網絡將機器學習算法應用於多層人工神經網絡，對高分辨率的日間衛星圖像中的特定特征進行分類，並估算社會經濟指標的細粒度測量結果。作為一項試點項目的一部分，我們處理完成了已公開的1985年至2019年日間衛星圖像，生成了土地覆蓋標簽以測量出朝鮮城市用地的增長情況。接下來，我們計劃結合此標簽數據集與衛星圖像和其他國家的社會經濟數據來訓練該深度學習網絡，以估算朝鮮各地的人口統計數據和經濟指標。之後我們將使用構建出的數據集來研究經濟改革和市場合法化對朝鮮經濟的影響。 據我們所知，這是第一個將深度學習與高分辨率日間衛星圖像相結合，以構建顯示人口統計和經濟发展的面板數據的研究。其面板特征使得我們可以探究與政治環境變化或經濟政策改革存在潛在相關性的社會經濟趨勢變化。具體來說，該項目存在三方面的潛在貢獻：（i）此朝鮮數據集使研究人員和政策制定者能夠深入調研該國經濟，制定更好的戰略和政策，（ii）這些解釋了經濟改革和市場如何影響朝鮮发展的发現將會對市場在轉型經濟中的作用提供有益的啟示，（iii）我們開发的深度學習網絡可用於收集其他存在嚴重數據缺口以及調查結果缺乏有效性的发展中國家的數據。

17504920.label: Realisation of objectives
17504920.value: 1. To develop a novel method, using deep-learning and high-resolution daytime satellite imagery, to estimate fine-grained demographic and economic indicators We developed a human-machine collaborative deep neural network model which predicts grid-level economic development by only using publicly available satellite images and lightweight human annotations. While economic development encompasses wide-ranging dimensions of human progress, our model generates a measure of economic development captured by different patterns of human settlements that are visually distinguishable using views from above. For example, satellite images with larger areas of rice paddies, higher building density, or the existence of a large stadium are positive indicators of economic development, whereas fewer roads and buildings, and larger areas of forest and barren lands are considered less developed. Our model operates in three stages. First, we utilize deep learning-based computer vision techniques to cluster satellite images based on vectorized visual features (Stage 1). Next, we ask human annotators to produce the subjective rankings of image clusters (Stage 2), which is summarized in the form of a partial order graph (POG). The POG is an essential element in our approach that addresses the limitations of current deep-learning and satellite imagery-based economic measurement methods: This lightweight and cost-effective labeling process applies to all regions captured by satellite imagery, irrespective of the availability of ground truth data. In the final stage, we train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to assign a numeric score for every satellite grid where the rank-wise score should be closest to the ranking generated by human annotators (Stage 3). The final output of the model is a score for every grid image, called siScore, in which a higher score represents a higher degree of economic development. To validate our measures, we conduct performance evaluations with five least developed countries in Asia. The results show that our predictions outperform existing machine-only learning approaches based on nightlight intensity and land cover classification. 2. To construct a panel dataset from 1985 to 2019 which contains economic development measures, including income, poverty, and urbanization, for North Korea at the county and district level We estimate urbanization rate, defined as portion of land grid classified as built-up area, using Landsat satellite images for every five years between 1995 and 2019. The reason for starting with 1995 instead of 1985 is that the resolution of satellite images before 1995 were inadequate (below 30 meter resolution) for application of current remote sensing techniques. Next, we apply our human-machine collaborative model to generate a spectrum of scores uncovering regional development in North Korea. In our paper (Ahn et. al., 2023, referred to as Journal Paper #1), we provide a grid-level map that shows the average siScores between 2016 and 2019. The map depicts several distinctive development patterns in North Korea; the western plains and eastern coastal port areas show high siScores, whereas the vast central and northern regions with high-altitude mountains show low siScores. Note that our measures provide a higher-resolution mapping of regional development than existing measures based on nightlight images. Notably, our model results are comparable to the maps of land cover classification or building footprints constructed by the South Korean government on a decennial basis. In contrast to our method, generating land cover classification and building footprints requires substantial resources, including access to proprietary satellite and aerial images, and extensive human inspection. Model predictions for five Low Developing Countries (LDCs) demonstrate that the applicability of our model extends beyond North Korea to a broader set of developing countries. We evaluate our model in six countries—North Korea and five LDCs. For five LDCs, we use ground-truth information from official census and survey data as ground-truth information. Such data are not available for North Korea for the period of study. Instead, the evaluation for North Korea uses three datasets for validation. The first is a manually constructed building footprint dataset, covering 70% of the country and contains each building’s outline marked by GIS experts in 2014. We extract the floor area of buildings and then aggregate them to compute the building area as a proxy for economic development. The second is the number of companies (establishments) by district, collected by counting company mentions in North Korean news outlets. The third is the district-level population density from the country’s most recent population census in 2008. The evaluation exercise shows that our human-machine collaborative model generates scores that are highly predictive of multiple proxies of economic development for North Korea at the grid-level (Spearman’s ρ=0.77) and at the district-level (with the highest R-squared value=0.83). It also achieves similar performance when tested on five LDC countries. Moreover, when compared to the four baseline models, our model attains comparable performance and, in many cases, outperforms other models. We additionally consider an alternative baseline method of first training the neural network on a different country where ground-truth data is available (e.g., using a convolutional neural network and OpenStreetMap data) then applying the learned model to North Korea. These findings suggest that the human-machine collaborative model is capable of generating high-quality predictions of economic development using publicly available satellite imagery in the absence of ground truth labels. 3. To examine the impact of economic reforms and markets on local economic development in a transition economy Applying our model to North Korean satellite images with 10meter resolution for the period from 2016 to 2019 we generate grid-level estimates of economic development. This period is of particular interest to researchers and policymakers because North Korea was subject to a wave of economic sanctions imposed by the United Nations Sanction Resolutions. Taking our numeric score as a proxy of economic development indicates that amid rising pressure from economic sanctions the centrally planned economy has been directing more resources towards its capital, Pyeongyang, and to regions with state-led development projects. We also observe significant development in areas with uranium mines raising the possibility of nuclear development in response to the sanctions. In a related paper (Kim et. al., 2023; referred to as Journal Paper #2), we investigate the economic costs of the recent United Nations sanctions on North Korea. Unlike Journal Paper #1, in this paper we use nighttime satellite images and focus on identifying a causal relationship between sanctions and economic development. Exploiting a novel data set on North Korean firms, we construct measures of regional exposure to export and intermediate input sanctions and show that trade sanctions cause sharp declines in local nighttime luminosity. Additional analysis of newly available product-level price data reveals that import sanctions led to significant increases in market prices. We then estimate a quantitative spatial equilibrium model using cross-region variations. The model implies that the sanctions reduced the country's manufacturing output by 13.4\% and real income by 16.3\%. Overall, these results may help us understand the consequences of sanctions on North Korean economy and political regime.

17504920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17504920.value: I have produced two peer-reviewed publications from this project. The first paper (Journal Paper #1) titled “A human-machine collaborative approach measures economic development using satellite imagery” was published at Nature Communications on October 26, 2023. The full publication version is attached in Part C. The main finding of this paper is to present a human-machine collaborative model which predicts grid-level economic development using publicly available satellite imagery and lightweight subjective ranking annotation without any ground-truth data. We apply our model to North Korea and produce fine-grained predictions of economic development for the nation where data is not readily available. Our model prediction suggests substantial development in the country’s capital and areas with state-led development projects in recent years. We show the broad applicability of our model by examining five of the least developed countries in Asia, covering 400,000 grids. The second paper (Journal Paper #2) titled “The Economic Costs of Trade Sanctions: Evidence from North Korea” was published at the Journal of International Economics on November 2023. The full publication version is attached in Part C. In this paper we seek to contribute to our understanding of the economic impacts of trade sanctions in the context of UN sanctions that imposed comprehensive bans on North Korea's exports and imports in 2016 and 2017. Combining a novel firm-level data set with national-level trade data, we construct a Bartik-style measure of regional exposures to export and intermediate input sanctions. We find robust evidence that sanctions on exports led to sharp declines in night light intensities and suggestive evidence that sanctions on intermediate inputs had a similar effect. Using product-level market price data, we also report significant increases in the price of import sanctioned products. Furthermore, our spatial equilibrium model predicts that North Korean manufacturing output drops by 13.4% following imposition of the trade sanctions, and the effects would be much larger if the country were forced to reduce or eliminate its current trade deficits.

17504920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17504920.value: Our human-machine collaborative model's predictions complement existing remotely sensed measures, such as nightlight intensity, and provide new information on the cross-regional distribution of economic development identified by human visions. Our model could create grid-level indicators of local economic development of North Korea and show that development has been concentrated in cities and areas with state-led agriculture or tourism projects in recent years. Overall, our model will be especially useful for policy design and implementation in countries with limited data. For example, governments can design targeted interventions by utilizing our model prediction scores to detect and monitor urban sprawl or inequality in urban development. Moreover, considerable efforts are underway to make the model more applicable in the future. First, the predictions can be enriched using alternative sources of remote sensing and other geo-located data. While we utilized publicly available satellite images, our model can readily be applied to other proprietary satellite images and aerial photographs to improve the prediction quality. Second, extending the model for cross-country assessments could be a valuable next step. We ultimately aim for applications at a global scale that would require the model to evaluate more diverse landscapes in various geographies and development stages.

17504920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17504920.value: Accurate measurements of social and economic characteristics are essential when governments and organizations allocate resources and design policies. However, many developing countries still lack regional-level data on key economic and human development indicators, despite recent progress in data gathering methods. Our human-machine collaborative approach addresses this issue by utilizing daytime satellite imagery combined with light-weight human annotation for relative scoring, enabling machine learning-driven predictions reducing the burden of generating ground truth labels. We apply our model to North Korea, a state with an economy in a blackbox. Our model predictions show that recent development activities have been mostly focused in major cities and regions with state-led development projects but have stagnated in other areas of the country. We expect this study to potentially assist the international community in addressing humanitarian challenges. While this paper primarily demonstrates how our approach can be utilized to measure economic development, these methods can be extended to various other socioeconomic or geographic measurements. For example, the model could be trained to identify areas with higher exposure and sensitivity to climate change and natural disasters which can help locate where economic and humanitarian resources and further studies should be directed.

17505020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17505020.value: How important is a first impression to you when you are judging other people's opinion or ability? If you think you and others are perfectly rational economic agents, then the importance of first impression loses its ground because people should be able to update their beliefs according to Bayes' rule and fully process any additional information provided later. Thus, the commonly shared belief that first impression is of a particular importance clearly reflects our lack of ability to fully process additional information and the fact that we put too much weight on the prior information in belief updating. Lee, Lim, and Zhao (2019) investigate how prior-biased inferences affect strategic information transmission in which a privately informed expert sends a cheap talk message to a decision maker. They characterize the set of equilibria and show that when the degree of preference misalignment between parties is small relative to the degree of prior bias, there exists a unique equilibrium that induces infinitely many actions. Moreover, this equilibrium Pareto dominates all other equilibria. They further show that, in the presence of prior bias, direct communication is optimal among all possible communication protocols. Furthermore, the ex ante social welfare achieved by this infinite equilibrium is strictly larger than the upper bound of social welfare for Bayesian agents across all communication protocols. Lee, Lim, and Zhao (2019) argue that the welfare gain results from the fact that information garbling takes place only in the mind of the prior-biased decision maker so that the direct cost of garbling is not paid by society. Prior bias implies that every message sent by the expert is garbled in the mind of the interim decision maker, i.e., in her wrong model. However, the message sent by the expert is not actually garbled in the true model. The strategic advantage of garbling is realized because knowing that the decision maker thinks messages are garbled, the expert sends more informative messages in equilibrium. However, since the messages transmitted are never garbled in reality, the society avoids the possibility that the transmitted message is complete noise, and, hence, avoids the corresponding welfare loss in standard information garbling. Thus, prior bias is a less costly garbling device which may be welfare enhancing. We propose an experimental design that aims at testing this main insight. 当您要对别人的意见或能力做判断时，第一印象有多重要？如果您认为自己是完全理性的经济人，那么第一印象的重要性便没有了基础，因为理性人能够遵循贝叶斯法则的要求，充分处理后续提供的信息。因此，人们对第一印象的重视体现了其缺乏充分处理信息的能力以及过分重视先验信息的事实。 Lee, Lim, and Zhao (2019) 在文章中探讨了先验偏差对信息传递的影响。他们设想了如下情境：一个知道真实状况的专家向具有先验偏差的决策者传递信息以影响其决策。文章描述了均衡的集合，并提出，当双方之间的利益冲突相对于先验偏差的程度较低时，存在一个独特的福利最高的均衡，其福利严格大于完全理性决策者下的任何均衡。他们进一步表明，在先验偏见足够大的情况下，直接沟通是最佳的信息传递方式，即中间人的存在不能增加沟通的效率。 Lee, Lim, and Zhao (2019) 认为福利收益的来源如下：在有利益冲突的前提下，决策者的先验偏差使专家能够有可信度地传递更加精确的信息。相对于中间人对信息的直接加工，这里信息的损耗仅发生在决策者的脑海中，因此没有直接的社会成本。从专家的方面考虑，决策者的先验偏差使其对信息的利用率变低，从而降低了传递过于精确的信息对专家的利益之损害。在理性情境下，中间人的存在和噪音的干扰可以达到相似的效果。 然而，不同于这些经典工具，先验偏差只发生在决策者的脑海里，没有在传递中实际损耗信息，避免了相应的福利损失。具有先验偏差的决策者和这些信息干扰模型里的理性决策者一样，对收到信息的利用率较低。二者的不同点在于前者收到的是未经干扰的更加精确的信息。因此，先验偏差可以视作一种成本较低的信息干扰工具，可以提高福利。我们的实验设计旨在验证这一主要见解。

17505020.label: Major findings and research outcome
17505020.value: We have finished a paper titled "Controlled Cursedness" and have submitted the paper to the American Economic Journal: Microeconomics. A previous version of the paper, titled "Mistrust and Garbling in Communication: Experimental Evidence," was accepted into the 2023 Asia-Pacific Economic Science Association Conference. We conduct experiments to investigate the effect of prior bias in standard cheap-talk settings. We consider a setting involving one sender and multiple receivers, one real and several fictitious. The sender knows the real receiver's type, but his message is shared with all receivers. Uninformed of whether she is real or fictitious, the real receiver will be prior-biased. We find that prior bias induces the sender to provide more information and generates a higher payoff for the real receiver. By adjusting the number of fictitious receivers, we find that the payoff of the real receiver with a moderate level of prior bias can exceed the payoff under optimal mediation, indicating that prior bias can be welfare-enhancing. We also observe both over- and under-communication in different treatments, which cannot be rationalized by the standard explanations available in the literature but can be captured by the existence of home-grown prior bias. Since prior bias and cursedness (Eyster and Rabin, 2005) are isomorphic in our setting, our experiments also serve as a test of the effectiveness of cursed equilibrium in organizing experimental data. Our findings, while they cannot be rationalized by standard explanations, align with the comparative statics predicted by cursed equilibrium. Thus, our paper has provided strong support for cursed equilibrium.

17505020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17505020.value: In this paper, we establish a strategic equivalence between implementing prior bias (cursed equilibrium) and introducing fictitious players in Bayesian games, allowing for the controlled manipulation of prior bias (cursedness) in lab settings. The paper lays the technical and methodological foundation for implementing and controlling incorrect beliefs in the players' minds without deception. The same method can be extended to investigate the effect of a large class of behavioral biases in games.

17505020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17505020.value: We investigate how the "stubbornness" of the information receiver affects the way information is provided by an informed sender with a conflict of interest. Our experiments show that the receiver's "stubbornness" actually causes the sender to provide more information, despite the conflict of interest. We also find that this effect can benefit both parties more than mediation. We have invented a method to implement and control behavioral biases in players' minds without deception. We achieve this by introducing fictitious roles in the game and not disclosing to the players whether their roles are fictitious or real. This method can be generalized to investigate a wide range of behavioral biases.

17505120.label: Project Objectives
17505120.value: The objective of this proposal is to examine the effect of CEO and board political ideology on firms' adoption of incorporating sustainability performance metrics in CEO compensation contracts, and the intended and unintended organizational implications of such contracting practices. Our study aims to advance our understanding of the antecedents of firms’ adoption of CSR contracting and highlight some potential “dark side” of such incentive designs.

17505120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17505120.value: This proposal examines how CEOs’ political ideologies, specifically their political inclinations toward liberalism versus conservativism, affect the likelihood of linking CEO compensation to CSR performance measures (i.e., CSR contracting). We propose that liberal and conservative CEOs hold different views about the instrumental merits of CSR contracting. Using a sample of CEOs in S&P 500 firms and their personal political donations to measure their political ideologies, we expect that liberal-leaning CEOs are more likely to have CSR contracting in their compensation schemes. We also expect cross-sectional variations in this relationship when (1) the prevailing political ideologies of the board compensation committee members are more liberal; (2) recent firm financial performance is better; and (3) the company’s external political environment is more liberal. 本文研究企业高管的党派政治立场与其社会责任薪酬合同的关系。我们从企业高管的高阶理论和政治心理学理论框架着手，提出偏向于自由派或者保守派的企业高管对于是否接受用企业的社会责任行为作为衡量其在职的经营业绩有着完全不同的看法。借助现行文献中常用的以个人对不同党派的捐助行为来衡量企业高管的对不同党派的政治立场，我们发现偏向于民主党派的美国标普500公司高管更可能接受含括社会责任衡量指标的薪酬合同。我们还发现当高管的薪酬合同含括社会责任衡量指标时，企业更愿意投资并且承担更多的社会责任。

17505120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17505120.value: This paper examines the effect of board members’ political ideology and their decisions to include CSR contracting in CEO compensation design. We find that a liberal-leaning board is more likely to use CSR contracting to guide its agent CEO to work on CSR endeavors, while conservative-leaning CEOs are more likely to have CSR-related performance measures in their incentive plans. We further examine the dynamic interplay between the political ideology of the board and the CEOs in CEO CSR compensation design, and find that the positive effect of board liberalism on CSR contracting is more pronounced for more conservative CEOs; this effect is stronger when CEOs have low power. Finally, we find CEO CSR contracting is positively associated with firms' CSR performance for the most conservative CEOs, while this effect is insignificant for the most liberal CEOs. Taken together, this result suggests that the motivational effect of CSR compensation on firms' CSR performance is muted for CEOs who are intrinsically motivated.

17505120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17505120.value: We are recently noted (June 18th, 2024) that the paper developed from the proposal was rejected in the third round of review at one of the Financial Times journals. We are in the process of reviewing the editorial comments and suggestions and plan to resubmit the paper to another journal for publication.

17505120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17505120.value: This paper examines firms' CEO CSR contracting decisions. We find that the political beliefs and attitudes of the boards and the CEOs play a big role. The more liberal the board, the more likely they are to use CSR contracting for the CEOs. On the other hand, a CEO who leans conservative is more likely to have CSR contracting because it helps make up for their lack of natural desire to engage in CSR activities. We also find the power balance between the boards and CEOs changes the design of the CEO CSR contract design. We also find CEO CSR contracting is positively associated with firms' CSR performance for the most conservative CEOs, while this effect is insignificant for the most liberal CEOs. Our findings that CSR contracting works best for improving a company's CSR performance when the CEO is conservative. Taken together, our results highlight the importance of aligning CEO pay incentives with the goals of the board in firms' CSR performance.

17505420.label: Project Objectives
17505420.value: Utilizing the more complex setting in China for patient hospital choices, we will first document the degree of mismatching (the percentage of patients switching from grade-2 hospitals to grade-3 hospitals and vice versa), and their variations across different disease categories. Next, we will estimate the factors determining the patient hospital choices, with an emphasis on the quality of hospital care, out-of-pocket expenses, and distance. Finally, we will conduct counterfactual analysis regarding how quality changes for hospital care and price adjustment for medical service (across hospitals of different grades) may impact on the welfare of patients.

Next, we will estimate the factors determining the patient hospital choices, with an emphasis on the quality of hospital care, out-of-pocket expenses, and distance.

17505420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17505420.value: Choice of hospital by patients has attracted a lot of research attention, because it shapes market competition in hospital industry and is also critical in determining consumer welfare of patients. Existing studies using data from advanced economies show that both quality ranking of hospitals and time costs of patients (distance to hospitals and waiting time at hospitals) are important determinants. However, there are two features of patient hospital choices in these economies, specifically, patients having informed choices among hospitals recommended by their general practitioners and they facing relatively little variations in their out-of-pocket expenses across those hospitals, which may limit the extent to which we can analyze the impact of patient choices on their consumer welfare. Here we propose to study choice of hospital by patients in a much more complex environment (the setting of a mainland Chinese city) where patients are not well informed about their medical conditions (because they rarely visit general practitioners before choosing hospital) and at the same time they face significant differences in their out of pocket expenses across hospitals of different grades. We aim to model how self-judgment of medical conditions by patients, financial constraints, and preferences over hospital characteristics jointly determine patients’ hospital choices. Utilizing patients’ transfers between hospitals (from low-grade hospitals to higher-grade hospitals apparently caused by misjudgment of medical conditions, and from higher-grade hospitals to low-grade hospitals presumably due to price sensitivity), we can estimate the relative importance of misjudgment of medical conditions, and patients’ elasticity to healthcare prices. We will also conduct counterfactual analysis regarding how referral service before patients choose hospitals and price adjustment for medical service (across hospitals of different grades) may impact on the welfare of patients. Our research is expected to uncover determinants of patient hospital choice under a more complex environment and provide policy recommendations to improve the consumer welfare of patients. 本研究计划探究在中国的医疗背景下，当病人对自身病情掌握信息不充分、且医院的医疗质量和价格有显著差异时，患有不同疾病的病人如何选择医院。我们将估计哪些医院的特征显著影响病人住院医院的选择，重点量化病人对医疗质量、自费费用以及医院距离的敏感程度。反事实分析将帮助我们观察当医院医疗质量和价格变化时病人经济福利如何变化，从而为政府医疗改革政策的制定提供依据。

17505420.label: Realisation of objectives
17505420.value: How patients choose hospital for medical care shapes the degree of market competition in the hospital industry, and it is also critical in determining the consumer welfare of patients. Much research using data from advanced economies found that both quality ranking of hospitals and time costs of patients (distance to hospitals plus waiting time at hospitals) are important determinants. However, in these economies, patients make informed choices of hospitals based on the recommendations from their general practitioners, and they face relatively little variations in their out-of-pocket expenses across those hospitals. These two features may limit the applicability of the existing findings based on data of advanced economies to other economies where these two conditions (informed choice across hospitals with little variations in out of pocket expenses) may not hold. In this study, we examine patient hospital choices in a setting where patients are not well informed about their medical conditions and at the same time they face significant differences in their out of pocket expenses across different hospitals. By modelling how self-judgment of health status, financial constraints, and preferences over hospital characteristics jointly determine patients’ hospital choices and by utilizing patients’ transfers between hospitals, we estimate the relative importance of misjudgement of medical conditions, patients’ elasticity to health care prices, quality of hospital care, and distance, so that we can conduct the counterfactual analysis. Specifically, we use a large patient discharge data set from a major city in China. Healthcare system in China is hospital-centric in that patients do not need to go through general practitioners before choosing hospitals, which are classified into different grades based on their level and quality of service (with Grade 3 being the highest, followed by grade 2 and finally grade 1). As a result, patients are uninformed about their medical conditions, in sharp contrast to patients in the United Kingdom and the United States who have been examined by their general practitioners and recommended with a set of hospitals that can address their medical concerns. Indeed, in our data set, we do observe patients switching from grade 2 hospitals to grade 3 hospitals, presumably because patients were not aware of the severity of their medical conditions and chose wrong hospitals. Meanwhile, patients in China face much higher out-of-pocket expenses when going to grade 3 hospitals than grade 2 hospitals. This is again different from the situation in the United Kingdom and the United States where patients face little variations in their out-of-pocket expenses among the hospitals recommended by their general practitioners. Not surprisingly, few of the existing studies has found price to be an important determinant for patient hospital choices. However, in our data set, we do observe Chinese patients switching from grade 3 hospitals to grade 2 hospitals, presumably because their medical conditions were not serious enough to warrant a more expensive medical service at grade 3 hospitals. From the data, we document the mismatching of patients with hospitals by identifying hospital transfers. Defining a hospital transfer as two inpatient records of the same person in two hospitals where the admission date of the second inpatient record is no later than one day after the discharge date of the first inpatient record, we find that there are over 17 thousand hospital transfers in the 21-month sample period, i.e., 27 transfers per day. For certain diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction (AMI), more than 10 percent of hospital admissions will lead to transfers to other hospitals. If we look at patients diagnosed with cerebral haemorrhage, 4.4 percent of the hospital admissions (392 out of 8,845) lead to transfers. 172 patients (44 percent of all transfers) are transferred from grade 2 hospitals to grade 3 hospitals; 61 patients (16 percent of the transfers) are transferred from grade 3 hospitals to grade 2 hospitals. The large number of two-way hospital transfers imply that mis-judgment of medical conditions may be a very important factor affecting patients’ hospital choices. The different percentages of transfers for different diseases categories indicate the level of mismatching may be related to disease categories, suggesting that some diseases are more difficult for patients to judge without doctor’s advice than others. We then construct a model in a two-choice framework and estimate the factors determining the patient hospital choices, with an emphasis on patients’ price sensitivity to quality of hospital care, out-of-pocket expenses, and distance, and patients’ misjudgement about their medical conditions. The model has two parts. First, a patient chooses a hospital to visit without knowing exactly their medical conditions; second, after their first admission to a hospital, they are fully informed of their medical conditions and then make a second decision whether to transfer to another hospital. Each hospital is classified into a high grade or a low grade, where only hospitals of high grade have the capability to cure the patient with a severe condition. To cope with the challenge that the traditional simulated maximum likelihood approach is computationally infeasible due to the high dimensionality of the random coefficients in the model, we take advantage of the Bayesian techniques and use a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimator. The estimated coefficients in the model are similar to those in the simple multinomial logit model. We find that patients prefer cheaper health care providers when the location, quality and size are constant. In addition, we find that patients prefer hospitals that are closer, those of larger size, public ownership, higher nurse-to-bed ratio, and lower mortality rate. As a measure of the difficulty of self-evaluating the severity of medical conditions, the estimated standard deviation of the signal error a patient receives before the first hospital admission is 1.3 time of the standard deviation of the severity for AMI. For cerebral haemorrhage patients, the average standard deviation of the signal error is 0.8 time of the standard deviation of the disease’s severity. It indicates that patients are less likely to misjudge their medical conditions of cerebral haemorrhage than AMI. We also simulate a counterfactual case that the government make policies to alleviate the misjudgement of medical conditions and examine the welfare implication. We first calculate the consumer surplus from our model to measure the social welfare. Using the sample of 2,919 AMI inpatient records in 21 months, the average ex-ante anticipated consumer surplus of one patient is 1.3 thousand RMB, while the actual ex-post actual consumer surplus of one patient is 1.2 thousand RMB. When the government manages to eliminate the uncertainty about medical conditions by, for example, introducing general practitioners, the average welfare gain is 0.1 thousand RMB or 0.3 thousand RMB if we still allow potential transfers or not. The total welfare gain amounts to 0.29 million RMB (41 thousand USD) and 0.88 million RMB (125 thousand USD) which shows the substantial benefits of alleviating patients’ uncertainty about medical conditions.

We find that there are over 17 thousand hospital transfers in the 21-month sample period, i.e., 27 transfers per day. For certain diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction (AMI), more than 10 percent of hospital admissions will lead to transfers to other hospitals. The average standard deviation of the signal error is 0.8 time of the standard deviation of the disease’s severity for cerebral haemorrhage patients. It indicates that the level of misjudgement is different across different disease categories. We also simulate a counterfactual case that the government make policies to alleviate the misjudgement of medical conditions and examine the welfare implication. Using our sample of 2,919 AMI inpatient records, the average ex-ante anticipated consumer surplus of one patient is 1.3 thousand RMB, while the actual ex-post actual consumer surplus of one patient is 1.2 thousand RMB. When the government manages to eliminate the uncertainty about medical conditions by, for example, introducing general practitioners, the total welfare gain amounts to 0.29 million RMB (41 thousand USD) and 0.88 million RMB (125 thousand USD) which shows the substantial benefits of alleviating patients’ uncertainty about medical conditions.

17505420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17505420.value: Our study is subject to two limitations. First, we assume that the difference of hospital quality mainly relates to the hospital grades and mismatch of patients with hospitals only occurs when patients choose hospitals of a wrong grade. However, hospitals within the same grade may have different specialties and thus different abilities to cure a particular illness. Though the difference of quality for hospitals of the same grade may not be as large as that for hospitals of different grades, further research is needed to model and estimate this dimension of quality variation and patient-hospital matching quality. Second, we assume that we take into account the major factors in patients’ hospital choices and thus the unobserved factors are either minor or uncorrelated with the observed factors. This assumption could be revisited and the potential issues arising from the violation of this assumption could be addressed.

17505420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17505420.value: How patients choose hospitals for medical care is critically important in determining treatment outcome and ultimately their wellbeing. Much research using data from advanced economies found that both quality ranking of hospitals and time costs of patients are important determinants. However, in these economies, patients make informed choices of hospitals based on the recommendations from their general practitioners, and they face relatively little variations in their out-of-pocket expenses across those hospitals hence the unimportance of price in patient choice of hospitals. These two conditions do not hold in many developing countries such as China where patients choose hospitals without any expert advice and they face substantial price differences across hospitals of different grades. In this study, utilizing a unique patient discharge dataset in a major Chinese city, we find substantial mismatching of patents with hospitals, as revealed by switching of hospitals by patients (either from hospitals of lower grade to those of higher grades, or vice versa), and the degree of mismatch varies across disease categories. Aside from the substantial misjudgment of their medical conditions in patient choice of hospitals, we also find patients’ preference of hospitals that are cheaper, closer to home, and those of better quality (measured by larger size, public ownership, higher nurse-to-bed ratio, and lower mortality rate). Finally, we conduct counterfactual analyses and find large welfare gain if the uncertainty about medical conditions can be alleviated.
