17600020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600020.value: Case-marking can be used to indicate structural relations, such as “I” (subject) and “me” (object) in English, but often cases are omitted, or a non-canonical case-marker is used. Such variation was treated as idiosyncratic, but recent work suggests that there are principles determining case variation, dependent on the nature of the subject/object, and contexts. Taking variable case-marking as a ‘system’, previous work has shown that micro-variation of a grammatical (sub)system (such as dialectal case variation) reveals subtleties in the range of grammatical possibilities that are invaluable for understanding the underlying workings of the phenomenon, and laying out desiderata for formal models. This project proposes to investigate case-marking variation in Nubri, an endangered Tibeto-Burman language spoken by ~2000 people in remote Nubri Valley, northern-central Nepal. Nubri has typical Tibeto-Burman case-markers, but the system of usage is quite atypical, with the only frequently occurring case being that of a ‘dative’ case to mark only certain objects, known as ‘differential object marking’ (DOM) (Donohue 2018, 2019,submitted). I recently carried out a valley-wide sociolinguistic survey establishing three main dialects (Donohue 2019a), and during this field trip I collected some preliminary data from Prok dialect in lower Nubri revealing DOM, but a different 'system' of factors determining where/when case-marking occurs. In this study I propose to investigate micro-variation in the case systems of Nubri by examining comparable data from all three dialects. I will make use of targeted elicitations, language tasks, as well as free speech. I also propose to investigate case variation from the languages in greatest contact with Nubri: Nepali, Kyirong-Tibetan and Ghale. I hypothesize that the dialectal variation may be a result of language contact, so collecting these data from the languages as they are spoken in/near the valley will enable me to compare the Nubri-internal variation with that of the particular contact languages, to observe the potential influence of these contact languages on Nubri variation. Empirically, the proposed project will provide a better understanding of the case systems in Nubri cross-dialectally, and neighbouring languages. It will thus contribute to case typology and shed light on the potential role of contact in language change. The project will also enable a timely return to Nubri to finalize early literacy materials to help with the introduction of a writing system. The booklets and recordings of narratives to accompany these literacy materials will be distributed throughout the community (and online), further contributing to ongoing documentary efforts. 格標記可以用來表示語法結構關係，如英語中的 “I” （主語）和 “me” （賓語)，但是格位通常被省略，或使用非常規的格標記。這種不定性一般被認為是特殊的，但最近的研究表明，有一些原則決定了變格的不定性，即這種變化取決於主語/賓語的性質以及語境。先前的研究已經表明，將不定的變格看做一個“系統”的情况下，語法（子）系統的微觀變化（比如方言中的不定變格）可以揭示對語法可能性範圍內的微妙之處。了解這些微妙之處對於認識語法現象的基本工作原理和列出形式模型必要的需求至關重要。 本研究擬調查努日語的格標記不定性。努日語是一種在尼泊爾中北部偏遠的努日山谷使用的瀕危藏緬語，现約有2000人使用。努日語具有典型的藏緬語格標記，但其使用系統則十分非典型: 唯一經常出現的格是一種標記特殊賓語的 “與格”，又被稱為 “受詞異相標記” （Differential Object Marking, DOM）（Donohue 2018, 2019a）。我最近進行了一項全山谷範圍內的社會語言學調查，確定了三種主要方言 （Donohue 2019b）。在這次實地考察中，我從下努日的Prok方言中收集了一些可以體現受詞異相標記的初步數據，但數據包括了決定格標記何時何處出現的不同係統性的因素。在這項研究中，我提議通過檢查來自所有三種方言的可比數據，从而調查努日語變格係統的微觀變化。我將使用有針對性的引導、語言任務、以及自由談話。 我同時計劃調查與努日語接觸最多的尼泊爾語、吉隆藏語和加勒語的變格不定性。我假設努日語的方言變化可能是語言接觸的結果。收集這些在努日山穀附近使用的語言的數據後，我能夠將努日語的內部變化與同努日語接觸的語言相比較，從而觀察這些接觸語言對努日語的影響。 從觀察性研究角度來講，本研究計劃將為努日語各方言以及鄰近語言的語法格系統提供更好的理解。因此，本計劃將有助於語法格標記的類型學，並闡明語言接觸在語言變化中的潛在作用。本研究計劃還將使我及時返回努日山谷最終確認努日語早期識字材料，以幫助引入文字係統。與這些識字材料搭配的冊子和口述錄音將在整個群體中和網上派發，以進一步促進正在進行的語言檔案編製工作。

17600120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600120.value: Helping young people understand cultural diversity is a common educational aim around the world. Yet curricula and textbook producers often overlook this basic 'multicultural' aim. This project intends to examine multicultural content in the curriculum in Mainland China, Macau, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Specifically, it compares how textbooks used in these societies represent ethnic and religious minorities and other topics related to diversity. This study builds upon the principal investigator’s previous research on multicultural education in Hong Kong (in Liberal Studies, General Studies, History, and Chinese History), to provide a systematic analysis of how curricula in these four societies represent cultural diversity. The primary objective of this research is to analyse how ethnic and religious minorities in Mainland China, Macau, and Taiwan are represented in current (and recent past) textbooks. The study focuses on textbooks in subjects most relevant to multicultural education used in government schools in these societies. These include History, Moral and Character Education, and Moral and Political Education in Mainland China; Moral and Civic Education, and Social and Humanities Education in Macau; and Social Studies, Civics and Society, and History in Taiwan. Representations of diversity will be examined using quantitative and qualitative content analysis. The proportion of multicultural content in texts will be identified, while text and picture coding will provide a more nuanced understanding of the approaches to multiculturalism taken in the textbooks. Parallel analyses by the researchers, and surveys of teachers (in Mainland China, Macau, and Taiwan), will be used to determine reliability. The study's methodology aligns with that used in the principal investigator’s previous research on multiculturalism across Hong Kong government schools' curricula. Therefore, the study's data and findings can be compared across Mainland China, Macau, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, with data from Hong Kong being updated as needed. This project will thus provide for a comparative understanding of the quantity and quality of curriculum content related to multicultural diversity in primary and secondary education in Mainland China, Macau, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. It will lead to articles, presentations, and a monograph examining multicultural curricula in the four societies since the 1980s. These outputs will be foundational sources for theorising multicultural education in Mainland China, Macau, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, in light of historical changes, while the research can also inform development of curriculum, teacher education, and school resources. 幫助年輕人瞭解文化多樣性是全世界共同的教育目標。 然而,課程與教科書設計者常常忽視這一基本的「多元文化」目標。 本研究旨在考察中國大陸、澳門、台灣和香港課程中的多元文化內容。 具體而言,它將比較在這四地中使用的教科書如何表述少數族裔和宗教少數群體以及其他跟多樣性有關的話題。本研究奠基於首席研究者先前對香港多元文化教育在下述四個科目中的研究:通識教育、小學常識、歷史及中國歷史，力圖系統地分析四地的課程如何體現文化多樣性。 鑒於對香港的已有研究，本研究的主要重心將放在分析中國大陸、澳門和台灣的少數族裔和宗教少數群體如何在現行的教科書中被表述上。 本研究選取四地公立學校所使用的與多元文化教育最相關的科目的教科書作為主要研究對象。 包括中國大陸的歷史、思想品德和思想政治科目；澳門的品德與公民教育和社會與人文教育科目；及台灣的社會研究、公民與社會、和歷史科目。通過採用定量和定性內容分析的方法考察對多樣性的表述，文本中多元文化內容的比例將得以確定，並且對文本和圖片的編碼將有助於更細致地理解教科書如何吸收多元文化主義。 本研究的可靠性主要通過以下兩種途徑得以建立：研究人員之間對內容的獨立同步分析，和對中國大陸、澳門和台灣教師的問卷調查。本研究的方法與首席研究者先前研究香港公立學校課程中多元文化主義的方法一致。 因此,本研究的數據和成果可以被用來比較中國大陸、澳門、台灣和香港的情況，並根據需要更新來自香港的數據。基於此，本研究項目將提供一個比較的視角來理解四地的中小學課程中關於多元文化多樣性內容的數量和品質。 它的研究成果將轉化為討論自1980年代以來四地的多元文化課程的學術文章、學術彙報和學術專著。 隨著歷史變遷，這些成果將成為理論化多元文化教育在中國大陸、澳門、台灣和香港的發展情況的基礎資料。同時本研究還將為課程、教師教育和學校資源的發展提供參考。

17600120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17600120.value: There are diverse groups that can be included as ethnic and religious minorities when you compare the situations of Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macau. These include ethnic minorities, new immigrant groups, diverse religious communities, and Indigenous communities. The way their histories and identities are recognised follow different strategies across the societies and over time. Additionally the project has yielded valuable insights about textbook and curriculum research methodology related to reliability, coding, and the way curriculum is conceived and used by teachers, students, and other stakeholders in different societies. The research has resulted in a number of journal articles, academic conferences, teaching and learning impacts, and related outputs.

17600120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17600120.value: In addition to previous publications and conference papers, some papers are still under development based on this research. The research can be developed more in the future through continuing historical analyses, and broadening the scope to more societies in East Asia.

17600120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17600120.value: Helping students to appreciate diversity is a goal of education across societies around the world. However, how appreciating diversity is understood differs across contexts. Meanwhile each society's internal composition is unique in relation to its political, cultural, and demographic history and its contemporary educational and social situation and challenges. This study compared the way multicultural education for learning about diversity has been undertaken through curriculum in Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan over time. In particular, it focused on how ethnic and religious minorities have been represented in social-studies related textbooks in the four societies. We found that each society's educational system has a different focus and attitude about how to best manage and understand diversity issues and diverse identities that is rooted in their different histories. The study also discovered important insights about the best ways to conduct and theorise about multicultural issues in curricula when societies produce and use textbooks in education in different ways. The research findings can help enhance the understanding of curriculum and multicultural education for educators and textbook and curriculum writers and producers in these societies, while it has also resulted in several conference papers and journal articles.

17600520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600520.value: 背景：精神疾病患者的病耻感和被歧视十分严重，这将严重阻碍患者的康复和复原。虽然证据显示增加与精神疾病患者的接触能减少公众对患者歧视的态度和行为，但尚不清楚提升接触干预是否能增加初级卫生专业人员精神卫生知识，减少对精神疾病患者的歧视态度和行为。在中国，至今尚无探索增加初级卫生专业人员与患者接触，减少病耻感干预的长期（如：11月随访）有效性的研究。 目的：本研究旨在：1）采用随机对照研究，探索提升接触模式（ECM）干预在增加初级卫生专业人员精神卫生知识，减少对患者歧视态度和行为的短期（干预后）和长期（11月随访）有效性；2）比较提升接触模式（ECM）干预是否较一般精神卫生知识培训（GTP）更能有效减少初级卫生专业人员对精神疾病的病耻感。 方法: 在成都市新津县将招募231名初级卫生专业人员参与。参与者将随机分配至：1）提升接触模式（ECM）组，2）一般精神卫生知识培训（GTP）组，3）对照组。ECM组将接受提升接触模式干预，增加精神卫生知识，提升与精神疾病患者（个体）及其他初级卫生专业人员（小组）的正性接触。GTP组将接受精神卫生知识的培训，增加精神疾病病因､病耻感､治疗和复原的知识。对照组将会定期随访，但不提供特殊干预。所有参与者将完成4次评估（包括精神卫生知识､歧视态度和行为）：干预前，干预后，干预后5月，干预后11月。 意义: 本研究将增加对新的､针对初级卫生专业人员的､ECM干预的认识，这将极大地增加和深化对接触模式减少精神疾病病耻感的认识。本研究还将探索ECM干预和GTP干预，在减少精神疾病病耻感方面的异同，这将有利于进一步提升精神卫生知识，发展综合的减少病耻感的干预，推动卫生专业人员精神卫生的培训，促进社区精神卫生服务。

17601220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601220.value: 本項目是基於主研者題為「（對比）歷時構式語法視角下之「構式消匿」研究」的GRF項目的後續研究。上一研究，理論上鞏固了「構式消匿」現象在日新月異的歷時構式語法領域中的研究焦點地位；描述上則詳錄了18-19世紀英語中「義務性NCI 構式」使用驟減的現象。所謂「義務性NCI 構式」，即是結合了【be動詞 + 過去分詞 + to 不定式】這一表達形式與“義務”和“允准”情態意義的構式。摘錄兩個18世紀英語例句，進行示例： (1) They all WERE DESIRED TO be present to give their advice. (2) Woollen yarn and worsted ARE PROHIBITED TO be exported. 前一項目使用“近現代英語文本語料庫”(Corpus of Late Modern English Texts)，該語料庫意為代表18-19世紀英國英語的用法。研究過程中，我們認識到，使用這種把個體語者或個體作者的語言使用進行抽象提煉而成的語料庫，並不能充分滿足歷時構式語法所要求的「認知承諾」。作為認知語言學首要研究領域之一的歷時構式語法，應該把“語言變遷”與“（個體）語言知識在時間維度上的變異”結合起來。這樣的認知，正是前一項目在理論上和方法上的所達到的重要成果之一。其實，這種思路已經在“新型構式產生”的相關研究中得到了開拓性運用，進而對“新型構式產生”提供具有認知充分性的解釋。此類研究仰賴歷史語料庫的使用，這種語料庫有如下二選一的特點：其一，文本材料不同作者的生命跨度基本重合；其二，文本材料不同作者分屬不同但卻連續的世代。該項目將沿用類似的方法（即使用“歷史性個人習語語料庫”）對「構式消匿」進行研究。內容上，該項目承接上一項目的研究核心，對「義務性NCI 構式」加以詳細描述；語料上，該項目將會擴展到Hansard語料庫的使用。Hansard語料庫涵蓋大量19-20世紀英語語者的語言使用；與18-19世紀的語料庫相結合，便可進行時間軸上的縱向研究，從而回答如下兩個問題：第一，超個人語言使用中日趨減少的構式是否在不同語者之間和同一語者內部均有所體現？第二，若有所體現，如何在這兩個不同的層面進行體現？此研究完全以實際語言使用作為依據，其研究結果預示著一個具有心理現實性的關於「構式消匿」的解釋；那將成為有關語言和語言改變的涵蓋極廣的認知模型的一部分。

17601220.label: Realisation of objectives
17601220.value: Objective 1: This project is both a descriptive and a theoretical contribution to the new but growing historical cognitive linguistic discipline that has come to be known as ‘diachronic construction grammar’ (cf. Barðdal et al., 2015; Hilpert, 2021; Noël & Colleman, 2021; Traugott, 2022). The perspective taken is a ‘radically usage-based’ one, i.e. one that gives considerably more attention to the role of the individual in constructional/language change than is typical practice in usage-based historical linguistics, not only in terms of theory formation, but also with regard to the data considered for its empirical foundation (Noël, 2016, 2017, 2019a). The three publications coming out of this project have helped to put this genuinely cognitive approach to historical linguistics on the map. Objective 2: My approach to this objective was to ask and consider how the phenomenon of constructional attrition fits into a recently formulated usage-based model of the “linguistic system”, viz. Schmid’s Entrenchment-and-Conventionalization Model (or EC-model). Also in its book-length elaboration in Schmid (2020), this model only explicitly accounts for how the (individual) entrenchment and (communal) conventionalization of linguistic expressions comes about and is sustained; it scarcely incorporates how already conventionalized and entrenched constructions can start to go into decline. Though Schmid himself rejects the construction as a theoretical notion (2020: 27-28), I contend in Noël (2023a), and essentially agree with Schmid’s (2021) own recent claim to this effect, that his EC-Model nevertheless provides an excellent basis for an all-encompassing framework for radically usage-based diachronic construction grammar, arguing that it is well suited to account not only for accumulative but also for subtractive developments. In Noël (2023b) I argue that the influence of culture on language change is mediated by entrenchment and that culture has a more extensive impact on entrenchment than the EC-model currently allows for. Objectives 3 and 4: Disappearing constructions do not simply “fall into disuse”. Languages do not change by themselves, they change because their speakers change them, usually unknowingly. They start using constructions differently, which adds new constructions to the language, and they stop using constructions, making constructions disappear. The latter is shorthand for two possible, non-mutually exclusive scenarios. One is that speakers never get to use a construction as much as their contemporaries and precursors, leading to a decrease in the average level of entrenchment of the construction attained by individual speakers from one generation to the next. The other scenario is that at some point in their lives individual speakers start using a construction less frequently than they had been doing previously, and if there are enough individuals exhibiting the concomitant diminished entrenchment of the construction, this too can be hypothesized to contribute to constructional attrition at the aggregate level. Noël (2022) focused on the second of these scenarios. It is the first study (initially intended as a pilot study only; see the interim report) to consider the question of whether constructional attrition is an intraindividual cognitive phenomenon. It looked for attritional lifespan change for the dwindling DEONTIC NCI construction in the 25 authors included in the historical idiolectal Corpus of English Novels (CEN) by comparing the frequencies of their use of the construction in a body of early-writing-career works and a body of late-career works. The original plan was to provide robust evidence for both scenarios, however, based on the Hansard Corpus. Due to the pandemic situation, an offline version of this corpus was slow in arriving, and when it did, turned out to be hardly wieldier than the online version. When Hendrik De Smet sent me a small complement to his CEN corpus, with novels from an earlier generation of writers, I consequently decided to use this instead and expand it to a fully-fledged corpus comparable in size and design to CEN 1.0. The data collection from this corpus was cut short by my retirement from HKU, however. My retirement also necessitated that this report be submitted a full year earlier than would normally have been the case. References Barðdal, J., Smirnova, E., Sommerer, L., & Gildea, S. 17601220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601220.value: The three publications coming out of this project have contributed substantially to putting a radically usage-based approach to diachronic construction grammar on the map, in terms of theory as well as description, and not only with reference to constructional attrition, but beyond that also in the context of cognitive historical linguistics generally. A genuinely cognitive approach to language change requires attention to individual speakers, both with regard to data collection and with reference to theory formation. Other research has started to do this in regard of grammaticalization/constructionalization. This project has been the first to do this for obsolescence/constructional attrition. The empirical study reported on in Noël (2022) looked for attritional lifespan change for the dwindling DEONTIC NCI construction in the 25 authors included in the historical idiolectal CEN corpus by comparing the frequencies of their use of the construction in a body of early-writing-career works and a body of late-career works. A sizeable group of authors were identified who used the schema significantly less frequently in later life, which confirmed that individuals can participate in language-level attritional developments and that constructional attrition is not merely a language-level development but that it can also occur as a change in the individual entrenchment of a construction. Noël (2023a) and Noël (2023b) are theoretical studies. The first one considers how the gradual disappearance of a construction from a language can be accounted for in a radically usage-based diachronic construction grammar through an exploration of how the phenomenon can be accommodated in Schmid’s (2020) Entrenchment-and-Conventionalization model. I conclude that while Schmid (2020) only cursorily mentions the possibility of a reversal of accumulative developments in language change, his EC-model is nevertheless well suited to account for subtractive developments. The second study reflects on how the impact of culture on language change should be accounted for from a radically usage-based diachronic construction grammatical perspective, focusing on how cultural change can cause constructions to disappear from a language, through an assessment of how culture is incorporated in Schmid’s model. I conclude that Schmid’s model provides a good basis for an explicit account of how culture impacts on language change generally, and particularly on constructional attrition, provided that a more comprehensive role is assigned to culture in the Entrenchment component of the model than is the case in its present formulation.

17601220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601220.value: The results of the lifespan study reported on in Noël (2022) are in need of corroboration from additional data sets. In addition, the weight of the impact on aggregate-level constructional attrition of intrapersonal intragenerational attritional developments relative to the impact of intergenerational subtractive change needs to be researched. I compiled a corpus with which to do this and made good progress with the data collection, but cannot finish this myself, having reached the HKU retirement age. Nor will I be in a position myself, therefore, to adjust the theoretical conclusions I arrived at in Noël (2023a,b), should additional data necessitate this.

17601220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601220.value: This project addresses the question of how grammatical constructions can disappear from a language, and specifically investigates what role speakers have in this, given that languages cannot change by themselves, and that linguistic change necessarily results from changes in speakers’ linguistic behaviour. The bulk of historical linguistic research to date has been about how new constructions come about and has taken a language perspective rather than a speaker perspective. Only some of this research on accumulative developments has looked at the role individual speakers play in them. This project has been the first to extend this rare speaker perspective to subtractive changes, aiming to describe and theorize how speakers make grammar disappear. The results so far provide good reason to believe that subtractive changes, like accumulative ones, can, in part at least, be attributed to changes in speakers’ linguistic knowledge, in view of significant drops in the usage of disappearing grammar during the lifetimes of a considerable proportion of speakers. The project has reflected on how this descriptive fact should be incorporated into a speaker-based model of language and language change, and on how it is compatible with the role of cultural change in language change, specifically in subtractive changes.

17601320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17601320.value: "小鮮肉"與"娘炮": 男性陰柔化的性別政治

17601320.label: Project Objectives
17601320.value: To investigate the various social, economic, and cultural factors that have given rise to the effeminate aesthetic of male beauty in contemporary China and to examine them at the intersection of queer studies, the political economy of popular culture, and the study of Chinese nationalism. To critically examine the anxiety over national virility and the obsession with a masculinity marked by national essence through the debates on masculinity and the discourse of sissyphobia (Bergling 2001) in the media and in daily life. To situate the aesthetic historically and explore its formation and emergence in both transnational and national settings; to unravel the influences of other major East Asian societies, Japan and South Korea in particular, and compare them in the context of the proliferation and reception of the images concerned. To reveal the influence of the effeminate aesthetic on Chinese youth and to examine the constructions and negotiations of generational masculinities through the lens of images of that aesthetic and the controversies they generate. To study this new gender imaginary’s relationship with existing heteronormative gender identities and hierarchies; to explore the tension and negotiations between market drive, state policies, and popular taste in relation to the popularity and stigmatization of the effeminate aesthetic; and to identify the main voices or forces critiquing male effeminacy. To examine the relationship between male effeminacy/sissyphobia and non-normative masculinities and to elucidate the intersection between sissyphobia and homophobia in China and, by so doing, enrich the development of current accounts of sissyphobia, primarily in homosexual contexts in the West, through analysis of its operation in heterosexual settings in an Asian society. To critically consider the shifting linguistic terms associated with this aesthetic and their relationship with similar terms in Japanese, Korean and English.

17601320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601320.value: Male actors with feminine beauty in television and films are today known as “little fresh meat” (xiao xian rou) or, more insultingly, “sissy pants” (niangpao) in China. Notwithstanding the long history of gender fluidity in Chinese performance art, these actors are currently suffering social criticism and a professional blacklist implemented by state media. “Sissyphobia,” the fear or hatred of effeminate men, is sweeping China. Such gender policing is closely linked with masculinist nationalism, as manifested in the celebration of macho national heroes in films such as Wolf Warrior II (2017). Yet, despite this masculinist backlash, effeminate-looking stars and the androgynous aesthetic they embody are enjoying increasing popularity among high-school students and other young people. Stylish men who wear makeup represent a new form of embodied masculinity for young middle-class men in urban China. How can we explain the disjuncture between urban youth culture and official attitudes? What do these tensions tell us about gender roles and subjectivity in contemporary China? The research proposal seeks to fill a gap in the scholarly literature on the interrelationship between the increasing number of relatively androgynous make-up wearing male youth and the simultaneous growth in masculinist nationalism in today’s China. It promises a multi-method, interdisciplinary investigation of mass-media images and editorial viewpoints, government policies and officials’ perspectives, and the habits and views of young male followers of the “sissy” aesthetic. Rising nationalism and rising diversity of gender presentations have been a feature of social transformation in China in the post-Tiananmen era, driven by the government’s desires to expand the consumer market on the one hand and to strengthen ideological education on the other. While much has been written on Chinese nationalism and there is growing scholarship on androgynous young Chinese men, no previous study has sought to use the perspectives of nationalism, masculinity and queerness to situate sissiness and sissyphobia in wider sociocultural, political and economic contexts.

17601320.label: Realisation of objectives
17601320.value: 1. The project has meticulously examined various forms of popular entertainment in recent years, including TV dramas, web dramas, social media texts, online fiction, and other mediums, to investigate the social, economic, and cultural factors that have contributed to the rise of effeminate aesthetics and other evolving male images in the contemporary Chinese context. Utilizing an interdisciplinary approach, this research places the problematic at the crossroads of queer studies, the political economy of popular culture, and the analysis of Chinese nationalism. The findings of this project reveal the intricate relationship between the construction and consumption of masculinity and the global agenda of neoliberal subject-making driven by capital forces. The research findings indicate that the “little fresh meat” is part of a larger picture of increasing diversity of gender presentations in postsocialist China and embodies shifting masculinity in a consumer society. 2. The study has critically examined the debate surrounding male effeminacy in both media and everyday life. This examination included an in-depth analysis of media representations as well as conducting interviews with individuals from various walks of life. In light of the theory of sissyphobia, the findings reveal that manhood and nationhood are closely linked in the severe criticism that this type of male aesthetic has attracted, as well as in the anxiety expressed over what an effeminate younger generation will mean for China. In addition, the study also examined the anxiety stemming from the potential failure to embody the entrepreneurial self in the context of the idolization of success. The study scrutinized marginal masculinities in this context and thus significantly enhanced and revised the original hypothesis about masculinity and subject-making. 3. The project encompasses a historical examination of the effeminate male aesthetic and its cultural meanings and evolution and transformation among East Asian countries. One icon examined in this regard is the Chinese holy monk Xuanzang (602-64). Xuanzang had posthumously become an icon of soft and queer masculinities in East Asian popular culture and a prototype of the fashionable “little fresh meat” aesthetic today. The character is played by women or even turned into a woman in many Japanese and Korean adaptations. One article resulting from this project offers a historical survey of the transformation of this image in various cultural forms in China, Japan, and Korea. It argues that the image of Xuanzang is the product of negotiations among a variety of cultural and economic forces and factors, such as the Buddhist notions of gender transgression and reincarnation, the Confucian discourse of scholar masculinity and androgyny, the cult of homosocial bond and brotherhood, as well as commercial concerns in TV and cinematic adaptations. Another case study explored the transnational flow and transformations of the “Pet Man” imaginary in East Asia. This phenomenon, influenced by Hallyu 4.0 and the toshishita romantic motif prevalent in Japanese and Korean popular cultures, has led to the emergence of an “older woman-younger man” relationship pattern as a new trend in Chinese digital entertainment, particularly TV dramas. Findings of the study indicate that the bodily rhetoric of “milky puppy” signifies a Chinese variant of moe culture and represents the commodification of the male body, as well as a female fantasy about a new mode of harmless and caring masculinity. Through a comparative study between Chinese and South Korean TV dramas, the project has identified distinctive Chinese characteristics in the portrayal of pet man masculinity in these dramas. By engaging with feminist and governmentality theories, the study has explored how gender dynamics in these dramas negotiate between neoliberal subjectivity and the resilience of patriarchal gender norms in postsocialist China. 4. The project involves ethnographic research on the reception of the male images by the Chinese younger generation, along with the diverse perspectives and critiques from individuals across various age groups. The ethnographic data collected has been integrated into multiple articles that represent the research outcomes. However, due to the pandemic, the scope and extent of the ethnographic component have been limited compared to the initial plan. Primary data has been gathered from online sources, such as forums and online articles. Conducting more comprehensive, face-to-face interviews remains a goal for future projects. 5. The project has successfully laid out the emerging male images’ relationship with heteronormative gender identities and hierarchies, in particular, its negotiations with hegemonic masculinity. A published article from the project scrutinizes the interplay of market forces, ideology, and public taste, centering on the image of the “overbearing CEO” (badao zaongcai) in popular entertainment. The research situates this archetype of a wealthy, domineering man within the broader context of gender and class in contemporary China. It investigates the ongoing negotiations surrounding gender politics and subjectivity in television’s reproduction of social power relations. The study contends that China’s gender hierarchy and ideals are closely associated with “positive energy” (zheng nengliang) moral values, which effectively serve as a new mode of governance in China. The socialist discourse on gender equality and women’s liberation has to coexist with the interests of a market that pragmatically promotes self-governing subjects. In addition, the project, by focusing on the gender policing of the state and society, has identified key voices and forces critiquing male effeminacy in contemporary China. It illustrates how masculinist nationalist discourse intertwines with the denigration of femininity and queerness. 6. Informed by Muñoz’s conceptualization of “disidentificatory performances,” which regards queer aesthetics as key for negotiating identity in a majoritarian world, the study situates the discourse of sissiphobia and homophobia in an East Asian context and draws comparisons with its Western cultural counterpart. The Western discussion of “sissyphobia” has primarily focused on the pressure gay men face to conform to heteronormative masculine images and traits in order to justify and empower their masculinity. This research, however, adopts a slightly different—and broader—definition of the term. Building on the premise of a national masculine persona, the term is used to discuss a nationally pervasive “fear of castration.” Thus, it encompasses a wider scope than homophobia, referring to the disdain for and anxiety over male effeminacy. While the pressures gay men experience to adhere to more “appropriate” masculine norms are unquestionably important for understanding anti-feminine behaviors and discourse, the case of China demonstrates that sissyphobia also operates in a heterosexual context and sometimes interacts with nationalist ideology and sentiment. 7. The project has undertaken a comprehensive linguistic and cultural examination of a selection of fashionable Chinese terms that encapsulate emerging masculinities. Notable examples include “little fresh meat” (xiao xianrou), “milky puppy” (xiao naigou), and “wolf pully” (xiao langgou), among others. This study delves into their etymological roots and cultural origins, tracing them back to Japanese and Korean influences, and draws comparisons with their counterparts in these respective languages. Furthermore, it probes the influence of gender-related Japanese and Korean discourses, such as moe, toshishita, and tanbi, on Chinese popular culture and gender discourse. By doing so, the project illuminates the transnational flows of gendered cultural symbols and their significant impacts on the construction and negotiation of masculinity in contemporary China.

17601320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601320.value: The research has so far produced five peer-reviewed journal articles/book chapters and five conference papers. Currently, a monograph proposal discussing the emerging male images in Chinese popular culture is under review. During the project term, two MPhil students have been trained, each with relevant research topics. Additionally, I have been invited to deliver talks about the interim research outcomes at several internationally reputable universities. I have also been interviewed by various international media outlets regarding male effeminacy and sissyphobia in China. The research has effectively identified certain Chinese characteristics of sissiness and sissyphobia by distinguishing between sissiness in heterosexual contexts and effeminacy in gay contexts. In doing so, it addresses regional and civilizational differences surrounding queer masculinities and contributes to a global understanding of homophobia and queerness. The media analysis in this study reveals that manhood and nationhood are closely linked in the intense criticism directed at this type of “shameful” male aesthetic, as well as in the anxiety expressed about the potential implications of an effeminate younger generation for China. Sissyphobia is thus intertwined with a fear of castration on a nationalist level (No. 1 of Part C). Drawing on the theory of “disidentificatory performances,” the project has also extensively explored the transnational flow and transformations of queer and soft male images in East Asia. Case studies reveal that the cultural proximity among East Asian countries has fostered similar trends and images related to masculinity, such as those influenced by the Korean Wave. However, the interpretation of these images varies based on local ideologies, cultural contexts, and their interaction with feminist movements within these countries. For example, the image of the “Pet Man” and the “older woman – younger man” romantic pattern in Chinese popular entertainment signifies female empowerment but simultaneously varies from Korean narratives by embodying a unique neoliberal message of self-entrepreneurship and the cult of success in contemporary China (No. 2 and No. 3 of Part C). This aligns with a new mode of cultural governance as discussed in No. 4 and No. 5 of Part C. In a predominantly heteronormative setting, gender hierarchy and ideals are closely associated with the “positive energy” moral values that drive neoliberal subject-making. As a result, the popular culture texts under discussion demonstrate how queerness and lad masculinity are co-opted and contained by the hegemonic, nationalist discourse of masculinity.

17601320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601320.value: The research thus far has primarily focused on gender performance in media and popular culture. A potential direction for future research involves investigating the ways in which people embody and enact masculinity discourses in their daily lives, as well as examining the impact of Asian queer modernity on the youth in China. To comprehensively address these questions, a larger scale and more extensive ethnographic research study is necessary. Furthermore, the politics of sissiness and sissyphobia point towards a broader landscape of gender, subjectivity, and nationalism in contemporary China. It would be advantageous to delve deeper into this direction, incorporating a wider range of media forms and diverse gender expressions. In today’s era of artificial intelligence and algorithm-driven platforms, it is crucial to explore how gender construction is regulated and manipulated by these algorithms, as well as how cultural production engenders affective transformations. With these considerations in mind, I plan to expand the scope of the research and apply for a new GRF grant. This extended research will not only contribute to a better understanding of the multifaceted nature of gender performance and identity but also shed light on the dynamic interplay between media, ideology, and technology in contemporary Chinese society.

17601320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601320.value: The project is the first comprehensive study of the effeminate aesthetic of male beauty and sissyphobia – the fear or hatred of effeminate men – in the context of contemporary China. The growing popularity of young and good-looking male stars, known as “little fresh meat,” reflects the empowerment of women alongside China’s economic growth and signifies a notable reversal of the traditional male gaze on women by commodifying the male body. At the same time, however, criticism of the male aesthetic reveals an underlying anxiety about national virility. The study uncovers the intricate relationship between nationhood and manhood while examining various social, economic, and political factors that have contributed to the emergence of this male beauty trend. Furthermore, the research delves into the transnational influence and interchange of unconventional male images and their cultural implications. It fills an important gap by comparing male images in various East Asian cultures and exploring the Chinese characteristics of soft masculinity. By offering a deeper understanding of queerness and masculinity from a global perspective, this study makes a significant contribution not only to research on gender, subjectivity, and nationalism in post-socialist China but also to that on homophobia and sissiness in a non-Western context.

17601420.value: 電子遊戲是一種廣受歡迎的消遣方式，但是長時間玩電子遊戲會削弱心理社交能力。電子遊戲障礙這問題引起了廣泛關注，世界衛生組織於二零一九年正式將其確認為心理疾病。我們的團隊通過開發一個預防計劃以解決這問題，我們的計劃評估研究已證明其在緩解兒童的電子遊戲障礙症狀方面的有效性。但是，花少時間玩電子遊戲的兒童是過著久坐不動還是過著活躍活動的生活方式仍未考究。 本項目旨在通過擴大現有的預防計劃範圍來增強我們計劃對社會的影響力。這個新計劃以置換理論和更替原理為基礎，具有附加的“數碼排毒” 部分，可促進家庭積極參與休閒活動以替代電子遊戲。我們將進行一項隨機對照試驗，以比較這兩項計劃的有效性。我們將評估兩項計劃在緩解電子遊戲障礙症狀和促進心理健康方面的功效，以及新計劃在促進活躍活動的生活方式（積極參與休閒活動和睡眠質量）方面之額外影響。

17601520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601520.value: Civil unrest during the 2019 social movements have profound social, political, economic consequences. The health burden of the social movements is also likely to be significant though less well studied, and indeed often ignored. The 2019 social movements in Hong Kong are unprecedented since the establishment of the Special Administrative Region in 1997. In the aftermath of social upheaval, most studies have focussed on mental health such as post-traumatic stress disorder, depression and generalized anxiety disorder; the burden of mental disorders is typically high in conflict-affected populations. However, the nature of the Hong Kong social movements may lead to wider health impacts including trauma, injuries, and respiratory illnesses. These non-mental health effects have not been rigorously characterised nor well-studied. Given the large degree of population exposure, the health burden of disease among the public is likely to be significant. This study will provide an independent assessment of the health impact of 2019 social movements using a mixed method approach that systematically integrates quantitative and qualitative data within a sustained program of study. Such integration permits a more complete and synergistic understanding than separate quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis. Our study will identify key perspectives of the health impact using qualitative research methods and address those views by adopting a rigorous approach to analyse quantitative data. For the qualitative analyses, we use a grounded theory approach without pre-specifying hypotheses to examine the beliefs held by different sectors of society, thus determining both specific areas of interest and also areas of concern. For the quantitative analyses, we conduct time-series analyses using ARIMA and difference-in-differences methodological approaches that permits a comparison of differences in health outcomes, before and after the social movements, controlling for bias from unobserved variables over time. Methods such as difference-in-differences offers a robust comparison of outcomes, when other risk-adjustment methods, such as propensity score matching, are not suitable. Finally, to help mend the polarisation of views and the divisions in society and also deliver positive societal impact, we will lead a focus group of community stakeholders to help interpret our findings. Consequently, we aim to determine areas of commonality, recognise areas of disagreement, as well as exploring any underlying socioeconomic and cultural factors that influence such interpretations. Our mixed methods study aims to contribute towards mending social divisions in Hong Kong by delivering a comprehensive evaluation of the health impact of the social movements. 2019年的社會動亂對於香港的社會、政治和經濟都具有深遠的影響，而其中所帶來的健康問題也可能相當嚴重。目前的研究大多數集中在心理健康上，例如創傷後遺症、抑鬱症和廣泛性焦慮症等。可是，香港的社會運動或會導致更廣泛的健康問題，包括創傷、傷害和呼吸系統疾病，而這些非心理性的健康問題到目前為止仍未得到嚴格的定性或研究。 本項研究將使用混合方法，為2019年的社會運動帶給香港大眾的健康影響進行獨立評估，把定量和定性的數據有系統性地整合到一項持續的研究計劃中。我們將使用定性的方法去確定一些有關健康影響的主要觀點，並通過對定量數據嚴格的分析來評論這些觀點。在定性分析方面，我們使用紮根理論，在没有任何預先假設的前提下，分析社會各階層所持的觀點，從而確定人們感興趣和關心的領域。 在定量分析方面，我們使用時間序列分析和差異中的差異法，比較不同健康狀況在社會運動前後的差別，籍此控制隨著時間推移由潛藏因素產生的偏誤。我們還將邀請社區利益相關人士參與一個焦點小組，透過他們的討論幫助我們進一步分析研究結果。我們的目標是確定共同點、承認分歧、以及了解導致分歧背後的社會經濟及文化因素。 我們期望透過這個混合方法研究，不但為2019社會運動帶來的健康問題進行一場全面性評估，亦有意為修復香港社會各界關係出一分力。

17601820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601820.value: Organizations attract, motivate, and retain talents by offering not just jobs, but careers. But the career advancement of a worker depends, in part, on the availability of promotion opportunities available. When there are not enough positions available, a worker may become impatient waiting for a promotion, causing the worker to be frustrated and even leave the organization. According to Peter Cappelli at Wharton, “Frustration with advancement opportunities is among the most important factors pushing individuals to leave for jobs elsewhere.” Frustration with waiting occurs not just within organizations. Angry customers hang up when it seems to take forever for their calls to be answered. Hungary diners go elsewhere when the line in front of them is moving too slowly. Extraordinary students settle for a different school if the waiting list for their top school is too long. Similar frustration can, in fact, happen anywhere with a line, be it a hospital, a post office, a checkout at supermarket, and agencies offering public housing. Organizations, in general, like to shorten lines to reduce waiting. But if lines get shortened because economic agents exited or failed to join, greater inefficiency—both to the organizations and to the society, may have occurred. Customers who hang up the unanswered call become disgruntled, giving firms a reputation for service quality. Diners who exited the line may cause the restaurants to have nobody to serve when tables become available. Students who settled for a different school may lead the original school to lose a student it is better suited. In all these situations, the basic environment has the following features. First, an organization has limited prizes—top positions in firms, seats in the restaurant, beds in hospitals, slots in schools and so on—that arises over time. Second, economic agents—workers, diners, patients, and students—may join the line and wait for the prizes. Third, if the line is too long, the agents may failure to join the line or even exiting, causing economic loss to the organization. How should the organization manage the line when many agents are waiting? Our preliminary result shows that in many situations, the optimal management of waiting incentive involves a combination of first-come-first-serve and random allocation. Agents who are waiting can be put in two tiers. The top tier agents are assigned prizes randomly, and the bottom tier agents line up, joining the top tier under the first-come-first-serve policy. 本項目開發了一個模型來研究等待激励的管理。我们得出分配獎品的最佳策略用来鼓励人员等待。我们探索此類政策對組織發展的影響， 并了解內部勞動力市場如何應對外來衝擊。

17602120.label: Project Objectives
17602120.value: To write a social history on how Christianity was disseminated along water and land routes in northeast, southeast and southwest China from 1750s to 1950s. To explore the role of religion in the historical process of defining and expanding urban China by examining how Christian churches, societies, missionaries, and immigrants brought about consequences to cities and regions under study. To develop a historical approach to the interdisciplinary study of transportation, routes, and immigration in the context of Christian evangelization in late imperial and modern China. 17602120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602120.value: This project studies the intricate and largely overlooked relationship between religious circulation, transportation routes and urban space in the historical context of state building and global connection in mid-eighteenth to mid-twentieth-century China. Focusing on the case of Christianity, it examines three cities and regions that have played a significant role in the flow of Christian groups, institutions and practices. In an era that China’s connection with the world increasingly relied on new transportation routes and means, these cities served as strategic hubs reinforcing the transnational religious exchange and the construction of indigenous religious identity. Case studies include borderland capital city of Shenyang in northeast China, coastal port cities of Hong Kong and Canton in southeast China, and inland city of Chongqing in southwest China. With geopolitical significance in different regions, they demonstrate how different cities in different historical and spatial contexts would construct ties within China and between China and the rest of the world through religious engagement. These case studies offer a multi-dimensional examination bringing religion firmly into conceptualizations of China’s state building and new century positioning embedded in its strategic initiatives such as the Belt and Road (BRI). Routes, religious space and mobility are crucial sites where social power is generated, deployed and institutionalized. Specifically, the case of Shenyang investigates how Christian Church, Qing government, regional leaders and Japanese in the borderland of northeast Asia have created religious power nexus by controlling Christian sites and communities, and how domestic migration and transnational railway capitalism have fundamentally changed the region’s religious spatial dimension. The case of Hong Kong and Canton examines Christian Church’s exploration of evangelistic strategy along the southeast coast and disputes on shifting the mission center to Shanghai around 1850s. Mobility is an important mission strategy. Geographic movements of missionaries and local believers on a regular and frequent basis, as well as this region’s exceptional transnational migration by overseas Christians challenged conventional social and cultural boundaries in Chinese society. Finally, a former treaty-port on the upper Yangtze River connecting the inland to the east coast, Chongqing has been striving to build up a logistics network in surrounding southwest China in the past decade. The Chongqing case looks at its historical trajectory of outward contact by examining two significant routes: the eastward water route and the westward railway. It asks whether such religious legacy contributes to the conceptualization of China’s intensification of ties and infrastructures along the BRI. 本課題以十八世紀中葉至二十世紀中葉來華基督教個案為例，探討在近代以來全球流動的歷史背景下，交通網絡與宗教流動、城市空間、及現代國家體系之間錯綜複雜的關係。自大航海時代以來，中國與世界的聯繫就日益依賴於新的交通路線和手段。新的交通網絡不但將沿海城市和地區逐漸納入世界體系，也逐步深入內陸城市。本課題集中研究的三個城市與區域，都在基督教的傳播與流動中發揮了重要作用，成為不同區域裡跨國宗教流動和建立本土宗教認同的核心樞紐。三個個案分別聚焦位於中國東北的邊疆省會沈陽，中國東南沿海及其港口城市香港和廣州，以及中國西南的內陸城市重慶。三個案例研究涉及中國沿海及內陸三個不同區域，各自具有強烈的地緣政治意義，展示了在不同的歷史和空間背景下，不同的區域中心如何藉助近現代世界交通網絡的建立，促成宗教流動，並在中國內部以及中國與世界其他地區之間建立起宗教和文化的互動。 這些個案的研究會提供一個多維的跨學科的視角，將宗教納入對歷史上國家建構的考量，並為新世紀中國對外發展的定位提供歷史經驗。交通，宗教空間及其流動性，是考察社會力量產生、融合及制度化的關鍵場域之一。具體而言，沈陽的個案研究將集中探討基督教在東北亞的傳播和發展，以及基督教移民對地方社會形成的作用。自晚清以來，基督教團體和清政府與東北地方社會及鄰國的互動，促成了基督教社群的建立和發展，成為東北地方社會形成不可忽視的一環。在宗教和政治的張力中，國內移民及跨國鐵路資本主義又從根本上改變了該地區的宗教生態。以香港和廣州為中心的個案研究，將考察基督教團體對東南沿海傳教戰略的探索，及其極具特色的地方宗教文化延展至亞洲和世界其他地區的歷史過程。以流動為中心的傳教活動，為當地信徒確立了定期的地域性活動。同時，東南沿海特有的海外基督徒的跨國遷徙，挑戰了中國社會固有的傳統社會和文化邊界。對內陸城市重慶的個案研究，則側重於歷史和當代發展的聯繫。作為最早的通商口岸之一，位於長江上游的的重慶是連接西南內陸和東部沿海的重要樞紐，在過去的一個世紀中，重慶逐漸成為西南地區物流網絡的中心。對重慶的研究將重點考察兩條重要的宗教傳播路線，即沿長江向東的水路和向西延伸至歐亞大陸的陸路及鐵路。對這兩條內陸中國對外聯繫的歷史軌跡的研究，將有助於我們理解和反思當下中國建立與世界聯繫的各種戰略構想。

17603120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603120.value: Imitation is a core part of learning and expressing language. In order to understand certain words, we must know what makes them imitative. These ‘certain words’ are ideophones. Ideophones exist in all known spoken languages. They are known to be easily understood by non-native speakers due to their imitative nature. Studies show that if, for example, a Dutch speaker hears a Japanese ideophone, even with zero Japanese experience, they can intuit that ideophone’s meaning. This implies that ideophones tap into a universal cognitive ability that gives sound a meaning under the right communicative circumstances. The goal of our research is to investigate how ideophones express meaning in terms of a universally accessible ability for all spoken language users: articulatory movement of speech organs. To date, linguistic research has largely ignored ideophones because most meanings cannot be expressed by imitation, e.g., foot, pink, mountain. Ideophones are limited to depictive meanings like sounds, motions, visuals, touch/feel, and inner feelings, e.g., plonk, zig-zag, bling-bling. Despite this, parent-child interactions are full of ideophones, so much so that ideophones have been proposed as a crucial component to language learning. Still, we do not know how ideophones are learnt, nor do we know what makes them easily learnable. What we do know is that ideophones frequently co-occur with what is also largely ignored by traditional linguists: depictive hand gestures. Some researchers claim that ideophones are incomplete without their co-occurring hand gesture, arguing that ideophones are analogous to depictive gestures made with the mouth instead of the hands. Given that movement is imperative for understanding hand gestures, this project hypothesizes that movement of speech organs is key to learning and understanding ideophones. No study has investigated ideophones in terms of articulatory (speech organ) movement or co-speech hand gesture. The current project seeks to close this gap by being the first to empirically incorporate mouth movement and hand gesture as factors into two ideophone learning studies. Our first study investigates whether articulatory complexity affects how well non-native speakers learn ideophones without gestures, following a well-established ideophone learning paradigm. Our second study investigates how participants use hand gestures to teach and learn ideophones of varying articulatory complexity in an iterated learning task, a pioneering study for ideophones. Cumulatively, our project will lead to a deeper understanding of how audio-visual movement can improve language learning and instruction, allowing for impact beyond the realm of research and into the classroom. 在學習和表達語言的過程中，擬態是重要的一環。對於某些單詞而言，若要徹底理解其意思，我們必須要先知道為何它們能夠表達其當中的含義，而這些「單詞」正是擬態詞。所有已知的口頭語言中都包含了擬態詞。擬態詞模擬事物特徵，所以非母語者也能輕鬆理解到它們的意思。一項研究發現，以荷蘭語為母語的人士即使在沒有學習過日語的情況下亦能夠意會到日語中的擬態詞的意思。這意味着擬態詞是屬於普遍認知能力的一部分，非母語者無須刻意學習某特定語言也能夠就相應的語境理解到該語言中的擬聲詞所表達的意思。是次研究的目的是探討擬聲詞如何透過發音器官的活動來傳達意思。 由於絕大部分的單詞，如腳、粉紅、山等，都並非擬態，因此，語言學研究大多都忽略了擬態詞。擬態詞所表達的意思，只是事物的特徵，例如聲音、動態、視覺、觸感、以及內在感受等。親子之間的互動中往往充滿着擬態詞，有人甚至提出，擬態詞是學習語言的一個重要元素。到目前為止，我們還未理解人類是如何學習擬態詞，也不知道為甚麼擬態詞能輕易被學習。我們只知道擬態詞經常伴隨一些具有含義的手勢出現，而傳統語言學者經常忽略這些手勢。有一些研究人員稱，沒有這些手勢的擬聲詞是不完整的，認為擬態詞類似於口部的活動而非手部的動作。 作出手勢的動作過程對理解手勢的意思十分重要。由此，本研究項目提出發音器官的運動是學習及理解擬態詞的關鍵。到目前為止，尚未有人從發音器官的運動或從伴隨話語的手勢的角度來研究擬態詞。因此，本項目將進行兩項研究，首次從口和手的動作分析擬態詞，以此加深對擬態詞的理解。第一項研究將透過一個學習擬態詞的範式為藍本，探討發音的複雜程度會否影響非母語者在沒有手勢的協助下學習擬態詞的效果。第二項研究則是學習擬態詞的一個嶄新研究，透過不斷重複學習，探討實驗對象如何利用各種不同的手勢去教導及學習在發音方面有不同複雜程度的擬態詞。綜合而言，是次項目將深入分析視聽相關的動作如何改善語言學習及教學，並將研究成果帶到日常教學裏。

17603120.label: Realisation of objectives
17603120.value: 1. Creation of the First Open-Access, Cross-Linguistic Database of Ideophones Objective: Establish a comprehensive, accessible database of ideophones from multiple languages. Achievements: Data Collection: Gathered ideophones from 23 languages, ensuring a diverse representation. Database Development: Implemented a user-friendly, searchable database. Accessibility: Ensured the database is open-access, with proper documentation and user guides. 2. Quantifying Articulatory Movement in Ideophones Objective: Develop methods to measure the degree of articulatory movement in ideophones. Achievements: (A) Theoretical Framework: Established a theoretically-rooted approach based on linguistic principles. (B) Physiological Measurements: Utilized tools like motion capture and ultrasound to quantify articulatory movements. ( C) Cross-Linguistic Analysis: Applied these methods to ideophones across 23 languages, providing comparative data. 3. Impact of Articulatory Movement on Learnability Objective: Demonstrate the relationship between articulatory movement and ideophone learnability. Achievements: (A) Experimental Design: Conducted experiments with participants to assess learnability of ideophones with varying degrees of articulatory movement. (B) Data Analysis: Analyzed results showing a significant correlation between higher articulatory movement and increased learnability. 4. Role of Co-Speech Depictive Hand Gestures Objective: Establish a baseline for the role of hand gestures in ideophone learning versus arbitrary word learning. Achievements: (A) Gesture Analysis: Collected and analyzed data on co-speech gestures accompanying ideophones and arbitrary words. (B) Comparative Study: Demonstrated that gestures significantly enhance the learning of ideophones compared to arbitrary words. (C) Baseline Data: Provided the first set of baseline data for future research on multimodal communication. 5. Creation of an Open-Access Gesture and Speech Database Objective: Develop a database of gestures and speech for multimodal and pragmatics-based research. Achievements: Data Compilation: Compiled a collection of gesture and speech data from multiple languages. Research Facilitation: Facilitated a follow-up research by creating a resource for studying the interplay between gesture and speech (this is my GRF 2023). For #5, I am currently updating the gesture database as I found that it will be best to further implement gesture not only from the angle of ideophone learning but also from sign language learning as the comparison of gestures and signs will enrich the quality of the data.

17603120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603120.value: Thompson, A. L., Van Hoey, T., & Do, Y.*, Dingemanse, M*. (2023). Iconicity in Ideophones: Guessing, Memorizing, and Reassessing. Cognitive Science, 47(4), e13268. Thompson, A. L., Chan, M. P. Y., Yeung, P. H., & Do, Y.* (2022). Structural markedness and depiction: The case of lower sequential predictability in Cantonese ideophones. The Mental Lexicon, 17:2, 300-324. Thompson, A. L., Van Hoey, T., & Do, Y.* (2021). Articulatory features of phonemes pattern to iconic meanings: evidence from cross-linguistic ideophones. Cognitive Linguistics, 32(4), 563-608. [Editor’s Choice Winner] The findings collectively highlight the significant role of iconicity, structural markedness, and articulatory features in ideophones. The 2023 study demonstrates that iconicity enhances the learnability of ideophones, making them easier to guess and memorize compared to arbitrary words. The 2022 research on Cantonese ideophones reveals that their lower sequential predictability and structural markedness help depict sensory imagery more effectively. The 2021 cross-linguistic analysis identifies consistent articulatory features that pattern with iconic meanings across languages, suggesting a universal basis for the iconicity of ideophones. Together, these findings underscore the unique linguistic and cognitive properties of ideophones, driven by their embodied, perceptuo-motor experiences and structural distinctiveness.

17603120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603120.value: Future studies could expand the cross-linguistic database to include more languages, particularly underrepresented ones, enhancing the diversity and comprehensiveness of the data. Additionally, integrating advanced technologies like machine learning could refine the quantification of articulatory movements, providing more precise and scalable analyses. Investigating the cognitive and neurological underpinnings of ideophone learnability could offer deeper insights into language acquisition processes. Longitudinal studies could examine how ideophones are retained and used over time, contributing to our understanding of their role in language evolution and development. The open-access gesture and speech database can be expanded to include more detailed annotations and multimodal interactions, facilitating richer analyses.

17603120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603120.value: This research project explored ideophones, which are words that vividly describe sensory experiences, like sounds, movements, or feelings. Think of words like “buzz” or “splash” that sound like what they describe. The project helped us to understand how these words work across different languages and why they are so memorable and easy to learn. The significance of this research lies in its potential to reveal universal patterns in how humans use language to convey sensory information. By studying ideophones, we uncovered how our mind process and remember these vivid words, which can help in language learning and teaching. The value of this project is diverse. It created the first open-access database of ideophones from various languages, making it a valuable resource for linguists and educators. Additionally, it examined how gestures that accompany speech enhance the learning of these words, providing insights into multimodal communication. This research not only advanced our understanding of language but also has practical applications in education, cognitive science, and artificial intelligence.

17603220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603220.value: 城市是社會運動的主要地點和人們高度依賴公共/大運量交通的地方。大運量公共交通是大量的人們的移動的必須，同時它也可能是社會運動前、後和當中的犧牲者：流量減少，服務被中斷和設施被破壞。此項目研究在社會運動中，什麼影響了大運量公交在網站、線路上的運量和韌性。它的分析將基於香港超過120天的反修例運動及其廣泛而多樣的對於香港大運量鐵路（“港鐵”）的干擾。在香港，公交分擔率達90%以上，而港鐵承擔著37%的公交運輸量。抗爭者也依賴於公交，特別是港鐵出行。 類似于反修例這樣的社會運動及其對港鐵的影響，為我們發現港鐵的運量、韌性及其在極端/異常情況下的影響因素提供了前所未有的“實驗基”。很少的既有研究利用了類似的社會運動提供的實證資料。這是因為以下兩者是非常挑戰的：(a)沒有創新性的感測器及相關大資料，卻要搜集有關實證資料；(b)僅僅依靠大資料去獲取有用、完整和全面的有關資料。 這個研究利用混合方法，將：（1） 收集和處理包括大（智慧公交卡）資料、實際踏勘、專家意見等資訊、資料，量化反修例運動中地鐵站、線的容量、韌性的影響和干擾因素；（2）利用一般線性和空間回歸模型，分析以上因素和容量、韌性的關係；（3）向港鐵提出處理社會運動的回應和恢復政策建議，確保安全服務和高/體面的機動性。這個研究將可以從研究者及其合作者已有的社會網路、資料、技術和演算法當中獲益。他們完成了若干針對智慧公交卡、專家諮詢和一般線性和空間回歸模型的專案。 這個研究將有學術和實踐上的貢獻。第一，它將提供關於地鐵如何應對不同的干擾回應和做出相應恢復的新的證據和洞見。第二，針對於香港，它將有基於實際的發現和基於證據的政策建議，這些將幫助港鐵應對社會運動前、中和後的情況。例如，在哪裡安排更多員工，怎麼能夠增加某站、某線的實際運量和韌性。

17603220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603220.value: 1. The public transportation system’s resilience in social movements has been under-explored in transportation scholarship. 2. On the one hand, public transportation enables mass mobilization of people and materials and large-scale public engagement in political/social events in transit-reliant cities like Hong Kong. On the other hand, public transportation can be an instrument for both the government and event participants—the former interferes with the public transportation service provision to manage and mitigate the adverse impacts of social movements it perceives on society, whereas the latter disrupt public transportation services or vandalize and damage related facilities to express their discontent and to put pressure on the former. 3. The dynamic resilience of the public transportation system against the above backdrop warrants more in-depth exploration. We incorporate both supply and demand shocks to theorize resilience as a public transportation system’s capability to return to a new equilibrium between the supply and demand after a disturbance. 4. Using empirical data and publicly available materials concerning the 2019 Anti-Extradition Law Amendment Bill movement in Hong Kong, we illustrate how the above theorization can be operationalized in the real-world setting.

17603220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603220.value: Like natural disasters, social movements can result in unplanned service disruptions for transit agencies like the MTRC. Theorizing, measuring, monitoring and managing resilience of transit services against this backdrop is thus very important for high-density and transit-reliant cities like Hong Kong. Proactive countermeasures in the mid- and long terms and agile responses in the short run can help us enhance resilience of transit services. Built on this project, the PI and his team hope to do more identify and prioritize the above countermeasures and responses in light of issues/complexities such as transit services were rendered by multiple entities, these entities have limited budget, and different stakeholders pursue divergent interests when coping with resilience of transit services.

17603220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603220.value: This project has come up with new indicators measuring transit stations or lines' carrying capacity and its resilience, i.e., how soon and to what degree the carrying capacity would come back to normal given an external shock such as social movements. It has also identified and quantified what might influence such carrying capacity and resilience using empirical data from Hong Kong. It thus has shed light on: 1. Transit services' carrying capacity and resilience given that there are external shocks; 2. Influencing factors of the above carrying capacity and resilience; 3. What we can possibly do to ensure the above carrying capacity and resilience to ensure a dencent level of mobility for all despite the occurrence of external shocks.

17603420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603420.value: China-Japan relations are central to the maintenance of peace and stability in East Asia. However, relations between the two nations have been fraught with difficulties. At the heart of China-Japan antipathy is the issue of history – specifically, the destructive history of Japanese imperialism in China during World War II, which fuels nationalistic outrage and controversy in China over an “unapologetic” Japan. The protracted apology controversies have aggravated mutual mistrust and animosity between Beijing and Tokyo, poisoning their bilateral relations. How do war apologies from Japan interact with the domestic nationalistic dynamics in China? In what form and under what conditions can Japanese war apologies promote or impede reconciliation in the shadow of Chinese popular nationalism? If they have the will, what are the public strategies that the Chinese or Japanese governments can use to promote reconciliation and put historical grievances to rest? While the war apology controversies are salient in public discourse, very few studies have looked at how international war apologies interact with domestic nationalistic dynamics. This is problematic as war apologies can elicit strong domestic reactions in apologizing states; and they are often filtered through the domestic media in the apology-receiver state before they reach the target public. Our project therefore studies the nexus between international war apologies and domestic nationalistic dynamics in China-Japan relations. We use a mixed-methods approach to (1) map the varieties of public narratives and nationalistic frames employed by the Chinese government to describe Japan in general and Japanese war apologies in particular; (2) uncover the varieties of nationalistic beliefs and reactions to Japan and Japanese war apologies among Chinese citizens; and (3) investigate how different public strategies toward Japanese war apologies can impact domestic opinion in China and international perceptions of China. These outputs have important implications not only for the scholarship on strategies of reconciliation, but also for countries embroiled in historical grievances who are trying to find a way out. 中日关系对于维护东亚地区的和平与稳定至关重要。然而，两国关系却困难重重。中日彼此抵触的情绪中，处于核心位置的是历史问题——特别是日本帝国主义在第二次世界大战期间在中国造成的破害，这激起了中国关于“没有歉意”的日本的民族愤慨和争议。旷日持久的道歉之争加剧了中日之间的互不信任和彼此敌对。日方的战争道歉与中国国内民族主义的变动是如何互相作用？日本的道歉在中国民族主义情绪的影响下以何种形式、在何种条件下会促进或阻碍两国和解？如果中日双方有意，两国政府可以使用哪些策略来推动和解？尽管围绕战争道歉的争论在公共话语中具有突出地位，很少有研究关注到国际战争道歉是如何与国内民族主义的变动相互作用。对这种相互作用的忽视很成问题，因为战争道歉会在致歉方国内引起反响，且常在道歉接收方经由其国内媒体的过滤之后才传达到目标公众。因此，本项目对国际战争道歉与国内民族主义变动在中日关系中的联结开展研究。我们通过多种研究方法，旨在（1）理解针对日本战争道歉的描述中的各种公共叙事和民族主义框架；（2）测量中国对日本及日方战争道歉的各种民族主义思想和反应；（3）探究针对日方战争道歉的不同公共策略如何影响舆论以及国际社会对中国的看法。上述三点不仅在学界对于和解策略的认识方面，而且对卷入历史怨愤，试图寻找出路的国家，都具有重要意义。

17603420.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603420.value: Major findings are highlighted in the abstracts of the publications/papers, adapted and summarised as follows: Research Output/Paper #1 (as listed in Part C) fielded national survey experiments to evaluate different public strategies used by the Chinese government to contain anti-foreign nationalistic sentiments, providing a first set of causal evidence on whether popular nationalism in China can be politically managed, and how. The results are published in the Journal of Conflict Resolution. Papers #2 and #3, drawn from the research conducted for Objectives #1 and #2, dived into the fundamental sources and features of Chinese popular nationalism. Using parallel national surveys in China and the United States, Paper #2 compared the sources of American and Chinese national pride, providing one of the first large-scale systematic evidence contrasting Chinese and U.S. popular nationalism. Paper #3 uncovered the substantively different understandings of what it means to be “patriotic” between and within China and the United States, and how the different understandings map onto different policy preferences. Nationalistic understandings of patriotism are dominant in the Chinese public and they, in turn, correspond to more hawkish foreign policy preferences. These results are published in Foreign Policy Analysis by the International Studies Association; and in Nations and Nationalism, the leading specialised journal on nationalism studies. Paper #4 identify the domestic dynamics that influence the effectiveness of war apologies in enabling reconciliation. Focusing on Japan's war apologies, the paper shows how negative Chinese media frames and negative Japanese public opinion reduce Chinese willingness to reconcile, yet positive frames and positive Japanese opinion do not improve goodwill. Paper #5 extends the research with cross-national experiments that randomized different forms of war apologies from Japan and how China officially responds. The results uncovered two sender-receiver gaps: The sender (Japan) sees its apology as more sincere than the receiver (China) seeing the same signal; but the sender (Japan) also significantly underestimates the receiver’s (China) willingness to conciliate. Together, the results show how receiver’s reaction shapes sender-side public support for apologies (Japan), receiver-side support for conciliation (China), and third-party observer’s sentiments (U.S.) toward both countries. Paper #6 is an additional project funded through the GRF undergraduate-training education initiative. The work is published in International Organization, the leading journal of international relations. To my knowledge, this is the first publication by a local Hong Konger (the undergraduate co-author) in the history of the journal.

17603420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603420.value: From the findings uncovered through this project, many promising avenues open for future research. For example, while we had focused on comparing the effects of positive and negative responses on the apology-receiver side, it is possible that the receiver might also hedge and respond in different ambivalent ways. Future research could explore a wider range of responses and build them into additional policy counterfactuals to investigate their effects experimentally. Also, while we have focused on the China-Japan case, our interactive theoretical framework and the methodological logic of constructing policy counterfactuals through experiments may potentially be applied to other important cases, such as Japan and South Korea, as well as other conciliation signals beyond war apologies. Finally, while we have developed a parsimonious theoretical framework that pivots on domestic audiences and payoffs, it is possible that policymakers may be motivated by more complex payoff functions; that these payoff functions may differ across different countries and institutions; and that different organizational and psychological biases might interfere with how policymakers perceive their interests. The door is thus open for future research to incorporate these variations into a similar interactive framework and field new experiments to investigate these intriguing possibilities.

17603420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603420.value: Descriptively, our work offers insights into important empirical features and fundamental nuances of mass nationalistic sentiments in China. The findings challenge conventional depictions of nationalism as a monolithic concept, and complexify but also enrich how we understand popular nationalism. More pressingly, our work also offers a potential alternative to the widespread pessimistic view that the “history problem” and conflict over war apologies between China and Japan are intractable. Through dyadic experiments in China and Japan, our data demonstrate that the extent to which Japan's war apologies can conciliate the Chinese and Japanese publics depends on the forms of apologies issued by the Japanese government, the official reactions by the Chinese government, and how the two interact with one another. Our work thus identifies the interactive crux that underpins the intractability of the war apology controversy between China and Japan, providing both the theoretical framework and experimental evidence on different policy options for managing the conflict, if and when conditions later permit.
