17603520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603520.value: 背景 懷孕、生產以及成為母親是三個緊密交織的重大人生轉變。由於在短期內經歷如此劇烈的身體和社會變化，女性往往會在生產前後感到頗多困擾。在香港這個競爭激烈，崇尚拼搏的社會裡，女性又面臨來自各方面的壓力。在全球最大年齡孕婦排行榜中，香港名列第五。孕婦年齡偏大是已知的產前抑鬱症的風險因素之一。香港女性勞動力參與率很高：20-39歲年齡組中為84.1%。而懷孕使女性更加難以平衡工作和生活。 壓力對生產及新生兒的不良影響廣泛而深遠，包括增加使用止痛藥和計劃外剖腹產、早產、出生體重輕、頭圍小、以及較低的阿普伽新生兒評分（Apgar score）、甚至重大先天性異常。有研究表明：心理困擾顯著的孕婦，其心血管系統可能因此被干擾，表現為心率變異度（HRV）低下，這可能解釋了心理壓力如何對生產造成不良的影響。但是，該發現並非定論。 基於靜觀的干預模式（MBI）可能對圍產期女性特別適用，因為它有助於培養對孕婦和新手媽媽至關重要的能力，例如：品味（savouring）、自我接納和心理韌性。最近十年的經驗研究已經顯示了產前MBI的有效性。通過干預前後的結果對比，MBI可以顯著降低壓力和抑鬱水平，效應值達到中度（Taylor，Cavanagh＆Strauss，2015）。而且對這兩個指標（壓力和抑鬱）的改善情況在後續隨訪中仍然持續可見。 在香港，我們已經開發出一套具有文化敏感性的MBI——針對孕婦的東方冥想干預（EBMI），並對其效果進行過評估（Chan，2014）。此干預措施不僅幫助參與計劃的女性應對產前壓力、減少唾液皮質醇水平，還顯示出與嬰兒的積極結果具有相關性，包括出生時臍帶血皮質醇水平升高和困難型氣質降低。較高的臍血皮質醇水平被認為可以預防新生兒健康異常（Tsuda，Kotani，Sumigama，Mano等，2016）。儘管在過去十年間，產前MBI的功效已有所展現，但由於各種實際原因，該干預模式的可用性和使用率仍然很低。此外，僅僅在產前提供有限幾次課程似乎是不夠的。圍產期女性需要更多的支持，以保障她們在產前和產後都能經常進行靜觀練習。 目標與設計 該項目旨在評估改編自“東方冥想干預（EBMI）”的“網上引導式靜觀干預模式”對孕婦的影響。此項目將招募孕中期的女性。她們可以通過網站輕鬆參與為期六週的課程，而不必在懷孕期間親自出門上課。此項目的研究助理（RA）將在主要研究者（PI）以及合作研究者（co-I）的指導下，為參與者提供在線支援直到其產後4個月。PI與co-I有著豐富的精神健康領域的臨床經驗和靜觀課程的教學經驗。其中一位還是從業多年的婦產科專家。 該研究採用平行雙組，隨機對照試驗（RCT）設計。其中包括兩項研究：一項是RCT的試點研究和一項是全面的RCT研究。為了控制干擾效應，例如：注意力和安慰劑效應，該試驗將採用“活性對照組”（active control）。對照組的參與者將接受圍產期護理的心理教育，其時間表和支持水平與實驗組相仿。試點研究的目標樣本大小為16人，而全面RCT的目標樣本大小為190人。 預期結果 在香港，每年約有50,000名新生兒分娩。為了滿足這一規模的服務需求，我們急需針對圍產期婦女的困擾，設計出一套具有成本效益，可及性和可接受的干預措施。針對圍產期女性參與障礙和成本問題，網上引導式靜觀干預模式對似乎是一個不錯的選擇。如果該模式被證明有效，那麼它將為大規模心理健康問題提供一種切實可行的解決方案：不僅可以令孕婦從中受益，而且還能提升新手媽媽的精神健康以及她們嬰孩的福祉。

17603520.label: Realisation of objectives
17603520.value: About one in five mothers experienced significant distresses during pregnancy. Previous studies have revealed the efficacy of mindfulness-based interventions (MBI) for stress reduction during pregnancy. To enhance the accessibility and practicality of the intervention, we developed an eight-week guided mobile-based perinatal mindfulness intervention (GMBPMI). The current study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of the innovative intervention through a 2-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT). To control for attention and placebo effects, the control group is an eight-week mobile-based psychoeducation programme for prenatal care. Outcomes included measures on both the mothers and newborn babies. To strengthen the scientific rigour, we included heart rate variability (HRV) as a stress biomarker in the mothers, on top of usual self-report measures. Low HRV is known to be associated with reduced parasympathetic activity, which is a core physiological response to stress. Key advantages of HRV as stress biomarker includes: 1) Avoid self-report bias 2) HRV measure devices are small and inexpensive 3) Measure procedure is noninvasive, safe and quick, and can be self-administered by users in their natural living environment. 4) HRV measure devices (designed for research) can record and transfer data to researchers directly, and thus reduce data loss/error. However, studies on the reliability of HRV as stress biomarker during pregnancy are still scarce. The rapid physical changes and challenges at different stages of pregnancy may have confounding effects on HRV. Thus we also carefully examined this critical issue with our dataset. Our analyses revealed important findings, which is a significant contribution to knowledge of the subject matter. These findings will be reported in the next section. Through careful search, we bought 198 pieces of HRV measure devices from the CorSense. The mobile phone APPS of the device is free and can be conveniently downloaded by participants. We only needed to purchase a license of central console software to retrieve data remotely from the participants’ HRV measure device. A large portion of money originally budgeted for software was thus saved and refunded to RGC. The study commenced in January 2021. We encountered severe challenges due to the prolonged COVID-19 pandemic. Many women deferred their childbirth plan. Those got pregnant were often hypervigilant of cleanliness and reluctant to join research. Moreover, because of stringent social distancing control, a core member of research team had to stay in Shenzhen, mainland China. To cope with all these exceptional challenges, we conducted RCT at two sites – HK and Shenzhen. With relentless effort, we eventually achieved a total effective sample size of 253 (178 and 75 respectively in HK and Shenzhen), surpassing our targeted sample size of 198. To increase reliability, at each measure timepoint, each participant took HRV measures for 7 consecutive days. Due to technical constraints, HRV measures could only be performed at HK site. Participants were expected to join the intervention during the second trimester (13-27 weeks of pregnancy). There were 4 measure timepoints: pre-intervention (T0), post-intervention (T1), 36-week gestation (T2) and five-week postpartum (T3). The completion rates of intervention arm at T3 (five-week postpartum) at the HK and Shenzhen sites were 73.1% and 86.8% respectively, which are highly commendable for such a long, complicated process. The findings of RCTs are positive on both the mothers and babies. They will be depicted in detail in the next section. Regarding publications, we have completed 4 papers: 1) Conceptual paper of the study: Published 2022. Reference: Ng, S.M., Leng, L.L., Chan, K.P., Lo, H.M.H., Yeung, A, Lu, S., Wang, A., & Li, H.Y. (2022, July 8). Study protocol of guided mobile-based perinatal mindfulness intervention (GMBPMI) - a randomized controlled trial. PLoS ONE, 17(7): e0270683. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0270683 2) Findings of RCT at Shenzhen site: Published 2023. Reference: Leng, L.L., Yin, X.C. Yin, Chan, C.L.W., & Ng, S.M. (2023, May 6). Antenatal mobile-delivered mindfulness-based intervention to reduce perinatal depression risk and improve obstetric and neonatal outcomes: A randomized controlled trial. Affective Disorders. 335: 216-227. DOI: 10.1016/j.jad.2023.04.133 3) Analysis of reliability of HRV at stress biomarker at different pregnancy stages: Under review in Journal of Biomarkers in Neuropsychiatry 4) Findings of RCT at HK site: Under review in China Journal of Social Work Similar to the experience of many researchers, we encountered severe delays in manuscript reviews after COVID-19 outbreak. We will make relentless effort ensuring publication of all the papers listed above. Other significant outputs arising from the study are: 1) We conducted a webinar on perinatal mindfulness practice for social work/mental health practitioners and general public in August 2021. The event attracted about two hundred participants. 2) I delivered invited lectures on mental health social work, including report of current study, at the Department of Social Work, Beijing University of Science and Technology, 17-21 July 2023. Continued communication channel for future research and education collaborations was established. 3) Grounded in the expertise gained in the project, I got a funding of $2.96M from the Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust for developing blended mode interventions for integrated family services centres - specifically two blended mode mindfulness-based interventions for the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society and HK SKH Welfare Council. Project period: January 2023 - December 2025. To conclude, despite all the exceptional challenges arisen during the prolonged COVID-19 pandemic, we have fully realized the objectives of the proposed study and revealed findings with significant theoretical and practical implications.

17603520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603520.value: EFFICIACY OF OUR NOVEL INTERVENTION GMBPMI The study adopted a 2-arm RCT design. Intervention and control groups were respectively the 8-week GMBPMI and prenatal psychoeducation programmes. Pregnant women joined programme during second trimester. There were 4 measure timepoints: pre-intervention (T0), post-intervention (T1), 36-week gestation (T2) and five-week postpartum (T3). The HK and Shenzhen sites achieved an effective sample size of 178 and 75 respectively. Completion rates at T3 were 73.1% and 86.8% respectively, which are commendable for such a long, complicated process. Intention-to-treat analyses were conducted. Key findings are summarized below. 1) Mothers’ outcomes a. Compared to control, GMBPMI showed significantly greater reduction in depression at T1, T2 and T3, with effect size (Cohen’s d) of 0.6, 0.6 and 1.0 respectively. b. Compared to control, GMBPMI showed significantly greater reduction in perceived stress at T1, T2 and T3, with effect size (Cohen’s d) of 0.6, 1.1 and 0.8 respectively. c. Compared to control, GMBPMI showed significantly greater reduction in pregnancy-specific stress at T2, with effect size (Cohen’s d) of 0.5. d. Mindfulness improvement at T1 significantly mediated reduction of pregnancy-specific stress at T2, accounting for 25.5% total intervention effect. 2) Babies’ outcomes a. Compared to control, GMBPMI showed significantly higher APGAR score (an newborn’s health indicator), with effect size (Cohen’s d) of 0.7. b. Compared to control, GMBPMI showed significant reduction in emergency cesarean, with relative risk of 0.5. c. Depression reduction at T2 significantly mediated reduction of emergency cesarean at delivery, accounting for 33% total intervention effect. RELIABILITY OF HRV AS STRESS BIOMARKER DURING PREGNANCY The rapid physical changes at different pregnancy stages may have confounding effects on HRV. Studies on this area are scarce. We examined ultra-short-term (1-minute measurement) HRV as stress biomarker by examining the association between HRV parameters and self-reported prenatal emotional distress among pregnant women (N = 230) across three trimesters of pregnancy. Subgroup linear regression analyses revealed that prenatal emotional distress was significantly associated time-domain HRV parameters, namely RMSSD, NN50 AND SDNN in the second trimester, but not in the first or third trimesters. The findings have significant theoretical and practical implications. In second trimester, ultra-short-term HRV can be an efficient stress biomarker. However in first and third trimesters, HRV measure needs to be interpreted cautiously. Further research is needed to identify a stress biomarker which is reliable in all pregnancy stages.

17603520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603520.value: The RCT findings are promising, revealing significant reduction of emotional distresses among pregnant women at moderate/large effect size. Regarding newborns, there were significant reduction of emergency cesarean and increase of APGAR scores. With satisfactory completion rates (73.1-86.8% at 5-week postpartum), overall findings support the efficacy and acceptability of GMBPMI. The study was conducted during COVID-19 pandemic, which had unclear impacts on the results. Impacts could be positive, e.g. service users preferred non face-to-face service more. Impacts could also be negative, e.g. service users experienced unusual disruptions. It is worthwhile repeating the RCTs to reassess the efficacy and acceptability of GMBPMI. It is also worthwhile repeating the RCTs in cities with different level of telecommunication development. To our best knowledge, our study is one of the rare studies carefully examined the reliability of HRV as a stress biomarker during pregnancy. Our analyses revealed time domain parameters of ultra-short-term (1 minute) HRV can be efficient stress biomarker in second trimester, but not in first or third trimesters. Further research is needed to identify a stress biomarker which is reliable in all pregnancy stages.

17603520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603520.value: The study adopted a randomized controlled trial design to evaluate our innovative 8-week guided mobile-based perinatal mindfulness intervention (GMBPMI). Pregnant women joined programme during second trimester. There were 4 measure timepoints: pre-intervention, post-intervention, 36-week gestation and five-week postpartum. The HK and Shenzhen study sites achieved an effective sample size of 178 and 75 respectively. Completion rates at five-week postpartum were 73.1% and 86.8% respectively, which are commendable for such a long, complicated process. Analyses revealed significant reduction in depression and stress in pregnant women. Regarding newborns, there were significant reduction of emergency cesarean at delivery, and increase of APGAR score, which is a widely used indicator of newborns’ health. Overall findings support the efficacy and acceptability of GMBPMI for pregnant women. To our best knowledge, our study is one of the rare studies carefully examined the reliability of heart rate variability (HRV) as a stress biomarker during pregnancy. Analyses revealed time domain parameters of ultra-short-term (1 minute) HRV can be efficient stress biomarker in second trimester, but not in first or third trimesters. HRV measure devices, which are small and inexpensive, may be used by pregnant mothers to monitor stress level in second trimester.

17604120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604120.value: 近年來，隨著香港小學發展及實施小班教學（SCT）政策，人們對研究優化本地小班教學策略及其效能日益關注。儘管西方研究對學校在協作學習上取得了一定成果（Cavas，2011; Ismail，Ngah，＆Umar，2010; Slavin，2015），卻很少研究探討在中國教育環境和儒家傳統文化下，如何引導教學策略致以學生為中心的教學範式。 基於對現存研究缺口的認識，本擬議的研究將探討並確立一套結合前線老師的反思經驗和香港小學小班教學框架的最新文獻為基礎的教學策略（例如小組學習和翻轉學習）。隨著香港學生群體愈趨多樣化（來自內地的雙非兒童數量增加），教師面對為學生提供足夠的社會和學術支援的挑戰愈來愈大。因此，研究員將舉辦一系列培訓研討會（和學習圈），以促進與會教師之間分享示範教學的實踐經驗。同時，這項研究還鼓勵教師積極參與同儕對話，知識交流和團隊合作，以模擬小班教學環境中教師合作的顯著好處。 從方法論的角度，本擬議的研究將包括四個階段：教師培訓講習班，所確定策略的實施，課堂觀察以及與老師和學生的訪談。來自12間小學，大約60名教師和600名學生將參加此研究（見圖1）。研究員將收集對教師的背景問卷調查以及有關學生在協作活動中學習經歷的問卷調查的數據，用以研究可能對上述範式轉變帶來挑戰並影響小班教學有效性的潛在因素（例如時間表和座位安排）。此外，研究員亦將進行後續訪談，以深入探討交互式學習環境如何有助於在建構主義課程中激勵和培養在學術上成功的學生。 與傳統課堂不同，社會各界普遍認為小班教學能提升學生在課堂的參與度和主動學習性。本擬議研究的結果將為倡導小班教學概念的各個知識領域提供重要見解。

17604120.label: Realisation of objectives
17604120.value: Objective 1 [i.e. To investigate the effectiveness of SCT in HK primary schools, thereby exploring the ways in which SCT can lead to a potential paradigm shift from a teacher-centred to student-oriented approach]: This objective had been met by the data collection of student learning experience questionnaires and interviews with teachers and students. In particular, the data elicited from the in-depth and focus group interviews of teachers and students indicated fairly consistent results. From the teaching perspective, most teachers agreed that each principle of the government recommended SCT framework (i.e. the ‘Six Guiding Principles’) was independent in nature and could not be mixed together to deal with certain issues (e.g. diverse learning needs and low motivation) arise in the classrooms. Rather, the ‘Six Guiding Principles’ focused more on the practical aspect and offered teachers a basic and fundamental framework for practising SCT in a reduced class size environment. In other words, this set of government recommended strategies was more favourable to novice teachers, who lack substantial experience in SCT but have to implement the scheme at a beginner level. For students, it is noteworthy that they felt stressed to express their opinions publicly in front of the whole class and could not catch the fast pace of learning within a short period of lesson time. While they might get fed up of too many group learning activities, some students preferred to stay alone and to learn in an individual way. Objective 2 [i.e. To identify and examine a set of effective teaching strategies in the SCT context to cater for larger class sizes and the increasingly diverse classroom environment in HK.]: This objective was fully achieved. More specifically, findings reported from this GRF project illustrated the positive implications of the project’s ‘Identified SCT Strategies’ for students engagement in classrooms with diverse learning needs and, further, demonstrate those strategies’ constructive effects on study interest and motivation. In this project, the students who were taught by the ‘Identified SCT Strategies’ demonstrated a higher interdependence, stronger confidence and better interpersonal skills than their counterparts, i.e. the control group students, who were exposed to ‘Six Guiding Principles’ in the learning experience questionnaires. At the same time, whilst the former group of students preferred more collaborative learning chances and appreciated collective achievements in working tasks, a significant amount of the latter group of students reported their preference for studying alone. In addition, teachers expressed that a hybrid mode of the ‘Identified SCT Strategies’ (e.g. ‘Teaching Thinking’ integrated with ‘e-Learning’) could create an interactive and open space for mutual dialogue, and serve as an inclusive and alternative strategy to mainstream instructions, thereby catering for learner diversity. Practically speaking, the participating teachers believed that the ‘Identified SCT Strategies’ in the project could deepen their understanding of the education value of SCT, and thus the strategies were more suitable for the experienced teachers to adopt in authentic classrooms. Objective 3 [i.e. To scrutinise the ideal conditions (e.g. timetabling and seating arrangements) for capitalising on the practical benefits of SCT in HK primary classrooms.]: This objective was fully completed by the end of the project. To achieve this objective, we had done interviews with the teacher participants. More specifically, the transcripts of interviews indicated that collaborating with the more experienced teachers can help junior colleagues to better prepare teaching materials and design learning activities. Furthermore, sufficient support from school in terms of workload reduction for teacher training, availability of timetabling resources and the space and flexibility to employ different SCT strategies also played a key role in sustaining the essence of SCT practices. On the other hand, the teachers reflected that the culture of traditional Chinese education context, such as the high pressure on student success in examinations, could cause the failure of schools to fully exploit the potential of SCT in classrooms. In this case, teachers intended to strictly stick on the content coverage of curriculum and complete lessons earlier to allow students enough time for doing revisions and preparation for examinations. Lastly, some teachers also concerned that very limited experienced teachers who were trained to use SCT strategies in their specific subjects and thus suggested for more subject-oriented SCT training provided by the government in the future.

17604120.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604120.value: 1. Since the research project was situated in the Hong Kong context, in which SCT has been developed as an increasingly significant notion of education by which to effect an instructional transformation from didactic to student-centred learning, the new dimensions of pedagogies it offers on addressing classroom learning difficulties, through the identified SCT strategies used in the project, is a timely one. In a broader sense, the results are not only aligned with those of many studies (e.g. Suebwongsuwan & Nomnian, 2020) in revealing the explicit benefits of an effective teaching paradigm on student commitment to active learning and schoolwork, but they also extend those findings to the domains of teacher education and professional development. In echoing Dinham et al. (2021), the study’s results illustrate the importance of teacher peer support and collaboration in enhancing pedagogical knowledge as fundamental to high-quality teaching practices. Along the same lines, the findings were also consistent with Carter et al. (2024)’s research showing that evidence-based teaching, backed up by frontline experiences, was a strategic vehicle for developing differential instruction, promoting classroom interaction and eventually advancing overall student learning. 2. Secondly, the study also provided insights for schools into how the favourable conditions and practical constraints affected the effectiveness of SCT. From a pedagogical standpoint, two suggestions were made to ease the constraints and create conditions in the quest for excellence in SCT. First, it is recommended that the EDB subsidises more teacher training courses in the forms of learning circles, through which novice teachers can acquire knowledge and practical skills via instructional coaching from experienced teachers. This policy recommendation resonated well with recent research (i.e. Shiu, 2024) demonstrating that learning circles equipped teachers with a lively experience of a more affiliated approach to pedagogical knowledge construction and raising their awareness of accountability in the classroom. Second, taking into the account of the teachers’ high pressure on student success in examinations, it is suggested that, a school-based peer support community that is emphasized on exemplary teaching reflection and teacher wellbeing be formed. On the one side, the community can function as a reflective model of peer mentoring and tutoring in the professional growth of early-career teachers (Forbes, 2004). On the other side, the community can be versatile in nature to develop peer support relationship, strengthen resilience and protect against potential mental health problems of teachers (Hansen et al., 2023).

17604120.value: Potential further development of the research includes: 1. A new GRF project, based on the practical and theoretical results of SCT in the current study, is under development. It is anticipated that this new proposed research project can be submitted in the coming round of GRF application. 2. Future writing and further research related to SCT effectiveness in Hong Kong primary schools are expected. In particular, the deeper investigation of the competency and pedagogic efficacy of teachers in SCT will be scrutinized in future potential research.

17604120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604120.value: This project investigated how the two sets of small-class teaching strategies had been applied to the primary schools with the rapidly changing classroom environment in Hong Kong (i.e. class sizes and learner diversity). To compare with the government suggested instructional framework (i.e. the ‘Six Guiding Principles’), the study identified four new dimensions of pedagogical strategies and incorporated both sets of strategies into a teaching intervention building upon a three-stage design and a quasi-experimental setting. Accordingly, the impact of different pedagogies on a potential paradigm shift was evaluated. Informed by the results of the questionnaires on students’ learning experiences, it was found that the students, who were taught by the project’s identified strategies, demonstrated a higher interdependence, stronger confidence and better interpersonal skills than the students exposed to the ‘Six Guiding Principles’. Favourable conditions and practical constraints on the implementation of small-class teaching were also revealed from the meeting notes and follow-up interviews with teachers and students in the study.

17604320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604320.value: 十二世紀初期的宋代中國，於中央和地方官學就讀的學生接近二十萬人，其中約四千名學生在位於全國教育中心的首都開封太學接受教育。這個研究項目主要考察這些太學師生在兩宋之際的生活和社交網絡。靖康二年（公元1127年），女真人攻入開封城，擄走了宋徽宗、宋欽宗和大部份宗室成員，標誌著北宋的滅亡。然而宋徽宗的第九子趙構（即宋高宗）成功避過金人的追擊逃往南方，且在那裡恢復了政治秩序，開創了南宋王朝。面對極端的政治環境，北宋晚年的太學師生——本研究項目把其定義為「太學社群」——之間的關係在南宋初年如何發展？他們的人際關係在多大程度上影響了南宋的復興？為了穩定宋王朝在江南的統治，高宗皇帝和他的大臣們長期致力於與女真征服者實現和平共處，重新掌控軍隊，建立國家與社會之間的聯繫，尋求政治支持和平定江南的叛亂。太學社群在這一政治過程中發揮了什麼作用？他們的社交網絡在多大程度上協助高宗鞏固南宋政權？他們的人際關係和政治傾向如何相互影響？ 本研究項目希望重建北宋晚期太學師生的社交網絡。通過全面剖析他們現存的著作，考察他們的社交網絡如何隨著時間演變。本項研究不僅旨在探尋那些導致人際關係發生變化的因素，還會闡釋太學社群如何應對重大政治和社會變化，從而讓我們對南宋初年的文武關係，與金和戰的討論，文人的身份認同，以至黨爭頻仍的政治制度有更深入的理解。這些發現有助我們重新思考北宋和南宋有何相似和差異之處，繼而探討南宋在何等程度上是北宋的延續。本研究將揭示北宋後期的太學社群如何鞏固南宋政權和在兩宋之際建立精英身份，藉以了解精英網絡如何連繫中古時期的國家和社會。

17604920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17604920.value: 瀕危的標誌：戰後日本從絕種邊緣拯救 「聖鶴」史

17604920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604920.value: The Red-crowned Crane is an auspicious symbol of longevity and happiness in Japan. It has been represented in art and literature for centuries, and today images of the crane are ever present in popular culture, advertising, and media. Although recognised as an invaluable asset for the people of Japan and designated a “natural monument” in 1935, by 1946 it was feared that only thirty cranes remained in Hokkaido. A winter-feeding programme initiated by a local farmer in 1952, and continued with the support of thousands of schoolchildren, renewed hope and marked the beginning of efforts to protect its habitat and rebuild the decimated population. Despite decades of local and international cooperation, however, the crane remains an endangered species. Why? What is its future? This project will shed light on postwar efforts to save the Japanese Red-crowned Crane from extinction. From farmers and schoolchildren, to volunteers and NPOs, members of the imperial family, the Self-Defense Force, and international experts, the crane has attracted significant attention by concerned stakeholders at key points of its threatened existence. During Japan’s postwar recovery and reconstruction, the crane faced threats to its habitat, food supply, and breeding patterns. What caused these threats? What role did television and other media play to publicise the plight of the bird referred to as the “sacred crane”? How were schools and education, as well as events such as an annual census and national Bird Week, used to promote knowledge, understanding, and appreciation of the crane? How did local authorities balance the demands of burgeoning domestic tourism, with conservation and preservation? When, how and why did Japan begin to cooperate with international experts from the United States, China, Korea, and Russia to assist the crane? My study will be the first in English or Japanese to examine the social, cultural, and environmental efforts to save the Red-crowned Crane in the postwar period. I will explore topics including education and public awareness campaigns, media and advertising, tourism and conservation, local and international research and cooperation, as well as rural development and sustainability. The findings from this project will be disseminated through a monograph, and two articles in high-impact journals. Today, with less than 1,500 cranes left, this study will offer an important window in to the changing relationship between humans and the natural environment of Japan’s iconic bird, as well as provide useful insights for other species on the brink of extinction. 在日本﹐丹頂鶴是吉祥的標誌﹐象徵長壽和幸福。多個世紀以來﹐藝術和文學裡也有描述丹頂鶴。在二十一世紀﹐丹頂鶴的圖像在流行文化、廣告和媒體中都經常出現。雖然日本人在1935年認定丹頂鶴為無價的資產﹐並把牠列為「自然文物」﹐至1946年北海道僅存三十隻丹頂鶴。1952年﹐當地農人展開冬季餵食計劃﹐並有數以千計學童隨後加入。此計劃燃點了希望﹐更啟動了為回復丹頂鶴的數量和保護棲息地的工作。任憑當地人和國際間數十年來的努力和合作﹐丹頂鶴至今仍然是瀕危物種。為甚麼？牠的未來會怎樣？ 此研究將展示戰後日本把丹頂鶴從絕種邊緣拯救的工作。丹頂鶴的瀕危狀態在各關鍵時刻得到農人、學童、義工、非牟利組織、皇室成員、自衛隊和國際專家等持份者的密切關注。戰後日本復甦和重建時期﹐丹頂鶴的棲息地、食物供應和繁殖習慣都面對著威脅。這些威脅從何以來？電視節目和其他媒體在宣傳「聖鶴」的困境中扮演甚麼角色？學校、教育、年度普查及全國雀鳥週怎樣增強國民對丹頂鶴的認識、了解和欣賞？當地政府怎樣平衡國內旅遊發展的急增需求與丹頂鶴的保護和保育？日本何時、怎樣、及為何因保護丹頂鶴而與來自美國、中國、南韓及俄羅斯的國際專家開始合作？ 我的計劃是首個以英語或日語研究戰後日本在社會、文化和環境保護方面拯救丹頂鶴的工作。我會探討教育與公眾意識宣傳活動、媒體與廣告、旅遊與保育、當地及國際研究和合作、及農村發展與其可持續性等議題。此計劃的成果將以一專著及兩篇於高影響因子期刊刊出的文章發佈。現時丹頂鶴的數量只剩不足1500隻。此計劃將揭示這代表日本之雀鳥的自然生態和人類社會之間正在改變的關係﹐並為保育其他瀕臨絕種的動物帶來啟示。

17605320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17605320.value: 專制與民主﹕十九世紀英國文學中的中國與美國

17605320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605320.value: It has long been recognized that the American and French Revolutions shaped nineteenth-century British attitudes towards democracy. Despots and Democrats expands beyond this Atlantic narrative by identifying the overlapping imaginative significance of China and the United States to British liberal and democratic thought. In doing so, I analyze the intersecting narrative and figurative representations of China and the United States in nineteenth-century British literature. British writers saw the United States alternately as a land of democratic promise and as a country ruled by despotic majority, in which individuality eroded under the pressure of social conformity. China, on the other hand, was seen as timeless and unchanging, under the rule of the “despotism of Custom.” I contend that British writers navigated debates about democracy by blurring together conceptual opposites: figures of Asian despotism and American democracy. This way of making opposites coincide allowed British thinkers to triangulate their own liberal political culture. Nineteenth-century Britain oversaw a series of electoral reforms that involved heated debates about the potentialities and pitfalls of democracy. However, many scholars argue that these reforms were implemented not to spread democracy but to impede further democratization. In this project, I contend that nineteenth-century British nationalist identity—specifically, a liberal individual ethos—was informed by contrasting political and cultural imaginaries. This manifested in parallel figurative, metaphorical, and narrative practices that arose in British literary depictions of China and the United States. Examples include the metaphor of contagion expressed in British fears of Americanization and Asian immigration, and the use of Bret Harte’s poem, “The Heathen Chinee,” in making sense of Americans through the lens of the Chinese immigrant. My research will draw on a range of source material, including novels, newspapers, and political and philosophical writings. Thus, I demonstrate that British political imaginations not only flowed from metropole to periphery but also involved complex, overlapping forms and modalities. I contend that British writers constructed the self-regulating individual British subject by identifying American democracy with stereotypes about Chinese despotism and the Asian crowd. Scholars have long understood nationalism as imaginary and constructed, often in contrast to perceived others; this project, however, will reveal the ways that British liberal self-constructions emerge through a triangulation of imagined Chinas and Americas. Thus, this project approaches the literary construction of nation through transnational thinking. 美國與法國革命塑造了十九世紀英國對民主的態度，這早已是不爭的論述。本文將分析十九世紀英國文學中對中美兩國的敘述及比喻，思考中美兩國交疊的意象對英國民主自由思想的重要性，試圖從更廣闊的角度探討這一論述。英國作家認為美國既是一片充滿民主希望的土地，又是一個被大多數人專制統治的國家，個人特質在社會規範下被消磨殆盡﹔而中國則被視為受「專制風俗」所限一成不變的國度。本文認為英國作家藉著模糊亞洲專制與美國民主兩個對立概念的界線為其立論爭辯，把兩個對立概念合二為一讓英國思想家從中構建出自身的自由主義政治文化。 在十九世紀，英國經歷了一連串選舉改革，就民主的潛力與隱患展開激烈討論。然而，很多學者認為之所以推動這些改革為的不是推廣民主，而是阻礙民主發展。本文認為十九世紀的英國民族身份——尤其是自由個體的價值觀——就是通過對比政治和文化意象衍生而成，以平行比喻、隱喻和敘述方式呈現，從英國文學如何描繪中國和美國可見一斑。本文引用的例子包括英國瀰漫恐懼美國化及恐懼亞洲移民的相關隱喻，以及透過美國作家布雷特．哈特(Bret Harte)的詩作《異教徒中國佬》(“The Heathen Chinee”)一窺美國人眼中的中國移民。本文對小說、報章和政治及哲學著作等各類文體進行研究，析述英國的政治意象不只從大都市流進地方社會，更牽涉各種複雜、相互重疊的形式和形態。 本文認為英國作家利用對美國民主、中國專制和亞洲群眾的刻板形象塑造出能自我調節的英國個體。學者長久以來認為民族主義乃文化虛構和構建之情感，通常與他人認知形成對比﹔本文則旨在揭示英國民族的自由個體形象乃英國文學借助對比自身與中國和美國人之刻板形象帶來的反差構建而成，循跨國角度思考文學作品如何塑造國家形象。

17605420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605420.value: This project investigates how the development of commercial aviation took shape in Hong Kong as the city developed into a powerful economy. As I examine how commercial aviation and Hong Kong’s historical trajectory influenced each other’s developmental path, I seek to understand the articulation of local specificities of an expanding global industry in the context of Hong Kong’s economic takeoff. Aviation facilitated intense flows of people, goods and capital. The development of the industry allowed Hong Kong to converge with a common platform while accommodating articulations of local variations. More than merely enhancing physical connections and economic flows, commercial aviation shaped the people, spaces, and institutions that it connected. Focusing on policymakers in Hong Kong and London, Cathay Pacific and local carriers that operated alongside industry titans such as B.O.A.C. and Pan American, this is the first academic study that combines the business history of aviation with an examination of the city’s economic and political transformations. Starting with aviation’s humble foray into Hong Kong in the 1930s and concluding with the move of the airport from Kai Tak to Chek Lap Kok in 1998, I will explore how commercial aviation fashioned regional and global connections against the backdrop of shifting geopolitics and in response to the exigencies of Hong Kong’s economic development. Initially deployed at the exclusion of most local residents, air traffic drove Hongkongers to seek inclusion in a worldwide network that embraced Hong Kong. Subsequent economic growth enhanced access to the skies for aspiring travelers in the city. Privatization and deregulation in the Western markets opened international airways to colonial Hong Kong just as the looming handover prompted a shift in business strategies among local operators to accommodate the incoming PRC regime. At the same time, the transformed airways allowed certain anxious Hongkongers to envision livelihood beyond the territory, fuelling the city’s diasporic impulse and enabling the expression of transnationalism. Rather than accepting air travel as Hong Kong’s arrival in the era of global mobility, this project examines through the airline industry how Hongkongers asserted themselves in a world construct in a bid to accrue socioeconomic benefits, negotiated their interests in the city’s economic success and articulated their expressions of modernity. The resulting monograph will examine how flight routes remapped and repositioned Hong Kong, how the infrastructures of air mobility shaped the city’s development, and how air travel engendered new worldviews and fueled aspirations in the high-growth economy of Hong Kong. 此項目研究民航業如何在香港經濟發展的過程中形成。在研究民航和香港歷史發展中如何彼此影響中，我試圖了解在香港經濟騰飛的背景下，民航這個全球性行業如何呈現本地特色。 航空促進了民眾˴貨物和資本的大量流動。航空業的發展使香港能夠在適應本地特色的同時，融入一個共同的平台。商業航空不僅增強了人際往來和經濟流動，還塑造了其聯繫的民眾˴空間和機構。以身處香港和倫敦的決策者˴國泰航空，以及英國航空和泛美航空公司為主要研究對象，此項目將會是首個把航空商業歷史與城市經濟和政治轉型結合起來的學術研究。 由1930年代的雛形，到1998年機場從啟德遷往赤鱲角，此項目將探討在地緣政治變化的背景下，民航業如何在迎合香港的經濟發展的同時，塑造了區域和全球的聯繫。 空中交通最初並沒有把大多數的本地居民包括在內，因此驅使了香港人尋求融入全球網絡的途徑。隨後經濟增長為城市中冀望旅行者提供了更多飛行機會。西方市場的私有化及放鬆管制，為殖民時代的香港開通了國際航道。正值九七回歸在即，本地運營商趕快改變了業務戰略，以迎合九七後的中國政權。與此同時，轉型後的航線使焦慮不安的港人能夠在海外生活，加劇了港人的流散。 該研究不接受航空把香港領進全球流動時代，反而通過航空業探討香港人如何在世界架構中，為自己佔一席位，以期獲得社經利益，並實現了他們對現代化的理解。研究成果將探討飛行路線如何把香港重新定位，以及空中交通基建如何改變了香港的發展，進而了解航空旅行如何帶來新的世界觀，並激發港人在香港經濟高度增長進程中的期盼。

17605720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605720.value: My research seeks to identify an institutional design for charities in Hong Kong that (re)builds trust and legitimacy for this sector. The history of charitable activities in Hong Kong can be traced to the colonial Hong Kong period, which began in the mid-19th century. Yet despite the importance of charitable activities to the well-being of a civilised, cohesive and caring society, there is still no comprehensive law governing charities in Hong Kong. Scandals, fraud, inadequate regulation, a lack of accountability and transparency, and poor governance and management practices are amongst some of the issues that have undermined trust in and the perceived legitimacy of the charitable sector in Hong Kong. At the same time, the existing legal regime – whereby the relevant rules governing charities are buried in discrete areas of law (such as trust, contract and company law) developed primarily to govern business relationships – may not be sufficient to address emerging trends in the sector, including growth and diversification of charities on the one hand, and commercialisation of them on the other. The primary objectives of my research project are to critically review the legal framework embodying the facilitative rules for charitable operations in Hong Kong and demonstrates that there are no corresponding coherent regulatory rules for charitable governance (including governance, management practices, and accounting and accountability systems). Thereafter, my research will compare the laws and operational experiences of laws governing charities in Hong Kong with those in the UK and Australia, both of which have recently undertaken substantial reforms on charity law – reforms which have also been subject to intense public debates. In light of the challenges faced by the charitable sector in Hong Kong, my research explores the necessity of a tighter, more transparent regulatory regime if the sector is to regain public confidence. There is a growing view globally that having an independent and dedicated charities regulator represents best practice. I seek to distil best practices from the UK and Australia, and then explore the desirability and feasibility of introducing a charities regulator in Hong Kong, as well as formulating recommendations to enhance the legal regime for governing charities more generally. 我的研究旨在找出可以重構對香港慈善組織的信任和其合法性的制度設計。香港慈善活動的歷史可以追溯到19世紀中葉開始的香港殖民時期。儘管慈善活動對文明、團結和關懷社會的福祉至關重要，但香港至今仍沒有一部全面的法律來規範慈善組織。醜聞 、欺詐、監管不力、缺乏問責制和透明度以及不良的治理削弱了公眾對慈善組織的信任和其合法性。同時，現有的法律法規埋在離散的法律領域中（主要是為管理商業活動而製定的信託法、合同法和公司法），可能不足以應對慈善組織的增長、多元化、商業化等新興趨勢。 透過審視香港慈善活動法律框架，本研究項冀證明慈善治理法規（包括治理，管理實踐以及會計和問責制）落後。研究也會比較香港與英國和澳大利亞的慈善法的法律和運作經驗。這兩個國家最近都對慈善法進行了重大改革，引起了激烈的討論。 鑑於香港慈善組織所面臨的挑戰，如果要恢復公眾對慈善組織的信任，就必須採取更嚴格和透明的監管制度。越來越多的人認為，擁有獨立而專門的慈善組織監管機構是最佳實踐。我試圖借鑒英國和澳大利亞的最佳做法，探討在香港引入慈善組織監管機構的可取性和可行性，並提出建議以改慈善機構法律制度。

17605720.label: Realisation of objectives
17605720.value: There was complete achievement of all 4 Objectives on schedule. Objective 1: I thoroughly examined the Hong Kong laws, regulations, and operational experiences pertaining to charities in Hong Kong. Several recent high-profile cases on charities were also examined. The study produced a detailed inventory of information on the relevant legal rules under examination. Objective 2: I thoroughly compared similar legal mechanisms in the UK and Australia. Specifically, I reviewed the recent reforms to charities laws in the UK and Australia, as well as the practical experience of establishing a charities regulator to regulate the charity sector in both jurisdictions. Additionally, in the course of my research, I found it relevant to examine the recent charity law reforms in mainland China in order to obtain a better understanding of the different modes of regulation of charities across different jurisdictions. A research framework was devised for a comparative baseline study of the laws, regulations, and operational experiences pertaining to charities in Hong Kong, mainland China, Australia and the UK. An inventory of materials was collected. Due to travel restrictions caused by COVID-19 (which were only lifted in late 2022/early 2023), I was not able to conduct field visits to Australia and England as planned. Instead, I (i) devoted extra time on collecting the necessary materials and comparing closely the legal rules and their practical operation as detailed above; and (ii) attended conferences via Zoom where possible. I was invited to speak at international conferences (via Zoom) organised by Singapore, Australia and UK law schools on the topic of charity law reforms and traditional Chinese religions in Hong Kong. Once the COVID-19 travel restrictions were lifted by the Hong Kong government in late 2022, I also made immediate plans to attend a conference in Melbourne, Australia in February 2023. Objective 3: In light of the research activities undertaken under Objectives 1 and 2, I identified several major issues of enquiry that are pertinent to Objective 3. Specifically, I examined a couple of unique features of charity law in Hong Kong that may call for reform/review, namely (1) whether ancestral worship trusts satisfy the requirement of ‘public benefit’ for the purpose of charitable trusts; and (2) whether a fiduciary duty should be imposed on members of charitable companies, being the most preferred structure of charity in Hong Kong. In relation to (1), I examined the interaction between English common law and Chinese customary law in the development and regulation of traditional ‘tso/tong’ in Hong Kong and whether they should be treated as religious charitable trusts. I attended an international academic conference (online) participated by eminent academics in the field to disseminate the research findings and the research findings were published in a book chapter published by a prestigious academic press in Law in the UK. In relation to (2), I also examined the issue of fiduciary duty of members of charitable companies in light recent UK Supreme Court and Hong Kong court decisions on the subject. I attended an international conference in Melbourne in February 2023 as soon as the COVID-19 travel restrictions were lifted to disseminate the research findings. The research findings in the form of an academic article is now under review by a peer-reviewed journal. Objective 4: Based on the research findings in Objectives 1 and 2, I addressed the desirability and feasibility for introducing a charities regulator in Hong Kong. Taking into the account the strengths and constraints of the existing institutional framework, as well as the difficulties experienced by the charities regulators in both jurisdictions examined in Objective 2, including the need to balance between accountability and support; politicisation of the charities regulator; and inadequate funding and accountability issues etc, I expressed caution on the introduction of a charities regulator. The findings will be published as a book chapter in a forthcoming edited collection on comparative and international perspectives on charity law by a leading academic Press in Law on open access to ensure wide circulation of the research findings to the international audience.

17605720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605720.value: I have conducted comprehensive research on charity law in Hong Kong. The major research findings are as follows :- (1) The history of charitable activities in Hong Kong can be traced to the colonial Hong Kong period, which began in the mid-19th century. English judges in the early colonial period adapted English trust principles to resolve disputes involving Chinese customary landholding devices known as tsos and tongs. Whilst there were suggestions to characterise these ancestral worship landholding devices as charitable trusts, care must be exercised to differentiate them from other traditional Chinese religions practised by the general public (Publication #1). (2) Having reviewed the evolution of a local charity landscape, my research then moved on to address how trust and legitimacy in the charity sector can be sustained. I examined the government-driven, regulator-based supervisory governance framework for charities in the UK, Australia and mainland China, as well as difficulties experienced by the charities regulators, including the need to balance between accountability and support; politicisation of the charities regulator; and inadequate funding and accountability issues etc. In light of the historical background of the development of the charity sector in Hong Kong, I suggest that care should be exercised in the introduction of a charities regulator and self-regulation of the sector can be enhanced through codes of conduct (Publication #2). (3) Given that company is the most preferred structure of charity in Hong Kong, I examined the implications of a recent landmark UK Supreme Court decision on imposing fiduciary duty on members of a charitable company for Hong Kong and explores the need to re-examine the interaction between company and fiduciary law in the charity context (Publication #3). I attended several international conferences to disseminate the above research findings. I have already published 2 book chapters and will publish another journal article in due course, meaning that I will be able to publish 3 journal articles/book chapters as stated in the objectives. Note: It is unfortunate that the field visits could not go ahead as planned due of the travel restrictions imposed by the HK government as a result of COVID-19. Consequently, a large portion of the funding designated for ‘travelling’ and ‘conferences’ was not utilised. The under-utilisation of the relevant funding should therefore be read in this light.

17605720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605720.value: Whilst my research focused on the different modes of regulation of charities in order to identify the most effective institutional design for the governance of charities in Hong Kong, I have identified further doctrinal and practical questions that will affect the institutional design. The doctrinal questions include: the distinction between activities and purposes in delineating the boundaries of charities; the public benefit requirement of charities etc. In terms of practical issues, the institutional design of the charity framework will be affected by the operational environment of charities, including the need to balance between accountability and support; politicisation of the charities regulator etc. It is hoped that field visits could be conducted in the future to obtain better understanding of the practical obstacles faced by charities regulators. Further, the relevance of charity law reform in China should not be underestimated. Given the increasingly close interaction between charities in Hong Kong and mainland China, some collaborative research can be explored. My current research has enabled further work on the above specific issues and I hope to seek further collaborative and/or interdisciplinary research funding in the near future to conduct further research identified above.

17605720.value: The history of charitable activities in Hong Kong can be traced to the colonial Hong Kong period, which began in the mid-19th century. My project first examined how English judges in the early colonial period adapted English trust principles to resolve disputes involving Chinese customary tsos and tongs that were preserved in Hong Kong. Whilst there have been suggestions to characterise these ancestral worship landholding devices as charitable trusts, care must be exercised to differentiate them from other traditional Chinese religions practised by the general public so as not to reinforce the entrenched privileges of an individual clan. 17605920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605920.value: The Soviet-Cuban relationship was once at the center of world politics. Political scientists, economists and journalists produced a large body of work on the subject; crucial insights into a central relationship in world geopolitics were at stake. As Cuba receded from the global imaginary, and later still, with the fall of the Soviet Union, interest on the subject retreated to two limited communities of scholars: Latin Americanists and scholars interested in the single most dangerous episode of the Cold War, the Cuban Missile Crisis. In other words, at the very moment when decades of speculation could finally be verified and put on sound archival footing, interest moved on. Over the ensuing three decade, very little research was carried out on the basis of primary documents on that critical relationship. Two major pieces of archival research have confirmed Cuban policy independence in its surprisingly bold involvement in Africa, a subject of much conjecture in the Cold War-era literature on the relationship. And if relatively small progress has been made empirically, less has been done to rethink the relationship theoretically. This project attempts to move both these undertakings forward by contrasting historiographical claims with archival evidence and reframing the relationship within the historical transformation of the political economy of the capitalist world order. Focusing on the political economy of the Soviet-Cuban relationship, this study will investigate the tension-inducing effects that sharply fluctuating international markets had on the relationship, how these were resolved, and what this says about the socialist world. Rather than pursuing a more accurate set of numbers in terms of Cuba’s economic dependence on the Soviet Union, an issue that engaged much of the scholarship on the relationship, the project will distill the ways in which the hegemony of the US dollar limited and redirected the political choices of both allies. But it will also examine the extent to which the Soviets were able to carve out over time a degree of monetary sovereignty in the debt-fueled global exchanges it engaged in, paradoxically offering Cuba the possibility of circumventing its reliance on Soviet technology and material production. In other words, along with promoting archive-based verifications of earlier arguments, the project will offer new theoretical venues for understanding this and other such relationships of the second-half of the 20th century, all the while looking to overcome the defunct frameworks that rendered this relationship irrelevant at the end of the Cold War. 苏古巴关系曾经是世界政治的中心。政治学家，经济学家和新闻工作者就这一主题开展了大量工作；对世界地缘政治中心关系的关键见解正处于危险之中。随着古巴从全球假想中退缩，后来，随着苏联解体，人们对该话题的兴趣又退回到了两个有限的学者群体中：拉丁美洲主义者和对冷战中最危险的一次事件感兴趣的学者，古巴导弹危机。换句话说，在几十年的投机活动最终可以得到验证并立于稳固的档案立足点的那一刻，人们的兴趣不断增强。在随后的三年中，基于主要文件的关于这种关键关系的研究很少。一项重要的档案研究已经证实了古巴政策在其出人意料地大胆介入非洲方面的独立性，这是冷战时期有关这种关系的文献中有很多推测。而且，如果凭经验取得的进展相对较小，那么从理论上重新考虑这种关系的工作就很少。该项目试图通过将史学主张与档案证据进行对比，并在资本主义世界政治经济学的历史转型内重新构架关系，来推动这两项事业向前发展。本研究着眼于苏古关系的政治经济学，将研究急剧波动的国际市场对这种关系产生的紧张影响，如何解决这些关系以及这对社会主义世界的看法。该项目不是在古巴对苏联的经济依赖上寻求一套更准确的数字，这个问题吸引了许多有关两国关系的研究，但该项目将提炼限制美元霸权并重新引导美元的方式。双方盟友的政治选择。但是，它也将研究苏联在一段时间内能够在其所进行的以债务为动力的全球交易所中实现一定程度的货币主权的悖论，这自相矛盾地为古巴提供了规避其对苏联技术和物质生产的依赖的可能性。换句话说，除了促进基于档案的对较早论点的验证之外，该项目还将为理解20世纪下半叶的这种和其他这种关系提供新的理论场所，同时力图克服那些已经失效的框架。这种关系在冷战结束时无关紧要。

17605920.label: Realisation of objectives
17605920.value: The project achieved most of the objectives it set out to achieve. It did so despite the challenges that covid presented, as most of the time period covered by the grant feel under the extraordinary circumstances of global shutdown, restrictions for meetings and face to face interactions, and barriers to travel here in Hong Kong. The application had been produced in 2019, and so this covid complications were simply not foreseen—nor, frankly, did I think them remotely possible. The difficulties were somewhat eased by extending the period of the grant, but the obstacles remained real, and no doubt left a mark in what was ultimately possible to do. I had hoped to travel to Cuban archives and develop some kind of network there. This has proved impossible, which in turn led to a refocus in the research that could use the Cuban example within a broader rubric for understanding the international political economy of the Socialist world. This has been quite a successful pivot that is already leading to further developments beyond this project. First and foremost, as promised in the application, the project delivered to articles published in internationally recognized journals. Importantly, I used the project to enlarge the kinds of scholarly communities that interact with one another. Latin American studies and Soviet/socialist historical studies have rarely been in conversation, but I provided one avenue with my first article. Likewise, the second article aimed for a more global interaction that included not just scholars of the Soviet Union and Latin America, but also China, Eastern Europe, business history and economic historians. The project further encouraged these interactions through a series of participations in conferences and scholarly workshops that include presentations in Mexico, Macau, Czechia, Holland, France, Austria, Germany, Hong Kong and the United States. Many of these were necessarily online. I also used my teaching to circulate knowledge gained from this project, especially in my courses on capitalism and late socialism. Most recently, this semester (Spring 2024) I am teaching a course on science fiction and socialism/capitalism/Cold War that departs from the global outlook on socialism I was able to gain through this project, and which is laying the groundwork for my next book project. I will now lay out more specifically which objectives the project achieved fully. As per the first objective, it certainly has improved our understanding of capitalism and socialism through the discovery not only of contrast but, especially, interpenetration of both worlds in the second half of the 20th century. The project has also put in circulation an array of empirical material that bore on this question. The 2022 article this project bore, then, helped achieve the first objective as well as the third and fourth. The project aimed to make important historiographical corrections, and one of the most rewarding achievements of the project, on a personal level, was the personal response that article elicited from its scholarly “target,” emeritus Harvard historian Jorge Dominguez, who has been the leading figure on Cuban studies for decades. He wrote a personal email to both respond to the article (a rare practice these days) and to praise it; in that email he expressed that he was largely convinced by my evidence and argument, despite the fact that it conflicted with much of what he had worked out as a political scientist with limited empirical sources decades ago. I included the email in my last progress report. This is a small—but personally satisfying and important—bit of evidence of the success the work had in putting the different fields in conversation and overturning some of the historiographical received wisdoms. The second article further helped in expanding the conversations to the many fields the project touched upon, as I said earlier. But it especially helped with the fifth objective, which aimed to advance theoretical perspectives on the question of international political economy and international history through the case of international socialist relations. This too has yielded a very tangible outcome beyond the article itself. I have been invited to be keynote speaker to a conference in Cambridge University on the global history of money outside the West, where the historical category of money has been largely studied. The scholar inviting me specifically mentioned that article as the reason for the invitation. This is because that article signified a rare attempt at theorizing money in a socialist context. I must admit that the other main attempt had been mine as well, in a 2019 article; but this time I was extending the theorizing into an international sphere with the help of this project. I have asked my hosts to make sure they invite one of my scholarly idols on theories of money, the sociologist Geoffrey Ingham, and I am happy to report that he too will be joining us in what promises to be a relatively large conference that will advance those theoretical approaches a great deal. There is one area in which this project fell short, and that is on the second objective. While I have now made Latin America part and parcel of my teaching, I have not been able together larger venues for developing interest in Latin American studies in Hong Kong (beyond my courses, where Latin America is present, but only in a limited manner). No doubt the failure to develop a network in Cuba was part of the reason. I had hoped to invite and in turn be invited to conferences, meetings and other sorts of scholarly interactions in Cuba and with Cubans as a consequence of this project. That proved impossible for much of it, and I ended up needing to pivot a bit in my second article toward a more global and theoretical direction. Nevertheless, the end of the project does not mean the knowledge gained from it disappears as well, and the articles have already generated various engagements as reviewer for work having to do with Cuban and Latin American relations with the socialist bloc. Furthermore, the University of Hong Kong has been expanding its offerings on Latin American studies. I expect that over the next few years my participation with that scholarly community will intensify as a consequence of the work related to this project, both in Hong Kong and abroad. Much of my future work will be building on this project. I hope in the future to reengage more specifically with Soviet-Cuban relations, on which I have developed a certain kind of expertise that could be used in the realization of another article or two. Inasmuch as the project has initiated me into an engagement with the 1970s, it has laid the basis for a more medium-term project I have in on the socialist world and the transformations of the 1970s. In time I will certainly be seeking GRF funding on this. Finally, the project has served to expand my horizons beyond the Soviet Union and into the socialist bloc more widely, which is having a fairly immediate impact on the research I am currently active with on the development of science fiction during the Cold War, with a strong socialist bloc component.

17605920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605920.value: Two kinds of findings have derived from the investigations of this project. The first has to do with relations between the Soviet Union and Cuba. While most scholars have seen these relationship as either an instrument of Soviet foreign policy, or within the prism of Cuban resistance of Soviet hegemony, this project uncovered the extent to which the relationship was mediated by the global economic forces of the capitalist world. Sugar and oil underpinned the relationship between the two socialist countries, but this exchange was not carried out autarkically. In their talks with one another, agents of both socialist countries were continuously referring to the capitalist world because each country hoped to use the other to change their relations to the capitalist world, which was ultimately preponderant. This realization has led to a second set of findings: a rethinking of what socialist relations were more generally. I laid these down in a think piece in the journal European Review of History/Revue européenne d’histoire. The particularities of the Cuban connection have really helped to tease these out. One of the major dynamics that shows is the way Cuba was able to use the construction of a set of debt relations within the socialist world to achieve something that otherwise seemed to escape the socialist world: multilateral economic relations. These expanded beyond the socialist world to encompass areas under US dollar hegemony in the 1970s. In fact one of the most interesting discoveries is the observation that as the dollar economic expanded in the 1970s on the back of the oil flows out of the Middle East, so did the kind of multilateral exchanges that had eluded socialist relations until then. This is to say, as I did in that article, that, in economic/monetary terms, one should think of the socialist bloc not as an alternative world—as is the norm in the field—but rather as a subaltern world.

17605920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605920.value: There are many potential venues for development. One obvious path is to begin the work of recasting the Soviet-Cuban relationship beyond the kinds of Cold War binaries to which it has been subject. Work both in Russian and Cuban archives would be necessary for this. Another path forward is to submerge knowledge of that relationship into wider debates over what socialism was, and how to think of the world it created. This would allow a rethinking of categories of political economy that sorely need to be introduced into the kinds of political understandings that have reigned in the historiographical thinking on Cuba. Money, labor, trade, value, resources exploitation and exchange, all these need to be reinscribed into our understanding of the socialist world and its relationship with the non-socialist world in order to arrive at a usefully global history of the second half of the 20th century.

17605920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605920.value: The socialist world continues to be understood almost exclusively as an ideological space, as a failed, often impossible, attempt to achieve some kind of utopian program. But we know that banks, corporations and economic life are categories for analysis that are supremely important for understanding the world we live in. The newspapers tell us so daily. We need to reintroduce those notion in historical analysis, and specifically in the analysis of what socialism was in practice. The archives show that these were the categories that drove relations among socialist countries, not least Soviet-Cuban relations. When agents of both countries sat down, they did not sit down to exchange ideas and thoughts on the global march of socialism, but mainly to negotiate prices, commodity exchange, development aid and material exchanges in the context of opportunities, difficulties and transformations elsewhere in the capitalist world. Embedding the socialist world needs to be about more than presenting it as an enemy alternative of the capitalist world, but rather as embedded within it, a set of countries navigating the same power dynamics, problems and prospects that much of the world likewise confronted.

17606620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17606620.value: Through a study of archival collections of popular North China urban narrative verse, this project aims to identify and contextualise nineteenth- and early twentieth-century cultural themes that are not available in other literary forms. Adapting methods focused on materiality of the book and common everyday experience, analysis of this popular corpus will expand understanding of China’s literary history beyond perspectives dominated by elite cultural production. “Bun booth books” (mantoupu ben), cheap and very small songbooks printed on the same paper used under steamed buns (mantou), were sold through bun booths and other street outlets in large numbers. While their content has been found to range across various popular song forms and themes, these local songbooks contain previously undocumented narrative verse current among urban commoners. Shidiao (popular songs) per se are not new to scholarship in Chinese literature, but the possibilities bun booth books present for placing a large corpus of such works in time and space, as well as within a distinct set of production and consumption practices, promises to enhance our understanding of how they fitted within cultural and social processes, and, equally importantly, how they fitted into the lives of the urban lower-class women who were their primary readership and audience. The project will collect data from known deposits of bun booth books and related songbook artefacts preserved in international libraries (and private collections) in Asia and Europe, analysing material and textual layers of information, as well as noting indicators of time and place of production and sale. Analysing textual and material data from this hitherto neglected body of texts will reveal new perspectives on urban lower-class cultural practices otherwise unavailable to Chinese literary history, notably the functioning of local or popular literacies. 本研究課題試圖通過考察大量華北大眾唱本的特殊收藏，揭示和重構十九世紀下半葉和二十世紀初期的一些在其他文本裡找不到的特殊文化主題。研究方法將特別注重對這些唱本實物以及當時平民日常生活經驗的分析，目的在於揭示這些一度極其流行的文本對於理解目前主要為精英階層文化產品所主宰的中國文學史的意義。 這些晚清華北的唱本因其在饅頭舖大量廉價出售而俗稱“饅頭舖本”。它們內容上包羅萬象、形式上亦多姿多彩，而作為在地方上流行的平民唱本，它們大部分從沒有被認真地收藏或整理。“時調”對於中國文學研究來說並非一個新的領域，但饅頭舖本中的大量文本非常具有時段性和地域性，給我們提供了研究其刊本的物質特點和閱讀消費習慣的可能性。當然研究者更可以由此進一步理解這些唱本的文化和社會背景，從而深入探討這些唱本如何進入當時城鄉平民——尤其是作為主要閱讀者的平民婦女的生活。 本課題將從亞洲和歐洲的許多收藏了饅頭舖本的圖書館或私人收藏中蒐集材料，並由材料和文本兩個方面進行分析，亦會關注刊本的時間以及出版和銷售的地點。對這些一直被忽略的地方流行唱本的材料和文本的分析，可以為我們呈現以往在中國史籍中缺席的關於市井平民文化生活的生動圖像及其社會影響。

17606820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17606820.value: In a world full of ambiguities and complexities, universities have a mission to prepare students to deal with unforeseen problems and empower them to carry out open, critical inquiry into those problems. That mission is driving the emergence of the ‘connected curriculum’, the aim of which is to create a closer connection among academics, students, and communities and to promote the systematic integration of undergraduate research experiences into university curricula. Embedding research into undergraduate curricula has many advocates, and is included in the policies of many higher education systems (see, e.g. the UGC’s 2010 report on Hong Kong’s higher education system). However, translating such policies into practical strategies to support a connected curriculum is challenging. Two major barriers to such translation are the traditional conceptualisation that separates teaching from research and academics from students and the lack of a transparent, integrated view of the curriculum. The paucity of research engaging students as co-inquirers in critical inquiries into both their own learning and the curriculum is further hindering the development of a connected curriculum. The aims of the proposed study are to investigate undergraduate research experiences as embedded in the curricula of the humanities, surveying, science, and an interdisciplinary subject in research-intensive universities and to elicit and integrate the perspectives of teachers and students through a multi-layered teacher-student collaborative inquiry model. The study’s results are expected to spark changes in the direction of a more connected, research-based curriculum. Collaborative inquiries will be adopted in four cases, following a multiple-case study approach. In each case, five students will be trained and empowered as co-inquirers who will conduct interviews and collaborate on analysis with teachers and the project team. The perspectives of both teachers and students will be investigated and consolidated through a scaffolded process aided by curriculum mapping tools to identify the connections between the taught curriculum and students’ experiences and generate actionable recommendations for curriculum enhancement. The study’s significance lies in its potential to push forward an important agenda that has been advocated at the policy level but not yet fully transferred to the curriculum level, the latter of which is arguably the real locus of the problem. It is also meaningful and timely in empowering students to be co-inquirers into the curriculum and their own learning experiences.

17606820.label: Realisation of objectives
17606820.value: Objective 1. To investigate the undergraduate research experiences embedded in the curricula of four undergraduate degree programmes in humanities, surveying, science, and environmental management and technology in research-intensive universities (100% achieved) Four degree programmes in humanities, social sciences, science, and environmental management and technology have been identified and investigated based on a multiple case study approach (Merriam, 1998). Altogether, document reviews of four sets of curricular documents (e.g. programme overview, syllabi of research-focused and research-related courses), 18 faculty interviews, 113 student interviews, and four collaborative analyses (each in one programme) have been conducted. Moreover, 13 student co-researchers studying in the four programmes joined the research as student partners assisting in the investigation. Their perspectives have offered unique contributions to the research. The insights obtained from working with student co-researchers are published in one journal paper (Zou, Kochhar-Lindgren et al., 2023) and one invited news story in the University World News. It is worth highlighting that the University World News contacted the research team, inviting us to publish our story of working with student partners in Asian contexts. Undergraduate co-researchers are also properly credited in publications where they make scholarly contributions (e.g. Zou, Susanto et al., 2023; Zou, Casupanan et al., under preparation). Objective 2. To identify the perspectives of students and teachers on the undergraduate research experience (100% achieved) Students' and teachers' perspectives on undergraduate research experiences have been identified through semi-structured interviews with 113 students and 18 teachers. The findings were compared and contrasted following Harden's (2011) approaches to comparing the 'taught curriculum map' and the 'learned curriculum map'. We identified that students and teachers shared similar views on the value and importance of undergraduate research experience. We also identified that the main differences between students' and teachers' perspectives lie in the different views of knowledge, research, and pathways to developing research identity (Zou, Lee et al., 2023). Objective 3. To conduct collaborative inquiries in an attempt to bridge the possible gaps between students and teachers and integrate both perspectives in moving towards a connected, research-based curriculum (100% achieved) Collaborative analyses have been conducted in each of the four programmes under study. Thirteen student co-researchers and eight teachers participated in collaborative analyses, generating four integrated curricular visual maps incorporating perspectives from students and teachers. The maps were constructed using MIRO software. The outcomes of the analyses were sent to the programme teams to provide a summary of the findings and seek further feedback. The feedback was also incorporated into the report of the findings.

17606820.label: Major findings and research outcome
17606820.value: Based on a multiple-case study covering four cases, our major findings cover some of the most important aspects of undergraduate research, including 1) students' experiences, 2) faculty members' approaches, 3) a comparison between students' and faculty's experiences, and 4) implications for research-based curricula. The details are shown below: 1) Students' experiences: Students perceived their undergraduate research experiences as positive and associated meaningful experiences with achievement, ownership, challenges, real-world relevance, collaboration, and, to a lesser extent, identification with research (Zou, Susanto, et al., 2023). 2) Faculty members' approaches: Faculty members adopted various approaches to guiding students in undergraduate research, and their approaches are influenced by their perceptions of undergraduate research and the research-teaching nexus. Faculty members who view reciprocal research-teaching nexus at both departmental and personal levels, and perceive undergraduate research holistically, were more likely to link students with their own research experiences (Zou, Chow, et al., 2023). 3) A research-based curriculum is interpreted differently in the document and by the faculty members and students on the degree programmes. Faculty members emphasised the learning and critical evaluation of knowledge. In comparison, students focused on exploring specific interesting issues and collecting and analysing information without fully recognising the potential of research in generating, applying, and validating knowledge (Zou, Lee, et al., 2023); 4) The different interpretations between students and faculty members reveal that the primary goals of research-based curricula to advance 'powerful knowledge' and induct students into disciplinary ways of researching have yet to be fully achieved (Zou, Lee, et al., 2023). The research outcomes include the following: four journal papers (all in Q1 and Q2), two conference presentations, one invited news story, one guidebook (with case examples and toolkits) on conducting undergraduate research, and one public seminar entitled 'Student research experiences transforming undergraduate education in the post-pandemic era'.

17606820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17606820.value: The findings of this research show great potential for further development. These potentials include: 1) expanding the research to cover more disciplines and universities to obtain more robust findings of undergraduate research in various settings and regions; 2) comparing and contrasting our findings with international studies. For example, a group of researchers in the University of Sydney have been researching similar topics (e.g. Mantai et al., 2024). Through our common collaborator, Prof. Angela Brew (Professor Emeritus, Macquarie University), we plan to conduct comparative research in future; 3) designing intervention studies to enhance the undergraduate research experiences in the programmes being studied. The intervention will draw upon our main findings in the current research on the development of a pathway, researchers' identity, and student-faculty collaborative research; and 4) examining undergraduate research experiences in light of generative AI (GenAI). GenAI has a considerable impact on education, and more research is needed in the areas of how undergraduate research will evolve, with students potentially being able to leverage and critically engage with GenAI. The proposed course of action is: 1) communicating with existing and potential collaborators regarding the possibilities of conducting further research in the above four prospects; 2) designing interventions and conducting a pilot study with one of the programmes; and 3) applying for funding to allow realisation of our research plans.

17606820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17606820.value: Undergraduate research as an impactful pedagogy can potentially develop students into critical thinkers and lifelong learners, but designing a research-based curriculum is challenging. This project investigated undergraduate research experiences across four curricula in two universities in Hong Kong. Through collaborations with 13 undergraduate co-researchers, four sets of curricula documents were reviewed, and eighteen faculty members and 113 students were interviewed. We identified factors to effective undergraduate research (Zou, Susanto, et al., 2023) and gaps between faculty members' perceptions and students' experiences (Zou, Lee, et al., 2023). Students focused on exploring interesting and personally relevant topics, whilst faculty members aimed at knowledge acquisition, application and evaluation. This project has a significant impact on higher education and beyond. First, it generates evidence-based recommendations for supporting and enhancing undergraduate research. Second, it promotes a culture of teacher-student partnership and cross-institutional collaboration. Third, it helps respond to the broader question about the meaning of university education given the increasing power of generative artificial intelligence. This study suggests that undergraduate research might offer partial solutions to tackling the emerging challenges through highlighting faculty members' role modelling and the role of a research community–elements that cannot be replaced by technology.
