17608020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17608020.value: 從網絡主權、規範及信息技術，探討中國在塑造全球信息秩序中所擔當的角色

17608020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608020.value: How does China shape a global information order, regarding the norms and institutions that manage the cross-border flows of data? Information is a most highly-prized resource, and information technologies are now ubiquitous in all aspects of life. ‘Cyber norms’ are the preferred tool to govern cross-border flows of information, given the rapidity of technological change. Concurrently, China’s technological advantages, growing material power, and ambitions to be a ‘cyber superpower’ all underscore the point that no major social or political issue can be multilaterally mediated without at least tacit PRC cooperation. China’s preferred set of ‘cyber-sovereignty’ norms reorient internet governance to the United Nations and specialist state-led international fora, and emphasise the dominant position of the state over that of the individual in regards to information management (i.e. limiting information access in a state’s ‘information space;’ minimising the need for individual consent; limiting concerns about individual privacy when collecting/repurposing personal data). This project addresses how China applies ‘cyber-sovereignty’ norms when information technologies (networked systems, drones, blockchain, internet etc.) are used in UN human protection operations – empirical material that is yet to be systematically interrogated in a theoretically-informed manner. Therefore, this project contributes to questions of enormous academic and popular interest on whether China will shape the use of information technologies; how a rising China will remake global orders, and China’s use of norm contestation to project discursive power internationally. With a focus on theory generation to establish a strong empirical base to support future conceptual and theoretical refinements regarding China’s norm promotion tactics, this research contributes to both academic research with publications in 3*/4* journals and to policy-driven knowledge exchange for impact. The first paper theorises China’s application of ‘cyber-sovereignty’ in constructing a global information order, developing a typology of China’s diplomatic and rhetorical adaptation tactics used to project its normative preferences. The second and third papers are in-depth case studies of how China shapes a global information order and the normative contestation regarding information technologies applied in peacekeeping (focusing on MONUSCO in the DRC), and information technologies applied in humanitarian operations (focusing on UN refugee camps in Jordan). To illuminate political dynamics of norm creation, the research draws from extensive multi-sited fieldwork, using participant observation and semi-structured interviews (primarily in New York and Beijing). Having utilised such research methods in my prior ECS and GRF projects, I am confident that I can complete the work as scheduled. 中國如何塑造全球信息秩序中，關於管理跨境數據流動的規範和機構？信息是一種極為珍貴的資源，而現時在生活的各方面，信息技術無處不在。基於技術上的急速發展，「網絡規範」是管理跨境信息流動的首選工具。同時，中國技術優勢、軍事經濟力量上升、以至成為「網絡強國」的決心皆證明此觀點——即是，任何重要的社會或政治問題，最低限度必須得中國政府默許配合，否則無法多邊解決。在信息管理方面，中國所接受的一套「網絡主權」規範強調國家，而非個人，的主導地位。這標誌著：在國家「信息空間」中限制信息接觸、盡量減少詢問個人的同意、限制個人對於收集及重用個人數據的私隱關注。這套規範同時亦將網絡治理重新定位至聯合國及國家主導的國際論壇。是次項目研究在聯合國人身保護行動中，使用信息技術（例如網絡系統，無人機，區塊鏈，互聯網等）時，中國如何應用「網絡主權」規範。這些實證材料尚未在理論層面上被系統性探索。因此，是次項目探討學術界以至公眾都極為關注的問題：中國會否影響信息技術的使用？崛起的中國將如何重塑全球秩序？以及中國利用「規範競爭」在國際上爭取話語權。 就中國推廣規範的策略，為完善日後有關的概念及理論，本研究着重於提出理論以支撐扎實的實證基礎，並且會以三星或四星刊物投稿及社會影響，分別作為對學術研究及政策知識交流的貢獻。

17608420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17608420.value: 網上善行：提高助人者的幸福感，並讓其他人避開傷害？

17608420.label: Project Objectives
17608420.value: To conceptualize the construct of online prosocial behavior (OPB), and to develop and psychometrically evaluate a more elaborate scale that assesses all possible subtypes of OPB engaged by ordinary people (Study 1). Given the importance of prosocial behavior in mankind and the high penetration of the Internet and web-enabled devices or gadgets, conceptualizing OPB can provide insights into OPB research for different disciplines, including psychology, sociology, economics, digital media studies, computer studies, and public health. However, none of the existing measures cover all aspects of OPB without overlooking some important dimensions. Besides, while the Internet and smartphones are used by people of different ages, all existing OPB measures have been developed based on adolescent and student samples. Thus, whether we can apply them to other age groups raises a serious concern. In view of such, a reliable and validated scale covering comprehensive aspects and applicable to the general public is much needed. A more elaborate scale which assesses all possible subtypes of OPB engaged by ordinary people can (1) benefit scholars from different disciplines for research purposes; (2) allow practitioners to measure this specific prosocial aspect of online social behavior; and (3) facilitate international research organizations (e.g., Gallup) or global projects (e.g., World Values Survey) in generating a country-level OPB index. To examine short-term (or momentary) and long-term temporal effects of various OPB on adult help-givers’ well-being by conducting an experience-sampling study (Study 2) and longitudinal study (Study 3), respectively. There is an emerging line of inquiry which examines the link between OPB and one’s well-being. While offline prosocial behavior is linked to OPB, none of the previous studies have taken into account its effect. Instead, these studies have only looked into one specific type of Internet volunteering at a time or adopted an overall score of OPB for analysis. Furthermore, past research in this area has focused on cross-sectional data only, thus the direction of effects is unclear. Academically, the present research will further enrich our understanding of the process that promotes well-being, and help estimate how long the possible effect may last. Practically, it will add to a growing body of work aiming to understand the precursors and antecedents of well-being, so that intervention for improving and maintaining well-being will be more effective. Based on the research, practitioners and scientists will be able to replace the one-size-fits-all model with personalized prosociality-focused interventions. To examine short-term (or momentary) and long-term temporal effects of various OPB on cyberbullying among adults through an experience-sampling study (Study 2) and longitudinal study (Study 3) respectively. There are no previous experience-sampling studies on possible momentary effects, and while some longitudinal results have provided the basis for theorizing a potential relationship between OPB and cyberbullying, not all findings are pointing to the same direction. In addition, all results showing possible effects of OPB on cyberbullying have been derived from samples comprising adolescents and students only. In terms of academic implications, the present research will demonstrate the momentary and long-term effects of various OPB on cyberbullying among people of all ages, thereby contributing to a limited body of work that conceptualizes OPB as a way to reduce cyberbullying. As for real-life implications, given the prevalence of cyberbullying, the research will enlighten practitioners and policymakers by providing valuable and nuanced data on the topic. For example, it may be useful for practitioners who are developing specific cyberbullying intervention programs for different people, with the aim of encouraging them to act more prosocially online. It may also provide scientific-based evidence for formulating public policies, such as advocating online volunteering for coping with online antisocial behavior.

17608420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608420.value: Prosocial behavior, defined as any voluntary act that benefits others or society, is a comprehensive topic attracting considerable attention from both academics and the general public. Extensive psychology and interdisciplinary studies have been carried out, covering from the positive effects of prosociality to its societal roles, yet many aspects remain understudied. One example is the influence of online prosocial behavior (OPB) on offline prosocial behavior. In recent years, there has been a global decline in the number of volunteers, which was coincidental to the emergence of Web 2.0 technologies. As some have pointed out, the use of the Internet and smartphones may have encouraged OPB, and consequently, people have less time to spend on “real-world” social activities or prosocial behavior. This raises the concern of whether human prosociality is fading in this post-digital era. Another aspect that requires more research is the measurement of OPB. Currently, there is not a reliable, validated and all-round scale available, hence existing studies only focus on certain age group (e.g., adolescents), look into one form of OPB at a time (be it retweeting, crowdsourcing or donating for charity cause) or adopt the overall score of online prosociality. Efforts should be made to develop a more elaborate measure for assessing all possible subtypes of OPB. The relationship between OPB and well-being is often overlooked as well. To date, no studies have taken into account the effect of offline prosocial behavior, and there is not enough non-cross-sectional data in this field. In other words, the temporal effect of OPB on well-being is understudied. When there is light, there must be shadow too. Internet users may be willing to offer helping hands to others; however, people may also do harm online. To name one, cyberbullying is not uncommon in all ages. Thus, it is important to examine the protective effects of various OPB on cyberbullying. The present study aims to address all of the above issues by adopting a mixed-methods approach in three empirical studies. Study 1 will focus on the development of OPB scale, and evaluate its factorial validity, convergent validity, and discriminant validity through a focus group study and two cross-sectional surveys. Study 2 explores the short-term (or momentary) temporal effort of OPB on well-being and cyberbullying through an experience-sampling study. Lastly, Study 3 will employ a three-wave cross-lagged panel design in testing the long-term temporal effort of OPB on well-being and cyberbullying. 親社會行為是指為他人或社會帶來益處的任何自願行為，有關研究獲得了學術界和公眾的重視。縱然目前已有不少針對這項複雜課題的心理學和跨學科研究，而且當中還涵蓋了有關行為的正面影響和社會角色，但多個領域仍然缺乏充分研究。 舉例而言，其中一個研究不足的範疇就是網上親社會行為對非網上親社會行為的影響。近年，適逢Web 2.0技術興起，全球義工服務的參與者減少。正如部分人所指出，互聯網和智能電話普及，可能使得網上親社會行為增加，令人們花較少時間在「現實世界」的社交活動或親社會行為上。故此，我們關注後數碼時代是否導致親社會行為式微。 另一個值得研究的領域是網上親社會行為的測量方式。目前，我們並無一套可靠、經驗證和全面的指標，因此現有研究存在多項缺點，包括年齡組別的限制（例如只限於青少年）、每次只可研究一類網上親社會行為（例如轉發推文、眾籌或向慈善組織捐款），以及只能計算網上親社會行為的總評分。有見及此，我們需要建立更細緻的測量方法，從而評估所有分類的網上親社會行為。 此外，網上親社會行為與幸福感之間的關係亦經常受到忽略。截至現時，尚未有研究解釋非網上親社會行為對上述關係的影響，而且該領域亦缺乏足夠的非橫斷面數據。換句話說，我們需要加強研究網上親社會行為在不同時間對幸福感造成的影響。 有光的地方必會有影。雖然我們可以利用互聯網幫助他人，但也能以此傷害他人。不論男女老幼，相信都不會對網絡欺凌感到陌生。有鑑於此，我們亦需要探討各項網上親社會行為如何協助預防網絡欺凌。 本研究結合多項方法，共進行三次實證研究，旨在探討上述全部問題。第一項研究的重點是制定網上親社會行為的測量標準，並透過焦點小組研究和兩次橫斷面研究，評估該項測量標準的因素效度、聚合效度和區別效度。第二項研究則利用經驗取樣法探討網上親社會行為對幸福感和網絡欺凌的短期（或暫時性）時間影響。最後，第三項研究會採用三波長期追蹤交叉延宕形式，藉此測試網上親社會行為對幸福感和網絡欺凌的長期時間影響。

17609220.value: 西夏字逐字字音構擬：以 12 及 13 世紀文獻為基礎

17609220.label: Project Objectives
17609220.value: To revisit the reconstruction of Tangut phonology based on updated and expanded manuscript evidence. To conduct an evidence-based reconstruction of around 6,000 Tangut characters. To describe the sources and rationale on the reconstruction of each Tangut character pronunciation.

To conduct an evidence-based reconstruction of around 6,000 Tangut characters.
To describe the sources and rationale on the reconstruction of each Tangut character pronunciation.

17609220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609220.value: Tangut is a medieval Tibeto-Burman language which was the official language of the Tangut, or Xixia Empire from 1038 CE to 1227 CE. It is one of the five classical Sino-Tibetan languages which provides critical evidence for the historical linguistics of the Sino-Tibetan language family. The only way to understand Tangut is to retrieve it from the manuscripts written in Tangut character script. There are around 6,000 Tangut characters, yet the structure of most characters tells little or no information on its pronunciation. The current pronunciation of Tangut characters as listed in Tangut-Chinese Dictionary (Lǐ 2008) is based on the reconstruction conducted by Sofronov (1968). His pioneering work a half-century ago was confined by limited accessibility to manuscripts. Different initial or rhyme categories were often reconstructed with the same sound value. Some characters were reconstructed unsystematically due to the lack of evidence. These ambiguities are not distinguishable in the current reconstructed pronunciation of Tangut characters. It would be confusing if these pronunciations are utilised in the comparative Sino-Tibetan linguistics. The proposed research aims to provide an updated and reliable reconstruction of the pronunciation of all Tangut characters, which readers can trace the sources and rationale of each reconstruction conveniently. It will set up an electronic database on phonological information of Tangut characters. It will contain 12th and 13th centuries Tangut manuscripts which can serve as internal and external evidence for the reconstruction. These manuscripts include Tangut rhyme books Ocean of Characters, Homophones, Tangut rhyme table, the Tangut-Chinese glossary Pearl in the Palm, Tibetan phonetic glosses of Tangut characters, and Tangut transliteration of Sanskrit chants. In the stage of reconstructing Tangut phonology, the research will focus on the chaining of fǎnqiè spellings of Tangut characters. It will lay the foundation of the reconstruction of Tangut initials. At the same time, the research will investigate the nature of “intra-rhyme cycles” in the rhyme book Ocean of Characters, hoping to clarify the question of medial in the reconstruction of Tangut rhymes. Based on the refined framework of Tangut phonology, the research will reconstruct the pronunciation of each Tangut character with an explanation on the sources and rationale. Phonological categories with the same sound value will be distinguished, and all uncertainties in syllable reconstruction will be highlighted. The study will not only provide a trustworthy source on the pronunciation of Tangut characters, but also shed new light on Sino-Tibetan comparative phonology. 西夏語是一種中古藏緬語，也是公元 1038 至 1227 年期間西夏王朝的官方語言。西夏語是五種古典漢藏語之一，能夠為原始漢藏語構擬提供重要的証據。可是西夏語早已經消亡，我們只能透過存留的西夏文文獻了解這個語言的面貌。西夏文是一種方塊文字，共有約 6,000 個西夏字。絕大多數的西夏字表音程度甚低，難以透過字符結構預測字音。目前學界多數採用《夏漢字典》（李範文 2008）提供的西夏字擬音，而這些字音是以索夫洛夫（Sofronov 1968）的構擬為基礎。索夫洛夫在半個世紀以前的字音構擬雖然極具開創性，卻因為當時文獻不足而受限，不同的聲母和韻母種類有時候會構擬為相同的音值，還有一些西夏字因為缺乏証據而作不規則的擬音，字音構擬裏哪些是可靠的、哪些是含有猜測成份的，往往難以識別。假如利用這些西夏字音進行漢藏語比較，可能會引起問題。本研究旨在以最新的資料為所有西夏字提供一套可靠的擬音，讀者將可以便捷地追溯每一個字音的文獻依據和構擬過程。本研究將會利用 12 及 13 世紀西夏文獻的字音構擬內部和外部証據，建立一個西夏字音電子數據庫，其中採錄文獻將包括《同音》、《文海》等西夏字韻書、西夏字韻圖《五音切韻》、夏漢對音的詞彙表《掌中珠》,還有附有藏文注音的西夏文殘片，以及西夏字記錄的梵咒。在構擬西夏語音系的階段，本研究將會為所有西夏字進行反切繫連，重新疏理西夏語的聲母類別。本研究還會探討《文海》裏「韻內小循環」的問題，以期釐清西夏語的介音性質。接下來本研究會根據構擬得出的西夏語音類別，為每一個西夏字擬定字音，並說明每一個字音的文獻依據和構擬原則。構擬音值相同的語音類別將會區別標記，因為証據不足而使音值不明之處也會特別標示。本研究期望能為學界提供一套可靠的西夏字音，同時促進學界未來使用西夏語進行漢藏語比較研究。

17609220.label: Realisation of objectives
17609220.value: This research aims to collate the manuscripts related to the phonology of Tangut, to reorganise the updated and expended Tangut phonological information into an extensive electronic database, which is then used to revisit the reconstruction of Tangut phonology and to conduct an evidence-based reconstruction of the pronunciation for all Tangut characters, as well as to describe the sources and rationale on the reconstruction of each Tangut characters. The implementation of this project has been slower than initially envisaged. The project required a full-time research assistant stationed in Hong Kong who knew the Tangut script. We have identified several suitable candidates from the Mainland. However, due to entry restrictions caused by the pandemic, none of them were willing to take up this position, and it took until the end of 2022 before a suitable candidate willing to learn Tangut could be identified from the HKU Department of Linguistics. As many Tangut characters are very similar for beginners, the PI needed extra time to check that the Tangut characters were entered correctly. It inevitably affected the progress of the project. In response, we have adjusted our procedure to prioritise the decipherment of the Tangut fragment with Tibetan phonetic glosses. Early in this project, when we reviewed the previous literature, we identified that the most crucial and largely unused evidence related to Tangut phonology was the direct phonetic gloss of Tangut characters in Tibetan spelling on these fragments. There are now 34 fragments in Russia and UK. We have conducted preliminary readings of these fragments in 2008, 2009, and 2018. We initially intended to use these preliminary readings as phonological data in our reconstruction. However, we soon realised that if the Tibetan phonetic glosses were to be used successfully in the reconstruction of Tangut phonology, we could not stay with the data from the preliminary readings, for there might still be many 'impurities' caused by misidentification. Therefore, we have taken the opportunity of this project to make a thorough, sentence-based decipherment of all fragments so that the misidentifications can be eliminated and fragments from different sources can be clearly distinguished. This refinement is essential to provide precise evidence for questions in Tangut phonology that are difficult to solve by previous scholars and lay a solid foundation for a more accurate reconstruction. The first objective of revisiting the reconstruction of Tangut phonology based on updated and expanded manuscript evidence has mainly been accomplished. We have inputted Tangut phonological data from the core manuscripts more than the original plan, including editions A and B of the rhyme book 'Ocean of Characters', editions A, B, C and D of another rhyme book 'Homophones', the Combined Edition of 'Homophones' and 'Ocean of Characters', the rhyme table 'Rhyme Cutting in Five Sounds', the 'Pearl in the Palm' which provides cross-referenced phonetic glosses of Chinese and Tangut characters, as well as the aforementioned Tangut fragments with Tibetan phonetic glosses. These data have been carefully proofread and incorporated into a comprehensive Excel spreadsheet. However, we have not yet published an updated reconstruction scheme of Tangut phonology because of two difficulties encountered in the process. This first issue is the credibility of the inferred results. Take the reconstruction of Tangut initials as an example. The internal reconstruction of the initials mainly relies on two shreds of evidence. The first is the fanqie spelling of Tangut characters provided by the 'Ocean of Characters'. Among the discovered Tangut manuscripts, only edition A of 'Ocean of Characters' preserves the fanqie spellings of the level tone Tangut characters. In contrast, the fanqie spellings of the rising tone characters have been almost lost. In order to determine the initials of the rising tone characters, it is necessary to rely on the second piece of evidence, that is, to compare the homophonic relationship between editions A and B of 'Homophones'. However, in addition to whether or not the homophonic characters of the two tones are mixed, there are other subtle differences between editions A and B of 'Homophones', making us wonder if these two versions reflect the same Tangut phonology, whether there are mistakes in the earlier edition A, or whether the two versions are reflecting two slightly different accents. Due to the lack of specific evidence and the discrepancy between different sources, there is not a dichotomy between 'having evidence / can be constructed' and 'having no evidence / cannot be constructed', but there is a degree of variation from 'strong evidence / more credible construction' to 'weaker evidence / less credible construction' in the inferring of Tangut phonology and character pronunciation. We are now considering how to describe this gradational credibility, for example, by listing all possible situations exhaustively and rating them according to the level of credibility. The second issue is the reconstruction of medial in Tangut phonology. While the Tangut initials and rhymes have been discussed more comprehensively, the reconstruction of Tangut medials, such as -i- and -u-, is somewhat ambiguous. In this project, we identified that the medials are reflected in the Tangut manuscripts in three ways. Firstly, as Sofornov (2004) stated, the upper fanqie characters in 'Ocean of Characters' do not merely reflect the initials, but also the medials. Secondly, the Tangut characters are first listed according to their rhymes in 'Ocean of Characters', but then within each rhyme, the characters are listed according to their initials, and there are often 'initial cycles' in the sequence. These 'initial cycles' are probably related to the medials. Thirdly, the rhyme tables in 'Rhyme Cutting in Five Sounds' should have referenced the Chinese rhyme table and listed Tangut characters with a medial separately. The question of medial would be clarified by analysing the above documents and using the Tibetan phonetic glosses of Tangut characters as external evidence. A more accurate understanding of the Tangut medials would probably further improve the reconstruction of Tangut initials and rhymes. For example, according to the Tangut rhyme books, there are 105 rhymes in Tangut. The differences between some of them are not apparent. If the medials are considered, it would be possible to organise the 105 rhymes described by the Tangut people into a more concise rhyme system. Nevertheless, this project’s second and third objectives have been largely accomplished. As mentioned above, we have established an electronic database of Tangut phonology that is more comprehensive than expected and includes the previously underutilised but critical data of Tibetan phonetic glosses. Except for the medial, this database makes it possible to reconstruct most of the Tangut characters' initials, rhymes, and tones and quickly check the evidence and rationale for constructing each part of the syllable. We have also set up a website. As a first step, this website can already search for the rhyme book data of each Tangut character. When the electronic database is completed, the information will be exported to this website and will be accessible for free for all scholars as well as the public.

17609220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609220.value: The most significant outcome of this project is the sentence-based decipherment of all Tangut fragments with Tibetan phonetic glosses, the first time in more than a century since the fragments were discovered. The Tibetan phonetic glosses would provide crucial evidence for reconstructing Tangut phonology and the pronunciation of individual Tangut characters. We have devoted much effort to understanding the content of these fragments, even if it seems to be of little relevance to Tangut phonology. It is because the handwriting on these fragments is scribbled, and the content leaves no title, author, or date. If we can identify other Tangut manuscripts or Tibetan texts with the same content as these fragments, it would be possible to minimise the misidentification of Tangut characters further and refine the phonological data. We found that the fragments under Tang. 1075 of the Russian collection and the fragments Or. 12380/3909-3911 in the British Library are most likely from the same source. We also successfully identified the content related to the great seal (mahāmudrā), dharmodayā, and Vajravārāhī in these fragments. Therefore, we proposed that these fragments are likely to be a kind of quintessential instruction (man ngag) on the teaching of the Six Yogas of Nāropa from the Kagyu School in Tibetan Buddhism, thus allowing future studies to be more targeted in the search for Tangut or Tibetan texts related to these fragments. In addition, as mentioned above, we have completed an electronic database of Tangut phonology, which is the most comprehensive to date and includes more Tangut manuscripts than initially expected. We have also constructed initials, rhymes and tones for most Tangut characters with this database. When the question of Tangut medials is solved, it will be able to completely describe the pronunciation of all Tangut characters with the sources and rationale provided. In our research, we also accidentally re-discovered the 'extended manual' of Tangut characters with Tibetan phonetic glosses compiled by the pioneering Tangutologist Nikolai Nevsky, which had been thought to be lost. On another occasion, because we shared the content on Vajravārāhī in these fragments, we were invited by the Center for Religious Studies of Ruhr-Universitat Bochum to give a lecture on Vajravārāhī in Tangut Buddhism. We also conducted the first-ever online course in English on the Tangut language, which attracted twelve academics and graduates from eight countries and regions. These are unexpected gains of the project.

17609220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609220.value: Through this project, we have developed a database that includes the core manuscripts related to Tangut phonology and a website that serves as a search platform. In the future, we will expand this database by adding more non-core phonological information, such as the Tangut phonetic translation of Chinese names and specific terms from the Tangut version of 'The Analects', 'Mencius', 'The Art of War', and 'The Forest of Categories'. Together with the website, this database has the potential to be developed into an online Tangut corpus, which can be used not only for phonological study but also for lexical and syntactic research. Regarding the reconstruction of Tangut phonology and Tangut character pronunciation, we will focus on the reconstruction of medial. As mentioned above, medial is the weakest part of studying Tangut phonology. Still, its reconstruction may impact the Tangut initials and rhymes, so a deeper understanding of the medial is essential for an accurate reconstruction of the sound of Tangut characters. Finally, we will continue to study the contents of the Tangut fragments with Tibetan phonetic glosses to identify Tangut or Tibetan texts that match these fragments. The content of these fragments also brings new information to the study of the Kagyu School of Tibetan Buddhism. We can explore related Tangut manuscripts from here, especially on the cult of Vajravārāhī during the Tangut period.

17609220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609220.value: Tangut is a medieval Sino-Tibetan language spoken in the present-day northwestern China. Although long extinct, a significant number of manuscripts written in the Tangut characters have remained. Based on the previous works, this project established an electronic database that includes all core materials related to Tangut phonology. It would facilitate us in re-examining the reconstruction of Tangut phonology and provide a detailed description of the reconstruction of the pronunciation of all Tangut characters. The result will be published on a website so everyone can easily access it. We recognise two key issues in the reconstruction of Tangut phonology: how to determine and describe the evidence for the reconstruction with different levels of reliability and how to analyse the medial in a Tangut syllable. We have also completed the first sentence-based decipherment of all Tangut fragments with Tibetan phonetic glosses, bringing critical evidence for Tangut phonology. We identified that the content of these fragments is an instruction from the Kagyu School of Tibetan Buddhism, which will help us further investigate the origin of these fragments. Last but not least, we organised the first online course in English on the Tangut language, making it possible for more people to learn about it.

17609920.value: 量化道德：中国社会信用体系的社会文化意蕴

17609920.label: Project Objectives
17609920.value: To understand the overall content and operation of the Social Credit System (SCS) in China. To analyze how the design and implementation of SCSs in different locales are shaped by local and national socio-cultural repertoires and institutional arrangements and to compare “successful” and “failing” cases in order to identify common factors that lead to positive vis-à-vis negative reception of SCS. To examine how individuals in different social strata are influenced by SCS and how their behaviors are shaped by it, and to assess and analyze the socio-cultural impact of SCS on local communities and on society overall. To theorize how socially desirable behaviors are defined, classified, evaluated, and negotiated and to advance the sociological theories of morality, classification, and evaluation to contexts beyond liberal market economies. To offer a sociological account of SCS in China to non-academic communities and serve as a knowledge base for public discussion and as a reference for policymakers.

17609920.value: 摘要： 2014年6月14日，國務院發布了一份正式文件，公布在2020年中國會在全國推行具有強制性的社會信用體系。該舉措旨在恢復社會的信任和誠信，其構想是通過實施獎懲分明的一攬子得分機制，塑造組織和個人的“道德”行為。許多行為都會導致個人信用得分的降低。到2018年底，數百萬人已經受到不同程度的懲罰。西方媒體和評論員都對該系統抱著懷疑的態度，但中國民眾對此計劃褒貶不一。本項目是對中國社會信用體系進行社會學研究，旨在研究該體系對民眾日常生活和行為的影響，並分析其對文化和社會的較深遠影響。 在過去的十年中，社會信用體系已經在中國的城市和農村嘗試推行。儘管具體實施過程中各地在規模，目標人群與數字化程度方面存在差異，但都不約而同地強調通過獎懲機制來激勵道德和守法行為。但是，不同地區的公眾對該制度的反應各不相同。在一些地區信用制度似乎受到當地人的歡迎，而在另一些地區它們則面臨爭議和抵制。為什麽會這樣呢？是什麽因素導致了地區接受度的差異？ 本研究將使用民族誌案例研究法來探究導致民眾對信用體系差異化接受結果的社會文化過程。通過理論化抽樣，四個田野點依據如下兩種比較思路被篩選出來：城市與農村，以及在接受社會信用體系過程中的積極/消極評價分野。一方面，浙江省的杭州市和寧波市代表中國大都市，而山東的榮成市和江蘇遂寧市則代表中國農村。另一方面，杭州和榮成是社會信用體系的積極接受者，而寧波和遂寧則對這一制度有不少爭議。針對這些案例的系統性比較，本研究將揭示導致民眾對制度評價的差異形成的原因。 本項目有助於理解特定的社會文化和制度條件如何定義、分類、評估和協商社會所期望的行為。它旨在完善和補充道德，分類和價值評估方面的社會學理論，並討論日常生活中的大數據和算法對自由市場經濟以外的日常生活的影響。同時，實證結果和分析將為社會信用體系袪魅，為香港的公眾和政策制定者提供知識基礎，以討論當社會信用體系在全國強制性推行時香港融入大灣區的深遠意蕴。

17610320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610320.value: This is a proposal for the first book-length, interdisciplinary study of how identities of sexual minorities are constructed in Hong Kong’s legal and political discourse. The discursive formation of identity is fundamental to sexual minority rights because it undergirds the doctrinal frame in a rights claim: for instance, if homosexuals are represented, either explicitly or implicitly, as disruptors of societal tradition or sexual outcasts, then they are less likely to be construed as full rights bearers in the context of, say, marriage equality. In this study, I investigate the relationship between rights and representation through an examination of four figures in legal and political discourse: the homosexual, the lesbian, the transsexual, and the bisexual. Since the Handover in 1997, sexual minority rights have developed at a rapid, but uneven, pace. Early cases on sexual-orientation discrimination such as Leung TC William Roy v. Secretary for Justice [2006] formed the foundation for the recent Court of Final Appeal decisions in QT v. Director of Immigration [2018] and Leung Chun Kwong v. Secretary for the Civil Service [2019], and more cases relating to same-sex unions are on the horizon. W v. Registrar of Marriages [2013], which held that a post-operative transsexual can marry in their new gender, sparked a series of cases on transgender rights which are still ongoing. The conditions behind bisexuality’s striking absence call out for investigation, as do the reasons for popular culture, and in particular film, to emerge as an alternative forum for bisexual representation. I will examine how the four identity categories are formed, perpetuated, and disseminated. The legal discourse includes both judgments of the key court cases as well as the strategies of the litigants and their lawyers, and the political discourse includes Legislative Council debates and news coverage of issues relating to sexual minorities. Building on a methodological framework posited by gender and queer theorists whose work foregrounds the complex process of identity formation, I approach each of these discursive domains as sites where identities are constructed and contested. This project builds on my background in both legal and literary-cultural studies. It draws on a strong publication record on law and sexuality, as well as on law and popular culture. The resulting monograph will make an original and important contribution to the study of sexual minority rights, constitutional law, the cultural study of law, and gender studies, as well as public debate about sexual minority issues.

17610520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610520.value: Worldwide, 7% to 11% of 5-year-old children have a pervasive impairment of oral language called Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), which negatively affects their vocabulary, grammar, subsequent academic and employment achievements. These children have difficulties with statistical learning, a basic cognitive ability of extracting regular patterns (e.g., the co-occurrence of the auxiliary verb-to-be with the morpheme -ing when the auxiliary is followed by a verb) in the language input. One way to make the extraction of grammar patterns easier for children with DLD is to provide them with enhanced input. An input-based enhanced Conversational Recast intervention approach was shown to lead to robust gains in the production of grammatical morphemes (e.g., past tense -ed) in English-speaking children with DLD. Persistent difficulty with grammatical morphemes is a hallmark of DLD in English, but not in Cantonese-Chinese. Instead, for Cantonese-Chinese speaking children with DLD (CC-DLD), the hallmark errors are in syntactic constructions. This enhanced version of conversational recast cannot help CC-DLD because learning grammatical morphemes is different from learning syntactic constructions. A syntactic construction occurs in sentences that are governed by a rule. For example, the rule for the dative syntactic construction is: subject + verb + object + object. This construction can be filled with different words (e.g., the boy gave me two books, Jane sent him a present). To form grammatical sentences, children need to develop an abstract representation of the syntactic construction. What kind of enhanced input is helpful for CC-DLD who need to learn syntactic constructions rather than morphemes? Research from a constructionist approach to language development has shown that typical English-speaking children learned a novel syntactic construction in meaningful contexts when the input was optimized, that is, when given skewed rather than balanced frequency input. In the skewed frequency condition, the children heard five nonsense verbs used in the eight sentences that represent the construction. Among the five verbs, one was heard four times while the other four were heard once each. In the balanced frequency condition, the five verbs were relatively evenly distributed with two verbs occurred once and three verbs occurred twice in the eight sentences. In this project, we ask if skewed frequency input provided through recast will lead to more gains in CC-DLD’s learning of syntactic constructions than balanced frequency input. Our goal is to evaluate the clinical viability of this enhanced version of recast in preparation for future larger-scale more expensive efficacy studies. 加強版語法重整對有發展性語言障礙兒童學習句式的早期成效研究 全球約有7%至11%的五歲兒童患有口語表達和理解困難，臨床診斷稱為發展性語言障礙(DLD)。DLD對他們的詞彙和語法學習，隨後的學業和工作都會產生負面影響。這些兒童在「統計學習」方面有困難。「統計學習」是一個從環境資訊中提取規則和內在結構的基本認知能力（例如，在英語is之後如果是個動詞，動詞必須加上這個語素 -ing）。其中一個可以幫助兒童更有效地提取語法規則和句式的方法，是加強版語法重整。 研究證明加強版語法重整可以幫助英語作為母語的DLD兒童成功學習語素（例如過去事態語素 -ed）。語素學習對英語DLD兒童是一個持久的挑戰，但是句式學習困難對廣東話DLD兒童的負面影響更大。現有的加強版語法重整無法幫助廣東話DLD兒童，因為學習語素與學習句式不同。句式受語法規則支配，例如與格句式的規則是：主語+動詞+賓語+賓語。由不同的詞語組成的句子都可以表現同一個句式（例如，男仔俾兩本書我，姐姐俾對襪爸爸）。兒童需要學習不同句子背後所表現的句式。 怎樣的加強版語法重整可以幫助兒童學習句式和語法呢？根據建構主義語言發展理論所作的研究顯示，英語兒童如果能夠在有意義的環境中聽到表現同一個句式，但偏重於一個動詞的不同句子，他們就能夠成功學習到新句式。 是項研究比較兩個加強版語法重整的語言治療方案：重整的句子側重一個動詞，相對於各動詞出現次數平衡的重整句子。研究結果將會為我們下一個階段，就加強版語法重整對DLD兒童句式學習成效的大型研究，提供實證。

17610920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610920.value: 本項目會進行首個對《中國信託法》自2001年生效起、近20年來司法判決的全面研究。此項研究處理的最重要問題，是要辨認本法中對接納信託存在甚麼概念差距，並審視這些差距如何阻礙了司法機關對中國信託制度的了解、及妨礙了該制度的正確發展。此項研究的目標是為這些難題提供解決方法。 2001年，中國，其私法主要取材自蘇聯法制的一大陸法系國家，大膽地頒佈了一部專門法律──《信託法》，並同時頒佈了一部行政法規，給予信託公司對其結構與集體投資信託相類的集體資本信託的獨有經營權。儘管《信託法》內容較基本及充斥着概念差距，它成功推動了集體資本信託的迅速增長。2003年，信託公司管理的資產總額為人民幣2億5千萬元（美金3千9百萬元）。但到2018年四月，資產總額已指數增長至人民幣25萬億（美金3萬6千億）。 但是這個數字卻未必是個好消息，因為《信託法》，作為中國首部信託法律，可以理解地充斥着概念基礎上的弱點。較弱的法律保障令萬億計受託的投資陷入危險。法院審理信託議題時，以對信託概念的堅實認可及結實應用填補法律中的差距變得尤其重要。本人將會審視中國法院於過去20年來的司法判決，以審慎評估他們對這中國式大陸法制中的嶄新概念的處理手法。如仍存有概念差距，本人將提出不同方法，改善現有法律以使中國信託於普通法信託框架及中國式大陸法制框架下皆變得更為合理。中國信託的合理化將可為中國信託業務健康及多元化的增長打下健全而穩定的基礎。 直至2014年，此項研究由於中國法院判決書缺乏公開的訪問權而受到嚴重阻礙。最高人民法院最近命令所有中文判決書需在線上刊登的公告，終於使此項研究成為可能。 此項研究的結果會以3篇受國際審稿的期刊文章出版。

17610920.label: Realisation of objectives
17610920.value: Objectives achieved With the assistance of a team of research assistants, in full-time and part-time mode during different periods of the research, I have completed all project objectives. Specifically, the project has examined the following areas closely : 1. Chinese trust legislation, a voluminous number of administrative regulations issued about trusts, notices and orders of government authorities, judicial decisions on the Chinese Trust Law, and academic commentaries pertaining to the three research questions about trusts law. 2. A comparative survey of proprietary remedies for breach of trust in common law jurisdictions such as England and Australia, and major Asian civil law jurisdictions such as Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. 3. A thematic, comparative analysis of Chinese rules and judicial decisions concerning the research questions, along with an in-depth examination of the societal, legal, and economic factors influencing the implementation of trust law in China, was conducted. The study delved into issues like shadow banking, collective capital trusts, and the reasons behind their failures. Additionally, the study explored the shortcomings of Chinese legal regulations in the context of collective capital trusts, Chinese inheritance law, intestacy rules, testamentary trusts, and family trusts. 4. The completion of 1 peer-reviewed journal article and 2 (invited) book chapters. See below in “Results achieved”. 5. Recommendations about reforming the Trust Law, trust regulations and the interaction between judicial and regulatory supervision of Chinese trusts as well as the broader intestacy rules, which form the contextual setting that informs the establishment of testamentary trusts were put forward in the publications produced by the research. I provided a consultation report, as invited, to a semi-official research body of the Chinese government on, among others, the duties of executors, who manage the estate of decedents with wills. Results achieved 1. The study produced a detailed inventory of information on Chinese judicial decisions involving the Trust Law. Hundreds of such decisions have been collected and summarised. The materials were collected, collated, summarised, and categorised according to themes and issues as well as legal provisions of the main trust legislation. 2. Numerous conference papers and international (and local) presentations, including: i. Conference paper presentations (mainly online due to Covid) on project publications: (with H Jing) “The Dominance of Regulatory Oversight in Chinese Investment Trusts”, Asia-Pacific Trust Law: Boundaries in Context, Tokyo (2023); “Trust Law in China”, Trust Law in the Asia-Pacific Region: Modern Trends and Contemporary Issues (Malaysian Bar Association, online, 2022); (with F Chang), “Intestacy with Chinese Characteristics”, Asia-Pacific Private Law Conference, Singapore online (2022); and (with F Chang), “Intergenerational Inequality and the Reform of Intestacy Rules in China”, Philanthropy in the Age of Covid-19: Asia and Global Perspectives, Singapore online (2021); The Protection of Investor Protection in Chinese Collective Investment Trusts (2021). These conferences were hosted by reputable law schools such as: the University of Cincinnati Law School, Singapore Management University and the University of Tokyo. A conference in Rutgers was cancelled due to Covid, so were visits to Edinburgh, Iowa and Israel. ii. Presentations on common law or civil law that pertain to the themes of the project and provide a useful comparison for understanding the position in Chinese law: “Tracing”, The Laws of Restitution, Oxford (2023); Commentary on Lionel Smith, The Duty of Loyalty, Hong Kong (2023); (with K Low) “Tracing (Con)fusion: Solving the Innocent Volunteers Conundrum”, Asia-Pacific Private Law Conference, Singapore online (2022) and keynote paper, Society of Legal Scholars Conference, Durham online (2021); “Recovery of Funds Lost in Email Scams – ‘True’ Constructive Trusts?”, Property Law Seminar Series, CUHK online (2021); “The Irreplaceable Trusts and Its Remedies”, City U online (2021). Some presentations were for scholars and students in mainland China, such as (with Rebecca Lee) “Trusts in Hong Kong: Historical Application and Current Practice”, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (2023); “Re-imagining the Trust: Lessons from the Trust and Succession (Scotland) Act”, Macau (February 2024). 3. Publications: - 1 article in the top comparative law journal in the world – the American Journal of Comparative Law (impact factor 1.5, 50% contribution) - 1 (invited, sole-authored) book chapter with Cambridge University Press - 1 (invited, co-authored, 50% contribution book chapter with Hart Publishing Problems encountered and deviations from the original plan There were two main problems caused by Covid-19 in this research project: 1. Illness of the full-time RA due to abrupt change of lifestyle and homesickness and difficulty in hiring a replacement, resulting in a backlog that was eventually addressed by the PI and part-time student RAs. This affected the PI's time spent on other research projects. 2. Cancellation of international conferences and visits, limiting opportunities for idea exchange and research deepening. Whilst some of these visits were cancelled, some took place online, while others were arranged once Covid travel restrictions lifted, but took place during the last months of the extended project period or beyond, in 2024. The extension of the project deadline enabled me to commit to in-person conference presentations after the lifting of Covid travel restrictions in Hong Kong in Nov 2022. Bearing in mind the need for planning time, most of these in-person events took place from May 2023 and the end of the project in December 2023. I organized the Asia-Pacific Private Law Conference held in Hong Kong in May 2023, the first major in-person conference of the HKU Law Faculty after the lifting of Covid travel restrictions. Mainland and common law trust and property law scholars presented at this conference. I had a fruitful exchange with them about the latest landmark decisions in trust law in mainland China. In December 2023, I presented on trust practices in Hong Kong to trust scholars at a conference in Shanghai. In the same month, I organised a workshop in Hong Kong for a delegation comprising trust company staff and NGOs from China, sharing the common law experience in financial planning for beneficiaries with special needs. I also initiated discussion for holding a trust law conference for upcoming mainland trust scholars. Due to preparation time and the longer planning time for mainland scholars to arrange travels to Hong Kong, we now expect the conference to take place in August 2024, even though planning and discussion with speakers began during the project period.

17610920.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610920.value: Major findings : - China’s rules on fiduciary duties and remedies are underdeveloped as the result of stunted legislative development and the dominance of regulation over judicial supervision - In light of the limits of the regulatory approach to developing trust law, detailed specification of fiduciary duties and remedial rules have been identified. - The 2020 intestacy rules in China, which provide the default rules for individuals to determine whether to establish testamentary trusts, perpetuate growing intergenerational inequality. The problem will likely be execrated if it is not actively addressed in the development of testamentary trusts. Research outcome: My research responded to significant developments in Chinese law that are of immense interest in the international literature. First, unlike in common law jurisdictions, most rules concerning the supervision of commercial trusts are laid down by regulators rather than judges. The dominance of regulatory oversight and the state’s new policy to not bail out irregular trusts by influential trust companies such as those connected to the Zhongzhi Enterprise Group has led to gaps in investor protection. Second, there is new state policy and law to encourage the development of family trusts in the succession context, including testamentary trusts and special needs trusts, thereby raising wider issues about inheritance law. My three promised publications incorporated these themes to deliver maximum impact in the international literature.

17610920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610920.value: My unique comparative research in this project has led to noteworthy theoretical and doctrinal discoveries in trust law. Theoretically, it has established the foundation for a new trust theory applicable to both civil and common law jurisdictions. Doctrinally, it provides valuable findings and data for identifying features that make trusts uniquely successful compared to companies and agencies. I plan to delve into these themes in a new GRF project. I also intend to edit an Oxford Handbook on Comparative Trusts Law, covering 40 jurisdictions and an exhaustive list of themes and key trust aspects. Furthermore, I will organize workshops in Hong Kong to explore comparative insights and practical trust applications in finance, wealth management, and philanthropy. These projects hold immense value for Hong Kong, as the government seeks to re-establish the city as a wealth management hub. Trusts play a critical role in this development. My comprehensive approach, which includes the civil law perspective, positions Hong Kong as a leading research hub for trust law. This facilitates the city's economic and financial integration with the Greater Bay Area and, on a larger scale, the One-Belt, One-Road initiative.

17610920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610920.value: Nature This project examines the law, regulation, and judicial decisions of the Chinese trust system. It identifies conceptual gaps in China's reception of trust and investigates how they have hindered judicial understanding and proper development of the trust regime in the country. Significance and value So far, China's trust regime has almost exclusively focused on collective investment trusts, which have become a major platform for shadow banking. This has led to the overheating of the property market and a large-scale economic downturn when it collapsed recently. The research shows that the stunted development of proper trust law rules in the realm of private law and the dominance of the regulatory regime have contributed to this phenomenon. The project proposes solutions to overcome these challenges. As China has now sought to expand the scope of trust application from the financial realm to that of family succession, the project examines the legal context pertinent to such a development. The value of the project lies in providing thought-leading commentary on the implementation of trust in China, from both conceptual, doctrinal and contextual angles, informed by comparative insights as international best practices in civil and common law jurisdictions.

17611220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611220.value: Various clinical interventions and services programs are in place to mitigate the heightened rates of mental health issues among sexual minority young people (SMYP) (i.e., non-heterosexual people). While evidence of the mentoring effects grows, most existing programs converge on an individual-focused approach to fostering SMYP’s coping capabilities and resilience. Given that relationship disruption, sense of isolation, and fear of rejection are the core of SMYP’s compromised mental health, service programs should incorporate a relational-focused, community-based approach into its design and implementation. A mentoring program where a mentee is matched with a nurturing mentor assumes a promising, yet untapped, benefits for SMYP's psychosocial development. Outcome studies on mentoring programs for at-risk individuals have demonstrated the positive changes mentees can experience; this proposed study will extend the mentoring literature by evaluating its outcomes specific to young gay mentees. With an experimental design, this study further attempts to investigate whether the mentor’s sexual orientation impacts mentoring outcomes. Moreover, process data will enhance integrity of this evaluative study by elucidating mechanism of change involved in the mentoring process and participants’ perceptions of it. Given that variability in, and extensive length of, a mentoring relationship constitute challenges to data collection, this study overcomes these methodological obstacles through the qualitative method of Photovoice to gather process-oriented and experiential data. This is a concurrent mixed-methods study that aims to document the efficacy and process of a mentoring program delivered to Chinese gay men in Hong Kong. Seventy-five young gay men will be recruited and randomized into three group: (1) gay mentoring; (2) gay-friendly mentoring, and (3) psychoeducation. Following a standardized protocol, participating mentees and mentors will be matched to engage in a one-year mentoring arrangement under the support and guidance of the research team. Quantitative data on changes in mental health, self-acceptance, and the perceived relationship with a mentor will be collected at the outset, 6 months, and 12 months of the program using established scales. Qualitative data will be gathered through the embedded use of Photovoice and dyadic interviews at the end of the program. This study will be the first to deliver and evaluate the process and outcomes of a mentoring program for SMYP. Findings can enrich effective community-based strategies to promote SMYP’s psychosocial well-being. Exploration of the relative benefits for a mentee between a gay mentor and a gay-friendly mentor will inform mentoring practice and advance theories about the paths to diversity and inclusivity. 現時有很多臨床介入和社會服務都以改善性小眾的精神健康為目標。雖然不少有實證基礎的介入方案都採個人導向的方式，去增強性小眾青少年處理壓力的能力和韌性，卻少有涵蓋到近年愈來愈被學術研究與實務關注的引導效應 – 來自於與一位有正向成功經驗的引導者建立的支持、陪伴、與引導的關係。由於關係破裂、孤立感、害怕被人拒絕等是影響性小眾青少年精神健康的主要因素，介入服務在設計和應用時更應該考慮運用關係導向和社群導向的方式。有鑑於此，如果性小眾青少年能在良師益友計劃中配對到一個專屬的引導者，相信能對他們的心理社會發展產生正向的效益。雖近年已有不少研究顯示高風險的參加者在參與良師益友方案後會有明顯的正面影響，但特別針對男同性戀青少年研究仍相當缺乏。是次研究會以隨機對照試驗的設計進行，並且更進一步了解導師的性取向會否對導師方案的成效帶來影響，有望更了解男同志在導師計劃中的得益。藉由闡釋指導/引導過程中的改變機制和參加者的看法，研究所得的數據相信有助提升整項研究的可信性。由於導師關係的可變性以及其長度會增加數據收集的困難，是次研究會嘗試以影像發聲法的質性方式去收集過程導向和實驗數據。是次研究會以交匯混合研究設計進行，記錄導師計劃應用在香港華人同志青少年的過程及效果。研究共有75個年輕男同志報名，並分成3組：1）男同志導師指導；2）同志友善導師指導；以及3）心理教育。導師和學員會根據標準化流程進行配對，並共同參與一個為期一年的導師計劃，期間研究團隊會為他們提供所需的支援和指導。有關精神健康、自我接受程度以及與導師的覺知關係的量化數據會於計劃的開端、第六個月和第十二個月以現有的量表來統計。質性數據則會於計劃的尾聲以影像發聲法和對偶訪談所收集。是次研究將會是第一個執行和評估針對性小眾青少年參與導師計劃的成效的學術研究，研究成果有望能加深了解如何以社群為本的方案去強化性小眾青少年的心理社會福祉。透過探索同志導師與同志友善導師對學員的不同潛在效益，希望能令日後的良師益友方案和相關理論變得更具包容性及多樣性。

17611220.label: Realisation of objectives
17611220.value: Objective 1: To examine the efficacy of a mentoring program in promoting Hong Kong young gay men’s mental health and self-acceptance This project has been implemented as planned despite some disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Fifty-eight young gay men were recruited to join the program as mentees and 35 as mentors. The design of the randomized control trial and the collection of both quantitative and qualitative data allowed us to rigorously and in-depth examine the efficacy of this mentorship program in promoting mentees’ mental health and self-acceptance. These data reveal distinct aspects of efficacy and benefits for the participants. Linear mixed-effects models showed that for both intervention and control conditions, internalized homonegativity declined while resilience, loneliness, and body acceptance improved over time. No time and group interactions were found, meaning that the mentorship intervention did not surpass the psychosocial education received by participants in the control arm. Yet, qualitative data highlight promising effects of mentorship. Interviewees cited various benefits of mentorship, including providing companionship, enriching connections with lesbian, gay, and bisexual communities, and adding knowledge and perspectives on LGB lives and identities. Although quantitative data did not support any exclusive benefits of mentorship, most mentees recognized mentorship as a vital source of affirmation and companionship. Objective 2: To unpack differential effects on young gay men through mentoring relationships with a gay and a gay-friendly mentor The results shed interesting light on the role of a mentor’s sexual orientation in shaping the course and outcomes of mentorship experiences. Specifically, the quantitative data indicate that the quality and engagement of mentorship relationships did not differ significantly between gay and gay-friendly mentors. However, the qualitative data highlight some intriguing differences between gay and heterosexual, gay-friendly mentors. It is important to note that in the interviews, mentees were prompted to comment on the (dis)advantages of having a mentor with the same or a different sexual orientation, although they did not have the opportunity to experience and compare both situations. Mentorship provided by a sexual minority mentor was marked by empathy and mutual understanding. Mentees perceived that a sexual minority mentor could better understand their experiences and needs, thus providing relevant advice. In contrast, mentees paired with a heterosexual mentor tended to comment on the differences and distance in their mentorship relationship. Several mentees cited their hesitation and reservation in their interactions with mentors mainly due to perceived “differences.” At the same time, several mentees described that having a heterosexual mentor reduced the possibility of crossing boundaries and developing an intimate relationship. Objective 3: To document the course of a mentoring relationship and qualitatively identify the mechanisms involved in changes in outcomes In this project, we collected comprehensive and detailed data to document how participants engaged in and benefited from a mentoring relationship. The project details and activities, including recruitment, training for mentors, matching, mentorship support, research team supervision, and closure, have been reported in an article published in the American Journal of Community Psychology. We found that the engagement in and perceived relationship quality with a mentor are responsible for the outcomes. Meanwhile, the qualitative data indicated that the provision of emotional support and companionship, expansion of social networks, and sharing knowledge and new perspectives on LGB lives and identities are cited as mechanisms of change.

17611220.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611220.value: Sexual minority young people (SMYP) are disproportionately exposed to emotional distress and behavioral problems due to stigma-based stressors. Mentorship is a promising service modality to empower marginalized youth. However, limited research has documented whether and how mentorship can promote SMYP’s identities and wellbeing. It is also unknown whether a mentor’s sexual orientation matters in the implementation and outcomes of mentorship. A three-arm randomized control trial design was employed to compare the outcomes across three conditions: Arm A (matched with a sexual minority mentor), Arm B (matched with a heterosexual mentor), and control arm who received psychoeducation materials only. In November 2021, a community sample of 60 mentees aged 18-25 years were randomly allocated to Arm A (n=25), Arm B (n=10), and control arm (n=25). Over 12 months, dyads engaged in interaction at least 2 hours per month while the mentors were required to attend monthly supervision meeting to report progress and difficulties encountered. Quantitative data were collected from self-reported surveys administered at baseline, 3-month, and 6-month of the program. Outcome measures included depression, anxiety, loneliness, internalized homonegativity, sexual identity development, resilience, and body image acceptance. Mentees’ perception of relationship quality was also measured to determine its relevance to the intervention effect. In addition, 15 mentees were selected to recount their mentoring experiences through in-depth interviews. Without dropout, a total of 56 mentees completed all the surveys. Linear mixed effects model identified main effects for time. For both intervention and control conditions, internalized homonegativity reduced while resilience, loneliness, and body acceptance improved over time. However, time and conditions did not interact in relation to the outcomes. Arm A and Arm B were comparable in that sexual orientation matching did not drive differential outcomes nor relationship qualities. Interviewees emphasized that mentorship benefitted them by providing emotional support and companionship, enriching connection with LGB communities, and adding new knowledge and perspectives in LGB lives and identities. They also commented on distinct benefits and challenges of a mentoring relationship with heterosexual mentors. This study is the first to evaluate the effectiveness of mentorship for YGM. While quantitative data did not support the exclusive benefits of mentorship, most mentees recognized this intervention as a vital source of companionship and support. Sexual orientation matching was not found to be a crucial determinant of mentorship. Future research is recommended to extend duration of mentorship, proactively facilitate relationship building, and collect relationship-focused data.

17611220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611220.value: The study demonstrates the feasibility and efficacy of a mentorship program to enhance psychosocial outcomes for young sexual minority men. Here are recommendations for future research on mentorship. The small sample size limited the external validity of this trial, potentially rendering the statistical power inadequate to detect small changes in key outcomes. Future studies should increase the sample size. Another source of bias stems from the sampling process. Despite open recruitment, enrollment required participants to be exposed to recruitment information and take the initiative to register. Consequently, most participants were likely active and resourceful in the local community, with adequate motivation to engage in a mentoring relationship. Future research should reach out to young gay men with lower levels of community connectedness or motivation. Additionally, other baseline characteristics, such as outness and whether mentees had someone they considered a mentor, were potential confounders and should be considered in future studies. The pandemic also undermined external validity by inflating the contextual specificity of the findings, limiting their generalizability in the post-pandemic era. Future research should fine-tune the program design and evaluate its efficacy in different contextual and temporal settings.

17611220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611220.value: Mentorship has been implemented and established in various settings. This study provides comprehensive and quality data to address a service and research gap in applying a mentoring relationship model to serve young gay men in Hong Kong. Although this study produced no strong quantitative evidence of the benefits of mentorship, its potential impact is supported by qualitative feedback. We have also provided details about the design and procedures to inform further implementation and fully powered trials. This study contrasted the process and outcomes between mentors with similar and different sexual orientations to their mentees, indicating that sexual orientation might not be the primary influencer in mentorship. A mentoring program tailored to sexual minority young people in need of psychosocial and affirmative support would strengthen efficacy and should be delivered widely.

17611520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611520.value: With respect to test formats, multiple-choice (MC) tests have been widely used in educational assessments because they are easy to implement and can cover diverse content efficiently. The most common way of analyzing MC responses is to treat them as dichotomous data (i.e., correct or incorrect). However, such an approach is suboptimal because it ignores potential diagnostic information in the form of incomplete understanding and possible misconceptions that is available in the distractors. With respect to psychometric frameworks, cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) have recently received considerable attention from researchers and practitioners. Compared to traditional item response theory (IRT) models, CDMs can provide detailed diagnostic information about the mastery or nonmastery of finer-grained skills in a particular domain. The information can be used by teachers to adapt their classroom instruction, or by students to direct their own learning. To date, the diagnostic value and practicability of MC tests have not been fully realized within the CDM framework, mainly for two reasons: first, students’ partial knowledge and misconceptions are typically not incorporated in writing MC distractors to make them more diagnostic; and second, even when distractors have been carefully developed, existing CDMs either ignore the distractors or can only handle a limited type of distractors, thus making it difficult for diagnostic information in these distractors to be harnessed. This proposal aims to address these issues with a two-component project. The first component will develop a more flexible CDM that can harness the diagnostic information in the distractors by accommodating not only incomplete knowledge but also misconceptions. The second component will develop a new mathematics assessment where the distractors are designed to reflect students’ partial knowledge and common misconceptions. Due to its foundational role in facilitating the acquisition of higher-level mathematical skills, the new assessment will be in the area of proportional reasoning (PR). The viability of the proposed CDM and PR assessment will be evaluated using simulated and real data. Therefore, the project will also develop a computer program that can analyze MC assessment data using the proposed framework. Overall, the project is expected to have both theoretical and applied contributions to educational assessment. The proposed CDM framework, together with the computer program, will allow researchers to conduct studies to better understand how MC assessments can be designed in the CDM context. The PR assessment will serve as a prototype for developing more diagnostic, informative—and hence, more efficient—MC assessments. 多選選擇題是一種廣泛應用於教育測評的題型，因為它們易於實施且能有效地涵蓋各種內容。最常用的分析多選選擇題的方法是把它們當作二分數據（即正確或不正確）。然而，該做法並不理想，因為它忽略了干擾項中所包含的對學生部分知識或迷思的診斷信息。 在心理測量領域，認知診斷模型（CDM）受到了研究人員和從業人員的極大關注。相較於傳統的項目反應理論模型，認知診斷模型可以提供更加有診斷性的信息，比如學生是否掌握某個認知領域的技能。老師可以利用這些信息來調節他們的課堂教學；學生可以用於指導自己的學習。 迄今為止，多項選擇題的診斷價值及在實踐中的應用在認知診斷模型的框架之下遠未實現。其原因有二：首先，出題者在撰寫干擾項時通常未考慮學生的部分知識和迷思，以至干擾項缺少了診斷功能；第二，即使當干擾項已精心開發，現有的認知診斷模型或者忽略了干擾項，或者只能處理某些類型的干擾項，從而使得難以獲取和利用這些干擾項中的診斷信息。 本研究項目包含了兩個部分：第一部分將開發更加靈活的認知診斷模型 ，該模型不僅可以容納學生的不完整的知識結構，還可以容納學生的迷思，從而可以利用干擾項中的診斷信息。第二部分將開發一種新的數學評估體系，其中的干擾項將反映學生的部分知識和普遍的迷思現象。新的評估將針對比例推理領域因為比例推理能力是學生學習高階數學技能的基礎。新的認知診斷模型 和數學評估體系的可行性將利用模擬研究和真實數據進行評估。同時，本項目將開發一個電腦系統以分析研究數據。 該項目將對教育測評有理論和應用的貢獻。研究者可以利用本項目所開發的認知診斷模型和電腦系統對多項選擇題的診斷功能進行深入研究。本項目所開發的比例推理技能的評估也可以作為原型，供研究者學習如何開發更有診斷功能及更有效的多項選擇測試。

17611520.label: Realisation of objectives
17611520.value: Upon the completion of the project, the four objectives have been successfully achieved. 1. To optimize the diagnostic value and practicability of MC tests within the CDM framework by developing a flexible CDM that can harness the diagnostic information in distractors regarding students’ incomplete knowledge and misconceptions; We have successfully extended the multiple-choice deterministic input noisy and gate (MC-DINA) model to arrive at the extended MC-DINA (eMC-DINA) model, which is a more general, useful, and accurate model for diagnosing skills, as well as misconceptions using MC test data. We have developed an expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to estimate the parameters of the new model efficiently. We have conducted extensive simulation studies to evaluate the parameter recovery of the estimation under various conditions. We have presented the models and results in prestigious international academic conferences. Also, we have completed a manuscript for publication that would be sent out either late September or early October, 2024. 2. To develop and validate a new PR assessment with cognitively-based MC options based on the proposed framework; In collaboration with Dr. Tjoe, a math educator for Pennsylvania State University, we have identified additional proportional reasoning (PR) attributes based on the HK mathematics curriculum. In addition to the previous attributes, which are deemed PR skills, we have identified a new PR misconception. We have modified a PR assessment with 31 items, where, in addition to the key, distractors were also coded using the set of attributes identified above. We have analyzed data involving responses to the PR assessment of 1,408 secondary students in Hong Kong. We fitted the data with the eMC-DINA and several other traditional CDMs, namely, the MC-DINA, G-DINA and DINA models. Note that MC-DINA model cannot handle misconceptions, whereas the G-DINA and DINA models can only accommodate right/wrong responses. We compared the fits of the four models, and found that the eMC-DINA had the best fit to the data, and yielded meaningful diagnostic information about students’ skills and misconception. The superiority of the fit of the eMC-DINA model to the PR assessment data and the meaningfulness of the results provide validity evidence of the appropriateness of eMC-DINA model vis-à-vis the PR assessment. 3. To evaluate the viability of the proposed framework with a comprehensive simulation study and real data analyses; Our team conducted extensive simulation studies to evaluate the viability and advantages of the eMC-DINA model. For one, we investigated how well the parameter of the new model can be estimated under various conditions, and found that satisfactory results can be obtained, particularly when high quality items were involved. For another, we also examined the advantages of the new model compared to existing models for MC tests, and found the former yielded higher correct classification rates than the latter. 4. To develop a free and stand-alone computer program with manuals and examples to facilitate the use of the proposed framework. We developed a customized EM-based computer program that can be used to estimate the new model efficiently. The computer program and the corresponding manual have yet to incorporated into an existing R package (GDINA) co-developed by the PI, and to date has been downloaded more than 100,000 times.

17611520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611520.value: The project has produced important results with broad theoretical and practical implications. The major findings are as follows: 1. A new CDM framework for optimizing the diagnostic value of multiple-choice data: The eMC-DINA model is innovative and more general doe two reason: (1) It relaxes the major limitations of the original MC-DINA model. Aside from skills embedded in the key, the new model can harness the diagnostic information in the distractors representing incomplete knowledge states and misconceptions. (2) It includes several existing CDMs as special cases, and is more useful because it provides a more accurate diagnosis of students’ true knowledge states. 2. An estimation algorithm: An expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm designed specifically for the eMC-DINA model was developed to estimate various versions of the new model. The algorithm was necessarily challenging to develop because of the generality and complex nature of the eMC-DINA model. 3. A customized computer program that implements the new approach and model: We developed a customized EM-based computer program that can be used to estimate the new model efficiently. The program for simulating data was also developed by the team. The corresponding codes will be added to the “GDINA” R package to allow users to download and use it for free, and conduct more simulated and empirical analyses. The results have been widely presented in keynote speeches and invited talks given in different countries and regions. One manuscript is currently ready for submission and a few other manuscripts are under preparation. The project team, in collaboration with other researchers, will continue to develop and apply the model to produce new manuscripts for publication.

17611520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611520.value: Although we have made great strides, more research is needed to extend the new model, and to develop new models and techniques for multiple-choice items. Below are two possible future topics: (1) This project proposed and implemented a new CDM framework for optimizing the diagnostic value of multiple-choice data; however, it can be computationally demanding in the context of the large-scale data. Future studies can find ways to reduce the number of parameters to be estimated. For one, the relationship between the skills, as well as the misconceptions can be constrained. For another, reasonable assumptions can be explored and imposed. (2) The current study re-examined an existing PR assessment, which is suboptimal because the distractors were not designed to conform to the eMC-DINA model. The best results can only be expected when the assessment and psychometric model are completed aligned. Thus, future study should consider developing an eMC-DINA-based assessment from the ground up.

17611520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611520.value: Cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) are psychometric models developed in recent decades for identifying mastery or non-mastery of students’ skills. As the most commonly used test format in assessments, multiple-choice questions are favored by the educators for easy data collection and evaluation of results. However, most of the existing CDMs can only analyze the test information included in the keys. Such an approach ignores the diagnostic information that can be found in the distractors in multiple-choice questions. To fully capture the information provided by the distractors, we developed a new model to extract the information that can be found in both the keys and the distractors. In addition to skills, the newly proposed model can also accommodate misconceptions. We tested the proposed model carefully using simulated data, as well as real data from Hong Kong students. The results show that the model can help better identify the presence/absence of students’ skills and their misconception. The finer-grained information afforded by the new model can serve as useful feedback to different stakeholders to inform learning, instruction, and policy-making. In the long term, this project can serve as an efficient psychometric tool for analyzing multiple-choice data.

17611620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611620.value: Responsive teaching is a student-centred approach of instruction that caters for and adapts to the diverse learning needs of learners. In responsive science classrooms, teachers purposefully elicit students’ thinking, carefully listen to the substance of that thinking, and use the information to direct instruction on a moment-to-moment basis (Robertson, Scherr, & Hammer, 2015). Responsive teaching is challenging as it hinges on teachers’ abilities to recognise and analyse students’ emergent thinking to make spontaneous teaching decisions on the next steps in instruction. Although developing responsive teaching ability is a valued goal of initial science teacher education, few studies have examined in detail pre-service science teachers’ (PSTs’) acquisition of this ability. In the proposed qualitative case study, we will investigate development of PSTs’ responsive teaching ability in the context of an innovative video-based teaching intervention within a post-graduate diploma science methods course. Three unique features make the teaching intervention distinct from prior initiatives aimed at promoting responsive teaching in PSTs. First, it uses trained student actors to stimulate PSTs’ in-the-moment teaching decisions and actions during their approximations of responsive teaching practices in teaching rehearsals. Second, it engages PSTs in individual and collective examination and analysis of their in-the-moment teaching decisions and actions filmed using new video technologies, including point-of-view (POV) wearable goggle cameras. Third, it uses interactive video cases to stimulate collective examination of PSTs’ immediate decisions and responses to emergent student thinking. By analysing the learning of two entire cohorts of PSTs in the teaching intervention, based on both perception and practice data captured from PSTs and teaching rehearsal audiences (i.e., student actors and in-service teachers), the research examines: (1) how the PSTs’ responsive teaching ability develops across teaching rehearsals, (2) whether PSTs can transfer such ability to a new science topic and the difficulties and challenges of transfer, and (3) how the intervention influences PSTs’ development of responsive teaching ability. The findings will not only offer a refined understanding of how PSTs may develop responsive teaching ability, but they will also reveal the affordances and limitations of using video footage captured by new video technologies to promote teacher learning. Methodologically, the project presents new ways to investigate teachers’ responsive teaching ability, such as using teacher’s POV footage and trained student actors as probes to access PSTs’ in-the-moment teaching decisions and actions. It will also make an impact on the local community by better preparing future science teachers for responsive teaching.
