17611720.label: Realisation of objectives
17611720.value: Objectives 1-4: To evaluate the effects of yoga and meditation compared to usual care, on (1) anxiety and depression, (2) mindfulness, (3) PD-related motor and non-motor symptoms, (4) HRQOL, and (5) biomarkers of stress and inflammatory responses among Chinese PD patients, over the 6-month study period. An assessor-blind, three-arm randomised waitlist-controlled trial using intention-to-treat principle was conducted in Hong Kong from March 30, 2021, and June 25, 2022. The trial was registered on WHO-Chinese Clinical Trials Registry (ChiCTR2100045939). A total of 196 adults with a clinical diagnosis of idiopathic PD, who were able to stand unaided and walk with or without an assistive device, were enrolled via convenience sampling from three neurology outpatient clinics in regional hospitals and three PD support groups in Hong Kong. Eligible participants were randomized 1:1:1 to meditation, yoga or usual care. The meditation and yoga group received 90-minute in-person group sessions for 8 weeks. The usual care group received routine outpatient services and received the tested yoga intervention upon completion of the 6-month study period. The primary outcomes were anxiety and depression assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. The secondary outcomes included motor and non-motor symptoms (Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale, Part I-III), HRQOL, mindfulness, and levels of serum interleukin-6, cortisol and TNF-alpha. Assessments were done at baseline, 2 months and 6 months. A total of 159 participants were randomised into meditation group (n=53), yoga group (n=52) and control group (n=54). The sample included 83 female (52.2%) with a mean (SD) age of 64.8 (7.9) years and a mean (SD) MDS-UPDRS score of 39.0 (10.6). Linear mixed model analyses revealed that, compared to control, both meditation and yoga groups had significant improvements in anxiety symptoms (meditation: mean difference [MD]=-1.36, 95%CI-2.46 to-0.26; yoga: MD=-1.61, CI-2.70 to -0.52), motor symptoms (meditation: MD=-5.35, CI-8.61 to-2.09; yoga: MD=-6.59, CI-9.82 to-3.36), HRQOL (meditation: MD=-2.01, CI-3.41 to-0.62; yoga: MD=-1.45, CI-2.83 to-0.08), and describing skills (meditation: MD=0.97, CI 0.04 to 1.89; yoga: MD=0.92, CI 0.01–1.84) at T1, and significant reductions in serum interleukin-6 levels(meditation: MD=-1.14, CI-2.18 to-0.10; yoga: MD=-1.11, CI -2.09 to-0.13) at T2. Only meditation significantly reduced depression (MD=-1.44, CI-2.57 to-0.30) at T1 and sustained the motor and HRQOL improvements at T2. Objective 5: To compare the effects of meditation and yoga on (1) anxiety and depression, (2) mindfulness, (3) PD-related motor and non-motor symptoms, (4) HRQOL, and (5) biomarkers of stress and inflammatory responses among Chinese PD patients, over the 6-month study period. When comparing meditation and yoga, insignificant findings were reported for all outcomes except meditation group reported significant less deterioration in perceived motor experiences of daily living (MD=-2.19, 95% CI -0.35 to -4.03, p < .013) at 6 months. To better elucidate the differences between meditation and yoga, we performed additional subgroup analyses based on participants' risks of psychological comorbidity, attendance and dropout. For participants at-risks of anxiety (HADS-Anxiety Subscale ≥7) and psychological distress (HADS ≥ 13), meditation group had significant greater improvement in several outcomes compared to yoga group, including overall trait mindfulness and mindful awareness at T1, as well as HRQOL, overall trait mindfulness, describing skills and perceived motor experiences of daily living at 6 months (p < .05). For participants at-risks of depression, meditation group had significant greater improvement in depression, overall trait mindfulness, non-reacting at 2 months (p < .05), as well as anxiety, HRQOL, overall trait mindfulness, describing skills and nonjudging at 6 months (p < .05). For subgroup analyses regrading attendance (attended ≥ 6 out of 8 sessions) and non-dropout (completed T0, T1 and T2 assessments), meditation group had significant less deterioration in perceived motor experiences of daily living at 2 months and 6 months (p < .05). Overall, these findings suggest that meditation may be more effective than yoga in improving various psychological and functional outcomes, particularly for individuals at risk of anxiety, depression, and psychological distress. Objective 6: To investigate whether bio-markers and level of mindfulness functioned as mediating variables in the effect that the mindfulness practice has on anxiety and depression. We conducted secondary analyses to explore potential associations between changes in trait mindfulness, psychological distress (anxiety and depression), and biomarkers of stress and inflammatory responses (serum interleukin-6, cortisol, and TNF-alpha) over a 6-month period. Linear regression analyses revealed significant negative associations between changes in overall trait mindfulness and changes in anxiety (β = -0.212, p < .001) as well as depression (β = -0.167, p < .001). Additionally, changes in serum cortisol demonstrated significant positive associations with changes in anxiety (β = 0.006, p < .006) and depression (β = 0.006, p < .017), respectively. However, no significant associations were observed between changes in trait mindfulness and changes in serum interleukin-6, cortisol, or TNF-alpha. We could not observe any significant mediating effects of serum interleukin-6, cortisol, or TNF-alpha on the relationship between trait mindfulness and psychological distress (anxiety and depression) were observed. The findings suggest the need for further research with larger sample sizes to elucidate the specific psychological and neurobiological pathways through which mindfulness exerts its beneficial effects on mental health. Objective 7: To explore the experiences of Chinese PD patients in using yoga and meditation as a lifestyle intervention for psychological distress management, particularly the perceived effects, how and why mindfulness works or does not work, and conditions which may influence their motivation, acceptability and real-life practice, using a qualitative research approach. We interviewed 61 participants (yoga: n=31; meditation: n=30) from May 2021 to September 2022 via purposive sampling. Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted via telephone, Zoom or face-to-face due to the public health constraints during the COVID-19 pandemic. All interviews were transcribed verbatim, coded and analysed using Braun and Clarke's approach. Three themes emerged: (1) reshaping illness experience through embodiment, (2) cultivating a sense of community by mindful engagement and (3) fostering mindfulness sustainability: a plea for more resources. Participants described mindfulness as a transformative tool for non-judgmental reflection and re-establishing mind–body connections. Benefits included the calming effect of mindful breathing on tremors and mindful walking for gait issues. Group dynamics and culturally relevant affirmations were crucial for motivation. Challenges such as physical limitations and environmental conditions hindered mindfulness learning, highlighting the need for tailored support. These qualitative findings provide valuable insights into the experiences of Chinese people living with PD who participated in mindfulness-based care for stress and symptom management. The findings emphasise the transformative psychotherapeutic benefits of mindfulness in empowering self-care practices. Integrating mindfulness into nursing care and health management of neurodegenerative diseases is crucial to optimise the holistic well-being of people living with Parkinson's disease. The findings have significant implications for nurses and other allied healthcare professionals in developing engaging, personalised and sustainable mindfulness-based programs for primary, secondary and tertiary health promotion and rehabilitation for people living with Parkinson's disease and similar conditions.

17611720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611720.value: Feasibility groundwork: A feasibility study of the tested meditation intervention was conducted, supported by the PI's university internal grant. This feasibility study was presented as a poster at the 16th International Congress of Behavioral Medicine. With the presentation of these feasibility findings and study protocol generated by the research project, the PI received an Outstanding New Researcher Award at the 16th International Congress of Behavioral Medicine, 07/06/2021, offered by the International Society of Behavioral Medicine (ISBM). The award recognizes an outstanding contribution by a new investigator to the science of behavioral medicine. The feasibility study of meditation intervention was published in NPJ Parkinson's disease in Jan 21, 2023. Study protocol: This randomized controlled trial (RCT) examined the effects of two different mindfulness practices - meditation and yoga - on the mental and physical well-being of people with Parkinson's disease. The trial protocol was published in BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies on July 13, 2023. Main RCT's quantitative findings: The main quantitative findings indicate that mindfulness practices, whether mental-focused or movement-guided, significantly reduced anxiety, chronic systemic inflammation, motor symptoms, and enhanced mindfulness-describing skills and HRQOL in PD patients. Meditation also showed additional benefits in reducing depressive symptoms and sustaining improvements in HRQOL, making it an ideal complementary therapy for PD patients with motor fluctuations. Findings also suggest that meditation may be more effective than yoga in improving various psychological and functional outcomes, particularly for individuals at risk of anxiety, depression, and psychological distress. The manuscript of the main RCT's quantitative findings has been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal (Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics, Impact Factor: 16.3) and is currently under revision. A conference abstract delineating the trial findings has been submitted and presented as an oral poster at the 2024 Health Policy Conference on October 31, 2024 in Washington DC. Baseline RCT's quantitative findings: The RCT's baseline data was also analyzed to examine the relationship and mediating roles of psychological distress on mindfulness and HRQOL. Findings highlighted the mediating role of reduced anxiety and depression in the positive relationships between mindfulness and HRQOL. A manuscript has been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal and currently under review. Qualitative findings: The preliminary qualitative findings were presented as an oral poster at the 17 International Symposium on Healthy Aging (ISHA) 2023 on Sept 9, 2023, in Hong Kong. The full qualitative analyses were also submitted as an oral poster and presented at the 2024 Summer Research Institute, Mind & Life Institute on Jun 6, 2024, in New York. With the qualitative findings generated by the research project, the PI has been selected as a 2024 Mind & Life Summer Research Institute Emerging Participant and received a full scholarship offered to attend the one-week immersive program. A manuscript has been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal and is currently under review.

17611720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611720.value: Our study findings provide valuable insights into mindfulness-based interventions as complementary therapies for managing PD and suggest several promising directions for further development. 1. Optimization and expansion: The distinct benefits of meditation versus yoga, particularly for distressed patients, indicate a need for personalized mindfulness interventions. Future research should explore how to match patients with the most suitable modality to enhance engagement and outcomes, while replicating positive effects in diverse populations, including those with advanced PD. 2. Knowledge transfer and implementation science: A critical next step is to prioritize strategies that facilitate the sustainable implementation of mindfulness-based PD care. Based on these findings, the Principal Investigator has secured a HK$12.8 million donation to launch the Movin' CARE for Parkinson's Disease project, which aims to develop strategies for public awareness, compassion-based care, professional training, and accessible delivery platforms. 3. Mechanistic investigations: This study provides biopsychosocial evidence of mindfulness in PD. Future studies should use a multidimensional approach to explore potential disease-modifying effects. The research team is also investigating gut-brain interactions related to mindfulness. Ultimately, our goal is to integrate effective mindfulness interventions into routine care. Collaborative efforts with stakeholders can enhance clinical guidelines and facilitate wider access, improving quality-of-life for patients with long-term care needs.

17611720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611720.value: This study examined the effects of two different mindfulness practices - meditation and yoga - on the mental and physical well-being of people with Parkinson's disease (PD). Compared to usual care, meditation and yoga provided significantly immediate improvements in anxiety symptoms, chronic inflammation, motor symptoms, mindfulness-describing facet and quality of life in patients with mild-to-moderate Parkinson’s disease. Meditation offered additional benefits in reducing depressive symptoms and sustaining motor and quality of life improvements. Importantly, for PD patients at risk of depression, meditation appears to be more effective than yoga in managing anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, mindfulness traits in terms of describing, non-judging, and non-reacting facets, and quality of life. The findings suggest that mindfulness-based interventions, whether driven by mental focus or physical movement, can be valuable complementary therapies for managing PD. Amongst distressed patients, those may benefit more from meditation practices. To promote participant engagement, strategies should target positive group experiences, rapport among peers and instructor, and personalized guidance. This research provides insights to improve care and quality of life for individuals living with this debilitating condition.

17611920.label: Project Objectives
17611920.value: 1. To analyse what communicative style and linguistic behaviour are required for a successful undergraduate admissions interview performance at the University of Cambridge across a variety of subject areas. a. It is assumed these requirements will differ between, for example, the Arts and Humanities, Social Sciences, and the Natural Sciences, Mathematics & Engineering. Academic publications arising from this project will therefore address these differences (see Research Plan and Methodology). 2. To determine whether or not candidates from specific educational, socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds are systematically disadvantaged by the communicative requirements of the admissions interview and, if so, how. a. One comparative focus will be the performance and evaluation of British state-educated candidates (who amount to 31% of candidates represented in the corpus) vs. British grammar school candidates (17%) vs. British privately-educated candidates (15%) across a variety of subject areas. b. 17611920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611920.value: The undergraduate admissions interview at Cambridge University is a high stakes gatekeeping encounter par excellence. All students seeking admission to the University must attend two or more such interviews in which they are asked questions on their intended field of study by academic fellows, who function as gatekeepers in those instances. In 2018, approximately 30,000 candidates applied to Cambridge, of which only 20% were admitted. Controversially, however, individual candidates from British state schools were relatively less likely to be successful than those from private schools, and nearly all nationalities from outside Britain were less successful than home students. Owing to the global prestige of the university, longstanding disparities such as these have made the admissions interview a politically sensitive encounter, one over which journalists, politicians and prime ministers regularly voice concern (and criticism). This, in turn, has prevented linguists from gaining access to the admissions interview, which has remained – up to this point – a “black box”. Despite the difficulty of acquiring data in such a sensitive socio-political context, the PI has obtained unique access and permission to use a sizeable corpus of 60 interviews (1800 minutes) across a wide range of subject areas in order to address these issues of social concern. Using an Interactional Sociolinguistics framework, the proposed project goals are to determine: (1) what communicative style and linguistic behaviour are required for a successful undergraduate admissions interview performance, and (2) whether or not candidates from specific educational, socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds may be systematically disadvantaged by these implicit requirements; a common occurrence in interviews that Roberts (2011) calls the “linguistic penalty”. The outcomes of the proposed project will be of interest to a wide range of stakeholders both within and outside of academia. It has already been agreed with Cambridge University that this research will result in a series of single-authored academic publications and presentations that address the project’s research goals. In addition, the analysis and conclusions arising from the project will form the academic basis of consultancy work for Cambridge University, comprising training days for present and future admissions interviewers and outreach officers, thus driving impact and change in the undergraduate admissions process itself. Finally, the project will also facilitate outreach work in Hong Kong and the UK to improve knowledge of the admissions interview, and to increase application and success rates among academically able candidates whose educational and/or socioeconomic backgrounds are under-represented at Cambridge University.

17612120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612120.value: Many mathematicians believe patterns to constitute the core concept of mathematics. Pattern activities are commonly seen in preschool and primary school classrooms. Although developmental scientists have recently begun to study pattern understanding, knowledge of its antecedents and consequences remains limited. It is thus unclear whether teaching and learning pattern concepts have educational value for children’s mathematical development and how such concepts should best be taught. Furthermore, different countries have different views on the resources that should be devoted to pattern concepts in curricula and assessments. In the proposed research, we will examine the role of pattern understanding in preschool and primary school children’s development of arithmetic skills using multi-wave longitudinal samples in Finland and China, two high-achieving countries in such skills with Western and Eastern cultures, respectively. In addition, we will explore two early cognitive precursors of pattern understanding, namely visuospatial skills and statistical learning. The proposed research comprises two studies. Study 1 aims to examine the cross-cultural difference between Chinese and Finnish children in number pattern understanding as precursor and outcome of their cognitive and arithmetic development. It is a cross-cultural study in which we will analyze secondary data collected in a longitudinal sample of 378 Finnish primary school children and new data to be collected in a longitudinal sample of 378 Chinese primary school children in Shanghai. Study 2 aims to extend our results into younger children and examine preschool children’s visual pattern understanding as precursor and outcome of cognitive development. To achieve this, we will study a sample of 200 young Chinese children in Hong Kong to be followed from their second to third kindergarten years. Together, the two studies will contribute to the scientific literature by unravelling the various types of pattern understanding (i.e., number patterns, visual repeating patterns, visual growing patterns, and visual rotation patterns) that contribute to arithmetic skills in two cultures and two age groups. The research will also attempt to identify the fundamental cognitive mechanisms (i.e., visuospatial skills and statistical learning) that promote or impede children’s pattern understanding. Findings are expected to shed light on cognitive development from a cross-cultural perspective and to provide information on the key elements that prevention and intervention programs should target to effectively facilitate children’s pattern understanding and arithmetic skills. 很多數學家都認為排列規律是數學的核心概念。幼稚園與小學課堂中充滿了各種各樣的排列規律活動。儘管發展心理學家最近開始研究兒童對排列規律的理解，我們對其前因後果知之甚少。因此，教授兒童對排列規律的理解是否有益於他們的數學學習以及如何教授，這些問題我們尚不清楚。不僅如此，世界各國對於數學課程和評估中應該投入多少資源的觀點也大相徑庭。在這項計畫中，我們會對芬蘭和中國兒童進行研究，以瞭解他們對排列規律的理解是否會影響他們的數學學習。此外，我們還會研究影響兒童規律理解的兩種認知因素：視覺空間能力和統計學習能力。

17612920.label: Project Objectives
17612920.value: (Objective 1) To characterise how perceptual training can promote plasticity of sensory eye balance and binocular mechanisms. o Task 1 will test the breadth of improvements that perceptual training can drive, using psychophysics to ask whether dichoptic signal-noise training (i.e., an increasingly popular paradigm where visual “signal” and “noise” are presented in separate eyes), can transfer to broader improvements in monocular and binocular functions beyond the immediately-trained paradigm (i.e., transfer to improvements in other tasks). (Objective 2) To understand the neural mechanisms underlying changes in sensory eye balance and binocular functions as driven by dichoptic noise-based training. o Task 2 will use whole-brain functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to image blood-oxygen-dependent (BOLD) activity before and after dichoptic training in visually normal individuals. o Task 3 will use magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) to ask whether neuroplastic changes driven by dichoptic training are accompanied by changes in brain biochemistry – particularly in terms of metabolic concentrations of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glutamate (Glu) in key areas of the visual cascade.

17612920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612920.value: In the normal population, only ~13% of individuals have perfectly balanced eyes, with the remaining 87% having varying extents of sensory eye dominance (i.e., where one eye’s input is weighted more heavily than the other). Notably, abnormal binocular balance is thought to underlie deficits in binocular function in clinical groups including those with strabismus (eye misalignment), or anisometropia (unequal refractive power). Much attention in recent years has been geared at developing methods for altering sensory eye balance with the eventual goal of improving binocular visual capacities, one of the most important of which is stereopsis (i.e., reconciling the slightly disparate information from the two eyes in order to judge depth-position). One such method is perceptual training, which has been shown to be effective in altering binocular balance both in visually normal individuals and in the visually impaired. Still, the mechanistic bases of sensory eye dominance and of their neuroplastic capacities are not well understood. The proposed project will use psychophysical measures integrated with neuroimaging (fMRI/MRS) methods in order to characterise mechanisms of binocular vision, particularly those underlying sensory eye dominance and their capacity for perceptual-learning-driven neuroplastic changes. The eventual goal of this work is to provide a platform upon which methods can be developed to ameliorate vision in the binocularly impaired. 在普通人群中，僅有約13%的人擁有完全平衡的眼睛，而其餘87%的人有不同程度的知覺性優勢眼（即一隻眼睛的輸入比另外一隻眼睛的輸入佔更大比重）。值得注意的是，雙眼平衡異常被認為是一些臨床上雙眼功能缺陷的原因，包括斜視（雙眼無法對準同一位置）和屈光參差（屈光力不相等）。近幾年，許多注意力都集中在開發各種方法來改變雙眼的平衡狀況，最終目標是提高雙眼視覺能力，其中最重要的一項是立體視覺（即通過調和雙眼中細微不同的信息來判斷深度位置）。其中一個受注目的方法是知覺學習，它已經被證實能夠有效改變正常人和視覺受損者雙眼的平衡。然而，我們對知覺性優勢眼及其神經可塑性能力背後的機制尚不完全清楚。本項目將使用心理物理學測量並結合神經影像（fMRI/MRS）的方法來表徵雙眼視覺的機制，特別是知覺性優勢眼以及其由知覺學習誘發的神經可塑性變化能力的機制。這項工作的最終目標是為開發改善雙眼視覺缺陷的方法提供新的思路。

17613220.label: Project Objectives
17613220.value: Aim 1. To examine independent longitudinal associations between green exposure and depression over 3-year follow-up period among residentially stable participants of Family Cohort, controlling for built environment, neighbourhood confounders as well as individual socio-demographic, lifestyle-related covariates and confounders. This will involve: a) spatial data modelling and calculation of individual-level metrics of green exposure and built environment confounders for study analytic sample b) developing longitudinal multi-level logistic regression models examining associations between greenness and depression, c) sensitivity analyses to measure differences in effect estimates across different exposure- and population-subgroups as well as c) developing non-linear dose-response models between odds of depression and change in green exposure over 3-year follow-up controlling for all covariates and confounders. Aim 2. To examine independent effects of residential migration from low green to high green areas upon depression over 3-year follow-up period controlling for all covariates and confounders. Aim 3. To test restorative stress-reduction effect of greenness, we shall investigate if the physiological mechanism from green exposure to depression proceed via the hypothesized restorative effect of greenness on chronic stress (stress-reduction). 17613220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613220.value: It has been widely evidenced that a city’s built environment and mental health are intrinsically interlinked, especially the protective effects of exposure to salutogenic green environments. The role of salutogenic green environment in ameliorating harmful aspects of city life and associated lifestyles is ever more important in high density vertical city like Hong Kong with low per-capita living space and reduced per-capita exposure to green space. There has thus far been no scientific population-based study examining detailed associations between exposure to greenness and depression in Hong Kong. We propose to leverage large scale data drawn from FAMILY Cohort, a population-representative Hong Kong-wide prospective cohort of health, happiness and family harmony to test a series of green exposure-mental health hypotheses. Objective and highly characterized indices of green exposures will be developed within residential street catchments of each geocoded participant of the FAMILY cohort. These will comprise high resolution satellite-derived measure of salutogenic green exposure collected at three time points as well as indices of density of public open spaces including parks and gardens (square footage within residential catchments) and proximity to public open spaces and sports facilities at neighbourhood-level, and country parks and natural green spaces at city-level. Built environment attributes including walkability, terrain and pollution exposures residential street catchments will also be measured for their confounding effects. Individual-level characteristics will also be adjusted for potential confounding. Longitudinal multi-level models will examine the associations of the measured greenness with depression over a 3-year follow-up period. A sub-sample of cohort participants relocating to new addresses during the follow-up period will be studied to examine the effects of relocating from low-green to high-green areas upon depression status. The study will also examine specific mechanism from green exposure to mental health via stress-reduction pathway using hair cortisol concentration as an objective marker of chronic stress. The study will be the first to provide longitudinal evidence on the links between green exposure and depression as well as providing insights into potential city-level urban interventions for public health benefit. The results generated from the study will have implications in optimizing allocation, size, density and configuration of green spaces to enhance accessibility and usage of these spaces, thereby reducing public health burdens of stress, mental health, and associated chronic disease. 廣泛的證據顯示，城市的建築環境和心理健康在本質上是相互聯繫的，尤其是身處於有益健康的綠化環境中所產生的保護作用。香港樓宇不斷以高密度向高空發展，人均居住空間淺窄，人均接觸綠化空間縮小，健康的綠化環境對改善城市生活和相關生活方式的角色變得越來越重要。至今香港缺乏有關綠化環境接觸與抑鬱症的關係的科學研究，我們提出利用「愛+人」隊列研究中的大數據，以檢驗一系列綠化環境接觸與心理健康的假設。「愛+人」是一項具人口代表性、有關香港的健康、幸福和家庭和睦的前瞻性隊列研究，我們將在每位參與者的住宅範圍進行地理編碼，開發具客觀性的綠化環境接觸指數，當中包括於三個時間點收集、並以高辨率衛星衍生的綠化指數，包含公園和花園在內的公共空間密度指數（住宅範圍內平方英尺），以及鄰近公共空間、體育設施、郊野公園和天然綠地的可及性指數。我們還會量度住宅範圍內的步行性，地形和污染接觸，以及個人層面的特徵，以對分析模型進行調整。 於三年追蹤期內，這項研究將以縱向多層模型檢測綠化環境接觸與抑鬱症之間的相關性。在追蹤期內，基於遷移到新住址的子樣本，我們會研究從低度綠化區域遷移到高度綠化區域對抑鬱狀態的影響。這項研究還將通過使用毛髮皮質醇濃度作為慢性壓力的客觀指標，研究透過綠化環境接觸減少壓力，以至心理健康的具體機制。 此項研究將首次提供有關綠化環境接觸與抑鬱症之間的關係的縱向證據，以及潛在城市干預措施的方向，惠及公共健康。這項研究的結果將對優化綠化空間的分配、大小、密度和配置產生影響，以增強這些空間的可及性和使用，從而減輕壓力、精神健康和相關慢性病的公共衛生負擔。

17613520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613520.value: On September 4 2019, I was invited to attend an annual gala dinner hosted by BigLove Alliance, a local NGO that advocates for lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) issues. Local celebrities such as Deanie Ip, Anthony Wong, and Joyce Cheng attended the event. At one point, the singer Anthony Wong gathered everyone onto the stage and sang Deanie Ip’s famous song “A Thousand Suns,” attesting to Ip’s long-standing commitment to the LGBT community. Three weeks later, I attended another event hosted by an NGO support group for aging gay men called Gay & Grey. The group emerged from an oral history project conducted by Dr. Travis Kong. The 5th year anniversary celebration that day also featured a photo exhibition. A new film called Suk Suk (dir. Ray Yeung, 2019) is inspired by the stories of these gay men, and it is already nominated for several awards at the upcoming Golden Horse Film Festival in Taipei. These two events underline the increasing synergy across the arts (literature, film, painting, photography, etc.), activism, and the creative industries in Hong Kong since the postcolonial handover in 1997. “Queer Hong Kong as Method” is the first research project on Hong Kong that combines the analytical strength of queer theory, Sinophone studies, social activism, and creative industry analysis. First, it explores the literary aesthetics of migration and queer sexuality in the works of Hong Kong writers like Wong Bik-wan, Ma Ka Fai, and others. Then, I examine the queer independent cinema of Scud, whose films often visualize transnational queer desire beyond the strictly Hong Kong-the UK-China postcolonial connections. This focus on visuality links to the queer arts that surfaced during the Umbrella Movement, in particular boys’ love fandom about student leaders. Next, I study transgender cinema as a particular type of creative industry through an analysis of Tracey (dir. Jun Li, 2018) and A Woman is a Woman (dir. Maisy Suen, 2018). Suen’s film also draws on autobiography and inspires an upcoming photo exhibit and fashion show. The concluding part of this project maps the LGBT NGO sector in Hong Kong, focusing on public events like Pink Dot, gender diversity and museum exhibit, and film festivals. Overall, this research provides an intersectional and integrative approach for tracing the often-overlooked linkage between art, activism, and the creative industries in contemporary queer Hong Kong culture. 2019年9月4日我應邀請參加大愛同盟的慈善晚會。大愛同盟是一間非政府組織主力於為男女同志，雙性戀和跨性別性小眾發聲。那天晚上出席的嘉賓有葉德嫻、黃耀明、鄭欣宜等明星和政商界名人。晚會上黃耀明呼籲所有人上台唱葉德嫻的首本名曲「千個太陽」，見證着她對這個群體一路以來的支持。三個星期後，我也應邀參加了另外一個非政府組織「晚同牽」的五周年紀念活動。這個組織是主要支持年長男同志的議題，也是香港大學社會學系教授江紹祺的口述史研究項目。在那個活動當中「晚同牽」辦了攝影展、一個關於這組織的電影《叔·叔》最近也獲得了香港，台灣及世界各項電影的獎項。 以上這兩項事件凸顯了藝術、行動主義、和創意產業之間日益增強的協同作用。「酷兒香港作為方法」是第一個結合了酷兒理論，華語語系研究，社會行動主義和創意產業分析的研究方針。一方面這個項目會探討黃碧雲、馬家輝等香港作家在他們的作品中展現出對移民和酷兒性的文學美學。另外我也考察香港同志獨立電影對於跨國同志的視覺文化怎樣呈現在雲翔的電影世界中。視覺文化和性別研究也跟雨傘運動後的耽美粉絲文化息息相關。其餘的研究方向包括跨性別電影與創意產業，以及性小眾非牟利組織在香港的各項活動以及影響力。總括，這個研究項目提供了一種交叉和綜合的方法來追溯當代香港酷兒藝術，行動主義和創意產業之間經常被忽略的聯繫。

17613520.label: Major findings and research outcome
17613520.value: “Queer Hong Kong as Method” is a transdisciplinary project that draws on the theoretical insights of feminist theory, postcolonial studies, queer theory, and Sinophone studies. It explores the creative synergy across various cultural domains such as literature, film, media, and the creative industries. My major finding is that queer Hong Kong culture exemplifies racial, gender, class, and sexual differences and incommensurability that challenge the existing confines of area studies and queer theory. The existing models of area studies tend to be national in scope, leaving small but globally significant regions like Hong Kong quite marginal to the field. Similarly, queer studies tends to treat non-Western countries and regions like Hong Kong as sites of information retrieval, thus overlooking how Hong Kong can also be a rich site of cultural comparison. As the project develops into the later stage of book manuscript publication and research output, I refine my conceptual model by proposing the concept of “unruly comparison.” Conceptually, “unruly comparison” intersects queerness, Hong Kong, and the Sinophone through friction, asymmetry, and perverse juxtapositions. To compare things in unruly ways is to acknowledge what Natalie Melas calls the “incommensurability” of comparative literature. My model of unruly comparison takes incommensurability as a given. A queer Sinophone approach shows that Hong Kong as a historic colonial city and postcolonial region under the shadow of China-centrism and global capitalism already evinces infinite possibilities of transnational comparison and worldliness. In other words, Hong Kong already embodies “all the difference in the world,” to borrow Melas’s provocative phrase. The notion of unruly comparison also draws on Shu-mei Shih’s model of relational comparison: “Comparison as relation means setting into motion historical relationalities between entities brought together for comparison, and bringing into relation terms that have traditionally been pushed apart from each other.” Each part of this project turns to a specific concept that has animated the fields of Sinophone studies, Hong Kong studies, and queer theory, including the archive (Chapter 1), transnationalism (Chapter 2), transgender (Chapter 3), intimacies (Chapter 4), and border (Chapter 5). Collectively, my project shows how an unruly entanglement of queerness, Hong Kong, and the Sinophone puts analytical pressure on these concepts, which in turn troubles the disciplinary habits of area studies, China studies, and queer theory.

We are applying the domain of http://www.queerhk.hku.hk to maintain the website for future development. I also fulfilled the objective of generating a new model for studying queer Hong Kong culture by coining the concept of “unruly comparison.” This concept also informs my book titled Unruly Comparison: Queerness, Hong Kong, and the Sinophone (forthcoming with Duke University Press, 2025). I have also disseminated my research at traditional academic platforms like the MLA and ACLA conferences as well as through public events like the Hong Kong Book Fair. 17613520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17613520.value: “Queer Hong Kong as Method” generates new conceptual tools for studying gender and sexuality in Asia. It demonstrates that marginal and small regions in Asia like Hong Kong can also be extremely productive sites for rethinking the existing theoretical models in area studies and queer theory. It shows how places like Hong Kong generate unruly models for global and cultural comparison that disrupt the Eurocentrism of existing studies. The knowledge exchange platforms generated by my project provide students, researchers, and the general public more access to information on queer Hong Kong culture. This knowledge can be quite scattered and incoherent at conventional archives and sites like the public library, Hong Kong film archive, Hong Kong Public Records office, and the like. By creating a website devoted to queer Hong Kong, my research makes this knowledge more accessible. I also disseminated the significance of the research through academic genres like journal articles, book chapters in edited volumes, and a book manuscript.

17613820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613820.value: 青春期是一個非常脆弱的過渡階段，常與心理健康和睡眠問題的出現相關聯。睡眠障礙，特別是失眠，是青少年中最常見的睡眠問題，患病率高達36%。失眠會對青少年的社會心理發展、行為、和身心健康等方面造成一系列不良的影響。然而，青少年失眠的最佳治療策略仍不確定。目前，美國食品和藥物管理局（FDA）沒有特別批準用於18 歲以下兒童青少年中治療失眠的藥物。盡管目前有大量研究證據支持失眠的認知行為治療（CBT-I）作為成年人失眠的一線治療方法，有關將CBT-I應用於治療青少年失眠的研究尚處於起步階段，并且缺乏長期隨訪的數據。在治療青少年失眠的過程中，還需要考慮青少年人群獨特的睡眠和節律特征以及導致其失眠持續存在的社會心理因素。有初步證據顯示CBT-I是治療青少年失眠的一個有效方法。此外，由於青少年常常使用網路和智能手機，他們較適合在線的治療方案。目前有關在線CBT治療青少年睡眠問題的研究依然有限，因為現有的治療研究大多是在成人樣本中進行。由於青少年失眠與一系列有害後果密切相關，青少年失眠的治疗研究數據會為臨床實踐提供重要的信息。此外，CBT-I在青少年中治療的持續效果有待進一步探討。為了解決現有文獻的局限性，我們提出進行隨機對照試驗，以檢驗基於小組形式和在線形式的CBT-I對於青少年失眠患者的睡眠和情緒症狀，以及其他臨床症狀和白天整體功能的治療效果。在這項研究中，150位符合資格的青少年將被隨機分配接受6週CBT-I治療（小組治療或者使用智能手機應用程序的在線治療）或進入等待列表對照組。評估將在治療前（第0週），治療期間（第2週和第4週）和治療後（第6週/最後一節治療結束後）進行。兩個積極治療組將在治療後六個月和十二個月進一步追蹤。本研究中建立的經驗數據，治療模型和方案將會為未來的臨床實踐提供重要信息，有助於未來青少年失眠的臨床治療。

17614320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614320.value: 功能城市通常是由鄰近城市城市化的區域所組成，這些區域具有緊密的功能性聯繫。 中國沒有官方劃定的功能城市。 由於許多城市的發展已經超出了行政範圍，因此中國的行政城市往往與功能城市的邊界並不一致。 但是，城市規劃和管治大多受到行政邊界的限制，因此不能有效地解決在行政邊界之外但在功能城市內部發生的問題。 同樣，使用行政城市作為分析單元可能會高估或低估城市間之出勤（或遷移），並導致對區域城市系統空間結構的錯誤分析。 因此，我們有必要厘定超越行政城市的功能城市。 以前我們通常用基於通勤指標，記錄等方法來分析和厘定功能城市。 然而，城市居民的日常活動不限制於通勤。 與通勤流量相比，活動空間作為不同類型日常活動的行為，應該是厘定功能性城市的更可靠指標。 這項研究主要是研究如何利用活動空間方法去分析和厘定中國特大城市群的功能城市，並驗證現有文獻中常用方法的可靠性。它以珠江三角洲的特大城市群進行分析。本研究有三個研究目標。首先，它將使用活動空間方法來分析和厘定功能城市。它將利用手機網絡大數據來構建個人的活動空間，然後基於個人活動空間的覆蓋來分析和厘定功能城市。其次，它將通過分析功能內和功能間城市的出行方式，探討珠三角洲特大城市群功能城市系統的空間結構。第三，它將評估現有文獻中常用的分析方法的可靠性，包括社會經濟方法，城市建築面積方法，夜間活動密度方法，道路/設施密度方法和通勤流量方法。這將有助於找到哪種方法是當沒有更詳細的手機網絡大數據時，是功能城市劃分的最佳方法。 這項研究將通過探討新興的跨地區旅行來豐富中國城市活動空間的知識。 它還將提供一種可靠的方法來分析和厘定功能城市，以進行空間分析和規劃，並深化對中國特大城市群空間結構的認識。 這以珠江三角洲特大城市群為例的研究，也可以應用於中國其他特大城市群的地區，增加我們對其空間結構的認知。

17614320.label: Realisation of objectives
17614320.value: 1. To delineate functional cities in mega city region using the proposed activity-space method with mobile phone cellular network data; Completed. This project develops a novel method based upon mobile phone cellular network data and fine-grained population data to delineate functional cities in China. At a spatial unit of 1 km grid cells, the fine-grained population data are used to infer population density to identify core areas of functional cities. Thereafter, mobile phone cellular network data are used to infer commuting flows to identify periphery areas that are economically integrated with the core areas. Using 9 prefecture-level cities in the Pearl River Delta of southern China as a case study, a total of 26 functional cities are identified. The robustness of functional city delineation is validated based on three criteria, namely sensitivity, realisticness, and compactness. This project thus unravels that prefecture-level cities in China are not good representation of functional cities. Some of the prefecture-level cities have multiple functional cities that are functionally separate from each other, while some functional cities may surpass the administrative borders and be shared by two or more prefecture-level cities. Through the empirical case, the project contributes a rigorous method to delineate functional cities that is not affected by the spatial configuration of administrative boundaries at any scales, which can facilitate more precise understanding of regional spatial interactions and more effective measures in regional governance. 2. To analyze the spatial structure of functional city system in the Pearl River Delta mega city region using the delineated functional cities; Completed. This project contributes important findings regarding spatial structure of functional city system, particularly whether people in the same social area have similar work mobility and whether location matters from an aggregated neighborhood perspective. A case study is conducted within the Pearl River Delta using mobile phone cellular network data and fine-grained census and mobile phone data, which are integrated into 500 m grid for analysis. Results show that different social areas have significantly different work mobility, and the within-group heterogeneity is also prominent. Three location factors are examined and it is found that there exist variations in the influence of spatial factors on work mobility for different social areas. These findings will supplement current knowledge about social areas, location and mobility in urban China at the mesoscale. In addition, the methodology provides a feasible framework of integrating city-scale socioeconomic information and mobility data from different sources for future urban studies, which is conducive to better understanding the spatial structure of functional city system in mega city regions such as the Pearl River Delta. 3. To evaluate the reliability of conventional methods in delineating functional cities that have been commonly used in existing literature in order find out which method is the best proxy for the delineation of functional cities when the more robust activity-space method using cellular network data is not available. Completed. The project presents a detailed review of conventional methods in delineating functional cities that have been commonly used. It finds that many studies adopted various methods to define functional cities in China. Some researchers used socioeconomic indicators from official statistical data to demarcate functional cities because commuting data are still unsystematically collected or publicly unavailable in China. For example, they defined functional cities based on socio-economic indicators, such as the percentage of non-agriculture sectors in GDP and labor force, per capita GDP, population density and urbanization rate. These were all proxy indicators used to calibrate and imply functional interactions between different locations. Nevertheless, mobility data are still the preferred approach used to delineate functional cities, particularly with the upsurge of massive spatio-temporal mobility data (e.g., smart card and mobile phone data) in the recent decade. Amongst these data, mobile phone data have facilitated the analysis of commuting patterns on a large scale with high accuracy. The project further argues that, while the big data-based studies have contributed innovative attempts to delineate functional cities in China by highlighting the interactions between different locations, their limitations in terms of sample bias and over-/under-estimation of commuting trips should be explicitly addressed. Also, while those efforts cast their focus on the spatial interactions by commuting trips, it is noteworthy that the daily activities of urban residents are not restricted to commuting. Furthermore, while these big data-based city delineation approaches are promising as being operationally practical and efficient, the reliability of these approaches was confined by the well-documented limitations of big datasets. The quality of the data utilized, and thus the robustness of findings, was also strongly affected by the algorithms for data processing and the areal units for data aggregation. Therefore, this project calls for combined datasets of multiple sources to alleviate the negative impacts of sample bias, algorithmic uncertainty, and modifiable areal unit problem on the reliability of city delineation, and to facilitate effective delineation of functional cities when cellular network data are not available.

17614320.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614320.value: This project develops a novel method using mobile phone cellular network data and fine-grained population data to delineate functional cities in China. At a spatial unit of 1 km grid cells, the fine-grained population data are used to infer population density to identify core areas of urban functional areass. Thereafter, mobile phone cellular network data are used to infer commuting flows to identify periphery areas that are economically integrated with the core areas. Using 9 prefecture-level cities in the Pearl River Delta of southern China as a case study, a total of 26 urban functional areas are identified. This project thus unravels that prefecture-level cities in China are not good representation of functional cities. Some of the prefecture-level cities have multiple urban functional area that are functionally separate from each other, while some urban functional area may surpass the administrative borders and be shared by two or more prefecture-level cities. On this basis, the project identifies spatial structure of functional city system, particularly whether people in the same social area have similar work mobility and whether location matters from an aggregated neighborhood perspective. It finds that different social areas have significantly different work mobility, and the within-group heterogeneity is also prominent. Three location factors are examined and it is found that there exist variations in the influence of spatial factors on work mobility for different social areas. The proposed method provides a feasible framework of integrating city-scale socioeconomic information and mobility data from different sources for future urban studies, which is conducive to better understanding the spatial structure of functional city system in mega city regions such as the Pearl River Delta. Finally, the project presents a detailed review of conventional methods in delineating functional cities that have been commonly used. It finds that many studies adopted various methods to define functional cities in China. It calls for combined datasets of multiple sources to alleviate the negative impacts of sample bias, algorithmic uncertainty, and modifiable areal unit problem on the reliability of city delineation, and to facilitate effective delineation of functional cities when cellular network data are not available.

17614320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614320.value: To further enhance the method, future studies will incorporate data of multiple days and multiple types of daily activities, and attempt to identify the most appropriate spatial unit to delineate functional cities by comparing the grid cells of different sizes. Also, given that urban systems are characterized by hierarchical structures at many different scales, future studies will attempt to uncover the hierarchies of functional cities to redefine regional/subregional entities at different scales in China. Furthermore, future studies will discuss the issues concerning the choice of place-specific and generalized thresholds in the delineation of functional cities. Finally, this project highlights that the definitions of cities vary substantially across countries. There is a need for more scholarly efforts in the future to develop universal criteria for (re)defining functional cities as supplements to the nationally developed definitions, in order to facilitate comparative studies across different countries.

17614320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614320.value: While this project focuses on the city definition in China, its implications are not limited to China but applicable to other countries and regions. The phenomenon that cities encompass rural areas is not unique to China. Several other countries, including Indonesia, Philippines, Republic of Korea, South Africa and the Democratic Republic of Congo, have also applied similar approach to identify urban units, and thus the critical challenges summarized from the analysis of China in this project may also be applicable in these countries. Moreover, defining functional cities of China in a proper way may also benefit global projections of urban population due to the large population of China which have implications for prognosing the magnitude of megacities and their potential problems, such as inadequate public services for rural-to-urban migrants, around the world, especially in the developing countries. The research has contributed to a paper "Defining a City - Delineating Urban Areas Using Cell-Phone Data" published in Nature Cities (Lei et al. 2024), 1:117-125

17614720.label: Project Objectives
17614720.value: Explore the formation mechanism of edu-featured GCs of various types amidst the state-market-society interplay. Education has long been an important factor influencing housing choice and price internationally. In China, the centrality of education in family lives, especially housing choice, is deeply rooted in the Confucian culture and reinforced at the present time due to the fierce competition and increased wealth in the urban society, particularly among the middle-class. Meanwhile, gated community (GC) has become the most prevalent residential form in China (He, 2013). Despite of a recent attempt by the central government to curb the rapid proliferation of GCs in 2016, GC remains a predominant residential form in Chinese cities, due to the lack of feasible alternative solutions for providing secure and efficient housing forms (Xu, et al., 2018). Feeding into the rising demands for high-quality education and privileged lifestyle, education-featured gated communities (edu-featured GCs) have become a prevalent form of residential development and accommodating tens of millions of Chinese urban middle-class, as widely documented in numerous Chinese reports on “education real estate” (教育地產). Yet, scholarly exploration on this topic is still lacking. This research thus first proposes to adopt the analytical framework of state-market-society interactions (He and Lin, 2015; He et al., 2017) that integrates political economy, socio-cultural and institutional approaches to examine how the interplay of the state (national policies and local authorities), market (developers and education providers) and society (middle-class) gives rise to various forms of edu-featured GCs. Examine the changing dynamics and patterns of housing differentiation induced by edu-featured GCs at both metropolitan and neighborhood scales. The exclusiveness of high-quality education and housing is mutually reinforced in edu-featured GCs, to which low-income households are denied access. After two decades’ development, edu-featured GCs have significantly transformed the residential and education landscapes of many Chinese cities. This is alarming for cities that already suffer from worsening housing affordability and social inequality. Since late 2018, some local governments (e.g. Shanghai and Chongqing) have started to realize the detrimental effects and have tried to curb the further expansion of edu-featured GCs. It is therefore a high time to empirically measure the impact of edu-featured GCs on housing development. In this research, we deliberately distinguish education from residential club goods in GCs because of its nature of public good and its importance in shaping the (re)production of social inequality. By so doing, this study will offer a more accurate and dynamic understanding of the capitalization effect of education (as a public good turned semi-club good) vis-à-vis residential club goods provided by edu-featured GCs in (re)shaping housing differentiation at both metropolitan and neighborhood levels, through applying Hedonic price modeling and Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM). Advance and bridge the scholarly inquiries into gated communities and the capitalization effect of education. This research considers edu-featured GCs in China as a new mechanism of residential sorting and housing differentiation primarily based on education choice, which is closely linked to the literature of gated communities and the capitalization effect of education. Providing education services (most commonly kindergartens and training services) within residential neighbourhoods as part of the amenity package is not a new practice, which can be found in certain GCs globally and China’s work unit compounds under planned economy. But it is uncommon that GCs are closely tied with primary/secondary schools and offers privileged access to them. More importantly, purposively exploiting education as a strategy to generate housing premium and the widespread of edu-featured GCs are unseen in any other contexts. Dwelling on the two bodies of literature on gated communities and the capitalization effect of education, this project will present an in-depth scrutiny into edu-featured GCs through a new conceptual lens. We aim to advance conceptual and methodological inquiries into the club economy of GCs by applying equilibrium sorting models, while refashioning the theoretical interpretations for housing differentiation in urban China that is often preoccupied by socioeconomic concerns and supply-side explanations, through scrutinizing the demand-side mechanism. Inform policy-making to promote more inclusive and equitable housing development in wider regions, including Hong Kong. Employing mixed-methods to carry out in-depth empirical investigations in Guangzhou, the birth place of edu-featured GCs, this research intends to enrich our empirical understandings by presenting a rich set of data for a new type of residential-cum-education development that still lacks scholarly examinations. By so doing, policy recommendations supported by rich empirical evidence and reliable analytical results will be presented to relevant government organizations, e.g. the education bureau, housing and construction bureau, development and reform commission, planning institutions, to inform their decision-making.

17614720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614720.value: Education has always played a significant role in residential choice. Meanwhile, a strong desire for high-quality urban living surges among Chinese middle-class households. Over the past two decades, education market has become a hot spot for real estate investment in urban China and gave birth to “education real estate” (教育地產) that widely documented in Chinese media and real estate consultancy and financial reports. Yet, there is a dearth of scholarly work on this eye-catching phenomenon. To fill this salient lacuna, the PI coins the term “education-featured gated communities (edu-featured GCs)” to delineate the most dominant form of “education real estate” that offers privileged access to primary/secondary schools and exclusive residential environment to form a special type of gated community (GC). First emerged in Guangzhou in 1994 and subsequently prevailing in the whole country, the development of edu-featured GCs is closely related to two types of policies: planning regulations requiring developers building schools in new urban areas, and national policies encouraging private involvement in education provision. As GC has taken up more than 80% of new residential development in China, edu-featured GCs also grows into a sizeable housing type nationally. Edu-featured GCs turn education from a public good to a semi-club good being capitalized in the housing price. The increasing magnitude of edu-featured GCs is alarming, because their privileged access to quality schools packaged with tailor-made residential services are very likely to intensify education and housing inequalities, and worsen housing affordability. Most recently, some local governments have tried to restrict the further expansion of edu-featured GCs. Yet, scholarly understanding of this special type of GC, especially its formation mechanism and implications on housing development, that can inform effective policy-making, is still lacking. Based on empirical studies in Guangzhou, a city spearheaded edu-featured GCs development, this research proposes to examine the formation of various types of edu-featured GCs amidst state-market-society interactions and quantitatively measure their impacts on housing differentiation at metropolitan and neighborhood scales. Bridging two lines of inquiry into GCs and the capitalization effect of education, this study fills theoretical, methodological and empirical lacunae in the literature. Combing quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methods, this research aims to capture a full picture of this prevalent trend of residential-cum-education development that significantly affects the equal access to education and housing. Taken together, it will inform policy making on inclusive housing development in mainland China and wider regions including Hong Kong. 教育在住房選擇中一直起著相當重要的作用。同時，中國中產階級家庭對高品質城市生活的需求與日俱增。近二十年來，教育市場已成為中國城市房地產投資的熱點議題，催生出中國媒體、房地產中介和財務報表中廣泛記載的“教育地產”。然而，針對這一引人注目的現象的相關學術研究卻很少。為彌補這一突出的研究空白，本課題創造了“教育特色門禁社區”(education-featured gated communities)這一術語去描述教育地產中最主流的一種居住形式，即為住戶提供中小學入學特權和高檔居住環境的封閉社區。教育特色門禁社區最早于1994年出現在廣州并隨後在中國全國範圍內流行，其發展和兩類政策密切相關：要求開發商在新區建立學校的規劃和鼓勵民辦教育的國家政策。隨著封閉社區占中國新開發住宅的比例超過八成，教育特色封閉社區也在全國範圍內發展為一種相當規模的住宅類型。 教育特色門禁社區將教育從公共物品轉變為一種被資本化的半俱樂部性質物品。教育特色門禁社區的規模增大是令人擔憂的，因為這些社區賦予的進入優質學校的特權和提供的量身定制的居住服務很有可能會加劇教育和住房不平等，並且惡化住房負擔能力。最近，一些地方政府試圖限制教育特色封閉社區的進一步發展。然而，學術界對這一特殊類型的封閉社區，尤其是其形成機制及其對住房發展的影響，尚缺乏足以提供有效政策依據的理解。本研究以廣州這一教育特色封閉社區領先發展的城市為例，探討在國家-市場-社會互動中不同類型的教育特色封閉社區的形成機制，並且定量地衡量其對住房分異在城市和鄰里尺度上的影響。 本研究連接了封閉社區和教育資本化效應兩條研究線索，填補了已有文獻在理論、方法和實證方面的空白。通過定量和定性相結合的數據收集和分析方法，本研究旨在全面了解這一影響教育與住房平等機會的普遍趨勢。綜上所述，本研究的成果將為中國內地乃至香港地區的包容性住房開發政策制定提供信息和依據

17614720.label: Realisation of objectives
17614720.value: 1) This project has successfully achieved all the pre-stated research objectives and yielded 15 high-quality journal articles, which has far exceeded the original goal. Papers published in The Geographical Journal, Urban Studies, Geoforum, Environment and Planning A: Economy and Space, Antipode, Applied Geography, and Annals of the American Association for Geographers, Housing studies etc. (please see the attached list of research outputs) have addressed the first three research objectives, and significantly contributed to the advancement of the critical geographies of education in multiple ways. Specifically, 1.1) These papers shed light on how the interplay of the state (national policies and local authorities), market (developers and education providers), and society (middle-class) gives rise to various forms of education-featured gated communities (see for instance Cai & He, 2024; Cai, Hu & He, 2022; He & Cai, 2023; He & He, 2024a,b). He (2022) in the Geographical Journal shows how the pursuit of quality living and good schools has given rise to ‘education-featured gated communities’ that package privileged access to K–12 schools with tailor-made residential services. Further, He & Cai (2023) in Urban Studies introduces a novel conceptual framework of multiscalar and multidirectional urban entrepreneurialism to understand the governance dynamics in these ‘education-featured gated communities’. Additionally, He & He (2024) shows that the recent process of school franchising (jiao yu ji tuan hua), which is implemented across cities and involves almost all the schools within cities, is underpinned by a nexus of entrepreneurial local states, profiteering developers, and expansionist schools. Particularly, the state strategically orchestrates and meticulously calibrates school franchising and its geography to enable desired mobilities and facilitate urban (re)development. Cai, Hu & He (2022) also show that the state facilitates gentrification through education expansion in Shanghai. 1.2) These papers advance conceptual and methodological inquiries into the club economy of gated communities (He & He, 2024a; He & Cai, 2023; Hu & He, 2024; Hu et al., 2020). Conceptually, He & Cai (2023) uses an novel conceptual framework of multiscale and multidimensional governance framework and shows that by turning education from a public good into a club good that can be capitalized in the housing price and leveraged in urban (re)development, education-featured gated communities are highly sought after by homebuyers, developers, and local states, becoming an important and integral component of urban entrepreneurialism. Such semi-private governance of gated communities forms the institutional basis for the ‘shareholding enterprise’ centering on property values. He & He (2024) draws on the Bourdieusian concept of ‘field’ and the theorization of ‘intersectionality’ and proposes the concept of ‘intersectional field’ to disentangle the complex interrelations between housing and education in China. They argue that these two fields mutually constitute and co-produce yet trouble and counteract each other, exerting simultaneous exclusion in cultural and economic (re)production. The equilibrium between them evolves over time and varies in space between the suburbs and city center. For instance, housing played a stronger role in residential choices in the 90s, while education and school quality have overtaken housing quality as the main consideration. This project also contributes to methodological innovations in exploring the club economy of gated communities. For instance, Hu & He (2024) employs machine learning algorithms to explore the nonlinear relationship between housing sales prices and the academic performance of nearby schools and challenges the prevalent linear understanding between them. First, they show that entrance opportunity, an integral part of school quality beyond academic performance, also affects both housing sales prices and housing rental prices. Housing rental prices, particularly in the lower-priced segment, are more determined by entrance opportunity than academic performance, while the latter is the most important factor influencing housing sales prices. The nonlinear capitalization effect suggests that tenants and homebuyers are willing to pay more for school quality increases only within specific ranges, namely, from median to a relatively high level of school quality. These findings contribute to a more nuanced and updated understanding of the education capitalization effect and thus inform more inclusive and equitable urban planning and governance. 1.3) These papers also refashion the theoretical interpretations for housing differentiation in urban China, which is often preoccupied with socioeconomic concerns and supply-side explanations, by scrutinizing the demand-side mechanism. For instance, He & He (2024a) shows how the middle class strategizes on the intersectional field of education and housing to achieve both economic reproduction and cultural reproduction. These strategic residential selections facilitate and reinforce socio-spatial inequalities. Those with limited socio-economic capacities remain extremely disadvantaged in both fields. Additionally, Hu et al. (2024) in Applied Geography employed a quasi-natural experiment based on 2013–2021 housing transaction data in Shenzhen, China, and estimated the causal effects of school-to-school collaboration (SSC) on housing market dynamics. They uncover the uneven capitalization of public schools into housing prices among schools of different qualities and between established and newly formed schools. They particularly emphasize the importance of school brands on residential/schooling choices for parents and consequently on housing price increases in neighborhoods where these schools are located. 2) Two post-doctoral fellows who worked on this project have secured positions at prestigious universities, including Sun Yat-Sen University in Guangzhou, Guangdong, and the University of St Andrews in Scotland. One fellow has also developed a National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) grant application that builds on and extends beyond the research direction of this project. Furthermore, one PhD candidate has just finalised heir doctoral thesis on relevant topics. 3) This project has also led to the establishment of more connections and collaborations with local government officials and urban planners, who are now involved in planning projects to ensure the even distribution of education resources and utilising education to facilitate urban (re)development. 4) Research findings have been disseminated through international conferences and workshops to wider academic and non-academic audience to inform schorlarly research and policy-making in wider regions.

17614720.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614720.value: 1) The rise of education-featured gated communities is intricately connected with four-dimensional processes, including the state-capital nexus (upward-looking), individual choices for social reproduction (downward-looking), middle-class parents' expectations and schooling choices (inward-looking), connections between education and urban (re)development (outward-looking). Specifically, education-featured gated communities emerged and developed at the nexus of an entrepreneurial state (to utilize education for urban governance and facilitate (re)development), profit-seeking developers, and the self-enterprising middle class in pursuit of successful social reproduction. 2). School quality positively correlates with property value but is unevenly distributed spatially. The capitalization effect of education on housing is more prominent in the city center than in the suburbs but has recently been reinforced. These spatial-temporal changes are closely connected with local education policies aimed at expanding quality schools from the city center, where they concentrate, to the suburbs. 3). Essentially, education-featured gated communities have formed a "shareholding enterprise," where the entrepreneurial local state, developers, gated communities, and individual homeowners/investor-citizens strive to maintain property value and facilitate urban (re)development. This involves multidirectional and multiscaler urban entrepreneurialism. 4). In the Chinese context, this intimate interaction between housing and education also forms an "intersectional field," where they co-produce and mutually shape each other, but also contradict with and cancel each other out. This, on the one hand, leads to the simultaneous and dual privilege of cultural and economic reproduction for those who can buy into such high-quality school districts, through receiving high-quality education and education-facilitated housing price increase, and relatedly and consequently dual marginalization and exclusion. While we celebrate the effectiveness and efficiency of education in facilitating urban (re)development, we have to be aware of the inequalities and marginalization imbricated within. On the other, this also reminds us that in the policymaking process, we must consider the intersection of these two fields, rather than the individual field, to avoid unintended effects.

17614720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614720.value: Besides the seven papers published, we have five more under review in top journals, based on our research projects. These include a critical analysis of recent education policies such as the "Double Reduction" and "School Franchising," focusing on how education is embedded within and (re)shapes broader social spatial structures and processes. We also examine education-led housing behaviors at the individual level, as well as the impact of school quality and policy on housing prices. Several others are in progress, exploring topics such as education-led residential mobility and gentrification, and school effect on neighborhood interaction. We aim also to apply our findings to inform policy-making processes. For example, our examination of the “intersectional field” of housing and education, where they co-produce yet trouble and counteract with each other, highlights the need to consider the dynamics of both fields and their intersection when making education or housing planning and governance policies. We are also in negotiations to collaborate with urban planners and state policy makers on an education-led urban (re)development project in Guangzhou.

17614720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614720.value: Education-featured gated communities are becoming increasingly prevalent, where K-12 schools are combined with residential services. This leads to inequalities in accessing education, housing affordability, and residential services. However, its formation mechanism amidst state-market-society interplay, and its impact on housing price and differentiation across time and space, have so far under-explored. This project uses 45 interviews with policymakers from education and urban planning departments, real estate developers, school principals and teachers, and middle-class parents, a survey of 1800 questionnaires across 60 neighbourhoods, and online housing transaction data. Main findings include that 1) Education-featured gated communities emerged and developed due to the interplay of an entrepreneurial state facilitating education-led urban development, profit-seeking developers, and the self-enterprising middle class seeking successful social reproduction. 2) This involves a multiscalar and multi-directional urban entrepreneurialism centered around keeping up the property value. 3)The capitalisation effect of education on housing is stronger in the city centre than suburbs, but was reinforced across the city due to policy intervention to spread quality schools from the city centre to the suburbs. 4) Housing and education interacted intensively and formed an "intersectional field". Policy-making needs to consider dynamics in each field and their interaction to avoid unintended effects.
