18300720.label: Major findings and research outcome
18300720.value: The research output was written in three papers with detail given as follows. In the first paper (refer to [1] in Section 8 Part C), we investigate the properties of an abstract family of advection diffusion equations in the context of the fractional Laplacian. Two independent diffusion parameters enter the system, one via the constitutive law for the drift velocity and one as the prefactor of the fractional Laplacian. We obtain existence and convergence results in certain parameter regimes and limits. We study the long time behaviour of solutions to the general problem and prove the existence of a unique global attractor. We apply results to two particular active scalar equations arising in geophysical fluid dynamics, namely the surface quasigeostrophic equation and the magnetogeostrophic equation, which address Objectives 1 and 2 for the case for the case of magnetogeostrophic equation. These are new and substantial results for the MG equations in the context of long time behaviour, which certainly deepen our understanding on the subject. In the second paper (refer to [2] in Section 8 Part C), we summarise our results on various general classes of active scalar equation, in particular with applications on physical models including surface quasigeostrophic (SQG) equation, MG equation and the incompressible porous media Brinkman equation. In particular, in the third paper (refer to [3] in Section 8 Part C), we revised the previous results and successfully showed that the incompressible porous media Brinkman equation has local-in-time analytic solutions, and such analytic solutions can be extended to global-in-time solutions when the initial data is chosen to be small with respect to the analytic norm. The obtained solutions will converge (with respect to Sobolev or analytic norms) to the corresponding solution to the system for ν=0 when ν tends to zero. These are new and fundamental results for these physical models which sets a new benchmark for the subject, in particular we may extend our understanding on other important physical models including SQG equations.

18300720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18300720.value: The results of the research project inspire the PI to address an abstract general class of active scalar equations, with emphasis on the (i) ill/well- posedness, (ii) long time behaviour and (iii) anomalous dissipation. We hope that by analysing the general results for active scalar equations, we can deepen our understanding on physical models which include MG equation, IPMB equation and SQG equation. The success of the research project also leads the PI to develop a new research project, which is funded by General Research Fund (GRF) from Research Grants Council (RGC) (Ref: 18300821).

18300920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18300920.value: 光催化氧化是在室溫和環境壓力下分解氮氧化物的最常見方法之一。常規的光催化劑（例如二氧化鈦）主要將一氧化氮(NO) 氧化為仍然是有毒的空氣污染物二氧化氮（NO2），以及會導致催化劑失活的硝酸鹽。與氧化反應相比，利用光催化將氮氧化物還原為氮氣，既不會引起二次污染，也不會導致催化劑失活。然而，在去除氮氧化物的反應過程中，氮氧化物通過光催化還原產生氮氣的選擇性極低。因此，從環境空氣中去除氮氧化物而不使其失活和產生二次污染是一個嚴峻的挑戰。本研究專案提議一種新的光催化與電化學系統耦合系統，以去除減少氮氧化物。在這種混合過程中，新的光電催化系統不僅在光催化過程中顯著抑制了光生電荷載流子（即電子和空穴）的複合，而且在處理過程中具有協同優勢，減少了能源的利用，令總體成本降低。與典型的電催化還原污染物相比，光電催化系統所需的陰極電位也相對較低。此項目將特別設計用於在氮氧化物還原中進行光電催化的相對複雜的反應設備，例如氣體、固體和液體三相反應界面。我們的初步研究結果表明，在該光電催化系統下，氮氧化物可以顯著還原。我們將通過理論計算及實驗表徵，研究催化劑表面化學對氧化和還原光電催化反應過程、氮氧化物氣體吸附、可見光吸收、能帶結構、界面電荷傳輸機理和氮氧化物的去除反應過程及其機理。這項目也是首次將具有高選擇性的光電催化系統用於將氮氧化物在大氣環境下還原為氮的研究。本項目引入了一種高效且廉價的方法，通過太陽能/可見光產生的光電催化反應，實現將環境中氮氧化物還原為環境友好的氮氣，從而促進利用太陽能來解決空氣污染而不失活和產生二次污染的實際應用。

18301320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18301320.value: 水源和供水處理系統中的藥物殘留

18301320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18301320.value: Pharmaceuticals are designed for disease treatment or prevention, therefore, they alter the physiological function of organisms, whether that’s of aquatic fauna or in humans. The widespread existence of pharmaceutical residues in water systems has been known about for years. The impact this has on human health, even when present at trace levels, is of increasing concern worldwide, including among governments as well as scientists and the general public. The potential risk to human health from exposure to these “pseudo-persistent” and “biologically active compounds” via drinking water cannot be overemphasised. The concern is that continual discharge of municipal wastewater and effluent that contain excretions from humans who have been taking medication, and also from the disposal of medication from a number of sources, contaminate the source waters and are then detected in our drinking water. In Hong Kong, source waters come from local catchments as well as imported source (mainly from the Dong River which is the eastern tributary of the Pearl River in Guangdong province). It’s a daily challenge to treat the vast amount of raw water created in one of the most densely and populated cities in the world and there are many treated different treatment methods being used. Despite these efforts, recent studies have found that the removal of these biologically active compounds by such water treatment processes is worryingly low. In addition, increasing contamination by pharmaceutical residues has been reported in the wastewater and corresponding receiving environments of South China. Given these low elimination rates alongside increasing demands for pharmaceuticals in populated regions (Hong Kong and cities in Guangdong), it is conceivable that chemicals are polluting the source waters. Furthermore, emerging concerns about the degradation products of pharmaceuticals has led to further concerns about the safety of drinking water. Undoubtedly, there is currently a lack of fundamental information about their distribution and fate of these water-borne and biologically active chemicals in the water treatment systems and source waters. It is therefore imperative to investigate them in different water treatment plants adopting conventional and advanced techniques, in order to keep track of changes in the water quality. Consequently, the overall aim of this study is to identify and quantify pharmaceutical residues and their possible degradation products at a number of water treatment works to investigate their source and fate by mass balance analysis, and to evaluate potential health risks based on exposure levels in the treated drinking water. Consequently, the overall aim of this study is to identify and quantify pharmaceutical residues at a number of water treatment works to investigate their source and fate by mass balance analysis, and to evaluate potential health risks based on exposure levels in the treated drinking water. 摘要: 藥物是專為疾病治療或預防而設計的，因此，它們會改變生物的生理功能，無論是水生動物還是人類。在水系統中藥物殘留物的廣泛存在已經知道了多年。在痕量水平上即使對人體健康的影響極低，其影響也日益受到全世界的關注，包括政府，科學家及公眾。縱然不能過分強調通過飲用水接觸這些“偽持久性”和“生物活性化合物”對人類健康的潛在風險。令人擔憂的是，不斷排放含有正在服藥的人以及其他來源的藥物處理過程中排出的排泄物的市政廢水和污水污染了水源，然後在我們的飲用水中被發現。在香港，水源既來自本地流域，也來自進口水源（主要來自廣東省珠江東岸的東江）。處理世界上人口最稠密的城市之一中產生的大量原水是每天的挑戰。儘管努力應用不同處理方法處理原水，但是最近的研究發現，通過水處理工藝去除這些生物活性化合物的數量令人擔憂地低。另外，據報導華南地區的廢水和相應的接收環境中的藥物殘留污染也不斷增加。鑑於去除率低，加上人口稠密地區對藥品的需求不斷增加，可以想像化學品污染了源水。此外，對藥物降解產物的新的關注已引起對飲用水安全性的進一步關注。 毫無疑問，目前在水處理系統和源水中缺乏有關這些生物活性化學品的分佈和命運的基本信息。因此，有必要在採用傳統技術和先進技術的不同水處理廠中對它們進行調查，以跟踪水質的變化。因此，本研究的總體目標是識別和量化許多水處理廠中的藥物殘留，通過質量平衡分析來調查其來源和命運，並根據處理後飲用水中的暴露水平評估潛在的健康風險。

18600320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600320.value: This project aims to examine the role of regularity of daily routines in the association between financial strain and mental health. Financial strain, whether indicated by objective income and education level or perceived subjectively, has been associated with poorer mental health. This includes more depressive symptoms and lower life satisfaction. Psychological factors such as a greater sense of control and having effective management strategies for life events have been found to explain the association between financial strain and mental health. Currently, little is known about the involvement of behavioral mechanisms in the association between financial strain and mental health. Major frameworks of stress adaptation and resilience consistently suggest that everyday life is the fundamental context for psychological resilience in post-traumatic conditions or when facing chronic stress. Empirical and theoretical literature has also suggested that people facing financial difficulty are more likely to demonstrate disrupted and irregular daily routines. This project has four objectives: (1) to assess associations of regularity of daily routines with multiple measures of financial strain and mental health, both concurrently and prospectively; (2) to offer empirical evidence on the role of regularity of daily routines in the association between financial strain and mental health; (3) to test the hypothesis that the inverse associations between financial strain and mental health are stronger when regularity of daily routines is lower; and (4) to test the hypothesis that financial strain predicts reduced regularity of daily routines, which, in turn, relates to poorer mental health. In Study 1, a population-based sample of adults will be recruited and administered a questionnaire on the regularity of their daily routines, psychological distress, and their background information. In Study 2, a separate sample of community-dwelling adults will be invited to participate in a 3-wave prospective study. The participants will be asked to report financial strain, regularity of daily routines, and psychological distress and well-being at baseline and at 3-month and 9-month follow-up. Overall, this proposed project will amass one of the first large-scale collections of empirical evidence on the everyday behavioral processes through which people adapt to financial strain in Hong Kong. Findings on the role of daily routines in adaptation to chronic and acute financial strain will provide new evidence to the current theoretical and empirical literature. This project will also provide one of the first evidence bases for developing cost-effective psychoeducational programs for mental health in populations, locally, regionally, and globally. 此研究旨在探討日常生活的規律性與財務壓力和精神健康的關係。財務壓力（無論是客觀收入和教育水平，還是主觀上的心理壓力）與精神健康息息相關。我們對這一關係中的行為機制卻知之甚少。當今主流的壓力適應和心理抗逆力理論一致表明，日常生活是經歷重大創傷或者面臨長期壓力時恢復精神健康的基本條件。一些實證研究也表明，人們在面臨財務困難時，生活規律更容易被擾亂。此研究有以下四個目標：（1）評估日常生活的規律性與財務壓力和精神健康的關係；（2）為日常生活的規律性在財務壓力和精神健康之間所起的作用提供實證依據；（3）分析日常生活規律性降低能否解釋財務壓力與較差精神健康的關係。研究項目一將對日常生活的規律性，心理困擾和其背景信息進行問卷調查。研究項目二將在社區招募市民，並邀請他們參加三次追踪研究。參與者被要求在基線，3個月，9個月的隨訪中報告他們的財務壓力，日常生活的規律性，心理困擾和幸福感。整體來說，此研究將收集首批有關人們適應香港財務壓力和日常行為調節過程的實證數據，並為心理教育方案奠定基礎。

18600620.value: Dr Chey, Hyoung-kyu Mr Petry, Johannes

18600620.value: To examine the responses of Hong Kong, Singapore and South Korea to the European Union’s initiatives in recent years to regulate financial benchmarks/indexes and promote derivatives market transparency To analyze the impacts of EU’s regulatory sanction mechanisms on the policy preferences and reactions of Asia’s regulators and financial interests To assess the coping strategy mechanisms adopted to mitigate impacts on local market development and the extent to which they can be effective To contribute to the scholarship of political economy on financial power and statecraft through empirical case studies of how Asian capital markets cope with the extra-territorial application of regulations from the EU, a leading authority in global financial regulation

To analyze the impacts of EU’s regulatory sanction mechanisms on the policy preferences and reactions of Asia’s regulators and financial interests
To assess the coping strategy mechanisms adopted to mitigate impacts on local market development and the extent to which they can be effective

18600620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600620.value: This research project explores the impact of two European Union-originated regulatory initiatives of the post-subprime crisis years on East Asia. It focuses on Brussels’ endeavors to rectify the uses of financial index/benchmarks, and to promote transparency in derivatives markets. The two initiatives mark Brussels’ direct and targeted applications of its legal instruments over not just European financial firms operating worldwide, but also third-country (i.e. non-EU) jurisdictions. Specific compliance and “punishment” mechanisms (for example, market access denial, suspension of transactions) were introduced to ensure that third-country jurisdictions would dovetail with the EU’s roadmap. Such extra-territorial applications of EU rules over non-EU jurisdictions, however, challenge the very notion of legal sovereignty in international law and global regulatory affairs, as the “targeted” states in Asia appear to have very little choice but to act in accordance to Brussels’ pressures. The consequences of the ratcheting up and hardening of EU’s regulatory pressures, including the political ramifications, have remained underappreciated by political economists and policy specialists (except Kalyanpur and Newman 2019; Vogt 2019; Brummer 2015). To understand better how these hard techniques have worked in practice, this project adopts a “Market Power Europe” framework to: i) examine the different responses of Hong Kong, Singapore and South Korea toward EU pressure, ii) analyze how the impacts of the EU’s sanction mechanisms for Asian financiers and regulators are mediated between public authorities and private interests in the transnational spheres, and iii) understand how the coping strategies adopted by Asian jurisdictions to mitigate the impact on local market development have been devised and what determines their effectiveness. These goals will be achieved via in-depth empirical studies of the three Asian jurisdictions that have borne the brunt of the two EU policy agendas. We will conduct a structured and paired comparison between South Korea and Singapore regarding the index/benchmark regulation episode, and between Singapore and Hong Kong for the derivatives market transparency initiative. Extensive data will be collected, notably EU policy directives and filings, and regulations and financier submissions from the three Asia markets. Understanding these issues is especially important to the three Asian jurisdictions as they continue to face the difficult tradeoff between maintaining their domestic rule-making autonomy and maintaining their connection with and access to EU market traffic. Expected deliverables from this project will be a monograph and high-impact journal articles that analyze this technically complex but inherently political application of extra-territorial jurisdiction on Asia’s soils. 本研究旨在探索兩個由歐盟發起的金融監管政策議題對后次貸危機時代東亞地區資本市場的影響。研究重點關注歐盟在監管基準金融指標的使用以及推動衍生金融產品市場透明化這兩方面做出的努力。這兩個政策領域標誌著歐盟將其法律管理直接并具針對性地應用到歐洲以外的第三方司法管轄區。通過引入具體的合規與「懲罰」機制，歐盟試圖讓第三方司法轄區的金融監管實踐與歐盟相吻合。然而，歐盟的域外管轄機制對國際法和全球治理領域的法律主權概念造成了衝擊，因為被「針對」的相關亞洲國家在歐盟的壓力下似乎並沒有選擇的餘地。目前，政治經濟學界和政策持分者對於歐盟日漸強硬的監管壓力及所造成的衝撃及影響研究程度尚淺。為了更全面及完整地理解這些監管手段在實踐層面的應用，本研究採用了「歐洲的市場性力量」這一分析框架來達成以下三個研究目標：第一，考察香港、新加坡和韓國三地對於歐盟金融監管壓力的應對；第二，分析亞洲金融監管當局和私人機構如何在跨國金融實務過程中消化歐盟的相關合規及制裁機制造成的影響；第三，理解以上亞洲各地在本地金融市場發展過程中採取的各種應對外界壓力的手段是如何產生的、以及哪些因素決定了這些應對手段的有效性。面對歐洲的金融域外管轄，香港、新加坡和韓國首當其衝。我們將進行有系統及深入的實證考察，收集分析包括歐盟委員會相關法規在內的大量文獻和金融管理數據，運用結構配對比較法進行研究。金融監管的境外治權問題在技術層面十分複雜，但其本質是國際政治沒權力在全球金融領域的延伸。上述三個亞洲司法管轄區當下面對區內管轄自主性和歐盟金融市場准入之間的取捨及張力，更凸顯出本研究的重要性。

18600620.label: Realisation of objectives
18600620.value: Objectives 1-2 Since the last reporting in March 2022, the PI has continued the documentary reviews related to the project’s empirical focus on EU’s extra-territorial regulatory initiatives with the support of the research assistant that helped exploited primary and secondary sources published by the three Asia’s regulatory authorities, the EU’s regulatory bodies and professional financial news sources. In addition to English sources, the PI also had chances to look into the Korean language sources with the support of a part-time research assistant so that the finding derived from English media will be corroborated by the local sources (and have better credibility). On the basis of the several Zoom based interviews carried out before by the PI and Co-Is, the PI has reached out several more market professionals with good knowledge about the regulatory matters and conducted short virtual interviews regarding the impacts of EU’s regulatory initiatives on Asia’s market players’ preferences and their plausible coping strategies— an issue raised in the mid-term report to be addressed in the second reporting period. These have shed light on the important questions about what might motivate the choices of a particular coping strategy over the other and what might be the intervening factors at work in a particular regulatory episode (whether they might be jurisdiction-specific, or structural to the market landscape). Nonetheless, further investigation into these issues were seriously interrupted by the prolonged social distancing and travel restrictions in place during the Covid pandemic that made face-to-face research interviews in/outside Hong Kong not quite possible for much of the project’s period (early 2021 until late 2022). Although virtual interviews helped offset such challenges, the Zoom-based interviews were often one-off (hard to develop good rapports with the interviewees in virtual settings) and proved difficult to go into additional issues and make requests for follow-up interviews. As well, it also appeared to be quite a challenge to “probe” for additional leads (e.g., solicit clues for further suggestions for other interviews) from the interviewees. In fact, the pandemic situation for much of the first half of 2022 (until international travel resumed in the 3rd quarter of 2022) has made contacts with interviewees familiar with the Hong Kong’s context challenging as some had already moved out from the city, or left the industry as a result of the pandemic To compensate for such missed opportunities, the PI and Co-Is have tried re-engaging some of the previous interviewees in Summer 2022 and have arranged fieldwork visits to South Korea and Singapore in late 2022/early 2023 making use of the allotted fundings for travel. With some success, the PI had identified several more interviewing opportunities in Seoul and Singapore by way of visiting some of the earlier connections with financial regulators and market professionals that have provided good enough insights about the outstanding issues related to the project’s objectives (1 and 2 in particular), including the devising of coping mechanisms to EU’s regulatory initiatives and the interplays between Asia’s regulatory authorities, their domestic financiers and EU-originated financiers operating in the Asia’s markets. Objectives 3-4 To supplement the findings related to the Asia’s responses and impacts of EU’s initiatives, the PI has also taken chances to visit London and Paris in November 2022 with the attempts to interview informants that might be knowledgeable about the sending end dynamics underlying the two cases the project concerned— an issue was not quite covered and well-addressed in the first reporting period. During the research trip, the PI has met market professionals with knowledge and familiarity bout the EU-Asia market interplays in London, and obtained good insights about the roles of European financial institutions operating in the Asia’s capital markets in mediating the EU’s pressure to implement its regulatory initiatives, and their specific concerns in managing the different multiple regulator’s pressures in the continent (i.e., the EU, and their domicile EU country) and those in Asia (where these firms operated and made profits from the region’s capital market). Efforts to interview EU’s regulators, however, was not quite successful and the PI/Co-Is have resorted to inferential analyses of their preferences and considerations through triangulating multiple pieces of evidences (for example, reports of the regulatory development, public speeches made by officials or quoted by other sources). These approach, albeit far from prefect, has helped get some good sense of how the EU regulatory authorities has come to understand and perceive the efficacy of their regulatory reach beyond Europe and the expected reactions from the Asia’s regulatory authorities and market players that would be affected by the Brussel’s initiatives. It also shed light on how the EU officials might have anticipated the coping responses from Asia’s regulators and market participants, and as such considered further responses and strategies so that the EU’s intended regulatory effects would be attained with little deviations. Since leaving the University in February 2023, the PI has continued to work on the project whenever possible, and managed to update the findings with some online conservations with former financial professionals and regulators with experience on related regulatory issued the project covered. These new findings (and the earlier ones) are being analyzed by the PI in preparing for the two manuscripts the project intends to deliver. Overall, the project’s findings from the regulatory receiving and sending ends have provided important basis for the project to attain its last and fourth objective that seeks to advance the international political economy (IPE) scholarship about financial power and statecraft. While the project’s findings have affirmed the validity and relevance of the overarching framework of “Market Power Europe” that focused on the extra-territorial flexing of EU’s regulatory power, the important findings in the receiving ends at the Asia’s political capitals (where the regulators are located) and the financial market places shall have supplemented and enriched the original framework by bringing the receivers of the regulatory exercises back into the picture. As well, the interplays between the two ends across continents, and the roles of transnational yet localized market players were largely the missing pieces of the puzzles in analyses adopting the “Market Power Europe” prism. Perhaps more intriguingly, the project has also found cases in which the assumptions of the original framework were defied (or shall be reconsidered at least). These included, for example, instances where the internal regulatory cohesion within the EU was compromised by individual member states, making possible efforts of Asia’s regulators and market players to exploit the internal disagreement and to water down or deflect Brussel’s pressure. Thus, the project’s empirical findings, despite its confined scope to two regulatory episodes over the 2010s, have illustrated the limits and plausible scope of extension and refinement for the “Market Power Europe” framework and the conceptualization of financial power (the sending and reacting parties’ interplays) and statecraft (the praxis of regulatory authorities and instruments) in general.

18600620.label: Major findings and research outcome
18600620.value: The project has unveiled several important findings about the flexing of regulatory power of the EU authorities in the two regulatory episodes over the three East Asia jurisdictions. Specifically, the project has found clear receiving end dynamics from Hong Kong, South Korea and Singapore in coping with the Brussel’s regulatory pressures. There are, however, interesting differences of specific strategies employed by the Asia’s authorities and political interplays involved across the two cases. In some instances, their reactions are more subtle, in others they sought to deflect the EU’s pressures through allying with market players and reaching out to third-party supports (e.g., EU-originated financial institutions for amplifying their views, or exploiting the dis-harmony between the EU, the US, and global regulatory standard setting bodies). Such variations of responses are supposedly related to the intervening factors at work, including for example the perceived efficacy of EU’s sanction mechanisms and the leverage of extra-regional market players. For the project’s outcomes, two journal articles’ manuscripts are under preparation. The first manuscript would touch on the empirical trends across the two regulatory episodes. It would summarize the receiving end responses of the EU’s initiatives to regulate derivate markets, to control third-country banking institutions, and to govern financial benchmarks and indexes with the purposes of imposing Brussel’s harmonized standards in the regulatory landscapes concerned such that there would be little regulatory loopholes to be exploited by EU or third-country financial institutions. The focus on receiving end reactions to the EU’s regulatory flexing would provide important insights on the different policy stances adopted by the Asian regulatory authorities, the market players (both local and international FIs), and the various coping strategies of the Asia’s regulators and financiers in face of a much stronger regulatory counterparty. This output will be related to the project objective 1, 2 and 3. The second manuscript in preparation would touch and shed light on the conceptual basis of the project— the “Market Power Europe” framework. The paper shall interrogate and reflect on the framework’s relevance (and limits) through the prism of the project’s empirical findings. In addition to suggesting how the original theoretical logic might have captured the regulatory development the project examined, the paper would also highlight plausible areas in which the notion of EU’s financial regulatory power shall be refined, and how the practices of regulatory externalization could be further integrated with the financial statecraft scholarships in the IPE studies.

18600620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18600620.value: Based on the project’s findings, there are two possible avenues of future research. First and foremost, along the “Market Power Europe” framework and its applications in the two regulatory episodes the project has looked into, future research could investigate how the EU authorities have exercised its regulatory power beyond in other new/emerging issue areas (including, for example, crypto-currencies). This would not just allow for better application (and extension) of the analytical framework, it would also make possible cross-cases’ comparison that help illustrate how other intervening factors might/could impact on the flexing of the EU’s regulatory power. Second, future research could delve further into the interplays between the regulatory sending and receiving ends in more refined terms, especially given international travel/fieldwork research has now become possible in the post-pandemic context. Whereas the present project has examined the receiving-end dynamics— specifically how the Asia’s regulators and financiers have responded to the EU’s initiatives— the present framework and findings have mostly captured the development unfolding in series, i.e., reactions by receiving-end parties following actions originating from the sending end. Much politics amongst regulators and financiers, shall be more dynamic and interactive. A more refined framework could accommodate these natures of regulatory politics at the transnational level, and provide more calibrated accounts of the development.

18600620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18600620.value: Is it a must for smaller powers in the global economy to bow to the pressures of the powerful states? While we always assume a yes, the reality is more nuanced and shaped by a host of political economic considerations. Often time smaller powers have found rooms to delay, deflect and push back the pressure from the stronger parties. With the focuses on the European Union’s initiatives in the 2010s to regulate the financial markets— including attempts to bring market order in the fast-growing but opaque derivatives markets and to regulate the uses of financial indexes/benchmarks, the project examines how Hong Kong, Singapore and South Korea, the three Asia’s markets with extensive linkages with and dependence for Europe, have reacted to the strong regulatory pressures from Brussels. Through in-depth reviews of documentary sources and interviews with financial regulators and market professionals, the project has demonstrated how the supposedly small Asia powers could cushion and in some cases water down the pressures from the Brussels by political maneuverings that amplified the leverage of the Asia’s states to tame the regulatory goliath in Europe. Powerplay in global financial regulation is far from static and the small can turn the table around sometimes.

18601120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18601120.value: This project examines how perceptions of income inequality and the sense of fairness affect people’s participation in democratic movements. The case of Hong Kong provides an interesting case for such an investigation: it has a notoriously high level of income inequality by international standards and has also seen a surge in political participation in recent years. It is hypothesized that, among other factors, individuals might be motivated to participate in social movements because of their concerns of inequality based on their perception of fairness and justice. As compared to existing studies, this project extends the discussion by exploring the role of inequality in a democratic movement. Curiously, despite Hong Kong’s inequality remaining at a high level with no signs of improvement, public discussion about inequality has actually faded significantly. Of course, this has to do with the attention on the political turbulence and on-going democratic movement, but this is precisely the question: Has inequality become irrelevant due to the more pressing concerns of democracy and freedom; or has it been transformed into those concerns or incorporated under the fight for democracy? Although inequality is often hypothesized as a crucial factor for mobilization and democratization, the precise relationship between them is seldom explored. This line of inquiry carries theoretical and practical significance as it speaks to the link between economic inequality and political inequality (lack of democracy). The underlying causal mechanism is how a strong sense of fairness and one’s perception of inequality as unacceptable would prompt him/her into actions. While inequality and fairness might both have an independent effect on participation, their interaction effect is the main focus. Those who find inequality to be unacceptable and have a strong sense of fairness should be more likely to participate; on the contrary, non-participation can be explained by either the acceptance of inequality or the weak norm of fairness. To assess this, this project utilizes a survey research with experimental components designed to assess the correlational and causal relationship between inequality and participation. In addition to enriching the literature on political participation and democratization, the results will further our understanding of the on-going political development in Hong Kong, in particular, if inequality has an explicit or implicit role in the democratic movement. This goes beyond the local literature focusing primarily on identity and political factors. It can also enlighten policymakers about the hidden costs of inequality. 該項目旨在研究人們對收入不平等以及公平性的感知會對民主運動參與度產生怎樣的影響。香港爲此類研究提供了一個有趣的案例：根據國際標準，香港的收入不平等現象極其嚴重；與此同時，政治參與度也在近年呈現激增的態勢。因此該研究假設，除其他的因素外，基於對公平和正義的看法而產生的對不平等現象的關注，可能會促使人們參與到社會運動中。 與現有研究相比，該項目通過探討不平等這一因素在民主運動中發揮的作用來延伸討論。令人感到奇怪的是，儘管香港社會中的不平等程度依然很高，且沒有任何改善的跡象，然而公衆對於該現象的討論熱情卻在與日遞減。當然，這與時局動亂以及當下進行中的民主運動息息相關，但這恰恰是問題所在：由於對民主和自由的愈發關注，不平等變得無關緊要了嗎？還是說，它已轉變成同類關注點或已被納入當前爭取民主的鬥爭中？雖然不平等常常被認爲是推進社會動員和民主化過程的關鍵因素之一，但兩者之間的具體關係卻很少為之探索。對此現象的研究具理論與實踐意義，正是因爲它指出了經濟不平等與政治不平等（缺乏的民主）之間的微妙聯係。 一個潛在的因果關係是，強烈的公平感和個人對於不平等現象的不接受程度往往會促使人們采取相應的行動。儘管不平等和公平各自會對政治參與產生獨立的影響，兩者閒的相互作用是該研究的主要關注點。拒絕接受不平等，并且具有強烈公平意識的人更有可能參與到政治活動中，而不參與的行爲則可以通過其對不平等現象的接受或擁有較弱的公平意識這一方面來解釋。 爲了對此進行評估，該項目將通過使用具有實驗性的調查研究法來評判不平等與政治參與之間的相關性以及因果關係。除了對有關政治參與以及民主化文獻的擴充，該研究結果還將進一步加深我們對當前香港正在進行的政治運動的理解，特別是當不平等在民主運動中發揮了一定的作用時。這不僅僅超越了地方文獻對於身份認同和政治因素的重視，并且可以對政策制定者有關不平等所帶來的隱性成本方面起到一定啓示的作用。

18601120.label: Realisation of objectives
18601120.value: All five objectives have been achieved successfully. The methodology and process of achieving them were summarized as follows: Study design and population: An online self-administered survey with a standardized questionnaire was conducted in November and December 2021. Participants were eligible if they were young adults in tertiary education in Hong Kong. Recruited participants were randomly assigned to either an experimental/treatment or active control group on 1:1 ratio where they received different information cues. A sample of 647 participants were recruited. Excluding those who provided incomplete and/or insincere answers, a total of 454 valid responses were given analytical consideration. All participants were given informed consent to participate. An information cue has been designed to study how respodents' attitude might change in relation to a hypothetical change in Gini. Three articles have been written directly resulting from the research conducted in this project. Although Article 3 is the study directly testing the arguments involved, the other two articles also examine the same research questions and make use of the data collected. They have been attached to this report: Article 1 (Published 2022; co-authored with Stan H. Wong): Income Inequality and Political Participation: A District-Level Analysis of Hong Kong Elections. Social Indicators Research Article 2 (Accepted; co-authored with Ying-ho Kwong): COVID-19 Direct Relief Payments and Political and Economic Attitudes among Tertiary Students: A Quasi-experimental Study. PS: Political Science and Politics. Article 3 (Under review; co-authored with Kin-man Wan): Income Inequality, Sense of Fairness, and Democratic Support: Experimental Evidence. Objective 1: To investigate if and how the ideas of distributive justice and fairness would trigger a reaction to income inequality by participation in democratic movement. This objective was fulfilled through two strategies – group-wise simple means comparison and a regression analysis. Our final results indicated that respondents with a low sense of fairness who learned about an increase in inequality expressed increased support for democracy. This argument was first suggested by the results of the preliminary means comparison where a significant difference in democratic support was identified between the treatment and control groups who reported a low level of perceived injustice (MControl = 4.61, MTreatment 5.17; p < 0.05). Regression analysis results further identified sense of fairness as a conditional factor, particularly through significant interaction effects between perceived injustice and rising inequality on democratic support (Article 1). This result is further supported by regression analysis of Hong Kong elections, and it is found that inequality does indeed suppress participation in elections (Article 3). A detailed discussion of the related results can be found in Articles 1 and 3. Objective 2: To identify the correlational and causal relationship between the perceived severity of inequality and political participation. This objective, on the one hand, was realized through the confirmed association between inequality and support for political equality and for democracy. It is then argued that rising inequality leads to a higher level of support for democracy and a growing desire for civil rights and free elections. Statistical details were as follows: In terms of democratic support, rising inequality (i.e., the treatment) were included in all three regression models where treatment, perceived injustice and the interaction term were added on, respectively. Treatment was consistently confirmed as being a significant contributor of democratic support. As for the other political polity (represented by civil rights and elections), our results came to a similar conclusion that treatment significantly associated with respondents’ understandings of civil rights and free elections as essential elements of democracy, when the interaction term was included alongside the main terms (Article 3). Similarly, this objective was also supported by another project, the results of which indicated that inequality influenced political participation in Hong Kong at both district- and individual-level (Article 1). A detailed discussion of the related results can be found in Articles 1 and 3. Objective 3: To investigate the causal pathways through which perception of income inequality and fairness jointly affect political participation and non-participation. This objective was achieved through two analyses. First, based on the survey results, it is found that the disbursement of welfare resources (COVID payment in our case) would trigger a fairness reaction among non-recipients, and that they would allocate greater importance to meritocratic factors in life success. This fairness concern provides a potential causal pathway through which inequality can affect participation outcomes. If one is faced with an unfair distribution, it will affect his/her worldview about the society, which in turn would determine how they react to this condition (Article 2). Second, income inequality also shapes one’s view of democracy. In particular, those who have a weak sense of fairness would respond to rising inequality by seeing election (as opposed to redistribution) as essential to democracy. This points to another potential pathway from income inequality to participation: by changing an individual’s political views, especially whether they will associate democracy with a fairer income distribution (Article 3). A detailed discussion of the related results can be found in Articles 2 and 3. Objective 4: To examine the wider relationship between economic inequality and the demand for political equality through participation in democratic movements. This objective was fulfilled when we took a further step in exploring the behind mechanism of the relationship between inequality and democratic support. As said, we measured “essential characteristics of democracy” and we included them in our final regression analysis. What is of note here is that, contrary to conventional ideas, our results indicated that civil rights and elections were significant indicators of a democratic system or for pursuing democracy, instead of redistribution and gender equality. Based on this finding, it is suggested that individuals’ desire for income equality can be transformed into a desire for political equality, and they might view economic equality as a way to assess political polity. A detailed discussion of the related results can be found in Article 3. Objective 5: To understand if income inequality has an explicit or implicit role in recent surge in political activism in Hong Kong at the individual-level. This objective was realized through both the analytical results and research design. When looking into the data analysis, we figured out that there was a causal relationship between rising inequality and political concerns regarding free elections and civil rights. This suggested an explicit role of economic inequality in one’s political-making, for example, whether or not individuals would take action to engage with concurrent or ongoing political movements (Article 2). This objective, on the other hand, was also achieved by finding economic concerns to play a significant role in individuals’ voting behavior (Article 1). Last but not least, survey data of the current study was collected in November and December 2021, which was after the social movement in 2019, so it is assumed that the respondents experienced or at least witnessed the recent surge of political activism in Hong Kong which would affect their views of democracy and democratic movements. As such, our results provided solid evidence to explain the potential relationship between income inequality and the surge of political activism in Hong Kong. A detailed discussion of the related results can be found in Articles 1 and 3.

18601120.label: Major findings and research outcome
18601120.value: Finding 1: Increased income inequality did transform into increased support for democracy under a non-democratic regime. Adopting the case of Hong Kong, our survey results has consistently identified rising inequality was positively associated with democratic support. Finding 2: Notwithstanding the above, there is also a negative relationship between economic inequality and voting behavior in Hong Kong. This is explained by the fact that inequality suppresses formal political participation (or makes it less attractive to do so) whereas it generates grievances for people to take part in more unconventional forms of participation Finding 3: Individuals with a stronger sense of justice demonstrated a higher level of democratic support; it is also found that respondents who reported a high sense of injustice/fairness had a higher level of democratic support, compared to those who had a low sense of injustice Finding 4: The effects of income equality on democratic support were conditioned on individuals’ perceived fairness and justice. Individuals with a weaker sense of fairness and injustice increased their level of democratic support in response to rising inequality; such a relationship was however not pronounced among those with a higher sense of injustice. Finding 5: Income inequality affected individuals’ worldview (views of success in life) and understandings of essential characteristics of a democratic system (election or redistribution). Both of these could be the underlying mechanism of the relationship between inequality and participation.

18601120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18601120.value: The present research engages with existing literature on inequality and political participation, especially through providing empirical evidence from a non-democratic society. What is more, it draws attention on possible socio-psychological factors (e.g., sense of fairness) in conditioning one’s level of support for democracy and potential political behavior as a reaction to inequality. And, it further explores the relationships among inequality, essential elements of democracy, and distributive justice to unfold the mechanism behind. Against this backdrop, this research project together with other relevant publications provides important insights on the dynamics between economic concerns especially those resulting from inequality and political decision-making in a certain social and cultural context. Moving forward, given the changing forms of political activism, promising research may be proposed to look into different ways that people engage with politics, how they normally participate and even how they create novel ways to get themselves engaged with politics under non-democracies, and how these are in turn influenced by economic inequality. Finally, since the present project touches upon political psychology, potential works in the future may also involve how objective factors such as economic concerns would interact with psychological elements, thereby affecting individuals’ political behavior, and even mobilization at a larger scale.

18601120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18601120.value: This project focuses on the relationship between income inequality and political participation, a question that has been at the heart of many political science models and debates, albeit without a clear-cut answer. This project tackles the question by implementing a survey experiment, aimed at examining how individuals would react to a changing inequality condition by their intention to participate in political activities, and if so, the pathway through which the effect takes place. Upon the successful conclusion of the research, it is found that inequality does impact participation, but it critically depends on one’s sense of fairness. Inequality only triggers a significant reaction among those with a weaker sense of fairness, likely because those with a strong sense have already accounted for the effect of inequality. This result is also supplemented by a further analysis on aggregate electoral patterns in Hong Kong, as well as an examination on how welfare payments shape one’s view on factors to success in life (using the same surveys as the main study). All of these analyses are novel in the inequality-participation literature, and introduce new perspectives into the field with new theoretical frameworks and methods.

18601420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18601420.value: ‘兩文三語’即鼓勵香港市民會以中文和英文書寫，並使用廣東話，英語和普通話三語進行口語交流的政策在影響著香港中小學課程的設計和實施。自1997年香港回歸以來，該政策對香港的語言使用產生了影響 (Wang＆Kirkpatrick, 2013)。大多數香港人已經意識到提升自己的第二語言和第三語言的水平並滿足日常交際和工作的迫切需要。但是，在我們的日常生活中通常可以觀察到，如果一位來自香港的粵語為母語的英語學習者（英語為第二語言），他/她 ‘three’ /θri:/ 這個單詞的發音可能會變成為 /fri:/。如果一位來自廣東省的粵語為母語的英語學習者（普通話為第二語言，英語為第三語言），‘three’ /θri:/ 這個單詞的發音可能會變為 /sri:/。人們似乎會注意到，當英語學習者說英文時，發音常常被當作最重要的考察因素之一。非母語發音幾乎可以立即被識別出，並且這種發音可能會產生一些不良後果 (Flege, 1995)。聽眾常常把不標準的非母語發音貼上“慢”，“需要幫助”以及可能會引起無效溝通的標籤。 關於華語環境下多語種的第三語言語音發展，以下兩個重要的問題應當被研究： 1）從第一語言到第二語言以及第三語言的語音特徵的跨語言轉換模式是什麼？ 2）第二語言在語音特徵向第三語言的轉移的程度跟語言水平的關系？ 該項目旨在通過以下方式回答上述兩個基本問題：a) 找到粵語學習者在英語和普通話的主要發音錯誤； b) 對母語為廣東話的學習者的第一語言，廣東話，在英語和普通話的習得的影響進行聲學研究； c) 確定多語言學習者習得第二語言以及第三語言語音特徵，特別關注第一語言或第二語言在第三語言學習過程中的影響。 該項目在兩方面創新：(a) 將設計更全面評估英語和普通話發音的任務。 上述任務將會被用於判定學習者學習英語以及普通話發音的困難；以及 (b) 將精心設計自我反思指引來幫助學習者對第二語言和第三語言語音學習過程和經驗進行自我反思。該項目將確定對語言學習者在第二語言以及第三語言語音習得影響最大的因素，從而為在多語言習得和多語言教育中的理論和實踐做出貢獻。該項目將設計考察語言學習者第二語言和第三語言發音的任務。研究結果可以用來開發語音教師培訓資源，以促進第二語言和第三語言語音教學，將英語和普通話教師聯繫在一起，來探索和解決母語為粵語的學習者的發音問題。

18601420.label: Realisation of objectives
18601420.value: Objective 1 has been fully achieved. A set of comprehensive evaluations tasks has been constructed for identifying pronunciation features of Cantonese learners of English and Mandarin. A series of speech tasks were designed for assessing phonological and phonetic features of three languages. The Cantonese tasks included a reading of a list of monosyllabic words and a reading of a passage. In the list of monosyllabic words, all Cantonese vowels were involved in two types of words, one meaningful word and one pseudo word with the test vowel preceded by a glottal fricative /h/. The passage was the Cantonese version of ‘The North Wind and the Sun’, adapted to include all Cantonese consonants, vowels, and tones. The English tasks included the read-aloud of a list of meaningful words containing all English vowels and consonants, a list of meaningful and pseudo words (with /h/ as the initial consonant) containing all English vowels, and a passage ‘The Boy Who Cried Wolf’ containing all English vowels and consonants. A controlled free speech task was also included, to elicit authentic and spontaneous speech by providing the topic ‘an unforgettable trip’ and a series of guided questions. The Mandarin tasks included the read-aloud of a list of monosyllabic and multisyllabic meaningful words, a list of monosyllabic meaningful and pseudo words, a passage, and a controlled free speech task. In the first reading task, the test monosyllabic words include all Mandarin vowels, consonants, and tones; the test multisyllabic words contain the 20 permutations of tones, the tone sandhi of 一 ‘yi’, 不 ‘bu’, and Tone 3 (dipping tone), and r-colouring. In the second reading task, all Mandarin vowels are included in one meaningful word and one pseudo word with the test vowel preceded by a glottal fricative /h/. The passage was the Mandarin version of ‘The North Wind and the Sun’, which includes all Mandarin vowels, consonants, and tones. In the controlled free speech task, the topic and guided questions are the same as those for eliciting English speech data. The evaluation tasks were used for collecting speech data in three phases, to assess the participants’ pronunciation features longitudinally. The speech data were analyzed to create a diagnostic profile of Cantonese learners' pronunciation errors in English and Mandarin. This profile aids multilingual education in the Greater Bay area and highlights negative transfer between the languages, linking cross-linguistic transfer to changes in language proficiency. Objective 2 has been fully achieved. The most frequently occurring pronunciation errors in a language identified by the phonological analysis were selected, along with the relevant sounds in the other two languages, to be the targets for the acoustic analysis across the three phases. Six categories of sounds were acoustically analyzed to investigate the possible cross-linguistic influences among Cantonese, English, and Mandarin. The first category concerned vowel tensing, since the errors of /ɪ/ pronounced as /i/ and /ʊ/ pronounced as /u/ were frequently found in the English speech for the participants. Therefore, the F1 and F2 values of /i/ and /u/ in the three languages and /ɪ/ and /ʊ/ in English were analyzed acoustically using Praat and compared in the F1/F2 plane. The second category is about vowel raising, because /æ/ was frequently pronounced as /e/ in English. /e/ in both English and Cantonese and /æ/ in English were analyzed acoustically for F1 and F2 values. The third category concerned vowel centralization, specifically, Mandarin /ɣ/ pronounced as the centralized vowels /ə/, /ɜː/, or /œ/. F1 and F2 values of /œ/ in Cantonese, /ə/ or /ɜː/ in English, and /ɣ/ in Mandarin were measured and compared in the F1/F2 plane. The fourth category concerned the lack of r-coloring for /ɚ/. The rate of change in F3 for /ɚ/ in Mandarin and /ər/ or /ɜːr/ in English were computed and compared. The fifth category considered the aspiration of /k/ in English and unaspiration and voicing of /ph/ in Mandarin. The last category is about the lack of neutral tone in Mandarin. The change in fundamental frequency (F0), the size of phrasal pitch span, and duration ratio for specific phrases in the three languages. There were two types of phrases in Mandarin, the first type contained a function word carrying the neutral tone preceded by content words (e.g., 拼命地 ‘desperately’ /pʰɪn55 mɪŋ51 tɤ0/), and the second type involved a content word with the second syllable carrying the neutral tone (e.g., 太陽 ‘the sun’ /tʰaɪ51 jɑŋ0/). The acoustic data were analyzed across languages and phases to explore dynamic cross-linguistic transfer. Additionally, a comparison of acoustic differences between participants and native speakers was conducted to further understand these variations. Objective 3 has been fully achieved. Immediately after the speech tasks, a series of verbal protocols adapted from Wrembel’s (2015) think-aloud protocols (TAPs) were conducted to elicit meta-phonological awareness from the participants. The verbal protocols include analytic listening, retrospective protocol and introspective protocol. During the analytic listening, the participants listened to the audio recordings of their L2 and L3 speech, compared their own pronunciation with that of native speakers, and noted down the pronunciation errors. This process allowed participants to identify discrepancies between their pronunciation and that of native speakers, fostering self-awareness. For the retrospective protocol, the participants provided commentaries on their L2 and L3 phonetic performances following the guided questions, prompting them to conduct self-analysis of pronunciation using meta-languages. For the introspective protocol, the participants performed self-reflection on their own L2 and L3 acquisition experiences , shedding light on cross-linguistic influences and the array of learning strategies employed. Their verbal performances of the protocols were audio recorded, transcribed, and coded. The retrospective protocol data were analyzed in terms of instances of successful and unsuccessful L2 and L3 self-repair and levels of complexity of reported phonological awareness. The introspective protocols were analyzed from two aspects, cross-linguistic influence and learning strategies. The latter aspect was further categorized into memory, cognitive, compensatory, metacognitive, effective, and social (Oxford, 1990). L2 listeners’ perceived comprehensibility and attitudes towards speech produced by L3 English learners from China were also collected and analysed. After a year of English and Mandarin learning, the participants showed notable improvement in high level awareness of meta-phonology, as they could use metalanguage to describe or explain features in their L2/L3 pronunciation. Both HK and GD groups reported progressive and regressive transfers in pronunciation among the three languages. HK participants used both L1 Cantonese and L2 English to facilitate the learning of L3 Mandarin, while most GD participants predominantly used their L1 Cantonese for facilitating the learning of L2 Mandarin. Additionally, both groups reported regressive transfer from L2/L3 Mandarin to L1 Cantonese resulting from the increasing use of Mandarin. The findings highlighted the complex and bidirectional nature of language interface for multilingual speakers, and provided more support and explanations for the language interaction patterns.

18601420.label: Major findings and research outcome
18601420.value: The findings highlight key pronunciation issues for Cantonese learners in English and Mandarin and how these errors change over time. For both Hong Kong (HK) and Guangdong (GD) speakers, common English pronunciation errors include substituting /æ/ with /e/ and /ɪ/ with /i/. Among HK speakers, the error of substituting /æ/ with /e/ decreased, while GD speakers increased in substituting /ɪ/ with /i/. Common consonant errors include substituting /ð/ with /d/ and /z/ with /s/, with the latter error decreasing among GD speakers. In Mandarin, common errors include issues with ‘erhua’ and the substitution of /ʂ/ with /ɕ/ among HK speakers. Tone errors are prevalent, especially with incomplete Tone 3, which is more common in GD speakers but has decreased over time. HK speakers frequently mispronounce Tone 3 as Tones 1, 2, or 4, and both groups often use lexical tones instead of the neutral tone in di- and multi-syllabic words, with a higher error rate in GD speakers. The acoustic analysis identified four potential cross-linguistic influence (CLI) patterns: L1→L3, L2→L3, L1+L2→L3, and L3→L2. CLI from L1 Cantonese to L2/L3 English was observed in the pronunciation of the English vowel [u], and a combined CLI from L1 Cantonese and L2/L3 English to L2/L3 Mandarin [u] was noted for both groups. Regressive CLI from L3 English to L2 Mandarin was detected for Mandarin [ɤ] in GD speakers. Among HK speakers with advanced English, CLI was observed from L2 English to L3 Mandarin. GD speakers exhibited a CLI from L2 Mandarin to L3 English in increased pitch span size, while HK speakers with advanced Mandarin showed a regressive CLI from L3 Mandarin to L2 English, resulting in increased pitch span size. Finally, meta-phonological awareness protocols revealed interaction patterns among the three languages. In Phase Three, both HK and GD participants demonstrated increased meta-phonological awareness compared to Phase One. Both groups reported experiencing progressive and regressive transfers in pronunciation across Cantonese, English, and Mandarin. HK participants utilized different strategies from both L1 Cantonese and L2 English when learning L3 Mandarin, while GD participants primarily relied on L1 Cantonese when learning Mandarin as their L2. Both groups noted that their L1 Cantonese was influenced by regressive CLI from Mandarin as its usage increased, regardless of whether Mandarin was their L2 or L3.

18601420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18601420.value: The project can be further developed from three aspects – L3 production training, L3 perception, and L3 phonology in other language contexts. Based on the findings in the current project, targeted training programs can be developed to improve pronunciation accuracy for the two groups of language learners. The effectiveness of such training program will be evaluated. It will be promoted through knowledge transfer activities if it is proven effective. Despite the examination of L3 production in this project, an investigation of L3 perception can be conducted in the future. Cantonese L1 speakers in Hong Kong and Guangdong and monolingual speakers of Cantonese, English, and Mandarin may be invited to perform a series of perception tasks using the production data in the current project, such as identification, discrimination, and dictation of target sounds, and ratings of comprehensibility and intelligibility of speech data. The perception data can be compared with production data in this project. Moreover, the examination of L3 phonology can be expanded to other linguistic contexts in Hong Kong, especially for the ethnic minority groups, who have languages such as Filipino, Hindi, Urdu as their L1, English as the L2, and Cantonese as the L3.

18601420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18601420.value: In the trilingual education system in Hong Kong, most learners speak Cantonese as their L1, English as their L2, and Mandarin as their L3. The acquisition of these languages is complex and dynamic, with significant cross-linguistic influences. A trilingual speaker’s pronunciation in one language can be positively or negatively impacted by their proficiency in the others. This project aimed to explore these cross-linguistic influences for Cantonese L1 speakers by a) identifying major pronunciation features in English and Mandarin through evaluation tasks; b) examining how Cantonese affects the acquisition of English and Mandarin, and investigating possible phonological transfers from L2 to L3 using acoustic analysis; and c) understanding how multilingual learners acquire L2 and L3 pronunciation, particularly how their L1 or L2 interacts with L3 during the learning process, through meta-phonological awareness protocols. The significance of this project is threefold. First, it provides empirical evidence to enhance language acquisition theories for L2 and L3. Second, it helps establish diagnostic profiles for pronunciation in L1, L2, and L3, supporting more effective lesson planning and teaching strategies. Lastly, the project's impact is amplified through visibility in open-access platforms, international conferences, and prestigious journals, contributing to the global discourse on language education.

18602520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18602520.value: Reading comprehension is a critical ability for children, starting in early primary school. According to the Componential Model of Reading (CMR), cognitive (e.g., word reading and language comprehension skills), ecological (e.g., socioeconomic status and home literacy environment) and psychological (e.g., general psychological status and reading-related motivation and self-efficacy) factors are important for developing reading comprehension skills. However, most previous studies mainly focused on the role of cognitive factors in reading comprehension, while factors in the three domains were rarely considered simultaneously. In addition, the original CMR paid little attention to the dynamic relations among these factors and how the factors jointly impact reading comprehension. This project, thus, aims to investigate the direct and indirect effects of each of the three components on reading comprehension and the bidirectional relations between the components and reading comprehension, with a three-year longitudinal design. A total of 250 Hong Kong primary school children and their parents will be recruited. All the children will be in the first grade at the beginning of the project and followed until grade three. They will be tested once per grade. In the cognitive domain, Chinese character reading, word reading fluency, listening comprehension and vocabulary knowledge will be measured. In the ecological domain, information about the socioeconomic status of the family (e.g., parents’ educational levels and occupations) and home literacy environment (e.g., number of children’s books, and the frequencies of parent-child reading activities) will be collected. In the psychological domain, both general and reading-related psychological status (e.g., reading motivation and reading self-efficacy) will be measured. Children’s non-verbal intelligence and school environment will be considered as controls. We hypothesize that 1) the contributions of the ecological and psychological components will decrease over time, while the contribution of the cognitive component will be large and remain stable throughout the three years. 2) the ecological and psychological components will have indirect effects on reading comprehension mediated through the cognitive component; these indirect effects will vary as children get older, and 3) the relations between the three components and reading comprehension will be reciprocal across all three testing points. Theoretically, this proposed project will help us understand the dynamic relations among various factors and reading comprehension in young graders and enrich the CMR model. Practically, the findings of this project can inform a wide group of stakeholders (e.g., teachers, parents and policy makers) for delivering quality literacy education. 從小學初期開始，閱讀理解便成為兒童需要具備的一項重要能力。依照閱讀成分模型（Componential Model of Reading，CMR），認知（如字詞閱讀和聽力理解）、生態（如社會經濟地位和家庭語文環境）以及心理（如一般心理狀態和閱讀動機和自我效能感）等因素對於閱讀理解能力的發展均具有重要作用。然而，大部分前人研究主要集中在認知因素對閱讀理解的作用上，而同時對三類因素加以考量的研究相對較少。另外，最初的CMR模型對三類因素的動態關係以及它們對閱讀理解作用的動態變化關注較少。因此，本研究旨在利用為期三年的縱向研究來探討三類因素對閱讀理解的直接與間接作用以及它們與閱讀理解之間的雙向關係。合共250名香港小學兒童及其家長將會被邀請參加本次研究。所有受試兒童將會從一年級被追蹤到三年級，每一年級測試一次。認知範疇的測驗包括漢字閱讀、閱讀流暢性、聽力理解以及詞彙量。生態範疇的測驗包括家庭社會經濟地位（如家長教育水平以及職業）和家庭語文環境（如兒童圖書數量和親子閱讀活動頻率）。心理範疇的測驗包括一般心理狀態和閱讀相關心理狀態（如閱讀動機和閱讀自我效能感）。兒童的非言語能力和學校環境將作為控制變量加以考量。我們假設：1）生態和心理因素的貢獻將隨時間而下降，而認知因素的貢獻將在三年內維持穩定重要水平；2）生態和心理因素將通過認知因素的中介效用對閱讀理解產生間接作用，而這種間接作用會隨著兒童年齡的變化而變化；3）三類因素與閱讀理解之間存在互惠關係。理論上，本研究可以增進我們對閱讀理解與各相關因素動態關係的理解並完善CMR模型。在實踐上，本研究可以為各持份者（如教師、家長和政策制定者）提供支持以確保高質量語文教育的實施。

18603120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18603120.value: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common developmental disorder in childhood, with a 5%-6% worldwide prevalence. Children with ADHD often demonstrate impaired executive function, which is closely related to the development of the commonly observed behavioral problems such as inattention, impaired inhibition, and hyperactivity. Although a number of methods have been proposed to treat ADHD, physical activity is regarded as one of the most effective ways to manage ADHD without the adverse side effects often associated with pharmacological interventions. Compared with traditional structured exercise such as running or cycling, game-based activities may more closely resemble the habitual physical activity patterns of children. Limited studies have suggested that game-based structured aerobic exercise program may benefit the executive function of children with ADHD. Recently, high-intensity interval training (HIIT) has emerged as a feasible and efficacious strategy for increasing physical health outcomes and cognitive function, including executive function, in healthy young people. However, research has yet to investigate whether the executive function of children with ADHD can be effectively enhanced through HIIT. Additionally, if the demands of HIIT could be embedded in a game-based activity, children may find it more acceptable and enjoyable. This study will examine whether a game-based HIIT program can improve the executive function of children with ADHD, compared with a traditional structured aerobic exercise program and a non-treatment control group. Additionally, the possible mechanism behind these beneficial effects will be explored through a non-invasive measurement based on functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). A total of 42 children with ADHD will be recruited to participate in this three-arm school-based randomized controlled trial. A 12-week specially designed game-based HIIT (GameHIIT) program and a traditional game-based structured aerobic exercise (GameSAE) program will be delivered to those children randomly assigned to these two intervention groups, while the children in the control group will maintain their regular physical activity over the same period. A number of outcome measures including executive function, cerebral hemodynamic response, physical activity, physical fitness, and enjoyment and adherence to the intervention will be assessed for both groups at baseline (T0), immediately after the intervention period (T1), and after the follow-up period (T2). If, as hypothesized, GameHIIT program improves outcomes for children with ADHD, the present research will inform the development of targeted exercise programs that can be more broadly used with this particular population. 專注力不足/過度活躍症是兒童當中比較常見的一種發育障礙，世界範圍內發生率大約為5%-6%。專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童經常會表現出執行功能障礙，而這與在這些兒童中經常觀察到的一些行為問題例如注意力不集中、抑制功能降低以及過度活躍等的發展密切相關。儘管目前已經有很多種方法被建議可用於治療專注力不足/過度活躍症，體力活動被認為是其中一種最有效的管理專注力不足/過度活躍症的方法，並且不會出現藥物治療等方法中常見的副作用。與傳統的結構性運動例如跑步或者踩單車相比，遊戲式體力活動或許更接近於兒童當中比較常見的體力活動模式。有限的研究已經指出，遊戲式的結構性有氧運動計劃或許有助於提升專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童的執行功能。 最近，高強度間歇性訓練（HIIT）被認為可以有效提升健康兒童和青少年的身體健康狀況和認知功能（包括執行功能）。然而，關於HIIT是否可以有效提高專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童執行功能的研究仍然比較缺乏。另外，如果HIIT當中的主要元素可以融合到遊戲式的活動當中，兒童或許會更加容易接受並且享受這種運動方式。這項研究將會對比一項傳統的結構式有氧運動計劃以及對照組，從而調查一項遊戲式高強度間歇訓練計劃是否能夠提升專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童的執行功能。另外，本研究也會探討這些效應背後的可能機理，主要是通過基於功能性遠紅外線成像技術（fNIRS）的非侵入式測量。 42名專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童將會參與這項以學校為基礎的三臂隨機對照實驗。一組兒童會給予12周特別設計的遊戲式HIIT（GameHIIT）計劃，另外一組接受12周的傳統的遊戲式結構性有氧運動（GameSAE）計劃，而對照組的學生則維持平常的體力活動。所有兒童會在計劃開始前、結束後以及追蹤期後進行一系列測試，主要包括執行功能、大腦血流動力學反應、體力活動，體適能、以及對於不同計劃的喜歡程度和參與程度。 如果研究結果證實此項GameHIIT計劃可以提升專注力不足/過度活躍症兒童的執行功能，此研究當中發展的運動計劃就可以更廣泛地應用於這個特殊的人群當中。

Islamic Dharwood Pau Memorial Primary School To achieve the proposed objectives, a three-arm partially-blinded randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted to evaluate the effects of two different kinds of 8-week game-based training programs on the executive function of children with ADHD. After screening, participants were randomly assigned to the game-based high-intensity interval training (GameHIIT) group, the traditional game-based structured aerobic exercise (GameSAE) group, or a non-treatment control group (CON). Participants were not blinded to treatment allocation because of the intervention nature. To avoid contamination between treatment groups, intervention deliverers were provided with a list of students in the intervention program. Only those on the list participated in the intervention. During the 8-week intervention period, participants in CON group maintained their regular PA levels. All assessments were conducted by trained research staff blinded to group allocation. Finally, a total of 63 children with ADHD were recruited which is larger than the proposed sample size (n=48). They were randomly assigned to three groups: GameHIIT group (n=23), GameSAE group (n=20), and the control group (n=20). The attrition rate of participants is 22.2%. At last, a total of 49 children with ADHD (GameHIIT group: n=16, GameSAE group: n=15; CON group: n=18) completed the programme and the post-intervention tests, whose data was enrolled in the further analyses. Number of participants involved in each test was documented, please see Sun et al. (under review). Among the 49 participants who provided valid data, (i) they were 10.10 ± 1.83 years old on average; (ii) 75.5% of them were males; and (iii) regarding ADHD type, 4.1% of them were diagnosed as having hyperactivity or impulsiveness, 24.5% of them were affected with inattention, and other 71.4% of them had the combined ADHD types. rows: To investigate the effect of a game-based high-intensity interval training (GameHIIT) program and a traditional structured exercise program on the executive function of children with ADHD.
To explore the possible mechanisms responsible for the potential improvements in executive function.

18603120.label: Major findings and research outcome
18603120.value: As included in our research paper (Sun et al., under-review), no significant intragroup difference was found among all EF measures between pre-/post-test for two game-based intervention groups. In contrary, a significant overall improvement was observed in the performance of ToLT test among control group (CON, all p<0.05). Furthermore, the only significant intergroup difference was observed in self-monitor score of parent-reported child’s EF measured by BRIEF-II between participants of GameSAE group and CON [effect size (ES)=0.743, medium effect]. In addition, neither significant intragroup nor intergroup difference was found in overall ADHD symptoms among all three groups. Furthermore, relationships between brain activity and two EF tests (i.e., CWST and ToLT) were explored. Given CWST, the repeated measures ANOVA only revealed a significant time effect at CH8 [F(1,31)=4.877, η2=0.136]. Based on the pairwise comparison and FDR correction, the significant effect were found at CH3 and CH7 between pre-/post-test in GameHIIT group. Regarding ToLT, the repeated measures ANOVA revealed a significant group effect at CH2 [F(1,31)=3.913, η2=0.202], and CH3 [F(1,31)=3.594, η2=0.188]. No significant interaction effect had been observed. Furthermore, based on the pairwise comparison and FDR correction, only the difference between GameHIIT and CON at pre-timepoint at CH3 survived. However, no significant results were found by the two-way repeated measures ANOVA for relationships between brain activity and WCST/CBTT. Moreover, significant intragroup enhancements were revealed in levels of physical fitness and PA levels of two game-based intervention groups (all p<0.05). These include (i) levels of physical fitness, i.e., right-handgrip (GameSAE), long-jump (GameSAE), 4×10m shuttle run (GameHIIT), and beep test (GameSAE); (ii) parent-reported PA levels, including lunch time PA (GameSAE) and evening PA (GameHIIT); and (iii) percentage of daytime exposed to light measured by accelerometer (GameHIIT). However, unfavourable changes were found in CON regarding BMI (a marginal increase, p=0.088), long jump test (a marginal decrease, p=0.057), and PA levels in PE class (a significant decrease, p=0.017). Furthermore, significant intergroup differences were observed among three groups in the long jump test [F(2,37)=4.675, η2=0.202, large effect] and the 4×10m shuttle run test [F(2,37)=4.559, η2=0.198, large effect]. Compared to CON, medium-to-large effect was found in both game-based intervention groups by long jump test, i.e., ES=0.790 (GameHIIT), and ES=0.921 (GameSAE). The large effect was also observed in GameHIIT group by 4×10m shuttle run test when it was compared with CON (ES= -0.981).

18603120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18603120.value: This study indicated a significant effectiveness of game-based interventions (both GameHIIT and GameSAE) on physical fitness of children with ADHD, including cardiovascular fitness, muscle strength, and speed-agility. Participants of game-based intervention groups showed an increased PA level in the leisure time (i.e., recess, lunch time, evening, or weekend), which may indicate their improved practice of healthy lifestyles. However, the assessment results failed to support these game-based PA interventions were significantly effective to improve executive function or mitigate the overall ADHD symptoms of children with ADHD. This may be partially caused by the negative influences of COVID-19 pandemic and relatively short period of intervention duration. Future studies may put more efforts on the optimization of intervention design for ADHD treatment, including sport type, intensity, or duration. Cognitive component may be synthesized into the intervention content. These may be conducted by the physical exercises and cognitive training as a dual-task or by the physical exercises with cognitive engagement. A proper PA intensity and intervention duration may enhance the adherence and implementation of intervention. Moreover, more studies are needed to clarify the potential mechanisms which may underline the benefits of different exercise strategies on the executive function of children and adolescents with ADHD.

18603120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18603120.value: In this study, a game-based HIIT program (GameHIIT) targeting on children with ADHD was evaluated by a three-arm RCT in terms of effectiveness on anthropometric indicators, PA levels, physical fitness, and executive function. When it was compared with a game-based structured aerobic exercise program (GameSAE), GameHIIT showed an advanced efficiency in improving child’s PA levels, or an equivalent effectiveness in enhancing the physical fitness among children with ADHD. Furthermore, both game-based interventions demonstrated a significant higher effect on weight management of children with ADHD than the non-treatment control group. However, the present study has no obvious evidence to support the effectiveness of game-based interventions on executive function or overall ADHD symptoms of children with ADHD. This may be partially caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Nonetheless, cerebral hemodynamic response in participants of GameHIIT group exhibited significant group effect in two EF tests (large effect, CWST and ToLT), which indicated the possible activation of left prefrontal cortex after GameHIIT training, although the performance of CWST was not improved. This implies that a larger intervention dosage or a tailored intervention design may be warranted to improve the executive function of children with ADHD with the maintenance of effect on physical health.

18603320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18603320.value: 典範與世變：慶曆至熙豐年間的頌詩、誥令和禮書——以北宋詩文革新人物為中心

18603320.label: Project Objectives
18603320.value: 本計畫建基申請人所獲「大學教育資助委員」撥款資助，探究「北宋古文家鬼神觀念與祭文」課題的基礎上，拓展對北宋文人撰作「公文」及其「斯文」觀念關係的研究。聚焦慶曆至熙豐「世變」之際，所建構的「斯文」典範。總而論之，則從撰作頌詩、制誥、禮書(包括編修禮儀和注釋禮經)的角度，呈現北宋文人文學觀念與公文著作的關係，剖析他們能否／如何通過「寫作」和「著述」，以建構「斯文」；以及能否／如何兼顧他們「士」和「文人」的雙重身份，以實踐「道」。 本研究並不假設北宋文人的斯文「理念」和「實踐」必然一致——這正是本計畫的研究對象——而非研究前設。本計畫先作分題式探討，分別撰寫四篇論文，再歸納現象，結合微觀及宏觀的視野把握北宋文人的文、道觀念及其具體實踐，亦將回答北宋政治與文體革新何以同時發生的問題。最後全部成果將出版成書，回饋學界。 就頌詩文體言之，學界已廣泛注意到歐陽修批評那些自謂「吾文士也，職于文而已」、「棄百事不關于心」的態度——另一方面，范仲淹謂「斯文也，既格乎雅頌」；孫復、石介均主張寫作「太平之頌聲」、 「洋洋治世音」；歐陽修亦說「美者美之，惡者刺之」，梅堯臣說「雅章及頌篇，刺美亦道同」；歐、梅、曾鞏、王安石在慶曆至熙豐年間撰作了不少頌詩(包括頌美時政詩歌、祭祀樂章、讚、挽辭)，本計畫從北宋當時人對「美刺」的理解和實踐出發，呈現北宋文人如何在坦承時政問題仍亟待解決的同時，按建構「斯文」的尺度，頌美王政？ 就誥令文體言之，探析北宋文人的公文寫作和私人著述的關係、異同及意義。如歐陽修說「白麻(按：制書)詔令追三代，青史文章自一家」，他在其〈《外製集》序〉中盼願「盡導天子難諭之意，而復誥命於三代之文」，文中又說「常遺恨於斯文也」；這裡的「斯文」顯然包括「誥命」。嘉祐三年(1058)歐陽修進言朝廷編輯宋朝誥令，毋使「聖宋之盛，文章詔令廢失湮淪」，朝廷從其請。歐陽修何以如此重視編修有宋誥令以傳後世？另外，歐陽修說北宋「禁浮華，使近古道」，是從天聖六年(1028)陳從易、楊大雅知制誥開始的；宋人又說蘇軾、王安石的四六文(主要是制誥)風格明顯不同——這反映了這些文章大家如何理解「制誥」之於立「王言之體」，建立典範的意義？ 就禮書編修言之，結合北宋文人「知制誥」、擔任禮官的身分，分析「文」在時局世變中所產生的迴響。如歐陽修知太常禮院，「奏禮院文字多散失，請差官編修」，此即後來的《太常因革禮》。歐陽修親自主領其事，蘇洵、姚闢等參與編輯工作。蘇、姚都不是以「通禮制」聞名的人物——朝廷何以委二人擔此重任？蘇洵在〈議修禮書狀〉屢次強調《太常因革禮》「是史書之類也」、「是史之體也」；這除了反映藉禮書「鑑古知今」的傳統論調外，還能見出「禮書」、「史著」之於斯文的何種意義？藉此是否能透視以歐陽修為首的北宋詩文領袖，更整全的「斯文」觀念？ 就禮經注釋言之，如學界對王安石《周官新義》的研究不少，大部分聚焦討論他的「字說」、「一部《周禮》理財居其半」思想、以及該書與熙豐變法的關係。除此以外，學界(劉子健)早已提出王安石變法更根本的目標是建立理想的社會風尚(social customs)和秩序(order)，那麼如果從〈《周禮義》序〉「其法可施於後世，其文有見於載籍」的準則看，配合王安石知制誥，一直到他闡述《周禮》之義的歷程，能否見出王安石——以及熙豐變法之際的文道和禮文觀？ (798 words in total for the project objectives in English version.)
