18603320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18603320.value: 慶曆至熙寧、元豐年間(1041-1085)的政治變革與文體革新，幾乎是同時發生的，如何解釋這個現象？北宋最負盛名的「文人」不僅是「文學」人物，也是當時的思想領袖；他們以「士」自居，任職朝廷，如歐陽修、王安石、曾鞏先後在這一時期負責撰作誥令(「王言之體」)、梅堯臣參與了《新唐書》的編撰，他們寫作了為數不少的雅頌詩篇；歐陽修、蘇洵等編修《太常因革禮》；王安石著《周官新義》──那他們如何理解這些著作與「斯文」的關係？換句話說：他們如何在「世變」的時代，通過更廣泛的「文」的形式，按自己的理念承傳「斯文」，並立天下之「典範」？ 針對上述問題，本研究在申請人所獲「大學教育資助委員」撥款資助，探究「北宋古文家鬼神觀念與祭文」課題的基礎上，進一步把研究領域拓展至北宋詩文革新人物所編撰的頌詩、誥令和禮書，以探討「文道觀念」和「王言之體」以及「禮」的聯繫。在這主題下的分題包括： 一． 慶曆至熙豐時期，古文家所撰的制誥文書，呈現了怎樣的褒貶尺度和涵意？其文體有何特色？其誥令是否/如何呼應了時局世變？古文家如何處理個人政見與禮文規範的差異？ 二． 這一時期詩文領袖所撰作，頌美王道時政的詩篇有何特色？所頌何事？其所揭示的「美」與「道」的觀念與時政關係謂何？ 三． 慶曆至熙豐年間的「文人」如何從「修文」的角度，編撰禮書，以及詮釋禮經？這呈現了他們對「文」和「禮」(包括禮文、禮書、禮儀)關係怎樣的認識？ 四． 綜合「一至三」，說明這一時期不同文體中，「文人」、「文道」、「禮文」、「文風」、「復古」、「革新」等觀念的異同。在全面整理「文人」所撰頌詩、公文、禮書以及上述觀念的研究以後，配合學界既有成果，是否能整合出更完整的──「斯文」觀念的全圖；藉此更有助闡述北宋中期政治變革與文體革新何以同時發生的現象？ (397 words in English version) 1. Based on the PI’s previous project funded by the UGC, which explored the ‘Conception of ghosts and spirits and ritual texts of Northern Song Gu-wen 古文 writers’, this research expands the scope of study of ‘official writings’ and that’s relationship with ‘Siwen’ 斯文, focuses on studying the setting-up of a model of Siwen amid the changes occurred during Qingli to Xifeng, presents how the Wenren 文人 of Northern Song constructed ‘Siwen’ through ‘writing’ and ‘compiling’ from the perspectives of composing odes, edicts, and writings on etiquettes and rites, as well as interpreting Book of Rites. It also presents the relationship between the conception of literature of Wenren of the Northern Song and their official works, analyzing whether they could / how could they construct Siwen through "writing" and "compilation" "; and whether they could / how could they practiced “Dao” 道 in-between the identities of “Elite” 士 and “Wenren”. This research DOES NOT assume the "conception" and "practice" of Siwen by Wenren of the Northern Song is necessarily consistent – On the contrary, this is the research object of this project - not the research presupposition. The PI will write 4 academic papers, each focusing on a sub-theme, then summarize phenomena, grasp the Northern Song Wenren’s perceptions and practice of Wen-Dao 文道from both micro and macro perspectives, and find out why the political and literary reforms took place simultaneously. Finally, all the works will be published as book, as a contribution to the academic field. 2. As for the stylistics of odes, scholars have noticed Ouyang Xiu’s criticism against the self-proclaimed Wenshi 文士who regarded writing as their only duty; Mei Yaochen said ‘laudatory texts accord with Dao no matter they are written for the purpose of praising or ridiculing’ 雅章及頌篇，刺美亦道同. Ouyang, Mei, Zeng Gong, and Wang Anshi composed many hymns (including poems praising the political condition, ritual eulogies, etc.) from Qingli to Xifeng. This approach starts from Northern Song people’s understanding and practice of praising or ridiculing, which explores how the praising in the imperial court in line with the standard of constructing Siwen while admitting the urgent need of social problems for solutions? 3. For the stylistics of edicts, exploring and analysing the relations, differences, and similarities between the official writings and personal works by Northern Song’s Wenren as well as the significance of those works. Ouyang said ‘imperial edicts should be comparable to those of Xia-Shang-Zhou’; in the preface of Waizhi-Ji 外製集, he disclosed his wish ‘to restore the earliest style in imperial edicts’. In 1058, to ‘avoid the loss of imperial edicts during the prosperous Song dynasty’, Ouyang initiated editing the Song edicts. Why were the editing and passing on of Song edicts important to him? Song people said Su Shi’s edict style differed from Wang Anshi’s --- how do their edicts reflect their perceptions of ‘the emperor’s style of writing’ 王言之體 as for setting up a model for the world? 4. For the redaction of etiquettes and rites, combined with the roles of Special Drafting Officials of the Secretariat 知制誥 of the Northern Song, as well as the Secretariat and Protocol Officers 禮官 of Wenren, analyzing the repercussions of this kind of "Wen" written by the literary figures in the age. For example, Ouyang served at the Bureau of Sacrificial Ritual 太常禮院where he ‘requested commissioners to recover and edit the lost texts’, resulting in the publication of Taichang-Yinge-Li 太常因革禮. He led the project while Su Xun and Yao Bi provided editing service. However, Su and Yao were not famous for their knowledge of the code of etiquette and rites --- why would the imperial court assign to them this important task? Su stressed that Taichang-Yinge-Li ‘fell within the category of history books’ 是史書之類and was written ‘in the style of historical writing’ 是史之體. What is the significance of such works and history books to Siwen? Will the answer enable us to study out a more comprehensive concept of Siwen perceived by the leading figures of Northern Song literature headed by Ouyang? 5. For Interpretation of the Book of Rites, James Liu suggested that the primary objective of Wang’s reform was to establish ideal social customs and order. Based on the principle of Wang’s preface of Zhouliyi 周禮義--- ‘to form a standard and writing style that could be passed on to later generations’ --- as well as Wang’s experience drafting imperial edicts and illustrating the meanings in Rites of Zhou, could we see the Wen-Dao and Liwen 禮文concepts in Wang’s mind during the Xifeng reform?

18603320.label: Realisation of objectives
18603320.value: 本計劃順利按所定下目標，圍繞課題切入點慶曆至熙豐年間的頌詩、誥令和禮書，以北宋詩文革新人物為中心，完成並發表四篇論文（Objective 1）。以下分就慶曆至熙豐觀念研究（Objective 1）、頌詩（Objective 2）、誥令（Objective 3）、禮書與禮經注釋（Objective 4 & 5），報告研究成果。 慶曆至熙豐觀念研究（Objective 1 / Research Output 8.2） 研究成果指出：1. 熙豐變法時期宋人從未直接比較范、王的改革主張、也不曾認為慶曆、熙寧更革是可比的對象——這些聯繫待朱熹而後始。今人或曰熙豐變法之時，慶曆革新派趨於保守——卻非宋人認識；2.徽宗朝以後卻出現慶曆之治說法，其內涵又被簡化或提升為諸如仁宗能「開納直言，善御羣臣，賢必進，邪必退」。這些說法無法揭示慶曆之政的真正特色，又故意忽略慶曆改革主事者因「眾訾成波，擠落在外」的事實，卻有利於范仲淹作為名臣、忠義第一人形象的建立；3. 宋人從不曾認為慶曆之政有違祖宗之法，這是宋人不言慶曆「新」政的根本原因。 頌詩研究（Objective 2 / Research Output 8.1） 研究成果指出：1. 宋詩中陳述上帝與個人關係者較唐詩多，惟宋詩中上帝並非可茲批評或開玩笑的對象，於是人與主宰爭辯，甚者嘲諷創造者的內容，常藉天公、造物的形象呈現，蘇軾是其中佼佼者；2. 宋代禮樂、宗教關於何謂上帝的複雜討論，對宋詩中主宰的形象幾無影響；3. 蘇軾是自唐迄宋運用天公、造物意象的集大成者，藉此豐富了宋詩對鬼斧神工之奇與美的想像，他云「造物豈不惜，要令工語言」，又以「勞心以耗神，盛氣以忤物」解釋何以詩人固窮。 誥令研究（Objective 3 / Research Output 9） 研究成果指出：1．典重温雅是宋詔令最推崇的文學風格；一生未曾知制誥者，就算抒發個人感懷的作品如何出色，他們的名字亦罕見於詔令。2．「文質彬彬」、「無尚空言」是北宋詩文革新人物，以及王言文體均一致肯定的文學追求，這也是唐宋古文革新與傳統典雅文觀相通之處。宋人又認為北宋更革文體的歷程，與詔令文風嬗變的幾個階段大致對應。3．北宋中葉以後詔令，已可見韓愈作為大儒、文宗的地位不可動搖，其言行常在王言中被引用，以之作為先朝典範；到了南宋，歐陽脩、蘇軾之典範的建立也類此，並出現了「韓歐」、「脩軾」等合稱，標誌着唐宋古文復興的意義得到絕對權威（天子）的認可。 禮書與禮經注釋研究（Objective 4 & 5 / Research Output 8.3） 研究成果指出：1．王安石主張「天人一氣」，並轉化《黃帝內經》、《難經》觀念，認為人若「養其氣體」，達精明之至，可通神明；2．王認為禮是溝通天人之道的中介：「外作器，以通神明之德；內作德，以正性命之情」，至誠之人與鬼神交通，鬼神必有所應；3．天道「任理而無情」是因為這符合「天地之大德」，王安石筆下的皇天與上帝顯具道德意志，能賞善罰惡；當刻意比較「天道」和「神」之別時，他更強調天道是相對於地道而言之，非如「神」能大能小，妙於萬物。4．王安石謂「人死為鬼，物死為物，物出為鬽」，他不否認鬼怪作祟之事，並非常可能和其子王雱一樣，認為聖人能廓其志氣，不累於形，其精氣與天地相通，故「聖人死曰神」。

18603320.label: Major findings and research outcome
18603320.value: 1. 「范仲淹變法」之說首見於明代，「慶曆新政」概念之使用不及百年。宋代語彙並非無「新政」等用語；宋人不言慶曆新政的現象，在於他們從不認為慶曆之政有違祖宗之法，南宋以後論者以范仲淹為「守我宋之家法者」，進一步確立這觀點。 2. 「文質彬彬」、「無尚空言」是北宋詩文革新人物，以及詔令文體均一致肯定的文學追求，這也是唐宋古文革新與傳統典雅文觀相通之處。宋人又認為北宋更革文體的歷程，與詔令文風嬗變的幾個階段大致對應。 3. 今存蘇軾詩（包括其頌詩）中含天公、造物者的數量超過了《全唐詩》相關用語的總和，也遠超蘇軾之前任何一位宋人。蘇軾是自唐迄宋運用天公、造物意象的集大成者，豐富了宋詩對鬼斧神工之奇與美的想像。 4.王安石主張「天人一氣」，並在詮釋禮經中結合《黃帝內經》、《難經》「精神魂魄意」觀念，與《易》「精氣為物，遊魂為變」思想，提出「禮」是溝通天人之道的中介：「外作器，以通神明之德；內作德，以正性命之情」的觀點。

18603320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18603320.value: 建基是項計劃及申請人同樣獲大學教育資助委員撥款資助，探究「北宋古文家鬼神觀念與祭文」課題的基礎上，進一步把研究領域拓展至宋代各體文中的思想史。初步計劃下一研究項目聚焦宋詔令中的思想觀念，在這主題下採個案研究，分論： 1. 宋詔令中上帝／天帝／玉帝／天／道的涵義及形象 2. 論析王言對孔子之靈神及其形象 3. 探討天子之「文」中，佛教和道教的思想內涵及其與政權的關係 綜合上述，以深化對宋代王權與思想史關係課題的認識。

18603320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18603320.value: 是項計劃成果能聯繫中國古代「文體」與「思想」研究，尤其是不囿於過去通常「以哲學史等同思想史」的成見，重新發現詩歌、詔令、禮經中的思想觀念，因而豐富了論者對於宋代 1. 天人關係、2. 王權運作、3. 文體本色、4. 禮文意義等課題的認識。其中最有意義的是首次辨明了蘇軾詩歌「天之主宰」的形象、首次條分縷述地考析了自宋迄今對於范仲淹「慶曆之政」的詮釋歷程，以及首次釐清了王安中的鬼神觀，及其與之相關的「天—禮—人」觀念。

18603520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18603520.value: 如何識別讀寫困難學童一直是學術界的研究焦點，近年的西方研究更是開始關注來自有讀寫困難傾向家庭（family at risk of dyslexia，FRD）的兒童的語文能力發展。研究發現，來自這些家庭的兒童早在入讀小學之前就已經出現多個方面的語文能力發展困難。然而，在FRD兒童當中，環境因素及認知能力如何影響他們的語文發展，至今仍是一個極少被探討的議題。事實上，儘管中國是世界上人口最多的國家，現有文獻卻非常缺乏以中文為母語的FRD兒童的研究數據。 對於該群體兒童的語文發展特質，以及環境因素和認知能力對其語文發展的影響，仍然是知之甚少。此外，相較於以字母系統為基礎的語言（如英文），中文在閱讀和書寫各方面都具備獨有的特點。因此，探討風險因素（包括家庭環境和兒童的認知能力）如何在華人文化背景的學校和家庭中影響兒童的語文發展，是非常必要的。 該項研究的目的是探討華人FRD兒童中，環境因素（例如家庭社經地位和家庭語文學習環境），兒童認知能力（例如執行功能和視覺注意廣度），和語文能力之間的關係，以及這些因素如何協同影響兒童的語文發展。我們將追蹤約190名就讀於香港幼稚園的華人兒童，連續三年（由幼稚園低班至高班）由幼兒和他們的家長身上抽取測試數據，評估幼兒及他們的家長的認知和語文能力。我們將採用追蹤和多元統計學的方法分析數據，探討（1）FRD兒童的特質和類別，（2）有讀寫困難傾向家庭的預測指標，（3）FRD兒童與普通家庭的兒童在環境因素，認知和語文能力各個方面的不同之處，和（4）FRD兒童在不同成長階段（幼稚園低班至高班）的發展困難。 該項研究不僅能幫助我們了解華人FRD兒童的特質和類別，還能為將來這一主題的相關生理學研究提供寶貴的參考資料。研究發現亦將有助於及早識別和支援有讀寫困難傾向的家庭和兒童。所以，這項研究對於教師，家長和教育政策制定者都將大有裨益，尤其對華人社會中有讀寫困難傾向的家庭更是有莫大的幫助。

18603820.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18603820.value: 中國學校中的馬克思主義信仰教育重塑

18603820.label: Project Objectives

18603820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18603820.value: 本研究主要關注習近平時代中國公民培養的教育方針，這是中國教育發展的基礎性問題之一，也是國際教育研究裡的重要議題。習近平時代再次強調了馬克思主義信仰教育的重要意義，但也對新時代背景下信仰教育的實踐注入了新的元素。改革開放以來，中國社會一直存在著信仰危機的大討論。有學者認為習近平時代對於公民信仰體系的重塑並不是單純地回歸毛澤東時代的政治教育系統，而是注入了“中國夢”的思想元素（Cheek and Ownby, 2018）。此課題中，在探析習近平時代公民培養的教育方針前，我們會梳理公民信念在近代中國教育中是如何被構建的。在此基礎上，我們會從三個方面具體分析現階段的教育方針：其一 、與建國以後其他階段對比，當前時代對馬克思主義信仰教育的理解是否有了新的內涵？其二、有研究者觀察到儒家思想在現階段執政理念裡扮演更為重要的角色（比如Zhao, 2016）。那麼，儒家思想是否以及如何影響現有公民信念的構建呢？其三、最近幾十年，中國學者對西方背景下的公民教育理念已有大量的討論並在實踐上嘗試本土化。那麼現有公民教育理念如何與之相結合呢？本研究的數據來源包括教育政策、教科書、和對政策研究者的訪談。我們的分析以公民信念為切入視角來探析習近平時代和建國後其他階段的教育發展和公民培養方針。我們的研究有助於豐富中國和國際背景下的公民教育研究、尤其是公民信念方面的理論探討。

18604720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18604720.value: 這項研究將探討高等教育中的學術企業主義對學者的日常生活、大學與學術界之間的互動、以及這些互動對東亞三個全球城市（香港，首爾，東京）世界一流大學之制度變遷的影響。自從1990年代以來新自由主義在全球蔓延，經濟全球化加劇了高等教育組織中的「企業化管治」，在這種社會組織制度中，競爭性撥款越來越多。隨著全球知識經濟的到來，大學使命發生了巨大的轉變，知識日益成為經濟發展的新動力。大學在日常管理中積極追求創新，以保證未來財政的可持續性，並獲得進一步的資源以推動大學的卓越發展。相關學術文獻探討了高等教育組織在多大程度上從學術象牙塔廣泛地轉型至「創業型大學」（Etzkowitz等，2008）。企業主義的全球趨勢（例如Etzkowitz & Leydesdorff，2000；Clark，1998a，1998b；Shattock，2009；Tang，2014）深刻影響著大學、學術專業與制度變遷之間的互動（Gumport，2019）。儘管此乃西方的政策趨勢並新興學術研究課題（Rhoades & Stensaker，2017），文獻仍缺乏學術企業主義在世界一流大學（Stensaker & Benner，2013）和亞洲學術專業的研究（Yang，2012）。如果長久缺乏相關研究，學術企業主義對東亞世界一流大學、學術生活和制度變遷的影響仍然未知。 本研究將採用制度/建制民族誌為研究方法（Smith，2005）。它與其他質性研究方法不同，因為它爲研究組織制度變遷作為「按文本組織的關係」提供了方法，而制度變遷唯有藉著日常工作的協調出現。制度民族誌的研究方法，能夠利用國際學術專業的「話語資源」（Marginson，2011a），就學術企業主義的大趨勢進行多樣、去中心化和具體的對話。本研究將重新聚焦並創建議論和政策的語言，在更大的民主情境下重塑我們對東亞世界一流大學和學術企業主義的理解（Marginson，2011；Tang，2015）。通過構建表述東亞大學制度變遷的多元聲音和批判見解的新詞彙，這項研究將有助於擬定「優秀大學」的另類敘述（Connell，2019）。

18604720.label: Realisation of objectives
18604720.value: To fulfill the three research objectives, the project has undergone and completed the following activities and tasks: 1. Robust and comprehensive review of updated conceptual and empirical bodies of literature (since proposal submission in November 2019) concerning the topics of (1) Academic entrepreneurialism, (2) Higher education policy, (3) Academic profession, and (4) World-class universities/ flagship universities in East Asia. 2. Documentary research on 100 official and institutional documents of the higher education sector of Hong Kong, South Korea, and Japan, and of the three case-study universities (University of Hong Kong/ HKU, Seoul National University/ SNU, and University of Tokyo/ UTokyo). The research tasks fulfilled Project Objective #1 and mapped the extent, processes, and patterns by which academic entrepreneurialism manifests in the institutional context and policies of East Asian flagship universities. The documents were scrutinised in two steps (1) mapping the significant instances that reflect the strategic planning, aspirations, visions, and the substantive dynamics involved in the development of Asian flagship universities in response to academic entrepreneurialism; (2) analysing the similar and contrasting/ competing values, attitudes and messages the texts communicate. Discourse analysis (Gee, 2004) was conducted to understand how institutional policies and practices construct the texts to coordinate the everyday work of academics and develop the textually-mediated ruling relation between the institution and academics, and among colleagues across different (inter-) disciplinary fields and academic positions. The analysis explicated the meanings expressed in the texts and relate those with the relevant social contexts. The inductive and iterative processes of data analysis helped enrich our understanding of the complexities and diversities in the institutionalisation process (Zilber, 2008), responding to the different socio-political, economic and cultural contexts of each case-study university. The analysis focussed on content (what was written) and discourse (how it was written) in the documents and attended to how inconsistencies and contradictions, if any, were resolved (Prior, 2008). Through analysis, three sources and streams of academic entrepreneurialism were identified: Stream & Source #1: Knowledge exchange, community engagement and public relations, student/graduate entrepreneurship, and alumni relations Stream & Source #2: Interdisciplinary teaching and learning programmes Stream & Source #3: High-impact use-inspired basic research, applied research and research commercialisation Based on a comprehensive and systematic analysis of 100 official documents of the three case-study universities, the research found a significant volume and a broad range and types of border-crossing practices in the three case-study universities. We further analysed the documentary data by conceptual categorisation and identified 17 dimensions of university policies and practices that embrace border-crossing innovation. The conceptualisations of borders, permeabilities, and cross-sectoral communications, collaborations, and partnerships enabled the thematisation of border-crossing innovations in three key domains: the university and the 'real world'; the academic profession and other professions or sectors [3 dimensions] academic disciplines and fields (interdisciplinary innovations) [9 dimensions] public and private spheres (e.g. public-private partnerships) [5 dimensions]. 4. To fulfil Project Objectives #2 and #3 (to identify how the academic profession of East Asian flagship universities make sense of the policies and practices of academic entrepreneurialism, and analyse the similarities and differences of the interactions between East Asian flagship universities, the academic profession and the institutional change in response to academic entrepreneurialism), the project has completed the research interviews with 52 academic professionals from diverse disciplinary, institutional and generational backgrounds at HKU, SNU, and UTokyo according to purposive sampling. This study was designed as an innovative form of qualitative inquiry, characterized by the creation of a reflective "dialogical space" during research interviews. The approach aimed to avoid privileging any particular perspective a priori, allowing new meanings to emerge within the spaces between the multitude of voices. Researchers embraced dialogicity throughout the process of gathering, interpreting, and documenting interview data. Rather than seeking a singular explanation and promoting a monologic discourse that demands unconditional allegiance, the study emphasised sensitivity to the unique and open-ended nature of interaction, dialogue, and meaning-making. This dialogic approach acknowledges a multitude of voices with different meanings without asserting authority. Furthermore, the study adopted the perspective that truth is always unfinalised, reflecting a commitment to embracing the dynamic and evolving nature of knowledge and understanding. 5. The project investigators initial findings and analysis in 7 international/ key academic conferences to receive fresh perspectives, novel ideas, and critical insights. Abstracts for the conference paper/ panel were peer reviewed for the key international conferences, including key conferences (AERA 2022 by the American Educational Research Association; CIES 2022 by the Comparative and International Education Society; AARE 2021 by the Australian Association for Research in Education; HKERA-APERA 2021 by the Hong Kong Educational Research Association and the Asia Pacific Educational Research Association). Outcomes of the conference presentations aim to turn the conference papers into high impact journal articles entitled “Border-crossing as innovation in world-class universities: Rethinking the isomorphic change of academic entrepreneurialism” (under review by Higher Education (SSCI-listed, Q1), “The ‘Post-entrepreneurial University’? Diverse voices and critical insights from the academic profession of world-class universities” (under review by Minerva (SSCI-listed, Q1), “Imagining the University Differently: Future of the Academic Profession at World-class Universities” (to be submitted to Studies in Higher Education (SSCI-listed, Q1), and “Neoliberal Citizenship? The case of the Academic Profession” (to be submitted to Discourse: Studies in the Cultural Politics of Education (SSCI-listed, Q1). 6. The project has published the articles “Higher education policies and academic entrepreneurialism: Conceptual linkages and a contextual approach” for Handbook of Education Policies (published by Edward Elgar Publishing), “Is academic entrepreneurialism a universal concept? New ideas and insights from contextualisation beyond East and West” in International Journal of Chinese Studies, and forthcoming article “Academic entrepreneurialism between east and west: Innovating future-oriented development of world-class universities in Hong Kong and Tokyo” in Education governance in the 21st Century: Dialogue between Chinese and Western perspective (published by Routledge). 7. Apart from training 3 doctoral students, the project has been involved in 10 different aspects of knowledge exchange work and activities internationally, regionally and locally to create impacts from the research. The Principal Investigator (PI) has benefited from the GRF project to develop his academic identity as an internationally-active researcher and scholar in the fields of innovation, future-oriented education, and entrepreneurship.

18604720.label: Major findings and research outcome
18604720.value: The research discovered that flagship universities in East Asia undergo isomorphic changes in response to the global trend of academic entrepreneurialism. The convergence of entrepreneurial behaviors among these institutions remains a prevailing trend, driven by factors such as legitimacy-seeking, organisational learning, resource concerns, network effects, and the path dependence of academic entrepreneurialism. It is crucial to note that the organizational identity, specifically being a leading public university within the nation and region, poses a significant consideration for HKU, SNU, and UTokyo to reconsider whether the external motivations and pressures for change align with their internal values and identity. The research highlights that world-class universities in East Asia widely adopt border-crossing as a form of innovation. Our study has mapped and profiled the key 17 dimensions of organizational innovation as different crossings of borders, boundaries, and permeabilities as well as inter-sectoral communications, collaborations and partnerships in three domains: (1) the university and the 'real world' [3 dimensions], (2) academic fields/ disciplines [9 dimensions], and (3) public and private spheres [5 dimensions]. However, the convergence of organizational innovation is juxtaposed with differentiation and fragmentation of the academic profession. Academics experience, perceive, and understand the meaning of being an academic, academic life, and higher education differently according to their own situations. Academics, as sensemakers, navigate the evolving landscape of academia by adapting their values, identities, professional learning, and career choices, which may involve transitioning between institutions, higher education systems, or even leaving the academic profession altogether. It is observed that academics who hold views endorsing the imagination of the ‘entrepreneurial university’ tend to be more optimistic about the future of the academic profession. Additionally, some disciplines are more instrumental to the knowledge trends and university strategic development. Academics from those disciplines tend to align with the institutional reasoning of the entrepreneurial university. The study also found that key stakeholders of the global knowledge economy—rather than the academic profession—take the lead in the ongoing ‘learning’ project of sensemaking to interpret change and crisis, as well as envisage the future of the University. Diverse voices and critical insights documented by the study reconfigure the understanding of the East Asian world-class universities and academic entrepreneurialism in a broader and more imaginative framework. This is instrumental in refocusing the terms of debate and policy, as well as formulating alternative narratives of a ‘good university'.

18604720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18604720.value: The research indicates that when the academic profession withdraws itself to the narrow imagination of academic entrepreneurialism, the future possibilities of the university are limited and hopelessly impoverished. Previous studies on the evolving academic profession have predominantly focused on contemporary issues, employing quantitative methodologies to examine current changes. However, there has been limited effort to advance scholarly discourse by comprehensively grasping the conceptual and empirical links that bind the past, present, and future of the academic profession, and exploring the foundations of its evolution and continuity. In light of this, the Principal Investigator (PI) has designed a new GRF research proposal to expand this line of inquiry that i) focuses on future orientation, forms and formation of imaginaries, ii) empirically, conceptually and dialogically relates future imaginaries to historicity and reflexivity of the academic profession, and iii) contextualises the conceptualisation of future imaginaries in the cases of East Asia and flagship universities. Consequently, this proposed research, by stretching the scope of future imaginaries and possibilities of the academic profession, seeks to address Ronald Barnett’s (2013) call for a more substantive empirical scholarship and by providing the first, international, qualitative and comparative analysis on this topic.

18604720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18604720.value: This study examines higher education change by exploring how the trend called 'academic entrepreneurialism' affects the work lives of academics in three major cities in East Asia: Hong Kong, Seoul, and Tokyo. The researchers interviewed 52 academics from different backgrounds and conducted thorough research on 100 official documents from three world-class universities: The University of Hong Kong, Seoul National University, and University of Tokyo. The findings show that these universities are undergoing significant organisational changes to embrace academic entrepreneurialism in order to acquire public trust, resources, competitiveness, university development, and stability. While they prioritise global well-being and academic excellence, this organisational innovation has led to differences and fragmentation within the academic profession. Academics are adapting to these changes by adjusting their values, identities, learning, and career paths, which may involve moving between institutions or even leaving academia altogether. The study also highlights that stakeholders in the global knowledge economy, rather than academics, are leading the way in interpreting and shaping the future of universities. These diverse insights challenge existing views of East Asian universities and academic entrepreneurialism, offering new perspectives and alternative narratives for the future of higher education.

18605220.value: 教師給予學生的社會支持可以從教師對學生的耐心和提供的幫助體現出來，包括在指導學生學習與及個人對教導學生的興趣 (Aldrup, Klusmann, Lüdtke, Göllner, & Trautwein, 2018)。社會支持是教學行為的一項特徵，與學生學習有著積極的關係 (Suldo 等人, 2009)，是熱誠教師的敬業行為 (Kunter 等人, 2008)，也是有效教學表現的重要元素(Lam, 2019)。社會支持行為被認為是利他行為，與給予支持者的幸福感是正相關的 (Weinstein, & Ryan, 2010)。目前，不少學者發表有關教師給予學生社會支持如何影響學習者在學習及發展各方面的研究 (Aldrup, et al., 2018)，然而有關於教師給予學生社會支持對教師個人幸福感有怎樣的影響的研究仍未受到關注。本研究試圖填補這一研究領域的空隙。 本研究旨在探討教師提供社會支持的成因與後效。本研究試圖探測“工作中的基本心理需求滿足感”（自主性、能力感和歸屬感）是否與“幸福感”（工作投入、心理意義和健康狀況）相關，與及這種預測的關係是否可以通過“提供社會支持”來調節。這個調節模式是建基於自我決定理論的觀點，強調個人有意義地與社會環境整合是成長發展的必要條件 (Ryan, Ryan, Di Domenico, & Deci, 2019)。此外，健康心理學提到提供社會支持的積極影響亦為這個調節模式的立論補充了理據。 研究者會向300位來自不同背景的香港學校的初中教師發放一組包含47個問題的調查問卷。問卷會量度教師在社會支持、工作中的基本需求滿足感、工作投入、心理意義和健康幾個方面的狀況。研究者亦會就上述各個量度導向的量表作出翻譯、回譯及試驗研究。研究者會以結構方程模型以提供社會支持為調節因子，探討教師基本心理需求對教師幸福感的預測能力。這種複雜的多變量分析，可以用來研究不同變數之間的相互關係。 這項研究的學術成就在於將自我決定理論的應用範圍擴展到教師幸福感的研究上，把教師幸福感與教師給予社會支持兩個概念聯繫起來。本研究的結果將會進一步加深我們對教師幸福感的認識，藉著設定教師給予學生的社會支持和教師工作上的心理需求之間的潛在關係作出驗證，本研究同時為以往有關教師滿足感的研究增添研究價值。如果本研究的結果確能顯彰社會支持有重大意義，那麼本研究就能為教師發展提供建議，並重新思考社會支持對社會的影響。

18605220.label: Realisation of objectives
18605220.value: The four objectives are generally achieved. The results of this study are based on 309 responses from teachers of ten local secondary schools who responded to a questionnaire. The variables planned to be explored in the research model include ‘basic psychological need at work’ (BPNSW), Social Support (SSPT)’, Work engagement (WE), Psychological Meaningfulness (PM), and Mental Health (MH). The last three variables suggest the composite content of well-being. The first three objectives are developed based on the three fundamental hypotheses echo the research model. The hypotheses assume ‘basic psychological need at work’ (BPNSW) positively predicts ‘social support’ giving (SSPT) and work engagement (WE) as a well-being factor, and SSPT positively predicts WE. Teachers’ SSPT, which means that teachers’ social support for learners is hypothesised as a mediator that impacts the relationship between BPNW and WE. Since MH and PM added to WE as a composite well-being factor generated insignificant results, in investigating the mediating role of SSPT we focus on WE as a single well-being factor in the research design. The investigation is conducted in two path models, one is to treat BPNSW as a variable, while the other considers the properties of BPNSW as three unique variables to be studied, i.e. competence (C), autonomy (A), and relatedness (R). The effect of both BPNW in model 1 and C-A-R in model 2 in relation to teachers’ SUPT and WE is explored; the mediating role of SUPT is also investigated in the two models, i.e. between BPNW and WE, and between C-A-R and WE respectively. The results of model 1 revealed that BPNSW significantly and positively predicted SUPT and WE, indicating that the higher the BPNW, the more the SUPT and the WE; SUPT also significantly and positively predicted WE which is a well-being variable, suggesting that the more the SUPT, the more the WE. The results of model 2 showed that competence (C), as a component of BPNSW, significantly and positively predicted SUPT and WE, suggesting that the higher the C, the more the SUPT and the WE. SUPT also significantly and positively predicted WE, suggesting the more the SUPT, the more the WE. However, there were no significant relationships between autonomy (A) and SUPT, between A and WE, between relatedness (R) and SUPT, and between R and WE. The above results proved objectives 1 and 2 with the details suggesting the overall effect of BPNSW (C, A, and R together) that works on WE, and the unique effect of C as one of the three nutrients of ‘basic psychological need satisfaction’ according to self-determination theory (SDT) (Ryan & Deci, 2017). For objective 3, the results proved the mediating effect of SSPT, which makes this study significant. The mediation analysis for model 1 suggested that the indirect path, i.e. BPNW to SUPT to WE, was significant. That is, SUPT is confirmed to have a prominent mediating effect between BPNSW on WE. In the same way, mediation analysis results of model 2 showed an indirect path, i.e. C to SUPT to WE, was also significant, indicating the prominent mediating role of SUPT between C and WE. Taken together, teachers’ SSPT makes the effect of ‘basic psychological need’ as a whole (in path model 1) and ‘competence’ (in path model 2) on teachers’ WE more salient. Additionally, the project team explores BPNSW and PM (Psychological Meaningfulness), with PM as one of the well-being factors in the original model. The result indicates a related strand in this project, highlighting the benefit of BPNW on eudaimonia factors. By regression analysis, model 1 treats BPNSW as a whole, and model 2 considers the BPNW components C, A, and R separately. Model 1 suggests that BPNSW as a whole predicts PM significantly, while model 2 shows that R (relatedness) is the highest predictor of psychological meaningfulness, followed by Autonomy and Competence. The unique effect of Relatedness satisfaction on teachers’ WE indicates the relationship of BPNSW and WE which should be affected by the nature of an occupation. The study suggests practical implications with reference to Objective 4. Policymakers in education planning should consider ways to support the senior management team of the schools to cultivate the school environment for promoting basic psychological need satisfaction as it improves teacher engagement, which may eventually contribute to the school. The policies may include: (a) to develop a sense of competence in teachers such as through recognition, constructive feedback, and the opportunities provided to teachers for learning and advancement; (b) enable teachers to do what they value, which means to provide opportunities to ensure that teachers can actualise their goals through work; and (c) making teachers feel connected, being cared for, and support each other. The study recommends that schools should enhance teacher competence, in one way teachers should be developed through their job, such as taking up tasks that are new and challenging, and in another way, teachers should experience accomplishment through chances provided to them. Since competence should be realised in an autonomous motivational state and through contributing to others, the three basic need components may also be equally considered to support competence satisfaction as the three basic psychological need is considered complementary (Vansteenkiste et al., 2020). Teacher training should focus on both leadership training, curriculum development and long-term teacher development and be based on basic psychological need and social support as the conceptual framework. An attitude of supporting students can be experienced in the experience of giving social support and it can further accord meaning to teachers to make them become engaged, this is explained by mental action and agentic engagement (Pacherie, 2011) in the cognitive science literature. Such social support experience can serve as a reflective probe for teachers to embrace, foster and evaluate their work, which can yield satisfaction and opportunities for learning ongoingly. Such self-generating, beneficial experience is the ingredient for teacher engagement that can enhance teacher development and teaching professionalism. These recommendations may eliminate the issues of stress and mental health that our research team addresses in the background of this GRF research. References: Pacherie, E., ' Self‐Agency', in Shaun Gallagher (ed.), The Oxford Handbook of the Self (2011; online edn, Oxford Academic, 2 May 2011), https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordhb/9780199548019.003.0020, accessed 20 Apr. 2023. Ryan, R. M., & Deci, E. L. (2017). Self-Determination Theory: Basic Psychological Needs in Motivation, Development, and Wellness. Guilford Publications. Vansteenkiste, M., Ryan, R. M., & Soenens, B. (2020). Basic psychological need theory: Advancements, critical themes, and future directions. Motivation and Emotion, 44(1), 1–31. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11031-019-09818-1

18605220.label: Major findings and research outcome
18605220.value: The study examines the mediating effect of social support between basic psychological need satisfaction (BPNSW) and work engagement (WE) on Hong Kong teachers via two path models. Model 1 examines the mediating effect of SSPT between BPNSW and work engagement (WE); model 2 examines the mediating role of social support (SSPT) between competence, autonomy and relatedness need (C, A, and R) separately on WE. SSPT is proved to be a prominent mediating factor. In model 1, SUPT revealed an indirect effect of BPNSW to SUPT to WE. Similarly, in model 2, SUPT showed an indirect path of C to SUPT to WE significantly. As a whole, SUPT mediates the relationship between the pair BPNSW and WE, and the other pair C and WE. The results highlighted the importance of BPNSW in the workplace. Teachers who experience BPNSW feel that their work is in line with their personal values and that they are competent and being cared for. By enacting SSPT, as a prosocial behaviour, teachers perceive meaningfulness and become more engaged at work. The three separate BPNSW components indicate a unique effect on the particular variable. In model 2, ‘SSPT’ partially mediates the relationship between ‘C’ and ‘WE’. The feeling of competence may serve as a psychological empowerment to make one engaged at work as it yields satisfaction. Nevertheless, the literature suggests that A, C and R complementarily fostering well-being outcomes (Vansteenkiste et al., 2020). As shown, A, C, and R are correlated, it indicates the interactive nature of the three components in BPNSW. The study supports self-determination theory in recognising ‘competence need’ and BPNSW in facilitating teachers’ WE. Schools should provide basic need satisfaction in general and competence need in specific, on top of that schools should enable teachers to be concentrated on social support giving. The relationships between the variables were presented in three international conferences (Part C, 9). The mediating role of social support and the predicting role of BPNSW on PM, is currently being developed into two draft journal papers to be submitted to two targeted high-impact journals, namely, Teaching and Teacher Education and Journal of Organisational Behaviour. We shared the results with the senior management team of schools and school teachers at a seminar in Dec 2021 and a research seminar for academics organised in Mar 2023 by our University.

18605220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18605220.value: We are currently working on the research outputs focusing on (1) mediating role of social support, and (2) the predicting role of BPNSW on PM, they are being developed into two draft journal papers to be submitted to two targeted high-impact journals, namely, Teaching and Teacher Education and Journal of Organisational Behaviour. We will follow up a literature review on the topics of BPNSW, PM, and WE which can be developed into a conceptual article to address eudaimonia outcomes with a self-determination theory perspective. The project is documented at https://aclass.eduhk.hk/research/grf-project-social-support-giving as a platform for wide dissemination. The study highlights the importance of social support, such practice can make teacher engagement in teaching become optimal with the support of a supportive environment. BPNSW. A few strands can be followed up based on this study. First, social support can add value to research on teaching and strengthen pedagogical studies. Second, the unique effect of competence, autonomy, and relatedness may predict need differences in variables such as work engagement. Organisational behaviour is recommended to be studied in a profession-specific context to address specificities of a profession. Third, the study recommends the complementary relationship and unique effects among the three needs, that contributes to the development of self-determination theory.

18605220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18605220.value: This study investigates whether teachers social support plays can enhance the effect of basic psychological need at work (BPNSW) on teacher work engagement, and whether social support can make the relationship between competence (C), autonomy (A), and relatedness (R) and teachers’ work engagement (WE) become more positive. The result agrees with these assumptions. Teachers’ social support can make the relationship between a working environment that offers BPNSW and WE more positive, it can also make the relationship between a working environment that offers C and WE more positive. Regarding the assisting role of SSPT to facilitate the relationship between BPNSW and WE, and C and WE. BPNSW can make teachers feel that their work is valuable and that they are competent and being cared for. SSPT, as teachers offer to students, is prosocial behaviour, and through enacting such behaviour, teachers can perceive meaningfulness and become more engaged. C may serve as psychological empowerment in motivating one to be engaged at work. The study recommends school planning to incorporate basic need satisfaction in general and competence need in specific in school policies, on top of that schools should enable teachers to be involved in social support giving.

18605520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18605520.value: Ten years ago, Michael Fullan predicted that educational system reform would “come of age”. The past decade has witnessed some ambitious attempts to reform educational systems in different societies, but few have delivered their intended outcomes. Among these societies, Shanghai seems to be a positive outlier which often attributes its success in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) to its system-wide reform efforts. Many cities in Mainland China have also followed the piloting role of Shanghai and adopted similar system reform strategies. System reform usually involves collaboration and networking across schools and districts for the purpose of narrowing the gaps between schools and enhancing teacher capacity on a large scale. System reform therefore requires displaying and executing leadership at different levels – teacher leaders, principals, district administrators, and government officials. A core challenge for system leaders is to design and deploy educational infrastructure, including coordinated roles, structures and resources, to create the conditions for successful system change. This study will examine the relationship between leadership, educational infrastructure and system-wide improvement through case studies of selected innovative system reform initiative implemented in three Mainland Chinese regions – Shanghai, Anhui and Guizhou. They are located in East, Central and West China. The study aims to deconstruct the innovative system reforms carried out in these provinces and examine the role of leadership in designing and deploying infrastructure necessary for successful systemic change. The study will employ a case study design and selects 4-6 municipal/provincial-level or district-level reform initiatives, such as commissioned administration (weituo guanli, which usually involves the commissioning of high-performing public schools to take over the administration of weaker ones), district-level teacher learning collaboration (which mainly refers to an established mechanism for expert teachers to network across schools and exert leadership beyond their immediate school level), as innovative cases for focused research. Data will be collected through observing cross-school collaborative learning activities, conducting in-depth interviews with different levels of leaders involved in the reform initiatives, and collecting documents and field notes. This study will make a unique contribution to three major bodies of educational literature: system reform; international understanding of system leadership; and educational leadership in China. The research findings will have important implications for system leadership and systemic improvement practices in Hong Kong and other societies. 十年前，迈克尔·富兰（Michael Fullan）预言教育体制内系统改革的热潮即将来临。过去的十年见证了不同国家和地区在教育系统改革方面雄心勃勃的探索，但这些探索几乎都未能达到预期的结果。在种种探索中，初获成功的上海似乎是一个例外。上海经常将其在国际学生评估项目（PISA）中的成功归功于其系统性的改革努力。系统改革通常涉及跨学校和跨地区的协作和网络，目的是缩小学校之间的差距、大规模提高教师能力等。因此，系统改革要求不同层级的领导者 – 教师领导、校长、区行政人员、政府官员 – 均能展现领导才能、发挥领导作用。系统领导者面临的一个核心挑战是设计和部署教育基础架构，包括协调的角色、结构和资源，以此为成功的系统改革创造条件。 本研究将通过对包括上海在内的三个地方省市（上海、安徽和贵州）实施的部分创新体制改革举措进行案例分析，来探讨领导力、教育基础架构与系统改进之间的关系。该研究旨在解构这些省份进行的创新性系统改革，并研究领导力如何设计和部署系统变革所必需的制度和文化等基础架构。研究将采用案例设计，并选择4-6个省/市级或区级改革举措作为重点研究的创新案例，例如委托管理（通常涉及委托表现突出的公立学校管理弱校）和区级教师协作学习（主要是指专家级教师建立校际网络，并领导来自不同学校的教师协作学习）。我们将通过观察跨校协作学习活动、与参与改革的各级领导进行深度访谈、收集资料和田野记录等方式收集数据。 本研究将在以下三方面为教育领域的研究有所贡献：系统改革；系统领导力的国际理解；以及中国的教育领导力。研究结果将为香港及其他社会在系统领导力和系统改进方面的探索带来重要启示。

18605520.label: Realisation of objectives
18605520.value: Since the project began, there has been a global revigorated interest in system leadership and system-wide reforms (partly due to the influence of pandemic). The research team is grateful for the timely RGC funding and believe the outputs generated from this project have enriched the knowledge base of systemic improvement and system leadership in China. The four objectives listed in the project proposal have been fully achieved. Objective 1 The study so far has investigated the role of these leaders: the head/executive principal of education groups; school principals, expert teachers or jiaoyanyuan as cross-school instructional leaders, hosts of Master Teacher/Principal studios. We have generated three sets of findings about the role of different levels of leadership in systemic improvement in China. The first set of findings explores the role of these leaders as boundary spanners. Boundary spanners are individuals who connect different communities of practice and broker relations between these communities. We have examined and reported the boundary-spanning practices of three types of leaders in China – the head principal of an education group; expert teachers; and district-level jiaoyanyuan. The study shows how these leaders mobilized resources within the school networks. The second set of findings explores how these leaders commit staff in their own and other schools to the improvement of teaching and learning and enhance their peers’ professional capital. The emphasis is to explore system leaders as lateral, inter-school leaders who promote collaborative, peer-to-peer networks. We have mainly focused on these two groups of leaders – hosts of Master Teacher Studios (MTSs) and Master Principal Studios (MPSs). We have explored and reported how they enhanced these peers’ capacity and professional capital via their role-modelling and personal charisma. The third set of findings attempt to depict the role of system leadership in a more holistic and synthesised way. To develop a holistic understanding of where these leaders lead, what distinguish them as leaders and how they influence peers, we have tried to explore their role from the perspective of different forms of capital and how they accumulate their human, social and symbolic capital. Objective 2 We have committed considerable efforts to decoding the complexities of the education system and the socio-political context in China. Concerning the education system, it has its own sets of distinctive educational infrastructures which facilitate interactions across communities of practices. The key features include a widely used school network mechanism to bring schools together; a well-structured and multiple-tiered teacher learning system; a tiered expertise ‘ladder’ acknowledging expert teachers at school, district and municipal/provincial levels; a system which provides expert teachers with incentives for taking on leadership responsibilities and dedicated posts. We explored the recent ‘Double Reduction’ (shuangjian) policy development and impact of the guiding goal of ‘common prosperity’ (gongtong fuyu) on schools. Concerning the socio-political and cultural context, the top-down, centralized system has both strengths and limitations, thus creating conditions and causing tensions for system leaders to exert their roles at the same time. Enabling conditions include policy-driven standards, the roles created to support teacher learning and shared responsibilities for collective learning in China. However, the same hierarchically-structured system also creates obstacles to building collective efficacy and constructing communities of professional learners. For example, there appears an over-reliance on government policies and mandates. System leaders tend to follow the directions of those above them in the hierarchy. The complexities of the Chinese system have been explored in our journal publications. Objective 3 The project proposed to develop four to six rich case studies. We have identified four themes of systemic improvement initiatives and included six case studies. Theme 1: School consortium/education groups (jiaoyu jituan). The first group of cases are about system leaders in education groups. We have examined two cases in Guizhou and Shenzhen. The first is an education group in Dushan, Guizhou and engaged the head principal of the education group as the key research participant. He built shared knowledge about instruction in the different schools and cultivated collective responsibility for student learning across the schools. The second is a larger education group with nine schools in Nanshan District, Shenzhen. It has created education group-level leadership positions to coordinate the teacher learning and student development resources across schools. The initial findings also inspired us to further explore education groups and juxtapose them with other similar school consortiums in the Greater Bay Area (GBA). We have developed a new GRF proposal which was submitted in 2023. Theme 2: Networked professional learning communities (PLCs). This theme also includes two cases, one is networked teacher PLC in Shanghai and the other is a networked principal PLC in Guizhou. The Shanghai case selected one expert teacher who is simultaneously a mentee of a municipal-level MTS, a district-level MTS mentor, and a subject leader in his district. The Guizhou case includes provincial-level master principal, county-level or district-level master principals and extended members who are junior principals or school leaders as the apprentices. Theme 3: District level teaching research officers (jiaoyanyuan). We developed a case in Shanghai where we focus on the leadership role played by formal teacher leaders. As our key participant, we selected one jiaoyanyuan and collected data from her peer teachers and colleagues. This jiaoyanyuan connected local education bureaus with individual schools and teachers and translated reform principles into classroom practices. Theme 4: Master Teacher Studios (MTSs). For this theme, we mainly focus on the role of the hosts of the MTSs and collected data from more than ten hosts and their mentees in Zhejiang Province. In these MTSs, the mentees were intentionally selected from different schools as a systemic improvement effort to close the gaps between high and low performing schools. Objective 4 A major purpose of the study was to delineate implications of system reform and system leadership for Hong Kong and other societies. This has been achieved through these pathways: The first pathway was to synthesise leadership practices in China and explicitly discuss the implications for other societies. For example, we have also synthesised leadership practices, including system leadership, in a UNESCO report. The second pathway has been various keynote talks the PI has given over the past few years in ICSEI, Education Summit (Chile), Beijing Normal University, and IPDA Conference (UK) to disseminate the research findings. The third pathway was to spread the research findings through knowledge transfer activities with HK school leaders. The PI has been a director of two EDB leader development programmes and also involved in teaching local vice principals and English Schools Foundation (ESF) school leaders. The PI has used the opportunities to introduce the systemic improvement initiatives and system leadership practices in China to accumulatively more than 4,000 HK local and international school leaders.

18605520.label: Major findings and research outcome
18605520.value: The study explored the role of system leaders in various system-wide reform initiatives in Mainland China. The data was collected from four types of systemic reforms (specifically six cases) and more than 60 research participants including head principals, principals, hosts of MTSs and MPSs, expert teachers, jiaoyanyuan as well as their mentees. Specifically, the study explored head principals of education groups who connect and mobilise resources within the group (Output 1 & 5); expert teachers who connect different layers of teacher learning communities (Output 3); jiaoyanyuan who connect classroom teaching across the district (Output 1 & 3); hosts of MPSs and MTSs who connect mentee teachers/principals and promote their collective capacity (Output 4, 6 & 7). These various system leaders span professional, organisational and other boundaries to lead and sustain system reform in China. They share a lot of characteristics as indicated in the international literature. They actively lead improvements in other schools; commit teachers in their own and other schools to the improvement of teaching and learning; lead the development of schools as PLCs; and manage strategically the impact on the classroom, school and system. Despite the similarities, the specific cultural and socio-political context in China plays a role in shaping context-specific system reform and system leadership in China. The key features of system reforms in China include: • Combine bottom-up initiatives with top-down support; • Invest heavily in teachers’ professional learning and promote models of collaborative enquiry; • Establish mechanisms for expert teachers to network across schools; • Take exceptionally skilled teachers out of their classrooms, and appoint them as mingshi or jiaoyanyuan to spread their influence across classrooms. A set of enabling conditions to frame leaders’ ability to exert their system leadership role rest heavily on the system-provided education infrastructure (Output 2, 5 & 7). This includes top-down and centralised education system that enables a high degree of coherence between policy and implementation; the various roles maximised by the system to support teacher learning; a shared belief that continuous personal development is an indispensable duty of all teachers; and the traditional Chinese values of collectivism. At the same time, the system has created tensions accompanying system leaders’ activities. These include the tension between the centre (more powerful and visible individuals) and periphery (less powerful and visible individuals); between expanded responsibility and professional power of these leaders; and between diversity and homogeneity (the tendency to reproduce or scale up existing good practices).

18605520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18605520.value: More research is needed to explore how system leadership at macro and micro levels works across different contexts. This includes how different political and cultural systems can shape infrastructures to support cross-school learning and how both systems themselves and the professionals comprising the system can be rewired to work effectively across different educational settings. In view of this need, a new GRF proposal entitled ‘An exploration of school networks and system leadership in the GBA’ was submitted in 2023. This study proposes to explore the nature of two school networks selected from different school systems in the GBA - an education group in Shenzhen and a long-serving international school network in Hong Kong. The study also proposes to adopt a mixture of methods – social network analysis and qualitative interviews. The initial findings about the school networks in Mainland China also inspired the PI to reflect on this question: Will it be possible to include Hong Kong schools in these networks to form reciprocal improvement communities? A RIF (Research Impact Fund) was developed to propose improving schools through networking in the GBA in 2023. The proposal got very positive comments and indicated it would be a promising research area.

18605520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18605520.value: The past two decades have witnessed an increasing global interest in promoting school-to-school collaboration and cross-school professional learning communities. What is rarely known internationally is that Mainland China has been implementing many of such improvement initiatives at a large scale. These include forming schools into consortiums (education groups); mobilising expert teachers to be cross-school teacher leaders; elevating outstanding teachers to be jiaoyanyuan to connect more classrooms; and adopting mechanisms such as Master Principal Studios (MPSs) and Master Teacher Studios (MTSs) to develop capacity of educators at different levels in more schools. This study has explored these improvement initiatives as cases (six cases) and the role played by various leaders, i.e., system leaders, in these initiatives. The data has been collected from over 60 research participants in Shanghai, Guizhou, Zhejiang and Shenzhen. This study has contributed rich case scenarios of system reform in China and expanded international understandings of system leadership. Many of the findings have been disseminated in academic outputs, in various leader development programmes in Hong Kong and keynote talks in international conferences. The Chinese cases have expanded international understandings of systemic improvement and system leadership.

18605720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18605720.value: Defined as “a temporary, controlled field-trial of a policy-relevant innovation that produces evidence for subsequent policy decisions” (Jordan & Huitema 2014), policy experiments are pervasive in contemporary policy process, playing a pivotal role in generating policy innovations, and driving incremental institutional transformations (Heilmann 2008a; Roland 2000). Policy experimentation is one of the defining characteristics of the Chinese style of governance. It is widely acknowledged that the extensive use of experimentation copes well with the enormous regional disparities in this large country, and effectively contains risks in the face of uncertainties (Heilmann 2008b, 2009). Steered by central authorities, sub-national governments are given substantial autonomy to undertake policy experiments based on local circumstances. When new policy solutions are believed to be applicable in other places, a host of diffusional mechanisms will take them to other localities, and possibly scale up to the entire country (Husain 2017; Zhu 2017). Therefore, experimentalist governance in China does not constitute solely of policy experimentation, but also entails possible inter-regional diffusion of innovations. Despite the wealth of literature on policy experimentation in China, notable gaps remain. First, the literature predominantly focuses on developmental areas, especially economic policies, while the dynamics of experimentation in the social policy sphere are much less known. It has been recognized that social policy innovation and diffusion may operate on a very distinct set of logics (Shi 2012; Zhu & Zhao 2017). Second, many previous studies were conducted in the form of single-locality case studies, lacking necessary power of generalizability due to small sample size. Third, the use of single case studies often takes a static view and fails to account for the longitudinal dynamics of policy experimentation and diffusion. This study seizes upon an ideal “lab”, China’s public hospital reform, to explain the logic and dynamics of health policy experimentation in an authoritarian state. Commencing in 2010, this large-scale nationwide experimental program is built on multi-phase and multi-level recursive experimentation, with the participation of nearly 200 Chinese cities. A wide range of experimental modalities and policy instruments are observed. Built on a mixed-methods research design, this study seeks to explain social policy innovation and diffusion in China’s public hospital reforms. Upon completion, this project will enrich theoretical knowledge on policy experimentation in authoritarian systems, and update scholarly understanding on the approaches of governance in contemporary China, especially in Xi’s era. 政策試驗廣泛存在於當代公共政策過程之中，它旨在培育解決現實世界政策難題的創新方案，因而在公共政策創新和制度變革中扮演重要角色。政策試驗亦是當代中國管治風格的顯著特徵之一。眾所周知，中國政府長期仰賴政策試點解決公共政策難題，鼓勵政策創新。雖然中央政府居中指導，但地方政府亦有相當大的自主權因地制宜，尋求適應本地情況之政策方案。當政策試點培育出可行方案，中央政府便不遺餘力地將其推廣至全國，從而上升為國家政策。在中國亦有一系列的政策擴散機制，讓一個地方的創新能夠擴散至其他地區。因此，中國的試驗性管治不僅包含政策試驗，亦包含了跨地區的創新擴散。儘管關於中國的政策試驗研究已經相當豐碩，但仍有明顯不足。首先，目前之文獻主要聚焦於經濟發展領域之政策，而對社會政策領域如何進行政策試點和擴散則知之甚少。越來越多的學者意識到，社會政策領域的試驗性管治有其一套非常不同之邏輯。其次，過往之研究大多以一地之個案研究形式呈現，缺乏必要的代表性和推論力。第三，個案研究容易以靜態之視角觀察試驗，而不易捕捉動態之長期試驗過程和擴散機制。本研究立足於一個非常理想之『試驗場』——中國公立醫院改革，並試圖解釋威權國家醫療政策試驗和創新的基本邏輯。這項全國範圍內的改革試點開始於2010年，並具有多階段、多層次的反复性特徵，前前後後有多達200座城市參加，規模龐大。在十年的改革試點中，許多不同的改革方式和政策工具不斷湧現。本研究採用混合研究方法，試圖闡明中國公立醫院改革創新和擴散的機制。研究完成之後，將會深化對威權國家政策試驗的理論闡釋，並幫助學界更好地理解當代中國政府管治的新特點。

18605720.label: Realisation of objectives
18605720.value: This project has realized the research objectives laid out in the proposal in a highly satisfactory manner, producing six research articles in leading international and national journals and one conference presentation. Significant efforts were made to overcome the difficulties created by the Covid-19 pandemic, especially those afflicting fieldwork. The research team fully explored secondary resources and managed to conduct a good number of interviews through online means. Both qualitative methods and quantitative methods were extensively used. We also experimented the use of large-N qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) method in public policy setting (article published in Governance) and comparative case studies (article published in Policy Sciences). Both outputs have yielded considerable methodological value. Within a very short period of time, the four publications in the English language have already registered more than a dozen of citations. We expect greater scholarly impact in the years to come. The article published in Health Policy and Planning has attracted keen attention of a US-based think tank which is approaching the PI for expert consultation, further reflecting the impact of this project. This project as a whole has well characterized and explained the mechanisms of the multi-phase multi-locality experimental program of China’s public hospital reform (Objective #1). Our key research outputs have rigorously explained the adoption of various innovational modalities in the experimental program (Objective #2). Both comparative case studies and the QCA method have let us explain versatile policy learning and policy diffusional mechanisms across localities in this experimental program (Objective #3). The six research outputs as whole have updated scholarly knowledge on policy experimentation in authoritarian China in the social policy sphere (Objective #4), and have drawn policy implications for experimentalist governance in China and other countries (Objective #5). We sincerely thank the RGC for funding this exciting project. We are delighted that the project has come to fruition amidst an unprecedented global pandemic.

18605720.label: Major findings and research outcome
18605720.value: Major findings arising from this project are reported in the six research outputs. In "Seeking policy solutions in a complex system: experimentalist governance in China’s healthcare reform" (published in Policy Sciences), we have characterized China's public hospital experimental program as a dynamic form of experimental governance. Four distinctive modalities of experimentation are identified, all associated with policy learning and diffusional mechanisms. In "Unpack the black box of pilot sampling in policy experimentation: A qualitative comparative analysis of China's public hospital reform" (published in Governance), we used the QCA method to explain the underlying logic of pilot selection in the massive experimental program of public hospital reforms. Five distinctive pathways were revealed. We argue that piloting can serve as a versatile governance tool that can fulfill multiple functions in complex reforms. In "Scaling-up through piloting: dual-track provider payment reforms in China’s health system" (published in Health Policy and Planning), we focus on the piloting program of provider payment mechanisms and examine how the central state manages the complex reform task and scales up innovations through dual track experimentation. In "Active stewardship in healthcare: Lessons from China's health policy reforms" (published in Social Policy and Administration), we zoom out to trace the macro development of China's health system reform and explain how experimentalist governance, political will, and policy capacity combine to foster active stewardship in the health sector with Chinese characteristics. This paper also seeks to offer policy implications for the vast developing world in their health system reforms. In the two research articles published in the Chinese language, we illustrate the mechanisms of experimentalist governance in the health sector, and the piloting program of provider payment reforms.

18605720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18605720.value: 1. Our successful trial of large-N QCA inspires to carry on this methodological innovation to other related policy settings. 2. Experimentalist governance as illustrated in this project appears to be a flexible pathway toward addressing social problems in a complex system. We will continue to examine it in other policy domains that may advance scholarly understanding on policy and governance.

18605720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18605720.value: Governance in the contemporary world faces a multitude of challenges, all requiring more adaptive and inclusive public policies. Experimentalist governance has arisen as a distinct paradigm of governance in which experimenting units try out a variety of methods and processes to find innovative solutions to predefined policy problems. The extensive use of policy experiments is one of the defining attributes of China’s success in economic reforms, Good experimentalist governance will not only continue to be crucial for the country’s socioeconomic development, but also offer valuable lessons for developing countries in their efforts of improving quality of governance. This project analyzes China’s massive public hospital reform to explain the logic and dynamics of health policy experimentation in an authoritarian state. Extensively using qualitative and quantitative methods, this project explains the dynamics of policy innovation and diffusion in China's public hospital reform, and enriches scholarly knowledge on policy experimentation in an authoritarian system.

18606920.label: Project Objectives
18606920.value: The proposed study will evaluate the impact of a unique intervention programme, the ECE Peace Ambassador Project (ECE-PAP), in reducing bullying in the early childhood years. To provide a rigorous test of the programme efficacy, a randomized controlled trail, with pre-test, post-test, and three-month follow-up assessments will be conducted. The specific objectives of the project will be: To investigate the impact of the ECE Peace Ambassador Project (ECE-PAP) on children’s emotional intelligence and social skills. It is hypothesized that children who completed the ECE-PAP training, compared to children who did not receive the training, will significantly improve on the five major components of emotional intelligence: a) understanding the emotions of the self and others (in the role of victimizer, victim and bystander); b) managing their emotions (e.g. anger and frustration) through increased self-regulation using positive coping strategies; c) taking the initiative to reduce bullying behaviour in others; d) showing empathy towards others; and e) using social skills to maintain good relationships with their peers. To examine the impact of ECE-PAP on children’s conflict resolution strategies. It is hypothesized that peace ambassadors, compared with children who did not receive the training, will significantly improve in using a greater variety of positive coping strategies (e.g. positive problem solving, seeking social support, positive thinking skills) to cope with bullying behaviour. To analyse the impact of ECE-PAP on children’s peer relationships. It is hypothesized that peace ambassadors, compared to children who did not receive the training, will show more prosocial behaviour with peers and less bullying behaviour. Children who have been through the training will also show fewer negative emotions (e.g. worried, distressed) in the context of peer relationships and will be less likely to be excluded by their peers. To refine and further develop the intervention programme (ECE-PAP) based on the findings of the study.

18606920.value: 這項研究是其中一項最早研究如何減少亞洲學齡前兒童之攻擊行為的研究。以下是一位家長在研討會上所闡述兒童之間欺凌行為的真實個案。 「我兒子今年8歲，患有抑鬱症。我們之前一直不知道他從一年級開始就被一群高年級學生欺負。那些高年級學生在小休時，扮成歹徒推撞並威脅他。操場上其他的孩子只充當了局外人，沒有提供任何幫助。我兒子沒有告訴我或老師這件事。有可能的話，他就在小息的時候躲到廁所裡。一直到他精神崩潰了，我們才知道這件事。我可憐的孩子遭受了整整兩年的欺凌。我真希望在他入學前能有一個課程來教他如何應對欺凌行為。」 由於儒家哲學中強調同齡人之間的和諧，中國的兒童很容易把與欺凌有關的挫折掩藏起來（Tam＆Taki，2007）。研究表明身體和語言欺凌在學齡前普遍存在（Alsaker＆Nägele，2008； Repo＆Sajaniemi，2015），而且，該問題在香港的學校中日益突出（Wong，2004）。此研究將調查「兒童和平大使計劃」在減少兒童早期欺凌行為方面的效力。首先，本研究旨在探討「兒童和平大使計劃」對兒童在如下幾個方面的影響：一）理解自我和他人的情緒；二）管理情緒的應對策略；三）減少欺凌行為的動機；四）對待別人的同理心；五）使用社交技能維持同輩間的良好關係。其次，本研究旨在根據研究結果，進一步發展和完善干預方案。參加者包括16所幼稚園的320名5歲至6歲的兒童及老師，這些幼稚園來自香港具有各種社會經濟地位家庭的地區。 本研究將通過測試兒童在處理早期欺凌行為，及預防和阻止同伴欺凌時的情緒智力（EI）和應對策略的效果，以期為反欺凌的研究計劃提供新的理論貢獻。

18606920.label: Realisation of objectives
18606920.value: This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of a SEL program - the ECE-Peace Ambassador project (ECEPAP) on children’s use of emotional intelligence skills to deal with bullying. The impact of each of the social and emotional competence in the framework of emotional intelligence (EI) on children’s ability to reduce bullying was investigated. The current study was composed of 3 groups of participants from: (1) 302 children (166 boys, 136 girls) aged from 5 to 6 years old (M =5.4, SD = 0.4); (2) 32 teachers; (3) 227 parents with 23 fathers and 204 mothers. All of the children were recruited from different socio-economic status (SES) families and kindergartens (16) in the city of Hong Kong. Using multiple reporters (child interviews, parents and teachers reports), assessments of children’s emotional competence, coping strategies, and aggressive behaviour were assessed using validated instruments the week before the programme starts (Time 1), the week after completion of the programme (Time 2), and three months later (Time 3). Questionnaires were given to all participating teachers and parents at different time phases of the study (Time 1-3). The questionnaire of the teacher was comprised of three parts: (1) Child Behavior Scale (CBS); (2) Teacher Rating Scale of Emotional Intelligence in Children; and (3) Child Strategies for confronting bulling. Regarding Objective 1: The impact of ECE-PAP on children’s emotional intelligence skills. According to teachers’ reports, the mixed model analysis yielded a significant condition by time interaction. Additional follow-up analyses showed that teachers ratings of children’s emotional intelligence in the experimental condition significantly increased from pretest to posttest and remained higher at follow-up. The two conditions did not differ on the emotional labeling scores at Time 1. However, the condition by time interaction was significant, with only children in the experimental condition showing significant increases in correctly label emotions in pictures from pretest to posttest--increases that were maintained at follow-up. Children in both conditions showed increases in successfully labeling emotions of others in different situations over time, as reflected in the significant time main effect, F(2,513.80) = 6.28, p < .01, and the nonsignificant condition by time interaction, F(2,513.92) = 0.47, n.s. Three effects were significant for the child report measures. In classrooms devoting a greater number of weeks to the curriculum, children scored higher on the emotion labeling task and were less likely to report that they would yell or push another child in response to bullying. Follow-up analyses of teachers’ report showed that although the control condition showed no changes over time, children in the experimental condition showed an increase in taking action and a decrease in avoidance from pretest to posttest. Both of these changes were sustained at follow-up. In response to the open-ended question at pretest about how their child would respond to bullying, a greater percentage of parents of children in the experimental condition mentioned that their child would take action than parents of children in the control condition, F(1,207) = 10.04, p < .01. There were no program effects on children’s overall empathy or emotion situation knowledge, possibly because these may be hard to change within a short intervention period (3 to 10 weeks), and they may have to do more with general cognitive development. Regarding Objective 2: The impact of ECE-PAP on children’s conflict resolution strategies. Numerous effects were significant (or marginally significant) for the number of weeks to complete the program variable (particularly for the teacher and child report outcomes—no effects were significant for the parent report outcomes). Findings showed that classrooms where the program was implemented over a larger number of weeks had children with better outcomes. Specifically, weeks to program completion was positively associated with more positive child strategies generated by teachers in response to the open-ended questions—higher levels of children taking action and seeking help and lower levels of avoidance and anger/aggression. Regarding Objective 3: Impact of ECE-PAP on children’s prosocial and aggressive behavior. Findings showed that classrooms where the program was implemented over a larger number of weeks had children with better outcomes. Specifically, weeks to program completion was positively associated with teacher ratings of prosocial behavior (e.g. offers help, recognizes peer’s feelings, concerned about others’ distress, kind toward peers, cooperative with peers). The anger/aggression measure (response to open-ended questions) did show a significant effect in the McNemar analyses. A dichotomous variable was created for this analysis with two levels: 0) no aggressive strategy was mentioned in any of the three hypothetical bullying situations and 1) the child mentioned an anger/aggressive strategy at least once across the three situations. A chi-square analysis of this dichotomous measure revealed no differences between the experimental and control conditions at pretest, X2(1) = 0.56, n.s. However, the McNemar test was significant for children in the control condition when comparing pretest and follow-up, p < .05. For children in the control condition, the percentage of children showing increases in anger/aggression from pretest to posttest was greater than the percentage of children showing decreases. There were no significant changes on this variable for children in the experimental condition. Regarding Objective 4: Refine and further develop the intervention programme (ECE-PAP) based on the findings of the study. Based on feedback from the participating teachers and findings of the study, the intervention program (ECEPAP teachers’ guide) were revised and published, copies of the teachers’ guide were delivered to 784 local kindergartens. Remaining 16 copies were were sent to the Central Library, university library and ECE educators.

18606920.label: Major findings and research outcome
18606920.value: This study aims at helping 5-year-olds to develop emotional intelligence skills and strategies to cope with bullying. It did so by implementing an anti-bullying interventions (ECE-PAP) in the Asian context during the outbreak of Covid-19. Mixed models analyses (controlling for child age, child gender, and teacher years of experience) showed that despite the numerous differences between children in the experimental and control conditions at pretest, all but one of these differences disappeared at posttest and were no longer significant at follow-up as well. Specifically, from pretest to posttest, children in the experimental group showed increases in emotional intelligence (teacher questionnaire) and actions to stop the bullying (teacher ratings and open-ended responses), and showed decreases in avoidance (teacher open-ended responses). Moreover, children in the experimental condition showed increases in their emotion labelling accuracy (control children did not show a corresponding increase). Although teacher, parent, and child reports showed that aggression occurred with low frequency in this sample, nonparametric analyses showed positive effects of the program on children’s aggression. Teacher reports of aggression showed that only the experimental group showed significant changes over time, with the percentage of children showing any aggression decreasing from pretest to posttest and pretest to follow-up. Analyses of the effect of implementation variables on child outcomes showed that although the number of lessons completed did not predict child outcomes (possibly due to insufficient variability), the number of weeks devoted to the program did. Specifically, implementing the program over a greater number of weeks was associated with more positive child outcomes: more prosocial behavior (teacher reports), greater emotion labeling (child task), more taking action (teacher open-ended), more help-seeking (teacher open-ended), less avoidance (teacher open-ended), and less anger/ aggression (teacher open-ended, child ratings and open-ended). Future studies should implement the ECE-PAP program in more than 4 weeks, in order to effectively decrease children’s anger/aggression. Recent studies had reported positive association of bullying, mental health problems and peer problems among children and Covid-19 (e.g. Forsberg & Thorvalden, 2022; Joo & Lee, 2022; Liu et al, 2020; Ravens-Sieberer et al., 2022). The present study had shown positive association of intervention program (ECE-PAP) in increasing children’s prosocial behaviour, labelling of emotions and taking action to cope with bullying; and decreasing frustration, aggression and use of avoidance to cope with bullying during the Covid-19 pandemic.

18606920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18606920.value: The present study had shown positive association of intervention program (ECE-PAP) in increasing children’s prosocial behaviour, labelling of emotions and taking action to cope with bullying; and decreasing aggression and use of avoidance to cope with bullying. By reducing bullying in the classroom, teacher satisfaction and retention should increase, and all children will benefit from a more positive classroom and school climate. Fewer school resources will need to be devoted to addressing student problem behaviour, and more time can be devoted to education and learning. An ECEPAP teachers’ guide had been published and sent to local kindergartens, public library and ECE educators. In order to increase awareness of the problem of bullying in early childhood settings, as well as greater attention directed towards this issue; ECEPAP teachers’ trainings should be provided widely in the community in the future, teachers should be involved as researchers to further refine the development of preschool anti-bullying programmes and resources. Based on findings of the present study, the research team can further provide consultant services to preschools and governments on implementing and evaluating ECE-PAP in preschools. These changes would have economic, social, and moral consequences for children, adolescents, and adults in Hong Kong and other Asian settings.

18606920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18606920.value: Children showed increases in emotional intelligence and behaviors to stop the bullying (and showed decreases in avoidance after joining the social emotional learning activities in the the ECE-Peace Ambassador project (ECEPAP). Moreover, evidence had shown that the ECEPAP activities had enhanced children’s ability to label emotion accurately (children who did not join the ECEPAP project did not show a corresponding increase). Finally, although teacher, parent, and child reports showed that aggression occurred with low frequency in participating children, there were positive effects of the program on children’s aggression. Teacher reports of aggression showed that children’s aggressive behavior decreased after joining the ECEPAP project. Analyses of the effect of implementation variables on child outcomes showed that teachers implementing the program over a greater number of weeks was associated with more positive child outcomes: more prosocial behavior, greater emotion labeling, more actions were taken to stop bullying, more help-seeking, less avoidance, and less anger/ aggression. In sum, the present study had shown positive association of intervention program (ECE-PAP) in increasing children’s prosocial behaviour, labelling of emotions and taking actions to cope with bullying; and decreasing frustration, aggression and use of avoidance to cope with bullying during the Covid-19 pandemic.
