18612420.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612420.value: A study of the Chinese language movement and the defending Diaoyutai movement offers us an opportunity for us to understand: i) why Hong Kong’s young generation growing up in the 1950s and 1960s became critical of the older generation’s aloofness and began an exploration of their identity of being Chinese living under British colonial governance after the two major social conflicts in the mid-1960s; ii) why these young then turned to the Chinese language movement and defending Diaoyutai movement, both of them were mainly nationalist in terms of their orientation and outlook, instead of articulating a local agenda of social reform; iii) how did these two social movements express their nationalist sentiments and orientation; iv) why many college students further turned to patriotism after the defending Diaoyutai movement; and v) why other college students either turned to radical ideology (e.g., anarchism or Trotskyist Marxism) or became activists for social reforms with a local agenda. Gradually by the end of the 1970s, patriotism, reformism, and radicalism came to constitute the three main strands of political perspectives prior to Hong Kong’s encounter with the question of its political future after Governor MacLehose visited Beijing in 1979. What drove young people to support the Chinese language campaign was mainly nationalist sentiment. This was more evident in the defending Diaoyutai movement. It is argued that sentiments and perspective drawn from the May Fourth Movement of 1919 helped energize the mobilization. Parallels were drawn between the two movements, and the sense of national humiliation sparked nationalism and the eagerness to take action to defend the national territory. What followed was the ‘Know China’ campaign. Many college students espoused patriotism, seeing their engagement in Hong Kong as a way to promote an identification with the nation. The patriotic turn met opposition from other college students and young activists. Some took up radical political ideologies and confronted the colonial government. In terms of the number of participants, their size was small. Another segment of the young activists saw social reforms as a way to continue their social engagement. They found a sense of urgency in addressing local social problems. By the end of the 1970s, they became the main force behind the rise of pressure group politics. The main outcome of this project will be a Chinese book for general readers. The manuscript is 40% completed (see attachment).

18612420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612420.value: I have included a discussion of Taiwanese students’ engagement in the defending Diaoyutai movement when they studied in the USA. It serves as a case to support my argument of how historical memory (in my discussion, the May Fourth Movement) facilitates strong emotional response to a crisis. The Diaoyutai incident in 1970-1972 was perceived as another case of national humiliation and people were aroused and mobilized to collective action in order to ensure the national territory would be defended. Taiwanese students’ defending Diaoyutai movement in the USA also went through heated debates and a split of opinion. Some championed the course of a unified China and turned to identify with the People’s Republic of China. Some continued to support the Kuomintang. Others saw a need to promote changes and reforms in Taiwan. There were similarities and differences between Hong Kong’s and Taiwanese students defending Diaoyutai movement. The subsequent courses of development were constituted and constitutive of future political development in Hong Kong and Taiwan. A comparative study will enrich our understanding of political change and development, particularly in the period of the 1980s when drastic changes made significant impacts, in the two places.

18612420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612420.value: Contextualizing the Chinese language movement and the defending Diaoyutai movement in Hong Kong’s evolving social and political environment, this study shows why young people in the late 1960s espoused nationalism after a search for identity and a sense of belonging. Nationalism energized the young college students, and they found their role in defending the national territory in a political environment just recovering from the 1967 Riots. It is important to recognize the role of nationalism in shaping social movements in post-war Hong Kong. While some of those nationalists further went on to embrace patriotism and turned to identify with the People’s Republic of China, other activists turned to radicalism and social reform. The latter played their parts in negotiating for new spaces of political participation under colonial governance. By the end of the 1970s, pressure group politics came to define the parameters of political life in the colonial setting.

21100420.label: Project Objectives
21100420.value: To develop a novel method to simultaneously identify lncRNA binding RBPs and the genomic binding sites of the RNA-protein complex in living human cells. Delineating the protein network associated with long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is fundamental to understanding the functional mechanisms of lncRNAs. Current methods to identify lncRNA binding proteins and associated DNA either rely on crosslinking mediated complex co-precipitation or require extensive molecular engineering, leading to drawbacks such as loss of cellular context and low capture efficiency, and limiting their broad application. To circumvent the limitations and detect RBPs that bind to endogenous lncRNA transcripts in living cells, we developed a CRISPR-Assisted RNA-Protein Interaction Detection method (CARPID), a novel strategy to identify RBPs of lncRNA molecules in living cells. CARPID leverages the RNA-targeting CRISPR/CasRx system to navigate an engineered promiscuous biotin ligase (BASU) to biotinylate RBPs of a specific lncRNA under physiological conditions. This enables the subsequent enrichment and analysis by quantitative mass spectrometry. CARPID has advantages in several aspects: 1) the experiments are conducted in a living condition without small molecule or UV-mediated crosslinking; 2) CRISPR/CasRx equipped with specific guide RNAs are exploited to target multiple loci of a given RNA transcript; 3) for each locus, two adjacent guide RNAs are simultaneously employed to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio. To establish an hESC platform to study the RBPs and the genomic binding of HERV-H. Recently, a primate-specific endogenous retrotransposon human endogenous retrovirus subfamily H (HERV-H) has been found playing a role in creating topologically associating domains (TADs) in hPSCs. The capability of creating TAD boundaries depends on high transcription of HERV-H. However, no molecular mechanism has been identified, although Cohesin was suggested as a potential candidate to mediate the formation of TADs. Therefore, we propose to apply CARPID to HERV-H in human embryonic stem cells to identify the associated proteins and genomic loci, aiming to fine-map the molecular mechanism of HERV-H driven TAD formation. In order to achieve this goal, we first need to establish an hESC line stably expressing the components of CARPID. Such system will allow us to apply CARPID to investigate the dynamics of binding proteins as well as its genomic associating loci of any lncRNA, including HERV-H transcript, in hESC and during cellular differentiation. To investigate the dynamics of RBPs and genomic binding sites of HERV-H during cellular differentiation. Lentivirus will be employed to deliver gRNAs specifically targeting HERV-H transcript, which has been known critical for TAD formation and maintanence. CARPID will be applied to the cells established in Objective 2, 48 hour post-infection. Proteins will be identified by MS, and DNA will be sequenced using BGI-seq to identify its genomic associating loci. These information are important clues for us to understand how HERV-H RNA is involved in creating TAD boundaries. Furthermore, such strategy could also be broadly applied to other distinct classes of repetitive elements in a broad range of cell types, ultimately depicting their potential function in genome organization.

21100420.value: 如果將三米長的染色質纖維折疊成高階結構，便可以將它們存放于哺乳動物細胞中幾微米大小的細胞核內。染色質高級結構可以將相聚較遠的DNA片段在空間上相互接觸和交換信息，這對于轉錄調控至關重要。例如，增強子（壹種用于基因表達的順式調控元件）可以通過染色質遠程相互作用激活目標基因啓動子，從而增強目標基因的表達 。然而，遠程染色質相互作用是如何調節的，我們還了解得很少。近年來，已經確定了壹些蛋白質分子在維持和組織染色質的高級結構中發揮作用。例如，結構蛋白（如CTCF和Cohesin）對于形成和維持自相互作用基因組片段（也稱爲拓撲關聯域）是必需的。最近，還發現另壹類叫做非編碼RNA的大分子，也可能具有調節拓撲關聯域結構的作用。科學家發現，靈長類動物特異的內源性H型逆轉錄病毒（HERV-H）是人類多能幹細胞拓撲關聯域形成和維持必不可少的元件。但是，HERV-H如何參與拓撲關聯域調節的分子途徑也沒有被清楚地揭示。 描繪與HERV-H RNA相互作用的蛋白質是了解HERV-H在各種生物學事件中分子機制的基礎。在本項目中，我們擬開發壹種可以同時檢測活細胞中HERV-H RNA結合蛋白以及其基因組結合位點的新方法。將這種方法應用于人類胚胎幹細胞及其衍生的心肌祖細胞和心肌細胞中的HERV-H，可爲我們揭示HERV-H如何參與調節染色質的高階結構提供線索。我們相信該項目的成果將讓我們能夠進壹步了解多能幹細胞分化過程中染色質3D結構調控的機理。同時，新技術還可以廣泛應用于揭示各個生物系統中非編碼RNA的功能。從長遠來看，這壹發現可能有益于臨床研究。例如，許多lncRNA已被用作診斷多種嚴重疾病（包括癌症）的生物標志物。理解這些lncRNA的分子功能無疑將幫助揭示相關疾病的致病途徑，並爲有效療法提供解決方案（例如尋找更好的藥物靶點）。

21100420.label: Realisation of objectives
21100420.value: Objective 1: To develop a novel method to simultaneously identify lncRNA binding RBPs and the genomic binding sites of the RNA-protein complex in living human cells. We developed a CRISPR-Assisted RNA-Protein Interaction Detection method (termed CARPID). We adopted a compact Type VI-D CRISPR single-effector system CasRx and use its nuclease activity free form (dCasRx) for specific lncRNA targeting. This dCasRx effector protein retains the capability of processing guide RNA (gRNA) arrays to two or more component gRNAs without cleaving targeted RNA transcripts. Taking this advantage, we can design a guide RNA array composed of two gRNA sequences spaced by a 30-nt direct repeat (DR) to target two adjacent loci on the same lncRNA transcript. This allows augmented targeting specificity and thus reduces background noise. To identify the RBPs bound to the target lncRNA, the dCasRx is fused with the engineered biotin ligase BASU. The BASU-dCasRx is in frame and co-expressed with a self-cleaving T2A peptide and an eGFP cDNA. The GFP signal will help to monitor and minimize the variation caused by heterogeneous expression of BASU enzyme among cells. To test the system, we designed gRNAs targeting lncRNA XIST in HEK293T cells. Since XIST is 19-kb long, we synthesized sgRNA targeting its L1 (pos: 1,804), L2 (pos: 6,326), and L3 (pos: 10,035) loci, respectively and using mock sgRNA as controls. Ultimately, identified 23 proteins significantly associated with all three regions (adjusted P<0.05, fold change >2.0). However, the CARPID system still heavily depends on the plasmid-mediated transfection of cells, which limits its applications in tissues and non-transfectable host. Therefore, we upgraded the CARPID method by directly applying proteins delivery. Briefly, we expressed the CARPID components, dCasRx-BASU, in E. coli and synthesized the sgRNAs for in vitro assembly of RNP (RNA-Protein) complex. To maximize the efficiency of protein labelling, we replaced dCasRx with a miniCas13 protein whose size is remarkably smaller (~49 kDa). Meanwhile, we also replaced BASU, a biotin ligase to APEX2 which is an engineered ascorbate peroxidase. Different from BASU, APEX2 can catalyse the oxidation of biotin-phenol at the presence of H2O2. The oxidized biotin-phenol will react with adjacent tyrosine and label the protein with biotin for subsequent purification with streptavidin-coated beads and identification with mass spectrometry. We termed the upgraded method CARPID2.0 and compared the results of XIST with those identified with CARPID. The result showed that a significant improvement over the original CARPID, which identified 31 proteins associated with the L1 locus near the 5’ region of XIST RNA. Using the same pair of guide RNAs, CARPID2.0 can now detect 306 significantly associated proteins. Of the original 31 XIST-associating proteins, 8 were recovered using the CARPID2.0 method. Additionally, we reconfirmed 65 known XIST-interacting proteins, including TAF15, which we previously characterized, as well as SPEN, hnRNPK, SAP18, PTBP1, and others identified by other researchers. Moreover, by leveraging the RNA labelling activity of APEX2, adjacent RNA can also be biotinylated. This enables us to conveniently evaluate the specificity of sgRNA in CARPID 2.0 using an RNA pull-down assay. Objective 2: To establish an hESC platform to study the RBPs and the genomic binding of HERV-H. Recently, a primate-specific endogenous retrotransposon human endogenous retrovirus subfamily H (HERV-H) has been found playing a role in creating topologically associating domains (TADs) in hPSCs. The capability of creating TAD boundaries depends on high transcription of HERV-H. However, no molecular mechanism has been identified, although Cohesin was suggested as a potential candidate to mediate the formation of TADs. Therefore, we propose to apply CARPID2.0 and ChIRP-seq to HERV-H RNA in human embryonic stem cells to identify the associated proteins and genomic loci, aiming to fine-map the molecular mechanism of HERV-H driven TAD formation. Using CARPID 2.0, we identified 252 proteins significantly associated with HERV-H1 RNA in hESCs, including many RNA-binding proteins as well as nuclear matrix proteins. We further validated the interaction between HERV-H RNA and hnRNPU (also known as SAF-A) using RIP-qPCR. Additionally, in situ fluorescent hybridization (FISH) imaging revealed that HERV-H RNA is abundant in the nuclear periphery, forming multiple bright foci that partially overlap with SAF-A protein, which is abundant near the nuclear envelope. These results suggest that HERV-H RNA may be associated with nuclear matrix and nuclear envelope proteins, potentially facilitating the organization of the high-order structure of chromatin. Interestingly, we also found that numerous HERV-H RNA-binding proteins are associated with ribosome biogenesis, a process closely linked to the maintenance of stemness in hESCs. To determine the genomic binding loci of HERV-H RNA, we conducted the ChIRP-seq assay. We first designed and validated a series of HERV-H RNA ChIRP-seq probes that demonstrated high specificity for enriching HERV-H RNA. The ChIRP-seq analysis revealed that the most substantial peaks displayed a stripe pattern, with the majority located at the HERV-H loci. For instance, the binding of transcriptionally active HERV-H1 RNA was observed at the LTR7 regions and the 5' gag region. In addition to the cis-binding of HERV-H RNA, we identified several trans binding sites, particularly in the rDNA regions and DUX4. Depletion of HERV-H RNA resulted in decreased ChIRP-seq signals, confirming the specific localization of HERV-H RNA at the HERV-H loci and rDNA regions. Objective 3: To investigate the dynamics of RBPs and genomic binding sites of HERV-H during cellular differentiation. Lentivirus will be employed to deliver gRNAs specifically targeting HERV-H transcript, which has been known critical for TAD formation and maintanence. CARPID will be applied to the cells established in Objective 2, 48 hour post-infection. Proteins will be identified by MS, and DNA will be sequenced using BGI-seq to identify its genomic associating loci. These information are important clues for us to understand how HERV-H RNA is involved in creating TAD boundaries. Furthermore, such strategy could also be broadly applied to other distinct classes of repetitive elements in a broad range of cell types, ultimately depicting their potential function in genome organization. Interestingly, the RBPs and genomic binding sites of HERV-H RNA in hESCs suggested that HERV-H RNA may play a critical role in ribosome biogenesis, which is essential for maintaining the pluripotency of stem cells. We then focused on studying the role of HERV-H RNA in ribosome biogenesis. Following the depletion of HERV-H RNA using shRNA or ASO, we observed a significant downregulation in the expression of pre-rRNA. Additionally, metabolic labeling of nascent RNA with 4sU confirmed the positive role of HERV-H RNA in pre-rRNA transcription. Further investigation into HERV-H RNA-binding proteins revealed that 49 of these proteins positively regulated pre-rRNA expression. These results suggested that both HERV-H RNA and its RBPs are involved in the regulation of pre-rRNA expression. HERV-H RNA was first discovered to function in ribosome biogenesis. To determine the molecular mechanism of HERV-H RNA in regulating pre-rRNA expression, we used an RNA-FISH assay to confirm the nucleolar localization of HERV-H RNA. Furthermore, ChIRP-qPCR assays confirmed the binding of HERV-H RNA to rDNA regions. To further elucidate the molecular mechanism of HERV-H RNA binding to the rDNA regions, we developed a novel SELEX method to identify the motif for HERV-H RNA and rDNA interaction. Finally, we identified two 9-bp motifs present in both HERV-H RNA and rDNA, which are likely crucial for the interaction between double-stranded rDNA and HERV-H RNA.

21100420.label: Major findings and research outcome
21100420.value: 1. Successful development of CARPID method and CARPID2.0 that can identify binding proteins of a specific RNA of interest CARPID fuses RNA targeting CRISPR dCasRx with the engineered biotin ligase BASU. Facilitated by a 30-nt guide RNA to target two adjacent loci on the same lncRNA transcript, CARPID can label the RNA binding proteins (RBP) bound to the target lncRNA with biotin, which allows subsequent identification of the RBPs. To upgrade CARPID with higher transfection and labelling efficiency, the dCasRx is replaced with miniCas13X with a smaller size and BASU is replaced with APEX2, which confers remarkable higher efficiency of protein labelling (~1 min). CARPID2.0 utilizes RNA-Protein (RNP) complex assembled in vitro, intead of episome-mediated transfection of cDNA, significantly increasing the efficiency and broadening applicablity. 2. HERV-H RNA regulates ribosome biogenesis in human embryonic stem cells essential for pluripotency and differentiation Employing the upgraded CARPID2.0 method, we identified 252 proteins associated with HERV-H RNA in human embryonic stem cells H9, with over 70% being ribosomal proteins. Further investigation into the role of HERV-H RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) revealed that both HERV-H RNA and 49 HERV-H RBPs positively regulate pre-rRNA expression. Additionally, taking advantage of ChIRP-seq and RNA-FISH, we demonstrated that HERV-H RNA was highly enriched in ribosomal DNA (rDNA) clusters, which supported the role of HERV-H RNA in transcription of pre-rRNA. And metabolic labeling of nascent RNA with 4sU further confirmed the positive role of HERV-H RNA in pre-rRNA transcription. Our findings suggest that HERV-H RNA and its associated proteins play a crucial role in ribosome biogenesis, a process closely linked to the maintenance of stemness. To further elucidate the molecular mechanism of HERV-H RNA in regulating pre-rRNA expression, we developed a novel SELEX method to identify the sequence motif involved in mediating the interaction between HERV-H RNA and rDNA loci. We identified two Alu motifs present in both HERV-H RNA and rDNA, which are confirmed crucial for the interaction between double-stranded rDNA and HERV-H RNA, suggesting a complex RNA:DNA:DNA triple helix was formed.

21100420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21100420.value: In this project, we developed two novel methods: CARPID2.0 and DNA-based RNA SELEX. CARPID2.0 can be widely applied to study the binding proteins of endogenous lncRNA in various living cells, while DNA-based RNA SELEX is suitable for screening the binding motifs between double-stranded DNA and single-stranded RNA in vitro. These two methods will be instrumental in elucidating the molecular mechanisms of lncRNA-mediated biological activities. The identification of HERV-H RNA and its associated proteins as key regulators of ribosome biogenesis in hESCs highlights the intricate relationship between non-coding RNAs and fundamental cellular processes. Further exploration could enhance our understanding of stem cell biology and the maintenance of pluripotency. Additionally, the motifs identified for HERV-H RNA and rDNA interaction provide a foundation for investigating the specific molecular interactions and regulatory mechanisms involved. This research could lead to broader insights into how retrotransposon-derived elements influence gene expression and cellular function. Furthermore, we aim to deepen our understanding of the molecular mechanisms HERV-H RNA-mediated ribosome biogenesis and pluripotency, and to translate these insights into therapeutic strategies for regenerative medicine and cancer treatment.

21100420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21100420.value: In this project, we explored the role of HERV-H RNA in human embryonic stem cells using cutting-edge techniques, including two new methods we developed: CARPID2.0 and DNA-based RNA SELEX. CARPID2.0 let us identify which proteins bind to HERV-H RNA molecule inside the embryonic stem cells. DNA-based RNA SELEX helped us pinpoint the exact DNA sequence, to which the HERV-H RNA molecule bound. Using these methods, we discovered that HERV-H RNA and its associated proteins played a significant role in producing pre-rRNAs, which are essential for creating ribosomes—the cell's protein production machinery. This process is crucial for maintaining pluripotency of human embryonic stem cells, allowing them to generate a high quantity of proteins, ready for differentiation upon receiving specific signals. Our research highlights the important roles of HERV-H RNA in an essential cellular processes. By understanding these roles, we gain insights into stem cell biology, potentially leading to advances in regenerative medicine and treatments for various diseases.

21201420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201420.value: Low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) communication technologies have emerged as a viable alternative to cellular and short-range wireless technologies to fulfill the diverse requirements of Internet of Things (IoT) applications. LPWAN technologies provide unique features that legacy wireless technologies do not yet offer, including wide-area connectivity for low-power and low data rate devices, at the cost of ultra-low bandwidth and long packet airtime. The new technology provides tremendous opportunities for the development of IoT; however, it also presents substantial potential risks. Recent studies have revealed many security vulnerabilities in LPWAN, and the lesson from Internet technology is that ignoring security at the outset leads to huge pain when the technology becomes ubiquitous. Motivated by this, the overall goal of this project is to advance the fundamental understanding of these emerging security concerns in LPWAN and to propose corresponding solutions. Specifically, we have two concrete research tasks in this project: secret key generation and secure code dissemination. In Task 1, we will investigate novel channel features and key generation schemes that can improve key generation rates significantly. In Task 2, we will design a secure over-the-air code dissemination protocol for LPWAN-based IoT, which includes a secure and energy-efficient protocol based on a multicast communication primitive, as well as a new encryption primitive to minimize the energy and memory consumption of constrained IoT devices. However, non-trivial research challenges must be surmounted if this goal is to be achieved. The unique features of LPWAN—namely, ultra-low bandwidth and long packet airtime, create new challenges for secure communication protocols. This project will address these challenges and investigate important aspects of LPWAN security that are poorly understood today. This project is timely because the need to safely manage critical infrastructure is urgent. There is now broad acceptance of IoT technology in our daily life, and security attacks on our cyberspace and IoT devices are escalating. The expected contributions from this work include new theories, methods and system mechanisms that will form the basis for a novel robust and energy-efficient framework to enable secure communication in LPWAN. The new techniques described here will provide better security features for the growing number of LPWAN-based IoT devices globally, and the principles on which these features are developed can be applied to a wide range of IoT devices. 低功率广域网通信技术是近年来新兴的一种无线通信技术。它弥补了蜂窝网和短距离无线通信技术的不足，并提供了传统无线通信技术所不具备的特征：远距离、低功耗、低速率。该技术为物联网的发展带来了大量的机遇；但同时，该技术本身也存在着很多的安全隐患。本项目的总体目标是提高对低功率广域网技术中出现的新安全问题的基本认识，并提出相应的解决方案。在该项目中，我们提出两个具体的研究任务：密钥生成和远程代码更新。在任务1中，我们将研究新颖的基于信道特征的密钥生成方案，以大幅度提高密钥生成速率。在任务2中，我们将为低功率广域网设计一个安全的空中代码更新协议。然而低功率广域网的低传输速率和长空中时间为该项目带来了全新的挑战。在该项目中，我们将研究、设计新的理论、方法和技术来解决这一难题。本项目的研究成果将为低功率广域物联网轻量级、易部署、鲁棒性高的安全通信机制的研究提供理论和实践基础，并为低功率广域网大规模部署和应用提供安全可靠的密钥生成和代码更新解决方案。因此，本项目的研究工作有着重要的研究价值和现实意义，并会产生较大的经济和社会效益。

21201420.label: Realisation of objectives
21201420.value: Throughout this project, extensive research efforts have been made to achieve the outlined objectives. Below are details of how each objective was addressed and the extent to which it was realized. 1) Objective 1 aims to develop approaches that can address the problem of low channel reciprocity in LPWAN. The long airtime of LoRa communication technology leads to the problem of low channel reciprocity which poses a major challenge for key generation in LPWAN. To solve this problem, we have developed novel approaches to improve channel reciprocity by exploiting fine-grained channel measurements and designing novel channel prediction methods. Specifically, we proposed a novel fine-grained channel state indicator named CLSSI. Compared to existing channel indicators, CLSSI can provide fine-grained and accurate channel state information. To improve the integrity of channel information, we proposed a lightweight channel state estimation method to comprehensively recover the channel information. Compared to existing solutions, the proposed method improves the robustness significantly. Evaluation results show that our methods improve key matching rate and key generation rate by 11.03-26.58% and 27-49 times compared to the state-of-the-art. 2) Objective 2 aims to design key generation schemes that can significantly improve key generation rates for LPWAN. To achieve this goal, we proposed several methods that can improve the key generation rates. First, we proposed a compressive sensing-based reconciliation approach that can correct more errors than existing error-correction codes. Based on this method, we further proposed a novel perturbed compressive sensing-based key delivery scheme to deliver secret keys. This method delivers a random key instead of generating keys directly, achieving significant performance improvements. 3) Objective 3 aims to design a secure, energy-efficient code dissemination protocol for heterogeneous LPWAN-based IoT devices. To achieve this goal, we proposed a novel energy-efficient, reliable, and beamforming-assisted over-the-air update system for LoRa networks, which features several techniques, including delta scripting, channel coding, and beamforming. In particular, we proposed a novel joint differencing and compression algorithm to generate the delta script for processing gain, unlocking the potential of incremental over-the-air update in LoRa networks. Afterward, we designed a concatenated channel coding scheme to enable reliable transmission against dynamic link quality. The proposed scheme uses a rateless code as outer code and an error detection code as inner code to achieve coding gain. Finally, we designed a beamforming strategy to avoid biased multicast and compromised throughput for power gain. Experimental results on a 20-node testbed demonstrate that the proposed method improves network transmission reliability by up to 1.51 times and energy efficiency by up to 2.65 times compared with the existing solution in LoRaWAN. In summary, all the objectives proposed in this project have been successfully achieved.

21201420.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201420.value: The major findings and the research outcomes of this project are as follows. (1) We studied the problem of physical layer key generation for LoRa-enabled Internet-of-Vehicles communication and proposed Vehicle-Key. In Vehicle-Key, we designed a novel deep learning model that can achieve channel prediction and quantization simultaneously. Additionally, we proposed an autoencoder-based reconciliation method that improves the performance significantly. The research outcomes have been published at IEEE ICDCS 2022 (PartC-9-[1]) and IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing (PartC-8-[4]). (2) Our research revealed that the limitations of previous studies are coarse-grained channel measurement and inefficient quantization process. To enable fine-grained channel information, we proposed a novel LoRa-specific channel measurement method that analyzes the chirp-level changes in LoRa packets. Additionally, we proposed a LoRa channel state estimation algorithm to eliminate the effect of asynchronous channel sampling. The research results have been published at INFOCOM 2023 (PartC-9-[3]). (3) We found that the low data rate of LoRa communication is one of the bottlenecks that limits the key generation rate. Therefore, we designed key generation schemes that significantly improve key generation rates. We applied a novel Bloom filter-based technology to protect the keys against reverse engineering attacks. Then, we leveraged the Karhunen-Loeve Transform (KLT) to remove the redundant information and enhance randomness. We proposed a compressive sensing-based reconciliation method to improve the key generation rates significantly. The research results have been published in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking (PartC-8-[5]) and UbiComp/ISWC ’22 (PartC-9-[4]). (4) We found that existing solutions for over-the-air update have several drawbacks, such as low energy efficiency, poor transmission reliability, and biased multicast grouping. To solve this problem, we proposed a novel energy-efficient, reliable, and beamforming-assisted over-the-air update system for LoRa networks, which features with delta scripting, channel coding, and beamforming. In particular, we proposed a novel joint differencing and compression algorithm to generate the delta script for processing gain, unlocking the potential of incremental over-the-air update in LoRa networks. Afterward, we designed a concatenated channel coding scheme to enable reliable transmission against dynamic link quality. Finally, we designed a beamforming strategy to avoid biased multicast and compromised throughput for power gain. The research results have been published at IEEE/ACM IPSN 2023 (PartC-9-[2]) and ACM Transactions on Sensor Network (PartC-8-[3]). (5) We found that there lacks a comprehensive survey on LoRa network and authentication systems for IoT devices; therefore, we completed two survey papers that are published in ACM Transactions on Sensor Network (PartC-8-[1]) and Digital Signal Processing (PartC-8-[2]).

21201420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201420.value: Building on the foundation of the completed research project, there are several promising topics for further development and potential applications. 1) Investigate more robust and adaptive key generation algorithms that can further exploit the unique propagation characteristics of LoRa in dynamic environments, such as urban areas or industrial IoT deployments. 2) Address challenges related to scaling the key generation process in dense LoRa networks. This could involve techniques to mitigate inter-node interference or optimize pairing strategies for key exchange in networks with thousands of devices. 3) Optimize the key generation process to reduce energy consumption, which is critical for battery-powered LoRa devices. This involves designing lightweight algorithms tailored to resource-constrained IoT devices. To advance these research directions, we propose the following actions. 1) Seek follow-up funding from government agencies, research councils, or industry partners to support further development. 2) Partner with academic institutions and industry stakeholders to address complementary challenges, such as integrating physical layer key generation into broader IoT security ecosystems. 3) Deploy pilot projects with industry collaborators to test the proposed solutions in real-world settings. 4) Develop educational materials, workshops, and tutorials to train engineers and researchers on physical layer security for LoRa networks.

21201420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201420.value: Low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) technologies are revolutionizing the Internet of Things (IoT) by enabling devices to communicate over long distances while using minimal power. However, its low data rates and long communication time pose unique challenges, especially when it comes to security. This project focuses on understanding and solving the security challenges of LPWAN. Two main tasks are tackled. (1) Key Generation: we have developed innovative methods to generate secure encryption keys faster using unique wireless channel features. (2) Secure Code Updates: we have proposed energy-efficient and secure protocols to securely update software on LPWAN devices over the air, using minimal resources. Overall, the research outcome of the project is a robust and efficient framework to secure LPWAN-based IoT devices, making them safer and more reliable while contributing to both research and real-world applications. This is crucial as IoT grows in importance and cyberattacks increase.

21207420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21207420.value: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases pose a great threat to public health in the world. They may last for several years, then deteriorate to cancers, but early detection and treatment of these diseases can significantly reduce the possible occurrence of cancers. Wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) has emerged as an important diagnostic tool for GI disease detection and therapeutic monitoring, thanks to its non-invasive, user-friendly and non-painful properties. A challenge in harnessing the WCE is that it requires clinicians to analyze a huge number of images (about 50,000 images per patient). Recently, deep learning based approaches have achieved significant progresses in automatic GI disease diagnosis. However, several challenges remain to be resolved for clinical applications. (1) The majority of existing models utilize whole images as inputs, which may introduce noise and redundant background information for feature learning. (2) Current approaches treat WCE images the same as conventional natural images by naively ignoring critical clinical information, often leading to biased conclusions. For instance, the bleeding areas show different colors while polyps have specific shape information. (3) These deep models usually address diagnosis in a supervised manner, requiring a large amount of training data with labels. Unfortunately, labeled medical images are usually difficult or time-consuming to acquire due to privacy issues. To deal with these challenges, we propose domain knowledge driven deep models for automatic GI disease diagnosis in this proposal. Firstly, we propose a hierarchical attention model to help the network focus on abnormal regions and thus improve its ability for discriminative representation. This will be achieved by proposing novel network structures and an attention strategy. Second, multi-scale clinical knowledge is introduced to the hierarchical attention model by exploiting the clinical understanding of GI diseases together with a multi-scale feature fusion strategy. Then, we propose a joint semi-supervised and self-paced learning model for GI disease diagnosis, which is capable of utilizing unlabeled dataset and adaptively learning features from simple images to complex ones so as to maintain the robustness. Finally, we will evaluate and validate the proposed deep models and implement a graphical user interface to display visual diagnosis results. Our preliminary experiments have demonstrated both the feasibility and the effectiveness of the proposed models. This project represents the first attempt to integrate comprehensive domain knowledge into deep learning models for GI disease diagnosis. It not only will produce high impacts in academic research of medical image analysis, but also can provide practical solutions to precision medicine. 腸胃道疾病是當今世界公共衛生的一大威脅。它們可能持續數年，惡化為癌症，但早期發現和治療這些疾病可以大大減少癌症的可能發生。無線膠囊內窺鏡由於其無創性、用戶友好性和無痛性的特性，已成為胃腸道疾病檢測和治療監測的重要診斷工具。利用無線膠囊內窺鏡的一個挑戰是，它需要臨床醫生分析大量的圖像(大約每個患者50,000張圖像)。近年來，基於深度學習的方法在腸胃道疾病自動診斷方面取得了顯著進展。然而，在臨床應用中仍然存在一些挑戰。(1) 現有的模型大多採用整體圖像作為輸入，可能會引入複雜和冗餘的背景信息進行特徵學習。(2) 目前的方法對無線膠囊內窺鏡圖像的處理與傳統的自然圖像一樣，忽略了關鍵的臨床信息，往往導致得出有偏差的結論。 (3) 深度模型通常需要大量帶標籤的訓練數據。由於隱私問題，標記醫學圖像通常很難且耗時。 為了應對這些挑戰，我們提出了領域知識驅動的深度模型來自動診斷腸胃道疾病。首先，我們提出了一個層次注意力模型，使得網路聚焦於異常區域，從而提高其特征表達能力。這將通過提出新的網絡結構和注意力策略來實現。其次，利用對胃腸道疾病的臨床知識和多尺度特徵融合策略，引入多尺度的臨床知識。然後，我們提出了一種聯合半監督和自步學習的胃腸疾病診斷模型，該模型能夠利用未標記數據集，自動調整地從簡單圖像學習特徵到複雜圖像，以保持魯棒性。最後，我們將評估和驗證所提出的深層模型。 我們的初步實驗證明了模型的可行性和有效性。該項目首次嘗試將全面的領域知識集成到基於深度學習的腸胃道疾病診斷中。它不僅將在醫學圖像分析的學術研究中產生很大的影響，而且可以為精准醫療提供切實可行的解決方案。

21207420.label: Major findings and research outcome
21207420.value: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases pose a great threat to public health in the world. They may last for several years, and then deteriorate into cancers, but early detection and treatment of these diseases can significantly reduce the possible occurrence of cancers. Wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) has emerged as an important diagnostic tool for GI disease detection and therapeutic monitoring, thanks to its non-invasive, user-friendly and non-painful properties. In this project, we develop domain knowledge-driven deep models for automatic gastrointestinal disease diagnosis. Firstly, we propose a hierarchical attention model to help the network focus on abnormal regions and thus improve its ability for discriminative representation (Part C, Conference 1,2). Secondly, multi-scale clinical knowledge is introduced for the GI disease diagnosis. As doctors always update the medical equipment to obtain more clearer image for the diagnosis, we proposed a super-resolution enhanced diagnosis framework to obtain high-resolution images and improve diagnosis performance (Part C, Journal 1). Considering different tasks for the GI disease may provide supplementary information for each other, propose a deep synergistic interaction network for joint classification and segmentation with WCE images (Part C, Journal 2). Thirdly, we propose a joint semi-supervised and self-paced learning model for GI disease diagnosis, which is capable of utilizing unlabeled datasets and adaptively learning features from simple images to complex ones so as to maintain robustness (Part C, Journal 3). Considering the time-consuming labeling issue, we also proposed a weakly supervised segmentation model via annotation calibration and gradient de-conflicting (Part C, Journal 4,5). Finally, we extensively evaluated and validated the proposed deep models and displayed visual diagnosis results in these published papers.

21207420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21207420.value: This project helped the PI address the automatic gastrointestinal disease diagnosis well, which laid a solid foundation for further medical image analysis. Though automatic polyp detection has been proven to be crucial in improving diagnosis accuracy and reducing colorectal cancer mortality during the precancerous stage, the performance of deep neural networks may degrade severely when being deployed to data in a distinct domain. This domain distinction can be caused by different scanners, hospitals, or imaging protocols. One promising strategy to address the limited labeled data and bridge the domain gaps is unsupervised domain adaptation, which effectively transfers essential knowledge from an off-the-shelf labeled source domain to a related unseen and unlabelled target one but with the same label space. The unsupervised domain adaptation models exploit domain-invariant information for the adaptation to the target domain, thereby achieving satisfactory performance even without annotations. Therefore, in our future work, we will work on domain adaptive models to bridge the domain gap between different colonoscopic datasets effectively.

21207420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21207420.value: The American Cancer Society predicts that around 140,250 new cases of stomach and intestine diseases will be found, leading to 26,730 cancer-related deaths in the US by the end of 2023. In Hong Kong, colorectal cancer is the second most common cancer. To help with these conditions, wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) is widely used for diagnosing and monitoring treatment. Currently, doctors spend a lot of time looking at the collected WCE images, which is time-consuming, tedious, and error-prone. This project proposed advanced computer models to assist doctors in diagnosing and segmenting disease regions more accurately and quickly. These models can highlight areas of concern in the images, reducing the time doctors spend analyzing them. This not only speeds up the diagnosis but also helps less experienced doctors make better decisions. For patients, this means earlier detection and better treatment outcomes. By integrating these models into existing hospital systems, doctors can identify issues sooner, potentially saving lives. This project aims to enhance GI disease diagnosis and improve related automated medical tools, building on the success of similar technologies in other medical fields. Feedback from doctors and patients will help gauge the immediate benefits.

21210820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21210820.value: Wearable systems enable measuring a broad range of biomedical, environmental and physiological signals to provide important information of human health and surroundings. Commercial available wearable electronics, such as wearable bands, smartphones and smart watches that can monitor and analyze some basic information including body temperature, heartbeats, and physical activities. However, these wearable electronics still has limitations from compatibility with body, to accuracy, and to physical demission, which may cause irritation/discomfort and inaccuracy. Thin, soft, skin-integrated and biocompatible electronics are considered as the key point to address the wearable technologies because they can not only facilitate conformably mounting on external surface of our body, such as skin, but also laminating on the internal surface of the organ tissues, such as heart and brain. Flexible and stretchable electronics provide the possibility to establish a platform for bio-integrated system, where long term integration is possible on different locations of the human body with negligible concerns of discomfort or irritation. With the assistance of wireless technologies, the information can be uploaded onto the cloud for real time monitoring and evaluating health status of the body. Thus, early detection of diseases and early warning of sudden illnesses may be possible with certain warning systems. Efforts toward to the flexible skin-integrated electronics have been made mainly in developing soft bio-sensors, however, the reports of the integration of early warning systems associated with stimulating to mechanoreceptors or thermoreceptors in flexible platforms is very seldom. Haptic actuators are no doubt the great candidate for the early warning system, as which can be triggered when the sensors detect any potential dangers of the body, such as high temperature, high pressure and abnormal heartbeat. Developing such a comprehensive system with both soft sensors and actuators can be considered as the next generation technology for wearable healthcare with the function of on-patient health monitoring and sudden illnesses early warning. Here we propose a concept of skin-integrated sensing and haptic electronics based on materials and devices for realizing ultra-thin, flexible electronics that incorporates functional healthcare related sensors and haptic mechanical actuators for the application in monitoring physiological signals and mechanically stimulating skin for early warning. Such platform can in-real time monitor qualitative and quantitative information on body temperature and pulse wave dynamics, and provide haptic actuation when needed for early warning of sudden illnesses that associate with abnormal physiological signals. 可穿戴電子在健康領域有著重要的應用，諸如生物醫療、環境和生理信號的檢測。目前商用的可穿戴電子包括手環、智能手機和手錶具有體溫、心跳和運動情況檢測的基本功能。儘管如此，這些電子設備卻仍然受限於準確度、和人體的適應性以及物理尺寸等因素，從而令佩戴缺乏舒適度以及精準性。輕薄、柔軟、皮膚集成且生物兼容良好的電子器件可以無感的貼附在皮膚上乃至內體的器官表面，被認為是覺得目前可穿戴設備缺點的重要突破口。柔性和可拉伸的電子是建立這類皮膚集成系統的基礎，並且在無線化模組的協助下，所檢測到的健康信息可以實時的上傳至雲端用於人體健康的智能評估和檢測。因此，此類電子使老年人的突發致命疾病的提早檢測與預防提供了可能性。目前為了實現這樣一個目標，大部分的研究重點關在柔性生物傳感器的開發，而忽略了疾病預警系統。這種預計系統可以採用聲音、機械或者電流刺激的方式提早的提醒病人潛在的併發症風險。觸覺驅動器毫無以為是這種預警系統的不二之選。在諸如傳感器檢測到了突發心臟病來領之前體溫及心率的變化，可以及時的發送指令到觸覺反饋驅動器，及時的提醒病人。因此開發皮膚集成化的觸覺執行器是實現下一代智能可穿戴電子的重點。 本研究計劃書提出了皮膚集成傳感和觸覺反饋與一體的智能可穿戴電子器件，通過材料和器件的開發實現超薄、柔性電子。且此類柔性電子兼具生理信號的檢測功能以及觸覺反饋的功能。從而實現實時的定性且定量的健康信息，如體溫、脈搏等信號的檢測，且在疾病來臨之前及時的發出觸覺反饋的警告。

21210820.label: Realisation of objectives
21210820.value: To achieve the goals. We conduct research on the following 3 parts. 1. developing sensors. 2. developing actuators. 3. developing integration systems. Here is how we achieve the goals. we developed a stretchable, wireless intelligent device based on soft electronics for real-time, healthcare signals monitoring and analyzing. We adopted the advanced mechanical design for the system, so the operational performance of the electronics is unaffected under various mechanical deformations, including bending, stretching, and twisting. To minimize the impact induced by human movements toward the healthcare measurement, a newly developed sensor patch based on hydrosol is introduced, exhibiting higher conductivity (~6.5 kΩ) and stronger adhesion strength (~9.9 kPa) over the traditional, commercial ones (45 kΩ and 3.4 kPa). In addition, actuators serves as the feedback system for timely reminding users once an abnormal signal is detected. To achieve this, we use Lorenz force based method to develop electromagnetic driven actuators to provide force feedback. For the integration of the system, the operational duration of the system is around 6.7 h, with the longest wireless communication distance extended to approximately 20.9 m, which could satisfy the fundamental usage requirement in daily life. To provide a real-time data interpretation, the machine learning tool is introduced here, applying a public ECG database (MIT-BIH arrhythmia database). As a result, the signals monitored by the device could be displayed on a screen of a self-developed handheld receiver with available diagnosis results in real-time. Then, we measured the signals from seven volunteers (males and females) by our device and a commercial one at the same time for comparison and found that the signals measured by both devices are comparable with similar P, Q, R, S, and T waves for each signal. It is believed that stretchable electronics have provided a promising alternative option to prevent the dangers of various cardiovascular diseases in humans' daily life in a more comprehensive approach.

21210820.label: Major findings and research outcome
21210820.value: In this proposal, we have developed soft, stretchable, skin-conformal wearable electronic devices, i.e. three-lead ECG monito, that can be directly mounting on the user's chest as a platform for bio signals collection, vibratory feedback delivery, and wirelessly interaction with the handheld device via Bluetooth. Newly developed hydrogel-based patches are used which provide stronger adhesion strength and better conductivity compared to traditional ECG electrodes. Comprehensive studies on mechanical design and performance, transmission distance, operation time, signal quality, and continuous monitoring ability are done by experimental and computational methods to support the usage of this system on targeted high-risk populations for continuous long-term ECG monitoring. Machine learning algorithms and graphical user interface on handheld devices are developed for CVD diagnosis and real-time ECG monitoring.

21210820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21210820.value: The potential for improvement exists in operation time and maximum transmission distance by optimizing power and wireless transmission design to satisfy the requirement of different scenarios. In the future, we believe, such technology will allow continuously analyzing human healthcare related signals during rest and excising for a long term, exhibiting a great potential in healthcare, fitness, and medical treatment.

21210820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21210820.value: Flexible electronics are a novel type of wearable devices that are mounted on the skin for physiological signal sensing and healthcare monitoring. Their thin, soft, and excellent mechanical properties (stretching, bending, and twisting) allow non-irritating and conformal lamination on the human skin for multifunctional intelligent sensing in real time. In this project, we developed a smart wearable system that can not only monitor healthcare signals, but also provide alarm to reminder user the potential risks. This technology contributes to the development of next-generation biomedical instrumentation.

21212720.label: Project Objectives
21212720.value: Develop an augmented reality (AR) -assisted image guidance system for percutaneous cardiac interventions. The proposed AR guidance system includes three major building blocks, which are: a. Reconstruction of 3D anatomical structures via segmentation of 3D diagnostic images. The 3D models will be used for rendering in the AR environment and for 3D printing of phantom models. b. Image registration and 3D localization of catheters by processing the real-time fluoroscopic and echocardiographic images. The image processing algorithms will be run on a server computer, and the processed results will be sent to the AR devices through a server-client framework. c. Rendering of the preoperatively-planned path and real-timely processed results as 3D holograms on the AR devices. The AR devices provide an intuitive 3D environment and extra interactive functions to allow the user to easily view and manipulate (e.g., rotate, reposition, and resize) the 3D virtual models. Develop machine learning algorithms for automated segmentation of diagnostic and real-time images. One class of algorithms will be developed to process 3D volumetric images (CT or MRI) for the segmentation and reconstruction of patient-specific anatomical models (i.e., spine, ribs, and heart). The second class of algorithms will be developed for the segmentation of real-time images (e.g., X-ray fluoroscopy and echocardiography) to (1) identify the fiduciary markers for registration of preoperative and intraoperative images and (2) detect the catheter for 3D localization and rendering in AR environment. Build a testing platform by 3D printing and soft robotic actuation. To well simulate the cardiothoracic environment, a phantom model of the anatomical structure will be fabricated by 3D printing of both hard and soft materials. Circulation of fluid and dynamic beating motions will be achieved by applying the soft robotic technology. This physical testing platform will be used for prototyping and evaluating the AR-guidance system. Additionally, it will also serve as a training setup for medical fellows/students to practice interventional procedures. Evaluate the existing algorithms and develop new machine learning methods for registration of the preoperative images (CT/MRI) and intraoperative images (X-ray fluoroscopy and echocardiography). Image registration is the critical step to build a coordinate system for rendering the localized catheters inside the 3D heart models. The classical rigid and deformable registration methods will be tested by using the spine as fiduciary markers and overlaying the segmented heart region on the projected images of the 3D heart model. Moreover, novel algorithms based on the deep-learning networks will be developed for direct image registration. Compensate the respiration and heart beating motion to achieve the optimized registration in real-time by integrating the preoperative imaging, real-time electrocardiographic (ECG) signal, and intraoperative imaging (i.e., fluoroscopy and echocardiography). A beating heart model will be created by interpolating the systolic and diastolic reconstructions from the two-phase CT or MRI scans. For real-time registration, the ECG data will be used to synchronize the beating cycles and improve the registration of the 3D model and the real-time images. Conduct a user study to quantitatively evaluate the usefulness of the AR guidance system. With the support from collaborators at Prince of Wales Hospital of Hong Kong, we will recruit medical students, imaging specialists, and doctors to use our developed AR system and ask them to complete a systematic survey. Based on their feedback, we will 1) further improve the user interface of the AR system and 2) report the fundamental pros and cons of using AR in the guidance of medical procedures.

21212720.label: Major findings and research outcome
21212720.value: The proposed AR-assisted image guidance system comprises three key technical components: (1) segmentation of the 3D heart model, (2) image registration to determine the catheter’s position relative to the heart, and (3) rendering of the AR model for display on HoloLens. Below is a summary of the progress for each component: 1. 3D Segmentation of the Heart Model We developed a novel dual-consistency semi-supervised learning method for left atrium segmentation from 3D MRI images. This technique addresses the challenge of limited labeled data by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data through model-level and structure-level perturbations. Our method significantly improves segmentation accuracy, achieving a Dice score of 90.05% and outperforming existing semi-supervised methods. The results have been validated on the Atrial Segmentation Challenge dataset, and a paper detailing this work is under major revision in Biomedical Signal Processing and Control. 2. Segmentation of Catheters from X-ray Fluoroscopic Images We implemented a Mask R-CNN-based video instance segmentation framework for tracking and classifying catheters in fluoroscopic images. Data augmentation and pre-trained weights were used to enhance accuracy. The model achieved a mean average precision of 0.53 and 79% precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5, with an inference time of 0.14s per frame. To address latency issues, we are developing lightweight neural networks, and related research has been submitted to Medical Image Analysis. 3. AR Rendering and Evaluation We conducted user studies with medical students to assess the effectiveness of AR visualization. The AR interface enables students to interact with a 3D heart model using gesture controls. Results show an overestimation of heart model size by 10.5%, attributed to irregular shape and reference placement. However, sphere size estimations had a percentage error below 10%, indicating reliable AR visualization. The AR system has proven to enhance medical training by allowing students to visualize and interact with anatomy in 3D. 4. Publications The research has resulted in multiple high-impact publications in Medical Image Analysis, IEEE Transactions, and Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, contributing to advancements in AR-guided cardiovascular interventions. For more detailed information, please refer to Part C of the report.

21212720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21212720.value: Ongoing research focuses on enhancing real-time catheter segmentation, optimizing registration accuracy, and refining the AR interface for clinical applications. To achieve real-time performance, a SWIN Transformer-based model is being developed to improve segmentation speed and robustness, targeting an update rate of 10 frames per second. In parallel, improving 2D-3D registration remains a challenge, as precise spatial alignment between fluoroscopic images and the heart model is critical for accurate catheter visualization. Machine learning-based registration techniques are being explored to achieve sub-centimeter accuracy. Clinical evaluation is progressing through collaboration with physicians at Prince of Wales Hospital, where qualitative and quantitative data are being collected to refine the system’s usability. Additionally, a phantom setup has been constructed for validation, but due to its limitations in replicating the heart environment, further testing using animal models is planned to advance the system toward clinical readiness. Industry collaboration with Shenzhen AR Technologies is also underway to develop a teleoperation AR system for medical training and surgical guidance. These efforts aim to bridge the gap between research and clinical application, facilitating the translation of AR-assisted image guidance into real-world medical practice.

21212720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21212720.value: This research focuses on developing an augmented reality (AR) system to help doctors perform heart procedures with greater accuracy. The system creates a 3D model of the patient’s heart, tracks the position of surgical tools inside the body, and overlays this information onto a HoloLens AR display. This allows doctors to “see” inside the body without making large incisions, improving precision and reducing risks. A key challenge in such procedures is identifying heart structures accurately, especially with limited medical imaging data. To solve this, we developed an advanced AI method that can recognize and segment the heart’s left atrium more efficiently, even with fewer labeled scans. Another breakthrough is an AI-powered tool that detects and tracks catheters in real-time X-ray videos, helping doctors navigate during surgery. The AR interface enhances medical training, allowing students and doctors to interact with 3D heart models as if they were real. This research has significant medical value, improving the safety and effectiveness of heart surgeries while also enhancing medical education. By collaborating with hospitals and industry partners, we aim to bring this technology from the lab to real-world healthcare settings, ultimately benefiting both doctors and patients.

21214720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21214720.value: In many data-driven applications like online retailing and social influence analysis, the dataset we can observe is often a collection of subsets of a ground set. The underlying distribution over all subsets is very important in many decision making algorithms. Learning such a distribution is a challenging task and existing studies mainly focus on modeling the frequency of each single item such that complex correlations among items are not captured well. Moreover, a generator that produces random subsets according to the underlying subset distribution is often missed in existing studies. In this proposal, we propose a learning framework that learns representations of items in the ground set which can help us generate random subsets via sampling an item graph. Our framework incorporates adversarial learning such that the performance of our generator can be improved through a competition with a discriminator. We also provide a solution for learning dynamic generator of subsets when the subset distribution evolves over time. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to combine representation learning and adversarial learning to learn subset distribution and subset generator. Moreover, many valuable applications can benefit from the subset generator learned by our framework, such as data-driven viral marketing and front-end warehouse inventory management. 在線上零售平台以及社會影響力分析等數據驅動型商業應用中，我們所能觀測並且需要分析的數據形式經常是一系列隨機集合。在這些場景下，隨機集合的概率分佈對於做出有效的商業決策來說是非常重要的信息。從觀測到的隨機集合數據學習隨機集合的概率分佈是一件極具挑戰性的任務。現有的研究往往只關注與建模單個元素屬於一個隨機集合的概率，從而忽略了不同元素之間複雜的相關性。除此以外，現有的研究並沒有解決如何根據隨機集合的概率分佈高效地生成隨機集合這一重要問題。在本項目中，我們提出了一個基於表示學習的框架模型，用於從大量的集合數據中學習隨機集合的概率分佈，並且我們的模型可以通過對元素相關性圖的採樣來快速生成隨機集合。我們的框架模型採用了對抗學習的思想，通過生成器和判別器之間的對抗來迭代提高所學到的隨機集合生成器的性能。對於隨時間演化的隨機集合概率分佈，我們提出了一個初步解決方案，用於學習隨機集合概率分佈隨時間演化的規律。據我們所知，結合表示學習和對抗學習用於學習隨機集合的概率分佈和生成器，是本項目的首創。本項目的研究目標將惠及許多重要的商業應用，比如數據驅動的病毒營銷方案設計和線上零售平台的前置倉庫存管理。

21214720.label: Major findings and research outcome
21214720.value: 1. We demonstrate that in theory, a biased model of subset distribution may still outperform the strong baseline of subsampling from historical data. The requirement of the biased model is that it should be able to generate random sets efficiently. 2. To learn the subset distribution from data, we propose a representation learning-based Markov Chain model that can capture item correlations, especially pairwise correlations. To mitigate the distribution-shifting issue, we utilize a sliding window model that only takes recent subsets in the training data to learn the model and the experimental results show that this simple strategy works well. 3. We also leverage the expressive power of neural nets and propose a deep-learning model that can fit any subset distribution with any accuracy if we increase the model capacity. We also develop the SubsetGAN framework that employs adversarial training in learning subset distribution. To accelerate the learning procedure, Importance Sampling techniques are used to boost the efficiency of stochastic gradient calculation. 4. We have applied the models developed in this project to various important downstream tasks, such as cloud manufacturing and warehouse inventory design. Worth noting that Alibaba has adopted our subset learning models in arranging the inventory of their front-end warehouses. Based on Alibaba's historical data, using our model can help improve the order fulfillment rate of front-end warehouses by 1%~2%.

21214720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21214720.value: This project focuses on improving how we analyze and generate groups of items, like products in online stores or social media connections. Often, we only see parts of the whole picture, which makes it hard to understand the relationships between items. Current methods usually look at each item separately, missing out on how they relate to one another. The researchers propose a new approach that not only learns how items are connected but also creates random groups of items based on these connections. They use a technique called adversarial learning, where two models compete to improve each other's performance. This allows the system to adapt as the relationships among items change over time. By developing this method, the researchers aim to help businesses better understand customer behavior and manage inventory efficiently. Their work could lead to more effective marketing strategies and smarter inventory decisions, benefiting various industries that rely on data-driven insights.

21300620.value: 基於共價鏈接的分子催化劑的高效二氧化碳還原反應的誘導效應和反應動力學研究

21300620.label: Project Objectives
21300620.value: To understand the inductive effect of peripheral functionalities on the electrochemical CO2 reduction performance of molecular catalysts in a general context. Molecular complexes with inexpensive metal centers have attracted tremendous attention due to their high selectivity in CO2-to-CO conversion. The engineering of the electronic properties of metal centers can effectively improve the CO2 electroreduction performance. According to the Sabatier principle, which stated that the interactions between the catalyst and the substrate should be neither too strong nor too weak, here we hypothesize that the effect of peripheral functionalization on molecular catalysts activities will depend on the binding strengths of the metal centers to the intermediates. To understand the inductive effect of the peripheral functionalities, first, we will compare the activities of molecular catalysts based on the derivatives of tetraphenylporphyrin and phthalocyanine with metal centers such as Co, Fe, and Ni. We will also use the Density Functional Theory to obtain the bond strengths of the metal-COOH, which is the intermediate structure at the rate-determining step. By correlating the activities to the bond strengths, we will draw a Volcano plot to delineate the structure-activity of the molecular catalysts. Our preliminary study on cobalt phthalocyanine suggests the electron-donating functionalities will deactivate the CO2 reduction performance, which is different from our previous study on the cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin system. This preliminary data supports our hypothesis. This objective will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the functions of the peripheral functionalities in CO2 electroreduction and help the molecular design in the future. To investigate the kinetics of electron transfer of covalently immobilized molecular catalysts on carbon nanotube. In addition to the intrinsic activity of molecular catalysts, the kinetics of the electrochemical CO2 reduction is an important extrinsic factor affecting the performance. The agglomeration of molecular catalysts is a common phenomenon during electrode preparation. Due to the poor conductivity of molecular catalysts, catalysts agglomeration will cause a sluggish reaction rate and reduce the electrochemical active sites. Immobilization of molecular catalysts onto conductive substrates by physical mixing can help the dispersion of the catalysts and improve the electron transfer. However, the agglomeration problems persist, and the leaching of catalysts happens during the long-term electrolysis due to the weak Van der Waals interaction between the catalysts and substrates. In comparison, covalent immobilization of molecular catalysts onto conductive substrates can achieve a high dispersion of catalysts while strengthening the interactions and improving the long-term stability. In our preliminary study, we covalently grafted cobalt phthalocyanine onto carbon nanotube (CNT), which achieved a high CO2 reduction performance and outperformed the gold catalyst. Further studies will be carried out to understand the kinetics effect of covalently immobilized molecular catalysts with different configurations, including the direct linkage of the metal center to CNT, the direct bonding of peripheral phenyl group to CNT, and the attachment of molecular catalyst via an aliphatic chain at the peripheral phenyl group. This objective will help to understand the significance of the electron transfer at the catalyst-substrate interfaces and assist the future electrode design. To achieve a commercially relevant current density and selectivity in a flow cell with optimal functionalities and interface configuration. The commercial use of electrochemical CO2 reduction will require the electrocatalysts to maintain high current densities with high selectivity and energy conversion efficiency. Conventional electrochemical CO2 reduction is performed in an aqueous media in a batch-type configuration such as H-cell, which cannot meet the demanded mass transport at high current densities. In a recent study, it was found that the use of a flow cell for electrochemical CO2 can accommodate current densities exceeding 150 mA/cm2 with high selectivity, which is a condition more relevant to an industrial application. Prompted by the advantages of the flow cell design and our mechanistic insights from the effect of peripheral functionalities and the kinetics of molecular CO2 reduction, we will optimize the design of the molecular catalysts and the covalent immobilization structure. This objective will apply the fundamental insights from Objective 1 and 2, and demonstrate that both high current densities and selectivity can be achieved at a low operating voltage.

Molecular complexes with inexpensive metal centers have attracted tremendous attention due to their high selectivity in CO2-to-CO conversion. The engineering of the electronic properties of metal centers can effectively improve the CO2 electroreduction performance. According to the Sabatier principle, which stated that the interactions between the catalyst and the substrate should be neither too strong nor too weak, here we hypothesize that the effect of peripheral functionalization on molecular catalysts activities will depend on the binding strengths of the metal centers to the intermediates. By correlating the activities to the bond strengths, we will draw a Volcano plot to delineate the structure-activity of the molecular catalysts. Our preliminary study on cobalt phthalocyanine suggests the electron-donating functionalities will deactivate the CO2 reduction performance, which is different from our previous study on the cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin system. This preliminary data supports our hypothesis. 21300620.label: Major findings and research outcome
21300620.value: The engineering of electronic properties in metal centers can significantly enhance the performance of CO2 electroreduction. Our research reveals that the impact of peripheral functionalization on the activity of molecular catalysts is contingent on the binding strengths of the metal centers to intermediates. Specifically, our study on cobalt phthalocyanine shows that electron-donating functionalities deactivate CO2 reduction performance, differing from previous findings on cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin. Conversely, the incorporation of electron-withdrawing quaternary ammonium groups enhances the activity of cobalt phthalocyanine. This discovery deepens our understanding of the role peripheral functionalities play in CO2 electroreduction and informs future molecular design strategies. Beyond the intrinsic activity of molecular catalysts, the kinetics of electrochemical CO2 reduction is a crucial extrinsic factor influencing performance. A common issue during electrode preparation is the agglomeration of molecular catalysts, which, due to their poor conductivity, leads to sluggish reaction rates and a reduction in electrochemically active sites. Immobilizing molecular catalysts onto conductive substrates through physical mixing can enhance catalyst dispersion and electron transfer. However, agglomeration persists, and catalysts often leach during prolonged electrolysis due to weak Van der Waals interactions between the catalysts and substrates. In contrast, covalent immobilization of molecular catalysts onto conductive substrates can achieve high catalyst dispersion, strengthen interactions, and improve long-term stability. In our study, we covalently grafted cobalt phthalocyanine onto carbon nanotubes (CNTs), achieving superior CO2 reduction performance that surpassed gold catalysts. This finding underscores the importance of electron transfer at catalyst-substrate interfaces and aids future electrode design. For the commercial application of electrochemical CO2 reduction, electrocatalysts must sustain high current densities with high selectivity and energy conversion efficiency. Conventional electrochemical CO2 reduction is typically conducted in aqueous media within batch-type configurations like H-cells, which are inadequate for the mass transport demands at high current densities. Inspired by the advantages of flow cell design and our mechanistic insights into the effects of peripheral functionalities and molecular CO2 reduction kinetics, we optimized the design of molecular catalysts and their covalent immobilization structure. This approach ultimately achieved high performance in a flow cell. This research not only provides a comprehensive understanding of the influence of peripheral functionalities and catalyst kinetics but also lays the groundwork for the future design of high-performance electrochemical systems for CO2 reduction.

21300620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21300620.value: Here are some potential directions: 1. Exploration of Peripheral Functionalities: Investigate a broader range of peripheral functional groups with both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing properties to systematically understand their effects on different metal centers. Study the synergistic effects of mixed functionalities on a single catalyst to fine-tune the electronic properties and optimize performance. 2. Advanced Catalyst Design: Develop new molecular catalysts with more complex structures that incorporate multiple active sites or co-catalysts to enhance CO2 reduction efficiency and selectivity. Explore the use of different metal centers beyond cobalt, such as iron, nickel, or copper, combined with various ligands to discover new high-performance catalysts. 3. Improved Immobilization Techniques: Refine covalent immobilization methods to enhance the stability and conductivity of the catalyst-support interface further. Investigate alternative conductive substrates, such as graphene or metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), to improve electron transfer and catalyst dispersion. 4. Mechanistic Studies: Conduct in-depth mechanistic studies using advanced spectroscopic and computational techniques to understand the reaction pathways and intermediate species involved in CO2 reduction on modified catalysts. Study the role of solvent and electrolyte interactions with the catalyst to optimize conditions for CO2 reduction.

21300620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21300620.value: In this proposal, we conducted a systematic study to understand the fundamental concepts in molecular catalysts for CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). We studied the inductive effect of peripheral functional groups on CO2RR activities. We also studied the kinetics of electron transfer for covalently immobilized catalysts. Prompted by the mechanistic studies, we built a flow cell with an optimized electrode structure for high-performance CO2RR. By using a covalent grafting strategy, we achieved a current density of 25.1 mA/cm2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 98.3% at -0.6 V with a low loading of 60 ug/cm2 for CO2-to-CO conversion. Our theoretical calculations further delved into the mechanistic origin of the high activity. We showed that the molecular functional groups can change the energy barriers for the reaction, attaining an optimized energy gap with the quaternary ammonium group. The design principle of molecular catalysts concluded in this project will help the future development of high-performance catalysts for CO2 reduction.

21302520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21302520.value: 摘要 紐結在日常生活很常見，比如鼠標線、耳機線等。在微觀尺度上，紐結也存在於高分子鏈中，比如DNA鏈、蛋白質等。由於在各種體系中的廣泛存在，紐結引起了各個領域研究者的興趣。除了數學家外，高分子物理學家研究紐結對高分子動力學的影響，生物學家研究DNA紐結與蛋白質紐結的生物功能，化學家研究紐結分子的特殊催化功能，一些測序技術開發者也研究DNA紐結對測序過程的影響。研究這些紐結問題需要弄清紐結的形成機理並找出製造穩定紐結的方法。 儘管經過多年研究，目前尚未找到製造穩定高分子紐結的方法。在良性溶劑中（高分子傾向於與溶劑分子接觸從而形成舒展態構象），壓縮高分子構象會形成紐結，但是在鬆開壓縮後，這些紐結會自發解開。在不良溶劑中（高分子傾向於與自己接觸從而形成緊緻構象），高分子構象塌縮會形成紐結，但是這些紐結缺乏結構特異性，較為雜亂。通過設計雜聚高分子鏈（不同單體聚合形成的鏈）的序列可得到特定的紐結結構，但是搜尋這樣的序列所需的計算量極大。 本研究課題將發展簡單而有效方法來製造出穩定紐結。在良性溶劑中，我們通過添加側鏈來卡住紐結，從而使紐結穩定存在。在不良溶劑中，我們選取均聚物紐結結構作為模板，通過修改特定位點上單體的相互作用來提高紐結結構的特異性。修改少數位點的相互作用後，高分子鏈將會非常大的概率形成指定的紐結結構。該方法已經得到我們初步結果的驗證。 上述製作穩定紐結的方法將會用於DNA紐結和蛋白質紐結。通過修改少數位點實現紐結結構特異性的結果將會用於弄清蛋白質紐結形成的原因：為什麼有些氨基酸序列會折疊成蛋白質紐結結構？是不是因為若干位點上的氨基酸相互吸引？ 本研究將會使用蒙特卡洛模擬以及分子動力學（包括粗粒化高分子鏈模型以及全原子蛋白質模型）。這些模擬可提供高分子紐結以及蛋白質紐結的構象以及動力學性質。 本研究製造的穩定DNA紐結與蛋白質紐結有若干潛在應用，比如通過紐結控制測序過程中DNA鏈行為。另外，本研究的結果也會協助找出決定蛋白質紐結形成的關鍵因素。

We developed the tube model for the mechanism of polymer knot formation, and published many papers as corresponding authors: “Application of the tube model to explain the unexpected decrease in polymer bending energy induced by knot formation”, Macromolecules 53, 9443 (2020) “Revisiting the Non-monotonic Dependence of Polymer Knotting Probability on the Bending Stiffness”, Macromolecules 54, 1623 (2021) “Tube model for polymer knots with excluded volume interactions and its application”, Macromolecules 54, 9299 (2021) 2. We have successfully employed sidechain to produce stable knots. In addition, we have employed crowding condition, spatical confinement, bending stiffness to control polymer behavior. We published many papers as corresponding authors: “Crowding-Induced Polymer Trapping in a Channel”, Physical Review E 104, 054502 (2021). “Quantifying the effects of slit confinement on polymer knots using the tube model”, Physical Review E 105, 024501 (2022). “Computational Design of Extraordinarily Stable Peptide Structures Through Sidechain-Locked Knots”, The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters, 13, 7741 (2022). “Knotting in Flexible-Semiflexible Block Copolymers”, Macromolecules, 57, 5330 (2024) 3. We have successfully used sidechain, salt condition, and temperature to modulate biomolecular conformations, interactions, knots, and supercoil formations. We published many papers as corresponding authors: “Twist-diameter coupling drives DNA twist changes with salt and temperature”, Science Advances 8, eabn1384 (2022). “Universality in RNA and DNA Deformations Induced by Salt, Temperature Change, Stretching Force, and Protein Binding”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA, 120, 2218425120(2023). “Computational Design of Extraordinarily Stable Peptide Structures Through Sidechain-Locked Knots”, The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters, 13, 7741 (2022). As an extra, we have developed a new computational algorithm to identify knot chirality. “A simple and efficient algorithm to identify the chirality of polymer knots”, Chinese Journal of Polymer Science, 42, 2030-2037 (2024).

In this project, we investigated the physical laws governing knot formation and effective approaches to control knot behavior. We find knot conformation is controlled by conformational entropy. We developed several approaches to controal knots, including bending stiffness, spatial confinement, crowding, and salt concentration.

21304020.label: Project Objectives
21304020.value: To identify the order parameters for the equilibrium quantum phase transition in interacting many-body systems and justify their relationships to the dynamical quantum phase transition (DQPT) when bringing the system out of equilibrium by a quantum quench. A quantitative description of the correlation between the equilibrium order parameters and DQPT (if any) will be established. To clarify the necessary and sufficient conditions for a DQPT to occur in interacting many-body systems and their relationship with the underlying equilibrium quantum phase transition. To develop a general and systematic scheme for deriving dynamical order parameters that characterises a DQPT. A scheme which is applicable to a general interacting quantum many-body system in the construction of the dynamical order parameter will be established. This will provide a useful tool for characterising the time-evolved quantum state in the vicinity of the DQPT.
