21304020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21304020.value: Phase transitions (e.g., when water boils into steam or ice melts into water as the temperature changes) are common phenomena in nature. Under certain external conditions, including temperature and pressure, one phase may be more energetically favourable than another and transformations between different phases occur when the external condition varies. Such transformations are referred to as phase transitions. In the past century, the study of phase transition phenomena in many-body systems at equilibrium has attracted much interest. Today, the subject is relatively well understood and the theories developed for this purpose have uncovered numerous applications across different disciplines. A case in point is the advancement in comprehending superconductivity. In recent years, research on phase transitions has reached the next level. When a quantum many-body system is brought out of equilibrium by, for instance, a sudden change in the system’s internal parameters such as the interaction strength amongst its constituents, new physics can emerge. Non-equilibrium phases and a new type of phase transition, known as dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs), arise. However, theoretical understandings of these phenomena are still far from complete. The overarching goal of this project is to identify the underlying principles and universal patterns of DQPTs using state-of-the-art analytical and computational techniques. This project will seek to answer the following open questions about DQPTs: 1) What criteria are necessary for DQPT to occur and how do the criteria relate to a system’s equilibrium quantum phase transitions; and 2) How can the dynamical order parameter that characterises the transition be determined systematically? The explorations of the fundamentals of DQPT will enable us to better understand the non-equilibrium phases of matter and the dynamics of quantum many-body systems. The insights derived from such examination will not only expand the boundaries of academic knowledge and interest but also lay the groundwork for future technological developments. These prospects hold true, especially in the realisation of a scalable quantum computer, in which the dynamics of quantum many-body systems will play an important role and the non-equilibrium phases of matter may also find an application. 相變是自然界中普遍的現象。最常見的例子包括當溫度降至冰點以下，液態的水會凝結成固態的冰。在過去一個世紀，科學家對處於平衡態的多體系統相變現象作出了深入且廣泛的研究。時至今天，我們對該領域已有相對深刻的理解，而且通過多年研究而建立出的理論亦在不同學科領域得到廣泛的應用。然而，對於非平衡態的量子多體系統中的相變現象，我們目前的認識還是比較初步的。當一個系統的內部參數 (譬如是粒子間的相互作用)突然產生變化時，新的非平衡相和一種新型的相變，稱為動力學量子相變（DQPT）有機會出現。本項目旨在利用不同的解析和模擬計算方法去探討關於DQPT的一些公開問題，這包括: 一）引發DQPT的必要條件是什麼，以及這些條件與系統在平衡態的量子相變有何關係；二）如何有系統地建構能描述DQPT的序參量？探索上例的問題有助我們理解物質的非平衡相以及量子多體系統中的動力學。這些理解不僅能擴闊學術知識界限，還可望為未來技術如量子計算機的發展奠定基礎。

21304720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21304720.value: Quantum technology, such as quantum computation, quantum cryptography, and quantum simulation, is likely to become one of the driving force for the development of human society in future. Such technologies have enormous potentials because they can achieve goals far beyond today's classical computer power. Recently, Google has announced that it has reached the first milestone towards such quantum supremacy. As a result, competitions on building infrastructures for future quantum technology has become increasingly important. One of the fundamental requirements for future quantum technology is that quantum information must be stored and coherent manipulated for an extended period of time. However, this is impossible for generic quantum many-body systems, because they will generally relax towards the state of thermalization (which we will call an `ergodic' system) under its own dynamics. As a result, any quantum information stored in the initial states will quickly become lost and can no longer be recovered by local measurements. One of the conventional solutions to this problem is to use the ground states of a quantum many-body system, which can be non-ergodic despite that the majority of the energy spectrum consists of ergodic eigenstates. The downside of this conventional solution is that it is not always easy or even practical to prepare a macroscopic quantum system in its ground states. Often, the most accessible states in the experiments are the highly excited states in the middle of the energy spectrum. Recently, people have realized that disorder may provide an alternative solution for us. In particular, an isolated interacting many-body quantum system can generally break ergodicity if strong quenched disorder is present. This phenomenon, now known as many-body localization (MBL), has attracted enormous interest in the research community because all eigenstates in the energy spectrum break ergodicity. Thus, quantum information stored in a generic initial state may be retained for an arbitrarily long time, which presents a great potential for quantum information storage and manipulation. In this work, we will study many-body localization in a quasiperiodic system, which is one of the most realistic platforms for MBL experiments to date. We will address outstanding challenges faced in current experiments, analyze how the phase transition between thermal and MBL phases occur, and also search for possible other novel quantum phases of matter in such out-of-equilibrium systems. During this project, we will also apply and develop new machine learning methods to analyze this type of novel quantum phases. 量子技术，如量子计算、量子密码学、量子模拟等，很可能成为未来人类社会发展的动力之一。这类技术具有巨大的潜力，因为它们可以实现远远超过当今传统计算机能力的目标。最近，谷歌宣布，它已经达到这种量子霸权的第一个里程碑。因此，为未来量子技术建立基础设施的竞争变得越来越重要。 未来量子技术的一个基本要求是，量子信息必须可以在较长的时间内被存储和操作。然而，对于一般的量子多体系统来说这是不可能的，因为它们通常会在自身的动力学演化下达到热力学平衡状态（我们称之为一个“各态历经”的系统）。因此，任何储存在初始状态的量子信息都将很快丢失，并且无法再通过局部测量来恢复。解决这一问题的传统方法之一是利用量子多体系统的基态。这个方法利用了这样一个事实，也就是说尽管能谱中大部分的态由这种各态历经的本征态组成，但唯独基态可以是非遍历的。这种传统解决方案的缺点是，制备宏观量子系统的基态并不容易，甚至有时候根本不现实——通常情况下，实验中最容易得到的量子态是能量谱中间的高激发态。 近年来，人们意识到无序系统可能为我们提供了另一种解决办法。特别地，如果杂质的浓度足够高，一个孤立的多体量子系统通常可以破坏遍历性。这一现象，现在称为多体局域化。这样的系统引起了研究界的极大兴趣，因为该系统的能谱中几乎所有本征态都打破了遍历性。因此，在一般初始状态下存储的量子信息可以保留足够长的时间，这为量子信息的存储和操作提供了巨大的潜力。 在本研究项目中，我们将研究一个一维准周期系统中的多体局域化问题。这样的系统是迄今为止研究多体局域化最现实的实验平台之一。我们将解决当前实验中面临的突出挑战，分析热力学平衡态和多体局域化相之间的相变是如何发生的，并在这种非平衡的系统中寻找可能的其他新的物质量子相。在这个项目中，我们还将应用和开发新的机器学习方法来分析这种新的量子相位。

21304720.label: Realisation of objectives
21304720.value: This report demonstrates the exceptional progress made in achieving the two primary goals of this funded research program: (1) addressing outstanding questions in existing many-body localization (MBL) experiments, and (2) analyzing the MBL-thermal phase transition using various theoretical tools, including innovative machine-learning techniques. Through nine high-quality published papers, we have made significant contributions that advance the fundamental understanding of MBL phenomena and develop new methodological approaches to study quantum phase transitions. The following citations [1-9] refer to the nine publications listed in Part C of this report. **Goal 1: Addressing Outstanding Questions in Existing MBL Experiments** Our research has successfully addressed several critical open questions in MBL experiments through systematic investigations of previously unexplored regimes and phenomena. In paper [1], we pioneered the investigation of quantum many-body scar states in two-dimensional PXP models on both square and honeycomb lattices. Our rigorous study clarified experimental uncertainties by demonstrating the persistence of scar states up to finite disorder strengths before eventual disappearance. This work elucidated the fascinating interplay between disorder and quantum many-body scarring in two-dimensional systems, significantly extending our understanding of no-nergodic many-body dynamimcs beyond one-dimensional systems. Paper [2] addressed the critical experimental challenge of identifying exact mobility edges in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic models. We developed an analytical method that precisely determines the mobility edge and connects it explicitly to spontaneous parity-time symmetry breaking. Additionally, we proposed a practical experimental protocol using photonic lattices, which paves the way for experimental exploration of non-Hermitian localization phenomena. In paper [3], we systematically investigated the role of short-range versus long-range interactions in MBL phenomena for one-dimensional lattice fermions. Our research demonstrated that strongly interacting systems with long-range interactions always remain many-body localized, independent of disorder strength, analogous to pinned Wigner crystals. This groundbreaking finding significantly clarified experimental observations in systems of ultracold atoms and trapped ions. Paper [4] thoroughly examined the impact of next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping on localization properties in a quasiperiodic t1-t2 model. We identified three distinct interaction regimes, revealing qualitatively new physics when strong interactions and NNN hopping are present, notably the breakdown of Hilbert space fragmentation. These insights are essential for interpreting experiments involving optical lattices where extended hopping is significant. In paper [5], we studied discrete time crystals realized by the introduction of nonsymmorphic dynamical symmetry, which is another form of non-ergodic dynamical behavior. Our analytical solution showed spontaneous period doubling, significantly enhancing understanding of non-equilibrium phases and their robustness against thermalization and decoherence, directly impacting experimental realizations of discrete time crystals. Paper [6] introduced a novel scheme exploiting Floquet scar states in generalized PXP models to generate robust subharmonic responses. Remarkably, we demonstrated the existence of such responses beyond conventional prethermalization regimes without requiring large frequencies or amplitudes. This work substantially advances theoretical and experimental frameworks for non-ergodic phases of quantum matter. **Goal 2: Analyzing the MBL-Thermal Phase Transition Using Various Theoretical Tools** We employed a diverse suite of theoretical and computational techniques, significantly advancing methodological approaches to studying the MBL-thermal transition. Paper [7] provided a rigorous statistical analysis of many-body mobility edges, establishing mathematical foundations that conclusively ruled out infinite-temperature mobility edges in generic noninteracting fermionic systems. By demonstrating multivariate normal distribution properties for the spectrum and conserved quantities, we offered critical theoretical insights that address longstanding experimental ambiguities. In paper [8], we unveiled an unexpected phenomenon of interaction-enhanced localization in the generalized Aubry-André (GPD) model. Through extensive numerical simulations enabled by exact diagonalization and DMRG-X algorithms, we elucidated the microscopic mechanism underlying this phenomenon—the instability of the highest-energy single-particle band against weak disorder—thus resolving previously unexplained experimental findings. To complement our numerical studies, we further developed mean-field theoretical descriptions for complex MBL transitions that are efficient and accurate approximations for highly excited many-body eigenstates in the MBL regime. This new mean-field theory, specially designed for highly excited many-body eigenstates, can be applied to many other problems well beyond MBL problems. Lastly, paper [9] made a groundbreaking methodological advancement by developing and employing unsupervised machine-learning techniques to analyze eigenstate entanglement spectra (ES) in interacting quasiperiodic systems. Our innovative algorithm quantitatively assessed the mutual dependence among thermal, MBL, and nonergodic extended (NEE) regimes, demonstrating that the NEE regime smoothly emerges from both the MBL and thermal phases. This analysis showed that NEE states exhibit both MBL-like fast decay and thermal-like long tails in their entanglement spectra, effectively settling a major debate and providing a robust framework for discerning complex phase boundaries relevant to the MBL-thermal transition. **Conclusion** Through these nine influential publications [1–9], our research has remarkably achieved both funded goals. By systematically addressing outstanding experimental questions and pioneering new theoretical and methodological frameworks, including innovative machine-learning approaches, our work has significantly advanced the understanding of MBL phenomena. These contributions lay a robust foundation for future experimental and theoretical explorations in this rapidly evolving field.

21304720.label: Major findings and research outcome
21304720.value: This research has significantly advanced the understanding of many-body localization (MBL), systematically addressing critical experimental questions and pioneering novel theoretical and computational methods. One major achievement is the detailed exploration of quantum many-body scar states in two-dimensional PXP models [1]. By showing scar states' robustness up to finite disorder strengths, we elucidated the complex interplay between disorder and weak ergodicity breaking in higher-dimensional systems, thereby addressing a significant gap in experimental MBL research. We have provided critical insights into the impact of interaction range on MBL. Our systematic analysis demonstrated that long-range interactions universally induce MBL regardless of disorder strength, likening these states to pinned Wigner crystals [3]. This finding profoundly clarifies previous experimental uncertainties and offers precise guidance for future experimental investigations. A remarkable counterintuitive phenomenon we identified is interaction-enhanced localization in the generalized Aubry-André model [8]. Through a combined mean-field and numerical approach, we uncovered the mechanism of instability in high-energy single-particle bands against weak disorder. This resolution significantly contributes to theoretical and experimental understanding, challenging conventional assumptions about interactions in localization transitions. The impact of next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping on MBL physics was thoroughly analyzed, revealing distinct phases driven by interaction strengths [4]. Particularly, we discovered that strong interactions coupled with NNN hopping fundamentally alter Hilbert space structure, shedding crucial light on experimental setups involving optical lattices. Additionally, our research has bridged MBL physics and discrete time crystals. Utilizing nonsymmorphic dynamical symmetry [5] and Floquet scar states [6], we demonstrated robust subharmonic responses that persist beyond conventional prethermalization limits, significantly broadening theoretical and experimental frameworks for nonthermal phases. We have also achieved significant theoretical advancements in understanding mobility edges, particularly through exact analytical methods for non-Hermitian quasiperiodic models [2]. Establishing a connection between mobility edges and spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking, we provided clear experimental pathways for observation using photonic lattices. Rigorous statistical analysis further reinforced our theoretical advancements by conclusively ruling out infinite-temperature mobility edges in generic fermionic systems, offering a rigorous mathematical underpinning for observed phenomena [7]. Finally, a groundbreaking methodological contribution was our introduction of unsupervised machine learning for analyzing quantum phase transitions [9]. This innovative technique decisively resolved the debate about the nonergodic extended regime, clarifying its dependence on both MBL and thermal phases. Collectively, these findings represent substantial theoretical progress, resolving experimental ambiguities, and developing powerful, innovative frameworks essential for future MBL research.

21304720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21304720.value: Our research opens multiple promising avenues for further exploration. First, the discovery of robust quantum many-body scar states in two-dimensional systems [1] motivates investigating higher-dimensional lattices and more complex interaction patterns. We propose to extend these studies using advanced numerical techniques like tensor network methods to address larger system sizes, providing a deeper understanding of dimensionality effects on nonergodic many-body quantum dynamics. Second, the identified connection between mobility edges and PT-symmetry breaking in non-Hermitian models [2] strongly suggests exploring experimental realizations in photonic and ultracold atom setups. Future efforts will involve collaboration with experimental groups to verify theoretical predictions, broadening the practical impact of our results. Third, the success of unsupervised machine learning techniques [9] highlights the potential of employing supervised and reinforcement learning methods to identify quantum phases in complex systems more effectively. Our proposed next step involves integrating machine learning with large-scale simulations to map unexplored regions of the MBL phase diagram precisely. Finally, interaction-enhanced localization phenomena [8] merit further theoretical and experimental investigations, particularly exploring similar phenomena in disordered superconductors and quantum circuits. We plan focused studies to understand broader implications and potential technological applications of this surprising effect.

21304720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21304720.value: This research explores a fascinating quantum phenomenon known as many-body localization (MBL), where quantum particles remain stuck in place rather than spreading out evenly, as typically expected. Imagine cars frozen in traffic jams—this research investigates how and why quantum particles get similarly "stuck" due to interactions and random disturbances. Our work resolves important puzzles from recent experiments by discovering special quantum states called "scar states" that resist spreading even when random disturbances increase. Surprisingly, we also found that certain types of particle interactions can strengthen localization, making particles even more "stuck"—contrary to common intuition. Moreover, we explored scenarios where particles behave differently when their movement rules slightly change, similar to drivers following alternate routes on a congested road. To advance our understanding, we introduced advanced computational tools, including machine-learning algorithms, that identify subtle transitions between localized and free-moving phases without prior assumptions. These discoveries not only deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum physics but also open new possibilities for designing future quantum technologies, like stable quantum memories and computers.

21500220.label: Project Objectives
21500220.value: The ultimate goal of this proposal is to develop a data-driven production-distribution system for perishable goods retailers. The system is designed to provide demand forecasting, production, and replenishment planning from data to decision making. To study the demand patterns of perishable products through internal supply chain data mining and external factor sensitivity analysis. To develop a multi-step demand forecasting model at the store-cluster level which integrates a multi-view store aggregation algorithm and a Sequence-to-Sequence deep learning prediction model. To develop a data-driven production planner for factories with L-days production lead time. The production planner is designed to integrate the demand predictors (with its forecast demand and prediction error bound) and a robust inventory model. To design a data-driven replenishment and transshipment algorithm for next-day perishable goods distribution from factory to retailer stores.

21500220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500220.value: Perishable goods are typically ordered, produced, and delivered on a daily basis. Due to the high demand volatility and short shelf lifetime, retailers have been facing the challenges to match perishable supply with uncertain demand. Prior literature has been focusing on inventory policy design and clearance price optimization to reduce sales loss due to demand misestimation. However, it is still not clear how to reduce the inevitable demand uncertainties at the individual store level. Furthermore, most of the prior studies on perishable inventory planning are built on the pre-defined demand distribution. However, in real-world implementation, the parameter distribution is sensitive to some external factors which change dynamically. To address the aforementioned issues, this proposal aims to develop a data-driven inventory planning system for perishable goods by integrating data mining techniques and robust inventory optimization algorithms. Specifically, we first propose an aggregate demand forecasting algorithm to guide factories for an L-day ahead production plan. The aggregate production is conducted at the station cluster level based on a deep sequential model, which reduces the demand volatility while preserving demand sensitivities to external factors. The prediction result, together with the prediction error distribution, is then used as parameter inputs for factory production optimization under certain constraints and inventory policies. The production amount, which is delivered after L days, is then distributed to retail stores based on a next-day demand forecasting and the day-end inventory at the individual store level. The proposed data-driven "L-day ahead aggregate production and next-day redistribution'' inventory planning attempts to provide a new scheme for perishable inventory control with the support of data mining and deep learning algorithms. A field experiment will be conducted to test the effectiveness of our designed system using real-world supply chain data and feedback from potential industry practitioners. 易腐產品通常需要以天為單位進行訂購，生產與交付。由於這類產品的需求波動性大及貨架期較短，零售商長久以來都面臨著難以將產品供應量與需求相對應的挑戰。先前的研究主要集中于通過庫存策略的設計以及清倉價格的優化來減少因錯誤估計需求而導致的銷售額損失。但是，如何在單個商店層面降低不可避免的需求不確定性仍然是一個無法解答的問題。此外，大多數先前研究中對易腐產品的庫存設計都是基於預先定義的需求分佈。然而，在現實世界中，實際的需求分佈可能對一些動態變化的外部因素相當敏感。爲解決上述問題，本提案提出了通過結合數據挖掘技術和具有高魯棒性的庫存優化算法，來開發針對易腐產品的數據驅動型庫存規劃系統。具體來説，我們首先提出一種總量需求預測算法來引導工廠制訂基於其交付時間的生產計劃。這一總量生產算法是由深層時間序列模型在銷售站群的層級實現的，既降低了需求的波定性又能適當保留需求對外部因素的敏感性。預測結果以及預測的誤差分佈將會作爲參數輸入進工廠的生產優化模型，從而在特定的約束條件和庫存策略下決定生產計劃。在交付日，生產出的產品將會基於次日的需求預測以及各個商店上一營業日末的庫存情況被分配。我們提出的“基於數據驅動的L日生產提前期總量生產與次日分配”庫存規劃方案旨在藉助數據挖掘技術與深度學習算法的支持，為易腐產品的庫存控制提供新方案。在未來，我們將使用真實的供應鏈數據以及潛在的行業内用戶的反饋來進一步測試該系統的有效性。

21500220.label: Realisation of objectives
21500220.value: Firstly, to respond to the second project objective, we explore the demand patterns of each perishable product. We study the heterogeneity of product demands in different stores mainly based on two perspectives. One is demand time series patterns based on internal supply chain data; the other is external sensitivity derived from fluctuations in demand resulting from weather and holiday condition variations. To get a representative sequence for demand, censorship in sales records needs to be addressed. We match out-of-stock sales records with the top five uncensored ones based on basic weather features with the restriction of the same day of the week. A combination of secant vectors generated by a trained deep sequential model describes the change of demand magnitude to external factors. Therefore, tackling censorship in sales records, we extract the demand patterns as well as external sensitivity to represent demand patterns for each store under each product. The developed data-driven production-distribution system for perishable goods retailers is constructed based on a two-phase framework, including an aggregate production module and a distribution planner. Building on the third and fourth research objectives concerning the production planning system, we construct a deep sequential prediction model followed by a multi-view store aggregation algorithm. Leveraging the extracted features based on internal supply chain data, we develop an aggregate algorithm following the Expectation and Maximization (E&M) scheme. It serves the purpose of aggregate production through this multi-view clustering algorithm, which captures the demand series' complementary nature and accounts for the similarities in sensitivity fluctuations to external environment factors. The proposed clustering algorithm balances two views through alternative iterations. The lead time demand prediction is conducted on the cluster level for aggregate production through a deep sequential model followed by the clustering algorithm. We construct a Long-term-short-term (LSTM) sequence encoder-decoder model for multi-step time series forecasting. The forecasting LSTM model is first implemented in the preliminary aggregate demand prediction phase, considering the production lead time within each store cluster. The fifth research object corresponds with the second phase in our formulated framework. Once the production is completed at the clustering center after production lead time, the produced products should be distributed to different individual stores. We have developed a replenishment optimizer for next-day perishable goods distribution to facilitate this constraint distribution. At this time, the sales records have been updated to the current date, thus the information during production lead time can be used. Therefore, the “next-day” demand prediction with refreshed sales information is conducted, and the prediction error distribution is also integrated to serve as a basis for the distribution planner. Overall, we have developed a data-driven aggregate production and distribution system for perishable goods retailers. Additionally, our proposed strategy can reduce lost profit when compared with industry standards. Therefore, the ultimate goal is addressed through the constructed two-phase framework.

21500220.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500220.value: Major Findings: In this project, we developed a data-driven aggregate production distribution planning framework to tackle a multi-store newsvendor problem with production lead time. To address the store's demand heterogeneity, mitigate demand volatility, and demand uncertainty due to production lead time, we first developed a multi-view clustering method to aggregate retail stores based on external demand sensitivities and demand time series complementarity. Then we conducted demand forecasting and guided aggregate production at the cluster level for different groups of stores. The production, once produced after d-days of production lead time, is then distributed to each store, facilitated by solving a constrained integer programming problem given the prediction with error distribution. We implemented our strategy on a leading perishable product retailer in China. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our model in reducing 22.22% loss of profit compared to industry standards. Since our framework complements existing literature on multi-store newsvendor problems and addresses industry challenges, we expect that our work offers valuable insights for retail companies. Research Outcome: The direct outputs of this project has supported disseminate emerging research at academic workshops. The work “The Newsvendor Problem with Location-aware Aggregate Production and Distribution” has been presented in 2023 POMS China International Conference. Furthermore, the work “A Data-Driven Optimization Framework of Aggregate Production and Distribution for Newsvendor Problems” has been submitted to KDD 2024 Applied Data Science Track. The journal version is under preparation and targeted on POMs journal. In addition, the data-driven prediction and optimization research framework has supported several ongoing research projects. Specifically, the PI has implemented the framework in research paper “A Cost-Effective Sequential Route Recommender System for Taxi Drivers”, which was published on a top-tier UTD24 journal, INFORMS Journal on Computing. Additionally, the PI, along with his PhD student investigate the spillover effect in sharing economies and the work “Spillover in Sharing Economies: Network Effect of Bike-sharing e-sharing Services on Home-sharing Performance” has been accepted by the top conference International Conference on Information Systems (ICIS) in 2023 and nominated best paper. The funding also enables several ongoing research. The first one explores how human managers’ presented in this project delegated their operational decsions to the AI system, which is undergoing minor revisions at MIS Quarterly. The second corresponds to the proposed research framework and is also in its minor revisions stage to INFORMS Journal on Computing.

21500220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500220.value: While the data-driven prediction and optimization framework achieves significant improvement in operational efficiency and motivates several AI-powered operations management algorithms, the framework lacks theoretical proof. The two-stage decision makes it difficult to interpret the optimality of the final decisions. Future development of the paper can follow a new framework of prediction-in-optimization that integrates the prediction model into the integer programming. In addition, the current framework was designed for single-period optimization. Future work can also be extended to a multi-period optimization framework for a more general optimization problem.

21500220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500220.value: The data-driven prediction and optimization framework has been demonstrated to reduce 22.22% loss of profit compared to industry standards by minimizing under- and over-supply from the perishable product replenishment system. This framework supports end-to-end decision-making from supply chain data to operational decision. It facilitates the development of AI systems for decision automation. The framework leverages the advantages of data mining and operations research technique. It facilitates the implementation of this integrated method on many other operations management problems, e.g., fleet repositioning in bike sharing and transshipment optimization for inventory management.

21500920.label: Project Objectives
21500920.value: Develop a game-theoretic model in which a firm sells a new product to consumers with superior information while consumers must incur deliberation costs to find out their true valuations of the firm's product. Analyze the properties of the equilibrium strategy and refine it using equilibrium refinement criteria such as the intuitive criterion and the divinity criterion D1. Then, investigate the effect of superior information and consumer deliberation on firm profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. Provide insights into how firms should manage their data collection practices and how public policy makers should regulate data collection and protect consumer welfare. Propose marketing and operational strategies that can be used by firms to alleviate consumer suspicion and reduce consumer deliberation, thereby improving firm profits and social welfare. Discuss the possible extensions such as product quality and consumer empowerment. Discuss how a firm's information advantage and consumer deliberation would affect these decisions.

21500920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500920.value: 如今，公司往往收集各种各样的消费者数据，例如网络点击，购买记录，社交数据等。利用这些丰富的数据和分析工具，公司很可能比消费者更了解他们自己(Xu and Dukes 2019a, 2019b)：公司同时知道产品的特性和消费者的偏好，因而可以判断一个产品是不是真正的适合消费者。 与此同时，对于新产品而言，消费者并不了解产品的特性，他们需要运用大脑来判断某个产品是否真的适合自己（例如，回忆自己的行为，想象产品的用途），这一过程被称为消费者思考(Wathieu and Bertini 2007, Guo and Zhang 2012)。 在本项目中，我们研究在消费者需要付出思考成本情况下的公司定价策略。我们指出：(1) 公司可能利用自己的信息优势去诱导消费者购买不适合的产品；(2) 当消费者遇到一个高价时，他们也会怀疑公司有没有欺骗自己，并会通过思考来做出购物决策；(3) 消费者思考会给社会带来资源浪费。在某些情况下，公司会被自己的信息优势反噬。 我们将构建一个博弈模型来研究公司的定价策略。公司可以利用数据对消费者个性化定价，消费者也会根据价格来判断自己的类型。这个模型可以帮助公司开发更好的定价话定价策略，并告诫他们如何采集和利用数据。在研究公司定价之外，我们还将考虑如何利用营销决策来帮助公司限制自己的诱导行为，从而降低消费者的疑虑并提高社会效益。最后，我们的研究还将帮助决策者制定大数据和消费者保护策略。

21500920.label: Realisation of objectives
21500920.value: Objective 1: Develop a game-theoretic model in which a firm sells a new product to consumers with superior information while consumers must incur deliberation costs to find out their true valuations of the firm's product. This objective was successfully achieved. I developed a complete model of the problem. This full model appears in Li and Xu (2022, Marketing Science). Objective 2: Analyze the properties of the equilibrium strategy and refine it using equilibrium refinement criteria such as the intuitive criterion and the divinity criterion D1. Then, investigate the effect of superior information and consumer deliberation on firm profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. This objective was successfully achieved. It is shown that the equilibrium outcome is semi-separating equilibrium in which the firm randomizes its price offers and consumers randomize their deliberation decisions. Their effects on firm profits, consumer surplus and social welfare have been obtained. Objective 3: Provide insights into how firms should manage their data collection practices and how public policy makers should regulate data collection and protect consumer welfare. This objective was successfully achieved. It is shown that the firm can be worse off collecting data from consumers, and that banning data collection can improve both consumer welfare and firm profit. Objective 4: Propose marketing and operational strategies that can be used by firms to alleviate consumer suspicion and reduce consumer deliberation, thereby improving firm profits and social welfare. This objective was successfully achieved. Two approaches have been proposed to alleviate consumer suspicion and reduce consumer deliberation: distorting product quality and limit the firm’s capacity. Objective 5: Discuss the possible extensions such as product quality and consumer empowerment. Discuss how a firm's information advantage and consumer deliberation would affect these decisions. This objective was successfully achieved. It is found that the firm benefits from offering a low-quality product and empowering consumers.

21500920.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500920.value: This project investigates a firm’s personalized pricing strategies when the firm knows consumers’ valuations while consumers need to incur a costly effort to find out their own valuations. We find that, in equilibrium, the firm will always charge a high-valuation consumer a high price but randomizes its price offer to a low-valuation consumer: It sometimes honestly charges the consumer a low price while at other times charges a high price to trick the consumer into overpaying for the product. When a consumer receives a low price from the firm, she knows her valuation is indeed low and makes a no-brainer purchase. When a consumer receives a high price from the firm, however, she is still unsure of her true valuation. In equilibrium, the consumer also mixes: With certain probability, she deliberates to make an informed purchase; with complementary probability, she makes a no-brainer purchase. We further show that the firm’s superior knowledge of consumer preferences does not necessarily benefit the firm. On the one hand, the firm can take advantage of its information advantage to price discriminate against consumers. On the other hand, the firm’s opportunistic incentive to trick consumers induces consumer suspicion, and the firm must compensate for it by lowering its price. Within certain parameter space, the downside of superior knowledge dominates its upside, and the firm is worse off collecting consumer data. Thus, public policies that prevent firms from collecting consumer data can end up benefiting the firm. We then discuss the tactics that the firm can employ to alleviate consumer suspicion and improve firm profit. We show that, even if offering a high-quality product is free, the firm may intentionally choose to offer a low-quality product, which discourages consumer deliberations and improve firm profit. The firm may also ration its capacity, which limits its opportunistic incentive. Overall, this research comprehensively analyzes the scenario in which the firm has better information about consumer valuation, and provides important suggestions to public policymakers and firms on how to regulate the market and improve profits.

21500920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500920.value: The research can be extended in a few directions. For example, the current research assumes that the firm can only signal consumer valuation through personalized price. Future research may consider other signalling devices such as targeted advertising. This can be done using the standard signalling models with multiple signalling devices. In addition, future research can consider the effect of superior knowledge on other decisions such as product package design. This can be done by allowing the firm to make these strategic decisions before offering prices to individual consumers. Overall, we believe that the research has great potential for future development.

21500920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500920.value: In the digital age, firms often know consumer valuations better than consumers do themselves. For instance, a dating APP can predict a consumer’s chance of getting matched with his or her profile and historical data, while a consumer cannot assess such likelihood easily. Nonetheless, a consumer can put into effort to find out her own valuations, e.g., asking an expert, searching information online or consulting a friend. In this project, we analyze how a firm should offer consumers personalized prices when it has superior knowledge of consumer preferences. We show that the firm will adopt a mixed-strategy: When the consumer’s valuation is high, the firm always charges the consumer a high price. When the consumer’s valuation is low, the firm will sometimes charge the consumer a high price but at other times charge her a low price. We also discuss the implication of superior knowledge on firms and consumers, and provide suggestions for firms to improve profits.

21501720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21501720.value: 企业家部门在货币政策传导中的作用

21501720.label: Project Objectives
21501720.value: The main objective of this project is to provide the first quantitative exploration of how entrepreneurs transmit monetary policy. In particular, we care about how much contribution entrepreneurs have and what makes them contribute that much/little. The results would enrich our understanding of monetary policy in academia as well as help improve the conduct of monetary policy for policymakers. We have established the analytical framework, a Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian model, and still need to take the following six steps to achieve our main objective. Step 1: Moments in the full-fledged model. We seek to decompose the impulse response of aggregate demand to monetary policy shocks along three dimensions: (1) workers vs. entrepreneurs vs. corporates, (2) consumption vs. investment, (3) direct substitution effect vs. general equilibrium income effect. We establish the connections between these decomposed components and data targets. Steps 2: Data for identification. To collect data for identification, we estimate the impulse responses of worker income, entrepreneur income, worker consumption, and entrepreneur consumption using the panel data of Consumer Expenditure Surveys (CEX). We also estimate the impulse response of corporate investment using the Compustat survey and the impulse response of aggregate investment using aggregate time series from Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). Step 3: Back-of-envelop calculation. We build and calibrate a simple model that does not have within-worker and within entrepreneur heterogeneity to do the same decomposition as in Step 1 as well as most of the counterfactual experiments as in the full-fledged model. The simplified model can help us obtain quick results. It is more transparent in mechanisms but has less discipline from data. Step 4: Solve the full-fledged model. Our model has a liquid and an illiquid asset, which is known to be computationally intensive. We plan to adopt the "Sequence-Space Jacobian" algorithm to solve the model following Auclert, Bardoczy, Rognlie and Straub (2019). A primary advantage of the algorithm is that once the steady-state equilibrium is solved, it is very fast to compute impulse responses by perturbation. Step 5: Calibrate the model. It is the step to choose parameter values to make all the critical moment conditions satisfied. The main difficulty is that when selecting a different parameter to match some impulse responses, we may need to recompute the steady-state and check whether the income and wealth distribution of the model matches PSID and SCF surveys. We currently need about 10 minutes to solve the steady-state for once on a personal desktop. Calibrating the full model is time-consuming but still feasible. Steps 6: Counterfactual experiments. We would explore the role of the four distinct features of entrepreneurs in monetary policy transmission. It is accomplished by shutting down each feature at a time. Entrepreneurs can be as wealthy as workers if we reparameterize their production technologies. The investment decision can be turned off by assuming infinite investment adjustment costs. Collateral constraints can be removed by resetting the corresponding parameters to allow for infinite leverage. Business income share is acyclical if we assume Cobb-Douglas instead of CES production functions. In each of these counterfactual experiments, we would like to do the same decomposition as in Step 1. The difference between a scenario and the baseline model can be interpreted as the role of the corresponding entrepreneur feature.

21501720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21501720.value: Although entrepreneurs bare a significant fraction of the aggregate economic fluctuations, their role in the transmission of monetary policy to aggregate demand is not yet well explored. How much do they contribute to the transmission? More importantly, what makes them contribute that much/little? To answer these questions, we need a structural model. In our project, we build the first Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian (HANK hereafter) model that has an entrepreneur sector on top of the workers and listed firms. Our model highlights four distinct features of the entrepreneurs: (1) they are wealthier than workers, (2) they consume like workers and invest like firms, (3) they rely on external financing that is subject to collateral constraints, and (4) their business income is very sensitive to monetary policy shocks. The first three features are standard in macrocosmic models that do not focus on business cycles, while the last one is entirely new. We conjecture that these four features are crucial for entrepreneurs’ role in monetary policy transmission. Here are the reasons. (1) More income and wealth allow entrepreneurs to have a larger share in aggregate demand on average. (2) Access to both consumption and investment doubles the channels through which monetary policy can affect their demand for goods. (3) Collateral constraints make their consumption and investment decisions more dependent on cash flow. (4) Business income is their primary source of cash flow. To verify our conjecture, we will calibrate the model to match data. The steady-state income and wealth distributions match PSID and SCF surveys. The marginal propensities to consume (MPC) are from natural experiments in the literature. The income and consumption responses of workers and entrepreneurs to monetary policy shocks match the CEX survey, while the investment responses of listed firms match the Compustat survey. We will demonstrate the answer to our research questions in two steps: (1) decompose the impulse responses of aggregate demand along multiple dimensions, (2) compare the scenarios in which one of the four entrepreneur features is absent to our baseline model. The results would enrich our understanding of monetary policy in academia as well as help improve the conduct of monetary policy for policymakers. 虽然企业家承担了很大一部分的总体经济波动，他们在货币政策向总需求传导过程中的作用并没有被很好地研究过。他们对传导机制的贡献有多大？更重要的，什么决定了他们的贡献大小？为了回答这些问题，我们需要一个结构模型。 在我们的项目中，我们第一次构建了一个在雇员和上市公司部门之上引入企业家部门的异质性个体新凯恩斯模型。我们的模型强调了企业家的几个突出的特征：（1）他们比雇员更富有；（2）他们像雇员一样消费却像企业一样投资；（3）他们依赖于外部资金并受到抵押约束的限制；（4）他们的营业收入对货币政策十分敏感。前面三个特征在不关注商业周期的宏观经济模型中是标准的设定，而最后一个特征则是我们独有的。 我们猜想这四个特征都是企业家在货币政策传导中作用的关键。原因如下：（1）更多的收入和财富让企业家在总需求中的份额高于其人口份额；（2）同时参与消费和投资使企业家能够通过双重渠道影响总需求波动；（3）抵押约束使他们的消费和投资决策更加依赖于现金流；（4）营业收入是他们的主要现金流来源。 为了验证我们的猜想，我们会校准模型拟合数据。稳态收入与财产分布拟合PSID与SCF调查数据。边际消费倾向从自然实验的文献中提取。雇员与企业家收入与消费对货币政策冲击的响应从CEX调查数据中获得，而上市公司投资的响应则匹配Compustat调查数据。 我们将从两个方面展现研究结果：（1）从多个维度分解总需求的脉冲响应，（2）将企业家的四个特征中有一个缺失的场景与我们的基准模型进行比较。这些结果将会丰富学界对货币政策的理解，同时有助于改进货币政策的制定。

21501720.label: Realisation of objectives
21501720.value: Objective 1 is the summary of the project. Therefore, I only state the realization of objectives 2-7, which correspond to steps 1-6 of the plan. The percentage of completion for objective 1 is the average of that for objectives 2-7. Obj 2: The objective has been fully accomplished. A conceptual framework for decomposing the aggregate demand has been established in the proposal. Our quantitative model has been numerically solved to generate the decomposition. All required empirical moments have been collected. The remaining concern (beyond the scope of this grant proposal) is our heavy reliance on indirect evidence to discipline the entrepreneur's marginal propensity to invest. Obj 3: This objective has been fully achieved. We find that under monetary policy shocks, entrepreneurs exhibit more procyclical income and consumption compared to workers. Additionally, we have estimated the impulse responses of both corporate and aggregate investment to monetary policy shocks in the data. Obj 4: This objective has been fully achieved. We construct a Two-Agent New Keynesian (TANK) model featuring a representative consumer and a representative entrepreneur, calibrated to match their marginal propensities to consume (MPCs) as observed in data. The model is numerically solved in DYNARE and successfully replicates the empirical impulse responses of consumption and investment to monetary policy shocks. Our results suggest that the entrepreneurs potentially amplify the aggregate real GDP response to monetary policy shocks. Obj 5: This objective has been fully achieved. We have acquired the Intel Fortran Compiler and developed a Fortran implementation of the "Sequence-Space Jacobian" method. The model can be numerically solved within 20 minutes per run on a PC workstation. However, the computational burden becomes significant during calibration, as this process requires solving the model for many runs. The primary limitation stems from the inability to fully adapt the endogenous grid point method to our model that features both collateral constraints and investment adjustment costs. We are still exploring alternative solution methods to enhance computational efficiency. Obj 6: This objective has been achieved by approximately 60%. Specifically, we have successfully matched 16 steady-state moments capturing key cross-sectional characteristics of entrepreneurs (income, wealth, investment, external financing, and hiring). We have also generated the model-implied average MPC for workers and entrepreneurs aligned with the established literature. However, our full-fledged model has not generated sufficient business income cyclicality relative to workers, a limitation notably absent in our successful TANK model implementation (Obj 4). This gap has led us to consider replacing our current modeling approach, a CES production function, with an endogenous occupancy rate model developed in Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) as a shortcut. (1) The CES production function approach. This approach can generate highly procyclical business income through capital income dynamics. When capital adjusts sluggishly, expansionary hiring during booms reduces the labor share. However, this approach faces challenges with two empirical patterns: matching the cross-sectional distribution of entrepreneurial wealth and generating empirically plausible entrepreneurial investment dynamics. Moreover, this model relies on a lower real wage to stimulate higher aggregate output when the aggregate demand is higher. (2) An endogenous occupancy rate approach. Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) and the subsequent refinements provide micro-founded evidence for two endogenous wedges during the monetary expansions: a positive efficiency wedge and a positive markup wedge. The model demonstrates that demand surges increase the occupancy of production capacity at no cost, generating gains in observed productivity. Concurrently, producers face reduced competitive pressures, enabling markup expansion. While Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) formalize the two wedges through search frictions, our entrepreneurial model can adopt reduced-form functions capturing these endogenous wedges. Additionally, this approach ensures that the highly procyclical business income, real wage dynamics, and inflation responses are all consistent with data. This part is still in progress. As a result, our paper, Qiu and Wang (2025), is not yet circulated as planned now. Obj 7: This objective has been 80% completed. We can numerically solve each counterfactual experiment by making minor modifications to the baseline model through parameter adjustments. However, since the calibration remains incomplete, we must finalize the parameterization before presenting the counterfactual analysis results. References: Qiu, Zhesheng and Jose-Victor Rios-Rull, "Procyclical Productivity in New Keynesian Models," NBER working paper 29769, 2021. Qiu, Zhesheng and Yicheng Wang, "Entrepreneurs, Idiosyncratic Investment Risk, and Monetary policy," 2025.

21501720.label: Major findings and research outcome
21501720.value: The primary research output is the working paper Qiu and Wang (2025), with Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) serving as its foundational companion paper. Companion Paper: Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) This paper demonstrates that a search friction capturing the endogenous occupancy of firms' production capacity can explain why business income exhibits stronger cyclicality than labor income in response to monetary policy shocks. It provides a framework for incorporating this feature into New Keynesian models while maintaining their good performance across all other dimensions. In the R&R stage, this paper has been widely circulated and cited in this field. Main Paper: Qiu and Wang (2025) Building on these insights, Qiu and Wang (2025) investigates the implications of procyclical business income for monetary policy transmission. Entrepreneurs amplify the effect of monetary policy shocks on aggregate output because their demand for real goods, which consists of both consumption and investment, is sensitive to income variations. While a complete draft exists, certain results require further refinement before formal circulation. At the current stage, the draft has been shared preliminarily on SSRN and discussed (not presented) in conferences and meetings with peers in this field. We aim to address the remaining limitations before submitting it to a top-tier economics journal. References Qiu, Zhesheng and Jose-Victor Rios-Rull. 2021. "Procyclical Productivity in New Keynesian Models." NBER Working Paper 29769. Qiu, Zhesheng and Yicheng Wang. 2025. "Entrepreneurs, Idiosyncratic Investment Risk, and Monetary Policy." Working Paper.

21501720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21501720.value: Potential for Further Development Despite the significance of this question, empirical evidence on entrepreneurial investment remains limited. In the current project, we rely on a structural model and indirect evidence to discipline entrepreneurs' investment behavior. Moving forward, we plan to leverage administrative data to refine our modeling of entrepreneurial investment, thereby strengthening the credibility of our quantitative results. With this model, we can explore several related research questions, such as the transmission of fiscal policy through entrepreneurs and the role of business formation in unemployment dynamics. The first question naturally complements our current work, while the second is the focus of an ongoing project. Proposed Course of Action In the short term, we will refine the model by incorporating insights from Qiu and Rios-Rull (2021) to address the cyclicality of business income. Following this, we will finalize the calibration (hopefully with an updated solution method) and conduct counterfactual experiments. In the medium term, we aim to advance the paper Qiu and Wang (2025) toward publication and develop additional companion papers based on this framework.

21501720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21501720.value: During economic expansions, business income grows faster than labor income, resulting in a redistribution of income from workers to business owners. With higher earnings, business owners tend to increase both consumption and investment, whereas workers primarily raise their consumption. This divergence in spending behavior significantly affects how monetary policy transmits to aggregate demand. A thorough understanding of this transmission mechanism—its causes and consequences—is essential for effective monetary policy implementation.

21502720.label: Project Objectives
21502720.value: We test whether skilled labor shortages increase M&A activities by employing two natural experiments: one based on random H-1B visa lotteries and the other based on a policy shock to the supply of high-skilled foreign labor. In the face of skilled foreign labor rationing, we anticipate that public firms are more likely to acquire talent through M&A or acquihiring. Identifying a skilled labor channel in M&A contributes to the academic literature as there are no studies that establish a causal relationship between skilled labor supply and M&A transactions. Additionally this sheds light on the startup ecosystem and provides valuable information to practitioners in the startup industry (founders, CEOs, skilled workers, etc.) on alternative startup exit pathways. We evaluate the characteristics of the target firms being acquired as a result of skilled foreign labor shortages. We hypothesize that targets are predominantly private, high-tech firms that have hired through the H-1B program. We expect skilled labor to come from acquisitions of smaller, private tech firms which would confirm anecdotal evidence that acquihirers are interested in specific teams with highly specialized skill sets. Additionally, we suspect such highly specialized workers would come from the H-1B labor pool. Corroborating this hypothesis contributes to the existing academic literature, as only a handful of working papers have attempted to characterize labor-driven acquisitions. Practitioners, particularly startup founders, may also find this knowledge relevant if they want to increase their likelihood of being acquihired. We determine if acquihiring can overcome frictions in labor mobility caused by labor law restrictions by testing whether acquihiring is more likely to occur in companies headquartered in US states that have stronger non-compete labor laws, resulting in higher costs of skilled labor hiring. Completing this objective contributes to the law and economics academic literature and therefore has policy implications on skilled worker immigration. Findings from completing this objective is relevant to policymakers as it informs them on how corporations can strategically circumvent labor laws through corporate restructuring. We determine if acquirers experience an exodus of skilled workers after M&A deal completion. The primary concern of acquihiring is whether the acquired talent is willing to stay with the acquirer long enough to have an impact. We plan to construct measures of worker turnover using LinkedIn data to verify that there is no outflow of skilled labor after deal completion. Completing this objective contributes to the literature on corporate culture and informs us on whether acquirers careful in considering labor compatibility with their targets. This is also valuable information for industry professionals who are considering acquihiring. The scraped LinkedIn data that we use, once refined, can also be used in future labor-related research projects. We demonstrate whether acquirers’ demand for skilled workers compounds in response to skill labor shortages. As a robustness check, we will verify whether our exogenous source of skilled labor shortages exacerbates skilled labor demand. This will be done by using unique job postings data provided by Burning Glass Technologies as a measure of skilled labor demand. Completing this objective serves to empirically support our initial findings and aforementioned objectives above. This is also valuable for future labor-related research projects in which one needs to measure skilled labor demand accurately. We show that labor-driven M&A transactions generate long-lasting synergies. We predict that, on average, acquihiring is not simply a consequence of empire-building. We follow the existing M&A literature and use exogenous M&A deal withdrawals to test whether completed acquisitions in which targets share similar labor skill demands with acquirers prior to deal-announcement produce positive long-run abnormal stock returns. Completing this objective contributes to the M&A literature on quantifying synergies. Our results would be unique in its focus on labor synergies. This finding would also be relevant and valuable to industry professionals interested in acquihiring. We write papers publishable in top tier finance or management journals.

21502720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21502720.value: In the knowledge-based economy, high-skilled labor has become increasingly influential in firm value creation. Yet the motivations for and consequences of strategically integrating skilled labor remain empirically unexplored in the M&A literature. In this project, we take a step towards understanding the role of skilled labor in M&A decision-making and ask whether changes to the skilled labor supply help explain M&A decisions of publicly traded firms. Large Silicon Valley technology companies such as Google and Facebook have faced significant talent shortages in recent years. This has resulted in the continued expansion of these large technology companies into other cities and states beyond Silicon Valley to access new populations of skilled labor. Anecdotal evidence suggests that in addition to direct hiring, "acquihiring", which is the practice of buying companies to acquire their talented employees rather than their projects and assets, has become a popular strategy to satisfy skilled labor demand. When the amount of highly talented individuals is in short supply, buying talent through M&A may be a more effective recruiting strategy for acquirers who are interested in teams rather than individuals. However, accurately identifying "acquihiring" is difficult, as acquirers rarely acknowledge their real intentions publicly. In this project, we seek first to answer the fundamental question: do firms pursue M&A in response to skilled labor shortages? Employing two natural experiments, one based on random lotteries that the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services uses to allocate H-1B visas and the other based on a policy shock to the overall supply of skilled foreign labor through the H-1B program, we test whether shortages of skilled foreign workers can cause firms to pursue acquisitions. Our goal is to establish empirically a labor market channel in M&A. Bias in estimating labor synergies by comparing firm performance between those engaging in M&A and those that do not is problematic due to the inability to control for unobservable confounding factors. We plan to address this issue with another natural experiment that compares the performance of acquirers of completed labor-driven M&A deals to acquirers of labor-driven M&A deals that are withdrawn due to reasons unrelated to skilled labor and beyond the control of those involved in the deals. We predict that exogenously completed M&A deals with high levels of labor complementarity between acquirers and targets, which we will measure using job classification data from our H-1B visa micro-dataset, will improve acquirer performance in the long-term. 在知識經濟裡，高級技術型人才對創造企業價值越來越重要。然而，戰略性雇用高級技術型人才的動因及結果在收購與兼併文獻上未有進行經驗性研究。在這個項目裡，我們將進一步研究技術型人才在收購與兼併決策中的角色，及改變雇用技術型人才是否有助於上市公司的收購與兼併決策。 近年來，矽谷大型科技公司如谷歌和臉書面臨大量人才緊缺問題。因此這些大型科技公司在矽谷以外的其他城市或洲尋找技術型人才。軼事顯示除直接雇用外，“收購”，通過購買公司以獲取他們的員工而不是其項目或資產，成為了滿足這些公司技術人才短缺需求的流行策略。在高級技術型人才短缺的時候，透過收購與兼併獲得人才，對那些對團隊而非個人更有興趣的公司來說或許是更有效的策略。然而，要準確定義“收購雇用”是比較困難的，因為收購者很少公佈其真正意圖。 在此項目裡，我們首先回答基本問題：公司是否通過收購與兼併解決其人才短缺問題？我們進行了兩項自然實驗，一項基於美國公民及移民局隨機分配的H-1B簽證，而另一項基於H-1B簽證裡對海外技術型人才的總體供應的政策衝擊。我們測試是否缺乏海外技術型人才可以導致公司進行兼併。我們的目標是在收購與兼併裡創建基於經驗的人才管道。 由於無法觀察到的混雜因素，通過比較從事並購的公司與未有從事並購公司間的業績來估計人才協同效應是有有失偏頗的。我們計畫通過另一項自然實驗解決該問題，通過比較順利完成人才並購公司的業績與因為與人才無關或無法控制因素導致人才並購未完成公司之間的業績。此經驗策略來自並購交易中量化協同效應的現有文獻。我們預計，通過使用我們的H-1B簽證微觀資料裡面的工作分類，通過完成並購交易獲取與被收購物件間人才互補的公司，長遠來看將提升其業績表現。

21502720.label: Realisation of objectives
21502720.value: All project objectives have been fully achieved using nearly the exact methodology described in the proposal that was submitted with the grant application. All research questions mentioned in the objectives were answered thoroughly. However, I refined some of my original econometric specifications and used alternative datasets to get cleaner and more compelling results. Those changes are the following: 1. In objective 2, I found that my results were stronger when only looking at M&A deals for which the transaction value were not disclosed. Firm size for private firms is typically not observable. I proxied for small (relative) size of the target firm being acquired using undisclosed transaction value as an indicator. 2. In objective 5, rather than using job posting data, I opted to measure skilled labor demand based on the proportion of STEM workers at the state and county levels. Job posting data from the company Burning Glass Technologies (now called “Lightcast”) has poor data coverage over the relevant time period in our study. 3. While the test mentioned in objective 6 were conducted, we chose not to include the results in our final published manuscript because empirical setting lacked statistical power (i.e., small sample size). Empirical results derived from achieving objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are documented in a research paper that is forthcoming the Journal of Quantitative and Financial Analysis, a top ranking finance journal (i.e., objective 7 achieved).

21502720.label: Major findings and research outcome
21502720.value: In a natural experiment based on random H-1B visa lotteries, I document that, when exposed to exogenous negative shocks to the supply of skilled workers, firms pursue more acquisitions, especially more acquisitions targeting firms that possess the skilled workers they need. I also find that acquihires are an effective means of obtaining high-skilled workers. Using employee profiles retrieved from LinkedIn and H-1B microdata, I provide direct evidence that firms acquihire high-skilled workers from target firms. To our knowledge, this is the first direct evidence that skilled workers are acquihired through M&As due to unmet skilled labor demand. I conclude that skilled labor is an important driver of acquisitions, and acquihires are an effective means of obtaining skilled workers.

21502720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21502720.value: This study advances our understanding of acquihiring but leaves some questions unanswered. For example, although the natural experiment allows us to show that shortages in skilled labor drive firms’ M&A activities, this study and previous studies cannot categorically identify which acquisitions are pure acquihires and which are not. To meet this challenge, future studies will need detailed information on the acquirers’ needs for skilled workers and more complete information on employees in the target firms. Additionally, our direct evidence of high-skilled workers based on the targets’ H-1B workers and workers on LinkedIn does not paint a complete picture of acquihiring. Future studies can continue to fill in this picture with the help of detailed information on all employees in both acquiring and target firms.

21502720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21502720.value: More and more firms have been hiring skilled workers through mergers and acquisitions rather than hiring them directly from the labor market. As competition for skilled workers intensifies, acquihiring has become commonplace in Silicon Valley and has also been widely adopted in virtually every industry. Nevertheless, academic research on acquihiring is rare. I provide causal evidence in this project that talent acquisition is conducted through M&A in response to firm-level labor shortages. For corporate executives and managers, this means that M&A is an effective way to recruit talent as it overcomes various labor market frictions such as non-compete laws. This research therefore helps expand the set of corporate human capital investment strategies.

21502820.value: 用於不確定性情形下決策的數據驅動型Hurwicz準則

21502820.label: Project Objectives
21502820.value: To revisit the Hurwicz criterion and renew it into a data-driven analytics framework for decision-making under distributional ambiguity. To incorporate distributional information of the uncertainty based on different levels of data availability. To quantify the best- and the worst-case expected losses for different combinations of loss function and distributional information. To study the potential applications of the proposed framework.

21502820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21502820.value: The Hurwicz criterion is arguably one of the most widely used rules in decision-making under uncertainty. It allows the decision maker to simultaneously take into account the best and the worst possible outcomes, by articulating a "coefficient of optimism" that determines the emphasis on the best end. The Hurwicz criterion can be viewed as a weighted average of the best and the worst uncertainty realizations. Hence, it generalizes the most optimistic Maximax criterion and the most pessimistic Maximin criterion---both are popular alternative rules for decision-making under uncertainty---in a unified manner. The classical Hurwicz criterion models uncertainty as a random variable governed by a known probability distribution. As such, the decision maker possesses perfect knowledge for precise evaluation of loss under the criterion. However, such a desirable perfection is rarely available in practice. For many real-world applications, the decision maker usually encounters a data-driven setting entailing distributional ambiguity: the distribution of the uncertainty is ambiguous and only partial knowledge, including the prior statistical information (such as support and moments) and historical observations of the uncertainty, is available. In addition, the classical Hurwicz criterion merely considers the best and the worst outcomes that may only happen with small probabilities, while neglecting all other aforementioned distributional information that is valuable for characterizing the uncertainty's ambiguous distribution. Hence, the classical Hurwicz criterion needs to be revised to address the challenge of incorporating distributional information under distributional ambiguity in emerging data-driven analytics. In this project, we plan to revisit and reformulate the Hurwicz criterion to articulate the tradeoff between optimism and pessimism under distributional ambiguity, by considering the best- and the worst-case expected losses that may arise from a family of distributions. We propose leveraging the distributionally robust optimization framework to incorporate distributional information of the uncertainty into this family based on available knowledge. 21502820.label: Realisation of objectives
21502820.value: For objective 1, I have successfully developed a general data-driven analytics framework for decision-making under distributional ambiguity. For objective 2, the proposed framework contains a generic format for a wide variety of ambiguity sets, each of which has its emphasis on modeling distributional information based on the amount of available data. For objective 3, the worst-case expectation of a loss function under an ambiguity set has been well studied in this project. Both the loss function and the ambiguity set are rich. Specifically, the result has been applied to study data-driven chance constrained programs and published in the UTD journal "Operations Research". Part of our results have been used to address adaptive optimization problems for dynamic decision-making and have been published in the UTD journal "INFORMS Journal on Computing". The best-case expectation has been well established for some special cases. These published papers acknowledge this project well. For objective 4, the proposed framework has been applied to study a stylized newsvendor problem with supply and demand uncertainty. The paper has been published in the UTD journal "Production and Operations Management". The proposed framework has also been applied to study a price-setting newsvendor problem with supply uncertainty, and we investigate the strategic interplay of two widely-used strategies---emergency supply and responsive pricing. The paper has been published in the UTD journal "Production and Operations Management". These published papers acknowledge this project well.

21502820.label: Major findings and research outcome
21502820.value: This project revisits the Hurwicz criterion and renews it into a data-driven analytics framework for decision-making under distributional ambiguity. Specifically, the framework well incorporates distributional information on the uncertainty based on different levels of data availability and well quantifies the best- and worst-case expected losses for different combinations of loss function and distributional information. The framework has been used to analyze stylized (price-setting) newsvendor problems with an emphasis on supply uncertainty. The results of this project have been published in UTD journals, including Operations Research, Production and Operations Management, and INFORMS Journal on Computing. These published papers acknowledge this project well.

21502820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21502820.value: The framework can be used to address other applications. Specifically, it can be tailored to characterize the uncertainty in each application's content, leading to a stronger reformulation and even closed-form solutions.

21502820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21502820.value: The project improves a decision-making method called the Hurwicz criterion, which helps people make choices when they don't know exactly what will happen in the future. It proposes a new, data-driven approach that uses available information to predict the best and worst possible outcomes better. This is especially useful when there's uncertainty about supply levels in a business setting. The project's significance lies in its ability to handle different amounts of data and still provide reliable predictions. This makes it a valuable tool for businesses, helping them make more informed decisions even when they face uncertainty. For example, it can help a company decide how much stock to order when they aren't sure about future supply conditions. Overall, the research offers a practical solution for improving decision-making in uncertain situations, which can lead to better business outcomes and reduced risks.

21504220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504220.value: I propose a disaster model in which the time variation comes from the speed of post disaster recovery. This model generates sizable and time varying equity risk premium. More importantly, this model quantitatively matches the two recent findings on the equity term structure, namely (1) the unconditional slope is downward and (2) the conditional level and slope are countercyclical. This model is very tractable and allows for extension into a cross sectional study of many stocks, or into a macro economy with production. It has the potential of becoming be the third workable disaster-based asset pricing framework, along with the time varying probability model of Wachter (2013) and the time varying impact model of Gabaix (2012). 此项目计划構建一個新的罕見災難模型,其中的時變因素來源於災后恢復速度。此模型能夠解釋時變股權風險溢價。同時，此模型可以解釋兩個關於股權期限結構的最新發現：(1)股權期限結構向下傾斜；(2)股權期限結構有逆週期的斜率。此模型有顯式解並可用於研究個股，或作為宏觀模型的一部分。在Gabaix(2012)和Wachter(2013)後，此模型有機會成為第三個罕見災難資產定價框架。

21504220.label: Realisation of objectives
21504220.value: The original objectives of our research project were three-fold: 1. Expanding the existing work into a full fledged general equilibrium framework fea- turing production. 2. Further expanding the work into an economy of many stocks. 3. Further expanding the work by allowing the probability of the disaster, as well as its impact to also vary over time. However, due to feedback from the journal editor, we were asked to simplify our model and focus on delivering the results. This resulted in a deviation from our original objectives. We did not include the production or the cross-section features in our work. However, we maintained the time-varying probability feature as part of our model. The main reason for this was the necessity to adhere to the journal editor's feedback. We had to simplify our model to ensure acceptance and publication. This was a significant challenge as it required us to revise our objectives and focus more on the most simple model that delivers the result. Despite this, we made attempts to overcome this problem by focusing on the core of our research - the time-varying probability feature. We believe that this feature, although a simplification of our original model, still holds significant potential for contributing to the body of knowledge in our field.

21504220.label: Major findings and research outcome
21504220.value: Our research project has provided significant insights into the disaster framework's ability to explain the time-varying equity term structure. Among the three alternative models we examined - varying recovery speed, varying disaster probability, and varying disaster impact - we found that the model with varying recovery speed was the most successful. This model was able to accurately match empirical findings, demonstrating its potential for understanding and predicting patterns in the equity term structure. The varying recovery speed model showed sensitivity to changes in the market, and was able to adapt to these changes more effectively than the other models. While the models with varying disaster probability and varying disaster impact did provide some insights, they were not as effective as the varying recovery speed model. This suggests that the speed at which markets recover from financial disasters is a crucial factor in understanding the equity term structure. These findings represent a significant step forward in our understanding of financial economics and the disaster framework. They show that the recovery speed from financial disasters is a key variable that can help us understand and predict changes in the equity term structure.

21504220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21504220.value: The findings from our research have opened up several avenues for further development. The success of the varying recovery speed model in explaining the time-varying equity term structure suggests that further exploration and refinement of this model could yield even more insights. Our proposed course of action involves a deeper investigation into the varying recovery speed model. We aim to understand why this model was more successful than the others and identify ways to enhance its predictive capabilities. This could involve incorporating additional variables or refining the existing ones to improve the model's accuracy. Additionally, we plan to revisit the other models - varying disaster probability and varying disaster impact - to see if modifications could improve their performance. We believe there is potential for these models to contribute to our understanding of the equity term structure, given the right adjustments.

21504220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21504220.value: Our research project is like a detective story that tries to understand the behavior of the stock market, specifically how the prices of stocks change over time. We looked at three possible explanations. These explanations consider different scenarios such as how quickly the market recovers after a financial crisis (recovery speed), how likely a financial crisis is to happen (disaster probability), and how severe a financial crisis could be (disaster impact). We found that the model considering the speed of recovery after a crisis was the most successful in explaining changes in stock prices. This means that how quickly the market bounces back after a crisis is a key factor in understanding stock price changes. This research is significant because it helps us understand the stock market better, which can lead to better financial decisions. It also opens the door for further research to refine these models and enhance our understanding of the stock market. In simple terms, our research is like a tool that can help us predict the financial weather and navigate the stock market more effectively.

21504720.label: Project Objectives
21504720.value: This project will provide a theoretical framework to consider imperfect competition, buyer-seller networks and global sourcing jointly. This framework is rich enough to accommodate stylized facts regarding buyer-seller networks (such as negative degree assortativity), firm sourcing (such as a pecking order), and imperfect competition (such as the bilateral markup). This project will provide reduced-form evidence for the model prediction. We will exploit changes in the market structure in China and study how firms importing from China and the underlying buyer-seller network responded to such a shock. This project will provide a method to estimate the model structurally. We will develop a new algorithm to solve and estimate the model using Chinese and French data. This project will investigate the impact of trade liberalization, deregulation, and lower matching friction on buyer-seller networks, individual firms' sourcing behaviour and productivity, and consumer welfare. Our estimated model permits rich counterfactual simulations for different policy scenarios and allows us to evaluate their impact.
