21504720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504720.value: In the past few decades, the fragmentation of production across national borders has given rise to the global value chain. Firms can now source inputs from the global market. Recent studies using micro-level trade data have allowed us to uncover new features of the underlying buyer-seller networks of trade. One of the most striking features of these networks is the dominance of large firms: the bulk of trade is between large firms which trade with many other firms. These phenomena call for novel frameworks to study firms' sourcing behaviour. This project aims to provide a new model with endogenous buyer-seller networks and imperfect competition in global sourcing. By exploiting panel datasets of firm production and transactional level trade data from China and France, we will estimate the model and use it to address the following new questions. How do firms exert market power in the presence of matching frictions with their buyers or sellers? How does imperfect competition shape the network structure and firms' sourcing behaviour? What are the pro-competitive gains by inducing tougher competition among buyers/sellers and the welfare gains from better matching between buyers and sellers? To that end, we first develop a new quantifiable international trade model with (i) two-sided buyer-seller heterogeneity, (ii) matching frictions, and (iii) oligopolistic competition upstream. Combining highly disaggregated data on firms and trade transactions for China and France, and exploiting exogenous variation in the market entry in China, we will present empirical evidence in line with the model that cannot be rationalized without features (i)-(iii). Downstream buyers import higher volumes and quantities at lower prices when upstream markets become more competitive. These effects are stronger for larger buyers and smaller when input suppliers are very heterogeneous. They also vary systematically with the elasticity of substitution across upstream input varieties and downstream output products. Our quantifiable model permits rich counterfactual analysis. The model allows us to assess the consequences downstream of upstream industrial policy and trade liberalization under different market structures and quantify the contributions of forces (i)-(iii). It also allows us to study the impact of lower barriers to entry upstream, lower matching costs and lower trade costs on firm productivity, firm size distribution, network structure, and aggregate welfare. These effects operate through a combination of matching of buyers and sellers, changes in the number of input varieties, and variable mark-ups. 在过去的几十年中，跨国界的生产分散孕育了全球价值链。企业现在可以从全球市场获取投入。最近使用微观贸易数据进行的研究使我们能够发现买卖双方贸易网络的新特征。这些网络最引人注目之一的特征是大公司的优势：大部分贸易是在大公司与其他公司之间。这些现象要求学者们采用新的框架来研究企业的采购行为。该项目旨在提供一个新的具有内生买卖网络和不完全竞争的全球采购模型。通过利用微观企业面板数据集和交易级别的贸易数据，我们将估算模型并将其用于解决以下新问题。在与买方或卖方发生匹配摩擦的情况下，企业如何运用市场力量？不完全的竞争如何影响网络结构和企业的采购行为？通过在买方/卖方之间进行更激烈的竞争以及更好的匹配而获得的福利收益是什么？ 我们为此首先构建一个可量化的国际贸易模型，该模型具有下列几个特征（i）买卖双方的异质性，（ii）匹配摩擦，以及（iii）上游寡头竞争。利用高度细分微观公司和贸易交易数据我们将为模型提供经验证据。我们的量化模型允许进行丰富的反事实分析。该模型使我们能够评估在不同市场结构下上游产业政策和贸易自由化的下游后果，并量化力量（i）-（iii）的贡献。它还使我们能够研究降低进入上游的壁垒，降低匹配成本和降低贸易成本对企业生产率，企业规模分布，网络结构和总体福利的影响。

21504720.label: Realisation of objectives
21504720.value: Thanks to the support of the research grant, all the objectives of the research project laid out in the proposal have been realized. The details are stated as follows. (1). The first objective is to build a theoretical framework to study imperfect competition in the global production network, which can reconcile stylized facts. To achieve this objective, we have first established three new stylized facts on the production network using data from China, France, and Chile (acquired during the project via the Chilean coauthor Oscar Perello). We show that there is imperfect competition among upstream firms (fact 1) in the production network, which is very sparse (fact 2), accompanied by input prices, which tend to be lower for more diversified buyers (fact 3). Motivated by these facts, we then set up a model of a bipartite production network, with oligopolistic competition between upstream firms and monopolistic competition between downstream firms. We characterize the optimal sourcing strategy for the downstream buyers and pricing strategy for the upstream sellers. The model makes several interesting predictions, including (i) more productive buyers tend to buy from suppliers, which helps induce tougher competition among the suppliers and lower markup; (ii) if there is entry upstream, it induces downstream buyers to source more inputs from upstream suppliers, with the effect stronger for high-productivity downstream buyers, (iii) when there is a reduction in variable or fixed cost of sourcing, downstream firms benefit as well, but the effect is stronger for the mid-productivity buyers. (2) The second objective is to provide reduced-form evidence for the model prediction. We exploit changes in the market structure in China across products and study input sourcing by French and Chilean firms importing from China. We examine three outcomes, including the value, the quantity, and the price of imports. We find that French and Chilean firms import more at higher quantities and lower prices for products, with more Chinese firms entering the export market. Consistent with the model, the effect is larger for the high-productivity downstream buyers. These results are robust to alternative measures, samples, and estimation using instrumental variables. (3) The third objective is to develop a new algorithm to solve and estimate the model. Based on the algorithm by Antras et al. (2017) and Arkolakis et al. (2023) for combinatorial binary discrete-choice problems, we first develop a new algorithm to solve combinatorial binary discrete-choice problems. Based on that, we quantify the model and estimate its key parameters using the Chilean data from which we observe trade data at the buyer-seller level, including the fixed cost of sourcing by the simulated method of moments. (4) The final project objective is to conduct policy evaluations by counterfactual simulations. Based on the estimated model, we change model parameters that capture trade policy, industrial structure, and matching frictions between upstream and downstream firms. We then investigate their effect on downstream sourcing outcomes and consumer welfare.

We are submitting the paper to the top 5 journals. For future research, the following directions can be pursued. First, our framework can be further extended to study bilateral oligopolies and consider endogenous production networks with market power on both sides. Second, our numerical method can be applied to study other multinomial discrete choice problems, such as optimal team size or the optimal number of subsidies within each country.

21504720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21504720.value: This project studies how companies of different sizes and levels of competition in global production networks impact trade and economic benefits. It finds that larger, more productive companies benefit most from competitive suppliers, leading to better deals and lower prices. Reducing barriers to entry and trade costs can further boost productivity and overall economic well-being. These findings can inform policymakers, businesses, and our understanding of the global economy.

21505520.value: 多渠道零售商-產品展示銷售策略

21505520.label: Project Objectives
21505520.value: To incorporate strategies used by omnichannel retailers into a multi-stage, omnichannel assortment optimization problem. To construct efficient algorithms which compute optimal or approximately optimal assortments for both the online store and the physical store, given that the decisions for each store can affect the operations of the other store. Where relevant, the algorithms may also customize the online assortment for each customer. To extract managerial insights on the optimal or approximately optimal assortments for both stores and gain a better understanding of how an omnichannel retailer can select assortments that reflect the strengths of each retail channel and that integrate the operations of both channels. To verify my models and the performance of my algorithms on industry data.

21505520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505520.value: Online shopping is popular and many retailers operate both online and offline in order to stay competitive. Operating two retail channels in the form of an online store and a physical store lets a retailer experiment with new strategies to improve revenue. Instead of treating the two retail channels as competitors, a retailer can make joint operating decisions that utilize the unique strengths of each channel. Such a retailer is known as an omnichannel retailer. In this proposal, I study assortment optimization in the context of two strategies that can help an omnichannel retailer improve his total revenue across retail channels. The first strategy recognizes that customers are more likely to make impulse purchases in a physical store. A retailer can redirect demand from his online store to his physical store by offering a Buy-Online-Pickup-In-Store option with discounts, so that customers can choose to wait for the product to ship or pick up the product immediately at the store. When customers choose the latter option, the retailer may earn supplementary revenue if customers purchase additional products at the store. Apart from deciding on assortments for each retail channel, the retailer also selects a subset assortment that is available across both retail channels to offer under BOPS, in order to encourage customers to visit the physical store. The second strategy recognizes that the retail space to operate a physical store is expensive and limited. Suppose products consume some combinations of resources when they are sold. A physical store can only display a small assortment and carries limited inventory of resources to assemble products. Although an online store is not subject to these limitations, research shows that customers prefer visiting a physical store when the products can be experienced with the five senses. Hence, a retailer can use the smaller assortment in his physical store to advertise his online store. I consider the assortment optimization problem of an omnichannel retailer faced with customers who arrive over time to his physical store. The retailer offers each customer an in-store assortment, as well as a discounted, larger assortment if she switches to the online store. In essence, the retailer uses his assortments and promotions to redirect demand to the unconstrained online store. For each of these problems, I will present approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees. I will extract managerial insights to understand the structure of the optimal assortments in the two retail channels. 為適應當前流行的網上購物消費方式，許多零售商同時運營網上與實體兩種渠道以維持競爭力。同時運營兩種渠道也使得零售商可以嘗試不同的銷售策略來進一步提高營收。與其視網上和實體兩種銷售渠道為對立競爭關係，零售商更可利用兩種渠道各自的獨特優勢去進行聯合運營決策，這樣的零售商被稱為全通路零售商。此項目主要研究全通路零售中的品類優化策略，以幫助零售商提高兩種渠道的總營收。 項目考慮的第一種策略主要基於實體渠道更容易引起消費者的消費衝動的這一實證結果。零售商通過提供一個“網上購買實體店取貨”的優惠折扣選項，引導更多網上購物的消費者在購物產品之後光臨實體店鋪。在其光臨實體店鋪取貨的時候，部分消費者會購買額外的產品，從而增加零售商的營收。除了在網上和實體兩個渠道各自有產品的品類優化策略之後，零售商也選取其中的某些產品同時開放於兩種渠道，用於“網上購買實體店取貨”的折扣優惠，以吸引網上消費者光臨實體店鋪。 第二種策略出發點在於實體店鋪通常面積有限而且租金昂貴。此情況下實體店鋪通常只能展示小部分的產品品類。相比而言，網上品類展示並不存在這一限制。然而，現有研究表明，消費者更傾向於訪問實體店鋪以獲得對產品的感官認識。因此，零售商可通過實體店鋪的少量品類展示以達到宣傳其網上店鋪的效果。在這一策略的研究中，本項目研究在消費者不定期訪問實體店鋪的情況下，全通路零售商如何採取最優的品類優化策略。在提供實體店少量品類展示的同時，零售商也提供大量的網上品類展示以及折扣優惠鼓勵消費者轉移到網上渠道進行消費。本質上，此策略通過實體店品類展示和營銷，將線下需求引導到沒有展示面積限制的網上渠道。 針對以上兩種策略，本項目著重研發具有準確性保證的近似算法。在此基礎上，本項目也將提煉管理層面的洞見，以更好理解全通路銷售中品類優化的最優策略的結構。

21508520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21508520.value: Derivative contract trading can change the properties of the underlying asset return process. These effects are appreciated by market practitioners but under appreciated in the academic literature, so there is a gap in our understanding of feedback effects from derivative markets to underlying asset markets. Simple models of option pricing which reflect the economics of financial market intermediation make rich predictions about the exact conditions which give rise to option markets changing the properties of stock markets. The direction and magnitude of this effect can be captured by the sign and size of market makers gamma exposure. In this proposal I suggest how to formally test the hypothesis of whether trader gamma-exposure can affect the volatlity of the underlying asset. 衍生品合約交易可改變標的物收益過程。業界對此機制已有較多共識而現有文獻缺乏相關探討，所以我們需要進一步理解衍生品交易對標的資產的反饋作用。期權定價模型可以反映金融市場中介的經濟學機制並給出關於期權可能改變股票市場屬性的具體條件的理論預測。衍生品對標的資產反饋作用的方向及大小可以反映在做市商伽瑪敞口的方向和大小。本開題報告將具體介紹如何實證檢驗交易者伽瑪敞口影響標的物波動這一假說。

21508920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21508920.value: 企業社會責任報導品質: 衡量、動機與效果

21508920.label: Project Objectives
21508920.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a firm-level time-varying measure of discretionary CSR reporting quality. This measure has the potential to assess the extent to which CSR reporting reflects a firm’s underlying CSR activities and performance. I will build this measure using large-scale textual analysis of the standalone CSR reports prepared by US-listed firms and obtain the qualitative information that is unexplained by firms’ CSR performance. Based on the measure developed, the determinants of discretionary CSR reporting quality will be examined. Managers have discretion over reporting through accrual-based and real earnings management activities. To extend this stream of literature, I will use a discretionary CSR reporting quality measure to examine how firms’ choices of financial versus non-financial manipulation activities vary as a function of firms’ ability to use accrual and real activities management. In addition, I will examine the compensation contracting role of CSR reporting quality. It has been a prevalent practice in corporate governance to integrate CSR criteria into executive compensation contracts. This project will examine whether CSR contracting alters managers’ utility functions and thus affects CSR reporting quality. To examine whether CSR reporting quality yields capital market effects, this project will examine the link between discretionary CSR reporting quality and the cost of capital and ownership structure. Overall, this project will contribute to three lines of accounting literature: CSR disclosure, textual analysis, and compensation contracting. The results will provide policy implications for nonfinancial reporting for regulators and standard setters.

21508920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21508920.value: Disclosure of nonfinancial information has become a mainstream business issue and policy tool (KPMG, 2017). While prior accounting research primarily focuses on the issuance of standalone corporate social responsibility (CSR) reports, CSR materiality, and value implications from the shareholders’ perspective (Dhaliwal, Li, Tsang, and Yang, 2011; Grewal, Hauptmann, and Serafeim, 2018; Khan, Serafeim, and Yoon, 2016), it is relatively unknown whether CSR reporting accurately reflects the firm’s CSR activities and provides unbiased information to stakeholders. This project will propose a new measure of CSR reporting quality and, based on the measure, provide the first large-scale evidence on the underlying incentives and effects of CSR reporting quality. To overcome the challenges of measuring CSR reporting quality (i.e., the multidimensional nature of CSR activities, qualitative CSR reporting, and dual endogeneity of CSR activities and disclosures), this project will use a topic modeling approach to identify the topics discussed in firms’ CSR reports and then construct a disclosure score (based on, e.g., readability and tone) using the narratives for each topic. Next, this project will map the ESG performance scores from MSCI ESG Ratings Database to each CSR topic, and the portion of the topic-specific disclosure score that is unexplained by CSR performance will be determined as discretionary CSR reporting quality. Based on the discretionary CSR reporting quality measure, this project will test three hypotheses regarding the association between CSR reporting quality, reporting incentives, and capital market effects. First, as prior research shows substitution between accrual and real activities management (Cohen and Zarowin, 2010; Zang, 2012), this project will examine the circumstances under which firms are more likely to engage in CSR reporting management. Second, this project will examine the contracting role of CSR reporting quality. As CSR compensation contracting has become prevalent over time (Flammer, Hong, Minor, 2018), this project will examine whether managers have incentives to manipulate CSR reporting for personal gain. Third, to extend the research on the issuance of CSR disclosure (Dhaliwal, Li, Tsang, and Yang, 2011), this project will take further steps to examine the effects of CSR reporting quality on firms’ cost of capital, ownership structure, and other capital market effects. Overall, this project will contribute to the literature on CSR disclosure, compensation contracting, and textual analysis. Moreover, it will provide policy implications for regulators and standard setters regarding the development of a transparent CSR information environment, which can enhance stakeholder discipline and strengthen the social impact of CSR.

21602920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21602920.value: This research asks how knowledge systems of urban climate resilience work in three Thai secondary cities: Khon Kaen, Udon Thani, and Ubon Ratchathani. Drawing upon insights from the field of Science and Technology Studies, this project takes the view that science is a social activity and knowledge production is historically contingent and contested. Therefore, my research will seek to find out the ways in which and whose knowledge is produced and then used to shape resilience trajectories. The research will also focus on how scalar politics affects urban climate resilience in three cities, particularly by what means global and national narratives about resilience influence knowledge production in these cities. This research is significant both academically and practically. Globally, those most vulnerable to climate change live in small- and medium-sized cities. However, researchers and policymakers alike have devoted more attention to megacities. Concurrently, international donors, agencies, and NGOs have been pushing forward the resilience agenda in urban governance. Resilience is being discursively utilized not only to represent the city and its residents, but also to frame policy responses to climate change and legitimate certain types of knowledge. However, most literature assumes that scientific knowledge is the primary source of credible knowledge needed to build urban climate resilience. Rarely are the ways in which science is created or challenged as a knowledge claim examined. Also, what is ignored is how scientific knowledge has become embedded within larger system of knowledge and power. This research fills both gaps. Further, a number of global rankings as well as widespread deaths and losses from floods and droughts earlier this year suggest that Thailand is highly vulnerable to climate change. The three selected cities face climate risks now and for the foreseeable future. Therefore, considering ways to improve their knowledge systems for climate resilience is of practical importance. To map out these systems, I will conduct a social-network analysis and analyse narratives promoted by actors and the distribution of ‘claimed’ expertise. To obtain data, I will conduct interviews with organisations whose actions affect knowledge of and actions affecting urban climate resilience, study scientific tools and assessments which help generate and maintain specific knowledge affecting urban resilience, undertake observations in meetings concerning urban climate, and analyse key documents. I hope my findings will enable state and international actors to better identify contrasting knowledge claims, improve the design and capacity of knowledge systems, and become more reflexive. N/A

21603520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21603520.value: 民主通常被概念化為一種政府體系，將高水平的選舉競爭與自由主義原則相結合，例如對行政權力的限制和對個人權利的規定。然而，實證研究表明，世界上存在著多種民主觀念，不同國家的公民對民主的看法或期望往往大相徑庭。 民主的公共概念值得學術關注，因為它們與民主合法性的概念緊密地交織在一起。當民主國家達不到公眾的期望時，公民對民主作為一種政府形式的幻想就會越來越幻滅，他們可能會更容易接受威權主義的信息。但是，由於現有的獎學金主要將民主概念作為結果而不是作為解釋性因素，因此它常常忽略了民主概念的含義。人們對民主的理解如何塑造他們評估其國家績效的方式？這些理解如何影響公眾對民主作為政府系統的支持？這些基本的理解如何與政治行為聯繫在一起？ 我提出的項目將通過一項針對印尼的研究來解決這些問題，該研究針對的是印度尼西亞，亞太地區經濟和政治力量不斷增強以及作為世界第三大民主國家。為了調查印度尼西亞的政治話語中現在盛行著哪些民主思想，以及這些思想如何隨著時間演變而來，我將對各個歷史時期印度尼西亞知名政治人物撰寫的文本進行定性的內容分析。為了研究大眾中民主概念的結構，以及它們與各種態度構造（例如對民主和政治伊斯蘭的滿意度）之間的關係，我將對印度尼西亞人口的大量有代表性的樣本進行調查，並進行一系列面對面對面的採訪。 擬議項目將為全球民主討論提供三項主要貢獻。首先，該項目將闡明人們對民主的普遍理解，對民主績效的評估以及政治合法性之間的聯繫。其次，該項目將開發一種研究公眾民主觀念的新方法，其概念框架從民主實踐的選舉，自由，協商，參與和平均主義角度考慮人們對民主的看法。第三，該項目將有助於我們對印度尼西亞這個民主機構表現出韌性和脆弱性跡象的國家有所了解。

21604520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21604520.value: The urban public realm includes all spaces which anyone can normally freely access, even if time or conditional restrictions exist - parks, open spaces, streets, housing estates, and privately owned public spaces. An effective public realm is essential for urban life. City governments strategically manage the public realm, to ensure its benefits are ‘appropriately’ distributed between its multiple stakeholders. To achieve this requires coordinating service delivery mechanisms managed by multiple organisations – ‘police’, ‘street cleansing’ and ‘transport’. This is a major challenge and requires not simply cross-departmental cooperation but strategic goal-setting and leadership. Hong Kong’s public realm complexity, congestion, and lack of transparent decision-making, makes the challenge acute. The research will identify, in Hong Kong, issues in the public realm important for its users, why they value those aspects, and what the perceived performance in those aspects are. Deploying the technique of Value Network Analysis (VNA) in an innovatively adapted form, we will examine how government roles, mechanisms and actions affect that performance in selected important aspects. A four-stage multi-method qualitative research design is adopted. Stage 1 Literature Review will identify the performance dimensions of public space governance regimes in selected cities, and investigate recent public realm developments in Hong Kong. Stage 2: Focus Groups will identify Hong Kong-specific performance dimensions, and the perceived performance in each dimension. Stage 3: Four Case Studies will analyse in depth selected dimensions which are important but currently perform poorly, and thoroughly investigate this for four contrasting locations. Stage 4: Action research workshops with key government departments will both inform the research design and share interim findings while obtaining data on the value network on the ‘service production’ side. The intellectual contribution of this research is twofold. First, the use of VNA to attribute public realm ‘performance’ to governance roles, mechanisms and actions in Hong Kong, is new. Second, the use of VNA refines the theory on which its use is based, a practical ‘value theory of public realm governance’, where governance = ‘management of the distribution of values’. Governance impacts are built into the methodology from the outset. Involving government actors in this action research can be a basis of a much-needed mechanism for dialogue between government and citizens about city management. The research reframes governance processes to focus on providing a user-focused service encounter, prioritising what users value, rather than management organisations’ administrative convenience. 城市公共領域是任何人，即使存在時間或條件上的限制，都可以自由使用的空間。這些空間包括公園、開放或休憩空間、街道、屋苑和私有公共空間。有效的公共領域對城市生活至關重要。為確保「適當地」分配各持份者的利益，各個市政府都會有策略地管理公共領域。因此，由多方管理的服務提供機制需要互相協調 - 當中包括 「警方」、「街道整潔」和「運輸」。這是一項重大挑戰，不僅需要跨部門的合作，還需要有效地制定目標和領導。 香港公共領域決策複雜，死板以及缺乏透明度，使這項挑戰變得更加困難。 這研究將識辨使用者在香港公共領域中視為重要的事項，其原因及意識到的表現。我們將以價值網絡分析（Value Network Analysis [VNA]）為基礎的創新形式來探討政府如何從角色，機制和行動在選定的重要方面上影響績效。 我們採用四階段的多模定性方法來設計本研究。 第一階段：以文獻綜述確定選定城市公共空間管理體制的效能層面，並查探香港公共領域的近期發展。 第二階段：以焦點小組確定香港特有的效能層面，以及他們在各個層面上意識到的成效。 第三階段：以四個案例深入分析選定重要但目前表現不佳的層面，並將針對四個對比地點進行徹底調查。 第四階段：與政府主要部門進行研討會為研究設計帶來意見，另一方面分享中期結論，同時也可在“服務生產”方面上獲取價值網絡的數據。 這項研究將會在學術上帶來雙重貢獻。其一，透過VNA方式把公共領域「效能」歸因於香港的施政角色，機制和行動是新的。其次，VNA可在此完善其使用的基礎理論，即務實的「公共領域管治價值理論」，施政 =「價值分配管理」。 施政影響從始至今是我們研究方法中的一部分。政府在本行動研究的參與可成為其與公民之間在有關城市管理上的對話基礎。這項研究可望重組施政流程，令其可專注提供以公共領域使用者為本的服務體驗，優先考慮他們的需求，而不是管理一方的行政便利。

21604820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21604820.value: The Song dynasty (960–1279) in Chinese history was a period that saw many transformative developments. These include the consolidation of a literati official class and literati culture, the rise of a print culture, and turbulent political upheavals brought on by foreign invasions and power struggles at the imperial court. This is a transformative and critical period in elite Chinese culture that sculpted most of what researchers know about the socio-cultural life of the traditional Chinese scholar-officials. These scholar-officials were constantly rotating in the empire's bureaucratic posts, and in order to communicate they had to write each other regularly. The writing of such personal letters has been an archaic practice, yet the methods of letter writing were never stagnant and impacted the cultural and social exchanges of the elites in China. Letters have not only become an increasingly important and sophisticated literary genre, but also the means of constructing a common cultural knowledge, a medium for ideas to transmit, and above all, an important form of communication of political and personal information among these “men of letters” in Song China. Most scholars who have worked on Chinese letters have simply mined them as a source of information for historical or literary research. In contrary, this project considers how they functioned as letters, a unique and powerful means of communication, through interpolating the writing practices that underpin the production of these documents. Other than these transcribed texts in the transmitted corpus, almost 400 manuscript letters are still extant from this period. The letters in these calligraphic collections are an extremely useful source of Song epistolary writings since they preserve not only the textual content, but also the letters' original form. This project will compile an annotated digital catalogue, to be disseminated for public access, of information about these Song epistolary manuscripts. Based on this useful information, the project also maps and analyzes digitally the social networks exemplified in these epistolary manuscripts, and presents those results in contextual and interpretive studies about Song epistolary culture and networks. The digital analysis is conducted by linking the manuscripts with biographical information in existing datasets, then visualizing them with the social network analysis software Pajek. In short, this project adopts a multidimensional research approach for profiling and examining the networks in epistolary manuscripts, especially drawing upon methods and concepts from social networks analysis in studying the relationships of letter writers and their communicative practices. 宋代是中國歷史上文化繁榮、社會發生重大變革的時代。當時官府右文崇儒，印刷術逐漸流行，士人文化繁盛；不過，終宋一代外患不止，朝廷內部鬥爭不斷。這時代塑造了中國的士大夫階層，是中國傳統精英文化的巔峰。士人在中央和地方崗位間輪調，不斷遷轉流動，往往要和千里之外的相識、家人溝通聯絡，所以互通書信傳遞消息不斷。當然，古人寫信的傳統遠早於有宋一代，寫信的方式、習慣也一直變化。這種「書信文化」，可視作中國文化精英進行溝通和社交的核心模式，富有文化史、社會史方面意義。作為文體，書信的重要性在文學昌盛的宋代一再提升；作為建構共同知識的方式，作為傳播思想的媒介，以及作為交流私人和官府資訊的工具，書信在當時也有著越來越大的重要性。過去史家研究尺牘書疏，往往只用作研究特定課題之史料來源，或視為古人文學創作的一個門類。本研究計劃則直接審視書信的作用，並集中探討宋人寫信的具體行為和過程。宋人留下之手札及手札之複製本（如拓本），約有四百之數——這些作為書法作品流傳下來的珍品，不只為我們揭示當時書信的內容，還保存了書信原來形制的寶貴面貌。這些材料對研究宋代書信文化非常珍貴，故本研究計劃會一一為之著錄，進行數碼編目，然後在網絡上公佈，供學界參考。根據編目的數碼資訊，本研究計劃還會進行社會網絡分析，並放在宋代書信文化和士人網絡的語境中討論，擬出相關研究論文，以求學界指正。進行社會網絡分析，是需要利用特定軟件，把書信的數碼資訊連接到現存的中國傳記資料庫數據，作人物社交網絡的視覺呈現，再合而觀之。總而言之，本研究計劃利用新的數碼工具，針對宋人手稿和拓本材料，以多視角審視當時之尺牘書疏和士人網絡，務求探討其中的士大夫溝通模式和具體操作。

21604820.label: Realisation of objectives
21604820.value: The project has made significant progress towards achieving its objectives, although some challenges have affected the pace. We have successfully initiated the systematic collection, profiling, and recording of epistolary manuscripts from the Song period (960–1279). A detailed digital catalogue has been developed in Excel format, with an additional text document providing complete formatting descriptions. To date, 391 entries by 191 distinct authors have been processed and logged, including 35 entries from _Yingguang Tang Tie_ (from its extant juan 3) focusing on Mi Fu’s calligraphy and 356 entries from collections such as Xu Bangda’s seminal _Gu Shuhua Guoyanlu_ and other sources. Each entry contains detailed information about the manuscripts, including content, dimensions, provenance, and related attributes, etc. As explained in earlier proposal and reports, these include data (whenever possible) of fields listed in Part C 12. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted research trips to Beijing and Taipei, which were crucial for gathering firsthand information and building the dataset. Travel restrictions and quarantine measures made it impossible to plan trips with certainty, further complicated by teaching responsibilities and Hong Kong’s regulations. To address this, I shifted focus to accessible resources, such as Xu Bangda’s catalogues and Nigensha Company’s works. These provided valuable data on well-known manuscripts, allowing progress on the digital catalogue. Additionally, I utilized the National Palace Museum’s Open Data offerings (https://theme.npm.edu.tw/opendata/index.aspx?lang=2) as an alternative to physical visits. While the platform does not fully cover planned fields like formatting descriptions and authenticity concerns, it served as a partial substitute. This highlights the importance of digital tools and online resources, which will remain integral to the PI’s scholarly work. The pandemic also disrupted opportunities to share findings at international conferences. For instance, I was unable to travel to the European Association for Chinese Studies (EACS) conference in 2021 to present my work on Dahui Zonggao’s use of letters for teaching, even though it was accepted. The Middle Period China conference in Yale was also severed delayed by 3 years (see Part C 9.). To address this, I engaged with local academic communities instead while I can, such as the Hong Kong Song History Reading Group. Another primary challenge of this has been the time-intensive nature of collecting and cataloging manuscripts. Ensuring that each manuscript’s attributes are thoroughly documented requires a slow and meticulous approach, which has affected the overall pace of the project. To address this, we have focused on ensuring the highest possible quality for each data entry, even if this means slower progress. Also, a number of ambiguities has arisen, including in transcriptions and in the identity of authors and receivers. Collating these naturally requires a large amount of scholarly detective work. However, the meticulous documentation process ensures the long-term value of the catalogue, which is central to this project and I believe, more importantly, for any research work on epistolary manuscripts of this period in imperial China. Preliminary analyses based on the manuscripts collected thus far have provided valuable insights into the letter-writing practices of Song literati. A key finding revolves around the frequent inclusion of attachments with letters, such as poems or physical objects to be gifted (e.g., Li Jianzhong’s “Tong Nian Tie” and Lin Bu’s “Qiu Liang Tie”). These findings highlight the gift-giving culture among literati, where physical items were often enclosed to reinforce social bonds, in addition to the calligraphic texts that were exchanged. Additionally, the range of letter recipients extends beyond literati officials to include religious figures (e.g., Mi Fu’s “Bu Er Chan Shi Tie” and Su Shi’s “Bei You Tie”). This demonstrates the diverse networks maintained by Song literati, which included both literary and religious figures. These findings align with and further develop the existing scholarship (e.g., Halperin 2006, Protass 2021). A challenge remains in fully exploring the nuances of genre overlap of poetry and letters, as many manuscripts were in hybrid forms, then were separated when compiled later into literary collections. This is one of the themes studied extensively in the project outputs. Social network analysis has begun using data from the catalogue, imported into Pajek and Gephi for visualizations. These compare manuscript relationships with those recorded in collected works (wenji), such as Quan Song wen. The challenge lies in refining methods to make them accessible to Chinese humanities scholars. Reflections on these methods have been shared through peer-reviewed presentations and workshops, fostering collaborations and promoting digital tools in the study of imperial Chinese manuscripts. In terms of consolidating digital analysis methods, the project has made substantial progress. The project team has met various issues when profiling and recording the manuscripts, and these reflections have been shared through peer-reviewed conference presentations and workshops, including occasions about middle period China, epistolary research across cultures, and the digital humanities. All these activities have facilitated discussions on the application of digital tools in the study of imperial Chinese manuscripts, helping to foster collaborations and share this project work beyond Hong Kong. In terms of educational impact, it also encouraged the adoption of digital humanities methodologies in other research and pedagogical contexts, helping the PI to train students and win awards even (see Part C 11.). The project has also initiated case studies of important manuscripts, focusing on Mi Fu’s calligraphy and its role within Song literati networks. The _Ying Guang Tang Tie_ entries have provided a strong foundation for understanding the dual role of these manuscripts as both personal communications and cultural artifacts. The primary challenge here is the time required to process and analyze each manuscript in detail with ample contextualization. Individual attention to the authors under concern require a deep understanding an takes months to develop. The diverse figures that this project is involved in studying includes primarily Mi Fu (1051-1107), Mi Youren (1074-1151), Sun Di (1081-1169), Yue Fei (1103-42), and Yang Wanli (1127-1206). Finally, based on the substantial data collected, some initial generalizations about Song epistolary culture have been made. These findings have been presented in an article and presented at various presentations, focusing on the role of epistolary manuscripts as both a communication tool and more important as a cultural artifact that was being collected and reproduced during Song China. The project has met its substantial objectives, even in face of the COVIID-19 pandemic restrictions and disruptions. The findings will contribute to the broader understanding of Song epistolary manuscripts and their role as cultural artifacts. Whenever possible, the financial support from this RGC project is duly acknowledged as required. However, not every publication outlet allows this, so this was not always possible.

By defining “letters” as personal, non-bureaucratic exchanges, the study has explored their significance in shaping literati culture, social networks, and intellectual exchanges. Case studies of figures like Mi Fu and Yue Fei and Yang Wanli, combined with data catalogues and visualizations, have revealed how letters facilitated interpersonal relationships and cultural transmission.

21604820.label: Major findings and research outcome
21604820.value: This project has made significant contributions to the study of Song dynasty epistolary manuscripts, focusing on their roles as communication tools and cultural artifacts within the literati community. Through the creation of a comprehensive digital dataset cataloguing 391 manuscripts authored by 191 individuals, this research has provided a robust foundation for understanding the interpersonal relationships and cultural practices of the Song elite. The dataset includes detailed metadata, such as authorship, recipients, formatting, script types, and authenticity concerns, facilitating any academic inquiry into middle period Chinese epistolary culture (see Part C 12. No. 1). Social network analysis, conducted using Pajek and Gephi, has visualized the interpersonal connections reflected in these manuscripts. This analysis has been compared with relationships documented in wenji (collected works), such as Quan Song wen, revealing differences between personal, informal exchanges in manuscripts and the more formalized connections often emphasized in literary collections. These findings underline the dynamic nature of Song literati networks, where letters served as a primary means of maintaining intellectual and social bonds after initial contact. Methodological insights from this analysis have been shared at international workshops and conferences, promoting the adoption of digital tools in Chinese humanities research. Case studies of key manuscripts, including those by Mi Fu and Mi Youren, Sun Di, Yue Fei, Yang Wanli, and others, have explored the dual role of letters as personal communications and collectible cultural artifacts. The _Ying Guang Tang Tie_ entries, for example, highlight how letters transcended their immediate purpose to become enduring symbols of cultural and artistic achievement in the carving of reproduced rubbings. These case studies have demonstrated the importance of letters in transmitting ideas, maintaining social networks, and shaping Song literati identity. The research findings have been disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, and presentations at key international conferences, such as the Association for Asian Studies Annual Conference, Middle Period China conference at Yale, and several epistolary research and digital humanities conferences (see Part C 8. and 9.). These activities have fostered collaborations, advanced digital humanities methodologies, and brought greater attention to the study of Chinese epistolary culture. They have also benefitted my project execution, such as bringing insights from other adjacent fields such as art history. Overall, the project outcomes has deepened our understanding of Song literati culture by situating their epistolary practices within broader social, cultural, and intellectual contexts and with the backing of the systematic collection of digital data.

21604820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21604820.value: This project has established a good foundation for further research into Song period epistolary and literati culture. Building on the catalogue of 391 manuscripts, future efforts will expand the collection by incorporating additional scattered Song literati letters. A significant focus will be placed on integrating letters from Buddhist monks, using sources like Hu Jianming’s research (2007, 2011). This will enhance our understanding of the interplay between religious and literati epistolary traditions. Further development of social network analysis (SNA) using tools like Pajek and Gephi will provide deeper insights into the relationships among literati, religious figures, and political elites. Efforts could be directed toward transitioning the catalogue into a more advanced digital platform interoperable with exisiting DH platforms to facilitate broader academic engagement and interdisciplinary collaboration. Also, building partnerships with other middle period research communities will enable cross-regional and cross-dynastic comparisons, particularly with the Jin and Yuan border regimes. These initiatives will not only deepen our understanding of Song Chinese epistolary practices but also position Chinese epistolary culture in a global context, fostering comparative research with other letter-writing traditions around the world. The project has already shown this is fertile ground for fruitful conversations.

21604820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21604820.value: This research examines the personal letters of scholar-officials (literati) during the transformative period of Song dynasty (960–1279). These letters were more than communication tools—they were vital for building relationships, exchanging ideas, and navigating political and intellectual life. By studying nearly 400 surviving manuscript letters, the project reveals how Song elites formed social networks, maintained ties, and shared knowledge across distances. The catalogued letters include details on authors, recipients, physical forms, and content, often featuring poems or gifts. These elements highlight the role of cultural expression and reciprocity in literati communication. The calligraphic forms of the letters also preserve the style and artistry of the writers, offering unique insights into how messages were crafted and received. Using digital tools like Pajek and Gephi, the project visualized the social networks embedded in these letters, uncovering the dynamic relationships among scholar-officials and other elites spanning political, cultural, translocal, and religious communities. The project ensures that these artefacts usually collected in museum collections inform our understanding of Chinese history and culture. By focusing on how these letters functioned as tools of communication and connection, this project offers new perspectives on the daily lives and social dynamics of Song elites.

21606520.label: Project Objectives
21606520.value: Kazakhstan has long been China’s ‘gateway to Central Asia’ and plays a crucial role in connecting China with Europe. This project seeks to investigate the changing state-level power dynamics and sub-national activities between the two countries, with particular attention to the issue of how state-led development plans have been affected by sub-national negotiations and sub-national activities have been shaped by the national policies. This project is also intended to fill a gap in our understanding of China’s involvement in the developing world, as the majority of the scholarly studies on China’s rise focus more on African countries than on Central Asian states. As the first comprehensive study of the political economy of China’s involvement in Kazakhstan, this study will generate insights and inform debates on China’s role in the countries participating in the BRI. As the power disparity between China and Kazakhstan is in a classic asymmetric structure, this project draws on asymmetry theory to research on the political economy of state-level interactions (Womack 2006; Anderson 2013). Moreover, as local dynamics have shaped national policies in both China and Kazakhstan, this project also draws on the theory of sub-national social conflict analysis (Rodan et al. 2001; Kneating 1999). This project is aimed at enhancing the theorization of China’s contemporary development by integrating these two perspectives and illuminating the complex set of actors and interests at work in China’s involvement in Kazakhstan. In terms of the first specific research objectives, the project will involve conducting an analysis of speeches on Sino-Kazakh relations by the respective national leaders of China and Kazakhstan from 1991 to 2021. The outcome of this phase of the research will be an understanding of the relative power dynamics between the two countries over three decades, which should be particularly illuminating in showing how the relationship changed following the introduction of the BRI in 2013. Second, the project will involve building a database of instances of both social conflicts and economic cooperation between China and Kazakhstan over the period 1991–2021, with particular attention to cooperation projects that are not related to connectivity infrastructure to produce a comprehensive dataset. This database will serve as the basis for investigating how the changing power dynamics between the two countries have led to cooperation and conflict. Third, the project will involve conducting in-depth case studies of three newly emerged Sino-Kazakh joint projects in three sectors, i.e. logistics and trade, value-added industry, and agricultural processing ventures, to illustrate both the local dynamics and the overall evolution of China’s regional involvement in Kazakhstan. In terms of academic significance, the PI will present the results at two international academic conferences and publish four high-impact journal articles on a) China’s BRI and the unbalanced Sino-Kazakh power dynamics, b) Kazakhstan’s logistics and trade development, c) Kazakhstan’s agricultural processing industry, and d) Kazakhstan’s value-added industry. The PI will also prepare a book manuscript on the political economy of China’s evolving regional involvement in Kazakhstan. In terms of impact on the primary stakeholders, the PI has enlisted the support of the Almaty Management University (AMU), the Eurasian Research Institute of the Khoca Akhmet Yasawi International Turkish-Kazakh University (ERI), and the China and Central Asian Studies Center of KIMEP University (KIMEP) to arrange focus group discussions with the relevant stakeholders in Kazakhstan, including business consultants, policymakers and economic actors. These two-way communications will also allow the PI to explore new explanations and, if necessary, adjust the research questions. In terms of impact on secondary stakeholders, the PI will publish op-ed pieces on China’s involvement in Kazakhstan in publications relevant to policymakers and the business community and give public talks on these issues for audiences such as logistics practitioners in Hong Kong and the mainland, and those involved in the logistics and trade, value-added industry and agricultural processing industry. In terms of educational impact, the proposed research project will provide invaluable opportunities for undergraduate students to work as helpers and receive training in the process of desk research and fieldwork preparation. In terms of public impact, the PI will build a research project website to share her research outcome during and after the research period, including the database of instances of Sino-Kazakh conflicts and cooperation, fieldwork journals and photo stories. The PI will also create a Facebook page and Instagram account and link them to the research web site to enhance the social impact.

21606520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21606520.value: This project seeks to give the first comprehensive picture of the political economy of China’s involvements in Kazakhstan over the past three decades, particularly since the introduction of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2013. The research is justified by Kazakhstan’s geo-strategic location for China to connect to Eurasia and the increasing co-existence of conflicts and cooperation between China and Kazakhstan. The analysis draws on two strands of the International Political Economy theories. First, the growing body of research on asymmetric state-to-state relations explains that a strong country such as China has limited attention to devote to a weaker one such as Kazakhstan, meaning that even though there is a massive power imbalance, China is likely to recognise Kazakhstan’s autonomy, and Kazakhstan is expected to show deference. But China’s BRI has given Kazakhstan more leverage to punch above its weight, and more risks to engage in a wider range of activities with China. Second, social conflict theory argues that states are increasingly fragmented, and the co-existence of conflicts and cooperation can only be explained by investigating the sub-national dynamics and how they shape national policy on the ground. These two sets of state-to-state and sub-national hypotheses will be tested in part through systematic tracing of state-level and sub-national dynamics by desktop research of national speeches, government reports, statistics, literature, and local newspapers in China and Kazakhstan. This will be supplemented and triangulated by fieldwork to investigate the reality on the ground of Chinese involvements in Kazakhstan, featuring in-depth interviews with local stakeholders, industrial practitioners, and focus groups. 哈薩克地處連接歐亞大陸要塞，近期與中國的經濟合作和社會矛盾與日俱增。有見及此，本研究是首個調研項目，集中分析過去30年間，尤其針對2013年一帶一路計劃開展前後，中國在哈薩克各種政經項目的發展。 本研究結合兩個當代國際政治經濟研究理論，為調研建立了一個雙視角的立論和分析基礎。一、基於「國際不對等關繫理論」，中國和哈薩克國力懸殊，中國過去一直沒有刻意經營與哈薩克的雙邊關繫，僅以尊重哈薩克的獨立主權，保持友好距離 ; 哈薩克也樂於認同中國的強勢地位，以維持穩定的政治格局。然而，當中國高調開展一帶一路政策時，雙方的關繫卻出現了微妙的變化 : 因為中方的積極，哈薩克享有更大的談判籌碼，成功向中國爭取更多有利經濟發展的合作空間，同時而亦承擔了更多社會風險。二、「社會矛盾理論」指出，國家在執行政策時經常出現失控和分裂的局面。故此，要深入瞭解國家政策如何影響社會的各種合作和矛盾，必須具體調研地方持份者的博弈行為。 綜觀國家和地方持份者兩個層面，本研究將有系統地收集中哈雙方的量性和質性數據，包括國家領導人致辭、政府報告、統計、文獻和報章等 ，輔以田野考察，與當地持份者和業內人士進行深人訪談和焦點小組討論，全面分析中國一帶一路對哈薩克經濟和社會發展的影響。

Utilizing 7,791 Chinese and 1,089 Kazakhstani articles and documents, the PI has completed a process tracing of state-level Sino-Kazakh relations and the sub-national implementation of Chinese projects in Kazakhstan during this period. 21606520.label: Major findings and research outcome
21606520.value: China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is often criticized as a strategic move to enhance China's global influence. Many initiatives have emerged from local actors and have been shaped by national politics, provincial subsidies, and market-oriented actors from China and Kazakhstan. Focusing on under-researched projects in Kazakhstan, this research reveals the complexities of China’s footprints in Kazakhstan. Four significant findings are elaborated as follows: 1. Kazakhstan's Leverage of China’s BRI for Economic Diversification: Over the past 30 years, Kazakhstan has adopted a multi-vector approach to balance relations with great powers like Russia and China. Kazakhstan’s oil-driven sovereign wealth funds and the public demand for responsible policies have further empowered Kazakhstan to leverage Chinese capital to diversify its economy (See research output 8-1,3,5; 9-3,4,5,9,11; 12-1,2,4,5). The following three case studies further illustrate this diversification. 2. China-Europe Freight Train Services: The unification of the China-Europe freight train network has led to a service surge with aggressive pricing and challenging operators. These operators have expanded their roles to explore trading opportunities between China, Europe, and Central Asia. By engaging with potential clients in Kazakhstan, they facilitate exports of products like grains, meat, and wine to China, resolving issues related to customs and packaging and opening business opportunities for local actors (See research output 8-2, 9-7) 3. Agricultural and Food Processing Sector: Kazakhstan has tried diversifying its economy by developing industrial policies and investing in agriculture and food processing. Initiatives like the State Agriculture and Food Programme and the establishment of KazAgro reflect this commitment. By comparing Western aid programs with China's investments from 2003 to 2023, this research highlights the shortcomings of state-level engagements, which often overlook Kazakhstan’s unique agricultural structure. A market-oriented initiative by China's Xi’an AiJu Cereals and Oil Industry Group demonstrates the potential for demand-driven projects benefiting local farmers (see research output 8-6; 9-2,8,10; 12-3,6). 4. Automobile Development: Kazakhstan's automobile sector exemplifies state-backed efforts to diversify the economy. From 2003 to 2023, Kazakhstan's multi-vector engagements with Japan, China, and Europe have enhanced its bargaining power. China's BRI has enabled Kazakhstan to join the global automobile value chain. Improved local perceptions of Chinese investments have facilitated industrial policies for localization and capacity building. A case study of a Sino-Kazakh joint venture underscores the importance of a multi-vector approach in product diversification (see research output 8-4; 9-2,6)

21606520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21606520.value: The PI has completed all research activities. She has co-edited a special issue and published three high-ranking peer-reviewed articles, with one more accepted, and two more articles under review. She presented at 12 international conferences and seminars in Kyoto, Taipei, Shenzhen, London, Toronto, the Netherlands, Almaty, and Astana. Additionally, and has contributed essays to think tanks, academic online forums, and magazines. Her research has been featured in two local newspapers. To further amplify these impacts, she has developed a website that will be regularly updated with new outputs. The PI plans to integrate findings from this project with her other GRF research on China's international development in Mongolia, aiming to offer a comprehensive contribution to global China studies. Her third GRF research on China's technology transfer to Thailand is currently under review; if approved, it will further enhance her research impact with insights from both Central and Southeast Asia. Future extensions of the research in Kazakhstan could explore China's green energy initiatives and the burgeoning e-commerce platform economy, providing a holistic view of China's multifaceted influence. She is also preparing a book proposal on China's role in Kazakhstan's economic diversification, which promises to deepen understanding in this field.

21606520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21606520.value: This research project explores the complex dynamics of China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in Kazakhstan, challenging the notion that it is solely a strategic move to expand China's influence. Instead, it highlights how local actors in Kazakhstan have leveraged the BRI to diversify their economy, particularly in sectors like agriculture, freight services, and automobile manufacturing. The study reveals that Kazakhstan has used Chinese investments to balance its relationships with major powers and enhance its economic resilience. For instance, Kazakhstan has tapped into the China-Europe freight train network to boost exports and has attracted Chinese investment in agriculture, benefiting local farmers. The automobile sector has also seen growth through Sino-Kazakh partnerships, showcasing Kazakhstan's strategic use of the BRI to join global value chains. The research is significant because it provides a nuanced understanding of China's impact in Kazakhstan, emphasizing local agency and economic diversification rather than mere geopolitical influence. The findings have been widely disseminated through academic publications, conferences, and media, contributing to global China studies. Future research will delve into areas like green energy and e-commerce, offering a comprehensive view of China's multifaceted role in Kazakhstan's development.

21607020.label: Project Objectives
21607020.value: Compare and contrast discursive constructions of domestic work across stakeholders in terms of the public/private distinction in the particular case of Filipina domestic workers in Hong Kong. Investigate the impact of these different discursive constructions on differing approaches to regulating domestic work across stakeholders. Theorize the real-world impact of language and labels on transnational migrants, adding to growing sociolinguistic engagement in this area through the particular case study of institutional language that impacts domestic workers in Hong Kong. Develop a method through which the ideologies of multiple, transnational stakeholders involved in the regulation of domestic work can be compared in particular ethnographic contexts through a focus on language in response to the call for such empirically grounded comparative scholarship on domestic work. Facilitate greater collaboration between various stakeholders involved in the regulation of domestic work by providing clear descriptions of how these organizations overlap and differ from one another in their understandings and discussions of domestic work. Advocate on behalf of domestic workers by working with APMM toward “the recognition of domestic work as work” through dissemination and through the mapping of various stakeholder discourses to frameworks for achieving more just labor conditions. Improve institutional pedagogy by training undergraduate and research degree students in textual discourse analysis and in how to trace the real-world impact of institutional language.

21607020.label: Realisation of objectives
21607020.value: (1) Comparisons have been carried out between the discourses of (Filipino and other) migrant domestic worker (MDW)-led organizations, the discourses of the Hong Kong Labour Department, the Philippine Consulate, Hong Kong-based employment agencies (that place domestic workers with private employers), and the International Labor Organization (ILO). Similarities have been identified in the fact that all of these stakeholders put forward public discourses about domestic work. The difference is in how these stakeholders (do or do not) draw on the private details of the lived experiences of MDWs in constructing these public discourses. Findings reveal that the discursive constructions of domestic work coming from the MDW-led organizations strongly emphasize the details of the lived experiences of workers. In other words, these MDW organizations bring the private details of MDW lives into the realm of their public discourse. In contrast, the other stakeholders either ignore, or are much more limited in their discursive engagement with, the private details of MDW lived experience. (2) In the case of the MDW-led organizations, their deeper engagement with the details of the lived experiences of MDWs also makes them more grounded, substantive, intersectional and critical in the demands they make for the rights of MDWs. The discourses of the ILO are similar to the discourses of MDW-led organizations in that they also advocate for the rights of MDWs. However, the ILO discourses are less substantive, intersectional and critical. This is in part because they are less engaged with the details of lived experiences of MDWs, and in part because the ILO tries to frame itself as a neutral organization mediating between employers, governments and domestic workers. Employment agencies produce advertising discourses that engage with the private details of the lived experiences of employers, but ignore the private details of MDW lived experiences. As such, these agencies contribute to public perception of domestic work that covers up the real experiences of domestic workers. In a case study examined, the Hong Kong Labour Department discursively constructs an image of domestic work that relies on prototypical imaginations of the home as a place for rest rather than a workplace. These imaginations were used to put forward COVID-19 appeals that further exacerbated social exclusion for MDWs. In a case study examined, the Philippine Consulate zoomed into the details of Filipino MDW experiences when these experiences were not directly related to their failures. However, when these experiences were related to failures on the side of the Consulate, their discourses mostly ignored the detailed experiences of MDWs. (3) The unequal power between these stakeholders is important in determining the real-world impact of the language they use to describe domestic work. Governments have the most power in determining how domestic workers are regulated, and thus their discourses are the most consequential. Furthermore, case studies examined as a part of this project reveal that Hong Kong government officials may also be influenced by broader social discourses, and may draw on these discourses when proposing policies or putting forward appeals. That is, they may draw on discourses of employers claiming that domestic workers become a part of the family and want to rest at home, or on the discourses of employment agencies that advertise domestic workers as products. Thus, the role of discourse is significant in terms of its real-world impact on domestic workers. At the same time, one of the theoretical contributions of this project has been to call sociolinguists and discourse analysts to consider the ways in which discourse does not always translate into material realities. This theoretical (re)orientation (which the PI has laid out in terms of a materially oriented chronotopic approach to discourse) allows researchers to observe how discourse can also be used to ignore or cover up material realities, rather than to constitute them. (4) To contrast the Hong Kong Labour Department and the Philippines Consulate with the MDW-led organizations the PI drew on case studies of their different responses to issues arising during the COVID-19 pandemic. To compare the discourses of the ILO vs. the MDW-led organizations the research team drew from a systematic, mixed-methods, ethnographically situated analysis of a corpus of texts relating to the various forms of social exclusion domestic workers face. To analyze employment agencies the PI and RD student drew on a broad multimodal analysis of the websites of ten employment agencies in Hong Kong. Overall, this project developed a comparative approach that used in-depth ethnography with the MDW-led organizations as the pivot point around which to orient the comparisons of the multiple stakeholders. On the one hand, despite attempts to contextualize the discourses of other stakeholders within the norms for their contexts through secondary sources, the lack of participant observation with these other stakeholders is a limitation of this research. On the other hand, there are a number of strong justifications for focusing participant observation on MDW-led organizations. First, as migrant domestic workers themselves, they are the organizational stakeholders most impacted by discourses on domestic work. Second, the MDW-led organizations comment on the discourses of other stakeholders in a way that other stakeholders do not. In this sense, in-depth ethnographic research conducted with the MDW-led organizations also offered more opportunities to observe the discourses of multiple stakeholders as they intersected with the lives and concerns of migrants. (5) For the ways in which these stakeholders overlap and differ with one another see 2 above. In terms of facilitating greater collaboration between stakeholders, one of the major findings of this research is that MDW-led organizations have expertise about domestic workers that other stakeholders do not have. On the basis of this finding, one of the calls of this research has been the [continued] inclusion of MDW-led organizations in these deliberation processes. While this call has been put forward in academic papers resulting from this work, it has also been disseminated more broadly, i.e. in consultations aimed at assessing multilateral norm setting for the rights of women. (6) (a) Academic publications detailing the Hong Kong Labour Department COVID-19 appeals to MDWs, and submissions directly to the Labour Department on the issue of job-hopping, argue for the importance of recognizing domestic work as work. (b) The research has also been used to support the calls of APMM for MDW-led organizations to be more meaningfully included in multilateral decision making processes about domestic work. (c) This research has been shared with MDW-led organizations to assist them in encouraging and empowering their members to continue to speak up about their experiences and their rights. (7) See the Education Plan for details on the two undergraduate students trained through this project. In addition to these students, a research degree student, LI Yating, was also recruited and supported through this project. The PI and research degree student are currently coauthoring a manuscript on the discourses of employment agencies that will be submitted to Critical Discourse Studies. Yating will continue to develop her critical analyses of employment agency discourses for her dissertation. All of the students were also engaged in the non-academic impact aspects of the project, which also allowed them to reflect on the real-world impact of institutional language.

21607020.label: Major findings and research outcome
21607020.value: The major finding of this research is that the language of the MDW-led organizations capture details of the lived experiences of migrants in a way that the language of other stakeholders does not (see 5.3 for details). These findings were disseminated to the academic community through four journal publications, three presentations at international conferences, and two local invited academic talks (see Part C for more details). In order to achieve impact beyond academia, these findings were also disseminated through a variety of other outputs, which are detailed here. Drawing on the finding that the Hong Kong Labour Department policies about MDWs do not always attend to the details of their lived experience, the PI and her research team involved themselves in the debates about job-hopping that took place in the Spring of 2023 as an extension of the research dissemination. Their involvement included (a) A formal submission to the Labour Department (b) Distribution of a sign-on version of the submission, which received 44 sign-ons, 32 of which were academics. (c) Participation in the in-person consultation with the Labour Department, where the PI and RA shared their views. (d) Co-organizing a Migrant Advocates Press Conference, which led to the submission of our research team being quoted at length by media coverage by the Philippine news agency Rappler. A community sharing of the comparison between ILO and AMCB language, titled Why Migrants’ Language and Experience Matters was arranged for more than 100 registrants including migrant domestic workers themselves, academics, students, NGO workers and other community members. Leaders of the AMCB assessed this sharing as useful in building the confidence of their members to continue speaking about their experiences and issues. The PI was invited to participate in the Beijing +30 Asia Pacific Civil Society Consultations by her NGO collaborators the Asia Pacific Mission for Migrants (APMM). During these online consultations, the PI shared her findings as a means to call for grassroots leaders of migrant-led organizations to be well represented in multilateral assessments and decision-making. The sharings from this consultation were documented by APMM and will be drawn on in further deliberations and discussions in the 69th Commission on the Status of Women hosted by the United Nations in 2025.

21607020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21607020.value: Inspired by the research conducted through this ECS grant, the PI has been able to develop new research projects that are now funded by two separate GRFs: Research Grants Council General Research Fund, Caring transnationally: A spatiotemporal model of moral discourse and action, Principal Investigator, HKD335,840, Ongoing Research Grants Council General Research Fund, Expanding discourse analytic applications through participation in grassroots advocacy, Principle Investigator, HKD753,758, Ongoing. The first GRF builds on the relationships built over the course of this project to ethnographically investigate how the migrant-led organizations enact transnational forms of care. The second builds on the findings of this project, regarding the importance of grassroots communication about migrant domestic work, and proposes a participatory action research project to help improve the effectiveness of their communication through discourse analytic theories. In addition to these grants, the PI is engaged in ongoing discussions with migrant-led AMCB and the NGO APMM, who have expressed a desire to continue programming in Hong Kong about the importance of the language and experience of migrants. APMM has also invited the PI to consider sharing her research about the ILO in international venues, such as the Asia Pacific Feminist Forum.

21607020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21607020.value: This project compared the language used by different stakeholders to talk about domestic work and migrant domestic workers in Hong Kong. The stakeholders included the Hong Kong Labour Department, the Philippine Consulate, Hong Kong based employment agencies (who place domestic workers with their private employers), the International Labor Organization (ILO), and organizations led by migrant domestic workers themselves (i.e. the Asian Migrants Coordinating Body and United Filipinos in Hong Kong). The major finding of this research is that the language used by the organizations led by migrant domestic workers capture details of the lived experiences of these workers in a way that the language of other stakeholders does not. In contrast to the migrant-led organizations, employment agencies and government discourses either consistently or selectively ignore the lived experiences of migrant domestic workers. Even the ILO, an organization that advocates for domestic workers, produces discourses that are less intersectional, less critical and less human than the discourses produced by migrant-led organizations. These findings highlight the unique expertise that migrant-led, grassroots organizations have about domestic work, and the importance of genuinely including them in the national and multilateral discussions that impact them.

22200320.label: Realisation of objectives
22200320.value: The objectives of this project are to develop D-truss community model in directed graphs and propose efficient algorithms for D-truss community search, in terms of structural graphs, attributed graphs, and also an interactive setting with users. We have designed a D-truss community model based on the support of flow triangles and cycle triangles. We have developed fast search solutions, I/O-efficient truss-based index construction, and also the updating methods. Finally, we have conducted several case studies and implemented the prototype system to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed algorithms.

22200320.label: Major findings and research outcome
22200320.value: The major findings and research outcomes of this project can be summarized as follows. First, we systematically study several tasks of community search problems over large-scale networks, e.g., directed graphs, streaming directed graphs, weighted graphs, labeled graphs, and multilayer graphs. We present a D-truss community model using flow triangles and cycle triangles in two direct graph settings of static and streaming, which brings nice structural and computational properties against existing ones. Exact solutions and efficient approximate algorithms are proposed. In addition, we design an I/O-efficient algorithm for k-truss community search, where a graph cannot entirely fit in main memory. Moreover, we motivate a novel problem of butterfly-core community search to find cross-groups over a labeled graph. We conduct four case studies on real-world global flight networks, international trade networks, complex fiction networks, and academic collaboration networks to show the usefulness of our model and algorithms. GCN-based learning models are also developed for structural and attributed community search. Extensive experiments on million-sacle graph datasets with ground-truth communities validate that our solutions take real-time response in a few seconds to find high-quality answers. We report these findings results in ICDE'24, PVLDB'22, TKDE'22, PVLDB'21, and VLDBJ'21. Second, we have worked and developed fast solutions for dense subgraph decomposition, indexing, and maintenance, which are fundamentally useful for online community search over various graphs (e.g., directed graphs, multilayer graphs, and probabilistic graphs). We present our finding results in ICDE'24, SIGMOD'23, PVLDB'21, PVLDB'22, and WWW'21. Third, we also studied relevant community detection problems leveraging the multihop nonnegative matrix factorization and the autoencoder-like nonnegative tensor decomposition, and report these findings results in TNNLS'24 and TKDD'23. Fourth, we have also investigated the problems of top-k representatives based graph summarization, community-aware social recommendation, and an efficient framework of finding potential transmission clusters. We report these findings results in TKDE'23 and TKDD'23. Fifth, we have studied the problem of k-core and k-truss maximization using fast insertion strategies and minimum cut approaches, of which finding results have been reported in ICDE'24, PVLDB'22, and CIKM'21. Sixth, we have studied an interactive graph search task to identify multiple targets in a hierarchy using a constrained budget of interactive questions. We report this finding results in PVLDB'21. We also have developed and implemented the prototype systems for proposed community search models and conducted D-truss case studies on EAT networks.

22200320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22200320.value: The models and algorithms for D-truss community search have been developed in this project. However, several opportunities for further investigation still exist, e.g., how to further accelerate the efficiency of D-truss index construction. We will explore these directions in the future.

22200320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22200320.value: Directed graphs widely exist in nature and society, where the directed edges represent the semantic relations between nodes, such as Twitter followers in social networks, money transfer diffusions in financial networks, and communication links in email networks. Community search is useful for finding densely connected subgraphs containing query vertices, enabling personalized circle discovery. This project investigates a series of novel community search problems over directed graphs, different from previous relevant studies on undirected graphs. We propose a wide set of efficient solutions and algorithms to tackle them. For instance, we proposed a peeling-based streaming algorithm for D-truss community search equipped with three optimizations and maintained the peeling order for fast search. Moreover, we proposed distributed D-core decomposition algorithms and truss maintenance solutions for potential index updating. We explore cross-layer group search and GCN-based learning models for attribute-driven community search. To validate the efficiency and quality of proposed methodologies, we have conducted extensive experiments on real-world graph datasets with ground-truth communities. Our findings are reported in reputed international reputed journals and top conferences.

22200720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22200720.value: Trustworthy learning from corrupted data is a vital research topic in modern machine learning (i.e., deep learning), since most real-world data are easily imperfect and corrupted, such as financial data, healthcare data and social-network data. However, existing works in trustworthy deep learning (TDL) tend to implicitly assume that corrupted data should be closed set: samples with corrupted labels own true classes known in the training data; samples with the set of known classes can be crafted as adversarial examples in the testing phase; and samples in source domain share the same class of samples in target domain. Such closed-set assumption is the crux of existing TDL methods, which is too restrictive for many real-world applications. This project aims to address this conundrum by developing models, algorithms, and prototype system for trustworthy deep learning from open-set corrupted data. The outcome of the research could significantly robustify TDL techniques in open-world knowledge discovery and decision-making processes such as those in personalized medicine, financial engineering, and scientific discoveries.
