22201820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22201820.value: 本研究擬發展同時同化地表PM2.5，臭氧和二氧化氮觀測數據的技術，以獲得更好的PM2.5和臭氧濃度時空分佈特徵，以減小污染健康暴露評估和空氣質量預測的不確定度。近年來有一些基於氣象-化學耦合模型的氣溶膠資料同化研究，而針對臭氧污染的同化研究仍然較少。然而，臭氧是華南區域非常嚴峻的污染問題，對於人類健康和作物生長都有不利影響。評價空氣污染的健康、氣候和生態效應也需要準確的污染物時空分佈特徵。本研究基於之前氣溶膠資料同化基礎，旨在開發同時同化PM2.5,臭氧和二氧化氮觀測數據的技術。開發的系統將應用於華南區域獲得PM2.5和臭氧時空分佈特徵，以及評估其對華南區域空氣污染暴露風險和空氣質量預測的改善效果。

22201820.label: Realisation of objectives
22201820.value: The project objectives focus on improving spatio-temporal representations of air pollutants (PM2.5, O3, NO2) for health, climate, and ecosystem impact assessments, enhancing air quality forecasts for emergency responses, and extending the Gridpoint Statistical Interpolation (GSI) system for chemical data assimilation. Our research revealed the spatial patterns and temporal trends of the frequency, intensity, and duration of co-occurring extreme heat and air pollution. We found a significant increase in the frequency of simultaneous exceedances of wet-bulb temperature and ozone, primarily in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei and Yangtze River Delta regions. Moreover, the growth rate of these co-exceedances surpasses that of wet-bulb temperature and ozone individually. Given the potentially greater compounded public health impacts of simultaneous exposure to heatwaves and air pollution, this rising trend of co-occurring heat and ozone pollution should be recognized as an emerging environmental issue in China. Further analysis showed that the interannual variability of summertime heatwave and ozone pollution co-occurrences in China is primarily regulated by springtime warming in the western Pacific, western Indian Ocean, and Ross Sea. These sea surface temperature anomalies influence precipitation, radiation, and other factors, modulating the co-occurrence of ozone pollution and heatwaves. Consequently, a multivariable regression model was developed to predict the co-occurrence of heat waves and O3 pollution a season in advance, achieving a high correlation coefficient of 0.81 in the North China Plain. This predictive capability enables proactive emergency responses, such as public health advisories or emission controls, to mitigate the compounded health risks from heat and pollution. This supports emergency response planning. The assimilation system was improved to enable the assimilation of aerosol optical depth (AOD) data from the polar-orbiting satellite MODIS and the geostationary satellite GOCI. The AOD data of MODIS are products at the wavelength of 550nm collected by the two satellites, Terra and Aqua, over both land and ocean. The GOCI data are products obtained by the research group led by Professor Jhoon Kim of Yonsei University in South Korea based on the second-generation retrieval algorithm (GOCI Yonsei aerosol retrieval version 2 products). Compared with the first-generation products, the second-generation products have been revised in terms of cloud marking and surface reflectance calculation. To ensure an adequate amount of available data and avoid cloud interference, MODIS and GOCI data are only used when the cloud cover within each pixel is lower than 70%. By comparing with the AOD observations from AERONET in the regions of eastern China, Japan, and South Korea, the simulation results without assimilation show a significant overestimation. When only MODIS AOD data are used for assimilation, the overall improvement compared with the observations is limited. After considering the AOD data of GOCI in the assimilation system, the simulation results have been greatly improved and are closer to the AERONET observations. The most remarkable improvement is observed in the relatively less polluted region of Japan. Using the monitoring data from the China National Environmental Monitoring Centre, hourly observation data of PM2.5, PM10, O3, SO2, NO2, and CO were assimilated. Compared with the observations, the PM2.5 without assimilation is underestimated in the Beijing area and overestimated in the southern part of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. Therefore, assimilation has improved the spatial distribution characteristics of PM2.5 simulation, and the increment field is mainly concentrated in the Beijing area, with positive increment values exceeding 20 µg/m3. The O3 simulated without assimilation is overestimated in the northern part of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, resulting in negative assimilation increment values. The simulation results after assimilating the surface observations have been greatly improved, and the simulated concentrations of various pollutants are closer to the observed values. The world's first geostationary air quality monitoring instrument, the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS), can monitor pollutant information hourly across nearly 20 Asian countries. Using a multi-output random forest model and GEMS data, considering the interactive nature of air pollutants and their common influencing factors, hourly estimations of PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, CO, and SO2 concentrations in China were achieved. Compared to traditional models, this approach significantly improves modeling efficiency, enabling high-precision and high-efficiency estimation of hourly changes in Chinese air pollutants, aiding in monitoring the evolution of pollution events. The cross-validated R2 of the estimation results reached 0.94, with high accuracy verified for a severe ozone pollution event in Guangdong Province and a dust storm event in northern China. It effectively enhanced the accuracy and efficiency of pollutant concentration estimation in China and facilitated the monitoring of pollution event dynamics. The study identified key meteorological factors influencing extreme PM2.5 and O3 pollution in summer and winter. Results show that surface winds and humidity are critical drivers of particulate matter pollution in both seasons, with greater sensitivity under high pollution conditions. In winter, higher humidity promotes hygroscopic particle growth, while in summer, it reduces PM2.5 concentrations through wet scavenging. For summer O3 extremes, surface temperature is dominant, particularly in volatile organic compound (VOC)-limited regions, followed by surface winds and solar radiation. China’s unprecedented urbanization has led to severe urban heat island (UHI) issues. Aerosol pollution’s impact on UHI intensity varies with circulation patterns. When northerly winds prevail in urban Beijing, UHI intensity is significantly higher day and night, minimally affected by aerosol concentrations. However, when southerly and westerly winds dominate rural Beijing, aerosols markedly reduce UHI intensity. Reduced aerosols exacerbate urban warming and high-pressure systems, intensifying ozone pollution. Numerical simulations assessed cool and green roof strategies’ effects on winter PM2.5 pollution in North China, finding that cool roofs aggravate PM2.5 pollution in lightly polluted areas. This negative effect is reduced as pollution worsens. Green roofs, with suppressed winter evapotranspiration, have a lesser impact on enhancing PM2.5 pollution. The studies enhance the understanding of air pollution’s health impacts through detailed spatio-temporal analyses. We employed a novel individual-level assessment of UHI exposure using temperature and satellite-derived land cover data, linking a 5°C UHI increase to a 27% higher preterm birth (PTB) risk. We also integrated hourly PM2.5, NO2, O3, and temperature data from the China Birth Cohort Study, revealing nonlinear associations with PTB risk (e.g., risk ratios of 1.32–1.70 for pollutants and temperature extremes). These precise, location-specific exposure assessments improve the granularity of pollutant impact evaluations, directly supporting health and ecosystem studies. The research fully meets the objectives by providing high-resolution exposure data and predictive models, enhancing health risk assessments and enabling timely interventions, particularly for vulnerable populations like pregnant women.

22201820.label: Major findings and research outcome
22201820.value: 1. Machine Learning in Air Pollution Applications Our research used machine learning (ML) to enhance air pollution monitoring and prediction. Zhou et al.(2022) applied proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based sensor placement algorithms, identifying the QR pivot algorithm as superior for optimizing PM2.5 monitoring site locations, outperforming existing China National Environmental Monitoring Center sites by prioritizing severe pollution areas. Zhang et al.(2023b) extended this approach to methane (CH4), using QR pivot-guided sensor placement to improve reconstruction accuracy over East Asia, addressing underrepresented high-CH4 regions. Yang et al.(2023) developed a multi-output random forest (MORF) model, achieving simultaneous hourly predictions of six pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, CO, SO2) with a high R2 of 0.94, improving efficiency over single-output models and enabling detailed spatial-temporal analyses. 2. Interactions Between Air Pollution and Meteorology Our studies elucidate meteorological influences on air pollution. Zhang et al.(2023a) used quantile regression to model PM2.5 in Indian megacities, predicting increased exceedances in northern cities under SSP585 due to stagnant conditions, with improvements in southern cities due to higher boundary layer heights. Zhang et al.(2022) identified surface winds and humidity as key drivers of PM2.5 extremes, with projections of worsening conditions in China’s key regions under SSP5-8.5. Zhang et al.(2024) linked early South China Sea summer monsoon onset to elevated O3 in southern China. Wang et al.(2024a) attributed declining dust loading in West and South Asia to Arctic amplification, altering atmospheric circulation. Wang et al.(2022) showed aerosol pollution’s varying impact on Beijing’s urban heat island intensity, modulated by wind direction.Gao et al.(2023) clarified the role of sea surface temperature on co-occurrence of heat wave and O3 pollution in China. 3. Impacts on Human Health Our work quantifies air pollution’s health impacts. Xiao et al.(2022) identified a rising frequency of heat and O3 co-extremes in China’s Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei and Yangtze River Delta, with a 7.0% increase in joint exceedances. Wang et al.(2024b) reported spatially heterogeneous wet bulb temperature trends in eastern China. Xiao et al.(2023) and Xiao et al.(2024) using the China Birth Cohort Study, linked maternal exposure to PM2.5, O3, NO2, temperature, and urban heat islands to increased preterm birth risk, with significant additive interactions (e.g., PM2.5–high temperature) and a 27% higher risk per 5°C UHI increment. Overall, we have published 14 papers, which advances air quality management, meteorological understanding, and health risk assessment.

22201820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22201820.value: The research presents significant potential for further development across the three directions. For machine learning applications, expanding the multi-output random forest (MORF) model to include additional pollutants and global datasets could enhance its scalability. In studies of air pollution-meteorology interactions, further exploration of climate change scenarios and extreme weather events will be beneficial for projections of air pollutants. For health impacts, studies on chronic exposure and multi-pollutant interactions could strengthen causal inferences. Expanding cohort studies to other regions would validate findings like preterm birth risks. Cross-disciplinary collaborations, using big data and policy integration, will drive actionable outcomes for air quality management and public health.

22201820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22201820.value: This project focuses on air pollution and its health impacts. We uses machine learning to better track harmful air pollutants like PM2.5 and methane in China and India, finding the best spots to place sensors for accurate monitoring. These tools predict pollution levels across wide areas, helping cities plan cleaner air strategies. The studies also show how weather, like wind or humidity, worsens or improves pollution. For example, climate change could make air quality worse in some Indian cities but better in others, guiding future cleanup efforts. Additionally, the research reveals how polluted air and heat together increase health risks, such as preterm births in China, especially in hot urban areas. This work matters because cleaner air means healthier people, fewer hospital visits, and safer environments. It helps governments make smarter policies to reduce pollution and protect vulnerable groups like pregnant women. By improving how we monitor and predict air quality, this research supports a future with less pollution, better public health, and stronger action against climate change, making our cities safer and more livable for everyone.

22501220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22501220.value: Using proprietary high-frequency credit card data from Singapore, we study the causal effect of a public policy introducing strict credit constraint, on household consumption and debt repayment behavior. The new policy requires the card issuers to completely suspend any credit provided to heavily indebted individuals after two years of the law announcement. While the punishment for heavy indebtedness is very severe, the law is not binding for most of the population, given that it is hard to trigger the law before personal bankruptcy. We investigate the response of household debt, payment, and spending behavior to the law change during the announcement period and implementation period under a difference-in-difference setting. The revolvers, who tend to accumulate credit card debt without paying it off in time, are expected to be more affected by the credit suspension threat policy. The significant response of households even far away from triggering the law could arise from two mechanisms: consumers’ precautionary motive to avoid future troubles, or the spillover effect from those consumers that have been punished. We disentangle the channels from two perspectives: the effective time, and the affected consumer group. Specifically, the spillover effect channel shall only work after the implementation, and driven by peer consumers of heavily indebted individuals; while the precautionary motive channel can take effect immediately after the announcement of law, and does not suggest concentration effect in the peer consumers only. Then we extend to investigate whether the individuals are truly reducing their debt or simply shifting the debt to other accounts. Similar responses in both revolving and non-revolving account of revolvers suggest change in individual’s attitude towards revolving debt accumulation, otherwise it is more likely to be debt shifting. Given the rich demographic characteristics, we are able to further look into the heterogeneity effects. Specifically, we can divide consumers into subsamples by gender, ethnicity, marital status, age, home ownership, income, credit utilization, etc. With the transaction level credit card spending data, we can also look at the heterogeneity in spending types. In the last part, we shall focus on the falsification and robustness checks, such as PS matching, constructing pseudo events, etc. This study bears both academic and practical contributions. Academically, we contribute to literatures on consumer financial regulations, credit constraints, and precautionary motives. Practically, our study estimate the effectiveness of a financial policy targeting reducing household revolving debt, which can serve as good reference for policy makers. 基於來自新加坡的高頻信用卡數據樣本，本文研究引入嚴格的信貸約束的公共政策與家庭消費和債務償還行為的因果關係。該政策要求在頒布該法兩年後，發卡機構需停止向嚴重負債的個人提供任何信貸。該法案雖然對嚴重負債個人的處罰非常嚴厲，但是對大多數人並沒有實質約束力，因為此類嚴重負債者很大概率在達到該法案觸發條件前已經申請破產。本文採用雙重差分模型研究個人在政策公告期和實行期的負債，還款和消費行為。我們預期該信貸約束政策將對那些傾向於累積信用卡債且不按時償還債務的負債者產生顯著更大的影響。這些遠未達到信貸約束政策懲罰標準的個人產生的顯著反應可能來自於兩種機制：消費者為了避免以後可能觸發懲罰的麻煩而採取的預防性措施，或者來自於被懲罰的消費者的溢出效應。本文從兩個角度辨析這兩種機制：政策起效時間和受影響的消費者群體。具體而言，溢出效應應該只在政策施行過後才發揮作用，且作用集中於被懲罰消費者的同儕；而預防性動機可以在政策宣佈過後立即起效，且不一定集中於被懲罰消費者的同儕。而後本文將研究負債者是否真正在減少債務，或者只是把債務轉移到其它賬戶內。如果負債者的負債賬戶和不負債賬戶有同樣趨勢的反應，那麼表示負債者對債務積累的態度產生了變化，反之則更有可能只是債務轉移。基於豐富的樣本信息，本文將進一步研究按照不同消費者特征（例如性別，種族，婚姻狀況，年齡，房屋所有狀態，收入，信貸使用率等）分割的子樣本的異質性反應。藉助信用卡交易數據，本文也可研究消費種類的異質性反應。最後，本文將進行一系列穩健性檢驗，包括傾向評分匹配，構造偽事件等。本研究在學術上和實踐上均有貢獻。在學術上，本研究對消費者金融法規，信貸限制和預防性動機的文獻做出了貢獻。在實踐上，本研究對針對減少家庭負債的公共政策的有效性作出了評估，為政策制定和施行提供了參考。

22501220.label: Major findings and research outcome
22501220.value: Using individual-level credit card data, this study examines the efficacy of a consumer financial regulation designed to curtail the accumulation of unsecured debt among households. The implementation of a non-binding penalty, entailing the suspension of all existing unsecured credit for heavily indebted individuals, leads to a 9.9% greater reduction in monthly credit card debt among credit card revolvers compared to non-revolvers following the policy announcement. We also document significant reductions in other outcome variables, including credit card spending, balance, and delinquency. Significant debt reductions are observed even among revolvers who are distant from the penalty threshold. Consistent with a decision weight mechanism whereby individuals tend to assign heightened importance to extreme negative events, the credit card debt response is more pronounced among revolvers whose existing unsecured credit is more important.

22501220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22501220.value: This paper is under submission to academic journals. In the meanwhile, I am gathering comments and suggestions for the paper by circulating and presenting it at conferences and seminars, and also from the journal referees. The development process encompasses all aspects of the paper, including, but not limited to, the identification of the research question, the methodology employed, the economic mechanisms explored, the robustness of the findings, and the clarity of the writing. By incorporating feedback from diverse perspectives, I aim to enhance the quality and rigor of the study.

22501220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22501220.value: We study the effect of the credit suspension policy introduced by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). This policy aims to reduce household unsecured debt accumulation by prohibiting financial institutions from granting new unsecured credit or allowing existing credit for heavily indebted individuals. We discovered that after the policy announcement, individuals who carried higher level of credit card debt, known as revolvers, reduced their monthly credit card debt by 9.9% more than non-revolvers. We also see significant declines in other credit card metrics, including spending, total balances, and delinquencies. Interestingly, the debt reductions are observed even among revolvers who are far from the penalty threshold. We think this is because people tend to weigh extreme negative events, like losing all their credit, heavily when making financial decisions. Overall, the study suggests this type of policy can be an effective way to curb excessive unsecured borrowing, even for households that aren't right on the edge of the penalty. The results provide valuable insights for policymakers, insititutions, and individuals seeking to manage and reduce unsecured debt such as credit card debt.

22501420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22501420.value: Section 1502 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act imposed an unprecedented disclosure requirement with a non-financial goal of protecting humans rights. Under this rule, US public firms using conflict minerals (including tin, tantalum, tungsten, and gold) in their production must disclose annually whether the minerals are from certain African countries with human right abuses. While the Securities Exchange Commission, public firms, and researchers have attempted to estimate the compliance costs and potential social benefits of this new mandate, no one has investigated its potential unintended impact on firm managers’ internal decisions. I attempt to fill this gap by investigating the effect of the mandatory conflict minerals disclosure on firm investment, one of the most important managerial decisions in daily operations of a business. To comply with the new disclosure requirement, managers have to exert tremendous effort to investigate their multi-level upstream suppliers and, as a result, gain better visibility into their supply chains. I hypothesize that complying firms, with better supply-chain visibility, would make better investment decisions after the implementation of the rule. I will examine supply-chain-specific investment, measured by relationship investment and mergers and acquisitions with firms in upstream supply chain industries, as well as overall investment to reveal the economic significance of the effects. Second, by analyzing the disclosure contents, I will identify the cross-sectional variation in supply-chain visibility achieved by complying firms. If new knowledge does indeed affect investment, I expect this effect to be stronger for firms that gain a higher visibility from their compliance efforts. 陶德-法蘭克華爾街改革與消費者保護法案第1502條出臺了一條前所未有的以保護人權為目的的披露要求。這條規則規定，美國所有在生產中使用沖突礦產（包括錫石、黑鎢、鈳鉭鐵礦和黃金）的上市公司必須每年披露他們使用的沖突礦產是否來源於特定的存在侵犯人權行為的非洲國家。雖然美國證監會，上市公司，和科研工作者都已試圖衡量遵守這項強制性規定為公司帶來的社會成本和收益，但還沒有研究探尋過這項規定對公司內部管理層日常決策的影響。為了填補這一空白，因為投資策略是上市公司管理層日常運營最重要的決定之一，我將研究沖突礦產的強制披露對公司投資行為的影響。公司管理層為了遵守這條新的披露要求，需要深度調查自己多層級的上遊供應商。因此我提出，公司在提供披露後，將提升對自己的供應鏈的了解，做出更好的投資決定。我將研究包括供應鏈關系專用投資和供應鏈並購的供應鏈有關投資，以及公司總投資。另外，我將通過分析公司披露的內容來探索不同公司獲得的不同的供應鏈透明度。如果供應鏈新知會影響投資決策，那麽因披露獲得更大供應鏈透明度的公司的投資決策會受到更大的影響。

22501920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22501920.value: 美國上市公司通常每季度向投資者和分析師提供財務績效（如收益公告）。為了幫助更好地理解所披露的財務信息，公司一般都會（通過電話或網絡直播）舉行財報會議來討論主要財務業績並提供對未來季度的預測。事實上，財報會議已經成為越來越重要的自願披露方式。根據2014國家投資者關系研究調查，97%的投資關系幹事報告說他們的公司會每季度舉辦財報會議，這個比例也在過去的18年中提高了21%。因為財報會議更普遍的成為公司與市場參與者溝通的渠道，現有文獻已經對財報會議做了研究。之前的經驗性證據表明相比收益公告，財報會議會為投資者提供更多的信息（Frankel et al. 1999; Bowen et al., 2002; Bushee et al., 2003; Matsumoto et al., 2011）。此外，公司會戰略性地設計財報會議內容，比如提前準備可能問題的答案文本 (Lee 2016), 和讓更多對公司有利的分析師參與會議 （Mayew 2008）。但是，公司對公司內部人員參與財報會議的戰略性選擇，我們知之甚少。為了拓展對財報會議的了解，我計劃研究公司對職能高管（比如，首席營銷官和首席運營官）參與財報會議的戰略性選擇和此項重要決定是否會影響財報會議的信息性。因為以下三個原因，我特別關註職能高管的參與。第一，首席執行官和首席財務官是財報會議的常規出席人員，公司對他們的參與沒有很大的自由決定權。第二，職能高管已經從商業專家進化成為了戰略顧問。 第三， 投資者對職能高管參與財報會議的需要和現行公司的做法有很明顯的鴻溝。我計劃利用財報會議的會議記錄研究職能高管參與財報會議的決定因素和市場對他們參與的反應。我預期，職能高管參與財報會議和影響公司的戰略性決策的因素有關，例如財報會議觀眾，重大事件，和CEO特征。另外，我將利用路徑分析來探究職能高管參與財報會議和市場反應之間的機制。

22600020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22600020.value: This book-length project aims to delineate the presence of Chinese filmmakers, or auteurs, in participatory cyberspace and analyze their negotiated status in relation to audiences’ motivations and activities. The escalating visibility of Chinese filmmakers in the global arena coincides with the advent of media technology which widens the reach of their fame beyond material constraints, yet redefining their central creative role in film. WWW platforms like IMDb, Douban, Facebook, Weibo, YouTube, and Youku facilitate audiences to rate films, write film reviews, (re)tweet film-related posts, and create parodies of famous titles, challenging the authorial intent and structure. By focusing on Jia Zhangke, Tsai Ming-liang, Wong Kar-wai, and Ang Lee, established Chinese filmmakers who are both celebrated and contentious as appearing on the Web, this study poses several questions. First, how does research on Chinese directors inform us about the changing image of an auteur in the participatory cyber-network? Second, how are Chinese auteurs’ style and vision recoded, reassessed and renegotiated in the fan exchange on the Web? Third, how do the filmmakers struggle to retain their independence and personality over cinephiles’ comments? Fourth, how do the director-viewer dynamics affect Chinese auteurs’ positioning in the global cinematic map? These questions need to be answered with the help of a systematic research of Chinese auteurs in cyberculture. This project entails multiple research tools, which are crucial in digital humanities and film/cultural studies, to examine Chinese filmmakers’ auteurism in the cinematic-cyber nexus. The PI renders an integrated approach of fan and cultural studies, combining inquiry of politics of participation to explore director-audience dynamics. The PI also undertakes a close textual reading of fan-generated materials including ratings of films, threads of discussion, parodies and mashups videos as well as the filmmakers’ feedback and press interviews. By venturing on a mix of methods, the project reveals holistic scenarios of global Chinese cinema, disentangling the complexity of authorial identity, participatory fandom, and media technology. Building on the thriving area of research of Chinese film studies, this project intervenes into the current debate of authorship by locating Chinese auteurs in the digital frontier, which is seriously under-studied. The analysis enriches and complicates our understanding of auteurism that has been dominated by Western theories and studied primarily within conventional director studies. The research outcome will lead to one refereed journal article and one international conference presentation, in addition to a book manuscript in progress.

22600020.label: Realisation of objectives
22600020.value: The three project objectives are realized to a very large extent. Objective 1: -The PI has identified four Chinese filmmakers from mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, Jia Zhange, Ang Lee, Tsai Ming-liang, Wong Kar-wai, who have been transnational and whose presence on online platforms are increasingly prominent. -The PI has surveyed chiefly 5 social media platforms including Weibo, Bilibili, YouTube, Douban, Facebook, on which the users are interested in Chinese directors and their films. -The PI come to grasp an overall picture of how popular the selected auteurs are among online cinephiles. About data sourcing and collection (in the first 6 months of the project): -sourcing data from online interactive behaviors (intra- and interpersonal) of fans, users, and filmmakers whereas document analysis involves sourcing data from finished, released films -Rather than working on an exhaustive sampling of online data, a set of film-based and director-based parameters for the data, presented in the form of indexing, is established and clearly defined in order to strategically limit the crawl discovery. -Working out indexes of key words or phrases, for example, film titles (in Chinese, Chinese pinyin, or English translation) and names of directors Objective 2: -The PI has done a comprehensive research and review of the existing literature of (i) the concept of film authorship and the evolvement of the concept especially in the digital age (ii) the global aspects of Chinese cinema and filmmakers (iii) Chinese film studies from national perspectives. -The PI has explored the identity and power status of the selected Chinese auteurs by looking at the posts and the discussion threads created or contributed by Web users. -The PI has paid special attention to the materials that are pertinent to Chinese auteurs' status and to the audience's cultural and ethnic identities. -The PI has observed how users respond to other posts related to certain Chinese filmmakers and how they interact with each other. Objective 3: -The PI has generated tentative conclusions of the politics of film authorship and the fan motivations in the interactive cyber realm based on the search and analysis results. -The PI has discussed the image of selected filmmakers in a way to compare or parallel with that in the cinematic era in order to foreground the alterations caused by the change of medium. -The PI has tried to advance the hypotheses of the auteur studies by integrating the theorization of the film authorship, cinephilia, and the globalization of Chinese cinema.

22600020.label: Major findings and research outcome
22600020.value: The main findings of this project include: first, the filmmakers of Chinese cinema has a notable presence in participatory Web space, including the China-based and international sites. Second, the users of various cyber platforms show keenness to post and share the texts related to their favorite movie directors. They are also enthusiastic to write about and rate the titles, both famous and lesser-known. Some of the viewers even rework the film clips, presenting them in the forms of mashups, spoil trailers, and memes. Third, most of the viewers who engage in the reinterpretation of the work and reputation of Chinese filmmakers in online space are knowledgeable to Chinese cinema and conscious in nurturing a taste culture. In these manners, I have argued that viewers display their love and intelligibility to Chinese filmmakers and their work on a range of digital platforms. They manage to exhibit greater agency and manipulation over the films and the director's image, consuming the cultural texts in a different fashion from before. The phenomenon, too, renews the persona of the filmmakers which were once established in but no longer stays within the cinematic realm, while potentially challenging the central creative role of filmmakers. The outcome have been realized in three pieces of academic work that I have produced (reference to Part C). In my published journal article, which focuses on internationally renowned Chinese independent filmmaker Jia Zhangke and his presence on Douban, I have contended that Jia's auteurism becomes increasingly contentious as it is open to renegotiation on the China-based cultural website. Another journal submission, which concentrates on Wong Kar-wai evinces Wong's films and his reputation have evoked fan creativity, realized in new hybrids featuring the cutting of Wong's movies to media texts from other cultures / industries such as Hollywood blockbusters and Chinese TV drama series. I have drawn the concluding remark in this project that as the Chinese directors' movies and their names are brought to the digital territory, their image become not limited within regional boundaries but are extended to the global frontier. The new director-audience dynamics illuminate the novel understanding of the Chinese-vs-global dialectics. The result of the research is also helpful for us to critically approach the auteurism of Chinese /Asian filmmakers, reflecting the ever-growing grassroots power in the media-saturated age.

22600020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22600020.value: The research can be further developed in the following aspects: 1. Expand the survey of Chinese filmmakers to East Asian or Asian filmmakers: Theorization of global cinema has been under vigorous expansion and revision. With the rise of Asia in intellectual and popular discourses, the power and identity of East Asian or Asian directors often become the center of critical explorations. While increasing scholarly effort has been evident in the field, the study of its filmmakers in the digital culture is still scarce. 2. Strengthen the research to compare the reception or consumption of Chinese or Asian filmmakers on more than one platform of the similar nature from East and West, for example, Tik Tok and Douyin, YouTube and Bilibili, Twitter and Weibo. In this way, the study can contribute to the comparative and cross-cultural analyses. 3. Increase the research effort to probe the films collaborated by Chinese / Asian filmmakers with popular streaming platforms such as Netflix. Explorations of what films are made and to what extent their directorial trademarks are retained would be useful to the understanding of the wider distribution of media content in the digital era.

22600020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22600020.value: This research project seeks to delineate the presence of Chinese filmmakers, or auteurs, in participatory cyberspace and analyze their evolving status in relation to audiences’ motivations and activities. The escalating visibility of Chinese filmmakers in the global arena coincides with the advent of media technology which widens the reach of their fame, yet redefining their central creative role in film. The analysis focuses on Jia Zhangke, Tsai Ming-liang, Wong Kar-wai, and Ang Lee, established Chinese filmmakers who are both celebrated and contentious as appearing on WWW platforms like Douban, Bilibili, Facebook, and YouTube on which audiences can rate films, write film reviews, (re)tweet film-related posts, and create parodies of famous titles. The overall significance of the project lies in its attempt to capture the emergent phenomenon in cyberculture, calling for a theoretical rethinking of film authorship. This project disrupts the theoretical inclination to the Anglo-European auteur politics, which has long been institutionalized within English-language scholarship. It also critically engages with auteurism in Chinese cinemas, a thriving yet under-explored area. Lastly, this project impinges on a constellation of principles and methods in understanding auteurism in global Chinese cinema, framing the relationship between filmmaking persona and audience engagement in multiple ways.

22601120.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22601120.value: 檢視大陸來港白領工作者與香港人的日常互動和群體界線

22601120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22601120.value: An issue of increasing concern for scholars and the Hong Kong government is the social, economic, and cultural integration of new mainland Chinese immigrants (NMCIs) into local society and their interaction with Hong Kongers. Research on integration difficulties has focused on one-way permit holder migrants from China, who are less skilled, face discrimination and problems with integration based on differences in language and human capital. These studies mostly discuss the impact one-way permit holders have on social welfare resources, while overlooking internal variation within NMCIs, who are not a homogeneous group—skilled professionals may have different integration experiences and receive different treatment from locals than one-way permit holders. Using Wimmer’s concept of boundary making and unmaking, this study takes a qualitative approach to the narratives, mutual perceptions, stereotyping, and everyday interaction experiences between mainland skilled professionals (MSPs) and Hong Kongers. Boundary making and unmaking affects how migrants and locals understand each other. Building upon the literature on the barriers and discrimination NMCIs face, this research seeks to investigate three sets of questions: (1) what do boundary making/unmaking processes between MSPs and locals look like in the workplace and other social settings; (2) how are specific stereotypes of the other group created, changed, or reproduced through boundary making/unmaking processes; and (3) which kinds of social integration are MSPs pursuing, do they face barriers during their integration process similar to those one-way permit holders face, and how do they react to the barriers? This study tests the concept of boundary making and unmaking in Hong Kong, where mainland Chinese immigrants migrate from a sovereign to host society but have problems of integration there. It asks whether MSPs experience boundary making and unmaking in different ways (than other NMCIs). It also helps better highlight the theoretical implications of different ideas of prejudice and integration, comparing MSP experiences of integration with those of one-way permit holders, students, tourists, etc. At a policy level, the findings can improve understanding between MSPs and Hong Kongers by highlighting internal variation within NMCIs and addressing the needs of different NMCI groups. 對於學者和香港政府來說，一個日趨重要的議題是大陸新移民在香港的社會、經濟和文化融入，及其和本地香港人的日常互動。既有研究大多集中在持單程證來港的大陸新移民，他們之中不少為低技術者，且由於語言和人力資本的關係經常面臨到各種歧視。然而這些研究忽略了大陸新移民的多樣性；舉例來說，白領工作者可能和持單程證來港者有相當不一樣的融入經驗。 本研究從Wimmer的族群界線劃分出發，採取質性研究的方式探索大陸來港白領工作者和本地香港人的日常互動經驗以及相互觀感。奠基在過往大陸新移民受到歧視和阻礙其融入因素的研究之上，本研究指在探索三個問題：(1)大陸來港白領工作者和香港人在工作現場的互動經驗為何？(2)對於其他群體的刻板印象是如何被建立起來、在什麼情況下可能改變或再製？以及(3)大陸來港白領工作者所追求的是什麼樣的社會融入經驗？他們在融入的過程中是否面臨和其他持單程證來港者類似的挑戰和困難？他們又是如何回應這些挑戰？ 本研究結果將能幫助我們更進一步了解不同群體的偏見，也能夠對比大陸來港白領工作者和其他大陸新移民（例如持單程證來港者、學生、遊客等等）的融入經驗。在政策層次上，本研究能夠幫助我們更加了解大陸新移民的內部多樣性，進而更有效回應各個群體在融入香港過程中的困難和需求。

22607320.value: 寂靜的色彩：揭開近代歐洲聾啞畫家鮮為人知的過去

22607320.label: Project Objectives
22607320.value: Investigate the interconnections between art and disability in the early modern period. Examine the socio-economic circumstances that led deaf and mute children to train in the visual arts and survey the training methods adopted. Analyse the careers of deaf and mute artists against the backdrop of the medical and philosophical literature that, starting from the second half of the sixteenth century, paved the way for our modern conceptualisation of disability. Conceptualise disability through visual culture and examine the role of visual culture in the history and process of marginalisation. Share the results with the academic community through (i) the creation of a database of the biographies and works of deaf and mute artists active in Europe in the period 1400–1700; (ii) participation in international conferences; (iii) two publications in major inter-national journals; and (iv) the organisation of an international seminar. Advance scholarly and public awareness of art and disability and encourage further analysis and contextualisation, especially at a global level. Deduce conclusions from past developments, events and decisions for contemporary discussion of education practices for deaf and mute students in the visual arts.

22607320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607320.value: 摘要： 本研究將透過聾啞畫家的仕途探討藝術與殘疾在近代歐洲（1400-1700）的相互關係。不少紀錄均顯示患有聽力及言語障礙的藝術家於中世紀後期開始活躍於歐洲，其中部份成就傑出，例如意大利畫家平圖里基奧（Pinturicchio）曾受教宗所託裝飾西斯汀教堂。事實上，大部份殘疾畫家即使表現卓越，他們的事跡包括如何跨過難關成為畫家也鮮為人知。本研究透過意大利、荷蘭及西班牙各地的個案，探究聾啞畫家如何透過藝術表達自我及解決自身殘疾帶來的困難，了解他們被世人所遺忘的成長遭遇，以及他們的教育與才能發展。本研究亦會提出研究框架闡釋社會經濟背景及分析十六世紀醫學文獻，探討其對聾啞畫家藝術生涯的影響。另外，透過研究視覺文化如何影響邊緣化的歷史和過程，從而理解「中心」的構成及其對「異常」的一群存在的排斥。本研究將為視覺藝術與殘疾的議題作出重大貢獻，並回應最近對藝術史、社會史及文學研究的相關議題。本研究以跨領域研究方式取代傳統的藝術史分析，從視覺文化、社會學、物質文化、文學及檔案研究、社會及經濟理論多方面進行研究。研究旨在加深大眾對早期現代藝術創作的認識，以及推動其他學者對東亞藝術進行類似研究。 本研究的預期研究成果如下： 一. 研討會發表 二. 於國際期刊發表兩篇經同行評審之文章 三. 建立數據庫，提供活躍於歐洲1400-1700年間聾啞畫家的事跡與作品 四. 於香港浸會大學視覺藝術院舉辦國際研討會 五. 與本地及國際的學術與非學術界進行交流 六. 於本地學府舉行公開演講

22607320.label: Realisation of objectives
22607320.value: (i) The project investigated interconnections between art history and disability in the early modern period by retracing the professional careers of twelve prelingually deaf painters. The study challenged the long-lasting assumption that people with disabilities were relegated to the margins of society from classical antiquity to the seventeenth century, demonstrating that the way in which modern societies understand disability did not fully exist in the past and that the consideration of intersectional factors such as age, gender and social status was essential to how people responded to impairment. The extent to which the project objectives were achieved is encapsulated in the motivation provided by the international committee responsible for awarding the Renaissance Studies Article Prize 2023 to the principal outcome of this project: the research essay “A visual testament by Luca Riva a deaf and mute pupil of the Procaccini’. The motivation states the following: "This article takes an impressively interdisciplinary approach to a remarkable source that provides a uniquely intimate encounter with the life, experiences and communicative strategies of a deaf and mute artist, Luca Riva. It is a study that sparks the imagination, skilfully blending art historical techniques with scholarly approaches to legal history in order to approach the source material from multiple angles. In doing so, it deftly reconstructs Luca Riva’s world in order to offer a fresh perspective on the Italian renaissance and on how our understanding of it can be transformed through the lens of disability studies." (ii) The project highlighted that in early modern societies deaf people were not ostracised or institutionalised but considered to be a part of society. The way in which they were treated depended on their personal circumstances. Those who lived in highly populated areas had more chances to develop sophisticated communication skills. Those born into wealthy families enjoyed an easier path to social integration and received a specialised education that favoured the start of their professional careers. In addition to family support, friendships and social connections played an essential role. These developed within the context of the early modern systems of care such as hospitals and charitable institutions. The findings of the project highlight that deaf people found employment in manual trades where copying tasks would be achieved through the practice of watching. Those who revealed a vocation for drawing found a career option in the visual arts, where the practice of copying was considered an essential step in the training of young artists. Several training approaches were surveyed, all of them included gestures. (iii) The project retracted the careers of twelve deaf painters active in early modern Europe: Luca Riva, Giuseppe Badaracco, Ercole Sarti, Filippo Ceppaluni, Aurelio Martelli, Giovanni Lo Coco, Wolfgang Heimbach, Juan Fernandez Navarrete, Alonso del Arco, Hendrick Avercamp, Jan Jansz and Marten Boulema. Their lives and professional careers were not only analysed from an art historical perspective but also interpreted within the historical, social, medical and philosophical context that, starting from the second half of the sixteenth century, informed the development of a new sensibility towards deaf education. The project recognised how the biographical accounts of European early modern deaf painters highlight a transition towards the development of a cultural model of deafness that prioritised deaf people’s ability to make sense of the world through their own visual skills and communicate both with each other and with members of the hearing community. In this connection, the successful stories of the painters rediscovered by this research project can be considered among the first indications of the empowerment of deaf people through education. (iv) Building upon the observations made in response to the previous point, the project demonstrated that the successful stories of prelingually deaf painters in early modern Europe might indicate how through visual arts deaf people found a way to communicate their understanding of the world in an era characterised by high level of illiteracy. While on the one hand the essential role played by visual culture helped deaf people to demonstrate their understanding of the world through the practice of art, on the other hand the growing presence of deaf painters in early modern workshops favoured the creation of discourses aimed at affirming the intelligence of deaf people. It is particularly relevant that this happened in the context of the visual arts which, from the mid-fourteenth century, aimed at elevating painting from the mechanical to the liberal arts. The project highlighted how through their professional careers, prelingually deaf painters used the prestige associated to high art to resist being categorised as primitives and demonstrate their intellectual capacities. This opened the field for a more nuanced understanding of deafness. (v) The project resulted in two peer-reviewed research articles published in major international journals. One of them was awarded the prestigious Renaissance Studies Article Prize 2023. In 2022, the research project was also awarded the RSA-Samuel H. Kress Fellowship in Renaissance Art History. Further scholarly outcomes are the presentation of three research papers in refereed international conferences; the organisation of a panel session titled “Disability and Bodily difference in Early Modern Europe” held at the 68th Annual Meeting of the Renaissance Society of America; and the organisation of an international symposium held at the Ateneo Veneto in Venice on 7 July 2022. Titled “Deaf History Symposium”, the conference featured the participation of twelve international scholars and interrogated deaf culture from historical visual, artistic, legal, social and cultural perspectives. (vi) By virtue of its pioneering nature and interdisciplinary approach, the project produced a wide-ranging impact demonstrated not only by publications and international accolades but also by the development of an extended transdisciplinary international network of collaborations involving colleagues researching in the fields of art history, social history, and disability studies. Aside from impacting the scholarly community, the project produced resources tailored for students and the general public. A database (www.speakingbrushes.com) exploring the lives and careers of deaf painters working in early modern Europe was created. With regard to knowledge transfer and community outreach, the PI participated in an episode of a podcast series dedicated to art and disability. Published by the Historians of the Netherlandish Art Association the podcast is open access and downloadable from Spotify, Google and Apple. A further outcome is a public lecture delivered at the Hong Kong Museum of Art in which the case study of Filippo Ceppaluni, a Neapolitan deaf painter was presented. (vii) The impact of the project on contemporary discussions on art practice and disability is highlighted by the invitation to participate as guest speaker to the international workshop “New Approaches on Disability and Art History” organised by the Institute of Art History at the University of Zurich. The project was also featured in the article ‘The silent study of art: the deaf artists of the Renaissance’, written by Dr Rosamund Oates for History Extra, the History Magazine of the BBC. The impact of the research transcended the field of art history, as it not only has allowed the wider population to learn about art and deafness, but it also increased the awareness of the benefits of including art practice in the education of students with deafness today. From the educational standpoint, the study contributed to the development of four modules currently offered in the History of Art programme at the Academy of Visual Arts.

22607320.label: Major findings and research outcome
22607320.value: The project is the first study ever dedicated to the study of interconnections between art practice and prelingual deafness in Europe in the early modern period (1400-1700). It has retraced the life stories and artistic careers of twelve previously unknown deaf painters, challenged the assumption that people with disabilities were relegated to the margins of society from classical antiquity to the seventeenth century, and emphasised the relevant and often neglected role played by visual culture in the history of deaf education. The project resulted in two peer-reviewed research articles published in major international journals: Renaissance Studies and Source: Notes in the History of Art. The essay titled "A visual testament by Luca Riva, a deaf and mute pupil of the Procaccini", was awarded the prestigious Renaissance Studies Article Prize 2023, presented annually by the Society for Renaissance Studies (the main academic organisation in Britain and Ireland for studies in the Renaissance) to the best article published in the field. Further scholarly outcomes are the presentation of three research papers in refereed international conferences, the organisation of a panel session titled “Disability and Bodily difference in Early Modern Europe” held at the 68th Annual Meeting of the Renaissance Society of America, and the organisation of an international conference held at the Ateneo Veneto in Venice on 7 July 2022. Titled “Deaf History Symposium”, the event featured the participation of twelve international scholars and interrogated deaf culture from historical visual, artistic and social perspectives. Research from the project was also presented at the international workshop “New Approaches on Disability and Art History” organised by the Institute of Art History at the University of Zurich. On this occasion, the PI was invited as a guest speaker. The outcomes related to the project also include www.speakingbrushes.com, an open access, educational database retracing the biographies and of twelve deaf painters active in early modern Europe. While the database features academic research, the information is presented to inform students and audiences outside academia. With regard to knowledge transfer and community outreach, the PI was invited to participate to a podcast dedicated to art and disability. Published by the “Historians of the Netherlandish Art Association” the podcast is available for download on Apple, Google and Spotify. A further outcome is a public lecture held at the Hong Kong Museum of Art in which the case study of Filippo Ceppaluni, a seventeenth century Neapolitan deaf painter was presented.

22607320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22607320.value: As a pioneering study situated at the crossroads between art history and disability studies, the project highlights an exceptional potential for further development. A transdisciplinary, international network of collaborations has been established with colleagues researching in the fields of art history, social history and disability studies in institutions such as the Centre for Cultures of Disability at Manchester Metropolitan University, the Institute for Medical Humanities at Durham University, the Institute of Art History at the University of Zurich and the Centre of Excellence in the History of Experience in Tampere. It is envisioned that this ever-expanding network will lead to further collaborations, including the organisation of workshops, the development of collaborative research projects as well as the creation of collaborative efforts in applying for major research grants both in Europe and Hong Kong, furthering historical research on art and disability. In addition to this, further and concrete developments of the project are incapsulated in my current research project which has been funded by the Research Grants Council of Hong Kong through the General Research Fund (12624122). Titled “Seeing the invisible: visual representations of disability in early modern Europe”, the project investigates further historical intersections between art and disability.

22607320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22607320.value: The research project is the first study ever dedicated to the analysis of interconnections between art practice and prelingual deafness in Europe in the early modern period (1400-1700). Situated at the crossroads between art history, social history and disability studies, the study interrogated historical understandings of disability through the rediscovery of the life experiences and professional careers of twelve prelingually deaf painters. By looking at a variety of sources including works of art, archival records, biographical accounts and poetry, the project retraced their pictorial education, career choices, and approach towards the painting profession. The research challenged the assumption that people with disabilities were relegated to the margins of society from classical antiquity to the seventeenth century, demonstrating that the way in which modern societies understand disability did not fully exist in the past and that the consideration of intersectional factors such as age, gender and social status were essential to how people responded to impairment. The project highlighted the ways in which art practice provided a viable career option for prelingually deaf people and emphasised the relevant and often neglected role played by visual culture in the history of deaf education.

23100020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23100020.value: 利用長期種群監測以規劃淡水龜的保育工作

23100020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23100020.value: 龜在地球上已經存活了超過兩億年，曾經與恐龍共存，可是在各種人為活動影響下，現在超過百分之六十的品種活在瀕臨絕種的邊緣。在亞洲情況更甚，我們對很多品種的生態了解很少，導致保育工作成效一直有限。鷹嘴龜跟很多淡水龜有相同的命運，因過度採集以致數量稀少﹐被列為極度瀕危物種。在香港，五個殘存的鷹嘴龜種群提供難得的研究機會，以增加我們對淡水龜種群生態的認識。我由2010年開始監測這五個種群，是次研究會延續監測工作到2024年，成為亞洲其中一個最全面的淡水龜監測項目。從這個項目得到的數據，我會估算出不同的種群參數，如存活率和繁殖成功率，再利用這些參數於種群模型以評估不同保育工作 (包括反偷獵巡查及種群引進等) 的成效，有助於計劃最有成本效益的保育策略。總括而言，是次研究會增加我們對淡水龜生態的認識，評估不同保育工作的成效和鼓勵更多類似的研究在亞洲開展。

23501720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23501720.value: 企业家的危机经历，创新和不道德的亲组织行为：自我认同的调节作用

23501720.label: Project Objectives
23501720.value: In the current high-velocity economy, the crisis events faced by venture firms have tended to intensify in both frequency and seriousness. During difficult times (e.g., technological obstacle), some venture entrepreneurs dedicated to creativity have been lured into engaging in unethical actions to further their own interests. For example, in 2003, Elisabeth Holmes launched Theranos, a blood-testing product that could have revolutionized healthcare services. After Theranos went public in 2013, she came into the spotlight for her creative idea. However, the product had a number of technical defects and Theranos was not able to remedy. Holmes and top management concealed the details and exaggerated its performance rather than make efforts to improve matters. Consequently, in 2016, the FDA inspected Theranos’s labs, finding critical problems with the equipment and quality control. In the following year, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Holmes of fraud for exaggerating the performance of the lab’s technology. Previous literature has focused on positive coping strategies when managers face a crisis. Events that challenge the structure of an organization can provide meaningful opportunities to innovate. However, little theoretical or empirical work has been done on the potential use of negative coping strategies to manage such events. Crisis, as an aberrant event for venture firms, can result in both positive and negative deviance from norms, routines, or traditional ways of working. Echoing the Theranos case, managers can cope with crisis situations by engaging in either problem-solving or unethical actions to further their organizations’ interests. I will present a typology of the different (i.e., transformative and sustaining) coping strategies that can boost resilience in times of crisis. The coping strategies are related to the way they focus on tackling a problem. However, they differ in the way they perceive and deal with crises. A transformative coping strategy approaches crisis events with a curiosity about their root causes, and an effort is made to unravel them by departing from the status quo. A sustaining strategy approaches crisis situations without addressing the root cause, but it attempts to endure them by relying on socially unacceptable solutions that benefit the organization. Second, I will advance the typology by identifying the psychological boundary condition of people engaging in either transformative or sustaining strategies in times of crisis. I will use identity theory as a psychological basis for organizing crisis coping strategies. Identity serves as a framework for interpreting experience. It is a cognitive basis for identifying situations, and it increases sensitivity and receptivity to certain behavioral information. Identity has been studied as a self-regulatory mechanism that motivates certain actions. People are motivated to engage in specific actions to verify, bolster, and authenticate their identity. Specifically, I will propose creative identity and moral identity as psychological conditions for coping strategies. In the face of crises, individuals regulate their behavior to be consistent with their identity and care about the things that are the most important to them. Entrepreneurs with a strong creative identity accept potentially creative activities as a function of their identity-coherent responses to crises. Accordingly, they will follow the transformative coping approach. In contrast, entrepreneurs with low levels of moral identity endorse unethical pro-organizational behavior as a solution to crises because it is not against their self-view. They are likely to implement the sustaining coping strategy. Drawing upon identity theory, I will test whether entrepreneurs’ experiences with crises stimulate bricolage at high levels of creative identity, in the case of transformative coping, or prompt unethical pro-organizational behaviors at low levels of moral identity, as a sustainining strategy. Last but not least, to test the hypotheses, I will focus on venture entrepreneurs as a unit of analysis. With the agreement of the chairman, I will survey and collect data from a Korean venture cluster to which about 200 venture firms belong. Most of the ventures are based on high technology and innovative business models (e.g., medical engineering, solar energy systems, high-tech fabrics). The context is suitable for study because such venture entrepreneurs inevitably face crisis while running their business. In addition, I will analyze how their coping strategies may directly impact firm performance (innovation and reputation). In the literature, little scholarly effort has been made to determine how unethical pro-organization behavior affects firm performance. Entrepreneurs’ crisis coping strategies can play a vital role in venture firm performance. By exploring the venture entrepreneurial context, I will develop a typology of coping strategies that can boost resilience in times of crisis, identify their potential effects on firm performance and uncover the boundary conditions for their effects.
rows: In the current high-velocity economy, the crisis events faced by venture firms have tended to intensify in both frequency and seriousness. During difficult times (e.g., technological obstacle), some venture entrepreneurs dedicated to creativity have been lured into engaging in unethical actions to further their own interests. For example, in 2003, Elisabeth Holmes launched Theranos, a blood-testing product that could have revolutionized healthcare services. After Theranos went public in 2013, she came into the spotlight for her creative idea. However, the product had a number of technical defects and Theranos was not able to remedy. Holmes and top management concealed the details and exaggerated its performance rather than make efforts to improve matters. Consequently, in 2016, the FDA inspected Theranos’s labs, finding critical problems with the equipment and quality control. In the following year, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Holmes of fraud for exaggerating the performance of the lab’s technology.

Previous literature has focused on positive coping strategies when managers face a crisis. Events that challenge the structure of an organization can provide meaningful opportunities to innovate. However, little theoretical or empirical work has been done on the potential use of negative coping strategies to manage such events. Crisis, as an aberrant event for venture firms, can result in both positive and negative deviance from norms, routines, or traditional ways of working. Echoing the Theranos case, managers can cope with crisis situations by engaging in either problem-solving or unethical actions to further their organizations’ interests. I will present a typology of the different (i.e., transformative and sustaining) coping strategies that can boost resilience in times of crisis. The coping strategies are related to the way they focus on tackling a problem. However, they differ in the way they perceive and deal with crises. A transformative coping strategy approaches crisis events with a curiosity about their root causes, and an effort is made to unravel them by departing from the status quo. A sustaining strategy approaches crisis situations without addressing the root cause, but it attempts to endure them by relying on socially unacceptable solutions that benefit the organization.

Second, I will advance the typology by identifying the psychological boundary condition of people engaging in either transformative or sustaining strategies in times of crisis. I will use identity theory as a psychological basis for organizing crisis coping strategies. Identity serves as a framework for interpreting experience. It is a cognitive basis for identifying situations, and it increases sensitivity and receptivity to certain behavioral information. Identity has been studied as a self-regulatory mechanism that motivates certain actions. People are motivated to engage in specific actions to verify, bolster, and authenticate their identity. Specifically, I will propose creative identity and moral identity as psychological conditions for coping strategies. In the face of crises, individuals regulate their behavior to be consistent with their identity and care about the things that are the most important to them. Entrepreneurs with a strong creative identity accept potentially creative activities as a function of their identity-coherent responses to crises. Accordingly, they will follow the transformative coping approach. In contrast, entrepreneurs with low levels of moral identity endorse unethical pro-organizational behavior as a solution to crises because it is not against their self-view. They are likely to implement the sustaining coping strategy. Drawing upon identity theory, I will test whether entrepreneurs’ experiences with crises stimulate bricolage at high levels of creative identity, in the case of transformative coping, or prompt unethical pro-organizational behaviors at low levels of moral identity, as a sustainining strategy.

Last but not least, to test the hypotheses, I will focus on venture entrepreneurs as a unit of analysis. With the agreement of the chairman, I will survey and collect data from a Korean venture cluster to which about 200 venture firms belong. Most of the ventures are based on high technology and innovative business models (e.g., medical engineering, solar energy systems, high-tech fabrics). The context is suitable for study because such venture entrepreneurs inevitably face crisis while running their business. In addition, I will analyze how their coping strategies may directly impact firm performance (innovation and reputation). In the literature, little scholarly effort has been made to determine how unethical pro-organization behavior affects firm performance. Entrepreneurs’ crisis coping strategies can play a vital role in venture firm performance. By exploring the venture entrepreneurial context, I will develop a typology of coping strategies that can boost resilience in times of crisis, identify their potential effects on firm performance and uncover the boundary conditions for their effects.

23501720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23501720.value: Creative entrepreneurs show remarkable resilience to today’s competitive and hostile economy. For example, the market capitalization of the five creative enterprises, Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and Google, accounted for 38% of the gains in the S&P 500 index in August 2018, up from lows in February. Organizational scientists have found that creative entrepreneurs become even more creative in the use of resources (i.e. bricolage) during a crisis. Recently, however, scientists begin to be concerned that creative entrepreneurs may engage in unethical behaviors while coping with crisis situations. Indeed, Theranos, a creative healthcare venture valued at $9 billion, ceased operations due to false claims about its medical products. Investors lost more than $600 million. Despite this, there has been a lack of understanding of whether and when an entrepreneur engages in creative actions or make unethical decisions to cope with troubles in times of disruption. In this proposed study, I will approach the issue from the perspective of crisis coping strategies. First, I will review and develop a typology of potential crisis coping strategies to extend the understanding of creative or unethical strategies that entrepreneurs may implement. I will provide an integrative synthesis of those strategies to explain how entrepreneurs’ experience of crises can lead not only to bricolage but also to unethical pro-organization behaviors. Second, I will explore the entrepreneur's psychological ground from which the decision to engage in creative or unethical actions emerges in the face of disrupting events. I will use self-identity theory (creative and moral identity) to examine when entrepreneurs become involved in creative bricolage or unethical pro-organizational behaviors in crisis situations. Third, I will test whether their coping strategies affect venture performance positively (bricolage enhances innovation) or negatively (unethical pro-organization behavior affects reputation). The proposed study is expected to make three contributions. First, it will show venture entrepreneurs may engage in either creative or unethical actions in the faces of disrupting events. Scholarly efforts to understand this issue have been lacking. I will propose a typology of potential coping strategies by assuming that an entrepreneur can submit to either creative use of resources (i.e. bricolage) or unethical deeds to manage crisis sitautions. Second, I will advance the typology by identifying the psychological foundation upon which super-organizers determine their choice of coping strategies based on identity theory. Finally, I will extend understanding of whether bricolage and unethical actions affect venture performance (i.e., innovation and reputation). 富有创造力的企业家在面对当今富有竞争和敌意的经济环境下，表现出了非凡的韧性。 数据上看，自标普500指数在2018年8月从2月份的低点上升后，Facebook，Apple，Amazon，Netflix和 Google五家企业的市值贡献了其38%的增长。 学者发现在危机期间，有创造力的企业家在利用资源方面变得更有创造力。 但是，最近，科学家开始担心 有创造力的企业家在应对危机的同时可能会做出不道德的行为。 比如，价值90亿美元的创意医疗保健企业Theranos因对其医疗产品的虚假声明而终止运营。 投资者因此损失超过600百万美元。 尽管如此，我们仍然不清楚参企业家何时会有创新行为、或做出不道德的决定，以应对危机。 在这项拟议的研究中，我将从危机应对策略的视角理解这一项。 首先，我将回顾并发展一种潜在的危机应对策略，以理解企业家可以实施的创新或不道德的策略。 我将整合这些策略，并运用其来解释企业家为何的危机经历不仅会导致贿赂，但也有不道德的亲组织行为。 其次，我将探讨企业家作出这些决策的心理机制。 我将使用自我认同理论（创意和道德认同），检验企业家在危机情况下，何时参与创意活动以及不道德的亲组织行为。 最后，我会进一步违反企业家这些的应对危机的策略是否对企业绩效产生积极影响（促进创新）或负面影响（不道德的亲组织行为降低企业声誉）。 拟议的项研究有望做出三项贡献。 首先，它将显示风险企业家应对危机时可能会参与创造性的或不道德的行为。 这项工作有利于弥补目前学术上对这一问题的忽略。 我提出企业家潜在应对策略既包括创造性地使用资源，也包括采取一些不道德的行为来管理危机。 其次，我将基于身份理论，梳理超级组织者选择不同处理策略的心理机制。 最后，我将进一步探索创新决策和不道德的行为对企业的绩效（即创新和声誉）的影响。

23501920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23501920.value: The explosion of the Internet has contributed to an emerging global network for businesses. It is reported that over 2.3 billion people have access to the Internet and this is expected to grow to five billion by 2020. Unfortunately, researchers have not reached an agreement about the influences of the Internet in employees' daily work. Some researchers have reported that employees use the Internet for personal purposes and related it to lower job performance (Kühnel et al., 2017). Others have found that when employees watch positive videos, they could have higher productivity (Coker, 2011). One of the main reasons for these contradictory views is that different studies focus on different Internet activities. To solve this contradiction, we need first to understand what employees do on the Internet during work hours. The author follows the work-home-leisure trichotomy of the allocation of time theory proposed by Gronau (1977) and starts with understanding Internet activities as work, home, and leisure-related. Work-related Internet usage refers to employees’ Internet activities that are of or related to their current work tasks. Home-related Internet usage refers to employees’ Internet activities that are of or related to dealing with the problems of their family and/or friends. Leisure-related Internet usage denotes employees’ activities that are of or related to their experiences of entertainment and/or recreation. The author then uses two studies to test this typology and investigate the impacts of different types of Internet usage on employee outcomes. In Study 1, the author uses supervised machine learning techniques to classify employees’ Internet usage. Supervised machine learning has been used in other areas (Anandarajan, 2002) and suggested as powerful in classifying such activity into different types (Kim, 2014). The author will first review the literature and list all the detailed descriptions and items of Internet usage. Supervised machine learning will be used to create and learn the features of work, home, or leisure-related Internet usage. After that, 1000 full-time employees will be invited to report their Internet usage on company time. The supervised algorithms will be used here to classify the various activities into work, home, or leisure clusters. In Study 2, based on the above classifications, the author will further refer to the interference and recovery perspectives to investigate the impacts of employees’ different Internet activities. Employees’ needs for work, home, and leisure are considered as important contingency factors that could alter these relationships.

23501920.label: Realisation of objectives
23501920.value: As the Principal Investigator (PI) of this project, I collaborated with my coauthors to achieve our two primary objectives: Classification of Personal Internet Usage (PIU) During Work Hours: We utilized various machine learning methods to classify employees' Internet activities. Impacts of PIU on Employees: We examined how PIU affects employees' well-being, work engagement, task performance, and creative performance. This project has led to three publications: one journal paper and two conference papers. I detail each point below. *Completing Objective 1: Classification of Internet Activities The first objective of this project is to utilize supervised machine learning techniques to classify Internet usage activities into three categories: work-related, home-related, and leisure-related, based on comprehensive datasets derived from literature and survey responses. *Literature Review (Data One) I worked with a recruited research assistant to conduct an extensive literature review on Internet usage activities. We searched the Web of Science and Google Scholar for related publications ranging from 1980 to 2022, using keywords like "Internet use at work" along with 29 other terms. As a supplement, we further used the same keywords to search key management and information management journals, including Academy of Management Journal, MIS Quarterly, and 15 other journals with the highest impact factors. Finally, to ensure a complete list of employees’ Internet usage behaviors, we backward and forward searched the reference lists of the papers. By doing so, we obtained 113 additional possible articles. In total, we initially found 8,813 articles. After screening and cleansing the data, we focused on 618 relevant activities from 102 papers for the following textual classification exercise. It should be noted that this sample is a holistic summary of previous PIU literature. The classification results by completing this objective are thus of substantial implication. *Survey Data (Data Two) To complement the literature data, we recruited 2,000 full-time employees via Prolific, yielding 10,927 valid Internet usage behaviors during work hours. Though this data was not included in the final journal paper due to complexity, it inspired another related project. *Classification using Machine Learning Technique We applied supervised machine learning techniques to classify Internet usage into work-related, home-related (HPIU), and leisure-related (UPIU) categories. Using a dataset of 618 activities, we split it into training (85%) and testing (15%) datasets. Two research assistants independently coded the training dataset, resolving disagreements through discussion. We trained classification models using multiple algorithms, achieving accuracy rates consistently over 90%. Our Python code is available online at OSF https://osf.io/gnyqb/?view_only=fb435b78456f49b3a8ce6a5f032b3fc5. *Completing Objective 2: Analysis of Internet Usage Consequences With the classification results of various personal Internet usage behaviors—work-related, HPIU, and UPIU—we further focused on completing our second project objective by exploring the impacts of categorized Internet activities on employees' psychological states, work engagement, and well-being, integrating recovery and interference perspectives with empirical data. *Development of Measurement Scales (Data Three) The first set of studies was to develop the measurement scales for HPIU and UPIU using four samples, with a total of 437 full-time employees from various industries. Following rigorous scale development processes, we first referred to the literature and conducted pilot interviews with prospective employees to initiate items for HPIU and UPIU. We then tested the factor structure of these generated items and examined their scale reliability and validity. Finally, we tested the discriminant validity of the newly developed scale. This newly developed scale is also an important instrument to inspire more research into understanding PIU. *Model Testing (Data Four) The second set of studies provided a direct test of the hypothesized model with 1,063 multi-wave daily inputs from 125 full-time employees. The findings generally supported our theorization. On a daily basis, HPIU was associated with improved recovery and well-being, whereas UPIU correlated with higher levels of depletion, which further reduced well-being and hampered work engagement. Moreover, we found that supervisor support for PIU activities plays a moderating role, strengthening the beneficial effect of HPIU. *Key Challenges and Solutions Despite the above achievements and research outputs, I have encountered quite a few challenges that are difficult to tackle during the process. I summarize the key challenges and our attempts to overcome the problems below. *Incomplete Profile of PIU. One of the key challenges for this project during the revision and publication process was that the editorial team expected us to explore all the PIU activities that employees may perform during their daily work hours. Although this goes beyond the project objectives and seems more appealing, the current theory and the available data limit this possibility. Although we have attempted to overcome these obstacles by gathering data from various sources, we are still limited in accessing larger and real-time data about employees’ PIU during work hours. We tried to contact several firms with good connections to us but failed to obtain the real-time large data due to privacy concerns. Therefore, we had to compromise by using self-reported data and summarized data from existing literature. Although the findings from these various data sources convey important information to us, they do limit us from providing a holistic classification of all the PIU activities. This is possibly a key reason for our paper rejection experiences below. *Publication Rejections. Another key obstacle was rejection. Although we devoted substantial effort to the project and writing up the paper, we encountered rejections from several journals. We initially submitted the paper to the Journal of Applied Psychology but got rejected. This was a significant setback given the journal's relevance and impact in the field. To achieve a decent publication from this funded project, we carefully reviewed the feedback from the journal reviewers and used it to significantly improve the quality and clarity of our manuscript. We then made some refinements and sent it to Personnel Psychology. Unfortunately, we got rejected again. The main reason for rejection was that the review team thought limited theoretical contribution was offered by the research, which was actually contradictory to the comments we received from the conference reviewers. Nevertheless, we tried to incorporate other comments into revising our paper and made further refinements, then submitted the paper to the Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology (a 4-star journal in the ABS list), hoping to secure a reputational output from this project given the limited time for completing this project. This time, we were lucky. Although the editor and the three reviewers were critical of our research, they offered us opportunities to revise our paper. After a one-and-a-half-year revision process, we got the paper accepted for publication in the journal. *Brief Conclusion All in all, we are very grateful for the support provided by the Research Grant Council to initiate our research in this vital area. Despite the challenges and obstacles in the process, our project has successfully met its objectives by producing three direct publications from this project, providing significant insights into the classification and impact of Internet usage in the workplace. Future research will focus on expanding our study to provide a deeper understanding of these behaviors.
