23501920.label: Major findings and research outcome
23501920.value: Across the three publications with four different sets of data involving around 2,562 full-time employees and over 3,000 data points related to employees’ personal Internet usage (PIU) at work, we have provided a systematic and robust explanation for the inconsistent findings from past research that PIU at work can carry both costs and benefits for employees. We have taken a progressive approach to explain this inconsistency. In the paper published in the Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology and the first conference paper presented at the 2022 AOM, we take a daily approach and propose that hedonic PIU (HPIU, i.e., relaxing oneself) benefits employees’ end-of-workday well-being and work engagement, while utilitarian PIU (UPIU, i.e., solving others’ problems) hinders their well-being and work engagement. We test our theorizing using three studies. In Study 1, we summarized previous PIU studies and relied on machine learning methods to classify the 618 PIU activities identified in prior studies. We found that prior research mixed HPIU and UPIU, which might lead to different conclusions. In Study 2, we condensed the PIU activity list from Study 1 and developed measurement scales for HPIU and UPIU. In Study 3, we analyzed 1,063 multi-wave daily inputs from 125 employees and found that on a daily basis, HPIU benefits employees’ well-being by fostering a state of recovery, while UPIU impedes well-being and work engagement by inducing a state of depletion. Moreover, supervisor support for employees’ personal behaviors strengthens the beneficial effect of HPIU. Additionally, we have carefully considered the reviewers’ suggestion to test whether there are other types of PIU and how they affect employees’ work outcomes. In the second conference paper presented at the 2023 AOM, we build on self-regulation theory and demonstrate that employees may reap benefits from their daily PIU by enhancing their daily task and creative performance. Employees’ cognitive flexibility works as the effective cognitive mechanism explaining the positive effects of PIU on task and creative performance. Moreover, the positive indirect effects of PIU on employee performance outcomes through cognitive flexibility are strengthened when employees have stronger supervisor support. Analyses of 1,056 data points from 122 employees and their 41 corresponding supervisors using a multi-wave experience sampling study across ten workdays supported our hypotheses. Overall, these studies advance our understanding of the effects of PIU.

23501920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23501920.value: A particularly intriguing and important direction for further expanding this study, which echoes the feedback from various journal reviewers, is to leverage accessible big data to explore all the potential Internet usage behaviors employees may perform at work. Current big data techniques and technology, such as electronic equipment, offer opportunities to collect such data without violating participants’ privacy. Based on this fundamental work, we can further extend the newly developed Internet usage behavior scales and inspire more research on understanding their effects. We consider two potential courses of action. First, we can collaborate with companies that desire to classify their employees’ various Internet usage activities. One of the team members is actively pursuing this. After gaining access to this objective data, we can utilize the machine learning techniques used in this research to significantly extend the current study and provide more insights into the pervasive phenomenon of Internet usage in the workplace. Second, we can use more traditional organizational methods to extend the current research project, for example, by employing qualitative methods such as in-depth interviews to exhaust all the potential Internet usage behaviors of employees and theorize their different impacts on employees.

23501920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23501920.value: This research project, with three research outputs using different methods and across different samples, jointly explores how nonwork-related Internet use at work affects various employee outcomes, including well-being, work engagement, task performance, and creative performance. Specifically, we found that overall nonwork-related personal Internet use at work is beneficial for fostering employees’ cognitive flexibility, which further improves their task and creative performance. This finding expands the previously dominant view that personal Internet usage is detrimental to employees. Moreover, we distinguish between two types of Internet use: hedonic PIU (HPIU), which involves using the internet for personal relaxation, and utilitarian PIU (UPIU), which involves using the internet to solve work-related problems for others. We found that the mixed positive and negative effects of PIU might be due to the combination of these two types of PIU. We found support for this proposition and revealed that HPIU helps employees recover and feel better at the end of the workday, enhancing their work engagement, whereas UPIU tends to drain employees, reducing their well-being and engagement. Additionally, the study found that when supervisors support personal internet use, the positive effects on relaxation and recovery are even stronger.

23600820.value: 2014年，香港一名外籍家庭傭工（下稱「外傭」）艾維亞納‧蘇利斯特亞（Erwiana Sulistyaningsih）遭受僱主殘酷對待。此後，外傭在港的工作情況受到廣泛報導。過去十年，研究人員與社會關社組一直提倡修改如留宿規定和法定工時等僱傭條例。然而，本港三十九萬名外傭中，有許多仍面臨著惡劣的居住環境、工時過長、遭受虐待及備受歧視的問題。 過去有研究指出，香港的英文報章對外傭的報導內容偏頗，惟未有研究對大量不同的報章以有系統的分析來驗證此觀點，亦未有找出有關外傭的正面和負面報導所採取的手法。人們由於缺乏相關知識，因此難以得知外傭的定型有否或如何隨著時間改變，亦無法作出有效的政策制定或介入來改變這些現象。 本文以三份中文報紙（超過5,000篇文章）和兩份英文報紙（超過1,500篇文章）為語料庫，旨在探討在2010年至2019年期間中文報紙與英文報紙如何描述外傭。我們將運用其在應用語言學、計算語言學及統計分析上的跨學科經驗，並使用經修正的語料庫輔助批判性話語分析法（Baker et al., 2008）。我們首先會根據三維模型（正負性、喚醒度和優勢度）將每句句子中含有情緒和情感的字詞分類，然後透過電腦軟件進行關鍵字分析，歸納出與外傭有關的主要議題，並藉由共詞分析與話語分析找出報章描述外傭時所採取的策略。接著，我們會運用多層次結構方程增長模式，測試各種因素（如權力或控制權、性別、種族、宗教和工作環境）及報章特質（如語言、日期和句子長度）如何影響描述外傭的句子所表達的情緒和情感。 本研究的意義體現在三個方面。第一，我們將應用一個全面的理論模式，以分析不同因素對報章描述外傭的影響。其次，我們會提出一個經改進的語料庫輔助批判性話語分析法。第三，我們會將研究結果分享予大眾，讓他們得知傳媒對外傭的正面和負面報導。研究結果可為記者、非政府組織和政策制定者提供資訊，並引導他們作出有效的政策制定或介入，以消除基於主流群體優越性（道德排他主義）而加諸於在港外傭和文化他者身上的定型觀念。本研究有助填補在外傭研究方面的不足，加深人們對外傭的認識，提升公眾對社會公義與人權的重視，從而促進本地人與少數族裔之間就社會議題達致共識，有助建構和諧社會。

23600820.label: Realisation of objectives
23600820.value: This study examined how Chinese-language and English-language newspapers in Hong Kong discursively portrayed migrant domestic workers (MDWs) from 2010 to 2019. In particular, we explored how news writers deployed five discursive strategies (Wodak 2001) to discursively represent MDWs: nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivation, and intensification/mitigation. We used a modified corpus-assisted critical discourse analytical approach (sentiment analysis of a text’s emotional tone, multilevel regression, and critical discourse analysis) to quantitatively and qualitatively study the portrayals of MDWs in Chinese and English news discourse. Major incidents that drove robust public discussions of MDWs in Hong Kong from 2010 to 2019 include the Manila Hostage Crisis (2010), the Right of Abode issue (2011-2013), and the abuse of Erwiana Sulistyaningsih (2014-2015). Thus, we focused on three three major incidents. Through the computational linguistic and critical discourse analytical approaches, we achieved all the three objectives. (1) Data collection and corpus compilation We collected news stories of Manila hostage crisis, right of abode debate, and abuse of Erwiana Sulistyaningsih published in three Chinese-language newspapers (Oriental Daily News, Apple Daily, and Ming Pao) and two English-language newspapers (South China Morning Post and The Standard) between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2019. These newspapers have various political stances and target specific subpopulations (citizens, elites, and expatriates). To collect the news articles, we deployed two news databases, WiseSearch and Factiva. We used WiseSearch to search the Chinese-language news articles for Chinese words (e.g., 外傭, 菲傭, 印傭, “foreign maid”). Likewise, we use Factiva to search the English news articles for English words (e.g., domestic helper, domestic worker, maid). We also retained the section, column, page numbers, and publication date. We then compiled five sub-corpora. The data comprise 1,512 articles; 23,489 sentences; and 50,540 words. Statistical power differs across levels. For  = .05 and an effect size of 0.10, statistical power is .96 for 1,512 articles, and exceeds .99 for both 23,489 sentences and 50,540 words (Konstantopoulos 2008). (2) Critical discourse analysis We read the concordance lines associated with the search words to identify six discursive strategies (nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivization, intensification and mitigation) Wodak (2001) suggested that the polarisation of self and others can be manifested through discursive strategies: nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivation, intensification, and mitigation. Nomination categorises the ingroup and outgroup members through membership categorisation devices and metaphors. Predication reveals the evaluative qualities, characteristics, and features assigned to social actors from evaluative attribution, collocations, and explicit predicates. Argumentation justifies positive or negative attributions through conditionality. Perspectivation or framing formulate the interlocutors’ viewpoints through direct and indirect speech. Intensification reinforces positive or negative discursive representations through augmentatives and hyperbole, whereas mitigation decreases the effects through diminutives. Discursive strategies often reflect news stances and hidden ideologies, with possible moral judgements or perceived problems vis-à-vis social power and control (Du Bois 2007). (3) Variables The first author and a research assistant coded sentences that discursively portrayed MDWs as burden, threat, danger, competitor, or having any other negative attributes (e.g., 菲蝗 “Filipino locusts”) as negative evaluations. Conversely, they coded sentences describing MDWs as contributing to society or when interlocutors expressed their empathy towards the MDWs’ experience as positive evaluations. (Many sentences are neither negative nor positive evaluations.) They also identified the linguistic cues and discourse strategies realizing these negative or positive evaluations (e.g., 努力工作養家 “working hard to earn a living” and 弱勢的菲傭 “disadvantaged MDWs”). Then, they resolved their disagreements through discussion and consensus. The inter-rater reliability was 99%. Other variables include the newspaper titles, news article features (section number, page number, gender of author, publication date, news articles or editorial op-eds), discursive strategies (nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivation, intensification, mitigation), linguistic underpinnings (evaluative attribution of negative traits, evaluative attribution of positive traits, hypothetical sentence, topoi, direct quote, indirect quote, metaphor), and grammatical features of the term “MDW” (MDW as a subject, as an object, as a pronoun, in main clause, in subordinate clause, pronoun). (4) Analytic Issues and Statistics Strategies To accurately analyze these data, we addressed the following issues with specific statistics strategies: (a) missing data (2% in this data set) with Markov Chain Monte Carlo multiple imputation, (b) similarities versus differences across sentences, articles, authors, or time with multilevel (ML) analysis (Hox et al. 2017), (c) dichotomous outcome with multilevel Logit (Hox et al. 2017), (d) multiple outcomes with multivariate outcome multilevel analysis (Hox et al. 2017), (d) indirect, ML mediation effects with multilevel M-tests (MacKinnon at al. 2004), (e) cross-level interactions (author x sentence) with random parameters in random effects models (Hox et al. 2017), (f) many hypotheses' false positives with the two stage linear step-up procedure (Benjamini et al. 2006), (g) compare effect sizes with Lagrange multiplier tests (Bertsekas 2014), (h) consistency of results across data sets (robustness) with analyses of data subsets and the original (unestimated) data (Kennedy 2008; for details, see Authors 2016). In another journal article, we applied this methodology to analyse 1,180 news articles on a different topic (Authors 2019). (5) Explanatory model We model the emotional valence, arousal, and dominance of each sentence with multilevel, multivariate outcome regression models (Goldstein 2011). P (Evaluationijkly) = F (y + eijkly + fjky + gky + syNewspaperky + tkyArticlejky + ujkyQuoteijkly+ vjkyDiscourse_Strategiesijkly + wjkyWordijkly + xjkyPhrasesijkly + zjkyInteractionijkly ) (1) The probability of each evaluation outcome variable y (positive, negative) for each sentence i in article j by author k in newspaper l of Evaluation is the expected value of the Logit function F, with a grand mean intercept βy with unexplained components (residuals) at the sentence-, article- and author-levels, eijkly, fjkly, and gkly. We enter explanatory variables in sequential sets to estimate the differences in the outcomes explained by each set (Kennedy 2008). First, we enter Newspaper (Oriental Daily News, Apple Daily, Ming Pao, The Standard (against the baselines of the South China Morning Post). As only omitting significant variables might yield omitted variable bias, we safely remove non-significant variables to increase precision and reduce multicollinearity (Kennedy 2008). Next, we enter article attributes: days after the earliest date, (days after the earliest date)2, page number, (page number)2, total number of sentences in article, and (total number of sentences in article)2 (Article). The squared terms (2) test for non-linear links between the explanatory variable and each outcome. Then, we enter sentence type (Quote vs. non-quote) and Discourse_Strategies (nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivation, intensification, mitigation). Next, we enter word attributes: total number of words in sentence, (total number of words in sentence)2, mean word length in sentence, and (mean word length in sentence)2 (Word). Then, we enter words/phrases found in sentence: (e.g., maid, 外傭 [foreign maid]) (Phrases). Lastly, we test the interactions among the above significant variables (Interaction). To broaden our critical discourse analysis, we interpreted and discussed our qualitative findings based on the statistics findings. To ensure reliability and validity of data interpretation, we invited a linguistics researcher to assess the identification of all discursive strategies. When there were inconsistencies, we discussed them until we reached an agreement.

23600820.label: Major findings and research outcome
23600820.value: Summary Statistics The average positive evaluation of sentences about MDWs is 0.013, while negative evaluations average 0.021, indicating that most sentences are neutral. Among the topics covered, 19% discuss hostage crises, 25% focus on the abuse of Erwiana Sulistyaningsih, and 56% relate to MDWs’ right of abode. Notably, nominations appear in nearly 24% of the sentences. Positive evaluations of MDWs are not significantly different across contexts, so we focus on negative evaluations. Most of the variance in negative evaluations comes from the article (58%) and sentence level (42%), with minimal variance at the author or newspaper levels. Negative evaluations are influenced by the topic, presence of MDWs, and discourse strategies. Sentences about the hostage crisis are 37% less likely to have negative evaluations compared to those about the right of abode, while discussions of Sulistyaningsih's abuse are 25% more likely to be negative. The topic explains less than 9% of the variance in negative evaluations. When MDWs are mentioned in various parts of a sentence, negative evaluations increase (by 29% in the subject position, for example). Discourse strategies such as argumentation and metaphor also correlate with negative evaluations, contributing nearly 4% to the variance. Interactions involving MDWs further affect negative evaluations. For instance, sentences about the hostage crisis that reference MDWs are 34% more likely to be negative. Conversely, some references, like MDWs in subordinate clauses, reduce the likelihood of negative evaluations. Main Findings and Implications Despite differing political views, media sources often delegitimize MDWs in discussions of their rights and during crises, reflecting broader societal attitudes in HK. Writers frame MDWs as threats to social stability, using language that emphasizes danger and burden. This portrayal creates a dichotomy between "us" (local people) and "them" (MDWs), intensifying the antagonism. The analysis reveals that commentators often position themselves as victims to deflect criticism and avoid responsibility, while simultaneously portraying MDWs as inferior yet threatening. This ambivalence serves to reinforce their perceived superiority over MDWs. In contrast, supportive voices depict MDWs as beneficial, emphasizing their contributions to society. The discussion around MDWs shifts focus from potential threats to the historical and present contributions they make, advocating for justice and fairness. Media narratives about MDWs vary significantly based on grammatical structures and discourse strategies, reflecting broader societal attitudes towards this group. Future research should explore broader contexts and incorporate various media forms to gain a comprehensive understanding of public attitudes towards MDWs.

23600820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23600820.value: The study on the discursive representation of Migrant Domestic Workers (MDWs) highlights critical insights into media portrayals and public perceptions. To further develop this research, future studies should expand the scope by including a broader range of media sources, such as online platforms and social media, to capture diverse public opinions on MDWs. This can help reveal how narratives evolve over time and across different contexts. Additionally, qualitative methods, such as interviews and conversational analyses, could provide deeper insights into personal experiences and societal attitudes towards MDWs, particularly in light of recent events like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Anti-Extradition Law Amendment Bill movement. Exploring how these events may have shifted perceptions can enrich the understanding of MDWs' social dynamics. Researchers should also consider longitudinal studies to track changes in discourse over time, potentially correlating these shifts with policy changes or major societal events. This comprehensive approach would enhance the current findings and contribute significantly to discussions on social justice, representation, and the rights of MDWs in Hong Kong and beyond. Such efforts could ultimately foster a more nuanced dialogue around the contributions and challenges faced by MDWs in society.

23600820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23600820.value: This research project investigates how migrant domestic workers (MDWs) are portrayed in Hong Kong newspapers from 2010 to 2019. By analyzing over 6,500 articles, the study aims to understand the language and strategies used to either stigmatize or humanize MDWs. It highlights significant trends in media representation, revealing how various factors—like power dynamics, gender, and culture—affect these portrayals. The findings show that despite different political viewpoints, media often depict MDWs negatively, framing them as threats to society. This creates a divide between "us" (local residents) and "them" (MDWs). Conversely, some articles recognize the valuable contributions of MDWs, advocating for their rights and humanity. The significance of this research lies in its potential to influence public perception and policy regarding MDWs. By shedding light on how language shapes attitudes, the study encourages a more nuanced understanding of these workers’ roles in society. Future research could expand to include online media and personal narratives, deepening the conversation about social justice and the challenges MDWs face in Hong Kong. Ultimately, this work aims to promote fairer representations and better support for MDWs in the community.

23601120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601120.value: 1 Abstract A central notion in the philosophy of mathematics is that of the consistency of mathematical theories. Roughly speaking, a theory is consistent if its implications can never be shown to contradict one another. Here are two main questions: Question 1. Are our best and most commonly accepted mathematical theories – for instance, arithmetic (as formalized by mathsf{PA}, the Peano axioms for arithmetic), and set theory (as formalized by mathsf{ZFC}, the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms plus the Axiom Choice) – consistent? And Question 2. What is the epistemic status of the consistency of these theories? Do we – or could we – have epistemically good (e.g. reliable, reasonable, justified, knowledgeable etc) beliefs that they are consistent? These questions are extremely important for our understanding of mathematics: consistency is a seemingly weak property, but our ability to know or justifiably believe claims about the consistency of our best theories are called into serious question due to results by Gödel and others in the foundations of mathematics. My project seeks to answer these questions by considering some of the most promising ways in which consistency might be justified. In Part 1, I will examine mathematical proofs of consistency. We know from Gödel that no consistent theory is capable of proving its own consistency. Nevertheless, there are mathematically interesting consistency proofs in which a theory's consistency is proven in some other theory. In this part of the project, my task is to figure out whether these mathematical proofs are capable of justifying consistency. This is not simple, since not all proofs give rise to justification: part of my task will be to distinguish those proofs which justify their conclusions from those which do not. In Part 2, I will provide a positive account, appealing to our ability to imagine scenarios. I will develop an account of imagination which, I hope, will support the conclusion that we can imagine situations in which certain mathematical scenarios are true, and that by doing so, we can gain justification of consistency.

23602520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602520.value: Creative citizens are socially and culturally engaged. To engage, they demonstrate creative agency in enacting citizenship by enabling new production of meanings and values. To meet the contemporary challenges of sustainable communities in the 21st century, artists, curators, and cultural workers arguably act as creative citizens at the frontiers of the fields of contemporary art, museums, and heritage. Creative citizenship is considered a civil culture imperative for building reciprocal responsibility between state and citizen, and amongst citizens. This project explores how artists, curators, and cultural workers contribute to the value of community and civic well-being in Hong Kong and Taiwan, taking creative citizenship as a normative theory. Drawing on the analytical framework of the ‘creative circuit’, this project investigates the regulation and production of creative practices which purposefully target specific civic goals through the involvement of the collaborative, community and civic forms of participation, on the one hand, and assesses the consumption patterns of participants, on the other. Bearing in mind both the potential and limitations of the civic-creative practices, the project finally discusses the policy implications of the practices for the management of creativity and cultural planning. Creative citizenship is mainly manifested in the West and grounded in the practices of media, design, and DIY. This research will expand related scholarship into Asia and will bridge the gap between it and the fields of contemporary art, museums, and heritage. It primarily raises the question of how the proposition, ‘creative citizenship’ might fit into the social and cultural landscapes of Hong Kong and Taiwan. Both regions deserve examination due to their prominent roles in Asia, with vibrant civil societies in which cultural citizenship is a growing concern. This research will be the first scholarly study to the under-explored relationship between creativity and citizenship in Asia. It will further advance a sociocultural paradigm shift in creativity studies, and contribute to the social turn in the studies of aesthetics, and museum and heritage practices. It will also be a source of inspiration and materials for arts professionals and cultural policymakers in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

23602520.label: Realisation of objectives
23602520.value: This research project is to investigate how artists, curators, and cultural workers contribute to the value of community and civic wellbeing in Hong Kong and Taiwan, taking into account creative citizenship as a normative theory. The study met its objectives effectively, despite the fact that the pandemic in Taiwan caused a delay in research. The research team has effectively identified and documented the creative-civic projects. Examples of Hong Kong case studies include creative productions of Lo Ting, curatorial productions of Chinese art as a creative heritage, Yim Tin Tsai and Lamma Island's art festivals, Wan Chai and North Point's community art initiatives, and the MaD School project on the revitalisation of the Tsui Ping River. Taiwanese case studies include the Guanci Social Housing public art project, the Meinung Anti-Dam Movement, the Yellow Butterfly Festival, Community University at Chao Huang Temple, and the Mattauw Land Art Season: In Search of One Thousand Names of the River. The projects cover the domains of art, museums, and heritage. In Hong Kong and Taiwan, we interviewed curators, artists, cultural workers, cultural researchers, and NGO project leaders, among other creative professionals, as part of our fieldwork on these initiatives. In addition to providing a critical discourse on the experiences of communities and participants in creative citizenship, the research work allowed an evaluation of how well their initiatives enhanced knowledge production and experience articulation for civic involvement. We looked at how communities in Taiwan and Hong Kong have exercised their citizenship through innovative forms of involvement, drawing on the ideas that community is the material foundation of citizenship and that creativity is a means of generating community engagement. We argued that by showcasing their capacity to co-create public or communal places, their creative endeavors have assisted communities in establishing an alternative kind of citizenship. They empower themselves to govern their spaces and advance their civic ideals in the process. Furthermore, though officials refused to be interviewed (thus 20 % of objective 4 was not completed), we have made some inferences on the role that governments play in these innovative endeavours. The study has hinted at potential tensions between the creative endeavours of communities and the state's focus on social welfare or cultural tourism. Overall, the study emphasised the contribution of the creative projects to civic engagement and the production of public or communal spaces and the manifestation of creative citizenship as an alternative form of citizenship in societies such as Hong Kong and Taiwan, where contentious creative industries and the entanglement between civic agency and state control are evident. Furthermore, PI has conducted research on specific projects by referencing other critical concepts. A study considers the creative productions of Lo Ting, a mythic figure, as borderscaping—active, signifying, discursive, and affective practices that involve dynamic processes of adaptation, contestation, or resistance in the subject-making of Hong Kong people. The study reveals the challenges creative citizens faced in identity-making between 1997 and 2014. Another study foregrounds the local citizens’ curatorial creativity, which can engage new community collaboration and utilize art heritage as a source of inspiration for generating new knowledge and expressions in culturally contested Hong Kong. Unofficial curators and artists in Hong Kong, through their curatorial works of Chinese art, are arguably producing a creative heritage that is inextricably linked to the concept of creativity, rather than the concept of continuity in the living heritage approach advocated by Poulios (2014). The studies contributed to a critical understanding of how these practices shape identities, generate new artistic interpretations, and establish new communities. The Education Plan was executed to realize the final objective - to foster platforms for citizens to develop original and innovative ideas for tackling complex and emerging problems in and of sustainable communities. PI set up an academic course entitled ‘Creative Citizens Project’ and realized it in the academic year 2023/24 in collaboration with socially engaged artist, Nanxi Liu, and the Diocesan Pastoral Centre for Workers – Ethnic Minority Service. Under the support of the organisation and the artist, the university students of the course, and a group of Napalese women co-produced creative works that convey their ideas and methods of dealing with their cultural experiences and living circumstances. Their works were festured in the 2023 exhibition ‘Home Away from Home (मातृभूमि)’, at the Art Gallery of the Lingnan University in December 2023. The public display underscored their cultural representation and participation as well as their capabilities in enacting creative citizenship. The initiative proposes a paradigm for engaging minority or politically and culturally marginalised persons in using creativity to express themselves and interact with society.

23602520.label: Major findings and research outcome
23602520.value: The research primarily reveals that the creative projects have enhanced new knowledge production and experience articulation for civic engagement while also providing a critical discourse on the experiences of communities and participants in creative citizenship. Two international journal papers, a book chapter, and an international conference present the research findings. All the findings/papers are peer-reviewed. At the international conference ‘The 14th Asian Conference on Arts & Humanities,’ PI and a researcher co-presented a paper on ‘Creative Citizenship in Taiwan and Hong Kong.’ By synthesising insights gained through studies of various creative projects in Hong Kong and Taiwan, it finds that different actors have shown ingenuity in devising strategies to interact with government and with society as well as to engage in the public cultural sphere. They also participate in the exchange and creation of meanings and affective registers of their surroundings, contributing to the formation of a creative class known as creative citizens. The study helps formulate the relationship between creativity and citizenship and reveals differences and similarities in the enactment of creative citizenship in the two places. In the paper, ‘Community as A Material Basis of Creative Citizenship in Taiwan and Hong Kong,’ it maintains that communities have effectively practiced their citizenship by creative modes of engagement in Taiwan and Hong Kong. They empower themselves to govern their spaces and promote their civic values, contributing to the production of public or communal spaces and the manifestation of creative citizenship as an alternative form of citizenship. Yet potential conflicts exist between the creative efforts of communities and the state’s agenda focused on social welfare or cultural tourism. The study also validates the concepts of community as the material basis of citizenship and creativity as a means of generating community engagement in Asian societies, where contentious creative industries and the interplay between civic agency and state control are evident. In the paper, ‘Borderscaping Hong Kong: Lo Ting and Its Creative Agency,’ it finds that Hong Kong curators, artists, filmmakers, and cultural workers co-create a mythical half-human and half-fish figure, Lo Ting, from the perspective of ‘borderscape’ in two different political-cultural contexts, post-1997 and post-2014. By addressing new (geo)political-cultural imaginations and social-spatial imaginaries, the paper argues that the practice can seek a new spatiality of politics, moving away from the rigid territorial spatialities of the nation-state and towards representing, negotiating, and contesting the 'where' of the border. This approach provides a counterhegemonic alternative to the nationalistic homeland orientation. The study highlights the creative agency of the productions in craving a new form of becoming or belonging and re-envisioning the Hong Kong-China border. In the paper, ‘Curating Chinese Art as Creative Heritage,’ it finds that unofficial curators and artists have considered traditional Chinese art as a creative heritage in culturally contested Hong Kong. Their practice suggests a new interpretation of heritage art, inextricably linked to the concept of creativity, rather than the concept of continuity in the living heritage approach espoused by Poulios (2014). The study foregrounds its citizens’ curatorial creativity, which can engage new community collaboration and utilize art heritage as a source of inspiration for generating new knowledge and expressions. A case study included the IP’s practice-based research exhibition, ‘Sensing Things,’ and its engagement activity with a group of Nepalese women, which is part of the Education Plan

23602520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23602520.value: This research project engages in an interdisciplinary exploration of citizens' creative productions and experiences as a form of citizenship, responding to their social context. In this context, state-led creative industries are increasing the economic value of cultural products and undermining the role of creative agencies in civic well-being. To facilitate the future development of creative productions and their relationship with local communities, the research team suggests further shaping creativity as a critical site for experiencing and negotiating citizenship in the contested environments of Hong Kong and Taiwan. Furthermore, it is crucial for the academic sector to initiate additional research projects that explore the various aspects of creative citizenship. 1. The role of governments and their policies in shaping the connection between creative arts and civic culture; 2. The capabilities (not only rights or responsibilities) of and the relationship between different citizens (not limited to creative professionals) in developing new creative practices and strategies for civic participation.

23602520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23602520.value: This research project conducts an empirical study on the role of creative agencies in enacting citizenship by facilitating the creation of new meanings and values in Taiwan and Hong Kong. It is the first scholarly study to explore the relationship between creativity and citizenship in the underexplored region of Asia and bridges creative citizenship with the fields of art, museums, and heritage. Despite the different narratives in Taiwan and Hong Kong regarding the development of creative citizenship, both communities face the challenge of shaping creativity as a critical site for experiencing and negotiating citizenship in their respective contested environments. The research contributes to advancing a socio-cultural paradigm shift in creativity studies and the social turn in the studies of aesthetics, museums, and heritage practices. Furthermore, it is arguable that artists, curators, and cultural workers serve as creative citizens at the forefront of society. In line with the shifting paradigm of citizenship studies from the political idealised conception of citizenship to the cultural dimension of citizenship, the research on creative citizenship has offered new conceptual inspiration and empirical materials for arts professionals and cultural policymakers in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

23602920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23602920.value: 情景，意義和主體性：香港自殺與政治危機研究

23602920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602920.value: Youth suicide rates are on the rise in many countries. According to the World Health Organisation, suicide is the second-leading cause of death among 15- to 29- year-olds. Political unrest is thought to be a factor associated with heightened distress among youth. With an increasing number of young people devoted to political protests around the world, which sometimes involve the use of suicide as a means of protest, understanding the rise and spread of suicide in the context of a political crisis is a pressing concern for suicide prevention professionals. The Anti-Extradition Bill (AEB) movement taking place in Hong Kong in 2019 reflects these trends, in that most of participants are young people. After a high profile jump by a protestor, several suicides believed to be related to the political crisis were publicised and mourned by protestors, and research indicates that the number of people who suffer from depression and suicidal ideation is on the rise since the beginning of the movement (The University of Hong Kong, 2019). This project will use the AEB movement of Hong Kong as a case study to understand how protestors and supporters of social movements perceive suicide in a political crisis and how they persevere in face of political uncertainties. The project will use a qualitative approach that attends to context, meaning and agency to explore how people’s structural and cultural milieu shape their meanings of suicide and hope. It will investigate 1) how the meaning of suicide is communicated through suicide notes, suicide acts and media; 2) how protestors and supporters of the movement make sense of protest-related suicides; and 3) what factors shape their meaning of hope. The method includes two parts. Documentary research of suicide notes and media reports will be carried out to interpret the meaning of suicides communicated by the deceased and by the media. Life history interviews will be conducted with the protestors and supporters of the movement to solicit their experience of exposure to protest-related suicide. In terms of theory, this research will contribute to the fields of sociology of mental health and suicide research through advancing our understanding of risk and protective factors against youth suicide, suicide diffusion and resilience. In terms of practice, the findings will have significant implications for the development of cultural-and context-specific suicide prevention strategies for youth in Hong Kong and in other conflict-affected areas. 情景，意義和主體性：香港自殺與政治危機研究 青少年自殺率在多個國家有上升趨勢。根據世界衛生組織的數據，自殺是15 至29歲人士的第二大死亡原因。政治動盪被認為是令青少年壓力加劇的一個重要因素。當全球越來越多年青人投身政治抗爭，有時並以自殺作為抗爭方法時，了解政治危機下自殺的出現和擴散成為了防止自殺專業人士的關注點。2019年香港的反修例運動反映了以上的趨勢，佔很大比數的參與者是年輕人士。其中一位抗爭者高調跳樓死亡後，接着幾單被認為與政治危機有關的自殺事件亦被廣泛傳播和哀悼。研究又顯示，反修例運動開始後，患上抑鬱和被自殺念頭困擾的人數增加（香港大學， 2019)。是次研究會用反修例運動作為個案去探索抗爭者和社會運動的支持者如何理解政治危機下的自殺，以及他們在政治不確定的環境下如何堅持下去。 是次研究採納質性方法從情境、意義和主體性三方面去探索社會結構和文化環境如何塑造人們對自殺和希望的理解和意義。研究會調查1) 自殺的意義如何透過遺書，自殺行為和傳媒表達出來；2) 運動抗爭者和支持者如何理解與抗爭有關的自殺；3）什麼因素構成抗爭者和支持者的希望。研究方法分兩部份。第一部份是自殺者遺書和傳媒報道的文件分析, 以詮釋自殺者和傳媒表達出來的自殺意義。第二部份是生命史訪談，以理解運動抗爭者和支持者接觸政治抗爭自殺的經驗。理論方面，這研究可促進精神健康社會學及自殺學中對自殺風險、避免年輕人自殺的保護因素、自殺擴散以及復元韌性的理解。實踐方面，研究結果可為香港及其他政治動盪地區發展文化及情景為本的青少年自殺預防策略提供啟示。

23603520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23603520.value: 不離巢？英國、中國內地及香港的年輕人與父母共同居住的研究

23603520.label: Project Objectives
23603520.value: To describe the trends of parent–adult child co-residence for the 25-year period from 1990 in the UK, mainland China, and Hong Kong. Recent studies and ongoing media attention suggest that young adults living with their parents is a growing trend in both Western and Chinese societies (e.g., Davidson 2014; Forrest and Xian 2018; Rudgard 2017; Stone et al. 2011). This phenomenon differs from the individualism that is thought to accompany economic development and modernisation. However, less is known about the changes of such co-residence. Drawing on representative survey and census data from 1990, the proposed study will examine the trends of the co-residence of young adults (21 to 35 years of age) with their parents in recent decades in three societies with differing family cultures: the UK (Western culture), mainland China (Chinese culture) and Hong Kong (Chinese culture with a British colonial history). Specifically, two main issues regarding the trends of co-residence will be addressed: (1) what are the main characteristics of co-residing adult children and their parents and (2) how these characteristics change. To the PI’s best knowledge, this study will be the first to describe co-residence trends in the UK, mainland China and Hong Kong over 25 years. A better understanding of the changes in co-residence provides insights into the transition to adulthood, in which the move to an independent residence is an important life marker that has significant implications for marriage, fertility, social mobility and inter- and intra-generational tension (Forrest and Yip 2012). To examine the key factors associated with changes in young adults’ co-residence with parents across the three societies. This study will use multiple waves of representative data to examine how the changes in parent–adult child co-residence are associated with factors derived from three perspectives: the perspective of cultural norms, the life course perspective and the social inequality perspective of intergenerational transfer. In addition, this study suggests that young adults’ co-residence with parents may stand out as a new type of intergenerational transfer that maintains family-based inequality through the transmission of resources. The occurrence of co-residence depends not only on the young adults’ economic situation, but also on their parents’ socioeconomic status; transfer could be bi-directional between parents and their offspring. The potential findings of this study will contribute to the theories on life course and intergenerational inequality and highlight the importance of considering residence, along with family formation and school-to-work transition, as concurrent and interlinked domains of youth transition. To investigate the causal relationships between the key factors and parent–adult child co-residence in Hong Kong through random telephone survey with hypothetical situations (survey experiment) Most previous studies used cross-sectional data (e.g., Stone et al. 2011; Ting and Chiu 1992) or macro-level statistics (e.g., Arundel and Ronald 2016) to examine the factors that contribute to parent–adult child co-residence. However, the association between key factors (e.g., cultural attitudes and delayed marriage) and co-residence cannot be simply described in causal terms. Their directions could be reversed; for example, co-residence with parents may delay young adults’ marriage (Yu and Kuo 2016) or change family attitudes (Cooper and Luengo-Prado 2018). To examine the causal dynamics between the key factors found in the analysis of survey and census data, this study will conduct a random telephone survey with hypothetical situations in Hong Kong, which has a strong Chinese cultural tradition of familism and a British cultural influence. This will allow an investigation of how the determinants of co-residence operate in a modern city that mixes Chinese and Western culture. This study will thus contribute to the literature on co-residence by identifying the key factors that contribute to parent–adult child co-residence. To provide policy recommendations for residential planning, mitigating intergenerational inequality, and supporting youth development in Hong Kong The potential findings of this study will have important policy insights. First, the study will increase the government’s awareness of the prevalence of the parent–adult child co-residence and its potential effects on social inequality. If prolonged parental support is found to be a main reason for parent–adult child co-residence, family-based social inequality may be solidified or even exacerbated. In addition, the potential findings regarding the importance of intergenerational transfer has implications for ageing policies. If parents’ limited savings are exhausted by co-residence with adult children, they may find it difficult to maintain a decent standard of living during their old age. If filial piety is found to be the main reason that the adult youth co-reside with and provide care for their parents, the government should seek to alleviate the caregivers’ burden and stress. Therefore, drawing on the key research findings, the proposed study will provide a policy report with concrete policy recommendations for planning residential policies, family policies and policies to support young people in the employment and housing domains in Hong Kong.

24100520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100520.value: 最近的研究表明，腫瘤內部只存在極小部分的細胞具有致瘤性。根據癌症幹細胞理論，腫瘤由癌症幹細胞（CSC）維持，這些癌症幹細胞會自我更新或分化為不同的細胞類型。CSC對化療有抗藥性，並促進復發和轉移。發展針對CSC的標靶是一個重要的方向。前期研究發現，線粒體谷氨酸轉運蛋白SLC25A22在帶有APC / KRAS突變的結直腸癌（CRC）為合成致死基因。在本課題中，我們進一步評估SLC25A22在APC / KRAS突變CRC中的作用。我們在CRC細胞系，小鼠和CRC類器官建立SLC25A22敲除模型，並研究了其對與CSC相關的特性的影響。SLC25A22敲除可降低TCA循環代謝產物琥珀酸，從而促進DNA去甲基化酶（TET1-3）和組蛋白去甲基化酶（KDMs）。TET1-3和KDMs的活性增加導致WNT /β-catenin活性降低，同時WNT靶向CSC標記（ASCL2，CD44，EPHB2 / 3和LGR5）的表達降低。機制研究表明，SLC25A22的敲除與組蛋白脫甲基酶（KDM5A / 5C）介導的H3K4me3的丟失有關。H3K4me3是維持CSC的決定性因素，染色質免疫沉澱-PCR分析表明，SLC25A22敲除導致組蛋白H3K4me3在ASCL2，CD44，EPHB2 / 3和LGR5的轉錄起始位點（TSS）丟失，尤其是LGR5。因此，SLC25A22敲除抑制LGR5 mRNA和蛋白表達，同時增加細胞分化的標誌物KRT20。在CRC 類器官和APC / KRAS小鼠模型，SLC25A22敲除顯著減少CRC的發生和發展。因此，我們假設SLC25A22通過琥珀酸對TET和KDM5A / 5C產生抑制作用，促進APC / KRAS突變CRC中的癌幹性。在本研究項目中，我們旨在：1）利用CRC類器官評估SLC25A22在APC / KRAS突變結直腸CSC中的作用；2）確定Slc25a22敲除對APC / KRAS小鼠中的CSC的影響；和3）探索SLC25A22驅動CSC的分子機制。通過這一系列的工作，說明SLC25A22促進CRC的分子機制。

24100520.label: Realisation of objectives
24100520.value: Objective #1: Results achieved: 1. SLC25A22 is essential for the maintenance of CSC-enriched tumorspheres. To test the role of SLC25A22 in colorectal CSCs, we cultured CSC-enriched tumorspheres (CSC28, LS174T, CSC28) generated from low-passage, CRC patient-derived CSC-enriched spheroids with >50% positivity in CD133/CD44. Flow cytometry sorting of POP66 into CD133highCD44high and CD133lowCD44low cells revealed higher SLC25A22 expression in the former. Forced differentiation of CSCs in 2D culture resulted in decreased SLC25A22 together with CD133, CD44 and EPHB2 compared to tumorspheres. SLC25A22 is thus increased in CSC-enriched tumorspheres. Next, we evaluated the function of SLC25A22. SLC25A22 knockdown reduced mRNA expression of CSC markers such as CD133, CD44, EPHB2/3, LGR5 and SOX9. Western blot verified downregulated CD133, CD44, EPHB2 and LGR5 proteins after SLC25A22 loss. Concordantly, SLC25A22 depletion suppressed CD133highCD44high cell fraction in POP66. Functionally, SLC25A22 knockdown suppressed tumorsphere formation and attenuated clonogenicity as determined by limiting dilution assay. These data suggest that SLC25A22 is critical for maintenance of CSC phenotypes. Objective #2: Results achieved: 1. Colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout in mice impairs colorectal tumorigenesis. We generated Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice to ablate SLC25A22 in the colon stem cell lineage. In parallel, Slc25a22fl/flCdx2-CreERT2 mice were established to delete SLC25A22 in differentiated enterocytes. Both mice strains were subjected to azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium (AOM/DSS)-induced CRC. Compared to wildtype, Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice showed reduced tumor number (P<0.01) and load (P<0.01) . Slc25a22fl/flCdx2-CreERT2 mice had no effect, implying colon stem cell-specific function of SLC25A22 in CRC. H&E and Ki67 staining showed that Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mouse tumors had lower histological grade and cell proliferation, respectively. Western blot revealed down-regulation of SLC25A22, LGR5 and EPHB2 in Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mouse tumors. Confirming this, IF showed co-staining of SLC25A22 and LGR5 in tumors from wildtype, which is abrogated in Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice. We next performed scRNA-seq of tumors, revealing six Epcam+ clusters, including CSCs (Lgr5high, Sox9high) and differentiated cells (Krt20high). Of note, Cdx2 is elevated in differentiated lineages, supporting that SLC25A22 deletion in differentiated enterocytes is ineffective compared to CSCs. Pseudotime analysis unraveled a trajectory from CSCs to proliferative cancer cells and then to differentiated, Paneth-like and metabolic clusters. Importantly, colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout depleted CSCs and proliferative clusters, while enriching differentiated, Paneth-like and metabolic clusters (all P<0.001), implying that SLC25A22 knockout accelerates evolution trajectory towards differentiation. These infer CSC-specific role of SLC25A22. 2. Colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout in mice reactivates intratumoral CD8+T cells. To explore the impact of colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout on TIME, we analyzed CD45+ cell populations based on scRNA-seq data from AOM/DSS model. Compared to wildtype, Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mouse tumors were enriched in T cells, while neutrophils were depleted. We next divided T and NK cell populations into 9 clusters. Among these cell clusters, naïve T cells were downregulated in Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice, whereas proliferating T, CD4+T, CD8+T and NK cells were significantly upregulated, implying that colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout re-activated antitumor immunity. Moreover, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and chemokine signaling were enriched in CD8+T cells from Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice. Corroborating these, CD8+T cells from Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice had elevated activation and effector scores, concomitant with reduced dysfunction and exhaustion scores. Flow cytometry validated increased intratumoral CD8+T cells and activation status (Granzyme B, IFN-γ, TNF-α) in Slc25a22fl/flLgr5-CreERT2 mice. Hence, colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout reactivates intratumoral CD8+T cells. Objective #3: Results achieved: 1. Colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 drives impairment of intratumoral CD8+ T cells to promote colorectal tumorigenesis. To ask if colorectal CSCs could directly modulate CD8+T cells, we respectively co-cultured PBMCs-derived human CD8+T cells with CSC tumorspheres or their conditioned medium, and determined T cell proliferation and cytotoxic markers. Direct CSCs-CD8+T cell co-culture impaired CD8+T cell proliferation and cytotoxic function (Granzyme B, IFN-γ, TNF-α), while CSC conditioned medium had no effect, implying that intercellular interaction is required for CSCs-mediated CD8+T cell inactivation. SLC25A22 knockdown in colorectal CSCs rescued CD8+T cell proliferation as well as cytotoxic function, underling the role of CSC-specific SLC25A22 in CD8+T cell inactivation. 2. A SLC25A22-fumarate-PVR axis underlies CRC stemness and its associated immunosuppression -Membrane proteomics unraveled SLC25A22-dependent expression of immune checkpoint PVR in colorectal CSCs. We analyzed membrane proteomes of CSC28/POP66 with SLC25A22 knockdown and overexpression. Overlap of proteins downregulated by SLC25A22 knockdown while being upregulated by SLC25A22 identified four membrane proteins among which PVR is a ligand for immune checkpoints. We validated that total and surface PVR protein was reduced by SLC25A22 knockdown in colorectal CSCs and in colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout tumors. This suggests that SLC25A22 might promote PVR to elicit immunotherapy resistance in CSCs. -Colorectal CSCs antagonize CD8+T cells via SLC25A22-PVR-TIGIT axis. PVR knockdown in CSCs rescued CD8+ T cell function after co-culture, inferring PVR as a functional checkpoint on CSCs. More importantly, re-expression of PVR in CSCs abolished the rescue effect of SLC25A22 knockdown on CD8+T cell inactivation. To probe the corresponding receptor on CD8+T cells, we performed CellChat analysis of scRNA-seq (AOM/DSS model), and identified crosstalk between CSC-PVR and TIGIT inhibitory receptor on CD8+T cells in our transgenic mouse model. SLC25A22-PVR-TIGIT axis thus underpins CD8+T cell suppression by colorectal CSCs. -SLC25A22 promotes PVR expression via its downstream metabolite fumarate. To ask how SLC25A22 regulates PVR levels, we treated SLC25A22-depleted CSCs with its downstream metabolites. Notably, fumarate, but not other metabolites, rescued PVR in SLC25A22- depleted CSCs. Furthermore, we demonstrated that fumarate binds to PVR by SPR assay (Kd=0.47mM) and inhibited PVR ubiquitination, thereby promoting its protein stability. Taken together, our work has comprehensively achieved all three objectives, and identified that colorectal cancer stem cell (CSC)-specific function of SLC25A22, where it plays a pivotal role in maintenance of stemness and fostering an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This has potential translational relevance, as targeting SLC25A22 might be a possible strategy to overcome chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance associated with cancer stem cells in CRC.

24100520.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100520.value: CRC is the third most common cancer worldwide. According to the stem cell theory of cancer, tumors are maintained by a subpopulation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) with self-renewal capacity and multipotent potential. CSCs are often considered seeds for tumor initiation, metastasis and drug resistance. However, the mechanisms underlying the regulation of CSCs remains poorly understood. In this study, we examined the role of SLC25A22-mediated metabolism in modulating CSCs functionality and its underlying mechanisms of action. In our study, we demonstrated that elevated SLC25A22 correlates with CRC stemness markers in human CRC cohorts, and SLC25A22 knockdown suppressed stemness features in human colorectal CSCs cell lines. To probe the function of SLC25A22 on CSCs in vivo, we established colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout mice and subject them to the AOM/DSS model of CRC. Colon stem cell-specific knockout of SLC25A22 suppressed colorectal tumorigenesis. Single cell RNA-sequencing of SLC25A22 knockout reduced proportion of colorectal CSCs, with a corresponding increase in differentiated CRC cells. This series of experiments confirmed the vital role of SLC25A22 in maintaining CSCs in CRC. Our research also first unveiled the interplay between CSCs and the tumor immune microenvironment. We found that colorectal CSCs have remarkably high expression of immune checkpoint PVR as compared to a panel of CRC cells. In AOM/DSS-induced CRC, scRNA-seq revealed that Lgr5+ CSCs subpopulation have increased PVR expression compared to non-CSCs fraction. Corroborating these findings, CSCs markers positively correlated to PVR in TCGA CRC cohort. In support of this, co-culture of CSCs (POP66, LS174T) with human CD8+ T cells impaired T cell proliferation and attenuated markers of T cell activity. We next asked if SLC25A22 is critical for this process. SLC25A22 knockdown in CSCs inhibited PVR, which in turn reversed the suppressive function of colorectal CSCs on CD8+ T cell proliferation and cytotoxic activation. Confirming this, colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout reduced intratumoral PVR expression, and increased infiltration and activation of CD8+ T cells. Mechanistically, we elucidated that SLC25A22 downstream metabolite fumarate binds to PVR to stabilize its protein expression, leading to elevated membrane PVR in CSCs. This work has been presented as an oral lecture at Digestive Disease Week meeting in 2023, and currently the manuscript is ready for submission. Apart from this work, we have also published several articles related to SLC25A22 and CRC (Nat Commun, Gut, Protein & Cell, Oncogene, etc). A total of 16 papers were published based on this funding.

24100520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100520.value: To improve our understanding of the role of SLC25A22 on cancer stem cells (CSC) in colorectal cancer (CRC), we will further open up collaborative networks with other academic researchers to investigate the impact of SLC25A22 with our colon stem cell-specific Slc25a22 knockout mice models. I have collaborated with researchers from the local and international institutions who has expertise with different aspects of oncology research. We will focus on other aspects of CSC-specific SLC25A22 on CRC, including the impact on tumor immunology, expression of immune checkpoints, and its impact on immunotherapy efficacy. For medium term plans, we will continue to develop the nanoparticle formulation encapsulating siSLC25A22 for boosting the efficacy of chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Based on our results, we will apply for further R&D grants and contracts available through a competitive basis.

24100520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100520.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cancer worldwide and it has recently surpassed lung cancer to become the most common cancer in Hong Kong. A subpopulation of cancer cells, termed cancer stem cells (CSCs), exhibits self-renewal capacity and are considered the seeds of tumor initiation and metastasis. More importantly, CSCs are associated with chemoresistance, and they contribute to relapse and metastasis. In this study, we demonstrated that SLC25A22-mediated tumor metabolism crosstalks with colorectal CSCs to promote stemness and immunosuppression using a series of in vitro and in vivo models, including colorectal cancer stem cell lines and colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout mice. Single cell deconvolution elucidated that colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 knockout could specifically repress colorectal CSCs and promote differentiation of cancer cells. In addition, we have identified that colon stem cell-specific SLC25A22 significantly modulated tumor immune microenvironment. Specifically, SLC25A22-mediated metabolite fumarate was found to promote the expression of an immune checkpoint PVR, which in turn could antagonize intratumoral CD8+ T cells infiltration and activation. Together, our study implies SLC25A22 as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming CSCs-associated chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance and provides a solid foundation for the development of metabolism-based targeting approaches for improving therapy efficacy in CRC.

24103120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24103120.value: 貧血在患有慢性腎病的患者中很常見。重組人促紅細胞生成素（rHuEPO）通過刺激紅細胞的產生，徹底改變了慢性腎病患者的貧血管理，從而大大減少了輸血的需要。但是，這種疾病人群中多達10％患者表現出促紅細胞生成素抗藥性。抗促紅細胞生成素的貧血患者在接受rHuEPO強化治療後仍需要輸血，這給他們帶來了額外的治療負擔和風險。而且，促紅細胞生成素抗藥性也與高死亡率有關。因此，學術和企業研究人員都在迫切尋找新的治療方案。 我們以前的研究表明，rHuEPO在增加血液中的紅細胞的同時，會耗盡骨髓紅系前體細胞，從而導致促紅細胞生成素抗藥性。因此，我們假設romiplostim（一种血小板生成素受體激動劑）與rHuEPO的組合可以治療抗促紅細胞生成素抗藥性貧血，因為romiplostim可以通過刺激早期紅系祖細胞的自我更新來減輕rHuEPO誘導的紅系前體細胞耗竭。另一方面，rHuEPO可能通過乾細胞競爭機制來阻止romiplostim誘導的血小板擴張，因為巨核細胞(血小板前體細胞)和紅系譜系具有共同的祖細胞。因此，在此項研究中，我們的目標是：1）確定rHuEPO和romiplostim單用和聯用在貧血慢性腎病大鼠動物模型中的促紅細胞生成和促血小板生成活性；2）通過基於機理的藥代動力學-藥效學數學模型分析來研究rHuEPO和romiplostim之間的藥效學相互作用；3）使用異速縮放和基於數學模型的模擬來預測最佳的人類給藥方案。 聯合用藥中romiplostim和rHuEPO最佳給藥方案將會刺激紅系細胞的連續擴增，同時避免血液中血小板的顯著增加。 通過證明組合療法在貧血慢性腎病大鼠中的安全性和有效性，該項目的結果將為臨床上進一步開發該策略治療促紅細胞生成素抗藥性貧血患者奠定關鍵基礎。因此，從長期來看，該項目可能為全球數百萬抗藥性貧血患者帶來新的治療方法，降低其死亡率並改善生活質量。該項目也可能有助於緩解香港面臨的嚴重血液供應短缺。

24103120.label: Realisation of objectives
24103120.value: In this project, we first conducted in vitro studies to evaluate the effects of recombinant human erythropoietin (rHuEPO) and thrombopoietin receptor agonist romiplostim on the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. The results indicated that romiplostim expands HSPCs and stimulates megakaryopoiesis simultaneously, while recombinant human erythropoietin (rHuEPO) drives the fate of HSPCs into the erythroid lineage. Based on these results, the monotherapy and combination therapy of rHuEPO and romiplostim in the anemic rats due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) were conducted to achieve objectives 1 and 2, and demonstrated that rHuEPO promotes red blood cell (RBC) production and inhibits platelet production, while romiplostim stimulates platelet production and synergizes with rHuEPO to promote RBC production. The results suggest that combination therapy of rHuEPO and romiplostim may hold promise for the treatment of EPO-resistant anemia. The series of in vitro and in vivo studies comprehensively elucidated the erythropoietic and thrombopoietic activity of romiplostim and rHuEPO, thus objective 1 and 2 were achieved completely. Based on the findings above and the data collected, a mechanism-based pharmacokinetic (PK)-pharmacodynamic (PD) model was established to dissect and quantify the interaction between rHuEPO and romiplostim. The modeling results revealed the interaction between romiplostim and rHuEPO on RBC and platelet production quantitatively. Therefore, the objective 3 was achieved completely. Finally, allometric scaling was performed to translate the PK-PD model from rats and humans. The scaled PD responses were compared with observed effects in humans for validation purposes. The translational mechanism-based PK/PD simulation was able to adequately describe the human RBCs and platelets following repeated IV or SC administration of rHuEPO and a single SC injection of romiplostim. These results provide confidence in the predictive power of the scaled PK/PD model in humans. The validated PK/PD model was subsequently utilized to predict the combination dosing regimen in humans and to support future clinical trials. Based on the simulation results, we recommend EPO 50 IU/kg thrice weekly + romiplostim 1 μg/kg once every 4 weeks from the second week for patients, considering the efficacy, compliance, and cost-effectiveness. In short, the objective 4 was achieved completely. In summary, the four objectives have been fully achieved through comprehensive in vitro, in vivo, and PK-PD modeling studies.

24103120.label: Major findings and research outcome
24103120.value: 1. We successfully established an in vitro culture system of rat hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). The flow cytometry analysis and colony forming unit assay results indicated that romiplostim expands HSPCs and stimulates megakaryopoiesis simultaneously, while recombinant human erythropoietin (rHuEPO) drives the fate of HSPCs into the erythroid lineage. 2. We further investigated the monotherapy and combination therapy of rHuEPO and romiplostim in the anemic rats due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and demonstrated that rHuEPO promotes red blood cell (RBC) production and inhibits platelet production, while romiplostim stimulates platelet production and synergizes with rHuEPO to promote RBC production. The results suggest that combination therapy of rHuEPO and romiplostim may hold promise for the treatment of EPO-resistant anemia. 3. Based on the findings above and the data collected, we established a mechanism-based pharmacokinetic (PK)-pharmacodynamic (PD) model to dissect and quantify the interaction between rHuEPO and romiplostim. The modeling results revealed that romiplostim stimulates platelet production primarily via the megakaryocyte (MK)-biased progenitor pathway. Additionally, the model indicated that the differentiation rate of HSPCs into erythroid is about six times greater than the differentiation rate into MK, and that this rate can increase up to 22-fold with the stimulation of rHuEPO. On the one hand, this explained why rHuEPO can deplete platelets to some extent through HSPCs competition. On the other hand, this shed light on the observation that romiplostim monotherapy has no significant effect on erythropoiesis, whereas combination therapy exhibits a synergistic effect on erythropoiesis, as the slight increase in HSPCs induced by romiplostim could be further stimulated and recruited by rHuEPO into the erythroid lineage to promote erythropoiesis. 4. Finally, we performed allometric scaling to translate the PK-PD model from rats and humans. The scaled PD responses were compared with observed effects in humans for validation purposes. The translational mechanism-based PK/PD simulation was able to adequately describe the human RBCs and platelets following repeated IV or SC administration of rHuEPO and a single SC injection of romiplostim. These results provide confidence in the predictive power of the scaled PK/PD model in humans. The validated PK/PD model was subsequently utilized to predict the combination dosing regimen in humans and to support future clinical trials. Based on the simulation results, we recommend EPO 50 IU/kg thrice weekly + romiplostim 1 μg/kg once every 4 weeks from the second week for patients, considering the efficacy, compliance, and cost-effectiveness.

24103120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24103120.value: Our series of preclinical investigations provided comprehensive in vivo and in vitro evidence for the use of a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA) and erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) combination therapy to treat ESA-resistant anemia. The underlying mechanism of action is that the TPO-RA stimulates the expansion of progenitors and thus corrects the EPO-induced precursor pool depletion, while rHuEPO drives the fate of HSPCs toward the erythroid lineage, thus reducing their MK lineage commitment and inhibiting platelet production. These findings build a solid foundation for a clinical study. Therefore, we propose to conduct a clinical trial to evaluate this combination therapy using romiplostim and an ESA (darbepoetin or Mircera) in ESA-resistant anemic patients. The likelihood of success of this innovative treatment is higher than previously proposed molecules because the specificity, safety, and efficacy of romiplostim have been demonstrated clinically.

24103120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24103120.value: Anemia is commonplace in patients with CKD. RHuEPO has revolutionized the management of anemia in patients with CKD by stimulating RBC production and thus dramatically reducing the need for blood transfusion. However, about 20% of these patients exhibit EPO resistance. EPO-resistant anemic patients require blood transfusion after intensive EPO treatment, which encumbers them with an additional treatment burden and associated risks. Moreover, EPO resistance is also associated with high mortality. Therefore, new treatment options are urgently needed and being pursued by both academic and industry researchers. In this project, we demonstrated that a combination of romiplostim, a TPO-RA, with rHuEPO holds promise for treating EPO-resistant anemia with safety and efficacy. The results of this project created a key foundation for the further development of this strategy clinically to treat EPO-resistant anemic patients. Therefore, this project in the long term may lead to a new treatment for millions of EPO-resistant anemic patients worldwide, reduce their mortality rate and improve their quality of life. This project may also help relieve the severe blood supply shortage Hong Kong faces.

24104920.value: 背景 抗菌素耐藥性(AMR)是指抗菌藥在治療感染方面變得無效。世界衞生組織已將生產廣譜β-內酰胺酶的腸桿菌科(ESBL-E)和生產碳青黴烯的腸桿菌科(CPE)視為迫切和嚴重的威脅，甚至將CPE列入研究和開發的優先名單。病人出院後帶菌(ESBL-E: 6.6月; CPE: 387天) 並在家居內傳播的潛力，突顯干預措施於遏制社區傳播的重要性。其中，越南附近的高CPE流行率(52％)預示其在香港社區的潛在流行性。 數學流行病學在ESBL-E及CPE方面的應用很少。至2016年，只有四個數學模型研究涉及這課題。很少文獻描述這兩種細菌在醫院和家居的傳播，而目前為止，只有一項研究利用模型研究家居傳播。因此，在量化ESBL-E和CPE在醫院和家居之間的傳播動力學方面仍有不少研究缺口。 目的及方法 這項目通過數學模型整合基因組和流行病學數據。其目的是: (一) 揭示ESBL-E和CPE在家居和醫院之間的傳播方式; (二) 評估減少它們傳播的干預措施的有效性。它包括:(一) 家居招募; 和 (二)數學模型。 家居招募：它建基於現有的隊列。研究組在18個月期間於五個時間點收集來自100個家居的所有成員的糞便樣本，以進行ESBL-E和CPE的篩選。對來自家居有ESBL-E的樣本，其相關性根據以下三點判斷: (一)細菌菌株; (二) ESBL基因; 和(三) 質體。對於來自家居有CPE的樣本，研究員會進行全基因組定序和Plasmidseeker來推斷傳播事件。此外，在研究期間，我們會詢問參加者相關資料(如: 求診狀況、抗生素使用、旅行等)。 數學模型：它勾勒家居和醫院之間的傳播途徑。家居研究的數據(如家居傳播的機會)為模型提供資料。我們會利用模型評估減少ESBL-E和CPE傳播的切實可行的干預措施的效用，如改善手部衞生水平。 預期結果 這項目支援感染控制政策以減少ESBL-E和CPE的傳播，並有這些科學和公共衞生價值: (一) 在少量科學依據下確立數學模型對控制ESBL-E 及CPE的貢獻; (二)指出ESBL-E和CPE在家居和醫院中傳播的關鍵因素; (三) 預測社區內ESBL-E和CPE的短/長期流行的趨勢; 和(四)量化減少CPE和ESBL-E傳播的干預措施的有效性。

24107020.value: 運用漸進視網膜神經纖維層趨勢圖所指引的降眼壓治療於治療高眼壓症之成本效益

24107020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24107020.value: The Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS) established the effectiveness of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering therapy in patients with ocular hypertension (OHT) by decreasing the risk of developing glaucoma – which is a leading cause of irreversible blindness, afflicting 21.8 million patients in China by 2020. However, the risk of glaucoma conversion was <10% in 5 years for untreated OHT patients and treating all OHT patients was considered not cost-effective. Some clinicians only treat the moderate to high-risk OHT patients (5-year risk >15%); the 5-year risk can be calculated by the OHTS-EGPS (European Glaucoma Prevention Study) prediction model. However, risk calculation can be highly volatile, rendering the discrimination of high-risk and low-risk OHT patients imprecise. Treating low-risk patients can lead to adverse effects that compromise visual function and quality of life. It will also incur unnecessary expenditure to the patients and the health-care system. We identified progressive retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thinning to be predictive of subsequent visual field (VF) progression and are conducting a 5-year multicentre study, randomising 310 OHT patients into two management paradigms with initiation of IOP-lowering treatment upon detection of (1) progressive RNFL thinning, as determined by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography Trend-based Progression Analysis (OCT TPA) of serial RNFL thickness maps (management paradigm I); or (2) a 5-year glaucoma conversion risk >15% calculated from the OHTS-EGPS prediction model (management paradigm II). All patients are followed-up 4-monthly for clinical examination, RNFL imaging and perimetry for 5 years. In the current proposal, we plan to compare the cost-effectiveness between the two management paradigms over the 5-year trial period and extrapolate the result for up to 20 years using a Markov model. We hypothesise that management paradigm I is more cost effective than management paradigm II. The findings of our study will not only inform health care policy makers about the most cost-effective management approach for OHT patients, but also improve the quality of life in OHT patients and enhance the rational re-allocation of resources within the healthcare system to those at most need. 高眼壓症治療研究(OHTS)發現高眼壓症的降壓治療有效減少青光眼症發生的機率。青光眼症是導致永久失明的主要疾病之一，在中國約有二千一百八十萬人患有青光眼。可是，以五年期基準預測，由於高眼壓症變成青光眼的風險少於10%，因此治療所有高眼壓病人並不合乎成本效益，部份臨床醫生只會治療中至高危的高眼壓症患者(5年風險高於15%)，5年風險由歐洲預防青光眼研究及高眼壓症治療研究(OHTS-EGPS)計算模式得出。但需要留意，風險計算是可以非常浮動的，病人實際上屬於高或低風險難於準確估算。治療低風險病人可得出反效果，例如令視覺功能受損及令他們的生活質素下降，亦令病人及醫療系統的成本增加。我們以視網膜神經纖維層(RNFL)變薄及視野圖(VF)的傳變為預測因子，進行一個為期5年的多地點研究，310個高眼壓症病人將會以隨機照對方式分成兩組，在以下測試下開始進行降眼理療程: (1)由OCT TPA的漸進視網膜神經纖維層趨勢圖得出的視網膜神經纖維層逐漸變薄(範式1)，或(2) 根據OHTS-EGPS預測模型（範式II）計算得出的5年青光眼病發風險高於15%，所有患者每4個月進行一次隨訪，以進行臨床檢查，視網膜神經纖維層(RNFL)檢查和視野(VF)檢查，為期5年。在目前的計劃中，我們計劃在5年的研究期內比較兩種範式的成本效益，並使用Markov模型作20年的推算。我們假設範式I比範式II更具成本效益，我們的研究的結果不僅使醫療保健決策者更了解高眼壓症患者最經濟有效的治療方法，而且改善高眼壓症患者的生活質素，與此同時增強醫療系統中對最需要的人的合理的資源再分配。

24108520.label: Project Objectives
24108520.value: To estimate the sex-specific heritability of ASD by using population-based family data. Hypothesis: we hypothesize males’ heritability, or more specifically, the genetic variance of male is larger than females’. Such findings will confirm the theory of higher genetic susceptibility in male. If the opposite is true, heritability is greater in females than males, female protective effect might be the explanatory factor to the sex-differences in ASD. To examine if aunt(s)/uncle(s)’ diagnosis of ASD is associated with the index child's ASD risk, and whether this risk differs between an aunt and a uncle being ASD diagnosed. Hypothesis: assuming the theory of higher threshold of genetic liability among female is true, we would expect higher risk in male offspring with an aunt diagnosed with ASD than an uncle diagnosed with ASD, since affected females have a higher genetic loading, therefore their relatives would likely also have greater genetic risk. To examine if aunt(s)/uncle(s)’ diagnosis of other non-ASD psychiatric disorders is associated with the index child's ASD risk, and whether this risk differs between an aunt and a uncle being diagnosed of non-ASD psychiatric disorders. Hypothesis: As literatures have shown, ASD shares a common genetic origin with other psychiatric disorders. Extending our hypothesis in objective 2, the ASD risk is expected to be higher in offspring with an aunt diagnosed with these psychiatric disorders than an uncle diagnosed with these psychiatric disorders.

24108520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24108520.value: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable which affects more males than females. How this observed sex-differences in ASD prevalence relates to the etiology of ASD has been widely discussed. In ASD genetics, two main theories have been suggested: 1) higher genetic susceptibility in males, and 2) female protective effect (FPE). The first theory predicts that more males than females show a higher number of autistic features as a result of higher genetic susceptibility of common genetic variants, whereas females will develop ASD due to additional factors. Example of such factors are de novo mutations and enriched copy-number variations with different penetrance rate between sexes. The classical twins study can test this theory by estimating sex-specific heritability. But due to limited sample size, previous twin studies suffer in statistical power to make any meaningful precision of the estimated heritability. The key concepts of the second theory, FPE, hypothesize that a higher threshold of genetic liability is required for females to reach an affected status than male. To test this multiplex families with ASD are needed, allowing us to ask questions like, do male siblings of affected females are more likely to develop ASD than male siblings of affected males, since an affected female presumably has more genetic risk factors. However, individuals with ASD might have harder to find a partner, and as a consequence less likely to have children. Our proposed study design will overcome this hurdle by studying the RECURRENCE RELATIVE RISK in aunt and uncle of the index children’s. Furthermore, this approach has the advantage of being robust against some aspects of stoppage, the phenomena that parents tend to stop having children after birth of an affected child. We will also estimate the CONCURRENCE RELATIVE RISK, of other psychiatric disorders, in aunt and uncle of the index children’s to further explore sex-differential etiology of ASD. In this proposal, we will estimate SEX-SPECIFIC HERITABILITY by using a multi-linkage Swedish database, which uses the Swedish personal number as the unique link, to construct informative family pedigrees tree, thus overcome the sample size issue in twin studies. The data will consist all born children between 1997-2015 in Sweden and their relatives. The sample data will comprise ~2 million children, more than 15,000 children diagnosed with ASD and 270,000 family pedigree trees. 自閉症譜系障礙（ASD）是一種遺傳度很高的疾病，其患病的男性多於女性。這種普遍存在的性別差異與ASD的病因和遺傳傾向之間的關聯機制，曾被廣泛討論和研究。遺傳學中，學者主要提出了兩種遺傳傾向閾值的理論：1）男性的高遺傳變異性理論 2）多因素性別差異傾向理論。 第一種理論假設男性擁有更大的遺傳變異性，因此男性會比女性會表現出更多的自閉症特徵，而女性最主要是受到遺傳變異性以外的其他因素影響而患上自閉症。有研究表明新生突變（de novo mutations）和拷貝數變異（CNVs）在不同性別之間的滲透率不同，而這一研究结果支持了這種理論。若使用傳統的傾向閾值模型，可以通過估計特定性別的遺傳度（例如通過比較性別之間的遺傳變異性）來直接驗證該理論。但是由於過去的研究只基於雙胞胎的實驗設計，導致統計功效的不足，無法得到有效精度下的遺傳度估計。 第二種理論的核心假設之一是女性保護作用（FPE）。 一種假說是，在患病閾值不變的條件下，女性保護作用會將遺傳傾向分佈向遠離閾值的方向移動。另一種假說是，在遺傳傾向分佈不變的條件下，由於女性保護作用，女性要達到患病狀態，需要比男性更高的閾值。為了測試這一理論，具有復合結構的患者家庭的信息是必須的，例如，女性患者家庭裡的男性患者，比起沒有女性患者的家庭的男性患者，會攜帶更高的ASD風險。作為第二種理論的擴展，檢驗那些與ASD具有共同遺傳病因的疾病的並發效應的研究，也將進一步推動探索性別差異病因結構的研究進程。目前，尚無關於ASD患者家庭中第二代復發/並發率的數據。 由於ASD的病因在很大程度上是由遺傳因子決定的（包括影响較小的常見變異和一些稀有遺傳標記），GWAS僅能提供有限的信息。因此，只有很少的數據源可以可靠地解決上述研究空白。在這項研究提案中，我們將使用瑞典的多代鏈接數據庫來估計特定性別的遺傳度，該數據庫使用瑞典公民的身份證號碼作為唯一鏈接。數據包含1997年至2015年期間瑞典所有的出生兒童，其父母和祖父母（用以識別其姑姑/叔叔）。樣本數據包括約200萬兒童，被診斷患有ASD的15,000多名兒童和270,000多戶家庭的家譜樹。本研究將會致力於探索ASD的複發率情況以及與ASD相關的疾病的並發率情況。

24108820.label: Project Objectives
24108820.value: To investigate the role of SH3P2 in mitochondrial dynamics and turnover. Maintenance of mitochondrial function for energy supply is largely dependent upon mitochondrial dynamics (e.g., fission or fusion) and turnover, yet the regulation mechanism for mitochondria turnover in plants is largely unclear. Our preliminary results suggest SH3P2 might function in regulating mitochondria turnover. To demonstrate a possible role of SH3P2 in mitochondrial dynamics and turnover, here we will first dissect the dynamic association between SH3P2 and mitochondria in real time using high-resolution imaging under different conditions/tissues; then we will examine the dynamics and morphological defects at ultra structural level with 3D information in sh3p2 mutant background. To characterize the molecular link between SH3P2 and mitochondria. To understand how SH3P2 is recruited to the mitochondria for its function in mitochondrial dynamics or turnover, here we will use pull down/screening methods to identify the mitochondria-related SH3P2 complex; then we will use recruitment, Co-IP, FRET and Y2H assays to confirm their relationship with SH3P2. On other hand, will screen the mutant plants for the identified mitochondrial-related proteins and use a combination of cellular, biochemical and genetic approaches to analyze the association among SH3P2, mitochondria and autophagosomes in the screened mitochondrial mutant plants.
