24108820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24108820.value: Regulation of energy homeostasis represents a major fundamental knowledge gap and an opportunity for discoveries in plant translational research. Macroautophagy (hereafter as Autophagy), has been shown to participate in various fundamental processes for the turnover of nutrient and energy to balance cell growth and development. A double-membrane structure named an autophagosome sequesters cargos and delivers them into the vacuole for degradation and recycling. Although the core AuTophaGy-related (ATG) proteins for autophagosome biogenesis are highly conserved in the plant genome, plants have evolved novel mechanisms to regulate autophagy. Using advanced tools including 3D tomography and real-time imaging analysis, we have unveiled a unique role for plant ATG9 in autophagosome formation from the endoplasmic reticulum. A previous study from our laboratory has identified a novel regulator named SH3P2 (SH3-domain protein 2), which functions in autophagosome formation via interaction with ATG8 and the PI3K complex. In another study, we found that SH3P2 directly interacts with a plant-unique endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) component, likely to serve as a link for the crosstalk between the endosomal and autophagic machineries. In addition, SH3P2 has been shown to be associated with clathrin coated vesicle components, suggesting multiple functions of SH3P2 in plant cells. Most selective autophagy for organelle degradation is mediated by an interaction between ATG8 and a receptor/adaptor. Recently, an essential role for autophagy in mitochondrial degradation (mitophagy) has been reported in plant-specific developmental processes (e.g. seed germination and pollen growth). However, little is known about how selectivity is achieved to maintain energy homeostasis. As a new PI since 2018, by supervising a PhD student and a RA, I have been able to develop independent research to generate useful materials and exciting preliminary data to support a possible role of SH3P2 in linking autophagy and mitochondria: 1) under normal conditions, SH3P2 is partially associated with the mitochondria; 2) upon stress treatment, mitochondria are sequestered by SH3P2-positive ring-like structures; 3) a SH3P2 mutant is dominant for the mitochondria; 4) SH3P2 has a direct interaction with ATG8. Therefore, we hypothesize that the mitochondria-localized SH3P2 might function in mitochondrial dynamics or mitophagy as an adaptor/receptor. 24108820.label: Realisation of objectives
24108820.value: Objective 1 : To investigate the role of SH3P2 in mitochondrial dynamics and turnover 1.1 SH3P2 functions as an autophagic adaptor via atypical interaction mode for interaction with the autophagosome marker ATG8. To understand the possible mechanism of SH3P2 as an autophagic adaptor in mitochondria turnover, we have firstly explored the interaction mechanism between SH3P2 and the autophagosome marker ATG8f protein. By solving the ATG8 protein structure in Arabidopsis thaliana, we uncovered an atypical interaction model between SH3P2 and ATG8f. Among the three SH3-domain-containing proteins (SH3P1, SH3P2, SH3P3) in Arabidopsis, analysis revealed that ATG8 only interacts specifically with SH3P2 dependent on a unique interface. In addition, the amount of receptor proteins NBR1 also competes the interaction affinity between ATG8 and SH3P2. This study thus provides a basis for SH3P2 as a possible adaptor in linking ATG8 proteins to balance autophagosome formation and selective autophagy. 1.2 SH3P2 participates in mitophagy and mitochondria fission process. We have used the SH3P2-GFP/Mito-mCherry transgenic plants to dissect the dynamic association between SH3P2 and mitochondria in real-time, showing SH3P2 might involve in both mitophagy and mitochondria fission events under different conditions. Objective 2 : To characterize the molecular link between SH3P2 and mitochondria. 2.1. Identification of the molecular link between SH3P2 and mitochondria: By comparing the interactome of SH3P2 and SH3P2m using mass spectrometry analysis, we have identified several mitochondria fission regulators enriched in SH3P2m interactomes, including ELM1, DRP3B. We have carried out interaction analysis including GFP-Trap Co-Immunoprecipitation(Co-Ip) and Yeast-two-hybrid (Y2H) assays. Our data showed that SH3P2 indeed is associated with ELM1 and DRP3A/B using co-IP and BiFC assays. 2.2 Loss-of-function studies: We have screened and obtained the T-DNA insertional mutants for the above candidates, including elm1, drp3a-1 and drp3b-1. We have gerneated SH3P2-GFP fusion proteins into these mutants to analyze their roles for SH3P2 to participate in mitochondrial dynamics. Surprisingly, SH3P2-GFP were detected on tubular structures in elm1 mutant, while SH3P2-GFP labeled large structures were observed in drp3a-1 mutant. When using MitoTracker to label mitochondria, we found that most of SH3P2-GFP were overlapped with MitoTracker in elm1 or drp3a-1 mutant, indicating SH3P2 is recruited to mitochondria. These results also suggest that deletion of ELM1 and DRP3A blocked the subsequent disassociation of SH3P2 from mitochondria, raising a possibility that ELM1 and DRP3A might function downstream of SH3P2 in mitochondria turnover. 2.3 Malfunction of mitochondria fission activity compromises efficient piecemeal of heat-induced mitophagy. Mitochondrial fission has long been suggested to promote mitophagy, but experimental evidence is lacking in plants. We have successfully generated double transgenic plants expressing YFP-ATG8e and mitochondria matrix protein IDH-mRuby in WT or elm1drp3a mutant to further access the mitophagic activity at the cell level. By subcellular analysis, we found that the mitochondria structures labeled by IDH-mCherry were sequestered by YFP-ATG8e in the wild type background upon heat stress. However, cluster of large mitochondria were partially enclosed by cup-like structures. Unexpectedly, they were finally sealed upon fusion with additional ATG8-positive punctate structure, likely due to delay in mitophagosome formation. Interestingly, the canonical selective autophagy receptor NBR1 participates in targeting these large mitochondria, as NBR1 proteins were accumulated on these large mitochondria and overlapped with YFP-ATG8e. 2.4. Spatial morphological analysis revealed piecemeal mitophagy for fission defective mitochondria. Damaged mitochondria have been suggested to be degraded via asymmetric fission to form two daughter mitochondria with distinct membrane potentials. Using 3D electron tomography analysis, we further illustrated the morphological features of the abnormal mitochondria as well as their spatial relationship with the phagophore for piecemeal degradation of mitochondria. These results provide strong evidence in supporting piecemeal mitophagy operates in plant cells for efficient mitochondria turnover.

24108820.label: Major findings and research outcome
24108820.value: 1. We have demonstrated that SH3P2 functions as an autophagic adaptor via atypical interaction mode for interaction with the autophagosome marker ATG8. This study thus provides a basis for SH3P2 as a possible adaptor in linking ATG8 proteins to balance autophagosome formation and selective autophagy. This result has been published in Autophagy in 2022（https://doi.org/10.1080/15548627.2021.1976965) as attached in Part C. 1.2 Updated reviews on plant mitochondrial homeostasis and mitophagy. Mitochondrial homeostasis refers to the balance of mitochondrial number and quality in a cell. It is maintained by mitochondrial biogenesis, mitochondrial fusion/fission, and the clearance of unwanted/damaged mitochondria. Mitophagy represents a selective form of autophagy by sequestration of the potentially harmful mitochondrial materials into a double-membrane autophagosome, thus preventing the release of death inducers, which can trigger programmed cell death (PCD). Recent advances have also unveiled a close interconnection between mitophagy and mitochondrial dynamics, as well as PCD in both mammalian and plant cells. We have summarized and discussed recent findings on the interplay between mitophagy and mitochondrial dynamics in plants, yeast and animals, with a focus on the molecular evidence for mitophagy crosstalk with mitochondrial dynamics and PCD. These updates been published on International Journal of Molecular Science in 2021 (doi: 10.3390/ijms22031236) and The Plant Cell in 2024 (doi: 10.1093/plcell/koae099) as attached in Part C. 2. We have illustrated that SH3P2 participates in both mitophagy and mitochondria fission process via forming a complex with the mitochondria fission factors, ELM1 and DRP3. Overaccumulation of SH3P2 on mitochondria leads to abnormal large mitochondria, while malfunction of mitochondria fission activity compromises efficient turnover of heat-induced mitophagy. These results suggest that a balance in mitochondria fission activity is essential to maintain mitochondria homeostasis. The manuscript is under preparation for submission as attached in Part C.

24108820.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24108820.value: We have also observed that portion of SH3P2 is translocated into the mitochondria. This unexpected result indicates that SH3P2 might play additional roles within mitochondria, likely by cooperating with other mitochondrial proteins to remodel intermitochondrial architecture. It is worthwhile to further explore the SH3P2 interaction network in mitochondria and their impacts on mitochondria morphology in multi-scale level. In addition, further investigations on SH3P2-ELM1-DRP3 complex at the structure level will provide novel insights into the regulatory mechanism of mitochondria fission process. Last but not least, what type of postmodifications for activation/deactivation of SH3P2 on mitochondria is another direction that deserve further investigations.

24108820.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24108820.value: In this study, we identifies an unrecognized role of SH3P2 on mitochondria to function together with the mitochondria fission machinery ELM1 and DRP3. Our results demonstrated that mitochondria fission activity is essential for both basal mitophagy and stress-induced mitophagy, which is supported by the abnormal accumulation of large unclosed mitophagosome in the fission deficient mutants. Moreover, we illustrated mitochondria fission machinery cooperates with the canonical selective autophagy receptor NBR1 for piecemeal mitophagy in plants. Our study reveals piecemeal mitophagy as an adaptive mechanism that can be leveraged to remove dysfunctional mitochondria in plant cells to cope with various stress conditions.

24117220.value: 剝奪性弱視是一種主要由單側先天性白內障引起的視力發育障礙。患眼視力模糊對初級視皮層（V1）回路的發育有不利影響。現時弱視的治療策略只對8歲或8歲以前的兒童有效，從那時起，由於經驗依賴性突觸可塑性在發育過程中顯著降低，有效治療急劇下降。雙目視覺V1皮層神經元的功能性反應變得不成比例地偏向於來自未受影響眼睛的輸入，從而導致視力的永久性損害。因此，進一步加深對視突觸可塑性的認識和開發新的治療方法具有重要意義。為了進一步闡明視覺突觸可塑性的機制，我們建議用單眼剝奪作為剝奪性弱視研究的實驗模型，該模型由單眼短閉導致V1神經元輸入不平衡。在小鼠中，一個半球（即左半球）的V1接收來自對側（即右眼）的主要輸入，而來自同側（即左眼）的相對較弱的輸入。在視覺發育的關鍵時期，MD導致眼優勢(ocular dominance)可塑性（視皮層可塑性的一種），剝奪（閉眼）眼的神經元反應减弱，而非剝奪（睜眼）眼的反應增强。已有研究表明，MD可在臨界期誘導樹突狀棘重構，導致V1神經元反應的功能可塑性。然而，樹突棘重塑的機制、棘的功能特性被消除以及MD誘發的脊柱强化或形成的分子機制尚不清楚。通過採用體內成像、分子突觸標記和可塑性範式等前沿技術，我們將：1）描述一種新的突觸機制，稱為合作突觸可塑性；2）研究這種可塑性的分子機制；3）揭示協同突觸可塑性的潜在機制在體內及其在齧齒類動物OD可塑性中的作用。我們假設協同突觸可塑性對於實現突觸特异性减弱和隨後在樹突內的强化都是至關重要的。其首要目標是為理解健康和疾病背景下突觸可塑性的機制提供關鍵資訊，並最終為治療視皮層發育障礙的治療策略提供見解。

24117220.label: Realisation of objectives
24117220.value: Neuronal circuits in the human brain are plastic and undergo experience-driven modifications, enabling neurons to adapt their functional connectivity and responses. Each neuron integrates inputs from numerous sources to generate appropriate outputs. This plasticity refers to the neuron’s ability to reorganize its synaptic connections and functions in response to changes in sensory experience or learning. It is a leading theory underlying brain functions such as learning and memory. Synapses can undergo dynamic changes through synaptic plasticity, which supports essential cognitive processes. Importantly, dysregulated synaptic plasticity is recognized as a key contributor to various neurodevelopmental disorders. Visual cortical plasticity serves as a powerful model for studying how visual activity shapes and modifies cortical circuits. Here, we investigated key regulatory mechanisms of cortical visual plasticity. We employed a cranial window and a procedure suitable for time-lapse in vivo two-photon microscopy of the mouse visual cortex. A cranial window that allows repeated optical access to cortical areas is essential for longitudinal studies. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, installation of the two-photon laser imaging system was delayed by eight months. Soon after installation, we successfully established the in vivo experimental setup required for the project. Our protocol involves an open-skull cranial window in which a small portion of the mouse skull is replaced with a glass coverslip. Sparse expression of GCaMP6s-mRuby2 was achieved via electroporation or viral injection. For viral injection, the visual cortex (V1) was injected with AAV-GCaMp6s-mRuby2 and AAV-Cre. The Cre virus titer was diluted at a 1:50,000 ratio with the other virus to achieve sparse yet strong expression. Transcranial two-photon time-lapse imaging was used to measure both spontaneous calcium signaling (frequency, duration, and amplitude under basal conditions) and responses of V1 neurons to oriented gratings of specific spatial and temporal frequencies during the critical period. We observed substantial dendritic spine turnover and eye-specific remapping of visual responses throughout the critical period. Spine retention was closely associated with calcium activity, particularly when activated by the soma’s preferred visual stimulus. Additionally, following development, spine responses showed increased correlation with those of neighboring spines. We also established a method for analyzing calcium imaging and performing spike inference, based on a U-Net deep neural network optimized for spike-rate and spike-event predictions from raw calcium inputs. Furthermore, we successfully implemented a novel super-resolution method, epitope-preserving magnified analysis of the proteome (eMAP), to visualize dendritic structure and molecules involved in visual plasticity signaling pathways. To study dendritic and molecular mechanisms of cortical visual plasticity, we induced ocular dominance plasticity through brief eyelid closure of one eye (monocular deprivation, MD), which unbalances inputs from the two eyes to V1 neurons. To visualize dendritic spines, we injected AAV-hSyn-DIO-EGFP (structural marker) and AAV-CaMKIIa-Cre virus to sparsely label neurons and quantified spine morphology in layer 2/3 V1 neurons from mice subjected to no MD, 3-day MD, or 7-day MD. For more detailed structural analysis than traditional confocal imaging allows, we expanded tissue samples using eMAP. Dendritic spines were classified into four morphological categories: mushroom, stubby, thin, and filopodia. After 3-day MD, we found a significant decrease in the density and proportion of mature mushroom spines compared to the no-MD condition. After 7-day MD, mature spine density and proportion remained lower, while the density of immature spines increased significantly. To identify novel molecular regulators underlying the dendritic alterations in cortical visual plasticity, we examined transcriptomic profiles after 3-day MD. We normalized RNA expression in the hemisphere contralateral to the deprived eye—where most synaptic drive changes occur—to expression in the ipsilateral hemisphere, which receives less input from the deprived eye and shows fewer gene expression changes. We identified 1,173 differentially expressed mRNAs, with more downregulated (701) than upregulated (472). Downregulated mRNAs during MD included immediate early genes Bdnf and Nptx2. We also examined long non-coding RNAs, including circular RNAs (circRNAs), and detected 1,489 unique circRNAs, 73 of which were differentially expressed. Interestingly, linear isoforms of circHomer1, circPrkce, and circDcun1d4 changed in the opposite direction compared to their circular counterparts, suggesting their circRNA expression is regulated independently of overall gene transcription. Using shRNA, we further validated that circHomer1 plays a crucial role in initiating ocular dominance plasticity. One novel regulator of cortical visual plasticity we identified is cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5). X-linked mutations in the CDKL5 gene cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by global developmental delay, motor dysfunction, early-onset epilepsy, learning disabilities, and autistic features. A distinct clinical feature of CDD is cortical visual impairment, affecting at least 75% of patients. CDKL5 is a serine/threonine kinase with several known substrates, yet how its deficits lead to circuit-specific visual processing impairment remains unclear. We established a sensory deficit model in knockout mice and used in vivo two-photon calcium imaging to examine how impaired neuronal activity in V1 leads to functional deficits in developmental plasticity. We observed reduced orientation selectivity in V1 neurons of CDKL5 knockout mice, along with impaired binocular matching—an important feature for visual processing. Using eMAP, we characterized dendritic alterations of synaptic molecules and found that CDKL5-depleted V1 neurons exhibited reduced dendritic spine density and fewer mature mushroom spines, indicating impaired spine development and developmental plasticity in the visual cortex. Mechanistically, a proteomics screen identified a novel CDKL5 substrate that regulates mRNA expression. Overall, our study identifies important and novel regulatory mechanisms in cortical visual plasticity and sheds light on potential therapeutic strategies for neurodevelopmental disorders.

24117220.label: Major findings and research outcome
24117220.value: Neuronal plasticity is a series of tightly controlled events. However, the molecular mechanisms and the coordinated reorganization of dendritic spines remain unclear. Here, we investigated key regulatory mechanisms of cortical visual plasticity. We employed in vivo two-photon microscopy of the mouse visual cortex to study the functional alterations of visual cortical neurons during development and plasticity. We have established a method to analyze calcium imaging and perform spike inference. This system, named ENS2 (effective and efficient neural networks for spike inference from calcium signals), is based on U-Net deep neural network and optimized for spike-rate and spike-event predictions using raw calcium inputs (Zhou et al., 2023). Optimizing the ENS2 system for spike-event prediction would produce a versatile inference system that benefits diverse neuroscience studies. We also observed substantial spine turnover and eye-specific reorganization of visual responses throughout development. These findings highlight the profound synaptic dynamics and underlying synaptic mechanisms that support developmental plasticity within visual cortical neurons (Tsimring et al., 2025). Combining with transcriptomics technology, we have identified more than twenty novel regulators of synaptic structure and surface receptor that regulates synaptic strengths during ocular dominance plasticity. These include both protein-encoding transcripts and long non-coding RNAs. We had characterized the functional roles of these novel regulators in visual cortical plasticity. One of the novel non-coding RNA we identified is named circHomer1. Using specific knockdown approached, we further demonstrated that circHomer1 mediates the initiation of ocular dominance plasticity (Jenks et al.,2025). With our experience and observations, we contributed to a review discussing dendritic mechanisms during experience-dependent plasticity (Jenks et al., 2021). Another regulator of cortical visual plasticity we identified is cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5). We established a sensory deficit model in knockout mice and used in vivo two-photon calcium imaging to examine how impaired neuronal activity in V1 leads to functional deficits in developmental plasticity. Mechanistically, we identified a novel CDKL5 substrate that regulates mRNA expression. The findings are reported in the manuscript authored by Yuan et al., which is under preparation (see attached).

24117220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24117220.value: This project elucidates the molecular and dendritic changes underlying visual synaptic plasticity and identifies novel regulators of this process. In particular, we have identified circHomer1 as a key regulator of dendritic spine morphogenesis during cortical visual plasticity. However, the mechanism by which circHomer1 exerts its regulatory effects remains unclear. This could be explored by identifying its potential binding partners and investigating its molecular functions using pull down assays. Additionally, as a future direction, a molecular probe for circHomer1 tagged with a fluorescent signal could be designed to visualize its trafficking in dendrites using in vivo two-photon microscopy. This would provide insight into its subcellular localization following plasticity induction in the visual cortex. Another key question for future studies is whether the dendritic and molecular mechanisms identified in visual cortical plasticity are conserved and applicable to learning and memory in other cortical regions, such as the prefrontal cortex or hippocampus. This could be investigated by designing learning and memory tasks and examining the associated dendritic and molecular changes.

24117220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24117220.value: Our brain circuits can change through experience, a process known as plasticity, which is crucial for learning, memory, and how we process what we see. This study investigates the experience-dependent synaptic plasticity within the mammalian visual cortex. Utilizing in vivo two-photon calcium imaging and a super-resolution imaging method, named eMAP, we characterized the dynamic remodeling of dendritic spines during the critical period of visual development in a mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis following monocular deprivation identified differentially expressed coding and non-coding RNAs, including circular RNAs. We validated circHomer1 as a novel regulator important for initiating ocular dominance plasticity. Furthermore, we examined the role of the serine/threonine kinase CDKL5, mutations of which cause a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with prominent cortical visual impairment. CDKL5 knockout resulted in altered orientation selectivity and deficits in dendritic spine maturation within the visual cortex. A proteomic screen identified a novel CDKL5 substrate involved in mRNA regulation. Collectively, this work delineates key molecular and synaptic mechanisms governing cortical plasticity and provides a mechanistic framework linking dysregulated plasticity to neurodevelopmental pathology.

24118220.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24118220.value: 闡明導致人類心臟再生能力下降的調節網絡和機制因素

24118220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24118220.value: 摘要 背景 與低等脊椎動物（如魚類和兩棲動物）的器官不同，成年哺乳動物，包括人類的許多器官無法自我修復，進而無法再生。在人類中，器官的無法再生會導致與年齡相關的器官衰竭，在患病或受傷的情況下這種衰竭甚至可能會加速。哺乳動物的器官之所以不能再生，很大程度上是由於構成器官的特定細胞類型（如心臟細胞和腦細胞）無法分裂/再生。也就是說，它們都是終末分化細胞。至於哺乳動物的細胞是如何變為終末分化的，目前為止我們知之甚少。理解細胞是如何變為終末分化的，將有助我們思考出對策來誘導其恢復到非終末分化（a non-terminally differentiated）的狀態（也就是我們在魚類或者兩棲動物的特定細胞中看到的那樣），以達到讓人類器官能夠再生與修復的目的。 具體重點 心臟衰竭是由心臟無法有效地抽血以滿足身體需求導致的。心臟衰竭是工業化國家的主要死亡誘因。此外，這種疾病在診斷後 5 年的生存率為 50％ - 與許多癌症相仿甚至更糟。心臟衰竭的原因之一是心臟病發作，導致被稱為心臟心肌細胞這一心臟專門收縮細胞的死亡。如前所述，與魚類或者兩棲動物的心肌細胞不同，哺乳動物/人類的心肌細胞為終末分化，導致心臟在受傷後無法再生。能夠誘導哺乳動物的心肌細胞逆轉其終末分化狀態並再次分裂/再生代表了一種再生患病心臟和治癒心臟衰竭的治療策略。然而，迄今為止，哺乳動物心肌細胞如何進行終末分化仍是未知的。 一種新的策略 類似於人類的器官（organs），細胞具有細胞器（organelles）。中心體是細胞分裂/再生所需的細胞器。魚類和兩棲動物的非終末分化心肌細胞都具有中心體，因而可以分裂/再生。相反，哺乳動物的終末分化心肌細胞沒有中心體。因此，中心體代表了一種新型的「生物標記」，可以預測心肌細胞的再生潛力。然而，缺少中心體是否一定是哺乳動物心肌細胞不可分裂和再生的直接原因還不得而知，有待進一步研究。 我的研究目標就是理解心肌細胞如何進行終末分化，並著重於中心體的生物特性，以期找到人類再生心臟的方法。

24201020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24201020.value: Exosomal microRNA-based liquid biopsies have shown great potential in early detection of cancers with a minimally invasive assay. Exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) can be measured using polymerase chain reaction-based testing, or RNA sequencing techniques. These sophisticated tests are time-consuming, costly, complicated, and often associated with biological interference that may disturb the detection sensitivity and specificity. There is a clinically unmet need for rapid and sensitive detection of low-abundance exosomal miRNA biomarkers in body fluids associated with early-stage cancers. Graphene-enabled field-effect biosensors are a promising tool for low-level detection of nucleic acids, offering the prospects of simple, multiplexed, and label-free testing, with high accuracy and selectivity. However, the absence of a bandgap in monolayer graphene and binding-affinity-dependent limit of detection hinder further improvements that could be made to its performance of low-level exosomal miRNA detection in early-stage cancer diagnosis. The objective of our proposed research is to develop a sensitive and rapid bioelectronic platform for the detection of exosomal miRNA biomarkers in early-stage colorectal cancer diagnosis, by using bilayer graphene (BLG) with a tunable bandgap. First, we will develop the capability to grow large-area BLG with controlled stacking order and layer numbers by chemical vapor deposition, based on which we will produce arrays of high-quality BLG field-effect-transistor (BLGFET) biosensors. Second, we will design and develop an exponential target recycling and hybridization chain reaction (TRHCR) that can operate on BLGFET biosensors for rapid detection of exosomal miRNAs in a clinically relevant range. The BLGFET devices will be further examined against complex human samples to validate the effectiveness of the exponential TRHCR scheme in a realistic clinical setting. Compared to the existing reports based on monolayer GFET, our BLGFET biosensors, coupled with exponential TRHCR, will lead to a substantial improvement in detection sensitivity and sensing time. This will be achieved through the use of BLG that has a bandgap and sensing signals that are exponentially amplified, making it exceptionally ideal for use in exosomal miRNA detection in early-stage cancer diagnosis. Project success will facilitate low-level exosomal miRNA detection with the prospect of multiplexed and label-free detection, bringing the limit-of-detection to a range, i.e., aM level, that could prove useful in the early-stage diagnosis of colorectal cancers and many other diseases. 基於外泌體微核糖核酸(microRNAs)的液體活檢在腫瘤疾病早期非侵入式診斷方面有著巨大的應用前景。外泌體 microRNAs可通過聚合酶鏈式反應（PCR）或核酸測序等技術進行檢測，但是現有檢測技術耗時、昂貴、繁複，且易受其他生物幹擾因素的影響，從而降低了檢測的靈敏度和特異性，無法滿足快速檢測體液中低濃度核酸生物標誌物的臨床迫切需求。石墨烯場效應生物傳感器是近年发展起來的有廣泛應用前景的高精度、高特異核酸檢測技術，具有簡單、無標記和多重並行檢測等顯著特點。但是，由於單層石墨烯沒有帶隙， 其基於結合親和力的檢測限阻礙了該技術在早期癌癥診斷中對低濃度外泌體microRNAs檢測性能的提升。 本研究旨在構建基於具有可調帶隙的雙層石墨烯（BLG）的生物電子平台，實現早期結直腸癌中外泌體microRNAs生物標誌物快速靈敏檢測。首先，我們擬采用化學氣相沈積法實現大面積雙層石墨烯的可控合成，製備高質量的雙層石墨烯的場效應生物傳感器陣列。進一步，我們將設計開發可在雙層石墨烯生物傳感器上進行的指數擴增雜交鏈式反應， 實現快速靈敏檢測腫瘤外泌體microRNAs。最後，我們將利用人體樣本對指數擴增雜交鏈式反應的檢測性能進行驗證。相比於目前的單層石墨烯，我們所開發的基於指數擴增雜交鏈式反應的雙層石墨烯生物傳感器，可顯著提升檢測靈敏度，並且大幅度縮短檢測時間。具有帶隙的雙層石墨烯以及被指數增強的信號，使該技術在早期癌癥診斷中用於外泌體microRNAs檢測具有其獨特優勢。該項目的完成將促進人體體液樣本中低濃度外泌體microRNAs檢測的發展，所開發的雙層石墨烯檢測平臺具有多重和無標記檢測的特點，檢測限可達aM水平，可在結直腸癌乃至其他重大疾病的早期診斷上發揮作用 。

24201020.label: Realisation of objectives
24201020.value: We have achieved the proposed objectives, with our project resulting in the publication of 15 peer-reviewed journal articles, the awarding of two Ph.D. degrees supported by this grant, and significant advancements contributing to the broader field of biomolecular sensing. First, we conducted a thorough investigation into the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of large-area bilayer and monolayer graphene. By depositing a Ni thin film (100 nm to 500 nm) onto Cu foils (25 um thick) to create a Cu-Ni alloy substrate, we leveraged the back-diffusion growth mechanism with optimized parameters. This enabled the synthesis of highly crystalline bilayer graphene with domain sizes reaching approximately 100 um, marking a significant milestone in scalable 2D material production. We refined the controlled CVD growth process for monolayer graphene, achieving high-purity (negligible multilayer flakes), continuous sheets with tunable grain sizes. These graphene materials, characterized by their high crystallinity, served as critical elements for fabricating high-performance biosensors. Using these high-quality graphene materials, we fabricated graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) through a scalable and reproducible photolithography process using a bilayer photoresist approach. The resulting GFETs demonstrated high carrier mobilities averaging 2610 cm^2/Vs, and excellent reproducibility. Using these GFETs, we fabricated aptasensors capable of highly sensitive arsenite detection and demonstrated the versatility of our platform by applying it to environmental monitoring. Detailed in PART C: Research Output #11, this work underscored both the scalability of our fabrication techniques and the adaptability of our biosensors to diverse analytical scenarios, including miRNA detection. The combination of high carrier mobility and large-scale production capabilities underscores the potential of our approach for developing practical biosensors. To enhance the sensitivity and speed of detection, we developed an exponential target recycling and hybridization chain reaction (TRHCR) method for miRNA detection, representing a novel advancement in biosensor technology. This scheme (detailed in PART C: Research Output #5) employed six metastable hairpin oligonucleotides that were strategically activated by the target miRNA. This activation triggered a cascade of hairpin opening and self-assembly reactions, resulting in exponential signal amplification. The process not only reduced the sensing time from a lengthy 15 hours (for linear amplification scheme) to just 30 minutes but also achieved an attomolar-level limit of detection (LOD) as low as 100 aM, a remarkable achievement in nucleic acid detection. Theoretical modeling with NUPACK software allowed us to confirm the secondary structures of the oligonucleotides involved in the TRHCR process. Agarose gel electrophoresis further validated the successful formation of amplification complexes, while fluorescence quenching experiments provided kinetic insights into the exponential amplification dynamics. By coupling TRHCR with GFETs, we fabricated scalable GFET arrays functionalized with hairpin probe DNA, achieving satisfactory LOD and selectivity. Electrical characterization revealed a significant positive Dirac voltage shift upon miRNA exposure, attributed to the chemical gating effect induced by the negatively charged hybridization products formed during TRHCR. These findings highlight the potential of combining TRHCR with graphene-based sensors for rapid and ultra-sensitive biomolecular detection. We then evaluated the performance of our GFET sensors in complex physiological environments. By detecting miRNA-21 in buffer solutions and human serum, we established the reliability and accuracy of our biosensors in complex biological matrices. The sensors demonstrated recovery rates ranging from 92.88% to 108.35%, with relative standard deviations (RSD) consistently below 6.65%. An independent samples t-test confirmed the consistency of sensor responses across different environments, showing no statistically significant differences between serum and buffer responses. These results underscore the robustness of our biosensors in both controlled and real-world settings. To further ensure reliability, we conducted comprehensive specificity tests, which revealed that our sensors could effectively discriminate between target miRNA and mismatched oligonucleotides. This high degree of specificity, combined with the rapid sensing capabilities, positions our GFET biosensors as promising tools for clinical diagnostics and beyond. The integration of TRHCR with scalable GFET arrays not only advances the state of the art in biosensing but also addresses critical needs for fast, reliable, and ultrasensitive biomolecular detection in various applications.

24201020.label: Major findings and research outcome
24201020.value: With this project, we have achieved the following major findings and research outcomes: We successfully synthesized high-quality monolayer and bilayer graphene using a scalable CVD process. This enabled the fabrication of high-performance graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) with high carrier mobilities and exceptional reproducibility. These GFETs, characterized by their consistency and scalability, provided a versatile platform for biosensing applications and were successfully adapted into various types of biosensors. Notably, we developed an exponential target recycling and hybridization chain reaction (Exp_TRHCR) scheme for miRNA detection, which incorporates an autocatalytic reaction pathway with exponential kinetics. By integrating this scheme with GFETs, we achieved an attomolar limit of detection (LOD) as low as 100 aM and reduced the sensing time by 30-fold, from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. This breakthrough significantly enhances the feasibility of rapid and highly sensitive point-of-care diagnostics. Our approach demonstrated high performance in spiked serum tests, achieving recovery rates of 92.88% to 108.35% and relative standard deviations (RSD) below 6.65%, confirming its reliability in complex biological matrices. The integration of this innovative approach with GFETs highlights the robustness and scalability of the platform for next-generation biosensors. These findings are detailed in the paper published in Biosensors and Bioelectronics (PART C: Research Output #5). In addition, these GFETs provided an ideal platform for other biosensing applications, such as aptasensors. We developed aptasensors with high sensitivity for arsenite detection, as detailed in the paper published in ACS Applied Nano Materials (PART C: Research Output #11). The GFET aptasensor utilized an arsenite-specific aptamer as the recognition element, which undergoes a conformational change upon binding to arsenite. This change alters the electrostatic interaction with the graphene surface, enabling highly sensitive detection with a LOD as low as 0.02 ppb, two orders of magnitude lower than previously reported GFET-based ion sensors and surpassing the WHO-recommended arsenic limit of 10 ppb for drinking water. To further enhance device performance, we developed an innovative surface modification strategy using persistent carbene on gold electrodes. This approach significantly reduced contact resistivity and minimized contact noise between graphene and gold contacts. The improvement is attributed to the pi-pi stacking interactions between graphene and the benzene rings of persistent carbene, along with a decrease in the work function of gold, as confirmed by Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy. These results are published in the ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces paper (PART C: Research Output #6). Our work establishes a robust, scalable platform for graphene-based biosensors for nucleic acid detection. This project has resulted in 15 peer-reviewed journal articles, the awarding of two Ph.D. degrees, and two presentations at international conferences.

24201020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24201020.value: The results of this project provide a robust foundation for advancing research into multiplex detection systems, a critical step in addressing the complexity and heterogeneity of cancer. Precise monitoring and analysis of multiple nucleic acid markers are essential for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and improving patient outcomes. Building on this, the exponential target recycling and hybridization chain reaction (Exp_TRHCR) developed in this research can be integrated into multiplexed detection platforms (e.g., GFET sensor arrays) to enable rapid, simultaneous, and highly sensitive detection of multiple biomarkers. Future work will focus on optimizing the sensitivity and specificity of the system for diverse targets while adapting it for real-time clinical applications. By combining Exp_TRHCR with GFETs and other advanced molecular devices, this research has the potential to create next-generation diagnostic tools that are scalable, precise, and well-suited for point-of-care settings, ultimately advancing disease diagnosis.

24201020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24201020.value: This research focuses on improving the detection of specific genetic markers (like miRNA) for early disease diagnosis, such as cancer, by developing a new, faster, and more sensitive testing method. We combined a graphene-based sensor, known as a graphene field-effect transistor (GFET), with a novel technique called Exponential Target Recycling and Hybridization Chain Reaction (Exp_TRHCR). This technique enhances the sensitivity and speed of detection by amplifying the signal without the need for complex labels (label-free) or expensive reagents. The effectiveness of Exp_TRHCR was verified through simulations and laboratory experiments. Using this approach, we were able to detect target miRNA at extremely low concentrations (~100 aM), and significantly reduce the testing time, from 15 hours to just 30 minutes or less. This research has great potential to improve early disease diagnosis by providing faster, more affordable, and highly sensitive tests for genetic biomarkers.

24201720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24201720.value: 影像辨識技術中的實體分割功能(instance segmentation)可以提供細胞狀態和行為等的重要形態學信息，但是在實現穩定性和準確性方面的技術困難阻礙了其在生物研究中的廣泛採用。現時, 在世界各地Zernike的相襯顯微技術(phase-contrast microscopy)在研究實驗室中已普遍應用。這技術將原本透明的細胞圖像轉換為能被肉眼觀察, 再加上通過對細胞無害(i.e.無標籤、無毒害)的檢視方式, 可以幫助研究人員得到的具有高對比度的圖像，所以它作為一項應用在細胞觀察及監測中的技術 是非常理想的。其對細胞無害的特性對於不引入染色試劑和成像條件就能連續監測整個細胞群體是至關重要，因為引入染色試劑或成像條件就可能會干擾細胞行為並改變實驗結果。儘管研究中很少對細胞形態進行量化，但細胞形態的變通常被認為是對，由靜止，增殖，遷移，分化，衰老或凋亡引起的細胞行為變化的第一個指標。因此，儘管在不利用染色試劑或成像條件下, 以相襯顯微鏡圖像達成實例細胞分割技術具有挑戰性，但一旦成功將使生物學和生物醫學研究中的幾乎所有領域受益。 儘管有許多用於相襯顯微鏡細胞分割的基於計算機視覺(computational visualization)的方法，但是現存模型的多樣性有限, 以及標註真實值基準過程的繁瑣和主觀性質阻礙了其廣泛應用。我們的研究目標是開發一種基於計算機視覺的流程，該流程可在相襯顯微鏡圖像中實現實例細胞註釋(semi-automated instance cell segmentation)的半自動化（目標1）；開發可促進無標籤分割的機器學習模型，利用細胞形態作為已知的測試場景/案例來檢測肌腱細胞的分化（目標2）；並將此系統作為一種未知的測試場景/案例的形式用於肌腱生物材料的開發（目標3）。 我們的方法解決了相位對比分割中不同重要的問題及限制。其中問題包括：1）前景和背景之間的低信噪比(signal-to-noise ratio)，2）使用低放大率的圖像，雖然對量化細胞數量指標是十分重要，但包含的信息會受到限制（每個細胞佔有很少的像素），3）細胞呈現的動態形狀和大小, 4）在2D圖像中展示3D信息（細胞重疊時），以及5）標註的繁瑣性和不客觀。 前期研究證明了我們方案的可行性, 包括達成快速準確的真實值基準標註，繼而優化了分割性能，並且得到了一種新穎，透明，可3D打印，和細胞相容性以及具有和肌腱相似的機械性能的生物材料。 我們最終的成果將會是一個多樣性高的，基於計算機視覺的半自動觀測流程，該流程可被廣泛應用於探尋科學問題或與細胞培養相關的應用，特別針對細胞異質性研究和乾細胞製造。此流程的半自動化特性避免了繁瑣又不客觀的真實值基準標註，從而提高了用戶採用率和生產率。研究完成後，我們還將展示一個使用細胞形態來識別肌腱組織工程中最佳生長因子(growth factor)和細胞形貌的實例。

24201720.label: Realisation of objectives
24201720.value: There is a 3 page pdf that I cannot upload as there is no space for it. Only the text is pasted here: We have fully achieved 100% of Aim 1 by developing Cell Morphome, a semi-automated computer vision-based pipeline that facilitates label-free cell instance segmentation via human intuition mimicking, multi-image radiance maping (HIM-MIRM) (Fig. 1). This created a moderate dataset of about 0.1 million biological entities (nuclei and cells) from multiple cell types. This dataset facilitated Cell Morphome’s label-free cell instance segmentation pipeline with superior performance metrics that include 2.41-fold improved F1 score and 20-fold faster training speed over state-of-the-art MaskRCNN (Fig. 2). The pipeline is data-lean and does not require large dataset training to achieve high performance (Fig. 3). We have achieved 80% of Aim 2 by applying Cell Morphome for tendon differentiation. We showed that HIM-MIRM’s model accuracy for label-free cell instance segmentation was heavily dependent on the information quality or richness (e.g., bit-depth and modal type) present within the images (Fig. 5). We were also able to train conditional generative adversarial network models (cGAN), i.e., Pix2Pix, for pseudo prediction of tendon-associated markers in the presence or absence of tendon-associated growth factors (Fig. 6). However, the results were less than satisfactory and attributed in part to differences in cell culture conditions between the trained model and actual conditions necessary for in vitro tendon differentiation as well as the difficulty for cGANs to generate a realistic pseudo fluorescence image in a single step. In the future, the cGAN may be replaced with a conditional diffusion model such as Palette to overcome this issue. We have achieved 100% of Aim 3 by applying label-free, cell morphology prediction for optimizing tendon differentiation in vitro (Fig. 6) and assessing the combined effect of growth factors and topography on cell morphology and tenocyte differentiation (Fig. 7).

24201720.label: Major findings and research outcome
24201720.value: The major findings and research outcome are the following: (1) Development of Cell Morphome, a computer vision-based pipeline that mimics human intuition for label-free cell segmentation (2) Cell Morphome achieves high performance (e.g., 2.41-fold improved F1 score and 20X more rapid training speed and execution than state-of-the-art MaskRCNN). Cell Morphome’s performance is due to its information richness and quality. Cell Morphome is broad ranging and can be used across different microscopes and different cell types. (3) The approach used in Cell Morphome was applied for in vitro tendon differentiation. However, difficulties with accurate pseudo fluorescence signal prediction were encountered. This was in part, attributed to the challenge of generative adversarial networks producing a realistic like pseudo fluorescence image under appropriate experimental conditions, which differed from those use to train and develop Cell Morphome. Nevertheless, we were able to continue demonstrate the utility of a label-free approach for image classification of ex vivo skeletal muscle samples using in vitro-derived data. (4) We were able to demonstrate that GDF-7 as well as a combination of FGF-2, IGF-1, and TGF-β3 have tendon-promoting activities. In addition, it was shown that both tendon-like topography and growth factors can synergistically interact to enhance tenogenesis. This was demonstrated in vitro and in vivo.

24201720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24201720.value: There is further potential for use of Cell Morphome for basic biological discovery, drug screening and cell biomanufacturing. This requires further optimization of Cell Morphome algorithm using newer advanced architectures for image-to-image translation. This will broaden the application possibilities of label-free microscopic cell analysis. Furthermore, continued use of Cell Morphome for studying tenogenesis and developing tendon therapeutics will play an important contributing role towards tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. Identified growth factor and biomaterials should be rigorously assessed in large pre-clinical animal models and if deemed successful and commercially viable, proceed towards human clinical trials.

24201720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24201720.value: The study aims to use artificial intelligence to perform stain-free imaging and quantification of cells in microscope images. A computer vision-based pipeline, called Cell Morphome was developed and was shown to have high performance for recognizing different cell types within images acquired from different microscope equipment. Cell Morphome was used to assess tenogenesis in vitro and growth factors such as GDF-7 as well as a combination of FGF-2, IGF-1, and TGF-β3 were demonstrated to have tendon-promoting activities in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, it was shown that growth factors and surface topography can synergistically interact to enhance tenogenesis. Discovering such knowledge has beneficial implications for the development of future tendon therapeutics. Overall, this study has successfully contributed towards the development of a label-free computer vision-based pipeline for recognizing cells in stain-free images and identified tendon-promoting growth factors, which holds significant promise for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

24203520.label: Project Objectives
24203520.value: We study a novel multiple structure factor analysis (MSFA) model which describes data matrices/tensors as outer products of complex & flexibly structured matrices (”factors”). Motivated by the diverse sources/types of data acquired, the model also allows for obser- vations with different modalities (numerics, counts, binary, etc.). We develop fundamental theories for the proposed MSFA with three sub-objectives - (i) analyze the model recovery error and establish convergence rate for a regularized maximum likelihood method; (ii) investigate and establish convergence rate for a Bayesian inference method with generic data distributions; (iii) propose new numerical solution methods for ‘Big-Data’ based on stochastic and distributed optimization. We study the applications of MSFA to multi-graph learning on real data, part of which will be collected as an integral part of this project. For example, we collect data from the stock market, Twitter/Facebook/Reddit, and potentially through a collaboration with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. We validate the MSFA approach to graph learning, illustrating if the proposed inference method produces trained model that predicts the out-of-sample real data, as well as comparing it to state-of-the-art methods. In addition, we develop a software for identifying structural features and diagnosing vulnerabilities in real world networks using the MSFA inference methods developed in Objective 1. The generated insights can help with understanding the structure of real networks, or detecting communities, or locating key individuals in social networks. Departing from the fixed dataset setting in Objective 1 & 2, we study an online learning setting for MSFA with data captured in a streaming or dynamical fashion, i.e., with an infinite dataset. In the setting of streaming data, we analyze the convergence of an online inference method based on independent and identically distributed observations. For dynamical data, we investigate active sampling strategies where data are collected sequentially as informed by the current MSFA model estimate. We derive bounds on the bias of applying vanilla online method to such scenarios, then we develop a bias-free method through combining active sampling with online optimization.

24203520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24203520.value: Extracting information from data has been the primary goal for many studies in signal processing, machine learning. A key problem faced by many practitioners is how to process the enormous amount of unorganized, diverse data. Taking the task of learning from social network as an example, nowadays data are acquired from sources that are cyber (interactions on online platforms), physical (movement sensors on cellphones), or cyber- physical (augmented reality like Pokemon Go), and the relevant inquiries include “who are the opinion leaders?”, “how are the individuals divided into communities?”. To answer these questions, a popular approach is to apply factor analysis, a form of unsupervised learning which views data as the product between the “loading matrix” and “factor”. The loading matrix encodes information about the unknown system, e.g., a social graph, and excitations represent the stimuli, e.g., rumors. Through inspecting the loading matrix, the above inquiries can be answered. This project proposes a novel multiple structure factor analysis (MSFA) model. Unlike traditional factor analysis, it applies on tensor data (covering matrix data as a special case) composed of multiple factors, each with a distinct complex structure. In addition, the MSFA supports heterogeneous observations modeled as random variables of exponential family distributions. Our study is motivated by the emerging problem of multi-graph learning that infers an ensemble of graph topologies from observed actions of nodes, described as graph signals. Inspired by the PI’s recent work, we illustrate that we can extract the graph(s)’ features through fitting the observed actions data into an MSFA model and inspecting the inferred factors. Our project has three aims: First, we study MSFA inference methods with multi-modal observations, and provide a thorough analysis for convergence, model recoverability in the arisen large-scale optimization problem. Second, we deploy MSFA to tackle multi-graph learning on real data from social/financial network to uncover the structure of these networks, e.g., answering the inquiries in the first paragraph. Third, we study an online version of MSFA with infinite datasets of streaming and dynamical data. If successful, the project will extend the capability of factor models to handle large-scale complex data, as well as suggesting new methods for multi-graph learning. 從數據中提取信息一直是信號處理及機器學習研究的主要目標。許多從業者面臨的關鍵問題是如何處理海量的無組織，多樣化的數據。以從社交網絡學習的任務為例，如今的數據是從網絡（在線平台上的交互），物理（手機上的移動傳感器）或網絡實體（增強現實（如Pokemon Go）等）獲取數據的，相關查詢包括“誰是意見領袖？”，“個人如何劃分為社區？”。為了回答這些問題，一種流行的方法是應用因子分析，這是一種無監督的學習形式，將數據視為“負載矩陣”和“因子”之間的乘積。其中"負載矩陣"包含關於未知系統的信息（如社交圖），而"因子"則包含了對系統的輸入（如謠言）。以上查詢均可通過檢查"負載矩陣"回答。 此項目提出了一種新穎的多結構因子分析（MSFA）模型。與傳統因子分析不同，它適用於由多個因子組成的張量數據（包括矩陣數據），每個因子具有不同的複雜結構。此外，MSFA還支持將異類觀測建模為指數族分佈的隨機變量。我們的研究受到多圖學習的新問題的啟發，該問題從觀察到的節點動作（稱為圖信號）推斷出圖拓撲的整體。受PI最近的工作啟發，我們說明可以通過將觀察到的動作數據擬合到MSFA模型中並檢查推斷的因素來提取圖形的特徵。我們的項目有三個目標：首先，我們研究具有多模式觀測值的MSFA推理方法，並對出現的大規模優化問題中的收斂性，模型可恢復性提供透徹的分析。其次，我們部署MSFA來處理來自社交/金融網絡的真實數據的多圖學習，以發現這些網絡的結構，例如，回答第一段中的查詢。第三，我們研究了MSFA的在線版本，其中包含無限量的流和動態數據集。 如果成功，該項目將擴展因子模型的能力以處理大規模複雜數據，並提出用於多圖學習的新方法。

24203520.label: Major findings and research outcome
24203520.value: Our major findings are as follows (with reference to the publications listed in Sec. 5.3): 1. We proposed a MSFA model for graph learning via a structured factor analysis approach. Our approach consists of (i) a rigorously derived inference model with provable identifiability for multi-graph inference, (ii) an efficient algorithm for online learning, (iii) practical data verification. The related publications are [1,2,3,5,6]. 2. We also extended the model to graph learning from partial observations, i.e., when the signals on nodes are not fully observable. This has led to new analysis to rigorously study the effects of such models. The related publications are [1,6,11]. Note that [11] has received a Best Student Paper award at the IEEE SAM Workshop 2024. 3. We have made contributions to other fields as well, including machine learning, optimization and game theory. These works involve developing new PCA algorithms for use in the MSFA model of the project, as well as a new network game analysis study with interplay between data and agents. The related publications are [8,9]. 4. We have investigated extension of the MSFA model to the closely related subject of multiplex graph and has resulted in the publications [7,10]. These works proposed new algorithms for inferring multiplex graphs.

24203520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24203520.value: During the project development, at least two new research directions have been inspired that has the potential for further development. The first one is the extension of multiple-graph signal processing models to multiplex graphs which are coupled. The latter system features interconnected graphs that is motivated by the multi-presence of individuals in different social network platforms. It remains an open problem regarding how the signal model should be extended to capture these interactions in a computationally efficient ways. The second one is the partial observation models that are motivated by practical needs where the nodes in a large graph are often not fully observed. It is an open problem regarding when it is required to use sophisticated algorithms to process such data without performance loss. The PI is working with his team to develop on this two fronts and will apply for further funding in the future.

24203520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24203520.value: This research has studied new algorithms and mathematical models that can unveil the structure of an unknown graph, such as social systems, in a provably efficient and accurate manner. The research has shown that it is possible to consider the observations from multiple graphs simultaneously to improve accuracy without sacrificing the performance. Moreover, the research has demonstrated that the proposed approach can be applied on real data such as social network, finance network, etc., to unveil previously unknown information, e.g., the relative importance among stocks in an exchange market. We anticipate that the findings from this research can be applied in a wide spectrum of fields involving graph-structured data.

24210220.value: 通過精確凸鬆弛和分佈式反饋設計進行多相潮流優化

24210220.label: Project Objectives
24210220.value: Develop a convex semidefinite program (SDP) relaxation to seek for the global optimum of nonconvex optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase radial networks with wye- and delta-connected power sources and loads. As a basis of the proposed relaxation, we shall develop a multiphase branch flow model which describes delta connections more accurately than the existing linear approximation while preserving exactness of the SDP relaxation. Obtain analytic conditions that can be checked a priori (before actually solving the SDP) to tell if the SDP relaxation would be exact, i.e., if the SDP solution would be feasible and globally optimal for the original OPF problem. These analytic conditions indicate whether the SDP relaxation is worth solving before solving it, and hence are especially important in large networks where solving SDP would spend significant computation overhead. Develop a scalable and computationally efficient algorithm through distributed feedback design. Prove convergence of the proposed algorithm to the global optimum of the proposed SDP relaxation, so that it also converges to the global optimum of nonconvex OPF under the exactness conditions derived above. Prove that the proposed algorithm can track the global optimum of time-varying OPF problems within a characterizable error bound. Numerically demonstrate and validate the proposed relaxation and algorithm through software simulations in realistic distribution network models, including IEEE 13-bus, 37-bus, 123-bus network models and an 11,000-node network model. The proposed SDP relaxation should yield rank-one solutions that are feasible and globally optimal for the original OPF problems. The proposed distributed feedback-based algorithm should demonstrate improvement in convergence speed compared to centralized and distributed algorithms without feedback. The proposed algorithm should also demonstrate a tracking error within the theoretical bound characterized above when implemented for solving time-varying OPF.

24210220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24210220.value: Optimal power flow (OPF) is a class of optimization problems that are fundamental to power system operations. Solving for the global optimum of OPF is important in reducing operational cost and emissions, yet it is also a hard task because of the nonconvexity of OPF. Moreover, the revolutionary transformation of power systems is gravely challenging OPF solution methods today in terms of computational efficiency and scalability, especially at the distribution-network level where tens of millions of distributed energy resources (DERs) are installed and coming into operation. The drastic growth of variable renewable generation, mainly solar photovoltaic (PV), requires faster OPF algorithms to cope with rapidly changing problem conditions caused by intermittent power supplies. Concurrently, OPF problem sizes are proliferating with the massive deployment of controllable DERs, such as smart appliances and buildings, electric vehicles, energy storage devices, and PV inverters, which calls for more scalable OPF algorithms. This project aims to develop a theoretical and algorithmic framework to overcome the challenges above. Specifically, our goal is to solve for the global optimum of nonconvex OPF in a scalable and computationally efficient manner, in distribution networks featuring radial topology, unbalanced multiple phases, and wye- and delta-connected power sources and loads. To achieve this goal, we shall develop a convex semidefinite relaxation technique for this kind of OPF problems and derive analytic conditions that can be checked a priori to ensure exactness of the proposed relaxation. We shall further design a distributed feedback-based algorithm that can be proved to converge to the global optimum of the relaxed problem (which is also the global optimum of the nonconvex OPF under the exactness conditions we derived). Through software simulations in realistic distribution network models, the proposed relaxation and algorithm will be numerically validated in terms of global optimality, convergence speed, and capability of tracking the global optimum of time-varying OPF problems. The project team is capable of and confident in accomplishing the proposed mission with solid expertise and rich experience in developing breakthrough theories, advanced algorithms, and realistic simulations for convex relaxation of OPF, feedback-based optimization, and distributed control of power systems. 最優潮流是電力系統運行中最根本的一類優化問題。求解該類問題的全局最優對減少運行成本和排放至關重要，但該類問題的非凸性也導致其十分困難。此外，電力系統的深刻變革正在計算效率和可擴展性方面對最優潮流的求解構成嚴峻挑戰，特別是在配電網層面，千萬數量級的分佈式能源正被安裝和投入運營的情況下。隨著以太陽能光伏為主的高變動性可再生能源大量增長，最優潮流算法需要更快的求解速度來應對間歇性電力供應導致的問題條件的快速變化。同時，分佈式可控能源，如智能家電和建築、電動汽車、儲能設備、光伏逆變器的大量部署使最優潮流問題的規模激增，因此需要可擴展性更佳的求解算法。 本項目致力於開發一套理論和算法框架來克服上述挑戰。項目的具體目標是以可擴展和高計算效率的方式來求解樹形結構、多相不平衡、星-三角型混合連接的配電網中非凸最優潮流問題的全局最優。為實現這一目標，團隊計劃開發針對此類問題的半正定凸鬆弛技術，並推導出能夠確保該鬆弛精確性的先驗分析條件。團隊將進一步設計基於分佈式反饋的求解算法，並證明其能收斂到鬆弛問題的全局最優（在上述精確性條件下，同時也是原非凸最優潮流問題的全局最優）。通過基於現實配電網模型的軟件仿真，團隊將數值驗證所提出的鬆弛技術和求解算法的全局最優性、收斂速度、以及對時變最優潮流問題全局最優解的追蹤能力。團隊在最優潮流的凸鬆弛、基於反饋的最優化、電力系統的分佈式控制領域具有開發突破性理論、先進算法、現實仿真的專長和經驗，因此有能力和信心完成所提出的項目任務。

24210220.label: Realisation of objectives
24210220.value: Objective 1. We developed a convex semidefinite program (SDP) relaxation for unbalanced three-phase optimal power flow (OPF) problems in radial (tree) networks. The relaxation is obtained by removing rank-1 constraints from the matrix-form three-phase power flow equations. The proposed OPF model and SDP relaxation can incorporate accurate models of three-phase power sources, loads, and transformers in wye and delta configurations (the primary and secondary sides of transformers may have different configurations, e.g., wye-delta or delta-wye). Our research output [J17] (which represents the journal publication No. 17 in Part C-8 of this report, the same below) contains further details, in which the three-phase device and network modeling is mainly performed by the project collaborators at Caltech, and the SDP relaxation for three-phase OPF and the proof of its exactness (in Section 6.3.2) are mainly performed by the PI and his team at CUHK. To supplement the proposed convex relaxation, we developed a set of simple yet accurate approximations to the nonconvex feasible region of nonlinear alternating-current (AC) power flow equations. In research output [J4], we utilized second-order cone relaxation to approximate the multiple-time-period feasible region of power transfer at the head of an AC distribution network that contains uncertain renewable generation and energy storage. Further in [J5], we built a linear model as an accurate inner approximation to the feasible region of power transfer at the head of an AC distribution network. To guarantee feasibility, the parameters in the proposed linear approximation are obtained by Brouwer's fixed point theorem applied to the quadratic-form power flow equations. In [J11] and [C3] (which represents the conference paper No. 3 in Part C-9 of this report, the same below), we extended the linear model of [J5] to incorporate controllable energy storage systems. Specifically, we developed a linear approximation to the nonconvex constraint that prohibits simultaneous charging and discharging and derived sufficient conditions to guarantee the exactness of the OPF solution solved from this approximate model. To further improve the accuracy of distribution network modeling, we applied Koopman operator theory to the physical rules and operational input-output data of power flow equations to learn an equivalent distribution network model [J12]. In [J7], we developed an accurate polytopic approximation to the feasible region of nodal power injections in a tree network of AC flows. The approximation is obtained by iteratively adding cutting planes to gradually approach the feasible region of the dual second-order cone relaxation (with zero duality gap) and by adaptively (to the desired tradeoff between feasibility and optimality) removing the inexactly relaxed region based on the complementary slackness condition. Objective 2. In the project midterm report, we had proved in a two-bus three-phase network that the globally optimal solution to the convex SDP relaxation is also feasible and thus globally optimal (i.e., exact) for the original nonconvex three-phase OPF problem, although the proof at that time required some conditions that might not hold in reality. In this reporting period, we have extended our proof for the exactness of SDP relaxation for three-phase OPF, from the two-bus network to general tree networks, under practical conditions on the line parameters, e.g., the series admittance matrix of each line is symmetric and its real part is positive definite. Please refer to [J17] for further details of our proof. Objective 3. We developed scalable, computationally efficient, distributed feedback-based algorithms to solve three-phase OPF problems faster and accurately, not only for solving one OPF problem at a time, but also for tracking the optimal solutions of time-varying OPF problems. In [C1], we developed a hierarchical distributed OPF algorithm based on the local nodal voltage feedback and a more accurate gradient calculation for the nonlinear power flow constraints in tree networks. Compared to the traditional algorithms based on linearized power flow models, the proposed algorithm effectively compensates for the influence of nonlinear terms (e.g., power losses) on the gradient calculation and hence alleviates the risk of voltage safety violation arising from the model linearization. In [J16], we extended the algorithm of [C1] from single-phase to unbalanced three-phase networks, proved its convergence to the OPF solution within a theoretical error bound, and verified its solution speed and quality through numerical experiments on large distribution network models. In [J9], we designed a primal-dual distributed feedback algorithm to solve OPF, in which the required state (voltage) feedback is obtained by state estimation from limited measurement data. In [J6], we further extended the distributed state estimation and optimization algorithm to track a series of time-varying OPF solutions in real time. Our other work related to this objective is summarized as follows. In [J2], we developed an efficient decomposed algorithm based on the second-order cone relaxation and the iterative convex-concave procedure to solve an integrated optimization problem that couples a single-phase power network, a municipal water network, and a district heating network. We extended the algorithm of [J2] to the one of [J1], which applies the SDP relaxation of unbalanced three-phase power flow to an integrated seaport energy system with on-shore power supplies, cranes, and cold chain logistics. We further enhanced the distributed OPF algorithms developed in this project by preserving the privacy of the distributed agents that exchange necessary information for OPF computation. In [J3], we developed a privacy-preserving distributed algorithm based on the encryption of the alternating direction method of multipliers to solve OPF problems with SDP relaxation and l-1 norm regularization. We proved theoretically and demonstrated by numerical simulations that the proposed algorithm can obtain near-optimal solutions with guaranteed privacy preservation and satisfactory computational efficiency. In [C2], we developed a differentially-private distributed stochastic optimization algorithm over a bounded convex constraint set, which can be applied to the SDP relaxation of OPF problems for fast and accurate solution with provable privacy guarantees of local computing agents. We also enriched the proposed distributed algorithms from a game-theoretic perspective, to deal with the competing interests and strategic behaviors of controllable distributed energy resources and to design a socially efficient and operationally reliable energy trading market mechanism, subject to the power flow constraints [J8], [J10]. We further applied this distributed mechanism to a coupled power and transportation system for optimizing the electric vehicle charging schedules considering the real-time traffic congestion and power system loading conditions [J15]. Besides, we applied our OPF algorithms as the basis of solving distribution network reconfiguration problems [J13], [J14]: The distribution network topology is optimized to achieve the minimum operational cost while ensuring safety and reliability, in which the cost of each candidate topology is solved by optimizing the continuous power flow, using the OPF algorithms developed by us. Objective 4. In our studies summarized in Objectives 1-3 above, the OPF solution quality (such as the power-flow feasibility, voltage safety, and cost-effectiveness) and computational efficiency (especially the speed of convergence) are verified through software simulations of realistic three-phase power distribution network models, including the IEEE 13, 37, and 123-bus network models and an 11,000-node network model. In particular, we constructed the 11,000-node model by connecting the IEEE 8,500-node model and the ERPI Ckt7 model; further, by merging the secondary-side loads into the primary side of transformers, we can implement our OPF algorithms on a reduced network of about 4,500 nodes [J9], [J16].

As a basis of the proposed relaxation, we shall develop a multiphase branch flow model which describes delta connections more accurately than the existing linear approximation while preserving exactness of the SDP relaxation.

Obtain analytic conditions that can be checked a priori (before actually solving the SDP) to tell if the SDP relaxation would be exact, i.e., if the SDP solution would be feasible and globally optimal for the original OPF problem. These analytic conditions indicate whether the SDP relaxation is worth solving before solving it, and hence are especially important in large networks where solving SDP would spend significant computation overhead.

Develop a scalable and computationally efficient algorithm through distributed feedback design. Prove convergence of the proposed algorithm to the global optimum of the proposed SDP relaxation, so that it also converges to the global optimum of nonconvex OPF under the exactness conditions derived above. Prove that the proposed algorithm can track the global optimum of time-varying OPF problems within a characterizable error bound.

Numerically demonstrate and validate the proposed relaxation and algorithm through software simulations in realistic distribution network models, including IEEE 13-bus, 37-bus, 123-bus network models and an 11,000-node network model. The proposed SDP relaxation should yield rank-one solutions that are feasible and globally optimal for the original OPF problems. The proposed distributed feedback-based algorithm should demonstrate improvement in convergence speed compared to centralized and distributed algorithms without feedback. The proposed algorithm should also demonstrate a tracking error within the theoretical bound characterized above when implemented for solving time-varying OPF.

24210220.label: Major findings and research outcome
24210220.value: 1. We proved theoretically that a convex semidefinite program (SDP) relaxation is exact for unbalanced three-phase optimal power flow (OPF) problems in general radial (tree) networks, if the following conditions are met: (i) the series admittance matrix of each line is symmetric and its real part is positive definite; and (ii) at the obtained optimal solution of the SDP relaxation, the limits to nodal power injections and the lower limits to nodal voltage magnitudes are not binding [J17]. Compared to previous theoretical conditions for the exact SDP relaxation of three-phase OPF problems, the conditions we found are easier to check in practice. Moreover, they are similar to previous conditions for exact relaxations of the simpler single-phase OPF problems, and hence it is a valuable finding that similar conditions also work for the more complicated three-phase OPF problems. 2. Besides convex relaxation, we developed other convex approximations to the nonlinear alternating-current (AC) power flow constraints, such as linear inner approximations [J5], [J11], [C3] and a simple yet accurate polytopic approximation [J7]. Numerical results showed that the proposed approximations, compared to the existing linearization, relaxation, and inner approximation methods, can attain a better tradeoff, which is more adaptable to system parameters and loading conditions, between guaranteeing feasibility (by shrinking the approximate feasible region) and improving optimality (by enlarging the approximate feasible region). 3. We developed hierarchical distributed algorithms, based on a more accurate gradient calculation than traditional linearization methods, to solve OPF problems in large tree networks [C1], [J16]. We theoretically proved that the proposed algorithms converge to OPF solutions within characterizable error bounds. Numerical simulations on realistic models of the IEEE 123-bus network and a reduced 11,000-node network (with 4,518 primary-side nodes) verified that the proposed algorithms can effectively alleviate the risk of voltage safety violation in the OPF solutions due to system modeling errors, at improved computation speeds compared to the traditional centralized solution methods (even if the centralized methods use simpler but less accurate linearized models). 4. We developed a primal-dual distributed feedback algorithm with state estimation from limited measurement data to solve OPF [J9] and implemented the algorithm in an online manner to track time-varying OPF solutions [J6]. Numerical results on the reduced 11,000-node network verified the improved feasibility and optimality of solutions, the faster and more accurate convergence to (or tracking of) the (time-varying) OPF solutions, and the robustness to missing or inaccurate measurements.

24210220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24210220.value: 1. We will extend our work from the nonconvex continuous optimization of nonlinear (unbalanced three-phase) power flow to the combinatorial optimization of power network topology. Specifically, for each feasible candidate topology, its cost is defined by solving the continuous optimal power flow (OPF) problem using the methods developed in this project. 2. We will extend the OPF problems and solution methods from deterministic settings to stochastic (i.e., optimizing the expectation of possible outcomes) and robust settings (i.e., optimizing the worst-case outcome), to deal with the uncertainties of solar and wind generation, load user behavior, et cetera. To relieve the heavy computational burdens due to the large set of random outcomes (i.e., the uncertainty set), we plan to adaptively (re)sample the uncertainty set and merge / cluster the samples that lead to similar optimal solutions, thus solving fewer sampled problems without significantly sacrificing the quality of the final solution. 3. To further enhance the speed of solving large-scale nonlinear OPF problems while ensuring the quality of solutions, we will extend the distributed feedback-based OPF algorithms developed in this project by learning decentralized neural network models from simulated data to predict the iterative descent directions of local decision variables.

24210220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24210220.value: This project developed novel mathematical solutions to the long-standing optimal power flow (OPF) problems. Solving OPF is fundamental for reducing the operational costs and emissions while ensuring safety and reliability of power systems, but it is also a hard problem considering the practical power flow models that are nonlinear, nonconvex, and unbalanced three-phase. The revolutionary transformation of power systems is gravely challenging the OPF solution methods today in terms of computational speed and scalability. The drastic growth of variable renewable generation, such as wind and solar, requires faster solution algorithms to cope with the rapidly changing OPF problem conditions caused by intermittent power supplies. Meanwhile, the OPF problem sizes are increasing with the massive deployment of controllable resources, e.g., demand-response appliances, batteries (including electric vehicles), and smart inverters, which calls for OPF algorithms that are more scalable in operational and computational efficiency. The research outputs of this project offer a set of mathematical reformulations and solution algorithms for the important yet difficult OPF problems in unbalanced three-phase networks. Compared to existing methods, ours have attained improved theoretical guarantees and numerical performance (in large-scale power network simulations) in terms of the speed and quality of OPF solutions.

24210420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24210420.value: 系統性風險管理之金融網絡多元壓力測試

24210420.label: Project Objectives
24210420.value: Systemic risk, often understood as financial institutions' exposure to possible losses due to other institutions' defaults, has increased considerably in recent years along with the evolution of interconnectedness in financial systems. The greater systemic risk financial institutions are exposed to, the more likely they are to suffer from domino effects of bank failures. As seen in the financial crisis of 2008, triggered by the subprime mortgage implosion, large financial institutions may face severe financial distress in quick succession. Since systemically risky events rarely happen in practice and they are caused by the amplification of multiple economic factors within the network structure of the financial system, stress testing has been considered an important tool, especially for systemic risk management. In a usual stress testing, by applying extreme yet plausible stress scenarios, we compute the resulting systemic risk measures which might not be easily captured by analyzing historical market data or by using stochastic models for market prediction. The proposed research is motivated by two practical issues on stress testing of the financial network that the PI faced when carrying out a collaborative research project with the Bank of Korea. Firstly, due to the complicated nature of the financial network, it is hard to identify stress scenarios that cause large systemic losses and threaten the stability of the financial system. Such identification of extreme-yet-plausible scenarios, called reverse stress testing, can help us understand the potential triggers of systemically risky events and remove the arbitrariness in the scenario selection for stress testing. Secondly, most of the papers on systemic risk assume that the complete information about financial networks is given, but such information is often not available in practice because financial institutions usually keep their transaction information confidential. Thus, the public, the institutions, or the regulators have only partial information about financial networks, which poses a huge challenge to measure systemic risk accurately. In this research, we plan to study two main topics that address the above issues. One is to develop a quantitative method of reverse stress testing for systemic risk. In this direction, we plan to provide an optimization approach to the selection and analysis of the most likely stress scenarios that could lead to the systemic risk measures exceeding certain thresholds. This is also closely related to the field of inverse optimization since the celebrated Eisenberg-Noe framework describes the mapping from the economic stress scenarios to the systemic risk measures using optimization problems. The other is to find robust bounds of systemic risk measures for any given stress scenarios. In particular, given that a financial network is partially observable, we plan to obtain the worst-case systemic risk measures using optimization techniques. In addition, we plan to apply the robust bounds to the analysis of the probability that the worst-case systemic risk measures exceed certain thresholds. Therefore, we believe that developing new quantitative methodologies for reverse stress testing and robust risk quantification in financial networks will shed new light on theoretical advances in the literature of systemic risk and financial networks. Beyond such theoretical contributions, practical contributions of this research directly associated with the aforementioned motivation of this research are also expected. The most likely shock scenarios in the first part could be utilized to demystify potential risk factors and applied to each institution's stress tests. Also, from the regulators' perspective, a systemic threat index can be developed by measuring a distance between current macroeconomic risk factors and the set of shock scenarios that result in different levels of the financial system distress. This index might lead to the development of an early-warning system against financial crises. Furthermore, along with the recent advances in capital requirements, the robust quantification of systemic risk is expected to contribute to the evolution of macroprudential policies based on incomplete information of financial networks since one of its possible applications is the estimation of the worst-case systemic risk capital.
