24210420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24210420.value: We propose to conduct research on systemic risk management focusing on multivariate stress testing of financial networks. Specifically, based on the celebrated Eisenberg-Noe network model, we address two computational and practical issues which have not been fully answered in the literature: reverse stress testing and robust quantification of systemic risk. Financial institutions are often intertwined with each other. For example, some of them lend money to others or hold others’ shares. Such interconnectedness is often viewed as a network structure which we call a financial network. In the network, one institution’s losses can be propagated to other institutions. Such vulnerability of financial networks due to the loss propagation is referred to as systemic risk. With the objective of supporting systemic risk management, stress testing of financial networks has become increasingly important since the global financial crisis in 2008 during which large financial institutions failed sequentially. In contrast to the stress testing of individual institutions, when conducting the stress testing of financial networks, in order to obtain systemic risk measures, we need to use full network information and investigate shock amplification caused by network effects. However, this approach leads to the following two open problems. The first problem is on selecting plausible stress scenarios that cause large systemic risk, which is essential for effective stress tests. However, this is a challenging problem since, due to the shock amplification, the mapping from scenarios to systemic risk measures is not easy to handle. Accordingly, in the first part of this research, we aim to explore a method of identifying stress scenarios that are extreme but plausible by finding the most likely scenarios leading to systemic risk measures greater than given thresholds. This is the so-called reverse stress testing. Specifically, we focus on scenarios with multiple stress factors under which each financial institution receives a distinct economic shock. In the second part, we tackle the issue of incomplete information on financial networks in conducting stress testing. In many jurisdictions, financial institutions are not required to report their inter-institution transactions to the financial regulators. In this case, the regulators have only partial information on the network, which makes them hard to measure systemic risk accurately for given stress scenarios. To cope with such difficulty, we will see how much unknown network components affect the systemic risk measures for any given stress scenarios by studying their robust quantification which leads to the worst-case systemic risk measures. 我們考慮一個金融機構互相影響的金融系統。譬如，有些從其他機構借款，有些貸款給其他機構，有些則持有其他機構的股份。這樣的相互聯繫常被視作一種網絡結構，我們稱之為金融網絡。在這個網絡中，一個機構的虧損可以傳播給其他機構。源於虧損傳播的金融網絡脆弱性被稱為系統性風險。我們關注金融網絡的壓力測試，自2008金融風暴期間許多大型金融機構相繼倒下以來，它已經成為越來越重要的系統性風險管理工具之一。在壓力測試中，我們使用多種可能的壓力場景并評估它們造成的系統性風險程度。 在此提出的研究中，我們將要解決計算上以及實際上曾出現於系統性風險管理金融網絡壓力測試的問題。確言之，基於著名的Eisenberg-Noe網絡模型，我們關注兩個在文獻中從未被完全回答的重要問題：逆向壓力測試及系統風險的穩健量化。 第一個問題來自於這樣的事實：選擇合適的場景儘管對有效的壓力測試是重要的，但也是有挑戰性的問題。因此，在此研究的第一部分，我們致力於探索一種通過找到導致系統性風險程度大於給定閾值的最有可能場景，從而識別極端但可信的壓力場景的方法，這就是所謂的逆向壓力測試。特別地，我們關注擁有多個壓力因子的場景，其下每個金融機構受到不同的經濟衝擊。 第二部分中，我們解決在進行壓力測試時金融網絡不完全信息的問題。許多轄區不要求金融機構向金融監管者報告它們的跨機構交易。在此情形中，監管者只有網絡的部分信息，使得他們難於準確測量在給定壓力場景下的系統性風險。為解決此難題，通過研究任何給定壓力場景下系統性風險的穩健量化，其給出最壞情況下的系統性風險程度，我們將會看到未知網絡分支對系統性風險程度有多少影響。

24210420.label: Realisation of objectives
24210420.value: The Principal Investigator (PI) successfully achieved all project objectives. The project focused on two primary areas: (1) the identification of extreme-yet-plausible stress scenarios, also known as reverse stress testing, for systemic risk management, and (2) the robust quantification of systemic risk in financial networks amidst network information uncertainty. To address the first objective, the PI and collaborators concentrated on selecting the most probable scenarios leading to adverse impacts on interbank networks. They proposed an optimization-based approach to this challenge, founded on the Eisenberg-Noe network model, a widely recognized risk contagion framework. Specifically, tractable mixed-integer programs were formulated. The optimal solutions to these programs identify the most likely stress scenarios among all extreme scenarios where the negative network impact (e.g., total payment shortfall, total asset value loss, and number of defaulting banks) surpasses a predetermined threshold. An extension of this approach was also developed to accommodate the disposal of illiquid assets. Regarding the second objective, the PI and collaborators proposed a robust optimization approach to determine worst-case default probabilities and associated capital requirements for specific banking groups (e.g., systemically important financial institutions) under conditions of network information uncertainty. Utilizing this tool, the effects of various incomplete network information structures on these worst-case quantities were analyzed. The comprehensive outcomes from these two primary research areas fulfilled Objectives 1 through 4. Furthermore, these studies provide significant regulatory insights into the development of an early-warning system and the collection of actionable network information. All research claims were numerically illustrated using data from the European banking system, thereby realizing Objective 5. Throughout this research, the PI identified the critical importance of developing appropriate computational and statistical methods to validate these optimization-based approaches for systemic risk management. Consequently, the PI, in collaboration with colleagues, conducted further investigations into developing numerical methods in this context. Firstly, the PI supervised a PhD student whose research on efficient simulation methods for systemic risk measurement resulted in one journal article and one conference paper. Secondly, the PI and collaborators have been developing sequential sampling methods to address model risk in learning the stochastic characteristics of different systems and optimizing relevant decisions.

rows: Systemic risk, often understood as financial institutions' exposure to possible losses due to other institutions' defaults, has increased considerably in recent years along with the evolution of interconnectedness in financial systems. The greater systemic risk financial institutions are exposed to, the more likely they are to suffer from domino effects of bank failures. As seen in the financial crisis of 2008, triggered by the subprime mortgage implosion, large financial institutions may face severe financial distress in quick succession.

Since systemically risky events rarely happen in practice and they are caused by the amplification of multiple economic factors within the network structure of the financial system, stress testing has been considered an important tool, especially for systemic risk management. In a usual stress testing, by applying extreme yet plausible stress scenarios, we compute the resulting systemic risk measures which might not be easily captured by analyzing historical market data or by using stochastic models for market prediction.

The proposed research is motivated by two practical issues on stress testing of the financial network that the PI faced when carrying out a collaborative research project with the Bank of Korea. Firstly, due to the complicated nature of the financial network, it is hard to identify stress scenarios that cause large systemic losses and threaten the stability of the financial system. Such identification of extreme-yet-plausible scenarios, called reverse stress testing, can help us understand the potential triggers of systemically risky events and remove the arbitrariness in the scenario selection for stress testing. Secondly, most of the papers on systemic risk assume that the complete information about financial networks is given, but such information is often not available because financial institutions usually keep their transaction information confidential. Thus, the public, institutions, or regulators have only partial information about financial networks, which poses a huge challenge to measure systemic risk accurately.

In this research, we plan to study two main topics that address the above issues. One is to develop a quantitative method of reverse stress testing for systemic risk. More specifically, we plan to provide an optimization approach to the selection of the most likely stress scenarios that could lead to systemic risk measures exceeding certain thresholds. The other is to find robust bounds of systemic risk measures for any given stress scenarios. In particular, given that a financial network is partially observable, we plan to obtain the worst-case systemic risk measures using optimization techniques and to apply the robust bounds to the analysis of the probability that the worst-case systemic risk measures exceed certain thresholds. Therefore, we believe that developing new quantitative methodologies for reverse stress testing and robust risk quantification in financial networks will shed light on theoretical advances in the literature of systemic risk and financial networks.

Beyond such theoretical contributions, practical contributions of this research directly associated with the aforementioned motivation of this research are also expected. The most likely shock scenarios in the first part could be utilized to demystify potential risk factors and applied to each institution's stress tests. Also, from the regulators' perspective, a systemic threat index can be developed by measuring a distance between current macroeconomic risk factors and the set of shock scenarios that result in different levels of the financial system distress. This index might lead to the development of an early-warning system against financial crises. Furthermore, along with the recent advances in capital requirements, the robust quantification of systemic risk is expected to contribute to the evolution of macroprudential policies based on incomplete information of financial networks since one of its possible applications is the estimation of the worst-case systemic risk capital.

24210420.label: Major findings and research outcome
24210420.value: The PI has 8 publications, including 5 journal articles (No. 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 in Item 8 of Part C) and 3 conference papers (No. 1, 3, 7 in Item 8 of Part C), supported by this project. These research outcomes were disseminated in 10 conferences (see Item 9 of Part C) and have received two awards (see Item 12 of Part C). With these results, the PI has trained and graduated one PhD student, Dr. Lewen Zheng. More speficifally, the PI has published one journal article on the first topic of the proposal (i.e., the identification of extreme-yet-plausible stress scenarios, also known as reverse stress testing) in the Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, which is the top journal of the field; see No. 2 in Item 8 of Part C. The PI has also published one journal article on the second topic of the proposal (i.e., the robust quantification of systemic risk amidst information uncertainty) in Operations Research, the flagship journal of the field; see No. 4 in Item 8 of Part C. In these two papers, the PI and his collaborators proposed novel mixed-integer programming approaches for reverse stress testing and robust quantification. In addition, the PI has produced two rare-event simulation papers (No. 1, 8 in Item 8 of Part C) and four sequential learning papers (No. 3, 5, 6, 7 in Item 8 of Part C) that develop numerical approaches to the related computational issues.

24210420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24210420.value: The research topics explored in this project continue to present numerous open challenges, such as bond pricing within financial networks and strategic liquidation decisions under information uncertainty. The Principal Investigator will pursue these issues further, with the goal of publishing the resulting insights in leading academic journals.

24210420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24210420.value: We conducted research on systemic risk management focusing on multivariate stress testing of financial networks. Specifically, based on the celebrated Eisenberg-Noe network model, we addressed two main issues that have not been fully answered in the literature: reverse stress testing and robust quantification of systemic risk. Banks lend money to others or hold others’ shares. Such interconnectedness is often viewed as a network structure. In this financial network, one bank’s losses can be propagated to other institutions. Such vulnerability due to loss propagation is referred to as systemic risk. To manage systemic risk, systemic stress testing has become increasingly important since the 2008 financial crisis during which large financial institutions failed sequentially. Hence, we focused on selecting plausible stress scenarios that cause large systemic risk, which is essential for effective stress tests. We handled the challenge due to the mapping from scenarios to systemic risk measures by establishing a tractable optimization problem. Furthermore, in many jurisdictions, banks are not required to report their inter-bank transactions to regulators. This led us to tackle the issue of incomplete information on financial networks by developing a comprehensive approach to calculate the worst-case systemic risk measures based only on partial information.

24211020.label: Project Objectives
24211020.value: To develop a portable 800-nm OCT system and a theranostic microneedle, together with a rotary joint to combine the volumetric imaging capability with laser ablation function into a single probe. To validate the microneedle in a patient-derived mouse brain cancer model for high-resolution 3D deep-brain imaging in vivo and power-efficient tissue ablation. To develop a deep learning neural network algorithm for 3D tissue assessment with the accuracy comparable to human expert, incorporate the deep learning algorithm into the portable OCT system and demonstrate the cancer detection in the mouse brain cancer model. To demonstrate the feasibility of image-guided cancer ablation in a pilot study with the mouse model.

24211020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24211020.value: 深腦部病變，如癌症，在診斷和治療方面都面臨著挑戰​​。現時的確診方法依靠立體定向活檢。對於治療，當前主要的外科手段是激光消融術。立體定向活檢和深腦激光手術均依靠術前或術中MRI成像。然而MRI只能提供有限的分辨率，影響其引導活檢針和激光探頭的準確放置和對病變和消融效果精確評估。 另一方面，當前的深腦微創光學成像技術面臨諸多問題，如低分辨率，小視野和慢成像速度。這些局限性限制了對各種深層腦部疾病的組織形態學成像和診斷。另外，雖然人工智能在自動分析醫學圖像方面展示出巨大的潛力，可以處理大量的診斷圖像以及應對專才匱乏的問題，其在實時處理三維診斷圖像並取得和專家媲美的準確性方面仍然存在挑戰。 本項目計劃（1）通過整合成像和消融激光到同一探頭中，開發基於OCT成像的診斷功能與治療功能相結合的超緊湊型微針，以實現快速，高分辨率和可量化的三維深腦成像以及高效的病灶消融；（2）開發基於深度學習的全自動高精度三維圖像處理技術，以實現對深層大腦的實時病灶檢測。 擬開發的診療用OCT微針將採用全光纖設計，以實現小於800微米的尺寸和最小的侵入性。該微針將提供小於2 微米的軸向分辨率，以高達每秒20幀的速度進行深腦三維成像。結合高效的近紅外激光，其同時可以實現有效的病灶組織消融。我們將集成此微針到立體定位系統中，並將深度學習算法集成到OCT系統中。我們將在小鼠腦癌模型中驗證此微針的性能。 我們預計OCT微針將可以有效的輔助在深腦中進行的活檢和激光消融手術，其可以引導探頭的準確放置，幫助對病灶進行體內評估，並能夠實時評估消融效果，最終優化對病患的治療效果。

24211020.label: Realisation of objectives
24211020.value: Objective 1: Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 1-6 and conference papers No. 1-4 (please refer to Part C), two patents (US 63/538,716; CN 2024109010426) are related to Aim 1.2. We have developed a portable endoscopic spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) system operating at 800 nm using a custom light source of broad spectrum (Superluminescent diodes, Superlum) and a fast spectrometer offering A-scan speed of 250 kHz (Cobra-S, Wasatch). In addition, we have developed a compact and high-speed fiber-optic rotary joint in order to perform high-speed imaging with a proximal scanning microneedle. This new rotary joint is able to correct the chromatic aberration and achieve one-way throughput >70%, optical coupling variation <±5% during continuous rotation, and back-reflection <-60 dB. With this rotary joint the imaging speed can be improved to up to 20 frames per second. We have successfully developed a new theranostic microneedle to integrate the high-resolution OCT imaging capability with the laser ablation function into one probe while maintaining a highly compact size. Our microneedle adopted a monolithic fiber-optic ball-lens design using a side-viewing halved fiber ball-lens, which is fabricated by utilizing the home-developed liquid shaping technology. To incorporate a near-infrared (NIR, 1,448 nm) laser into the same needle for ablation, we used a coating-striped single-mode fiber (HI780, Corning Inc.). In the needle probe, the bare fiber worked as a double-clad fiber with a single-mode core that transmits and receives OCT light and a multi-mode light-guiding cladding that transmits the NIR ablation laser. The side-viewing halved ball-lens engineered at the distal end of the fiber provided focused and co-registered OCT and NIR laser spots on the tissue. The monolithic fiber-optic imaging/ablation needle was encased in a hypodermic tube of a 360-µm outer diameter (OD) and had a preset rigid length of about 10 to 50 cm. The distal end of the needle was further protected with a glass microcapillary of a 580-µm OD and the rest with a plastic sheath (glued with the microcapillary). The microneedle can rotate freely within the glass microcapillary and the plastic sheath. The measurement of resolution is about 1.7 µm in tissue (2.4 µm in air). Objective 2: Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 4-6 and conference papers No. 1 and 3 (please refer to Part C). Mouse brain cancer model and in vivo imaging protocols were approved by the Animal Ethics Experimentation Committee (AEEC) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Ref No. 20-062-ECS). To test the ability of the microneedle for in vivo cancer detection, 8-week-old immunodeficient male BALB/c nude mice were stereotactically inoculated with brain cancer cells (GBM1A) with coordinates X: 1.5 mm, Y: 1.3 mm, and Z: -1.6 mm based on bregma. We injected approximately 106 GFP labeled GBM1A cells cultured from a patient-derived primary stem cell line, which recapitulates the migratory and invasive behavior of human glioblastoma (GBM). To validate the development of a mouse brain cancer model, GBM1A cells were genetically engineered to express green fluorescent protein (GFP). After four weeks post-inoculation, GFP excitation using ultraviolet (UV) light and detection with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) confirmed successful cancer development in the mouse brain. In an in vivo study on a BALB/c nude mouse, deep-brain volumetric imaging was conducted. Following anesthesia, two 1 mm diameter burr-holes were made in the skull post-scalp incision. A computer-controlled microneedle was inserted through the burr-hole into the mouse brain along a normal trajectory, reaching a depth of approximately 4.5 mm. A 4.5-mm deep-brain cylindrical volume was imaged within 20-25 seconds, generating a 3D color-coded image showcasing detailed brain microstructures such as the cerebral cortex, corpus callosum, caudate putamen, ventral striatum, and thalamus. Notably, OCT images revealed filament bundle structures of striatopallidal fibers in the caudate putamen. To demonstrate the clinical utility of the dual-function microneedle, in vivo laser ablation was performed in a mouse brain followed by on-site evaluation. A laser power of approximately 350 mW was applied for tissue ablation. Deep-brain structures were imaged by advancing the microneedle to a depth of 4.5 mm below the cortical surface, followed by laser ablation. Subsequent histological analysis of the brain tissue confirmed the observed microstructural changes, including tissue cavitation and coagulation areas in the caudate putamen, as depicted in OCT images. Objective 3: Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 7-10 and conference papers No. 5 and 6 (please refer to Part C). We developed an automated assessment model using mouse brain data. The deep-learning neural network employed a novel small data learning approach with Transformer architecture, considering tissue continuity in 3D datasets and limited annotated data. This method reduced reliance on large annotated datasets, utilized unannotated data effectively, captured long-range spatial features, and enabled semantic segmentation of sequential data. To achieve real-time processing, we implemented two strategies: minimizing raw data-to-mask latency and data transfer overhead, and employing novel model compression techniques to balance computation burden and performance. The performance of our automated detection network was evaluated using a test dataset. Results showed high similarity to manually labeled ground truth by an experienced OCT reviewer, with an average IoU of about 0.92 for automated detection of each brain structure in mouse brain. Integrating the deep-learning algorithm into the OCT system enabled brain structure segmentation and cancer detection at over 20 frames per second. Objective 4: Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 6 and conference papers No. 1 and 3 (please refer to Part C). To showcase the microneedle's capability for in vivo evaluation of deep brain lesions in a mouse model of orthotopic GBM, we conducted imaging procedures. Volumetric OCT imaging was performed on both hemispheres of the brain to examine cancerous tissues in real-time. Cancerous brain tissues were successfully identified in the OCT dataset obtained from the right hemisphere using a 4.4-mm microneedle insertion depth, whereas no cancerous lesions were observed in the left hemisphere. The detailed brain microstructures and cancer distribution depicted in the OCT images were corroborated by corresponding H&E micrographs. With the advanced high-resolution imaging capability, we have developed a head-mounted stereotactic system for precise placement of laser probes and optimal planning for ablation in situ. By co-localizing the ablation laser and imaging beam, we are able to perform real-time guided ablation procedures. Using the stereotactic microneedle system, we initially imaged the brain by inserting the microneedle to a depth of 4.5 mm below the cortical surface. Subsequently, the stereotactic system positioned the microneedle near the lesions for the ablation procedure. Ablation was conducted along a linear path by retracting the microneedle at a rate of 0.05 mm/s. Following this, the microneedle was advanced to the caudate putamen and rotated approximately 180 degrees within the glass microcapillary. A focal ablation was then performed using a docked needle with an exposure time of 2 seconds. Immediate in situ imaging was carried out post-ablation to assess the efficacy of the procedure.

24211020.label: Major findings and research outcome
24211020.value: The major research outcome includes 10 published journal papers, 6 conference papers, and two patents (please refer to Part C). The major findings include: (1) successful development of novel OCT imaging system at 800 nm achieving ultrahigh axial resolution of 1.7 µm (in tissue) and fast A-scan speed up to 250 kHz (versus conventional speed of 100 kHz); (2) successful development of a compact rotary joint to enable high-speed endoscopic OCT imaging up to 20 frames per second, a critical feature for in vivo imaging study; (3) successful development of a theranostic microneedle of 580 µm in diameter to integrate the high-resolution OCT imaging capability with the laser ablation function into one probe; (4) successful development of mouse brain cancer model using the stereotactical inoculation of brain cancer cells into mouse brain; (5) successful validation of the dual-function microneedle for in vivo imaging of brain structures and brain cancer in mouse brain cancer model, the laser ablation of brain tissue was further demonstrated using the microneedle; (6) successfully development of the transformer based small data learning method for detection of brain structures with an accuracy comparable to the experienced OCT reviewers, with an average IoU of about 0.92 in mouse brain; (7) integrating the deep-learning algorithm into the OCT system enabling brain structure segmentation and cancer detection at over 20 frames per second, which is faster than the imaging speed. Such an inference speed enables real time application; (8) We developed a head-mounted stereotactic system for precise microneedle placement and optimal ablation planning in deep brain regions. Additionally, we conducted a pilot study using a mouse model to demonstrate image-guided ablation.

24211020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24211020.value: For the next phase of the project: 1. We aim to enhance the deep-learning algorithm for real-time integration into the OCT system, focusing on model compression and hardware acceleration to improve inference speed. 2. We intend to develop an AI copilot method to automate stereotactic microneedle placement in deep brain regions using intraoperative MRI guidance. This will optimize the clinical utility of the microneedle system and facilitate its seamless integration into clinical workflows. 3. While we have met our technological objectives, further validation of the microneedle system in preclinical settings is needed. We plan to conduct additional preclinical studies in pig models to validate the functionality, safety, and clinical potential of the developed microneedle system.

24211020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24211020.value: This research project seeks to enhance the diagnosis and treatment of deep-seated brain lesions, such as cancer. Current methods involve stereotactic biopsy for diagnosis and laser surgery for treatment. However, the current imaging techniques used have limitations in providing detailed high-resolution images of these lesions in situ. The project has developed a small microneedle capable of capturing high-resolution images and delivering laser treatment directly to affected tissues in the deep brain. This minimally invasive tool enables real-time diagnosis and treatment of brain lesions with precision. Additionally, a deep learning algorithm aids in interpreting these images swiftly and accurately. By integrating advanced imaging technology with artificial intelligence, this project aims to transform the approach to diagnosing and treating deep-brain lesions. Ultimately, this innovation has the potential to significantly enhance patient care and outcomes by equipping doctors with improved tools for treatment decision-making.

24304920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24304920.value: 21世紀最重大的挑戰之一是構築清潔低碳的能源體系。 “液態陽光”利用水和可再生電能將二氧化碳轉化為易於存儲和運輸的液體燃料，從而構築成一個平衡的碳循環體系，以達到碳減排的目的。其中，乙醇作為一種高能量密度（26.8 MJ / kg）的二氧化碳還原的產物，引起了廣泛的關注。 當前對此過程的機理研究仍在初期階段，這阻礙了二氧化碳轉化為乙醇技術的應用。該領域面臨的主要挑戰描述如下： （i）乙烯對乙醇的選擇性未知。乙烯和乙醇都是十二個電子還原形成的產物，其反應路徑有許多共同中間體。而當前的大量研究表明，二氧化碳還原到乙烯的選擇性高於乙醇。 （ii）CO2轉化為乙醇的電流密度和效率通常較低。為了達到技術經濟的實用水平，建議CO2還原反應的電流密度至少需達到-100 mA / cm2。 （iii）當前電化學轉化CO2的常用鹼性條件下產品損失嚴重。 在該項目中，我們將深入了解乙烯對乙醇的選擇性，並在酸性條件下提供CO2到乙醇的基準性能，以進一步開發工業應用。具體來說，我們將（i）引入新的自由度-表面吸附氫，以了解在Cu基催化劑上二氧化碳對乙烯/乙醇的選擇性，（ii）開發原位電化學表徵技術以探測界面pH值，以提供直接的實驗依據研究CO2-乙醇的機理，並且（iii）在酸性條件下及高電流密度下將CO2還原成乙醇，從而防止高電流密度下的產品損失。 用電化學方法將二氧化碳轉化為乙醇是將CO2轉化為有價值的液體燃料的有前途的技術。較低的選擇性和效率限制了該技術的發展。了解反應機理並提供合適的工作條件對於解決這些問題至關重要。該項目將（i）揭示電化學CO2還原為乙醇的機理，（ii）開發合理的催化劑設計以提高乙醇生產效率，以及（iii）在酸性條件下以可觀的商業水平實現乙醇生產。

24304920.label: Realisation of objectives
24304920.value: The details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. Objective 1: We conducted mechanistic studies focusing on the effects of the local environment and catalyst development on CO₂ reduction. Product selectivity was found to be significantly influenced by the composition of the electrolyte, particularly the K:Na ratio. This is attributed to changes in the local electronic environment caused by adsorbed alkali metal ions, a phenomenon observed across various metallic catalysts where surface adsorption of cations is unavoidable. Additionally, the surface concentration of active sites was found to play a crucial role in determining the reaction pathway, affecting whether CO₂ is converted into single-carbon or multi-carbon products. Under acidic conditions, the availability of protons further altered the selectivity of the electrochemical CO₂ reduction reaction (CO₂RR), highlighting the importance of proton concentration in product formation. 2. Objective 2: With the aid of computational calculations, we screened a series of Cu-based bimetallic catalysts (X-Cu, where X = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re, Fe, Ru, Co, Rh, Ir, Ni, Pt, and Pd) to identify candidates with a strong affinity for CO*. This aimed to enhance local CO concentration by suppressing hydrogen evolution (HER). A scaling relation between ∆G_OCCOH* and ∆G_OCCOH* − ∆G_CHO* was established, identifying Pd-Cu as the most promising catalyst for CO₂RR in acidic environments. Based on this, we synthesized a series of Pd-Cu catalysts using the galvanic exchange reaction, precisely controlling Pd content between 4–8%. 3. Objective 3: To understand the impact of the local environment on product distribution, we employed multiphysics modelling to characterize interfacial pH changes as a function of bulk pH and applied current density. The results demonstrated that interfacial pH is governed by the balance between consumption (electrochemical reaction) and supply (bulk pH). Strongly acidic conditions accelerated HER on Cu-based catalysts, while conditions near-neutral pH (≥4) led to complete depletion of CO₂ in the diffusion layer. Mildly acidic conditions were found to balance interfacial pH, mitigating carbonate formation while maintaining CO₂ availability. We also developed in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) to enable rapid gas product characterization during CO₂RR. With a response time of less than 1 second (versus 15 minutes for conventional GC methods in our lab), DEMS provided critical feedback on activity and selectivity, greatly enhancing our ability to study interfacial pH and product distribution in real time. 4. Objective 4: Building on the above findings, we developed flow cell reactors optimized for CO₂RR under mildly acidic conditions. These reactors overcame the limits of CO₂ mass transport and the high proton concentration typically encountered in traditional H-cell systems. By creating an alkaline interface within an acidic bulk environment, we achieved high CO₂ conversion to multi-carbon products and alcohols under industrially relevant conditions. This approach successfully balanced reactivity, selectivity, and operational stability, demonstrating the potential for scalable and practical CO₂RR technologies.

24304920.label: Major findings and research outcome
24304920.value: This research project has been successfully completed by our group, focusing on CO₂ reduction reaction (CO₂RR) in acidic environments. Key areas of investigation included catalyst development, reaction mechanisms, and device stability, resulting in 9 high-quality publications in prestigious journals, including a "Top Downloaded Article," a contribution to a "Rising Star" Special Issue, and one in Nature Catalysis. These outcomes have significantly advanced the understanding of CO₂RR under acidic conditions. Despite challenges from the Covid-19 pandemic, the project also contributed to the training of 1 PhD student and led to 5 invited conferences/talks, further showcasing its impact. The main findings are summarized below: 1. Influence of Reaction Conditions and Electrolyte Effects: The effect of reaction conditions, particularly the electrolyte environment, on the selectivity and activity of CO₂ reduction in acid was systematically investigated using various catalysts. These studies revealed the critical role of electrolyte composition and pH in governing product selectivity and reaction efficiency. The findings provided foundational insights into optimizing reaction conditions for acidic CO₂ reduction systems. (ChemCatChem, 2022, e202200052, Top Downloaded Articles in 2022) 2. Development of Cu-Based Bimetallic Catalysts for CO₂RR in Acid: Pd-Cu bimetallic catalysts were synthesized, achieving 89% Faradaic efficiency for C₂+ products at 500 mA/cm² with a CO₂ utilization more than 60%. The Faradaic efficiency for alcohol production reached nearly 40%, and product crossover was significantly reduced. Computational modeling using COMSOL revealed that mildly acidic conditions (pH 2) provided an optimal balance between carbon utilization efficiency and activity/selectivity towards C₂+ products. (Nature Catalysis, 2022, 5, 564). 3. Active Site Dispersity and Product Selectivity: Monodispersed Cu catalysts were synthesized to investigate the relationship between active site dispersity and C₂+ product formation. It was found that increased dispersity of active sites led to a decrease in C₂+ product selectivity, emphasizing the importance of catalyst structure in guiding reaction pathways. (Energy & Fuels, 2023, 37, 8707, featured in the 2023 Energy & Fuels Rising Star Special Issue.) 4. Development of Online Differential Electrochemical Mass Spectroscopy (DEMS): A novel online DEMS technique was developed to monitor product distribution during high-current-density CO₂RR (1.25 A/cm²) under acidic conditions. The study revealed that the evolution of the reaction interface, influenced by operational modes (pause vs. constant electrolysis), significantly impacted reaction selectivity and stability. (Materials Reports: Energy, 2022, 100173).

24304920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24304920.value: This project successfully demonstrated the electrochemical reduction of CO₂ to multicarbon products and alcohols under acidic conditions with industrially relevant performance, showing significant potential for scale-up. Mechanistic studies revealed that the local chemical environment (electrolyte composition and interfacial pH) and catalyst design are critical in determining the reaction pathway. In acidic systems, enhancing local CO concentration by suppressing local H is particularly vital. Our online analysis method provided high time resolution to monitor selectivity and activity changes during electrolysis, offering valuable insights into electrode evolution. However, challenges remain for long-term operation. While carbonate formation was suppressed in mildly acidic conditions, it could not be fully avoided during extended electrolysis, leading to device failure. Future research should investigate whether CO₂RR to target products can be achieved in strong acidic environments (pH = 0), where carbonate formation can be completely eliminated. Additionally, while the flow reactor achieved high current densities (>500 mA/cm²), the produced liquid products were highly diluted due to the large electrolyte volumes used, leading to high energy costs in downstream separation. Exploring alternative reactor designs, such as solid-state electrolyzers or membrane electrode assemblies, could enable more concentrated liquid products and improve energy efficiency during scale-up.

24304920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24304920.value: Carbon dioxide (CO₂), a major greenhouse gas, is both a challenge and an opportunity for sustainable energy systems. Converting CO₂ into valuable liquid fuels, such as ethanol, offers a promising solution to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions while addressing global energy demands. However, the process of electrochemical CO₂ reduction (CO2RR) under acidic conditions for industrial applications, faces significant challenges in low efficiency, poor selectivity and durability. This project successfully demonstrated significant advancements in the CO₂RR under acidic conditions. By combining advanced catalyst design with online analysis techniques, we quantitatively measured the effects of local chemical environments, such as electrolyte composition and interfacial pH, on the reaction pathways. We discovered that mildly acidic conditions strike a critical balance between reducing carbonate formation and maintaining reaction efficiency. Furthermore, we developed acidic flow reactor that enabled high CO₂ conversion rates to multi-carbon products and alcohols at industrially relevant current densities. This study enhances our fundamental understanding of CO₂ reduction mechanisms in complex environments. It provides valuable guidelines for designing next-generation catalysts and reactor systems, paving the way for scalable CO₂ utilization technologies to address climate change and support renewable energy systems.

24500520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500520.value: The objective of this project is to build a structural model to analyze market structure in a product category by leveraging online consumer search data and aggregate market share data corresponding to products in that category. Recent approaches to recovering the competitive structure underlying a market have typically required temporal variation in product attributes and aggregate market share or individual level panel data on brand choices. Such methods would, however, pose a challenge when the product categories have small, if any, temporal variations in product attributes and/or long period of time between purchases. For example, in the automobile industry, a model’s features are invariant in a given model year. If the information on products’ features is available only for a short period of time (e.g. few months), there will be no temporal variation in product attributes to help researchers infer the market structure. Also, even if researches have access to individual panel data, the long inter-purchase times can affect the validity of the market structure derived from the panel information. For instance, as car purchases take place once every several years, consumers can have changes in their incomes, preferences, etc. between one purchase and the next. To overcome such challenges, this project proposes an approach that combines aggregate market share data (that fully reflect brand performance in the market) with individual consumer’s online search data collected close to the time of purchase (that capture the "consideration sets" of consumers). The sequential search algorithm proposed by Weitzman (1979) is employed to rationalize consumers' observed search sequences. Predicted choices from this model are then aggregated to provide the analog to observed market shares in the data. This project makes two important methodological contributions: (i) a new simulated maximum likelihood estimation method and (ii) flexibility that allows consumers to search for a subset of product characteristics and idiosyncratic match values. Simulation studies demonstrate that (i) the proposed method can recover the true parameter values and (ii) the market structure generating the data cannot be recovered if the search process is ignored. Next, the proposed model will be applied to search and market share data from the SUV market—a sub-market of the US automobile industry. Taken together, this project makes a substantive contribution in terms of understanding market structure for long inter-purchase time product categories, while providing useful methodological tools for researchers interested in estimating the parameters of sequential search models.

24500520.label: Realisation of objectives
24500520.value: 1. We have devised a new framework of sequential search model by converting it into a two-stage problem. In the first stage, consumers scroll down the product list they have received as a result of their search queries, and in the second stage, they make the search decisions according to the sequential search model among products that have been scrolled through. We are currently preparing an academic journal article with the new framework. 2. We have successfully devised a new likelihood-based method to estimate the sequential search model, and the academic paper has been accepted by Quantitative Marketing and Economics. 3. We have successfully devised an estimation strategy that allows researchers to recover parameters of interest even when the search sequence is not available to researchers by incorporating the expectation-maximization algorithm. 4. We have sucessfully examined the distortion in understanding the market structure when the consideration set formation is not considered in the modeling approach. 5. The proposed model and estimation strategy successfully produce a perceptual map that represents the competitive relationship among brands (or products) perceived by consumers. 6. The proposed model and estimation strategy is capable of calculating the value of carrying a particular brand name.

24500520.label: Major findings and research outcome
24500520.value: The major finding of this project so far is that we have proposed a new estimation staretgy for the sequential search model which was proposed by Weitzman and is popular in modeling the online consumer search behavior. In the published paper, we show that the proposed modeling approach and estimation strategy 1) produce parameter estimates that are better in terms of bias and spread than other existing estimation strategies and 2) approximates the true probabilities of consumers' search and purchase decisions better than existing estimation methods, and 3) produces the final model estimates faster than existing methods. Another major finding is that we show that the market structure of a product category can be inferred from online search data. The traditional market structure analysis approaches rely on the switching behavior recorded in a purchase history of a panel of consumers. Such a reliance implies that the data must have multiple purchase occassions per consumer and rather frequent switches made by consumers in order for the market structure to be inferred. However, many product categories fail to satisfy these requirements due to their nature. For instance, the time interval between two consecutive purchase occasions may be so long that the sample period is too short to record multiple purchases by a consumer. We find that, in such cases, the consumer search data contain the cross-sectional switchings by consumers and that researchers can elicit the consumer preferences to brands. By imposing a factor structure on the brand preferences of consumers, we can visualize the market structure of a product category even when the category fails to satisfy the aforementioned requirements.

24500520.value: Based on the new method, we are working on two additional projects--1) incorporating consumers' scroll decisions in the model and 2) performaing the market structure analysis with online search data. We expect to complete submission to top academic journals by the end of this year.

24500520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24500520.value: This project contributes to the consumer search literature by proposing a new estimation method that will help researchers better understand consumers' online search behavior. As this is an estimation method, we expect a number of ensuing research outputs based on this project. This project will prove valuable because the proposed method performs better than other existing estimation methods.

24502020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502020.value: 從理論上講，企業在面對外部挑戰時會進行重組。對於企業而言，特別重要的挑戰是技術變革會影響現有資源。一些現有資源可能會失去其價值，而另一些資源可能會越來越重要。重組是公司應對現有資源挑戰的一種方式。 我專注於一種重要的資源類型：互補資產。創新商品化需要補充性資產。補充資產包括有助於重點創新的分銷，服務，營銷，銷售和最終使用的資源。 該項目的目的是調查在補充資產演變過程中進行的公司重組是否以及如何影響公司績效。

24502020.label: Realisation of objectives
24502020.value: All the intended project objectives have been achieved. A brief overview of the specifics of these four objectives is given below. OBJECTIVE 1: Dataset development Particularly, two principal datasets have been developed. (I) First, publicly available sources were consulted to identify global telecom companies. A list of 89 companies was put together by going through public sources like Wikipedia, GSMA, and Gartner analyst reports. For these companies, detailed information on M&A deals by telecom operators was collected using the Orbis Global database provided by Bureau van Dijk. (II) Second, a subscription to the GSMA Intelligence data was purchased. Using this access, I was able to create a dataset with comprehensive information about global mobile operators from more than 150 countries across the world. I also extracted annual reports and analyst call transcripts available on the GSMA intelligence platform. Overall, a comprehensive dataset on restructuring activity, performance, and mobile applications has been developed for MNOs across the world. The coverage of this dataset includes the population of all GSM operators in the world. The time horizon is from 2000 to 2021. ----------------- OBJECTIVE 2. To study the effects of complementary assets on corporate restructuring. This objective has been achieved. The findings have been developed into a research paper on how an MNO's market share shapes its MVNO strategy. Brief explanation: An MVNO is a firm that neither has its own licensed radio spectrum, nor the entire infrastructure required to provide mobile telephone services. Instead, an MVNO uses the capacity shared by an operator. The MVNO develops its own brand and sales channels to sell mobile services. Mobile operators earn revenue by hosting MVNOs on their networks. Importantly, a mobile operator retains control over its own network resource when it hosts an MVNO. Moreover, an operator continues to sell mobile services using the same network. An investigation into industry articles revealed that a central issue in the restructuring of MNOs, especially in the years after the rise of smartphones, was whether or not to host an MVNO. Furthermore, a literature survey on the extant strategy research on MNOs suggests that MNO market share in a given location is an accepted measure of the MNO's stock of complementary assets in that location. Thus, complementary assets were operationalized in terms of an MNO's market share in a given location (country or territory). This measure for complementary assets has been used in prior research on mobile operators. An empirical study on the effect of an MNO scale on its MVNO strategy was undertaken and completed. ----------------- OBJECTIVE 3: To study the moderating influence of a firm's institutional environment. This project objective has been achieved. Brief explanation: The empirical model in objective (2) was extended to conduct this analysis. Different relevant measures for the institutional environment, in the context of MNOs, were considered and tested. The analysis reinforced the findings from the second project objective. In particular, a key aspect of the institutional environment that affects MVNO hosting is the strength of contracting institutions in a country. I accessed data from the World Bank to construct measures of the contracting environment in every country of our dataset. I tested the moderating influence of the institutional environment on the scale-hosting relationship. Thus, this moderating variable allowed for the completion of objective 3. ----------------- OBJECTIVE 4: Restructuring and firm performance This project objective was successfully completed. Brief explanation: A key finding is that the location of existing capabilities can be a particularly important complementary asset in shaping the influence of restructuring on sales growth.

24502020.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502020.value: ***MAJOR FINDINGS*** 1. Mobile operator scale is positively associated with the likelihood of MVNO hosting. Conceptually this finding shows that a firm's prior investments in complementary assets for the product market play an important role in shaping its subsequent resource allocations to the factor market. 2. The scale effect is strengthened by the scope of a mobile operator's operations. 3. The scale effect is strengthened by mobile number portability regulations in a country. Moreover, the scale effect is weakened by the contracting environment in a country. Both results show that institutional conditions are important. 4. For multinational companies, the impact of restructuring on sales growth depends on the location at which firms have invested in complementary assets. ***RESEARCH OUTCOME*** Working papers: - “When do Firms Care to Share? An Examination of Resource Sharing Beyond Firm Boundaries”, co-authored with Rama Devarakonda (Tilburg University); This paper was submitted to the Special issue on Resource Allocation in the Strategic Management Journal. However, it was rejected after review. The paper is currently being revised for submission to Organization Science. 24502020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502020.value: The strength of the data collected allows for multiple research questions to be tested. 1. Since this is a global dataset, it offers an opportunity for comparing the strategies of MNC operators versus domestic operators. A potential research question is to study the variation in MVNO strategies in MNC operators versus domestic operators. 2. Mobile operators have been very important during the COVID-19 pandemic. One potential study is to examine the variation in mobile operators' performance during the COVID-19 shock. Anecdotal evidence suggests that mobile operators in emerging markets may be done better during COVID-19. However, there is no systematic empirical study yet. This study can also help us develop theory about how firms adapt to exogenous shocks.

24502020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502020.value: Building a mobile network is very expensive for companies. Therefore mobile operators (e.g. AT&T, PCCW, China Mobile, etc.) need a sound strategy for how to make money from their large investments in networks. The challenge is that it is often difficult to make more money from directly selling services to customers. This project studies how mobile network operators facing such a situation make money from their investments in networks. Through this project, we gain important managerial insights into how firms manage resources during their growth. Firms need resources to grow, but they frequently obtain more resources than they need. The firm's managers thus face the question of how to use these excess resources. Sometimes, managers can use excess resources for internal growth. But managers may not do so to avoid the administrative challenges of managing a larger size of operations. The insights from this project suggest that managers can lease excess resources to other firms rather than using them within the firm. This can be at least a temporary option to monetize the firm's prior investments. For practicing managers, the project suggests that a firm's resource allocation strategy should include an assessment of the opportunity to lease resources to outsiders.

24502720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502720.value: 在經濟危機期間，人們普遍認為不動產抵押貸款證券(MBS)沒有價值。然而，假若 人們繼續持有此證券直至到期日，實則可以大幅獲利。長期以來，金融分析師和政策 制定者一直認定消費者信心低迷是經濟在危機後復蘇緩慢的原因。這指向一個更根本 的問題:為什麼經濟個體會對經濟前景如此悲觀?此外，在現實世界中，家庭收入和 財富均存在巨大的不平等。富人和窮人會對經濟狀況形成不同的信念嗎?這種不平等 會擴大信念對總體波動的影響嗎?信念形成的過程及其與貧富差距的相互作用將會是 答案的核心。 在此項目中，我們首先以實證方式歸納出各類家庭對經濟前景的信念。然後，我們以此事實為據，建立了一個有微觀基礎的經濟周期理論，以提供新的角度來理解信念和貧富差距在推動經濟周期中的作用。 我們從數據可知，富人和窮人家庭都對一年後的失業率感到悲觀。而富裕和貧窮家庭的悲觀情緒與大多數經濟周期波動皆呈反週期關係。同時，富人的悲觀情緒對經濟周期波動的影響亦比窮人更大。由此，我們建立了一個經濟周期模型，而在這模型中，悲觀情緒的變化是由於經濟總體衝擊而內生的。該模型包含兩種類型的家庭:(一)勉強糊口的窮人和(二)不受借貸限制的富人，而這兩種人都是厭惡經濟體中的模棱两可的。由於有經濟提中模稜兩可的存在，厭惡模稜兩可的家庭會對經濟狀況形成悲觀信念，繼而有悲觀行為。在經濟衰退中，隨著消費下降，消費的邊際效用會上升。這意味著經濟波動對家庭造成了更大的代價，由此，所有家庭都進一步變得更加悲觀。此外，由於貧困家庭被排除在資產市場之外，而同時富人擁有企業並控制其生產要素需求，所以不受借貸限制的富人的主觀信念對於經濟總波動有更大的影響。我們的模型側重於對短期經濟的悲觀情緒，而非經濟的長期前景。對於任何總體衝擊，這都會產生非通貨膨脹的總需求的變化，並確保了實際因素的聯動。這項目將為經濟周期的理解提供新的見解以及提供政策建議。

24502720.label: Realisation of objectives
24502720.value: All objectives have been realized. 1. The project aims to document some empirical facts regarding consumers’ or households’ pessimistic beliefs both in the cross-section and in the cyclical behavior. We constructed two time series to measure the level of pessimism among households in the top 20% and bottom 20% income brackets. We conduct a Vector Autoregression (VAR) analysis on a selection of macroeconomic aggregates alongside measures of pessimism for the rich and the poor households from the period 1985:I to 2017:IV. we conduct the principal component analysis at the frequency domain, which "cuts" the data so that each of them corresponds to a Structural VAR (SVAR)-based shock designed to capture the maximum volatility in one variable of interest across a specific frequency range. Through the comparison of the variance contributions and impulse response functions (IRFs) of each SVAR shock, we uncover the business cycle properties of household pessimism in the cross-section. Our empirical analysis shows that in the long run, it is the poor households that are more pessimistic. Moreover, the main business cycle shock, which explains most variations in real quantities, is more connected with the pessimism of the rich, but not much with the pessimism of the poor. As a result, recessions are periods of convergence in the level of pessimism for households in the cross-section of income distribution. The same picture emerges if we target other real quantities, the pessimism of the rich households, or the pessimism of the poor households. 2. The project also plans to set up a fully micro-founded business cycle model to explain the documented facts. We develop a theory of endogenous pessimism that rationalizes the above salient features of the anatomy of business cycle pessimism. The model is otherwise standard except for the assumption that households perceive ambiguity about the income process and are ambiguity averse. Consequently, when faced with ambiguity about future income, households tend to place greater emphasis on models predicting weak income prospects, leading to an endogenous increase in pessimism. More importantly, our theory endogenously maps household heterogeneity into differential levels and cross-sectional distributions in the impulse response functions of pessimism to income shock. Specifically, in addition to the difference in the level of income over the long run, households are allowed to differ in their exposure to the aggregate income shock. Furthermore, To account for the discriminatory treatment of poor households in the financial market, we assume that they are hand-to-mouth (HtM) consumers. In contrast, the rich households, who are unconstrained, can hold risk-free bonds to smooth consumption in response to fluctuations in income. We separate the pessimism of any household into the trend component, i.e., long run pessimism, and the cyclical component, i.e., cyclical pessimism. Our theory of endogenous pessimism predicts that households, who are (1) HtM constrained, (2) with lower income at the non-stochastic steady state, and (3) with larger exposure to the aggregate income shocks, exhibit larger long run pessimism. On the other hand, the cyclical pessimism of those households, who are with (1) a lower level of consumption and (2) higher exposure to aggregate income shock, demonstrates larger counter-cyclical movements, i.e., heightens more after a contractionary aggregate income shock. 3. The project further plans to analyze the quantitative performance of the business cycle models in capturing salient features of aggregate and survey data. We solve the model quantitatively by the method of undetermined coefficients. It is closely related to the log-linearization of the standard DSGE model. The method is very similar to the one employed by Pei (2024) in jointly solving policy function, value function, and endogenous belief distortion due to ambiguity aversion. The additional novelty is that we combine first-order approximation of the policy function with second-order approximation of the value function, which is necessary when the utility function is not log utility and important to capture the endogenous variations in pessimism. We calibrate our model to match the relative income levels between the bottom 20% and top 20% of the income distribution. The quantitative exercise demonstrates that our model predicts relative long-term pessimism and business cycle variations in cyclical pessimism that align with empirical observations. 4. Finally, the welfare cost of business cycles and policy implications are to be analyzed within the DSGE framework extended with our transmission mechanism of endogenous variations in pessimism. We discuss to the extent to which our theory of endogenous pessimism contributes to a new propagation mechanism that mirrors the fluctuations in aggregate demand, in line with the concept of expectation-driven business cycles. The fluctuations in overall economic activity inherently lead to an increase in pessimism among households, which consequently amplifies the welfare cost of business cycles. Additionally, we delve into the implications for policy design. Whether in productivity-driven business cycles like the recent COVID-19 crisis or financial-friction-driven business cycles such as the financial crisis, our theory underscores the significance of managing expectations during crises. In such scenarios, restoring confidence among households may hold greater importance than merely focusing on repairing their balance sheets.

24502720.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502720.value: On the empirical front, this project first documents that in the long run poor households are more pessimistic than rich households about the outlook of the economy. Along the business cycles, macroeconomic data extended with measures of the pessimism of the rich and poor households admits a non-inflationary aggregate demand shock in explaining most variations in real quantities and the pessimism of rich households, whereas its impact on the pessimism of lower-income households is less pronounced. Furthermore, the pessimism of richer households displays more pronounced counter-cyclical fluctuations in response to business cycles. It provides additional insights into understanding the driving forces of business cycles through the cross-sectional distribution of households' pessimism. On the theory front, this project develops a theory of endogenous pessimism, where income fluctuations drive cyclical variations in household pessimism across different income brackets. Our theoretical framework can quantitatively replicate the documented empirical variations in household pessimism across various income groups. Our theory contributes a common propagation mechanism for all types of structural shocks, suggesting that the dominant non-inflationary aggregate demand shock driving business cycles may be a combination of structural shocks rather than an exotic one. It provides new insights into understanding the importance of expectation management. Restoring confidence serves as an important policy target during the recession. All the above mentions results and contributions have been collected in the research paper attached in Part C.

24502720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502720.value: Understanding how households deviate from rational expectations serves as an important research frontier of modern theoretical macroeconomics. This research project belongs to this sub-field of research. However, due to the limitation of data, almost all works focus on documenting empirical facts using survey data on expectations and then proceed to delve into the theory to comprehend the implications of any identified anomalies in expectation formation. To fully understand the mapping from pessimism to economic decisions, it would be ideal if we could merge survey data on expectation with population census on households' consumption, asset holding, and occupation choices. Enhancing this research project could lead to a broader range of theoretical predictions that offer valuable insights in this area. It is worth noting that the Danish census possesses the capability to link households' expectations with their actual decisions. If access to this dataset can be obtained, the current project has the potential to be expanded further, moving towards a HANK-style approach that reveals the business cycle characteristics of households' pessimism even at the micro level.

24502720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502720.value: There is widespread recognition that households' subjective beliefs about the economic outlook often differ from the rational expectations (RE) projections, with a tendency towards increased pessimism compared to professional forecasters. In an economy characterized by substantial income inequality, an intriguing question arises: Do wealthy and less affluent households demonstrate similar deviations from rational expectations, or do their perspectives diverge significantly? On the empirical front, we present evidence indicating that poor households tend to be more pessimistic in the long run. However, it is the rich households, whose pessimism is more closely linked to business cycles. During economic recessions, both rich and poor households experience increased pessimism, with rich households exhibiting a more pronounced response. Consequently, recessions are characterized by heightened pessimism across all households, leading to a convergence of pessimism levels among households in different income brackets. We propose a theory to explain the cross-sectional differences in the trend and cyclical components of household pessimism. The theory emphasizes the significance of expectation management, suggesting that restoring confidence is a crucial policy objective during a crisis. Furthermore, it implies that targeting rich households for expectation management policies may be more effective.

24504520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24504520.value: 在過去的幾十年中，許多國家的房價持續上漲，住房財富可以被認為是家庭資產中最重要的部分。因此，研究房價上漲如何影響家庭消費具有非常重要的意義。最近的實證研究提出了不同的證據：一些研究表明在美國經歷了房價上漲之後，家庭的日常消費增加了（Campbell and Cocco，2007; Mian et al。，2013），而一些研究表明價格上漲導致消極的消費反應（Waxman et al。，2019）和生產率下降（Gu et al。，2018）。然而，由於難以識別財富衝擊是外生且始料未及的，很少有文獻研究 居民消費對這種財富衝擊的反應（Jappelli和Pistaferri，2010； Agarwal和Qian，2014）。為了填補研究空白，在本項目中，我們使用2016年10月至2018年12月來自中國最大的電子商務網站的交易數據研究住房財富增值對個人網絡消費的影響。該項目研究了中國獨特的製度環境並使用了中國最新的經濟特區雄安新區的公告，作為對土地和房價的外來衝擊。該項目关注四个研究问题：首先，我們研究外生的財富衝擊是否會影響家庭的在線消費。更具體地說，我們研究家庭是否由於資產增值而增加消费。其次，我們研究财富冲击是否会对消費模式的變化有長期持續的影响。第三，我們研究潛在的財富衝擊的影響機制， 如消費模式，行為和工作態度。特別是，我們測研究財富衝擊是否會產生怠工行為或養成不健康的消費習慣，例如多喝酒和香煙。此外，獨特的政策設置使我們能夠區分升值對可出售資產和不可出售資產的消費行為。

24504520.label: Realisation of objectives
24504520.value: Objective 1: The project achieved this objective by analyzing the impact of the unexpected announcement of the Xiong'an New Area in China on housing prices and online consumption patterns. Using comprehensive datasets from China's largest e-commerce platforms, we examined individual-level online transactions to provide robust evidence. Our findings showed that the housing wealth shock led to significant increases in online consumer spending, particularly in discretionary categories. Realizable wealth had a more pronounced impact on consumption than unrealizable wealth, especially for homeowners with multiple properties. Objective 2: We provided strong empirical evidence supporting the prediction that unanticipated wealth shocks lead to positive consumption responses. By exploiting the exogenous nature of the Xiong'an announcement and unique housing policies, we observed significant increases in online spending among affected households. These findings were presented at high-profile conferences and submitted to top academic journals. Objective 3: We achieved this objective by using detailed transaction data, including demographic and geographical information. Machine learning-based analyses were conducted to profile consumers and predict their demographic and socio-economic characteristics. We also collaborated with a large Multi-Channel Network company in Hangzhou to update the model in real-time with new data on consumer behavior and preferences. This collaboration aims to offer businesses a more accurate and timely way to predict consumer preferences, ultimately increasing customer satisfaction, loyalty, and sales revenue. Objective 4: The study thoroughly examined the heterogeneity of consumption responses by categorizing goods into various types and analyzing the responses of different household types, including homeowners versus renters, and locals versus new immigrants. Objective 5: The research findings have significant implications for policymakers and firms. Policymakers can use these insights to design policies that mitigate potential negative effects on consumption. For firms, the study provides valuable information on consumer behavior in response to wealth shocks, enabling better targeting and marketing strategies in the online retail sector. The project successfully met its main goals, offering insights into how changes in housing wealth affect online shopping behavior. We overcame challenges such as ensuring the reliability of our findings and addressing data limitations through thorough analysis. Our research papers are currently under review and will soon be published, helping to disseminate our findings and apply them in policy and business contexts. Future research will build on this work, exploring new areas and deepening our understanding of what drives changes in consumer spending when housing wealth changes.

24504520.label: Major findings and research outcome
24504520.value: The paper titled “Housing Wealth and Online Consumer Behavior: Evidence from Xiong'an New Area in China” is available in the NBER Working Paper Series No. 30465. We presented this paper at several seminars in different universities and conferences from 2021 to 2023 to gather feedback from experts. The project has produced two additional research papers, which are currently under review in peer-reviewed academic journals: 1. “From Unrealizable Dreams to Realizable Wealth: Distinguishing Housing Wealth Effects on Consumption”, under review at the American Economic Review – Insights - This paper examines the impact of an unanticipated housing wealth shock on online consumption using a proprietary dataset. Exploiting the exogenous variation in housing price appreciation across counties due to unexpected policy announcements, we employed a DID approach to analyze consumption responses in counties with (C3) and without (C9) transaction restrictions, using C37 as the control group. Our findings indicate that the ability to realize housing wealth significantly influences consumption behavior. The study differentiates between realizable and unrealizable wealth effects, providing insights into how the capacity to liquidate assets impacts spending. The dataset’s rich information allowed us to categorize consumers by the number of properties owned and examine their differential responses to the wealth shock. This research enriches the literature on online consumption, establishes a causal relationship between housing wealth and spending, and highlights the distinct effects of realizable versus unrealizable wealth. 2. “The Impact of Temporary Price Shocks on Consumer Behaviors and Store Performance: Evidence from China”, under review at the Journal of Urban Economics - We analyzed consumer and store responses to price shocks during Alibaba's Singles' Day and JD's 6.18 Mid-Year Shopping Festival in China. Using detailed online consumption data from January 2017 to December 2018, we observed increased spending, a preference for discounted products, and a surge in return orders during these events. Spending per order increased during the festivals but decreased before and after, leading to an overall rise in consumption. Consumers showed significant increases in shirking propensity, especially during Singles' Day. On the supply side, stores experienced higher sales but faced challenges like increased return orders and excessive discounts, impacting profitability, particularly for smaller stores. There was a positive correlation between discount amount and sales performance, presenting a dilemma for stores balancing discounts and profitability. Our findings suggest that shopping festivals do not uniformly benefit all consumers and stores, highlighting the need for targeted approaches to ensure equitable benefits. This study provides valuable insights for policymakers and businesses on managing online promotions effectively.

24504520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24504520.value: The current research focuses exclusively on online consumption data, which may limit the external validity of the findings as it excludes in-person transactions and is based on a specific sample. To address this limitation, future research will aim to broaden the scope of the study. One proposed course of action is to incorporate both online and offline consumption data to provide a more comprehensive analysis of consumer behavior. This approach will help validate the findings across different transaction types and offer a more holistic view of the impact of housing wealth on consumption. Additionally, expanding the research to explore the housing wealth across the entire country will provide deeper insights into regional variations and enhance the generalizability of the results. By examining a diverse set of geographic locations and economic contexts, the study can offer more robust conclusions that are applicable on a national scale.

24504520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24504520.value: This research project examines how changes in housing wealth affect online shopping habits. Using data from major e-commerce platforms in China, we analyzed how the unexpected announcement of the Xiong'an New Area influenced housing prices and online spending. Our findings show that when housing prices rise, people spend more online, especially on non-essential items. This effect is stronger for those who can sell their homes to access the increased wealth. In a separate study, we examined how temporary discounts during major shopping festivals impact consumer behavior and store performance. We found that while spending increases during these events, there are also more return orders and challenges for smaller stores due to heavy discounting. Our research has produced two papers currently under review in top academic journals and has been presented at high-profile conferences and seminars. We collaborate with industry partners to model how real-time transaction data can predict consumer preferences and demand. These insights are valuable for policymakers and businesses. Policymakers can design better housing and economic policies, while businesses can develop more effective marketing strategies. Future research will include both online and offline shopping data and explore regional differences across China for a more comprehensive understanding of consumer behavior.

24601320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24601320.value: 十九世紀大英帝國流浪法的輸出與演變：從加勒比海到香港

24601320.label: Project Objectives
24601320.value: To explore the imposition of vagrancy laws across the British Empire, how vagrancy law frameworks were drafted and implemented differently across contexts and over time, and the extent to which those developments were linked to developments in professional police services. To investigate similarities in the manner and extent to which the pejorative legal categorizations embedded in vagrancy laws were applied both to the poor in Britain as well as to colonial subjects, and to foreground the legacy of these legal and ideological frames. To consider the purposes to which vagrancy law frameworks were put historically, and the debates and controversies surrounding their implementation, with the aim of better elucidating the underlying aims of such laws considered in broad, transnational historical perspective. To produce material that will support the production of a more comprehensive book project, examining the evolution of public order legality in the nineteenth century British Empire more broadly. To cast greater light on the problematic origins of key features of contemporary criminal law regimes around the world, with the aim of supporting progressive law reform.
