24601320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24601320.value: During the long nineteenth century, two developments occurred simultaneously. First, the British Empire dramatically expanded across the globe. Second, the structure of British law and governance was dramatically reformed, across many areas. While both of these developments have been widely observed, their close interrelationship has not been adequately explored to date. My research aims to address this shortcoming. In particular, my past and ongoing research focuses on the evolution of public order laws and institutions in Britain and the British Empire over the course of the long nineteenth century. Work I have already done has explored the manner in which colonial legality evolved out of emergency law regimes, leading to the incorporation of various aspects of exceptional legality into everyday legal contexts (Roberts, 2019), as well as the manner in which the repressive tools of the British state expanded dramatically in response to progressive activism in the late eighteenth century (Roberts, 2020). Currently, I am exploring the manner in which approaches to public order governance developed between 1800 and 1900 in Britain, including through the development of a more modern, professionalized police service, as well as through new laws governing and penalizing ‘vagrancy’ and similar categories. My proposed new project will build on this past work. In particular, the aim of the project is to explore the manner in which the vagrancy law model that developed in England was exported to the British colonial world, how the model changed over time, and how developments in the colonial context reflected back on experiences in Britain in turn. In that context, the research will explore the implementation of vagrancy laws in the Caribbean and Mauritius, Ceylon, Ireland, India, the Cape Colony, the Straits Settlements, the East African Protectorate, Northern Nigeria, and Hong Kong. As well as examining similarities and differences amongst these laws, their aims and modes of enforcement, and the manner in which approaches to ‘vagrancy' evolved over time, the research will also consider the connections between those laws and the development of key public order institutions, including the police in particular, as well as exploring the different ideologies relied upon to justify those laws. Ultimately, the aim is both to produce scholarship that will reframe debates about the nature of public order law and the role of the colonial experience in the shaping of that law, as well as to contribute to contemporary efforts towards progressive legal reform. 在漫長的十九世紀，兩種發展同時發生。首先，大英帝國在全球範圍內迅速擴張。其次，英國的法律和治理結構在許多領域進行了重大變革。雖然這兩項發展已得到廣泛的關注，但迄今尚未充分探討它們之間的密切相互關係。我的研究旨在解決這一缺點。 特別是，我過去和現在的研究重點是在漫長的十九世紀中，英國和大英帝國公共秩序法律和制度的演變。我已經完成了探討從緊急狀態法進化出來的殖民的合法性政權，導致異常合法性擴展到日常法律語境的各個方面(罗伯茨,2019)，以及英國的專制工具為應對在十八世紀晚期的進步運動的急劇擴大(罗伯茨,2020)的工作。目前，我正在探索1800年到1900年英國公共秩序治理方法的發展方式，包括通過發展一個更現代、更專業化的警察服務，以及通過管理和懲罰“流浪”和類似類別的新法律。 我提出的新項目將以過去的工作為基礎。特別是，該項目的目的是探索在英國發展起來的流浪法模式是如何被輸出到英國殖民世界的，這種模式是如何隨著時間的推移而改變的，以及殖民背景下的發展是如何反過來反映在英國的經驗上。在此背景下，本研究將探討流浪法在加勒比海地區、毛里求斯、錫蘭、愛爾蘭、印度、開普殖民地、海峽殖民地、東非保護國、尼日利亞北部和香港的實施情況。以及研究在這些法律中，它們的目標和執行模式，和“流浪”隨著時間的推移進化的方式方法的異同，這項研究還將考慮這些法律和關鍵公共秩序機構的發展，特別是警察之間的聯繫，以及探索用來證明這些法律正當性的不同的意識形態。最終，目標是產生一種理論，它將重新組織關於公共秩序法的性質的探討，以及殖民經驗在法律形成過程中所起的作用，同時也將有助於當代努力實現的漸進的法律改革。

24601320.label: Realisation of objectives
24601320.value: The project objectives were all successfully achieved. Through the project, it was possible to explore vagrancy laws' legacies across the United Kingdom, the British Empire, including Hong Kong in particular, and the British settler colonial world. This exploration considered how those laws were drafted; when and where they were exported; what other institutional and theoretical developments they were connected to; the similarities and differences in the application of these laws across contexts; the changing function of such laws over time; connections between these laws and other laws with similar effect and/or intent; challenges to such laws and legal orders, and their significance; and the problematic, ongoing legacy of such laws today. In doing so, the project constituted the first attempt to map the history of such laws across the entirety of the broader British imperial world, as well as one of the most globalized histories of vagrancy law to date. There is no doubt this would not have been possible without the inspired, pioneering work in different contexts that has come before. At the same time, mapping the long-term, global trajectory of such laws is also crucial, not least because it helps to make clear the limitations of accounts that are too narrowly grounded in one context. Indeed, one of the key insights of the work was the recognition that vagrancy laws have been justified on dozens of different bases, and have served dozens of different precise purposes, in different times and places; understanding such laws in the aggregate, however, and their persistence over time, requires not only understanding any of those particular rationales and functions, but rather the endurance of such laws across contexts and purposes as well. Most overarchingly in this context, the project was able to highlight the significance of the evolution of vagrancy laws to the evolution of the ‘rule of law’ as such. In particular, such laws accompanied expansions in executive, judicial, and police powers in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, and provided new authorities a ready source of discretionary they could utilize while their mandates were being more firmly established. This observation is to a degree critical of the idea of the rule of law, that was also developing at the time, insofar as it recognizes that far from absolutely opposed to discretionary authority, the rule of law in actuality relied on discretionary authority to expand itself, at least relative to the poorest. Over time, however, the more idealistic vision of the rule of law was able to have its moment too, especially through challenges in United States courts between the 1950s and 1970s, which led to vagrancy laws being declared unconstitutional there. These developments soon had echoes in other polities around the common law world as well. In addition to piecing together the different pieces of this history, the project was also able to highlight a further, global legacy to the relevant developments – a second wave of challenges to vagrancy laws that gathered steam in several African jurisdictions in the twenty-first century, was crowned by a 202 Advisory Opinion by the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights, and which is still ongoing. Despite waves of challenges to vagrancy laws, however, those laws are still very much with us. In the first place, some jurisdictions still have explicitly ‘vagrancy’-penalizing laws on the books, law which are, at times, justified in constitutional text. More broadly, however, even where vagrancy laws have been repealed, ‘vagrancy-type’ laws on various sorts, including prohibitions of loitering, begging, homelessness, broad and vague nuisance laws and overly-broadly applied traffic offences have taken their place. While operating under different headings, these legal orders replicate a great deal of the harms initially enabled by vagrancy laws. The project thus contains a double call to action – both to complete the process of repealing the more explicit vagrancy law legacy, and to address its ongoing presence in legal orders under different names. In terms of outputs, the proposal imagined two journal articles, one conference presentation and a policy reform report. In reality, these goals were exceeded, with one lengthy journal article, a solo-authored book chapter, two book chapters co-authored with my research assistant, and the policy reform report produced and shared via the Transnational Legal History's Group's webpage. In addition, the outcomes of the research were shared at five different international conferences, in five different jurisdictions in Asia and Europe, at conferences that were livecast to participants around the world. The research conducted will also help support a future book project, on the history of public order legality in the British Empire. This is a large project, on which work is still ongoing, that will draw on future research activities as well. At the same time, the research conducted through this ECS grant provided invaluable inputs to that broader work.

To cast greater light on the problematic origins of key features of contemporary criminal law regimes around the world, with the aim of supporting progressive law reform.

24601320.label: Major findings and research outcome
24601320.value: The project resulted in five research outputs: one article in a U.S. law journal; one solo-authored book chapter; two book chapters co-authored with my research assistant; and a policy reform report, published by the Transnational Legal History Group at CUHK. The article in the U.S. law journal is lengthy (around 30,000 words), and provides an extensive overview of the history of vagrancy laws in the British Empire between the early nineteenth century and today, bringing numerous contexts that are normally considered alone into conversation, and highlighting geographical diversity and, even more noticeably, change over time. The insights of that article are too extensive to highlight in brief, but overarchingly it takes the study of vagrancy law significantly further than it has gone to date, and provides a solid basis on which comparative investigation may develop in future. The solo-authored book chapter provides a different sort of account, arguing that vagrancy laws are connected to the development in the nineteenth century of particularly problematic ways of viewing the world, that at their extreme led to eugenicist, racist theories. As such it extends the import of the investigation more directly into the history of ideas as such, providing a new vantage point from which to consider the relevant histories. The two articles co-written with my research assistant are based on extensive archival research in Hong Kong’s archives, and provide a detailed history of the development of vagrancy laws from the 1840s through to the late twentieth century in Hong Kong specifically. The policy reform report provides a brief history of vagrancy laws not only in the British but also in other European empires, outlines several of the legal measures forming part of the vagrancy law legacy still on the books in numerous jurisdictions around the world today, and presents a summary of legal arguments that may be used to challenge such laws. As such, it provides a valuable resource for all those interesting in combatting such legal orders.

24601320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24601320.value: Vagrancy laws are an interesting and compelling component of legality because they combine labor discipline and public order functions. The project’s exploration can be further developed through historical investigation of other components of legality that sit at this intersection. From a different perspective, this is the subject of the PI’s current GRF, focused on the history of forced labor regulation (encompassing vagrancy laws as well as many other legal orders). As such, many of the insights are already being developed in ongoing research.

24601320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24601320.value: The project explores the history of vagrancy and vagrancy-type laws in the British Empire. These are very broad and vague laws that penalize a range of activities seen, by the laws’ framers at least, as related, including being poor and/or unemployed, moving around, seeming suspicious, engaging in the informal economy, and engaging in activity deemed of questionable morality. The project considered how such laws were generated, the manner in which such laws were disseminated across the British Empire over its long history, and the challenges they have come under in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. In presenting a global history, the project helps make clear how connected the legal experiences of numerous different jurisdictions today have been. In exploring the challenges that have and have not been made to vagrancy laws, the project helps to bring out the lack of attention, in much discourse and practice focus on the development of ‘the rule of law,’ to the discretionary application of the law against the poor. In exploring the challenges vagrancy laws have faced, and the state of such laws around the world today, the project helps provide additional resources to those who seek to challenge such laws.

24602020.label: Project Objectives
24602020.value: To investigate in depth the tone-melody relationship in sung Cantonese, as exemplified in the creative praxes of Hong Kong composers. I will identify all optimal musical intervals for each combination of Cantonese tone succession that enable the correct perception of the lyrics. I will further scrutinize how different textual and musical conditions, including lexical syntax, harmony, rhythm, and texture, work together to influence the intelligibility of the lyrics and to promote text-setting strategies. To examine the specific text-setting approaches used by Hong Kong composers in Cantonese choral works, as they seek to overcome the text-setting constraints imposed by a tonal language, and especially in conditions where multiple melodic lines are performed simultaneously and moving in contrary directions. I will further investigate how the constraints of the lexical contour extend beyond melody and offer creative opportunities in other musical parameters, including harmony and texture. To create an online database of Cantonese choral repertoire in order that choral directors, composers, and music educators will have easy access to the repertoire. The database is intended to facilitate the promotion of Cantonese choral music in the Hong Kong music scene with a direct impact on composers, performers, and educators. To organize a workshop and a project culminating conference-concert as a means of disseminating the research and developing impact. The participants – composers, students, and music-educators – will be invited to contribute new choral works with reference to the research findings. The new works will be performed in the conference-concert to collect further feedback on the findings and promote cross-disciplinary conversations pertinent to tone-music relationships and text-music interactions.

24602020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24602020.value: At first hearing, the words in everyday songs are often incomprehensible to listeners. Owing to discrepancies between verbal language and music composition, the semantics of the text can become lost in the musical sounds. More so than Romance languages, tonal languages pose a particular challenge for composers and listeners. Relying on pitch to differentiate word meanings, tonal languages are imbued with musicality; yet, ironically, their musical expressions are often limited by the pitch structure of the language. With more linguistic tones than standard Chinese, Cantonese poses still greater challenges for musical perception and composition. As Bell Yung has demonstrated in his landmark book on Cantonese opera (1989), Cantonese syllables have an array of possible combinations with tune-types. Meanwhile, linguists have examined the tone-melody interface in Cantonese popular music and its implications for lyrics writing (Ho, 2010; Wong and Diehl, 2002), showing that Cantonese texts are only intelligible in a musical setting if the pitches of successive syllables are appropriately distanced. However, no one to date has similarly mapped out the manifold possibilities in contemporary Cantonese compositions to understand how composers deal with the text-setting constraints. Drawing upon interviews, musical analysis, and empirical tests, this project defines linguistic constraints as a source of creativity in the Cantonese choral repertoire written in postcolonial Hong Kong. With a stylistic spectrum reaching from the conventional to the avant-garde, choral music poses additional challenges not found in other genres, notably the issue of textual intelligibility where multiple vocal lines move simultaneously in different directions. My methodology includes musical scores collection and database compilation based on stylistic, text-generic, and social criteria. I will then perform perception tests in which participants listen to recordings of original and altered musical passages from the assembled works to determine their textual intelligibility. Complemented by composer interviews that aim to reveal their aesthetic orientations and text-setting strategies, I will also perform harmonic, rhythmic, and textural analysis on the music and evaluate composers’ approaches to writing multiple vocal lines and dealing with word-music interactions. Addressing the perceptual and creative aspects, this project will show how Hong Kong composers work with instead of against the linguistic constraints to create a new music that is at once comprehensible and expressive. I expect this research to inform scholarship in music creativity, linguistics, and Hong Kong studies while offering creative tools for musicians and lyricists across multiple Cantonese genres. 初聽一首歌，往往不容易立刻把歌詞都聽得明白。歌唱與言語截然有異，故此文本配上旋律之後可能會變得難以辨識，而聲調語言的歌曲比起非聲調語言的歌曲，歌詞可能更難辨識，創作也因而更加困難。聲調語言運用聲調之高低差異去表達不同語義，本身充滿音樂感，但正因如此，要為聲調語言配上旋律，則受語言的音高結構限制。榮鴻曾的粵劇研究（Yung, 1989），說明了粵劇的板腔體中，相同的文本和聲調組合可以配上不同的旋律；語言學家亦探索過粵語流行曲的詞樂配合如何影響歌詞創作，並證明唯有旋律音高之間的距離，配合歌詞字與字之間的聲調差異，歌詞才能聽得明白（Ho, 2010; Wong and Diehl, 2002）。然而，目前仍未有人研究現代音樂中的粵語創作，聲調與旋律以何種形式配合，亦未著作探討香港作曲家如何應對據詞譜曲時面對的各種難處。 這項研究將聚焦於後殖民時代的香港粵語合唱曲目，透過訪問、音樂分析、觀察實驗，重新檢驗粵語創作的挑戰，探討這些作品如何將語言賦予的制約化成創意的泉源。粵語合唱作品風格森羅萬象，既有傳統，亦有前衛；而多聲部合唱中，各聲部的旋律常在同時間有相異的走向，此時聲調與旋律應當如何配合，才能令聽眾理解歌詞，是為研究的重點之一。研究過程將會收集樂譜，並建構資料庫，根據樂曲風格、文本體裁、社會功能等條件分門別類。研究方法包括聆聽實驗，即讓參與者聆聽不同的錄音，判斷原本的樂段和經修改的樂段，能否讓他們辨識歌詞，由此探討各種音樂元素如何影響歌詞的辨識。研究亦包括作曲家的訪問，藉以了解不同作曲家的美學觀及其據詞譜曲的創作策略。此外，透過分析樂譜的和聲、節奏、織體，則可以了解作曲家如何處理多聲部創作以及詞樂之間的互動。 這項研究計劃從感知和創作兩個角度出發，展示香港作曲家如何把語言本身的創作制約轉化為靈感，譜出易於理解而又變化萬千的音樂。研究預期可以為音樂創作、語言學、香港研究等領域作出貢獻，同時為各類粵語樂種的音樂家和歌詞創作人帶來新的創作工具。

24602020.label: Realisation of objectives
24602020.value: As of March 2024, all the proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. Objective 1: My research has resulted in a renewed understanding of Cantonese text-setting constraints and the relationship between tones and melody. Through empirical tests, I have identified the optimal intervals between each Cantonese tone succession. These findings have been shared through two conference presentations in Lithuania (2021) and Austria (2023). Additionally, two journal articles are produced. One article, titled "From Constraints to Creativity: Musical Inventions in Hong Kong Contemporary Music" has been published in Principles of Music Composing (2021), and the other is undergoing review by Tempo (Cambridge University Press). Objective 2: My research has uncovered several text-setting approaches employed by Hong Kong composers when working with the constraints of Cantonese choral works. These approaches ensure intelligibility across all voice parts in a choral setting. They include utilizing parallel or similar motion in the vocal lines, condensing and repeating text, employing varying rhythms for the same text, incorporating staggered entries, creating harmony through multiple optimal intervals, and incorporating melisma. These findings are discussed in detail in my article titled "Writing Choral Music in a Tone Language: Problems, Practices, and Potentialities," which is currently under review by Tempo (Cambridge University Press). Objective 3: Since 2021, I have established an online database of Cantonese choral repertoire. As of March 2024, the database has recorded 203 works composed by 88 composers. Objective 4: In 2023, I organized the first-ever conference on Cantonese contemporary music featuring a lecture demonstration, a presentation session, and a choral showcase with repertoire drawn from an international call for scores. The conference was attended by scholars, librettists, composers, educators, secondary and tertiary students, as well as general audiences, totalling 711 participants.

24602020.label: Major findings and research outcome
24602020.value: The scarcity of Cantonese works, especially within the choral genre, can be attributed to the challenge of effectively writing music that aligns with the text. Cantonese is a tone language that uses pitch changes to differentiate word meanings. Unless Cantonese texts are skillfully set to a melody according to the tone contour, they run the risk of being incomprehensible or significantly misconstrued. While conditions of intelligible tone-melody relationships have been explored in studies on Cantonese opera and popular music, these text-setting constraints have not been examined in Cantonese choral music and other classical genres. My practice-led research have addressed this gap by identifying the constraints through empirical tests. By analyzing representative choral works by Hong Kong composers, I have demonstrated how those constraints can be transformed into creative resources in multiple aspects of music, such as melodic writing, harmony, and textures. My findings have been shared in lecture demonstrations in 2021 and 2023; two conference/key-note presentations in Lithuania (2021) and Austria (2023); as well as two peer-reviewed journal articles. One article, titled "From Constraints to Creativity: Musical Inventions in Hong Kong Contemporary Music" is published in Principles of Music Composing (2021), and the other is undergoing review by Tempo (Cambridge University Press). In 2023, I organized a project-culminating conference titled "From Constraints to Creativity: A Conference on Cantonese Contemporary Music" The conference offered an opportunity for composers worldwide to write for Cantonese-speaking choirs at a professional level for the first time, gathering 73 submissions from Asia, Europe, North America, and Australia, enhancing the genre’s international reach and awareness. The conference received wide media coverage on CASH FLOW (Hong Kong, 2023), The News Lens (Taipei, 2023), and Radio Television Hong Kong (Hong Kong, 2023). It was recognized by RTHK as the Top 10 Music Headlines of 2023 based on the event’s influence on the cultural and academic development in Hong Kong.

24602020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24602020.value: My research and impact development team will continue to bolster the social impact of my work through international outreach. Beginning in 2024, we will collaborate with choirs in the USA, the UK, and Canada to organize Cantonese choral workshops that enable immigrants, non-Cantonese speakers, and other Cantonese diasporas to better understand Cantonese choral singing and its culture. Additionally, the findings of this ECS project have catalyzed the development of a proposed GRF project that examines how the Cantonese text-setting constraints are harnessed in instrumental compositions derived from hidden Cantonese texts. I have invited an award-winning violin professor from USA to be my Co-Investigator, and we seek to present to all-new compositions with cross-cultural instrumentations (violin and Chinese instruments) alongside presentations and lecture demonstrations on the new findings from the proposed project. Our future research and creative collaborations will focus on challenging the stereotypical image of East Asian musics as the cultural Other.

24602020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24602020.value: This research project addressed the challenges faced by composers and listeners when trying to understand song lyrics sung in tonal languages, such as Cantonese. Tonal languages use pitch variations to convey word meanings, which inherently adds a musical aspect. However, this poses difficulties when setting the language to music, as the language's pitch structure can limit musical expression. Through perception tests and musical analysis, the study examined the specific constraints of setting Cantonese text to music. It identified optimal musical intervals for different tone successions and explored how these constraints can be used creatively in Hong Kong's contemporary music scene. By analyzing works by Hong Kong composers, the study revealed the potential of combining tonal Cantonese language with speech and text to create unique effects in choral music. Overall, this research highlighted how Hong Kong composers embrace these constraints and use them to create new and innovative music. The aim was to provide audiences with fresh ways to appreciate the language and culture embedded within the music.

24606820.label: Project Objectives
24606820.value: To describe the patterns and dynamics of inequality in Tokugawa-era Japan as a case of an early modern agrarian economy so as to fill in gaps in previous research. On an explanatory level, to investigate the causal effect of political and economic institutions and developments on these patterns and dynamics of inequality. To develop comparative hypotheses on variations in levels and trends in inequality across early modern agrarian economies, as an exploratory starting-point for future research.

24606820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24606820.value: In recent years, the study of economic inequality has been injected with renewed energy and relevance by heightened public debate around the increasing concentration of income in many countries. This interest has also extended to the question of the longer-run historical dynamics and determinants of inequality. One current leading edge of this research is the challenging task of estimating levels and changes of inequality in economies before the advent of the industrial revolution and modern bureaucratic states. This project will contribute to the advancement of this body of research by undertaking an in-depth case study of Japan in the Tokugawa era (1600-1867). Tokugawa-era Japan represents a case of an early modern agrarian economy that displays a mix of generic and distinctive characteristics that give it substantial comparative interest. In terms of urbanization, commercialization, and growth patterns, its trajectory runs in rough parallel with that of many other economies across Eurasia before the industrial revolution. Yet, previous research has suggested that the level of inequality in the mid-nineteenth century was remarkably low by comparative standards, particularly in terms of the divide between elites and the agrarian majority (Saito 2015). These suggestive findings are in need, first, of further elaboration and confirmation and, then, of explanation. Addressing this gap in the literature, this project will involve descriptive, explanatory, and exploratory tasks. First, it will combine multiple sources of evidence to describe the structure and change over time of preindustrial Japanese inequality. Secondary research and primary documents on the changing distribution of income between regions, within villages, and among the ruling class will provide material for a more complete picture than is currently available. Second, connecting the study of inequality with the economic and political dynamics analyzed in my previous research (Cohen 2015), this project will offer an explanation of the causal forces driving Tokugawa-era Japan’s distinctive patterns. The consequences for inequality of demographic pressure, the shift of commerce into rural areas, and the increasing tensions within the ruling class have not been sufficiently explored in previous research. Finally, on an exploratory level, this case study will aid in hypothesis formation for future, directly comparative studies of historical inequality. Precisely because Tokugawa-era Japan was in many ways typical for early modern commercialized agrarian economies, a deeper understanding of inequality in it will serve as a base for further exploring the determinants of variations in inequality across cases and over time. 近年來，對許多國家收入日益集中問題的公開辯論為對經濟不平等現象的研究注入了新的活力和關注度。這種關注也被延伸到了對不平等問題一貫以來的歷史動態和決定因素的研究。當前該等研究的前沿領域的一個挑戰是對工業革命和現代官僚國家出現之前的經濟不平等狀態的水平和改變做出估測。本項研究將會通過對德川時代（1600-1867年）的日本進行深入個案分析，從而對這個體系內的研究做出貢獻。德川時代的日本是早期現代農業經濟的一個代表性案例，它所展現的種種特殊及普遍的特質使其具有相當的比教學意義。在城市化，商業化和增長方式方面，其軌跡與工業革命之前歐亞大陸許多其他經濟體的軌跡大致相同。然而，先前的研究表明，與其他類似的經濟體相比，十九世紀中葉日本的不平等程度非常低，特別是在精英階層和多數農業階層之間的鴻溝方面（Saito 2015）。這些有指向性的研究發現首先需要要進一步的深化和論證，然後需要進一步解釋。本項研究將以描述性，解釋性和探索性的方式彌補文獻中的空白。首先，它將綜合多種證據來描述前工業化時期日本不平等狀況的結構和隨時間而發生的變化。關於不同區域之間，村落內部以及統治階級內部收入分配變化的原始資料和研究將會就該問題提供一個比現有資料更為完整圖像。其次，將對不平等的研究與我之前的研究（Cohen 2015）中分析的經濟和政治動態聯繫起來，本項研究將解釋推動德川時代日本獨特模式的成因。而在我先前的研究中，人口壓力不均，商業向農村轉移以及統治階級內部日益緊張的關係所帶來的後果尚未被充分討論。最後，在探索的層面上，本項研究將有助於未來就歷史不平等的比較研究建立假說。正是由於德川時代的日本在許多方面都是農業經濟早期現代商業化的典型案例，因此，對其不平等現象更深入的了解將為進一步探討各種情況以及各種時期下的不平等現象的決定因素奠定基礎。

24609620.label: Project Objectives
24609620.value: To move the PI’s doctoral research (“The Lost-wax Casting in Bronze Age China”) forward by conducting a more inclusive investigation of the investment cast objects in early China. The proposed project will compare different technological variations of investment casting and multiple conventions of the lost-wax casting. Especially, it plans to investigate the pre-Han investment castings from the novel angle of social agency, which is barely discussed by the PI’s dissertation, and almost never touched upon by previous studies. To conduct a thorough and comprehensive study of textual records, archaeological reports, and other published materials relevant to early Chinese investment castings, with a particular focus on metal garment hooks. The PI's methodology combines visual analysis and scientific examinations of particular metal objects, interviews with metal founders and artists, and research with archaeological materials and related literature. This methodology is interdisciplinary, bridging art history, archaeology, metallurgy, ethnography, the history of technology, and digital humanities. To conduct a case study on well-selected garment hooks from accessible collections that are potentially investment cast. This research will be both object-centered and object-driven, studying the target objects and stylistically relevant ones from early China in chronology and social context. One case study attempts to explore the social actors (e.g., makers and consumers) through early Chinese garment hooks. With a particular emphasis on the interplay of design, technology and social agency in making garment hooks, this case study aims to explore ancient Chinese metalworking and metallurgy in archaeological perspectives. To investigate the social dynamics behind early investment castings with the following questions: who were the investment casters in early China? Were they independent craftsmen with multiple clients, or attached to a specific patron? Was the investment casting technique the prerogative of a single foundry? This project aims to better understand early Chinese investment casters, foundries, as well as their relationships with patrons and other metallurgical artisans/workshops. To compare investment casting with other major metallurgical processes in early China, such as the dominant section-mold casting, and the innovative pattern-block technique. With special attentions to the production, consumption, circulation, patronage, and marketing of investment castings, this comparative study will try to reveal a more complete picture of metalworking, art, and agency in pre-Han China. To evaluate the involvement of regional nobilities and princely households in the commission, production, and circulation of investment castings. Working together with the Art Museum, CUHK, the PI will specifically prepare a follow-up exhibition in the near future with the tentative title, “Metal Garment Hooks in Early China: Design, Craft and Agency.”

24609620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24609620.value: 通常認為，失蠟法是鑄造的規範性操作，即鑄造金屬最佳甚至唯一“正確”的方法。通過揭露中國青銅鑄工常不選用其所精通的失蠟工藝的現象，研究者的博士論文駁斥了上述錯誤的假設。對失蠟法而言，“失模”為其核心原理。作為包裹或覆蓋在蠟模上的泥范，無需分塊成形，從模上取下並重新組裝。因此，該法也被稱為“熔模鑄造”，這對於其它偶而替代蠟的熔融材料，是一更具兼容性的術語。 本項目擬對不晚於漢代（即早於公元前206年）的熔模鑄件進行全面考察，進一步深入業已完成的博士研究。研究者旨在對比早期中國所有已知的熔模鑄法（如失蠟鑄造的不同傳統，以及“失鉛”法、“失繩” /“焚失”法、“失蠟和失紡”法 ）的技術差異。本研究將細檢全球範圍內與熔模鑄件有關的文物，並調查其年代、分佈、相關變化以及埋藏背景。 尤其是，本研究將探討早期中國熔模鑄件背後的社會能動性：哪些工匠參與了熔模鑄造？他們究竟是獨立工匠，還是隸屬於特定的贊助者？熔模鑄術是否被個別作坊所壟斷？掌握熔模法的鑄工與其他金屬工匠之間的關係如何？由此新視角所見的許多問題仍未得到解答，甚或尚未提出。此外，該研究將進一步把熔模鑄造與早期中國其他主要的金屬工藝進行比較，尤其是較常見的分范鑄造和批量生產的侯馬陶鑄。這些比較將特別關注工藝品的生產、消費、流通、贊助和市場，以構建早期中國有關金屬技術、工藝和相關行為者的整體圖景。

24609620.label: Realisation of objectives
24609620.value: The "Early Chinese Investment Casting in Comparative Perspective" research project has made significant progress in achieving the stated objectives. The project has expanded the investigation of investment cast objects in early China beyond the PI's original dissertation focus. It has taken a more inclusive and comparative approach, examining different technological variations of investment casting as well as multiple conventions of the lost-wax casting process. Rather than just focusing on the technical aspects, the research has examined how access to specialized investment cast objects reflected and utilized state-of-the-art analytical methods to map out the extensive network of specialized metalworking centers across ancient China. This project has moreover undertaken a rigorous, multi-pronged approach to examining the available textual, archaeological, and material evidence related to early Chinese investment casting. In addition, the project has successfully conducted a case study on well-selected garment hooks from accessible collections in both object-centered and object-driven approach, which aligns with the project's stated methodological framework. It has further explored the social actors through early Chinese garment hooks and uncovered fascinating insights into the dynamics that shaped the patronage and consumption of these bronze artifacts. This indicates the case study on garment hooks has indeed delved into the interplay between design, technology, and social agency, as outlined in the project's goals. The PI has successfully integrated object-based analysis, technological examination, and social contextualization to shed new light on the intricate dynamics of ancient Chinese metalworking and the role of these specialized artifacts within the broader social and cultural landscape. The project has delved into the complex social, economic, and cultural factors that governed the production, circulation, and use of investment cast objects in pre-Han China. Revealing a more complete picture of metalworking, art, and agency, the research has achieved a more nuanced and holistic understanding of the intersections between art, technology, and social agency in the pre-Han period. Collaborating with the Art Museum at CUHK, the PI has created an exhibition on metal garment hooks in early China, with the catalogue provided as one of the research outputs. Overall, this new project goal demonstrates the research team's ambition to not only uncover the broader social dynamics surrounding investment casting, but to also translate their findings into a tangible public-facing outcome through the planned exhibition. The partnership with the Art Museum, CUHK and the decision to highlight metal garment hooks as a case study suggests the researchers have made substantial progress in evaluating the involvement of regional nobilities and princely households in the commission, production, and circulation of these important bronze artifacts.

24609620.label: Major findings and research outcome
24609620.value: The project on investment cast objects in early China has investigated the historical significance, techniques, and cultural context of the technology by comparing different technological variations of investment casting and multiple conventions of the lost-wax casting. By examining artifacts and relevant archaeological remains, the project sought to shed light on the development, usage, and artistic achievements of investment casting in early China. My research has revealed that the investment casting in China originated no later than Eastern Zhou (770–256 BCE) with its technical knowledge mastered in the northern Chinese frontiers perhaps during the late second millennium BCE. The technique involved creating intricate bronze and other metal objects by sculpting a meltable model, encasing it in a clay mold, and then melting the model away to replace it with molten metal. The project also highlighted the remarkable artistic achievements of investment casting in early China. Various metal artifacts created through this method showcased exceptional craftsmanship, intricate details, and unusual designs. This project has also conducted close visual analysis of some metal garment hooks in pre-Han China (before 202 BCE), the openwork design of many leads some researchers to announce that they were cast by the investment casting. Yet the research has not found any conclusive evidence in verifying the pre-Han belt hooks I have closely observed as cast by the investment method. By exploring the synthesis of sophisticated metallurgical and metalworking skills used on the manufacture of these belt hooks, involving section-mold casting, hammering, soldering, gilding, and inlaying of lapis lazuli, jade, and turquoise, I have also analyzed other shaping and decorative schemes in early China other than the investment casting. By comparing investment casting with other major metallurgical processes in early China, especially the traditional section-mold casting and the innovative patten-block technique, this project has touched upon several topics concerning the production, consumption, and patronage of early Chinese metalwork, revealing a fuller picture of metalworking, art, and agency in pre-Han China. By arguing against Donna Strahan’s prestigious lecture, “Debating the Use of Lost-wax Casting in Ancient China,” I sincerely invite scholars of metal technology to emerge from the “doubting of investment casting” era to tackle new challenges in early Chinese archaeo-metallurgy.

24609620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24609620.value: For a long time, research on the pre-Han use of investment casting in China has been driven primarily by the discovery that, in a tradition with massive metalwork casting, lost wax was rarely used. For some scholars, it was curious that the Chinese cast the highly sophisticated bronzes invariably by the cumbersome method of “direct casting into piece-moulds,” as they had always heard that “the ‘finest castings’ were achieved by means of the cire-perdue process.” Since the early 2000s, moreover, a number of scholars have once again turned against the hypothesis that investment casting was practiced in the Chinese Bronze Age. After surging first in China, this new tide of doubt spilled over from the academic world to the media and the public. It took some time to arrive in the West, and several open-minded scholars are still inviting this vigorous wave. Further efforts are still in need to give a firm answer to these disputes and more importantly, move forward to more detailed questions of investment casting.

24609620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24609620.value: The project on investment casting in early China provides valuable insights into the historical, artistic, and cultural aspects of this technique. The research outcomes have showcased that the technical prowess and artistic achievements of pre-Han (before 202 BCE) Chinese metalworkers while shedding light on the broader social-cultural context in which investment casting was utilized. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of early Chinese art, technology, and material culture in a metallurgical perspective. The project has also identified regional variations in investment casting techniques across early China. Different periods and regions employed recognizably distinct applications of investment casting, resulting in variations in style, form, and decoration. These regional variations provide valuable insights into the diverse artistic expressions and cultural dynamics of early Chinese civilization.

24610320.value: 香港患糖尿病患者人數仍然上升，超過百分之九十為2型糖尿病患者。糖尿病人需要透過自我管理健康行為維持血糖的穩定性。以往研究主要透過2型糖尿病患者的認知及健康資訊等因素去了解自我管理行為，但不少外國研究指出正向心理特質可以促進2型糖尿病患者的自我管理行為。自我調節資源模型指出自我關懷可以透過增加自我調節資源來促進健康行為， 但相關的本地研究不足。本研究希望探討2型糖尿病患者的自我關懷與自我管理行為變化的關係。 採用縱向研究設計，本研究假設自我關懷與2型糖尿病患者自我管理行為有正面關係，而兩者的關係可能受三個因素(正負面情緒的平衡、自我效能及創傷後成長)的中介作用所解釋。 是次研究會從門診診所招募400位2型糖尿病患者，參加者將回答有關患糖尿病的經歷（自我關懷、正面及負面情緒、自我效能及創傷後成長）以及自我照顧行為的問卷。參加者會於不同時間(基線評估, 一個月後及三個月後評估)回答問卷。數據將以潛在成長曲線模型進行分析。 本研究您所提供的資訊能夠説明研究者們更好地瞭解2型糖尿病患者的心理適應情況，從而為促進香港2型糖尿病患者的心理及行為健康提出更好的建議。

To analyse how the EEMN-related changes in environmental data collection and analysis have provoked changes in China’s environmental governance institutions, in terms of the instruments, incentives and capacities of central and local state agents in environmental regulation, noting that new environmental data demands may in turn emerge. 24610420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24610420.value: Aim: This project challenges the commonly held view that ‘more data leads to better urban governance’, promoted by recent enthusiasm for smart city, by drawing attention to the political nature of data. It argues that data are never neutral reflections of urban realities but purposefully produced by different actors to promote certain urban futures. To illustrate this argument, this project will examine how China’s urban environmental governance (UEG) is a function of struggles between the central and local governments over environmental data collection and analysis. Background: China’s central government has struggled to arrest urban environmental problems through imposing environmental targets on its growth-minded local leaders. Exploiting the existing bottom-up environmental monitoring system, local leaders have reported falsified environmental data to conceal their failures in target compliance. To address this data muddle, since 2015, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment has been constructing a nationwide Ecological and Environmental Monitoring Network (EEMN) under its direct control. The EEMN involves recentralising the management of locally-run environmental monitoring stations and expanding the use of digital technologies in environmental data collection and analysis. The Ministry hopes that, with its environmental monitoring capacity enhanced by the EEMN, its power in environmental regulation can be strengthened. Despite its significance, the EEMN has not been researched for its impacts on central-local relations in UEG. Research tasks: This project applies the perspective of urban data politics, which stresses that data and their embedded urban social conditions are mutually constituted, to investigate China’s UEG. Focusing on the construction and implications of the EEMN in Shenzhen and Guiyang, it will analyse how changes in environmental data collection and analysis may reshape China’s central-local relations in UEG. First, it will identify the changes introduced by the EEMN in environmental monitoring and the resultant improvements on environmental data, with attention to the challenges involved in realising such changes. Second, it will examine how the EEMN-related changes in environmental monitoring have provoked changes in environmental governance institutions, in terms of the instruments, incentives and capacities of central and local state agents in environmental governance, noting that new environmental data demands may in turn emerge. Significance: This project will advance a new analytical framework on the ‘central-local politics of environmental data’ to clarify the centrality of data in the struggles around China’s UEG. It will also add a significant non-Western case to the critical urban scholarship on data, whose works have concentrated on Euro-American contexts. 目的：在近年智慧城市的熱潮下，不少人以為「數據越多，城市治理就能越好」。本研究旨在通過關注數據的政治屬性，來挑戰這一普遍觀點。本研究認為數據從來都不是城市實際情況的中立反映，而是由不同人各自有意創造出來的，並被用於引導城市在未來往特定方向發展。為論證上述主張，本研究將探討以下命題：在中央與地方政府圍繞環境數據收集和分析进行博弈的背景下，中國城市環境治理如何受這種博弈所影響。 背景：中國中央政府一直試圖將環保目標下達给著眼經濟增長的地方官員，以解決城市環境問題。由於現行的環境監測系統是自下而上的，當環保任務未能達標時，有地方官員利用這系统上報偽造的環境數據進行掩飾。為了解決數據造假的問題，自2015年起，生態環境部開始建設由其直接控制的全國生態環境監測網絡（EEMN）。EEMN涉及重新集中現時由地方政府運行的環境監測站的管理權，以及在環境數據收集和分析中擴大使用數碼技術。生態環境部希望通過EEMN鞏固其環境監測能力，從而強化其環境監管力量。儘管EEMN具有重要意義，目前仍鮮有研究探討該系統如何影響中央與地方政府在城市環境治理方面的關係。 研究任務：本研究從城市數據政治的角度出發，強調數據及其根植的城市社會條件是相互構成的，並基於此觀點探討中國城市環境治理的情況。通過調查EEMN在深圳和貴陽的建設及其意義，本研究將分析環境數據收集和分析的變化，了解這些變化如何重塑中國城市環境治理的央地關係。分析會從兩方面展開：首先是辨別EEMN如何改變環境監測的模式及改善環境數據的質量，並且關注實現這些改變時所面臨的挑戰；其次是剖析EEMN對環境監測的影響如何重塑環境治理機構，包括中央和地方政府在環境治理方面的政策工具、激勵機制和治理職能等諸多範疇，並且留意這些變化可能帶來的新的環境數據需求。 研究意義：本研究將就「環境數據的中央與地方政治」提出新的分析框架，闡明數據在中國城市環境治理博弈中的核心地位。此外，先前以數據為主題的批判城市研究普遍基於歐美案例，本研究將通過一個非西方的案例，擴展該領域的探討範圍。

24612620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24612620.value: 規劃與秩序：比較憲法中的中國

24612620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24612620.value: China has a centennial experience of modern constitution-making. In more than one hundred years, numerous constitutional documents were produced, re-produced, and revised in China. Unfortunately, new writings on comparative constitution-making has not yet significantly engaged with China. At the same time, a rich body of national scholarship in English on China’s centennial experience of modern constitution-making has not yet significantly engaged with the general literature on comparative constitution-making. This project seeks to bridge this scholarly gap by locating China’s centennial experience of modern constitution-making with the general scholarship of comparative constitution-making. The project classifies China’s modern constitution-making into three models: the imperial constitution-making of the late Qing dynasty, the liberal constitution-making of the Republic of China, and the socialist constitution-making of the People’s Republic of China. The project seeks to demonstrate that to situate China within comparative constitution-making scholarship can facilitate a better understanding of Chinese constitution making, and enrich the general study of comparative constitution-making. That is due to three comparative patterns in China’s constitution-making, namely: resonance, variation, and innovation. China’s constitution-making as human’s constitutional project is resonated with the global norms, institutions, and phenomena in constitution-making. But, China’s distinctive constitution-making as elite’s top-down constitutional project induces variations in Chinese practice of the global norms and institutions of constitution-making. In addition, due largely to constitutional exceptionalism, China’s constitution-making has innovative practices which are not addressed in the global scholarship of constitution-making. This project situates China’s centennial experience of modern constitution-making within recurring themes of comparative constitution-making and innovative themes drawing on China’s experience of constitution-making, including foundational themes (revolution, evolution and constitution-making, constitutional replacement and amendment), procedural themes (the party’s role, public participation, and transnational engagement in constitution-making process), and substantive themes (the party in the constitution, constitutional directive principles, structural institutions, and constitutional rights). The project hopes to facilitate a dialogue between comparative constitutional law scholars and Chinese constitutional law specialists. 規劃與秩序：比較憲法中的中國 中國擁有多於一百年制定成文憲法的經驗。一百多年來，在中國產生、複製和修改了許多成文憲法文件。不過，有關比較憲法制定的新著作尚未與中國充分接觸。同時，關於中國近代制憲經驗的英語學術研究也尚未與比較憲法的一般研究問題充分的聯繫。 本項目旨在通過將中國近代憲政的百年經驗與比較憲政的一般學術研究聯繫起來，以彌合這一學術鴻溝。本項目將中國的現代憲法制定分為三種模式：晚清的帝國憲法制定，中華民國的自由憲法制定和中華人民共和國的社會主義憲法制定。本項目旨在證明，將中國置於比較憲法制定的學術研究之內可以更好地促進對中國憲法制定的理解，並能豐富比較憲法制定的一般研究。這是由於中國憲法制定中的三種比較模式，即共鳴、變化和創新。中國的憲法制定作為人類的憲法項目，與全球的憲法制定準則、制度和現象產生了共鳴。但是，作為由精英主導的自上而下的制憲項目，中國獨特的制憲機制亦產生了與全球制憲準則與制度相異的變化。此外，很大程度上由於憲法上的例外主義，中國的制憲具有創新性實踐，卻未有全球研究憲法制定的學者們進行探討。 本項目將中國在現代憲法制定方面的百年經驗置於比較憲法制定這一反復出現的主題上，同時也置於以中國的制憲經驗為基礎的創新主題上：其中包括基本主題（革命、演變和憲法制定、憲法替代和修正），程式性主題（政黨的角色、公眾參與和跨國參與憲法制定過程）和實質性主題（政黨在憲法、憲法指示原則，結構性制度和憲法權利中的作用）。本項目希望促進比較憲法學學者與中國憲法學專家之間的對話。

If they are present, identifying which psychological traits correlate with the mix of political ideologies in different East Asian countries. 24618520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24618520.value: The purpose of the proposed investigation is: 1) to uncover whether one of the most amply evidenced theories of political psychology in the West is universal, applying in regions with significantly different cultures, political systems, and ideologies; 2) refine the theory to better identify how and why psychological traits “attach” to different ideological beliefs; 3) and make the theory of immediate practical utility in bridging political divides and reducing polarization. This theory proposes that psychological traits make some ideologies more likely to be adopted than others; that is, psychological traits evince “elective affinities” with political beliefs, making either stasis and hierarchy (an affinity for rightwing ideology), or change and equality (an affinity for leftwing ideology), more attractive. As such, one’s choice of ideology is not made on a blank slate; rather, we are more likely to develop an ideology attuned to our psychological dispositions. However, while hundreds of studies have been done in Europe and the US – and reviews of the literature emphasize the large number of countries where this theory has been tested – there are no studies attempting to demonstrate whether the theory is applicable (and if so, how) in East Asia. This is a major gap in the accumulated evidence: if this theory about human psychology is true – that is, if it describes a phenomenon innate in universal human psychology – then results should show similar relationships between ideology and orientations toward social dominance and authoritarianism, disgust, fear, and threat sensitivity, personality, etc., among diverse samples of East Asian participants. If, however, the extensive and often replicated results in the West are the sole product of ideational/discursive influences, not due to psychological universals, then applying the same tests to samples of East Asian participants would give null results. Alternatively, differing relationships between psychological traits and political ideology in East Asian countries may help refine the theory, better elucidating the psychological “elective affinities” with political ideologies. This proposed study could provide substantial evidentiary backing for the theory, or lead to a significant revision. Beyond its importance for theory development, this study can help provide an understanding of the psychological factors underpinning ideological conflict; this understanding can form the basis of efforts to reduce ideology-driven conflict and political polarization. With knowledge of the psychological needs to which various ideologies are attuned, political partisans and civil society actors can devise messaging campaigns that more effectively bridge ideological divides. 擬進行的調查的目的是：1）揭露西方政治心理學理論中最充分證明的理論之一是否具有普遍性，適用於文化，政治制度和意識形態迥然不同的地區； 2）完善理論以更好地確定心理特徵如何以及為什麼“附著”於不同的意識形態信念； 3）並在縮小政治分歧和減少兩極分化方面做出了直接的實際應用。這種理論認為，心理特質使某些意識形態比其他意識形態更容易被接受。也就是說，心理特徵表明“選舉親和力”與政治信仰之間的聯繫使停滯和等級制（對右翼意識形態的親和力）或變化與平等（對左翼意識形態的親和力）更有吸引力。因此，對意識形態的選擇並非一a而就。相反，我們更有可能發展出與我們的心理傾向相適應的意識形態。但是，儘管在歐洲和美國進行了數百項研究，並且文獻回顧強調了對該理論進行過測試的許多國家，但尚無研究試圖證明該理論是否適用（如果可以，如何）在東亞。這是積累的證據中的一個主要空白：如果這種關於人類心理學的理論是正確的-也就是說，如果它描述了人類普遍存在的一種現象-那麼結果應該表明意識形態與社會主導地位和威權主義傾向之間存在相似的關係，令人厭惡。 ，恐懼和威脅敏感度，個性等，在東亞參與者的不同樣本中。但是，如果西方廣泛而經常重複的結果是觀念性/話語性影響的唯一產物，而不是出於心理普遍性的緣故，那麼對東亞參與者的樣本進行相同的測試將得出無效的結果。另外，東亞國家的心理特徵和政治意識形態之間的不同關係可能有助於完善理論，更好地闡明與政治意識形態之間的心理“親和力”。這項擬議的研究可以為該理論提供實質性的證據支持，或導致重大修改。除了對理論發展的重要性外，這項研究還可以幫助理解支撐意識形態衝突的心理因素。這種理解可以成為減少意識形態驅動的衝突和政治兩極分化的基礎。有了對各種意識形態所適應的不同心理需求的了解，政治黨派人士和民間社會參與者就可以設計出更有效地彌合意識形態鴻溝的宣傳活動。

24621120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24621120.value: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition that causes impairments in social relationships and communication as well as idiosyncratic and repetitive patterns of behaviors. Due to their unique profiles and behaviors, individuals with ASD are easily misunderstood by people around them who may not be completely familiar with them. In primary and secondary school, students with ASD are often perceived as one of the most difficult types of student to teach, while teachers do not have adequate knowledge and awareness of the condition to facilitate these students to learn in inclusive classrooms. In university, students with ASD continue to struggle with interacting with peers who may have misconceptions and negative attitudes about ASD. Consequently, students with ASD in postsecondary settings are reported to exhibit high rates of mental health challenges. The proposed study aims to promote better understanding of ASD by adapting an online autism training to fit with the local context and evaluate its effect on teacher trainees and university students. In Phase 1, multiple focus groups will be conducted with individuals with ASD, their family members, and their teachers to gather their opinions on factors that contribute to misunderstanding of and stigma towards ASD in Hong Kong. Thematic analysis of qualitative data will be used to involve community stakeholders in adapting a brief autism training to address issues and concerns that are important to the local autistic community. To further investigate the impact of the adapted autism training on knowledge and stigma, a randomized control trial will be conducted in Phase 2. University students and teacher trainees will be recruited to and randomized to receive either the adapted autism training or the original version. Measures of autism knowledge, stigma towards autism, social desirability, and demographic information will be administered immediately before and after the training, as well as after a 6-month follow-up period. In addition, university students will be assessed of their openness to a peer with ASD, while teacher trainees will be assessed of their attitudes towards inclusive teaching practices. Statistical analyses will be performed to evaluate the effects of the adapted training on knowledge, stigma, and behavioral intention associated with ASD in university students and teacher trainees, respectively. Results from this study will produce an effective autism training that is responsive to the needs of local autistic community and the culture of Hong Kong. 自閉症人士大多有不同的社交、溝通和行為模式，他們獨特的行為很容易被其他人錯誤理解。在中小學，很多老師對自閉症的認識不足，視他們為最難應付的學生，亦對自閉症學生融入主流班房造成很大挑戰。在大學，自閉症青少年仍然面對不同的困難，如同儕和教職員的誤解和負面態度，令他們的精神健康承受很大的壓力。 本項研究希望建立一個切合本地社區需要的簡短網上訓練，增加大學生和準教師對自閉症的認識，並評估其成效。在第一階段，我們會透過多個焦點小組，收集自閉症人士、家庭成員或照顧者及現職教師的意見，探討香港對自閉症人士的誤解及污名的成因。透過質性數據的分析，結果能夠幫助研究人員更有效地設計課程，並與社區人士緊密合作，調整由國外引進的訓練版本，去配合本地自閉症人士和不同持分者的需要。 第二階段集中研究訓練課程的成效，邀請大學學生和準教師參與隨機對照實驗，隨機安排進行本地版本或外國版本的訓練，並量度他們對自閉症人士的知識、態度和行為意向，評估前測、後測和跟進測試的改變。透過量化數據分析，評估網上訓練的成效，藉此提高課程質素，去回應自閉症人士的需要及切合香港的本地文化。

25100420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100420.value: Obesity is a global epidemic and is associated with enhanced risks of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and metabolic disorders. However, the mechanistic link between obesity and metabolic disorders are unclear. Increasing evidences suggested that deficient expandability of adipose tissue, instead of obesity per se, contributes to systemic metabolic syndromes. Therefore, understanding the molecular regulation of adipose tissue expansion and its role in obesity-related diseases are critical to provide insights for the further development of therapeutic strategies. Adipose tissue expansion is characterized by increasing adipocyte number and size, both of which are associated with lipid droplet (LD) development and enlarged cholesterol reservoir. Acyl-coenzyme A: cholesterol acyltransferase (ACAT) enzymes catalyzing the formation of cholesteryl ester from free cholesterol are known to play critical roles in cholesterol metabolism and the development of CVDs. Our previous study elucidated that ACATs are required for adipogenesis in vitro, suggesting a potential role of ACATs in regulating adipose tissue expandability in vivo and subsequently effecting systemic metabolism. In our preliminary study, we demonstrated that 1) ACAT1 and cholesterol level increased during LD development in murine 3T3-L1 adipocytes; 2) knocking down ACAT1 or 2 leads to impaired LD formation in vitro with reduced expression of genes involved in lipogenesis; 3) ACAT1&2 inhibition suppressed the maturation of sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP), a transcriptional factor regulated by cholesterol on the endoplasmic reticulum membrane; 4) knocking down ACAT1 upregulated intracellular ceramide and oxylipin levels, which are associated with systemic metabolic disorders. Based on the information above, we hypothesize that ACATs regulate adipocyte-LD expandability through SREBP-dependent manner and consequently effect systemic metabolism in a high fat diet induced obese mouse model. Accordingly, in this project, we will use in vitro cell culture model and in vivo transgenic mouse model to (1) characterize the functional role of ACATs in LD development during LD initiation and expansion stages, (2) elucidate the molecular mechanism by which ACATs functionally contribute to LD development in adipocytes, (3) evaluate the physiological significance of adipocyte-ACAT1 in systemic metabolism in vivo. The expected outcome from this proposal will reveal how ACATs mediate adipocyte-LD expandability, as well as demonstrate a link between adipose tissue expansion and metabolic disorders, providing essential insights for further developing pharmaceutical strategies to ameliorate obesity associated metabolic syndrome by targeting adipose tissue expandability. 肥胖是全球流行病，且是众多疾病发生与恶化的重要风险因素，严重威胁着人类健康。然而肥胖与代谢疾病的机理关联尚不清楚。越来越多的证据表明脂肪组织扩增能力与系统性代谢紊乱相关。所以，理解脂肪组织扩增的调控机制以及其在肥胖相关疾病中扮演的角色将有助于开发新型治疗思路与措施。脂肪组织扩增与脂滴发育和胆固醇含量增加有关。胆固醇酯化酶（ACAT）能催化胆固醇酯的生成，对细胞内胆固醇代谢平衡起重要作用。我们通过体外细胞模型，阐明了ACAT对脂肪细胞正常分化有其必要性，提示脂肪细胞的ACAT在体内环境中或影响脂肪组织扩增。在前期研究中，我们继续阐述了ACAT1和胆固醇水平均与脂滴发育呈正相关，敲低ACAT1或2的表达抑制脂滴生成且降低脂质合成基因的表达，且抑制ACAT1&2活性导致受胆固醇调控的SREBP成熟过程下调。此外，敲低ACAT1上调了与系统代谢疾病密切相关的ceramide与oxylipin的水平。基于这些前期数据，我们假设ACATs通过调控SREBP影响脂肪细胞脂滴扩增能力，从而影响高脂饮食诱导的肥胖小鼠系统能量代谢状态。综上，我们将使用细胞模型和转基因小鼠模型来研究1）ACAT对脂滴发生发育的详细影响 2）ACAT调控脂滴的机理 3）脂肪细胞特异性ACAT1敲除的小鼠的系统性能量代谢特点。顺利完成此项目，将揭示ACAT对脂滴发育的调控机制，并且阐明脂肪组织扩增能力与代谢疾病之间的一条新联系，有助于为发展靶向脂肪组织扩增能力来设计肥胖及其相关代谢疾病的治疗措施提供新思路。

25104220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25104220.value: 人口遺傳學研究發現 Bridge Intergrator 1（BIN1）為遲發性阿爾茨海默氏症的第二大遺傳危險因子。與其他年齡相關的認知障礙症的遺傳危險因子不同，BIN1是一種已知的腫瘤抑制因子，並在細胞週期調節和脫氧核糖核酸損傷反應中有積極的作用。儘管如此，即使有 37％的人口遺傳了 BIN1的致病變異，BIN1功能性缺陷與認知障礙症的致病機理之間的聯繫尚待研究。基於髓鞘降解是導致腦部衰老和認知障礙症之早期結構性變化，是次項目將研究BIN1功能性缺陷在髓鞘降解機制的角色和其可能做成的影響。我們團隊最近提出並發佈了與年齡相關的脫氧核糖核酸雙鏈斷裂（DSB）觸發的異常細胞週期重啟，與及製造髓鞘的寡樹突膠質細胞（OLs）之選擇性凋亡。雖然發達OLs對DSBs高度脆弱性的原因尚不清楚，其潛在的細胞機制可能是在衰老大腦中保持髓鞘完整性的關鍵。 我們在初步的研究上，證明了大腦中的發達OLs 選擇性地表達 BIN1 。而令人驚訝的是，在正常衰老，認知障礙症及多發性硬化症患者的腦組織中，BIN1基因的轉錄有顯著減少。而在多發性硬化患者的腦組織中，我們也發現髓鞘降解和神經元細胞週期重入之間有很強的關連，這表明髓鞘流失和認知障礙之間存在聯繫。在認知障礙症和多發性硬化症的小鼠實驗模型中，我們也發現髓鞘流失與OLs中Bin1表達的減少有密切關係。由於在Atm基因剔除小鼠（一種DSB修復缺陷 實驗模型）裏，表達Bin1的 發達OLs也顯著減少，我們的初步數據清楚地證明了BIN1 在DSBs 損傷反應 、細胞週期調控和髓鞘形成之間有不可或缺的作用。總括而言，我們假設在髓鞘OL中的BIN1 對DNA損傷反應、細胞週期調控和維持髓鞘完整性有著多重及制衡的作用。 因此，我們是次項目的目標是（1）測試寡樹突膠質細胞中的BIN1是否對細胞週期進程、髓鞘形成及DSBs 損傷反應會調節，以及（2）證明BIN1功能性缺陷對髓鞘形成及其在持續衰老的大腦中的神經退化和認知障礙中牽連。我們將使用細胞培養模型以及一種新型的，OL特定的，Bin1剔除小鼠去研究BIN1功能性缺失對髓鞘的後果 。 通過了解Bin1於大腦的表達模式及拆解Bin1細胞信號軸 ，是次項目將會把人口遺傳學中的大數據連結到導致髓鞘流失的特定細胞學機制。這種基於大數據而確立的研究結果，很可能會對治療與年齡有關的認知障礙症產生正面而長遠的影響。

25104220.label: Realisation of objectives
25104220.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to delineate the relationship between BIN1 expression and oligodendrocytes biology in the context of sporadic Alzheimer’s disease. We have realised the proposed plan for objective 1 and objective 2 as detailed below. In Objective 1, we aimed to test if BIN1 in oligodendrocytes regulates cell cycle progression, myelination and DSBs responses through ATM-Bin1-cMyc axis. First, we have delineated the spatiotemporal pattern of Bin1 expression in OLs in human and mouse brain. In two different cohorts of Alzheimer's disease postmortem tissue, we have thoroughly characterized the nuclear and cytoplasmic BIN1 expression in both the white matter and gray matter. Importantly, we have identified a divergent expression pattern of high (BIN:H) and low molecular weight (BIN:L) in the AD, compared with control. This observation was reproduced in mouse model of AD at a very advanced age (18 months). These new findings suggest that the genetic risk of BIN1 variants has to be pinned down at the isoform level in order to fully reveal its dysfunction. More importantly, we are the first to confirm the function of nuclear Bin1 in the Oligodendrocyte population. The existing literature on BIN1 has been suggesting that its cytoplasmic function in the endocytosis of tau is the underlying mechanism of genetic risk. However, our new knowledge suggest an alternative pathway where the nuclear BIN1 function in cell cycle regulation is loss in OL and cause early myelin deficits in prodromal sporadic Alzheimer’s disease, at a stage before any misfolded protein is aggregated. The cell cycle regulation mediated by BIN1-c-Myc interaction was found to be pivotal to both the postmitotic oligodendrocyte and the proliferative progenitor cells. In the former cell type, Bin1 appears to inhibit unwanted cell cycle progression or the occurrence of cellular senescence through the p53 pathway activation. In contrast, Bin1 appears to regulate cell proliferation in the progenitor cells. Despite the divergent consequences, we identified that Cyclin D1 could be the effector of BIN1-c-Myc interaction in both scenarios. The findings above were then investigated further in the context of age-associated DNA double strand breaks or the deficits of DNA repair in the model of Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T). While we do not observe a major difference in the expression pattern of Bin1 in young Alzheimer’s disease model mice and up to 18 months old, we identify that either DNA damage induction or DNA repair deficits in ATM-knockout mice were significantly associated with BIN1 alternation between 1 and 4 months old. Importantly, the BIN1 positive oligodendrocyte population where significantly higher in the ATM-knockout mice at juvenile age than the wildtype, but such trend was reversed at 4 months. This suggested that ATM-mediated DNA repair or its signalling pathway may regulate BIN1 expression level, and support the mechanism of ATM-Bin1-c-Myc-mediated regulation of division and differentiation of oligodendrocyte. For Objective 2, we have demonstrated the impact of BIN1 dysfunction on myelination where we’ve found a significant impact of BIN1 loss in the cell cycle regulation of OPC. This has an impact on the myelination potential of the brain in Alzheimer's disease. Importantly, despite such findings, there was not significant association between BIN1 expression, OL loss and amyloid plaque aggregation in the Alzheimer's disease brain both in human and mouse. This is an important finding that the second most important genetic risk factor of sporadic Alzheimer's disease do not impact on the cognitive function of the brain through amyloid cascade hypothesis. In contrast, in the cuprizone-mediated demyelination mouse model and in human multiple sclerosis cases, we have identified a significant loss of BIN1 in all the regions with myelin loss. When such demyelination was induced BIN1 loss in wild-type mice, it has no effect on any BIN1 isoforms of the APP/PS1 model. Although such treatment induced the accumulation of intracellular amyloid, but it did not trigger an early adverse event in cognitive function in the mouse model, and we found no evidence to suggest that BIN1 is related to amyloid deposition. Such finding was consistent between mice ranging from 3 months to 18 months old, and suggested that aging has no direct implication on BIN1 expression and function, at least in the oligodendrocyte population. For drawbacks, despite our best efforts, the conditional knockout mice did not show cell-type specific BIN1 silencing as hypothesised (see PhD Thesis 1). By using silencing RNA technology coupled with RNA-sequencing as the back-up, we have then successfully showed the effects of Oligodendrocyte-specific loss-of-BIN1 in vitro, and unveiled the important cell cycle regulation function of BIN1 in the oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. In terms of output, there is a delay in the publication process as the PI has relocated overseas on 30/6/2024, due to family reasons. There are in total two publication in preparation for this project. Output 1 is deposited on bioRxiv and being submitted to journal Alzheimer’s & Dementia TRCI, and the Output 2 is being deposited on bioRxiv for the submission to the journal Glia and the draft is attached. This project has completed the training of one PhD student, Ms MA Wai Ting, Iris. Her thesis (PhD Thesis 1) is submitted in April 2025 with her oral examination confirmed on 7/7/2025 (a week after this report is due). These research outcomes are described in section 6. Together, this ECS project has been a success, and we have unveiled the nuclear function of the second most significant genetic risk factor in sporadic Alzheimer’s disease, and such function may not have any association with amyloid cascade hypothesis but directly implicated on the cell cycle regulation of the oligodendrocyte population during the early stage of the disease. Further investigations are warranted for studying the regulation of BIN1 isoform expression in neuons and axons, and how does the nuclear and cytoplasmic functions of BIN1 is balanced in the cells.

25104220.label: Major findings and research outcome
25104220.value: We have made a number of important findings per the objectives above. These findings resulted in three international conference presentations (Conference Paper #1-3), two manuscripts (Output 1, Output 2, in preparation) and a submitted PhD thesis. First, we confirmed that (1) BIN1 expression is oligodendrocyte-specific in the brain with a clear nucleocytoplasmic distribution, and (2) BIN1 isoforms are distributed in the nucleus and cytoplasm and are putative for the cell cycle regulation and differentiation of oligodendrocytes (Conference Paper #1, Output 2, PhD thesis 1). To our knowledge, we are the first to confirm that the second most important genetic risk factor of sporadic Alzheimer’s disease is a nuclear protein with cell cycle regulation function. Second, during the demyelination events in human and mouse, we’ve identified the loss of BIN1 in the brain, especially in the gray matter (Conference paper #2, Conference paper #3, Output 1 and PhD Thesis 1). This finding is consistent with our overarching hypothesis that myelination and oligodendrocytes in the gray matter (intracortical) is more vulnerable than those the white matter (Tse et al 2018 Alz Dement). Third, in cell culture model and in the transgenic mouse model of Alzheimer’s diseases and ATM-knockout, we have confirmed that the presence of DNA damage or the deficits of DNA repair will reduce the BIN1 expression in the oligodendrocytes. Importantly, BIN1 expression persist in the ageing mouse brain up to 18 months old, but it was not affected by the presence of amyloid plaques (Output 2 and PhD Thesis 1). Finally, our silencing RNA experiments have confirmed that the loss of BIN1 in oligodendrocyte will induce cell cycle dysregulation and lead to a state of cellular senescence. By using a range of selective inhibitor, we have showed that the ATM-BIN1-c-Myc signalling pathway could be an important mechanism underlying the cell cycle progression, cellular senescence and differentiation of the oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, especially during the condition of DNA damage (Output 2 and PhD Thesis 1, Conference Paper #3). In terms of other research outcomes, we have successfully trained one PhD student, Ms MA Wai Ting based on this project. We have also developed at least five undergraduates for research training throughout this project period.

25104220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25104220.value: First, the major finding in this project is the identification of BIN1 expression pattern among oligodendrocytes in different ages across a strain of mouse model of Alzheimer's disease and of DNA-damage associated accelerated aging. Second, we have fully characterised the complex BIN1 isoform regulation in the human and mouse brain. With these two solid findings, we identified that nuclear BIN1 is paramount to the switch of cell cycle progression or cellular senescence for oligodendrocytes. Given these findings, the next question to ask would be whether these nuclear BIN1 is regulated together with the cytoplasmic BIN1 for controlling the endocytosis of tau. Given the importance of tau in neuronal cell death, the possible involvement of oligodendrocyte BIN1 in clearing tau will be the next step for further research. The PI will pursue further grant applications with colleagues in Hong Kong and Macau if he remains eligible for RGC funding mechanism as an overseas participant.

25104220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25104220.value: Genetic studies of the population have identified a gene, BIN1 (Bridging Integrator 1), as the second most important genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease, the – the major type of age-related dementia. In this study, we have confirmed that BIN1 is expressed in the brain cells specialised in making the white matter in the brain. This protein is expressed in such oligodendrocyte populations for controlling their survival and functions. In ageing, the DNA damage is accumulated in these myelinating cells and influence their expression of BIN1. We have showed that such changes in BIN1 results in an out-of-control cell cycle in these myelinating cells and their ability to repair the white matter in the brain is compromised. Importantly, we have dissected the molecular pathway that may regulate how BIN1 is functioning during the cell cycle of these myelinating cells. With such demonstration of BIN1’s function on myelination, our results present a new way to understand genetic risk factor by focusing on the lipid-rich white matter and their maintenance by these specialised cells. Together, our experimental findings support that BIN1 is a target for restoring myelination or slowing down white matter loss in the ageing human brain and warrants further investigations.

25201620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201620.value: Freshwater scarcity is a global challenge, and there are growing demands for freshwater in daily life, agricultural and the industrial usages. Solar energy and seawater are both unlimited resources. By combining the strength of these two resources, solar steam generators possess high potentials for production of freshwater, using exclusive solar energy without any carbon print. This interfacial solar steam generation method can absorb solar energy and transform it into the form of heat, which can be used for generating freshwater from seawater. This emerging technology has been rapidly developed in recent years, and the evaporation rate up to several kilograms every square metre per hour has been established. Our previous research had demonstrated that laser scribed graphene can be used for solar steam generation with high scalability. However, there are still some limitations on the current technologies achieved. Although the optical absorption of the material is very high within the visible light range, however, its absorption for the infrared solar energy is relatively low. The Janus superwetting state of the desalination membrane can help the mass transportation of the water, however, there has been limited studies with the 3D configuration for the enhanced thermal management. For the water passage medium using the laser scribed membrane, there are few studies about introducing the gel type polymer for the enhanced transportation of water. In addition, there are also few studies about the employment of laser scribed membrane for the mass transportation phenomena of the salts. This project is going to comprehensively study these essential aspects for this emerging technology. By introducing the plasmonic nanoparticles within the carbonized membranes, the enhancement of the absorption of light within the IR range will be studied. By presenting the gel type polymer in the membranes, the improvement of water transportation in the membrane will be explored. By hosting Janus superwetting states on different sides of the membrane, the salt rejection performance will be experimented for the laser scribed membrane. Eventually, after all these parameters are optimized, the final membranes will possess higher performance for generating fresh water using solar energy. This project is not only benefiting the fundamental understanding of the mass transportation and solar energy conversion for the solar steam generation, but also has strong potential for real applications, to use this knowledge for seawater desalination in remote islands and other places, as a sustainable developing technology. 淡水資源緊缺是一個亟待解決的世界性難題，隨著日常生活、農業和工業對淡水的需求日益增加，此問題更為凸顯。太陽能和海水都是可再生資源，通過結合這兩種資源的優勢，利用太陽能蒸汽發生器從海水中提取淡水，完全使用太陽能而不會導致任何碳排放。這種界面蒸汽發生的方法通過吸收太陽能並將其轉化為熱能，進而將海水轉化為淡水。近年來，這項新興技術得到了快速發展，每小時每平方米的蒸發速率已經達到了公斤量級。前期研究表明，激光碳化石墨烯薄膜可以用於太陽能蒸發海水化淡，其在可見光範圍內的光吸收率非常高，但是對紅外太陽能的吸收較低，成為該技術的發展瓶頸。各向異性超潤濕狀態有助於水的質量輸送，然而對於其熱力學三維分佈的研究卻很少。另一方面，對於激光石墨烯薄膜中引入凝膠型聚合物來增強水的輸運的研究不多。此外，對激光石墨烯薄膜中鹽的輸運研究也很少。本項目將從上述角度對這項新興技術展開全面的研究，通過將等離子基元顆粒引入激光石墨烯薄膜中，研究其在紅外範圍內的光吸收。通過在膜中引入水凝膠聚合物，來增強水分子的輸運。通過在膜的不同側面上分別製備超疏水和超親水表面，對激光石墨烯薄膜的抗鹽性能進行測試。經過優化以上各參數，激光石墨烯薄膜的太陽能蒸汽產生速率將會顯著提高。該項目不僅有益於對水分子輸運和太陽能能源轉換的基礎研究，而且在將其用於偏遠島嶼和其他方面的海水淡化中作為可持續發展的實際應用方面具有強大的潛力。

25201620.label: Realisation of objectives
25201620.value: For Objective 1, we conducted experimental studies to explore the laser manufacturing of nanomaterials across a wavelength range of 300 to 2500 nm. The laser-printed nanomaterials achieved nearly 100% absorption across the entire spectrum. We successfully laser-printed plasmonic nanoparticles, specifically copper (Cu) and manganese dioxide (MnO2), utilizing laser-induced forward transfer methods, and assessed their performance in solar-steam evaporation applications. Consequently, we developed a portable interfacial evaporator using a 3D-structured plasmonic-enhanced photothermal nanocomposite of Cu nanoparticles and laser-induced graphene (Cu NPs/LIG) through a one-step deposition method. This innovative evaporator demonstrated an impressive solar absorption rate of 98% over a broad spectrum (250 to 2500 nm) and rapidly attained a high surface temperature exceeding 80 degrees C under 1 sun irradiation. Furthermore, the fabricated solar-driven evaporator exhibited a high evaporation rate of 2.29 kg per meter square per hour with pure water. Notably, due to spontaneous salt diffusion along vertical concentration gradients facilitated by unobstructed and continuous pathways, we observed exceptional anti-salt performance, achieving a high evaporation efficiency of 1.82 kg per meter square per hour even with brine at high salinity (20 wt%) during long-term applications. For Objective 2, we introduce an in-situ imaging approach utilizing the electrical impedance tomography (EIT) system to dynamically visualize the water desorption process within aerogels in real time. We integrated cellulose nanocrystal-based aerogels with laser-induced graphene (LIG) as a photothermal layer, which significantly improves solar absorption rates. The use of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) enables real-time visualization of the desorption dynamics, revealing that factors such as heat concentration, geometric configurations, and temperature gradients play pivotal roles in facilitating rapid water transport through the polymer network. By manipulating these variables, including optimizing the internal structure and thermal properties of the gel polymers, researchers can enhance water vapor diffusion while minimizing resistance, thus improving overall desalination performance. This interdisciplinary approach not only addresses the challenges of water scarcity but also provides insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing water transport in solar-driven systems, paving the way for more efficient and practical applications in solar evaporation technologies. For objective 3, we investigated the superwetting properties and salt transportation mechanisms in a novel evaporator design that utilizes nano-crystal cellulose (NCC) combined with manganese dioxide (MnO2) nanoparticles and laser-induced graphene (LIG). This innovative combination enables tunable superhydrophilic and superhydrophobic surfaces, which are essential for effectively managing salt accumulation during evaporation. The hydrophilic NCC promotes water absorption, while the hydrophobic LIG helps repel salt crystals, thereby reducing scaling on the evaporator surface. To monitor salt movement within the evaporator, we employed an in situ technique using electrical impedance tomography (EIT), which revealed that salt concentration tends to migrate toward superhydrophilic areas due to evaporation-driven water flow. This real-time observation enhances our understanding of how superwetting influences salt rejection during solar evaporation, providing valuable insights for the development of more efficient solar desalination systems. For Objective 4, we used the optimized parameter to achieve a high solar evaporation rate of up to 1.82 kg per meter square per hour even with brine at high salinity (20 wt%) For objective 5, we developed a prototype for solar evaporation and performed a bacterial test to verify the evaporated and condensed water collected is bacteria-free, which can be used for future implementation of freshwater generation with this solar steam generation method.
