25215020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25215020.value: Future efforts should be spent on how to utilize the deep learning technique in massive machine-type communication (mMTC). For example, the temporal correlation in device activity is not directly available in practice. Via the historical data, we need to keep updating the statistics of temporal correlation in device activity. In such a scenario, deep learning is a good tool to simultaneously estimate the temporal correlation statistics and update the denoiser function in the approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. We will investige the role of deep learning in mMTC in the future.

25215020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25215020.value: In this project, we have investigated the massive machine-type communication (mMTC) in cellular network. Different from the conventional human-type communication technique whose focus is on high-speed communication, mMTC faces the new challenge about how to facilitate the communication from a huge number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices with low latency. In this project, we have focused on two research problems in mMTC – how to detect the active devices from a large number of IoT devices accurately and quickly, and how to decode the short packets sent from the active devices accurately and quickly. Specifically, we have designed a framework based on the approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm that can detect the active devices with a very high accuracy, when the pilot sequence length is linear to the number of devices. Moreover, we have built a covariance-based framework that can detect the active devices and decode their short messages embedded in pilot selection simultaneously. These results can contribute to the real development of the mMTC technique in both 5G and 6G cellular network.

25301320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25301320.value: Movement is one of the vital features in living systems to allow various functions related to survival and reproduction. Although, hard actuators enable energy conversion to mechanical motions for animal-like functions, soft actuators remain their technological infancy in potentially creating the next generation of biocompatible and safe actuating robotic systems and providing a link between living systems and artificial systems at multiple levels. To exert the full functional potential of soft actuators, in addition to the shape transformation/cargo transport, the comprehensive and systematic control of the intrinsic structural parameters is fundamentally crucial. Thus, developing hierarchical supramolecular soft actuators would open novel strategies for fabricating shape transformable, transportable, and tissue regenerative materials. In this proposal, we plan to explore and identify the next generation visible light driven molecular machine motifs, instead of using UV-light, and to develop the visible light driven supramolecular soft actuators. We aim to apply photoswitching donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts (DASA) amphiphiles for the proposed new visible light driven supramolecular soft actuators. We propose to develop a modular synthesis of DASA amphiphiles (DA) in order to control (a) activation wavelength of photocyclization, (b) aqueous solubility and packing parameters, and (c) mechanical strength of DAs. In addition, we will develop the DAs into novel visible light driven and mechanical strength improved supramolecular soft actuators. Through systematic studies, we plan to investigate multiple controlled transportable supramolecular soft actuators to finish sophisticated cargo transport tasks in biomimetic conditions. The proposed supramolecular soft actuator is achievement of interdisciplinary research areas between Chemistry, Materials Science, and Biotechnology. On the basis of our track record in supramolecular soft actuators of molecular motor amphiphiles research, we propose to apply the directing capability of the supramolecular soft actuators of DAs to align living cells to allow post-structural modifications and transportation. The success of this project would have a great impact on the research areas of Supramolecular Chemistry, Soft Robotic Science, and Tissue Regenerative Materials Science. 運動是生命系統中允許與生存和繁殖有關的各種功能的重要特徵之一。 硬驅動器可以將能量轉換為機械運動，以實現類似動物的功能。 軟驅動器仍處於技術起步階段，它們有可能創造出下一代的生物兼容且安全的驅動器機器系統，從而在多個層次上為生命系統和人造系統之間提供聯繫。 為了發揮軟驅動器的全部功能潛力，除了進行形狀轉換/貨物運輸外，對內在結構參數進行全面而係統的控制至關重要。 開發分級的超分子軟驅動器可能會為製造形狀可轉換，可運輸和組織再生的材料打開新的策略。 在本計劃書中，我們計劃探索下一代可見光驅動的分子機器結構，而不是利用光損壞的紫外線驅動，並開發可見光控制的超分子軟驅動器。我們旨在將光開關供體-受體Stenhouse加合物（DASA）用兩親結構來製造新型可見光控制的超分子軟驅動器。我們建議開發模塊合成來製造DASA兩親結構（DA），以控制（一）光環化的控制波長，（二）水溶性和填充參數以及（三）DAs的機械性強度。此外，我們將把DAs開發成新型的可見光控制和機械強度提高的超分子軟驅動器。通過系統的材料研究，我們計劃研究多個可控制的可運輸超分子軟驅動器，以在仿生條件下完成複雜的貨物運輸任務。當前提出的超分子軟驅動器是化學，材料科學和生物技術之間跨學科研究領域的重要產品之一。基於我們在分子運動兩親分子的超分子軟致驅動器研究中的往績，我們建議應用DAs的超分子軟驅動器的定向能力來排列活細胞，以允許進行結構後修飾和運輸。該項目的成功將對超分子化學，軟機器人科學和組織再生材料科學的研究領域產生重大影響。

25301320.label: Realisation of objectives
25301320.value: The Early Career Scheme supported the developments of hierarchical supramolecular assemblies of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adduct amphiphiles into macroscopic soft scaffold for potential macroscopic functional applications. This proposal has been completely fulfilled with fruitful research output for five publications with acknowledgement to this proposal, including, Adv. Colloid Interface Sci., Dyes Pigm., J. Colloid Interface Sci., Eur. J. Inorg. Chem., and a book chapter in Springer, Cham. In the book chapter, we were reviewing the latest development of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles in different interfaces and aqueous solutions. Amphiphilic molecules, are composed of hydrophobic and hydrophilic parts and the intrinsic tendence to assemble in aqueous conditions, producing numerous supramolecular assembled structures and functional systems. Some of the recent challenges in the design of adaptive, responsive, far-from-equilibrium functional systems in aqueous environments, the proper design of photo-controlled moieties in intrinsic charged amphiphilic molecular structures offers fruitful opportunities to create supramolecular assembly systems, based on electrostatic interaction, with response to light in aqueous environment. In this chapter, we discuss the design strategy of photo-controlled molecular amphiphiles, the supramolecular assembled structures in aqueous environment and at air–water interfaces, as well as different strategies for producing dynamic functions in both isotropic and anisotropic supramolecular assembled materials. The motions at air–water interface, foam formation, reversible supramolecular assembly at nanometer length-scale, and life-like artificial muscle function are discussed. Manipulating the molecular structural design, supramolecular assembling conditions, and external stimulation, the photo-controlled molecular amphiphiles open directions toward applications ranging from controlled bio-target delivery to soft robotic. Furthermore, the inspiration of supramolecular assembling processes observed in the publication of Eur. J. Inorg. Chem., it enabled us for developing the first visible-light controlled supramolecular transformations of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts amphiphiles at multiple length-scale (J. Colloid Interface Sci.). Designing responsive, adaptive, and dynamic supramolecular systems in water, the incorporation of photoresponsive units in amphiphilic molecular structures enables functional responses in a non-invasive way by using light. However, in aqueous media, vast majority of reported synthetic photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles are commonly driven by high energy and bio-damaging UV-light for supramolecular transformation at multiple length-scale. Herein, we present newly designed visible-light controlled supramolecular assembly of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts amphiphiles (DA) with excellent stability and solubility in aqueous media. The excellent photoswitchability in organic media and photoresponsiveness in aqueous media driven by visible-light are found, as confirmed with UV–vis absorption and NMR spectroscopies. Supramolecular assembly at multiple length-scale of DAs is investigated with electron microscopies and X-ray diffraction to show large aspect-ratio of nanostructures assembled into macroscopic soft scaffolds. Upon visible-light irradiation, the large geometrical transformation of DAs enables supramolecular transformations, and subsequently destabilizes the macroscopic soft scaffold to release fluorophores from the scaffolds. These results provide the feasibility in developing the next generation of visible-light controlled macroscopic soft functional scaffold from supramolecular assembly across multiple length-scale without and offer ample opportunity to design future soft robotic materials and functional biomaterials. However, this first demonstration of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts amphiphiles were limited by strong light source for further biological study, due to significant heat generated. In this connection, we reported the extensive work to overcome this concern by reporting red-light controlled supramolecular co-assembly transformations of stiff stilbene and donor acceptor Stenhouse adduct amphiphiles. Amphiphiles are of great interest in the search of biomimicking supramolecular assembly for their assembling into complex and hierarchical structures in aqueous media across multiple length-scale. Incorporations of photoswitching units into amphiphiles provide a means to control the morphology of the resultant assembled structures by light irradiation, which is non-invasive and generally biocompatible. The use of light to induce morphological changes offers several extra merits, including selective excitation of photoswitches by different wavelengths, high temporal- and spatial-resolution. Macroscopic soft materials assembled from donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts (DASA) amphiphiles (DA) in aqueous media are generally suffered from absorption peak broadening due to aggregation and requires strong white-light irradiation to induce a morphological change. Herein, we provide a new strategy for the restoration of red-light sensitivity of DA in aqueous medium, which requires a co-assembly system of DA with a six-membered fused ring stiff stilbene amphiphile (6SA). This 6SA:DA co-assembly forms supramolecular structures in both microscopic and macroscopic length-scale. Morphological changes of these supramolecular structures can be fine adjusted with red-light irradiation. The structural design, supramolecular assemblies and co-assemblies, and macroscopic scaffolds of photoresponsive SA and DA could enable potential visible-light controlled soft functional materials with improved biocompatibility and photosensitivity. Finally, over past three years development of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts amphiphiles, we envisioned the importance of the potential applications of donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts amphiphiles as supramolecular soft robotic systems. Lately, we have published a review manuscript as “Exploration of molecular machines in supramolecular soft robotic systems”. Soft robotic system, a new era of material science, is rapidly developing with advanced processing technology in soft matters, featured with biomimetic nature. An important bottom-up approach is through the implementation of molecular machines into polymeric materials, however, the synchronized molecular motions, acumination of strain across multiple length-scales, and amplification into macroscopic actuations remained highly challenging. This review presents the significances, key design strategies, and outlook of the hierarchical supramolecular systems of molecular machines to develop novel types of supramolecular-based soft robotic systems. 25302420.label: Project Objectives
25302420.value: Motivated by the limitations of the existing literature on distributional robustification and by the attractive properties of the celebrated Fisher-Rao distance, a new type of ambiguity set, called the Fisher-Rao ambiguity set, for distributional robustification will be explored from both modeling and algorithmic perspectives. Two new statistical tools emerged from the idea of distributional robustification with Fisher-Rao ambiguity sets will be focused and investigated thoroughly. One is the distributionally robust quadratic discriminant analysis recently proposed by the PI and his co-authors. The other is a distributionally robust covariance matrix estimator newly proposed in the project. In particular, statistical guarantees of these tools, such as finite-sample bounds and asymptotic convergences, are studied. Numerical experiments on real datasets will also be conducted to examine their practical performance. To accommodate the high-dimensional and large-scale data setting, dedicated algorithms will be developed to efficiently solve the distributionally robust optimization problems associated with the two new statistical tools. Geometric properties of these specific optimization problems, such as the KL and error bound conditions, will be studied. Theoretical results and algorithmic techniques applicable to general geodesically convex manifold optimization problems will also be developed.

25302420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25302420.value: Many computational procedures for decision making, estimation or prediction involve optimizing an objective function that depends on an input probability distribution. Procedures of this form include Kalman filtering, chance-constrained programming and stochastic programming. Very often, the ideal input distribution is unknown and replaced with an approximating distribution constructed by using some training samples generated from the ideal distribution. The decision, estimation or prediction thus obtained could be compromised or systematically biased, because of the approximation error in the input distribution. Distributional robustification emerges as an effective approach for addressing such an issue, which robustifies the computational procedure against the error by replacing the objective function in the optimization with its worst-case counterpart (maximum or minimum) over a set of probability distributions, called the ambiguity set. The resulting optimization problem is called a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problem. Due to its strong modeling power, distributional robustification finds applications across a wide range of areas including machine learning, signal processing and energy systems. Existing literature on distributional robustification focuses mainly on ambiguity sets of non-parametric probability distributions, such as those defined by Wasserstein distance, Kullback-Leibler divergence or moments. Motivated by its attractive theoretical properties, the PI and his co-authors recently proposed a novel ambiguity set, called the Fisher-Rao ambiguity set, for the parametric family of Gaussian distributions to distributionally robustify the quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA), a statistical classification tool. Although the associated DRO problem is a non-convex optimization problem, surprisingly, the PI and his co-authors developed an algorithm to solve the problem to global optimality by treating it as a manifold optimization problem and establishing its geodesic convexity. The classification performance of the new QDA is consistently better than other variants of QDAs over real datasets. In this project, the PI and his collaborator Professor Daniel Kuhn at EPFL plan to thoroughly explore distributional robustification with Fisher-Rao ambiguity sets, from both algorithmic and modeling perspectives. Besides the above-mentioned robustified QDA, distributional robustification for covariance matrix estimation with Fisher-Rao ambiguity set will also be studied. Expected contributions of the project are threefold. First, two new statistical tools, the robustified QDA and covariance matrix estimator, are investigated both theoretically and empirically. Second, efficient dedicated algorithms for solving the emerging DRO problems in high-dimensional and large-scale data setting are developed. Third, the algorithmic studies will not only contribute to these two specific problems but also advance the area of geodesically convex manifold optimization. 很多決策、估计、及預測的計算過程都涉及以某個概率分佈作为輸入的優化問題。具體例子包括Kalman濾波器、機會約束規劃和隨機規劃。许多实际场景下，由于無法为優化問題输入一个理想的概率分佈，我們常以分佈樣本作为近似。通过这一近似分布所求得的決策、估计或預測皆會受到样本誤差的影響。分佈式魯棒優化是一個减小这一影响的有效途徑。分佈式魯棒優化的原理是首先建構一個跟理想分佈相近的分布集合，然後在该分布集合中選取對决策者最不利的分佈作為優化問題的輸入。分佈魯棒優化已被廣泛應用到包括机器学习、信号处理和能源在内的多個領域。 上述提到的跟理想分佈相近的分布集合稱為歧義集。现有的分佈式魯棒優化的歧義集多基于Wasserstein距離、Kullback-Leibler散度或矩信息。項目負責人及其合著者最近提出了一種新的基于統計學中Fisher-Rao距離的歧義集 并應用于二次判別分析。雖然所涉及到的優化問題是非凸的，但通过把問題轉化成一個流形優化問題，可證明了這一流形優化問題是測地線凸的。因此，可利用流形優化演算法求出全局最優解。通过真實數據上的實驗結果，基于分布式魯棒優化所建立的二次判別分析比傳統的二次判別分析效果更好。有見及此，項目負責人和項目合作者Daniel Kuhn希望進一步探討基于Fisher-Rao歧義集的分佈式魯棒優化及其应用，并设计相应的演算法。本项目的主要貢獻將有以下三個。第一，項目負責人和項目合作者Daniel Kuhn會集中探討兩类由Fisher-Rao分佈魯棒優化所產生的統計工具：二次判別分析和共變異數矩陣估計。第二，為這兩类問題设计專門的演算法，以提升計算速度及其在大规模问题中的应用。第三，研發專門演算法的過程亦會促進一般的測地線凸流形優化問題的發展。

25302420.label: Realisation of objectives
25302420.value: Objective 1 has been very successfully achieved. In this project, I have thoroughly studied the use of Fisher-Rao distance in distributionally robust optimization from both modelling and algorithmic perspectives. In particular, the proposed approach, Fisher-Rao distributional robustification, has been incorporated into several machine learning tools, including discriminant analysis, covariance matrix estimation, domain adaptation, and recourse generation. Moreover, since modern applications of these machine learning tools are often high-dimensional and data-intensive, and also since the robustified models are more complicated than their non-robust counterparts, solving the resulting optimization problems is very challenging. Therefore, for all these robustified machine learning tools, I have also developed specialized algorithms to facilitate fast solution. For Objective 2, I have studied the asymptotic consistency and established a non-asymptotic finite sample performance bound of the robustified machine learning approaches. The empirical performance of all these robustified machine learning approaches have also been studied through extensive numerical experiments based on both synthetic and real datasets. As for Objective 3, the geometric properties of distributionally robust optimization models under Fisher-Rao ambiguity and other closely related ambiguity concepts have been analyzed. These geometric properties are in turn also utilized in the above-mentioend algorithmic studies. All in all, all the three objectives are satisfactorily attained.

25302420.label: Major findings and research outcome
25302420.value: The major findings of this project are threefold. First, Fisher-Rao robustification can indeed be integrated into many existing machine learning, signal processing and statistical approaches. Second, the resulting distributionally robust optimization problems enjoy many interesting geometric properties. Carefully exploiting these properties can lead to fast algorithms. Third, the practical performance of distributionally robust optimization under Fisher-Rao ambiguity is promising in many applications, not only outperforming the non-robust approaches but also the robust apporaches under other ambiguity sets. These findings are published in 4 journal (Mathematical Programming, SIAM Journal on Optimization, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis, Computational Optimization and Applications) papers and 1 conference paper (ICML). These are all top journals or conference in the area of optimization and machine learning.

25302420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25302420.value: There are several problems for further research. First, in parctical applications, it is often difficult for the decision maker to know which type of ambiguity sets would perform well beforehand. Thus, an important research direction is to theoretically compare the performance of distributionally robust optimization models under different ambiguity sets. This would provide the decision maker useful insights about when to adopt the Fisher-Rao robusitification and when not. Second, the success of distributionally robust optimization often relies critically on the size of the ambiguity set, as parametrized by the radius. In practice, this model parameter is often tuned by heuristics or by the computationally expensive cross validation procedure. It would be interesting to see whether one can develop a data-driven approach for tuning the radius parameter that is computationally friendly.

25302420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25302420.value: In many real-world situations, one is tasked with making a decision with using input data. However, the data is often noisy, biased, incomplete or unreliable in some other manner. This project develops methodologies for tackling such decision making problems. The conducted research is particularly important in some high-stake applications (such as those involing human or a large amount of money) where the decision makers tend to be risk-averse. The methodologies developed in this project enjoys not only robustness against the uncertain data but also scalable algorithms for computing the decisions.

25500520.label: Project Objectives

To develop a methodology for optimal keyword selection and effective feature selection with the aim of achieving ideal predictive performance using online big data. To generate demand forecasts for a tourism destination (i.e., Hong Kong) and tourist attractions in Hong Kong by incorporating online big data from multiple sources, including search traffic data and social media data. To examine whether tourism demand prediction models based on a combination of search traffic and social media data are superior to those based on search traffic data or social media data alone; and to compare whether prediction models based on the sentiment and volume of social media data can obtain accuracy similar to or greater than prediction models using search traffic data.

25500520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25500520.value: Given the tourism industry’s substantial contributions to the economy, researchers continue to seek optimal ways to accurately monitor and forecast tourism demand (including demand for tourism destinations and attractions). Internet big data provide a valuable opportunity: compared to traditional variables, internet big data possess advantages such as being publicly available, free of charge, and accessible in real time and at high frequencies. These data also constitute a direct and comprehensive measure of tourist behaviour and are thus sensitive to shifts in tourism demand and tourists’ preferences. These benefits make internet big data an effective supplement to conventional determinants of tourism demand. Precise and timely tourism demand monitoring and forecasting provide crucial information for policy development and decision making in the government and business sectors. However, most studies on tourism demand forecasting using internet big data have focused on individual sources and search engine data; few have incorporated social media data or internet big data from multiple sources into forecasting models. Yet search engine data simply indicate tourists’ interest levels; whether growing interest arises from positive or negative circumstances remains unknown. Therefore, an estimated demand forecasting model may not work well if negative circumstances occur but high attention persists toward a specific tourism destination or attraction. This project proposes a new direction to bridge this gap: tourism demand monitoring and forecasting that incorporate tourist interest and tourist sentiment analysis based on internet big data from multiple sources. To achieve this research objective, this study takes tourism demand in Hong Kong and tourist attractions in Hong Kong as sample cases and gathers two types of internet big data via a crowd-based keyword selection method: (1) search traffic data from search engines and official websites of given tourism destinations/attractions; and (2) social media data from internet forums, microblogs, and online review platforms. The collected data are then analysed, after which volume- and valence-based variables are calculated using frequency analysis and aspect-based sentiment analysis, respectively. These calculated variables will then be used to monitor real-time tourist activities. The most useful variables, per extraction via a machine-learning-based feature selection approach, will be applied to forecast tourism demand in a timely manner by incorporating traditional time series/econometric models and nonlinear artificial intelligence models. The results are expected to provide valuable practical implications for Hong Kong SAR and destinations in terms of tourism demand monitoring and forecasting. 鉴于旅游业对经济的巨大贡献，研究人员继续探索能够准确的监测和预测旅游需求（包括对旅游目的地和景点的需求）的最佳方法。互联网大数据提供了宝贵的机会：与传统变量相比，互联网大数据具有诸如可公开获得，免费，以及实时且高频率的优势。这些数据还可以直接和全面地衡量游客的行为与活动，因此对旅游需求和游客偏好的变化十分敏感。这些优势使互联网大数据成为传统的旅游需求预测因素的有效补充。 准确及时的旅游需求监测与预测能够为政府和商业部门的政策制定和决策提供重要信息和依据。但是，大多数基于互联网大数据的旅游需求预测研究都集中在使用单个来源的大数据和搜索引擎数据上；很少有人将社交媒体数据或多来源的互联网大数据纳入预测模型中。然而，搜索引擎数据只能表明游客的关注/兴趣水平；人们不断增长的关注/兴趣是由积极还是消极的情况产生仍然未知。因此，如果出现消极情况但对特定旅游目的地或景点的高度关注/兴趣依然存在，基于搜索引擎数据的需求预测模型可能无法很好地发挥作用。该项目为弥合这一研究差距提出了一个新的方向：基于多来源互联网大数据游客关注/兴趣和游客舆情分析的旅游需求监测和预测。为了实现这一目标，本研究以香港和香港特定旅游景点的旅游需求为例，通过基于人群的关键词选择方法收集了两种类型的互联网大数据：（1）来自搜索引擎以及特定旅游目的地/景点官方网站的搜索流量数据；（2）来自互联网论坛，微博和在线评论网站的社交媒体数据。在此基础上，对收集到的数据进行分析，即使用频数分析法来计算基于量的变量和使用基于方面的情感分析来计算基于价的变量。这些计算出的变量将用于监测实时游客活动。然后，通过基于机器学习的特征选择方法提取出最有用的变量，并将这些变量输入传统的时间序列/计量经济模型和非线性人工智能模型用于及时的旅游需求预测。研究结果预期将对香港特别行政区和目的地的旅游需求监测及预测提供宝贵的实践意义。

25500520.label: Realisation of objectives
25500520.value: The objectives of our project have been fully met, as illustrated by the substantial research output. First, by integrating tourist-generated online review data from TripAdvisor into the demand forecasting system, we forecasted tourism demand for Hong Kong using online reviews data of tourist attractions, hotels, and shopping markets. Multiple models (e.g., SARIMA-MIDAS, SARIMAX) were estimated, and ex-post forecasts were generated and compared. One group compared SARIMA-MIDAS (1) to time-series models like SARIMA and SNAIVE. The other group compared SARIMA-MIDAS(1) to the constant frequency SARIMAX model, which used the total number of monthly online reviews and ratings as an explanatory variable. Finally, the third group compared SARIMA-MIDAS(1) with the number of online reviews and ratings to the SARIMA-MIDAS(2) model with decomposed weekly online review variables. Forecasting performance measures (MAE, MAPE, RMSE, RMSPE, and MASE) were calculated for each model. Findings confirmed that tourism demand forecasting based on online review data using mixed-frequency model can significantly improve forecasting performance. The research output has been successfully published in Tourism Management as an ESI Highly Cited Paper: ‘Hu, M., Li, H., Song, H., Li, X., & Law, R. (2022). Tourism demand forecasting using tourist-generated online review data. Tourism Management, 90, 104490.’ Afterwards, we further incorporate online big data from multiple sources, including search traffic data and social media data, into the tourism demand forecasting system. We also applied the ‘crowd-squared’ approach to select the optimal keywords for tourism demand forecasting. Utilizing surveys involving 500 participants, we obtained the optimal keywords for the collection of search query data. On the basis of fine-grained aspect-level sentiment analysis and hybrid feature engineering, we used multisource data (i.e., official announcement data, search engine data, and online review data) to forecast tourism demand for tourism attractions. In order to achieve the objective of a tourism demand monitoring and forecasting framework based on online search queries and reviews data, we used data from dianping.com (online reviews data) and baidu.com (search volume data) to forecast the tourist arrivals for tourist attractions in China. By employing aspect-based sentiment analysis technologies (e.g., the ernie_1.0_skep_large_chit model) and search volume frequency analysis, we mined a series of variables, including high-frequency search query volume and tourists’ attitude information towards different aspects of tourist attractions. Further, we compared multiple groups of models' performance, both externally and internally. From an external perspective, we compared the predictive accuracy of the models without Internet big data and the models with single-source Internet big data to investigate whether search engine data remained effective for tourism demand forecasting. We further compared the predictive accuracy of models with single-source Internet big data and models with multisource Internet big data to examine whether tourism demand prediction models based on a combination of search traffic and social media data are superior to those based on search traffic data. From an internal perspective, we compared models with and without aspect-based sentiment variables to investigate whether prediction models based on the aspect-based sentiment and volume of social media data can obtain accuracy similar to or greater than prediction models using search traffic data. Findings confirmed that the tourism demand forecasting framework via aspect-based sentiment analysis-based online review data and search engine data maintain stable predictive power, especially during times of uncertainty; and the combination of search engine data, generic review sentiment data, and aspect-based review sentiment data is superior to search engine data when forecasting tourism demand. The research output has been successfully published in the Annals of Tourism Research: “Li, H., Gao, H., & Song, H. (2023). tourism forecasting with granular sentiment analysis. Annals of Tourism Research, 103, 103667.” Meanwhile, to achieve an effective feature selection framework with the aim of obtaining ideal predictive performance using online big data, we used Baidu search query data from mobile devices and PCs to forecast tourist arrivals for tourist attractions in China. Search query data was then divided into three categories by terminal: search queries via PCs, search queries via mobile devices, and their simple aggregate. Then we adopted the feature selection method based on a Boruta algorithm to choose search keywords with the most predictive power. Afterwards, we developed several models to test the forecasting power of search query data via different terminals: benchmark models (e.g., autoregressive integrated moving average model), main forecasting models (e.g., ARIMAX), and robustness check forecasting models (e.g., AR). Findings confirmed that patterns of tourism-related search queries differed significantly across mobile devices and PCs. Findings also confirmed that models incorporating Boruta algorithm-based search queries from PCs can greatly improve the accuracy of tourism demand forecasting compared with other models. The research output has been successfully published in the International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management: ‘Hu, M., Xiao, M., & Li, H. (2021). Which search queries are more powerful in tourism demand forecasting: searches via mobile device or PC?. International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management, 33(6), 2022-2043.’

25500520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25500520.value: The research has significant potential for further development. Future work will focus on two aspects: the first aspect will be based on multimodal big data fusion forecasting in tourism, and the second aspect will be based on tourism forecasting via interpretable machine learning. We aim to expand and propose noval data fusion technology for forecasting tourism demand based on multimodal big data involving numeric data, text data, image data, and video data from multiple sources (e.g., online review platforms and search engine platforms). The outcomes of this study will also contribute to enhancing the efficiency of planning and management for tourist attractions or destinations. Meanwhile, with the increasing development of artificial intelligence, we will also develop different interpretable machine learning frameworks for forecasting tourism demand, which will allow us to mine the crucial features or factors influencing tourism demand. The result will also help practitioners rellocate resources in the tourism industry according to the importance of interpretable factors.

25500520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25500520.value: We monitored and forecasted tourism demand using online search traffic and sentiment analysis-based social media data to investigate the predicting power of multisource big data in tourism forecasting. The significance and value of the research project are multifold. We make an initial and meaningful attempt to incorporate online review data into destination-based tourism demand forecasting. By employing the sentiment analysis-based online review data reflecting different tourism industry dimensions into tourism demand forecasting, decision makers can determine which sectors contribute most to fluctuating destination demand based on tourists’ attention and sentiments. Furthermore, by integrating the Internet data from multiple sources, capitalizing on their unique strengths, we enrich and enhance tourism demand prediction by harnessing multisource and complementary Internet information to forecast tourism demand. Meanwhile, our study extends previous studies by comparing forecasting performance based on mobile search query data and PC data. This finding holds particular value for the tourism industry in identifying effective search terminals to predict tourism demand. Overall, our research will advance techniques for tourism demand analysis and provide a comprehensive understanding of using multiple forms of online big data to improve forecasting accuracy. Such outcomes will promote more efficient planning and management for tourism development.

25508220.label: Project Objectives
25508220.value: While firms generally prefer to select bigger and more active online influencers to promote their brands/products on social media, some marketers caution that working with influencers with an extremely large following, or extremely high posting activity, can be detrimental to post engagement (eMarketer 2017; Pierucci 2018), suggesting possible nonlinearity in their effects. However, previous studies have limited their attention to the linear effects of influencers’ following size and posting activity on post engagement (Hughes, Swaminathan, and Brooks 2019; Stephen et al. 2017). That is, they have failed to consider both the benefits and the costs associated with these influencer characteristics. To fill this gap, the first objective of this proposal is to examine the nonlinear impact of influencers’ following size and posting activity on post engagement. Specifically, this research posits that an online influencer’s following size (H1) and posting activity (H2) have an inverted U-shaped effect on post engagement. Second, building on recent literature examining the interactive effects of source and post characteristics on campaign outcomes (Hughes et al. 2019; Kupfer et al. 2018), this proposal identifies two meaningful post-level moderators—post authenticity and post content type (promotional vs. nonpromotional)—for the effect of influencer characteristics on post engagement. Specifically, this research proposes that an influencer’s post authenticity positively moderates the effect of following size (H3a) and posting activity (H3b) on post engagement. The study further proposes that the effect of following size is stronger (H4a), and that of posting activity is weaker (H4b), on post engagement for promotional than nonpromotional content. Third, I will conduct two lab studies (Studies 1 and 2) to test the main effect of an online influencer’s following size and posting activity on people’s actual engagement behavior with the influencer’s post (H1 and H2). By manipulating these influencer characteristics, the studies aim to establish the causal effects of following size and posting activity on post engagement. Fourth, a longitudinal study (Study 3) will test the interplay between influencer and post characteristics on post engagement (H1–H4) by using a rich set of OIM campaign field data on Weibo from one of the largest OIM platforms in China. While prior studies on OIM use different metrics, such as the number of post likes, comments, or shares, to measure engagement (Hughes et al. 2019; Lee, Honsanagar, and Nair 2018), they have not taken into account firms’ investments in OIM. Firms offer incentives (e.g., money, free products) to online influencers to write about their brands/products, ranging from several hundred to millions of US dollars per post. To more accurately evaluate the efficiency of each OIM post in driving engagement, Study 3 will utilize unique cost data of OIM posts to measure the posts’ engagement ROI (or total number of likes, comments, and shares per invested dollar). Practically, the findings will provide guidance to marketers in their influencer selection decisions. As firms are paying substantial fees to engage extremely large and active online influencers to promote their brands/products, this research forewarns marketers that this tactic may backfire and lead to lower post engagement. Firms are also advised to encourage post authenticity by granting influencers more creative freedom in content creation because it will enhance the effects of both following size and posting activity on post engagement. Moreover, firms are advised that the importance of influencers’ following size and posting activity in driving post engagement depends on whether an OIM post is promotional (vs. nonpromotional). Specifically, the effect of following size is stronger, but that of posting activity is weaker, on post engagement for promotional versus nonpromotional content.

25508220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508220.value: Online influencer marketing (OIM) has become an integral component of firms’ marketing strategies. With OIM, firms select and incentivize online influencers to create and/or share content about their brands/products with followers on social media to increase product awareness, reinforce favorable brand attitudes, and strengthen firms’ relationships with consumers. Firms often consider two influencer characteristics—following size (i.e., number of followers) and posting activity (i.e., frequency of content transmission on social media)—when they select influencers. While firms generally prefer to select bigger and more active influencers, marketers caution that working with influencers with an extremely large following, or extremely high posting activity, can be detrimental to post engagement, suggesting possible nonlinearity in their effects. However, prior studies have limited their attention to the linear effects of influencers’ following size and posting activity in driving consumer engagement with an influencer post. To fill this gap, this proposed research draws on the theory of engagement to examine the nonlinear impact of these influencer characteristics on post engagement. Specifically, by jointly considering the benefits and costs associated with these influencer characteristics, this research posits that both an influencer’s following size and posting activity have an inverted U-shaped effect on post engagement. The study also identifies two unique post characteristics—post authenticity (i.e., the extent to which an influencer’s post is genuine, real, and true to her/his own voice) and post content type (i.e., promotional vs. nonpromotional)—that are expected to moderate the effect of influencer characteristics on post engagement. Three empirical studies are planned to test the proposed conceptual framework. Studies 1 and 2 are laboratory studies that manipulate an influencer’s following size and posting activity, respectively, to test their causal effects on post engagement. Study 3 is a longitudinal study that tests the full conceptual model by using a rich set of OIM campaign field data from one of the largest OIM platforms in China. This proposed research is expected to contribute to the emerging literature on OIM by identifying the nonlinear effects of influencers’ following size and posting activity on post engagement. It will also build on recent literature examining the interactive effects of source and post characteristics on OIM campaign outcomes. Furthermore, the findings are expected to provide practical guidance to marketers in their selection of influencers based on both influencer and post characteristics to increase consumer engagement. 網絡紅人營銷已經成為企業營銷策略中不可或缺的組成部分。通過網絡紅人營銷，企業挑選並激勵網絡紅人在社交媒體上分享關於其品牌或產品的內容，以提高產品知名度、增強良好的品牌態度、並加強企業與消費者的關系。企業經常以網絡紅人的粉絲數量和發帖數量作為挑選網絡紅人的標准。雖然企業通常喜歡選擇更多粉絲、更活躍的網絡紅人，但亦有市場營銷人員提醒說，與擁有大量粉絲或經常發帖的網絡紅人合作可能對發布內容的參與度有害，表明他們可能存在非線性的影響。 然而，過去的文獻主要研究網絡紅人的粉絲數量和發帖數量在驅動消費者參與度的影響上的線性效應。為了填補這一空白，本項目擬利用參與度理論來研究這些網絡紅人特征對社交媒體內容參與度的非線性影響。通過綜合考慮與這些網絡紅人特征相關的利益和成本，本項目假設網絡紅人的粉絲數量和發帖數量對內容參與度有倒U型曲線的影響。本項目還識別了兩個獨特的帖子特征——帖子真實性（即帖子是否忠於網絡紅人本人真實的聲音）及帖子內容類型（促銷型或非促銷型）——將改變網絡紅人特征對內容參與度的影響。 本項目計劃通過三個實証研究來檢驗所提出的概念模型。其中兩個是實驗室研究，分別操縱網絡紅人的粉絲數量和發帖數量，以檢驗他們對內容參與度的因果影響。第三項研究是一項縱向研究，通過使用來自中國最大的網絡紅人營銷平台之一的豐富數據來測試完整的概念模型。 通過識別網絡紅人的粉絲數量和發帖數量對內容參與度的非線性影響，本項目有望為網絡紅人營銷方面的新興文獻作出貢獻。它還將為近期關於發帖者和帖子特征對網絡紅人營銷效果的互動影響的文獻作出貢獻。此外，本項目的研究結果可為市場營銷人員提供通過網絡紅人和帖子特征挑選網絡紅人以提高消費者參與度的實用指導。

25600120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25600120.value: Background Empirical studies have identified over-exposure of screen time to be associated with negative physical health and mental health. However, previous findings mainly derived from cross-sectional data and the temporal relationships between variables remain uncertain. Although local and international health organizations recommend children be exposed to no more than 2 hours of screen time per day, the recommendations are oversimplified and do not consider whether different types of screen media and content have different impacts on children’s health and mental health. Furthermore, little is known about the mechanisms underlying the association between screen time and health and mental health outcomes. Objectives The proposed longitudinal study will examine the effects of the amount of screen time on children’s health and mental health. It will also investigate the effects of different types of screen media and content on different aspects of health and mental health in children, and to test the individual and relationship factors mediating the association between screen time and children’s health and mental health. Study design 2,352 parents of children attending Grades 1 to 6 (ages 6 to 11 years) of ten primary schools in Hong Kong will be recruited using stratified random sampling by five major districts in Hong Kong and two school types. The parents will be invited to complete a questionnaire regarding their children’s screen time, health and mental health at baseline and at 12-month follow up. A sub-sample of 300 parents will be randomly selected to report children’s screen time and health at three-month intervals during the 12-month period. Contributions The proposed study will provide academic and practical implications on the issue. In particular, the study will provide evidence on different health impacts associated with specific types of screen media and content, which is under-explored in the current literature. Also, the study’s findings on the mediating factors influencing the association between screen time and health and mental health will inform the development of prevention and intervention programs. In terms of practical implications, the findings will provide practical recommendations for parents, teachers, and professionals regarding children’s use of ST, and inform development of evidence-based guidelines and recommendations for children’s screen time. 研究背景 大量的實證研究已確認過多的螢幕時間與負向身心健康的關聯。然而，過往的研究結果主要來自橫截面數據，而不同變量之間的時間關係仍不明確。儘管本地及國際間的健康組織均建議兒童每天的螢幕時間不應超過兩小時，但此建議實為過於簡單化，而且並未將不同類型的屏幕媒體及內容對兒童所帶來的各種身心健康的影響納入考量。再者，現時關於螢幕時間與身心健康之間關聯性的底層機制還知之甚少。 研究目標 本縱貫性研究旨在檢視螢幕時間的長短對兒童健康和心理健康的影響，亦將探討不同類型的螢幕媒介及內容對兒童各方面的健康和心理健康的影響。此外，本研究亦將測量個人與人際關係因素在螢幕時間與兒童健康和心理健康之間關聯的中介效果。 研究設計 本研究對象為就讀小一至小六（年齡為6至11歲）的學生家長，採用分層隨機抽樣，以香港五個主要地區及兩類學校為依據，抽取十所小學，招募人數共計2,352人。家長將被邀請在基線階段及十二個月後的跟進調查時，完成一份有關其子女的螢幕時間及身體及心理健康狀況的問卷。其後，將在總樣本中隨機抽取300位家長作次樣本，他們將需要在研究開始的十二個月期間，每三個月報告子女的螢幕時間及健康狀況。 貢獻 是項擬議研究將能就此議題提供學術及實務上的應用。這研究尤其將針對現有文獻未被充分探索的部分，能就著各種健康影響與特定的屏幕媒體及內容之間的關聯提供證據。本研究中有關中介因素影響螢幕時間與身心健康間關聯的結果，能有助制訂相關的預防和介入計劃。在實務應用方面，此研究的成果能為家長、教師及專業人士於兒童的螢幕使用時間上提供切實可行的建議，並有助建立實證為本的指引及與此議題相關的建議。

25600220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25600220.value: On Sept 2015, 193 United Nations member-state countries ratified the Sustainable Development Goals, which is a call for action by all countries (rich, poor, and middle-income) to tackle some of the biggest problems all societies face. Goal 1 is to “end poverty in all its forms everywhere” by 2030. In 2016, The American Academy of Social Work and Social Welfare announced its initiative, The Grand Challenges for Social Work, which outline 12 calls for action for social work researchers and practitioners to prioritize and work together to address, including “reduce extreme economic inequality” and “building financial capacity for all.” As societies worldwide experience unprecedented rates of population ageing and the risk of entry into or deepening of poverty may increase with old age, achieving these ambitious goals requires a deepened understanding of poverty in late life and innovative interventions to address old age poverty. While old age poverty is not a new phenomenon, it is a persistent problem in many societies (e.g., according to the most recent data, old age poverty rates in Switzerland, Japan, United States, Australia, and Korea, were 19.5%, 19.6%, 19.6%, 23.2%, and 43.8% respectively) and a growing problem in Hong Kong, whereby old age poverty rates have increased significantly over the past three decades, from 27.7% in 1991 to 44.4% in 2017. Old age poverty has adverse consequences including various negative physical and mental health outcomes for individuals and greater public expenditure on healthcare and social services, constraints on GDP and economic growth, and widening of the societal inequality gap. It is a complex and multi-faceted problem, and there is a lack of knowledge on how contextual factors and processes across the life span (e.g., childhood, adolescence, early adulthood, middle adulthood, and older adulthood) shape and influence the current poverty situation of older adults. Addressing this population as a static and homogenous rather than a diverse and dynamic group is another reason why old age poverty continues to be a problem. The proposed study seeks to address these two gaps by examining, through qualitative life history interviews, the poverty dynamics across the life span of a growing subgroup of the elderly poor – elder-headed household with older adults who live alone or with their spouse only. The proposed impact is that unique patterns of poverty across the life span will be identified that implicate late life poverty; thus informing old age poverty interventions for this target group. 2015年9月，193個聯合國會員國簽署了多項可持續發展目標，目的為呼籲所有國家（富裕，貧窮和中等收入）解決現今各社會面臨的多個最重大的問題。第一項目標是到2030年，在世界各地消 除一切形式的貧窮。相似地,，美國社會工作與社會福利學院於2016年宣布了其倡議：「社會工作的重大挑戰」。倡議中概述了十二項行動呼籲，包括「減少極端的貧富差距」及「為所有人建立財務能力」，要求社會工作研究人員和從業人員將之列為首要並共同解決。由於世界各地的社會正經歷著前所未有的人口老齡化，長者步入或深陷於貧困的風險亦隨之而增加，因此，要實現上述這些宏偉的目標，就必須加深對晚年貧困的認識，並採取創新的解決措施。儘管晚年貧困不是一個新的社會現象，它仍然是一個持續困擾不少國家的社會問題（例如， 據最新數據顯示，瑞士、日本、美國、澳大利亞和韓國的晚年貧困率分別為19.5％，19.6 ％，19.6％，23.2％和43.8％），也是一個香港正面對的嚴重問題。在過去的三十年間，香港的晚年貧困率已從1991年的27.7％增加到2017年的44.4％，情況日益嚴峻。事實上，晚年貧困會為長者和社會帶來各種不良的後果，包括對個人的身心健康造成各種負面影響，令醫療保健和社會服務上的公共支出增加、GDP和經濟增長受到限制以及社會不平等差距擴大等。這是一個既複雜又多元化的問題，而對於壽命期間的情境因素和過程（如童年，青春期，成年初期，成年中期和成年年齡）如何形成及影響老年人當前面對的貧困處境，社會也缺乏認知。晚年貧困持續成為問題的另一個原因，是社會將老年人視為不變和相似的，而非多樣而不斷變化的群體。因此，本擬議的研究項目旨在通過生活史訪談，探討晚年貧困長者中的次群「獨居或僅與配偶同住的長者家庭」在壽命期間中的貧困動態。擬議項目的學術及社會層面貢獻是，將確定整個壽命期間形成晚年貧困的獨特模式，從而為這目標群組提供解決晚年貧困的介入措施。

25600220.label: Realisation of objectives
25600220.value: Objective 1: Exploring and Describing Poverty Dynamics across the Life Span of Poor Elder-Headed Households in Hong Kong This first research objective was effectively realized through the use of life history interviews. This retrospective longitudinal approach allowed us to delve into and describe the patterns of entry into and exit from poverty, as well as the duration of poverty experiences. The research encompassed data gathered from 60 poor elder-headed households (at the mid-term we had 59, but in the end, we were able to recruit 1 more participant to complete the original sample of 60). Each interview, lasting between 1.5 to 2 hours, provided rich and detailed data that provided an extensive description of the poverty dynamics across the lifespan of these households. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the data. A hybrid approach to coding was used, utilizing both deductive codes derived from the theoretical framework and inductive codes specific to the Hong Kong context. The findings revealed an extensive history of chronic poverty amongst almost all participants, extending back to their childhood. Specifically, early school dropouts, extreme poverty experiences, and/or war and the cultural revolution during childhood and youth were identified as significant events leading to the entry into poverty. In-work poverty and divorce during young and middle adulthood were found to maintain poverty, while acquisition of public rental housing served as an interrupter. Late-life events such as involuntary retirement and spousal caregiving were identified as maintainers of poverty, whereas social protections in old age served as interrupters. In conclusion, the research project successfully realized its first objective of exploring and describing the poverty dynamics across the lifespan of poor elder-headed households in Hong Kong. Objective 2: Identifying and Explaining How Earlier Life Events Impact Poverty in Older Adulthood The second objective of this research project was effectively accomplished. The study findings helped to explain how various individual actions (e.g., divorce/separation) and institutional mechanisms (e.g., PRH) across the life span, impacted late-life poverty. The common trajectory identified among participants involved entering extreme poverty during childhood and youth, transitioning into working poor status in adulthood, and maintaining their poverty status in late life but feeling more secure through old-age social security. When interpreting the study findings to explore the implications for enhancing older adults’ lives, there is a need for cradle-to-grave institutional mechanisms to address late-life poverty – particularly, social protection policies and interventions for the working poor in adulthood. Research consistently demonstrates the effectiveness of various safety net programs in improving childhood poverty and wellbeing, and also inclusion of child tax credits and universal child allowances or in-kind benefits such as early childhood education. Similarly, but for older adults, research has supported the anti-poverty effects of social pensions, while less attention has focused on institutional mechanisms for the working poor and on examining the relationships between in-work poverty during people’s working life and their late-life poverty. This focus (which this study highlights) is particularly important, in the context of rapidly aging populations, fiscal austerity, and the redesigning of pension systems toward defined-benefit pension plans, which is the case in Hong Kong with the MPF (shifting the responsibility of savings to the employee) and toward expansion of private pension provisions to supplement or replace public pension systems. As governments reform their pension systems in response to population aging, they need to examine the implications for the working poor who are entering their later-life years. Longitudinal panel research can be particularly useful for examining the policy effects of safety net programs for the working poor in late life. The findings also suggest that social and public housing is a central intervention for addressing late-life poverty, especially in contexts like Hong Kong, with some of the least affordable housing in the world and consequently where social and public housing may be more important than individual cash benefits. Most discussions on safety net programs for older adults have focused on pension systems as a key intervention for addressing late-life poverty. However, with increasing housing prices and an affordability crisis, and a trend away from traditional investments in public housing and toward market-based/demand-side initiatives such as housing vouchers, the implications of social and public housing programs should be a central focus in discussions and practices for addressing late-life poverty. Such programs significantly influence older adults’ capacities to age in place. In conclusion, through the identification of key life events leading to poverty in older adulthood and the explanation of their impact, the research project has successfully realized its second objective. The comprehensive analysis of individual actions and institutional mechanisms, coupled with a detailed understanding of poverty trajectories, provides a framework to inform future policy and intervention strategies aimed at mitigating late-life poverty. Objective three Examine the implications of gender and living arrangements on poverty dynamics across the life span experienced by different elder-headed households: female living alone, male living alone, and living only with spouse. The third objective was partially met due to recruitment hurdles. We worked only with HKCNP instead of three organizations due to difficulty in recruiting more partners. Albeit, we were able to engage 17 community-based entities under HKCNP across Hong Kong, ensuring participant diversity. Despite aiming at a balanced subsample, we ended up with 38 single females, 11 single males, and 11 living with a spouse only. Efforts to achieve a balanced subsample included multiple meetings with HKCNP, targeted recruitment efforts, and outreach calls. Despite these, we couldn't reach the 20/20/20 subsample balance. Even with these limitations, the sample offered in-depth insights (due to the large amount of data collected from each participant) into how gender and living arrangements impact poverty. Two unique insights emerged. First, is around the theme of divorce/separation as a poverty maintainer, showing notable gender differences. Most of the older women living alone, related how their divorce/separation early on in life (e.g., adulthood) contributed to their poverty during their working adulthood age. Conversely, for some male participants who married late (55+) and to younger non-Hong Kong resident partners they faced late-life divorces or separations (60+), often losing public housing, that intensified their poverty in later life. While the financial impacts of divorce on women especially are well documented, late life or “grey divorces” are underexamined, and can worsen financial strain due to limited recovery opportunities. Thus, this area is a future area that can be explored. Another key insight was that late-life caregiving maintained poverty in elder-headed households with a dependent spouse. This underlines the need to support spousal caregiving in such households, as it risks poverty, particularly for independent-elder-headed households. Several crucial areas need further exploration. Firstly, early intervention is vital, through raising awareness, enhancing help-seeking behaviour, and increasing public support for older couples when one becomes a caregiver. Secondly, we must investigate the support mechanisms for older caregivers, considering both financial aid and in-kind assistance like home-care services, besides old-age provisions. Lastly, with changing living arrangements of older adults, the impact of spousal caregivers needs special attention. Thus, the research still provided in-depth insights into answering this objective, but more male and spouse only participants may have provided additional themes.

25600220.label: Major findings and research outcome
25600220.value: This qualitative study investigated poverty dynamics across the lifespan in underprivileged elder-headed households in Hong Kong, considering significant events and their impact on poverty transitions and duration. It examined how past life events cumulatively influence poverty in older adulthood and assessed the role of gender and living arrangements in poverty experienced by different elder-headed households. This research revealed that individuals who work in precarious jobs their whole working life often remained impoverished in later life, especially those recently retired due to health issues or ageism, not residing in public housing, and ineligible for social assistance due to their pension. Their pension (the Mandatory Provident Fund) amount, exceeded the allowable amount to be eligible for social assistance, yet only ensure one to two years under substandard living conditions. This highlights a crucial subgroup falling through policy gaps, pointing to an intervention need. This research also found that alleviating poverty in old age and challenges of living alone necessitates activating not only external and systemic resources but also the intrinsic capacities and strengths of older adults themselves. It also revealed the unmet needs of low income, older men living alone, a subgroup whose needs may not be met by mainstream social care programs. The key research outcomes included a local research dissemination workshop (shared in Part C) that engaged 40 practitioners/service providers from the Hong Kong Church Network for the Poor, who support impoverished older adults. This led to the creation of a working group to co-design a "train-the-trainers" program for low-income, older men living alone. This workshop also fostered collaboration with HKCNP on the PI's recently funded GRF project (to start Jan 2024) examining early retirement among Hong Kong's older working poor. Key international research outcomes include 2 published articles (see Part C, 2022 and 2023 publications) and 1 under review. One article (Conducting LifeHistory Interviews with Older Adults with Lived Experiences of Poverty: Reflections from Millennial and Gen Z Researchers) is in a top 5% Scopus-ranked journal. Other outcomes include two guest lectures (one for academics, and students; another for practitioners) at the University of the Philippines, sharing study findings (also mentioned in Part C, Dec 2023 event).

25600220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25600220.value: As noted in 6.1, research development and actions have commenced. A future research direction emerged, focusing on understanding and supporting income-poor older men living alone. A HKCNP working group was established, implementing a "train-the-trainers" program to co-design, implement, and evaluate a pilot program - a walking group for this subgroup, blending physical and social aspects. The evaluation involves interviews with participants to understand their experiences and the group's impact. Funded by the PI's Thetos Foundation grant, this program is in progress, due to complete in June 2024. Another critical finding from the study was that individuals with a history of precarious employment often remain impoverished in later life, particularly those recently retired due to health or ageism, not living in public housing, and ineligible for social assistance due to their pension. Their pension (Mandatory Provident Fund) exceeds the eligibility limit for social assistance, yet only provides for one to two years of substandard living, illustrating a policy gap. This finding informed the PI's recently funded GRF proposal to study early retirement experiences among Hong Kong's older working poor, commencing in Jan 2024.

25600220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25600220.value: Working towards the Sustainable Development Goal to "end all poverty" by 2030 is certainly a daunting task, given the persistent or even rising rates of poverty among our older population. This study attempts to contribute to this endeavor by exploring the intricate issue of old-age poverty, focusing on older individuals living independently in Hong Kong. Through life stories from 60 households, the study provided insights into the factors that contribute to, sustain, and potentially interrupt the cycle of poverty. This information could help to highlight possible root causes and ongoing factors of poverty, such as early school dropouts, underpaid jobs, and compulsory retirements. The findings of our study suggest the potential importance of systemic changes, including enduring poverty prevention strategies, stronger protections for low income working adults, increased availability of public housing, and enhanced support for spousal caregivers. While the research may provide a more nuanced understanding of late-life poverty and suggest possible solutions to address it, there's much more to learn and many more perspectives to consider. The study can be a stepping stone to more extensive research and discussions, which may inform policy decisions and shape interventions to improve the lives of the elderly.

25602620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25602620.value: 透過虛擬實境的創新測試，提早發現社區老年人的認知障礙

25602620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25602620.value: 本項目是去驗證一個互動的虛擬實境空間記憶測試（VRWMT），透過這一個容易實施的測試，去提早發現社區老年人的認知障礙。 空間工作記憶的功能障礙是早期認知障礙症患者的常見病徵。研究文獻已經確立了這些功能障礙和海馬體的缺損有相互關係。VRWMT是一個容易實施、只需很少指導、並且無需監督的虛擬實境空間記憶測試。透過這個空間工作記憶測試，可以有助檢測早期的認知障礙的，進而去評估老年人的認知功能、並了解與年齡之間的關係。 本研究會以年齡配對去區分已知的輕度認知障礙老年人和健康的老年人、並預測這兩個組別的老年人在十二個月後的空間工作記憶功能和認知能力。這項研究會將透過VRWMT 和其他的臨床認知測試工具作同時效度比對。此外，透過炎性標記和代謝失調生物標記的檢測，以檢視早期認知障礙缺損的風險和VRWMT預測的有效性。 這是一項結合了行為與生物標記的研究，為社會需要和老年人口的臨床研究作出確切的貢獻。

25607320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25607320.value: 當農民工成為小城房主：“流動人口”的終結？

25607320.label: Project Objectives
25607320.value: To evaluate whether small cities can play a critical role in eliminating the spatial separation of rights and income for rural migrants: Achieving this objective hinges on determining whether small cities can offer sufficient employment opportunities to enable migrant families to generate enough income to make a livelihood. As a small city in western China, Meishan is distinctive in its own right and indicative of a general trend whereby China seeks to expand small-city urbanization. The study will evaluate whether Meishan offers ample, decent local job opportunities for migrants-turned-homeowners, and whether these jobs are gender- or age-restricted or are able to absorb only a limited influx of migrant labor. This research will also examine other income-generating strategies adopted by rural migrants, such as launching their own entrepreneurial projects or reverting to farming. With only a few exceptions (Kipnis 2016; Garcia 2011), most studies on China’s migrant labor focus on metropolitan or coastal areas. The Meishan case will therefore complement existing studies. To investigate whether migrant families will be granted full urban citizenship in small cities where they have purchased homes: Studies have shown that large Chinese cities strictly control rural migrant inflow (backed by the household registration system). This makes it very difficult, if not impossible, for rural migrants to settle on their own as urban citizens. It has also been documented that rural migrants are reluctant to obtain small-city household registrations because they are concerned that they might lose their access to farm plots if they were to do so (Chen and Fan 2016). Now small-city homeownership has become another tool with which to unlock a similar set of urban benefits (Huang et al. 2019). Little is known, though, about how rural migrants navigate the rural/urban governance labyrinth with their newly acquired homeownership. This study will identify the major obstacles that rural migrants-turned-homeowners must overcome to access urban services in small cities, and further document strategies they adopt to overcome these obstacles. To evaluate whether buying a home in a small city can generate attachment and values that will encourage people to settle there: Even though migration is often explained as a response to labor market demand, many have recognized that it is also a cultural and meaning-making process through which people construct their desired destinies (Yan 2003; Chu 2006). It has been documented that small cities have served important market and commercial functions (Fei 1984) because of their spatial and psychological proximity to rural migrants. Little is known, however, about whether small cities serve as desired destinations for rural migrants that enable them to fulfill their aspirations. Also unclear is the extent to which, and in what ways, urban homes and small cities might serve as sources of identity for rural migrants-turned-homeowners. This study will investigate these questions, which are key to understanding not only rural migrants’ settlement intentions but also the cultural meaning they attach to small-city urban homes. To provide an ethnographically informed analysis of the social differentiation of migrants-turned-homeowners: For rural migrant families, small-city homeownership offers an opportunity, instead of a destined trajectory, for rural migrants to settle. It enables migrants to negotiate their futures and produces diverse settlement outcomes. This study will identify the common and less common pathways rural migrant families follow after obtaining homeownership. It will further identify factors that contribute to such differentiation and analyze the challenges associated with each of these pathways. Achieving this objective will be crucial to providing a nuanced understanding of Chinese rural migrants as a social group undergoing transformation. Insights into their settlement differentiation will enable me to contribute to the existing literature on the class formation and social integration of Chinese rural migrants.
rows: To evaluate whether small cities can play a critical role in eliminating the spatial separation of rights and income for rural migrants: Achieving this objective hinges on determining whether small cities can offer sufficient employment opportunities to enable migrant families to generate enough income to make a livelihood. As a small city in western China, Meishan is distinctive in its own right and indicative of a general trend whereby China seeks to expand small-city urbanization. The study will evaluate whether Meishan offers ample, decent local job opportunities for migrants-turned-homeowners, and whether these jobs are gender- or age-restricted or are able to absorb only a limited influx of migrant labor. This research will also examine other income-generating strategies adopted by rural migrants, such as launching their own entrepreneurial projects or reverting to farming. With only a few exceptions (Kipnis 2016; Garcia 2011), most studies on China’s migrant labor focus on metropolitan or coastal areas. The Meishan case will therefore complement existing studies.

To investigate whether migrant families will be granted full urban citizenship in small cities where they have purchased homes: Studies have shown that large Chinese cities strictly control rural migrant inflow (backed by the household registration system). This makes it very difficult, if not impossible, for rural migrants to settle on their own as urban citizens. It has also been documented that rural migrants are reluctant to obtain small-city household registrations because they are concerned that they might lose their access to farm plots if they were to do so (Chen and Fan 2016). Now small-city homeownership has become another tool with which to unlock a similar set of urban benefits (Huang et al. 2019). Little is known, though, about how rural migrants navigate the rural/urban governance labyrinth with their newly acquired homeownership. This study will identify the major obstacles that rural migrants-turned-homeowners must overcome to access urban services in small cities, and further document strategies they adopt to overcome these obstacles.

25607320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25607320.value: 自20世紀80年代，中國的改革帶來了農村人口在城鄉之間的流動。他們在城市工作，但因為戶口制度和土地制度，他們的福利卻留在了農村。這種工作和權利的空間分離，保證了勞動力低價，也支持了中國的出口導向的發展策略。最近，中國政府在重新定位發展策略，試圖將十億人口定居在小城鎮。在政策的刺激下，已經有大量的農民的小城鎮購買了房屋，成為了房主。四川的眉山就是這個政策試點。過去眉山的勞動力外流到珠三角，目前，很多人在回流，而且購買了房屋。根據統計，在2015年眉山的房地產銷售上浮了56.9％。其中68.3％的購買者是農民工。全國范圍內，統計數字表明2016年，有17.8％的農民工成為了小城鎮的房主。 這會不會意味著過去的流動人口的模式，開始終結呢？這個研究替代進一步分解為：農村背景的房主會不會得到城市的福利和工作機會，而最終穩定下來？小城市和房屋權會不會帶來新的文化和社會價值，從而構造新的身份認同？房地產市場會怎樣逐步分化農民工群體？為了回答這些問題，我將通過多點民族志的方法，在四川眉山開展調查。我的研究地點包括新的農民工主體的社區，售房處，小城鎮的工作地點。這研究將提供理論和政策貢獻。理論依據，這將促進城市鄉變遷的中國經驗。政策措施，此研究將提供有關房地產市場能否影響農民工的流動性的政策依據。同時，此研究也會考察，是否中國能超越依賴外資和廉價勞動力的出口導向的經濟發展模式。

25609920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25609920.value: 中國改革開放後，伴隨1988年《土地管理法》的出台，土地出讓收入是地方政府的重要財政來源。土地開發催生了「政府企業家主義」。地方政府通過出讓土地和發展新區，獲取外來投資和經濟效益。「政府企業家主義」強調政府積極引入和運用市場工具以謀求增長。既有文獻對於「政府企業家主義」的理解比較籠統，其含義被簡單的等同為具有市場化傾向的政府行為。對於「政府企業家主義」的理解需更全面探討「政府」（state）的政治經濟學內涵。 是項研究創建了新的理論框架分析「政府企業家主義」。政府在城市發展過程中，運用監管彈性、以更務實的取態創造出不同的管治模式配合市場的發展，形成了不同的土地開發策略。「彈性」強調權力干預的準則、機制、主體和被監管的對象非一成不變；「務實」強調干預的目的非單一經濟增長。然而，這一框架在中國的實證研究中並不多見。 圍繞上述框架，是項研究選取前海自貿區內三個土地發展的案例做實證研究。三個案例中所體現出的監管彈性和務實，解釋了為何同一地方、不同土地開發項目，政府參與的程度和形式並非一致。多元化的「政府企業家主義」創造出不同的監管動機及管治模式。 是項研究有兩重意義。從理論角度看，研究將更好的完善「政府」和管治的理論框架。從實證角度看，研究將提出更因地制宜的土地發展策略，提出如何完善政府和市場在城市發展過程中的夥伴關係。研究將為未來中國城市新區的土地開發提供經驗和參考。

25609920.label: Realisation of objectives
25609920.value: Part A: Realization of the four objectives by various research methods I. Fieldwork and first-hand data collection (Obj. 1 & 2) We conducted in-depth qualitative fieldwork in Qianhai, including more than 10 field visits from May 2023 to November 2024, immediately following the implementation of quarantine-free travel between Shenzhen and Hong Kong. A total of 13 semi-structured interviews were conducted with: i. Nine senior officials (section chief) from various departments of the Qianhai Authority: • Technology and Innovation Division (1) • Development and Reform Division (1) • Institutional Innovation Division (1) • Hong Kong and Macau Services Division (1) • Planning Management Division (5) ii. Two general managers of Qianhai Construction Investment Holdings Group Co., Ltd. iii. The General Manager of Vanke Co., who oversees the development of Vanke Qianhai Enterprise Dream Park, based on which the first REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) in China was issued. The research team also conducted a detailed analysis of secondary sources, including official documents, policy reports, and newspapers. These materials provided critical context on development plans, stakeholder perspectives, and institutional policies at local, regional, and national levels. Key documents include • Plan for Comprehensively Deepening Reform and Opening-Up of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone (2021). • Vision and Actions on Jointly Building Silk Road Economic Belt and 21st-Century Maritime Silk Road (2015). • Overall Development Plan for the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone (2021). • Interim Measures for Land Supply in the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone (2013). • Updated Prospectus of the Penghua Qianhai Vanke REITs Closed-End Hybrid Securities Investment Fund (2023). • Measures for the Administration of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone Authority (2024). • Measures for Land Supply in the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone, Shenzhen Municipality (2021). II. Theoretical reconceptualization (Obj. 3) To reconceptualize state entrepreneurialism, the PI and a supervised PhD student conducted a scoping review of 75 research publications from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. This review examined current trends in state entrepreneurialism and its manifestations across different contexts. The synthesis of this scoping review with empirical findings led to a high-impact conceptual paper published in Progress in Human Geography. III. Peer feedback and dissemination of project findings through conference engagement (Obj. 1, 2 & 3) To refine the empirical findings for further publications, the PI and research team actively participated in three international conferences in 2024 (Beijing, New York and Hawaii). These engagements yielded highly positive and constructive feedback, which informed the preparation of two manuscripts. IV. Policy engagement through scholarly dialogue: translating research into pragmatic policy recommendations (Obj. 4) To discuss policy implications and amplify the reach of our conceptual framework, the research team organized a special session entitled “Actually Existing State Entrepreneurialism: From Conceptualization to Materialization” at the 2023 Urban China Research Network (UCRN) Conference on 28 October 2023 at Peking University. The session fostered intellectually stimulating discussions and generated valuable insights on applying state entrepreneurialism in non-Western contexts, as well as implications for “good governance” in other pilot zones across China. During the session, we received valuable feedback from Prof. Fulong Wu of UCL. Session Participant include the PI (Chair) and Prof Shenjing He (discussant, from the University of Hong Kong), as well as four Panelists including Prof Roger C.K. Chan (PolyU), Prof Zhigang Li (Wuhan University), Jia Ling (PolyU), and Prof Siu Wai Wong (PolyU). To advance scholarly dialogue and fulfill the project’s education plan, the research team facilitated a six-month academic attachment for PhD candidate Ms. Jia Ling, supported by this project, to conduct research at TU Delft’s Department of Urbanism under the supervision of Dr. Qu Lei. This attachment programme facilitated knowledge transfer, enabling comparative analysis of state entrepreneurialism across different urban contexts. Part B: A concise overview of findings based on various objectives I. Qianhai Authority and new governance framework (Obj. 1 & 2) The Qianhai Authority exemplifies a new form of entrepreneurial governance; it is empowered to formulate and authorize urban planning, land-use-rights transfer, and construction projects independently of the Shenzhen Municipal Government, reporting directly to the provincial government. Besides, Qianhai Construction Investment Holdings Group Co., Ltd. (SQCIH), an authority-owned entity, is the sole legally authorized body tasked with land development, infrastructure construction, and project investments in Qianhai. In this capacity, SQCIH functions as a developer on the government’s behalf. Qianhai pilots a new urban development model that embodies an economic concept. Jurisdictionally, Qianhai falls under the Nanshan and Bao’an districts of Shenzhen. The Qianhai authority oversees economic development, while the management of social and public affairs—such as education, healthcare, and social security—falls to Nanshan and Bao’an. Therefore, Qianhai shares some of its revenue with both district governments. II. Innovation in Land Development: The 1.5-Level Model (Obj. 1 & 2) 1.5-level land development adopts a phased approach, allowing temporary land use without full land-use-rights transfer—typically under short-term tenures of 5 to 10 years. Inspired by the Built-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model from infrastructure projects, this innovative framework applies similar principles to land development. The Qianhai Authority grants private developers temporary land appropriation without upfront premiums, incentivizing rapid investment in office spaces and infrastructure to meet immediate needs. Upon lease expiration, all developments revert to the Authority, enabling dynamic land-use optimization and long-term planning flexibility. III. REITs as an instrument for innovation in land financialization (Obj. 1 & 2) REITs are a financialization model that securitizes portfolios of income-generating real estate assets—such as Vanke Qianhai Enterprise Dream Park in this case—transforming illiquid holdings into tradable equity instruments. By pooling and capitalizing on stable cash flows (e.g., rents), it enhances market liquidity and brings immediate cash flows to Vanke. For Qianhai Authority, it mobilizes the incentive for private capital without significant public spending and fulfills its strategic role for financial innovation. IV. Reconceptualize State Entrepreneurialism (Obj. 3) Our reconceptualization of SE consists of three cornerstones, viz., politics of scale, regulatory flexibility, and financialization as means of internalizing financial logics as state capacities. The emphasis on “actually existing” uncovers how political discourses are materialized into variegated policy outcomes and territorial politics. V. Evidence-based suggestions for improving land use efficiency and good governance in other pilot zones (Obj. 4) Qianhai offers valuable insights into how governments can adjust to urban entrepreneurialism while preserving strategic control. The case transcends a simplistic dichotomy of state intervention versus market liberty in achieving good governance, acknowledging the dynamic interplay of financial, regulatory, and societal logics in fostering development and social prosperity. China’s financialized urban governance continues to be a process of active experimentation. Unlike the deregulated financial markets of the West, where financialization is often driven by the private sector, Qianhai’s approach remains highly state-guided, with financial instruments aligning well with the development agendas set by the Qianhai authority. Financialization does not inherently undermine state authority but provides avenues for the state to mediate and guide urban development. The current challenge is whether such models will remain sustainable in the face of global financial pressures and domestic economic shifts.
