25609920.label: Major findings and research outcome
25609920.value: This study investigates land development in China’s pilot development zone with five research findings: i. Qianhai authority, a statutory body with strong characteristics of entrepreneurialism, in driving an innovative governance for urban development (Obj. 1&2); ii. 1.5-level land development model in granting flexibility in land tenure (Obj. 1&2); iii. new land financialization mode, viz., Real Estate Investment Trust (REITs) (Obj. 1&2); iv. reconceptualization of state entrepreneurialism, with a triadic framework for future analysis (Obj. 3); and v. evidence-based suggestions for improving land use efficiency and good governance in other pilot zones (Obj. 4) Key outcomes and deliverables: i. Publications and papers under preparation • “Actually Existing State Entrepreneurialism: From Conceptualization to Materialization”, published in Progress in Human Geography in 2024. • A research article incorporating the key findings from (i), (ii), and (iii) above has been completed. The PI intends to submit it to Transactions in Planning and Urban Research in June 2025. • A research article incorporating findings from REITs has been completed. After considering feedback from four conference presentations and previous journal submissions, we have revised the manuscript and intend to submit it to the Annals of the American Association of Geographers. ii. Supervise PhD students • The project fully supports Miss Jia Ling (enrolled in 2021), who will complete her dissertation by the end of July 2025. The dissertation is entitled “Examining State Entrepreneurialism in China’s Land Development from the Regulation Approach: A Case Study of Qianhai”. • The project partially supports (with matching funds from the university) Mr. Wilson Kodwo McWilson, a student from Ghana, who extends the state entrepreneurialism framework to analyze the spatial transformation of Ghana. There are beneficial synergies between studying city-regionalism in Ghana and the land development of Qianhai—two cases from the Global South. A journal article entitled “City Regionalism in the Global South: Evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa” was published in the Annals of the American Association of Geographers, in dialogue with the Chinese case. He did an oral defense on 6 June 2025. iii. 25609920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25609920.value: Building on the insights from the Qianhai case, this research can be further developed through comparative case studies of other national-level development zones such as Nansha (Guangzhou) and Hengqin (Zhuhai). Both zones share characteristics with Qianhai in terms of state-led financial innovation, cross-border collaboration, and experimental governance, yet differ in institutional arrangements, land finance strategies, and levels of market involvement. The research team also had the opportunity, through interviews, to learn about the development pathways of other new areas. The development of Nansha is overseen by an ad hoc commission under the Nansha district government. The development of Hengqin receives the highest administrative attention, which is jointly led by the Macau SAR government and the Guangdong Province government. A comparative analysis will help assess the transferability and variation of state entrepreneurialism across different contexts. We propose: (1) fieldwork and stakeholder interviews in Nansha/Hengqin to build comparative datasets; (2) Development of a typology framework of land financialization across zones; (3) policy engagement to translate findings into scalable land development practices. This approach will advance theoretical understanding while generating practical insights for China’s new areas, particularly in optimizing cross-border collaboration and financial innovation under varying administrative structures.

25609920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25609920.value: China’s 1988 land reforms and subsequent decentralization catalyzed state entrepreneurialism (SE) – an interventionist governance approach pursuing market functionality, business opportunities, and social development. This pioneering study examines Shenzhen’s Qianhai Pilot Zone through three innovative lenses. First, the Qianhai Authority exemplifies entrepreneurial governance, exclusively managing economic development (such as land, planning, and project construction) while delegating social affairs to Nanshan and Bao’an districts encompassing Qianhai (through a revenue-sharing mechanism). Second, a 1.5-level land development model is created to accelerate the land development process through temporary land leases (5-10 years) without full land-use-right transfer, incentivizing private developers to rapidly deliver offices and infrastructure. Third, Qianhai pioneers land financialization via China’s first REITs, creating liquidity for developers while fulfilling Qianhai’s mission as a hub of financial innovation. This study offers new conceptual insights into SE in China, emphasizing its diverse implications across different contexts and spatial scales. The findings also illuminate ways to enhance partnership arrangements and promote good governance in urban development for other pilot zones.

26100120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26100120.value: Coral reefs are vitally important ecosystems but are globally threatened. They are estimated to support at least 500 million people, by providing habitat for fisheries, protecting coastlines and supporting livelihoods, but are in a state of significant decline, largely due to climate change. The coincidence of accelerating warming and increasingly frequent El Niño temperature anomalies have led to a succession of global bleaching events and widespread coral death. Marine heat waves have already caused mortality on more than 90 % of the world’s reefs, with some predictions suggesting that coral reefs as an ecosystem, and the immense value they provide, may be lost within the next 30 years without immediate management intervention. In order to develop effective management strategies, we urgently require greatly improved understanding of how oceanic and climatic drivers interact to influence the ecological structure and function of the world’s coral reefs. Despite increasing evidence of tight coupling between reefs and physical conditions in the surrounding ocean, quantitative consideration of the role of oceanic processes in coral reef structure, function and long-term survival remain rare. The PI has recently demonstrated that internal waves may be a significant driver, cooling reefs threated by warming and creating climate change refuges. The proposed research will build on these findings to quantify the broader ecological significance of internal-wave upwelling in supplying nutrients and shaping reef communities. Internal waves are a ubiquitous process across the global oceans but are largely invisible at the ocean surface. In addition to upwelling cold water, internal waves transform the chemical environment over reefs. This has as yet unknown implications for the ecological function of internal-wave refuges. The proposed work will leverage a suite of established long-term data sets from global reef locations to quantify the influence of internal-wave upwelling on (1) nutrient flux rates, (2) the trophic function and heath of reef communities, (3) changes in community-level metabolism, (4) spatial patterns in ecosystem structure, and (5) interactions between internal waves and coral bleaching patterns. Finally, long-term analyses will be used to assess (6) the implications and quantitative importance of internal waves for coral reef ecosystems in the context of ongoing climate change and El Niño events. The proposed research will provide fundamental understanding that is urgently required to guide effective stewardship of coral reefs, which are vitally important to human health and security but are being degraded on a global scale at an unprecedented rate. 珊瑚礁為人類提供漁場及海岸線保護，並作為全球至少五億人的生計來源，是十分重要的生態系。然而主要因為氣候變遷，全球珊瑚礁都受到威脅並已嚴重衰退。因為加速的暖化現象及越趨頻繁的聖嬰海溫異常現象（El Niño temperature anomalies）的偶合，已經導致全球性的珊瑚白化事件（bleaching event）以及大範圍的珊瑚死亡。目前全球已有超過九成的珊瑚礁因為海洋熱浪而發生過珊瑚死亡，有預測指出若無即刻的管理介入，我們將會在未來30年內完全失去珊瑚礁生態系以及其所提供的生態服務。為了建立有效管理策略，我們急需更深入地了解在海洋與氣候因子間的交互作用是如何影響全球珊瑚礁的生態結構及功能。縱使越來越多證據已經指出珊瑚礁與周遭海洋物理環境緊密關係，仍少有研究量化的考慮海洋過程（oceanic processes）對於珊瑚礁結構、功能及長期生存所扮演之角色。本人早前已經證明內波（internal waves）或許可以作為一重要因子，冷卻受暖化威脅的珊瑚礁和創造氣候變遷避難所（climate change refuges）。本研究提案將會以過去的研究發現為基礎，更廣泛的量化內波湧升流對於營養鹽供給和珊瑚群聚之塑造的生態意義。內波現象廣泛發生於世界上各個海域，大多數卻無法由海水表層觀測到。內波湧升流除了帶來冷水團，亦同時能夠改變該珊瑚礁區的化學環境，然而此一改變對於內波避難所之生態功能有何相關意義仍不明確。本研究提案將會充分利用世界各個珊瑚礁區的長期資料庫來量化內波湧升流對於以下幾個面向的影響：（1）營養鹽通量（nutrient flux rates）、（2）珊瑚礁群聚的攝食功能（trophic function）與健康狀態、（3）群聚層級上代謝作用的變化、（4）生態系結構的空間格局（spatial patterns）及（5）內波—珊瑚白化模式間的交互作用。最後，長期資料分析將用來評估（6）在持續的氣候變遷及聖嬰事件的情境下，內波對於珊瑚礁生態系的意義與量化重要性。珊瑚礁對於人類的健康及安全至關重要，然而目前世界各地的珊瑚礁衰退速度卻是前所未見。本研究提案將會對於列舉的6個面向提供迫需的基礎認識、亦為制定珊瑚礁的有效管理辦法提供方向。

26100120.label: Major findings and research outcome
26100120.value: This project generated significant new insight into how internal waves, and their interactions with other oceanographic processes, govern environmental variability and disturbance exposure across coral ecosystems. Despite substantial COVID-19-related fieldwork delays, major research outputs were delivered: two peer-reviewed publications, two manuscripts in preparation, and a completed stable isotope dataset underpinning a fifth manuscript. 1. Cryptic coral diversity and environmental niche differentiation (Moorea, French Polynesia): Johnston et al. (2022), Coral Reefs, examined 673 Pocillopora colonies at Moorea, revealing strong niche differentiation among co-occurring cryptic species across depths and sites. Depth-dependent differences in abundance were linked to environmental variability, especially internal-wave-driven temperature variance, highlighting how fine-scale oceanography may enhance reef resilience. 2. Hidden heatwaves and subsurface bleaching (Moorea, French Polynesia): Wyatt et al. (2023), Nature Communications, used 15-year in situ temperature records to show that weakening of internal-wave cooling, modulated by mesoscale eddies, led to a severe subsurface marine heatwave in 2019. This hidden heatwave caused widespread coral bleaching despite moderate surface conditions, introducing the concept of “hidden heatwaves” as a critical but under-recognised global threat. 3. Biogeochemical variability driven by internal waves and typhoons (Dongsha Atoll): A manuscript (King et al., in prep for Journal of Geophysical Research - Oceans) based on high-resolution oxygen and temperature data explores how internal waves and typhoons drive reef-scale biogeochemical variability, demonstrating dynamic benthic oxygen fluxes linked to physical forcing and advancing understanding of internal-wave impacts on reef metabolism. 4. Coral reef thermal variability in an internal wave hotspot (northern South China Sea): A manuscript (Wyatt et al., in prep for Geophysical Research Letters) presents long-term analysis of temperature variability at Dongsha Atoll. Internal-wave-driven cooling dominates but is seasonally suppressed by winter Kuroshio Intrusion and anticyclonic eddy shedding. Variability is also shaped by mesoscale processes and short-term disruptions from typhoons, underscoring the temporal instability of thermal refuges. 5. Atoll-scale variation in energy and nutrient acquisition (Dongsha Atoll): Stable isotope samples 2023 have now been analysed after COVID-related delays at HKU. A fifth manuscript will examine spatial variation in trophic dynamics across reef zones using bulk and compound-specific stable isotope analysis of coral and fish tissues. Together, these findings provide novel insights into the interplay between oceanographic variability and coral reef resilience, contributing to both regional understanding (northern South China Sea) and global frameworks for identifying climate refuges.

26100120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26100120.value: This research has laid the foundation for a broader investigation into how internal-wave-driven variability contributes to the formation and stability of coral reef climate refuges. Building on these findings, ongoing work will focus on integrating multi-year, high-resolution environmental datasets with advanced modelling to predict the spatial distribution and persistence of thermal refuges across depth and regionally within the Coral Triangle. Two manuscripts in preparation will extend key results from this project: one characterising internal-wave modulation of reef metabolism under variable physical forcing, and another examining vertical patterns of thermal exposure relevant to refuge persistence. A third manuscript based on compound-specific stable isotope analysis (CSIA) will clarify trophic structure and particulate food dynamics at the atoll scale, with relevance for understanding biogeochemical constraints on refuges. Future research will scale up from Dongsha to a comparative framework across key sites in Southeast Asia. This will be achieved through international collaborations, field campaigns, and ongoing postgraduate researcher student projects. The long-term goal is to inform targeted conservation of functionally resilient reef habitats using predictive frameworks grounded in oceanographic drivers, ensuring that climate adaptation strategies explicitly incorporate subsurface processes like internal waves and mesoscale variability.

26100120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26100120.value: Coral reefs are among the most diverse and valuable ecosystems on Earth, yet they are increasingly threatened by marine heatwaves driven by climate change. This project investigated how powerful underwater waves, known as internal waves, can help protect reefs by delivering cooler, deeper water to shallow habitats. Using long-term environmental records and high-resolution instruments at Moorea (French Polynesia) and Dongsha Atoll (northern South China Sea), we showed that internal waves strongly influence reef conditions such as temperature, oxygen, and nutrients – shaping potential natural “climate refuges.” However, this protective effect can break down due to larger-scale ocean currents, typhoons, and climate oscillations. These findings provide vital insight into where and when reefs may be naturally buffered from extreme heat, offering a foundation for identifying and conserving climate-resilient coral ecosystems across Asia and globally.

26200420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26200420.value: Transportation network companies (TNCs), such as Uber, Lyft and DiDi, are disrupting the urban transportation sector. The rapid growth of these companies raises several public policy concerns. First, they transformed the landscape of the taxi industry and left taxi drivers in financial strain. This sparked massive strikes in numerous cities in China, South Korea, North America and Europe. Second, TNCs are blamed for increasing the traffic congestion in large metropolitan areas and underpaying their drivers. The San Francisco County Transportation Authority estimated that TNCs contributed to 50% of the increase in congestion in San Francisco between 2010-2016. Data from the New York Taxi and Limousine Commission suggested that 85% of the TNC drivers in New York City are paid below the minimum wage (after expense). These concerns have prompted policy makers to take actions to regulate TNCs. We propose this project to evaluate the impacts of various TNC regulations that limit congestion and promote equity. We will (a) construct general-equilibrium models to capture the behaviors of passengers, drivers, and the TNC platform; (b) analyze the interactions between TNCs and other transport modes such as private vehicles and taxicabs; and (c) evaluate the impacts of various TNC regulations on the TNC business model and the transportation system. The first thrust of this project will develop a network equilibrium model to evaluate the impact of a cordon price, which imposes a surcharge on all vehicles that pass a cordon line to enter the congestion area. Our central thesis is that TNC vehicles have advantage (in mode choice) over private vehicles under the cordon price as they complete multiple trips within the congestion area after passing the cordon without paying again, while private vehicles make much fewer trips for each crossing. The second thrust of the project studies the competition between TNCs and taxicabs under regulations. We will develop a game-theoretic model to capture the competition between TNCs and taxicabs. We will use this model to quantify the impact of TNCs on the taxicab industry, and offer regulatory insights for policy makers to formulate coordinated strategies that jointly regulate TNCs and taxicabs. The two thrusts of this project will form an integrated framework for understanding the externalities of TNCs in a multimodal transportation system. It will inspire a new direction of research that addresses TNC regulations, and offer valuable regulatory insights for city planners to limit congestion and promote equity through policy innovations. 網約車平台的普及對城市交通系統帶來了深刻的影響，也因此在公共政策層面產生了諸多問題。首先，網約車平台對傳統出租車行業帶來了巨大的衝擊，並在世界各地引發了出租車司機的大規模抗議活動。其次，網約車平台加劇了大城市的交通堵塞問題，並引發了各界對於網約車司機收入水平的質疑。這些問題在近年來相繼引起世界各地相關監管部門的重視。 本項目將深入研究不同監管策略對於網約車市場的影響。我們將通過市場均衡模型刻畫網約車市場中乘客，司機以及平台的決策行為，分析網約車同其他交通模式的相互關係，量化研究網約車監管政策對網約車市場的影響及其形成機制。在本項目的第一部分中，我們將通過網絡均衡模型研究車輛擁堵附加費對網約車市場的影響。我們將著重分析不同擁堵附加費下網約車相對於私家車的優勢與劣勢。 在本項目的第二部分中，我們將研究監管政策下網約車平台與出租車之間的市場競爭。我們將通過博弈論模型刻畫這些市場競爭行為，從而為監管部門制定相應監管政策提供科學依據。 本項目的研究內容將會形成一個完整的理論框架以了解網約車平台在多模態交通系統中的負外部性。同時，我們的研究將為監管部門制定相關政策提供可靠的科學依據，以通過制度創新的方式來解決網約車平台的負外部性問題。

26200420.label: Realisation of objectives
26200420.value: During the course of this project, both research objectives outlined in the original proposal have been fully realized through a sequence of five peer-reviewed journal publications. The first objective was to develop a network equilibrium model to evaluate the impacts of congestion-limiting policies under the interactions between transportation network companies (TNCs) and non-commercial private vehicles. This objective was addressed across three major studies, each of which built upon the previous in complexity and practical relevance. The first study, titled "Spatial pricing in ride-sourcing markets under a congestion charge" established a networked economic equilibrium framework that captures the interplay among passenger demand, driver supply, passenger and driver waiting times, platform pricing, vehicle repositioning, and traffic flow balance over the transportation network. This model was used to examine the effect of various cordon-based congestion charges on the ride-hailing market. Among the charge schemes analyzed, the results showed that the one-directional cordon charge not only effectively reduces ride-sourcing traffic in the congestion area, but also leads to service improvements and greater accessibility for passengers in underserved areas outside the cordon. Compared to bi-directional and trip-based congestion charges, the one-directional scheme achieves congestion relief with a lower burden on passengers, drivers, and the platform. This work directly addressed the first objective by providing a rigorous and spatially-detailed equilibrium model for evaluating congestion pricing policies in a realistic urban context. The second study, titled "Impact of congestion charge and minimum wage on TNCs: A case study for San Francisco" advanced the equilibrium analysis by incorporating regulatory measures that are increasingly relevant in major cities: the joint imposition of congestion surcharges and wage floors for TNC drivers. The study developed a market equilibrium model that accounts for the incentives of passengers, drivers, and the platform, while explicitly modeling the congestion externalities associated with TNC vehicles. The research found that while both trip-based and time-based congestion surcharges can reduce TNC ridership, these effects are substantially mitigated by the existence of a driver wage floor, meaning that the number of TNC vehicles is not significantly reduced unless the surcharge is extremely high. Importantly, the research demonstrated that a time-based congestion surcharge—unlike the trip-based alternative—can offer a true Pareto improvement: it raises vehicle occupancy, enhances passenger and driver surplus, increases platform profitability, and generates higher tax revenue for the city. These results provide clear, actionable insights for policymakers about the design and expected impacts of congestion regulation in the presence of wage floors. The third study, titled "Shared parking for ride-sourcing platforms to reduce cruising traffic", recognized the limitations and potential drawbacks of regulatory interventions, such as reduced platform profitability or unintended consequences for passengers and drivers. To address these challenges, the research proposed an alternative, market-based approach: the integration of shared parking services into ride-sourcing platforms. By matching idle TNC vehicles with vacant parking spots, the proposed business model reduces cruising traffic and associated congestion without the need for restrictive regulation. The equilibrium model developed for this three-sided market (passengers, drivers, garage operators) demonstrated that even a small allocation of urban parking resources can dramatically reduce cruising traffic (by over 80% in the San Francisco case study), while simultaneously increasing platform profits, driver wages, and passenger surplus. This approach offers a new direction for congestion management that leverages platform innovation rather than regulatory constraint. Together, these three studies provide a comprehensive and robust realization of the first project objective. They establish a network equilibrium modeling toolkit capable of rigorously assessing regulatory and market-based interventions, and produce clear, data-driven guidance for optimizing ride-hailing system performance in urban environments. The second objective of the project was to develop a game-theoretic model to capture the competition between TNCs and taxicabs, and to investigate coordinated strategies that jointly regulate these competing services. This objective was addressed in two subsequent studies, which extended the modeling framework to encompass multimodal, multi-operator competition and regulation in the rapidly evolving landscape of urban mobility. The fourth study, titled "Regulating for-hire autonomous vehicles for an equitable multimodal transportation network", focused on the emerging role of autonomous vehicles (AVs) in the ride-hailing market and the regulatory challenges associated with ensuring equitable access to mobility. The research developed a game-theoretic network equilibrium model that incorporates a ride-hailing platform operating a fleet of AVs in competition with a public transit agency, while accounting for the heterogeneity of passengers across income groups and locations. The study provides a rigorous assessment of how AV deployment, in the absence of regulation, can unintentionally exacerbate both spatial and social inequities in urban mobility. To address these issues, the research evaluated two forms of regulation: (a) a minimum service-level requirement for ride-hailing platforms, and (b) the use of ride-hailing taxes to subsidize public transit. The results showed that while minimum service requirements can improve spatial equity, they may worsen social inequity, whereas targeted subsidies for transit can simultaneously narrow both spatial and social equity gaps. These findings are directly aligned with the second project objective, as they offer a unified, game-theoretic framework for analyzing and designing coordinated regulatory strategies across competing modes and operators. The fifth and final study, titled "Competition between autonomous and traditional ride-hailing platforms: Market equilibrium and technology transfer", pushed the frontier further by examining the competition between autonomous ride-hailing platforms and traditional, human-driver-based platforms, with a particular focus on the implications of AV technology transfer. The model considers an autonomous ride-hailing platform that can lease its AV fleet to a traditional platform, thereby enabling mixed-fleet operations and creating a dynamic interplay between competition and cooperation. Through a detailed game-theoretic analysis validated with real-world data from Manhattan, the research uncovers a nuanced set of outcomes: technology transfer can create win-win scenarios for both platforms, but may come at the cost of reduced surplus for human drivers and passengers. The study also reveals that as AV operational costs decrease, the autonomous platform captures most of the benefits via increased market share and higher rental revenues, while the traditional platform is compelled to rent more AVs at higher prices, suffering profit erosion despite technological advances. These insights are highly relevant to the project’s second objective, as they not only model the competitive dynamics between old and new mobility providers, but also offer actionable guidance for regulatory coordination and strategic decision-making in a future with mixed-autonomy fleets. In summary, the five studies produced under this project have collectively and comprehensively achieved both stated objectives. They deliver new theoretical models, computational tools, and policy insights that address the core challenges of congestion management, equity, and competition in urban multimodal transportation systems, providing a strong foundation for future research and practical regulation.

26200420.label: Major findings and research outcome
26200420.value: The project has yielded several major findings and research outcomes that advance both the theoretical understanding and the practical policy design for regulating transportation network companies and multimodal urban transportation systems. A central contribution is the development of advanced network equilibrium and game-theoretic models that explicitly capture the interactions among ride-hailing platforms, drivers, passengers, public transit, and regulatory authorities. These models have enabled rigorous, data-driven evaluation of congestion-limiting policies, wage regulations, and innovative market-based interventions across a range of realistic urban scenarios. One key research outcome is the identification of the differential impacts of various congestion pricing schemes. The studies show that a one-directional cordon charge imposed on vehicles entering a congestion zone can effectively reduce ride-hailing traffic in the urban core while also improving accessibility and service quality in outlying areas. Compared to bi-directional and trip-based congestion charges, the one-directional cordon price achieves congestion relief at a lower cost to both users and service providers. Another important finding is that while both trip-based and time-based congestion surcharges can reduce TNC ridership, their effect on curbing the number of TNC vehicles is limited when a minimum driver wage is also imposed. In this context, a time-based surcharge that penalizes idle vehicle hours emerges as a superior policy, as it increases vehicle occupancy and can generate Pareto improvements across passengers, drivers, platforms, and municipal revenue. Beyond congestion management, the project has advanced the state of the art in modeling platform competition and regulatory coordination in mixed-autonomy and multimodal environments. The studies reveal that, without careful regulation, the proliferation of autonomous ride-hailing vehicles can exacerbate both spatial and social inequities in mobility, as market-driven AV deployment tends to concentrate benefits among higher-income groups and well-served areas. However, targeted regulatory interventions—such as service-level requirements or using TNC taxes to subsidize public transit—can mitigate these inequities. Furthermore, the analysis of AV technology transfer between autonomous and traditional ride-hailing platforms uncovers complex strategic interactions: while technology sharing can enhance industry-wide efficiency and profit, it may also erode the welfare of human drivers and passengers, and the distribution of benefits is highly sensitive to cost structures and market power.

26200420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26200420.value: This project lays a strong foundation for further development in both theoretical modeling and practical policy applications for urban mobility systems. Future research can extend the developed models to capture dynamic, time-varying demand and supply, self-scheduling behaviors of drivers, and more complex traveler preferences, enabling a finer analysis of peak and off-peak effects. Incorporating the competition among multiple TNC platforms, as well as explicitly modeling public transit integration and high-capacity, on-demand services, would provide a richer framework for policy analysis. In terms of concrete actions, the research team plans to apply for further funding to continue and expand this line of investigation. Additional resources will support new empirical studies, pilot projects in collaboration with city authorities and industry partners, and the development of more advanced educational materials and courses for students and practitioners. By building on the strong foundation laid by this project, the team aims to provide robust, data-driven guidance for the next generation of urban transport policy and innovation.

26200420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26200420.value: This research tackles the challenges of ride-hailing services and the coming wave of driverless cars in busy cities. As these services have grown, they have made getting around more convenient, but have also led to more traffic congestion and worries about fair treatment for drivers and passengers. Our work developed new ways for governments and companies to understand and manage these impacts. Using real-world data and advanced models, we tested different policies like charging extra for entering crowded areas or making sure drivers earn a fair wage. We also explored creative solutions, such as letting ride-hailing cars park in underused garages instead of endlessly circling the streets, which can cut down on unnecessary traffic. Our research found that targeted policies can reduce congestion and help everyone—passengers, drivers, companies, and the city—benefit together. We also looked ahead to a future with more driverless cars and found that, if left unregulated, these technologies could make existing inequalities in transportation worse. However, with the right rules and cooperation between new and old transport services, cities can ensure better access and fairness for all. This research provides practical tools and guidance for making urban transportation smoother, fairer, and more sustainable.

26200520.label: Project Objectives
26200520.value: Fabricate three types of heterostructures: graphene/ferromagnet (control experiment), twisted bilayer graphene (TBG)/ferromagnet, and transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/ferromagnet. In this proposed study, we aim to achieve unconventional and large spin-orbit torques in low-symmetry 2D material/ferromagnet heterostructures. TBG and 1T’-phase TMDs have low crystalline symmetries, which allow unconventional spin-orbit torques (SOTs). Besides, TBG has strong orbital Hall effect and TMDs have strong spin-orbit coupling; both could generate large SOTs. We will use the transfer technique, magnetron sputtering, and nanofabrication to fabricate these heterostructures. Investigate SOTs in these three types of heterostructures: experiments and theoretical understanding. SOT effect allows us to investigate the charge-to-spin conversion in 2D materials, which is of fundamental interest and critical for spintronic applications. SOTs generated by TBG have not been studied; the efficiency with which this orbital momentum can be converted into spin momentum remains a fundamental issue. Another open question is the origin of SOTs in the 1T’-TMD/ferromagnet. We will use the customized integrated magneto-optical-electrical platform, which enables second-harmonic, loop shift, magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE), and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance techniques, to accurately determine the SOT efficiency. To understand the mechanism, we will actively collaborate with the theoretical group. Investigate current-induced perpendicular magnetization switching in these three types of heterostructures. Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) is required for high-density spintronic applications. The unconventional out-of-plane damping-like SOT generated by low-symmetry 2D materials allows the most efficient perpendicular magnetization switching. We will first deposit ferromagnets with PMA on top of 2D materials and then investigate current-induced magnetization switching. We will directly resolve magnetization dynamic process via magneto-optical Kerr effect.

26200520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26200520.value: Two-dimensional (2D) materials such as graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) show unconventional and highly tunable electronic and optoelectronic properties. They have the potential for use in many applications, including nanoelectronic devices, photodetectors, and sensors. Low-symmetry 2D materials are promising for generating a large and unconventional out-of-plane damping-like spin-orbit torque (DL-SOT), which is a critical objective in spintronics. To achieve magnetization reversal with the least current, we need to have the largest possible charge-to-spin conversion or SOT efficiency. The applicant has shown that topological insulators (TIs) exhibit a giant SOT efficiency and can be used to switch magnetization. The applicant has also demonstrated the strong Rashba effect-induced SOT in the monolayer 2H-TMD/ferromagnet. However, for magnetization reversal, both the magnitude and direction of SOTs are critical. In heavy metal/, TI/, and 2H-TMD/ferromagnet heterostructures, the DL-SOT that compensates magnetic damping is required to lie in the thin-film plane because of preserved rotational symmetry. As a result, the conventional in-plane DL-SOT is incapable of switching perpendicular magnetization that is needed for high-density spintronic applications. Low-symmetry 2D materials break rotational symmetry and offer an unprecedented opportunity to generate unconventional out-of-plane DL-SOT. Two important classes of low-symmetry 2D materials the applicant proposes to study are twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) and 1T’-TMDs. Recently, TBG emerged as a new platform to host orbital magnetism, quantized anomalous Hall effect, and a giant orbital Hall effect. It is thus of great fundamental interest to determine the efficiency with which this orbital momentum is converted to spin momentum. 1T’-TMDs only have one mirror plane perpendicular to the low-symmetry axis. Strong spin-orbit coupling of 1T’-TMDs leads to various topological states, such as Weyl semimetal and TI. Recent experiments indicated that the out-of-plane DL-SOTs can be generated by 1T’-TMDs by applying current along the low-symmetry axis. However, there is no report on current-induced perpendicular magnetization switching using this unconventional SOT. In this proposed study, we will investigate SOTs and current-induced switching in graphene/, TBG/, 1T’-TMD/ferromagnet with perpendicular anisotropy at room temperature. We will fabricate these heterostructures by using dry transfer, magnetron sputtering, and nanofabrication techniques. Then, we will measure SOTs using various techniques and strive to understand the origin of SOTs by collaborating with the theory group. Finally, we will demonstrate current-induced perpendicular magnetization switching. The proposed study will provide fundamental spintronic knowledge of these 2D materials and pave the way for 2D material-based energy-efficient and high-density spintronic applications. 二維材料，例如石墨烯和過渡金屬硫族化合物（TMD），具有非常規且高度可調的電子和光電特性。它們有許多潛在應用，包括納米電子設備，光電探測器和傳感器。低對稱二維材料有望產生巨大的非常規平面外阻尼樣自旋軌道扭矩（DL-SOT），這是自旋電子學中的關鍵目標。為了以最小的電流實現磁矩反轉，我們需要具有盡可能大的電荷到自旋轉換或SOT效率。申請人已經表明，拓撲絕緣體（TI）表現出巨大的SOT效率，可用於翻轉磁矩。申請人還已經證明了在單層2H相 TMD/鐵磁體中強Rashba效應誘導的SOT。但是，對於磁矩翻轉，SOT的大小和方向都至關重要。在重金屬/，TI /和2H相 TMD /鐵磁體異質結構中，由於保留了旋轉對稱性，因此補償磁阻尼所需要的DL-SOT嚴格位於薄膜平面中。結果，傳統的平面內DL-SOT不能翻轉高密度自旋電子學應用所需的垂直磁矩。低對稱性二維材料打破了旋轉對稱性，提供了前所未有的機會來生成非常規的平面外DL-SOT。申請人提議研究的兩類重要的低對稱二維材料是扭角雙層石墨烯（TBG）和1T’相TMD。最近，TBG成為研究軌道磁場，量子化的反常霍爾效應和巨大的軌道霍爾效應的新平台。從基本物理的角度看，確定軌道動量轉換成自旋動量的效率非常重要。 1T’相TMD僅具有一個垂直於低對稱軸的鏡平面。 1T’相TMD的強自旋軌道耦合會導致各種拓撲狀態，例如Weyl半金屬和TI。最近的實驗表明，通過沿低對稱軸施加電流，可以由1T’相TMD生成面外DL-SOT。但是，沒有關於使用這種非常規SOT翻轉垂直磁矩的報導。在這項擬議的研究中，我們將研究室溫下具有垂直各向異性的石墨烯/，TBG /，1T’-TMD /鐵磁體中的SOT和電流翻轉磁矩。我們將使用乾轉移，磁控濺射和納米製造技術來製造這些異質結構。然後，我們將使用各種技術來測量SOT，並與理論組合作，了解SOT的起源。最後，我們將演示電流翻轉垂直磁矩。擬議的研究將提供有關這些二維材料的基本自旋電子學知識，並為基於二維材料的高能效和高密度自旋電子學應用鋪平道路。

26200520.label: Realisation of objectives
26200520.value: Our objectives listed in 5.2 can be divided into three major parts: (1) fabricate the heterostructures with low-symmetry spin-orbit torque (SOT) source materials; (2) measure and understand the SOTs in these heterostructures; (3) realize field-free switching in these heterostructures. We have achieved the above-mentioned objectives by realizing following items: (1) We have fabricated various types of low-symmetry SOT source material/ferromagnet heterostructures, where the SOT source material can be low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDs, like MoS2, WTe2, TaIrTe4) and spin-splitting antiferromagnet (RuO2), and the ferromagnetic material can be conventional magnetic multilayers, like NiFe, Ni, Fe, CoFeB with in-plane anisotropy and Ti/CoFeB, Mo/CoFeB with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, or 2D ferromagnets, like Fe3GaTe2. We have fabricated graphene/ferromagnet heterostructures and due to its high symmetry, there is no unconventional SOT being identified. We have also tried to fabricate twisted bilayer graphene (TBG), however, the uniformity was poor and the TBG films were easily relaxed to homogenous bilayers. Considering the practical applications, we need to further address these issues before studying TBG-based SOT heterostructures and devices. (2) We have measured the SOTs and their efficiencies in various heterostructures. We have employed the techniques such as second-harmonic Hall method, current-induced loop shift method, spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance methods to determine the SOTs. We understand these SOTs from the crystalline and magnetic symmetry analysis together with the first-principle calculations and tight-binding models. (3) We have realized field-free switching in low-symmetry TMD/ferromagnet heterostructures at room temperature. First, in collaboration with Prof. Guoqiang Yu’s group at Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Science, Beijing, we demonstrated the field-free switching in TaIrTe4/Ti/CoFeB heterostructures, where TaIrTer4 is low-symmetry Weyl semimetal. We showed that along the high-symmetry axis, the current cannot induce unconventional SOT and thus the current-induced magnetization switching has to be field-assisted. Then, we showed that along the low-symmetry axis, the current induces unconventional SOT along the out-of-plane direction and thus causes field-free switching. The results were published in Science Advances [1]. Second, to further study the interface effect and enhance the SOT efficiency, we have prepared various TaIrTe4/ferromagnet heterostructures. We found a giant unconventional SOT in TaIrTe4/Fe3GaTe2, where Fe3GaTe2 is a 2D ferromagnet with room-temperature perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. As a result of this giant unconventional SOT, we realized the field-free switching that is the most robust against the in-plane field disturbance. The results were published in Advanced Materials [2]. In the progress to achieve the objectives listed in 5.2, We have a few postgraduate (PG) students (Kun, Zheyu, Ruizi, Yiyang, Shun Kong, and Xuezhao) and one postdoc (Yuting) being involved in this project. We have additional result output in this project: 1. As the PI, I have trained my postgraduate students and postdoc to understand SOT, fabricate SOT devices, and perform SOT measurements. We have written four review articles about SOT and SOT from 2D materials [3-4]. Ref. [3] was featured as a cover and has been cited more than 400 times in Google Scholar. Together with collaborators from Yale and Teaxs A&M, my PG student Ruizi and I have written semi-metals for spintronics on Nature Reviews Electrical Engineering [4]. 2. To enhance the SOT switching efficiency, we have utilized the magnetic topological insulators (MTIs) at room temperature, which have giant SOTs due to topological surface states. Together with MTIs’ giant anomalous Hall resistance due to chiral edge states, my PG student Kun and postdoc Yuting have recently demonstrated the cryogenic in-memory computing with high energy efficiency and high accuracy. This cryogenic in-memory computing scheme can be used for quantum control with high energy efficiency and minimal inference delay. The results have been published at Nature Materials [5]. 3. PG student Zheyu has worked on another SOT device system (tungsten/terbium iron garnet, W/TbIG) and demonstrated SOT switching in this device. We have quantified the SOT efficiency and understand how the thermal effect contributes to the SOT switching. In particular, we solve the puzzle of SOT switching of compensated ferrimagnetic insulator, which behaves like a static antiferromagnet [6]. 4. In collaboration with Institute of Microelectronics, we have shown that with inhomogeneous ion implantation in a Hall bar device to achieve structural symmetry breaking, we can realize field-free magnetization switching [7]. 5. Other publications are listed as refs. [8-11]. 26200520.label: Major findings and research outcome
26200520.value: We have made significant advancements in using low-symmetry van der Waals (vdW) materials to achieve field-free spin-orbit torque (SOT)-driven magnetization switching, with important implications for spintronic devices. Both refs [1] and [2] focus on the Weyl semimetal TaIrTe4, a material with low crystal symmetry that enables unconventional spin currents with out-of-plane polarization (σz). This property allows for field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization at room temperature, eliminating the need for external magnetic fields, which is a critical step toward compact spintronic devices. Ref. [2] demonstrates robust field-free switching in an all-vdW TaIrTe4/Fe3GaTe2 heterostructure. A high SOT efficiency of 0.37 is achieved at 300 K, with deterministic switching occurring at a current density of 2.56 × 10¹⁰ A/m². The switching polarity remains stable against in-plane magnetic fields up to 252 mT, highlighting the robustness of the system. Numerical simulations show that the large unconventional SOT reduces switching currents while enhancing stability, making vdW heterostructures promising candidates for energy-efficient spintronic devices. Similarly, ref. [1] investigates TaIrTe4/Ti/CoFeB heterostructures and confirms field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization at room temperature with an unconventional SOT efficiency (ξσz) of 0.03. Magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) imaging further verifies deterministic switching driven by σz with repeatability and high switching stability. Both studies emphasize the importance of high-quality interfaces achieved through advanced fabrication methods (e.g., vacuum exfoliation). The vdW nature of TaIrTe4 ensures atomically flat interfaces, contributing to the observed high SOT efficiency and robust switching performance. These findings position vdW heterostructures, particularly TaIrTe4-based systems, as strong candidates for next-generation spintronic devices such as magnetic random-access memory (MRAM). The low switching current densities and high robustness make these systems highly attractive for industrial applications. As a side product, we introduce magnetic topological memristors (MTMs) based on magnetic topological insulators (MTIs) for cryogenic in-memory computing (IMC), leveraging the coexistence of chiral edge states (CESs) and topological surface states (TSSs). MTMs exhibit energy-efficient, stable, and low-stochasticity memristive SOT switching at cryogenic temperatures (2 K), making them ideal for machine learning and quantum computing applications (ref. [5]). MTMs achieve software-level accuracy in neural network tasks, such as 96% accuracy on the Iris dataset and comparable performance to floating-point networks in MNIST digit recognition and CIFAR-10 image classification. Their ability to natively support bipolar weights enhances matrix-vector multiplication efficiency, outperforming unipolar memristors. MTMs also enable reinforcement learning for quantum state preparation with shorter training times and lower energy consumption.

26200520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26200520.value: The two articles (refs. [1] and [2]) highlight significant advancements in spintronics, focusing on field-free magnetization switching using van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures and spin-orbit torque (SOT) mechanisms. To further develop this research, key areas of potential and proposed actions include: Material Optimization and Scalability: Improve the growth techniques for high-quality vdW heterostructures, such as TaIrTe4 and Fe3GaTe2, to achieve wafer-scale production with controlled thickness and uniformity. Explore alternative vdW materials (e.g., MnBi2Te4 or twisted magnetic topological insulator) with enhanced SOT efficiency and stability for broader applications. Device Integration and Industrial Application: Develop scalable device architectures for integrating vdW heterostructures into spintronic devices like magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) and logic circuits. Investigate gate-controlled spin generation to enable energy-efficient, programmable spintronic devices. Cryogenic and Quantum Technologies: Extend the application of vdW topological materials to cryogenic in-memory computing and quantum technologies, leveraging their robust SOT and high energy efficiency at low temperatures. Theoretical and Numerical Modeling: Conduct in-depth simulations to optimize device performance and understand the role of interfacial effects, spin transparency, and unconventional spin currents in vdW systems. These actions will enable efficient, scalable, and robust vdW-based spintronic devices for future quantum and classical computing technologies.

26200520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26200520.value: This research focuses on using cutting-edge materials called two-dimensional (2D) materials, which are just a few atoms thick, to develop the next generation of energy-efficient and compact electronics. These materials, like Weyl semimetals and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), have unique properties that make them ideal for creating faster and more efficient electronic devices. One key challenge in spintronics—a field that uses the spin of electrons to store and process information—is to control the magnetic state of a material using electric currents without needing external magnetic fields, which are bulky and inefficient. In our project, we studied TaIrTe4, a material with a special low-symmetry structure that enables the generation of unusual spin currents. These spin currents allowed us to achieve field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization at room temperature, a significant breakthrough for creating ultra-dense and energy-efficient memory devices. This achievement eliminates the need for external magnetic fields and paves the way for more compact, faster, and environmentally friendly spintronic devices, such as next-generation memory and computing devices. Our work provides a critical step forward in understanding these advanced materials and their potential to revolutionize modern electronics.

26206520.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26206520.value: 軟件反編譯器功能性測試

26206520.label: Project Objectives
26206520.value: To extend a metamorphic testing scheme, equivalent module inputs (EMI) testing, to test decompilers. EMI should be able to pinpoint decompiler flaws that can generate mal-functional decompiled outputs. Such erroneous outputs can cause much confusion of users and break the root trust of many cybersecurity and software re-engineering applications. To design a novel metamorphic testing scheme, program structure-correlation (PSC) testing, to test decompilers. PSC should also be able to pinpoint decompiler defects yielding mal-functional outputs. PSC testing is complementary to EMI testing, in that PSC can expose more flaws comparing to EMI testing, but can produce false positives. To design a novel fuzz testing method that leverages generative deep learning techniques to synthesize syntactically and semantically valid inputs to test decompilers. The fuzz testing technique should be able to expose crashes and hangs in decompilers, which presumably indicate decompiler vulnerabilities that can be leveraged for exploitation. To summarize findings and demystify the capability of modern decompilers. To collaborate with decompiler developers and perform root cause analysis of the decompiler flaws we find and push for the fix.

26206520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26206520.value: 軟件反編譯器將可執行文件（編譯器的輸出）轉換為源代碼。反編譯出來的源代碼一旦重新被編譯，將產生同原始可執行文件相同功能的新的可執行文件。經過二十多年的發展，反編譯器已廣泛用於生產中，以支持基於逆向工程的各種應用程序與場景，包括軟件重用，軟件安全性加固，軟件漏洞查找，並作為很多軟件惡意攻擊的第一步。作為眾多計算機安全任務中最核心的組成部分和信任的基礎，反編譯器被應用於幾乎所有對惡意軟件（計算機病毒）的分析過程中，極大的幫助了計算機安全專業人員對現實軟件係統中漏洞的查詢與理解。儘管如此，反編譯器的功能性錯誤很少得到足夠的重視。這類錯誤，一旦出現，就會給用戶造成很大的困擾，而且有可能被惡意攻擊者利用（漏洞經常從IDA-Pro這樣的流行的商用反編譯器中發現）。總的來說，反編譯器的錯誤會極大程度破壞對計算機安全和軟件工程領域諸多應用場景的信任鏈，從而危及許多現實應用場景。 我們這項研究課題的目的是對反編譯器進行系統的功能性測試， 以衡量其反編譯的正確性。具體來說，我們提出了三種技術，即等效模塊輸入（EMI Testing）測試，程序結構相關性（PSC Testing）測試和模糊（Fuzz Testing）測試，以測試反編譯器的功能正確性。反編譯器包含是一個複雜的對輸入可執行文件進行分析和變換的流程。我們提出的這三種測試技術將首次共同被應用，檢測出反編譯流程中隱藏的錯誤。從蛻變測試（metamorphic testing ）技術派生的EMI和PSC測試可以巧妙地解決軟件測試中的測試準則定義問題，從而迅速暴露錯誤的反編譯輸出。擬議的模糊測試通過利用生成型深度學習技術（generative deep learning ）的最新突破，快速生成大量格式正確的反編譯器輸入測試樣例，以暴露導致反編譯器崩潰（crash）的錯誤。 我們的初步實驗結果，以及JEB3和RetDec反編譯器開發人員的確認表明，該項研究課題以及其所提出的測試技術已顯示出發現反編譯器缺陷的巨大潛力。一旦該研究課題被完成，我們預期軟件逆向工程的可靠性會大大增加。兩家的反編譯器供應商PNF Software和Avast Software對支持該項目表現出了濃厚的興趣。他們將就我們研究中的發現提供反饋，並有可能在他們的反編譯器開發中採用該項目。

26206520.label: Realisation of objectives
26206520.value: The research project has successfully achieving its objectives, with 9 papers published in top-tier venues and 1 paper still under peer review. Defects found in the research project have been responsibly reported to the vendors/developers, with corresponding fixes deployed to production. Through surveying existing works, our research revealed that current decompiler frameworks are typically optimized for readability rather than enabling downstream tasks and ensuring correctness. To address this, we developed a new metamorphic testing methodology called program structure-correlation (PSC) testing for decompilers. By combining our testing techniques with deep learning, we generated test cases that effectively stress decompiler. We successfully applied this testing methodology to various frameworks, including IDA Pro, Ghidra, and BinaryAI. Furthermore, our methodology can be generalized to test other software engineering tools, such as code completion systems, static analyzers, and simulators.

26206520.label: Major findings and research outcome
26206520.value: In all, this research project is leading to the publication of 9 papers in top-tier venues, with 1 paper still under peer review. We start this project by surveying the capabilities and limitations of decompilers [Reference C9.6] through testing, which revealed that decompilers widely used in the field are usually targeted for analysis rather than correctness, leading to confusion and misinterpretations. This survey provided a comprehensive understanding of decompilers and their limitations, which served as the foundation for our subsequent research. Notably, this survey is published in the IEEE S&P, the most prestigious venue in security research. (Corresponding to Objective 1, 2, 4) Building on these findings, we further enhance the metamorphic testing scheme with program structure-correlation (PSC) testing and fuzz testing to identify in-depth correctness issues in these analysis platforms [Reference C9.2, C9.3, C9.7 ,C9.8]. After working with the vendors to conduct a root cause analysis, we summarized our findings and proposed several lightweight enhancements to address these issues [Reference C9.5]. As remark, the issue we reported has been resolved and the corresponding fix is being released in production. (Corresponding to Objective 1,2,3,4) Throughout this process, we recognized the challenges in fixing decompiler defects, as it often takes vendors considerable time to implement fixes due to the complexity of these systems. To help address this, we proposed a novel approach leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify and synthesize correct program snippets corresponding to identified defects [Reference C8.1]. The repaired outputs generated can further support downstream security analysis tasks such as vulnerability detection. (Corresponding to Objective 4) In addition, we generalized our PSC testing methodologies and applied them to other critical systems, e.g. code completion systems [Reference C9.1], static code analyzer [Reference C9.1] and physics simulator [Reference C9.4]. It is important to note that traditional software testing techniques are often focused on crashes, making these defects not exposed for years. On the other hand, our method can reveal these critical non-crash issues. Notably, our work evaluating physics simulator [Reference C9.4] received the Best Paper Award at the ASE 2023. (Corresponding to Objective 1,2,3) In summary, our research has made significant progress in developing novel testing methodologies for decompilation platforms, successfully identifying defects in these critical systems. We then further generalized and extended our methodologies to other critical systems.

26206520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26206520.value: Our research has identified two potential areas for further development: 1. Automated Defect Localization in Decompilers Output: Currently, decompiler developers are required to spend hours localizing errors in decompilers' outputs. This is inherently challenging due to the undecidability nature of the problem. While formal verification offers potential solutions, they are often impractical due to manual model creation requirements and high FP/FN from the analysis. At the moment, 2 PhD students are working on this, and exploring the possibility of combining program validation techniques to tackle this problem. 2. LLM-Enhanced Automated Repair Techniques: Building on our preliminary work with LLM, we've observed both promise and limitations, particularly for complex defects. A future research direction is to develop a novel repair technique that combines LLMs with Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Our tentative research indicates that using a typical RAG technique can improve the quality of the repaired outputs. Yet, this technique still shows deficiency when handling complex defects, due to the fuzzy nature of embeddings. So far, 2 PhD students are working on this, and researching on potential solutions to enhance the confidence of the retrieval.

26206520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26206520.value: Our research project is about making sure tools(decompilers) that reconstruct CPU instruction into human-readable code are working correctly. For cybersecurity professionals, decompilers are essential, especially when analyzing malware and software vulnerabilities that have the potential to have a significant negative impact on society. In all, our team found that a large number of popular decompilers aren't as accurate as they should be. We created new methods to test these decompilers and identify such problems. After that, we collaborated with the vendors of these tools to address the issues we discovered. We even looked into using LLM to fix some of these problems in real-time. But we did not stop there. We also apply our knowledge to other critical computer systems, such as code completion tools that assist programmers in writing safer code and simulators used in scientific research. By enhancing these tools, we make them more precise and dependable, lowering the impact software flaws and vulnerabilities have on society.

26210320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26210320.value: 基於超聲全波形幾何反演的缺陷表徵

26210320.label: Project Objectives
26210320.value: To establish fundamental algorithms for directly inverting the geometrical parameters of various defects, such as length and angle, by optimising the defect shape until the simulated waveforms match the measured waveforms. To investigate approaches to ensure that the defect model will be updated iteratively towards the real defect geometries during the inversion; FWI is solving an optimisation problem and hence it is critical to avoid the optimisation being trapped in local minima, causing erroneous updates of the defect model. To investigate the effects of array configuration (e.g., array aperture size and element spacing) on the waveform inversion, and to investigate the capability of the new approach to identify small features of the crack (e.g., resolution limit). To conduct experiments with a commercial ultrasonic phased array system to evaluate the performance of developed FWI approaches, using manufactured defects.

26210320.value: 超聲波相控陣成像以及後續的圖像處理現在成為無損檢測領域一個快速發展的方向。相對於單個超聲探頭，相控陣能夠更為準確地表征缺陷的關鍵特徵（如角度和傾角等）。然而傳統的相控陣圖像由於精度的限制難以提供缺陷的細節以及形狀，因此缺陷的特徵只能從比較模糊的圖像中獲得。從地震波勘探領域發展出來的全波反演技術通過有效利用測量的全波形信息，有潛力對缺陷進行更為精確的描述。全波反演技術通過有限元模型逐步地更新缺陷的物理模型，直到模擬和測量的信號一致。然而，與地震波勘探相比無損檢測的應用具有不同的挑戰：無損檢測尋求直接反演缺陷的幾何形態，而不是傳統地震波勘探的波速反演。因此需要新的研究，將地震波全波反演的概念和技術發展到無損檢測領域，有可能在超聲缺陷表征方向取得突破。 該項目的主要目的是建立一套新的全波反演算法，結合拓撲/幾何優化的手段用於直接重構真實缺陷的幾何特征（例如長度和傾角等）。前期的部分模擬和實驗結果有力地驗證了該項目的基本概念以及可行性。研究將從以下幾個方面展開：(i)發展基於波形反演的算法，用於重構各種二維和三維缺陷形狀；(ii)研究陣列設置以及參數（如視角和陣源的排布）對反演算法的影響，並且研究反演的精度；(iii)探尋不同方法，避免幾何優化反演陷於局部最小值，從而使反演的缺陷形狀逐漸更新到真實的形狀；(iv)利用超聲相控陣的實驗驗證。該項目的成果將影響無損檢測領域很多應用方向，包括開發出一套全自動化高精度的超聲缺陷表征算法。成果將對香港和內地關鍵工業和經濟產生有利的影響。

26211120.label: Project Objectives
26211120.value: Develop a stochastic control model for a firm facing production uncertainty and a generalized setup of investment frictions. Propose an explicit characterization of the optimal control policies. Clarify the contradiction between the ``bad news" and ``good news" principles, and investigate the joint effects of different investment frictions on a firm's optimal policies. Extend our analysis further to three cases: (1) analyzing the conventional NPV method and comparing it with our method, thereby complementing the analysis in Milne and Whally (2000); (2) including an abandonment option to examine the firm’s optimal abandonment choice for investments under development during the investment lag; and (3) incorporating investment tax incentives to examine how they affect a firm’s investment decisions given investment lag. Conduct an empirical study with firm level data to examine how various investment frictions affect a firm's investment decisions.

26211120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26211120.value: 資本投資是公司最重要的綜合活動之一。然而，現有研究中關於投資時機的結果是有爭議的。生產率的不確定性可能對公司的投資時機產生負面和正面影響。例如，Bernanke（1983）首次提出的，公司的投資有一個“壞消息原則”；即公司應該在投資回報不穩定的情況下要謹慎投資（參見 Dixit和Pindyck 1994）。相反，在後來的研究中，Bar-Ilan和Strange（1996）發現了“好消息原理”；即在存在投資滯後的情況下，不確定性可能對投資產生積極影響。此外，文獻中確定投資時機的不同方法之間的比較可能會不一致。例如，一些文獻強調了淨現值方法（NPV）的不准確性（例如，Dixit和Pindyck 1994），而其他研究則表明當當存在較大投資滯後時，NPV方法是實物期權方法一個很好的近似（例如，Milne和Whally 2000）。本質上，現有文獻和模型僅考慮了部分投資成本，從而在選擇投資時機上缺乏共識。 在本項目中，我們建議在廣義的投資成本設置中研究公司最優投資。我們將嘗試解決上述爭議並實現以下研究目標：（1）我們將提出一個隨機控制模型來研究面臨各種投資成本時公司的最優投資決策，投資成本包括投資滯後，機會成本調整，交易成本，和可逆性成本。常規方法可能很難求解此模型，因為它是二維且部分為非馬爾可夫的模型。我們將對模型的解提出一個解析刻畫以及漸近分析，以獲得最佳控制政策。 （2）通過研究投資滯後和各種調整成本對公司的共同影響，來探查“好消息”和“壞消息”原則之間的聯繫，從而得以補充Bar-Ilan和Strange（1996）中的分析。 （3）我們將擴展模型來進一步分析以下三種情況：（a）檢查NPV方法並將其與我們的方法進行比較，從而在一般框架內補充了Milne和Whally（2000）中的分析； （b）允許公司在投資滯後期間放棄項目；和（c）投資稅收優惠的影響。 （4）我們將利用企業層面的數據來進行實證研究並探查各種投資摩擦如何影響公司的投資決策。

26211120.label: Realisation of objectives
26211120.value: All four stated objectives in the proposal have been fully achieved in the research working paper "A Positive Model of Corporate Investment". We begin by introducing the motivation of the paper and then outline how each objective is addressed. This paper explores how investment frictions, such as lags and adjustment costs, influence corporate investment decisions, challenging the classic q theory’s emphasis on contemporaneous fundamentals. Firm-level data reveals a strong correlation between investment and historical profitability, raising questions about the role of past fundamentals. Additionally, the real options literature presents conflicting theories on how uncertainty affects investment. Using a generalized framework of investment frictions, we reconcile these theories, showing that investment lags and adjustment costs jointly determine whether uncertainty delays or hastens investment. We also explain observed investment patterns and provide insights into firm behavior with significant implications for capital-intensive industries and policy design. Regarding objective 1: In Section 2, we develop a continuous-time stochastic control model incorporating key investment frictions, including lags, adjustment opportunity costs, and non-convex transaction costs, extending standard models (Abel and Eberly, 1996; 2011). Sections 3 and 4 characterize the firm’s optimal two-trigger investment policy, showing how the marginal value of capital depends on the state variable (productivity-to-capital ratio) and fluctuates between two trigger values. Importantly, we demonstrate that investment decisions rely heavily on historical fundamentals, with the investment-productivity relationship shaped by the structure of frictions. Regarding objective 2: In Section 7, we conduct numerical analysis to evaluate the joint effects of investment frictions on optimal policies. Our model shows that: (1) in the absence of lags and adjustment costs, high volatility delays investment, confirming the "Bad News" principle (Bernanke, 1983); (2) with lags, high volatility can hasten investment, consistent with the "Good News" principle (Bar-Ilan and Strange, 1996); and (3) introducing adjustment costs reverses this effect, with high volatility delaying investment. Simulations further reveal that the correlation between investment and lagged profitability critically depends on the coexistence of these frictions. Regarding objective 3: In Sections 8 and 9, we extend the model to practical scenarios. For example, when uncertainty is ignored in industry practice, we establish sufficient conditions for firms to prefer immediate investment over waiting. In such cases, the NPV rule aligns with the real options method. When significant lags exist, we show how a simple adjustment to the NPV rule ensures consistency with the real options approach, providing practitioners with a reliable rule of thumb for investment decisions. Regarding objective 4: Sections 5 and 6 provide empirical validation for the model using firm-level data from 1980 to 2020. The analysis documents a significant correlation between investment and lagged profitability, consistent across firms of varying sizes and fixed asset levels. Model calibration shows that incorporating investment frictions explains this relationship, while ignoring lags or adjustment costs results in mismatched predictions. In conclusion, our paper bridges the q theory of investment and real options models by introducing a framework that highlights the critical roles of investment lags and adjustment costs. These frictions shape the investment-profitability relationship, determine the dominance of the “Good News” or “Bad News” principle, and inform the validity of the NPV rule as a benchmark for investment decisions.

26211120.label: Major findings and research outcome
26211120.value: The outcome of this project is a working paper titled "A Positive Model of Corporate Investment". Our paper examines a model where corporate investment faces a general structure of frictions. In equilibrium, determining investment levels lags behind their inception, creating a significant link between investments and past productivity-to-capital ratios. Evidence from firm-level data spanning 1980 to 2020 supports this result and simulation shows it depends critically on the structure of frictions. Key findings include: i) the model reconciles the dark side (Bernanke, 1983) and bright side (Bar-Ilan and Strange, 1996a) of uncertainty in investment timing; ii) risk hedging may diminish investment rate; iii) without uncertainty, the net present value rule remains effective for optimal investment decisions.

26211120.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26211120.value: Future research avenues could explore more complex and realistic processes, such as stochastic productivity volatility or random construction lags in capital investment. Integrating these factors into our model may provide valuable insights into the relationships among profitability, uncertainty, and investment dynamics, as explored by Bloom (2007).

26211120.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26211120.value: How to invest in a general frictional environment is central in firm's decision makings. We develop a positive model that provides a general structure of investment frictions, bridging the q theory of investment and real option models. Our research provides several important insights into firm investment behavior dynamics. On the one hand, we provide a rationale for the empirical findings that a firm's investment choices depend on its historical profitability, emphasizing that this relationship is significantly influenced by investment lags and adjustment opportunity costs. Moreover, our general structure of investment frictions enriches existing real option models in three important aspects. We reconcile the "good news principle" and "bad news principle" identified in the literature, illustrating that the dominance of either principle is contingent on the interaction between investment lags and adjustment opportunity costs. Next we uncover a downside to uncertainty driven by risk management incentives, suggesting that firms may strategically reduce their investment levels to mitigate risks. Lastly, we highlight that when uncertainty is overlooked, the efficiency of the widely accepted NPV rule as a benchmark for investment decision-making can be improved through a simple adjustment.

26212320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26212320.value: Modern digital service platforms, such as ride sharing, online advertisement, and cloud computing, are dramatically different from those in the industrial era. Traditional service industries, including transportation and logistics, usually deal with bulk orders from relatively static groups of customers. Thus, these service providers are usually certain about the demand from their customers. By contrast, digital services are much more accessible to ordinary people than traditional service industries. Modern service platforms have attracted a considerably large user base, and the heterogeneous needs of the individuals have led to a highly dynamic customer pool. New challenges arise when service providers are facing uncertainties in both the service rewards and the dynamically changing customer pools. The proposed research aims to provide quantitative insights into the optimal operation strategy and the optimal design of the service platform under uncertain rewards and customer dynamics. Service platforms aim to maximize the revenue, which is the rewards less the penalties for service delays. To achieve this goal, the service provider makes the crucial operational decision to allocate available servers to the customers. A smart allocation policy must balance multiple goals: the minimization of service delays, the learning of random rewards, and the maximization of revenue. Solving the optimal operation strategy is non-trivial because it involves the interaction among queueing theory, online learning theory, and non-convex optimization. We shall develop a theoretical framework for the platforms' operation in which the decision-makers can devise real-time resource allocation strategies with theoretical guarantees. We will then use the analytical framework to address critical managerial questions. For individual business practitioners, we focus on the design problems of the platform, such as the initial planning and future adjustments of the service capacity. For the service market, we leverage our understanding of individual firms to study the pricing of service resources and the regulation of the service industry. In post-industrial economies, modern service platforms are dramatically reshaping the daily lives of individuals and opening new possibilities for small businesses. We believe that the potential outcome of the proposed project may lead to insightful implications for the transformation of the modern service industries. 共享經濟、在線廣告和雲計算等現代數字服務平台相較於工業時代的傳統服務系統有顯著的不同之處。傳統服務行業，包括運輸和物流系统，通常處理相對固定的客戶群的大宗訂單。因此，這類服務提供者對客戶及其需求有相對準決的認知。相較之下，普通人更容易獲得在線數字服務，後者因而吸引了相當廣泛的用戶群。個人的異質化服務需求導致了高度動態變化的客戶群。當服務回報和客戶群的構成方面都有高度的不確定性時，服務提供商就會面臨新的挑戰。 擬議的研究旨在為不確定獎勵和客戶動態下的最佳運營策略和服務平台的最佳設計提供定量分析。服務平台旨在最大程度地增加收入，即服務所產生的收益減去服務延誤導致的罰款。為了實現這一目標，如何合理的將可用服務器分配給客戶是至關重要的運營決策。明智的分配策略必須在多個目標之間取得平衡：服務延遲的最小化，隨機獎勵的學習以及收益的最大化。尋找最佳操作策略並非易事，因為它涉及排隊理論，在線學習理論和非凸優化之間的相互作用。我們將為平台的運行建立一個理論框架，決策者可以在此框架下設計具有理論保證的實時資源配給策略。 我們亦將使用這一理論框架來解決關鍵的運營管理問題。對於個體從業者，我們專注於平台的設計問題，例如服務資源的初期規劃和動態調整。對於服務市場，我們利用對單個公司的了解來研究服務資源的定價和服務行業的監管。 在後工業時代，現代服務平台正在極大地改變個人的日常生活，並為中小型企業提供了新的可能性。我們認為，擬議項目的潛在結果會為現代服務業的轉型帶來深刻的啟示。

26300020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26300020.value: The ocean plays a central role in the evolution of the Earth's climate evolution through its role in transporting large amounts of heat, carbon and chemicals via its circulation. A central tool at our disposal for studying and modeling the ocean circulation is ocean general circulation models (OGCMs), i.e. numerical representations of oceanic physical and biogeochemical processes. The OGCM's ability to represent a circulation that responds ``correctly'' to changes in atmospheric conditions is thus of paramount importance, notably for climate projection exercises. However, it is increasingly recognized that a large class of OGCMs employed for past and present Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports display responses to atmospheric changes that diverge from those expected from basic process and modeling studies. This divergence is of particular concern because it raises doubts about the margins of uncertainty in climate projections provided by the international coordinated efforts. A principal source of the above disagreement in OGCMs has been attributed to the representation of mesoscale turbulence and its feedback onto the mean circulation. Recent works utilizing eddy energy information to inform the strength and distribution of turbulent feedback have shown particular promise in rectifying the observed divergences in ocean circulation sensitivity. The associated results have led to the proposed adoption of such schemes in the next generation of European and North American OGCMs (NEMO and MOM6), paving the way for further refinement and research. The relevant body of work highlights a paradigm shift, with an increasing focus on understanding and modeling eddy energetics, to be tackled through a combination of theory, numerical and observation based research in physical oceanography. Motivated by the above, the present proposal centers around using mathematically well-established inverse methods to infer and constrain uncertain parameters relating to the physical process of eddy energy dissipation, highlighted recently as a critical process with significant consequences for ocean climatology. The inference problem will use data from state-of-the-art OGCM as well as observations and provide leading order constraints on eddy energy dissipation, which future studies into eddy energetics will be based on. Sensitivities of the modeled circulation to eddy energy dissipation and its consequences for climate projections will be examined in IPCC-class OGCMs, to demonstrate the efficacy of the research product as well as the methodology, paving the way for future research in oceanography using analogous approaches. 海洋在地球氣候演變中起著核心作用，它的海流運輸大量熱量，碳和化學物質。現在可以使用來研究和建模海洋環流的主要工具是海洋總環流模型(OGCM)，即以數值模式展示海洋物理和生物地球化學的過程。OGCM有能力表達一個環流 "正確" 地反應大氣條件的變化，這是至關重要，尤其是在氣候的投射推演上。 但是，越來越多研究發現過去和現在的聯合國政府間氣候變化委員會 (IPCC) 的報告使用的大量應用OGCMs去展示大氣變化的狀况,是與部分從基本過程和模型研究中獲得的期望有分別。這種分歧是特別令人關注，因為這對國際努力協調的氣候預測的不確定性增加了懷疑。 上述的一個主要異議是來自對 OGCMs有關中尺度湍流的屬性和它對意義上的反饋循環。最近利用渦流能量訊息以知悉湍流回饋的强度和分怖，這說出正特別在意糾正對海洋環流敏感性的分歧。相關的結果導致了在下一代的歐洲和北美OGCMs (NEMO和MOM6)採用利用渦流能量訊息的方案，為進一步完善和研究鋪平了道路。相關工作的重點思考改變，越來越多聚焦渦流能量的認知和模型建立，要通過結合理論，數值和基於觀測的物理海洋學研究加以解決。 由於以上原因，本提案主要圍繞使用完備的數學逆方法來推斷和約束不確定參數與渦流能量耗散的物理過程, 從而突顯最近對海洋氣候學造成重大關鍵過程的影響。研究推論將使用最先進的OGCM數據作為觀察，並提供渦流能量耗散的精确約束，這將是未來對渦流能量學研究的基礎。模擬環流對渦流能量耗散的敏感性，及其 IPCC級OGCMs將能檢測研究氣候變化的结果。從而驗證研究產品中的方法學應用和效能，為使用類似方法研究海洋學鋪平了道路。

26300020.label: Realisation of objectives
26300020.value: All except the second objective can be regarded as 100% completed. During the research it was decided that the second objective using ECCO and MITgcm, while of interest, leads somewhat to a dead-end where extensions are not entirely trivial, or requires rather quite a large amount of work certainly when compared to forward calculations based on the third objective. It was deemed better use of time and resources to perform inference using using observational data, developing "regional state estimates" (the present work utilises a the global state estimate ECCO), and establish further demonstrations and developments relating to the GEOMETRIC code, for its possible use with the next round of the IPCC reports (in this case via the French partners at IPSL, through collaborators at LOCEAN at based at Sorbonne University). In total, four articles in leading internationally recognised journals resulted from the work from this grant, with one mis-attributed to another grant (see later), and possible follow on publications that will be pursued by the PI beyond the grant period. As non-publication based outputs, the GEOMETRIC code is now part of the code base in MITgcm, a popular ocean general circulation model favoured by the academic community, as well as the NEMO and MOM6 models, respectively the underlying ocean general circulation code for some of the European and North American IPCC-class models. Such outputs allow for impact generation via related algorithms being used in models that participate in the next CMIP exercises and IPCC reports; see other research outputs for some extra details. One piece of work that had a mis-attribution to another RGC grant (should really be for this grant; https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2023MS003886) is the development of the relevant code for eddy-permitting resolutions. This recent piece of work has already been taken up by the NEMO and MOM6 code developers, and is currently under further development, and forming the basis of a future RGC grant in relation to development of ocean models for use with the next generation of Earth System Models. The part that is unfinished in the second objective will be picked up by the PI together with Patrick Heimbach (UT Austin) and Martin Losch (AWI Bremerhaven), which was discussed recently when the GEOMETRIC code was merged into the MITgcm code base. The approach will likely use the more up-to-date software Tapenade, which is open-source and free to use (unlike the requested TAF license), so will not require extra financial resources other than PI time to perform. Success with objective four on establishing inverse methods and its use in oceanography in Hong Kong can be measured through one funded RGC grant (16304021), one Royal Society travel grant (KTPR1231008), participation in a recently funded CRF proposal (C5013-23GF, lead by PolyU), and a HKPFS student (PE22-72533) that will perform research using related experiences and inverse methodologies established through the present grant.
