26307720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26307720.value: 近海與開放海域之間的生物地球化學及物理性質的交換廣泛影響著海洋生態及氣候系統：深海營養鹽的輸入可顯著提高大陸架海域的生物生產力；面向格陵蘭島和南極洲的海洋熱通量可有效融化當地冰川，進而導致全球海平面上升；河源物質，如污染物等，最終可流經大陸架區域並散佈至全球海域。在過去的十年中，越來越多的文獻表明，海洋中尺度渦，即水平尺度為10-100 km的“海的風暴”，可有效驅動近海與開放海域之間的交換過程。然而，目前尚沒有一套理論工具能夠系統的預報該過程的分佈及強度。此外，因計算速度所限，即便最新的全球生物地球化學及海洋氣候預報模式也無法解析大陸邊緣區域的中尺度過程。該限制在可預見的未來將持續存在，而針對渦流所驅動的近海與開放海域交換過程的參數化方案尚未得到開發。 通過該項目，我們將採用一套過程導向的渦旋解析模式，配備無源示踪劑以追踪流體運動，以量化近海與開放海域之間的交換過程。我們將評估不同海洋動力過程在該交換過程中的相對重要性、以及中尺度渦所起的作用。為了使我們的結果具有普遍適用性，所採用模式將包含多數真實大陸邊緣區域所具備的環境條件。我們從初步實驗中推測，等密混合，即中尺度渦流所驅動的水平絕熱混合，在近海和開放海區之間的交換過程中起著關鍵作用，因此其效應必須在全球海洋預報模式中得到準確實現。根據先前對海洋環流的研究和初步結果，我們將首次為跨大陸邊緣的渦流交換過程建立參數化方案。該方案的建立將基於三個假設：（i）較強的沿岸環流可有效抑制渦流驅動的跨岸交換；（ii）在大陸邊緣區域，渦流所驅動的交換將受到地形陡峭程度的限制；（ iii）應用於開闊海域的“臨界層理論”，可以通過合併地形效應使其適用於大陸邊緣區域。我們將依據渦解析模式的結果，對該參數化方案進行驗證。該研究課題對關注區域過程的近岸海洋學家和致力於精確數值預報的氣候學家均有著重要意義。

26307720.label: Realisation of objectives
26307720.value: The project started formally on 01 Jan 2021 and has been completed with abundant research outputs. In what follows, the PI summarizes all details of research objective realizations and research outputs of the completed project. Objective 1: Following the original research plan, we successfully constructed a suite of simulations including both passive tracers and continental margins based on existing numerical frameworks built by the PI. The expanded simulations are characterized by a broad range of environmental parameters, including varied surface wind strengths, topographic steepness and shapes, and ocean stratification. These simulations were constructed using both the MIT general circulation model (MITgcm), as stated originally in the proposal, and the version 1.0 of Meridionally-Averaged Model of Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems (MAMEBUSv1.0), which was a computationally efficient, physical-biogeochemical-embedded model developed recently by University of California, Los Angeles. Employing two different models allowed us to cleanly investigate and parameterize the model-independent process of interest (eddy stirring), with a vision of applying our research outcomes to address not only physical but also biogeochemical research themes in future studies. In line with our model diagnostics, we analyzed several high-resolution ocean reanalysis datasets to verify that oceanic advective processes were relatively insensitive to the changing forcing over 1998--2017 across realistic continental margins with upwelling flows (Liao et al., 2022), which motivated us to focus initially on the variations of cross-shore eddy stirring under varied upwelling-favorable forcing. Using our numerical simulations, we adopted several approaches to seeding passive tracers and quantifying cross-shore tracer fluxes (Xie et al., 2023a). For diagnosing tracer fluxes, we set up an ensemble of eddy-resolving simulations, each of which was prescribed with multiple passive tracers for extracting the advective and isopycnal mixing components of eddy transport tensor. For parameterizing tracer exchanges due to eddy stirring, we considered two scenarios: (i) tracers occupying the entire water column of the continental slope region and evolving freely thereafter, corresponding to an initial value problem, and (ii) tracers sourced from the continental shelf (open-ocean) region and received by the open-ocean (continental shelf) region, corresponding to a forced-dissipative problem. Objective 2: The multiple-tracer simulations following the completion of Objective 1 enabled us to diagnose tracer fluxes across continental margins and to evaluate the role of eddy stirring in cross-shore exchanges, which constituted the Objective 2 of the proposal. Upon comparing the diagnosed total tracer fluxes and those derived from the eddy transport tensor component-wise, we found that it is the eddy stirring that dominates the exchanges of tracers across continental margins. Our conclusion was further verified by our finding that the cross-shore tracer fluxes calculated via the diffusive part of the eddy transport tensor alone almost reproduced the diagnosed net cross-shore tracer fluxes in our multiple-tracer simulations (Xie et al., 2023a). It also echoed with the diagnosed flows of global upwelling systems in ocean reanalysis datasets showing no apparent trend in the upwelling strength; these flows directly related to the net advective transport of cross-shore tracers in major Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems under intensified winds (Liao et al., 2022). These findings implied that eddy stirring is crucial to coast-ocean exchanges in different climate conditions. The dominant effects of eddy stirring were further investigated using a batch of reduced-order barotropic, inviscid QG "spin-down" simulations with rough topography, in which the barotropic vorticity served as the sole tracer fluxed passively but behaving dynamically (He and Wang, 2024). These simulations allowed us to enrich the seafloor configurations by including a full spectrum of topographic features and to focus solely on eddy stirring over such topography by excluding eddy restratification processes. In these simulations, we found that the strengths and effects of eddy stirring to depend sensitively on both the energy and the initial enstrophy of the flow, which calls for the implementation of scale-awareness in future eddy parameterization efforts. Objective 3: Leveraging the research outcomes of Objective 2, we calculated the cross-shore isopycnal eddy tracer diffusivity in our primitive equation models. We then constructed a theoretical framework for quantifying the spatial variability of eddy diffusivity by hypothesizing that (i) strengthened along-shore currents suppress cross-shore eddy tracer fluxes and that (ii) mesoscale turbulence becomes anisotropic over a sloping seafloor due to the the strong topographic potential vorticity gradient, which further weakens the cross-shore eddy diffusivity compared to the case of a flat-bottomed ocean. We then successfully validated our framework for cross-shore eddy diffusivity diagnostically using our primitive equation models. To convert the framework of cross-shore eddy diffusivity into a parameterization and examine its predictive skill, we implemented a set of increasingly sophisticated parameterization schemes of isopycnal eddy diffusivity in the MAMEBUS model code. To disentangle eddy stirring from other oceanic processes (i.e., mean and eddy advection), we leveraged the residual-mean framework embedded in MAMEBUS and prescribed the residual (i.e., net advective) flow based on our high-resolution MITgcm model outputs. In parallel, to stay aligned with the frontiers of eddy parameterization efforts, we implemented two machine learning-based parameterizations for cross-shore eddy diffusivity in MAMEBUS. We conducted a comprehensive set of prognostic numerical experiments and verified that our proposed parameterization outperforms existing ones across continental margins occupied by upwelling flow systems and that machine learning approaches can augment physics-based schemes in terms of constraining uncertain physical parameters (Xie et al., 2023a). With the vision of applying our proposed parameterization in actual climate model predictions, we simultaneously parameterized the eddy advection, a process that governs several mean flow properties controlling the strengths of eddy stirring but was circumvented by our MAMEBUS residual-mean simulations. Specifically, we implemented a suite of parameterizations for eddy advection in MITgcm, with the goal of rectifying the background flow in non-eddying simulations for supporting the additional, parameterized tracer exchanges. Our model experiments yielded a comprehensive recipe for parameterizing eddy advection (Xie et al., 2023b). By employing the MAMEBUS and MITgcm codes, we had focused initially on upwelling flow systems, which, contrasted to downwelling flow systems, naturally open up the along-isopycnal exchange pathways between shelf and open-ocean environments. In a recent investigation, we leveraged a suite of baroclinic QG simulations (the QG setup, unlike primitive equation models, would ensure to open up the exchange pathways between shallow and deep regions over topography) to further identify the qualitative similarities and the quantitative distinctions of eddy stirring effects between upwelling and downwelling flow cases, with additionally suggested approaches to accurately parameterizing eddy stirring across bottom slopes with downwelling flows. For the first time, we theorized the effects of bottom slope, depending on the relative topographic direction to those of tilted isopycnals, in adjusting the responses of nonlinear eddy energetics, which in turn control the strengths and spatial variability of cross-shore eddy stirring (Deng and Wang, 2024). Lastly, we extended the scope of the original research plan by "chasing after" the ultimate fate of a crucial oceanic tracer (i.e., heat), sourced from continental shelf and slope flows in high-latitude regions, within the open-ocean environment based on observational data in the Arctic Ocean. We found that eddies in the Arctic ocean, by stimulating smaller-scale processes (double-diffusive-convection staircase mergers), would further deliver the heat stored within the ocean interior across isopycnals toward the sea surface (Chai et al., 2024).

26307720.label: Major findings and research outcome
26307720.value: 1. We quantified the impacts of a sloping seafloor on the anisotropy of mesoscale turbulence over continental margins and incorporated such impacts into parameterizations for mesoscale eddy stirring. 2. We provided the community's first suite of prognostic numerical experiments for assessing the efficacy of existing parameterization schemes of mesoscale eddy stirring across continental margins and verified that our proposed framework outperforms other physics-based parameterization schemes. 3. We further provided the community's first suite of prognostic experiments for parameterized eddy advection across continental margins, in parallel to and numerically supporting those for parameterized eddy stirring. 4. We systematically investigated and quantified the physical transitions of mesoscale turbulence in driving interior stirring with varied initial enstrophy above rough topography. 5. We theorized fully nonlinear mesoscale energetic responses over continental margins occupied by upwelling versus downwelling flow systems. 6. We "chased after" and quantified the fate of heat sourced from high-latitude boundary currents into the Arctic Ocean away from continental margins.

26307720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26307720.value: The current project laid solid theoretical and numerical foundations for implementing the research outputs in global ocean models and assessing the impacts of cross-shore eddy stirring on realistic ocean physical and biogeochemical responses.

26307720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26307720.value: This project addresses the quantification and prediction of exchanges between shallow coastal and deep open-ocean environments, driven by ubiquitous mesoscale ocean currents. Throughout this project, we established a new theoretical framework for interpreting and predicting such exchanges, and successfully implemented this framework as a numerical tool into ocean models. This project will thus contribute to improving the fidelity of predictive ocean climate models, in which large-scale topography can be well represented but mesoscale ocean currents are unresolved.

26309420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26309420.value: 2015年，香港遭受嚴重的水危機，當時發現向住宅提供的水含有過量的鉛，Pb2+和鎘，Cd2+。其首先在啟晴邨被發現，後來在其他許多邨發現。這是壹種嚴重的污染，因為重金屬離子是人類致癌物，會對腎臟，骨骼和呼吸系統的健康產生嚴重影響。通常，吸附方法用於凈化水。活性炭或沸石被廣泛使用，因為它們便宜，儘管它們的低孔隙率限制了動力學（即可以多快的除去吸附物）和吸收（即可以除去多少被吸附物）。另壹類高度多孔的合成材料（例如有機框架）的性能更好地達到了香港飲用水標準（HKDWS，Cd2+和Pb2+分別<3和<10 ppb）。然而，它們在水性環境中的穩定性差，麻煩且昂貴的化學反應以及不方便的回收方法阻礙了它們的商業應用。上述情況表明，尚無法獲得滿足五個標準（高吸收，快速動力學，長期穩定性，可回收性和選擇性）的吸附劑。 最近，聚光燈轉向了壹種電化學方法，該方法能夠可逆地捕獲和釋放污染物，同時還滿足以上五個標準。該方法使用電化學活性材料作為吸附劑，即在其天然狀態下，吸附劑捕獲污染物，但是當其表面化學勢改變以排斥陽離子時，其釋放污染物。在先前的研究中，我們在合成包含許多重金屬螯合基團的高度多孔和穩定的網絡方面積累了專業知識。我們還開發了壹種導電聚合物網絡，可以捕獲或釋放汞Hg2+，以響應其電化學勢的變化。遺憾地是，這方面的研究很少，因此迫切需要不僅開發滿足實際純化目標的技術，而且研究可逆吸附現象背後的科學原理。在這個擬議的項目中，我們的主要目標是生產經濟，能夠快速，可靠和可逆地捕獲和釋放大量Cd2+和Pb2+的吸附劑，以滿足HKDWS。該項目的成功成果將是不僅為大灣區而且為中國乃至世界其他地區的其他大都市建立後續的研究和凈化污染水的設計準則。

26309420.label: Realisation of objectives
26309420.value: (Please refer to the "Poly(norbornene-diphenothiazine) for Electrochemical Capture and Release of Chromium and Arsenic Oxyanions from Water" under review.) Our polymer design is slightly different from what we proposed. However, the new structure is more suitable for reversible, renewable systems, thus a proper modification has been made. With the new design and scope, we fully achieved the three objectives and here below we demonstrate the scope of the work. We made phenothiazine-functionalized polynorbornenes (poly(norbornene-diphenothiazine); PNP2) to electrochemically remove heavy metal oxyanions. The PNP2 had two N-methylphenothiazines on a repeating unit, yielding an enhanced adsorption capacity. Those two sulfur-containing phenothiazines per repeating unit enabled the PNP2 to undergo two distinct redox processes, resulting in the formation of a divalent polymer with two positive charges. This high density enabled a large formula-weight-based theoretical redox density, 14.2%, and promoted rapid electron self-exchange reactions within the polymer layer. The prepared PNP2 showed a high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 384.4 m2 g−1. Using this PNP2, we fabricated electrochemically modulated heavy metal ion remover. The base electrodes were prepared by cutting stainless steel wire cloth (325 × 325 mesh, wire diameter: 0.0035 cm) into 1 cm × 2 cm. We prepared three samples containing different ratios of PNP2 – 80, 67, and 40 wt.% from 80 mg PNP2 and 20 mg CNT, 40 mg PNP2 and 20 mg CNT, and 20 mg PNP2 and 30 mg CNT, respectively. Each solution was prepared by dissolving the respective amounts in 5 mL of chloroform. The solution was sonicated for 30 min in an ice bath. For active material coating, the base electrodes were dip-coated into the solution, with 10 sec of contact time for each dip, and left to dry at room temperature for 60 sec between each dip. Five dippings led to the final loading of approximately 2 mg PNP2 per electrode for all three samples. For all the experiments, the electrochemical active area immersed in electrolyte was 1 cm × 1 cm. Cyclopentane backbone from ROMP of norbornene exhibits hydrophilicity due to the nature of C–H bonds. Additionally, the rigid cyclopentane-based polymers hinder the formation of hydrogen bonding networks with water molecules, owing to the close packing arrangement. With such a polymer design, PNP2-CNT effectively prevents the redox polymers from being physically dissipated when used in aqueous electrolyte solutions. Such chemical nature yielded excellent stability in both 10 M NaOH and 10 M HCl aqueous solutions. After the 10 days of acid/base treatments, the PNP2-CNT electrode’s Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra remained the same as the original one, and the weight loss was less than 1%. However, polyethylene-based PVP, having a more flexible backbone and less number of phenothiazine pendants, had more favorable interactions with the polar water molecules, thus became exfoliated from the substrate during the adsorption/desorption cycles, thereby reducing its electrochemical activity. To show the economic advantages of this electrochemically modulated adsorption process, we evaluated energy integration and consumption of the redox-active PNP2-CNT systems. We significantly improved energy efficiency by using the spontaneous adsorption and conversion processes with redox-active materials. Specifically, the PNP2-CNT//Pt only consumed 0.23 and 0.19 kWh mol–1 for the total separation, conversion, and regeneration process of Cr(VI) and As(III), respectively. For both cases, the adsorption happened with minimal energy of only 1.1 and 9.5% of the total energy for Cr(VI) and As(III), respectively. This redox-mediated removal of toxic ions is particularly useful for As(III) as their conversion into less toxic As(V) happened with adsorption, and it did not require additional energy input. When comparing the energy consumption of the adsorption process using different electrode materials, the PNP2-CNT electrode exhibited significantly lower energy consumption than the PVP-CNT and CNT electrodes. Specifically, the PNP2-CNT electrode only consumed 1.14 and 0.17% of the PVP-CNT and the CNT electrodes for adsorption. The low energy consumption of the PNP2-CNT electrode can be attributed to three reasons. First, the PNP2-CNT electrode exhibited higher selectivity in capturing the target species, allowing for more efficient adsorption, and reducing energy waste. Second, the high concentration of two phenothiazine units per repeating unit in the polymer facilitated a rapid electron self-exchange reaction within the polymer layer, resulting in a fast electron transfer rate and more efficient utilization of electrical energy during the adsorption process. Third, the PNP2-CNT electrode, with its larger specific surface area, offered an increased number of adsorption sites, facilitating enhanced contact between the target species and the electrode. This pseudocapacitance effect allowed for additional charge storage at the electrode-electrolyte interface, enabling efficient charge storage and release. Thus, by utilizing PNP2-CNT as the working electrode, electrons can be effectively transferred through the redox electrochemistry of PNP2. During desorption/discharging, these obtained electrons can serve as both an electron acceptor for the regeneration of PNP2-CNT and actively participate in the coupled conversion of Cr(VI) to Cr(III). The adsorption/charging process releases electrons from the PNP2-CNT electrode, and the electrons are used for the adsorption of As(III) and simultaneously facilitate the conversion of As(III) to As(V). Finally, we evaluated the performance of the PNP2-CNT electrode system using real secondary effluent wastewater collected from the Sha Tin Sewage Treatment Works in Hong Kong, which was spiked with approximately 100 ppb Cr(VI) and As(III). It was observed that within 2 hours of electrosorption, a removal efficiency of over 90% was achieved, meeting the 10 ppb guideline for As and 50 ppb for Cr set by the World Health Organization . Furthermore, by using 10 mM NaCl as the electrolyte, the system achieved notable removal efficiencies with rates of 96.2% for Cr(VI) and 94.1% for As(III).

26309420.label: Major findings and research outcome
26309420.value: This study developed a composite electrode material, PNP2-CNT electrode, combining a redox-active/Faradaic polymer, PNP2, with high specific surface area non-faradaic CNTs. This pseudocapacitance platform incorporates the advantages of PNP2 polymer, which enables rapid electron transfer, selective adsorption, and exceptional stability in aqueous systems, along with the large specific surface area of CNTs that facilitates efficient charge storage and release. Thus, this PNP2-CNT electrode achieved fast adsorption rates, 0.03 g mg−1 min−1 for As(III) and 0.008 g mg−1 min−1 for Cr(VI), surpassing the adsorption rates of other reported materials by 3 to 200 times, while demonstrating high adsorption capacity, 666.3 mg g−1 for Cr(VI) and 612.4 for As(III). Additionally, this electrode achieved nearly 100% conversion of As(III) to its lower toxic state As(V) during adsorption, and facilitated the reduction of Cr(VI) to its less toxic Cr(III) during desorption. Furthermore, the energy consumption of this system was significantly lower, only 0.17% of traditional conductive CNT materials. Lastly, when applied to real wastewater, it demonstrated outstanding performance in effectively removing As(III) and Cr(VI) contaminants. Therefore, combining the redox-active/Faradaic polymer and the high specific surface area non-faradaic CNTs presents a promising platform for efficient adsorption and remediation of As and Cr oxyanions. This research opens avenues for developing advanced electrode materials with low energy consumption and high adsorption performance for treating heavy metal-contaminated water systems.

26309420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26309420.value: The chemical interaction between heteroatom-containing polymers and target species strongly depends on their chemical potential. In this work, we used sulfur-containing phenothiazine to remove Cr(VI) and As(III). However, instead of phenothiazine, simpler aromatic rings, such as thiane, thiazole, thiophene, etc., have a high potential to selectively interact with other heavy metal ions. Our electrode samples had a high BET surface of over 384.4 m2 g−1. We can potentially increase the surface area by making more porous materials to positively correlate the kinetics and update performance with highly porous materials. This surface engineering is a promising next direction. Last but not least, we can commercialize our recyclable, renewable materials. Our system to remove heavy metal ions strongly depends on environmental potential of the system. Releasing the adsorbed ones also requires counter potential. This facile mechanism can be applied to the real industry. We filed patent applications on our core technology. Thus, we will actively communicate with industry partners to realize this concept.

26309420.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26309420.value: Drinking water contamination by heavy metals, particularly chromium and arsenic oxyanions, is a severe challenge threatening humanity’s sustainable development. Electrochemically-mediated water purification is gaining attention due to its high uptake, rapid kinetics, modularity, and facile regeneration. Here, we designed a composite electrode by combining a redox-active/Faradaic polymer, poly(norbornene-diphenothiazine) (PNP2), with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) – PNP2-CNT. The PNP2-CNT demonstrated exceptional pseudocapacitance behavior, resulting in significantly accelerated adsorption rates for dichromate (Cr(VI)) and arsenite (As(III)), surpassing reported materials by a margin of 3 to 200 times, while demonstrating a high adsorption capacity. Furthermore, it effectively converted As(III) to the less toxic arsenate (As(V)) during adsorption and Cr(VI) to the less toxic chromium (Cr(III)) during desorption. This PNP2-CNT system also showed significantly lower energy consumption, only 0.17% of the CNT control system. This study demonstrated for the first time the use of PNP2 redox-active polymers in the separation and conversion process, meeting the six criteria of high uptake, rapid kinetics, selectivity, stability, recyclability, and energy efficiency. This achievement expands the scope of advanced materials that address environmental concerns and make an impact by generating energy- and cost-effective water purification.

26309620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26309620.value: Interfacial mechanics is an essential subject in understanding mechanical properties of a broad class of soft interfaces, including emulsions, foams, surfactant and protein laden-interfaces, and bio-membranes. Similar to bulk mechanics, interfacial mechanics focuses on surface stress-strain relationship to understand the underlying dynamics of microstructures on surface. Besides interfacial materials, concepts in interfacial mechanics can be theoretically extended to solid materials. However, conventional methods face tremendous difficulties in directly measuring surface stresses of solids due to their dominating bulk effects. For example, to study capillary effects for normal solids with modulus around 10 GPa, the effective length scale, often called as elastocapillary length, needs to be smaller than 1 nm, which is not feasible for most experimental approaches. To address this issue, we use soft gels as “model systems” to investigate interfacial mechanics of solids. Since their modulus is as low as KPa, the elastocapillary length becomes as large as 10 μm. Our experimental approach relies on a newly developed interference microscope, which will image surface deformation from the interference patterns. With the help of interferometry, we can reconstruct surface deformation in 3D without scanning through the vertical axis. We expect to measure surface strain with a recording speed up to 10^4 frames per second. This feature allows us to investigate fast surface dynamics that is difficult to measure with conventional interfacial rheometers. The key physical parameter on which we will focus is the surface stress of solids. While liquid surface tension has been well studied in various scenarios, our understanding of solid surface stress is much less developed. Our recent work on static wetting shows that solid surface stress is fundamentally different from liquid surface tension. Instead of being a constant material parameter, solid surface stress has been shown to greatly depend on surface strain. We plan to perform both relaxation and vibrational mechanical measurements on the surface of soft gels and to quantify how surface stress depends on strain and strain-rate. The results will help us to measure the surface elasticity and surface viscosity of soft solids. By determining these parameters, we can quantitatively obtain complete descriptions for their interfacial mechanics. The proposed projects will provide a new experimental approach to investigate surface mechanics of solids. Particularly, the potential results from the study are expected to reveal new features at the interfaces of soft gels, and provide us an opportunity to design the engineering materials with highly adjustable interfacial properties. 表面力學是理解多種軟物質介面力學性質（包括乳濁液，泡沫，表面活性劑及蛋白質介面，生物膜）的一個重要課題。與材料體力學性質研究類似，表面力學研究專注於通過表面應力-應變關係來理解表面微結構的動力學。表面力學的概念，不僅侷限於介面材料，同時在理論上也能推廣到固體材料。然而，由於固體有非常強的體積效應，傳統的實驗方法難以直接測量固體表面應力。 例如，對於模量約為10GPa的常見固體，研究固體表面張力的有效長度將小於1納米。這顯然對於大多數的實驗測量手段是不可行的。 為了解決這個問題，我利用軟膠作為“模型系統”來研究固體表面張力。由於軟膠的模量大約為KPa的量級，其彈性張力尺寸約為10微米。我們的實驗方法將依賴於設計一個新型的干涉顯微鏡，其用來觀測表面形變引起的干涉條紋。通過干涉學方法，我可以在不通過縱向掃描的基礎上而建立表面的三維形變圖。我們預計將能夠在10^4 幀每秒的速率下測量表面應變。這一特點能幫助我們研究傳統的介面流變儀所不能測量的表面動力學。 我們最為關注的物理參數將是固體的表面應力。儘管液體表面張力在不同的問題中被詳細地研究了，我們對固體表面應力的理解卻非常缺乏。 我們最近的工作證明液體表面張力和固體表面應力在本質上是不同的。固體表面張力並非常數，且隨表面應變的變化而變化。在此，我們計劃通過測量軟膠表面的弛豫和振動力學，定量地研究表面應力是如何隨表面應變和表面應變速率改變的。這些結果能幫助我們測量固體表面彈性係數和表面黏滯阻力。通過這些參數的確定，我們可以定量而完整地描述固體表面力學性質。 該項目將會提供一個全新的實驗方法來研究固體表面力學。其潛在的研究結果將揭示軟膠表面的新特徵，並且提供了用於設計表面性質可調的工程材料的可能。

26309620.label: Realisation of objectives
26309620.value: To fulfill the three research objectives, we systematically studied the interfacial mechanics of soft polymeric gels by combining high-resolution optical imaging with contact mechanical characterizations. Specifically, the conducted research can be categorized into three subprojects: (1) designing an interference microscope, (2) investigating the impact of crosslinking density on surface mechanics, and (3) characterizing the contact dynamics at soft interfaces. Below, we outline the key research activities conducted for each subproject. (1) In the first subproject, we successfully constructed an interference microscope to study de-wetting relaxation at soft surfaces. Due to the high compliance of soft substrates, de-wetting at soft interfaces is a multi-scale process. Initially, during the contact line retraction, micron-sized contact ridges relax in a viscoelastic manner within a second. Furthermore, over a longer period, surface relaxation is controlled by poroelastic diffusion on a nanometer scale. This poses a challenge for conventional imaging methods (e.g., confocal microscopy and X-ray imaging) in studying de-wetting dynamics across a wide range of spatial-temporal scales. The interference microscope was designed based on a Linnik-type interferometer where the reflected light from a sample surface interferes with a reference beam. To accurately measure the surface deformations on a micrometer scale, we utilized a red LED light source with a coherence length of about 20 μm, resulting in a z-resolution of 20 nm. As three-dimensional (3D) interference imaging does not require vertical scanning, this imaging system excels in capturing rapid surface dynamics on a small length scale. By analyzing the relaxation of contact ridges at various length and time scales, we demonstrated that viscoelasticity and poroelasticity play key roles in different time domains. Our experimental findings illustrate how the interplay between these two mechanisms governs the interfacial dynamics of soft solids. The research was published in Physical Review Letter (2020). (2) In the second subproject, we conducted a systematic study on the surface stress and surface energy of soft polymeric gels with different crosslinking densities (k). It is well known that the surface stress and surface energy are identical for liquids, but different for crystalline solids. However, the relationship between the two parameters has remained unclear for amorphous solids, such as soft elastomers and polymer glasses. We examined the wetting behaviors of both glycerol and fluorinated oil droplets on soft silicone gels with different crosslinking densities. The apparent contact angles of liquid droplets reflect the surface energy of substrates, while the geometry of local capillary ridges is determined by surface stresses. Through multi-scale optical imaging of wetting profiles, we experimentally demonstrated that the surface stress of soft gels greatly depends on the crosslinking density while the surface energy remains constant. In particular, the difference between surface stress and surface energy of soft gels increases with the crosslinking density (k). Close to the percolation transition point of the crosslinked network (k = k0), the surface stress and surface energy of soft gels become nearly equal. At this critical point k0, the bulk rheology displays gel-like viscoelasticity while the surface properties remain liquid-like. To demonstrate this unique material feature, we showed that a critically crosslinked soft gel can spontaneously heal from fractures due to solid capillarity. This research was published in Soft Matter (2022) and featured on the back cover. Based on the classical Shuttleworth effect, we further predicted that the surface energy of soft gels could change quantitatively with substantial variations in crosslinking density. To test this hypothesis, we fabricated a soft gel surface with a bulk gradient in crosslinking density. When a liquid droplet was deposited on the substrate, it spontaneously moved along the surface gradient, confirming a spatial variation in the surface energy. The manuscript (arXiv:2407.10480) has been invited for submission to the “Emerging Investigator” series in Soft Matter and is currently under review. (3) In the third subproject, we investigated the growth dynamics of capillary ridges under surface contacts induced by the wetting of liquid droplets. Once a liquid droplet is deposited at a soft interface, the interaction between Laplace pressure and bulk elastic stresses leads to a slow growth of capillary ridges. Characterizing this process is essential for comprehending the interfacial rheology of soft solids. Experimentally, we performed in-situ imaging of local wetting profiles and observed the formation of phase separation at contact points. The local geometry of the phase separation region clearly indicates the phase boundary between crosslinked networks and uncrosslinked free chains. However, modeling such a non-equilibrium process poses challenges for traditional mechanical and statistical methods. To tackle this, we developed a phenomenological model based on Onsager’s principle. By comparing the experimental results with the model prediction, we elucidated how the diffusion of uncrosslinked polymers governs the dissipative dynamics at soft interfaces. The small diffusivities of these free chains are pertinent to their viscoelastic rheology. This work has been accepted by Physical Review Research (2024). (4) In addition to the subprojects mentioned above, our developed imaging method has significantly contributed to our research on the surface mechanics of soft materials. For example, we explored how swelling-induced surface instabilities affect the adhesion energy of the soft substrates. By varying the sample thickness from micrometer to millimeter scales, we adjusted the dimensions of the instability patterns by three orders of magnitude. We show that these patterns effectively enhance the adhesion energy of substrates. Using the interference microscope, we imaged the contact area in situ when the soft surfaces were deformed under contact. The results indicate that the enhanced adhesion energy is related to unstable contact lines induced by instability patterns. The work has been published in Materials (2022). Moreover, leveraging our understanding of the role of crosslinking density in soft gel mechanics, we engineered soft composites using different elastic matrices. By developing a scaling theory based on critical transitions, we uncovered the close relationship between the shear-jamming of dense suspensions and the strain-stiffening of dense composites. This work has been published in Nature Communications (2024).

26309620.label: Major findings and research outcome
26309620.value: First, our investigations into soft wetting unveiled the crucial role of crosslinking density in determining the surface properties of soft solids. Traditionally, it was assumed that the surface stress and surface energy of soft polymeric gels were similar due to the structural resemblance between disordered polymer networks and liquid molecules. However, due to the challenges in mesoscale measurements of interfacial mechanics, the underlying relationship between the surface stress and surface energy of soft gels has remained largely unknown. In this project, using newly developed imaging methods, we meticulously characterized the multi-scale contact profiles on soft substrates with various crosslinking densities. Our findings highlight a significant difference between the surface stress and surface energy of soft gels, which increases with the level of crosslinking of the networks. As a result, the surface properties of soft gels display characteristics of both solids and liquids. Second, we elucidated how the interplay between viscoelasticity and poroelasticity governs the relaxation dynamics at soft interfaces. Given that both dissipations are associated with the frictional interactions between the crosslinked networks and uncrosslinked free chains, distinguishing the influence of the two relaxation mechanisms experimentally is challenging. Using the newly designed interference microscope, we were able to precisely capture the relaxation process across a broad range of spatiotemporal scales. Our experimental findings clearly demonstrate how viscoelasticity and poroelasticity dictate the dynamic responses at different timescales. To the best knowledge, we provided the first experimental signatures of these two dissipative regimes. Third, we revealed the key roles played by migrating free chains in controlling the interfacial rheology of soft polymeric solids. The presence of the free chains not only overrides the stress singularity at contact points but also governs the local relaxations. The free chains gradually accumulate at contact points driven by a phase-separation process. The dynamics are characterized by an effective diffusivity, which is determined by the frictional interactions between free chains and polymer networks.

26309620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26309620.value: Our investigations offer valuable insights for future research in two main areas. First, we expect that the experimental findings regarding the influence of crosslinking density pave the way for a new approach to designing soft interfaces with intelligent functions. For instance, the realization of a soft substrate featuring a continuous gradient in crosslinking density holds great promise. We anticipate that intricate control over droplet motion can be possibly achieved on such substrates, which will potentially benefit emerging engineering fields, such as microfluidics and drug delivery. Second, our studies on the mechanics of soft interfaces are biologically relevant. In particular, poroelastic diffusion, a prevalent phenomenon in bio-membranes, plays essential roles in various physiological processes. Therefore, studying relaxation dynamics at soft interfaces is vital for understanding the evolution and morphogenesis of bio-membranes. In our future studies, we aim to explore the underlying connection between soft polymeric surfaces and active biological materials.

26309620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26309620.value: The mechanical properties of soft interfaces play important roles in many engineering applications, such as flexible electronics, soft robots, and biomimetic tissues. Due to the complex and nonlinear nature of compliant interfaces, directly charactezing their mechanical responses has remained experimentally challenging. In this project, we developed a novel interference microscope capable of precisely capturing the interfacial dynamics of elastocapillary ridges across a broad range of spatiotemporal scales. Through systematic investigations of soft wetting behaviors, we identified the key material parameters governing the contact mechanical performance at soft interfaces. First, we observed that the crosslinking density determine the disparity between the surface stress and surface energy of soft polymeric gels. Second, we found that the migration of free chains near soft interfaces regulates the relaxation and interfacial rheology of soft surfaces. Building upon these experimental findings, we established phenomenological models that effectively describe these diverse mechanical characteristics. Our research outcomes not only shed light on the fundamental surface properties of soft materials but also offer valuable insights for engineering functional interfaces based on soft solids.

This will advance our understanding of the implications of information asymmetry, a key friction in many financial activities. To provide new empirical insights into the impact of information acquisition in IPO markets. We focus on the IPO markets to test our theoretical implications, and first show information acquisition behavior by firms and their information sets before IPOs. To inform policy-making about regulations mandating access by firms to public markets. We present the unintended consequences of some regulations, i.e., higher underpricing after firms are allowed to gather more information, which call for a careful re-investigation of the policy.

26500720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500720.value: 信息在现代经济运转中扮演着核心作用。一方面，金融市场参与者的活动越来越以信息为中心，从而使得信息采集成为他们决策过程至关重要的一环。另一方面，信息不对称是许多金融活动，比如企业融资，中主要的摩擦因素。鉴于以上两个事实，研究信息采集对于企业融资有何影响显得至关重要。 企业通常比其潜在投资者更了解其基本面。众所周知，这样的信息不对称可能带来带来企业融资的无效率。一个自然而然的问题是，如果企业可以获取更多信息从而扩大他们已有的相对于投资者的信息优势，他们会选择这样做吗？企业在融资前的信息采集活动又会带来什么样的影响？这些问题不仅具有学术价值，而且关乎政策制定。例如，为了鼓励企业在公开资本市场融资，一些国家的法规允许这些企业预先收集有关投资者估值的信息。这些政策中隐含的假设在于企业将受益于采集更多的信息。但是，这一假设本身就值得仔细研究。 我们的研究为企业信息采集及其对其融资的影响提供了新的见解。尽管采集更多信息可以增强单个公司的决策水平，但是它加剧了企业与投资者之间的信息不对称，从而可能导致更多无效率。例如，如果企业首次公开募股（IPO），其获取更多信息后抑价可能会加剧，这意味着上市企业筹资减少。这样的结果明显有悖于监管机构的上述隐含假设，从而也意味着我们需要更好地理解信息采集在公开资本市场中的作用。 我们的研究包括理论分析和实证分析。首先，我们用一个 博弈论模型来阐明企业信息采集的影响，并以此指导随后的实证检验。其次，我们将通过企业首次公开募股的数据验证该模型的结论。通过这些分析，我们旨在进一步了解信息采取在企业筹集资金中的作用。

26500720.label: Realisation of objectives
26500720.value: All three stated objectives in the proposal have been achieved 100% in our research working paper. We first briefly introduce the motivation of the paper and then discuss how each objective is achieved. The project’s general objective is to understand the impact of firms’ information acquisition on the process of capital raising. Given that the capital-raising process is inherently affected by information asymmetry between firms and prospective investors, it is important to ask if firms would acquire more information if given the opportunity (increasing their information advantage over investors) and if so, what are the consequences. One important set of changes made by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to support the public equity market is the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012 (the JOBS Act). Tightly related to our research questions, this act allows eligible emerging growth companies (EGCs) to interact with investors before filing for an IPO (so-called ‘testing the waters’). We thus conduct both theoretical and empirical analyses based on this concrete and relevant setting. The central message of our paper is that these regulatory changes have led to a decrease rather than an increase in the number of firms going public, an outcome opposite to the regulators’ stated goal. Regarding Objective 1: In Section 4 of the paper, we build a conceptual framework, focusing on the ability of firms to test the waters, to explain why the JOBS Act reduced eligible firms’ relative propensity to go public (contrary to the regulators’ stated goals) and to generate testable implications. We consider a model in which a firm seeks financing for a project. In the benchmark, the firm and its investors have the same prior about the probability of the firm being ‘good’ (higher net present value) or ‘bad’. However, after the JOBS Act, the firm tests the waters and learns more information about its type while investors remain with their prior. The effect of testing the waters is thus captured by comparing the post-JOBS-Act economy with the benchmark. We find that after the JOBS Act, the good firm signals its type through devices such as underpricing or through underwriter certification, while the bad firm opts out of the IPO process. This self-selection out of the IPO process results in lower likelihood of an average firm going public, thereby explaining the decline in the number of IPOs after 2012. This finding points out the importance of exploring the general equilibrium implications of the regulatory policy. While the regulators implicitly assume that firms will benefit from the option to gather more information (which is true for individual firms in the partial equilibrium sense), we show that the interaction between different types of firms and the response of prospective investors should be considered to gain a more holistic understanding of this policy’s reverberating influences. Regarding Objective 2: Sections 3, 5, and 6 of the paper contain our empirical analyses. We perform our analysis in a difference-in-difference setting around the introduction of the JOBS Act. The sample period is from 2001 to 2020. Our treatment group is U.S. EGCs, which are defined in the JOBS Act as firms with less than US$1 billion in revenue in the year before IPO. We adopt two different control groups. The first is U.S. non-EGCs (firms with more than US$1 billion in revenue). The second is the U.K. firms with the equivalent of less than US$1 billion in revenue in the year before IPO. In Section 3, we establish our central finding that the JOBS Act, instead of increasing IPOs, is in fact associated with the decreasing number of IPOs. The validity of the test requires us to control for the pool of underlying firms that may plausibly be willing to go public, and we do this by using three different variables of interest: listing propensity, IPO propensity, and PE exit via IPO. We find that the treated firms in the post-JOBS period have lower listing propensities and lower IPO propensities, and the PE exits of EGCs have become significantly less likely to be via IPO in the post-JOBS period. Overall, all three tests point to the fact that firms targeted by the reforms in the JOBS Act have experienced a diminished propensity to go public. In Section 5, we explore the other implications of our theoretical framework. First, it is reasonable to expect that a firm that acquires more information should make more informed individual decisions. We find that 90% of EGCs indeed exercise this information-acquisition option and they experience a lower likelihood of withdrawal. Second, in terms of the signaling device for the high quality firms to separate themselves, we find that, consistent with our model predictions, EGCs experience higher underpricing. In addition, the results for underwriter certification as the signaling device are mixed: EGCs are willing to pay their underwriters relatively more in the post-JOBS period to overcome increased information asymmetry, but they don’t seem to hire more reputable bookrunners which would bolster the certification effects. Third, we find suggestive evidence that the post-JOBS period is associated with higher firm quality, as measured by sales growth, ROA and profitability. Finally, in Section 6, we conduct more analyses to rule out the alternative reduced-disclosure explanation. Because the JOBS Act also allows small firms to provide reduced disclosure, a plausible alternative framework assumes that firms know their type and the JOBS Act allows low quality firms to better hide this from investors. This alternative framework and ours share one theoretical prediction: underpricing should increase for EGCs, but the predictions for firm quality and listing propensity are opposite. In addition to some subsample tests to try and disentangle these two theories, we also conduct a difference-in-difference setting using the small reporting company (SRC) exemption for firms with less than US$75 million in market capitalization, which allowed reduced disclosure as of 2008. Using U.S. SRCs as our treatment group and two control groups (U.K. IPO firms with less than US$75 million in market capitalization and U.S. IPO firms which are classified as EGCs but not SRCs), we show that the introduction of reduced disclosure did not materially increase underpricing or reduce IPO propensity, but the introduction of the ability to test the waters resulted in both of these outcomes (consistent with our model). Regarding Objective 3: The issue of information asymmetry and its negative impacts on the ability for trade have long been understood. In this paper, we examine how the regulatory quest to solve a very real and important problem (the decrease in the number of companies raising capital publicly) seems to have ignored this primitive issue of information asymmetry, and led to unintended consequences. Specifically, the JOBS Act of 2012, which allowed firms to test the waters before deciding to pursue an IPO, exacerbated the informational advantage that firms have over investors and was associated with a decrease in the number of firms going public (though can be welfare-enhancing). Therefore, our paper highlights the importance of analyzing regulatory policy changes from multiple perspectives; in particular, changes to the IPO process must consider responses from both firms and prospective investors.

26500720.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500720.value: The outcome of this project is a working paper titled “Too much information? Increasing firms’ information advantages in the IPO process,” coauthored with Michele Dathan from Federal Reserve Board. Now it has been submitted to one of the top three finance journals. In 2012, the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act (JOBS Act) was enacted in the U.S., allowing eligible firms to test the waters with investors before initial public offering (IPO). This setup provides a concrete, relevant setting for us to study firms’ information acquisition before capital raising, which is the focus of our project. The major findings of our project are summarized as follows. First, while the JOBS act aimed to make the public equity market more welcoming for new firms, we find that it has led to a decrease rather than an increase in the number of firms going public. This novel finding is the opposite of the regulators’ stated goal and stands in contrast to the previous studies (e.g., Dambra, Field, and Gustafson, 2015). Second, we show theoretically that the decrease in the number of IPO firms can be attributed to testing the waters, which permits firms to meet with qualified institutional buyers before the filing of any registration statement. Specifically, we build a game-theoretic model to show that by allowing firms to acquire more information, testing the waters exacerbates information asymmetry between firms and prospective investors. The highest quality firms in turn employ various signaling devices to separate themselves from low quality firms, and the exit of the latter type of firms thus contributes to the decreasing number of IPO firms. Third, we conduct empirical analysis to test other model implications and these empirical results further corroborate our testing-the-water explanation. Specifically, we predict and find that (i) the JOBS Act benefit individual eligible firms by reducing withdrawal rates and shortening book-building periods, (ii) underpricing has significantly increased and underwriter certification has somewhat increased, and (iii) the IPO firms in the post-JOBS period are of higher quality. Finally, we rule out reduced disclosure as an alternative explanation of our empirical findings.

26500720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26500720.value: In the current project, we focus on the implications of testing the waters (TTW) for firms’ IPO outcomes. More broadly, this early information exchange may affect firms’ private market outcomes as well. For instance, some firms may use TTW to collect the market demand information for their securities and shop it back to the private markets, thereby affecting the overall going-public versus staying-private trade-off. In this sense, the regulator intervention to make public equity markets more welcoming and attractive relative to private markets may achieve the opposite goal. Therefore, our project can be further developed to understand the implications of TTW, or more broadly, public firms’ regulatory environment, for private capital markets. Such investigation helps enhance our understanding of the contributing factors to the IPO decline and the development of private equity markets. To conduct this future research, we need collect information about private-capital-backed startups. We can employ diff-in-diff tests around the JOBS Act to examine its effect on the private capital markets.

26500720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500720.value: A decrease in the number of public companies in the U.S. has attracted significant concern from regulators, prompting changes to the initial public offering (IPO) process to make it more welcoming for young, high growth firms. One set of changes (the JOBS Act of 2012) was designed to reduce the costs of going public by allowing eligible firms to test the waters with investors before IPO and reducing required disclosure, both of which increase firms’ information advantage over prospective investors. We model firm behavior in response to this increased information advantage and using a difference-in-difference setting, we show that while these changes have had benefits for some firms, they have led to a decrease rather than an increase in the number of firms going public, which is opposite to the regulators’ stated goals. Our paper thus provides a framework and evidence that can inform policy makers interested in improving the design of the capital raising process: regulators both in the U.S. and globally should expand their focus from de-risking and de-burdening the IPO process for entrepreneurs and consider the impacts of information asymmetry on both firms and potential investors.

26502320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502320.value: Most studies on gender pay gaps find a widespread female penalty (women earning lower pay than men on average), although a few studies find a female premium (women earning higher pay than men on average) in special cases. I propose to develop and test a novel theory that provides a unifying explanation for both the female penalty and the female premium. Imagine employers are searching through a large number of job applications, where each application includes the applicant’s “first offer” for negotiating their wage. Employers’ willingness-to-pay (WTP) for an applicant’s wage is higher for applicants that the employer believes to be of higher quality. I assume that (1) employers believe that women make less than men on average, (2) employers’ WTP for an applicant’s wage is stereotypically biased towards what the employer believes is average pay for the applicant’s gender (biased upwards for men, biased downwards for women), and (3) employees penalize applicants whose first offer asks for more than the employer thinks would be reasonable. These assumptions create two countervailing gender effects. The first effect is an overall female penalty. The second effect is that high-quality female applicants (compared to high-quality male applicants) can more credibly signal their high quality by making a high first offer. Thus, my theory predicts that women who ask for low wages will earn less than a man who asked for the same amount: a female penalty. However, my theory also predicts that women who ask for sufficiently high wages will earn more than a man who asked for the same amount (because of the second effect): a female premium. I will test these predictions using both field data and laboratory experiments. My preliminary field data results, analyzing a unique scraped dataset from an online labor marketplace, support my theory. I find a significant female penalty at the lowest end of the wage distribution (~US$5/hr), but a significant female premium at the highest end of the wage distribution (~US$120/hr); the female penalty “reverses” and becomes a female premium at around US$90/hr. I will use this field dataset to conduct many additional analyses, but it also has limitations: it cannot be used to test some implications of my theory, and it is not a controlled setting. To overcome these limitations, I will conduct a series of laboratory experiments that attempt to recreate a labor marketplace in which job negotiations take place, using relevant participants (e.g., managers). 26506620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26506620.value: It is widely documented that some institutional investors earn higher returns on their portfolios than others, but the reason for such superior performance---so called ``skills’’---is unclear in the literature. We take advantage of data on corporate bond holding by institutional investors to study the time-varying performance of investment returns. We compare the major classes of investor in corporate bonds, including insurance firms, mutual funds and pension funds and examine the link between superior performances by one class and underperformance by the other classes. That is, for some investors to reliably outperform the market, they need to take advantage of portfolio constraints that other investors face. Such portfolio constraints may be based on liquidity or regulatory constraints, which restrict investor choice. However, the degree of tightness of these restrictions is likely to vary over time, depending on market conditions. For example, insurance firms face regulatory constraints that force them to sell corporate bonds downgraded from investment grade to speculative grades, potentially at a discounted price. Then the other investors, free from any regulatory constraint, can purchase those downgraded bonds at a discount, leading to higher returns going forward. Thus, we can deduce that investor performance varies according to how many bonds are downgraded in the recent past, as well as the regulatory capital ratio of insurance firms. The corporate bond holding data allows us to establish such a linkage in performance in the data, and to quantify the magnitude of performance. We then show that investor ability to take advantage of the constraints on other investors generates substantial ``skills’’ in portfolio management that explains the heterogeneous performance in corporate bond investment. Unlike other predictors of investment performance, the skill of taking advantage of other investors is likely to be persistent over time, and help explain why some investors perform better than others. Identifying the source of performance reliably is important for two reasons: first, with our performance predictor, retail investors can identify better investment opportunities; second, we can evaluate the cost of regulatory and liquidity constraints that binds decision making by some investors. Though these constraints help make financial institutions stable, there is an associated cost, which ultimately is borne by households. In conclusion, by studying the portfolio performance of all types of institutional investors jointly, we aim to explain how outperformance by certain classes of investors is due to underperformance by other classes, who make suboptimal choices because of portfolio constraints. 现有研究发现一些机构投资者的投资决策能够带来更高的回报， 但是目前的研究没有回答关于产生这些高绩效—也称为“投资能力”—的具体原因。本研究中，我们利用机构投资者的公司债券的持有数据来研究机构投资者的因时空而变的机构投资者投资绩效。 我们对包括保险公司，共同基金，养老基金等主要机构投资者进行分类比较以及合并分析。进行合并分析是基于资本市场中一些投资者的优异表现在于他们利用了其他投资者受到的财务约束或监管限制。一些投资限制可能来源于流动性原因或者监管限制。而且这些限制是动态随时间变化的，深受金融市场行情的影响。譬如，如果公司债券由投资级降为投机级债券， 根据保险监管要求保险公司需要出售持有的这些债券很可能需要折价出售。而其他不受监管政策限制的投资者因此可以低价购买这些降级债券并在随后的投资期间提高其基金绩效。有鉴于此，我们可以根据近期被降级的债券数量和保险行业对保险公司的资本充足率要求等情况分析和预测投资者的绩效变化。 利用机构投资者的持有公司债券的数据我们能够根据投资者持有公司债券的情况与机构投资者的投资表现进行联动分析， 并精确分析其投资绩效。我们进一步发现投资者可以利用那些受投资约束的同行来获得高回报—也就是更好的投资能力。这个发现能够解释公司债券投资市场投资者的绩效的巨大差异。不同于其他的投资绩效预测因子，部分投资者利用其他投资者的限制来实现绩效提高的能力是可持续的，这也可以解释为啥一些投资者投资回报高于其他投资者。 可靠地甄别出投资绩效的来源非常重要。主要原因有两点：一是二级市场投资者可以用本研究提出的绩效预测因子来甄别投资机会；二是我们据此可以估计监管和流动性约束条件对那些需要遵守的投资者造成的成本。尽管这些投资限制有助于保持金融系统的稳定，但是不是零成本的，这些成本最终由公众承担。 一言以蔽之，通过对所有机构投资者的绩效研究，本课题的研究目标是通过对那些投资受监管限制的投资者的低绩效去探究特定群体的投资者的优异表现的深层原因。

26600020.label: Realisation of objectives
26600020.value: Objective 1: The project has fully achieved this objective by providing strong empirical evidence that anti-PAE laws influence IT firms' innovation strategies. Using a difference-in-differences approach on a panel of 1,086 IT firms from 2012 to 2019, the study finds that the laws shift firms toward more exploitative innovation overall. Further analysis reveals a dual mechanism: firms heavily exposed to prior patent troll litigation increase exploratory innovation following the reduction in litigation risks, while firms operating in denser patent thickets reduce exploration due to higher compliance costs. These results demonstrate not only that anti-PAE laws affect innovation, but also clarify the pathways through which they exert their influence. Objective 2: The project has successfully advanced this scholarly conversation by showing that the governance of patent trolling, while reducing certain risks, also introduces new innovation constraints. Prior studies mainly emphasized the litigation threat posed by patent trolls; this study adds important nuance by highlighting that anti-PAE laws, though aimed at curbing abusive practices, simultaneously create compliance burdens that can discourage exploratory innovation. By uncovering this dual impact—risk reduction and compliance cost—the project provides a deeper understanding of how institutional governance shapes the innovation environment in IT industries, opening new questions about how best to balance protection with innovation incentives. Objective 3: The project has achieved this objective by offering clear evidence that anti-PAE laws, while effective at reducing opportunistic litigation, also impose significant compliance costs that can unintentionally deter exploratory innovation. The findings show that firms embedded in complex patent environments are particularly sensitive to these costs, which may lead to a narrowing of their technological exploration. Based on these insights, the study informs policymakers that while anti-PAE laws play an important role in curbing abusive litigation, attention must also be given to minimizing unintended barriers to innovation. This highlights the need for a more balanced design of patent governance to preserve long-term technological dynamism.

26600020.label: Major findings and research outcome
26600020.value: This project investigates how anti-patent-assertion-entity (anti-PAE) laws affect IT firms’ innovation strategies. Using a difference-in-differences approach and panel data from 1,086 IT firms over the period 2012–2019, the study finds that anti-PAE laws reshape innovation behavior through two countervailing mechanisms: reduced litigation risk and increased compliance costs. First, the overall effect of anti-PAE laws is a shift toward more exploitative innovation. IT firms increasingly focus on refining and deepening existing technological capabilities after the enactment of these laws. However, this aggregate pattern masks important heterogeneity. Firms that had previously faced higher exposure to patent troll litigation respond differently: they increase exploratory innovation once the threat of opportunistic lawsuits declines. In contrast, firms operating in dense patent thickets, where many overlapping patent rights create legal complexity, reduce exploratory innovation, reflecting the increased compliance burden imposed by the laws. Second, the study finds that anti-PAE laws are effective in reducing opportunistic patent troll litigation, confirming their intended function. However, they also create new strategic costs by requiring firms to provide detailed disclosures when asserting their own patents, thus raising the risk of revealing sensitive technological information during enforcement efforts. This unintended side effect particularly burdens firms in complex technological landscapes, discouraging them from venturing into new technology domains. These findings have important theoretical and practical implications. Theoretically, the project enriches the Information Systems and Innovation Strategy literatures by framing anti-PAE laws as a dual institutional force—simultaneously reducing external risks and increasing internal compliance burdens. Practically, the study highlights the need for policymakers to balance legal protections against abusive litigation with minimizing barriers to legitimate innovation activities. Overly burdensome compliance requirements may undermine long-term technological progress, especially in fast-cycle IT sectors. In sum, the project provides the first empirical evidence that anti-PAE laws, while effective in their primary goal, produce complex side effects that influence firms' strategic innovation decisions. It shows that legal interventions, even when aimed at curbing abuse, can reshape the direction of industry innovation in subtle but significant ways. The paper is in the 2nd round of review at Information Systems Research, a highly regarded journal in the field. The publication process for this journal typically takes 2–3 years, and the timeline is consistent with these norms.

26600020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26600020.value: This research opens several promising directions for further development within the IT sector. First, future studies can investigate the long-term effects of anti-PAE laws on IT firms’ innovation, especially whether the shift toward exploitation leads to reduced breakthrough inventions over time. Second, deeper analysis can explore heterogeneity across different types of IT firms, such as startups versus incumbents, to understand how firm size and technological maturity moderate responses to anti-PAE laws. Third, there is a need to study how firms adapt their IP management strategies—for example, by adopting modular patenting or defensive publishing—to better navigate the compliance burdens introduced by these laws.

26600020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26600020.value: This research studies how laws against "patent trolls" affect innovation in the Information Technology (IT) industry. IT firms are especially vulnerable because their products, like software and electronic devices, combine many interconnected parts, making them easy targets for trolls who exploit vague patents. Our study shows that these laws have a dual role. They reduce the risk of being sued unfairly, but they also increase the cost of protecting inventions, because companies must now reveal more technical details in legal claims. Using real-world data from over 1,000 IT firms between 2012 and 2019, our empirical analysis finds that, after these laws, firms generally focus more on improving existing technologies rather than exploring new areas. Importantly, the effects are not the same for all firms. Firms that had more experience with patent troll attacks became more exploratory, taking advantage of a safer environment. In contrast, firms facing more complex patent landscapes became more conservative, focusing on familiar technologies to manage compliance risks. These results show that even well-intentioned laws can reshape innovation in unexpected ways. To support a healthy IT industry, policymakers must balance protection from abuse with minimizing new barriers to breakthrough innovation.

26601720.label: Project Objectives
26601720.value: To trace the spread of Russian nihilism, populism, and anarchism in Europe and Japan by tracing newspapers, periodicals, and books published at the end of the nineteenth and the beginning of the twentieth centuries, with a special focus on publications that might have been available to Chinese readers at the time. To compare the Chinese introduction to and translations of Russian nihilist and anti-nihilist texts with European and Japanese materials, and to identify possible appropriation and distortion. To elucidate the transformation of nihilism into anarchism in Chinese discourse, and identify the role of European and Japanese intermediary texts in the transformation.

26601720.label: Realisation of objectives
26601720.value: Due to the pandemic, which lasted for more than half of the period of this project, I was not able to carry out the field trips as I initially planned in the first two years. I was only able to travel to the US in the summer of 2023. As a result, I had to alter my initial research plan, and the majority of the research output I had so far was based on the materials I collected through interlibrary loans. I switched to focus on anarchist books and their translations in East Asia. This is an easier target to achieve during the pandemic because of the accessibility of books and their translations. I also tried to gain access to digital databases that contain materials useful for my research. Despite the difficult, due to my adjustment, I managed to carry out profound research on the early Chinese translation of Russian nihilist stories and the Japanese intermediary that inspired the Chinese intellectuals. I focused, in particular, on several key figures in Japan and China, and traced the route of the transculturation of nihilism/anarchism. The case studies I concentrated on normally involved all the cultures I planned to study (Russia, Japan, China, and Western Europe), and I largely enhanced my comprehension of the process through my close analysis. Although the texts I worked on were mostly positive towards Russian nihilism, I have also included criticism or negative voices. I also gained a better understanding of the transformation of nihilism into anarchism in East Asia.

26601720.label: Major findings and research outcome
26601720.value: To better understand the route taken by Russian nihilist ideas, I examined the development of Russian nihilism and the philosophical discussions that shaped the movement in the nineteenth century. These investigations delineated how Russian nihilism converged with the discourse of populism, and how it was eventually recognized as a crucial component of the global anarchist movement. I also studied Russian literary works inspired by or critical of radical nihilists and their reckless methods. My research laid the foundation for my further inquiry into how concepts such as nihilism, populism, and anarchism were transformed and applied in imprecise and diverse ways outside of Russia. By focusing on a movement of key importance in Chinese modernism, my research improves our understanding of the complexities of the Chinese reception of “Western” knowledge at the beginning of the twentieth century. It also sheds new light on the global cultural exchange process, which can often be understood only by expanding beyond a source culture and a target culture (in this case, Russia and China) to include intermediaries (such as Europe and Japan) that participate in the appropriation of existing cultures and the production of new cultural constructions. Despite the pandemic that lasted through the majority of my research years (2020-2023) which caused tremendous difficulty for any field trip outside Hong Kong, I still achieved a reasonable outcome in the past three years: two articles accepted and multiple presentations in international conferences. In addition to these journal publications, I have also presented my findings at multiple international conferences throughout the years. In particular, among the two publications, the second article will come out in Comparative Literature Studies, which is one of the two representative journals on comparative literature in the English world. Given the low acceptance rate of the journal, it is a major achievement. This speaks to the recognition of the value of this research project in the English world. Below please find the articles’ information: 2024. “Relayed Revolutionary Sentiment: Chinese Appropriation of Russian Nihilism in Popular Literature.” Comparative Literature Studies. (Forthcoming) This article examines the relay translation of William Tufnell Le Queux’s (1864–1927) Strange Tales of a Nihilist, which the prominent Chinese translator of nihilist fiction, Chen Jinghan 陳景韓 (1878–1965), completed based on Matsui Shōyō’s 松居松葉 (1870–1933) Japanese rendering. 2022. “The Transfiguration of Russian Revolutionary Spirit: Chinese Translations of Kemuyama Sentarō’s Modern Anarchism in the Early Twentieth Century.” International Comparative Literature 5 (3): 77-99. By outlining how Kemuyama’s scholarly research into Russian revolutionary politics eventually served as a crucial impetus for early twentieth-century Chinese social and revolutionary movements, the article explores the relationship between transcultural texts and politics, and the implications for translation as a cultural mediator.

26601720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26601720.value: My research has made me realize the connection between nihilism/anarchism and Chinese leftist literature/culture at the beginning of the twentieth century. Instead of Marxism and Leninism, Russian anarchism exerted a profound impact on the early development of Chinese leftist literature/culture in the 1910s and 1920s. I plan to further explore the connection and influence to understand the diverse intellectual sources that inspired the Chinese construction of leftism. This will help me better understand the plurality of Chinese leftism, which is not dictated by Marxist socialism.

26601720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26601720.value: The core objective of this project is to examine the convoluted journey undertaken by Russian nihilism/anarchism when it was transplanted to Chinese soil at the beginning of the twentieth century. While research to date primarily focuses on the target culture (China) as a site of cultural reception, this project contextualizes Chinese manifestations of Russian nihilism in a comparative perspective by reconstructing the route by which Russian nihilism traveled around the globe. By tracing how Chinese people learned about Russian nihilism from European (mostly English-language) and Japanese sources, this project explores the reasons for the enthusiasm with which Chinese intellectuals appropriated Russian nihilist themes at the beginning of the twentieth century.

27107320.label: Project Objectives
27107320.value: Genome mining has become a powerful technology to exploit natural product diversity and to guide their discovery. However, it remains challenging to prioritize and identify the biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) of interest in a high-throughput manner. Here, we propose to develop a big data genome mining strategy capable of the systematic investigation and the high-throughput prioritization of BGCs from a large-scale genome dataset. Integrating big data genome mining with the established LC-MS-based metabolomics and antibiotics bioassay in our department, we aim to fully establish a powerful genomics-guided discovery platform for the efficient and targeted discovery of new antibiotics. The preliminary BGC analysis of 163,037 sequenced bacterial genomes indicated that the majority of the bacterial peptide is still uncharacterized, representing a huge untapped source for peptide antibiotic discovery. We will next apply the genomics-guided approach to the continuously growing genome datasets to discover novel peptide antibiotics with new modes of action including, but not limited to, calcium-dependent antibiotics (CDA). Study the mechanism of action and resistance of lead compounds, which can be targeted and be more straightforward by our big data genome mining.
