27124120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27124120.value: Platelets, anucleate blood cells, can detect the blood vessel damage, and patch the injury to prevent excessive bleeding. At the resting state, biconvex discoid platelets circulate in the blood vessels. This unique shape, which allows the resting platelets to pass narrow intercellular space, is maintained by the microtubule bundle that circles around the cell periphery (i.e., the marginal band). Stimulated by injury, within one minute, the discoid resting cells transform into the spherical activated platelets with extended filopodia. This rapid shape transition from biconvex disc to spiny sphere depends on the coiling and the reorganization of the marginal band. However, it is currently unclear how microtubules, the rigid non-covalent polymers of α/β-tubulin heterodimers with persistence length at millimeter range, respond to the force and coil in the micrometer scale platelets. Human genome encodes at least nine α- and ten β-tubulin gene families (i.e., isotypes) that show cell type-specific protein expression profile. The α4A- and β1-tubulin are the predominant tubulin isotypes expressed in human platelets. Mutations distributed in different structure domains of α4A- and β1-tubulin have been identified in patients with inherited bleeding disorders. Without affecting the protein expression level, these mutations cause similar phenotypes that patients’ resting platelets are spherical with ~30% larger cell volume than normal cells; the marginal band becomes straight microtubule segments in the cytoplasm. These disease-related mutations suggest that wild-type α4A- and β1-tubulin form microtubules with unique properties that are essential for the function and organization of the cytoskeletal filaments in the micrometer size platelets. However, due to the limited accessibility to recombinant human tubulin, biochemical and biophysical characterization of human tubulin isotypes was challenging. We have overcome this challenge through developing a strategy to generate good quantity of recombinant human tubulin with any isotypes of interest, such as wild-type and mutant α4A/β1-tubulin. The biological function of microtubules depends on the intrinsic properties of the polymers: the polymerization dynamics, the mechanical properties (i.e., response to force), and the binding of microtubule associated proteins. With recombinant human α4A/β1-tubulin, we can reconstitute the platelets’ microtubules and dissect the effects of the disease-related mutations on these intrinsic properties of α4A/β1 microtubules. Through combinatorial approaches involving high-resolution fluorescence microscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, chemical biology, and quantitative proteomics, our study will not only reveal the molecular mechanism by which α4A/β1-tubulin regulates microtubule network in platelets, but also provide the general guidelines for understanding tubulin isotypes’ unique function in different cell types. 血小板主要的功能為偵測並修補受損的血管。處於靜息態的血小板為雙凸圓盤狀。此特徵形狀的維持仰賴於平行緊密排列的微管環繞著血小板周圍而形成相鄰於細胞皮層(cortex)的微管(microtubule)架構(又稱緣帶，marginal band)。當接觸到傷口或激活劑時，圓盤狀的血小板會在一分鐘內轉變細胞型態而成為球型且具有絲狀偽足(filopodia)的激活態。血小板型態的轉變伴隨著微管結構迅速地重組。微管在經歷延伸、扭轉、纏繞、聚合及解聚等過程後，於激活態的血小板細胞中心形成更為扭曲的環狀微管結構(曲率半徑小於緣帶的70%)。來自肌動球蛋白(actomyosin)收縮以及微管動力蛋白(motor proteins)的應力在血小板形態以及高度纏結的微管架構的轉變過程扮演著重要角色。然而，目前的研究顯示微管具有毫米等級的持久長度(persistence length)，是剛性最高的細胞骨架。因此，我們仍不瞭解微管是如何在微米尺度的血小板中扭轉及纏繞。 α/β微管蛋白(α/β-tubulin)聚合形成中空圓柱絲狀的微管。在人類基因體中存在至少九種α微管蛋白及十種β微管蛋白同種型(isotype)。α4A及β1微管蛋白為血小板中主要的同種型。當α4A或β1微管蛋白上發生點突變時會導致巨大血小板減少症(macrothrombocytopenia)，一種凝血功能不全的遺傳疾病。病人的血小板不僅型態改變(為球狀且體積增大約50%)，而且鬆散的微管直線片段取代環繞細胞皮質的緊密緣帶架構。β1微管蛋白缺失(β1-/-)的小鼠因血小板數量降低以及功能減退而導致凝血功能異常。由於其他β微管蛋白同種型(β2及β5)的補償性表達，β1-/-小鼠的血小板中β微管蛋白的整體表現量相較於野生型並未有明顯降低。然而，β1-/-小鼠的血小板不具有特徵的雙凸圓盤狀。其環繞著細胞皮質的緣帶消失，且微管數量大幅降低(約70%)並頻繁地斷裂與彎折。種種證據顯示α4A及β1微管蛋白與血小板的生成及正常功能有著高度關聯。然而，由於生物物理及生物化學實驗上的限制，目前對於α4A/β1微管的性質仍然缺乏瞭解。 微管的生物功能仰賴於微管的動力學特性、力學性質以及微管結合蛋白(microtubule-associated proteins) 。我們發展出了一個方法可以得到高度純化的專一微管蛋白同種型。 藉由純化的重組人類α4A /β1微管蛋白，我們將應用高解析度單分子瑩光顯微鏡以及光鉗來解析α4A /β1微管蛋白如何調控微管的性質並進而在血小板的生成及正常功能中扮演獨特且重要的角色。

27200520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200520.value: 本項目旨在研究一類系統化化的方法，將三維點雲數據重建為建築及城市信息模型（BIM/CIM）。構造語法（architectonic grammar）不僅普遍存在于建築設計語言中，也是建築及城市信息模型的數據語言的基本標準。本研究將以構造語法最優化的視角來探索模型重建的問題。首先，定義構造語法來反應建築及城市信息模型，主要包括多種構件模型在參數化建模配置中的語義（例如類型、尺寸及顔色）及其文法規則（例如拓撲關係及多樣性）。然後，將構造語法設計映射至點雲數據匹配，建立一類非綫性優化數學模型，從而剋服點雲中的噪音、遮蔽及雜物等數據缺陷。第三步，研究運用高階無導數優化算法計算該非綫性優化問題，求解出最符合輸入數據和構造語法集的參數化構造方案。最終，最優化的參數化構造方案將剋服點雲數據缺陷，並自動重建出準確的建築及城市信息模型。研究成果將為處理非結構化點雲數據的相關研究和實踐提供一種新的自動化手段，並能為建築和建設的課堂教學提供前沿討論案例。

27200520.label: Realisation of objectives
27200520.value: 5.1 Scope of investigation -- Building/city information modeling (BIM/CIM) is vital to smart and sustainable development in the digital twin era. However, the BIM/CIM of existing buildings is hindered by the imperfections of 3D measurement data, such as noises, occlusions, and clutter in point clouds. The research team notices that buildings/cities' innate architectonic designs may overcome some data imperfections. -- This project studies architectonic grammar optimization methods to find the best design for BIM/CIM reconstruction. -- We define a nonlinear problem of architectonic grammar by integrating the global features (e.g., symmetry, enclosure, and urban patterns) and local features (e.g., local section backbones, deep learning-based semantics) in architectonic grammar and conventional 3D geometric error metrics. -- We apply heuristic optimization, DFO (derivative-free optimization), and deep learning algorithms to realize an automatic “best-fit” BIM/CIM reconstruction and apply the grammar/skeleton-guided model back to BIM/CIM to analyze and improve the overall performance. 5.2 Objectives achieved -- Objective 1 was achieved [100%]. The focused architectonic grammar includes global features and local features, sometimes the shape grammars can be inherited from established data sources according to [4]. We have identified and presented the foundation, example grammar, three global features, and two local features in the following publications: o Paper [9] [Note: #9 in Sect. 8]: A novel Building Section Skeleton theory as a foundation of architectonic grammar. o Paper [10]: A Symmetric Skeleton Grammar was defined and formulated. o Optional architectonic features for the grammar: -->> Paper [5]: Architectural symmetry for BIM/CIM, which won a Merit Award of Research in The Hong Kong OpenBIM / OpenGIS Awards 2022, -->> [Award #3 in Sect. 11]: enclosure of indoor space for BIM, -->> [3]: acoustic patterns of indoor settings for BIM, -->> Papers [2,8,11]: deep transfer learning-based semantics -->> Objective 2 was achieved sustainably [95%]. In addition to the general architectonic grammar optimization formulation in the proposal, Chapter [1] also defines a level of automation for architectonic optimization in the case of historical BIM. Papers [7, 10] extended the general formulation to building floor plan and individual building elements. Conference papers [3, 4, 2, 7] showcased the extended formulations for further BIM/CIM scenarios. -- Objective 3 was achieved sustainably [90%]. Papers [3,5,10] have demonstrated that DFO algorithms can successfully solve the architectonic optimization and its global/local features. Papers [2,8,11] also confirmed deep learning can be transferred for semantic segmentation for BIM/CIM, in terms of both 2D images and 3D point clouds for BIM/CIM reconstruction. -- Objective 4 was achieved [100%]. The approach was integrated and applied to several related problems. First, Paper [9] presented a state-of-the-art (SOTA) BIM/CIM compact reconstruction that bested all existing methods in terms of error and model compactness. The integrated approach has been piloted in a taught MSc course RECO7613 in 2021-2024, and in BSc course RECO2041 in 2022-2024. Grammar-guided parametric 3D reconstruction was taught in a popular gamified education environment, Minecraft Education Edition (Conference paper [6]). Our BIM reconstruction methods on architectonic regularities and enclosure won 6 awards from 2nd to 4th International Scan-to-BIM Challenge, CVPR 2022-2024[Awards 3, 10, 13 in Sect. 11]. Some papers have opened their source codes to the public via HKU Library and GitHub. 5.3 Deviations from the original plan -- There was a minor deviation in achieving Objective 3. We realized not only DFO algorithms but also heuristics optimization and deep learning algorithms for solving the architectonic grammar optimization formulations. The reason was that the optimization would be too sophisticated to be solved solely by DFO, if the scale of 3D point clouds went large. 5.4 Extensions and success beyond the original plan Apart from the successful execution of the project, we also looked into a few topics related to the project. -- Journal papers [2,11] proposed a 3D window view assessment based on CIM. -- Chapters [6, 1] extended the architectonic concept to digital heritage. -- Journal papers [10,8] applied the symmetric skeleton grammar and associated deep features to BIM design and details reconstruction.

27200520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27200520.value: The research project aimed to enhance building/city information modeling (BIM/CIM) reconstruction from 3D point clouds for smart and sustainable development. We focused on resolving the imperfections in existing buildings' 3D point cloud data using architectnoic grammar. The team studied a fundamental theory of 'building section skeleton.' We then investigated architectonic grammar optimization and studied global features like urban patterns and local features like deep learning-based semantics. We combined derivative-free optimization, heuristic optimization, and deep learning algorithms to achieve an automatic "best-fit" BIM/CIM reconstruction. Key objectives were met. The outcomes were validated through experiments in different fields, peer-reviewed as academic publications (8 journal papers), integrated into educational courses, and attracted 16 peer-reviewed awards. The project also extended its impact from BIM/CIM to digital heritage and 3D window view assessment. 27202920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202920.value: 物聯網（IoT）的爆炸式增長意味著我們正面臨如何為接入網路中的數十億電子設備進行供電的問題，這些電子設備需要消耗大量能量。自供電電子設備使用可再生能源為自己供電，正在成為一種可為未來技術供電的新興手段。壓電和摩擦電納米發電機，可將機械能轉換為電能，由於其易於製造，便於攜帶和高轉換效率，作為自供電電子設備極具前景的電源平臺的得到了人們的大量關注。儘管在過去的幾十年中，它們的能量輸出性能已經取得了重大進展，但是仍然需要進行改進，以滿足將其用於自供電電子產品的要求。一類新型的多孔材料，例如金屬有機框架材料（MOFs）和多孔芳族框架材料（PAFs），具有易於改性的化學結構，可用於製備各類多功能材料。人們預測在原子尺度上控制材料本征特性是調節材料壓電性和摩擦電表面化學勢的關鍵因素。 本研究將開發一類新型的多孔材料，通過其進行系統設計，以滿足我們對壓電和摩擦電納米發電機改進性能的需求。我們設想了兩種不同的路徑來為每種納米發電機的應用定制多孔材料：1）壓電MOFs的孔隙率調節和2）MOFs和PAFs的表面化學勢的調節。通過精心設計材料的本征特性，我們將這些材料整合到納米發電機中，並評估其在自供電設備中的使用性能。這些新型的多孔材料不僅能夠提高納米發電機的輸出性能，而且能夠讓我們深入理解無機和有機材料摩擦起電的基本機理，這將有助於我們建立起用于納米發電機的材料設計準則。我們相信我們的方法將能夠使納米發電機順利過渡到工業應用。同時，我們也相信配備這些納米發電機的自供電電子產品將有助於建設以創新和先進技術為特徵的世界領先的智慧香港。

27202920.label: Realisation of objectives
27202920.value: This project aimed twofold: 1) developing a new class of functional materials and 2) demonstrating their functionality in several nanogenerators. We have successfully achieved the objectives set out in the proposal, which range from new material development, characterization, and demonstration for nanogenerator applications. Specifically, the project objectives achieved are detailed below. First, in order to demonstrate one of the main postulations in which the low dielectric constant of the piezoelectric materials can make significant improvements on the figure of merits in nanogenerators, the effect of the dielectric constant of the piezoelectric layer on electrical outputs of the piezoelectric nanogenerator was investigated using ZnO/PDMS composites with differing ZnO coverage. We adjusted the porosity of the ZnO membrane from 11.6% to 35.7% by changing the ZnO concentration in the precursor solution, and then the elastomeric PDMS was permeated into the porous ZnO membrane, yielding the ZnO/PDMS composites with the dielectric constants in the range of 3.37 and 6.75. The output voltage of the piezoelectric nanogenerator comprising the piezoelectric composite with the lowest dielectric constant was found to be boosted approximately 11 times compared to that of the nanogenerator with the highest dielectric constant. Additionally, the results found in experiments were well-matched with those of the simulation study. We also successfully demonstrated another postulation where the higher permittivity of polymer can reduce the charge loss of electrostatic induction in triboelectric nanogenerators. We have reported a series of composite ﬁlms comprising the silver nanostructures and polyimide matrix, which exhibits outstanding performance as a triboelectriﬁcation layer, with an elevated dielectric constant of 5.43 in the presence of NRs, and heightened output power. The 1D nanostructures in the polymer matrix enable the alignment of interfacial polarization arising from single nanostructures, leading to remarkable improvement in permittivity as well as electrostatic induction on electrodes. Importantly, a straightforward yet cost-effective approach was successfully demonstrated to reduce the loss in conversion efﬁciency from mechanical energy to electrical energy, allowing this method to be further applicable to wearable and portable nanogenerator technologies. With the help of functional materials, the boosted electrical outputs in nanogenerators have been demonstrated in several forms of device architectures. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are put forward as a state-of-the-art energy-scavenging technology for self-powered electronics, but their severe wear and degradation driven by inevitable friction can pose significant durability and sustainability concerns. As a preliminary experiment, an array of microfibers reported that functions as a robust and sustainable TENG in both in-plane sliding and vertical contact-separation modes, with excellent electrical potential as high as 20 V and a high cyclability of 3000. The design flexibility of this microbrush TENG (MB-TENG) on the counter materials facilitates the further improvement of electrical outputs, benefiting numerous applications of human-interactive triboelectrification. Significantly, these MB-TENGs offer sufficient output power for successfully driving a smartwatch as well as an electromyography module. This technology uses a simple and cost-effective manner to provide a robust and reliable monolithic TENG module, which is expected to serve as a promising energy-harvesting source for self-powered electronics in the near future. This study allows us to optimize the device structure of TENGs, helping the implementation of porous functional materials into nanogenerators. We have then reported the customized nanogenerators, comprising the quadrant electrodes and the horizontal nanorods array, that act as the protocol for decoupling of compositive electrical outputs from the device under inhomogeneous stress. From three different characterization configurations, we found that the horizontal ZnO nanorods array and M13 bacteriophages exhibit the in-plane flexoelectricity of μZnO = 10.4 ± 5.5 nC m−1, μM13 wild = 17.3 ± 2.7 nC m−1, and μM13 4E = 24.2 ± 5.1 nC m−1, corresponding to the 12–20 % of total electrical outputs in the electromechanical devices. Such decomposition of an electrical signal will provide not only the fundamental insights into the flexoelectric mechanism but also the further engineering of architecture in advanced flexible devices. Namely, the additional built-in electric potential originating from the in-plane strain gradient will offer the controllability in the electrical outputs by tailoring the device designs. The demonstrated significant contribution of flexoelectricity in the flexible device may find its potential applications in improving the performance of electromechanical devices. Lastly, there has been a surge of interest in droplet-based triboelectric nanogenerators, facilitating the durable and sustainable harnessing of slow and periodic mechanical energy resources. A major challenge faced by most of these devices is the concurrent achievement of high electrical outputs and omnidirectionality, which hampers their immediate implementation in real-world slow and periodic energy harvesting scenarios. We present a floating droplet-activated electricity generator featuring asymmetric electrodes together with switching of an internal circuit, with a current output of ~107.6 μA, a power density of 1.2 kW/m3, and a charge density of 31.2 mC/m3, is reported. When multiple devices were parallelly integrated, the current output reached 1.2 mA at a waving frequency of 0.28 Hz. The omnidirectionality and stability of the device are also demonstrated. Furthermore, electrostatic charging derived from charge transfer throughout friction is commonplace, but understanding charge species transferred still remains a debated and contradictory issue. The electron has been widely believed to be the dominant charge carrier for contact electrification between solids, liquids, and gases. However, emerging evidence points to the trait that mobile ions can also contribute to the process, making it more complicated to elucidate even in solid-solid contact electrification. Here, we demonstrate that electrons and ions concurrently play a role in solid contact-electrification of solid-ionomer pairs and their contribution differs with environmental humidity levels. Our results showed that ionic charge transfer can improve contact electrification at high humidity levels. Moreover, adding ions to a non-ionic polymer surface can make contact electrification more resistant to humidity. Overall, our findings highlight the significant role of mobile ions in contact electrification, which could lead to new and improved technologies for electrophotography, electrospraying, energy harvesting, and self-powered sensing.

27202920.label: Major findings and research outcome
27202920.value: In this project, we successfully developed a new class of functional materials for nanogenerator applications, which helps to exhibit impressive enhancement in electrical performance in piezoelectric and triboelectric nanogenerators. Control over the dielectric permittivity of functional materials is found to be a critical factor in engendering systematic regulation of electrical performance in nanogenerators. Implementation of such findings into nanogenerator devices demonstrated that a significant improvement in electrical outputs can be controlled by the rational design of functional materials. Based on these findings, we have been successful in publishing our results, as demonstrated by 7 publications and 1 manuscript under review in total. All findings from this project have been published in highly esteemed academic journals, including Advanced Materials (IF=29.4), Nano Energy (IF=17.6), Small (IF=13), Device (IF=TBD, Cell Press), and Advanced Engineering Materials (IF=3.4). The findings have been publicized by PI in 7 international conferences (5 of them are invited talks), such as ENGE 2022, IEEE NEMS 2023, Nano Korea 2023, AMF-AMEC 2023, and MRS 2024 Spring. Two students, Xiaoting Ma and Jiaming Zhou, received the best poster award and Hanson outstanding/creative award at EcoMat 2023 conference and Energy Saving Championship hosted by EMSD, respectively. Both students are trained under partial support of this project.

27202920.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27202920.value: In this project, we found that inter-material ion transfer contributes significantly to the process of contact electrification between ionomers and counter materials (5th objectives), especially at high humidity, even though only less than 2% of ions participate in the ion transfer. Nonetheless, our understanding of the role and mechanism of ion transfer has been constrained by the difficulty in systematically controlling ion concentrations, distributions, and binding affinity at the polymeric surface due to short-range ordering inherent in polymers. The urgent need to develop materials with controllable characteristics has prompted further development of research project. This research requires to aim to utilize covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and porous aromatic frameworks (PAFs) as the platforms for developing new model materials. Our aim is to generate materials with physical and chemical properties that can be manipulated as per requirement, thus offering greater control and customization.

27202920.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27202920.value: The surge in the use of Internet of Things devices presents a challenge of how to power billions of electronic devices that demand significant energy from the grid. Electronics that power themselves through renewable energy sources are emerging as an alternative solution for powering future technologies. Piezoelectric and triboelectric nanogenerators, which convert mechanical energy into electrical energy, have gained considerable interest due to their easy manufacturing process, portability, and high energy conversion efficiency. However, despite notable advancements in their power output performance over the years, further enhancements are necessary to meet the needs of self-powered electronics. Here, in order to improve the power outputs of nanogenerators, we developed a new class of functional materials for nanogenerator applications. Manipulating the dielectric permittivity of functional materials has been identified as a crucial element in systematically controlling the electrical performance of nanogenerators. Incorporating these insights into nanogenerator devices has shown that significant enhancements in electrical outputs can be governed by the logical design of functional materials. Our findings will facilitate the seamless integration of nanogenerators into industrial applications. Furthermore, self-powered electronics equipped with these nanogenerators will contribute to the creation of a globally leading Smart Hong Kong, recognized for its innovative technology.

27203720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27203720.value: The proposed research will investigate the fundamental issues of chemo-geomechanics related to emerging engineering problems of underground energy solutions and safety – including unconventional shale hydrocarbon production, enhanced geothermal systems, geological sequestration of CO2 – where cracking plays an important role across length and time scales. The main objective of this proposed project is to develop a mechanism-based predictive tool for a fluid pressure induced propagation of a subcritical fracture in a variable chemical field, with a variable permeability. Based on our preliminary results and previous work, we postulate that the propagation of a single tensile crack is driven by the coupling of 1) emerging dissipative shear micro-cracking along the logarithmic spirals around the crack tip, 2) the chemical reactions occurring at the surface of the generated micro-cracks and the transport of dissolved minerals, and 3) the micro-cracking induced change in local hydraulic conductivities and delivery of acid. These postulates will be examined by numerical tools and controlled laboratory experiments. The main challenge in the numerical investigation is the implementation of the coupling of chemical reactions (and transport) with the mechanical response of the rock and the dissipative nature of the degradation process. By tackling this challenge, the interaction modes between mechanical properties, hydraulic properties and each chemical/physical variable will be identified. A coupled chemo-hydro-mechanical model will be combined with local-global dissipative feedbacks and implemented into REDBACK, a multi-physics high performance computing finite element simulator we have been developing. The numerical results will be benchmarked using the analytical and semi-analytical methods from our previous work. The layer of dissipative feedbacks allows for the self-organization of local shear instabilities (i.e. micro-cracks) and hence a visualization of crack growth/branching paths and evolutionary topology of fluid compartmentalization. This will be validated by analogue experiments in parallel with a particle image velocimetry system. The last stage of this project is to investigate the coalescence of two adjacent fluid-driven cracks, with the goal of identifying the onset of crack bridging (i.e. dissolution piping) instability. This plays a key role in predicting the evolution of effective permeability in a fractured rock. The anticipated outcomes of the proposed project include 1) a multi-physics based model for crack propagation/bifurcation in a chemically aggressive environment, 2) a multi-physics based model for coalescence of two adjacent cracks subject to a chemically aggressive environment, and 3) fundamental knowledge of a new regime of hydro-chemically induced solid instabilities. 擬議課題將致力於研究能源地下工程（包括非常規頁岩油氣生產，增強地熱系統，二氧化碳地質儲存等）在安全應用推廣時需考慮的化學-力學場耦合的基礎問題。在這幾項新興科技的作用過程中，裂化在長度尺度和時間尺度上均扮演著重要角色 。該擬議項目的主要目標是開發一種基於機理的預測工具，用於預測由流體壓力驅動的亞臨界態裂縫在化學變量場和可變滲透率影響下的擴展。根據我們已獲得的初步結果和先前工作累積的經驗，我們提出如下假設：單拉伸裂紋的反應擴展由以下因素耦合驅動：1）單裂紋尖端附近出現對數螺旋狀的耗散型剪切微裂紋； 2）化學反應在新產生的微裂紋的表面產生，同時經溶解的礦物質按濃度梯度擴散，以及3）微裂紋引起的局部水力滲透率和酸介質運輸狀態的變化。該假設將通過數值模擬和受控實驗室實驗進行檢驗。 數值研究中的主要挑戰是如何實現化學反應（及輸運）與岩石的力學響應以及降解過程本身的耗散性質的耦合作用。該問題的解決，將確定材料力學性能，水力性能與各個化學/物理變量之間的相互作用模式。我們將開發化學-水力-力學耦合模型與局部-全局耗散反饋模型，並將其整合到多物理場高性能計算有限元開源模擬器REDBACK中進行實現。所獲得的數值結果將使用我們先前工作中獲得的分析和半分析方法進行基準測試。耗散性反饋層的引入將允許局部剪切不穩定（呈現為微裂紋）形成自組織結構，從而可以直接觀測到裂紋擴展/分支路徑以及注入液體分流的演化拓撲。同時我們將通過使用粒子圖像測速系統（PIV）進行模擬實驗來驗證。假定該項目進展順利，我們將繼而研究兩個相鄰的液壓化學驅動裂紋的合併，其目標是確定裂紋橋接（亦可理解為溶解貫通）不穩定的啟始。這在預測裂隙岩體有效滲透率的演變中起到關鍵作用。擬議項目的預期結果包括：1）基於多物理場的化學侵蝕環境下裂紋擴展/分叉模型； 2）基於多物理場的相鄰裂縫在化學侵蝕環境下合併的模型；以及3 ）關於水力-化學誘導下的固體不穩定性新機制的基礎認知。

27205320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27205320.value: 泥石流是壹種泥水混合物，常以極快的速度傾瀉而下，極易造成人員傷亡、損毀基礎設施。爲攔截泥石流，通常采用封閉式剛性擋牆來阻斷泥石流溝道的整個過流斷面。然而，壹旦封閉擋牆被泥石流物質於滿，擋牆會對後續泥石流失去調節作用，從而導致軌迹難以預測的災難性漫頂溢流。此外，封閉式擋牆後方常堆積微細顆粒（溝道淤積物），這進壹步削弱了其原本就有限的攔蓄效能，從而極易引發規模更大、危害更強的泥石流災害。底部與溝床之間留有壹定間隙的開放式擋牆可替代傳統的封閉式擋牆。這種底部間隙結構形式可以：i）減小沖擊面積，減弱沖擊力；ii）調節峰值流量，避免漫頂溢流；iii）減緩淤積物堆積。底部間隙結構形式可用于設計具有自排放功能的擋牆群，既可逐級耗散泥石流能量，又可確保沈積物安全地向下遊輸移。設計時,遠端上遊擋牆應設計有較大的底部間隙，在耗散泥石流能量的同時可以最大程度地減少淤積物堆積。下遊擋牆應設計較小的底部間隙，便于設施保護和沈積物清淤。底部間隙結構形式雖然具有重要的科學研究意義和工程應用價值，但現有設計主要依賴工程經驗。若間隙設計過大，則無法控制泥石流下遊排量；若間隙設計過小，則又無異于封閉式擋牆。相關研究主要掣肘于：i) 缺乏涉及該領域的泥石流沖擊基礎機理；ii) 泥石流具有尺度效應，需特殊試驗裝置來模擬其恰當的動力學特性；iii) 泥石流動力特征與其複雜的流體組成（如，顆粒粒徑）密切相關。本項目擬利用目前世界上規模最大的水槽裝置開展物理模擬試驗來獲取泥石流的相關動力學特性。試驗數據將被用于校核數值模型和開展參數研究，從而缺失的試驗數據可以利用插值方法進行補充完善。此外，本項目還將構建和評估壹套新的用于設計具有多尺度底部間隙的自排放擋牆群的理論分析體系。由國際專家學者所組成的泥石流和陡溪災害委員會（本項目首席負責人爲該委員會主席）將負責本項目的研究成果轉化，擬形成該領域內世界首套工程設計指南。

27205320.label: Realisation of objectives
27205320.value: All of the project revised project objectives have to achieved. A series of unique physical experimental data has been produced and used to reveal the fundamental impact mechanisms of debris flows against two rigid barriers with basal clearances. Both experiments and simulations have been leveraged to investigate the effects of a basal clearance on the impact force, discharge, and overflow dynamics. The new insights are expected to enable advancements in more sustainable barrier designs. The effects of boulders on impact of rigid barriers has been investigated using both experiments and simulations. As a result, guidance on jamming and impact force predictions are achieved. Numerical parametric studies have been conducted to study the effects of overflow dynamics, which govern barrier spacing design. All of the findings from this study have been taken holistically to provide guidelines for multiple barriers with basal clearances to self-clean.

27205320.label: Major findings and research outcome
27205320.value: -Both the Froude numbers and normalised basal clearance by the characteristic particle diameter are key design considerations when assessing the discharge, jump height and impact force. -An impact equation, with consideration of a basal clearance, was proposed and demonstrated that it can capture the impact dynamics of flow-type landslides into rigid barriers with different size clearances. The impact equation is suitable for flows with characteristics Froude numbers from 3 to 6 before impact. The proposed impact model, can reasonably predict the jump height and impact force for granular flows with Froude conditions ranging from 3.2 to 5.7. -The height of the discharge debris from the clearance is 30% less than that before impact. This rule-of-thumb can be used as a basis to design rigid barriers with basal-clearances in series. The discharge height is maintained for a flow distance of up to 28 times the initial flow depth before impact. As such, it is unreasonable to assume that the flow discharging from the basal clearance will have the same height as that of the clearance. In contrast, for cases if overflow occurs. The overflow can increase the discharge flow depth by up to three times. -The ratio between basal clearance height and the maximum particle size (i.e., boulder) in the debris material (i.e., the particle size larger than 90% of the debris material of 2.0 may induce clogging or jamming at the clearance. If the ratio between basal clearance height and the maximum particle size (i.e., boulder) in the debris material increases to 4.0, clogging or jamming at the clearance can be eliminated. -With a normalised basal clearance greater or equal to 0.5 by the initial flow depth before impact, the impact force and runup height of debris flow on the barrier can be reduced by more than 20%. -Upstream barrier with a normalised basal clearance height by the initial flow depth less than or equal to 0.8 is recommended for optimum dissipation of flow kinetic energy, and in turn reduce the impact force on the downstream barrier.

27205320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27205320.value: The work carried out in this study was for rigid barriers. Flexible steel net barriers have become increasingly used owing to their ease of installation, lower resisting forces required owing to deformation. Hence, the effects of deformation on the overflow and basal discharge characteristics of a multiple barrier system with basal clearances would add much value to existing practice. Furthermore, idealized straight channels were simulated in this study. An investigation on the effects of channel curvature on superelevation of the flow, resulting in barrier flanking and centrifuge effects between barriers are warranted. In reality debris flows occur in multiple surges, resulting in combined static and dynamic loading before and after overflow. In the current design practice in Hong Kong, impact forces from each surge are directly superposed to ensure a conservative barrier design. However, the intensive energy dissipation induced by the interaction between surges may greatly decrease the impact force exerted on the barrier. A conservative design may be acceptable for a massive reinforced concrete barrier as it usually has a higher strength. Understanding multiple surge dynamics would help progress towards smaller size barriers, which are in fact the advantages of multiple barrier systems.

27205320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27205320.value: The combined stress of human encroachment on hillsides and increase in heavy rainfall, as reported by the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, will increase the threat posed by landslides, which annually cause about US$4 billion in damage and 3,000 deaths globally. Debris flows, mixtures of soil and water surging downslope at high speeds, account for about 50% of the fatalities. Engineering practice considers physical barriers as the first line of defence against debris flows. To arrest large volumes of debris flows, multiple barriers are installed are the flow path to progressively intercept debris and dissipate its energy as it fills behind and cascades over each barrier. In the field, barriers are detailed with a gap underneath it (i.e., basal clearance) to enable smaller particles and discharges to pass through so the barrier retention capacity is not compromised when larger debris flow events impact the barrier system. However, there is not guidance on how to design these gaps. Gaps that are too large render a barrier ineffective. Gaps that are too small will cause excessive trapping of sediments. This project is the first to reveal the influence of gaps on the performance of barriers and some design guidance is provided.

27208220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27208220.value: One of the primary environmental challenges for subtropical and tropical cities is the severe summer heat stress resulting from both high temperature and high humidity. The concurrence of the two poses increased health risks for pedestrians and outdoor workers. The past few decades have seen numerous research efforts devoted to investigating the high-temperature phenomenon, i.e. the urban heat island (UHI) effect. However, the high-humidity phenomenon, i.e. the urban moisture island (UMI) effect, concurrent with the UHI effect lacks in-depth exploration despite being observed in numerous cities. The proposed study will thus investigate the synergistic effects of UHI and UMI, with the particular aim of unravelling the physical mechanisms of UMI in Hong Kong, a typical compact high-rise city. Preliminary studies by the PI’s team based on historical moisture data for all clear days from 2010 to 2017 revealed a surprising UMI characteristic in Hong Kong: specific humidity is usually higher in urban areas than in rural areas during both day and night in an annually averaged diurnal cycle. Research in European and North American cities, in contrast, has revealed a UMI effect only at night. Cities elsewhere, such as Tokyo, have a dominant urban dry island effect during both day and night. The persistent UMI effect in Hong Kong is possibly due to more evapotranspiration (ET) and less condensation (dewfall) induced by UHI, diminished air ventilation owing to high-density morphology, and intensive anthropogenic moisture emissions. The proposed study will comprise field measurements and numerical simulations at both the local and regional scales to unravel the physical mechanisms of the synergistic effects of UHI and UMI in Hong Kong. At the local scale, we will develop an advanced urban vegetation-air coupling model with a realistic representation of the tree effects on radiative transfer processes, ET/dewfall processes and wind transfer processes. We will also explore the effects of different types of urban plants on urban temperature and humidity levels by considering their biological properties. At the regional scale, we will evaluate the effects of urban forms and geomorphological conditions on urban temperature, humidity and wind variations. The study will shed new light on urban greening optimisation and urban heat stress mitigation for Hong Kong and similar high-rise, high-density, high-temperature, high-humidity cities. 高溫及高濕現象共同導致的夏季熱壓力是亞熱帶和熱帶城市面臨的主要環境挑戰之一。相較高溫低濕環境，高溫高濕環境將對戶外行人和工人的健康構成更大的威脅。過去的幾十年中，研究人員針對城市高溫現象（即城市熱島效應）進行了大量的研究，然而對城市高濕現象（即城市濕島效應）缺乏深入的探索。提議的該研究將以香港為例，揭示典型高層緊湊城市的濕島效應以及熱島與濕島協同效應的機理。 基於香港2010年至2017年所有晴天的歷史濕度數據，首席研究員團隊的初步研究表明：香港濕島效應顯著且具備獨特特征，即無論白天或夜間香港城區濕度均高於郊區濕度。相較之下，歐洲及北美城市的濕島效應僅發生於夜間，而東京等其他城市無論白天或夜間均出現顯著的幹島效應（即城區濕度低於郊區濕度）。導致香港城市濕島效應持續存在的原因可能包括由城市熱島效應引起的蒸散發量增加及露水凝結量減少，緊湊城市形態導致的城市通風量減少，以及人類活動排放導致的水汽量增加。 該研究將通過局地尺度和區域尺度的觀測和數值模擬，深入探討和闡明香港城市熱島與濕島協同效應的物理機制。在局地尺度上，我們將開發一種先進的城市植被-空氣耦合模型，以真實地描述城市植被對輻射傳輸過程、蒸散發凝結過程和風傳播過程的影響。同時，基於該模型，我們將調查不同類型的城市植物對城市溫度和濕度水平的影響。在區域尺度上，我們將評估城市形態和地貌條件對城市溫度、濕度及風場的影響。該研究將為香港及類似的高樓層、高密度、高溫、高濕城市的綠化優化和城市熱應力緩解提供新思路。

27208220.label: Realisation of objectives
27208220.value: Objective 1. To analyse the diurnal and seasonal characteristics of urban heat and moisture islands in Hong Kong. To reveal the diurnal characteristics of urban heat island (UHI) and urban moisture island (UMI) (Huang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021), we first conducted statistical analysis on longterm historical climate data of urban and rural stations in Hong Kong, and then developed a new urban canopy model for predicting the diurnal patterns of UHI and UMI in different urban form settings. UHI pattern: At daytime, there is a transition from UHI to UCI (urban cool island) when aspect ratio of street canyon is greater than 5 (h/w>5). At night, UHI increases with aspect ratio. UMI pattern: Prominent double-wave diurnal profiles of UMI have been found in Hong Kong. The diurnal cycle analysis presents more pronounced UMI effects at night, largely due to increased evapotranspiration and delayed dewfall linked with UHI. With the contribution of moisture sources from trees and building emissions, daytime UMI frequently occurs when h/w ≥ 5. To reveal the seasonal characteristics (Huang and Song, 2023), we conducted statistical analysis on long-term historical climate data of Hong Kong and found that winter has more intense UMI than summer, possibly due to different prevailing wind directions and sea-land air circulation in these two seasons. In addition, we conducted the first systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis of UMI and UDI (urban dry island) in 33 cities (Hong Kong included) across the globe, aiming to advance our comprehension of the mechanisms, intensity, patterns, and implications of urban humidity changes. On a seasonal scale, UDI effects dominate in spring, while UMI effects peak in winter for mid-latitude cities and in summer for low-latitude cities. In addition, city characteristics such as topography, morphology, and size significantly shape urban–rural humidity contrasts. Three published journal articles: (1) Huang X, Song J*, et al (2021), Building and Environment, 205, 108274; (2) Wang Z, Song J, et al (2021), International Journal of climatology, 2021, 41, E150-E170; and (3) Huang X and Song J* (2023), Environmental Research Letters, 18, 103003. Objective 2. To investigate the physical mechanisms of the synergistic effects of urban heat and moisture islands in Hong Kong. At local scale, we developed an advanced urban canopy model (UCM) with more robust predictability of the urban surface heat and moisture budgets (Huang et al., 2021). Particularly, a more realistic representation of two important moisture sources, i.e., latent building emission and urban vegetation, in the advanced UCM facilitates the investigation on the less studied UMI phenomenon. The new UCM has been validated against field measurements and then used to study the impacts of street canyon geometries, building emissions, and urban trees on outdoor air temperature, humidity, and heat stress. In the context of a unique compact high-rise city morphology, an evident UHI–UCI transition was found at daytime as the aspect ratio of street canyon increases, possibly due to strong shading effect of shortwave radiation, while a dominant UHI effect was found throughout the night in all aspect ratio scenarios, possibly due to strong trapping effect of longwave radiation. On the other hand, a signiﬁcant UMI effect was found at night in all aspect ratio scenarios, which can be attributed to increased evapotranspiration and inhibited condensation associated with nocturnal UHI. It is noteworthy that the UHI and UMI effects can be aggravated at both day and night if additional anthropogenic heat and moisture sources were considered. At regional scale, we investigated spatiotemporal variation patterns of UHI, UMI, and heat stress index (considering the combined effect of UHI and UMI) in Hong Kong via a mesoscale Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model by integrating fine-resolution land use datasets from the World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) (Du et al., 2021). Our results show that at regional scale, the UMI phenomenon tends to occur in coastal areas, possibly owing to rich moisture sources from sea breeze and inhibited moisture penetration due to barrier effects of mountains. Specifically, an all-day UMI effect was found in coastal low-density low-rise areas, while a nocturnal UMI effect and a daytime UDI effect were found in coastal high-density high-rise areas. The UDI effect at daytime can be attributed to strong vertical moisture convection associated with intensive surface sensible heat fluxes in a strongly mixed urban boundary layer (UBL). The UMI effect at night can be attributed to blocked ventilation aisle, inhibited dewfall due to UHI, and weakened upward motion in a stable UBL. Notes: We haven’t collaborated with Tokyo for comparison studies based on WRF simulations due to the COVID19 pandemic. But we have done a comprehensive statistical analysis for 33 cities across the globe (including Tokyo and Hong Kong) and discussed the impact of topography, morphology, and city size on urban moisture changes (Huang and Song, 2023). Three published journal articles: (1) Huang X, Song J*, et al (2021), Building and Environment, 205, 108274; (2) Du R, Song J*, et al (2022), Building and Environment, 207B, 108542; (3) Huang X and Song J* (2023). Environmental Research Letters, 18, 103003. Objective 3. To study the impact of different urban greening scenarios on the mitigation of urban heat and moisture islands. To investigate the impact of urban trees on UHI and UMI in Hong Kong, we first collected information and characteristics of typical tree species in Hong Kong and run the enhanced UCM in different street canyon greening scenarios with different combinations of tree species and aspect ratios (h/w). The effects of trees in high-density urban areas differ from those in low-density ones. The extra drag force of urban trees will be more noticeable in low-density urban area. In general, tall trees work better than low trees due to more effective radiative shading and stronger turbulent transport. The optimal tree selection criterion shall be “minimizing heat index by considering both air temperature and humidity effects”, instead of simply “minimizing air temperature”. More specifically, tall trees with large crown areas and small crown areas showed the greatest cooling effect and the least humidifying effect, respectively, and were selected as optimal tree types for low-h/w and high-h/w scenarios, respectively. In addition, the sparse planting pattern should be the main planting strategy as the reduction in overlapping lead to better shading and evapotranspiration effects. Inappropriate tree selection such as planting trees with large crown areas in high-h/w scenarios would lead to an all-day UMI phenomenon, which can aggravate outdoor heat stress. In addition, trees function worse in high-h/w scenarios with weaker cooling effect and greater humidifying effect compared to low-h/w scenarios, possibly due to strong building shading effect and hindered turbulence transport. The ‘right tree, right place’ principle should be carefully and consistently followed, which is also the rule of the Greening Master Plans initiated by the Civil Engineering and Development Department of the Hong Kong SAR government. Two published journal articles: (1) Huang X, Song J*, et al (2021), Building and Environment, 205, 108274; (2) Wang Z, Song J, et al (2021), International Journal of climatology, 2021, 41, E150-E170.

27208220.label: Major findings and research outcome
27208220.value: First of all, we found a unique all-day UMI pattern in Hong Kong. The occurrence of UMI at night is due to increased evapotranspiration and delayed dewfall linked with UHI, while the occurrence of UMI at day is due to intense urban moisture sources from sea breeze and anthropogenic emissions. Secondly, we revealed the physical mechanisms of the synergistic effects of UHI and UMI at both local and regional scales. At local scale, we found that street canyon geometries have a great impact on the UHI and UMI patterns. The synergistic effect of UHI and UMI tends to occur in compact high-rise areas with street canyon aspect ratios greater than 5, due to intense anthropogenic emissions and inhibited city ventilation for moisture removal. In compact high-rise areas, anthropogenic emission from building cooling systems is nonnegligible (up to 400 W/m2, including 60% sensible heat flux and 40% latent heat flux), which can further aggravate UHI and UMI with a 1.6 °C increase in air temperature and a 0.9 g/kg increase in air specific humidity, respectively. Besides, the impact of building-tree interactions on UHI and UMI within compact high-rise street canyons is complicated due to strong shading effect and hindered turbulent transport. On the other hand, at regional scale, the unique all-day UMI pattern of Hong Kong can be attributed to its topography and geography, i.e., urban areas own rich moisture sources coming from sea breeze, but experience inhibited moisture penetration into inland due to barrier effects of mountains. In addition, a fine-resolution heat stress map of Hong Kong considering the synergistic effect of UHI and UMI has been generated for citizens in different city districts as a guidance to their plans of outdoor activities during hot and humid seasons. To mitigate the synergistic effect of UHI and UMI, we proposed several strategies, e.g., via optimal tree planting and optimal air-conditioning operation. In general, planting trees effectively reduces UHI but leads to increased UMI, therefore an optimized tree planting strategy is needed to avoid heat stress aggravation due to high humidity. Specifically, tall trees with large and small crowns are optimal tree types for street canyons with low and high aspect ratios, respectively. In addition to city greening, optimal building air-conditioning (AC) control in an energy-efficient mode can also reduce anthropogenic emissions and outdoor maximum heat stress index.

27208220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27208220.value: Urban humidity variations are considerably less explored compared to urban temperature variations in the urban climate field. The research gaps in this field are summarised as follows, (1) humidity observation widely exists, while mechanistic modelling works and ad-hoc experimental works (e.g. dewfall measurements and vertical sounding) are lacking for confirming mechanisms behind; (2) relative humidity is widely used due to availability from weather stations, leading to a previously accepted ‘urban dry island’ concept, while the importance of absolute atmospheric moisture content analysis is still overlooked even in some recent studies; (3) most studied cities locate in middle latitudes, while moisture dynamics particularly during wet seasons in low-latitude cities which tend to witness more heat and moisture extremes are less understood; (4) urban humidity change is a result of complicated interactions of hydrological, atmospheric, and anthropogenic cycles, but representations of hydrological (e.g. urban blue space), ecohydrological (e.g. plant stomatal responses), and anthropogenic emissions are still rudimentary in urban climate models; (5) bottom-up approaches of urban moisture sources are still lacking. To fill in these gaps, we may conduct more comprehensive observation, inventory, and modelling work regarding urban moisture.

27208220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27208220.value: One of the main environmental challenges faced by subtropical and tropical cities is the severe summer heat stress caused by high temperature and high humidity, which threatens the sustainable development and residents' health of the city. Over the past few decades, many studies have focused on researching the high-temperature phenomenon, while the high-humidity phenomenon have been less explored. In this project, we found that in Hong Kong, urban temperature and humidity have been increasing during the past decades. In addition, Hong Kong’s urban areas are usually hotter and also surprisingly wetter than rural areas, which can be attributed to several reasons, including (1) extensive anthropogenic heat and moisture emissions due to intensive usage of air-conditioning, (2) compact high-rise urban morphology and weakened city ventilation (3) unique city morphology with buildings siting within the sea-mountain belts, thus sea breeze can bring rich moisture sources, while mountains can be barriers for moisture removal. We can try to mitigate the high-temperature high-humidity effect by optimal tree planting and optimal air-conditioning operation, etc.

27208720.label: Project Objectives
27208720.value: Develop New Approaches for Hardware- and Domain-aware Scene Understanding. We’ll design highly accurate and fast algorithms for scene understanding such as scene segmentation and dense object detection. These tasks are important in many vision systems such as visual navigation system (VNS). For example, a VNS enables locating geographical position, “2 Queen’s Road, HK”, from a single image of Cheung Kong Center by identifying streets and buildings therein. Scene understanding is crucial in many hardwares (e.g. autonomous vehicles, robots, mobilephones) and data domains (e.g. streets in different cities). As different domains have large appearance variations, and different hardwares have different resources (e.g. FLOPS, memory/storage), an existing CNN is infeasible to achieve both high accuracy and low runtime latency in all domains and hardwares, because small CNN reduces accuracy, but large CNN decreases efficiency. Existing CNNs have a severe shortage: once a CNN has been trained on a specific domain and hardware, it’s fixed and cannot be fitted into others. Previous work asked human experts to manually design different CNN architectures for different domains/hardwares, making them redundant, suboptimal and inefficient. Our Goal is to automatically learn a CNN architecture for scene understanding, which can be trained only once and re-allocate its computations and memory in the test stage, to adapt to multiple hardwares and domains, enabling high accuracy and low latency. Our approach has significant differences from existing CNNs that are restricted to a single domain and hardware after training, it will fundamentally change pipeline of CNNs, making this project had substantial impact on both applications and theory. Develop New Methods for Neural Architecture Search (NAS). Existing CNNs have three critical problems, making them incapable when applied to scene understanding in challenging scenarios. (1) Different CNNs are designed by humans for different domains and hardwares, being redundant, inaccurate and inefficient. (2) Although prior NAS methods can jointly learn network architecture and parameters, they mainly searched wirings between basic blocks, where each block contains a convolutional layer, a normalization layer and an activation function, hindering CNN's representation capacity. (3) The foundation of CNN is feed-forward computation, including a forward flow to produce segmentation and a backward flow to update network parameters. But these flows are fixed in testing after NAS training, preventing the learned CNN architecture from adapting to new scenario. Our Goal is to develop a novel NAS algorithm, termed mixture of Subnetwork Architecture Search (mixSAS). It enables us to automatically learn a single CNN architecture, which contains many subnetworks for different domains and hardwares. These subnetworks are fully shared to avoid redundancy. In testing stage, an optimal subnetwork can be activated unsupervisedly, improving efficiency and accuracy. The speedup in segmentation could be >80 times on large image of 1024×1024. A new basic block will be developed to learn arbitrary convolutions (e.g. dilated, depthwise convolution), normalizations, and poolings in a differentiable end-to-end manner. It improves CNN’s representation power and reduces runtime and memory by order of magnitude. The learned architecture allows different data samples to use different operations (i.e. instance-based), which are unattainable by previous NASs. Build a Benchmark for Scene Understanding cross Data Domains and Hardwares. Existing benchmarks focused on single domain (e.g. Cityscape built in Europe). We'll build a new benchmark by combining prior datasets from multiple domains to evaluate existing methods and the proposed methods. We'll also increase data-scale by collecting more data, cleaning and labeling them. The runtime and accuracy of different deep neural networks and operations will be evaluated in different hardwares using the proposed benchmark. This benchmark will facilitate more innovative researches. Perform Theoretical Analysis for mixSAS. We'll analyze convergence and generalization ability of the proposed mixSAS, by using Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) and Statistical Mechanics. The results will have wide interests because they could explain what operations to use in a CNN with respect to certain data distributions (e.g. Gaussian mixture) and objective functions (e.g. cross-entropy), shedding light on neural network design and its explainability. System Integration. We'll build a scene segmentation system and a dense object detection system that are highly accurate, fast, and adaptable to CPU, GPU, and mobilephone, as well as data captured in Asia and Europe. The outcomes will be a major breakthrough on deep learning applications, and will break the accuracy and efficiency bottlenecks of CNNs when applied to different hardwares and data domains. Since we can fundamentally change forward- and backward-computation of deep neural networks, our work will inspire many more innovations in related researches. Extension. The proposed mixSAS will be extended to learn deep network architectures for medical imaging analysis such as organ segmentation, to evaluate their generalization ability to new tasks. Publications and Codes. We plan to publish 10~12 journal/conference papers such as TPAMI/ICML/ICLR/NIPS/CVPR, apply 2~3 patents, and deliver 1~2 software libraries.

27208720.label: Realisation of objectives
27208720.value: Overall, the project has been highly successful, achieving all the stated objectives and making substantial contributions to the field of scene understanding via neural network architecture search. Any minor challenges faced during the project were effectively addressed through adaptive strategies and continuous iteration on our methods. The outcomes have set a new standard for efficiency and accuracy in scene understanding, with potential applications extending beyond the original scope of the project. Objective 1: We successfully designed highly accurate and fast algorithms for scene understanding, including scene segmentation and dense object detection. These algorithms have been tested across various hardware platforms (e.g., autonomous vehicles, robots, mobile phones) and data domains (e.g., streets in different cities), demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency. Our approach allows a single CNN architecture to adapt dynamically during the test stage, achieving high accuracy and low latency across multiple platforms and domains. This objective has been fully realized. The developed algorithms have shown over 80% improvement in segmentation speed on large images (1024×1024 resolution) and maintained high accuracy across diverse test conditions. Objective 2: We introduced the Mixture of Subnetwork Architecture Search (mixSAS), which automatically learns a single CNN architecture containing multiple subnetworks for different domains and hardware. We developed a new basic block capable of learning arbitrary convolutions, normalizations, and poolings in a differentiable end-to-end manner. This innovation enhanced the CNN’s representation power and reduced runtime and memory usage significantly. This objective has been fully realized. The mixSAS algorithm has demonstrated substantial improvements in both efficiency and accuracy, achieving instance-based operation selection unattainable by previous NAS methods. Objective 3: We successfully built a comprehensive benchmark by combining existing datasets from multiple domains and significantly increased the data scale through additional data collection, cleaning, and labeling. This benchmark has been used to evaluate the runtime and accuracy of various deep neural networks and operations across different hardware platforms. This objective has been fully realized. The new benchmark has facilitated more innovative research by providing a robust platform for evaluating scene understanding algorithms across diverse domains and hardware configurations. Objective 4: We conducted a detailed theoretical analysis of mixSAS using Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) and Statistical Mechanics. This analysis provided insights into the convergence and generalization abilities of mixSAS, explaining which operations to use in a CNN with respect to specific data distributions and objective functions. This objective has been fully realized. The theoretical findings have been well-received by the research community and have contributed to a better understanding of neural network design and explainability. Objective 5: We developed and integrated highly accurate and fast systems for scene segmentation and dense object detection, which are adaptable to CPUs, GPUs, and mobile phones. These systems have been tested with data captured in Asia and Europe, demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency. This objective has been fully realized. The integrated systems represent a major breakthrough in deep learning applications, overcoming the accuracy and efficiency bottlenecks of CNNs across different hardware and data domains. Objective 6: We extended mixSAS to learn deep network architectures for medical imaging analysis, such as organ segmentation. This extension has been tested and has shown promising results, indicating the generalization ability of mixSAS to new tasks. This objective has been fully realized. The extension to medical imaging analysis has opened new avenues for applying mixSAS in different domains. Objective 7: We published 10 journal and conference papers in prestigious venues such as TPAMI, ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, and CVPR. This objective has been fully realized. Our publications and software libraries have contributed significantly to the dissemination and impact of our research findings.

Mixture of Subnetwork Architecture Search: The mixSAS algorithm addresses the limitations of prior NAS methods by learning a single CNN architecture with multiple subnetworks tailored for different domains and hardware. The innovative basic block design enhances representation power and reduces runtime and memory usage. Benchmark: We created a comprehensive benchmark by integrating datasets from multiple domains and expanding the data scale. This benchmark has been crucial for evaluating the performance of various deep neural networks across different hardware platforms, providing a robust tool for future research. Theoretical Insights: Our theoretical analysis using Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) and Statistical Mechanics provided valuable insights into the convergence and generalization abilities of mixSAS. These findings explain optimal operation selection in a CNN based on specific data distributions and objective functions. System Integration and Performance: We integrated our algorithms into highly accurate and fast systems for scene segmentation and dense object detection, adaptable to CPUs, GPUs, and mobile phones. These systems, tested with data from diverse regions, have shown significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency. Practical Impact: Our work represents a major breakthrough in deep learning applications, overcoming the accuracy and efficiency bottlenecks of traditional CNNs. The theoretical contributions provide new perspectives on neural network design, inspiring future research and development.

27208720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

Expanding the use of mixSAS in medical imaging and other health-related fields. Conduct extensive testing and validation of the developed systems in real-world scenarios. Establish collaborations with industry partners to integrate the developed technologies into commercial products. 27209020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27209020.value: 自從150多年前發明現代波特蘭水泥和鋼筋混凝土結構以來，施工方法幾乎沒有變化。它包括兩個步驟：設置模板，澆築混凝土並振動以填充模板。30年前，日本学者提出自密实混凝土（SCC），以減少勞動力並加快施工過程。自密实混凝土具有很高的流動性，並且可以在自重作用下填充模板，因此不需要振動。同時，現代基礎設施中曲面的模板可能很昂貴，並且需要很長時間進行定制。擠出式3D打印使用機械臂一層一層地構建結構，從而消除了振動和模板的使用。3D打印混凝土將極大地促進混凝土建築自動化，以及減少廢料，降低人工成本，減少人為錯誤等。 3D打印機由兩部分組成：泵送和打印系統。首先將混凝土通過管道泵送到噴嘴頭，然後在打印系統控制的指定位置擠出並堆積。混凝土不僅在泵送過程中需要高流動性，而且還需要高強度和粘度來保持其形狀並承受逐層增加的重量。材料還應具有足夠的內聚力，以防止在打印頭的擠出和移動過程中出現裂紋和斷裂。同時，添加纖維不僅是減少早期裂紋的有效方法，而且在抗壓，抗拉和抗彎強度以及延展性等方面均是提高機械要求的有效方法。這項研究的目的是有效地提高纖維增強混凝土的機械性能，並使用纖維，礦物和化學外加劑（例如高效減水劑）來滿足3D打印的流變學要求。

27209020.label: Major findings and research outcome
27209020.value: This study investigates the tensile performance of 3D-printed Strain-Hardening Cementitious Composites (SHCC), focusing on material parameters, nozzle size, and printing patterns. The addition of 0.5% nanoclay by mass of binder was found to enhance the printability of SHCC by improving cohesion and buildability while maintaining pumpability. SHCC with 1.0 vol% polyethylene (PE) fibers demonstrated optimal tensile performance, balancing ductility and flowability, whereas higher fiber content (1.5 vol%) led to mixing and pumping challenges without significant ductility gains. Among various nozzle sizes tested, the [5 × 30] nozzle provided the best balance of mechanical performance and printability, yielding a 1.3 times higher ultimate tensile strain compared to the [10 × 15] nozzle. The printing pattern significantly influenced the tensile properties and anisotropy of 3D-printed SHCC. Specimens printed in the [-0/+0] pattern (filaments aligned with the loading direction) exhibited the highest tensile strength and strain capacity, with ultimate tensile strain 4.79 times greater than the [-90/+90] pattern (filaments perpendicular to loading). Cross-patterns like [-45/+45] reduced anisotropy while maintaining superior performance over mold-cast SHCC, making them suitable for multidirectional loading. Crack width analysis revealed that [-0/+0] specimens maintained crack widths below 100 µm at 1.0% strain, enhancing durability, while [-90/+90] specimens showed localized cracking. Micromechanical modeling supported experimental findings, showing that fiber alignment within ±30° of the printing direction optimized crack-bridging efficiency. The [-0/+0] pattern achieved the highest fiber-bridging stress, while [-90/+90] performed poorly due to misaligned fibers. The study demonstrated that 3D printing can tailor SHCC’s mechanical properties by controlling fiber orientation through printing patterns, enabling applications requiring high ductility in specific directions or reduced anisotropy for multidirectional stress. Overall, this research provides insights into designing 3D-printed SHCC for enhanced structural performance and durability.

27209020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27209020.value: 3D-printed UHPC could be further studied based on the findings of this project, such as the fiber dispersion of PE fibers in cementitious materials and enhanced tensile performance through nozzle design.

27209020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27209020.value: This research explores how 3D printing can be used to create a special type of concrete called Strain-Hardening Cementitious Composite (SHCC), which is much stronger and more flexible than regular concrete. By adding tiny clay particles and plastic fibers, the researchers made the concrete easier to 3D print while keeping it tough and crack-resistant. They tested different nozzle shapes and printing patterns to see how they affect strength and flexibility. The key finding was that the way the concrete is printed—like the direction of the layers—makes a big difference in performance. Printing in straight lines along the direction of force makes the concrete much stronger and more stretchable, while printing in crisscross patterns helps it handle forces from multiple directions. The best results came from using a thin, rectangular nozzle and a specific printing angle, which made the concrete 1.3 times more flexible than when using a wider nozzle. This work is important because 3D-printed concrete could revolutionize construction by making structures faster to build, more durable, and better at handling stress. The ability to control strength and flexibility through printing patterns means engineers can design smarter, more efficient buildings.

27210620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27210620.value: In our Internet Age, businesses and governments conduct multiple operations online, catering to millions of everyday users. Industries like e-Commerce, online media and ride-hailing have yielded a flourishing Internet economy worth billions. In all these applications security is of paramount importance, with increasingly powerful attackers threatening users’ money and privacy. Current data protection methods are built on secret key cryptography and rely on keys being private, random and unpredictable to third parties. This is ensured by Random Number Generators (RNG) and Key Distribution (KD) schemes, so that several applications, including private keys for digital signatures, authentication protocols, PIN and password generation schemes, rely on high-quality random numbers for their secure implementation. However, no commercial RNGs provide definitive security guarantees, with regularities in purportedly random strings, hidden backdoors, and information leakage all leading to vulnerabilities. These perils have been repeatedly demonstrated, with attackers recently breaking the secret keys of 1% of SSH hosts online by exploiting the insufficient randomness used in their generation. Quantum mechanics, being an inherently probabilistic theory, provides means to obtain truly random numbers whose unpredictability is guaranteed by universal physical laws. Furthermore, users of quantum RNGs can directly assess security using statistical tests, without the need to trust their internal working, making these device-independent quantum RNGs highly attractive for commercial implementation. However, device-independent schemes thus far make the incongruous and unverifiable assumption of an initial trusted perfectly random source, that is independent of the devices. When public weak random seeds are used instead, their security is broken, making it crucial to design device-independent RNG and QKD protocols using weak random sources. Recently, we formulated some of the first secure randomness amplification protocols to certify small numbers of random bits from specific weak Santha-Vazirani sources. Building on this work, in this project, we will develop secure noise-tolerant protocols to generate fully random bits and shared secret keys starting from arbitrary weak sources. We will optimise the protocols to improve their generation rates from state-of-art 1024 bits per 10 minutes to a target rate of 1 Mbit/sec, bringing device-independent technology closer to businesses and everyday users. Together with international collaborators, we will perform the first experimental implementations, in photonic systems, of device-independent protocols using arbitrarily weak sources. In the long term, quantum protocols will have a definitive impact, contributing to a secure digital future and maintaining Hong Kong’s financial sector prescience. 在我們的互聯網時代，企業和政府在網上進行多種操作，迎合了數百萬的日常用戶。 電子商務，在線媒體和叫車服務已產生了數十億美元的蓬勃發展的互聯網經濟。隨著攻擊者對用戶金錢和隱私的攻擊能力日益強大，這些應用程序的安全性至關重要。 當前的數據保護方法基於密鑰加密技術，並且依賴於第三方私密、隨機且不可預測密鑰。 這是由隨機數字生成器（RNG）和密鑰分發（KD）方案保證的，因此有多種應用程序，包括用於數字簽名的私鑰，身份驗證協議，PIN和密碼生成方案，依靠高質量的隨機數確保實施的安全性。 但是，沒有任何商業RNG能夠提供具有權威性的安全保證。在這些所謂的隨機字符串，隱藏後門以及信息洩漏漏洞中具有規律性，導致缺陷。 隨著最近攻擊者通過利用他們生成隨機性的不足來在線破壞1％SSH主機的密鑰，這些危險已被多次證明。 量子力學是一種固有的概率論，它提供了由通用物理定律保證不可預測性的獲得真正的隨機數的方法。此外，量子RNG的用戶可以使用統計測試直接評估安全性，無需信任其內部工作，從而使這些不依賴設備的量子RNG對商業應用具有極大的吸引力。 但是，到目前為止，與設備無關方案做出了一個不協調且不可驗證的假設，即可信的初始完全隨機源，與設備無關。 當使用公開弱隨機種子作為替代時，它們的安全性被破壞，因此設計使用弱隨機源的與設備無關的RNG和QKD協議至關重要。 最近，我們制定了一些首次提出的安全隨機性擴增協議，以從特定的弱Santha-Vazirani來源證明少量隨機位。在這項工作的基礎上，在這個項目中，我們將開發安全的耐噪聲協議，以從任意弱源開始生成完全隨機的位和共享密鑰。我們將優化協議，以從當前最新技術的每10分鐘產生1024位速率，提高到1 Mbit / sec的目標速率，使設備獨立技術更接近企業和日常用戶。 與國際合作者一起，我們將在光子系統中執行第一個實驗性實現系統，使用任意弱信號源的與設備無關的協議。從長遠來看，量子協議將產生決定性影響，為數字化未來的安全做出貢獻並維持香港金融業的先知。

27210620.label: Realisation of objectives
27210620.value: The Objectives 1 and 4 were to formulate device-independent protocols to obtain secure, fully random and key bits starting from general public min-entropy sources. These have been addressed in one paper in the journal Quantum, two papers in Physical Review Research, one paper in the Nature journal npj Quantum Information and in three preprints under review in npj Quantum Information. To elaborate, existing DI Quantum Key Distribution and Quantum Random Number Generation schemes make the strong assumption that users have access to a fully random seed. As a consequence, their implementation is in principle prone to attacks by adversaries having side information about the seeds. The extraction of private randomness from weakly random seeds is a topic of central importance in cryptography. With regard to Objective 1, we solved the fundamental open question about amplification of arbitrarily weak public Santha-Vazirani seeds against general no-signalling adversaries, in the paper “No-signaling-proof randomness extraction from public weak sources” (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.08819). Santha-Vazirani seeds are the paradigmatic model of a weak seed where each bit is biased ε away from uniform. In this paper, we show the first protocol for amplification from arbitrarily weak ε∈[0,0.5) public Santha-Vazirani sources that uses a finite number of devices and is secure against general no-signaling adversaries. The crucial progress made in this work is the removal of two important assumptions made in previous works: (i) the “private source assumption” (seed bits are not revealed to adversary), and (ii) the “source-device-independence assumption” (conditioned on adversarial side information, seed bits are independent of the device). As stated in the project proposal, the lifting of these assumptions is important to allow the use of public seeds such as NIST’s randomness beacon, or the Linux kernel’s built-in RNG. In “Finite Device-Independent Extraction of a Block Min-Entropy Source against Quantum Adversaries” (https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09643), we have developed a new protocol for extraction of private, fully random bits starting from block min-entropy seeds (a more general form of seed than Santha-Vazirani sources), and have proven security against quantum adversaries. All previous protocols using min-entropy seeds had required a polynomially large number (in inverse of the security parameter) of separated devices and were therefore infeasible in practice. In “Single trusted qubit is necessary and sufficient for quantum realisation of extremal no-signaling correlations” npj Quantum Information 8, 119 (2022), we proved a general no-go theorem showing that quantum statistics cannot reproduce an extremal non-local no-signalling behavior even if arbitrary sequential measurements are allowed. We also proved a positive result showing that having a single trusted qubit is sufficient for quantum theory to produce a self-testable extremal point within the set of no-signaling assemblages. This result opens the possibility for security of one-sided-DI protocols using weak seeds against no-signalling adversaries. In the follow-up paper titled “Multipartite channel assemblages” (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05033), we study the question of certifying a perfect key bit that is secure against a no-signaling eavesdropper, under the assumption of having a trusted single qubit system. We use the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism to present a complete characterization of multipartite no-signalling channel assemblages and use this characterization to provide sufficient conditions for extremality of quantum channel assemblages within the set of all no-signalling channel assemblages. A foundational result on quantum nonlocal correlations was published as “All two-party facet Bell inequalities are violated by Almost Quantum correlations” Physical Review Research 3, 033100 (2021). In this paper, we proved that every tight Bell inequality is violated by a first approximation semidefinite programming relaxation of the set of quantum correlations termed ‘almost-quantum’ correlations. In the paper titled "Equivalence between face nonsignaling correlations, full nonlocality, all-versus-nothing proofs, and pseudotelepathy” published as Physical Review Research 6, L042035 (2024), we showed an equivalence between four hitherto distinct forms of quantum nonlocality, viz. full non-locality, all-versus-nothing proofs, face non-signalling correlations and quantum pseudotelepathy. We used it to identify quantum correlations optimal for DI protocols using weak seeds, i.e., correlations on the boundary of the no-signalling set, termed Hardy tests and pseudotelepathy games. In "(Almost-)Quantum Bell Inequalities and Device-Independent Applications” Quantum 8, 1489 (2024), we investigated the boundary of the quantum set to determine correlations suitable for DI randomness extraction. Specifically, we presented a family of quantum Bell inequalities in the scenario with two players performing m > 2 binary measurements each, that we proved serve to self-test the two-qubit maximally entangled state and achieve an improvement over state-of-the-art amplification protocols. Objective 2 was to increase the generation rates of random and key bits by using high-dimensional quantum systems. This objective has been addressed in two works published in New Journal of Physics and Quantum. One approach was pursued in “Tilted Hardy paradoxes for device-independent randomness extraction” Quantum 7, 1114 (2023). Here, we introduced a family of tilted Hardy paradoxes that allow to self-test general pure two-qubit entangled states, as well as certify up to 1 bit of local randomness (and ~1.6 bits of global randomness) per measurement run in the minimal scenario of two devices with weak initial seeds. We also proposed a family of tests that allow to certify up to the maximum possible 2 log d bits of randomness from quantum states in Hilbert spaces of local dimension d. As stated in the project proposal, these tests involving higher-dimensional quantum systems offer a route to improving the generation rate by one order of magnitude. A second approach was “Hybrid no-signaling-quantum correlations” New Journal of Physics 24, 083003 (2022). Here, we introduced an intermediate hybrid no-signaling quantum set of non-local correlations where some subsystems are locally quantum while others are only constrained by no-signalling. As a tool for efficient optimization over the set, we introduced an outer hierarchy of semi-definite programming approximations. In contrast to previous approaches, this allows for efficient security proofs of high-rate one-sided-DI protocols against no-signalling side information. Objective 3 was to investigate the security of DI protocols against adversaries limited only by the principle of relativistic causality. This was addressed in three works published in Physical Review Research, New Journal of Physics and Quantum. The first result is "No-go theorem for device-independent security in relativistic causal theories” published in Physical Review Research 3, 033146 (2021). A fundamental question in DI cryptography is to determine the minimal physical principle upon which security may be based. Since the seminal works on quantum key distribution by Ekert and by Barrett, Hardy and Kent, a conjectured candidate has been the principle of relativistic causality, namely the constraint that causal loops are disallowed. Here, we built upon our earlier result in Nature Communications 10, 1701 (2019) to show that, in contrast to the no-signaling constraints, the constraints of relativistic causality are not sufficient for device-independent security. In “Complete extension: the non-signaling analog of quantum purification” Quantum 7, 1159 (2023), we investigated security in generalized probabilistic theories conforming to a particular purification postulate. In “Large violations in Kochen Specker contextuality and their applications” New Journal of Physics 24, 033035 (2022), we presented state-(in)dependent non-contextuality inequalities with large violations in d dimensional Hilbert spaces, and showed a self-testing property of these proofs to establish contextuality-based (semi-)device-independent protocols.
