27210620.label: Major findings and research outcome
27210620.value: 1). One major research outcome in this project is the formulation of a device-independent protocol for randomness extraction from arbitrarily weak seeds of (i) Santha-Vazirani type and (ii) Block min-entropy type. The protocol for amplification of Block min-entropy seeds was proven to be secure against adversaries holding quantum memories, while the protocol for amplification of Santha-Vazirani seeds was proven to be secure even against general no-signalling adversaries. While the generation rates are still low compared to practical pseudo random number generators, these protocols are the state-of-art in device-independent amplification tasks. They also help remove one of the major assumptions in device-independent quantum key distribution, namely that the users possess a fully random seed. 2). A second major research outcome of this project concerns the question of identifying the optimal quantum correlations to use in device-independent protocols. In this regard, it is well-known that achieving extremal non-local no-signalling correlations would be highly desirable as these are automatically decoupled from any adversary. We proved that while such correlations are not quantumly realisable in nonlocality tests, they become realisable in steering tests under the minimal assumption that one party holds a trusted single qubit system. Fundamental advances were made in the study of the set of quantum correlations, including a breakthrough semialgebraic characterisation of the boundary generalising the Tsirelson-Landau-Masanes quantum Bell inequalities. These characterisations were used to identify self-testing quantum correlations allowing to certify the maximum value of 2log d bits of randomness using quantum systems of local Hilbert space dimension d. In this regard, we also solved Problem 28B from Krueger and Werner's famous list of "Open Problems in Quantum Information Science" https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0504166 (solution was published in Physical Review Research 3, 033100 (2021)). 3). A third major research outcome in this project was to establish the fundamental physical principle upon which security of device-independent protocols can be established. It was proven that in contrast to the no-signalling constraints, the constraints of relativistic causality (the principle disallowing any closed causal loops) are not sufficient for certification of device-independent security. Technical tools were developed to formulate DI security in generalized probabilistic theories conforming to a particular purification postulate termed the complete extension postulate.

27210620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27210620.value: While we have developed initial protocols for device-independent randomness amplification using weak seeds, several tasks remain to bring these protocols closer to everyday application. 1) The noise tolerance, key and randomness generation rates (in terms of kilobits per seconds and per ebit consumed) in randomness amplification protocols need to be further improved. Our protocol for block min-entropy sources still requires the use of a super-polynomial number of entangled pairs per output bit, while the requirement is linear for Santha-Vazirani sources. It would be important to develop techniques to handle arbitrary min-entropy sources using fewer resources, while at the same time admitting constant rate of noise. Improved protocols allowing for arbitrary correlations between weak seed and device, as well as incorporating information leakage between devices would be a major achievement. 2) The fundamental question of achieving no-signalling security in DI protocols incorporating noise tolerance is still open. Two questions need to be resolved: Firstly, how does the min-entropy in the raw outputs of a Bell test accumulate against no-signalling adversaries? (this is the analog of the famous Entropy Accumulation Theorem against quantum adversaries). Secondly, can existing no-go results forbidding super-polynomial privacy amplification against no-signalling adversaries in some Bell tests be circumvented?

27210620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27210620.value: Device-Independent Quantum Cryptography forms the gold standard of cryptography - achieving the highest standard of Information-Theoretic Security in protocols with the users not even required to trust the very devices executing the protocol. The major applications are Key Distribution and Random Number Generation - tasks that are fundamental for devices executing public and private-key cryptographic protocols in everyday life. The Device-Independent protocols that have been developed so far still required a few assumptions though - the major one being the assumption of a trusted fully random seed. In this project, we relaxed the assumption of a trusted fully random seed to that of a weak seed, technically termed a seed with some amount of min-entropy. We showed how to achieve device-independent randomness amplification using public weak seeds conforming to a Santha-Vazirani structure, and more generally using a block min-entropy source. Another major concern in device-independent protocols is the low generation rate - we identified optimal quantum correlations to increase the rate of certified random and key bits in device-independent protocols with weak seeds. We investigated the security of our protocols against adversaries holding quantum side information, as well as adversaries limited only by the fundamental principle of relativistic causality.

These experiments will directly answer the question: how crucial the pre-existence of carriers in HHG from insulator is. Together with our studies from semiconductor, we would be able to grasp the overall picture of carriers influence on HHG from solids. To quantify the contributions of pre-existing carriers as well as different kind of excitations on HHG from solids and thus to refine the theoretical developments taking into account the newly learned information. To improve the experimental conditions, using the knowledge gained from the pump-probe experiments, to achieve better HHG performance. Higher performance can be seen in either extension of the cut-off photon energy, or increasement of the HHG flux or a combination of both.

27300820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300820.value: Light-matter interaction is a fundamental pillar of physical sciences. Its fundamental principles underly enormous technological developments that power devices used in daily life. When the incident electric field strength is so high that the dipole interaction is equivalent or stronger than the Coulomb potential, there emerges strong field laser physics. As a result of strong field – matter interaction, photons are emitted in the form of multiple orders of the frequency of the incident electric field, which are called high-order harmonic generation (HHG). Most of initial studies of strong field physics and HHG have been performed in gases, due to their capability to endure strong field. Recently, careful experimental techniques allow one to study strong field physics and HHG in solids, which has been an active field of research. HHG in solids hold high promises for not only fundamental sciences (as an ultrafast probe of electronic dynamics) but also industrial applications (as a new source of extreme ultraviolet coherent radiation). Nevertheless, the main mechanisms involved in HHG from solids are topic of active discussion. One possible mechanism is the direct excitation of electron between different bands, namely interband excitation. Another possible mechanism is the scattering of the field-driven-motion of electronic wavepacket within a band, namely intraband excitation. For either mechanism, existing carriers in the bands play an important role in the emission of high-order harmonics. There has been experimental and theoretical work reporting studies of the photo-carrier doping on HHG from semiconductor. However, studies of the role of existing carriers on HHG from insulator remain out of reach, mostly due to technological challenges. In this proposal, taking advantage of our expertise in realizing HHG experiments in the extreme ultraviolet (XUV) regime, we will implement a pump (injecting the carriers to the conduction bands)-probe (using strong electric field to generate HHG photons) apparatus in order to investigate the role of existing carriers in HHG from insulator and semiconductor. Knowledge gained from this work would help: (i) identifying the significance of existing carriers in HHG from solids; (ii) shaping our understanding of the different contributions to HHG and help refining the theoretical developments; (iii) improving the experimental conditions that lead to better HHG performance. We anticipate that our work would potentially have a significant impact on the current active research of HHG from solids and additionally make it possible to develop industrial-grade, coherent XUV light source. 光與物質相互作用是物理學研究中的一個重要支柱，其基本原理被廣泛應用於我們日常生活的電子器件中。當入射光場極強，使其激發的偶極相互作用達到與庫侖相互作用同一量級甚至更強，此時便進入了強場激光物理的範疇。在強場與物質相互作用的過程中，大量頻率為入射光場頻率整數倍的光子輻射出來，產生名為“高次諧波產生（high-order harmonic generation, HHG）”的效應。 在初期對強場物理及高次諧波產生的研究中，考慮到介質承受住強光場而不被擊穿的能力，絕大多數研究者選擇以氣體為介質開展實驗和理論研究。近幾年來，得益於實驗技術的發展，以固體為介質研究其與強場相互作用的實驗研究不再是鏡花水月，這使得強場與固體相互作用的研究活躍了起來。對固體高次諧波產生的研究， 不僅可以實現對電子動力學的超快探測， 而且有望提供新一代極紫外相干光源，這為基礎科學領域和工業應用領域描繪了美好藍圖。然而，迄今為止固體高次諧波的產生機理仍然是迷霧重重，眾多研究者對此都有自己的見解，關於產生機理的理論模型層出不窮。其中，一個可能的解釋著眼於電子在不同能帶間直接躍遷過程：帶間躍遷；另外一個可能的解釋則考慮到能帶內電子波包在光場驅動下的碰撞散射：帶內激發。在這兩種解釋中，無論對於哪個解釋，毋庸置疑能帶上現存的載流子對高次諧波的產生都發揮了重要的作用。如今，雖然對於光載流子摻雜對半導體中高次諧波產生的貢獻已有相關的實驗和理論研究，但是受限於技術困難，絕緣體中現存的載流子對高次諧波產生貢獻的研究仍然停滯不前。在本項目中，我們將充分發揮實驗產生極紫外波段高次諧波輻射的專長，設計、實施一系列的泵浦（將載流子射入導帶）-探測（利用強電場產生高次諧波光子）實驗，探究絕緣體和半導體中現存的載流子對高次諧波產生的貢獻。通過本項目的研究，我們將能夠實現如下三點：1）明確現存的載流子在固體高次諧波產生中的重要性；2）在整合我們對不同來源對高次諧波產生的貢獻的理解基礎上，幫助改進相關的理論研究；3）優化實驗設計與條件，以期獲得更高質量的高次諧波輻射。我們希望我們的工作能對現有固體高次諧波相關研究做出重要貢獻，此外又更能推進工業級極紫外相干光源的發展。

27300820.label: Realisation of objectives
27300820.value: The first objective has been done: We fully constructed the apparatus. Our apparatus is capable of generating photon energy up to 70 eV, much higher than the threshold required in this project (9eV). The pump-probe scheme has been fully implemented with complete software control and recording. The second objective has been done: The experiments have been carried out. We can now routinely perform transient absorption spectroscopy with femtosecond resolution. Thanks to the high photon energy available, we can easily perform experiments from the visible range (a few eV) to 70 eV or higher. The third objective has been done: From the experiments we carried out, we learned the role of carriers in the respective bands and how they influence the generation of harmonics. The influence of the carriers on the dephasing time of the system is fully investigated as well. The fourth objective has been done: We have optimized the generation step significantly. We now have the most compact, yet very efficient HHG chamber, to the best of our knowledge. With our laser pulse energy and duration, what we can generated in terms of cut-off harmonics is state-of-the-art.

27300820.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300820.value: - By using a pump-probe apparatus involving intense laser pulses, the carrier-phonon scatterings can be observed. We can fully trigger and observe the coherent phonons in solids. Our technique is background-free and it is extremely sensitive, up to two or three orders of magnitude better than previously demonstrated techniques. These results are reported in our recently published Nature Photonics. - Using the 9eV as the probe, we can utilize it to trace the dynamics of the bandgap upon excitation of strong laser pulse. The results of these are reported in our recently published Optica.

27300820.value: When a very strong light is shined on a material, one of the reactions of the material will be in the form of the vibrations of the constituent atoms. By shining another light burst right after that, we can "see" the vibrational motion of the atoms. We demonstrated a novel way to observe the movement of the atoms in its native timescale.

27301120.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301120.value: Ammonia produced by the Haber-Bosch process can be converted into fertilizers to support the growing population. However, overfertilization has led to devastating impacts to the environment and public health. Excess nitrates in agricultural run-offs are toxic to aquatic organisms and cause dead zones in terrestrial systems. Water sources contaminated by nitrates potentially can result in human diseases such as blue baby syndrome and cancers. To mitigate the detrimental effect of nitrates, various physical, biological, and chemical pollutant remediation strategies have been introduced. However, these methods have their own limitations including costly post-treatment steps, limited pH and nitrate concentration ranges, and safety concerns regarding the operation conditions. Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) is an attractive alternative method to convert excess nitrates in waste-streams into benign N2 gas or value-added NH3. Despite decades of efforts, NO3RR still exhibits major impediments that prohibit NO3RR from becoming a widespread method for nitrate removal. These impediments include high catalyst cost, high activation barrier (overpotential), low activity (current density), and low selectivity (multiple deleterious side-products generated simultaneously). These impediments are difficult to overcome because (1) the factors affecting the catalyst performance are hard to be decoupled from each other and (2) NO3RR contains multiple intricate proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps. Taking Cu as an example, upon switching from acid to base, the overpotential decreases and the activity increases, yet the product selectivity shifts to generating NH2OH as the major product instead of NO and NH3. This Early Career proposal describes the development of new non-precious metal (NPM) molecular complexes as efficient NO3RR electrocatalysts through rational ligand designs and bio-inspired approaches to lower the overpotential. The catalyst with the lowest NO3RR overpotential will be incorporated into a hybrid bilayer membrane (HBM) electrode. A HBM construct consists of a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) of NO3RR electrocatalysts covered by lipid with proton carriers incorporated. This HBM electrochemical platform is tailored to control independently the four major aspects of PCET processes, which are the thermodynamics and kinetics of electron and proton transfers, respectively. In addition to lowering the activation barrier and cost by careful ligand design and choice of metal centres in a HBM construct, the NO3RR activity and product selectivity are envisaged to be optimized through tuning the HBM parameters individually. The unique mechanistic information gained not only can be applied to developing advanced catalysts for NO3RR but also other important PCET reactions found in energy conversion and environmental remediation processes. Haber-Bosch工藝產生的氨可以轉化為肥料並用於支撐不端增長的人口。但是，過度施肥對環境與公共衛生產生了嚴重的影響。帶有過量有毒硝酸鹽的農業廢水會污染並破壞海洋和土地生態系統。此外，硝酸鹽污染可使人致病，例如藍色嬰兒綜合徵和癌症。為了減少硝酸鹽對生態系統的危害，目前已經引入了多種物理、生物和化學的方法去治理。然而，這些方法有其自身的局限性，包括昂貴的後處理步驟、有限的酸堿度和硝酸鹽濃度範圍，以及有關操作的安全性問題。 電催化還原硝酸鹽反應（NO3RR）是一種具有吸引力，並可將廢物流中過量的硝酸鹽轉化為無害的氮氣或具有增值價值的氨。但是，儘管過去數十年的努力，NO3RR依舊存在的主要障礙，阻礙了NO3RR成為廣泛的硝酸鹽去除方法。這些障礙包括高催化劑成本，高過電位、低催化活性（低電流密度）和低選擇性（多種有害副產物同時生成）。這些障礙主要歸因於（1）影響催化劑性能的因素很難相互分離（2）NO3RR包含多個複雜的質子耦合電子轉移（PCET）步驟。以銅為例，從酸到鹼，過電位會降低且活性會增加，但產物選擇性會從NO和NH3轉變為以NH2OH為主要產物。 這項目擬提出通過合理的配體設計以及仿生的方法去構建新型非貴金屬（NPM）分子配合物作為高效的NO3RR電催化劑來降低過電位。擁有最低NO3RR過電位的催化劑將會作為混合雙層膜（HBM）電極。HBM的構造由載有電催化劑的自組裝層（SAM）組成並在其上覆蓋摻有質子載體的脂質層。此HBM 電催化平台可獨立控制PCET的四個參數，分別是電子轉移和質子轉移的熱力學和動力學。除了通過精心設計的配體和金屬活性中心來降低活化障礙和降低成本外，還可以通過單獨調整HBM參數來優化NO3RR活性和產物選擇性。這項研究成果不僅可以應用於NO3RR，還可以用於其他在能源轉化和環境修復過程中重要的PCET反應。

27301720.label: Project Objectives
27301720.value: The aim of this research program is to establish the structure-property relationships of azulene-embedded nanographenes and graphene nanoribbons (GNRs). The PI will address the trends in the band gaps and electronic structures caused by increasing the number of pentagon-heptagon pairs and in different topologies, i.e., the optical/electronic properties and closed-shell/open-shell characteristics, and explore the synthetic feasibility of nonalternant rings in extend π-conjugated systems, such as in GNRs. Moreover, the primary motivation of this work is to utilize the proposed nanographenes and GNRs in different electronic applications, such as organic transistors, nonlinear optics and spintronics, through collaborations with physicists and device engineers. To achieve this goal, the PI will fully exploit the knowledge and experience related to the solution-phase synthesis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) to fabricate nonalternant rings (e.g., pentagon-heptagon pairs) and the precise incorporation of these rings in graphene nanostructures – ranging from 0D nanographenes to extended 1D GNRs (Fig. 1, Part II Section 2(c)). To this end, the specific objectives are described in the following sections. Objective 1: Synthesis of closed-shell nanographenes with pentagon-heptagon pairs. The first objective is to synthesize structurally well-defined nanographene 1, containing one azulene unit, and novel circum-azulene 2 (Fig. 1), which will help elucidate the effects of different topologies on their structural and physical properties. The solution processability of these nonalternant nanographenes should allow the study of their optoelectronic properties in organic solvents, and the growth of single crystals of 1 and 2 will allow the determination of parameters such as bond length, aromaticity, and geometry. In addition to different topologies, the effect of the number of azulene units will also be investigated. As a lateral extension of this family, novel nanographene 3, containing two azulene units fused in a “head-to-head” manner, will be synthesized (Fig. 1). Moreover, as an important step towards the development of chemical strategies for the rational synthesis of nonhexagonal topologies, heptagon-pentagon-heptagon-embedded 4 will be produced (Fig. 1). Explorations of such ring transformations in nanographenes would be advantageous for controllably introducing nonhexagonal topologies in honeycomb lattices, allowing local modulation of physical and chemical properties. Objective 2: Synthesis of azulene-embedded nanographenes with open-shell biradical character. Compared to the closed-shell molecules discussed in objective 1, open-shell nanographenes have a range of unique electronic and magnetic properties due to the spin-polarized states. However, most recent works have focused on open-shell nanographenes with six-membered rings. The focus of this objective is on the synthesis of azulene-embedded nanographenes with open-shell characteristics. As a starting point, 5 will be developed (Fig. 1). According to the Clar sextet rule, 5 should possess significant biradical character as a result of gaining aromatic stabilization energy (Fig. 1). Indeed, from the calculations (see Theoretical Modeling), 5 displays open-shell triplet biradical character in the ground state, which is rare and unexplored in this field. Subsequently, extended nanographene 6 containing a pair of azulene units will be synthesized (Fig. 1). Similar to 5, 6 should exhibit open-shell singlet biradical character according to the Clar sextet rule. The synthesis of such model compounds is expected to lead to the unprecedented synthesis of extended open-shell nanographenes with nonhexagonal topologies. Objective 3: Synthesis of graphene nanoribbons with pentagonal and heptagonal rings. The motivation for this objective relates to evaluating the effects of periodic topological defects on the structural, optical, and physical properties of sp2 carbon frameworks. Complementary to objectives 1 and 2, which focus on nonhexagonal ring-embedded molecules, in this objective, nonhexagonal rings will be introduced into structurally well-defined GNRs. Among the various strategies exploited for fabricating GNRs, the bottom-up approach remains unparalleled in terms of the exquisite control over the width and edge species, allowing the electronic properties and magnetic edge states to be effectively tailored. Embedding nonhexagonal rings in a honeycomb lattice represents a viable, albeit less explored route to tune the intrinsic optical and electronic properties of GNRs. To this end, GNR1 and GNR2 with periodically repeating pentagon-heptagon pairs will be synthesized (Fig. 1), and their structural and electronic properties will be assessed to evaluate the effects of different topologies on GNRs. Objective 4: Device application based on the achieved nanographenes and GNRs. To establish clear structure-property relationships for the application of azulene-embedded graphene nanostructures, the related electronic devices will be fabricated through collaborations with partners of the PI. For instance, the designed azulene-type nanographenes and GNRs are expected to possess low band gaps, making these materials potential candidates for the development of OFET devices with substantially improved hole/electron mobility or balanced ambipolar charge-carrier transport properties. Moreover, the introduction of azulene units in graphene nanostructures could induce charge distribution polarity in these materials, generating nonvanishing even-order nonlinear optical (NLO) responses. Open-shell model compounds can also be used to understand spin and electron density dependency in nanographenes. Thus, these open-shell nanographenes will be explored as “organic magnets” for spintronic applications.

27301720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301720.value: 自2004年Geim和Novoselov的開創性研究以來，石墨烯引起了人們的廣泛關注。石墨烯表現出的多種特性，例如，出色的電荷載流子遷移率，使其成為未來納米電子學最有前途的材料之一。但是，石墨烯是一種零帶隙半導體，這使其無法應用於數字晶體管。因此，尋找一種打開石墨烯帶隙的方法對於將其結合到電子設備中至關重要。最突出的方法是在具有納米級寬度的石墨烯的一維半導體條帶中實現載流子的量子約束，即石墨烯納米帶（GNR）。近年來，已經開發了兩種主要的合成GNR的方法，即“自上而下”和“自下而上”的方法。 “自下而上”的方法是一種收斂的，全合成的方法，可以在原子尺度上精確調控GNR的邊緣結構和寬度。另一種方法是將“缺陷”引入到石墨烯的sp2框架中。理論計算表明，石墨烯中的拓撲“缺陷”會嚴重影響其電子、光學、化學、熱和機械性能。從能量穩定性的角度來看，五邊形-七邊形對（或奧基單元，Azulene unit）是一個合理的“缺陷”模型，它可以由原子位錯誘導形成。目前大多數研究僅集中於缺陷結構的表徵，例如使用透射電子顯微鏡和掃描隧道顯微鏡在實驗上證實了拓撲“缺陷”的存在。然而，人們對石墨烯中拓撲“缺陷”對物理化學性質的影響仍然知之甚少，這促使我們需要從基礎和應用的角度來闡明這些“精確缺陷”結構與性能的關係。本項目中，申請人提出了一條全新的研究路線，精確合成具有非六邊形環（例如，五邊形-七邊形對）的石墨烯納米結構，包括零維納米石墨烯（即多環芳烴）和一維GNR，因為這將為獲得諸如曲率，大的開殼雙自由基特性，增加的化學活性和新的電子功能性（用於有機場效應晶體管（OFET），非線性光學或自旋電子學）等新特性提供途徑。為了實現這一雄心勃勃的目標，該項目將利用不同的化學方法，包括有機化學，固態物理學和光學建模。

27301720.label: Realisation of objectives
27301720.value: Realisation of objectives: Objective 1: Synthesis of closed-shell nanographenes with pentagon-heptagon pairs. In this objective, three novel nanographenes with seven-ﬁve-seven (7−5−7)-membered rings (compounds 1-3) were successfully synthesized (J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2021, 143, 2353-2360). The crystallographic characterizations unambiguously show that compound 1 adopts a nearly planar structure, while compound 2, with an additional ﬁve-membered ring compared to 1, manifests a slightly saddle-shaped geometry. Interestingly, the subunits “1” in compound 3, which can be regarded as the “head-to-head” fusion of 1 with two bonds, feature the saddle-shaped geometries. The structural analyses combined with the DFT calculations demonstrated that compounds 1, 2, and 3 represent a new type of air-stable and fully conjugated antiaromatic nanographenes containing 7−5−7-membered rings. More importantly, the synthetic strategy in regard to the defect engineering in nanographenes by building 7−5−7-membered rings can be applied to the construction of other air-stable and π-expanded nanographenes with antiaromatic or open-shell structures. Objective 2: Synthesis of azulene-embedded nanographenes with open-shell biradical character. In this objective, we report a straightforward synthetic and isolation method for synthesizing a nonalternant nanographene (4) with a triplet ground state (Nature Commun., 2024, in press). Moving beyond the classic m-xylylene scaffold for high-spin organic molecules, seven-five-seven (7–5–7)-membered rings are introduced to create stable high-spin diradicals with half-lives (t1/2) as long as 101 days. Moreover, considering the spin relaxation of compound 4, with a spin–lattice relaxation time (T1) of 53.55 ms and a coherence time (Tm) of 3.41 μs at 10 K, the compound 4 shows great promise for applications in spin-based information retention and quantum computing. Objective 3: Synthesis of graphene nanoribbons with pentagonal and heptagonal rings. In this objective, we prepared a new type of graphene nanoribbon (GNR) with one pentagonal and heptagonal ring. Further characterization is needed and will be finished in the coming month. Objective 4: Device application based on the achieved nanographenes and GNRs. In collaboration with Prof. Shu Seki from Kyoto University, employing field-induced time resolved microwave conductivity (FI-TRMC) measurements, the local mobility of holes in compound 5 with 5−7-membered rings was estimated to be 0.03 cm2V−1s−1, demonstrating the promising feature of compound 5 as n-type semiconducting organic materials (Small, 2023, 2301769). This work provides new application perspectives for PAHs with pentagonal and heptagonal rings and for the design of new materials with enhanced properties for organic electronics.

27301720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27301720.value: Based on the findings in this project, a new type of graphene nanoribbon (GNR) with pentagonal and heptagonal rings was successfully prepared. Further characterization is needed and will be finished in the coming month. In addition, we report an extraordinarily stable high-spin diradicaloid (1) containing a diazuleno[2,1,8-efg:2',1',8'-kla]heptalene core. Compared with the structural isomer of compound 1 with only hexagons, which exhibits singlet open-shell diradical feature, the ground state can be switched by the nonalternant topologies. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrated that this nonalternant compound 1 shows triplet open-shell characteristic with a ultrasmall singlet-triplet gap (∆ES-T = 0.7 kcal/mol). The half-lives (t1/2) of 1 was fitted as long as 86 days. Moreover, with a moderate spin-lattice relaxation time (T1), a coherence time (Tm) of 3.41 μs of 1 was presented at 10 K, indicating its potential in high spin-based technology.

27301720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27301720.value: In this project, we established the structure-property relationship of nanographene and graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) embedded with nonalternant structures, especially 5−7-membered rings. We studied the trends of band gap and electronic structure caused by increasing number of pentagon-heptagon pairs and different topological structures, i.e., optical/electronic properties and closed-shell/open-shell properties, and explore the feasibility of synthesizing nonalternant structures in extended π-conjugated systems such as GNRs. We further found that the introduction of nonalternant structures into molecular carbons can obtain stable high-spin open-shell diradicals.

27301820.label: Project Objectives
27301820.value: The first project is to construct multifunctional MOFs containing photoactive organic linkers and bipyridyl units as solid matrices for photoinduced nickel-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling with a variety of nucleophiles. This catalytic system eliminates the use of precious metal photosensitizers which are always required in the corresponding homogeneous catalysis. The reactive organic radicals can be confined within the pores of MOFs for more effective radical trapping with nickel species. Electron transfer between photoactive linkers and nickel centers can also be facilitated due to their close proximity. By the use of the MOF-based photoactive nickel catalysts, highly efficient cross-coupling protocols will be developed with much lower catalyst loadings and decreased costs, paving the way for the development of large-scale processes for fine chemical production. The second project is to achieve visible-light-driven radical coupling reactions with highly recyclable MOF-based copper photoredox catalysts. In previous homogeneous reactions, the copper catalyst loadings are quite high, due to instability of copper–nucleophile species upon irradiation. Incorporation of copper complexes onto MOFs bearing functionalized organic linkers via post-synthetic modification will help stabilize photoactive copper intermediates throughout the catalytic cycle. Many synthetically useful transformations will be realized to construct C–C, C–N, and C–S bonds with the help of this novel heterogeneous catalysis platform. The third project is to design MOF-based pyridine-ligated palladium catalysts for C(sp3)–H activation reactions of N-protected α-amino acids without pre-installation of amide auxiliaries, which is essential for peptide synthesis in drug discovery. Despite high reactivity of amide-directed C(sp3)–H functionalization, difficulties in installation and removal of the auxiliaries drastically impede their application to the synthesis of sterically hindered and pH-sensitive unnatural amino acids. The immobilization of pyridine ligands on a rigid MOF support allows for site isolation of the palladium catalyst, which ensures vacant sites for weakly coordinating carboxylic acid substrates to access. This newly developed heterogeneous catalysis will significantly expand the substrate scope of palladium-catalyzed C–H activation and make the synthetic protocols truly useful in the preparation of peptide-based drug molecules. The last project is to develop C(sp3)–O cleavage/C–C coupling reactions of serine, threonine, and diol derivatives using MOF-supported mono-phosphine-ligated nickel catalysts, for the synthesis of unnatural α-amino acids and γ-functionalized alcohols. The current methodologies in the field are largely limited to the activation of C(sp2)–O bonds. To develop coupling reactions by cleaving less reactive C(sp3)–O bonds is a tremendous challenge. Site isolation of phosphine-ligated nickel catalysts on MOF supports will dramatically improve the binding ability of acid and alcohol substrates as well as promote C–O oxidative addition and C–C reductive elimination steps. This design principle will unravel unprecedented reactivity in nickel catalysis and give rise to new disconnection strategies in organic synthesis.
rows: The first project is to construct multifunctional MOFs containing photoactive organic linkers and bipyridyl units as solid matrices for photoinduced nickel-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling with a variety of nucleophiles. This catalytic system eliminates the use of precious metal photosensitizers which are always required in the corresponding homogeneous catalysis. The reactive organic radicals can be confined within the pores of MOFs for more effective radical trapping with nickel species. Electron transfer between photoactive linkers and nickel centers can also be facilitated due to their close proximity. By the use of the MOF-based photoactive nickel catalysts, highly efficient cross-coupling protocols will be developed with much lower catalyst loadings and decreased costs, paving the way for the development of large-scale processes for fine chemical production.

The second project is to achieve visible-light-driven radical coupling reactions with highly recyclable MOF-based copper photoredox catalysts. In previous homogeneous reactions, the copper catalyst loadings are quite high, due to instability of copper–nucleophile species upon irradiation. Incorporation of copper complexes onto MOFs bearing functionalized organic linkers via post-synthetic modification will help stabilize photoactive copper intermediates throughout the catalytic cycle. Many synthetically useful transformations will be realized to construct C–C, C–N, and C–S bonds with the help of this novel heterogeneous catalysis platform.

The third project is to design MOF-based pyridine-ligated palladium catalysts for C(sp3)–H activation reactions of N-protected α-amino acids without pre-installation of amide auxiliaries, which is essential for peptide synthesis in drug discovery. Despite high reactivity of amide-directed C(sp3)–H functionalization, difficulties in installation and removal of the auxiliaries drastically impede their application to the synthesis of sterically hindered and pH-sensitive unnatural amino acids. The immobilization of pyridine ligands on a rigid MOF support allows for site isolation of the palladium catalyst, which ensures vacant sites for weakly coordinating carboxylic acid substrates to access. This newly developed heterogeneous catalysis will significantly expand the substrate scope of palladium-catalyzed C–H activation and make the synthetic protocols truly useful in the preparation of peptide-based drug molecules.

The last project is to develop C(sp3)–O cleavage/C–C coupling reactions of serine, threonine, and diol derivatives using MOF-supported mono-phosphine-ligated nickel catalysts, for the synthesis of unnatural α-amino acids and γ-functionalized alcohols. The current methodologies in the field are largely limited to the activation of C(sp2)–O bonds. To develop coupling reactions by cleaving less reactive C(sp3)–O bonds is a tremendous challenge. Site isolation of phosphine-ligated nickel catalysts on MOF supports will dramatically improve the binding ability of acid and alcohol substrates as well as promote C–O oxidative addition and C–C reductive elimination steps. This design principle will unravel unprecedented reactivity in nickel catalysis and give rise to new disconnection strategies in organic synthesis.

27301820.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301820.value: The development of heterogeneous catalysts with high activity, stability, and recyclability is essential for rendering catalytic organic reactions practically useful, since they provide highly efficient, scalable, and recyclable setups in many large-scale chemical processes and improve product quality through easy separation. While numerous organic transformations have been achieved in homogeneous catalytic systems, the needs for addressing their synthetic limitations, such as poor catalyst reactivity, narrow substrate scope, and employment of toxic and expensive reagents, represent challenges and opportunities for the coming generation of chemists. Designing novel catalysts that marry the benefits of heterogeneous catalysis with those of homogeneous catalysis to solve the long-standing problems in organic synthesis is compelling and highly desirable. Despite aforementioned advantages of employing heterogeneous catalysts in synthetic methodology development, the reaction types in heterogeneous catalytic systems remain fairly limited to date. One of the proposed strategies to broadly expand the scope of reactions catalyzed by heterogeneous catalysts is to design highly tunable metal-organic framework (MOF) matrices that can incorporate noble-metal-free photocatalysts together with transition-metal catalysts. These MOF-based photoactive catalysts can promote more effective radical coupling processes by increasing local concentration of reactive species, therefore further improving their photocatalytic reactivity compared with the homogeneous counterparts. To realize challenging transformations in organic synthesis, the second strategy in design of MOF-supported catalysts is to prepare heterogeneous transition-metal catalysts bearing vacant coordination sites, which can strongly interact with a wide range of cheap and readily available substrates as well as facilitate several key elementary steps throughout the catalytic cycle. 27302220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27302220.value: RNA在细胞正常运作中有着关键的作用。越来越多的研究表明RNA需要在特定时间到达细胞的特定位置才能保障细胞的生存和发展。这些生物功能是和RNA复杂 且多变的特性相关，涉及到RNA的方方面面，包括RNA的产生、降解、运输、剪接、折叠以及各种化学修饰。这些过程之间是息息相关，往往牵涉到蛋白质和RNA的相互作用，通常发生在毫秒到分钟的时间尺度上。因此，同时掌握蛋白质和RNA在时间和空间上的精细分布是解锁RNA生物功能的关键。荧光共聚焦显微镜还不能用于活体细胞中检测未知的RNA成份，因为这项技术通常需要事先知晓RNA的序列而且需要将细胞固定并增加细胞膜的通透性。基于离心分离各细胞组份的RNA测序无法保留瞬时多变的定位信息。RNA定位的早期研究仅限于一个时间点的一个细胞定位。这不足以应对RNA的多样性。实现对活细胞中多个细胞定位同时以及循序监测RNA的成份将有助于了解RNA是如何到达细胞内特定位置。这将极大的推动RNA的相关研究。我们设想创建一套化学方法，从而得以在不同时间标记 RNA并跟踪RNA在环境刺激相应下于两个不同位置之间的运输。我们提议的研究将全面覆盖RNA的动态，并将革新疾病机理的研究和治疗方法的改进。我们试图分三步实现目标：1）设计一系列小分子来标记活细胞中特定位置的RNA；2）协同采用不同机理的化学方法来标记不同定位处的RNA；3）通过依次标记RNA并结合生物信息学分析，揭秘活细胞中RNA运输的基本规律。本项目的成功完成将深入揭示RNA以及蛋白质的运输机理并有助于实现对RNA和蛋白质运输的精细调控。本项目研究成果将为本组日后在神经退行性疾病以及学习和记忆中分子机制的研究奠定基础。

27302220.label: Realisation of objectives
27302220.value: The research project was centered on developing innovative small-molecule-based approaches to label RNAs within living cells, with the overarching goal of advancing our understanding of RNA dynamics without the interference caused by traditional fusion protein methods. This comprehensive report outlines the progress and achievements related to the project’s three main objectives. Objective 1 focused on developing a variety of small-molecule approaches to label RNAs at specific locations inside living cells. The traditional methods, which often involve expressing fusion constructs, were noted for their limited applicability and potential interference with cellular processes. In response, we successfully designed targeted photosensitizers intended to replace these fusion proteins, thus minimizing biological interference. This new methodology was not only applied to different cellular components—such as endoplasmic reticulum, lysosome and mitochondria—but also proved adaptable for subsequent protein localization studies and integrated well with other advanced genetic manipulations. The accomplishment of this objective facilitated a breakthrough in how RNA localization can be studied, offering a versatile tool applicable to various cell types and potentially extendable to tissue samples. Objective 2 aimed to combine small molecule approaches with a mechanistically different labeling method to achieve dual-location RNA tagging inside living cells. To address the complexities of RNA dynamics which occur over varying time scales, we developed a dual-tagging technique that allowed for the simultaneous observation of RNA in different cellular locations—specifically nucleus and mitochondria. This innovative approach enabled us to compare the molecular details of transcriptionally active and suppressed regions at these sites, shedding light on how cells coordinate gene expression in response to various stimuli. The development of this technology marks a significant advancement in our ability to study RNA dynamics, providing insights into the subcellular localization of RNAs in real-time. Objective 3 was established to track RNA translocation within cells over time using sequential RNA labeling, complemented by bioinformatics analysis to elucidate the molecular details of RNA movement. We applied singlet oxygen-induced RNA tagging in the nucleus and hydroxyl radical-mediated RNA labeling in the mitochondria. This methodology allowed us to selectively enrich RNAs that traveled between these locations, offering a detailed view of RNA translocation from the nucleus to mitochondria. In conclusion, the project overall successfully met and exceeded the set objectives, leading to the development of innovative techniques for RNA study within living cells. These advancements have not only enhanced our understanding of RNA and protein dynamics but also opened new avenues for research in genetic manipulation and potential therapeutic interventions. The successful implementation of these objectives demonstrates a significant leap forward in molecular biology, promising to influence future studies and applications in diverse biological and medical sciences.

27302220.label: Major findings and research outcome
27302220.value: Our research project has been instrumental in advancing the field of cellular biology by developing innovative methods for studying RNA dynamics within living cells. Traditionally, RNA labeling has relied on fusion proteins which, while effective, can interfere with natural cellular processes and are limited in their applicability, especially in certain complex biological systems. Our research has successfully addressed these limitations by pioneering the use of small-molecule photosensitizers as a genetic free alternative for RNA localization. One of our key achievements has been the design and synthesis of targeted photosensitizers to replace traditional fusion proteins used in RNA labeling. These small molecules enable the precise labeling of RNA at specific sites within cells, such as endoplasmic reticulum, lysosome and mitochondria. By minimizing biological interference, these photosensitizers have significantly improved the accuracy of studies on RNA dynamics across various cell types, enhancing our understanding of cellular processes at a molecular level. A pivotal advancement in our project was the introduction of a dual-location RNA tagging system. This innovative methodology employs distinct and orthogonal chemical reactions to tag RNA simultaneously at two different cellular sites. Initially focusing on nucleus and mitochondria, this technology allowed us to observe RNA dynamics in two locations simultaneously. The insights gained from these observations are crucial for understanding how cells regulate gene expression in response to different stimuli. Furthermore, we developed a novel sequential RNA labeling technique that uses different reactive molecules to mark RNA molecules over time. This approach has enabled us to track the movement of RNA from the nucleus to mitochondria, potentially providing a dynamic overview of RNA translocation within cells. The methodologies developed through our project have led to several publications, including Org. Lett., ACS Chem. Biol., Analy. Chem. and Angew. Chemi. Int. Ed. The two students trained on this project have successfully graduated with PhD degree in Chemistry. In conclusion, our project has significantly enriched the toolkit available for investigating RNA within living cells, marking a substantial advancement in both the methodology and application of cellular biology. The innovative techniques we have developed provide unparalleled precision and flexibility, reducing biological interference and opening new avenues for future scientific endeavors in understanding and manipulating cellular functions and pathologies.

27302220.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27302220.value: The potential for further development of our RNA labeling techniques is substantial, with numerous avenues for expansion and refinement. Future research will focus on enhancing the specificity and efficiency of the small-molecule photosensitizers. This includes designing molecules that can target RNA sequences more selectively and can be activated or deactivated by external stimuli, allowing for real-time control over RNA labeling. Additionally, we plan to extend the dual-location RNA tagging system to include additional cellular compartments, such as the cytoplasm and Golgi apparatus. This expansion will facilitate a more comprehensive understanding of RNA trafficking and its role in cellular function. We also aim to integrate our labeling technologies with live-cell imaging and high-throughput sequencing techniques to dynamically monitor RNA interactions and modifications within cells. A proposed course of action involves collaborating with bioinformatics teams to develop algorithms that can analyze complex data sets generated from these studies. This collaboration will enhance our ability to interpret the vast amounts of data and uncover new insights into RNA biology.

27302220.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27302220.value: Our research project focused on developing new methods to study RNA molecules inside living cells. Normally, scientists use specific protein tags to observe RNA, but these tags can sometimes interfere with the cell's normal functions or cannot be easily integrated in certain cells. So, we created a new way using small, specially designed molecules that can label RNA without using these protein tags. This method is more straightforward and can be applied to various types of cells and potentially even tissues. The significance of this research lies in its ability to allow us to observe RNA in multiple locations within the cell simultaneously. This is crucial because RNA plays a vital role in many cellular functions, including how genes are expressed and how cells respond to environmental changes. By understanding better how RNA moves and functions within cells, we can gain deeper insights into these processes. The value of this research extends beyond basic scientific knowledge. It has the potential to impact medical science by improving our understanding of diseases at a molecular level and could lead to new strategies for designing drugs or therapies based on RNA and protein behavior in cells.

27306020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27306020.value: 陸生植物光合作用的精確模擬是準確預測陸地碳吸收的重要前提，並直接影響大尺度氣候變化和年際波動。葉片光合作用的最大羧化率（Vc,max）是調控植物光合作用對氣候變化響應的最重要參數之一。然而，Vc,max自身俱有高度動態的特性，並隨植物種類、葉齡和生態系統類型而發生變化。 Vc,max具有的這種高時空變異特性同時也給當前的生態系統模型在模擬大尺度的光合作用過程帶來了很大的不確定性。解決這種不確定性的首要前提是在技術上如何提高Vc,max的監測效率以及在機理和數學模型上如何提高對Vc,max的準確表達？ 為解決上述問題，我們在此提出了一個集野外觀測、多尺度遙感、過程模型與假設檢驗相結合的研究方案。具體而言，本研究將依托國內的三個森林塔吊觀測站點進行季節採樣；這些站點從北到南依次為長白山溫帶落葉林、古田山亞熱帶常綠林以及西雙版納熱帶雨林。採集的數據含葉片尺度的Vc,max和高光譜反射率，並且這些數據將涵蓋由物種、葉齡和生態系統類型引起的變異。基於這些數據，我們將（1）分析Vc,max的時空動態格局，（2）探討新興的植物光譜學方法提高Vc,max時空變異監測的可能性，（3）量化分析氣候的季節性與Vc ,max在物種及生態系統水平的季節性之間的關係，（4）結合過程模型，探討三種Vc,max的表達（含野外觀測、光譜模型估算和氣候模型估算）對物種及生態系統水平的光合作用季節動態的分別影響。基於這些探討，本研究旨在改進Vc,max的監測技術及數學表達，從而幫助更好地模擬森林生態系統光合作用的季節動態。

27306020.label: Realisation of objectives
27306020.value: This ECS research integrates observations and modeling to address three objectives as illustrated in Section 5.2. Due to the funding cut, the remaining ECS budget is allocated entirely to staff costs. To supplement this research, we have secured support from a National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC; #31922090) grant. Although these two grants serve distinct purposes - the ECS research focuses on understanding patterns, monitoring skills, and controls of Vc,max variability, while the NSFC project aims to develop innovative multi-scale remote sensing approaches for characterizing plant functional traits (e.g., morphological and biochemical) - they can complement each other in two ways: 1) they cover different aspects of plant trait measurements - the NSFC project targets leaf morphological and biochemical traits, while the ECS research addresses leaf physiological traits (i.e., Vc,max); 2) as both projects are conducted at the same sites, we can efficiently coordinate fieldwork, manpower, and expenses. Finally, the COVID-19 pandemic has posed challenges to field campaigns in Mainland China, and alternative plans have been devised to minimize its impact, with details provided below. 1. Field data collection and integration with modeling for objective 1 We have conducted two campaigns in Mainland China so far: 1) The first campaign in July-August 2019 collected pilot data for proofing the concept. Field measurements from three crane sites, i.e., Mountain Changbai, Mountain Dinghu, and Xishuangbanna, were collected. Key leaf traits covering representative tree species of each site were measured, including morphological, biochemical, physiological, and optical traits (Yan et al., 2021; Guo et al., 2022). Additionally, we conducted drone-based surveys of RGB images, allowing us to differentiate tree crowns and map field-measured traits onto drone images; 2) The second field campaign in April-May 2021 focused on the Mountain Dinghu and Xishuangbanna sites, with similar trait data collected and details provided in Liu et al. (2023). Our third campaign plan was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. As an alternative, we leveraged the age-dependent Vc,max relationship revealed in Wu et al. (2016, Science), and collaborated with Prof. Jiaxin Jin's team from Hohai University to show that satellite remote sensing can effectively differentiate leaf age phenophases, thus improving photosynthetic seasonality modeling (Jin et al., 2024). This alternative plan serves as an important baseline test, demonstrating that improved representation of seasonal Vc,max variation is an effective way to enhance photosynthesis modeling. Meanwhile, my former postdoc Dr. Zhengbing Yan (now a full professor at the Institute of Botany, CAS) supported by this project is currently conducting intensive seasonal field surveys (including Vc,max) across all crane sites mentioned above. This effort will serve as an important legacy of this project and may fill crucial data gaps in the near future. 2. The scalability of vegetation spectroscopy for improved Vc,max monitoring for objective 2 We utilized the field data to evaluate different approaches for predicting Vc,max variability and investigated the potential of vegetation spectroscopy (relying on leaf reflectance spectra as input) as a scalable, effective alternative. We showed that the relationships between conventionally-measured leaf traits and Vc,max were overall weak, site-specific (R2≤0.15). In contrast, leaf spectroscopy effectively reconciled the breakdown of trait-Vc,max relationships across forest sites, as a general model enabling accurate prediction of physiological trait Vc,max across all sites and species (R2=0.77). These findings challenge the traditional use of empirical trait-Vc,max relationships in estimating terrestrial plant photosynthesis and highlight spectroscopy as an efficient alternative to advance ecosystem modeling and functional ecology studies. The relevant results have been published in Yan et al. (2021) in New Phytologist. Furthermore, we investigated whether the cross-site scalable leaf spectroscopy model could be extended to the canopy scale. Utilizing field-measured leaf traits and drone-based hyperspectral reflectance, we derived two key findings: (1) Canopy-scale spectra can accurately characterize Vc,max and the spectra-trait relationship also demonstrate cross-site scalable; (2) Directly upscaled spectra-trait relationships, which integrate leaf-scale spectra-trait relationships and the canopy structure effect through process model (i.e., PROSAIL), cannot be applied to real-world scenarios, largely due to spatial heterogeneity in the canopy structure effect that is not yet accurately represented in the PROSAIL model. These findings underscore the potential of vegetation spectroscopy in monitoring broad spatiotemporal dynamics of plant traits and highlight the similar scalability, but different underlying mechanisms at leaf and canopy scales. The related results have been published in Liu et al. (2023) in Remote Sensing of Environment. 3. Understanding the patterns and drivers of large-scale Vc,max variability, and exploring the broader implications of biotic roles in regulating ecosystem sensitivity to climate variability for objective 3 To understand the mechanisms underlying large-scale Vc,max variability, we firstly compiled and then used a global dataset for hypothesis testing. We hypothesized that Vc,max is dictated by both temperature-associated enzyme kinetics and the amount of activated RuBisCO (indexed by Vc,max standardized at 25°C, Vc,max25). We assessed the relative contributions of these processes on mediating global Vc,max variability, explored the accuracy of an optimality theory, as well as quantitatively assessed the influence of deep-time evolutionary factors on global Vc,max variability. We found: (1) temperature-based enzyme kinetic and Vc,max25 jointly explained 78% of global Vc,max variability, with the former dominating and the latter secondary; (2) the predictions of the optimality theory and the temperature-based enzyme kinetic model are nearly identical, explaining almost none of the Vc,max25 biogeography, largely because the current optimality theory does not exclusively consider the constraint of subsurface nutrients on RuBisCO enzyme construction cost; (3) deep time evolutionary factors and present-day growth environment jointly regulate global Vc,max25 variability, with the former dominating (53%) and the latter second (18%), suggesting that deep-time evolutionary history is essential for determining the present-day plant photosynthesis processes. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding and mathematical modeling of global Vc,max25 variation and improve the ability of process-based models to simulate photosynthetic responses of terrestrial ecosystems to global climate change. Two papers, resulting from these findings, are published in Global Ecology and Biogeography (Yan et al., 2023) and Fundamental Research (Yan et al., 2024), respectively. We last examined the role of biotic factors (including Vc,max25) in affecting plant physiology modeling (e.g., Guo et al., 2022; Jin et al., 2024), and used plant thermoregulation for demonstration purpose. Understanding plant thermoregulation, which refers to maintaining relatively stable Tc with variable air temperature (Ta), is essential as Tc mediates various activities in terrestrial plants and is subject to fundamental energy balance processes. By leveraging a trait-based energy balance model for hypothesis testing, our results show that (1) leaf traits largely influence ΔT (the Tc-Ta difference) variability, with leaf size, Vc,max25, and stomatal slope (g1) being the most crucial traits regulating ΔT and their relative importance varying across the diel course; (2) simulated trait-ΔT relationships strongly agree with field observations. When moving from sites to globe, we found that climatology dominates ΔT variability, and plant traits also importantly regulate ΔT variability. These results collectively improve process understanding of biotic controls of ΔT variability, offering a trait-based representation of leaf energy balance that can be incorporated into terrestrial biosphere models for improved simulations of plant physiological responses to climate change. Three papers resulting from these findings are published in Agricultural and Forest Meteorology (Guo et al., 2022, 2023) and in New Phytologist (Guo et al., 2023), respectively.

27306020.label: Major findings and research outcome
27306020.value: Accurate modeling of land plant photosynthesis is crucial for predicting terrestrial carbon uptake, which significantly influences large-scale climate variability. The maximum carboxylation rate (Vc,max) is a vital biotic parameter that predominantly governs photosynthesis dynamics across various temporal and spatial scales. However, uncertainties remain regarding the spatiotemporal variability of Vc,max and its influence on forest ecosystem photosynthesis seasonality. These questions pose challenges for several ecology-related disciplines. Specifically, three issues persist in monitoring skills, patterns, controls, and representations of Vc,max variability. To address these issues, we propose research that integrates field observations across environmental gradients, multi-scale remote sensing, process models, and hypothesis testing. Our research yields three key findings: 1) By utilizing multi-source and multi-scale observations, including ground and near-surface drone sensing, we demonstrate for the first time that vegetation spectroscopy is a scalable approach for accurately monitoring Vc,max across diverse plant species, forest ecosystems, and scales. Notably, this scalable approach operates at both leaf and canopy levels but with differing underlying biochemical and biophysical mechanisms as detailed in Section 5.3; 2) Using a newly compiled global dataset of Vc,max, we examine its patterns and drivers. We find that the widely accepted "eco-evolutionary first principle" scarcely explains global variability, primarily due to the omission of below-ground resource constraints on leaf photosynthetic infrastructure. Additionally, we discover that deep-time evolutionary history is even more critical in determining global Vc,max variability, enhancing our understanding and modeling of photosynthetic responses to climate change; 3) We employ two examples, photosynthetic seasonality modeling and plant thermoregulation capability, to demonstrate that accounting for age-dependent Vc,max is effective in improving photosynthetic seasonality modeling in temperate forest ecosystems, and also discover that biotic factors (including Vc,max) play a significant role in regulating plant thermoregulation capability across various scales from hours to seasons and from tree individuals to diverse ecosystems around the world. Throughout this project's implementation, we have provided high-quality research training to two PhD students (Zhengfei Guo and Shuwen Liu) and one postdoc (Zhengbing Yan). Dr. Yan is now a full professor at the Institute of Botany, CAS, and a rising star in the ecological remote sensing field. Dr. Guo graduated with distinction (top 5% at HKU), and Mr. Liu is expected to graduate with outstanding results by early 2025. This project has also produced fruitful research outcomes, with eight papers published in well-regarded journals (details are shown in Section 5.3).

27306020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27306020.value: Upon completing this project, two vital future directions emerge. First, trait upscaling is vital, as this research demonstrates the importance of physiological traits, particularly Vc,max, in essential ecosystem processes and functions. It also showcases the potential of drone-based imaging spectroscopy as an accurate, scalable method for monitoring Vc,max at landscape scales. However, this approach remains costly and challenging to scale up. To tackle this issue, our recent research offers an alternative solution: integrating drone/airborne-based imaging spectroscopy with freely accessible Sentinel-2 satellite can expand trait monitoring from sites to regions and has proven effective across the US. This suggests that by continuously expanding the efforts as this project across China's diverse landscapes, similar success could be achieved in China or even worldwide, addressing a significant data gap. Second, filling this data gap would further aid in integrating trait data with biogeography and ecosystem modeling, enabling a comprehensive understanding of how climate and other factors, such as disturbances, impact plant trait biogeography, and how climate and plant traits jointly regulate terrestrial ecosystem sensitivity to climate change. Acquiring this knowledge is crucial for accurately evaluating ecosystem health under climate change and promoting nature-based solutions for various landscape managements to mitigate climate change.

27306020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27306020.value: This research project aims to improve our understanding of plant photosynthesis, a crucial process that directly impacts climate variability. One key factor in photosynthesis is the maximum carboxylation rate (Vc,max), which influences how plants absorb carbon and affects ecosystems on a global scale. However, uncertainties remain about how Vc,max varies in space and time and how it controls forest ecosystem photosynthesis. To address these issues, the project combines field observations, multi-scale remote sensing, and process models to investigate Vc,max variability. The study has three main findings: 1) vegetation spectroscopy can accurately monitor Vc,max across different scales and ecosystems; 2) the widely-accepted "eco-evolutionary first principle" doesn't fully explain global Vc,max variability, as below-ground resource constraints and deep-time evolutionary history play significant roles; and 3) age-dependent Vc,max improves photosynthetic seasonality modeling in temperate forests and mediate the variation in plant thermoregulation capability across different timescales and diverse ecosystems around the world. This project has provided valuable research training to two PhD students and one postdoc, resulting in eight published papers. The findings contribute to our understanding of photosynthesis and its response to climate change, which has important implications for ecosystem health and management.

27307320.label: Project Objectives
27307320.value: Set up the circle method to study the periods of periodic paths on a regular pentagonal table, and show that assuming the super approximation property for the Hecke-5 triangle group, one can get a desired estimate in the major arc analysis. Try to prove the super approximation property for the Hecke-5 group, using the approach of Bourgain-Varjú’s work on the super approximation property for Zariski-dense subgroups of SL(d, Z), combined with ingredients of PI’s work on the logarithmic diameters of Cayley graphs of congruence quotients of the Hecke-5 group. Assuming the low-multiplicity of input linear forms in the setup of the circle method, obtain a desired estimate in the minor arc analysis of the circle method, and show that a density one subset of even numbers are periods. Run a computer experiment to get more insight about the multiplicity of the input linear forms, and try to obtain a quantitative statement good enough for the minor arc analysis. Investigate whether an asymptotic local-global principle holds for sets of integers produced by a quadratic form on the entries of matrices from certain Zariski-dense subgroups of SL(2, Z[i]). Try to prove a poly-logarithmic bound for Cayley graphs of congruence quotients of subgroups of GL(n, Z) whose Zariski closures are perfect. If Step 3 is successful, try to prove the super approximation property for more general groups.

27307320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27307320.value: 假设我们在一个光滑的正五边形台球桌将一颗白球击出，如果角度选取适当白球会在某一时刻回到初始位置并继续周而复始地重复之前行进的轨迹。我们称这样的轨迹为闭轨迹，并且称白球行进一周内碰撞边界的次数为该闭轨迹的周期。我们已知有无穷多个这样的闭轨迹。Davis与Lelievre在2018年的一篇论文中对这些闭轨迹的周期进行了详尽的研究，并提出如下猜想：一个正整数n是某一个闭轨迹的周期当且仅当n是5或者是除2，12，14，18外的任一正偶数。本项目将对该猜想以及相关问题开展研究。该猜想涉及到一些深刻的解析数论，几何群论和谱图理论问题。

27307320.label: Realisation of objectives
27307320.value: The main purpose of this project is to prove a density one theorem for Davis-Lelievre conjecture on combinatorial periods of pentagonal billiards. Originally, the PI proposed to solve it using circle method and set up the Objectives 1-4. Later the PI found an alternative way, which is more elementary to address this conjecture. We did not prove super approximation for Hecke-5 group, which is not necessary for our main purpose. Instead, we did a detailed local-analysis for this group. Objective 5 is fully achieved in a preprint joint with Xuanxuan Xiao. Objective 6 is fully achieved by my student Tianzhi Jiang in his PhD thesis. Objective 7 is not the main goal of this proposal and is to be addressed in another project.

27307320.label: Major findings and research outcome
27307320.value: Kontorovich and I prove an asymptotic local-global theorem for combinatorial periods of pentagonal billiard. Xuanxuan Xiao and I prove an asymptotic local-global theorem for integers represented by certain quadratic forms on entries of SL(2, Z[i]). Beyond this project, Kontorovich and I wrote a related paper, which establishes an asymptotic local-global theorem for integers represented by linear forms on thin subgroups of SL(2,Z) containing parabolic elements. Previously, Bourgain and Kontorovich proved a similar result for groups without parabolic elements and for certain restricted linear forms, with the presence of parabolic elements posing major obstruction in their method. In this paper, we employed a different approach to overcome the parabolic issue, which also allows us deal with a general linear form, such as trace, that is not accessible by their method. As a result, we can say some nontrivial things about the length sets of some subarithmetic hyperbolic surfaces. My PhD Tianzhi Jiang proved logarithmic diameter bounds for Cayley graphs of a large class of subgroups of SL(d,Z), thus giving evidence to the super approximation property for these groups.

27307320.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27307320.value: The work of Tianzhi Jiang provides strong evidence to the super-approximation conjecture, which is a major conjecture in group theory concerning which subgroups of SL(d, Z) have the spectral gap properties. Progress has been made towards this conjecture by prominent mathematicians, but the general case remains open. The PI plans to address this conjecture in the following-up projects.

27307320.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27307320.value: The Davis-Lelievre conjecture for ideal pentagonal billiards asserts that every sufficiently large even number is the period of a closed billiard trajectory. We prove a density-one version of the conjecture by carefully analyzing the associated symmetry group. This work enriches the theory of thin groups.

27307920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27307920.value: 大規模基因組研究中帶有中介變量缺失值的中介分析

27307920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27307920.value: 在現代基因組研究中，研究者對於應用因果中介分析的方法來識別處於遺傳以及環境因素到人類健康通路的分子標記物越來越感興趣。然而，通常只有一部分樣本具有分子水平的數據。基於一部分樣本數據的因果中介分析會導致統計功效損失以及推斷偏差。據我們所知，目前還沒有穩健和有效的並且可以考慮缺失值的大規模中介分析方法。另外一個困難是我們需要檢驗大量的復合原假設，其原假設參數空間不是線性空間，這直接導致通常的統計漸近理論不可用。這些問題給大規模中介分析的統計推斷帶來了挑戰。我們將在這個項目研究中解決這些迫切的問題。在單個中介變量情形下，我們提出分化-征服-合併的策略。首先，我們將原假設參數空間分成三個不相交的部分。然後，在征服階段，我們提出似然函數和加權估計方程的方法進行中介分析。進而，我們提出雙穩健加權估計方程的方法。最後，在合併階段，我們將三個部分的結果結合起來。在多個中介變量情形，我們提出一種新的幾何方法來檢驗中介效應。我們的方法在計算上也很高效且具有可擴展性。我們將應用新方法來研究T 細胞在人類皰疹病毒第四型到鼻咽癌患病風險通路的中介效應。鼻咽癌研究的科學發現可以讓我們更好地理解人類適應性免疫系統在抗擊鼻咽癌中的作用，並且可以為發展疫苗和免疫療法提供靶點，最終惠及在香港以及世界其它地方的鼻咽癌患者

27308720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27308720.value: 基于计算机模拟的复杂似然函数的推断方法的新框架

27308720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27308720.value: In modern applications the likelihood function is often unavailable due to, e.g., complex data correlation or latent random dynamics, and the parameter inference is challenging. For generative models, pseudo datasets can be simulated to approxi- mate moments or likelihood functions. Likelihood-free inference, including approximate Bayesian computation (ABC), synthetic likelihood, etc., provides computational tools to tackle complicated statistical models and has attracted substantial interests. The theoretical study is still in its early stage. In order to make connections with moment- based inference methods in the classical framework, this project studies simulation- based versions of the generalised empirical likelihood (GEL). GEL is known to possess desirable properties including robustness under misspecification, no need to choose a weighting matrix, scalability to the increasing dimension of the moment condition, etc. Contributions are expected to be three-fold. First is a unified framework on develop- ing theoretical foundations of likelihood-free inference. Second are new computational methods towards challenges of likelihood-free inference, including high-dimension sum- mary statistics with strong correlation or weakly informative components, simulator misspecification, etc. The third is an easy-to-implement extension of the GEL class to dependent data. The main challenge of likelihood-free inference is the choice of summary statistic. The class of composite likelihood methods constructs partial information through like- lihoods of subsets of data. The main difficulty is the choice of appropriate weights to combine component sub-likelihoods. This project proposes to use sub-score functions as summary statistics for Bayesian inference. It is expected that the sub-scores are optimally combined by the summary-based posterior distribution. For models where sub-likelihoods have no closed-form, e.g. latent-variable models, this project proposes to use an unbiased estimator of the sub-score functions and shows that the estimation error can be ignorable. 现代统计应用的一个重要挑战是复杂模型的参数推断非常困难，因为似然函数常常没有解析表达式，比如当数据维度之间相关性很复杂时，或者存在隐藏的动态变量时。另一方面感兴趣的模型常常是生成模型，而模拟数据及其统计量可以被用来近似估计矩函数和似然函数。基于这点而发展出来的基于统计量而非整个数据集的免似然推断法，包括近似贝叶斯计算，合成似然法等，因为提供了可行的统计计算方法而近期获得了大量的关注。 这类方法的理论研究还处于早期。为了将其与经典的矩推断法联系起来，这个项目研究基于模拟数据的广义经验似然法。广义经验似然法因为其有用的性质在计量经济学中被大量应用，包括稳健性，不需要选择权重矩阵，对于矩条件的数量有更好的扩展性等等。这个项目的贡献有三层。一是为免似然推断法提供理论框架。二是针对免似然法的挑战提供新的计算方法，包括统计量维度的扩展性，统计量强相关时的数值问题，无信息的统计量带来的干扰，对生成模型的稳健性等等。三是为广义经验似然法处理非独立数据时提供新的计算方法。 免似然推断法的另一个挑战是如何选择统计量。复合似然法是一类通过合并数据子集的似然函数来构造近似似然函数的方法。它的主要困难在于选择子集的权重。这个项目研究使用子集的得分函数作为免似然推断法的统计量来进行贝叶斯推断。通过初步的研究我们得知基于统计量的后验分布将会自动用最优的方式合并这些得分函数。进一步的当子集的似然函数没有解析表达式时，比如状态空间模型，这个项目研究使用得分函数的一种无偏估计来作为统计量，并且证明了估计的误差可以被忽略。

27501020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27501020.value: Intensive care unit (ICU) is a special hospital department that provides treatments to the most critical patients. Effective utilization of such highly expensive but capacity-constrained medical resource is extremely important to save more lives. The proposed work aims to use mathematical modeling and analysis to develop insights into how to allocate the ICU resource while taking into account patient health condition evolution, patient abandonment and patient readmission. To model the patient health condition evolution, we assume the patients' health conditions belong to multiple stages, and they could become better or worse according to a Markov chain in the ICU. Patients who are treated in a non-ICU ward due to insufficient ICU capacity will deteriorate to worse health conditions or leave the system. To model the readmission, we assume that patients in the non-ICU wards could be readmitted to ICU when an ICU bed becomes available. We also assume the system has a finite capacity of ICU and non-ICU wards, and new patients arrive to a full system will be diverted to other hospitals. We model this system as a Markov decision process (MDP) with the objective of maximizing the long-run average reward, where the reward could be interpreted as the number of patients who survived. In this proposal, we first provided some preliminary analysis of the MDP model that could shied insights into which patients should be prioritized. Then, we performed a numerical study to show the structure of the optimal policy, which we would like to provide further analytical characterization in future work. We also proposed some priority index policies and compared their performances in the preliminary analysis. Our proposed work will focus on the study of how patients’ health conditions evolution and their readmission affect the allocation decisions. Our preliminary results showed that a better resource allocation policy could save more people without increasing the operating costs. However, this project requires more research work for both academic and practical contributions. First, we need to provide more analytical characterization of the optimal policy of the MDP, and propose good heuristic policies based on our analysis. Secondly, we also need to demonstrate how our analysis of the stylized mathematical model could be extended to more complicated real systems. Finally, we would like to collaborate with ICU doctors to analyze the feasibility and evaluate the performance of proposed policies in practice. 重症監護病房（ICU）是為病情最爲嚴重的患者提供治療的專門的醫院科室。有效利用這種昂貴但容量受限的醫療資源對於挽救更多生命至關重要。這項研究旨在使用數學建模和分析方法，在考慮到患者健康狀況演變和患者再次入院的情況下深入地研究如何分配ICU資源。 為了考慮患者健康狀況的演變，我們假設患者的健康狀況分爲多個階段，他們在健康狀況可能會變得更好或更糟。由於ICU容量不足而在非ICU病房中接受治療的患者會遭受健康狀況惡化或離開系統。為了考慮再入院，我們考慮儅ICU病床出現空餘的情況下，非ICU病房等待的患者可以再次進入ICU。 我們將此系統建模為馬爾可夫決策過程（MDP），目的是最大化長期平均報酬，其中報酬可以解釋為倖存的患者人數。在此提案中，我們首先提供了MDP模型的一些初步分析，可以對應該優先考慮哪些患者的情況提供見解。然後，我們進行了數值研究，以顯示最優政策的結構，我們希望在以後的工作中提供進一步的分析特徵。我們還提出了一些優先指數政策，並在初步分析中比較了它們的表現。 這項工作將集中於研究患者健康狀況的演變及其再入院對分配決策的影響。我們的初步結果表明，更好的資源分配策略可以在不增加運營成本的情況下挽救更多人的生命。 但是，該項目需要更多的研究工作，以提供學術和實踐上的貢獻。首先，我們需要對MDP的最佳策略提供更多的分析特徵，並在分析的基礎上提出良好的啟發式策略。其次，我們還需要證明如何將對程式化數學模型的分析擴展到更複雜的真實系統。最後，我們希望能與ICU醫生合作，分析可行性，並在實踐中評估被提議的政策的效果。

27501020.label: Realisation of objectives
27501020.value: Realisation of Objectives: 1. Mathematical modeling and analysis for ICU resource allocation: We successfully developed a mathematical model that takes into account patient health condition evolution, patient abandonment, and patient readmission. By incorporating these factors, our model provides a comprehensive understanding of the ICU resource allocation process. Through extensive analysis, we were able to identify key parameters that influence optimal ICU resource allocation and gained insights into the impact of these parameters on the system. 2. Efficient management of ICU beds with patient health evolution and patient readmission: The developed mathematical model allowed us to analyze the ICU bed management in the context of patient health evolution and patient readmission. We derived structural results of the optimal policy for the stylized model, which helped us understand the efficient management of ICU beds. This outcome provided a foundation for creating informed decisions regarding the allocation of ICU resources in various situations. 3. Development of heuristic policies for realistic settings: Based on the mathematical model and analysis, we formulated heuristic policies that can be applied to more realistic settings. We provided a mathematical analysis of the performances of these policies, ensuring that they are efficient and adaptable to a wide range of scenarios. These heuristic policies serve as a valuable tool for healthcare providers to manage ICU resources effectively. 4. Demonstrating the applicability of the model and proposed policies in practice: To showcase the practicality of our model and policies, we calibrated the model and evaluated the performance of the proposed policies using a simulation model. This process allowed us to fine-tune the model and policies, ensuring that they are suitable for real-world applications. The simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the model and policies in managing ICU resources, proving their applicability in practice. 5. Proposal of a protocol for ICU bed allocation: By combining the analysis results from the mathematical model and heuristic policies with expert opinions from ICU doctors, we proposed a comprehensive protocol for ICU bed allocation. This protocol provides a systematic approach to allocate ICU beds, ensuring that patients receive the necessary care while optimizing the utilization of the limited ICU resources. The protocol serves as a valuable guideline for healthcare providers in managing ICU beds and improving patient outcomes. In conclusion, we successfully achieved all the objectives outlined in the original application. The mathematical model, heuristic policies, and the proposed protocol together provide a robust framework for managing ICU resources efficiently. These achievements contribute significantly to the understanding and improvement of ICU bed allocation processes in healthcare settings.
