27501020.label: Major findings and research outcome
27501020.value: Our research project primarily focused on developing a comprehensive understanding of the resource allocation process in Intensive Care Units (ICUs). The project's significant findings and outcomes are as follows: 1. Mathematical Model Development: We developed a robust mathematical model to optimize the allocation of ICU resources. This model considers critical factors such as patient health condition evolution, patient abandonment, and patient readmission. The development of this model is a key outcome of our research, providing a mathematical basis for understanding and improving ICU resource allocation. 2. Insight into ICU Management: The analysis of the mathematical model yielded crucial insights into efficient ICU bed management. We discovered that parameters such as ICU capacity, patient characterization, and demand process significantly influence optimal ICU resource allocation. Understanding these parameters and their effects on resource allocation can guide ICU management decisions. 3. Heuristic Policies: The project led to the creation of effective heuristic policies that can be applied in realistic settings. These policies, validated through mathematical analysis, provide practical solutions for managing ICU resources efficiently and effectively. 4. Practical Applicability: We demonstrated the practical applicability of our model and proposed policies through a simulation model. This simulation showed that our model and policies can be effectively used in real-world scenarios, supporting their practicality and adaptability. 5. ICU Bed Allocation Protocol: One of the significant outcomes of our research is the proposal of a comprehensive protocol for ICU bed allocation. This protocol combines our mathematical and heuristic analysis results with expert opinions from ICU doctors. It provides a systematic approach to ICU bed allocation, contributing to the efficient utilization of resources and improved patient outcomes. 6. Contribution to Healthcare Management: Our research offers significant contributions to healthcare management, particularly in ICU settings. By providing a mathematical model, heuristic policies, and a comprehensive protocol, we offer tools and strategies that can significantly improve ICU resource allocation. This improvement can lead to better patient care and outcomes, highlighting the real-world impact of our research. In conclusion, our project has led to major advancements in understanding and improving ICU resource allocation. The findings and outcomes of our research have the potential to significantly influence healthcare management, leading to more efficient resource use and better patient care.

27501020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27501020.value: The potential for further development of this research is vast, as the healthcare industry continues to evolve and face new challenges. Several avenues can be explored to expand upon the current findings and enhance their applicability. Firstly, our current mathematical model can be expanded to include other important factors, such as varying patient acuity levels, staff availability, and the influence of external factors like pandemics or seasonal fluctuations in patient admissions. Incorporating these factors will lead to an even more comprehensive understanding of ICU resource allocation. Secondly, the developed model and policies can be adapted and applied to other healthcare settings, such as emergency departments, operating rooms, and general wards. This would allow for further improvements in resource allocation across the healthcare system, ensuring efficiency and effectiveness in various care settings. Another direction for future research is the integration of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics. These technologies can enhance the model's predictive capabilities and optimize resource allocation decisions in real-time, providing a cutting-edge approach to healthcare management. Furthermore, conducting longitudinal studies to evaluate the long-term effects of implementing the proposed allocation protocol can provide valuable insights into its overall impact on patient outcomes, staff satisfaction, and cost efficiency. These studies would help validate the research outcomes and promote their adoption in healthcare settings. Lastly, partnering with hospitals and healthcare providers to implement the proposed model, policies, and protocol will enable the collection of real-world data and feedback. This collaboration will not only refine the research outcomes but also facilitate their widespread adoption, leading to better resource management and improved patient care in healthcare settings.

27501020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27501020.value: This research project focused on improving the way resources, specifically beds, are allocated in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) at hospitals. ICUs provide critical care to severely ill patients, and the efficient management of ICU beds is essential to ensure timely treatment for those in need. Our project aimed to develop a mathematical model and practical guidelines to help healthcare providers make informed decisions about ICU bed allocation. We considered various factors, such as the changing health conditions of patients, the possibility of patients leaving the ICU prematurely, and the likelihood of patients needing to return to the ICU. Our model helped us understand how different aspects of ICU management affect the best allocation of resources. We also created practical policies that can be applied in real-life hospital settings to manage ICU beds more effectively. Additionally, we proposed a comprehensive protocol for ICU bed allocation, which combines our research findings with expert opinions from ICU doctors. This protocol provides a systematic approach to manage ICU beds and improve patient outcomes. Our research has the potential to significantly impact healthcare management by providing valuable insights and tools for better resource allocation in ICUs. Ultimately, this can lead to more efficient use of resources, improved patient care, and better overall outcomes in critical care settings.

27504520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27504520.value: As news aggregator apps have grown in popularity, so has newsfeed native advertising. It is estimated that native advertisements, so called because they are strategically displayed to fit into their surrounding context, will account for 63% of mobile ad revenue by 2020 in the US. In China, the newsfeed native advertising market is expected to reach $22 billion in 2019. While studies have investigated native ad detection and the effects of ad customization, the literature on native advertising remains limited. Native advertisements are designed to impose minimal disruption; a feature that might also call their effectiveness into question. For instance, a native ad may fail to expose the advertised product or induce readers to the ads they are not intended to. Hence, how to strategically design and display newsfeed native ads is an important yet under-investigated topic for both advertisers and advertising platforms. The primary goals of the proposed research are: 1) to investigate when and how newsfeed native advertising should be fed to readers, and 2) to understand how between- and within-consumer heterogeneity affects consumers’ reactions to newsfeed native advertising. Specifically, the proposed research plans to investigate the effects of various advertisement features on two sequential outcome variables: click-through and dwell time. The research will also investigate behavior patterns of newsfeed readers, i.e., the various patterns of readers’ reactions toward newsfeed ads and the mechanism underlying these patterns. The findings of the research are expected to make contributions from three perspectives. Theoretically, the research is expected to contribute to the mobile personalized native advertising literature. It will be among the first to empirically investigate constantly updating native advertisements. The research also plans to explore various behavior patterns along multiple dimensions, further advancing understanding of consumer journeys. Methodologically, the study will be among the first to process unstructured newsfeed data with machine learning techniques. The research incorporates Type II Tobit model and Hidden Markov Model to analyze sequential outcomes while addressing for within- and between-consumer heterogeneity. Managerially, the findings of the proposed research are expected to help news aggregator apps feed native ads more strategically. In addition, the findings of the research are expected to shed light on the key features newsfeed native advertising and their potential influences on advertising efficiency. 随着信息流应用的流行，信息流原生广告在广告商中愈发流行。由于其较好的嵌入的周遭环境的特点，信息流广告受到了广告商的青睐。原生广告预计在2020年会达到63%的美国移动段广告收入，并且在中国市场达到22亿美元。 尽管信息流广告在业界中非常流行，学术圈鲜有研究。现有的文献研究了原生广告的甄别(Campbell & Evans, 2018; Wojdynski & Evans, 2016)和定制化广告的效果(Aribarg & Schwartz, 2018)。虽然原生广告被设计成尽量少的影响消费者的浏览体验，但是这些特点可能会对其广告效果产生影响。比如，原生广告可能会误导消费者点击广告，从而产生不好的效果。因此，如何有计划的设计和展示信息流广告是一个重要但是并没有得到深入研究的问题。 本研究的主要目的有两个：一是研究何时与如何将信息流广告推送给消费者，二是了解消费者浏览过程中与消费者之间差异对于信息流广告推送效果的影响。更准确的说，本研究计划研究信息流广告的性质对于两个结果变量—点击率与浏览时间—的影响。此外，本研究也计划研究信息流app使用者的多种行为方式，即不同的消费者与消费者在不同时间对于信息流广告特点的反应的差异，与背后的行为原理。 本研究的发现将会对三个方面产生贡献。理论上，本研究将会对移动定制化广告与原生广告的文献做出贡献。本研究是最先的几个从实证角度研究信息流广告的文章，同时探究了消费者的几种行为方式与消费者的行为发展历程。方法上，本研究是第一批利用机器学习方法来处理非结构性文字信息的文中之一。除此之外，本研究结合了第二类Tobit模型和隐马尔可夫模型来研究次序性结果变量，并且控制了消费者之间和消费者变化的差异性。实践角度上，本研究提出了对于信息流广告商策略的建议。此外，本研究还提出了信息流原生广告的几个关键特性与其对于广告效果的影响。

27504520.label: Realisation of objectives
27504520.value: 1. To identify the key features of newsfeed native advertisements and investigate the effects of the features on two sequential outcome variables. Response: The PI has identified various features of newsfeed native ads (hereafter infeed ads) from channel, format, and design perspectives. First, in a published journal paper (Journal of Marketing), the PI demonstrated that the effectiveness of infeed native advertisements is influenced by the advertising channel (subscription vs. recommendation), the advertising appeal (informational vs. emotional), and advertising conversion type (direct vs. indirect). Further, in a working paper (4th round revision at Journal of Marketing), the PI investigates the effects of channel characteristics and the interplay among ads appearing in the newsfeed, social feed, and video feed on the click-through rate and conversion rate. The PI quantifies the direct, carryover, and spillover effects among the infeed native ads across the three infeed channels. Lastly, in another working paper, the PI investigates the effects of infeed ads' relevance and organicity (regarding surrounding organic content) on the click-through and dwell time. 2. To explore various newsfeed readers' behavioral patterns toward newsfeed advertisements with different features and uncover the underlying mechanisms. Response: The PI has studied consumer behavioral patterns that could impact the effectiveness of infeed ads and the underlying mechanism from channel, format, and design perspectives. Firstly, in a published journal paper, the PI discovered that consumers in the subscription channel tend to perceive higher source credibility and more content control than those in the recommendation channel. These differences lead consumers to perceive stronger intrusiveness of infeed ads. Further, in a working paper (4th round revision at Journal of Marketing), the PI found that consumers in the social feed channel tend to have the highest cognitive engagement, those in the video feed channel tend to have the highest emotional engagement, while consumers in the newsfeed channel typically have the weakest cognitive and emotional engagement. These varying behavioral patterns result in differences in direct, carryover, and spillover effects across the three channels. Lastly, in another working paper, the PI identified three latent statuses of newsfeed consumers. These statuses differ in the depth and width of engagement, and these differences lead to varying effects of different infeed ads. 3. To investigate the impacts of within- and between-consumer heterogeneity on advertising effectiveness. Response: The PI has examined how the effectiveness of infeed ads varies between consumers and evolves within consumers. For variations between consumers, the PI: 1) explored how the effects of infeed ads differ among consumers using various types of social media, finding that the types of social media reflect consumers' usage status, and 2) studied how consumers' initial usage status affects their overall attitude towards infeed ads. For variations within consumers, the PI: 1) researched the effects of repeated ad exposure across different infeed advertising channels, finding that repeated ad exposure could lead to either synergy (through mere exposure) or wear-out (through fatigue) effects, and 2) investigated how consumers' attention evolves as the length of a usage session increases, further explaining why certain infeed ads might or might not be effective. 4. To provide strategic guidance for native advertisers and advertising platforms who aim to either increase the effectiveness of the click-through or increase click-through rates. Response: Given the popularity of social media, infeed native ads are widely used in the mobile advertising industry. Due to the distinct features of infeed ads, marketers should consider the nuanced impacts of the interplay between the surrounding context and the infeed ads themselves when implementing these ads. Through examining how consumers perceive the fit between an infeed ad and its surrounding context across three research studies, the PI has provided various actionable strategies for optimal infeed advertising in terms of ad placement, ad design, and resource allocation. These strategies take into account multiple desired metrics, including maximizing clicks, dwell time, conversions, and cost-efficiency.

27504520.label: Major findings and research outcome
27504520.value: Supported by the ECS project, the PI and collaborators have completed three papers that examine different aspects of infeed ads in various contexts. -- The first paper was published in the Journal of Marketing (one of the top four journals in the field of marketing) in 2023: Dong, Beibei, Mengzhou Zhuang, Eric Fang, and Minxue Huang. "Tales of two channels: digital advertising performance between AI recommendation and user subscription channels." Journal of Marketing 88, no. 2 (2024): 141-162. This research investigates how the performance of infeed ads, in terms of click-through rates and conversion rates, differs between subscription and recommendation channels. The study examines whether these effects are mediated by ad intrusiveness and moderated by ad attributes. The findings reveal that the recommendation channel generates higher click-through rates but lower conversion rates than the subscription channel. These effects are amplified by informational ad appeal and direct ad links -- The second paper is currently under fourth round revision at the Journal of Marketing (one of the top four journals in the field of marketing): Yiyi Li, Mengzhou Zhuang, and Eric Fang. “Multichannel Effects of Mobile Infeed Advertising.” Working paper In this research, an integrated model is proposed, and the direct, carryover, and spillover effects of infeed ads in multiple types of mobile apps (newsfeed, social, and video) are empirically investigated. The findings show that social feed ads have the strongest contemporaneous effects on both ad clicks and conversions. Second, video feed ads have the strongest carryover effect, followed by social feed ads, while newsfeed ads have a negative carryover effect. Third, the strongest spillover effect is observed for newsfeed ads. -- The third paper is prepared for journal submission: Mengzhou Zhuang and Eric Fang. “Newsfeed Advertising Effectiveness Under Different Consumer Behavior States.” Working paper This research examines the effects of ad-organic features, i.e., relevance (the consistency between the post and consumers' interests) and organicity (the extent to which the post looks like organic posts), on two advertising effectiveness measures. The study identifies three browsing behavior statuses and demonstrates that the effects of ad relevance and organicity on clicking and reading vary with these behavior states. -- In addition to the aforementioned journal publications/submissions, the PI has presented the major findings in seminars at major universities in Hong Kong or Mainland China, as well as at leading international conferences, such as the ISMS Marketing Science annual conference.

27504520.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27504520.value: First, future research could explore the market dynamics of infeed ads in relation to various pricing strategies. Commonly adopted pricing strategies in the market include click-based (pay-per-click), action-based (pay-per-action), and impression-based (pay-per-thousand impressions). These pricing strategies could significantly impact ad design and placement. For example, advertisers on a click-based platform may be less likely to use native infeed ads (i.e., ads that look like organic content) to avoid clicks with low engagement, while they prefer native infeed ads for an impression-based platform to increase reachability. Second, future research could investigate how consumers react to different ad disclosure. Although most countries require platforms to disclose the sponsored nature of infeed ads, platforms or advertisers might intentionally design the label to be less obvious. Such misleading labeling could potentially benefit advertisers and platforms in the short run (i.e., click bait), but it might backfire in the long run as it frequently misleads consumers and disrupts their usage experiences. Lastly, future research could extend the current research to examine the interplay between infeed ads and other popular types of mobile ads, such as embedded ads and banners. This would provide a more comprehensive advertising allocation and design strategies for platforms and advertisers.

27504520.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27504520.value: Infeed advertising is an expanding type of native advertising. Native advertising involves sponsored content like paid search and advertorial content that looks like the surrounding organic content. An infeed ad seamlessly appears in the organic feed, matches its format and aesthetics, and is disclosed as sponsored or promoted. Through research, the PI explored how infeed ads could help advertisers achieve goals, such as promoting products or attracting traffic in various social media contexts. Additionally, the PI discovered that infeed ad effectiveness depends on the surrounding context and alignment with the advertiser's goal. In contrast to the contradicting and confusing suggestions on the Internet, the PI provides clear and practical guidance for advertisers or platforms regarding optimal ad design, allocation, and placement strategies based on desired advertising metrics. This guidance leads advertisers to use their advertising budget more effectively and avoid disrupting consumers with inappropriate products at the wrong time. The platform could also rely on the findings to arrange the infeed ad placement.

27504620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27504620.value: 积极股东与公司价值：董事会的作用

27504620.label: Project Objectives
27504620.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to develop a corporate governance model to understand the implications of shareholder activism. Specifically, the effect of direct shareholder intervention on the investment decision. The model has potentials to explain the joint determination of board composition, optimal contracting and investment decisions. This is a hybrid model that combines strategic communication and moral hazard in the optimal contracting framework. Formalize the mechanism of how shareholder activism affects firm value in a three-player game. This model enables a rigorous analysis of how shareholder intervention affects the incentives of the intermediary, i.e., the board of directors and how that, in turn, affects the communication and investment decision making by the CEO. Based on the analysis, derive conditions under which shareholder activism lead to a higher level of board effort, better communication outcome and more efficient investment decision-making. Further, characterize the conditions under which shareholder activism is beneficial to shareholder value, firm value and social welfare. Provide policy implications to policy makers and regulators on shareholder activism. There is an ongoing debate internationally on whether shareholder activism is value-enhancing or destructive. This project has the potential to identify cases where shareholder activism is beneficial. The model also has potentials to shed light on the mixed empirical evidence on shareholder activism and highlights the importance of endogeneity of the incentives of the board of directors.

27504620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27504620.value: In a typical corporate setting the CEO is endowed with private information relevant for decision making, but there is an agency problem – specifically, the CEO is an empire builder. To alleviate the dependence on the CEO for information, the shareholders can hire an intermediary (e.g., a board consisting of industry expert or a consultant) to collect information about the environment. If the intermediary’s information gathering fails, the shareholders need to turn to the CEO for information. This move helps avoid the strategic communication problem due to the CEO’s misaligned preferences. However, it creates a moral hazard problem. Instead of making decisions themselves, the shareholders can delegate the decision right to the intermediary ex-ante. Such ex-ante delegation will improve the intermediary’s incentive to collect information, however at the cost of the potential investment distortion (to the shareholders). My aim is to evaluate whether the shareholders benefit from keeping the decision right to themselves. In either case, the shareholders have the option to appoint an intermediary with a possibly biased preference over the decision to be made that deviates from that of the shareholders. Such a decision bias on the part of the intermediary may help motivate the latter to collect information. 在典型的公司环境中首席执行官拥有与决策相关的信息，但存在代理人问题：首席执行官倾向于大工程。为了减轻对首席执行官信息的依赖，股东可以聘请中介机构（例如由行业专家或顾问组成的董事会）收集有关环境的信息。如果中介的信息收集失败，股东需要向首席执行官寻求信息。此举有助于避免由于首席执行官的偏好不一致而导致沟通出现问题。然而这造成了道德风险问题。除了自己做决定外，股东可以事前将决定权委托中介机构。事前放权将改善中介机构收集信息的动机，但是会潜在扭曲投资成本（对股东而言）。本研究的目的是评估股东是否从保留自己的决定权中受益。无论哪种情况下，股东都可以选择可能偏向于偏离股东偏好的中介机构。中介机构的这种决策偏见可能有助于激发信息收集。

27504620.label: Realisation of objectives
27504620.value: The project successfully achieved its primary objectives, as evidenced by the development of a dynamic model that has been accepted for publication in The Accounting Review. This model addresses the impact of large shareholders on capital markets, focusing on the effects of disclosure in a dynamic market with imperfect competition. Below is a detailed account of how each project objective was realized: Objective 1: Develop a Dynamic Model to Understand Large Shareholders’ Impact on the Capital Market The main objective of the project was to create a dynamic model that could elucidate the impact of large shareholders on capital markets, particularly in terms of their influence on asset supply and market dynamics. This objective was fully realized. The developed model demonstrates that large shareholders, due to their market power, trade gradually to diversify their concentrated ownership, affecting asset prices over multiple trading rounds. The model captures the interplay between large shareholders and small investors, highlighting how market dynamics evolve when a large shareholder lacks commitment to a pre-determined trading strategy. This dynamic approach offers new insights into the complexities of risk-sharing in markets with significant ownership concentration. Objective 2: Formalize the Mechanism of How Large Shareholders Affect the Cost of Capital in a Dynamic Trading Game The project successfully formalized the mechanism by which large shareholders influence the cost of capital within a dynamic trading framework. The model shows that the presence of large shareholders, who possess market power, alters the relationship between disclosure and cost of capital across multiple trading stages. The analysis reveals that the gradual trading by large shareholders due to their price impact introduces a non-monotonic relationship between disclosure precision and the cost of capital. This finding is significant as it reconciles mixed empirical results in the literature by providing a coherent theoretical explanation for how dynamic trading affects market outcomes. Objective 3: Derive Conditions Under Which Large Shareholders Influence the Relationship Between Mandatory Disclosure Precision and Cost of Capital This objective was achieved by deriving specific conditions under which the presence of large shareholders leads to a non-monotonic relationship between mandatory disclosure precision and the cost of capital. The model demonstrates that while precise disclosure can impede risk-sharing by resolving uncertainty too early, it can also promote risk-sharing by encouraging more trading. The research identifies an optimal level of disclosure precision that maximizes total market surplus, benefiting small investors at the expense of large shareholders’ monopoly rents. The conditions outlined in the model provide clear empirical implications, helping to explain the variations in cost of capital observed across different disclosure regimes. Objective 4: Provide Empirical Implications for Research on Disclosure and Cost of Capital The project has generated valuable empirical implications that advance the literature on disclosure and cost of capital. By proposing a novel theoretical channel through which large shareholders and dynamic trading opportunities influence the cost of capital, the research offers a framework for understanding previously inconsistent empirical findings. The model’s predictions suggest that the impact of disclosure on the cost of capital is contingent on the degree of market power held by large shareholders and the timing of their trades relative to disclosure events. These insights are expected to guide future empirical studies and contribute to a more nuanced understanding of the role of disclosure in capital markets. In conclusion, the project has successfully met all its objectives, making substantial contributions to the understanding of large shareholders’ influence on capital markets, particularly in the context of disclosure and cost of capital. The research outputs, including the forthcoming publication, reflect the thorough and innovative approach taken to achieve these goals.

Based on the analysis, derive conditions under which the large shareholder who can dynamically diversify away from initial holdings leads to a non-monotonic relationship between mandatory disclosure precision and cost of capital. Further, characterize the conditions under which disclosure promotes trades and enhances risk-sharing.

Provide empirical implications for research on disclosure and cost of capital. Prior research finds mixed empirical evidence and lacks a coherent underlying theory. This project can contribute to the literature by reconciling the mixed findings by proposing a novel channel of how disclosure affects the cost of capital in presence of a large shareholder and multiple trading opportunities.

27504620.label: Major findings and research outcome
27504620.value: This project has produced significant findings that contribute to the understanding of large shareholders' impact on capital markets, particularly in the context of disclosure and cost of capital. The major findings and research outcomes can be summarized as follows: 1. Dynamic Model of Large Shareholders' Impact: The project developed a dynamic model that captures the interaction between large shareholders and small investors in a market characterized by imperfect competition. The model demonstrates that large shareholders, due to their market power, trade gradually to diversify their concentrated ownership. This gradual trading affects asset prices over multiple rounds, illustrating how large shareholders' actions can influence market dynamics and risk-sharing. 2. Non-Monotonic Relationship Between Disclosure and Cost of Capital: A key finding of the research is the non-monotonic relationship between mandatory disclosure precision and the cost of capital. The model shows that while precise disclosure can destroy risk-sharing opportunities by resolving uncertainty too early, it can also enhance risk-sharing by promoting more trading. The optimal level of disclosure precision, as identified by the model, maximizes total market surplus and benefits small investors, albeit at the expense of the large shareholder's monopoly rents. 3. Empirical Implications for Disclosure and Capital Markets: The research provides empirical implications that reconcile mixed findings in the literature regarding the effects of disclosure on the cost of capital. The model offers a novel theoretical channel that explains how dynamic trading by large shareholders, in conjunction with varying disclosure regimes, influences the cost of capital. These insights are expected to inform future empirical studies, providing a deeper understanding of the conditions under which disclosure affects market outcomes. 4. Publication and Dissemination: The research findings have been recognized for their contribution to the field, with the paper resulting from this project being accepted for publication in The Accounting Review, a leading academic journal. This publication will disseminate the findings to a broader academic audience, further validating the significance of the research outcomes. In summary, this project has successfully achieved its objectives, producing a dynamic model that advances the theoretical and empirical understanding of large shareholders' influence on capital markets. The major findings offer new insights into the relationship between disclosure precision and cost of capital, providing a solid foundation for future research in this area.

27504620.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27504620.value: The research conducted in this project has opened several avenues for further exploration and development. One promising direction is the empirical validation of the model’s predictions, particularly in different market settings and with various types of large shareholders, such as activist investors or institutional funds. This would enhance the generalizability of the findings and provide robust empirical evidence supporting the theoretical model. Additionally, extending the model to incorporate more complex disclosure regimes, including voluntary disclosures and differential timing of disclosures, could provide deeper insights into how firms strategically manage information release in the presence of large shareholders. This would be particularly relevant in the context of recent regulatory changes and the growing importance of transparency in corporate governance. The proposed course of action includes applying for additional funding to support empirical studies that test the model’s predictions and collaborating with other researchers to expand the theoretical framework to include a wider range of market conditions and shareholder behaviors.

27504620.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27504620.value: This research project focused on understanding how large shareholders, such as company founders or major investors, influence the financial markets. The study developed a model to explore how these large shareholders trade their shares over time and how this trading affects the prices of those shares and the overall cost of raising money for companies. One of the key findings is that the timing and amount of information companies share with the public can either help or hinder the sharing of financial risks among different investors. The research shows that when companies share too much information too soon, it can prevent investors from effectively managing their risks. However, sharing the right amount of information at the right time can encourage more trading, leading to greater welfare. This research is valuable because it offers new insights into how financial markets work, especially in situations where a few big players have a lot of influence (for example, the "Mega 7" companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet). The findings can help policymakers and regulators design better rules for how and when companies should disclose information, ultimately leading to more stable and efficient markets.

27505320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27505320.value: 了解在线劳动力市场中的匹配动态

27505320.label: Project Objectives
27505320.value: The overall objective is to better understand the matching dynamics between buyers and sellers of online labor markets. The four points below are objectives that will help us achieve this overall objective. To understand how clients of OLMs trade off quality and price. A client may be willing to pay more for a more qualified freelancer, or she may willing to hire a less qualified freelancer that charges a lower price. We must also define a metric for a freelancer’s quality. Since clients’ needs and freelancers’ skills are heterogeneous, a freelancer that is of high quality for one job may be of low quality for another job. Therefore, the freelancer’s quality must be defined using a combination of observable features, including but not limited to skill, experience, expertise, reputation, etc. To understand how freelancers decide what price to charge. Freelancers submit applications for job requests that include the price they expect to be paid for completing the job. In response to how clients trade off quality and price, freelancers must decide on a price that maximizes their overall utility. To understand how clients and freelancers respond to exogenous shocks to demand and supply.

27505320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27505320.value: Online labor markets (OLM) are platforms that allow buyers to purchase specific skills and services from freelancers possessing the required skills and offering said services. Together with the rise of ride-hailing platforms such as Uber and room-sharing platforms such as Airbnb, OLMs are increasingly popular in matching the supply and demand for human capital. Unlike traditional labor markets where employees work for a company that serves clients, freelancers on OLMs serve clients directly and are paid for the work that they do. The platform, through mechanisms such as feedback, reputation systems, and recommendations, is able to provide quality matches for buyers and sellers and reduce search frictions. A key difference between OLMs and other sharing economy platforms is that client needs and freelancer skills are extremely heterogeneous. This creates a high level of complexity for both parties when deciding whether to work together and at what price. Moreover, as they are able to consider multiple suitors concurrently, choosing to match with one freelancer means foregoing another (and potentially better) option, and vice versa. In this setting, the incentive of clients is to hire the candidate who can successfully complete their request at the lowest cost, the incentive of freelancers is to win and complete jobs that require the least effort but earn the greatest payment, and the incentive of the platform is to facilitate as many matches as possible for the largest amount of monetary exchange. The general aim of this research is to improve our understanding of how clients and freelancers decide on matches through rigorous empirical analysis. Given the client-freelancer dynamics of OLMs, this naturally leads to the following questions. First, how do clients trade off between the quality of the freelancer and the price that is charged? Second, how do freelancers decide what price to charge? Finally, how do clients and freelancers respond to exogenous demand or supply shocks, especially when the pool of potential suitors become heavily unbalanced? By answering these questions, OLMs will be able to better facilitate matches through their managerial levers. In a collaboration with an industry-leading OLM, we study the matching dynamics between clients and freelancers of such a platform. We have obtained historical data of all job postings, applications, matches, and results from our partner and will combine empirical and experimental analyses to answer these three questions. 在线劳动力市场（OLM）是允许购买者从拥有所需技能并提供所需服务的自由职业者那里购买特定技能和服务的平台。随着Uber等打车平台和Airbnb等房间共享平台的兴起，OLM在匹配人力资本供求方面也越来越受欢迎。与传统的劳动力市场不同的是，传统的劳动力市场中公司雇佣员工继而公司作为一个整体为客户提供服务，而在在线劳动力市场（OLM）中，自由职业者直接为客户提供服务，客户直接向自由职业者支付报酬。OLM平台通过诸如反馈，信誉系统和推荐之类的机制，为买主和卖主提供高质量的匹配，并减少搜索摩擦降低搜索成本。 OLM与其他共享经济平台之间的主要区别在于，OLM上客户的需求和自由职业者所拥有的技能存在着极大的差异。由于这种差异，在决定是否一起工作以及以什么价格工作时，双方的决策都面临着高度的复杂性。此外，由于他们能够同时考虑多个求职的自由职业者，选择与一个自由职业者匹配意味着放弃了另一个（并且可能更好）的求职者，反之亦然。在这种情况下，客户的动机是聘用能以最低成本完成其需求的求职者，自由职业者的动机是尽可能地赢得报酬高且工作量少的工作并且成功地完成这些工作，而平台的动机是促成尽可能多的匹配，以实现最大程度的人力资本交换。 我们的这项研究的总体目的是通过严格的实证分析来提高我们对OLM中客户和自由职业者动态匹配的理解。具体来说，我们考虑以下问题。首先，客户如何在自由职业者所具备的技能和其所要求的价格之间进行权衡？其次，自由职业者如何确定要求的价格？最后，客户和自由职业者如何应对外来的需求或供应冲击，尤其是当潜在的求职者群体严重失衡时？通过回答这些问题，OLM将能够通过各种平台机制更好地促进人力和资本的匹配。在这项研究中，我们与行业领先的OLM达成合作，研究此类平台的客户与自由职业者之间的匹配动态。从合作伙伴处，我们已经获得了所有职位发布，申请，匹配过程和结果的历史数据，并将结合实证分析和实验来共同回答这三个问题。

27601920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27601920.value: 電氣中國: 中國電器工業史，1870–1937

27601920.label: Project Objectives
27601920.value: Conduct the first comprehensive archival-based study of the Chinese electrical and electronics industries from the late 19th century to 1937 and thereby make a crucial contribution to modern Chinese business history and the history of capitalism in modern China. Bring the history of the electrical and electronics industries in modern China into conversation with the wider growing scholarly literature on the global business history of electrification. Make an important contribution to the scholarly literature on the history of technology and consumption in modern China by explaining the historical development of a consumer market for electrical goods in China. Provide students, professionals, policymakers and the general public with crucial historical background knowledge of the development of two key industries—the electrical and electronics industries—in the current Chinese economy, thereby affording them a better understanding of the contemporary and future development of these industries.

27601920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27601920.value: The proposed study will constitute the first comprehensive archival-based study of the electrical and electronics industries in prewar China. Today, these two sectors are leading industries in China and major contributors to China’s economic growth. However, despite their current importance to the Chinese economy, very little is known about the historical development of the electrical and electronics industries. Without this critical historical background knowledge of the long-term development of these industries, we remain unable to fully comprehend their contemporary and future development. The aim of the proposed research project, situated at the intersection of business history, the history of technology and the history of consumption, is to address this gap in the scholarly literature. It will do so by making use of British, German, American, Japanese and Chinese primary sources to trace the history of these two key industries during the period in which they first emerged in China – the period between the first influx of electrical technology in the late 19th century and the beginning of World War II in East Asia in 1937. The study will begin by investigating the early history of multinational electrical companies in China in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It will explore how these companies first introduced electrical goods and services into China and how they started to interact with Chinese entrepreneurs, officials and consumers. The study will then turn to the first private Chinese electrical companies that began to manufacture and market electrical goods in China and examine how they adapted foreign electrical products to the Chinese market between the 1910s and 1937. Finally, it will investigate the role that the Nationalist government and state-run electrical companies, and their competition and cooperation with other private Chinese and foreign companies, played in the growth of the electrical and electronics industries during the Nanjing Decade (1927-1937). In addition to its primary focus on the business history of the two industries, the study will also reconstruct Chinese consumers’ use and integration of electrical goods into their daily lives and how businesses interacted with those consumers. In sum, the proposed study will explain the role that the electrical and electronics industries played in the electrification of modern China and how the two industries can be situated in the broader development of Chinese business and the Chinese economy during the 19th and 20th centuries. 本研究項目為對於抗戰前中國電器工業史（即電氣及電子工業）的首個全面及以檔案史料為基礎的研究。今天，電器工業是構成中國工業的主導產業，也是中國經濟增長的主要貢獻者。然而，雖然電器工業對目前的中國經濟非常重要，人們對其歷史發展卻知之甚少。若缺乏對這些行業長期發展的重要歷史背景知識，我們會無法充分理解其當代和未來的發展。 本研究項目的目的是填補學術文獻中的這一空白。它位於商業史、技術史和消費史的交叉點, 將利用英國、德國、美國、日本和中國的原始資料來研究電器業在中國最初出現的歷史時期，即電氣技術首次湧入中國的19世紀末到1937年第二次世界大戰在東亞的爆發。 本研究將首先調查19世紀末和20世紀初跨國電器公司在中國的早期歷史. 它將探討這些公司如何將電器和電氣服務首次引入中國，以及它們如何開始與中國企業家、官員和消費者交流。然後，本研究將轉向最早開始在中國生產和銷售電器的中國私營電器公司，並研究他們如何在20世紀10年代至1937年間使外國電器適用於中國市場的條件。最後，本研究探討1927年–1937年期間內國民黨政府和國營電器公司與其他中外私營公司的競爭與合作，以及他們在電器工業發展所扮演的角色。除了主要關注電器工業的商業歷史外，本研究亦會調查中國消費者如何開始使用電器並將電器融入他們的日常生活，以及企業如何與這些消費者互動。 總括而言，本研究將解釋電器工業在近代中國電氣化過程中所發揮的作用和闡明我們可以如何將電器工業置於19世紀和20世紀中國商業及中國經濟發展的大環境中。

27602020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27602020.value: 用多源高分辨率遙感進行紅樹林分類及其分帶模式研究

27602020.label: Project Objectives
27602020.value: To classify the mangrove species at the local scale from multisource high-resolution remote sensing data using the Optical-SAR-LiDAR dictionary sparse representation classification (OSLD-SRC); To discriminate mangrove species at local and regional scales by developing a small-patched deep residual network (SDRN) from optical and dual-polarimetric SAR data using the Google Earth Engine cloud computing platform; To quantify and understand the mangrove species zonation patterns using the standard deviational ellipse (SDE) and landscape matrices at local and regional scales.

27602020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27602020.value: Mangroves are the only woody salt tolerant plants living in the transitional zones between the land and sea along the tropical and subtropical coastlines. They are among the most productive ecosystems and play an important role in the ecological functions of the coastal ecosystem and global carbon cycle. Mangroves provide commercial products and nursery habitats for assemblages of both fauna and flora and protect coastal regions from natural disasters and coastal erosion. However, due to increasing human activities, such as urbanization and aquaculture, mangrove forests have been continuously destroyed in the last few decades, causing significant ecological and economic losses with local, regional and global impacts. Zonation is the predictable and discrete ordering or pattern of mangrove species due to the unique intertidal environment. Describing and understanding the zonation patterns of mangrove species has preoccupied mangrove researchers for centuries. Understanding mangrove zonation patterns is important for assessing the functioning of these specific ecosystems as it has been attributed to the responses of individual species to variation in abiotic, biotic and human factors. However, most previous studies on the zonation of mangroves were based on field surveys, which lacked continuity in both the spatial and temporal dimensions. Remote sensing is a faster and more cost-effective way to monitor ecosystems and to assess regions that are inaccessible by humans due to their challenging environmental conditions or protected status. However, it remains difficult to accurately monitor mangroves using single remote sensing data due to the high diversity of mangrove species and the cloudy weather in tropical and subtropical regions. Quantifying mangrove zonation patterns using multisource remote sensing data at large scales is urgently needed to better understand the dynamics of mangrove communities and support their conservation and sustainability. To understand the zonation patterns of mangrove species from local to regional scales, the proposed research attempts to synergize multisource remote sensing data, including optical data, dual- and fully polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data and light imaging detection and ranging (LiDAR) data, which will be obtained from both satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). The Optical-SAR-LiDAR dictionary sparse representation classification (OSLD-SRC) and the small-patched deep residual networks (SDRN) will be developed for mangrove species discrimination at local and regional scales. Landscape metrics will be employed to quantify the zonation patterns of mangrove species at various scales. The developed methodology can be used to monitor mangrove species at local, regional and global scales. 紅樹林是唯一生長在熱帶和亞熱帶海岸線沿岸的海陸過渡帶中的木本耐鹽植物。紅樹林生態系統是生產力最高的生態系統之一，其在海岸生態系統的生態功能和全球碳循環中都發揮著重要作用。紅樹林能夠提供豐富的生態服務，為動植物群落提供棲息地，並保護沿海地區免受自然災害和海岸侵蝕。然而，在過去的幾十年中，由於城市化和水產養殖等人類活動的日益增加，紅樹林不斷遭到破壞，對當地乃至全球都造成了巨大的生態和經濟損失。 由於紅樹林處於獨特的潮間帶環境，分帶現象是紅樹林物種的可預測且離散的分佈模式。近幾十年來，紅樹林專家一直潛心鑽研如何描述和理解紅樹林物種的分帶形態。瞭解紅樹林分帶模式對於評估這些特定的生態系統功能非常重要，因為其主要歸因於單個物種對生物、非生物和人為因素變化的反應。然而，關於紅樹林分帶的大多數研究都是基於野外實地調查，缺乏在空間和時間維度上的連續性。遙感是一種更快、更具成本效益的監測和評估生態系統的方式，尤其是對於一些由於惡劣或受保護狀態的環境條件使得人類無法進入的區域。但是，由於紅樹林種類的多樣性以及熱帶和亞熱帶地區的多雲天氣，使用單一的遙感資料進行準確的紅樹林監測仍然存在困難。因此，使用多源遙感資料大規模量化紅樹林的分帶模式是一種迫切需求，以便更好地瞭解紅樹林群落的變化並支持其保護和穩定性。 為了瞭解紅樹林物種從本地到區域尺度的分區模式，此研究嘗試進行多源遙感數據協同，包括從衛星和無人機（UAV）獲取的光學數據，雙極化和全極化合成孔徑雷達數據（SAR）以及激光雷達數據（LiDAR）。此研究將建立Optical-SAR-LiDAR分類字典的稀疏表示（OSLD-SRC）和小斑塊深度殘差網路（SDRN），以在本地和區域範圍內對紅樹林物種進行區分。將使用景觀指數量化不同尺度下的紅樹林物種的分帶模式。此方法可應用於本地、區域和全球範圍內的紅樹林物種監測。

27602320.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27602320.value: 創造生活：冷戰時期好萊塢陰影中的虛構藝術

27602320.label: Project Objectives
27602320.value: To research and complete a book-length project which combines art-historical, political, social, and theoretical methodologies to recover and analyze the role of pseudonymity in artistic practice in the United States during the Cold War. To challenge the dominant art historical narrative of the post-World War II avant-garde art scene that conventionally situates New York as the art world center while ignoring the politically contentious and conceptually provocative programs of the California art scene. To integrate a discussion of pseudonymous artistic production (that is, artists realizing politically suspicious artworks under fictional names/characters and secret identities) into existing considerations of formal and conceptual artistic devices and developments. To consider how creative endeavors became a lightning rod for a national identity born in the conflict between freedom of expression and contemporaneous concerns—an inflated communist threat, class, gender, and racial inequality, and expanding U.S. involvement in Vietnam. To trace the important role that fake names and secret identities played in ideas about the intersection of art and politics in the U.S. during the Cold War.

27602320.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27602320.value: This research project examines how a group of California-based artists used the tools of anonymity, pseudonymity, heteronymity, public persona, biografiction, autobiografiction, and alter ego to critically examine not only the politics of the Cold War Era, but also the discipline of art history itself, which values and analyzes work by connecting a practice to a single, named artist-author or entity. Art historical scholarship has passingly noted the presence of pseudonyms within the art world, yet literature has yet to present a sustained, in-depth study of the larger phenomenon and its social, political, and market-based implications. As I demonstrate, within a 1940s and ’50s era colored by an inflated communist threat—leading to xenophobia, the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC), loyalty oaths, and the blacklisting of film industry professionals—artists baited and critiqued the paranoia then-gripping California by realizing politically suspicious artworks attributed to fictional artists and secret identities. As political concerns shifted in the 1960s and ’70s to calls for gender and racial equality and anti-Vietnam War protests, artists re-directed the tools of fiction and invention toward frustrating the prevalence of gendered and racial bias and criticizing the rise of celebrity culture and the administrative state. Using undiscussed archival records documenting pseudonymous artistic practices, this project accounts for, writes, and theorizes the history of fabricated authorship and fictional creativity in the United States (and primarily California) during the Cold War Era. The second purpose of this project is to trace how fictitious practices offer an overarching disciplinary critique. Historical discussions of art are built on documentation and archival evidence. Artists on the West Coast manufactured the documentation of ‘lives lived’ while also showing how those lives were fabricated, thus demonstrating the power and the fallibility of nominal identity and biography as interpretative tools. Here, I present two historiographical interventions. First, by showcasing previously undiscussed pseudonymous artworks realized by well-known artists, I demonstrate how the West Coast avant-garde critiqued a commodified art market assigning value according to name-brand. Second, I theorize the many techniques of nominal obfuscation, demonstrating how such tools offered a mechanism for realizing politically contentious artworks within a conservative, racialized, and masculinist environment. The project’s principal objective is to complete a book manuscript offering the first account of pseudonymous artistic practice as a prominent mode of social and political engagement. I also anticipate realizing one additional article which contributes to the fields of art history, legal studies, and American studies. 這個研究項目將分析一群加利福尼亞的藝術家如何通過使用匿名、假名、異名、公眾角色、傳記小說、自傳小說和另我分析，不僅反思了冷戰時期的政治，而且批判了藝術史本身，因為傳統的藝術史通常將一種藝術實踐和單個藝術家或單一實體聯繫起來。藝術史學已經註意到了藝術世界中存在假名，但是既有文獻尚未對這種更普遍的現象及其社會，政治和市場影響進行持續、深入的研究。 我的研究將展示，在1940年代和50年代，共產主義威脅的加劇導致了仇外心理—眾議院成立非美活動調查委員會（the House Un-American Activities Committee，HUAC），受懷疑者被逼迫發「效忠」誓，部分電影業人士被列入黑名單—藝術家將可疑的藝術品歸功於虛構的作者和神秘的身份，從而迷惑和批評當時加州大行其道的政治妄想。在1960年代和70年代，當政治重心轉向呼籲性別與種族平等和反越南戰爭抗議時，藝術家又利用起小說和虛構的手法，打擊盛行的性別和種族偏見，批評興起的名人文化和日漸強勢的行政國家。 通過使用記載假名應用實踐的新歷史檔案，這項研究將冷戰時期美國（主要是加州）偽造身份和虛構創作的歷史進行記錄和理論化。 此研究的第二個目的是追溯虛擬實踐如何提供總體的學科批評。有關藝術史的討論是建立在文獻和檔案證據基礎之上的。美國西海岸的藝術家製造出人們「生活」的檔案，同時也展示了這些生活是如何被創造出來的。因此，他們揭示出名義身份和傳記作為解釋工具既可以十分強大，又可能存在謬誤。在這裡，我將應用兩種歷史學的研究方法。首先，通過揭示知名藝術家的匿名作品鮮有人問津，我將顯示西海岸的前衛藝術家如何批評商業化的藝術市場根據品牌名稱來定作品價值。其次，我將混淆名義的種種技術理論化，說明這些技術如何在保守、種族化和男性主義當道的環境中，為具有政治爭議性的藝術品提供平台。 這個項目的主要目標是完成一本書的手稿。該書將首先介紹匿名藝術實踐如何成為社會和政治參與的重要手段。我還預期完成另一篇論文，並希望該論文對藝術史，法學研究和美國研究有所貢獻。

27602720.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27602720.value: 藝術與女性的 ‘四海為家’之夢

27602720.label: Project Objectives
27602720.value: To fill a long-standing gap in scholarly research on the study of contemporary transnational art by not only conducting in-depth research into the practices of six women artists from vastly different geopolitical backgrounds and working conditions, but also by addressing the role of art in mediating issues of gender, place, identity and belonging in a global context. This project responds to the urgent need to reconsider women’s contributions to the constitution and representation of sociocultural and geopolitical realities within the international art world beyond Euro-American centres. The publications, especially the monograph, arising from this project will introduce new content and theoretical paradigms to the ongoing construction of a feminist history of art and to the discussion of contemporary art in relation to globalisation, transnational migration and cross-cultural identification and negotiation. To explore the notion of ‘homemaking’ at three different levels, by analysing these chosen artists’ various forms of engagement with domesticity in their practices, their negotiations with international art institutions and the market, as well as their artistic habitation of ‘home’ across regional and national boundaries, which creates productive conditions of identification and disidentification with multiple places, cultures and people. This project considers how contemporary art might enable us to imagine alternative ways of inhabiting the world with others and to reflect on the unprecedented fluidity and uprootedness of human life in connection with the intertwining engagement of global capitalism and local development. To conduct research into theoretical debates on affective labour, ethics of care, neoliberal globalisation, embodied subjectivity and queer disidentification in the fields of feminist philosophy, queer studies, the social sciences and cultural studies, so as to bring to the fore the discussion of the three thematic issues of ‘homemaking’ in this project: affective domesticity, embodied habitation and transcultural (dis)identification. By adopting a transdisciplinary approach, this project investigates how theoretical enquires provoke insightful reflections on these women artists’ multifaceted exploration of social development and transnational engagement. It also considers how their works also shed light on the discussion of identity, human agency and social collectivity in connection with the practices and processes of globalisation. To analyse the works of Yin, Tan, Hatoum, Shen, Lee and Akiyoshi via three interrelated chapters on artistic fantasies of ‘homemaking’: ‘Domestic Preservation’ (Yin and Tan), ‘Conflictual Connection’ (Hatoum and Shen) and ‘Vernacular Conviviality’ (Lee and Akiyoshi). This analysis will also further elaborate and cross-fertilise with the three central themes of ‘homemaking’ mentioned above. To incorporate collected materials and research findings into the PI’s undergraduate teaching on feminist art history and contemporary transnational art; and to collaborate with local art organisations, such as the Asia Society and Asia Art Archive, and deliver one or two public talks on women making art and transnational ‘homemaking’ to local audiences. To compile collected primary and secondary materials and build up a research archive on each woman artist, which will eventually be donated to the Asia Art Archive after the completion of the project to support relevant research by scholars and students. To present two academic conference papers on the topic which will help disseminate the findings and insights gained from this project to the broader international academic community; and to complete the manuscript of a full-length, single-authored monograph and prepare its submission to an international university press.

27602720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27602720.value: This project examines the intricate interrelation between women, domesticity and artistic practice in association with growing international travel and cross-cultural exchange, which significantly challenge the conventional notions of home, identity and belonging. A series of deliberately chosen images, objects and installations created over the past two decades by six women artists—Beijing-based Chinese artist Yin Xiuzhen; Indonesian-born, Australian-raised artist Fiona Tan; Beirut-born, London-based Palestinian artist Mona Hatoum; Paris-based Chinese artist Shen Yuan; New York-based South Korean artist Nikki S. Lee; and New York-based Japanese artist ON-Megumi Akiyoshi—will be particularly studied. While there are apparent differences in their artistic formats and engagements with transnational flows, the works of these women artists, discussed in this project, articulate a process of ‘homemaking’ that is fluid but grounded on their creative interactions with mundane domestic materials and activities, which enable them to materialise connections with multiple geographical localities and people. ‘Homemaking’, in this study, refers not to the construction of a material structure of dwelling, but rather to an embodied habitual way of living, which constitutes and reconstitutes the relation to places where one inhabits with other individual subjects. Rather than simply giving an account of certain women artists’ personal experience of exile, diaspora and voluntary or forced transnational migration, this project places its primary focus on the material construction, presentation and circulation of artworks. It explores themes of inhabitation, displacement and belonging less as biographic narratives than as material and affective conditions of physical and conceptual interactions with works of art that provoke reflections on one’s encounters, identification and disidentification with places, cultures and people without negating possible conflicts and disparities. By looking into these women artists’ fantasies of inhabiting a global ‘home’, this project also attends to their inevitable negotiations with the increasingly marketised contemporary art world, which allows and, at times, compels them to travel. In this way, it investigates the complex intersection of women, art labour and networks of power under globalisation. This project discusses how these women artists’ globally oriented but locally situated artworks might create moments of intimate engagement between human bodies and their ever-changing spatial environments that interrupt a constant state of unsettledness and fluidity. It considers in what ways their itinerant, border-crossing artistic practices of ‘homemaking’ challenge normative discourses of social advancement, global capitalism and international migration, which often push women aside, forging immediate interpersonal connectedness across cultural and geographical boundaries.

27602720.label: Realisation of objectives
27602720.value: Peer-reviewed Articles & Monograph Book The PI published a peer-reviewed article at the end of 2021 in the leading art history journal, Third Text, especially dedicated to the critical analysis of contemporary art in the global field. Meanwhile, another peer-reviewed article developed from the discussion of artworks in the preface and epilogue has been accepted by Art Journal—one of the most important academic journals on twentieth- and twenty-first-century art and art history in national and global frameworks. More importantly, the PI has submitted the full manuscript of the proposed book, titled Women, Arts and Fantasies of ‘Homemaking’: Affective Domesticity, Embodied Inhabitation and Transnational (Dis)identification, to Manchester University Press’s Rethinking Art’s Histories series. In response to suggestions and feedback from the editors and reviewers, the relevant revision is currently under review. The book truly takes much longer time than expected. Due to multiple lockdowns and travel restrictions between 2020-22, the progress of this project on contemporary art and homemaking in transnational and transcultural circumstances was significantly affected by the pandemic, even if the PI tried the best to use virtual means for research. Some on-site research was eventually done in Spring 2023. However, the PI managed to submit the revised full manuscript, originally submitted in November 2022, in July 2023. In response to the feedback and suggestions from editors and reviewers, further revisions have been done and sent back to the publisher in December 2023 which are currently under review. Interviews & Research Archive The PI conducted four in-depth interviews with artists, Shen Yuan (February 2021 and May 2023) and ON-Megumi Akiyoshi (April 2021) and Fiona Tan (November 2022). The edited interview notes have been sent to the artists and their galleries for approval. As soon as the PI receives the confirmation from the artists and their representative galleries, the collected materials, both primary and secondary, will be deposited to Asia Art Archive as an individual research archive for on-site research only. Public Events Although public talks were not really delivered as planned, the PI participated in a number of online events in conversations with artists and curators on the artworks studied in the project, which attracted a worldwide audience of more than 400 art professionals, teachers, students, and members of the public (Please see below) 26 November 2022: Moderator and respondent; Zoom Webinar ‘Yin Xiuzhen: Materiality & Spirituality in Everywhere’, (in conversation with Song Dong, Curator of the exhibition Yin Xiuzhen: Everywhere; and Wong Weiwei, Curator of Exhibitions and Collections at CHAT HK), Pace Gallery Hong Kong. 3 November 2022: Organiser, Moderator and Respondent; ‘The Drifting Gaze: An Artist Talk by Yushi Lí’, Art History Research Lecture, Centre for Contemporary Art, University of St Andrews. 31 March 2022: Organiser, Moderator and Respondent; Art History Research Seminar (HKU) ‘Queer Chinese Feminist Archipelago: Shanghai, Miami, and San Francisco’ (Speaker: Dr Alpesh Kantilal Patel, Tyler School of Art and Architecture, Temple University, US). Conference Papers The PI delivered five academic papers in international conferences on relevant topics investigated in this project; moreover, the PI was also invited to give two research seminar lectures on the book project in March and December 2022 respectively at two leading UK universities—University of St Andrews and Loughborough University. Teaching & Learning In association with the research findings from this project, the PI updated the syllabi of three courses taught at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels—ARTH4009 Perspectives in Contemporary Art; ARTH3020 Women Making Art After 1960 and ARTH2100 Body, Gender and Sexuality in Contemporary Art. With the educational fund, the PI also conducted several Experiential Teaching & Learning activities (Please see C11 for more details).

27602720.label: Major findings and research outcome
27602720.value: This project provides a distinctive insight into women’s engagements with both mundane domesticity and art practices closely tied to intensified transnational flows and transcultural exchanges. The discussion offers several interventions into the study of contemporary art. Firstly, it attends to the increasing feminisation of migration in association with transnational East Asia, shedding light on the important role played by women in the practices of dwelling and travelling which are largely left unacknowledged in mainstream literature on globalisation. Secondly, in this project, works of art are studied as dynamic embodied processes of production, perception and interpretation which underline the contribution of both artists and viewers to co-constituting varied artistic configurations of home. Thirdly, this study neither celebrates a romanticised and privileged form of nomadism in the artworld, nor merely attend to the loss and struggles caused by forced displacement and migration. It enriches and expands existing literature on relevant topics. Based on research findings from this project, the PI published a peer-reviewed article at the end of 2021 in the leading art history journal, Third Text. Meanwhile, another peer-reviewed article has been accepted by Art Journal—one of the most important academic journals on modern and contemporary art and art history in national and global frameworks. Furthermore, the PI has submitted the full manuscript of the monograph book to Manchester University Press’s Rethinking Art’s Histories series (see C8). In response to suggestions and feedback from the editors and reviewers, the relevant revisions are currently under review. Between 2021 and 2023, the PI delivered five papers in international academic conferences (see C 9); and gave two research seminar lectures in 2022 at university of St Andrews and Loughborough University respectively. In addition, the PI participated in a number of online public events in conversation with artists and curators on the artworks studied in the project, including ‘Yin Xiuzhen: Materiality & Spirituality in Everywhere’, Pace Gallery Hong Kong (26/11/2023) and ‘The Drifting Gaze: An Artist Talk by Yushi Lí’, Centre for Contemporary Art, University of St Andrews (3/11/22), which both attracted a worldwide audience of more than 400 art professionals, teachers, students, and members of the public. In association with this project, the PI updated the syllabi of three courses taught at HKU. With the educational fund, the PI also conducted several Experiential Teaching & Learning Activities (see C11).

27602720.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27602720.value: The relevant research into feminist, post/decolonial and queer theories, as well as new materialist methodologies in this project has lead to a new research proposal, titled Forging Intimacies: ‘Queering’ Contemporary Chinese Art. The written transcripts of collected primary and secondary materials will become part of an individual research archive donated to Asia Art Archive after receiving the approval from the artists and their representative galleries and made accessible to scholars and students for on-site research only. The PI has been also discussing with local art and cultural institutions, such as Oi! Hong Kong, for an exhibition focusing on Shen Yuan's works.

27602720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27602720.value: Women, Arts and Fantasies of Homemaking examines deliberately chosen works created during the 1990s and 2000s by five women artists of different East Asian heritage—Beijing-based Chinese artist Yin Xiuzhen, Indonesian-born Australian-raised Dutch artist Fiona Tan; Paris-based Chinese artist Shen Yuan; New York- and Seoul-based South Korean artist Nikki S. Lee and New York-based Japanese artist ON-Megumi Akiyoshi. In association with these women artists’ practices of artmaking and homemaking in transnational transcultural circumstances, East Asia, in this book, is not taken as a stably defined geopolitical location. Rather, it comes to the fore as a mutable and shifting material and sociocultural positioning which is relational and subject to continuous reworkings through specific encounters in and via art with different places and people. Far beyond exploring each artist’s individual histories of travel, migration, displacement or (re)settlement, the present study considers how Yin, Tan, Shen, Akiyoshi and Lee, with their works which configure or evoke mundane domesticity, enable themselves and viewers to foster intimate embeddedness in a range of living environments, whether familiar or foreign, while reflecting on diverse conditions of cross-border mobility and connectivity.

27602920.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27602920.value: 考古中東古代歷史：以實地考察與數碼科技探討古亞美尼亞人類活動和人口流動

27602920.label: Project Objectives
27602920.value: Fill a gap in archaeological knowledge about the past in the Vedi river valley by excavating stratigraphic sequences at the Vedi Fortress and surveying the landscape to locate sites. Advance research and publish about three theoretical topics: the lived experience at mountain-plain intersections, militarization and remilitarization of directed-mobility landscapes, and differential identity expression through pottery. Expand connections, dialogue, and idea sharing between the scholars studying the ancient Near East and the east Asian archaeological community. Increase the efficiency of digital data collection in the field, while maintaining or improving accuracy, through software and hardware experimentation and development. Establish engineering requirements and parameters for implementing 3d scanning of every object collected from excavation and survey, by testing multiple potential solutions in the field.
