27602920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27602920.value: This project conducts archaeological fieldwork in the Vedi river valley on the southeastern edge of the Ararat plain in Armenia. The Ararat plain sits within the northern extents of the ancient Near East, a region known for early advances in societal complexity, including the first agriculture, writing, and cities. This research project is a collaborative effort between the University of Hong Kong (HKU) and the Institute of Archaeology and Ethnography of the National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia. HKU is one of the first east Asian institutions, and perhaps the first from Hong Kong, to help lead a major research expedition to the Near East. The Vedi river valley connects the fertile Ararat plain with the resource-rich Gegham mountain range, serving as an important route for travel, trade, and communications. Despite its vital position, relatively little archaeological attention has been paid to this area compared with surrounding regions. Thus, fieldwork in this valley will contribute important new data to archaeological inquiry on the ancient Near Eastern Bronze and Iron ages (ca 1500BCE–300CE) and the Medieval period (ca 1100–1400CE). Furthermore, based on the unique local landscape, this fieldwork aims to advance scholarly dialogue on three critical topics. First, this project examines the lived experience at a mountain-plain intersection, a place where climatic and topographic conditions change rapidly over short distances. Second, the research explores the societal and political factors that influence landscape militarization and remilitarization. Third, through detailed analyses of pottery, this project investigates the material manifestations of identity formation. Each summer, an international team travels to Armenia to conduct surface survey and undertake excavations to map and investigate archaeological sites. The main excavation focuses on the Vedi Fortress, a site with monumental fortification walls situated with a commanding view of the valley. The first two seasons (2019–2020) of this five-year project will stabilize the working logistics, enabling intensive data collection and analysis during the final three seasons (2021–2023), the focus of this application. This project also serves as a laboratory for experimentation with innovative digital methods in archaeological fieldwork, especially in 3d scanning. The long scholarly tradition of archaeology in the ancient Near East provides an important comparative example for studying ancient complex societies in China and east Asia. This project intends to engage in scholarly dialogue and the exchange of theoretical and methodological ideas with the east Asian archaeological community. 該項目於亞美尼亞阿拉拉特平原東南邊緣的河谷（Vedi river valley）進行考古學實地考察。阿拉拉特平原位於古代近東北部的延伸地帶，該地區以早期發展複雜的社會系統聞名，是農業、書寫系統和城邦國家的誕生地。這項研究項目由 香港大學（HKU）與 亞美尼亞共和國國家科學院考古學與民族誌研究所 （Institute of Archaeology and Ethnography of the National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia）合作進行。香港大學是東亞地區其中一所最早帶領進行近東大型研究考察的機構，很可能是香港首間支持此類學術發展的機構。 Vedi 河谷 位於土地肥沃的阿拉拉特平原和資源豐富的Gegham山脈的交匯處，成為交通，貿易和通訊的重要路線。儘管這個地區處於如此重要的位置，但與周圍地區相比，缺少相關的考古研究。因此在這個河谷進行的實地考察，將為研究古代近東銅、鐵器時代（約公元前一千五百年至公元前三百年）和中世紀（約公元一千一百年至一千四百年）考古學研究提供重要的新數據。另外，根據當地獨特的地理地貌，此次實地考察將針對性的促進三方面的關鍵學術討論。其一，由於項目所在地位於山區和平原的交匯點，氣候和地形在短距離範圍內變化劇烈，通過對出土實物的研究，研究人員得以了解當時生活在此的人群的生產生活情況。其二，項目意在研究探索影響地形軍事化和再軍事化的社會和政治因素。其三，通過對出土陶器的詳細分析，試圖研究相應的身份形成的物質表現。 每年夏天，都會有一支國際團隊遠赴亞美尼亞進行地面調查，發掘並記錄當地的考古遺址。发掘集中在可以俯瞰山谷的一个制高點，帶有巨大防禦城牆的古城遺跡 Vedi Fortress。這個五年項目的前兩個季節（2019–2020年）的主要任务是穩定後勤工作，為後三個重點季節（2021-2023年）需進行的密集數據收集和分析鋪路。該項目還可為創新科技在考古學領域的應用提供實驗經驗，特別是3D掃描的應用。 近東古代考古學悠久的學術傳統為研究中國和東亞古代複雜社會系統提供了重要的比較範例。該項目旨在推進與東亞考古界學術對話及理論和方法論的交流。

27603020.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27603020.value: 女性天皇與日本早期佛教藝術發展史

27603020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603020.value: This project will be the first study to investigate the patronage of Buddhist art by female emperors in Japan from the sixth to eighth centuries. The early Japanese period under examination witnessed the unprecedented succession of eight female emperors. As active patrons of Buddhist art, they promoted Buddhism as the state religion, and facilitated the recruitment of foreign monks and artisans skilled in metal-casting, printing, the Chinese writing system, and wooden architecture, thereby fostering the centralization of court rule across the archipelago. This rich history at the intersection of art, gender, politics, technology, and religion has, however, been glossed over in the existing scholarship, which prioritizes male emperors and courtiers as the instigators of these changes. Such gender prejudice has also reduced the Buddhist artifacts associated with female emperors to the category of “private” commissions as opposed to the “public” commissions of their male counterparts, which are thus accorded greater historical significance. To redress these biases, this project will contextualize the production of Buddhist art in early Japan by delineating the networks of patrons, bureaucrats, and artisans involved. It will closely examine the inscriptions and production processes of extant Buddhist artifacts from early Japan and compare them with archaeological materials and textual records documenting Buddhist patronage by female emperors. As a whole, the project has three historiographical implications. First, it will call attention to the indispensable roles of female emperors in refashioning early Japan as a Buddhist state. Second, it will position Buddhist artifacts as vessels charged with social-political ambitions that operated beyond the ritual or aesthetic contexts. Third, it will demonstrate that Buddhism gained court endorsement in Japan precisely by offering a new discursive framework that justified female rulership and political centralization. The project’s academic output will take the form of a book proposal, a full monograph draft, and three journal articles contributing to the disciplines of art history, gender studies, and the history of religion. 是項計劃將探討女性天皇對日本早期佛教藝術發展史所作出的貢獻。在六至八世紀之間，多位女性天皇統治日本皇室，並積極資助佛教藝術。除了奠定國家佛教的基礎，她們招募大量精通冶金、印刷、漢字書寫和木建築的僧尼和工匠，並透過這些技術促進權力的集中化。然而，先行研究大多忽視這段涉及藝術、性別、政治、科技和宗教的歷史，並把焦點集中在男性天皇和政治家上。先行研究亦多假設與女性天皇有關的佛教資助為「私人」宗教活動，以區別於與男性天皇有關的佛教資助。因此，是項計劃將透過佛教文物的銘文、考古資料和歷史記錄重新探討日本早期佛教藝術的生產背景，以及日本皇室、官僚和工匠的合作關係。總括而言，是項計劃有三個意義。首先，它將闡明女性天皇對國家佛教所作出的貢獻。其次，它探討佛教文物於宗教儀式及美學以外對社會及政治產生的功用。第三，它將分析佛教如何為女性天皇登位和權力的集中化提供了適當的理由。本研究的主要目標是完成一部專著的計劃書及完整草稿，以及於藝術史、性別史和宗教史有關的學術期刊出版三篇文章。

27603620.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27603620.value: 透過機器學習和傳統風險預測設計一個簡單易用的風險計算機以識別在社區中可能患有抑鬱症的中國藉長者

27603620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603620.value: Mental health in older adults forms an integral part of healthy aging. Facing stressors in later life, such as chronic diseases, financial strain and bereavement, may induce psychosocial distress, feelings of worthless and social isolation. Depression is common at older ages, but is under-recognized due to stigma, misperception, and under-diagnosis. Identifying older adults at risk of depression in the community is urgently needed for timely support and early preventive interventions. Risk prediction models for later life depressive symptoms can be valuable tools in primary care settings, but have not been extensively developed and hence are under-utilized. Risk prediction tools developed in the West are based on limited predictors and small cohorts and do not make full use of machine learning. No tools have been recalibrated in Chinese. This study will generate a locally applicable risk prediction tool for use in routine healthcare to identify potentially depressed older Chinese adults in the community. Objectives: To generate a risk prediction tool for identifying older Chinese adults at risk of developing depressive symptoms by: i) comparing performance between machine learning and conventional modeling; ii) assessing the added predictive power of electronic medical records and neighborhood attributes; and iii) building an easy-to-implement online risk calculator. Design: A prospective cohort study of Hong Kong older Chinese adults (>65 years). Participants: Hong Kong’s Elderly Health Service (EHS) cohort without depressive symptoms at baseline (n=~156,000) enrolled during 1998-2017, of which electronic medical records and neighborhood attributes will be obtained from a sub-sample (n=~16,000). Exposure: Risk predictors (including demographics, socio-economic position, lifestyle, physical health and illnesses, social support, functional ability, and cognitive performance). Outcomes: Probability of developing symptoms of later life depression within 2 years. Data analysis: Machine learning algorithm will be developed in a 3-step process: automated feature selection, model building with a boosted ensemble algorithm, and cross-validation. This model will be compared with two conventional algorithms: an existing recalibrated logistic algorithm and a newly developed Cox algorithm. Expected results: The locally developed machine learning risk prediction tool for identifying potentially depressed older Chinese adults will outperform recalibration of an existing model or a conventionally developed model. Including electronic medical records and neighborhood attributes will improve predictability. The online risk calculator will be readily usable in local primary care settings. Significance: These findings will provide a state of the art means of identifying older Chinese adults in the community who need psychosocial support to promote healthy aging. 長者的心理健康是健康活齡不可或缺的一部分。長期病患，財務壓力和至親離世等因素都有可能導致心理社會壓力，令長者感覺被社會孤立，產生無助感。抑鬱症在長者中很常見，但由於偏見、誤解和檢查不足而往往未能得到重視。 因此我們必須及早識別在社區中有較高風險患上抑鬱症的長者，以及時預防和提供支援。 基層醫療需要一個能有效評估長者出現抑鬱症狀的風險預測工具。然而，這類型的風險預測工具發展得並不成熟，以致使用率偏低。現時西方國家開發的風險預測工具未有完全利用機器學習。這些預測工具亦大多只以少量預測因素及規模較小的隊列研究為基礎，更尚未被重新校準以適用於中國。這項研究將會發展一個香港本地適用的風險預測工具，用以恆常檢測社區中可能患有抑鬱症的長者。 目的：通過下列方法研究出一個風險預測工具，以識別較高風險出現抑鬱症狀的中國藉長者：i）比較機器學習和傳統模型的表現； ii）評估電子病歷和鄰里特徵的預測能力； iii）建立易用的風險計算機。 設計：一項針對香港中國藉長者（65歲或以上）的前瞻性隊列研究。 參加者：曾於1998年至2017年期間使用香港長者健康服務（EHS），而過往未有出現抑鬱症狀的中國藉長者（n =〜156,000）。部份長者亦會提供電子病歷和鄰里特徵（n =〜16,000） 。 因素：風險預測因素（包括人口特徵，社會經濟地位，生活方式，健康狀況，社交支援，身體機能和認知能力）。 結果：預測長者在2年內出現抑鬱症狀的可能性。 數據分析：機器學習模型將分為3個演算步驟：自動特徵篩選，利用增強集成算法建立模型，及交叉驗證。 該模型將與兩種傳統模型： 一個經過重新校準的邏輯算法和一個新建立的比例風險算法作比較。 預期結果：由本地開發並以機器學習為核心的風險預測工具將會比經重新校準或以傳統算法建立的預測工具更為優勝。加入長者的電子病歷和鄰里特徵後，新的風險預測工具將更有效預測長者出現抑鬱症狀的風險。網上風險預測計算機將更易為基層醫療廣泛應用。 啟示：研究結果將會更有效識別有較高風險出現抑鬱症狀的長者，以及時提供支援並達致健康活齡。

27604520.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27604520.value: Until recently, arguably due to twentieth-century political circumstances, Spain has been underrepresented in mainstream art historical narratives and often positioned as a receiver of influences from other European centers. Spain, however, was an incredibly dynamic place in the Middle Ages that not only participated in larger currents spanning Western Europe, but also differed significantly from its neighbors in its religious and cultural heterogeneity. This project contributes to the reinsertion of Spanish culture into mainstream discourses and advances the study of larger issues within medieval art history through the example of the important Spanish city of Carrión de los Condes and its monuments. Despite being one of the regions richest in Romanesque art across Europe, Palencia, with Carrión at its heart, has been largely overlooked in scholarship. Its position directly between the kingdoms of Castile and León, today a sparsely populated and unassuming area, provided in the eleventh and twelfth centuries a particular centrality leading to the region’s exceptionally rich development. Carrión was the capital and seat of powerful counts, a prominent stop along the popular pilgrimage the Camino de Santiago, and home to the second-largest Jewish community in northern Spain. The project will produce the first art historical monograph on the medieval city of Carrión as well as an article on Carrión’s role as an artistic center within greater Palencia. The book narrates the story of Carrión and its diverse communities. Its chapters lead the reader through an account of the rise and decline of the city told through its buildings, while advancing discussion of the intersecting issues of pilgrimage, urbanization, and social and religious authority central to Spanish art history. Within its evolving urban plan, Carrión’s monuments and institutions negotiate several audiences: from a major monastery catering to nobles and its community of monks, to parish churches that balance the needs of a transitory pilgrimage audience with those of locals, to a mudbrick synagogue serving Carrión’s Jewish community. From these buildings emerges a story of social upheaval as well as new conclusions on pilgrimage. Along with the book, the project will produce web resources that enable virtual access to medieval Spanish monuments for the book’s readers as well as the general public. N/A

27609420.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27609420.value: 之下、之間、之後：香港微型都市公園研究

27609420.label: Project Objectives
27609420.value: To examine the story of Hong Kong’s urbanization through an analysis of the smallest artefacts in the city’s open space network: Hong Kong’s network of open space has been assembled over a period of rapid urban transformation and geopolitical and socioeconomic change. Scholars have described Hong Kong’s big parks, greenbelts, urban forest, and nature reserves in relation to this history (Jim 1986; Bristow 1989; Jim 2000; Tian, Jim, Tao and Shi 2011). This research examines this story of urbanization through a critical spatial analysis of the city’s smallest, most overlooked spaces. Usually measuring less than half a hectare, Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens are the smallest components of the city’s public open-space network. This research weaves these abundant small public open spaces into the story of the city itself, connecting their smallness and publicness to something unique about Hong Kong. To speculate on new roles for these understudied small public spaces in the continuous social and ecological evolution of the urban form of Hong Kong: This research examines expanded notions of nature and publicness within the context of Hong Kong, positioning “Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens” as a unique landscape/urban open space typology with social and ecological value in the territory. In recent years, ecologists and landscape theorists have expanded notions of “nature” in the city (Gandy 2006; Del Tredici 2006; Pickett 2013) while social scientists and urban theorists have complicated notions of “publicness” (Yeoh 2003; De Magalhães 2010), resulting in a discourse on the city as an ecosystem in which natural and urban processes overlap, cooperate, and hybridize. Meanwhile, far from concrete, notions of “open-ness” and “public-ness” are relative and negotiable. It is in this context that Hong Kong’s Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens offers a unique narrative within a larger practice of creating small-scale, opportunistically-achieved, networked open spaces around the world. To create a much-needed database of these ordinary spaces to inform design and planning disciplines and instruct future allocation and design of small public spaces: This research builds on other typological studies of urbanism and urban structures of Asian cities such as Greg Girard’s work on the Kowloon Walled City (1993), Atelier BowWow’s Made in Tokyo (2001), and Jonathan Solomon’s Cities Without Ground (2012), excavating lessons and operations embedded in ordinary spaces through “typomorphological studies” (Moudon 1994). In this research, documentation and critical analysis help to form a database of Hong Kong’s Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens. As an important component of this database, innovative categories are proposed to frame the key spatial and environmental challenges of each Sitting-out Area or Rest Garden and position them in relation to the material processes of the city’s urbanization. To frame a critical analysis of development, governance, and techno/bureaucratic practices in Hong Kong through these spatial anomalies: This research facilitates possible policy change towards provision of site specific and highly accessible public open space in Hong Kong. The current guidelines for planning and designing Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens are based on a territorially scaled two-dimensional statutory planning framework, where scraps of lesser value urban space are allocated to fulfil the modest minimum 2 sqm per person open space provision in urban areas. In the future, Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens in this ever more built-up context will require a design and maintenance framework able to satisfy government requirements and local community aspirations, respond to the unique and contradictory forms and functions of the urban fringe, and be sensitive to the ecology of their site-specific flora, fauna and human beneficiaries. To contribute to a larger public conversation on the form, function, distribution and accessibility of public space in high-density cities: This research develops the community’s awareness of an overlooked aspect of the high-density urban fabric. “Everyday” public spaces have been and will continue to be a vehicle for knowledge exchange within the local community. In terms of dissemination, in addition to a publicly accessible database and journal articles, the PI will build upon her connections with local NGOs to organize public exhibitions and community workshops, facilitating an interchange of resources concerning the public realm in Hong Kong. These public events will allow the PI to share her scholarly research with daily users of these small public spaces, in turn receiving and incorporating users’ feedback into the conceptualization and evaluation of these spaces, linking their formation in the past, present condition, and possible future alternatives.

To contribute to a larger public conversation on the form, function, distribution and accessibility of public space in high-density cities: This research develops the community’s awareness of an overlooked aspect of the high-density urban fabric. “Everyday” public spaces have been and will continue to be a vehicle for knowledge exchange within the local community. In terms of dissemination, in addition to a publicly accessible database and journal articles, the PI will build upon her connections with local NGOs to organize public exhibitions and community workshops, facilitating an interchange of resources concerning the public realm in Hong Kong. These public events will allow the PI to share her scholarly research with daily users of these small public spaces, in turn receiving and incorporating users’ feedback into the conceptualization and evaluation of these spaces, linking their formation in the past, present condition, and possible future alternatives.

27609420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27609420.value: Hong Kong, with some of the most valuable land in the world, is planned and built-out to shockingly high densities. Yet between introverted complexes, below the smooth-flowing arterials and behind adjoining high-rise buildings, a different urban form emerges: small public parks called “Sitting-out Areas”, miniature interventions in an otherwise monumental Hong Kong, reflecting another narrative for the city. Referred to locally as saam kok see hang, literally a “three-cornered shit pit”, most Sitting-out Areas feature little more program than, eponymously, a place to sit and rest. Hard-to-find and overlooked, their ubiquity gives them an outsized impact and suggests a latent potential to operate as a landscape network. In the past two decades, increasing interest in the notion of small urban parks in high-density cities has challenged long-standing arguments about open and public spaces, where substantial size was thought necessary to provide recreation and restorative quality for city dwellers (Czerniak and Hargreaves 2007). The practice of creating small-scale, opportunistically achieved, networked open spaces has emerged in recent years, particularly in European and American cities with vest-pocket parks and parklets becoming foci of urban regeneration (de Mello Franco 2007; De Monchaux 2016). Unlike the coherently planned and managed micro-park programs in cities such as San Francisco, Philadelphia and London, Hong Kong’s Sitting-out Areas are the products of an ad hoc bureaucratic process. Though each contributes to a fulfilment of the city’s overall green space allocation guidelines, there are no clear expectations at the level of the site, leaving as undefined outcomes related to community, geology, ecology and history. More than five hundred Sitting-out Areas along with the allied Rest Gardens comprise the smallest features in the city’s formal network of public open space amenities. This project carries out a critical exploration of these understudied and undervalued open spaces to reveal their existing and potential benefits for the overall urban system. How do these spaces integrate with the daily public life of Hong Kong residents? How do these spaces interact with the hydrological and ecological environment of the city? What processes motivate or create these spaces? Collectively, these questions paint a bigger picture of how Hong Kong’s planning policies interface with the daily lives of people and inform future open space policies. Ultimately, this research contributes to a larger debate on the form, function, distribution and accessibility of public space in high-density urban settings. 作為全球土地價值最高地區之一的香港，其規劃和建設已達到驚人的密度。然而，在封閉的建築群之間，在順暢的交通動脈之下，在摩肩接踵的高層建築之後，存在著一種截然不同的城市形態。被稱為“休憩處”的小型公園，是對宏大香港城市空間的微型干預，講述了一個關於這座城市的不同故事。被當地人叫做“三角屎坑”的休憩處，其功能正如其名稱所指，是坐下和休息的地方。這些位置隱秘且常被人忽視的小型公園，因數量繁多且無處不在而具有鮮為人知的巨大影響，以及作為這座高密度城市景觀網絡的潛力。 在過去的二十年中，對高密度城市中的小型城市公園這一概念的興趣日益濃厚。這一概念的興起挑戰了長期以來有關開放和公共空間的論點，即認為若要為城市居民提供娛樂和修養服務，大型的開放和公共空間必不可少。近年來，出現了對小型的、見縫插針地置入的、網絡化的開放空間的積極營造，特別是在歐美城市中，構建口袋公園和停車位公園成為城市復興的焦點。與舊金山、費城和倫敦等城市中那些統一規劃和管理的微型公園計劃不同，香港的休憩處可被視作本地官僚程序的產物。從數據上來看，每一個休憩處都通過其設立而對滿足城市總體綠色空間分配標準有所貢獻；然而，對特定場地潛力的明確構思的缺乏，導致休憩處與社區、地質、生態或歷史條件相關的實際效益不明確。 分佈在香港城區各處的超過五百個休憩處和休憩花園，是這座城市正規休憩用地設施網絡中尺度最小的組成部分。本項目對這些未被充分研究和重視的開放空間進行批判性探索，以揭示其對於整個城市系統的現有和潛在利益。例如，這些空間如何與香港居民的日常公共生活融為一體？這些空間如何與城市的水文和生態環境相互作用？究竟是哪些過程激發或創造了這些空間？本項目對這些問題的提出和回應，將使我們更好地理解香港的規劃政策如何與人們的日常生活互動，並為未來開放空間政策的製定提供參考。最終，本研究旨在為有關高密度城市環境中公共空間的形式、功能、分佈和可達性的更大範圍的討論做出貢獻。

27609420.label: Realisation of objectives
27609420.value: During the project period (01/07/2020–30/04/2023), by means of (1) a territorial-scale survey and typomorphological studies, (2) journal publications, (3) exhibition and public engagement activities, and (4) a publicly accessible online database, all five project objectives outlined in the proposal have been achieved to the fullest extent. (1) A territorial-scale survey and typomorphological studies The PI carried out survey and typomorphological studies for 100 Sitting-out Areas and Rest Gardens, located in distinct areas and neighborhoods in Kowloon (no.=40), New Territories (no.=40), Outlying Islands (no.=5), Hong Kong Island (no.=15). The 100 sites studied in this project were strategically selected based on the insights gain through archival research and discussion with communities. Notably, each of the 100 sites are allocated into one or two of the six categories identified in the project proposal, namely Heritage Signifier (no.=41), Infrastructural Spanner (no.=30), Geodynamic Filler (no.=25), Terrestrial Anchor (no.=14), Density Deconstructor (no.=34), and Ecological Amplifier (no.=24). Moreover, typomorphological studies are conducted to unfold spatial, organizational or procedural attributes of each focused site and to create strategic adaptation toolkits within a dynamic urban, social, and ecological context. Measured analytical drawings including plans, sections and axons, as well as bilingual descriptions have been created for each site. Research activates related to the territorial-scale survey and typomorphological studies contribute to the achievement of the following project objectives: 1. To examine the story of Hong Kong’s urbanization through an analysis of the smallest artefacts in the city’s open space network; 2. To speculate on new roles for these understudied small public spaces in the continuous social and ecological evolution of the urban form of Hong Kong; 4. To frame a critical analysis of development, governance, and techno/bureaucratic practices in Hong Kong through these spatial anomalies. (2) Journal publications Again, six categories are deployed in this project to frame the key spatial and environmental challenges of each site and position them in relation to the material processes of the city’s urbanization. During the first reporting period (01/07/2020–30/06/2021), the PI published one journal article in Journal of Landscape Architecture. Entitled “Terra infirma: The evolution of ground culture in Hong Kong,” this article focuses on the role that small public spaces play as Geodynamic Filler. Notably, this article features four exemplary case studies, including Kotewall Road Rest Garden, Belcher’s Street Sitting-out Area, Kennedy Road Sitting-out Area, and Wing Lee Street Rest Garden. https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/18626033.2020.1852687 During the second reporting period (01/07/2021–30/09/2022), the PI published another journal article in Landscape Research. Entitled “Ambiguous temporariness: production of time-space territories in Hong Kong’s small urban open spaces,” this article focuses on the role these small public spaces play as Heritage Signifier. Notably, this article features three exemplary case studies, including Kotewall Road Rest Garden, Centre Street Sitting-out Area, and Kennedy Town Bus Terminus Sitting-out Area. https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01426397.2022.2131744 These activates contribute to the achievement of the following project objectives: 1. To examine the story of Hong Kong’s urbanization through an analysis of the smallest artefacts in the city’s open space network. 4. To contribute to a larger public conversation on the form, function, distribution and accessibility of public space in high-density cities. (3) Exhibition and public engagement activities With the help from local NGOs such as Hong Kong Public Space Initiative (HKPSI), the project team organized public exhibitions and community workshops, facilitating an interchange of resources concerning the public realm in Hong Kong. The PI originally planned to set up a conventional exhibition in a gallery in Hong Kong Island. In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly group gathering restrictions, the PI reconsidered the format and venue of the exhibition to minimize the public health risk and maximize the exposure of the project to the general public. In addition to coping with the pandemic situation, the out-door projection installation is designed and curated for the following two reasons. First, carrying out the exhibition within the Sitting-out Areas allow the project team to have direct conversations with the audience, who are the users of these pocket parks. Second, the exhibition itself allows the team to project the realities of the study sites to the anomalies, gaps, interstices and mismatches of the city. During the first reporting period, the PI and her research team carried out four outdoor projection exhibitions in Kowloon. Each event lasted for 2 hours from 7 to 9PM on June 18–21 of 2021. Six Sitting-out Areas and their adjacent neighborhoods were used as the venues for the event, including Nathan Road/ Boundary Street Siting-out Area, Sycamore Street Rest Garden, Portland Street/ Man Ming Lane Sitting-out Area, Ning Po Street/ Shanghai Street Rest Garden, Waterloo Road/ Ferry Street Sitting-out Area, and Station Lane Sitting-out Area. During the second reporting period, the project team carried out another four outdoor projection exhibitions on Hong Kong Island. Each event lasted for 2 hours from 6 to 8PM on September 21–24 of 2022. Six Sitting-out Areas and their adjacent neighborhoods were used as the venues for the event, including Queen’s Street Rest Garden, Lok Hing Lane Sitting-out Area, Kwun Hoi Path Sitting-out Area, Eastern Hospital Road Temporary Rest Garden, Quarry Bay Street Sitting-out Area, Lei King Wan Sitting-out Area. The beta version of this evolving database was developed and launched during the first reporting period, featuring 30 analytical case studies by the end of June 2021. The database currently includes 300 original drawings, 1000 original photographs, as well as bilingual analytical description for each of the case studies, totaling 28,000 words in Chinese, and 18,000 words in English. The case studies included in the database can either be arranged by their geographical locations, or by typologies. As an important component of this database, innovative categories are applied to frame the key spatial and environmental challenges of each Sitting-out Area or Rest Garden and position them in relation to the material processes of the city’s urbanization. 27609420.label: Major findings and research outcome
27609420.value: This project carries out a critical exploration of understudied and undervalued small open spaces to reveal their existing and potential benefits for the overall urban system. Key findings and research outcome are showcased by two journal articles included in the Research Output (Part C) of this report. The first article published in Landscape Research challenges the dominant Hong Kong narrative that fetishizes how land value and spatial efficiency have shaped the city’s urban spaces, by enlightening the role of geotechnical risk management as a catalyst for urban reconfiguration. It casts new light on the urbanist interventions through a close study of the geotechnical expertise and commitment invested in consolidating the city’s historically unstable ground. Specifically, it examines how the design, construction and upgrading of slopes and retaining structures shape the city’s small public spaces such as sitting-out areas and rest gardens to this day. Seen through a landscape architectural and geographical eye, urban grounds are revealed as a single dynamic entity in which biotic and abiotic, human and natural processes are constantly at play. It suggests how fragments of open space in hyper-dense Hong Kong point the way to a more deliberate dialogue and possible changes in policy to encourage the provision of site-specific, highly accessible public open spaces. The second article published in Landscape Research integrates temporality into territoriality theories and investigates Hong Kong’s small urban open spaces through a territorial perspective. Focusing specifically on sitting-out areas and rest gardens, the smallest components of the city’s official network of open-spaces that are often created through temporary government land allocations, it investigates the ambiguous temporariness of these small open spaces through the conceptual lens of time-space territories. This conceptual lens allows us to view Hong Kong’s small urban open spaces as territorial landscapes in the making, a phenomenon as much about time as space. It conceptualizes these compact public open spaces as landscapes of different territorial events and analyses the frictions between the various social and environmental processes that define the city’s formative cycles. Responding to the unique socio-economic and political context of Hong Kong, this article argues that the nature of the impermanence of sitting-out areas and rest gardens created through temporary land allocations is ambiguous and diverse due to the complexity of each site’s history and/or the uncertainty surrounding the form and speed of future transformation. These research findings open up urban open spaces to a new territorial perspective and recognises public open space use as a complex system. The scholarly contributions of this project include: 1) offering a glimpse into the potential future evolution of a unique public open-space typology and points to a means of more deliberate dialogue in the city, interweaving large and small, public and private, and permanent and temporary; 2) shedding light on the important role these temporary open spaces play in filling a gap in our collective memory, which represent an important yet so far undervalued aspect of the discussion about conservation in a rapidly changing city; 3) defining the publicness of public open space within the context of the growing socio-economic polarisation and segregation in our cities.

27609420.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27609420.value: The PI aims to continue the research project that examines the story of Hong Kong’s urbanization through an analysis of the smallest components of the city’s open space network, and in doing so frames a critical analysis of development, governance, and techno/bureaucratic practices in Hong Kong as illustrated by these spatial anomalies. Development and related course of action will be exemplified in the following three aspects, namely (1) database maintenance and expansion, (2) design intervention, and (3) academic publication. There are more than 500 sitting-out areas and rest gardens in Hong Kong. This project completed analysis and typomorphological studies of a selected collection of 100 cases in both Hong Kong Island and Kowloon. Further development of the research includes surveying and mapping sites that are not covered in this ECS project, but can be studied and added to the evolving database of Hong Kong’s compact public open spaces. The PI had previously been invited by the local NGO Design Trust to give talks about her research on small public open spaces in Hong Kong. The PI’s ideas on the potential sites of design intervention were adopted by the Design Trust Futures Studio program, which proceeded to transform three liminal small public spaces in collaboration with the government. The PI aims to seek future collaboration with local NGOs such as Design Trust will make a visible impact in the city. The PI has recently been reached out by Shanghai-based Tongji University Press, who is interested in publishing a book about 100 case studies completed in this ECS project that are currently featured on the publicly accessible database. The PI plans to put together a book proposal for a bilingual publication over the latter half of the year.

27612020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27612020.value: Regulated pharmaceuticals are readily available for over-the-counter purchase throughout Tanzania and global health policymakers regularly decry this situation as dangerous and disordered, as if no rules govern the use of such drugs in Africa. As antibiotic use becomes more widespread on the continent, for instance, there has been an outpouring of concern over the increase of antimicrobial resistance, with the World Health Organization reporting that this is one of the greatest challenges to global health today. Meanwhile, as in much of the Global South, biomedical markets in Tanzania have been flooded by a proliferation of counterfeit pharmaceuticals, with 30-60% of drugs estimated to be fake. As a result, representatives from major global pharmaceutical companies have started formulating strategies around fears that counterfeit medicines could push their customers to use traditional medicines instead of biomedicine. Despite such concerns, scholarship about the vernacular uses and meanings of pharmaceuticals remains limited. This study will contribute to these critically important issues by detailing why and how pharmaceuticals are used by differently situated social actors in Iringa, Tanzania. It will build upon research done for my dissertation, in which I found that bodily ways of knowing played a crucial role in enabling people to identify counterfeit medicines through their material qualities like color, texture, and taste. I will expand upon this work by studying the impact of the newly instantiated National Action Plan for Antimicrobial Resistance in Tanzania, which seeks to change how people use pharmaceuticals. Data will be collected on how the uses and meanings of pharmaceuticals are shaped in dialogue with such public campaigns, as well as in relation to other treatment options and broader cultural understandings of health and the body. I will employ qualitative research methods—including participant observation, interviews, and media analysis—in Iringa, Tanzania, a regional capital in the Southern Highlands (population 150,000) which is well-known for its preponderance of pharmacies. This research will contribute to a better understanding of pharmaceutical use in Tanzania and beyond, helping policymakers and medical practitioners who want to influence or understand how people use these medications. It will also challenge stereotypes about health in Africa and increase cultural awareness among Hong Kong residents and globally. While Africans tend to be portrayed as under-educated about proper pharmaceutical use in much of the international press coverage, this project will reveal the embodied practices through which Tanzanians apprehend the capacities of pharmaceuticals under prevailing conditions of radical uncertainty. 在坦尚尼亞各地，受管制的藥品很容易就能在櫃檯購買到。全球衛生政策制定者經常對這種危險和混亂的情況進行譴責，仿佛在非洲沒有任何管理這類藥品使用的規則。例如, 隨著抗生素在非洲大陸的使用越來越廣泛，人們對抗菌素耐藥性的增長愈加擔憂，世界衛生組織報告說，這是當今全球衛生面臨的最大挑戰之一。與此同時，正如在許多南半球國家一樣，坦尚尼亞的生物醫學市場充斥著大量的偽造藥品，據估計，其中30-60%的藥品是假藥。因此，基於假藥會促使客戶使用傳統藥物而不是生物醫學藥品的擔心，全球主要製藥公司的代表開始制定對策。 儘管存在這些問題，對於藥物的本地用法和意義的學術研究依然有限。這項研究將通過詳細探討坦尚尼亞伊林加地區(Iringa)社會行為者在不同環境中使用藥物的原因和方式，對這些至關重要的問題做出貢獻。本研究將建立在我博士論文的基礎之上，在研究中我發現身體化的認知方式在使人們通過諸如顏色、質地和味道等材質來識別假藥方面起著至關重要的作用。我將通過探討新施行的坦尚尼亞抗菌素耐藥性國家行動計畫的影響來擴展這項研究，該計畫的目的是改變人們使用藥物的方式。研究將對藥物的用途和意義如何在與此類公共運動的對話中形成，以及對其他治療選擇和對健康和身體更廣義的文化理解進行資料的收集。我將在坦尚尼亞南部高地有15萬人口，以藥品行業聞名的地區首府伊林加進行定性研究——包括參與觀察、訪談和媒體分析。 這項研究將有助於更好地瞭解坦尚尼亞和其他地區的藥物使用情況，為希望影響或瞭解人們如何使用這些藥物的決策者和醫療從業者提供幫助。它還將挑戰人們對非洲健康問題的刻板印象，在香港和世界中提高人們的文化意識。雖然在許多國際新聞報導中，非洲人往往被描述為在適當的藥物使用方受到的教育不足，但這專案將揭示坦尚尼亞人在普遍極為不確定的情況下理解藥物性能的具體方式。

27612420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27612420.value: Primaprous mothers who plan to breastfeed but who did not go on to breastfeed often face high levels of emotional and psychological challenges in their transition to parenthood. This can adversely affect their breastfeeding experiences and general well-being, and are associated with stress, anxiety and postnatal depression. While family psychoeducation and other supportive group programs are available in health services, these require face-to-face education sessions over a long interval and high engagement and trusting relationships and often result in low attendance and high drop outs. Mothers have expressed the need for psychological support of peer counsellors that allow them to support each other, helps in decision making and subsequently empower them. In views of the above challenges occur during Chinese mothers’ doing the month, are often housebound and find it difficult to attend group support or seek help during the first month postpartum which is the critical period in sustaining exclusive breastfeeding and at high risk of postpartum depression. This multi-center randomized control trial adopts two arm design to examine and compare the effects between home-based peer support program compared with breastfeeding information leaflet among women with low breastfeeding self-efficacy. Its three objectives are (1) to increase the exclusivity and duration of breastfeeding, (2) higher breastfeeding self-efficacy postnatally and (3) lower postpartum depressive symptoms. With significant positive outcomes found in the feasibility study, this home-based peer support program can be adopted by community maternal and child health services in Hong Kong to increase the proportion of exclusive breastfeeding and lower the risk of postpartum depression among mothers and infants with low self-efficacy in breastfeeding. Thus, these interventions have potential to improve breastfeeding practices and child wellbeing. Such interventions have therefore been considered as sustainable alternatives to counseling in primary health care settings. 計劃進行母乳餵養但沒有經驗的初產母親在過渡至父母的過程中常常面臨很大的情緒和心理挑戰。這可能會對她們的母乳餵養經歷和整體健康產生負面影響，並與出現壓力，焦慮和產後抑鬱相關。儘管健康服務中心提供了家庭心理教育和其他支援小組計劃，這些面對面教育課程需要進行一段長時間，而且需要母親們的高度參與和建立信任關係，這經常導致低出席率和高退出率。母親們表示需要朋輩輔導員的心理支援，她們能夠互相支持，幫助決定並增強自信心。 鑑於中國母親在坐月子遇到上述挑戰時，她們不能經常外出，所以難以在產後第一個月內參加支援小組或尋求協助，這是維持全母乳餵養和產後抑鬱高風險的關鍵時期。 這項多中心隨機對照試驗採用兩臂設計，以檢查和比較家庭式的朋輩輔導員計劃和普通保健之間的影響。它的三個目標是（1）增加全母乳餵養率和母乳餵養的持續時間；（2）提高母乳餵養的自我效能和（3）降低產後抑鬱症狀。 隨著可行性研究中發現的明顯積極成果，這個家庭式的朋輩輔導員計劃可以被香港的社區母嬰健康服務採用，增加母乳餵養自我效能低的母親的全母乳餵養率和降低產後抑鬱症風險。因此，這計劃有可能改善母乳餵養習慣和兒童健康。這計劃因此被當作是在基層醫療機構服務中，除輔導外可持續的選擇方案。

27613020.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613020.value: Integrated writing, where writing skills are usually deployed in concert with other skills, is vital to academic literacy in any language and is recognized globally as one of the important competencies in academic discourse communities. In the case of Chinese language in the Hong Kong context, integrated writing skills has been introduced in the existing curriculum and assessment frameworks since 2007. However, research suggests that both the teachers’ instruction and the students’ approaches are reduced to rhetorically formulaic practices for writing tests. Previous studies found factors influencing the performance separately, while this proposed study uniquely extended from prior work, will explore the inter-relationships of these factors collectively, and their contribution towards integrated writing performance. The factors under investigation included task representation, strategy use, multiple-text reading and independent writing skills. Reading and writing skills in particular are commonly taught in Chinese language classrooms. With the educational context taken into consideration, the findings will potentially enhance the learning of integrated writing, and further benefit students’ cognitive development. Quantitative and qualitative methods will be used in this study to triangulate the data collected. 300 secondary five students in Hong Kong will create an organizing plan, complete an integrated writing task, and answer a questionnaire on their strategy use. They will also attempt an independent writing task and a multiple-text comprehension task, which will reveal their literacy capabilities. A hypothesized model will be developed and tested using the quantitative data. Stimulated recall interviews will also be conducted with 36 of the participants to elicit a deeper understanding of the ongoing changes of task representation and strategy use during the course of writing. The proposed study has important theoretical and educational implications. Firstly, it offers a holistic view of the integrated writing process, with task representation and strategy use placed centrally, which will contribute to building integrated writing theoretical models. Secondly, it builds understanding of how the successful learners approach such tasks, and identifies the relationship with independent reading and writing skills that are commonly taught in literacy lessons. Essentially, the study adds value by linking the current practice to facilitate better maneuvering of the information read and integration of learners’ thoughts in their writing. Lastly, with a deeper understanding of the effect of their learners’ varied aptitudes, the study provides instructional and assessment support for teachers, assessors and learners, and thereby contribute to Chinese language learning that cater to individual needs. 綜合寫作任務要求學生理解多篇章中的信息，之後運用當中的意念與信息寫成一篇文章。在國際間的教學與評核中，綜合寫作能力已認定為重要的學術能力。香港中文教育也在2007年將此能力歸入課程與評估中。然而，研究顯示無論是教師的教學或學生的學習，均採用應對考試的模板，缺少了真實地建構學生的能力的學習方式。之前的研究顯示學生的讀寫能力、任務表征與策略應用等皆對綜合寫作表現有顯著影響。本研究基於之前的研究推前一步，探究這些因素之間的互動關係。 本研究為量化與質性並用的研究，搜集300名中學五年級學生的數據，並且訪問當中的36名學生。300學生完成一份寫作計劃、一份綜合寫作任務、一份獨立寫作任務、一份多篇章閱讀理解試卷，以及一份關於策略應用的調查問卷。這些數據將用以驗證本研究中假設的模型。半結構訪問則深入地探討學生的任務表征與策略應用在寫作過程中所產生的變化。 本研究對理論的推進與教學有重要的意義。首先，學界將對綜合寫作能力用更全面的認識。尤其是本研究以「任務表征」與「策略應用」這兩個元素為焦點，將顯示綜合寫作過程中的變化，對理論頗具意義。其次，我們將更了解讀寫能力對綜合寫作的表現的影響程度，從而建構各種語言能力之間的關係。最後，具備了以上的知識，將對設計更符合學習需要的課程與評估內容，教師、評估者與學生都將受益。尤其是針對不同讀寫素養、不同任務表征與不同策略應用的學生，均可利用研究結果進行差異性的學與策略。

27613020.label: Realisation of objectives
27613020.value: Objective 1: Task representation and strategy of the integrated writing (IW) task In this project, we developed a new framework to elucidate the task representation created and strategy used by Chinese secondary students in Hong Kong when attempting an integrated writing (IW) task. The characteristics of task representation, specifically source use, rhetorical purpose, and text format were identified. It offers a holistic view of the integrated writing process, with task representation and strategy use placed centrally. Unlike scholarly inquiry on independent writing that had constructed various systematic models to illustrate the process, research in integrated writing is only now emerging to highlight the complex challenges learners face. Previous studies point to the writers’ task representation and strategy use as the core in the processing of integrated writing task (e.g., Flower, 1990; Yang & Plakans, 2012), but none investigated both these aspects concurrently. These studies either proved writers faced great challenges in creating a consistently constructive representation in a dynamically changing rhetorical requirements of the task; or determined that the writers’ strategy use during composing resulted in the extent of their written product portrayed their conceptualized task representation. Thus, this study takes a step further, to investigate these two aspects simultaneously to offer holistic understanding of the L1 integrated writing process in order to facilitate model-building of integrated writing performance. Objective 2: Direct and indirect linkages of multiple-text reading and independent writing skills towards IW task Acknowledging the importance of integrated skills as an essential component of 21st century skills, both the Hong Kong Chinese and English language curricula implemented integrated writing instructional programmes over the last decade. However, students’ conception of integrated writing is rather naïve, as illustrated in their own words: “integrated writing is shifting the words from one text to another” (Li et al., 2020). Using Bereiter and Scardamalia’s (1987) conception of “knowledge telling” and “knowledge transformation”, we transposed the writers’ skills from “knowledge telling” as novice writers who “shift the words from one text to another” to “knowledge transformation” which involves expert writers scrutinizing between the content and the rhetorical presentation. As the scholars pointed out, knowledge transformation, as a more difficult model, will not only produce higher quality of literary, but also benefit the writer by providing the opportunity for cognitive engagement from the process of writing itself (Bereiter & Scardamalia, 1987), which is perhaps more important. The design of this study takes into consideration the current practice in the literacy classrooms in Hong Kong. We found out that both teachers and students pay attention to the cultivation of independent reading and writing skills, and only drill for integrated writing examination. When conceptualizing this study, we purposefully examine the relationship between independent reading and writing skills and integrated writing skills, in order to increase the opportunity of incorporating teaching and learning of integrated writing with the independent skills in the Hong Kong literacy classrooms. Objective 3: Ongoing changes of conceptualization of IW task and the decisions in strategy use during the writing process Alongside the curriculum, understanding of task representation and strategy use of integrated writing are also beneficial to assessment. Some testing organizations have developed and used integrated writing tasks in their tests, but most tests neglected the synthesizing skills required for using the information in the source texts. It is not unusual that a common set of rubrics was used to score on both the independent and integrated tasks. There is a need to develop specific rubrics to address the uniqueness of such task type. As one of the examination-oriented Asian contexts, Hong Kong’s implementation of integrated writing is observed to be formulaic examination preparation rather than acquisition of skills authentically. For instance, some teachers referred to integrated writing as “the integrated test paper” (Li et al., 2020), and thus restricted the students’ thinking and motivation to cultivate integrated skills. Furthermore, test design is also simplified to discrete scoring items and the students’ performance is vaguely represented in the recent annual reports of Diploma of Secondary Examination (Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority, 2017). By researching the process and strategies used by students, the project team gained a deeper understanding of students' thinking on these tasks. This in turn contributed to validating the use of integrated writing as an assessment type. The schools that participated in the project received performance reports, which helped them develop an awareness of writing skills as developmental through the secondary years. This also allowed them to gain more effective teaching strategies, and to design school-based curriculum and assessment. Besides, on September 28, 2023 from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM, a two-hour seminar was conducted to report the project’s findings on the transition of DSE Chinese integrated writing skills to university-level academic writing. The seminar also provided practical suggestions to enhance students’ academic writing abilities. 38 students and teachers attended the seminar, and they felt that the sharing session deepened their understanding of the difficulties secondary students face in practical writing and they will try to apply the insights from the seminar to planning their teaching and assessment of practical writing in the classroom.

27613020.label: Major findings and research outcome
27613020.value: 1) Structural equation modeling was used to examine the main effects of multiple-text reading comprehension and independent writing on integrated writing, as well as investigated the interaction between multiple-text reading comprehension and independent writing. The results indicate that the effects of multiple-text reading comprehension and independent writing on IW performance is not independent; the influence of either one on integrated writing depends on the state of the other. Its implication on instruction is that it is doubtful that the writing experiences provided to these students were sufficient to allow them to attain higher levels of proficiency. 2) The characteristics of task representation, specifically source use, rhetorical purpose, and text format were identified. A significant positive correlation between these three factors and integrated writing performance was found, indicating the validity of the task representation scale and revealing the relationship between task representation and integrated writing performance. By analyzing think aloud and interview data, it was observed that students focused more on integrating the content from the reading materials with their own writing goals and incorporating their prior knowledge. They also adhered to a structured template they had in mind. However, they exerted less effort in summarizing, evaluating, or demonstrating a comprehensive understanding of the given reading materials. 3) The conjunct effect of two motivational theories (i.e., Growth Mindset framework and Self-determination theory) and strategy use in integrated writing performance were explored. Three major findings were observed. First, growth mindset was a significant positive predictor of autonomous motivation, strategy use, but not controlled motivation. Second, growth mindset indirectly promoted integrated writing through the mediation of strategy use and autonomous motivation. Third, neither autonomous motivation nor controlled motivation exerted direct effect on integrated writing performance, whereas both did so via the mediation of strategy use. 4) The relationship between achievement goals, strategy use, and IW performance was explored, and the results partly supported our hypotheses, the results showed that task-based goal positively influence all four strategies; self-based goal only significantly influence self-regulatory strategy; other-based goal positively predict discourse synthesis and test-wiseness. Deep-level strategies (e.g., planning and self-regulatory) positively influenced IW performance, while surface-level strategy (e.g., test-wiseness) negatively predicted IW performance.

27613020.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27613020.value: Our longer-term goal is to include integrated skills in the various developmental stages and level descriptors in the Hong Kong curriculum documents as found in other countries and regions. For instance, Deane (2011) has pioneered studies of multi-literacies for adolescents’ writing in English as L1 which highlighted the linkages between writing competence and other literacy skills. These experiences in other parts of the world and the promise of higher levels of literary quality and cognitive engagement will be shared with the EDB and HKEAA policy makers. The PI will continue to investigate in this area in order to attain this goal.

27613020.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27613020.value: Integrated writing has been recognized as a crucial academic proficiency in international teaching and assessment. Studies indicated that both teachers’ instruction and students’ learning were based on examination-oriented templates, lacking a learning approach that genuinely develops students’ competence. Previous studies have demonstrated that students’ literacy, task representation, and strategy application significantly impact their performance in integrated writing. This study builds upon previous research and takes a step forward in investigating the interactions among these factors. This study holds important implications for the advancement of theory and teaching. Firstly, the academic community will gain a more comprehensive understanding of integrated writing skills. Specifically, this study focuses on the elements of “task representation” and “strategy use”, which highlight the changes in the process of integrated writing, contributing to the theoretical framework. Secondly, we will acquire a better understanding of the extent to which literacy affects integrated writing performance, thereby establishing the relationship between various language abilities. Lastly, this knowledge will be valuable in designing curriculum and assessment content that better cater to learning needs, benefiting teachers, assessors, and students.

27613420.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613420.value: 不论社会经济地位如何，全球越来越多的家长在为孩子的学业寻求额外辅导。通常，这些额外辅导采取的是课外补习的形式，也就是我们熟知的影子教育。此研究拟定以多地点案例来探讨家长的阶级身份与影子教育之间的关系。这些关系体现在家长对补习类型（学术的以及/或者非学术的）的选择和意愿上。尽管目前有几项研究将家长对学习成就的需求与种族和民族联系在一起， 但全球范围内关于社会阶级对家长影子教育需求的影响的文献仍然很有限。因此，该研究将促进大众对香港家长影子教育需求的性质与模式的理解。 有人认为，家长的焦虑很大程度上促使了他们对影子教育的需求。他们焦虑自己对正规学校教育的认识不足。他们害怕被其他送孩子补习的家长“超越“。他们担忧自己的孩子在升学考试中表现不佳。他们认为有必要为保障自己孩子的未来“出力”。由于家长的意愿与机会结构相关，不同社会阶级的家长为孩子不同的未来做着不同的准备。因此，通过关注国际学校和公立学校补习的选择，本研究可以揭露家长意愿以及家长通过(给孩子的)额外辅导，如补习，来缓解自身焦虑的方式的阶级差异性。 此研究将采取比较案例研究法， 注重全球、区域和本地层面，对香港多个地点和学校进行探索。为了呈现学校类型的多样化，本研究有目的地挑选了香港四所英语授课的学校：两所国际学校，两所本地（资助）学校，并对学校和家长同时进行三轴（垂直的，水平的以及横向的）比较。通过样本变化最大化涵盖多种社会阶级，性别，年龄，教育水平和民族的家长（总计80位家长）。本研究将会揭示不同社会阶级和不同学校的父母对影子教育偏好的差异性。这是已有研究中一个很重要但常常被忽略的方面。 该研究将发现更多形成观念，意愿和不平等的社会经济条件和教育条件。因此它能为影子教育与社会阶级关系的理论发展提供信息，同时也能给予政策制定者，学校领导，老师和家长启发。

27613720.label: Project Objectives
27613720.value: Offer a new perspective on colonial sovereignty and violence in British India, the largest colony in the British Empire. Develop the first detailed historical examination of the Indian Penal Code, the legal system which still forms the basis of criminal justice in contemporary India, and which influenced the legal systems in multiple other countries (Uganda, Singapore, Brunei, Malaysia, Sri Lanka). Analyze unpublished and previously unused records from the High Court of Allahabad, the fourth oldest high court in South Asia. Offer the first proper historical study of hitherto unstudied legal procedures in colonial India, including capital punishment, corporal punishment and the royal pardon. Present an analysis of colonial violence that takes seriously the intersecting role of race, gender, age, class and caste in modern colonial power relations.

27613720.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613720.value: In 1857 soldiers, landlords, nobles and peasants from across northern India joined arms to participate in the largest rebellion in nineteenth-century imperial history. Quelled only through the declaration of martial law and considerable state violence, these events would fundamentally transform the ideological basis for colonial rule in India and the British Empire writ large. Representing the death-knell for the East India Company, the rebellion saw the transfer of sovereignty from Mughal state to British Crown, alongside a significant centralization of state powers. While scholarship has examined this as a turning point for Victorian liberal imperialism, an example of subaltern resistance, or as an important episode of colonial violence, this project situates this moment and its aftermath squarely within the legal history of South Asia, a relatively new and expanding field. Beginning with the show-trial of the Mughal King for his complicity in the movement (1858), the Queen’s Proclamation (1858), and the codification of criminal law (1860), this project explores how these constitutional and legal responses to rebellion attempted to address its violence, fashioning a new political order upon which Indian society would be governed. Examining this reconstruction of colonial sovereignty under the shadow of the most public rejection of its legitimacy since the American Revolution, this project then charts how the relationship between state violence, law and sovereignty developed over the subsequent seventy years of colonial rule, informing every level of legal practice. To explore this history of criminal law and colonial justice, one that connects charges faced by the King and national leaders such as Mahatma Gandhi, to the experiences of corporally punished lower-caste men, and illiterate widows brought to courts without legal aid, the project threads together wide-ranging case studies and archival materials that have hitherto received little historical analysis. This includes the practice of royal amnesty first instigated after rebellion; the reintroduction of whipping as a judicial punishment; capital punishment and the function of the prerogative powers of mercy; unpublished and previously unseen case-law for individuals charged with criminal offences; and the targeting of political leaders with sedition. One of the strengths of this project is its focus on both elite and ordinary figures. This project will produce the first book length study to centre the impact of the rebellion on criminal law in colonial India. Two academic articles will also be submitted to high-impact journals in the fields of legal and South Asian history. 1857年，印度北部各地的士兵，地主，貴族和農民聯合起來參加了19世紀帝國歷史上最大的叛亂。僅通過宣布戒嚴令和相當大的國家暴力來平息這些事件，這些事件將從根本上改變印度和大英帝國殖民統治的思想基礎。叛亂代表了東印度公司的喪鐘，叛亂使主權從莫臥兒邦移交給了英國王室，同時國家權力的顯著集中。雖然學術研究將此視為維多利亞自由主義帝國主義的轉折點，次生抵抗運動的一個例子，或者是殖民暴力的重要事件，但該項目將這一刻及其後果正當地置於南亞的法律史上，這是一個相對較新的歷史。擴大領域。 從莫臥兒王因參與運動（1858年），皇后公告（1858年）和刑法編纂（1860年）而進行的審判開始，該項目探索了這些針對叛亂的憲法和法律對策如何試圖解決暴力問題，形成一種新的政治秩序，以印度社會為基礎。該項目考察了自美國大革命以來公眾對其合法性的最強烈拒絕，在此背景下對殖民地主權的重建進行了研究，然後，該圖繪製了在隨後的七十年殖民統治中國家暴力，法律與主權之間的關係如何發展，並向各個層面提供了信息。法律實踐。 為了探索這一刑法和殖民司法的歷史，該項目將國王和聖雄甘地等國家領導人面臨的指控與受到嚴厲懲罰的低種姓男子以及文盲寡婦在沒有法律援助的情況下的經歷聯繫起來，迄今幾乎沒有進行過歷史分析的廣泛案例研究和檔案材料結合在一起。這包括在叛亂後首先煽動皇家大赦的做法；重新引入鞭打作為司法懲罰；死刑和憐憫特權的功能；對於被指控犯有刑事罪行的個人，尚未發布的，以前從未見過的判例法；以及針對具有煽動性的政治領導人的目標。該項目的優勢之一是同時關注精英人物和普通人物。 該項目將進行第一本書的研究，以研究叛亂對印度殖民地刑法的影響。還將向法律和南亞歷史領域的高影響力期刊提交兩篇學術文章。

27613720.label: Realisation of objectives
27613720.value: This project is completed and I have realized the project objectives. This culminated in two research articles in leading journals recognized internationally, and a book which has been submitted and is currently under review with the flagship series in legal history at Cambridge University Press. My first journal article "Killing in the Name of? Capital Punishment in Colonial and Postcolonial India" studied the politics of this enduring form of legal violence and its uneven application across society (objectives 4 and 5). This has been published by Law and History Review (Cambridge University Press) as part of a special issue I co-edited. My second journal article "Unpublished Records from the Allahabad High Court" explains the significance of unpublished court records from the perspective of the legal historian (objetive 3). This has been accepted and is forthcoming in History Workshop Journal, published by Oxford University Press, under a special section tackling archives and methodologies. Finally the most important objective of this project was the completion of my book manuscript, which tackles all five objectives through a deep study of criminal law, sovereignty and politics in India from 1857 through to 1922. To complete this project I worked closely with two academic editors at the Studies in Legal History Series at Cambridge University Press. Working with their advice, the book evolved to have a more fixed focus on mercy. This required significant extra and unexpected archival research and editing. The funding and teaching relief made available through this funding proved vital.

27613720.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27613720.value: The major intervention from this research is my book manuscript - Trials of Sovereignty. This book represents the first sustained study of the role of mercy and discretionary justice in modern South Asia. In doing so, it makes three larger interventions in the legal histories of South Asia and the British Empire. Firstly, I approach colonial terror and mercy as related expressions of colonial sovereign power. Whether it be along lines of class, status, caste, religion or gender, colonial officials and judges thought carefully about these social hierarchies, and developed a legal apparatus to ensure the violence of the state would be applied unevenly accordingly. Secondly, Trials of Sovereignty moves beyond approaches to violence and sovereignty that have exclusively focused on the ideas and practices of the colonial state. Instead, it shows how colonial subjects negotiated, tested, and over time rejected the ideological foundations of colonial rule. Finally, this book offers the first legal history to examine how the early development of India’s modern criminal justice system would be shaped by both the violence of 1857 and the subsequent emergence of an anticolonial political nation. This is both a significant chapter in the history of colonial justice, but also important context for the postcolonial present.

27615620.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27615620.value: The production of innovations is the key driver of long-run economic growth. Recent decades have seen shifts in the geography of innovation with the rise of China as a global innovative power. Although the production of innovations is a complex system connecting places and people across the world, the knowledge that functions as inputs to innovations is highly geographically localized, giving rise to specialized economic regions across the globe. The agents in these specialized regions don’t operate in isolation but are connected in global networks of various nature, for example R&D, production chain, collaboration, input-output and citation networks. Through these networks, agents access external materials, products, information and knowledge. It is widely accepted that the competitiveness of firms and regions is strongly linked to their ability to construct such networks and successfully source inputs from it. The innovative performance of Hong Kong has long been of special nature, given its central position in trade, production and knowledge networks and function as global hub between the West and East. However, little is known how the rise of China has impacted the innovativeness of Hong Kong. To what extent have Hong Kong’s innovation networks shifted towards China and away from traditional innovative powers in Europe and North America? How did this impact the scope, pace and direction of Hong Kong’s innovation system? Are these shifts similar across technological fields, disciplines and types of networks? Answers to these questions will contribute to the literature on the geography of innovation and globalization and are of great relevance to the current political debates in Hong Kong and China. The potential findings of this research have (geo-)political implications and great potential to inform governmental (innovation) policies and corporate strategies concerning knowledge sourcing and competition. To answers these questions, I propose to examine collaboration and citation networks in global academic and patent data. The paper-trails in these data reveal the connectedness among agents and places involved in innovation. I identify Hong Kong inventors, corporations, scholars and academic institutions, and retrieve information on their collaborators and agents they cite. Using this information, I build collaboration and citation networks that we can subset, plot, map and statistically examine for certain periods, industries, technologies, types of agent and disciplines. The resulting powerful database is used (1) for three academic papers and (2) an interactive website for journalists, policymakers and corporate executives to make informed news, policies and strategies. 創新的產生是長期經濟增長的重要驅動力。近幾十年來，隨著中國崛起為全球創新強國，創新地理領域發生了變化。儘管創新的產生是一個複雜的系統，它將世界各地的人們聯繫在一起；但是作為創新投入的知識具有地理局部性的特點，因此在全球範圍內形成了經濟特區。 這些經濟特區的各方參與者不是孤立運作的，而是通過各種性質的全球網絡相互鏈接，例如研發、生產鏈、協作、投入產出和引用網絡。通過這些網絡，各方參與者可以了解到外部的材料、產品、信息和知識。人們普遍認為，企業及地區的競爭力與它們建立此類網絡並從中成功獲取信息的能力緊密相關。 鑑於香港在貿易、生產和知識網絡方面的中心地位，以及香港為東西方間的全球樞紐，長期以來，香港在創新方面的表現具有特殊性。 然而，很少有人知道中國的崛起是如何影響香港創新能力的。香港的創新網絡在多大程度上已從歐洲和北美的傳統創新大國向中國轉移？這對香港創新體系的範疇、步伐和方向會有何影響?這些轉變在技術領域，學科和網絡類型之間是否相似？ 這些問題的答案將有助於學界對創新地理學和全球化的研究，並且對當前香港和中國的政治討論具有重要意義。同時，本研究的潛在發現具有(地緣)政治意義，將對政府(創新)政策以及對企業關於知識來源及企業競爭的戰略提供指導信息。 為了回答這些問題，我希望能夠調查研究全球學術和專利數據中協作和引用的情況。這些數據揭示了研究人員和參與創新的地點之間的聯繫。我將搜尋香港發明家、企業、學者及學術機構的資料，並檢索他們的合作者及各方參與者信息。利用以上信息，我將建立協作和引文網絡，可以對這些網絡進行子集、繪圖，並對特定時期、行業、技術、代理和學科類型進行統計檢驗。由此產生的數據庫將會用於(1)三篇學術論文和 (2)一個可供記者、政策制定者和企業高管了解相關新聞、政策和戰略的交互式網站。

27617920.value: 韩日对退休途径多元化的比较研究 & 退休后的心理健康结果

27617920.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27617920.value: 随着许多国家面临退休基础金融资金的高成本，政府实行鼓励个人晚些时候从事有偿业务的政策. 近些年,此前显赫的提前退休趋势似乎已经止步不前. 因此,延长工作寿命的动机和退休激励之间的紧张关系在许多国家加剧. 老年人改变劳动参与的社会环境对于理解退休的各种途径十分重要. 工作和家庭领域的经验在多大程度上影响了老年人的退休决定尚未得到充分理解. 拟议的研究将通过调查从家庭和性别规范到制度设置的确定因素,填补理论框架和经验发现方面的空白. 随着近年来老工人退出劳动力市场的模式越来越不规范,我们需要将退休理解为影响老年人的心理健康状态的长期过程. 我们需要进一步证据证明不同类型的退休途径与老年人的心理轨迹有何关系. 这一点在工作-退休过渡进程复杂的国家尤其重要. 该研究将采用序列分析及生长混合模型. 我们把退休途径相似的个人归类到退休年龄,捕捉到每条途径对心理健康的影响.

28300220.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28300220.value: The provision of clean water for all is now a global challenge in environmental health, and has been listed as one of the Sustainable Development Goals by the United Nations. With our increasing living standard, we are using more and more electronic devices, pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) in our daily lives. However, disposal of the used and non-recyclable materials has eventually resulted in the contamination of waters in the environment. While the harmful effects of heavy metals have been extensively investigated, the adverse effects of PPCPs on the ecosystem and human health are not yet well-understood and hence PPCPs represent a class of emerging contaminants of concern. However, methods for the detection of PPCPs remain rather limited and the development of new sensing methods for the rapid, convenient and real-time monitoring of PPCPs is therefore essential. We aim to design and synthesize a class of multi-functional flexible porous coordination polymers, also known as soft porous crystals, for the luminescence sensing of water pollutants ranging from heavy metals to PPCPs. Soft porous crystals, which are a class of crystalline materials constructed by the combination of organic ligands and metal clusters, exhibit highly porous structures that enable the encapsulation of and interaction with guest species. Light-emitting functional groups will be introduced into the structural backbones of these soft porous crystals to prepare luminescent chemosensors for the selective molecular recognition of heavy metals and/or PPCPs. More importantly, the soft porous crystals could also serve as a host to capture the target contaminant species, providing a rapid and relatively low-cost pathway for remediation. Previous work of us has demonstrated that the extent of hydrogen bonding interactions in soft porous crystals can be manipulated with the introduction of appropriate functional groups. By carefully controlling the hydrogen bonding and other non-covalent interactions in the system, we will design and synthesize soft porous crystals that can adsorb selected heavy metal ions as well as organic PPCP compounds for their detection and removal. As a further step, we will test the effectiveness of the newly-synthesized soft porous crystals in binding heavy metals and PPCPs from surface waters and wastewaters from the local environment. It is anticipated that the proposed study will lead to the development of a simple supramolecular tool for chemosensing of water pollutants, and will open up new opportunities in water remediation. 為所有人提供乾淨的水資源目前是一項環境健康方面的全球挑戰，且被列為聯合國可持續發展目標之一。隨著生活水平的提升，我們在日常生活中使用越來越多電子產品以及藥物和個人保健用品（ＰＰＣＰｓ）。然而，這些物料使用後不能循環再造，其廢棄最終導致水污染。重金屬的害處早已有廣泛研究；而ＰＰＣＰｓ對生態系統和人體健康的不良影響仍存在未知之數，是一類新興汚染物，惟探測ＰＰＣＰｓ的方法仍然有限。因此，發展新穎的感測方法來便利地實時監測ＰＰＣＰｓ有其必要性。 我們的目標是設計和合成一系列靈活的多功能多孔配位聚合物——又稱柔性晶體多孔材料——以供發光感測重金屬和ＰＰＣＰｓ等水污染物之用。柔性晶體多孔材料是一類由有機配體和金屬簇組成的晶狀材料，擁有高度多孔的結構，可封裝客體分子並與其產生相互作用。把發光功能性基團加入這些柔性晶體多孔材料的框架內，可製備發光傳感器並用於重金屬及／或ＰＰＣＰｓ的選擇性探測。更為重要的是，這些柔性晶體多孔材料也可用來當主體分子以捕捉目標污染物，提供了一種快速又相對便宜的去除方式。我們過往的研究顯示，柔性晶體多孔材料的氫鍵強度可透過適當的官能基來調節。通過氫鍵與其他非共價相互作用的精心控制，我們將設計和合成出可以選擇性探測和吸付重金屬和ＰＰＣＰｓ的柔性晶體多孔材料，並進一步測試這些新型柔性晶體多孔材料在本地地表水和污水裏的效能。可以預見，這項工作將發展出一套用來感測水污染物的簡單分子工具，為水污染物去除的研究開拓出新方向。

28300220.label: Realisation of objectives
28300220.value: Despite the influence of the pandemic that has caused unexpected delays in staff recruitment, purchase of consumables and research collaborations, the project has been successfully completed before the original project completion date. All of the objectives have been completely (100 %) and successfully realized. In this project, several classes of porous coordination polymers have been successfully synthesized based on various newly-synthesized organic linkers. These include (1) a series of mesoporous copper(II) coordination polymers for the removal of organic dyes, (2) a series of biocompatible porous coordination polymers based on alkaline earth metals for the removal of heavy metals, and (3) a series of modulated iron(III) porous coordination polymers for the removal of pharmaceuticals. The design and synthesis of all the compounds have been completed, and hence objective 1 has been 100 % achieved. All of the newly-synthesized organic linkers/ligands and precursor compounds have been characterized using spectroscopic methods such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and mass spectroscopy. For the newly-synthesized porous coordination polymers which exhibit low solubility in most organic solvents, they have been characterized by a combination of methods including single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), elemental analysis, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), as well as scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy. Objective 2 has been 100 % achieved. The photophysical properties, including the electronic absorption and emission properties, of the newly-synthesized porous coordination polymers and their corresponding free ligands have been studied by spectroscopic methods in the solid state. Thus, objective 3 has been 100 % achieved. For all the three classes of newly-synthesized porous coordination polymers, they exhibit remarkable porous properties and have been used for the adsorptive removal of various water pollutants, including pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) and heavy metals. As aforementioned, a series of coordination polymers based on alkaline earth metals has been successfully prepared. They have been utilized for both the adsorptive removal and luminescence sensing of metal ions such as copper(II) in water to address objective 4. For the removal of PPCPs as stated in objective 5, we have successfully synthesized a series of copper(II) porous coordination polymers for the removal of organic dyes, and a series of acid-modulated iron(III) coordination polymers for the removal of two non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), namely piroxicam and ketoprofen. UV-Visible absorption spectroscopy has been used as the major method to monitor the changes in the amounts of pollutants in the samples. Additional methods such as XPS, SEM and TGA have been used to monitor the changes in the elemental composition, morphology and heat stability of the samples before and after the adsorption process, respectively. For the porous coordination polymers based on alkaline earth metals, they also exhibit emission properties in the solid state and can be employed as luminescence sensors for the detection of copper(II) ions, and emission spectroscopy has been used to study the sensing properties. In this regard, the binding properties of the porous coordination polymers have been thoroughly studied to 100 % achieve objectives 4 and 5. The adsorptive removal and luminescence sensing properties of the porous coordination polymers have been comprehensively analyzed with respect to the chemical structures and porous properties. The final objective, namely objective 6, has also been 100 % achieved.
